n606033f0be2.s: A Rig Vedic hymn in which the speaker is a poet, his father a physician and his mother a grinder of corn illustrates:
o: Craft work being reserved for slaves
A priestly monopoly over all occupations
n606033f0be2.x: The hymn shows members of one family following different occupations, so occupation was not strictly birth-bound in Rig Vedic society.
xa: The physician was called **Bhishak**.
Broad groups: **priests, warriors, common people** — not rigid caste.
Later Vedic = **birth-based varna**.

na9eb9025d04.x: The early Vedic family was patriarchal, patrilineal and generally joint.
xa: Units: **Kula > Grama > Vis > Jana** (Kula smallest).
**Sons were preferred**; daughters treated kindly once born.
**Duhitri** (daughter) = "one who milks the cow".

n6ff5b14e46d.s: The Vaishya group is described as having developed from which group?
n6ff5b14e46d.x: Vaishyas were described as emerging from vis, meaning the mass of the people or tribespeople.
n6ff5b14e46d.tq: Match the social category with its stated origin term.
xs: The **Vaishya** grew out of the **Vis** — option **(3)**.
**Vis** = the mass of the people / tribespeople.
xa: Purusha Sukta: Vaishya came from the **thighs**.
**Rajanya** = Kshatriya, from the **arms**.
**Dasa/Dasyu** captives were slaves.

n374d56262a4.s: The Purusha Sukta occurs in which Mandala of the Rigveda?
n374d56262a4.x: The Purusha Sukta (Rigveda 10.90), a late addition, is in Mandala X and is the first statement of the four-fold varna.
xa: Gotra in the lineage sense first appears in the **Atharvaveda**.
Body parts: Brahmana = **mouth**, Kshatriya = **arms**, Vaishya = **thighs**, Shudra = **feet**.

nf0e6a4a857a.s: The distinction between Arya varna and Dasa varna in the early Vedic period primarily reflected a:
o: Cultural and linguistic distinction between groups
Religious division between two priestly orders
nf0e6a4a857a.x: Arya and Dasa varna reflected a cultural, linguistic and partly colour-based distinction between Vedic groups and conquered local groups; it was not yet a rigid caste system.
nf0e6a4a857a.tq: Distinguish an early cultural distinction from the later birth-based caste structure.
xs: **Arya varna vs Dasa varna** was a **cultural and linguistic** (and colour-based) distinction — option **(1)**.
It separated Vedic groups (conquerors) from conquered local groups — **not rigid caste**.
xa: Early society was tribal and largely **egalitarian**.
Broad groups: **priests, warriors, common people**.
Occupations were **not birth-based**.

na03da87613f.s: Early Vedic texts mention slave women being given as gifts to:
na03da87613f.x: Dasa and Dasyu captives and slave women are mentioned, including slave women gifted to priests, though slavery was not the base of the economy.
xa: **Untouchability** and **gotra** were absent.
Society was tribal and largely **egalitarian**.
Priests were also paid in **cows, horses, gold**.

ncb5f2b1d759.s: Marriage in Early Vedic society was largely:
ncb5f2b1d759.x: Early Vedic marriage was largely monogamous; adult marriage and choice in marriage were recognised and child marriage was absent.
xa: **Swayamvara** was practised.
**Niyoga** = union of a childless widow with her husband's brother.
Later, the **Aitareya Brahmana** called daughters a source of misery.

n1115554b840.s: The practice of niyoga in the Vedic context referred to:
o: The selection of a king by the Sabha
The exchange of cattle during marriage
The union of a childless widow with her husband’s brother
The marriage of a girl before puberty
n1115554b840.x: Niyoga was a levirate practice in which a childless widow could unite with her deceased husband’s brother.
n1115554b840.tq: Test the exact meaning of a specialised marriage custom against nearby social practices.
xs: **Niyoga** = **union of a childless widow with her husband's brother** (levirate) — option **(3)**.
Child marriage was **absent**; the king's selection involved the **Samiti**, not niyoga.
xa: **Widow remarriage** was allowed.
**Swayamvara** was practised.
Marriage was largely **monogamous**.

ne8528970a42.s: Early Vedic society preferred sons, yet women could:
o: Take no part in household religious rites
Receive education and take part in sacrifices and assemblies
ne8528970a42.x: Early Vedic women received education, took part in sacrifices and assemblies and could own cattle; there is no evidence of land ownership.
xa: Women seers: **Apala, Ghosha, Lopamudra, Vishvavara**.
Women attended the **Sabha** and **Vidatha**.
Debate: texts praise women seers, but society stayed **patriarchal** with son-preference.

n0f29d7c8c9c.s: Which one of the following does NOT belong to the group of Rigvedic women seers?
n0f29d7c8c9c.x: Gargi was a later Vedic scholar associated with Upanishadic dialogue, whereas Apala, Ghosha and Vishvavara were Rigvedic women seers.
n0f29d7c8c9c.tq: Use period discrimination to separate a later scholar from Rigvedic seers.
xs: **Gargi** is **not** a Rigvedic woman seer — option **(3)** (**BPSC 2025** odd-one-out).
**Apala, Ghosha, Lopamudra, Vishvavara** composed Rig Vedic hymns.
xa: Gargi held a **dialogue with Yajnavalkya** in the **Brihadaranyaka Upanishad**.
**Maitreyi** was also a later (not Rigvedic) scholar.
Women attended the **Sabha** and **Vidatha**.

n67834d39cb5.s: Which one of the following represents the broad sequence of the Later Vedic eastward expansion?
o: Punjab → Ganga-Yamuna Doab → Kosala, Kashi and Videha
n67834d39cb5.x: The movement proceeded from Punjab into the Ganga-Yamuna Doab, including Kurukshetra and the Delhi-upper Doab, and then towards Kosala, Kashi and Videha by about 600 BCE.
n67834d39cb5.tq: Solve the sequence by identifying the western starting point and the eastern endpoint.
xs: The expansion ran **Punjab → Ganga-Yamuna Doab → Kosala, Kashi and Videha** — option **(1)**.
In the Doab: **Kurukshetra**, then the **Delhi-upper Doab**; the east was reached by **c. 600 BCE**.
xa: **Kosala** = eastern UP; **Videha** = north Bihar.
**Kosala, Kashi, Videha** were the **new kingdoms** of the east.
**Iron weapons and horse-drawn chariots** helped the eastward push.

nea571693222.s: The legend of Videgha Madhava is narrated in the:
nea571693222.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana narrates how Videgha Madhava and Gautama Rahugana followed Agni Vaishvanara eastward from the Sarasvati.
xa: The land beyond the Sadanira was settled as **Videha**.
The legend reflects **iron axes and fire** clearing the Ganga forests.

n7ad063b2239.s: The Kurus were formed by the union of which two groups?
n7ad063b2239.x: The Kurus resulted from the union of the Bharatas and Purus; Kuru-Panchala, with its capital at Hastinapur, became the centre of Aryan culture.
xa: **Hastinapur** is also a PGW and iron site.
Upanishadic king **Pravahana Jaivali** ruled **Panchala**.

nc505b378b32.s: In Later Vedic texts, iron is referred to as:
nc505b378b32.x: Iron is called krishna ayas or shyama ayas ('black metal') in Later Vedic texts. Lohita ayas denotes copper, plain ayas in the Rigveda meant copper or bronze, hiranya is gold and nishka was a gold ornament later used as a unit of value.
nc505b378b32.tq: Krishna/shyama ayas = black metal = iron; lohita ayas = copper.
xs: Iron is **krishna ayas** (also **shyama ayas**), "black metal" — option **(2)**.
**Lohita ayas** = copper; Rigvedic **ayas** = copper/bronze.
**Nishka** was a unit of value, not a metal term.
xa: Iron was introduced in the north **c. 1000-800 BCE**.
Iron was **common at most PGW sites**.

nf91779d988f.s: Iron technology in North India emerged approximately between:
nf91779d988f.x: Iron technology in North India is dated to about 1000-800 BCE and was common at most Painted Grey Ware sites.
xa: Other sites: **Atranjikhera, Hastinapur, Kaushambi**.
Iron = **krishna ayas / shyama ayas** ("black metal").
New TN dates push Indian iron far before the Gangetic **c. 1000 BCE** date.

n6fbc98e5b45.s: Which archaeological site in Krishnagiri district, Tamil Nadu, has yielded iron AMS-dated to about 2172 BCE?
n6fbc98e5b45.x: Mayiladumparai (Krishnagiri district, Tamil Nadu) is AMS-dated to 2172 BCE and is described as the earliest iron-use evidence in India. Sivagalai (Thoothukudi) is the site with iron dated to about 2953 BCE, Thirumalapuram (Tenkasi) has an Iron Age urn chamber, and Adichanallur is the type-site for urn burials.
n6fbc98e5b45.tq: Link the exact date to the correct site before comparing the nearby South Indian sites.
xs: **Mayiladumparai** (Krishnagiri, TN) is AMS-dated to **2172 BCE** — option **(1)**.
It is noted as the **earliest iron-use evidence in India**.
**Sivagalai** (Thoothukudi) = iron about **2953 BCE**; **Thirumalapuram** (Tenkasi) = urn chamber; **Adichanallur** = urn-burial type-site.
xa: South Indian Iron Age now placed around **2100 BCE**, earlier than the Gangetic Iron Age.
BPSC **2022** asked when iron use began; the key was "**none of the above**".
n6fbc98e5b45.fixed: Mayiladumparai no longer the earliest: Sivagalai iron dated c. 2953-3345 BCE (2025); also removed duplicated A-D list

nd668fbe2dec.s: The legend of Videgha Madhava is associated with which use of iron technology?
o: Clearing the forests of the Ganga region with iron axes and fire
Introducing bronze metallurgy into the Indus cities
Constructing stone megaliths in the far south
nd668fbe2dec.x: The Videgha Madhava legend is connected with the clearing of Ganga-region forests through the use of iron axes and fire. It illustrates the role of iron in eastward expansion.
nd668fbe2dec.tq: Link the named legend with the specific technological process it illustrates.
xs: The legend reflects **clearing the forests of the Ganga region with iron axes and fire** — option **(2)**.
**Agni Vaishvanara** "burnt the forests" eastward from the **Sarasvati** to the **Sadanira (Gandak)**.
**NBPW** is post-Vedic (from **c. 600 BCE**), so option 1 is wrong.
xa: Source: **Shatapatha Brahmana**; priest **Gautama Rahugana**.
Land beyond the Sadanira = **Videha**.
nd668fbe2dec.fixed: stem carried a duplicated A-D list in a different order from the options

n2a5b6284e02.s: The emergence of the ‘second urbanisation’ is associated with which pottery phase and which group of settlements?
o: Black and Red Ware; Videha and Kekaya
Northern Black Polished Ware; Shravasti, Kausambi and Hastinapur
Painted Grey Ware; Kurukshetra and Bhagwanpura
n2a5b6284e02.x: True towns emerged after the Vedic period during the Northern Black Polished Ware phase, including Shravasti, Kausambi and Hastinapur.
n2a5b6284e02.tq: Match the urbanisation phase with its characteristic pottery and town examples.
xs: Second urbanisation = **Northern Black Polished Ware**; **Shravasti, Kausambi and Hastinapur** — option **(2)**.
True towns came only **after the Vedic period**.
**PGW**, **BRW** and **Red Ware** are Later Vedic village-phase wares.
xa: NBPW runs from **c. 600 BCE** with the **Mahajanapadas**.
**Rajghat** (Varanasi) yielded **pre-NBPW** pottery about **3,000** years old.

n965502748b4.s: Ochre Coloured Pottery is generally placed in which period?
n965502748b4.x: Ochre Coloured Pottery is post-Harappan and belongs to the second millennium BCE; the hallmark Later Vedic pottery is Painted Grey Ware.
xa: PGW = **c. 1000-600 BCE**, Gangetic plain.
OCP comes **first** in the protohistoric pottery sequence.

n7b2926d47f4.s: Which of the following groups contains the four wares known in the Later Vedic phase?
o: Ochre Coloured Pottery, Black and Red Ware, Northern Black Polished Ware and Red Ware
Black Slipped Ware, Painted Grey Ware, Northern Black Polished Ware and Ochre Coloured Pottery
Black and Red Ware, Black Slipped Ware, Painted Grey Ware and Red Ware
Painted Grey Ware, Northern Black Polished Ware, Red Ware and Amphora Ware
n7b2926d47f4.x: The four Later Vedic wares are Black and Red Ware, Black Slipped Ware, Painted Grey Ware and Red Ware. Northern Black Polished Ware is associated with the later Mahajanapada and second-urbanisation phase, not the Later Vedic group.
n7b2926d47f4.tq: Use the exclusion clue: identify the ware that belongs to the later urbanisation phase.
xs: The four wares are **Black and Red Ware, Black Slipped Ware, Painted Grey Ware and Red Ware** — option **(3)**.
Options with **NBPW** or **OCP** are wrong: OCP is post-Harappan, NBPW post-Vedic.
xa: Later Vedic phase: **1000-600 BC**.
⚠ Trap: **not NBPW** (APPSC-G1 **2024**).
Sequence: **OCP → BRW → BSW → PGW → Red Ware → NBPW**.
n7b2926d47f4.fixed: stem's A-D list mislabelled vs options (A in stem = option 3)

nb0961bac923.x: Adichanallur is associated with urn burials and is not a Painted Grey Ware site, unlike Atranjikhera, Hastinapur and Bhagwanpura.
xa: Other PGW sites: **Ahichchhatra** (Bareilly), **Noh** (Bharatpur), Kurukshetra.
About **700** PGW sites, mostly in the **upper Ganga basin**.
nb0961bac923.fixed: stem's A-D list mislabelled vs options

n90a3f9149dd.s: Which Vedic text contains spells and charms against disease?
n90a3f9149dd.x: The Atharvaveda contains spells and charms; the Samaveda sets Rigvedic hymns to music and the Yajurveda gives ritual procedures.
xa: ⚠ **Udgatri** = Samaveda priest; **Adhvaryu** = Yajurveda priest.
The **Atharvaveda** is the **latest Veda** and records folk practice.
**Brahmanas** = ritual commentaries (**Shatapatha, Aitareya**); **Aranyakas** = "forest texts".

n8b4b526fd25.s: Which Veda is associated with the Adhvaryu priest?
n8b4b526fd25.x: The Yajurveda gives ritual procedures in prose, is linked with the Adhvaryu and has Krishna and Shukla branches.
xa: **Samaveda** = hymns set to music, sung by the **Udgatri**.
**Atharvaveda** = spells and charms; the **latest Veda**.
**Upanishads**: **108** in all, **13** principal.

n54ebaf7dfa5.s: In the Later Vedic period, rice was known as:
n54ebaf7dfa5.x: Rice (vrihi) became a chief crop with ritual importance, while barley continued to be grown.
xa: Chief crops: **rice (vrihi)** and **wheat**.
Other crops: pulses/lentils, millets, **sugarcane, sesame**.
AP angle: **Sankalia** says rice was first harvested in AP in this era.

ncd307e03556.s: Which one of the following officials was responsible for collecting the king’s share of revenue?
ncd307e03556.x: Bhagadugha was the revenue or tax collector who collected the king’s share. Sangrahitri was the treasurer, Akshavapa the accountant and superintendent of dice, and Palagala the messenger.
ncd307e03556.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish related officials.
xs: The **Bhagadugha** collected the **king's share** of revenue — option **(3)**.
**Sangrahitri** = treasurer; **Akshavapa** = accountant / superintendent of dice; **Palagala** = messenger.
xa: Exam angle: Bhagadugha = **revenue collector** (**UPPSC 2023**).
⚠ Older notes say the **Sangrahitri** collected taxes.
**Bhaga** = king's share, **1/6** of produce.

n5b55be6a0ad.s: In the Later Vedic polity, the Sangrahitri was the:
n5b55be6a0ad.x: The Sangrahitri was the treasurer; the Senani was army chief, the Purohita chief priest and the Suta charioteer and herald.
xa: The **12 ratnins** were honoured in the **Ratnahavimshi** rite of the **Rajasuya**.
**Kshata / Kshatri** = chamberlain; **Govikartana** = keeper of game.

ndda274eb6f9.s: Which of the following correctly lists the taxes that became compulsory in the Later Vedic period?
ndda274eb6f9.x: The compulsory taxes were Bali, a tribute; Bhaga, the king’s share; and Shulka, customs or tolls.
ndda274eb6f9.tq: Match the tax names with the Later Vedic revenue context rather than later fiscal terminology.
xs: The compulsory taxes were **Bali, Bhaga and Shulka** — option **(4)**.
**Bali** = tribute; **Bhaga** = king's share (**1/6**); **Shulka** = customs/tolls.
**Rajasuya** is a sacrifice and **Samiti, Vidatha** are assemblies — not taxes.
xa: **Vaishyas** were the tribute-payers.
Collector = **Bhagadugha**.

n584830e876d.s: The king’s share of agricultural produce, known as Bhaga, was generally:
n584830e876d.x: Bhaga represented the king’s share and was fixed at one-sixth of the produce. Vaishyas were the tribute-payers.
n584830e876d.tq: Remember the fraction attached specifically to the king’s share, not to the other taxes.
xs: **Bhaga** was **one-sixth** (**1/6**) of produce — option **(2)**.
It was the **king's share**, collected by the **Bhagadugha**.
xa: Other compulsory taxes: **Bali** (tribute) and **Shulka** (customs/tolls).
**Vaishyas** paid tribute.
Early Vedic bali was **voluntary**; Later Vedic taxes were **compulsory**.

nindian-history-56-12.s: In Vedic sacrifice, the Adhvaryu was the priest who:
o: Handled the practical, manual work of the sacrifice
Taught the Veda and Vedangas for a living
nindian-history-56-12.x: The Adhvaryu handled the manual work of the sacrifice; the Hotri recited hymns, the Upadhyaya taught and the Suta was the charioteer.
n: Suta was the charioteer. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 130-131]
Suta was associated with the royal court. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 130-131]
Hotri was a Rigvedic priest who recited hymns. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 130-131]
Hota was a Rigvedic priest who recited hymns. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 130-131]
Adhvaryu was the priest responsible for the practical aspects of sacrifice. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 130-131]
Adhvaryu was the priest responsible for the manual aspects of sacrifice. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 130-131]
Upadhyaya was a teacher who taught the Veda as a profession. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 130-131]
Upadhyaya was a teacher who taught the Vedanga as a profession. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 130-131]
xa: ⚠ **Udgatri** = **Samaveda**; **Adhvaryu** = **Yajurveda**.
**Ratnins**: the king's council of **12 functionaries**, honoured in the **Ratnahavimshi** rite of the **Rajasuya**.
**Bhagadugha** = revenue collector; **Sangrahitri** = treasurer; **Palagala** = messenger.

n4b91a499b72.s: The largest number of oxen mentioned for yoking a plough in the Later Vedic evidence is:
n4b91a499b72.x: Ploughs were described as yoked with 6, 8, 12 and even 24 oxen, showing the growing scale of plough agriculture.
xa: **Buffalo** was also used for ploughing.
Iron **ploughshares** came into use.
Agriculture became the **primary** livelihood.

n9d80bc507cc.s: Which one of the following best characterises settlements during the Later Vedic period?
o: Large cities with extensive burnt-brick architecture were common.
Villages with mud and wattle houses predominated, while true towns emerged later.
All settlements were fortified imperial capitals.
Nomadic camps were the only form of settlement.
n9d80bc507cc.x: Settlements were mainly villages with mud and wattle houses. Burnt bricks were not prevalent, and true towns emerged after the Vedic period during the NBPW phase.
n9d80bc507cc.tq: Distinguish the dominant settlement pattern from the later urban phase.
xs: **Villages of mud and wattle houses** predominated; **true towns emerged later** — option **(2)**.
**Burnt bricks were not prevalent**; Hastinapur's mud structures were modest.
xa: True towns came in the **NBPW** phase — "**second urbanisation**": Shravasti, Kausambi, Hastinapur.
BHU's **Rajghat** finds date **Varanasi's urban origins to about 800 BCE**.

n844fffb470e.s: In the Later Vedic context, the term ‘Shresthins’ refers to:
n844fffb470e.x: Shresthins point to merchant groups. Nishka functioned as a unit of value, while barter continued as the main form of exchange.
n844fffb470e.tq: Use the occupational context to distinguish merchant groups from administrative and religious groups.
xs: **Shresthins** = **groups of merchants** — option **(1)**.
They point to growing trade, though **barter** was still the main mode.
xa: **Nishka** = unit of value.
**Ox-drawn wagons** carried goods.
True towns came only in the **NBPW** phase.

n6b4503250c3.s: Which god became supreme in the Later Vedic period?
n6b4503250c3.x: In the Later Vedic period Indra and Agni lost prominence and Prajapati became supreme.
xa: **Pushan** became the god of the **Shudras**.
**Vishnu** was a **minor god** in the Rigveda before his rise.

na0047a7f9c5.s: The Upanishadic thinkers criticised which tendency of Later Vedic religion?
na0047a7f9c5.x: Later Vedic worship became centred on elaborate rituals, which prompted the Upanishadic critique.
xa: The Upanishads (**c. 800-600 BCE**) dealt with **Atman, Brahman, Karma, Moksha**.
**Prajapati** became the supreme god.

n4b6b12e3d87.s: The term ‘Ratnins’ in the Later Vedic polity referred to:
o: A body of twelve military commanders
A council of twelve royal functionaries
A group of twelve provincial governors
A group of twelve village assemblies
n4b6b12e3d87.x: The Ratnins, or ‘jewels’, were the king’s council of twelve functionaries. They were honoured during the Ratnahavimshi rite of the Rajasuya.
n4b6b12e3d87.tq: Directly identify the institutional meaning of an important technical term.
xs: **Ratnins** ("jewels") were the king's **council of twelve functionaries** — option **(2)**.
They were honoured in the **Ratnahavimshi** rite of the **Rajasuya**.
xa: List: purohita, rajan, mahisi, senani, **bhagadugha**, **sangrahitri**, suta, kshata, govikartana, gramani, **parivakti**, akshavapa.
Some lists add **palagala** (messenger).

nf0a1a0a3b89.s: The Ratnins were honoured in which rite associated with the Rajasuya sacrifice?
nf0a1a0a3b89.x: The Ratnahavimshi rite involved offerings at the houses of the Ratnins and honoured the king’s twelve functionaries.
nf0a1a0a3b89.tq: Use the sacrifice–rite association to distinguish closely related Vedic rituals.
xs: The Ratnins were honoured in the **Ratnahavimshi** rite — option **(1)**.
It is part of the **Rajasuya** sacrifice.
xa: The ratnins were **12** royal functionaries.
**Bhagadugha** = revenue collector; **Sangrahitri** = treasurer.

nb595070fcc9.s: In contrast to tribe-based Early Vedic society, Later Vedic society became:
o: Urban and based on coined money
Territory-based with agriculture and compulsory taxes
nb595070fcc9.x: The Early Vedic phase meant tribe, cattle and voluntary bali; the Later Vedic phase meant territory, agriculture and compulsory taxes.
xa: Later Vedic crops: rice (**vrihi**) and **wheat**.
Compulsory taxes: **Bali, Bhaga** (**1/6**), **Shulka**.
Collector = **Bhagadugha**.

n28b284eec78.s: The Later Vedic transition from tribal chiefdom to hereditary territorial monarchy primarily prepared the way for the emergence of which political formations in the 6th century BCE?
n28b284eec78.x: The shift to hereditary territorial monarchy during the Later Vedic period prepared the political ground for the rise of the Mahajanapadas in the 6th century BCE.
n28b284eec78.tq: Directly connect the major political transition with its historical consequence.
xs: The shift to **hereditary territorial monarchy** prepared the way for the **Mahajanapadas** of the **6th century BCE** — option **(3)**.
**Kosala, Kashi, Videha** rose in the east, leading to the Mahajanapadas.
xa: Shift: **jana** → **janapada**.
**Kuru-Panchala** dominated the upper Ganga valley.

n7d256d0ce9f.s: Which term referring to territory appears for the first time in the Later Vedic political context?
n7d256d0ce9f.x: The term rashtra, meaning territory, first appears in this political context and reflects the rise of territorial kingship.
n7d256d0ce9f.tq: Test the exact political term rather than a general synonym for settlement.
xs: The word **rashtra** (territory/state) first appears — option **(2)**.
It marks the rise of **territorial kingship**.
xa: Shift: **jana** (tribe) → **janapada** (territorial kingdom).
Regions were **named after the tribes** that first settled there.
**Ekarat** = "sole ruler" (Aitareya Brahmana).

n74a243e98b3.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the state forms named in the Aitareya Brahmana?
n74a243e98b3.x: The Aitareya Brahmana names Rajya, Bhojya, Swarajya, Vairajya and Samrajya. Ganatantra is not included in this list.
n74a243e98b3.tq: Compare the option directly against the complete named list and avoid importing a later political term.
xs: **Ganatantra** is not in the Aitareya list — option **(4)**.
The forms are **Rajya, Bhojya, Swarajya, Vairajya, Samrajya**, by region.
xa: ⚠ East = **Samrat**; North = **Virat**; West = **Svarat**; South = **Bhoja**.
Middle country = **Raja** (hereditary Kshatriya).
**Ekarat** = sole/paramount ruler.

n06bec5f7117.s: In the Later Vedic period, royal succession usually favoured:
n06bec5f7117.x: Later Vedic kingship became generally hereditary, with succession usually favouring the eldest son, though traces of election continued.
xa: The king came from the **Kshatriya** varna.
Early Vedic = **elective chief**; Later Vedic = **hereditary king**.

n0c2beb42b76.s: Which Vedic assembly disappeared in the Later Vedic period?
n0c2beb42b76.x: The Vidatha disappeared, while the Sabha and Samiti continued under the control of chiefs and wealthy nobles.
xa: **Women were excluded** from assemblies.
**Village assemblies** handled local cases.
Early Vedic = **strong assemblies**; Later Vedic = assemblies in decline.

n325a799a64a.s: Which of the following belongs to the Later Vedic polity rather than the Early Vedic polity?
n325a799a64a.x: Ratnins were part of the Later Vedic polity; an elective chief, voluntary bali and strong assemblies marked the Early Vedic polity.
xa: **Vidatha disappeared** in the Later Vedic period.
Ratnins were honoured in the **Ratnahavimshi** rite.

nddae75f5e49.s: In Later Vedic texts, the ruler of the eastern region was called:
nddae75f5e49.x: The eastern ruler was Samrat, the southern Bhoja, the western Svarat and the northern Virat.
xa: Forms: **samrajya**, **bhojya**, **swarajya**, **vairajya** (with **Rajya**).
Middle country = **Raja**.
Source: **Aitareya Brahmana**.

nc7a1888d767.s: Which Later Vedic royal ritual included a chariot race in which the king defeats his kinsmen?
nc7a1888d767.x: The Vajapeya included the chariot race; the Rajasuya was a consecration and the Ashvamedha a horse sacrifice asserting supremacy.
xa: **Punarabhisheka** = re-consecration of the king.
Rajasuya includes **Ratnahavimshi** (offerings at the ratnins' houses).

n829b972fc29.s: According to the Aitareya Brahmana, kingship originated when:
o: The villages appointed a ruler to supervise agriculture
The gods, losing to the Asuras, chose a king to lead them
The Asuras selected a king to defeat the gods
The Brahmanas elected a king to collect customs duties
n829b972fc29.x: The Aitareya Brahmana gives an early account in which the gods, suffering defeat at the hands of the Asuras, selected a king as their war leader. This linked kingship with the need for military leadership and divine sanction.
n829b972fc29.tq: Identify the correct actor, crisis and institutional response in a traditional origin narrative.
xs: In the **Aitareya Brahmana**, **the gods, losing to the Asuras, chose a king to lead them** — option **(2)**.
It is the **earliest account** of the origin of kingship — need for a **war leader**.
xa: Kingship was later backed by **divine sanction**.
The Aitareya calls the king the **protector of Brahmins**.
The **Shatapatha Brahmana** links the king to **Prajapati**.

n6ffd485e399.s: Which Brahmana regarded the king as a protector of Brahmins?
n6ffd485e399.x: The Aitareya Brahmana regarded the king as protector of Brahmins; Brahmanical ritual monopoly supported royal legitimacy.
xa: Kingship arose from the need for a **war leader**.
**Shatapatha** links the king to **Prajapati**.

n67069b045b9.s: The performance of large Shrauta sacrifices strengthened the power of the Brahmanas mainly because such sacrifices:
o: Transferred all military authority to village assemblies
Required many priests and involved heavy dakshina
n67069b045b9.x: Large Shrauta sacrifices required numerous priests and substantial dakshina, thereby increasing Brahmanical influence and strengthening the ritual basis of royal power.
n67069b045b9.tq: Link the institutional requirement of a ritual to its political consequence.
xs: Large **Shrauta** sacrifices **required many priests and heavy dakshina** — option **(3)**.
This raised the power of the **Brahmanas** and **reinforced royal power**.
xa: The **Brahmanas' ritual monopoly** supported royal legitimacy.
**Rajasuya, Ashvamedha, Vajapeya** were the major royal sacrifices.

nfa68effa0d7.s: Which development contributed to the emergence of the Mahajanapadas?
o: The exclusive expansion of Kuru power into the Deccan
The rise of Kosala, Kashi and Videha in the east after Kuru–Panchala dominance in the upper Ganga valley
The replacement of agriculture by maritime trade in North India
The disappearance of all territorial kingdoms in favour of tribal units
nfa68effa0d7.x: The Kuru–Panchala alliance dominated the upper Ganga valley, while Kosala, Kashi and Videha rose in the east. This political development contributed to the emergence of the Mahajanapadas.
nfa68effa0d7.tq: Connect regional political change with the larger process of state formation.
xs: The **rise of Kosala, Kashi and Videha in the east** after **Kuru–Panchala** dominance led towards the Mahajanapadas — option **(2)**.
Kuru-Panchala held the **upper Ganga valley** through marriage and military links.
xa: The shift to **hereditary territorial monarchy** prepared the way for the **Mahajanapadas** of the **6th century BCE**.
**Videha** lay beyond the **Sadanira/Gandak**.

n1149aebbe4f.s: According to the Aitareya Brahmana, the Shudra was described as
n1149aebbe4f.x: The Aitareya Brahmana described the Shudra as ‘a servant of another’ and stated that he could be expelled or struck at will.
n1149aebbe4f.tq: Link the source text with its distinctive description of social status.
xs: The **Aitareya Brahmana** calls the Shudra "**a servant of another**" — option **(3)**.
He could be **expelled** and beaten/slain at will.
The **tribute payer** in the same text is the **Vaishya**.
xa: Shudras had **no Upanayana**, no right to study the Vedas.
Discrimination existed against **Shudras and Chandalas**.
The Aitareya also calls the daughter a **source of misery**.

n10e68d81acf.s: Which of the following occupations were associated with the Vaishyas in Later Vedic society?
n10e68d81acf.x: Vaishyas engaged in farming, trade and craft production and paid tribute.
n10e68d81acf.tq: Use the occupational cluster rather than selecting a single profession.
xs: **Vaishyas** were **farmers, traders and artisans** — option **(1)**.
They were also **cattle-rearers** and the **tribute payers**.
Warriors/kings = **Kshatriyas**; priests/teachers = **Brahmanas**.
xa: Vaishyas formed **guild-like bodies (gana)** headed by a **shreshthin**.
Vaishyas were **dvija** — entitled to upanayana (metre **Jagati**).

nc0b15b72567.s: In Later Vedic sacrifice, which priest chanted the Samaveda?
nc0b15b72567.x: The Udgatri chanted the Samaveda; the Hotri recited the Rigveda and the Adhvaryu performed sacrificial acts.
xa: **Acharya** taught the whole Veda **not for a fee**.
**Purohita** = family/royal priest and a **ratnin**.

ne436d794760.s: The term ‘Dvija’ in the context of later Vedic society referred to
o: the three upper varnas entitled to the Upanayana rite
ne436d794760.x: Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas were collectively called Dvija, or twice-born, because of their entitlement to Upanayana.
ne436d794760.tq: Distinguish the collective ritual category from the individual varnas.
xs: **Dvija** = **the three upper varnas entitled to the Upanayana** — option **(1)**.
Dvija means **twice-born**; second birth comes through **upanayana**.
**Shudras** and **women** were excluded from upanayana.
xa: Upanayana metres: **Gayatri** (Brahmana), **Trishtubh** (Kshatriya), **Jagati** (Vaishya).
Education (gurukula) was confined largely to the **Dvija**.
**Vratyas and Nishadas** stood outside the varna order.

n39e457cf9c5.s: The proliferation of jatis is a feature of which period?
n39e457cf9c5.x: The proliferation of jatis was post-Vedic, including Gupta-era diversification; the later Vedic period saw birth-based occupation and rigid hierarchy.
xa: Jati growth: **Gupta-era** diversification; **post-Satavahana** mixed castes in Andhra.
Exam angle: varna **rigidified after the Rig Vedic phase**.
Rig Vedic society was relatively **fluid and egalitarian**.

ne206d35ce38.s: The first reference to money-lending in the Vedic literature is found in the
ne206d35ce38.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana contains the first reference to money-lending.
ne206d35ce38.tq: Match the economic practice with the specific textual source.
xs: The **Shatapatha Brahmana** has the **first reference to money-lending** — option **(4)**.
It also gives the **elaborate description of Upanayana**.
**Chhandogya** = earliest reference to the first three ashramas; **Aitareya** = Shudra as servant of another.
xa: The Shatapatha says the "**wife is half her husband** and completes him".
Guild-like Vaishya bodies (**gana**) appear in later Vedic texts.

n34f9f32af9c.s: Which of the following groups stood outside the formal four-varna order?
n34f9f32af9c.x: Vratyas and Nishadas were groups placed outside the formal four-varna order.
n34f9f32af9c.tq: Separate excluded groups from the four recognised varnas.
xs: **Vratyas and Nishadas** stood **outside the varna order** — option **(2)**.
**Brahmanas, Kshatriyas (Rajanyas), Vaishyas, Shudras** are the four varnas themselves.
xa: **Rathakaras** kept the **sacred-thread** privilege.
Discrimination targeted **Shudras and Chandalas**.
The **Chhandogya Upanishad** names the Chandala a despised birth.

n6778383b1e7.s: Untouchability as a formal rule is associated with the:
n6778383b1e7.x: Later Vedic society discriminated against Shudras and Chandalas, but formal untouchability belongs to the post-Vedic Dharmasutras.
xa: The **Chhandogya Upanishad** calls the Chandala a despised birth.
The Aitareya: Shudra could be **expelled** and **struck at will**.
Satavahana Andhra: **anuloma** offspring = **Ugra**; **pratiloma** = **Chandala**.

n4b622900ae1.s: Which ashrama was added later and was not well established in the Later Vedic period?
n4b622900ae1.x: Only Brahmacharya, Grihastha and Vanaprastha were prevalent in Later Vedic times; Sannyasa was added later.
xa: ⚠ **3 – 4** ashramas = **Chhandogya – Jabala**.
All four are fully listed in **post-Vedic** texts.
Varna + ashrama = **Varnashrama dharma**.

n6fdfd6c561b.s: The earliest reference to the first three ashramas is found in the:
n6fdfd6c561b.x: The Chhandogya Upanishad first refers to the first three ashramas; all four are first listed in the Jabala Upanishad.
xa: ⚠ **3 – 4** ashramas = **Chhandogya – Jabala**.
**Sannyasa** was **added later**; only the **first three** were prevalent in Later Vedic times.
The **Grihastha** performs the **Pancha Mahayajnas** (MPPSC **2025**).

n1b3a702e5cb.s: In the Later Vedic period, women lost the right of ____, the initiation ceremony.
n1b3a702e5cb.x: The status of women declined through loss of Upanayana, restricted education and exclusion from religious and public activities.
xa: References to **sati** and **child marriage** appear.
Exceptions: **Gargi** and **Maitreyi**.
In Rig Vedic times women attended the **Sabha**; the **Atharva Veda** mentions women in the **Samiti**.

nae3363ad9d4.s: In the Later Vedic period, varna increasingly came to be based on:
nae3363ad9d4.x: Varna became increasingly birth-based in the Later Vedic period, and gotra exogamy became important.
xa: Rig Vedic society was **relatively fluid and egalitarian**.
**Harappan** society had differentiation but **no textual caste**.
In Rig Vedic times women attended the **Sabha**.

n05d6aafc6d0.s: In Satavahana Andhra, the offspring of an anuloma union and a pratiloma union were respectively known as:
n05d6aafc6d0.x: Anuloma offspring were called Ugra, whereas pratiloma offspring were called Chandala. The other pairs refer either to teachers and priests or reverse these two designations.
n05d6aafc6d0.tq: Discriminate between two easily reversed social classifications by fixing their exact order.
xs: In Satavahana Andhra, **anuloma** offspring = **Ugra** and **pratiloma** offspring = **Chandala** — option **(3)**.
Option 2 reverses them; **Acharya/Upadhyaya** are teachers and **Purohita/Adhvaryu** priests.
xa: **Anuloma** = higher-varna man with lower-varna woman (tolerated).
The **Chhandogya Upanishad** names the Chandala a **despised birth**.
Post-Satavahana (**Ikshvaku**) society saw **mixed castes and sub-castes**.

nf8564dc47c1.s: Which Satavahana ruler claimed to have protected varnashrama dharma?
nf8564dc47c1.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni claimed to have protected varnashrama dharma.
xa: Jati proliferation is **post-Vedic** (Gupta-era diversification).
**Anuloma** offspring = **Ugra**; **pratiloma** = **Chandala**.

nd39d095a77d.s: Which ashrama involved gradual withdrawal from worldly life?
nd39d095a77d.x: Vanaprastha was gradual withdrawal; Brahmacharya was Vedic study, Grihastha household life and Sannyasa complete detachment.
xa: The **Grihastha** performs the **Pancha Mahayajnas**.
Sannyasa was **added later**.
Women followed the ashrama chosen by their **husbands**.

n5b8677d24b4.s: Varnashrama Dharma combines the varna system with the:
n5b8677d24b4.x: Varnashrama Dharma denotes the combined framework of varna and Ashrama.
xa: It became the **normative frame** of later Hindu society.
AP angle: **Gautamiputra Satakarni** protected varnashrama dharma and opposed **varna-sankara**.

n74e8b15fdcf.s: The Pancha Mahayajnas were regarded as daily duties primarily of the
n74e8b15fdcf.x: The Pancha Mahayajnas were daily duties of the Grihastha, or householder, Ashrama.
n74e8b15fdcf.tq: Apply the social-role clue: regular family and ritual obligations belong to the householder.
xs: The **Pancha Mahayajnas** were daily duties of the **Grihastha** (householder) — option **(3)**.
Exam: **MPPSC 2025**.
xa: The five: **Brahma** (Vedic study), **Deva** (gods), **Pitri** (ancestors), **Bhuta** (living beings), **Nri/Manushya** (guests).
Grihastha duties: **marriage, family, economic** duties.

na1b677750e7.x: Gotra literally means cow-pen; as an institution of descent from a common male ancestor it was established in Later Vedic times.
xa: Rule: **gotra exogamy** — no marriage within the same gotra.
Plus caste endogamy and **sapinda** prohibition ("sasan" rule).

n0d3b2ea2cba.s: Who analysed sapinda and gotra rules and divided India into four kinship zones in the work titled Kinship Organization in India?
n0d3b2ea2cba.x: Irawati Karve analysed sapinda and gotra rules and divided India into four kinship zones in Kinship Organization in India, published in 1953.
n0d3b2ea2cba.tq: Use the author–work association as the deciding clue.
xs: **Irawati Karve** wrote **Kinship Organization in India** (**1953**) — option **(3)**.
She analysed **sapinda and gotra** rules and divided India into **four kinship zones**.
**Gargi** and **Maitreyi** were Upanishadic women philosophers.
xa: **Gotra exogamy** + caste endogamy + **sapinda** prohibition = North Indian pattern.
⚠ **Kosa** (treasury) is not a kinship term.

n348d2807c14.s: The number of samskaras (shodasha samskaras) traditionally recognised in Hindu tradition is
n348d2807c14.x: The traditional total number of samskaras is sixteen.
n348d2807c14.tq: Recall the exact numerical value from the ritual classification.
xs: There are **16** samskaras (**shodasha samskaras**) — option **(3)** (**MPPSC 2015**).
They run from **Garbhadhana** (conception) to **Antyeshti** (funeral).
xa: Key ones: **Upanayana** and **Vivaha**.
**Pumsavana** = to procure a male child.
n348d2807c14.fixed: stem 'in this context' has no referent

n453e1c110b7.s: References to which of the following practices appear in accounts of the declining status of women in Later Vedic society?
o: Compulsory female military service and polyandry
Abolition of marriage and communal ownership
Female kingship and universal widow remarriage
n453e1c110b7.x: References to child marriage and sati appear in accounts of the declining status of women in Later Vedic society.
n453e1c110b7.tq: Select the pair of practices directly associated with the stated social trend.
xs: References to **child marriage and sati** appear as women's status declined — option **(2)**.
Women **lost Upanayana**, had **restricted education** and were **excluded from rites and assemblies**.
xa: The **Aitareya Brahmana** calls the daughter a **source of misery**.
The **Maitrayani Samhita** names **liquor, dice and women** as three evils.
Exceptions: **Gargi** debated **Yajnavalkya**; **Maitreyi** was his wife.

nf73906f31cb.s: In the Arsha form of marriage, the groom gave the bride's father:
nf73906f31cb.x: In the Arsha form, the groom gave a token cow and bull to the bride's father.
xa: Arsha is an **approved** form.
⚠ **Asura** = purchase; **Rakshasa** = capture; **Paishacha** = lowest.

n77139d7a125.s: Which one of the following was regarded as the lowest form of marriage in the Dharmashastra classification?
n77139d7a125.x: Paishacha, involving the seduction of a sleeping or intoxicated girl, was regarded as the lowest form of marriage.
n77139d7a125.tq: Use the evaluative description to identify the exceptional form.
xs: **Paishacha** — seduction of a sleeping, intoxicated or incapacitated girl — is the **lowest form** — option **(3)**.
**Daiva, Prajapatya, Arsha** are **approved** forms.
xa: Disapproved forms: **Asura, Gandharva, Rakshasa, Paishacha**.
**Brahma** form: father gives daughter with gifts to a learned man.

nab777c7a3f3.s: Payment of a bride price characterised which form of marriage?
nab777c7a3f3.x: Bride price characterised Asura marriage; Gandharva marriage was based on mutual consent.
xa: **Prajapatya**: given without dowry, the couple told to perform **dharma together**.
**8 forms** in both **Manu** and **Kautilya**.

n9907d352569.s: The elaborate description of the Upanayana ceremony is found in the
n9907d352569.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana gives an elaborate description of the Upanayana ceremony.
n9907d352569.tq: Use the text–ritual association and avoid swapping closely related Vedic works.
xs: The elaborate Upanayana description is in the **Shatapatha Brahmana** — option **(4)**.
**Chhandogya** = three ashramas; **Brihadaranyaka** = Gargi's debate; **Aitareya** = Shudra as servant.
xa: Metres: **Gayatri – Trishtubh – Jagati** = **Brahmana – Kshatriya – Vaishya**.
The Shatapatha also has the **first reference to money-lending**.

ne8286a35eb8.s: Gargi's debate with Yajnavalkya is recorded in the:
ne8286a35eb8.x: The Brihadaranyaka Upanishad records Gargi's debate with Yajnavalkya.
xa: ⚠ **Aitareya** = daughter a misery; **Shatapatha** = wife is half her husband.
**Maitreyi** was **Yajnavalkya's wife**.

n8897b293431.s: Which one of the following is the odd one out in relation to ancient Indian kinship terminology?
n8897b293431.x: Kula, Vamsha and Gotra are kinship terms, whereas Kosa means treasury.
n8897b293431.tq: Identify the term that belongs to a different conceptual group.
xs: **Kosa** is the odd one out — it means **treasury** — option **(1)** (**UPSC 1996**).
**Kula** = family; **Vamsha** = lineage/dynasty; **Gotra** = exogamous clan.
xa: Gotra literally means **cow-pen**.
**Irawati Karve** analysed kinship in *Kinship Organization in India* (**1953**).
**Gotra exogamy** = no marriage within the same gotra.

n39b126d80fb.x: Gotra exogamy prohibited marriage within the same gotra, operating alongside caste endogamy and sapinda restrictions.
xa: **Irawati Karve** analysed **sapinda + gotra** rules.
Gotra as an institution was established in **Later Vedic** times.

nindian-history-22-13.s: In the varna order, priestly functions belonged to the:
nindian-history-22-13.x: Priestly duties belonged to the Brahmanas; Kshatriyas were warriors and rulers, Vaishyas farmed and traded, and Shudras did manual work.
n: Brahmana is associated with priestly and religious functions. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Kshatriya is associated with warrior and ruling functions. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Vaishya is associated with agriculture, cattle-rearing, and trade. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Shudra is associated with servile and manual occupations. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
xa: Vaishyas were the **tribute payers**.
The upper three varnas were **dvija** (twice-born, via upanayana).
⚠ **Jati** (birth-based groups) is **distinct** from **Varna**.

n205ef270617.s: In the gurukula system of education, the pupil generally
o: lived separately from the teacher and studied independently
received instruction only from guild heads
n205ef270617.x: In the gurukula system, pupils lived with the guru. Education was confined largely to the Dvija communities.
n205ef270617.tq: Test the defining institutional feature of the education system.
xs: In the **gurukula** the pupil **lived with the guru** — option **(1)**.
Education was confined largely to the **Dvija**.
xa: **Brahmacharya** = student stage — Vedic study under a guru.
**Acharya** initiated the pupil and taught **not for a fee**.

o: The first three Vedas excluding the Atharvaveda
The three divisions of the Yajurveda
All four Vedas including the Atharvaveda
n29c117c62c9.x: Trayi denotes the first three Vedas—Rigveda, Samaveda and Yajurveda. Atharvaveda was initially excluded from this grouping.
n29c117c62c9.tq: Discriminate between the three-Veda grouping and the complete four-Veda classification.
xs: **Trayi** = **the first three Vedas, excluding the Atharvaveda** — option **(1)**.
The **Atharvaveda** was **first excluded** from Trayi.
xa: Atharvaveda = **latest Veda** — spells, charms, healing.
All Vedic texts are **Shruti** ("heard"), called **apaurusheya**.

n5ef344afbe3.s: The expression ‘Kshetra-patni’, meaning ‘mistress of the field’, is found in the:
n5ef344afbe3.x: The expression Kshetra-patni originates in the Atharvaveda.
n5ef344afbe3.tq: Use the exact technical term as a source-identification clue.
xs: **Kshetra-patni** ("mistress of the field") originates in the **Atharvaveda** — option **(3)** (**UPSC 2026** key).
The **Atharvaveda** is the **latest Veda**, rich in folk practice — not the Rig, Sama or Yajur.
xa: It deals with **spells, charms, healing** and folk beliefs.
It has **731 hymns** in **20 kandas**.
Recensions: **Paippalada, Shaunaka**.

n7bc8e62ee74.s: Which Veda borrows almost all of its verses from the Rigveda?
o: None of the Vedas borrows from the Rigveda
n7bc8e62ee74.x: The Samaveda borrows almost all its verses from the Rigveda (about 1,549 verses, all but about 75 from the Rigveda), setting them to melody. The Yajurveda is a ritual prose manual and the Atharvaveda a collection of spells and charms; option D is false.
xs: The **Samaveda** borrows almost all its verses from the Rigveda — option **(3)**.
~**1,549** verses, all but **75** from the Rigveda (some notes: all but **99**).
The **Yajurveda** is a ritual prose manual; the **Atharvaveda** has spells and charms.
xa: Samaveda = root of **Indian music**; priest = **Udgatri**.
Its Brahmanas: **Panchavimsha (Tandya), Jaiminiya**.

n8baf9157dc8.s: Which branch of the Yajurveda contains mantras only?
n8baf9157dc8.x: The Shukla (White) Yajurveda contains mantras only, while the Krishna (Black) Yajurveda mixes mantras with prose.
xa: Exam: **UKPSC 2025**.
Shukla: **Vajasaneyi** Samhita, **Shatapatha** Brahmana.
Krishna: **Taittiriya**, Maitrayani, Kathaka, Kapishthala Samhitas.

n9b68df1091c.s: Veda Vyasa, also known as Krishna Dvaipayana, is traditionally associated with which of the following?
o: Compilation and classification of the Vedas
n9b68df1091c.x: Veda Vyasa, or Krishna Dvaipayana, is traditionally remembered as the person who classified the Vedas.
n9b68df1091c.tq: Use the person–work association and eliminate authors of other grammatical and Buddhist texts.
xs: **Veda Vyasa (Krishna Dvaipayana)** is recalled as the **classifier of the Vedas** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Ashtadhyayi** is by **Panini**; the **Mahabhashya** is by **Patanjali**.
Vyasa is also the traditional author of the **Mahabharata**.
xa: A **Vijayawada** discourse in **Mar 2026** recalled Vyasa as classifier of the Vedas.
The four Vedas: **Rig** (hymns), **Sama** (melody), **Yajur** (ritual formulas), **Atharva** (spells, charms).
⚠ Priests: **Hotri – Udgatri – Adhvaryu – Brahman** = **Rig – Sama – Yajur – Atharva**.

na5e0c446c1c.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the latest among the four Vedas?
na5e0c446c1c.x: Among the four Vedas, the Atharvaveda is regarded as the latest composition. The Rigveda is regarded as the oldest.
na5e0c446c1c.tq: Use the first/last contrast to distinguish the latest Veda from the oldest one.
xs: The **Atharvaveda** is the **latest** of the four Vedas — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Rigveda** is the **oldest** — the "First Testament of Mankind".
The **Samaveda** borrows almost all its verses from the Rigveda; the **Yajurveda** is a ritual manual.
xa: **Trayi** = the first three Vedas; the Atharvaveda was at first **excluded** from it.
The Atharvaveda has **731 hymns, 20 kandas**, and mentions **Pashupati**.
It calls the **Sabha** and **Samiti** daughters of **Prajapati**; the term **kshetra-patni** originates in it.

nindian-history-53-12.s: What is the literal meaning of Vedanta?
nindian-history-53-12.x: Vedanta literally means the end of the Vedas, Veda plus anta, since the Upanishads come at the close of Vedic literature and mark its climax.
nindian-history-53-12.tq: Split the word into its parts.
n: Vedanta means the end of the Vedas or the climax of Vedic ideology. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 127-128]
xs: **Vedanta** literally means the **End of the Vedas** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is the **climax** of **Vedic ideology**; the **Upanishads** are also called **Vedanta**.
xa: Foundations of Vedanta: **Prasthanatrayi** — **Upanishads**, **Brahma Sutra**, **Bhagavad Gita**.
Upanishads were composed c. **800-600 BCE**; teaching: **Atman = Brahman**, **Karma**, **Moksha**.
Upanishads = **Shruti**; Puranas = **Smriti**.

n2ad35031702.s: Which Mandala of the Rigveda is devoted to Soma hymns?
n2ad35031702.x: Mandala IX is the Soma Mandala; VI is linked with Bharadvaja, VII with Vasishtha and X with the Purusha Sukta.
xa: ⚠ **III – VII – IX – X** = **Gayatri – Ten Kings – Soma – Purusha/Nasadiya**.
Mandala II seer = **Gritsamada**.

n21ef3df83d9.s: The Gayatri Mantra is traditionally associated with which of the following?
n21ef3df83d9.x: The Gayatri Mantra is associated with the sage Vishvamitra and the deity Savitri.
n21ef3df83d9.tq: Match the mantra with both its associated sage and deity.
xs: The **Gayatri Mantra** is by **Vishvamitra** to **Savitri** — option **(2)**.
It is in the **Third Mandala**.
**Vasishtha** is tied to Mandala VII and **Bharadvaja** to Mandala VI.
xa: Family-book seers: **Gritsamada, Vishvamitra, Vamadeva, Atri, Bharadvaja, Vasishtha**.
AP angle: in the **Sunahshepa** story, **Vishvamitra** cursed his **50 sons** to become non-Aryan peoples, including the **Andhras**.

nd3604e48b4f.s: The Gayatri Mantra occurs in which Mandala of the Rigveda?
nd3604e48b4f.x: The Gayatri Mantra is in the Third Mandala; the Seventh has the Battle of Ten Kings and the Ninth the Soma Pavamana hymns.
xa: Mandala X also mentions **Ganga**, **Rajanya**, **Shudra**.
**Nasadiya Sukta** = the creation hymn.

n721fd667ebd.s: The Vaisheshika school of philosophy is associated with:
n721fd667ebd.x: Vaisheshika is associated with Kanada; Nyaya with Gautama, Sankhya with Kapila and Purva Mimamsa with Jaimini.
xa: **Yoga** = **Patanjali**; **Uttara Mimamsa** = **Badarayana**.
Patanjali also wrote the **Mahabhashya**.

ndbff9268325.s: The Mahabharata is also known as the:
ndbff9268325.x: The Mahabharata is also called the Jaya Samhita and Satasahasri Samhita; the Harivamsa is appended to it.
xa: The Mahabharata was compiled between the **10th century BC** and the **4th century AD**.
The **Ramayana** (Valmiki) has **24,000 verses**, composed in **five stages** from the 5th century BC.
In the Mahabharata the **Andhras** sided with the **Kauravas** at Kurukshetra.

nindian-history-53-8.s: The Prasthanatrayi consists of the Upanishads, the Brahma Sutra and the:
nindian-history-53-8.x: The Prasthanatrayi - the Upanishads, Brahma Sutra and Bhagavad Gita - forms the foundation of Vedanta.
n: Prasthanatrayi forms the foundations of Vedanta. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 127-128]
Prasthanatrayi consists of the Upanishads, Brahma Sutra, and Bhagavad Gita. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 127-128]
Vedanta consists of the Upanishads, Brahma Sutra, and Bhagavad Gita. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 127-128]
xa: The **Prime Prasthan** is the **Upanishads**.

n4ee9f6c2f35.s: Vedic texts, regarded as 'heard', are classed as:

n650bbaaddc9.s: The Ashtadhyayi, the classic work on Sanskrit grammar, was composed by:

nindian-history-53-15.s: Patanjali set out Yoga as a compact philosophical system in the:

nafc37e3849f.s: How many hymns does the Rigveda contain?

n63250873c5c.s: Which Ikshvaku ruler performed the Ashvamedha, Rajasuya, Vajapeya and Agnistoma sacrifices, with an Ashvamedha altar found at Nagarjunakonda?

The six orthodox systems include Vedanta. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Lokayata is not among the six orthodox systems. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Kapalika is not among the six orthodox systems. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xa: **Samkhya is the oldest** of the six (APPSC-GS **2018**).
Pairs: **Nyaya-Vaisheshika**, **Samkhya-Yoga**, **Mimamsa-Vedanta**.
**Nastika** schools reject the Vedas: **Charvaka, Buddhism, Jainism, Ajivika**.

nindian-history-51-5.s: In Mimamsa philosophy, which terms respectively refer to Purva and Uttara divisions?
nindian-history-51-5.x: Purva Mimamsa deals with Karmakanda, the ritual portion of the Vedas, and Uttara Mimamsa (Vedanta) deals with Jnanakanda, the knowledge portion. Option C reverses the pair.
nindian-history-51-5.tq: Watch the order of the pair.
n: Mimamsa is a Vedic philosophy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Purva Mimamsa is associated with Karmakanda. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Uttara Mimamsa is associated with Jnanakanda. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xs: **Karmakanda** (Purva) and **Jnanakanda** (Uttara) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Purva Mimamsa** goes with **Karmakanda**; **Uttara Mimamsa** with **Jnanakanda**.
**Yama** and **Niyama** are limbs of **Yoga**; **Satkaryavada** belongs to **Samkhya**.
xa: **Apurva** in **Mimamsa** is the **unseen force** **linking karma** with its **result**.
Purva Mimamsa founder: **Jaimini** (**Mimamsa Sutras**); Uttara Mimamsa: **Badarayana**.
⚠ **Kumarila Bhatta** = Purva Mimamsa, not Vedanta.

nindian-history-51-40.s: Who is identified as the earliest exponent of Sankhya and associated with Satkaryavada?
nindian-history-51-40.x: Kapila is the earliest teacher of Sankhya, whose Satkaryavada holds that the effect already exists in its cause. Patanjali is linked with Yoga, Lakulisha with Pashupata and Makkhali Gosala with the Ajivikas.
nindian-history-51-40.tq: Match each school with its founder.
n: Kapila was associated with Sankhya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Kapila was the earliest exponent of Sankhya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Kapila was associated with Satkaryavada. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xs: **Kapila** is the **earliest exponent** of **Sankhya**, associated with **Satkaryavada** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Patanjali** — **Yoga**; **Lakulisha** — **Pashupata**; **Makkhali Gosala** — **Ajivika** (**Niyati**).
xa: **Satkaryavada**: the effect pre-exists in the cause (MPPSC **2025**).
Samkhya: dualism of **Purusha** and **Prakriti**.
⚠ **Kapila – Kanada – Gautama** = **Samkhya – Vaisheshika – Nyaya**.

nf81c23e2aea.s: Which of the following limbs of Ashtanga Yoga belongs to the antaranga (inner) group?
nf81c23e2aea.x: Samadhi is antaranga; yama, niyama, asana, pranayama and pratyahara are the five bahiranga (outer) limbs.
xa: **Antaranga** (inner) = **dharana, dhyana, samadhi**.
Yoga's founder is **Patanjali**, author of the **Yoga Sutras**.
⚠ **Patanjali** also wrote the **Mahabhashya** on Panini.

nindian-history-51-76.s: In Patanjali's Ashtanga Yoga, the fourth limb is:
nindian-history-51-76.x: Yama is the first limb, Niyama the second, Asana the third and Pranayama the fourth.
n: The first limb of Yoga is Yama. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The second limb of Yoga is Niyama. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The third limb of Yoga is Asana. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The fourth limb of Yoga is Pranayama. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xa: Then **Pratyahara** (fifth), **Dharana** (sixth), **Dhyana** (seventh), **Samadhi** (eighth).
**bahiranga** (outer) = yama to pratyahara; **antaranga** (inner) = dharana, dhyana, samadhi.
Yoga's key text: **Yoga Sutras** of **Patanjali**.

n70a338a1cf2.s: Swami Vivekananda's Neo-Vedanta is best understood as a reworking of which philosophical doctrine?
n70a338a1cf2.x: Vivekananda's Neo-Vedanta reworked and presented the Advaita Vedanta tradition in a modern form.
n70a338a1cf2.tq: Discriminate between closely related schools of Indian philosophy by identifying the doctrine directly associated with the reformulation.
xs: **Vivekananda's Neo-Vedanta** reworked **Advaita** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Vaisheshika** (atomism), **Nyaya** (logic) and **Mimamsa** (ritual) are other darshanas.
xa: **Advaita Vedanta** is associated with **Shankaracharya**.
Vedanta (Uttara Mimamsa) was founded by **Badarayana** — **Brahman** the only reality.
Upanishadic concepts are the **base of later Hinduism**.

nindian-history-61-2.x: Pashupata Shaivism was founded by Lakulisha.
n: Bauddha is a Nastika school. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 136-137]
Jain is a Nastika school. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 136-137]
Ajivika is associated with Niyativada or determinism (fate). [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 136-137]
Pashupata is associated with Lakulisha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 136-137]
xa: Astika schools **accept Vedic authority**; Nastika: **Charvaka, Buddhism, Jainism, Ajivika**.
**Niyati** is linked with **Makkhali Gosala**.

nap-history-41-1.s: The Madhyamika school of Buddhism is associated with:
nap-history-41-1.x: Madhyamika is Nagarjuna's school; Syadvada is linked with Kundakundacharya, Dvaita with Madhvacharya and Purva Mimamsa with Kumarila Bhatta.
n: Syadvada was propounded by Kundakundacharya. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 52-53]
Madhyamika, also called Soonya Vaadam, was propounded by Nagarjuna. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 52-53]
Dvaita was propounded by Madhavacharya. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 52-53]
Purva Mimamsa was propounded by Kumarila Bhatta. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 52-53]
xa: Kumarila wrote **Slokavartika** and **Tantravartika** (APPSC G2 **2012**, **2019**).
Kumarila **defended Vedic ritual** and opposed Buddhist doctrines.
**Madhyamika** is also called **Soonya Vaadam**.

n0ba08c08fa2.s: Which was the only Mahajanapada situated south of the Vindhyas?
n0ba08c08fa2.x: Assaka was the only Mahajanapada south of the Vindhyas; eight of the sixteen lay in present-day Uttar Pradesh.
xa: Assaka's capital **Potana/Potali** = **Bodhan** (Nizamabad, Telangana) (APPSC G2 2012).
The sage **Bavari** had his ashram on the Godavari in Assaka (**Suttanipata**).
Assaka lay on the **Dakshinapatha** route.

nd9e5e0231b6.s: The Vatsa Mahajanapada was associated with which river?
nd9e5e0231b6.x: Vatsa lay on the Yamuna; Kosala was linked with the Sarayu, Avanti with the Sipra and Kashi with the Ganga-Varuna confluence.
xa: **Assaka** lay on the **Godavari**; **Surasena** also on the **Yamuna**.
⚠ UPSC 2025: **Asmaka-Godavari, Kosala-Sarayu** correct; **Kamboja-Vipas, Avanti-Mahanadi** wrong.
**Vaishya Tekri** near Ujjain (on the Sipra) is to be re-excavated by MP.

nf00e05cc5a8.s: The capital of the Vatsa Mahajanapada was:
nf00e05cc5a8.x: Vatsa's capital was Kaushambi; Shravasti was Kosala's, Champa Anga's and Ujjain Avanti's.
xa: **Assaka**'s capital = **Bodhan** (APPSC G2 2012).
Avanti's **southern** capital was **Mahishmati**.
Kosala lay on the **Sarayu**; ruled by **Prasenajit (Pasenadi)**.

n90a6876bf8f.s: By which period had Magadha become the most powerful Mahajanapada?
n90a6876bf8f.x: Magadha became the most powerful Mahajanapada during the 6th to 4th centuries BCE.
n90a6876bf8f.tq: Select the correct chronological range rather than a neighbouring period.
xs: Magadha was the most powerful Mahajanapada by the **6th-4th centuries BCE** — so option **(4)** is correct (APPSC 2018).
In this period the four powers were **Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, Avanti**.
xa: Dynasties: **Haryanka** (c. 544-460 BCE), **Shishunaga** (c. 413-345 BCE), **Nanda** (345-321 BCE).
Magadha's rise = **second urbanisation** + first large Indian state.
Heterodox sects rose on the **same economic change**.

na7a85fdfd54.s: The Second Buddhist Council at Vaishali was held during the reign of:
na7a85fdfd54.x: Kalashoka of the Shishunaga dynasty was associated with the Second Buddhist Council at Vaishali.
na7a85fdfd54.tq: Apply the ruler–event association and avoid confusing the two Buddhist councils.
xs: The **Second Buddhist Council** at **Vaishali** was held under **Kalashoka** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Kalashoka was of the **Shishunaga** dynasty (c. **413-345 BCE**).
**Bimbisara** and **Ajatashatru** were **Haryankas**; **Dhana Nanda** was the last Nanda.
xa: **Shishunaga** ended **Avanti's** power.
**Vaishali** was the capital of the **Vajji** confederacy.
Order: **Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya**.

n24f40abcbd7.s: Which Achaemenid ruler annexed Punjab and Sindh around 516 BCE?
n24f40abcbd7.x: Cyrus began the Persian invasions, and Darius I annexed Punjab and Sindh c. 516 BCE.
xa: Impact: spread of the **Kharosthi** script.
Alexander crossed the **Indus** in **326 BCE**.

nea00cee5327.s: Which ruler of Taxila submitted to Alexander?
nea00cee5327.x: Ambhi of Taxila submitted to Alexander, whereas Porus fought him at the Battle of Hydaspes.
xa: Alexander crossed the Indus in **326 BCE** and died at **Babylon** in **323 BCE**.
The army refused to go beyond the **Beas**.

nd5073a18112.s: Potana or Potali, the capital of Assaka, has been identified with:
nd5073a18112.x: Potana or Potali is identified with Bodhan in present-day Nizamabad district of Telangana.
nd5073a18112.tq: Discriminate between the ancient name and its modern Andhra-Telangana identification.
xs: Assaka's capital **Potana/Potali** = **Bodhan in Nizamabad, Telangana** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Rajagriha** was Magadha's capital, **Ujjain** Avanti's, **Taxila** Gandhara's.
xa: Assaka capital = **Bodhan** was asked in **APPSC G2 2012**.
Sage **Bavari** had his ashram on the **Godavari** in Assaka (**Suttanipata**).
Assaka lay on the **Dakshinapatha** route.

n94cd5380774.s: The earliest Andhra-region link in Buddhist texts is associated with:
o: Sage Bavari’s ashram on the Godavari in Assaka
n94cd5380774.x: The Suttanipata refers to sage Bavari’s ashram on the Godavari in Assaka, providing an early Andhra-region link in Buddhist literature.
n94cd5380774.tq: Match the textual reference with the person, place and regional connection.
xs: The **Suttanipata** places **sage Bavari's ashram on the Godavari in Assaka** — option **(1)** is correct.
This is the **earliest Andhra-region link** in Buddhist texts.
xa: Assaka = **only Mahajanapada south of the Vindhyas**.
Its capital **Potana/Potali** = **Bodhan** (Nizamabad).
The first literary mention of the Andhras overall is in the **Aitareya Brahmana**.

nd7a66d3b8c4.s: The re-studied Rajghat artefacts have been used to date the urban origins of Varanasi to approximately:
nd7a66d3b8c4.x: The Rajghat artefacts indicate that Varanasi’s urban origins date to approximately 800 BCE.
nd7a66d3b8c4.tq: Use the archaeological date association and distinguish it from nearby period values.
xs: The Rajghat finds date **Varanasi's urban origins** to c. **800 BCE** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**BHU** opened **22 boxes** of finds from the **1957-69** digs.
xa: **Rajghat** was the capital of the **Kashi** janapada under the **Brahmadatta** dynasty.
Kashi lay at the **Ganga-Varuna** confluence.
Kashi was later annexed by **Kosala**, then taken by **Magadha**.

n5eaf10127f2.s: Before its annexation by Kosala, Kashi was ruled by the:
n5eaf10127f2.x: Kashi, with its capital at Rajghat, was ruled by the Brahmadatta dynasty until Kosala annexed it.
xa: Rajghat finds date Varanasi's urban origins to c. **800 BCE**.
**Bimbisara** got part of **Kashi** as dowry from Kosala.
**Ajatashatru** took Kashi and fought **Prasenajit**.

nindian-history-138-6.s: The Mahajanapada of Anga corresponds to the modern region of:
nindian-history-138-6.x: Anga lay in Bhagalpur and Munger; Kashi was around Varanasi, Koshala in Awadh and Malla in Kushinagar and Deoria.
n: Koshala's modern region was Awadh/Ayodhya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
Malla's modern region included Kushinagar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
Malla's modern region included Deoria. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
Kashi's modern region was Varanasi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
Anga's modern region included Bhagalpur. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
Anga's modern region included Munger. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
xa: **Anga**'s capital was **Champa**; **Kashi**'s was **Varanasi** (Rajghat).
APPSC-G1 **2024**: **Anga-Champa**, **Kosala-Shravasti**.

nindian-history-138-13.s: The capital of the Ashmaka (Assaka) Mahajanapada was:
nindian-history-138-13.x: Ashmaka ruled from Potan/Potali; Gandhara from Taxila, Avanti from Ujjayini and Mahishmati, and Kamboja from Rajpur/Hatak.
n: Ashmaka's capital was Potan/Potali. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
Avanti's northern capital was Ujjayini. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
Avanti's southern capital was Mahishmati. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
Gandhara's capital was Taxila. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
Kamboja's capital was Rajpur/Hatak. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
Ashmaka is also known as Assaka. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
xa: Kamboja was known for **horse-breeding**.
UPSC **2025**: **Kamboja-Vipas** and **Avanti-Mahanadi** were wrong pairs.
**Chanda Pradyota** ruled **Avanti**.

nindian-history-10-3.s: Who shifted the capital of Magadha from Rajagriha to Pataliputra?
nindian-history-10-3.x: Udayin moved the capital of Magadha from Rajagriha to Pataliputra.
n: Magadha had Rajagriha as its capital. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
Magadha later shifted its capital to Pataliputra. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
Udayin shifted the capital of Magadha to Pataliputra. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 51-53]
xa: Order: **Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya**.
**Kalashoka** held the **Second Buddhist Council** at **Vaishali**.
**Bimbisara** treated as founder of the Haryankas (APPSC-GS **2018**).

n1ae03c605bc.s: The Bhagavati Sutra is particularly noted for adding names such as
n1ae03c605bc.x: The Jain Bhagavati Sutra gives a different list and includes eastern and southern names such as Vanga, Malava and Ladha or Radha.
n1ae03c605bc.tq: Recall the distinctive additions in the alternate list rather than the common Mahajanapada names.
xs: The Jain **Bhagavati Sutra** adds **Vanga, Malava** and **Ladha (Radha)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Its list differs from the Buddhist **Anguttara Nikaya** list of the **16 Mahajanapadas**.
xa: The Anguttara Nikaya is part of the **Sutta Pitaka**.
The added names are **eastern and southern** ones.
**Assaka** is the only Mahajanapada of the standard list **south of the Vindhyas**.

nindian-history-138-19.s: Panini's Ashtadhyayi mentions how many Janapadas?
nindian-history-138-19.x: Panini's Ashtadhyayi mentions 22 Janapadas, while the Anguttara Nikaya and Bhagavati Sutra list 16 Mahajanapadas.
n: Anguttara Nikaya gives a list of 16 Mahajanapadas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
Bhagavati Sutra also mentions 16 Mahajanapadas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
Panini's Ashtadhyayi mentions 22 Janapadas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
Ashtadhyayi specifically mentions Magadha among important Janapadas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
Ashtadhyayi specifically mentions Ashmaka among important Janapadas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
Ashtadhyayi specifically mentions Kamboja among important Janapadas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #138 · pp 241-242]
xa: Bhagavati Sutra adds **Vanga**, **Malava**, **Ladha/Radha**.
The Anguttara Nikaya is part of the **Sutta Pitaka**.

n6e4070c6872.x: Gana-sanghas shared power in a clan assembly, while monarchies had a hereditary king.
xa: Gana-sangha weakness: **slow decisions**, factional, open to conquest — **absorbed by Magadha**.
Monarchy weakness: **succession fights**, despotism.
Clan heads met in an assembly hall, the **santhagara**.

ncb5cf1e6202.s: The assembly hall in which the affairs of a gana-sangha were conducted was called the
ncb5cf1e6202.x: Clan chiefs of a gana-sangha met in an assembly hall called the santhagara to conduct public affairs.
ncb5cf1e6202.tq: Test the exact institutional term instead of a generic word for assembly.
xs: The gana-sangha's clan heads met in an assembly hall called the **santhagara** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Power was **shared** among clan heads, unlike a **single hereditary king**.
xa: Gana-sangha revenue came from **contributions from members**.
Strength: **collective wisdom**, checks on tyranny; weakness: **slow decisions**, factional.
Republics: **Vajji, Malla**, and later **Kamboja**.

n14814a8c85f.s: Which of the following Mahajanapadas was a gana-sangha?
n14814a8c85f.x: Vajji, like Malla, was a gana-sangha; not all Mahajanapadas were monarchies.
xa: **Vajji** = confederacy of **8-9 clans** (Lichchhavis, Videhas, Jnatrikas, Vajjis), capital **Vaishali**.
**Malla** = **9 clans**; Kusinara and Pava.
Gana-sanghas were eventually **absorbed by Magadha**.

n57b8ea34752.x: The Buddha attained parinirvana at Kusinara, a Malla centre; Mahavira died at Pava and the Shakyas were linked with Kapilavastu.
xa: ⚠ Both **Kusinara** and **Pava** are **Malla** centres — do not swap them.
**Koliyas** were another clan.
**Malla** had **9 clans**; Malla's region was **Eastern UP**.

ne6b8192a4dc.x: Pukkusati ruled Gandhara, while Bimbisara ruled Magadha, Prasenajit Kosala and Udayana Vatsa.
xa: **Chanda Pradyota** ruled **Avanti** (MPPSC 2019).
**Avantiputra**, a Buddha's disciple, ruled **Surasena**.
"**Contemporary of Buddha**" = **Bimbisara** (APPSC 2018).

n9952b07ffab.s: Udayana, the hero of the Vasavadatta romance, ruled:
n9952b07ffab.x: Udayana ruled Vatsa and married Vasavadatta, daughter of Chanda Pradyota of Avanti; Bhasa's Svapnavasavadatta tells the story.
xa: Vatsa's capital was **Kaushambi**.
**Pradyota** rivalled both **Bimbisara** and **Udayana**.
The four big powers: **Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, Avanti**.

n00022e1abff.s: Chanda Pradyota of Avanti was a rival of:
n00022e1abff.x: Chanda Pradyota of Avanti rivalled Bimbisara of Magadha and Udayana of Vatsa.
xa: Udayana married **Vasavadatta**, Pradyota's daughter (Bhasa's **Svapnavasavadatta**).
Magadha emerged supreme in the **6th-4th c. BCE**.

nea6ed646761.s: Bimbisara received part of ____ as dowry from Kosala.
nea6ed646761.x: Bimbisara's marriage alliance with Kosala brought part of Kashi as dowry; he also allied with the Lichchhavis and Madra.
xa: Anga's **Champa** was the trade port he gained.
Bimbisara ruled **544-492 BCE** (**52 years**).
"Bimbisara's dynasty" = **Haryanka** (APPSC 2025).

nf4174d0a9d1.x: Mahashilakantaka was a catapult; the chariot fitted with a mace was the Rathamusala.
xa: The Vajjis were led by his grandfather **Chetaka**.
Ajatashatru ruled **492-460 BCE** (Haryanka).
His successor **Udayin** built **Pataliputra**.

na276dae2c2f.s: Which Nanda ruler was known as Ekarat?
na276dae2c2f.x: Mahapadma Nanda was called Ekarat; Dhana Nanda was the last Nanda ruler.
xa: Nanda rule: **345-321 BCE**.
The **Hathigumpha inscription** of Kharavela shows Nanda control over **Kalinga** (APPSC-G1 2022).

n86a38182941.s: Which ruler is treated as the founder of the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha?
n86a38182941.x: Bimbisara (544-492 BCE) is treated as the founder of the Haryanka dynasty (APPSC-GS 2018, BPSC 2024). Ajatashatru and Udayin were his Haryanka successors, while Shishunaga founded the next dynasty.
xs: **Bimbisara** is treated as the **founder** of the **Haryanka** dynasty — so option **(4)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2018, BPSC 2024).
**Ajatashatru** and **Udayin** were his successors; **Shishunaga** founded the **next** dynasty.
xa: Bimbisara ruled **544-492 BCE**; conquered **Anga**.
"Contemporary of Buddha" = **Bimbisara** (APPSC 2018).
Some notes add that his **grandfather** began the line.

nf68155e346e.s: Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa and ____ were the four dominant powers of the Mahajanapada period.
nf68155e346e.x: Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa and Avanti were the four dominant powers of the period.
xa: **Pradyota** (Avanti) rivalled **Bimbisara** (Magadha) and **Udayana** (Vatsa).
Kosala annexed **Kashi**; Magadha later took it as **dowry and by war**.
**Shishunaga ended Avanti**.

ne0dd98e61ed.s: Which of the following was NOT a factor in the rise of Magadha?
o: Availability of iron ore for tools and weapons
Dependence on a purely pastoral economy
ne0dd98e61ed.x: Magadha benefited from fertile agriculture, iron resources, elephants and rivers. Dependence on a purely pastoral economy was not a stated factor in its rise.
ne0dd98e61ed.tq: Find the outsider by separating the listed advantages from an unrelated economic feature.
xs: A **purely pastoral economy** was **not** a factor — so option **(2)** is the answer.
Magadha had **fertile alluvium**, ample rainfall and **rice** — an agrarian base.
**Iron ore** (tools, weapons), **elephants** (war) and **rivers** (transport, defence) were real factors.
xa: Rivers: **Ganga** and **Son**.
**Towns + metallic money** raised revenue.
Magadha was the most powerful Mahajanapada by the **6th-4th centuries BCE** (APPSC 2018).

n6f66b819f87.s: Pataliputra stood at the confluence of the Ganga and the:
n6f66b819f87.x: Pataliputra was established at the Ganga-Son confluence; the earlier capital Rajagriha was protected by five hills.
xa: Rajagriha was also called **Girivraja**.
**Udayin** built Pataliputra.
Rivers **Ganga** and **Son** gave Magadha **transport and defence**.

n075ae3ad0b1.s: At the time of Alexander's invasion of north-west India, Magadha was ruled by:
n075ae3ad0b1.x: Magadha was then ruled by the Nandas under Dhana Nanda, the last Nanda king. Mahapadma Nanda was the earlier Nanda empire-builder, Chandragupta Maurya came to power later (c. 321 BCE) and Kalashoka was a Shishunaga ruler.
xs: At Alexander's invasion, Magadha was ruled by **Dhana Nanda** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Mahapadma Nanda** was the earlier Nanda "**Ekarat**".
**Kalashoka** was a **Shishunaga** ruler; the **Mauryas** came after the Nandas.
xa: Nanda rule: **345-321 BCE**.
Alexander crossed the **Indus** in **326 BCE**.
Order: **Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya**.

nac44caeceea.s: Use of which language, placing religious teaching beyond common people, encouraged the rise of heterodox sects?
nac44caeceea.x: Sanskrit-centred religious practice, along with costly yajnas, animal sacrifice and dissatisfaction with ritualism, encouraged heterodox sects.
xa: Vedic sacrifices consumed **cattle** needed for **iron-plough agriculture**; **ahimsa** fitted farmers.
Newly rich **Vaishyas** wanted higher status and a creed not frowning on trade.
**Varna rigidity**: Kshatriyas resented **Brahmin dominance**.

n635a09d9bb4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the causes of the rise of heterodox sects?
o: Vedic sacrifices consumed cattle needed for iron-plough farming
Mahavira and Buddha were both Kshatriyas
Newly rich Vaishyas favoured the Vedic sacrificial religion
n635a09d9bb4.x: The newly rich Vaishyas wanted higher status and did not favour the Vedic sacrificial religion; the other three statements are correct.
xa: **Ritualism**: costly yajnas, **jeeva himsa** and Sanskrit-only religion put religion out of reach of common people.
**Ajivikas**: founded by **Nanda Vachcha**, popularised by **Makkhali Gosala**; doctrine **Niyati**.

ncbc54f00766.s: The rise of the Mahajanapadas and Magadha is associated with:
ncbc54f00766.x: The Mahajanapadas and Magadha were linked with the second urbanisation and the emergence of the first large Indian state.
xa: Magadha was the most powerful Mahajanapada by the **6th-4th centuries BCE**.
Factors: **iron ore**, **elephants**, **Ganga and Son** rivers, towns + **metallic money**.
Newly rich **Vaishyas** backed creeds not frowning on trade.

ncc58d545c1b.s: Which Mauryan ruler is traditionally associated with Bhadrabahu in the southward spread of Jainism?
ncc58d545c1b.x: Chandragupta Maurya adopted Jainism and is traditionally associated with Bhadrabahu in its southward movement.
xa: **Udayin** was a **Jain devotee** per Jain tradition.
**Jain monks** were present on the Indus during Alexander's invasion.
**Mahavira** died at **Pava** (Malla).

ndb3b27eaa4a.s: The Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela indicates that:
o: Alexander built a canal connecting the Ganga and Son
Nandaraja dug a canal which was later extended by Kharavela
Shishunaga constructed irrigation works in Avanti
Bimbisara constructed a canal in Anga
ndb3b27eaa4a.x: The Hathigumpha inscription states that a canal dug by Nandaraja, identified with Mahapadma Nanda, was extended by Kharavela. It also indicates Nanda control over Kalinga.
ndb3b27eaa4a.tq: Match the inscription with the ruler, work and later extension mentioned in it.
xs: The **Hathigumpha inscription** of **Kharavela** says a canal dug by **Nandaraja (Mahapadma Nanda)** was **extended by Kharavela** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It shows **Nanda control over Kalinga** (APPSC-G1 2022).
xa: Kharavela was the king of **Kalinga**.
Mahapadma Nanda = "**Ekarat**", first non-Kshatriya dynasty.
AP angle: **Nanda reach into Kalinga/Deccan**.

n85fa1a14d31.s: Which cultural development is associated with the Achaemenid Persian presence in north-western India?
o: Introduction of Brahmi script from the Deccan
Replacement of all local scripts by Greek
n85fa1a14d31.x: The Persian presence contributed to the spread of the Kharosthi script in the north-western region.
n85fa1a14d31.tq: Match the foreign influence with its specific script-related consequence.
xs: The Persian presence led to the **spread of the Kharosthi script** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Gandhara** was the **20th and richest** satrapy (Herodotus).
xa: **Cyrus** began the invasions; **Darius I** annexed **Punjab/Sindh** (c. **516 BCE**).
Gandhara's capital was **Taxila**.
**Ambhi** of Taxila later submitted to **Alexander**.

n769e5ac929a.x: Alexander crossed the Indus in 326 BCE and died at Babylon in 323 BCE.
xa: ⚠ **Hydaspes = Jhelum** (battle with Porus); **Beas** = limit of the advance.
**Ambhi** of Taxila submitted.
