It also means freedom from the **cycle of rebirth**; it is the **main goal** (APPSC GS **2012**).
Vedic sacrifice was **rejected**, and God was neither affirmed nor denied.
xa: **Nirodha**, the third Noble Truth, says suffering can end — that cessation is Nirvana.
**Karma**: rebirth continues **till nirvana**.
Three marks: **Anicca**, **Anatta**, **Dukkha**.

n46cf736db99.s: According to Buddhist teaching, karma is primarily understood as:
o: A ritual sacrifice prescribed in the Vedas
A denial of rebirth and moral causation
Intention-based morality in which present conditions arise from past actions
A divine decree that completely removes human choice
n46cf736db99.x: Buddhist karma is intention-based morality; the present state is linked to past actions, and rebirth continues until nirvana.
n46cf736db99.tq: Distinguish Buddhist moral causation from divine decree and ritual action.
xs: Buddhist karma is **intention-based morality**: the present state comes from **past actions** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Rebirth continues **till nirvana**.
Vedic authority and **sacrifice** were rejected, so (1) is wrong.
xa: The Buddha neither affirmed nor denied **God**.
**Nirvana** brings freedom from the **cycle of rebirth**.

nf9d1fdb7fc9.s: In the Eightfold Path, Right Mindfulness belongs to:
nf9d1fdb7fc9.x: Right Mindfulness is part of mental discipline; ethics consists of Right Speech, Right Action and Right Livelihood.
xa: **Prajna** (wisdom) = **Right View**, **Right Intention**.
Pali terms: Mindfulness = **sati**; Livelihood = **ajiva**; Action = **kammanta**.

ne76ef93106e.s: In the Eightfold Path, 'Sankappa' means Right:
ne76ef93106e.x: Sankappa is Right Intention; Samma-ditthi is Right View, Vaca Right Speech and Samadhi Right Concentration.
xa: Others: **Kammanta** = Action, **Ajiva** = Livelihood, **Vayama** = Effort, **Sati** = Mindfulness.
Groups: **Prajna** (wisdom), **Sila** (ethics), **Samadhi** (mental discipline).

n85492606448.s: The Buddhist doctrine which explains that every phenomenon arises owing to a cause is known as:
n85492606448.x: Pratityasamutpada is the doctrine of dependent origination, according to which phenomena arise through causal conditions.
n85492606448.tq: Test the exact doctrinal term against closely related Buddhist concepts.
xs: The doctrine that every phenomenon **arises from a cause** is **Pratityasamutpada** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is **dependent origination**, a chain of **12 nidanas**.
**Nirodha** = cessation; **Anicca** = impermanence; **Anatta** = no permanent self.
xa: The chain begins **avidya (ignorance) → samskara → vijnana** and ends in **old age and death**.
Links **9-12**: Upadana → Bhava → Jati → **Jara-marana**.

n84da9650d44.x: Jina, Kevalin and Nigantha Nataputta are all designations of Mahavira.
xa: The Buddha's epithets: **Buddha** (Awakened One), **Tathagata** ("thus-gone"), **Shakyamuni** (sage of the Shakyas).
"**Light of Asia**" is the title of **Edwin Arnold**'s poem.
⚠ This is a common **odd-one-out** trap.

n62961770bcf.s: The Buddhist Middle Path primarily rejects which of the following?
o: Both extreme asceticism and sensual indulgence
n62961770bcf.x: The Middle Path avoids both the extreme of severe asceticism and the opposite extreme of sensual indulgence.
n62961770bcf.tq: Identify the principle by applying it to the two extremes it avoids.
xs: The **Middle Path (Madhyama Marga)** rejects both **extreme asceticism** and **sensual indulgence** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The Buddha himself abandoned **six years** of austerities before enlightenment.
xa: The path to the end of suffering is the **Noble Eightfold Path** (**Magga**).
The teaching is likened to a **raft** — **upaya** (skilful means), not dogma.

n5b3b4c63ace.s: The phrase “Appamadena sampadetha”, associated with the last words of Gautama Buddha, conveys which of the following meanings?
n5b3b4c63ace.x: “Appamadena sampadetha” means “strive diligently” and is associated with Buddha's last words.
n5b3b4c63ace.tq: Translate a distinctive phrase rather than relying on the surrounding historical event.
xs: "**Appamadena sampadetha**" means **strive diligently** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The full last words: "**All composite things decay**, strive diligently".
xa: Mahaparinirvana: **Kusinara** (Kushinagar, UP), age **80**, **483 BCE**; some notes give c. **486** BC.
The Buddha named **no successor** — the **Dhamma and Vinaya** were to be the teacher.
The **last convert** was **Subhadda**, at Kusinara.

nbef6ae97bd3.s: Who were regarded as the first lay disciples of Gautama Buddha?
nbef6ae97bd3.x: The merchants Tapassu and Bhallika are regarded as Buddha's first lay disciples.
nbef6ae97bd3.tq: Separate lay disciples from ordained companions, family members and royal followers.
xs: The first lay disciples were the merchants **Tapassu and Bhallika** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Kondanna** and **Assaji** were among the **five former companions**; **Rahula** was his son and **Channa** his charioteer.
**Bimbisara** and **Ajatashatru** were **royal disciples** of Magadha.
xa: The **last convert** was **Subhadda**, at Kusinara.
**Sariputta** and **Mahamoggallana** were the **chief disciples**.
**Upasaka** = lay follower.

n59bca193dd5.s: Who recited the Vinaya Pitaka at the First Buddhist Council?
n59bca193dd5.x: Upali recited the Vinaya Pitaka; Ananda recited the Sutta Pitaka and Mahakassapa presided.
xa: The First Council was held at **Rajagriha** (Rajgir).
Mahakassapa led the Sangha after the Buddha.
⚠ **Ananda** = Sutta; **Upali** = Vinaya; **Mahakassapa** = president.

n85803c37554.s: Bavari’s disciples, who came from the Godavari region, are associated with which development in the history of Buddhism?
o: They carried Buddhist relics from Sanchi to Mongolia.
They founded the Maha Bodhi Society at Bodh Gaya.
They secured UNESCO recognition for the Maha Bodhi Temple.
n85803c37554.x: Bavari’s disciples from the Godavari region met the Buddha and helped bring Buddhism to Andhra.
n85803c37554.tq: Connect the regional group with its specific role in the spread of Buddhism rather than with later institutional or heritage developments.
xs: **Bavari's disciples** from the **Godavari region** met the Buddha and **brought the faith to Andhra** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The relics went to **Mongolia** via the Ministry of Culture; the **Maha Bodhi Society** was founded by **Anagarika Dharmapala**.
xa: The **Mahabodhi Temple** is a **UNESCO** site since **2002**.
The organised **Sangha** drove Buddhism's spread.

n09198c7ddde.s: Who tempted Gautama before his enlightenment?
n09198c7ddde.x: Mara is associated with the temptation of Gautama Buddha before his enlightenment.
xa: Enlightenment: **Uruvela**, under the **Bodhi tree**, on the bank of the **Niranjana** — today **Bodh Gaya**, Bihar.
⚠ Ages **29 – 35 – 80** = **Renunciation – Enlightenment – Parinirvana**.

ne71f74c94f5.s: The title 'Light of Asia', used for the Buddha, comes from
ne71f74c94f5.x: 'Light of Asia' is the title of Edwin Arnold's poem on the Buddha. It is not from an Ashokan inscription, the Mahavamsa or Dharmapala; the Buddha's own epithets are Buddha, Tathagata and Shakyamuni.
xs: "**Light of Asia**" is the title of **Edwin Arnold's poem** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Buddha's own epithets are **Buddha**, **Tathagata** and **Shakyamuni**.
**Anagarika Dharmapala** founded the **Maha Bodhi Society** (**1891**); the **Rumindei** pillar confirms the birthplace.
xa: **Tathagata** = "thus-gone"; **Shakyamuni** = sage of the Shakyas.
⚠ **Jina**, **Kevalin** and **Nigantha Nataputta** = **Mahavira**, not the Buddha.

na7419f9d047.s: The three refuges or pillars of Buddhism are:
na7419f9d047.x: The Triratna consists of Buddha as teacher, Dhamma as teaching and Sangha as the order.
na7419f9d047.tq: Test a standard three-part list with related doctrinal distractors.
xs: The three refuges (**Triratna**) are **Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Buddha** = teacher; **Dhamma** = teaching; **Sangha** = order of monks and nuns.
xa: The Sangha were the **torch-bearers of Dhamma**; the organised Sangha drove Buddhism's spread.
**Vinaya** = the monastic code; **Uposatha** = fortnightly confession.

n57388914c65.s: Which of the following was NOT a bar to admission into the Buddhist Sangha?
n57388914c65.x: Criminals, lepers and people with infectious diseases were excluded, but caste was no bar to admission.
xa: **Women** were admitted after requests of **Ananda** and **Mahapajapati Gotami**.
Significance: Buddhism was a **caste-open**, socially accessible path.

n820fc5f53fe.s: Vassa, the Buddhist rainy-season retreat, lasted:
n820fc5f53fe.x: Vassa was a three-month rainy-season retreat.
xa: The Sangha had **democratic functioning** with power to punish.
**Uposatha** = fortnightly confession and rule-recitation.
**Parajika** = grave offence — expulsion.

nindian-history-51-41.s: Who donated the Jetavana Vihara to the Buddhist Sangha?
nindian-history-51-41.x: Anathapindika donated the Jetavana Vihara; Vishakha built Pubharama and Bimbisara gave Venuvana.
n: The Buddhist Sangha was a monastic order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Anathapindika donated Jetavana Vihara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Vishakha built Pubharama. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Bimbisara built Venuvana. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xa: **Jetavana Vihara** was at **Shravasti**, the site of the **Twin Miracle**.
Women were admitted after requests of **Ananda** and **Mahapajapati Gotami**.
**Bhikkhuni Sangha** was taken to Sri Lanka by **Sanghamitta**.
**Uposatha** = fortnightly confession; **Upasampada** = full ordination.

nindian-history-50-9.s: Which group consists of places associated with Buddhist council traditions?
o: Sarnath, Bodh Gaya, Kushinagar and Bihar
nindian-history-50-9.x: The four Buddhist councils were held at Rajgir, Vaishali, Pataliputra and Kashmir. Sarnath, Bodh Gaya and Kushinagar are linked with the Buddha's life, not the councils.
nindian-history-50-9.tq: Recall the venues of the four Buddhist councils.
n: Buddhist council traditions are associated with Rajgir. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 118-121]
Buddhist council traditions are associated with Vaishali. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 118-121]
Buddhist council traditions are associated with Pataliputra. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 118-121]
Buddhist council traditions are associated with Kashmir. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 118-121]
xs: **Rajgir, Vaishali, Pataliputra and Kashmir** are the Buddhist council places — so option **(2)** is correct.
1st council at **Rajgir** (Rajagriha), 2nd at **Vaishali**, 3rd at **Pataliputra**, 4th in **Kashmir** (Kundalvana).
**Sarnath, Bodh Gaya, Kushinagar** are sites of the Buddha's **life events**, not councils.
**Rajasthan** and **Gujarat** are IVC fire-ritual sites; **Delhi** belongs to the **Sufi** tradition.
xa: **Rajgir** also saw the taming of the elephant **Nalagiri**.
**Vaishali** was the site of the monkey's honey offering.
**Mahavira's activities** in the Jain tradition: the **Bihar region**.
**Ashtamahasthanas**: **7 of the 8** are in India.

nfe70ad600be.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of the five former companions who became arhats after hearing Buddha's first sermon?
o: Bimbisara, Ajatashatru, Prasenajit, Udayana and Pradyota
Kondanna, Bhaddiya, Vappa, Mahanama and Assaji
Alara Kalama, Uddaka Ramaputta, Mara, Subhadda and Mahapajapati
Tapassu, Bhallika, Rahula, Channa and Ananda
nfe70ad600be.x: The five former companions were Kondanna, Bhaddiya, Vappa, Mahanama and Assaji; they became arhats after the first sermon.
nfe70ad600be.tq: Check completeness of a named list and reject options containing persons from other groups.
xs: The five former companions were **Kondanna, Bhaddiya, Vappa, Mahanama and Assaji** — so option **(2)** is correct.
They heard the first sermon at **Sarnath** and became **Arhats**.
(1) lists **royal** followers; **Tapassu and Bhallika** were the first **lay disciples**; **Alara Kalama** and **Uddaka Ramaputta** were his **teachers**.
xa: They were the five ascetics with whom he had practised austerities for **six years**.
The sermon covered the **Four Noble Truths** and the **Eightfold Path**.

n517ccbc658c.s: Who founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891?
n517ccbc658c.x: Anagarika Dharmapala founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891 to work for the restoration of Bodh Gaya to Buddhist control.
n517ccbc658c.tq: Apply the founder–organisation association, a common history question pattern.
xs: The **Maha Bodhi Society (1891)** was founded by **Anagarika Dharmapala** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its aim was to **restore Bodh Gaya** to Buddhist control.
**Shashanka** and **Pushyamitra Sunga** destroyed the original Bodhi tree; **Sariputta** was a chief disciple of the Buddha.
xa: The **Mahabodhi Temple** has been a **UNESCO site since 2002**.
Bodh Gaya = ancient **Uruvela**, on the **Niranjana**, where the Buddha was enlightened at **35**.

nd34249fa329.s: The First Buddhist Council at Rajagriha was held under the patronage of:
nd34249fa329.x: The First Council met at Rajagriha under Ajatashatru; the Second met at Vaishali under Kalashoka.
xa: Dates: First **483 BCE**; Second **383 BCE**.
Presidents in order: **Mahakassapa – Sabakami – Moggaliputta Tissa – Vasumitra**.
Patrons in order: **Ajatashatru – Kalasoka – Ashoka – Kanishka**.

nd9de7bc2160.s: Which one of the following was a major outcome of the First Buddhist Council held at Rajagriha?
o: Translation of Buddhist texts into Sanskrit
Expulsion of heretics from the Sangha
Compilation of the Vinaya and Sutta Pitakas
nd9de7bc2160.x: At the First Buddhist Council, the Vinaya Pitaka was compiled through the recitation of Upali and the Sutta Pitaka through Ananda.
nd9de7bc2160.tq: Distinguish the outcome of the first council from those of the later councils.
xs: The First Council compiled the **Vinaya and Sutta Pitakas** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Upali** recited the **Vinaya**; **Ananda** the **Sutta**.
The **Abhidhamma Pitaka** and the **expulsion of heretics** came at the **Third** Council; **Sanskrit** was used at the **Fourth**.
xa: Venue: **Sattapanni cave, Rajagriha**, **483 BCE**; patron **Ajatashatru**; president **Mahakassapa**.
The Vinaya covers monastic rules — **Patimokkha**, **Vibhanga**, **Khandhaka**.

n7a5dbe12efc.s: Ashoka's stupa at Sanchi was encased in stone during the ____ period.
n7a5dbe12efc.x: Built by Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE, Sanchi was encased in stone under the Shungas and became a World Heritage Site in 1989.
xa: It is in **Raisen, MP**; its **four toranas** are by the **Satavahanas**.
Some notes call Sanchi the **largest stupa in India**.
**Bharhut** (Satna, MP) is also of the **Shunga** period.

n27606637dff.s: The four toranas of the Sanchi Stupa are associated with which dynasty?
n27606637dff.x: The four toranas of Sanchi are associated with the Satavahanas, although the stupa had earlier origins under Ashoka and was later encased under the Shungas.
xs: Sanchi's **four toranas** are by the **Satavahanas** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The stupa was built by **Ashoka** and **encased in stone under the Shungas**.
xa: Sanchi is in **Raisen, MP**; UNESCO **1989**.
**Torana** = gateway; **Vedika** = railing around the stupa.

nfa405bc65a0.s: Which one of the following sets contains texts belonging to the Vinaya Pitaka?
nfa405bc65a0.x: Patimokkha, Vibhanga and Khandhaka are sub-texts of the Vinaya Pitaka, which deals with monastic discipline.
nfa405bc65a0.tq: Start with the content category and match the texts belonging to it.
xs: **Patimokkha, Vibhanga and Khandhaka** belong to the **Vinaya Pitaka** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Yamaka** and **Kathavatthu** are **Abhidhamma**; **Jatakas**, **Theragatha** and **Buddhavamsa** are **Khuddaka Nikaya** (Sutta).
The **Mahaparinibbana Sutta** is in the **Digha Nikaya**; **Nettipakarana** is a non-canonical Pali text.
xa: The Vinaya (monastic rules) was recited by **Upali**.
The **Sutta** was compiled by **Ananda**, in **5 Nikayas**.

n414c9c54f07.x: Yamaka and Kathavatthu belong to the Abhidhamma, described as having seven books; Patimokkha belongs to the Vinaya Pitaka.
xa: The Abhidhamma is **philosophy in Q&A form**.
It is linked with **Moggaliputta Tissa** and the **3rd council**.
⚠ **Kathavatthu** = **Abhidhamma**; **Jatakas** = **Khuddaka**; **16 Mahajanapadas** = **Anguttara**.

nba8c34a0791.s: The Mahaparinibbana Sutta belongs to which Nikaya?
nba8c34a0791.x: The Digha Nikaya holds the long discourses, including the Mahaparinibbana Sutta.
xa: The **Anguttara** is arranged by number and lists the **16 Mahajanapadas**.
The **Khuddaka** has **15 books** — Jatakas, Dhammapada, Suttanipata, Buddhavamsa, Theragatha, Therigatha.

nbd1d4f76c3e.s: Which one of the following sets contains only the six paramitas of the Bodhisattva?
o: Ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha, brahmacharya, prajna
Dana, sila, kshanti, virya, dhyana, prajna
Dharma, artha, kama, moksha, dana, sila
Mantra, mudra, tantra, mandala, vajra, dhyana
nbd1d4f76c3e.x: The six paramitas are dana, sila, kshanti, virya, dhyana and prajna.
nbd1d4f76c3e.tq: Check a complete named list without substitution.
xs: The six **paramitas** are **dana, sila, kshanti, virya, dhyana, prajna** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Mantra**, **mudra** and **mandala** are the practices of **Vajrayana**, not paramitas.
xa: The **Bodhisattva** ideal — postponing nirvana for all beings — is the mark of **Mahayana**.
Mahayana's key idea is **Sunyata**; its texts include the **Prajnaparamita** and **Lotus Sutra**.

nindian-history-57-4.s: Which combination correctly represents the Tripitaka?
nindian-history-57-4.x: The Tripitaka is Vinaya + Sutta + Abhidhamma Pitaka. Vibhanga, Dhammasangani and Patthana are books inside the Abhidhamma Pitaka, not Pitakas themselves.
nindian-history-57-4.tq: Separate the three Pitakas from the books within them.
n: Vinaya Pitaka, Sutta Pitaka and Abhidhamma Pitaka together constitute the Tripitaka. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 131-132]
xs: The Tripitaka = **Vinaya + Sutta + Abhidhamma** Pitakas — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Vibhanga**, **Dhammasangani** and **Patthana** are books **inside the Abhidhamma Pitaka**, not Pitakas themselves.
**Vinaya** was recited by **Upali**, **Sutta** by **Ananda** at the **First Council**.
xa: **Abhidhamma Pitaka** is linked to **Moggaliputta Tissa** and the **3rd council**.
The **Sutta Pitaka** is arranged in **5 Nikayas**.
Vinaya Pitaka contains **Patimokkha**, **Vibhanga**, **Khandhaka**.
The Abhidhamma has **7 books**, including **Kathavatthu** and **Yamaka**.

nindian-history-57-17.s: Which Buddhist text contains the rules and discipline of the Sangha?
nindian-history-57-17.x: The Vinaya Pitaka holds the rules of the Sangha; the Sutta Pitaka has discourses and the Abhidhamma the analysis of Dhamma.
n: Vinaya Pitaka contains the rules and discipline of the Buddhist Sangha or monastic order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 131-132]
Sutta Pitaka contains Buddha's teachings, discourses and sayings. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 131-132]
Abhidhamma Pitaka contains a philosophical and analytical exposition of Dhamma. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 131-132]
Vinaya Pitaka, Sutta Pitaka and Abhidhamma Pitaka together constitute the Tripitaka. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 131-132]
xa: Vinaya and Sutta Pitakas were compiled at the **First council** at **Rajgriha** (**483 BCE**).
**Abhidhamma** gives philosophy in **Q&A form**.
⚠ **16 Mahajanapadas** = **Anguttara**; **Jatakas** = **Khuddaka**; **Kathavatthu** = **Abhidhamma**.

n13be8cf6daa.s: Which Nikaya contains the Mahaparinibbana Sutta?
n13be8cf6daa.x: The Digha Nikaya consists of long discourses and includes the Mahaparinibbana Sutta.
n13be8cf6daa.tq: Match the named sutta with the correct Nikaya by its discourse category.
xs: The **Mahaparinibbana Sutta** is in the **Digha Nikaya** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Digha has the **long discourses**.
**Anguttara** is arranged by number; **Majjhima** has medium discourses; **Samyutta** has kindred sayings.
xa: The **Majjhima** includes debates with **Jains** and **Ajivikas**.
The **Anguttara** lists the **16 Mahajanapadas**.
The **Khuddaka** has **15 books**, including the **550 Jatakas**.

n7968eb9cca9.s: The Dhammapada is part of which Nikaya?
n7968eb9cca9.x: The Khuddaka Nikaya includes the Dhammapada, Theragatha, Therigatha and Jatakas.
xa: The Khuddaka has **15 books**; there are **550 Jatakas** (birth stories).
It also holds the **Suttanipata** and **Buddhavamsa**.

n1aa52894f39.s: Which of the following Buddhist works belongs to the Sanskrit group rather than Pali literature?
n1aa52894f39.x: Divyavadana is a Sanskrit work, whereas Dipavamsa, Mahavamsa and Visuddhimagga are Pali works.
xa: Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa are **Sri Lankan chronicles**; the Mahavamsa is by **Mahanama**.
The **Visuddhimagga** was written by **Buddhaghosha** at **Anuradhapura**.
The **Milindapanho** and **Nettipakarana** are also Pali.

n178cc8ff0d3.x: Mahavamsa is a Pali Sri Lankan chronicle written by Mahanama.
n178cc8ff0d3.tq: Test the author of a named chronicle.
xs: The **Mahavamsa** was written by **Mahanama** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is a **Pali** Sri Lankan chronicle, like the **Dipavamsa**.
**Ashvaghosha** wrote the Buddhacharita; **Buddhaghosha** the Visuddhimagga; **Nagasena** is the monk of the Milindapanho.
xa: ⚠ **Pali** = Milindapanho, Dipavamsa, Mahavamsa; **Sanskrit** = Divyavadana, Buddhacharita.
Buddhism reached **Sri Lanka** through **Ashoka**'s mission (**Mahendra**, **Sanghamitra**).

n85b6b5792ce.s: Which form of Buddhism seeks salvation through mantras, mudras and mandalas?
n85b6b5792ce.x: Vajrayana uses mantras, mudras and mandalas; the Arhat ideal belongs to Hinayana and the Bodhisattva ideal to Mahayana.
xa: Vajrayana seeks salvation through magical power (**vajra**), with **Taras** and wrathful deities.
Hinayana worships **symbols**, not idols; Mahayana practises **idol worship**.
⚠ **Arhat** = Hinayana; **Bodhisattva** = Mahayana; **vajra** = Vajrayana.

ncfd885fbd09.s: Which one of the following regions is NOT correctly associated with Mahayana Buddhism?
ncfd885fbd09.x: Myanmar is traditionally associated with Hinayana or Theravada. Mahayana spread prominently in China, Japan, Korea and Tibet.
ncfd885fbd09.tq: Find the region belonging to a neighbouring sect.
xs: **Myanmar** is a **Hinayana / Theravada** land, not Mahayana — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Mahayana** spread to **China**, **Japan**, **Korea** and **Tibet**.
xa: Hinayana spread to **Sri Lanka**, **Myanmar** and **Thailand**, using the **Pali canon**.
Mahayana texts are in **Sanskrit** — **Prajnaparamita**, **Lotus Sutra**.
Mahayana arose after the **4th council**.

n6b1f51205f2.s: Which of the following is associated with the spread of Vajrayana Buddhism?
n6b1f51205f2.x: Vajrayana is linked with Padmasambhava. Vikramashila and later Nalanda were important centres associated with it.
xs: **Padmasambhava** is the founder/link of **Vajrayana** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Nagasena** is the monk of the **Milindapanho**; **Mahanama** wrote the **Mahavamsa**.
xa: Vajrayana developed c. **8th c. CE**, with centres at **Vikramashila** and later Nalanda.
Some notes credit **Siddha Nagarjuna** of **Sriparvata** as its founder.
In **Tibet**, Mahayana (entered in the **7th century**) merged with **Vajrayana** and **Bon**.

ne16b0e0d6cb.s: The Buddhist mission to Sri Lanka traditionally associated with Ashoka included:
ne16b0e0d6cb.x: Ashoka’s mission to Sri Lanka is associated with Mahendra and Sanghamitra.
ne16b0e0d6cb.tq: Distinguish missionary figures from later Andhra Buddhist philosophers and Pala rulers.
xs: Ashoka's mission to Sri Lanka was led by **Mahendra and Sanghamitra** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Dinnaga**, **Bhavaviveka**, **Nagarjuna** and **Aryadeva** were Andhra Buddhist scholars, not missionaries to Lanka.
xa: Andhra-Lanka ties ran via **Nagarjunakonda**.
The **Third Council** (**Ashoka**, c. **250 BCE**) sent missions abroad.
**Buddhaghosha** worked at **Anuradhapura** in Sri Lanka.

n2fd4040576b.s: Besides maritime trade, Buddhism reached Central Asia and China along the Kushan-era:
n2fd4040576b.x: The Kushan-era Silk Route and sea trade spread Buddhism abroad; Turkish raids contributed to its decline in India.
xa: **Sri Lanka**: Ashoka's mission (**Mahendra**, **Sanghamitra**).
**Tibet**: Mahayana entered in the **7th century**; the **Gelug** school was dominant by the **15th** c.

n5b6b3f1ca57.s: Which pair of texts constitutes the canon associated with Tibetan Buddhism?
n5b6b3f1ca57.x: The Tibetan Buddhist canon is associated with the Kangyur and Tengyur.
n5b6b3f1ca57.tq: Discriminate between Tibetan canonical terms and the textual collections of other traditions.
xs: The Tibetan canon is the **Kangyur and Tengyur** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Vinaya and Sutta** are Pitakas of the Pali canon; **Agamas and Angas** are Jain texts.
**Jatakas** belong to the Khuddaka Nikaya; **Milindapanha** is a non-canonical Pali dialogue.
xa: Tibetan Buddhism merges **Mahayana + Vajrayana**; Mahayana entered Tibet in the **7th century**.
China insists on the **1793 Golden Urn rule** for the Dalai Lama succession.

nindian-history-51-9.s: Which Buddhist sect associated dharmas with the past, present and future?
nindian-history-51-9.x: The Sarvastivada school held that dharmas exist in the past, present and future. The Ajivikas were a separate sect, Vajrayana is tantric Buddhism and the Chishtis are a Sufi order.
nindian-history-51-9.tq: Recall the doctrine of each Buddhist school.
n: Sarvastivada was a Buddhist sect. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Sarvastivada associated dharmas with the past. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Sarvastivada associated dharmas with the present. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Sarvastivada associated dharmas with the future. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xs: **Sarvastivada** associated **dharmas** with the **past, present and future** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Vajrayana** is the tantric school of salvation through **magical power (vajra)**, mantras and mandalas.
**Ajivikas** were a separate sect led by **Makkhali Gosala**, preaching **niyati** (fate).
xa: **Vaibhashika (Sarvastivada)** is based on the **Mahavibhasa** of **Vasumitra** — "All exists".
The **4th council** addressed **Sarvastivada** disputes of **Kashmir-Gandhara**.
**Sautrantika** (Kumaralata) relies on the **Suttas** and rejects Abhidharma authority.
⚠ **Sunyavada** = **Nagarjuna**; **Vijnanavada** = **Asanga / Vasubandhu**.

nindian-history-51-27.s: The Guhyasamaja is an important text of which Buddhist school?
nindian-history-51-27.x: The Guhyasamaja is an important tantric text of Vajrayana, which flourished from the eighth century.
n: Vajrayana is associated with Buddhism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Vajrayana flourished particularly from the eighth century. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Guhyasamaja is an important Vajrayana text. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xa: Vajrayana sought salvation through **magical power (vajra)** — mantras, mudras, mandalas.
Its founder/link is **Padmasambhava**; some notes credit **Siddha Nagarjuna** of Sriparvata.
Centres: **Vikramashila**, later **Nalanda**; in Andhra, **Salihundam**.
⚠ **Arhat** = Hinayana; **Bodhisattva** = Mahayana; **vajra** = Vajrayana.

n3777c71661e.s: The central doctrine of the Madhyamika school is:
o: All dharmas exist in the past, present and future
Strict adherence to the Vinaya alone
n3777c71661e.x: Madhyamika philosophy is based on Sunyata, or emptiness, and seeks a middle position between the extremes of existence and non-existence.
n3777c71661e.tq: Use doctrine-based elimination among closely related Buddhist schools.
xs: **Madhyamika** is built on **Sunyata (emptiness)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It seeks the **middle between existence and non-existence**.
"**Only consciousness is real**" is **Yogachara**; "dharmas exist in past, present, future" is **Vaibhashika**; strict Vinaya is **Sthaviravada**.
xa: Founder: **Nagarjuna**; later **Aryadeva**, **Buddhapalita** (Prasangika), **Bhavaviveka** (Svatantrika).
⚠ **Sunyavada** = Nagarjuna; **Vijnanavada** = Asanga / Vasubandhu.

n881b160f7e5.s: Kumaralata is associated with which Buddhist school?
n881b160f7e5.x: Kumaralata is associated with Sautrantika, which relies on the Suttas; Asanga and Vasubandhu are linked with Yogachara.
xa: Asanga was a pupil of **Maitreyanatha**; Vasubandhu was Asanga's **brother**.
Vasubandhu wrote the **Abhidharmakosa**.
**Vaibhashika (Sarvastivada)** is based on the **Mahavibhasa**.

n62bbee3a258.s: Nagarjuna was known as the ‘Einstein of India’ mainly because of his association with the idea of:
n62bbee3a258.x: Nagarjuna was called the ‘Einstein of India’ in connection with his idea of relativity.
n62bbee3a258.tq: Test a distinctive epithet by linking it to the exact idea given with it.
xs: **Nagarjuna** was called the "**Einstein of India**" for his idea of **relativity** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He founded **Madhyamika** and **Sunyavada** (APPSC G1 **2012**).
xa: Works: **Mulamadhyamakakarika** and **Suhrlekha**.
⚠ "**Kant of India**" = **Dharmakirti**; "**Father of Indian logic**" = **Dinnaga**.

n886426d8d53.s: The Maha Vihara or Parvata Vihara at Sriparvata was built by:
n886426d8d53.x: The Maha Vihara, also called Parvata Vihara, at Sriparvata is associated with Satavahana ruler Yajna Sri Satakarni, who was contemporary and friendly with Nagarjuna.
n886426d8d53.tq: Apply the history trap of distinguishing a ruler from another ruler of the same dynasty.
xs: The **Maha Vihara (Parvata Vihara)** at **Sriparvata** was built by **Yajna Sri Satakarni** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It had **1,500 rooms**; the king was **Nagarjuna**'s royal friend.
**Kanishka** was the patron of the **Fourth Council**; **Ashoka** of the **Third**.
xa: Some notes name **Gautamiputra** as Nagarjuna's friend instead.
Nagarjuna's **Suhrlekha** was a letter to this Satavahana king.

n94eecd61081.x: Ashvaghosha wrote Buddhacharita and Saundarananda; Abhidharmakosa is Vasubandhu's and Tarkajvala Bhavaviveka's.
xa: Ashvaghosha was at **Kanishka**'s court and was Vasumitra's deputy at the **4th council**.
Both his works are in **Sanskrit**.
**Bhavaviveka** was an **acharya at Sriparvata** (APPSC G2 **2019**).

nb796d4b128e.x: Buddhaghosha, born near Guntur, composed the Visuddhimagga at Anuradhapura, not Amaravati.
xa: He belonged to the **Theravada** school and wrote in **Pali**.
⚠ The Visuddhimagga is often wrongly paired with **Dignaga**, whose work is the **Pramana Samucchaya**.
Andhra produced **Nagarjuna**, **Aryadeva**, **Buddhaghosha**, **Dinnaga** and **Bhavaviveka**.

n2921c359413.s: Who is known as the “Kant of India” in the field of Buddhist logic?
n2921c359413.x: Dharmakirti is known as the “Kant of India” and wrote Pramana Vartika and Nyaya Bindu.
n2921c359413.tq: Test an identifying epithet with its scholar.
xs: **Dharmakirti** is the "**Kant of India**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
He worked on **logic** in the **7th c.** and wrote **Pramana Vartika** and **Nyaya Bindu**.
**Dignaga** is the "**Father of Indian logic**"; **Nagarjuna** the "**Einstein of India**".
xa: **Bhavaviveka** was an **acharya at Sriparvata** and wrote the **Tarkajvala**.
Dignaga's work: the **Pramana Samucchaya**.

nbee0c5aec4d.s: Which Buddhist scholar, author of the Tarkajvala, was an acharya at Sriparvata?
nbee0c5aec4d.x: Bhavaviveka, author of the Tarkajvala, was an acharya at Sriparvata (APPSC G2 2019). Buddhaghosha worked at Anuradhapura (Visuddhimagga), Dharmakirti wrote Pramana Vartika and Nyaya Bindu, and Asanga is linked with Yogachara.
xs: **Bhavaviveka**, author of the **Tarkajvala**, was an **acharya at Sriparvata** — so option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2019**).
**Buddhaghosha** worked at **Anuradhapura**; **Dharmakirti** wrote Pramana Vartika; **Asanga** is linked with **Yogachara**.
xa: In Madhyamika, Bhavaviveka led the **Svatantrika** line; **Buddhapalita** the **Prasangika**.
**Sriparvata** was the **Mahayana** centre of Andhra, with the **Maha Vihara** built by **Yajna Sri Satakarni**.

n9618d721b0f.s: The replacement of Pali by which language is associated with the decline of Buddhism?
n9618d721b0f.x: Replacement of Pali by Sanskrit, corruption of the Sangha, Brahmanical-Bhakti revival and loss of royal patronage are associated with decline.
xa: **Turkish raids** — **Nalanda** sacked by **Bakhtiyar Khalji**.
The original **Bodhi tree** was destroyed by **Pushyamitra Sunga** and **Shashanka**.

n1c5f4d76540.s: Which place is regarded as the birthplace of the Mahasanghika sect?
n1c5f4d76540.x: Dhanyakataka is the birthplace of the Mahasanghika sect; Mahadeva, who led the Mahasanghikas, began Chaitikavada in Andhra.
xa: Andhra monks under Mahadeva demanded **Vinaya reforms** at **Vaishali**.
The **Andhakas** attended the **3rd council** (Kathavatthu).
The **Vinayavatthu** mentions the "**Andhra path**" (APPSC G2 **2019**).

n8e03d6080c4.s: Which Buddhist text mentions the 'Andhra path' (Andhrapatha)?
n8e03d6080c4.x: The Vinayavatthu mentions the 'Andhra path' (APPSC G2 2019). Milindapanho is the Menander-Nagasena dialogue, Dipavamsa a Sri Lankan Pali chronicle and Divyavadana a Sanskrit collection of legends.
xs: The **Vinayavatthu** mentions the "**Andhra path**" — so option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2019**).
**Milindapanho** is the **Menander-Nagasena** dialogue; **Dipavamsa** is a Sri Lankan Pali chronicle; **Divyavadana** is a Sanskrit book of legends.
xa: **Dhanyakataka** is the birthplace of the **Mahasanghika** sect.
The **Andhakas** attended the **3rd council**.
In Andhra all three sects coexisted: **Hinayana** (Amaravati), **Mahayana** (Sriparvata), **Vajrayana** (Salihundam).

n99b2a96861c.s: The Purvasaila branch of the Chaityakas was centred at:
n99b2a96861c.x: Purvasaila was at Amaravati, Aparasaila at Nagarjunakonda and Siddhadhika at Gudivada.
xa: Other branches: **Uttarasaila** — **Jaggayyapeta**; **Rajagirika** — **Guntupalli**.
**Mahadeva Bhikshu** began **Chaitikavada** in Andhra.
**9 of the 18** early sects existed in Andhra.

n45f778b54ef.s: In stupa architecture, the hemispherical dome symbolising the cosmos is called the:
n45f778b54ef.x: The anda is the hemispherical dome of a stupa and symbolises the cosmos.
n45f778b54ef.tq: Identify the architectural term from its function.
xs: The hemispherical dome that symbolises the **cosmos** is the **Anda** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Harmika** = railed square on top of the dome; **Medhi** = raised terrace/drum at the base; **Vedika** = railing.
xa: **Chhatra** = umbrella over the harmika.
**Pradakshinapatha** = circumambulation path; **Torana** = gateway.

n76d8ca5fa21.s: The railed square structure placed on top of the stupa dome is known as the:
n76d8ca5fa21.x: The harmika is the railed square placed above the dome. The chhatra is the umbrella above it.
xs: The railed square on top of the dome is the **Harmika** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Chhatra** is the umbrella above it; **Torana** is the gateway; **Pradakshinapatha** is the circumambulation path.
xa: **Anda** = hemispherical dome (symbolises the cosmos).
**Chaitya** = prayer hall; **Vihara** = monastery.

n1177c000806.s: A stupa containing relics is classified as a:
n1177c000806.x: A Dhatugarbha stupa contains relics. A Paribhogika stupa contains objects used by the Buddha, while an Uddeshika stupa is commemorative and has no relics.
n1177c000806.tq: Distinguish stupa types by their contents.
xs: A stupa holding **relics** is a **Dhatugarbha** stupa — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Paribhogika** holds **objects used**; **Uddeshika** is **commemorative**, with no relics.
xa: Andhra Dhatugarbha stupas: **Amaravati**, **Bhattiprolu**, **Jaggayyapeta**.
The relics of **Sariputta and Mahamoggallana** are kept at **Sanchi**.

n779b5d6c964.s: How many of the eighteen early Buddhist sects existed in Andhra?
n779b5d6c964.x: Nine of the eighteen early Buddhist sects existed in Andhra.
xa: The circuit plan dates to **2024-25**.
Chaityaka branches: **Purvasaila** (Amaravati), **Aparasaila** (Nagarjunakonda), **Uttarasaila** (Jaggayyapeta), **Rajagirika** (Guntupalli), **Siddhadhika** (Gudivada).

n9b028b4d0fa.s: Which Chinese pilgrim observed students memorising Nagarjuna's Suhrlekha?
n9b028b4d0fa.x: I-tsing noticed the memorisation of Suhrlekha, Nagarjuna's letter to a Satavahana king.
xa: I-tsing's note on the Suhrlekha was asked in **APPSC G2 2012**.
His main philosophical work is the **Mulamadhyamakakarika**.
⚠ Distinct from **Siddha Nagarjuna**, founder of **Vajrayana** at Sriparvata.

n7e6fb00b05f.s: Which of the following best reflects the pattern of lay patronage of Buddhist institutions in Andhra?
o: It was financed only through land grants by the Ikshvakus.
It was restricted to foreign monks and royal governors.
It was dominated exclusively by kings and military officers.
It was mainly provided by queens, merchants, guilds and artisans.
n7e6fb00b05f.x: Lay patronage was prominent and came from queens, merchants, guilds and artisans. One recorded example is a deposit of 2,000 karshapanas with a weavers’ guild for monks’ robes.
n7e6fb00b05f.tq: Apply the social-patronage pattern to a general historical situation.
xs: Lay patronage was dominated by **queens, merchants, guilds and artisans** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Example: a deposit of **2,000 karshapanas** with a **weavers' guild** for monks' robes.
So it was neither exclusively royal nor limited to Ikshvaku land grants.
xa: The **Satavahanas** were Vedic kings but **lavish donors**.
Royal women donors: **Gautami Balashri** (Nasik cave) and **Naganika** (Naneghat).
**Upasika Bodhisri** gave outstanding service in the reign of **Ehuvala Chantamula** (APPSC G2 **2012**, **2019**).

n3cc594ae62d.s: Which of the following missions of Ashoka was sent to Suvarnabhumi?
n3cc594ae62d.x: Ashoka sent Sona and Uttara to Suvarnabhumi. Mahinda and Sanghamitta were sent to Sri Lanka.
n3cc594ae62d.tq: Discriminate between the two pairs of Ashokan missionary names by destination.
xs: Ashoka sent **Sona and Uttara** to **Suvarnabhumi** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Mahinda** and **Sanghamitta** went to **Sri Lanka**.
**Nagarjuna** and **Bhavaviveka** were Sriparvata scholars; **Dharmapala** and **Gopala** were **Pala** kings.
xa: **Mahadeva Bhikshu** took Buddhism to Sri Lanka with **100,000** followers (**Mahavamsa**).
**Thotlakonda**, **Bavikonda** and **Bojjannakonda** had **Sri Lanka-SE Asia** trade links.

nddf1903d003.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Ikshvaku phase of Buddhism in Andhra?
o: A trampled Shivalinga sculpture reflects Veerapurushadatta's hostility to Saivism
Veerapurushadatta rebuilt the Nagarjunakonda Maha Chaitya
According to the Mahavamsa, Mahadeva Bhikshu brought Buddhism from Sri Lanka to Andhra
nddf1903d003.x: The Mahavamsa says Mahadeva Bhikshu took Buddhism from Andhra to Sri Lanka, not the other way round.
xa: Mahadeva went with **100,000** followers.
**Upasika Bodhisri** served in the reign of Ikshvaku **Ehuvala Chantamula**.
**Nagarjunakonda** had a **Sinhalese vihara**.

n2bf0d9671c6.s: Which dynasty is regarded as the last dynasty to patronise Buddhism in Andhra?
n2bf0d9671c6.x: The Vishnukundins are regarded as the last dynasty to patronise Buddhism in Andhra; the Indrapalanagara vihara is associated with this phase.
n2bf0d9671c6.tq: Test the superlative claim by distinguishing the final patron dynasty from earlier patrons.
xs: The **Vishnukundins** were the **last dynasty** to patronise Buddhism in Andhra — so option **(3)** is correct.
Their Buddhist site is the **Indrapalanagara vihara**.
The **Satavahanas** and **Ikshvakus** were earlier patrons.
xa: Later came the **Vajrayana** phase: **Salihundam**, **Bojjannakonda**; **Siddha Nagarjuna** at Sriparvata.
⚠ **Bodhisri** = Ehuvala Chantamula's reign; **Vishnukundins** = LAST Andhra patrons.

n829bae6d8fb.s: Upasika Bodhisri, known for her outstanding service to Buddhism, was active during the reign of
n829bae6d8fb.x: Upasika Bodhisri rendered outstanding service in the reign of the Ikshvaku king Ehuvala Chantamula (APPSC G2 2012, 2019). Gautamiputra and Yajna Sri were Satavahanas, and Kharavela was the Chedi king of Kalinga.
xs: **Upasika Bodhisri** served in the reign of **Ehuvala Chantamula** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC G2 **2012**, **2019**).
**Gautamiputra** and **Yajna Sri** were **Satavahanas**; **Kharavela** was the king of **Kalinga**.
xa: Some notes list her with **Veerapurushadatta**'s officials.
Lay patronage came from **queens, merchants, guilds and artisans**.
⚠ **Bodhisri** = **Ehuvala Chantamula**'s reign.

n3daa961f50a.s: Which of the following groups contains rulers or invaders associated with hostility towards Buddhism and its institutions?
o: Gautamiputra Satakarni, Naganika and Gautami Balashri
n3daa961f50a.x: Pushyamitra Shunga, Shashanka and Mihirakula are identified as hostile rulers associated with the decline of Buddhism. The other groups contain patrons, donors or missionaries.
n3daa961f50a.tq: Group hostile figures together while eliminating patrons and missionaries.
xs: **Pushyamitra Shunga, Shashanka and Mihirakula** were the hostile rulers — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Mahinda**, **Sanghamitta** and **Sona** were Ashoka's **missionaries**.
**Gautamiputra Satakarni**, **Naganika**, **Gautami Balashri** and **Kumaragupta I**, **Dharmapala**, **Gopala** were **patrons**.
xa: **Turkish raids** on **Nalanda** were another blow.
Decline factors: loss of patronage, **Bhakti** revival, **Vajrayana ritualism**.

nd4b010168b2.s: What did Hiuen Tsang observe about Sriparvata during the seventh century CE?
o: It had been converted into a Jain centre.
It contained only a royal palace and no monastery.
It had just been founded by the Ikshvakus.
nd4b010168b2.x: Hiuen Tsang found Sriparvata without patronage in the seventh century CE.
nd4b010168b2.tq: Test the traveller’s observation rather than the site’s earlier period of prosperity.
xs: **Hiuen Tsang** found **Sriparvata without patronage** (**7th** c.) — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was not newly founded then — its vihara had been built by **Yajna Sri Satakarni**.
xa: Sriparvata's acharya was **Bhavaviveka**.
The **Vishnukundins** were the **last** Andhra dynasty to patronise Buddhism.

n29771423195.s: In a stupa, the central mast is called the:
n29771423195.x: The yashti is the central mast; the anda is the hemispherical mound, the vedika the railing and toranas the gateways.
xa: **Harmika** = railed balcony on top — the abode of gods.
**Chhatri** = umbrella(s), symbol of royalty and protection.
**Ayaka pillars** = an **Andhra-only** feature.

n2b3d4569a79.s: Ayaka pillars and Ayakapata are particularly characteristic of Buddhist architecture in:
n2b3d4569a79.x: Ayaka pillars or Ayakapata are a distinctive Andhra feature; the Purna Kumbha is among their associated symbols.
n2b3d4569a79.tq: Associate the distinctive architectural feature with its regional tradition.
xs: **Ayaka pillars / Ayakapata** are a feature found only in **Andhra** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Their symbols include the **Purna Kumbha**.
xa: AP's largest stupa is **Amaravati**; its oldest is **Bhattiprolu**.
The **Amaravati School** used **white limestone**.

nc197e525974.s: In early Buddhist art, the Dharmachakra symbolises the Buddha's:
nc197e525974.x: The Dharmachakra represents the first sermon; the horse Kanthaka represents renunciation and footprints represent parinirvana.
xa: **Lotus and bull** = birth; **Bodhi tree / empty seat** = enlightenment.
**Hinayana** used **symbols**; **Mahayana** used **idols**.

na7885c63016.s: Buddha was first represented in human form in which period and at which major artistic centres?
o: 5th century CE at Nalanda and Vikramashila
1st century BCE at Sanchi and Bharhut
3rd century CE at Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda
1st century CE at Gandhara and Mathura
na7885c63016.x: The first human-form representations of Buddha appeared in the 1st century CE, particularly in the Gandhara and Mathura schools.
na7885c63016.tq: Combine the date and place rather than selecting a familiar Buddhist art centre alone.
xs: The Buddha was first shown in human form in the **1st century CE** at **Gandhara and Mathura** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Earlier art showed him only through **symbols** — e.g. **Bodhi tree / empty seat** for enlightenment.
xa: **Hinayana vs Mahayana**: symbols vs idols.
**Bharhut** (Shunga, **2nd c. BCE**) and **Sanchi** belong to the earlier phase.

nb2075f37f47.s: Which one of the following is regarded as one of the earliest stupas and is associated with an inscribed relic vessel linked to the Buddha’s kin?
nb2075f37f47.x: Piprahwa in Uttar Pradesh, identified with ancient Kapilavastu, has an inscribed relic vessel linked to the Buddha’s kin and is dated among the earliest stupas, around the fifth century BCE.
nb2075f37f47.tq: Match the earliest-period clue and relic evidence with the correct stupa.
xs: **Piprahwa** has an **inscribed relic vessel** linked to the **Buddha's kin** and is among the earliest stupas — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is in **UP**, at ancient **Kapilavastu**.
**Dhamek** is **Gupta** (c. **500 CE**); **Devnimori** is **Western Kshatrapa**; **Chandavaram** is in **Prakasam**.
xa: Its date is c. **5th c. BCE**.
**Kapilavastu** is one of the **nine stupas** built after the Buddha's death.

n7e3d869de09.s: Vaishya Tekri, near Ujjain, is believed to be associated with which of the following?
o: A Mauryan third-century BCE stupa linked to Ashoka’s wife Devi
A Satavahana vihara built by Gautamiputra Satakarni
A Gupta-period chaitya linked to Kumaragupta
A Jain cave complex built by Kharavela
n7e3d869de09.x: Vaishya Tekri is believed to contain a Mauryan third-century BCE stupa associated with Ashoka’s wife Devi and possibly identified with Kanakagiri Vihara.
n7e3d869de09.tq: Combine the excavation site, period and patron-linked tradition.
xs: **Vaishya Tekri** is believed to be a **Mauryan 3rd c. BCE stupa** linked to **Ashoka's wife Devi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is thought to be the **Kanakgiri Vihara**.
xa: Estimated size: **350 ft diameter, 100 ft high** — possibly larger than **Sanchi**.
The MP government will resume excavation after **~90 years**.

n93eaf9e551e.s: What was indicated by B. R. Mani’s excavations at Sarnath during 2013–14?
o: That activity at the site existed before Ashoka
That Sarnath was originally a Jain-only site
That Buddhist activity began only after the Gupta period
That the Dhamek Stupa was built by the Western Kshatrapas
n93eaf9e551e.x: The 2013–14 excavations led by B. R. Mani indicated activity at Sarnath before the time of Ashoka.
n93eaf9e551e.tq: Identify the archaeological finding, not a later monument’s dynastic attribution.
xs: **B R Mani**'s **2013-14** excavations showed **activity at Sarnath before Ashoka** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Dhamek** at Sarnath is a **Gupta** stupa (c. **500 CE**), not Western Kshatrapa.
xa: Sarnath was nominated for the **UNESCO** list **2025-26**; on the Tentative List since **1998**.
The first sermon (**Dharmachakra**) is shown by the **wheel** in aniconic art.

n1734813207b.s: The Bagh caves are located in:
n1734813207b.x: Bagh is in Madhya Pradesh; Bhaja is in Maharashtra, Udayagiri-Khandagiri in Odisha and Sittanavasal in Tamil Nadu.
xa: Udayagiri-Khandagiri (Kharavela) and Sittanavasal (cave paintings) are **Jain**.
Bagh has **9 Buddhist viharas**; Cave 4 is "**Rang Mahal**".

n5ff5996e8d0.s: The Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves of Kharavela in Odisha are:
n5ff5996e8d0.x: Udayagiri-Khandagiri are Jain caves of Kharavela; Karle and Guntupalli are Buddhist sites.
xa: Karle has a **great chaitya**.
Guntupalli is the only **rock-cut cave temple** in AP — the **Siddharthaka Chaitya**.

n6845d012722.s: The correct distribution of the 34 caves at Ellora is:
n6845d012722.x: Ellora has 34 caves, comprising 17 Hindu, 12 Buddhist and five Jain caves.
n6845d012722.tq: Use the total and three-part composition together to verify the distribution.
xs: **Ellora**'s **34 caves** are **17 Hindu, 12 Buddhist and 5 Jain** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is in **Maharashtra**.
xa: **Ajanta** (Maharashtra): **25 viharas + 4 chaityas**.
⚠ **Sittanavasal** and **Udayagiri-Khandagiri** = **Jain**.

nindian-history-76-3.s: The monolithic Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved under the:
nindian-history-76-3.x: Ellora's Kailasa temple was carved under the Rashtrakutas; Ajanta belongs to the Satavahana and Vakataka phases.
n: Ashoka is associated with Barabar Caves. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Ajanta Caves have Satavahana and Vakataka phases. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Rashtrakutas are associated with Ellora Caves. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Rashtrakutas are associated with Elephanta Caves. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
xa: **Ellora** comprises **34 caves**: **17 Hindu**, **12 Buddhist**, **5 Jain**.
At Ajanta, caves **9-10** are **Satavahana**; Ajanta has **25 viharas + 4 chaityas**.
**Elephanta** (Maharashtra) is linked to **Shaivism**.
**Ajanta** is famous for **murals** like **Padmapani**.

nindian-history-76-11.s: Which cave complex contains Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves?
nindian-history-76-11.x: Ellora mixes Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves; Ajanta and Kanheri are Buddhist and Elephanta is Shaiva.
n: Ajanta Caves are Buddhist caves. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Ellora Caves are associated with Buddhism, Hinduism, and Jainism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Elephanta Caves are associated with Shaivism and Hinduism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Kanheri Caves are Buddhist caves. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
xa: **Kanheri** caves date from the **1st century BCE**; famous for an **11-headed Avalokiteshvara**.
**Ellora** has the **Kailasa temple** (Rashtrakutas); **Elephanta** has the **Trimurti Shiva**.
⚠ **Sittanavasal** and **Udayagiri-Khandagiri** are **Jain** caves.

nindian-history-76-16.s: The largest and most evolved Hinayana chaitya hall in India is at:
nindian-history-76-16.x: The Karla chaitya near Lonavala, cut in the Satavahana period, is the largest and most developed Hinayana chaitya.
n: Karla Caves belong to the Satavahana period. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Karla Caves are the largest and most evolved Hinayana Chaitya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Karla Caves are Buddhist caves. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
xa: **Pulumavi II** donated a village to the **Mahasanghikas** at Karla.
**Nasik / Pandavleni** caves are also **Satavahana period**, reflecting Buddhist devotional practices.
**Bhaja** caves are early Buddhist caves on the **Deccan trade route**.

nindian-history-76-20.s: Which of the following cave sites has Ashokan inscriptions?
nindian-history-76-20.x: Barabar has Ashokan inscriptions; Kanheri has over 100 caves and Bagh shows scenes of public life.
n: Barabar Caves contain Ashokan inscriptions. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Nasik or Pandavleni Caves reflect Buddhist devotional practices. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Kanheri Caves number more than 100. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Bagh Caves depict public-life scenes. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Nasik or Pandavleni Caves are Buddhist caves. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
xa: **Nasik** caves belong to the **Satavahana period**.
**Kanheri** (Mumbai) has an **11-headed Avalokiteshvara**.
**Bagh** caves are of the **Gupta period**, late **4th** to **6th centuries AD**.

nindian-history-71-28.s: Ajanta's Buddhist cave paintings belong mainly to which period?
nindian-history-71-28.x: Ajanta's Buddhist paintings belong to the Gupta and post-Gupta periods, mainly the 5th-6th century Vakataka phase.
n: Ajanta contains Buddhist cave paintings. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 147-150]
Ajanta paintings belong to the Gupta and post-Gupta periods. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 147-150]
xa: **Cave 1**: **Bodhisattva Padmapani** painting.
**Cave 10**: **Swetagaja Jataka** painting.
**Cave 17**: an important **Vakataka-period** painting.
Ajanta (Maharashtra) has **25 viharas + 4 chaityas** with **Jataka** paintings.

nindian-history-71-25.s: Ajanta Cave 17 is noted for an important painting cycle of which period?
nindian-history-71-25.x: Ajanta Cave 17 has an important Vakataka-period painting cycle, including Jataka scenes.
n: Ajanta Cave 17 contains an important Vakataka-period painting. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 147-150]
Bani Thani was a famous painting of the Kishangarh School. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 147-150]
xa: **Cave 1** has the **Bodhisattva Padmapani**; **Cave 10** the **Swetagaja Jataka**.
Caves **9-10** belong to the **Satavahana** phase.
Ajanta's paintings span the **Gupta** and **post-Gupta** periods.

nindian-history-76-15.s: Which feature is associated with the Kanheri Caves?
nindian-history-76-15.x: Kanheri is noted for the 11-headed Avalokiteshvara. Padmapani is at Ajanta, Trimurti Shiva at Elephanta, and the famous rock-cut façade at Lomas Rishi.
nindian-history-76-15.tq: Link each cave with its signature artwork.
n: Ajanta Caves feature Padmapani. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Elephanta Caves feature the Trimurti Shiva. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Lomas Rishi Cave is famous for its rock-cut façade. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
Kanheri Caves feature an 11-headed Avalokiteshvara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 154-155]
xs: **Kanheri Caves** are noted for an **11-headed Avalokiteshvara** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Padmapani** is the famous painting of **Ajanta** (Cave 1).
**Trimurti Shiva** is at **Elephanta**.
xa: **Kanheri** (Mumbai) has **more than 100** Buddhist caves, dating from the **1st century BCE**.
**Karla** has the **largest and most evolved Hinayana Chaitya**.
**Nasik / Pandavleni** caves reflect **Buddhist devotional practices**.

n80bae97fa19.s: Which one of the following Buddhist learning centres was founded under the patronage of Kumaragupta I?
n80bae97fa19.x: Nalanda is associated with a Gupta foundation under Kumaragupta I. Vikramashila and Odantapuri were associated with the Palas, while Vallabhi was associated with the Maitrakas.
n80bae97fa19.tq: Identify the founder or patron by separating the learning centres and their dynasties.
xs: **Nalanda** was founded by Gupta **Kumaragupta I** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Vikramashila** = **Pala Dharmapala**; **Odantapuri** = **Pala Gopala**; **Vallabhi** = **Maitrakas**.
xa: **Dharmapala** and **Dharmakirti** taught at Nalanda; it is a **UNESCO** site.
⚠ **Nalanda** = Kumaragupta I; **Vikramashila** = Dharmapala; **Odantapuri** = Gopala.

n933dc119aba.s: The Buddhist centre of Odantapuri is associated with the Pala ruler:
n933dc119aba.x: Odantapuri is associated with Gopala, while Vikramashila is linked with Dharmapala.
xa: Vikramashila was a **Vajrayana** centre; Valabhi a **Hinayana** centre.
**Nalanda** was founded by **Kumaragupta I**.

nindian-history-14-18.s: Somapura Mahavihara at Paharpur was founded by:
nindian-history-14-18.x: The Pala king Dharmapala founded Somapura Mahavihara at Paharpur, now in Bangladesh.
n: Somapura is also known as Sompura Mahavihara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
Somapura Mahavihara was founded by Dharmapala. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
Somapura Mahavihara was located in Paharpur. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
Somapura Mahavihara belonged to the Pala period. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
Somapura Mahavihara was a famous Buddhist monastery. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
xa: **Dharmapala** also founded **Vikramshila** (Bhagalpur, Bihar).
**Odantapuri** was founded by **Gopala** in the Pala period.
**Nalanda** was founded by Gupta **Kumaragupta I**; it is a **UNESCO site**.

nf138786463e.s: The oldest stupa in Andhra Pradesh is located at:
nf138786463e.x: Bhattiprolu in Guntur district is known for the oldest stupa in Andhra Pradesh.
nf138786463e.tq: Use the superlative clue and distinguish the oldest site from the largest chaitya.
xs: The **oldest stupa in AP** is at **Bhattiprolu** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Amaravati** is the **largest** in AP, not the oldest.
xa: Bhattiprolu (Krishna delta) was built by Yaksha kings **Savaru and Kuberaka**.
⚠ AP largest = **Amaravati**; oldest = **Bhattiprolu**; only Divya stupa = **Adurru**.

nfce32a96a56.s: Amaravati is identified with the ancient city of:
nfce32a96a56.x: Amaravati is ancient Dhanyakataka on the Krishna; its stupa, the largest in Andhra Pradesh, was identified by Colin Mackenzie in 1797.
xa: It was built in **Pulomavi II**'s time and enlarged by the **Ikshvakus**.
**Ferguson** called it the "**Epitome of Indian Architecture**"; it is on the **UNESCO** tentative list.
⚠ Discovered by: Salihundam = **Gidugu Ramamurthy (1919)**; Sankaram = **Alexander Rea, 1906**.

n2c36046824e.s: The Amaravati School of art is particularly noted for the use of which material?
n2c36046824e.x: The Amaravati School is associated with sculptures executed mainly in white limestone.
n2c36046824e.tq: Distinguish artistic schools through their characteristic material.
xs: The **Amaravati School** is noted for **white limestone** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It grew around the **Amaravati Mahachaitya**, the **largest stupa in AP**.
xa: The Mahachaitya was built in **Pulomavi II**'s time and enlarged by the **Ikshvakus**.
**Ferguson** called it the "**Epitome of Indian Architecture**".
Amaravati (**Dhanyakataka**) was identified by **Colin Mackenzie (1797)**.

n3f248ccd97e.s: The Bhattiprolu stupa is located in which district and is traditionally attributed to which patrons?
o: Guntur; Yaksha kings Savaru and Kuberaka
n3f248ccd97e.x: Bhattiprolu is in Guntur district and its oldest stupa is attributed to the Yaksha kings Savaru and Kuberaka.
n3f248ccd97e.tq: Combine location and patronage to defeat swapped-person and swapped-place distractors.
xs: **Bhattiprolu** is in **Guntur** (now Bapatla) and was built by Yaksha kings **Savaru and Kuberaka** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is the **oldest stupa in AP**, in the **Krishna delta**.
xa: It is a **Dhatugarbha** (relic) stupa.
⚠ AP largest = **Amaravati**; oldest = **Bhattiprolu**; only Divya stupa = **Adurru**.

n550920e07ac.s: Which site is regarded as the only rock-cut cave temple and the oldest chaitya in Andhra Pradesh?
n550920e07ac.x: Guntupalli in West Godavari is the only rock-cut cave temple and oldest chaitya in AP. Bhattiprolu has the oldest stupa, Salihundam was a Mahayana-Vajrayana centre and Adurru has the only Divya stupa.
xa: Guntupalli is in **West Godavari / Eluru**, with "**house-viharas**".
It is the **Siddharthaka Chaitya** (APPSC G2 **2008**).
It was Buddhist, with an **earlier Jain** phase.

n0aac0c5515d.s: Salihundam, situated on the bank of the Vamsadhara, is especially associated with which tradition and find?
o: Theravada and bronze images of Maitreya
Mahayana-Vajrayana and bronze images of Tara
n0aac0c5515d.x: Salihundam in Srikakulam district was a Mahayana-Vajrayana centre and yielded bronze images of Tara.
n0aac0c5515d.tq: Pair the site with both its religious tradition and characteristic find.
xs: **Salihundam** was a **Mahayana-Vajrayana** centre known for **bronze images of Tara** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is in **Srikakulam**, on the **Vamsadhara** river.
xa: It was found by **Gidugu Ramamurthy (1919)**.
It was a **port town**, called the "**Tibet of AP**".

ne46aabf7e85.s: The Buddhist site of Sankaram (Bojjannakonda) was brought to notice in 1906 by:
ne46aabf7e85.x: Alexander Rea found Sankaram in 1906; Gidugu Ramamurthy found Salihundam in 1919.
xa: Sankaram includes **Bojjannakonda** and **Lingalakonda**.
⚠ Amaravati = **Colin Mackenzie (1797)**.

n1986f4ba926.s: Which Buddhist heritage site is popularly described as the “Tibet of Andhra Pradesh”?
n1986f4ba926.x: Salihundam in Srikakulam district is known as the “Tibet of Andhra Pradesh” and is noted for Vajrayana sculptures and an ancient port.
n1986f4ba926.tq: Test the exact nickname rather than the broader Buddhist association.
xs: **Salihundam** is the "**Tibet of AP**" — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was a **Mahayana-Vajrayana** port town on the **Vamsadhara**, with **Tara bronzes**.
xa: It was found by **Gidugu Ramamurthy (1919)**.
**Nagarjunakonda** is called "**Dakshina Gaya**".

nac70359156a.s: Guntupalli is also identified with which Buddhist literary name?
nac70359156a.x: The Buddhist literary name Siddharthaka Chaitya is identified with Guntupalli.
nac70359156a.tq: Test the exact literary-name and present-site correspondence.
xs: **Guntupalli** is the **Siddharthaka Chaitya** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC G2 **2008**).
**Sriparvata** = Nagarjunakonda; **Dhanyakataka** = Amaravati; **Kanakgiri Vihara** = Vaishya Tekri near Ujjain.
xa: Guntupalli is the only **rock-cut cave temple** and the **oldest chaitya** in AP.
It lies in **West Godavari / Eluru**.

n6a077835d66.s: Vijayapuri, the ancient name associated with Nagarjunakonda, was a Buddhist centre mainly during the
n6a077835d66.x: Vijayapuri was a Buddhist centre during the 3rd–4th centuries CE.
n6a077835d66.tq: Use the century range to distinguish the site from earlier Buddhist centres.
xs: **Vijayapuri** was a Buddhist centre in the **3rd-4th centuries CE** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is now **submerged under Nagarjuna Sagar** (GS **2025**).
xa: Nagarjunakonda was the **Ikshvaku capital**.
It has **30+ stupas** and a **Sinhalese vihara**.

nindian-history-26-2-35.x: Kondaveedu was a Reddy kingdom capital; Warangal was the Kakatiya capital and Penukonda a Vijayanagara stronghold.
n: Warangal was the capital of the Kakatiyas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Kondaveedu was associated with the Reddy kingdom. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Penukonda was associated with Vijayanagara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
xa: **Lepakshi** shows **Vijayanagara architecture** and paintings of the **Vijayanagara School**.
**Kakatiya mural paintings** are found at **Pillalamari**.
The **Kohinoor Diamond** was discovered in the diamond mines at **Kolluru**.

nap-history-24-12.s: The eight Bhairavakonda caves are located in which district?
nap-history-24-12.x: The Bhairavakonda caves, eight in number, are in Nellore district.
n: Bhairavakonda Caves are located in Nellore. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 34-35]
Bhairavakonda Caves number eight. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 34-35]
The Mandhata sculpture was discovered at Jaggayyapet. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 34-35]
xa: **Jaggayyapeta** on the Krishna had an early relic stupa; the **Uttarasaila** branch is placed there in some notes.
**Guntupalli** (West Godavari / Eluru) = only rock-cut cave temple in AP; = **Siddharthaka Chaitya**.
**Adurru** (Konaseema) has the only **Divya stupa** in AP.
**Chandavaram** (Prakasam) has a Mahastupa + **115** small stupas.

n35e68b244b7.s: An Arama in Buddhist architecture refers to a complex comprising:
o: A stupa, vihara, chaitya and school
Only a stupa and a relic chamber
A vihara and a Jain cave shrine
n35e68b244b7.x: An Arama was a larger Buddhist complex containing a stupa, vihara, chaitya and school. Nandaluru is cited as an example.
n35e68b244b7.tq: Recognise the comprehensive institutional complex rather than an individual monument.
xs: An **Arama** is a complex of **stupa, vihara, chaitya and school** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Example: **Nandaluru**.
xa: **Stupa** = relic mound.
**Ayaka pillars / Ayakapata** are an Andhra feature, with symbols such as the **Purna Kumbha**.

n0b8d8e87a2c.s: Nagarjunakonda was the capital of the:
n0b8d8e87a2c.x: Nagarjunakonda, now an island in the Nagarjuna Sagar, was an Ikshvaku capital with over thirty stupas and a Sinhala vihara.
xa: It is called "**Dakshina Gaya**" and has an island museum.
It was the **Aparasaila** centre and is named after **Acharya Nagarjuna**.
Ancient **Vijayapuri** (**3rd-4th century CE**) is now submerged under Nagarjuna Sagar (GS **2025**).

nf1c571457e8.x: Sriparvata is Nagarjunakonda, while Dhanyakataka is Amaravati.
xa: Sriparvata had Nagarjuna's **1,500-room vihara**, built by **Yajna Sri Satakarni**.
Dhanyakataka and Nagarjunakonda were the great **Ikshvaku-era** educational centres.

n101b4ee716a.s: Purana Kassapa’s doctrine of Akriyavada held that:
o: All actions are fixed by fate before birth
The body is composed of four elements and nothing survives
Reality consists of seven eternal elements
Actions produce neither merit nor demerit
n101b4ee716a.x: Akriyavada, associated with Purana Kassapa, held that actions have no moral consequence; even killing or charity produces neither merit nor demerit.
n101b4ee716a.tq: Match the technical doctrine with its distinctive implication.
xs: **Akriyavada** of **Purana Kassapa** held that actions produce **neither merit nor demerit** — option **(4)**.
Even **killing or charity** has no moral effect in this view.
Actions fixed by fate before birth is **Niyativada** of **Makkhali Gosala**; the **four-element** body is **Ajita Kesakambalin**'s materialism.
**Seven eternal, uncreated elements** is the doctrine of **Pakudha Kaccayana**.
xa: **Sanjaya Belatthiputta** taught **scepticism/agnosticism** — refusing to affirm or deny.
⚠ Do not confuse **Akriyavada** (Purana Kassapa) with **Niyativada** (Gosala, fate).
The views of the six teachers are reported by **Ajatashatru** to the Buddha in the **Samannaphala Sutta** (**Digha Nikaya**).

nb08c9edb069.s: Who was the most important leader and populariser of the Ajivika movement?
nb08c9edb069.x: Makkhali Gosala was the most important Ajivika leader and the third chief who popularised the movement.
nb08c9edb069.tq: Distinguish the principal leader from other contemporary heterodox teachers.
xs: **Makkhali (Makkali) Gosala** was the most important Ajivika leader and its populariser — option **(2)**.
He was the **third chief** who popularised the sect, and is the usual exam answer for "founder" (**UKPSC 2024**).
**Pakudha Kaccayana** taught **seven eternal elements**, **Sanjaya Belatthiputta** **scepticism**, **Purana Kassapa** **Akriyavada**.
xa: Gosala's core doctrine: **Niyati** — all thoughts and actions fixed before birth; **no free will**.
The Ajivikas were popular under **Bindusara**; **Ashoka** gave them the **Barabar caves**.
They survived nearly **2,000 years**, until the **14th century CE**, in **Karnataka and Tamil Nadu**.

ne6f3fd94589.s: The decline of the Ajivikas and other heterodox sects is mainly attributed to:
o: The Puranic-Bhakti revival and loss of royal patronage
The spread of Greek rule in the north-west
The adoption of Ajivika doctrines by Buddhism
ne6f3fd94589.x: The heterodox traditions declined with the Puranic-Bhakti revival (including under the Pallavas) and the loss of royal patronage.
xa: The Ajivikas lasted nearly **2,000 years**, until the **14th century CE**, in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
Under the Mauryas they were popular under **Bindusara** and given the **Barabar caves** by **Ashoka**.
**Charvaka** left no surviving texts; it is known via opponents' refutations.

n8fffaf63609.s: The Ajivikas held that human thoughts and actions were:
n8fffaf63609.x: The Ajivikas were determinists: actions were fixed before birth, there was no free will, and karma could not alter destiny.
xa: The Ajivikas also held an **atomic theory** of matter that influenced later **Vaisheshika**.
Exam angle: determinism **and** austerity true; "order of rebirth can be changed" false (**RPSC 2024**).
⚠ In the comparison table, Jainism and Buddhism say **effort decides**; only Ajivika says **all is predetermined**.

n3404999f615.s: For about how many years was Makkhali Gosala Mahavira's companion?
n3404999f615.x: Gosala spent about six years as Mahavira's companion before breaking away to lead the Ajivikas.
xa: Some notes call Gosala Mahavira's "**guru**" — a confusable point.
The **Bhagavati Sutra** (Jain Anga) gives the fullest account of their **quarrel**.
In the list of six teachers, Mahavira appears as **Nigantha Nataputta**.

nbf886d43d70.s: The Ajivikas' theory about matter, which influenced the later Vaisheshika school, was
o: the doctrine that matter is unreal
the theory of seven eternal elements with no killer or killed
nbf886d43d70.x: The Ajivikas held an atomic theory of matter that influenced the later Vaisheshika. The seven eternal elements belong to Pakudha Kaccayana, dependent origination (Pratityasamutpada) is Buddhist, and the Ajivikas did not hold that matter is unreal.
xs: The Ajivikas held an **atomic theory of matter**, which influenced the later **Vaisheshika** — option **(1)**.
**Seven eternal elements with no killer or killed** is **Pakudha Kaccayana**'s doctrine, not the Ajivikas'.
xa: Ajivika core doctrine: **Niyati** — fate/determinism, **no free will**, karma cannot change destiny.
Lifestyle: **extreme asceticism** — nakedness, lying on nails, walking through fire, sitting in large earthen pots.
Social base: **no caste discrimination**; appealed to warrior, industrial and mercantile classes.

n2cc214dc73d.x: Ajivika ascetics, who practised extreme austerities, were often called Sudra sannyasins; the sect had no caste discrimination.
xa: Caste discrimination "false" was the key in **BPSC 2024**.
Other austerities: sitting in **large earthen pots**.
The Ajivikas were popular under **Bindusara** and received the **Barabar caves** from **Ashoka**.

n9d92c00530e.s: The Barabar caves are significant in Indian architectural history because they are regarded as:
o: Among the earliest rock-cut caves in India
The earliest surviving cave paintings of the Gupta period
The first brick stupas built by the Kushanas
The earliest structural temples of the Pallava period
n9d92c00530e.x: The Barabar caves are among the earliest rock-cut caves in India and were donated by Ashoka to the Ajivikas.
n9d92c00530e.tq: Separate the architectural significance of a monument from later temple traditions.
xs: The **Barabar caves** are among the **earliest rock-cut caves** in India — option **(1)**.
They were donated by **Ashoka** to the **Ajivikas** (**UPPSC 2023**).
xa: The caves are in **Bihar**.
⚠ Made by **Ashoka**, not **Chandragupta Maurya** (**UPSC 2013** statement false).
⚠ Ashoka was a **Buddhist**, not an Ajivika, though he honoured them.
The **Barabar cave inscriptions** are a source for the Ajivikas.

n6710b5ad718.s: Ashoka’s Seventh Pillar Edict mentions the Ajivikas along with:
n6710b5ad718.x: The Seventh Pillar Edict of Ashoka, associated with Delhi-Topra, names the Ajivikas along with Brahmanas, the Sangha and Nirgranthas.
n6710b5ad718.tq: Recall the exact group of religious communities named in the edict.
xs: The **Seventh Pillar Edict** (**Delhi-Topra**) names the Ajivikas with **Brahmanas, the Sangha and Nirgranthas** — option **(1)**.
It reflects the great respect for the Ajivikas in the **Maurya** era.
xa: **Ashoka** donated the **Barabar caves** (Bihar) to the Ajivikas.
The Ajivikas were popular under **Bindusara**.
The Ashokan edicts and Barabar inscriptions are key **inscriptional sources** for the sect.

n3ebeabd77cd.s: The Charvaka school is also known as:
n3ebeabd77cd.x: Charvaka is also called Lokayata and Barhaspatya; Niyativada is the Ajivika doctrine of Makkhali Gosala.
xa: Charvaka is **complete materialism**: body formed of matter, ends in matter.
It accepts only **perception (pratyaksha)** as a means of knowledge.
Its original **Brihaspati Sutra** is lost; known mainly via the **Sarvadarshanasangraha** of Madhava.

n0f387a8271d.s: According to the Charvaka school, the soul is:
o: An eternal entity that survives death
n0f387a8271d.x: Charvaka identifies the conscious body with the soul and denies that any separate soul survives death.
xa: Contrast: Jainism — **eternal jiva** in all things; Buddhism — **Anatta**, no permanent self.
Charvaka is **complete materialism**; aim of life = **material pleasure** (kama).
Aphorism: "once the body is **ash**, how can it return?"

ndf8d723cb30.s: The only pramana (means of valid knowledge) accepted by the Charvaka school is:
ndf8d723cb30.x: Charvaka accepts only perception, while Nyaya accepts perception, inference, comparison and testimony.
xa: Perception is called **pratyaksha**.
Charvaka body-soul view: "**The conscious body is the soul**".
Charvaka is also called **Lokayata** (**APPSC GS 2025**).

n599dcc3cbfa.s: In which text does Ajatashatru report the views of the six teachers to the Buddha?
o: Samannaphala Sutta of the Digha Nikaya
n599dcc3cbfa.x: The Samannaphala Sutta, contained in the Digha Nikaya, presents Ajatashatru’s report of the views of the six teachers to the Buddha.
n599dcc3cbfa.tq: Use the source-and-content pair rather than recognising only the title.
xs: In the **Samannaphala Sutta** of the **Digha Nikaya**, **Ajatashatru** reports the views of the six teachers to the Buddha — option **(2)**.
The **Bhagavati Sutra** is a **Jain Anga** on Gosala's quarrel with Mahavira; the **Majjhima Nikaya** records the Buddha's debates with Jains and Ajivikas.
The **Brihaspati Sutra** is the lost Charvaka original.
xa: Charvaka is known mainly through opponents, e.g. Madhava's **Sarvadarshanasangraha**.
**Ashokan edicts** (**7th Pillar Edict**) and **Barabar cave inscriptions** name the Ajivikas / record the caves gifted.
The six teachers include **Makkhali Gosala**, **Purana Kassapa**, **Ajita Kesakambalin**, **Pakudha Kaccayana**, **Sanjaya Belatthiputta** and **Nigantha Nataputta**.

n85de20ef7be.s: The fullest account of Gosala and his quarrel with Mahavira is found in the:
n85de20ef7be.x: The Bhagavati Sutra, a Jain Anga, provides the fullest account of Gosala and his quarrel with Mahavira.
n85de20ef7be.tq: Identify the principal source by linking the text to its religious tradition and subject.
xs: The **Bhagavati Sutra**, a **Jain Anga**, gives the fullest account of **Gosala** and his quarrel with **Mahavira** — option **(2)**.
The **Sarvadarshanasangraha** (Madhava) refutes **Charvaka**; the **Seventh Pillar Edict** names the Ajivikas; the **Samannaphala Sutta** reports the six teachers' views.
xa: Gosala spent about **six years** as Mahavira's companion before breaking away.
Some notes call Gosala Mahavira's "**guru**"; **Jain texts** make him Mahavira's **disciple**.
The **Majjhima Nikaya** records the Buddha's debates with **Jains and Ajivikas**.

n70a43b0ec9c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the heterodox schools' views on karma?
o: Jainism: karma is material bondage removable by penance
n70a43b0ec9c.x: Charvaka does not accept karma as a determining force of rebirth; the other three views are correctly stated.
xa: Fate: Jainism and Buddhism — **effort decides**; Ajivika — **Niyati**, all predetermined.
Soul: Jainism — **eternal jiva**; Buddhism — **Anatta**.
Common ground of all four: **rejection of Vedic authority** and ritualism.

n71f57bfea5b.s: Who was the first Achaemenid ruler to campaign into the north-western part of the Indian subcontinent?
n71f57bfea5b.x: Cyrus, the founder of the Achaemenid Empire, was the first Achaemenid ruler to campaign into the Indian north-west, particularly the Gandhara region.
n71f57bfea5b.tq: Distinguish the first campaign from the later annexation of territory.
xs: **Cyrus**, the founder of the Achaemenid empire (c. **558-530 BC**), was the first to campaign into the Indian **north-west** — option **(4)**.
His campaign touched the **Gandhara** region.
**Darius I** came later and annexed Punjab/Sindh as the **20th satrapy**; **Xerxes** used Indian soldiers against the Greeks.
xa: ⚠ **FIRST** into the north-west = **Cyrus**; **20th satrapy** = **Darius I**.
**Herodotus**: the Indian satrapy was the **most populous and fertile**, paying **360 talents of gold dust**.
That tribute was **one-third** of the empire's revenue.

nf329b83cfdb.s: Which Achaemenid ruler annexed Punjab and Sindh west of the Indus?
nf329b83cfdb.x: Darius I annexed Punjab and Sindh west of the Indus. This territory became the twentieth satrapy of the Achaemenid Empire.
nf329b83cfdb.tq: Match the ruler with the specific territorial achievement rather than with the earlier campaign.
xs: **Darius I** (c. **522-486 BC**) annexed **Punjab/Sindh west of the Indus** — option **(2)**.
It became the **20th satrapy** of the Achaemenid empire.
**Cyrus** only campaigned first into the north-west; **Xerxes** used Indian soldiers against the Greeks; **Darius III** was the king **Alexander** defeated.
xa: The Indian satrapy paid **360 talents of gold dust** = **one-third** of imperial revenue (**Herodotus**).
Ashokan edicts copy the **Darius** model — words **"lipi/dipi"**, third person shifting to first person.
The **satrapy system** of administration became known in the north-west.

nindian-history-20-1.s: Darius I, who annexed parts of north-western India, ruled Persia during:
nindian-history-20-1.x: Darius I ruled Persia from 522 to 486 BC and annexed parts of north-western India.
n: Darius-I’s campaign occurred during 522–486 BC. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Darius-I conquered parts of northwestern India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Darius-I’s campaign was part of Persian expansion. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Darius-I conquered the Indus region. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Darius-I conquered Punjab. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Darius-I conquered Rajputana. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
xa: ⚠ Other notes say Darius I annexed **Punjab/Sindh** (west of the Indus) — the **20th satrapy**.
⚠ Other notes make **Cyrus** the **first** Achaemenid to campaign into the Indian north-west.
**Herodotus**: the Indian satrapy paid **360 talents of gold dust** — one-third of the empire's revenue.
**Kharosthi** script, derived from **Aramaic**, is a Persian legacy.

n05aac64f75b.s: According to Herodotus, the Indian satrapy of the Achaemenid Empire paid a tribute of:
n05aac64f75b.x: Herodotus called the Indian satrapy the most populous and fertile; it paid 360 talents of gold dust, said to be one-third of the empire's revenue.
xa: The satrapy was Punjab/Sindh **west of the Indus**, annexed by **Darius I** as the **20th satrapy**.
**Cyrus** (founder) was the first Achaemenid into the north-west.
**Xerxes** used Indian soldiers against the Greeks.

n8e9388e203b.s: The Kharosthi script, derived from Aramaic, was written:
n8e9388e203b.x: Kharosthi was written from right to left; Persian influence also showed in Aramaic edicts and the satrapy system.
xa: Ashokan edicts copy **Darius** — words **"lipi/dipi"**; third person opening, then first person.
Ashokan pillars resemble Persian ones in **polished surface** and **animal capitals**.
But they differ: **no base**, **inverted lotus**, **smooth** (not fluted) shaft.
