n4c425e30c32.s: Which of the following sets contains only early Telugu or Desi words associated with Gathasaptasati?
n4c425e30c32.x: Atta, Addam, Potta and Pilla are among the early Telugu words associated with Gathasaptasati. Other recorded examples include Padi, Pandi, Ammi and Tuppu.
n4c425e30c32.tq: Recognise the linguistic list by separating vernacular words from technical historical terms.
xs: **Atta, Addam, Potta, Pilla** are early Telugu (Desi) words — option **(4)** is correct.
The other sets are **Buddhist** or **administrative** terms.
xa: Fuller list: **Atta, Addam, Potta, Padi, Pandi, Pilla, Ammi, Tuppu**.
They are the **earliest traces of Telugu**.
First Telugu word: **"Nagabu"** (Amaravati); **"Vepuru"** in Myakadoni.

n462fbb5e808.s: The Gundaram Forest inscriptions associated with the Satavahana period were found in which present-day location?
n462fbb5e808.x: The newly found Satavahana-era Prakrit-Brahmi inscriptions were discovered in Gundaram Forest in Jayashankar Bhupalpally district of Telangana.
n462fbb5e808.tq: Use the location-specific clue to distinguish the newly reported inscription site from other Deccan archaeological centres.
xs: **Gundaram forest** is in **Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Telangana** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Vinukonda**, **Salihundam** and **Nagarjunakonda** are Roman-coin sites in AP.
xa: The inscriptions are in **Prakrit/Brahmi**.
They record **administrative divisions, local chiefs, land grants**.

n30aa19a9e4a.s: The Desi words occurring in the Gathasaptasati are important in the history of Telugu because they represent:
o: The earliest examples of Tamil-Brahmi writing
The first official language of the Mauryan court
n30aa19a9e4a.x: The Desi words in the Gathasaptasati are regarded as the earliest traces of Telugu, and the Satavahana period laid the foundation of the language.
n30aa19a9e4a.tq: Distinguish linguistic evidence for Telugu from the separate evidence of Sanskrit and Tamil-Brahmi.
xs: Gathasaptasati's Desi words are the **earliest traces of Telugu** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **first complete Sanskrit inscription** is Rudradaman's **Junagadh**.
xa: The Satavahana period laid the **foundation** of Telugu.
Words: **atta, addam, potta**, also ammi, padi.
First Telugu word: **"Nagabu"**.

nap-history-11-14.s: The Telugu script developed from which source?
nap-history-11-14.x: The Telugu script developed from Brahmi, through the Bhattiprolu and later Telugu-Kannada scripts. Prakrit and Pali are languages, not scripts.
nap-history-11-14.tq: Discriminate a script from a language.
n: Brahmi is the source of the Telugu script. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 16-17]
xs: The Telugu script developed from **Brahmi** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Pali** is the language of most early **Buddhist literature**, not a script source.
**Prakrit** was a language — the Satavahana **official** language — written in **Brahmi**.
xa: All Satavahana inscriptions are in **Prakrit-Brahmi**.
First Telugu word: **"Nagabu"** (Amaravati inscription).
The **British** called Telugu the "**Italian of the East**".

n2382eaf6205.s: Hala's Gathasaptasati is an important source for:
n2382eaf6205.x: Gathasaptasati is an important source for Satavahana social life and describes rural life and nature, not early political history.
xa: It has **700 Prakrit gathas**, mainly **love and romance** (G2 **2025**).
It is the first work covering all the **Navarasas**.

n5623a1597c5.s: The use of maternal gotra names by Satavahana rulers is known as the practice of:
n5623a1597c5.x: Satavahana rulers used matronymics, or names derived from the mother’s lineage or gotra. This practice began with Gautamiputra Satakarni.
n5623a1597c5.tq: Distinguish the maternal naming practice from the more familiar paternal term.
xs: Maternal gotra names are **matronymics** — option **(3)** is correct.
They began with **Gautamiputra Satakarni**.
xa: Examples: **Gautamiputra**, **Vasishthiputra**.
They show **respect for mothers**, yet society stayed **patriarchal**.
Gautamiputra's titles: **Ekabrahmana**, **Varnasankarya nirodhaka**.

n2c348d465ec.s: Mahatalavaras or Mahasenadhipatis in the later Satavahana phase were primarily:
o: Generals placed in charge of border provinces
n2c348d465ec.x: Mahatalavaras or Mahasenadhipatis were generals entrusted with border provinces and later developed into feudal lords.
n2c348d465ec.tq: Match the military title with its territorial responsibility.
xs: **Mahatalavaras / Mahasenadhipatis** were **generals in charge of border provinces** — option **(3)** is correct.
They belong to the **later phase** and **grew into feudal lords**.
Land surveyor = **Rajjugahaka**; treasurer = **Heranika**.
xa: Distant aharas were also run by **Mahasenadhipatis**.
After the fall, many feudatories became **independent**.

n16f9f17ae43.s: Which route correctly represents the inland commercial connection from Ujjain to Bharuch?
n16f9f17ae43.x: The inland route from Ujjain to Bharuch passed through Paithan and Tagara.
n16f9f17ae43.tq: Reconstruct the route by identifying the intermediate inland centres.
xs: **Ujjain → Bharuch (Barygaza)** ran **via Paithan and Tagara** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Paithan → Sopara** ran via **Aurangabad**; **Arikamedu → Red Sea** via **Sri Lanka** and the **Arabian Sea**.
xa: **Tagara (Ter)** was an emporium linked to coastal ports.
**Pratishthana (Paithan)** was capital + inland trade centre on the **Godavari**.
NextGenIAS **2026** maps the **Ujjain-Paithan-Tagara-Bharuch** route.

ncd3b8c3d028.s: Bhavaviveka is associated with which vihara in the Satavahana sphere?
ncd3b8c3d028.x: Bhavaviveka is described as the acharya at the Sriparvatam vihara.
ncd3b8c3d028.tq: Identify the person–institution association without confusing nearby Buddhist centres.
xs: **Bhavaviveka** was acharya at the **Sriparvatam** vihara — option **(3)** is correct (G2 **2019** key).
⚠ Some notes say **Dhanyakataka**; the key says Sriparvatam.
xa: Buddhist viharas grew beside the trade centres.
**Nagarjuna** is linked to **Sriparvata** in Andhra.

ne85801acd4e.s: Which of the following sets consists only of sites specifically associated with Dhatugarbha stupas containing bodily relics?
o: Karle, Bhaja, Nasik, Kanheri and Junnar
Nagarjunakonda, Amaravati, Jaggayyapeta, Salihundam and Bhattiprolu
Ghantasala, Sankaram, Guntupalli, Ajanta and Bagh
Sanchi, Bharhut, Kesariya, Bedsa and Pitalkhora
ne85801acd4e.x: The listed Dhatugarbha stupa sites are Nagarjunakonda, Amaravati, Jaggayyapeta, Salihundam and Bhattiprolu.
ne85801acd4e.tq: Test the complete membership of a named list rather than identifying only one site.
xs: The **Dhatugarbha** (relic) stupas listed are **Nagarjunakonda, Amaravati, Jaggayyapeta, Salihundam and Bhattiprolu** — option **(2)**.
**Karle, Bhaja, Nasik, Kanheri, Junnar** are **western Deccan rock-cut cave** sites, not relic-stupa sites.
**Sanchi** (largest in India), **Bharhut** (most ancient in India) and **Kesariya** (largest brick) are stupas outside Andhra.
xa: The other two types: **Uddeshika** (memorial, no relics) and **Paribhogika** (objects used by the Buddha / monks).
**Bhattiprolu** = **oldest stupa in Andhra**; **Amaravati (Mahachaitya)** = **largest in AP** (G2 **2019**).
⚠ Bhattiprolu = oldest in Andhra; **Bharhut** = most ancient in India — do not swap them.

n138d0d35f4c.s: The ancient port Kantakossyla is associated with which Buddhist site?
n138d0d35f4c.x: Ghantasala is associated with Kantakossyla; Bhattiprolu has the oldest stupa, Jaggayyapeta the Mandhata sculpture and Nagarjunakonda over 30 stupas.
xa: **Bhattiprolu** relic-casket inscriptions name king **Kubiraka** and the **'Nigama-sabha'**.
**Alexander Rea** excavated the **Bhattiprolu** stupa in **1892**.
Ancient name of Ghantasala in the sect table: **Kantakasala**.

nbe0d648cdc8.s: Who is named as the ruler in the Bhattiprolu relic-casket inscriptions?
nbe0d648cdc8.x: The Bhattiprolu relic-casket inscriptions name the ruler Kubiraka and refer to the Nigama-sabha.
xs: The **Bhattiprolu** relic-casket inscriptions name king **Kubiraka** — option **(1)**.
They also refer to the **'Nigama-sabha'**.
**Veerapurushadatta** = Ikshvaku records; **Yajnasri Satakarni** = Chinaganjam donor; **Pulumavi II** = Amaravati.
xa: **Bhattiprolu** = **oldest stupa in Andhra**; a **Dhatugarbha** stupa.
**Alexander Rea** excavated it in **1892**.
Bhattiprolu also has an **Ayaka platform**.

n6c84b295aa9.s: Which of the following is part of Andhra Pradesh's Buddhist International Tourism Circuit?
n6c84b295aa9.x: The circuit comprises Amaravati, Thotlakonda-Bavikonda, Bojjannakonda-Sankaram, Salihundam and Ghantasala.
xa: It targets visitors from **Japan, Korea, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Myanmar**.
"**Discover Andhra**" Buddhist-circuit campaign (**Feb 2026**).
**Amaravati Stupa** is on India's **UNESCO tentative list**.

ndaff364918e.s: Which of the following Andhra Pradesh heritage sites is included in India’s UNESCO tentative list?
ndaff364918e.x: The Amaravati Buddhist Stupa is included in India’s UNESCO tentative list. Lepakshi, including the Veerabhadra Temple and monolithic Nandi, was added in 2022.
ndaff364918e.tq: Distinguish tentative-list heritage sites from tourism proposals.
xs: The **Amaravati Buddhist Stupa** is on India's **UNESCO tentative list** — option **(3)**.
Amaravati was the **Satavahana capital** and site of the **Mahachaitya**.
xa: It is part of the **Buddhist International Tourism Circuit** with Thotlakonda-Bavikonda, Bojjannakonda-Sankaram, Salihundam, Ghantasala.
Amaravati sculptures are in the **British Museum, London** and the **Amaravati Museum**.
**Colin Mackenzie** discovered it in **1797**.

nindian-history-77-11.s: A relic casket with gold items was found at which Andhra site?
nindian-history-77-11.x: A relic casket with gold items was found at Bhattiprolu; the 'Sakiyanam' casket came from Piprahwa.
n: A gold casket with relics was found at Bhattiprolu. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #77 · pp 155-156]
Eight Ashokan Dharmachakras were found at Sopara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #77 · pp 155-156]
Remains of a Buddhist monastery were found at Devnimori, Gujarat. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #77 · pp 155-156]
Remains of a Buddhist stupa were found at Devnimori, Gujarat. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #77 · pp 155-156]
xa: **Dharmarajika, Taxila**: the Buddha's **bone relic casket**.
**Kumrahar**: remains of **Chandragupta Maurya's palace**.
**Sopara**: **eight Ashokan Dharmachakras**.

nindian-history-77-13.s: The 'Sakiyanam' relic casket was found at:
nindian-history-77-13.x: The 'Sakiyanam' casket came from Piprahwa; a bone relic casket was found at Dharmarajika, Taxila, and Kumrahar has the Mauryan pillared hall.
n: A relic casket bearing the Brahmi inscription “Sakiyanam” was found at Piprahwa Stupa. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #77 · pp 155-156]
Buddha’s bone relic casket was found at Dharmarajika, Taxila. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #77 · pp 155-156]
A gold casket with relics was found at Bhattiprolu. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #77 · pp 155-156]
Eight Ashokan Dharmachakras were found at Sopara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #77 · pp 155-156]
xa: **Devnimori** (Gujarat): remains of a Buddhist monastery and stupa.
**Bulandibagh**: remains of the **Pataliputra city wall**.
Amaravati, Jaggayyapeta and Nagarjunakonda stupas stand over **relics of Gautama Buddha** (G2 **2002**).

n6b3f0898731.s: A stupa containing bodily relics is called a:
n6b3f0898731.x: A Dhatugarbha stupa contains bodily relics; an Uddeshika stupa is devotional or memorial without relics, and a Paribhogika stupa holds objects associated with the Buddha or monks.
xa: **Dhatugarbha** examples in Andhra: **Nagarjunakonda, Amaravati, Jaggayyapeta, Salihundam, Bhattiprolu**.
**Amaravati, Jaggayyapeta and Nagarjunakonda** stupas stand over the **relics of Gautama Buddha** (G2 **2002**).
The Nagarjunakonda **Ayaka inscription** reads "**Samma Sambhudha Dhatu Parigahita**".

n22427ff357b.s: The horseshoe-shaped opening on the facade of a chaitya hall is called the:
n22427ff357b.x: The facade opening is the horseshoe-shaped chaitya window; Ayaka refers to stupa platforms.
xa: **Screen walls** shield the chaitya interior (UPSC).
**Vihara** = monastery with cells around a central hall (**Madhyashala**).
**Karle** has the **largest chaitya hall** (Hinayana).

n412947038f9.s: In a Buddhist vihara, Uposatha meetings were held in the central hall every:
n412947038f9.x: The vihara's central hall (Madhyashala) was used for fortnightly Uposatha meetings, every 15 days.
xa: A **chaitya** is a prayer hall, rectangular or apsidal, with a **stupa at the apse end**.
Chaitya roof: **barrel-vaulted**; facade: **horseshoe (chaitya) window**.
**Guntupalli** has "**house viharas**".

nc173ed49342.s: The first structural Hindu temples in Andhra were built under the:
nc173ed49342.x: The first structural Hindu temples came under the Ikshvakus; Satavahana chaitya and vihara forms were the base of later temple architecture.
xa: Oldest stupa in AP → **Bhattiprolu**.
Only rock-cut Buddhist cave temple in AP → **Guntupalli**.
The Amaravati Stupa is on India's **UNESCO tentative list**.

n3f82cce1f5d.s: Which Satavahana ruler enlarged the Amaravati stupa by adding limestone sculptures and a stone railing (vedika)?
n3f82cce1f5d.x: Vasishthiputra Satakarni is credited with enlarging the Amaravati stupa, adding limestone sculptures and a stone railing (APPSC 2001 key). Satakarni I is known for the Naneghat yajnas, Hala for the Gathasaptasati, and Gautamiputra Satakarni for the Nasik prasasti, not for the Amaravati railing.
xs: **Vasishthiputra Satakarni** enlarged Amaravati with **limestone sculptures** and a **stone railing (vedika)** — option **(2)** (APPSC **2001** key).
The notes link **Pulumavi II** (not Satakarni I, Hala or Gautamiputra) to the stupa's construction.
xa: **Acharya Nagarjuna** built its **prakara**; the **Ikshvakus** did the final enlargement.
Origin under **Ashoka's** age: **Mahadeva Bhikshu** and Naga king **Nagashoka**.
Amaravati inscriptions: **Pulumavi II**, "**Nagabu**", the **Chaitika Sangha**.

n4f55ca1906a.s: Colin Mackenzie, associated with the discovery of Amaravati, was the first
o: Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India
n4f55ca1906a.x: Colin Mackenzie is identified as the first Director General of the Survey of India.
n4f55ca1906a.tq: Discriminate between similarly named colonial survey institutions.
xs: **Colin Mackenzie** was the first **Director General of the Survey of India** — option **(4)**.
The trap is the **Archaeological Survey** — the notes say **Survey of India**.
xa: He discovered **Amaravati** in **1797**; relics went to **London and Madras** museums.
Amaravati sculptures now: **British Museum, London**, **Amaravati Museum**, Government Museum, **Chennai**.
**James Fergusson** called them the "**Epitome of Indian architecture**".
n4f55ca1906a.fixed: Mackenzie was the first Surveyor General of India

n208397ab52f.s: Dhanyakataka is the ancient name associated with:
n208397ab52f.x: Dhanyakataka is associated with Amaravati, while Sriparvata and Vijayapuri are ancient names of Nagarjunakonda.
xa: Nagarjunakonda = **Ikshvaku capital**; tutelary deity **Hariti** (APPSC **2012**).
**Aparasaila** sect centre = **Sriparvata**; **Purvasaila** = **Dhanyakataka**.
Other ancient names: **Siddharthaka chaitya** = Guntupalli; **Kantakasala** = Ghantasala.

naf1d6c3f033.s: Nagarjunakonda (Vijayapuri) was the capital of the:
naf1d6c3f033.x: Nagarjunakonda (Vijayapuri) was the Ikshvaku capital, and Ikshvaku queens were major donors to its Buddhist establishments.
xa: The Ikshvaku tutelary deity was **Hariti** (APPSC **2012**).
It has more than **30 stupas**, viharas and apsidal chaityas.
It was submerged by the **Nagarjunasagar dam**; monuments rebuilt as an **island museum**.
Nagarjunakonda was **discovered** by **A.R. Saraswati** (**1926**) and excavated by **Longhurst** (**1927-31**).

na219caeed87.s: At Nagarjunakonda, a special vihara existed for monks from:
na219caeed87.x: A Sinhalese vihara at Nagarjunakonda housed Sri Lankan monks.
xa: Other sects there: **Bahushrutiya, Aparashaila**.
**9 of the 18** sects existed in Andhra; **5 Chaitika** branches of the Mahasanghikas.
Nagarjuna's university drew **SE Asian students**.

n78e6a311069.s: Yajna Sri Satakarni is associated with the construction of a 1,500-room vihara known as the
n78e6a311069.x: Yajna Sri Satakarni built the 1,500-room Sriparvata Sangharama for Acharya Nagarjuna.
n78e6a311069.tq: Combine the exact number, builder and name of the institution.
xs: **Yajna Sri Satakarni** built a **1,500-room vihara**, the **Sriparvata Sangharama**, for **Acharya Nagarjuna** — option **(1)**.
The **Sinhalese vihara** was for Sri Lankan monks — a different building.
xa: Nagarjuna = **Madhyamika**, **Shunyavada**; patron **Yajnasri Satakarni**.
**Yajnasri Satakarni** is also named as donor at **Chinaganjam (Prakasam)**.
**Feb 2026** excavations revealed a massive university complex at Nagarjunakonda.

n89cda87712b.x: A. R. Saraswati discovered Nagarjunakonda in 1926 and Longhurst excavated it in 1927-31; Mackenzie discovered Amaravati in 1797.
xa: **Robert Sewell** excavated Amaravati in **1877**; **Alexander Rea** dug Bhattiprolu in **1892**.
Nagarjunakonda was submerged by the **Nagarjunasagar dam** → now an **island museum**.

nb6f4ed69711.s: What happened to the ancient site of Vijayapuri after the construction of the Nagarjunasagar dam?
o: It was completely destroyed by fire.
It was submerged, and selected monuments were rebuilt on a hilltop.
It was shifted to Amaravati without reconstruction.
It remained entirely in its original location.
nb6f4ed69711.x: Vijayapuri was submerged by the Nagarjunasagar dam, while monuments were rebuilt on a hilltop.
nb6f4ed69711.tq: Apply the cause-and-effect relationship between dam construction and heritage conservation.
xs: Vijayapuri was **submerged** by the **Nagarjunasagar dam**; monuments were **rebuilt on the hilltop** — option **(2)**.
The site is now an **island museum** in the reservoir.
xa: **New finds (Feb 2026):** a massive **university complex**.
Nagarjunakonda had more than **30 stupas**, viharas and apsidal chaityas.
Telangana's **Buddhavanam** theme park (**279** acres) lies at Nagarjuna Sagar across the Krishna.

necc2d5ca2b9.s: Which deity was the tutelary deity of the Ikshvakus of Nagarjunakonda?
necc2d5ca2b9.x: Hariti was the tutelary deity of the Ikshvakus (APPSC 2012 key). Virupakshapati (Shiva) and Mahasena (Kartikeya) were family deities worshipped by Chamtamula, and Vasudeva is a Bhagavata deity of the Naneghat inscription.
xs: **Hariti** was the tutelary deity of the Ikshvakus — option **(2)** (APPSC **2012**).
The notes name no other Ikshvaku tutelary deity; Hariti is the keyed one.
xa: Ikshvaku capital: **Nagarjunakonda** (**Sriparvata / Vijayapuri**).
Golden age of Mahayana under **Virapurushadatta**.
First **structural Hindu temples** in the region came under the Ikshvakus.

n062336d8da0.s: The first Sanskrit inscription of Andhra and South India is found at which monument of Nagarjunakonda?
n062336d8da0.x: The Golden Temple (Swarna Devalayam) at Nagarjunakonda bears the first Sanskrit inscription of Andhra and South India, of Ehuvala Shantamula. The Mahachaitya ayaka-pillar records are in Prakrit; the Sinhala Vihara and amphitheatre are not linked to this first.
n062336d8da0.tq: First Sanskrit inscription = Golden Temple, Ehuvala.
xs: The **Golden Temple** at Nagarjunakonda bears the **first Sanskrit inscription** of Andhra / South India — option **(3)**.
The inscription is of **Ehuvala Shantamula**.
xa: Nagarjunakonda Ayaka inscription: "**Samma Sambhudha Dhatu Parigahita**".
The **Sinhalese vihara** there was for Sri Lankan monks.
Monuments were rebuilt on the hilltop after the **Nagarjunasagar dam**.

n823ad377c67.s: Which Satavahana king is named as a donor at Chinaganjam?
n823ad377c67.x: Yajnasri Satakarni is named as a donor at Chinaganjam; Amaravati records mention Pulumavi II.
xa: **Bhattiprolu** = king **Kubiraka**; **Jaggayyapeta** = **Mandhata sculpture**.
**Ghantasala** = stupa at the port **Kantakossyla**.
**Kondapur** (Telangana) = terracotta figurines, beads, coins.

nbbca18f024d.s: The Buddhist site of Thotlakonda was first spotted through an aerial survey by the:
nbbca18f024d.x: Thotlakonda was spotted by an Indian Navy aerial survey; its 1988-92 digs found stupas and Satavahana and Roman coins.
xa: A new **interpretation centre** opened on **1 March 2026**.
The site shows **rainwater harvesting**.
**Nelakondapalli** has a post-Satavahana mahastupa and a **sculptor's workshop**.

n7e8550b7669.x: Aryadeva, Nagarjuna's disciple, wrote Chittasuddhi Prakaranam; Dinnaga is the father of Buddhist logic.
xa: ⚠ Bhavaviveka's vihara at **Sriparvatam** is the G2 **2019** key; some notes say **Dhanyakataka**.
**Aryasangha** = **Yogachara**; **Maitreyanatha** = **Vijnanavada**.
**Padmasambhava** from Andhra took **Vajrayana** to **Tibet**.

nd5146ba9a47.s: Along with Satavahana officials, which foreign group was among the patrons of the western Deccan rock-cut caves?
nd5146ba9a47.x: Yavana merchants and Satavahana officials were among the patrons; the caves were not supported by monks alone.
xa: **Women donors** dominated: Satavahana **queens** (Gautami Balasri's vihara) and **Ikshvaku queens**.
**Dimikudu**, a leather-worker, was an artisan donor.
"**Tambaya Danamu**" = donation term at a Buddhist site in **Krishna district** (APPSC **2017**).

n99fd6dcc1d9.s: The final and most mature phase of the Amaravati school of art came under the:
n99fd6dcc1d9.x: The Amaravati school flourished from the 2nd century BCE to the 3rd century CE under the Satavahanas, and its most mature phase was under the Ikshvakus.
xa: Ikshvaku phase also used **green stone**.
Influence spread to **Sri Lanka and SE Asia**.
Amaravati is among India's **three major ancient art schools**.

nc4a75156cda.s: In the Buddhist inscriptions of Satavahana-Ikshvaku Andhra, the dominant group of donors was:
nc4a75156cda.x: Women donors dominate the records, above all Satavahana and Ikshvaku queens; merchants, guilds, Yavanas and artisans also donated.
xa: Cave patrons: **Yavana merchants and Satavahana officials** (NextGen CA **2026**).
"**Tambaya Danamu**" is a donation term found at a Buddhist site in **Krishna district** (APPSC **2017**).
**Satavahana queens** patronised **Buddhism**.

n1344802adbe.s: 'House viharas' are a distinctive feature of which Buddhist site in Andhra Pradesh?
n1344802adbe.x: Guntupalli is known for its 'house viharas' among its Buddhist monuments.
xs: "**House viharas**" are a feature of **Guntupalli** — option **(2)**.
**Guntupalli** (Eluru district) is the **only rock-cut Buddhist cave site in Andhra**.
xa: Its chaitya is the **most ancient in Andhra**.
**Siddharthaka chaitya** = **Guntupalli** (G2 **2008** key; some notes say Gudiwada).
**Bhattiprolu** = **oldest stupa in Andhra**; **Amaravati** = largest in AP.

n40bbe44c0c7.s: Which western Deccan site has the largest chaitya hall?
n40bbe44c0c7.x: Karle has the largest chaitya hall; Bhaja has early caves, Nasik viharas with Satavahana inscriptions and Bedsa bell-capital pillars.
xa: **Kanheri** = major Buddhist monastery; **Junnar** = large cave complex.
**Pitalkhora** (Aurangabad) = early chaityas and viharas.
⚠ Some notes call **Karle** the most ancient chaitya, but **Bhaja** is earlier.

nb863f1e2fd5.s: Rock-cut activity associated with the Satavahana period reached its peak in which region?
o: The Sahyadris of the western Deccan
nb863f1e2fd5.x: Rock-cut work peaked in the Sahyadris of the western Deccan, including sites such as Nasik, Naneghat, Karle, Bhaja, Kanheri, Junnar and Ajanta.
nb863f1e2fd5.tq: Link the regional concentration with the representative site cluster.
xs: Satavahana rock-cut work peaked in the **Sahyadris of the western Deccan** — option **(4)**.
Sites: **Nasik, Naneghat, Karle, Bhaja, Kanheri, Junnar, Ajanta**; also Bedsa and Pitalkhora.
xa: **Madhya Pradesh**: **Bagh** cave viharas linked to the Satavahanas.
In Andhra, **Guntupalli** is the only rock-cut Buddhist cave site.
**Ajanta caves 9, 10** = Satavahana-era chaityas with paintings.

n414ba66c644.s: The Satavahana-era Cave 10 chaitya at Ajanta is known for a painting of which Jataka?
n414ba66c644.x: Ajanta Cave 10, a Satavahana-era chaitya, carries the painting of the Shwetagaja (Chhadanta) Jataka (G2 2012). The Vessantara, Mahajanaka and Sibi Jatakas are not linked to this cave.
xs: **Cave 10** carries the **Shwetagaja (Chhadanta) Jataka** painting — option **(2)** (G2 **2012**).
**Ajanta caves 9, 10** are **Satavahana-era chaityas** with paintings of the **Chhadanta / Shwetagaja Jatakas**.
xa: Cave 10 holds the **earliest chaitya** there.
**Ajanta** lies in the **Sahyadris** peak region of Satavahana rock-cut work.
Amaravati themes also used **Jataka panels**.
n414ba66c644.fixed: site missing; Chhaddanta painting is Ajanta Cave 10

nap-history-28-14.s: Which of the following is associated with the patronage of Jainism?
nap-history-28-14.x: Bethanamathya and the early Kakatiya kings patronised Jainism; Satavahana and Ikshvaku queens patronised Buddhism and the Salankayanas were devotees of Chitrarathaswami.
n: Satavahana queens patronised Buddhism. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 39-40]
The Salankayanas patronised Saivism. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 39-40]
Early Kakatiya kings patronised Jainism. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 39-40]
Bethanamathya patronised Jainism. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 39-40]
xa: **Rajaraja** patronised **Nannayabhattu**.
**Veera Bhadra Reddy** patronised **Srinatha**.
**Women donors** dominated Buddhist patronage in Andhra.

n9fe11d0ff80.s: Nagarjuna is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Guntupalli, Buddhist logic and Mahishasaka doctrine
n9fe11d0ff80.x: Nagarjuna was associated with Sriparvata/Nagarjunakonda and is linked with Madhyamika and Shunyavada. Yajnasri Satakarni is mentioned as his patron.
n9fe11d0ff80.tq: Match the acharya with his centre and philosophical school.
xs: **Nagarjuna** = **Sriparvata**, **Madhyamika** and **Shunyavada** — option **(2)**.
**Yogachara** = **Aryasangha**; **Vijnanavada** = **Maitreyanatha**; **Vajrayana** = **Padmasambhava**; **Buddhist logic** = **Dinnaga**.
**Chittasuddhi Prakaranam** is the work of **Aryadeva**, Nagarjuna's disciple.
xa: Patron: **Yajnasri Satakarni** — built the **1,500-room** Sriparvata Sangharama.
Nagarjuna built the **prakara** of the Amaravati stupa.
Nagarjuna's university drew **SE Asian students**.

nbd51218396f.s: Padmasambhava, who hailed from Andhra, took which form of Buddhism to Tibet?
nbd51218396f.x: Padmasambhava took Vajrayana to Tibet; Aryasangha founded Yogachara and Maitreyanatha is associated with Vijnanavada.
xa: **Nagarjuna** = Madhyamika, **Shunyavada**.
**Dinnaga** = father of **Buddhist logic**.
**Aryadeva** (Nagarjuna's disciple) wrote **Chittasuddhi Prakaranam**.

n79b7bbd6ba2.s: The Purvasaila and Aparasaila sects of Andhra Buddhism had their centres respectively at:
n79b7bbd6ba2.x: Purvasaila was centred at Dhanyakataka (Amaravati) and Aparasaila at Sriparvata (Nagarjunakonda). The first option reverses them; Jaggayyapeta is listed for Uttarasaila, Guntupalli for Rajagirika and Gudivada for Siddharthika.
xs: **Purvasaila** was centred at **Dhanyakataka** (Amaravati) and **Aparasaila** at **Sriparvata** (Nagarjunakonda) — option **(2)**.
Option (1) reverses them; **Jaggayyapeta** = **Uttarasaila**, **Gudivada** = **Siddharthika**, **Guntupalli** = Rajagirika (some lists).
xa: These are **5 Chaitika** branches of the **Mahasanghikas**, founded by **Mahadeva Bhikshu**.
**9 of the 18** sects existed in Andhra; **Mahishasakas** = the only Hinayana one.
⚠ G2 **2011** key marked **Uttarasaila-Jaggayyapeta** as the wrong pair — follow the key in the exam.

n36314807859.s: Which Naga king helped build the Amaravati stupa at Dharanikota?
n36314807859.x: Nagashoka helped build the stupa at Dharanikota; Mahadeva Bhikshu, sent by Ashoka, was the first Buddhist teacher in Andhra.
xa: Mahadeva Bhikshu also founded the **Mahasanghika** branches — the **5 Chaitika** sects.
Later phases: **Vasishthiputra Satakarni** (vedika), **Pulumavi II**, final enlargement by the **Ikshvakus**.
Ancient name of Amaravati-Dharanikota = **Dhanyakataka**.

nc4f442bfd5b.s: On the Amaravati stupa sculptures, the leather-worker Dimikudu is shown offering a:
nc4f442bfd5b.x: Dimikudu the leather-worker offers a Purnakumbha; the themes include the Jatakas and the life of the Buddha.
xa: The Amaravati stupa is a **Dhatugarbha** (relic) stupa.
Its inscriptions include **Pulumavi II**'s and the first Telugu word "**Nagabu**".
It was **discovered** by **Col. Colin Mackenzie** in **1797**.

nc44e90f44a7.s: Who featured the Amaravati sculptures in 'Tree and Serpent Worship' and called them the 'Epitome of Indian architecture'?
nc44e90f44a7.x: James Fergusson featured Amaravati in Tree and Serpent Worship and called its sculptures the 'Epitome of Indian architecture'. Colin Mackenzie identified the stupa in 1797, Robert Sewell excavated Amaravati in 1877, and Alexander Rea excavated the Bhattiprolu stupa in 1892.
xs: **James Fergusson** featured Amaravati in **Tree and Serpent Worship** and called it the "**Epitome of Indian architecture**" — option **(3)**.
**Colin Mackenzie** identified Amaravati (**1797**); **Robert Sewell** excavated it (**1877**); **Alexander Rea** dug **Bhattiprolu** (**1892**).
xa: Amaravati sculptures today: **British Museum, London** and the **Amaravati Museum**.
Material of the Amaravati school: **white limestone**; patrons **Satavahanas** and Ikshvakus.
Amaravati is listed among India's **three major ancient art schools**.

nb0a58c68636.s: The sculptor's workshop at Nelakondapalli is associated with which archaeologist?
nb0a58c68636.x: Nelakondapalli has a post-Satavahana mahastupa, Amaravati-style Buddhas and a sculptor's workshop identified with V. V. Krishna Sastry.
xa: **Kondapur** (Telangana) = terracotta figurines, beads, coins.
**Chinaganjam (Prakasam)** = **Yajnasri Satakarni** as donor.
Amaravati school influence spread to **Sri Lanka and SE Asia**.

nc3aa86da66e.s: The five Chaitika branches mentioned in relation to Andhra Buddhism belonged to which larger Buddhist group?
nc3aa86da66e.x: Purvasaila, Aparasaila, Uttarasaila, Rajagirika and Siddharthika were five Chaitika branches of the Mahasanghikas, associated with Mahadeva Bhikshu.
nc3aa86da66e.tq: Identify the parent sect rather than one of its regional branches.
xs: The **5 Chaitika** branches belonged to the **Mahasanghikas** — option **(4)**.
Their founder was **Mahadeva Bhikshu**.
xa: The branches: **Purvasaila** (Dhanyakataka), **Aparasaila** (Sriparvata), **Uttarasaila** (Jaggayyapeta), **Rajagirika**, **Siddharthika** (Gudivada).
**9 of the 18** sects existed in Andhra.
**Mahishasakas** = the **only Hinayana** sect among them.

n99b88970593.s: What is the correct sequence in the depiction of the Buddha in Amaravati sculptural panels?
o: Symbols in the early phase, followed by human form in the later phase
Human form in the early phase, followed by symbols in the later phase
Only royal and animal forms in both phases
n99b88970593.x: The early phase is aniconic, using the Bodhi tree, empty throne, footprints, wheel and stupa; the later phase depicts the Buddha in human form, seated on a lotus with dancing Gandharvas and Yakshas.
n99b88970593.tq: Track the transition from aniconic symbols to anthropomorphic representation.
xs: **Symbols first**, then **human form** — option **(1)**.
**Early phase**: aniconic — **bodhi tree, empty throne, footprints, wheel, stupa**.
**Later phase**: Buddha in **human form** on a lotus with dancing **Gandharvas and Yakshas**.
xa: Symbols: **Birth** = lotus and bull; **Great Departure** = horse; **First sermon** = wheel.
**Mahaparinirvana** = **stupa**; **Enlightenment** = **Bodhi tree**.
These events appear on the **Ayaka slabs**.

nbcbaa1a5507.s: The Sanchi gateway was carved by the ivory carvers of:
nbcbaa1a5507.x: The Sanchi gateway was carved by the ivory carvers of Vidisha; ivory guilds also made donations at Amaravati.
xa: The Amaravati school used **white marble-like limestone**; the Ikshvaku phase also used **green stone**.
Amaravati school period: **2nd century BCE to the 3rd century CE**.
Early phase showed the Buddha only through **symbols**; later phase in **human form**.

n36a96ee8e03.x: Kielhorn identified Sri Parvataswamy as the Buddha.
n36a96ee8e03.tq: Match the inscriptional identification with the correct religious figure.
xs: **Kielhorn** identified "**Sri Parvataswamy**" as **the Buddha** — option **(4)** (APPSC **2019**).
**Hariti** was the Ikshvaku tutelary deity; **Nagarjuna** was the acharya at Sriparvata.
xa: **Sriparvata / Vijayapuri** = ancient names of **Nagarjunakonda**.
**A.R. Saraswati** discovered Nagarjunakonda (**1926**); **Longhurst** excavated it (**1927-31**).
**Yajna Sri Satakarni** built a **1,500-room vihara** there for Nagarjuna.

n13007b80e37.s: The artistic influence of the Amaravati school extended particularly to:
n13007b80e37.x: The Amaravati school influenced Buddhist art in Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia.
n13007b80e37.tq: Test the direction of cultural influence rather than the school’s internal features.
xs: The **Amaravati school** influenced **Sri Lanka and SE Asia** — option **(3)**.
It developed on its own in the **lower Krishna-Godavari valley**, with **indigenous** influence.
xa: Period: **2nd century BCE to the 3rd century CE**, under the **Satavahanas**.
Final, most mature phase under the **Ikshvakus**.
Material: **white marble-like limestone**.

n9f32c54be8e.s: The donation term ‘Tambaya Danamu’ is associated with which of the following?
o: A Brahmanical site in the Guntur district
A Buddhist site in the Visakhapatnam district
A Buddhist site in the Krishna district
A Jain site in the Prakasam district
n9f32c54be8e.x: ‘Tambaya Danamu’ is an inscriptional donation term found at a Buddhist site in the Krishna district.
n9f32c54be8e.tq: Use the precise term and match it with its associated location.
xs: "**Tambaya Danamu**" is a donation term at a **Buddhist site in Krishna district** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2017**; G2 **2017**).
It is not Brahmanical or Jain.
xa: Cave patrons: **Yavana merchants and Satavahana officials**.
Women donors dominated: Satavahana **queens** and **Ikshvaku queens**.
Other donors: **merchants, guilds, Yavanas**, artisans (**Dimikudu**).

n2f10e7dc694.s: Which set of sacrifices is recorded in the Naneghat inscription as having been performed by Satakarni I?
o: Two Rajasuya sacrifices and one Ashvamedha
One Ashvamedha, one Vajapeya and one Rajasuya
n2f10e7dc694.x: The Naneghat inscription records two Ashvamedha sacrifices and one Rajasuya performed by Satakarni I.
n2f10e7dc694.tq: Separate the number and type of sacrifices instead of relying on a general association with Vedic rituals.
xs: Satakarni I performed **two Ashvamedhas and one Rajasuya** — option **(4)**.
The record is the **Naneghat inscription** of **Devi Naganika**.
xa: Other yajna-performing kings: **Satakarni II, Gautamiputra, Yajna Sri**.
Names like **Vedasri** and **Yajnasri** themselves show Vedic faith.
The dynasty patronised both **Brahmanism (Ashvamedha)** and **Buddhism**.

n788d0dd2f52.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about titles in Satavahana inscriptions?
o: Nasik calls Gautamiputra Satakarni Agama nilaya
Naneghat calls Satakarni I Agama nilaya
n788d0dd2f52.x: Agama nilaya (abode of traditional learning) is Gautamiputra's title in the Nasik record, not Satakarni I's in the Naneghat inscription.
xa: ⚠ **Apratihatachakra / Dakshinapathapati** = **Satakarni I**; **Agama nilaya** = **Gautamiputra**.
Gautamiputra's inscriptions carry **Bhagavata symbols**.

n9724c8d3c70.s: In the Naneghat inscription, Vasudeva and Sankarshana are invoked as:
n9724c8d3c70.x: The Naneghat inscription combines Vedic deities such as Indra, Yama and Varuna with the Bhagavata deities Vasudeva and Sankarshana.
xa: Full list invoked: **Indra, Vasudeva, Sankarshana, Surya, Chandra, Yama, Varuna**.
**Bhagavata** religion was founded by **Vasudeva-Krishna**, centred at **Mathura**.
It reached Andhra under **Krishna** (the **2nd** king).

n94dfbf92fa0.s: Under the Satavahanas, Buddhism relied more on:
n94dfbf92fa0.x: Buddhism relied more on public support than on royal support, though queens were notable patrons and kings followed Vedic religion.
xa: Royal women patronised **both Buddhism and Jainism**.
Guilds at **Nasik, Junnar, Kanheri** paid deposit **interest to monks**.
Yajna kings: **Satakarni I, Satakarni II, Gautamiputra, Yajna Sri**.

n11943c29672.s: According to the Kathasaritsagara, Acharya Nagarjuna was killed by a:
n11943c29672.x: Kathasaritsagara states that Nagarjuna was killed by a Satavahana prince, while Lilavati Parinayam mentions his patronage by a Satavahana king.
xa: Patron: **Yajna Sri Satakarni**, to whom the **Suhrullekha** is addressed.
Place: **Sriparvata** (Nagarjunakonda).
Title: "**Second Buddha**".

nc8e4ee6a2b0.s: The religious character of the Satavahana period in Andhra is best described as:
o: Religious pluralism, with both Brahmanism and Buddhism patronised
Absence of public participation in religion
nc8e4ee6a2b0.x: The period shows religious pluralism: Brahmanical rites such as the Ashvamedha alongside Buddhist centres like Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda.
xa: Rule: **kings Vedic, queens Buddhist** (G2 **2008**).
**Prakrit** (people's language) made Buddhism a **mass movement**.
**Yavana merchants** funded caves at Karle, Bhaja, Nasik, Junnar, Kanheri.

n2681670177d.s: Gautami Balasri’s Buddhist patronage included which of the following?
o: A cave vihara at Nasik for the Bhadrayaniya sect
A village at Karle for Mahasanghika monks
A vihara at Sriparvata for Nagarjuna
Toranas at Sanchi for the Chaityaka sect
n2681670177d.x: Gautami Balasri donated a cave vihara at Nasik for the Bhadrayaniya sect, reportedly for the recovery of her son.
n2681670177d.tq: Start from the sure patron–gift pair and distinguish it from the other royal donations.
xs: **Gautami Balasri** gave a **cave vihara at Nasik** for the **Bhadrayaniya** sect — option **(1)**.
She gave it for her **son's recovery**.
**Karle village** = **Pulumavi II**; **Sriparvata vihara** = **Yajna Sri**; **Sanchi toranas** = **Gautamiputra**.
xa: **Krishna** (2nd king) gave a **Nasik cave** for shramanas.
Nasik, Karle and Kanheri caves are in **Maharashtra**.
**Gautamiputra** also gave a village at **Tirasmri** and **100 nivartanas** to monks.

n3b62298f178.s: Who built the Sriparvata vihara for Acharya Nagarjuna?
n3b62298f178.x: The Sriparvata vihara for Nagarjuna was built by Yajna Sri Satakarni; Pulumavi II gave a village to monks at Karle and Krishna gave a Nasik cave.
xa: **Gautamiputra** gave a village at **Tirasmri**, **100 nivartanas**, and the **toranas of Sanchi**.
**Gautami Balasri** gave a **Nasik** cave vihara to the **Bhadrayaniya** sect.

n4c7ab745f0b.s: Guilds at Nasik, Junnar and Kanheri supported monks by:
o: Issuing gold coins exclusively for Buddhist rituals
Compulsorily collecting taxes from villages for monasteries
Replacing monasteries with Vedic sacrificial centres
Holding money on deposit and giving the interest to monks
n4c7ab745f0b.x: Guilds held money on deposit and gave the interest to monks. Ushavadata’s deposit with the Govardhana weavers is an example.
n4c7ab745f0b.tq: Apply the institutional deposit-and-interest mechanism to the stated historical context.
xs: Guilds **held money on deposit** and gave the **interest to monks** — option **(4)**.
Example: **Ushavadata's** deposit with the **Govardhana weavers**.
xa: Guild types among donors: **ivory workers, coral dealers**.
Nasik, Junnar and Kanheri caves are in **Maharashtra**.
Buddhism relied on **public > royal** support.

n9c40c0027dd.s: Sriparvata, associated with Acharya Nagarjuna, is identified with which of the following places?
n9c40c0027dd.x: Sriparvata is identified with Nagarjunakonda. Yajna Sri Satakarni built a vihara or Mahachaitya there for Nagarjuna.
n9c40c0027dd.tq: Distinguish the place associated with Nagarjuna from other Andhra religious centres.
xs: **Sriparvata** = **Nagarjunakonda** — option **(3)**.
**Dhanyakataka** = Mahasanghika centre; **Konakondla** = Kundakunda; **Gudimallam** = Shiva temple.
xa: **Yajna Sri Satakarni** built the **Sriparvata vihara** (**1,500 rooms**) for Nagarjuna.
**Rajagirika** sect centre = **Sriparvatam**.
AP anchors: **Amaravati/Dhanyakataka, Sriparvata, Gudimallam**.

ndbfc68ee1e1.s: The Chaityaka sect founded by Mahadeva Bhikshu was centred on the worship of:
ndbfc68ee1e1.x: Mahadeva Bhikshu, the first Buddhist acharya in Andhra, founded the Chaityaka sect, centred on chaityas as its name shows.
xa: **Mahasanghika** main centre: **Dhanyakataka**; followers called **Mahasanghis / Chaityakas**.
**Rajagirika** = **Sriparvatam** (G2 **2012** key).
**Bhadrayaniya** = **Nasik** (Gautami Balasri's gift).

n9c5f3152c60.s: Which of the following groups consists only of Satavahana rulers associated with the performance of yajnas?
o: Satakarni I, Subendran, Gautamiputra and Hala
Satakarni I, Satakarni II, Gautamiputra and Yajna Sri
Krishna, Pulumavi II, Nagarjuna and Yajna Sri
Satakarni II, Kundakunda, Krishna and Pulumavi II
n9c5f3152c60.x: The rulers associated with yajnas are Satakarni I, Satakarni II, Gautamiputra and Yajna Sri. The names Vedasri and Yajnasri also reflect Vedic religious affiliation.
n9c5f3152c60.tq: Identify the complete ruler group and reject names belonging to other religious or literary contexts.
xs: The yajna-performing kings are **Satakarni I, Satakarni II, Gautamiputra and Yajna Sri** — option **(2)**.
**Subendran** is a king of Tibetan tradition; **Nagarjuna** and **Kundakunda** are acharyas, not kings.
xa: Rule: **kings followed Vedic religion; queens patronised Buddhism** (G2 **2008**).
Names **Vedasri** and **Yajnasri** show Vedic faith.
Satakarni I did **two Ashvamedhas + a Rajasuya**.

n1046c67859b.s: The Parasurameswara temple, associated with the oldest Shivalinga of the Satavahana period, is located at:
n1046c67859b.x: The Parasurameswara temple is at Gudimallam in the present Chittoor, now Tirupati, district, and contains the oldest Shivalinga of the Satavahana period.
n1046c67859b.tq: Use the exact site rather than nearby-place distractors.
xs: The **Parasurameswara temple** is at **Gudimallam** — option **(4)**.
It is in **Chittoor** (now **Tirupati** district) and has the **oldest Shivalinga** of the Satavahana period.
**Thondawada, Renigunta, Jogulamba** are the listed distractors.
xa: Gudimallam is called the **oldest Shiva temple** (G2 **2008**).
The **Gathasaptasati** opens with a prayer to **Shiva**.
Gudimallam is one of the **AP anchors** with Amaravati and Sriparvata.

n96c54d636dd.s: To whom was Nagarjuna's Suhrullekha addressed?
n96c54d636dd.x: Nagarjuna's Suhrullekha ('friendly letter') was addressed to his patron and close friend Yajna Sri Satakarni. Hala and Kuntala Satakarni were other Satavahana kings, and Gunadhya was the author of the Brihatkatha.
n96c54d636dd.tq: Distinguish the addressee of Nagarjuna's work from the patrons of other literary works.
xs: Nagarjuna's **Suhrullekha** ("friendly letter") was addressed to **Yajna Sri Satakarni** — option **(3)**.
Yajna Sri was his **patron and close friend**.
xa: Yajna Sri built the **Sriparvata vihara / Mahachaitya** (**1,500 rooms**) for him.
Other works: **Ratnavali**, **Mulamadhyamakakarika**.
Philosophy: **Madhyamika / Sunyavada** school of Mahayana.

na62d557af37.s: The Jain work Samayasara was written by:
na62d557af37.x: Kundakundacharya, who preached Syadvada, wrote the Samayasara; the Suhrullekha is Nagarjuna's letter to Yajna Sri Satakarni.
xa: Kundakundacharya is linked with **Konakondla (Anantapur)**.
⚠ **Sunyavada** = Nagarjuna; **Syadvada** = Kundakunda.
Nagarjuna's titles: "**Second Buddha**", "**Indian Einstein**", "Indian Martin Luther".
Yajna Sri built the **Sriparvata vihara** (**1,500** rooms) for Nagarjuna.

n78136c07e20.s: Which historian derives the name 'Ikshvaku' from ikshu (sugarcane)?
n78136c07e20.x: B.S.L. Hanumantha Rao links the name Ikshvaku to ikshu, sugarcane.
xa: ⚠ Trap: G2 **2025** marks "their inscriptions call them descendants of the Ikshvakus of Ayodhya" as **incorrect**.
Later **Shakya** descent is also a claim of tradition.
Rule lasted **c. 75 years** (about **AD 225-300**).

nc5aae2135ec.s: Who among the following was the founder of the Ikshvaku dynasty at Vijayapuri?
nc5aae2135ec.x: Vasishthiputra Sri Chamtamula, also called Santamula, founded the Ikshvaku kingdom at Vijayapuri.
nc5aae2135ec.tq: Use the founder–dynasty association and eliminate later rulers.
xs: The founder was **Vasishthiputra Sri Chamtamula** (Santamula) — option **(1)**.
**Virapurushadatta** = golden age of Buddhism; **Ehuvala** = first Sanskrit inscriptions; **Rudrapurushadatta** = last ruler.
xa: Chamtamula was first a **feudatory of the Satavahanas**.
He performed **Ashvamedha, Vajapeya, Agnishtoma, Agnihotra** + **Rajasuya**.
Titles: **Gosatasahasra**, **Halasatasahasra**.

n3649af28bd4.s: Which Ikshvaku ruler is associated with the golden age of Buddhism and the large-scale donations of royal queens?
n3649af28bd4.x: The reign of Virapurushadatta is regarded as the golden age of Buddhism under the Ikshvakus, and his queens were important donors.
n3649af28bd4.tq: Match the ruler with the distinctive contribution rather than with the dynasty generally.
xs: The reign of **Virapurushadatta** was the **golden age of Buddhism**; his **queens were great donors** — option **(2)**.
He issued the **Alluru** and **Nagarjunakonda** inscriptions.
xa: Title: **Sri Parvatadhipati**.
He married **Rudrabhattarika**, princess of **Ujjain** (G2 **2025**); other wives **Bhattidevi**, **Bapisri**.
His son **Ehuvala Chamtamula** was born of **Bhatti Mahadevi**.

n44bcd94b3ef.s: The first Sanskrit inscriptions in the Telugu lands belong to the reign of:
n44bcd94b3ef.x: Ehuvala Chamtamula, son of Virapurushadatta, issued the first Sanskrit inscriptions in the Telugu lands; the Gummadidurru inscription is also his.
xa: Ehuvala's mother: **Bhatti Mahadevi**; he ruled about **24 years**.
Last ruler: **Rudrapurushadatta**.
Royal language otherwise **Prakrit**.

n78ec40c44da.s: An Ashvamedha platform corroborating the Vedic sacrifices of Vasishthiputra Chamtamula has been found at:
n78ec40c44da.x: Chamtamula performed the Ashvamedha, Vajapeya and Rajasuya; the Ashvamedha platform at Nagarjunakonda is the evidence.
xa: Chamtamula's titles: **Gosatasahasra and Halasatasahasra** (giver of lakhs of cows and ploughs).
He tried to make the **intelligentsia partners in agricultural development** (G2 **2012**).
⚠ **Sri Parvatiyas** = Puranic name of the dynasty; **Sri Parvatadhipati** = Virapurushadatta.
Ikshvaku rule lasted **c. 75 years** (about **AD 225-300**).

n52f3de41ea1.s: Who was the last ruler of the Ikshvaku dynasty?
n52f3de41ea1.x: Rudrapurushadatta was the last Ikshvaku ruler. Vasishthiputra Chamtamula was the founder, Virapurushadatta presided over the golden age of Buddhism, and Ehuvala Chamtamula issued the first Sanskrit inscriptions.
xs: The last Ikshvaku ruler was **Rudrapurushadatta** — option **(3)**.
**Vasishthiputra Chamtamula** = founder; **Virapurushadatta** = golden age of Buddhism; **Ehuvala** = first Sanskrit inscriptions.
xa: Rule: **c. 75 years**, about **AD 225-300**.
Puranas list **7 kings**; inscriptions confirm **4**.
Ehuvala ruled about **24 years**.

nc49bbfa1af4.s: Which combination correctly represents the symbol and royal language of the Ikshvakus?
nc49bbfa1af4.x: The lion was the Ikshvaku symbol and Prakrit was their royal language.
nc49bbfa1af4.tq: Start from the sure symbol–language pair and reject swapped cultural attributes.
xs: The Ikshvaku symbol was the **Lion** and the royal language **Prakrit** — option **(2)**.
Yet **Ehuvala Chamtamula** issued the **first Sanskrit inscriptions** in the Telugu lands.
xa: Puranic names: **Sri Parvatiyas**, **Andhrabhrityas**.
Family deities: **Virupakshapati** and **Mahasena**.
Title of Virapurushadatta: **Sri Parvatadhipati**.

nf62ff94ac85.s: Which evidence supports the Andhra origin of the Ikshvakus?
o: Their exclusive dependence on Roman administrators
Their use of only northern royal titles
Southern names and the practice of marrying a maternal uncle’s daughter
Their inscriptions being written only in Sanskrit
nf62ff94ac85.x: Southern names and the southern custom of cross-cousin marriage are cited as evidence supporting the Andhra origin of the Ikshvakus.
nf62ff94ac85.tq: Apply the cultural-evidence approach rather than relying on a dynastic name alone.
xs: **Southern names** and marrying a **maternal uncle's daughter** support Andhra origin — option **(3)**.
Their royal language was **Prakrit**, not only Sanskrit, so option (4) fails.
xa: **Gopalachari** proposed the **Telugu/Andhra** theory (G2 **2011** key).
Tradition links them by name to the **Solar/Rama (Ayodhya)** lineage — not in their own inscriptions.
**Cross-cousin marriage** (maternal uncle's daughter) was practised.

ncbf9db8b961.s: The terms ‘Sri Parvatiyas’ and ‘Andhrabhrityas’ in the Puranic tradition refer to the:
ncbf9db8b961.x: The Puranas refer to the Ikshvakus as Sri Parvatiyas or Sri Parvatiya Andhras and as Andhrabhrityas.
ncbf9db8b961.tq: Discriminate between similar dynastic names by identifying the Puranic designation.
xs: "**Sri Parvatiyas**" (Sri Parvatiya Andhras) and "**Andhrabhrityas**" are **Puranic names** of the **Ikshvakus** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Do not confuse with **Sri Parvatadhipati**, the title of one king, **Virapurushadatta**.
xa: Ikshvaku **symbol** = **lion**; royal language = **Prakrit**.
**Family deities**: **Virupakshapati (Shiva)** and **Mahasena (Kartikeya)**.
Chamtamula's titles: **Gosatasahasra** and **Halasatasahasra** (giver of lakhs of cows and ploughs).

ncbb94f61248.s: Vasishthiputra Chamtamula is particularly associated with which of the following measures for agricultural development?
o: Gifts of land, ploughs, bullocks and cows
Granting ports exclusively to Buddhist monasteries
Distribution of salt, iron and horses
Construction of irrigation dams by Roman engineers
ncbb94f61248.x: Chamtamula attempted to make the intelligentsia partners in agricultural development by giving land, ploughs, bullocks and cows.
ncbb94f61248.tq: Identify the concrete instruments linked with the stated policy objective.
xs: Chamtamula gave **land, ploughs, bullocks and cows** — option **(1)**.
He tried to make the **intelligentsia partners in agricultural development** (G2 **2012**).
xa: Titles to match: **Gosatasahasra** and **Halasatasahasra** — giver of lakhs of cows and ploughs.
He invited **Brahmins from the north**.
The dynasty moved Andhra towards an **agrarian, Puranic order**.

nd3f74ee9998.s: Inscriptions giving dates and the names of sculptors are among the notable firsts of which dynasty?
nd3f74ee9998.x: Dated inscriptions naming sculptors are listed among the Ikshvaku firsts, along with early Hindu temples such as Pushpabhadraswami and Ashtabhuja Narayana at Nagarjunakonda.
xa: Another first: the **first Sanskrit inscription** in the Telugu lands (**Ehuvala**).
Last ruler: **Rudrapurushadatta**.
The dynasty is called a **bridge dynasty**.
nd3f74ee9998.fixed: 'first Hindu temples in India' is false (earlier temples e.g. Besnagar/Nagari); they are the earliest in Andhra

n90559a5e96c.s: Virapurushadatta’s marriage with Rudrabhattarika was politically significant because she was a princess of:
o: Kanchi and linked the Ikshvakus with the Pallavas
Ujjain and linked the Ikshvakus with the Sakas or Western Kshatrapas
Vengi and linked the Ikshvakus with the Eastern Chalukyas
Pataliputra and linked the Ikshvakus with the Mauryas
n90559a5e96c.x: Rudrabhattarika was a princess of Ujjain, and the marriage connected the Ikshvakus with the Sakas or Western Kshatrapas.
n90559a5e96c.tq: Use the marriage alliance to identify both the bride’s origin and its political connection.
xs: **Rudrabhattarika** was the princess of **Ujjain**, tying the Ikshvakus to the **Sakas / Western Kshatrapas** — option **(2)** (G2 **2025**).
**Virapurushadatta's** other wives: **Bhattidevi**, **Bapisri**.
xa: **Cross-cousin marriage** (maternal uncle's daughter) was practised.
His son **Ehuvala Chamtamula** was born of **Bhatti Mahadevi**.
Title of Virapurushadatta: **Sri Parvatadhipati**.

n2521272ddbc.s: Upasika Bodhisri, ranked first among women donors at Nagarjunakonda, was the daughter of Revanta of:
n2521272ddbc.x: Bodhisri was a non-royal donor, the daughter of Revanta of Amaravati; Chamtisri is regarded as the first woman donor.
xa: Bodhisri built the **Sinhala Vihara** (Chuladhammagiri) for foreign monks.
"Woman who served Buddhism most" = **Bodhisiri** (G2 **2018**, **2019**).
Chamtisri restored the **Maha Chaitya** in Virapurushadatta's **6th regnal year** with **9 Ayaka pillars**.
⚠ **Chamtisri** = first woman donor; **Bodhisri** = ranked first among women donors.

n9a39d7b6e72.s: Chamtisri built or restored the Maha Chaitya at Nagarjunakonda in which regnal year of Virapurushadatta?
n9a39d7b6e72.x: Chamtisri, sister of Sri Santamula and paternal aunt of Virapurushadatta, built or restored the Maha Chaitya in his sixth regnal year.
xa: CDI: she built the **Mahavihara** for monk **Bhadanta (Bhagata) Ananda**.
Her inscription prays for Virapurushadatta's **long life, victory and prosperity**.
She gave **170 dinari-masakas**.

ne99dd9657fd.s: The inscriptions of Ikshvaku royal women show that their donations to Buddhism were made:
ne99dd9657fd.x: While the kings were Vedic, queens and royal women were major patrons of Buddhism, and their inscriptions record donations made without male intervention.
xa: First woman donor: **Chamtisri**.
Non-royal donor: **Upasika Bodhisri**.
Merchant's daughter **Rathavasya** built the **Nodageshwara** temple.

n9ebe6f8f6bc.s: In the Ikshvaku economy, Bhaga represented:
n9ebe6f8f6bc.x: Bhaga was the land tax and amounted to one-sixth of the produce.
n9ebe6f8f6bc.tq: Distinguish the exact tax fraction from standard-looking alternatives.
xs: **Bhaga** was the land tax (**revenue**) of **one-sixth (1/6)** of the produce — option **(2)**.
The other fractions (one-tenth, one-fourth, one-half) are not the **Bhaga** rate in the notes.
xa: Farmers were called **Halikas**.
Economy: mainly **agrarian**.
**Brahmadeya** grants were exempt from **18 taxes**.

nc2504c6a743.s: The farmers in Ikshvaku records were known as:
nc2504c6a743.x: Farmers were called Halikas. Telikas, Sale and Kammarus were occupational groups connected with oil pressing, weaving and blacksmithing respectively.
nc2504c6a743.tq: Separate the agrarian term from the occupational guild names.
xs: Farmers were called **Halikas** — option **(1)**.
**Sale** = weavers; **Telika** = oil pressers; **Kammaru** = blacksmiths.
xa: Land tax **Bhaga** = **1/6** of produce.
Guilds were called **Nigamalu** (Negimalu).
**Parnika Sreni** (betel-leaf traders) was the most prominent guild.

n83da713aee3.s: In the Ikshvaku inscriptions, guilds were called:
n83da713aee3.x: Guilds were called Nigamalu; the spelling Negimalu also occurs. They continued the Satavahana sreni tradition.
n83da713aee3.tq: Distinguish the institutional term from occupational and social terms.
xs: Guilds were called **Nigamalu** (also **Negimalu**) — option **(2)**.
They continued the **Satavahana srenis**.
**Varnasankara** = mixing of varnas; **Brahmadeya** = grant to Brahmins; **Halikas** = farmers.
xa: **Parnika Sreni** = betel-leaf traders (most prominent).
**Poosika Sreni** = sweetmeat traders.
**Nagarjunakonda** was home to merchants and artisans in guilds.

n4fbbac6dfc1.s: Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula brought Brahmins from which region and granted them what kind of land grants?
n4fbbac6dfc1.x: Santamula brought Brahmins from the north and granted them agraharas.
n4fbbac6dfc1.tq: Pair the person with both the direction and the specific grant to avoid location–institution swaps.
xs: Santamula brought **Brahmins from the north** and gave them **agraharas** — option **(1)**.
Brahmins also rose through **Brahmadeya** grants (exempt from **18 taxes**).
xa: The period moved Andhra to an **agrarian, agrahara-based** early medieval order.
Revenue also went to **poets + scholars** and **gifts to religious bodies**.
Preventing **Varnasankara** was the king's duty.

nab247808c4f.s: Which Ikshvaku ruler performed the Ashvamedha, Vajapeya and Agnistoma sacrifices?
nab247808c4f.x: Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula performed the Ashvamedha, Vajapeya and Agnistoma; an Ashvamedha altar has been found at Nagarjunakonda.
xa: Titles: **Goshatasahasra Halashatasahasra**, **Mahadanapati**.
He brought **Brahmins from the north** with **agraharas**.
Romans were said to have built a **stadium** under him.

n64aca5a1b76.s: According to the recorded four-way division of state revenue, which one of the following was NOT one of the specified major allocations?
n64aca5a1b76.x: The four specified allocations were administration and army, temples and festivals, poets and scholars, and gifts to religious bodies. Expansion of overseas colonies was not listed; some revenue also went to tanks and canals.
n64aca5a1b76.tq: Find the option outside the four stated revenue heads rather than choosing a merely less familiar allocation.
xs: **Expansion of overseas colonies** was not an allocation — option **(1)**.
The **four** shares: **administration + army**, **temples + festivals**, **poets + scholars**, **gifts to religious bodies**.
xa: Some revenue also went to **tanks and canals**.
Land tax **Bhaga** = **1/6** of produce.
Economy: mainly **agrarian**.

n9cfd32acbe2.s: Which of the following provides evidence of Roman contact with the Ikshvaku region?
o: Roman gold and silver coins at Nagarjunakonda and a Roman-style amphitheatre at Vijayapuri
Roman ships engraved at Amaravati and Persian coins at Ujjain
Latin manuscripts at Guntur and Roman pillars at Sopara
Roman inscriptions at Motupalli and Greek temples at Ghantasala
n9cfd32acbe2.x: Roman gold and silver coins found at Nagarjunakonda and a Roman-style amphitheatre at Vijayapuri indicate foreign contact. Romans were said to have built a stadium under Sri Santamula.
n9cfd32acbe2.tq: Combine two independent archaeological indicators of foreign contact.
xs: **Roman gold and silver coins** at Nagarjunakonda and a **Roman-style amphitheatre** at Vijayapuri — option **(1)**.
Romans were said to have built a **stadium under Sri Santamula**.
xa: Ports: **Motupalli and Ghantasala**; also **Maisolia (Machilipatnam)**.
Exports: **spices, iron, coconuts, cotton textiles**.
Roman trade was **lower than under the Satavahanas**.

n3a1b830ea14.s: Which of the following was an export from the Ikshvaku region?
n3a1b830ea14.x: Exports included spices, iron, coconuts and cotton textiles. Gold, silver, wine and glassware were imported.
n3a1b830ea14.tq: Separate export items from the paired import list.
xs: **Spices** were exported — option **(4)**.
**Gold, wine, glassware** (and silver) were **imports**.
xa: Other exports: **iron, coconuts, cotton textiles**.
Roman trade was **lower than under the Satavahanas**.
Ports: **Motupalli, Ghantasala**.

n1214eaf273c.s: Ikshvaku coins were mainly made of:
n1214eaf273c.x: Ikshvaku coins were of lead and copper and bore the Ujjain symbol, the elephant and the lion; they are found in Guntur, Krishna and Godavari districts.
xa: Ujjain link: **Rudradhara Bhattarika**, daughter of Kshatrapa **Rudrasena of Ujjain**.
**Roman gold and silver coins** also turn up at Nagarjunakonda.

n8156281534b.s: Under the Ikshvakus, which varna constituted the majority of society?
n8156281534b.x: Shudras were the majority under the Ikshvakus, while Brahmins benefited from Brahmadeya grants and a new landlord class emerged.
xa: Local clans: **Pugiya, Hiranyaka, Munda, Dhanika**, Nagulu.
**Sati (sahagamana)** was practised.
Kings used **matronymics** (Vasishthiputra).

nb69aab8831f.s: Ikshvaku marriage alliances linked them with the Kshatrapas of Ujjain and the:
nb69aab8831f.x: Ikshvaku marriage alliances linked them with the Kshatrapas of Ujjain and the Chutus; cross-cousin marriage also began with them.
xa: Queen **Rudradhara Bhattarika** was daughter of Kshatrapa **Rudrasena of Ujjain**.
**Sati (sahagamana)** was practised.
Children were named after the **grandfather** (Ehuvala Santamula).

n129fdb5213a.s: The naming of Ehuvala Santamula after his grandfather is a social practice recorded in the inscriptions of the:
n129fdb5213a.x: Ikshvaku inscriptions record names derived from the grandfather (Ehuvala Santamula), matronymics such as Vasishthiputra, and sati.
xa: **Cross-cousin marriage** (maternal uncle's daughter) began with them.
Women's general status **declined**, but royal women kept religious and economic agency.
Preventing **Varnasankara** was the king's duty.

n2bc5eca95db.s: Which Ikshvaku king granted agraharas to Brahmins from the north?
n2bc5eca95db.x: Sri Santamula worshipped Virupakshapati and Mahasena and granted agraharas to northern Brahmins.
xa: Ehuvala's mother **Bhatti Mahadevi** is linked to the Bahushrutiya vihara.
**Rudrapurushadatta's** presiding deity was **Mahasena**.
⚠ **Hariti** = tutelary deity; **Virupakshapati / Mahasena** = deities the kings worshipped.

nd2b71f420ea.s: Which Ikshvaku ruler was described by the titles ‘Ashoka of the South’ and ‘Sri Parvatadhipati’?
nd2b71f420ea.x: Virapurushadatta bore the titles ‘Ashoka of the South’ and ‘Sri Parvatadhipati’.
nd2b71f420ea.tq: Match the ruler with the distinctive titles rather than with a religious act.
xs: **Virapurushadatta** bore the titles "**Ashoka of the South**" and "**Sri Parvatadhipati**" — option **(2)**.
He was the **only Ikshvaku king to adopt Buddhism**.
xa: His reign = **golden age of Buddhism**; greatest patronage (G2 **2008**).
He rebuilt the **Maha Chaitya** under **Acharya Bhadanta Ananda**.
Some notes credit him with the **Sriparvata University**.

n5fa0a940e5c.s: Ehuvala Santamula built a vihara in his mother's name for which Buddhist sect?
n5fa0a940e5c.x: Ehuvala Santamula, who revived Brahmanism, also continued Buddhist patronage by building a vihara for the Bahushrutiyas in his mother's name.
xa: **Upasika Bodhisri** served Buddhism in his reign (G2 **2012**).
His commander **Elisri** built the **Sarvadeva** shrine (Kartikeya).
He completed the **Pushpabhadraswami** shrine.

n9346a036456.s: Which religious feature is specifically associated with the reign of Rudrapurushadatta?
o: The beginning of the custom of erecting chhaya-stambhas near graves
The rebuilding of the Maha Chaitya
The first construction of Hindu temples
The issue of the first Sanskrit inscriptions
n9346a036456.x: The custom of erecting chhaya-stambhas, or shadow pillars, near graves began during the reign of Rudrapurushadatta.
n9346a036456.tq: Identify the ruler by a distinctive custom rather than by a broad religious label.
xs: **Chhaya-stambhas** (shadow pillars) near graves began under **Rudrapurushadatta** — option **(1)**.
Maha Chaitya rebuilding = **Virapurushadatta**; first Hindu temples and Sanskrit inscriptions = **Ehuvala**.
xa: Rudrapurushadatta was the **last** Ikshvaku king and **Vedic**.
His presiding deity was **Mahasena**.
The Ikshvakus = **last royal Buddhist zenith** in Andhra.

n533d9d4426e.s: Sriparvata is identified with which place and is also known by which traditional name?
n533d9d4426e.x: Sriparvata is identified with Nagarjunakonda, or Vijayapuri, and is traditionally called Dakshina Gaya.
xs: **Sriparvata** = **Nagarjunakonda (Vijayapuri)**, called "**Dakshina Gaya**" — option **(2)**.
It was sacred to **Mahayana**.
xa: It was named after **Acharya Nagarjuna**.
Comparison: **Bodh Gaya** = Hinayana; **Sriparvata** = Mahayana.
⚠ **Sriparvataswami** (Vishnukundin deity) = **Srisaila Mallikarjuna** — a different place.

n095781a89b8.s: Hiuen Tsang, who travelled in the seventh century, found the Sriparvata vihara in which condition?
n095781a89b8.x: Hiuen Tsang found the Sriparvata vihara neglected during his seventh-century visit.
xs: **Hiuen Tsang** (**7th c.**) found the **Sriparvata vihara neglected** — option **(3)**.
⚠ He is a trap for the **Suhrllekha** question — that was **Itsing**.
xa: **Itsing (c. 700 CE)** saw students memorising Nagarjuna's **Suhrllekha** (G2 **2012**).
Sriparvata = **Nagarjunakonda (Vijayapuri)**.
**Virapurushadatta** set up the **Sriparvata University**.

n3f9814571b8.s: Which Chinese traveller saw Indian students memorising Nagarjuna's Suhrllekha, the letter to Yajnasri Satakarni?
n3f9814571b8.x: Itsing (c. 700 CE) recorded Indian students memorising the Suhrllekha (G2 2012). Fahien and Hiuen Tsang are the trap options; Hiuen Tsang instead found the Sriparvata vihara neglected. Sung Yun is not associated with this account.
xs: **Itsing** (**c. 700 CE**) saw students memorising the **Suhrllekha** — option **(3)** (G2 **2012**).
**Fahien** and **Hiuen Tsang** are the traps; Hiuen Tsang found the Sriparvata vihara **neglected**.
xa: The **Suhrllekha** is Nagarjuna's letter to **Yajnasri Satakarni**.
Nagarjuna = **Madhyamika** philosopher.
**Yajnasri Satakarni** built viharas and chaityas at Sri Parvatam.

n200c32d7ee5.s: The Ceylonese monks who came to Nagarjunakonda are associated with which description?
o: They established the first Brahmanical temple at Nagarjunakonda.
They made Nagarjunakonda a base for Mahayana only.
They introduced Vedic sacrifices into the Ikshvaku court.
They made Nagarjunakonda their base for Hinayana.
n200c32d7ee5.x: Ceylonese monks made Nagarjunakonda their base for Hinayana, strengthening the Sri Lankan Buddhist connection.
n200c32d7ee5.tq: Distinguish the Buddhist doctrinal affiliation from the site-based association.
xs: Ceylonese monks made Nagarjunakonda their **Hinayana** base — option **(4)**.
They lived in **Bodhisri's Sinhala Vihara** (Chuladhammagiri), of the **Mahaviharavasin** (Theravada) school.
xa: Bodhisri also built viharas for monks from **Kashmir, China, Gandhara**.
**Mahadeva Bhikshu** took Buddhism to **Sri Lanka** (Mahavamsa).
⚠ **Sriparvata** itself was sacred to **Mahayana**.

n02fdae7ec00.s: Bodh Gaya and Sriparvata are respectively associated with which Buddhist traditions?
n02fdae7ec00.x: Bodh Gaya is associated with Hinayana, while Sriparvata is associated with Mahayana.
n02fdae7ec00.tq: Reversed-comparison trap between two Buddhist centres.
xs: **Bodh Gaya** = **Hinayana**; **Sriparvata** = **Mahayana** — option **(3)**.
Option (1) reverses the pair.
xa: Sriparvata = "**Dakshina Gaya**".
Sriparvata = **Nagarjunakonda (Vijayapuri)**, named after **Nagarjuna**.
Ceylonese monks used Nagarjunakonda as a **Hinayana** base.

n97337a33aa2.s: Bodhisri's Sinhala Vihara at Nagarjunakonda belonged to which sect?
n97337a33aa2.x: Bodhisri's Sinhala Vihara belonged to the Mahaviharavasins; the Maha Chaitya was Aparamahavinaseliya and Kodabalisri's vihara Mahishasaka.
xa: Nagarjunakonda was the **Aparamahavinaseliya (Aparasaila)** sect's main centre.
The Sinhala Vihara served **Sri Lankan (Tambapanni)** monks.
Maha Chaitya donors: **Chamtisri, Harmyasri**.

nf4185216669.s: Which one of the following was NOT identified as a Mahasanghika branch or related sect in the Nagarjunakonda religious context?
nf4185216669.x: Purvasailiya, Rajagirika and Siddharthika were among the Mahasanghika branches or related sects named. Mahaviharavasin was the Theravada tradition associated with the Sinhala Vihara.
nf4185216669.tq: Separate the Mahasanghika-related names from the Sri Lankan Theravada designation.
xs: **Mahaviharavasin** is the **Theravada** sect of the **Sinhala Vihara**, not a Mahasanghika branch — option **(4)**.
**Purvasailiya** is a Mahasanghika branch; **Rajagirika** and **Siddharthika** are among the related sects named.
xa: **Aparasailiya** and **Bahushrutiya** are also Mahasanghika branches.
**Nikaya** sect chanted the Nikayas as mantras.
Ceylonese monks made Nagarjunakonda their **Hinayana** base.

n35bb409bef6.s: Bodhisri built a stone mandapa at the eastern gateway of the Maha Chaitya at Kantakasala, identified with:
n35bb409bef6.x: Kantakasala is identified with Ghantasala. Bodhisri built a stone mandapa at the eastern gateway of the Maha Chaitya there and another opposite the Paravata Vihara.
n35bb409bef6.tq: Resolve the ancient-place and modern-place identification pair.
xs: **Kantakasala** = **Ghantasala** — option **(1)**.
**Bodhisri** built a stone mandapa at the **eastern gateway** of the Maha Chaitya there.
xa: She built another mandapa opposite the **Paravata Vihara**.
Her **Sinhala Vihara** stood at **Chuladhammagiri**.
She built **seven viharas at Papili**.

n11d0d4581d4.s: The Maha Chaitya at Nagarjunakonda was primarily a:
o: Dhatugarbha stupa containing the Buddha's bodily relics
Memorial pillar erected near a grave
n11d0d4581d4.x: The Maha Chaitya was a Dhatugarbha, or relic stupa, built over the Buddha's bodily relics.
n11d0d4581d4.tq: Identify the monument by its defining function rather than by its location alone.
xs: The Maha Chaitya was a **Dhatugarbha (relic) stupa** over the **Buddha's bodily relics** — option **(2)**.
Its Prakrit inscription: "**Samma Sambudhasa dhatuvara parigahita**" ("enshrining the excellent relics of the Buddha").
xa: Built by **Chamtisri** in Virapurushadatta's **6th year** with **9 Ayaka pillars**.
**Chhaya-stambhas** near graves are a different, later custom (Rudrapurushadatta).
Pillar donors include **Adavi Chamtisri, Harmyasri, Bapisri, Rudrabhattarika**.

n5af19849967.s: The Paravata Mahachaitya, later rebuilt by Chamtisri, had earlier been built for Acharya Nagarjuna by:
n5af19849967.x: The earlier Paravata Mahachaitya was built by Yajnasri Satakarni for Acharya Nagarjuna; Chamtisri rebuilt it in Virapurushadatta's sixth year with nine Ayaka pillars.
xa: Pillar inscriptions: **Chamtisri, Adavi Chamtisri, Harmyasri, Chathasri, Bapisri, Chatisri, Rudrabhattarika**.
**Virapurushadatta** rebuilt it under **Acharya Bhadanta Ananda**.
Type: **Dhatugarbha** stupa.

n167f21db7da.s: Upasika Bodhisri built seven viharas at:
n167f21db7da.x: Bodhisri built seven viharas at Papili and viharas for monks from Sinhala, Kashmir, China and Gandhara.
xa: Countries receiving the Dhamma: **Kashmir, Gandhara, China, Chila(ta), Tosali, Aparanta, Vanga, Vanavasi, Yavana, Damila, Palura**.
Ceylonese monks made Nagarjunakonda their **Hinayana** base.

n00c42f24304.s: The Pushpabhadraswami shrine at Nagarjunakonda followed which plan?
n00c42f24304.x: The Shaiva Pushpabhadraswami shrine had a Gajaprishtha or elephant-back plan; it was begun by Virapurushadatta and completed by Ehuvala.
xa: ⚠ CDI lists it under **Vishnu**.
**9 Shaiva temples + 1 Vaishnava** at Nagarjunakonda.
**Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami** = the Vaishnava one.

n744b035ac5e.s: The Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami temple at Nagarjunakonda was built by Shivasena, commander of the Abhira king:
n744b035ac5e.x: Shivasena, commander of the Abhira king Vasusena, built the Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami, the first Vaishnava temple in Andhra.
xa: **Pushpabhadraswami** temple was constructed by **Virapurushadatta** and completed by **Ehuvala**.
**Sarvadevadhivasam** was built by **Elisri**, commander of Ehuvala, for **Kumara Swami (Kartikeya)**; its inscription is in **Sanskrit**.
Temple count at Nagarjunakonda: **9 Shaiva temples + 1 Vaishnava temple**.
⚠ **Hariti** was the **tutelary deity of the Ikshvakus**; **Virupakshapati / Mahasena** were deities the kings worshipped.

na0c185edbe2.s: The last royal Buddhist zenith in Andhra was under the:
na0c185edbe2.x: The Ikshvakus represented the last royal Buddhist zenith in Andhra; their period also saw the first Vaishnava temple, Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami.
xa: Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami was built by **Shivasena**.
Golden age of Buddhism: **Virapurushadatta**.
Ikshvakus built **India's first structural Hindu temples**.

nap-history-6-18.s: The Harati, Mahajana, Kumara Swami and Pushpabhadra Swami temples were discovered in the excavations at:
nap-history-6-18.x: Harati, Mahajana, Kumara Swami, Pushpabhadra Swami and Ashtabhuja Narayana Swami are temples found in the Nagarjunakonda excavations.
n: Harati is one of the temples discovered in the Nagarjunakonda excavations. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
Mahajana is one of the temples discovered in the Nagarjunakonda excavations. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
Kumara Swami is one of the temples discovered in the Nagarjunakonda excavations. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
Pushpabhadra Swami is one of the temples discovered in the Nagarjunakonda excavations. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
Ashtabhoji Narayana Swami is one of the temples discovered in the Nagarjunakonda excavations. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
xa: The Ikshvakus built **India's first structural Hindu temples**.
**Hariti (Harati)** was the **tutelary deity of the Ikshvakus** — a goddess who **protected children**; women offered **bangles** at her shrine.
**Shakti worship began** with the installation of Hariti's image.
Vishnu was worshipped as **Narasimha** (Nemalipuri slab).
Inscriptions of **Vasisthiputra Santamula** were found in the **Rentala and Kesavapath temples** near Nagarjuna Konda.

nap-history-7-17.s: Who was the tutelary deity of the Ikshvakus?
nap-history-7-17.x: Hariti was the tutelary deity of the Ikshvakus; Kumara Swami was the deity of commander Elisiri's temple.
n: Hariti was the tutelary deity of the Ikshvakus. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 12-13]
The Pushpa Bhadra Swami temple was constructed by Virapurushadatta. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 12-13]
Kumara Swami was associated with the Ikshvakus. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 12-13]
Elisiri was a commander of the Ikshvakus. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 12-13]
The temple of Ashtabhuja Narayana was located at Nagarjuna Konda. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 12-13]
xa: Elisiri's **Sarvadevadhivasam** inscription is in **Sanskrit**.
Pushpabhadraswami followed the **Gajaprishtha** (elephant-back) plan.
Ashtabhuja Narayana was built by **Shivasena**, commander of Abhira king **Vasusena** — the **first Vaishnava temple** in Andhra.
**Hariti** was also a mother goddess of the **Early Chalukyas**.

ne230abcd224.s: Sriparvataswami, the family deity of the Vishnukundins, is identified with:
ne230abcd224.x: Sriparvataswami, the family deity of the Vishnukundins, is identified with Srisaila Mallikarjuna.
xa: ⚠ A one-liner credits **N. Venkataramanayya** — the key says Kielhorn.
**Sriparvata** itself = Nagarjunakonda, "**Dakshina Gaya**".
ne230abcd224.fixed: y51506655ca1 key: N. Venkata Ramanaiah identified Sriparvata Swamy with Buddha, not Kielhorn

n6443f279d1d.s:
Which of the following flourished under the Ikshvakus?
1. Puranic Shaivism
2. Vaishnavism
3. Shakti worship
Select the correct answer:
n6443f279d1d.x: Puranic Shaivism, Vaishnavism and Shakti worship all flourished under the Ikshvakus.
xa: Deities: **Skanda (Kartikeya), Ganapati, Yakshas, Hariti**.
Vishnu worshipped as **Narasimha** (**Nemalipuri** slab).
Ikshvakus built **India's first structural Hindu temples**.

n8406c1e2b06.s: The installation of the image of Hariti in the Ikshvaku period marks the beginning of:
n8406c1e2b06.x: Hariti, tutelary deity of the Ikshvakus and protector of children, marks the beginning of Shakti worship, not Vaishnava worship.
xa: She is the mother goddess of children (**Saptamatrika** shrine).
First **Vaishnava** temple = **Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami**.

nba18efe93ea.s: Besides one Vaishnava temple, how many Shaiva temples stood at Nagarjunakonda?
nba18efe93ea.x: Nine Shaiva temples and one Vaishnava temple (Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami) stood at Nagarjunakonda.
xa: **Ehuvala Santamula** was the first king to build Hindu temples.
Minor shrines: **Nodageshwara, Nandikeshwara, Navagraha, Kubera**.

nap-history-7-15.s: The Pedavegi inscription recording a land grant to Vishnu belongs to the Salankayana king:
nap-history-7-15.x: The Pedavegi inscription of the Salankayana king Nandivarman II records a land grant to Vishnu.
n: The Pushpa Bhadra Swami temple was constructed by Virapurushadatta. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 12-13]
Vishnu was associated with the Salankayanas. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 12-13]
A land grant to Vishnu was mentioned in the Pedavegi inscription. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 12-13]
Nandi Varma-II was associated with the Pedavegi inscription. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 12-13]
xa: The Salankayanas followed **Vaishnavism**; capital **Vengi (Pedavegi, Eluru dt)**.
Their **family deity** was **Chitraratha Swamy** (the **Sun**).
They called themselves devotees of **Bappa Bhattaraka**.
⚠ **Pedavegi** = Salankayana record; **Pushpa Bhadra Swami** = Ikshvaku temple at Nagarjuna Konda.

nap-history-7-3.s: The Salankayanas called themselves devotees of Bappa Bhattaraka, a term meaning:
nap-history-7-3.x: The Salankayanas were devotees of Bappa Bhattaraka, a term meaning consideration of the father as God.
n: Bappa Bhattaraka was associated with the Salankayanas. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 12-13]
Bappa Bhattaraka means consideration of father as God. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 12-13]
The Salankayanas declared themselves devotees of Bappa Bhattaraka. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 12-13]
xa: The **family deity** of the Salankayanas was **Chitraratha Swamy**, meaning the **Sun**.
A **land grant to Vishnu** is recorded in the **Pedavegi inscription** of **Nandi Varma-II**.
Salankayana capital: **Vengi (Pedavegi, Eluru dt)**; they followed **Vaishnavism**.
**Sriparvata Swamy** was the family deity of the **Vishnukundins**.

nap-history-7-9.s: Chitraratha Swamy, the family deity of the Salankayanas, means which of the following?
nap-history-7-9.x: Chitraratha Swamy, the family deity of the Salankayanas, means the Sun god.
nap-history-7-9.tq: Recall the meaning of each family deity.
n: Chitraratha Swamy means Sun. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 12-13]
xs: **Chitraratha Swamy**, the family deity of the **Salankayanas**, means the **Sun** — option **(2)**.
**Vishnu** received a land grant from the Salankayanas (Pedavegi inscription), but he is not Chitraratha Swamy.
**Buddha** is linked to **Sriparvata Swamy** of the Vishnukundins; the **mother goddess** is **Hariti**.
xa: The Salankayanas **declared themselves devotees** of **Bappa Bhattaraka** — **father as God**.
The Salankayanas followed **Vaishnavism**; capital **Vengi (Pedavegi, Eluru dt)**.
**Pedavegi inscription** — land grant to **Vishnu** by **Nandi Varma-II**.
Salankayanas were conquered by Vishnukundin **Madhava Varma II**.

nca00aa38928.s: The Mandhata sculpture, the first depiction of a Chakravarti in Indian art, is found at:
nca00aa38928.x: The Mandhata sculpture at Jaggayyapeta, the most important Ikshvaku sculpture, is the first depiction of a Chakravarti.
xa: Carving sculptors' names started the **"Sculptor's Style"** (e.g. **Badantacharya** at the Mahavihara).
Nagarjunakonda was the main centre of the **Amaravati School**, which reached its **final, most mature phase** under the Ikshvakus.
Ikshvaku FIRSTs: first **Sanskrit inscription in South India**, first **structural Hindu temples**, first **sculptor signatures**.
The Buddha appears in **human form** in this later phase.

n384bb8e0660.s: Which development is associated with the practice of carving sculptors' names at Nagarjunakonda?
o: Beginning of royal portraiture in India
