n384bb8e0660.x: The carving of sculptors' names is associated with the beginning of the Sculptor's Style; Badantacharya at the Mahavihara is an example.
n384bb8e0660.tq: Link an artistic practice with its historical consequence.
xs: Carving sculptors' names began the "**Sculptor's Style**" — option **(4)**.
Example: **Badantacharya** at the **Mahavihara**.
xa: This is listed as the Ikshvakus' **first sculptor signatures**.
Other FIRSTs: **first Sanskrit inscription** in South India; **first structural Hindu temples**.
**Mandhata** sculpture = first **Chakravarti** depiction.

n6d184ad3282.s: The Ikshvakus are regarded as having laid the foundation of which temple architecture?
n6d184ad3282.x: The Ikshvakus laid the base of Dravida temple architecture.
xa: Agamic parts: **garbhagudi, antarala, mantapa, dhvajastambha, prakara**.
**Pushpabhadraswami** = **Gajaprishtha** plan.
The **Amaravati school** was at its peak under them.

nap-history-23-18.s: The Mandhata sculpture was discovered at which place?
nap-history-23-18.x: The Mandhata (Chakravarti Mandhata) sculpture was discovered at Jaggayyapet, a Buddhist stupa site in the Krishna valley.
nap-history-23-18.tq: Recall the find-spot of the Mandhata panel.
n: A Mandhata sculpture was discovered in Jaggayyapet. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 32-33]
xs: The **Mandhata sculpture** was discovered at **Jaggayyapet** — option **(3)**.
It is the **most important Ikshvaku sculpture** and the **first depiction of a Chakravarti** in Indian art.
The same Jaggayyapet finds list **Harati, Mahajana, Kumara Swami, Pushpabhadra Swami, Ashtabhoji Narayana Swami** sculptures.
xa: The **Sati** panel is the **first depiction of sati** in Indian art.
**Viragallu (hero stones)** also began under the Ikshvakus.
Themes: scenes from the **Buddha's life and Jataka stories** on panels.
**Early Ikshvaku style** — **low relief**, the "last flicker" of the Satavahana Amaravati tradition.

ne00334b5cfc.s: Nagarjunakonda was a main centre of which school of sculpture?
ne00334b5cfc.x: Nagarjunakonda was a main centre of the Amaravati School, which reached its final, mature phase with Mahayana themes under the Ikshvakus.
xa: Panels show the **Buddha's life and Jataka stories**.
Early Ikshvaku style = "**last flicker**" of the Satavahana Amaravati tradition.

nd9314b15ab5.s: Early Ikshvaku carving is called the 'last flicker' of which tradition?
nd9314b15ab5.x: Early Ikshvaku carving, with less stylisation and low relief, is called the 'last flicker' of the Satavahana Amaravati tradition.
xa: The Amaravati School reached its **final, most mature phase** under the Ikshvakus.
The **Mandhata sculpture, Jaggayyapeta** = the most important Ikshvaku sculpture.
Sculptors' names carved → the "**Sculptor's Style**".

n79c6ca08531.s: The major stupas at Nagarjunakonda were built on which plan?
n79c6ca08531.x: The major stupas at Nagarjunakonda had a wheel-shaped, spoked plan with Ayaka platforms in the four directions.
xa: **Apsidal** plans belong to the **chaityas** and the **Pushpabhadraswami** temple.
More than **30 stupas** were excavated.
The **Maha Chaitya** = **Dhatugarbha** stupa.

n1a05d14422c.x: Ayaka platforms belong to stupas; the Agamic temple plan has garbhagudi, antarala, mantapa, dhvajastambha and prakara.
xa: **Pushpabhadraswami** temple = **Gajaprishtha** (apsidal, elephant-back) plan.
Ayaka platforms stand in the **four directions** of big stupas.
Ikshvakus built the **first structural Hindu temples**.

n4806c042680.s: The amphitheatre or Kreeda Vedi at Vijayapuri is notable because it was:
o: A water tank used for ritual bathing
A sports arena thought to have been built with Roman help
A temple exclusively following the Agamas
A royal residence found throughout South India
n4806c042680.x: The Kreeda Vedi was a sports arena, thought to have been built with Roman assistance, and it has been described as having no parallel elsewhere in India.
n4806c042680.tq: Identify the structure from its purpose and foreign association.
xs: The **Amphitheatre (Kreeda Vedi)** was a **sports arena** thought to be built with **Roman** help — option **(2)**.
It is **found nowhere else in India**.
xa: **Kummakundam** = water tanks / bathing pools.
**Rajaprasadam** = palace complex with **prakaras**.
**Acoustic building** = the site's most unique find.

n3bd3dd6a8c5.s: Which secular structure at Vijayapuri was designed according to principles of sound and regarded as the site's most unique find?
n3bd3dd6a8c5.x: The acoustic building was designed on principles of sound and is regarded as the most unique find at the site.
n3bd3dd6a8c5.tq: Use the unusual functional feature to identify the structure.
xs: The **Acoustic building**, designed on principles of sound, is the site's **most unique find** — option **(3)**.
**Kummakundam** = tanks; **Ashvamedha altar** = Vedic sacrifice; **Rajaprasadam** = palace.
xa: **Amphitheatre (Kreeda Vedi)**: built with **Roman** help, found nowhere else in India.
**Yeleswaram** = town credited to commander **Elisri**.
The **1954-60** dig uncovered the **palace complex**.

ne2a938abe70.x: Kummakundam denotes water tanks or bathing pools excavated at Vijayapuri.
ne2a938abe70.tq: Distinguish a utilitarian structure from nearby monumental remains.
xs: **Kummakundam** = **water tanks / bathing pools** — option **(1)**.
**Sports stands** = the **Amphitheatre (Kreeda Vedi)**; **palace** = **Rajaprasadam**.
xa: **Acoustic building** = designed on principles of sound.
**Ashvamedha altar** of Santamula = proof of Vedic sacrifice.
**Yeleswaram** = town of commander **Elisri**.

nccc8280769b.s: The earliest Sanskrit inscription of Andhra and South India is associated with the:
nccc8280769b.x: The earliest Sanskrit inscription of Andhra and South India is at the Swarna Devalayam, or Golden Temple, at Nagarjunakonda.
nccc8280769b.tq: Identify the earliest record by site rather than by ruler alone.
xs: The first Sanskrit inscription of Andhra and South India is at the **Swarna Devalayam** (Golden Temple), Nagarjunakonda — option **(4)**.
It dates to **Ehuvala Santamula's 11th regnal year**.
**Elisri's Sarvadeva** record is also Sanskrit but not the first; **Gummadidurru** is **Prakrit**.
xa: Gummadidurru is in **Guntur**.
Sanskrit replaced Prakrit from the **4th c. CE**.
The **Mandhata** sculpture is art, not an inscription.

n006806b1ad7.s: Which of the following is NOT a Telugu word found in Ikshvaku records?
n006806b1ad7.x: Bapi, Remmanaka, Adavi, Ehuvala and Anikki are Telugu words found in Ikshvaku records. Dhanyakataka is a place associated with Buddhist learning, not one of the listed Telugu words in the records.
n006806b1ad7.tq: Find the outsider in a vocabulary list.
xs: **Dhanyakataka** is not in the Telugu-word list — option **(3)**.
The Telugu words are **Bapi, Remmanaka, Adavi, Ehuvala, Anikki**.
xa: **Kuvalayamala** records foreign students at **Dhanyakataka** and Nagarjunakonda.
Inscriptions were mainly **Prakrit**, then **Sanskrit** under Ehuvala.

n0c7e75bd672.s: Suhrllekha, described as a letter to Yajnasri, is associated with:
n0c7e75bd672.x: Suhrllekha, along with Madhyamika works, is associated with Acharya Nagarjuna.
n0c7e75bd672.tq: Recall the author of a named Buddhist work.
xs: **Suhrllekha** (letter to **Yajnasri**) is by **Acharya Nagarjuna** — option **(1)**.
**Buddhaghosha** = **Visuddhimagga**; **Aryasangha** = **Sutralankara** (per CDI).
xa: Nagarjuna also wrote **Madhyamika** works.
**Udyotana's Kuvalayamala** (**8th c.**) records foreign students at Nagarjunakonda.
**Dharmamrita** (Jain) mentions a **panchangam**.

n5c967fc9b11.s: Udyotana's Kuvalayamala, dated to the eighth century, records foreign students at:
n5c967fc9b11.x: The eighth-century Kuvalayamala records the presence of foreign students at Dhanyakataka and Nagarjunakonda.
n5c967fc9b11.tq: Match a literary source with its recorded places.
xs: **Udyotana's Kuvalayamala** (**8th c.**) records foreign students at **Dhanyakataka and Nagarjunakonda** — option **(3)**.
**Anupu** is the relocation site of monuments; **Yeleswaram** is Elisri's town.
xa: **Visuddhimagga** (Pali) = **Buddhaghosha**.
**Dharmamrita** is a **Jain** work.
**Suhrllekha** = **Nagarjuna**.

n6999aacb516.s: The first sculptor signatures and the first Sanskrit inscription in South India are associated with the:
n6999aacb516.x: The Ikshvakus are associated with the first sculptor signatures, the first Sanskrit inscription in South India and the first structural Hindu temples.
xa: The first Sanskrit inscription is at the **Swarna Devalayam**.
Other art firsts: **sati** panel, **Chakravarti** (Mandhata), **Viragallu**.
Ikshvakus laid the base of **Dravida** temple architecture.

n6032943afe5.s: Who discovered the site of Nagarjunakonda in 1926?
n6032943afe5.x: A. Ranganatha Saraswati discovered the site in 1926.
n6032943afe5.tq: Match the earliest excavation milestone with its discoverer.
xs: The site was discovered in **1926** by **A. Ranganatha Saraswati** — option **(2)**.
**Longhurst** = **1927-31**; **T.N. Ramachandran** = **1938**; **R. Subrahmanyam** = **1954-60** rescue dig.
xa: ⚠ Discovered **1926** ≠ Nagarjuna Sagar foundation **1955**.
CDX writes "**N.H. Longhurst**" and "**B.N. Ramachandran**".
Habitation span: **Palaeolithic** → **1960 CE**.

nc4bdc259449.s: Who laid the foundation stone of the Nagarjuna Sagar Project on 10 December 1955?
nc4bdc259449.x: Jawaharlal Nehru laid the foundation stone of the Nagarjuna Sagar Project on 10 December 1955.
nc4bdc259449.tq: Combine the event, date and responsible personality.
xs: **Jawaharlal Nehru** laid the foundation stone on **10 December 1955** — option **(2)** (G2 **2012**).
xa: The valley was **submerged after 1960**.
ASI's **salvage archaeology** rebuilt monuments on higher ground.
Nagarjunakonda = India's **only island museum**.

n70cf5fcde87.s: The archaeological operation in which monuments are dismantled and rebuilt at safer locations is known as:
n70cf5fcde87.x: The Archaeological Survey of India used salvage archaeology to dismantle and rebuild monuments before submergence.
n70cf5fcde87.tq: Identify the archaeological method from the described situation.
xs: Dismantling and rebuilding monuments elsewhere = **salvage archaeology** (by the **ASI**) — option **(3)**.
They were rebuilt at **Anupu** (Krishna bank) and **Nagarjunakonda island**.
xa: These are called "**transplanted monuments**".
Valley **submerged after 1960**.
Nagarjunakonda has the **only island museum in India**.

naacb65a32e3.s: The monuments shifted from the submerged valley to higher ground at Anupu and Nagarjunakonda island are known as:
naacb65a32e3.x: The monuments relocated to Anupu and Nagarjunakonda island are called transplanted monuments.
naacb65a32e3.tq: Distinguish the official descriptive term from plausible substitutes.
xs: They are called "**Transplanted monuments**" — option **(1)**.
They stand at **Anupu** (Krishna bank) and on **Nagarjunakonda island**.
xa: The method: **salvage archaeology** by the **ASI**.
Reconstructed remains are kept on the island and at Anupu (**May 2025**).
Nagarjuna Sagar Project: foundation **10 December 1955**.

n15d90d85ca5.s: Which is the largest stupa in Andhra Pradesh?
n15d90d85ca5.x: Amaravati is the largest stupa in Andhra Pradesh (G2 2019). Bhattiprolu is the oldest stupa in Andhra, the Nagarjunakonda Mahachaitya is the Ikshvaku relic stupa, and Jaggayyapeta is known for the Mandhata sculpture.
n15d90d85ca5.tq: Largest in AP = Amaravati; oldest = Bhattiprolu.
xs: **Amaravati** is the **largest stupa in AP** — option **(2)** (G2 **2019**).
**Jaggayyapeta** is known for the **Mandhata** sculpture; the Nagarjunakonda **Maha Chaitya** is a **Dhatugarbha** stupa.
xa: Nagarjunakonda has more than **30 stupas**.
Big stupas use a **wheel-shaped (spoked)** plan.
**Paribhogika** stupas hold objects like **alms bowls**.

nab384588c35.s: Which of the following represents the correct sequence after the Ikshvakus in the Andhra dynastic order?
nab384588c35.x: After the Ikshvakus came the Brihatpalayanas or Pallavas in the relevant territories, followed by the Salankayanas, Vishnukundins and Eastern Chalukyas.
nab384588c35.tq: Anchor the sequence at the Ikshvaku–Brihatpalayana transition and proceed forward.
xs: After the Ikshvakus: **Brihatpalayanas / Pallavas → Salankayanas → Vishnukundins → Eastern Chalukyas** — option **(1)**.
G2 **2008** order key: **a, d, c, b** (Ikshvakus, Brihatpalayanas, Salankayanas, Vishnukundins).
xa: The land **south of the Krishna** went to the **Pallavas** after the Ikshvakus.
Periods (APHQ): Ikshvakus **c. 225-325**; Brihatpalayanas **c. 275-325**; Salankayanas **c. 300-420**; Vishnukundins **c. 420-624**.
The Ikshvakus were ended by the **Pallavas** (**c. 301**).
nab384588c35.fixed: option 1 had odd 'Brihatpalayanas/Pallavas'; standard G2 2008 order

nd160775e0a7.s: In which year did Pulakeshin II defeat Manchana Bhattaraka at Kunala (Kolleru), ending Vishnukundin rule?
nd160775e0a7.x: Pulakeshin II ended Vishnukundin rule at Kunala near Kolleru in 624 CE; his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana then founded the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi.
xa: **Indrabhattaraka** was defeated by **Maukhari Ishanavarma** (Jaunpur inscription) and killed in the **Kalinga** war.
**Manchana Bhattaraka** was the **last** Vishnukundin ruler.
Founder of the Vishnukundins: **Indravarma**; greatest: **Madhava Varma II**.
Dates differ: **358-569 CE** vs **c. 420-624 CE**.

ndc799cb3e15.s: The Vishnukundins are historically significant because they formed a link between which two political phases?
o: The Pallava age and the Maukhari age
The Satavahana age and the Ikshvaku age
The Ikshvaku age and the Eastern Chalukyas
The Gupta age and the Kushana age
ndc799cb3e15.x: The Vishnukundins link the Ikshvaku age with the Eastern Chalukyas. The Eastern Chalukyas took over their agrahara system and administration.
ndc799cb3e15.tq: Test the broader historical transition rather than an isolated ruler or inscription.
xs: The Vishnukundins link the **Ikshvaku age** and the **Eastern Chalukyas** — option **(3)**.
The Eastern Chalukyas took over their **agrahara system and administration**.
xa: Dynasty order: Ikshvakus → **Brihatpalayanas** → **Salankayanas** → Vishnukundins → Eastern Chalukyas.
Founder of the Eastern Chalukyas: **Kubja Vishnuvardhana**.
Their records lie across **both Telugu states**.

ncd49864bd1c.s: Most historians regard the Vishnukundins as belonging to which social group?
o: Only hereditary feudatories of the Pallavas
ncd49864bd1c.x: Most historians regard the Vishnukundins as Brahmins belonging to the Vishnukundina gotra, although alternative caste theories have also been proposed.
ncd49864bd1c.tq: Identify the mainstream interpretation while distinguishing it from alternative theories.
xs: The majority view: the Vishnukundins were **Brahmins of the Vishnukundina gotra** — option **(4)**.
Other theories: **Agnikula Kshatriyas** (K. Gopalachari); **Shudras** raised through the **Hiranyagarbha** rite.
xa: **B.V. Krishna Rao** = Brahmins; **N. Venkataramanayya** = Brahmins who took up Kshatriya ways.
Name "**Vishnukundi**" = **Vinukonda** (Guntur).
Original home: **Telangana** (Amrabad, Keesaragutta, Indrapalanagara).

n9513e91f846.s: Which region is indicated by the early records and forts as the original home of the Vishnukundins?
o: Telangana, including Amrabad, Keesaragutta and Indrapalanagara
The Krishna-Godavari coast after the Pallava wars
The coastal delta around Vengi alone
The southern Tamil region around Kandarapuram
n9513e91f846.x: Early records and forts at Amrabad, Keesaragutta and Indrapalanagara point to Telangana as the original home. The Vishnukundins later expanded into coastal Andhra.
n9513e91f846.tq: Infer the original homeland from the distribution of early forts and records.
xs: Early records and forts show **Telangana** — **Amrabad, Keesaragutta, Indrapalanagara** — as the original home — option **(1)**.
They first ruled Telangana **north of the Krishna**, then expanded to **coastal Andhra**.
xa: **Keesaragutta** = possibly their start as **Vakataka feudatories**.
**Indrapalanagara** = **Tummalagudem**, built by **Indravarma**.
**Amarapura** = **Munnanuru** (Amrabad, Nagarkurnool), where **yaga-vedikas** were found.

n310f3f73135.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler is described as the founder and as a Vakataka vassal?
n310f3f73135.x: Indravarma, who ruled from 358 to 370 CE, is described as the founder of the Vishnukundin dynasty and a Vakataka vassal.
n310f3f73135.tq: Use the founder–political status association rather than the name alone.
xs: **Indravarma** (**358-370**) was the **founder** and a **Vakataka vassal** — option **(3)**.
He built **Indrapalanagara** and issued the **Ramatirtham** plates.
xa: ⚠ A note naming **Govindavarma** as founder contradicts the other sources.
Successor: **Madhava Varma I** (**370-398**).
Indrapalanagara = **Tummalagudem** (Telangana).

n59faf74a300.s: For how many years did Madhava Varma I rule?
n59faf74a300.x: Madhava Varma I ruled for 22 years, married a Vakataka princess and is associated with the Undavalli, Bhairavakona and Mogalrajapuram caves.
xa: His capital: **Indrapalanagara**.
**Ipur** plates (Tenali) are linked to him.

n8de907f6bfe.s: Which ruler is regarded as the greatest Vishnukundin monarch and is associated with the golden age and Vedic revival?
n8de907f6bfe.x: Madhava Varma II is described as the greatest Vishnukundin ruler. His reign is associated with a golden age and Vedic revival.
n8de907f6bfe.tq: Match the evaluative description with the correct ruler.
xs: **Madhava Varma II** (**440-495**) was the **greatest** — **golden age**, **Vedic revival** — option **(1)**.
He moved the capital to **Denduluru**.
xa: Sacrifices: **11 Ashvamedhas**, **16 Rajasuyas**, **1 Purushamedha**, about **1,000** other yagas.
Title: **Janasraya** (G2 **2025** key).
He fought **100+ battles**.

n02658bdf7a2.s: The Vishnukundin ruler Indrabhattaraka Varma was defeated by the Maukhari king:
n02658bdf7a2.x: Indrabhattaraka Varma was defeated by Maukhari Ishanavarma and was killed in the Kalinga war.
xa: Ishanavarma's son married Indrabhattaraka's daughter (**Jaunpur** inscription).
Killers: **Prithvimula** of the Ranadurjayas + a **Kalinga** king.
Vikramendra I = "**Mahakavi**", **Parama Saugata**.

n07e82514502.s: Indrapalanagara, the early Vishnukundin capital, is identified with:
n07e82514502.x: Indrapalanagara (Sukrapuram), built by Indravarma and the capital of Madhava Varma I and Govinda Varma, is Tummalagudem in Telangana.
xa: Also called **Sukrapuram**.
**Tummalagudem** plates = **first Sanskrit inscription found in Telangana**.

n371c56506c3.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler bore the title Satyasraya?
n371c56506c3.x: Indrabhattaraka Varma bore the title Satyasraya; Govinda Varma was Shadabhigna and Vikramendra Varma I was Mahakavi.
xa: Vikramendra II = **Sakala Bhuvana Rakshabharanaikashraya**.
Indrabhattaraka also = **Paramamaheshwara**, **Chaturdhayaka Yuddha Veera**.
MV II = **Janasraya**, **Trisamudradhipati**.

nc2dc66b2ca4.s: The Salankayanas of Vengi were conquered by which Vishnukundin ruler?
nc2dc66b2ca4.x: Madhava Varma II conquered the Vaishnava Salankayanas, whose capital was Vengi (Pedavegi in Eluru district).
xa: Salankayana copper plates: **Tripurantakam, Denduluru, Eluru**.
MV II later moved his capital to **Denduluru**, near Vengi.

n228b1ac42f8.s: The rise of the Vishnukundins followed which development in the Deccan and Andhra region?
o: The Salankayanas established a new empire in Telangana.
Samudragupta’s southern campaign weakened the Pallavas.
The Mauryas restored Ikshvaku rule in Vijayapuri.
The Pallavas strengthened their authority after defeating Samudragupta.
n228b1ac42f8.x: The Vishnukundins rose after Samudragupta’s southern campaign of 358 CE weakened the Pallavas.
n228b1ac42f8.tq: Identify the political cause preceding the rise of a dynasty.
xs: The Vishnukundins rose after **Samudragupta's southern campaign** (**358 CE**) **weakened the Pallavas** — option **(2)**.
Founder **Indravarma** ruled **358-370** (APP dates).
xa: Dates differ: **358-569 CE** vs **c. 420-624 CE**.
The **Pallavas** held the land south of the Krishna after the Ikshvakus.
Indravarma began as a **Vakataka vassal**.

n63a7f6db84c.s: Which combination correctly represents the sacrifices attributed to Madhava Varma II?
n63a7f6db84c.x: Madhava Varma II is credited with performing 11 Ashvamedhas, 16 Rajasuyas and one Purushamedha.
n63a7f6db84c.tq: Separate the three numerical counts carefully because the figures are deliberately similar.
xs: **MV II**: **11 Ashvamedhas, 16 Rajasuyas and 1 Purushamedha** — option **(3)**.
Option (2) swaps the **11** and **16**.
xa: Also **Hiranyagarbha**, **Agnistoma** and about **1,000 other yagas**.
His reign = **Vedic revival**.
Titles: **Parama Brahmanya**, **Trisamudradhipati**.

nb0b188dfa6e.s: A twelfth-century inscription from Bezawada preserves which legend about Madhava Varma II?
o: He sentenced his own son to death after the prince’s chariot killed a poor woman’s son.
He founded the Eastern Chalukya dynasty at Vengi.
He married his daughter to Ishanavarma of the Maukharis.
He abdicated after losing Vengi to the Salankayanas.
nb0b188dfa6e.x: The Bezawada inscription narrates that Madhava Varma II sentenced his own son to death after the prince’s chariot killed the son of a poor woman.
nb0b188dfa6e.tq: Identify the ruler through a distinctive justice legend rather than through a military event.
xs: The **12th-c. Bezawada inscription**: MV II **sentenced his own son to death** after the prince's chariot killed a poor woman's son — option **(1)**.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana** founded the Eastern Chalukyas; **Ishanavarma** is linked to **Indrabhattaraka**.
xa: MV II = **greatest** Vishnukundin, **golden age**.
Title: **Janasraya**.
Bezawada was a Vishnukundin capital for a time.

na147fb1acda.s: The Khanapur plates, found in Satara district of Maharashtra, record the marriage of Madhava Varma II with a daughter of which ruler?
o: Pulakeshin II of the Badami Chalukyas
na147fb1acda.x: The Khanapur plates record Madhava Varma II’s marriage with a daughter of Vakataka ruler Prithvisena II.
na147fb1acda.tq: Use the marriage alliance to distinguish the correct dynasty and ruler from other figures in the political narrative.
xs: The **Khanapur** plates (Satara) record MV II's marriage to a daughter of Vakataka **Prithvisena II** — option **(2)**.
**Pulakeshin II** ended the dynasty; **Ishanavarma** defeated Indrabhattaraka; **Prithvimula** killed him.
xa: Their son **Vikramendra Varma I** was "**Mahakavi**".
**Madhava Varma I** also married a **Vakataka** princess.
**Chikkulla** plates also mention **Vakataka** marriage ties.

n2590dc58b4b.s: Which of the following was regarded as the first capital of the Vishnukundins?
n2590dc58b4b.x: Amarapura was the first capital of the Vishnukundins. The rulers referred to themselves as Amarapurishulu.
xs: The first capital was **Amarapura** — option **(2)**.
The kings called themselves "**Amarapurishulu**".
xa: Identified as **Munnanuru** (Amrabad, Nagarkurnool), where **yaga-vedikas** were found.
**B.S.L. Hanumantha Rao** places it at **Velpuru** (Guntur).
**Bezawada** and **Denduluru** were later capitals.

n65aaae72f46.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler moved the capital from Amarapuri to Denduluru?
n65aaae72f46.x: Madhava Varma II shifted the capital from Amarapuri to Denduluru because of constant Pallava wars and fortified Amarapuri.
n65aaae72f46.tq: Use the capital-shift clue to identify the ruler.
xs: **Madhava Varma II** moved the capital from **Amarapuri** to **Denduluru** — option **(2)** (G2 **2025**).
Reason: constant **Pallava** wars; he also **fortified Amarapuri**.
xa: **Denduluru (Dendulurapura)** lies near **Vengi/Pedavegi**, Eluru dt.
He took **Vengi** from the **Salankayanas**.
APPSC keys: **MV II = Janasraya**; **MV II = Amarapuri → Denduluru**.

nb07bd0774ee.s: After acquiring the Krishna region, the Vishnukundins used which place as a capital for some time?
nb07bd0774ee.x: Bezawada, or Vijayawada, was used as a capital for a period after the Vishnukundins acquired the Krishna region.
nb07bd0774ee.tq: Identify the temporary capital from the territorial-expansion context.
xs: After taking the **Krishna** region, they used **Bezawada** (Vijayawada) as capital for a time — option **(2)**.
They carved the **Indrakeeladri** and **Mogalrajapuram** caves there.
xa: **Keesaragutta** = possibly their start as **Vakataka feudatories**.
**Indrapalanagara** = capital of **MV I** and **Govinda Varma**.
**Denduluru** = **MV II's** capital.

nb14ea9d2c04.s: Which title is most specifically associated with Madhava Varma II?
nb14ea9d2c04.x: Madhava Varma II bore the title Janasraya. Shadabhigna belonged to Govinda Varma, Mahakavi to Vikramendra Varma I, and Sakala Bhuvana Rakshabharanaikashraya to Vikramendra Varma II.
nb14ea9d2c04.tq: Use a title–ruler match and separate similar royal epithets.
xs: **Janasraya** = **Madhava Varma II** — option **(2)** (G2 **2025** key).
**Mahakavi** = **Vikramendra I**; **Shadabhigna** = **Govinda Varma**; **Sakala Bhuvana Rakshabharanaikashraya** = **Vikramendra II**.
xa: ⚠ APP also gives **Janasraya** to **Vikramendra I**.
Other MV II titles: **Trisamudradhipati, Devadhideva, Parameshti, Parama Brahmanya**.
**Trikuta-Malayadhipati** = MV II (CDX p.100, APP).

n5e6a34e8467.s: The title Trikuta-Malayadhipati was connected with the conquest of which rulers?
n5e6a34e8467.x: Madhava Varma II acquired the title Trikuta-Malayadhipati after defeating the Anandagotrikas. Trikuta was identified with Kotappakonda in Guntur.
n5e6a34e8467.tq: Connect a victory-based title with the defeated power.
xs: **Trikuta-Malayadhipati** came from defeating the **Anandagotrikas** — option **(2)**.
**Trikuta** = **Kotappakonda**, Guntur.
xa: Title holder: **Madhava Varma II** (CDX p.**100**, APP); CDX p.**104** gives it to **Madhava Varma III**.
**Anandagotrikas** = **Kandara** kings, capital **Kandarapuram** (Chejerla inscription).
Anandagotrikas were former **Ikshvaku feudatories**.

n0f03bef60eb.s: The Chikkulla plates, containing the Telugu phrase 'Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul', belong to:
n0f03bef60eb.x: The Chikkulla plates (Tuni, East Godavari) are of Vikramendra Varma II and carry the Telugu phrase 'Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul'.
xa: Vikramendra II also issued the **Tundi** and **Tummalagudem-2** plates.
Godavari-region records: **Chikkulla, Polamuru**.

n9c10ed05247.s: Which is regarded as the first Sanskrit inscription found in Telangana?
n9c10ed05247.x: The Tummalagudem plates, associated with Govinda Varma I, are regarded as the first Sanskrit inscription found in Telangana.
xa: They also give the **genealogy**.
Tummalagudem = **Indrapalanagara** (Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri/Nalgonda).
Govinda Varma's **Chaitanyapuri** record is in **Prakrit**.

ncd2f6273412.s: Govinda Varma's Chaitanyapuri inscription was written in:
ncd2f6273412.x: Of the 21 Vishnukundin inscriptions, Govinda Varma's Chaitanyapuri record was in Prakrit, so not all were in Sanskrit.
xa: **Tummalagudem** = **first Sanskrit inscription found in Telangana**.
**Chikkulla** has the Telugu phrase "**Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul**".
Records span both Telugu states: **Godavari, Guntur, Telangana**.

n6232b900adf.s: According to the feudalisation interpretation, tax-free Brahmadeyas with administrative rights contributed to the creation of
o: a class of royal coin inspectors
n6232b900adf.x: The feudalisation interpretation holds that tax-free Brahmadeyas with administrative rights created a landed intermediary class.
n6232b900adf.tq: Identify the social consequence linked to the land-grant system.
xs: Tax-free **Brahmadeyas** with administrative rights created **a landed intermediary class** — option **(4)**.
This is the **feudalisation** reading of Vishnukundin grants.
xa: Agraharas served as **centres of Vedic learning**.
Grants: **Mutukali** (Indravarma, Agnivarma), **Tundi** (Shivavarma), **Ipur** plates (Agnisarma, Easwarasarma).
Social criticism: **varna** rules hardened; women's status fell.

n8dc060b89d8.s: Under the Vishnukundins, the tax called Bhaga represented what share of the produce?
n8dc060b89d8.x: Bhaga was one-sixth of the produce; Vishti was forced labour, later called vetti in Telugu.
xa: Land was measured in **Nivartanas** (1 nivartana = **1.5 acres**).
The **Rajjuka** measured land with ropes; the **Phaladara** fixed the king's share of grain.
**Akshapataladhikrita** was the keeper of records.

o: iron with a thin copper coating
n1c104c774a6.x: Vishnukundin coins were of iron with a thin copper coating (APPSC GS 2018 key); Rayaprolu Subrahmanyam brought them to light.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **Satavahanas**, **Ikshvakus** and **Eastern Chalukyas** are distractors for the copper-coated iron coinage.
Some notes claim **gold, silver and copper** coins — this conflicts with the key; follow copper-coated iron.
Symbols: **lion** (royal emblem), **Nandi**, **ship**, **trishula**, **conch**, "Sriparvata".
AP find-spots: **Bojjannakonda**, **Yelamanchili** (Anakapalli dt), **Pedavegi** (Eluru dt).

n64914d2f3c3.s: Ship-marked Vishnukundin coins found in coastal Andhra, together with the title Trisamudradhipati, indicate the dynasty's association with
n64914d2f3c3.x: Ship-marked coins and the title Trisamudradhipati point to the importance of sea trade.
n64914d2f3c3.tq: Infer the economic activity from the symbol and royal title.
xs: Ship-marked coins and the title **Trisamudradhipati** show **sea trade** — option **(2)**.
The ship coins come from **coastal Andhra**; the title belonged to **Madhava Varma II**.
xa: A **Roman gold coin of Constantine** was found at **Kudali Sangameswaram** near Alampur.
**Fahien** noted **cowrie shells (gavvalu)** also used as money.
Outside find-spots: **Nasik**, **Nagpur**, **Khanapur** (Maharashtra) and **Brahmagiri**.

n79e95aed0ce.s: The family deity of the Vishnukundin dynasty was
n79e95aed0ce.x: Sriparvataswami was the family deity, and the kings described themselves as Sriparvataswami-padanudhyata.
n79e95aed0ce.tq: Direct identification of the dynastic deity.
xs: The family deity was **Sriparvataswami** — option **(1)**.
Kings styled themselves "**Sriparvataswami-padanudhyata**"; the deity is identified with **Srisaila Mallikarjuna**.
**Bhutagrahaka Swami** was Yama; **Dantamukha Swami** was the Ganapati at Velpuru; **Dharmapuri** became a Narasimha kshetra.
xa: "**Sriparvata**" also appears on Vishnukundin coins.
Royal titles: **Paramamaheshwara** (Indrabhattaraka, Vikramendra), **Parama Bhagavata**, **Parama Brahmanya**.
**Ramalingeswara** temples: Keesaragutta, Velpuru, Ipur, Indrapalanagara.

n47a49b4daa6.s: At which place was Dantamukha Swami installed during the 33rd year of Madhava Varma II?
n47a49b4daa6.x: Dantamukha Swami was installed at Velpuru in the 33rd year of Madhava Varma II.
n47a49b4daa6.tq: Combine the deity, place and regnal-year clues.
xs: **Dantamukha Swami** was installed at **Velpuru** — option **(1)**.
It marks the **beginning of Ganapati worship**, in **MV II's 33rd year**.
**Keesaragutta** had a Ramalingeswara temple; **Dharmapuri** became a Narasimha kshetra; **Indrapalanagara** had a vihara and a Ramalingeswara temple.
xa: **Velpuru** (Guntur) was also a **Rashtra**.
**Bhutagrahaka Swami** was identified with **Yama**.
MV II performed **11 Ashvamedhas** and **16 Rajasuyas**.

n156a1623724.s: Which development was associated with the decline of Jainism during the Vishnukundin period?
n156a1623724.x: Jainism declined as Kapalika Shaivism rose; Jain shrines such as Srisailam were converted, and Kumarilabhatta attacked Jainism.
n156a1623724.tq: Link the religious decline with its stated historical cause.
xs: Jainism declined as **Kapalika Shaivism** rose — option **(2)**.
Jain shrines such as **Srisailam** were converted, and **Kumarilabhatta** attacked Jainism.
xa: Buddhism too declined from **MV II** onward.
MV II turned Buddhist sites at **Undavalli** and **Mogalrajapuram** into Hindu shrines.
Family deity **Sriparvataswami** = **Srisaila Mallikarjuna**.

n5f990147e27.s: The Paramabhattarika Mahadevi Vihara was founded by the queen of:
n5f990147e27.x: The queen of Govinda Varma I founded the Paramabhattarika Mahadevi Vihara; Govinda Varma I himself founded the Govinda Vihara.
xa: The Mahadevi Vihara at **Indrapalanagara** housed **Chaturdasharya bhikshus**; Govinda Varma I granted it **Penkapura and Enmadala**.
Govinda Vihara has a **Prakrit inscription on the Musi**.
Buddhism declined from **MV II** onward.

n6fccb1fdc93.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler is called a 'destroyer of Buddhism'?
n6fccb1fdc93.x: Buddhism declined from Madhava Varma II onward, and sites like Undavalli and Mogalrajapuram became Hindu shrines. Govinda Varma I and his queen founded viharas, and Vikramendra Varma II granted a village to a vihara.
xa: MV II performed **11 Ashvamedhas** and **16 Rajasuyas**.
⚠ Some notes say royal grants to monasteries stopped entirely — this contradicts the **Tummalagudem** grants.
Jainism declined as **Kapalika** Shaivas rose.

n0e6c0443ff3.s: Who is associated with the first mention of Ghatikas in Andhra inscriptions?
n0e6c0443ff3.x: The inscriptions of Indrabhattaraka Varma provide the first mention of Ghatikas in Andhra.
n0e6c0443ff3.tq: Identify the ruler directly associated with the specific epigraphic evidence.
xs: Ghatikas are first mentioned in **Indrabhattaraka Varma's** inscriptions — option **(3)**.
He is also credited with the **Ghatikeshwara temple at Keesara**.
xa: **Govinda Varma** = "**Shadabhigna**"; **MV II** = "**Vidyadvijaguru**".
**Vikramendra Varma I** is called "**Mahakavi**" in the Indrapalanagara plates.
Ghatikas taught **14 vidyas**; special ones at **Amaravati** and **Vengi**.

n22ef28ba505.s: The number of vidyas taught at the special Ghatikas of Amaravati and Vengi was:
n22ef28ba505.x: The Ghatikas taught fourteen vidyas: four Vedas, six Vedangas, Mimamsa, Nyaya, Dharmashastra and Puranas.
n22ef28ba505.tq: Check the numerical total against the component subjects rather than relying on a rounded figure.
xs: Ghatikas taught **14** vidyas — option **(3)**.
**4 Vedas** + **6 Vedangas** + **Mimamsa** + **Nyaya** + **Dharmashastra** + **Puranas** = 14.
xa: Special Ghatikas: **Amaravati** and **Vengi**.
First mention in Andhra: **Indrabhattaraka Varma's** inscriptions.
Buddhist teacher **Dasabalabali** knew the **four Vedas**.

n4eb14750e0d.s: Janasraya Chhandovichiti, associated with Madhava Varma II, is a Sanskrit work on:
n4eb14750e0d.x: Janasraya Chhandovichiti is a Sanskrit work on prosody, credited to Madhava Varma II (title Janasraya) or to the poet Gunaswami writing in his name.
xa: **Vikramendra Varma I** is called "**Mahakavi**" but no surviving Sanskrit work is named.
⚠ **Prabodha Chandrodayam** is a Telugu work by **Nandi Mallaya and Ghanta Singaya**, about a thousand years later — not Vishnukundin.
Official language: **Sanskrit**.

n0e0b240778e.s: The Vishnukundin Tundi plates record the grant of Tundi village to the scholar:
n0e0b240778e.x: The Tundi plates record the grant of Tundi village to Shivavarma; the Ipur plates name Agnisarma and Easwarasarma, and Mutukali went to Indravarma and Agnivarma.
xa: The Mutukali grant is assigned to **MV III** in some notes and **Vikramendra I** in others.
Ipur plates granted **cows, gold and land** to Brahmins.
Agraharas were **centres of Vedic learning**.

na5ce530fc36.s: Ghatikas in the Vishnukundin period were primarily:
o: Residential institutions for Buddhist monks only
Higher colleges of Sanskrit and Vedic learning
na5ce530fc36.x: Ghatikas were higher Sanskrit and Vedic colleges concerned with advanced Brahmanical learning.
na5ce530fc36.tq: Use the precise institutional definition to distinguish Ghatikas from other contemporary establishments.
xs: Ghatikas were **higher colleges of Sanskrit and Vedic learning** — option **(3)**.
They were Brahmanical, not Buddhist monasteries, military schools or guilds.
xa: First mention in Andhra: **Indrabhattaraka Varma's inscriptions**.
Special Ghatikas: **Amaravati** and **Vengi**.
Curriculum of **14 vidyas**: **4 Vedas**, **6 Vedangas**, Mimamsa, Nyaya, Dharmashastra, Puranas.

n8cb5c225088.s: Which language served as the official language during the Vishnukundin period?
n8cb5c225088.x: Sanskrit was the official language of the Vishnukundin period, although Telugu began to enter the records.
n8cb5c225088.tq: Separate the official administrative language from the language beginning to appear in records.
xs: The official language was **Sanskrit** — option **(4)**.
**Telugu** only entered records — e.g. Chikkulla plates' "**Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul**" and Telugu village names.
xa: **Prakrit** appears in Govinda Varma I's inscription on the **Musi** (Govinda Vihara).
**Janasraya Chhandovichiti** is a **Sanskrit** work on **prosody**.
Ghatikas were higher **Sanskrit/Vedic** colleges.

n4e3b15adaa0.s: The Undavalli cave temples are located near which city?
n4e3b15adaa0.x: Undavalli lies on the Krishna bank near Vijayawada (APPSC GS 2019 key), in Guntur district. Nellore is linked with Bhairavakonda, Visakhapatnam with Bojjannakonda, and Hyderabad with Keesaragutta and Chaitanyapuri.
n4e3b15adaa0.tq: Undavalli: city key Vijayawada; revenue district Guntur.
xs: Undavalli is near **Vijayawada** — option **(1)** (the **APPSC GS 2019** key).
It lies on the **Krishna** bank; its revenue district is **Guntur**.
**Nellore** is linked with **Bhairavakonda**; **Keesaragutta** is in Medchal-Malkajgiri near Hyderabad.
xa: Precisely: **Tadepalli mandal**, inside the **Amaravati** capital area near **Mangalagiri**.
**Mogalrajapuram** is in Vijayawada itself, now **NTR district**.
**Akkanna-Madanna** caves are on **Indrakeeladri hill**, Vijayawada.

n13bb487ec76.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Undavalli caves?
o: They are situated in Guntur district.
They are situated on the bank of the Godavari.
Their architecture is a Vishnukundina adaptation of the Gupta rock-cut style.
They contain a five-metre reclining image of Ananta Padmanabha Vishnu.
n13bb487ec76.x: The Undavalli caves are on the Krishna in Guntur district, not on the Godavari; the other three statements are correct.
xa: Earlier use: **Jain** abode, then **Buddhist** monks, then **Hindu** temple.
Undavalli: **four storeys**, carved **top-down**, ground floor **unfinished**.
**Purnakumbha** motifs throughout.

ndff0a54ef4c.s: The Undavalli caves contain a monolithic reclining statue of:
ndff0a54ef4c.x: Undavalli, a Vishnukundin cave of the 4th-5th c. CE on the Krishna, contains a monolithic reclining Ananta Padmanabha Swamy.
xa: This exact framing appeared in an **Aug 2026** test.
Undavalli is in **Tadepalli mandal**, Guntur, in the **Amaravati** capital area.
AP held the two-day **Telugu Mahotsavam** at Undavalli on **25-26 Jul 2026**.

n8efb7655d59.s: The Mogalrajapuram cave complex consists of how many caves?
n8efb7655d59.x: Mogalrajapuram has five caves in all. The fifth cave is the largest and contains the Shiva Tandava Nataraja sculpture.
n8efb7655d59.tq: Separate the total number of caves from the numbers associated with individual cave groups.
xs: Mogalrajapuram has **five** caves — option **(2)**.
**Cave 5**, the largest, has **Shiva Tandava Nataraja**.
⚠ **8** caves = **Bhairavakonda**; **4** storeys = **Undavalli**.
xa: **Caves 1-3**: sanctums behind a pillared mandapa for the **Trimurti**.
**Cave 4**: **Durga** cave, **Ardhanarishvara** painted on the back wall.
Some notes file these under "**Akkana-Madanna**" — assign them to **Mogalrajapuram**.

n77e09d0cad6.s: How many storeys do the Undavalli caves have?
n77e09d0cad6.x: Undavalli has four storeys with three main caves; it was carved top-down, with finely detailed upper levels and a crude ground floor.
xa: Centrepiece: **monolithic reclining Vishnu, Ananta Padmanabha Swamy**, about **5 m (16 ft)**.
**Purnakumbha** motifs appear throughout.
Date: **4th-5th c. CE**, regional form of the **Gupta** rock-cut style.

nb4d7ba66987.s: How many rock-cut caves are there at Bhairavakonda?
nb4d7ba66987.x: Bhairavakonda, a Kapalika Shaiva centre, has eight rock-cut caves; 4, 9 and 12 are the usual traps.
xa: **G2 2012** asked the cave count; **G2 2008** asked the religion (traps: Buddhism, Jainism, Vaishnavism).
Attribution: **Madhava Varma I** vs **Pallava (7th-8th c.)**.
Bhairavakonda is where the **Vishnukundin and Pallava styles overlap**.

nb6e7d0f17d0.s: The Undavalli caves were first used as a/an:
nb6e7d0f17d0.x: Undavalli was first a Jain abode, then used by Buddhist monks, and later converted into a Hindu temple.
xa: The present deity is **Ananta Padmanabha Swamy**, about **5 m (16 ft)** long.
⚠ **Aug 2026** test: "built by the **Cholas** as a Hindu temple, later Buddhist" is **false**.
Dated **4th-5th c. CE**.

n9ce16784400.s: Which architectural plan is characteristic of Vishnukundin cave temples such as Mogalrajapuram?
o: A circular stupa without any shrine cell
A free-standing tower enclosing a circumambulatory passage only
A pillared mandapa in front of one or more rock-cut garbhagriha cells
A rectangular palace with no religious chamber
n9ce16784400.x: The typical plan consists of a pillared mandapa or ardhamandapa in front of one or more garbhagriha cells cut into the rock. At Mogalrajapuram, the shrines lie behind the mandapa.
n9ce16784400.tq: Translate the architectural description into a plan-based identification.
xs: The plan is **a pillared mandapa in front of one or more rock-cut garbhagriha cells** — option **(3)**.
The early hall is the **ardhamandapa**; at **Mogalrajapuram** shrines sit behind it.
xa: **Dwarapalas** flank shrine entrances.
**Undavalli** is storeyed (**four storeys**) on the same plan.
**Structural temples** were of **brick**, with garbhagriha, antarala-mandapa and mukhamandapa (**Keesaragutta**).
n9ce16784400.fixed: stem refers to an absent passage ('described here')

n40eef71c738.s: The rock-cut caves of the Pallava king Mahendravarman I are dated to the:
n40eef71c738.x: Mahendravarman I's caves belong to the 7th century, while the Vishnukundin caves are generally dated to the 4th-6th centuries.
xa: Pallavas introduced **mandapa + garbhagriha** and **lion-based (simha-mukha) pillars**.
Vishnukundin pillars: **lion pedestals**, **pot capitals** (Bhairavakonda).
Pallava style was later taken up by **Telugu Chodas** and **Eastern Chalukyas**.

n717dbc6aa09.s: The rock-cut cave style of the Pallava ruler Mahendravarman I, with lion-based pillars, was later taken up by the
n717dbc6aa09.x: The Pallava (Mahendravarman I) cave style of the 7th c. was later taken up by the Telugu Chodas and Eastern Chalukyas. The Kushanas, Guptas, Mauryas, Sungas, Satavahanas and Ikshvakus all came earlier, so could not take up a 7th-century style.
n717dbc6aa09.tq: Mahendravarman caves -> later Telugu Chodas, Eastern Chalukyas.
xs: The Pallava style was later taken up by the **Telugu Chodas and Eastern Chalukyas** — option **(3)**.
**Mahendravarman I's** style (**7th c.**) used **lion-based (simha-mukha) pillars** and the **mandapa + garbhagriha** plan.
xa: Vishnukundin caves (**4th-6th c.**) rest on a **Gupta-Vakataka** base.
**Bhairavakonda** is where the two styles overlap.
**Undavalli** shows Pallava influence.

n3ae7b39acb8.s: The earliest Hindu cave temples in India, at Udayagiri in Madhya Pradesh, are associated with the:
n3ae7b39acb8.x: The Guptas at Udayagiri in Madhya Pradesh are credited with the earliest Hindu cave temples in India, whereas the Vishnukundins are associated with the first Hindu cave temples in the Telugu states.
n3ae7b39acb8.tq: Distinguish the broader Indian claim from the regional Telugu-states claim.
xs: India's first Hindu cave temples, at **Udayagiri (MP)**, are credited to the **Guptas** — option **(3)**.
The **Vishnukundins** made the first Hindu cave temples of the **Telugu states**, not of India.
xa: Undavalli is a regional form of the **Gupta** rock-cut style, dated **4th-5th c. CE**.
Vishnukundin style blends **Ikshvaku and Vakataka** traditions with Pallava borrowings.
**Pallava** (Mahendravarman I) caves are of the **7th c.**

n4648ab0d056.s: Madhava Varma I of the Vishnukundin dynasty is credited with which group of cave temples?
n4648ab0d056.x: Madhava Varma I is credited with the Undavalli, Bhairavakonda and Mogalrajapuram caves in the attribution followed by APP and CDX.
n4648ab0d056.tq: Match the ruler with the complete group of monuments, avoiding substitution by a nearby cave site.
xs: **Madhava Varma I** is credited with **Undavalli, Bhairavakonda and Mogalrajapuram** — option **(4)**.
**Mahabalipuram** caves are **Pallava**; **Udayagiri** is **Gupta**; Keesaragutta is not in the attribution.
xa: **APHQ** dates Bhairavakonda to the **Pallava** period (**7th-8th c.**).
Undavalli = **Vishnukundins** (**G2 2025**).
**Vishnukundins** built the first Hindu cave temples in the Telugu states.
n4648ab0d056.fixed: oddly worded 'attribution followed in one scholarly tradition'

na500ce61b1a.s: Some sources credit the Bhairavakonda caves to which Vishnukundin ruler?
na500ce61b1a.x: APP and CDX credit Madhava Varma I, while APHQ dates the caves to the Pallava period of the 7th-8th centuries CE.
xa: **8 rock-cut caves**, all to **Shiva**.
**Kapalika** Shaiva centre.
District: **Nellore** (exam key) vs **Prakasam** (CDI).

n64cda755694.s: Vishnukundin cave architecture combines which two traditions, along with borrowings from the Pallavas?
n64cda755694.x: The style is described as a blend of Ikshvaku and Vakataka traditions, with additional influence borrowed from the Pallavas.
n64cda755694.tq: Identify the paired stylistic traditions rather than a single dynastic influence.
xs: The style blends **Ikshvaku and Vakataka traditions** with Pallava borrowings — option **(3)**.
The hills were cut **from the south**.
xa: Undavalli adapts the **Gupta** rock-cut style; base is **Gupta-Vakataka**.
Undavalli shows **Pallava influence**; Vishnukundins "**imitated the Pallava style**".
Structural temples: **brick** (Keesaragutta).
n64cda755694.fixed: stem refers to an absent passage ('described')

n6bef2c534ec.s: The two-day Telugu Mahotsavam associated with the Undavalli caves was held in
n6bef2c534ec.x: The AP government's two-day Telugu Mahotsavam at the Undavalli Caves was held on 25–26 July 2026, so July 2026 is right; the April and 2025 dates are distractors.
n6bef2c534ec.tq: Separate close current-affairs dates by retaining both the month and year.
xs: The two-day **Telugu Mahotsavam** at Undavalli was held in **July 2026** (**25-26 Jul**) — option **(4)**.
The April and 2025 dates are distractors.
xa: Minister **Kandula Durgesh** said it will be an **annual** festival in every region.
Undavalli is in **Tadepalli mandal** in the **Amaravati** capital area.
Undavalli's centrepiece: **monolithic reclining Vishnu**, about **5 m (16 ft)**.

nfb3da07bd6a.s: Which Satavahana-period inscription refers to Brahmins trained in Vedic learning and rituals?
nfb3da07bd6a.x: The Nanaghat inscription mentions Brahmins trained in Vedic learning and ritual; Satavahana kings enforced varna-dharma and granted tax-free villages to Brahmins.
xa: **Gautamiputra Satakarni** claimed to have **stopped varna-sankara** (mixing of castes).
Nasik prasasti: "**Ekabrahmana**" and humbler of **Kshatriya pride**.
Agrahara recipients named: **Agnisarma**, **Easwarasarma**.

n1285da03d2c.s: The assimilation of which groups into the Kshatriya order is referred to in the context of early Andhra society?
n1285da03d2c.x: Greeks, Sakas, Pahlavas and Kushanas adopted Indian names and faiths and were assimilated into the Kshatriya order. The list also includes the Kardhamakas and Western Kshatrapas.
n1285da03d2c.tq: Discriminate between the historically associated groups rather than selecting a familiar dynastic list.
xs: **Greeks, Sakas, Pahlavas and Kushanas** took Indian names/faiths and gained **Kshatriya status** — option **(2)**.
The list also includes the **Kardhamakas** and **Western Kshatrapas**.
xa: Examples: Saka **Nahapana's daughter Dakshamitra**, son-in-law **Rishabhadatta**, and **Rudradaman**.
**Vasishthiputra Satakarni** married the daughter of Saka **Rudradaman**.
Kshatriya claims continued later: **Vanniyakula Kshatriya Mahasabha (1888)**, **Akhil Bharatiya Kshatriya Mahasabha (1897)**.

na70fe75486c.s: Under the Vishnukundins, which group was regarded as 'the backbone' of society and received land grants?
na70fe75486c.x: Farmers were 'the backbone' and received land grants; Vaisyas carried on trade, and Sudras such as carpenters and weavers had a recognised place.
xa: The Vishnukundins followed **varnasramadharma**.
They founded **Ghatikasthanas** (Vedic colleges).
Family deity **Sriparvataswamy**; titles **Paramamaheswara**, **Parama Brahmanya**.

n850684eeed9.s: Which of the following best characterises the position of women in early Andhra society?
o: Society was patriarchal and based on joint families, but women enjoyed considerable respect and freedom.
Women enjoyed authority only within Buddhist monasteries.
Women were excluded from festivals, assemblies and public life.
Society was entirely matrilineal and had no joint-family system.
n850684eeed9.x: The society was patriarchal and organised around joint families, yet women enjoyed considerable respect and participated in festivals, assemblies and public life.
n850684eeed9.tq: Choose the balanced statement and reject extreme claims that deny one side of the comparison.
xs: Society was **patriarchal with a joint family**, yet women had **considerable respect and freedom** — option **(1)**.
Women joined men in **festivals, assemblies and public life**.
xa: Donative inscriptions record women's gifts on such occasions.
**Matronymics**: **Gautamiputra** Satakarni, **Vasishthiputra** Pulumavi.
Titles from husbands: **Mahasenapatni**, **Mahabhojaki**, **Maharathi**.
Female poets in Hala's Gathasaptasati: **Madhavi**, **Revati**, **Anupamalabdha**, **Anulakshmi**.

nf3c52a1d5ce.s: In early Andhra society, the Selavaddikas were:
nf3c52a1d5ce.x: Selavaddikas were stone sculptors or masons; Halikas were farmers, Sethis merchants and Swarnakaras goldsmiths.
xa: **Gandhikas** = perfumers; **Tailapishakas** = oil pressers; **Golikas** = cowherds.
Sub-castes grew from **varna-sankara** + occupational diversification (**Gathasaptasati**, **Kamasutra**).
Halikas were **the emerging agricultural group**.

n24e1d6493c1.s: The offspring of a Viloma (Pratiloma) union was termed:
n24e1d6493c1.x: Viloma, a lower-caste man with a higher-caste woman, produced offspring termed Chandala; Anuloma offspring were termed Ugra.
xa: ⚠ **Anuloma → Ugra**; **Viloma → Chandala** — a frequent swap trap.
**Kathasaritsagara** mentions inter-caste marriages: caste was **not fully rigid** at first.
**Polygamy** among upper classes; widows kept **celibacy**.

n118f3db2bc5.s: Which evidence is associated with the practice of sati in early Andhra society?
o: A Nagarjunakonda sculpture and the account of the Greek writer Strabo
n118f3db2bc5.x: A Nagarjunakonda sculpture depicts a woman committing sati, and the Greek writer Strabo also noted the practice.
n118f3db2bc5.tq: Combine archaeological and literary evidence without adding unrelated inscriptions.
xs: Sati is shown in a **Nagarjunakonda sculpture** and noted by the Greek writer **Strabo** — option **(3)**.
**Amaravati reliefs** show dress and popular worship; the **Nanaghat inscription** mentions Vedic Brahmins.
xa: **Widows** were expected to observe **celibacy**.
**Polygamy** existed among the **upper classes**.
Marriage was a **sacred institution**.

nfad55407200.s: The Satavahana royal woman Gautami Balasri funded a cave-vihara at:
nfad55407200.x: Gautami Balasri, a Satavahana woman patron, funded a cave-vihara at Nasik; she is not among the Gathasaptasati poets.
xa: Gathasaptasati: by **Hala**, about **700 verses**, **Maharashtri Prakrit**.
It is the **most important literary source** of Satavahana society (**APPSC 2019**).
⚠ **Bodhisiri** and **Chantisiri** were **Ikshvaku** patrons, not Satavahana.

n912cd994fcd.s: Unlike the Ikshvaku queens, who patronised Buddhism, the Ikshvaku kings performed:
n912cd994fcd.x: Ikshvaku kings performed Vedic sacrifices, whereas Ikshvaku queens patronised Buddhism.
xa: Queens: **Bodhisiri** (greatest woman patron) and **Chantisiri** (**Mahachaitya**).
Nagarjunakonda had Brahmanical shrines such as **Pushpabhadraswami**.
Nagarjunakonda became a leading Buddhist learning centre under **Ikshvaku** patronage.

ndca52c5308f.s: The expression ‘Ghatika Vapta punyasancharya’ is associated with which Vishnukundin ruler?
ndca52c5308f.x: Indrabhattaraka Varma is associated with the expression ‘Ghatika Vapta punyasancharya’ and was credited with founding ghatikas.
ndca52c5308f.tq: Recognise the distinctive inscriptional expression linked to the ruler credited with founding ghatikas.
xs: **'Ghatika Vapta punyasancharya'** belongs to **Indrabhattaraka Varma** — option **(3)**.
He is credited with **founding ghatikas**.
**Vasishthiputra Chantamula** was an **Ikshvaku**, not a Vishnukundin.
xa: **Govindavarma** = **'shadabhigna'**; **Vikramendra Varma** = **'mahakavi'**.
**Ghatikasthanas** were Vedic colleges set up by the Vishnukundins.
Vishnukundin titles: **Paramamaheswara**, **Parama Brahmanya**.

n45770835f85.s: Along with Paramamaheswara, the Vishnukundins bore the title:
n45770835f85.x: The Vishnukundins, whose family deity was Sriparvataswamy, bore the titles Paramamaheswara and Parama Brahmanya.
xa: **Vikramendra Varma** was called **'Parama Sogatasya'**.
They followed **varnasramadharma**.
They established **Ghatikasthanas**.

nb49d8dc79bb.s: The reliefs at Amaravati depict the popular worship of which of the following, alongside Buddhist symbols?
o: Only Vedic fire altars and sacrificial posts
Jain tirthankaras, yakshas and lion pillars
nb49d8dc79bb.x: Amaravati reliefs show the worship of nagas, yakshas and sacred trees alongside Buddhist symbols.
nb49d8dc79bb.tq: Identify the complete set of folk-cult elements rather than selecting an unrelated religious group.
xs: Amaravati reliefs show worship of **nagas, yakshas and sacred trees** — option **(3)**.
They appear beside **Buddhist symbols**.
xa: **Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda reliefs** are the main visual evidence of dress and adornment.
Men: **lower cloth + turban**; women: **heavy anklets, bangles, girdles, necklaces**.
Early Andhra combined **Vedic varna order** with strong **Buddhist patronage**.

n8c6a16316b0.s: Which literary work mentions inter-caste marriages, showing that caste was not completely rigid in the early period?
n8c6a16316b0.x: Kathasaritsagara mentions inter-caste marriages, showing that caste practices were not completely rigid at that stage.
xa: **Anuloma** offspring = **Ugra**; **Viloma** offspring = **Chandala**.
Sub-castes arose from **varna-sankara** + occupations.
Marriage = **sacred institution**.

n39036830b54.s: Which of the following is regarded as the most important literary source for the social and cultural life of the Satavahana period?
n39036830b54.x: Hala's Gathasaptasati, about 700 verses in Maharashtri Prakrit on family, marriage, agriculture, trade and festivals, is the most important literary source for Satavahana society (APPSC 2019). The Puranas mainly give dynastic lists, while the Aitareya Brahmana and the Dharmasutras are not sources for Satavahana everyday life.
xs: **Gathasaptasati** is the most important literary source of Satavahana society — option **(3)** (**APPSC 2019**).
**Puranas**, **Aitareya Brahmana** and **Dharmasutras** are the standard wrong options.
It is **Hala's** work of about **700 verses** in **Maharashtri Prakrit**.
xa: It covers family, marriage, women, agriculture, trade, festivals and occupations.
Same **APPSC 2019**: **'Maiputa'** dancers = **Kusuma Lepanam**.
Its female poets: **Madhavi**, **Revati**, **Anupamalabdha**, **Anulakshmi**.

nap-history-45-17.s: Samayamu were caste associations during the rule of the:
nap-history-45-17.x: Samayamu were caste associations of the Kakatiya period; Kayasthas were record-keepers.
n: Samayamu referred to caste associations during the Kakatiya period. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 56-57]
Kayasthas were the caste of record-keepers. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 56-57]
Bhogam disappeared from Andhra society due to the efforts of Venkataratnam Naidu. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 56-57]
The Satavahanas belonged to the Brahmin caste. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 56-57]
xa: The **fourfold caste system** existed under Satavahana rule.
The **Vishnukundins** followed **varnasramadharma**; farmers were **"the backbone"**.
Occupational terms: **Halikas** = farmers, **Sethis** = merchants, **Golikas** = cowherds.
⚠ **Anuloma** offspring = **Ugra**; **Viloma** offspring = **Chandala**.

na9ce97f1650.s: According to tradition, the second Sangam was held at:
na9ce97f1650.x: Tradition places the first Sangam at Then Madurai, the second at Kapatapuram and the third at Madurai, all under Pandya patronage.
xa: ⚠ First and Third both at **Madurai**; Second at **Kapatapuram**.
The tradition comes from the preface of **Iraiyanar Agapporul**.
Presiding scholars: **Agastya** (First), **Agastya / Tolkappiyar** (Second), **Nakkirar** (Third).

n8aecbf18988.s: The traditional account of the three Tamil Sangams comes from the preface of which work?
n8aecbf18988.x: The three-Sangam tradition is given in the preface of Iraiyanar Agapporul. Tolkappiyam is the grammar said to survive from the second Sangam; Pattinappalai describes Puhar; Silappadikaram is the post-Sangam epic of Kannagi.
n8aecbf18988.tq: Three-Sangam legend: preface of Iraiyanar Agapporul.
xs: The three-Sangam tradition comes from the preface of **Iraiyanar Agapporul** — option **(2)**.
**Tolkappiyam** is the grammar surviving from the Second Sangam; **Pattinappalai** describes **Puhar**; **Silappadikaram** is the post-Sangam epic of **Kannagi**.
xa: "Sangam" = assemblies/academies of poets under **Pandya** patronage.
Presiding scholar of the Third Sangam: **Nakkirar**.
⚠ First and Third Sangams at **Madurai**; Second at **Kapatapuram**.

ndcacda52711.s: The Sangams, assemblies of Tamil poets, were held under the patronage of the:
ndcacda52711.x: The Sangams were held under Pandya patronage, not Chola; the corpus has about 2,400 poems.
xa: Language: **old Tamil**.
Themes divide into **aham** (interior) and **puram** (exterior).
Sangam poets **knew the varna classification** (**UPSC 2022** key).

n93c91dd601f.s: Ettuthogai and Pattupattu poems are divided into aham and:
n93c91dd601f.x: Ettuthogai and Pattupattu are divided into aham and puram themes.
xa: Corpus: about **2,400 poems**, including women poets.
One of the earliest bodies of **secular** literature in India.
Puram covers **war, valour, deeds of kings, ethics**.

n8b7eb8b6d7a.s: Which of the following belongs to the Ettuthogai (eight anthologies)?
n8b7eb8b6d7a.x: Padirruppattu, on the Chera kings, is one of the Ettuthogai; Pattinappalai, Mullaippattu and Tirumurugarruppadai belong to Pattupattu.
xa: Other Ettuthogai: **Ainkurunuru**, **Narrinai**, **Akananuru**, **Purananuru**, **Kuruntogai**, **Kalittogai**, **Paripadal**.
Ettuthogai = **8 anthologies** of **short poems**.
Pattupattu = **10 idylls**, longer poems.

n6b0c1bd0889.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sangam corpus?
o: Pathinenkilkanakku is older than Ettuthogai and Pattupattu.
n6b0c1bd0889.x: Pathinenkilkanakku, the eighteen minor works on ethics, is largely post-Sangam, so it is not older than Ettuthogai and Pattupattu (the Melkanakku).
xa: **Ettuthogai** = **8 anthologies** of short poems; **Pattupattu** = **10 idylls** of longer poems.
Both are divided into **Aham** (love, emotion) and **Puram** (war, valour).
**Padirruppattu** is on **Chera** kings; **Pattinappalai** describes **Puhar** and **Karikala**.
The corpus has about **2,400 poems**, including **women poets**.

n9d0a5b4e3cb.s: In the Tirukkural, the book Porul deals with:
n9d0a5b4e3cb.x: The Tirukkural's 1,330 couplets are in three books: Aram (virtue), Porul (wealth) and Inbam (love).
xa: Author: **Tiruvalluvar**.
The Kural is part of **Pathinenkilkanakku** and is **post-Sangam**.
UPPSC 2014 key: Tirukkural = **philosophy**.

o: The first Tamil epic centred on Kannagi and Kovalan
A collection of ten idylls on Chola ports
A Buddhist grammar composed by Tolkappiyar
A Jain epic concerning Jivaka Chintamani
n637a5c556ea.x: Silappadikaram, written by Ilango Adigal, is regarded as the first Tamil epic and tells the story of Kannagi and Kovalan through the motif of the anklet.
n637a5c556ea.tq: Match the work with its distinctive story and literary status.
xs: Silappadikaram is **the first Tamil epic**, about **Kannagi and Kovalan** — option **(1)**.
The story turns on **the anklet**; author **Ilango Adigal**.
**Jivaka Chintamani** is the Jain epic; **Tolkappiyar** wrote the grammar.
xa: Kovalan is executed by the **Pandya** king; **Kannagi burns Madurai**.
Characters: merchant **Kovalan**, wife **Kannagi**, dancer **Madhavi**.
Sequel: **Manimekalai** by **Sittalai Sattanar**.

n0a3792c63f9.s: Manimekalai tells how the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi became a:
n0a3792c63f9.x: Manimekalai relates how the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi becomes a Buddhist nun and reflects Buddhist philosophy.
xa: Author: **Sittalai Sattanar**.
UPPSC 2014 key: Manimekalai = **merchant story**.
Kannagi, not Madhavi, is Kovalan's wife; she **burns Madurai**.

nf2aab0d9234.s: Silappadikaram and Manimekalai are generally regarded as
nf2aab0d9234.x: Both Silappadikaram and Manimekalai are considered post-Sangam works.
nf2aab0d9234.tq: Separate the chronology of the twin epics from that of the Sangam corpus.
xs: Silappadikaram and Manimekalai are **post-Sangam works** — option **(3)**.
The **Tirukkural** too is post-Sangam.
xa: Silappadikaram = **first Tamil epic** (Ilango Adigal).
Manimekalai = **Buddhist epic** (Sittalai Sattanar).
Oldest Tamil work = **Tolkappiyam**.

nindian-history-13-4.s: The oldest extant Tamil grammar is the:
nindian-history-13-4.x: Tolkappiyam, which deals with grammar and poetics, is the oldest extant Tamil grammar.
n: Tolkappiyam is the oldest extant Tamil grammar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 57-60]
Tolkappiyam deals with grammar and poetics. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 57-60]
xa: Tolkappiyam is the only survivor of the **Second Sangam** (at **Kapatapuram**).
**Silappadikaram** by **Ilango Adigal** is the **first Tamil epic**.
**Tirukkural** by **Tiruvalluvar** — **1,330 couplets** in **Aram**, **Porul**, **Inbam**.
UPPSC 2014 key: **Tolkappiyam = grammar**, **Tirukkural = philosophy**.

n958f5b63a2c.s: Which classical account is associated with information on Muziris, pepper and Arikamedu?
n958f5b63a2c.x: The anonymous Greek work Periplus of the Erythraean Sea provides information on ports, Muziris, pepper and Arikamedu.
n958f5b63a2c.tq: Match the source with its distinctive geographical and commercial references.
xs: **Periplus of the Erythraean Sea** records **Muziris** pepper and **Arikamedu** — option **(3)**.
It is by an **anonymous Greek** and describes the **ports**.
**Iraiyanar Agapporul** gives the three-Sangam tradition; **Pliny** records spices, pearls, muslin.
xa: Periplus calls Arikamedu the **"market street of the Romans"**.
**Ptolemy's Geography** is another classical account.
Other classical writers: **Megasthenes**, **Strabo**.

nb4c6a3a81f8.s: Keezhadi is particularly important because it provides evidence of
o: The earliest Roman settlement in northern India
The first Gupta capital in the Tamil region
South Indian urbanisation contemporary with the Gangetic Second Urbanisation
The exclusive use of Sanskrit in the Pandya country
nb4c6a3a81f8.x: Keezhadi is considered the most important Sangam urban excavation and indicates South Indian urbanisation contemporary with the Gangetic Second Urbanisation.
nb4c6a3a81f8.tq: Infer the historical significance from the excavation’s comparative context.
xs: Keezhadi shows **South Indian urbanisation contemporary with the Gangetic Second Urbanisation** — option **(3)**.
It is the **most important Sangam urban excavation** (NextGen CA **2026**).
xa: **Arikamedu** = Indo-Roman trading settlement near Puducherry.
**Kaveripattinam (Puhar)** = Chola port with Yavana settlements.
Jul **2025**: a Tamil Nadu dig gave **Tamil-Brahmi potsherds**, **carnelian beads**, **weaving tools**.

naf3cf420808.s: The Pugalur inscription of the 1st century CE is important because it records
o: the founding of Arikamedu by Roman traders
naf3cf420808.x: The Pugalur inscription (1st c. CE) records three generations of Chera rulers. The Pandya embassy to Augustus is known from classical accounts; Arikamedu was an Indo-Roman trading settlement, not founded by an inscription's record; the Battle of Venni is known from Sangam poems on Karikala.
xs: The **Pugalur inscription** (**1st c. CE**) records **three generations of Chera rulers** — option **(1)**.
**Arikamedu** was an Indo-Roman trading settlement known from the **Periplus**.
xa: **Padirruppattu** (Ettuthogai) is about **Chera kings**.
**Ilango Adigal** was brother of **Chera Senguttuvan**.
Pliny: **spices from Chera**.

ncde45732ad2.s: Sangam literature was composed in Tamil, while the contemporary Satavahanas used:
ncde45732ad2.x: Tamil was the language of Sangam literature, while the contemporary Satavahanas used Prakrit.
xa: Sangam corpus: about **2,400 poems** in old Tamil.
**Tamil-Brahmi** dating to the **3rd c. BCE** supports the early limit.
Oldest Tamil work: **Tolkappiyam** (grammar and poetics).

nd80a221db0a.s: Korkai was the port of which Sangam kingdom?
nd80a221db0a.x: Korkai was the Pandya port; the Chola port was Kaveripattinam (Puhar), with the capital at Uraiyur.
xa: Chera **Vanji** is identified with **Karur (Karuvur)**; Chera ports also include **Tondi**.
Chola capital shifted **Uraiyur → Puhar**.
Heartland rivers: Chola **Kaveri**, Pandya **Vaigai**.

n94048f30835.s: The heartland river of the Sangam-age Pandya kingdom was the:
n94048f30835.x: The Pandya heartland around Madurai lay on the Vaigai. The Kaveri was the Chola river and the Periyar the Chera river.
xa: Pandya capital **Madurai**, port **Korkai**, emblem **fish**.
Pandya territory: **southern Tamil Nadu**.
Last renowned Pandya: **Ugra Peruvaludhi**.

nd169329b9d1.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the shift in the Chola capital?
nd169329b9d1.x: The Chola capital shifted from Uraiyur to Puhar. Vanji and Madurai were associated with the Cheras and Pandyas respectively.
nd169329b9d1.tq: Test the direction of a capital shift rather than merely naming the two places.
xs: The Chola capital shifted **Uraiyur to Puhar** — option **(4)**.
**Vanji** was Chera; **Madurai** was Pandya; **Korkai** was a Pandya port.
xa: Chola port: **Kaveripattinam (Puhar)**.
Chera **Vanji** is identified with **Karur**.
Chola emblem **tiger**, river **Kaveri**.

ne593c7eb791.s: In Sangam polity, the minor hill and forest chieftains were called:
ne593c7eb791.x: Minor hill and forest chieftains were the Velir; Enadi was a title of army commanders and Avai the royal court.
xa: **Aimperunkulu** — **five-member advisory body** of ministers, priests, commanders, envoys and spies.
Velir chiefs **Pari, Athiyaman, Ay** were allies or rivals of the **Muvendar**.
**Seven great patrons (Kadai ezhu vallals):** Pari, Kari, Ori, Pegan, Ay, Athiyaman, Nalli.
Sangam polity = **hereditary monarchy** + subordinate chieftains.

o: Military unit under the Velir chiefs
Royal court consisting only of poets
n1f70725044c.x: Aimperunkulu was a five-member advisory body consisting of ministers, priests, commanders, envoys and spies.
n1f70725044c.tq: Identify an institution from its numerical composition and functions.
xs: **Aimperunkulu** was a **five-member advisory body** — option **(4)**.
Members: **ministers, priests, commanders, envoys, spies**.
The court with poets was the **Avai**; the seven great patrons were the **Kadai ezhu vallals**.
xa: King = **Ko, Kon, Mannan, Vendan**.
Army commanders' title: **Enadi**.
**Velir** = minor hill/forest chieftains.

n91cf90e6d8c.s: In the Sangam age, Nalli was one of the:
n91cf90e6d8c.x: Nalli was one of the seven great patrons, not a minister of the Aimperunkulu.
xa: Seven patrons: **Pari, Kari, Ori, Pegan, Ay, Athiyaman, Nalli**.
Aimperunkulu: ministers, priests, commanders, envoys, spies.
Velir chiefs were **allies or rivals** of the Muvendar.

n510820a3b67.s: The three crowned kings of early Tamilakam were collectively known as:
n510820a3b67.x: Chera, Chola and Pandya rulers were collectively called the Muvendar, meaning the three crowned kings.
n510820a3b67.tq: Identify the collective political term from a group of related institutions and titles.
xs: The three crowned kings were the **Muvendar** — option **(1)**.
**Aimperunkulu** = five-member advisory body; **Velir** = minor hill/forest chiefs; **Kadai ezhu vallals** = seven great patrons.
xa: Muvendar = **Chera** (bow), **Chola** (tiger), **Pandya** (fish).
Muvendar rivalry + **Roman trade** shaped early Tamil polity.
**Pallavas** were not a Sangam dynasty.

n7e55bc1dd52.s: Senguttuvan is known in early Tamil history as the:
o: Chola king who shifted the capital to Puhar
Pandya king who defeated the Cheras at Venni
Chera king who founded the Chola dynasty
Red Chera who founded the Pattini cult
n7e55bc1dd52.x: Senguttuvan, known as the Red Chera, founded the Pattini cult centred on Kannagi.
n7e55bc1dd52.tq: Use the title and distinctive achievement to distinguish closely associated rulers.
xs: Senguttuvan was the **Red Chera** who **founded the Pattini cult** — option **(4)**.
He ruled in the **2nd c. CE**; his brother **Ilango Adigal** wrote **Silappadikaram**.
xa: Pattini cult = worship of **Kannagi** as the **ideal wife**.
The idol stone was brought from the **Himalayas**.
Sri Lankan king **Gajabahu** is said to have attended the consecration.

n327bf6f54b6.s: Udiyanjeral (Perum Sorru Udhiyan Cheralathan) of the Sangam age was an early ruler of which dynasty?
n327bf6f54b6.x: Udiyanjeral was an early Chera ruler; the pair 'Udiyanjeral - Chola' was the wrong pair in UPSC 2026. The Cholas and Pandyas were the other Muvendar, and the Pallavas were not a Sangam dynasty.
xs: **Udiyanjeral** (Perum Sorru Udhiyan Cheralathan) was an early **Chera** ruler — option **(2)**.
⚠ **UPSC 2026**: "Udiyanjeral-Chola" was the **wrong pair**.
**Pallavas** were not a Sangam dynasty.
xa: Other Chera: **Imayavaramban Nedunjeral Adan** — boundary up to the **Himalayas**.
**Senguttuvan** ("Red Chera") founded the **Pattini cult**.
Chera capital **Vanji (Karur)**; port **Muziris**.

n07c355708c7.s: Who among the following rulers is associated with both the title ‘Arya Padai Kadantha’ and the execution of Kovalan?
n07c355708c7.x: Arya Padai Kadantha Nedunjeliyan was the Pandya ruler who executed Kovalan. Imayavaramban Nedunjeral Adan bore a different title connected with the Himalayas.
n07c355708c7.tq: Separate rulers by their distinctive titles and associated deeds.
xs: **Arya Padai Kadantha Nedunjeliyan**, a **Pandya**, executed **Kovalan** — option **(3)**.
**Senguttuvan** was Chera; **Karikala** was Chola; **Imayavaramban Nedunjeral Adan** was a Chera whose title refers to the **Himalayas**.
xa: Another **Nedunjeliyan** won **Talaiyalanganam** (Tanjore) — title Talaiyalanganattu Cheruvenra Nedunjeliyan.
Other Pandyas: **Nediyon**, **Mudathirumaran**; last renowned: **Ugra Peruvaludhi**.
After Kovalan's execution, **Kannagi** burnt Madurai and became the Pattini deity.

n9bf4df7cbc3.s: The Telugu Choda families of Renati, Pottapi and Nellore claimed descent from:
n9bf4df7cbc3.x: The Renati, Pottapi and Nellore Choda families claimed descent from Karikala Chola.
n9bf4df7cbc3.tq: Link regional dynastic claims with the ancestor named in the tradition.
xs: The **Renati, Pottapi and Nellore Chodas** claimed descent from **Karikala Chola** — option **(2)**.
Karikala won **Venni** and built **Kallanai** across the **Kaveri**.
xa: Chola territory reached **southern Andhra**.
Chola capital shifted **Uraiyur → Puhar**.
Karikala is the subject of **Pattinappalai**.

ndf55074cfde.s: Which Chola ruler, victor at Venni and Vahaipparandalai, is the subject of Pattinappalai?
ndf55074cfde.x: Karikala Chola won the battles of Venni and Vahaipparandalai, reclaimed forest land and is associated with Pattinappalai.
xa: Venni: Cheras, Pandyas and **11** chieftains defeated.
**Kallanai (Grand Anicut)** across the **Kaveri**.
Telugu Choda families claimed descent from **Karikala**.

n5de97a54cbc.s: The Battle of Talaiyalanganam resulted in:
o: Chera control over the Kaveri delta
The establishment of Roman authority at Muziris
Pandya control over the Tamil country under Nedunjeliyan
Chola defeat by nine Velir chiefs
n5de97a54cbc.x: Nedunjeliyan of the Pandyas won at Talaiyalanganam and gained control over the Tamil country.
n5de97a54cbc.tq: Match the battle with its victor and political result.
xs: Talaiyalanganam gave **Pandya control over the Tamil country under Nedunjeliyan** — option **(3)**.
The battle was fought at **Tanjore**.
xa: His title: **Talaiyalanganattu Cheruvenra Nedunjeliyan**.
⚠ **Venni** (Karikala): Cheras, Pandyas and **11** chieftains defeated; **Vahaipparandalai**: **9** chieftains submitted.
Last renowned Pandya: **Ugra Peruvaludhi**.

n260458cdc52.s: The Cheras are associated with which of the following developments?
o: Establishing Korkai as the Chola capital
Building a temple of Augustus near Muziris
Founding the Pattini cult at Madurai
n260458cdc52.x: The Cheras traded with Rome and are said to have built a temple of Augustus near Muziris.
n260458cdc52.tq: Match the foreign-trade connection with the correct kingdom and port.
xs: The Cheras are said to have built **a temple of Augustus near Muziris** — option **(3)**.
They **traded with Rome** through **Muziris (Musiri)**.
**Korkai** was a Pandya port; **Kallanai** was on the **Kaveri** (Karikala); the **Pattini cult** was founded by Chera **Senguttuvan**, not at Madurai.
xa: Chera capital **Vanji (Karur)**; emblem **bow**.
Chera territory: **central/north Kerala + Kongu**.
**Senguttuvan** ("Red Chera", **2nd c. CE**) founded the Pattini cult.

nindian-history-15-11.s: Naura, Tondi, Mushiri (Muziris) and Nelisanda were major Sangam-age ports on the:
o: eastern coast, mainly in the Chola country
western coast, mainly in the Chera country
nindian-history-15-11.x: All four were major western-coast ports of the Sangam age, mainly in the Chera country.
n: Naura was a major Sangam western-coast port. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 64-67]
Tondi was a major Sangam western-coast port. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 64-67]
Mushiri or Muziris was a major western-coast port. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 64-67]
Nelisanda was a major western-coast port. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 64-67]
Tondi and Mushiri were important western-coast ports. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 64-67]
xa: **Tondi** and **Mushiri** were the **Chera** ports.
East-coast ports: **Puhar** (Chola) and **Korkai** (Pandya).
**Arikamedu** — Sangam-period site with **Roman objects**.
**Uraiyur** — Chola **cotton** centre, mentioned in the **Periplus**.

n984037a0487.s: The Chola territory during the Sangam period was primarily centred on the:
o: Southern Tamil Nadu around Madurai and Korkai
Central and northern Kerala and Kongu region
Kaveri delta, extending from Tiruchi up to southern Andhra
n984037a0487.x: The Chola heartland was the Kaveri delta, extending from Tiruchi up to southern Andhra. Central and northern Kerala and Kongu were associated with the Cheras.
n984037a0487.tq: Use territorial boundaries to distinguish the three Sangam kingdoms.
xs: Chola territory centred on the **Kaveri delta (Tiruchi) up to southern Andhra** — option **(4)**.
**Central/north Kerala + Kongu** was **Chera**; **southern Tamil Nadu** (Madurai, Korkai) was **Pandya**.
xa: Chola capital: **Uraiyur**, later **Puhar**; emblem **tiger**.
Chola port: **Kaveripattinam (Puhar)**.
**Telugu Choda** families (Renati, Pottapi, Nellore) claimed descent from **Karikala Chola**.

n63e3cb34d67.s: The Pallavas, who were not a Sangam dynasty, rose from which century CE?
n63e3cb34d67.x: The Pallavas rose from the fourth century CE; the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas were the three Sangam dynasties.
xa: Capitals: **Vanji** (Chera), **Uraiyur/Puhar** (Chola), **Madurai** (Pandya).
Ports: **Muziris** (Chera), **Kaveripattinam** (Chola), **Korkai** (Pandya).
Pandya power waned under the **Kalabhra** invasion.

n63a4563cf42.s: The Pattini cult founded by Senguttuvan centred on the worship of Kannagi as the:
n63a4563cf42.x: The Pattini cult centred on Kannagi, regarded as the ideal wife. Senguttuvan brought stone from the Himalayas for her idol.
n63a4563cf42.tq: Identify the central idea of a cult rather than its political or geographical setting.
xs: The Pattini cult worshipped **Kannagi** as the **ideal wife** — option **(1)**.
It was founded by **Chera Senguttuvan**.
xa: The idol stone came from the **Himalayas** (Himalayan expedition).
Sri Lankan king **Gajabahu** is said to have attended the consecration.
Kannagi's husband Kovalan was executed by **Arya Padai Kadantha Nedunjeliyan**.

n6b444d014ea.s: The power of the Pandyas declined under the:
n6b444d014ea.x: Pandya power waned under the Kalabhra invasion.
n6b444d014ea.tq: Identify the cause of political decline from a set of nearby historical events.
xs: Pandya power declined under the **Kalabhra invasion** — option **(4)**.
The **Himalayan expedition** was Senguttuvan's; **Vahaipparandalai** was a Karikala victory.
xa: Last renowned Pandya: **Ugra Peruvaludhi**.
Pandya capital **Madurai**, port **Korkai**, emblem **fish**.
**Nedunjeliyan's** win at **Talaiyalanganam** gave control over the Tamil country.

n6a77562d075.s: Pari, Kari, Ori, Pegan, Ay, Athiyaman and Nalli are collectively known as the:
n6a77562d075.x: These seven were the great patrons, the Kadai ezhu vallals; Nedunjeliyan, a Pandya ruler, was not among them.
xa: **Pari**, **Athiyaman** and **Ay** were also **Velir** chiefs.
Velir = minor hill/forest chieftains.
Other Pandyas: **Nediyon**, **Mudukudumi Peruvaludhi**, **Mudathirumaran**.

n6920160fc89.s: The Leiden copper plates are significant in relation to early Tamil history because their ring seal depicts the:
o: Chola tiger with the Pandya two fish and the Chera bow
Tiger and fish together as symbols of Roman authority
Chera bow alone, signifying Chera independence from Rome
Pandya fish with the Chola elephant and Pallava lion
n6920160fc89.x: The seal shows the Chola tiger with the Pandya two fish and the Chera bow, marking Chola victory over both the Pandyas and Cheras.
n6920160fc89.tq: Interpret a symbol-bearing historical artefact by linking each emblem to its dynasty.
xs: The ring seal shows the **Chola tiger with the Pandya two fish and the Chera bow** — option **(1)**.
It marks a **Chola victory over both** Pandyas and Cheras.
xa: **Leiden copper plates** (**18 May 2026**) record Chola grants to the **Chulamanivarma vihara, Nagapattinam**.
Muvendar emblems: Chera **bow**, Chola **tiger**, Pandya **fish**.
Muvendar rivalry + Roman trade shaped early Tamil polity.

n291f22eebd0.s: In the Tolkappiyam's list of four castes, which group stands fourth?
n291f22eebd0.x: The Tolkappiyam lists Arasar, Anthanar, Vanigar and Vellalar, with Vellalar fourth.
xa: **APPSC-G1 2024**: "Vellalars were rich peasants who formed the fourth caste".
Distractors in that question: poets, labourers, forest tribes.
**Brahmins** were present and respected.
