Last ruler **Kirtivarman II** fell to **Dantidurga** (c. **753-757 CE**).

nindian-history-144-2-1.s: The Badami Chalukyas ruled approximately during which period?
nindian-history-144-2-1.x: The Badami (Vatapi) Chalukyas ruled from about 543 CE, under Pulakeshin I, to 753 CE, when Dantidurga overthrew Kirtivarman II. The other ranges are reigns of single kings: Vikramaditya I, Pulakeshin II and Kirtivarman II.
nindian-history-144-2-1.tq: Discriminate the dynasty's span from individual reigns.
n: The Badami Chalukya dynasty existed from c. 543 to 753 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
The Badami Chalukya dynasty was also called the Chalukyas of Badami. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
The Badami Chalukya dynasty was also called the Vatapi Chalukyas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
xs: The Badami Chalukyas ruled **c. 543–753 CE** — option **(2)**.
They began with **Pulakeshin I** (c. **543**) and ended when **Dantidurga** overthrew **Kirtivarman II**.
The other ranges are single reigns: **Vikramaditya I** (c. **655-680**), **Pulakeshin II** (**610-642**), **Kirtivarman II** (c. **746-753**).
xa: ⚠ Other notes give the span as c. **543-757 CE**.
Capital **Vatapi** = present-day **Badami**, **Bagalkot**, Karnataka.
Their rule was mainly confined to the **Deccan** and **Southern India**.
**Vikramaditya II** (c. **733-746**) captured **Kanchi** three times.

nindian-history-144-2-2.s: Which Badami Chalukya ruler annexed the Kadambas, the Gangas and the Mauryas of Konkan?
nindian-history-144-2-2.x: Kirtivarman I annexed the Kadambas, Gangas and Mauryas of Konkan; Pulakesin I performed the Ashvamedha and Pulakesin II took the title Dakshinapatheshwara.
n: The Ashvamedha was associated with Pulakeshin I. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Kirtivarman I annexed the Kadambas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Kirtivarman I annexed the Gangas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Kirtivarman I annexed the Mauryas of Konkan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Mangalesha was an important ruler between Kirtivarman I and Pulakeshin II. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Pulakeshin II held the title Dakshinapatheshwara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
xa: Mangalesha made the **earliest rock-cut caves at Badami**.
Kirtivarman I performed the **Bahusuvarna-Agnishtoma** (Mahakuta pillar inscription).
Pulakesin II killed Mangalesha at **Elapattu-Simbige**.
Pulakeshin I fortified Vatapi — Badami cliff inscription of **543 CE**.

nindian-history-144-2-9.s: Which Pallava king captured and destroyed Vatapi in 642 CE and took the title Vatapikonda?
nindian-history-144-2-9.x: The Pallava Narasimhavarman I destroyed Vatapi in 642 CE and took the title Vatapikonda; Chalukya power was later restored by Vikramaditya I.
n: Pallava king Narasimhavarman I captured Vatapi in 642 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Narasimhavarman I destroyed Vatapi in 642 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Narasimhavarman I assumed the title Vatapikonda. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Vikramaditya I restored Chalukya power after the Pallava invasion. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
xa: **Narasimhavarman I** and **Pulakeshin II** were an important enemy pair.
Pulakeshin II and **Harsha** were the other enemy pair.
**Kirtivarman II** was the **last ruler**, overthrown by **Dantidurga**.
**Vikramaditya II** defeated the Pallavas **three times**.

n2642807d06f.s: Pulakesin II defeated and killed Mangalesha at
n2642807d06f.x: After exile, Pulakesin II attacked and killed Mangalesha at Elapattu-Simbige in the Bana territory around 609-10 CE.
n2642807d06f.tq: Match the succession conflict with its specific place, avoiding better-known Chalukya battle sites.
xs: Exiled **Pulakesin II** attacked and killed **Mangalesha** at **Elapattu-Simbige** in the **Bana territory** (c. **609-10 CE**) — option **(4)**.
**Narmada** is where **Harsha** was stopped; **Kanchi** is the Pallava city taken by **Vikramaditya II**; **Pithapuram** was the Eastern Chalukya capital.
xa: Cause: Mangalesha, regent for Kirtivarman I's minor sons, **refused to hand over power**.
Pulakesin II then reigned **609-642 CE** — the zenith of the dynasty.
Mangalesha's regency: **597-609**.

n7004cd5267e.s: Pulakesin II exchanged embassies with which Persian king?
n7004cd5267e.x: Pulakesin II exchanged embassies with the Persian king Khusrau II; the Ajanta Cave 1 painting once read as this embassy is now doubted.
xa: China-India relations under the Chalukyas are described by **Ma Twan-lin** (UPPSC 2014 key: "Matwalin").
Pulakesin II was the first South Indian king to issue **gold coins**.
Hiuen Tsang's account is the **Si-yu-ki**.

n7b660ac8cce.s: Which one of the following inscriptions records the appointment of Kubja Vishnuvardhana as viceroy of Vengi?
n7b660ac8cce.x: The Satara inscription of 617 CE records Pulakesin II's appointment of his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana as viceroy of Vengi.
n7b660ac8cce.tq: Use the inscription–event pair; nearby inscriptions are used as person-and-deed traps.
xs: The **Satara inscription (617 CE)** records the appointment of Pulakesin II's brother **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** as viceroy of **Vengi** — option **(2)**.
The **Badami cliff inscription** (543 CE) records Pulakesin I's fortification of Vatapi; the **Aihole inscription** is Ravikirti's prasasti; **Kopparam** records the defeat of Mahendravarman I.
xa: Vishnuvardhana declared independence in **624 CE** = **Eastern Chalukyas**.
⚠ **617 CE** = appointment; **624 CE** = independence.
His own inscriptions: **Chipurupalli, Kopparam, Chejarala, Timmapuram**.

na4f16640bb8.s: In which year did Kubja Vishnuvardhana declare independence at Vengi, founding the Eastern Chalukya line?
na4f16640bb8.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana was appointed at Vengi in 617 CE after Pulakesin II's conquest and declared independence in 624 CE, with Pithapuram as capital.
xa: **Dandin** called Vengi "**Andhra Nagaram**".
The appointment is recorded in the **Satara inscription (617 CE)**.
First epigraphic reference to **Guntur** (as Kumturu) = **Pune copper plates** of Eastern Chalukya **Vishnuvardhana II**, **669 CE**.

nindian-history-144-2-24.s: The Aihole inscription, composed by Ravikirti, is written in which language?
nindian-history-144-2-24.x: The Aihole inscription is in Sanskrit (not Prakrit), in the Southern Brahmi script, and is the key source for Pulakeshin II.
n: The Aihole Inscription is a key source for Pulakeshin II. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Ravikirti composed the Aihole Inscription. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
The Aihole Inscription is in Sanskrit and Southern Brahmi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
xa: Dated **634 CE** by the **Saka era**; preserved at the **Meguti Jain Temple**.
It names **Kalidasa** and **Bharavi**.
It calls **Kirtivarman I** "the night of doom" to Nalas, Mauryas and Kadambas.
⚠ **Ravikirti** = poet; **Gunda Anivaritachari** = architect.

nebc98a59b94.s: Pulakesin II assumed the title Paramesvara after defeating:
nebc98a59b94.x: Pulakesin II took the title Paramesvara after defeating Harsha, not Mahendravarman I; his other titles included Dakshinapatheshwara, Satyashraya and Prithvivallabha.
xa: Reign: **609-642 CE**; first South Indian king to issue **gold coins**.
He did defeat Pallava **Mahendravarman I**, recorded in the **Maruturu and Kopparam** inscriptions.
The **Aihole inscription** records the victory over **Harsha** at the **Narmada**.

n0d7a1efd335.s: The Aihole inscription of Pulakesin II (634-35 CE) is engraved on which temple?
n0d7a1efd335.x: The Aihole prasasti by Ravikirti is on the Meguti Jain temple at Aihole; the Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal was built by Lokamahadevi.
xa: It names the poets **Kalidasa** and **Bharavi** (UPSC 1994, UPPSC 2013).
Victories listed include **Harsha** (Narmada), **Kadambas** (Banavasi), **Kalinga** and **Pishtapura (Pithapuram)**.
It calls **Kirtivarman I** "the **night of doom**" to the Nalas, Mauryas and Kadambas.

n64502f2e34d.s: According to the Aihole inscription, Pulakesin II defeated Harsha on the banks of which river?
n64502f2e34d.x: The Aihole inscription says Pulakesin II defeated Harsha at the Narmada; it also records victories over Kosala, Kalinga and the Pallavas.
xa: Other opponents: **Kadambas** (Banavasi), **Gangas**, **Alupas**, **Mauryas of Konkan**, **Latas**, **Malavas**, **Gurjaras**.
Author **Ravikirti**; date **634-35 CE**; at the **Meguti Jain temple**.
Pithapuram later became the capital of the **Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi**.

nindian-history-144-2-5.s: Ravikirti, author of the Aihole inscription, compared his fame with that of:
nindian-history-144-2-5.x: Ravikirti names Kalidasa and Bharavi in the Aihole inscription, claiming to equal their fame.
n: Kalidasa is mentioned in the Aihole Inscription. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Bharavi is mentioned in the Aihole Inscription. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Ravikirti compared his fame with the fame of Kalidasa and Bharavi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
xa: It is in **Sanskrit** and **Southern Brahmi**, dated **634 CE** (Saka era).
It is preserved at the **Meguti Jain Temple**, Aihole.
Ravikirti was the **Jain court poet** of Pulakesin II.
It lists Pulakesin II's victories over **Harsha**, Kadambas, Gangas, **Kalinga**, **Pishtapura**.

n59ff7772905.s: The Maruturu and Kopparam inscriptions associate Pulakesin II with which achievement in Andhra?
o: Foundation of the Eastern Chalukya kingdom at Pithapuram
Defeat of Harsha on the banks of the Godavari
Defeat of the Pallava ruler Mahendravarman I and control over the land between the Krishna and Godavari
Appointment of Kubja Vishnuvardhana as governor of Kalinga
n59ff7772905.x: The Maruturu and Kopparam inscriptions record Pulakesin II's defeat of Mahendravarman I and his securing of the territory between the Krishna and Godavari rivers.
n59ff7772905.tq: Match the inscription with the achievement rather than with a nearby Chalukya event.
xs: The **Maruturu and Kopparam** inscriptions record Pulakesin II's defeat of Pallava **Mahendravarman I**, securing the land between the **Krishna and Godavari** — option **(3)**.
**Harsha** was stopped at the **Narmada**, not the Godavari; the **Eastern Chalukya** kingdom grew from **Kubja Vishnuvardhana**'s independence in **624 CE**.
Kubja Vishnuvardhana was appointed viceroy of **Vengi** (Satara inscription), not of Kalinga.
xa: Mangalagiri = "**Mangalapura**": APPSC-GS 2018 key → **Marturu**; APPSC G2 2019 → **Kopparam**.
⚠ If both appear as options, choose **Marturu**.
Kubja Vishnuvardhana's own inscriptions: **Chipurupalli, Kopparam, Chejarala, Timmapuram**.

ne0ef9e08d1b.x: The literary author Dandin called Vengi ‘Andhra Nagaram’.
ne0ef9e08d1b.tq: Match the literary author with the distinctive geographical designation.
xs: **Dandin** called Vengi "**Andhra Nagaram**" — option **(4)**.
"**Mangalapura**" is Mangalagiri in the Marturu/Kopparam inscription; **Vatapi** is the Badami capital.
xa: Vengi conquest by Pulakesin II created the **Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi**, capital **Pithapuram**.
Before the conquest Vengi was held by the **Durjaya** dynasty.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana**: appointed **617 CE**, independent **624 CE**.

n3d1b354cf6c.s: The first epigraphic reference to Guntur, as Kumturu, is found in the Pune copper plates of
n3d1b354cf6c.x: The Pune copper plates of Eastern Chalukya Vishnuvardhana II, dated 669 CE, contain the first epigraphic reference to Guntur as Kumturu.
n3d1b354cf6c.tq: Separate the similarly named Vishnuvardhana rulers by linking the record to the specific copper plates.
xs: The first epigraphic reference to **Guntur** (as **Kumturu**) is in the **Pune copper plates** of Eastern Chalukya **Vishnuvardhana II**, **669 CE** — option **(1)**.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana** was the first Eastern Chalukya; his inscriptions are **Chipurupalli, Kopparam, Chejarala, Timmapuram**.
xa: Name evolution: **Kumturu → Gomturu → Gunturu**.
Source: **ASI Epigraphy**.
Mangalagiri appears as "**Mangalapura**" in the **Marturu** inscription of Pulakesin II.

n6c68aa176fe.s: The Vajapeya and Hiranyagarbha sacrifices performed by Chalukya kings were connected with their claim to
n6c68aa176fe.x: The Vajapeya and Hiranyagarbha sacrifices were used by Chalukya kings to claim Kshatriya status.
n6c68aa176fe.tq: Infer the social-political purpose of a ritual rather than merely recalling its name.
xs: The Chalukyas performed **Vajapeya** and **Hiranyagarbha** sacrifices to claim **Kshatriya status** — option **(3)**.
These were Vedic sacrifices; they had nothing to do with Buddhist authority, Vengi viceroyalty or the Persian embassy.
xa: **Pulakesin I** performed the **Ashvamedha**.
**Kirtivarman I** performed the **Bahusuvarna-Agnishtoma** (**Mahakuta pillar inscription**).
Embassies with Persia were exchanged by **Pulakesin II** with **Khusrau II** — a separate topic from the sacrifices.

n2f5c4e6d377.s: The Chinese account of China–India relations under the Chalukyas is credited to
n2f5c4e6d377.x: The account of China–India relations under the Chalukyas is credited to Ma Twan-lin, also rendered in some references as Matwalin. Hiuen Tsang visited Pulakesin II's kingdom and praised him in comparison with Harsha and Narasimhavarman.
n2f5c4e6d377.tq: Separate the Chinese historian credited with the account from the visiting traveller.
xs: The Chinese account of China-India relations under the Chalukyas is credited to **Ma Twan-lin** — option **(4)**; the **UPPSC 2014** key spells it "Matwalin".
**Hiuen Tsang** visited Pulakesin II and praised him in the **Si-yu-ki**, but the relations account is Ma Twan-lin's.
**Ravikirti** was the Jain court poet who wrote the **Aihole inscription**.
xa: Pulakesin II exchanged embassies with Persian **Khusrau II**.
The **Ajanta Cave 1** painting once read as the Persian embassy — identification **now doubted**.
Hiuen Tsang praised him along with **Harsha** and **Narasimhavarman**.

ne82af07e635.s: Which inscription of Pulakesin II refers to Mangalagiri as 'Mangalapura'?
ne82af07e635.x: The APPSC-GS 2018 key gives the Marturu inscription. The Aihole inscription is Ravikirti's prasasti and the Satara inscription records Kubja Vishnuvardhana's appointment to Vengi.
xa: ⚠ **APPSC G2 2019** (Carpe Diem PYQ book) names the **Kopparam inscription** — learn both; if both are options, choose **Marturu**.
Maruturu and Kopparam record the defeat of **Mahendravarman I** and the land between **Krishna and Godavari**.

n2e5a5048a2e.s: The Aihole inscription recording the Narmada victory of Pulakesin II belongs to which year?
n2e5a5048a2e.x: The Aihole record is dated 634 CE. It was composed by Ravikirti and records the defeat of Harsha.
n2e5a5048a2e.tq: Distinguish the date of the inscription from dates associated with Harsha's reign and the battle.
xs: The **Aihole inscription** recording the Narmada victory is dated **634 CE** — option **(3)**.
**618** is the date of the battle itself (JPSC 2016 key), not of the record.
It was composed by **Ravikirti**.
xa: ⚠ Since Aihole (634 CE) records the battle, the **637** date in some notes cannot be right — the battle must be earlier.
**Hiuen Tsang's** account confirms Harsha's defeat.
Victor **Pulakesin II** (UPPSC 2016); river **Narmada** (UPSC 2003).

nb79a7c0e787.s: The Battle of Pullalur (c. 618-619 CE), whose victor is disputed, was fought near:
nb79a7c0e787.x: Pullalur was fought near Kanchi around 618-619; Pallava records credit Mahendravarman I and Chalukya records claim victory for Pulakesin II.
xa: **Manimangala** (c. **642**): **Narasimhavarman I** over Pulakesin II.
**Vatapi** (**642**): capital sacked; general **Paranjoti**.
Round 1 gave Pulakesin II the **Krishna-Godavari** land (**Maruturu, Kopparam**).

n7873303308e.s: Which inscription, composed by Ravikirti, records the conflict between Pulakesin II and Harsha?
n7873303308e.x: The Aihole inscription by Ravikirti, together with Hiuen Tsang's account, is the source for the Pulakesin II-Harsha conflict; the Kailasanatha inscription is not.
xa: Battle date: **618 CE** (JPSC 2016 key); must predate **634 CE**.
Victor: **Pulakesin II** (UPPSC 2016).
Titles from this war: **Paramesvara** and **Dakshinapatheshwara**.

n2bc6010e857.s: In the first round of the Chalukya-Pallava conflict, Pulakesin II advanced up to:
n2bc6010e857.x: In the first round Pulakesin II advanced to Kanchi and won territory in the Krishna-Godavari region; in the second round Narasimhavarman I defeated him and took Vatapi.
xa: Round 1 won the **Krishna-Godavari** land for Pulakesin II (**Maruturu, Kopparam** inscriptions).
**Pullalur** (c. **618-19**) in Round 1 has a disputed victor.
Narasimhavarman I took the title **Vatapikonda**.

nd9c2b989ea0.x: Vikramaditya II took the title Kanchiyamkonda after taking Kanchi during the reign of Nandivarman II.
xa: He took Kanchi **three times** but spared it; entered c. **740**.
He gifted gold to the **Rajasimheshvara (Kailasanatha)** temple and left a **Kannada inscription** on its pillar.
Commemoration: Lokamahadevi's **Virupaksha temple**, Pattadakal.

n7672b045a08.s: Vikramaditya II occupied Kanchi around 740 CE during the reign of which Pallava king?
n7672b045a08.x: Vikramaditya II entered Kanchi c. 740 CE in Nandivarman II's reign, gifted gold to the Rajasimheshvara temple and left a Kannada inscription on a pillar.
xa: Rajasimheshvara = **Kailasanatha** temple.
The **Virupaksha temple**, Pattadakal, built by **Lokamahadevi**, copies the Kailasanatha of Kanchi.
His title: **Kanchiyamkonda**.

n9ae3b63a27c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Badami Chalukya society and administration?
o: Agraharas were land grants made to Brahmins.
Vatapi and Aihole had no urban or trade role.
R.S. Sharma called their spread the 'proliferation of the feudal land grant system'.
n9ae3b63a27c.x: Vatapi and Aihole were urban and trade centres, not purely religious ones, so that statement is false; the other three are correct.
xa: Units: **Rashtra / Vishaya** under **Vishayapati**; **Grama** under **Gramakuta / Gavunda**.
Feudatories: **Rashtrakutas**, **Alupas**, **Gangas**, **Sendrakas**.

ncfc948ae760.s: Vijayabhattarika, who issued land grants in her own name, was the queen of:
ncfc948ae760.x: Vijayabhattarika (Vijaya-mahadevi) was the queen of Chandraditya; she governed and issued land grants in her own name.
xa: PYQ: **UPPSC 2007** key — the **Chalukyas** frequently gave ladies high administrative positions.
Kalyani Chalukya princess **Akkadevi** governed **Kisukad**.
Queens **Lokamahadevi** and **Trailokyamahadevi** were temple patrons at **Pattadakal**.

neff315d3f34.s: Pulakesin II assumed the title ‘Paramesvara’ after his conflict with Harsha. He was also styled as:
neff315d3f34.x: Pulakesin II was styled Dakshinapatheshwara, meaning lord of the south, in opposition to Harsha’s title Uttarapatheshwara.
neff315d3f34.tq: Discriminate between the similar directional titles of Pulakesin II and Harsha.
xs: Pulakesin II was styled **Dakshinapatheshwara** ("lord of the south") — option **(1)**.
**Uttarapatheshwara** was **Harsha**'s title; **Vatapikonda** = Pallava **Narasimhavarman I**; **Kanchiyamkonda** = Chalukya **Vikramaditya II**.
xa: **Paramesvara** (Parameshvara) was assumed after defeating **Harsha**.
⚠ **Vatapikonda** = Narasimhavarman I (also **Mamalla**); **Kanchiyamkonda** = Vikramaditya II.
The Narmada victory is recorded in the **Aihole inscription** (**634 CE**).

nd1f96e08287.x: Narasimhavarman I assumed the title Vatapikonda, meaning conqueror of Vatapi, after capturing the Chalukya capital.
nd1f96e08287.tq: Use the title’s literal connection with the captured city.
xs: **Vatapikonda** ("conqueror of Vatapi") was the title of **Narasimhavarman I** — option **(1)**; he is also called **Mamalla**.
**Vikramaditya II** was **Kanchiyamkonda**; **Pulakesin II** was **Paramesvara / Dakshinapatheshwara**; **Vikramaditya I** recovered Vatapi.
xa: Narasimhavarman I captured Vatapi in **642 CE**, with general **Paranjoti**.
He also won at **Manimangala**, **Pariyala** and **Suramara**.
⚠ Vatapikonda = **Pallava**; Kanchiyamkonda = **Chalukya**.

ne2e55849814.s: The Renati Chodas of Rayalaseema were first feudatories of the early Pallavas and later of the:
ne2e55849814.x: The Renati Chodas were initially feudatories of the early Pallavas and subsequently of the Badami Chalukyas.
xa: The Pallava-Chalukya wars made **Rayalaseema** politically active → rise of **Renati Chodas, Banas, Vaidumbas**.
Other Chalukya feudatories: **Rashtrakutas, Alupas, Gangas, Sendrakas**.
An **8th-century Telugu inscription** at **Pitikayagulla** shows post-Badami Chalukya influence in Rayalaseema.

nd1640dc2788.s: The Pallava–Chalukya wars stimulated the rise of which powers in Rayalaseema?
nd1640dc2788.x: The wars stimulated political activity in Rayalaseema, including the rise of the Renati Chodas, Banas and Vaidumbas.
xa: **8th-century Telugu inscription** at **Pitikayagulla** → post-Badami Chalukya influence.
Records of Eastern and Kalyani Chalukyas lie in the **Nallamala Tiger Reserve**.
The **Renati Chodas** were feudatories first of the early **Pallavas**, then of the **Badami Chalukyas**.

nb964062a375.s: Which pair of queens commissioned the Virupaksha and Mallikarjuna temples at Pattadakal?
nb964062a375.x: Lokamahadevi and Trailokyamahadevi, queens of Vikramaditya II, commissioned the Virupaksha and Mallikarjuna temples at Pattadakal.
nb964062a375.tq: Start from the sure association between Vikramaditya II’s queens and the Pattadakal temples.
xs: **Lokamahadevi** and **Trailokyamahadevi**, queens of **Vikramaditya II**, patronised the **Virupaksha** and **Mallikarjuna** temples at **Pattadakal** — option **(2)**.
**Ayyana Mahadevi** and **Chamakamba** were Eastern Chalukya queens; **Vijayabhattarika** was Chandraditya's queen; **Akkadevi** a Kalyani Chalukya princess.
xa: The **Virupaksha** temple copies the **Kailasanatha** of Kanchi, commemorating Vikramaditya II's Kanchi victory.
**Vijayabhattarika** governed and issued land grants in her own name.
UPPSC 2007 key: the **Chalukyas** often gave women high administrative posts.

nc71621f8a82.s: An eighth-century Telugu inscription in early Telugu script found at Pitikayagulla is significant because it indicates:
o: The origin of the Rashtrakuta dynasty in Kanchi
The direct rule of Harsha in Rayalaseema
nc71621f8a82.x: The Pitikayagulla inscription indicates post-Badami Chalukya influence in Rayalaseema and is written in early Telugu script.
nc71621f8a82.tq: Use the inscription’s place, date and script to identify its historical significance.
xs: The **8th-century Telugu inscription** in early Telugu script at **Pitikayagulla** (Rayalaseema) shows **post-Badami Chalukya influence** — option **(1)**.
It has nothing to do with the Pallava occupation of Vatapi (**642**), Rashtrakuta origins or Harsha.
xa: Records of the **Eastern** and **Kalyani Chalukyas** are found in the **Nallamala Tiger Reserve**.
Rayalaseema powers that rose in this period: **Renati Chodas, Banas, Vaidumbas**.
The **Renati Chodas** were feudatories of the early Pallavas, then of the Badami Chalukyas.

nindian-history-144-2-15.s: Which Badami Chalukya queen administered the kingdom after the death of her husband Chandraditya?
nindian-history-144-2-15.x: Vijaya Bhattarika, queen of Chandraditya, governed after his death, reflecting how the Badami Chalukyas often gave women high administrative posts.
n: The Chalukyas frequently gave high-ranking administrative positions to women. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
Vijaya Bhattarika administered the kingdom after her husband's death. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #144-2 · pp 252-254]
xa: Vijaya Bhattarika **issued two copper plates** in her own name and was a **poetess**.
**Kumkumdevi**, sister of **Vikramaditya I**, got a village granted to a **Jain monastery**.
Queens **Lokamahadevi** and **Trailokyamahadevi** built the **Virupaksha** and **Mallikarjuna** temples, Pattadakal.
Kalyani Chalukya princess **Akkadevi** governed a province (**Kisukad**).

n410fd6c1a0d.s: Aihole is popularly described by K. A. Nilakanta Sastri as the:
n410fd6c1a0d.x: K. A. Nilakanta Sastri described Aihole as the “Cradle of Indian temple architecture.”
n410fd6c1a0d.tq: Recall the distinctive epithet associated with the architectural centre.
xs: **K.A. Nilakanta Sastri** called **Aihole** the "**Cradle of Indian temple architecture**" — option **(2)**.
Aihole represents the **experimental, structural** phase; the **coronation** site was **Pattadakal**.
xa: Aihole temples: **Lad Khan** (flat roof), **Durga** (apsidal), **Meguti** (Jain, with the Aihole inscription), **Huchimalligudi** (Nagara).
**Lad Khan** has the earliest massive bracket capital (RPSC 2018: early Chalukya temple).
**Pattadakal**: UNESCO World Heritage Site (**1987**).

nd5db2abb4d8.s: The architectural importance of Pattadakal lies especially in the fact that it:
o: Represents the exclusive triumph of the Nagara style in the Deccan
Contains only rock-cut temples of the Badami period
Was built entirely without royal patronage
Contains Nagara and Dravida temples standing side by side
nd5db2abb4d8.x: Pattadakal displays Nagara and Dravida temple forms side by side and represents the mature phase of Chalukyan architecture.
nd5db2abb4d8.tq: Use the side-by-side comparison of styles as the distinguishing feature of the site.
xs: **Pattadakal** has **Nagara and Dravida temples standing side by side** — option **(4)**.
It is the **mature** structural phase, not rock-cut; it had royal patronage (queens **Lokamahadevi** and **Trailokyamahadevi**).
xa: Nagara: **Papanatha**, **Kashi Vishwanatha**, **Galaganatha**.
Dravida: **Virupaksha** (modelled on Kailasanatha, Kanchi), **Mallikarjuna**, **Sangameshvara**.
UNESCO World Heritage Site: **1987**.

nap-history-6-1.s: Which temple is regarded as the oldest Saivite temple?
nap-history-6-1.x: Parasurameswara Temple at Gudimallam, with its early Shiva linga, is regarded as the oldest Saivite temple. Arasavalli is a Surya temple and Hampi and Alampur temples are much later.
nap-history-6-1.tq: Recall the earliest Saivite site in Andhra.
n: Parasurameswara Temple is located at Gudimallam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
Parasurameswara Temple is the oldest Saivite temple. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
xs: The **Parasurameswara Temple, Gudimallam** is the **oldest Saivite temple** — option **(2)**.
Temple architecture in Andhra was **initiated** during the **Ikshvaku period**.
The **Navabrahma** temples at **Alampur** are a later **Badami Chalukya** complex of **9 temples** (7th-8th century CE).
xa: Alampur lies on the **Tungabhadra**, in **Jogulamba Gadwal**, Telangana.
The Navabrahma temples are in **Nagara** style.
Alampur is called **Dakshina Kashi** and has the **Jogulamba Shakti Peetha**.
Eastern Chalukyas carried the Vesara style into Andhra (**Bikkavolu, Draksharama**).

nce748586bd4.s: Which of the four main Badami cave temples is a Jain cave?
nce748586bd4.x: Badami has four principal sandstone caves of the 6th-7th centuries, the earliest made under Mangalesha; the fourth cave is Jain.
xa: Cave 1: Shiva as **18-armed Nataraja**; Caves 2 and 3: **Vishnu**.
Cave 3 is the largest, with Mangalesha's inscription of **578 CE**.
The caves lie in sandstone around **Agastya lake**.

n87111d7cf33.s: Which temple at Aihole has the earliest massive bracket capital?
n87111d7cf33.x: The Lad Khan temple, rectangular with a flat roof and stone grilles (and no shikhara), has the earliest massive bracket capital.
xa: It has **12 carved pillars** in the mukha mandapa; dedicated to **Shiva**.
RPSC 2018: Lad Khan = **early Chalukya temple**.
⚠ The **Durga temple**, also at Aihole, does have a **Nagara** shikhara on an apsidal plan.

na4897fd95bd.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the temples at Pattadakal?
o: The Papanatha temple is built in the Dravida style.
The Mallikarjuna temple was built by Queen Trailokyamahadevi in the Dravida style.
The Virupaksha temple is modelled on the Kailasanatha temple of Kanchi.
The Virupaksha temple was built by Queen Lokamahadevi to mark Vikramaditya II's victory over the Pallavas.
na4897fd95bd.x: The Papanatha temple (like Kashi Vishwanatha) is in the Nagara style, not Dravida; the other three statements are correct.
xa: Other Pattadakal Nagara temples: **Kashi Vishwanatha**, **Galaganatha**; **Sangameshvara** is Dravida.
Virupaksha architects: **Gunda Anivaritachari** and **Sarvasiddhi Acharya**.

n71c272e9ec2.s: The narrative friezes at Pattadakal depict scenes from the Ramayana, the Mahabharata and the:
n71c272e9ec2.x: Pattadakal is noted for narrative friezes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Panchatantra, along with Nandi mandapas and polished pillars.
xa: Pattadakal = **mature** phase, **Nagara and Dravida side by side**.
Royal **coronation** site; UNESCO **1987**.
**Virupaksha** copies the Pallava **Kailasanatha**; the Rashtrakuta **Kailasa (Ellora)** continues the line.

na7eba33215d.s: The Navabrahma temples of the Badami Chalukyas at Alampur stand on the banks of which river?
na7eba33215d.x: The Navabrahma group is a complex of nine Nagara temples on the Tungabhadra at Alampur, built by the Badami Chalukyas in the 7th-8th centuries.
xa: Alampur = **Dakshina Kashi**; has the **Jogulamba Shakti Peetha**.
District: **Jogulamba Gadwal, Telangana** (earlier **Mahabubnagar**, undivided AP).
Alampur is the place in the **Telugu region** with Badami Chalukyan temples.

na956d4f6d88.s: The plan of the Durga temple at Aihole is best described as:
o: Apsidal or gajaprishtha, with a pillared gallery around the shrine
Square, with a pyramidal vimana and four gopurams
Rectangular, with a flat roof and stone grilles
na956d4f6d88.x: The Durga temple has an apsidal, or gajaprishtha, plan and a pillared gallery running around the shrine.
na956d4f6d88.tq: Use the plan and circumambulatory arrangement to identify the temple.
xs: The **Durga temple**, Aihole, has an **apsidal (gajaprishtha) plan** with a **pillared gallery** round the shrine — option **(1)**.
The rectangular, flat-roofed temple with stone grilles is **Lad Khan**.
xa: Durga temple carries a **Nagara** shikhara on its apsidal plan.
Aihole = "**Cradle of Indian temple architecture**" (Nilakanta Sastri).
Other Aihole Nagara temple: **Huchimalligudi** (UPSC 2026).

n26dca81718e.s: Alampur is also known by which of the following names, and is associated with which religious centre?
o: Dakshina Gaya and the Kamakhya Shakti Peetha
Uttarapatha Kashi and the Bhramaramba Shakti Peetha
Karnataka Kashi and the Mahalakshmi Shakti Peetha
Dakshina Kashi and the Jogulamba Shakti Peetha
n26dca81718e.x: Alampur is called Dakshina Kashi and contains the Jogulamba Shakti Peetha.
n26dca81718e.tq: Test the paired association of a place epithet and its religious significance.
xs: **Alampur** is called **Dakshina Kashi** and has the **Jogulamba Shakti Peetha** — option **(4)**.
⚠ Do not confuse it with **Dakshina Gaya** or other "Kashi" epithets in the options; the notes give only **Dakshina Kashi**.
xa: It has the **Navabrahma** complex of **9 temples** on the **Tungabhadra**, in **Nagara** style.
Built by the **Badami Chalukyas**, **7th-8th century CE**.
District: **Jogulamba Gadwal, Telangana** (earlier Mahabubnagar).

nb646ea2b131.s: Ravikirti, associated with the Meguti inscription at Aihole, was primarily a:
nb646ea2b131.x: Ravikirti was the poet and composer named in the Aihole Meguti inscription, not the architect of the temple.
nb646ea2b131.tq: Test the professional identity of the named individual rather than merely recalling the inscription’s location.
xs: **Ravikirti** was a **poet and composer**, named in the **Meguti inscription, Aihole** — option **(1)**.
He was **not an architect**; the architects (sutradhari) named at Virupaksha are **Gunda Anivaritachari** and **Sarvasiddhi Acharya**.
xa: ⚠ **Ravikirti** = poet; **Gunda Anivaritachari** = architect.
The **Meguti** (Jain) temple at Aihole is **Dravida** and bears the Aihole inscription.
Royal patrons were queens **Lokamahadevi** (Virupaksha) and **Trailokyamahadevi** (Mallikarjuna).

nf89a991555b.s: The inscriptions at the Virupaksha temple, Pattadakal, name which individuals as architects or sutradharis?
nf89a991555b.x: The Virupaksha temple inscriptions name the architects Gunda Anivaritachari and Sarvasiddhi Acharya.
nf89a991555b.tq: Distinguish named architects from patrons, rulers and literary figures.
xs: Virupaksha inscriptions name the architects (sutradhari) **Gunda Anivaritachari and Sarvasiddhi Acharya** — option **(4)**.
**Lokamahadevi** and **Trailokyamahadevi** were royal **patrons**, not architects; **Ravikirti** was a poet.
xa: ⚠ **Ravikirti** = poet (Meguti inscription); **Gunda Anivaritachari** = architect.
Virupaksha was built by **Lokamahadevi** for **Vikramaditya II**'s victory over the Pallavas.
It is **Dravida**, modelled on the **Kailasanatha, Kanchi**.

nc0584a2d5fa.s: According to Percy Brown's assessment, the Chalukyas were significant because they:
o: Introduced the first gopurams into Tamil Nadu
Were the first to break the monopoly of the rock-cut tradition in the Deccan
Abandoned structural temples in favour of Buddhist caves
Developed the Nagara style exclusively in North India
nc0584a2d5fa.x: Percy Brown credited the Chalukyas with being the first to break the monopoly of the rock-cut tradition in the Deccan.
nc0584a2d5fa.tq: Identify the historian’s specific interpretation instead of confusing it with the general description of Aihole.
xs: **Percy Brown**: the Chalukyas were **first to break the monopoly of the rock-cut tradition** in the Deccan — option **(2)**.
They moved from **Badami** rock-cut caves to **structural** temples at **Aihole** and **Pattadakal**, not the reverse.
xa: **Nilakanta Sastri**: Aihole = "**Cradle of Indian temple architecture**".
**Pattadakal**: **Nagara and Dravida side by side** — mature phase.
This evolution is the birth of the **Vesara** style.

n4c9c0616037.s: Which of the following places in Andhra are cited as examples of the Eastern Chalukyan transmission of the Vesara or Chalukyan style?
n4c9c0616037.x: Bikkavolu and Draksharama are cited as Andhra examples of the Vesara or Chalukyan style carried by the Eastern Chalukyas.
n4c9c0616037.tq: Use the Andhra-specific examples rather than the original Karnataka centres of the style.
xs: The **Eastern Chalukyas** carried the Vesara/Chalukya style into Andhra at **Bikkavolu and Draksharama** — option **(4)**.
**Alampur** temples were built by the **Badami** Chalukyas; **Aihole, Badami, Pattadakal** are in Karnataka; **Ellora** is Rashtrakuta and **Kanchi** Pallava.
xa: **Alampur Navabrahma**: **9** Nagara temples on the **Tungabhadra**.
Line of influence: Pallava **Kailasanatha** → **Virupaksha**, Pattadakal → Rashtrakuta **Kailasa (Ellora)**.

n5515b6529e6.s: The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal copies the tradition of which temple?
n5515b6529e6.x: The Dravida-style Virupaksha temple copies the Pallava Kailasanatha tradition of Kanchi, a line continued by the Rashtrakuta Kailasa at Ellora.
xa: Virupaksha was built by Queen **Lokamahadevi** for Vikramaditya II's victory over the **Pallavas**.
Its architects: **Gunda Anivaritachari** and **Sarvasiddhi Acharya**.
⚠ UPSC 2026 trap: **Malegitti** and **Virupaksha** are Dravida, not Nagara.

n49554a3c001.s: The traditional territory of the Pallavas was known as:
n49554a3c001.x: Tondaimandalam was the traditional territory associated with the Pallavas, with Kanchipuram as their capital.
n49554a3c001.tq: Identify the territorial term rather than the capital city.
xs: The Pallava territory was **Tondaimandalam** — option **(2)** (APPSC-GS 2023).
Its capital was **Kanchipuram**.
**Vengi** was the seat of the **Eastern Chalukyas**, not the Pallavas.
xa: One origin theory places them as **local Tamil** people of Tondaimandalam; others say **Parthian (Pahlava)** or **Andhra** origin.
Andhra angle: early Pallava charters **Mayidavolu** and **Manchikallu** are in Andhra.

n25f3b1ee0ec.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the theories proposed regarding the origin of the Pallavas?
o: Scythian origin from the north-western frontier
n25f3b1ee0ec.x: The major theories mentioned are Parthian or Pahlava origin, Andhra origin and local Tamil origin in Tondaimandalam. A Scythian-origin theory is not included.
n25f3b1ee0ec.tq: Separate the stated origin theories from an unrelated foreign-origin claim.
xs: A **Scythian origin** is not among the theories — option **(3)**.
The three theories are **Parthian (Pahlava)** foreign origin, **Andhra** origin and **local Tamil** origin in Tondaimandalam.
xa: Andhra theory: earliest **Prakrit** charters from the **Krishna-Guntur** region; early Pallavas replaced the **Ikshvakus** there.
Territory **Tondaimandalam**, capital **Kanchipuram**.

n69143c34722.s: The Andhra-origin theory of the Pallavas is supported chiefly by which combination of evidence?
o: Their association with the Kaveri delta and Chola inscriptions
Their Sanskrit inscriptions and control of Vatapi
Early Prakrit charters from the Krishna-Guntur region and replacement of the Ikshvakus
n69143c34722.x: The Andhra-origin theory draws support from early Prakrit charters found in the Krishna-Guntur region and the Pallavas’ replacement of the Ikshvakus there.
n69143c34722.tq: Identify the evidence that directly supports a proposed historical theory.
xs: The Andhra theory rests on the earliest **Prakrit charters** from the **Krishna-Guntur** region and the Pallavas' **replacement of the Ikshvakus** there — option **(4)**.
The **Talagunda inscription** concerns **Mayurasharman** and the Kadambas; **Vatapi** was held by Narasimhavarman I only after **642**.
xa: **Manchikallu** inscription of **Simhavarman**: conquest of **Vijayapuri** after defeating the Ikshvakus (APPSC-GS 2018).
Last Ikshvaku **Rudrapurushadatta** was defeated by **Simhavarma**.
**Mayidavolu** plates of **Sivaskandavarman** (as yuvaraja) — Prakrit, among the earliest Pallava records.

ne918aab4483.s: The Prakrit Mayidavolu plates, among the earliest Pallava records, were issued as yuvaraja by:
ne918aab4483.x: The Mayidavolu plates were issued by Sivaskandavarman as yuvaraja; the Manchikallu inscription belongs to the Pallava Simhavarman.
xa: Manchikallu records the conquest of **Vijayapuri** from the **Ikshvakus** (APPSC-GS 2018).
Last Ikshvaku: **Rudrapurushadatta**.
**Kudumiamalai** music inscription — credited to **Mahendravarman I**.

n05612d366a3.s: Which Pallava ruler’s defeat of the last Ikshvaku ruler Rudrapurushadatta helped establish Pallava rule in the Krishna valley?
n05612d366a3.x: Pallava Simhavarman defeated the last Ikshvaku ruler Rudrapurushadatta, an event associated with the establishment of Pallava rule in the Krishna valley.
n05612d366a3.tq: Distinguish the early Simhavarman from the better-known imperial Pallava rulers.
xs: Pallava **Simhavarman** defeated the last Ikshvaku **Rudrapurushadatta** → Pallava rule in the **Krishna valley** — option **(4)**.
Proof: the **Manchikallu inscription** records the conquest of **Vijayapuri** (APPSC-GS 2018).
⚠ **Simhavishnu** is a different, later ruler (c. **575-600**) who defeated the **Kalabhras**.
xa: APPSC-G2 2025: Manchikallu and Maidavolu = **Pallavas**.
This replacement of the Ikshvakus supports the **Andhra origin** theory.

n80f72a59a68.s: Narasimhavarman I defeated and killed Pulakesin II in 642 CE at:
n80f72a59a68.x: Narasimhavarman I killed Pulakesin II at Manimangala in 642 CE and sacked Vatapi through his general Paranjoti.
xa: Title: **Vatapikonda**; also **Mamalla**.
**Two naval expeditions** to Sri Lanka to restore ally prince **Manavarma**.
**Hiuen Tsang** visited Kanchi c. **640 CE** and praised him with Harsha and Pulakesin II.

n4566f656c97.s: Nandivarman II Pallavamalla came to the throne under which circumstances?
o: He was appointed by Vikramaditya II after the fall of Kanchi.
He inherited the throne directly from Simhavishnu as his eldest son.
He was elected by the public as an adult military commander.
He was chosen as a twelve-year-old by ministers and nobles from a collateral line.
n4566f656c97.x: After the death of Paramesvaravarman II around 731 CE, ministers and nobles selected Nandivarman II, a twelve-year-old from a collateral line.
n4566f656c97.tq: Distinguish hereditary succession from selection by ministers and nobles.
xs: **Nandivarman II Pallavamalla** was chosen as a boy of **12** by **ministers and nobles** from a **collateral line** — option **(4)**.
This followed the death of **Paramesvaravarman II** (c. **731**).
xa: He was an ardent **Vaishnavite** — built **Vaikuntha Perumal**, Kanchi; contemporary of Alvar **Tirumangai**.
He lost Kanchi temporarily to **Vikramaditya II** (Chalukya).
Title: **Pallavamalla**.

n05ef0e3ebd1.s: The Pallava dynasty was brought to an end when Aparajita was killed by:
n05ef0e3ebd1.x: Aditya I Chola killed Aparajita, bringing the Pallava dynasty to an end around 897–898 CE.
n05ef0e3ebd1.tq: Apply the ruler–ruler succession trap to the final event of a dynasty.
xs: **Aditya I Chola** killed **Aparajita**, ending the Pallavas — option **(3)** (c. **897-898 CE**).
**Vikramaditya II** and **Pulakesin II** were Chalukya enemies; **Simhavishnu** founded the imperial Pallava line.
xa: Later rulers before Aparajita: **Dantivarman, Nandivarman III, Nripatunga**.
Dynasty span: c. **275-897 CE**; capital **Kanchipuram**.

n63e9924a04d.s: The Pallava king Mahendravarman I was converted from Jainism to Shaivism by:
n63e9924a04d.x: Mahendravarman I began as a Jain and was converted to Shaivism by Appar (Tirunavukkarasar), not Sambandar.
xa: He wrote **Mattavilasa Prahasana** (APPSC-G1 2012).
He began **rock-cut temples** in South India — **Mandagapattu, Mahendravadi, Dalavanur, Mamandur**.
⚠ **Appar** → Mahendravarman I (Shaiva); **Tirumangai** → contemporary of Nandivarman II (Vaishnava).

n4e615db6adb.s: The Sanskrit satirical farce 'Mattavilasa Prahasana', which mocks Kapalikas and Buddhist monks, was written by:
n4e615db6adb.x: Mahendravarman I (c. 600-630) wrote the Mattavilasa Prahasana (APPSC-G1 2012), and Mattavilasa was also one of his titles. Narasimhavarman I was his son, known as Mamalla, Dandin wrote Dashakumaracharita and Kavyadarsha, and Nandivarman II was a later Vaishnavite ruler.
xs: **Mattavilasa Prahasana** was written by **Mahendravarman I** — option **(2)** (APPSC-G1 2012).
It is a **Sanskrit satirical farce** mocking **Kapalikas** and **Buddhist monks**; "Mattavilasa" was also his title.
**Dandin** wrote **Dashakumaracharita** and **Kavyadarsha**; **Narasimhavarman I** and **Nandivarman II** are not authors in the notes.
xa: **Bharavi** wrote **Kiratarjuniya** at **Simhavishnu**'s court.
Dandin called Vengi "**Andhra Nagaram**".
Mahendravarman I's other titles: **Vichitrachitta, Gunabhara, Chitrakarapuli**.

nb96b919553e.s: The inscriptional claim that a temple was built without brick, timber, metal or mortar is associated with which site?
nb96b919553e.x: The Mandagapattu cave temple carries the celebrated claim that it was constructed without brick, timber, metal or mortar.
nb96b919553e.tq: Match the distinctive architectural claim with its site.
xs: **Mandagapattu** is the temple "without **brick, timber, metal or mortar**" — option **(2)**.
It belongs to **Mahendravarman I**'s rock-cut programme, the start of rock-cut temples in South India.
**Vaikuntha Perumal** was built by **Nandivarman II**; **Mahabalipuram** has **Narasimhavarman I**'s monolithic rathas.
xa: Other Mahendravarman I caves: **Mahendravadi, Dalavanur, Mamandur**.
He was a staunch **Shaivite** after conversion by **Appar**.

ne946308d1b6.s: Narasimhavarman I sent naval expeditions to Sri Lanka primarily to:
o: support Pulakesin II against the Cholas
conquer the island for permanent Pallava rule
establish a Buddhist monastery at Kanchi
ne946308d1b6.x: Narasimhavarman I sent two naval expeditions to Sri Lanka to restore his ally, Prince Manavarma.
ne946308d1b6.tq: Identify the political objective behind a military expedition.
xs: **Narasimhavarman I** sent **two naval expeditions** to Sri Lanka to **restore** his ally prince **Manavarma** — option **(1)**.
He was Pulakesin II's enemy, not his supporter.
xa: He killed **Pulakesin II** at **Manimangala (642)** and sacked **Vatapi**.
Titles **Mamalla** and **Vatapikonda**.
He built the monolithic **rathas** at Mahabalipuram.

n1473767a470.s: Which of the following architectural achievements is associated with Narasimhavarman I?
o: Construction of the first Kadamba capital at Banavasi
Construction of the monolithic rathas at Mahabalipuram
Construction of the Vaikuntha Perumal temple at Kanchi
n1473767a470.x: Narasimhavarman I is associated with the monolithic rathas at Mahabalipuram and was a staunch Shaivite.
n1473767a470.tq: Match the architectural monument with the correct patron.
xs: **Narasimhavarman I** is linked with the monolithic **rathas at Mahabalipuram** — option **(3)**.
**Vaikuntha Perumal** is **Nandivarman II**'s; the **Hirahadagalli plates** are **Sivaskandavarman**'s charter.
xa: Mahabalipuram is called **Mamallapuram** after his title **Mamalla**.
He was a staunch **Shaivite**.
His father **Mahendravarman I** began rock-cut **cave temples** (Mandagapattu).

n9612b7f978a.s: Which Pallava ruler built the Vaikuntha Perumal temple at Kanchi?
n9612b7f978a.x: Nandivarman II Pallavamalla, an ardent Vaishnavite and contemporary of Tirumangai Alvar, built the Vaikuntha Perumal temple at Kanchi.
xa: ⚠ **Appar** = Mahendravarman I (Shaiva); **Tirumangai** = Nandivarman II (Vaishnava).
Nandivarman II came to the throne aged **12** (c. **731**).
He temporarily lost Kanchi to **Vikramaditya II**.

n48f695338e6.s: Mayurasharman founded the Kadamba kingdom after being insulted by a Pallava horseman at:
n48f695338e6.x: According to the Talagunda inscription, Mayurasharman, a Brahmin student at the Kanchi Ghatika, was insulted by a Pallava horseman and subsequently took up arms and founded the Kadamba kingdom.
n48f695338e6.tq: Link the person, incident and institution in a connected historical narrative.
xs: **Mayurasharman**, a Brahmin student at the **Kanchi Ghatika**, was insulted by a Pallava horseman — option **(4)**.
He took up arms and founded the **Kadamba** kingdom, as told in the **Talagunda inscription**.
xa: A **Ghatika** = higher learning centre attached to temples.
**Hiuen Tsang** visited Kanchi c. **640 CE**.
**Mandagapattu** is Mahendravarman I's cave temple; **Mamallapuram** is named after Narasimhavarman I.

n6d1ca3265fd.s: Which Pallava ruler is associated with the Pancha Rathas, Varaha Mandapa and Mahishasuramardini Cave at Mahabalipuram?
n6d1ca3265fd.x: The Pancha Rathas, Varaha Mandapa and Mahishasuramardini Cave are attributed to Narasimhavarman I, also known as Mamalla.
n6d1ca3265fd.tq: Match the monument with its patron rather than relying on the general Pallava association.
xs: The **Pancha Rathas**, **Varaha Mandapa** and **Mahishasuramardini cave** are attributed to **Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla)** — option **(2)**.
**Narasimhavarman II** built the **Shore Temple**; **Mahendravarman I** the rock-cut mandapas; **Nandivarman II** Vaikuntha Perumal.
xa: **Arjuna's Penance** is also attributed to Narasimhavarman I.
APPSC-GS 2025: "**Seven Ratha**" temples = **Narasimhavarman**.
Mahabalipuram was a **7th-century Pallava port city**.

n8e03b12aa98.s: Each of the Pancha Rathas at Mahabalipuram was carved out of a single rock of:
n8e03b12aa98.x: The Pancha Rathas are monolithic, each carved from a single granite rock, imitating earlier wooden and structural forms.
xa: **Dharmaraja** is the largest — precursor of the **Dravida vimana**; **Draupadi** the smallest.
**Nakula-Sahadeva** ratha has an **apsidal** end.
Patron: **Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla)**.

nceee4abd48f.s: Which is the largest ratha at Mahabalipuram and a precursor of the Dravida vimana?
nceee4abd48f.x: The Dharmaraja ratha is the largest and a precursor of the Dravida vimana; the Draupadi ratha is the smallest, a hut-shaped single cell.
xa: Each ratha is carved from a single **granite** rock.
Rathas gave the **vimana + ardhamandapa** to early Andhra temples.
⚠ Aihole's **Durga temple** is also apsidal — a confusable Chalukya example.

n14f69dcf0f4.s: Arjuna's Penance, also known as the Descent of the Ganga, is best described as:
o: A Jain cave mural depicting a lotus pond
A structural temple with three sanctums
The largest open-air rock relief in India depicting Bhagiratha's penance
A monolithic shrine dedicated exclusively to Vishnu
n14f69dcf0f4.x: Arjuna's Penance or the Descent of the Ganga is the largest open-air rock relief in India and is associated with Bhagiratha's penance.
n14f69dcf0f4.tq: Identify the monument through its defining subject and scale.
xs: **Arjuna's Penance / Descent of the Ganga** is the **largest open-air rock relief in India**, showing **Bhagiratha's penance** — option **(3)**.
The **Jain lotus-pond mural** is at **Sittannavasal**; the three-shrine structural temple is the **Shore Temple**.
xa: Attributed to **Narasimhavarman I**.
Mahabalipuram's other reliefs: **Varaha Mandapa** (Varaha rescuing Bhudevi), **Krishna Mandapa** (Govardhana).
Mahabalipuram = **open-air reliefs + monolithic rathas + structural temple**.

n97898e1a4b2.s: The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram was constructed during the reign of:
o: Narasimhavarman II, also known as Rajasimha
n97898e1a4b2.x: The Shore Temple is attributed to Narasimhavarman II, or Rajasimha, and is a structural temple.
n97898e1a4b2.tq: Distinguish the patron of the structural Shore Temple from the patron of the monolithic rathas.
xs: The **Shore Temple** belongs to **Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha)** — option **(3)**.
It is a **structural** temple with **three shrines** — two Shiva, one Vishnu.
**Narasimhavarman I** made the monolithic **rathas**; **Mahendravarman I** the rock-cut mandapas.
xa: "**Seven Pagodas**": Shore Temple + six temples believed lost to the sea.
Rajasimha also built the **Kailasanatha**, Kanchi.
UNESCO: Mahabalipuram group — **1984**.

n9ee025f6082.s: Besides two Shiva shrines, the structural Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram contains a shrine of:
n9ee025f6082.x: The Shore Temple is a structural temple with two Shiva shrines and one Vishnu shrine, the surviving temple of the Seven Pagodas tradition.
xa: Builder: **Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha)**.
Rajasimha's structural temples → Chola **Brihadeshwara**.
UNESCO (Mahabalipuram group): **1984**.

n5cc2e2ea1f9.s: The Mandagapattu inscription, describing a temple made without brick, timber, metal or mortar, was issued by:
n5cc2e2ea1f9.x: The Mandagapattu inscription of Mahendravarman I (not Narasimhavarman I) records a temple for Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva made without brick, timber, metal or mortar.
xa: It marks the **beginning of rock-cut cave temples** in South India.
**Dvarapalakas** at the entrance — later common in South Indian temples.
**Narasimhavarman I** is linked with the **Pancha Rathas**, not Mandagapattu.

n1a02d3fb47f.s: The construction of the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchi was completed by:
n1a02d3fb47f.x: The Kailasanatha temple, rich in Shiva sculptures and a model for later Chola temples, was completed by Mahendravarman III.
xa: Built by **Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha)**, 8th c., in **sandstone**; early Dravida.
Oldest surviving Pallava **structural** temple.
Carries **Vikramaditya II**'s **Kannada inscription**; model for **Virupaksha**, Pattadakal.

n6805a7f4084.s: The Kailasanatha (Rajasimheshvara) temple at Kanchi, the oldest surviving Pallava structural temple, was built by:
n6805a7f4084.x: Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha) built the sandstone Kailasanatha in the 8th century. Mahendravarman I made rock-cut mandapas, Narasimhavarman I made the monolithic rathas, and Nandivarman II built the Vaikuntha Perumal temple.
xs: The **Kailasanatha (Rajasimheshvara)** at Kanchi was built by **Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha)** in the 8th century — option **(3)**.
**Mahendravarman I** made rock-cut mandapas; **Narasimhavarman I** the rathas; **Nandivarman II** **Vaikuntha Perumal**.
xa: Material: **sandstone**; early **Dravida**; completed by **Mahendravarman III**.
Rajasimha also built the **Shore Temple**.
Kailasanatha → **Virupaksha** (Pattadakal) and the Chola temples.

n4ea0699addf.s: Which dynasty is associated with the rock-cut caves at Undavalli, Mogalrajapuram and Bhairavakonda in Andhra?
n4ea0699addf.x: The caves at Undavalli, Mogalrajapuram and Bhairavakonda are attributed to the Vishnukundins, who imitated the Pallava cave style in the Telugu lands.
n4ea0699addf.tq: Identify the dynasty responsible for the Andhra caves rather than assuming that their Pallava-like style indicates Pallava patronage.
xs: **Undavalli, Mogalrajapuram** and **Bhairavakona** caves are attributed to the **Vishnukundins** — option **(2)** (APPSC G2 2025 for Undavalli).
The Vishnukundins **started Hindu cave temples in Telugu lands**, imitating the **Pallava** style.
xa: **Undavalli**: Guntur dist., Krishna banks; multi-storeyed; reclining **Anantasayana Vishnu**.
**Mogalrajapuram** (Vijayawada): Shiva and Vishnu shrines; early **ardhamandapa + garbhagriha**.
**Bhairavakona**: **8 caves**; centre of **Shaivism**.

n2c1d140f120.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Undavalli caves?
o: They were built by the Cholas.
They are located in Guntur district on the banks of the Krishna.
They contain a monolithic reclining Anantasayana Vishnu.
n2c1d140f120.x: Undavalli is a Vishnukundin complex, not a Chola work; the location, multi-storeyed form and reclining Anantasayana Vishnu are correct.
xa: History: originally a **Jain** abode → **Buddhist** → **Hindu**.
A test (Aug **2026**) framed Undavalli as a **4th-5th c.** monolithic complex on the Krishna.

nbd1c1f60796.s: Bhairavakonda, whose eight caves resemble early Pallava caves, was a centre of:
nbd1c1f60796.x: Bhairavakonda, with eight caves resembling early Pallava caves, was a centre of Shaivism, not Jainism.
xa: ⚠ District of Bhairavakona: **Nellore** (APPSC keys); CDI says Prakasam.
**Undavalli** began as a **Jain** abode — don't transfer that to Bhairavakona.
The **Vishnukundins** started Hindu cave temples in Telugu lands.

n71b5c10eef8.s: Kubja Vishnuvardhana declared his independence and founded the Eastern Chalukya line in:
n71b5c10eef8.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana became viceroy in 617 CE and declared independence in 624 CE.
n71b5c10eef8.tq: Separate the appointment year from the later year of independence.
xs: **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** declared independence in **624 CE** — option **(3)**.
**617** is his appointment as viceroy; **616** is a date some notes give for Pulakesin II's conquest of Vengi.
xa: ⚠ **617** = viceroy; **624** = independence.
The line ruled **624-1075 CE**.
First capital **Pithapuram**; built the **Kunti Madhava** temple.

nc5b6c298024.s: Which one of the following was the royal emblem of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
nc5b6c298024.x: The boar, or Varaha, was the royal emblem of the Eastern Chalukyas.
nc5b6c298024.tq: Discriminate among dynastic emblems rather than titles or capitals.
xs: The royal emblem was the **Boar (Varaha)** — option **(4)**.
It marks the line's descent from the **Badami Chalukyas**, of which they were a branch.
xa: Official language: **Sanskrit** (about **100** donation inscriptions, mostly Sanskrit).
Matronymic "**Hariti Putra**" — like the Satavahanas, Ikshvakus, Kadambas.
Founder **Kubja Vishnuvardhana**; greatest **Gunaga Vijayaditya III**; last **Vijayaditya VII**.

n725e5ba3570.s: The use of the matronymic ‘Hariti-putra’ by the Eastern Chalukyas is comparable to its use by the
n725e5ba3570.x: The matronymic Hariti-putra was also used by the Satavahanas, Ikshvakus and Kadambas, indicating a southern cultural connection.
n725e5ba3570.tq: Use the comparison group stated with the distinctive title or matronymic.
xs: The matronymic "**Hariti Putra**" was used like the **Satavahanas, Ikshvakus and Kadambas** — option **(4)**.
It is read as a sign of **southern origin**.
xa: Official language: **Sanskrit**; Telugu rose later as a literary language.
Emblem: **Boar (Varaha)**.
The line branched from the **Badami Chalukyas**.

nac5f50b67b0.s: Which ruler is regarded as the greatest king of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
nac5f50b67b0.x: Gunaga Vijayaditya III (Tripura Martya Maheshwara) is regarded as the greatest ruler of the line (APHQ 2011). Kubja Vishnuvardhana was the founder, Rajaraja Narendra the patron of Nannaya, and Chalukya Bhima I the builder of the Pancharamas.
nac5f50b67b0.tq: Founder = Kubja; greatest = Gunaga Vijayaditya III.
xs: **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** was the greatest king — option **(2)** (APHQ 2011).
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana** was the **founder**; **Rajaraja Narendra** the patron of **Nannaya**; **Chalukya Bhima I** built the **Pancharamas**.
xa: Title: **Tripura Martya Maheshwara** — for victories over **Kiranapuram, Achalapuram and Kandukur**.
He developed **Kandukuru as Bejawada** and built the **Bikkavolu** Shiva temples.
His commander **Panduranga** issued the **Addanki inscription**.

n5a7318b32f4.s: What was the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas, used in most of their about 100 donation inscriptions?
n5a7318b32f4.x: Sanskrit was the official language, and most of the about 100 donation inscriptions are in Sanskrit. Telugu rose later as a literary language under their patronage; Prakrit and Kannada were not their official language.
xs: The official language was **Sanskrit** — option **(3)**; most of the about **100** donation inscriptions are in Sanskrit.
**Telugu** rose later as the literary language, under **Rajaraja Narendra**'s patronage of **Nannaya**.
xa: **Addanki** = first Telugu **verse** inscription; **Kalamalla** (c. **575 CE**) = first Telugu inscription.
Emblem: **Boar (Varaha)**.
They turned Telugu into a **literary language**.

n52a19930549.s: After 973 CE, the principal rival of the Eastern Chalukyas was the
n52a19930549.x: After 973 CE, the Kalyani Chalukyas emerged as the principal rival of the Eastern Chalukyas. Satyasraya and Someshvara I are associated with this later phase.
n52a19930549.tq: Identify the change in the rival dynasty by using the chronological marker.
xs: After **973 CE** the main rival was the **Kalyani Chalukyas** — option **(4)**.
Kalyani kings involved: **Satyasraya** (**1006**) and **Someshvara I**.
xa: **Saktivarma I** beat Satyasraya's general **Bayyalanambi** with Chola help.
In the succession war **Kalyani Jayasimha II** backed **Vijayaditya VII**.
After **Koppam (1053)** Rajaraja Narendra had to accept **Kalyani suzerainty**.

n9267482336c.s: The Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi ruled approximately during:
n9267482336c.x: The Eastern Chalukyas ruled approximately from 624 to 1075 CE; 1076-1210 belongs to the Chalukya-Chola phase.
xa: End date debate: **1075**, or **1189 CE** counting the Chalukya-Chola phase.

n4f78cca8083.s: Which of the following best expresses the major cultural significance of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
o: They confined literary activity exclusively to Sanskrit.
They ended the use of Telugu in the Vengi region.
They turned Telugu into a literary language.
They replaced Telugu with Tamil as the court language.
n4f78cca8083.x: A major significance of the Eastern Chalukyas was that they helped turn Telugu into a literary language and laid the foundation for Telugu literature.
n4f78cca8083.tq: Identify the positive cultural consequence and reject absolute or reversed statements.
xs: The Eastern Chalukyas **turned Telugu into a literary language** — option **(3)**.
Though **Sanskrit** was the official language, the **Vengi court** laid the base for Telugu literature with **Nannaya**.
xa: First Telugu literary work: Nannaya's **Mahabharata**, under **Rajaraja Narendra**.
They ruled Andhra about **4.5 centuries** (**624-1075**).
Also: **Pavuluri Ganitamu**, first scientific text in Telugu.

nindian-history-145-17.s: Kulottunga I, who united the Eastern Chalukya and Chola lines, was earlier known as:
nindian-history-145-17.x: Kulottunga I was Rajendra Chalukya, who united the Eastern Chalukya and Chola lines.
n: The Eastern Chalukyas had repeated political interaction and conflict with the Cholas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Eastern Chalukya succession became increasingly intertwined with the Chola dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Rajendra Chalukya emerged from the Eastern Chalukya–Chola line. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Rajendra Chalukya was also known as Kulottunga I. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
xa: **Vimaladitya** married **Kundavva (Kundavai)**, daughter of **Rajaraja Chola I**.
⚠ **Kundavva** = mother of **Rajaraja Narendra**; **Melama** = mother of **Vijayaditya VII**.
**Vijayaditya VII**, the last ruler, died in **1075**.
First Chalukya-Chola king = **Kulothunga I**.

n801f8d8c029.s: 'Rajamartanda' was a title of which Eastern Chalukya ruler?
n801f8d8c029.x: Vimaladitya bore the title Rajamartanda; Chalukya Bhima was Kollabhiganda, Saktivarma I Chalukya Chandra and Rajaraja Narendra Rajarajanarayana.
xa: Vimaladitya also bore **Mummadi Bhima**.
Rajaraja Narendra also: **Kavyageetha Priyudu**, **Baraganda Bhairava**.
⚠ Some notes give **Kollabhiganda** to **Vijayaditya IV**.

n14fca5639ed.s: Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram is associated with which ruler?
n14fca5639ed.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana is credited with the Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram.
n14fca5639ed.tq: Use the temple–builder pair rather than confusing it with later Vengi temples.
xs: The **Kunti Madhava** temple at **Pithapuram** is credited to **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** — option **(2)**.
**Rajaraja Narendra** built the **Rajaraja temple**, Bikkavolu; **Chalukya Bhima I** the **Bhimeswara** temples.
xa: Pithapuram (**Pishtapura**) was Kubja's **first capital**.
Kubja = founder; brother of **Pulakesin II**; independent in **624 CE**.
⚠ "108 Shaivalayas" → **Vijayaditya II**, not Kubja.

nb3e0fbe5e86.x: Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara was Narayana Bhattu's title; Nannaya was known as Adikavi, Vagadheeshwara and Shabda Shasanudu.
xa: Narayana Bhattu was Nannaya's **collaborator** and received **Nandampudi** agrahara.
**Chellavva**: "**Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada**".
Nannaya wrote **Andhra Mahabharatamu** in **Champu** style.

naa67a30bd10.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler granted Mushikonda village to the Jains?
naa67a30bd10.x: Vishnuvardhana III patronised Vedic and Jain faiths and granted Mushikonda village to the Jains.
xa: He took the throne back from **Kokkili**, who then set up the **Yalamanchili** kingdom.
APP gives him the titles **Tribhuvanankusa, Samasta Bhuvanashraya** (with Jayasimha I).
**Potla Cheruvu** was a popular Jain centre of the period.

n294e87c9799.s: According to the Pithapuram inscription of Mallappadeva, Chalukya Bhima I fought how many battles?
n294e87c9799.x: The Pithapuram inscription of Mallappadeva credits Chalukya Bhima I, who ruled 30 years and built the Pancharamas, with 360 battles.
xa: ⚠ Some notes credit the **360 battles** to **Gunaga Vijayaditya**.
Title: **Kollabhiganda** (G2 2012 key).
He repelled **Krishna II** at **Niravadyapura and Peruvanguru**; **Kakumanu** inscription names a **Setti Shreshthi**.

n0bf30585857.s: The Addanki inscription was issued by Panduranga, the commander of:
n0bf30585857.x: Panduranga, the commander of Gunaga Vijayaditya III, issued the Addanki inscription.
n0bf30585857.tq: Identify the subordinate–ruler relationship instead of attributing the inscription directly to a king.
xs: The **Addanki inscription** was issued by **Panduranga**, commander of **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** — option **(2)**.
It is the **first Telugu verse inscription**.
xa: ⚠ **Addanki** = first Telugu **verse** inscription; **Kalamalla** (c. **575 CE**, Renati Choda **Dhananjaya**) = first Telugu inscription.
Gunaga Vijayaditya III = **greatest** Eastern Chalukya (APHQ 2011).
He defeated **Krishna II** and Kalinga king **Devendravarma**.

n780ffc25560.s: Who seized Vengi after killing Danarnava during the interlude in Eastern Chalukya history?
n780ffc25560.x: The Telugu Choda ruler Jatachoda Bhima killed Danarnava and seized Vengi until Danarnava’s sons recovered it with Chola assistance.
n780ffc25560.tq: Track the succession interruption through the killer and the displaced ruler.
xs: **Jatachoda Bhima**, Telugu Choda of **Pedakallu**, killed **Danarnava** and occupied Vengi — option **(4)**.
**Kokkili** was the rival of **Vishnuvardhana III**; **Satyasraya** was the Kalyani king of **1006**.
xa: Danarnava's sons **Saktivarma I** and **Vimaladitya** fled to **Rajaraja Chola**.
They recovered Vengi with **Chola** help.
Vimaladitya later married **Melama**, daughter of Jatachoda Bhima.

n8f51d6acc9d.s: Vijayaditya II is traditionally associated with which of the following achievements?
o: Winning 18 battles in one regnal year
n8f51d6acc9d.x: Vijayaditya II is traditionally said to have fought 108 battles in 12 years. The 108 temples were commemorative constructions associated with these victories.
n8f51d6acc9d.tq: Match the distinctive number with the correct activity rather than with a related monument or inscription.
xs: **Vijayaditya II** traditionally fought **108 battles in 12 years** — option **(3)**.
He built **108 Shiva temples** (not Buddhist monasteries) to commemorate the victories (APPSC G2 2019).
xa: Title: **Narendramrigaraja**.
Opponent: Rashtrakuta **Amoghavarsha**.
Temples recorded in the **Sataluru** inscription.

n5f60b69721a.s: In 1006 CE, Satyasraya sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi. Who defeated Bayyalanambi?
o: Vijayaditya VII with Rajendra Chola's assistance
n5f60b69721a.x: Saktivarma I defeated Bayyalanambi with Chola help in 1006 CE. Satyasraya of the Kalyani Chalukyas had sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi.
n5f60b69721a.tq: Track the combatant, the opposing commander and the external support separately.
xs: **Saktivarma I** beat **Bayyalanambi** with **Chola** help in **1006** — option **(4)**.
Bayyalanambi was sent by **Satyasraya** of Kalyani.
xa: Saktivarma's coins are found in **Arakan (Burma)**.
He and **Vimaladitya** had recovered Vengi from **Jatachoda Bhima** with Chola help.
Title: **Chalukya Chandra**.

nfcee24d5d1c.s: Who among the following developed Kandukuru as another ‘Bejawada’?
o: Vijayaditya III, also known as Gunaga Vijayaditya
nfcee24d5d1c.x: Vijayaditya III, or Gunaga Vijayaditya, developed Kandukuru as another Bejawada.
nfcee24d5d1c.tq: Distinguish the ruler associated with town development from rulers linked with capitals.
xs: **Vijayaditya III (Gunaga Vijayaditya)** developed **Kandukuru** as another "**Bejawada**" — option **(4)** (APPSC G2 2019 key).
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana** = Pithapuram; **Jayasimha Vallabha I** = Vengi; **Ammaraja I** = Rajamahendravaram.
xa: **Vijayawada** was developed by **Yuddhamalla** (CDX); APP says Bezawada took the name after Vijayaditya.
Gunaga Vijayaditya III: **greatest** king; **Bikkavolu** temples.

nd912dbb9a97.s: The capital of the Eastern Chalukyas was shifted to Vengi by
nd912dbb9a97.x: Jayasimha Vallabha I shifted the capital from Pithapuram to Vengi, identified with Pedavegi.
nd912dbb9a97.tq: Match a capital change with the ruler responsible for it.
xs: **Jayasimha Vallabha I** shifted the capital to **Vengi** (Pedavegi, near Eluru) — option **(4)**.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana** ruled from **Pithapuram**; **Amma I** made **Rajamahendravaram** capital.
xa: Jayasimha I issued the **Vipparla inscription** (G2 2017 key).
Title: **Samastha Bhuvanashraya**.
Core territory: **Venginadu** (Krishna-Godavari doab).

n4d960d236af.s: The Nandampudi inscription, recording Rajaraja Narendra's grant to Narayana Bhattu, was written by:
n4d960d236af.x: The Nandampudi inscription of Rajaraja Narendra, recording his grant to Narayana Bhattu, was written by Nannaya.
xa: **Nandampudi**: grant to **Narayana Bhattu**, written by **Nannaya**.
⚠ APPSC G2 2017 key marked Nannaya as the **donee** — know both.
**Sataluru** = Vijayaditya II; **Chekurru** = Ammaraja I.

n6dd8e8c9d4f.s: Which group of temples at Bikkavolu is associated with Gunaga Vijayaditya III?
n6dd8e8c9d4f.x: The Bikkavolu Shiva temples of Mukteshwara, Vijayeshwara and Chandrashekhara are attributed to Gunaga Vijayaditya III.
n6dd8e8c9d4f.tq: Start from the sure temple group and match it to its builder.
xs: **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** built the **Bikkavolu** Shiva temples — **Mukteshwara, Vijayeshwara, Chandrashekhara** — option **(1)**.
**Kunti Madhava** = Kubja; **Bhimeswara** = Chalukya Bhima I; **Rajaraja temple**, Rajahmundry **Vishnu** temple and **Kalidindi** = Rajaraja Narendra.
xa: **Vijayeshwara** has carved **Ganga and Yamuna** figures.
Gunaga Vijayaditya III = **greatest** king (APHQ 2011).
He developed **Kandukuru as Bejawada**.

n9bfeb5dc1ec.s: The Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot are attributed to:
n9bfeb5dc1ec.x: The Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot, also called Chalukya Bhimavaram, are associated with Chalukya Bhima I.
n9bfeb5dc1ec.tq: Distinguish the Bhimeswara temples from the separate 108-temple tradition.
xs: The **Bhimeswara** temples at **Draksharama** and **Samalkot (Chalukya Bhimavaram)** are attributed to **Chalukya Bhima I** — option **(2)**.
**Vijayaditya II** = **108 Shiva temples**; **Kubja** = **Kunti Madhava**; **Rajaraja Narendra** = Rajaraja temple.
xa: Chalukya Bhima I built the **Pancharamas** (Bhimarama, Draksharama).
He ruled **30 years**; **360 battles** per Mallappadeva's Pithapuram inscription.
Title: **Kollabhiganda**.

nc4b811c0496.s: Which of the following is included among the Pancharamas associated with the Eastern Chalukya temple tradition?
nc4b811c0496.x: Bhimarama and Draksharama are included among the key Pancharama temples mentioned in the Eastern Chalukya tradition.
nc4b811c0496.tq: Recognise a Pancharama name rather than a nearby Bikkavolu or Pithapuram temple.
xs: **Bhimarama** is one of the **Pancharamas** — option **(4)**; **Draksharama** is another.
**Vijayeshwara** and **Chandrashekhara** are Bikkavolu temples; **Kunti Madhava** is at Pithapuram.
xa: The Pancharamas were built by **Chalukya Bhima I**.
**Bhimeswara** temples: **Draksharama** and **Samalkot**.
Dominant faith: **Shaivism**.

n564b59a2402.s: Which inscription records Vijayaditya II's association with 108 temples?
n564b59a2402.x: The Sataluru inscription records Vijayaditya II's association with the 108 temples. Addanki is associated with Pandaranga and the first Telugu verse inscription.
n564b59a2402.tq: Separate two inscription records by matching their distinctive content.
xs: The **Sataluru** inscription records **Vijayaditya II**'s **108 Shiva temples** ("**Narendra Mrigeswara**") — option **(3)**.
**Addanki** = Pandaranga (first Telugu verse inscription); **Cheepurupalli** = Kubja's 18th regnal year; **Kopparam** = Pulakesin II.
xa: Vijayaditya II fought **108 battles in 12 years** (APPSC G2 2019).
Title: **Narendramrigaraja**.
⚠ "108 Shaivalayas" → **Vijayaditya II**, not Kubja or Vishnuvardhana III/IV.

n643e8990a8b.s: The Magallu inscription is significant in Andhra history because it is regarded as the first inscription to mention the
n643e8990a8b.x: The Magallu inscription is noted as the first inscription mentioning the Kakatiyas.
n643e8990a8b.tq: Identify the dynasty connected with a landmark inscription rather than the dynasty ruling at the time.
xs: The **Magallu inscription** is the first to mention the **Kakatiyas** — option **(4)**.
It is listed among the Eastern Chalukya-era inscriptions, but its fame is this first reference to the Kakatiyas.
xa: First Telugu inscription: **Kalamalla** (c. **575 CE**).
**Addanki** = first Telugu **verse** inscription.

nap-history-36-20.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler is credited with building 108 Saiva temples, also known as Narendraeswara temples?
nap-history-36-20.x: Vijayaditya II (Narendra Mrigaraja) of the Eastern Chalukyas built 108 Saiva temples called Narendreswara temples. Vijayaditya IV was Kollabhighanda, Gunaga Vijayaditya was Vijayaditya III, and Rudra Deva was a Kakatiya.
n: Vijayaditya II belonged to the Eastern Chalukya dynasty. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Vijayaditya II built 108 Saiva temples. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Vijayaditya II built Narendraeswara temples. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Rudra Deva belonged to the Kakatiya dynasty. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
xs: **Vijayaditya II** built the **108 Saiva temples**, the **Narendraeswara** temples — option **(1)**.
He fought **108 battles** and built **108 Shiva temples** (APPSC G2 2019); title **Narendramrigaraja**.
**Vijayaditya IV** had the title **Kollabhighanda**; **Gunaga Vijayaditya** had **Tripura-Martya-Maheswara**.
xa: The **Sataluru** inscription records the 108 temples ("Narendra Mrigeswara").
⚠ Other notes (G2 2012 key; APHQ) give **Kollabhiganda** to **Chalukya Bhima I**.
Gunaga Vijayaditya won victories over **Kiranapuram, Achalapuram and Kandukur** (G2 2012 key).
Exam angle: "**108 Shaivalayas**" → Vijayaditya II, not Kubja or Vishnuvardhana III/IV.

nap-history-3-14.s: The Porumamilla inscription is related to which person?
nap-history-3-14.x: The Porumamilla tank inscription, which lays down 12 rules for tank construction, is associated with Prince Bhaskara Bhavadura. Rudrapurushadatta was an Ikshvaku king and Dhananjaya Varma issued the Kalamalla inscription.
nap-history-3-14.tq: Recall the patron named in the Porumamilla tank record.
n: The Porumamilla inscription is associated with Prince Bhaskara Bhavadura. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xs: The **Porumamilla** inscription is related to **Prince Bhaskara Bhavadura** — option **(4)**.
It lays down **12 rules** for **tank construction**.
**Rudrapurushadatta** was not its author; **Dhananjaya** (Renati Choda) issued the **Kalamalla** inscription (c. **575 CE**).
xa: **Pithapuram** inscription of **Prithvisvara** of Velanadu mentions **Kolleru Lake**.
**Chekurru** plate — **Ammaraja I**.
**Kakumanu** — **Chalukya Bhima I**, names a **Setti Shreshthi**.
**Chipurupalli** inscription — Kubja's **18th regnal year**, names the scholar **Madhavasharma**.

n154d49fe97d.s: In which year was the Eastern Chalukya ruler Rajaraja Narendra crowned?
n154d49fe97d.x: Rajaraja Narendra was crowned in 1022 CE; Saktivarman I defeated Satyasraya in 1006 CE and Vijayaditya VII was ousted in 1070 CE.
xa: Vimaladitya was crowned in **May 1011**.
**Koppam (1053)**: Rajadhiraja I killed by **Ahavamalla Someshwara**.
Line ends with **Vijayaditya VII**'s death in **1075**.

n1f9f0aafad0.s: Vijayaditya VII, the last ruler of the Eastern Chalukyas, was ousted in 1070 CE by:
o: Rajendra Chalukya, later known as Kulottunga I
n1f9f0aafad0.x: Rajendra Chalukya ousted Vijayaditya VII in 1070 CE and later became known as Kulottunga I.
n1f9f0aafad0.tq: Identify the successor’s alternate name to avoid a person–title confusion.
xs: **Vijayaditya VII** was ousted in **1070** by **Rajendra Chalukya**, later **Kulottunga I** — option **(2)**.
**Jatachoda Bhima** killed Danarnava earlier; **Satyasraya** attacked Vengi in **1006**; **Rajaraja Chola I** was Kundavva's father.
xa: Vijayaditya VII (**1070-1075**) was the last ruler; his death in **1075** = end of the line.
He was the son of **Melama**, backed by **Kalyani Jayasimha II** in the succession war.
First Chalukya-Chola king = **Kulothunga I**; end date debated: **1075**, or **1189 CE** counting the Chalukya-Chola phase.

nf6da8b57812.s: The Rashtrakuta Dhruva, after defeating Vishnuvardhana IV, married his daughter:
nf6da8b57812.x: Vishnuvardhana IV, who backed Govinda III, was defeated by Dhruva, who then married his daughter Sheela Mahadevi.
xa: The Rashtrakuta conflict began under **Vijayaditya I** with **Dantidurga**.
**Vijayaditya II** fought **Amoghavarsha**; **Gunaga Vijayaditya** defeated **Krishna II**.

nc964989de70.s: Who supported Rajaraja Narendra in his succession war against Vijayaditya VII?
nc964989de70.x: Rajaraja Narendra, the son of Kundavva, was supported by Rajendra I. Vijayaditya VII, the son of Melama, was supported by Kalyani Jayasimha II.
nc964989de70.tq: Distinguish the two rival claimants by matching each with his external supporter.
xs: **Rajaraja Narendra** (son of Kundavva) was backed by **Rajendra I** — option **(1)**.
**Vijayaditya VII** (son of Melama) was backed by **Kalyani Jayasimha II**.
**Satyasraya** attacked in **1006**; **Ahavamalla Someshwara** killed Rajadhiraja I at Koppam.
xa: Rajaraja Narendra was crowned **16 August 1022**.
He married **Ammanga Devi**, daughter of Rajendra Chola.
After **Koppam (1053)** he had to accept Kalyani suzerainty.

n3ef2db30302.s: At Koppam in 1053, who killed Rajadhiraja I?
n3ef2db30302.x: Ahavamalla Someshwara killed Rajadhiraja I at Koppam in 1053. Rajadhiraja had earlier won at Dharanikota and burnt Kollipaka.
n3ef2db30302.tq: Match the battlefield casualty with the ruler responsible for the decisive reversal.
xs: At **Koppam (1053)**, **Ahavamalla Someshwara** killed **Rajadhiraja I** — option **(4)**.
Rajadhiraja I had earlier won at **Dharanikota** and burnt **Kollipaka**.
xa: Result: **Rajaraja Narendra** had to accept **Kalyani suzerainty**.
**Jayasimha II** of Kalyani had backed **Vijayaditya VII**.
**Satyasraya** was the Kalyani king of **1006**.

n5d8b2f318a1.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler made Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry) his capital?
n5d8b2f318a1.x: Ammaraja I made Rajamahendravaram his capital, and Rajaraja Narendra later ruled from it and made it famous; Jayasimha Vallabha I had shifted the capital to Vengi.
xa: Ammaraja I's title: **Rajamahendra**; **Chekurru** copper plate.
Rajaraja Narendra built a **Vishnu temple** at Rajahmundry.

nb20cbd473f2.s: The core territory of the Eastern Chalukyas, known as Venginadu, was the:
nb20cbd473f2.x: The core territory was the Krishna-Godavari doab (Venginadu), with capitals at Pithapuram, Pedavegi and Rajahmundry.
xa: Pithapuram = first capital (**Kubja**); Vengi/Pedavegi = **Jayasimha I**; Rajahmundry = **Ammaraja I**, beautified by **Rajaraja Narendra**.
Dandin called Vengi "**Andhra Nagaram**".

n8f8d41e4450.s: Who among the following is associated with the Kaluchumbarru grant for a Jain temple?
n8f8d41e4450.x: Chamekamba, a courtesan during the reign of Ammaraja II, secured the Kaluchumbarru grant for a Jain temple.
n8f8d41e4450.tq: Test an unusual person–grant association, a common source of identity traps.
xs: **Chamekamba**, courtesan under **Ammaraja II**, won the **Kaluchumbarru** grant for a Jain temple — option **(4)**.
**Ayyana Mahadevi** built the Jain **Nedumba (Nadumbi) Vasati** near Vijayawada; **Kundavva** was the Chola mother of Rajaraja Narendra.
xa: ⚠ Ayyana Mahadevi = queen of **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** per G2 2025 key (some notes: Gunaga Vijayaditya III).
**Vishnuvardhana III** granted **Mushikonda** to Jains; **Potla Cheruvu** was a popular Jain centre.
Mother goddess: **Kushmandini** (APPSC G2 2019 key).

nafc6f9b3988.s: Ayyana Mahadevi, who built the Jain Nedumba (Nadumbi) Vasati near Vijayawada, was the queen of
nafc6f9b3988.x: The 2025 key makes Ayyana Mahadevi the queen of Kubja Vishnuvardhana. Some sources say Gunaga Vijayaditya III, but the key disagrees. Ammaraja II is linked to Chamekamba and the Kaluchumbarru grant; Vimaladitya married Kundavai.
