nafc6f9b3988.tq: Nedumba Vasati = Ayyana Mahadevi, queen of Kubja (key).
xs: Per the **G2 2025** key, **Ayyana Mahadevi** was queen of **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** — option **(2)**.
She built the Jain **Nedumba (Nadumbi) Vasati** near/at **Vijayawada**.
⚠ Some notes make her queen of **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** — the official key disagrees.
xa: **Chamekamba**, courtesan under **Ammaraja II**, won the **Kaluchumbarru** grant for a Jain temple.
**Vimaladitya** married **Kundavva** and **Melama**.
Kubja also built the **Kunti Madhava** temple, Pithapuram.
nafc6f9b3988.fixed: drop meta 'as per key' wording; Kubja Vishnuvardhana is the established answer (PYQ ye9f9f46687d key flagged)

nc8df9d64f30.s: Nannaya Bhattaraka is regarded as the Adi Kavi of Telugu literature primarily because he
o: composed the first Telugu literary work, Andhra Mahabharatamu
founded the first Telugu literary academy at Vengi
translated the complete Ramayana into Telugu
introduced the prose style into Sanskrit literature
nc8df9d64f30.x: Nannaya Bhattaraka is regarded as Adi Kavi because Andhra Mahabharatamu is considered the first major Telugu literary work.
nc8df9d64f30.tq: Use the exact title and achievement associated with the poet.
xs: **Nannaya** is Adi Kavi because his **Andhra Mahabharatamu** (c. **1045-65**) is the **first Telugu literary work** — option **(1)**.
It was a Mahabharata, not a Ramayana; and his style was **Champu** in Telugu.
xa: He was court poet of **Rajaraja Narendra**.
Titles: **Adikavi, Vagadheeshwara, Shabda Shasanudu**.
Collaborator **Narayana Bhattu** received the **Nandampudi** agrahara.

n47366e07181.s: Andhra Mahabharatamu of Nannaya is written in which literary style?
o: Champu style combining verse and prose
n47366e07181.x: Nannaya's Andhra Mahabharatamu follows the Champu style, which combines verse and prose.
n47366e07181.tq: Discriminate between closely related literary forms by identifying the defining feature.
xs: **Andhra Mahabharatamu** is in **Champu** style — **verse + prose** — option **(3)**.
It is neither purely prose nor a single metre: Champu mixes both forms.
xa: Written c. **1045-65**; the **first Telugu literary work**.
Nannaya = **Adi Kavi**, court poet of **Rajaraja Narendra**.
His title **Shabda Shasanudu**.
The Vengi court laid the base for **Telugu literature**.

ne4bb8accbe0.s: Regarding the Nandampudi inscription, which of the following is correct?
o: Nannaya composed it and Narayana Bhattu received the agrahara
Narayana Bhattu composed it and Nannaya received the agrahara
Pandaranga composed it and Nannaya received the agrahara
Nannaya composed it and Ugradityacharya received the agrahara
ne4bb8accbe0.x: Nannaya composed the Nandampudi inscription, which records the agrahara granted to his collaborator Narayana Bhattu under Rajaraja Narendra. Trap: the APPSC G2 2017 key marked Nannaya as the donee, so know both. Pandaranga is linked to Addanki and Ugradityacharya to Kalyanakaraka.
ne4bb8accbe0.tq: Nandampudi: written by Nannaya, grant to Narayana Bhattu.
xs: **Nannaya composed** the **Nandampudi** inscription and **Narayana Bhattu received** the agrahara — option **(1)**.
⚠ Trap: the **APPSC G2 2017** key marked Nannaya as the **donee** — know both.
**Pandaranga** belongs to **Addanki**; **Ugradityacharya** to **Kalyanakaraka**.
xa: The grant was made by **Rajaraja Narendra**.
Narayana Bhattu's title: **Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara**.

nc8922f78d70.s: Pavuluri Ganitamu, regarded as the first scientific text in Telugu, is a verse rendering of
nc8922f78d70.x: Pavuluri Ganitamu renders Mahaviracharya's Ganitasarasangraham in Telugu verse. Kalyanakaraka is a medical work, Kavijanasrayam a work of Vemulavada Bhimakavi, and Andhra Mahabharatamu the first Telugu literary work.
nc8922f78d70.tq: First Telugu science text = Pavuluri Ganitamu (maths).
xs: **Pavuluri Ganitamu** is a Telugu verse rendering of **Mahaviracharya's Ganitasarasangraham** — option **(2)**.
**Kalyanakaraka** is Ugradityacharya's medical work; **Kavijanasrayam** is Vemulavada Bhimakavi's; **Andhra Mahabharatamu** is Nannaya's.
xa: It is the **first scientific text in Telugu**.
First Telugu **literary** work = Nannaya's **Mahabharata**.

n0fbb3095c9e.s: Who held the title 'Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada' in the Eastern Chalukya period?
n0fbb3095c9e.x: Chellavva, the court singer and dancer, held the title Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada (APPSC G2 2019). Chamekamba won the Kaluchumbarru grant, Kundavva was Vimaladitya's Chola queen, and Ayyana Mahadevi built the Nedumba Vasati.
xs: **Chellavva** held the title "**Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada**" — option **(3)** (APPSC G2 2019).
**Chamekamba** won the **Kaluchumbarru** grant; **Kundavva** was Vimaladitya's Chola queen; **Ayyana Mahadevi** built the **Nedumba Vasati**.
xa: Nannaya's titles: **Adikavi, Vagadheeshwara, Shabda Shasanudu**.
Narayana Bhattu: **Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara**.

n6570d6efd44.s: In Dandin's Dashakumaracharita, Vengi is referred to as
n6570d6efd44.x: Dandin calls Vengi 'Andhra Nagaram'. Mangalapura is Mangalagiri in the Kopparam inscription, Pishtapura is Pithapuram, and Rajamahendra is a title of Ammaraja I.
xs: **Dandin**'s **Dashakumaracharita** calls Vengi "**Andhra Nagaram**" — option **(2)**.
**Mangalapura** = Mangalagiri (Kopparam inscription); **Pishtapura** = Pithapuram; **Rajamahendra** = Ammaraja I's title.
xa: Vengi = **Pedavegi**, near **Eluru**.
Capital moved to Vengi by **Jayasimha Vallabha I**.

ne47899377ef.s: The Addanki inscription is notable because it is associated with
o: Pandaranga and the first Telugu verse inscription
Chalukya Bhima I's military victory at Peruvanguru
Rajaraja Narendra's grant to Narayana Bhattu
ne47899377ef.x: The Addanki inscription is associated with Pandaranga, the general of Gunaga Vijayaditya III, and is regarded as the first Telugu verse inscription.
ne47899377ef.tq: Identify the record through its unique person-and-content combination.
xs: **Addanki** is linked with **Pandaranga** (general of Gunaga Vijayaditya III) and is the **first Telugu verse inscription** — option **(1)**.
Kubja's **18th** regnal year = **Chipurupalli**; Peruvanguru = Chalukya Bhima I; grant to Narayana Bhattu = **Nandampudi**.
xa: ⚠ **Kalamalla** (c. **575 CE**, Renati Choda Dhananjaya) = first Telugu inscription.
Kalamalla **predates Nannaya**.
**Magallu inscription** first mentions the **Kakatiyas**.

nc3c632bcef1.s: The earliest Telugu inscription mentioned in connection with the pre-Nannaya period is the
nc3c632bcef1.x: The Kalamalla inscription, dated approximately to 575 CE and associated with Renati Choda Dhananjaya, predates Nannaya.
nc3c632bcef1.tq: Use the earliest-date clue to distinguish inscriptions from different periods.
xs: The first Telugu inscription, predating Nannaya, is **Kalamalla** (c. **575 CE**, Renati Choda **Dhananjaya**) — option **(1)**.
**Vipparla** = Jayasimha I; **Magallu** first mentions the **Kakatiyas**; **Nandampudi** = Rajaraja Narendra's grant written by Nannaya.
xa: ⚠ **Addanki** = first Telugu **verse** inscription; Kalamalla = first Telugu inscription.
Eastern Chalukya official language: **Sanskrit**.

n566957e3b7b.s: The Ashtadasa Tirthas in Eastern Chalukya administration referred to:
n566957e3b7b.x: The kingdom followed the Saptanga idea and had Ashtadasa Tirthas, meaning eighteen offices.
n566957e3b7b.tq: Discriminate between an administrative number and similarly structured territorial or religious lists.
xs: **Ashtadasa Tirthas** = **18 offices** — option **(1)**.
They went with the **Saptanga** idea of the state; the territorial units were **Vishaya / Mandala** and the **Nadus**.
xa: **Tirthulu** = council of ministers; **Samaharta** = chief.
**Vishayapati / Mandaleswara** headed a Vishaya / Mandala.
**Vanneyus** = toll collectors.

n148f26275b8.s: Under the Eastern Chalukyas, the council of ministers was called:
n148f26275b8.x: The Eastern Chalukya council of ministers was called Tirthulu, and the Samaharta was its chief member.
xa: The king was assisted by the **Yuvaraja**.
**Ashtadasa Tirthas** = 18 offices.
**Sthanadhipati** managed temples.

na8022e96973.s: Which of the following Nadus was associated with the Nellore region?
na8022e96973.x: Pakanadu was associated with Nellore. Venginadu covered parts of Krishna and Godavari, while Kammanadu included Bapatla, Ongole and Narasaraopet.
na8022e96973.tq: Use the geographical association to distinguish the named territorial units.
xs: **Pakanadu** = **Nellore** — option **(4)**.
**Venginadu** = Krishna, Godavari; **Kammanadu** = **Bapatla, Ongole, Narasaraopet**; **Palnadu** is listed without a region.
xa: The **Asanapura** Ghatika, headed by **Mandasharma**, was in **Kammanadu**.
Core territory of the dynasty = **Venginadu**.

nf524ea841ea.s: Brahmins who received agraharas are stated to have performed which rituals?
nf524ea841ea.x: Brahmins receiving tax-free agraharas performed Hiranyagarbha and Bahusuvarna rituals.
nf524ea841ea.tq: Match the social beneficiaries with the rituals associated with their privilege.
xs: Brahmins of the **agraharas** performed **Hiranyagarbha and Bahusuvarna** rituals — option **(4)**.
**Hallisaka (Kolatam)** is a dance; **Tarka** and **Vyakarana** are Ghatika subjects.
xa: Agraharas were **tax-free villages**.
Grants came from the **Badami Chalukya** model.
**Jayasimha I** performed the **Ashvamedha**.

n19f08161ede.s: The dispatch of 72 merchants to China is associated with:
n19f08161ede.x: The 72-merchant mission to China is associated with Kulothunga I; Saktivarma's coins have been found in Arakan, Burma.
xa: Merchant guild HQ (medieval Andhra): **Penugonda**.
Saktivarma I had beaten Kalyani Satyasraya's army with Chola help.

nb003b3c0af5.s: Which place was the headquarters of the merchant guilds in medieval Andhra?
nb003b3c0af5.x: Penugonda was the headquarters of the merchant guilds. Pithapuram and Vengi were Eastern Chalukya capitals, and Arakan in Burma is where Saktivarma's coins were found.
xs: **Penugonda** was the HQ of the merchant guilds — option **(2)**.
**Pithapuram** and **Vengi** were capitals; **Arakan (Burma)** is where **Saktivarma**'s coins were found.
xa: **Kulothunga I** sent **72 merchants to China**.
Trade with the **eastern islands** under **Rajaraja Narendra**.

n5d29e1a0be6.s: Hallisaka, identified with Kolatam, was regarded as:
n5d29e1a0be6.x: Hallisaka, or Kolatam, was a popular dance associated with the cultural life of the period.
n5d29e1a0be6.tq: Distinguish a performing art from administrative and fiscal terminology.
xs: **Hallisaka (Kolatam)** was a **popular dance** — option **(2)**.
It is not a revenue, office or Jain formula — the Jain opening formula was "**Om Namah Siddham**".
xa: Court singer and dancer: **Chellavva**.
Instrument sculptures at **Bhairavakona**: **veena, mridangam, cymbals**.

nac6014b88aa.s: Ghatikas in the Eastern Chalukya period were:
o: Military cantonments attached to royal forts
Jain cave temples used for royal burials
Advanced Sanskrit schools attached to agraharas or temples
Merchant guilds situated at coastal ports
nac6014b88aa.x: Ghatikas were advanced Sanskrit schools attached to agraharas or temples.
nac6014b88aa.tq: Apply the institutional definition while rejecting misleading associations with military, commercial and temple structures.
xs: **Ghatikas** were **advanced Sanskrit schools** attached to **agraharas or temples** — option **(3)**.
Merchant guilds were headquartered at **Penugonda**, a separate institution.
xa: Heads: **Ghatika Samanyulu** — e.g. **Mandasharma** at **Asanapura**, Kammanadu.
Subjects: **Vedas, Vedangas, Dharmashastras, Tarka, Vyakarana, Arthashastra, Dhanurveda, Ayurveda**.

n9456c7a868a.s: Which of the following subjects was NOT included among the subjects taught in Ghatikas?
n9456c7a868a.x: Ghatikas taught subjects such as Vedas, Vedangas, Dharmashastras, Tarka, Vyakarana, Arthashastra, Dhanurveda and Ayurveda. Hallisaka was a popular dance, not an academic subject.
n9456c7a868a.tq: Separate the educational curriculum from a performing-art term.
xs: **Hallisaka** was not a Ghatika subject — option **(4)**; it is a popular dance (**Kolatam**).
Subjects taught: **Vedas, Vedangas, Dharmashastras, Tarka, Vyakarana, Arthashastra, Dhanurveda, Ayurveda**.
xa: Ghatikas were **advanced Sanskrit schools**.
Jain pupils began with "**Om Namah Siddham**".

n114a04dd415.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler is stated to have performed the Ashvamedha?
n114a04dd415.x: Jayasimha I performed the Ashvamedha, while royal prashastis also boast of several Ashvamedhas.
n114a04dd415.tq: Directly identify the ruler associated with a specific Vedic ritual.
xs: **Jayasimha I** performed the **Ashvamedha** — option **(4)**.
**Vijayaditya II** built **108 temples**; **Vimaladitya** became a Jain; **Danarnava** was Vaishnava.
xa: Royal prashastis boast of many Ashvamedhas.
Danarnava built the **Mandavya Narayana** temple, **Samalkot**.
**Chalukya Bhima I**: **Pancharamas**.

nb7621d4a652.s: Vimaladitya built the Ramakonda cave temple at Ramatirtham for whom?
o: His Jain guru Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva
nb7621d4a652.x: Vimaladitya built the Ramakonda cave temple for his Jain guru Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva, as recorded in the Ramateertham inscription.
nb7621d4a652.tq: Link the donor, monument and religious teacher rather than confusing the site with another grant.
xs: **Vimaladitya** built the **Ramakonda** cave temple for his Jain guru **Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva** — option **(1)**.
Source: the **Ramateertham inscription**; site **Ramatirtham** (Vizianagaram).
xa: Vimaladitya was the **only Vengi Chalukya king to become a Jain**.
Other Jain grants: **Mushikonda** (Vishnuvardhana III), **Kaluchumbarru** (Ammaraja II), **Nedumba Vasati** (Ayyana Mahadevi).

n8a446f9dccc.s: Who built the Jain Nedumba Vasati at Vijayawada?
n8a446f9dccc.x: Queen Ayyana Mahadevi built the Nedumba Vasati (APPSC G2 2025; the key makes her the wife of Kubja Vishnuvardhana). Chamekamba obtained the Kaluchumbarru grant, Kundavva was Vimaladitya's Chola queen and Chellavva was a court singer.
xs: Queen **Ayyana Mahadevi** built the **Nedumba Vasati**, Vijayawada — option **(2)**.
**Chamekamba** obtained the **Kaluchumbarru** grant; **Chellavva** was a court singer and dancer.
xa: ⚠ G2 2025 key: wife of **Kubja Vishnuvardhana**; the APHQ book says **Gunaga Vijayaditya**.
Leading Jain centre: **Potlacheruvu** (G2 2017 key).

n31bd9bfab47.s: The persecution of Jains at Potlacheruvu took place during the:
n31bd9bfab47.x: The persecution of Jains at Potlacheruvu occurred in the Kakatiya age, not under the Eastern Chalukyas, who patronised Jainism, Buddhism and Hinduism.
xa: **Vimaladitya** even became a Jain.
Buddhism survived at **Amaravati** and **Nagarjunakonda**.

n910b93c002d.s: Which of the following were the Shaiva sects prevalent under the Eastern Chalukyas?
n910b93c002d.x: The Shaiva sects of the period were Kapalika, Kalamukha and Pasupata. Pancharatra and Vaikhanasa are Vaishnava traditions, and Virashaiva persecution came later in the Kakatiya age.
xs: The Shaiva sects were **Kapalika, Kalamukha and Pasupata** — option **(1)**.
**Virashaiva** persecution of Jains came later, in the **Kakatiya** age; **Pancharatra** and **Vaikhanasa** are not Shaiva sects.
xa: Shaivism was **dominant**; custom of a **temple for each battle**.
Kapalikas emerged from the **Misra Saivam** school.
Royal title **Parama Maheshwara** reflects Shaiva faith.

nc8fb52518d5.s: The heads of Ghatikas were known as:
nc8fb52518d5.x: The heads of Ghatikas were called Ghatika Samanyulu.
nc8fb52518d5.tq: Match the educational institution with its specialised headship title.
xs: Ghatika heads were the **Ghatika Samanyulu** — option **(3)**.
**Sthanadhipati** managed temples; **Vanneyus** collected tolls; **Vishayapati** headed a Vishaya.
xa: Example: **Mandasharma** at **Asanapura** Ghatika, Kammanadu.
His son **Katikasharma** appears in the **Nidamarru** inscription.

n7e6334345cb.s: Under the Eastern Chalukyas, Chellavva is an example of a:
n7e6334345cb.x: Musicians and dancers were attached to Eastern Chalukya temples and courts, and Chellavva is an example of such a court-linked singer and dancer.
xa: Popular dance: **Hallisaka (Kolatam)**.
Instrument sculptures at **Bhairavakona** (Nellore): **veena, mridangam, cymbals**.
Temple manager: **Sthanadhipati**.

nd6ff89a3cb5.s: Who composed the medical treatise Kalyanakaraka?
nd6ff89a3cb5.x: Ugradityacharya composed Kalyanakaraka, a medical treatise of the Eastern Chalukya period.
nd6ff89a3cb5.tq: Directly match an author with a specialised work while avoiding the previously tested item wording.
xs: **Ugradityacharya** composed the medical treatise **Kalyanakaraka** — option **(1)** (G2 2012, 2019 keys).
**Bhattavamana** wrote the **Kavyalankara Sutras**; **Katikasharma** and **Mandasharma** were Ghatika scholars.
xa: Ghatikas also taught **Ayurveda**.
Bhattavamana's title: **Kavi Vrishabha**.

n319a6b718a7.s: 'Kavigayaka Kalpataru' was the title of which Eastern Chalukya ruler?
n319a6b718a7.x: Ammaraja II was Kavigayaka Kalpataru; Vishnuvardhana III was Kavi Pandita Kamadhenu and Rajaraja Narendra Kavyageetha Priyudu.
xa: Vishnuvardhana III also granted **Mushikonda** to Jains.
Ammaraja II made the **Kaluchumbarru** grant at **Chamekamba**'s request.

n0ed2c0aa319.s: Eastern Chalukya temples of the Vengi School mainly followed which architectural style?
n0ed2c0aa319.x: The Eastern Chalukyas mainly followed the Dravida style, blending Pallava and Badami Chalukya influences with local Andhra features; this tradition is called the Vengi School.
xa: Another name for it: **Vesara (Chalukya) style** — a blend of the **Dravidian vimana** with **Buddhist art**.
Model temple: **Draksharama Bhimeswara** = **Chalukya-Chola style** (G2 **2025** key, asked twice).
⚠ Trap distractors: **Brihadeeswara** (Imperial Chola, Thanjavur), **Padmakshi** (Kakatiya, Hanamkonda), **Lepakshi** (Vijayanagara).

n3a18ceadcc2.s: Eastern Chalukya temple building was concentrated in the:
n3a18ceadcc2.x: Eastern Chalukya (Vengi school, Vesara/Chalukya style) temple building was concentrated in the Krishna-Godavari delta.
xa: Base style: mainly **Dravida** + **Pallava (Kanchi)** and **Badami Chalukya** influences.
**Draksharama Bhimeswara** = model **Chalukya-Chola style** temple (G2 2025 key).
⚠ Distractors: **Brihadeeswara** (Chola), **Padmakshi** (Kakatiya), **Lepakshi** (Vijayanagara).
**Vijayeswara** temple at Bikkavolu has **Ganga and Yamuna** carvings.

n425af6e17dc.s: Which temple is the model of the Chalukya-Chola style, combining Pallava and early Chalukya features into an independent regional style?
n425af6e17dc.x: The Draksharama Bhimeswara temple exemplifies the Chalukya-Chola style (APPSC G2 2025 key, asked twice). Brihadeeswara is Imperial Chola, Padmakshi is Kakatiya and Lepakshi is Vijayanagara: the trap distractors.
xs: The **Draksharama Bhimeswara temple** is the model of the **Chalukya-Chola style** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Brihadeeswara** (Thanjavur) is Imperial Chola; **Padmakshi** (Hanamkonda) is Kakatiya; **Lepakshi** is Vijayanagara.
This was the G2 **2025** key, asked twice.
xa: Draksharama Bhimeswara was built by **Chalukya Bhima I**.
Draksharama is one of the **Trilinga kshetras** and one of the **Pancharamas**.
Its twin: the two-storeyed **Kumararama** at **Samalkot**, closely similar in plan.

n5ff2f2fb08e.s: The Navabrahma temple complex at Alampur was constructed during the rule of which dynasty?
n5ff2f2fb08e.x: The nine Navabrahma temples at Alampur were built by the Badami Chalukyas during the 7th–8th centuries CE.
n5ff2f2fb08e.tq: Use the dynasty–monument association and avoid confusing the Badami and Eastern Chalukyas.
xs: The **Alampur Navabrahma** temples were built by the **Badami Chalukyas** — option **(2)** is correct.
The Badami Chalukyas developed **Vesara** in Karnataka; Alampur is their example in AP.
The **Eastern Chalukyas (Vengi)** followed a Dravida-based style leading to the **Chalukya-Chola** phase.
xa: Badami Chalukya features also shaped the **Vengi School** of the Eastern Chalukyas.
Chalukya-Chola model temple: **Draksharama Bhimeswara**.

n2c40dc6d600.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 108 Shiva temples of the Eastern Chalukyas?
o: The source for this claim is the Kopparam inscription.
They were called Narendresvaralayas or Narendra Mrigeswaralayas.
One temple was built at each of his 108 battle sites.
They were built by Vijayaditya II (Narendramrigaraja).
n2c40dc6d600.x: The source is the Sataluru inscription; the Kopparam inscription is Pulakesin II's record. The other three statements are correct.
xa: This fact was keyed in G2 **2008, 2012, 2019 and 2025**.
**Chalukya Bhima I** built the **Pancharamas** / made them Shaiva kshetras.
**Kubja Vishnuvardhana** built the **Kunti Madhava** temple at **Pithapuram**.

n61d703b0197.s: Which temple at Rajahmundry later became the Pedda Masjid under the Tughlaqs?
n61d703b0197.x: The Vishnu temple at Rajahmundry, linked with Rajaraja Narendra like the Kotilingala and Markandeya temples, later became the Pedda Masjid under the Tughlaqs.
xa: Rajahmundry is called the **cultural capital of the Andhras**.
**Ammaraju** and **Chalukya Bhima I** are linked with **Bhimeshwara** temples on the Godavari.
Rajaraja Narendra built **three Shiva temples** at **Kalidindi** for fallen Chola soldiers.
⚠ 2025 key marked "Rajaraja Narendra built the **Rajarajeswara temple at Biccavole**" as **incorrect**.

nfebb8c267f7.s: Which city is known as the cultural capital of the Andhras?
nfebb8c267f7.x: Rajahmundry is called the cultural capital of the Andhras.
nfebb8c267f7.tq: Recall the direct cultural-geographical epithet associated with the city.
xs: **Rajahmundry** is the **cultural capital of the Andhras** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Samalkot** is Chalukya Bhimavaram (Kumararama); **Amaravati** is Amararama.
xa: **Rajaraja Narendra** built the **Kotilingala, Markandeya and Vishnu** temples at Rajahmundry.
The Vishnu temple later became the **Pedda Masjid** under the **Tughlaqs**.

nap-history-18-7.s: Who built the twin Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot?
nap-history-18-7.x: Chalukya Bhima I built the twin temples Draksharama Bhimeswara and Kumararama Bhimeswara (Samalkot). Prola Raju II and Rudra Deva were Kakatiyas and Anavema Reddy a Reddi king.
n: Chalukya Bhima I built the twin temples of Draksharama Bhimeswara and Kumararama Bhimeswara. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Kumararama Bhimeswara is located at Samalkota. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
xa: He also built **Somarama** at Gunupudi and the Kumaraswamy temple at **Chebrolu**.
His commander **Bhattupu** built the **Parvateswara** temple at Indrakeeladri.
Both shrines were later **renovated by the Reddis**.
Draksharama is one of the **Trilinga kshetras**.

n08a20893633.s: Who is associated with building the Pancharamas or making them Shaiva kshetras?
n08a20893633.x: Chalukya Bhima I is associated with building the Pancharamas or establishing them as Shaiva kshetras.
n08a20893633.tq: Use the builder–religious foundation association rather than the place-based clues.
xs: **Chalukya Bhima I** built the **Pancharamas** or made them Shaiva kshetras — option **(1)** is correct.
**Danarnava** built the **Mandavya Narayana** temple at Samalkot; **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** built **Kunti Madhava** at Pithapuram.
xa: Chalukya Bhima I also built **Bhimeswara (Draksharama)**, **Kumararama (Samalkot)** in memory of his son, and **Someswara (Somarama)** at Gunupudi.
He also built the **Kumaraswamy temple** at **Chebrolu**.
His commander **Bhattupu** built the **Parvateswara** temple on **Indrakeeladri**, Bezawada.

n4a177e6921d.s: Ksheerarama, one of the Pancharamas, is located at:
n4a177e6921d.x: Ksheerarama is at Palakollu (West Godavari); Kumararama is at Samalkot, Amararama at Amaravati and Draksharama at Draksharama.
xa: The fifth: **Somarama** at **Gunupudi, Bhimavaram** (West Godavari).
All except **Ksheerarama** are **two-storeyed**.
Literary sources: **Skanda Purana** and Srinatha's **Bhimeswara Puranam**.

ndd57a192038.s: Somarama, one of the Pancharamas, is located at:
ndd57a192038.x: Somarama is at Gunupudi near Bhimavaram; Samalkot is Bheemarama/Kumararama (Chalukya Bhimavaram) and Palakollu is Ksheerarama.
xa: The five: **Draksharama, Kumararama, Ksheerarama, Somarama, Amararama** (Amaravati).
All except **Ksheerarama** are **two-storeyed**.
**Chalukya Bhima I** built / made the Pancharamas Shaiva kshetras.
Literary sources: **Skanda Purana** and Srinatha's **Bhimeswara Puranam**.

n7a8e2c25644.s: The two-storeyed Bhimeswara shrines at Draksharama and Samalkot were built by:
n7a8e2c25644.x: Both are two-storeyed Bhimeswara shrines of Chalukya Bhima I, later renovated by the Reddis; the Samalkot gopuram is a later addition.
xa: Draksharama has a massive lingam and a huge **Nandi mandapa**.
**Kumararama** at Samalkot was built in memory of Chalukya Bhima's **son**.
**Somarama** at Gunupudi was also built by Chalukya Bhima I.
⚠ Some notes wrongly list a "Chalukya Bhimavaram Shiva temple (Palakollu)".

nab1f4c0d3cc.s: The Bikkavolu (Biccavolu) temple group belongs to the time of:
nab1f4c0d3cc.x: The Bikkavolu group belongs to Gunaga Vijayaditya's time (9th century); Chalukya Bhima I built the Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot.
xa: Other members: **Mukteswara, Chandrasekhara, Raja Raja**.
Some notes (Block10) call Bikkavolu a **Chalukya-Reddi transition** group with later Reddi additions.

n9166283126a.s: Which of the Pancharama temples is NOT two-storeyed?
n9166283126a.x: All the Pancharamas except Ksheerarama are two-storeyed; the Skanda Purana and Srinatha's Bhimeswara Puranam are literary sources on them.
xa: The five: **Draksharama**, **Kumararama (Samalkot)**, **Ksheerarama (Palakollu)**, **Somarama (Gunupudi)**, **Amararama (Amaravati)**.
**Chalukya Bhima I** built them / made them Shaiva kshetras.
Draksharama and Samalkot were both later renovated by the **Reddis**.

nap-history-18-6.s: Who fought 108 fierce battles over 12 years against the Rashtrakutas and their Gangavadi allies?
nap-history-18-6.x: Vijayaditya II (Narendra Mrigaraja) of the Eastern Chalukyas fought 108 battles over 12 years against the Rashtrakutas under Govinda III and Amoghavarsha I and their Gangavadi allies.
nap-history-18-6.tq: Recall the Eastern Chalukya ruler of 108 battles.
n: Vijayaditya II fought 108 fierce battles over 12 years. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Vijayaditya II fought against the Rashtrakutas. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Vijayaditya II fought against the Gangavadi allies of the Rashtrakutas. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Govinda III led the Rashtrakutas in the conflict with Vijayaditya II. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Amoghavarsha I led the Rashtrakutas in the conflict with Vijayaditya II. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
xs: **Vijayaditya II** fought **108 fierce battles** over **12 years** — option **(3)**.
He fought the **Rashtrakutas**, led by **Govinda III** and **Amoghavarsha I**, and their **Gangavadi allies**.
He built **108 Saiva temples** (**Narendraeswara**), one at each battle site.
xa: His title: **Narendramrigaraja**.
The **Sataluru** inscription records the temples.
**Chalukya Bhima I** built the twin **Draksharama** and **Kumararama** Bhimeswara temples.
Gunaga Vijayaditya defeated **Krishna II**.

nb79bd6a7115.s: The Renati Cholas claimed descent from:
nb79bd6a7115.x: The Renati Cholas claimed Suryavamsa Kshatriya descent from Karikala Chola, although their culture and administration were Telugu.
nb79bd6a7115.tq: Separate claimed ancestry from cultural and administrative identity.
xs: The Renati Cholas claimed **Suryavamsa Kshatriya** descent from **Karikala Chola** — option **(1)** is correct.
Yet their culture and administration were **Telugu**.
**Madhurantaka** is the Pottapi Choda ancestor of the Nellore Chodas, not of the Renati line.
xa: Period: **5th to the 8th centuries**.
Territory: **Renadu**, where **Kadapa, Kurnool and Chittoor** meet, in the upper **Pennar** basin.
The Nellore Chodas also traced descent from Karikala via **Madhurantaka Pottapi Choda**.

n9c2bbe1d104.s: The capital of the Renati Cholas was:
o: Peddachapalli, in Kamalapuram taluk of Kadapa
n9c2bbe1d104.x: The principal capital was Peddachapalli in Kamalapuram taluk of Kadapa. Chimbapuram was specifically Dhanunjaya's capital.
n9c2bbe1d104.tq: Distinguish the dynasty’s capital from the founder’s capital.
xs: The Renati Chola capital was **Peddachapalli**, in **Kamalapuram taluk of Kadapa** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Chimbapuram** was only **Dhanunjaya**'s capital; **Vikrama Simhapuri** is Nellore of the Nellore Chodas; **Konidena** near Narasaraopet was the Konidena Chodas' capital.
xa: Renadu = **Renadu Saptasahasra** (**7,000** villages).
Ruled from the **5th to the 8th centuries**.

n2cd2ef6da97.s: The Telugu epigraphic practice of the Renati Cholas was later taken up by the:
n2cd2ef6da97.x: The Eastern Chalukyas later adopted the Telugu epigraphic practice associated with the Renati Cholas.
n2cd2ef6da97.tq: Trace the transmission of an administrative and epigraphic practice.
xs: The **Eastern Chalukyas** took up the Renati Telugu epigraphic practice — option **(3)** is correct.
The Renati Cholas were the **first to make Telugu a royal and legislative language**, replacing **Prakrit + Sanskrit**.
xa: First Telugu inscription: **Kalamalla** (**575 CE**).
Credit: "Keeping Telugu in the history of Andhra" (G2 **2019** key).
Renadu art shows **Pallava** influence.

n674954f030d.s: Who among the following was regarded as the progenitor of the Renati Chola line?
n674954f030d.x: Nandivarma is identified as the progenitor of the Renati Chola line.
n674954f030d.tq: Separate the progenitor from the founder and the last ruler.
xs: **Nandivarma** was the **progenitor** of the Renati Cholas — option **(1)** is correct.
**Dhanunjaya Varma**, his son, was the **founder**; **Satyaditya** bore the title Chola Maharaja; **Elachola Maharaja** was the last ruler.
xa: ⚠ Progenitor = **Nandivarma**; founder = **Dhanunjaya Varma**.
**Mahendra Vikramavarman**, grandson of Nandivarma, had the title **Muditha Silakshara Navarama**.
⚠ For the Nellore Chodas, the progenitor is **Bijjana**.

nfb401b242cf.s: Who is regarded as the greatest ruler of the Renati Cholas?
nfb401b242cf.x: Punyakumara (625-650 CE), with titles such as Pormukharama and Prithvivallabha, was the greatest Renati Chola ruler. Nandivarma was the progenitor, Dhanunjaya Varma the founder and Elachola Maharaja the last ruler.
nfb401b242cf.tq: Progenitor Nandivarma, founder Dhanunjaya, greatest Punyakumara, last Elachola.
xs: **Punyakumara** (**625-650 CE**) was the greatest Renati Chola ruler — option **(3)** is correct.
**Nandivarma** was the progenitor, **Dhanunjaya Varma** the founder, **Elachola Maharaja** the last ruler.
xa: Titles: **Pormukharama**, **Purushashardula**, Uttamottama, **Prithvivallabha**; wife **Vasantapori**.
His inscriptions: **Potladurthi**, **Malepadu** and **Erragudipadu**.

n38e416ad160.s: The Kalamalla inscription is associated with which ruler and date?
n38e416ad160.x: The Kalamalla inscription belongs to Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya, also known as Dhanunjaya Varma, and is dated to 575 CE.
xs: The **Kalamalla** inscription is of **Dhanunjaya Varma**, dated **575 CE** — option **(2)** is correct.
He is also called **Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya**; it is in **Kadapa district**.
**Punyakumara** (**625-650 CE**) left Potladurthi, Malepadu and Erragudipadu records.
xa: Kalamalla = the **first Telugu inscription** (G2 **2012** key); in prose; not fully available today.
⚠ "Erragudipadu inscription of 575 CE" is a trap that merges two records.

nd0cc73b03ef.s: How many Telugu inscriptions of the Renati Cholas, mostly donation records, are known?
nd0cc73b03ef.x: Thirty-three Renati Chola Telugu inscriptions are known, most of them donation records (dana sasanalu).
xa: The Renati Cholas replaced **Prakrit + Sanskrit** with Telugu in records.
First Telugu inscription: **Kalamalla** (**575 CE**) of **Dhanunjaya Varma**.

ne91301fd9b2.s: Between 575 and 848 CE, Telugu appeared in full prose sentences in the records of which dynasty?
ne91301fd9b2.x: The Renati Cholas made Telugu a royal and legislative language, replacing Prakrit and Sanskrit, and from 575 to 848 CE Telugu appeared in full prose sentences.
xa: Before **575 CE**, only names were in Telugu.
Credited with "Keeping Telugu in the history of Andhra" (G2 **2019** key).
They gave Telugu its first royal dignity, **five centuries before Nannaya**.

n6287e788f81.s: Before 575 CE, Telugu appeared in the available records mainly in the form of:
n6287e788f81.x: Before 575 CE, Telugu appeared mainly in names; complete prose sentences became characteristic from 575 to 848 CE.
n6287e788f81.tq: Use the chronological contrast between names and prose sentences.
xs: Before **575 CE**, Telugu appeared only as **individual names** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Full prose sentences** came only in **575 to 848 CE**.
xa: The **Kalamalla** inscription (**575 CE**) is the first Telugu inscription.
The Renati Cholas made Telugu a **royal and legislative language**.

n949b3d353c0.s: The Nellore Chodas were associated with:
n949b3d353c0.x: The Nellore Chodas were associated with Vikrama Simhapuri; the Konidena Chodas with Kammanadu, the Pottapi Chodas with Pottapi (Kadapa) and the Renati Chodas with Renadu.
xa: Konidena capital: **Konidena (Kotyadona)** near **Narasaraopet**; from the mid-**10th** c.
Pottapi Chodas came from **Madhurantaka**, a vassal of **Chola Parantaka**.
**Nannuru** was another branch.

n91a96012eeb.s: The Velanati Chodas came to an end when:
o: Dhanunjaya Varma shifted the capital to Peddachapalli
Kakatiya Ganapatideva killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola
n91a96012eeb.x: The Velanati Choda line ended when Kakatiya Ganapatideva killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola.
n91a96012eeb.tq: Use the ruler–event trap to distinguish the end of a branch.
xs: The Velanati Chodas ended when **Kakatiya Ganapatideva killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Tikkana Choda** was a Nellore Choda king; **Dhanunjaya Varma** and **Punyakumara** were Renati Cholas.
xa: Ganapati also helped **Manumasiddhi II** against **Vijayaganda Gopala**.
Nellore (**Vikrama Simhapuri**) = foremost Telugu Choda clan.

n9c0036e32f5.s: Which one of the following was NOT a title of Punyakumara?
n9c0036e32f5.x: Pormukharama, Purushashardula and Uttamottama were titles of Punyakumara. Chola Sthapanacharya was the title taken by Tikkana Choda.
n9c0036e32f5.tq: Find the title belonging to a different ruler.
xs: **Chola Sthapanacharya** was not Punyakumara's title — option **(3)** is correct.
It was taken by **Tikkana Choda** (Nellore Chodas) after putting **Rajendra Chola** on the Chola throne.
Punyakumara's titles: **Pormukharama**, **Purushashardula**, **Uttamottama**, **Prithvivallabha**.
xa: Punyakumara (**625-650 CE**) was the greatest Renati ruler; wife **Vasantapori**.
⚠ **Tikkana Choda** (king) ≠ **Kavi-Brahma Tikkana** (poet-minister).

nb26b1987eea.s: Kavi-Brahma Tikkana was minister and court poet to:
nb26b1987eea.x: Tikkana was minister and court poet of Manumasiddhi II and sought Kakatiya Ganapati's help against Vijayaganda Gopala.
xa: ⚠ In the notes, the help from Ganapati is recorded under **Manumasiddhi II**, Tikkana's patron.
⚠ Tikkana Choda (king) ≠ Kavi-Brahma Tikkana (poet-minister).

n70efa5ffc87.s: The Vaidumbas are particularly associated with the issue of:
o: Gold coins bearing only Sanskrit legends
Prakrit inscriptions from the Godavari delta
n70efa5ffc87.x: The Vaidumbas issued Telugu hero-stone inscriptions, also known as veerakal records.
n70efa5ffc87.tq: Identify the distinctive epigraphic practice of the Vaidumbas.
xs: The Vaidumbas issued **Telugu hero-stone (veerakal) inscriptions** — option **(4)** is correct.
They succeeded the Renati Cholas along with the **Banas**.
xa: The Renati Telugu epigraphic practice was taken up by the **Eastern Chalukyas**.
The Renati Cholas left **33** Telugu inscriptions, mostly **dana sasanalu**.

na95d518cbb9.s: The Renati Cholas gave Telugu its first royal dignity approximately how many centuries before Nannaya?
na95d518cbb9.x: By using Telugu in royal and legislative records, the Renati Cholas gave it royal dignity about five centuries before Nannaya.
xa: First Telugu inscription: **Kalamalla** (**575 CE**); last Renati ruler: **Elachola Maharaja**.
Credited with "Keeping Telugu in the history of Andhra" (G2 **2019** key).

ne1dc88ce0f1.s: The Musunuri Nayakas emerged in which period, and which rulers are associated with them?
ne1dc88ce0f1.x: The Musunuri Nayakas emerged in the 1330s and are associated with Prolaya Nayaka and Kapaya Nayaka.
ne1dc88ce0f1.tq: Match the dynasty with its emergence period and principal rulers.
xs: The **Musunuri Nayakas** emerged in the **1330s** under **Prolaya Nayaka** and **Kapaya Nayaka** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Rudradeva/Ganapatideva** were Kakatiyas; **Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk** founded the Imad Shahis; **Sultan Quli/Muhammad Quli** were Qutb Shahis.
xa: **Kapaya Nayaka (1336-1368)** ruled from **Orugallu**.
He ceded **Golconda fort** to Bahmani **Muhammad I** after his son **Vinayaka** was killed (**1361**).
After the Musunuris, **76 Nayaks** carved out states.

n72e54897830.s: Who founded the Imad Shahi dynasty of Berar, and what was its capital?
n72e54897830.x: Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk founded the Imad Shahis, whose capital was Ellichpur, also called Achalpur.
n72e54897830.tq: Start from the sure founder–capital pair to eliminate the other Deccan dynasties.
xs: **Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk** founded the Imad Shahis of Berar, capital **Ellichpur (Achalpur)** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Hasan Gangu** founded the Bahmanis (**Gulbarga**); **Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk** founded the Qutb Shahis (**Golconda**).
xa: Imad Shahis began in **1490**.
**Berar** was annexed by **Ahmadnagar** in **1574**.
Berar did **not** join the coalition at Talikota.

nc12dbbc9d11.s: Which dynasty is regarded as the second unifier of all Telugu lands?
nc12dbbc9d11.x: The Satavahanas, Kakatiyas and Qutb Shahis are regarded as the first, second and third unifiers of the Telugu lands.
xa: **1323** ended Telugu imperial unity until the **Qutb Shahis** reunited the region.
Qutb Shahis ruled **1518-1687** with **7 sultans**.

n1159a3805c0.s: Who shifted the Reddi capital from Addanki to Kondavidu?
n1159a3805c0.x: Anavema Reddy shifted the Reddi capital from Addanki to Kondavidu.
xa: Reddi kingdom began **1325**; later a **Rajahmundry** branch.
After **Talikota (1565)**, Golconda took **Kondavidu** and **Machilipatnam**.
n1159a3805c0.fixed: capital moved Addanki -> Kondavidu by Anavota Reddy (Anavema later)

ned8d24e2b46.s: The Musunuri Nayakas, Reddis and Velamas became independent kingdoms after 1323 because they were:
o: Three of Prataparudra's generals who survived the fall of the Kakatiyas
Three governors appointed by the Qutb Shahis
Three branches of the Imad Shahi dynasty
Three commanders of the Gajapati army
ned8d24e2b46.x: The Musunuri Nayakas, Reddis and Velamas were three of Prataparudra's generals who survived the Kakatiya collapse in 1323 and established independent kingdoms.
ned8d24e2b46.tq: Identify the common political background shared by three emerging houses.
xs: The Musunuris, Reddis and Velamas were **three of Prataparudra's generals who survived 1323** — option **(1)** is correct.
They were **Kakatiya Nayakas**, not Qutb Shahi governors, Imad Shahi branches or Gajapati commanders.
xa: Telangana succession: Kakatiyas → **Delhi Sultanate (1323)** → **Musunuri Nayakas** → Velamas / Bahmanis → Qutb Shahis.
Founders: **Singama** (Velama), **Prolaya Vemareddy** (Reddi).

n76300cbf19e.s: In which year did the Delhi Sultanate replace the Kakatiyas at Warangal?
n76300cbf19e.x: The Telangana succession ran Kakatiyas, Delhi Sultanate (1323), Musunuri Nayakas, Velamas/Bahmanis and then the Qutb Shahis.
xa: First Muslim attack on **Orugallu** = **1303**.
**1323** ended Telugu imperial unity until the Qutb Shahis.

n3b3f269f7e0.s: After the Musunuri period, Prolaya Vemareddy is associated with which political formation?
n3b3f269f7e0.x: Prolaya Vemareddy is associated with the Reddis; Singama with the Velamas, Harihara-Bukka with Vijayanagara and Hasan Gangu with the Bahmanis.
xa: After the Musunuris, **76 Nayaks** carved out states.
Singama was of **Racherla**; Prolaya Vemareddy began in **Pakanadu**.

ne30098c4aae.s: The year 1323 is historically significant in the political history of Andhradesa because it marks:
o: The beginning of the Vijayanagara Empire in Rayalaseema
The defeat of the Gajapatis by Krishnadevaraya
The beginning of the Reddi rule in Coastal Andhra
The end of Telugu imperial unity until the Qutb Shahis reunited the region
ne30098c4aae.x: The fall of the Kakatiyas in 1323 ended Telugu imperial unity; the Telugu lands stayed divided among Musunuris, Reddis, Velamas, Vijayanagara, Bahmanis and Gajapatis until the Qutb Shahis reunited the region. Vijayanagara began in 1336 and the Reddis in 1325, and Krishnadevaraya's Gajapati wars came in the 16th century.
ne30098c4aae.tq: Link the date to its broad political consequence rather than to a particular battle.
xs: **1323** = **end of Telugu imperial unity** until the **Qutb Shahis** reunited the region — option **(4)** is correct.
Vijayanagara began in **1336** and the Reddis in **1325**, not 1323.
xa: In **1323** the Kakatiyas fell to the **Delhi Sultanate**.
First Muslim attack on Orugallu: **1303**.

nap-history-16-8.s: Who founded the Ikshvaku dynasty of the Krishna valley?
nap-history-16-8.x: Shantamula I founded the Ikshvaku dynasty; Simuka founded the Satavahana dynasty.
n: The Satavahana Dynasty was founded by Simuka. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 22-23]
The Ikshvaku Dynasty was founded by Shantamula-I. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 22-23]
The Vijayanagara Empire was founded by Harihara-I and Bukka Raya I. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 22-23]
Hyderabad State was founded by Chin Qilich Khan. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 22-23]
xa: Unifiers of all Telugu lands: **Satavahanas**, **Kakatiyas**, **Qutb Shahis**.
Vijayanagara: **1336-1646**; Bahmanis from **1347** (**Hasan Gangu**).
Qutb Shahis: **1518-1687**, **7 sultans**.
**Imad Shahis** (Berar) — **1490**, **Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk**.

n959a1c4a914.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about political succession in Coastal Andhra?
o: The Qutb Shahis came after 1565 in the later succession.
The Kakatiyas succeeded the Velanati Chodas.
The Eastern Chalukyas preceded the Velanati Chodas.
n959a1c4a914.x: The Reddis succeeded the Kakatiyas, not the other way round; the other three statements are correct.
xa: Eastern Chalukyas merged with the Cholas under **Kulottunga I** (**1070**).
The Velanati Chodas ended when Ganapatideva killed **Mummadi Rajendra Chola**.

ne92a470e3af.s: Which of the following correctly describes the sequence of events concerning the Bahmani kingdom?
o: It was founded in 1490 and divided into five sultanates in 1518.
It was founded by Sultan Quli and later merged with the Vijayanagara Empire.
It split after the Battle of Talikota in 1565 and Berar was annexed in 1574.
It split into five Deccan Sultanates after Mahmud Gawan's execution in 1482.
ne92a470e3af.x: Mahmud Gawan was executed in 1482, after which the Bahmani kingdom split into the five Deccan Sultanates. Berar was later annexed by Ahmadnagar in 1574.
ne92a470e3af.tq: Test the causal sequence by identifying the event that preceded the political fragmentation.
xs: The Bahmani kingdom split into **five Deccan Sultanates** after **Mahmud Gawan's execution (1482)** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was founded in **1347** by **Hasan Gangu**, not by Sultan Quli; **1490** is the Imad Shahi date.
**1574** is when **Ahmadnagar annexed Berar**, not a Bahmani split.
xa: The five: **Golconda** (Qutb Shahi), **Bijapur** (Adil Shahi), **Ahmadnagar** (Nizam Shahi), **Bidar** (Barid Shahi), **Berar** (Imad Shahi).
Bahmani capital: **Gulbarga**.

n48da46faf2a.s: The Charminar at Hyderabad was constructed in:
n48da46faf2a.x: Hyderabad city was founded in 1591, while the Charminar was constructed in 1594.
n48da46faf2a.tq: Distinguish two closely associated years by linking the monument to its specific event.
xs: The **Charminar** was built in **1594** — option **(4)** is correct.
**1591** is the founding of **Hyderabad city** by **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah**; **1518** is the Golconda state; **1565** is Talikota.
xa: ⚠ State = **Sultan Quli** (**1518**); city = **Muhammad Quli** (**1591**).
Hyderabad became the capital (some notes: from **1592**).

n4f62d5a3a09.s: Who was the last ruler of the Qutb Shahi state?
n4f62d5a3a09.x: The Shia, Persian-using Qutb Shahi state ended under Abul Hasan Tana Shah.
xa: Tana Shah's reign ended in **1687**.
Founder of the state: **Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** (**1518**).

n16c336dab9c.s: After the Battle of Talikota in 1565, Golconda acquired:
o: Kondavidu, Machilipatnam and the coastal districts
n16c336dab9c.x: After Talikota, Golconda took Kondavidu, Machilipatnam and the coastal districts.
n16c336dab9c.tq: Test the territorial consequences of a major battle through the acquired places.
xs: After **Talikota (1565)**, Golconda took **Kondavidu, Machilipatnam** and the coastal districts — option **(3)** is correct.
**Addanki/Kondavidu** were Reddi capitals; **Rachakonda/Devarakonda** Velama; **Gulbarga** Bahmani; **Ellichpur** Imad Shahi.
xa: Coastal Andhra: ... → Gajapatis / Vijayanagara → **Qutb Shahis (after 1565)**.
Vijayanagara's capital moved to **Penugonda and Chandragiri** after 1565.

n998e2e0788e.s: Which of the following territories was later annexed by Sultan Quli Qutb Shah in the Krishna–Godavari region?
n998e2e0788e.x: Sultan Quli Qutb Shah later annexed Rajahmundry, Eluru and the Krishna–Godavari region.
n998e2e0788e.tq: Identify the later annexation associated with the correct ruler and regional pair.
xs: **Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** annexed **Rajahmundry, Eluru** and the **K-G** region — option **(3)** is correct.
**Bidar** and **Berar** were separate Deccan Sultanates (Barid Shahi, Imad Shahi).
xa: After **Talikota (1565)**, Golconda added **Kondavidu, Machilipatnam** and coastal districts.
Sultan Quli founded the Golconda state in **1518**.

ne8be5ff2d8f.s: In which year was the Battle of Muttukur fought?
ne8be5ff2d8f.x: Muttukur was fought in 1263; Raichur in 1520, Rakshasi-Tangadi on 26 January 1565 and Palnadu in the 12th century.
xa: At Talikota, **Aliya Rama Raya** was killed.
**Kondavidu and Kondapalli** sieges (**1515-16**): Krishnadevaraya vs Gajapatis.

n52753c86ad4.s: Which Vijayanagara leader was killed in the Battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi (Talikota)?
n52753c86ad4.x: Aliya Rama Raya was killed at Rakshasi-Tangadi (also called Talikota or Bannihatti), fought against Golconda, Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Bidar.
xa: "Bannihatti" is **H.K. Sherwani**'s name for it.

n45d3c99b976.s: The Kayasthas of the Kadapa region revolted under Ambadeva with the support of the:
n45d3c99b976.x: Ambadeva led the Kayastha revolt in the Kadapa region in 1272 with Pandya support.
n45d3c99b976.tq: Identify the external supporter in a feudatory revolt.
xs: **Ambadeva** led the Kayastha revolt with the support of the **Pandyas** — option **(4)** is correct.
The Kayasthas were Kakatiya loyalists in the **Kadapa** region (**1272**).
xa: Rayalaseema succession: **Kakatiyas (Kayastha chiefs) → Vijayanagara → Qutb Shahis**.
**Muttukur** (**1263**): Ganapatideva vs the **Pandyas**.

ne455b203ac2.s: The Raichur Doab (Raichur Antarvedi), the main cause of the Bahmani-Vijayanagara wars, lies between which rivers?
ne455b203ac2.x: The Raichur Doab lies between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra; the Krishna-Godavari doab was a separate coastal contest.
xa: **Adil Khan** held the Doab at Krishnadevaraya's accession.
**Battle of Raichur** (**1520**): **Krishnadevaraya** defeated the Adil Shah of Bijapur.

ne42526d718d.s: Kapaya Nayaka ceded Golconda fort to Muhammad I of the Bahmani kingdom after:
o: his capital was shifted to Kondavidu
ne42526d718d.x: Kapaya Nayaka ceded Golconda fort to Bahmani ruler Muhammad I after the death of his son Vinayaka in 1361.
ne42526d718d.tq: Connect the territorial concession with its immediate personal and political cause.
xs: Kapaya Nayaka ceded **Golconda fort** to Bahmani **Muhammad I** after **his son Vinayaka was killed** (**1361**) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Mahmud Gawan's execution** came in **1482** and **Talikota** in **1565**; **Kondavidu** was a Reddi capital.
xa: **Kapaya Nayaka (1336-1368)** ruled from **Orugallu**.
Musunuri Nayakas emerged in the **1330s** under **Prolaya Nayaka**.

n90733c54396.s: The first Muslim attack on Orugallu is associated with which year?
n90733c54396.x: The first Muslim attack on Orugallu is stated to have taken place in 1303.
n90733c54396.tq: Distinguish the first attack date from the later date marking the end of Telugu imperial unity.
xs: The first Muslim attack on **Orugallu** was in **1303** — option **(2)** is correct.
**1263** = Muttukur; **1323** = fall of the Kakatiyas; **1565** = Talikota.
xa: Last Qutb Shahi: **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** (**1687**).
Kakatiya capital moved from **Hanamkonda** to **Orugallu (Warangal)**.

nd48807918e0.s: In which year did Kulottunga I take the Chola throne?
nd48807918e0.x: Kulottunga I took the Chola throne in 1070 and Vengi in 1075, after the death of Vijayaditya VII, the last Eastern Chalukya.
xa: Hence he is the **First Chalukya-Chola king** (APPSC **2011**).
Viceroys used Eastern Chalukya titles **Sarvalokasraya, Sri Vishnuvardhana**, crowned at **Jananathapura (Draksharama)**.
Last of the line: **Parantaka Chola**.

ncbe3205a9e8.s: The Kalingattuparani, describing Kulottunga I's conquest of Kalinga by sea, was written by:
ncbe3205a9e8.x: Jayangondar's Kalingattuparani describes Kulottunga I's maritime conquest of Kalinga; Kulottunga I also sent 72 merchants to China and built Kulottunga Cholapuram.
xa: The Kalinga conquest is recorded in **Kalingattuparani** by **Jayangondar**.
**Kota Bhimaraju I** also led **Kalinga campaigns**.

n193d9256e61.s: Kalingattuparani, associated with Kulottunga I’s conquest of Kalinga, was written by:
n193d9256e61.x: Jayangondar wrote Kalingattuparani, which describes Kulottunga I’s conquest of Kalinga by sea.
n193d9256e61.tq: Use the author–literary work pairing and reject names associated with other events.
xs: **Kalingattuparani** was written by **Jayangondar** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Srinatha** wrote **Palnati Veera Charitra**; **Tikkana** was a Nellore Choda; **Brahmanaidu** was a Palnadu minister.
xa: It records Kulottunga I's conquest of **Kalinga by sea**.
Kulottunga I also sent a **72-merchant mission to China**.

n13620a9a725.s: The Kona Haihayas were associated with which region and capital?
n13620a9a725.x: The Kona Haihayas ruled in Konaseema, with Rakuduru as their capital or seat.
n13620a9a725.tq: Match the dynasty directly with its region and seat.
xs: Kona Haihayas: **Konaseema**, capital **Rakuduru** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Palnadu/Gurajala** = Palnadu Haihayas; **Kammanadu/Dhanyakatakam** = Kota kings; **South Telangana/Vardhamanapuram** = Gona Haihayas.
xa: Kona Haihaya progenitor: **Kirti Varma**.
Kulottunga I raised the Kona Haihayas to **Mandaleswara** rank.

nc2f12f3bed3.s: The Gona Haihayas were associated with:
nc2f12f3bed3.x: The Gona Haihayas were associated with Vardhamanapuram; the Palnadu Haihayas with Gurajala and the Panchadhara Haihayas with the Visakhapatnam-Yelamanchili region.
xa: Palnadu Haihayas claimed descent from **Kartavirya Arjuna**; feudatories of the **Velanati Chodas**.
Palnadu Haihaya founder: **Betaraju I** (**Satrasala** inscription).
**Kona Haihayas**: Konaseema, **Rakuduru**.

nb01a4293606.s: Who founded the Kota line, and where was its seat?
o: Bhimaraju II; Vardhamanapuram in South Telangana
nb01a4293606.x: Betaraju I was the founder of the Kota line, whose seat was Dhanyakatakam in Kammanadu.
nb01a4293606.tq: Pair the founder with the dynasty’s original seat.
xs: **Betaraju I** founded the Kota line, seat **Dhanyakatakam in Kammanadu** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Gurajala** = Palnadu Haihayas; **Vardhamanapuram** = Gona Haihayas; **Chandavolu** = Velanati Chodas.
xa: ⚠ Betaraju I also founded the **Palnadu Haihaya** line — match by seat (Dhanyakatakam vs Gurajala).
**Bhimaraju I (1108-1127)** backed the Chalukya-Cholas.

n7b08d7e11ae.s: In post-Eastern Chalukya Andhra, the vassals of the nadus accepted the overlordship first of Velanadu and later of the:
n7b08d7e11ae.x: Post-Eastern Chalukya Andhra was a web of nadus under vassals, who accepted Velanadu and later Kakatiya overlordship when those powers were strong.
xa: Kulottunga I raised many families to **Mandaleswara** rank.
The Kotas served **Chalukya-Cholas → Velanati Chodas → Kakatiyas**.

n3daa1a1e966.s: The Velanati Choda line ended when its last member was killed by the Kakatiya ruler:
n3daa1a1e966.x: The Velanati line ended when Kakatiya Ganapatideva killed its last member (named in some sources as Prithvisvara).
xa: Some notes name the last member **Mummadi Rajendra Choda**.
Some notes add that Nellore Choda **Tikkana** helped Ganapati kill **Prithvisvara**.

n3905551c450.s: A Kota chief is recorded as having married Ganapamba, the daughter of:
n3905551c450.x: A Kota chief married Ganapamba, daughter of Kakatiya Ganapatideva; some sources name him Bhimaraju II. This marriage reflects the Kotas becoming Kakatiya vassals.
n3905551c450.tq: Use the marriage alliance to identify the connected Kakatiya ruler.
xs: A Kota chief married **Ganapamba, daughter of Kakatiya Ganapatideva** — option **(1)** is correct.
Some notes name this chief **Bhimaraju II**.
xa: Kota overlords: **Chalukya-Cholas → Velanati Chodas → Kakatiyas**.
The **Kota Vamsiyas of Venadu** became Kakatiya vassals.

n12fb75ffecc.s: The Palnadu war was fought in 1182 CE at which place?
n12fb75ffecc.x: The Palnadu war, or Palnati Yuddham, was fought at Karempudi in 1182 CE.
n12fb75ffecc.tq: Separate the battle site from the capitals and other places in the same region.
xs: The Palnadu war was fought in **1182 CE** at **Karempudi** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Gurajala** was the Palnadu Haihaya capital; **Dhanyakatakam** the Kota seat; **Chandavolu** the Velanati capital.
xa: Rival factions: all sons of Palnadu Haihaya **Alugaraju (Anugaraju)**.
Epic: Srinatha's **Palnati Veera Charitra**.

na15d8e8fddd.s: Who joined Kakatiya Rudradeva in supporting Nalagamaraju during the Palnadu conflict?
na15d8e8fddd.x: Kota Bhimaraju II joined Kakatiya Rudradeva to support Nalagamaraju.
na15d8e8fddd.tq: Identify the ally by linking the local chief with the larger ruling power.
xs: **Kota Bhimaraju II** joined Kakatiya **Rudradeva** to back Nalagamaraju — option **(4)** is correct.
**Malideva** and **Brahmanaidu** were the rival faction; **Gonka II** was Nalagama's grandfather (mother **Mailama Devi**'s father).
xa: The war: **1182 CE** at **Karempudi**.
Bhimaraju II absorbed **Kondapadamati**.

n1da7c2a6185.s: The epic account of the Palnadu war is known as:
n1da7c2a6185.x: Srinatha’s Palnati Veera Charitra is the epic account associated with the Palnadu war.
n1da7c2a6185.tq: Apply the author–work association without importing unrelated literary works.
xs: The epic of the Palnadu war is **Palnati Veera Charitra** by **Srinatha** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Kalingattuparani** (Jayangondar) is on Kulottunga I's conquest of Kalinga.
xa: Factions: **Nalagamaraju** vs half-brothers **Malideva** and others (sons of **Veeravijjaladevi**).
Ministers: **Nagamma** (Nalagama) and **Brahmanaidu** (Malideva).

nb827e592dc3.s: The Pithapuram inscription of Velanati Prithvisvara names which lake?
nb827e592dc3.x: The Pithapuram inscription of the Velanati Choda Prithvisvara names Kolleru Lake (APPSC 2017).
xa: Prithvisvara was killed by **Ganapati**, helped by Nellore Choda **Tikkana** (some notes).
Velanati capital: **Chandavolu (Dhanadapuram)**.

n98dc9dd38b2.s: Which community was described as having entered Palnadu as ‘intruders’ and being driven out in the Battle of Karempudi?
n98dc9dd38b2.x: The Velamas were described as intruders into Reddi-dominated Palnadu and were driven out in the Battle of Karempudi.
n98dc9dd38b2.tq: Distinguish the community involved in the battle from the named dynastic factions.
xs: APPSC GS **2018** key: the **Velamas**, "intruders" into Reddi-dominated Palnadu, were driven out in the **Battle of Karempudi** — option **(4)** is correct.
The **Kotas** were a Kammanadu dynasty and the **Matsyas** were northern Andhra chieftains.
xa: Karempudi = site of the **Palnadu war** (**1182 CE**).
Epic: **Palnati Veera Charitra** by **Srinatha**.

n4ee5eb94cd7.s: Draksharama, also known as Jananathapura, is described in the inscriptions as the coronation seat of which of the following?
n4ee5eb94cd7.x: The Draksharama inscription identifies the place as the coronation seat of a Chalukya-Chola viceroy.
n4ee5eb94cd7.tq: Use the place–office association and avoid swapping rulers of neighbouring minor dynasties.
xs: **Draksharama (Jananathapura)** was the coronation seat of a **Chalukya-Chola viceroy** — option **(4)** is correct.
Viceroys took Eastern Chalukya titles **Sarvalokasraya, Sri Vishnuvardhana**.
xa: ⚠ The viceroy is named **Rajaraja Chodaganga** in the PYQ book, but **Vikrama Chola** in the APPSC **2025** key in your bank.
Last of the line: **Parantaka Chola**.

n9288c655ecf.s: Who among the following overthrew the last Rashtrakuta ruler Karka II in 973 CE?
n9288c655ecf.x: Tailapa II overthrew the last Rashtrakuta ruler, Karka II, in 973 CE and founded the Kalyani Chalukya line.
n9288c655ecf.tq: Match the ruler with the specific overthrow and foundation event.
xs: **Tailapa II** overthrew the last Rashtrakuta **Karka II** in **973 CE** — option **(2)** is correct.
He founded the **Kalyani Chalukya** line.
**Satyasraya** and **Someshvara I** were later rulers.
xa: ⚠ The Chalukya-Vikrama era starts in **1076** (Vikramaditya VI), not **973**.
Capital: **Kalyani** (Basavakalyan); UPSC notes credit **Tailapa II** with the shift, others **Someshvara I**.

nf8e27aae2b7.s: Which of the following Kalyani Chalukya rulers came earliest?
nf8e27aae2b7.x: Tailapa II preceded Satyasraya, who was followed by Someshvara I and later Vikramaditya VI.
xa: After them: **Someshvara III** (**1126-1138**), author of **Manasollasa**.
Someshvara I killed Chola **Rajadhiraja I** at **Koppam (1053)**.

n2f4acf74eed.s: The Kalyani Chalukya Someshvara I granted Hanamkonda to which Kakatiya chief?
n2f4acf74eed.x: Someshvara I granted Hanamkonda to Kakatiya Prola I; he also killed Rajadhiraja I at Koppam and took the title Vengi Purveshwara.
xa: Someshvara I reigned **1042-68**.
The **Khazipet inscription** records Hanamkonda granted with **hereditary rights**.

n6b64082c730.s: Which Kalyani Chalukya ruler bore the title Tribhuvanamalla and ruled for 50 years?
n6b64082c730.x: Vikramaditya VI, the greatest Kalyani Chalukya ruler, ruled for 50 years as Tribhuvanamalla and brought the Vengi feudatories under his control.
xa: He was the **greatest** Kalyani ruler; reign **1076-1126** (APPSC **2018**).
His court had **Bilhana** and **Vijnaneshwara**.
He started the **Chalukya-Vikrama era**.

n1dcdeabb9bb.x: Vikramaditya VI ruled from 1076 to 1126 CE.
n1dcdeabb9bb.tq: Test the exact reign period using closely spaced historical dates.
xs: Vikramaditya VI ruled **1076-1126 CE** — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC **2018**).
xa: He ruled **50 years**, title **Tribhuvanamalla**.
The **Chalukya-Vikrama era** begins with his accession in **1076**.

o: started by Someshvara III in 1126 CE to commemorate Manasollasa
founded by Tailapa II in 973 CE after defeating the Rashtrakutas
introduced by Someshvara I after the battle of Koppam in 1053 CE
founded by Vikramaditya VI in 1076 CE and used in place of the Saka era in royal records
n81f6eb6b3f0.x: Vikramaditya VI founded the Chalukya-Vikrama era in 1076 CE, the year of his accession, replacing the Saka era in royal records.
n81f6eb6b3f0.tq: Match the era with its founder, starting year and administrative use.
xs: The **Chalukya-Vikrama era** was founded by **Vikramaditya VI** in **1076 CE**, replacing the **Saka era** in royal records — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ **1076** = his accession, not Tailapa II's (**973**); Koppam (**1053**) was Someshvara I's battle.
xa: Vikramaditya VI ruled **1076-1126** (APPSC **2018**).
**Someshvara III** wrote **Manasollasa**.

nindian-history-147-2.s: The Kalyani Chalukyas flourished approximately during which period?
nindian-history-147-2.x: The Kalyani Chalukyas ruled from about 973 CE, when Tailapa II overthrew the Rashtrakutas, to 1195 CE. 543–753 CE is the Badami Chalukya period.
nindian-history-147-2.tq: Recall the period of each Chalukya line.
n: The Kalyani Chalukyas flourished from approximately 973 to 1195 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #147 · pp 256-257]
xs: The Kalyani Chalukyas flourished **c. 973–1195 CE** — option **(1)**.
**Tailapa II** overthrew the **Rashtrakutas** (last ruler **Karka II**) in **973 CE**.
They are also called the **Western Chalukyas**; ⚠ other notes say the dynasty ended c. **1189 CE**.
xa: Greatest ruler: **Vikramaditya VI** (**1076-1126**), title **Tribhuvanamalla** (APPSC 2018).
The **Chalukya-Vikrama era** began in **1076 CE**, his accession.
Capital: **Kalyani** (Basavakalyan, Karnataka).
**Someshvara I** killed Chola **Rajadhiraja I** at **Koppam (1053)**.

n64e44c30fa5.s: Vijnaneshwara wrote the Mitakshara at the court of:
n64e44c30fa5.x: Vijnaneshwara wrote the Mitakshara, a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti, at the court of Vikramaditya VI.
xa: Asked in APPSC G1 **2018**.
Rival school: **Dayabhaga** of **Jimutavahana** (Bengal).

n91e96cbcbf2.x: Jimutavahana wrote the Dayabhaga; Vijnaneshwara wrote the Mitakshara and Hemadri the Chaturvarga Chintamani.
xa: Medieval jurists (UPSC **1995**): **Vijnaneshwara, Hemadri, Jimutavahana**.
Mitakshara is a commentary on the **Yajnavalkya Smriti**; Dayabhaga belongs to **Bengal and Assam**.

n6e63cfc7271.s: The 100-chapter Sanskrit encyclopaedia Manasollasa is also called:
n6e63cfc7271.x: Manasollasa, also called Abhilashitartha Chintamani, covers statecraft, agriculture, medicine, astronomy, music, dance and cuisine.
xa: Author: **Someshvara III** (**1126-1138**).
⚠ Not to be confused with **Vikramankadevacharita** (**Bilhana**) or **Mitakshara** (**Vijnaneshwara**).

n1f124762065.s: The Kalyani Chalukyas were significant in Indian history because they:
o: abolished hereditary rights in ancestral property
checked Chola expansion northwards and contributed to the development of Hindu legal tradition through Mitakshara
unified all of northern India under one empire
ended the Gupta Empire and introduced Persian administration
n1f124762065.x: The Kalyani Chalukyas checked Chola expansion towards the north, while the Mitakshara tradition associated with their court shaped Hindu inheritance law for about a millennium.
n1f124762065.tq: Select the option combining the dynasty’s political and legal significance without an unrelated claim.
xs: They **checked Chola expansion northwards** and gave Hindu law the **Mitakshara** — option **(2)** is correct.
Mitakshara **shaped Hindu law for a millennium**; it did not abolish hereditary rights.
xa: Mitakshara is by **Vijnaneshwara** at **Vikramaditya VI**'s court.
**Someshvara I** killed Chola **Rajadhiraja I** at **Koppam (1053)**.

nindian-history-37-14.s: The Mitakshara is based on which Smriti?
nindian-history-37-14.x: The Yajnavalkya Smriti is the basis of the Mitakshara; the Manusmriti is ascribed to Manu.
n: Manusmriti was authored by Manu. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 103-104]
Yajnavalkya Smriti is the basis for Mitakshara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 103-104]
Dayabhaga is associated with Jimutavahana. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 103-104]
xa: **Mitakshara** — by **Vijnaneshwara** at the court of **Vikramaditya VI** (APPSC G1 2018).
Mitakshara is the basis of Hindu inheritance law — the **Hindu Succession Act** still rests largely on it.
⚠ UPSC 2021: "Mitakshara for upper castes, Dayabhaga for lower castes" is **wrong**.
**Parashar Madhav** — **Madhvacharya**.

nindian-history-37-15.s: The legal digest Smriti Chandrika was written by:
nindian-history-37-15.x: Devana Bhatta wrote Smriti Chandrika; Hemadri compiled Chaturvarga Chintamani and Ballal Sena wrote Daan Sagar.
n: Smriti Chandrika is associated with Devana Bhatta. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 103-104]
Chaturvarga Chintamani is associated with Hemadri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 103-104]
Daan Sagar is associated with Ballal Sena. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 103-104]
xa: Hemadri was a **Yadava minister** who contributed to **jurisprudence**.
**Dayabhaga** — **Jimutavahana**; **Mitakshara** — **Vijnanesvara**.
**Parashar Madhav** — **Madhvacharya**.
**Manusmriti** — **Manu**.

nindian-history-37-17.s: Parashar Madhav, a commentary on the Parashara Smriti, was written by:
nindian-history-37-17.x: Parashar Madhav is Madhavacharya's commentary on the Parashara Smriti; Mitakshara is Vijnanesvara's and Chaturvarga Chintamani is Hemadri's.
n: Manusmriti deals with dharma and social/legal rules. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 103-104]
Mitakshara is a commentary on inheritance. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 103-104]
Chaturvarga Chintamani deals with dharma/legal literature. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 103-104]
Parashar Madhav deals with dharma/legal literature. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 103-104]
xa: Under Mitakshara, sons have a right in ancestral property **during the father's lifetime** (UPSC 2021).
**Dayabhaga** — **Jimutavahana**, on **inheritance**.
**Smriti Chandrika** — **Devana Bhatta**, on **Hindu law**.
**Daan Sagar** — **Ballal Sena**.

nindian-history-147-17.s: Which languages flourished under the royal patronage of the Kalyani Chalukyas?
nindian-history-147-17.x: Sanskrit and Kannada flourished under Kalyani Chalukya patronage: Bilhana and Vijnaneshwara wrote in Sanskrit, and Nagavarma II wrote in Kannada.
nindian-history-147-17.tq: Recall the languages of the court writers.
n: Royal patronage under the Kalyani Chalukyas enabled Sanskrit to flourish. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #147 · pp 256-257]
Royal patronage under the Kalyani Chalukyas enabled Kannada to flourish. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #147 · pp 256-257]
xs: **Sanskrit and Kannada** flourished under Kalyani Chalukya **royal patronage** — option **(1)**.
Sanskrit: **Bilhana**'s **Vikramankadeva Charita**, **Vijnaneshwara**'s **Mitakshara**, **Someshvara III**'s **Manasollasa**.
Kannada: **Nagavarma II**'s **Kavyavalokana** and **Karnataka Bhashabhushana**.
xa: **Manasollasa** (= **Abhilashitartha Chintamani**) is a **100-chapter** Sanskrit encyclopaedia.
Bilhana was a **Kashmiri** poet at **Vikramaditya VI**'s court.
Vachana literature: **Basavanna, Allama, Akka** (Virashaiva movement).
Manasollasa is the earliest major record of **South Indian recipes**.

n4d064794254.s: Under the Dayabhaga system, sons acquire a right in ancestral property:
n4d064794254.x: Dayabhaga recognises the sons' right in ancestral property only after the father's death, whereas Mitakshara gives it by birth.
xa: UPSC **2021** correct statement: sons can claim ancestral property **during the father's lifetime (Mitakshara)**.
The **Hindu Succession Act** still rests largely on Mitakshara.

nb75669c2c27.s: Kalyani Chalukya temples in the mature Vesara (Gadag) style were built mainly of:
nb75669c2c27.x: The Kalyani Chalukyas built mainly in chloritic schist (soapstone), not granite; their stellate plans later became a model for the Hoysalas.
xa: **Mahadeva** temple at **Itagi** = "Emperor among temples".
**Kasivishveshvara** is at **Lakkundi**.

na3ea3dadba7.s: The Itagi Mahadeva temple is popularly described as the:
na3ea3dadba7.x: The Itagi Mahadeva temple is popularly known as the “Emperor among temples.”
na3ea3dadba7.tq: Recall the distinctive epithet attached to the monument.
xs: The **Itagi Mahadeva** temple is the "**Emperor among temples**" — option **(3)** is correct.
It is in mature **Vesara (Gadag style)**.
xa: Others: **Kasivishveshvara** (Lakkundi), **Doddabasappa** (Dambal), **Kedareshwara** (Balligavi).
Material: **chloritic schist (soapstone)**.

n7efd941f251.s: The Mahadeva temple of the Kalyani Chalukya period is located at:
n7efd941f251.x: The Mahadeva temple is at Itagi; Kasivishveshvara is at Lakkundi, Doddabasappa at Dambal and Kedareshwara at Balligavi.
xa: Itagi Mahadeva = "**Emperor among temples**".
**Stellate plans** were later used by the **Hoysalas**.

n5225e95e6dd.s: After the weakening of the Kalyani Chalukyas, the Yadavas (Seunas) ruled from:
n5225e95e6dd.x: The Yadavas or Seunas ruled from Devagiri; the Hoysalas from Dwarasamudra, the Kakatiyas from Hanamkonda-Warangal and the Kalachuris from Kalyani.
xa: **Beta I and Prola I** of the Kakatiyas were **Kalyani feudatories**.
**Bijjala** seized the Kalyani throne c. **1156**.
The dynasty ended c. **1189 CE**.

n7dc0850b48c.s: Who seized the throne at Kalyani around 1156 CE?
n7dc0850b48c.x: Kalachuri ruler Bijjala seized the throne at Kalyani around 1156 CE.
n7dc0850b48c.tq: Match the seizure of the central throne with the correct successor power.
xs: **Bijjala of the Kalachuris** seized Kalyani c. **1156** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Prola I** was a Kakatiya feudatory; **Hemadri** was a Yadava minister.
xa: The Kalyani Chalukya dynasty ended c. **1189 CE**.
Successors: **Hoysalas, Yadavas (Seunas), Kakatiyas, Kalachuris**.

nb3942ab2297.s: The Kalyani Chalukya dynasty came to an end around:
nb3942ab2297.x: The Kalyani Chalukyas ended around 1189 CE, and the Kakatiyas, Hoysalas and Yadavas emerged as successor powers.
xa: **Bijjala** seized the throne c. **1156**.
Kakatiyas rose as Kalyani feudatories (**Khazipet inscription**).

n734f90c550d.s: The capital of the Kalyani Chalukyas was:
n734f90c550d.x: Kalyani, now known as Basavakalyan in Karnataka, was the capital of the Kalyani Chalukyas.
n734f90c550d.tq: Distinguish the capital of one Chalukya branch from those of other branches and successor powers.
xs: The capital was **Kalyani, present-day Basavakalyan** (Karnataka) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Vatapi** was the **Badami** Chalukya seat; **Dwarasamudra** was Hoysala; **Vengi** was the Eastern Chalukya branch.
xa: Made capital under **Someshvara I**; UPSC notes credit **Tailapa II**.
⚠ The UPSC table garbles names ("Someshvara I (Vikramaditya VI)") — ignore it.

n10b4a7ed9b4.s: According to the Khazipet inscription, the Kakatiyas’ early rise was connected with:
o: the conquest of Devagiri from the Yadavas
the founding of Dwarasamudra by the Hoysalas
the seizure of Kalyani by Bijjala
a grant of Hanamkonda with hereditary rights
n10b4a7ed9b4.x: The Khazipet inscription records Hanamkonda being granted with hereditary rights, reflecting the Kakatiyas’ rise as feudatories.
n10b4a7ed9b4.tq: Use an inscriptional clue to identify the political basis of a dynasty’s rise.
xs: The **Khazipet inscription** records a **grant of Hanamkonda with hereditary rights** — option **(4)** is correct.
The Kakatiyas rose as **Kalyani feudatories**.
xa: **Someshvara I** granted Hanamkonda to Kakatiya **Prola I**.
**Beta I and Prola I** were Kalyani feudatories.

ne8afaa221f4.s: Who among the following was killed at Koppam while mounted on an elephant?
ne8afaa221f4.x: Rajadhiraja I was killed at Koppam on the back of an elephant and was known by the title Yanai-mel-thunjina Devar.
ne8afaa221f4.tq: Link the unusual death description with the correct ruler.
xs: **Rajadhiraja I** was killed at **Koppam (1053)** on an elephant's back — option **(1)** is correct.
Hence his title **Yanai-mel-thunjina Devar**.
**Rajendra II** was crowned on the battlefield and claimed victory.
xa: His opponent: Western Chalukya **Ahavamalla Someshwara I**, who then took the title **Vengi Purveshwara**.
Rajadhiraja I ruled from **1044**; other title **Vijaya Rajendra**.

n7afba60559d.s: The Chola king Rajaraja I (985-1014 CE) was also known as:
n7afba60559d.x: Rajaraja I, also known as Arumolivarman, ruled 985-1014 CE and made the Chola state the largest in South India.
xa: Titles: **Ulakalanda Perumal** (land survey) and **Mummudi Chola** (northern Sri Lanka = **Mummadichola Mandalam**).
Built **Brihadeshvara (Rajarajeshwara)** temple, **1010**.

n00802edf164.x: 'Coromandel' comes from Cholamandalam, not Tondaimandalam (the former Pallava country); the Chola core was the Kaveri delta.
xa: **Tondaimandalam** was annexed by **Aditya I** from the Pallavas.
Early capital **Uraiyur**; imperial capital **Thanjavur**.

n546e9310869.s: The Chola princess Madhurantaki was married to
n546e9310869.x: Madhurantaki married Rajendra Chalukya, who became Kulottunga I. Kundavai married Vimaladitya, Ammanga Devi married Rajaraja Narendra, and Saktivarman I was Vimaladitya's elder brother who ruled Vengi with Rajaraja I's help.
n546e9310869.tq: Her father is given as Virarajendra or Rajendra I — the APPSC 2025 key rejected 'daughter of Rajendra II'.
xs: **Madhurantaki** married **Rajendra Chalukya (Kulottunga I)** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Vimaladitya** married **Kundavai**; **Rajaraja Narendra** married **Ammanga Devi**.
xa: Her father: some notes **Virarajendra**, another **Rajendra I**.
⚠ "Daughter of **Rajendra Chola II**" was marked **incorrect** in the **APPSC 2025** key.

n160d6ba26e0.s: The last ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line in Vengi was
n160d6ba26e0.x: Parantaka Chola was the last ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line in Vengi. Vijayaditya VII was the last Eastern Chalukya before the merger under Kulottunga I.
n160d6ba26e0.tq: Distinguish the last ruler of the line from the last ruler of the earlier Eastern Chalukya branch.
xs: The last ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line in Vengi was **Parantaka Chola** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Rajaraja Chola Ganga** was a Vengi viceroy (Tekkali inscription); **Rajendra Chalukya** became **Kulottunga I**, the first of the line.
**Vijayaditya VII** died in **1075**, after which Kulottunga I merged Vengi.
xa: Viceroys (sons of Kulottunga I): **Rajaraja III (Mummadi Chola)** and **Vira Chola**, at **Jagannathapuram**.
Vira Chola was viceroy **twice** and **crowned at Jagannathapuram**.

n0502690668f.s: Which of the following factors contributed to the decline of the Chalukya-Cholas after Kulottunga I?
o: Complete withdrawal of the Cholas from Vengi before Kulottunga I
Strengthening of the central bureaucracy and disappearance of local chiefs
Abolition of local authority by the Pandyas
Weakening of the central bureaucracy and growth of local chieftains
n0502690668f.x: After Kulottunga I, the central bureaucracy weakened and local chieftains grew in power. The Chalukya-Cholas subsequently declined with the rise of the Pandyas.
n0502690668f.tq: Identify the cause–effect chain and reject the option that reverses the administrative trend.
xs: After Kulottunga I, the **central bureaucracy weakened** and **local chieftains grew** — option **(4)** is correct.
The opposite (stronger centre, chiefs gone) is wrong.
xa: The Chalukya-Cholas declined with the **rise of the Pandyas**.
Last ruler **Rajendra III** was gone by **1279**.
Kulottunga I ruled **1070-1120**.

n8334240eb0b.s: Which ruler united the Tamil (Chola) and Andhra (Vengi) kingdoms?
n8334240eb0b.x: Kulottunga I united the Tamil and Andhra kingdoms; Vengi had been a prize in the Chola-Chalukya wars, and the Mandalika Yugam followed (1076 to c. 1210).
xa: The **Kundavai** and **Ammanga Devi** marriages made Kulottunga I heir to both thrones.
After **Koppam**, Someshwara took the title **Vengi Purveshwara**.

nindian-history-148-1.s: Who founded the Imperial Chola dynasty by capturing Tanjavur?
nindian-history-148-1.x: Vijayalaya founded the Imperial Chola line in the mid-9th century by taking Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars. Aditya I, Parantaka I and Rajaraja I were later rulers.
nindian-history-148-1.tq: Recall the founder of the dynasty.
n: Vijayalaya Chola founded the Imperial Chola dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Vijayalaya Chola captured Tanjavur. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
xs: **Vijayalaya Chola** founded the Imperial Chola dynasty by **capturing Tanjavur** — option **(2)**.
He took **Thanjavur in 850 CE** from the **Muttarayars**.
**Aditya I** succeeded him; **Parantaka I** and **Rajaraja I** came later.
xa: ⚠ The empire was **not** founded by **Parantaka I** or **Rajendra I**.
Aditya I defeated the Pallava **Aparajita**.
Imperial Cholas: c. **850-1279 CE**, rising from the **Kaveri delta**.
Last ruler **Rajendra III** was gone by **1279**.

nindian-history-148-3.s: Which Sri Lankan king was defeated and captured by Rajendra I when he completed the Chola conquest of Ceylon?
nindian-history-148-3.x: Rajendra I completed the conquest of Ceylon by taking its southern part and capturing Mahinda V, building on Rajaraja I's conquest of the north.
n: Rajendra I completed the Chola conquest of Ceylon. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Rajendra I captured the southern part of Sri Lanka. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Rajendra I defeated Mahinda V. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
xa: He seized the royal insignia; the Cholas held the island for about **five decades**.
Sri Lanka's **Vijayabahu I** expelled the Cholas around **1070**.
Rajendra I's titles: **Gangaikondachola, Kadaramkondan**, Pandita Chola.
Northern Sri Lanka was named **Mummadichola Mandalam**.

nindian-history-148-11.s: The Chola king Kulottunga I (1070-1122 CE) is noted for abolishing:
nindian-history-148-11.x: Kulottunga I abolished tolls and married his daughter to a Sinhala prince; the Brihadeeswara temple was built by Rajaraja I.
n: Kulottunga I ruled from 1070 to 1122 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Kulottunga I abolished tolls. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Kulottunga I gave complete freedom to Sri Lanka. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Kulottunga I married his daughter to a Sinhala prince. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
xa: ⚠ Other notes give his reign as **1070-1120**.
He was born **Rajendra Chalukya**, son of **Rajaraja Narendra** and **Ammanga Devi**.
He sent **72 merchants to China** (UPPSC 1992).
Title **Sungam Tavirtta Chola** (abolisher of tolls); built **Kulottunga Cholapuram**.

na60a369bf76.s: The Uttaramerur inscriptions are associated with which Chola ruler?
na60a369bf76.x: The Uttaramerur inscriptions are associated with Parantaka I. He was defeated at Takkolam in 949 CE.
na60a369bf76.tq: Use a ruler–inscription association rather than a broad dynastic clue.
xs: The **Uttaramerur inscriptions** belong to **Parantaka I** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Vijayalaya** was the founder; **Rajaraja I** built Brihadeshvara; **Kulottunga I** began the Chalukya-Chola line.
xa: Parantaka I took **Madurai** → title **Madurai-konda**.
His forces were beaten at **Takkolam (949)** by Rashtrakuta **Krishna III**.

nea08a530092.s: Which Chola king defeated the Sailendra ruler at Kadaram in the 1025 CE expedition?
nea08a530092.x: Rajendra I defeated the Sailendra ruler at Kadaram in 1025 CE; Rajaraja I built the Brihadeshvara temple, conducted a land survey and captured the Maldives.
