xa: Rajaraja I also destroyed **Anuradhapura** and attacked the Chera fleet at **Kandalur Salai**.
Rajaraja I had earlier sent a naval expedition against the **Sailendras**.
Kadaram = **Kedah**; the **1025** expedition is called **India's first overseas expedition**.

n3119a3b321d.s: Who expelled the Cholas from Sri Lanka around 1070?
n3119a3b321d.x: Vijayabahu I expelled the Cholas from Sri Lanka around 1070.
n3119a3b321d.tq: Use the ruler–event association rather than confusing the Sri Lankan ruler with a Chola ruler.
xs: **Vijayabahu I** expelled the Cholas from Sri Lanka around **1070** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Mahinda V** was the king defeated by **Rajendra I**.
xa: Rajaraja I destroyed **Anuradhapura**.
The Cholas held the whole island for about **five decades**.

na0837de9d49.s: Rajendra I’s northern expedition of 1022 CE is particularly associated with which achievement?
o: Defeat of Vijayaditya VII at Kalidindi
Crossing the Ganga and defeating the Pala ruler Mahipala I
Conquest of Madurai and Sri Lanka
Defeat of the Rashtrakuta king Krishna III
na0837de9d49.x: In 1022 CE, Rajendra I led a northern campaign, crossed the Ganga and defeated the Pala ruler Mahipala I.
na0837de9d49.tq: Use the distinctive ruler-and-event association to identify the correct option.
xs: The **1022 CE** northern campaign crossed the **Ganga** and defeated **Pala Mahipala I** — option **(2)** is correct.
It followed **Samudragupta's route** and earned the title **Gangaikondachola**.
**Kalidindi** was against **Vijayaditya VII**; **Krishna III** won Takkolam (**949**) against Parantaka I.
xa: Rajendra I then built **Gangaikondacholapuram** and the **Chola Gangam tank**.
⚠ "Victor of the Ganges" = **Rajendra I**, not Aditya I.

na256b294e3c.s: 'Ulakalanda Perumal', a title reflecting a land survey and revenue reorganisation, belonged to:
na256b294e3c.x: Ulakalanda Perumal and Mummudi Chola were titles of Rajaraja I; Madurai-konda was Parantaka I's and Gangaikonda Chola Rajendra I's.
xa: Rajendra I's other titles: **Kadaram Kondan** (Kedah) and **Pandita Chola** (patron of learning).
⚠ Gangaikonda + Kadaram Kondan + Pandita = **Rajendra I**; Mummudi + Ulakalanda = **Rajaraja I**.

n35bc5cec72d.s: The naval expedition of Rajendra I in 1025 CE was directed against
n35bc5cec72d.x: Rajendra I's 1025 CE naval expedition was against the revived Srivijaya empire: he defeated the Sailendra king and took Kadaram (Kedah) in Malaya and parts of Sumatra. Anuradhapura was destroyed by Rajaraja I, and Kalinga was conquered by Kulottunga I.
n35bc5cec72d.tq: Anchor the expedition to its year and destination before considering the distractors.
xs: Rajendra I's **1025 CE** naval expedition was against **Srivijaya** — option **(2)** is correct.
He defeated the **Sailendra** king and took **Kadaram (Kedah)** (APPSC **2000**, **2003**).
**Anuradhapura** was destroyed by **Rajaraja I**; **Kalinga** was **Kulottunga I**'s.
xa: Srivijaya covered **Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Java**.
Exam angle: "Who led the campaign against Srivijaya?" — **Rajendra I** (UPSC **2025**).

n26ddfb74dd2.s: Which historian said the Cholas turned the Bay of Bengal into a 'Chola Lake'?
n26ddfb74dd2.x: K.A. Nilakanta Sastri described the Bay of Bengal as a 'Chola Lake'; the 1025 CE Srivijaya expedition was led by Rajendra I.
xa: It is called "**India's first overseas expedition**".
Cholas = first Indian power with **overseas naval campaigns**.

n2693be04b9d.s: The Chola hold over Sri Lanka developed in which of the following ways?
o: Kulottunga I first conquered the north, and Rajendra III retained the whole island
Vijayabahu I established Chola rule over the whole island for about five decades
Rajaraja I controlled the whole island, while Rajendra I restricted Chola control to the north
Rajaraja I controlled the north, while Rajendra I extended control to the whole island for about five decades
n2693be04b9d.x: Rajaraja I established Chola control in northern Sri Lanka, and Rajendra I extended it to the whole island, which remained under Chola control for about five decades.
n2693be04b9d.tq: Split the comparison into ruler, territorial extent and duration instead of relying on a single familiar name.
xs: **Rajaraja I** took the **north** of Sri Lanka; **Rajendra I** the **whole island**, for about **five decades** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Vijayabahu I** expelled the Cholas around **1070**; he did not establish Chola rule.
xa: Rajendra I defeated **Mahinda V** and seized the royal insignia.
Northern Sri Lanka was named **Mummadichola Mandalam**.

ncbb481b8378.s: Which Chola ruler placed Saktivarman and Vimaladitya as Eastern Chalukya princes in Vengi?
ncbb481b8378.x: Rajaraja I arranged Vengi by placing Saktivarman and Vimaladitya there; he also captured Quilon, annexed Madurai and conquered the Maldives.
xa: Rajaraja I also hit the Chera fleet at **Kandalur Salai** and destroyed **Anuradhapura**.
⚠ **Whole Sri Lanka** and complete subjugation of Pandyas and Cheras = **Rajendra I**.

nc0f68498254.s: Which Chola ruler conquered the whole of Sri Lanka, defeating Mahinda V and seizing his royal insignia?
nc0f68498254.x: Rajendra I completed the conquest of Sri Lanka by defeating Mahinda V and seizing the royal insignia; the island stayed under the Cholas for about five decades. Rajaraja I had taken only the north, Rajadhiraja I fell at Koppam, and in Kulottunga I's time Vijayabahu I expelled the Cholas (c. 1070).
nc0f68498254.tq: North of Lanka = Rajaraja I; whole Lanka + Mahinda V = Rajendra I.
xs: **Rajendra I** conquered the whole of Sri Lanka, defeating **Mahinda V** and seizing the royal insignia — option **(2)** is correct.
**Rajaraja I** had taken only the **north**; **Rajadhiraja I** was killed at **Koppam**.
In **Kulottunga I**'s time, **Vijayabahu I** expelled the Cholas (around **1070**).
xa: Chola hold on the island lasted about **five decades**.
Northern Sri Lanka was named **Mummadichola Mandalam**.

n9d78d045f1b.s: Chola overseas naval activity helped spread which art tradition to Southeast Asia?
n9d78d045f1b.x: The Cholas, described as the first Indian power with overseas naval campaigns, helped spread Dravidian art to Southeast Asia.
xa: **K.A. Nilakanta Sastri**: the Bay of Bengal became a "**Chola Lake**".
The **1025** Srivijaya expedition = "India's first overseas expedition".

nindian-history-148-7.x: Gangaikondacholapuram was built by Rajendra I; his father Rajaraja I took northern Sri Lanka, conquered the Maldives and built a navy.
n: Rajaraja I captured northern Sri Lanka. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Rajaraja I conquered the Maldives. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Rajendra I built Gangaikonda Cholapuram around 1035 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Rajaraja I is credited in the source as the first Chola king to create a naval army. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
xa: Rajaraja I built the **Brihadisvara Temple** at **Thanjavur** (**1010**).
He **destroyed Anuradhapura**.
His titles: **Ulakalanada Perumal**, **Mummudi Chola**.
He destroyed the **Chera navy** at **Trivandrum** and captured **Quilon**.

n8c17519be74.s: Which of the following was the earliest capital associated with the Sangam Cholas?
n8c17519be74.x: Uraiyur was the early Sangam Chola capital. Thanjavur became important under the Imperial Cholas, while Gangaikondacholapuram was established by Rajendra I.
n8c17519be74.tq: Use the chronological distinction between early and Imperial Chola capitals.
xs: **Uraiyur** was the early **Sangam Chola** capital — option **(3)** is correct.
**Thanjavur** = imperial capital from Vijayalaya; **Gangaikondacholapuram** = Rajendra I; **Kulottunga Cholapuram** = Kulottunga I (Visakhapatnam).
xa: The Chola core was the **Kaveri delta**.
**Poompuhar** (early Chola capital): third phase of underwater exploration began **8 Sep 2026**.

n2058b957ce3.s: At the battle of Koppam in 1053 CE, which event occurred?
o: Virarajendra defeated Someshvara I and installed Vijayaditya VII.
Rajendra I defeated Vijayaditya VII at Kalidindi.
Rajadhiraja I killed Someshvara I and captured Kalyani.
Someshvara I killed Rajadhiraja I, while Rajendra II was crowned on the battlefield and claimed victory.
n2058b957ce3.x: At Koppam, Someshvara I killed the Chola ruler Rajadhiraja I. Rajendra II was then crowned on the field and claimed victory.
n2058b957ce3.tq: Use the battlefield succession event to distinguish Koppam from the other battles.
xs: At **Koppam (1053)**, **Someshvara I** killed **Rajadhiraja I**; **Rajendra II** was crowned on the field and claimed victory — option **(4)** is correct.
**Kalidindi** was a separate battle of **Rajendra I**'s army; **Virarajendra**'s win was at **Kudalasangamam**.
xa: Rajadhiraja I's title: **Yanai-mel-thunjina Devar**.
Rajendra II's victory pillar: **Kolhapur**.

n87f0cad7a6d.s: The Battle of Kudalasangamam was won by the Cholas under:
n87f0cad7a6d.x: Virarajendra won at Kudalasangamam; Krishna III's Rashtrakutas won Takkolam and Rajendra I's army won at Kalidindi.
xa: **Dharanikota**: **Rajadhiraja I** won, then burnt **Kollipaka**.
At Kalidindi, **Rajaraja Narendra** built **three Shiva temples** for fallen Chola commanders.

na4d66ca41ae.s: After his victory at Dharanikota over Vijayaditya VII and the Kalyani army, which Chola ruler burnt Kollipaka?
na4d66ca41ae.x: Rajadhiraja I won at Dharanikota and then burnt Kollipaka. Rajendra I's army won at Kalidindi, Virarajendra won at Kudalasangamam, and Kulottunga I later merged Vengi in 1075.
na4d66ca41ae.tq: Dharanikota + Kollipaka = Rajadhiraja I (later killed at Koppam).
xs: **Rajadhiraja I** won at **Dharanikota** and then burnt **Kollipaka** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Rajendra I**'s army won **Kalidindi**; **Virarajendra** won **Kudalasangamam**; **Kulottunga I** merged Vengi in **1075**.
xa: Rajadhiraja I was later killed at **Koppam (1053)**.
Opponents at Dharanikota: **Vijayaditya VII** and the Kalyani army.

n8db93a351fc.s: After the death of Vijayaditya VII in 1075, Kulottunga I
o: merged Vengi with his Chola dominions
abandoned the Chola kingdom and returned to China
transferred the Chola capital to Uraiyur
n8db93a351fc.x: After Vijayaditya VII’s death in 1075, Kulottunga I merged Vengi with his Chola dominions and ruled both regions, giving rise to the Chalukya-Chola association.
n8db93a351fc.tq: Follow the succession event to determine its political consequence.
xs: After **Vijayaditya VII**'s death (**1075**), Kulottunga I **merged Vengi** with his Chola dominions — option **(2)** is correct.
Ruling both = **"Chalukya-Chola"**.
xa: First king of the Chalukya-Chola line (APPSC G2 **2011**).
**Mandalika Yugam** (**1076** to about **1210**) followed.

n18202bfefd9.s: The principal cause of the Chola–Chalukya wars was:
o: control of Vengi and the struggle for supremacy in the Deccan
competition over the port of Kolhapur alone
a religious conflict between Shaivism and Buddhism
a dispute over the succession to the Rashtrakuta throne alone
n18202bfefd9.x: The wars arose mainly from succession disputes in Vengi, with each side backing a claimant, and from the wider struggle for supremacy in the Deccan.
n18202bfefd9.tq: Separate the immediate succession issue from the broader political objective.
xs: Cause: **control of Vengi** and **supremacy in the Deccan** — option **(1)** is correct.
Vengi saw **succession disputes**, each side backing a claimant.
xa: **Kolhapur** was where **Rajendra II** set up a victory pillar.
After Koppam, Someshwara took the title **Vengi Purveshwara**.
Coastal Andhra was the prize; **Kulottunga I** united Tamil and Andhra kingdoms (**1075**).

ne0fd4f0db09.s: Who married Vimaladitya, according to the Chola–Eastern Chalukya matrimonial alliances?
o: Ammanga Devi, daughter of Rajendra I
ne0fd4f0db09.x: Kundavai, the daughter of Rajaraja I, married Vimaladitya. Ammanga Devi married Rajaraja Narendra.
ne0fd4f0db09.tq: Discriminate between similarly named Chola princesses and their spouses.
xs: **Kundavai, daughter of Rajaraja I**, married **Vimaladitya** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC G2 **2025**).
⚠ Not **Saktivarman**; **Ammanga Devi** (daughter of **Rajendra I**) married **Rajaraja Narendra**.
xa: **Madhurantaki** married **Rajendra Chalukya = Kulottunga I**.
**Saktivarman I** was Vimaladitya's elder brother.

ne923b53a751.s: Ammanga Devi, daughter of Rajendra I, married
ne923b53a751.x: Ammanga Devi married Rajaraja Narendra in 1022. Their son was Rajendra Chalukya, who later became Kulottunga I.
ne923b53a751.tq: Test the matrimonial alliance through the bride–groom pair.
xs: **Ammanga Devi** married **Rajaraja Narendra** (**16 Aug 1022**) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Rajendra Chalukya** was their son; **Vimaladitya** married **Kundavai**.
xa: Their son became **Kulottunga I**.
The **Kundavai** and **Ammanga Devi** marriages made Kulottunga I heir to both thrones.

na65f693b55b.s: Saktivarman I ruled Vengi with the assistance of Rajaraja I after the ouster of
na65f693b55b.x: Saktivarman I, the elder brother of Vimaladitya, ruled Vengi with Rajaraja I’s help after Jatachoda Bhima was ousted.
na65f693b55b.tq: Use the political sequence of ouster, assistance and rule to identify the correct figure.
xs: **Saktivarman I** ruled Vengi with Rajaraja I's help after **Jatachoda Bhima** was ousted — option **(1)** is correct.
**Someshvara II** was defeated by Virarajendra; **Mahinda V** by Rajendra I; **Pallava Aparajita** by Aditya I.
xa: Saktivarman I was **Vimaladitya's elder brother**.
**Rajaraja I** placed **Saktivarman and Vimaladitya** in Vengi.

n61dc487657c.s: Rajendra Chalukya (Kulottunga I) was the son of Rajaraja Narendra and:
n61dc487657c.x: Kulottunga I, also called Rajendra Chalukya, was the son of Rajaraja Narendra and Ammanga Devi and took the Chola throne in 1070 CE.
xa: He merged **Vengi** in **1075**.
Ammanga Devi was the daughter of **Rajendra I**.

nb4c88cf6d15.s: The principal cause given for the Chola expedition against Srivijaya was that Srivijaya
o: blocked Indian traders on the China route
nb4c88cf6d15.x: Chola-Sailendra ties, once cordial, soured when Srivijaya blocked Indian traders on the China route; Rajendra I's 1025 CE expedition cleared these obstacles and widened Chola trade with China.
nb4c88cf6d15.tq: Apply the cause–effect relationship instead of selecting a familiar military opponent.
xs: Srivijaya **blocked Indian traders on the China route** — option **(4)** is correct.
Chola-**Sailendra** ties, once cordial, soured; the Cholas cleared obstacles and widened trade with **China**.
xa: The expedition (**1025 CE**) was led by **Rajendra I**.
**Rajaraja I** had earlier sent a naval expedition against the Sailendras.

n120a850f9d9.s: The Chola Gangam tank was dug at Gangaikondacholapuram by
n120a850f9d9.x: Rajendra I dug the Chola Gangam tank at his new capital Gangaikondacholapuram after the Ganga expedition. Rajaraja I built the Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur, Kulottunga I is linked with Kulottunga Cholapuram, and Parantaka I with the Uttaramerur inscriptions.
n120a850f9d9.tq: Ganga water -> Chola Gangam -> Gangaikondacholapuram -> Rajendra I.
xs: **Rajendra I** dug the **Chola Gangam tank** at Gangaikondacholapuram — option **(2)** is correct.
**Rajaraja I** = Brihadeeswara at Thanjavur; **Kulottunga I** = Kulottunga Cholapuram; **Parantaka I** = Uttaramerur.
xa: UPSC notes misprint the tank as "**Chodagarg**".
Gangaikondacholapuram followed the **1022** Ganga expedition.

nb52d82f7332.s: How many merchants did Kulottunga I send in his embassy to China?
nb52d82f7332.x: Kulottunga I sent 72 merchants to China as part of the diplomatic and commercial contact recorded for his reign.
nb52d82f7332.tq: Treat the merchant count as a direct numerical recall point and compare the close alternatives.
xs: Kulottunga I sent **72 merchants to China** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is recorded as a **72-member merchant mission** (UPPSC **1992**).
xa: He conquered **Kalinga** (Jayamkondar's **Kalingattuparani**).
He built **Kulottunga Cholapuram** (Visakhapatnam).

nindian-history-82-7.s: Which ruler is associated with the construction of Kallanai, also called the Grand Anicut?
nindian-history-82-7.x: Karikala Chola of the Sangam age built the Kallanai, or Grand Anicut, across the Kaveri for irrigation. Rajaraja I, Rajendra I and Kulottunga I were later imperial Cholas.
nindian-history-82-7.tq: Discriminate the Sangam Cholas from the imperial Cholas.
n: Karikala Chola built Kallanai, also known as the Grand Anicut. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Karikala Chola contributed to irrigation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
xs: **Karikala Chola** built the **Kallanai**, the **Grand Anicut** — option **(3)**.
Karikala belonged to the **Sangam period**; the Kallanai served **irrigation**.
**Rajaraja Chola I**, **Rajendra Chola I** and **Kulottunga I** were later Imperial Cholas.
xa: **Mahendravarman I** (**7th century CE**) — early **rock-cut architecture**.
**Narasimhavarman I** — monuments of **Mamallapuram**.
**Krishnadeva Raya** (**1509–1529 CE**) — zenith of **Vijayanagara**.
**Rajendra Chola I** — **Ganga expedition** and **Chola Gangam**.

n603385cc41b.s: In the Chola period, the nattar was the assembly of:
o: merchants of the nadu's market town
Brahmin landholders of a single village
leading vellala landholders of the nadu
n603385cc41b.x: The nattar was the nadu assembly of leading vellala landholders, handling revenue and disputes above village level; the merchant body was the nagaram.
xa: ⚠ **Ur** = non-brahmadeya; **Sabha** = brahmadeya; **Nagaram** = merchants.
The **ur** dealt with land sale, gift and **tax exemptions**.

nb30e5fbebb5.s: The ‘ur’ in Chola local administration was the general assembly of residents in:
nb30e5fbebb5.x: Ur was the general assembly in ordinary non-brahmadeya, or vellanvagai, villages.
nb30e5fbebb5.tq: Distinguish village assemblies by settlement type and social composition.
xs: The **ur** was the general assembly of **non-brahmadeya (vellanvagai)** villages — option **(4)** is correct.
**Brahmadeya** villages had the **sabha**; merchant centres had the **nagaram**.
xa: The ur dealt with **land sale, gift, tax exemptions**.
It generally had **fewer than ten** members.
⚠ **Ur** = non-brahmadeya; **Sabha** = brahmadeya (Brahmans only); **Nagaram** = merchants.

ne156ac75e82.s: Which Article of the Constitution recognises the Gram Sabha under the Panchayati Raj framework?
ne156ac75e82.x: Article 243A deals with the Gram Sabha. Article 243C concerns the composition of Panchayats, Article 243D reservations, and Article 243E duration.
xs: The **Gram Sabha** is in **Article 243A** — option **(2)** is correct.
**243C** = direct election; **243D** = **1/3** reservation for women; **243E** = **5-year** term.
xa: PRIs have **3 tiers**; intermediate tier optional below **20 lakh** population.
Chola village administration = an **early example of the Panchayati Raj System**.

nindian-history-148-5.s: In Chola administration, the 'Nagaram' denoted the assembly of:
nindian-history-148-5.x: Nagaram was the body of merchant towns; Ur was the ordinary village assembly, Sabha the Brahmana village assembly, and Variyams were village committees.
n: Ur referred to ordinary villages in the Chola administration. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Sabha referred to Brahmana villages in the Chola administration. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Nagaram referred to merchant towns in the Chola administration. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Variyams were specialized village committees. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
xa: Hierarchy: **Mandalam → Kottam/Valanadu → Nadu → Ur**.
Sabha (Mahasabha) was in **Brahmadeya** villages — **Brahmans only**.
**Nattar** = assembly of the **nadu**.
**Eri variyam** managed tanks; **Pon variyam** — gold/finance.

nf76254a4e8a.s: The Uttaramerur inscriptions (919 and 921 CE) belong to which Chola ruler?
nf76254a4e8a.x: The two Uttaramerur inscriptions are of Parantaka I, dated 919 and 921 CE; Uttaramerur is in Kanchipuram district.
xa: Most detailed record of **village administration** in ancient India.
Asked in APPSC G2 **2000**, **2003**.

n0b385f7fe1c.s: Which of the following is regarded as the principal source for reconstructing Chola village government?
n0b385f7fe1c.x: The Uttaramerur inscriptions provide detailed information about Chola village government and administration.
n0b385f7fe1c.tq: Identify the direct epigraphic source instead of literary works or a place-name distractor.
xs: The **Uttaramerur inscriptions** are the source for Chola village government — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC G2 **2000**, **2003**).
⚠ Trap: not **Kudimiamalai**, **Gangaikondacholapuram**, **Silappadikaram**, **Tolkappiyam** or **Periya Puranam**.
xa: Two inscriptions of **Parantaka I**, **919 and 921 CE**, in **Kanchipuram district**.
They describe the **kudavolai** lottery and **variyams**.

nindian-history-148-12.s: The unusually rich record of Chola history comes largely from extensive inscriptions engraved on:
nindian-history-148-12.x: The Cholas engraved long inscriptions on temple walls, which give an unusually rich record of their history.
n: Chola inscriptions include extensive temple-wall inscriptions. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Chola temple-wall inscriptions provide an unusually rich historical record. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
xa: **Rajaraja I** and **Rajendra I** commissioned **temple-wall inscriptions**.
The **Uttaramerur** inscriptions (**919 and 921 CE**) of **Parantaka I** detail village government.
**Kudavolai** = palm-leaf lottery in a pot.
Village divided into **30 wards (kudumbus)**.

n9803a9f50bb.s: Which of the following South Indian polities is described as highly centralised?
n9803a9f50bb.x: The Badami Chalukya polity is described as highly centralised, whereas Pallava, Chola and Rashtrakuta records show active local and village assemblies.
xa: The Chola system was the **culmination**: elected assemblies, committees and lottery.
**Burton Stein**: Chola **segmentary state**.

nc45b40dbd47.s: Under the Uttaramerur system, a candidate for a Chola village committee had to own at least:
nc45b40dbd47.x: Qualifications included owning at least 1/4 veli of land, an own house, age 35-70 and Vedic knowledge; recent committee service was a disqualification.
xa: Disqualifications also: failure to submit **accounts**, **sins**, **stolen** property.
Term: **three years**.

nafb70f46fe8.s: The term ‘kudavolai’ in Chola local administration referred to:
o: A system of collecting land revenue
A lottery system using palm-leaf ballots placed in a pot
nafb70f46fe8.x: Kudavolai was the selection procedure in which names written on palm leaves were placed in a pot and drawn by lot.
nafb70f46fe8.tq: Discriminate between similar administrative terms by identifying the precise procedure involved.
xs: **Kudavolai** = **lottery system** with palm-leaf ballots in a pot — option **(3)** is correct.
A ward is a **kudumbu**; tank management is the **eri variyam**.
xa: Names were drawn from the **pot (kudam)** by a **young boy/girl**.
**PM Modi** cited the Kudavolai "ballot pot" as proof of India's early democratic traditions (**Aug 2025**).

n27db28947b0.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the areas covered by the committees recorded at Uttaramerur?
o: Foreign trade, naval warfare, diplomacy and coin minting
Royal succession, military conquest, espionage and taxation alone
Agricultural slavery, overseas colonisation, astronomy and medicine
n27db28947b0.x: The Uttaramerur record refers to committees dealing with irrigation, gardens, justice and finance.
n27db28947b0.tq: Select the combination formed entirely from documented local administrative functions.
xs: The **Uttaramerur record** covers committees for **irrigation, gardens, justice and finance** — option **(1)** is correct.
These match **eri**, **thotta**, **samvatsara** and **pon** variyams.
xa: Other committees: **law and order**, justice.
**Variyam** = committee system.

n9a173f44462.s: Who described the Chola system of elected assemblies, committees and lottery as an example of “grassroots democracy”?
n9a173f44462.x: Nilakanta Sastri regarded the Chola system as a remarkable example of grassroots democracy. Burton Stein is associated with the segmentary-state interpretation.
xs: **Nilakanta Sastri** called the Chola system "**grassroots democracy**" — option **(3)** is correct.
**Burton Stein** called the Chola polity a **segmentary state**.
xa: Sastri also called sabha members an "**educated and propertied elite**".
The system is often called an **early Panchayati Raj**.

n8f774d0c5ba.s: A person who had served on a Chola village committee during the preceding three years was:
o: Eligible only for a finance committee
n8f774d0c5ba.x: Persons who had served on a committee during the previous three years were disqualified from selection.
n8f774d0c5ba.tq: Identify the cooling-off rule by distinguishing a disqualification from re-election eligibility.
xs: Anyone who had served in the **past three years** was **barred** — option **(2)** is correct.
This ensured rotation; members held **three-year** terms.
xa: Other disqualifications: failure to submit **accounts**, **sins**, **stolen** property.
Selection was by **kudavolai** (palm-leaf lottery).

naa3dfd4f65c.s: The lottery system used to select members of the Chola village assembly from among qualified persons was called:
naa3dfd4f65c.x: The Cholas used the kudavolai lottery among qualified persons, whereas Panchayat members under the 73rd Amendment are directly elected.
xa: Chola term **3 years**; PRI term **5 years** (**Art. 243E**).
Chola committees = **variyams**; PRIs have standing committees under state law.

n8cafb30bfd3.s: Under the 73rd Amendment, the intermediate tier of Panchayats may be omitted in a State whose population does not exceed:
n8cafb30bfd3.x: The intermediate tier is optional in a State with a population not exceeding twenty lakh; Panchayats have five-year terms and elections follow dissolution within six months.
xa: **Gram Sabha**: **Art. 243A**.
Chola members served only **3 years**.

nd86bfa87717.s: Which Article of the Constitution reserves not less than one-third of Panchayat seats for women?
nd86bfa87717.x: Article 243D reserves one-third of Panchayat seats and chairperson posts for women, unlike the Chola village assemblies, which had no quota for women.
xa: PRIs also have **SC/ST reservation**.
PRI elections must be held within **6 months** of dissolution.

n040482b3e6e.s: Participation in Chola sabhas was associated with:
n040482b3e6e.x: Sabha participation was tied to propertied, Vedic-learned Brahmins, so the system is criticised as elitist; it was not based on universal adult franchise.
xa: **Burton Stein**'s "segmentary state" view stresses **local autonomy**.
Eligibility: **1/4 veli** of land, **own house**, age **35-70**.

n0db289e952b.s: Which one of the following was NOT a disqualification for membership of a Chola village committee?
n0db289e952b.x: Owning a residence was a qualification, whereas failure to submit accounts, committing sins and stealing property were disqualifications.
n0db289e952b.tq: Find the qualification wrongly placed among the disqualifications.
xs: **Owning a residence** was a **qualification**, not a disqualification — option **(2)**.
Disqualifications: **stealing** property, committing **sins**, **failure to submit accounts**.
xa: Another disqualification: serving on a committee in the **past three years**.
Other qualifications: **1/4 veli** of land, age **35-70**, Vedic knowledge.

n10b1d4082d4.s: Chola village assemblies collected royal dues:
n10b1d4082d4.x: Royal dues were collected in cash, kind or both; the assembly also owned village lands, raised loans, levied taxes and auctioned defaulters' land.
xa: It held **proprietary rights over communal lands** and control of private lands.
Tanks were run by the **eri variyam**.

ne9abfbec70e.s: In Chola village administration, the term 'kudumbu' meant:
ne9abfbec70e.x: Kudumbu meant ward; perumakkal meant assembly members, variyapperumakkal elected committee members, and variyam the committee system.
xa: This four-term match was asked in **APPSC-G1 2022 and 2023**.
The key was **a-IV, b-I, c-II, d-III**.

n2565064f807.s: Rajaraja I directed the Cholamandalam sabhas to provide services to the:
n2565064f807.x: Rajaraja I directed the Cholamandalam sabhas to serve the Brihadeshvara temple.
n2565064f807.tq: Use the ruler–temple association while avoiding famous South Indian temple distractors.
xs: **Rajaraja I** directed **Cholamandalam sabhas** to serve the **Brihadeshvara temple** — option **(3)** is correct.
This was one of the assemblies' **temple services**.
xa: Assemblies could **raise loans**, **levy taxes**, **auction land** of defaulters.
They collected **royal dues** in cash, kind or both.

ncd30a4390aa.s: Rajaraja I was described by the title ‘Ulakalanada Perumal’ because he was regarded as:
o: the king who abolished hereditary officials
the ruler who measured the earth, like Vishnu’s three strides
the conqueror of the entire island of Sri Lanka
the patron who built all the major Chola temples
ncd30a4390aa.x: Ulakalanada Perumal means one who measured the earth, an image associated with Vishnu’s three strides.
ncd30a4390aa.tq: Use the literal meaning of the title to identify the correct royal association.
xs: **Ulakalanada Perumal** means **one who measured the earth**, like **Vishnu's three strides**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rajaraja I** earned it through his detailed **land survey and assessment** and revenue reorganisation.
The title is about measuring land, not abolishing officials, conquering **all of Sri Lanka** (that was **Rajendra I**) or building every temple.
xa: Rajaraja I's surveys were **repeated periodically** and recorded holdings and transfers.
Other royal titles: **ko**, **perumal**, **raja-rajadhiraja**, **ko-konmai kondan**, **perumal adigal** ("the great one").
Rajaraja I also named northern Sri Lanka **Mummudicholamandalam**.

n7a9e413be06.s: A ‘Samanta’ in the Chola political system was:
o: A royal secretary who countersigned orders
A tank committee member elected by villagers
A temple servant given tax-free land
A defeated king restored after accepting overlordship, tribute and military obligations
n7a9e413be06.x: A Samanta was a defeated king restored on condition that he accepted overlordship, paid tribute and provided military help.
n7a9e413be06.tq: Use the political relationship rather than the official title alone.
xs: A **Samanta** was a **defeated king restored** on accepting **overlordship**, paying **tribute** and giving **military help**, so option **(4)** is correct.
The countersigning secretary was the **Olai-nayagam**, and the tank committee was the **eri variyam**.
xa: Some provinces were **samanta** (vassal) territories paying tribute; others were **annexed principalities**.
**Burton Stein** called the Chola state **"segmentary"**.
The **Leiden plates** seal carries the **Chola tiger**, **Pandya fish** and **Chera bow**.

na3f2fe4bf92.s: Who wrote down the king’s oral orders on palm leaf in the Chola administration?
na3f2fe4bf92.x: The tirumandira-olai was the royal secretary who recorded the king’s oral orders on palm leaf.
na3f2fe4bf92.tq: Distinguish the drafting official from the checking official.
xs: The **Tirumandira-olai** was the royal secretary who wrote the king's **oral orders** on **palm leaf (olai)**, so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Olai-nayagam** was the **chief secretary** who checked and countersigned orders.
A **Samanta** was a restored vassal king, and **Rajapratinidhi** was the title of the Vengi viceroys.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **Tirumandira-olai** writes, **Olai-nayagam** countersigns.
Orders were **bilingual**: a **Sanskrit preamble** (genealogy, conquests) and a **Tamil** operative part.
**Perundaram** = highest officials; **Sirudaram** = lower officials.

ncf4fa6748c9.s: The principal function of the olai-nayagam was to:
ncf4fa6748c9.x: The olai-nayagam, or chief secretary, checked and countersigned royal orders before they were sent to officials.
ncf4fa6748c9.tq: Ask who would perform the final verification before dispatch.
xs: The **Olai-nayagam** (chief secretary) **checked and countersigned** royal orders before they went to officials, so option **(4)** is correct.
Water from tanks was distributed by the **eri variyam**, revenue in kind was **Kadamai**, and the **Kaikkolar** were infantry regiments.
xa: The **Tirumandira-olai** wrote down the king's **oral orders** on palm leaf.
Its full form is **tirumandira-olai-nayagam**.
**Dharmasana** = royal court of justice.

nb70275f2d8d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Chola officials and departments?
o: Dharmasana was the royal court of justice.
Puravu-varitinaikkalam or Shrikaranam was the revenue department.
nb70275f2d8d.x: Sirudaram denoted the lower officials; it was Perundaram that denoted the highest officials. The other statements are correct.
xa: **Adhikari** = royal officer supervising local bodies; **Nattar** = members of the nadu assembly.
**Tirumandira-olai** = royal secretary; **Olai-nayagam** = chief secretary.
The bureaucracy grew from **Rajaraja I** and weakened after **Kulottunga I**.

nce57a4bc218.s: Chola royal orders generally consisted of:
o: A Sanskrit preamble followed by a Tamil operative part
Tamil genealogy followed by a Sanskrit grant
nce57a4bc218.x: The royal orders had a Sanskrit preamble containing genealogy and conquests, followed by the Tamil operative portion.
nce57a4bc218.tq: Test the sequence and function of the two languages.
xs: Royal orders had a **Sanskrit preamble** followed by a **Tamil operative part**, so option **(2)** is correct.
The Sanskrit preamble gave the **genealogy and conquests**. The order was neither in one language only nor in the reverse arrangement.
xa: **Tamil** was the language of administration in the Chola inscriptions.
The **Leiden plates** follow the same pattern: **Sanskrit** genealogy and a **Tamil** grant.
The **Tirumandira-olai** recorded oral orders; the **Olai-nayagam** countersigned them.

n2649f5c95b2.s: Chola provincial territories that were not annexed but paid tribute were known as:
n2649f5c95b2.x: Chola provincial territories included annexed principalities and samanta or vassal territories that paid tribute.
xa: A **samanta** was a defeated king restored on accepting **overlordship**.
**Burton Stein** called the Chola state **"segmentary"**, with local autonomy intact at the periphery.
Vengi viceroys (**Rajapratinidhi**) were **Kulottunga I's sons**.

n8e1d52b390c.x: Mummudicholamandalam denoted northern Sri Lanka and was so named by Rajaraja I.
n8e1d52b390c.tq: Avoid reversing the three mandalam–region pairs.
xs: **Mummudicholamandalam** was **northern Sri Lanka**, named by **Rajaraja I**, so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Kaveri delta** was **Cholamandalam**, and the former **Pallava** country was **Jayankondacholamandalam** (Tondaimandalam).
xa: **Rajaraja I** took **northern Sri Lanka** and the **Maldives**.
**Rajendra I** went on to take **all of Sri Lanka**.
Chola overseas footholds: **Sri Lanka**, **Maldives**, **Kadaram/Srivijaya**.

nc80b00f6b9c.s: Burton Stein described the Chola state as a:
nc80b00f6b9c.x: Burton Stein used the concept of a segmentary state, while K.A. Nilakanta Sastri presented a more centralised picture.
xa: Nilakanta Sastri called the **Bay of Bengal** a **"Chola Lake"**.
Provinces mixed **annexed principalities** and **samanta** tributaries.
The bureaucracy weakened after **Kulottunga I** as local chieftains gained power.

nae99dafd56f.s: The Velaikkarar were distinguished in the Chola military system as:
o: Cavalry units recruited from Sri Lanka
Loyal bodyguard troops sworn to die with the king
Provincial governors appointed from among princes
nae99dafd56f.x: The Velaikkarar were loyal bodyguard troops who were sworn to die with the king.
nae99dafd56f.tq: Test the distinctive function of a named military group.
xs: The **Velaikkarar** were **loyal bodyguard troops sworn to die with the king**, so option **(3)** is correct.
Provincial governors were **viceroys/princes**, and land surveys were tied to **Rajaraja I's** survey. Neither describes the Velaikkarar.
xa: **Marco Polo** noted bodyguards ready to die for the king.
**Hereditary bodyguards** were paid in land revenue.
**Kaikkolar** = infantry; **Kadagams** = cantonments.

ncfd98440ead.s: Which Chola ruler is credited with building the Chola navy?
ncfd98440ead.x: Rajaraja I is credited with building the Chola navy. Rajendra I later expanded its operations significantly.
ncfd98440ead.tq: Directly identify the ruler associated with the institution rather than the ruler who later expanded it.
xs: **Rajaraja I** is credited with building the Chola **navy**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Rajendra I** carried it furthest (all of Sri Lanka, **Srivijaya**), and **Kulottunga I** conquered **Kalinga** with naval power.
xa: Rajaraja I destroyed the **Chera navy at Trivandrum** and took **northern Sri Lanka** and the **Maldives**.
Exam angle: "Which South Indian state was famous for naval power?" → **Chola**.
Bay of Bengal = **"Chola Lake"** (**K.A. Nilakanta Sastri**).

n4ded58ba811.s: Rajendra I's 1025 CE expedition against Srivijaya captured Kadaram, identified with:
n4ded58ba811.x: Rajendra I's Srivijaya expedition took Kadaram (Kedah) in Malaya and parts of Sumatra.
xa: **Rajendra I** also conquered **all of Sri Lanka**.
**Rajaraja I** built the navy and took the **Maldives**.
**Kulottunga I** conquered **Kalinga** "with great naval power".

n4761c11a49b.s: The normal rate of Chola land revenue was approximately:
n4761c11a49b.x: The normal Chola land revenue was one-sixth of the produce.
n4761c11a49b.tq: Distinguish the exact revenue fraction from nearby historical rates.
xs: Chola land revenue was normally **1/6th of the produce**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**One-third** was the rate of the **Mughals** and **Sher Shah**, not the Cholas.
xa: The Chola **1/6** was also the Pallava and Kakatiya standard.
Revenue was paid in **cash, kind or both**, through **village assemblies**.
**Kadamai** = land revenue collected in kind.

n98437ade3af.s: Which of the following terms collectively denoted forced labour service in Chola administration?
n98437ade3af.x: Vetti, Muttaiyal and Kudimai denoted forced labour service.
n98437ade3af.tq: Identify the complete group belonging to one administrative category.
xs: **Vetti**, **muttaiyal** and **kudimai** denoted **forced labour** owed by villagers to the state, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Kadamai** = revenue in kind, **Antarayam** = cash tax, **Eccoru** = feeding officials. **Devadana**/**Eripatti** are land types, and **Kadagams** were cantonments.
xa: **Nettal** also meant compulsory labour.
⚠ Trap: **Vetti/Nettal** = labour, not money.
**Kasu** = gold coin.

n5f86b85d059.s: The Chola land tax of one-sixth of the produce was comparable to the standard associated with the
n5f86b85d059.x: The Chola rate of one-sixth matched the standard associated with the Pallavas and Kakatiyas. The Mughals and Sher Shah are associated with one-third, while the Gupta rate was about one-seventh.
n5f86b85d059.tq: Use the rate comparison to pair the Cholas with the dynasties sharing the same standard.
xs: The Chola land tax of **1/6** matched the standard of the **Pallavas and Kakatiyas**, so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Mughals** and **Sher Shah** took **one-third**, and the **Gupta** rate was about **1/7**.
xa: Later South Indian states (**Kakatiyas**, **Vijayanagara**) kept the 1/6 rate.
Chola revenue was paid in **cash, kind or both**.
**Kadamai** = revenue in kind; **Antarayam** = cash tax.

n230c9ebe8bc.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP)?
o: Its first phase ran from 2016 to 2026.
The DILRMP 3.0 operational guidelines were issued by the Ministry of Rural Development.
DILRMP 3.0 covers survey/resurvey, ULPIN and cadastral maps.
n230c9ebe8bc.x: The first phase ran from 2008 to 2016; 2016-26 was the second phase, which brought ULPIN (Bhu-Aadhaar). The other statements are correct.
xa: The **'Land Stack'** portal and **'Glossary of Revenue Terms'** were launched in **Jan 2026**.
DILRMP is a modern successor to **Rajaraja I's** land survey.
AP: **Mee Bhoomi-Mee Hakku** re-survey and passbook camps (**9 Sep 2026**).

ndb270863d3f.x: Karanmai was the right to cultivate and mitachi the superior possessory right; ulukudi were tenants and kaniyudaiyar the land-owning farmers.
xa: **Kani** = possession with **rights and duties**.
**Vellanvagai** = land of non-Brahmin peasant proprietors.
**Brahmadeya** = rent-free villages granted to Brahmins.

nd71a258cab5.s: In the Chola period, 'eripatti' was land whose revenue was set apart for the maintenance of:
nd71a258cab5.x: Eripatti revenue maintained the village tank; ghatikas were colleges attached to temples, and land gifted to temples was devadana.
xa: ⚠ The UPSC 2016 trap: **Taniyur** as "village donated to a single Brahmin" is wrong.
**Salabhoga** = land for a school; **Pallichchandam** = land for Jaina institutions.
**Brahmadeya** villages had a **sabha**.

nb9b23dd9311.s: The maintenance and repair of village tanks were financed from:
nb9b23dd9311.x: Eripatti land was set aside to finance the maintenance and repair of village tanks.
nb9b23dd9311.tq: Distinguish irrigation endowment land from temple and provincial land.
xs: **Eripatti** land financed the **repair and maintenance** of village tanks, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Devadana** was temple land, **Mummudicholamandalam** was northern Sri Lanka, and **samanta** refers to vassals.
xa: **Eripatti** was a correct pair in **UPSC 2016**.
The **eri variyam** distributed tank water.
The temple was the locality's biggest **landholder**, employer and lender.

n70adc119823.s: The term ‘Devadana’ in the Chola period referred to:
o: Land used exclusively for tank repairs
n70adc119823.x: Devadana lands were grants made to temples.
n70adc119823.tq: Distinguish temple endowment terminology from irrigation and military terms.
xs: **Devadana** was **land gifted to temples**, so option **(4)** is correct.
Tank repair land was **Eripatti**; cantonments were **Kadagams**.
xa: Temples received large **devadana** grants.
The temple was the biggest **landholder**, employer and lender, and the venue for village assembly meetings.
**Pallichchandam** = land for **Jaina** institutions; **Brahmadeya** = land for **Brahmins**.

n0da3dc9d915.s: Which committee was responsible for managing village tanks and distributing water to fields?
n0da3dc9d915.x: The eri variyam was the tank committee responsible for managing tanks and distributing water to fields.
n0da3dc9d915.tq: Identify the body by its specific functional responsibility.
xs: The **eri variyam** (tank committee) ran every village tank and **distributed water** to fields, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Puravu-varitinaikkalam** was the revenue department, the **ur** was the village assembly, and the **Olai-nayagam** was the chief secretary.
xa: **Eripatti** land financed tank repairs.
The **Grand Anicut (Kallanai)** was built by **Karikala**.
AP angle: a **47.84-acre** tank near **Kanipakam** had **16** acres allegedly encroached.

n0bac377a691.s: Chola inscriptions praised the king as a warrior, a patron of the arts and the protector of:
n0bac377a691.x: Chola kings were compared to gods, their images were installed beside deities, and inscriptions praised them as warriors, patrons of art and protectors of varnashrama dharma.
xa: Inscriptional titles: **ko**, **perumal**, **raja-rajadhiraja**, **ko-konmai kondan**.
**Marco Polo** noted bodyguards ready to die for the king.
**Rajaraja I** directed the **sabhas of Cholamandalam** to perform services for the **Brihadeeswara** temple.

n514b48ccc7c.s: How many Mandalams (provinces) did the Chola Empire have?
n514b48ccc7c.x: The Chola Empire had eight Mandalams, each under a viceroy or governor who could be a prince or noble.
xa: **Cholamandalam** = the **Kaveri delta** core; **Mummudicholamandalam** = **northern Sri Lanka**.
**Jayankondacholamandalam** = **Tondaimandalam**, the former Pallava country around **Kanchi**.
Some provinces were **annexed principalities**; others were **samanta** territories paying tribute.

nc36882a2871.s: Besides being landholders, employers and lenders, Chola temples served as venues for meetings of the:
nc36882a2871.x: Chola temples were major landholders, employers and lenders, and also provided venues for village assembly meetings.
xa: **Rajaraja I** directed the **sabhas of Cholamandalam** to serve the **Brihadeeswara** temple.
Temple income came from **guild donations** and royal grants of **land and paddy**.
**Devadana** = land gifted to temples; **Pallichchandam** = land for **Jaina** institutions.

nc9ca8bd5526.s: The Tiruvalangadu copper plates are particularly associated with:
o: The genealogy and conquests of Rajendra I
The survey of land by Rajaraja I
The construction of the Grand Anicut by Karikala
The abolition of tolls by Kulottunga I
nc9ca8bd5526.x: The Tiruvalangadu plates of Rajendra I provide Chola genealogy and accounts of conquests.
xs: The **Tiruvalangadu plates** are copper plates of **Rajendra I** giving Chola **genealogy and conquests**, so option **(1)** is correct.
The land survey was **Rajaraja I's**, the Grand Anicut was **Karikala's**, and toll abolition was **Kulottunga I's**. None is the subject of these plates.
xa: The **Anbil plates** were issued under **Sundara Chola**.
**Rajendra I's 1025 CE** expedition took **Kadaram (Kedah)**.
The **Larger Leiden plates** were engraved under **Rajendra I**.

n0db6359050e.s: The Larger Leiden (Anaimangalam) plates record a grant to the Chulamanivarma-vihara built by the king of:
n0db6359050e.x: The plates, ordered by Rajaraja I and engraved under Rajendra I, grant Anaimangalam village to the vihara built by the Srivijaya king Sri Mara Vijayotunga Varman; they use Sanskrit and Tamil.
xa: They have **21 large + 3 small** sheets.
The ring seal shows the **Chola tiger**, **Pandya fish** and **Chera bow**.
Rajaraja I granted **8,943 kalam**; **Kulottunga I** added **4,500 kalam**.

n416b6c1020c.s: The smaller Leiden plates associated with the Chudamani Vihara comprise:
o: 21 sheets and record the construction of the vihara by the Srivijaya king
21 sheets and record Rajaraja I’s original grant only
3 sheets and record Kulottunga I’s extension of the grant after an appeal by two Javanese envoys
3 sheets and record Rajendra I’s expedition to Kadaram
n416b6c1020c.x: The smaller plates contain three sheets and record Kulottunga I’s extension of the grant after two Javanese envoys appealed to him.
n416b6c1020c.tq: Distinguish the smaller three-sheet record from the larger 21-sheet plates.
xs: The **smaller plates** (**3 sheets**) are **Kulottunga I's**, extending the grant after **two Javanese envoys** appealed, so option **(3)** is correct.
The **21** large sheets are the Larger Leiden plates, which hold Rajaraja I's original grant.
xa: Kulottunga I added **4,500 kalam** of paddy plus land on top of Rajaraja I's **8,943 kalam**.
The grant went to the **Chudamani Vihara** at **Nagapattinam**.
The vihara was built by the Srivijaya king **Sri Mara Vijayotunga Varman**.

n7a16deab8a1.s: Which merchant guild originated from Aihole and operated pan-regionally and overseas?
n7a16deab8a1.x: Ayyavole-500 originated from Aihole; Manigramam was a foreign-trade corporation, Ubhaya Nanadesi handled domestic and foreign trade, and Nagaram was a market-town assembly.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **Nagaram** = local; **Nanadesi/Manigramam** = foreign; **Ubhaya Nanadesi** = both.
Ayyavole-500 was also called **Ainnurruvar**, the "Five Hundred".
**Manigramam** as a foreign-trade body was asked in **UPSC 1997**.

n4dea105bbf7.s: Under the Eastern Chalukyas, the Nakaras (merchant bodies) were headed by:
n4dea105bbf7.x: Nakaras headed by Shreshthis traded under the Eastern Chalukyas, and Ayyavole and Manigramam were active in Andhra, especially around Penugonda.
xa: **Penugonda** had **18** branches across Vengi (**APPSC G2 2012**).
The guild head was the **Sreshthi / Setti**.
**Ayyavole-500** came from **Aihole**, Karnataka.

nafe62207f22.s: As Chola power declined, the independence of the merchant guilds:
nafe62207f22.x: Merchant guilds, which had emblems and militias, acted as bankers and donated to temples, became more independent as the Cholas declined.
xa: The guild head was the **Sreshthi / Setti**.
**Ayyavole-500** inscriptions are found in **Sumatra**, **Sri Lanka** and elsewhere.
**Penugonda** was the Andhra trade centre, with **18** branches.

nb3047e3f437.s: In the Andhra region, which place served as the central trade centre and had 18 branches across Vengi?
nb3047e3f437.x: Penugonda was the central trade centre in Andhra and had 18 branches across Vengi.
nb3047e3f437.tq: Combine a location clue with the associated branch count.
xs: **Penugonda** was the central trade centre in Andhra, with **18 branches** across **Vengi**, so option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2012**).
**Nagapattinam** was the main Chola port, **Quilon** a Kerala port and **Kaveripattinam** the Sangam Chola port.
xa: **Ayyavole** and **Manigramam** were active in Andhra ports and towns.
**Nakaras** headed by **Shreshthis** traded under the **Eastern Chalukyas**.
⚠ **Nagaram** = local merchant assembly.

nfecfdaace42.s: The wider historical significance of the Chola merchant-guild networks was that they:
o: replaced all temple institutions with royal agencies
confined trade to inland Tamil markets
ended commercial contacts with China and Southeast Asia
carried Chola trade and Dravidian culture across the Bay of Bengal
nfecfdaace42.x: The guild networks extended Chola commerce and Dravidian cultural influence across the Bay of Bengal.
xs: Guild networks **carried Chola trade and Dravidian culture across the Bay of Bengal**, so option **(4)** is correct.
They did not end contact with **China** or Southeast Asia: imports included **Chinese silk and porcelain**.
xa: Guild inscriptions are found at **Takua Pa** (Thailand), **Pagan** (Myanmar) and **Barus** (Sumatra).
The Chola navy made the Bay of Bengal a **"Chola Lake"**.
Guilds also **donated to temples**. They supported temples rather than replacing them.

nindian-history-148-8.s: Ayyavole 500 and Manigramam of the Chola age were:
nindian-history-148-8.x: Ayyavole 500 and Manigramam were merchant guilds of the Chola age, part of a sea trade running from Sri Lanka through Malaya and Sumatra to Southeast Asia.
n: Ayyavole 500 was a Chola merchant guild. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Manigramam was a Chola merchant guild. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
The Chola maritime network extended from Sri Lanka to the Malay Peninsula. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
The Chola maritime network extended from the Malay Peninsula to Sumatra. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
The Chola maritime network extended from Sumatra to Southeast Asia. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
xa: **Ayyavole-500** originated from **Aihole (Ayyavolu)**, Karnataka.
⚠ **Nagaram** = local; **Nanadesi / Manigramam** = foreign trade; **Ubhaya Nanadesi** = both.
Guild head: **Sreshthi / Setti**.
**Penugonda** was the central trade centre in Andhra (APPSC G2 2012).

n42ad01041b7.s: The Nagara style of temple architecture emerged prominently in which region and period?
o: The Deccan from about the 8th century CE
North India from about the 5th century CE
South India from about the 3rd century CE
Eastern India from about the 10th century CE
n42ad01041b7.x: The Nagara style is associated with North India and is identified from about the 5th century CE.
n42ad01041b7.tq: Link the style with both its region and approximate period instead of relying on the tower description alone.
xs: The **Nagara** style belongs to **North India**, from the **5th century**, so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Deccan** is linked to the **Vesara** style, and **South India** to the **Dravida** style.
xa: Nagara tower: a curvilinear **shikhara** over the garbhagriha, on a **stone platform**.
Nagara temples usually have **no elaborate boundary walls or gateways**.
Examples: **Kandariya Mahadeva**, **Lakshmana** (Khajuraho), **Kedarnath**.
n42ad01041b7.fixed: 'according to the stated classification' refers to app notes, not an exam phrasing

n419ff396a45.s: The Vesara style of temple architecture was pioneered by the:
n419ff396a45.x: Vesara, blending Dravida vimana tiers with the Nagara curvilinear profile, was pioneered by the Badami Chalukyas; the Hoysalas came later.
xa: Vesara is also called **"Chalukyan"** or **"Karnata Dravida"**.
Its tower is a **stepped shikhara**, a hybrid of Nagara and Dravida.
⚠ **Vimana** = Dravida tower; **shikhara** = Nagara tower.

n201bcc12262.s: The Nagara style of temple architecture is associated with a:
n201bcc12262.x: The Nagara temple has a curvilinear shikhara, while the Dravida temple has a pyramidal vimana and elaborate prakara walls and gateways.
xa: ⚠ In Dravida temples, the **shikhara** is only the crowning part of the vimana.
Dravida examples: **Kailasanatha** (Kanchipuram), **Brihadeeswara**.
Nagara examples: **Kandariya Mahadeva**, **Kedarnath**.

n31bef3d93a6.s: Chola temples represent the zenith of which temple style?
n31bef3d93a6.x: Chola free-standing structural temples are the zenith of the Dravida style, not Nagara; the style continued under the Kalyani Chalukyas and Hoysalas.
xa: "The **Pallavas** laid the foundation, the **Cholas** built the cathedral."
Dravida zenith features: massive **vimanas**, **Nandi mandapas**, **enclosure walls**.
Early Chola structural temple: **Koranganatha**, Srinivasanallur.

n777ff246268.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the term ‘Garbhagriha’ in Dravida temple architecture?
o: The womb-house containing the principal icon
The pillared hall used for gatherings
The raised platform of the temple
n777ff246268.x: Garbhagriha literally denotes the womb-house and houses the principal deity or icon of the temple.
n777ff246268.tq: Use the exact architectural meaning rather than confusing the sanctum with the hall or gateway.
xs: The **Garbhagriha** is the **womb-house** that holds the **main icon**, so option **(1)** is correct.
The pillared hall is the **mandapa**, the gateway tower is the **gopuram** and the raised platform is the **jagati**.
xa: The **vimana** is the pyramidal tower **over the garbhagriha**.
The **antarala** is the vestibule between the garbhagriha and the mandapa.
The **vahana** and **dhvaja** pillar stand axially before the sanctum.

nba1ffb2b1b8.s: In temple architecture, the 'antarala' is the:
o: vestibule between the sanctum and the mandapa
nba1ffb2b1b8.x: The antarala is the vestibule between sanctum and mandapa; the mandapa is a pillared hall, the jagati a raised platform and the gopuram the entrance gateway.
xa: **Prakara** = enclosure walls; **Nandi mandapa** = pavilion for Nandi.
The gopuram as the gateway tower of South Indian temples was the **BPSC 2017** key.
The **shikhara** is the dome-like crown of the vimana.

n24f73bff0d5.s: In a South Indian temple, the principal entrance gateway is generally known as the
n24f73bff0d5.x: Gopuram refers to the imposing entrance gateway tower characteristic of South Indian temples.
n24f73bff0d5.tq: Test the precise function of a familiar architectural term.
xs: The **Gopuram** is the mighty, elaborate **gateway tower** at the entrance of South Indian temples, so option **(1)** is correct (**BPSC 2017**).
**Antarala** = vestibule, **Shikhara** = crown of the vimana, **Jagati** = raised platform.
xa: Dravida temples have **prakara walls with gopurams**.
Nagara temples usually lack elaborate **gateways**.
The **vimana** is the dominant tower in Chola temples.

nf52b415b2a3.s: The topmost, dome-like crowning part of the vimana is called the
nf52b415b2a3.x: Shikhara denotes the topmost, dome-like crowning portion of the vimana; the monolithic shikhara of the Thanjavur temple is especially noted.
nf52b415b2a3.tq: Distinguish the crowning element from the entire tower and its surrounding structures.
xs: The **Shikhara** is the topmost, **dome-like** crowning part of the vimana, so option **(1)** is correct.
At **Thanjavur** it is **monolithic**.
**Mandapa** = pillared hall, **Prakara** = enclosure wall, **Antarala** = vestibule.
xa: ⚠ In Nagara temples the whole curvilinear tower is called the **shikhara**.
Thanjavur's **monolithic capstone** weighs about **80 tonnes**.
The **vimana** is a multi-storied pyramidal tower.

n029aa627df9.s: The Brihadeeswara Temple is also known by which of the following names?
n029aa627df9.x: Brihadeeswara Temple is also called Dakshina Meru.
n029aa627df9.tq: Test the alternate-name trap by separating titles of closely related Chola temples.
xs: **Brihadeeswara** (Rajarajeshwara) is also called **"Dakshina Meru"**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Airavatesvara** (Darasuram) and **Kampaharesvara** (Tribhuvanam) are separate temples.
xa: It was completed by **Rajaraja I** in **1010 CE**.
The great **Nandi** was **added later by the Nayakas**.
Its frescoes show **Shiva as Tripurantaka**.

na35b368fd35.s: The granite vimana of the Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur is about how high?
na35b368fd35.x: The vimana is about 216 feet high with a monolithic capstone of about 80 tonnes, and is built of granite, not brick.
xa: ⚠ **216 ft** = Thanjavur; **180 ft** = Gangaikondacholapuram.
Completed by **Rajaraja I** in **1010 CE**.
The shikhara at Thanjavur is **monolithic**.

nfed07bd99ca.s: The 'Musical Steps' and the horse-drawn stone chariot are features of which Chola temple?
nfed07bd99ca.x: The Musical Steps and stone chariot belong to the Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram, built by Rajaraja II; Kulottunga III built the Kampaharesvara at Tribhuvanam.
xa: Airavatesvara is called a **miniature masterpiece**.
Airavatesvara is one of the UNESCO **Great Living Chola Temples**.
The other two in the group are **Thanjavur** and **Gangaikondacholapuram**.

n2908fcf29a9.s: Which of the following correctly describes the vimana of the Gangaikondacholapuram Temple?
o: It is 216 feet high and has a straight, rigid profile.
It is 216 feet high and has a circular plan.
It is 180 feet high and is entirely made of brick and mortar.
It is 180 feet high and has a concave curvilinear profile.
n2908fcf29a9.x: The vimana of Gangaikondacholapuram is about 180 feet high and has a curvilinear concave profile.
n2908fcf29a9.tq: Use the height and profile together to distinguish it from Thanjavur’s vimana.
xs: The Gangaikondacholapuram vimana is **180 ft** high with a **concave curvilinear** profile, so option **(4)** is correct.
**216 ft** is the **Thanjavur** vimana, which has a "masculine" bulk.
xa: ⚠ **216 ft – 180 ft** = **Thanjavur – Gangaikondacholapuram**.
Its profile is said to show "feminine" grace.
Built by **Rajendra I** to mark the **Ganga expedition**.

n8c53697c5c1.s: The Chit Sabha, containing carvings of 108 classical dance poses, is associated with the
n8c53697c5c1.x: The Chit Sabha of the Thillai Nataraja Temple at Chidambaram contains carvings of 108 classical dance poses.
n8c53697c5c1.tq: Identify the shrine through its distinctive dance-related architectural feature.
xs: The **Chit Sabha** (Hall of Consciousness), with **108 classical dance poses**, is in the **Thillai Nataraja temple, Chidambaram**, so option **(4)** is correct.
The temple is a shrine of **Shiva as Nataraja**, enlarged by **Chola kings**.
xa: ⚠ Chidambaram is **not** among the UNESCO **Great Living Chola Temples**.
**APPSC-GS 2018**: Chidambaram, Thanjavur and Gangaikondacholapuram were built by the **Cholas**.
**Airavatesvara** has the **"Musical Steps"**.

nad9efe3a348.s: The temples at Chidambaram, Thanjavur and Gangaikondacholapuram were built or enlarged by the
nad9efe3a348.x: All three are Chola temples (APPSC-GS 2018 key): Thanjavur's Brihadeeswara by Rajaraja I, Gangaikondacholapuram by Rajendra I, and the Thillai Nataraja temple at Chidambaram enlarged by Chola kings. The Pallavas built the Mahabalipuram monuments; the Pandyas and Vijayanagara rulers are not the builders asked about here.
nad9efe3a348.tq: Chidambaram is Chola-enlarged but NOT one of the three UNESCO Great Living Chola Temples.
xs: The temples at **Chidambaram**, **Thanjavur** and **Gangaikondacholapuram** were built or enlarged by the **Cholas**, so option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC-GS 2018**).
Thanjavur = **Rajaraja I**; Gangaikondacholapuram = **Rajendra I**; Chidambaram was enlarged by **Chola kings**.
The **Pallavas** built the **Mahabalipuram** monuments (Seven Pagodas, Shore Temple).
xa: The Chit Sabha at Chidambaram has **108** dance poses carved.
"The Pallavas laid the foundation, the Cholas built the cathedral."
AP: **Draksharama Bhimeswara** = independent **Chalukya-Chola** style.

n0cf15ba78d3.s: The early friendly relations between the Cholas and Srivijaya are associated with the vihara at:
n0cf15ba78d3.x: Chola-Srivijaya relations began amicably, as seen in the Nagapattinam vihara, until obstruction of Indian traders led to Rajendra I's 1025 expedition to Kadaram.
xa: Freeing trade with **China** was one motive.
**Kulottunga I** confirmed the Nagapattinam grant and added **4,500 kalam** of paddy.
**Rajaraja I** endowed the vihara.

nindian-history-148-4.s: The Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram was built by:
nindian-history-148-4.x: Rajaraja II built the Airavatesvara temple; Rajaraja I built Brihadeeswara, Rajendra I built Gangaikondacholapuram and Kulottunga I abolished tolls.
n: Rajaraja I was associated with the Brihadeeswara Temple. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Gangaikondacholapuram is associated with Rajendra I. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
The Airavatesvara Temple is associated with Rajaraja II. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
Rajendra I built the Chola Gangam, a huge artificial lake. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #148 · pp 257-259]
xa: All three temples form the UNESCO **"Great Living Chola Temples"** (Thanjavur **1987**, extended **2004**).
⚠ **Chidambaram** is **not** in the group.
Vimanas: Thanjavur **216 ft**, Gangaikondacholapuram **180 ft**.
Airavatesvara has a stone chariot and **"Musical Steps"**.

nfc70ae07524.s: Which of the following temple sites is NOT part of the UNESCO group 'Great Living Chola Temples'?
nfc70ae07524.x: The group comprises the temples at Thanjavur, Gangaikondacholapuram and Darasuram; Chidambaram is not included.
xa: Thanjavur was listed in **1987**, and the listing was extended to the other two in **2004**.
Darasuram's **Airavatesvara** was built by **Rajaraja II**.
Gangaikondacholapuram was built by **Rajendra I**.

nf050c3e05bb.s: In the Chola Nataraja bronze, the lower right hand in abhaya mudra signifies:
nf050c3e05bb.x: Abhaya mudra means 'fear not', i.e. protection; the standard Nataraja is four-armed and the lower left hand points to the raised left foot.
xa: The lower left hand gesture is **gaja-hasta**, meaning release or **liberation / refuge**.
Upper right hand: **damaru** (creation); upper left hand: **agni** (destruction).
Trampling **Apasmara** = conquest of **ignorance**.

na6fedd2680c.s: The man's earring in the right ear and the woman's earring in the left ear of the Chola Nataraja symbolise:
o: the fusion of male and female principles
na6fedd2680c.x: The different earrings of the Nataraja image represent the fusion of male and female principles.
xa: **UPPSC 2021**: "four hands" and "man's earring right, woman's left" were **both correct**.
The ring of flames, the **Prabhamandala**, stands for the cosmic cycle.
The **damaru** = creation; **agni** = destruction.

n98f4120094d.s: In the Nataraja image, the damaru held in the upper right hand symbolises:
n98f4120094d.x: The damaru symbolises creation, the agni in the upper left hand destruction, and the prabhamandala the cosmic cycle; Apasmara represents ignorance.
xa: The standard form is **four-armed**.
**Abhaya mudra** = "fear not", i.e. protection.
The two different earrings show the fusion of **male and female** principles.

n96ccd77acdb.s: The lost-wax technique perfected by the Cholas for making bronze icons is known as
n96ccd77acdb.x: The Cholas perfected the cire perdue, or lost-wax, casting technique for bronze icons.
n96ccd77acdb.tq: Test the exact technical term rather than a general description of metal casting.
xs: The Cholas perfected **cire perdue (lost-wax)** casting for bronzes, so option **(2)** is correct.
Their masterpiece is the **Nataraja**.
xa: Chola bronzes were **worshipped icons**.
They are noted for **fine craftsmanship**, **intricate jewellery** and **expressive faces**.
Nataraja is **four-armed** in the standard form (**UPPSC 2021**).

nba3f5a9a88f.s: The dark ambulatory passage of the Brihadeeswara temple contains paintings depicting
o: The Alvars composing the Divya Prabandham
Shiva as Tripurantaka and portraits of Rajaraja I with Karuvur Thevar
Only scenes from the Kalinga war
The coronation of Kulottunga II by Ottakuthar
nba3f5a9a88f.x: The Brihadeeswara frescoes show Shiva as Tripurantaka and royal portraits of Rajaraja I together with his guru Karuvur Thevar.
nba3f5a9a88f.tq: Combine the deity image and the royal portrait clues to identify the correct fresco tradition.
xs: The dark ambulatory passage frescoes show **Shiva as Tripurantaka** and portraits of **Rajaraja I** with his guru **Karuvur Thevar**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ottakuthar** was a court poet and the **Kalinga** war is the subject of the **Kalingattupparani**, not these frescoes.
xa: **Gangaikondacholapuram** has other murals.
**Narthamalai**: cave paintings of Shiva-Parvati.
**Dakshinamurthy** panels: the finest stone carving.

nff4a150d2d8.s: The Chola-period cave paintings at Narthamalai depict:
nff4a150d2d8.x: Narthamalai paintings show Shiva and Parvati; Chola murals are also known at Gangaikondacholapuram, with fine Dakshinamurthy panels at Thanjavur.
xa: Thanjavur frescoes: **Shiva as Tripurantaka**.
They also show **Rajaraja I** with guru **Karuvur Thevar**.
The frescoes are in the **dark ambulatory passage**.

n1589dc171af.s: Who composed the Kamba Ramayanam, also known as Ramavataram?
n1589dc171af.x: Kamba Ramayanam or Ramavataram was composed by Kamban and is a Tamil adaptation of the Ramayana, not merely a translation of Valmiki.
n1589dc171af.tq: Use author-work matching with closely associated Tamil literary names as distractors.
xs: **Kamban** wrote the **Kamba Ramayanam (Ramavataram)**, so option **(3)** is correct (**UPPSC 2010**).
It is a **Tamil adaptation**, not a mere translation of **Valmiki**.
**Jayamkondar** wrote the **Kalingattupparani**, **Sekkilar** the **Periya Puranam** and **Pavanandhi** the **Nannul**.
xa: **Ottakuthar** wrote **Moovar Ula**.
**Pugalendi** wrote **Nalavenba** (the Nala-Damayanti story).
**Amirthasagarar** (a Jain) wrote **Yapperungalam**, on prosody.

n2dd6d493c0b.s: Periyapuranam, which describes the lives of the 63 Nayanars, was written by
n2dd6d493c0b.x: Sekkilar authored Periyapuranam, also called Tiruttondarpuranam, dealing with the lives of the 63 Nayanars.
n2dd6d493c0b.tq: Match the religious subject of the work with its correct author.
xs: **Sekkilar** wrote the **Periya Puranam (Tiruttondarpuranam)** on the lives of the **63 Nayanars**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ottakuthar** wrote **Moovar Ula**, and **Amirthasagarar** wrote **Yapperungalam**.
xa: The Periya Puranam was added as the **12th** book of the **Tirumurai**.
The **Tirumurai** was compiled by **Nambi Andar Nambi**.
The **Nayanars** were Shaiva devotees; the **Alvars** were Vaishnava.

n71fe49792fb.s: The Tamil grammar Nannul was written by:
n71fe49792fb.x: Nannul is by Pavanandhi; Kalingattupparani is by Jayamkondar, Moovar Ula by Ottakuthar and Nalavenba by Pugalendi.
xa: Kalingattupparani is a war poem on **Kulottunga I's Kalinga campaign**.
Ottakuthar was court poet of **Kulottunga I**, **Vikrama Chola** and **Kulottunga II**.
**Nannul** is the standard **Tamil grammar**; **Nalavenba** tells the **Nala-Damayanti** story.

nd7e0f4d5600.s: The Saiva canon Tirumurai was compiled in the time of Rajaraja I by:
nd7e0f4d5600.x: Nambi Andar Nambi compiled the Tirumurai, the 12-book Saiva canon of Nayanar hymns (Periya Puranam the 12th); it does not include the Vaishnava Alvar hymns.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes wrongly lump Alvar hymns into "**11 volumes**" of the Tirumurai.
It is called the "**Fifth Veda**" / "**Tamil Veda**"; it includes the **Tevaram**.
The Periya Puranam (by **Sekkilar**) covers the **63 Nayanars**.

nb4a5b2ddddd.s: Rajaraja I’s inscriptions at the Thanjavur temple are significant because they record
o: The election of village assemblies through the Kudavolai system
Only the names of foreign merchants visiting the Chola ports
About 400 temple dancing women, musicians and temple staff supported by grants
The complete list of Nayanar hymns in the Tirumurai
nb4a5b2ddddd.x: The inscriptions mention about 400 temple dancing women and also refer to musicians and other staff who were paid through grants. The Kudavolai election system is recorded in Uttiramerur inscriptions.
nb4a5b2ddddd.tq: Distinguish the social records of Thanjavur inscriptions from the administrative record at Uttiramerur.
xs: Rajaraja I's **Thanjavur inscriptions** record about **400 temple dancing women**, with **musicians and staff paid by grants**, so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ The **Kudavolai** elections are in the **Uttiramerur** inscriptions of **Parantaka I**.
xa: Rajaraja I sent an embassy to **China** in **1015**.
He endowed the **Chulamanivarma-vihara** at **Nagapattinam**.
The **Tirumurai** was compiled by **Nambi Andar Nambi** in Rajaraja I's time.

n4be5b14121e.s: The Uttiramerur inscriptions of the time of Parantaka I are especially important for their reference to the
o: Kudavolai system of village assembly elections
n4be5b14121e.x: The Uttiramerur inscriptions, associated with Parantaka I, record the Kudavolai or pot-ballot system used in village assembly elections.
n4be5b14121e.tq: Associate the inscription site and ruler with the specific administrative institution recorded there.
xs: The **Uttiramerur** inscriptions of **Parantaka I** record the **Kudavolai** (pot-ballot) system of village assembly elections, so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Kudavolai belongs to **Parantaka I**, not **Rajaraja I**.
xa: **Rajaraja I's** Thanjavur inscriptions record about **400** temple dancing women.
The **Tirumurai** was compiled in **Rajaraja I's** time.
**Airavatesvara** was built by **Rajaraja II**.

nf3da96a4e4e.s: Which one of the following North Indian temples has a pinnacle (superstructure) in the Dravida style?
nf3da96a4e4e.x: The Teli temple at Gwalior has a pinnacle in the Dravida style (UPPSC 2016 key). Bhitargaon, Kandariya Mahadeo and the Osian temples are all Nagara-style temples.
nf3da96a4e4e.tq: Teli ka Mandir, Gwalior = Dravida-style top in the north.
xs: The **Teli temple, Gwalior** has a pinnacle in the **Dravida** style, so option **(3)** is correct (**UPPSC 2016**).
**Bhitargaon**, **Kandariya Mahadeo** and **Osian** are **Nagara** temples.
xa: ⚠ **Brihadeeswara** is a classic Dravida temple. Some notes call it a fusion, but follow "Dravida" for exams.
Nagara tower = curvilinear **shikhara**; Dravida tower = **vimana**.
Vesara = **stepped shikhara**, a hybrid.

n2d6f10282b4.s: Which one of the following was the earlier capital of the Hoysalas?
n2d6f10282b4.x: Belur was the earlier capital of the Hoysalas, before Dwarasamudra became their capital.
n2d6f10282b4.tq: Use the capital-sequence distinction rather than confusing a capital with a temple site.
xs: **Belur** was the **earlier capital** of the Hoysalas, so option **(2)** is correct.
The later capital was **Dwarasamudra** (modern **Halebid**). **Somanathapura** is a temple site, **Talakad** a battle site and **Devagiri** the Yadava capital.
xa: ⚠ **Dwarasamudra** = old name; **Halebid** = modern name.
Hoysala monuments at **Halebid and Belur** (**UPSC 2001**).
Belur's **Chennakeshava** temple was built by **Vishnuvardhana** in **1117**.

nindian-history-149-3.s: Dwarasamudra is identified with which present-day place?
nindian-history-149-3.x: Dwarasamudra, the Hoysala capital, is present-day Halebidu in Hassan district, Karnataka. Belur, also in Hassan, was the earlier capital.
n: Dwarasamudra is present-day Halebidu. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149 · pp 259-260]
Halebidu is in Hassan district, Karnataka. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149 · pp 259-260]
xs: **Dwarasamudra** is present-day **Halebidu, Hassan district, Karnataka** — option **(3)**.
**Halebid** is the **modern name** of Dwarasamudra (UPPSC 2003 key).
**Belur** was the **earlier capital**, not Dwarasamudra.
xa: **Halebidu** = "old city" — named after Dwarasamudra was sacked by the Delhi armies.
**Malik Kafur** took Dwarasamudra in **1311**.
Hoysala monuments: **Halebid and Belur** (UPSC 2001 key).
⚠ **Dwarasamudra** = old name; **Halebid** = modern name.

nindian-history-149-1.s: The Hoysala Dynasty was associated primarily with which region?
nindian-history-149-1.x: The Hoysalas ruled from the Karnataka region, with capitals at Belur and later Dwarasamudra (Halebidu).
nindian-history-149-1.tq: Recall the home region of the dynasty.
n: The Hoysala Dynasty was associated with Karnataka. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149 · pp 259-260]
xs: The Hoysalas were associated with **Karnataka** — option **(4)**.
Their capital **Dwarasamudra** is present-day **Halebidu** in **Hassan district**, Karnataka.
Earlier capital: **Belur**.
xa: **Vishnuvardhana** (original name **Bittideva**) converted from Jainism to **Vaishnavism** under **Ramanuja**.
He defeated the Cholas at **Talakad** — title **Talakadugonda**.
His queen **Shantala Devi** stayed a **Jain**.
**Veera Ballala II** (**1170-1220**) defeated Yadava **Bhillama**.

n614b58610e6.s: What was the original name of Vishnuvardhana?
n614b58610e6.x: Vishnuvardhana was originally known as Bittideva, also called Bittiga.
n614b58610e6.tq: Test a ruler’s original name directly, a common history recall pattern.
xs: Vishnuvardhana's original name was **Bittideva (Bittiga)**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Ketamalla** was his officer who built **Hoysaleswara**, **Pedarudru** was a **Kakatiya** commander and **Bhillama** was a **Yadava**.
xa: He converted from **Jain** to **Vaishnava** under **Ramanuja**.
His queen **Shantala Devi** remained a **Jain**.
⚠ **Bittideva** = Vishnuvardhana; **Talakadugonda** = his Talakad title.

ndf53204aeb1.s: The Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana (Bittideva) converted from Jainism to Vaishnavism under the influence of:
ndf53204aeb1.x: Bittideva became a Vaishnava under Ramanuja, who had taken refuge from Chola persecution; his queen Shantala Devi remained a Jain.
xa: Vishnuvardhana built **Chennakeshava, Belur** in **1117**.
He defeated the Cholas at **Talakad** and took the title **Talakadugonda**.
A **veeragallu** found at **Neeragunda** may settle the date of his death.

n729f55fa5dc.s: Vishnuvardhana assumed the title ‘Talakadugonda’ after his victory over the:
n729f55fa5dc.x: Vishnuvardhana defeated the Cholas at Talakad and assumed the title Talakadugonda.
n729f55fa5dc.tq: Connect the victory site with the title derived from it.
xs: **Vishnuvardhana** took the title **Talakadugonda** after defeating the **Cholas at Talakad**, so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Yadavas of Devagiri** and the **Pandyas** were later Hoysala rivals, not the enemy at Talakad.
xa: After Talakad he built **Chennakeshava, Belur** (**1117**).
He expanded the kingdom and built **Belur**.
His original name was **Bittideva**.

n0fb0552724e.s: A veeragallu with a Kannada inscription found at Neeragunda in Arsikere taluk may help settle which historical question?
o: The date of the construction of the Keshava Temple
The date of Malik Kafur’s death
n0fb0552724e.x: The hero stone, unearthed on 28 June 2026, may help settle the long-disputed date of Vishnuvardhana’s death.
n0fb0552724e.tq: Apply the archaeological discovery to the specific historical problem it may resolve.
xs: The **veeragallu (hero stone)** at **Neeragunda, Arsikere taluk** may settle the long-disputed date of **Vishnuvardhana's death**, so option **(2)** is correct.
It carries a **Kannada** inscription.
xa: It was unearthed on **28 June 2026** and reported on **7 Aug 2026**.
Vishnuvardhana's original name was **Bittideva**.
He built **Chennakeshava, Belur** (**1117**).

n91e07656966.s: Which Hoysala ruler made the Hoysalas independent after defeating Yadava Bhillama?
n91e07656966.x: Veera Ballala II defeated Yadava Bhillama and made the Hoysalas independent; his reign is given as 1170–1220.
n91e07656966.tq: Link the victory and political consequence to the correct ruler.
xs: **Veera Ballala II** (**1170-1220**) defeated Yadava **Bhillama** and made the Hoysalas **independent**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Narasimha II** (**1220-1254**) fought the Yadavas, and **Narasimha III** was defeated by the Pandyas.
xa: **Nripa Kama II** was an early chief under the **Western Chalukyas**.
**Vishnuvardhana** took **Talakad** from the Cholas.
The Yadavas of **Devagiri** fought constant wars with the Hoysalas.

nd8900efce5e.s: Which event is associated with Narasimha III?
o: Victory over the Cholas at Talakad
Defeat of Yadava Ramachandra’s forces in 1305
nd8900efce5e.x: Narasimha III was defeated by the Pandya ruler Maravarman Kulasekhara. The Keshava Temple at Somanathapura was also built during his reign.
nd8900efce5e.tq: Use the swapped-ruler trap by matching the achievement to the correct reign.
xs: **Narasimha III** (**1254-1295**) was defeated by Pandya **Maravarman Kulasekhara**, so option **(1)** is correct.
Bhillama's defeat was **Veera Ballala II's**, Talakad was **Vishnuvardhana's**, and the **1305** victory was **Ballala III's**.
xa: **Somanathapura** was built in his reign, by his general **Somanatha** (**1268**).
Its **Keshava** temple has the best-preserved **star-shaped plan**.
The sculptor **Mallitamma** signed his work at Somanathapura.

n30d60d931f0.s: In which year did Malik Kafur take the Hoysala capital Dwarasamudra?
n30d60d931f0.x: Malik Kafur took Dwarasamudra in 1311 in a campaign affecting the Yadavas, Kakatiyas, Hoysalas and Pandyas.
xa: **Halebidu** ("old city") got its name after the **Delhi armies** sacked Dwarasamudra.
The ruler then was **Ballala III** (**1295-1342**).
Vijayanagara architecture followed the **Hoysala** and **Pandya** styles.

n245d03e3ed0.s: In which year did Ballala III die, after which the Hoysala territory passed to Vijayanagara?
n245d03e3ed0.x: Ballala III died in 1342, and the political space of the Hoysala kingdom then passed to Vijayanagara.
xa: He was defeated by Kakatiya commander **Pedarudru** after **1316**.
Kafur attacked the **Yadavas**, **Kakatiyas**, **Hoysalas** and **Pandyas**.

nf1cb74fab4e.s: The Hoysaleswara (Shiva) temple at Halebid was built by:
nf1cb74fab4e.x: Ketamalla, an officer of Vishnuvardhana, built the Hoysaleswara temple (c. 1121); Vishnuvardhana himself built the Chennakeshava at Belur (1117).
xa: ⚠ Hoysaleswara = **Shiva**; Belur and Somanathapura = **Vishnu**.
**Somanathapura** was built in **Narasimha III's** reign (**1268**).
Hoysaleswara is classed as **Vesara** (**CGPSC 2023**).
