nba841991614.s: The Keshava temple at Somanathapura (1268) was built by Somanatha, the general of:
nba841991614.x: The Vishnu (Keshava) temple at Somanathapura was built in 1268 by Somanatha, general of Narasimha III.
xa: It has the best-preserved **star-shaped plan** (**UPSC**).
The sculptor **Mallitamma** left his signature there.
It is part of the UNESCO **Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas** (**2023**).

nindian-history-149-7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Hoysalas?
o: Belur was the earlier Hoysala capital.
Dwarasamudra (Halebidu) was the later Hoysala capital.
The Hoysaleshwara temple at Halebidu is dedicated to Vishnu.
The Chennakeshava temple was built by Vishnuvardhana.
nindian-history-149-7.x: The Hoysaleshwara at Halebidu is a Shiva temple, so that statement is false; the other three are correct.
n: Dwarasamudra was the capital of the Hoysala Dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149 · pp 259-260]
Kedroz was the architect of the Hoysaleshwara Temple. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149 · pp 259-260]
Vishnuvardhana built the Chennakeshava Temple at Belur. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149 · pp 259-260]
Narasimha I's reign was associated with the construction of the Hoysaleshwara Temple. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149 · pp 259-260]
xa: ⚠ Hoysaleswara = **Shiva**; Belur and Somanathapura = **Vishnu**.
Keshava temple, **Somanathapura** — best-preserved **star-shaped plan**.
UNESCO **Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas** inscribed in **2023**.
Hoysaleshwara: architect **Kedroz**; ⚠ other notes credit **Ketamalla**, c. **1121**.

n7db0322b1b4.s: Hoysala temple architecture is generally classified under which style?
n7db0322b1b4.x: Hoysala architecture is generally classified as Vesara in examination keys, although it is also described as an evolution of the Dravida style.
n7db0322b1b4.tq: Test the examination classification while distinguishing it from a broader architectural description.
xs: Exam keys class Hoysala architecture as **Vesara**, so option **(3)** is correct (Hoysaleshwara = Vesara, **CGPSC 2023**).
Some sources (**CDI**) call it an evolution of **Dravida**, but follow **Vesara** for exams.
xa: Vesara = **Dravida vimana tiers** + **Nagara** curvilinear profile, pioneered by the **Badami Chalukyas**.
Hoysala features: **stellate plan**, **soapstone**, **lathe-turned** pillars.
Vesara builders in the Deccan: Badami and **Kalyani Chalukyas**, **Rashtrakutas**, **Hoysalas**.
n7db0322b1b4.fixed: odd stem wording; Vesara per ya6a3beb3bab

n7b93603b0c9.s: Hoysala temples with stellate plans were built on a raised platform of about one metre called the:
n7b93603b0c9.x: Hoysala temples stand on a raised jagati platform of about one metre, and their stellate plan peaked in the twelfth century.
xa: Best-preserved star plan: **Keshava, Somanathapura**.
The **Kalyani Chalukyas** passed on soapstone and star plans.
Pillars were **lathe-turned** and finely polished.

n798836854b7.s: The Madanika (Salabhanjika) bracket figures are especially associated with which Hoysala temple site?
n798836854b7.x: The Madanika bracket figures are associated with Belur, not Somanathapura.
xa: Pillars were **lathe-turned** and finely polished.
Stone: **chloritic schist (soapstone)**.
**Mallitamma** is the sculptor associated with **Somanathapura**.

nindian-history-149-11.s: Hoysala temples with lathe-turned pillars and star-shaped plans were built of soft:
nindian-history-149-11.x: Hoysala temples used soft chlorite schist (soapstone), had stellate plans and lathe-turned pillars, and were richly carved.
n: Hoysala temples have star-shaped or stellate plans. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149 · pp 259-260]
Hoysala temples were built using soft chlorite-schist stone. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149 · pp 259-260]
Hoysala temples have lathe-turned pillars. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149 · pp 259-260]
Hoysala sculpture has highly detailed friezes. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149 · pp 259-260]
Hoysala sculpture contains mythological depictions. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149 · pp 259-260]
xa: Temples stand on a raised **jagati** platform about **1 m** high.
Bracket figures **Madanikas/Salabhanjikas** at Belur.
The stellate plan originated under the **Chalukyas** and peaked under the Hoysalas.
Sculptors: **Mallitamma** (Somanathapura), **Jakanachari** (Belur, by tradition).

nd6f5aedd56e.s: Which Yadava ruler threw off Kalyani Chalukya overlordship and founded Devagiri as the capital?
nd6f5aedd56e.x: Bhillama V founded Devagiri (c. 1187) after throwing off Kalyani Chalukya overlordship; the Seuna Yadavas' mother tongue was Marathi.
xa: The Yadavas encouraged **Marathi** (**APHQ**).
Bhillama V was defeated by Hoysala **Veera Ballala II**.
⚠ **Bhillama V** founded Devagiri; **Singhana II** = greatest; **Harapaladeva** = last.

na6213e663c8.s: Which Yadava ruler killed the Kakatiya Rudradeva and later released Ganapatideva in 1199?
na6213e663c8.x: Jaitugi killed Rudradeva, held Ganapatideva captive, released him in 1199 and married his daughter Somaladevi to him.
xa: The **Paithan copper plate** of Ramachandra confirms Jaitugi killed Rudradeva and imprisoned Ganapatideva.
Court poet **Hemadri** claimed Jaitugi captured and **sacrificed** Rudra.
Ganapatideva was released as a **counterweight** to Hoysala **Veera Ballala**.

n5ba19d2d137.s: Which Yadava ruler was known as the greatest of the Yadava rulers and assumed the title ‘Teluguraya Sthapanacharya’?
n5ba19d2d137.x:
Singhana II, who ruled from 1200 to 1247, was regarded as the greatest Yadava ruler and bore the title ‘Teluguraya Sthapanacharya’.
⚠ Sources differ: Singhana II's reign is given as 1200-1247 in some sources and c.1210-1246 in others. This key follows the notes.
n5ba19d2d137.tq: Link the title with the ruler who held it.
xs: **Singhana II** (**1200-1247**), the **greatest Yadava**, took the title **'Teluguraya Sthapanacharya'**, so option **(4)** is correct.
The title means **installer of the Telugu king**.
**Bhillama V** founded Devagiri, **Jaitugi** killed Rudradeva, and **Mahadeva** was repulsed by Rudramadevi.
xa: Singhana II **defeated the Hoysalas**.
His court musician **Sarngadeva** wrote the **Sangita Ratnakara**.
His son **Sarangapanideva** later served at **Rudramadevi's** court.

n40a74b7eefc.s: Which Yadava ruler’s attack on the Kakatiyas was repulsed by Rudramadevi?
n40a74b7eefc.x: Rudramadevi repulsed the attack launched by Yadava ruler Mahadeva against the Kakatiyas.
n40a74b7eefc.tq: Identify the ruler involved in the specific military encounter.
xs: The Yadava ruler **Mahadeva** attacked the Kakatiyas and was **repulsed by Rudramadevi**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Jaitugi** killed **Rudradeva**, and **Ramachandra** was defeated by Delhi in **1295**.
xa: Mahadeva (**1261-1271**) was also defeated by the **Hoysalas**.
AP angle: **Rudrama beat Mahadeva**.
**Hemadri** served Mahadeva as **Shrikaranadhipa**.

n976b62bfe1d.s: Sarangapanideva, who later served at Rudramadevi's court, was the son of which Yadava ruler?
n976b62bfe1d.x: Singhana II's son Sarangapanideva served at Rudramadevi's court.
xa: **Jaitugi** killed Kakatiya **Rudradeva** and held **Ganapatideva** captive, releasing him in **1199**.
Singhana II's title: **'Teluguraya Sthapanacharya'** (installer of the Telugu king).
Yadava **Mahadeva**'s attack on the Kakatiyas was repulsed by **Rudramadevi**.
The **Paithan copper plate** of Ramachandra confirms Jaitugi killed Rudradeva.

nb43f49add06.s: The school at Patan for teaching Bhaskaracharya's works was established by:
nb43f49add06.x: Changadeva, an astronomer and grandson of Bhaskaracharya, established the school at Patan; Sarngadeva was associated with music.
xa: Sarngadeva wrote the **Sangita Ratnakara**.
⚠ **Sangita Ratnakara** = **Sarngadeva**; **Chaturvarga Chintamani** = **Hemadri**.
**Lilacharitra** (by **Mhaimbhat**) is the first Marathi prose work.

n120053f3681.s: The Sangita Ratnakara, a basic text of both Hindustani and Carnatic music, was written by:
n120053f3681.x: Sarngadeva, the court musician of Singhana II, wrote the Sangita Ratnakara.
xa: **Hemadri** — **Chaturvarga Chintamani** (APPSC G2 2000 key).
**Mhaimbhat** — **Lilacharitra**, the **first Marathi prose** work.
**Chakradhar Swami** founded the **Mahanubhava sect**.
Astronomer **Changadeva**, grandson of **Bhaskaracharya**, ran a school at **Patan**.

nefa4160ea73.s: Hemadri’s Chaturvarga Chintamani is best described as a Sanskrit work dealing with
o: dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas
nefa4160ea73.x: Chaturvarga Chintamani is a Sanskrit encyclopaedia dealing with dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas.
nefa4160ea73.tq: Identify the subject coverage of the named work.
xs: The **Chaturvarga Chintamani** is a **Sanskrit encyclopaedia** on **dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas**, so option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2000**).
Music was **Sarngadeva's** field (**Sangita Ratnakara**), and astronomy was **Changadeva's**.
xa: Its author **Hemadri** was a scholar, administrator and minister.
He served as **Shrikaranadhipa**.
He is credited with the **Hemadpanti** temple style.

nb23686dbe37.s: The Dnyaneshwari, written in 1290 at Nevasa, is a Marathi commentary on the:
nb23686dbe37.x: The Dnyaneshwari is a Marathi commentary on the Gita, written in 1290 at Nevasa in the reign of Ramachandra.
xa: Bhakti saints **Dnyaneshwar, Namdev**, later **Tukaram, Ramdas** took Gita ideas into Marathi.
The Yadavas encouraged **Marathi**; Sanskrit was the language of scholarship.
**Hemadri** served **Mahadeva and Ramachandra** as **Shrikaranadhipa**.
⚠ **Sangita Ratnakara** = **Sarngadeva**; **Chaturvarga Chintamani** = **Hemadri**.

ne69e6040677.s: Hemadri served as Shrikaranadhipa under which Yadava rulers?
ne69e6040677.x: Hemadri served Mahadeva and Ramachandra as Shrikaranadhipa, the head of the secretariat or records.
ne69e6040677.tq: Associate an office-holder with the rulers under whom he served.
xs: **Hemadri** served **Mahadeva and Ramachandra** as **Shrikaranadhipa**, head of the secretariat/records, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Singhana II's** court is linked with **Sarngadeva**, not Hemadri.
xa: Hemadri wrote the **Chaturvarga Chintamani** (**APPSC G2 2000**).
He is credited with the **Hemadpanti** style.
Mahadeva reigned **1261-1271**; Ramachandra **1271-1311**.

nbc750db8340.s: Which architectural style is traditionally credited to Hemadri?
nbc750db8340.x: Hemadri is credited with the Hemadpanti style of temple architecture.
nbc750db8340.tq: Match the architect-scholar with the architectural style.
xs: **Hemadri** is credited with the **Hemadpanti** style of temple architecture, so option **(4)** is correct (**APHQ**).
**Nagara**, **Vesara** and **Dravida** are the three broad temple styles. None is credited to Hemadri.
xa: Hemadpanti uses local **black basalt**.
Its dressed stones are **interlocked without mortar** (dry masonry).
Hemadri wrote the **Chaturvarga Chintamani**.

n78d315f757c.s: Hemadpanti architecture, using local black basalt with dressed stones interlocked without mortar, is described as:
n78d315f757c.x: Hemadpanti buildings interlocked dressed black basalt stones without mortar, a technique known as dry masonry.
xa: The style is credited to **Hemadri**, minister of the Devagiri Yadavas.
Hemadri served as **Shrikaranadhipa**.
He wrote the **Chaturvarga Chintamani**.

n8b3fe927df0.s: The last Yadava ruler Harapaladeva was killed during the invasion of:
n8b3fe927df0.x: Harapaladeva was killed in Mubarak Khalji's invasion of 1317-18; Shankaradeva died during Malik Kafur's invasion in 1313.
xa: Shankaradeva reigned **1311-1313**; Harapaladeva **1313-1317**.
The first invasion (**1295**) was by **Alauddin Khalji** for **Jalaluddin**.
Kafur's earlier **1307-08** campaign made **Ramachandra** submit.

n404db0ecfd7.s: In which year was the Yadava ruler Shankaradeva killed?
n404db0ecfd7.x: The sequence was the first invasion in 1295, Malik Kafur's campaign in 1307-08, Shankaradeva's death in 1313 and Harapaladeva's death in 1317-18.
xa: The 1295 invasion was the **first Muslim invasion of the South**.
In 1307-08 **Ramachandra** submitted and was taken to Delhi.
Devagiri was the first southern kingdom to fall, opening the road to **Warangal**, **Dwarasamudra** and **Madurai**.

n4ce9b68d82e.s: The importance of Devagiri in the expansion of the Delhi Sultanate lay in the fact that it
o: was the first southern kingdom to fall to Delhi and opened routes towards major southern kingdoms
prevented all further Delhi campaigns into the Deccan
was the first capital established by the Hoysalas in northern India
served as the original capital of the Kakatiyas
n4ce9b68d82e.x: Devagiri was the first southern kingdom to fall to Delhi, opening the road to Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai.
n4ce9b68d82e.tq: Apply the historical significance of a strategic conquest.
xs: **Devagiri** was the **first southern kingdom to fall to Delhi** and opened the road to **Warangal**, **Dwarasamudra** and **Madurai**, so option **(1)** is correct (**UPSC**).
Devagiri was the **Yadava** capital, founded by **Bhillama V**, not a Hoysala or Kakatiya capital.
xa: First raid: **1295**, by **Alauddin Khalji**.
After **1323**, Devagiri = the Sultanate's **Deccan base**.
**Malik Burhanuddin** was the vizier of Devagiri.

n9e2d3cf0466.s: One tradition names the progenitor of the Kakatiyas as Kakara Gundana of:
n9e2d3cf0466.x: The progenitor is identified either as Kakara Gundana of Magallu or as Venna Bhupati of Bayyaram.
xa: The Bayyaram inscription traces the line from **Durjaya**.
The **Bayyaram tank** inscription (**1219**), by **Mailamba**, gives the best genealogy of the early Kakatiyas.
First mention of the Kakatiyas = **Magallu 956**.

n6a5bc86de71.s: The early Kakatiyas were followers of Jainism who later became:
n6a5bc86de71.x: The early Kakatiyas were Jains who later became Shaivas (APPSC G2 2011); their sovereign phase ran from 1163 to 1323.
xa: Emblem: **Garuda** (Rashtrakuta phase) → **Varaha** (Kalyani Chalukya phase).
Clan deity **Kakatamma (Kakati Devi)** = the Jain **Kushmandini** absorbed into Hinduism.
**Telugu** replaced Sanskrit in inscriptions from **Ganapatideva's** reign.

n13bf68e2feb.s: ‘Kakati’ in the explanation of the Kakatiya clan deity is associated with which meaning?
n13bf68e2feb.x: Kakati means gourd. Kakatamma, or Kakati Devi, was associated with the Jain Kushmandini before being absorbed into Hindu tradition.
n13bf68e2feb.tq: Discriminate the exact etymological meaning from emblem and deity associations.
xs: **"Kakati"** means **gourd**, so option **(1)** is correct.
The clan deity **Kakatamma (Kakati Devi)** was the Jain **Kushmandini**, absorbed into Hinduism.
xa: The early Kakatiyas were **Jains** (**APPSC G2 2011**), later **Shaivas**.
The **Varaha** (boar) was their emblem in the Kalyani Chalukya phase.
The **Garuda** was their emblem in the Rashtrakuta phase.

n0fdd843157a.s: The early territorial base of the Kakatiyas was the:
n0fdd843157a.x: The early Kakatiya base was Hanamkonda Vishaya (modern Karimnagar, Warangal, Khammam); they served the Rashtrakutas first and then the Kalyani Chalukyas.
xa: ⚠ Another key answers **Eastern Chalukyas** — first mention in **Danarnava**'s **Magallu** grant.
Phases: **samanta 956-1162**, **sovereign 1163-1323**.
Emblem changed **Garuda → Varaha**.
Early Kakatiyas were **Jains** (APPSC G2 2011 key), later **Shaivas**.

n688f057ed28.s: Which change is associated with Prola I during the development of the Kakatiya polity?
o: The capital changed from Orugallu to Anumakonda.
The emblem changed from Varaha to Garuda.
The capital changed from Hanamkonda to Kanchi.
The emblem changed from Garuda to Varaha.
n688f057ed28.x: During Prola I’s period, the Kakatiya emblem changed from Garuda to Varaha.
n688f057ed28.tq: Discriminate between the two directions of an emblem change.
xs: Under **Prola I** the emblem changed from **Garuda to Varaha**, so option **(4)** is correct.
Option (2) reverses the change. Prola I also made **Anumakonda**, not Orugallu or Kanchi, the capital.
xa: Garuda belonged to the **Rashtrakuta** phase; Varaha to the **Kalyani Chalukya** phase.
Prola I served **Someshwara I** and **Vikramaditya VI**.

n2fa3961b40c.s: The Magallu grant of 956, containing the first mention of the Kakatiya family, was issued by the Eastern Chalukya ruler:
n2fa3961b40c.x: The Magallu grant of Eastern Chalukya Danarnava (956) first mentions the Kakatiya family through Gundyana.
xa: The Magallu grant names **Kakara Gundana** as progenitor; Bayyaram names **Venna**.
Phases: **Samanta 956-1162**, sovereign **1163-1323**.
First sovereign = **Rudradeva 1163**; last = **Prataparudra II**.

n7d8736db19a.s: Beta II was initiated into Saivism by Rameswara Pandita of which institution?
n7d8736db19a.x: Beta II was initiated into Saivism by Rameswara Pandita of the Srisailam Mallikarjuna matha.
n7d8736db19a.tq: Identify the religious teacher through the institution associated with him.
xs: **Beta II** was initiated into Saivism by **Rameswara Pandita** of the **Srisailam Mallikarjuna matha**, so option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC 2025**).
He gave his guru **Vaijanapalli**, as recorded in the **Thousand Pillar** inscription.
xa: Beta II ruled **1076-1108**.
His title was **Vikrama Chakri**.
**Mahadeva's** guru was **Dhruveshwara Pandita**.

ndf9a33a9cf9.s: Which Kakatiya ruler reigned from 1158 to 1195?
ndf9a33a9cf9.x: Rudradeva ruled 1158-1195, after Beta II (1076-1108) and Prola II (1116-1157), and before Mahadeva (1195-1199).
xa: **Ganapatideva** followed (**1199-1262**).
Then **Rudrama Devi** (**1262-1289**).
Last ruler: **Prataparudra II**.

n792c3c67dac.s: Which Kakatiya ruler completed the city of Orugallu and fully moved the court there?
n792c3c67dac.x: Rudradeva shifted the capital and began fortifying Orugallu; Ganapatideva completed the city and fully transferred the court there.
xa: The fortification became the **Warangal fort**.
Under Ganapatideva the city was called **Andhranagari**.
After **1323** it was **Sultanpur**.

n12189b782ea.s: The first inscription of Ganapatideva (26 December 1199) is found at:
n12189b782ea.x: Released from Yadava captivity in 1199, Ganapatideva issued his first inscription at Manthena; he later bore the title Andhra Deshadhiswara.
xa: General **Recherla Rudra** crushed revolts and installed him.
He married Pinnachodi's daughters **Narama and Perama**; their brother **Jayapa** became Gajasahani.
He ruled **1199-1262** (**63 years**), the greatest Kakatiya.
**Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (**1244**) protected foreign traders.

ncde45919207.s: 'Andhra Deshadhiswara' was the title of which Kakatiya ruler?
ncde45919207.x: Andhra Deshadhiswara was Ganapatideva's title; Chola Chamuvardhi was Beta I's, Vikrama Chakri Beta II's and Vinaya Vibhushanudu Rudradeva's.
xa: Rudradeva was also **Vidyabhushana**.
**Arigajakesari** = **Prola I**.
**Rayagajakesari** = **Rudramadevi**.

nap-history-3-17.s: According to the Musunuri inscription, how did Pratapa Rudra die?
o: He died while constructing a tank.
He died in a battle at Vijayapuri.
He died jumping into the Narmada.
nap-history-3-17.x: The Musunuri (Vilasa) record of the Musunuri Nayakas says Prataparudra, captured by the Delhi army, died by jumping into the Narmada on the way to Delhi.
nap-history-3-17.tq: Recall how the last Kakatiya king died.
n: Pratapa Rudra died by jumping into the Narmada. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xs: **Pratapa Rudra** **died by jumping into the Narmada** — option **(4)**.
The notes record that he died by jumping into the **Narmada**.
He was not killed at **Motupalli** or **Vijayapuri**; Motupalli is linked with **Ganapatideva**'s **1244** Abhaya Sasanam.
xa: **Motupalli** inscription protected foreign traders.
**Tripuranthakam** inscription records **Ambadeva**'s victories.
**Dharmasagar** inscription names the instrument **Jalakaranda** (APPSC 2019).
**Bayyaram tank** inscription of **Mailamba** (**1219**) gives the best early genealogy.

n9468177aa18.s: In which year did Ganapatideva and Choda Tikka of Nellore kill Prithviswara, ending the Velanati kingdom?
n9468177aa18.x: Prithviswara was killed in 1210, ending the Velanati kingdom, and both rulers took the title Prithviswara Shirakhandika Kreeda Vinoda.
xa: Final end of the Velanati Chodas: **Mummadi Rajendra Chola** killed in **1257**.
Prithviswara's **Pithapuram** inscription names **Kolleru Lake**.
General **Mutyalachaundaraya** took **Divi**.

n9c7074ad2b4.s: In 1257, Ganapatideva, allied with Akkana and Bayyana, killed which ruler, finally ending the Velanati Chodas?
n9c7074ad2b4.x: The 1257 alliance killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola, the final end of the Velanati Chodas; Tikkana dedicated his Nirvachanottara Ramayana to Manumasiddhi, not Ganapatideva.
xa: Ganapatideva restored **Manumasiddhi II** to the Nellore throne.
**Tikkana** went as envoy to seek his help.
**Akkana** and **Bayyana** were enemies of Manumasiddhi.

ncbec8be23c7.s: After the Battle of Muttukur (1263), Nellore fell to the:
ncbec8be23c7.x: The Pandyas defeated Ganapatideva at Muttukur in 1263, and Nellore fell to them.
xa: Despite this, he still held **coastal Andhra** firmly.
The battle is also spelt **Muthukuru**.
He had earlier restored **Manumasiddhi II** at Nellore.

n3b3ad3aff04.s: Ganapatideva restored which ruler to the Nellore throne after the poet Tikkana came to him as envoy?
n3b3ad3aff04.x: Ganapatideva restored Manumasiddhi II to the Nellore throne; Tikkana went to him as envoy.
xa: In **1210** Ganapati and **Choda Tikka** killed **Prithviswara** — end of the Velanati kingdom.
**1257**: killing of **Mummadi Rajendra Chola** = final end of the Velanati Chodas.
General **Mutyalachaundaraya** took **Divi** (from **1201**).
Tikkana dedicated his **Nirvachanottara Ramayana** to Manumasiddhi.

n918b40913a9.s: Rudrama Devi's training as successor to Ganapatideva was guided by her mother:
n918b40913a9.x: Her mother Kupama Devi guided her training; Mailamba was Ganapatideva's sister. Rudrama Devi ruled 1262-1289.
xa: Ganapati's daughters: **Rudramamba** (m. **Veerabhadra**) and **Ganapamba** (m. the **Kota** chief).
Sisters **Mailamba** and **Kundamamba** married sons of **Natavadi Buddharaja**.
Mailamba issued the **Bayyaram tank** inscription (**1219**).
Rudrama Devi was the **fourth independent ruler**.

nindian-history-149-2-17.s: Which of the following powers was NOT defeated by Rudrama Devi?
nindian-history-149-2-17.x: Rudrama Devi defeated the Pandyas, the Eastern Gangas and the Seunas of Devagiri; the Western Chalukyas had declined long before her reign.
n: Kakatiya Rudrama Devi defeated the Seuna rulers of Devagiri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149-2 · pp 260-261]
Rudrama Devi defeated the Pandyas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149-2 · pp 260-261]
Rudrama Devi defeated the Eastern Gangas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #149-2 · pp 260-261]
xa: She was the **daughter** of **Ganapati Dev** and the **fourth independent ruler**.
She was a **female ruler** who succeeded as **putrika**.
Her title **Rayagajakesari** is credited for her victory over the **Yadavas** (APPSC-GS 2018 key).
⚠ Another APPSC key (2017) gives **Rayagajakesari** to **Prataparudra**.

nced6cdf9c2d.s: After the conquest of 1323, the Kakatiya capital Orugallu was renamed:
nced6cdf9c2d.x: Orugallu was renamed Sultanpur after 1323; Andhranagari was a name used under Ganapatideva.
xa: **Prola II** developed Hanamkonda.
⚠ "Who shifted the capital to Orugallu?" → **Rudradeva**.
**Ganapatideva** completed Orugallu.

nfae2529bd8f.s: Prola I is associated with which combination of titles and achievement?
o: Arigajakesari; Samadhigata Panchamahasabda; construction of Kesamudram tank
Cholachamu Vari Pramathana; Vidyabhushana; construction of the Thousand Pillar Temple
Vidyabhushana; Kanchi Churakara; construction of Arikesari Samudram
Samadhigata Panchamahasabda; Rayagaja Kesari; construction of Ramappa temple
nfae2529bd8f.x: Prola I bore the titles Arigajakesari and Samadhigata Panchamahasabda and built Kesamudram tank.
nfae2529bd8f.tq: Start from the sure title and verify the achievement attached to the same ruler.
xs: **Prola I** bore the titles **Arigajakesari** and **Samadhigata Panchamahashabda** and built the **Kesamudram** tank, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Vidyabhushana** was **Rudradeva's** title, and **Rayagajakesari** was **Rudramadevi's**.
xa: ⚠ **Kesamudram** = Prola I; **Kesari Samudram** = Rudradeva; **Arikesari Samudram** = Prola II.
⚠ **APPSC 2025** treated "Prolaraja bore the title Arikesari" as **incorrect**.
Prola I made **Anumakonda** the capital (**1052-1076**).

n27e6e5665a4.s: Which set contains only works or grants of Ganapatideva's reign?
o: Arikesari Samudram, victory pillar at Srisailam and Betesvaralayam
Ramappa temple, Lakkavaram tank, Ghanapur tank and Ganapavaram villages
Thousand Pillar Temple, Kadalalaya Jainavasadi and Kesamudram tank
Kesamudram tank, Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya and Swayambhu temple
n27e6e5665a4.x: Ramappa temple, the Lakkavaram and Ghanapur tanks and the grant of Ganapavaram villages belong to Ganapatideva's reign.
xa: **Chouda Samudram** was built by **Malyala Chauda Senani**.
**Betesvaralayam** was built by **Beta II**.
Exam angle: match **tank → builder** and **ruler → temple**.

n96886416470.s: Recherla Rudra is associated with which combination?
o: Saving the kingdom during Ganapati’s captivity and constructing the Ramappa temple and tank at Palampet
Restoring Manumasiddhi II and serving as an envoy to the Pandyas
Building Chouda Samudram and making Garuda Beta a Chalukya vassal
Defeating Hoysala Ballala III and ruling the Nellore region
n96886416470.x: Recherla Rudra saved the kingdom during Ganapati’s captivity and is associated with the Ramappa temple and tank at Palampet.
n96886416470.tq: Start from the sure achievement and reject combinations assembled from different feudatories.
xs: **Recherla Rudra** saved the kingdom during **Ganapati's captivity** and built the **Ramappa** temple and tank at **Palampet**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Chouda Samudram** was **Malyala Chauda Senani's**, and **Kamasani** made Garuda Beta a vassal.
xa: His title was **'Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya'** (bearer of the Kakatiya realm's burden).
The **Palampet** inscription is dated **1213**.
He crushed revolts and installed **Ganapatideva**.

nd7046ab421d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Thousand Pillar inscription?
o: It records the Kakatiya declaration of independence.
It is also known as the Anumakonda inscription.
nd7046ab421d.x: The Thousand Pillar (Anumakonda) inscription of 1163 is associated with Rudradeva, not Ganapatideva.
xa: It was found by **J.S. Fleet** and composed by **Achitendru**.
⚠ The **APPSC 2025** key matched Anumakonda to **Prolaraja**, because it records Prola II's conquests.
The **Thousand Pillar (Rudreshwara)** temple was built by Rudradeva in **1163**.

nc90e0516e9f.s: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam of 1244 was issued by which Kakatiya ruler?
nc90e0516e9f.x: Ganapatideva, who ruled 63 years, issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam in 1244; the Ramappa temple was built in his reign by Recherla Rudra.
xa: His reign: **1199-1262**; title **Andhra Deshadhiswara**.
He granted the **Ganapavaram** villages.
He built the **Lakkavaram** and **Ghanapur** tanks.

ne10137169b2.s: The Kakatiya inscription referring to the Ramappa temple is the one at:
ne10137169b2.x: The Palampet inscription refers to the Ramappa temple; Sanigaram refers to Juddha Mallajinalaya, Dharmasagara to Jalakaranda and Pithapuram to Kolleru Lake.
xa: Pithapuram is a **Velanati** (Prithvisvara) record.
**Motupalli** (**1244**) = protection for foreign traders.
**Bayyaram** (**1219**) = best early genealogy.

n3f94f23780f.s: The title 'Kumara Rudradeva' was borne at his accession by:
n3f94f23780f.x: Kumara Rudradeva was the title borne by Prataparudra II at his accession.
xa: Prataparudra II was the **last** Kakatiya.
His commander **Pedarudru** defeated Hoysala **Ballala III** after **1316**.
An **APPSC 2017** key gives **Rayagajakesari** to **Prataparudra**.

n3ab291b82d1.s: Telugu replaced Sanskrit in Kakatiya inscriptions from the reign of:
n3ab291b82d1.x: Telugu replaced Sanskrit in Kakatiya inscriptions from Ganapatideva's reign, not Rudradeva's.
xa: The Kakatiyas left **1,000+** inscriptions.
**Ramappa temple (Palampet)** became a UNESCO site in **2021**.
First mention = **Magallu 956**; first sovereign = **Rudradeva 1163**.
Last ruler = **Prataparudra II**.

nap-history-3-25.s: The Kazipet inscription records the accession to the throne of:
nap-history-3-25.x: The Kazipet inscription, associated with Betha Raju II (Durgaraja), records Durga Nripathi coming to the throne.
n: The Kazipet inscription is associated with Betha Raju II and Durgaraja. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
Durga Nripathi ascended the throne. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xa: It also records **Durgaraja**'s donations to the **Betesvara** temple.
**Anumakonda** inscription (**1163**) of **Rudra Deva** declares independence; found by **J.S. Fleet**.
**Draksharama** inscription (**1158**) calls Rudra Deva **Vinaya Bhushan**.
APPSC 2025 key: Anumakonda = **Prolaraja**, Bayyaram = **Mailamba**.

n2ed9138dd68.s: Which commander of Prataparudra defeated the Hoysala Ballala III after 1316?
n2ed9138dd68.x: Prataparudra's commander Pedarudru defeated Ballala III after 1316; earlier, Veera Ballala II's advance had led Jaitugi to release Ganapatideva.
xa: **Jaitugi** killed **Rudradeva**; **Mahadeva** died in the revenge war.
The Yadava conflict began under **Prola II**.
**Velanati Chodas** killed **Prola II**; Rudradeva avenged him.
Rudradeva defeated the **Kalachuri** confederacy in **1159**.

n9aa20f69335.s: The Kakatiya conflict with the Yadavas (Sevunas) of Devagiri began in the reign of:
n9aa20f69335.x: The Yadava conflict began under Prola II, who was killed by the Velanati Chodas; Rudradeva defeated the Kalachuri confederacy in 1159.
xa: Prola II (**1116-1157**) set up a **victory pillar** at **Srisailam**.
He is credited with **Arikesari Samudram** and the **Swayambhu** temple.
Rudradeva made **Vellanki Gangadhara** viceroy of Sabbinadu.
Rudradeva declared **independence** in **1163**.

n1d1ce65e429.s: Which of the following was defeated by Rudradeva?
n1d1ce65e429.x: Rudradeva defeated the Telugu Chodas and Tailapa III. The Muttukur victory over Ganapatideva belonged to the Pandyas, while Ballala III was defeated later by Pedarudru.
n1d1ce65e429.tq: Find the option assigning a later or different ruler’s victory to Rudradeva.
xs: **Rudradeva** defeated the **Telugu Chodas** and **Tailapa III**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ballala III** was defeated by **Pedarudru** after **1316**, and the **Pandyas** defeated Ganapati at **Muttukur** (**1263**).
xa: Rudradeva defeated the **Kalachuri** confederacy (**Mailagi**, **Medaraja**, **Dommaraja**) in **1159**.
He avenged Prola II against the **Velanati Chodas**.
He declared independence in **1163**.

n3ea0643bdfc.s: The Kakatiya general Recherla Rudra bore the title:
n3ea0643bdfc.x: Recherla Rudra was Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya; Prasadaditya was Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya.
xa: Prasadaditya was also **'Raya Pitamahanka'**.
Kamasani (**Viriyala**) made **Garuda Beta** a Chalukya vassal.
**Malyala Gundiya** and **Viriyala Suri** backed **Rudrama**.

nf09b42f8978.s: Which family of Kakatiya feudatories is associated with Kamasani?
nf09b42f8978.x: Kamasani belonged to the Viriyala family and made Garuda Beta a Chalukya vassal, as recorded in the Gudur inscription.
nf09b42f8978.tq: Use the family–member association to separate the four feudatory groups.
xs: **Kamasani** belonged to the **Viriyala** family, so option **(3)** is correct.
She made **Garuda Beta** a Chalukya vassal (**Gudur** inscription).
xa: **Beta I** got **Anumakonda Vishaya** through his aunt **Viriyala Kamasani**.
**Viriyala Suri** backed **Rudrama**.
**Recherla** = Rudra; **Kayastha** = Prasadaditya; **Malyala** = Gundiya, Chauda Senani.

nap-history-6-22.s: In which year was the Rudreshwara (Thousand Pillar) Temple built by Rudradeva?
nap-history-6-22.x: The Rudreswara (Thousand Pillar) Temple is a Kakatiya temple built in 1163 CE by Rudradeva, also called Prataparudra I.
n: Rudreshwara Temple belongs to the Kakatiya Dynasty. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
Rudreshwara Temple was built in 1163 CE. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
Rudreshwara Temple was built by Rudradeva, also called Prataparudra I. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
xa: The **Thousand-Pillar Temple** is credited to **Rudra Deva**; one note credits **Prola II** — follow Rudradeva, **1163**.
**Ramappa Temple**, Palampet — **Recharla Rudra**, **1213 AD**.
**Swayambhu Devalayam** and **Kesavala** — **Prola Raju II**.
Rudradeva shifted the capital from **Hanamkonda** to **Orugallu** (APPSC G2 2019).

nindian-history-150-1.s: Which dynasty ruled the Eastern Deccan during the 12th–14th centuries CE?
nindian-history-150-1.x: The Kakatiyas ruled the eastern Deccan from Warangal in the 12th–14th centuries. The Seunas (Yadavas) ruled the western Deccan, and the Eastern Gangas ruled Odisha.
nindian-history-150-1.tq: Discriminate the eastern and western Deccan dynasties.
n: The Kakatiya dynasty was located in the Eastern Deccan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #150 · pp 261-261]
The Kakatiya dynasty existed during the 12th–14th centuries CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #150 · pp 261-261]
xs: The **Kakatiya Dynasty** ruled the **Eastern Deccan** in the **12th–14th centuries CE** — option **(3)**.
Their capital was **Warangal**.
The **Seuna / Yadava** dynasty ruled from **Devagiri** — they were the Kakatiyas' rivals.
xa: Rulers: **Rudradeva**, **Mahadeva**, **Ganapati Dev**, **Rudrama Devi**.
Rudrama Devi defeated the **Eastern Gangas** of **Orissa**.
The Kakatiyas were **Shudras** with **Sanskrit** as official language.
Clan deity: **Kakatamma (Kakati Devi)** = Jain **Kushmandini**.

nindian-history-150-20.s: Which Kakatiya ruler was also called Prataparudra I?
nindian-history-150-20.x: Rudradeva was also called Prataparudra I; Mahadeva came after him, and Ganapatideva was Rudrama Devi's father.
n: Rudradeva was also known as Pratap Rudradeva I. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #150 · pp 261-261]
Mahadeva came after Rudradeva. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #150 · pp 261-261]
Ganapati Dev was the father of Rudrama Devi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #150 · pp 261-261]
Rudrama Devi was the daughter of Ganapati Dev. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #150 · pp 261-261]
xa: Rudradeva (**1163-1195**) founded **Orugallu** and wrote **'Nitisara'**.
Mahadeva (**1195-1199**) died fighting the Yadavas; guru **Dhruveshwara Pandita**.
Ganapatideva ruled **1199-1262**.
Rudrama Devi ruled **1262-1289**.

n39cf31da630.s: Rudrama Devi, daughter of Ganapatideva, was married to the Chalukya prince:
n39cf31da630.x: Rudrama Devi married the Chalukya prince Veerabhadra; her daughter Rudramma married the Yadava prince Ellanadeva.
xa: Another daughter **Ruyyamma** married **Induluri Annayya**.
She ruled as **'Rudradeva Maharaja'** from **1258** (co-regency).
Royal guru: **Visveshwara Shivacharya** (Mandaram agrahara).
She was the second great woman ruler of medieval India after **Razia Sultana**.

n2a516e552f3.s: Rudrama Devi was trained from childhood as a son, a practice referred to by which term?
n2a516e552f3.x: Rudrama Devi was groomed as a son under the putrika tradition and trained in war and administration.
n2a516e552f3.tq: Test the exact technical term rather than its broad meaning.
xs: Rudrama was groomed from childhood as a son, a **putrika**, so option **(2)** is correct.
Her training covered **war**, **statecraft** and **administration**.
**Nayankara** was the military-fief system. **Samanta** means feudatory, and **agrahara** was a Brahmin settlement (her guru's Mandaram agrahara).
xa: She ruled under the male regnal name **'Rudradeva Maharaja'**.
Her mother **Kupama Devi** guided her training.
She later trained her grandson **Prataparudra II** for the throne.

ne669af0e0bc.s: In which year did Rudrama Devi begin ruling as Rudradeva Maharaja under co-regency with Ganapatideva?
ne669af0e0bc.x: Rudrama began co-regency in 1258; the 1266 Tripurantakam inscription still called her a vassal, and she was fully crowned after Ganapatideva's death in 1262.
xa: She ruled **1262-1289**, about **26 years**.
Her royal styles: **Maharaja**, **Parameshwara**, **Tirthakrit**.
⚠ A different Tripurantakam inscription records **Ambadeva's** victories.

nd66e92f2a1d.s: Prataparudra II, crowned in 1289, was Rudrama Devi's grandson through her daughter:
nd66e92f2a1d.x: Prataparudra II was Rudrama Devi's grandson through Mummadamma; she trained him and he was crowned in 1289.
xa: His title at accession: **'Kumara Rudradeva'**.
Early revolts: Ambadeva's son **Tripurari II**.

n789dceb2b2c.s: Rudrama Devi ruled under which of the following male regnal names?
n789dceb2b2c.x: Rudradeva Maharaja was the male regnal name under which Rudrama Devi ruled as a monarch in her own right.
n789dceb2b2c.tq: Use the exact title–ruler association and distinguish a regnal name from an honorific title.
xs: Rudrama Devi ruled as **'Rudradeva Maharaja'** — so option **(3)** is correct; she ruled as a monarch in her own right.
**Andhra Deshadhiswara** was **Ganapatideva's** title; **Ravaddar Dev** was **Amir Khusrau's** name for **Prataparudra II**.
xa: She ruled as Rudradeva Maharaja from **1258** in co-regency; full reign **1262-1289**, about **26 years**.
She was groomed from childhood as a son (**putrika**) in war, statecraft and administration.
Her title **Rayagajakesari** commemorates her victory over the **Yadavas of Devagiri**.
**Prataparudra II** took the title **'Kumara Rudradeva'** on his coronation in **1289**.

n10f096b2c4d.s: The title 'Rayagajakesari', for a victory over the Yadavas of Devagiri, is associated with:
n10f096b2c4d.x: APPSC keys (GS 2018, G2 2017) give Rayagajakesari to Rudrama Devi for repulsing the Yadavas; one PYQ book key gives it to Prataparudra. Prola I was Arigajakesari and Ganapatideva Andhra Deshadhiswara.
xa: ⚠ Trap: one AP History PYQ book key gives Rayagajakesari to **Prataparudra** — read the options; answer **Rudramadevi**.
Rudrama also ruled under the male regnal name **Rudradeva Maharaja**.
Royal styles: **Maharaja**, **Parameshwara**, **Tirthakrit**.

n4b01a725e68.s: Vengi, occupied by Ganga Narasimhadeva in 1262, was recovered by the Kakatiyas in:
n4b01a725e68.x: Vengi was recovered in 1278 after Poti Nayaka and Prolinayaka defeated Virabhanudeva.
xa: Yadava **Mahadeva** attacked and was repulsed.
**Ambadeva** became head of the **Kadapa region** in **1272**, then revolted.
After **Muttukur** (**1263**), **Nellore** was under the Pandyas.

n500f77eb65c.s: The Yadava ruler who invaded Rudrama Devi’s kingdom was:
n500f77eb65c.x: Yadava Mahadeva attacked Rudrama Devi, but she repulsed the invasion.
n500f77eb65c.tq: Distinguish the named invader from other rulers of the Yadava line.
xs: The Yadava **Mahadeva** attacked Rudrama's kingdom and was **repulsed**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ramachandra** later fell to Delhi, and **Singhana II** and **Bhillama V** belong to earlier reigns.
xa: The victory is commemorated by her title **Rayagajakesari** (**APPSC-GS 2018**).
⚠ One key gives Rayagajakesari to **Prataparudra**. Answer **Rudramadevi**, but read the options.
Rudrama married her daughter **Rudramma** to the Yadava prince **Ellanadeva**.

n5fbae372409.s: During Prataparudra's campaigns, Ranganatha of Nellore, a Pandya ally, was replaced by:
n5fbae372409.x: Ranganatha of Nellore was replaced by Manuma Gandapalu; Ambadeva's principality was annexed and Gonavithala pushed towards Devagiri.
xa: Early revolts: **Kayastha**, **Velama** and **Reddy** factions.
Ambadeva's son **Tripurari II** also revolted.
Ambadeva had killed **Rudrama** in **1289**.

nap-history-29-11.x: Kumaragiri Reddy succeeded Anavema Reddy; among the Kakatiyas, Rudra Deva came after Prola Raju II and Mahadeva succeeded Rudra Deva.
n: Rudra Deva succeeded Praia Raju. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 40-41]
Mahadeva succeeded Rudra Deva. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 40-41]
Kumaragiri Reddy succeeded Anavema Reddy. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 40-41]
Durga Nripathi succeeded his father Betha Raju II. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 40-41]
xa: Rudra Deva ascended in **1158**; Mahadeva in **1196**.
Kumaragiri Reddy ascended in **1386**.
**Rudramadevi** (**Rudramba**) ascended in **1260**.
**Pratapa Rudra** ascended in **1296**.

n60a87b356af.s: Rudrama Devi is regarded as the second great woman ruler of medieval India after:
n60a87b356af.x: Rudrama Devi is regarded as the second great woman ruler of medieval India after Razia Sultana.
n60a87b356af.tq: Directly test the comparative historical designation attached to the ruler.
xs: Rudrama Devi is the **second great woman ruler of medieval India** after **Razia Sultana**, so option **(3)** is correct.
She was a woman monarch in her own right, ruling as **'Rudradeva Maharaja'**.
xa: **Marco Polo** described her as a woman ruler of **martial ability**.
That is the **first foreign reference** to a female ruler in India (**APHQ**).
She is the leading example of a woman monarch in **medieval South India**.

n445269adcc8.s: Rudrama Devi was killed in 1289 while fighting the rebel:
n445269adcc8.x: She died in 1289 fighting Kayastha Ambadeva, with Mallikarjuna Nayaka as her general; her servant Puvvula Mummadi set up the Chandupatla inscription.
xa: ⚠ **Tripurantakam** = Ambadeva's victories; **Chandupatla** = Rudrama's death.
Chandupatla is in **Nalgonda district**.
Ambadeva had been made head of the **Kadapa region** in **1272**.

na604131785c.s: Marco Polo was a traveller belonging to which country or region?
na604131785c.x: Marco Polo was a Venetian traveller who visited the eastern coast during Rudramadevi’s reign.
na604131785c.tq: Use the traveller’s identity as a direct name–origin association.
xs: **Marco Polo** was a **Venetian** traveller, from **Venice**, so option **(3)** is correct.
His work is **Il Milione / The Travels**.
xa: He landed at **Motupalli (Mutfili)** port.
He travelled **1271-1295** and reached the Coromandel coast in **1292**.
Exam keys place his visit in **Rudramadevi's reign** (**APPSC G2 2011**).

na3c157838a2.s: Marco Polo’s Motupalli is identified with:
na3c157838a2.x: Motupalli, also written as Mutfili, was the port visited by Marco Polo on the Coromandel Coast.
na3c157838a2.tq: Resolve the alternate-name pair for the port.
xs: Marco Polo landed at **Motupalli**, i.e. **Mutfili** port, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Tripurantakam**, **Nellore** and **Devagiri** are unrelated places.
xa: Exam keys place his visit in **Rudramadevi's reign** (**APPSC G2 2011**).
He noted **flourishing sea trade** with **no oppressive taxes** on merchants.
He also mentioned **diamond mines** in the **Golconda** region.

nd50979f44be.s: According to Marco Polo, the local grain of the Kakatiya realm was:
nd50979f44be.x: Marco Polo noted rice as the local grain, along with sea trade, fine textiles and diamonds, and said merchants were not oppressively taxed.
xa: He mentioned **diamond mines** in the **Golconda** region.
He noted a **hot climate**, with people wearing loincloths.
He described a strict, efficient **administration** and prosperity.

nfe80ba3b942.s: The Venetian traveller Marco Polo visited the Kakatiya kingdom during the reign of:
nfe80ba3b942.x: The APPSC G2 2011 key places Marco Polo's visit (landing at Motupalli) in Rudramadevi's reign; he reached the Coromandel coast in 1292, at the very end of her reign or just after.
xa: Marco Polo travelled **1271-1295**.
He described a **woman ruler** of martial ability.
Rudrama ruled **1262-1289**.

n6f2b29f5939.s: Which title was associated with Prataparudra before or in connection with his accession?
n6f2b29f5939.x: Prataparudra was associated with the title ‘Kumara Rudradeva’.
n6f2b29f5939.tq: Separate the ruler’s title from titles and names used by other figures in the period.
xs: **Prataparudra II** was crowned in **1289** with the title **'Kumara Rudradeva'**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Ravaddar Dev** was the name **Amir Khusrau** used for him in wartime. **Rayagajakesari** is Rudrama's title, and **Ulugh Khan** was his captor.
xa: He was Rudrama's grandson through **Mummadamma**.
His prime minister was **Muppidi Nayudu**.

n85991b7091e.s: Under the Nayankara system, the kingdom was organised into principalities held by:
n85991b7091e.x: The Nayankara system assigned principalities and forts to military officers known as Nayakas, who maintained troops and paid fixed tribute.
n85991b7091e.tq: Infer the institutional role from the system’s military and administrative structure.
xs: Under the **Nayankara** system, principalities were held by **military officers (Nayakas)**, so option **(2)** is correct.
Each Nayaka held a **fort**, kept **troops** and paid a **fixed tribute**.
xa: Prataparudra reorganised the kingdom into **72 Nayankaras**; other notes say **75 (or 77)**.
About **one-fourth of the land** was under the Nayakas.
Later forms: Vijayanagara's **Amara Nayankara** (Amaranayakas), then the **Poligars**.

n6fbae187227.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the institutional succession mentioned in relation to the Nayankara system?
o: Nayankara system → Vijayanagara Amaranayakas → later Poligars
Later Poligars → Nayankara system → Vijayanagara Amaranayakas
Vijayanagara Amaranayakas → later Poligars → Nayankara system
Nayankara system → later Poligars → Vijayanagara Amaranayakas
n6fbae187227.x: The comparative sequence is the Nayankara system, followed by the Vijayanagara Amaranayakas and later the Poligars.
n6fbae187227.tq: Identify the initial institutional form and follow the stated progression to its later forms.
xs: The succession runs **Nayankara system → Vijayanagara Amaranayakas → later Poligars** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Prataparudra II** reorganised the kingdom into **72 Nayankaras** (other notes: **75** or **77**), each Nayaka holding a **fort**.
xa: Nayakas kept troops and paid a **fixed tribute**; **one-fourth of the land** was under them.
Vijayanagara continued it as the **Amara Nayankara** system.
Some notes say **Rudrama Devi** introduced the Nayankara system in her father's time.

n32b83a1434c.s: The first attack on Orugallu in 1303 was repulsed at Upparapalli by:
n32b83a1434c.x: The 1303 expedition was defeated at Upparapalli by Pothuganti Aili and Recherla Venna.
n32b83a1434c.tq: Match the military outcome with the correct local commanders.
xs: The **1303** attack was repulsed at **Upparapalli** by **Pothuganti Aili** and **Recherla Venna**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Kolanu Munumagammayya** and **Induluri Annayya** won at Tripurantakam (**1291**), and **Gonavithala** fought the Yadavas.
xa: The commander was **Malik Fakhruddin Juna**, under **Alauddin Khalji**.
"First Muslim attack on Orugallu" → **1303** (**APPSC 2012**).
Alauddin's **1294/1295** raid hit the **Yadavas**, not Andhra.

n93ccf5100f3.s: The second Khalji invasion of Warangal (1309-10) was led by:
n93ccf5100f3.x: Malik Kafur led the 1309-10 invasion; Prataparudra submitted, paid a large tribute and accepted Delhi's overlordship.
xa: **Amir Khusrau** accompanied the campaign.
His **Khazain-ul-Futuh** describes the **double-walled fort with a moat**.
In **1311** Prataparudra's forces joined Kafur's march on **Madurai**.

n7af0c68d0d8.s: In 1311, Prataparudra's forces joined Malik Kafur's march on Madurai under the command of:
n7af0c68d0d8.x: Prataparudra's forces under Muppidi Nayaka joined Malik Kafur's march on Madurai in 1311; after Alauddin's death in 1316 he stopped paying tribute.
xa: The first attack on Orugallu was in **1303**.
The stopped tribute drew the **1318** expedition of **Khusrau Khan**.
Kafur's Warangal campaign was in **1309-10**.

n57362b54795.s: After the Tughlaq conquest of Orugallu in 1323, who was placed in charge of Andhra?
n57362b54795.x: After the 1321-22 and 1323 invasions, Orugallu was renamed Sultanpur and Malik Burhanuddin was placed in charge of Andhra.
xa: **Ulugh Khan** and **Juna Khan** are the same man, the future **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**.
**Malik Maqbul** (the converted **Jagannatha Pandit**) was stationed at Warangal.
The **1323** siege lasted **5 months**.

n6831c0ff573.s: Which event directly weakened the Kakatiya resistance during the 1323 siege of Orugallu?
o: The revolt of Harihara and Murari
The occupation of Vengi by Ganga Narasimhadeva
n6831c0ff573.x: Bobbareddi’s desertion or withdrawal of forces during the battle weakened the Kakatiya defence and contributed to the surrender of Prataparudra.
n6831c0ff573.tq: Identify the immediate military cause from among events belonging to different periods.
xs: **Bobbareddi's desertion**, withdrawing his forces mid-battle, weakened the **1323** defence, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Harihara and Murari's** revolt and **Narasimhadeva's** occupation of Vengi belong to Rudrama's reign. **Ganapatideva** died long before.
xa: After **5 months**, Prataparudra surrendered and was **captured**.
Causes of the fall: **southern disunity**, **weak cavalry**, **internal betrayal**, exhaustion from raids.
Of **75** generals, **Prolaya Nayaka**, **Racherla Singama** and **Prolaya Vema** survived and led the liberation.

nbbedc87ad8a.s: According to the Vilasa copper plate, the captured Prataparudra drowned himself in the river:
nbbedc87ad8a.x: Prataparudra surrendered in 1323 and, while being taken towards Delhi, drowned himself; the Vilasa record names the Narmada (another account names the Kaveri).
xa: He was held captive by **Ulugh Khan**.
Orugallu was renamed **Sultanpur (Sultanpurti)**.
The fall opened the **Musunuri**-led liberation movement.

nea1be2084e5.s: Which one of the following was NOT mentioned as a cause of the fall of the Kakatiya kingdom?
o: A prolonged maritime blockade by European powers
nea1be2084e5.x: The stated causes were disunity among southern kingdoms, weak cavalry, betrayal by chiefs and exhaustion caused by repeated raids. A maritime blockade by European powers was not a cause.
nea1be2084e5.tq: Find the anachronistic option while retaining the causes that directly weakened the kingdom.
xs: A **maritime blockade by European powers** is not among the causes, so option **(3)** is the answer.
The causes given: **disunity** of southern kingdoms, **weak cavalry**, **betrayal by chiefs** (Bobbareddi) and **exhaustion** from repeated raids.
xa: The fall of Warangal (**1323**) ended the Kakatiyas.
The **Musunuri** and **Reddi** states rose from the liberation movement.
Andhra was placed under **Malik Burhanuddin**.

n55f2fd95a39.s: After the fall of Warangal in 1323, the Kakatiya ruler Prataparudra II was held captive by
n55f2fd95a39.x: Ulugh Khan (Juna Khan, later Muhammad bin Tughlaq) took Prataparudra captive after the 1323 siege (APPSC G2 2019 key). Malik Kafur led the 1309-10 invasion for Alauddin Khalji, and Khusrau Khan led the 1318 expedition; none of them captured him.
n55f2fd95a39.tq: Captor of Prataparudra = Ulugh Khan, not Malik Kafur or Alauddin.
xs: After the **1323** fall, Prataparudra II was held captive by **Ulugh Khan** (Juna Khan, later **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**), so option **(3)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2019**).
**Malik Kafur** led the **1309-10** invasion for **Alauddin Khalji**, and **Khusrau Khan** the **1318** one. None of them captured him.
xa: He died on the way to Delhi in the **Narmada** (**Vilasa** copper plate).
**Bobbareddi's** desertion weakened the final defence.
He was the **last Kakatiya ruler**.

n639a958ec96.s: Prataparudra Yashobhushanam, a Sanskrit treatise on alankara, was written by Prataparudra II's court poet
n639a958ec96.x: Vidyanatha, court poet of Prataparudra II, wrote Prataparudra Yashobhushanam (APPSC G2 2011 key). Agastya wrote Nalakirtikaumudi, Balabharata and Krishnacharita. Ekamranatha wrote Prataparudra Charitramu. Sakalya Malla was a court poet, but he is not credited with this work.
xs: **Vidyanatha**, Prataparudra II's court poet, wrote the **Prataparudra Yashobhushanam**, so option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2011**).
**Agastya** wrote Nalakirtikaumudi and Balabharata, **Ekamranatha** wrote Prataparudra Charitramu, and **Sakalya Malla's** works are not named.
xa: ⚠ **Prataparudra Yashobhushanam** = Vidyanatha; **Prataparudra Charitramu** = Ekamranatha.
Ekamranatha's work records Kakatiya traditions such as the **Jaitugi-Ganapati** marriage.
**Gangadevi's Madhura Vijayam** describes post-conquest hardships.

nbed73ba39d5.s: Khazain-ul-Futuh, describing Malik Kafur's 1310 siege of Warangal, was written by:
nbed73ba39d5.x: Amir Khusrau wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh, describing the double-walled Warangal fort with a moat; he called Prataparudra 'Ravaddar Dev'.
xa: Khazain-ul-Futuh also mentions **diamonds**.
**Barani's Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** covers Delhi's southern campaigns.
**Gangadevi's Madhura Vijayam** describes post-conquest hardships.

n4bf62b35678.s: Which source is associated with the Kakatiya traditions concerning the marriage of Jaitugi and Ganapati?
n4bf62b35678.x: Ekamranatha’s Prataparudra Charitramu records Kakatiya traditions, including the Jaitugi–Ganapati marriage.
n4bf62b35678.tq: Match the source with its specific historical use.
xs: The Jaitugi–Ganapati marriage tradition is recorded in **Prataparudra Charitramu** of **Ekamranatha** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Khazain-ul-Futuh** is **Amir Khusrau's** account of **Malik Kafur's 1310 siege** of Warangal.
**Madhura Vijayam** of **Gangadevi** describes the **post-conquest** hardships; **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** of **Barani** covers Delhi's southern campaigns.
xa: ⚠ **Prataparudra Charitramu** = **Ekamranatha**; **Prataparudra Yashobhushanam** = **Vidyanatha**, a Sanskrit alankara treatise.
**Siddheswara Charitra** of **Kase Siddhappa** throws light on socio-economic and religious life.
**Agastya** wrote **Nalakirtikaumudi**, **Balabharata** and **Krishnacharita**.

n3dc4632f1ea.s: The Kakatiya Ayagar system of village administration consisted of how many functionaries?
n3dc4632f1ea.x: The Ayagars were twelve village functionaries (APPSC G2 2012), paid by shares of produce and service lands.
xa: Ayagars were paid by **shares of produce and service lands**.
Village officers: **Karanam** (accountant), **Reddi** (headman), **Talari** (watchman/police).
The **72 Niyogas** worked under the **Bahattara Niyogadhipati** (Shivadevayya's **Purushartha Saram**).

ne9ee35aac7f.s: In the Kakatiya village, the Talari was the:
ne9ee35aac7f.x: The Talari was the village watchman; the Karanam was the accountant and tolls were collected by the Sunkadhikari/Sunkamanya.
xa: ⚠ **Karanam** = village accountant; **Sthalakaranam** = accountant of a **Sthala**; **Kayastha** = scribes; **Pradvivaka** = judicial adviser.
**Ayagarlu**, **twelve (12)** village functionaries, enjoyed land **without any cess or tax**.
**Arigapulu** were the **farmers who paid taxes**.
⚠ **Ayagars** = **Twelve** (village); **Niyogas** = **72** (central departments under the **Bahattara Niyogadhipati**).

nf9d5943da92.s: The 72 central departments under the Kakatiyas were known as Niyogas and were placed under the:
nf9d5943da92.x: The central departments were called 72 Niyogas and were supervised by the Bahattara Niyogadhipati.
nf9d5943da92.tq: Link the distinctive number with the corresponding supervising authority.
xs: The **72 Niyogas** were placed under the **Bahattara Niyogadhipati** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Naduvizhupati** headed a **Nadu**; **Parupathyam Garu** headed a **Sthala**; **Pradvivaka** was the judicial adviser.
xa: The source for the 72 Niyogas is Shivadevayya's **Purushartha Saram**.
⚠ **72 Niyogas** (central departments) vs **twelve Ayagars** (village) vs **72 Nayankaras** (forts).
Council: **Pradhani**, **Pragada**, **Amatya**, **Mantri**, **Senadhipati**.

n4e685160f30.s: The Nayankara system in its reorganised Kakatiya form is principally associated with which ruler?
n4e685160f30.x: Prataparudra II is identified with the introduction or reorganisation of the Nayankara system in the Kakatiya kingdom.
n4e685160f30.tq: Use the ruler–administrative reform association without confusing earlier Kakatiya rulers.
xs: The reorganised Nayankara system is credited to **Prataparudra II** (**APPSC 2025** key) — option **(1)** is correct.
Other notes say **Rudrama Devi** began it in **Ganapatideva's** time and Prataparudra strengthened it — but the exam answer is Prataparudra II.
**Prolaya Vemareddy** was one of the generals who survived **1323**, not the system's author.
xa: The kingdom was reorganised into **72 Nayankaras**, each guarding a fort (other notes: **75** or **77**).
Sources: Baddena's **Neeti Sastra Muktavali** and Ekamranatha's **Pratapa Charitra**.
Vijayanagara continued it as the **Amara-Nayankara** system; its break-up produced the **Poligars**.

n04e825dcfb0.s: Under the Kakatiya Nayankara system, villages given to Nayakas instead of a salary were called:
n04e825dcfb0.x: Nayakas received Nayakasthalam villages in lieu of salary, maintained a fixed army for the king, paid a fixed annual sum and remitted the rest.
xa: Nayankaras controlled **one-fourth (1/4)** of the kingdom's land.
**Prataparudra II** introduced the system (APPSC **2025** key); other notes say **Rudrama Devi** began it.
Number: **72 Nayankaras**, each guarding a **fort**; other notes say **75 (or 77)**.
Sources: Baddena's **Neeti Sastra Muktavali** and Ekamranatha's **Pratapa Charitra**.
Vijayanagara continued it as **Amara Nayankara** (land = **Amaram**, tribute = **Kappam**); its break-up led to **Poligars**.

n32884c33752.s: Under the Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara system, the land assigned to a nayaka was called:
n32884c33752.x: The land was Amaram and the tribute was Kappam or Kist; the break-up of the system produced the Poligars.
xa: Sequence: **Nayankara** (Kakatiya) → **Amaranayaka** (Vijayanagara) → **Poligars**.
The Nayankara system was reorganised by **Prataparudra II** (APPSC 2025 key).
Kakatiya Nayakas held villages called **Nayakasthalam** instead of salary.

nc654ddc4e2c.s: The Pratapa Charitra, a source for the Nayankara system, was written by:
nc654ddc4e2c.x: Ekamranatha wrote the Pratapa Charitra and Baddena the Neeti Sastra Muktavali, both sources on the Nayankara system; Shivadevayya's Purushartha Saram informs on the 72 Niyogas.
xa: **Palnati Veeracharitra** records **1,500 painters' houses** in Orugallu.
The **Tripurantakam inscription (1282)** records the **Virabanajam** licence for Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda.
The **Porumamilla** tank inscription (**1369**) lists the **12 requisites of a good tank**.

n7227af66044.s: According to one account, how many Nayankaras were there in the Kakatiya kingdom?
n7227af66044.x: One account gives 72 Nayankaras, each guarding a fort; together they controlled one-fourth of the kingdom's land.
xa: The villages held by Nayakas were called **Nayakasthalam**.
Fort types: **Giridurga** (hill), **Jaladurga** (water), **Vanadurga** (forest), **Sthaladurga** (plain).
The Warangal fort had **concentric walls and a moat**.

nb5fddaa7cc0.s: Who was the prime minister of the Kakatiya ruler Ganapatideva?
nb5fddaa7cc0.x: Malyala Hemadri Reddi was Ganapatideva's prime minister; Muppidi Nayudu was prime minister under Prataparudra.
xa: **Jayapa Senani** was **Gaja Sahini** (elephant corps head) under **Ganapatideva**.
⚠ **Gaja Sahini** = elephants (**Jayapa Senani**); **Ashwa Sahini** = cavalry (**Gangaya Sahini**).
Most scholars call the Kakatiya state a **"decentralised monarchy"**; **Romila Thapar** — **"metropolitan state"**; **Burton Stein** — segmentary state.
**Padmanayakas** were **Recherla Velama** chiefs, later founders of the Velama kingdom.

nc8289ac3201.s: Which one of the following best describes the Nayankara system?
o: Military commanders were made administrators of Sthalas or Mandalams and were assigned responsibility for forts.
Temple authorities collected all taxes and maintained the royal army.
Civil scribes were appointed as village accountants without military duties.
Merchants were granted exclusive control over provincial administration.
nc8289ac3201.x: Under the Nayankara system, military commanders served as administrators of Sthalas or Mandalams and protected specified forts.
nc8289ac3201.tq: Identify the institutional arrangement from the roles performed by the Nayakas.
xs: Under the Nayankara system, **military commanders (Nayakas)** were made **administrators of Sthalas/Mandalams**, each protecting a **fort** — option **(1)** is correct.
It joined land control to military duty; temples, scribes and merchants had no such role in it.
xa: Nayakas received villages called **Nayakasthalam** in place of salary.
The Nayankaras controlled **one-fourth (1/4)** of the kingdom's land.
The system is compared to the Mughal **jagir**, which also linked land with military duty.

n9c7b18a8904.s: In the Kakatiya army, 'Mula Balam' was:
o: the contingents maintained by the Nayakas
the four arms of the army
n9c7b18a8904.x: Mula Balam was the king's own standing army; the Nayakas' contingents formed the separate Nayankara army and chaturanga bala meant the four arms.
xa: Prataparudra's army: **100 elephants**, **20,000 cavalry**, **900,000 infantry**.
Fort types: **Giridurga** (hill), **Jaladurga** (water), **Vanadurga** (forest), **Sthaladurga** (plain).
⚠ **Mula Balam** = king's army; **Nayankara army** = Nayakas' contingents.

nfda6dcc9b94.s: In Kakatiya central administration, the Kayasthas were:
nfda6dcc9b94.x: The Kayasthas were scribes (APPSC 2012); the Pradvivaka advised the king on the judicial system.
xa: Most scholars call it a **"decentralised monarchy"**; **Burton Stein** compared it to a **segmentary state**.
**Sthalakaranam** = accountant of a Sthala; **Kolagadu** = measurer of grain sold in markets.
Central departments: **72 Niyogas** under the **Bahattara Niyogadhipati**.

n16564b8e449.s: In Kakatiya military terminology, a 'Giridurga' was a:
n16564b8e449.x: Giridurga was a hill fort (Jaladurga water, Vanadurga forest, Sthaladurga plain); the Warangal fort had concentric walls and a moat.
xa: Other fort types: **Jaladurga** (water), **Vanadurga** (forest), **Sthaladurga** (plain).
The army had **two divisions**: **Mula Balam** (king's standing army) and the **Nayankara army**.
Each of the **72 Nayankaras** guarded a specific **fort**.

ne3304825f8a.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Magani from Metta?
o: Magani was irrigated wet land, whereas Metta was rain-fed dry land.
Magani was rain-fed dry land, whereas Metta was irrigated wet land.
Both terms denoted newly cultivated forest land.
ne3304825f8a.x: Magani denoted irrigated wet land, generally used for food crops, while Metta denoted rain-fed dry land.
ne3304825f8a.tq: Test the reversed meaning of two similar land-classification terms.
xs: **Magani** was **irrigated wet land** (food crops) and **Metta** was **rain-fed dry land** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Thotapolam** was garden land and **Podu** newly cultivated land — neither Magani nor Metta.
xa: Metta was also called **Velipolam**.
⚠ **Koru** = tax on wet (**Magani**) land; **Putti Pahindi** = tax on dry land.
Land revenue (**Ari**) was generally **1/6** of produce.

n51513d4d43b.s: Which of the following crops was NOT grown in the Kakatiya period?
n51513d4d43b.x: Maize reached India only after 1500; betel, rice, sugarcane and cotton were among Kakatiya crops.
xa: Land classes: **Magani** (irrigated wet), **Metta / Velipolam** (rain-fed dry), **Thotapolam** (garden), **Podu** (newly cultivated).
A **fragrant rice** variety grew near **Orugallu**.
Fruits: **coconut, mango, banana, guava**.
Other new villages: **Ghanpur, Mahadevapur, Rudravaram, Muppavaram**.

n29eaa9329e8.s: Kakatiya land revenue (Ari or bhaga) was generally what share of the produce?
n29eaa9329e8.x: Land revenue was generally one-sixth of the produce; Koru was the cess on wet (Magani) land and Putti on dry land.
xa: Tax-paying farmers were called **Arigapulu**.
**Pullari** = tax on **grass** (grazing); **Adhi** = land cess.
**Exempt:** **temple lands, Brahmin grants, Ayagar lands**; **Dashabandhamu** = tax-free land for tank upkeep.
⚠ Other notes call the dry-land tax **Putti Pahindi** and spell land revenue **Ari**.

ne08410c6cef.x: Pellipannu was the wedding tax; Angadi Sunkam was the weekly-market tax, Dari Sunkam a road toll and Kanika a customary gift.
xa: **Sunkam** = customs/tolls, collected by **Sunkamanya Garlu**.
**Alam** = tax on vegetables / produce.
Other sunkams: **Burra, Madiga, Gandi, Revu**.
Other agricultural levies: **Siddhayam, Sangam, Pannu, Darshanam, Niruvidi, Ardhayam**.

n9a8215e8f4c.s: According to the Palnati Veeracharitra, Orugallu had about how many painters' houses?
n9a8215e8f4c.x: The Palnati Veeracharitra mentions about 1,500 painters' houses in Orugallu; Machaladevi was a woman painter of the time.
xa: **Warangal** was famed for **carpets/rugs**; **Ratna kambalu** (diamond blankets) and **Mukkul vastralu** were made there.
Iron — **Guthikonda and Palnadu**; knives — **Nirmal**.
**Diamonds** came from the **Golconda** region (noted by Marco Polo).

n5859bf05bd7.s: In the Kakatiya period, the head of a merchant guild was called:
n5859bf05bd7.x: The guild head was Setti or Sreshthi; a merchant was a Behari and trade was Vyavaharam.
xa: **Samayas** were caste/occupational groups (APPSC G2 2019 key) that allowed **caste mobility**.
The Kakatiyas were themselves **Shudras**; Cynthia Talbot called it the **"Golden Age of the Shudras"**.
**Chitrameli** was the samaya of agricultural farmers.

n2e88f90a900.s: Under the Kakatiyas, ports that collected import and export duties were called:
n2e88f90a900.x: Kara Pattanam were ports collecting duties; Krishnapatnam was on the Nellore coast and Hamsaladeevi in the Krishna delta.
xa: **Motupalli** was the chief port, also called **Desiyakonda Pattanam** (APPSC G2 **2019** key).
**Machilipatnam** was another port on the Krishna.
**Siddayya Devudu** was the official posted at **Motupalli**.

n08c0319e003.s: Who described the Kakatiya state as a 'metropolitan state'?
n08c0319e003.x: Romila Thapar used 'metropolitan state', while Burton Stein's label was 'segmentary state' - two different interpretations.
xa: Most scholars call it a **"decentralised monarchy"**.
Cynthia Talbot called the period the **"Golden Age of the Shudras"**.
Under the Kakatiyas, religion and politics became **non-Brahmin** (APPSC 2019 key).

nap-history-37-17.s:
Which of the following taxes are associated with the Kakatiyas?
1. Koru
2. Meruka
3. Pullari
nap-history-37-17.x: Koru and Pullari were Kakatiya levies. Meruka was a wet-land tax of the Reddis.
n: Koru was a cess on wet lands under the Kakatiyas. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 48-49]
Putti Wahindi was a cess on dry lands under the Kakatiyas. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 48-49]
Pullari was a tax on grass under the Kakatiyas. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 48-49]
Meruka was a tax on wetlands under the Reddis. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 48-49]
xa: **Adhi** = Kakatiya land cess; **Aari** = land tax (land revenue).
**Pellipannu** = Kakatiya wedding tax; **Angadi Sunkam** = weekly-market tax.
**Moturpha** = tax on trade, occupations and looms under **British rule**.

n606715fe223.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler totally withdrew the marriage tax?
n606715fe223.x: Krishnadevaraya withdrew the marriage tax; Moturpha, a British-era tax on trades and looms, was abolished in 1861.
xa: In Kakatiya times the wedding tax was called **Pellipannu**.
**Meruka** was the **Reddy** tax on wetlands.
**Pullari** was the Kakatiya tax on **grass**.

nap-history-13-2.s: In the Kakatiya revenue system, 'Pullari' was a tax levied on:
nap-history-13-2.x: Pullari was the grazing tax on grass; Putti was the dry-land cess, Ayagarlu held tax-free land and Arigapulu were tax-paying farmers.
n: Putti was a cess levied on dry lands. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 18-19]
Pullari was a Kakatiya tax levied on grass. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 18-19]
Ayagarlu enjoyed land without any cess or tax. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 18-19]
Arigapulu were Kakatiya farmers who paid taxes. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 18-19]
xa: The Ayagarlu numbered **twelve (12)**.
**Pedakapu** (**Reddy**) levied taxes based on the **Karanam's** assessment.
**Bahathara Viyog** = collective name of **all administration departments**.
**Koru** = cess on **wet lands**.

nec63f34ea8f.s: The Pakhala tank of the Kakatiya period was built by:
nec63f34ea8f.x: Mummadi Nayaka built the Pakhala tank; Prola II built Arikesari Samudram, Recherla Rudra the Ramappa tank and Ganapatideva Laknavaram.
xa: ⚠ **Kesari Samudram** = **Rudradeva**; **Arikesari Samudram** = **Prola II** (APPSC G2 2012).
**Ghanapuram** was also built by **Ganapatideva**.
**Bayyaram** (Khammam) – **Mailamba**; **Kunda Samudram** – **Kundamamba**.

nac829a8d662.s: The Kesari Samudram tank of the Kakatiya period was built by
nac829a8d662.x: The APPSC G2 2019 key credits Kesari Samudram to Rudradeva (some sources give Prola I). Prola II built Arikesari Samudram (APPSC 2012), Ganapatideva built Laknavaram and Ghanapuram, and Mailamba built the Bayyaram tank.
nac829a8d662.tq: Kesari Samudram = Rudradeva; Arikesari Samudram = Prola II.
xs: The **APPSC G2 2019** key credits **Kesari Samudram** to **Rudradeva** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Prola II** built **Arikesari Samudram** (APPSC G2 2012); **Ganapatideva** built **Laknavaram** and **Ghanapuram**; **Mailamba** built **Bayyaram**.
xa: ⚠ One source credits Kesari Samudram to **Prola I** — follow the APPSC key.
Rudradeva also built the **Hanamkonda** tank.
**Ramappa** tank (Palampet) – **Recherla Rudra**.
nac829a8d662.fixed: stem oddly cites an answer key; exams ask it directly

n3732fd84682.s: In Kakatiya tank irrigation, linked chain tanks were called:
n3732fd84682.x: Golusukattu cheruvulu were linked chain tanks passing surplus water downhill; Samudrams were large tanks and Dashabandhamu was tax-free land for tank upkeep.
xa: Tank-building was one of the **Sapta Santanalu** (seven meritorious acts).
The **Porumamilla** tank inscription (**1369**) lists **12 requisites of a good tank**.
The Kakatiya tank network still irrigates **Telangana**.

n2cb1694243a.s: Tank-building was one of the Sapta Santanalu, which were the seven:
n2cb1694243a.x: The Sapta Santanalu were seven meritorious acts: son, temple, garden, tank, agrahara, literature and treasure.
xa: **Chain tanks (Golusukattu cheruvulu)** passed surplus water to the next tank.
**Samudrams** = large tanks; **Dashabandhamu** = tax-free land for tank upkeep.
⚠ **Kesari Samudram** = **Rudradeva**; **Arikesari Samudram** = **Prola II**.
**Ramappa** tank — **Recherla Rudra**; **Pakhala** tank — **Mummadi Nayaka**; **Laknavaram** — **Ganapatideva**.

nfa630832aca.s: In the Kakatiya period, Nirmal was famous for:
nfa630832aca.x: Knives were associated with Nirmal, ratna kambalu with Warangal and diamonds with the Golconda region; iron came from Guthikonda and Palnadu.
xa: Warangal was also famed for **carpets/rugs** and **Mukkul vastralu**.
The Golconda diamonds were noted by **Marco Polo**.
Exports: textiles, spices, **diamonds**, gold, iron, rubies; imports: **Arabian war horses**, pearls, silk.

n664d5554782.s: Which of the following was NOT a function or characteristic of the Kakatiya merchant guilds?
o: Exercising an exclusive royal monopoly over all trade
Maintaining their own seal or emblem
n664d5554782.x: Guilds maintained seals or emblems, settled disputes and kept private military forces, but they did not possess an exclusive royal monopoly over all trade.
n664d5554782.tq: Find the overbroad and exclusive statement that goes beyond the guild functions.
xs: Guilds had **no exclusive royal monopoly over all trade** — option **(1)** is the answer.
They did have their **own seal and emblem**, **settled disputes**, and kept a **private militia**.
xa: Guilds gave part of their profit to temples and acted as **bankers** and local administrators.
They bargained with the king for **tax concessions**, e.g. the **Motupalli** charter.
Samayas met in **temple mandapams** and had an emblem.

nf0ef6194908.s: In the Kakatiya period, 'Chitrameli' was a samaya (occupational group) of:
nf0ef6194908.x: Samayas were caste or occupational groups, and Chitrameli was the samaya of agricultural farmers (APPSC G2 2019).
xa: **Ubhaya Nanadesi** Pekkandru traded in both domestic and foreign markets.
**Ayyavole 500** (Ayyavali Ainuraru) was the great trans-regional guild.
The Kakatiyas were themselves **Shudras**; samayas allowed **caste mobility**.

n031388c7bec.s: Which of the following was imported, rather than exported, in Kakatiya trade?
n031388c7bec.x: Arabian war horses were imported for the cavalry; textiles, spices, diamonds and gold were exported.
xa: Other imports: **pearls, silk, perfumes, spices**.
Trade partners: **China, Persia, Arabia, Ceylon, East Indies**.
Main inland centre: **Orugallu**; other centres: Pedaganjam, Ghantasala, **Tripurantakam**.
⚠ Export = **diamonds**, textiles; import = **Arabian war horses**.

n4c325d1936a.s: Ganapatideva's Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam guaranteed safety to:
n4c325d1936a.x: The charter protected foreign merchants, remitted arbitrary taxes, promised compensation for shipwreck or theft and stopped harassment by officials.
xa: Issued by **Ganapatideva** in **1244 CE**; beneficiaries were **foreign and seafaring traders**.
**Siddayya Devudu** was the official posted at Motupalli (APPSC PYQ).
It is rated the **most important commercial document** of the period.

n5cabfa9472f.s: Who was appointed at Motupalli under the Abhaya Sasanam of Ganapatideva?
n5cabfa9472f.x: Siddayya Devudu was the official posted at Motupalli under Ganapatideva’s charter.
n5cabfa9472f.tq: Match the official with the charter and port, avoiding confusion with later rulers and builders.
xs: **Siddayya Devudu** was the official posted at **Motupalli** (APPSC PYQ) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Anavota Reddi** issued a later bilingual Motupalli charter (Reddi period); **Bhaskara** issued the **Porumamilla** tank inscription (**1369**).
**Malyala Chauda Senani** built the **Chouda Samudram** tank.
xa: The Abhaya Sasanam was issued by **Ganapatideva** in **1244 CE**.
Motupalli was also called **Desiyakonda Pattanam**.
The **Motupalli Dharma Sasanam (1416)** belongs to Vijayanagara's **Deva Raya I**.

n7bcfdd3fc01.s: Motupalli, the chief port of the Kakatiyas, was also known as
n7bcfdd3fc01.x: Motupalli was also called Desiyakonda (Deseeyakkonda) Pattanam (APPSC G2 2019 key). Kara Pattanam is a general term for ports that collected import and export duties. Hamsaladeevi (Krishna delta) and Krishnapatnam (Nellore coast) were separate ports.
n7bcfdd3fc01.tq: Motupalli = Desiyakonda Pattanam = Marco Polo's Mutfili.
xs: Motupalli was also called **Desiyakonda Pattanam** (Deseeyakkonda Pattanam; **APPSC G2 2019** key) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kara Pattanam** is a general term for ports collecting duties; **Hamsaladeevi** and **Krishnapatnam** were separate ports.
xa: Ganapatideva issued the **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** there in **1244 CE**.
**Siddayya Devudu** was the official posted at Motupalli.
Vishnukundin-era ports: **Motupalli and Kodur**.

n4aaec362096.s: Our knowledge of Kakatiya coin types such as Mada, Gadyana and Ruka comes mainly from:
n4aaec362096.x: Few Kakatiya coins survive, so their types are known mainly from inscriptions.
xs: Kakatiya coin types are known mainly from **inscriptions**, as **few coins survive** — option **(3)** is correct.
So there are no large surviving hoards to rely on.
xa: **Mada** = gold, the Kakatiya-period coin; **Gadyana** = gold; **Ruka** = silver.
**Visa** = small fraction; **Adduga** and **Padika** are other types.
The **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (**1244**) is itself an inscription — a pillar inscription.

n25911d774fe.s: The Motupalli charter is regarded as the most important ____ document of the Kakatiya period.
n25911d774fe.x: The Motupalli charter is called the most important commercial document of the period, showing the state's stake in sea trade.
xa: The **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** was issued by **Ganapatideva** in **1244 CE**, giving **safety to foreign merchants**.
⚠ **1244** Abhaya Sasanam = **Ganapatideva**; **1416** Dharma Sasanam = **Deva Raya I**.
A later bilingual (Telugu-Tamil) Motupalli charter was issued by **Anavota Reddi**.

nindian-history-26-17.s: Sandal, camphor, rose-water and ivory appear among the goods traded at which Kakatiya port?
nindian-history-26-17.x: Sandal, camphor, rose-water and ivory all appear among the goods traded at Motupalli.
n: Motupalli had trade in sandal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 89-90]
Motupalli had trade in camphor. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 89-90]
Motupalli had trade in rose-water. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 89-90]
Motupalli had trade in ivory. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 89-90]
xa: Other goods named: **pearls, corals, copper, zinc, lead, silk, pepper** and **areca nuts**.
The **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** was issued by **Ganapatideva** in **1244 CE**.
Its purpose: **safety to foreign merchants**, remission of arbitrary taxes, compensation for **shipwreck** or theft.
Motupalli's other name: **Desiyakonda Pattanam**.

n1b6a7f1923a.s: The Motupalli Dharma Sasanam of 1416 belonged to the reign of:
n1b6a7f1923a.x: The 1416 Motupalli Dharma Sasanam belonged to Vijayanagara ruler Deva Raya I; Ganapatideva's Abhaya Sasanam dates to 1244 CE.
xa: Deva Raya I issued it after taking Motupalli from **Kondavidu**.
The Abhaya Sasanam assured **safety** to foreign merchants and remitted arbitrary taxes.
Motupalli's long life: a **Vishnukundin-era** port and later one of **Vijayanagara's** Andhra ports.

nf73f3e2b52a.s: Padmanayakas in the Kakatiya period were
o: A group of port merchants from Motupalli
Village accountants paid only in cash
Recherla Velama chiefs and important Kakatiya commanders
nf73f3e2b52a.x: Padmanayakas were Recherla Velama chiefs and key Kakatiya commanders. They later founded the Velama kingdom.
nf73f3e2b52a.tq: Use the person-group and later political role to identify the correct description.
xs: **Padmanayakas** were **Recherla Velama chiefs** and **key Kakatiya commanders** — option **(4)** is correct.
They later founded the **Velama kingdom**.
xa: **Racherla Singama**, one of the three generals who survived **1323**, came from this line.
**Recherla Rudra** built the **Ramappa** tank at Palampet.
**Siddayya Devudu** was the official posted at **Motupalli** (APPSC PYQ).

n27dda45b6ef.s: Virabanajam was licensed to operate in which of the following regions?
n27dda45b6ef.x: The Virabanajam guild was licensed for Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda, as recorded in the Tripurantakam inscription of 1282.
n27dda45b6ef.tq: Recall the specific licensed regions rather than confusing them with ports or foreign trading partners.
xs: **Virabanajam** was licensed for **Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda** — option **(3)** is correct.
The licence is recorded in the **Tripurantakam inscription** of **1282**.
**China, Persia, Arabia** were overseas trade partners; **Motupalli**, **Krishnapatnam**, **Hamsaladeevi** were ports.
xa: **Nakaram** = domestic-trade guild; **Nanadesi** = foreign; **Ubhaya Nanadesi** = both.
**Ayyavole 500** was the great trans-regional guild.
**Tripurantakam** was also one of the trade centres.
