n4e7a2b44c3f.s: The Kakatiyas controlled routes connecting the
o: Tamil interior and the Arabian Peninsula exclusively
Deccan interior and the eastern coast
Western coast and the Himalayan region
n4e7a2b44c3f.x: Kakatiya control extended over routes between the Deccan interior and the eastern coast.
n4e7a2b44c3f.tq: Identify the broad geographical direction of the controlled trade routes.
xs: The Kakatiyas controlled routes between the **Deccan interior and the eastern coast** — option **(2)** is correct.
Sources name only **ports** and **licensed regions** — no highway list.
xa: Main inland centre: **Orugallu**; chief port: **Motupalli**.
**Virabanajam** was licensed for **Pakanadu**, **Vengi** and **Hanumakonda** (Tripurantakam inscription, **1282**).
Ports: **Krishnapatnam** (Nellore coast), **Hamsaladeevi** (Krishna delta), **Machilipatnam** (Krishna).

n9dd23e6403c.s: During the Kakatiya period, caste associations were known as:
xs: Kakatiya caste associations were called **Samayas** (**APPSC G2 2019** answer) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Nakaram** was the body of the **Vaishyas (Komatis)**; **Mahajanas** were the **Brahmins**.
**Simha** and **Shakti Parishat** were the two Kalamukha divisions, not caste bodies.
xa: Each samaya elected a **senior head** who settled disputes; members paid dues to the caste head.
**Ashtadasha kulas** = **18 occupational groups** inside Warangal fort (Kreedabhiramam).
Rising Sudra warrior-peasant groups: **Reddis**, **Kammas**, **Velamas** (Padmanayakas).

n9683bb8aa7a.s: The term 'Ashtadasha kulas' in the Kakatiya context refers to:
o: Eighteen royal dynasties of the Deccan
Eighteen occupational groups living inside Warangal fort
n9683bb8aa7a.x: Ashtadasha kulas denotes the 18 occupational groups that lived inside Warangal fort, as mentioned in Kreedabhiramam.
n9683bb8aa7a.tq: Decode the numerical social classification from its context.
xs: **Ashtadasha kulas** were the **18 occupational groups** living **inside Warangal fort** — option **(4)** is correct.
The term comes from **Kreedabhiramam**.
xa: Caste associations were called **Samayas**, each with an elected senior head.
Weavers were called **Sales**; other castes included **Telikas**, **Gollas**, **Boyas**, **Gandla**.
⚠ **Eighteen** = Ashtadasha kulas; **twelve** = Ayagars; **72** = Niyogas.

n59b18e42cb5.s: The early Kakatiyas were followers of which religion before becoming Shaivas from the time of Prola II or Rudradeva?
n59b18e42cb5.x: The early Kakatiyas were Jains; they later became Shaivas from the period of Prola II or Rudradeva.
n59b18e42cb5.tq: Test the religious transition in chronological form.
xs: The **early Kakatiyas** followed **Jainism** (**APPSC G2 2011**) — option **(3)** is correct.
They became **Shaivas** from **Prola II / Rudradeva**.
xa: **Prola II** built the **Padmakshi temple**, originally a **Jain shrine**.
Jainism declined under **Kalamukha** and **Veerashaiva** hostility.
**Visveshwara Shambhu**, Ganapatideva's guru, destroyed **36 Jain villages**.

ndc65d2d2d8f.s: Which of the following contributed to the decline of Jainism in the Kakatiya region?
o: The decline of all temple institutions
The spread of Vaishnava temple festivals alone
The rise of the Aradhya stream alone
ndc65d2d2d8f.x: The decline of Jainism was associated with hostility from Kalamukha and Veerashaiva groups and persecution by certain Kakatiya authorities.
ndc65d2d2d8f.tq: Identify the stated cause rather than an adjacent religious development.
xs: Jainism declined because of **Kalamukha and Veerashaiva hostility** — option **(3)** is correct.
Temple institutions did not decline — temples were **landed corporations**.
xa: **Visveshwara Shambhu** destroyed **36 Jain villages**; **Brahmayya** destroyed Jain settlements.
**Ganapati** persecuted Jains at **Anmakonda**.
The Kakatiyas are credited with the **final eradication** of Jainism in the region.

n68f23536cba.s: The Kakatiya age is often characterised as the:
n68f23536cba.x: The Kakatiya age is called the Shaiva era because Shaivism had a prominent position during the period.
n68f23536cba.tq: Directly identify the period-label relationship without confusing the presence of other religious traditions with the dominant characterisation.
xs: The Kakatiya age is called the **"Shaiva era"** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Svayambhu Shiva** was the dynastic deity; the Kakatiyas patronised **Pasupata** and **Kalamukha** sects.
Jainism was the faith of the **early Kakatiyas** only, and it declined under the dynasty.
xa: Vaishnava shrines (**Thousand Pillar Temple**) were still endowed — **religious tolerance and syncretism**.
The Kakatiyas turned Shaiva from **Prola II / Rudradeva**.
Shaiva-Shakta axis: **Srisailam**, **Alampur**, **Draksharama**.

nb59c235caeb.s: Who is regarded as the founder of the Pasupata sect?
nb59c235caeb.x: Pasupata is identified as the oldest Shaiva sect and is associated with Lakulisa, also called Nakulisa.
xs: **Pasupata**, the oldest Shaiva sect, was founded by **Lakulisa (Nakulisa)** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Basaveshwara** founded **Veerashaivism**; **Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya** led the **Aradhya** stream.
**Kalasana/Kalanana**, Lakulisa's disciple, is linked to the **Kalamukha** sect.
xa: **Kapalikas** (skull-bowl ascetics) were an offshoot of **Pasupata** (APPSC G2 2019).
Pasupata Shaivism stayed popular into the **Reddi** period (APPSC G2 2011) and declined under Vijayanagara.
The Kakatiyas patronised the "extremist" **Pasupata and Kalamukha** sects.

ne7b8c913279.s: The Kapalikas, the skull-bowl ascetics, were an offshoot of which Shaiva sect?
ne7b8c913279.x: The Kapalikas were an offshoot of the Pasupata sect (APPSC G2 2019), not of the Kalamukhas.
xa: Exam angle: "Kapalikas arose from which doctrine" and "popular religion of the Reddi Rajas" — both **Pasupata**.
Pasupata founder: **Lakulisa (Nakulisa)**.
⚠ **Simha Parishat** = Andhra; **Shakti Parishat** = Karnataka.

n6c86dcfc4ea.s: Basaveshwara, founder of Veerashaivism, was a minister of:
n6c86dcfc4ea.x: Basaveshwara was a minister of Kalachuri Bijjala in Karnataka.
xa: Veerashaivism's texts were the **Agamas**; it was the **first social-reform religion** in Andhra.
Followers wore the **Ishtalinga** on the body.
It rejected **Vedas**, **caste**, **untouchability**, **child marriage** and **animal sacrifice**.

n21234cf4153.s: The main centre of Veerashaivism in Andhra was:
n21234cf4153.x: Srisailam was the main Veerashaiva centre in Andhra; Kolanupaka is listed among Jain centres.
xa: Founder: **Basaveshwara**, minister of **Kalachuri Bijjala**.
Followers = **Lingayats**; gurus = **Jangamas**; texts = **Agamas**.
The Kakatiyas stayed **neutral** and did not persecute Lingayats.

n3096adc1773.s: The Padmakshi temple at Hanumakonda was originally:
o: A Pasupata temple built by Lakulisa
n3096adc1773.x: The Padmakshi temple, built by Prola II, was originally a Jain shrine.
n3096adc1773.tq: Use the temple's original religious identity rather than its later association.
xs: The **Padmakshi temple** was originally a **Jain shrine** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was built by **Prola II**, from whose time the Kakatiyas turned Shaiva.
xa: **Hanumakonda** was a refuge for Jains persecuted under the **Eastern Chalukyas**.
Jain deities were absorbed as Hindu goddesses: **Kakitamma** and **Jogulamba**.
The Kakatiyas are credited with the **final eradication of Jainism** in the region.

n06466edfedc.s: According to the Kakatiya-period legal principle, a woman's property passed to her:
o: Sons alone through the male line
The king after the woman's death
n06466edfedc.x: The recorded principle (cited from Ketana's Vijnaneswaramu and Purushartha Saramu) was that a woman's property passed to her daughters and daughter's daughters, a comparatively progressive outlook.
xa: Author: **Sivadevayya**.
The same book describes the **72 Niyogas** and the king's daily council routine.
⚠ Distractors: **Vignaneswaram** (Ketana), **Nitisara** (Rudradeva), **Niti Shastra Muktavali** (Baddena).
n06466edfedc.fixed: yf9ff5650f59 key = Vignanesvaram of Ketana, not Purushartha Saramu

n4b363a18200.s: Hero-stones, or viragallu, commemorated warriors who died:
n4b363a18200.x: Viragallu were memorial stones for warriors who died in battle or during cattle raids.
n4b363a18200.tq: Link the memorial object with the two stated circumstances of death.
xs: **Viragallu** (hero-stones) commemorated warriors who died **in battle or cattle raids** — option **(3)** is correct.
Temple women (**Kalavatis**) were linked to dance and music, not to hero-stones.
xa: Social customs included **superstition**, **animal sacrifice** and **self-sacrifice by devotees of Shiva**.
Festivals were royal occasions.
Kalamukhas gave **anna dana** at feeding houses.

n3b8c7e21463.s: Royal endowments mentioned in connection with Kakatiya temples include:
o: Prataparudra II's grant to Chennakeshava and Lakshmidevi's grant to Ramanatha at Yelledu
Ganapatideva's grant to Padmakshi and Basava's grant to Srisailam
Prola II's grant to Tripurantakam and Brahmayya's grant to Vemulawada
Rudradeva's grant to Nakaram and Durgaraja's grant to Warangal fort
n3b8c7e21463.x: Prataparudra II endowed the Chennakeshava temple in 1321, while his queen Lakshmidevi endowed the Ramanatha temple at Yelledu.
n3b8c7e21463.tq: Match donor, temple and place without swapping the royal patron.
xs: **Prataparudra II** endowed **Chennakeshava** (**1321**) and his queen **Lakshmidevi** endowed the **Ramanatha temple at Yelledu** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Basaveshwara** was a Karnataka minister of **Kalachuri Bijjala**; **Brahmayya** destroyed Jain settlements; **Nakaram** was a Vaishya body.
xa: Royal women were active donors to **temples and tanks**.
**Prola II** built the **Padmakshi temple**.
Vaishnava shrines like the **Thousand Pillar Temple** were also endowed.

n8a2351722eb.s: Which one of the following was the dynastic deity of the Kakatiyas?
n8a2351722eb.x: Svayambhu Shiva was the dynastic deity of the Kakatiyas.
n8a2351722eb.tq: Test the exact deity associated with the ruling dynasty rather than a prominent regional shrine.
xs: The Kakatiya dynastic deity was **Svayambhu Shiva** — option **(1)** is correct.
The period is thus called the **"Shaiva era"**.
xa: Yet Vaishnava shrines (**Thousand Pillar Temple**) were endowed — tolerance and syncretism.
**Prataparudra II** endowed **Chennakeshava** in **1321**.
Early Kakatiyas were **Jains** before becoming Shaivas from **Prola II / Rudradeva**.

n608ae6b712a.s: Purushartha Saramu of Sivadevayya is an important administrative source because it gives information about:
o: The military conquests of the Reddi kings
The 72 Niyogas and the king's daily council routine
The 18 occupational groups inside Warangal fort only
The division of Kalamukha sects into two parishads
n608ae6b712a.x: Purushartha Saramu also describes the 72 Niyogas, or departments, and the daily routine of the king's council.
n608ae6b712a.tq: Distinguish the administrative content of the text from unrelated social facts.
xs: **Purushartha Saramu** also describes the **72 Niyogas** (departments) and the **king's daily council routine** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **18 occupational groups** inside Warangal fort come from **Kreedabhiramam**, not this book.
xa: Author: **Sivadevayya**.
Its legal content: a woman's property passed to her **daughters and daughter's daughters** (APPSC G2 2019).
Kalamukha divisions: **Simha Parishat** (Andhra) and **Shakti Parishat** (Karnataka).
n608ae6b712a.fixed: the women's-property tenet belongs to Vignaneswaram (yf9ff5650f59)

n8c6421aff33.s: Who built the Prasanna Keshava Temple at Hanamkonda?
n8c6421aff33.x: Vellanki Gangadhara, a Vaishnava minister of Rudradeva, built the Prasanna Keshava Temple at Hanamkonda.
xa: Rudradeva built the **Thousand Pillar Temple** (**1163 CE**) and gave **Maddi Cheruvu** village for its upkeep.
Ganapatideva built the **Swayambhu Shiva** temple (**1254**) in Warangal fort.
The **Dharmasagara inscription** mentions the instrument **'Jalakaranda'** (APPSC 2019).

nd1685146043.s: How many pillars does the Thousand Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda actually have?
nd1685146043.x: It has 369 pillars; its lathe-turned pillars only give the illusion of a thousand.
xa: Rudradeva gave **Maddi Cheruvu** village for its upkeep.
Deities: **Rudreshwara (Shiva)**, **Vasudeva (Vishnu)**, **Surya**.
⚠ Both called **Rudreshwara**: Thousand Pillar = **1163** (Hanamkonda); Ramappa = **1213** (Palampet).

n5d1b131e846.s: Ramappa Temple, also known as Rudreshwaralayam, is located at which place?
n5d1b131e846.x: Ramappa Temple is situated at Palampet in Mulugu district of Telangana.
n5d1b131e846.tq: Use the location-based elimination method and distinguish Palampet from Hanamkonda.
xs: Ramappa (Rudreshwaralayam) is at **Palampet in Mulugu district**, Telangana — option **(2)** is correct.
**Hanamkonda** has the other Rudreshwara — the **Thousand Pillar Temple**.
xa: Built c. **1213 CE** by general **Recherla Rudra** in **Ganapatideva's** reign.
Deity: Shiva as **Ramalingeswara**.
**Ramanujapuram** (Mulugu, near Palampet) has the only **Panchakuta** temple of the Kakatiya era.

n5f509d88cfa.s: The presiding deity of the Ramappa Temple is worshipped as:
n5f509d88cfa.x: The presiding deity is Shiva as Ramalingeswara.
n5f509d88cfa.tq: Apply the confusable-name method by separating the temple name from the deity's name.
xs: Ramappa's presiding deity is **Shiva as Ramalingeswara** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Vasudeva** is **Vishnu** in the Thousand Pillar Temple, and **Mallikarjuna** is the Srisailam deity.
xa: Ramappa is also called **Rudreshwaralayam**.
A **Nandi** faces the sanctum.
It is named after its sculptor **Ramappa**.

naa36c1bae93.s: Why is the temple at Palampet popularly known as the Ramappa Temple?
o: It is named after its sculptor Ramappa
It was built beside the Ramappa tank
It was dedicated by a ruler named Ramappa
It was consecrated on the festival of Rama Navami
naa36c1bae93.x: It is the only temple in India known by the name of its sculptor, Ramappa.
naa36c1bae93.tq: Test the unusual person–monument relationship rather than the more common ruler–monument association.
xs: The temple is **named after its sculptor Ramappa** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is the **only temple in India known by its sculptor's name**.
The **Ramappa tank** was also built by **Recherla Rudra**, the temple's builder.
xa: Built c. **1213 CE** in **Ganapatideva's** reign.
Deity: Shiva as **Ramalingeswara**.
UNESCO World Heritage Site on **25 July 2021**.

n0ade622d38e.s: The Ramappa (Rudreshwara) temple at Palampet was built around 1213 CE by
o: Rudradeva, as the dynastic shrine at Hanamkonda
Recherla Rudra, a general of Ganapatideva
Jayapa Senani, during Rudrama Devi's reign
n0ade622d38e.x: Recherla Rudra, the Kakatiya general, built the Ramappa temple around 1213 during Ganapatideva's reign; he also built the Ramappa tank. Rudradeva built the Thousand Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda in 1163. Ganapatideva built the Swayambhu Shiva temple in Warangal fort in 1254. Jayapa Senani wrote Nritta Ratnavali.
xs: Ramappa was built c. **1213 CE** by **Recherla Rudra**, a Kakatiya general of **Ganapatideva** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Rudradeva** built the **Thousand Pillar Temple** at Hanamkonda in **1163**.
**Ganapatideva** built the **Swayambhu Shiva** temple in Warangal fort in **1254**; **Jayapa Senani** wrote **Nritta Ratnavali**.
xa: Recherla Rudra also built the **Ramappa tank**.
The temple is named after sculptor **Ramappa**.
Deity: **Ramalingeswara** (Shiva).

n2cb23582027.s: Who built the Thousand Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda?
n2cb23582027.x: The Thousand Pillar Temple was built by Rudradeva; Recherla Rudra built the Ramappa Temple.
xa: Prasanna Keshavalayam, Padmakshi and Siddheshwaralayam are all at **Hanamkonda**.
**Pillalamarri** (Erakeshwara etc.) was built by the **Recherla feudatories**.
Swayambhu Lingalayam (**1254**) is in **Warangal (Orugallu) fort**.

nddbc3eae89a.s: The Ramappa (Rudreshwara) Temple at Palampet is named after its:
nddbc3eae89a.x: The Palampet temple, associated with floating bricks, is named after its sculptor Ramappa; it was built by Recherla Rudra.
xa: Thousand Pillar has **369 pillars** and a **monolithic Nandi**.
Ramappa: **UNESCO** site on **25 July 2021**; **sandbox foundation**.
⚠ The **APPSC G2 2012** key calls Ramappa Trikuta — the notes give Trikuta to the Thousand Pillar Temple.

nd8331e27800.s: Which site is associated with the only Panchakuta temple of the Kakatiya era?
nd8331e27800.x: Ramanujapuram in Mulugu, near Palampet, is noted for the only Panchakuta temple of the Kakatiya era.
nd8331e27800.tq: Use the unique or only-item clue to identify the site.
xs: The only **Panchakuta** temple of the Kakatiya era is at **Ramanujapuram** — option **(4)** is correct.
Ramanujapuram is in **Mulugu**, near **Palampet**.
xa: ⚠ **Trikuta** = Thousand Pillar (3 shrines); **Panchakuta** = Ramanujapuram (5).
**Ghanapur** has the **Ganapeswara** group; **Pillalamarri** has **Erakeshwara**.
Ramappa is the only temple named after its **sculptor**.

nap-history-36-24.s: Which of the following did NOT belong to the Kakatiya dynasty?
nap-history-36-24.x: Recharla Rudra was a Kakatiya general from the Recherla family, not a member of the dynasty.
n: Ganapatideva belonged to the Kakatiya dynasty. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Rudramadevi belonged to the Kakatiya dynasty. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Recharla Rudra belonged to the Kakatiya dynasty. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
xa: Recharla Rudra built the **Ramappa Temple** (c. **1213 CE**) and the **Ramappa tank**.
His title: **Kakatiya Stapanacharya**.
**Ganapatideva** was a devout **Shaivite**.

nap-history-36-8.s: Up to which place did Ganapatideva expand the Kakatiya kingdom?
nap-history-36-8.x: Ganapatideva, the greatest Kakatiya ruler, extended the kingdom south as far as Kanchi. Kondaveedu and Addanki were later Reddy capitals, and Nellore was one of his conquests on the way.
nap-history-36-8.tq: Recall the southern limit of Ganapatideva's kingdom.
n: Ganapatideva expanded the kingdom up to Kanchi. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
xs: **Ganapatideva** expanded the Kakatiya kingdom up to **Kanchi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He also shifted the capital from **Hanamakonda** to **Warangal** in **1254**.
xa: He completed **Warangal fort** and built the **Swayambhu Shiva** temple (**1254**).
His successor **Rudramadevi** ascended in **1260**.
⚠ His successor's title **Rayagaja Kesari** belongs to **Rudramadevi**, not Ganapatideva.

n4a32a775ed7.s: Which set correctly identifies the three presiding deities of the Thousand Pillar Temple?
n4a32a775ed7.x: The Trikuta temple is dedicated to Rudreshwara or Shiva, Vasudeva or Vishnu, and Surya. Surya occupies the place usually associated with Brahma in the Trinity.
n4a32a775ed7.tq: Test the unusual deity combination and the substitution of Surya for Brahma.
xs: The Thousand Pillar Temple's deities are **Rudreshwara (Shiva)**, **Vasudeva (Vishnu)** and **Surya** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Surya** takes the place **Brahma** has in the usual Trinity (**APPSC G2 2025** statement III), so Brahma is absent.
xa: It is a **Trikuta** (three-shrine) temple on a star-shaped platform.
Built by **Rudradeva (Prataparudra I)** in **1163 CE**.
⚠ **Trikuta** = Thousand Pillar (3 shrines); **Panchakuta** = Ramanujapuram (5).

n26d3f3407f7.s: On which date was the Ramappa Temple inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
n26d3f3407f7.x: The Ramappa Temple was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site on 25 July 2021.
n26d3f3407f7.tq: Use exact-date discrimination among closely related years.
xs: Ramappa became a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** on **25 July 2021** — option **(3)** is correct.
It stands at **Palampet**, **Mulugu district**.
xa: Engineering highlights: **floating bricks** in the vimana and a **sandbox foundation**.
Sculpture: **Madanika** bracket figures and **28 elephant-lion figures** (Gajakesari title).
Painted ceilings show **Ramayana-Mahabharata** scenes.

n71e3a529ac5.s: The bracket figures on the outer walls of the Ramappa Temple are called:
n71e3a529ac5.x: The Ramappa Temple has madanika bracket figures on its outer walls, besides a star-shaped platform and painted ceilings.
xa: Statues of the **Recherla Rudra couple** and **28 elephant-lion figures** (Gajakesari title).
**Floating bricks** in the vimana; **sandbox foundation** below.
⚠ The **APPSC G2 2012** key calls Ramappa **Trikuta**, but the notes give the Trikuta plan to the Thousand Pillar Temple.

n0570af85e8f.s: Jayapa Senani held which post under Ganapatideva?
n0570af85e8f.x: Jayapa Senani served as Gaja Sahini, the head of the elephant force, under Ganapatideva.
n0570af85e8f.tq: Use the office-based clue and distinguish Gaja Sahini from military and administrative posts.
xs: Jayapa Senani was the **Gaja Sahini** — **head of the elephant force** under Ganapatideva — option **(4)** is correct.
Exam angle: "Jayapa's main profession" — answer **Gajasahini**, not dancer.
xa: He wrote **Nritta Ratnavali** (Sanskrit, **8 prakaranas**).
He also wrote **Gita Ratnavali** and **Vadya Ratnavali**.
Ramappa's madanika poses follow his Nritta Ratnavali (**APPSC GS 2018**; **G2 2019**).

ncd6859a59ce.s: The sandbox foundation technology of Kakatiya temples involved
o: pits filled with sand, stone chips and earth to absorb shocks
a timber framework surrounded by lime mortar
floating bricks placed beneath the temple platform without any earth filling
solid granite blocks laid directly on black cotton soil
ncd6859a59ce.x: Sandbox foundations consisted of deep pits filled with sand, stone chips and earth, creating a shock-absorbing base on black cotton soil.
ncd6859a59ce.tq: Apply the engineering principle to the described construction method.
xs: The **sandbox foundation** was **deep pits filled with sand, stone chips and earth** acting as a **shock absorber** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was laid on **black cotton soil**, not granite blocks placed directly on it.
**Floating bricks** were used in Ramappa's **vimana**, not under the platform.
xa: The sandbox foundation is why **Ramappa** has survived earthquakes.
⚠ **Floating bricks** = lighter tower; **sandbox foundation** = earthquake cushion.
**Stellate (star) plan** = raised star-shaped platform giving more wall surface for sculpture.

n68d25d293b2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Kakatiya architectural terms?
o: Floating bricks reduce the dead weight of the tower
Kirtimukha means the 'face of glory' motif
Stellate plans give greater wall surface for sculpture
n68d25d293b2.x: Monolithic carving is denoted by Ekasila; Kirtimukha is the 'face of glory' motif.
xa: Ekasila examples: the monolithic **Nandi** and pillars in **black basalt**, as at the Thousand Pillar Temple.
The **sandbox foundation** acted as a shock absorber on black cotton soil.
Pillars were **lathe-turned** and polished granite.

nb8c8e71a998.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principal features of Kakatiya temple architecture?
o: A square platform without a foundation, unpolished pillars and animal-free walls
A sunken platform, plain wooden pillars and undecorated exterior walls
A circular mud platform, Persian arches and glazed tile brackets
A raised star-shaped platform, polished lathe-turned pillars and madanika or bracket figures in dance poses
nb8c8e71a998.x: Kakatiya temples commonly feature a raised star-shaped platform on a sandbox foundation, polished lathe-turned pillars and projecting madanika or bracket figures in dance poses.
nb8c8e71a998.tq: Select the option containing the complete and precise architectural combination.
xs: Kakatiya temples have a **raised star-shaped platform**, **polished lathe-turned pillars** and **madanika (bracket) figures in dance poses** — option **(4)** is correct.
They rest on a **sandbox foundation**, not on no foundation.
xa: Other features: high **adhisthana**, **jaali** parapets, **toranas**, **rangamandapas**, swan and lotus motifs.
**Kirtimukha** ("face of glory") motif and **Ekasila** monolithic carving.
Ramappa's madanika poses follow **Jayapa Senani's Nritta Ratnavali**.

n5a924f96793.s: Which one of the following is an example of the engineering significance of Ramappa Temple?
o: Its sandbox foundation illustrates earthquake-resistant heritage engineering.
Its floating bricks were used exclusively to support temple sculptures.
Its moat demonstrates the earliest use of defensive hydraulic engineering in India.
Its star-shaped plan eliminated the need for a structural foundation.
n5a924f96793.x: The sandbox foundation of Ramappa is cited as an example of heritage engineering because it helped the temple withstand earthquakes.
n5a924f96793.tq: Apply the architectural feature to its broader heritage significance.
xs: Ramappa's **sandbox foundation** is a cited example of **earthquake-resistant heritage engineering** — option **(1)** is correct.
The star plan did not remove the need for a foundation; **floating bricks** lightened the **tower**, not the sculptures.
xa: Sandbox = deep pits of **sand, stone chips and earth** on **black cotton soil**.
Floating bricks are light porous bricks that **float on water**.
Ramappa: **UNESCO** World Heritage Site on **25 July 2021**.

nap-history-35-6.s: Who ascended the Kakatiya throne after Ganapathi Deva in 1260?
nap-history-35-6.x: Rudramadevi, also called Rudramba, succeeded her father Ganapatideva in 1260. Mahadeva ruled before Ganapatideva, Pratapa Rudra came in 1296 and Kumaragiri Reddy was a Reddy king.
nap-history-35-6.tq: Place Kakatiya rulers in order: Rudra Deva, Mahadeva, Ganapatideva, Rudramadevi, Pratapa Rudra.
n: Rudramba ascended after Ganapathi Deva in 1260. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 46-47]
xs: **Rudramadevi (Rudramba)** succeeded **Ganapatideva** in **1260** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Mahadeva** ascended after **Rudra Deva**, before Ganapatideva; **Pratapa Rudra** ascended in **1296**.
xa: Rudramadevi's title: **Rayagaja Kesari**.
**Marco Polo** visited **Andhra Desa** during her reign.
She added a **step-arch** to **Warangal fort**.

n0a3e9ee314d.s: Kakatiya temple architecture is principally associated with which style?
n0a3e9ee314d.x: Kakatiya temple architecture follows the Chalukyan, or Vesara, style and is also described as transitional between early Chalukyan and Vijayanagara styles.
n0a3e9ee314d.tq: Distinguish the named architectural style from broad regional alternatives.
xs: Kakatiya temples follow the **Chalukyan (Vesara)** style — option **(2)** is correct.
Other notes call it a **transitional style** between **early Chalukyan and Vijayanagara**.
The main influence was the **Western Chalukyas of Kalyani**: carved pillars, star-shaped platforms, ornate doorways, sculptured ceilings.
xa: Local innovations: **stellate plan**, **sandbox foundation**, **floating bricks**, **Ekasila** carving.
**Early Kakatiya kings built Jain temples** (APPSC G2 2025 statement I).
Other features: high **adhisthana**, **jaali** parapets, **toranas**, **rangamandapas**, swan and lotus motifs.

n7b95d465e24.s: Kakatiya temple architecture shows the influence of the:
n7b95d465e24.x: Kakatiya style shows Western Chalukya (Kalyani) influence in carved pillars, star platforms and ceilings (APPSC G2 2025).
xa: Prola II also built **Siddheshwaralayam** at Hanamkonda.
The Vaishnava temple at Hanamkonda was **Prasanna Keshavalayam**, by **Vellanki Gangadhara**.
Jain-Shaiva conflicts began under **Rudradeva**.

n9a5a5e7b5e1.s: Pillalamarri is particularly associated with which of the following?
o: Kunduru Chodas, the Chaya Someswara temple and Trikuta architecture
Ganapatideva, the Ganapeswara temple and 22 shrines
The only Panchakuta temple of the Kakatiya era
Recherla feudatories, the Erakeshwara temple and Kakatiya paintings
n9a5a5e7b5e1.x: Pillalamarri is associated with the Recherla feudatories, the Erakeshwara temple and Kakatiya paintings.
n9a5a5e7b5e1.tq: Use the builder–temple–art association to distinguish sites in the temple table.
xs: **Pillalamarri** is linked with the **Recherla feudatories**, the **Erakeshwara** temple and **Kakatiya paintings** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Kunduru Chodas / Chaya Someswara** belong to **Panugallu**; **Ganapeswara** and **22** shrines to **Ghanapur**; the **Panchakuta** to **Ramanujapuram**.
xa: Pillalamarri is in **Suryapet** district.
Its paintings paved the way for Vijayanagara's **Lepakshi** style.
**Recherla Rudra**, of the same family, built Ramappa.

n5bc91cebb6c.s: The dance poses depicted in the madanika brackets of the Ramappa Temple are associated with which work?
n5bc91cebb6c.x: The madanika poses at Ramappa follow Jayapa Senani's Nritta Ratnavali.
n5bc91cebb6c.tq: Distinguish the specifically linked dance treatise from other well-known music and dance works.
xs: Ramappa's madanika poses follow **Jayapa Senani's Nritta Ratnavali** (**APPSC GS 2018**; **G2 2019**) — option **(1)** is correct.
Not **Natya Shastra** or **Sangita Ratnakara** (Sarangadeva, Yadava court of Devagiri).
**Gita Ratnavali** is Jayapa's work on **music**, not dance.
xa: Nritta Ratnavali is in **Sanskrit**, with **8 prakaranas**.
It covers **Marga** (classical) and **Desi** (regional/folk) dance and describes **Perini**.
Jayapa was **Gaja Sahini** (head of the elephant force) under Ganapatideva.

nf67ebf5baa1.s: The innermost defensive enclosure of Warangal Fort was called:
nf67ebf5baa1.x: Warangal had three concentric lines of defence; Puttakota was the innermost and Kalukota the outer stone fort.
xa: The middle **mud fort** (about **20 ft**) had a **moat** and **4 cardinal gates**.
Kalukota had **77 towers**.
Founded by **Rudradeva**; completed by **Ganapatideva**.

n303fb4b27d2.s: The Kakatiya Kala Thoranam consists of
o: eight gateways surrounding the Kalyana Mandapam
four ornate stone gateways around the Swayambhu Shiva temple
four brick gateways at the entrance to Puttakota
three mud gateways around the outer fort
n303fb4b27d2.x: The Kala Thoranam comprises four ornate stone gateways situated around the Swayambhu Shiva temple inside Warangal Fort.
n303fb4b27d2.tq: Use the number, material and location together to identify the monument.
xs: The **Kakatiya Kala Thoranam** is **four ornate stone gateways** of the **Swayambhu Shiva temple** — option **(2)** is correct.
It stands inside **Warangal (Orugallu) fort**.
xa: The temple was the dynastic shrine, built by **Ganapatideva** in **1254**.
It was ruined by **Ulugh Khan** in **1323**.
Today it is the **official emblem of Telangana state**.

n71ae7b04843.s: The official emblem of Telangana State incorporates the
n71ae7b04843.x: The Kakatiya Kala Thoranam is the official emblem of Telangana State.
n71ae7b04843.tq: Test a present-day symbolic association rather than an architectural detail.
xs: Telangana's official emblem is the **Kakatiya Kala Thoranam** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is the set of **four ornate stone gateways** of the **Swayambhu Shiva temple**, Warangal fort.
xa: The temple was built by **Ganapatideva** in **1254**.
The **Thousand Pillar Temple** has a massive **monolithic Nandi**.
**Puttakota** was the fort's innermost defence.

n1f5aa905898.s: The musical instrument 'Jalakaranda' is mentioned in which Kakatiya-period inscription?
n1f5aa905898.x: The Dharmasagara inscription mentions the instrument Jalakaranda (APPSC 2019). The Motupalli inscription (1244) protected foreign traders, the Magallu grant (956) first mentions the Kakatiyas, and the Chandupatla inscription records Rudrama Devi's death.
xs: **'Jalakaranda'** is mentioned in the **Dharmasagara inscription** (**APPSC 2019**) — option **(1)** is correct.
The notes link no musical instrument to the other inscriptions.
xa: Temple counts: **1,300 Vaishnava**, **2,400 Mallara Devudu**, **4,400 Bhairava/Durga/Ganesha** temples.
**52 villages** were endowed to the **Srisailam Mallikarjuna** temple.
Music treatises: **Gita Ratnavali** and **Vadya Ratnavali** of **Jayapa Senani** (now lost).

n703148092e4.s: The 'Maiputa' of Satavahana-era dancers is equated with
n703148092e4.x: The Satavahana dancers' Maiputa is equated with Kusuma Lepanam (APPSC 2019). Perini is the warrior dance described in Nritta Ratnavali, madanikas are the bracket figures at Ramappa, and Desi is the regional dance form contrasted with Marga.
n703148092e4.tq: Maiputa = Kusuma Lepanam (Satavahana); Perini = Kakatiya warrior dance.
xs: The Satavahana dancers' **'Maiputa'** is **Kusuma Lepanam** (**APPSC 2019**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Perini** is the warrior dance in **Nritta Ratnavali**; **madanikas** are Ramappa's bracket figures.
**Desi** is the regional dance form contrasted with **Marga**.
xa: Nritta Ratnavali was written by **Jayapa Senani**, Gaja Sahini under Ganapatideva.
Perini Shiva Tandavam was revived by **Nataraja Ramakrishna**.
**Kridabhiramam** calls Orugallu an **abode of drama artists and actors**.
n703148092e4.fixed: stem cites 'asked in APPSC 2019'; no exam words it so

nap-history-36-16.s: Which title was associated with Ketana?
nap-history-36-16.x: Ketana, a Kakatiya-period poet, bore the title Abhinava Dandi. Desha Bhakta was Konda Venkatappaiah's title, Kollabhighanda Vijayaditya IV's and Andhra Kesari Tanguturi Prakasam's.
nap-history-36-16.tq: Link each title to its holder.
n: Vijayaditya IV held the title Kollabhighanda. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Ketana held the title Abhinava Dandi. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Tanguturi Prakasam held the title Andhra Kesari. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Konda Venkatappaiah held the title Desha Bhakta. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
xs: **Ketana** of the **Kakatiya period** bore the title **Abhinava Dandi** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The notes link none of the other titles to Ketana.
xa: **Rudramadevi's** title: **Rayagaja Kesari**.
**Recharla Rudra's** title: **Kakatiya Stapanacharya**.
**Jayapa Senani** wrote the **Nritta Ratnavali**.

n630a3dc4a5b.s: Which temple at Pattadakal is built in the Nagara form?
n630a3dc4a5b.x: At Pattadakal the Papanatha temple is Nagara, while the Virupaksha temple is Dravida.
xa: **Nagara** = curvilinear shikhara; **Dravida** = pyramidal vimana, enclosure walls, gopurams.
**Vesara** = blend of both, stepped shikhara (Kakatiya temples).
Vahana and **dhvaja** pillar stand axially before the sanctum.

nfdfc649717d.s: Kakatiya temples represent which temple order?
nfdfc649717d.x: Kakatiya temples are Vesara, the stepped blend of Nagara and southern features.
xa: Dravida examples: **Eastern Chalukya** delta temples and **Vijayanagara** temples.
At **Pattadakal**, Nagara (**Papanatha**) and Dravida (**Virupaksha**) stand side by side.
⚠ **Shikhara** = north (Nagara); **vimana** = south (Dravida).

n6a3e90c40e8.s: A temple with three shrines on one plan is called a:
n6a3e90c40e8.x: A trikutalaya has three shrines on one plan, e.g. the Thousand Pillar temple.
xa: The **Thousand Pillar temple** (**1163**) is a Trikutalaya for **Shiva, Vishnu and Surya**, not Brahma.
Core parts: **Garbhagriha** (sanctum) + **mandapa** (hall).
⚠ **Shikhara** = north (Nagara); **vimana** = south (Dravida).

nbf05058a6a1.s: Which one of the following best describes the temple architecture of the Eastern Chalukyas in the Krishna-Godavari delta?
o: Pure Vesara style based on Hoysala models
Nagara style based entirely on northern prototypes
Dravidian style influenced by Pallava and Badami Chalukya forms, with increasing local features
Kalinga style introduced by the Eastern Gangas
nbf05058a6a1.x: Eastern Chalukya temples followed a Dravidian idiom influenced by Pallava and Badami Chalukya forms, while gradually acquiring local characteristics.
nbf05058a6a1.tq: Use the dynasty–style association and eliminate the swapped regional styles.
xs: Eastern Chalukya temples were **Dravidian**, drawing on **Pallava and Badami Chalukya** forms and growing **more local** — option **(3)** is correct.
They cluster in the **Krishna-Godavari delta**, built in **laterite and limestone**.
xa: Examples: **Draksharama Bhimeswara** (**Chalukya Bhima I**), **Kumararama** at Samalkot, the **Biccavole** group.
**Vijayaditya II** is credited with **108 temples**.
⚠ **APPSC 2025**: Biccavole's **Rajarajeswara** temple is **not** Rajaraja Narendra's.

n9568df3b8aa.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about temple architecture in Andhradesa?
o: The Chalukya-Chola style joined Pallava planning to early Chalukya elements
Vijayanagara temple architecture drew mainly on Hoysala and Kalinga styles
The Chalukya-Chola style became the model for the Godavari region
Kakatiya architecture is transitional between early Chalukyan and Vijayanagara styles
n9568df3b8aa.x: The statement that Vijayanagara architecture drew mainly on Hoysala and Kalinga styles is wrong; the other three are correct.
xa: Chalukya-Chola example: **Draksharama** (**APPSC 2025**).
Kakatiya style is also called **Chalukyan/Vesara**.
Vijayanagara hallmark: the **Sahasra Stambha Mandapa** (thousand-pillared hall).

n61bf3210c00.s: A 1233 CE Tamil-Grantha inscription recording the western gopuram is found at:
n61bf3210c00.x: At Siddhavatam in Kadapa, a 1233 CE Tamil-Grantha inscription of Chola Rajendra III records the western gopuram.
n61bf3210c00.tq: Combine inscription date, script, ruler and location to identify the site.
xs: The **1233 CE** Tamil-Grantha inscription on the **western gopuram** is at **Siddhavatam (Kadapa)** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was set up under Chola **Rajendra III**.
xa: Siddhavatam fort is the **southern gateway to Srisailam**, called **"Dakshin Kashi"**.
**Mangalagiri** has a **19th-century gopuram** about **153 ft** high.
**Draksharama** was built by **Chalukya Bhima I**.

nca84304aff3.x: Ramappa dates to 1213; the Thousand Pillar Temple is of 1163 and the Siddhavatam inscription of 1233.
xa: **Prolaya Vema Reddy** completed the steps to **Patalaganga**, Srisailam, in **1346**.
Ramappa became a **UNESCO** World Heritage Site in **2021**.
ASI restored the Thousand Pillar **Kalyana Mandapam** on **13 May 2026**.

nc0833bd8a42.s: Who built the Veera Siromandapam at Srisailam?
nc0833bd8a42.x: Anavema Reddy built the Veera Siromandapam; Prolaya Vema's 1346 work was completing the steps to Patalaganga.
xa: Siddhavatam has the **1233 CE** western gopuram inscription of Chola **Rajendra III**.
Srisailam's Shakti peetha is **Bhramaramba**.
Reddi fort building: **Kondaveedu**.

n44f60af227e.s: Kumararama, one of the Pancharamas, is located at:
n44f60af227e.x: Kumararama is at Samalkot (Chalukya Bhimavaram); Somarama is at Bhimavaram, Ksheerarama at Palakollu and Amararama at Amaravati.
xa: **Draksharama** is the fifth Pancharama — the most architecturally significant.
Kumararama has **Reddi** sculptural additions.
Shakti peethas: **Bhramaramba** (Srisailam), **Manikyamba** (Draksharama).

n17ed03dc8c4.s: Who revived the Perini Shiva Tandavam from the dance panels of the Ramappa Temple?
n17ed03dc8c4.x: Nataraja Ramakrishna revived the Perini Shiva Tandavam using the dance panels of Ramappa Temple.
n17ed03dc8c4.tq: Test the modern revivalist separately from the medieval ruler, commander and painter associated with the temple tradition.
xs: **Nataraja Ramakrishna** revived **Perini Shiva Tandavam** from the Ramappa panels — option **(4)** is correct.
**Jayapa Senani** wrote the **Nrittaratnavali**; **Machaladevi** was linked to Kakatiya **painting**; **Ganapatideva** was the king.
xa: Ramappa's **madanika** brackets show dance postures from Nrittaratnavali.
Nrittaratnavali covers **marga** and **desi** dance.
Ramappa is at **Palampet**.

n7eea1a653ac.s: In which year was the Ramappa Temple at Palampet inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
n7eea1a653ac.x: Ramappa (built 1213, famous for its Nrittaratnavali-based madanika brackets) became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021. The years 2014, 2017 and 2023 are distractors.
xs: Ramappa became a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **2021** — option **(3)** is correct.
It was built in **1213** and is famed for its **Nrittaratnavali**-based **madanika** brackets.
xa: Its **sandbox** foundation let it survive earthquakes.
It uses **floating bricks** and a **star-shaped platform**.
Its pillars are **black basalt** ekasila carvings.

n41ce7d2c32c.s: Which is the only temple in Andhra Pradesh with two flagpoles?
n41ce7d2c32c.x: Simhachalam, the temple of Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha, is the only AP temple with two flagpoles (APPSC 2002).
xa: **Krishnadevaraya** gifted Simhachalam a **diamond necklace**.
ASI documented **17 inscriptions in 1899** (South Indian Inscriptions Vol. VI).
Mukhalingam and Simhachalam show the **Kalinga** variant of **Nagara**.

n1817f4d4425.s: The Shakti peetha of Manikyamba is at:
n1817f4d4425.x: Manikyamba is associated with Draksharama, while Bhramaramba is associated with Srisailam.
xa: Draksharama is a **Pancharama**, built by **Chalukya Bhima I**.
Srisailam has Reddi works: **Patalaganga** steps (**1346**) and the **Veera Siromandapam**.
Srisailam, Draksharama and Samarlakota were renovated by the **Reddis**.

nap-history-6-14.s: The Trikoteswara Swamy Temple at Kotappa Konda is famous for which deity?
nap-history-6-14.x: Trikoteswara Swamy Temple at Kotappa Konda is a famous Lord Shiva temple. Kumara Swami, Ashtabhuja Narayana and Surya are deities of other shrines.
nap-history-6-14.tq: Recall the deity of each temple.
n: Trikoteswara Swamy Temple is located at Kotappa Konda. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
Trikoteswara Swamy Temple is famous as a Lord Shiva temple. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 11-12]
xs: The **Trikoteswara Swamy Temple** at **Kotappa Konda** is famous as a **Lord Shiva** temple — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Surya** is linked to **Arasavalli**, the famous **Sun Temple** of Andhra.
xa: **Simhachalam** — **Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha**; **Srikurmam** — **Kurma** avatar.
**Mukhalingam** — **Madhukeswara**.
**Srisailam** is the **Jyotirlinga**; its Shakti peetha is **Bhramaramba**.

nb519d530749.s: The Undavalli caves were excavated under which dynasty?
nb519d530749.x: The Undavalli caves (4th-5th c.) are Vishnukundina, cut top-down into a sandstone hill; the reclining Ananta Padmanabha is a Vishnukundina granite monolith.
xa: Kakatiya **black basalt** works: **Thousand Pillar Nandi**, **Ramappa** pillars (ekasila).
Kakatiya **sandbox** foundations helped **Ramappa** survive earthquakes.
Undavalli is in **Guntur**.

nf8850b862c5.s: The Kakatiya 'sandbox technology' used in temples such as Ramappa refers to:
o: Foundation pits filled with sand, stone chips and earth that cushioned the temple against earthquakes
Sand-cast bronze images placed in the garbhagriha
Hollow sand-filled pillars that lightened the vimana
A sand moat dug around the temple for defence
nf8850b862c5.x: Kakatiya builders filled foundation pits with sand, stone chips and earth to cushion temples on black cotton soil, which is why Ramappa survived earthquakes.
xa: Other Kakatiya innovations: **star-shaped platforms**, **floating bricks**.
The **Thousand Pillar Nandi** is a black basalt ekasila carving.
Ramappa became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in **2021**.

n13ea47968ab.s: The madanika bracket figures of the Ramappa Temple at Palampet were carved in
o: warrior postures based on military manuals
royal postures based on Chola inscriptions
meditative postures based on Buddhist texts
n13ea47968ab.x: The madanika bracket figures at Ramappa were carved in dance postures based on Jayapa Senani's Nrittaratnavali.
n13ea47968ab.tq: Match the artistic feature with the specific treatise rather than with a broad cultural category.
xs: Ramappa's **madanika** brackets are carved in **dance postures based on Nrittaratnavali** — option **(2)** is correct.
The treatise is **Jayapa Senani's** (**APPSC 2019**).
xa: Nrittaratnavali covers **marga** and **desi** dance.
**Nataraja Ramakrishna** revived **Perini Shiva Tandavam** from the Ramappa panels.
Exam angle: treatise → temple → author: **Nrittaratnavali – Jayapa – Ramappa**.

n65262429102.s: Kakatiya painting associated with ____ led on to the Lepakshi style.
n65262429102.x: Kakatiya painting associated with Machaladevi led on to the Lepakshi style.
xa: Vijayanagara's hallmark: the **Sahasra Stambha Mandapa**, peak of the pillared-hall tradition.
Vijayanagara also built **ornate gopurams**.
Kakatiya sculpture: Ramappa's **madanika** brackets from **Nrittaratnavali**.

n8e1c2e3957c.s: Kondaveedu, associated with Reddi fort building, is located in the:
n8e1c2e3957c.x: Kondaveedu lies in the Guntur–Palnadu area near Chilakaluripet. Its placement near Eluru in West Godavari is incorrect.
n8e1c2e3957c.tq: Apply the location trap by distinguishing the correct district region from a nearby but incorrect one.
xs: **Kondaveedu** is in the **Guntur-Palnadu area near Chilakaluripet** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes wrongly place it near **Eluru, West Godavari**.
xa: Kondaveedu fort is a **Reddi** work.
Reddis renovated and endowed **Draksharama**, **Samarlakota** and **Srisailam**.
**Siddhavatam** (Kadapa) is the southern gateway to **Srisailam**.

nd57b4d6e911.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler is credited with building 108 temples?
nd57b4d6e911.x: Vijayaditya II is credited with building 108 temples; Chalukya Bhima I built Draksharama.
xa: The **Biccavole group** is an Eastern Chalukya cluster.
Draksharama is cited as the **Chalukya-Chola** style.
**Kumararama** at Samalkot is another Eastern Chalukya temple.

n321b1566c90.s: Jayapa Senani, author of Nrittaratnavali, was a commander of:
n321b1566c90.x: Jayapa Senani was Ganapatideva's commander; his Nrittaratnavali covers both marga and desi dance.
xa: Ramappa's **madanika** brackets follow his Nrittaratnavali (**APPSC 2019**).
Ramappa became a UNESCO site in **2021**.
**Nataraja Ramakrishna** revived **Perini Shiva Tandavam** from the Ramappa panels.

n0959ed9532d.s: The Reddi kingdom was established approximately during which period?
n0959ed9532d.x: The Reddi kingdom flourished approximately from 1325 to 1448 CE. The Kondaveedu line continued from about 1325 to 1424, while the Rajamahendravaram line continued from 1402 to 1448.
n0959ed9532d.tq: Use the broad chronological range to distinguish the kingdom from the dates of individual ruling lines.
xs: The Reddi kingdom lasted **c. 1325–1448 CE** — option **(1)** is correct.
Two lines: **Kondaveedu** (**1325-1424**) and **Rajamahendravaram** (**1402-1448**).
xa: Reddi rule is called the **"second golden age"** of Telugu culture and literature.
The Reddis were one of three successor states after **1323**, with the **Musunuris** and the **Recherla Velamas**.
Kondaveedu fell to **Vijayanagara (Deva Raya II)** in **1424**; Rajahmundry to **Kapileswara Gajapati** in **1448**.

nab0ae712306.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the principal dynastic features of the Reddis?
o: Panta vamsam, Bull emblem, Mula Guramma as family deity and Sanskrit as royal language
Deseti kula, Garuda emblem, Durga as family deity and Telugu as royal language
Panta vamsam, Lion emblem, Mula Guramma as family deity and Prakrit as royal language
Yadava kula, Bull emblem, Lakshmi as family deity and Kannada as royal language
nab0ae712306.x: The Reddis belonged to the Panta vamsam, were also associated with the Deseti kula, used the Bull as their emblem, worshipped Mula Guramma and used Sanskrit as the royal language.
nab0ae712306.tq: Match several closely related dynastic identifiers and reject options containing one or more swapped features.
xs: The Reddis were of the **Panta Vamsam**, with the **Bull** emblem, **Mula Guramma** as family deity and **Sanskrit** as royal language — option **(1)** is correct.
Option 2 is wrong on emblem, deity and language, though **Deseti kula** is a valid Reddi identity.
xa: **Panta Rashtra** = the **Guduru** and **Muttembaka** areas of **Nellore**.
Many Reddi kings were **scholar-poets**.
Faith of the kings: **Pashupata Shaivism**; of the people: **Veerashaivism**.

n815644d922a.s: Prolaya Vema Reddi is credited with building how many forts, including Kondaveedu, Kondapalli and Dharanikota?
n815644d922a.x: Prolaya Vema Reddi is credited with building 74 forts, including Kondaveedu, Kondapalli and Dharanikota.
n815644d922a.tq: Test the exact quantitative figure while using nearby numerical distractors.
xs: **Prolaya Vema Reddi** built **74 forts**, including **Kondaveedu, Kondapalli and Dharanikota** — option **(2)** is correct.
He was the **founder** of the Reddi line, ruling **1324/1325-1353** from **Addanki**.
xa: He had served earlier in the court of **Prataparudra**.
He built steps to **Pathala Ganga at Srisailam** (done **1346**) and to **Ahobilam** hill.
Titles: **Dharma Pratishtana Nagarudu**, **Nissivu Bhudana Parasurama**.

na3403b590ee.s: Which fort replaced Addanki as the Reddi capital?
na3403b590ee.x: Kondaveedu replaced Addanki as the Reddi capital and later became a battleground between the Gajapatis and Vijayanagara.
xa: Both forts are credited to **Prolaya Vema Reddi**, builder of **74 forts**.
⚠ Placing Kondavidu "near **Eluru** in West Godavari" is wrong.
Gajapati **Kapileswara** attacked in **1448**; Kondaveedu fell to him around **1450**.

n0e696875acc.s: Which of the following represents the sequence of capitals of the Reddi kingdoms?
n0e696875acc.x: The capitals successively shifted from Addanki to Kondaveedu and later to Rajamahendravaram.
n0e696875acc.tq: Use the first-to-last sequence to eliminate options that reverse the capital shifts.
xs: Reddi capitals ran **Addanki → Kondaveedu → Rajamahendravaram** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Addanki** (Prakasam) was Prolaya Vema's capital; **Rajahmundry** was the second seat, **1402-1448**.
xa: The **Manyapuram** inscription credits the Addanki → Kondavidu move to **Anavota Reddi**.
The **APPSC G2 2012** key credits the move to **Anavema Reddi**.
**Kumaragiri** carved out the **Rajahmundry** division.

n0905f6aea88.s: The Manyapuram inscription is particularly associated with which event in Reddi history?
o: The restoration of Veerabhadra Reddi in 1429
The establishment of Addanki as the first capital by Prolaya Vema Reddi
The shifting of the capital from Addanki to Kondavidu by Anavota Reddi
The creation of the Rajahmundry division by Kumaragiri Reddi
n0905f6aea88.x: The Manyapuram inscription records the shifting of the capital to Kondavidu by Anavota Reddi.
n0905f6aea88.tq: Link an inscription with the specific administrative event it records, not merely with the dynasty.
xs: The **Manyapuram inscription** records **Anavota Reddi's** move of the capital from **Addanki to Kondavidu** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **Kaluvacheru inscription (1423)** was issued by **Anitalli** after the recapture of Rajahmundry.
xa: The **Srisailam** inscription (**1346**) records Prolaya Vema's Patala Ganga steps.
**Sarpavaram** records Kataya Vema's family and treaty with Harihara II.
⚠ The APPSC G2 2012 key credits the same move to **Anavema**.

n5040f8b1f2a.s: The Kaluvacheru inscription of 1423 was issued after which event?
o: The seizure of Kondavidu by Pedakomati Vema
The construction of Patala Ganga steps at Srisailam
The abolition of the gold tax by Anavota
n5040f8b1f2a.x: Anitalli issued the Kaluvacheru inscription in 1423 after the recapture of Rajahmundry. It also provides information on the Musunuri-led liberation and Prolaya Vema Reddi’s service under the Nayakas.
n5040f8b1f2a.tq: Associate an inscription with its date and the event immediately preceding its issue.
xs: **Anitalli** issued the **Kaluvacheru inscription** in **1423** after the **recapture of Rajahmundry** — option **(1)** is correct.
**1402** was Pedakomati's seizure of Kondavidu; the **Patala Ganga** steps were finished in **1346**.
xa: Kaluvacheru is a key source on the **Musunuri-led liberation**.
It also records **Prolaya Vema Reddi's** service under the **Nayakas**.
**Veerabhadra** and his brother **Vema** recovered Rajahmundry in **1423**.

n1c71b237663.s: Which religious combination is correctly associated with the Reddi period?
n1c71b237663.x: The Reddi kings followed Pashupata Shaivism, while the people largely followed Veerashaivism.
n1c71b237663.tq: Use the kings-versus-people comparison to avoid reversing the two sectarian affiliations.
xs: Reddi **kings** followed **Pashupata Shaivism**; the **people** followed **Veerashaivism** — option **(4)** is correct.
Option 2 swaps them; Buddhism and Jainism are not the Reddi faiths.
xa: **Bhairava** and **Mailara** worship were common.
Reddi kings were disciples of **Ghoderayacharulu** (Tripurantakam).
Later the Reddis moved towards **Vaishnavism** (Kumaragiri, Kataya Vema).

n60aba817b0a.s: The Reddi rule, approximately dated from 1325 to 1448, is described as which of the following?
o: The beginning of the Bahmani golden age
The second golden age of Telugu culture
The final age of Chola imperial expansion
The first golden age of Sanskrit culture in the Deccan
n60aba817b0a.x: Reddi rule, approximately from 1325 to 1448, is called the second golden age of Telugu culture.
n60aba817b0a.tq: Combine the date range with the distinctive historical label instead of selecting a generic golden-age description.
xs: Reddi rule (**c. 1325-1448**) is called the **second golden age of Telugu culture** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was the **peak of Telugu literature before Vijayanagara**, and the kings were themselves authors.
xa: Court poets: **Errana** and **Srinatha**.
Royal language **Sanskrit**; emblem the **bull**; faith **Pashupata Shaivism**.
Lineage: **Panta Vamsam** (**Deseti kula**); family deity **Mula Guramma**.
Capitals in sequence: **Addanki → Kondavidu → Rajahmundry**.

n6cec2f0d383.s: Kavyalankara Chudamani, linked to Rajahmundry as a literary hub, was written by:
n6cec2f0d383.x: Kavyalankara Chudamani is by Vinnakota Peddana; Sivalila Vilasamu is by Sivaleka Kommana and Kashikhandam by Srinatha.
xa: The Rajahmundry court under **Kataya Vema** was a competitive literary centre.
**Kataya Vema Reddi** wrote **Kumaragiri Rajiyam**, a commentary on Kalidasa's three plays.
After Kondaveedu fell (**1424**), Srinatha joined the Rajahmundry court under **Veerabhadra Reddi**.

nf6cecf23be4.s: The Anavemagiri mandapas at Simhachalam were built by:
nf6cecf23be4.x: Anavema Reddi built the Anavemagiri mandapas at Simhachalam and the Veera Siromandapam at Srisailam.
xa: His danas were guided by **Vemadri Pandit**.
Officials: minister **Mamidi Peddanamatya**; army chief **Chennamanayaka**.
Titles: **Rachuru Durga Vibhala** (APPSC G2 2017), **Andhra Suratrana** (APPSC G2 2011).

nb841bd349fe.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the early political career of Prolaya Vema Reddi?
o: He served in the court of Prataparudra and expelled Tughluq forces from coastal Andhra around 1325.
He served in the court of Deva Raya I and conquered Kalinga around 1404.
He served in the court of Firoz Shah and captured Rajahmundry around 1396.
He served in the court of Harihara II and expelled Gajapati forces from Kondaveedu around 1450.
nb841bd349fe.x: Prolaya Vema Reddi had served in Prataparudra's court and expelled Tughluq forces from coastal Andhra around 1325, with one account placing the event in 1324.
nb841bd349fe.tq: Match the founder with his patron court, enemy and approximate date.
xs: **Prolaya Vema Reddi** served in **Prataparudra's** court and **expelled Tughluq forces** from coastal Andhra c. **1325** — option **(1)** is correct.
Some notes date the expulsion to **1324**.
xa: He belonged to the **Panta** clan.
He made **Addanki** his capital.
The **Kaluvacheru** inscription also records his service under the **Nayakas**.

nf965e06feb9.s: Which of the following was NOT among Anavema Reddi's conquests from the Kalinga Gajapatis?
nf965e06feb9.x: Anavema took Nidadavolu, Rajahmundry, Pithapuram, Simhachalam and Konaseema; Kandukur is not among them.
xa: Kandukur was the seat of **Mallareddi's** branch; a Bahmani attack on it was repelled in **1398**.
**Deva Raya I** later annexed the **Kandukuru Reddis**.
Anavema defeated the Kalinga Gajapatis with **Padmanayaka** and **Vijayanagara** help.

ne05f0361d1a.s: Which Reddi ruler is described as the most charitable among the Reddi kings?
ne05f0361d1a.x: Anavema Reddi is noted as the most charitable Reddi king.
ne05f0361d1a.tq: Match the evaluative distinction with the correct ruler.
xs: **Anavema Reddi** was the **most charitable** Reddi king — option **(2)** is correct.
His danas: **agraharas**, **Brahmanda**, **Kalpataru**, **Kanakadhara**, **Gosahasra** — guided by **Vemadri Pandit**.
**Racha Vema** was hated for the **Puriti** tax.
xa: Anavema (**1364-1386**) is also called the **greatest** Reddi.
Titles: **Rajashri Ramani**, **Vasantarayadu**.
He built the **Veerashiro Mantapa** at Srisailam.

n7364d649ddb.s: In which year did Pedakomati Vema oust Kumaragiri Reddi?
n7364d649ddb.x: Pedakomati Vema ousted Kumaragiri in 1402, after which Kumaragiri fled to Rajahmundry.
xa: Kumaragiri died in refuge at Rajahmundry.
The rivalry ended with **Kondavidu's fall (1424)**.
Kataya Vema was killed at **Kakaraparthi (1414)**.

n5b873c20289.s: The crop share given to village Ayagars as remuneration was called:
n5b873c20289.x: Ayagars were paid in Manyam land or through a crop share called Mera.
xa: There were **12 Ayagars**, a **Kakatiya** pattern.
Ayagar lands, temple lands and Brahmin grants were **tax-exempt**.
**Karnam**, **Reddi** and **Talari** held judicial and police powers.

nf7b34b67ef3.s: In Kakatiya usage, Pullari was a tax on:
nf7b34b67ef3.x: Pullari was the cattle-grazing tax; Illari was the house tax, Ari the land tax and Kanika the gifts.
xa: **Puriti Pannu** = tax on childbirth (**Rachavema**).
Inherited Kakatiya taxes: **Kanika**, **Pullari**, **Pannu**, **Siddhayam**, **Sangam**, **Darshanam**, **Niruvidi**, **Ardhayam**.
**Anavota** abolished the tax on gold.

n8771d8a5974.s: Which Reddi ruler levied the oppressive 'Puriti Pannu' and was killed by his own people for it?
n8771d8a5974.x: Racha Vema Reddi (1420-1424), the last Kondaveedu Reddi ruler, levied the Puriti Pannu (a tax on childbirth) and was killed by the public (APPSC G2 2019; PYQ 2018). Kumaragiri is known for Vasantotsavams and Anavema for charities. Anavota abolished a tax (on gold) rather than imposing one.
n8771d8a5974.tq: Puriti Pannu = Rachavema, the last Kondaveedu ruler, killed by his people.
xs: **Racha Vema Reddi** levied the **Puriti Pannu** and was **killed by his own people** — option **(3)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2019**; PYQ **2018**).
He was the **last Kondaveedu ruler** (**1420-1424**).
**Kumaragiri** is known for **Vasantotsavams**; **Anavema** for **charities**; **Anavota** **abolished** the gold tax.
xa: Puriti Pannu = tax on the **delivery of a child**.
It is the textbook example of burdensome taxation in the **late, weakened Reddi phase**.
Rachavema also cut the **Jaganobbaganda** canals to feed his mother **Surambika's** tank.

n9489f04310d.s: Who was the brother of Prolaya Vema Reddi associated with the capture of Motupalli?
n9489f04310d.x: Mallareddi, the brother of Prolaya Vema Reddi, took Motupalli from Hasan Gangu of the Bahmani Sultanate.
n9489f04310d.tq: Separate a family relationship from ministerial and military offices.
xs: **Mallareddi (Mallaya Reddy)**, Prolaya Vema's brother, took **Motupalli** by defeating **Hasan Gangu** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kataya Vema** was Kumaragiri's brother-in-law; **Chennamanayaka** and **Mamidi Peddanamatya** were **Anavema's** army chief and minister.
xa: Hasan Gangu was the **Bahmani** founder.
**Anavota** later developed the Motupalli dock.
The **Kandukur** branch was Mallareddi's line.

n4b7e3e4d76a.s: Who constructed the Jaganobbaganda canals to supply water to the tank dug by Surambika?
o: Somaya, the minister of Anavota Reddi
n4b7e3e4d76a.x: Racha Vema, the son of Surambika, constructed the Jaganobbaganda canals to feed water into the tank dug by his mother.
n4b7e3e4d76a.tq: Identify the family relationship first, then connect the person with the associated irrigation work.
xs: **Racha Vema**, Surambika's **son**, cut the **'Jaganobbaganda'** canals to feed her tank — option **(3)** is correct.
**Surambika** was the wife of **Pedakomati Vema Reddi**.
xa: Tank name: **Govardhana Samudram** (APPSC G2 2019) or **Santana Sagaram** (APPSC GS 2018).
Royal women took an active part in welfare works such as tanks.
Racha Vema was the last Kondaveedu ruler, killed over the **Puriti** tax.

n699dfc559f3.s: Errana's Harivamsam was dedicated to which ruler?
n699dfc559f3.x: Errana dedicated his Harivamsam to Prolaya Vema Reddi.
n699dfc559f3.tq: This tests the author–patron relationship directly, a common history question pattern.
xs: **Errana's Harivamsam** was dedicated to **Prolaya Vema Reddi** — option **(2)** is correct.
Errana was his court poet at **Addanki** (PYQ G2 2011).
xa: Errana also wrote **Nrisimha Puranam** (PYQ G2 2017) and a **Ramayana**.
Titles: **Prabandha Parameswara**, **Sambhudasa**.
He completed the Telugu **Mahabharata** — last of the **Kavitrayam**.

na099326a64e.s: Which one of the following works of Srinatha is specifically associated with Bhimeswara of Draksharamam?
na099326a64e.x: Bhimakhandam, also known as Bhimeswara Puranam, praises Bhimeswara of Draksharamam.
na099326a64e.tq: Use the work–theme association rather than confusing similarly named literary titles.
xs: **Bhimakhandam**, also called **Bhimeswara Puranam**, praises **Bhimeswara of Draksharamam** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Haravilasam** describes the **Motupalli sea trade** and was dedicated to **Tippayya Setti**.
**Sringara Naishadham** is based on **Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita**, dedicated to **Mamidi Singana**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say Bhimakhandam is about the **Bhima river** — the main reading is the **Draksharamam** deity.
**Draksharama Bhimesvara** is one of the **Pancharama** shrines renovated in the Reddi era (Godavari region).
Other Srinatha works: **Palnati Veeracharitra**, **Maruttarat Charitra**, **Sivaratri Mahatyam**, **Kasikhandam**.

nap-history-2-5.s: Who was the last ruler of the Kondaveedu Reddy kingdom?
nap-history-2-5.x: Racha Vema Reddy was the last ruler of the Kondaveedu Reddy line.
n: Vasanta Raju was the last Reddy king. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 5-6]
Errana was the last poet of the Kavitrayam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 5-6]
Errana was the court poet of Prolaya Vema Reddy. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 5-6]
xa: Racha Vema was killed by his own people over the **Puriti tax**; Kondavidu fell to **Vijayanagara (Deva Raya II)** in **1424**.
Errana's titles: **Prabandha Parameswara**, **Sambhudasa**; he wrote **Harivamsa** and **Nrisimha Puranam**.
Errana translated the remaining part (**Seshabhaga**) of the **Aranya Parva**, completing the Telugu Mahabharata.

nap-history-21-13.s: Saptha Sathi Saara Teeka was written by:
nap-history-21-13.x: Pedakomati Vema Reddy wrote Sahitya Chintamani and Saptha Sathi Saara Teeka.
n: Pedakomati Vema Reddy wrote Sahitya Chintamani. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
Pedakomati Vema Reddy wrote Saptha Sathi Saara Teeka. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
Bammera Potana wrote Narayana Satakam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
xa: Pedakomati's other works: **Sangeeta Chintamani** (music), **Srungara Deepika**.
His court poet **Vamana Bhanu Bhattu** wrote **Kanaka Rekha Kalyanam** and **Usha Parinayam**.
Pedakomati's title: **Sarvagna**.

nap-history-21-19.s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Bammera Potana?
nap-history-21-19.x: Sahitya Chintamani was written by Pedakomati Vema Reddy; Potana wrote Narayana Satakam, Andhra Bhagavatam and Bhogini Dandakam.
n: Pedakomati Vema Reddy wrote Sahitya Chintamani. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
Bammera Potana wrote Andhra Bhagavatam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
Bammera Potana wrote Narayana Satakam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
Bammera Potana wrote Bogini Dandakam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
xa: Potana also wrote **Virabhadra Vijayam**.
Potana was a **contemporary** of **Pedakomati Vema Reddy** and **Srinatha**.
Pedakomati's **Sangeeta Chintamani** is a **work on music**.

n081438972dc.s: Anavema Reddi defeated the Kalinga Gajapatis with the assistance of
n081438972dc.x: Anavema Reddi defeated the Kalinga Gajapatis with assistance from the Padmanayakas and Vijayanagara.
n081438972dc.tq: Identify the allied powers rather than the defeated opponent.
xs: Anavema beat the **Kalinga Gajapatis** with help from **the Padmanayakas and Vijayanagara** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **Bahmanis** were Reddi enemies (Hasan Gangu, Firoz Shah), not allies here.
xa: Gains: **Nidadavolu**, **Rajahmundry**, **Pithapuram**, **Simhachalam**, **Konaseema**.
Anavota had earlier halted the **Kalinga Gangas** on the **Krishna**.
**Kataya Vema** later raided up to **Cuttack**.

n663d3c9f7b9.s: Which Rajamahendravaram figure was killed at Kakaraparthi in 1414 by Gajaraju Tippa?
n663d3c9f7b9.x: Kataya Vema was killed at Kakaraparthi (1414) by Gajaraju Tippa; Allada Reddi then ran the state as regent.
xa: Allada's sons **Vema Reddi**, **Veerabhadra Reddi** and **Doddareddi** helped him in the east.
**Anitalli**, Kataya Vema's daughter, married **Veerabhadra Reddi**.
The line ended with **Veerabhadra** and **Vema** when **Kapileswara Gajapati** took Rajahmundry (**1448**).

n6cfa126c091.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the role of Vijayanagara in Allada Reddi's conflict?
o: Deva Raya I supported Kataya Vema against the Kondavidu forces.
Mallappa Odayar founded the Rajahmundry branch of the Reddis.
Kapileswara Gajapati allied with Allada Reddi against Kondavidu.
Deva Raya II supported Annadeva in capturing Vengi.
n6cfa126c091.x: Deva Raya I of Vijayanagara backed Kataya Vema, making Vijayanagara an ally of Allada Reddi's side.
n6cfa126c091.tq: Identify the correct ally by matching the ruler with the action attributed to him.
xs: **Deva Raya I** of Vijayanagara backed **Kataya Vema** — option **(1)** is correct, making Vijayanagara **Allada Reddi's ally**.
**Annadeva** took Vengi with **Velama** support, not Deva Raya II's; **Kapileswara Gajapati** later annexed Rajahmundry.
**Mallappa Odayar** was a Vijayanagara commander who came to help in **1444**.
xa: Pedakomati beat Kataya Vema and **Deva Raya I's** army at **Attili-Kakaraparthi**.
The **Sarpavaram** treaty married **Harihara II's** daughter to Kataya's son.
**Deva Raya II** restored the Reddis as feudatories in **1429**.

n8c0cb63bb04.s: Annadeva captured parts of Vengi from Allada Reddi with the support of the:
n8c0cb63bb04.x: Annadeva captured parts of Vengi with Velama support, one of the challenges faced by Allada Reddi.
xa: Allada's ally was **Vijayanagara**.
Allada was helped in the east by his sons **Vema Reddi**, **Veerabhadra Reddi**, **Doddareddi**.
Kataya Vema was killed by **Gajaraju Tippa**, Pedakomati's ally.

na718e53d9e9.s: What was the immediate political consequence of the fall of Kondavidu in 1424?
o: Rajahmundry became a Gajapati province immediately.
Kondavidu became independent of both Vijayanagara and the Gajapati kingdom.
Rajahmundry survived for another 24 years as a Vijayanagara feudatory.
The Reddi rule over Rajahmundry ended in 1402.
na718e53d9e9.x: Although Kondavidu fell in 1424, Rajahmundry continued for another 24 years as a feudatory of Vijayanagara.
na718e53d9e9.tq: Distinguish the fall of one branch from the continued survival of the other branch.
xs: After Kondavidu fell in **1424**, **Rajahmundry survived another 24 years as a Vijayanagara feudatory** — option **(3)** is correct.
Kondavidu itself fell to **Vijayanagara (Deva Raya II)**.
Rajahmundry was annexed by **Kapileswara Gajapati** only in **1446-48**.
xa: Kondavidu's last ruler **Racha Vema** was killed by his own people over the **Puriti** tax.
**Srinatha** moved to the Rajahmundry court (patron **Veerabhadra Reddi**) after **1424**.
**Deva Raya I** annexed the **Kandukuru Reddis**.

nde791a51faf.s: Who expelled Veerabhanu Deva up to Simhachalam and restored the Reddis as feudatories?
nde791a51faf.x: Deva Raya II expelled Veerabhanu Deva up to Simhachalam and restored the Reddis as Vijayanagara feudatories.
nde791a51faf.tq: Apply the who-did-what test to distinguish the two Deva Rayas.
xs: **Deva Raya II** expelled **Veerabhanu Deva** up to **Simhachalam** and restored the Reddis as feudatories (**1429**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Deva Raya I** backed **Kataya Vema** earlier; **Mallappa Odayar** came to help in **1444**; **Kapileswara** annexed Rajahmundry later.
xa: After Deva Raya II's death, **Kapileswara Gajapati** annexed Rajahmundry (**1446-48**).
Deva Raya II also ended the **Kondavidu** line in **1424**.
Srinatha defeated **Gauda Dindima Bhatta**, court poet of **Devaraya II**.

n4601603396a.s: Which Gajapati ruler annexed Rajahmundry during 1446–48?
n4601603396a.x: After the death of Deva Raya II, Kapileswara Gajapati annexed Rajahmundry (1446–48).
xa: Kapileswara attacked in **1448**; Kondaveedu fell to him around **1450**.
The last Rajahmundry rulers were **Veerabhadra Reddi** and **Vema Reddi**.
After Rajahmundry fell (**1448**), **Srinatha** lived in poverty in **Palnadu**.

n2ccc3ee6ea4.s: Kondavidu passed to Vijayanagara in 1424 during the reign of:
n2ccc3ee6ea4.x: After the death of Racha Vema Reddi, Kondavidu passed to Vijayanagara under Deva Raya II in 1424.
xa: After **1424**, **Srinatha** joined the Rajahmundry Reddis (patron **Veerabhadra Reddi**).
Rajahmundry survived another **24 years** as a Vijayanagara feudatory.
Gajapati **Kapileswara** took Kondaveedu around **1450**.

n2b57b7e51db.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the end of the Rajahmundry branch of Reddi rule?
o: It was absorbed into Kondavidu after the fall of Racha Vema.
It was conquered by Deva Raya I in 1402.
It was annexed by Kapileswara Gajapati of Orissa in 1448.
It ended with the death of Kataya Vema in 1424.
n2b57b7e51db.x: The Rajahmundry branch, ruled at the end by Veerabhadra Reddi and Vema Reddi, was ended by Kapileswara Gajapati of Orissa in 1448.
n2b57b7e51db.tq: Distinguish the separate endings of the Kondavidu and Rajahmundry branches.
xs: The Rajahmundry branch was **annexed by Kapileswara Gajapati of Orissa in 1448** — option **(3)** is correct.
Its last rulers were **Veerabhadra Reddi** and **Vema Reddi**.
**Kataya Vema** died at **Kakaraparthi** in **1414**, not 1424.
xa: Kapileswara took **Cuttack** in **1435** and pressed on the Reddis.
A **1444** Draksharama inscription records **Mallappa Odayar** coming to help.
After Rajahmundry fell, **Srinatha** lived in poverty in **Palnadu**.

ne02d434c6d1.s: The village administrative system of the Reddis included how many Ayagars?
ne02d434c6d1.x: A Reddi village had twelve Ayagars, or village servants.
ne02d434c6d1.tq: Identify the exact numerical value instead of confusing the total with the principal office-holders.
xs: A Reddi village had **twelve (12) Ayagars** (village servants) — option **(2)** is correct.
The pattern was **inherited from the Kakatiyas**.
xa: Key Ayagars: **Karnam** (accountant), **Reddi/Peddakapu** (headman), **Talari** (watchman).
They were paid in **Manyam** land or a crop share (**Mera**).
The same decentralised pattern continued under the **Gajapatis**.

n609adb636df.s: The warrior-farmer backbone of Kakatiya–Reddi society, supplying most soldiers, was formed by:
n609adb636df.x: Kammas, Kapus, Reddis and Velamas formed the warrior-farmer backbone and supplied most of the soldiers.
xa: **Komatis** ran inland and coastal trade.
Village administration also continued in the same decentralised pattern under the Gajapatis.
Village servants: the **12 Ayagars**.

n8fe8aeeccad.s: The Kaluvacheru inscription was issued by Anithalli, the wife of which ruler?
n8fe8aeeccad.x: Anithalli, wife of Veerabhadra Reddi, issued the Kaluvacheru inscription.
n8fe8aeeccad.tq: Apply the relationship trap by matching the named queen with the correct husband.
xs: **Anithalli** was the wife of **Veerabhadra Reddi** — option **(1)** is correct.
She was the daughter of **Kataya Vema Reddi** and his **rightful heir**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes call her "**Allada Reddi's** wife" — most say Veerabhadra's, which is followed.
Veerabhadra was **Allada's second son** and nominal king (restored **1423** and **1429**).
The **Kaluvacheru inscription** dates to **1423**.

n53823713ba3.s: The Ghoderayas, whose disciples included the Reddi kings, propagated Shaivism from:
n53823713ba3.x: The Ghoderayas spread Shaivism from Tripurantakam; the Vadagalai matha was at Ahobilam.
xa: Vadagalai is **Vedanta Desika's** line.
**Kumaragiri** and **Kataya Vema** were Vaishnava patrons.
Kings: **Pashupata Shaivism**; people: **Veerashaivism**.

nebf11294d29.s: The musical instrument 'Jalakaranda', associated with the Reddi court of Kumaragiri, is mentioned in which inscription?
nebf11294d29.x: The Dharmasagara inscription mentions the 'Jalakaranda' (PYQ G2 2019). The Manyapuram inscription records Anavota's capital shift, Kaluvacheru was issued by Anitalli in 1423, and Sarpavaram concerns Kataya Vema's family and treaty with Harihara II.
xs: **'Jalakaranda'** is mentioned in the **Dharmasagara inscription** (**PYQ G2 2019**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Manyapuram** records Anavota's capital shift; **Kaluvacheru** was issued by **Anitalli** (**1423**); **Sarpavaram** concerns Kataya Vema's family.
xa: Kumaragiri's court dancer: **Lakumadevi**.
**Vasantotsavam** was the most popular festival, funded by **Avachi Tippaya Setti**.
**Pedakomati** wrote **Sangeeta Chintamani** on music.

n710a2e1aed5.s: In which year did Gajarao Tippa defeat Firoz Shah's army at Kambhammetta?
n710a2e1aed5.x: Gajarao Tippa defeated Firoz Shah's army at Kambhammetta in 1396; the Bahmani attack on Kandukur was repelled in 1398.
xa: Senani **Mallareddy** drove Bahmani forces from **Amaravati** and restored the **Amareswara** temple.
Mallaya Reddy was **Prolaya Vema's brother**.
**Sivalinga Reddi** of Kandukuru wrote **Tatva Prakashika**.

nba4d1ba00e7.s: The Sarpavaram inscription records the marriage of Kataya Vema's son to Vijayalakshmi, daughter of:
nba4d1ba00e7.x: The Sarpavaram inscription refers to a treaty in which Harihara II gave his daughter Vijayalakshmi in marriage to Kataya Vema's son.
xa: Srisailam was later returned to Vijayanagara.
**Deva Raya I** of Vijayanagara later backed **Kataya Vema**.
Kataya Vema's title: **Kataka Churakara**.

nefd5be5087b.s: The Reddi kingdoms emerged as one of the three successor states after 1323 along with which two states?
nefd5be5087b.x: The Reddis were one of three successor political formations after 1323, the other two being the Musunuris and the Recherla Velamas.
nefd5be5087b.tq: Use the three-state comparison and eliminate dynasties that belonged to different political contexts.
xs: The Reddis were one of three successor states after **1323**, with the **Musunuris and Recherla Velamas** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The other options (Cholas, Hoysalas, Vijayanagara, Bahmanis) are not the post-**1323** successor trio named in the notes.
xa: The Reddi period is **c. 1325-1448**: Kondaveedu line **1325-1424**, Rajamahendravaram line **1402-1448**.
**Prolaya Vema Reddi** expelled **Tughluq** forces from coastal Andhra c. **1325**.
⚠ **Singabhupala II** (Sangeeta Sudhakaram) was a **Recherla Velama** of **Rachakonda**, not a Reddi.
The Reddis expelled the **Velamas** from Palnadu at the **Battle of Bhimavaram** (APPSC G2 2019 key).

nap-history-42-7.s: Which Reddy ruler was an expert in Bharata Natya?
nap-history-42-7.x: Kumaragiri Reddy was an expert in dance and wrote Vasantarajeeyam on it. Pedakomati Vema Reddy wrote Sangeeta Chintamani, Prolaya Vema Reddy founded the kingdom, and Ganapatideva was a Kakatiya.
nap-history-42-7.tq: Recall the Reddy ruler linked with dance.
n: Kumaragiri Reddy belonged to the Reddy dynasty. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 53-54]
Kumaragiri Reddy was an expert in Bharata Natya. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 53-54]
xs: **Kumaragiri Reddy** was an **expert** in **Bharata Natya** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He wrote **Vasantarajeeyam**, a Sanskrit work on dance; **Pedakomati Vema Reddy** wrote **Sangeeta Chintamani** on music.
**Prolaya Vema Reddy** founded the kingdom in **1324**; **Ganapatideva** was not a Reddy ruler.
xa: Kumaragiri's title: **Karpura Vasanta Rayalu**; he celebrated **Vasantotsavam** grandly.
His court dancer **Lakumadevi** (APPSC G2 **2012**) was renowned in Bharatanatyam.
Kumaragiri occupied the throne **after Anavema Reddy** (**1386-1402**).
⚠ **Kumaragiri Rajiyam** is by **Kataya Vema Reddi**, his brother-in-law.

nap-history-42-11.s: Surambika Reddy was the queen of which ruler?
nap-history-42-11.x: Surambika was the queen of Pedakomati Vema Reddy and dug the Santana Sagaram tank. Kumaragiri and Prolaya Vema were other Reddy kings, and Ganapatideva was a Kakatiya.
nap-history-42-11.tq: Link each queen to her king.
xs: **Surambika Reddy** was the **queen** of **Pedakomati Vema Reddy** — so option **(2)** is correct.
She **excavated** the **Santana Sagaram tank**.
xa: Tank name keys differ: **Govardhana Samudram** (APPSC G2 **2019**) vs **Santana Sagaram** (APPSC GS **2018**); also **Santana Payonidhi**.
Their son **Rachavema** cut canals (**'Jaganobbaganda'**) to feed the queen's tank.
**Anitalli**, daughter of **Kataya Vema Reddi**, married **Veerabhadra Reddi**.

nap-history-35-14.s: Who occupied the Reddi throne after Anavema Reddy?
nap-history-35-14.x: In the Kondaveedu line Prolaya Vema was followed by Anavema, and Anavema by Kumaragiri Reddy.
xa: **Anavema Reddi** (greatest): **1364-1386**; **Kumaragiri Reddi**: **1386-1402**.
In **1402** **Pedakomati** seized Kondavidu; Kumaragiri fled to **Rajahmundry** and died there.
**Racha Vema Reddi** (**1420-1424**) was the last Kondavidu ruler.

nap-history-44-11.x: Dharma Durgavibhala was Prolaya Vema Reddy's title; Pedakomati Vema Reddy was known as Sarvagna.
n: Prolaya Vema Reddy is known by the title Dharma Durgavibhala. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 55-56]
Pedakomati Vema Reddy is known by the title Sarvagna. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 55-56]
xa: Pedakomati (**1402-1420**) wrote **Sangeeta Chintamani**, **Sahitya Chintamani**, **Srngara Dipika**.
His court poets: **Srinatha** and **Vamana Bhatta Bana**.
Pedakomati died fighting the **Velamas** in **1420**.

nap-history-21-17.x: Bogini Dandakam is by Bammera Potana, a contemporary of Pedakomati Vema Reddy and Srinatha.
n: Bammera Potana was a contemporary of Pedakomati Vema Reddy. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
Bammera Potana was a contemporary of Srinatha. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
Bammera Potana wrote Bogini Dandakam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
xa: Other works: **Andhra Bhagavatam** (**Maha Bhagavatha**), **Narayana Satakam**, **Virabhadra Vijayam**.
**Kumaragiri Reddy** wrote **Vasantha Rajeeyam**.
**Marana** wrote **Markandeya Purana**.

n98f1d08fb90.s: Which architectural work at Srisailam is attributed to Anavema Reddi?
n98f1d08fb90.x: Anavema Reddi built the Veerashiro Mantapa at Srisailam. The Anavemagiri mandapas were built by him at Simhachalam, while the steps to Ahobilam are associated with Prolaya Vema.
n98f1d08fb90.tq: Distinguish monuments by ruler and location.
xs: At **Srisailam**, Anavema built the **Veerashiro Mantapa (Veera Siromandapam)** (**APPSC G2 2011**) — option **(3)** is correct.
