The **Anavemagiri mandapas** are his too, but at **Simhachalam**; the **Ahobilam** steps were **Prolaya Vema's**.
The **Amareswara temple** was restored by **Vallaya Vemana**, Anavota's minister.
xa: Prolaya Vema built the **Patala Ganga** steps at Srisailam (**1346**).
Reddi endowments: **Srisailam**, **Simhachalam**, **Ahobilam** and the **Pancharamas**.
Reddi kings were disciples of **Ghoderayacharulu** (Tripurantakam).

n12f5e4771e4.s: Pedakomati Vema, who opposed Kumaragiri's accession, was pacified by being made the feudatory of:
n12f5e4771e4.x: Kumaragiri made Pedakomati Vema the feudatory of Chandolu and designated him heir.
xa: Kataya Vema took charge in **1395**; Pedakomati **resented** the division.
In **1402** Pedakomati seized **Kondavidu** and ousted Kumaragiri.
Kumaragiri was a **patron of dance** and celebrated **Vasantotsavams**.

na5d5edeff56.s: In 1404, Pedakomati Vema recovered lost territory from:
na5d5edeff56.x: Pedakomati Vema recovered lost land from Vijayanagara in 1404.
xa: Kataya Vema took **Tripurantakam** and **Vinukonda** from Vijayanagara (Srisailam later returned).
The **Sarpavaram** inscription records the treaty marrying Harihara's daughter **Vijayalakshmi** to Kataya's son.
**Anavema** defeated the **Kalinga Gajapatis**; Kataya Vema raided up to **Cuttack**.

na217945e0b6.s: During the Reddi period, Devadasis trained in music, dance and ritual were respected performers at:
na217945e0b6.x: Devadasis were respected performers at Shiva temples, including the Pancharamas.
xa: The Reddis **renovated and endowed** the Pancharama shrines.
Reddi-era renovations: **Draksharama Bhimesvara**, **Samarlakota Kumararama**.
Court dancer **Lakumadevi** served **Kumaragiri**.

nf31ccdac1f6.s: 'Sangeeta Chintamani', a work on music, was written by which Reddi ruler?
nf31ccdac1f6.x: Pedakomati Vema Reddi, the scholar-king (1402-1420), wrote Sangeeta Chintamani (PYQ 2011, 2019) as well as Sahitya Chintamani and Srngara Dipika. Kumaragiri wrote Vasantarajiyam on dance, and Kataya Vema wrote Kumaragiri Rajiyam. No work is credited to Anavema.
nf31ccdac1f6.tq: Sangeeta Chintamani = Pedakomati Vema. Do not confuse it with Sangeeta Sudhakaram, which is Velama Singabhupala's.
xs: **Sangeeta Chintamani** (music) was written by **Pedakomati Vema Reddi** (PYQ **2011**, **2019**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kumaragiri** wrote **Vasanta Rajiyam** (dance); **Kataya Vema** wrote **Kumaragiri Rajiyam**.
xa: Pedakomati (**1402-1420**) also wrote **Sahitya Chintamani** and **Srngara Dipika**.
⚠ **Sangeeta Sudhakaram** is by **Singabhupala II**, a **Recherla Velama** ruler, not a Reddi.
His court had **Srinatha** and **Vamana Bhatta Bana**.

nacc0f9405fd.s: Kumaragiri Rajiyam, a commentary on Kalidasa's three plays, was written by:
nacc0f9405fd.x: Kumaragiri Rajiyam was written by Kataya Vema Reddi, Kumaragiri's brother-in-law, and only named after Kumaragiri.
xa: ⚠ Some notes credit Kumaragiri Rajiyam to Kumaragiri himself — the trap.
Kumaragiri Rajiyam is a commentary on **Kalidasa's three plays**.
Kumaragiri's title: **Karpura Vasanta Rayalu**.

n5f272ea394a.s: Which of the following works was NOT associated with Errana?
n5f272ea394a.x: Errana is associated with Aranya Parva shesham, Harivamsam and Nrusimha Puranam. Palnati Veera Charitra was one of Srinatha's works.
n5f272ea394a.tq: Identify the one work belonging to another poet in the same literary tradition.
xs: **Palnati Veera Charitra** is **Srinatha's**, not Errana's — option **(3)** is the answer.
Errana's works: **Aranya Parva shesham**, **Harivamsam**, **Nrusimha Puranam**.
xa: Srinatha's other works: **Sringara Naishadham**, **Kasikhandam**, **Bhimakhandam**, **Haravilasam**.
Srinatha also wrote **Maruttarat Charitra** and **Sivaratri Mahatyam**.
Errana bridges **Nannaya** and **Tikkana**.

ne7fb73ce66f.s: The poet Errana was associated with which Reddi ruler?
ne7fb73ce66f.x: Errana was associated with Prolaya Vema; Bala Saraswati with Anavota, and Srinatha and Vamana Bhatta Bana with Pedakomati Vema.
xa: Srinatha was **Vidyadhikari** (minister of education) and composed Pedakomati's Sanskrit inscriptions.
Bala Saraswati composed **Anavota's** Sanskrit inscriptions.
Srinatha defeated **Gauda Dindima Bhatta**, court poet of **Devaraya II**.

n534ebf3e4d6.s: Srinatha dedicated his Sringara Naishadham to:
n534ebf3e4d6.x: Sringara Naishadham, based on Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita, was dedicated to Mamidi Singana; Haravilasam went to Tippayya Setti.
xa: Other Srinatha works: **Kasikhandam**, **Bhimakhandam / Bhimeswara Puranam** and **Sivaratri Mahatyam**.
**Haravilasam** describes the **sea trade** and the **imports and exports** of the Reddi age (APPSC 2019).
Srinatha bore the title **Kavi Sarvabhauma** (c. **1365-1441**) and was court poet of **Pedakomati Vema Reddi**.
⚠ **Kasikhandam**: some notes say it was written at **Kataya Vema's** request.

n4cb0a6288e3.s: Singabhupala II, the author of Sangeeta Sudhakaram, belonged to which political group?
n4cb0a6288e3.x: Singabhupala II was a Recherla Velama ruler of Rachakonda, not a Reddi ruler, and he wrote Sangeeta Sudhakaram.
n4cb0a6288e3.tq: Discriminate between a work associated with the Reddi period and its non-Reddi author.
xs: **Singabhupala II** was a **Recherla Velama ruler of Rachakonda** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He wrote **Sangeeta Sudhakaram** on musicology (PYQ 2012).
⚠ He was **not a Reddi** of Addanki, although he appears in Reddi-era book lists.
xa: Do not confuse with **Sangeeta Chintamani**, the music work of **Pedakomati Vema Reddi** (PYQ 2011, 2019).
The **Recherla Velamas** and the **Musunuris** were the other two successor states after **1323**, with the Reddis.
**Vasanta Rajiyam** (on dance) was by **Kumaragiri Reddi**.

nap-history-21-14.x: Vamana Bhanu Bhattu wrote Usha Parinayam; Bammera Potana wrote Veera Bhadra Vijayam.
n: Vamana Bhanu Bhattu wrote Usha Parinayam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
Bammera Potana wrote Veera Bhadra Vijayam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
xa: Potana's other works: **Andhra Bhagavatam**, **Narayana Satakam**, **Bogini Dandakam**.
Potana was a **contemporary** of **Pedakomati Vema Reddy** and **Srinatha**.
Vamana Bhatta Bana's titles: **Sahitya Samrajya Dhurandhara**, **Sahitya Chudamani**.

nap-history-21-18.s: Kanaka Rekha Kalyanam was written by:
nap-history-21-18.x: Kanaka Rekha Kalyanam is by Vamana Bhanu Bhattu; Haravilasam, Srungara Naishadham and Palnati Veera Charitra are Srinatha's.
n: Srinatha wrote Haravilasam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
Srinatha wrote Srungara Naishadham. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
Srinatha wrote Palnati Veera Charitra. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
Vamana Bhanu Bhattu wrote Kanaka Rekha Kalyanam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
xa: Srinatha's other works: **Kasikhandam**, **Bhimakhandam**.
**Bhimakhandam** praises **Bhimeswara** of **Draksharamam**.
Haravilasam is **dedicated** to **Tippayya Setti**.

n30a8477db17.s: Which of the following descriptions of Errana is correct?
o: He was the first of the Kavitrayam and initiated the Telugu Mahabharata.
He was the last of the Kavitrayam and completed the Telugu Mahabharata.
He opened the Kavya Yuga through his independent Sanskrit compositions.
He was a court poet of the Vijayanagara emperor who translated the entire Sanskrit Mahabharata.
n30a8477db17.x: Errana was the last of the Kavitrayam and completed the Telugu Mahabharata by translating the remaining portion of the Aranya Parva.
n30a8477db17.tq: Use the first/last distinction to separate Errana from the other members and from Srinatha.
xs: Errana was the **last of the Kavitrayam** and **completed the Telugu Mahabharata** — option **(2)** is correct.
He translated the remaining part of the **Aranya Parva**.
**Srinatha**, not Errana, opened the **Kavya Yuga**.
xa: Errana was court poet of **Prolaya Vema Reddi**, not of Vijayanagara.
He bridges **Nannaya** and **Tikkana**.
Harivamsa was dedicated to **Prolaya Vema**.

n7af0e5afee3.s: Which of the following titles was borne by the poet Errana?
n7af0e5afee3.x: Errana was called Prabandha Parameswara and Sambhudasa. Kavi Sarvabhauma was Srinatha's title, and Sahitya Chudamani was Vamana Bhatta Bana's. Andhra Suratrana was a royal title (Anavema in the APPSC key, first borne by Kapaya Nayaka), not a poet's.
n7af0e5afee3.tq: Errana = Prabandha Parameswara, Sambhudasa; Srinatha = Kavi Sarvabhauma.
xs: Errana bore the title **Prabandha Parameswara** (also **Sambhudasa**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kavi Sarvabhauma** was **Srinatha's**; **Sahitya Chudamani** was **Vamana Bhatta Bana's**.
**Andhra Suratrana** was a royal title — **Anavema** in the APPSC G2 2011 key, first borne by **Kapaya Nayaka**.
xa: Vamana Bhatta Bana was also **Sahitya Samrajya Dhurandhara**.
Srinatha was honoured with **Kanakabhishekam** and **Ganda Penderam**.
Errana completed the Telugu Mahabharata.

n2e0d502ff52.s: At Vijayanagara, Srinatha defeated which court poet of Devaraya II?
n2e0d502ff52.x: Srinatha defeated Gauda Dindima Bhatta of Devaraya II's court and was honoured with Kanakabhishekam.
xa: Srinatha was **Vidyadhikari** (minister of education) to **Pedakomati Vema Reddi** and composed his Sanskrit inscriptions.
After Kondaveedu fell (**1424**) he joined the Rajahmundry Reddis (patron **Veerabhadra Reddi**) with **Bendapudi Annamatya's** help.
After Rajahmundry fell (**1448**) he lived in **poverty in Palnadu**.
He wrote more kavyas than any other Telugu poet.

n0b31822f333.s: Srinatha held which office at the court of Pedakomati Vema Reddi?
n0b31822f333.x: Srinatha (Kavi Sarvabhauma) was Vidyadhikari, the minister of education, at Pedakomati Vema Reddi's court, and he composed Pedakomati's Sanskrit inscriptions. He held no post as chief minister, commander or royal preceptor.
xs: Srinatha was **Vidyadhikari (minister of education)** at **Pedakomati Vema Reddi's** court — so option **(1)** is correct.
In that office he composed **Pedakomati's Sanskrit inscriptions**.
The notes record no post for him as chief minister, commander or royal preceptor.
xa: Srinatha's title: **Kavi Sarvabhauma** (c. **1365-1441**); court poet of Pedakomati (PYQ 2002).
He defeated **Gauda Dindima Bhatta**, court poet of **Devaraya II**, and got **Kanakabhishekam**.
Pedakomati was a scholar-king titled **Sarvajna Chakravarti**.

n9833c123b47.s: Who is traditionally associated with opening the Kavya Yuga in Telugu literature?
n9833c123b47.x: Srinatha is described as the poet who opened the Kavya Yuga, whereas Errana completed the Andhra Mahabharata as the last of the Kavitrayam.
n9833c123b47.tq: Separate the literary-period milestone from the Mahabharata-completion milestone.
xs: **Srinatha** opened the **Kavya Yuga** in Telugu literature — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Errana** completed the **Andhra Mahabharata** as the **last of the Kavitrayam**, so he closes the Bharata phase.
Errana is said to bridge **Nannaya's** classical style and **Tikkana's** style.
xa: Srinatha wrote more kavyas than any other Telugu poet and prepared the way for the **Prabandha** style.
Errana translated the **Seshabhaga of the Aranya Parva**; titles **Prabandha Parameswara** and **Sambhudasa**.
Errana was court poet of **Prolaya Vema Reddi** (PYQ G2 2011); his **Harivamsa** is dedicated to him.

nap-history-21-5.s: Who was the last poet of the Kavitrayam?
nap-history-21-5.x: Errana was the last poet of the Kavitrayam.
n: Errana Reddy was the last poet of the Kavitrayam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
Srinatha defeated Dindima Bhattu. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
Srinatha dedicated Haravilasam to Tippayya Setti. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 30-31]
xa: Srinatha's title: **Kavisarvabhauma**; he opened the **Kavya Yuga**.
Errana was court poet of **Prolaya Vema Reddy** and wrote **Narasimha Puranam**.
Srinatha is cited as evidence that **paper** was used for writing in the **15th** century (G2 **2012**).

n7a03e2d930c.s: Who financed the Vasantotsavams celebrated at the Reddi court?
n7a03e2d930c.x: The merchant Avachi Tippayya Setti funded the Vasantotsavams; this patronage is recorded in Srinatha's Haravilasam.
n7a03e2d930c.tq: Identify the patron by distinguishing the merchant from political and religious figures.
xs: Merchant **Avachi Tippayya Setti** funded the **Vasantotsavams** — option **(2)** is correct.
This is recorded in **Srinatha's Haravilasam**.
**Mallappa Odayar** was a Vijayanagara commander; **Ghoderayacharulu** were Shaiva gurus.
xa: Haravilasam was dedicated to **Tippayya Setti**, famous for overseas trade.
Haravilasam describes Reddi sea trade and **imports and exports** (APPSC 2019).
**Kumaragiri** celebrated the Vasantotsavams grandly.

ndb5e357d83a.s: The court dancer Lakumadevi, who was renowned in Bharatanatyam, was associated with the court of
ndb5e357d83a.x: Lakumadevi was the celebrated Bharatanatyam dancer at Kumaragiri Reddi's court. C. Narayana Reddy later wrote Karpura Vasanta Rayalu on Kumaragiri.
ndb5e357d83a.tq: Use the court–artist association and avoid substituting a neighbouring ruler.
xs: **Lakumadevi** was the court dancer of **Kumaragiri Reddi** (**APPSC G2 2012**) — option **(2)** is correct.
She was renowned in **Bharatanatyam**; Kumaragiri himself was an expert in it.
xa: **C. Narayana Reddy** wrote **Karpura Vasanta Rayalu** on Kumaragiri.
Kumaragiri's dance treatise: **Vasanta Rajiyam**.
**Devadasis** performed at Shiva temples such as the **Pancharamas**.

n24078cf58f7.s: Which Reddi ruler abolished the tax on gold?
n24078cf58f7.x: Anavota abolished the gold tax; his minister Somaya issued the Abhaya Sasanam at Motupalli to encourage trade.
xa: It guaranteed merchants **protection from sea pirates**.
**Motupalli** was the chief Reddi port; Anavota developed its dock.
**Mallaya Reddy** had taken Motupalli from **Hasan Gangu**.

na2e61caf6ee.s: The 'Andhra Path', an earlier trade route, is mentioned in which Buddhist text?
na2e61caf6ee.x: The Buddhist text Vinayavatthu mentions the 'Andhra Path' (APPSC 2019). Mahavamsa, Dipavamsa and Divyavadana are other Buddhist texts not linked to the Andhra Path.
na2e61caf6ee.tq: Andhra Path = Vinayavatthu; Reddi sea trade = Haravilasam.
xs: The **'Andhra Path'** is mentioned in the Buddhist text **Vinayavatthu** (**APPSC 2019**) — option **(2)** is correct.
It is an **earlier trade route** that preceded the Reddi port trade at Motupalli.
xa: **Motupalli** was the chief Reddi port.
**Srinatha's Haravilasam** describes Reddi sea trade (APPSC 2019).
The **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** of **Somaya** encouraged trade.

n7b80f9c9cd2.s: Which community was primarily associated with inland and coastal trade during the Reddi period?
n7b80f9c9cd2.x: The Komatis were mainly engaged in inland and coastal trade.
n7b80f9c9cd2.tq: Distinguish occupational roles among the major social groups.
xs: The **Komatis** ran **inland and coastal trade** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Kammas, Kapus, Reddis and Velamas** were the **warrior-farmer** backbone, supplying most soldiers.
xa: The Brahmin-warrior-merchant order survived into **Gajapati** rule.
Merchant **Tippayya Setti** was famed for overseas trade.
**Motupalli** was the chief Reddi port.

n0ff8181682f.s: Which ruler is associated with the construction of pilgrim rest-houses at Ahobilam and Srisailam and the rebuilding of the ramparts of Ahobilam and Mahanandi?
n0ff8181682f.x: Prolaya Vema Reddi built the pilgrim rest-houses at Ahobilam and Srisailam and rebuilt the ramparts of Ahobilam and Mahanandi.
n0ff8181682f.tq: Match the cluster of related temple works with the ruler rather than relying on one isolated monument.
xs: **Prolaya Vema Reddi** built the pilgrim **rest-houses (Vasatulas)** at **Ahobilam and Srisailam** and rebuilt the ramparts of **Ahobilam** and **Mahanandi** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Anavema** built the Veerashiro Mantapa; **Vallaya Vemana** restored the Amareswara temple.
xa: Prolaya Vema also built steps to **Patala Ganga** (**1346**) and **Ahobilam** hill.
He restored **agraharas** to Brahmins.
Title: **Nissivu Bhudana Parasurama**.

nindian-history-1-90.s: The Motupalli epigraph is chiefly known for fixing:
nindian-history-1-90.x: The Motupalli epigraph fixes commodity tariffs and shows imports and exports; famine relief belongs to the Mahasthan inscription.
n: The Mahasthan Inscription concerns famine relief. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The Motupalli Epigraph concerns trade and tariff rates. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The Motupalli evidence concerns imports and exports through Motupalli port. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The Motupalli Epigraph is associated with port trade and commodity tariffs. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
xa: Commodities listed: **sandal, camphor, rose water, ivory, pearls, corals, copper, zinc, lead, silk, pepper, areca nuts**.
**Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** was issued by **Somaya**, minister of **Anavota Reddi**, guaranteeing protection from **sea pirates**.
**Mallaya Reddy**, Prolaya Vema's brother, took Motupalli by defeating Bahmani founder **Hasan Gangu**.
**Anavota Reddi** **abolished the tax on gold** to encourage trade.

nap-history-42-20.s: Which tank was excavated by Surambika Reddy?
nap-history-42-20.x: Surambika, queen of Pedakomati Vema Reddy, dug the Santana Sagaram tank. The other names are made-up distractors.
nap-history-42-20.tq: Recall the tank linked with Surambika.
xs: **Surambika Reddy** excavated the **Santana Sagaram** tank — so option **(3)** is correct.
She was the queen of **Pedakomati Vema Reddy**; **Srinatha** is linked with the Santhana Sagaram record.
xa: ⚠ APPSC G2 **2019** key calls it **Govardhana Samudram**; some notes say **Santana Payonidhi**.
Exam rule: if only one of **Govardhana Samudram** or **Santana Sagaram** is offered, that is the answer.
Their son **Rachavema** cut the **'Jaganobbaganda'** canals to feed it.

nap-history-3-19.s: According to the Mutnuri inscription, the steps to Pathala Ganga at Srisailam were completed in:
nap-history-3-19.x: The Mutnuri inscription records the steps being finished in 1346; Prolaya Vema Reddy ruled till 1353.
n: Prolaya Vema Reddy ruled until 1353. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The Mutnuri inscription records the completion of the steps to Pathala Ganga at Srisailam in 1346. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xa: ⚠ Other notes call the **1346** record the **Srisailam** inscription.
He also built **Vasatulas** (rest-houses) at **Ahobilam** and Srisailam.
He built **74 forts**, including **Kondaveedu, Kondapalli and Dharanikota**.

nap-history-18-5.s: The Pakala Tank, built in Ganapatideva's reign, was constructed by his general:
nap-history-18-5.x: The Pakala tank was built in Ganapatideva's reign by his general Jagadala Mummadi.
n: Recharla Rudra built the Ramappa Temple at Palampet. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Rudra built the Pakala Tank. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Rudra was an army officer of Ganapathi Deva. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
The Pakala Tank was built across the Munneru river basin in Warangal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Prolaya Vema Reddy built the steps to Pathala Ganga at Srisailam and Ahobilam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Prolaya Vema Reddy built stepped stone pathways called Sopanamargas. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
xa: **Betha Raju II** built **Setti Samudram, Kete Samudram, Kesari Samudram**.
**Kesari Samudram** was named after his title **Vikrama Kesari**.
**Anavema Reddy** built the **Veera Siro Mandapam** at **Srisailam**.

n1f1457f07da.x: Dweepa Vijetha was Anavota Reddi's title; Prolaya Vema was Dharma Pratishtana Nagarudu.
xa: Prolaya Vema also bore **Nissivu Bhudana Parasurama**, stressing land gifts.
**Anavema Reddi**: **Rajashri Ramani**, **Rachuru Durga Vibhala** and **Andhra Suratrana**.
**Kataya Vema Reddi**: **Kataka Churakara**; **Sivalinga Reddi**: **Bharatamata Patanga**.
Anavota and Anavema were also styled **Vasantaraya**.

n4dd3d9b4f47.s: Kumaragiri Reddi was known by the title:
n4dd3d9b4f47.x: Karpura Vasantaraya was Kumaragiri's title; Veeranna Pothu belonged to Anavota, Andhra Suratrana to Anavema and Bharatamata Patanga to Sivalinga Reddi.
xa: ⚠ **Andhra Suratrana** was first borne by **Musunuri Kapaya Nayaka**.
Anavema's other titles: **Rajashri Ramani**, **Vasantarayadu**, **Rachuru Durga Vibhala**.
**Sivalinga Reddi** also wrote **Tatva Prakashika**.

n8a3a539bbca.s: According to the APPSC Group 2 (2017) key, the title 'Rachuru Durga Vibhala' belonged to which Reddi ruler?
n8a3a539bbca.x: The APPSC G2 2017 key gives Rachuru Durga Vibhala to Anavema Reddi, who also bore Rajashri Ramani and Andhra Suratrana. Prolaya Vema bore Dharma Pratishtana Nagarudu and Nissivu Bhudana Parasurama, Anavota bore Dweepa Vijetha, and Kataya Vema bore Kataka Churakara.
xs: The APPSC G2 2017 key gives **Rachuru Durga Vibhala** to **Anavema Reddi** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Prolaya Vema** bore **Dharma Pratishtana Nagarudu** and **Nissivu Bhudana Parasurama**.
**Anavota** bore **Dweepa Vijetha**; **Kataya Vema** bore **Kataka Churakara**.
xa: Anavema also bore **Rajashri Ramani**, **Vasantarayadu** and **Andhra Suratrana**.
**Anavema Reddi** (**1364-1386**) was the **greatest Reddi**, with the widest conquests.
He built the **Veerashiro Mantapa at Srisailam** (APPSC G2 2011) and mandapas at **Simhachalam**.
He was the **most charitable** Reddi king, guided by **Vemadri Pandit**.

nap-history-36-4.s: Prolaya Vema Reddy founded the Reddy kingdom in:
nap-history-36-4.x: Prolaya Vema Reddy founded the Reddy kingdom in 1324.
n: Prolaya Vema Reddy founded the Reddy Kingdom in 1324. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Kumaragiri Reddy was an expert in Bharata Natya. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Kumaragiri Reddy wrote Vasantarajeeyam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Pedakomati Vema Reddy wrote Sangeeta Chintamani. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Pedakomati Vema Reddy wrote Sahitya Chintamani. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Kapaya Nayaka held the title Andhra Suratran. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
xa: **Andhra Suratrana** was also given to **Anavema Reddi** (APPSC G2 **2011**), but first borne by Kapaya.
**Errana**, last poet of the **Kavitrayam**, was Prolaya Vema's court poet.
Reddi capitals: **Addanki** → **Kondavidu** → **Rajahmundry**.
Reddi period: **c. 1325-1448 CE**; emblem **Bull**; official language **Sanskrit**.

nap-history-36-15.s: Which title was associated with Srinatha?
nap-history-36-15.x: Srinatha, the Reddy-period poet, was known as Kavisarvabhauma. Abhinava Dandi was Ketana's title, Sarvagna Pedakomati Vema Reddy's and Rayagaja Kesari Rudramadevi's.
nap-history-36-15.tq: Link each title to its holder.
n: Rudramadevi held the title Rayagaja Kesari. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Pedakomati Vema Reddy held the title Sarvagna. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Srinatha held the title Kavisarvabhauma. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
Ketana held the title Abhinava Dandi. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 47-48]
xs: **Srinatha** of the **Reddy period** bore the title **Kavisarvabhauma** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Abhinava Dandi** = **Ketana**; **Sarvagna** = **Pedakomati Vema Reddy**; **Rayagaja Kesari** = **Rudramadevi**.
xa: Srinatha (c. **1365-1441**) was court poet of **Pedakomati Vema Reddi** and his **Vidyadhikari**.
He defeated **Dindima Bhattu**, court poet of **Devaraya II**, and was honoured with **Kanakabhishekam** + **Ganda Penderam**.
Works: **Haravilasam**, **Sringara Naishadham**, **Kasikhandam**, **Bhimakhandam**, **Palnati Veeracharitra**.

nap-history-3-18.s: Prolaya Vema Reddy served in whose court, according to the Anitalli inscription?
nap-history-3-18.x: The Anitalli inscription states that Prolaya Vema Reddy served in the court of Kapaya Nayaka, the Musunuri leader who freed Andhra from the Delhi Sultanate.
nap-history-3-18.tq: Recall the court named in the Anitalli inscription.
n: The Anitalli inscription was issued by Kaluva Anitalli. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
Prolaya Vema Reddy served in Kapaya Nayaka’s Cheru court. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xs: Prolaya Vema Reddy served in **Kapaya Nayaka's court** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Anitalli / Kaluvacheru inscription (1423)** records **Prolaya Vema Reddi's service under the Nayakas** and the Musunuri-led liberation.
The **Mani Kesavara** record also says he served in **Kapaya Nayaka's Cheru court**.
xa: The Kaluvacheru inscription was issued by **Anitalli** after the recapture of **Rajahmundry**.
**Mutnuri** inscription: completion of the steps to **Pathala Ganga**, Srisailam, in **1346**.
**Manyamapura** inscription: **Anapota Reddy** shifted the capital from **Addanki** to **Kondaveedu**.

n3b93716c436.s: After its fall, Muhammad bin Tughlaq renamed Warangal as:
n3b93716c436.x: Warangal was renamed Sultanpurti and Andhra placed under Malik Burhanuddin, assisted by Malik Maqbul.
xa: Of Prataparudra's **75 generals**, only **Prolaya Nayaka, Recherla Singama and Prolaya Vema Reddi** survived.
Tughluq misrule (from **1326**) and revolts freed Andhra within about **2 years**.
**Kapaya Nayaka** took **Orugallu** back from **Malik Maqbool** in **1336**.

n838eeb10699.s: Prolaya Nayaka, Recherla Singama and Prolaya Vema Reddi survived the fall of Warangal as generals of:
n838eeb10699.x: These three were the surviving generals of Prataparudra after the fall of Warangal.
xa: The **Kaluvacheru grant** (Anitalli, **1423**) names **75 Nayakas** who backed Prolaya.
The three founded successor states: **Musunuri**, **Recherla Velama** and **Reddi**.
**Recherla Singama** later cleared **Nalgonda-Mahabubnagar**; **Prolaya Vema Reddi** cleared **Kammanadu-Pakanadu**.

n03630b96397.s: Who led the confederacy of Nayakas that freed Andhra from Tughluq rule after the fall of Warangal in 1323?
n03630b96397.x: Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka led the liberation confederacy, the Vimochanodyamam (APPSC GS 2018; G2 2019). Recherla Singama, Prolaya Vema Reddi and Kolani Rudra were chiefs who took part in the movement but did not lead it.
n03630b96397.tq: Leader of the liberation = Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka; Kaluvacheru grant names 75 Nayakas who backed him.
xs: **Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka** led the liberation confederacy (APPSC GS 2018; G2 2019) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Recherla Singama**, **Prolaya Vema Reddi** and **Kolani Rudra** were participating chiefs, not the leader.
xa: Prolaya Nayaka was son of **Potinayaka**, of the **Kamma** clan.
He ruled from **Rekapalli** on the Godavari, near **Bhadrachalam** (APPSC G2 2017).
His **Vilasa copper-plate grant (1330)** records Tughluq atrocities and his relief measures.
Childless, he was succeeded by **Kapaya Nayaka**.

n091fad26979.s: Prolaya Nayaka ruled from which place?
n091fad26979.x: Prolaya Nayaka ruled from Rekapalli, situated on the Godavari in the forest region near Bhadrachalam.
n091fad26979.tq: Separate the capital of Prolaya from the later Musunuri capital of Kapaya.
xs: Prolaya Nayaka ruled from **Rekapalli** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC G2 2017).
**Orugallu** was **Kapaya Nayaka's** capital from **1336**; **Rachakonda** and **Devarakonda** were **Recherla Velama** capitals.
xa: Rekapalli lay **on the Godavari**, in forest near **Bhadrachalam**.
The Velamas moved their capital from **Amanagallu to Rachakonda** under **Anapota Nayaka**.
Reddi capitals: **Addanki → Kondavidu → Rajahmundry**.

nc068a385a35.s: The Vilasa copper-plate grant of 1330 was issued by:
nc068a385a35.x: The Vilasa grant of Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka describes Tughluq atrocities and his restoration of agraharas; Anitalli issued the Kaluvacheru grant of 1423.
xa: The Vilasa grant was issued by **Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka**.
The **Kaluvacheru grant** names **75 Nayakas** who backed Prolaya.
**Polavaram, Ganapeshwaram and Palasamarri** records belong to **Kapaya Nayaka**.

nf274fa12cd0.s: In the recovery of Warangal in 1336, Kapaya Nayaka acted together with
o: Hoysala Veera Ballala III, Prolaya Vema Reddi and Singama
Bukka I, Mahmud Gawan and Sultan Quli Qutb Shah
Annadevu, Kataya Vema and Pedakomati Vema Reddi
Hasan Gangu, Firoz Shah Tughlaq and Vinayaka Deva
nf274fa12cd0.x: In 1336, Kapaya Nayaka, Hoysala Veera Ballala III, Prolaya Vema Reddi and Singama took Warangal from Malik Maqbul.
nf274fa12cd0.tq: Start with the sure association of the liberation coalition and reject later-period figures.
xs: In **1336** Kapaya took Warangal with **Hoysala Veera Ballala III, Prolaya Vema Reddi and Singama** — so option **(1)** is correct.
They took **Orugallu** from **Malik Maqbool**.
**Bukka I** was sought later against the Bahmanis; **Hasan Gangu** was helped by Kapaya in **1347**; **Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** came much later.
xa: Kapaya then ruled the old **Kakatiya** realm from **Orugallu**.
Simultaneously **Singama** cleared Nalgonda-Mahabubnagar and **Prolaya Vema Reddi** cleared Kammanadu-Pakanadu.

nfc8985e0dbb.s: Kapaya Nayaka helped Hasan Gangu in founding the Bahmani kingdom in
nfc8985e0dbb.x: Kapaya Nayaka helped Hasan Gangu, also known as Zafar Khan, establish the Bahmani kingdom at Gulbarga in 1347.
nfc8985e0dbb.tq: Keep the year and place together to avoid confusing the Bahmani foundation with later territorial losses.
xs: Kapaya helped **Hasan Gangu (Zafar Khan)** found the **Bahmani** kingdom in **1347 at Gulbarga** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**1356** is the loss of **Bhuvanagiri**, **1367** Bhimavaram, and **1336** the recovery of Warangal.
xa: Kapaya then lost to the Bahmanis: **Kaulas (1350)**, **Bhuvanagiri (1356)**, **Golconda (1364-65)**.
His son **Vinayaka Deva** was burnt alive by **Muhammad Shah I** (1361-62).
Same wave: **Harihara-Bukka** founded Vijayanagara in **1336**.

n8f2f8d76d24.s: In which year did Kapaya Nayaka recover Warangal from Malik Maqbul?
n8f2f8d76d24.x: Warangal was recovered in 1336; the Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347 and Bhuvanagiri was lost in 1356.
xa: **Kaulas Durgam** was lost in **1350**.
Son **Vinayaka Deva** was killed in **1361/1362**.
Kapaya died at **Bhimavaram (1367-68)**.

n8c116d69343.s: Under the truce of 1364–65 with the Bahmanis, Kapaya Nayaka ceded:
n8c116d69343.x: Kapaya ceded Golconda fort with huge wealth, and Golconda became the boundary between the two powers.
xa: Wealth ceded: **400 elephants**, **250 horses** and **33 lakhs** in treasure.
A **turquoise throne** was among the gifts.
Kapaya sought help from **Bukka I** and **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** against the Bahmanis.

n680b0c9e6f6.s: The Vilasa grant, dated 1330, is particularly important for information regarding which of the following?
o: The foundation of the Bahmani kingdom and the reign of Hasan Gangu
The rise of Prolaya Nayaka and the atrocities committed under the Tughluqs
The conquest of Dharanikota by Madanayudu and Naganayudu
The establishment of the Vijayanagara kingdom by Harihara and Bukka
n680b0c9e6f6.x: The Vilasa grant of 1330 records Prolaya Nayaka’s rise and the atrocities committed under the Tughluq rule.
n680b0c9e6f6.tq: Identify the source by matching it with its distinctive subject matter.
xs: The **Vilasa grant (1330)** records **Prolaya Nayaka's rise** and **Tughluq atrocities** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It also records **agrarian relief** and **restoration of agraharas** to Brahmins.
The Bahmani founding (**1347**) and Vijayanagara's founding (**1336**) came after this grant.
xa: The **Kaluvacheru grant (1423)** of Reddi queen **Anitalli** records the Nayaka confederacy.
**Polavaram, Ganapeshwaram and Palasamarri** records belong to **Kapaya Nayaka**.

n9c8119f20f2.s: Ferishta's Persian work Tarikh-i-Ferishta refers to Telangana as:
n9c8119f20f2.x: Tarikh-i-Ferishta calls Telangana 'Tilang' and describes the Bahmani-Kapaya conflicts.
xa: Other sources: **Ganapeshwara** and **Kaluvacheru** inscriptions; **Gangadevi's Madhura Vijayam**.
Bahmani gains from Kapaya: **Kaulas (1350)**, **Bhuvanagiri (1356)**, **Golconda (1364-65)**.
Kapaya helped **Hasan Gangu** found the Bahmani kingdom in **1347**.

nap-history-31-18.s: Vengipuram was the capital of the:
nap-history-31-18.x: The Salankayanas ruled from Vengipuram; the Ikshvakus from Vijayapuri and the Satavahanas from Paithan.
n: Satavahana had Paithan as its capital. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
Ikshvaku had Vijayapuri as its capital. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
Salankayana had Vengipuram as its capital. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
Kakatiya later had Warangal as its capital. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
Warangal was also called Orugallu. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
xa: Kakatiya first capital: **Anamakonda** (**Hanamakonda**).
**Musunuri** capital: **Rekapalli** (on the Godavari).
**Recherla Velamas**: **Amanagallu** → **Rachakonda**; **Devarakonda** second branch capital.

nap-history-31-20.s: The capital of Anupa under Gautamiputra Satakarni was:
nap-history-31-20.x: Mahishmathi was the capital of Anupa; Koduru was the Brihatpalayana capital and Penugonda the post-Tallikota Vijayanagara capital.
n: Brihatpalayana had Koduru as its capital. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
Jayavarma is associated with Brihatpalayana. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
Andhra State had Kurnool as its capital in 1953. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
Vijayanagara had Penugonda as its capital after Tallikota. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
Anupa was under Gautamiputra Satakarni. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
Anupa had Mahishmathi as its capital. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
xa: **Assaka Janapada** — **Bodhan**.
**Reddy** capitals: **Addanki** → **Kondaveedu** → Rajahmundry.
**Ikshvaku** — **Vijayapuri**.

nap-history-43-5.s: The capital of the Musunuri kingdom was:
n: The capital of the Musunuri kingdom was Rekapalli. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 54-55]
The capital of Andhra State was Kurnool. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 54-55]
The capital of the Assaka Janapada was Bodhan. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 54-55]
xa: **Anupa** — **Mahishmathi**; **Brihatpalayana** — **Koduru**.
**Vijayanagara after Tallikota** — **Penugonda**.
Musunuri kingdom: **1325-1368**, led first by **Prolaya Nayaka**.

nf080982fba4.s: The Musunuri Nayaks belonged primarily to which community?
nf080982fba4.x: The Musunuris belonged to the Kamma community, also described as Chaturthanvayas.
nf080982fba4.tq: Distinguish the Musunuri community from the neighbouring ruling groups.
xs: The Musunuris belonged to the **Kamma** clan (the **Chaturthanvaya** lineage) — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Velamas** were their rivals (Recherla of Rachakonda), and the **Reddis** formed a separate successor state.
xa: The surname comes from **Musunuru** village near **Vuyyuru** (Krishna district).
Prolaya Nayaka was the son of **Potinayaka**.
Velamas are also called **Padmanayakas**.

nap-history-31-4.s: Anapota Reddy moved the Reddy capital from Addanki to:
nap-history-31-4.x: Prolaya Vema Reddi ruled from Addanki and Anapota Reddy moved the capital to Kondaveedu.
n: Reddy had Addanki as its capital under Prolaya Vema. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
Reddy later had Kondaveedu as its capital under Anapota Reddy. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
Kondaveedu was also called Kondavidu. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
Vijayanagara had Penugonda as its capital after Tallikota. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
xa: Reddy sequence: **Addanki → Kondavidu → Rajahmundry**.
**Andhra State** (**1953**) — **Kurnool**.
**Musunuri** — **Rekapalli**; **Recherla Velamas** — **Rachakonda**.

n9c6a618fe60.s: Which one of the following best describes the Vimochanodyamam?
o: A religious movement founded by the Velamas
The first organised resistance to Muslim rule in Andhra
A military expedition of the Cholas into Telangana
A revenue settlement introduced by the Reddis
n9c6a618fe60.x: Vimochanodyamam was the first organised resistance to Muslim rule in Andhra and was associated with the Musunuris.
n9c6a618fe60.tq: Identify the movement by its character and historical significance.
xs: **Vimochanodyamam** was the **first organised resistance to Muslim rule in Andhra** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was led by **Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka** (APPSC GS 2018; G2 2019), not a Velama religious movement or a Reddi revenue settlement.
xa: Chiefs involved: **Prolaya Vema Reddi, Recherla Singama, Koppula Prolaya Nayaka**, Kolani Rudra, Vengi Bhupala, Kapaya Nayaka.
The Musunuri kingdom lasted **1325-1368**.
It is called the first organised/successful Telugu resistance to the **Delhi Sultanate**.

ne2d4fa88447.s: Which of the following was NOT a title associated with Kapaya Nayaka?
ne2d4fa88447.x: Andhradeshadhiswara, Katakachurakara and Andhra Suratrana were associated with Kapaya Nayaka. Kavirajamarga is not one of his titles.
ne2d4fa88447.tq: Identify the unrelated famous term among titles belonging to the same historical setting.
xs: **Kavirajamarga** is not a title of Kapaya Nayaka — so option **(3)** is the answer.
His titles were **Andhra Suratrana**, **Andhradeshadhiswara** and **Katakachurakara**.
xa: Kapaya was the **first** to bear **Andhra Suratrana** (APPSC GS 2019); later **Anavema Reddi** too (APPSC G2 2011 key).
**Andhradesadhisvara** had earlier been held by Kakatiya **Ganapatideva**.
⚠ "First borne by" → **Kapaya**; "popular title of" with Anavema in the options → **Anavema Reddi**.

n5b2a9a8a4d9.s: The title Andhradesadhisvara, used by Kapaya Nayaka, had earlier been held by Kakatiya:
n5b2a9a8a4d9.x: Andhradesadhisvara had earlier been used by Kakatiya Ganapatideva.
xa: Kapaya was the **first holder** of **Andhra Suratrana** (APPSC GS 2019).
⚠ **Kataka Churakara** is also listed as a title of Reddi **Kataya Vema** in Reddi notes.
Kapaya ruled **1336-1368** from **Orugallu**.

na073c47ffd7.s: The title 'Andhra Suratrana' was first borne by:
na073c47ffd7.x: Musunuri Kapaya Nayaka was the first to bear Andhra Suratrana (APPSC GS 2019). Anavema Reddi used it later and is the APPSC G2 2011 key answer for 'popular title of'. Prolaya Vema and Singama Nayaka I did not bear it.
na073c47ffd7.tq: 'First borne by' = Kapaya; 'popular title of', with Anavema among the options = Anavema.
xs: **Kapaya Nayaka** was the first to bear **Andhra Suratrana** (APPSC GS 2019) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Anavema Reddi** bore it later (APPSC G2 2011 key for "popular title of").
**Prolaya Vema Reddi** and **Singama Nayaka I** are not recorded with this title.
xa: Kapaya's other titles: **Andhradeshadhiswara** and **Katakachurakara**.
⚠ "First borne by" → Kapaya; "popular title of" with Anavema in options → Anavema.
Kapaya was paternal nephew (some notes: cousin) of **Prolaya Nayaka**.

nc0cbb50efaf.s: Kapaya Nayaka received help from which Vijayanagara ruler?
nc0cbb50efaf.x: Kapaya received help from Bukka I of Vijayanagara and also sought help from Firoz Shah Tughlaq.
xa: The truce of **1364-65** ceded **Golconda**, which became the boundary.
A **turquoise throne** was among the gifts.
He lost **400 elephants**, **250 horses** and **33 lakhs** with Golconda.

nec991674286.x: Kapaya recovered Warangal, while Singama cleared Nalgonda–Mahabubnagar and Prolaya Vema Reddi cleared Kammanadu–Pakanadu.
xa: Kapaya's ally was **Hoysala Veera Ballala III**; Warangal was taken from **Malik Maqbul** in **1336**.
Kapaya appointed **Anapota Nayaka** as governor at **Vengi**.
**Singama Nayaka I** later expanded up to the **Krishna** and into the **Krishna-Tungabhadra doab**.

n80507eb686a.s: Who founded the Recherla Velama lineage?
n80507eb686a.x: Betala Nayudu is identified as the founder of the Recherla lineage.
n80507eb686a.tq: Use the founder-versus-successor distinction, a common dynasty trap.
xs: **Betala Nayudu** founded the Recherla Velama lineage — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Singama Nayudu I** founded the **independent kingdom**; **Anapota Nayaka** moved the capital to **Rachakonda**.
**Sarvagna Singa Bhupala** was a later Sanskrit **scholar-king** of Rachakonda.
xa: Family history: **Velugoti Varivamsavali**.
Velamas are also called **Padmanayakas**.
The kingdom ended when **Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** annexed Rachakonda and Devarakonda.

n6acbabc424a.s: The Recherla Velama kingdom is generally dated to:
n6acbabc424a.x: The Recherla kingdom is dated c. 1325–1475, about 150 years; it began as loyal feudatories of the early Kakatiyas.
xa: Founder of the lineage: **Betala Nayudu**.
The end came under **Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** (Golconda, **1518-43**).
Rachakonda and Devarakonda were **Vastu Shilpa** centres with high adhisthanas, carved pillars and toranas.

nba322e6412a.s: Madanayudu and his nephew Naganayudu invaded the Reddi kingdom primarily to avenge the death of whom?
nba322e6412a.x: Madanayudu and Naganayudu invaded the Reddi kingdom to avenge Singama.
nba322e6412a.tq: Identify the person linked to the stated motive for an invasion.
xs: **Madanayudu** and nephew **Naganayudu** invaded the Reddi kingdom to avenge **Singama** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Singama had been killed at **Jallipalli** fighting the **Jallipalli Kshatriyas aided by the Reddis**.
xa: They defeated **Anavota Reddi** at **Dharanikota** (Dannala Kota).
The victors took titles **Jagadabbaganda** and **Rayavesa Bhujanga**.
**Vinayaka Deva** (Kapaya's son) was killed by the Bahmanis, not the Reddis.

n7a11753340e.s: Which work was composed by Sarvagna Singa Bhupala of Rachakonda?
n7a11753340e.x: Sarvagna Singa Bhupala, a Sanskrit scholar-king, composed Rasarnava Sudhakara, a work on dramaturgy.
xa: Rasarnava Sudhakara is on **Sanskrit dramaturgy and poetics**.
**Sangeeta Sudhakaram** (PYQ G2 2012) is on music, a commentary on **Sarngadeva's Sangita Ratnakara**.
He was a **Sanskrit scholar-king** of Rachakonda.
⚠ Some notes link **Errana** with **Singama Nayaka**, but APPSC keys make **Prolaya Vema Reddi** his patron.

n44ad5e8fdf5.s: Sangeeta Sudhakaram is significant in the history of music mainly because it is described as which of the following?
o: A manual of Sanskrit dramaturgy and poetics
A commentary on Sarngadeva’s Sangita Ratnakara
A record of the Nayaka confederacy
A Persian account of the Bahmani wars
n44ad5e8fdf5.x: Sangeeta Sudhakaram is a musical work associated with Singabhupala II and serves as a commentary on Sarngadeva’s Sangita Ratnakara.
n44ad5e8fdf5.tq: Test the distinctive contribution or character of a work rather than its author.
xs: **Sangeeta Sudhakaram** is a **commentary on Sarngadeva's Sangita Ratnakara** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The dramaturgy manual is **Rasarnava Sudhakara**; the Persian account of Bahmani wars is **Tarikh-i-Ferishta**.
The Nayaka confederacy is recorded in the **Kaluvacheru grant (1423)**.
xa: Author: **Singabhupala II** of Rachakonda (PYQ G2 2012).
He is styled **Sarvagna (Sarvajna) Singa Bhupala**, a Sanskrit scholar-king.
Do not confuse with **Sangeeta Chintamani** of Reddi king **Pedakomati Vema**.

o: The initial capital of Prolaya Nayaka
The capital of Kapaya Nayaka before 1323
The second branch capital of the Recherla Velamas
The capital of the Reddis before Addanki
ne7d2ec2ed60.x: Devarakonda in Nalgonda was the second branch capital of the Recherla Velamas.
ne7d2ec2ed60.tq: Distinguish a branch capital from the principal capital and from Musunuri capitals.
xs: **Devarakonda** was the **second branch capital of the Recherla Velamas** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Prolaya Nayaka** ruled from **Rekapalli**; the Reddis began at **Addanki**.
xa: Devarakonda is in **Nalgonda**.
**Lingamanidu** of Devarakonda sought Gajapati **Hamvira's** help against the Bahmanis.
Rachakonda and Devarakonda were **Vastu Shilpa** centres.

nb897b54483e.s: Anapota Nayaka, the son of Singama Nayaka I, shifted the capital from Amanagallu to
nb897b54483e.x: Anapota Nayaka transferred the capital from Amanagallu to Rachakonda.
nb897b54483e.tq: Test the capital shift through a direct place-name distinction.
xs: **Anapota Nayaka** moved the capital from Amanagallu to **Rachakonda** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Devarakonda** was the second branch capital; **Orugallu** was Kapaya's; **Golconda** was ceded to the Bahmanis.
xa: Anapota defeated and killed **Kapaya Nayaka** at **Bhimavaram (1367-68)**.
His father **Singama Nayaka I** founded the independent kingdom.
**Sarvagna Singa Bhupala** was a later scholar-king of Rachakonda.

nc61241c8c7d.s: The Reddi successor state is approximately dated to:
nc61241c8c7d.x: The Reddi state is dated 1325–1448, while the Recherla Velama state is dated 1325–1475.
xa: The Velamas ruled Telangana for **about 150 years**.
The Reddi capitals ran **Addanki → Kondavidu → Rajahmundry**.
Vijayanagara (**1336**) and the Bahmanis (**1347**) emerged alongside.

nap-history-31-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Paithan was the capital of the Satavahanas.
Vengipuram was the capital of the Salankayanas.
Vijayapuri was the capital of the Ikshvakus.
Anamakonda was the only capital of the Kakatiyas.
nap-history-31-2.x: Anamakonda (Hanamakonda) was only the first Kakatiya capital; the capital later moved to Warangal (Orugallu).
n: Satavahana had Paithan as its capital. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
Ikshvaku had Vijayapuri as its capital. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
Salankayana had Vengipuram as its capital. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
Kakatiya initially had Anamakonda as its capital. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
Kakatiya later had Warangal as its capital. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 42-43]
xa: **Musunuri** — **Rekapalli**, then **Warangal** under **Kapaya Nayaka** from **1336**.
**Assaka Janapada** — **Bodhan**; **Brihatpalayana** — **Koduru**.
**Andhra State** (**1953**) — **Kurnool**.

n575750b98a3.s: The later alliances of the Velamas were directed mainly against
n575750b98a3.x: The Velamas allied with the Bahmanis and Gajapatis against Vijayanagara and the Reddis.
n575750b98a3.tq: Separate the allies from the common opponents in a multi-power conflict.
xs: The Velamas later sided with the Bahmanis and Gajapatis **against Vijayanagara and the Reddis** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Bahmanis and Gajapatis** were their **allies**, not targets, so option (2) reverses the relation.
xa: Bahmani minister **Mahmud Gawan** put down Telangana revolts **with Velama help**.
They helped the **Gajapatis** invade Vijayanagara after **Deva Raya II** (**1446** onwards).
**Lingamanidu** of Devarakonda sought help from Gajapati **Hamvira** against a Bahmani attack.
Earlier, **Devaraya I** of Vijayanagara had allied with them.

n4f44c888a4b.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler allied with the Velamas?
n4f44c888a4b.x: Devaraya I of Vijayanagara formed an alliance with the Velamas.
n4f44c888a4b.tq: Distinguish the specific Vijayanagara ruler from other rulers mentioned in the alliances.
xs: **Devaraya I** of Vijayanagara allied with the Velamas — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Bukka I** is linked with **Kapaya Nayaka** against the Bahmanis.
After **Deva Raya II**, the Velamas helped the **Gajapatis** invade Vijayanagara.
xa: The Velamas switched allies as it suited them.
**Pedakomati Vema Reddi** died fighting them in **1420**.

n10ff4adcb23.s: Pedakomati Vema Reddi died while fighting the Velamas in
n10ff4adcb23.x: Pedakomati Vema Reddi died fighting the Velamas in 1420.
n10ff4adcb23.tq: Identify the specific date associated with the Reddi–Velama conflict.
xs: **Pedakomati Vema Reddi** died fighting the Velamas in **1420** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**1367** is Bhimavaram, **1446** the Gajapati invasion after Deva Raya II, and **1518** the start of **Sultan Quli Qutb Shah's** reign.
xa: The Velamas helped **Annadevu** take parts of Vengi from **Kataya Vema**.
They later sided with the **Bahmanis and Gajapatis** against Vijayanagara and the Reddis.
The Reddis held coastal Andhra; the Velamas contested it from the **north**.

n6142f4406a1.s: Mahmud Gawan suppressed the Telangana revolts with the assistance of the
n6142f4406a1.x: Bahmani minister Mahmud Gawan put down the Telangana revolts with Velama assistance.
n6142f4406a1.tq: Use the minister–supporting force association rather than the rival dynasty’s name.
xs: Bahmani minister **Mahmud Gawan** put down the Telangana revolts **with Velama help** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The Velamas later sided with the **Bahmanis and Gajapatis** against Vijayanagara and the **Reddis**, so the Reddis were their foes.
xa: The Velamas switched allies as it suited them; earlier **Devaraya I** of Vijayanagara had allied with them.
They helped the **Gajapatis** invade Vijayanagara after **Deva Raya II** (**1446** onwards).
**Pedakomati Vema Reddi** died fighting the Velamas in **1420**.

n6ff19df8ab3.s: Under the Poligar system, which landed families became zamindars?
n6ff19df8ab3.x: Under the Poligar system, Velama, Reddi and Raju landed families became zamindars.
xa: Velama zamindari lines: **Damerla** (Kalahasti), **Velugoti** (Venkatagiri), **Ravu** (Bobbili), **Pithapuram**.
The **Recherla** line ruled Telangana from Rachakonda and Devarakonda.
**Damerla — Sri Kalahasti** was asked in PYQ GS 2022.

nf29361b69b9.s: Which Sultan defeated the Velama chiefs and annexed both Rachakonda and Devarakonda?
o: Muhammad I of the Bahmani dynasty
nf29361b69b9.x: Sultan Quli Qutb Shah, who ruled at Golconda from 1518 to 1543, defeated the Velama chiefs and annexed Rachakonda and Devarakonda.
nf29361b69b9.tq: Distinguish the final conqueror from earlier Bahmani opponents and ministers.
xs: **Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** (Golconda, **1518-43**) defeated the Velama chiefs and annexed **Rachakonda and Devarakonda** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Mahmud Gawan** was a Bahmani minister who crushed Telangana revolts **with Velama help**.
**Muhammad I** burnt **Vinayaka Deva**; **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** was approached by Kapaya for help.
xa: The Velamas later sided with the **Bahmanis and Gajapatis** against Vijayanagara and the Reddis.
**Devarakonda** (Nalgonda) was the second Velama branch capital.

n24c54d64d86.s: What was the principal consequence of Kapaya Nayaka’s decline in relation to the Reddis and Velamas?
o: The Reddis recovered coastal Andhra and the Velamas absorbed Musunuri Telangana
The Velamas restored the Musunuri kingdom in coastal Andhra
The Reddis captured Telangana and the Velamas occupied coastal Andhra
Both groups lost their territories to the Bahmanis
n24c54d64d86.x: Kapaya’s decline enabled the Reddis to take coastal Andhra, while the Velamas absorbed Musunuri Telangana.
n24c54d64d86.tq: Test the paired consequence by keeping the two territorial changes together.
xs: After **Kapaya's** decline, the **Reddis took coastal Andhra** and the **Velamas absorbed Musunuri Telangana** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Kapaya was killed at **Bhimavaram (1367-68)** by the Velamas under **Anapota Nayaka**.
xa: Telangana passed to the **Velamas of Rachakonda**.
Three successor states: **Musunuri (1325-1368)**, **Recherla Velama (1325-1475)**, **Reddi (1325-1448)**.
The Velamas ruled Telangana for about **150 years**.

n6a1760bea1a.s: The successor states that arose after the loss of Kakatiya unity were the:
o: Musunuri, Recherla Velama and Reddi states
Kalyani Chalukya, Velama and Reddi states
n6a1760bea1a.x: The loss of Kakatiya unity gave rise to the Musunuri, Recherla Velama and Reddi successor states.
xa: Periods: **Musunuri (1325-1368)**, **Recherla Velama (1325-1475)**, **Reddi (1325-1448)**.
The movement was the first organised/successful Telugu resistance to the **Delhi Sultanate**.
Of Prataparudra's **75 generals**, only **Prolaya Nayaka, Recherla Singama and Prolaya Vema Reddi** survived.

nbf0053b9a59.s: The Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347 by:
o: Hasan Gangu, also known as Zafar Khan
nbf0053b9a59.x: Hasan Gangu, or Zafar Khan, founded the Bahmani kingdom in 1347.
nbf0053b9a59.tq: Use the founder–event association; the alternative names are a common confusable pair.
xs: The Bahmani kingdom was founded in **1347** by **Hasan Gangu (Zafar Khan)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Ahmad Shah I** later moved the capital to **Bidar**; **Mahmud Gawan** was a later minister.
**Kapaya Nayaka** only **helped** Hasan Gangu found it.
xa: The first capital was **Gulbarga** (PYQ UPPSC 2005, 2016).
The founding falls in the **14th century**.
The first breakaway state was **Bijapur** (**1489**).

ne4dd7f76b74.s: Which Bahmani Sultan shifted the capital from Gulbarga to Bidar?
ne4dd7f76b74.x: Ahmad Shah I moved the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar (PYQ G2 2003). Hasan Gangu founded the kingdom with Gulbarga as its capital in 1347. Muhammad Shah I fought Kapaya Nayaka, and Muhammad III ruled with Mahmud Gawan as his minister.
ne4dd7f76b74.tq: Gulbarga to Bidar = Ahmad Shah I.
xs: **Ahmad Shah I** moved the Bahmani capital from **Gulbarga to Bidar** (PYQ G2 2003) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Hasan Gangu** founded the kingdom at Gulbarga (**1347**).
**Muhammad Shah I** fought **Kapaya Nayaka**; **Muhammad III** ruled with **Mahmud Gawan**.
xa: Muhammad Shah I burned **Kapaya's son Vinayaka** alive (**1361**).
First breakaway: **Bijapur** (**1489**).
**Kapaya Nayaka** helped Hasan Gangu found the kingdom.

n423f0295e10.s: Firoz Shah's army was repulsed at Kandukuru in 1398 by:
n423f0295e10.x: Machareddi repulsed Firoz Shah at Kandukuru in 1398; Gajarao Tippa beat him at Kambhammetta in 1396.
xa: Firoz Shah's reign: **1397-1422**.
Later **Muhammad III** and **Mahmud Gawan** put down Telangana revolts (from **1453**).

n2e36976a9be.s: Which Bahmani leader subdued Orugallu and took Kondaveedu?
n2e36976a9be.x: With Muhammad III, Mahmud Gawan suppressed Telangana revolts from 1453, subdued Orugallu and took Kondaveedu.
xa: Gawan also **pushed into Odisha** (**1471**).
The kingdom was **largest under Gawan**.
**Purushottama** Gajapati refused to help **Muhammad III**.

n8fa7cd044df.s: Which of the following correctly describes Kapilendra Gajapati's Andhra campaigns?
o: He defeated Saluva Narasimha and occupied Cuttack.
He founded the Bahmani kingdom at Gulbarga and annexed Bidar.
He recovered Udayagiri from Krishnadevaraya and restored Gajapati control over Kondapalli.
He attacked Tiran Andhra in 1448 and captured Kondaveedu around 1450.
n8fa7cd044df.x: Kapilendra attacked Tiran Andhra in 1448 and captured Kondaveedu around 1450. The other alternatives attribute later or unrelated events to him.
n8fa7cd044df.tq: Match the ruler with his own campaign rather than a later Gajapati–Vijayanagara event.
xs: **Kapilendra** attacked **Tiran Andhra in 1448** and captured **Kondaveedu around 1450** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Saluva Narasimha** drove the Gajapatis out by **1470**; **Udayagiri** was lost under **Prataparudra**.
The Bahmani kingdom was founded by **Hasan Gangu**.
xa: The **1448** attack is recorded in the **Penugonda inscription**.
Kapilendra annexed **Rajamahendravaram** after **Devaraya II's** death, ending the Rajahmundry Reddis.
He also took **Bellamkonda, Velugodu, Addanki, Srisailam** and besieged **Vijayanagara**.

nf285c0fc764.s: Prataparudra Gajapati lost Udayagiri, Kondaveedu and Kondapalli to:
nf285c0fc764.x: Prataparudra Gajapati lost these forts to Krishnadevaraya (1513–1519).
xa: Purushottama overturned the **1471** puppet rule of **Hamvira**.
Peace terms: lands **north of the Krishna** returned; Prataparudra stayed a **feudatory**.

n0ad2cf6a159.s: Kondaveedu, held by Vijayanagara until 1449, fell to the Gajapatis around:
n0ad2cf6a159.x: Kondaveedu was under Vijayanagara until 1449 and fell to the Gajapatis around 1450.
xa: **Mahmud Gawan** took Kondaveedu in **1471**.
**Prataparudra** later lost Kondaveedu to **Krishnadevaraya**.
Kondaveedu, Udayagiri, Kondapalli, Rajahmundry, Simhachalam = AP sites of the Gajapati wars.

n955a267b58f.s: Hamvira, who defeated the Bahmani army attacking Devarakonda, was the son of:
n955a267b58f.x: Hamvira was the son of Kapileswara Gajapati and defeated the Bahmani army that attacked Devarakonda.
xa: **Lingamanidu** of Devarakonda had sought Hamvira's help.
**Saluva Narasimha** drove the Gajapatis out of the south-east by **1470**.

na81ea4617c9.s: The Gajapatis ruled approximately during which period?
na81ea4617c9.x: The Gajapati rule is dated approximately from 1434 to 1541.
na81ea4617c9.tq: Recognise the approximate beginning and ending years rather than confusing them with individual inscription dates.
xs: The Gajapatis ruled c. **1434–1541** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Kapilendra** (founder) reigned from **1434** per CDI.
xa: Capital: **Cuttack**; Gajapati = **"Lord of Elephants"**.
**Uttarandhra** culture shows their influence.
The whole of **north coastal Andhra** was under their rule.

n13c6b125ccc.s: Krishnadevaraya's campaign against Prataparudra Gajapati began with the capture of:
n13c6b125ccc.x: The campaign went through Udayagiri, Kondaveedu, Kondapalli and Bejawada, then the march to Cuttack in 1518.
xa: The campaign ran **1513 to 1519**.
Victory pillars at **Simhachalam, Potnuru**.
Prataparudra then accepted peace as a **feudatory**.

n81618e0de86.s: In the southern Andhra territories of the Gajapati Empire, the revenue officers were known as:
n81618e0de86.x: Naidu was the title used for revenue officers in the southern Andhra regions of the Gajapati Empire.
n81618e0de86.tq: Directly identify the exact administrative title rather than confusing it with neighbouring officer designations.
xs: Revenue officers in the Gajapati **southern (Andhra) regions** were **Naidus** (PYQ GS 2025) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Khandadhipati**, **Bisayi** and **Pradhan** were other officer titles in the PYQ options; the notes do not define them.
xa: **Nayakas and samantas** collected revenue and kept order.
The **Brahmin-warrior-merchant** order of the Reddi era was left intact.
**Devadanas** and **brahmadeyas** went to scholars and temples.

n4f44606a05c.s: Under Gajapati rule in Andhra, revenue was collected and order maintained by local chiefs called:
n4f44606a05c.x: Nayakas and samantas collected revenue and maintained order; the Reddi-era social order was retained.
xa: Endowed temples included **Puri**, **Srisailam** and coastal shrines.
Southern revenue officers were called **Naidu** (PYQ GS 2025).

nb5c26e7ed0b.s: Which one of the following is NOT associated with the terms of peace between Krishnadevaraya and Prataparudra Gajapati?
o: Annexation of Cuttack and the Gajapati heartland to Vijayanagara
Marriage of Prataparudra's daughter to Krishnadevaraya
Return of lands north of the Krishna to the Gajapati
nb5c26e7ed0b.x: The terms included a marriage alliance, the Balakrishna idol, and return of lands north of the Krishna to the Gajapati. Permanent annexation of all Gajapati territories south of the Krishna was not stated.
nb5c26e7ed0b.tq: Reject the extreme territorial claim when testing a list of treaty terms.
xs: **Permanent annexation of all Gajapati territories south of the Krishna** is not among the stated terms — so option **(1)** is the answer.
The terms were a **marriage alliance**, the **Balakrishna idol**, and **return of lands north of the Krishna**.
xa: The princess was **Bhadradevi** (Tukkadevi/Jaganmohini).
Prataparudra remained a **feudatory**.
Settlement: c. **1518-19**.
nb5c26e7ed0b.fixed: Vijayanagara did keep lands south of the Krishna, so old option 1 was actually a peace term

n6fe74593bd0.s: The Madala Panji is best described as which of the following?
o: A temple chronicle of Jagannath at Puri dealing with Gajapati history
A Persian history of the Deccan sultans
A military account of Kapileswara's attack on Andhra
An inscription describing Vijayanagara assistance to the Reddis
n6fe74593bd0.x: Madala Panji is the temple chronicle of Jagannath at Puri and contains material on Gajapati history.
n6fe74593bd0.tq: Use the source–content association and distinguish the chronicle from the Persian history and inscriptions.
xs: **Madala Panji** is the **temple chronicle of Jagannath, Puri**, on Gajapati history — so option **(1)** is correct.
A Persian history of the Deccan sultans is **Ferishta**; Vijayanagara help to the Reddis is in the **Draksharama inscription (1444)**.
Kapileswara's attack on Tiran Andhra is recorded in the **Penugonda inscription**.
xa: **Anantavaram inscription** (Prataparudra): the **Virupaksharayas** defeated and made to pay **Kappam**.
Victory pillars at **Simhachalam** and **Potnuru** mark **Krishnadevaraya's** triumph.

n60984726262.x: Gajapati means 'Lord of Elephants'; the Gajapatis ruled from Cuttack.
xa: The Gajapatis ruled c. **1434** to **1541**.
**Uttarandhra** culture shows their influence.
**Udayagiri (Nellore)** was their major stronghold in southern Andhra.

n948d7addd44.s: The epithet 'Italian of the East' for Telugu was coined by:
n948d7addd44.x: It was coined by the 15th-century Venetian traveller Niccolo de' Conti; 'Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa' is Krishnadevaraya's.
xa: ⚠ **Italian of the East** = a foreign traveller; **Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa** = a king.
The reason for "Italian of the East": Telugu's **rounded, vowel-ending, highly phonetic** character (APPSC GS **2021**).
Other names of the language: **Tenugu** (from tene, honey), **Andhra / Andhrika**.

n46223f57800.s: Who identified the word ‘Nagabu’ in the Amaravati inscription?
n46223f57800.x: Veturi Prabhakara Sastri identified ‘Nagabu’ as the first Telugu word in the Amaravati inscription.
n46223f57800.tq: Test the scholar associated with a specific epigraphic identification.
xs: **Veturi Prabhakara Sastri** identified **"Nagabu"** in the **Amaravati** inscription — so option **(3)** is correct.
**D.C. Sircar** studied Desi words close to Telugu; **Sakalya Mallabhattu** was a Kakatiya-court Sanskrit author.
xa: "Nagabu" is called the **first Telugu word**.
**"Vepuru"** appears in the **Myakadoni** inscription.
**"Andhrapatha"** is first recorded in the **Mayidavolu** plates.

n169f766248f.s: The Kalamalla inscription, regarded as the earliest Telugu inscription, belongs to which dynasty?
n169f766248f.x: The Kalamalla inscription of about 575 CE is associated with the Renati Chola ruler Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya.
n169f766248f.tq: Identify the dynasty linked with the earliest inscription.
xs: **Kalamalla** (Kadapa, c. **575 CE**) belongs to the **Renati Cholas** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Issuer: **Dhanunjaya Varma** (Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya).
It is the **first Telugu inscription**, in **prose** (G2 2012 key).
xa: **Erragudipadu** (Punyakumara, Renati Chola) is the first **fully available** Telugu inscription, in geya style.
**Arumbhaka** is by **Erikal Mutturaju**, the same line as Kalamalla.
⚠ **Kalamalla** = first inscription (prose); **Addanki** = first poetic inscription.

n53111a0ba0e.s: Which inscription is regarded as the first fully available Telugu inscription and is written in a song or geya style?
n53111a0ba0e.x: The Erragudipadu inscription of Punyakumara of the Renati Cholas is regarded as the first fully available Telugu inscription and uses a song or geya style.
n53111a0ba0e.tq: Distinguish between the earliest inscription and the first fully available inscription.
xs: **Erragudipadu** is the **first fully available Telugu inscription**, in **song (geya) style** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was issued by **Punyakumara**, a **Renati Chola**.
**Kalamalla** is the first Telugu inscription (prose); **Addanki** the first poetic one; **Vipparla** the "first complete early Telugu text".
xa: **Chejarla** (Kubja Vishnuvardhana) has over **50% Telugu** words.
**Vipparla** is credited to **Jayasimha Vallabha I** (APPSC key).

n49fb426adf5.s: Which inscription contains the first Madhyakkara poem?
n49fb426adf5.x: Bezawada has the first Madhyakkara poem; Addanki is the first Telugu poetic inscription in Taruvoja metre.
xa: Addanki was issued by **Panduranga**, commander of **Gunaga Vijayaditya III**.
Bezawada was issued by **Yuddhamalla II** (Nagamalleswara temple).
Sataluru, Kandukur and Dharmavaram belong to **Gunaga Vijayaditya**.

n00283878f4b.s: The Addanki inscription, the first Telugu poetic inscription, was issued by:
o: Panduranga, commander of Gunaga Vijayaditya III
n00283878f4b.x: The Addanki inscription in Taruvoja metre was issued by Panduranga (Pandaranga), commander of the Eastern Chalukya king Gunaga Vijayaditya III. Yuddhamalla II issued the Bezawada inscription, Punyakumara the Erragudipadu inscription and Kubja Vishnuvardhana the Chejarla inscription.
n00283878f4b.tq: Addanki = Panduranga (general of Gunaga Vijayaditya III), Taruvoja
xs: **Addanki** was issued by **Panduranga**, commander of Eastern Chalukya **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Yuddhamalla II** issued **Bezawada**; **Punyakumara** issued **Erragudipadu**; **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** issued **Chejarla**.
xa: Addanki is in **Taruvoja** metre — the **first Telugu verse**.
Bezawada is the **first Madhyakkara** poem.
**Sataluru**: Champakamala with prasa; **Kandukur**: Seesa and Ataveladi.

n37a9dbda156.s: Which of the following is NOT among the inscriptions showing written Telugu before Nannaya?
n37a9dbda156.x: Kalamalla, Vipparla, Addanki and Bezawada show pre-Nannaya written Telugu; the Motupalli epigraph is a later Kakatiya-era record.
xa: Nannaya relied on a written form tested through **five centuries** of inscriptions.
**Kalamalla** (Kadapa) by **Dhanunjaya Varma**, **Renati Chola** = **first Telugu inscription**.
**Bezawada** (**Yuddhamalla II**) = **first Madhyakkara** poem.
**Erragudipadu** (**Punyakumara**) = first fully available Telugu inscription.

n3f2de0f28aa.s: Sarala Dasa composed the Mahabharata in:
n3f2de0f28aa.x: Sarala Dasa composed the Mahabharata in Odia; Kasirama Das composed it in Bengali.
xa: The **Nannaya-Tikkana-Errana** Andhra Mahabharatam is the **Telugu** version.
⚠ One note block wrongly applies "Vikramarjuniya Vijayamu" to Nannaya's work — keep them apart.

na66c28b5e78.x: Parijatapaharanam is by Nandi Timmana; Manucharitra is by Allasani Peddana.
xa: Manucharitra is also called **Swarochisha Manu Sambhavamu**.
Vasucharitra was dedicated to **Tirumala Raya**; its author is also called **Bhattu Murti**.
Peddana was **Andhra Kavita Pitamaha**.

n49275e9dc18.x: Ubhayakavimitrudu is Tikkana's title; Nannaya was Vaganusasana and Errana Sambhudasa.
xa: Errana's other title: **Prabandha Parameswara**.
Nannaya: **Adikavi**, **Vagadheeshwara**, **Vidyadvaitudu**, **Shabda Shasanudu**.
Tikkana: **Kavibrahma**, **Kavijana Raja**.
⚠ **Srinatha, Potana and Nannechoda are NOT in the Kavitraya**.

n6debf23fcc3.s: How many parvas of the Mahabharata did Tikkana translate into Telugu?
n6debf23fcc3.x: Tikkana translated the remaining 15 parvas, from Virata to Swargarohana, and called it Prabandha Mandali.
xa: **Nannaya** did **Adi, Sabha** and part of **Aranya** (**142 padyas**).
**Errana** completed the rest of **Aranya Parva**, linking the other two.
Tikkana's philosophy: **Harihara Advaita** — Bharatam dedicated to **Hariharanatha**.
Tikkana's patron: Nellore Choda **Manumasiddhi II**.

n22840772289.s: Tikkana was the court poet of:
n22840772289.x: Tikkana served Manumasiddhi II of Nellore; Errana was at Prolaya Vema Reddi's court and Rajaraja Narendra patronised Nannaya.
xa: Nannaya's patron **Raja Raja Narendra** ruled **1018-1061 CE** at **Rajamahendravaram**.
Telugu Mahabharata took **three** eras: **Eastern Chalukya, Kakatiya, Reddi**.
Errana's **Harivamsam** was dedicated to **Prolaya Vema**.

n517f488189e.s: Errana completed which parva of the Mahabharata left unfinished by Nannaya?
n517f488189e.x: By completing the Aranya Parva, Errana linked Nannaya's work with Tikkana's.
xa: Nannaya did **Adi, Sabha** and **142 padyas** of Aranya.
Errana's titles: **Prabandha Parameswara**, **Sambhudasa**.

ndee0d1a5ff6.s: Nannaya’s contribution to the Telugu Mahabharata is correctly described as:
o: The complete Virata to Swargarohana Parvas
The Adi and Sabha Parvas and 142 padyas of Aranya Parva
The Adi, Sabha and the remaining part of Aranya Parva
ndee0d1a5ff6.x: Nannaya translated the Adi and Sabha Parvas and 142 padyas of the Aranya Parva. Errana later completed the remaining portion of Aranya.
ndee0d1a5ff6.tq: Use the precise numerical detail to separate Nannaya’s share from those of Tikkana and Errana.
xs: Nannaya did the **Adi and Sabha Parvas** and **142 padyas of the Aranya Parva** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **rest of Aranya** was **Errana's**; **Virata to Swargarohana** was **Tikkana's**.
xa: That share is called **2.5 parvas**.
⚠ "First three parvas and part of the fourth" (one note) is wrong.
**Andhra Mahabharatamu** is called the **first book in Telugu**.

ncd29517f604.s: Nannaya, the Adikavi whose Andhra Mahabharatamu is regarded as the first book in Telugu, was the court poet of:
ncd29517f604.x: Nannaya was court poet, teacher and adviser of the Eastern Chalukya king Rajaraja Narendra (r. 1018-1061) at Rajamahendravaram. Prolaya Vema Reddi patronised Errana; Manumasiddhi II patronised Tikkana; Ganapatideva was the Kakatiya ruler of Tikkana's age.
xs: Nannaya was court poet, teacher and adviser of **Rajaraja Narendra** at **Rajamahendravaram** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Prolaya Vema Reddi** (Addanki) patronised **Errana**; **Manumasiddhi II** (Nellore) patronised **Tikkana**.
**Ganapatideva** was the Kakatiya ruler of Tikkana's age.
xa: Rajaraja Narendra reigned **1018-1061 CE**.
Nannaya's titles: **Adikavi**, **Vagadheeshwara**, **Vidyadvaitudu**, **Shabda Shasanudu**.
Rajaraja Narendra also granted **Navakhandavada** to **Pavuluri Mallana**.

nf3778b1c053.s: Srinatha wrote Kashikhandam at the request of:
nf3778b1c053.x: Kashikhandam was written at Kataya Vema's request; Haravilasam was dedicated to Tippayya Setti.
xa: Srinatha: c. **1365-1441**, bridge between the **Kavitraya** and the **Prabandha** age.
⚠ **Veerabhadra Vijayam** is by **Bammera Potana**, not Srinatha.
⚠ APPSC **2025** key treated **Palnati Vira Charitra** as not his.

nd280a814143.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Prabandha form?
o: The epic kavya gave way to the prabandha
The prabandha has elaborate descriptions and strong shringara
The prabandha generally treats a single episode
The prabandha dispenses with strict metrical rules
nd280a814143.x: The prabandha follows strict metrical rules, so the statement that it dispenses with them is false.
xa: Set descriptions were introduced by **Nannechoda's Kumarasambhava**.
The style peaked with the **Ashtadiggajas** at **Krishnadevaraya's** court.

n123350ab8c2.s: Which courts supported Srinatha and Errana in the Prabandha tradition?
n123350ab8c2.x: The Reddi courts supported Srinatha and Errana, and the Vijayanagara Nayaka courts helped spread the style.
xa: The peak was the **Ashtadiggajas** at **Krishnadevaraya's** court.
Telugu literature was "first influenced" by the **Vijayanagara Empire** (APPSC-GS 2019 key).

n92dac74c84f.s: The Telugu Mahabharata was completed over which of the following three historical eras?
o: Eastern Chalukya, Kakatiya and Reddi eras
Vijayanagara, Qutb Shahi and Asaf Jahi eras
n92dac74c84f.x: The Telugu Mahabharata was completed over three successive eras: the Eastern Chalukya, Kakatiya and Reddi periods.
n92dac74c84f.tq: Use the dynasty sequence to identify the correct historical span.
xs: The Telugu Mahabharata took three eras: **Eastern Chalukya, Kakatiya and Reddi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Nannaya** (Rajaraja Narendra, Eastern Chalukya); **Tikkana** (Manumasiddhi II, Kakatiya era); **Errana** (Prolaya Vema Reddi).
xa: Nannaya: **11th c.**; Tikkana: **13th c.**; Errana: **14th c.**
Errana's section **links** the other two.
The Kavitraya started with Nannaya's Bharatam.

n4183fa6a7bb.s: Nannaya borrowed the Akkara metre from:
n4183fa6a7bb.x: The Akkara metre was borrowed from Kannada, not Tamil; Nannaya also pioneered the Champu style.
xa: He fitted **Sanskrit metres** to Telugu.
⚠ CDX names **Bhaskara Ramayanam** (Hulakki Bhaskara) as the **first champu kavya**.

n9a1eb7274ad.s: The evidence for Narayana Bhattu's assistance to Nannaya in translating the Mahabharata is provided by which source?
n9a1eb7274ad.x: The Nandampudi donation inscription is cited as evidence of Narayana Bhattu's assistance in the translation. The other inscriptions belong to the evidence for pre-Nannaya Telugu.
n9a1eb7274ad.tq: Separate inscriptional evidence for a literary collaboration from inscriptions used for language history.
xs: The **Nandampudi donation inscription** is the evidence of **Narayana Bhattu's** help (G2 2019 key) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Nannaya** himself wrote it.
**Addanki**, **Kalamalla** and **Vipparla** are evidence of pre-Nannaya Telugu.
xa: Narayana Bhattu's titles: **Kaviraja Shekhara**, **Karibha Vajrankudu**, **Vangmaya Durandharudu**.
**Someshwara I** of Kalyani made him his representative at **Rajamahendravaram**.
Nannaya's patron **Rajaraja Narendra** reigned **1018-1061 CE**.

nc00a9b19c9e.s: Narayana Bhattu, who knew eight languages, bore the title:
nc00a9b19c9e.x: Narayana Bhattu was Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara and represented Someshwara I of Kalyani at Rajamahendravaram.
xa: He was **Nannaya's assistant** in translating the Mahabharata.
The **Nandampudi** agrahara was given to him; the **Nandampudi donation inscription** is the evidence (G2 2019 key).
Other titles: **Kaviraja Shekhara**, **Karibha Vajrankudu**, **Vangmaya Durandharudu**.

nb8a6fc27e2e.s: Andhra Shabda Chintamani, associated with Nannaya, is best described as a work on
nb8a6fc27e2e.x: Andhra Shabda Chintamani is a Sanskrit grammatical work dealing with Telugu grammar.
nb8a6fc27e2e.tq: Match the work with its subject and language rather than with the author's better-known epic.
xs: **Andhra Shabda Chintamani** is a treatise on **Telugu grammar written in Sanskrit** — so option **(4)** is correct (G2 2017, 2025 keys).
It is traditionally ascribed to **Nannaya**; authorship is debated by some scholars.
xa: ⚠ **Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam** of **Ketana** is the **first grammar written in Telugu** (**196 padyas**).
The first Telugu **mathematics** book is **Pavuluri Mallana's Sara Sangraha Ganitam**.
Nannaya's other works: **Indra Vijayam**, **Chamundika Vilasam**.

ne050f4221c6.s: Tikkana, who dedicated his work to Hariharanatha, preached:
ne050f4221c6.x: Tikkana preached Harihara Advaita, the unity of Shiva and Vishnu; Ketana was his disciple.
xa: Some notes call his philosophy **Harihara Dvaitam**.
Ketana dedicated his work to Tikkana → Tikkana was the **first poet to receive a literary dedication**.
Tikkana's titles: **Kavibrahma**, **Ubhayakavimitrudu**.

n0ba92d27268.s: Tikkana's first work, dedicated to Manumasiddhi, was:
n0ba92d27268.x: Nirvachanottara Ramayanam was Tikkana's first work, dedicated to Manumasiddhi; Basava Puranam is by Palkuriki Somanatha.
xa: Tikkana's other work: **Kavi Vakbandham**.
His disciple: **Ketana**; **Marana** too was his disciple.
Match pair (APPSC G2 **2023**, **2025**): **Tikkana - Nirvachanottara Ramayanam**.

n28630df029e.s: Narasimha Puranam (Nrusimha Puranam), the first Kshetra-mahatmya kavya in Telugu, was written by:
n28630df029e.x: Errana wrote Narasimha Puranam, the first Kshetra-mahatmya kavya in Telugu (APPSC G2 2017 key); he also wrote Harivamsam. Tikkana wrote Nirvachanottara Ramayanam, Srinatha Kashikhandam and Bhimakhandam, and Marana Markandeya Puranam.
xs: **Errana** wrote **Narasimha Puranam**, the first **Kshetra-mahatmya kavya** in Telugu (G2 2017 key) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Tikkana** wrote Nirvachanottara Ramayanam; **Srinatha** Kashikhandam and Bhimakhandam; **Marana** Markandeya Puranam.
xa: Errana also wrote **Harivamsam**, dedicated to **Prolaya Vema**.
Errana's titles: **Prabandha Parameswara**, **Sambhudasa**.
He completed the **rest of the Aranya Parva**.

n7478804e8f5.s: Who is identified as the first prabandha writer in Telugu?
n7478804e8f5.x: Errana is identified as the first prabandha writer; Nannechoda began the tradition of the eight descriptions.
xa: ⚠ Other notes call **Srinatha** the prabandha pioneer (Sringara Naishadham, Haravilasam).
CDX names **Bhaskara Ramayanam** (Hulakki Bhaskara) the first champu kavya.
The **Prabandha** age peaked with the **Ashtadiggajas** at Krishnadevaraya's court.

n159717ad691.s: The Sanskrit work Varadambika Parinayam was written by:
n159717ad691.x: Varadambika Parinayam is by Tirumalamba (APPSC G2 2017); Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam.
xa: **Raghavapandaviyam** = **Dvyarthi kavya** (Ramayana and Mahabharata at once).
**Manucharitra** — **Allasani Peddana**; **Parijatapaharanam** — **Nandi Timmana**.
**Bhadraparinayamu** — **Allamaraju Subrahmanya Kavi** (APPSC-GS **2022**).

n0a7d54dfdfa.s: The Chebrolu inscription is significant because it shows which of the following?
o: The transition from Sanskrit to Tamil exclusively
The first use of the Madhyakkara metre
n0a7d54dfdfa.x: The Chebrolu inscription is noted for showing the Marga and Desi forms.
n0a7d54dfdfa.tq: Identify the distinctive linguistic feature associated with an inscription.
xs: The **Chebrolu inscription** shows the **Marga and Desi** forms — so option **(2)** is correct.
The first **Madhyakkara** poem is the **Bezawada** inscription.
The earliest Telugu prose is **Kalamalla**.
xa: Kakatiya-era inscriptions: **Guduru** (Beta II), **Konidena** (Opili Siddhi), **Upparapalle** (Katamaraju), **Karimnagar** (Gangadhara).
The **Desi vs Marga** debate: Bhakti poets brought native Telugu idiom against heavy Sanskrit.

n1e795fb41de.x: Vrushadhipa Satakam is by Palkuriki Somanatha; Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya wrote Sivatattvasaram.
xa: Vrushadhipa Satakam = **First Telugu Satakam**, **100 verses**.
**Sivatattvasaram** (~**400** kanda poems); Mallikarjuna = originator of the **Sataka** form.
⚠ "First Satakam" claims differ: **Sivatattvasaram** vs **Vrushadhipa Satakam**.

nc939ce577ff.s: Palkuriki Somanatha's Basava Puranam was composed in which metre?
nc939ce577ff.x: Basava Puranam is in the native dwipada metre, which Somanatha popularised, not in Champu style.
xa: **Champu** (mixed prose + verse) was pioneered by **Nannaya**.
⚠ CDX names **Markandeya Puranam** (**Marana**) as the first Telugu Purana.
**Ranganatha Ramayanam** (**Gona Budda Reddy**) was the first dwipada kavya.

n3ca16d30856.s: Palkuriki Somanatha, hailed as Prathama Andhra Viplava Kavi, led which literary movement?
n3ca16d30856.x: He led the Desi kavita movement against the Sanskritised marga style, popularising dwipada, ragada and other desi metres.
xa: He popularised desi metres: **dwipada, ragada, manjari, kanda**.
Works: **Basava Puranam**, **Panditaradhya Charitra**, **Vrushadhipa Satakam**.
He wrote **Rudra Bhashyam** in **Sanskrit** and **Ragadas** in **Kannada**.

ne3ce7b139a3.s: Nannechoda is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Vrushadhipa Satakam and the title Gajasahini
Basava Puranam and the title Prabandha Parameswara
ne3ce7b139a3.x: Nannechoda wrote Kumarasambhavam and bore the title Kavirajasekhara. He is also associated with eight descriptions characteristic of the prabandha tradition.
ne3ce7b139a3.tq: Combine the work and title that belong to the same poet.
xs: **Nannechoda** wrote **Kumarasambhavam** and bore the title **Kavirajasekhara** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Gajasahini** was **Jayapa Senani's** office; **Ubhayakavimitrudu** is **Tikkana's**; **Prabandha Parameswara** is **Errana's**.
xa: Kumarasambhavam is **Kannada-influenced** and began the **"eight descriptions"** of prabandha.
