xa: Timur's invasion **severely weakened** the Sultanate, under **Nasiruddin Mahmud Tughlaq**.
⚠ "First Mongol invasion under **Jalaluddin**" is **false** (UPSC **2022**).
Jalaluddin settled converted Mongols as **"New Mussalmans"**.

n59301ec3ab2.s: Which of the following events occurred immediately after the death of Alauddin Khalji in 1316?
o: Ghazi Malik founded the Tughlaq dynasty.
Malik Kafur set aside Khizr Khan and enthroned the minor Shihabuddin Umar.
Khusrau Khan subdued Warangal for the first time.
n59301ec3ab2.x: After Alauddin's death in 1316, Malik Kafur set aside Khizr Khan and placed the minor Shihabuddin Umar on the throne.
n59301ec3ab2.tq: Use the immediate-successor sequence to eliminate events belonging to other reigns.
xs: After Alauddin's death (**1316**), **Malik Kafur set aside Khizr Khan and enthroned the minor Shihabuddin Umar** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Kafur himself was then murdered.
**Ghazi Malik** founded the Tughlaqs only in **1320**; Khusrau Khan's Warangal campaign was the **3rd** (**1318**).
xa: Next Sultan: **Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah (1316-20)**.
⚠ This **Khizr Khan** ≠ the **Sayyid** Sultan Khizr Khan (**1414-1421**).

n16b88968e9e.s: Khusrau Khan's campaign against Warangal during the reign of Mubarak Shah is regarded as which invasion of the Kakatiya kingdom?
n16b88968e9e.x: Khusrau Khan subdued Warangal again in 1318, which is identified as the third invasion.
n16b88968e9e.tq: Separate the ordinal number of the campaign from its date and commander.
xs: Khusrau Khan's campaign was the **third invasion in 1318** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It came under **Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah (1316-20)**.
**1309-10** was Malik Kafur's treaty; **1303** the Kakatiya defeat at **Upparapalli**.
xa: Khusrau Khan became **Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah** after murdering Mubarak.
Kakatiya tribute had stopped after **1316**.

n98ca3999cf7.s: Ghazi Malik's victory over ____ marked the end of Khalji rule.
n98ca3999cf7.x: Ghazi Malik's victory over Khusrau Khan ended Khalji rule.
xa: Ghazi Malik then founded the **Tughlaq** dynasty.
Ghazi Malik had been Alauddin's governor of **Punjab**.

n6587ac70407.s: The story of Padmini is narrated in the work Padmavat, written by:
n6587ac70407.x: Padmavat was written by Malik Muhammad Jayasi. It presents the Padmini story, which some scholars regard as a legend.
n6587ac70407.tq: Match the literary work with its author and avoid the famous court-poet trap.
xs: **Padmavat** was written by **Malik Muhammad Jayasi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was written in **1540** in **Awadhi**.
**Amir Khusrau** was Alauddin's court poet; **Barani** was Ala-ul-Mulk's nephew.
xa: Some scholars treat the **Padmini** motive as **legend**.
The story rests on a text written **two centuries later** than the events.

n97deab4cb62.x: Malik Muhammad Jayasi composed Padmavat in Awadhi. Some descriptions place it within the broader Hindi literary tradition.
n97deab4cb62.tq: Distinguish the precise literary language from the broader language classification.
xs: Padmavat was written in **Awadhi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Malik Muhammad Jayasi** wrote it in **1540**; some notes call it **15th-century Hindi**.
xa: It tells of **Rani Padmini's jauhar** at **Chittor** (**1303**).
Some scholars treat the Padmini motive as **legend**.

n1e7d8eccf1e.s: The Padmini story, linked with Alauddin Khalji's conquest of Chittor, was recorded in Padmavat in:
n1e7d8eccf1e.x: The Padmini narrative was recorded in Padmavat in 1540; some scholars treat it as legend.
xa: Padmavat is by **Malik Muhammad Jayasi**, in **Awadhi**.
Chittor's king was **Rana Ratan Singh**.

nc9df559d2d1.s: Which ruler is associated with the creation of the first standing army paid in cash, along with the systems of dagh and huliya?
nc9df559d2d1.x: Alauddin Khalji created the first standing army paid in cash and introduced dagh and huliya in military administration.
nc9df559d2d1.tq: Link the military reform, payment method and identifying administrative terms to one ruler.
xs: **Alauddin Khalji** created the first standing army paid in **cash**, with **dagh** and **huliya** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was recruited by the **Ariz-i-Mumalik** (army minister).
xa: Ferishta puts its cavalry at about **4,75,000**.
Dagh = **branding of horses**; huliya = **descriptive roll** of soldiers.

n11be0b72707.s: The principal objective of Alauddin Khalji's market control regulations was to:
o: increase the profits of grain merchants in Delhi
maintain a large standing army on low, fixed salaries by keeping prices low
raise revenue for the construction of mosques and madrasas
promote free trade with Central Asian merchants
n11be0b72707.x: Prices of daily goods were lowered and fixed so that soldiers could live comfortably on low, fixed pay; military need shaped the economic policy. The regulations curbed merchants rather than enriching them, and they were not aimed at religious building or free trade.
n11be0b72707.tq: Cheap goods for a cheap army (APPSC G2 2017).
xs: The aim was to **maintain a large standing army on low, fixed salaries** by keeping prices low — so option **(2)** is correct.
Soldiers could live comfortably on low pay (APPSC G2 **2017** key); **military need shaped economic policy**.
The controls curbed merchants and **ended monopolies** — not merchant profit or free trade.
xa: Criticism: the controls may have been **confined to Delhi** and hurt **merchants and peasants**.
Mubarak Shah abolished them after **1316**.

n00a19cb38be.s: Which one of the following best explains the contradictory effects of Alauddin Khalji’s reforms?
o: They weakened the army but eliminated all opposition among the nobles.
They raised prices and ended the use of spies, but strengthened provincial autonomy.
They benefited merchants and peasants while weakening the central government.
They kept prices low and strengthened the army, but espionage and repression generated discontent.
n00a19cb38be.x: The reforms helped maintain low prices and a strong army capable of resisting the Mongols, but repression and espionage created widespread discontent.
n00a19cb38be.tq: Balance positive and negative consequences instead of selecting a one-sided claim.
xs: The reforms **kept prices low and strengthened the army, but espionage and repression bred discontent** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The army became strong enough to **beat the Mongols**.
**Rule by espionage + repression** hollowed out the state.
xa: The dynasty **fell soon after his death in 1316**.
Criticism: controls may have been **confined to Delhi**, and they hurt **merchants and peasants**.

n41734c47546.s: Under Alauddin Khalji, the Sarai Adl market dealt in:
o: cloth, sugar, dry fruits, butter and oil
n41734c47546.x: Sarai Adl dealt in cloth and similar commodities; the Mandi handled food grains.
xa: ⚠ **Mandi** = grain; **Sarai Adl** = cloth and other goods.
Each market had a **Shahna-i-Mandi** (superintendent).

ncce1360aa51.s: Under Alauddin Khalji, the superintendent of an individual market was the:
ncce1360aa51.x: The Shahna-i-Mandi supervised each market; the system ran under the Diwan-i-Riyasat, who worked under the Naib-i-Riyasat.
xa: **Barids** (intelligence officers) and **munhiyan** (secret spies) sent daily reports.
⚠ **Diwan-i-Riyasat** = markets; **Diwan-i-Mustakhraj** = revenue arrears.

nac216cf0ec2.s: Which officer was associated with the recovery of arrears from revenue officials?
nac216cf0ec2.x: The Diwan-i-Mustakhraj was established to recover arrears from revenue officials. The Diwan-i-Riyasat was concerned with market administration.
nac216cf0ec2.tq: Separate the similarly named market and revenue departments by their functions.
xs: The **Diwan-i-Mustakhraj** recovered **arrears from revenue officials** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Diwan-i-Riyasat** (under the **Naib-i-Riyasat**) ran the markets; the **Shahna-i-Mandi** supervised one market.
xa: ⚠ **Diwan-i-Riyasat** = markets; **Diwan-i-Mustakhraj** = revenue arrears.
**Malik Naib** (deputy) was the rank **Malik Kafur** rose to.

n79d8f4413dc.s: Alauddin Khalji defeated the Mongols at which of the following places in 1298, 1299, 1305 and 1306 respectively?
n79d8f4413dc.x: The Mongol defeats associated with the four years were Jalandhar in 1298, Kili in 1299, Amroha in 1305 and Ravi in 1306.
n79d8f4413dc.tq: Match each year with its place and reject sequences with swapped battle sites.
xs: The victories were **Jalandhar, Kili, Amroha and Ravi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Jalandhar 1298**, **Kili 1299**.
xa: During one invasion he took shelter in **Siri** fort.
He **repaired old frontier forts** and built new ones, completing Balban's frontier policy.

n410fc88b32b.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes dagh from huliya or chehra?
o: Dagh was the cash payment of soldiers, whereas huliya was the recruitment of cavalry.
Dagh was a land-revenue assessment, whereas huliya recorded the wealth of nobles.
Dagh was the registration of peasants, whereas huliya was the measurement of land.
Dagh was the branding of horses, whereas huliya was the descriptive roll of soldiers.
n410fc88b32b.x: Dagh referred to branding horses and huliya or chehra to the descriptive roll of each soldier. Neither was a land-revenue measure or an assessment of nobles’ wealth.
n410fc88b32b.tq: Discriminate between two closely associated military terms.
xs: **Dagh** = **branding of horses**; **huliya / chehra** = **descriptive roll of each soldier** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Both stopped **fraud / false musters**.
⚠ Notes that call dagh a land-revenue measure, or huliya an assessment of nobles' wealth, are wrong.
xa: Alauddin was the **first Sultan** to keep a large **permanent standing army**, paid in **cash**.
The Bahmani minister **Mahmud Gawan** later brought in **dagh and chehra**.

nc5d5709c5e8.s: Alauddin Khalji fixed the state's share of produce (kharaj) at:
nc5d5709c5e8.x: The state share was one-half (50%); he was also the first Sultan to measure land, using the biswa.
xa: New taxes: **ghari** (house) and **charai** (grazing); **jizya** continued.
Resumed **inam** and **waqf** grants enlarged the **khalisa**.

n150a9a2426c.s: The headman's cess abolished by Alauddin Khalji was called:
n150a9a2426c.x: Alauddin abolished the kismat-i-khuti and brought khuts, muqaddams and chaudharis under taxation.
xa: The state share (**kharaj**) was **half** of produce.
Land was measured in **biswa**.

nindian-history-23-7.s: Under Alauddin Khalji, Ghari was a tax on:
nindian-history-23-7.x: Ghari was the house tax; Charai was the grazing tax and Kharaj 50% of yield.
n: Alauddin Khalji reclaimed Milq lands. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Alauddin Khalji reclaimed Waqf lands. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
The reclamation of Milq and Waqf lands expanded Khalisa land. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Kharaj was a land tax under Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Kharaj was fixed at 50% of the yield under Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Ghari was a house tax under Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Charai was a grazing tax on milch animals under Alauddin Khalji. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
xa: ⚠ **Ghari** = house; **Charai** = grazing.
**Khalisa** = crown land, grew as **inam, waqf** grants were resumed.
**Jizya** continued; ⚠ some notes give the state share as one-fifth.
State share of **half (50%)**: BPSC **2018**.

nafe95f9d5da.s: Barani's causes of revolt perceived by Alauddin were noble wealth, noble marriages and gatherings, drinking and:
nafe95f9d5da.x: Barani's four causes were noble wealth, noble intermarriage and gatherings, a weak intelligence system and drinking.
xa: Answers: confiscated **inam, waqf**; reorganised **spies**; **prohibited liquor**, gambling; royal permission for feasts and marriages.
APPSC G1 **2018**: prohibition + market control + severe punishment = **Alauddin**.

n7e827f452bb.s: Which of the following was NOT one of Alauddin Khalji's ordinances?
o: Confiscation of religious grants and free lands
Permission for nobles to form unrestricted marriage alliances
n7e827f452bb.x: Noble marriages and gatherings required royal permission; the other three were part of his ordinances.
xa: Offenders got **severe punishment**; rape was punished severely.
The causes come from **Barani**.

n5918c2e32db.s: Malik Kafur's second expedition against Warangal (1309–10) was accompanied by:
n5918c2e32db.x: Malik Kafur and Khwaja Haji besieged Warangal, won Prataparudra's submission and sent loot to Delhi on 1,000 camels.
xa: By tradition the **Koh-i-Noor** was part of the Kakatiya treasure surrendered in **1310**.
**Amir Khusrau** went with the 1310 campaign.

n12dd027100d.s: What was the principal purpose of Alauddin Khalji's Deccan expeditions according to the policy described?
o: To obtain plunder and tribute for maintaining the army
To establish permanent provinces ruled by Delhi governors
To transfer the Delhi capital to Warangal
To spread a new religious order in the southern kingdoms
n12dd027100d.x: The Deccan expeditions were primarily financial ventures intended to secure plunder and tribute for paying the army, rather than to annex the southern states.
n12dd027100d.tq: Distinguish the stated economic objective from the stronger but incorrect claim of annexation.
xs: The aim was **plunder and tribute** to pay for the **army** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was **not annexation**: southern kings **kept their thrones** and paid tribute.
xa: **Ramachandra** of Devagiri and **Prataparudra II** of Warangal both agreed to tribute.
The **Pandya** kingdom of Madurai was **sacked** (**1311**).

n817a8fa63c5.s: Amir Khusrau's Khazain-ul-Futuh describes the Warangal fort as:
o: a single mud wall with no moat
n817a8fa63c5.x: Khazain-ul-Futuh describes Warangal's double-walled fort, its moat and the diamond mines; Khusrau accompanied the 1310 campaign.
xa: The **1309-10** siege by Kafur and **Khwaja Haji** made **Prataparudra** a tributary.
Traditionally the **Koh-i-Noor** was surrendered in **1310**.

n443599ebd2f.s: Token currency, transfer of capital and canals are associated with the:
n443599ebd2f.x: The Tughlaqs are known for token currency, capital transfer and canals; the Khaljis for market control and the Lodis as the first Afghan dynasty.
xa: Khaljis' contribution also included **taxation reforms**.
Alauddin's reign = the **"imperial period"**.

n848bdd04bef.s: The first attack on Warangal in 1303 ended in failure at Upparapalli. Which pair of Kakatiya commanders defeated Malik Fakhruddin Juna there?
o: Hamir Deva and Rana Ratan Singh
n848bdd04bef.x: Potuganti Maili and Recherla Venna defeated Malik Fakhruddin Juna at Upparapalli during the failed 1303 attack on Warangal.
n848bdd04bef.tq: Use the local commanders as the decisive clue in an Andhra-specific military question.
xs: **Potuganti Maili and Recherla Venna** beat **Malik Fakhruddin Juna** at **Upparapalli** (**1303**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Ramachandra** and **Vira Ballala III** were Yadava and Hoysala kings; **Hamir Deva** and **Ratan Singh** were Rajputs.
xa: The **1309-10** attack made **Prataparudra** a tributary.
⚠ **1303** = Delhi defeated; **1309-10** = treaty and **annual tribute**.

nfbc033477ae.s: In matters of state policy, Alauddin Khalji declared that he would be guided by:
nfbc033477ae.x: Alauddin refused the Ulema's guidance and declared his actions would be governed by the interests of the state.
xa: He revived **Balban's** harsh, centralised rule, but without Balban's dependence on **religious sanction**.
He took the title **Sikandar-i-Sani** (second Alexander).

nf88b42c3a7e.s: The office of Ariz-i-Mamalik under Alauddin Khalji was associated principally with which department?
nf88b42c3a7e.x: Ariz-i-Mamalik was the head of the army department. It was not a ministerial office concerned with law or religious endowments.
nf88b42c3a7e.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to an administrative title.
xs: **Ariz-i-Mamalik** headed the **army department** — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes call it "minister of law" — a trap.
Under Jalaluddin, Alauddin held this post along with **Amir-i-Tuzuk**.
xa: The Ariz-i-Mumalik **recruited the standing army**.
**Diwan-i-Riyasat** ran the markets; **Diwan-i-Mustakhraj** recovered revenue arrears.

n27447158f87.s: Unlike Balban, Alauddin Khalji did not depend on ____ to justify his policies.
n27447158f87.x: Alauddin revived Balban's harsh, centralised rule but, unlike Balban, did not depend on religious sanction.
xa: He declared he would act in the **state's interest** whatever the ulema advised.
Kotwal **Ala-ul-Mulk** talked him out of world conquest and a **new religion**.

n4d0ac697458.s: Who persuaded Alauddin Khalji to abandon both his plans for world conquest and a new religion?
n4d0ac697458.x: Kotwal Ala-ul-Mulk talked Alauddin out of both the plan for world conquest and the proposal for a new religion.
n4d0ac697458.tq: Identify the adviser associated with restraining a ruler’s ambitious proposal.
xs: **Kotwal Ala-ul-Mulk** talked Alauddin out of **world conquest** and a **new religion** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Alauddin's world-conqueror dream gave him the title **Sikandar-i-Sani**.
xa: ⚠ **Nusrat Khan** acquired **Malik Kafur**; **Barani** is the main source on the market control.
Alauddin openly overrode the **ulema** in state matters.

n7ba22793dc2.s: Alauddin Khalji's market regulations aimed at price fixation, guaranteed supply, controlled distribution and:
n7ba22793dc2.x: The regulations fixed prices, guaranteed supply, controlled distribution and ended monopolistic practices.
xa: Aim: keep a large army on **low, fixed salaries** (APPSC G2 **2017** key).
The granaries are called the **first public distribution system** of the Sultanate (BPSC **2020**).

n1f9ea6a903e.s: The main source for Alauddin Khalji's market control measures is:
n1f9ea6a903e.x: Barani is the main source; Mubarak Shah later abolished the controls.
xa: UPPSC keys call the market control **"highly successful"**.
Prices stayed **stable** during Alauddin's reign.

ncced8fe04cf.s: Prohibition of liquor and gambling, control of markets and severe punishment of offenders are associated with which Delhi Sultan?
ncced8fe04cf.x: All three measures belong to Alauddin Khalji: his ordinances prohibited liquor and gambling, he regulated the markets, and offenders were punished severely. Balban was harsh but did not control markets; Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Firoz did not impose these measures together.
xs: Prohibition, market control and severe punishment = **Alauddin Khalji** (APPSC G1 **2018**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
His ordinances **prohibited liquor**, intoxicants and gambling.
His **market control** fixed prices for a cheap standing army.
xa: Barani's four causes of revolt: **wealth**, **intermarriage**, **weak spies**, **drinking**.
**Mubarak Shah** withdrew the harsh regulations after **1316**.

n1c6163ff8f0.s: Which Sultan abolished Alauddin Khalji’s price controls, restored confiscated lands and withdrew harsh regulations after ascending the throne?
n1c6163ff8f0.x: Mubarak Shah, who ruled from 1316 to 1320, abolished the price controls, restored confiscated lands and withdrew the harsh regulations.
n1c6163ff8f0.tq: Link a ruler with the specific reversal of a predecessor’s measures.
xs: **Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah (1316-20)** reversed Alauddin's system — so option **(3)** is correct.
He **abolished price controls**, **restored confiscated lands** and **withdrew harsh regulations**.
xa: Alauddin died in **1316**; the dynasty fell soon after.
Under Alauddin **prices stayed stable** and the army beat the Mongols.

nbb634329a78.s: Which of the following is regarded as a major significance of Alauddin Khalji’s economic and revenue measures?
o: They made religious institutions solely responsible for land measurement.
They introduced paper currency and decentralised all revenue administration.
They introduced the first state-run price-control and rationing system in India and the first land measurement for revenue.
They abolished all forms of taxation and ended state supervision of markets.
nbb634329a78.x: Alauddin’s measures are regarded as the first state-run price-control and rationing system in India and the first land measurement system for revenue assessment.
nbb634329a78.tq: Select the option containing both linked historical significances without an exaggerated claim.
xs: They were the **first state-run price control and rationing system** in India and the **first land measurement for revenue** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Land was measured in **biswa**; granaries rationed grain in scarcity.
There was no paper currency and no end of taxation — taxes like **ghari** and **charai** were added.
xa: His reign = **"imperial period"** of the Sultanate.
Despotism and heavy spying hollowed out the state.

n4f095f79f59.s: Ghazi Malik became Sultan Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq in 1320 after killing:
n4f095f79f59.x: Ghazi Malik, earlier governor of Punjab, killed Khusrau Shah and became Sultan in 1320.
xa: He built the **Tughlaqabad** fort.
He was the **first Sultan to start irrigation/canal works**.

n0b526f6a169.s: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq limited any increase in land revenue to about:
n0b526f6a169.x: Ghiyasuddin limited any increase to about one-tenth and raised it gradually, besides drought remission and cultivation of waste land.
xa: He was the **first Sultan to start canal works**; **Firoz** dug the most.
He improved the **postal system** with runners and horsemen.

ne9752d0d373.s: Warangal was renamed Sultanpur after it was conquered during the reign of
ne9752d0d373.x: Warangal fell in 1323 during Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's reign and was renamed Sultanpur.
ne9752d0d373.tq: Link the conquered place, its new name and the ruler responsible for the conquest.
xs: Warangal fell in **1323** under **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq** and was renamed **Sultanpur** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The attack was led by Prince **Juna Khan** (later **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**).
xa: Andhra was then run by **Malik Burhanuddin** of Devagiri, assisted by **Malik Maqbul**.
**Prataparudra II** was taken towards Delhi and died in the **Narmada**.

nee15df5483d.s: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq died in 1325 when a wooden pavilion collapsed at:
nee15df5483d.x: He died at Afghanpur in 1325 (Ibn Battuta suspected Juna Khan); he had built Tughlaqabad.
xa: **Ibn Battuta** suspects a plot by **Juna Khan**.
Cities of Delhi: **Siri** — **Alauddin Khalji**; **Tughlaqabad** — **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**.

n6a3890d3621.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq transferred his capital to Devagiri in:
n6a3890d3621.x: The capital was transferred in 1327; token currency followed around 1329–30.
xa: Khurasan: a huge army raised, then **disbanded unpaid / unused**.
Qarachil (**Kumaon** hills): **army destroyed in the hills**.

nc89991724dd.s: The token currency introduced by Muhammad bin Tughlaq around 1329–30 consisted of:
o: Gold and silver coins issued to overcome a gold shortage
Silver and copper coins issued exclusively for the army
Copper and brass coins intended to function as tokens
Lead and potin coins modelled on Satavahana currency
nc89991724dd.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced token currency in copper and brass because of a shortage of silver. Widespread forgery led to its recall and redemption at heavy cost.
nc89991724dd.tq: Discriminate the metal composition and the economic purpose of the token currency.
xs: The token currency was of **copper and brass**, meant to function as tokens — so option **(3)** is correct.
Cause: a **silver shortage** and the idea of a token coin.
Result: **mass forgery**; the coins were **recalled and redeemed at heavy cost** to the treasury.
xa: It came c. **1329-30**, after the move to Daulatabad (**1327**).
Exam line: "token currency was **copper and brass**".

n5a99810398c.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq's higher taxation of the Doab, coinciding with a famine, led to:
n5a99810398c.x: Meant to raise revenue, the Doab tax increase coincided with famine and caused peasant revolts and flight.
xa: During the famine the Sultan moved to the **Swarga-dwari** relief camp on the **Ganga** near **Kannauj**.
**Taqavi** (sondhar) loans for seed and wells came from MBT.

n8ffa67950fc.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq's Qarachil (Kumaon hills) expedition aimed at:
n8ffa67950fc.x: The Qarachil expedition aimed to secure the hill frontier; the Khurasan expedition aimed at Central Asian conquest.
xa: Khurasan army: **disbanded unpaid / unused**; Qarachil army: **destroyed in the hills**.
Barani called MBT a **"mixture of opposites"**.

n5d220c11bb6.s: During the famine associated with Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign, the relief and cultivation camp near Kannauj on the Ganga was called:
n5d220c11bb6.x: Swarga-dwari was a famine-relief camp on the Ganga near Kannauj, established for relief and cultivation.
n5d220c11bb6.tq: Use the place-name association to distinguish a famine-relief camp from Firoz Shah's institutions and towns.
xs: The relief camp was **Swarga-dwari** (Swargadwari), on the **Ganga near Kannauj** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It gave **relief and cultivation** during the **Doab famine**.
**Dar-ul-Shifa** (free hospital) and **Diwan-i-Khairat** (charity) are **Firoz's**; **Firozabad** is his town.
xa: The **Doab tax rise** coincided with the famine; peasants revolted and fled.
MBT gave **taqavi** loans for **seed + wells**.

na61103a4cea.s: Which one of the following is NOT a town associated with Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
na61103a4cea.x: Firozabad, Fatehabad and Hisar Firoza were associated with Firoz Shah. Daulatabad was the renamed capital under Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
na61103a4cea.tq: Find the odd location by separating Firoz Shah's town-building from Muhammad bin Tughlaq's capital transfer.
xs: **Daulatabad** is not a Firoz town — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Daulatabad was **Devagiri**, renamed by **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** (**1327**).
Firoz founded **Firozabad** (Firoz Shah Kotla), **Fatehabad**, **Hisar Firoza** and **Jaunpur**.
xa: He laid about **1,200** fruit gardens around Delhi.
He moved **Ashokan pillars** from **Topra** and **Meerut** to Delhi.

nindian-history-10-17.s: Who shifted the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad and then back to Delhi?
nindian-history-10-17.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq moved the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (Devagiri) in 1327 and later back to Delhi.
xa: Other experiments: **token currency** of **copper and brass**, **Doab** tax rise, **Khurasan** and **Qarachil** expeditions.
The Doab tax rise **coincided with a famine**.
MBT died at **Thatta** (**1351**).

n9bb0e831170.s: The Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi established by Muhammad bin Tughlaq was primarily concerned with
n9bb0e831170.x: Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi was an agriculture department intended to extend cultivation, especially by bringing waste land under the plough.
n9bb0e831170.tq: Identify the administrative department from the function assigned to it.
xs: **Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi** was MBT's **agriculture** department to **bring waste land under cultivation** — so option **(4)** is correct (UKPSC **2025**; UPPSC **2017**).
It also pushed farmers towards **better crops**.
Horse branding (**dagh**) and **market control** were **Alauddin's**; **jizya on Brahmins** was **Firoz's**.
xa: ⚠ **Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi** = MBT; **Diwan-i-Khairat** and **Diwan-i-Bandagan** = Firoz.
**Taqavi** loans were later **written off by Firoz**.

n4ff88874fc6.s: Taqavi, or sondhar, loans during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign were provided mainly for
n4ff88874fc6.x: Taqavi or sondhar loans were agricultural advances intended to help cultivators purchase seed and dig wells.
n4ff88874fc6.tq: Match the specialised administrative term with its precise practical purpose.
xs: **Taqavi** (sondhar) loans were for **seeds and wells** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They were MBT's state loans to cultivators.
xa: **Firoz** later **wrote off** MBT's taqavi loans and all debts owed to the state.
MBT's **Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi** worked to **extend cultivation**.

n4ea57ec434e.s: According to Ibn Battuta, horse couriers (uluq) were posted at intervals of:
n4ea57ec434e.x: Horse couriers were every four miles; foot couriers (dawa) had three stations to every mile.
xa: ⚠ **Uluq** = horse; **dawa** = foot.
Ghiyasuddin had already improved the post with **runners + horsemen**.

nbcbb960b1bd.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq was placed on the throne at Thatta in 1351 after the death of:
nbcbb960b1bd.x: Firoz Shah succeeded Muhammad bin Tughlaq at Thatta in 1351 and ruled until 1388.
nbcbb960b1bd.tq: Test succession through a direct ruler-event association.
xs: Firoz was enthroned at **Thatta** after **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** died there (**1351**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Jam Babaniya** of **Sind** only agreed to pay tribute; **Haji Iliyas** was Bengal's ruler.
xa: Firoz ruled **1351-88**.
Badauni: on MBT's death the Sultan was **freed from his people, and they from him**.

n4074b6e01cf.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq's irrigation cess, haq-i-sharb, was:
n4074b6e01cf.x: Haq-i-sharb was one-tenth; his canals carried water from the Yamuna and Sutlej to Hisar.
xa: Firoz built **more canals than any other Sultan** (BPSC **2019**).
His towns include **Hisar Firoza** and **Fatehabad**.

n142de7f50db.s: The Ashokan pillars brought to Delhi during the reign of Firoz Shah Tughlaq came from:
n142de7f50db.x: Firoz Shah transported Ashokan pillars from Topra in the Ambala region and from Meerut to Delhi.
n142de7f50db.tq: Test the pair of source locations and reject the nearby religious and inscriptional sites.
xs: The Ashokan pillars came from **Topra** (Ambala) **and Meerut** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Jwalamukhi** at **Nagarkot** is where he seized **Sanskrit texts**, not pillars.
xa: Firoz founded **Firozabad** (Firoz Shah Kotla).
He laid about **1,200** fruit gardens around Delhi.

nc06fd6f7826.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq's wazir Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul is noted for:
o: Paying compensation to people who had suffered under Muhammad bin Tughlaq
Introducing token currency in copper and brass
Leading the Qarachil expedition into the Kumaon hills
nc06fd6f7826.x: Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul paid compensation to persons who had suffered during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's rule.
nc06fd6f7826.tq: Identify the responsible official by matching the administrative action with the correct office-holder.
xs: **Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul** **paid compensation to people who had suffered under Muhammad bin Tughlaq** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Nagarkot texts were translated by **Azizuddin Khalid Khani**; **token currency** and **Qarachil** were **MBT's**.
xa: Maqbul was the Brahmin **Jagannatha Pandit**, converted to Islam.
He had assisted **Malik Burhanuddin** at **Warangal** before becoming Firoz's chief minister.

n908c32bfabc.s: Which Delhi Sultan set up a separate Public Works Department to run his building programme?
n908c32bfabc.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq created a Public Works Department for his canals, towns and buildings. Alauddin is known for market control, Muhammad bin Tughlaq for his experiments and Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi, and Sikandar Lodi for founding Agra.
xs: **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** set up a **Public Works Department** for his buildings (APPSC G2 **2017**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Alauddin** is known for **market control** and **dagh**; **MBT** for **token currency** and **Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi**.
xa: Firoz's other departments: **Diwan-i-Khairat**, **Diwan-i-Bandagan**, **Dar-ul-Shifa**, **Diwan-i-Istihqaq**.
**Sikandar Lodi** had a Sanskrit medical treatise translated into Persian.

nf7b4b3b31de.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq made the iqtas:
nf7b4b3b31de.x: Firoz made iqtas hereditary; he also wrote off taqavi loans, fixed land revenue and kept the four Islamic taxes.
xa: He levied **jizya** even on **Brahmins**, for the first time.
Hereditary iqtas and the slave corps **weakened central control**.

n0c7896f04e7.s: The autobiography of Firoz Shah Tughlaq is:
n0c7896f04e7.x: Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi is the autobiography of Firoz Shah Tughlaq.
n0c7896f04e7.tq: Distinguish the ruler's autobiography from Barani's historical and political works.
xs: Firoz Shah's autobiography is **Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Dalail-i-Firozshahi** is the Persian translation of Sanskrit texts from **Nagarkot**, by **Azizuddin Khalid Khani**.
**Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** and **Fatawa-i-Jahandari** were written by **Barani** under Firoz's patronage.
xa: **Ragadarpan**, a work on music, was also translated in his reign.
⚠ **Sikandar Lodi** had a Sanskrit medical treatise translated into Persian — a different Sultan.

n5d20f5e2bbb.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq's two failed expeditions to Bengal were against:
n5d20f5e2bbb.x: Both Bengal campaigns against Haji Iliyas failed; Jam Babaniya of Sind agreed to pay tribute.
xa: Firoz did take **Jajnagar** and **Nagarkot**.
His military record is summed up as **mixed results**.

n00c1c84c2fe.s: The first Sultan of Delhi to dig canals was:
n00c1c84c2fe.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq first dug canals; Firoz Shah dug the largest number.
xa: Firoz's canals ran from the **Yamuna and Sutlej to Hisar**, with **haq-i-sharb** (one-tenth).
Ghiyasuddin also capped revenue rises at **one-tenth** and improved the **postal system**.

nindian-history-23-2-8.s: Under Firuz Tughlaq, about 1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts were obtained from the temple library of:
nindian-history-23-2-8.x: The manuscripts came from the Jawalamukhi temple library at Nagarkot, and Azizuddin Khalid Khani translated some into Persian.
n: Various scholars translated Sanskrit texts into Persian during Firuz Tughlaq’s rule. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23-2 · pp 84-85]
Approximately 1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts were associated with the Jawalamukhi library. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23-2 · pp 84-85]
Azizuddin Khan translated the Sanskrit manuscripts from the Jawalamukhi library into Persian. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23-2 · pp 84-85]
xa: The translation was **Dalail-i-Firozshahi** by **Aizuddin (Azizuddin) Khalid Khani** (UPPSC **2023**).
**Ragadarpan**, on music, was also translated in his reign.
Firoz's autobiography: **Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi**.
Firoz took **Jajnagar** and **Nagarkot**.

n97fc38832f0.s: In 1342 Muhammad bin Tughlaq sent Ibn Battuta, the Qazi of Delhi, as envoy to:
n97fc38832f0.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq made Ibn Battuta Qazi of Delhi and sent him as envoy to China in 1342.
xa: He was a **Moroccan**, born at **Tangiers**, **1304**; real name **Abu Abdullah Muhammad**.
His **Rihla (Kitab-ul-Rehla)** is in **Arabic**.

nfb3359a71b5.s: Which of the following observations is associated with Ibn Battuta's account of the Delhi Sultanate?
o: Sati was permitted only to members of the royal family.
Sati was completely prohibited throughout the Sultanate.
Sati was not recorded by any contemporary traveller.
nfb3359a71b5.x: Ibn Battuta recorded the practice of sati and stated that it required the Sultan's permission.
nfb3359a71b5.tq: Select the precise recorded condition rather than an absolute statement about the practice.
xs: Ibn Battuta records that **sati required the Sultan's permission** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He also recorded the **spy system** and the **postal system**.
xa: He found MBT **eccentric**, **severe in temper**, but **generous**.
He was the **first foreign traveller** to visit **Vijayanagara**, in **Harihara I's** reign (APPSC PYQ).

n7588fb4c072.s: Ibn Battuta, who came to India in 1333 during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, was a native of:
n7588fb4c072.x: Ibn Battuta (Abu Abdullah Muhammad) was a Moroccan, born at Tangiers in 1304. He came to India in 1333, was made Qazi of Delhi and wrote the Rihla in Arabic. He was not from Persia, Egypt or Turkey.
xs: Ibn Battuta was from **Morocco** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was born at **Tangiers** in **1304**; real name **Abu Abdullah Muhammad**.
He came in **1333** and was made **Qazi of Delhi**.
xa: He was sent as **envoy to China** (**1342**).
He wrote the **Rihla** in **Arabic**.

n213bde8f2db.s: The Madurai Sultanate was established in:
n213bde8f2db.x: The Madurai Sultanate dates to 1335, Vijayanagara to 1336 and the Bahmani kingdom to 1347.
xa: Madurai Sultanate: **Jalaluddin Ahsan Shah**.
Bahmani founder: **Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah** (**Hasan Gangu**).

n7084ad7edb4.s: The Reddis expelled the Tughlaq forces from coastal Andhra around:
n7084ad7edb4.x: Coastal Andhra was freed around 1325, before the Madurai Sultanate (1335), Vijayanagara (1336) and the Bahmani kingdom (1347).
xa: **Kapaya Nayaka** recaptured Warangal also in **1336**.
These break-aways followed MBT's **badly carried out** schemes.

n91e7e4991bd.s: Harihara and Bukka founded Vijayanagara under the guidance of:
n91e7e4991bd.x: Harihara and Bukka, sent by Muhammad bin Tughlaq, founded Vijayanagara under Vidyaranya's guidance.
xa: **Ibn Battuta** visited Vijayanagara in **Harihara I's** reign.
⚠ In **1336** Kapaya Nayaka also recaptured **Warangal**.

n7e3dcb19510.s: The Tughlaq period of the Delhi Sultanate is generally placed between
n7e3dcb19510.x: The Tughlaq period began with Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq in 1320 and ended when Khizr Khan took Delhi in 1414.
n7e3dcb19510.tq: Identify the dynasty's beginning and end points rather than confusing it with neighbouring dynasties.
xs: The Tughlaq period runs **1320 to 1414** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It began with **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq Shah in 1320** and ended when **Khizr Khan** took Delhi in **1414**.
xa: Ghiyasuddin ruled **1320-25**; Firoz **1351-88**.
**Timur's invasion** came in **1398**.

n23d40676ba8.s: Who was the Tughlaq Sultan on the throne of Delhi at the time of Timur's invasion in 1398?
n23d40676ba8.x: Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah Tughlaq, the last Tughlaq, ruled during Timur's invasion of 1398. Firoz had died in 1388, and Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq II and Abu Bakr were earlier weak successors who fought each other.
xs: **Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah Tughlaq** was on the throne during **Timur's invasion (1398)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He was the **last Tughlaq**; some notes call him "Nasiruddin Muhammad Tughlaq".
**Firoz** had ruled to **1388**; **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq II** and **Abu Bakr** were weak successors who fought each other.
xa: After Sultan Mahmud's death **Daulat Khan Lodi** was briefly recognised.
**Khizr Khan** took Delhi in **1414**.

n2c8b7e0c678.s: The Vilasa copper plate of Prolaya Nayaka and Gangadevi's Madhura Vijayam are important for understanding:
o: The conditions under Tughlaq rule in the southern regions
The revenue system of the Bahmani kingdom
The maritime trade policy of the Madurai Sultanate
The succession disputes among the Mughal emperors
n2c8b7e0c678.x: The Vilasa copper plate and Madhura Vijayam describe the conditions prevailing under Tughlaq rule in the southern regions.
n2c8b7e0c678.tq: Associate each source with the historical situation it records, not with a later administrative theme.
xs: They describe **conditions under Tughlaq rule in the southern regions** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Vilasa copper plate** is **Prolaya Nayaka's**; **Madhura Vijayam** is **Gangadevi's**.
xa: Prolaya Nayaka led the fight to free Andhra (**Vilasa** grant, c. **1330**).
**Kapaya Nayaka** then **recaptured Warangal in 1336**.

ncd1b4b1837d.s: Who described Muhammad bin Tughlaq as a 'mixture of opposites'?
ncd1b4b1837d.x: Barani described Muhammad bin Tughlaq as a 'mixture of opposites'. Ibn Battuta characterised him as eccentric, severe in temper and generous.
ncd1b4b1837d.tq: Separate the judgements of the court chronicler, foreign traveller and other contemporary figures.
xs: **Barani** called MBT a **"mixture of opposites"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ibn Battuta** called him **eccentric**, **quick-tempered**, but **generous**.
**Badauni** commented on his **death at Thatta (1351)**.
xa: Barani's **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** is the main account of these reigns.
Verdict: experiments **sound in idea, poor in execution**.

n9757630f281.s: Ibn Battuta is described as the first foreign traveller to visit Vijayanagara during the reign of
n9757630f281.x: Ibn Battuta is identified in this context as the first foreign traveller to visit Vijayanagara during the reign of Harihara I.
n9757630f281.tq: Distinguish the earliest associated ruler from the more famous later Vijayanagara monarchs.
xs: Ibn Battuta was the first foreign traveller to visit Vijayanagara, in **Harihara I's** reign (APPSC PYQ) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Vijayanagara was founded in **1336** by **Harihara and Bukka**.
xa: He came to India in **1333** and served MBT as **Qazi of Delhi**.
He was sent as **envoy to China** in **1342**.

nd255830d09c.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with Balban?
o: The doctrine of blood and iron
nd255830d09c.x: Branding of horses, or dagh, was a measure of Alauddin Khalji. Balban was associated with Sijda, paibos, the Zil-i-Ilahi theory and the policy of blood and iron.
nd255830d09c.tq: Find the one measure belonging to a neighbouring Sultan rather than the ruler named.
xs: **Branding of horses** (**dagh**) was not Balban's — so option **(4)** is the answer.
Dagh belongs to **Alauddin Khalji** (APPSC-G2 **2023** match key).
Balban's: **Zil-i-Ilahi** theory, **sijda and paibos**, **blood and iron**.
xa: Alauddin's other measures: **huliya**, **market control**, **land measurement**.
Balban also created **Diwan-i-Arz** and ended the **Chahalgani**.

nc20362a3fce.s: Alauddin Alam Shah ended the Sayyid dynasty by:
o: Voluntarily giving up the throne to Bahlol Lodi in 1451
Being defeated and killed by Babur
nc20362a3fce.x: Alauddin Alam Shah voluntarily gave up the throne to Bahlol Lodi in 1451.
nc20362a3fce.tq: Test the unusual voluntary-succession detail rather than a battlefield transfer.
xs: **Alauddin Alam Shah** voluntarily **gave up the throne to Bahlol Lodi in 1451** — option **(1)**.
**Babur** killed **Ibrahim Lodi**, not a Sayyid, at **Panipat (1526)**; **Mubarak Shah** ruled before Alam Shah.
xa: ⚠ Bahlol got the throne **without a battle**.
**Bahlol Lodi** had been **Governor of Punjab**; he ruled **1451-1489** and conquered **Jaunpur**.
The **Sayyid dynasty** lasted **1414-51**.

n19359dfebde.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the religious policy and cultural activity of Sikandar Lodi?
o: He adopted Buddhism and commissioned translations into Pali.
He patronised only Persian religious works and permitted no temple destruction.
He destroyed temples and imposed jizya, but also had a Sanskrit medical work translated into Persian.
He abolished jizya and prohibited the translation of Sanskrit works.
n19359dfebde.x: Sikandar Lodi was religiously intolerant in several actions, including destruction of images and temples and imposition of jizya, yet he had a Sanskrit medical treatise translated into Persian.
n19359dfebde.tq: Handle a seemingly contradictory ruler profile by separating religious policy from cultural patronage.
xs: Sikandar Lodi **destroyed temples and imposed jizya**, yet had a **Sanskrit medical treatise translated into Persian** — option **(3)**.
He destroyed **Jwalamukhi (Nagarkot)** images and **Mathura** temples, so "no temple destruction" (2) is wrong; he **imposed** jizya, so (4) is wrong.
xa: Pen name **Gulrukhi** for his **Persian poetry**.
Built **Moth ki Masjid** and the royal tombs of the **Lodi Gardens**.
Abolished several **taxes and trade restrictions** → necessities cheaper.

nd2b8f5c011d.s: Which of the following was NOT a contemporary of Ibrahim Lodi?
nd2b8f5c011d.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq belonged to an earlier period. Krishnadevaraya, Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk and Rana Sanga were contemporaries of Ibrahim Lodi.
nd2b8f5c011d.tq: Use the period filter to identify the ruler separated from the contemporary group.
xs: **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq** was **NOT** a contemporary of **Ibrahim Lodi (1517-26)** — option **(2)**.
Contemporaries of Ibrahim: **Krishnadevaraya** (Vijayanagara), **Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk** (Golconda) and **Rana Sanga** (Mewar).
xa: **Golconda** became independent in **1518** under Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk.
**Rana Sanga** defeated Ibrahim at **Khatauli (1517-18)**.
The **Deccan** was then split into **five Sultanates**.

n54ba43caa31.s: Babur was descended from which two conquerors through his paternal and maternal lines respectively?
o: Mahmud of Ghazni and Muhammad Ghori
n54ba43caa31.x: Babur was descended from Timur on his father’s side and from Chengiz Khan on his mother’s side.
n54ba43caa31.tq: Keep the two genealogical lines in the correct paternal–maternal order.
xs: Babur descended from **Timur** (father's side) and **Chengiz Khan** (mother's side) — option **(1)**.
Option (3) reverses the two lines.
xa: **Timur** invaded India in **1398** and sacked **Delhi**.
Babur, with about **12,000** men, defeated **Ibrahim Lodi** (about **1,00,000**) at **Panipat** in **1526**.
He was invited by **Daulat Khan Lodi**, Governor of Punjab.

n14f15594a77.s: At Khatauli (1517-18), Ibrahim Lodi was defeated by:
n14f15594a77.x: At Khatauli Ibrahim was defeated by Rana Sanga; earlier he had made Vikramajit of Gwalior a vassal.
xa: ⚠ **Khatauli** = Ibrahim defeated by **Rana Sanga**; **Panipat** = Ibrahim killed by **Babur**.
Ibrahim reigned **1517-1526**.
He is the only Delhi Sultan to **die on the battlefield**.

n9a28d3a1fd3.s: Ibrahim Lodi occupies a unique position among the Delhi Sultans because he was the only one who:
o: Founded a new capital at Agra
n9a28d3a1fd3.x: Ibrahim Lodi was the only Delhi Sultan to die on the battlefield.
n9a28d3a1fd3.tq: Use the unique-exception clue to identify the ruler associated with a rare outcome.
xs: **Ibrahim Lodi** was the only Delhi Sultan to **die on the battlefield** — option **(3)**.
**Gaz-i-Sikandari** and **Agra** belong to **Sikandar Lodi**; **Khizr Khan** ruled as Timur's deputy.
xa: He died at the **First Battle of Panipat** (**21 April 1526**).
Ibrahim Lodi = the **last Delhi Sultan**.
Babur then captured **Delhi and Agra** and the Lodi treasure.

n57d80ba33bc.s: When Vasco da Gama reached India in 1498, who was on the throne of Delhi?
n57d80ba33bc.x: Sikandar Lodi was the Delhi Sultan when Vasco da Gama arrived in 1498.
n57d80ba33bc.tq: 1498: Sikandar ruled when the sea route opened.
xs: **Sikandar Lodi (1489-1517)** was on the throne when **Vasco da Gama** arrived in **1498** — option **(3)**.
**Bahlol** ruled till **1489**, **Ibrahim** from **1517**, and **Khizr Khan** in **1414-21**.
xa: Sikandar founded **Agra (1504)** and moved the capital there.
**Gaz-i-Sikandari** = land-measuring yard.
Pen name: **Gulrukhi**.

n21001cb40b9.s: Which feature was associated with the tomb of Mubarak Shah?
o: A tower decorated with red sandstone screens
Blue enamelled tiles and guldasta motifs
A marble dome and pietra dura work
A bronze gateway and granite pillars
n21001cb40b9.x: Mubarak Shah’s octagonal tomb is noted for blue enamelled tiles and guldasta motifs.
n21001cb40b9.tq: Distinguish architectural features attached to a specific ruler’s monument.
xs: Mubarak Shah's **octagonal tomb** is noted for **blue enamelled tiles and guldasta motifs** — option **(2)**.
Mubarak Shah was the **second Sayyid** ruler (**1421-34**), after **Khizr Khan**.
xa: Mubarak Shah failed against the **Khokhars**.
**Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi** by **Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi** was written in his reign.
**Sikandar Lodi** built the **Moth ki Masjid** and the royal tombs of the **Lodi Gardens**.

n1802ca6d087.s: The Gaz-i-Sikandari, a yard used to measure land, is associated with:
n1802ca6d087.x: Gaz-i-Sikandari was Sikandar Lodi's land-measuring yard; he also abolished several taxes and used audits and spies.
xa: **Sikandar Lodi** reigned **1489-1517** and founded **Agra (1504)**.
Pen name: **Gulrukhi** (Persian poetry).
Buildings: **Moth ki Masjid** and the royal tombs of the **Lodi Gardens**.

nb60c8cc2fad.s: Which of the following monuments is associated with Sikandar Lodi?
o: Adhai Din ka Jhonpra and Alai Darwaza
Moth ki Masjid and the royal tombs of the Lodi Gardens
nb60c8cc2fad.x: Sikandar Lodi built Moth ki Masjid and royal tombs in the Lodi Gardens.
nb60c8cc2fad.tq: Use the ruler–monument association while rejecting monuments from neighbouring periods.
xs: **Moth ki Masjid** and the royal tombs of the **Lodi Gardens** are linked to **Sikandar Lodi** — option **(3)**.
Sikandar Lodi reigned **1489-1517**, the second Lodi after **Bahlol**.
xa: **Mubarak Shah's** octagonal tomb: **blue enamelled tiles** + **guldasta motifs**.
Sikandar founded **Agra (1504)**.
**Gaz-i-Sikandari** = his yard for measuring land.

n13263c1174e.s: Which Delhi Sultan wrote Persian poetry under the pen name 'Gulrukhi'?
n13263c1174e.x: Sikandar Lodi wrote Persian poetry under the pen name Gulrukhi. Bahlol and Ibrahim Lodi are not known for this, and Firoz Shah's own work was his autobiography Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi.
xs: **Sikandar Lodi** wrote Persian poetry under the pen name **Gulrukhi** — option **(2)**.
**Bahlol** is noted for conquering **Jaunpur**, and **Ibrahim** for his arrogance to the nobles, not for poetry.
xa: Sikandar reigned **1489-1517**.
He had a **Sanskrit medical treatise** translated into **Persian**.
**Gaz-i-Sikandari** = yard to measure land.

n0c4d256e0c5.s: At the First Battle of Panipat, Babur's flanking manoeuvre was called:
n0c4d256e0c5.x: Tulughma was the flanking manoeuvre; Araba carts chained together formed the defensive line.
xa: Field **artillery** and **muskets** were the decisive factor.
Gunners: **Ustad Ali** and **Mustafa**.
Date: **21 April 1526**; older notes say **20 April**.

n33354d230a8.s: Which was the route followed by Timur during his invasion of India?
o: Indus – Punjab, through Multan and Bhatnair – Delhi
n33354d230a8.x: Timur crossed the Indus, passed through Punjab via Multan and Bhatnair, and sacked Delhi in December 1398.
n33354d230a8.tq: Reconstruct the route from the first crossing to the final target.
xs: Timur's route was **Indus – Punjab (through Multan and Bhatnair) – Delhi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He crossed the **Indus**, passed through **Multan** and **Bhatnair** in Punjab, and sacked **Delhi** in **December 1398**.
xa: Effects: Delhi **plundered** and its people **massacred**; the **Tughlaq** state broke up into regional kingdoms (**Jaunpur**, **Malwa**, **Gujarat**).
Timur's nominee **Khizr Khan** later founded the **Sayyid dynasty** (**1414**).
**Babur** descended from **Timur** on his father's side and **Chengiz Khan** on his mother's side.

n60ab8f8b6d3.s: Which of the following was NOT an effect of Timur's invasion of India?
o: Immediate establishment of the Mughal Empire in Delhi
Break-up of the Tughlaq state into regional kingdoms
Later rise of Khizr Khan's Sayyid dynasty
n60ab8f8b6d3.x: The Mughal Empire was established much later, by Babur in 1526.
xa: Timur sacked **Delhi** in **December 1398**, after crossing the **Indus** and passing **Multan** and **Bhatnair**.
Regional kingdoms that emerged: **Jaunpur**, **Malwa**, **Gujarat**.
Khizr Khan founded the **Sayyid dynasty (1414-51)**.

n790751f3cb3.s: Khizr Khan, Timur's viceroy, captured Delhi in:
n790751f3cb3.x: Khizr Khan arrested Daulat Khan Lodi and took Delhi in 1414, ruling as Timur's deputy without the title Sultan.
xa: He founded the **Sayyid dynasty (1414-51)**.
Sayyid order: **Khizr Khan – Mubarak Shah (1421-34) – Muhammad Shah (1434-45) – Alauddin Alam Shah**.
⚠ **Khizr Khan** ruled without the title of Sultan; **Bahlol Lodi** got the throne from **Alam Shah** without a battle.

nef75c914267.s: Bahlol Lodi received the throne of Delhi from:
nef75c914267.x: Bahlol received the throne from Alam Shah, the last Sayyid; Khizr Khan founded the Sayyids.
xa: Bahlol conquered **Jaunpur**.
**Sikandar Lodi** ruled **1489-1517**; **Ibrahim Lodi** **1517-1526**.
Lodi kingship: the king was "**first among equals**" among the Afghan nobles.

n81aa3a3cc8f.s: Daulat Khan Lodi and Alam Khan Lodi are remembered in the context of Babur's invasion because they:
o: commanded Ibrahim Lodi's artillery at Panipat
invited or sought Babur's help against Ibrahim Lodi
founded the Sayyid dynasty after Timur's departure
n81aa3a3cc8f.x: Daulat Khan Lodi, governor of Punjab, and Alam Khan, Ibrahim's uncle, invited or sought Babur's help against Ibrahim Lodi; Rana Sanga too offered to join him, according to Babur. They did not run Ibrahim's guns, Khizr Khan founded the Sayyid dynasty, and Khatauli was Rana Sanga's victory over Ibrahim.
n81aa3a3cc8f.tq: Inviters of Babur: Daulat Khan, Alam Khan, Rana Sanga.
xs: **Daulat Khan Lodi** (Governor of Punjab) and **Alam Khan Lodi** (Ibrahim's uncle) **invited or sought Babur's help** against Ibrahim — option **(2)**.
Babur's gunners were **Ustad Ali** and **Mustafa**; **Khizr Khan** founded the Sayyids; **Khatauli** was **Rana Sanga's** win over Ibrahim.
xa: Babur says **Rana Sanga** also offered to join against Ibrahim.
**Khizr Khan** had arrested **Daulat Khan Lodi** in **1414** — a different, earlier Daulat Khan.
Babur won at **Panipat** on **21 April 1526**.

nbead8a3a745.s: Which military technology was described as the decisive factor in Babur’s victory at the First Battle of Panipat?
nbead8a3a745.x: Babur’s field artillery and muskets were decisive factors in the victory at Panipat.
nbead8a3a745.tq: Identify the decisive technology instead of a general feature of medieval warfare.
xs: Babur's **field artillery and muskets** were the decisive factor at Panipat — option **(3)**.
They let Babur's small army beat a far larger one on **21 April 1526**.
xa: Tactics also included the **Tulughma** flanking manoeuvre and **Araba** carts chained as a defensive line.
Gunners: **Ustad Ali** and **Mustafa**.
Babur (about **12,000**) defeated **Ibrahim Lodi** (about **1,00,000**).

nindian-history-4-12.s: Who established Mughal rule in India?
nindian-history-4-12.x: Babur established Mughal rule after defeating Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526; Sher Shah Suri founded the Sur dynasty.
n: Babur established Mughal rule in India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Babur established the Mughal dynasty in India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Vijayalaya established the Chola Empire. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Vijayalaya established the Chola Empire in the 9th century. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Gopala founded the Pala dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Gopala founded the Pala dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Sher Shah Suri founded the Sur dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Sher Shah Suri founded the Sur dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
xa: Panipat ended the **Delhi Sultanate**; **Ibrahim Lodi** was the last Delhi Sultan.
Babur's gunners: **Ustad Ali Quli** and **Mustafa**.
**21 April 2026** = **500th anniversary** of the battle.

nindian-history-19-6.s: The Battle of Khanwa was fought in:
nindian-history-19-6.x: First Panipat was 1526, Khanwa 1527, Chanderi 1528 and Ghaghra 1529.
n: The 1st Battle of Panipat took place in 1526. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 74-76]
The Battle of Khanwa took place in 1527. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 74-76]
The Battle of Chanderi took place in 1528. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 74-76]
The Battle of Ghaghra took place in 1529. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 74-76]
xa: Khanwa: Babur beat **Rana Sanga** and took the title **Ghazi**.
Chanderi: Babur beat **Medini Rai**.
Ghaghra: Babur beat the **Afghans**, consolidating his position.

nindian-history-21-17.s: Babur defeated Medini Rai in 1528 at the Battle of:
nindian-history-21-17.x: Medini Rai was defeated at Chanderi (1528); Rana Sanga at Khanwa (1527) and the Afghans at Ghaghra (1529).
