Firoz also set up **Diwan-i-Khairat**.

n1338f4bdf49.s: The Sadr-us-Sudur in the Delhi Sultanate was primarily associated with which of the following functions?
n1338f4bdf49.x: The Sadr-us-Sudur supervised religious affairs and endowments; the Chief Sadr was also the Chief Qazi.
n1338f4bdf49.tq: Discriminate between officials whose functions belonged to religion, intelligence and court administration.
xs: The **Sadr-us-Sudur** headed the **Diwan-i-Risalat**: **religious affairs and endowments** — option **(4)**.
News and intelligence = **Barid-i-Mumalik**; despatch of decrees = **Khareetadar**; court decorum and household = **Wakil-i-Dar**.
xa: The Chief Sadr was also the **Chief Qazi**.
Risalat made grants to **mosques and madrasas**.
Older notes call Diwan-i-Risalat the **foreign ministry**; learn the religious-affairs meaning first.

n5ebb6383b9f.s: The wizarat of the Delhi Sultanate reached its heyday under:
n5ebb6383b9f.x: The wizarat's heyday was under Firoz Tughlaq, when Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul ran the government.
xa: **Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul** ran Firoz's government as **wazir**.
**Malik Kafur** was **Naib Malik** of Alauddin.
The Wazir headed the **Diwan-i-Wizarat** (finance and revenue).

n3f48e60f918.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, the Barid-i-Mumalik headed the:
n3f48e60f918.x: The Barid-i-Mumalik headed intelligence; the Qazi-ul-Quzat was Chief Justice and the Wakil-i-Dar ran the court and royal household.
xa: **Amir-i-Hajib** = master of ceremonies.
**Khareetadar** = despatcher of royal decrees.
**Naib** = second only to the Sultan.

n22f811a9c15.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, the despatcher of royal decrees was the:
n22f811a9c15.x: The Khareetadar despatched royal decrees; a Khut was a hereditary rural landholder.
xa: **Alauddin** abolished the **khut's cess**.
**Shiqdar** = in charge of a **shiq** (division/district).
**Muqaddam / Chaudhari** = village headman (**BPSC 2022**).

n7239035f28c.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk Junaidi served Iltutmish, not Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
xa: Malik Kafur was Alauddin's **Naib Malik**.
**Ain-ul-Mulk Multani** conquered **Malwa** in **1305** for Alauddin.
Imad-ul-Mulk headed Balban's **army department**.

ndfeb619c0bc.s: Who destroyed the political influence of the Turkan-i-Chahalgani (the Forty)?
ndfeb619c0bc.x: Iltutmish created the Forty of Turkish slave-nobles; Balban destroyed their power.
xa: The Forty made and unmade Sultans after Iltutmish, including over **Razia**.
⚠ **Iltutmish** created the Forty; **Balban** destroyed it.
After Balban, nobles set aside his nominee **Kai Khusrau** and raised **Kaiqubad**.

neabe99e0cc1.s: Which Delhi Sultan took the titles 'Yamin-ul-Khilafat Nasir-i-Amir-ul-Mominin' without seeking investiture from the Caliph?
neabe99e0cc1.x: Alauddin Khalji took these titles but did not seek investiture. Iltutmish received investiture from the Caliph of Baghdad (c.1229), Mubarak Shah Khalji proclaimed himself Caliph, and Muhammad bin Tughlaq sought investiture from the Caliph in Egypt.
xs: **Alauddin Khalji** took **Yamin-ul-Khilafat Nasir-i-Amir-ul-Mominin** without seeking investiture — option **(2)** (**UPPSC 2023** key).
**Iltutmish** received investiture (**c.1229**); **Mubarak Shah Khalji** proclaimed himself Caliph; **MBT** sought investiture from **Egypt**.
xa: Alauddin put **state interest above the ulema** and law.
His title: **Sikandar-i-Sani**.
He set up **Diwan-i-Mustakhraj** and **Diwan-i-Riyasat**.

n01b00516f47.s: Which of the following offices did NOT exist under the Delhi Sultans?
n01b00516f47.x: Mir Bakshi was a Mughal office; the others belonged to the Sultanate.
xa: Sultanate diwans prefigured the Mughal **Diwan**, **Mir Bakshi** and **Sadr-us-Sudur**.
The Ariz-i-Mumalik's department was set up by **Balban**.

nindian-history-1-20.s: Whose coins showed Goddess Lakshmi on one side and the Kalma in Arabic on the other?
nindian-history-1-20.x: Muhammad Ghori's coins showed Lakshmi with the Kalma; Mahmud's silver coins used Arabic and Devanagari Sanskrit.
n: Mahmud Ghazni issued silver coins with Arabic on one side. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
Mahmud Ghazni's silver coins had Sanskrit on the other side. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
The Sanskrit script on Mahmud Ghazni's coins was Devanagari. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
Muhammad Ghori's coins had Goddess Lakshmi on one side. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
Muhammad Ghori's coins had the Kalma in Arabic on the other side. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
Iltutmish placed the Caliph's name on coins after recognition by the Caliph. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
Alauddin Khalji used the title Sikandar-i-Sani. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
Alauddin Khalji inscribed the title Sikandar-i-Sani on coins. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-17]
xa: Iltutmish got investiture (**mansur**) from the **Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad** in c. **1229**.
**MBT's** coin legend: **"Al Sultan Zilli Allah"**; he sought investiture from the Caliph in **Egypt**.
**Mubarak Shah Khalji** **proclaimed himself Caliph**.
**Balban's** **Garhmukteshwar** inscription calls him **"Helper of a Caliph"**.

n6e0754a62c5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the responsibilities of a muqti?
o: He was exempt from maintaining law and order
He sent the surplus revenue to the central government
n6e0754a62c5.x: A muqti maintained troops, collected revenue, preserved law and order and remitted the surplus to the centre, so he was not exempt from maintaining law and order.
xa: The muqti held an **iqta**, a revenue assignment, **not ownership of land**.
Iqtas were **transferable**; muqtis moved periodically until **Firoz** made them hereditary.
**Alauddin** tightened the **audit** of muqtis.

ndf4c9cec7c3.s: The first iqta grant in India, of Hansi, is credited to:
o: Muhammad Ghori, granted to Qutbuddin Aibak
Alauddin Khalji, granted to Malik Kafur
ndf4c9cec7c3.x: Muhammad Ghori granted Hansi (some sources say Kuhram) to Qutbuddin Aibak, the first iqta. Iltutmish later built the iqta into a system; Balban and Alauddin are not linked with the first grant.
ndf4c9cec7c3.tq: First iqta: Hansi, Ghori to Aibak.
xs: The first iqta, **Hansi**, was granted by **Muhammad Ghori** to **Qutbuddin Aibak** — option **(2)**.
Some notes say **Kuhram** instead of Hansi.
xa: **Iltutmish** later built the iqta into a system (**UPPSC 2010**).
Some notes credit **Aibak** with introducing it.
Iqta = a **Turkish, non-indigenous** institution.

n0cabcc564fa.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, crown land whose revenue supported the court and royal household was called:
n0cabcc564fa.x: Khalisa was crown land; iqta was assigned to officials in place of salary and inam was granted to religious men and institutions.
xa: **UPPSC 2025**: Sultanate territory broadly **Khalisa and Iqta**.
Bahmani khalisa **paid the central army**.
**Alauddin** enlarged the **khalisa**.

ned5e002d5d1.s: Which Sultanate system of revenue assignments financed the army by linking military obligations with the administration of territories?
ned5e002d5d1.x: The iqta system provided the financial basis for maintaining troops while connecting military service with the administration of assigned territories.
xa: The muqti **kept troops** and sent the **fawazil** to the centre.
The iqta is the ancestor of the Mughal **jagir/mansab** system.

nc8a44657002.s: Which Sultan appointed khwajas (auditors) to check the accounts of the muqtis?
nc8a44657002.x: Balban appointed khwajas to audit the muqtis' accounts.
xa: ⚠ **Alauddin** = cash pay; **Firoz** = hereditary iqtas.
**Balban** tried to resume the iqtas of **old soldiers**.

n0a68c2aa535.s: Under which Sultan were iqtas made hereditary?
n0a68c2aa535.x: Iqtas were made hereditary under Firoz Tughlaq; Iltutmish had organised the system and Balban and Alauddin tightened control over it.
xa: **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** (between Alauddin and Firoz) inquired into grants.
**Ghori** made the first iqta grant (**Hansi**) to **Aibak**.
⚠ **Alauddin** = cash pay; **Firoz** = hereditary iqtas.

nfde36d8dc49.s: What was the position of iqtas before the policy of Firoz Tughlaq?
o: They were permanently owned by the muqtis.
They were administered exclusively as khalisa lands.
They were granted only to religious leaders.
They were periodically transferable between muqtis.
nfde36d8dc49.x: Before Firoz Tughlaq made iqtas hereditary, muqtis were transferred periodically from one iqta to another.
nfde36d8dc49.tq: Distinguish a transferable assignment from a hereditary one.
xs: Before Firoz, iqtas were **transferable** and muqtis were **moved periodically** — option **(4)**.
Iqtas were **not ownership of land**; **khalisa** was the separate crown land; grants to religious men were **inam**.
xa: **Firoz Tughlaq** made iqtas **hereditary**.
Iqta = **land revenue** assigned instead of a **cash salary**.
Muqti sent the **fawazil** (surplus) to the treasury.

nb796c694d6e.s: Which Sultan introduced large-scale cash payment to his standing army?
nb796c694d6e.x: Alauddin Khalji paid his standing army in cash, whereas Iltutmish and Balban used iqtas and Firoz Tughlaq returned to assignment-based payment.
xa: Firoz also made iqtas **hereditary**.
Alauddin enlarged the **khalisa** to fund cash pay.

ne60843cb478.s: Who improved the postal system by using runners and horsemen?
ne60843cb478.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughluq improved the postal system by employing both runners and horsemen.
ne60843cb478.tq: Associate a communication reform with the correct Sultan.
xs: **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** improved the post with **runners and horsemen** — option **(1)**.
**Sher Shah** later set up the **dak chowki**.
xa: **Ibn Battuta** described two relays: **ulaq** (horse) and **dawa** (foot).
⚠ **Ulaq** = horse; **dawa** = foot.
Ghiyasuddin also held an **inquiry into grants/jagirs**.

n1edb7decc01.s: Which was the highest rank in the Sultanate military hierarchy?
n1edb7decc01.x: The order from lowest to highest was sar-i-khail, sipah-salar, amir, malik and khan, so khan was the highest.
xa: Ranks followed a **decimal** pattern — a **Turko-Mongol** feature.
Cavalry = **core arm**; also infantry and elephants.

nc63753d50c0.s: Who introduced the branding of horses and the descriptive roll of soldiers in the Delhi Sultanate?
nc63753d50c0.x: Alauddin Khalji introduced dagh, the branding of horses, and huliya, the descriptive roll of each soldier. Sher Shah later revived dagh.
nc63753d50c0.tq: Match paired military controls with the ruler who introduced them.
xs: **Alauddin Khalji** introduced **dagh** (branding of horses) and **huliya** (descriptive roll) — option **(3)**.
**Sher Shah** only **revived** the dagh later.
⚠ "**Balban** introduced the branding of horses" is **false** (**UPSC 2002**).
xa: Purpose: stop **substandard horses** or **proxies** at the muster.
The army was run by the **Ariz-i-Mumalik**.

n7033833af10.s: The primary purpose of dagh and huliya was to
o: Record the revenue of each iqta
Determine the hereditary rights of military officers
Prevent the presentation of substandard horses and substitute soldiers at muster
Classify villages according to agricultural production
n7033833af10.x: Branding horses and maintaining descriptive rolls helped prevent soldiers from bringing inferior horses or sending proxies in their place during inspection.
n7033833af10.tq: Infer the administrative purpose from the control mechanism.
xs: Dagh and huliya stopped **substandard horses** and **proxy soldiers** at the muster — option **(3)**.
**Dagh** = branding of horses; **huliya** = descriptive roll of each soldier.
xa: Introduced by **Alauddin Khalji**; dagh revived by **Sher Shah**.
The **Ariz's department** recruited, inspected and paid the army.

n1c4aa65e395.s: Which of the following military innovations is associated with the Turks in medieval India?
n1c4aa65e395.x: The Turks introduced or strengthened horse-based warfare, mounted archery, the iron stirrup, armour and stronger fortifications.
xa: The **horse** became a key military and economic resource, **imported from West Asia**.
**War elephants** = a royal preserve.

n9ed4e5773e5.s: Alauddin Khalji received daily market reports from
n9ed4e5773e5.x: Alauddin Khalji obtained daily market reports from barids and munhiyans, the latter functioning as secret spies.
n9ed4e5773e5.tq: Match information sources with the ruler who used them.
xs: Alauddin got daily market reports from **barids and munhiyans** (secret spies) — option **(3)**.
**Barids** were news-reporters and intelligence agents under the **barid-i-mumalik**.
xa: **Khwajas** were **Balban's** auditors; **amils** were pargana revenue officers.
Alauddin's **market control** kept the army's cash pay adequate.

nba1f2771032.s: In the Sultanate postal system, the horse post was called:
nba1f2771032.x: The horse post was the ulaq, used even to bring Khorasan fruit to Delhi; dawa was the foot post.
xa: Both relays are from **Ibn Battuta's** account.
⚠ **Ulaq** = horse; **dawa** = foot.
**Sher Shah's dak chowki** = precursor of the modern post.

nindian-history-23-12.s: Sardeshmukhi, a Maratha revenue claim on neighbouring territory, amounted to:
nindian-history-23-12.x: Sardeshmukhi was one-tenth, while chauth was one-fourth; both were the main Maratha revenue claims.
n: Chauth was an important Maratha revenue claim. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Sardeshmukhi was an important Maratha revenue claim. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
xa: **Jizya** = tax on **non-Muslims**; **Zakat** = religious tax on **Muslims**.
**Hundi** = a **credit / bill-of-exchange** instrument.
**Zabt** = a **Mughal land-revenue assessment** system.

nindian-history-23-22.s: Madad-i-Mash revenue-free grants were given to:
nindian-history-23-22.x: Madad-i-Mash grants went to saints, religious institutions and mashaikhs; mansabdars were paid through jagirs or cash.
n: Madad-i-Mash was associated with saints. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Madad-i-Mash was associated with religious institutions. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Madad-i-Mash was associated with mashaikhs. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
xa: **Maal** = land revenue under the **Mughals**.
**Inam** = land granted to religious leaders/institutions.
**Jagir** = revenue assignment to a **Mansabdar or Jagirdar**.

nindian-history-83-15.s: The tanka introduced by Iltutmish was a:
nindian-history-83-15.x: The tanka was a silver coin introduced by Iltutmish; it was a coin, not a tax.
n: Jizya was a tax imposed on non-Muslims. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
Zakat was a religious tax on Muslims. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
Chauth was a Maratha levy generally amounting to one-fourth. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
Tanka was a silver coin introduced by Iltutmish. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
xa: **Sardeshmukhi** = Maratha levy of about **10%**.
**Madad-i-Mash** = revenue-free grant under the Mughals.
**Dagh** = branding of horses in Sultanate military administration.

nindian-history-83-18.s: In medieval Indian administration, the term 'dagh' referred to:
o: Crown land under direct state control
nindian-history-83-18.x: Dagh was the branding of horses; Zabt was the Mughal revenue system, khalisa was crown land and iqta/jagir were revenue assignments.
n: Iqta was a revenue assignment in the Delhi Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
Khalisa was land under direct state control. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
Jagir was a revenue assignment to a Mansabdar or Jagirdar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
Zabt was a Mughal land-revenue assessment system. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
Dagh was the branding of horses in Sultanate military administration. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #83 · pp 165-166]
xa: **Mahrousa** = **protected town/territory** (UPPSC **2023**).
**Shiq** = division of a province under a **shiqdar**.
UPPSC **2025**: Sultanate territory = **Khalisa and Iqta**, not "Khalsa and Jagirs".
**Amaram** = Vijayanagara land to **Amaranayakas**, paying **kappam**.

n65fc0dcb4a3.s: The amaram system of land assignment belonged to which state?
n65fc0dcb4a3.x: Amaram was the Vijayanagara assignment system, comparable to the Sultanate iqta and the Mughal jagir.
xa: The **jagir** also appears in **Bahmani** and **Qutb Shahi** usage.
Bahmanis used **iqta** as a synonym for **jagir**.
**Amaram** holders paid **kappam**.
n65fc0dcb4a3.fixed: UPSC 2000 key pairs Mokasa with Marathas (ycfe68eef657)

ncb7b87e6194.s: The territory of the Delhi Sultanate was broadly divided into:
ncb7b87e6194.x: Sultanate land was broadly khalisa (crown land) and iqta (revenue assignments); the jagir belongs to the Bahmani, Qutb Shahi and Mughal systems.
xa: Khalisa revenue went to the **royal treasury, court and household**.
The **Mughal jagir** was tied to **mansab** rank.

na4fc47a8e62.s: Ushr, the land tax on Muslim-held land in the Delhi Sultanate, was levied at:
na4fc47a8e62.x: Ushr was levied at one-tenth on Muslim-held land; kharaj, paid mainly by non-Muslim cultivators, was usually one-third.
xa: **Zakat** = religious tax of about **2.5%** of wealth, on **Muslims** only.
**Khams** = **one-fifth (1/5)** of war booty (APPSC-G1 **2012**).
**Alauddin and MBT** took **4/5** of booty; **Firoz** restored **1/5**.
⚠ **Kharaj** = non-Muslims' land tax; **Ushr** = Muslims' land tax.

o: The state's one-fifth share of war booty and treasure-troves
A religious tax payable by Muslims
A land tax on non-Muslim cultivators
nc853cd9f628.x: Khams was the state's one-fifth share of booty and treasure-troves; jizya was on non-Muslims and zakat on Muslims.
xa: "Khams = 1/5 of war booty" and "Zakat = tax on Muslims only" are the **standard traps**.
**APPSC-G1 2012** asked khams as the state's share of booty.
**Firoz** extended jizya to **Brahmins**.

nd5612f53acb.s: Which one of the following sets consists only of the four Sharia taxes retained by Firoz Tughlaq?
nd5612f53acb.x: Firoz Tughlaq abolished the many illegal cesses and kept only the four Sharia taxes: kharaj, jizya, zakat and khams. The other sets include non-Sharia items such as ghari, charai, haq-i-sharb (cesses), taccavi (loans) and iqta or inam (land assignments).
nd5612f53acb.tq: Separate the standard Sharia taxes from additional cesses, loans and land assignments.
xs: Firoz kept only the four sharia taxes: **kharaj, jizya, zakat and khams** — option **(3)**.
**Ghari, Charai, Haq-i-sharb** are cesses; **taccavi** is a loan; **iqta** and **inam** are land categories.
xa: Firoz **abolished many illegal cesses**.
He restored the **1/5** khams share.
He extended **jizya** to **Brahmins**.

n4dd250dc68d.s: An iqta in the Sultanate administrative system was:
o: A grant to religious institutions only
Land assigned to officials in place of salary
Crown land reserved for the royal household
n4dd250dc68d.x: An iqta was a land assignment made to officials instead of paying them a direct salary.
n4dd250dc68d.tq: Separate the official land assignment from Khalisa and religious inam grants.
xs: An **iqta** was land **assigned to officials in place of salary** — option **(2)**.
Grants to religious men and institutions were **inam**.
xa: **Maagani** (irrigated) and **Metta** (rain-fed) were **Kakatiya** land types.
Kakatiya land tax = **Ari**.
Nobles **held iqtas**.

n089c9b74b48.s: During the Sultanate period, silk and porcelain were imported from:
n089c9b74b48.x: Silk and porcelain came from China; West Asia supplied textiles, glassware and horses.
xa: India was tied into the **Islamic world economy**.
Caravans used **roads and sarais**.

nfdaf139684f.s: In Sultanate society, the custodians of religious law were the:
nfdaf139684f.x: The ulema were the custodians and interpreters of religious law; khuts and muqaddams collected revenue from peasants.
xa: **Slaves** were traded in slave markets (**Ibn Battuta**).
Hindu society: caste order kept; **sati** and **purdah** spread.

n1c72c22316b.s: In the Kakatiya land classification, 'Maagani' denoted:
n1c72c22316b.x: Kakatiya land was classed as Maagani (irrigated) and Metta (rain-fed).
xa: Kakatiya land tax = **Ari**.
Sultanate **kharaj** was also usually **1/3**, varying from **1/10 to 1/2**.
**Alauddin** raised land revenue to **1/2**.

n26a565c7bd4.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, 'charai' was a:
n26a565c7bd4.x: Charai was a grazing tax; ghari was a house tax and haq-i-sharb an irrigation tax.
xa: Ghari and Charai: **Alauddin Khalji**; Haq-i-sharb: **Firoz Tughlaq**.
Charai was on **milch cattle** (cattle and sheep).
Haq-i-sharb ≈ **1/10** of produce on **canal-watered** land.

n5f70658939c.s: Alauddin Khalji’s enhancement of land revenue resulted in the land tax being raised to approximately:
n5f70658939c.x: Peasants generally paid one-third of the produce as land revenue, but Alauddin Khalji raised the demand to one-half.
n5f70658939c.tq: Compare the normal assessment with the exceptional rate associated with a specific ruler.
xs: **Alauddin** raised land revenue to **one-half (1/2)** of produce — option **(3)**.
Peasants normally paid **one-third (1/3)**, sometimes **one-half**.
xa: Alauddin also introduced **Ghari** (house tax) and **Charai** (grazing tax).
**Sher Shah's** revenue: **1/4 to 1/3** of produce, based on survey.
Alauddin's **price-control** markets show military needs shaping economic policy.

n5704705ccc9.s: Which Sultan introduced Ghari and Charai as additional cesses?
n5704705ccc9.x: Alauddin Khalji introduced Ghari, the house tax, and Charai, the grazing tax on milch cattle.
n5704705ccc9.tq: Use the ruler–measure association rather than confusing the tax with its later reform.
xs: **Alauddin Khalji** introduced **Ghari** (house tax) and **Charai** (grazing tax) — option **(3)**.
**Haq-i-sharb** (irrigation tax) was **Firoz Tughlaq's**.
xa: Charai fell on **milch cattle** (cattle and sheep).
Alauddin raised land revenue to **1/2**.
Other levies: **octroi** and **customs duties**.

nindian-history-38-17.s: Haqq-i-Sharb, the irrigation tax of Firuz Tughlaq, was fixed at:
nindian-history-38-17.x: Firuz Tughlaq's Haqq-i-Sharb was an irrigation tax fixed at 10% of the yield.
n: Firuz Tughlaq imposed Haqq-e-Sharb as an irrigation tax. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 104-105]
Haqq-e-Sharb was 10% of the crop yield. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 104-105]
xa: Firoz built the **most canals**; longest **Yamuna → Hisar**.
⚠ **First** canal-builder = **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq** (UPPSC **2017**); **most** canals = **Firoz**.
**Ghari** = house tax and **Charai** = grazing tax under **Alauddin Khalji**.

n11d7f73b801.s: Which one of the following crops was NOT grown in India during the 13th–14th centuries?
n11d7f73b801.x: Maize was not grown in India during the 13th–14th centuries. It was introduced later by the Portuguese.
n11d7f73b801.tq: Find the crop associated with later European introduction rather than the established medieval crops.
xs: **Maize** was **not grown** in the 13th-14th centuries (**UPPSC 2011**) — option **(3)**.
Maize and **tobacco** came later with the **Portuguese / Europeans**; **gram**, **barley** and **wheat** were grown.
xa: Other crops: **rice**, **sugarcane**, **cotton**, **oilseeds**.
**Ibn Battuta** saw two harvests a year: **rabi** and **kharif**.
Rice was sown **three times** a year.

n25462845c30.s: Which irrigation device was popularised by the Turks in medieval India?
n25462845c30.x: The Turks popularised the Persian wheel, known as saqiya, for irrigation.
n25462845c30.tq: Separate the specific Persian wheel from other irrigation and revenue terms.
xs: The Turks popularised the **Persian wheel (saqiya)** — option **(4)**.
**Araghatta** was an existing water-wheel; **taccavi** was a loan; **Samudrams** were **Kakatiya** tanks.
xa: Paper and the Persian wheel = **lasting gains**.
Other Turkish technologies: **paper-making**, **glass-making**, **spinning wheel**.

nd5066b1bdca.s: Which Tughlaq Sultan built the largest number of canals?
nd5066b1bdca.x: Firoz Tughlaq built the most canals, the longest running from the Yamuna to Hisar; Muhammad bin Tughlaq is known for the Diwan-i-Kohi and taccavi loans.
xa: ⚠ **First** canal-builder of the 14th century = **Ghiyasuddin** (**UPPSC 2017**).

na52e0aee3f4.s: Who is regarded as the first canal-builder of the fourteenth century?

n51d567aafe5.s: Taccavi, also called sondhar, referred to:

**MBT and Firoz** both pushed irrigation and "**superior crops**".

n94c9ba6a60d.s: Which one of the following was NOT founded by Firoz Shah Tughlaq?

**Agra (1504)** = Sikandar Lodi.

n1bf04e947ba.s: Gold dinars became popular under Alauddin Khalji mainly after:

The establishment of the horse-post system

Alauddin raised land revenue to **1/2**.

n0b300846b38.s: Alauddin Khalji's price-control markets primarily demonstrate that:

Military needs could shape economic policy
Agriculture had no connection with state policy
Economic policy was independent of military requirements

xs: Alauddin's **price-control markets** show **military needs shaping economic policy** — option **(2)**.
They kept his army's **cash pay** adequate.
xa: Alauddin got daily market reports from **barids** and **munhiyans**.

nindian-history-12-18.s: Which Muslim ruler issued gold coins bearing the image of goddess Lakshmi?
nindian-history-12-18.x: Muhammad Ghori issued gold coins showing the goddess Lakshmi, copying the earlier Gahadavala type.

Iltutmish introduced the **Tanka** (silver) and **Jital** (copper) — the two basic Sultanate coins.
Tanka = ancestor of the **rupee**.

n: Fatehpur Sikri was associated with Akbar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Fatehpur Sikri had the Buland Darwaza. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Fatehpur Sikri had the Ibadat Khana. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Daulatabad was also known as Devagiri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]

Daulatabad was associated with the transfer of the capital. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Nagarkot was associated with Firuz Tughlaq. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
The Jawalamukhi library had approximately 1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Nagarkot was associated with approximately 1,300 Sanskrit manuscripts from the Jawalamukhi library. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
xa: **Allahabad (Prayagraj)** — **Akbar's fort**.
**Hampi** — the **Vijayanagara Empire**.
**Jahanpanah** was founded by **Muhammad bin Tughlaq**.

n9e5f9292be2.s: Paper-making was particularly significant for the Sultanate administration because it:
n9e5f9292be2.x: The availability of paper strengthened bureaucratic record-keeping in the Sultanate administration.
n9e5f9292be2.tq: Link a technological development to its administrative consequence.
xs: Paper-making **strengthened bureaucratic record-keeping** — option **(2)**.

n9fdbd4a3d4f.s: Khorasan fruit was brought to Delhi by which mode of transport?
n9fdbd4a3d4f.x: Khorasan fruit was brought to Delhi through the horse-post system.

**Banjaras** carried bulk grain on oxen.

neccb72d9fe7.s: Which group carried bulk goods such as grain using oxen in medieval India?
neccb72d9fe7.x: Banjaras carried bulk goods such as grain on oxen; Multanis and Khurasanis handled overseas trade and financing, and Bohras inland trade.
xa: Gujarati merchants included **Hindus, Jains and Muslims**.

Banjaras moved goods over **long distances**.

n5386ce88812.s: Which combination correctly represents crafts that flourished during the Sultanate period?
n5386ce88812.x: Leather work, metal-work and carpet-weaving flourished during the Sultanate period, along with textiles; printing, tea processing and rubber came much later.
xa: Royal **karkhanas** made luxury goods; **Firoz** ran about **36**.
**Sericulture** reduced the need to import raw silk.

nf796fc1ac24.s: Which Delhi Sultan is known to have run about 36 royal karkhanas producing goods for the court?
nf796fc1ac24.x: Royal karkhanas made luxury goods for the court, and Firoz Shah Tughlaq ran about 36 of them. Iltutmish, Alauddin and Sikandar Lodi are not credited with this figure.
xs: **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** ran about **36 royal karkhanas** — option **(3)**.
Karkhanas made **luxury goods** for the court.
xa: Firoz also had a separate **department for slaves**.
Firoz founded **Hisar, Firozabad, Fatehabad, Jaunpur**.

n39c330ab461.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq's token currency (c. 1329-30) failed mainly because of:

MBT also set up the **Diwan-i-Kohi** and gave **taccavi** loans.

na88c6a5e5b7.s: Sher Shah's revenue system served as a model for the later:
na88c6a5e5b7.x: Sher Shah's surveyed revenue system became the model for Todar Mal's bandobast.
na88c6a5e5b7.tq: Match the earlier revenue system with the later administrative adaptation.

Sher Shah took **1/4 to 1/3** of produce, **based on survey**.
The **canal** work was **Ghiyasuddin's** and **Firoz's**; the **karkhanas** were Firoz's; the iqta was organised by **Iltutmish**.
xa: Sultanate peasants paid **1/3**, sometimes **1/2**.
Sher Shah also set up the **dak chowki**.

nindian-history-35-12.s: Sher Shah's Rupiya contained ____ grains of pure silver.
nindian-history-35-12.x: Sher Shah's Rupiya held 173 grains of pure silver; his currency was in pure gold, silver and copper.

The Rupiya contained 173 grains of pure silver. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 101-102]

Exchange ratio **Rupiya : Daam** = **1:64**.
Sher Shah's revenue = **1/4 to 1/3** of produce, a model for **Todar Mal's** bandobast.

nindian-history-35-16.s: Under Sher Shah, one silver Rupiya was equal to how many copper Daams?
nindian-history-35-16.x: One Rupiya of Sher Shah was worth 64 copper Daams, a ratio of 1 : 64.
n: The exchange ratio of the Rupiya to the Daam was 1:64. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 101-102]
xa: Sher Shah's currency: **pure gold, silver and copper**.
**Iltutmish's** **Tanka** = silver, **Jital** = copper.
**Bahloli** coins of **Bahlol Lodi** were **copper**.

n8702d728ff1.s: Before the Delhi Sultanate, which coin was minted at Delhi by the Tomaras and Chauhans?
n8702d728ff1.x: The dehliwal was minted at Delhi before the Sultanate under the Tomaras and Chauhans.

The **tanka** and **jital** came later under **Iltutmish**; **Bahloli** coins were **Bahlol Lodi's**.
xa: Tanka = ancestor of the **rupee**.
Iltutmish's coins were standard **Arabic** coinage.

nc30aa0260d3.s: Which social developments are associated with medieval Hindu society during the Sultanate period?
o: The disappearance of caste distinctions and purdah
The abolition of sati and caste by royal decree
The replacement of caste by iqta administration
The continuation of caste order and the spread of sati and purdah
nc30aa0260d3.x: Hindu society retained its caste order, while sati and purdah spread during this period.
nc30aa0260d3.tq: Identify the option that preserves both social features rather than reversing them.
xs: Hindu society kept its **caste order**, while **sati and purdah spread** — option **(4)**.

xa: **Nobles** held iqtas; **ulema** kept religious law.
**Peasants** bore the revenue burden.

nde851fc77ef.s: According to Amir Khusrau, the wealth and diamonds of Kakatiya Warangal attracted:
nde851fc77ef.x: Amir Khusrau's account of Warangal's diamonds and wealth helps explain why it attracted invasions from Delhi.
nde851fc77ef.tq: Link the reported source observation with its historical consequence.
xs: Warangal's **diamonds and wealth**, noted by **Amir Khusrau**, drew **the Delhi invasions** — option **(1)**.
**Warangal** was the **Kakatiya** capital.
xa: Kakatiya land: **Maagani** (irrigated) vs **Metta** (rain-fed); land tax **Ari**.
Kakatiya **Samudrams** were linked in chains.
**Ibn Battuta** described the **Malabar pepper trade** with **China and Persia**.

n3fec3d6d548.s: In the Sultanate period, the term 'kulah-daran' (wearers of the pointed cap) referred to the:
n3fec3d6d548.x: Kulah-daran were the Sayyids; dastar-bandan (turban-wearers) were the ulema.
xa: ⚠ **Kulah** (cap) = **Sayyids**; **Dastar** (turban) = **Ulema** (UPPSC **2014**).
**Rais, Rana, Rawat** = Hindu chiefs in **Barani's** vocabulary.
**Qalandars** = wandering dervishes.

n774374debcc.s: In Qutb Shahi Golconda, foreign Muslims were known as:
n774374debcc.x: Foreign Muslims in Golconda were the Afaqis; Brahmins received agraharas and Mustajir (tax-farming) rights.

The **Qutb Shahis** were **Shia** and never imposed jizya.

n5b05bc642c4.s: Which one of the following best describes Alauddin Khalji’s attitude towards the ulema in matters of state?
o: He reduced ulema interference and declared that he would act in the state’s interest.
He abolished the office of the Qazi-ul-Quzat.
He ruled strictly according to the ulema’s theocratic interpretation.
He placed all state decisions under the ulema.
n5b05bc642c4.x: Alauddin Khalji reduced the ulema’s interference in state affairs and told Qazi Mughisuddin that he would decree what he considered good for the state.
n5b05bc642c4.tq: Distinguish Alauddin’s state-centred policy from Firoz Tughlaq’s theocratic orientation.
xs: **Alauddin** **reduced ulema interference** and acted in the **state's interest** — option **(1)**.
He told **Qazi Mughisuddin** he decreed whatever he judged **good for the state**, so the state was **not a true theocracy**.
xa: ⚠ **Alauddin** = ulema shut out; **Firoz** = ulema followed.
**MBT** leaned on the **Sufis** against the ulema.

nd502375f435.s: Who among the following was regarded as the first Sultan of Delhi to adopt a benevolent attitude towards Hindus?
nd502375f435.x: Jalaluddin Khalji was regarded as the first Sultan to show a benevolent attitude towards Hindus.

xs: **Jalaluddin Khalji** was the **first Sultan with a benevolent attitude towards Hindus** — option **(4)**.

xa: **Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah (1320)**: Hindu gods worshipped in the royal palace (**UPPSC 2021**).
**MBT** visited the **Ajmer** shrine.

n238506fbccb.s: During whose reign were Hindu gods and goddesses worshipped in the royal palace in 1320?
n238506fbccb.x: Hindu gods and goddesses were worshipped in the royal palace during the reign of Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah in 1320.
n238506fbccb.tq: Link the specific year and court practice to the correct ruler.
xs: In **1320**, under **Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah**, **Hindu gods** were **worshipped in the royal palace** — option **(3)** (**UPPSC 2021**).
**Jalaluddin Khalji** was the first Sultan **benevolent** to Hindus; **Sikandar Lodi** was orthodox.
xa: **MBT** visited the **Ajmer** shrine.
**Iltutmish** gave non-Muslims posts.

n07c026592e0.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, the chief judge was the:

nb8dbb17d755.s: Ziauddin Barani set out his ideal of governance in:

xa: Debate: **theocracy** (Barani) vs a **military state** adjusting to local realities.
**Alauddin** said he decreed whatever he judged good for the state.

nf026be672b8.s: Jizya in the Sultanate was a protection tax on non-Muslims in place of:

xa: **Sikandar Lodi** enforced it.
The **Qutb Shahis** of Golconda **never imposed** jizya.

naf96c1e4bd5.s: Which Sultan followed the counsel of the ulema, ruled on theocratic principles and extended jizya to Brahmins?
naf96c1e4bd5.x: Firoz Tughlaq followed the ulema, adopted theocratic principles, respected the Egyptian Caliph and extended jizya to Brahmins.

He ordered **temples destroyed**.

n2d47ecb7606.s: Which traveller described the practice of sati during the Sultanate period?
n2d47ecb7606.x: Sati was prevalent and documented in the Sultanate period, including in Ibn Battuta's description.
xa: Purdah was brought by **Arabs and Turks**.
**Jauhar** at **Ranthambhor (1301)** and **Chittor (1303)**.

n91ea92281cd.s: Jauhar was performed at which of the following places in the resistance against Alauddin?
n91ea92281cd.x: Jauhar was performed at Ranthambhor in 1301 and Chittor in 1303 during resistance against Alauddin.

xs: Jauhar was performed at **Ranthambhor (1301)** and **Chittor (1303)** against **Alauddin** — option **(4)**.
**Mathura** and **Nagarkot** are linked to **Sikandar Lodi's** temple destruction, not jauhar.
xa: **Sati** was described by **Ibn Battuta**.
**Purdah** spread among the elite.

n28f1a386293.s: Who among the following was the only woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate?

n28f1a386293.tq: Razia (1236-40) = only woman on the Delhi throne.
xs: **Razia Sultana (1236-40)** was the **only woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate** — option **(2)**.

**Purdah** spread among the elite with **child marriage**.

na250d40a769.s: Besides the grain market and the cloth market (Sarai-i-Adl), which other market did Alauddin Khalji regulate?

The market for gold and silver
The market for books and manuscripts

nc5d06fe4c1d.s: The 'Slave' or 'Mamluk' dynasty is so called because which of its rulers had themselves been slaves (bandagan)?

nfa3c18d17d6.s: The Bhakti movement had its indigenous roots in the:

nf679623ed2f.s: Which theory of conversion in medieval India is rejected by current scholarship as a colonial trope?
nf679623ed2f.x: Current scholarship rejects the 'sword' theory as a colonial trope, holding that coercion was isolated; patronage and social liberation are seen as contributing or partial factors.

nd5a01080bee.s: Along with agrarian expansion, Sufi influence was a major factor in conversion especially in:

**Social liberation** was partial: caste-like stratification survived among converts.
Conversion was a **multi-causal**, gradual process.

nb8d063e9dce.s: The Rishi movement of Kashmir was founded by:
nb8d063e9dce.x: Sheikh Nuruddin founded Kashmir's Rishi movement, practised vegetarianism and served all castes.

Breath control entered almost every Sufi order except the **Naqshbandis**.

n18772d9287e.s: Which Sufi order was especially associated with speaking to people in Hindavi?
n18772d9287e.x: Sufis, especially the Chishtis such as Muinuddin, Nizamuddin Auliya and Baba Farid, communicated with people in Hindavi.

n98c0ba26935.s: The Sufi poem Padmavat was written by:

n8259f3c8135.s: The arcuate style introduced by the Turks in India is primarily characterised by the use of:

o: Brick dust used in the mortar

nc9aeac4c361.s: In Indo-Islamic architecture, the 'mihrab' is the:

xa: **Arcuate** style (arch, dome, vault) was brought by the **Turks**; **true arch** held by a **keystone**.

Decoration avoided human/animal figures: **geometric** patterns, **arabesque**, **Quranic calligraphy**.

n9056fdd8b43.s: The decorative vocabulary of the Indo-Islamic style moved away from:
n9056fdd8b43.x: Indo-Islamic decoration moved away from human and animal figures towards geometric patterns, arabesque and Quranic calligraphy.
xa: **Jali** (pierced stone screens) was the other key decorative device.

Two broad styles: **Imperial** (Delhi Sultans) and **Provincial** (regional dynasties).

na2e3cc6a570.s: Which of the following features is associated with Sayyid and Lodi architecture rather than with the principal Tughlaq style?

Hindu-style gateways, plaster ornament and external drip-stones

xs: **Hindu-style gateways, plaster ornament and external drip-stones** belong to the **Sayyid and Lodi** builders — option **(4)**.
Massive plain fort-like buildings, **battered walls**, pointed domes and **false arches** (Syrian/Byzantine) are **Tughlaq** features.
xa: Tughlaq style arose from the **Mongol threat** and finances — the "**crisis period of architecture**".
Lodi (also Sayyid) features: **octagonal tombs** and **double dome**.
Lodi Garden tombs date to the **15th-early 16th c.**

n44c38f289aa.s: Sultan Ghari, the first Indo-Islamic tomb in India, dates to:
n44c38f289aa.x: Sultan Ghari dates to 1231, before Balban's tomb, Alai Darwaza and the octagonal tomb of Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani.
xa: ⚠ **Sultan Garhi – Balban's tomb – Alai Darwaza** = first **tomb – true arch – true dome**.
Sultan Ghari was the tomb of Iltutmish's son **Nasiruddin Mahmud**.
**Octagonal tombs** became a hallmark of the **Lodi** (and Sayyid) style.

na65728f8451.s: The first true dome and the first building based fully on Islamic principles by Indian craftsmen are associated with:
na65728f8451.x: Alai Darwaza is credited with the first true dome and with being the first building based fully on Islamic principles by Indian craftsmen.
na65728f8451.tq: Distinguish the ‘first true dome’ from the separately tested first tomb and first true arch.
xs: The **first true dome** and first building on fully **Islamic principles** by Indian craftsmen = **Alai Darwaza** — option **(3)**.
Built by **Alauddin Khalji** in **1311** as the gateway of the **Quwwat-ul-Islam** mosque, Qutb complex.
**Sultan Ghari** is the first tomb; **Tughlaqabad** is Ghiyasuddin's fort-city; **Atala Masjid** is the Sharqi mosque of Jaunpur.
xa: Khalji hallmark: **horse-shoe arch with lotus-bud (spearhead) fringe**, red sandstone and marble inlay.
⚠ First tomb = **Sultan Garhi**; first true arch = **Balban's tomb**.
Alai Darwaza is part of the **UNESCO** site "Qutb Minar and its Monuments" (inscribed **1993**).

n956159a5d0d.s: The first true arch in India is found in the:
n956159a5d0d.x: Balban's tomb has the first true arch; Alai Darwaza has the first true dome and Sultan Ghari is the first Indo-Islamic tomb.
xa: ⚠ **Sultan Garhi – Balban's tomb – Alai Darwaza** = first **tomb – true arch – true dome**.
Sultan Ghari was the tomb of Iltutmish's son **Nasiruddin Mahmud**.
Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani's tomb dates from **Firoz Tughlaq's** reign.

n93a5e4abde1.s: The tank at Hauz Khas, known as Hauz-i-Alai, was dug by:
n93a5e4abde1.x: Alauddin Khalji excavated the Hauz-i-Alai; Firoz Shah Tughlaq later added the madrasa and tomb.
xa: Alauddin's other works: **Alai Darwaza** (**1311**), **Siri fort**, **Hazar Situm**, **Jamat Khana Masjid**.
Firoz Tughlaq also built **Firoz Shah Kotla** (Firozabad) with the **Topra Ashokan pillar**.

n98112204839.s: The tomb of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq at Tughlaqabad is noted for:
o: A double dome on an octagonal plan
Sloping walls and a marble dome
A horseshoe arch with lotus-bud fringe
n98112204839.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's tomb is noted for its sloping (battered) walls and marble dome.
xa: **Tughlaqabad** fort-city was built by **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** — massive, rugged, built for security.
Tughlaq style is called the "**crisis period of architecture**" (Mongol threat, finances).
Qutb complex holds the **Tomb of Iltutmish**, not the Tughlaq tombs.

n7a712497f16.s: The Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and the Adhai Din ka Jhonpra, both built by Qutbuddin Aibak, are located respectively at:
n7a712497f16.x: Quwwat-ul-Islam stands in the Qutb complex at Delhi and Adhai Din ka Jhonpra at Ajmer; both were built by Aibak. Option A reverses them; Lahore and Badaun are not the sites of these mosques.
n7a712497f16.tq: Quwwat = Qutb complex Delhi; Jhonpra = Ajmer.
xs: **Quwwat-ul-Islam** is at **Delhi** and **Adhai Din ka Jhonpra** at **Ajmer** — option **(2) Delhi and Ajmer**.
Option (1) reverses the two; both were built by **Qutbuddin Aibak**.
xa: Quwwat-ul-Islam reused **temple pillars** and stands in the **Qutb complex** (APPSC-G1 2024).
Adhai Din ka Jhonpra is the "mosque at Ajmer" of the imperial style (JPSC 2021).
The **Iron Pillar** (Gupta era) stands in the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque court.

ne462eae1842.s: Which of the following is part of the 'Qutb Minar and its Monuments, Delhi' World Heritage Site?
ne462eae1842.x: The site includes the Qutb Minar, Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, Alai Darwaza, Iron Pillar, Iltutmish's tomb, Alauddin's tomb and madrasa, and Imam Zamin's tomb; Tughlaqabad Fort is separate.
xa: The site was inscribed by UNESCO in **1993**.
**Iron Pillar**: Gupta era (king "Chandra" = **Chandragupta II**), famous for resisting rust.

n0a428b77b09.s: The Iron Pillar standing in the courtyard of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque belongs broadly to which period?
n0a428b77b09.x: The Iron Pillar is a Gupta-era pillar. Its king Chandra is generally identified with Chandragupta II, and it is famous for its resistance to rust.
n0a428b77b09.tq: Identify the period from the associated ruler and distinctive material feature.
xs: The **Iron Pillar** belongs to the **Gupta period** (Gupta-era) — option **(3)**.
Its king "**Chandra**" is identified with **Chandragupta II**.
xa: It is famous for **resisting rust**.
It stands in the **Quwwat-ul-Islam** mosque court, part of the **UNESCO** Qutb site (**1993**).
⚠ The **Topra Ashokan pillar** is a different pillar, at **Firoz Shah Kotla**.

nadc9e3e9a1b.s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of monuments associated with Bengal architecture?
o: Mahmud Gawan Madrasa, Bidar Fort and Ashtur tombs
Atala Masjid, Chand Minar and Gol Gumbaz
Charminar, Adina Mosque and Jami Masjid of Mandu
Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid
nadc9e3e9a1b.x: The Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid are all Bengal monuments. Option A is Bahmani (Bidar), B mixes Jaunpur, Daulatabad and Bijapur, and C mixes Hyderabad, Bengal and Mandu (Malwa).
nadc9e3e9a1b.tq: Identify the complete regional cluster rather than matching only one monument.
xs: **Eklakhi tomb, Dakhil Darwaza and Chota Sona Masjid** are all **Bengal** monuments — option **(4)**.
Option (1) is **Bahmani** (Bidar); (2) mixes **Jaunpur**, Daulatabad and **Bijapur**; (3) mixes **Hyderabad**, Bengal and **Mandu**.
xa: Bengal style: **brick** building, **curved roofs**.
**Adina Mosque** and the **Pandua** mosques are the earliest Bengal examples.

nindian-history-74-18.s: The Lal Darwaza Mosque is an example of which architectural style?
nindian-history-74-18.x: Lal Darwaza is a Sharqi mosque; Moth ki Masjid is Lodi.
n: The Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque was the first major mosque of the Delhi Sultanate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #74 · pp 152-153]
The Adhai Din Ka Jhopra is an early Sultanate mosque. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #74 · pp 152-153]
The Moth Ki Masjid represents Lodi architecture. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #74 · pp 152-153]
The Lal Darwaza Mosque represents Sharqi architecture. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #74 · pp 152-153]
xa: ⚠ Pair asked: Quwwat-ul-Islam and Adhai Din ka Jhonpra = **Delhi and Ajmer**.
Jaunpur (**Sharqi**) style: massive **propylon** screen before the prayer hall, no minarets.
**Lodis** pioneered the **double dome** on tombs.

n016727c6571.s: The city of Jahanpanah was built by:
n016727c6571.x: Jahanpanah and a fortress at Allahabad are associated with Muhammad bin Tughlaq; Siri Fort is Alauddin's and Firoz Shah Kotla is Firoz's.
xa: **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq** built the **Tughlaqabad** fort-city — massive, rugged, built for security.
Tughlaq style: **sloping (battered) walls**, pointed domes, false arches.

n16c77bd7ea4.s: How many tapering storeys does the Qutb Minar have?
n16c77bd7ea4.x: The Qutb Minar has five tapering storeys, is about 72.5 metres high and bears bands of Quranic calligraphy.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "Qutb Minar is 180 ft high" is **false** (CGPSC 2023) — actually about **238 ft**.
Some notes give **73 m**.
Dedicated to Sufi saint **Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki**.

nbdcd878216c.s: Why does the present Qutb Minar have five storeys although its upper portion was altered?
o: Iltutmish added two storeys after completing the entire monument.
Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the lightning-damaged top storey with two storeys.
Alauddin Khalji added two marble storeys to the original tower.
Sikandar Lodi added two storeys after rebuilding the monument.
nbdcd878216c.x: Lightning damaged the upper portion of the Qutb Minar. Firoz Shah Tughlaq replaced the damaged top storey with two storeys made of marble and sandstone.
nbdcd878216c.tq: Follow the cause-and-repair sequence rather than associating every addition with the original builder.
xs: **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** replaced the **lightning-damaged top storey** with **two storeys** — option **(2)**; hence **five storeys** today.
The new storeys were in **marble and sandstone**.
**Iltutmish** built storeys 2nd-4th and completed it; **Sikandar Lodi** only **repaired** it.
xa: ⚠ **Aibak** began (first storey) – **Iltutmish** completed – **Firoz Tughlaq** rebuilt the top.
Height about **72.5 m** (some notes **73 m**).

nffd781096d0.s: The Qutb Minar is dedicated to:
nffd781096d0.x: It is dedicated to the Sufi saint Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki; Aibak built only the first storey and Iltutmish completed it.
xa: **Firoz Tughlaq** replaced the lightning-damaged top with two storeys → **five storeys** today.
**Sikandar Lodi** also repaired it.

n38c5f867f18.s: The Chand Minar at Daulatabad was built in 1435 by:
o: Alauddin Ahmad Shah of the Bahmani dynasty
n38c5f867f18.x: The Chand Minar at Daulatabad was built in 1435 by the Bahmani Sultan Alauddin Ahmad Shah.
n38c5f867f18.tq: Match the monument with its correct builder and date while rejecting nearby Sultanate rulers.
xs: The **Chand Minar**, Daulatabad, was built in **1435** by Bahmani Sultan **Alauddin Ahmad Shah** — option **(2)**.
It dates to the **15th century** (statement correct, CGPSC 2023).
**Mahmud Gawan** is linked to his **madrasa at Bidar**, not the Chand Minar.
xa: Bahmani works: **Gulbarga Jama Masjid** (fully covered courtyard), **Bidar Fort** (Gagan Mahal), **Ashtur** tombs.
**Firoz Shah Bahmani's** tomb has a **Sanskrit inscription**.

nb2c06a5d08a.s: A massive propylon screen in front of the prayer hall and the absence of minarets, as seen in the Atala Masjid, characterise the provincial style of:
nb2c06a5d08a.x: The Sharqi style of Jaunpur is marked by massive gateway facades with a propylon screen and no minarets, as in the Atala Masjid. Bengal used brick and curved roofs, Malwa is known for the Jami Masjid at Mandu, and Gujarat for strong Hindu-Jain carving.
nb2c06a5d08a.tq: Propylon + no minarets = Jaunpur's Atala Masjid.
xs: A massive **propylon** screen and **no minarets**, as in the **Atala Masjid**, mark **Jaunpur (Sharqi)** — option **(3)**.
**Bengal** used brick and curved roofs; **Malwa** = Jami Masjid, Mandu; **Gujarat** = strong Hindu-Jain carving.
xa: ⚠ **Atala Masjid** = Jaunpur; **Adina Mosque** = Pandua (Bengal).
Jaunpur's style is known for **massive gateway facades**.

n97b5a1bebb0.s: The horseshoe arch with a lotus-bud fringe is a feature of which architecture?
n97b5a1bebb0.x: The lotus-bud horseshoe arch is Khalji; battered walls are Tughlaq, octagonal tombs and double domes Lodi, and the propylon screen Sharqi.
xa: **Sayyid and Lodi** revived Hindu elements: Hindu-style gateways, **plaster ornament**, external **drip-stones**.
Tughlaq period = "**crisis period of architecture**", due to the **Mongol threat** and finances.
Lodi examples: **Sikandar Lodi's tomb**, **Bara Gumbad**, **Shisha Gumbad** (Lodi Garden).

n68baeb6e978.s: The domes and false arches of Tughlaq architecture show the influence of:
n68baeb6e978.x: Tughlaq domes and false arches show Syrian and Byzantine influence.
xa: The Tughlaq period is called the "**crisis period of architecture**".
Examples: **Tughlaqabad** fort-city and **Ghiyasuddin's tomb** (battered walls, **marble dome**).
First **octagonal** tomb (Khan-i-Jahan Tilangani's) also dates from the **Tughlaq** period.

nd456c29be88.s: The Charminar is traditionally associated with which event?
o: The completion of the Golconda Fort water system
The founding of the Bahmani kingdom
nd456c29be88.x: The Charminar was built to mark the end of a plague. It has four arches and four minarets and combines Persian arches with Deccani stucco.
nd456c29be88.tq: Link the monument with its commemorative purpose rather than with a general architectural feature.
xs: The **Charminar** was built to mark the **end of a plague** — option **(3)**.
It has **four arches + four minarets** and blends **Persian arches with Deccani stucco**.
xa: Dates differ: some notes say **1591-92**, others **1594**.
Its design is said to be inspired by the minarets of **Sultan Quli's Juma Masjid**, Golconda.
**Hyderabad** was founded in **1591**, planned on **Isfahan** by **Mir Momin Astarabadi**.

n10dc76c6f63.s: Hyderabad was planned on the model of Isfahan by:
n10dc76c6f63.x: Mir Momin Astarabadi planned Hyderabad on the model of Isfahan.
xa: Charminar marked the **end of a plague**.
Capital moved from **Golconda** to Hyderabad in **1592**.

n02608dc7298.s: Which of the following features is associated with Golconda Fort?
o: A fully covered courtyard and a Persian madrasa
An acoustic system and piped water supply
Curved brick roofs and a Bengal-style mosque plan
n02608dc7298.x: Golconda Fort is known for its remarkable acoustics and its provision of piped water.
n02608dc7298.tq: Identify the monument through its unusual functional features rather than its dynasty alone.
xs: **Golconda Fort** is known for its **acoustics** and **piped water** — option **(2)**.
A handclap at the gate is heard at **Bala Hisar**, nearly **1 km** away.
Covered courtyard = **Gulbarga**; curved brick roofs = **Bengal**; propylon = **Jaunpur**.
xa: **Qutb Shahi Tombs** at **Ibrahim Bagh** hold the **seven** rulers.
Golconda Jami Masjid gateway has fine **Nastaliq** calligraphy.

nde4038648a0.s: The Qutb Shahi Tombs at Ibrahim Bagh are notable because they:
o: Have no domes and are decorated only with pierced stone screens
Contain the tombs of seven Bahmani rulers and have octagonal domes on circular bases
Were built entirely in the Bengal brick tradition
Contain the tombs of seven Qutb Shahi rulers and have onion domes on square bases
nde4038648a0.x: The Qutb Shahi Tombs at Ibrahim Bagh contain the seven rulers of the dynasty and are characterised by onion domes resting on square bases.
nde4038648a0.tq: Combine the number of rulers with the distinctive tomb form to identify the correct description.
xs: The **Qutb Shahi Tombs** at **Ibrahim Bagh** hold the **seven** rulers and have **onion domes on square bases** — option **(4)**.
They are **Qutb Shahi**, not **Bahmani**, and their domes are not octagonal on circular bases.
xa: Qutb Shahi architecture = **Indo-Saracenic** blend of Persian and Hindu traditions (AP angle).
**Golconda Fort**: acoustics, handclap heard at **Bala Hisar**.

ne67715cf8c1.s: In which year was Hyderabad founded?
ne67715cf8c1.x: Hyderabad was founded in 1591, and the capital moved there from Golconda in 1592.
xa: The city plan was modelled on **Isfahan** by **Mir Momin Astarabadi**.
**Charminar** marked the **end of a plague**.

n027a49a6847.s: Qutb Shahi architecture is best described as which of the following?
o: An Indo-Saracenic blend of Persian and Hindu traditions
A Buddhist-Greek style centred on stupas
A purely Persian style without Indian elements
n027a49a6847.x: Qutb Shahi architecture combined Persian and Hindu traditions and is described as an Indo-Saracenic blend.
n027a49a6847.tq: Distinguish a blended architectural tradition from styles described as purely belonging to one cultural stream.
xs: Qutb Shahi architecture is an **Indo-Saracenic blend of Persian and Hindu traditions** — option **(1)**.
So it is neither **purely Persian** nor a Dravidian or Buddhist style.
**Charminar** shows the blend: **Persian arches with Deccani stucco**.
xa: **Qutb Shahi Tombs** at **Ibrahim Bagh** hold the **seven** rulers, with **onion domes on square bases**.
**Hyderabad** (founded **1591**) was planned on **Isfahan** by **Mir Momin Astarabadi**.
⚠ Golconda Jami Masjid: **Nastaliq** on the gateway, **Naskh** around the mihrab.

n83fd14b3889.s: The gateway of the Golconda Jami Masjid is noted for fine calligraphy in:
n83fd14b3889.x: The gateway has fine Nastaliq calligraphy (Yazdani); Naskh is used for the Quranic verses around the mihrab.
xa: ⚠ **Nastaliq** = gateway calligraphy; **Naskh** = Quranic verses around the mihrab.
**Golconda Fort** is known for **acoustics** — a handclap at the gate is heard at **Bala Hisar**, nearly **1 km** away.
**Qutb Shahi Tombs** at **Ibrahim Bagh** hold the **seven** rulers, with **onion domes on square bases**.

n1f5b2219b81.s: Which group of writers is specifically associated with accounts of the fall of Warangal in 1323?
o: Kumara Kampana, Gona Budda Reddy and Kase Siddhappa
n1f5b2219b81.x: Isami, Barani and Ferishta describe the fall of Warangal in 1323.
n1f5b2219b81.tq: Use the event–chronicler association to reject writers from unrelated literary traditions.
xs: The **fall of Warangal (1323)** is described by **Isami, Barani and Ferishta** — option **(4)**.
The other groups are Telugu or Kannada poets (Tikkana, Errana, Srinatha, Kumara Kampana).
xa: Ferishta calls Telangana "**Tilang**".
**Isami's Futuh-us-Salatin** covers the Tughlaq army's victories over Warangal.
**Kumara Ramana Charitam** describes the south after the conquest of Warangal.

n3bdf9ab71bb.s: Amir Khusrau was given the title Tuti-i-Hind (Parrot of India) by:
n3bdf9ab71bb.x: His patron Alauddin Khalji called him Tuti-i-Hind.
xa: He served about **seven Sultans**, from **Balban's** time to Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.
⚠ **Tutinama** (Nakhshabi) ≠ **Tuti-i-Hind** (Khusrau's title).
He founded **Sabaq-i-Hindi**, the Indian style of Persian poetry.

n8fcd09a5f06.s: Amir Khusrau wrote riddles and poetry in ____, which later developed into Rekhta or Urdu.
n8fcd09a5f06.x: Khusrau wrote riddles and poetry in Hindavi, which later developed into Rekhta or Urdu.
xa: Hindavi grew into **Urdu** in **camps and bazaars**.
He founded **Sabaq-i-Hindi**, the Indian style of Persian poetry.
Title **Tuti-i-Hind** (Parrot of India), from **Alauddin Khalji**.

n9a611f483ea.s: Amir Khusrau is associated with the development of which style of Persian poetry?
n9a611f483ea.x: Amir Khusrau is credited with founding the Indian style of Persian poetry known as Sabak-i-Hindi or the Hindustani style.
n9a611f483ea.tq: Match the exact technical term rather than a geographically similar distractor.
xs: Amir Khusrau founded **Sabak-i-Hindi**, the Indian style of Persian poetry — option **(4)**.
Also spelt **Sabaq-i-Hindi**.
xa: He pioneered **Hindavi-Urdu** poetry (riddles + verse in Hindavi).
Disciple of **Nizamuddin Auliya** (Chishti).
**Poet laureate** under **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq**.

n209f9ff86cc.s: The earliest Persian treatise on Indian music (1375) is:
n209f9ff86cc.x: The Ghunyat-ul-Munya (1375) is the earliest Persian treatise on Indian music; it is not Amir Khusrau's work.
xa: Ragas credited to him: **Aiman (Yaman)**, **Zilaf**, **Sazgiri**.
Tradition also credits him with **qawwali**.

nindian-history-45-10.s: Amir Khusrau was given which of the following titles?
nindian-history-45-10.x: Amir Khusrau was called Tuti-i-Hind, the Parrot of India. Homer of the East refers to Firdausi, Andhra Bhoja to Krishnadevaraya and Kaviraja to Samudragupta.
nindian-history-45-10.tq: Link each literary title with its bearer.
n: Amir Khusrau was known as Tuti-i-Hind. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Firdausi was known as the Homer of the East. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Unsuri was a Persian poet. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Uzari was a Persian poet. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Hastimalla was associated with the Hoysala rulers. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Hastimalla was a Kannada poet. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Hastimalla was a Kannada playwright. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
xs: **Amir Khusrau** was called **Tuti-i-Hind** (Parrot of India) — so option **(3)** is correct.
The title was given by his patron **Alauddin Khalji**.
xa: He became **poet laureate** under **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq**.
He was a **disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya** (Chishti).
⚠ **Tutinama** (**Nakhshabi**) ≠ **Tuti-i-Hind**.
He founded **Sabaq-i-Hindi**, the Indian style of Persian poetry.

nindian-history-46-10.s: Which of the following was written by Amir Khusrau?
nindian-history-46-10.x: Tughluq Nama is by Amir Khusrau. Tarikh-i-Subuktigin is Baihaqi's, Shahnama is Firdausi's and Mitakshara is Vijnaneshvara's.
nindian-history-46-10.tq: Link each work to its author.
n: Amir Khusrau wrote Tughluq Nama. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
Firdausi wrote Shahnama. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
Baihaqi wrote Tarikh-i-Subuktigin. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
Vigyaneshvara wrote Mitakshara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
Amir Khusrau wrote Ashika. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
Amir Khusrau wrote Nuh Sipihr. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
xs: **Tughluq Nama** was written by **Amir Khusrau** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is a **Persian historical work** on the rise of **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq**.
xa: ⚠ "**Tughluqnama - Ibn Battuta**" is the **wrong** pair (UPPSC **2019**).
**Ibn Battuta** wrote the **Rihla** (Arabic).
Khusrau's ragas: **Aiman (Yaman), Zilaf, Sazgiri**.

nc69af076b8b.s: Which one of the following works of Amir Khusrau deals with the conquests of Alauddin Khalji, including those in the Deccan?
nc69af076b8b.x: Khazain-ul-Futuh describes the conquests of Alauddin Khalji, including his Deccan campaigns.
nc69af076b8b.tq: Match the work with its subject, not merely with its author.
xs: **Khazain-ul-Futuh** describes **Alauddin's conquests**, including the **Deccan** — option **(2)**.
**Miftah-ul-Futuh** = **Jalaluddin Khalji's** campaigns; **Qiran-us-Sadain** = meeting of **Bughra Khan** and **Kaiqubad**.
**Tughluqnama** = rise of **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq**.
xa: ⚠ **Miftah** = Jalaluddin; **Khazain** = Alauddin; **Nuh Sipihr** = Mubarak Shah.
Khazain-ul-Futuh was asked in **UKPSC 2021**.
Khazain-ul-Futuh and Nuh Sipihr are **separate** works.

o: The meeting of Bughra Khan and his son Kaiqubad
n8832e8cd67c.x: Qiran-us-Sadain describes the meeting of Bughra Khan and Kaiqubad; Miftah-ul-Futuh covers Jalaluddin's campaigns and Nuh Sipihr Mubarak Shah's reign.
xa: Nuh Sipihr also **praises India and its languages**.
**Khazain-ul-Futuh** = Alauddin's conquests incl. the Deccan.
All four main works are Khusrau's (**UKPSC 2025**).

n5311c85a355.s: The work Ashiqa, also known as Deval Rani–Khizr Khan, deals with
o: The meeting of Bughra Khan and Kaiqubad
The romance involving Alauddin Khalji’s son
n5311c85a355.x: Ashiqa, or Deval Rani–Khizr Khan, deals with the romance involving Alauddin Khalji’s son.
n5311c85a355.tq: Use the alternative title to identify the work’s narrative subject.
xs: **Ashiqa** (Deval Rani-Khizr Khan) is the **romance of Alauddin Khalji's son** — option **(2)**.
Bughra Khan–Kaiqubad = **Qiran-us-Sadain**; Jalaluddin's campaigns = **Miftah-ul-Futuh**; Ghiyasuddin's rise = **Tughluqnama**.
xa: Ashiqa was asked in **UPPSC 2019**.
**Khazain-ul-Futuh** covers Alauddin's own conquests.
**Nuh Sipihr** = Mubarak Shah's reign.

nindian-history-45-9.s: The Tughluq Nama was written by:
nindian-history-45-9.x: Tughluq Nama, like Miftah-ul-Futuh and Ashika, is Amir Khusrau's work; Firdausi wrote the Shahnama.
n: Amir Khusrau wrote Miftah-ul-Futuh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Amir Khusrau wrote Ashika. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Amir Khusrau wrote Tughluq Nama. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
Firdausi wrote Shahnama. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 112-113]
xa: His other works: **Khazain-ul-Futuh**, **Nuh Sipihr**, **Qiran-us-Sadain**.
⚠ **Miftah** = Jalaluddin; **Khazain** = Alauddin; **Nuh Sipihr** = Mubarak Shah.
⚠ "**Tughluqnama - Ibn Battuta**" is the wrong pair (UPPSC **2019**).

na7fcfe11b88.s: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and Fatawa-i-Jahandari were written by:
na7fcfe11b88.x: Ziauddin Barani, a nadim of Muhammad bin Tughlaq who wrote under Firoz Tughlaq, wrote both works.
xa: His view: the Sultan protects the sharia but rules through **zawabit** → state not truly Islamic (UPSC 2002).
He wanted office for the **high-born** and opposed promoting low-born men.
⚠ **Shams Siraj Afif** wrote a work with the same title, Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

ne4b8f40c16e.s: According to Ziauddin Barani, kingship (jahandari) followed the ____ model, resting on awe and force.
ne4b8f40c16e.x: Barani held that jahandari followed the Persian model; he also wanted high office kept for the high-born.
xa: Sultan protects the sharia but rules through **zawabit** (state laws) → state not truly Islamic (UPSC 2002).
Barani was a **nadim** of **MBT** and wrote under **Firoz Tughlaq**.
His political theory is set out in **Fatawa-i-Jahandari**.

nb1a15992c56.s: The state laws through which the Delhi Sultans governed in practice, leading Barani to deny the state was truly Islamic, were called:
nb1a15992c56.x: The Sultan was expected to protect the sharia but governed through zawabit (state laws), so Barani did not regard the state as truly Islamic.
xa: His kingship (**jahandari**) followed the **Persian model**, resting on awe and force.
He opposed promoting **low-born** men to office.
Works: **Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi** and **Fatawa-i-Jahandari**.

n98e8e160b70.s: Which ruler is associated with the Persian translation of the Mahabharata and Rajatarangini?
n98e8e160b70.x: Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir is associated with translating the Mahabharata and Rajatarangini into Persian.
n98e8e160b70.tq: Identify the patron from the translated Sanskrit works rather than from the translator’s name.
xs: **Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir** had the **Mahabharata** and **Rajatarangini** translated into Persian — option **(3)**.
**Firoz Tughlaq** is linked to **Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi**; **MBT's** time to the **Tutinama**; **Man Singh Tomar** to Man Kautuhal.
xa: Later Mughal translation: **Razmnama** = Mahabharata.
**Kalila wa Dimna** = Persian version of the **Panchatantra**.

nfa3a25344a3.s: The music treatise Man Kautuhal is associated with:
o: Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior
nfa3a25344a3.x: Man Kautuhal is associated with Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior; Rag Vibodh is by Somnath.
xa: ⚠ Don't swap them: Man Kautuhal is Man Singh's, Rag Vibodh is Somnath's.
**Amir Khusrau** credited with ragas **Aiman, Zilaf, Sazgiri**.

n5b3ff892806.s: Who translated the Sanskrit Suka Saptati into Persian as the Tutinama?
n5b3ff892806.x: Ziya-uddin Nakhshabi made the Tutinama from the Suka Saptati in Muhammad bin Tughlaq's time (UPPSC 2022). Amir Hasan Sijzi compiled Fawaid-ul-Fuad, Shay Akbar translated Sringaramanjari into Sanskrit, and Barani was a historian.
n5b3ff892806.tq: Tuti Nama - Nakhshabi (both sound like 'N' for Nakhshabi's parrot tales).
xs: **Ziya-uddin Nakhshabi** made the **Tutinama** from Suka Saptati — option **(2)** (UPPSC 2022).
**Amir Hasan Sijzi** compiled **Fawaid-ul-Fuad**; **Shay Akbar** translated Sringaramanjari into Sanskrit; **Barani** was a historian.
xa: It dates to **Muhammad bin Tughlaq's** time.
⚠ **Tutinama** ≠ **Tuti-i-Hind** (Amir Khusrau's title).

nec35280b85d.s: Who wrote Chandayan, the Awadhi premakhyan composed in 1379?
nec35280b85d.x: Chandayan, an Awadhi premakhyan composed in 1379, was written by Mulla Daud.
nec35280b85d.tq: Use the distinctive date and language to identify the author among premakhyan poets.
xs: **Chandayan** (Awadhi, **1379**) is by **Mulla Daud** — option **(1)** (UPPSC 2019).
**Padmavat** is by **Jayasi**, **Padmavati Katha** by **Damodar Kavi**, **Mrigavati** by **Qutban**.
xa: ⚠ **Padmavat** = Jayasi; **Padmavati Katha** = Damodar Kavi.
**Ghulam Ali**, court poet of **Tana Shah**, translated Padmavat into Urdu.

n6d1f999db90.x: Fawaid-ul-Fuad is by Amir Hasan Sijzi; Qutban wrote Mrigavati.
xa: Fawaid-ul-Fuad = conversations (**malfuzat**) of **Nizamuddin Auliya**.
**Chandayan** (**1379**) is by **Mulla Daud**.
Padmavat is dated **1540**; one source says **15th century**.

n16224e69124.x: Kasi Khandam is Srinatha's work; Errana completed the Aranya Parva and Tikkana rendered 15 parvas of the Mahabharata.
xa: Errana's patron: **Prolaya Vema** (Reddi); Srinatha's: **Pedakomati Vema**.
**Marana** — **Markandeya Puranam** (Kakatiya era).
**Gona Budda Reddy** — **Ranganatha Ramayanam**.

n435cbb6970f.x: Ranganatha Ramayanam is by Gona Budda Reddy; Palkuriki Somanatha wrote the Basava Puranam.
xa: **Kumara Ramana Charitam** (Kannada) describes the south after the fall of **Warangal**.
**Tikkana** — **Nirvachanottara Ramayanam**.
**Addanki Gangadhara** dedicated a Telugu work to **Ibrahim Qutb Shah**.

n844c442feb5.s: Which Sufi order popularised sama and institutionalised qawwali in its khanqahs?
n844c442feb5.x: The Chishtis popularised sama, and qawwali was institutionalised in Chishti khanqahs using Indian ragas.
n844c442feb5.tq: Match the musical practice with the Sufi order most closely associated with it.
xs: The **Chishtis** popularised **sama** and institutionalised **qawwali** in their khanqahs — option **(4)**.
Qawwali in Chishti khanqahs used **Indian ragas**.
xa: **Sama** = devotional music to induce **ecstasy**; a core Sufi practice.
**Amir Khusrau**, disciple of Chishti **Nizamuddin Auliya**, is credited by tradition with qawwali.
Persian contributions listed in **PT365**: sitar, santur, **qawwali**, ghazal.

nf73d81bec4b.s: In the Qutb Shahi kingdom, the language used among the people and in revenue records was:
nf73d81bec4b.x: Telugu was used among the people and in revenue records; Persian was used at court and Dakhni Urdu in camps and bazaars.
xa: **Abdullah Qutb Shah** and **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** first issued farmans in **Telugu**.
Golconda was a Persian literary centre under **Mir Momin Astarabadi**.
**Addanki Gangadhara** dedicated a Telugu work to **Ibrahim Qutb Shah**.

nd931597729b.s: Which Qutb Shahi rulers first issued farmans in Telugu?
o: Abdullah Qutb Shah and Abul Hasan Tana Shah
Ibrahim Qutb Shah and Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah
Abul Hasan Tana Shah and Kumara Kampana
Mir Momin Astarabadi and Abdullah Qutb Shah
nd931597729b.x: Abdullah Qutb Shah and Abul Hasan Tana Shah are identified as the first Qutb Shahi rulers to issue farmans in Telugu.
nd931597729b.tq: Distinguish the rulers linked with Telugu administrative usage from other Qutb Shahi figures.
xs: **Abdullah Qutb Shah and Abul Hasan Tana Shah** first issued farmans in **Telugu** — option **(1)**.
**Mir Momin Astarabadi** was not a ruler; **Kumara Kampana** was not Qutb Shahi.
xa: **Ghulam Ali**, court poet of **Tana Shah**, translated Padmavat into Urdu.
**Addanki Gangadhara** dedicated a Telugu work to **Ibrahim Qutb Shah**.
**Telugu** was the language of the people and revenue records.

n958b2ec389b.s: Which ruler unified Bengal in 1342 and made Pandua his capital?
n958b2ec389b.x: Haji Ilyas, who assumed the title Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah, unified Bengal in 1342 and established Pandua as his capital.
n958b2ec389b.tq: Distinguish the unifier of Bengal from the rulers connected with its monuments and later dynasty.
xs: **Haji Ilyas (Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah)** unified Bengal in **1342** with **Pandua** as capital — option **(1)**.
He founded the **Ilyas Shahi** line; **Alauddin Hussain Shah** founded the later **Hussain Shahi** line.
**Sikandar Shah** built the **Adina Mosque**; **Jalaluddin Muhammad Shah** lies in the **Eklakhi Tomb**.
xa: ⚠ **1342** Bengal (Ilyas) – **1347** Bahmani – **1394** Sharqi – **1401** Malwa – **1407** Gujarat.
Akbar annexed **Bengal** in **1576**.
Bengal chronicle: **Riyaz-us-Salatin**.

n0ee447af477.s: Besides the Doab, which of the following was a disputed zone in the Bahmani-Vijayanagara conflicts?
n0ee447af477.x: The Krishna-Godavari delta and Marathwada were other disputed zones; Mewar and Khandesh belonged to other regional contexts.
xa: Exam angle: "main cause of conflict" = **Raichur Doab**.
AP angle: **Telangana revolts** against the Bahmanis, quelled by Mahmud Gawan with **Velama** help.

ne1eb628b751.s: The Bahmani Sultanate was founded in 1347 by:
ne1eb628b751.x: Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah, also called Hasan Gangu, founded the Bahmani Sultanate in 1347 with Gulbarga as capital. Muhammad Shah I built the Gulbarga Jama Masjid, Ahmad Shah I shifted the capital to Bidar, and Firuz Shah was the scholar-king.
xs: The Bahmani Sultanate was founded in **1347** by **Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu)** — option **(3)**.
**Muhammad Shah I** built the Gulbarga Jama Masjid; **Ahmad Shah I** shifted to **Bidar**; **Firuz Shah** was the scholar-king.
xa: Capital: **Gulbarga**; first independent Muslim kingdom of the **Deccan**.
**Kalaburagi (Gulbarga) Fort** is his fort, flagged by the PM for neglect.

nbf642a34923.s: Who founded the Sharqi dynasty of Jaunpur in 1394?
o: Malik Sarwar, also known as Khwaja Jahan
nbf642a34923.x: Malik Sarwar, known as Khwaja Jahan, founded the Sharqi dynasty in 1394 after receiving the title Malik-us-Sharq.
nbf642a34923.tq: Distinguish the founder of the dynasty from the founder of the city and its last ruler.
xs: The **Sharqi** dynasty (**1394**) was founded by **Malik Sarwar (Khwaja Jahan)** — option **(4)**.
His title was **Malik-us-Sharq** ("**Lord of the East**").
**Firoz Shah Tughlaq** founded the **city** of Jaunpur; **Bahlul Lodi** conquered it in **1479**.
xa: Jaunpur = "**Shiraz of India**" (Shiraz-i-Hind), a centre of learning.
**Jaunpur school** of architecture dated **1394-1479**.

n129e46115df.s: Who moved the capital of Malwa from Dhar to Mandu?
n129e46115df.x: Hoshang Shah moved the capital to Mandu; Dilawar Khan Ghuri broke away from Delhi in 1401 and Mahmud Khalji founded the Khalji line.
xa: Hoshang Shah's Tomb = **India's first marble tomb**.
Last Sultan **Baz Bahadur** was defeated by **Akbar**.

n5d0497438e2.s: Which ruler of Gujarat founded Ahmedabad in 1411 on the banks of the Sabarmati?
n5d0497438e2.x: Ahmad Shah I founded Ahmedabad in 1411 on the Sabarmati River.
xs: **Ahmad Shah I** of Gujarat founded **Ahmedabad** (**1411**) on the **Sabarmati** — option **(1)**.
**Zafar Khan** (Muzaffar Shah I) founded the Gujarat Sultanate (**1407**).
**Mahmud Begarha** took Girnar and Champaner; **Bahadur Shah** died at Diu.
xa: ⚠ Bahmani **Ahmad Shah I** is a different ruler — he shifted the capital to **Bidar**.
Gujarat style: **Jama Masjid, Ahmedabad**.

nf3dd86f05fd.s: Chaitanya lived during the reign of which Sultan of Bengal?
nf3dd86f05fd.x: Chaitanya lived in Hussain Shah's reign; Hussain Shah and Nusrat Shah also patronised Bengali Mahabharata translations.
xa: ⚠ **Butshikan** = Sikandar; **Bud Shah** = Zain-ul-Abidin, the **"Akbar of Kashmir"**.
Zain-ul-Abidin had the **Mahabharata** and **Rajatarangini** translated into Persian.
He built the **Zaina Kadal** bridge in Srinagar.

n1dd03a23fb3.s: In which year did Akbar annex Gujarat?
n1dd03a23fb3.x: Akbar annexed Gujarat in 1572; Bengal followed in 1576.
xa: **Jaunpur** fell to **Bahlul Lodi** in **1479**.
The **Bahmani** kingdom ended in **1527** under **Kalimullah**.
⚠ Akbar: Gujarat **1572** → Bengal **1576**.

n5836da7acd5.s: Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir was popularly known by which of the following titles?
o: Bud Shah and the Akbar of Kashmir
Butshikan and Lord of the East
n5836da7acd5.x: Zain-ul-Abidin was called “Bud Shah”, meaning Great King, and the “Akbar of Kashmir”.
n5836da7acd5.tq: Match the ruler with his distinctive epithets, avoiding famous but unrelated titles.
xs: **Zain-ul-Abidin** was called **"Bud Shah" (Great King)** and the **"Akbar of Kashmir"** — option **(1)**.
**Butshikan** was **Sikandar's** epithet; **Lord of the East** (Malik-us-Sharq) was **Malik Sarwar's** title; **Shiraz-i-Hind** = Jaunpur.
xa: Original name: **Shahi Khan**; ruled **1420-1470**.
He **abolished jizya**, rebuilt temples and recalled Brahmins.

nfd63060a981.s: Which ruler of Kashmir abolished jizya, permitted the rebuilding of temples and called back the Brahmins?
nfd63060a981.x: These measures marked the conciliatory religious policy of Zain-ul-Abidin.
xa: This reversed the policy of **Sikandar Butshikan**, who imposed jizya.
He had the **Mahabharata** and **Rajatarangini** translated into Persian.
Works: **Zaina Kadal** bridge (Srinagar), **Zaina Lank** island (Wular lake).

ncf3bed66057.s: Which of the following works was translated into Persian under Zain-ul-Abidin?
ncf3bed66057.x: Zain-ul-Abidin had the Mahabharata and Kalhana's Rajatarangini translated into Persian; Mirat-i-Sikandari and Riyaz-us-Salatin are original histories of Gujarat and Bengal.
xa: **Jonaraja** continued the Rajatarangini.
Zain-ul-Abidin = "**Akbar of Kashmir**".

n2833b773136.s: Mahmud Begarha’s name is associated with the capture of which two forts?
n2833b773136.x: Mahmud Begarha captured Girnar in Junagadh and Champaner, the two forts associated with his name.
n2833b773136.tq: Test the ruler–two-forts association using nearby regional monuments as distractors.
xs: **Mahmud Begarha** took **Girnar (Junagadh) and Champaner**, the "two forts" of his name — option **(1)**.
**Chittor/Kumbhalgarh** are Mewar; **Asirgarh** is Khandesh; **Raichur/Gulbarga** are Bahmani.
xa: He ruled **1458-1511**; joined **Egypt** against the Portuguese (**Chaul 1508**, lost at **Diu 1509**).
**Mirat-i-Sikandari** describes his prosperity and administration (UPPSC 2023).

nbeb7647a8ac.s: With whose help did Mahmud Gawan quell the Telangana revolts?
nbeb7647a8ac.x: Mahmud Gawan, the Persian Afaqi wazir of Muhammad Shah III, quelled the Telangana revolts with Velama help, not the Reddis.
xa: His letters: **Riyaz-ul-Insha**.
Framed by rival nobles and **executed in 1481** → break-up of the kingdom.

n6ee9bc11a7c.s: Mahmud Gawan divided the four tarafs of the Bahmani kingdom into:
n6ee9bc11a7c.x: To strengthen the centre and curb provincial nobles, Mahmud Gawan divided the four tarafs into eight provinces and placed forts under central commanders.
xa: **Crown (khalisa) land** was reserved in each taraf.

naeebe49fd44.s: Mahmud Gawan's madrasa at Bidar was built on which model?
naeebe49fd44.x: The three-storeyed, tile-decorated madrasa followed a Persian (Herat/Samarkand) model; the Cordoba comparison belongs to the Gulbarga Jama Masjid.
xa: **Bidriware** of Bidar: **14th century** under the Bahmanis; GI tag **2006**.
Mahmud Gawan's letters: **Riyaz-ul-Insha**.

n57df86dfffd.s: Mahmud Gawan, whose fall contributed to the break-up of the Bahmani kingdom, met his end in 1481 through:
o: Execution after being framed by rival nobles
Assassination during a court revolt in Gulbarga
n57df86dfffd.x: Mahmud Gawan was framed by rival nobles and executed, traditionally dated to 1481; his fall contributed to the break-up of the Bahmani Kingdom.
xa: Under him the kingdom had reached its **greatest extent**; Bahmanis took **Goa (1472)**.
Last Sultan **Kalimullah**; kingdom ended **1527**.
**Golconda (Qutb Shahi)** grew out of the Bahmani break-up.

nc4540aa8da8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Bidriware?
o: It received a Geographical Indication tag in 2006
It was among the Prime Minister's diplomatic gifts on 22 May 2026
It developed in the fourteenth century under the Vijayanagara rulers
nc4540aa8da8.x: Bidriware developed in the fourteenth century under the Bahmanis, not the Vijayanagara rulers; the other statements are correct.
xa: **Ahmad Shah I** shifted the Bahmani capital from **Gulbarga → Bidar**.
Bidar also has **Mahmud Gawan's madrasa**: three storeys, **glazed tiles**, huge library.

nd18b8b2cace.s: The Adina Mosque at Pandua (1373-75) was built by:
nd18b8b2cace.x: Sikandar Shah built the Adina Mosque, one of India's largest; the Eklakhi Tomb is of Jalaluddin Muhammad Shah.
xa: The Eklakhi Tomb was the **prototype for Bengal buildings**.
Hussain Shahi works: **Chhota Sona Masjid** (**1510**), mosque at **Bagerhat**.

neb4a26e3132.s: The Lal Darwaza Mosque at Jaunpur was built by:
neb4a26e3132.x: Bibi Raje built the Lal Darwaza Mosque; the Atala Masjid and Jama Masjid are associated with Ibrahim Shah Sharqi.
xa: Atala Masjid: **three-storey facade**, **blue tiles** (UPSC).
⚠ **Lal Darwaza** = a queen (**Bibi Raje**, JPSC 2023 key); **Atala** = **Ibrahim Shah Sharqi**.
