nd944a530ab8.s: Hoshang Shah’s Tomb at Mandu is significant because it is regarded as:
o: The first fort built by Akbar
The first covered courtyard mosque in the Deccan
nd944a530ab8.x: Hoshang Shah’s Tomb is regarded as India’s first marble tomb.
nd944a530ab8.tq: Match the monument with its distinguishing architectural feature.
xs: **Hoshang Shah's Tomb** at Mandu is **India's first marble tomb** — option **(4)** (UPSC).
The first covered-courtyard mosque in the Deccan is not it — that feature belongs to **Gulbarga Jama Masjid**.
xa: Hoshang Shah moved Malwa's capital from **Dhar → Mandu**.
He began the **Jami Masjid**, Mandu, completed by **Mahmud Khalji**.

nec5fbfabbe0.s: The Hindola Mahal at Mandu was built by:
nec5fbfabbe0.x: Ghiyasuddin Khalji built the Hindola Mahal; Hoshang Shah began the Jami Masjid and Mahmud Khalji completed it.
xa: ⚠ **Jahaz Mahal** and **Hindola Mahal** = **Ghiyasuddin Khalji**, not Hoshang Shah (JPSC 2023 key).
Late Malwa: **Baz Bahadur's Palace**, **Rupmati's pavilion**, **Ashrafi Mahal**.

ne593d00ce62.s: The Jahaz Mahal at Mandu was built by:
ne593d00ce62.x: The Jahaz Mahal at Mandu was built by Ghiyasuddin Khalji (JPSC 2023 key), who also built the Hindola Mahal. Hoshang Shah is known for his marble tomb and for beginning the Jami Masjid, Baz Bahadur for his palace of the late Malwa period, and Dilawar Khan Ghuri for breaking away from Delhi in 1401.
xs: The **Jahaz Mahal** at Mandu was built by **Ghiyasuddin Khalji** — option **(2)** (JPSC 2023 key).
He also built the **Hindola Mahal** — **not Hoshang Shah**.
**Hoshang Shah** = first marble tomb; **Baz Bahadur** = late Malwa palace; **Dilawar Khan Ghuri** = broke from Delhi (**1401**).
xa: Jami Masjid, Mandu: begun by **Hoshang Shah**, completed by **Mahmud Khalji**.
Late Malwa: **Baz Bahadur's Palace**, **Rupmati's pavilion**, **Ashrafi Mahal**.

n76d12740d92.s: Who wrote Mirat-i-Sikandari, the Persian history of the Gujarat Sultanate?
n76d12740d92.x: Mirat-i-Sikandari was written by Sikandar bin Muhammad as a Persian history of the Gujarat Sultanate.
xa: It describes **Mahmud Begada's** prosperity and administration (UPPSC 2023).
**Burhan-i-Maasir** = Ahmadnagar (Nizam Shahis).

n4943bfb5b1b.s: The last Sultan of the Bahmani kingdom, which ended in 1527, was:
n4943bfb5b1b.x: The Bahmani kingdom, first ruled from Gulbarga, ended in 1527 under its last Sultan, Kalimullah.
xa: **Ahmad Shah I** shifted the capital to **Bidar**.
**Golconda (Qutb Shahi)** grew out of the Bahmani break-up.
Main conflict with Vijayanagara: the **Raichur Doab**.

n714458ff4ea.s: The capital of Berar, a Bahmani successor state, was:
n714458ff4ea.x: Berar, founded by Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk, had its capital at Ellichpur or Achalpur and was annexed by Ahmadnagar in 1574.
xa: Exam angle: "Berar was founded by" = **Imad Shahis** (APPSC G2 2005).
At **Talikota (1565)** four of the five combined — **all except Berar**.

na0a0d990b3a.s: Amir Ali Barid, known as the ‘cunning fox of the Deccan’, was associated with which successor state?
na0a0d990b3a.x: Amir Ali Barid was associated with the Barid Shahi state of Bidar and was referred to as the ‘cunning fox of the Deccan’.
na0a0d990b3a.tq: Use the sobriquet as the clue for identifying the correct successor state.
xs: **Amir Ali Barid**, "**cunning fox of the Deccan**", belonged to **Bidar** (Barid Shahi) — option **(3)**.
**Bijapur** = Adil Shahi; **Golconda** = Qutb Shahi; **Berar** = Imad Shahi.
xa: Barid Shahi founder: **Qasim Barid**.
Bidar was absorbed by **Bijapur** in **1619**.
Jamsheed of Golconda won the **Battle of Koulan** over Bidar (**1544**).

n91b76f6d782.s: The Barid Shahi dynasty was centred at:
n91b76f6d782.x: Barid Shahi was at Bidar, Adil Shahi at Bijapur, Nizam Shahi at Ahmadnagar and Imad Shahi at Berar.
xa: **Qutb Shahi — Golconda**, later **Hyderabad**.
⚠ **Bijapur** first to break away (**1489**); **Golconda** last (**1518**).

n852cc22f84e.s: The Qutb Shahi dynasty of Golconda was ended by:
n852cc22f84e.x: Aurangzeb ended the Qutb Shahi dynasty in 1687; he ended the Adil Shahi in 1686, and Shah Jahan ended the Nizam Shahi in 1633.
xa: ⚠ **1633** Nizam Shahis – **1686** Bijapur – **1687** Golconda.
In **1636** Golconda only signed an **ahdnama** (Inqiyad Nama) accepting Mughal suzerainty.

naeab0727047.s: Chand Bibi was the daughter of:
naeab0727047.x: Chand Bibi was the daughter of Hussain Nizam Shah I; her marriage to Ali Adil Shah sealed the anti-Vijayanagara alliance.
xa: ⚠ **Chand Bibi** ≠ **Chand Sultana** (Muhammad Quli's sister).
**Akbar** took **Ahmadnagar city** in **1600**.

n16fe414e8e9.s: Kondavidu was gained by which Qutb Shahi ruler after 1565?
n16fe414e8e9.x: Kondavidu was gained by Ibrahim after 1565; Sultan Quli had conquered Rachakonda, Devarakonda and Rajahmundry.
xa: Ibrahim also gained **Machilipatnam** and annexed coastal Andhra (**1570-78**).
Warangal was taken from **Shitab Khan**.

n6d519d6d876.s: The murder of Akkanna and Madanna in 1686 weakened Golconda because it occurred
o: before the Qutb Shahis acquired coastal Andhra
during the establishment of the Nizam Shahi dynasty
immediately after the founding of Khirki
just before the Mughal fall of Golconda
n6d519d6d876.x: The brothers were murdered in 1686, shortly before Golconda fell to Aurangzeb in 1687, thereby weakening the state’s administration and defence.
n6d519d6d876.tq: Connect the event’s timing with its political consequence rather than treating it as an isolated date.
xs: The brothers were **murdered in 1686**, **just before the Mughal fall of Golconda** — option **(4)**.
**Aurangzeb** took Golconda on **21 September 1687**.
xa: Aurangzeb annexed **Bijapur** the same year (**1686**).
⚠ **1633** Nizam Shahis – **1686** Bijapur – **1687** Golconda.

nb978b6c00f6.s: During the Qutb Shahi period, Muharram came to be celebrated in Andhra as:
nb978b6c00f6.x: Muharram came to be celebrated as Peerla Panduga during the Qutb Shahi period.
nb978b6c00f6.tq: Separate closely associated regional festival names by linking the specific festival with its religious occasion.
xs: **Muharram** was celebrated as **Peerla Panduga** — option **(2)**.
**Bonalu** is a separate Telangana festival begun at Golconda fort.
xa: Hindus held high office (**Murari Rao**, **Jagadeva Rao**, **Madanna**).
The Qutb Shahis united the Telugu lands for the **third time**.

nindian-history-4-6.s: The Nizamshahi dynasty was founded by:
nindian-history-4-6.x: Malik Ahmad founded the Nizamshahi; Yusuf Adil Shah, Fatehullah Imad Shah and Quli Qutb Shah founded the Adilshahi, Imadshahi and Qutbshahi.
n: Malik Ahmad founded the Nizamshahi dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Malik Ahmad founded the Nizamshahi dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Yusuf Adil Shah founded the Adilshahi dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Yusuf Adil Shah founded the Adilshahi dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Fatehullah Imad Shah founded the Imadshahi dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Fatehullah Imad Shah founded the Imadshahi dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Quli Qutb Shah founded the Qutbshahi dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
Quli Qutb Shah founded the Qutbshahi dynasty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
xa: **Amir Ali Barid** — **Baridshahi** of **Bidar**, "cunning fox of the Deccan".
⚠ **Bijapur** = first to break away (**1489**); **Golconda** = last to break away and last to fall (**1687**).
Berar: **Imad Shahis** (APPSC G2 **2005**).

ne07ad913c6e.s: Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk was killed by his son:
ne07ad913c6e.x: Sultan Quli, who gave the dynasty its name and strengthened Golconda fort, was killed by his son Jamsheed.
xa: He was defeated by **Krishnadevaraya at Goni** (**1517**).
He built the **Golconda Jama Masjid** and the new city of **Muhammad Nagar**.

nfe23713b6af.s: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah wrote Dakhni poetry under the pen name:
nfe23713b6af.x: Muhammad Quli wrote as 'Maani' (Kulliyat-e-Quli Qutb Shah); Zillullah was the pen name of Muhammad Qutb Shah.
xa: ⚠ Pen names: **Maani** = Muhammad Quli; **Zillullah** = Muhammad Qutb Shah.
Some notes call **Ibrahim** the **"Chaucer of Urdu"**.
Muhammad Quli **founded Hyderabad** (**1591**) and built the **Charminar**.

n7393eedd7e7.s: The Inqiyad Nama of 1636 was signed by:
n7393eedd7e7.x: The Inqiyad Nama was signed by Abdullah Qutb Shah, not Ibrahim.
xa: Abdullah also issued the **Bangaru Farmana** (**1636**) to the English.
**Tavernier** visited in **Abdullah's** reign.

n46db8cf9e3c.s: The Inqiyad Nama of 1636 signified which development?
o: Acceptance of Mughal suzerainty by Abdullah Qutb Shah
The declaration of independence from the Bahmani kingdom
The formation of the Talikota alliance
The treaty between Abul Hasan and Shivaji
n46db8cf9e3c.x: Through the Inqiyad Nama of 1636, Abdullah Qutb Shah accepted Mughal suzerainty.
n46db8cf9e3c.tq: Match a document with its political consequence.
xs: The **Inqiyad Nama (1636)** = **Abdullah Qutb Shah's acceptance of Mughal suzerainty** — option **(1)**.
It was a **deed of submission** to **Shah Jahan**.
Independence was declared in **1518**; Talikota was **1565**; the Shivaji treaty was **1677**.
xa: In **1636** both **Bijapur and Golconda** signed **ahdnamas** — suzerainty + indemnity.
The same year Abdullah issued the **Bangaru Farmana** to the English.

n632d7daf13a.s: What was the Bangaru Farmana issued by Abdullah Qutb Shah in 1636 associated with?
o: Accepting the Shia faith as the state religion
Granting trading privileges to the English
Beginning construction of the Mecca Masjid
n632d7daf13a.x: The Bangaru Farmana of 1636 was issued to the English and is associated with their trading privileges.
n632d7daf13a.tq: Distinguish two documents issued in the same year by their purpose.
xs: The **Bangaru Farmana** (**1636**) was issued to the **English** — option **(2)**, trading privileges.
The **Mecca Masjid** was begun by Muhammad Qutb Shah; **Madanna** became Diwan under Abul Hasan.
xa: The English first came to **Machilipatnam** in **1611** (Captain **Hippon**, ship **Globe**).
In the same year Abdullah signed the **Inqiyad Nama**.

n571d9a87f01.s: The Dar-ul-Shifa (1595) at Hyderabad was built by:
n571d9a87f01.x: Muhammad Quli built the Charminar and the Dar-ul-Shifa; the Mecca Masjid was begun in 1614 by Muhammad Qutb Shah.
xa: Muhammad Quli also built the **Jama Masjid** (**1598**).
⚠ Mecca Masjid completed by **Aurangzeb**; Charminar = **Muhammad Quli**.

n0df26b7f0f4.s: Under Abul Hasan, the office of Peshwa was renamed as which office, held by Madanna?
n0df26b7f0f4.x: Under Abul Hasan, the Peshwa or Wakil was renamed Diwan, and the office was held by Madanna.
n0df26b7f0f4.tq: Test an institutional name change and its office-holder together.
xs: Under Abul Hasan the **Peshwa / Wakil** was renamed **Diwan**, held by **Madanna** — option **(4)**.
**Kotwal** = city police; **Shahbandar** = port; **Jumlat-ul-Mulk** = Mir Jumla (finance).
xa: Madanna's titles: **Surya Prakasa Rao** and **Alampana**; **Akkanna** was **Sar Lashkar**.
Madanna and Akkanna were **murdered in 1686**.

n5fcd1414d19.s: The city of Hyderabad was planned by which official?
n5fcd1414d19.x: Peshwa Mir Momin Astarabadi planned Hyderabad after its foundation by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.
n5fcd1414d19.tq: Use the official–institution or official–project association.
xs: Hyderabad was planned by Peshwa **Mir Momin Astarabadi** — option **(2)**.
**Hussain Shah Wali** built Hussain Sagar; **Mir Jumla** gave the Kohinoor to Shah Jahan; **Firishta** was a historian.
xa: Capital shifted from **Golconda** in **1592**.
Original name **Bhagyanagar**; founded by **Muhammad Quli** in **1591**.

nceb32b456a7.s: Which monument is famous for acoustics by which a handclap at the gate carries to the Bala Hisar?
nceb32b456a7.x: Golconda fort is known for this acoustic effect; Charminar is linked with the Char Kaman gateways.
xa: Golconda fort also had **piped water**; old name **Mangalavaram/Mankal**.
**Ibrahim** built Golconda's **high walls**.

nae11679992c.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the construction of the Mecca Masjid?
o: It was begun in 1591 and completed in 1614 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.
It was begun in 1614 by Muhammad Qutb Shah and completed by Aurangzeb in 1692–93.
It was begun by Aurangzeb in 1692 and completed by Muhammad Qutb Shah.
It was built in 1562 by Hussain Shah Wali.
nae11679992c.x: Muhammad Qutb Shah began the Mecca Masjid in 1614, and Aurangzeb completed it in 1692–93.
nae11679992c.tq: Separate the initiator, successor and completion date in a long construction history.
xs: Begun in **1614** by **Muhammad Qutb Shah**, completed by **Aurangzeb** in **1692-93** — option **(2)**.
Option (3) reverses the two; **1591** is the Charminar; **1562** is Hussain Sagar.
xa: **Tavernier** saw **4,000** workers on it.
Muhammad Qutb Shah's pen name: **Zillullah**.

n380a5734d19.s: Who built the high walls of Golconda Fort?
n380a5734d19.x: Ibrahim Qutb Shah built the high walls of Golconda, which had been the Qutb Shahi capital from Sultan Quli's time.
xa: Golconda fort: **acoustics** (handclap heard at **Bala Hisar**) and **piped water**.
Hussain Sagar date: **1562** / **1563** — notes differ.

n83007ce1137.s: The English obtained permission to establish their presence at Machilipatnam from:
n83007ce1137.x: The English came to Machilipatnam with the permission of Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah. The attribution to Ibrahim Qutb Shah is chronologically inconsistent because he died in 1580.
n83007ce1137.tq: Use chronology to reject a ruler who could not have granted the permission.
xs: The English came to Machilipatnam with **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah's** permission — option **(1)**.
APPSC 2025 accepted "**Quli Qutub Shah**".
xa: ⚠ Trap: the **APPSC G2 2008** key gave **Ibrahim Qutb Shah**, though he died in **1580** — choose him only if Muhammad Quli is absent.
The English factory dates to **1611** (Captain **Hippon**, ship **Globe**).

nindian-history-32-13.s: Rudradaman I is associated with the patronage of:
nindian-history-32-13.x: Rudradaman I goes with Sanskrit; the Satavahanas with Prakrit, Krishnadeva Raya with Telugu and Zain-ul-Abidin with translation.
n: Satavahana rulers patronised Prakrit. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
Rudradaman-I supported cultural arts. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
Rudradaman-I supported Sanskrit literature. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
Krishnadeva Raya supported Telugu literature. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
Krishnadeva Raya supported scholars. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
Zain-ul-Abidin supported translation activities. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
Zain-ul-Abidin supported cultural activities. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
xa: **Rana Kumbha** — **music, literature and art**.
**Sawant Singh** — **Kishangarh painting**.
**Ibrahim Adil Shah II** — **arts**.

nindian-history-32-18.s: Kishangarh painting flourished under the patronage of:
nindian-history-32-18.x: Sawant Singh backed Kishangarh painting; Jahangir supported European and Persian arts and Rana Kumbha music, literature and art.
n: Jahangir patronised painting. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
Jahangir supported European arts. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
Jahangir supported Persian arts. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
Rana Kumbha patronised music. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
Rana Kumbha patronised literature. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
Rana Kumbha patronised art. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
Sawant Singh supported art. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
Sawant Singh supported learning. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
Sawant Singh supported Kishangarh painting. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
Zain-ul-Abidin supported translation activities. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
Zain-ul-Abidin supported cultural activities. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-99]
xa: **Krishnadeva Raya** — **Telugu literature** and scholars.
**Firishta** dedicated **Tarikh-i-Firishta** to **Ibrahim Adil Shah II**.
Ibrahim Adil Shah II's tomb = **Ibrahim Rauza**.

neb7b26f6306.s: Ponnaganti Telaganarya’s Yayati Charitra is notable as
o: the first Telugu work on revenue administration
the first Telugu poem written under Abul Hasan
the first kavya in pure Telugu
neb7b26f6306.x: Yayati Charitra is identified as the first kavya in pure Telugu. Its dedication is attributed to Amir Khan in one account and to Ibrahim in another.
neb7b26f6306.tq: Distinguish the work’s literary distinction from its disputed dedication.
xs: **Yayati Charitra** is the **first kavya in pure Telugu** — option **(4)**.
The **first Telugu Yakshagana** is **Sugriva Vijayam** (Rudrakavi).
xa: It was dedicated to **Amir Khan**, Ibrahim's governor of **Patancheru** (some notes: to Ibrahim).
⚠ FIRSTs: **Tapati Samvaranopakhyanam** = dedicated to a Muslim ruler; **Yayati Charitra** = pure Telugu.

nbaaffc21146.s: A Tarafdar in the Qutb Shahi administration was primarily responsible for which combination of functions?
o: Judicial administration at the village level
Customs collection at a port only
Law and order, revenue and troops in a province
nbaaffc21146.x: The Tarafdar was the governor of a Taraf and was responsible for law and order, revenue and troops.
nbaaffc21146.tq: Apply the office’s territorial level to its functions.
xs: The **Tarafdar** governed a **Taraf** (province): **law and order, revenue and troops** — option **(4)**.
Port customs = **Shahbandar**; auditing = **Majumdar / Dabir**.
xa: ⚠ **Taraf – Sarkar – Pargana** = **Tarafdar – Fauzdar – Tahsildar**; **6 – 37 – 517**.
**Abdullah** had **6 Tarafs**.

n353529a172b.s: The Qutb Shahi system of justice was organised in which order from the Sultan downward?
o: Sultan – Qazi – Shariat Panch – Pargana Majlis
Sultan – Shariat Panch – Qazi – Pargana Majlis
Sultan – Pargana Majlis – Qazi – Shariat Panch
n353529a172b.x: The judicial hierarchy was Sultan, Shariat Panch as chief justice, Qazi, and Pargana Majlis.
n353529a172b.tq: Arrange judicial authorities by hierarchical order.
xs: Justice ran **Sultan → Shariat Panch → Qazi → Pargana Majlis** — option **(2)**.
The **Shariat Panch** was the **chief justice**, above the Qazi.
**Kotwal** and **Faujdar** were police/district officers, not the judicial chain.
xa: The **Kotwal** sometimes **judged cases** besides policing.
**Mahasibs / Mustasibs** supervised **public morals**, like the Mughal **Muhtasib**.

nbd2758a0f21.s: In Qutb Shahi administration, a Sarkar was headed by the:
nbd2758a0f21.x: A Sarkar was under a Faujdar, a Pargana under a Tahsildar or Deshmukh, and the village under the Mukaddam; the Shahbandar was a port officer.
xa: **Tarafdar** governed a **Taraf**: law and order, revenue, troops.
Under **Abul Hasan**: **37 Sarkars**, **517 Parganas**.

n571f77ab3be.s: The Malik-e-Maidan associated with Bijapur is a famous:
n571f77ab3be.x: The Malik-e-Maidan is a cannon, not a gateway.
xa: **Gol Gumbaz** (Muhammad Adil Shah) has a **whispering gallery**.
**Ibrahim Rauza** = tomb of **Ibrahim Adil Shah II**.

n920942c47b0.s: Malik Ambar revived revenue administration on the lines of:
n920942c47b0.x: Malik Ambar followed Todar Mal's lines with land survey and fixed assessment, avoiding revenue farming.
xa: He founded **Khirki**, later **Aurangabad**.
His son **Fath Khan** made peace with the Mughals.
n920942c47b0.fixed: Maratha guerrilla cavalry is military, not a revenue-system feature; answer is 1, 2 and 3 only

nd6161403c79.s: The official language of the Qutb Shahi court was:
nd6161403c79.x: The Shia Qutb Shahis used Persian as the official language; Telugu and Dakhni received patronage but were not the court language.
xa: The dynasty had **7 rulers** (**1518-1687**).
Hindus held high office (**Murari Rao**, **Jagadeva Rao**, **Madanna**).

n0ee197db94c.s: In Qutb Shahi administration, the Mir Jumla was the:
n0ee197db94c.x: The Mir Jumla was the finance minister; the Kotwal headed city policing and the Tahsildar a pargana.
xa: ⚠ One block calls Mir Jumla **war and foreign affairs** — the standard view is finance.
**Kotwal** sometimes also **judged cases**.

nd1d4d028900.s: Under the Qutb Shahis, Dasabandhu lands paid:
nd1d4d028900.x: Dasabandhu lands paid only one-tenth; haveli meant crown lands and Mustajirs were the highest bidders in tax farming.
xa: Chief source of revenue: **land revenue**; some notes call the leased **diamond mines** the highest single source.
**Machilipatnam** was leased for **1,80,000 pagodas** a year.
State monopolies: **salt, betel leaf, tobacco**.

nd155dca9d76.s: Under the Qutb Shahis, Akkanna served as:
nd155dca9d76.x: Akkanna was the Sar Lashkar (army chief), while his brother Madanna was Mir Jumla or Diwan.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes (Block 03) **reverse** their roles.
They made an alliance with **Shivaji** (**1677**); were **murdered in 1686**.

ne97ea74be98.x: Bhagyanagar is identified as Hyderabad's original name; Mankal and Mangalavaram are names associated with old Golconda.
xa: Golconda was the Qutb Shahi capital from **Sultan Quli**, who renamed it **Muhammadnagar**.
Capital moved to Hyderabad in **1592**.

n70fadee3927.s: Hussain Sagar was declared the UNWTO 'Heart of the World' in:
n70fadee3927.x: Hussain Sagar, named after Hussain Shah Wali and built under Ibrahim, received the UNWTO 'Heart of the World' designation in 2012.
xa: Date given as **1562** / **1563** — notes differ.
The **Ibrahimpatnam** tank also dates from Ibrahim's reign.

n3ec64356b98.s: The roots of Telangana's Bonalu festival are traced to the:
n3ec64356b98.x: Bonalu, which began at the Jagadamba Mahankali temple in Golconda fort, has roots in the Kakatiya and Qutb Shahi periods.
xa: Muharram was celebrated as **Peerla Panduga**.
Golconda fort's old name: **Mangalavaram / Mankal**.

n0851f1cd379.s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of Hindus who held high office under the Qutb Shahis?
o: Murari Rao, Jagadeva Rao and Madanna
Hussain Shah Wali, Ibrahim and Madanna
Murari Rao, Abul Hasan and Jagadeva Rao
Madanna, Muhammad Quli and Jagadeva Rao
n0851f1cd379.x: Murari Rao, Jagadeva Rao and Madanna are identified as Hindus who held high office under the Qutb Shahis.
n0851f1cd379.tq: Eliminate options containing rulers or other non-matching personalities and retain the complete administrative trio.
xs: **Murari Rao**, **Jagadeva Rao** and **Madanna** were Hindus in high office — option **(1)**.
**Hussain Shah Wali**, **Ibrahim**, **Abul Hasan** and **Muhammad Quli** were Muslims.
xa: Madanna was **Mir Jumla / Diwan**; his brother **Akkanna** was **Sar Lashkar**.
**Mustajirs** (tax farmers) were also **mostly Hindus**.

n601fef561d9.s: Tavernier visited the Andhra diamond mines during the reign of:
n601fef561d9.x: Tavernier visited the mines during the reign of Abdullah Qutb Shah.
n601fef561d9.tq: Apply the traveller–ruler association while avoiding a neighbouring ruler trap.
xs: **Tavernier** visited the Andhra diamond mines in **Abdullah Qutb Shah's** reign — option **(1)** (APPSC G2 2019).
He was a **French jeweller / diamond merchant** (**17th century**) and wrote **Six Travels**.
xa: He recorded the **Kohinoor** and saw **4,000** workers at the Mecca Masjid.
Mines: **Kollur** (Guntur), **Paritala** (Krishna), **Ramallakota** (Kurnool), **Vajrakarur** (Anantapur).

nee808fee64f.s: The Kohinoor diamond was presented to Shah Jahan by:
nee808fee64f.x: Mir Jumla presented the Kohinoor, found in 1656 at the Kollur mines on the Krishna, to Shah Jahan; Tavernier only recorded it.
xa: It is now in the **British crown**, in British hands since **1849**.
Pakistan's **1976** claim was recalled in the news.

n9283152dec0.s: The English factory at Machilipatnam was established in:
n9283152dec0.x: The English factory dates to 1611, after the Dutch factory of 1605; Captain Hippon arrived in the ship Globe.
xa: The Dutch factory was the **first European factory in Andhra**.
The English came with **Muhammad Quli's** permission.

n887525d099f.s: Machilipatnam was particularly famous for the manufacture and trade of:
n887525d099f.x: Machilipatnam was famed for muslin and Kalamkari, in addition to its importance as a trading centre.
n887525d099f.tq: Identify the characteristic goods associated with a historic port.
xs: **Machilipatnam** was famed for **muslin** and **Kalamkari** — option **(1)**.
Diamonds came from the **Kollur** and other mines, traded at **Moti Darwaza**.
xa: It was leased for **1,80,000 pagodas** a year.
Port works revive the old **Gilakaladindi** port.

n99d52da73d5.s: Who opened the gates of Golconda Fort to Aurangzeb on 21 September 1687?
n99d52da73d5.x: The gates were opened by the traitor Abdullah Khan Pani, also referred to as Abdullah Phani in the accounts.
n99d52da73d5.tq: Use the person–deed trap by associating the gate-opening with the named traitor rather than the defender.
xs: The traitor **Abdullah Khan Pani** (Abdullah Phani) opened the gates on **21 September 1687** — option **(4)**.
**Abul Razak Lari** was honoured for **defending** Golconda; **Fath Khan** was Malik Ambar's son.
xa: Golconda became the Mughals' **21st Suba**.
Last ruler **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** was imprisoned at Bidar, then **Daulatabad**.

ndaccbd03dfe.s: Kitab-i-Nauras was written in Dakhni by:
ndaccbd03dfe.x: Ibrahim Adil Shah II wrote Kitab-i-Nauras, invoked Saraswati as his muse and received Firishta's dedication.
xa: His tomb is the **Ibrahim Rauza** (UPSC).
⚠ **Chand Sultana** (his wife) ≠ **Chand Bibi** (wife of Ali Adil Shah).

n717b771c5c3.s: Gol Gumbaz at Bijapur, with its whispering gallery, is the tomb of:
n717b771c5c3.x: Gol Gumbaz, among the world's largest domes, is the tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah.
xa: **Malik-e-Maidan** cannon is also at Bijapur.
**Ibrahim Rauza** = tomb of Ibrahim Adil Shah II.

n8e6a2633a86.s: Who was the Abyssinian regent of the Nizam Shahis who resisted Jahangir?
n8e6a2633a86.x: Malik Ambar was an Abyssinian regent of the Nizam Shahis and resisted the Mughal emperor Jahangir.
n8e6a2633a86.tq: Match the distinctive identity and political role with the correct Deccan administrator.
xs: **Malik Ambar** was the **Abyssinian regent** of the Nizam Shahis who resisted **Jahangir** — option **(4)**.
**Fath Khan** was his son; **Abul Razak Lari** defended Golconda; **Abdullah Khan Pani** betrayed Golconda.
xa: He revived land revenue on **Todar Mal's lines**.
He founded **Khirki** → later **Aurangabad**.

n3c97be09f97.s: Malik Ambar founded Khirki, which later came to be known as
n3c97be09f97.x: Malik Ambar founded Khirki, which was later known as Aurangabad.
n3c97be09f97.tq: Distinguish the original and later names of the city from nearby Deccan centres.
xs: Malik Ambar's **Khirki** later became **Aurangabad** — option **(2)**.
**Daulatabad** is where **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** was imprisoned; **Bidar** was the Barid Shahi capital.
xa: Malik Ambar resisted **Jahangir**.
Revenue system on **Todar Mal's lines**.

nb43553d5d68.s: The Qutb Shahis are credited with uniting the Telugu lands for the:
o: First time, after the Mauryas and Satavahanas
Second time, after the Cholas and Kakatiyas
Third time, after the Satavahanas and Kakatiyas
Fourth time, after the Vijayanagara and Bahmani kingdoms
nb43553d5d68.x: The Qutb Shahis united the Telugu lands for the third time, following the earlier unifications under the Satavahanas and Kakatiyas.
nb43553d5d68.tq: Use the stated sequence of earlier unifying powers to identify the correct ordinal position.
xs: The Qutb Shahis united the Telugu lands for the **third time**, after the **Satavahanas and Kakatiyas** — option **(3)**.
**Sultan Quli** took Telangana forts; **Ibrahim** annexed **coastal Andhra** (**1570-78**).
xa: Ibrahim gained **Kondavidu** and **Machilipatnam** after **1565**.
Muharram was celebrated as **Peerla Panduga**.

n469c1f2280f.s: Under the Qutb Shahis, which of the following commodities were state monopolies?
n469c1f2280f.x: Salt, betel leaf and tobacco were state monopolies.
xa: Other sources: **trade taxes**, **port customs**, taxes on courtesans and professions.
Chief source: **land revenue**.

n783ca084dc9.s: The first inscription to call Harihara I a king was the:
n783ca084dc9.x: The Nellore inscription is regarded as the first inscription to call Harihara I a king; it dates his reign to 1336–1355.
n783ca084dc9.tq: Match the inscription with the precise historical claim associated with it.
xs: The first record to call Harihara I king is the **Nellore inscription** — option **(3)**.
It dates his reign **1336-1355**.
xa: First seat of the kingdom: **Anegondi**.
Harihara I was crowned on **18 April 1336** at the **Virupaksha** temple.
The city was completed by **1343** (some notes: entered **1344**).

n7a87b0e4773.s: Vidyaranya, who is associated with the reconversion of Harihara and Bukka, was the head of the:
n7a87b0e4773.x: Vidyaranya headed the Sringeri Shankara Math and is associated with the brothers' return to Hinduism.
n7a87b0e4773.tq: Match the religious institution with its associated spiritual leader.
xs: **Vidyaranya** headed the **Sringeri Shankara Math** — option **(4)**.
He **reconverted** the brothers to Hinduism before the **1336** coronation.
xa: The brothers visited **Sringeri** in **1346** after the **Hoysala** victory.
He wrote the **Vidyaranya Kalajnana**; his brother **Sayana** was minister of Harihara II.
⚠ **Madhava-Vidyaranya** (Advaita head) ≠ **Madhava** the minister who took **Goa**.

n3596564c1d6.s: Which of the following correctly represents the sequence in the founding legend?
o: Fall of Warangal → conversion in Delhi → dispatch against Deccan rebels → meeting with Vidyaranya → return to Hinduism
Meeting with Vidyaranya → fall of Warangal → conversion in Delhi → foundation of Anegondi
Conversion in Delhi → fall of Warangal → visit to Sringeri → appointment by Prataparudra
Foundation of Anegondi → conversion in Delhi → fall of Warangal → meeting with Vidyaranya
n3596564c1d6.x: The legend proceeds from the fall of Warangal and conversion in Delhi to the Deccan campaign, meeting Vidyaranya, and return to Hinduism.
n3596564c1d6.tq: Arrange the narrative by identifying the first event and following the linked sequence.
xs: Sequence: **fall of Warangal → conversion in Delhi → sent against Deccan rebels → met Vidyaranya → return to Hinduism** — option **(1)**.
Then they founded **Anegondi** in the name of **Virupaksha**.
xa: The meeting took place near **Pampa**.
Harihara I was crowned **18 April 1336**.

n99215c141c2.s: Anegondi is significant in the early history of Vijayanagara because it was:
o: The site of the Sringeri Shankara Math
The place where Saluva Narasimha began the first usurpation
The first seat of the kingdom, established in the name of Sri Virupaksha
The final capital of the Aravidu dynasty
n99215c141c2.x: Anegondi was the first seat of the kingdom, and it was set up in the name of Sri Virupaksha.
n99215c141c2.tq: Distinguish the founders' first seat from later dynastic capitals and religious centres.
xs: **Anegondi** was the **first seat** of the kingdom, set up "**in the name of Sri Virupaksha**" — option **(3)**.
**Harihara I** later moved the capital from Anegondi to **Vijayanagara**.
**Saluva Narasimha** was lord of **Chandragiri**; the Aravidu capitals were **Penukonda, Chandragiri, Vellore**.
xa: Vidyaranya headed **Sringeri**, not Anegondi.
City completed by **1343**.

nf6c6819400c.x: Vijayanagara means 'City of Victory'; it was built by Harihara and Bukka on the south bank of the Tungabhadra, and its ruins lie at Hampi.
xa: Built on the **south bank of the Tungabhadra**; ruins at **Hampi**.
**7 stone ramparts**; completed by **1343**.

ndee1f38a99a.s: The royal emblem of the Vijayanagara empire was the:
ndee1f38a99a.x: The Vijayanagara emblem was the Varaha; the Sangamas were Shaiva and the later three dynasties Vaishnava.
xa: **Devaraya I's** coronation copper plates (Apr **2025**) carry a **Vamana** seal instead of the usual **Varaha**.
The family deity was **Virupaksha**.

nc8a730ded8d.s: Which ruler shifted the capital of the Vijayanagara kingdom from Anegondi to Vijayanagara?
nc8a730ded8d.x: Harihara I shifted the capital from Anegondi to Vijayanagara.
xs: **Harihara I** moved the capital from **Anegondi** to **Vijayanagara** — option **(1)**.
**Bukka I** completed the city; **Devaraya I** built the dam.
xa: Harihara I annexed the **Hoysala** kingdom (**1346**) and the **Kadambas** (**1347**).
Title: **Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati**.

n15b8b14e07f.s: The Kakatiya-service theory regarding Harihara and Bukka holds that they had served under:
n15b8b14e07f.x: The Kakatiya theory states that Harihara and Bukka served Prataparudra of Warangal before being taken to Delhi after 1323.
n15b8b14e07f.tq: Apply the ruler–regional power association without confusing it with the Kampili or Hoysala theories.
xs: The Kakatiya-service theory says they served **Prataparudra of Warangal** — option **(1)**.
After **1323** they were taken to **Delhi** and converted.
Service under **Veera Ballala III** is the **Kannada/Hoysala** theory; service to **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** is the Delhi version.
xa: **APPSC G2 2005** key: Sangama was "**a Kakatiya chief**".
There are **7 theories** of origin; **Sewell** records **seven** local traditions.

n2a50e2c2ddb.s: How many local traditions about the founding of Vijayanagara did Robert Sewell record?
n2a50e2c2ddb.x: Sewell recorded seven local founding traditions.
xa: ⚠ **Sewell** appears twice: records the seven traditions + backs the **Andhra** theory.
Kannada theory backers: **Father Heras**, **Rice**, **S.K. Ayyangar**, **H. Krishna Sastri**, **P.B. Desai**.

n60d78f9af2f.s: Who among the following is associated with the Kannada or Hoysala theory of the origin of Harihara and Bukka?
n60d78f9af2f.x: Father Heras, Rice, S. K. Ayyangar, H. Krishna Sastri and P. B. Desai supported the Kannada or Hoysala theory.
n60d78f9af2f.tq: Separate the scholars supporting the Kannada/Hoysala theory from those associated with the Andhra theory.
xs: **Father Heras** backs the **Kannada/Hoysala** theory — option **(2)**.
**N. Venkataramanaiah**, **Nilakanta Sastri** and **Sewell** back the **Andhra** theory.
xa: Other Kannada-theory backers: **Rice**, **S.K. Ayyangar**, **H. Krishna Sastri**, **P.B. Desai**.
The theory makes them officers of **Veera Ballala III**.
Heras also wrote **The Aravidu Dynasty of Vijayanagara**.

n51ec828de69.s: The capture of Srisailam and Dupadu near Markapur is attributed to:
n51ec828de69.x: The capture of Srisailam and Dupadu is attributed to Bukka I; Devaraya I fought the Kandukuru Reddis and allied with the Velamas.
xa: Devaraya I took southern **Kondaveedu**, including **Motupalli**, recorded in his **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam**.
Devaraya I built a **dam on the Tungabhadra** with canals to carry water to the city.
**Nicolo Conti** visited in his reign; CDX calls him the first to recruit Muslims.

nindian-history-20-13.s: Harihara II's campaigns extended Vijayanagara rule over Kanara, Mysore, Kanchi and:
nindian-history-20-13.x: As part of the Vijayanagara-Bahmani struggle, Harihara II extended his rule over Kanara, Mysore, Kanchi and Trichinopoly.
n: Harihara-II’s campaign was part of the Vijayanagara–Bahamani conflict. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Harihara-II expanded into Kanara. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Harihara-II expanded into Mysore. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Harihara-II expanded into Kanchi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
Harihara-II expanded into Trichinapalli. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 76-78]
xa: Bone of contention: **Raichur Doab** between the **Krishna and Tungabhadra**.
⚠ Other notes say Goa was taken in **1366** by minister **Madhava**; lost in **1472**.
**Mudgal (1358)** under **Bukka I** = **first Indian war with artillery**.

nindian-history-68-4.x: Ibrahim Adil Shah II founded Nauraspur.
n: Ajatashatru established Pataliputra as a fortified settlement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 144-145]
Harihara and Bukka founded Vijayanagara in 1336 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 144-145]
Ghiyasuddin Tughluq established Tughluqabad as a city in Delhi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 144-145]
Ibrahim Adil Shah II established Nauraspur as a new township. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 144-145]
xa: Nauraspur was known as a **musical city**.
**Udayin** shifted the capital from **Rajagriha** to **Pataliputra**.
**Nagalapuram** — **Krishnadeva Raya**, for his mother **Nagala Devi**.

n1cfacf005f8.s: After the battle of Talikota, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire was shifted in which sequence?
n1cfacf005f8.x: After Talikota, the capital moved from Hampi to Penukonda and subsequently to Chandragiri; both later capitals were in present-day Andhra Pradesh.
n1cfacf005f8.tq: Follow the first and second capital shifts in sequence.
xs: After Talikota: **Hampi → Penukonda → Chandragiri** — option **(2)**.
Both **Penukonda** and **Chandragiri** are in **AP**.
xa: The **Aravidu** capitals were **Penukonda, Chandragiri, Vellore**.
**Talikota (1565)**: Deccan sultanates defeated **Rama Raya**.

n830c3569769.s: The first usurpation in the history of the Vijayanagara Empire is associated with:
o: Saluva Narasimha and the Saluva dynasty
Harihara I and the Sangama dynasty
Tirumala Raya and the Aravidu dynasty
Vira Narasimha and the Tuluva dynasty
n830c3569769.x: Saluva Narasimha ended the Sangama line and established the Saluva dynasty, an event described as the first usurpation.
n830c3569769.tq: Match the political event ‘first usurpation’ with its ruler and dynasty.
xs: The **first usurpation** = **Saluva Narasimha**, founding the **Saluva** dynasty — option **(1)**.
In **1485** he expelled **Praudha Raya** with **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka's** help.
xa: He was lord of **Chandragiri**; clan from **Kalyana**.
**Annamacharya** (**1408-1503**) was his contemporary.

nba268a369f1.s: Which Vijayanagara dynasty ruled the longest, with Devaraya II as its greatest ruler and Praudha Raya as its last?
nba268a369f1.x: The Sangama dynasty was the longest-ruling dynasty; Devaraya II was its greatest ruler and Praudha Raya its last.
xa: ⚠ **Harihara II** = longest-reigning Sangama king; **Sangama** = longest-ruling dynasty.
Praudha Raya was expelled by **Saluva Narasimha** in **1485**.

n8c0b563f22e.s: In the First Usurpation of 1485, Saluva Narasimha seized the throne by expelling:
n8c0b563f22e.x: Saluva Narasimha, lord of Chandragiri, expelled Praudha Raya, the last Sangama ruler, with the help of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka.
xa: His clan came from **Kalyana**; ancestor **Saluva Mangu** served **Kumara Kampana**.
He took the **Machilipatnam** area and repelled a **Bahmani raid on Kanchi (1481)**.
The **Saluva** dynasty ruled **1485-1505**.

n11f81e44061.s: Which symbol appears on the seal of the copper plates connected with Devaraya I’s coronation?
n11f81e44061.x: The copper plates carry a Vamana seal, rather than the usual Varaha seal.
n11f81e44061.tq: Focus on the exceptional symbol and avoid reversing the unusual seal with the customary one.
xs: The plates carry a **Vamana** seal — option **(1)**.
This replaces the usual **Varaha** (boar), the Vijayanagara emblem.
xa: The plates record Devaraya I's coronation and grant **Gudipalli**, renamed **Devarayapura-Agrahara**.
Sangamas were **Shaiva**; the later three dynasties were **Vaishnava**.
Harihara I's coronation was at the **Virupaksha** temple, **18 April 1336**.

n53bd864d9fc.s: Which two Vijayanagara dynasties are described as being of Andhra origin?
n53bd864d9fc.x: Only two of the four dynasties, Sangama and Aravidu, are described as Andhra in origin; later capitals Penukonda and Chandragiri are in Andhra Pradesh.
xa: Aravidu origin: **Araviti**, Kurnool; capitals Penukonda, Chandragiri, **Vellore**.
Founders' origin theories: **7**; the APPSC key says Sangama was **"a Kakatiya chief"** (G2 **2005**).
⚠ Order **S-S-T-A** = Sangama – Saluva – Tuluva – Aravidu.

nindian-history-4-5.s: Which Vijayanagara dynasty came immediately after the Sangama dynasty?
nindian-history-4-5.x: The order of the four dynasties was Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu.
n: Harihara I and Bukka I established the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 AD. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
The Sangama dynasty was the first dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
The Vijayanagara Empire was ruled successively by the Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu dynasties. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 29-35]
xa: **Sangama** and **Aravidu** = Andhra origin (CDX).
The **Sangama** dynasty ruled longest; greatest king **Devaraya II**.

nindian-history-28-6.s: Who immediately succeeded Prauda Deva Raya?
nindian-history-28-6.x: Narasimha Saluva ended Sangama rule in 1485 by taking the throne from Prauda Deva Raya, the last Sangama king, and began the Saluva dynasty.
nindian-history-28-6.tq: Recall who ended the Sangama line.
n: The immediate successor of Prauda Deva Raya was Narasimha Saluva. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 94-95]
xs: **Narasimha Saluva** immediately succeeded **Praudha Raya** — so option **(2)** is correct.
In **1485** he expelled Praudha Raya, the **last Sangama** ruler, with **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka's** help — the **First Usurpation**.
**Vira Narasimha** came later (**1505**, Tuluva); **Krishnadevaraya** ruled **1509-29**; **Achyutaraya** was also Tuluva.
xa: Saluva Narasimha was lord of **Chandragiri**; clan from **Kalyana**.
**Annamacharya** (**1408-1503**) was his contemporary.
**Jaimini Bharatam** by **Pillalamarri Pinaveerabhadra** was dedicated to him.

nindian-history-68-12.s: What was the name of Krishnadeva Raya’s mother in whose honour Nagalapuram was founded?
nindian-history-68-12.x: Krishnadeva Raya founded Nagalapuram near Hampi in honour of his mother, Nagala Devi. Tirumala Devi and Chinna Devi were his queens.
n: Krishnadeva Raya founded Nagalapuram in honour or memory of his mother, Nagala Devi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 144-145]
xs: **Krishnadeva Raya** founded **Nagalapuram** in honour of his mother **Nagala Devi** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Nauraspur** is a township of **Ibrahim Adil Shah II**, not a person's name.
xa: Krishnadevaraya (**1509-29**) marked the empire's **zenith**.
**Paes** and **Barbosa** visited in his reign.
He retook **Raichur** (**1520**) and took **Gulbarga** (**1523**).

n6893b542f6b.s: In which year did Harihara I annex the Hoysala kingdom?
n6893b542f6b.x: Harihara I annexed the Hoysala kingdom in 1346 and the Kadambas in 1347; Udayagiri was taken by Bukka in 1343.
xa: **Ibn Battuta** visited in Harihara I's reign — the first foreign traveller.
Title: **Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati**.

neb37c01d42b.s: Which Sangama ruler took the title 'Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati'?
neb37c01d42b.x: Harihara I took this title; Bukka I was Vedamarga Pratishthapaka and Rajavyasa/Rajavalmiki were Harihara II's titles.
xa: ⚠ **Gajabetekara** = **Devaraya II**; **Dakshina Samudradhipati** = **Lakkanna Dandanayaka**.
**Harihara II** = **longest-reigning** Sangama king; **first to attack Sri Lanka**.
**Devaraya I** built a **dam on the Tungabhadra**.

n5817177f6e9.s: The Ganigitti Jain temple was built by:
n5817177f6e9.x: The Ganigitti Jain temple was built by Irugappa, minister of Harihara II; Bukka I completed the city and reconciled Jains and Vaishnavas.
xa: Bukka sent an **embassy to Ming China (1374)**.
He took **Srisailam** and **Dupadu**.

n0b7c0872c6d.x: Gajabetekara was Devaraya II's title; Harihara II, the longest-reigning Sangama king, bore Rajavyasa and Rajavalmiki.
xa: He was the **first to attack Sri Lanka**.
His minister was **Sayana**.

n2585226c6e7.s: Bukka I sent an embassy to the Ming emperor of China in which year?
n2585226c6e7.x: Bukka I sent an embassy to the Ming emperor in 1374.
n2585226c6e7.tq: Direct year recall using four distinct chronological values.
xs: **Bukka I** sent an embassy to the **Ming emperor of China** in **1374** — option **(2)**.
**1366** = Kampana overthrew Sambhuvaraya; **1424** = Kondaveedu annexed; **1443** = Abdur Razzaq's visit.
xa: Bukka's title: **Vedamarga Pratishthapaka**.
He patronised **Nachana Somana**.

n9256e652fa2.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler enrolled 10,000 Muslim soldiers and kept a Quran near his throne?
n9256e652fa2.x: Devaraya II enrolled Muslim soldiers, gave them jagirs and a mosque, kept a Quran near his throne and improved cavalry and archery.
xa: Titles: **Gajabetekara**, **Praudha Devaraya**, **Ilanti Raikonda**.
He was the **greatest** Sangama ruler (**1422-46**).

n60a63d00e19.s: Which of the following titles was NOT associated with Devaraya II?
n60a63d00e19.x: Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati was the title of Harihara I. Devaraya II was known as Gajabetekara, Praudha Devaraya and Ilanti Raikonda.
n60a63d00e19.tq: Find the title belonging to a different ruler.
xs: **Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati** is NOT Devaraya II's — option **(2)**; it was **Harihara I's**.
Devaraya II's titles: **Gajabetekara** (elephant hunter), **Praudha Devaraya**, **Ilanti Raikonda**.
xa: ⚠ **Dakshina Samudradhipati** = **Lakkanna Dandanayaka**.
Devaraya II wrote **Mahanataka Sudhanidhi**.

n86e034cd21a.s: In which year did Devaraya II annex Kondaveedu?
n86e034cd21a.x: Devaraya II annexed Kondaveedu in 1424; the Draksharama inscription recording his repulse of the Gajapatis is of 1444.
xa: He honoured **Srinatha** with a **kanakabhishekam** after he beat **Gauda Dindima**.
**Vinukonda Vallabharaya** (Kridabhiramam) was his governor of **Vinukonda**.

ne5eb5c066e1.s: Devaraya II's own literary work was:
ne5eb5c066e1.x: Devaraya II wrote Mahanataka Sudhanidhi; Navaratnamala was by Irugappa, minister of Harihara II.
xa: **Vinukonda Vallabharaya**, author of **Kridabhiramam**, was governor of **Vinukonda** under Devaraya II.
Devaraya II's titles: **Gajabetekara** (elephant hunter), **Praudha Devaraya**, **Ilanti Raikonda**.
Irugappa also built the **Ganigitti Jain temple**.

nbd7e846c76e.s: Devaraya I’s capture of southern Kondaveedu, including Motupalli, is recorded in which inscription?
nbd7e846c76e.x: Devaraya I’s capture of southern Kondaveedu, including Motupalli, is recorded in the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam.
nbd7e846c76e.tq: Match the specific inscription with the ruler’s territorial achievement.
xs: Devaraya I's capture of southern **Kondaveedu**, including **Motupalli**, is recorded in the **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** — option **(1)**.
The **Draksharama inscription** (**1444**) belongs to **Devaraya II**, recording help sent to **Rajahmundry** against the Gajapatis.
xa: Devaraya I also fought the **Kandukuru Reddis** and allied with the **Velamas** and **Kataya Vema**.
**Devaraya II** annexed **Kondaveedu** fully in **1424**.
Devaraya I gave his daughter to **Firoz Shah Bahmani** with **Bankapur** as dowry.

n15527032035.s: Which ruler is identified as the first Vijayanagara ruler to attack Sri Lanka?
n15527032035.x: Harihara II is identified as the first Vijayanagara ruler to attack Sri Lanka.
n15527032035.tq: Separate the first external attack from the foreign-traveller association and Andhra campaigns.
xs: **Harihara II** was the **first to attack Sri Lanka** — option **(1)**.
**Harihara I** was visited by **Ibn Battuta**; **Bukka I** sent the embassy to **Ming China (1374)**; **Devaraya II** received tribute from Sri Lanka via **Lakkanna Dandanayaka**.
xa: Harihara II (**1377-1404**) was the **longest-reigning** Sangama king; titles **Rajavyasa**, **Rajavalmiki**.
His minister **Sayana** wrote **Vedartha Prakasha**.
Last Sangama ruler: **Praudha Raya**.

na7e783608aa.s: Which foreign traveller is noted as the first to visit Vijayanagara, during the reign of Harihara I?
na7e783608aa.x: Ibn Battuta is listed as the first foreign traveller, in Harihara I's reign. Nicolo Conti came under Devaraya I/II, Abdur Razzaq under Devaraya II (1443) and Domingo Paes under Krishnadevaraya.
na7e783608aa.tq: Firsts: traveller Ibn Battuta (Harihara I); attack on Sri Lanka Harihara II.
xs: **Ibn Battuta** was the first foreign traveller, in **Harihara I's** reign — option **(2)**.
**Nicolo Conti** came under Devaraya I/II, **Abdur Razzaq** under **Devaraya II** (**1443**), **Domingo Paes** under **Krishnadevaraya**.
xa: Harihara I moved the capital from **Anegondi** to **Vijayanagara**; title **Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati**.
He annexed the **Hoysala** kingdom (**1346**) and the **Kadambas** (**1347**).
Vijayanagara was founded in **1336** on the **southern bank of the Tungabhadra**.

n9307e307f73.s: Who led the conquest of Madurai during the reign of Bukka I?
n9307e307f73.x: Kumara Kampana, son of Bukka I, overthrew Sambhuvaraya in 1366 and destroyed the Madurai Sultanate.
n9307e307f73.tq: Direct identification of the commander in a dynastic conquest.
xs: **Kumara Kampana**, Bukka I's son, led the **Madurai** conquest — option **(1)**.
He overthrew **Sambhuvaraya** (**1366**) and destroyed the **Madurai Sultanate**.
xa: General **Saluva Mangu** killed the Sultan — title "**Parapakshi Saluva**".
Kampana's wife **Gangadevi** wrote **Madhura Vijayam**.

neb32c9d2465.s: The title 'Parapakshi Saluva' was given to:
neb32c9d2465.x: General Saluva Mangu killed the Sultan of Madurai and received the title 'Parapakshi Saluva'.
xa: Saluva Mangu was an **ancestor of Saluva Narasimha**.
The campaign is told in **Madhura Vijayam** by **Gangadevi**.

nd3ba09b15ae.s: Sayana, the Vedic commentator, served as minister during the reign of:
nd3ba09b15ae.x: The Vedic commentaries begun under Bukka Raya I continued under Harihara II, whose minister Sayana was.
xa: Sayana's commentary: **Vedartha Prakasha**.
Bukka's title **Vedamarga Pratishthapaka** fits this Vedic patronage.

n08e9e104c47.s: Madhava, the minister and general associated with the conquest of Goa, was known by which title?
n08e9e104c47.x: Madhava was known by the title Bhuvanaikavira in connection with his military achievement and conquest of Goa.
n08e9e104c47.tq: Test the title–person association rather than the broader event.
xs: **Madhava**, minister/general who conquered **Goa**, was titled **"Bhuvanaikavira"** — option **(1)**.
He is distinct from **Madhava-Vidyaranya**, Advaita head of Sringeri; some notes merge the two.
xa: Goa was taken in **1366** and lost to the Bahmanis in **1472**.
Sayana and Madhava wrote **Vedic commentaries**.

n1912bbeae2f.s: Madhura Vijayam, the Sanskrit account of Kumara Kampana's southern campaign, was written by:
n1912bbeae2f.x: Gangadevi, wife of Kumara Kampana, wrote Madhura Vijayam on his campaign and the conquest of Madurai.
xa: She was a **disciple of Agastya**.
Kampana overthrew **Sambhuvaraya** in **1366**.

n382bb2ca39f.s: A Forgotten Empire: Vijayanagar is best described as which of the following?
o: A Sanskrit poem describing the conquest of Madurai
A Telugu account of the twelve Sangama kings
A Persian chronicle presenting the Bahmani view of the wars
An English translation of the accounts of Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz
n382bb2ca39f.x: Robert Sewell’s A Forgotten Empire: Vijayanagar is an English translation of the Portuguese accounts of Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz.
n382bb2ca39f.tq: Distinguish the nature and source-language tradition of the work from other historical sources.
xs: **A Forgotten Empire** is **Robert Sewell's** English translation of the accounts of **Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz** — option **(4)**.
The Sanskrit poem on Madurai's conquest is **Madhura Vijayam** by **Gangadevi**.
The list of **12 Sangama kings** is in **Virupakshaya Kalajnana**; the Bahmani view comes from **Ferishta**.
xa: Asked in APPSC G2 **2011** and **2017**.
**Paes** visited under **Krishnadevaraya**; **Nuniz** under **Achyutaraya**.
Sewell also records the **seven** founding traditions of Vijayanagara.

n624349c68bd.s: Which traveller described Vijayanagara's open diamond bazaars, its three hundred ports and the taxation of prostitution?
n624349c68bd.x: Abdur Razzaq described the open diamond bazaars, the large number of ports and the taxation of prostitution.
xa: He was the Persian envoy of **Shah Rukh**, **1443**, in **Devaraya II's** reign.
**Paes** and **Barbosa** came under **Krishnadevaraya**; **Nuniz** under **Achyutaraya**.

n77ea01f556c.s: Abdur Razzaq, who visited Vijayanagara in 1443 during the reign of Devaraya II, came as the envoy of:
n77ea01f556c.x: Abdur Razzaq was the Persian envoy of Shah Rukh and visited in 1443 under Devaraya II. Firuz Shah Bahmani fought Devaraya I; the Ming emperor received Bukka I's embassy (1374); the Portuguese came later, under the Tuluvas.
n77ea01f556c.tq: Razzaq - Persia - Shah Rukh - 1443 - Devaraya II.
xs: **Abdur Razzaq** came as the Persian envoy of **Shah Rukh** in **1443** — option **(1)**.
**Firuz Shah Bahmani** fought **Devaraya I** (War of the Goldsmith's Daughter), not Devaraya II.
The **Ming emperor of China** received **Bukka I's** embassy of **1374**.
xa: Abdur Razzaq described open **diamond bazaars**, **300 ports**, and a tax on prostitution.
Travellers by reign: **Paes** and **Barbosa** (Portugal) → **Krishnadevaraya**; **Nuniz** → **Achyutaraya**; **Cesare Federici** (Italy) → **Sadasivaraya**.
⚠ **Nicolo Conti**: APPSC G2 **2011** key places him under **Devaraya II**; some notes date his visit **1420-21** under **Devaraya I**.

n245ed06afba.s: Cesare Federici, the Italian traveller, was associated with the reign of which Vijayanagara ruler?
n245ed06afba.x: Cesare Federici visited Vijayanagara during the reign of Sadasivaraya.
n245ed06afba.tq: Use nationality and reign as a paired identification clue.
xs: **Cesare Federici** (Italy) visited in the reign of **Sadasivaraya** — option **(2)**.
**Devaraya II** received **Abdur Razzaq**; **Achyutaraya** received **Nuniz**; **Devaraya I** is linked in some notes to **Nicolo Conti**.
xa: Sadasivaraya (Tuluva) ruled with **Rama Raya** as regent; **Talikota (1565)** fell in his reign.
**Paes** and **Barbosa** came under **Krishnadevaraya**.
Order of dynasties: **Sangama – Saluva – Tuluva – Aravidu**.

nap-history-28-1.s: Marco Polo visited which Andhra port during the reign of Rudramadevi?
nap-history-28-1.x: Marco Polo visited Motupalli port under Rudramadevi.
n: Marco Polo visited Motupalli port in Andhra Desa during Rudramadevi’s rule. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 39-40]
Nicolo Conti visited South India during the reign of Devaraya I of the Vijayanagara Empire. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 39-40]
Nuniz visited the Vijayanagara Empire during the rule of Achyutadeva Raya. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 39-40]
Abdul Razzaq visited the court of Devaraya II. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 39-40]
xa: Abdur Razzaq was envoy of **Shah Rukh**, **1443**; noted **300 ports**.
⚠ Other notes say **Nuniz** was from **Portugal**.
**Cesare Federici** (Italy) visited under **Sadasivaraya**.
**Robert Sewell's** **A Forgotten Empire** used **Paes and Nuniz**.

n4d7406cd0e9.s: The principal bone of contention between the Vijayanagara and Bahmani kingdoms was the Raichur Doab, situated between which two rivers?
n4d7406cd0e9.x: The Raichur Doab, or Raichur Antarvedi, lies between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers and was the main cause of the recurring wars.
n4d7406cd0e9.tq: Test the geographical boundaries of a disputed region.
xs: The **Raichur Doab** lies between the **Krishna and Tungabhadra** — option **(1)**.
Also called the **Raichur Antarvedi**, it was the main cause of the Vijayanagara-Bahmani wars (APPSC G2 **2000**, **2003**; PYQ **2017**).
xa: The two kingdoms also fought over the **Krishna-Godavari delta** and **Marathwada**.
Key contested points: **Mudgal** and **Raichur**.
**Krishnadevaraya** retook Raichur in the **Gobburi/Raichur war (1520)** with Portuguese help.

nf4aa3bef68e.s: The Mudgal conflict of 1358, regarded as the first Indian war involving artillery, took place under:
nf4aa3bef68e.x: Bukka I took Mudgal in 1358 in a war noted as the first in India to involve artillery.
xa: In **1347**, the Bahmani general **Mubarak Khan** took land west of Raichur.
Under **Devaraya I**, the **"War of the Goldsmith's Daughter"** (Nehal of Mudgal) was fought against **Firuz Shah**.
**Devaraya II** fought two wars over **Mudgal**, **Raichur** and **Bijapur**.

ne1a476c7f4f.s: The 'War of the Goldsmith's Daughter' was fought between Devaraya I and:
ne1a476c7f4f.x: The war, over Nehal of Mudgal, was between Devaraya I and Firuz Shah Bahmani; Devaraya gave his daughter and Bankapur as dowry.
xa: The **Mudgal (1358)** war under **Bukka I** was the **first Indian war with artillery**.
Main bone of contention: the **Raichur Doab** between the **Krishna and Tungabhadra**.
**Nicolo Conti** visited Vijayanagara under Devaraya I (per some notes, **1420-21**).

n578c18dab8d.s: In which year did Krishnadevaraya retake Raichur in the Gobburi (Raichur) war?
n578c18dab8d.x: Krishnadevaraya retook Raichur in 1520 with Portuguese help and took Gulbarga in 1523.
xa: Krishnadevaraya (**1509-29**, Tuluva) marked the empire's **zenith**.
**Paes** and **Barbosa** (Portugal) visited during his reign.
The conflict ended at **Talikota (1565)**, where the Deccan sultanates defeated **Rama Raya**.

ncb67cb593d6.s: Who among the following was the author of Kridabhiramam and served as governor of Vinukonda under Devaraya II?
ncb67cb593d6.x: Vinukonda Vallabharaya wrote Kridabhiramam and was the governor of Vinukonda under Devaraya II.
ncb67cb593d6.tq: Link the author, work and office rather than confusing the poet with a military officer or ally.
xs: **Vinukonda Vallabharaya** wrote **Kridabhiramam** and was governor of **Vinukonda** under **Devaraya II** — option **(1)**.
**Srinatha** was the poet honoured with **kanakabhishekam**; **Mallappa Odayar** was sent to help **Rajahmundry**.
**Kataya Vema** was an ally of **Devaraya I**, not a governor-poet.
xa: Srinatha's kanakabhishekam followed his victory over **Gauda Dindima**.
Devaraya II's own work: **Mahanataka Sudhanidhi**.
⚠ **Gajabetekara** = Devaraya II; **Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati** = **Harihara I**.

nb2f53a94ddc.s: Annamacharya (1408-1503) is associated with the patronage of which Vijayanagara ruler, who was his contemporary?
nb2f53a94ddc.x: Annamacharya (1408–1503) was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha and is also placed in his court.
nb2f53a94ddc.tq: Use overlapping life dates to identify the contemporary ruler.
xs: **Annamacharya (1408-1503)** was a contemporary of **Saluva Narasimha** — option **(3)**.
Some notes even place him in Saluva Narasimha's **court** (PYQ **2011**).
xa: Saluva Narasimha seized the throne in **1485** from **Praudha Raya** — the **First Usurpation**.
He repelled a **Bahmani raid on Kanchi (1481)** and took the **Machilipatnam** area.
**Jaimini Bharatam** by **Pillalamarri Pinaveerabhadra** was dedicated to him.
nb2f53a94ddc.fixed: as worded, Devaraya I (r. 1406-22) was also a contemporary; ambiguous

nbb1a8167076.s: Rayavachakam, a source for Vijayanagara history, was written by:
xa: Other sources: **Kaifiyats** and foreign travellers; **Ferishta** gives the Bahmani view.
**Vidyaranya** wrote the **Vidyaranya Kalajnana**.
**The Aravidu Dynasty of Vijayanagara** is by **Father H. Heras**.

n1c7315ffeed.s: The mother tongue of the Tuluva ruling family was:
n1c7315ffeed.x: Kannada was the mother tongue of the Tuluva family, whose progenitor was Timmaraju; Telugu was nonetheless favoured at court.
xa: The name comes from **Tulunadu** (Mysore region), conquered by Harihara in **1342**.
Krishnadevaraya's reign (**1509-1529**) was the **golden age of Telugu literature**, the **Prabandha era**.
⚠ Founder in the key = **Vira Narasimha**, not **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka**.

naf6ddb05ad5.s: Who was the real ruler under Immadi Narasimha?
naf6ddb05ad5.x: Tuluva Narasa Nayaka, a Saluva general, was the real ruler under Immadi Narasimha.
naf6ddb05ad5.tq: Match the ruler with the political role actually held.
xs: **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka**, a Saluva general, was the real ruler under **Immadi Narasimha** — option **(3)**.
He died in **1503**; his son **Vira Narasimha** then killed Immadi Narasimha at **Penugonda** in **1505**.
xa: ⚠ Narasa Nayaka helped both usurpations: general in **1485**, father of the usurper in **1505**.
The APPSC key names **Vira Narasimha** the Tuluva founder (G2 **2002**).
**Saluva Narasimha** ruled **1485-91**.

n4b7c16f84ab.s: Who was the Prime Minister of Krishnadevaraya, popularly known as Appaji?
n4b7c16f84ab.x: Saluva Timmarusu, popularly known as Appaji, served as the Prime Minister of Krishnadevaraya.
xa: Timmarusu helped take **Kondaveedu** by splitting **Veerabhadra Gajapati's** army.
Krishnadevaraya was crowned on **8 Aug 1509** (Hampi inscription).
The Kalinga campaign ran **1513-1519**.

nb89da59de9a.s: Who made peace after Sadasiva and Rama Raya defeated Governor Martin de Souza for damaging temples?
nb89da59de9a.x: João de Castro made peace after the defeat of Martin de Souza, whose actions had included damaging temples.
nb89da59de9a.tq: Apply the wrong-person-with-the-deed trap to distinguish Portuguese governors and peace-makers.
xs: **Joao de Castro** made peace — option **(4)**.
**Sadasiva / Rama Raya** had defeated Governor **Martin de Souza** for damaging temples.
**Almeida** allied with **Vira Narasimha**; **Albuquerque** took Goa in **1510**; **Duarte Barbosa** visited Krishnadevaraya's court.
xa: **Aliya Rama Raya**, Krishnadevaraya's son-in-law of the **Aravidu** family, made **Sadasiva** a figurehead.
He killed **Salakam Tirumala** in **1543**.
His **divide and rule** policy united the Sultanates against him → **Talikota (1565)**.

n2948a3419df.s: Which Vijayanagara king was the only one crowned at Tirumala (Tirupati)?
n2948a3419df.x: Achyutaraya was crowned at Tirupati (and Srikalahasti); Nuniz visited during his reign.
xa: Achyutaraya ruled **1529-42**, named heir by **Krishnadevaraya**.
**Rama Raya** killed **Salakam Tirumala** in **1543**.

nbff0e8dff95.s: Aliya Rama Raya was related to Krishnadevaraya as his:
o: maternal uncle from the Gajapati family
younger brother from the Tuluva family
nbff0e8dff95.x: Aliya Rama Raya was Krishnadevaraya's son-in-law and belonged to the Aravidu family.
nbff0e8dff95.tq: Discriminate between relationship and dynastic affiliation rather than relying on the title alone.
xs: **Aliya Rama Raya** was Krishnadevaraya's **son-in-law from the Aravidu family** — option **(3)**.
The **Salakam** brothers were **Achyutaraya's** brothers-in-law.
xa: He killed **Salakam Tirumala** (**1543**) and made **Sadasiva** a figurehead king.
He used **divide and rule** against the Sultanates, which united against him.
He was beheaded at **Talikota** (January **1565**).

n27631ec3661.s: After Rama Raya was beheaded at Talikota (1565), Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to:
n27631ec3661.x: After Talikota, Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to Penukonda.
xa: Some notes say he was beheaded by **Hussain Nizam Shah**.
Talikota is also called **Rakshasi-Tangadi / Bannihatti**.

n13a72702111.s: The last ruler of the Tuluva dynasty was:
n13a72702111.x: Sadasiva was the last Tuluva ruler; the usurpations were by Saluva Narasimha (1485) and Vira Narasimha (1505).
xa: ⚠ **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka** helped both usurpations: general in **1485**, father of the usurper in **1505**.
Vira Narasimha killed **Immadi Narasimha** at **Penugonda**.
Saluva Narasimha was lord of **Chandragiri**, called **Raya Maharasu**.

nindian-history-28-7.s: In 1509 Krishnadeva Raya succeeded his half-brother:
nindian-history-28-7.x: Krishnadeva Raya succeeded Vira Narasimha, who began the Tuluva dynasty; the Saluva dynasty was founded by Narasimha Saluva.
n: The immediate successor of Vira Narasimha was Krishnadeva Raya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 94-95]
xa: Vira Narasimha killed **Immadi Narasimha** at **Penugonda** in **1505** — the **second usurpation**.
Founder of Tuluva = **Vira Narasimha** (APPSC G2 **2002**).
⚠ **Tuluva Narasa Nayaka** helped both usurpations but is not the keyed founder.

nd253805052b.s: Which campaign resulted in the defeat of Yusuf Adil Khan?
nd253805052b.x: During the Diwani or Kovilkonda campaign of 1509–10, the Bahmani jihad was crushed and Yusuf Adil Khan was killed.
nd253805052b.tq: Match the military result with the correct campaign.
xs: **Yusuf Adil Khan** was killed in the **Diwani / Kovilkonda** campaign (**1509-10**) — option **(1)**; the Bahmani "jihad" was crushed.
**Udayagiri**, **Kondaveedu** and **Simhachalam** belong to the **Kalinga campaign (1513-1519)** against the Gajapatis.
xa: ⚠ **Yusuf Adil Khan** killed at Kovilkonda; **Ismail Adil Shah** routed at **Raichur (1520)**.
**Raichur Doab (1510)**: Raichur taken; freed **Sultan Mahmud Shah** from **Ali Barid**.
Ummattur / Sivasamudram (**1512-13**): **Gangaraja** defeated.

n6872687a9bd.s: The title “Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya” was associated with Krishnadevaraya’s:
n6872687a9bd.x: After taking Raichur and freeing Sultan Mahmud Shah from Ali Barid, Krishnadevaraya acquired the title Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya.
n6872687a9bd.tq: Link an honorific title with the event that produced it.
xs: The title came from the **Raichur and Bidar** campaign (**1510**) — option **(4)**: he freed **Sultan Mahmud Shah** from **Ali Barid**.
**Ummattur** defeated **Gangaraja**; **Udayagiri** and the **Kalinga campaign** were against the Gajapatis.
xa: The title **Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya** is celebrated in **Manucharitra**.
Other titles: **Andhra Bhoja**, **Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma**, **Kannada Rajya Rama Ramana**, **Gajapati Gajakuta Pakaveni**.
Raichur was again won in **1520**, routing **Ismail Adil Shah** with **Portuguese** help.

nd28c668cf76.s: During Krishnadevaraya's Kalinga campaign, Udayagiri fell after a siege of about:
nd28c668cf76.x: Udayagiri fell after an 18-month siege in the Kalinga campaign of 1513-1519.
xa: Aim: win back **Tirandhra** and **Telangana** from **Prataparudra Gajapati**.
Telangana forts taken: **Devarakonda, Nalgonda, Kambhamettu, Jallipalli and Warangal**.
Victory pillars: **Potnuru** and **Simhachalam**.

n51a76f4d225.s: After the conquest of Udayagiri, which idol was taken to Hampi?
n51a76f4d225.x: Krishnadevaraya brought the Balakrishna idol from Udayagiri to Hampi, where the Krishna temple was built for it.
n51a76f4d225.tq: Use the deity–campaign association to separate three Narasimha-related locations.
xs: The **Balakrishna idol** was taken from **Udayagiri** to **Hampi** — option **(3)**, for the **Krishna temple**.
**Varaha Narasimha** (Simhachalam) got a **diamond necklace**; **Lakshmi Narasimha** (Mangalagiri) got land.
xa: Udayagiri (**1513-14**) fell after an **18-month siege**.
Udayagiri had earlier been lost by **Saluva Narasimha** to Gajapati **Purushottama**.
After **Kondaveedu**, the king performed **Talapurusha Danam** at **Amaravati**.

n133799af429.s: In the Raichur campaign of 1520, Krishnadevaraya routed:
n133799af429.x: Ismail Adil Shah was defeated in 1520 with Portuguese help.
xa: ⚠ **Yusuf Adil Khan** was killed earlier, at **Kovilkonda (1509-10)**.
Raichur had first been taken in **1510**, when **Sultan Mahmud Shah** was freed from **Ali Barid**.
In **1510** Krishnadevaraya backed **Albuquerque's** capture of **Goa** through envoy **Luis**.

n576979a1790.s: For his support to Albuquerque in capturing Goa, Krishnadevaraya permitted the Portuguese to build a fort at:
n576979a1790.x: Krishnadevaraya received horses and military training and allowed the Portuguese a fort at Bhatkal.
xa: Goa was captured by **Albuquerque** from **Bijapur** in **1510**, through envoy **Luis**.
Bhatkal had earlier been taken by **Saluva Narasimha**.

n116e96994be.s: Which one of the following was NOT a title of Krishnadevaraya?
n116e96994be.x: Andhra Bhoja, Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma and Kannada Rajya Rama Ramana were titles of Krishnadevaraya. Gajabetekara (elephant hunter) was the title of the Sangama ruler Devaraya II.
n116e96994be.tq: Gajabetekara = Devaraya II; Andhra Bhoja = Krishnadevaraya.
xs: **Gajabetekara** was not Krishnadevaraya's title — option **(4)**; it means "elephant hunter" and belongs to **Devaraya II**.
**Andhra Bhoja**, **Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma** and **Kannada Rajya Rama Ramana** are his titles.
xa: **Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya**: for restoring the Bahmani Sultan; celebrated in **Manucharitra**.
Others: **Gajapati Gajakuta Pakaveni**, **Dakshinapatha Swami**, **Mururaya Raganda**, **Paribhuta Suratrana**.

o: One who wears the garland of victory
One who offers the garland she has worn
One who conquers the garlanded city
One who worships Vishnu with flowers
n99a3b30d683.x: Amuktamalyada means “one who offers the garland she has worn,” referring to the devotional story associated with Goda Devi or Andal.
n99a3b30d683.tq: Test the exact meaning of a title rather than its broad theme.
xs: Amuktamalyada means **"one who offers the garland she has worn"** — option **(2)**.
It tells the story of **Goda Devi (Andal)** and her marriage to **Sri Ranganatha**.
xa: Also called **Vishnuchittiyam**; written in **Telugu**.
It is the **first Telugu work named after its heroine**.
One of the **Telugu Pancha Kavyas**.

nf6e221d34cb.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the locations of Krishnadevaraya’s victory pillars?
nf6e221d34cb.x: Victory pillars were erected at Potnuru and Simhachalam after the Kalinga campaign. The pillar at Potnuru marked the conquest of coastal Andhra.
nf6e221d34cb.tq: Use location-based discrimination among campaign and religious centres.
xs: Victory pillars stood at **Potnuru and Simhachalam** — option **(3)**.
PYQ **2025**: the pillar marking the conquest of coastal Andhra = **Potnuru**.
**Amaravati** saw **Talapurusha Danam**; **Mangalagiri** got a land grant; **Udayagiri** and **Kondaveedu** were forts taken.
xa: **Simhachalam**: a **diamond necklace** to **Varaha Narasimha**.
The Kalinga campaign ran **1513-1519**; **Cuttack** reached in **1518**.
AP angle: **Udayagiri, Kondaveedu, Kondapalli** forts of the campaign lie in AP.

na28a658ff3b.s: After the Kalinga campaign, Krishnadevaraya married the daughter of:
na28a658ff3b.x: Prataparudra Gajapati gave his daughter to Krishnadevaraya, and lands north of the Krishna went back to the Gajapati.
xa: Her name: **Annapurnadevi** (some notes) vs **Bhadradevi (Tukka / Jaganmohini)**.
The campaign reached **Cuttack** in **1518**, when the Gajapati sued for peace.
Aim: win back **Tirandhra** and **Telangana**.

n78c67366166.s: Vira Narasimha entered into an alliance with which Portuguese Viceroy for securing horses and military training?
n78c67366166.x: Vira Narasimha allied with Viceroy Francisco de Almeida for horses and military training.
n78c67366166.tq: Identify the person directly associated with the stated diplomatic and military arrangement.
xs: **Vira Narasimha** allied with Viceroy **Francisco de Almeida** for **horses** and **military training** — option **(2)**.
**Albuquerque** was backed by **Krishnadevaraya** in taking **Goa (1510)**; **Joao de Castro** made peace with Sadasiva/Rama Raya; **Duarte Barbosa** was a visitor.
xa: ⚠ **Almeida** = Vira Narasimha; **Albuquerque** = Krishnadevaraya.
In return for Goa, the Portuguese supplied **horses** and were allowed a fort at **Bhatkal**.
Portuguese help counted at **Raichur (1520)**.

n8af692a917f.s: The Bhuvana Vijayam mentioned in accounts of Krishnadevaraya’s court was also called the:
n8af692a917f.x: Bhuvana Vijayam is identified as the House of Victory and formed part of the royal courtly setting described by travellers.
n8af692a917f.tq: Test an alternative name rather than asking for the traveller’s identity.
xs: Bhuvana Vijayam was also called the **"House of Victory"** — option **(2)**, as described by **Domingo Paes**.
It literally means **"conquest of the world"** and was where the **Ashtadiggajas** met.
xa: Paes's account was asked in APPSC G2 **2019**.
Paes also described the palace, festivals, army and markets.
⚠ **Nuniz** visited under **Achyutaraya**, not Krishnadevaraya.

n4b2c0b11fa6.x: It was written during the Kalinga campaign after Andhra Mahavishnu of Srikakulam commanded him in a dream; it is dedicated to Lord Venkateswara.
xa: Its subject: **Goda Devi (Andal)** and her marriage to **Sri Ranganatha**.
It describes **Villiputtur** and **Madhura**.
AP angle: **Srikakulam** (Krishna district) is linked to the work.

n26c9a484ca2.s: The phrase “Desa Bhashalandu Telugu Lessa” occurs in which work?
n26c9a484ca2.x: The famous expression praising Telugu among regional languages occurs in the preface to Amuktamalyada.
n26c9a484ca2.tq: Match a famous quotation with its exact literary source.
xs: **"Desa Bhashalandu Telugu Lessa"** is in the preface of **Amuktamalyada** — option **(1)**.
It means **"Telugu is the best of the regional languages"**.
**Jambavati Kalyanam** and **Madalasa Charita** are Krishnadevaraya's **Sanskrit** works; **Madhura Vijayam** is Gangadevi's.
xa: Amuktamalyada is **Telugu**, one of the **Telugu Pancha Kavyas**.
⚠ Only **Amuktamalyada** is Telugu among his works.

nf8d7c8264dc.s: Amuktamalyada, one of the Telugu Pancha Kavyas, is the first Telugu work named after its:
nf8d7c8264dc.x: It is named after its heroine, Goda Devi, not its author.
xa: Its title means **"one who offers the garland she has worn"**.
Also called **Vishnuchittiyam**; dedicated to **Lord Venkateswara**.

n5e45ea1776f.x: Madalasa Charita, Rasamanjari, Jnana Chintamani and Satyavadhu Parinayam are Sanskrit; Amuktamalyada is his only Telugu work.
xa: **Jambavati Kalyanam** is a Sanskrit drama (PYQ **2019**).
Court poets (**Ashtadiggajas**) wrote in **Telugu**.
**Sakala Katha Sara Sangrahamu** is also listed as Sanskrit.

nd6cc8218363.s: Krishnadevaraya's drama Jambavati Kalyanam, which mentions Virupaksha and the Vasantotsavams, was written in:
nd6cc8218363.x: Jambavati Kalyanam is a Sanskrit drama (APPSC G2 2019). Telugu is wrong - his Telugu work is Amuktamalyada. Kannada and Tamil are wrong - none of his listed works are in these languages.
nd6cc8218363.tq: Only Amuktamalyada is Telugu; the rest of KDR's works are Sanskrit.
xs: **Jambavati Kalyanam** is a drama in **Sanskrit** — option **(2)** (APPSC G2 **2019**).
**Telugu** is wrong: Krishnadevaraya's only Telugu work is **Amuktamalyada**.
None of his listed works is in **Kannada** or **Tamil**.
xa: The drama mentions **Virupaksha** and the **Vasantotsavams**.
Other Sanskrit works: **Usha Parinayam**, **Madalasa Charita**, **Rasamanjari**, **Jnana Chintamani**, **Satyavadhu Parinayam**.
Amuktamalyada's preface: **"Desa Bhashalandu Telugu Lessa"**.

n9bcb8aeea4b.s: The Ashtadiggajas, the eight pillar-poets of Bhuvana Vijayam, were patronised by:
n9bcb8aeea4b.x: Their patron was Krishnadevaraya (APPSC G2 2019), not Achyutaraya.
xa: The **Tippalur inscription** calls them **"Kavula Samstha"** and records the gift of **Tippalur agrahara** (Kadapa).
**Bhuvana Vijayam** means **"conquest of the world"**.
**Allasani Peddana** was titled **Andhra Kavita Pitamaha**.

nc4386ce94e3.s: The dvyarthi kavya (poem with double meaning) is associated with:
nc4386ce94e3.x: Dvyarthi kavya is associated with Pingali Surana; Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu wrote Ramabhyudayamu.
xa: Mallana's work: **Rajasekhara Charitramu**.
Tenali Ramakrishna wrote **Panduranga Mahatmyamu**.

n348bc92e5b7.s: Which of the following is NOT a title associated with Krishnadevaraya?
n348bc92e5b7.x: Andhra Kavita Pitamaha was the title conferred on Allasani Peddana. The other three are titles of Krishnadevaraya.
n348bc92e5b7.tq: Separate the ruler's titles from an honorific belonging to his court poet.
xs: **Andhra Kavita Pitamaha** was not Krishnadevaraya's title — option **(2)**; it was conferred on **Allasani Peddana** (APPSC G2 **2019**).
**Mururaya Raganda**, **Sahiti Samarangana Sarvabhauma** and **Andhra Bhoja** are Krishnadevaraya's titles.
xa: The king himself fixed the **Gandapenderam** anklet on Peddana's foot.
Peddana wrote **Manucharitramu (Swarochisha Manu Sambhavam)**.
Other royal titles: **Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya**, **Kannada Rajya Rama Ramana**, **Dakshinapatha Swami**.

ncc11a3e33dd.s: What special honour did Krishnadevaraya himself bestow on Allasani Peddana?
o: He appointed him governor of Chandragiri.
He fixed the Gandapenderam anklet on Peddana's foot.
He made him commander of the Arab cavalry.
ncc11a3e33dd.x: Krishnadevaraya personally fixed the Gandapenderam anklet on Allasani Peddana's foot.
ncc11a3e33dd.tq: Recall a distinctive ceremonial act instead of a general patronage relationship.
xs: Krishnadevaraya himself **fixed the Gandapenderam anklet on Peddana's foot** — option **(2)**.
**Vasucharitra** was by **Ramarajabhushana**, dedicated to **Tirumala Raya** — not to Peddana.
xa: Peddana bore the title **Andhra Kavita Pitamaha** (APPSC G2 **2019**).
His main work: **Manucharitramu (Swarochisha Manu Sambhavam)**.
**Manucharitra** celebrates the king's title **Yavana Rajya Sthapanacharya**.

ne621aaf2c41.s: Which Ashtadiggaja poet, titled 'Andhra Kavita Pitamaha', wrote Manucharitramu?
ne621aaf2c41.x: Allasani Peddana wrote Manucharitramu (Swarochisha Manu Sambhavam) and was titled Andhra Kavita Pitamaha.
xa: The king fixed the **Gandapenderam** anklet on Peddana's foot.
**Dhurjati**: **Sri Kalahastiswara Satakam** and **Mahatmyam**.
**Madayyagari Mallana**: **Rajasekhara Charitramu**.

ndb371849fca.s: Which foreign traveller, besides Domingo Paes, is associated with a visit to Krishnadevaraya’s court?
ndb371849fca.x: Barbosa also visited the court of Krishnadevaraya; Domingo Paes described the Bhuvana Vijayam or House of Victory and the king.
ndb371849fca.tq: Distinguish travellers associated with the Vijayanagara court from travellers of other periods.
xs: **Barbosa** (**Duarte Barbosa**) also visited Krishnadevaraya's court — option **(4)**.
**Domingo Paes** described the **Bhuvana Vijayam / "House of Victory"** and the king.
xa: **Fernao Nuniz** wrote on the king's rise but visited under **Achyutaraya**.
**Babur** praised Krishnadevaraya in the **Tuzuk-i-Baburi**.
Paes and Barbosa were **Portuguese**.

n5f5c6ca4a65.s: Which foreign traveller described the looks of Krishnadevaraya and the beauty of the city?
n5f5c6ca4a65.x: Domingo Paes described Krishnadevaraya's appearance and the beauty of the city. Duarte Barbosa also visited Vijayanagara, but the stated description is attributed to Paes.
n5f5c6ca4a65.tq: Distinguish the visitor who made a particular observation from other foreign visitors to Vijayanagara.
xs: **Domingo Paes** described the king's **looks** and the **city's beauty** — option **(1)**.
**Fernao Nuniz** wrote on the king's **rise to power** (visiting under **Achyutaraya**); **Babur** praised him in the **Tuzuk-i-Baburi**; **Duarte Barbosa** simply visited his court.
xa: Paes also called the Bhuvana Vijayam the **"House of Victory"** (PYQ **2019**).
Paes described the palace, festivals, army and markets.

n7f67a23063e.s: Who praised Krishnadevaraya in the Tuzuk-i-Baburi?
n7f67a23063e.x: Babur praised Krishnadevaraya in the Tuzuk-i-Baburi.
n7f67a23063e.tq: Match the historical work with its author rather than with a contemporary European traveller.
xs: **Babur** praised Krishnadevaraya in the **Tuzuk-i-Baburi** — option **(4)**.
**Paes** described the king and his court; **Nuniz** wrote of his rise to power.
xa: **Duarte Barbosa** also visited his court.
⚠ **Nuniz** visited under **Achyutaraya**.
Krishnadevaraya's reign (**1509-1529**) was the golden age of Telugu literature.
