ne3ddf942cce.s: The Sirimanu utsavam is the chief ritual of which festival?
ne3ddf942cce.x: Sirimanu utsavam belongs to Paidithalli Ammavaru of Vizianagaram, not the Gangamma Jatara of Tirupati.
xa: **Mahanandi** (Nandyal district) has a **Shivaratri** fair.
**Kotappakonda Jatra** lies in the Guntur region, now **Palnadu**.
**Tappeta Gullu** dancers also appease **Gangamma** while invoking rain.

n5c9a0aa89a6.s: In Andhra folk culture, 'Jola patalu' are:
xa: Gangamma Jatara: **nine days**, **Perantalu Vesham**, **Chapparalu**.
Paidithalli Ammavaru is known for the **Sirimanu utsavam**.
Mahanandi lies in **Nandyal district**.

nc9a1b70f57c.s: Narasapur in Andhra Pradesh is known for:
nc9a1b70f57c.x: Narasapur is known for crochet lace; Eluru for carpets, Udayagiri for wooden cutlery and Etikoppaka for lacquerware toys.
xa: Eluru carpet designs **Farishkhani and Ashunkhani** drew attention at the **London Exhibition, 1851**.
Etikoppaka toys are **GI-tagged**, from **Anakapalli** district.
A **90-foot** Etikoppaka installation stands at the new **Bhogapuram** airport (**2 Aug 2026**).
nc9a1b70f57c.fixed: stem said 'which one pair' but options are combinations

nb3ece7e2d49.s: The Eluru carpet designs 'Farishkhani' and 'Ashunkhani' attracted attention at the:
nb3ece7e2d49.x: Farishkhani and Ashunkhani, designs of Eluru carpets, attracted attention at the London Exhibition of 1851.
xa: APPSC-GS **2025** key: carpets-**Eluru**, cutlery-**Udayagiri**, crochet-**Narasapur**, lacquerware-**Etikoppaka**.
**Dharmavaram** sarees are GI-tagged.
**Budithi** (Srikakulam) is known for **bell metal**.

nb8b643606fe.s: GI-tagged Etikoppaka lacquerware toys belong to which district?
nb8b643606fe.x: Etikoppaka is in Anakapalli district, not Guntur.
xa: Kondapalli toys and Dharmavaram sarees are exported via **Lepakshi (APHDC)**'s e-commerce portal (Mar **2026**).
⚠ Kalamkari: **Srikalahasti** = pen; **Machilipatnam-Pedana** = block.

n5ca8205feb1.s: The Machilipatnam-Pedana Kalamkari tradition is known for:
n5ca8205feb1.x: Machilipatnam-Pedana Kalamkari is block-printed, while Srikalahasti is known for pen or freehand Kalamkari.
xa: Srikalahasti is also called **Dakshina Kailasam**.
**Kondapalli toys** are made of light **Tella Poniki** wood.
**Budithi** (Srikakulam) is known for **bell metal**.

n40c2267770c.s: Which of the following is an Andhra Pradesh craft tradition rather than a Telangana one?
n40c2267770c.x: Dharmavaram sarees are an Andhra Pradesh tradition; Bidri, Cherial scrolls and Nirmal paintings are associated with Telangana.
xa: Telangana crafts also include **banjara needle craft** and **dokra metal craft**.
APPSC-GS **2022** key: the craft NOT traditional to AP = **Bidri work**.
Dharmavaram sarees are exported via **Lepakshi (APHDC)**'s portal.

n173339fa171.s: The first book on the theory of folk knowledge in Telugu was written by:
n173339fa171.x: It was written by Biruduraju Ramaraju; Annamacharya wrote Kolatam kirtanas.
xa: **World Folk Day** is **22 August**.
**Jola patalu** = lullabies.
The **Gathasaptasati** records couple and choir dances of rural folk.

na31efb1062f.s: At the time of Talikota, who was the Tuluva king of Vijayanagara with Aliya Rama Raya as regent?
na31efb1062f.x: Sadasiva Raya was the nominal Tuluva king and Rama Raya his regent.
xa: Rama Raya was **captured and killed**; **Venkatadri** was also killed.
**Sadashiva and Tirumala** fled to **Penukonda**.
Last Tuluva ruler = **Sadasiva**; first Aravidu = **Tirumala**.

n79bb8b4eae1.s: Berar, the Deccan Sultanate that stayed out of the alliance against Vijayanagara at Talikota, was ruled by the:
n79bb8b4eae1.x: Berar was ruled by the Imad Shahis and stayed out; Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar formed the alliance.
xa: **Ibrahim Qutb Shah** of Golconda organised the alliance.
Vijayanagara faced the **Deccan Sultanates**, not the Bahmani kingdom (G1 **2018**).

n04386d9562e.s: In the Battle of Talikota (1565), the Vijayanagara Empire fought against
o: A confederacy of the Deccan Sultanates
n04386d9562e.x: Vijayanagara under Aliya Rama Raya fought the confederacy of the Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar). The Bahmani kingdom had already broken up into these Sultanates, so 'Bahmani' is a common trap. The Mughals and the Gajapatis were not parties to the battle.
xs: At Talikota, Vijayanagara fought **a confederacy of the Deccan Sultanates** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Trap: it was **NOT the Bahmani kingdom** (G1 **2018**; UPPSC **2014**).
Members: **Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar**.
xa: Vijayanagara's de-facto ruler was **Aliya Rama Raya**, regent of **Sadasiva Raya**.
Date: **23 January 1565**.
After victory, the Sultanates **went back to fighting each other**.

n7197e4334ad.s: Jagadeva Rao, whose sheltering by Rama Raya helped provoke the Deccan coalition, was a rebel from:
n7197e4334ad.x: Rama Raya sheltered Jagadeva Rao, a rebel from Golconda, one of the causes of the coalition.
xa: Marriage links: **Bibi Jamal** married Ibrahim; **Chand Bibi** married Ali Adil.
**Ferishta** also alleges religious insults.
Rama Raya **sacked Ahmadnagar** in **1557-63**.

n1f06517c2e7.s: In 1546-47, by backing Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar, Rama Raya acquired the:
n1f06517c2e7.x: In 1546-47 Rama Raya supported Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar and took the Raichur doab.
xa: This **divide-and-rule** diplomacy is listed as a cause that **united the Sultans** against him.
Rama Raya had earlier served under **Golconda** and the **Bahmanis**.
He also sheltered **Jagadeva Rao**, a rebel from Golconda.

n88eca6c8f17.s: Who was the key organiser of the Deccan Sultanates' alliance that fought at Talikota (1565)?
n88eca6c8f17.x: Ibrahim Qutb Shah of Golconda was the key organiser of the coalition.
xa: **Robert Sewell** called it **Talikota**; **Fr. Heras** and **Nilakanta Sastri** called it **Rakshasi-Tangadi**.
Date: **23 January 1565**; some notes give **26 January**.
**Ali Adil Shah** ruled **Bijapur**; **Ali Barid Shah** ruled **Bidar**.
⚠ **Berar** (Imad Shahi) stayed out of the battle.

n48e9796e37a.s: Among the marriage alliances before Talikota, Chand Bibi was married to:
n48e9796e37a.x: Chand Bibi married Ali Adil Shah, while Bibi Jamal married Ibrahim Qutb Shah.
xa: Rama Raya sheltered **Jagadeva Rao**, a rebel from Golconda.
In **1546-47** he took the **Raichur doab**.

nf4aa43a0555.s: After the Battle of Talikota, Hampi was looted for about:
nf4aa43a0555.x: Hampi was looted for about six months; the damage was severe but not total.
xa: Sewell's **"graveyard"** account may exaggerate.
Golconda gained **Kondavidu and Machilipatnam** + coastal tracts.
Sadashiva and Tirumala fled to **Penukonda**.

n86965a2599f.s: After the defeat at Talikota, Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to:
n86965a2599f.x: They fled to Penukonda; Chandragiri became a capital later, under Venkata II.
xa: Capital order: **Penukonda (1570) → Chandragiri → Vellore (1600)**.
After **1565**, the empire's centre moved into AP.
**Sriranga Raya I** later lost **Kondaveedu** to Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

nc1d6fd7509b.s: The Aravidu dynasty was the ____ ruling dynasty of Vijayanagara.
nc1d6fd7509b.x: The Aravidu dynasty was the fourth dynasty of Vijayanagara and ruled from 1570 to 1680 with seven rulers.
xa: Some notes date the empire's end to **1646**.
Founder **Tirumala** shifted the capital to **Penukonda** in **1570**.
Greatest ruler: **Venkatapati Raya II** (**1585-1614**).

n8d8a13edb28.s: Who founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at Penukonda in 1570?
n8d8a13edb28.x: Tirumala Raya founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at Penukonda in 1570.
n8d8a13edb28.tq: Match the founder with his accession place and year.
xs: **Tirumala Raya** founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at **Penukonda** in **1570** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Sriranga Raya I** (**1572-85**) succeeded him; **Venkatapati Raya II** (**1585-1614**) was the greatest.
**Ramadeva** (**1616-30**) fought the **Battle of Toppur**.
xa: Tirumala was crowned at the age of **90**.
He wrote a commentary on the **Gita Govinda**; **Vasucharitra** was dedicated to him.
⚠ **Tirumala Raya** = Aravidu founder; **Tirumala Nayaka** = Madurai.

n1ca3254af08.s: The Vilapakam inscription of 1601 is important primarily because it provides information about the genealogy of which dynasties?
n1ca3254af08.x: The Vilapakam inscription of 1601 gives the genealogy of the Tuluva and Aravidu dynasties.
n1ca3254af08.tq: Identify the inscription through its specific genealogical content.
xs: The **Vilapaka(m) inscription (1601)** gives the genealogy of the **Tuluva and Aravidu** dynasties — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is an inscription of **Venkatapati Raya II**.
xa: ⚠ Vilapaka = Venkatapati II's (**1601**); **Siddhavatam** fort inscription = Venkatapati II's (**1605**).
The Siddhavatam inscription says **Matli Ananta** built the fort walls.
His Penukonda inscription records villages given to the saint **Babanathu**.

nc00cfe025c2.s: Venkatapati Raya II permitted the Dutch to trade at:
nc00cfe025c2.x: Venkatapati Raya II permitted Dutch trade at Pulicat and also allowed Jesuit churches at Nellore and Chandragiri.
xa: His coins bore **"Om Venkateshwaraya Namah"**.
He gave villages to the Muslim saint **Babanathu**.

nddb62d251c4.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler was called the 'Second Andhra Bhoja'?
nddb62d251c4.x: Venkatapati Raya II was called the 'Second Andhra Bhoja' (and 'Second Krishnadevaraya').
xa: He is also called the **"Second Krishnadevaraya"**.

n474cfc53984.s: Shaivarka Mani Dipika was written by:
n474cfc53984.x: Shaivarka Mani Dipika is the work of Appayya Dikshita; Vasucharitra is associated with Ramaraja Bhushanudu.
xa: Appayya Dikshita was at **Venkatapati Raya II**'s court.
**Vasucharitra** was dedicated to **Tirumala Raya**, the Aravidu founder.
**A Forgotten Empire** (**1900**) by **Robert Sewell** brought Vijayanagara to wide notice.

n1e57df90199.s: Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka granted Madras to Francis Day in 1639 during the reign of which Vijayanagara ruler?
n1e57df90199.x: The 1639 grant of Madras to Francis Day of the Machilipatnam council came in the reign of Venkatapati Raya III.
xa: Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka was the **Kalahasti-Wandiwash** chief.
⚠ Some notes give the grant date as **1630**.
**Sriranga Raya III** (1643-80) was the **last** Aravidu ruler.

nf1c3ce29797.s: Which pair of leaders won the Battle of Toppur in 1616?
o: Velugoti Yachama Nayaka and Raghunatha of Tanjore
Mir Jumla and Sriranga Raya III
Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka and Veerappa Nayaka
nf1c3ce29797.x: Velugoti Yachama Nayaka and Raghunatha of Tanjore won the Battle of Toppur in 1616.
nf1c3ce29797.tq: Start with the battle year and match the associated victorious commanders.
xs: **Velugoti Yachama Nayaka** and **Raghunatha of Tanjore** won **Toppur (1616)** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Jagga Raya** was killed there; it is called the **"second Talikota"**.
**Mir Jumla** defeated **Sriranga III** at **Vandavasi (1642)**, a different battle.
xa: Toppur came in **Ramadeva**'s reign (**1616-30**).
Jagga Raya had killed **Sriranga II** in **1614**.
**Tanjore** was founded by **Sevappa Nayaka**.

na69552f26e0.s: The Nayaka kingdom of Tanjore was founded by:
na69552f26e0.x: Tanjore was founded by Sevappa Nayaka; Madurai by Vishwanatha Nayaka, Gingee by Krishnappa Nayaka and Mysore by Raja Wodeyar.
xa: Raja Wodeyar took **Srirangapatna** in **1610**.
**Ikkeri (Keladi)** was founded by **Chowdappa Nayaka**.
Madurai fell to **Chanda Sahib** in **1739**.

n3ec8b5db5ec.s: Vishwanatha Nayaka was granted Madurai after capturing his rebel father, ____.
n3ec8b5db5ec.x: Vishwanatha Nayaka captured his rebel father Nagama and was granted Madurai; his son Krishnappa Nayaka made it independent c. 1565.
xa: Tirumala Nayaka allied with **Golconda** and built the **Tirumala Rayala Mahal**.
Madurai's contemporary rulers: **Krishnadevaraya** / Achyutaraya.
Madurai fell to **Chanda Sahib** in **1739**.

n17da0502d30.s: The Tirumala Rayala Mahal at Madurai was built by:
n17da0502d30.x: Tirumala Nayaka, who ruled Madurai from 1623 to 1659, built the Tirumala Rayala Mahal.
xa: ⚠ **Tirumala Raya** = Aravidu founder (Penukonda); **Tirumala Nayaka** = Madurai.
**Krishnappa** made Madurai independent c. **1565**.

ne985d3976ed.s: After Vijayanagara weakened, the amara-nayakas became hereditary ____, the forerunners of the zamindars.
ne985d3976ed.x: The amara-nayakas developed into hereditary Palegars, who were the forerunners of the zamindars.
xa: After Talikota, the **Nayakas** became autonomous → later **zamindars and poligars**.
Local Nayaka **Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka** granted **Madras** to the English.
**Velugoti Yachama Nayaka** won the Battle of **Toppur (1616)**.

n8516e320d83.s: At Gandikota in 1657, who is recorded as having melted temple idols into cannon?
n8516e320d83.x: Mir Jumla of Golconda is recorded as having melted temple idols into cannon at Gandikota in 1657.
n8516e320d83.tq: Link the place and year with the named military commander.
xs: **Mir Jumla of Golconda** melted temple idols into cannon at **Gandikota** in **1657** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Jagga Raya** was killed at **Toppur**; **Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka** granted **Madras**; **Raghunatha of Tanjore** won Toppur.
xa: Mir Jumla defeated **Sriranga III** at **Vandavasi (1642)**.
Sriranga III died in **1680**, ending the empire.
Gandikota was a Vijayanagara fort.

nb50cee96d7c.s: Who surveyed and mapped the ruins of Hampi in 1800?
nb50cee96d7c.x: Colin Mackenzie surveyed and mapped the Hampi ruins in 1800 and later became the first Surveyor General of India.
nb50cee96d7c.tq: Associate the survey date with the correct investigator.
xs: **Colin Mackenzie** surveyed and mapped the Hampi ruins in **1800** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He later became the first **Surveyor General of India**.
**Robert Sewell** wrote **A Forgotten Empire** (**1900**); **Caesar Frederick** visited in **1567**; **Mir Jumla** was a Golconda general.
xa: Caesar Frederick was a **Venetian merchant** who saw the ruined capital.
Sewell's **"graveyard"** account of the sack may exaggerate.

naf5269232d9.s: Which European visitor left an eyewitness account of the ruined Vijayanagara capital in 1567?
naf5269232d9.x: Caesar Frederick, a Venetian merchant, visited Vijayanagara in 1567 and left an eyewitness account of the ruined capital.
naf5269232d9.tq: Use the visitor–description–year association to separate similar foreign accounts.
xs: **Caesar Frederick**, a **Venetian merchant**, visited in **1567** and left an eyewitness account of the ruined capital — so option **(2)** is correct.
The visit came two years after **Talikota** (**1565**).
xa: **Colin Mackenzie** mapped Hampi's ruins in **1800**.
**Robert Sewell**'s **A Forgotten Empire** came out in **1900**.
Hampi was looted for about **six months** after Talikota.

o: Chingiz Khan on his father's side and Timur on his mother's side
Timur on his father's side and Chingiz Khan on his mother's side
ne8f1a60854f.x: Babur was descended from Timur through his father and from Chingiz Khan through his mother.
xa: Born **1483**, **Farghana**.
His coins were silver **Shahrukhi** in **Timurid** style.
He wrote the **Tuzuk-i-Baburi** in **Chagatai Turki**.

n0f5be14110b.s: The Mansabdari system was introduced under:
n0f5be14110b.x: The Mansabdari system was introduced under Akbar, not during Babur's four-year rule.
xa: Babur left no administrative system; the treasury was empty.
Panipat ended the **Delhi Sultanate**.

n56e5ef054d4.s: Besides Daulat Khan Lodi and Alam Khan, Babur was invited to India by:
n56e5ef054d4.x: The three inviters were Daulat Khan Lodi (Governor of Punjab), Alam Khan (Ibrahim Lodi's uncle) and Rana Sanga of Mewar.
xa: Rana Sanga later fought Babur at **Khanwa (1527)**.
Babur's first raid: **1519**.

n4a62072d7bb.s: Babur's lavish distribution of the Lodi treasure after Panipat earned him the nickname:
n4a62072d7bb.x: Lavish sharing of the treasure earned him the nickname 'Qalandar'; 'Ghazi' was the title taken after Khanwa.
xa: The lavish sharing left the treasury **depleted for Humayun**.
The **Kabuli Bagh mosque** at Panipat commemorates the **1526** victory.

nb6799fcc128.s: At the Battle of Khanwa, the Rajput confederacy led by Rana Sanga was joined by
o: Daulat Khan Lodi and Medini Rai
Mahmud Lodi and Hasan Khan Mewati
nb6799fcc128.x: Rana Sanga’s coalition included the Afghan Mahmud Lodi and Hasan Khan Mewati.
nb6799fcc128.tq: Identify the members of the coalition rather than confusing them with Babur’s earlier opponents.
xs: Rana Sanga's Rajput confederacy was joined by **Mahmud Lodi** and **Hasan Khan Mewati** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Daulat Khan Lodi** had invited Babur; **Ibrahim Lodi** was already defeated at Panipat (**1526**).
xa: Babur used **trenches and barricades** against Sanga's **elephants**.
Before Khanwa he declared a **jihad**, renounced wine and remitted the **tamgha**.
Khanwa **broke Rajput power**; Babur took the title **"Ghazi"**.

ne89f7d17396.s: After his victory at Khanwa, Babur took the title:
ne89f7d17396.x: After Khanwa Babur took the title 'Ghazi'; before the battle he had declared jihad, renounced wine and remitted tamgha for Muslims.
xa: ⚠ **"Qalandar"** = for sharing the Lodi treasure; **"Ghazi"** = after Khanwa.
Rana Sanga was wounded and retreated.

n2b1c4af0bc1.s: At Khanwa, Babur used trenches and barricades mainly to counter Rana Sanga's:
n2b1c4af0bc1.x: Babur used trenches and barricades against Rana Sanga's elephants; his artillery also played a decisive role.
xa: Sanga's allies: **Mahmud Lodi** and **Hasan Khan Mewati**.
Khanwa (**1527**) broke **Rajput power**.
Babur then took the title **"Ghazi"**.

n1d0a9549821.s: The silver coins Babur issued in the Timurid style were called:
n1d0a9549821.x: Babur issued silver Shahrukhi coins in the Timurid style and introduced the charbagh garden.
xa: He built the **Kabuli Bagh mosque** at Panipat and a mosque at **Agra**.
His paternal descent was from **Timur**.

n27460c9a436.s: Which one of the following was NOT a limitation of Babur’s rule in India?
o: The Afghans continued to claim Delhi
Gujarat and Malwa were united under Bahadur Shah
A fully developed administrative system was established
n27460c9a436.x: D is the answer because Babur set up no administrative system at all (his rule had shallow roots and the treasury was empty), so 'a fully developed administrative system' was not one of his limitations. A, B and C are listed limits: the Afghans still claimed Delhi, Bengal stayed unconquered, and Gujarat-Malwa was united under Bahadur Shah.
n27460c9a436.tq: Find the option that reverses a stated weakness of Babur’s administration.
xs: **A fully developed administrative system** was not something Babur had — so option **(4)** is the answer.
He left **no administrative system** and an **empty treasury**.
The others are real limits: **Afghans** still claimed Delhi, **Bengal** unconquered, **Gujarat-Malwa** under **Bahadur Shah**.
xa: Mughal authority had **shallow roots** in his **4-year** rule.
⚠ The **Mansabdari system** is **Akbar's**, not Babur's.

n1c24b4f879b.x: The Baburnama was written in Chagatai Turki; Persian was the language of the Mughal court.
xa: English translators: **Leyden and Erskine** (**1826**); **Annette Beveridge**.
It counts **five Muslim and two Hindu powers** in India.
It praises **Krishnadevaraya** as the most powerful ruler.

n40a751a9015.s: In his account of India, Babur praised which ruler as the most powerful?
n40a751a9015.x: Babur praised Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara as the most powerful ruler in India.
xa: Babur was a contemporary of **Krishnadevaraya** and Golconda's **Sultan Quli**.
The Baburnama is in **Chagatai Turki**; translated by **Leyden and Erskine** (**1826**).

n02eddbe6f25.s: At Babur's death, his dominions extended from Kabul and Badakhshan to the borders of:
n02eddbe6f25.x: Babur's dominions ran from Kabul and Badakhshan through Punjab, Delhi and Agra to the borders of Bihar.
xa: The Bihar border was reached after **Ghaghra**.
He died in **1530** at Agra; **Humayun** took the throne on **29 Dec 1530**.
Mughal authority had **shallow roots**.

n02dcb5e905d.s: At the Battle of Dourah (1532), Humayun defeated the Afghans and drove Mahmud Lodi from:
n02dcb5e905d.x: Dourah (Devara), 1532, on the Gomati, drove Mahmud Lodi from Jaunpur.
xa: Humayun acceded on **29 Dec 1530**, three days after Babur's death.
At Dourah he also lifted the siege of **Kalinjar**.
**Chausa (1539)** and **Kannauj/Bilgram (1540)** were Sher Shah's victories over Humayun.

nb302e156116.s: Sher Khan assumed the title 'Sher Shah' after the Battle of:
nb302e156116.x: He took the title Sher Shah after Chausa (1539); after Kannauj (1540) he took the throne.
xa: ⚠ **"Sher Khan"** = from **Bahar Khan** (tiger).
Sher Shah's reign: **1540-45**.
He died in **1545** during the siege of **Kalinjar**.

n3ded4ce2b06.s: During his exile, Humayun retook Kandahar and Kabul with the help of:
n3ded4ce2b06.x: The Safavid Shah Tahmasp of Persia helped him retake Kandahar and Kabul.
xa: Humayun went to **Persia**, forming an alliance with the **Safavids**.
He returned in **July 1555**.

nb5321979334.s: Humayun died in January 1556 after falling from the stairs of the Sher Mandal library in:
nb5321979334.x: He fell from the stairs of the Sher Mandal library in the Purana Qila, Delhi.
xa: The **Purana Qila** was begun by Humayun and rebuilt by Sher Shah.
**Humayun-nama** was written by his sister **Gulbadan Begum**.

n8c61654d5cf.x: The Humayun-nama was written by Humayun's sister Gulbadan Begum. Hamida Banu Begum was Humayun's wife and Akbar's mother; Abul Fazl wrote the Akbarnama; Babur wrote the Tuzuk-i-Baburi.
xs: The **Humayun-nama** was written by Humayun's sister **Gulbadan Begum** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Hamida Banu Begum** was Humayun's wife and **Akbar's** mother.
**Babur** wrote the **Tuzuk-i-Baburi**.
xa: Akbar was born at **Amarkot** (**1542**).
Humayun died in **January 1556** at the **Sher Mandal** library, **Purana Qila**.

nindian-history-17-52.s: The Battle of Kannauj (1540), in which Sher Shah defeated Humayun, is also called the Battle of:
nindian-history-17-52.x: Kannauj is also called the Battle of Bilgram.
n: The Battle of Kannauj is also called the Battle of Bilgram. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Battle of Kannauj or Bilgram was fought in 1540. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Battle of Kannauj or Bilgram was fought between Humayun and Sher Shah. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xa: **Chausa** (**26 June 1539**) preceded Bilgram.
⚠ Some notes wrongly list "Bilgram (1540)" as a Humayun victory.
Humayun reoccupied Delhi after **Sirhind** (**1555**).

n83766e2928c.s: After the First Battle of Panipat, Babur occupied:
n83766e2928c.x: After Panipat Babur occupied Delhi and Agra.
xa: His memoir **Tuzuk-i-Baburi** is in **Chaghatai Turkish** and praises **Krishnadevaraya**.
Panipat was the first large-scale use of **gunpowder artillery** in Indian warfare.
Babur's battles in order: **Panipat I → Khanwa → Chanderi → Ghaghra** (UKPSC **2024**).

n5c681d88161.s: Farid received the title 'Sher Khan' for slaying a tiger from:
n5c681d88161.x: The title 'Sher Khan' was given by Bahar Khan of Bihar, not Babur.
xa: He studied at **Jaunpur** and managed his father's jagir from **1511**.
⚠ **"Sher Shah"** was assumed after **Chausa (1539)**.

neef60953fc2.s: Jaita and Kumpa were generals of:
neef60953fc2.x: Jaita and Kumpa were Maldeo's generals at the hard-fought battle of Samel (1544).
xa: Samel is also called **Sammel / Giri-Sumel**.
**Bahadur Shah** of Gujarat let the **Portuguese** fortify **Diu** (**1535**).
Sher Shah's other conquests: **Malwa** and **Raisen** (Puran Mal).

n2ba014b465e.s: Sher Shah died in 1545 in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of
n2ba014b465e.x: Sher Shah died in 1545 in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of Kalinjar.
n2ba014b465e.tq: Associate the ruler's death with the exact military operation rather than merely the year.
xs: Sher Shah died in **1545** in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of **Kalinjar** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Raisen** was taken from Puran Mal; **Gaur** was taken in **1538**.
xa: Humayun had earlier lifted a siege of **Kalinjar** after **Dourah**.
Successor: **Islam Shah** (**Jalal Khan**, **1545-53**).
Sher Shah's tomb is at **Sasaram** (Bihar), an **octagonal tomb in a tank**.

n6bfb7641104.s: Who succeeded Sher Shah on the Sur throne?
n6bfb7641104.x: Islam Shah (Jalal Khan) succeeded Sher Shah and ruled 1545-53.
xa: Hemu lost **Panipat II (5 Nov 1556)**: an arrow struck his eye; Afghan power ended.
**Sikandar Sur** was Adil Shah's rival; Humayun defeated him at **Machhiwara and Sirhind**.
The Surs were the **last Afghan dynasty** to rule Delhi.

n71a074d1989.s: The Second Battle of Panipat was fought on:
n71a074d1989.x: Panipat II was fought on 5 November 1556; Hemu was struck in the eye by an arrow and captured.
xa: The Mughal side was led by **Akbar/Bairam Khan**.
⚠ "Tipu vs Marathas" is **not** Panipat II.
**Panipat III (1761)**: Marathas vs **Ahmad Shah Abdali**.

n52c528f0210.s: The last Afghan dynasty to rule Delhi was the:
n52c528f0210.x: The Surs were the last Afghan dynasty to rule Delhi; Sher Shah's revenue, coinage and roads set the Mughal pattern.
xa: Sher Shah took **1/3** of average produce with **three** land classes.
Akbar-Todar Mal kept **1/3** but used **ten-year averages** and **four** classes (**polaj, parauti, chachar, banjar**).
The **Rupiya** began with Sher Shah.

nbec68be0777.x: The Baburnama was written in Chaghatai Turkish; Persian was the Mughal court language.
xa: Babur's tactics: **Tulughma** (cavalry flanking) and the **Rumi (Ottoman) method**.

**Sultan Quli Qutb Shah** of Golconda (**1518-43**) was Babur's contemporary.

n420247b4fa2.s: To stop officers building local interests, Sher Shah's administration:

Appointed officers in their home areas

n771e4386f7d.s: In Sur administration, the Chief Shiqdar (shiqdar-i-shiqdaran) of a sarkar looked after:

Officers were **frequently transferred**.

n7cf185fcc35.s: In a Sur-era pargana, the Fotedar functioned as the:
n7cf185fcc35.x: The Fotedar was the pargana treasurer; Karkuns were the Hindi and Persian writers.
xa: The pargana also had an **Amin** (munsif).
Sarkar level: **Chief Shiqdar** (law and order) and **Chief Munsif** (revenue/civil).

n11e3e205031.x: Dagh was the branding of horses; chehra/huliya was the descriptive roll of soldiers.
xa: Both measures were aimed **against fraud**.
**Hindus** held high army posts.

na49916726f7.s: The Rumi method of warfare used by Babur was of ____ origin.
na49916726f7.x: The Rumi method (carts linked as a barrier for matchlockmen and artillery) was Ottoman; Tulughma was Uzbek.
xa: Panipat I (**21 Apr 1526**): Babur beat **Ibrahim Lodi**; artillery decisive.
These tactics were tested in a PMF IAS practice item (**Apr 2026**).
**Kabuli Bagh Mosque** at Panipat marks **1526**.

nbc4297a041d.s: Sher Shah took the fort of Raisen from:
nbc4297a041d.x: Raisen was taken from Puran Mal.
xa: At **Samel (1544)** Sher Shah fought **Maldeo of Marwar**.
He died in **1545** in a gunpowder explosion during the siege of **Kalinjar**.
⚠ Title **"Sher Khan"** came from **Bahar Khan**; **"Sher Shah"** was assumed after **Chausa (1539)**.

nebef73d980f.s: Sher Shah's land survey measured land uniformly with the:
nebef73d980f.x: Land was measured with the sikandari gaz and the jarib, and classified into good, middling and bad.
xa: State share: **one-third** of average produce, paid in **cash or grain**.
⚠ APPSC-G1 **2024** key: "one-fourth" is false.
**Patta** = title deed given to the cultivator; **Qabuliyat** = deed of acceptance signed by the peasant.

n4a5a04dde0d.s: Under Sher Shah, the state's share of land revenue was fixed at:
n4a5a04dde0d.x: The state share was one-third of average produce; the system became the model for Todar Mal's Bandobast.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say "one-fourth to one-third".
Some notes call Sher Shah the first to introduce a **ryotwari**-type system.

n1b9a527bc17.s: In Sher Shah's revenue system, the Qabuliyat was
o: the title deed given to the peasant stating his revenue dues
the deed of agreement signed by the peasant accepting the revenue demand
the fee paid to the surveyor
the fee paid to the revenue collector
n1b9a527bc17.x: The Qabuliyat was the peasant's deed of acceptance of the revenue demand, signed by him. The Patta was the title deed given to the cultivator. Jaribana was the surveyor's fee and muhasilana the collector's fee.
n1b9a527bc17.tq: Patta given to peasant; Qabuliyat signed by peasant
xs: The **Qabuliyat** was the peasant's **deed of agreement** accepting the revenue demand, **signed by him** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Patta** was the **title deed** given to the cultivator.
**Jaribana** = surveyor's fee; **Muhasilana** = collector's fee.
xa: ⚠ **Patta** = given by the state; **Qabuliyat** = signed by the peasant.
Assessment was by the **Amin**, with shiqdar, qanungo and patwari.

n4e2b7c90542.s: In Sher Shah's currency, the dam was a coin of:
n4e2b7c90542.x: The rupiya was silver, the dam copper and the mohur gold.
xa: The rupiya weighed about **178 grains** and was introduced **1540-45**.
Sher Shah minted **pure** gold and silver coins.
He restored the **Grand Trunk Road** (Sadak-e-Azam) from **Sonargaon** to the **Indus**.

ncedc8bde2b6.s: The Sadak-e-Azam constructed or restored by Sher Shah connected
o: Sonargaon in Bengal with the Indus
ncedc8bde2b6.x: The major road, also called the Grand Trunk Road, ran from Sonargaon in Bengal to the Indus.
ncedc8bde2b6.tq: Distinguish the principal imperial highway from the other roads associated with Sher Shah.
xs: The **Sadak-e-Azam (Grand Trunk Road)** ran from **Sonargaon (Bengal) to the Indus** — so option **(4)** is correct.

xa: APPSC-G1 **2022** answer: "Indus to Sonargaon"; APPSC-GS **2018**: he **restored** it.
⚠ Some notes say **Chittagong-Kabul**, about **1,500 miles**.
Another road: **Agra-Jodhpur-Chittor**.

n5dfb2b32285.s: Besides lodging travellers, Sher Shah's sarais served as ____ for relaying news and mail.
n5dfb2b32285.x: The sarais served as dak-chowkis; market towns also grew around them.
xa: Dak-chowkis were post stations relaying news and mail, with **horses**.
The **Grand Trunk Road** ran from **Sonargaon** to the **Indus**.

n49d98e9c5fd.x: Sadak-e-Azam was the major road from Bengal to the Indus; the others were separate Sur routes.
xa: The Grand Trunk Road still exists.
Sarais along the roads doubled as **dak-chowkis**.

n781c218676e.s: Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram is notable for being
o: a four-domed marble mausoleum in Agra
an octagonal tomb set in a tank
a circular tomb built inside the Purana Qila

nf019875bccd.s: Balban's Tomb, with the first true arch in India, is located at:
nf019875bccd.x: Balban's Tomb is at Mehrauli, Delhi; Sasaram has Sher Shah's octagonal tomb.

Sher Shah's octagonal tomb in a tank at Sasaram was **completed** by **Islam Shah**.

nindian-history-62-12.x: The Qila-e-Kuhna Mosque was built inside the Purana Qila (Old Fort).

n29265ea3835.s: Babur's last battle, fought in 1529 against the Afghans under Mahmud Lodi, was the Battle of:
n29265ea3835.x: Ghaghra (1529) was Babur's last battle; the order was Panipat I, Khanwa, Chanderi, Ghaghra.

nb1313edf903.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the revenue systems of Sher Shah and Akbar-Todar Mal?

n8f0ec0acd9b.s: Sultan Quli Qutb Shah, contemporary of Babur, Humayun and Sher Shah, ruled Golconda from:
n8f0ec0acd9b.x: Sultan Quli Qutb Shah ruled Golconda from 1518 to 1543.
xa: Babur's **Tuzuk-i-Baburi** praises **Krishnadevaraya**.
Sher Shah's reign: **1540-45**.
Humayun acceded on **29 Dec 1530**.

n843f93b51e8.s: Bairam Khan, Akbar's regent (1556-60), was killed in 1561 while on his way to:
n843f93b51e8.x: Dismissed in 1560, Bairam Khan was killed on the way to Mecca in 1561.
xa: Bairam Khan enthroned Akbar at **Kalanaur**.
His son **Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan** translated the **Baburnama** into Persian.
n843f93b51e8.fixed: y1afd9cc98a2 key: statement that title was NOT given at wazir appointment is wrong, so statement 3 is correct

n6bac3d60446.s: The expression 'petticoat government' in Akbar's early reign refers to the dominance of:
o: Ruqaiya Sultan Begum and Man Singh I
Hamida Banu Begum and Salima Sultan Begum
Maham Anaga and her son Adham Khan
n6bac3d60446.x: The term refers to the period from 1560 to 1564 when Maham Anaga and her son Adham Khan exercised considerable influence.
n6bac3d60446.tq: Match the political expression with the persons and period it denotes.
xs: **Petticoat government** (**1560-64**) was the dominance of **Maham Anaga** and her son **Adham Khan** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It followed **Bairam Khan's regency** (**1556-60**).
xa: Bairam Khan was dismissed in **1560** and killed in **1561**.
**Man Singh I** was a Kachhwaha general; **Todar Mal** was the revenue minister.
Akbar married the daughter of **Raja Bharmal of Amber** in **1562**.

n5b5f808155b.s: The Second Battle of Panipat (5 November 1556), which ended Afghan power, was fought between Akbar's forces and:
n5b5f808155b.x: At Panipat II (1556) Hemu was hit in the eye by an arrow and captured, ending Afghan power. Daud Khan Karrani opposed Akbar in Bengal (1576), Baz Bahadur in Malwa (1561), and Ibrahim Lodi lost the First Battle of Panipat (1526) to Babur.
n5b5f808155b.tq: Panipat II = 1556 = Hemu (arrow in the eye).
xs: At **Panipat II (5 Nov 1556)**, Akbar's forces fought **Hemu** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Hemu was **hit in the eye by an arrow** and captured; **Afghan power ended**.
**Daud Khan Karrani** opposed Akbar in **Bengal** (**1576**); **Baz Bahadur** in **Malwa** (**1561**).
xa: Akbar was then **14**, under **Bairam Khan**.
Malwa (**1561**) was Akbar's first listed conquest.

n81a825e1e6f.s: Guru Gobind Singh, who fought 14 wars against Aurangzeb's forces, wrote the:
n81a825e1e6f.x: Guru Gobind Singh wrote the Zafarnama, which advocated the sword only when all other avenues failed.
xa: He founded the **Khalsa** on **13 April 1699** (Baisakhi) at **Takht Keshgarh Sahib** with the **Panj Pyaras**.
His **four Sahibzade** were martyred.
**Battle of Muktsar**: the **Chali Mukte** (40 liberated ones) died defending him — commemorated as **Maghi**.

nindian-history-18-14.s: On which date was Akbar enthroned?
nindian-history-18-14.x: Akbar was enthroned at Kalanaur on February 14, 1556, after Humayun's death. The 1658 and 1659 dates are Aurangzeb's two coronations.
nindian-history-18-14.tq: Match each coronation date with its ruler.
xs: Akbar was enthroned on **February 14, 1556** — option **(3)**.
He was crowned at **Kalanaur** in **Gurdaspur, Punjab**, by **Bairam Khan**.
**July 21, 1658** and **June 5, 1659** are **Aurangzeb's** two coronations.
xa: **Bairam Khan's regency**: **1556-60**; dismissed **1560**, killed on the way to Mecca **1561**.
**Petticoat government** (**1560-64**): **Maham Anaga** and **Adham Khan**.
Akbar gave Bairam Khan the title **"Khan-i-Khanan"**.

n486f49e08eb.x: Rani Durgavati opposed Akbar in Gondwana; Baz Bahadur in Malwa, Rana Udai Singh at Chittor, Surjan Rai at Ranthambore.
xa: ⚠ Women who resisted: **Rani Durgavati** (Gondwana) and **Chand Bibi** (Ahmednagar).
In **Marwar**, **Rao Chandrasena** resisted.
Last campaign: **Asirgarh (1601)**.

n72f1502792c.s: Akbar's last campaign was associated with the conquest of:
o: Gujarat, where Buland Darwaza was built
Khandesh, including the capture of Asirgarh fort
n72f1502792c.x: Akbar's last campaign was the conquest of Khandesh in 1601, during which the Asirgarh fort was taken from Miran Bahadur.
n72f1502792c.tq: Identify the last event in a sequence of conquests rather than the most famous one.
xs: Akbar's **last campaign** was **Khandesh**, taking **Asirgarh** fort (**1601**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was taken from **Miran Bahadur**.
**Gujarat** (Buland Darwaza), **Bengal** and **Kashmir** were earlier conquests.
xa: **Ahmednagar** fell in **1600**, resisted by **Chand Bibi**.
Akbar's empire reached the **Godavari** in the south.

nf7c40c49def.s: Akbar's empire stretched from Bengal to Afghanistan and from Kashmir to the:
nf7c40c49def.x: Akbar's empire extended from Bengal to Afghanistan and from Kashmir to the Godavari.
xa: **Kashmir** was taken in **1586** from Yusuf Shah Chak.
**Kabul** was taken in **1581** from Mirza Hakim.
Golconda's **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** kept friendly relations with Akbar.

n2438bf87753.s: Which Mughal emperor was known as 'Zinda Pir'?
n2438bf87753.x: Aurangzeb was known as Alamgir and Zinda Pir.
xa: **Akbar** was the **unlettered** emperor.
**Shah Jahan** got his title from **Jahangir**.
Jahangir was crowned as **Nur-ud-din Muhammad Jahangir**; Aurangzeb played the **veena**.

nf5116a05800.s: The Chali Mukte are associated with which event?
o: The release of Guru Hargobind from Gwalior Fort
The founding of the Khalsa at Anandpur
The compilation of the Adi Granth at Amritsar
The defence of Guru Gobind Singh at Muktsar
nf5116a05800.x: The Chali Mukte, or 40 liberated ones, died defending Guru Gobind Singh at Muktsar; the event is commemorated as Maghi.
nf5116a05800.tq: Identify the event linked to a distinctive commemorative name.
xs: The **Chali Mukte** died **defending Guru Gobind Singh at Muktsar** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Chali Mukte** = the **40 liberated ones**; the event is commemorated as **Maghi**.
Guru Hargobind was imprisoned at **Gwalior**; the **Adi Granth** was compiled by **Guru Arjan Dev**.
xa: The **Khalsa** was founded on **13 April 1699** (Baisakhi) at **Takht Keshgarh Sahib**.
Guru Gobind Singh fought **14 wars** with Aurangzeb and wrote the **Zafarnama**.
His disciple **Banda Singh Bahadur** conquered **Sirhind (1710)** to avenge the Guru's younger sons.

n4115b49b09f.s: The Khalsa was founded by Guru Gobind Singh on Baisakhi day in the year:
n4115b49b09f.x: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa on 13 April 1699 (Baisakhi) with the Panj Pyaras. 1675 is Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom, and 1710 is Banda Singh Bahadur's conquest of Sirhind; 1704 is not the Khalsa's date.
xs: The **Khalsa** was founded on **13 April 1699** (Baisakhi) — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was founded at **Takht Keshgarh Sahib** with the **Panj Pyaras**.
**1675** = Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom; **1710** = Banda Singh Bahadur's conquest of **Sirhind**.
xa: **Baisakhi** is recalled as Khalsa foundation day.
Guru Gobind Singh fought **14 wars** with Aurangzeb and wrote the **Zafarnama**.
⚠ **Sirhind Fateh Diwas (12-14 May)** marks Banda Singh's **1710** conquest — not Baisakhi.

nindian-history-82-15.s: Mughal painting reached its zenith under:
nindian-history-82-15.x: Jahangir's reign was the peak of Mughal painting; Humayun laid its foundation.
n: Humayun was associated with the foundation of Mughal painting. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Akbar undertook imperial expansion. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Akbar introduced administrative reforms. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Akbar pursued a religious policy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Jahangir's reign marked the zenith of Mughal painting. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Shah Jahan's reign marked the architectural zenith of the Mughal Empire. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
xa: Humayun was learned in Persian, Arabic, Turkish, mathematics and **astronomy**.
Jahangir wrote the **Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri**; ⚠ not the Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Babur's).
The title **"Shah Jahan"** was given by **Jahangir**.

nindian-history-23-9.s: Along with the Banaras pandits, who petitioned Shah Jahan to abolish the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Allahabad?
nindian-history-23-9.x: Kavindracharya and the Banaras pandits sought the abolition of the pilgrim tax.
n: Shah Jahan levied a pilgrim tax at Banaras. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Shah Jahan levied a pilgrim tax at Allahabad. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Kavindracharya sought the abolition of the pilgrim tax. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Banaras pandits sought the abolition of the pilgrim tax. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
xa: Akbar abolished the pilgrim tax in **1563** and jizya in **1564**.
Aurangzeb reimposed **jizya** in **1679**.
**Shah Jahan** abolished **Sijda**, an Iranian court tradition.

nindian-history-23-10.s: Under Aurangzeb's jizya, children below what age were exempted?
nindian-history-23-10.x: Children below 14 were exempt, along with women, slaves, beggars and the unemployed.
n: Women were exempt from Jizya under Aurangzeb. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Slaves were exempt from Jizya under Aurangzeb. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Children below 14 were exempt from Jizya under Aurangzeb. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Beggars were exempt from Jizya under Aurangzeb. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Unemployed persons were exempt from Jizya under Aurangzeb. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
xa: Below **200 dirhams**: **12 dirhams** a year.
**200 to 10,000 dirhams**: **24 dirhams**.
Above **10,000 dirhams**: **48 dirhams**.

nindian-history-47-11.s: Tansen's early patron, Raja Ramchandra Singh, ruled:
nindian-history-47-11.x: Tansen was first patronised by Raja Ramchandra Singh of Rewa before joining Akbar's court as a Navaratna.
n: Raja Ramchandra Singh of Rewa was an early patron of Tansen. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #47 · pp 115-116]
Tansen was a Navaratna in Akbar’s court. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #47 · pp 115-116]
Swami Haridas was associated with Dhrupad. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #47 · pp 115-116]
Vilas Khan was a main singer in Jahangir’s court. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #47 · pp 115-116]
xa: Tansen (**Ramtanu Pandey**) is credited with **Miyan ki Malhar** and **Miyan ki Todi**.
**Hari Vijay Suri**, a Jain monk, was a **Jagadguru**; **Jin Chandra Suri** a **Yug Pradhan**.
**Faizi** supervised Akbar's **translation department**.

n1ff8ba02cef.s: The Battle of Haldighati formed part of Akbar's campaign against:
n1ff8ba02cef.x: The Battle of Haldighati was part of Akbar's Mewar campaign. It was fought between the Mughal forces led by Man Singh and Maharana Pratap.
n1ff8ba02cef.tq: Distinguish the broader campaign from nearby Rajput regions.
xs: **Haldighati** was part of Akbar's campaign against **Mewar** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes wrongly place it in the **Gujarat** campaign.
In **Marwar** it was **Rao Chandrasena** who resisted; **Khandesh** and **Malwa** were separate campaigns.
xa: Haldighati (**1576**): **Maharana Pratap** vs Mughals under **Man Singh**; not decisive.
Mewar submitted only under **Jahangir** (**Amar Singh**).
The siege of **Chittor** (**1568**) was against **Rana Udai Singh**.

n7ff6fb9ecee.s: In 1562, Akbar entered into a matrimonial alliance with the daughter of:
n7ff6fb9ecee.x: In 1562, Akbar married the daughter of Raja Bharmal of Amber, a Kachhwaha ruler.
n7ff6fb9ecee.tq: Test the exact person and state connected with the matrimonial alliance.
xs: In **1562** Akbar married the daughter of **Raja Bharmal of Amber** (Kachhwaha) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Miran Bahadur** lost Asirgarh; **Rao Chandrasena** resisted in Marwar; **Rana Udai Singh** defended Chittor.
xa: **Man Singh** and **Bhagwan Das** were top mansabdars.
**Man Singh I**, Kachhwaha of Amber, led the Mughals at **Haldighati**.

nindian-history-17-29.s: In the Battle of Haldighati (1576), the Mughal side was led by:
nindian-history-17-29.x: Man Singh led Akbar's forces against Rana Pratap at Haldighati in 1576.
n: The Battle of Haldighati was fought in 1576. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Battle of Haldighati was fought between Mughal forces and Rana Pratap's forces. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
Man Singh led the Mughal side in the Battle of Haldighati. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Battle of Haldighati resulted in a Mughal victory. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Battle of Haldighati is associated with Akbar and Rana Pratap. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xa: **Mewar** never submitted under Akbar; it submitted under **Jahangir** (**Amar Singh**).
⚠ Some notes place Haldighati in the **Gujarat** campaign; it was part of the **Mewar** campaign.
**Man Singh** and **Bhagwan Das** were top Rajput mansabdars.

n536d55e5c30.s: The Mahzar of 1579, which made Akbar supreme arbiter in religious disputes, was drafted by:
n536d55e5c30.x: The Mahzar was drafted by Shaikh Mubarak.
xa: It is also called the so-called **Infallibility Decree**.
**Din-i-Ilahi** followed in **1582**.

ne6cabd468ff.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature associated with Din-i-Ilahi?
o: Reverence for the sun and fire
ne6cabd468ff.x: Din-i-Ilahi included belief in one God, reverence for the sun and fire, and avoidance of meat-eating. It was never forcibly imposed on anyone.
ne6cabd468ff.tq: Reject the extreme compulsory feature that contradicts the voluntary character of the order.
xs: **Compulsory conversion of all subjects** was not a feature — Din-i-Ilahi was **never forced on anyone** — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Its features included **one God**, **reverence for sun and fire** and **avoiding meat**.
xa: Other features: greeting **"Allah-hu-Akbar"**, readiness to sacrifice wealth, high character.
Proclaimed in **1582**.
Orthodox critics: **Badauni** and Naqshbandi **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi**.

n85e981217fd.s: Who among the following Mughal emperors was unlettered but became a great patron of learning and culture?
n85e981217fd.x: Akbar was unlettered, yet he was a great patron of learning, literature and culture.
n85e981217fd.tq: Use the distinctive contrast between personal literacy and cultural patronage.
xs: **Akbar** was the **unlettered** (illiterate) Mughal emperor, yet a great patron — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Babur** wrote his memoirs (**Tuzuk-i-Baburi**) in **Turki**; **Humayun** was learned in Persian, Arabic, Turkish, mathematics and **astronomy**.
**Jahangir** wrote his memoir, the **Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri**.
xa: Akbar's court produced the **Razmnama** (Persian translation of the **Mahabharata**); the **Atharvaveda** was also translated.
**Abul Fazl** wrote the **Akbarnama** and **Ain-i-Akbari**.
Akbar broadened the curriculum to include ethics, arithmetic, agriculture, geometry, astronomy, medicine, logic and history.
**Aurangzeb** was learned in Arabic and Persian and played the **veena**.

n7559667ccbf.s: Jahangir's religious policy is best described as:
o: A complete break from Akbar's tolerance
Broadly continuing Akbar's tolerance, though Guru Arjan Dev was executed for political reasons
n7559667ccbf.x: Jahangir broadly continued Akbar's tolerance; Guru Arjan Dev was executed for political reasons linked to support for the rebel prince Khusrau.
xa: **Guru Arjan Dev** was executed in **1606** for supporting rebel prince **Khusrau**.
Jahangir imprisoned **Guru Hargobind** at **Gwalior**.
Jahangir gave Prince Khurram the title **"Shah Jahan"**.

nc36c6e0d85d.s: What condition is described as the jagirdari crisis under Aurangzeb?
o: Too many jagirdars competing for too few jagirs, placing pressure on the peasantry
The complete abolition of jagirs by Akbar
The transfer of all jagirs to Rajput rulers
Too few mansabdars controlling an excessive number of jagirs
nc36c6e0d85d.x: The jagirdari crisis arose because too many mansabdars chased too few jagirs, which increased pressure on the peasantry.
nc36c6e0d85d.tq: Translate the economic consequence into an administrative scenario.
xs: The **jagirdari crisis**: **too many mansabdars chased too few jagirs**, pressing the peasantry — so option **(1)** is correct.
It arose under **Aurangzeb**, not Akbar; jagirs were not abolished or handed to Rajput rulers.
xa: **Mansabdari-jagirdari** and **Zabti** were the core of Mughal governance for **150 years**.
Aurangzeb's reversal of tolerance (jizya **1679**) is also cited among **causes of decline**.
Many of Aurangzeb's Hindu nobles were **Marathas and Rajputs** taken in during the **Deccan wars**.

nindian-history-51-84.s: In which year did Aurangzeb reimpose jizya?
nindian-history-51-84.x: Aurangzeb reimposed jizya in 1679, reversing Akbar's abolition. 1582 is Din-i-Ilahi, 1579 the Mahzar and 1675 the execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur.
nindian-history-51-84.tq: Recall the year of each event.
n: Aurangzeb reimposed jizya in 1679. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xs: Aurangzeb reimposed **jizya** in **1679** — option **(1)**.
**Akbar** had abolished jizya in **1564**.
xa: The **pilgrimage tax** was abolished in **1563** (some notes say **1564**).
**Ibadat Khana**: established **1575**, opened to different religions in **1578**.
**Zakat** = alms tax on Muslims; **Ushr** = land tax on Muslims; **Khums** = one-fifth of war booty.

nindian-history-82-16.s: The Mughal Empire reached its maximum territorial extent under:
nindian-history-82-16.x: Aurangzeb's Deccan conquests of Bijapur and Golconda gave the empire its greatest extent.
n: Aurangzeb's reign marked the maximum territorial expansion of the Mughal Empire. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
Aurangzeb commissioned the Fatawa-i-Alamgiri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #82 · pp 162-165]
xa: Aurangzeb had the **highest number of Hindu nobles** in absolute terms (UPPSC **2000** key), largely Marathas and Rajputs.
Aurangzeb was called **Alamgir** and **Zinda Pir / Darvesh**; he played the veena.
He reimposed **jizya** in **1679**.

nindian-history-84-9.s: The Iranian court practice of Sijda (prostration) was abolished by:
nindian-history-84-9.x: Shah Jahan abolished Sijda; Akbar had acted against child marriage and Sati.
n: Akbar's reign abolished child marriage. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #84 · pp 166-167]
Akbar's reign abolished Sati. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #84 · pp 166-167]
Shah Jahan abolished Sijda, an Iranian court tradition. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #84 · pp 166-167]
xa: **Sikandar Lodi** abolished the **tax on grains**.
**Zain-ul-Abidin** of Kashmir abolished **jizya** and **cow slaughter**.
Akbar also abolished **jizya** and the **pilgrimage tax**.
nindian-history-84-9.fixed: Akbar discouraged/regulated child marriage and sati, did not abolish them; Shah Jahan did abolish sijda

n87e7509c0ef.s: The first Jesuit mission to Akbar's court (1580) was led by:
n87e7509c0ef.x: The first Jesuit mission from Goa in 1580 was led by Rudolf Acquaviva and Antonio Monserrate; Jerome Xavier led the third mission in 1595.
xa: The second mission came in **1591**.
The missions came from **Goa**.

ncbd7a337e98.s: The third Jesuit mission to Akbar's court in 1595 was conducted under the leadership of:
ncbd7a337e98.x: The third Jesuit mission, sent in 1595, was under Jerome Xavier.
ncbd7a337e98.tq: Distinguish the leader of the later mission from those of the first mission.
xs: The **third** Jesuit mission (**1595**) was led by **Jerome Xavier** (CGPSC **2022**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rudolf Acquaviva** and **Antonio Monserrate** led the **first** (**1580**).
**Dastur Meherji Rana** was a **Parsi** leader.
xa: The second mission came in **1591**.
The Ibadat Khana was opened to **Christians** among others.

n7387c0d207b.s: Akbar gave the title 'Jagat Guru' to the Jain scholar:
n7387c0d207b.x: Hiravijaya Suri was given 'Jagat Guru'; Jinachandra Suri received 'Yuga Pradhan'.
xa: ⚠ "Jagat Guru" = Hiravijaya Suri; "Yuga Pradhan" = Jinachandra Suri.
Land to **Guru Ram Das** → growth of **Amritsar**.

nc7418a0cd3b.s: Akbar's grant of land to Guru Ram Das is associated with the growth of:
nc7418a0cd3b.x: Land granted to Guru Ram Das became associated with the growth of Amritsar.
nc7418a0cd3b.tq: Link the religious leader with the place connected to the grant.
xs: Akbar's land grant to **Guru Ram Das** is where **Amritsar** grew — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Fatehpur Sikri** housed the **Ibadat Khana**.
xa: **Guru Arjan Dev** built the **Golden Temple (Harmandir)** at Amritsar.
Guru Arjan Dev was **executed by Jahangir (1606)**.
Akbar also gave land to Parsi **Dastur Meherji Rana**.

n007cf192dd8.s: Who was the only Hindu member of Din-i-Ilahi?
n007cf192dd8.x: Birbal was the only Hindu member of Din-i-Ilahi. The circle of members was small, numbering about 18 according to the cited account.
n007cf192dd8.tq: Distinguish the sole Hindu member from other prominent Hindu officials at Akbar's court.
xs: **Birbal** was the **only Hindu** disciple of Din-i-Ilahi — so option **(3)** is correct.
The circle was small — about **18** members.
xa: Other members: **Abul Fazl, Faizi and Shaikh Mubarak**.
Birbal (Mahesh Das) was killed in **1586** fighting the **Yusufzai**.
**Man Singh** and **Todar Mal** are not listed as members.

n23678d89ce2.s: Din-i-Ilahi did not become a mass religion mainly because it:
o: Was confined to the Rajput nobility
Was abolished by Akbar soon after its launch
Was never forced on anyone and drew only a small circle
Was banned by the ulema in 1579
n23678d89ce2.x: Its voluntary nature and small membership explain why Din-i-Ilahi never became a mass religion.
xa: Debate: new religion or a **discipleship order**?
**Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi** (**Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**) attacked it and propounded **Wahdat-ul-Shuhud**.
The **Naqshbandi** order, founded by **Baha-ud-din Naqshband**, came to India with **Babur**.

n62261bc68c2.s: The Adi Granth was compiled in 1604 by:
n62261bc68c2.x: Guru Arjan compiled the Adi Granth in 1604.
n62261bc68c2.tq: Use the specific contribution and year to distinguish the Gurus.
xs: The **Adi Granth** was compiled in **1604** by **Guru Arjan** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Guru Arjan Dev was the **5th** Guru; he also built the **Golden Temple** (Harmandir), Amritsar.
**Guru Tegh Bahadur** (9th) founded **Anandpur Sahib**; **Guru Gobind Singh** (10th) founded the **Khalsa**.
xa: Guru Arjan Dev was **executed by Jahangir (1606)** for supporting rebel prince **Khusrau**.
**Guru Tegh Bahadur** has **116 hymns** in the Guru Granth Sahib.
Akbar granted land to **Guru Ram Das**, where **Amritsar** grew.

nec745d943c0.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of Akbar's Rajput policy?
o: Appointment of Rajputs to high posts
Immediate loss of autonomy for every Rajput state after submission
nec745d943c0.x: Submission could be followed by restoration of autonomy and honour, so blanket loss of autonomy was not part of the policy.
xa: The policy was **conquest and conciliation**.
Prominent Rajputs: **Raja Man Singh**, **Raja Todarmal**, **Raja Birbal**.

nf7bfd9aee3f.s: Mewar finally submitted to the Mughals under which emperor?
nf7bfd9aee3f.x: Mewar submitted under Jahangir through Amar Singh, whose son Karan Singh became a mansabdar.
xa: Haldighati was **not decisive**.
Haldighati is a UPPSC **2023** question.

ndf7ce29c37b.s: The Zabti or Dahsala system was designed by
ndf7ce29c37b.x: Raja Todar Mal designed the Zabti, also called Bandobast or Dahsala, revenue system.
xs: **Raja Todar Mal** designed the **Zabti / Bandobast / Dahsala** system — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Abul Fazl** wrote the **Akbarnama**; **Man Singh** was a general; **Birbal** a wit and adviser.
xa: It was modelled on **Sher Shah's** survey-based system.
Land was measured with the bamboo **Gaz-i-Ilahi** (about **82** cm).
Revenue = **one-third** of average produce of the last **10** years.

o: A fixed cash rate per bigha
n2fbf360d1e9.x: Kankut estimated the standing crop; Batai was crop-sharing and Nasaq was based on past payments.
xa: **Zabti** used measurement and **10**-year averages, paid in cash.
Relief came through **Taccavi** loans.

na53ff701604.s: Under Akbar's Zabti system, land that had been left fallow for three to four years was classified as:
na53ff701604.x: Chachar was land fallow for 3-4 years. Polaj was cultivated every year, Parauti was fallow for 1-2 years, and Banjar was uncultivated for 5 years or more.
xs: Land fallow for **3-4 years** was **Chachar** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Polaj** = cultivated every year; **Parauti** = fallow **1-2** years; **Banjar** = uncultivated **5** years or more.
xa: Sher Shah had only **three** land classes.
Akbar-Todar Mal used **four** classes and **ten-year averages**.

n6250c89ad19.s: Akbar built the Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri in:
n6250c89ad19.x: The Ibadat Khana was built in 1575; 1582 is the year of Din-i-Ilahi.
xa: **1579**: the **Mahzar** made Akbar supreme arbiter.
Guiding principle: **Sulh-i-Kul**.

n0700226ad28.s: Which one of the following represents the central meaning of Sulh-i-Kul?
o: Compulsory conversion to a single faith
n0700226ad28.x: Sulh-i-Kul means universal peace or peace with all and served as a guiding principle of Akbar's policy.
n0700226ad28.tq: Discriminate the exact meaning of a Persian administrative-religious term.
xs: **Sulh-i-Kul** means **"peace with all"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was the **guiding principle** of Akbar's religious policy.
**Din-i-Ilahi** was **never forced** on anyone, so compulsory conversion is wrong.
xa: Measures: abolition of **jizya** (**1564**) and **pilgrimage tax** (**1563**), **Ibadat Khana**, **Mahzar**.
Shaikh Ahmad **Sirhindi** attacked Sulh-i-kul and Din-i-Ilahi.
Akbar's coins showed **Rama and Sita** with the legend **'Rama-Siya'**.

n1063d462cb1.s: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi was known as:
n1063d462cb1.x: Sirhindi was Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani and propounded Wahdat-ul-Shuhud.
xa: **Wahdat-ul-Wujud** was the stand of the **Qadiri** order; **Dara Shikoh** followed it.
Sirhindi attacked Akbar's **Sulh-i-kul** and **Din-i-Ilahi**.
The **Naqshbandi** order was founded by **Baha-ud-din Naqshband** and came to India with **Babur**.

nef284ffb126.s: Under Akbar, the Mahabharata was translated as the:
nef284ffb126.x: The Mahabharata was rendered as the Razmnama; the Atharvaveda was also translated.
xa: **Faizi** (Abul Fazl's brother) made the Persian **Lilavati**.
**Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan** made a Persian translation of the **Baburnama**.
**Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh** — **Badauni**; **Tabaqat-i-Akbari** — **Nizamuddin Ahmad**.

n8024bd338b7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Guru Tegh Bahadur?
o: He was the ninth Sikh Guru, born Tyag Mal in 1621.
He was executed by Jahangir in 1606.
n8024bd338b7.x: Execution by Jahangir in 1606 describes Guru Arjan Dev; Tegh Bahadur was executed on Aurangzeb's orders in Delhi in 1675.
xa: ⚠ **Sis Ganj Sahib** = execution site; **Rakab Ganj Sahib** = cremation site.
His martyrdom is observed as **Shaheedi Divas, 24 November**.
He was the son of **Guru Hargobind**.

n9c132a2a61b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Banda Singh Bahadur?
o: He was originally named Lachhman Dev.
He defeated Wazir Khan at Chappar Chiri and conquered Sirhind in 1710.
His sovereign Sikh state had its capital at Anandpur Sahib.
He was executed in Delhi in 1716 by Farrukhsiyar.
n9c132a2a61b.x: The capital of his Sikh state was Lohgarh; Anandpur Sahib was founded by Guru Tegh Bahadur.
xa: He founded the **first sovereign Sikh state**.
Sirhind was conquered to avenge the Guru's **younger sons**.
**Sirhind Fateh Diwas (12-14 May)** commemorates the **1710** conquest.

n5cb8a4598d0.s: Which Mughal emperor had the highest number of Hindu nobles and generals in absolute terms?
n5cb8a4598d0.x: Aurangzeb had the highest absolute number, many of them Marathas and Rajputs recruited during the Deccan wars.
xa: This is the counter-intuitive tested fact, since Aurangzeb **reversed tolerance** (jizya **1679**).
Aurangzeb also banned **Navroz** and patronised the **Fatawa-i-Alamgiri**.
Shah Jahan destroyed some **newly built temples**.

nb4cfb5f30e9.s: Which Mughal emperor, slightly more orthodox than Akbar, destroyed some newly built temples yet kept many Hindu nobles?
nb4cfb5f30e9.x: Shah Jahan was slightly more orthodox and destroyed some newly built temples but continued to employ many Hindu nobles.
xa: Shah Jahan abolished the **pilgrim tax at Banaras and Allahabad** after a deputation led by **Kavindracharya**.
**Aurangzeb** had the highest number of Hindu nobles in absolute terms.
Shah Jahan got his title from **Jahangir**.

n736670794da.x: Aurangzeb reimposed jizya in 1679 and banned festivals such as Navroz.
xa: The reversal is cited among the **causes of decline**.
Akbar had abolished jizya in **1564**.
⚠ Aurangzeb still had the **highest number of Hindu nobles** in absolute terms.

need446c17e3.s: Din-i-Ilahi, joined by only a handful of people, lapsed with the death of:
need446c17e3.x: Din-i-Ilahi lapsed with Akbar and did not continue as a major institution.
xa: Proclaimed **1582**; features: one God, greeting **"Allah-hu-Akbar"**, avoiding meat, reverence for **sun and fire**.
Members included **Abul Fazl**, **Faizi** and **Shaikh Mubarak**; **Birbal** was the only Hindu.
It was never forced on anyone.

n4d6160d5b44.s: Bhakta Ramadasu was related to Madanna and Akkanna as their:
n4d6160d5b44.x: Bhakta Ramadasu was the nephew of Madanna and Akkanna.
xa: Akbar's southern limit reached the **Godavari**.
**Ahmednagar (1600)**: Akbar's forces opposed **Chand Bibi**.
Akbar's **last campaign**: **Asirgarh (1601)** in Khandesh.

nce6c15d9a2a.s: Abul Fazl was murdered in 1602 by:
o: Man Singh I at Akbar's instance
Adham Khan at Bairam Khan's instance
Bir Singh Bundela at Salim's instance
nce6c15d9a2a.x: Abul Fazl was murdered in 1602 by Bir Singh Bundela at the instance of Prince Salim.
nce6c15d9a2a.tq: Use the wrong-person and wrong-instigator trap in a court event.
xs: **Abul Fazl** was murdered in **1602** by **Bir Singh Bundela** at **Salim's** instance — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Adham Khan** belongs to the **petticoat government**; **Hemu** died at **Panipat II**.
xa: Abul Fazl wrote the **Akbarnama** and **Ain-i-Akbari**.
He was the chief exponent of **Din-i-Ilahi**.
Order of deaths: **Sheikh Mubarak → Faizi → Abul Fazl → Prince Daniyal** (UPPSC **2024**).

n5b67f4b280c.s: Who translated the Baburnama into Persian?
n5b67f4b280c.x: Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan, son of Bairam Khan, translated the Baburnama into Persian.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly credit **Tabaqat-i-Akbari** to Badauni.
Faizi was **poet laureate** and Abul Fazl's brother.
The **Razmnama** is the translation of the **Mahabharata**.

nad92b5db426.s: Which one of Akbar's court figures, originally named Ramtanu Pandey, is associated with the ragas Miyan ki Malhar and Miyan ki Todi?
nad92b5db426.x: Tansen (Ramtanu Pandey) was the court musician credited with Miyan ki Malhar and Miyan ki Todi. Faizi was the poet laureate, Birbal (Mahesh Das) the wit and adviser, and Abdur Rahim a poet known for Hindi dohas.
xs: **Tansen** (Ramtanu Pandey) is linked to **Miyan ki Malhar** and **Miyan ki Todi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Faizi** was the **poet laureate**; **Birbal** (Mahesh Das) the wit and adviser; **Abdur Rahim** a poet of Hindi **dohas**.
xa: Tansen is credited with a **gharana** tradition and linked to **Gwalior**.
**Man Singh I** led the Mughals at Haldighati.

nindian-history-46-13.s: Who wrote Akbarnama and was associated with Akbar as a scholar and court intellectual?
nindian-history-46-13.x: Abul Fazl, Akbar's court historian, wrote the Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari and rendered the Panchatantra as Ayar-i-Danish. Faizi was his brother and poet laureate.
nindian-history-46-13.tq: Link the work to its author.
n: Abul Fazl was a scholar and court intellectual. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
Abul Fazl was associated with Akbar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 113-115]
xs: **Abul Fazl** — option **(1)**.
He wrote the **Akbarnama** and **Ain-i-Akbari** and was Akbar's **scholar and court intellectual**.
**Faizi**, his brother, was the **poet laureate**; **Nizamuddin Panipati** translated the **Yogavasistha** into Persian.
xa: Abul Fazl translated the **Panchatantra** into **Ayar-i-Danish**.
He was **murdered** in **1602** by **Bir Singh Bundela** at **Salim's** instance.
Order of deaths: **Sheikh Mubarak → Faizi → Abul Fazl → Prince Daniyal**.

n0e78d0a99e5.s: Which Mughal emperor issued coins bearing figures of Rama and Sita with the Devanagari legend 'Rama-Siya'?
n0e78d0a99e5.x: Akbar, in keeping with Sulh-i-Kul, issued coins with Rama and Sita and the legend 'Rama-Siya' (UPPSC 2011). Babur was an orthodox Sunni who took the title Ghazi, Jahangir is known for his own portrait/zodiac coinage, and Aurangzeb reversed tolerance.
xs: **Akbar** issued coins with **Rama and Sita** and the Devanagari legend **'Rama-Siya'** (UPPSC **2011**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Babur** was an orthodox Sunni who took the title **Ghazi**; **Aurangzeb** reversed tolerance.
xa: The coins reflect **Sulh-i-Kul** ("peace with all").
**Jahangir** broadly continued Akbar's tolerance.
Akbar was the **unlettered** emperor, yet a great patron.

n89010b5bc25.s: Who among the following criticised Din-i-Ilahi and Sulh-i-Kul from an orthodox Islamic standpoint?
n89010b5bc25.x: Badauni and the Naqshbandi scholar Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi criticised Akbar's religious innovations, including Din-i-Ilahi and Sulh-i-Kul.
n89010b5bc25.tq: Match the criticism with the correct orthodox scholars rather than with supporters or foreign visitors.
xs: Orthodox criticism of Akbar's religious innovations came from **Badauni** and the Naqshbandi **Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sirhindi** (**Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**) attacked Akbar's **Sulh-i-kul** and **Din-i-Ilahi**.
**Faizi** and **Abul Fazl** were members of Din-i-Ilahi; **Abul Fazl** was its chief exponent.
**Hiravijaya Suri** and **Jinachandra Suri** were Jain monks honoured by Akbar; **Acquaviva** and **Jerome Xavier** led Jesuit missions from Goa.
xa: **Naqshbandi** order: founded by **Baha-ud-din Naqshband**; came to India with **Babur**; stressed strict **Sharia**.
Sirhindi propounded **Wahdat-ul-Shuhud** (Unity of Appearance) against **Wahdat-ul-Wujud**.
**Badauni** wrote the **Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh**.
Din-i-Ilahi (**1582**) had about **18** members; **Birbal** was the only Hindu disciple.

n43df49ce756.s: Dara Shikoh was a follower of which Sufi order?
n43df49ce756.x: Dara Shikoh followed the Qadiri order, associated with Abdul Qadir Jilani.
xa: The Naqshbandi order came to India with **Babur** and stressed strict **Sharia**.
**Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi** (**Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**), a Naqshbandi, criticised **Sulh-i-kul** and **Din-i-Ilahi**.
Later Naqshbandi scholars: **Shah Waliullah** and **Shah Abdul Aziz**.

n432906613ce.s: Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed by Aurangzeb at Chandni Chowk, Delhi, in
n432906613ce.x: Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed at Chandni Chowk in Delhi in 1675 by order of Aurangzeb.
n432906613ce.tq: Match the execution site and ruler with the correct year.
xs: Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed at **Chandni Chowk, Delhi** in **1675** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was beheaded on **24 Nov 1675** on **Aurangzeb's** orders.
xa: **Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib** marks the execution site; **Rakab Ganj Sahib** the cremation site.
Called **"Hind-di-Chadar"** for shielding **Kashmiri Brahmins** from forced conversion.
**1699**: his son **Guru Gobind Singh** founded the **Khalsa** on Baisakhi.
Aurangzeb reimposed **jizya** in **1679**.

ndd9d5dee0b6.s: Under Akbar's Karori experiment (1574), each revenue circle was meant to yield:
ndd9d5dee0b6.x: Each circle was to yield one crore dams, hence the name 'karori'.
xa: **Raja Todar Mal** was **Diwan** of the empire and one of the **Navratnas**; he had served **Sher Shah**.
**Gaz-i-Ilahi** = unit of length, about **82 cm**.
The **jarib** used **bamboo pieces joined with iron rings** instead of hemp rope.

n8fd403ef53a.s: Under the Mughals, the Nasaq method of revenue assessment was mainly used in:
n8fd403ef53a.x: Nasaq was used mainly in Bengal; Batai in Thatta, Kabul and Kashmir, Zabti in the core provinces, plough-based assessment in parts of the Deccan.
xa: **Kankut** estimated the yield on the **standing crop** where measurement was impractical.
**Zabti** fixed cash rates per crop per **bigha** after measuring land.
**Batai** is also called **Ghalla-bakhshi**.

nf9156a9207a.s: The 'Bandobast' system of land revenue under Akbar is another name for:
nf9156a9207a.x: The Bandobast system is the Dahsala (Zabti) reform of Todar Mal, introduced in 1580 (JPSC 2013). Batai (ghalla-bakhshi) was crop-sharing, Nasaq a rough assessment from past records mainly in Bengal, and Iqta the Sultanate revenue assignment.
xs: The **Bandobast** system is another name for the **Dahsala** system — so option **(1)** is correct (JPSC **2013** key).
**Batai** was crop-sharing; **Nasaq** a rough assessment from past records, mainly in **Bengal**.
xa: Some notes use "**Zabti or Bandobast**" for the same **Todar Mal** reform.
Dahsala (**1580**) fixed revenue on the average produce and prices of the **last ten years**.
**Kankut** estimated yield on the **standing crop**.

n6755135828b.s: Together, the mansabdari and zabti-dahsala systems gave the Mughal state:
o: A salaried, transferable nobility and predictable cash revenue
A hereditary nobility and tribute from autonomous chiefs
Religious endowments in place of military service
Revenue in kind collected directly from every village
n6755135828b.x: Mansabdari and zabti-dahsala together provided a salaried, transferable nobility and a predictable stream of cash revenue.
xa: ⚠ Mughal mansabdars combined **civil-military** roles; the British **ICS** was purely civil with a fixed salary.
Dahsala (**1580**) fixed cash revenue on the average of the **last ten years**.
State share: **one-third**, paid in **dam**.

na523fcd30ab.s: The improved jarib used in land measurement was made of ____, which avoided shrinking or stretching.
o: Bamboo pieces joined with iron rings
na523fcd30ab.x: The jarib was made of bamboo pieces joined with iron rings, which avoided the shrinkage or stretching of hemp rope.
xa: The **Gaz-i-Ilahi** was the unit of length, about **82 cm**.
⚠ Some notes call the **gaz** itself a bamboo rod.
Measurement underpinned **Zabti**: land measured and cash rates fixed per crop per **bigha**.

nebe7ebafc7c.s: Todar Mal held which office in the Mughal Empire?
nebe7ebafc7c.x: Todar Mal served as the Diwan, or finance minister, of the empire and was also counted among the Navratnas.
nebe7ebafc7c.tq: Use the office–portfolio association while avoiding neighbouring central offices.
xs: **Raja Todar Mal** was the **Diwan (finance minister)** of the empire — so option **(1)** is correct.
He was also one of Akbar's **Navratnas** and designed the **dahsala** system.
xa: He had earlier served **Sher Shah** and built on his survey-based system.
Before dahsala, the **Karori experiment (1574)** put circles yielding **one crore dams** under **karoris**.
Under dahsala, the state share was **one-third** of average produce, paid in cash (**dam**).

n0838e6c72bc.s: Akbar's Dahsala system was introduced in:
n0838e6c72bc.x: Dahsala, based on ten-year average produce and prices commuted into cash, came in 1580; 1574 was the Karori experiment.
xa: Dahsala is also called **Ain-i-Dahsala**; it was the APPSC-G2 **2017** answer.
**Bandobast** system = **Dahsala** (JPSC **2013** key).
State share: **one-third** of average produce, paid in **dam**.

n183f8e4334a.s: Under Akbar's land classification, land left fallow for one or two years was called:
n183f8e4334a.x: Parauti lay fallow one or two years; Polaj was cultivated every year, Chachar fallow three or four years, Banjar five or more.
xa: ⚠ Do not confuse **Parauti** (1-2 yrs) with **Chachar** (3-4 yrs).
Relief measures: **Taccavi** loans and remissions.
Golconda's classes were different: **wet, dry, garden, waste**.

ne0663c69686.s: The head of a Mughal suba, served by a Diwan, Bakhshi, Sadr and Qazi, was the:
ne0663c69686.x: The Subedar headed the suba; the Diwan, Bakhshi, Sadr and Qazi were the other suba officials.
xa: **Sarkar**: **Faujdar** (law and order) and **amalguzar** (revenue).
**Pargana**: **Shiqdar**, amil, qanungo.

na289a7fc6ca.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about land revenue in Qutb Shahi Golconda?
o: Land was classified as wet, dry, garden and waste.
The khalisa was expanded under Abdullah and Tana Shah.
Revenue was collected through amalguzars with hereditary deshmukhs and deshpandes.
The state generally took one-half of the produce.
na289a7fc6ca.x: Golconda generally took one-third of the produce, not one-half.
xa: Mughal dahsala also took **one-third** of average produce.
Mughal land classes: **Polaj, Parauti, Chachar, Banjar**.
In the Mughal **sarkar**, the **amalguzar** handled revenue.

n93bf8597687.s: Mughal crown land whose revenue went straight to the imperial treasury was called:
n93bf8597687.x: Crown land was khalisa; suyurghal and madad-i-maash were charitable revenue-free grants.
xa: **Khalisa** revenue went straight to the imperial treasury; cash (**naqd**) salaries were paid from it.
A **jagir** was a right to collect revenue in lieu of salary — not ownership.
Khalisa expanded in Golconda under **Abdullah** and **Tana Shah**.

na293e846978.s: A jagir under the Mughal system represented:
o: A direct cash payment from the khalisa treasury
The right to collect revenue in lieu of salary, without ownership
A permanent revenue-free grant to scholars
na293e846978.x: A jagir was an assignment of the right to collect revenue in lieu of salary; it did not confer ownership of the land.
na293e846978.tq: Apply the distinction between revenue-collection rights and ownership.
xs: A **jagir** was the **right to collect revenue in lieu of salary**, not ownership — so option **(3)** is correct.
Direct cash salaries came from **khalisa** revenue (**naqd**); revenue-free grants to scholars were **madad-i-maash**.
xa: Mansabdars held **non-hereditary**, combined civil-military ranks **paid by jagir**.
⚠ British **ICS** = purely civil, fixed salary from the treasury.
**Suyurghal** = another name for charitable revenue-free grants.

ne6fab38c861.s: Jahangir's eldest son Khusrau rebelled in:
ne6fab38c861.x: Khusrau rebelled in 1606; Khurram's revolt (1622-26) was the one provoked by Nur Jahan backing Shahryar.
xa: Khusrau was **blinded** and later died (**1622**) in Khurram's custody.
**Shahryar** was Nur Jahan's **son-in-law**.
**1626**: **Mahabat Khan** seized Jahangir on the **Jhelum**.

n44e59c3f239.s: Jahangir lost Kandahar to Persia in:
n44e59c3f239.x: Jahangir annexed neither Kabul nor Kandahar; he lost Kandahar to Persia in 1622.
xa: Amar Singh's son **Karan Singh** became a **mansabdar**.
English factory at **Surat** came in **1613**.
Kandahar was recovered (**1638**) and finally lost (**1649**) under **Shah Jahan**.

nc2f716e1ee8.s: Which tribes were involved in the Afghan revolt against Aurangzeb?
nc2f716e1ee8.x: The Afghan revolt involved the Yusufzai and Afridi tribes of the north-west.
nc2f716e1ee8.tq: Distinguish tribal groups from the regional and dynastic participants in other revolts.
xs: The Afghan revolt involved the **Yusufzai and Afridi** tribes of the north-west — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Jats** (Mathura) and **Satnamis** (Narnaul) were separate revolts; **Marathas and Rajputs** were other opponents.
xa: Jats: under **Gokula** (**1669**).
Satnamis: **Narnaul** (**1672**).
Rajputs: **Marwar and Mewar**, under **Durgadas Rathore**.

nindian-history-63-17.s: In Akbar's reign, Salim Chishti is associated with:
nindian-history-63-17.x: Salim Chishti lived at Sikri in Akbar's time.
n: Guru Arjan Dev was executed during the reign of Jahangir. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 138-139]
Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed during the reign of Aurangzeb. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 138-139]
Salim Chishti was associated with Sikri during the reign of Akbar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 138-139]
xa: **Fa-Hien** visited under **Chandragupta II**; **Hiuen-Tsang** under **Harsha**.
**Ibn Battuta** came under **Muhammad bin Tughluq**.
Arjan Dev was executed for supporting rebel prince **Khusrau**.

nbba482b3e6f.s: Nur Jahan's father, who served as Jahangir's diwan, was:
nbba482b3e6f.x: Ghiyas Beg was Nur Jahan's father and Jahangir's diwan; Asaf Khan was her brother.
xa: **Asaf Khan** was **Khan-i-Saman** and later Shah Jahan's key adviser.
The junta ran the empire for about **ten years**.
Nur Jahan's name on coins is a standard **"first/only"** question.

n862d695454d.s: Nur Jahan wrote poetry under the pen name
n862d695454d.x: Nur Jahan was also a poet and used the pen name Makhfi.
n862d695454d.tq: Identify the literary pseudonym associated with the political personality.
xs: Nur Jahan wrote poetry under the pen name **"Makhfi"** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Jahanara** was Shah Jahan's **daughter**; **Padshah** was a title, not her pen name.
xa: Her titles: **Nur Jahan** ("Light of the World"), later **Padshah Begum**.
She built the **tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah** (Agra), with marble inlay — a precursor of the Taj.
Born **Mehrunnisa** in **1577** at **Kandahar**.

n7d56aac593a.x: Nur Jahan married Jahangir in 1611 and received the title Padshah Begum.
xa: **Mumtaz Mahal** was Asaf Khan's daughter.
She was the widow of **Sher Afghan**.
The junta split when she pushed **Shahryar** as heir.

nd3add5f0957.s: The tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah at Agra, noted for its marble inlay and regarded as a precursor of the Taj Mahal, was built by:
nd3add5f0957.x: Nur Jahan built the tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah (her father, Ghiyas Beg) at Agra. Ghiyas Beg was also Jahangir's diwan, and Asaf Khan was his son, but the builder was Nur Jahan; Shah Jahan's father-in-law was Asaf Khan, not Itimad-ud-Daulah.
nd3add5f0957.tq: Itimad-ud-Daulah's tomb = Nur Jahan for her father ('Baby Taj').
xs: **Nur Jahan** built the tomb of **Itimad-ud-Daulah** for **her father** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Itimad-ud-Daulah = **Ghiyas Beg**, Jahangir's **diwan**; the tomb's **marble inlay** made it a precursor of the Taj.
**Asaf Khan** was Ghiyas Beg's son, not the builder; Shah Jahan's father-in-law was **Asaf Khan**.
xa: Nur Jahan was also a poet, pen name **"Makhfi"**.
The **Taj Mahal** holds **Mumtaz Mahal**.
Jahangir's own tomb is at **Shahdara (Lahore)**.

nc9fbbd139b6.x: Mumtaz Mahal, born Arjumand Banu Begum, was Asaf Khan's daughter and is entombed in the Taj Mahal.
xa: She married **Prince Khurram** in **1612**.
Asaf Khan was **Nur Jahan's brother**, so Mumtaz was Nur Jahan's niece.
Asaf Khan later became **Shah Jahan's key adviser**.

n4ff807da693.s: Jahangir gave William Hawkins a mansab and the title:
n4ff807da693.x: Hawkins received the title 'English Khan'; trading rights came later through Sir Thomas Roe.
xa: Hawkins was sent by **James I** of England.
⚠ **Roe** = official ambassador (**1615-1619**) who **won trade rights**.
**Captain Best's** naval win (**1612**) led to the **Surat factory (1613)**.

nba92238295d.s: The English factory at Surat was established in:
nba92238295d.x: The Surat factory came in 1613, after Captain Best's 1612 victory over the Portuguese off Surat.
xa: **Hawkins** had reached Surat in **1608** but failed to get a farman.
**Sir Thomas Roe** (**1615-1619**) followed the moving court (**Ajmer, Mandu**) and won trade rights.
All of this falls in **Jahangir's** reign.

ne150b433ccc.s: Sir Thomas Roe's embassy to Jahangir secured for the English:
o: Rights to trade and establish factories
