xa: Abdali's motive: the Marathas had driven his son **Timur Shah** out of the Punjab.
Maratha commander: **Sadashiv Rao Bhau**.

nc0613be513f.s: The First Anglo-Maratha War arose from a succession dispute after the murder of:
nc0613be513f.x: The war arose from the succession dispute after Narayan Rao's murder, when Raghunath Rao turned to the British.
xa: Barabhai = **twelve chiefs** led by **Nana Phadnavis**.
⚠ **Surat (1775)** = British back Raghunath Rao; **Purandar (1776)** = annulled; **Salbai (1782)** = end.

nb0995431c2b.s: The Treaty of Salbai of 1782 was concluded between
o: Lord Hastings and Baji Rao II
nb0995431c2b.x: The Treaty of Salbai was concluded in 1782 between Warren Hastings and Mahadji Scindia. It restored the status quo and helped establish peace for twenty years.
nb0995431c2b.tq: Discriminate the negotiators from the leaders associated with other Maratha wars.
xs: **Salbai (1782)** was concluded with **Mahadji Scindia**, in **Warren Hastings**'s time — option **(1)**.
It **ended the First Anglo-Maratha War** and kept the **status quo**.
**Lord Hastings** belongs to the Third war; **Baji Rao II** to Bassein (**1802**).
xa: Salbai = **first Anglo-Maratha peace**; it recognised **Madhav Rao II**.
⚠ **Warren Hastings** = First war (rejected Wadgaon); **Lord Hastings** = Third war.

n3b589f9981c.s: The death of Nana Phadnavis in 1800 was followed by which development?
o: The Marathas immediately restored Mughal authority at Delhi
The Nizam recognised Maratha control over Malwa
Holkar and Scindia fought over the weak Peshwa, contributing to the Treaty of Bassein and the Second Anglo-Maratha War
Baji Rao I founded the Barabhai council
n3b589f9981c.x: After Nana Phadnavis’s death, Holkar and Scindia competed for influence over the weak Peshwa in 1801–02. This contributed to the Treaty of Bassein and the Second Anglo-Maratha War.
n3b589f9981c.tq: Follow the political cause-and-effect sequence after a leader’s death.
xs: After Nana Phadnavis died (**1800**), **Holkar and Scindia fought over the weak Peshwa**, leading to **Bassein** and the **Second War** — option **(3)**.
The fight took place in **1801-02**.
xa: **Treaty of Bassein (1802)** was signed by **Baji Rao II** = **subsidiary subordination**.
Holkar's seat = **Indore**; Scindia's = **Gwalior**.

n91a97bb3dbe.s: Which Governor-General rejected the Convention of Wadgaon (1779)?
n91a97bb3dbe.x: After the British defeat at Talegaon, the Convention of Wadgaon forced them to give up their gains, but Warren Hastings rejected it.
xa: ⚠ **Surat (1775)** = British back Raghunath Rao; **Purandar (1776)** = annulled; **Salbai (1782)** = end.
⚠ **Warren Hastings** = First war; **Lord Hastings** = Third war.

nbe648b4243e.s: Who was the Governor-General of India during the Third Anglo-Maratha War?
nbe648b4243e.x: The Third Anglo-Maratha War was fought during the tenure of Lord Hastings, also known as the Marquess of Hastings.
nbe648b4243e.tq: Apply the who-was-in-office trap to distinguish neighbouring Governor-Generals.
xs: The Governor-General in the Third Anglo-Maratha War was **Lord Hastings** (Marquess of Hastings) — option **(1)**.
Causes: his **imperial designs** and the **Pindari campaigns**.
xa: ⚠ **Warren Hastings** was GG in the First war and rejected **Wadgaon**.
Outcome: **Peshwaship abolished in 1818**.

nb077db96eb0.s: Which of the following battles was NOT associated with the Third Anglo-Maratha War?
nb077db96eb0.x: Khadki, Koregaon, Sitabuldi and Mahidpur were associated with the Third Anglo-Maratha War. Assaye belonged to the Second Anglo-Maratha War.
nb077db96eb0.tq: Find the battle belonging to the neighbouring war rather than the listed conflict.
xs: **Assaye** is the battle NOT of the Third Anglo-Maratha War — option **(4)**.
The Third war's battles were **Khadki (Kirkee)**, **Koregaon**, **Sitabuldi** and **Mahidpur**.
xa: The war was fought in **1817-18** (some notes say **1817-19**).
**Nagpur (Bhonsle)** and **Indore (Holkar)** joined the Peshwa.

n727703ee075.s: After Shahu's reign real power in the Maratha state passed from the Chhatrapati at Satara to the Peshwa, whose seat of power was at
n727703ee075.x: Poona (Pune) was the Peshwas' seat of power (APPSC 2018). Nagpur was the seat of the Bhonsles, Kolhapur of Tarabai's line, and Raigad was Shivaji's capital and coronation site.
xs: The Peshwas' seat of power was **Poona** (Pune) — option **(3)** (APPSC **2018**).
**Nagpur** was the **Bhonsle** seat; **Kolhapur** was Tarabai's line; **Raigad** was Shivaji's capital.
xa: ⚠ **Holkar** = Indore; **Scindia** = Gwalior; **Gaekwad** = Baroda; **Bhonsle** = Nagpur.
**Peshwa Daftar** at Pune holds Peshwa-era records, largely in **Modi script**.
n727703ee075.fixed: Chhatrapati became a non-entity only under Balaji Bajirao (Sangola 1750), not from 1713 (y3f7a87a1593)

nab3ba0ed9f9.s: The Treaty of Mungi-Shevgaon was concluded between
o: the Marathas and the English East India Company
nab3ba0ed9f9.x: Mungi-Shevgaon was a treaty between the Marathas and the Nizam (APPSC 2025), signed after Baji Rao I defeated the Nizam at Palkhed (1728); it conceded chauth and sardeshmukhi of the Deccan. It did not involve the Mughals, the English or the Portuguese.
nab3ba0ed9f9.tq: Palkhed battle -> Mungi-Shevgaon treaty, Marathas vs Nizam.
xs: **Mungi-Shevgaon** was between **the Marathas and the Nizam** — option **(4)** (APPSC **2025**).
It came after **Baji Rao I** beat the Nizam at **Palkhed (1728)**.
It did not involve the Mughals, the English or the Portuguese.
xa: Repeated defeats of the Nizam: **Palkhed, Udgir, Kharda**.
**1795**: the Nizam blamed **Sir John Shore**'s neutrality → **Subsidiary Alliance (1798)**.

n312c890b897.s: The Nizam, defeated by the Marathas in 1795, blamed his defeat on the neutrality of:
n312c890b897.x: The Nizam blamed Sir John Shore's neutrality, which pushed him to the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.
xa: Kharda was won under **Madhav Rao II**.
Earlier defeats of the Nizam: **Palkhed**, **Udgir**.

n55b21ed5c09.s: The word ‘bhakti’ is derived from the root ‘bhaj’, which means:
n55b21ed5c09.x: The word bhakti is derived from the root bhaj, meaning to share or participate.
xs: **Bhaj** means **to share or participate** — option **(3)**.
Bhakti derives from this root.
xa: The **Bhagavata Purana** first put bhakti at the **centre of religion**.
It lists **ninefold (navadha) bhakti**: shravana, kirtana, smarana, padasevana, archana, vandana, dasya, sakhya, atmanivedana.

n967ebe95361.s: Which text put bhakti at the centre of religion and described a ninefold bhakti?
n967ebe95361.x: The Bhagavata Purana put bhakti at the centre; its ninefold bhakti includes kirtana, smarana and atmanivedana.
xa: Dating: some notes say the **6th c.**; most scholars **c. 9th-10th c.**
Other roots of bhakti: the **Upanishads** and the **Bhagavad Gita**.

nc6eb145c1d5.s: Which of the following is NOT regarded as a root of the Bhakti movement?
nc6eb145c1d5.x: The Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita and Bhagavata Purana are identified as roots of the Bhakti movement; the Arthashastra is not.
xa: **Gita Chapter 12 = Bhakti Yoga**.
Both streams drew on the **Upanishadic doctrine of Advaita**.

n974838d8f03.s: Which one of the following sequences represents the beginning of the Bhakti movement and its later spread most accurately?
o: Tamil region in the sixth–ninth centuries, followed by spread to northern India by the fifteenth century
Northern India in the fifteenth century, followed by spread to Tamil Nadu in the eighteenth century
Bengal in the ninth century, followed by spread to Tamil Nadu in the twelfth century
Rajasthan in the sixth century, followed by spread to Tamil Nadu in the fifteenth century
n974838d8f03.x: The movement first developed in the Tamil region through the Alvars and Nayanars during the sixth–ninth centuries and reached the northern belt by the fifteenth century. Its overall span is described as the sixth to the eighteenth century.
n974838d8f03.tq: Use the first regional centre and the later northern expansion to establish sequence.
xs: Bhakti began in the **Tamil region (6th-9th c.)** and reached **northern India by the 15th c.** — option **(1)**.
It started with the **Alvars and Nayanars**.
xa: Overall span: **6th to 18th c.**
**Ramananda** brought it to the north.

ndbb15c0e7bb.s: The Alvars and Nayanars, who challenged Brahmanical dominance, came from:
ndbb15c0e7bb.x: The Alvars and Nayanars came from different castes, high and low, and challenged Brahmanical dominance.
xa: ⚠ **Alvars = 12** (Vishnu); **Nayanars = 63** (Shiva).
Women saints include **Andal** and **Karaikkal Ammaiyar**.

n8f91224f35d.s: The Nalayira Divya Prabandham, the "Tamil Veda" of 4,000 Alvar hymns, was compiled by:
n8f91224f35d.x: The Nalayira Divya Prabandham contains 4,000 Alvar hymns and was compiled by Nathamuni.
xa: ⚠ "Tamil Veda" = **Nalayira Divya Prabandham**; "Fifth Veda" = **Tirumurai**.
**Alvars = 12** Vishnu devotees.

n3e49520c1d3.x: The Tiruvasagam is by Manikkavachakar; Sekkizhar wrote the Periya Puranam.
xa: Tevaram = the first seven books of the **Tirumurai**.
Periya Puranam was written under **Kulottunga II** on the **63 Nayanars**.

n3eccdc2ffb7.s: The Tirumurai, the 12-book Shaiva canon called the "Fifth Veda", was compiled by:
n3eccdc2ffb7.x: Nambi Andar Nambi compiled the 12 books of the Tirumurai; Sekkizhar's Periya Puranam is its 12th book.
xa: Sekkizhar wrote it under **Kulottunga II**.
⚠ "Tamil Veda" is the Alvars' **Nalayira Divya Prabandham**.

nc6ae2807231.s: How many Nayanars (Shiva devotees) were there?
nc6ae2807231.x: There were sixty-three Nayanars, devotees of Shiva, and twelve Alvars, devotees of Vishnu.
xa: Alvar hymns: **Nalayira Divya Prabandham** (**4,000** hymns).
Nayanar lives: **Periya Puranam** by **Sekkizhar**.

nf3c2d27fad5.s: The Bhakti movement arose partly because ordinary people found which paths difficult?
nf3c2d27fad5.x: The paths of knowledge (gyana) and action (karma) were considered difficult for ordinary people, alongside reaction against ritualism, priestly dominance and caste.
xa: Core beliefs: **monotheism**, **guru essential**, **salvation through devotion**.
Limit: it only **moderated** caste rigidity.

nd697a8d0f93.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of Nirguna saints?
o: Surdas, Guru Nanak, Chaitanya and Dadu Dayal
Kabir, Guru Nanak, Dadu Dayal and Ravidas
nd697a8d0f93.x: Kabir, Guru Nanak, Dadu Dayal and Ravidas are associated with the Nirguna stream, which worships a formless God.
nd697a8d0f93.tq: Classify each saint by the stream with which he is associated.
xs: **Kabir, Guru Nanak, Dadu Dayal and Ravidas** are all **Nirguna** saints — option **(2)**.
**Surdas, Chaitanya, Tulsidas, Mirabai** are **Saguna** saints.
xa: Kabir as Nirguna was asked in **APPSC GS 2024**.
⚠ **Ramamargi** = Tulsidas; **Krishnamargi** = Surdas, Mirabai, Chaitanya.

n9728e976c3d.s: Tulsidas belonged to which branch of the Saguna Vaishnava stream?
n9728e976c3d.x: Saguna Vaishnavas split into Ramamargis and Krishnamargis; Tulsidas, a devotee of Rama, was a Ramamargi.
xa: **Vallabha** was also a Krishnamargi.
⚠ **Ramcharitmanas** = Awadhi; **Sur Sagar** = Braj.

nf7856de736d.s: Who is regarded as the first medieval reformer to denounce caste outright?
nf7856de736d.x: Ramananda is described as the first medieval reformer to denounce caste outright and he admitted disciples from all castes.
nf7856de736d.tq: Recall the reformer linked with the strongest anti-caste position.
xs: **Ramananda** was the **first medieval reformer to denounce caste outright** — option **(3)**.
He **admitted disciples of all castes** and brought bhakti to the **north**.
xa: His disciples: **Kabir** (weaver), **Raidas** (shoemaker), **Dhanna** (Jat cultivator), **Sena** (barber).
⚠ **Ramanuja → Ramananda → Kabir / Ravidas → Mirabai**.

n9bed7526948.s: Akkamahadevi was a 12th-century woman saint of:
n9bed7526948.x: Akkamahadevi was a 12th-century woman saint of Karnataka.
xa: Other women saints: **Mirabai**, **Daya Bai**.
**Andal** = the only female Alvar.

n2caa39d092f.s: Which of the following best describes the social impact of the Bhakti movement?
o: It strengthened priestly dominance and rigid caste practices
It brought Hindus and Muslims closer and weakened caste bondage, without ending caste
It permanently established Hindu-Muslim unity and abolished caste
It remained confined to one linguistic region and one social group
n2caa39d092f.x: The movement brought Hindus and Muslims closer and weakened caste bondage, but did not achieve lasting unity or abolish caste.
xa: It only **moderated** caste rigidity.
Vernacular literature flourished across regions.

ncb99e3172eb.s: Who was the only female Alvar?
ncb99e3172eb.x: Andal was the only female Alvar.
xa: ⚠ **Ramanuja → Ramananda → Kabir / Ravidas → Mirabai**.
**Shankaracharya** (**788-820**) was a forerunner.

nindian-history-22-3.s: The Bhakti movement challenged caste hierarchy by placing devotion above:
nindian-history-22-3.x: The Bhakti saints placed devotion above birth and status, and that is how they challenged caste hierarchy.
n: The Bhakti Movement emphasized devotion over birth and status. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
The Bhakti Movement challenged caste hierarchy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
xa: **Guru Nanak**'s **Guru Ka Langar** = common dining without caste discrimination.
**Alvars and Nayanars** came from **all castes, high and low**.
Limit: it only **moderated** caste rigidity to an extent.

n9859b1caec4.s: The Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis made devotional religion popular mainly in:
n9859b1caec4.x: They made devotional religion popular in Northern India; their practices included hatha yoga, meditation and renunciation.
xa: Leading figures: **Gorakhnath**, **Matsyendranath**.
They used the **vernacular** and influenced **Kabir's nirguna idiom**.

nbcb207b912a.s: Gorakhnath and Matsyendranath were leading figures of which group?
nbcb207b912a.x: Gorakhnath and Matsyendranath were leading figures of the Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis, who criticised caste, ritualism and orthodox religion.
xa: Practices: **hatha yoga, meditation, renunciation**.
They popularised devotion in **Northern India** (BPSC **2023**).

n1af36146437.s: Both the Nirguna and Saguna streams drew upon which Upanishadic doctrine?
n1af36146437.x: Both Nirguna and Saguna traditions drew on the Upanishadic doctrine of Advaita; the movement was essentially monotheistic.
xa: **Shankaracharya** (b. **788**, Kaladi) was the Advaita forerunner.
**Gita Chapter 12** holds both Saguna and Nirguna **valid**.

n9ea79848567.s: Daya Bai was a disciple of:
n9ea79848567.x: Daya Bai was a disciple of Charandas.
xs: **Daya Bai** was a disciple of **Charandas** — option **(2)** (RPSC **2018**).
**Ravidas**'s disciple was **Mirabai**; **Ramananda**'s were Kabir, Raidas, Dhanna and Sena.
xa: **Namdev**'s disciple: **Janabai**.
**Vallabhacharya**'s disciple: **Surdas**.

n858cb7c45d9.s: Who was the guru of Mirabai?
xa: **Charandas — Daya Bai** (RPSC **2018**).
Ramananda's disciples: **Kabir, Raidas, Dhanna, Sena**.

n21197123bca.s: Who among the following was described as the most influential saint of the Maharashtra Bhakti tradition?
n21197123bca.x: Namdev was identified as the most influential saint of the Maharashtra tradition; Eknath, Tukaram and Narhari were also associated with it.
n21197123bca.tq: Distinguish the leading figure from other members of the same regional group.
xs: **Namdev** was the **most influential** Maharashtra saint — option **(4)**.
**Eknath, Tukaram and Narhari** also belong to this Marathi tradition.
xa: **Tukaram** composed **abhangas**.
Namdev's disciple was **Janabai**.

nd7a2ca8a25b.s: Veerashaivism reached Andhra through Palkuriki Somanatha and:
nd7a2ca8a25b.x: Veerashaivism reached Andhra through Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya and Palkuriki Somanatha.
xa: **Palnadu**: **Veeravaishnavism** + the Chapakudu.
**Panditaradhya** is also among the **Panchacharyas**.

n462439e484e.s: Vallabhacharya, the exponent of Pushtimarg, was:
o: A Telugu Brahmin who visited Krishnadevaraya's court
A Sufi saint who founded Dera Sachkhand Ballan
A Marathi saint who served Shivaji
A Tamil Alvar who composed the Jnaneshwari
n462439e484e.x: Vallabhacharya was a Telugu Brahmin who visited the court of Krishnadevaraya.
n462439e484e.tq: Use the person–regional identity–court association without confusing it with other saint traditions.
xs: **Vallabhacharya** was a **Telugu Brahmin** who visited **Krishnadevaraya's** court — option **(1)**.
**Dera Sachkhand Ballan** is the Ravidassia seat, unrelated to him.
xa: His disciple was **Surdas**.
He was a **Krishnamargi** Saguna Vaishnava.
n462439e484e.fixed: odd stem wording ('described in the Andhra-related context')

n1ef2d29e5bb.x: Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi.
xa: ⚠ **Ramcharitmanas** = Awadhi; **Sur Sagar** = Braj.
**Namdev** was the most influential Maharashtra saint.
n1ef2d29e5bb.fixed: stem said 'which one pair' but uses multi-item codes

n8b4eac621bd.s: Modern scholars trace the indigenous roots of the Bhakti movement to the:
n8b4eac621bd.x: Modern scholars emphasise the movement's indigenous Alvar–Nayanar roots and see Islam as influencing mainly its later egalitarianism.
xa: Bhakti began in the **Tamil region (6th-9th c.)**.
It brought **Hindus and Muslims closer**, but lasting unity was not achieved.

ne7ec495e229.s: Vallabhacharya’s teaching is best described as
o: Dvaita, with exclusive emphasis on ritual sacrifice
Shuddhadvaita, with Pushtimarg and Vatsalya bhakti
Vishishtadvaita, with rejection of Krishna worship
Advaita, with salvation through knowledge alone
ne7ec495e229.x: Vallabhacharya taught Shuddhadvaita or pure non-dualism. He advocated Pushtimarg, the path of grace, Vatsalya bhakti towards child Krishna and householder life for devotees.
ne7ec495e229.tq: Combine school, path and devotional emphasis to identify the precise option.
xs: Vallabhacharya taught **Shuddhadvaita**, with **Pushtimarg** and **Vatsalya bhakti** — option **(2)**.
Pushtimarg = "**path of grace**"; vatsalya bhakti to **child Krishna**; **householder life** for devotees.
xa: He set up **84** Pushtimarg centres.
Pushtimarga = Vallabhacharya (APPSC-G1 **2018**).

n304d9e86eb1.s: Ramananda's principal object of devotion was:
n304d9e86eb1.x: Ramananda worshipped Rama; child Krishna was the focus of Vallabha.
xa: Ramananda **replaced Vishnu worship with devotion to Rama**.
**Chaitanya**'s deity: **Krishna**.

n26996262ffc.s: Which acharya's tradition worshipped child Krishna along with Radha-Krishna?
n26996262ffc.x: Vallabha worshipped child Krishna and Radha-Krishna; Ramananda worshipped Rama, Chaitanya Krishna and Nimbarka Radha-Krishna.
xa: Chaitanya founded **Gaudiya Vaishnavism**.
Nimbarka's centre: **Brindavan**.

ne194e409a66.s: Who was the first Bhakti saint to preach in Hindi?
ne194e409a66.x: Ramananda was the first Bhakti saint to preach in Hindi; he replaced Vishnu worship with devotion to Rama.
xa: Ramananda and his Muslim disciple **Kabir** helped Hindi grow.
His centre: **Varanasi**.

n: Shankaracharya was associated with Bhakti and philosophy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Shankaracharya propounded Advaitavada. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Ramanuja was associated with Bhakti and philosophy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Ramanuja propounded Vishishtadvaita. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Tulsidas was associated with Bhakti. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Ramcharitmanas was written in Awadhi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Raskhan wrote Prem Vatika. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xa: **Madhva** = **Dvaita**; **Nimbarka** = **Dvaitadvaita**; **Vallabha** = **Shuddhadvaita**.
Shankara (**788-820**) = forerunner; Ramanuja (**1017-1137**) = **first true exponent** of Bhakti.
**Ramananda** = first Bhakti saint to preach in **Hindi**.

n1a5cc4eec61.s: Which exponent of monism (Advaita) is regarded as a forerunner of the Bhakti cult?
n1a5cc4eec61.x: Shankaracharya taught Advaita or monism and is described as a forerunner of the Bhakti cult.
xa: ⚠ Shankara = forerunner (Advaita, knowledge); **Ramanuja** = first true exponent (devotion).
Dates: **788-820**, born at **Kaladi**.

naadad4053c5.x: Gaudiya Vaishnavism was associated with Chaitanya; Pushtimarga with Vallabhacharya and Sri Vaishnava with Ramanuja.
xa: **Brahma (Madhva) Sampradaya** = Madhvacharya.
**Nimbarka (Sanaka) Sampradaya** = Nimbarka.

n3bfb8362e18.s: Pushtimarga, the "path of grace", is also called the:
n3bfb8362e18.x: Pushtimarga is the Vallabha Sampradaya; Vallabhacharya set up 84 Pushtimarg centres.
xa: Pushtimarga ("a religion of grace") = Vallabhacharya (APPSC-G1 **2018**).
"**Shashti Margam**" in some notes is a misprint for Pushti Margam.

n53a9452e39f.s: Vedanta Desika is associated with which sub-sect of Sri Vaishnavism?
n53a9452e39f.x: Sri Vaishnavism split into Vadakalai, associated with Vedanta Desika, and Tengalai; both remained Vishishtadvaita.
xa: ⚠ Trap: calling Tengalai "**Dvaita-influenced**" is wrong.
Vedanta Desika spread Vadakalai in Andhra in the **14th c.**

n3eb0d0c6ffa.s: Vedanta Parijata Saurabha was written by:
n3eb0d0c6ffa.x: Nimbarka wrote Vedanta Parijata Saurabha; Vallabhacharya wrote Anubhashya, Subodhini and Vedanta Rahasyam.
xa: **Sri Bhashya** = Ramanuja.
**Tattva Teeka**, **Nyaya Siddhanjanam** = Vedanta Desika.

n7994bc81d83.s: Which work of Krishnadevaraya, containing the Mala Dasari Katha, is regarded as a prime literary example of the inclusion of lower groups?
n7994bc81d83.x: Krishnadevaraya's Amuktamalyada, referred to in this context as Mala Dasari Katha, is cited as a prime example of social inclusion.
n7994bc81d83.tq: Discriminate between the correct author–work association and plausible literary substitutions.
xs: **Amuktamalyada**, the "**Mala Dasari Katha**", is the prime example — option **(3)**.
It illustrates Sri Vaishnavism giving **Panchamas temple entry**.
xa: Krishnadevaraya's royal guru was **Vyasa Tirtha**.
**Vallabha** visited Krishnadevaraya's court.
n7994bc81d83.fixed: Mala Dasari Katha is an episode within Amuktamalyada, not another name for it

n2da4d7b7cf5.x: Sriperumbudur was the birthplace of Ramanuja; Shankaracharya is linked to Kaladi and Madhva to Udupi.
xa: Nimbarka's school: **Dvaitadvaita**; deity **Radha-Krishna**.
Kaladi lies in **Malabar, Kerala**.

n03121aec4d4.x: Madhva's main centre was the Udupi Krishna Matha; Ramanuja's was Srirangam, Nimbarka's Brindavan and Ramananda's Varanasi.
xa: **Vallabha** preached Krishna bhakti in **Gujarat**, Varanasi and Braj.
Shankara's **Sringeri** head **Vidyaranya** was the Vijayanagara-era proponent.

nae9bad9893e.s: Which disciple of Ramananda was a barber by background?
nae9bad9893e.x: Sena was a barber; Kabir was a weaver, Raidas a shoemaker and Dhanna a Jat cultivator.
xa: Other disciples: **Padmavati** (woman), **Pipa** (Rajput ruler).
Ramananda's dictum: "**Let no man ask a man's sect or caste.**"

nca48be35159.s: Vallabhacharya visited the court of which ruler, where he refuted Shaiva propositions and defeated Vyasaraya?
nca48be35159.x: Vallabhacharya visited the court of Krishnadevaraya, refuted Shaiva propositions and defeated the Dvaita scholar Vyasaraya, also known as Vyasa Tirtha.
nca48be35159.tq: Match the religious debate with the correct ruler’s court.
xs: Vallabhacharya visited the court of **Krishnadevaraya** — option **(4)**.
There he **refuted Shaiva propositions** and **defeated** the Dvaita scholar **Vyasaraya** (Vyasa Tirtha).
xa: ⚠ Vallabha **defeated** Vyasaraya; Vyasa Tirtha = **royal guru** of Krishnadevaraya.
Vallabha came from a **Telugu Brahmin family**.
**Saluva Narasimha** also had Vyasa Tirtha as royal guru.

n1f37f7d1312.s: In Andhra, Sri Vaishnavism was patronised by the Palnati Haihayas and the:
n1f37f7d1312.x: The Velanati Cholas and the Palnati Haihayas patronised Sri Vaishnavism in Andhra.
xa: It inspired **Brahmanayudu's Veera Vaishnava** movement in Palnadu.
It gave **Panchamas temple entry**.

nc2793038232.s: The Statue of Equality at Hyderabad commemorates:
nc2793038232.x: The Statue of Equality at Hyderabad commemorates Ramanuja and his message of spiritual and social equality.
nc2793038232.tq: Use the monument–person association rather than confusing neighbouring Bhakti teachers.
xs: The **Statue of Equality** at Hyderabad honours **Ramanuja** — option **(4)**.
It is the world's **second-tallest sitting statue**, inaugurated by the PM (UPSC **2022**).
xa: Ramanuja gave **Panchamas temple entry**.
He taught any eager student **without the customary long wait**.

nc11ddb3ab74.s: The Bhakti acharyas gave Bhakti a philosophical base in opposition to:
nc11ddb3ab74.x: The acharyas provided a philosophical basis for Bhakti against Advaita and helped open temple worship to lower groups.
xa: **Ramananda** admitted disciples like **Kabir, Raidas, Sena, Dhanna**.
Ramanuja taught any eager student without the customary long wait.

nf7526d60e49.s: Vyasa Tirtha, royal guru to Saluva Narasimha and Krishnadevaraya, was a scholar of:
nf7526d60e49.x: Vyasa Tirtha was a Dvaita scholar and author of Nyayamrita.
xa: His other works: **Tatparya Chandrika**, **Tarka Tandava**.
He was defeated in debate by **Vallabha**.

nd0615856a45.s: The movement led by Ramanuja in Andhra, stressing devotion to Vishnu and social equality, is known as the:
nd0615856a45.x: Ramanuja's movement in Andhra, with devotion to Vishnu and social equality, is identified as the Bhakti movement.
xa: His **Vishishtadvaita** (**11th-12th c.**) grounded Bhakti in Andhra.
Centres: **Tirupati**, Kanchi, Mangalagiri, Pushpagiri.

n0fe4486f0af.s: Narahari Tirtha, a disciple of Madhva, spread which philosophical doctrine in Andhra-Kalinga from Srikurmam?
n0fe4486f0af.x: Narahari Tirtha, a disciple of Madhva, spread Dvaita in Andhra-Kalinga, beginning from Srikurmam.
n0fe4486f0af.tq: Separate the disciple, doctrine and regional centre in a teacher–philosophy question.
xs: **Narahari Tirtha**, a disciple of **Madhva**, spread **Dvaita** from **Srikurmam** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Madhva's school is **Dvaita**; **Advaita** is Shankaracharya's and **Vishishtadvaita** is Ramanuja's.
xa: All three are schools of **Vedanta** (Uttara Mimamsa), founded by **Badarayana**.
⚠ **Kumarila Bhatta** belongs to Purva Mimamsa, not Vedanta.
Vedanta holds **Brahman** the only reality.

nb587f0a4cb7.s: Vallabhacharya was associated with which of the following royal or family connections?
o: A Telugu Brahmin family and a visit to Krishnadevaraya’s court
The family of Prataparudra Gajapati at Puri
The court of Akbar as a royal poet
A Rajput family of Merta and marriage into the Mewar house
nb587f0a4cb7.x: Vallabhacharya belonged to a Telugu Brahmin family and visited the court of Krishnadevaraya.
nb587f0a4cb7.tq: Match the saint with the specific family or court connection rather than the region alone.
xs: Vallabhacharya came from **a Telugu Brahmin family** and **visited Krishnadevaraya's court** — option **(1)**.
**Prataparudra Gajapati** is linked to **Chaitanya**; **Merta / Mewar** to **Mirabai**.
xa: Vallabha preached **Krishna bhakti in Gujarat**; dates **1479-1531**.
His disciple: **Surdas**.

nindian-history-5-7.s: Which of the following Bhakti saints is the earliest?
nindian-history-5-7.x: Namdev (1270–1350) predates Kabir (1398–1518), Guru Nanak (1469–1539) and Mirabai (1498–1546).
n: Namdev lived from 1270 to 1350. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 35-40]
Kabir lived from 1398 to 1518. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 35-40]
Guru Nanak lived from 1469 to 1539. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 35-40]
Mirabai lived from 1498 to 1546. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 35-40]
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: other notes give Kabir c. **1440-1518** and Nanak **1469-1538**.
UPPSC **2025** key: **Namdev, Kabir, Nanak, Chaitanya**.
**Vallabha** (**1479-1531**) and **Chaitanya** (**1485-1533**) came between Nanak and Mirabai.

nindian-history-5-17.x: Mirabai's life overlapped with Guru Nanak (1469–1539) and Chaitanya.
n: Mirabai was contemporary with Guru Nanak. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 35-40]
Mirabai was contemporary with Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 35-40]
xa: Mirabai was a **Rajput princess of Merta**, married into the **Mewar** royal house.
Her guru was **Raidas (Ravidas)**.
She was born at **Kudki**.

nindian-history-80-2.x: Guru Nanak was born at Talwandi (Nankana Sahib); Kabir at Varanasi, Basavanna at Bagewadi and Chaitanya at Nabadwip.
n: Basavanna was born in Bagewadi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 159-160]
Kabir was born in Varanasi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 159-160]
Guru Nanak was born in Talwandi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 159-160]
Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was born in Nabadwip. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 159-160]
xa: **Adi Shankaracharya** — **Kaladi**; **Ramanujacharya** — **Sriperumbudur**.
**Gautama Buddha** — **Lumbini**; **Mahavira** — **Kundagrama**.
**Nizamuddin Auliya** — **Badaun**; **Amir Khusrau** — **Patiyali**.

n6b3efc75f9e.x: Tukaram was associated with Maharashtra; Vallabhacharya with Gujarat and Chaitanya with Bengal and Odisha.
xa: APPSC-G1 **2024** key: Vallabhacharya-Gujarat; Tulsidas-UP; Chaitanya-Bengal; Tukaram-Maharashtra.
**Mirabai** = **Rajasthan** (APPSC-GS **2025**).
Tukaram was **Shivaji's** contemporary.

n897870cc703.s: Chaitanya at Puri is associated with the reign of:
n897870cc703.x: Chaitanya was associated with Prataparudra Gajapati's reign at Puri.
xa: **Kabir**'s contemporary ruler: **Sikandar Lodi**; **Nanak**'s: **Babur**.
**Tukaram and Ramdas** laid the spiritual foundation of the Maratha movement.

n2b5127172f8.x: Kabir is paired with Sikandar Lodi; Guru Nanak with Babur and Tulsidas and Surdas with Akbar.
xa: **Akbar** was the contemporary of **Surdas** and **Tulsidas**.
Chaitanya visited **Puri** in **Prataparudra Deva's** reign.

nd8fd45aa5da.x: Rag Govind is matched with Mirabai, Sursagar with Surdas and Ramcharitmanas with Tulsidas.
xa: Tulsidas: **Vinaya Patrika, Kavitavali, Gitavali** too.
⚠ Tulsidas = **Awadhi**; Surdas = **Braj Bhasha**.

nf7649a433d5.x: Surdas used Braj Bhasha; Tulsidas used Awadhi and Kabir Sadhukkadi.
xa: **Mirabai** used **Rajasthani** (with Braj).
**Guru Nanak** used **Punjabi**.

nindian-history-85-14.x: Madhuravijayam is by Gangadevi; Molla wrote the Molla Ramayanam.
n: Baburnama is associated with Babur. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Ramcharitmanas is associated with Tulsidas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Molla Ramayanam is associated with Molla. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
Madhuravijayam is associated with Gangadevi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #85 · pp 167-168]
xa: **Vinaya Patrika**, **Kavitavali**, **Gitavali** are also Tulsidas's.
⚠ **Sahitya Lahari** is **Surdas**'s, not Tulsidas's (BPSC **2025**).
**Jnaneshwari** is **Jnaneshwar**'s Marathi rendering of the Bhagavad Gita.

n44563407803.s: Mardana is associated as a disciple with:
n44563407803.x: Guru Nanak was associated with Mardana; Ramananda with Kabir, Raidas with Mirabai and Vallabhacharya with Surdas.
xa: UPPSC **2025** also matched **Nizamuddin Auliya → Amir Khusrau**.
**Namdev — Janabai**; **Ramdas — Shivaji**.

nca610ee6bb6.s: Surdas was associated as a disciple with:
nca610ee6bb6.x: Surdas was associated with Vallabhacharya; Kabir, Raidas and Pipa belong to Ramananda's lineage.
xa: Other Ramananda disciples: **Sena, Dhanna, Padmavati**.
Surdas wrote **Sursagar** and **Sahitya Lahari** in **Braj Bhasha**.

nbb94a3e46de.s: Kabir's dohas and sakhis are collected in the:
nbb94a3e46de.x: Kabir's dohas and sakhis are collected in the Bijak; the Sursagar is by Surdas.
xa: Birth legend: born to a **Brahmin widow**.
Kabir's language: **Sadhukkadi**.

n6dc401e7ebe.s: Chaitanya founded or is chiefly associated with which sect?
n6dc401e7ebe.x: Chaitanya founded or is chiefly associated with Gaudiya Vaishnavism and preached passionate devotion to Krishna.
n6dc401e7ebe.tq: Distinguish Chaitanya’s sect from the Varkari and Kabir traditions.
xs: **Chaitanya** founded **Gaudiya Vaishnavism** — option **(4)**.
**Varkari** = Vithoba of Pandharpur; **Kabirpanth** = Kabir's followers.
xa: He turned saint after his **wife's death**; passionate devotion to **Krishna**.
He spread bhakti in **Bengal and Odisha**; followers saw him as an **incarnation of Vishnu**.

nc100e3c06e8.s: Sankirtan, popularised by Chaitanya, refers to
nc100e3c06e8.x: Sankirtan means collective devotional singing. It later found literary expression in Padavali kirtans.
nc100e3c06e8.tq: Apply the exact meaning of a religious term rather than choosing a related institutional term.
xs: **Sankirtan** = **collective devotional singing** — option **(1)**.
Popularised by **Chaitanya**, later written up as **Padavali kirtans**.
xa: ⚠ Varkari = **Vithoba of Pandharpur**; Gaudiya = **Chaitanya**.
Chaitanya was born in **1485** at **Nabadwip**.

nbab81617a28.s: The Varkari sect is primarily associated with the worship of:
nbab81617a28.x: The Varkari sect worships Vitthala, also called Vithoba, at Pandharpur.
xs: The **Varkari** sect worships **Vitthala (Vithoba) of Pandharpur** — option **(3)**.
It has an **annual pilgrimage** to Pandharpur.
xa: Varkari saints: **Jnaneshwar, Namdev, Eknath, Tukaram**.
**Abhangas** to Vithoba were composed by **Tukaram** (also Namdev).

o: Renunciation of all political activity and social duties
Exclusive devotion to Vitthala at Pandharpur
Strength, discipline and devotion to Rama
Ritual sacrifice, priestly authority and Sanskrit learning
n44955bb27df.x: Ramdas stressed strength, discipline and devotion to Rama, and these ideas aided the Maratha political awakening.
n44955bb27df.tq: Select the option combining the three distinctive elements of Ramdas's teaching.
xs: **Ramdas** stressed **strength, discipline and devotion to Rama** — option **(3)**.
This aided the **Maratha political awakening**; he was **Shivaji's guru**.
xa: Ramdas wrote the **Dasbodh**.
With **Tukaram**, he laid the spiritual foundation of the Maratha movement.

na0e9dac3a34.s: The Bhakti saints are credited with contributing to the early stirrings of Maratha and ____ awakening.
na0e9dac3a34.x: Besides enriching Hindi, Bengali, Marathi and Gujarati literature, the saints contributed to the early stirrings of Maratha and Sikh awakening.
xa: **Tukaram and Ramdas** laid the spiritual base of the Maratha movement under **Shivaji**.
**Namdev**'s hymns are in the **Guru Granth Sahib**.

n44a8cb948b6.s: Which one of the following groups represents the NIRGUNA tradition of Bhakti?
n44a8cb948b6.x: Kabir, Guru Nanak and Guru Ravidas are associated with the Nirguna tradition, which emphasises devotion to the formless divine.
n44a8cb948b6.tq: Separate the two doctrinal groups by identifying the members of the Nirguna tradition.
xs: **Kabir, Nanak and Ravidas** are **Nirguna** saints — option **(3)**.
**Tulsidas, Surdas, Mirabai, Chaitanya** are **Saguna** saints.
xa: Kabir as Nirguna was asked in APPSC-GS **2024**.
Ravidas was a contemporary of **Kabir**.

nindian-history-80-16.x: Basavanna is linked to Bagewadi, Shankaracharya to Kaladi, Ramanuja to Sriperumbudur and Chaitanya to Nabadwip.
n: Adi Shankaracharya was born in Kaladi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 159-160]
Ramanujacharya was born in Sriperumbudur. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 159-160]
Basavanna was born in Bagewadi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 159-160]
Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was born in Nabadwip. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 159-160]
xa: **Kabir** — **Varanasi**; **Guru Nanak** — **Talwandi**.
**Ramananda** — **Prayag**; **Tulsidas** — **Rajapur**.
**Mirabai** — **Kudki**; **Surdas** — **Sihi**.

nc269c5cbdaa.s: Who among the following lived later than Kabir and so could not have influenced him?
nc269c5cbdaa.x: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi lived from 1564 to 1624, later than Kabir.
xa: Kabir is a **Nirguna** saint.
Ramananda's other disciples: **Raidas, Pipa, Sena, Dhanna, Padmavati**.

nb8062ef6180.s: The traditional number of Alvars and Nayanars respectively is:
nb8062ef6180.x: There are traditionally 12 Alvars (Vaishnava, devotees of Vishnu) and 63 Nayanars (Shaiva, devotees of Shiva). '63 and 12' reverses them, and the other two options give both groups the same number.
xs: **12 Alvars** and **63 Nayanars** — option **(2)**.
Alvars were **Vaishnava** (Vishnu); Nayanars **Shaiva** (Shiva) (UPPSC **2014**, MPPSC **2022**).
Option 1 reverses the numbers.
xa: **Rajaraja I** consecrated bronzes of all **63 Nayanmars** at Chidambaram.
**Andal** = only female Alvar.

n63a123223a0.s: Who recovered and edited Annamacharya's sankirtanas preserved on copper plates at Tirumala?
n63a123223a0.x: Veturi Prabhakara Sastry recovered and edited the copper-plate songs; C.P. Brown is linked with Vemana.
xa: Veturi said Annamacharya **created the science of sankirtana**.
**Annamayya district** is named after him.

n742f8b12cf6.x: Padakavita Pitamaha, Sankirtanacharya and Harikirtanacharya are titles of Annamacharya.
xa: China Tirumalacharya was the **eldest son of Peda Tirumalacharya**; he wrote **Sankirtana Lakshanamu**.
Praise: "**Right hand to Telugu words**" (Puttaparthi Narayanacharyulu); "**Incarnated Telugu**" (Arudra).

n7288f21a7ca.s: Annamacharya is known in Telugu literary history as the:
o: Author of the first Telugu Dandakam
Father of the Telugu keertana and pioneer of padakavita
First translator of the Ramayana into Telugu
Founder of the Sanskrit court epic tradition
n7288f21a7ca.x: Annamacharya is regarded as the father of the Telugu keertana and a pioneer of the padakavita or pada form.
n7288f21a7ca.tq: Identify the exact literary contribution rather than a related but incorrect achievement.
xs: Annamacharya is the **Father of the Telugu keertana** and **pioneer of padakavita** — option **(2)**.
The first Telugu **Dandakam** is **Potana's Bhogini Dandakam**; the first woman Ramayana translator is **Molla**.
xa: His **Sri Venkateswara Satakam** = first Telugu **Shringara Satakam**.
⚠ Sri Venkateswara Satakam is **Annamacharya's**, not Pedda Tirumalacharya's.

n1ee3c9d1fec.s: Annamacharya, the composer of sankirtanas on Lord Venkateswara, was a contemporary of which ruler?
n1ee3c9d1fec.x: Annamacharya (1408-1503) was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha (APPSC-G2 2011). Pedakomati Vema Reddy was Srinatha's patron, Abul Hasan Tana Shah imprisoned Bhakta Ramadasu, and Krishnadevaraya is not the ruler linked with Annamacharya.
xs: Annamacharya (**1408-1503**) was a contemporary of **Saluva Narasimha** (APPSC-G2 2011) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Pedakomati Vema Reddy** was **Srinatha's** patron at Kondaveedu, not Annamacharya's.
**Abul Hasan Tana Shah** imprisoned **Bhakta Ramadasu** in Golconda fort.
xa: Annamacharya was met by the Kannada saint **Purandara Dasa**.
Some notes give his dates as **1424-1508**.
**Annamayya district** is named after Annamacharya of **Tallapaka**.

ne66e45ec64c.s: Peda Tirumalacharya, author of Vairagya Vachanamalika, was Annamacharya's:
ne66e45ec64c.x: Peda Tirumalacharya was Annamacharya's son; his works include Vairagya Vachanamalika and Sudarshana Ragada.
xa: Peda Tirumalacharya's other works: **Sankirtanas**, **Seesa padya satakam**, **Sudarshana Ragada**, **Chakravala Manjari**.
⚠ **Trap:** **Sri Venkateswara Satakam** is **Annamacharya's**, not Pedda Tirumalacharya's.

n9bb76123d22.s: Who held the title Ashtabhasha Kavi Chakravarti?
n9bb76123d22.x: China Tirumalacharya, Annamacharya's grandson, held the title and wrote the Ashtabhasha Dandakam.
xa: He also wrote **Sankirtana Lakshanamu**.
⚠ **Trap:** Do not credit China Tirumalayya with the **first Telugu Dandakam** — that was Potana's **Bhogini Dandakam**.

nb2c6d99e0f6.s: The poets associated with the Bhakti tradition in Telugu contributed to Carnatic music chiefly through:
o: Only Persian ghazals and court chronicles
Padams, keertanas, satakas and dvipada compositions
Only Sanskrit inscriptions and copper plates
nb2c6d99e0f6.x: Telugu Bhakti poets carried devotional expression through padams, keertanas, satakas and dvipada compositions, helping establish the Telugu base of the Carnatic music repertoire.
nb2c6d99e0f6.tq: Identify the common cultural contribution across different literary forms.
xs: Telugu Bhakti was carried through **padams, keertanas, satakas and dvipada** compositions — option **(3)** is correct.
These became the **base of Carnatic music's Telugu repertoire**; Persian ghazals, military ballads and Sanskrit inscriptions are not the channel.
xa: **Annamacharya** = **Father of the Telugu keertana**; about **32,000 sankirtanas** to **Lord Venkateswara**.
**Kshetrayya** composed over a thousand **Movva Gopala padams** at **Abdullah Qutb Shah's** court.
**Tyagaraja** composed Telugu kritis and the **Pancharatna kritis** at **Tiruvaiyaru**; Carnatic Trinity with **Dikshitar** and **Syama Sastri**.
**Bhakta Ramadasu** composed the **Ramadasu kirtanas** and **Dasarathi Satakam**.

n3aeaa0481eb.s: Veerabhadra Vijayam, written at the request of Ivaturi Somanaradhya, is regarded as the first work of:
n3aeaa0481eb.x: The cited accounts regard Veerabhadra Vijayam as Potana's first work, written at the request of his guru Ivaturi Somanaradhya.
xa: Potana's other works: **Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu**, **Bhogini Dandakam**, **Narayana Satakam** (lost).
Potana's title: **Sahaja Panditudu**.

nd4576dda79e.s: The first Telugu Dandakam, the Bhogini Dandakam, was written by:
nd4576dda79e.x: The first Telugu Dandakam was Potana's Bhogini Dandakam.
xa: **Bhogini Dandakam** is about **Sarvajna Singabhupala** and **Bhogini**.
Other FIRSTs: **Sri Venkateswara Satakam** (Annamacharya) = first Telugu **Shringara Satakam**; **Vrushadhipa Satakam** = first full-featured satakam.
**Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya** = originator of the **Sataka form** in Telugu.

n4a686a83191.s: Potana dedicated his Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu to:
n4a686a83191.x: The Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu, the Telugu Bhagavata Purana, was offered to Lord Rama; Potana wrote eight of its twelve skandhas.
xa: Other skandhas: **Bopparaju Gangana** (5th), **Erchuri Singana** (6th), **Veligandala Narayana** (11th-12th).
**C.P. Brown** printed Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu in **1840**.
Potana vowed **never to dedicate his work to a human king**.

n13df5bd42be.s: Srinatha served as Vidyadhikari (education minister) at the court of
n13df5bd42be.x: Srinatha was Vidyadhikari at the Kondaveedu court of Pedakomati Vema Reddy and wrote the king's Sanskrit inscriptions. Under Veerabhadra Reddy at Rajahmundry he wrote Bhimakhandam and Kasikhandam; at Devaraya II's court he won the title Kavi Sarvabhauma; Sarvajna Singabhupala is linked with Potana's refusal of patronage.
xs: Srinatha was **Vidyadhikari** under **Pedakomati Vema Reddy of Kondaveedu** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2001/2002**).
He also wrote the king's **Sanskrit inscriptions**.
**Veerabhadra Reddy** = Rajahmundry phase; **Devaraya II** = Kavi Sarvabhauma; **Sarvajna Singabhupala** = Potana's refused patron.
xa: Kondaveedu fell in **1424**.
Haravilasamu describes **Reddi-era sea trade**.

n18d3d5cffa8.s: Haravilasamu of Srinatha is particularly significant as a literary source for which aspect of the Reddi period?
o: Sea trade, including imports and exports
Temple land grants in the Rayalaseema region
Military organisation of the Vijayanagara Empire
n18d3d5cffa8.x: Haravilasamu, dedicated to Avachi Tippaya Setti, describes sea trade during the Reddi period, including imports and exports.
n18d3d5cffa8.tq: Identify the work through its distinctive socio-economic subject rather than its author alone.
xs: **Haravilasamu** is the source for Reddi-era **sea trade, imports and exports** — option **(1)** (APPSC **2019**).
It was dedicated to **Avachi Tippaya Setti**.
xa: Sringara Naishadhamu was dedicated to **Mamidi (Madiki) Singana**.
Srinatha's **Palnadu** chatu verses picture poverty and coarse food.

ncfa749e2757.x: Ramanuja preached Vishishtadvaita and stressed the worship of Narayana and Lakshmi.
xa: He is the **first true exponent** of Bhakti; centre **Srirangam**.
The **Statue of Equality** at Hyderabad honours him.
⚠ Ramanuja = **Vishishtadvaita**; Basavanna = **Shakti Vishishtadvaita**.

nee6d6a84a79.s: Vemana's poetry is best known for:
o: criticism of caste, superstition and empty ritual
nee6d6a84a79.x: Vemana criticised superstition, empty ritual, idol worship and hypocrisy and advocated humanism and equality.
xa: **C.P. Brown** edited and translated his verses as **Verses of Vemana** (**1829**).
Vemana is paired with **Potuluri Veerabrahmam** as Andhra's **anti-caste voices**.

nc4e5032cfe4.s: Who translated Vemana's verses into English as 'Verses of Vemana' (1829)?
nc4e5032cfe4.x: C.P. Brown collected, edited and translated Vemana's verses, published in 1829.
xa: Refrain: **"Vishwadabhirama Vinura Vema"**.
⚠ C.P. Brown dates: Verses of Vemana **1829**; Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu **1840**.

n573b6dba696.s: Vemana's verses are mostly composed in which metre and commonly end with which refrain?
n573b6dba696.x: Vemana mainly used the Ataveladi metre, and his verses commonly conclude with the refrain “Vishwadabhirama Vinura Vema.”
n573b6dba696.tq: Pair the distinctive metre with its recurring refrain rather than recognising either in isolation.
xs: Vemana mostly used the **Ataveladi** metre with the refrain **"Vishwadabhirama Vinura Vema"** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Dvipada** is the metre of works like **Basava Puranam** and **Annamacharya Charitra**, not Vemana's verses.
xa: His verses are short, **satakam-style**, in **colloquial Telugu**.
**Dating disputed:** **17th c.** vs **14th-15th c.** — learn both.

nd8c85f3999e.s: Which one of the following best reflects the social message of Veerabrahmendra Swamy?
o: He condemned caste differences and accepted disciples across castes and faiths.
He rejected vernacular literature in favour of Sanskrit.
He supported ritual hierarchy as the basis of social order.
He defended caste distinctions and restricted discipleship to one community.
nd8c85f3999e.x: Veerabrahmendra Swamy strongly condemned caste differences and accepted disciples from different castes and faiths, including Siddaiah, a Muslim.
nd8c85f3999e.tq: Apply the reformer’s stated social principles to a concrete description.
xs: Veerabrahmendra Swamy **condemned caste differences** and **accepted disciples across castes and faiths** — option **(1)** is correct.
His disciple **Siddaiah** was a **Muslim**, so options (3) and (4) are the opposite of his message.
xa: His prophecies are in **Kalagnanam**.
He is paired with **Vemana** as Andhra's anti-caste voices.

n07ea867f39e.s: Basavanna was associated with which of the following?
o: The Virashaiva movement and Shakti Vishishtadvaita theology
The Alvar tradition and Advaita philosophy
The Nayanar canon and Dvaita philosophy
The Siddha tradition and Vishishtadvaita philosophy
n07ea867f39e.x: Basavanna founded the Virashaiva movement, and its theology was termed Shakti Vishishtadvaita, according to which the soul and Shiva are fundamentally identical.
n07ea867f39e.tq: Match the founder with both the movement and its distinctive theology.
xs: **Basavanna** led **Veerashaivism**, whose theology is **Shakti Vishishtadvaita** — option **(1)**.
It holds the **soul and Shiva fundamentally identical**.
**Advaita** = Shankara; **Dvaita** = Madhva; plain **Vishishtadvaita** = Ramanuja.
xa: Basavanna was minister of Kalachuri ruler **Bijjala II** (**12th century**).
He led the **Sharana** movement; its ideas spread through Kannada **Vachanas**.

n55a3f4fcb52.s: Basavanna, also known as Basaveshwara, was the minister of which ruler?
o: Rajaraja I of the Eastern Chalukyas
Bijjala II of the Kalachuri dynasty
Bijjala I of the Chola dynasty
n55a3f4fcb52.x: Basavanna was the minister of the Kalachuri king Bijjala II in the 12th century.
n55a3f4fcb52.tq: Use the ruler–reformer association and avoid swapping neighbouring royal names.
xs: Basavanna was minister of **Bijjala II of the Kalachuri dynasty** — option **(3)**.
He founded the movement in **Karnataka** in the **12th century**.
xa: He led the **Sharana** movement.
**Anubhava Mantapa** at **Kalyana** was its early "religious parliament".

n412c3a7fff6.s: The Virashaiva or Lingayat movement was founded by:
n412c3a7fff6.x: Basavanna, or Basaveshwara, founded the Virashaiva or Lingayat movement in the 12th century.
n412c3a7fff6.tq: Distinguish the founder from later Andhra transmitters of the movement.
xs: **Basavanna** (Basaveshwara) founded the Virashaiva movement — option **(3)**.
**Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya** **brought it into Andhra**; **Palkuriki Somanatha** wrote the **Basava Puranam**; **Brahmanayudu** led Veeravaishnavism.
xa: **Allama Prabhu** and **Akka Mahadevi** were also prominent.
Theology: **Shakti Vishishtadvaita**.

n93c3771ae8d.s: The Anubhava Mantapa, an early 'religious parliament' of the Virashaivas, was at:
n93c3771ae8d.x: The Anubhava Mantapa was at Kalyana; its discourses were compiled in the Shunya Sampadane.
xa: ⚠ **Kayaka** = labour; **Dasoha** = sharing.
**Ishtalinga**: Shiva worshipped as a **linga worn on the body**.

n52aaa48de36.s: Who is credited with introducing Virashaivism into Andhra?
n52aaa48de36.x: Virashaivism entered Andhra through Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya, after which Pandita reformers helped spread it.
n52aaa48de36.tq: Separate the figure who introduced a movement from the later literary propagator.
xs: **Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya** brought Virashaivism into Andhra — option **(2)**.
**Pandita reformers** (Mallikarjuna, **Manchana** and others) spread it; initial impact was limited.
**Ivaturi Somanaradhyudu** was **Potana**'s guru; **Dhurjati** wrote the **Srikalahasteeswara Satakam**.
xa: Panditaradhya wrote **Sivatattvasaram** and founded **Aradhya Saivism**.
He is the **originator of the Sataka form** in Telugu.

n952d951c8b4.s: Which work of Palkuriki Somanatha is regarded as the first Telugu satakam with all satakam features?
n952d951c8b4.x: Somanatha's Vrushadhipa Satakam is the first Telugu satakam with all satakam features; his Basava Puranam spread Basava's teachings in simple Telugu.
xa: Somanatha belonged to the **Kakatiya** period.
⚠ Sataka form = **Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya**; first full-featured satakam = **Vrushadhipa Satakam**.

n405140c5b16.s: Which of the following is NOT a work of Palkuriki Somanatha?
n405140c5b16.x: Sivatattvasaram was written by Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya. Basava Puranam, Panditaradhya Charitra and Basavana Ragada are associated with Palkuriki Somanatha.
n405140c5b16.tq: Find the work belonging to the neighbouring author in a closely related literary group.
xs: **Sivatattvasaram** is NOT Somanatha's — option **(1)**; it is by **Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya**.
Somanatha wrote **Basava Puranam**, **Panditaradhya Charitra**, **Basavana Ragada** and **Vrushadhipa Satakam**.
xa: Sivatattvasaram has about **400 kanda** poems.
Panditaradhya founded the moderate **Aradhya Saivism**.

n79c86a14440.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Aradhya Saivism?
o: A Vaishnava sect centred exclusively on Venkateswara worship
A radical sect that rejected Vedic learning and varna distinctions
A court tradition that opposed all forms of devotional worship
A moderate Andhra Shaiva sect that retained Vedic learning and varna while preaching Shiva bhakti
n79c86a14440.x: Aradhya Saivism was the moderate Andhra Shaiva tradition associated with Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya; it retained Vedic learning and varna while preaching devotion to Shiva.
n79c86a14440.tq: Distinguish a moderate reform tradition from an incorrectly exaggerated radical description.
xs: **Aradhya Saivism** was a **moderate Andhra Shaiva sect** that **kept Vedic learning and varna** while preaching **Shiva bhakti** — option **(4)**.
So it did not reject Vedic learning and varna.
xa: Founder: **Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya**.
It is among **Andhra's contributions** with Tallapaka sankirtana and Kshetrayya's padams.

n63b62c72cec.s: After the fall of Rajahmundry, Srinatha's chatu verses chiefly portrayed which condition?
o: The maritime wealth of Avachi Tippaya Setti
The religious debates at the Vijayanagara court
The prosperity of the Gajapati court
The hard life and coarse food of poverty-stricken Palnadu
n63b62c72cec.x: After Rajahmundry fell in 1448, Srinatha lived in poverty in Palnadu. His chatu verses provide a literary picture of its hardship and coarse food.
n63b62c72cec.tq: Connect a biographical event with the social content of the poet’s verses.
xs: Srinatha's chatu verses portray the **hard life and coarse food of poverty-stricken Palnadu** — option **(4)**.
He lived in poverty there after **Rajahmundry fell (1448)**.
**Avachi Tippaya Setti**'s sea trade is in **Haravilasamu**, not the chatu verses.
xa: Later he found refuge with **Santhalingayya** of the Bhikshavritti matha at **Srisailam**.
⚠ Kondaveedu fell **1424**; Rajahmundry fell **1448**.

nce14688462a.s: Dhurjati is associated with which work?
nce14688462a.x: Dhurjati wrote Srikalahasteeswara Satakam, regarded as a foremost Shaiva satakam.
nce14688462a.tq: Distinguish similarly named satakams by their author and deity.
xs: Dhurjati wrote the **Srikalahasteeswara Satakam**, the foremost **Shaiva satakam** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Venkateshwara Satakam** = **Annamacharya**; **Narayana Satakam** = **Potana** (lost); **Vrushadhipa Satakam** = **Palkuriki Somanatha**.
xa: **Vrushadhipa Satakam** = first Telugu satakam with all satakam features.
**Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya** = originator of the **Sataka form** in Telugu.

n9e4b055ad51.s: Which literary forms helped spread Bhakti ideas among common people in Andhra?
n9e4b055ad51.x: The satakam and dwipada forms helped communicate Bhakti ideas to common people in Telugu-speaking regions.
n9e4b055ad51.tq: Identify the regional literary forms associated with popular religious communication.
xs: The **Satakam and dwipada** forms spread bhakti to common people — option **(2)** is correct.
**Vachanas** are Kannada prose-poems and **Tevaram** is the Tamil Shaiva canon — not Andhra's forms.
xa: **Desi kavita**: simple native metres (**dwipada, ragada, manjari, kanda**) vs the Sanskritised **Marga** style.
**Palkuriki Somanatha** wrote **Basava Puranam** in simple Telugu **Dwipada** metre.

n7d1608e3a26.s: Bhakta Ramadasu (Kancharla Gopanna) used state revenue to rebuild the Rama temple at:
n7d1608e3a26.x: Ramadasu, a Golconda revenue official, rebuilt the Bhadrachalam Rama temple and was jailed by Tana Shah for 12 years.
xa: Bhakta Ramadasu = **Kancharla Gopanna**, born **1620** at **Nelakondapalli** (Khammam).
Guru **Raghunatha Bhattacharya**; nephew of **Akkanna and Madanna**.
He wrote **Dasarathi Satakam** in prison.

n77ad4db4a55.s: Which of the following works is associated with Bhakta Ramadasu?
n77ad4db4a55.x: Dasarathi Satakam, written in prison, and the Ramadasu kirtanas are associated with Bhakta Ramadasu.
n77ad4db4a55.tq: Match the devotional author with his literary work.
xs: **Dasarathi Satakam**, written in prison, is Bhakta Ramadasu's — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kalagnanam** = **Potuluri Veerabrahmam**; **Nalayira Divya Prabandham** = **Alvars**; **Molla Ramayanam** = **Molla**.
xa: He also composed the **Ramadasu kirtanas / keertanas**.
English translation of Dasarathi Satakam: **Dr. Bhanumathi Ramakrishna** (APPSC-G2 2001).

nea883232536.s: Kshetrayya is associated with which form of composition?
nea883232536.x: Kshetrayya is associated with padams; Tallapaka is linked with sankirtana.
xa: Andhra's contributions: Dvaita at **Srikurmam**, **Aradhya Saivism**, **Tallapaka sankirtana**, **Bhadrachalam (Ramadasu)**, **Kshetrayya's padams**.
**Aradhya Saivism** was founded by **Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya**; it kept Vedic learning and varna while preaching Shiva bhakti.
**Dvaita** (dualism) is the philosophy of **Madhvacharya**.

nf6bbfc4453e.s: Madhura Vijayam, also known as Veera Kamparaya Charitam, describes:
o: The conquest of Madurai by Kumara Kampana
The marriage of Achyuta Deva Raya and Varadambika
The legends of Rama in Telugu
The life of Venkateswara at Tirumala
nf6bbfc4453e.x: Gangadevi's Sanskrit work Madhura Vijayam describes her husband Kumara Kampana's conquest of Madurai.
nf6bbfc4453e.tq: Link the literary work to its historical subject rather than merely its author.
xs: **Madhura Vijayam** describes the **conquest of Madurai by Kumara Kampana** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was written in **Sanskrit** by **Gangadevi**, a **Sangama princess**, about her husband.
The marriage of Achyuta Deva Raya is **Varadambika Parinayam** (Oduva Tirumalamba).
xa: ⚠ PYQ (APPSC-G2 2023 and 2025): wrong match = **Gangadevi — Marichi Parinayam**.
**Molla Ramayanam** gives Rama's story in simple, elegant **Telugu**.

ne9dc3e1076e.x: Timmakka wrote Subhadra Kalyanam; Molla wrote Molla Ramayanam and Vengamamba Venkatachala Mahatyamu.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** the **2025** answer key marked **Molla-Ramayanam** instead, but the explanation confirms Molla-Ramayanam is correct.
**Gangadevi** was a **Sangama princess**; husband **Kumara Kampana**.

ncb43d753d2f.s: Which of the following languages replaced Sanskrit as vehicles for the spread of Bhakti among common people?
ncb43d753d2f.x: Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam became important vernacular vehicles that carried Bhakti ideas to common people instead of relying exclusively on Sanskrit.
ncb43d753d2f.tq: Recall the complete language list rather than selecting a partially correct combination.
xs: **Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam** replaced Sanskrit as Bhakti's vehicles — option **(3)** is correct.
Options with **Persian**, **Arabic**, **Sanskrit**, **Pali** or **Prakrit** are not the vernaculars the notes list.
xa: **Satakam** and **dwipada** forms spread bhakti to common people.
The Alvars and Nayanars sang **Tamil hymns**; Basava's movement spread through Kannada **Vachanas**.

nb527c2277f5.s: Annamacharya composed his sankirtanas primarily in praise of:
nb527c2277f5.x: Annamacharya composed about 32,000 sankirtanas to Lord Venkateswara.
nb527c2277f5.tq: Use the deity association to distinguish Annamacharya from other devotional composers.
xs: Annamacharya's sankirtanas were to **Lord Venkateswara** of **Tirumala** — option **(2)**.
He composed about **32,000**; only about **12,000** survive.
**Rama** was the deity of **Ramadasu** and **Tyagaraja**; **Krishna** (Muvva Gopala) of **Kshetrayya**.
xa: Born at **Tallapaka**; dates **1408-1503**.
Contemporary ruler: **Saluva Narasimha** (APPSC-G2 **2011**).

n6904561de4f.s: Sri Venkateswara Satakam, regarded as the first Telugu Shringara Satakam, was written by
n6904561de4f.x: Sri Venkateswara Satakam is Annamacharya's work and the first Telugu Shringara Satakam. Crediting it to his son Peda Tirumalacharya is the common trap; China Tirumalacharya wrote Ashtabhasha Dandakam and Chinnanna wrote Annamacharya Charitra.
n6904561de4f.tq: Venkateswara Satakam = Annamacharya, not Pedda Tirumalacharya.
xs: **Sri Venkateswara Satakam**, the first Telugu Shringara Satakam, was written by **Annamacharya** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Crediting it to his son **Peda Tirumalacharya** is the common trap.
**China Tirumalacharya** wrote Ashtabhasha Dandakam; **Chinnanna** wrote Annamacharya Charitra.
xa: Annamacharya's other Telugu works: **Sringara Manjari** (**258 dvipadas**), **Dvipada Ramayanam**, **Alivelumangamma Satakam**.
His Sanskrit works: **Sankirtana Lakshanam**, **Venkatachala Mahatyam**.

n45a10f26b06.s: Bhakta Ramadasu's Dasarathi Satakam was translated into English by
n45a10f26b06.x: Dr. Bhanumathi Ramakrishna translated Dasarathi Satakam into English (APPSC-G2 2001). C.P. Brown translated Vemana's verses, Veturi Prabhakara Sastry recovered Annamacharya's copper-plate songs, and Arudra called Annamacharya 'Incarnated Telugu'.
xs: **Dr. Bhanumathi Ramakrishna** translated the Dasarathi Satakam into English (APPSC-G2 2001) — option **(3)** is correct.
**C.P. Brown** translated **Vemana's** verses (**1829**).
**Veturi Prabhakara Sastry** recovered Annamacharya's **copper-plate songs**; **Arudra** called Annamacharya **"Incarnated Telugu"**.
xa: Ramadasu wrote the Dasarathi Satakam **in prison** in **Golconda fort**.
Ramadasu = **Kancharla Gopanna**, nephew of **Akkanna and Madanna**.

na8a5778c29f.x: Nimbarka preached Dvaitadvaita; Ramanuja preached Vishishtadvaita and Madhva Dvaita.
xa: Shankara (Kaladi, **AD 788-820**) = **forerunner** of the Bhakti cult.
**Vedanta Desika** led Vishishtadvaita in that era.

n71ad513d6eb.s: Which of the following was a Nayanar saint?
n71ad513d6eb.x: Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar and Manikkavachakar are notable Nayanars; Nammalvar, Andal and Tirumangai were Alvars.
xa: Nayanar canon: **Tevaram**, the earliest part of the **Tirumurai**.
⚠ Alvars = **12** = Vishnu; Nayanars = **63** = Shiva.

nf2f1e10e0ad.s: Rajaraja I consecrated bronzes of all 63 Nayanmars at:
nf2f1e10e0ad.x: Rajaraja I consecrated the bronzes at Chidambaram; Parantaka I had installed statues of Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar.
xa: Chola temples: **Thanjavur**, **Gangaikondacholapuram**, **Chidambaram**.
Chola patronage was a key **spread factor** for bhakti.

n94299765316.s: Narahari Tirtha, associated with Srikurmam, is remembered for spreading:
n94299765316.x: Narahari Tirtha is associated with Srikurmam and spread the Dvaita tradition.
n94299765316.tq: Distinguish the philosophical affiliation from the nearby Shaiva traditions.
xs: **Narahari Tirtha** at **Srikurmam** spread **Dvaita** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Dvaita** (dualism) was **Madhvacharya's** philosophy; **Advaita** was **Shankaracharya's**.
**Aradhya Saivism** was founded by **Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya**; **Virashaivism** by **Basavanna**.
xa: Andhra's contributions: **Dvaita at Srikurmam**, Aradhya Saivism, Tallapaka sankirtana, Bhadrachalam, Kshetrayya's padams.
**Ramanuja** (**1017-1137**) = **Vishishtadvaita**.

n86c47080dd6.s: Sufism absorbed ideas from Vedanta, Yoga and:
n86c47080dd6.x: Sufism absorbed Vedanta, Yoga and Neo-Platonism while accepting the Quran and the Prophet.
xa: Sufis freely used **music**, which orthodox Islam did not generally sanction.
**Ba-shara** orders followed Sharia; **Be-shara** ones (wandering **Qalandars**, Madaris) were not bound by it.
Origin of 'Sufi': **Suf** (coarse wool), **Safa** (purity) or Greek **Sophia**.

n5078d24a2c3.s: Which Sufi order was strictly orthodox and opposed Akbar's Sulh-i-Kul?
n5078d24a2c3.x: The Naqshbandis opposed Sulh-i-Kul; the Chishtis kept aloof from the court, the Suhrawardis accepted royal service and the Shattaris absorbed yogic practices.
xa: ⚠ Chishti (aloof, sama) vs Suhrawardi (close to court) = **most-asked contrast**; Naqshbandi = the **orthodox pole**.
Naqshbandis also opposed **Shia influence**.

neacc9d16aae.s: The Naqshbandi order originated in Central Asia with:
neacc9d16aae.x: The order began with Bahauddin Naqshband; in India it was associated with Khwaja Baqi Billah and Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi.
xa: Naqshbandis were the **most orthodox** (JPSC 2016); **opposed sama** and visits to saints' tombs.
Sirhindi was **imprisoned by Jahangir**.

ncbeef691a36.s: Which of the following was a Be-shara group?
ncbeef691a36.x: The Madaris and wandering Qalandars were Be-shara; the Naqshbandi and Firdausi were Ba-shara orders.
xa: Other Ba-shara orders: **Chishti**, **Suhrawardi**, **Qadiri**.
Ba-shara = follow the **Shariat**; Be-shara = **outside it**.

n8303b288caf.s: Early Chishtis avoided ____, which later Deccan Chishtis accepted.
n8303b288caf.x: Early Chishtis avoided court patronage and state grants, while later Deccan Chishtis accepted grants; they encouraged sama and qawwali.
xa: The **Naqshbandis** opposed sama.
**Amir Khusrau**, disciple of Nizamuddin, introduced **Qaul**.

nf88a9c1403f.s: Bahauddin Zakariya was given which title after supporting Iltutmish against Qabacha?
nf88a9c1403f.x: Bahauddin Zakariya received the title Shaikh-ul-Islam after backing Iltutmish against Qabacha.
nf88a9c1403f.tq: Test the exact title associated with a named Sufi saint.
xs: **Bahauddin Zakariya** backed **Iltutmish against Qabacha** and got the title **Shaikh-ul-Islam** — option **(3)** is correct.
He was the **Suhrawardi** saint of **Multan**; the order stayed close to rulers.
xa: ⚠ Chishti = aloof + sama; Suhrawardi = court + **Shaikh-ul-Islam**; Naqshbandi = most orthodox.
Suhrawardis accepted **wealth and posts**.

n785b73ad3b8.x: The Naqshbandis opposed sama, while the Chishtis encouraged sama and qawwali and the Suhrawardis adopted sama and raqs.
xa: 'Majlis-i-Sama' belonged to the **Chishtis and Suhrawardis**.
Naqshbandis also opposed **visits to saints' tombs**.

ndf2a413b953.s: Which comparison between the Chishti and Suhrawardi orders is correct?
o: Chishtis were close to the court, whereas Suhrawardis rejected sama entirely.
Chishtis were the orthodox pole, whereas Suhrawardis were wandering Qalandars.
Chishtis were generally aloof and associated with sama, whereas Suhrawardis maintained closeness to the court.
Both orders were Be-shara and rejected Islamic law.
ndf2a413b953.x: The Chishtis are contrasted with the Suhrawardis as relatively aloof and associated with sama, while the Suhrawardis were closer to the court.
ndf2a413b953.tq: Use the central contrast rather than a shared feature.
xs: **Chishtis** were **aloof and associated with sama**; **Suhrawardis** stayed **close to the court** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **orthodox pole** was the **Naqshbandi**, not the Chishti; **Qalandars** were Be-shara wanderers.
Both Chishti and Suhrawardi were **Ba-shara**, following Sharia.
xa: ⚠ This Chishti vs Suhrawardi contrast is the **most-asked** one.
Bahauddin Zakariya (Suhrawardi) got the title **Shaikh-ul-Islam** from Iltutmish.

nafe770f0dc9.s: Which of the following best expresses the social and cultural significance of Sufism in India?
o: It restricted religious interaction to Persian-speaking court elites.
It eliminated the use of local languages and music in religious life.
It functioned exclusively as a military organisation.
It gave Islam a tolerant, vernacular face and made khanqahs welfare centres.
nafe770f0dc9.x: Sufism gave Islam in India a tolerant and vernacular character, while khanqahs served as welfare centres.
nafe770f0dc9.tq: Apply the broader social significance to a description.
xs: Sufism gave Islam in India a **tolerant, vernacular face**, and **khanqahs served as welfare centres** — option **(4)** is correct.
It did the opposite of options (1) and (2): Chishtis adapted to **local language and music**.
xa: Chishti adaptation made Sufism the **bridge for Indo-Islamic composite culture**.
Khanqahs gave **food and shelter to the poor**.

nindian-history-51-35.s: The Firdausi order, led by Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri, flourished in:
nindian-history-51-35.x: The Firdausis followed Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri in Bihar; the Suhrawardis followed Bahauddin Zakariya in Multan and Sindh.
n: The Suhrawardi Sufi Silsilah is associated with Bahauddin Zakariya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Suhrawardi Sufi Silsilah is associated with Multan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Suhrawardi Sufi Silsilah is associated with Punjab. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Suhrawardi Sufi Silsilah is associated with Sindh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Firdausia Sufi Silsilah is associated with Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Firdausia Sufi Silsilah is associated with Bihar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Naqshbandi Sufi Silsilah opposed Sama. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Naqshbandi Sufi Silsilah emphasized Shariat. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Ahmad Sirhindi was associated with the Naqshbandi Sufi Silsilah. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Qadiri Sufi Silsilah followed the tradition of Abdul Qadir Jilani. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xa: **Chishti** — **Muinuddin Chishti**, **Ajmer**.
Bahauddin Zakariya backed **Iltutmish against Qabacha** and got the title **Shaikh-ul-Islam**.
⚠ **Wahdat-ul-Wujud** = Qadiri/Chishti; **Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** = Sirhindi (Naqshbandi).

nindian-history-59-1.s: Who established the Chishti Sufi silsilah in India?
nindian-history-59-1.x: Muinuddin Chishti brought the Chishti silsilah to India and set it up at Ajmer. Shahabuddin Suhrawardi is linked to the Suhrawardi order, Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri to the Firdausi order and Bahauddin Naqshband to the Naqshbandi order.
nindian-history-59-1.tq: Link each silsilah to its founder.
n: Muinuddin Chishti is associated with the Chishti Sufi silsilah. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 134-135]
Shahabuddin Suhrawardi is associated with the Suhrawardi Sufi silsilah. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 134-135]
Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri is associated with the Firdausi Sufi silsilah. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 134-135]
Bahauddin Naqshband is associated with the Naqshbandi Sufi silsilah. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #59 · pp 134-135]
xs: **Muinuddin Chishti** established the Chishti silsilah in India — option **(4)**.
He settled at **Ajmer**, having come with **Muhammad Ghori** in **1192**.
**Shahabuddin Suhrawardi** founded the **Suhrawardi**; **Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri** — **Firdausi**; **Bahauddin Naqshband** — **Naqshbandi**.
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: the order was founded at **Chisht** (Herat) by **Khwaja Abu Ishaq Shami**.
The Chishtis **kept aloof** from court and encouraged **sama** and qawwali.
Chishti = **most popular order** in India.

n3c4a17ae647.s: A khanqah in the Sufi tradition was primarily a place that
o: served as a hospice where disciples lived and trained, while also providing food and shelter to the poor
was a military camp maintained by Sufi rulers
functioned exclusively as a court for settling criminal disputes
served only as a shrine over a saint’s tomb
n3c4a17ae647.x: A khanqah was a Sufi hospice for the residence and training of disciples, and it also provided food and shelter to the poor.
n3c4a17ae647.tq: Identify the institution from its combined training and charitable functions.
xs: A **khanqah** was a **Sufi hospice** where disciples lived and trained, also giving **food and shelter to the poor** — option **(1)** is correct.
A shrine at a saint's tomb is a **Dargah**, not a khanqah.
xa: At **Golconda**, khanqahs served as **higher-education centres**.
Khanqahs served as **welfare centres**, giving Islam in India a tolerant face.
**Nizamuddin Auliya's** hospice drew both **common people and nobles**.

ncb932ac0e5b.s: Sama in Sufi practice refers to
o: the spiritual path leading through the maqamat
devotional music intended to produce ecstasy
the death anniversary of a saint
ncb932ac0e5b.x: Sama means devotional music intended to produce spiritual ecstasy. Raqs refers to the ritual dance associated with it.
ncb932ac0e5b.tq: Distinguish closely related Sufi technical terms by their precise meanings.
xs: **Sama** is **devotional music meant to produce ecstasy** — option **(2)** is correct.
The spiritual path is **Tariqa**; repetition of God's name is **Zikr**; a saint's death anniversary is **Urs**.
xa: **Raqs** = ritual dance; **'Majlis-i-Sama'** of **Chishtis and Suhrawardis**.
⚠ **Chishtis encouraged** sama and qawwali; **Naqshbandis opposed** sama.
**Amir Khusrau** introduced **Qaul**, the opening hymn of Qawwali.

n293e78d346e.s: The bond between a spiritual master and his disciple in Sufism is known as
n293e78d346e.x: The pir–murid relationship is called Piri-Muridi. The pir or murshid is the spiritual master and the murid is the disciple.
n293e78d346e.tq: Test the exact term for a relationship rather than for an individual role.
xs: The pir-murid bond (preceptorship) is called **Piri-Muridi** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** is Sirhindi's doctrine; **Fana-Baqa** is annihilation / subsistence in God; **Ba-shara** means following the Shariat.
xa: **Pir / Murshid** = spiritual master or guide.
**Murid** = disciple pledged in **absolute submission** to the pir.

o: remembrance of God and ritual dance
annihilation of the self in God and subsistence in God
n9721cce4a5f.x: Fana denotes annihilation of the self or ego in God, while Baqa denotes subsistence in God.
n9721cce4a5f.tq: Test the paired terms together to prevent reversal of their meanings.
xs: **Fana** = **annihilation of the self in God**; **Baqa** = **subsistence in God** — option **(4)** is correct.
Remembrance of God = **Zikr**; ritual dance = **Raqs**; guide and disciple = **Pir and Murid**.
xa: **Kashf-ul-Mahjub** of Ali Hujwiri treats **fana** as a theme.
The **10 maqamat** run from **Tauba** (repentance) to **Riza** (submission).

nf206129bf62.s: Alberuni noted similarities between Sufi ideas and the Gita and:
nf206129bf62.x: Alberuni compared Sufi ideas with Patanjali's Yoga Sutra and the Gita.
xa: Sufis also met the **Kanphata (Nath) yogis** of **Gorakhnath**.
Sufism absorbed **Vedanta**, **Yoga** and **Neo-Platonism**.

n745e15b5060.s: In the Sufi scheme of ten stages (maqamat), the first and the last stages are respectively
n745e15b5060.x: The ten maqamat begin with Tauba (repentance) and end with Riza (submission), passing through Wara, Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr, Shukr, Khauf, Raja and Tawakkul. Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr and Shukr are intermediate stages, and 'Riza and Tauba' reverses the order.
xs: The maqamat begin with **Tauba** (repentance) and end with **Riza** (submission) — option **(2)** is correct.
**Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr, Shukr** are intermediate stages; option (4) reverses the order.
xa: The **10 stages**: Tauba → **Wara, Zuhd, Faqr, Sabr, Shukr, Khauf, Raja, Tawakkul** → Riza.
**Tariqa** = spiritual path through stages.

nf0d5d2faf32.s: The doctrine of Wahdat-ul-Wujud is associated with:
nf0d5d2faf32.x: Wahdat-ul-Wujud was associated with Ibn Arabi; Sirhindi represented Wahdat-ush-Shuhud.
xa: Wujud = **Unity of Being** (Haq and Khalq are one); Shuhud = **Unity of Appearance/Witness**.
The **Qadiri** order **backed Wahdat-ul-Wujud**.

nf456ce95a4e.s: ‘Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani’ is best described as which of the following?
o: An anti-Shia tract by Abdul Haqq Dehlavi
A tazkira written by Mir Khwurd Kirmani
nf456ce95a4e.x: ‘Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani’ consists of the letters of Ahmad Sirhindi.
xs: **Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani** = **letters of Ahmad Sirhindi** — option **(3)** is correct.
The anti-Shia tract is Sirhindi's **Radd-i-Khawafiq**; the tazkira by **Mir Khwurd Kirmani** is **Siyar-ul-Auliya**.
xa: ⚠ **maktubat** = letters; **malfuzat** = conversations; **tazkiras** = biographies.
Sirhindi = **Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**, a **Naqshbandi**.

n0563819c6cb.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of saints belonging to the Chishti Silsila?
o: Miyan Mir, Muhibullah Shah, Dara Shikoh and Burhanuddin Gharib
Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi, Burhanuddin Gharib, Gesudaraz and Hamiduddin of Nagaur
Khwaja Baqi Billah, Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi, Shah Waliullah and Hamiduddin Nagori
Bahauddin Zakariya, Ruknuddin Abul Fath, Jalaluddin Tabrizi and Gesudaraz
n0563819c6cb.x: Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi, Burhanuddin Gharib, Gesudaraz and the Chishti Hamiduddin of Nagaur are all associated with the Chishti order.
n0563819c6cb.tq: Use group identification to separate closely related saints belonging to different Sufi orders.
xs: **Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi, Burhanuddin Gharib, Gesudaraz and Hamiduddin of Nagaur** are all Chishtis — option **(2)** is correct.
**Miyan Mir, Muhibullah Shah, Dara Shikoh** = **Qadiri**; **Baqi Billah, Sirhindi, Shah Waliullah** = **Naqshbandi**.
**Bahauddin Zakariya, Ruknuddin Abul Fath, Jalaluddin Tabrizi** = **Suhrawardi**.
xa: ⚠ **APPSC-G1 2018:** **Gesudaraz** = the Chishti in the list.
Other Chishtis: **Moinuddin**, **Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki**, **Baba Farid**, **Nizamuddin Auliya**.

n127d4ce1a16.s: Nizamuddin Auliya was a disciple of:
n127d4ce1a16.x: Nizamuddin Auliya, born at Badaun and buried in Delhi, was a disciple of Baba Farid.
xa: Dates **1238-1325**; title **Mahboob-i-Ilahi**.
His hospice drew both **common people and nobles**.
**Amir Khusrau**, his disciple, introduced **Qaul** in Qawwali.

n48df9208f20.s: The dargah of Gesudaraz is at:
n48df9208f20.x: Gesudaraz's dargah is at Gulbarga; Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki's is at Mehrauli and Haji Waris Ali Shah's at Dewa Sharif.
xa: **Moinuddin Chishti — Ajmer**; **Baba Farid — Ajodhan** (Pakpattan).
**Nizamuddin Auliya** and **Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi** — **Delhi**.

n288f3a55a34.s: The dargah of Gesudaraz, also known as Bande Nawaz, is located at which place?
n288f3a55a34.x: The dargah of Gesudaraz or Bande Nawaz is at Gulbarga, where he settled under the Bahmanis.
xs: **Gesudaraz (Bande Nawaz)** has his dargah at **Gulbarga** (Kalaburagi) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Khuldabad** = **Burhanuddin Gharib**; **Bijapur** = later Chishti centre; **Golconda** = **Shah Raju Qattal**.
xa: He settled there under the **Bahmanis**.
⚠ **APPSC-G1 2018:** **Gesudaraz** = the Chishti in the list.

nindian-history-58-18.s: Which Sufi saint was known as Chirag-i-Delhi?
nindian-history-58-18.x: Nasiruddin Mahmud was Chirag-i-Delhi; Nizamuddin Auliya was Mehboob-i-Ilahi and Salim Chishti Shaikh-ul-Hind.
n: Nizamuddin Auliya was known as Mehboob-i-Ilahi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Nasiruddin Mahmud was known as Chirag-i-Delhi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Salim Chishti belonged to the Chishti order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Salim Chishti is associated with Fatehpur Sikri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Salim Chishti was known as Shaikh-ul-Hind. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Shahabuddin belonged to the Suhrawardi order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Shahabuddin is associated with Suhrawardiya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
xa: **Baba Farid** = **Ganj-i-Shakar**; **Moinuddin Chishti** = **Garib Nawaz**.
**Ali Hujwiri** = **Data Ganj Bakhsh**, author of **Kashf-ul-Mahjub**.
Nasiruddin was the last great Chishti saint of Delhi.

nindian-history-58-21.s: Baba Farid is also known as:
nindian-history-58-21.x: Baba Farid was called Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar; his verses are in the Guru Granth Sahib.
n: Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki belonged to the Chishti order. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki was a disciple of Muinuddin Chishti. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Baba Farid is also known as Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Baba Farid's compositions are included in the Guru Granth Sahib. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
xa: Kaki's dargah is at **Delhi** (Mehrauli); the Qutub Minar's first storey was dedicated to him by **Aibak**.
Baba Farid's dargah is at **Ajodhan** (Pakpattan).
Baba Farid was the **teacher** of **Nizamuddin Auliya**.

nd0ca84f4eb4.s: One derivation of 'Sufi' is from 'suf', meaning:
nd0ca84f4eb4.x: Suf means coarse wool; the word is also explained through safa (purity) and the Greek sophia.
xa: First prominent Sufi in India: **Ali Hujwiri (Data Ganj Bakhsh)**, author of **Kashf-ul-Mahjub**.
Most popular order in India: **Chishti**.
Sufis accepted the **Quran and the Prophet** but absorbed **Vedanta, Yoga, Neo-Platonism**.
