n7b58024d66a.s: Breath control became vital in almost every Sufi order after the translation of:
n7b58024d66a.x: Breath control spread after the translation of Amritakund, the Naqshbandis being the exception.
xa: Amritakund was translated into **Arabic and Persian** in the **13th c.**
**Shattaris** were liberal and **absorbed yogic practices**.

ncd85470d954.s: Ahmad Sirhindi criticised Akbar’s Sulh-i-Kul and was subsequently imprisoned by which Mughal ruler?
ncd85470d954.x: Ahmad Sirhindi criticised Akbar’s Sulh-i-Kul and was imprisoned during the reign of Jahangir.
ncd85470d954.tq: Separate the ruler whose policy was criticised from the ruler who ordered the imprisonment.
xs: **Ahmad Sirhindi** criticised Akbar's **Sulh-i-Kul** and was **imprisoned by Jahangir** — option **(2)** is correct.
As a strictly orthodox **Naqshbandi**, he opposed Sulh-i-Kul and **Shia influence**.
xa: Sirhindi's title: **Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**.
He propounded **Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** against Wahdat-ul-Wujud.
His works: **Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani** (letters), **Radd-i-Khawafiq** (anti-Shia tract).

nc76a3052e57.s: Amir Khusrau, the disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya, introduced which element of Qawwali?
o: Fana, the final stage of spiritual union
nc76a3052e57.x: Amir Khusrau introduced Qaul, the opening hymn of Qawwali.
nc76a3052e57.tq: Associate a cultural contribution with its contributor.
xs: **Amir Khusrau** introduced **Qaul**, the opening hymn of Qawwali — option **(1)** is correct.
**Malfuzat** are recorded conversations; **Fana** is annihilation of self in God; **Khanqah** is a hospice — none is a Qawwali element.
xa: Khusrau was a disciple of **Nizamuddin Auliya**.
The **Chishtis encouraged sama and qawwali**; the Naqshbandis opposed sama.

ncd49bf4d3d5.x: Ali Hujwiri (Data Ganj Bakhsh), considered the first prominent Sufi in India, wrote Kashf-ul-Mahjub.
xa: **Siyar-ul-Auliya** = **Mir Khwurd Kirmani** (tazkira); **Akhbar-ul-Akhyar** = **Abdul Haqq Muhaddis Dehlavi**.
⚠ FIRST = **Ali Hujwiri**; last great Chishti of Delhi = **Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Dehlavi**.

nindian-history-58-9.s: Ahmad Sirhindi was known by which title?
nindian-history-58-9.x: Ahmad Sirhindi of the Naqshbandi order was called Mujaddid Alif Sani, the reviver of the second Islamic millennium. Chirag-i-Delhi was Nasiruddin Mahmud and Mehboob-i-Ilahi was Nizamuddin Auliya.
nindian-history-58-9.tq: Link each title to its saint.
n: Nizamuddin Auliya was known as Mehboob-i-Ilahi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Nasiruddin Mahmud was known as Chirag-i-Delhi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Salim Chishti was known as Shaikh-ul-Hind. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Ahmad Sirhindi was known as Mujaddid Alif Sani. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Ahmad Sirhindi is associated with Wahdat-ul-Shuhud. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
xs: Ahmad Sirhindi was called **Mujaddid Alif Sani** — option **(4)**.
He belonged to the **Naqshbandi** order.
**Chirag-i-Delhi** = **Nasiruddin Mahmud**; **Mehboob-i-Ilahi** = **Nizamuddin Auliya**; **Shaikh-ul-Hind** = **Salim Chishti**.
xa: Sirhindi criticised Akbar's **Sulh-i-Kul** and was **imprisoned by Jahangir**.
He propounded **Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** ("Unity of Appearance").
His letters: **Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani**; anti-Shia tract: **Radd-i-Khawafiq**.

n1eca0e711a9.s: Qazi Hamiduddin Nagori belonged to which Sufi order?
n1eca0e711a9.x: Qazi Hamiduddin Nagori was a Suhrawardi, unlike the Chishti Hamiduddin of Nagaur, a disciple of Moinuddin Chishti.
xa: ⚠ Some notes list "Hamiduddin Nagori" under the Suhrawardis — keep the two apart.
Moinuddin Chishti (**1143-1235**) has his dargah at **Ajmer**.

nc7d6f165894.s: Abul Hasan Tana Shah, the last Qutb Shahi ruler of Golconda, was a disciple of which saint?
nc7d6f165894.x: Abul Hasan Tana Shah was a disciple of the Chishti saint Shah Raju Qattal.
nc7d6f165894.tq: Use the ruler–saint association to avoid confusing different Sufi personalities.
xs: **Abul Hasan Tana Shah**, last Qutb Shahi, was a disciple of the Chishti saint **Shah Raju Qattal** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Sirhindi** was Naqshbandi; **Bahauddin Zakariya** was Suhrawardi of Multan; **Bakhtiyar Kaki** was a Delhi Chishti.
xa: At **Golconda**, Sufi gurus settled and Sufism **"gained immense popularity"**.
Golconda khanqahs = **higher-education centres**.

nb5f55a0615e.s: Who took the Chishti order to the Deccan, at Khuldabad, in the 14th century?
nb5f55a0615e.x: Burhanuddin Gharib took the order to Khuldabad in the 14th century; a migration of Chishtis to Gulbarga followed.
xa: **Gesudaraz (Bande Nawaz)** settled at **Gulbarga** under the **Bahmanis**.
**Bijapur** became a later key Chishti centre in the Deccan.

nc945114f6ee.s: The Baba Fakhruddin Dargah is located at:
nc945114f6ee.x: Baba Fakhruddin Dargah is at Penukonda; the Ameen Peer Dargah is at Kadapa and Gesudaraz's at Gulbarga.
xa: **Bijapur** was a later key **Chishti** centre in the Deccan.
Ameen Peer Dargah = **Peerullah Hussaini**, **17th c.**

o: a saint's death anniversary, seen as union with God
a friend of God or saint
a shrine at a saint's tomb
ncf5e486069e.x: Urs is a saint's death anniversary viewed as union with God; dargah is the shrine, wali the saint and tariqa the path.
xa: The **ulema** stood for **legalistic orthodoxy and the Shariat**.
**Chilla** = solitude or retreat; **Zikr** = continuous remembrance of God's name.

n6ecab3185ac.s: Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki is associated with which Sultan?
n6ecab3185ac.x: Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki was linked with Iltutmish; Nasiruddin Chiragh with Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Firuz Tughlaq.
xa: ⚠ **Iltutmish** = contemporary of both **Bakhtiyar Kaki** (Chishti) and **Bahauddin Zakariya** (Suhrawardi).
**Nizamuddin Auliya** lived under **Alauddin Khalji** and **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**.

n29997978a40.s: Jahangir imprisoned Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi at:
n29997978a40.x: Jahangir imprisoned Sirhindi at Gwalior Fort; his letters are the Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani.
xa: Title: **Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**.
He propounded **Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** vs Wahdat-ul-Wujud.

n21f1be45abb.s: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi was known by which title?
n21f1be45abb.x: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi was known as Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani.
n21f1be45abb.tq: Match the religious personality with the exact title.
xs: Sirhindi was titled **Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani** — option **(3)** is correct.
He was a **Naqshbandi**, disciple of **Khwaja Baqi Billah**.
xa: His letters: **Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani**; anti-Shia tract **Radd-i-Rawafiz**.
He criticised Akbar's **Sulh-i-kul** and **Din-i-Ilahi**; **imprisoned by Jahangir** at **Gwalior fort**.

n7b5d22fe7bb.s: Who among the following opposed Akbar's Sulh-i-kul and Din-i-Ilahi, as well as sama?
n7b5d22fe7bb.x: Sirhindi criticised Sulh-i-kul and Din-i-Ilahi and opposed sama and visits to saints' tombs.
xa: He **urged limited contact with Hindus and Shias**.
Comparative: **Nizamuddin** (Chishti, sama, aloof) vs **Sirhindi** (Naqshbandi, orthodox, political critic).
n7b5d22fe7bb.fixed: sama and tomb visits are not Akbar's policies; stem wrongly called all four Akbar's initiatives

n72eec644281.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Sirhindi’s position on Wahdat-ush-Shuhud and Wahdat-ul-Wujud?
o: He rejected both doctrines as non-Sufi ideas.
He treated both doctrines as identical and interchangeable.
n72eec644281.x: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi propounded Wahdat-ush-Shuhud in opposition to Wahdat-ul-Wujud.
n72eec644281.tq: Test the direction of opposition between two closely resembling doctrinal terms.
xs: Sirhindi propounded **Wahdat-ush-Shuhud** against **Wahdat-ul-Wujud** — option **(4)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the doctrines; he did not treat them as identical or reject both.
xa: He was a **Naqshbandi**, titled **Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani**.
He was **imprisoned by Jahangir** at **Gwalior fort**.

nfdbbd98261c.x: Fawaid-ul-Fuad was compiled by Amir Hasan Sijzi. Amir Khusrau, Barani and Hasan Nizami are associated distractors, not its compiler.
nfdbbd98261c.tq: Use the compiler–work association and avoid confusing it with famous literary contemporaries.
xs: **Amir Hasan Sijzi** compiled **Fawaid-ul-Fuad** (UPPSC 2021) — option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **Amir Khusrau**, **Barani** and **Hasan Nizami** are the usual distractors.
xa: Fawaid-ul-Fuad = conversations of **Nizamuddin Auliya**, a **malfuzat**.
**Radd-i-Rawafiz** = **Sirhindi's** anti-Shia tract.

na2af8b6f4f4.s: Which one of the following best explains the difference between Bhakti devotion and formal Sufi religious practice?
o: Bhakti rejected personal devotion, whereas Sufism confined worship to idol rituals.
Bhakti emphasised Vedic ritual, whereas Sufism rejected all forms of devotion.
Bhakti stressed devotion over Vedic ritual, while Sufism valued inner experience over formal Shariat.
Both movements exclusively supported priestly authority and formal ritual.
na2af8b6f4f4.x: Bhakti traditions placed devotion above Vedic ritual and priestly mediation, while Sufism emphasised inner spiritual experience rather than merely formal observance of the Shariat.
na2af8b6f4f4.tq: Test a comparison by matching each tradition with its characteristic emphasis.
xs: **Bhakti** put devotion over **Vedic ritual and priests**; **Sufism** put **inner experience over the formal Shariat** — option **(3)** is correct.
Neither movement backed priestly authority or idol rituals, so options (1), (2), (4) are wrong.
xa: The **guru / pir** bond was central to both.
Also shared: **vernacular preaching** and **spiritual equality of all castes**.

n35e8725c682.s: Which of the following was NOT shared by the Bhakti and Sufi traditions?
n35e8725c682.x: Both valued the guide-disciple bond, devotion over ritual and vernacular preaching; exclusive idol worship was not common to them.
xa: APPSC 2022 and 2023 keyed **monotheism, asceticism, tolerance** as common.
Both stressed **spiritual equality of all castes**.

n1205aff2c05.s: Which of the following was NOT common to the Bhakti and Sufi movements?
n1205aff2c05.x: Monotheism, asceticism and religious tolerance were common; idol worship was rejected by the Sufis and the Nirguna saints.
xa: Bhakti monotheism: **Nirguna saints**; Sufi: **Tawhid**, **Wahdat-ul-Wujud**.
Tolerance: Kabir and Nanak criticised **both Hindu and Muslim orthodoxy**.

n198909d1dac.s: Which of the following correctly describes a social impact of the Bhakti and Sufi movements?
o: Khanqahs were closed to lower social groups
They weakened priestly and Brahmanical dominance
n198909d1dac.x: The movements weakened priestly dominance and khanqahs welcomed different groups, but caste was not completely abolished.
xa: Limitations: **sectarianisation**, **orthodox pushback**, no end to **purdah**.
Veerashaivism at times turned to **physical violence (Himsa)**.

n1763289fc5f.s: Kabir and Nanak criticised the rigid orthodoxy of:
n1763289fc5f.x: Kabir and Nanak criticised the orthodoxies of both Hinduism and Islam and stressed spiritual equality.
xa: Kabir's mission: **Hindu-Muslim unity**; God as Ram, Rahim, Allah, Khuda, Hari.
**Kabir, Nanak, Ravidas, Dadu** = **Kabirpanth + Sant (Nirguna) tradition**.

n7319b64aab2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the interaction between Nath yogis and Sufis?
o: Hath-yogic techniques influenced some Sufi practices
It was confined exclusively to temple rituals
Sufis adopted certain yogic meditation practices
n7319b64aab2.x: The interaction involved dialogues, meditation and breath control; it was not confined to temple rituals.
xa: **Amritakund** was translated into **Arabic and Persian in the 13th century**.
It gave Sufis **breath control** in all orders except the **Naqshbandis**.

ne5ef68380ae.s: Which Sufi equated 'Alakh Niranjan' with 'Khuda' in Hindi verse?
ne5ef68380ae.x: Hamiduddin Nagori equated the Nath term 'Alakh Niranjan' with 'Khuda' in Hindi verse. Nizamuddin Auliya noted the yogic Siva-Sakti division of the body, Ahmad Sirhindi was an orthodox Naqshbandi, and Bahauddin Zakariya was a Suhrawardi close to the court.
xs: **Hamiduddin Nagori** equated **'Alakh Niranjan'** with **'Khuda'** in Hindi verse — option **(2)** is correct.
**Nizamuddin Auliya** noted the **Siva-Sakti** division; **Ahmad Sirhindi** was the orthodox **Naqshbandi** reaction.
xa: **Dara Shikoh** (Qadiri) carried forward the **syncretic line**.
**Sheikh Nuruddin** founded the **Rishi movement** (Kashmir).

n0e64b11abc9.s: The Sant tradition, which blended Hindu and Islamic ideas, included Kabir, Nanak, Ravidas and:
n0e64b11abc9.x: The Kabirpanth and Sant tradition included Kabir, Nanak, Ravidas and Dadu and blended Hindu and Islamic ideas.
xa: **Dadupanth** = **Dadu Dayal** (Rajasthan).
Kabir: one God as **Ram, Rahim, Allah, Khuda, Hari**.

n34ba29bfea2.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly describes the Rishi movement of Kashmir?
o: Courtly luxury, military conquest and Persianisation
Purdah, child marriage and priestly monopoly
Universal love, service to all castes and vegetarianism
Caste exclusiveness, animal sacrifice and compulsory meat-eating
n34ba29bfea2.x: The Rishi movement served all castes, emphasised universal love and adopted vegetarianism, although the Shariat permitted meat.
n34ba29bfea2.tq: Match the movement with its distinctive ethical and social features.
xs: The **Rishi movement** stood for **universal love**, **service to all castes** and **vegetarianism** — option **(3)** is correct.
It adopted vegetarianism **though Shariat permitted meat**.
xa: Founder: **Sheikh Nuruddin**; it echoed the poetess **Lalla** (Lal Ded).
Region: **Kashmir**.

n8376dc82955.s: Who carried forward the syncretic tradition of Akbar's Sulh-i-kul and Din-i-Ilahi?
n8376dc82955.x: Dara Shikoh carried the syncretic tradition forward, while Ahmad Sirhindi attacked these policies.
xa: Limitation: **Naqshbandi orthodoxy** pushed back against Sufi-Bhakti liberalism.
Din-i-Ilahi = **1582**.

n9fe9c985b90.s: Which one of the following Sufi orders was opposed to musical practices such as sama?
n9fe9c985b90.x: The Naqshbandis opposed sama and associated musical practices, in contrast to the Chishti and Suhrawardi traditions mentioned in this context.
n9fe9c985b90.tq: Test the exception among Sufi orders associated with devotional music.
xs: The **Naqshbandi** order opposed sama — option **(1)** is correct.
**Chishtis and Suhrawardis** held **"Majlis-i-Sama"** gatherings.
xa: Naqshbandis also stood apart on **breath control**, the one order that did not adopt it.
**Naqshbandi orthodoxy** was the main pushback against Sufi-Bhakti liberalism.

n56126c125e9.s: Lal Ded, also known as Lalla, is associated with:
o: Kashmir and the inspiration of the Rishi movement
Tamil Nadu and the Alvar tradition
Andhra and the composition of Molla Ramayanam
n56126c125e9.x: Lal Ded or Lalla belonged to Kashmir and inspired the Rishi movement.
n56126c125e9.tq: Match the saint with the distinctive regional and movement association.
xs: **Lal Ded (Lalla)** belongs to **Kashmir** and inspired the **Rishi movement** — option **(2)** is correct.
Rajasthan and Krishna = **Mirabai**; Alvar = **Andal**; Molla Ramayanam = **Molla**.
xa: The Rishi movement was founded by **Sheikh Nuruddin**.
It stood for **universal love**, service to all castes, and **vegetarianism**.

n7d5d342a6ce.s: Sheikh Nuruddin is associated with the:
n7d5d342a6ce.x: Sheikh Nuruddin is associated with the Rishi movement; Basaveswara led the Lingayat/Veerasaiva tradition.
xa: Veerashaivism (**12th c.**) opposed caste, animal sacrifice and **child marriage**; backed **widow remarriage**.
It spread in Andhra through **Mallikarjuna, Inpati and Manchana Panditas**.

n8cd0e8f3098.s: The Nathpanthi tradition of Hath Yoga is particularly associated with which of the following figures?
n8cd0e8f3098.x: The Kanphata Yogis followed the Nath tradition of Gorakhnath and were practitioners of Hath Yoga.
n8cd0e8f3098.tq: Apply the founder-or-associated-person trap by separating Nath yogis from Sufi figures.
xs: Nathpanthi Hath Yoga belongs to the **Kanphata** yogis of **Gorakhnath's** Nath tradition — option **(4) Gorakhnath**.
**Hamiduddin Nagori** equated **'Alakh Niranjan'** with 'Khuda'; **Faqirullah** wrote **Raga Darpan**; **Amir Khusrau** introduced the **Qaul**.
xa: **Kanphata** = split-eared yogis.
Sufis adopted Hath-yogic techniques (UPPSC 2019: **both statements correct**).

n2e67876e21f.s: The Qaul, associated with the early development of qawwali, was introduced by
n2e67876e21f.x: Amir Khusrau is credited with introducing the Qaul, which became associated with qawwali traditions around Sufi shrines.
n2e67876e21f.tq: Use the author-or-originator association to identify the correct contributor to a musical form.
xs: **Amir Khusrau** introduced the **Qaul** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Faqirullah** wrote **Raga Darpan**; **Chaitanya** = **sankirtan**; **Annamacharya** = Telugu padam / keertana.
xa: **Qawwali** grew around **Sufi shrines**.
**Hindustani music** absorbed Persian, Bhakti and Sufi influences (**Amir Khusrau**, **Tansen**).

na8d5fb0940b.s: Which music tradition remained closely tied to temple Bhakti?
na8d5fb0940b.x: Carnatic music remained linked with temple Bhakti, while Hindustani absorbed Persian, Bhakti and Sufi influences.
xa: Hindustani influences: **Amir Khusrau**, **Tansen**.
Carnatic's temple link: the **Trinity**.
Persian works on Indian music: **Ghunyat-ul-Munya** (**1375**) and **Raga Darpan** (Faqirullah).

ned8abab6e61.s: Who among the following used satire in common Telugu to criticise birth-based inequality?
ned8abab6e61.x: Vemana, associated with the seventeenth century, used satire in common Telugu against birth-based inequality.
ned8abab6e61.tq: Link the poet’s language and literary method with the social theme.
xs: **Vemana** (**17th c.**) used **satire in common Telugu** against **birth-based inequality** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Baba Farid** = Punjabi verses; **Surdas** = Hindi; **Amir Khusrau** = Urdu / Hindavi.
xa: Vemana is part of Andhra's pre-colonial reform line with **Veerabrahmam**, **Nasaraiah**, **Brahmanaidu**.
Telugu bhakti literature also includes **Annamacharya's sankirtanas** and **Kaalagnanam**.

nfb6b7453326.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the growth of vernacular literature under the Bhakti and Sufi saints?
o: Saints used the people's speech in their teaching
Hindi, Marathi, Kannada and Bengali grew as literary languages
Sufis used Hindavi, Punjabi and Urdu in preaching
nfb6b7453326.x: The saints used the people's speech instead of relying exclusively on Sanskrit, which helped regional languages grow.
xa: This laid the **foundations for modern Indian literature**.
**Amir Khusrau** is the key Urdu / Hindavi figure.

nf173ef385fb.s: The early feelings of national awakening associated with the Bhakti movement among the Marathas are linked with:
o: Kabir, Dadu Dayal and Guru Nanak
nf173ef385fb.x: Among the Marathas, early national awakening was associated with Tukaram, Ramdas and Shivaji.
nf173ef385fb.tq: Use the regional grouping of personalities rather than choosing a general Bhakti figure.
xs: Maratha national awakening is linked with **Tukaram, Ramdas and Shivaji** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Tukaram and Ramdas** shaped the Maratha movement under **Shivaji**.
xa: The other echo was among the **Sikhs** (early Sikh awakening).
Bhakti also **revived Hinduism around devotion** and weakened **priestly dominance**.

n838be04e2b2.s: Veerashaivism associated with Basava advocated which one of the following combinations?
o: Vedic ritualism, animal sacrifice and purdah
Caste hierarchy, child marriage and widow seclusion
Priestly monopoly, child marriage and caste exclusiveness
Caste opposition, widow remarriage and gender equality
n838be04e2b2.x: Basava’s Veerashaivism condemned caste and child marriage and supported widow remarriage and gender equality.
n838be04e2b2.tq: Match the reform movement with its positive social reforms.
xs: Basava's Veerashaivism stood for **caste opposition, widow remarriage and gender equality** — option **(4)** is correct.
It **opposed** caste, **animal sacrifice**, **Vedic ritualism** and **child marriage** — so options (1)-(3) are its opposite.
xa: It spread in Andhra through **Mallikarjuna, Inpati and Manchana Panditas**.
⚠ Limitation: it at times turned to violence, spread by the **"Sivapasa"** (sword).
**Lingayat / Veerasaiva** sect: founder **Basaveswara**; region **Karnataka, Andhra**.

n0e4404c6e4e.s: Which Andhra saint had disciples like Siddayya (a Dudekula) and Kakkaiah (a Madiga)?
n0e4404c6e4e.x: Veerabrahmam's disciples cut across castes and he admitted women; he opposed untouchability and idol worship.
xa: **Nasaraiah**, a Sayyid reformer (until **1825**), was popular among the **Madigas** of Vinukonda and Narasaraopeta.
Nasaraiah also opposed **untouchability** and **idol worship**.

n2f81719cf59.s: Who is regarded as the first medieval reformer to denounce caste outright, with disciples such as Kabir, Raidas, Sena and Dhanna?
n2f81719cf59.x: Ramananda was the first medieval reformer to denounce caste outright; his disciples included Kabir (weaver), Raidas (shoemaker), Sena (barber) and Dhanna (Jat cultivator). Ramanuja preached Vishishtadvaita, Basavanna led Veerashaivism, and Chaitanya is linked with sankirtan; none had this group of disciples.
n2f81719cf59.tq: Ramananda: first to denounce caste; disciples Kabir, Raidas, Sena, Dhanna.
xs: **Ramananda** was the **first medieval reformer to denounce caste outright** — option **(3)** is correct.
His disciples: **Kabir** (weaver), **Raidas** (shoemaker), **Sena** (barber), **Dhanna** (Jat cultivator).
**Ramanuja** is linked with **Srivaishnavism**; **Basavanna** with **Veerashaivism**; **Chaitanya** with **sankirtan**.
xa: ⚠ Even with Srivaishnavism and Veerashaivism, **caste inequalities could not be eradicated**.
**Namdev** the tailor was another low-caste saint.

n8b7660e4969.s: The interaction between Bhakti and Sufi traditions contributed to the emergence of:
n8b7660e4969.x: Bhakti-Sufi interaction produced a composite Indo-Islamic culture, with shrines and vernacular traditions acting as shared spaces.
n8b7660e4969.tq: Identify the broad cultural result of the interaction.
xs: Bhakti-Sufi interaction produced a **composite Indo-Islamic culture** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Shared Sufi shrines** and **vernacular** traditions were its common spaces, not Sanskritic or purely Persian culture.
xa: Political echo: **early Sikh and Maratha awakening**.
Limitation: sects **hardened into separate panths**.

n9c833d5f38e.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of women associated with open expression of devotion?
o: Mirabai, Andal, Lal Ded, Janabai and Bahinabai
Andal, Kabir, Janabai, Bahinabai and Lal Ded
Mirabai, Ravidas, Andal, Janabai and Bahinabai
Mirabai, Surdas, Andal, Lal Ded and Janabai
n9c833d5f38e.x: Mirabai, Andal, Lal Ded, Janabai and Bahinabai are the women named for expressing their devotion openly.
n9c833d5f38e.tq: Identify the complete list without admitting a male saint into it.
xs: **Mirabai, Andal, Lal Ded, Janabai and Bahinabai** expressed devotion openly — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kabir**, **Ravidas** and **Surdas** are men, so options (2)-(4) fail.
xa: **Mirabai** = Rajasthan, Krishna bhakti; **Andal** = only woman Alvar, Tamil Nadu.
**Lal Ded (Lalla)** = Kashmir, inspired the **Rishi movement**.
**Molla** = Telugu **Molla Ramayanam** (**16th c.**).

n7e910e83e23.s: Which one of the following developments represents the later limitation of the Bhakti and Sufi movements?
o: The movements became confined only to royal courts.
Vernacular devotional traditions were entirely abandoned.
Their traditions hardened into separate sects and panths.
n7e910e83e23.x: The movements later hardened into separate sects and panths, despite their earlier emphasis on broad spiritual and social interaction.
n7e910e83e23.tq: Identify the later reversal of an initially inclusive tendency.
xs: The movements later **hardened into separate sects and panths** — option **(4)** is correct.
They did not abandon vernaculars or stay in courts — vernacular preaching was their strength.
xa: Other limitation: **Naqshbandi orthodoxy** pushed back against Sufi-Bhakti liberalism.
Criticism: **egalitarian preaching did not dismantle caste**.

n3416cd5d768.s: Which of the following continued despite the Bhakti and Sufi movements?
n3416cd5d768.x: The movements did not end purdah or restrictions on women's public life, and caste inequalities persisted.
xa: Medieval norms grew **more restrictive** for women and lower castes: purdah, limited education and work.
Yet women like **Mirabai, Andal, Lal Ded** found room for open spiritual expression.

n621e0fcca15.s: Hath Yoga, whose techniques some Sufis adopted, was practised by the:
n621e0fcca15.x: Hath Yoga was practised by the Nathpanthi yogis of Gorakhnath's tradition, and Sufis adopted techniques such as breath control.
xa: The **Naqshbandis** were the exception to breath control.
Nath yogis and Sufis held **spiritual dialogues**.

nfcb9f0701ba.s: In medieval India, many Sanskrit works on music were translated into:
nfcb9f0701ba.x: Many Sanskrit musical works were rendered into Persian; the early Chishtis too were fond of music.
xa: **Chishti and Suhrawardi** held **"Majlis-i-Sama"**; the **Naqshbandis** opposed it.
**Ghunyat-ul-Munya** (**1375**) and **Raga Darpan** are Persian works on Indian music.

n8ba17b2e605.s: The Rishi movement is associated with:
n8ba17b2e605.x: The Rishi movement belongs to Kashmir; Dadupanth to Rajasthan and Mahanubhava to Maharashtra.
xa: Founders: **Dadu Dayal** (Dadupanth), **Chakradhara** (Mahanubhava), **Sheikh Nuruddin** (Rishi movement).
**Sikhism**: **Guru Nanak** (b. **1469**, Talwandi), Punjab.
**Lingayat / Veerasaiva**: **Basaveswara**, Karnataka and Andhra.

nindian-history-52-17.s: The Faraizi sect was formed by the followers of:
nindian-history-52-17.x: Haji Shariatullah's followers formed the Faraizi sect; Haridas's the Haridasi school and Dadu's the Dadu Panth.
n: Followers of Swami Haridas followed the Haridasi school of mysticism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 126-127]
Followers of Haji Shariatullah followed the Faraizi sect. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 126-127]
Followers of Dadu followed Dadu Panth. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 126-127]
Followers of Arya Samaj followed Arya Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 126-127]
xa: **Mahanubhava** sect: **Chakradhara**, **Maharashtra**.
**Rishi movement**: **Sheikh Nuruddin**, **Kashmir**.
**Kabirpanth**: followers of **Kabir**.

nd4c6ff35b87.x: Kabir was a disciple of Ramananda, not Guru Nanak; his followers are the Kabirpanthis.
xa: Kabir taught **one God by many names** (Ram, Rahim, Allah, Hari).
Kabir is a **non-Sikh contributor** to the Guru Granth Sahib.

nf578b3d6a59.s: Which of the following best represents Kabir’s religious teaching?
o: Caste hierarchy is necessary for spiritual progress.
One God may be called by names such as Ram, Rahim, Allah and Hari.
Only one religious community can attain salvation.
Rituals of both Hinduism and Islam are indispensable.
nf578b3d6a59.x: Kabir taught belief in one God known by many names and condemned the rituals of both faiths, advocating Hindu–Muslim unity.
nf578b3d6a59.tq: Apply the core teaching to a short doctrinal situation.
xs: Kabir taught **one God** called by names such as **Ram, Rahim, Allah and Hari** — option **(2)** is correct.
He **condemned rituals of both faiths** and stood for **Hindu-Muslim unity**, so options (1), (3), (4) contradict him.
xa: He was a disciple of **Ramananda**; raised by **Niru and Nima**.
Work: **Bijak**; followers: **Kabirpanthis**.

na22cbcc4416.s: Guru Nanak was born in 1469 at:
o: Talwandi, also known as Nankana Sahib, near the Ravi
na22cbcc4416.x: Guru Nanak was born in 1469 at Talwandi, now known as Nankana Sahib, near the Ravi.
na22cbcc4416.tq: Combine the year, alternate place name and geographical clue.
xs: Guru Nanak was born at **Talwandi (Nankana Sahib)** near the **Ravi** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Talwandi** and **Nankana Sahib** are the same place, so options naming other towns and rivers are wrong.
xa: Dates: **1469-1539** (some notes give 1469-1538).
Before death (**1539**) he chose **Guru Angad** as successor (UPPSC 2023).
His teachings were later compiled in the **Adi Granth**.

nf62fa67e36e.s: Which of the following was part of Guru Nanak's teachings?
o: Worship of child Krishna through Pushtimarga
nf62fa67e36e.x: Guru Nanak taught Nirguna devotion, Ek Onkar, Naam Simran and Sangat, rejecting the rituals of both religions.
xa: **Ek Onkar** = God is one.
Nanak = **founder** of Sikhism; region **Punjab**.

n4079bf126d5.s: Ramdaspur, later known as Amritsar, was founded by:
n4079bf126d5.x: Guru Ram Das founded Ramdaspur; Guru Amar Das strengthened langar and introduced the Manji system.
xa: **Guru Arjan** built the **Harmandir Sahib** (Golden Temple).
Amar Das was the **3rd** Guru, Ram Das the **4th**.

n39e2b288a43.s: Who is regarded as the first martyr Guru of the Sikhs?
n39e2b288a43.x: Guru Arjan Dev is regarded as the first martyr Guru.
xa: **350th martyrdom** year of Guru Tegh Bahadur was observed (**26 Jan 2026**).
Tegh Bahadur, born **Tyag Mal** in Amritsar, is called **"Hind-di-Chadar"**.

n4d388c33706.s: Anandpur Sahib was founded by which Sikh Guru?
n4d388c33706.x: Guru Tegh Bahadur founded Anandpur Sahib, also called Chak-Nanki.
n4d388c33706.tq: Apply the founder-versus-associated-event distinction to Sikh sacred places.
xs: **Guru Tegh Bahadur** founded **Anandpur Sahib** (Chak-Nanki) — option **(2)** is correct.
The **Khalsa** was later born there (Keshgarh Sahib) under **Guru Gobind Singh**.
xa: Anandpur Sahib hosts **Holla Mohalla**.
Tegh Bahadur has **116 hymns** in the Guru Granth Sahib.

n063e21f1ac1.s: After the death of Guru Gobind Singh, to whom did the Guruship pass permanently?
n063e21f1ac1.x: After Guru Gobind Singh, the Guru Granth Sahib was declared the eternal Guru.
n063e21f1ac1.tq: Test the institutional succession after the ten human Gurus.
xs: After Gobind Singh, Guruship passed to the scripture — the **Guru Granth Sahib** became the **eternal Guru** — option **(4)** is correct.
The **Panj Pyare** were five baptised volunteers; the **misls** were later Khalsa units.
xa: Gobind Singh **finalised** the Guru Granth Sahib; **Arjan** compiled the Adi Granth.
Gobind Singh died **1708**; his final resting place is **Nanded** (Hazur Sahib).

nd85eb1a0348.s: Which Sufi saint was a contributor to the Guru Granth Sahib?
nd85eb1a0348.x: Sheikh Farid, along with Namdev and Ravidas, contributed to the Guru Granth Sahib.
xa: ⚠ **116 hymns** = Tegh Bahadur; **41 shabdas** = Ravidas.
APPSC 2019: Sikh scripture = **Adigranth**.

n2d589487eba.s: The Guru Granth Sahib is written in which script?
n2d589487eba.x: The Guru Granth Sahib is written in the Gurmukhi script.
n2d589487eba.tq: Distinguish the script of the scripture from scripts used in neighbouring traditions.
xs: The Guru Granth Sahib is in **Gurmukhi** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Gurmukhi** was introduced by **Guru Angad**.
xa: Compiled by **Arjan** (5th); finalised by **Gobind Singh** (10th).
APPSC 2019: Sikh scripture = **Adigranth**.

n1f7d0be708f.s: Banda Bahadur was executed at Delhi in 1716 by:
n1f7d0be708f.x: Farrukhsiyar executed Banda Bahadur at Delhi in 1716 for refusing to convert.
xa: He was executed **for refusing to convert**.
**Gurdas Nangal** fell after an **eight-month siege** (**1715**).

n7230cbe72f5.s: Ranjit Singh's high court at Lahore was called the:
n7230cbe72f5.x: His high court was the Adalat-i-Ala; the Dal Khalsa was the combined force of the misls.
xa: Origin: **Sukerchakia misl**; title **"Lion of Punjab"**.
Kohinoor obtained from **Shah Shuja** (**1813**).

nindian-history-58-17.s: Which Sikh Guru organised the 22 Manjis?
nindian-history-58-17.x: Guru Amar Das set up the 22 Manjis.
n: Guru Angad was the successor appointed by Guru Nanak. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Guru Amar Das organised 22 Manjis. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Guru Tegh Bahadur was the 9th Guru. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
xa: **Guru Angad** standardised **Gurmukhi**.
**Guru Ram Das** received land from **Akbar** and founded **Amritsar**.
**Guru Gobind Singh** established the **Khalsa** in **1699**.

nindian-history-60-7.s: Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth in:
nindian-history-60-7.x: Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth in 1604.
n: Guru Ram Das received land from Akbar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 135-136]
Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth in 1604. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 135-136]
xa: Guru Arjan Dev **built Harmandir Sahib** and was the **first martyr Guru**.
The Adi Granth includes compositions of **Kabir**, **Baba Farid**, **Namdev** and **Raidas**.
⚠ Compiled by **Arjan** (5th); finalised by **Gobind Singh** (10th).

n5ec68234488.x: 'Sikh' means disciple, from the Sanskrit shishya. 'Pure' is the meaning of Khalsa; 'warrior' and 'brotherhood' are not the meaning of the word.
xs: **'Sikh'** means **disciple**, from Sanskrit **shishya** — option **(3)** is correct.
**'Pure'** is the meaning of **Khalsa**.
xa: **Ek Onkar** = God is one.
**Panj Pyare** = five volunteers baptised with **sacred nectar**.

n1c938e6c9d5.s: Which Guru finalised the Guru Granth Sahib and introduced the Five Ks?
n1c938e6c9d5.x: Guru Gobind Singh finalised the Guru Granth Sahib and introduced the Five Ks.
n1c938e6c9d5.tq: Distinguish finalisation of the scripture from its earlier compilation.
xs: **Guru Gobind Singh** finalised the Guru Granth Sahib and gave the **Five Ks** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Guru Arjan** only **compiled** the Adi Granth; **Ram Das** founded **Ramdaspur (Amritsar)**.
xa: Gobind Singh founded the **Khalsa (1699)**; died **1708**.
After him, the **Guru Granth Sahib** became the **eternal Guru**.
Five Ks: **Kesh, Kangha, Kara, Kachera, Kirpan**.

ndbd1b6ed655.s: The Adi Granth, later finalised as the Guru Granth Sahib, was compiled by
ndbd1b6ed655.x: Guru Arjan compiled the Adi Granth (APPSC 2019 named Adigranth as the Sikh scripture); Guru Gobind Singh finalised it as the Guru Granth Sahib. Guru Nanak's teachings were later compiled in it, Guru Angad introduced Gurmukhi, and Guru Tegh Bahadur's 116 hymns are included in it.
ndbd1b6ed655.tq: Adi Granth compiled = Guru Arjan; finalised = Guru Gobind Singh.
xs: **Guru Arjan** compiled the **Adi Granth** — option **(3)** is correct; **Guru Gobind Singh** finalised it.
**Guru Nanak's** teachings were compiled in it; **Guru Angad** introduced Gurmukhi.
**Guru Tegh Bahadur** contributed **116 hymns** but did not compile it.
xa: APPSC 2019: Sikh scripture = **Adigranth**.
Arjan also built **Harmandir Sahib** and was the **first martyr Guru**.

n0e685aea863.s: The Khalsa was founded on 13 April 1699 at:
n0e685aea863.x: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa on Baisakhi, 13 April 1699, at Takht Keshgarh Sahib in Anandpur.
n0e685aea863.tq: Combine the exact date with the correct sacred place.
xs: The Khalsa was founded at **Takht Keshgarh Sahib, Anandpur** (**13 April 1699**, Baisakhi) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Harmandir Sahib** is at Amritsar; **Damdama Sahib** = Talwandi Sabo; **Takht Sachkhand** = Nanded.
xa: Founder: **Guru Gobind Singh**; he baptised the **Panj Pyare** with sacred nectar.
**Khalsa** = "pure".

nab5b2aa179e.x: Khalsa means 'pure'. The Panj Pyare were baptised with sacred nectar at its founding.
nab5b2aa179e.tq: Distinguish the literal meaning of Khalsa from related Sikh terms.
xs: **Khalsa** means **"pure"** — option **(2)** is correct.
**'Disciple'** is the meaning of **'Sikh'**.
xa: Founded **13 April 1699** at **Anandpur**.
**Dal Khalsa** = combined force of the Sikh **misls**.

nce1554bac9b.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the Five Ks of the Khalsa?
nce1554bac9b.x: The Five Ks are Kesh, Kangha, Kara, Kachera and Kirpan; Kirtan is not one of them.
xa: The Five Ks came with **Guru Gobind Singh**, founder of the **Khalsa (1699)**.
Khalsa = **"pure"**.

nc762bfee016.s: The combined force of the Sikh misls was known as the
nc762bfee016.x: The combined force of the Sikh misls was called the Dal Khalsa. Ranjit Singh united the Sikh misls.
nc762bfee016.tq: Distinguish the collective force of the misls from the later modernised army.
xs: The combined force of the misls was the **Dal Khalsa** — option **(4)** is correct.
The **Khalsa army** was Ranjit Singh's army modernised with **European officers**.
xa: ⚠ **Adalat-i-Ala** = Ranjit Singh's **high court** at Lahore.
**12 misls** formed after Banda.

nc092df0c317.s: The autonomous administration established by the Khalsa after 1708 lay between which two rivers?
nc092df0c317.x: After 1708, the Khalsa established an autonomous administration in the region between the Sutlej and Jamuna.
nc092df0c317.tq: Use the geographical boundary pair to identify the correct region.
xs: The Khalsa's autonomous administration after **1708** lay between the **Sutlej and Jamuna** (UPSC) — option **(4)** is correct.
This followed Guru Gobind Singh's death in **1708** and Banda Bahadur's campaigns.
xa: After Banda, the Khalsa organised into **12 misls**.
⚠ The **Treaty of Amritsar** (**1809**) fixed the **Sutlej** as the British-Ranjit Singh boundary.

n616d7507a9e.s: Ranjit Singh captured Lahore, which became the capital of his kingdom, in:
n616d7507a9e.x: Ranjit Singh captured Lahore in 1799 and made it his capital.
xa: His high court at Lahore: **Adalat-i-Ala**.
⚠ Capital and Treaty of Amritsar are the **most-asked** facts.

n7c1019bcacc.s: The Treaty of Amritsar of 1809 fixed which river as the boundary between the territories of Ranjit Singh and the British?
n7c1019bcacc.x: The Treaty of Amritsar, concluded in 1809 with Lord Minto, fixed the Sutlej as the boundary between the British and Ranjit Singh's territories.
n7c1019bcacc.tq: Test the specific territorial consequence of a treaty rather than its parties.
xs: The **Treaty of Amritsar** (**1809**) with **Lord Minto** fixed the **Sutlej** as boundary — option **(1)** is correct (JPSC 2023).
It divided **British** territory from **Ranjit Singh's** territories.
xa: Treaty of perpetual friendship with **Bentinck**: **1831**.
Ranjit Singh's capital: **Lahore**.

n5ffb9af7d58.s: Who was the regent of the minor Dalip Singh?
n5ffb9af7d58.x: Rani Jindan acted as regent for the minor Dalip Singh, who was the last ruler of Punjab before its annexation.
n5ffb9af7d58.tq: Match the minor ruler with the correct regent.
xs: **Rani Jindan** was regent for the minor **Dalip Singh** — option **(4)** is correct.
Dalip Singh came after **Kharak Singh, Nau Nihal Singh, Sher Singh**.
xa: Dalip Singh was the **last Sikh ruler**.
Ranjit Singh died **1839**; Punjab was **annexed 1849**.

n507c4905494.s: Ranjit Singh obtained the Kohinoor diamond in 1813 from
n507c4905494.x: Ranjit Singh obtained the Kohinoor from the Afghan ruler Shah Shuja in 1813. Lord Minto signed the Treaty of Amritsar (1809) with him, and Duleep Singh was his last successor. Nadir Shah took the Kohinoor from Delhi in 1739, long before 1813.
n507c4905494.tq: Kohinoor to Ranjit Singh from Shah Shuja, 1813.
xs: Ranjit Singh obtained the **Kohinoor** from the Afghan ruler **Shah Shuja** (**1813**) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Lord Minto** signed the **Treaty of Amritsar (1809)**; **Duleep Singh** was his last successor.
xa: Ranjit Singh's army was **modernised with European officers**.
Treaty of perpetual friendship with **Bentinck**: **1831**.

n4f5475b6d52.s: Who was the last Sikh ruler?
n4f5475b6d52.x: Duleep Singh was the last Sikh ruler.
n4f5475b6d52.tq: Distinguish the last ruler from earlier Sikh leaders and founders by focusing on the succession endpoint.
xs: **Duleep Singh** was the **last Sikh ruler** — option **(2)** is correct.
He was a **minor**, with **Rani Jindan** as regent; **Banda Bahadur** was the **first** sovereign Sikh ruler.
xa: Ranjit Singh's successors: **Kharak Singh, Nau Nihal Singh, Sher Singh, Duleep Singh**.
Two **Anglo-Sikh Wars** → **Punjab annexed 1849**.

n60b9b6b47e0.s: Which event directly disrupted the principal overland route from Europe to India in the fifteenth century?
o: The capture of Constantinople by Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II in 1453
The signing of the Treaty of Tordesillas in 1494
The first voyage of the English East India Company in 1602
The Portuguese occupation of Calicut in 1498
n60b9b6b47e0.x: Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II captured Constantinople in 1453, closing the main overland route through Constantinople and Central Asia to India.
n60b9b6b47e0.tq: Connect the geopolitical event with its commercial consequence.
xs: Ottoman **Mehmed II** captured **Constantinople** in **1453**, closing the main overland route — option **(1)** is correct.
**Tordesillas (1494)** divided new lands between Spain and Portugal; it did not close any route.
xa: ⚠ Some notes give the year as **1452**.
The old route: **Europe → Constantinople → Central Asia → India**.
**1453/1498** mark the beginning of the **Modern Age** for India and Andhra.

nindian-history-87-18.s: Vasco da Gama's final visit to India took place in:
nindian-history-87-18.x: 1502 was his second voyage; his final visit was in 1524.
n: Vasco da Gama discovered a new or alternative sea route to India from Europe. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #87 · pp 169-170]
Vasco da Gama's arrival opened a new era of Portuguese–Indian trade. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #87 · pp 169-170]
Black pepper was an important commodity. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #87 · pp 169-170]
Vasco da Gama's first return or revisit mentioned in the notes was in 1502 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #87 · pp 169-170]
Vasco da Gama later visited India in 1524 CE. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #87 · pp 169-170]
xa: On the 2nd voyage (**1502**) the Zamorin refused trade; he settled at **Kochi**.
He died at **Kochi** in **1524**.
In **1498** the Delhi ruler was **Sikandar Lodi**; Vijayanagara's was **Immadi Narasimha Raya**.

nbb6a3d65b71.s: Which of the following technological aids made long-distance voyages safer during the Age of Discovery?
nbb6a3d65b71.x: The caravel and astrolabe are identified as navigational advances that made long voyages safer.
nbb6a3d65b71.tq: Select the paired navigational advances actually associated with the period.
xs: The **caravel** and **astrolabe** made long voyages safer (UPSC) — option **(1)** is correct.
Telegraph, steamship and railway are not in this age's navigational advances.
xa: **Prince Henry "the Navigator"** set up **naval training centres** in Portugal.
He was the **first European to actively promote navigation**.

n638ad3084f1.s: Which of the following was NOT a major motive behind European expansion towards Asia?
o: Establishing a permanent Roman imperial administration in India
Breaking the Arab control over Asian trade
n638ad3084f1.x: Spices, silk, religion, wealth, prestige, rivalry and the desire to break Arab control were stated motives. Establishing a Roman imperial administration was not one of them.
n638ad3084f1.tq: Reject the historically unrelated imperial association.
xs: A **Roman imperial administration in India** was never a motive — option **(1)** is the answer.
Real motives: **spices and silk**, breaking the **Arab** monopoly, **spreading Christianity**, wealth, prestige, rivalry, curiosity.
xa: Spices sought: **pepper, cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, cloves, nutmeg**.
**Italy** (Venice, Genoa) was the distribution centre of Asian trade.
Rivals: **Spain, Portugal, Netherlands, England, France**.

na98d47b9918.s: Who reached the southern tip of Africa in 1488 and called it the Cape of Storms?
na98d47b9918.x: Bartholomew Dias reached the southern tip of Africa in 1488 and named it the Cape of Storms. King John II later renamed it the Cape of Good Hope.
na98d47b9918.tq: Associate the achievement, date and original name with the explorer.
xs: **Bartholomew Dias** reached Africa's southern tip (**1488**) and called it the **"Cape of Storms"** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Magellan** = first circumnavigation; **John Cabot** = North America; **Cabral** = Brazil.
xa: **John II** renamed it the **Cape of Good Hope**.
⚠ Sequence: **1488** Dias - **1492** Columbus - **1494** Tordesillas - **1498** da Gama - **1500** Cabral.

nba3471d6b46.s: Which Portuguese navigator reached Brazil and India in 1500?
nba3471d6b46.x: Cabral reached Brazil and India in 1500 and set up factories at Calicut, Cannanore and Cochin.
xa: Cabral reached Brazil **two years after** da Gama reached India.
AP angle: Brazil's **Nelore** cattle (**80%** of its livestock) come from **Nellore**.

nad80b623a2c.s: Who commissioned Vasco da Gama's expedition that sailed from Lisbon in July 1497?
nad80b623a2c.x: King Manuel I commissioned Vasco da Gama's expedition. The fleet sailed from Lisbon on 8 July 1497.
nad80b623a2c.tq: Use the patron-and-expedition association rather than the better-known explorer association.
xs: **King Manuel I** of Portugal sponsored da Gama's voyage — option **(4)** is correct.
**John II** renamed the **Cape of Good Hope**; **Prince Henry** promoted navigation earlier.
xa: He left **Lisbon on 8 July 1497** with four ships (**São Gabriel, São Rafael, Berrio** + supply ship).
Manuel I was among the **contemporaries in 1498**, with the Zamorin, Sikandar Lodi and Immadi Narasimha Raya.

n3617a8a905d.s: During Vasco da Gama's second voyage (1502), after the Zamorin refused trade, the Portuguese settled at:
n3617a8a905d.x: The Zamorin refused trade, Calicut was occupied, and the Portuguese settled at Kochi.
xa: 1st voyage (**1497-99**): Calicut, **Zamorin's welcome**.
⚠ CGPSC 2022: only "**Zamorin ruled Calicut**" was correct.

n933707e80b1.s: Vasco da Gama's third voyage to India in 1524 is associated with which of the following?
o: His appointment as Viceroy and his death at Kochi
His discovery of Brazil and establishment of factories
His meeting with Jahangir at Surat
His first departure from Lisbon and rounding of the Cape
n933707e80b1.x: Vasco da Gama returned in 1524 as Viceroy and died at Kochi in the same year.
n933707e80b1.tq: Link the office, year and place of death as one distinct episode.
xs: On the **3rd voyage (1524)** he came as **Viceroy** and **died at Kochi** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Brazil** = **Cabral** (**1500**); the first departure from Lisbon was in **1497**.
xa: 2nd voyage (**1502**): Zamorin refused trade; settled at **Kochi**.
⚠ CGPSC 2022: he did **not stay a year** in India.

ncb3b2c4e89a.s: The Dutch East India Company, established in 1602, was granted which of the following powers by the States-General?
o: Sovereign powers such as waging war, building forts and making treaties
Exclusive authority to mint coins throughout Asia
The power to appoint Mughal governors in coastal provinces
Only the right to collect customs duties in Indian ports
ncb3b2c4e89a.x: The States-General granted the VOC sovereign powers, including making war, constructing forts and concluding treaties.
ncb3b2c4e89a.tq: Match the company with the distinctive authority granted to it.
xs: The **States-General** gave the **Dutch VOC (1602)** **sovereign powers** — to wage **war**, build **forts** and make **treaties** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The notes record no grant of minting rights or power over Mughal governors; the powers were wider than mere customs collection.
xa: Dutch first factory: **Masulipatnam 1605**; headquarters **Pulicat (1610)**, later **Nagapatnam**.
Some notes date the Dutch company to **1592** — use **1602**.
The Dutch were defeated by **Travancore** at **Colachel (1741)**.

n90c53b5b8c9.s: The French established their first factory in India at Surat in:
n90c53b5b8c9.x: The French first factory was at Surat in 1668; the Dutch began at Masulipatnam in 1605 and the Danes at Tranquebar in 1620.
xa: The **English** first factory was also at **Surat** (farman **1613**).
Danish headquarters: Tranquebar, and **Serampore (1755)**; both sold to the British in **1845**.
French headquarters: **Pondicherry**; Dutch headquarters: **Pulicat (1610)**, later **Nagapatnam**.

n426004f9623.s: Which of the following European companies was formed first?
n426004f9623.x: The order of formation was English (1600), Dutch (1602), Danish (1616) and French (1664).
xa: English charter: **31 Dec 1600** by **Elizabeth I**, with a **15-year** monopoly, later perpetual.
Dutch **VOC 1602** got sovereign powers from the **States-General**.
Some notes date the Dutch company to **1592** — use **1602**.

n0d66cd34dbc.s: The charter of the English East India Company (31 December 1600) was granted by:
n0d66cd34dbc.x: Elizabeth I granted the charter, with a 15-year monopoly between the Cape of Good Hope and the Magellan Straits.
xa: The EIC was a **private joint-stock** company run by a **Court of Directors**.
First voyage **1602** under **James Lancaster** to **Bantam**.
**1707:** rival companies merged into the "**United Company of Merchants**".

n7d7a992d724.s: With reference to Thomas Best, which one of the following is correct?
o: He represented the Danish Company at the court of Shah Jahan.
He defeated the Portuguese at Swally and obtained the Surat farman in 1613.
He was refused permission for trade under Portuguese pressure in 1608.
He secured the right to establish factories throughout the Mughal Empire in 1615.
n7d7a992d724.x: Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese at Swally in 1612, and the English obtained the Surat farman in 1613.
n7d7a992d724.tq: Separate closely associated English envoys by their specific achievement.
xs: **Thomas Best** beat the **Portuguese at Swally (1612)** and secured the **Surat farman (1613)** — option **(2)**.
Revocation under Portuguese pressure (1608) relates to **William Hawkins**; factories across the empire (**1615**) to **Sir Thomas Roe**.
Best was English, at **Jahangir's** court — not Danish or at Shah Jahan's.
xa: **Swally** was near **Surat**; the English won.
English vs Portuguese again at **Jask / Ormuz** (**1620 / 1622**) — Ormuz taken for the Shah of Persia.
**Roe** got factories at **Agra, Ahmedabad, Broach** but no treaty.

n8c5dc4d0a70.s: Pulicat was important in the European trade network because it was
o: the English capital of the Madras Presidency
the French headquarters and a centre for indigo
a Portuguese settlement captured by the Dutch and later their headquarters
the Danish headquarters after the acquisition of Serampore
n8c5dc4d0a70.x: Pulicat was initially Portuguese, was captured by the Dutch and became the Dutch headquarters in 1610; pepper and cloth were important commodities there.
n8c5dc4d0a70.tq: Combine the place, change of control, headquarters and commodities clues.
xs: **Pulicat** was a **Portuguese** settlement captured by the **Dutch**, who made it their **headquarters (1610)** — option **(3)**.
It traded in **pepper and cloth**.
The French headquarters was **Pondicherry**; Danish bases were Tranquebar and **Serampore**.
xa: Dutch HQ later moved to **Nagapatnam**.
Dutch first factory: **Masulipatnam 1605**.
**Madras** (Fort St. George, **1639**) was the English base.

n4992e2f08d7.s: Which development most directly marked the end of the Portuguese naval monopoly in the Indian Ocean?
o: The expulsion of the Portuguese from Hooghly by Shah Jahan alone
The rise of the Dutch and English as competing maritime powers
The establishment of the French settlement at Yanam
The sale of Serampore and Tranquebar by the Danes
n4992e2f08d7.x: The Portuguese naval monopoly ended with the emergence of the Dutch and English as competing maritime powers.
n4992e2f08d7.tq: Identify the broad historical significance rather than a single local event.
xs: The Portuguese **naval monopoly** was ended by the **Dutch and English** as competing maritime powers — option **(2)**.
Hooghly's loss (**1632**), Yanam and the Danish sale (**1845**) are local events, not the cause.
xa: **Swally (1612)** and **Jask / Ormuz (1620 / 1622)**: English beat the Portuguese.
The Dutch captured **Pulicat** from the Portuguese.
Portuguese monopoly tools: **Cartaz**, **Caes**, customs duties.

nindian-history-33-12.s: In which year was the Portuguese first factory established at Calicut?
nindian-history-33-12.x: The Portuguese set up their first factory at Calicut in 1500, under Pedro Alvares Cabral. 1503 is the Cochin fort, 1534 is Chatgaon, and 1611 is the English at Masulipatnam.
nindian-history-33-12.tq: Recall the year of each European settlement.
n: Calicut had the first Portuguese factory in 1500. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 99-100]
xs: The first Portuguese factory at **Calicut** was set up in **1500** — option **(1)**.
**1503** = the **first Portuguese fort**, at **Cochin (Kochi)**.
**1534** = Portuguese factories at **Satgaon** and **Chatgaon**.
xa: **Goa** was taken from **Bijapur** in **1510**.
**Cabral** reached India in **1500**, with factories at Calicut, Cannanore, Cochin.
**Batavia** was the **Dutch** eastern centre.

n7221a2211a2.s: Who formulated the Blue Water Policy in Portuguese India?
n7221a2211a2.x: Francisco de Almeida, the first Portuguese viceroy in India, followed the Blue Water Policy, which emphasised naval mastery rather than territorial expansion inland.
n7221a2211a2.tq: Use the governor–policy association and distinguish naval control from land conquest.
xs: The **Blue Water Policy** was formulated by **Francisco de Almeida** — option **(1)** is correct.
It meant **naval mastery of the Indian Ocean**, not land conquest; Almeida (**1505-09**) was the **first viceroy**.
⚠ Not **Albuquerque**, who reversed it for territorial conquest, nor **Nuno da Cunha**.
xa: APPSC-G2 **2023** and **2025** asked this — Blue Water Policy = **Portuguese**, **Almeida**.
Other Portuguese maritime monopoly tools: **Cartaz** (naval pass), convoy (**Caes**), customs duties.
**Albuquerque (1509-15)** took **Goa (1510)**, **Malacca (1511)** and Hormuz.

n3a87420b899.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with Afonso de Albuquerque?
o: Capture of Goa from Bijapur in 1510
Transfer of the Portuguese headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530
Abolition of Sati in Portuguese territories
n3a87420b899.x: Nuno da Cunha moved the Portuguese headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530. Albuquerque captured Goa, encouraged mixed marriages and abolished Sati.
n3a87420b899.tq: Find the deed belonging to another governor rather than the principal governor named.
xs: Moving the headquarters from **Cochin to Goa (1530)** was done by **Nuno da Cunha**, not Albuquerque — option **(2)**.
**Albuquerque** did take **Goa from Bijapur (1510)**, promoted **mixed marriages** with local women and abolished **Sati** in his territories.
xa: Albuquerque (**1509-15**) is the **real founder** of Portuguese power; also took **Malacca (1511)** and Hormuz.
Nuno da Cunha (**1529-38**) made a treaty with **Bahadur Shah** of Gujarat (**1535**) → fort at **Diu**; got **Diu** and **Bassein**.
Goa was the first European territorial acquisition in India since **Alexander**.

n8705729401f.s: Which Portuguese governor reversed Almeida's naval policy and pursued territorial conquest, including Goa?
n8705729401f.x: Albuquerque reversed Almeida's exclusively naval approach and took Goa, Malacca and Hormuz.
xa: Albuquerque served **1509-15** and died **1515** (notes giving "1509-1550" are misprints).
He promoted **mixed marriages** and abolished **Sati** in his territories.
**Hooghly** was a Portuguese settlement later expelled by **Shah Jahan (1632)**.

n1e864768f80.s: The treaty negotiated by Friar Luis with Krishnadevaraya during 1509–10 was associated with which development?
o: The Portuguese acquisition of Bombay from Charles II
The Portuguese capture of Goa with assistance from Timmaju
n1e864768f80.x: Friar Luis negotiated with Krishnadevaraya, and the Vijayanagara naval commander Timmaju assisted the Portuguese in capturing Goa.
n1e864768f80.tq: Link the diplomatic negotiator and regional ally with the event they facilitated.
xs: Friar Luis's treaty with **Krishnadevaraya (1509-10)** links to the **Portuguese capture of Goa**, helped by **Timmaju** — option **(3)**.
**Timmaju** was the Vijayanagara **naval commander**; Goa was taken from **Bijapur** in **1510**.
**Bombay** came via Charles II's dowry in **1661**, and **Shah Jahan** expelled the Portuguese from **Hooghly** in **1632** — unrelated.
xa: **Bhatkal:** Portuguese fort with Vijayanagara consent, linked to Krishnadevaraya's **horse trade**.
Albuquerque's capture of Goa was the first European territorial acquisition since **Alexander**.
Portuguese and Arab traders supplied **horses** to the Deccan.

nff8536e6e25.s: The Portuguese obtained Diu in 1535 from:
nff8536e6e25.x: Diu came from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat in 1535; Goa was taken from the Bijapur Sultan in 1510.
xa: **Bombay:** **1661** dowry of Catherine of Braganza to Charles II → to the EIC **1668**.
**Marathas** took **Salsette and Bassein (1739)**.
The Goa capture was helped by Vijayanagara naval commander **Timmaju**.

n986438b5697.s: Who obtained the site for Madras from the Raja of Chandragiri and built Fort St. George in 1639?
n986438b5697.x: Francis Day obtained the site from the Raja of Chandragiri and built Fort St. George at Madras in 1639.
n986438b5697.tq: Apply the founder–work trap by distinguishing Francis Day from Job Charnock.
xs: **Francis Day** got the Madras site from the **Raja of Chandragiri** and built **Fort St. George (1639)** — option **(1)**.
**Thomas Roe** was envoy to Jahangir (**1615**); **Job Charnock** founded the settlement at **Sutanuti (1690)**.
⚠ Some tables wrongly say the site came "from the Portuguese" — it came from the Raja of Chandragiri.
xa: Calcutta: zamindari of **Sutanuti, Gobindapur, Kalikata** bought **1698**; **Fort William 1700**.
Bombay: dowry **1661**, to the EIC **1668**.
**Golden Farman (1636)** from **Abdullah Qutb Shah** of Golconda.

nb114bb41444.s: Fort William at Calcutta was built in:
nb114bb41444.x: Job Charnock settled at Sutanuti in 1690, the zamindaris were bought in 1698 and Fort William was built in 1700.
xa: **Madras:** Fort St. George, **1639**, by **Francis Day**.
**Farrukhsiyar's farman (1717):** duty-free trade in Bengal.
**Hooghly** was earlier a Portuguese settlement, expelled by **Shah Jahan (1632)**.

n499d1da2e50.s: The farman issued by Farrukhsiyar in 1717 is associated with which concession to the English East India Company?
o: Transfer of Bombay at nominal rent
Permission to build a fort at Bhatkal
n499d1da2e50.x: Farrukhsiyar’s farman of 1717 granted the English East India Company the privilege of duty-free trade in Bengal.
n499d1da2e50.tq: Link the ruler and year with the precise commercial concession.
xs: **Farrukhsiyar's farman (1717)** gave **duty-free trade in Bengal** — option **(4)**.
**Bombay** at nominal rent came from the Crown in **1668**; **Bhatkal** was a Portuguese fort; Hooghly was Portuguese, expelled by Shah Jahan.
xa: **Golden Farman ('Bangaru Farmana'):** **1636** (many books say **1632**), from **Abdullah Qutb Shah** of Golconda.
**Surat farman 1613** followed Best's victory at Swally.
**Sir Thomas Roe (1615):** right to set up factories across the empire.

naa09d5f0e65.s: Who led the English victory over the Portuguese at Swally in 1612?
naa09d5f0e65.x: Thomas Best led the Swally victory; Hawkins's Surat permission had been revoked under Portuguese pressure, and Edward Terry was Roe's chaplain.
xa: Hawkins was envoy of **James I** to **Jahangir** (**1608-09**); left **Nov 1611**.
Title "**English Khan**".
**Surat farman 1613** came after Best's win.

n85dccffd856.s: Sir Thomas Roe’s mission to Jahangir in 1615 resulted in:
o: The defeat of the Portuguese at Swally
The establishment of the first English factory at Machilipatnam
A formal treaty and the transfer of Bombay to the Company
Factories at Agra, Ahmedabad and Broach, though no treaty was concluded
n85dccffd856.x: Sir Thomas Roe concluded no treaty with Jahangir, but factories were established at Agra, Ahmedabad and Broach during his mission.
n85dccffd856.tq: Distinguish the actual result of a diplomatic mission from military and territorial events.
xs: **Roe's** mission (**1615**) won factories at **Agra, Ahmedabad and Broach**, but **no treaty** — option **(4)**.
He was envoy of **James I** and got the **right to set up factories** across the empire.
**Swally** was **Thomas Best's** victory (**1612**); **Bombay** came via dowry (**1661**) to the EIC (**1668**).
xa: The **Dutch**, not the English, had the first factory at **Masulipatnam (1605)**.
Edward Terry was **Roe's chaplain**.
Order of envoys: Fitch → Hawkins → Best → Roe.

nb64e487f20c.s: The Golden Farman of 1636 granting English trade concessions was issued by
nb64e487f20c.x: Abdullah Qutb Shah of Golconda issued the Golden Farman in 1636, granting trade concessions to the English.
nb64e487f20c.tq: Use the ruler–grant association and distinguish Golconda from neighbouring Deccan powers.
xs: The **Golden Farman (1636)** was issued by **Abdullah Qutb Shah of Golconda** — option **(4)**.
The **Raja of Chandragiri** gave Francis Day the **Madras** site; the **Bijapur** Sultan lost Goa (**1510**).
xa: Telugu name: **'Bangaru Farmana'**; many books date it **1632**.
**Farrukhsiyar's farman (1717):** duty-free trade in Bengal.
Portuguese religious intolerance alienated **Golconda**.

nbcffa209e32.s: Bheemunipatnam in North Coastal Andhra was a settlement of the:
nbcffa209e32.x: Bheemunipatnam was a Dutch settlement; Yanam was French.
xa: **Masulipatnam:** Portuguese first (APPSC key), Dutch factory **1605**, later English and French.
**Yanam:** one of the **4 French enclaves**.
AP angle also includes the **Golden Farman** and **Kalamkari** export trade.

ne4ab148c808.s: The Battle of Swally, fought near Surat in 1612, was fought between the
ne4ab148c808.x: At Swally in 1612, the English under Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese near Surat.
ne4ab148c808.tq: Match the battle with its two European participants.
xs: Swally (**1612**) was fought between the **English** and the **Portuguese** — option **(4)**.
The English under **Thomas Best** won near **Surat**, leading to the **Surat farman 1613**.
xa: **Jask / Ormuz (1620 / 1622):** English beat the Portuguese again.
**Colachel (1741):** **Travancore** beat the **Dutch**.
**Wandiwash (1760):** English (**Eyre Coote**) beat French (**Lally**).

n5084bc7c223.s: The Battle of Wandiwash (1760) was fought between:
o: The English under Eyre Coote and the French under Lally
The English under Thomas Best and the Portuguese
Travancore under Marthanda Varma and the Dutch
The English under Francis Forde and the Dutch
n5084bc7c223.x: Wandiwash (1760): English (Eyre Coote) defeated French (Lally). Thomas Best vs Portuguese was Swally 1612; Marthanda Varma vs Dutch was Colachel 1741; Forde vs Dutch was Bedara 1759.
xs: **Wandiwash (1760):** English under **Eyre Coote** beat the French under **Lally** — option **(1)**.
**Thomas Best vs Portuguese** was **Swally (1612)**; **Marthanda Varma vs Dutch** was **Colachel (1741)**.
xa: French company: **1664**, state-controlled; HQ **Pondicherry**.
French first factory: **Surat 1668**.
**Yanam** was one of the **4 French enclaves**.

ne6305fa4e4a.s: The Portuguese cartaz system was primarily a system of
ne6305fa4e4a.x: Cartaz was a naval-pass system used to regulate shipping and enforce the Portuguese maritime monopoly, along with convoys and customs duties.
ne6305fa4e4a.tq: Identify the practical function of an unfamiliar administrative term from its context.
xs: The **Cartaz** was a **naval pass** system controlling maritime trade — option **(3)** is correct.
It was a **maritime monopoly tool**, used with **convoys (Caes)** and **customs duties**.
It had nothing to do with military recruitment, conversion or land revenue.
xa: **Blue Water Policy:** **Almeida's** naval mastery of the Indian Ocean.
**Estado da India:** the state-controlled Portuguese venture.
Locals in Andhra called the Portuguese **'Budata Keechu'**.

nf3618edd32c.s: Which one of the following was introduced in India by the Portuguese?
nf3618edd32c.x: Tobacco is one of the New World crops the Portuguese brought to India, along with potato, chilli, maize, pineapple, papaya, cashew and groundnut. Rubber, tea and coffee are not in that list.
nf3618edd32c.tq: Recognise a crop contribution and avoid importing unrelated colonial crops.
xs: **Tobacco** was introduced by the Portuguese — option **(2)** is correct.
The Portuguese crops list: **tobacco, potato, chilli, maize, pineapple, papaya, cashew, groundnut** — rubber, tea and coffee are not in it.
xa: The Portuguese set up the **printing press** at **Goa** in **1556**.
Portuguese and Arab traders supplied **horses** to the Deccan.
Andhra's **calico / Kalamkari** export trade drew European traders.

nf789f082beb.s: The first printing press in India was introduced by the Portuguese at Goa in
nf789f082beb.x: The Portuguese introduced the printing press at Goa in 1556.
nf789f082beb.tq: Separate the printing-press year from the arrival, Goa-capture and English-charter years.
xs: The first printing press was set up by the Portuguese at **Goa** in **1556** — option **(3)**.
**1498** is the Portuguese arrival, **1510** the capture of **Goa**, and **1600** the English charter.
xa: Portuguese crops: **tobacco, potato, chilli, maize, pineapple, papaya, cashew, groundnut**.
Portuguese were **first to come, last to leave** — Goa freed in **1961**.
**Goa** became Portuguese headquarters (Cochin earlier).

n2a52b3c3648.s: Goa, Daman and Diu were liberated from Portuguese rule in 1961 through:
n2a52b3c3648.x: The Portuguese, first to arrive and last to leave, lost Goa, Daman and Diu in 1961 through Operation Vijay.
xa: The **Danes** left first among the late powers, selling **Serampore and Tranquebar** in **1845**.
The **Marathas** took **Salsette and Bassein (1739)**; the Portuguese held Goa against them (**1798**).
Portuguese naval monopoly was ended by the **Dutch** and **English**.

n2100220be7d.s: The Marathas captured Salsette and Bassein from the Portuguese in:
n2100220be7d.x: The Marathas took Salsette and Bassein in 1739, though the Portuguese held Goa against them in 1798.
xa: **Bassein** had been obtained from Gujarat under **Nuno da Cunha**.
**Shah Jahan** expelled the Portuguese from **Hooghly (1632)**.
Portuguese: **first to come, last to leave** (**Operation Vijay**).

nf0150cadc81.s: In the Battle of Diu fought in 1509, Almeida defeated the combined fleet of:
o: Gujarat, the Egyptian Mamluks and the Zamorin
The English, the Persians and Bijapur
nf0150cadc81.x: Almeida defeated the combined fleet of Gujarat, the Egyptian Mamluks and the Zamorin at Diu in 1509.
nf0150cadc81.tq: Recall the complete composition of the opposing coalition.
xs: At **Diu (1509)** **Almeida** beat the combined fleet of **Gujarat**, the **Egyptian Mamluks** and the **Zamorin** — option **(1)**.
The **English**, **Persians**, **Marathas**, **Arakanese** and **Dutch** were not part of that fleet.
xa: Almeida was the **first Viceroy**.
The **Zamorin of Calicut** clashed constantly with the Portuguese over **monopoly and heavy duties**.
⚠ Battle of Diu (**1509**) ≠ Diu fort by treaty (**1535**) ≠ Diu conquered (**1546**).

n6a1ac499f90.s: Which one of the following was associated with the Goa Inquisition?
o: Use of state machinery for conversions and action against religious dissent
Suppression of Arakanese piracy by Shaista Khan
Promotion of religious dissent by Portuguese officials
n6a1ac499f90.x: The Goa Inquisition in the sixteenth century acted against religious dissent and used state machinery for conversions.
n6a1ac499f90.tq: Identify the institutional function from the action described.
xs: The **Goa Inquisition** acted **against religious dissent** and used **state machinery for conversions** — option **(2)**.
It belonged to the **16th century**.
**Hugli** was granted by **Akbar (1579)**; **Shaista Khan** suppressed Arakanese pirates — unrelated.
xa: Forced conversion and inter-marriage **alienated Indians** — an internal cause of decline.
Religious intolerance alienated the **Golconda Sultans**.
**St. Francis Xavier** arrived in Goa in **1542**.

n8bddbdf2556.s: Who was the first Portuguese Viceroy in India?
n8bddbdf2556.x: Almeida was the first Viceroy and won the Battle of Diu in 1509.
xa: **Diu** fort came by treaty with **Bahadur Shah** in **1535**; conquered **1546**.
**St. Francis Xavier** arrived in Goa in **1542**; his remains are in the **Basilica of Bom Jesus**.
Portuguese printing press: **1556**.

na37ef882e03.s: The Portuguese, the first Europeans to come to India, finally left India in:
na37ef882e03.x: The Portuguese were the last European power to leave, in 1961; 1510 is when Goa was taken.
xa: Goa: first European territory since **Alexander**.
**Goa statehood:** **May 1987**.
New World crops **reshaped Indian cuisine**.

n8b192511a0d.s: The Portuguese obtained Daman by treaty in:
n8b192511a0d.x: Daman was obtained in 1559; Bassein in 1534, and Diu was conquered in 1546.
xa: **Hugli** was granted by **Akbar (1579)**.
**Diu Fort** was built **1535-41**.
Other settlements: **San Thome** (near Madras) and **Salsette**.

n8148f54c31d.s: Which Portuguese settlement was granted by Akbar in 1579?
n8148f54c31d.x: Akbar granted the Portuguese permission to establish themselves at Hugli in 1579.
n8148f54c31d.tq: Identify the settlement from the Mughal grantor and year.
xs: **Hugli** was granted to the Portuguese by **Akbar** in **1579** — option **(4)**.
**Bassein (1534)** came from **Bahadur Shah**; **Daman (1559)** by treaty with the Shah.
xa: **Shah Jahan** captured Hugli in **1632**.
Portuguese raided the Bay of Bengal from **Hugli and Chittagong** with **Arakanese pirates**.
**Shaista Khan** later took **Sondip and Chittagong**.

nb70d7143f55.s: The constant conflict between the Portuguese and the Zamorin of Calicut was mainly caused by Portuguese:
o: Alliance with the Arakanese pirates against Calicut
nb70d7143f55.x: The Portuguese monopoly over trade and their heavy duties led to continuing conflict with the Zamorin of Calicut.
nb70d7143f55.tq: Identify the stated economic cause behind the political conflict.
xs: Portuguese **monopoly and heavy duties** caused constant conflict with the **Zamorin of Calicut** — option **(4)**.
The Zamorin had **welcomed** them at Calicut at first.
xa: The Zamorin's fleet joined Gujarat and the Mamluks against **Almeida** at **Diu (1509)**.
The Portuguese shifted to **Cochin and Cannanore (1503)**.
The **Cartaz** enforced the monopoly — ships without it were **confiscated or sunk**.

nacfaa7f5f7a.s: The remains of St. Francis Xavier, who reached Goa in 1542, are preserved in the:
nacfaa7f5f7a.x: Xavier's remains are at the Basilica of Bom Jesus, Goa.
xa: Other missionaries: **Father Rudolf** and **Father Monserrate**.
**Goa Inquisition (16th c.):** state machinery used for conversions.
Forts: **Aguada**, Bassein, **Diu Fort (1535-41)**.

nde1f3aedd17.s: The Portuguese set up the first printing press in India at Goa in the year:
nde1f3aedd17.x: The printing press came to Goa in 1556. 1510 is the capture of Goa, 1542 the arrival of St. Francis Xavier, and 1661 the Bombay dowry.
xs: The Portuguese set up the printing press at Goa in **1556** — option **(3)**.
**1510** is the capture of **Goa**; **1542** the arrival of **St. Francis Xavier**.
xa: The Bible was printed in **Kannada and Malayalam**.
Xavier's remains: **Basilica of Bom Jesus**, Goa.
Crops: **tobacco**, **chilli**, groundnut, sapota, pineapple.

nc84b61a306e.s: Which one of the following was NOT a major factor in the decline of Portuguese power in India?
o: A sustained increase in support from the Dutch and English
The merger of Portugal with Spain in 1580
nc84b61a306e.x: Dutch and English competition contributed to Portuguese decline rather than supporting Portugal. Weak successors, official corruption and the 1580 merger with Spain were among the causes of decline.
nc84b61a306e.tq: Find the option that reverses the direction of a stated historical cause.
xs: **Support from the Dutch and English** is NOT a factor — they were **competitors** — option **(1)**.
Real causes: **weak successors** after Albuquerque, **corrupt, poorly paid officials**, Portugal's **merger with Spain (1580)**.
xa: Discovery of **Brazil** diverted attention.
**Forced conversion and inter-marriage** alienated Indians.
Losses to the Dutch: **Pulicat (1610)**, **Cochin (1663)**.

n7e9cffa1f52.s: Which Mughal emperor captured Hugli from the Portuguese in 1632?
n7e9cffa1f52.x: Shah Jahan took Hugli in 1632; Akbar had granted it to the Portuguese in 1579.
xa: Portuguese raided the **Bay of Bengal** from Hugli and Chittagong with Arakanese pirates.
Portugal merged with **Spain** in **1580**.
The Portuguese lost **Cochin** to the Dutch in **1663**.

ne0abcd288e1.s: Which of the following territories was lost by the Portuguese to the Dutch in 1663?
ne0abcd288e1.x: The Portuguese lost Cochin to the Dutch in 1663. Their other losses to the Dutch were Pulicat (1610) and Nagapattinam (1658); Daman, Diu and Hugli were not lost to the Dutch (Hugli fell to Shah Jahan in 1632).
ne0abcd288e1.tq: Distinguish the territory associated with the specific year.
xs: The Portuguese lost **Cochin** to the **Dutch** in **1663** — option **(1)**.
Other losses to the Dutch: **Pulicat (1610)** and **Nagapattinam**.
**Hugli** fell to **Shah Jahan (1632)**, not the Dutch.
xa: Losses to the English: **Swally (1612)**, off **Jask (1620)**, **Ormuz (1622)**.
Cochin had been a Portuguese base since **1503**.
Daman (**1559**) and Diu (**1546**) stayed Portuguese till **1961**.

n604373147c2.x: Goa became a state in May 1987; Portuguese rule had ended earlier with Operation Vijay on 19 December 1961.
xa: Goa was taken in **1510** — the first European territory since **Alexander**.
Goa was the main **Portuguese HQ**.
**St. Francis Xavier's** remains lie in the **Basilica of Bom Jesus**, Goa.

n4c456371c63.s: The term 'Cartaz' in the context of Portuguese rule in India refers to:
o: A naval trade licence or pass
n4c456371c63.x: A Cartaz was a Portuguese naval trade licence or pass required for ships sailing in the Indian Ocean.
n4c456371c63.tq: Discriminate the exact administrative meaning of a Portuguese term.
xs: The **Cartaz** was a **naval trade licence (pass)** — option **(2)**; asked in **APPSC-GS 2018**.
Every ship sailing the **Indian Ocean** had to buy one.
xa: It was backed by the **Caes** (convoy system) and **customs duties**.
Ships without it were **confiscated or sunk**.
It was used in the **Bay of Bengal** too.

n8625d5f5636.s: In the Telugu country the Portuguese were popularly called:
n8625d5f5636.x: Locals called the Portuguese Budata Keechu. Bangaru Farmana is the Golden Farman given to the English, Kalamkari is a painted textile, and Petapoli is another name for Nizampatnam.
xs: In the Telugu country the Portuguese were called **Budata Keechu** — option **(1)**.
**Bangaru Farmana** is the **Golden Farman** given to the English; **Kalamkari** is an Andhra textile.
xa: **Tomato, chilli, groundnut** came to Telugu country via the Portuguese.
Portuguese Andhra posts: **Masulipatnam, Pulicat, San Thome**.
Influence waned by mid-**17th c.**

n00d3eef6999.s: The Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie (VOC) was formed on:
n00d3eef6999.x: The VOC was formed on 20 March 1602 by merging Dutch companies. The year 1592 is a commonly noted misprint.
n00d3eef6999.tq: Reject the near-date trap by retaining the exact formation date.
xs: The VOC was formed on **20 March 1602** by **merging Dutch companies** — option **(2)**.
⚠ "**1592**" in some notes is a **misprint**; **1610** is Pulicat and **1605** is Machilipatnam.
xa: Full name: **Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie**.
Charter from the **Dutch States-General** — sovereign powers.
Asian HQ: **Batavia** (Jakarta).

n5cd2b92976d.s: The VOC received sovereign powers to wage war, build forts and sign treaties from:
n5cd2b92976d.x: The Dutch States-General granted the VOC powers to wage war, build forts and sign treaties.
xa: VOC formed **20 March 1602**.
Focus: **Spice Islands**, not India.
Dutch were the first to get the right to **mint coins** in Andhra.

n1451c2aa031.x: Bussy immediately installed Salabat Jang, the fourth son of Nizam-ul-Mulk, after Muzaffar Jang was killed.
n1451c2aa031.tq: Distinguish the replacement ruler from the earlier rival claimants.
xs: **Bussy** at once installed **Salabat Jang** after Muzaffar Jang's death — option **(4)**.
**Salabat Jang** was **Nizam-ul-Mulk's 4th son**.
**Nasir Jang** was already murdered; **Chanda Sahib** and **Muhammad Ali** were Carnatic (Arcot) claimants, not Hyderabad.
xa: **Muzaffar Jang** was killed at **Rayachoti (1751)** by the Nawabs of **Kadapa, Kurnool, Nayanur**.
**Bussy** was French; **Dupleix** was the architect of the **policy of interference**.
Comparative note: Dupleix **won the Deccan (Hyderabad)** but lost the Carnatic.

na9ae0db66d0.s: Which Maratha chief joined the English during Clive's Carnatic campaign?
na9ae0db66d0.x: Mysore, Tanjore and the Maratha chief Morari Rao joined the English.
xa: **Clive and Stringer Lawrence** relieved **Trichinopoly**.
French commander **Law** surrendered at Trichinopoly; **Muhammad Ali** became **Nawab of Carnatic**.
**Raja Sahib** (Chanda Sahib's son) fought on the **French side**.

n8a98152afd6.s: Who jointly relieved Trichinopoly, leading to the surrender of the French commander Law?
n8a98152afd6.x: Robert Clive and Stringer Lawrence relieved Trichinopoly. The French commander Law surrendered during this operation.
n8a98152afd6.tq: Match the two English commanders with the relief operation and avoid swapping them with French leaders.
xs: **Robert Clive and Stringer Lawrence** relieved Trichinopoly — option **(4)**.
The French commander **Law** surrendered; **Chanda Sahib** surrendered and was **executed** (**June 1752**).
**Bussy and Dupleix** were French leaders; **Chanda Sahib and Raja Sahib** were on the French side.
xa: **Muhammad Ali** then became **Nawab of Carnatic**.
The defeat at **Trichinopoly** was a reason for **Dupleix's recall (1754)**.
Allies of the English: **Morari Rao**, **Mysore**, **Tanjore**.

n464c496719d.s: Who succeeded Dupleix as the French Governor in India and made peace with the English?
n464c496719d.x: Godeheu succeeded Dupleix in 1754 and made peace with the English.
n464c496719d.tq: Use the successor–policy association to distinguish Godeheu from military commanders.
xs: **Godeheu** succeeded Dupleix and **made peace with the English** — option **(4)**.
**Law** was the French commander who **surrendered at Trichinopoly**; **Bussy** installed **Salabat Jang**.
**Salabat Jang** was Nizam-ul-Mulk's **4th son**, not a French governor.
xa: Dupleix was **recalled in 1754**.
Reasons: **heavy cost** + failures of the **interference policy**; defeat at **Trichinopoly**.

na17da42caa7.s: Robert Clive proposed the attack on Arcot during the siege of Trichinopoly mainly to:
o: create a diversion and relieve Muhammad Ali
na17da42caa7.x: Chanda Sahib and the French were besieging Muhammad Ali at Trichinopoly; Clive attacked Arcot, the Carnatic capital, as a diversion.
xa: Clive took Arcot with **210 men** (UPSC); some notes say **200 English + 300 sepoys**.
He held it against **Raja Sahib** for **53 days** (some notes say 50).
Clive then beat Raja Sahib at **Arni** and **Kaveripak**.

n8a937973435.s: Which place did Muzaffar Jang grant to Dupleix as a jagir?
