n8a937973435.x: Muzaffar Jang made Dupleix Governor of Mughal territory south of the Krishna and gave him Valapadu as a jagir.
xa: Territories near **Pondicherry**: **Villianur, Bahur, Valapadu**.
On the **Andhra coast**: **Diviseema and Machilipatnam**.
Dupleix was **recalled in 1754**; successor **Godeheu**.

n8c6941d7cf6.s: Why did the French Company recall Dupleix in 1754?
o: His surrender of Madras to the English
The heavy cost and failures of his policy of intervention
His grant of the Northern Circars to the English
n8c6941d7cf6.x: The Company was alarmed by the heavy expense and failures of Dupleix's interventionist policy, especially the defeat at Trichinopoly.
xa: His successor **Godeheu** **made peace with the English**.
Rewards to the French: jagir of **Valapadu**; **Diviseema and Machilipatnam** on the Andhra coast.
Comparative note: Dupleix **won the Deccan** but **lost the Carnatic**.

n0d0774c1b25.s: Which one of the following correctly compares Dupleix's fortunes in the Deccan and the Carnatic?
o: He won the Deccan but lost the Carnatic
He lost both the Deccan and the Carnatic
He lost the Deccan but won the Carnatic
He won both the Deccan and the Carnatic
n0d0774c1b25.x: Dupleix succeeded in the Deccan, particularly through influence at Hyderabad, but lost the Carnatic struggle at Arcot and Trichinopoly.
n0d0774c1b25.tq: Use the paired regional comparison to avoid reversing the Deccan and Carnatic outcomes.
xs: Dupleix **won the Deccan** (Hyderabad) but **lost the Carnatic** (Arcot, Trichinopoly) — option **(1)**.
In the Deccan, **Bussy** installed **Salabat Jang** after Muzaffar Jang's death.
In the Carnatic, Clive's **Arcot** siege and the relief of **Trichinopoly** made **Muhammad Ali** Nawab.
xa: The defeat at **Trichinopoly** led to **Dupleix's recall (1754)**.
Successor **Godeheu** made peace with the English.

n974c569ae74.s: The Battle of Wandiwash is regarded as a turning point in Indian history mainly because it:
o: brought the Seven Years' War to an end in Europe
established French control over the Northern Circars
removed the last major European rival to British political power in India
ended the Mughal Empire in India
n974c569ae74.x: The English victory at Wandiwash, along with Plassey, removed the last serious European rival to British political supremacy in India.
n974c569ae74.tq: Move from the battle result to its wider political consequence.
xs: Wandiwash, with **Plassey**, **removed the last European rival** to British power in India — option **(3)**.
It **ended French political power in India** (BPSC 2020, UPPSC 2015).
The **Seven Years' War** ended with the **Treaty of Paris (1763)**, not Wandiwash.
The **Northern Circars** went to the **English**, not the French, after **Chandurti**.
xa: Wandiwash: **22 January 1760**, **Eyre Coote** vs **Count de Lally**; **Bussy taken prisoner**.
After 1763 the French stayed **as traders only**.

n8d427ecae29.s: Which of the following was NOT retained by the French as an enclave under the Treaty of Paris, 1763?
n8d427ecae29.x: Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam and Chandernagore were retained as French enclaves. Machilipatnam was transferred to the English through the Hyderabad agreement.
n8d427ecae29.tq: Eliminate the recognised French enclaves and identify the Andhra territory transferred to the English.
xs: **Machilipatnam** was not a French enclave — option **(2)**.
It went to the English in **April 1759**, when **Salabat Jang** changed sides (first **British-Hyderabad agreement**).
Retained French enclaves: **Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam** + **Chandernagore**.
xa: Enclaves were restored only as **trading posts** that **could not be fortified**.
AP angle: **Yanam** stayed French though the English held the **Northern Circars**.

n92d476cd407.s: The Third Carnatic War was concluded by the Treaty of ___ in 1763.
n92d476cd407.x: The Treaty of Paris (1763) ended the Seven Years' War and the Third Carnatic War. Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) ended the First war, Pondicherry (1754) the Second, and Allahabad (1765) followed Buxar.
xs: The Third Carnatic War ended with the **Treaty of Paris** (**1763**) — option **(3)**.
It also ended the **Seven Years' War (1756-63)** (**APPSC 2025**).
xa: Terms: French settlements **restored** as trading posts that **could not be fortified**.
Retained: **Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam** + **Chandernagore**.
Significance: settled the **Anglo-French contest**; French stayed **as traders only**.

n680046922ae.s: The Battle of Chandurti (Condore) near Rajahmundry was fought in:
n680046922ae.x: Chandurti was fought on 7 December 1758; the English took Machilipatnam in April 1759.
xa: At Chandurti, the **English + Vizianagaram army** defeated the French under **Conflans**.
**Tumnapalem (1756)**: Bussy aided by Vizianagaram ruler **Vijayaramaraju**.
Malleson on Chandurti: "**small battle, great results**".

n2f9924911e6.s: Which French commander was taken prisoner at Wandiwash?
n2f9924911e6.x: Eyre Coote routed Lally at Wandiwash, where Bussy was taken prisoner.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **Lally** was captured at **Pondicherry (1761)**, not at Wandiwash.
Lally held Pondicherry **eight months** before surrendering on **16 January 1761**; **Jinji + Mahe** also fell.

n891faa8d48b.s: Count de Lally surrendered at Pondicherry in:
n891faa8d48b.x: Lally surrendered at Pondicherry on 16 January 1761, while Bussy was taken prisoner at Wandiwash.
xa: Earlier, Bussy had been aided by **Vijayaramaraju** at **Tumnapalem (1756)**.
Lally had taken **Fort St. David** (Cuddalore) in **1758**.

n6497ad9cd45.s: The immediate significance of the English victory at Chandurti was that it:
o: ended the rule of Salabat Jang in Hyderabad
drove the French out of the Northern Circars
gave the French control over Bengal
n6497ad9cd45.x: The victory at Chandurti drove the French out of the Northern Circars and was later described as a small battle with great results.
n6497ad9cd45.tq: Identify the regional consequence rather than the later treaty settlement.
xs: Chandurti **drove the French out of the Northern Circars** — option **(3)**.
**Salabat Jang** was not removed; after Machilipatnam fell (**April 1759**) he **changed sides** to the English.
**Pondicherry** fell to the English in **1761**; France never controlled Bengal.
xa: Chandurti: **7 December 1758**, near **Rajahmundry**; English + Vizianagaram army beat **Conflans**.
Malleson: "**small battle, great results**".
AP angle: Chandurti and Machilipatnam gave the English their **first foothold in the Northern Circars**.

n94e596a6f6a.s: The English victories at Chandurti and Machilipatnam gave them their first foothold in:
n94e596a6f6a.x: Chandurti and Machilipatnam gave the English their first foothold in the Northern Circars, while Yanam remained French.
xa: Chandurti: **7 December 1758**, near **Rajahmundry**.
Salabat Jang's grant: **Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam, Vakal Mannar, part of Kondapalli**.

n50ca67b2017.s: Chandurti is to the foundation of British rule in Andhra as which of the following is to the foundation of British rule in India?
n50ca67b2017.x: Chandurti is described as the foundation of British rule in Andhra, in a parallel often drawn with Plassey as the foundation of British rule in India.
n50ca67b2017.tq: Recognise the historical analogy rather than a military sequence.
xs: **Chandurti (1758)** is the foundation of British rule in Andhra, as **Plassey (1757)** is for India — option **(2)**.
**Wandiwash** removed the last European rival; **Bobbili** was the **24 Jan 1757** battle.
xa: Malleson: Chandurti was a "**small battle, great results**".
Chandurti was won by **Colonel Forde** with **Ananda Gajapati**'s Vizianagaram army.

n00bee968e61.s: The Third Carnatic War in India formed the Indian theatre of which wider conflict?
n00bee968e61.x: The Third Carnatic War was the Indian theatre of the Seven Years' War, fought from 1756 to 1763.
n00bee968e61.tq: Connect the regional conflict with its wider international war and dates.
xs: The Third Carnatic War was the Indian theatre of the **Seven Years' War (1756-63)** — option **(1)**.
The **Treaty of Paris (1763)** ended both the **Seven Years' War** and the Third Carnatic War.
xa: By **1758** Clive had won **Plassey (1757)** and taken French **Chandernagore**; Bengal revenue paid for the Carnatic campaign.
Decisive battle: **Wandiwash**, **22 January 1760** — **Eyre Coote** routed **Count de Lally**.
"Third Carnatic War concluded by the Treaty of ___ in 1763" — **Paris** (**APPSC 2025**).

n2a4e07e663d.s: Which development enabled the English to finance the Carnatic campaign from Bengal?
o: Clive's victory at Plassey and the resulting availability of Bengal revenue
The French conquest of Chandernagore after Plassey
The surrender of Madras to Salabat Jang
The transfer of Pondicherry revenue to Calcutta
n2a4e07e663d.x: After Clive's victory at Plassey in 1757 and the capture of French Chandernagore, Bengal revenue helped finance the English Carnatic campaign.
n2a4e07e663d.tq: Trace the resource link between an earlier victory and a later campaign.
xs: **Clive's victory at Plassey (1757)** made **Bengal revenue** available to pay for the Carnatic campaign — option **(1)**.
Chandernagore was a **French** settlement **taken by Clive**, not a French conquest — option (2) inverts it.
**Pondicherry** was the only French base; its revenue was never transferred to Calcutta.
xa: English advantage: **Bengal's wealth and men after Plassey**; the French suffered a **chronic shortage of funds** and **unpaid troops**.
**UPPSC 2016**: both "Bengal wealth and manpower" and "**naval superiority**" are correct reasons for English success.
Clive sent **Colonel Forde** from Bengal, who won **Chandurti**.

n3573f71494e.s: The Treaty of Paris of 1763 provided that the French factories and settlements in India would be:
o: Placed under the joint control of France and Hyderabad
Restored to France but retained only as trading posts without fortifications
Transferred permanently to the English East India Company
n3573f71494e.x: The French settlements were restored, but they could function only as trading posts and could not be fortified.
n3573f71494e.tq: Test the legally significant qualification attached to territorial restoration.
xs: Under the **Treaty of Paris (1763)**, French settlements were **restored** only as **trading posts** that **could not be fortified** — option **(2)**.
They were **demilitarised**, not transferred to the English or made into states.
xa: Retained enclaves: **Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam** + **Chandernagore**.
⚠ Some notes list only "**Pondicherry, Yanam, Mahe**" – incomplete.
The treaty ended the **Seven Years' War** + Third Carnatic War (**APPSC 2025**).

nd0fb46bcead.s: Which feature distinguished the English East India Company from the French company?
o: It was a private company with a yearly elected board
nd0fb46bcead.x: The English company was privately organised with a yearly elected board and quicker decisions; the French company was state-controlled.
xa: English **naval superiority**; the French fleet (**d'Ache**) was beaten.
English leadership: **Clive, Lawrence, Coote**; French: Lally quarrelled, **Dupleix recalled**.

n25778915fb0.s: During the Carnatic struggle, the only French base in India was:
n25778915fb0.x: Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were English bases, while the French had only Pondicherry.
xa: French company: **state-controlled**, dependent on **royal subsidy**; **chronic shortage of funds**.
**Lally** was left **without sea support**.

n557c1337f31.s: Which French commander quarrelled with his officers and failed to understand Indian conditions?
n557c1337f31.x: Lally's quarrels with his officers and poor grasp of Indian conditions weakened the French effort.
xa: The French also lost **Dupleix**, who had been **recalled**.
Lally lost **Wandiwash (1760)** and **surrendered Pondicherry (1761)**.
French company: **bureaucratic**, **state-controlled**.

n58862f2414a.s: The First Carnatic War was primarily
o: an extension of the Seven Years’ War
an extension of the War of Austrian Succession in Europe
a conflict caused by the Anglo-Burmese War
a local conflict arising from the death of Nizam-ul-Mulk
n58862f2414a.x: The First Carnatic War was an extension of the War of Austrian Succession in Europe, bringing the British and French into conflict in India.
n58862f2414a.tq: Separate the European background of each Carnatic War.
xs: The First war was an extension of the **War of Austrian Succession** — option **(2)**.
The **Seven Years' War** lay behind the **Third** war; **Nizam-ul-Mulk's death (1748)** triggered the **Second**.
xa: It ended with the **Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle** (**18 Sep 1748**): **Madras restored** for **Louisburg**.
**La Bourdonnais**'s fleet took **Madras (1746)**; **Captain Paradis** won at **St. Thome/Adyar**.

n7d2e19fc8fe.s: In the Hyderabad succession dispute of the Second Carnatic War, the English backed:
n7d2e19fc8fe.x: The English backed Nasir Jang, son of Nizam-ul-Mulk, and the French backed his grandson Muzaffar Jang.
xa: **Muhammad Ali** (Anwaruddin's son) = English candidate after **1749**.
**Bussy** kept **Salabat Jang** in power at Hyderabad.

na72c87bd1ad.s: The First Carnatic War ended with the Treaty of:
na72c87bd1ad.x: The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) ended the First war and returned Madras to the English.
xa: APPSC-G2 **2025** asked this war–treaty pairs question.
Third war → **Treaty of Paris (1763)**.

nb3942d89f29.s: The Carnatic Wars made the ____ the kingmakers of South India.
nb3942d89f29.x: The wars showed the power of disciplined European infantry and made the English the kingmakers of South India.
xa: Example: at **St. Thome (1746)** about **930** French beat about **10,000**.
AP angle: the war in Andhra decided who held the **Northern Circars**.

n9dffdac6477.s: The Treaty of Pondicherry, under which each company kept its existing possessions, was signed in:
n9dffdac6477.x: The Treaty of Pondicherry (1754) bound both companies not to interfere in princes' quarrels and was inconclusive.
xa: **Godeheu**, Dupleix's successor, made this peace.
Failure: the **Seven Years' War** broke out before England + France **ratified** it.
⚠ The Second war was **not** ended by the **Treaty of Yandabo** (First Anglo-Burmese War, **1826**).

nfc23592a22a.s: Which development occurred before England and France ratified the Treaty of Pondicherry?
o: The Seven Years' War broke out, leading to the Third Carnatic War
Dupleix was appointed Governor of Mughal territory
nfc23592a22a.x: The Seven Years' War broke out before the treaty was ratified by England and France, thereby beginning the Third Carnatic War.
nfc23592a22a.tq: Place the outbreak of the Seven Years' War between the treaty and its ratification.
xs: The **Seven Years' War** broke out before ratification, starting the **Third Carnatic War** — option **(2)**.
So the Third war began **before the Treaty of Pondicherry could be ratified**.
**Forde** took Machilipatnam only in **1759**, years later.
xa: Third war: **1756-63** (UPSC gives **1758-63**), ended by the **Treaty of Paris (1763)**.
Treaty of Pondicherry terms: **non-interference** in Indian princes' quarrels; existing possessions kept.

ne8bac269c66.s: During the First Carnatic War, Nawab Anwaruddin of the Carnatic came in on the side of the
ne8bac269c66.x: Anwaruddin supported the English during the First Carnatic War, which was fought between the British and the French.
ne8bac269c66.tq: Test the participant-side relationship in a two-sided conflict.
xs: Nawab **Anwaruddin** came in on the side of the **English** — option **(2)**.
The First war was fought **between the British and the French** (APPSC 2018).
xa: His army, under **Mahfuz Khan**, was beaten by **Captain Paradis** at **St. Thome/Adyar (1746)**.
About **930** French beat about **10,000** of the Nawab's men.
Anwaruddin was later killed at **Ambur (1749)**.

n5ee3d955a13.s: Who captured Madras, including Fort St. George, in 1746?
n5ee3d955a13.x: La Bourdonnais, the French governor of Mauritius, captured Madras or Fort St. George in 1746.
n5ee3d955a13.tq: Match the military action with the correct French commander and office.
xs: **La Bourdonnais**, Governor of **Mauritius**, took **Madras (1746)** with his fleet — option **(2)**.
**Captain Paradis** beat **Anwaruddin**'s army under **Mahfuz Khan** at **St. Thome/Adyar** — not Madras's capture.
xa: La Bourdonnais agreed to **ransom Madras** back; **Dupleix overruled** him and kept it.
Madras was **restored to the English** by **Aix-la-Chapelle (1748)**.

n6b177d07fe6.s: What was the central issue in the dispute between La Bourdonnais and Dupleix after the capture of Madras?
o: La Bourdonnais agreed to ransom Madras to the English, but Dupleix overruled him and retained it
La Bourdonnais wanted to retain Pondicherry, whereas Dupleix wanted to surrender it
Dupleix wanted to ransom Madras, but La Bourdonnais transferred it to the Nawab
Both commanders agreed to return Madras, but Anwaruddin refused to accept it
n6b177d07fe6.x: La Bourdonnais agreed to return Madras to the English in return for a ransom, but Dupleix overruled him and kept the city.
n6b177d07fe6.tq: Identify the opposing decisions of the two French commanders.
xs: **La Bourdonnais** agreed to **ransom Madras** back to the English; **Dupleix overruled him and kept it** — option **(1)**.
La Bourdonnais was **Governor of Mauritius**; his fleet took **Madras (1746)**.
xa: **Dupleix** was **Governor of Pondicherry from 1742**.
Madras went back to the English under **Aix-la-Chapelle** in exchange for **Louisburg**.

n3796a143011.s: Who among the following led the English forces in the Battle of Condore or Chandurti and subsequently captured Machilipatnam?
n3796a143011.x: Colonel Francis Forde led the English forces at Chandurti in 1758 and captured Machilipatnam in 1759.
n3796a143011.tq: Link a commander with two consecutive operations rather than with the better-known Wandiwash.
xs: **Colonel (Francis) Forde** won **Chendurthi (1758)** and took **Machilipatnam (1759)** — option **(3)**.
**Eyre Coote** won **Wandiwash**; **Pocock** was the English **admiral**; **Lawrence** relieved Tiruchirappalli in the Second war.
xa: At Chendurthi (**7 Dec 1758**), Forde and the **Vizianagaram army** beat **Conflans**.
Chendurthi = "**Plassey of Andhra**" (Malleson).

n59ae2655bf8.s: Who was the English admiral in the Third Carnatic War?
n59ae2655bf8.x: Pocock was the English admiral and d'Ache the French admiral; the English fleet defeated d'Ache.
xa: The English navy also beat **d'Aché's** fleet off **Pondicherry (1759)**.
**Naval superiority** was a main reason for English success.

n6297a302437.s: Who was the Governor of Pondicherry from 1742 and the principal French architect of interference in Indian politics?
n6297a302437.x: Dupleix became Governor of Pondicherry in 1742 and developed the policy of intervention in Indian succession disputes.
n6297a302437.tq: Match the office and policy with the correct French official.
xs: **Dupleix** — **Governor of Pondicherry from 1742**, architect of **interference in Indian politics** — option **(3)**.
**Godeheu** was his **successor**; **La Bourdonnais** governed **Mauritius**; **Lally** commanded in the **Third** war.
xa: Dupleix captured **Madras (1746)** and overruled La Bourdonnais's ransom.
He fought in the **1st and 2nd** wars and was **recalled** after the Second.

na8a1005be29.s: Which of the following events is associated with Count de Lally?
o: Defeat of Anwaruddin at St. Thome
Capture of Fort St. David in 1758 and surrender of Pondicherry in 1761
na8a1005be29.x: Count de Lally, the French commander and Governor in the Third Carnatic War, captured Fort St. David in 1758 and surrendered Pondicherry on 16 January 1761.
na8a1005be29.tq: Link a commander with two events from the same war and reject swapped deeds.
xs: **Count de Lally** took **Fort St. David (1758)** and **surrendered Pondicherry** (**16 Jan 1761**) — option **(4)**.
**Machilipatnam (1759)** was taken by **Forde**; **St. Thome** was won by **Paradis**; **Madras (1746)** by **La Bourdonnais**.
xa: Count de Lally = **Third** Carnatic War (**APPSC-GS 2019**); defeated at Wandiwash (**UKPSC 2016**).
Lally **quarrelled with officials**; his **troops went unpaid**.

n7c1faa3a46c.s: The battles of Arni and Kaveripak were victories of Clive over
n7c1faa3a46c.x: During the Second Carnatic War, Clive defeated Raja Sahib and Chanda Sahib at Arni and Kaveripak in 1751–52.
n7c1faa3a46c.tq: Identify the opposing commanders associated with a pair of battles.
xs: At **Arni and Kaveripak** (**1751-52**) Clive beat **Raja Sahib and Chanda Sahib** — option **(4)**.
**Conflans** was beaten at **Chendurthi**; **Lally** at **Wandiwash**.
xa: This followed Clive's **siege of Arcot (1751)**.
**Stringer Lawrence** and Clive then forced **Law** to surrender at **Tiruchirappalli**.

n986411df7d8.s: Chendurthi is known as the ‘Plassey of Andhra’ because it
o: drove the French out of the Northern Circars
established French control over all the Northern Circars
n986411df7d8.x: Chendurthi, fought in 1758, has been called the ‘Plassey of Andhra’ because it drove the French out of the Northern Circars.
n986411df7d8.tq: Connect a famous comparative title with the specific political consequence of the battle.
xs: Chendurthi **drove the French out of the Northern Circars** — hence "**Plassey of Andhra**" (Malleson) — option **(2)**.
**Pondicherry** surrendered in **1761** after Wandiwash, not after Chendurthi.
xa: **Forde** and the **Vizianagaram army** beat **Conflans** on **7 Dec 1758**.
Forde then took **Machilipatnam (1759)**.

ne52e423d7da.s: The Battle of Wandiwash was fought on 22 January:
ne52e423d7da.x: Wandiwash was fought on 22 January 1760; Chendurthi on 7 December 1758, Ambur in 1749 and Arcot in 1751.
xa: Ambur and Arcot belong to the **Second** war; Chendurthi and Wandiwash to the **Third**.
**St. Thome / Adyar (1746)** was the **First** war's battle.

n79b7de5ac6d.s: At the Battle of St. Thome (Adyar), 1746, about 930 French troops defeated roughly 10,000 men of:
n79b7de5ac6d.x: At St. Thome/Adyar (1746) about 930 French troops beat about 10,000 of the Nawab's men.
xa: The French were led by **Captain Paradis**; the Nawab's army by **Mahfuz Khan**.
Lesson: **disciplined European infantry** beat **much larger Indian armies**.

n764b7e96fb9.s: The English naval advantage in the Carnatic struggles was demonstrated by the defeat of
n764b7e96fb9.x: The English navy defeated d’Aché’s fleet off Pondicherry (1759), after which he withdrew to Mauritius.
n764b7e96fb9.tq: Distinguish naval action from land battles by identifying the fleet commander.
xs: The English navy beat **d'Aché's fleet off Pondicherry (1759)** — option **(2)**.
d'Aché then **withdrew to Mauritius**.
**Chendurthi**, **Wandiwash** and **St. Thome** were **land** battles.
xa: **Pocock** was the English admiral; he beat d'Ache in the **Bay of Bengal**.
Other reasons: **Bengal's resources after Plassey (1757)** and **better commanders** (Clive, Lawrence, Coote).

nb0e9243bcce.s: Who was the last Subahdar (Governor) of Bengal appointed by the Mughal Emperor?
nb0e9243bcce.x: Murshid Quli Khan, Nawab from 1717 and founder of the autonomous Bengal Nawabi, was the last Subahdar of Bengal appointed by the Mughal Emperor. Shuja-ud-din, Alivardi Khan (who seized the throne by killing Sarfaraz) and Siraj-ud-Daula came later.
xs: **Murshid Quli Khan** was the **last Subahdar/Governor of Bengal appointed by the Mughal Emperor** — option **(3)**.
Asked in **UPPSC 2013 and 2021**.
**Alivardi Khan** seized the throne by **killing Sarfaraz**; **Shuja-ud-din** and **Siraj-ud-Daula** came later.
xa: Murshid Quli became **Nawab of Bengal in 1717** and founded the **autonomous Bengal Nawabi**.
By **1735** Shuja-ud-din was "**too absolute to regard any orders from court**".

n6d5ff60bf15.s: Who ruled Bengal immediately before Siraj-ud-Daula?
n6d5ff60bf15.x: The order was Shuja-ud-din, Sarfaraz Khan, Alivardi Khan and Siraj-ud-Daula.
xa: All followed **Murshid Quli Khan (1717-27)**.
**Alivardi** seized the throne by **killing Sarfaraz**.
**Siraj-ud-Daula** was Alivardi's **grandson** and lost **Plassey**.

na4aefc048cd.s: Which Nawab of Bengal was the son-in-law of Murshid Quli Khan?
na4aefc048cd.x: Shuja-ud-din was the son-in-law of Murshid Quli Khan. Sarfaraz Khan was Shuja-ud-din’s son and Murshid Quli Khan’s grandson.
na4aefc048cd.tq: Use family relationships to distinguish the two successive Nawabs connected with Murshid Quli Khan.
xs: **Shuja-ud-din** was the **son-in-law of Murshid Quli Khan** — option **(4)**.
**Sarfaraz Khan** was **Shuja-ud-din's son** (Murshid Quli's **grandson**).
**Siraj-ud-Daula** was the **grandson of Alivardi Khan**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes call **Sarfaraz** the "son of Murshid Quli Khan" — wrong.
Shuja-ud-din ruled **1727-39**.

n1b6485c1984.x: Alivardi Khan, earlier Deputy Governor of Bihar, was succeeded by his grandson Siraj-ud-Daula.
xa: Alivardi seized the throne by **killing Sarfaraz** (**1740**).

nf4dd48e0d72.s: Murshid Quli Khan is associated with which one of the following administrative changes in Bengal?
o: Shifting the capital from Dacca to Murshidabad
Shifting the capital from Murshidabad to Dacca
Shifting the capital from Calcutta to Dacca
Shifting the capital from Patna to Murshidabad
nf4dd48e0d72.x: Murshid Quli Khan shifted the capital of Bengal from Dacca to Murshidabad.
nf4dd48e0d72.tq: Test the location change directly by distinguishing the old capital from the new one.
xs: **Murshid Quli Khan** shifted the capital from **Dacca to Murshidabad** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) reverses the direction of the shift.
xa: He rose from **Diwan** → **Subahdar** → **Nawab of Bengal in 1717**, founding the **autonomous Bengal Nawabi**.
He was the **last Subahdar of Bengal appointed by the Mughal Emperor** (UPPSC 2013, 2021).
Revenue: **ijaradari** (revenue farming) and conversion of jagir land into **khalisa**.

n91e15959c7e.s: The term ‘ijaradari’ in the revenue administration of Bengal refers to
o: Collection of land revenue through contractors
Collection of customs duties only from European companies
Direct collection of revenue by village headmen
Assignment of jagirs exclusively to Mughal princes
n91e15959c7e.x: Ijaradari was revenue farming: contractors called ijaradars collected the land revenue (APPSC 2018), the contract-based collection also called mal jasmani under Murshid Quli Khan.
n91e15959c7e.tq: Discriminate between a revenue-collection method and unrelated forms of land assignment or customs collection.
xs: **Ijaradari** (revenue farming) meant **contractors (ijaradars) collected land revenue** — option **(1)**.
This was asked in **APPSC 2018**.
xa: The contract-based revenue collection was called **mal jasmani**.
Murshid Quli converted **jagir land** into **khalisa** (crown land).
⚠ Don't confuse with **dastaks** — trade passes misused by Company servants for private trade.

n6d37803813d.s: What was the principal significance of converting jagir land into khalisa under Murshid Quli Khan?
o: It transferred the land permanently to the English Company
It converted the land into private property of the zamindars
It exempted the land from all forms of revenue
It placed the land under direct state revenue administration
n6d37803813d.x: Conversion of jagir land into khalisa brought the land under direct state control for revenue purposes.
n6d37803813d.tq: Apply the distinction between assigned jagir land and directly administered khalisa land.
xs: Converting jagir land into **khalisa** made it **crown land** under direct state revenue — option **(4)**.
It did not go to the English or to zamindars, nor was it exempt from revenue.
xa: Revenue on such land was collected by **ijaradars** (revenue farming, APPSC 2018).
The contract-based collection = **mal jasmani**.

n0c7e213ae2c.s: The English misuse of dastaks primarily resulted in
o: Transfer of Calcutta to the French
Recognition of Mir Jafar as Subahdar
Loss of revenue to the Nawab
n0c7e213ae2c.x: The 1717 farman allowed duty-free Company trade, but Company servants misused dastaks for private trade, causing the Nawab to lose revenue.
n0c7e213ae2c.tq: Connect the misuse of a fiscal privilege with its direct administrative consequence.
xs: The misuse of **dastaks** caused a **loss of revenue to the Nawab** — option **(4)**.
**Company servants** used dastaks for **private trade**.
xa: The **Farman of 1717 (Farrukhsiyar)** gave **duty-free trade**.
Misuse of the farman was a cause of conflict with **Siraj-ud-Daula**.

n1b67f32ed43.s: Which of the following events of 1756–57 in Bengal came first?
o: Recapture of Calcutta by Clive and Watson
n1b67f32ed43.x: Kasimbazar was seized in May 1756, before Calcutta fell (June 1756), its recapture (January 1757) and Alinagar (February 1757).
xa: Black Hole: **20 June 1756**.
After Alinagar, Clive took French **Chandernagore**.

n813cdb59500.s: The Black Hole story of June 1756 rests mainly on the account of:
n813cdb59500.x: The story rests mainly on the account of J.Z. Holwell, a survivor; historians doubt the reported numbers.
xa: Reported: **146** prisoners, about **120** died; Holwell's own figure = **123**.
Governor **Drake** fled to **Fulta**.
**Clive** and **Admiral Watson** retook Calcutta in **January 1757**.

nb0e1263111c.s: After Plassey, Mir Jafar rewarded the Company with the zamindari of:
nb0e1263111c.x: The Company got the zamindari of the 24 Parganas, duty-free trade in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, and a large payment.
xa: Mir Jafar = **puppet Nawab installed after Plassey**.
Result: the Company turned from **traders to political power**.

ndc3ba17a031.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the significance of the Battle of Plassey?
o: It turned the Company from a trading body into a political power
It is seen as a victory of treachery and political-financial arrangement
Bengal's wealth helped finance the defeat of the French
It was a prolonged contest between equally matched armies
ndc3ba17a031.x: Plassey is viewed as a victory of treachery and a political-financial deal, not a prolonged contest between equal armies.
xa: **Buxar (1764)** was the **real military test**.
Plassey = **conspiracy** vs Buxar = **open military victory**.

n3b09eeedbb8.s: Which battle is commonly called the foundation of British rule in India?
n3b09eeedbb8.x: Plassey is commonly called the foundation of British rule, though some assessments treat Buxar as the more decisive battle.
xa: Plassey = a **victory of treachery**; Buxar = the **real military test**.
Both "**Plassey vs Buxar**" and the **Black Hole numbers** remain open debates.

n6166c8dc375.s: Clive's Plassey conspiracy involved Jagat Seth, Omichund and:
n6166c8dc375.x: Clive's deal involved Jagat Seth, Omichund and Mir Jafar.
xa: **Jagat Seth** = "**world banker**"; **Mir Jafar** = **puppet Nawab** after Plassey.
Mir Jafar paid **Rs 1,77,00,000** and gave the **24 Parganas** zamindari.

nbdfb7b4c6a6.s: The Treaty of Alinagar, concluded in February 1757, restored the Company’s
o: French trading rights and prohibited English fortification
1717 privileges and permitted the fortification of Calcutta
1740 privileges and transferred Murshidabad to the Company
1764 privileges and granted the Diwani of Bengal
nbdfb7b4c6a6.x: The Treaty of Alinagar restored the Company’s privileges under the 1717 arrangement and allowed it to fortify Calcutta.
nbdfb7b4c6a6.tq: Match the treaty with its specific privileges and avoid attributing the later Diwani settlement to it.
xs: Alinagar restored the Company's **1717 privileges** + the **right to fortify Calcutta** — option **(2)**.
The **1717** privilege was **duty-free trade** under **Farrukhsiyar's farman**.
xa: Concluded **February 1757**, after **Clive + Admiral Watson** retook Calcutta.
Clive then took French **Chandernagore**.

n504774ccd7a.s: The 1717 farman of Farrukhsiyar is popularly known as the:
n504774ccd7a.x: The 1717 farman granted important trading privileges to the Company and is popularly called the Magna Carta of the Company.
n504774ccd7a.tq: Recall the distinctive title associated with the 1717 farman.
xs: The **1717 farman** of **Farrukhsiyar** is called the **"Magna Carta" of the Company** — option **(3)**.
It gave **duty-free trade** in Bengal for **Rs 3,000** a year.
xa: **Diwani** = **revenue + civil justice** — a later grant (**1765**), not the farman.
**Dastak** misuse caused quarrels with **Siraj** and later **Mir Qasim**.

nec7260056be.s: A dastak under the Bengal trading system was a:
o: land grant issued to a zamindar
permit for fortifying a European settlement
military order issued by the Nawab
nec7260056be.x: A dastak was a free pass that enabled duty-free trade. Its misuse became a major source of conflict between the Company and the Nawabs.
nec7260056be.tq: Test the precise meaning of a confusable administrative term.
xs: A **dastak** was a **free pass for duty-free trade** — option **(4)**.
**Company servants misused dastaks** for **private trade**, draining the Nawab's revenue.
xa: Dastak misuse caused quarrels with **Siraj** and later **Mir Qasim**.
**Mir Qasim** **abolished all internal trade duties**, so the dastak advantage vanished.

n44923319f4a.s: Following the Battle of Plassey, which one of the following combinations of concessions was obtained by the Company?
o: Kora and Allahabad, together with the Nizamat of Bengal
Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa and control of Awadh
The whole of Bengal without the appointment of a Nawab
Zamindari of the 24 Parganas, duty-free trade and resources to fight the French
n44923319f4a.x: After Plassey, the Company obtained the zamindari of the 24 Parganas, duty-free trade in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, and resources to fight the French.
n44923319f4a.tq: Group the immediate commercial, territorial and strategic results of one event.
xs: After Plassey the Company got the **zamindari of the 24 Parganas**, **duty-free trade** in Bengal, Bihar, Orissa, and **resources to beat the French** — option **(4)**.
**Diwani** and **Awadh's** dependence came after **Buxar**; **Kora and Allahabad** went to **Shah Alam II** in **1765**.
xa: Mir Jafar became Nawab and paid **Rs 1.77 crore**.
Plassey: **puppet Nawab, 24 Parganas**; Buxar: **Diwani**, Awadh dependent.

n0f19706f1da.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Diwani granted to the East India Company?
o: The right to collect revenue and administer civil justice in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa
The right to appoint the Mughal Emperor and control Delhi
The right to conduct foreign affairs on behalf of Awadh
The right to administer criminal justice and maintain the police in Bengal alone
n0f19706f1da.x: Diwani comprised revenue collection and civil justice in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
n0f19706f1da.tq: Discriminate between Diwani functions and the Nizamat functions retained by the Nawab.
xs: **Diwani** = **revenue collection and civil justice** in **Bengal, Bihar and Orissa** — option **(1)**.
**Criminal justice and police** form the **Nizamat**, kept by the Nawab.
xa: Granted by **Shah Alam II** under the **Treaty of Allahabad (1765)**.
**Naib diwans**: **Muhammad Reza Khan** (Bengal) + **Raja Shitab Rai** (Bihar).

n392d0f5e0c0.s: Who was the last independent Nawab of Bengal?
n392d0f5e0c0.x: Siraj-ud-Daulah, the last independent Nawab, was defeated by Clive at Plassey despite French support.
xa: Conspirators inside his army: **Mir Jafar**, **Rai Durlabh**, **Jagat Seth**, **Omichund**, **Manik Chand**.
Loyal: **Mir Madan** + **Mohan Lal**.

n8118c045756.s: Which of the following correctly represents the two periods of Mir Jafar's tenure as Nawab of Bengal?
n8118c045756.x: Mir Jafar served as Nawab from 1757 to 1760 and again from 1763 to 1765, after the fall of Mir Qasim.
n8118c045756.tq: Test the two-tenure pattern instead of treating the office as a single continuous term.
xs: Mir Jafar ruled **1757-1760** and again **1763-1765** — option **(4)**.
**1760-63** was **Mir Qasim**; **1756-57** was **Siraj-ud-Daulah**.
xa: First term: after Plassey; removed in **1760** — could not meet Company demands.
Second term: restored after **Mir Qasim's fall**; accepted **limits on his army**; died soon after **Buxar**.

nf9963050d18.s: Mir Jafar's intrigue with which European power led to the Company's victory at Chinsura or Bidara in 1759?
nf9963050d18.x: Mir Jafar plotted with the Dutch against the English, but Clive defeated the Dutch at Chinsura or Bidara in 1759, after which the Dutch left India.
nf9963050d18.tq: Match the Indian political actor with the European ally involved in the intrigue.
xs: Mir Jafar plotted with the **Dutch**; Clive beat them at **Chinsura/Bidara (1759)** — option **(4)**.
After this the **Dutch left India**.
xa: Mir Jafar was removed in **1760** — he could not meet **Company demands**.
Pension: **Rs 15,000 a month** (some notes print "Rs 1,500 annually").

n399d3ddb2ba.s: Mir Qasim was placed on the throne of Bengal in 1760 by
n399d3ddb2ba.x: Mir Qasim, the son-in-law of Mir Jafar, was placed on the throne in 1760 by Governor Vansittart.
n399d3ddb2ba.tq: Use the ruler–appointing authority pair rather than confusing the successive Governors of Bengal.
xs: **Governor Vansittart** put **Mir Qasim** on the throne in **1760** — option **(1)**.
Mir Qasim was **Mir Jafar's son-in-law**.
**Warren Hastings** came in **1772**; **Clive** returned in **May 1765**.
xa: **Treaty of 1760**: ceded **Burdwan, Midnapur and Chittagong**.
He moved the capital **Murshidabad to Monghyr (Munger), Bihar**.

n3c5027fc8a2.s: Why did the abolition of internal trade duties by Mir Qasim lead to conflict with the Company’s servants?
o: It prevented Indian merchants from trading outside Bengal.
It made Indian merchants compete on equal terms with English merchants and removed the advantage derived from dastaks.
It transferred the Company’s Diwani rights to the Nawab.
It imposed a new uniform duty exclusively on English merchants.
n3c5027fc8a2.x: By abolishing internal duties, Mir Qasim placed Indian merchants on an equal footing with English merchants and removed the advantage that Company servants obtained through misuse of dastaks.
n3c5027fc8a2.tq: Trace the economic consequence of equal trade treatment to identify the cause of the conflict.
xs: Abolishing internal duties made **Indian merchants pay the same as the English**, ending the **dastak** advantage — option **(2)**.
**Company servants**, angry at lost **private-trade profits**, went to war.
xa: Asked in **APPSC G2 2017**.
Mir Qasim was **defeated in 1763** and fled to **Awadh**.

n77ed6540c91.s: Which Nawab of Bengal shifted his capital from Murshidabad to Monghyr and abolished all internal trade duties?
n77ed6540c91.x: Mir Qasim (1760-63) moved the capital to Monghyr (Munger) in Bihar and abolished all inland duties, so Indian merchants paid the same as the English. Mir Jafar was the puppet after Plassey, Siraj lost Plassey, and Najm-ud-Daula was Nawab from 1765 in name only.
n77ed6540c91.tq: Mir Qasim = Monghyr + abolished internal duties (APPSC G2 2017)
xs: **Mir Qasim** moved the capital to **Monghyr (Munger)** and **abolished all internal trade duties** — option **(2)**.
**Mir Jafar** was a **puppet**; **Siraj** lost Plassey; **Najm-ud-Daula** kept the **Nizamat** in name only from **1765**.
xa: He also **modernised the army**.
He was **Mir Jafar's son-in-law**.

nc6e2a0af6a1.s: Najm-ud-Daula, who became Nawab of Bengal in 1765, was the son of:
nc6e2a0af6a1.x: Najm-ud-Daula was Mir Jafar's son; he held the Nizamat in name only.
xa: **Diwani** = revenue + civil justice; **Nizamat** = police, criminal justice.
**Dual Government** lasted **1765-72**; **Warren Hastings** ended it.
**Raja Shitab Rai** was naib diwan for **Bihar**.

n9ee93abbc92.s: Which of the following was NOT a cause of conflict between the English Company and Siraj-ud-Daulah?
o: Fortification of Calcutta without the Nawab's consent
Misuse of dastaks by Company servants
Sheltering of the Nawab's enemies by the Company
French refusal to obey the Nawab's order to stop fortification
n9ee93abbc92.x: The French obeyed the order to stop fortification; it was the English who continued fortifying Calcutta.
xa: **Black Hole (June 1756)**: Siraj took **Qasim Bazar** → **Calcutta (Fort William)**.
Governor **Drake** fled to **Fulta**.

n30589aad3d0.s: The immediate result of the Company’s conflict with Mir Qasim in 1763 was that he
o: was restored to the throne of Bengal
surrendered directly to Shah Alam II at Delhi
fled to Awadh after being defeated
joined the British and became Governor of Bengal
n30589aad3d0.x: The Company defeated Mir Qasim in 1763, after which he fled to Awadh and later became one of the allies against the British at Buxar.
n30589aad3d0.tq: Link the defeat year with the correct subsequent movement of the defeated ruler.
xs: Mir Qasim was **defeated in 1763** and **fled to Awadh** — option **(3)**.
**Mir Jafar**, not Mir Qasim, was **restored** in **1763**.
xa: At **Buxar (1764)** he fought as the **deposed Nawab of Bengal** alongside **Shuja-ud-Daulah** and **Shah Alam II**.
Mir Qasim ruled **1760-63**.

n90e8dcc5db1.s: Who commanded the British forces at the Battle of Buxar?
n90e8dcc5db1.x: Hector Munro commanded the British at Buxar against Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II.
xa: Buxar: **October 1764** (22-23 Oct), Bihar.
The Nawab of Bengal at the time was **Mir Jafar** (restored **1763**).

n427ff6c107c.s: After his defeat at Buxar, Shuja-ud-Daulah sought help from the Rohillas and the:
n427ff6c107c.x: Shuja fled and sought help from the Rohillas and the Marathas before surrendering.
xa: Buxar was a **decisive English win** under **Major Hector Munro**.
**Most decisive battle:** **Buxar** (UPPSC 2016).

n4d305c7dd0f.s: Who was the Nawab of Bengal at the time of the Battle of Buxar (October 1764)?
n4d305c7dd0f.x: Mir Jafar had been restored in 1763 and was Nawab during Buxar. Mir Qasim fought at Buxar as the deposed ex-Nawab, Siraj died after Plassey (1757), and Najm-ud-Daula became Nawab only in 1765.
n4d305c7dd0f.tq: Buxar: Mir Qasim = ex-Nawab; Mir Jafar = sitting Nawab
xs: **Mir Jafar**, restored in **1763**, was Nawab during Buxar — option **(4)**.
**Mir Qasim** fought as the **deposed** Nawab; **Siraj** was executed after **Plassey**.
**Najm-ud-Daula** became Nawab only from **1765**.
xa: Mir Jafar's second term: **1763-1765**; he died soon after Buxar.
In this term he accepted **limits on the size of his army**.

nindian-history-17-10.s: Who was the British commander in the Battle of Buxar?
nindian-history-17-10.x: Major Hector Munro led the British at Buxar (1764). Clive won Plassey, Eyre Coote won Wandiwash, and Count Lally led the French.
nindian-history-17-10.tq: Recall the commander of each battle.
n: Hector Munro led the British in the Battle of Buxar. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xs: **Major Hector Munro** — option **(3)**.
He led the British at **Buxar** (**October 1764**).
**Robert Clive** won **Plassey**; **Sir Eyre Coote** won **Wandiwash**; **Count Lally** led the French.
xa: Buxar was an **open military victory**, unlike Plassey's treachery.
After Buxar, **Shuja** fled and later surrendered; **Shah Alam** joined the English.
Buxar was fought on **22-23 Oct** in **Bihar**.

nac7ce5e2304.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Battle of Buxar from the Battle of Plassey?
o: Buxar occurred before Plassey and established Mir Qasim’s rule.
Buxar ended in a defeat of the English and restoration of Shah Alam II’s independent rule.
Buxar was won through open fighting, whereas Plassey is associated with treachery.
Buxar was fought against the French, whereas Plassey was fought against the Marathas.
nac7ce5e2304.x: Buxar was a decisive victory achieved through fighting, unlike Plassey, which is traditionally associated with treachery. Buxar strengthened British control in eastern and northern India.
nac7ce5e2304.tq: Use the contrast in the character of the two victories rather than their common British outcome.
xs: **Buxar** was an **open military victory**, while **Plassey** was won by **treachery** — option **(3)**.
Buxar (**1764**) came after Plassey (**1757**) and was an **English win**.
Buxar's enemies were **Bengal + Awadh + Mughal Emperor** — not the French or Marathas.
xa: Plassey laid the **foundation**; Buxar made the British **masters** of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
Plassey was called "**a transaction**", won through conspiracy.

n9e1e84af175.s: Which one of the following was a consequence specifically associated with the Battle of Buxar rather than the Battle of Plassey?
o: The Company restored the privileges of the 1717 farman.
The Company obtained the zamindari of the 24 Parganas.
Mir Jafar became Nawab of Bengal.
The Company secured the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa and made Awadh dependent.
n9e1e84af175.x: Buxar led to the grant of Diwani over Bengal, Bihar and Orissa and reduced Awadh to a dependent position. The other consequences relate to Plassey or the Treaty of Alinagar.
n9e1e84af175.tq: Separate the consequences of two closely connected events.
xs: **Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, Orissa** and a **dependent Awadh** came from **Buxar** — option **(4)**.
**1717 farman privileges** were restored at **Alinagar (Feb 1757)**.
**24 Parganas** and **Mir Jafar as Nawab** were results of **Plassey**.
xa: Buxar's enemy: **Bengal + Awadh + Mughal Emperor** together.
Plassey's result: **puppet Nawab**, **24 Parganas**.

n2650929cead.s: The annual tribute associated with the grant of Diwani to the East India Company was payable to the Mughal Emperor at the rate of
n2650929cead.x: The Company agreed to pay an annual tribute of Rs 26 lakh to Shah Alam II.
n2650929cead.tq: Distinguish the fixed annual tribute from other monetary payments connected with Bengal politics.
xs: The tribute was **Rs 26 lakh a year** to **Shah Alam II** — option **(2)**.
**Rs 5 lakh** was Mir Qasim's **1760** payment; **Rs 50 lakh** was Shuja-ud-Daulah's **war indemnity**.
xa: Shah Alam II became a **Company pensioner** — the **first Mughal ruler** to do so.
**Warren Hastings (1772)** **stopped the tribute** to Shah Alam.

n855baab35ac.s: Under the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), Shuja-ud-Daulah of Awadh paid a war indemnity of:
n855baab35ac.x: Shuja paid Rs 50 lakh and recovered his dominions except Kora and Allahabad, which went to Shah Alam II.
xa: Shah Alam II granted the **Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa** for **Rs 26 lakh a year**.
**Balwant Singh** of Banaras was confirmed in his estate.
The treaty was signed by **Clive** in his second governorship.

nba4471e1ca2.s: The combined significance of the Battles of Buxar and the Treaty of Allahabad was that they:
o: restored the independent authority of the Mughal Emperor over Bengal and Bihar
transferred the administration of Bengal entirely to the French
ended the Company's right to collect revenue in eastern India
made the Company the real ruler of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa and reduced the Mughal Emperor to a pensioner
nba4471e1ca2.x: Buxar and Allahabad made the Company the real ruler of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, while the Mughal Emperor became its pensioner.
nba4471e1ca2.tq: Identify the broad political consequence rather than an individual military event.
xs: **Buxar** + **Allahabad** made the Company the **real ruler of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa** and the **Mughal Emperor its pensioner** — option **(4)**.
They gave the Company the **Diwani**, not ended its revenue rights.
xa: **Shah Alam II** = **first Mughal ruler** to become a Company **pensioner**.
Buxar made the British a **major power in North India**; **Awadh** became a **buffer state**.

n95af22f864e.s: The Battle of Plassey was fought on which of the following dates and at which place?
n95af22f864e.x: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 at Palashi, also known as Plassey, on the Bhagirathi River.
n95af22f864e.tq: Use the date-place combination to distinguish closely related battles.
xs: Plassey: **23 June 1757**, at **Plassey (Palashi)** — option **(3)**.
It lay on the **Bhagirathi**, in **Nadia** district, **West Bengal**.
**22 October 1764** is **Buxar**, fought in Bihar.
xa: **Clive** (about **3,000**) defeated **Siraj-ud-Daulah** (about **50,000**).
**23 June 2026** = **269th** anniversary of Plassey.

nb7db73f4097.s: Warren Hastings became Governor of Bengal in:
nb7db73f4097.x: Warren Hastings became Governor of Bengal in 1772, after Buxar (1764) and the Treaty of Allahabad (1765).
xa: Allahabad was signed in Clive's **second term** (**1765-67**); his first was **1758-60**.
Hastings ended the **Dual Government (1765-72)** and **stopped the tribute** to Shah Alam.

n53a03a85f39.s: Under the Dual Government in Bengal (1765–1772), the Diwani was held by:
n53a03a85f39.x: The Company held the Diwani (revenue and civil justice) while the Nawab kept the Nizamat.
xa: Criticism: **power without responsibility** → **1770 Bengal famine** (**John Cartier**'s time).
**Warren Hastings (1772)** ended it.

n7e246ba8ff1.s: Which development in 1772 is associated with Warren Hastings?
o: Restoration of Mir Jafar for a second tenure
Formation of Awadh as a buffer state
End of Mughal pretence and rule by right of conquest
Grant of the Diwani to Shah Alam II
n7e246ba8ff1.x: In 1772, Warren Hastings ended the Mughal pretence and ruled Bengal by right of conquest.
n7e246ba8ff1.tq: Match the administrator with the institutional change associated with his tenure.
xs: **Warren Hastings (1772)** "**tore the mask of Mughal sovereignty**" and ruled **by right of conquest** — option **(3)**.
He ended the **Dual Government** (**1765-72**).
xa: He **stopped the tribute** to Shah Alam.
**Awadh** became a buffer state in **1765**, not **1772**.

naeeced9dd2b.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the relationship between the Dual Government and the Bengal Famine of 1770?
o: The Dual Government combined revenue collection and administrative responsibility in one authority, preventing famine relief.
The Dual Government ended Company revenue collection and restored the Nawab's fiscal authority.
The Dual Government separated power from responsibility, while revenue was squeezed as the famine spread.
The Dual Government was introduced after the famine solely to regulate private European trade.
naeeced9dd2b.x: The Dual Government separated power from responsibility. At the same time, revenue was squeezed even as the famine spread, contributing to the disastrous conditions.
naeeced9dd2b.tq: Apply the power–responsibility distinction to the famine context.
xs: The **Dual Government** separated **power from responsibility** while revenue was squeezed as the famine spread — option **(3)**.
It did not combine revenue and administration; Company = **Diwani**, Nawab = **Nizamat**.
It ran **1765-72**, so it came **before** the **1770 Bengal famine**, not after.
xa: The famine came in **John Cartier**'s time.
**Warren Hastings (1772)** ended the Dual Government.

nf2c6b6287c2.s: Which one of the following was NOT a conspirator against Siraj-ud-Daula at Plassey?
nf2c6b6287c2.x: Mir Madan was loyal to Siraj-ud-Daula and was not among the conspirators. Mir Jafar, Rai Durlabh and Jagat Seth were associated with the conspiracy.
nf2c6b6287c2.tq: Find the loyal commander hidden among the names of the conspirators.
xs: **Mir Madan** was **loyal to Siraj** — not a conspirator — option **(1)**.
Conspirators: **Mir Jafar** (Mir Bakshi), **Rai Durlabh**, **Jagat Seth**, **Amir Chand (Omichund)**, **Manik Chand**.
xa: **Mohan Lal** was also loyal to Siraj.
⚠ Trap: listing **Mir Madan** among the traitors is WRONG (**Jul 2026** practice question).

n8341ec06445.s: Which treaty followed the Battle of Buxar (1764)?
n8341ec06445.x: The Treaty of Allahabad (1765) followed Buxar and gave the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. Salbai (1782) ended the First Anglo-Maratha War, Bassein (1802) was the Peshwa's subsidiary treaty, and Sugauli (1816) ended the Anglo-Nepal War.
xs: The **Treaty of Allahabad (1765)** followed Buxar — option **(2)**.
**Salbai** belongs to **1782**; the notes stress **Allahabad**, not **Salbai, Bassein or Sugauli**.
xa: It gave the **Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, Orissa** for **Rs 26 lakh** a year.
Treaty chronology: **Allahabad (1765)**, **Madras (1769)**, **Salbai (1782)**, **Mangalore (1784)**.

n7bc5af20349.s: Who called Robert Clive a 'heaven-born general'?
n7bc5af20349.x: William Pitt called Clive a 'heaven-born general'; Clive was Governor of Bengal twice.
xa: Record: **Arcot (1751)**, **Chandannagar (1757)**, **Plassey (1757)**, **Condore (1758)**.
Treaty of Allahabad was signed in his **second term**.

n3bcd2bd3647.s: The conflict between the Nizamat and the Diwani under the Dual Government primarily resulted in which consequence?
o: Sidelining of local nobility and the growth of resentment
Transfer of political power to peasants
n3bcd2bd3647.x: The conflict between the two authorities sidelined the local nobility and generated resentment.
n3bcd2bd3647.tq: Infer the political consequence from divided authority and responsibility.
xs: The **Nizamat** vs **Diwani** conflict **sidelined the local nobility** → **resentment** — option **(1)**.
It did not strengthen the nobility or end Company privileges.
xa: **Revenue extortion** ruined the Bengal economy.
**Weavers** were forced to sell to Company agents at low prices.

n6438dfdb1ab.s: The Dual Government in Bengal continued during which period?
n6438dfdb1ab.x: The Dual Government was introduced in 1765 and continued until its abolition in 1772.
n6438dfdb1ab.tq: Fix both the starting and ending years of the arrangement.
xs: The Dual Government lasted **1765-1772** — option **(1)**.
It began with the **Second Treaty of Allahabad (1765)** and ended with **Warren Hastings (1772)**.
xa: **Shah Alam II** granted the **Diwani** of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa for **₹26 lakh** a year.
Verdict: "**a sham**" → economic ruin of Bengal + **famine of 1770**.

n657d4137ef9.s: Who introduced the system of Dual Government in Bengal?
n657d4137ef9.x: Robert Clive introduced the Dual Government in Bengal during his second term as Governor of Bengal from 1765 to 1767.
n657d4137ef9.tq: Use the direct architect–institution link and distinguish Clive from Hastings.
xs: **Robert Clive** was the **architect** of the Dual Government — option **(1)**.
He was Governor of Bengal for the 2nd term, **1765-67**.
**Warren Hastings** **abolished** it (**1772**); **John Cartier** was Governor during the **1770** famine.
xa: Exam angle: "The dual system was enforced by" — **Robert Clive**, not Warren Hastings.
⚠ **Clive** enforced (**1765**); **Hastings** abolished (**1772**).

n81a7634b263.s: R.P. Dutt placed the drain of Bengal's surplus revenue after 1765 in the mercantilist phase, which he dated:
n81a7634b263.x: R.P. Dutt dated the mercantilist phase 1757-1813, when Bengal's surplus revenue bought Indian goods for export.
xa: R.P. Dutt described **three stages**.
Scholars trace the **drain of wealth** + **deindustrialisation** to the Dual Government.

n4e88f13e937.s: The Great Bengal Famine of 1770 occurred during the term of:
n4e88f13e937.x: The Great Bengal Famine of 1770 occurred during John Cartier's term as governor, which lasted from 1769 to 1772.
n4e88f13e937.tq: Match the event with the correct contemporary administrator.
xs: The **1770** famine fell in **John Cartier**'s term (**1769-72**) — option **(2)**.
**Warren Hastings** came in **1772**; **Robert Clive**'s 2nd term was **1765-67**.
xa: Exam angle: "Governor during the 1770 famine" — **John Cartier**.
"Famine and Dual Government" — direct **cause-effect**.

nfe7330e66a1.s: What was the immediate effect of Company policies on Bengal weavers?
o: They were exempted from all contractual obligations.
They received tax-free access to European markets.
They were compelled to sell to Company agents at low prices.
They were appointed as Company revenue officers.
nfe7330e66a1.x: Company agents forced weavers to sell their products at low prices, contributing to the decline of handicrafts.
nfe7330e66a1.tq: Test the producer–Company agent relationship and its economic effect.
xs: **Weavers** were **forced to sell to Company agents at low prices** — option **(3)**.
Result: **handicrafts declined**.
xa: Company servants also misused the **dastak** for inland trade.
In under two decades Bengal fell into **acute poverty, famines, epidemics**.

nceb73bd19ca.s: By the period following the establishment of Dual Government, Bengal, formerly regarded as India’s richest province, was reduced to:
o: A province free from Company intervention
nceb73bd19ca.x: In under two decades, Bengal was reduced to acute poverty, famines and epidemics despite its earlier wealth.
nceb73bd19ca.tq: Use the before–after comparison to identify the correct historical consequence.
xs: Bengal, **India's richest province**, fell into **acute poverty, famines, epidemics** — option **(4)**.
This happened **in under two decades**.
xa: Causes: **revenue extortion**, **wealth drain**, decline of **weavers**' handicrafts.
Climax: the **famine of 1770**.

n31b2092efb1.s: Under the Dual Government, the East India Company collected revenue through:
o: Direct collection by British district collectors
Indian deputies acting on its behalf
Village panchayats appointed by the Nawab
n31b2092efb1.x: The Company did not collect revenue itself at first; it worked through Indian deputies.
xa: **Muhammad Reza Khan** = Naib Diwan, **Bengal (Murshidabad)**; **Raja Shitab Rai** = **Bihar (Patna)**.
After **1772** the Company collected revenue **directly through its own servants**.

nd95e5709c41.s: Mir Qasim had earlier abolished internal duties for everyone primarily as a protest against:
o: The Company’s use of duty-free dastaks for private trade
The famine relief measures of the Nawab
The transfer of the treasury to Calcutta
The abolition of the Diwani by Shah Alam II
nd95e5709c41.x: Mir Qasim abolished internal duties for all traders in protest against the Company servants’ misuse of duty-free dastaks.
nd95e5709c41.tq: Link a reform measure with the commercial grievance that prompted it.
xs: **Mir Qasim** abolished internal duties for everyone in protest against the Company's **duty-free dastaks** for **private trade** — option **(1)**.
The **treasury shift to Calcutta** came only in **1772**, under Hastings.
xa: Dastak = **duty-free trade pass**.
**Weavers** too were exploited — forced sales at low prices.

n0cc8028b75c.s: Before the Bengal Famine of 1770, the high land revenue was collected in ____, forcing peasants to sell grain.
n0cc8028b75c.x: High land revenue demanded in cash forced peasants to sell grain, one of the causes of the 1770 famine.
xa: Governor: **John Cartier (1769-72)**.
Company response: **little or no relief**; revenue collection continued.

n92fa16fee19.s: During the Bengal Famine of 1770, the Company:
o: provided extensive relief and suspended revenue collection
stopped all exports and remitted land revenue permanently
handed famine administration to the Nawab without conditions
gave little or no relief and kept collecting revenue
n92fa16fee19.x: The Company offered little or no relief and continued collecting revenue during the famine.
xa: This **hurt the Company's reputation** + **increased local opposition**.
Deaths: about **10 million** (UPSC notes); "**about two million lives**" (APP); textbook: about **one-third**.

n46016b991aa.s: After abolishing the Dual Government in 1772, Warren Hastings shifted the treasury from Murshidabad to:
n46016b991aa.x: Hastings moved the treasury from Murshidabad to Calcutta after ending the Dual Government in 1772.
xa: Revenue was now collected **directly through Company servants**.
Hastings = **last Governor of Bengal (1772-73)**, **first Governor-General (1773)**.

n37ec6b9af19.s: Which combination correctly identifies the principal causes of the Sanyasi-Fakir Revolt?
o: The famine of 1770, Company insensitivity and restrictions on pilgrims
The Subsidiary Alliance, the Doctrine of Lapse and missionary education
The Carnatic Wars, salt taxation and the Ilbert Bill
The Permanent Settlement, the Revolt of 1857 and railway construction
n37ec6b9af19.x: The revolt was caused by the famine of 1770, Company insensitivity and restrictions on pilgrims visiting holy places.
n37ec6b9af19.tq: Group the causes of a revolt and reject causes belonging to later periods.
xs: Causes: the **famine of 1770**, **Company insensitivity** and **restrictions on pilgrims** — option **(1)**.
The other options list later policies unrelated to this revolt in the notes.
xa: **Sanyasi (Fakir) Revolt** = **1763-1800**.
Leaders: **Majnum Shah, Bhawani Pathak, Devi Chaudhurani**.

n0d0e411c2a5.s: Who among the following was a leader of the Sanyasi-Fakir Revolt?
n0d0e411c2a5.x: Majnum Shah (with Bhawani Pathak and Devi Chaudhurani) led the Sanyasi-Fakir Revolt; Shah Alam II was not a leader of it.
xa: Revolt period: **1763-1800**.
Shah Alam II lost the **₹26 lakh** payment in **1772**.

n7af215a5baa.s: Anandamath (1882), which contains the song Vande Mataram, was written by:
n7af215a5baa.x: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay published Anandamath in 1882; it contains Vande Mataram.
xa: Sanyasi revolt leaders include **Bhawani Pathak** and **Devi Chaudhurani**.
Revolt period: **1763-1800**.

n288ec2c5338.s: On which date was Tipu Sultan killed while defending Seringapatam?
n288ec2c5338.x: Tipu Sultan was killed on 4 May 1799 while defending Seringapatam during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.
n288ec2c5338.tq: Distinguish the exact date of the event from the year of the earlier treaty.
xs: Tipu was killed on **4 May 1799** defending **Seringapatam** — option **(3)**.
**1792** was the **Treaty of Seringapatam**; **1800** the **Ceded Districts**.
xa: This was the **4th war**; the **British won**.
**Arthur Wellesley** (later **Duke of Wellington**) served in this campaign.

n633a0fc9683.s: During which Anglo-Mysore War did both the Nizam and the Marathas join the British in a grand alliance?
n633a0fc9683.x: Both the Nizam and the Marathas were with the British in the Third Anglo-Mysore War, forming part of the grand alliance.
n633a0fc9683.tq: Use the common position of two powers to distinguish the Third War from the other wars.
xs: Both the Nizam and the Marathas were **with the British** in the **Third** war (grand alliance) — option **(1)**.
⚠ Only the **Third** war had both on the British side.
xa: The 3rd war **ended Tipu's supremacy in the south**.
It closed with the **Treaty of Seringapatam (1792)**.

n2158f054e5e.s: The Treaty of Mangalore (1784) was concluded between the British and:
n2158f054e5e.x: The Treaty of Mangalore (1784) was made with Tipu Sultan; the Treaty of Madras (1769) was made with Haidar Ali.
xa: 3rd war → **Treaty of Seringapatam (1792)**.
⚠ Trap: **Madras (1769)** = Haidar vs **Mangalore (1784)** = Tipu.

nindian-history-17-39.s: The First Anglo-Mysore War, led on the Mysore side by Haidar Ali, ended in 1769 with the Treaty of:
nindian-history-17-39.x: Haidar Ali came out on top near Madras and the war ended with the Treaty of Madras (1769).
n: Haidar Ali led Mysore in the First Anglo-Mysore War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
Haidar Ali was victorious in the First Anglo-Mysore War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Treaty of Madras was concluded in 1769. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xa: ⚠ **Treaty of Madras (1769)** = with Haidar; **Treaty of Mangalore (1784)** = with Tipu.
Haidar won over the **Marathas** and detached the **Nizam** from the British.
Haidar became **de facto ruler** in **1761**.

nindian-history-17-41.s: At the start of the Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780-84), Haidar Ali was allied with:
o: the Nawab of Arcot and the Marathas
the Nizam and the Nawab of Arcot
nindian-history-17-41.x: The Second Anglo-Mysore War began with Haidar Ali allied to the Nizam and the Marathas.
n: The Second Anglo-Mysore War was fought from 1780 to 1784. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Second Anglo-Mysore War was fought between the British and Mysore. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan were associated with the Second Anglo-Mysore War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Second Anglo-Mysore War was a major Anglo-Mysore conflict. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
Haidar Ali allied with the Nizam and the Marathas during the Second Anglo-Mysore War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: other notes say the Nizam was later bought off and the Marathas made peace with the British at **Salbai 1782**.
**Pollilur** (**1780**) and **Porto Novo** (**1781**) were its battles.
It ended with the **Treaty of Mangalore** (**1784**).

nindian-history-19-19.s: Which battle reversed the British defeat at Pollilur (1780)?
nindian-history-19-19.x: Coote's defeat of Haidar Ali at Porto Novo (1781) reversed the British disaster at Pollilur (1780).
n: Sir Eyre Coote defeated Haidar Ali in the Battle of Porto Novo. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 74-76]
The Battle of Porto Novo reversed the result of the Battle of Pollilur. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 74-76]
xa: At Pollilur Haidar and Tipu had defeated **Colonel Baillie**.
Both battles belong to the **Second Anglo-Mysore War**.
Third war: Tipu defeated **General Meadows** (**1790**); **Cornwallis** took **Bangalore** (**March 1791**).

n2bdd7f61b79.s: In 1790, Tipu Sultan defeated the British army commanded by
n2bdd7f61b79.x: In 1790, Tipu Sultan defeated the British army under General Meadows during the Third Anglo-Mysore War.
n2bdd7f61b79.tq: Avoid swapping commanders from different battles and years.
xs: In **1790** Tipu defeated the British army under **General Meadows** — option **(1)**.
**Col. Baillie** was beaten at **Pollilur (1780)**; **Hector Munro** and **Sir Eyre Coote** were early-wars commanders.
xa: In **1791** **Cornwallis** took **Bangalore (March 1791)** via **Ambur** and **Vellore**.
The 3rd war ended with Cornwallis's coalition win at **Seringapatam (1792)**.

nindian-history-17-42.s: At the Battle of Porto Novo (July 1781), Haidar Ali was defeated by:
nindian-history-17-42.x: Sir Eyre Coote led the British to victory over Haidar Ali at Porto Novo in the Second Anglo-Mysore War.
n: The Battle of Porto Novo was fought in July 1781. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Battle of Porto Novo was fought between Sir Eyre Coote and Haidar Ali. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
Sir Eyre Coote led the British side in the Battle of Porto Novo. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The British won the Battle of Porto Novo. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Battle of Porto Novo was part of the Second Anglo-Mysore War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xa: It reversed the British defeat at **Pollilur** (**1780**).
Coote later won **Wandiwash** against the French.
**Thomas Munro** served under both **Hector Munro** and **Eyre Coote**.

ncf8eef50c25.s: Haidar Ali became Faujdar of Dindigul in 1755 under the Mysore minister:
ncf8eef50c25.x: Haidar Ali rose under the Wodeyars and became Faujdar of Dindigul in 1755 under the minister Nanjaraja.
xa: He adopted **Western techniques** and set up a **modern arsenal at Dindigul** with French help.
In the 1st war he **won over the Marathas** and **detached the Nizam** from the British.

n24c3bd3b142.s: Which development at Dindigul is associated with Haidar Ali?
o: A naval dockyard was established under British supervision.
A modern arsenal was established with French help.
The Ryotwari system was first introduced by Read and Munro.
A Jacobin Club was established with Maratha help.
n24c3bd3b142.x: Haidar Ali adopted Western military techniques and established a modern arsenal at Dindigul with French help.
n24c3bd3b142.tq: Use the military institution and foreign assistance as the identifying pair.
xs: Haidar Ali set up a **modern arsenal at Dindigul** with **French help** — option **(2)**.
**Ryotwari** began in the **Bara Mahal** (Read and Munro); the **Jacobin Club** was Tipu's, at **Seringapatam (1797)**.
xa: Haidar was **Faujdar of Dindigul in 1755**.
⚠ **Dindigul** arsenal = Haidar; **French embassy + navy + Jacobin Club** = Tipu.

na063bf469f0.s: The Jacobin Club at Seringapatam, of which 'Citizen Tipu' became a member, was established in:
na063bf469f0.x: The Jacobin Club was set up at Seringapatam in 1797; Tipu joined it, called himself 'Citizen Tipu' and planted a Tree of Liberty.
xa: Other titles: **"Tiger of Mysore"**, **Padshah**.
He sent ambassadors to **France** and built a **navy**.

n0629eb8a48b.s: Which Mysore ruler sent ambassadors to France for European technology and used it to build a navy?
n0629eb8a48b.x: Tipu Sultan sent ambassadors to France and built a navy (APPSC-G1 2018 key). Statement questions on the 'French embassy + navy' point to Tipu, not Haidar Ali or the Wodeyars.
xs: **Tipu Sultan** sent ambassadors to **France** and built a **navy** — option **(3)**.
This is the **APPSC-G1 2018** key; "French embassy + navy" points to Tipu, **not Haidar or the Wodeyars**.
xa: **Haidar**'s French link was the **arsenal at Dindigul**.
**Krishnaraja Wodeyar III** was the **boy ruler** restored in **1799**.

nb7222ee23c9.s: The Third Anglo-Mysore War is significant because it
o: made the Marathas neutral in all subsequent wars.
ended Tipu Sultan's supremacy in southern India.
brought the Ceded Districts directly under the British in 1800.
established the French-backed threat in Mysore.
nb7222ee23c9.x: The Third Anglo-Mysore War ended Tipu Sultan's supremacy in the south. The Ceded Districts came to the British in 1800 as a consequence of the Mysore wars, not as the stated significance of the Third War alone.
nb7222ee23c9.tq: Separate the significance of the Third War from consequences associated with the Fourth War and 1800 settlement.
xs: The **Third war** **ended Tipu's supremacy in the south** — option **(2)**.
The **Ceded Districts (1800)** and removal of the **French-backed threat** belong to the **Fourth** war.
xa: Tipu ceded about **half his territory** in **1792**.
Cornwallis took **Bangalore (March 1791)**.

na8bba5b337c.s: Under the Treaty of Seringapatam of 1792, Tipu Sultan was required to
o: transfer his capital to Bangalore and join the Maratha confederacy
surrender the whole of Mysore and abdicate permanently
cede about half his territory, pay ₹3 crore and give two sons as hostages
cede Dindigul alone and pay no indemnity
na8bba5b337c.x: Tipu Sultan ceded about half his territory, paid a war indemnity of ₹3 crore and gave two sons as hostages under the Treaty of Seringapatam.
na8bba5b337c.tq: Combine the territorial, financial and hostage terms of the treaty.
xs: Tipu ceded about **half his territory**, paid **₹3 crore** and gave **two sons as hostages** — option **(3)**.
**Half the indemnity** was paid at once; the sons returned after the rest was paid.
xa: **Nizam** gained from the **Krishna to beyond the Pennar**; **Marathas** around the **Tungabhadra**.
**British** gained **Malabar, Coorg, Dindigul and the Bara Mahal**.

n58072dd0729.s: Under the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792), Malabar, Coorg (as protectorate), Dindigul and the Bara Mahal went to:
n58072dd0729.x: The British took Malabar, Coorg, Dindigul and the Bara Mahal; the Nizam got the Krishna-Pennar area and the Marathas the Tungabhadra area.
xa: The Nizam's share included half of **Rayalaseema**: **Bellary, Gurramkonda, Gandikota, Kambham, Kadapa**.
**Bara Mahal** (Salem region) is where **Read and Munro** began **Ryotwari**.

naa9b2a72617.s: The Bara Mahal, obtained by the British after the Treaty of Seringapatam, is associated with the beginning of the Ryotwari system by
naa9b2a72617.x: The Bara Mahal, identified with the Salem region, was where Read and Thomas Munro began the Ryotwari system.
naa9b2a72617.tq: Match the administrative experiment with the place and officials associated with it.
xs: **Read and Munro** began the **Ryotwari** system in the **Bara Mahal** — option **(4)**.
Bara Mahal = **Salem region**, gained by the **British** in **1792**.
xa: **Arthur Wellesley** served in the **1799** campaign; **Cornwallis** won the **3rd war**.
British share in 1792 also included **Malabar**, **Coorg** and **Dindigul**.

ndc0d9be7bb2.s: During the First Anglo-Mysore War, Haidar Ali weakened the British position by
o: winning over the Marathas and detaching the Nizam from the British
restoring the Wodeyar dynasty to the Madras Presidency
forming a permanent alliance with Lord Cornwallis
ndc0d9be7bb2.x: Haidar Ali used diplomacy to win over the Marathas and detach the Nizam from the British during the First Anglo-Mysore War.
ndc0d9be7bb2.tq: Identify the diplomatic combination that changed the balance of the war.
xs: Haidar **won over the Marathas** and **detached the Nizam** from the British — option **(2)**.
The **Wodeyar** restoration came in **1799**; **Cornwallis** belongs to the **Third** war.
xa: The Nizam had first **joined the British**, and the Marathas had **joined against Haidar** (UPSC).
The war ended with the **Treaty of Madras (1769)** with Haidar.

n05d2020f80b.s: Which one of the following best describes the position of the Nizam during the Second Anglo-Mysore War?
o: He supported Haidar Ali without interruption until the Treaty of Salbai.
He was part of an anti-British confederacy but was later bought off.
He remained a subsidiary ally of the British from 1798.
He formed a grand alliance with the British throughout the war.
n05d2020f80b.x: During the Second Anglo-Mysore War, the Nizam was associated with an anti-British confederacy but was later bought off.
n05d2020f80b.tq: Use the specific alliance description to distinguish the Second War from the other Anglo-Mysore Wars.
xs: In the 2nd war the Nizam was in an **anti-British confederacy**, later **bought off** — option **(2)**.
He became a **subsidiary ally** only **since 1798** (4th war); the **grand alliance** was the **3rd** war.
xa: The **Marathas** made peace with the British at **Salbai 1782**.
2nd war battles: **Pollilur (1780)**, **Porto Novo (1781)**; ended by **Mangalore (1784)**.

n85888f9d3c7.s: After the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War, who was placed on the restored Wodeyar throne of Mysore as a boy ruler?
n85888f9d3c7.x: After the Fourth War the Wodeyar dynasty was restored with the boy ruler Krishnaraja Wodeyar III, under a Subsidiary Alliance.
xa: The Nizam's share → handed to the Company in **1800** as the **Ceded Districts**.
The 4th war **removed the French-backed threat**.

nfdfc1dbd7e1.s: The Nizam's share of Mysore lands after the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War later became known as the
nfdfc1dbd7e1.x: The Nizam's share of Mysore lands became known as the Ceded Districts.
nfdfc1dbd7e1.tq: Identify the later administrative name given to the territorial transfer.
xs: The Nizam's share of Mysore lands became the **Ceded Districts** — option **(2)**.
**Bara Mahal** was a **British** gain of **1792**.
xa: They were handed to the Company in **1800** to pay for the **subsidiary force**.
Ceded Districts: **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary**.

n6b9f040fbef.s: The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War had which one of the following broader consequences?
o: It ended all British relations with the Nizam.
It restored Tipu Sultan's supremacy in southern India.
It transferred Mysore and Andhra to the Marathas.
It removed the French-backed threat and brought Mysore and Andhra under Company control.
n6b9f040fbef.x: The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War removed the French-backed threat and brought Mysore and Andhra, through the Ceded Districts, under the Company.
n6b9f040fbef.tq: Link the war with its two stated strategic consequences instead of focusing on only one region.
xs: The Fourth war **removed the French-backed threat** and brought **Mysore + Andhra** under the Company — option **(4)**.
Andhra came via the **Ceded Districts**; the Nizam stayed a **British ally**.
xa: Tipu was killed on **4 May 1799**; **Wodeyar** rule restored.
Ceded Districts: **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary** (**1800**).

n8e173b18ef2.s: Which of the following districts constituted the Ceded Districts that came to the British in 1800 as a direct result of the Mysore Wars?
o: Chittoor, East Godavari, West Godavari and Visakhapatnam
n8e173b18ef2.x: The Ceded Districts were Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary. They came to the British in 1800 as a direct result of the Mysore Wars.
n8e173b18ef2.tq: Test the complete district list and avoid substituting neighbouring Andhra or Telangana districts.
xs: The **Ceded Districts** were **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary** — option **(2)**.
They came to the British in **1800** as a **direct result of the Mysore wars**.
xa: They were the Nizam's share of Mysore lands, handed over to pay for the **subsidiary force**.
In **1792** the Nizam's share had included **Bellary, Gurramkonda, Gandikota, Kambham, Kadapa**.

n6fe018df7a3.s: Which ruler of Sivaganga took Haidar Ali's help to recover her kingdom and is called the first queen to wage war against the British?
n6fe018df7a3.x: Velu Nachiyar of Sivaganga recovered her kingdom with Haidar Ali's help and is called the first queen to wage war against the British (APPSC-G1 2022). Chennamma (Kittur) and Lakshmibai (Jhansi) fought later, and Durgavati fought the Mughals.
xs: **Velu Nachiyar** of **Sivaganga** took Haidar Ali's help to recover her kingdom — option **(2)**.
She is called the **first queen to wage war against the British** (**APPSC-G1 2022** key).
xa: Haidar Ali was **de facto ruler** of Mysore from **1761**.
Haidar's allies-and-diplomacy also turned the **Marathas** and **Nizam** in the 1st war.

nd961b833d38.s: In the early Anglo-Mysore Wars, Thomas Munro served under Hector Munro and:
nd961b833d38.x: Hector Munro and Sir Eyre Coote were British commanders in the early wars, and Thomas Munro served under both.
xa: ⚠ Don't confuse **Hector Munro** (commander) with **Thomas Munro**.
**Eyre Coote** defeated Haidar at **Porto Novo (1781)**.

n60443e67535.s: The Treaty of Hyderabad of 1766 provided for the leasing of the Northern Circars to the British in return for
o: lands between the Krishna and the Pennar
a yearly payment of ₹9 lakh or military aid
a yearly payment of ₹7 lakh and the surrender of Guntur
the cession of Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary
n60443e67535.x: Under the 1766 Treaty of Hyderabad, the Northern Circars were leased to the British for military aid or an annual payment of ₹9 lakh.
n60443e67535.tq: Separate the terms of the 1766 treaty from later territorial cessions.
xs: The **1766 Treaty of Hyderabad** leased the **Northern Circars** for **military aid or ₹9 lakh a year** — option **(2)**.
**₹7 lakh** was the **Guntur (1788)** figure; **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary** were ceded in **1800**.
xa: Envoy **Calliaud** signed it; **Kandregula Jogipanthulu** mediated.
⚠ **₹15 lakh** = proposed lease; **₹9 lakh** = **1766/1768**; **₹7 lakh** = Guntur.

n7af4241b654.s: Who granted the Northern Circars to the East India Company through a Mughal firman in 1765?
n7af4241b654.x: The Mughal firman granting the Circars to the East India Company was issued by Shah Alam II in 1765, though some sources date it to 1766.
n7af4241b654.tq: Identify the issuing authority directly, while distinguishing it from the later Nizam agreement.
xs: The **Farman of Shah Alam II** (**1765**), received by **Clive**, granted the Circars to the EIC — option **(3)**.
Some notes date the firman to **1766**.
xa: **Nizam Ali refused to accept it at first**.
Some notes put the firman payment at **₹20 lakh** a year.
