nf67210b7260.s: In which year did Nizam Ali agree to lease the Northern Circars to the British?
nf67210b7260.x: Nizam Ali leased the Circars in 1766, after Salabat Jung's grant (1759) and before the Treaty of Masulipatnam (1768) and the Guntur handover (1788).
xa: **Basalat Jung** died in **1782**; Guntur came after **6 years of talks**.
Guntur's handover completed the **Northern Circars**.

n88970b88019.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the Circars handed over in 1766?
n88970b88019.x: Mustafanagar, Eluru, Rajamahendravaram and Srikakulam were among the Circars handed over in 1766. Kurnool formed part of the Ceded Districts transferred in 1800.
n88970b88019.tq: Find the item belonging to the later Ceded Districts transfer rather than the 1766 Circars.
xs: **Kurnool** was not one of the 1766 Circars — option **(1)**.
The **1766** Circars: **Mustafanagar (Kondapalli), Eluru, Rajamahendravaram, Srikakulam**.
Kurnool was one of the **Ceded Districts** (**1800**).
xa: The 1766 lease was for **military aid or ₹9 lakh** a year.
**Guntur** (**Kondaveedu / Murtazanagar**) was the **5th Circar**, handed over in **1788**.

n3b1f039ca41.s: Which combination correctly describes the final transfer of Guntur to the Company?
o: Basalat Jung died in 1782; the transfer followed payment of 7 lakh rupees on 18 September 1788.
Basalat Jung died in 1788; the transfer followed payment of 9 lakh rupees in 1798.
Basalat Jung died in 1766; the transfer followed payment of 15 lakh rupees in 1768.
Basalat Jung died in 1800; the transfer followed the Cession Treaty.
n3b1f039ca41.x: Basalat Jung died in 1782. Nizam Ali received 7 lakh rupees and handed Guntur over on 18 September 1788.
n3b1f039ca41.tq: Match the two dates and the payment figure as a single transfer sequence.
xs: **Basalat Jung** died in **1782**; Guntur was handed over for **7 lakh rupees** on **18 September 1788** — option **(1)**.
The handover came after **6 years of talks** and completed the **Northern Circars**.
xa: **₹9 lakh** was the **1766/1768** Circars figure; **₹15 lakh** the proposed lease.
The **Ceded Districts** came separately in **1800**.

nf251dff82fd.s: The territories ceded by the Nizam to the British came to be known as:
nf251dff82fd.x: The ceded territories of Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary were known as Dattamandalalu, or the Ceded Districts.
nf251dff82fd.tq: Distinguish the regional label for the ceded inland districts from the coastal Northern Circars.
xs: The ceded lands were called **Dattamandalalu**, the **Ceded Districts** — option **(3)**.
The **Northern Circars** were a separate, earlier transfer (**1766-1788**).
xa: **Rayalaseema** was proposed by **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** in **1928**.
It was approved at the **Andhra Mahasabha, Nandyal**.

neec81a3bb6c.s: The Battle of Padmanabham (1794) is associated with:
o: the defeat of Chinna Vijayaramaraju of Vizianagaram by the Company
the cession of the Ceded Districts by the Nizam
the transfer of Guntur Circar to the Company
neec81a3bb6c.x: At Padmanabham (10 July 1794) the Company defeated Chinna Vijayaramaraju of Vizianagaram. The Ceded Districts came in 1800, Conflans was beaten at Chandurti (1758), and Guntur was handed over in 1788.
xs: At **Padmanabham (1794)**, **Chinna Vijayaramaraju** of **Vizianagaram** was defeated — option **(1)**.
The **Ceded Districts** came in **1800**; **Guntur** in **1788**.
xa: The battle was fought on **10 July**.
By **1801** the whole Andhra region was under the Company.

nebdd5ada81c.s: Which region remained under the Nizam, while the Northern Circars and Ceded Districts formed the main territorial basis of present-day Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema?
nebdd5ada81c.x: Telangana remained under the Nizam, whereas the Northern Circars and Ceded Districts together broadly correspond to Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema.
nebdd5ada81c.tq: Use a regional contrast to distinguish Nizam-held territory from ceded Andhra regions.
xs: **Telangana** stayed under the **Nizam** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Northern Circars** and **Ceded Districts** became almost all of **Coastal Andhra** and **Rayalaseema**.
xa: Circars handed over (**1766**): **Mustafanagar (Kondapalli), Eluru, Rajamahendravaram, Srikakulam**; **Guntur** followed in **1788**.
Ceded Districts = **Dattamandalalu**; the name **Rayalaseema** was proposed by **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** in **1928**.
**Nellore and Chittoor** were taken from the Carnatic Nawab in **1801**.

n983bc79beac.s: Kandregula Jogipantulu proposed ₹15 lakh a year for the Circar lease, but the final 1766 treaty fixed it at:
n983bc79beac.x: Jogipantulu proposed ₹15 lakh using the Gollapudi pay mutiny, but the 1766 treaty fixed ₹9 lakh a year.
xa: This is the **APPSC G2 2019** key.
⚠ **₹15 lakh** proposed; **₹9 lakh** final; **₹7 lakh** = Guntur (**1788**).

na8408bcb2a8.s: Which Circar became the principal area of conflict between Nizam Ali and the British?
na8408bcb2a8.x: Guntur Circar was the area of conflict because it was held by Nizam Ali's brother, Basalat Jung. It was the fifth Circar and was also called Kondaveedu or Murtazanagar.
na8408bcb2a8.tq: Apply the specific conflict clue instead of choosing the broader regional term Northern Circars.
xs: The **Guntur Circar** was the area of conflict — option **(1)**.
It was held by the Nizam's brother **Basalat Jung** (APHQ 2011).
Exam angle: the answer is **Guntur Circar**, not the Northern Circars as a whole.
xa: Guntur = **5th Circar**, also **Kondaveedu** / **Murtazanagar**.
Handed over on **18 September 1788** for **₹7 lakh**.

nad89711283b.s: Nizam Ali Khan (Asaf Jah II) shifted the capital of the Nizam's dominions in 1763 from:
nad89711283b.x: Nizam Ali Khan moved the capital from Aurangabad to Hyderabad in 1763. Golconda and Bidar were earlier Deccan sultanate seats, and the move was towards Hyderabad, not away from it.
xs: Nizam Ali Khan moved the capital from **Aurangabad to Hyderabad** (**1763**) — option **(2)**.
Option (4) reverses the direction.
xa: **Secunderabad** cantonment is named after **Sikandar Jah** (Asaf Jah III).

n18c331bd787.s: The Berar Treaty of 1853, concluded during the reign of Nasir-ud-Daula, transferred which territories to the British?
n18c331bd787.x: The Berar Treaty of 1853 gave Berar, Raichur and Osmanabad, also known as Dharashiv, to the British.
n18c331bd787.tq: Test the treaty-territory association against nearby Hyderabad territorial cessions.
xs: The **Berar Treaty 1853** gave **Berar, Raichur and Osmanabad/Dharashiv** to the British — option **(2)**.
It was signed under **Dalhousie**, in **Nasir-ud-Daula**'s reign.
**Kadapa, Kurnool, Bellary** were **Ceded Districts** of **1800**.
xa: **Salar Jung I** became **Diwan** in **1853**.
Nasir-ud-Daula's reign also saw the **Wahabi conspiracy 1839**.

nbeebb34f9c3.s: Which Nizam ruled Hyderabad during the Revolt of 1857 and was given the title “Star of India” for his loyalty?
nbeebb34f9c3.x: Afzal-ud-Daula, or Asaf Jah V, ruled from 1857 to 1869, was the Nizam during the Revolt of 1857 and received the title “Star of India” for his loyalty.
nbeebb34f9c3.tq: Combine the reign period with the associated political event and honour.
xs: **Afzal-ud-Daula (Asaf Jah V)** was Nizam during the **Revolt of 1857** and got "**Star of India**" — option **(1)**.
He ruled **1857-69**; asked in **APPSC G2 2001**.
**Nasir-ud-Daula** died on **16 May 1857**, before the revolt reached Hyderabad.
xa: **17 July 1857**: **Turrebaz Khan** attacked the Residency to free **Chida Khan**.
The attack was **repulsed by Davidson**.

n14ebce44128.s: Salar Jung I served under which of the following three Nizams?
o: Nasir-ud-Daula, Afzal-ud-Daula and Mir Mahbub Ali Khan
Nizam Ali Khan, Sikandar Jah and Nasir-ud-Daula
Sikandar Jah, Afzal-ud-Daula and the last Nizam
Afzal-ud-Daula, Mir Mahbub Ali Khan and Nizam Ali Khan
n14ebce44128.x: Salar Jung I served Nasir-ud-Daula, Afzal-ud-Daula and Mir Mahbub Ali Khan, dying in 1883 during the period of the latter's reign.
n14ebce44128.tq: Use the overlapping reign sequence to identify all three associated rulers.
xs: **Salar Jung I** served **Nasir-ud-Daula, Afzal-ud-Daula and Mahbub Ali Khan** — option **(1)**.
He served until his death in **1883**.
xa: **Mir Turab Ali Khan** was made **Diwan** on **31 May 1853**, after **Siraj-ul-Mulk**'s death.
He took the title **Salar Jung I**.

n2ed0862b35a.s: Which event most directly explains why Lord Wellesley compelled Nizam Ali Khan to accept the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798?
o: The Nizam's alliance with Holkar during the Second Maratha War
The Nizam's refusal to lease the Northern Circars in 1766
The Nizam's defeat by the Marathas at Kharda and his reliance on French troops under Raymond
The Nizam's annexation of Mysore after the Fourth Mysore War
n2ed0862b35a.x: After the defeat at Kharda in 1795, Nizam Ali Khan blamed Sir John Shore's neutrality, dismissed his British battalions and relied on French troops under Raymond. Wellesley used this situation to force the alliance.
n2ed0862b35a.tq: Link the political cause, foreign military influence and British response.
xs: After defeat by the Marathas at **Kharda (1795)**, the Nizam relied on **French troops under Raymond** — option **(3)**.
He blamed **Sir John Shore's neutrality** and **dismissed the British battalions**.
Resident **Kirkpatrick** reported the French battalions → **Wellesley** forced the **1798** alliance.
xa: The Subsidiary Alliance aimed to **keep the French out**.
**Holkar** resisted the system longest; the Nizam did not ally with him.

n74bbde52648.s: Which British Resident reported the presence of French battalions in the Nizam's forces during the 1790s and pressed him into the 1798 alliance?
n74bbde52648.x: Resident James Kirkpatrick reported the Nizam's French battalions in the 1790s and pushed him into the Subsidiary Alliance of 1798.
n74bbde52648.tq: Use the person–action association and distinguish the Resident from the military officer who repulsed the later attack.
xs: **(James) Kirkpatrick** reported the Nizam's French battalions in the **1790s** — option **(3)**.
**Wellesley** then forced the **1798** alliance on the Nizam.
**Calliaud** signed the **1766** treaty; **Davidson** repulsed the **1857** Residency attack.
xa: Kirkpatrick built the Residency, the **"Koti"**.
The French troops were commanded by **Raymond**.

n542e9bd20e6.s: Awadh served as a classic buffer state because it
o: Blocked the advance of the Burmese into Assam
Shielded Bengal from the Marathas and Afghans
Separated Bombay from the Portuguese territories
Protected Madras from French naval attacks
n542e9bd20e6.x: Awadh acted as a buffer protecting Bengal from the Marathas and Afghans.
n542e9bd20e6.tq: Match the buffer state with the frontier threat it was meant to contain.
xs: **Awadh** was the classic buffer state because it **shielded Bengal from the Marathas and Afghans** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was set up as a buffer after **Buxar (1764)** under Warren Hastings' **Ring-fence** policy.
xa: **Warren Hastings** sold **Kora and Allahabad** to the Nawab of Awadh.
Awadh was a Company-protected buffer from **1764-65**; some notes treat the **Treaty of Allahabad (1765)** as the first subsidiary-type treaty — **Shuja-ud-Daulah** accepted a subsidiary force.
Awadh accepted Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance in **Nov 1801**, and was annexed by Dalhousie in **1856** for misgovernment.

n7d81e95188d.s: The Subsidiary Alliance system introduced by Lord Wellesley in 1798 was primarily intended to
o: provide direct British administration at the lowest possible cost
restore the authority of Mughal provincial governors
promote free trade between Indian states and European powers
counter French influence and establish British paramountcy without direct administration
n7d81e95188d.x: Wellesley designed the system to counter French influence and establish British paramountcy without assuming the cost of direct administration.
n7d81e95188d.tq: Identify the stated aim rather than confusing political control with direct annexation.
xs: The aim was to **counter French influence** and **establish British paramountcy** without the cost of **direct administration** — option **(4)**.
Option (1) is the opposite: the system avoided direct administration.
Another aim: maintain a large army **at the Indian states' cost**.
xa: Introduced by **Lord Wellesley**, **1798**.
First state: **Hyderabad (1798)**.

n707299097da.s: Under the Subsidiary Alliance system, which one of the following was NOT a condition imposed on the Indian ruler?
o: Surrender of control over foreign affairs
Permission to employ other Europeans without British approval
Acceptance of a British Resident at the court
Maintenance of a permanent British subsidiary force
n707299097da.x: The ruler could not employ other Europeans without the consent of the Company. Acceptance of a Resident, surrender of foreign affairs and maintenance of the subsidiary force were terms of the alliance.
n707299097da.tq: Find the reversed condition in a NOT question.
xs: The ruler could **not employ other Europeans** without British consent — so option **(2)** was NOT a condition.
Real terms: **foreign policy** surrendered, a **British Resident** at court, a **permanent subsidiary force**.
xa: The ruler **paid for its upkeep**, in cash or by **ceding territory**.
In return the Company **protected the state's borders**.

nb0fc548a430.s: The Rajput states entered into subordinate alliances in 1818 primarily to
o: Secure independence from all external powers
Restore French influence in western India
Obtain protection from the Marathas and Pindaris and accept British paramountcy
nb0fc548a430.x: The alliances aimed to protect the Rajput states from the Marathas and Pindaris, bring them under British paramountcy and isolate them from Maratha powers.
nb0fc548a430.tq: Select the option containing the combined strategic aims rather than one isolated purpose.
xs: The Rajput states accepted the **1818** alliances to get **protection from the Marathas and Pindaris** and came under **British paramountcy** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The treaties also aimed to **isolate** them from the Maratha powers — the opposite of independence from all external powers.
Keeping the **French out** was an aim of Wellesley's **Subsidiary Alliance** (1798), not of the 1818 treaties; **Awadh** was annexed only in **1856**.
xa: States: **Jodhpur, Jaipur, Bundi** + other Rajput states; negotiator **Charles Metcalfe**, under **Lord Hastings** (**1813-23**).
Under paramountcy, states ran internal affairs but had **no external or international life**.
The British stepped in **to give effect to their international commitments** (**APPSC-G2 2017**), and also over succession disputes and misgovernment.

nindian-history-91-12.s: Which policy provided for the annexation of states without a natural male heir?
nindian-history-91-12.x: The Doctrine of Lapse annexed states without a natural male heir.
n: Subsidiary Alliance aimed to bring Indian states under British political control. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
Subsidiary Alliance aimed to bring Indian states under British military control. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
Doctrine of Lapse involved the annexation of states without a natural male heir. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
Blue Water Policy aimed at Portuguese naval supremacy in the Indian Ocean. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
Blue Water Policy aimed at Portuguese trade supremacy in the Indian Ocean. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
Policy of Non-Alignment aimed at maintaining an independent foreign policy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
Policy of Non-Alignment aimed to avoid alignment with power blocs. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
xa: The Blue Water Policy belongs to **Francisco de Almeida**.
States annexed by lapse: **Satara** (**1848**), **Jhansi** (**1853**), **Nagpur** (**1854**).
**Awadh** (**1856**) was annexed for **misgovernment**, not lapse.

n8df2d73a433.s: Under the Subsidiary Alliance, which of the following was a function of the British Resident at Hyderabad?
o: Exercising hereditary succession to the Nizam's throne
Presiding over the Madras Board of Revenue
n8df2d73a433.x: The Resident controlled the Nizam's foreign relations and supervised the subsidiary force; he had no hereditary right to the throne.
xa: Resident **Kirkpatrick** built the Residency building, the **"Koti"**.
On **17 July 1857**, **Turrebaz Khan** attacked the Residency.

n4971cb9fdd7.s: Under the Subsidiary Alliance, if a ruler failed to pay for the subsidiary force, the result was:
o: transfer of the force to a neighbouring state
an increase in the subsidy rate
n4971cb9fdd7.x: The ruler paid in cash or by ceding territory; failure to pay led to territorial cession, not withdrawal of the force.
xa: Example: the Nizam's **Ceded Districts** (**1800**).
Finances were **drained by the subsidy**.

n100de4c3e5e.s: The Nizam's 'Ceded Districts' arose from which consequence of the Subsidiary Alliance?
o: Territorial cession when subsidies were unpaid
Conquest in the Fourth Mysore War
Annexation under the Doctrine of Lapse
n100de4c3e5e.x: The Subsidiary Alliance led to territorial cessions when subsidies were unpaid, such as the Nizam's Ceded Districts.
xa: Neglected government became a later **pretext for annexation**.
**Disbanded soldiers** were left without work.

n24550f643a0.s: Which was the first state to accept the Subsidiary Alliance, in 1798?
n24550f643a0.x: Hyderabad was the first state (1798); Tipu refused it, and Holkar signed only in 1818 as the last Maratha power.
xa: The first state was **Hyderabad (1798)** (APPSC-G1 2004).
Holkar was **the last Maratha** power to accept.

nebcc07662d9.s: Which one of the following groups entered into the Subsidiary Alliance in 1818?
o: Holkar, Bharatpur, Jodhpur, Jaipur and Bundi
Mysore, Tanjore, Awadh, Peshwa and Scindia
Punjab, Awadh, Holkar, Tanjore and Jaitpur
Hyderabad, Berar, Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur
nebcc07662d9.x: Holkar, Bharatpur, Jodhpur, Jaipur and Bundi entered into the arrangement in 1818. Holkar was the last Maratha power to sign it.
nebcc07662d9.tq: Recognise the final group in the alliance chronology and avoid mixing it with earlier signatories.
xs: **Holkar, Bharatpur, Jodhpur, Jaipur and Bundi** came in **1818** — option **(1)**.
**Mysore, Tanjore, Awadh, Peshwa, Scindia** came in **1799-1804**.
xa: The **1818** Rajput treaties were negotiated by **Charles Metcalfe** under **Lord Hastings**.
Aim: protect them from the **Marathas and Pindaris**.

n3d0351cdc9a.s: Who led the attack on the Hyderabad Residency on 17 July 1857 to free Chida Khan?
n3d0351cdc9a.x: Turrebaz Khan attacked the Residency on 17 July 1857 to free Chida Khan; Davidson repulsed the attack.
xa: The Nizam then was **Afzal-ud-Daula**, given "**Star of India**" for loyalty.
The Residency building was called the **"Koti"**.

neafaaf5397f.s: Besides succession disputes and misgovernment, the British justified intervening in princely states' internal affairs by the need to:
neafaaf5397f.x: The British claimed intervention to fulfil their international commitments, and also intervened in succession disputes and misgovernment.
xa: States ran internal affairs but had **no external or international life**.
**Awadh (1856)** was annexed for **misgovernment**.

n32ab88c4f78.s: Who negotiated the 1818 treaties with Jodhpur, Jaipur, Bundi and other Rajput states?
n32ab88c4f78.x: Charles Metcalfe negotiated the treaties with the Rajput states in 1818 under Lord Hastings.
xa: Aims of the Rajput treaties: protect the states from the **Marathas and Pindaris**, bring them under **British paramountcy**, and isolate them from the Maratha powers.
**Holkar**, the last Maratha, also came into the alliance system in **1818**, along with **Bharatpur**.
Subordinate isolation: each state bound **separately** to the paramount Company and cut off from the others.

nd6cec858b4a.s: Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the ground of:
nd6cec858b4a.x: Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the ground of maladministration (Punjab, by contrast, was annexed by conquest).
xa: Punjab's ruler **Duleep Singh** was deposed.
**Punjab annexed 1849** (**APPSC-GS 2012**; the key there was blank, but 1849 is correct).
Awadh's annexation rested on reports by **Sleeman** and **Outram**; **Wajid Ali Shah** lost his throne.

nde90ba7fd5d.s: The proposal to rename Dattamandalalu as Rayalaseema was approved at the Andhra Mahasabha held at Nandyal under the presidency of:
nde90ba7fd5d.x: The Andhra Mahasabha at Nandyal, presided over by Dr S. Radhakrishnan, approved the name Rayalaseema proposed by Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.
nde90ba7fd5d.tq: Use the role distinction between the proposer and the presiding authority.
xs: The Nandyal **Andhra Mahasabha** was presided over by **Dr S. Radhakrishnan** — option **(4)**.
**Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** **proposed** the name **Rayalaseema** (**1928**), but did not preside.
xa: Earlier name: **Dattamandalalu** (Ceded Districts).
Districts: **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary**.

n2ed332605df.s: The expression “breakwaters to the storm” was used in relation to the princes under the policy of
n2ed332605df.x: After 1858, the princes were described as “breakwaters to the storm” under the policy of subordinate union.
n2ed332605df.tq: Match the distinctive phrase with the later policy rather than the earlier annexation policies.
xs: After **1858**, under **subordinate union**, the princes were called the "**breakwaters to the storm**" — so option **(4)** is correct.
Subordinate union came through the **Crown** (**Queen's Proclamation**): annexation stopped, the **right of adoption** was recognised and borders were guaranteed.
**Doctrine of Lapse** was **Dalhousie's** (1848) and **Ring-fence** was **Warren Hastings'** — both belong to the Company era, before 1858.
xa: Policy sequence: **Ring-fence** (Warren Hastings) → **Subsidiary Alliance** (Wellesley, **1798**) → **Subordinate isolation** (Lord Hastings, **1813-23**) → **Doctrine of Lapse** (Dalhousie, **1848**) → **Subordinate union** (Crown, after 1858).
Lapse annexations and the Awadh takeover turned rulers, **taluqdars** and sepoys against the Company → policy abandoned after **1857**.
⚠ **Warren Hastings** = ring-fence; **Lord Hastings** = subordinate isolation.

nd833588fa1d.s: The Ring-fence policy of Warren Hastings was intended to
o: Protect the Company's frontiers by defending neighbouring states
Annex every state without a natural male heir
Transfer Indian territories to the French
End all relations with princely states
nd833588fa1d.x: The Ring-fence policy sought to guard the Company's own frontiers by defending the borders of neighbouring states.
nd833588fa1d.tq: Infer the policy objective from the frontier-protection scenario.
xs: **Warren Hastings'** **Ring-fence** policy aimed to **protect the Company's frontiers by defending the borders of neighbouring states** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Annexing states without a natural heir was **Dalhousie's** **Doctrine of Lapse** (**1848**), a different policy.
xa: **Awadh** was the classic buffer: set up after **Buxar (1764)**; it shielded **Bengal** from the **Marathas** and the **Afghans**.
Hastings sold **Kora and Allahabad** to the Nawab of Awadh to keep the buffer strong.
⚠ **Warren Hastings** = ring-fence; **Lord Hastings** = subordinate isolation (**1813-23**).

n031e989c6f7.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of states annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse?
n031e989c6f7.x: Satara, Jaitpur, Sambalpur and Jhansi were all annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse.
n031e989c6f7.tq: Separate the lapse cases from conquest, misgovernment and revenue-related cases.
xs: **Satara, Jaitpur, Sambalpur, Jhansi** were all taken by **lapse** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Punjab** and **Lower Burma** were taken by **conquest**, and **Berar** from the Nizam for **arrears** — option 1 fails.
**Awadh** was annexed for **misgovernment**; for **Tanjore** and the **Carnatic** only titles and pensions were abolished — option 2 fails.
**Sindh (1843)** and **Punjab (1849)** were **conquests** — option 4 fails.
xa: Lapse dates: **Satara 1848**, **Jaitpur 1849**, **Sambalpur 1849**, **Baghat 1850**, **Udaipur 1852**, **Jhansi 1853**, **Nagpur 1854**.
**UPPSC 2025** key: **Karnataka (Carnatic)** was not a lapse case.

nbd721aace22.s: Which of the following states was annexed on the ground of maladministration, rather than under the Doctrine of Lapse?
nbd721aace22.x: Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the ground of maladministration, based on Outram's reports. Nagpur, Jhansi and Sambalpur were annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse.
nbd721aace22.tq: Find the exception by separating policy-based annexations from administrative grounds.
xs: **Awadh** was annexed in **1856** for **maladministration** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The ground rested on reports by Residents **Sleeman** and **Outram**; the ruler dispossessed was **Wajid Ali Shah**.
**Sambalpur (1849)**, **Jhansi (1853)** and **Nagpur (1854)** were all **lapse** annexations.
xa: Other non-lapse cases: **Punjab** and **Lower Burma** by conquest; titles and pensions abolished for **Tanjore** and the **Carnatic**.
The Awadh takeover turned **taluqdars** and sepoys against the Company before **1857**.
Earlier, Awadh was Warren Hastings' classic **buffer** state, shielding Bengal.

n9aec15cb913.s: Subordinate isolation is associated with the administration of
n9aec15cb913.x: Lord Hastings pursued subordinate isolation during 1813–1823, binding each princely state separately to the paramount Company.
n9aec15cb913.tq: Discriminate between the similarly named Hastings and the other policy-makers.
xs: **Subordinate isolation** belongs to **Lord Hastings** (**1813-23**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Warren Hastings** = **Ring-fence**; **Lord Wellesley** = **Subsidiary Alliance (1798)**; **Lord Dalhousie** = **Doctrine of Lapse (1848)**.
xa: Under subordinate isolation each state was bound **separately** to the paramount Company and cut off from the others.
Its showpiece: the **1818** treaties with **Jodhpur, Jaipur, Bundi**, negotiated by **Charles Metcalfe**.
⚠ **Warren Hastings** and **Lord Hastings** are different men — a frequent trap.

na826683ab9f.s: Lord Dalhousie's policy of annexing states whose rulers died without a natural heir is known as the:
na826683ab9f.x: Dalhousie's annexation policy (from 1848) is the Doctrine of Lapse (APPSC-GS 2018 key). Ring-fence was Warren Hastings', the Subsidiary Alliance Wellesley's (1798), and subordinate isolation Lord Hastings'.
xs: Annexing states whose rulers died without a natural heir = **Doctrine of Lapse** (Dalhousie, **1848**) — so option **(3)** is correct (**APPSC-GS 2018** key).
**Ring-fence** = **Warren Hastings**; **Subsidiary Alliance** = **Wellesley (1798)**; **Subordinate isolation** = **Lord Hastings**.
xa: Lapse states: **Satara, Jaitpur, Udaipur, Sambalpur, Nagpur, Baghat, Jhansi**.
Not lapse: **Punjab** and **Lower Burma** (conquest), **Awadh** (misgovernment), **Berar** (arrears).
**APPSC-G1 2024**: of Awadh, Jhansi, Satara, Nagpur, Sindh → only **Jhansi, Satara, Nagpur** by lapse.

n163e4413fdd.s: The lapse annexations and the takeover of Awadh contributed to the Revolt of 1857 because they alienated
n163e4413fdd.x: The annexations and Awadh takeover turned rulers, taluqdars and sepoys against the Company, contributing to the revolt.
n163e4413fdd.tq: Connect a political policy with its stated social and military reaction.
xs: The **lapse** annexations and the **Awadh** takeover turned **rulers, taluqdars and sepoys** against the Company — so option **(2)** is correct.
As a result the policy was **abandoned after 1857**.
xa: After **1858**, annexation stopped and the **right of adoption** was recognised (subordinate union).
**Awadh (1856)** was annexed for **misgovernment**; its Nawab **Wajid Ali Shah** was dispossessed.
At **Hyderabad** in **1857**, **Turrebaz Khan** attacked the Residency on **17 July** to free **Chida Khan**; repulsed by **Davidson**.

nindian-history-91-18.s: The Doctrine of Lapse is associated with:
nindian-history-91-18.x: The Doctrine of Lapse belongs to Dalhousie, not Warren Hastings.
n: Dhamma Policy is associated with Ashoka. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
Blood and Iron Policy is associated with Balban. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
Doctrine of Lapse is associated with Lord Dalhousie. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
Policy of Non-Alignment is associated with Jawaharlal Nehru. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #91 · pp 173-174]
xa: Dhamma aimed at **welfare** and **religious tolerance**.
Blood and Iron aimed to **suppress rebellion**.
**Lord Hastings** (**1813-23**) = **subordinate isolation**.

n3bc853063e1.s: Which of the following was one of the five traditional Circars of the Northern Circars?
n3bc853063e1.x: The five Circars were Chicacole, Rajahmundry, Ellore, Mustafanagar and Guntur; Masulipatnam was a Company station, not a Circar.
xa: Modern districts of the Circars: **Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, East and West Godavari, Krishna + Guntur**.
**Guntur** was the last Circar to pass to the Company, in **1788**, for **7 lakh**.
Krishna district had its HQ at **Machilipatnam**.

n5c8fd3adae6.s: The annual payment obtained through Kandregula Jogipantulu's negotiations for the lease of the Circars was:
n5c8fd3adae6.x: Jogipantulu used the Gollapudi mutiny to get the Circars leased to the Company for 15 lakh rupees a year (1766). 9 lakh is the reduced peshkash of the 1768 Treaty of Masulipatnam, and 7 lakh the Guntur payment of 1788.
n5c8fd3adae6.tq: Distinguish the lease payment from the later reduced peshkash and the Guntur payment.
xs: **Jogipantulu** got the Circars leased to the Company for **15 lakh rupees** a year — option **(2)**.
**9 lakh** was the reduced peshkash of the **1768 Treaty of Masulipatnam**; **7 lakh** was paid for **Guntur (1788)**.
xa: He exploited the **Gollapudi** mutiny of the Nizam's army over unpaid pay, while the Nizam was at **Rajamahendravaram**.
Jogipantulu was a famous **dubashi** (interpreter-negotiator), respected by Diwan **Ruknudaula**.
**Salabat Jung's** grant (**1759**) had earlier given **Machilipatnam** and nearby parganas to the British.

o: a dubashi and envoy between the Nizam's court and the Company
the first Collector of the Ceded Districts
a poligar who resisted the Company in Rayalaseema
the zamindar of Vizianagaram defeated at Padmanabham
n8dfbf4cc36c.x: Kandregula Jogipantulu was a prominent dubashi and envoy between the Nizam's court and the Company's men at Machilipatnam.
xa: He was respected by the Nizam's Diwan **Ruknudaula** (**APPSC 2019**).
He negotiated the Circar lease at **15 lakh rupees** a year.
⚠ Collectors who knew no Telugu depended on corrupt **dubashis** — a standing criticism.

n429eac2c0fc.s: In the Bobbili War (1757), Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram took the help of:
n429eac2c0fc.x: Vijayarama Raju took French help through Bussy during the Bobbili War of 1757.
xa: Ranga Rao's brother-in-law **Tandra Papayya** later killed Vijayaramaraju.
**Bobbili** = **Velama** family; **Vizianagaram** = **Pusapati** — rivals.
⚠ **Vijayaramaraju** = Bobbili 1757; **Chinna Vijayaramaraju** = Padmanabham 1794.

n560185d25d3.s: Which of the following communities formed the hereditary zamindari families of the Northern Circars?
n560185d25d3.x: The hereditary zamindari families of the Northern Circars included Velamas, Reddis and Kshatriya Rajus.
n560185d25d3.tq: Recall the exact social composition of the regional zamindari houses.
xs: The hereditary zamindari families were **Velamas, Reddis and Kshatriya Rajus** — option **(4)**.
Their heartland was the **Northern Circars**.
xa: **Bobbili** and **Venkatagiri** = Velama; **Vizianagaram** = **Pusapati**; **Peddapuram** = **Vatsavayi**.
Before **1802** zamindaris were given by **auction**.
Peshkash = tribute zamindars paid to the British; **Korunu** = what they collected from farmers.

n0ebbb9fe44e.s: In the aftermath of the Battle of Bobbili (1757), who killed Vijayaramaraju of Vizianagaram?
n0ebbb9fe44e.x: Tandra Papayya, brother-in-law of Bobbili Ranga Rao, later killed Vijayaramaraju to avenge the destruction of Bobbili. Bussy led the French who fought alongside Vijayaramaraju. Ranga Rao himself was killed in the battle. George Russell took charge of the Vizianagaram forts after Padmanabham in 1794.
n0ebbb9fe44e.tq: Ranga Rao killed; Papayya took revenge.
xs: **Tandra Papayya**, brother-in-law of **Bobbili Ranga Rao**, killed **Vijayaramaraju** after the battle — option **(3)**.
**Ranga Rao** himself was killed at Bobbili; **Bussy** was Vijayaramaraju's French ally; **George Russell** took the forts after **1794**.
xa: Battle date: **24 Jan 1757**.
**Bobbili** = **Velama** estate; **Vizianagaram** = **Pusapati**.

nbfde8881932.s: The Nizam ceded the 'Ceded Districts' to the British in:
nbfde8881932.x: The Nizam ceded them in 1800 because he could not pay the Subsidiary Alliance subsidy in cash.
xa: Districts: **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary**.
First Principal Collector: **Sir Thomas Munro**, with four sub-collectors at **Harpanahalli, Kadapa, Adoni, Kurnool**.

n361b5e78835.s: Which of the following was a major consequence associated with the Ryotwari system in the Andhra region?
o: Abolition of direct contact between cultivator and government
Over-assessment, indebtedness to moneylenders and land alienation
Fixed revenue payable only by zamindars
n361b5e78835.x: Ryotwari areas experienced heavy assessment, often exceeding 50 percent of the produce, along with dependence on moneylenders and alienation of land.
n361b5e78835.tq: Link the revenue arrangement with its stated economic consequences.
xs: **Ryotwari** brought **over-assessment** (often **50%+** of produce), **moneylenders** and **land alienation** — option **(2)**.
Ryotwari was settled with the **ryot directly** — it did not abolish that contact or work through zamindars.
xa: First region: **Baramahal (1792)** under **Captain Alexander Read** with **Munro**.
In Andhra it began in the **Ceded Districts in 1802**; extended across Madras in **1820**.
Zamindari's effect: absentee landlordism, impoverished tenants.

nb3bfc1a3b7a.s: Which of the following correctly represents the regional distribution of Zamindari and Ryotwari in Andhra?
o: Zamindari in the Northern Circars and Ryotwari in Rayalaseema, later extending to most of Andhra
Zamindari in Rayalaseema and Ryotwari in the Northern Circars
Ryotwari in the Northern Circars and Zamindari in the Ceded Districts
Both Zamindari and Ryotwari were confined to Nellore
nb3bfc1a3b7a.x: Zamindari prevailed in the Northern Circars, while Ryotwari was associated with Rayalaseema and later covered most of Andhra.
nb3bfc1a3b7a.tq: Use the AP regional contrast as the decisive clue.
xs: **Zamindari** in the **Northern Circars**; **Ryotwari** in **Rayalaseema**, later most of Andhra — option **(1)**.
Circar estates: **Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram**; Ryotwari began in the **Ceded Districts in 1802**.
xa: **Mahalwari** is placed in **Nellore**.
Zamindari settled with the zamindar (intermediary); Ryotwari with the ryot directly.
Effects: zamindari → absentee landlordism; ryotwari → over-assessment, moneylenders.

na05e849bf4b.s: The Permanent Settlement, introduced by Cornwallis in 1793, was applied to the Andhra zamindaris in:
na05e849bf4b.x: It was applied in Andhra in 1802, replacing the earlier auction of zamindaris with a fixed demand. 1794 is when the Collector system began. 1800 is the cession of the Ceded Districts. 1820 is when Ryotwari was extended across Madras under Munro.
xs: The **Permanent Settlement** (**Cornwallis**, **1793**) was applied in Andhra in **1802** — option **(3)**.
**1802** is also when **Ryotwari** began in the **Ceded Districts**.
xa: Before **1802**, zamindaris were given by **auction**.
**1794** = Collector system; **1800** = Ceded Districts; **1820** = Ryotwari across Madras.

n6f6605cceb9.s: The Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam was concluded in:
n6f6605cceb9.x: The Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam came in 1798, after the Treaty of Masulipatnam (1768), the Guntur handover (1788) and Padmanabham (1794).
xa: **1800**: Ceded Districts; **1801**: Nellore and Chittoor.
Masulipatnam (**1768**) fixed a **peshkash of 9 lakh** plus military help to the Nizam.

n9bd44af3ade.s: The Battle of Padmanabham was fought in:
n9bd44af3ade.x: The Battle of Padmanabham was fought in 1794.
xa: **1794** also saw the **Collector system** begin.
**1801**: Andhra merged into the **Madras Presidency**.
**1808**: Ceded Districts split into **Bellary and Cuddapah**.

n79b85f088ce.s: Zamindari was abolished in the Madras Presidency in:
n79b85f088ce.x: Zamindari in Madras was abolished in 1948, after Guntur (1788), Padmanabham (1794) and the extension of Ryotwari (1820).
xa: The 1948 Act came into force on **7 Sep 1949**.
Ryotwari was extended across Madras under Governor **Munro**.

n490ac31d469.s: During the early administration of the Northern Circars, collectors relied on which intermediaries?
n490ac31d469.x: Collectors relied on dubashis for administrative and local assistance. Munro and C.P. Brown were noted as rare Company officials who learned Telugu.
n490ac31d469.tq: Identify the local intermediary rather than the formal revenue officer.
xs: Collectors who did not know Telugu depended on corrupt **dubashis** — option **(2)**.
**Munro** and **Brown** were the exceptions — rare Telugu learners; Munro needed no interpreters.
xa: The famous dubashi **Kandregula Jogipantulu** negotiated the Circar lease.
The **District Collector** held revenue, magisterial and police powers.

n30a7ae4d76e.s: Which of the following are present-day silk hubs of Rayalaseema?
n30a7ae4d76e.x: Dharmavaram and Madanapalle are present-day silk hubs; sericulture was promoted by the British in the Ceded Districts in the late 19th-early 20th centuries.
xa: Ceded Districts = **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur, Bellary**.
Name **Rayalaseema** adopted in **1928**.

n0a445c739c1.s: Which of the following came under Company rule last?
n0a445c739c1.x: The Circars came in 1766, Guntur in 1788, the Ceded Districts in 1800 and Nellore-Chittoor last, in 1801.
xa: The Circars and Ceded Districts came from the Nizam; **Nellore-Chittoor** from the **Carnatic**.
**Telangana** stayed under the Nizam.

n3677bee87bb.s: The growing divergence between the fertile and educated Circars and the arid and neglected Ceded Districts later influenced debates surrounding the:
n3677bee87bb.x: The contrasting development of the Circars and the Ceded Districts later shaped the Sri Bagh Pact debate. The other pacts belong to different political contexts.
n3677bee87bb.tq: Link a regional socio-economic contrast with the agreement it later influenced.
xs: The divergence between the **fertile, educated Circars** and the **arid, neglected Ceded Districts** later shaped the **Sri Bagh Pact** debate — option **(2)**.
The Circars came to the Company in **1766**; the Ceded Districts only in **1800**, and they grew apart under British rule.
xa: Ceded Districts = today's **Rayalaseema**; name adopted at **Nandyal, 1928**.
The Circars correspond to **Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, East and West Godavari, Krishna + Guntur**.

na842d1872c7.s: The firman relating to the Mughal grant of the Northern Circars was secured by Robert Clive from which Mughal emperor?
na842d1872c7.x: Robert Clive secured the firman from Shah Alam II; the firman is dated 1765 in the detailed chronology.
na842d1872c7.tq: Use the ruler–document association to avoid confusing Mughal emperors.
xs: **Robert Clive** secured the firman from **Shah Alam II** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The firman is dated **1765** (some notes: **1766**).
xa: The **Nizam** at first refused it → the Company negotiated a **lease** from him in **1766**.
**Treaty of Masulipatnam (1768)**: Company kept the Circars for a reduced **peshkash of 9 lakh** a year + military help.
⚠ Trap: the **1753** grant to the French was not a Mughal grant; **Forde**'s campaign was **1758-59**.

nf40fce76f7d.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the territories included in the Ceded Districts in 1800?
nf40fce76f7d.x: The Ceded Districts comprised Kadapa, Kurnool and Anantapur in present-day Andhra Pradesh, together with Bellary, now in Karnataka.
nf40fce76f7d.tq: Check membership in a historically defined regional group.
xs: The **Ceded Districts (1800)** = **Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary** — option **(1)**.
**Nellore** and **Chittoor** came from the **Carnatic** in **1801**; **Guntur** and **Krishna** were Circar lands.
xa: **Bellary** is now in **Karnataka**; the rest form today's **Rayalaseema** (**APPSC GS 2024**).
Old name: **Dattamandalam / Dattamandalalu**; **Rayalaseema** adopted at **Nandyal, 1928**.
Ceded in lieu of the **Subsidiary Alliance** subsidy.

n283a89c12d4.s: The name 'Rayalaseema' for the Ceded Districts was suggested by:
n283a89c12d4.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao suggested the name, which was adopted at the Andhra Mahasabha at Nandyal in 1928 (APPSC G2 2012 key). Jogipantulu was a dubashi in the Circar lease of 1766. Munro was the first Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts. C.P. Brown was a Telugu scholar.
xs: **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** suggested **Rayalaseema** — option **(1)** (**APPSC G2 2012** key).
**Jogipantulu** was the dubashi of the Circar lease; **Munro** was the first Principal Collector; **C.P. Brown** published **Vemana**.
xa: Adopted at the **Andhra Mahasabha, Nandyal, 1928**, under **S. Radhakrishnan**.
Earlier name: **Dattamandalalu**.
⚠ Other notes credit **Chilukuri Narayana Rao**.

n75c2d3b6e6f.s: After the Second Carnatic War, the British installed whom as the Nawab of the Carnatic?
n75c2d3b6e6f.x: After the Second Carnatic War, the British installed Muhammad Ali as Nawab of the Carnatic, though his position became secure only after 1763.
n75c2d3b6e6f.tq: Distinguish the ruler installed after the war from the later Nawab who signed the treaty.
xs: The British installed **Muhammad Ali** as Nawab after the **Second Carnatic War** — option **(1)**.
His position was secure only after **1763**.
xa: He was shielded from **Najibullah** of Nellore, the **Marathas** and **Hyder Ali**.
After his death, the Carnatic districts were annexed in **1801**.
⚠ **Azim-ud-Daula** signed the **Carnatic Treaty**; Muhammad Ali was the one installed.

ne70be36bffb.s: Who became the first Collector of the Ceded Districts in 1800?
ne70be36bffb.x: Thomas Munro became the first Collector of the Ceded Districts in 1800, with sub-collectors stationed at Harpanahalli, Kadapa, Adoni and Kurnool.
ne70be36bffb.tq: Identify the official associated with the first administrative appointment.
xs: **Sir Thomas Munro** became the **first Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts** in **1800** — option **(1)**.
**Arthur Cotton** was an irrigation engineer; **C.P. Brown** a Telugu scholar; **George Russell** took the Vizianagaram forts after **1794**.
xa: Munro had **four sub-collectors** at **Harpanahalli, Kadapa, Adoni, Kurnool**.
⚠ Some notes say "first Collector … in **1802**" (CDX).
He suppressed the **palegars**, introduced **Ryotwari**, and died at **Pattikonda** on **6 July 1827**.

n54d0b5f9748.s: Which work is associated with C.P. Brown?
o: The construction of the Krishna anicut
Publication of Vemana’s verses and a Telugu-English dictionary
A survey of the Ceded Districts from 1802 to 1807
Suppression of the palegars of Rayalaseema
n54d0b5f9748.x: C.P. Brown studied Telugu thoroughly and published Vemana’s verses as well as a Telugu-English dictionary.
n54d0b5f9748.tq: Match the scholar with his literary contribution.
xs: **C.P. Brown** published **Vemana**'s verses and a **Telugu-English dictionary** — option **(2)**.
The **Krishna anicut** was **Cotton's**; the **1802-07** survey and the suppression of **palegars** were **Munro's**.
xa: Brown studied Telugu thoroughly; with **Munro**, a rare Telugu-learning official.
⚠ **Brown** = Vemana; **Cotton** = anicuts.

nap-history-10-4.s: Which Andhra officer helped Sir Arthur Cotton build the Godavari barrage?
nap-history-10-4.x: Veneti (Veenam) Veeranna helped Cotton build the Godavari barrage; G.N. Taylor opened Anglo-vernacular schools at Rajahmundry.
n: The ancient and medieval Pradvivaka was an advisor to the king in judiciary. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 15-16]
Reddy Srinatha served as an educational officer in the court of Pedakomati Vema Reddy. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 15-16]
G. N. Taylor was the Sub-Collector of Rajahmundry. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 15-16]
G. N. Taylor opened Anglo-vernacular schools. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 15-16]
V. Veeranna was an Andhra officer who helped Sir Arthur Cotton in the construction of the Godavari Barrage. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 15-16]
xa: Cotton's assistant was **Veenam Veeranna** (APPSC G2 **2019**).
**C.P. Brown** published **Vemana**'s verses.
**Sir Thomas Munro** was the first Principal Collector of the **Ceded Districts**.

nb0e861e974e.s: After Chinna Vijayarama Raju's defeat at Padmanabham (1794), who was placed over Vizianagaram's forts?
nb0e861e974e.x: After the defeat, the minor son Narayana Babu was made zamindar and George Russell was placed in charge of Vizianagaram's forts.
xa: The British defeated and killed **Chinna Vijayaramaraju** on **10 July 1794**.
**Vizianagaram** (Pusapati) later became a Northern Circars zamindari under the **Permanent Settlement (1802)**.
**Gajapati Vijayarama** belonged to the Vizianagaram kingdom (**APPSC GS 2022**).

ne4f6e01768f.s: Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram were estates under the ____ system.
ne4f6e01768f.x: Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram were Zamindari estates; Ryotwari dealt directly with the ryot.
xa: Ryotwari began in **Rayalaseema** and later spread to most of Coastal Andhra.
Zamindari abolished by the **Madras Estates Act, 1948**.

n9c916e396a9.s: An important effect of the Zamindari system in the Northern Circars was:
o: uniform assessment limited to one-fourth of the produce
transfer of all land rights to village headmen
absentee landlordism and impoverishment of tenants
n9c916e396a9.x: The Zamindari system encouraged absentee landlordism and impoverished tenants.
xa: Estates: **Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram**, under the **Permanent Settlement (1802)**.
Ryotwari's effect, by contrast: **over-assessment** (often **50%+** of produce), moneylenders and land alienation.
Abolished by the **Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948**.

n0bcb4db64e6.s: Under Company revenue administration, the officer at the taluk level was the:
n0bcb4db64e6.x: The Board of Revenue was at state level, the Collector at district, the Tahsildar at taluk and the Karanam and Munsab at village level.
xa: Division: **Sub-Collector / Revenue Officer**; Firka: **Deputy Tahsildar / Firka Revenue Inspector**.
Karanam and Munsab were **hereditary** village officers.
The **Madras Board of Revenue** dates from **1786**.

nac910501cf5.s: The Zilla or District Court functioned under a District Judge. The post of District Judge was created by the:
nac910501cf5.x: The post of District Judge was created under the Cornwallis Code of 1793. The Madras Regulations of 1816 related chiefly to Munsiff and Panchayat courts.
nac910501cf5.tq: Use the legislation–office association and reject neighbouring judicial enactments.
xs: The **District Judge** post was created by the **Cornwallis Code, 1793** — option **(1)**.
The **Madras District Police Act** came in **1859**; the **Madras Regulations of 1816** set up **Munsiff** and **Panchayat** courts.
xa: District courts were also called **Zilla** courts.
After the **1816** separation, civil justice stayed with the District Judge.

nfe17e1c270f.s: The introduction of British judicial procedure in place of village panchayats was criticised mainly because it:
o: was slow and costly and contributed to litigation and debt
made justice quicker and less expensive
reduced litigation and eliminated rural debt
transferred all judicial powers to hereditary village officers
nfe17e1c270f.x: British judicial procedure displaced village panchayats and was criticised as slow and costly. It increased litigation and contributed to indebtedness.
nfe17e1c270f.tq: Select the option that combines all the stated consequences without reversing the criticism.
xs: British procedure was **slow and costly** and fed **litigation and debt**, displacing village panchayats — option **(1)**.
It did not make justice quicker or cheaper, nor reduce rural debt.
xa: **Munro**'s **1816** Regulations set up **Munsiff** and **Panchayat** courts as courts of first instance.
Village officials handled **petty thefts**.
The **District Collector** became the pivot of British rule and ended village autonomy.

o: The share of revenue paid by zamindars to the British
Revenue collected by zamindars from farmers
n9fa2b8d596e.x: Peshkash was the share of revenue paid by zamindars to the British.
n9fa2b8d596e.tq: Discriminate among closely related colonial revenue terms.
xs: **Peshkash** = the share of revenue / tribute **zamindars paid to the British** — option **(2)**.
**Haveli lands** = land under direct British control; **Korunu** = revenue zamindars collected from farmers; **Moturpha** = tax on looms.
xa: **APP** spells it "**peshcush**"; "Peshcush is the revenue collected from zamindars" is true (**PYQ 2025**).
Zamindari lands: **9/10** of estimated revenue to government, **1/10** to the zamindar.
⚠ "**Moturpha** is a salt tax" is false — it was a **tax on looms** (**APPSC G2 2011**).

nd3bf52aee5c.s: Haveli lands in coastal Andhra were lands:
o: Assigned to the Nizam as military grants
nd3bf52aee5c.x: Haveli lands were under the direct control of the British in coastal Andhra.
nd3bf52aee5c.tq: Identify the exact ownership or control category.
xs: **Haveli lands** were lands **held directly under British control** in coastal Andhra — option **(3)**.
Lands held by zamindars were **zamindari lands**, a separate category.
xa: Zamindari lands: **9/10** of estimated revenue to government, **1/10** to the zamindar; agreements ran for **10** years.
**Peshkash** = tribute zamindars paid to the British; **Korunu** = revenue zamindars collected from farmers.
⚠ **Peshkash** = zamindar → British; **Korunu** = farmer → zamindar.

o: a tax on looms and occupations
inland transit and customs duties on goods
n42f83d81a0a.x: Sayer was the inland transit and customs duty; Abkari was excise on liquor and Moturpha a tax on looms and trades.
xa: The Madras Native Association's **1861** petition complained about Moturpha.
⚠ **Peshkash** = zamindar → British; **Korunu** = farmer → zamindar.
**Haveli lands** = under **direct British control** in coastal Andhra.

n0fd23889ddc.s: The Indian Penal Code was enacted in:
n0fd23889ddc.x: The IPC dates to 1860; the CPC to 1859 and the CrPC to 1861.
xa: **Madras District Police Act** — also **1859**.
Criticism: slow, costly British procedure displaced village **panchayats** → litigation and debt.

n72801583fd4.s: Thomas Munro was President of the Judicial Commission constituted in:
n72801583fd4.x: Munro presided over the Judicial Commission of 1814; its report was submitted in April 1816 and largely accepted.
xa: Result: the **Madras Regulations of 1816** — Munsiff and Panchayat courts.
**1818**: magistrates got powers to punish.

n79d60a84705.s: The Madras Regulations of 1816 provided for:
o: Abolition of all village-level judicial institutions
Munsiff and Panchayat courts as courts of first instance
Transfer of civil justice from District Judges to Collectors
Creation of the Madras High Court
n79d60a84705.x: The Madras Regulations of 1816 established Munsiff courts and Panchayat courts in every large village and district as courts of first instance.
n79d60a84705.tq: Match the regulation with its immediate institutional reform.
xs: The **Madras Regulations of 1816** set up **Munsiff and Panchayat courts** as **courts of first instance** — option **(2)**.
They strengthened, not abolished, village-level justice: village officials handled **petty thefts**.
xa: Panchayat courts were set up in every large village and district.
Same year (**1816**): Collectors lost judicial powers; civil justice stayed with **District Judges**.
Munro (**1816**) moved **police supervision** from judges to **Collectors**.

nd4e10f24e73.s: Who created thanas under the supervision of darogas in the early British police administration?
nd4e10f24e73.x: Cornwallis created thanas under darogas, who were Indian officers assisted by constables. Darogas were criticised for abusing their power.
nd4e10f24e73.tq: Use the founder–institution association and avoid swapping judicial and police reformers.
xs: **Lord Cornwallis** created **thanas** under **darogas** (Indian officers) with constables — option **(4)**.
Darogas were known for **abuse of power**.
xa: In **Madras**, village watchmen were supplemented by central police under a **District Superintendent**.
**Munro (1816)** moved police supervision from judges to **Collectors**.
**Madras District Police Act**: **1859**.

n76d0e3c9062.s: Munro's police reforms of 1816 transferred police supervision from:
o: Darogas to the Board of Revenue
n76d0e3c9062.x: Munro's changes in 1816 transferred police supervision from judges to Collectors. This was part of the reorganisation of administrative powers.
n76d0e3c9062.tq: Test the direction of transfer by identifying both the former and new authority.
xs: **Munro**'s **1816** reform moved police supervision **from judges to Collectors** — option **(1)**.
**Darogas** belonged to **Cornwallis'** thana system; the **District Superintendent** headed the central police.
xa: Munro presided over the **Judicial Commission (1814)**; report **April 1816**.
Under ryotwari, some magisterial powers returned to Collectors.
The Collector combined **revenue + magisterial + police** powers — the pivot of British rule.

n2a6b5537f74.s: A Supreme Court plea seeking a separate revenue judicial service cadre, since revenue officers lack legal training to decide land-title disputes, invoked:
n2a6b5537f74.x: The plea invoked Article 14; the Supreme Court issued notice on it.
xa: After **1816**, civil justice stayed with the **District Judge**, apart from the Collector.
The **Andhra Board of Revenue** was formed in **1953**.

n44337136ef5.s: The Circuit Committee, while examining revenue administration in the Andhra region, recommended which of the following?
o: Replacement of ryotwari by permanent settlement
Abolition of the auction system of revenue collection
Continuation of the auction system with higher minimum bids
Transfer of revenue collection entirely to village panchayats
n44337136ef5.x: The Circuit Committee recommended against the highest-bidder auction system because it harmed both the government and the ryots. Munro subsequently abolished auctions in Rayalaseema.
n44337136ef5.tq: Identify the recommendation by linking the committee with the administrative problem it addressed.
xs: The **Circuit Committee** recommended **against the auction (highest-bidder) system** — option **(2)**.
Auctions hurt both the government and the **ryots**.
xa: **Munro** then abolished auctions in **Rayalaseema**.
Before **1802**, zamindaris were given by **auction**; the **Permanent Settlement** replaced auctions with a fixed demand.

n703177a5849.s: In the Madras Presidency, the Collector's administration was introduced in place of the Revenue Board in the year:
n703177a5849.x: The APPSC Group 2 (2012) key gives 1786, the year the Madras Board of Revenue was set up. 1766 is the Circar lease. 1802 is when the Permanent Settlement and Ryotwari were applied in Andhra. 1816 is when Collectors lost their judicial powers.
n703177a5849.tq: PYQ wording 'Collector in place of Revenue Board' = 1786.
xs: In the PYQ wording, the Collector's administration replaced the Revenue Board in **1786** — option **(2)** (**APPSC G2 2012** key).
The notes date the **Collector system** in coastal Andhra to **1794**; for this exact wording, answer **1786**.
xa: **1786** is also the year of the **Madras Board of Revenue**.
**1816**: Collectors lost judicial powers.
**1802**: Permanent Settlement in Andhra; Ryotwari in the Ceded Districts.

nc85a83b9789.s: Chittoor district was carved out, giving Kadapa its present area, in the year:
nc85a83b9789.x: Chittoor was carved out in 1911, which gave Kadapa its present area. 1858 is when Kurnool district was created, 1882 Anantapur, and 1904 Guntur and East Godavari.
xs: **Chittoor** was carved out in **1911**, giving **Kadapa** its present area — option **(4)**.
**1858** = Kurnool; **1882** = Anantapur; **1904** = Guntur and East Godavari.
xa: **West Godavari** followed in **1925**.
Chittoor and Nellore had been taken from the Carnatic in **1801**.

n06ce72f4c17.s: After Crown rule, Rajahmundry and Machilipatnam were reorganised into Godavari and Krishna districts in:
n06ce72f4c17.x: In 1859, Rajahmundry and Machilipatnam were reorganised into Godavari and Krishna districts respectively.
n06ce72f4c17.tq: Test the chronology of district renaming and reorganisation.
xs: In **1859** (Crown rule), **Rajahmundry** and **Machilipatnam** were reorganised into **Godavari** and **Krishna** districts — option **(3)**.
**1802** was the union of Rajahmundry and **Kakinada** collectorates; **1904** was Guntur and East Godavari.
xa: The new names were given on the suggestion of **Cotton**.
**West Godavari** followed in **1925**.
⚠ **1904** = Guntur + East Godavari; **1925** = West Godavari; **1859** = Godavari + Krishna.

nb5dcd88dfd3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Dowleswaram anicut?
o: Arthur Cotton reported to the Board of Revenue on it in 1844.
Its Indian assistant Veenam Veeranna was made Rao Bahadur and Assistant Engineer.
Work on it began in 1847 and its main work was completed in April 1852.
nb5dcd88dfd3.x: Cotton reported in 1844, but the anicut was sanctioned only in late 1846.
xa: Cost: **Rs 1.5 lakh**.
⚠ **PYQ key = 1855** (**APPSC G2 2012**) for the Dowleswaram year.

n4e5afc7ac53.s: Automated crest-gate telemetry and SCADA were installed at which barrage in February 2026?
n4e5afc7ac53.x: Automated crest-gate telemetry and SCADA were installed at the Prakasam Barrage in February 2026.
n4e5afc7ac53.tq: Apply the location-and-year pair to distinguish similar irrigation structures.
xs: Telemetry and **SCADA** were installed at the **Prakasam Barrage** in **Feb 2026** — option **(3)**.
The Prakasam Barrage stands on the old **Krishna anicut** at **Bezwada**.
xa: The **Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage** (Godavari) is getting **117** new gates.
The Krishna anicut was built by **Charles Orr** on Cotton's plan, **1852/53-1855**.

nap-history-18-1.s: Who designed and constructed the Dowleswaram Anicut in 1852?
nap-history-18-1.x: Sir Arthur Cotton designed and built the Dowleswaram Anicut across the Godavari, completed in 1852.
n: Sir Arthur Cotton designed the Dowleswaram Anicut. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
Sir Arthur Cotton constructed the Dowleswaram Anicut. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
The Dowleswaram Anicut was completed in 1852. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 25-27]
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: other notes say **1850**; PYQ key = **1855** (APPSC G2 **2012**).
Trigger: the **Guntur famine (1832-33)**; Cotton reported in **1844**.
Cotton is called "**Apara Bhagiratha**" and "**Cotton Dora**"; knighted in **1861**.

n7271808e98b.s: The immediate trigger for Arthur Cotton's proposal for an anicut near Rajahmundry was the:
n7271808e98b.x: The Guntur famine of 1832–33 prompted the proposal for an anicut near Rajahmundry.
n7271808e98b.tq: Link a public-works proposal with its immediate historical cause.
xs: The trigger was the **Guntur famine (1832-33)** — option **(2)**.
Cotton's report followed in **1844**, leading to the **Dowleswaram** anicut.
xa: The **Buckingham Canal** was extended as famine relief in **1876-78**.
Reduced land under food crops made the region **famine-prone**.

n1021a84b8de.s: The Godavari and Krishna deltas are together known as the ____ of Andhra.
n1021a84b8de.x: The Godavari and Krishna deltas are called the Rice Bowl of Andhra because of their importance for rice cultivation.
xa: **Rice** was the main crop under British rule.
The Cotton Barrage irrigates **10 lakh acres**.

n315cecddbdf.s: Which of the following was associated with C.P. Brown?
o: Serving as the first Surveyor General in 1815
Introducing ryotwari and suppressing the palegars
Editing the Madras Literary Journal and serving as Curator of the Madras Manuscript Library
n315cecddbdf.x: C.P. Brown contributed to Telugu revival, edited the Madras Literary Journal and served as Curator of the Madras Manuscript Library.
n315cecddbdf.tq: Use a contribution cluster to distinguish one administrator from neighbouring personalities.
xs: **C.P. Brown** edited the **Madras Literary Journal** and was **Curator of the Madras Manuscript Library** — option **(4)**.
**Anglo-Vernacular schools** = **G.N. Taylor**; first **Surveyor General (1815)** = **Colin Mackenzie**.
xa: Brown was **Kadapa Collector** and a leader of the **Telugu revival**.
**Mackenzie** (**1754-1821**) preserved manuscripts and records.
**Taylor**'s schools were a **PYQ 2017** question.

ndea9e166e9e.s: G.N. Taylor is associated with which of the following contributions?
ndea9e166e9e.x: G.N. Taylor, Rajahmundry Sub-Collector, started Anglo-Vernacular schools across Andhra.
ndea9e166e9e.tq: Avoid the swapped-contribution trap among British administrators.
xs: **G.N. Taylor**, **Rajahmundry Sub-Collector**, started **Anglo-Vernacular schools** across Andhra — option **(1)** (**PYQ 2017**).
**Dowleswaram** = **Cotton**; Surveyor General = **Mackenzie**.
xa: **C.P. Brown** = Telugu revival, **Madras Literary Journal**.
**M.G. Ranade** called **Veeresalingam** "South India's **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**".

n95847959b75.s: The Ramapada Sagaram project, the forerunner of today's Polavaram project, was proposed by:
n95847959b75.x: Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy proposed Ramapada Sagaram (PYQ 2019). Cotton built the Dowleswaram anicut. Veenam Veeranna was Cotton's Indian assistant there. Charles Orr built the Krishna anicut at Bezwada.
xs: **Ramapada Sagaram** was proposed by **Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy** — option **(3)** (**PYQ 2019**).
It is the forerunner of today's **Polavaram** project.
xa: **Veenam Veeranna** was Cotton's assistant at **Dowleswaram**.
**Charles Orr** built the **Krishna anicut**.

nf3c63668d71.s: The principal role of the railways that reached Andhra in the late nineteenth century was to:
o: Link the interior with the Madras port
Link Andhra exclusively with Bombay port
Connect only the Agency tracts with Calcutta
nf3c63668d71.x: The railways linked the interior of Andhra with the port of Madras, facilitating movement and trade.
nf3c63668d71.tq: Test the direction and commercial purpose of an early transport link.
xs: Railways reaching Andhra in the late 19th century **linked the interior to Madras port** — option **(1)**.
They did not replace coastal waterways — the **Buckingham Canal** was still extended in **1876-78**.
xa: **Vizagapatnam port** began developing for **iron ore + farm exports**.
The **Buckingham Canal** ran along the coast through **Pulicat Lake**.

n5c79a6373cf.s: The Buckingham Canal, a salt-water navigation canal along the coast through Pulicat Lake, is part of:
n5c79a6373cf.x: The Buckingham Canal is part of NW-4 (Kakinada-Puducherry), not NW-5.
xa: NW-4 runs **Kakinada-Puducherry**.
Railways linked Andhra's interior to **Madras** port.

n4e015153002.s: Which one of the following was a major feature of the economic impact of British rule on handicrafts in Andhra?
o: Handicrafts were protected by complete prohibition of imported goods.
Artisans received increased traditional patronage from local courts.
British manufactured goods entered the market duty-free and artisans lost patronage.
Artisans were shifted exclusively to government employment.
n4e015153002.x: Deindustrialisation occurred because artisans lost traditional patronage and British goods entered duty-free.
n4e015153002.tq: Identify the correct cause-effect explanation for deindustrialisation.
xs: **British goods entered duty-free** and **artisans lost patronage** — option **(3)** (deindustrialisation).
Imports were not banned, and local patronage shrank rather than grew.
xa: Revenue payable in **cash** pushed a shift to **commercial crops**.
Less land under food made the region **famine-prone**.

ncc1438b5c10.s: Under the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792), which ended the Third Anglo-Mysore War, Tipu Sultan:
o: was killed and Mysore was partitioned
gave up half his territory, paid Rs 3 crore and sent two sons as hostages
accepted a subsidiary alliance and restored the Wodeyars
returned all conquests under mutual restitution
ncc1438b5c10.x: Under the Treaty of Seringapatam, Tipu gave up half his territory, paid Rs 3 crore and handed over two sons as hostages to the British, Marathas and Nizam, who were allied against him. Tipu was killed and Mysore partitioned in 1799, in the Fourth war, when the Wodeyars were restored. Mutual restitution was agreed in the Treaty of Madras of 1769.
xs: By the **Treaty of Seringapatam (1792)**, Tipu gave up **half his territory**, paid **Rs 3 crore** and sent **two sons as hostages** — option **(2)**.
Tipu's death and **partition** came in **1799**; **mutual restitution** was the **1769** Treaty of Madras.
xa: GG: **Lord Cornwallis**; the **Nizam** and **Marathas** were British allies.
**Nizam Ali** got back half the Rayalaseema lands — **Bellary, Gurramkonda, Gandikota, Kambham, Kadapa**.

ned3efcb0fe9.s: The Second Anglo-Maratha War was precipitated by which event?
o: the murder of Narayan Rao in 1773
Holkar’s defeat of the Peshwa at the Battle of Poona in 1802
the Nizam’s defeat at Kharda in 1795
Mahadji Scindia’s recapture of Delhi in 1771
ned3efcb0fe9.x: Holkar defeated Baji Rao II at Poona in 1802. Baji Rao II then fled and signed the Treaty of Bassein, leading to the Second Anglo-Maratha War.
ned3efcb0fe9.tq: Trace the immediate chain of events leading to the war.
xs: The trigger was **Holkar's defeat of Peshwa Baji Rao II at Poona (1802)** — option **(2)**.
The Peshwa then signed **Bassein (1802)**, accepting the Subsidiary Alliance.
**Kharda (1795)** was the Nizam's defeat by the Marathas — not this war's cause.
xa: Battles: **Assaye, Argaon** (Arthur Wellesley); **Delhi, Laswari** (Lake).
GG: **Wellesley**; war **1803-05** (some notes **1801-04**).

nafe80518ee3.s: Who was the Governor-General during the Second Anglo-Maratha War?
nafe80518ee3.x: Lord Wellesley was the Governor-General during the Second Anglo-Maratha War.
nafe80518ee3.tq: Distinguish the Governor-General of the second war from those of the first and third wars.
xs: **Lord Wellesley** was GG during the **Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803-05)** — option **(1)**.
**Warren Hastings** = First Maratha war; **Lord Hastings** = Third.
xa: Wellesley (**1798-1805**) also fought the **4th Anglo-Mysore** war.
⚠ **Arthur Wellesley** (Assaye, **1803**) ≠ Lord Wellesley the GG.

n62e962f5341.s: The First Anglo-Maratha War was fought during the tenure of:
n62e962f5341.x: The First Anglo-Maratha War, generally dated 1775–1782, occurred during the tenure of Warren Hastings.
n62e962f5341.tq: Link each war with the Governor-General in office.
xs: The **First Anglo-Maratha War (1775-82)** was under **Warren Hastings** — option **(2)**.
**Lord Hastings** = Third; **Wellesley** = Second; **Cornwallis** = 3rd Mysore.
xa: Warren Hastings (**1772-85**) also fought the **Rohilla War (1774)** and 2nd Mysore war.
He was impeached in **1787** (Burke).

n1e55782f489.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the early treaties of the First Anglo-Maratha War?
n1e55782f489.x: The sequence was the Treaty of Surat in 1775, Treaty of Purandar in 1776, Convention of Wadgaon in 1779 and Treaty of Salbai in 1782.
n1e55782f489.tq: Arrange intermediate agreements before the final settlement.
xs: Order: **Surat (1775)** → **Purandar (1776)** → **Wadgaon (1779)** → **Salbai (1782)** — option **(1)**.
**Wadgaon** followed the British defeat at **Talegaon**.
xa: Salbai brought **20 years of peace**.
Salbai = **British and Marathas** (**APPSC 2018**).

na110978a441.s: The Convention of Wadgaon followed the British defeat at:
na110978a441.x: The Convention of Wadgaon followed the British defeat at Talegaon in 1779, after which the British had to give up their gains.
na110978a441.tq: Match the battlefield event with the immediate treaty consequence.
xs: The Convention of **Wadgaon (1779)** followed the defeat at **Talegaon** — option **(2)**.
**Argaon, Assaye, Laswari** were British victories in the **Second** war.
xa: First war: **1775-82**, under **Warren Hastings**.
Treaties: **Surat → Purandar → Wadgaon → Salbai**.

n6d4a14b48c9.s: Which of the following was NOT a term associated with the Treaty of Bassein?
o: The Peshwa ceded lands yielding Rs 26 lakh.
The Peshwa surrendered Surat to the British.
The Peshwa obtained additional chauth claims on the Nizam.
A subsidiary force was to be maintained in Maratha territory.
n6d4a14b48c9.x: Under the Treaty of Bassein, the Peshwa gave up his chauth claims on the Nizam; he did not obtain additional claims. The other three were terms of the treaty.
n6d4a14b48c9.tq: Find the reversed provision in a list of treaty terms.
xs: The Peshwa **gave up** chauth claims on the **Nizam** — he did not obtain more — so option **(3)** is not a term.
Actual terms: **subsidiary force**, lands yielding **₹26 lakh** ceded, **Surat** surrendered.
xa: **Bassein (1802)** was between the Peshwa and the British.
The **Second Maratha War** followed.

ne1b2b7b14d5.s: The Third Anglo-Maratha War, in which the Peshwa attacked the Poona Residency, occurred under:
ne1b2b7b14d5.x: The Third Anglo-Maratha War came during Lord Hastings' tenure; afterwards the office of Peshwa was abolished.
xa: Treaties: **Poona, Gwalior (1817)**, **Mandasor (1818)**.
After **1851**, the Peshwa pension was stopped for **Nana Sahib**.

nfca3a2eea03.s: Which of the following best describes the result of the Treaty of Salbai?
o: The status quo was restored, the British retained Salsette and peace followed for twenty years
The British surrendered Salsette and recognised Raghunath Rao
The Marathas accepted the Subsidiary Alliance
The Peshwaship was abolished and Poona was annexed
nfca3a2eea03.x: The Treaty of Salbai restored the status quo, allowed the British to retain Salsette and ushered in approximately twenty years of peace.
nfca3a2eea03.tq: Separate the settlement terms of Salbai from those of Bassein and the later war.
xs: At **Salbai** the **status quo** was restored, the British kept **Salsette**, and **20 years of peace** followed — option **(1)**.
The Subsidiary Alliance came with **Bassein (1802)**; the Peshwa-ship ended in **1818**.
xa: Signed by **Warren Hastings and Mahadji Scindia**.
Some notes add **Bassein** to Salsette.

nece24a88fb4.s: Who among the following was associated with the Rohilla War of 1774, the First Anglo-Maratha War and the Second Anglo-Mysore War?
nece24a88fb4.x: Warren Hastings was Governor-General from 1772 to 1785 and his tenure included the Rohilla War, the First Anglo-Maratha War and the Second Anglo-Mysore War.
nece24a88fb4.tq: Match the Governor-General with the cluster of wars fought during his tenure.
xs: **Warren Hastings** (**1772-85**) — **Rohilla War (1774)**, First Anglo-Maratha, Second Anglo-Mysore — option **(1)**.
**Cornwallis** = 3rd Mysore; **Wellesley** = 4th Mysore + 2nd Maratha; **Lord Hastings** = 3rd Maratha.
xa: Warren Hastings was impeached in **1787** (**Burke**).
He concluded **Salbai (1782)**.

nindian-history-81-4.s: The Treaty of Salbai was signed in:
nindian-history-81-4.x: Salbai was 1782; Madras 1769, Allahabad 1765 and Bassein 1802.
n: The Treaty of Madras dates to 1769. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #81 · pp 160-162]
The Treaty of Allahabad dates to 1765. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #81 · pp 160-162]
The Treaty of Salbai dates to 1782. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #81 · pp 160-162]
The Treaty of Bassein dates to 1802. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #81 · pp 160-162]
xa: Madras ended the **First Anglo-Mysore War**; Salbai ended the **First Anglo-Maratha War**.
Bassein: **Peshwa Baji Rao II** accepted the **Subsidiary Alliance**.
**Treaty of Mangalore** (**1784**) ended the Second Anglo-Mysore War.

nindian-history-81-16.s: The Treaty of Salbai made peace between the British and the:
nindian-history-81-16.x: The Treaty of Salbai brought British-Maratha peace.
n: The Treaty of Madras ended the First Anglo-Mysore War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #81 · pp 160-162]
The Treaty of Mangalore ended the Second Anglo-Mysore War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #81 · pp 160-162]
The Treaty of Salbai established British–Maratha peace. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #81 · pp 160-162]
The Treaty of Amritsar established the Sutlej boundary. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #81 · pp 160-162]
xa: Salbai (**1782**) was made by **Warren Hastings** and **Mahadji Scindia**; **20 years of peace**.
**Treaty of Seringapatam** (**1792**) ended the Third Mysore War.
⚠ **Madras (1769)** = with Haidar; **Mangalore (1784)** = with Tipu.

nindian-history-106-1.s: Warren Hastings served as Governor-General of Bengal during:
nindian-history-106-1.x: Warren Hastings, the first Governor-General of Bengal, held the post from 1774 to 1785.
n: Warren Hastings served as Governor-General from 1774 to 1785. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
Warren Hastings abolished the Dual Government. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
Sir John Shore followed the policy of non-intervention. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: other notes give his tenure as **1772-85**.
He founded the **Asiatic Society of Bengal**.
His wars: **Rohilla War (1774)**, the **1st Anglo-Maratha** and **2nd Anglo-Mysore** wars; impeached in **1787** (**Burke**).

nindian-history-106-2.s: The policy of non-intervention is associated with:
nindian-history-106-2.x: Sir John Shore followed non-intervention; Hastings the Ring Fence, Cornwallis the Permanent Settlement, Wellesley the Subsidiary Alliance.
n: Warren Hastings followed the Ring Fence policy, also called the Security policy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
Lord Cornwallis reformed the Civil Services. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
Lord Cornwallis introduced police reforms. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
xa: Permanent Settlement and the **Cornwallis Code**: **1793**.
Shore stayed neutral at **Kharda** (**1795**).
**Lord Hastings** (**1813** to **1823**) **ended** the policy of non-intervention.

n0a82a661bcc.s: Who was the Governor-General of India during the First Anglo-Sikh War (1845–46)?
n0a82a661bcc.x: Lord Hardinge was the Governor-General during the First Anglo-Sikh War, fought in 1845–46.
n0a82a661bcc.tq: Use the ruler-period association and distinguish Hardinge from Dalhousie.
xs: **Lord Hardinge** was GG during the **First Anglo-Sikh War (1845-46)** — option **(3)**.
**Dalhousie** = Second Anglo-Sikh war; **Ellenborough** = Sindh.
xa: Battles: **Mudki, Ferozeshah**, Aliwal, **Sobraon (1846)**.
Ended by **Lahore (1846)**; **Amritsar (Mar 1846)** sold **Kashmir** to **Gulab Singh**.

n9a5dec32cde.s: Which one of the following was the immediate cause of the First Anglo-Sikh War?
o: The murder of Vans Agnew and Anderson at Multan
The refusal of the Nizam to assign Berar
The Sikh army crossing the Sutlej
The detention of two British doctors in Sikkim
n9a5dec32cde.x: The First Anglo-Sikh War began when the Sikh army crossed the Sutlej, whose boundary had been fixed by the Treaty of Amritsar of 1809.
n9a5dec32cde.tq: Identify the immediate cause rather than a later Anglo-Sikh event.
xs: The **Sikh army crossed the Sutlej**, the boundary fixed at **Amritsar (1809)** — option **(3)**.
The **Multan** murders of **Vans Agnew and Anderson** caused the **Second** war.
xa: Punjab fell into chaos after **Ranjit Singh**'s death (**1839**, not 1836).
**Sobraon** was lost through the betrayal of **Lal Singh and Tej Singh**.

ne650ec15728.s: The Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848-49) was triggered by:
o: the Sikh army crossing the Sutlej
the murder of British officers Vans Agnew and Anderson at Multan
the death of Maharaja Ranjit Singh
the sale of Kashmir to Gulab Singh
ne650ec15728.x: It began after the British officers Vans Agnew and Anderson were murdered at Multan, under Dalhousie. The Sutlej crossing caused the First war (1845). Ranjit Singh's death in 1839 was the background to both wars. Kashmir went to Gulab Singh in 1846, after the First war.
xs: The **murder of Vans Agnew and Anderson at Multan** triggered the Second war — option **(2)**.
Crossing the **Sutlej** was the First war's cause; Ranjit Singh died in **1839**; Kashmir was sold in **1846**.
xa: Battles: **Ramnagar, Chillianwala, Gujrat (1849)**.
Result: **Punjab annexed 1849**; **Kohinoor** taken.

n9cec66a8174.s: The lands of the Carnatic Nawab in Nellore and Chittoor were annexed in 1801 on the charge of
n9cec66a8174.x: Nellore and Chittoor were taken from the Carnatic Nawab in 1801 on the charge of collusion with Tipu Sultan, an early pretext annexation.
n9cec66a8174.tq: Match the Andhra territories with the specific annexation pretext.
xs: **Nellore and Chittoor** were annexed in **1801** on a charge of **collusion with Tipu** — option **(3)**.
It was an early "**pretext**" annexation.
xa: **Rayalaseema** had come to the Company in **1800** through the subsidiary alliance.
**Wellesley** merged Andhra into the **Madras Presidency**.

nindian-history-17-49.s: Who led the Sikhs at the Battle of Chillianwala?
nindian-history-17-49.x: Sher Singh Attariwala led the Sikhs and Lord Gough the British; the battle was undecided.
n: Lord Gough and Sher Singh were associated with the Battle of Chillianwala. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Battle of Chillianwala was undecided. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
The Punjab was annexed by the British in 1849. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 69-73]
xa: ⚠ Chillianwala was **not** a simple decisive British victory.
The Second war ended at **Gujrat** (**21 Feb 1849**); **Duleep Singh** was the last Sikh ruler.
The Second war began after the murder of **Vans Agnew and Anderson** at **Multan**.

nb34db7ba5bc.s: After the First Anglo-Sikh War, Kashmir was transferred to Gulab Singh under the Treaty of:
nb34db7ba5bc.x: Kashmir went to Gulab Singh under a separate Treaty of Amritsar; Bhairowal also followed the First Anglo-Sikh War.
xa: **Lahore (1846)**: land south of the Sutlej ceded, indemnity paid, Kashmir handed over.
⚠ Kashmir price: **Rs 75 lakh**; some notes say **Rs 1 crore**.

n354b792887e.s: Who adopted a bullying policy towards the Amirs of Sindh and annexed Sindh after the battles of Miani and Dabo?
n354b792887e.x: Sir Charles Napier used coercive diplomacy against the Amirs and annexed Sindh after the battles of Miani and Dabo.
