n354b792887e.tq: Use the commander-deed association and avoid confusing Napier with the Governors-General.
xs: **Sir Charles Napier** bullied the **Amirs of Sindh** and annexed it after **Miani and Dabo** — option **(2)**.
**Bentinck** annexed **Coorg (1834)**; **Lord Hastings** fought the Third Maratha War.
xa: GG: **Lord Ellenborough** (**1843**).
Nickname: "**Tail of the Afghan Storm**".

n1b6098c7550.s: The annexation of Sindh was described as the:
n1b6098c7550.x: The British annexation of Sindh was called the ‘Tail of the Afghan Storm’.
n1b6098c7550.tq: Test the exact historical expression rather than a plausible geographical description.
xs: Sindh's annexation was called the "**Tail of the Afghan Storm**" — option **(1)**.
It aimed to recover prestige lost in the **1st Afghan War** (**1839-42**).
xa: Annexed **1843** under **Ellenborough**, by **Charles Napier**.
Other aims: counter **Russia**; secure **Indus** trade.

n6a4ac55216a.s: At the Battle of Kharda in 1795, the Marathas defeated the Nizam while the Governor-General was
n6a4ac55216a.x: Sir John Shore, Governor-General from 1793 to 1798, followed a policy of neutrality at Kharda, where the Marathas defeated the Nizam.
n6a4ac55216a.tq: Use the neutral-policy clue to identify the Governor-General.
xs: **Sir John Shore** (**1793-98**) stayed **neutral** at **Kharda (1795)** — option **(2)**.
The Nizam blamed Shore's neutrality and hired French troops under **Raymond**.
xa: This led to the Nizam's **Subsidiary Alliance (1798)** under **Wellesley**.
Resident **Kirkpatrick** reported the French battalions.

nef259dddff6.s: Which of the following was NOT an objective of the British conquest of Sindh?
o: Recovering prestige lost in the First Afghan War
Securing the trade of the Indus
Introducing the Doctrine of Lapse in Sindh
nef259dddff6.x: The stated objectives were recovery of prestige after the First Afghan War, countering Russia and securing Indus trade. The Doctrine of Lapse was not an objective of the conquest of Sindh.
nef259dddff6.tq: Eliminate the policy that belongs to Dalhousie’s annexations rather than Sindh.
xs: **Introducing the Doctrine of Lapse** was not an aim — Sindh was a **conquest** — option **(3)**.
Real aims: recover prestige lost in the **1st Afghan War**, counter **Russia**, secure the **Indus** trade.
xa: Annexed **1843**, under **Ellenborough**.
Nickname: "**Tail of the Afghan Storm**".

nd8e2c7421d8.s: Coorg was annexed in 1834 on the plea of misgovernance by:
nd8e2c7421d8.x: Bentinck took Coorg in 1834 citing misgovernance, along with Central Cachar.
xa: The Sikkim pretext: two British doctors detained.
Misgovernance cases: **Coorg, Awadh**.

nindian-history-106-7.s: The First Anglo-Burmese War took place under:
nindian-history-106-7.x: The First Anglo-Burmese War came under Amherst; Auckland had the First Afghan War and Ellenborough annexed Sindh.
n: Lord Amherst was associated with the First Anglo-Burmese War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
Lord William Bentinck abolished Sati. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
Lord Auckland was associated with the First Afghan War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
Lord Ellenborough annexed Sindh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
xa: Sindh was annexed in **1843**, after **Miani and Dabo**, by **Sir Charles Napier**.
Bentinck (**1828** to **1835**) also **promoted English education**.
Amherst's war ended with **Yandabo** (**1826**).

n2a30b0b9ebb.s: Discontent among many sepoys before the Revolt of 1857 was linked to the annexation of:
n2a30b0b9ebb.x: The annexation of Awadh fed discontent among many Awadh sepoys, one of the causes of resentment before 1857.
xa: Lapse annexations **1848-54** + Awadh (**1856**) = grievances behind **1857**.
By **1856** British India stretched from the **Hindukush** to **Burma**.

n1de5abc5a71.s: The Anglo-Nepal War of 1814–1816 and the Treaty of Sugauli were associated with:
n1de5abc5a71.x: The Anglo-Nepal War took place during the tenure of Marquess Hastings, and the Treaty of Sugauli was concluded in 1816.
n1de5abc5a71.tq: Use the war period and treaty year together to identify the correct tenure.
xs: The **Anglo-Nepal War (1814-16)** and **Sugauli (1816)** belong to **Marquess (Lord) Hastings** — option **(4)** (**APPSC-GS 2018**).
**Amherst** = 1st Burmese; **Minto I** = Amritsar (1809); **Auckland** = 1st Afghan.
xa: Lord Hastings also fought the **3rd Anglo-Maratha** war and the **Pindaris**.
⚠ **1813-23** is his tenure, not the war's dates.

nindian-history-81-7.s: The Treaty of Yandabo ended the:
nindian-history-81-7.x: Yandabo (1826) ended the First Anglo-Burmese War; Sugauli (1815) ended the Anglo-Nepal War.
n: The Treaty of Amritsar dates to 1809. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #81 · pp 160-162]
The Treaty of Amritsar was associated with Ranjit Singh and the British. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #81 · pp 160-162]
The Treaty of Sugauli dates to 1815. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #81 · pp 160-162]
The Treaty of Sugauli was associated with the British and Nepal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #81 · pp 160-162]
The Treaty of Yandabo ended the First Anglo-Burmese War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #81 · pp 160-162]
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: other notes date Sugauli to **1816**.
Amritsar 1809 was under **Minto I**; Yandabo under **Amherst**.
⚠ **Amritsar 1809** = Sutlej boundary; **Amritsar 1846** = Kashmir sold to **Gulab Singh**.

nindian-history-81-14.s: The Treaty of Lahore (1846) followed which war?
nindian-history-81-14.x: The Treaty of Lahore (1846) followed the First Anglo-Sikh War and extended British control in Punjab.
n: The Treaty of Sugauli ended the Anglo-Nepal War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #81 · pp 160-162]
The Treaty of Lahore was associated with the First Anglo-Sikh War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #81 · pp 160-162]
The Treaty of Lahore expanded British control in Punjab. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #81 · pp 160-162]
xa: Under Lahore, territory south of the Sutlej was ceded and **Kashmir** handed over.
⚠ Kashmir price: **Rs 75 lakh** (Treaty of Amritsar, 1846); some notes say **Rs 1 crore**.
First Anglo-Sikh War GG: **Lord Hardinge**; Nepal war (**1814-16**) under **Lord Hastings**.

n92638334fbe.s: Which of the following series of wars began first?
n92638334fbe.x: The Anglo-Mysore Wars began in 1767, before the Anglo-Maratha (1775) and Anglo-Sikh (1845) Wars.
xa: Mysore: **4** wars; Maratha: **3** wars; Sikh: **2** wars.
The **Carnatic Wars (1746-63)** came before all three.

nce09a810bd0.s: The Treaty of Madras (1769), which ended the First Anglo-Mysore War, provided for:
o: cession of half of Mysore's territory
mutual restitution of conquests and a defensive alliance
nce09a810bd0.x: The Treaty of Madras gave mutual restitution of conquests and a defensive alliance.
xa: Hyder reached **Madras** in this war.
Nizam + Marathas + British had allied against **Hyder**.

n77dbb8bc18b.s: Who was the Governor-General during the Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780-84)?
n77dbb8bc18b.x: Warren Hastings was Governor-General during the Second war; Cornwallis fought the Third.
xa: Hyder died in **1782**, during the war.
**Porto Novo (1781)**: **Eyre Coote** defeated Hyder.

nbcb6b31688d.s: Tipu Sultan's attack on Travancore in 1789 was significant because Travancore was
o: a Maratha dependency controlling the Tungabhadra
the capital of the Nizam's dominions
a French possession and Mysore's principal naval base
a British ally and the Company's only pepper supplier
nbcb6b31688d.x: Travancore was a British ally and the East India Company's only pepper supplier. Tipu's attack helped precipitate the Third Anglo-Mysore War.
nbcb6b31688d.tq: Connect the attacked place with its political and commercial importance.
xs: **Travancore** was a **British ally** and the Company's **only pepper supplier** — option **(4)**.
Tipu's attack on it in **1789** triggered the **Third Mysore War**.
xa: The British, **Marathas** and **Nizam** allied against Tipu; GG **Lord Cornwallis**.
**Treaty of Seringapatam (1792)**: Tipu gave up **half his territory**, paid **Rs 3 crore**, sent **two sons as hostages**.

nfde2916ba94.s: Tipu Sultan is said to have planted a 'Tree of Liberty' at:
nfde2916ba94.x: The Tree of Liberty was planted at Srirangapatnam, his capital; Dindigul is where Haidar Ali set up an arsenal in 1755.
xa: Tipu is said to have joined the **Jacobin Club**.
**Dindigul** = Haidar Ali's arsenal (**1755**).

n7d4010c3500.s: Which of the following correctly states the British concern behind the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War?
o: Warren Hastings feared Haidar Ali's control of Mahe.
Lord Cornwallis feared a Maratha alliance with France.
The Madras Government feared the restoration of the Wodeyars.
Lord Wellesley feared Tipu Sultan's alliance with Napoleon.
n7d4010c3500.x: Lord Wellesley feared Tipu Sultan's alliance with Napoleon, which contributed to the decision to wage the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.
n7d4010c3500.tq: Avoid the ruler-and-event swap by matching the correct Governor-General with the concern.
xs: **Wellesley** feared a **Tipu-Napoleon alliance** — option **(4)**.
Result: Tipu killed defending **Seringapatam (1799)**; **Wodeyars** restored under a subsidiary alliance; Mysore partitioned.
xa: **APPSC-G1 2004**: Wellesley defeated Tipu in **1799**.
No treaty ended the Fourth war.
In **1800** the Nizam ceded the **Ceded Districts** after Tipu's fall.

nd88f62819fd.s: Mysore's control over which Malabar spices was a factor in the British conflicts with Mysore?
nd88f62819fd.x: The British were concerned about Mysore's control of Malabar pepper and cardamom, its threat to Madras and its French ties.
xa: Mysore wars: **1767-99**, **4** wars.
**Travancore**, the only **pepper** supplier, was attacked by Tipu in **1789**.

n0763ccc365e.s: During the First Anglo-Mysore War, the Nizam, the Marathas and the British were allied against
n0763ccc365e.x: In the First Anglo-Mysore War, the Nizam, the Marathas and the British formed an alliance against Haidar Ali.
n0763ccc365e.tq: Identify the opponent from the alliance configuration.
xs: In the **First Mysore War**, the **Nizam, Marathas and British** allied against **Haidar Ali** — option **(3)**.
**Tipu** was the Mysore ruler only in the later wars; **Ranjit Singh** was the Sikh ruler.
xa: First war: **1767-69**; ended by the **Treaty of Madras (1769)**.
Hyder reached **Madras**.

n3e5603c618b.s: The Ceded Districts, given up by the Nizam in 1800, came to be called:
n3e5603c618b.x: Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary, ceded in 1800, were called the Ceded Districts or Dattamandalalu.
xa: **Nellore and Chittoor** were annexed in **1801**.
**Wellesley** merged Andhra into the **Madras Presidency**.

n923f57313b9.s: The Treaty of Deogaon (1803) was signed by the British with:
n923f57313b9.x: Deogaon was with the Bhonsle of Nagpur; Bassein with the Peshwa, Surji-Arjangaon with Scindia and Rajpurghat with Holkar.
xa: Surji-Arjangaon gave the British **Delhi** and control of the **Mughal emperor**.
Third-war treaties: **Poona, Gwalior (1817)**, **Mandasor (1818)**.

ne96baec166d.s: The Treaty of Salbai (1782) was concluded between:
ne96baec166d.x: Salbai was signed by the British (Warren Hastings) and the Marathas (Mahadji Scindia), and it ended the First Anglo-Maratha War (APPSC 2018). The British made peace with Mysore at Mangalore in 1784. The Marathas fought the Nizam at Kharda in 1795. The Nizam's treaties with the British came at Masulipatnam (1768) and Hyderabad (1798).
xs: **Salbai (1782)** was between the **British and the Marathas** — option **(1)** (**APPSC 2018**).
Signed by **Warren Hastings** and **Mahadji Scindia**.
xa: It ended the First Anglo-Maratha War; status quo, **Salsette** kept.
**APPSC-G2 2023** match: Hastings → **Salbai**; Minto I → **Amritsar**; Hardinge I → **Lahore**.

nd1f0508e5b1.s: Under British paramountcy, Indian states generally retained:
o: the right to make war on neighbours
nd1f0508e5b1.x: Indian states kept their internal administration but had no independent international life.
xa: Another ground: **misgovernance** (**Coorg, Awadh**).
**Lord Hastings** turned subsidiary alliances into **paramountcy**.

n9f1f7b8f41c.s: Who converted the policy of subsidiary alliances into a wider system of paramountcy?
n9f1f7b8f41c.x: Lord Hastings developed subsidiary alliances into the system of British paramountcy and imposed humiliating treaties on the Peshwa and Scindia.
n9f1f7b8f41c.tq: Distinguish the architect of paramountcy from the Governor-General associated with the Doctrine of Lapse.
xs: **Lord Hastings** turned subsidiary alliances into **paramountcy** — option **(2)**.
**Wellesley** began the Subsidiary Alliance; **Hardinge** and **Dalhousie** fought the Sikh wars.
xa: He imposed humiliating treaties on the **Peshwa** and **Scindia**.
**Rajputana (1818)**: Udaipur, Jaipur, Jodhpur accepted subordinate alliances.

n6715a28fcdd.s: Under the subordinate alliances accepted by Rajputana states in 1818, the states:
o: surrendered their internal administration but retained foreign relations
were exempted from all British political control
gave up their external relations in return for British protection
became directly administered provinces of the Company
n6715a28fcdd.x: The Rajputana states accepted British protection and surrendered control over their external relations under subordinate alliances in 1818.
n6715a28fcdd.tq: Apply the protection-for-external-control structure of a subordinate alliance.
xs: Rajputana states **gave up external relations in return for British protection** — option **(3)**.
They kept their **internal administration**, but had **"no international life"**.
xa: States: **Udaipur, Jaipur, Jodhpur** and others (**1818**).
Lord Hastings' era: Anglo-Nepalese War (**1814-16**), 3rd Anglo-Maratha, Pindaris.

nb85a63a8bcc.s: Baji Rao II, whose adopted son Nana Sahib was denied the Peshwa pension, died in:
nb85a63a8bcc.x: Baji Rao II died in 1851, after which Nana Sahib's pension was stopped.
xa: Baji Rao II had been deposed and pensioned after the **Third Maratha War**.
Loss of pensions turned **princes** against the Company before **1857**.

nf3174b31410.x: By 1856 British India stretched from the Hindukush to Burma, giving geographical unity and a basis for common resistance.
xa: Lapse (**Jhansi**) and lost pensions (**Nana Sahib**) alienated the princes.
After **1818** British **paramountcy** was unchallenged.

nae13c7e91c8.s: The First Anglo-Sikh War was fought when the Governor-General was:
nae13c7e91c8.x: The First Anglo-Sikh War belonged to Hardinge; Dalhousie fought the Second.
xa: Dalhousie did annex **Lower Burma (Pegu)**.
Nepal war: **1814-16** — ⚠ **1813-23** is Lord Hastings' tenure.

nf84a965c19a.s: Who commanded the British forces at Assaye?
nf84a965c19a.x: Arthur Wellesley commanded at Assaye; Lord Lake at Delhi and Laswari; Gough at Mudki and Chillianwala.
xa: **Eyre Coote** commanded at **Porto Novo (1781)**.
Chillianwala was **costly and indecisive**.

n19dc8087560.s: The office of Governor-General of Bengal was created by the:
n19dc8087560.x: The Regulating Act of 1773 created the office of Governor-General of Bengal, with Warren Hastings as its first holder.
n19dc8087560.tq: Match the constitutional title with the Act that created it.
xs: The title **Governor-General of Bengal** dates from **1773** — the **Regulating Act, 1773** — option **(4)**.
The **Government of India Act 1858** created the **Viceroy and GG**; **1833** made the GG of Bengal the **GG of India**.
xa: Title sequence: **Governor of Bengal** → **GG of Bengal (1773)** → **GG of India (1833)** → **Viceroy (1858)**.
The office of Governor of Bengal existed **1757-1772**; first holder **Robert Clive (1758)**.
First GG: **Warren Hastings** (**1773-85**).

n2f9b2147fc3.s: Who became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833?
n2f9b2147fc3.x: Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833; Canning was the first Viceroy.
xa: Bentinck: GG **1828-35**, GG of India from **1833**.
First **Governor of Bengal**: **Robert Clive (1758)**.

ncc57737640e.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the successive changes in the title of the head of British administration in India?
o: Governor of Bengal → Governor-General of Bengal → Governor-General of India → Viceroy
Governor-General of Bengal → Governor of Bengal → Viceroy → Governor-General of India
Governor of Bengal → Governor-General of India → Governor-General of Bengal → Viceroy
Governor of Bengal → Viceroy → Governor-General of Bengal → Governor-General of India
ncc57737640e.x: The sequence was Governor of Bengal, Governor-General of Bengal from 1773, Governor-General of India from 1833, and Viceroy from 1858.
ncc57737640e.tq: Fix the first and last titles, then place the two intermediate constitutional changes in order.
xs: **Governor of Bengal** → **GG of Bengal (1773)** → **GG of India (1833)** → **Viceroy (1858)** — option **(1)**.
The office of Governor of Bengal existed **1757-1772**; the Viceroy title came with the **Government of India Act 1858**.
xa: First holders: **Clive**, **Warren Hastings**, **Bentinck**, **Canning**.
The title changes by Act are a common statement question.

nf43431371ca.s: Which Governor-General died at Ghazipur during his second term in office?
nf43431371ca.x: Cornwallis returned for a second term in 1805 and died at Ghazipur during that term.
nf43431371ca.tq: Use the exceptional second tenure to distinguish Cornwallis from the regular succession.
xs: **Cornwallis** died at **Ghazipur** during his **second term (1805)** — option **(3)**.
His first term was **1786-93** (Permanent Settlement, **Cornwallis Code**, **1793**).
xa: **Sir George Barlow** (**1805-07**) succeeded him.
Cornwallis created the post of **District Judge** and reformed the civil service.

n288b69eec32.s: The Vellore Mutiny of 1806 occurred during the tenure of:
n288b69eec32.x: The Vellore Mutiny occurred in 1806 during the tenure of Sir George Barlow.
n288b69eec32.tq: Use the event year to identify the Governor-General in office.
xs: The **Vellore Mutiny (1806)** fell under **Sir George Barlow** — option **(1)** (**APPSC-GS 2019**).
Barlow served **1805-07**, after Cornwallis' brief second term.
xa: **Minto I** followed (**1807-13**).
Wellesley's **Anti-Infanticide Act** was **1802**.

n853c511d189.s: The Charter Act of 1813 was passed during the tenure of:
n853c511d189.x: The Charter Act of 1813 was passed at the transition between Minto I and Marquess Hastings, whose tenure began in 1813.
n853c511d189.tq: Handle an event falling at the boundary between two consecutive tenures.
xs: The **Charter Act 1813** fell in the time of **Minto I** and **Marquess Hastings** — option **(3)**.
Minto I served **1807-13**; Hastings **1813-23**.
xa: Often mixed up with other GGs' acts — a known trap.
Hastings introduced **Mahalwari** in **1822**.

n49da67cda2c.s: The post of District Judge was created by:
n49da67cda2c.x: Cornwallis created the post of District Judge; his Code of 1793 separated revenue from justice.
xa: **Permanent Settlement (1793)** was also Cornwallis'.
He reformed the **civil service**.

nfa6ccbadc7b.s: In 1831 William Bentinck concluded a treaty of perpetual friendship with:
nfa6ccbadc7b.x: Bentinck concluded a treaty of perpetual friendship with Ranjit Singh in 1831.
xa: Bentinck revised Mahalwari by the **1833 Regulation IX** (**APPSC-G1 2024**).
Mahalwari was devised by **Holt Mackenzie**.

n8924a607515.s: The Anti-Slavery Act of 1843 was passed under:
n8924a607515.x: The 1843 Anti-Slavery Act was Ellenborough's; Hardinge I is linked to the Anti-Human-Sacrifice Act of 1845.
xa: **Hardinge I** passed the **Anti-Human-Sacrifice Act (1845)**.
Ellenborough: **1842-44**.

n354b30af5fe.s: Which of the following was among the impeachment charges against Warren Hastings?
o: Application of the Doctrine of Lapse
Introduction of the Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam
Plunder of the Begums of Awadh
n354b30af5fe.x: The charges included the Rohilla War, Chait Singh, the plunder of the Begums of Awadh and the judicial murder of Nand Kumar.
xa: Impeachment **1787**; trial **1788 to 1795**; **acquittal**.
Impeached by **Edmund Burke** and the **Whigs** for administrative excesses.

n5cf739ebcca.x: Sati was abolished under Bentinck in 1829 (after Wellesley's infanticide measure of 1802 and before Ellenborough's 1843 slavery abolition).
xa: Then **Dalhousie**: caste disabilities **1850**, widow remarriage **1856**.
Bentinck also suppressed **female infanticide** and **Thuggee**.

nindian-history-97-10.s: The Regulating Act and the Ring Fence policy are associated with:
nindian-history-97-10.x: Warren Hastings is linked with the Regulating Act and Ring Fence policy; Clive with Plassey, Cornwallis with the Permanent Settlement, Wellesley with the Subsidiary Alliance.
n: Robert Clive is associated with the Battle of Plassey. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Warren Hastings is associated with the Regulating Act. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Warren Hastings is associated with the Ring Fence policy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Cornwallis is associated with the Permanent Settlement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Cornwallis is associated with the Cornwallis Code. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Wellesley is associated with the Subsidiary Alliance. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
xa: Clive = first **Governor of Bengal** (**1758**).
**Bentinck** = first **GG of India**; **Lord Canning** = first **Viceroy** (**1858**).
**Dalhousie** = **Doctrine of Lapse**, **railways** and **telegraph**.

nec7a47ebc8d.s: Which one of the following measures is associated with Warren Hastings?
nec7a47ebc8d.x: Warren Hastings abolished the Dual Government in 1772. The Permanent Settlement was introduced by Cornwallis, the Subsidiary Alliance by Wellesley and Sindh was annexed during Ellenborough’s tenure.
nec7a47ebc8d.tq: Use the ruler–measure association and reject measures belonging to neighbouring administrations.
xs: **Warren Hastings** abolished the **Dual Government** (**1772**) — option **(1)**.
**Permanent Settlement** = **Cornwallis**; **Sindh** = **Ellenborough**; **Subsidiary Alliance** = **Wellesley**.
xa: Hastings also set up the **Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774)** and the **Code of Gentoo Laws (1776)**.
He founded the **Asiatic Society of Bengal**.

n11dfcc18d8c.s: The College of Fort William (1800) was founded by:
n11dfcc18d8c.x: The College of Fort William (1800) was Wellesley's, not Warren Hastings'.
xa: Hastings moved the treasury to **Calcutta** and set up **Diwani and Fauzdari Adalats**.
He set up a bank in **Calcutta**.

n17f81cd063c.s: The press in India was liberated under:
n17f81cd063c.x: Metcalfe liberated the press; Bentinck suppressed Thuggee, Dalhousie set up the PWD and Hastings had the Code of Gentoo Laws compiled.
xa: **Metcalfe** served **1835-36**.
Dalhousie also brought railway, post and telegraph.

n52ad6de3f38.s: The impeachment trial of Warren Hastings (1788-1795) ended in his:
n52ad6de3f38.x: Burke and the Whigs impeached Hastings in 1787; the trial ran 1788-1795 and ended in acquittal.
xa: Charges: **Rohilla War (1774)**, **Chait Singh**, **Begums of Awadh**, **Nand Kumar** (**1775**).
Hastings was the first **GG of Bengal** (**1773-85**).

n7c483c33a11.s: The first universities in India were established in 1857 during the tenure of:
n7c483c33a11.x: The first universities came in 1857 under Canning, not Bentinck.
xa: Bentinck also suppressed **Thuggee** with **Sleeman**.
Called the **Father of Modern Western Education in India**.

n2ac0236c5c0.s: Which Governor-General is credited with easing the entry of British investors and traders into India?
n2ac0236c5c0.x: The APPSC-GS 2025 key names William Bentinck. Warren Hastings is known for abolishing the Dual Government and for the Ring Fence policy. Wellesley is known for the Subsidiary Alliance. Ellenborough annexed Sindh and passed the Anti-Slavery Act.
xs: **Bentinck** "eased the entry of **British investors and traders** into India" — option **(2)** (**APPSC-GS 2025**).
**Warren Hastings**, **Wellesley** and **Ellenborough** are tied to wars and annexations, not this opening to investors.
xa: Bentinck also abolished **Sati (1829)** and took **Coorg (1834)**.
First **GG of India** (**1833**).

nfac3d6c7a40.s: Who was the only Viceroy of India to be murdered while in office?
nfac3d6c7a40.x: Lord Mayo was the only Viceroy murdered in office. He was killed in 1872 in the Andamans by the convict Sher Ali Afridi.
nfac3d6c7a40.tq: Use the uniqueness clue and verify it with the place, year and assassin.
xs: **Lord Mayo** is the only Viceroy murdered in office — option **(3)**.
He was killed by the convict **Sher Ali Afridi** in the **Andamans (1872)**.
**Hardinge II** survived the **Delhi Conspiracy** bomb of **1912**.
xa: Mayo (**1869-72**): **financial decentralisation (1870)**, **Mayo College**, statistical survey.
First census under Mayo, **1872** (some notes **1871**) — non-synchronous.
FIRST/LAST: first Viceroy **Canning**; last Viceroy **Mountbatten**.

n7792d7d866c.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the two early censuses of British India?
o: The first census was synchronous in 1881, while the first non-synchronous census was held in 1901.
The first census was synchronous in 1872 and the first non-synchronous census was in 1881.
The first census was non-synchronous in 1872, while the first synchronous census was held in 1881.
Both the first census and the first synchronous census were held in 1872.
n7792d7d866c.x: The census conducted under Mayo in 1872 was the first, but it was non-synchronous. The first synchronous census was held in 1881 during Lord Ripon's tenure.
n7792d7d866c.tq: Separate the first census from the first synchronous census instead of treating them as identical.
xs: The **first census (1872)** under **Mayo** was **non-synchronous**; the **first synchronous census** was in **1881** under **Ripon** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Some notes date the first census to **1871**.
xa: Mayo also ordered a **statistical survey**.
Ripon: **First Factory Act**, **Local Self-Government Resolution 1882**.
n7792d7d866c.fixed: stem carried a duplicate (a)-(d) list in a different order from the options; confusing

nindian-history-106-12.s: The Vernacular Press Act (1878) was repealed in 1882 by:
nindian-history-106-12.x: Lytton passed the Vernacular Press Act in 1878 and Ripon repealed it in 1882.
n: Lord Lytton introduced the Vernacular Press Act. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
Lord Lytton was associated with the Delhi Durbar of 1877. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
Lord Ripon repealed the Vernacular Press Act. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
Lord Ripon was associated with the Factory Act. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
xa: The **first synchronous census** came in **1881** under **Ripon**.
Lytton also passed the **Arms Act (1878)** and the **Royal Titles Act**; held the **Delhi Durbar** of **1877**.
Ripon's **Local Self-Government Resolution 1882** earned him the title "**Father of Local Self-Government**".
⚠ Lytton owns three Acts (Royal Titles, VPA, Arms); **Ripon** only **repealed** the VPA.

nff32f4fad91.s: Lord Lytton's Royal Titles Act was passed in:
nff32f4fad91.x: The Royal Titles Act came in 1876, after Mayo's 1870 resolution and before Ripon's 1881 Factory Act.
xa: Lytton also passed the **Vernacular Press Act** and **Arms Act (1878)**.
Ripon repealed the **VPA (1882)**.

n6ea5f8ccbe7.s: The portfolio system was introduced during the tenure of:
n6ea5f8ccbe7.x: Canning's tenure saw the Indian Councils Act 1861, the portfolio system, the first universities and the IPC.
xa: He also withdrew the **Doctrine of Lapse** and introduced **income tax**.
The 1861 Act nominated **3** Indians: **Raja of Benaras, Maharaja of Patiala, Sir Dinkar Rao**.
The **ASI** was set up in **1861** under Canning.

n22052dd2693.s: The term 'Magna Carta of Local Self-Government' is associated with the
o: Financial decentralisation resolution of Lord Mayo
Local Self-Government Resolution of Lord Ripon
Indian Councils Act of Lord Lansdowne
n22052dd2693.x: Lord Ripon's Local Self-Government Resolution of 1882 is described as the Magna Carta of Local Self-Government. Ripon is consequently called the Father of Local Self-Government.
n22052dd2693.tq: Connect the famous title with the exact resolution and viceroy.
xs: The "**Magna Carta**" of local self-government = **Ripon's Local Self-Government Resolution (1882)** — option **(2)**.
Ripon is the "**Father of Local Self-Government**"; **Mayo**'s **1870** resolution was financial decentralisation.
xa: Ripon also: **Hunter Commission (1882)**, **Ilbert Bill (1883)**, repeal of **VPA**.
First synchronous census: **1881** under Ripon.

nb34ebe3d5ac.s: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 during the viceroyalty of:
nb34ebe3d5ac.x: The INC was founded under Dufferin; the Durand Commission came under Lansdowne and the Chapekar killings under Elgin II.
xa: Elgin II: **Great Famine 1896-97**, **Lyall Commission (1897)**, **Munda uprising (1899)**.
Lansdowne: **Indian Councils Act 1892**.

nbb2b363095d.s: The anti-Partition movement which contributed to the revocation of the Partition of Bengal was known as the
nbb2b363095d.x: The anti-partition Vande Mataram movement contributed to the revocation of the Partition of Bengal, which was announced through King George V in 1911.
nbb2b363095d.tq: Separate similarly placed movements by linking each one to its specific viceroy-era context.
xs: The anti-partition **Vande Mataram** movement forced revocation — option **(1)**.
The **Munda uprising (1899)**, **Kuka** movement (Northbrook) and **Wahabi** movement (Elgin I) are unrelated.
xa: Partition by **Curzon** in **1905**; revocation announced through **King George V** (**1911**).
**Bihar and Orissa** were made a separate province at the same Durbar.

nf085b049907.s: The Indian Councils Act of 1861, under which three Indians were nominated to the Viceroy's Legislative Council, was passed during the tenure of:
nf085b049907.x: The Indian Councils Act of 1861 was passed during Lord Canning's tenure. The nominated Indians included the Raja of Benaras, the Maharaja of Patiala and Sir Dinkar Rao.
nf085b049907.tq: Match the Act with the Viceroy by using the year and the distinctive provision.
xs: The **Indian Councils Act 1861** was **Canning**'s — option **(1)**.
**3** Indians nominated: **Raja of Benaras, Maharaja of Patiala, Sir Dinkar Rao**.
xa: Canning also introduced the **portfolio system**.
Next Councils Act: **1892** under **Lansdowne**.

nc76d0fb6eb3.s: The Indian Councils Act of 1892 was passed during the tenure of:
nc76d0fb6eb3.x: The Indian Councils Act of 1892 was passed during Lord Lansdowne's tenure.
nc76d0fb6eb3.tq: Distinguish the 1892 Indian Councils Act from the 1861 and 1909 Acts by their Viceroys.
xs: The **Indian Councils Act 1892** was **Lansdowne**'s — option **(1)**.
**Dufferin** preceded him (INC, **1885**); **Elgin II** and **Curzon** followed.
xa: Lansdowne also: **Second Factory Act (1891)**, **Durand Commission (1893)**.
He split the civil services into **imperial, provincial, subordinate**.
Earlier Councils Act: **1861** (Canning); later: **1909** (Minto II).

n70f689a143f.s: Which of the following developments contributed to the growth of early nationalism during Lord Lytton's tenure?
o: The establishment of the Archaeological Survey of India
The holding of a Durbar during famine conditions along with the Vernacular Press Act and Arms Act
The introduction of elected local bodies and financial autonomy
The appointment of the Royal Commission on Labour
n70f689a143f.x: Lytton's reactionary policies, including the Durbar during famine conditions, the Vernacular Press Act and the Arms Act, fuelled early nationalist criticism.
n70f689a143f.tq: Identify the cluster of policies that generated political opposition rather than later reform measures.
xs: **Lytton**'s **Durbar during famine**, **VPA** and **Arms Act** fuelled early nationalism — option **(2)**.
The **ASI** came under **Canning**; elected local bodies under **Ripon**; the **Labour Commission** under **Irwin**.
xa: Lytton also cut the ICS age from **21** to **19**.
**Second Afghan War (1878-80)**.

nca8746bc1eb.s: The controversy surrounding the Ilbert Bill is significant because it exposed:
o: Racial discrimination in the colonial judicial system
The financial conflict between the central and provincial governments
The dispute over the Afghan boundary
The division between famine and irrigation administration
nca8746bc1eb.x: The Ilbert Bill controversy revealed the racial discrimination involved in preventing Indian judges from exercising jurisdiction over European British subjects on equal terms.
nca8746bc1eb.tq: Connect the controversy with its underlying constitutional and racial issue.
xs: The **Ilbert Bill** exposed **racial discrimination** — option **(1)**.
Introduced in **1883** under **Ripon**; the reaction was the "**White Mutiny**".
xa: Ripon is the "**Father of Local Self-Government**".
**Lytton**'s reactionary policies also fed early nationalism.

nindian-history-106-13.s: Which Governor-General is associated with the Third Anglo-Burmese War and the last major territorial expansion?
nindian-history-106-13.x: Lord Dufferin (1884 to 1888) fought the Third Anglo-Burmese War of 1885, which annexed Upper Burma as the last major territorial expansion.
nindian-history-106-13.tq: Recall the war of each Viceroy.
n: Lord Dufferin was associated with the Third Anglo-Burmese War. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
Lord Dufferin's tenure saw the last major territorial expansion. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
Lord Dufferin served as Governor-General from 1884 to 1888. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #106 · pp 197-199]
xs: **Lord Dufferin** (**1884** to **1888**) is linked with the **Third Anglo-Burmese War** — so option **(4)** is correct.
His tenure saw the **last major territorial expansion**; the Third Burma War was fought in **1885**.
**Curzon** is linked with the **Partition of Bengal**, **Minto II** with the **Morley-Minto Reforms**, **Hardinge II** with the shift of the capital to **Delhi**.
xa: The **Indian National Congress** was founded in **1885** during Dufferin's viceroyalty.
Dufferin was followed by **Lord Lansdowne** (**1888-94**) — **Indian Councils Act 1892**, **Durand Commission (1893)**.
Before him came **Lord Ripon** (**1880-84**) — **Ilbert Bill (1883)**.

nindian-history-125-3.s: The policy of 'Masterly Inactivity' towards Afghanistan is associated with:
nindian-history-125-3.x: Masterly Inactivity was Lord Lawrence's (1864-69) policy of non-interference in Afghanistan.
n: Lord Lawrence was Viceroy from 1864 to 1869. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Lawrence followed the Policy of Masterly Inactivity. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
xa: Lawrence's measures: **telegraph link with Europe**, the **Indian Forest Department**, canals and state-managed railways.
**Sir John Lawrence** declared **Shimla** the **summer capital** in **1864** (APPSC 2018 key).
He was followed by **Lord Mayo** (**1869-72**).

nb1e0c039671.s: Which Viceroy came immediately after Lord Minto II?
nb1e0c039671.x: The order is Curzon, Minto II, Hardinge II, Chelmsford and Reading.
xa: **Irwin** (**1926-31**) followed Reading.
**21 Viceroys** ruled from **1858** to **1947**.

nccc0672f637.s: The August Offer was made in:
nccc0672f637.x: The August Offer was in 1940, between the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) and the Wavell Plan (1945).
xa: **Cabinet Mission 1946** came under Wavell.
**Quit India 1942** under Linlithgow.

n982a05063d7.s: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 consisted of Cripps, A.V. Alexander and:
n982a05063d7.x: The Cabinet Mission members were Cripps, A.V. Alexander and Pethick-Lawrence.
xa: The **Interim Government** under **Nehru** was formed under Wavell.
**Irwin**'s memoir: "**Fullness of Days**".

n32a06fb52f1.s: The Indian Independence Act, which abolished the offices of Viceroy and Secretary of State, was passed on:
n32a06fb52f1.x: The Indian Independence Act of 18 July 1947 abolished the offices of Viceroy and Secretary of State.
xa: Mountbatten = last Viceroy and first GG of free India.
**C. Rajagopalachari** = first and last Indian GG.

ne9c90245f51.s: The annulment of the Partition of Bengal and the transfer of the capital to Delhi were announced at the Delhi Durbar on:
ne9c90245f51.x: Both, with the creation of Bihar and Orissa, were announced on 12 December 1911.
xa: The 1909 Act (Morley-Minto) belonged to **Minto II**.
The 1911 Durbar marked **George V**'s coronation.

nb04b4aff4dd.s: The first Telugu political prisoners referred to in connection with 18 July 1908 were:
o: Alluri Sitarama Raju and Tanguturi Prakasam
nb04b4aff4dd.x: Gadicherla and Bodi Narayana Rao are identified as the first Telugu political prisoners on 18 July 1908, during Minto II's tenure.
nb04b4aff4dd.tq: Use the distinctive date and names to avoid substituting better-known later Andhra nationalists.
xs: The first Telugu political prisoners were **Gadicherla** and **Bodi Narayana Rao** (**18 July 1908**) — option **(4)**.
This was in **Minto**'s time.
xa: Telangana was then under the **Nizam**.
Minto II: **Indian Councils Act 1909**.

nindian-history-125-9.s: The capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi during the viceroyalty of:
nindian-history-125-9.x: Hardinge II is linked with the shift of capital and the Delhi Durbar of 1911.
n: Lord Curzon was associated with the Partition of Bengal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Curzon was associated with the Universities Act. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Curzon was associated with the Ancient Monuments Act. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Minto II was associated with the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Minto II was associated with separate electorates. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
The capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi during Lord Hardinge II's viceroyalty. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Hardinge II was associated with the Delhi Durbar of 1911. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Chelmsford was associated with the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Chelmsford was associated with Jallianwala Bagh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
xa: The **1911 Durbar** also annulled the **Partition of Bengal** and made **Bihar and Orissa** a separate province.
**Chelmsford** also saw the **Rowlatt Act (1919)**.
**Curzon**'s Police Commission **1902** was headed by **Andrew Frazer**.
**Hardinge II** wrote **"My Indian Years"**.

nindian-history-125-13.s: Who was the only Jewish Viceroy?
nindian-history-125-13.x: Lord Reading (Rufus Isaacs, 1921 to 1926) was the only Jewish Viceroy of India.
nindian-history-125-13.tq: Recall the distinctive fact about each Viceroy.
n: Lord Reading was the only Jewish Viceroy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
xs: **Lord Reading** (**1921** to **1926**) was the **only Jewish Viceroy** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Irwin** is linked with the **Simon Commission**, **Willingdon** with the **Poona Pact**, **Wavell** with the **Wavell Plan**.
xa: Reading's period saw **Chauri Chaura** and the **Swaraj Party**.
Reading followed **Chelmsford** (**1916-21**) and was followed by **Irwin** (**1926-31**).
**Irwin** wrote **"Fullness of Days"** (as **Lord Halifax**).

nindian-history-125-17.s: Chauri Chaura and the Swaraj Party belong to the viceroyalty of:
nindian-history-125-17.x: Reading is linked with Chauri Chaura and the Swaraj Party; Irwin with the Simon Commission and Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
n: Lord Reading was associated with Chauri Chaura. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Reading was associated with the Swaraj Party. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Irwin was associated with the Simon Commission. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Irwin was associated with the Civil Disobedience Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Irwin was associated with the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Wavell was associated with the Wavell Plan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Wavell was associated with the Simla Conference. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Wavell was associated with the Cabinet Mission period. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Mountbatten was associated with Indian independence. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Mountbatten was associated with the Partition. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #125 · pp 227-229]
xa: The **Simla Conference (1945)** failed on **Jinnah**'s stand.
**Cabinet Mission 1946**: **Cripps**, **A.V. Alexander**, **Pethick-Lawrence**.
Mountbatten replaced Wavell after **Attlee's statement (20 Feb 1947)**; the **Indian Independence Act (18 July 1947)** abolished the office of Viceroy.

n9336414b3c7.s: Queen Victoria was proclaimed Empress of India at the 1877 Delhi Durbar under:
xa: The 1877 Durbar was held while millions starved in the **1876** famine.
**1911** announcements: Bengal partition annulled, **Bihar and Orissa** separate, capital to **Delhi**.

n1e6677f9917.s: The Delhi Conspiracy Case of 1912 was associated with an attempt to assassinate
o: Lord Lytton during the 1877 Delhi Durbar
Lord Curzon during the 1905 Partition announcement
Lord Mayo during his tour of the Andamans
Lord Hardinge II during the state-entry procession into Delhi
n1e6677f9917.x: In 1912, Rash Behari Bose and Sachin Sanyal attempted to assassinate Lord Hardinge II during his state-entry procession into Delhi.
n1e6677f9917.tq: Match the conspiracy with its target, year and setting.
xs: The **Delhi Conspiracy Case (1912)** was the attempt on **Hardinge II** during the **state-entry procession into Delhi** — option **(4)**.
Plotters: **Rash Behari Bose** and **Sachin Sanyal**.
xa: The capital had shifted from **Calcutta to Delhi** (**1911**).
Hardinge II's memoir: "**My Indian Years**".

n61bc9895b3a.s: Shimla was declared the summer capital of British India in 1864 by:
n61bc9895b3a.x: Sir John Lawrence declared Shimla the summer capital in 1864 (APPSC 2018 key). Canning was Viceroy until 1862. Mayo came in 1869 and is known for financial decentralisation. Lytton held the 1877 Durbar.
xs: **Sir John Lawrence** declared **Shimla** the summer capital in **1864** — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2018** key).
**Canning**, **Mayo** and **Lytton** are tied to other firsts — Councils Act, decentralisation, Royal Titles.
xa: Lawrence (**1864-69**): telegraph to **Europe**, **Indian Forest Department**.
The capital moved from **Calcutta** to **Delhi** in **1911**.

n711de1f6a2c.s: Victoria was proclaimed Empress of India through the Royal Titles Act during the viceroyalty of:
n711de1f6a2c.x: The Royal Titles Act was passed in 1876 during Lord Lytton's viceroyalty and recognised Queen Victoria as Empress of India.
n711de1f6a2c.tq: Use the distinctive title and year to identify the correct Viceroy.
xs: The **Royal Titles Act (1876)** — Victoria as Empress — came under **Lytton** — option **(4)**.
She was proclaimed at the **1877 Durbar**.
xa: Lytton owns three Acts: **Royal Titles**, **VPA**, **Arms (1878)**.
**Second Afghan War (1878-80)**; ICS age cut to **19**.

ncf71b418b55.s: The Hunter Commission of 1882 was appointed during the viceroyalty of:
ncf71b418b55.x: The Hunter Commission of 1882 was an Education Commission appointed during Lord Ripon's tenure.
ncf71b418b55.tq: Match the commission's subject and year with the correct Viceroy.
xs: The **Hunter Commission (1882)** on education came under **Ripon** — option **(1)**.
**Lytton** preceded Ripon; **Dufferin** and **Lansdowne** came after.
xa: Ripon: **Local Self-Government Resolution 1882**, repeal of **VPA (1882)**.
Other education body: **Universities Commission (Raleigh, 1902)** under Curzon.

n99eb020d0e3.x: Raleigh dealt with universities; Hunter with education, Durand with the Afghan boundary and Lyall with famine.
xa: Viceroys: Ripon, Lansdowne, Elgin II, Curzon.
Famine chain: **Strachey → Lyall → MacDonnell**.

na2e7c577595.s: The Irrigation Commission of 1901, the Police Commission of 1902 and the Universities Commission of 1902 were all appointed during the viceroyalty of:
na2e7c577595.x: All three commissions were appointed during Lord Curzon's viceroyalty. Their chairmen or associations were Scott-Moncrieff, Andrew Frazer and Raleigh respectively.
na2e7c577595.tq: Group several commissions under one Viceroy by recognising their common period.
xs: **Irrigation (1901)**, **Police (1902)**, **Universities (1902)** — all under **Curzon** — option **(1)**.
Curzon (**1899-1905**): **Indian Universities Act 1904**, **Partition of Bengal 1905**.
xa: He also set up the **Dept of Commerce and Industry** and **NWFP**.
**MacDonnell** famine commission also came under Curzon.

n580fcd35b19.s: The motto of the Archaeological Survey of India is
n580fcd35b19.x: The motto of the Archaeological Survey of India is 'Pratnakirti Apavarini'.
n580fcd35b19.tq: Test the exact official expression rather than a familiar national motto.
xs: The ASI's motto is "**Pratnakirti Apavarini**" — option **(3)**.
The ASI was set up in **1861** under **Canning**, founder **Alexander Cunningham**.
xa: **Curzon** revived it; DG **John Marshall (1902)**.
**AMASR Act 1958** protects monuments over **100 years** old.

nab91790f524.s: The Archaeological Survey of India was set up in 1861 under:
nab91790f524.x: The ASI was set up in 1861 under Canning, with Cunningham as founder; Curzon later revived it.
xa: ⚠ **1861** = ASI (Canning); **1904** = Monuments Act (Curzon).
**APPSC 2012** key: Department of Archaeology = **Canning**.

nindian-history-25-16.s: Who was the first Archaeological Surveyor of India?
nindian-history-25-16.x: Alexander Cunningham was the first Archaeological Surveyor; John Marshall later became Director-General.
n: William Jones founded the Asiatic Society in 1784. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 86-89]
Cunningham became Archaeological Surveyor in 1861. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 86-89]
Curzon appointed Marshall as Director-General in 1901. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 86-89]
The Ancient Monuments Preservation Act was enacted during the viceroyalty of Lord Curzon. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 86-89]
xa: The **Department of Archaeological Survey** was established in **1871**.
ASI motto: **"Pratnakirti Apavarini"**.
⚠ **1861** = ASI set up under **Canning** (founder **Alexander Cunningham**); **1904** = Monuments Act under **Curzon**.
If Canning is not among the options for "who created the ASI", **Curzon** (who revived and reorganised it) is the intended answer.

nf3ae880af3f.s: The Select Committee appointed by Parliament in 1772 to inquire into Company affairs was headed by:
nf3ae880af3f.x: In 1772 Parliament appointed a Select Committee under Burgoyne along with a Secret Committee.
xa: The two committees' reports led to the **Regulating Act, 1773**.
Background: after **Buxar (1764)**, **Shah Alam** granted the **Diwani** of Bengal, Bihar, Orissa in **1765**.
The Regulating Act **recognised the political and administrative functions** of the Company.

n271cc3532a6.s: The first step by the British Parliament to control the East India Company was the:
n271cc3532a6.x: The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first parliamentary measure to control the Company and recognised its political and administrative functions.
xa: **1784** (Pitt's India Act) set the **dual system** that lasted until **1858**.
The Act followed the **1772** Select Committee (**Burgoyne**) and Secret Committee reports.
APPSC-GS **2019** trap: the Act did **not** abolish the **Court of Directors**.

n5d64e573342.s: The Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774) consisted of one Chief Justice and:
n5d64e573342.x: It had one Chief Justice and three judges with civil and criminal jurisdiction.
xa: The **1781** Act of Settlement later excluded **revenue** matters from the Court's jurisdiction.
The **1781** Act also exempted the **GG, Council and Company servants** for **acts in their official capacity**.
Undefined jurisdiction over the Council and Indians caused **Council-Court clashes** — a defect of 1773.
AP angle: a **Madras Supreme Court (1801)** was set up for British subjects.

n0e44160bcf6.s: The Act of 1786 was passed to meet the condition of which Governor-General for accepting office?
n0e44160bcf6.x: The Act of 1786 met Cornwallis's condition, letting the GG override his Council and act as Commander-in-Chief.
xa: ⚠ **1781** = **Act of Settlement** (curbs the Supreme Court); **1786** = override power (Cornwallis).
The **1786** Act corrected the **1773** defect under which **Hastings** was repeatedly outvoted.
The **Regulating Act 1773** set up the **Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774)**: **1 Chief Justice + 3 judges**.

nda842c3edfb.s: The overriding power given to the Governor-General by the Act of 1786 corrected which defect of the Regulating Act?
o: The repeated outvoting of the Governor-General by his Council
The absence of a Supreme Court at Calcutta
The absence of a Board of Control
nda842c3edfb.x: The Act of 1786 addressed the Governor-General, including Hastings, being repeatedly outvoted by his Council.
xa: The other 1773 defect — **Council-Court clashes** — was remedied by the **1781** Act of Settlement.
The **1786** Act was passed for **Lord Cornwallis**, who also became **Commander-in-Chief**.
The **Charter Act of 1793** extended the override power to presidency governors.

n4391584716e.s: Pitt's India Act was passed in:
n4391584716e.x: The order was Regulating Act 1773, Amending Act 1781, Pitt's India Act 1784 and Act of 1786.
xa: ⚠ **1781** = Act of Settlement (curbs Supreme Court); **1786** = override power (**Cornwallis**).
The **Charter Act of 1793** extended the override power to the presidency governors.
The **1784** dual system lasted until the **GoI Act 1858** ended **"Double Government"**.

n3e16fe38c9a.s: Which Act directed the Supreme Court at Calcutta to respect the personal laws of Hindus and Muslims?
n3e16fe38c9a.x: The Amending Act of 1781 (Act of Settlement) required the Court to respect Hindu and Muslim personal laws and exempted official acts.
xa: The **1781** Act is also called the **Act of Settlement**.
It remedied the **1773** defect of undefined jurisdiction that caused **Council-Court clashes**.
The Supreme Court at Calcutta had been set up in **1774** with **1 Chief Justice + 3 judges**.

n2e2b2da8e1d.s: The 'Double Government' set up by Pitt's India Act (1784) was ended by the:
n2e2b2da8e1d.x: Pitt's India Act created the dual system, which lasted until the Government of India Act of 1858.
xa: The **1781** Act of Settlement curbed the Supreme Court; the **1786** Act gave the GG override power.
The **Ministry of Law and Justice** traces to the **Charter Act 1833**, not to 1773.
AP angle: **Madras Supreme Court (1801)** and **Madras Regulations 1816** (Munsiff and Panchayat courts).

n21a3dc03e72.s: Under the Regulating Act of 1773, the Governor-General:
o: could override his Council in special cases
had an unrestricted veto over his Council
could be outvoted by his Council
n21a3dc03e72.x: The Governor-General had no veto and could be outvoted by his Council; the override power came only with the Act of 1786.
xa: Remedy for the outvoting: the **Act of 1786** gave the GG **override power**.
Remedy for the clashes: the **1781 Act of Settlement** exempted **official acts** and **revenue** matters.
The **Charter Act of 1793** extended the overriding power to the **governors of the presidencies**.

n96e05d32c1d.s: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly in India but retained its exclusive trade in:
o: Spices, and trade with the East Indies
n96e05d32c1d.x: The 1813 Act ended the general monopoly in India but kept the Company's exclusive trade in tea and with China.
xa: CGPSC **2022** trap: "the 1813 Act abolished the Company's trade monopoly" is marked **not true** because tea and China trade were kept.
The **1813** Act extended the charter by **20 years** and asserted the **sovereignty of the British Crown**.
It also gave **Rs 1,00,000 (1 lakh) a year** for education and let **missionaries** enter India.

n38995401e55.s: The Company's exclusive right to trade in tea and with China was abolished by the:
n38995401e55.x: The Charter Act of 1833 removed the Company's remaining monopoly over tea trade and trade with China.
n38995401e55.tq: Separate the general Indian trade monopoly from the later tea-and-China exception.
xs: The tea and China trade monopoly was abolished by the **Charter Act of 1833** — option **(3)**.
The **1813** Act had ended only the general India trade monopoly, keeping **tea** and **China**.
**1833** ended **all commercial functions**; the Company became **purely administrative**.
xa: 1833 also removed curbs on **European immigration and property purchase** in India.
1833 made the **Governor-General of Bengal** the **Governor-General of India** (first: **Bentinck**).
1833 is called the **"final step towards centralisation"**.

n059b196169a.s: Which Charter Act officially allowed Christian missionaries to enter India?
n059b196169a.x: Under Evangelical pressure (Wilberforce, Charles Grant), the Charter Act of 1813 allowed missionaries to enter and preach.
xa: The same Act gave **Rs 1 lakh a year** for education — the **first step towards State responsibility for education**.
**1813** is remembered for opening India to **free trade** and missionaries.
⚠ Do not confuse Wilberforce/Grant (1813) with **Trevelyan** and **Robert Lowe**, who backed open competition (1853).

n88a33e6ad92.s: Under the Charter Act of 1833, laws made by the Governor-General-in-Council were called:
n88a33e6ad92.x: From 1833 laws were called Acts instead of Regulations, and legislative power for all British India went to the GG-in-Council.
xa: The presidencies' power was restored by the **Indian Councils Act 1861** to **Bombay** and **Madras**.
1833 added a **Law Member** as the **4th** member of the GG's council.
1833 is the **peak of centralisation**.

ndc3e8b59576.s: Which Act abolished the Directors' patronage and introduced open competition for civil-service recruitment?
ndc3e8b59576.x: The Charter Act of 1853 abolished the patronage of the Court of Directors and introduced open competition for civil-service recruitment.
xa: **Charles Trevelyan** and **Robert Lowe** supported open competition.
The **Macaulay Committee (1854)** replaced nomination with competitive exams, preferring **university graduates**.
⚠ Some notes give the Macaulay report as **1855**.

nc8596183b79.s: The last Charter Act of the East India Company was the Charter Act of:
nc8596183b79.x: The Charter Act of 1853 was the last; the Government of India Act of 1858 then transferred authority to the Crown.
xa: The **1853** Act is also called the **Government of India Act 1853**.
1853 opened the path to a **legislature** and a **merit-based ICS**.
1853 held territories "in trust" **until Parliament should otherwise provide**.

n5f586d123fd.s: Who was the first Law Member (the fourth member) of the Governor-General's Council under the Charter Act of 1833?
n5f586d123fd.x: The 1833 Act added a Law Member as the fourth member of the Council; T. B. Macaulay was the first to hold the post.
xa: The **first Law Commission (1834)** under Macaulay drafted the **Indian Penal Code**.
Macaulay also wrote the **Minute on Education (1835)**.
The **Ministry of Law and Justice** is traced to this **1833** Act.

n64ea4edd269.s: The first Law Commission (1834), which drafted the Indian Penal Code, was chaired by:
n64ea4edd269.x: The first Law Commission was set up in 1834 under Macaulay and drafted the IPC.
xa: Macaulay was the **first Law Member (1834)**, the **4th** member of the GG's council under the **1833** Act.
His Commons speech on the **1833** Bill: "The Company is an **anomaly**..." (UPPSC **2017**).

nf0dc0051206.s: Which of the following is correct about the Charter Act of 1833?
o: It was the first Charter Act to renew the Company's authority for a fixed 20-year term.
It abolished the Governor-General's office without creating a successor.
It was the final step towards centralisation and made the Company purely administrative.
It restored the law-making powers of the presidencies.
nf0dc0051206.x: The Charter Act of 1833 is regarded as the final step towards centralisation and converted the Company into a purely administrative body.
xa: 1833 ended the **tea** and **China** trade monopoly.
1833 removed curbs on **European immigration and property purchase**.
1833 added a **Law Member** (**Macaulay**) as **4th** member.

n6c1e82a2360.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Charter Act of 1853?
o: Four members were appointed by Madras, Bombay, Bengal and Agra, the first local representation.
Six new legislative members were added.
The new members formed a separate Central Legislative Council.
The other two new legislative members were the Commander-in-Chief and the Law Member.
n6c1e82a2360.x: The two remaining members were not the Commander-in-Chief and the Law Member; they included the Chief Justice.
xa: The Council is called the **"mini-Parliament"**.
The **1853** Act separated the **legislative and executive functions** of the GG's Council.
**1853** is the **last Charter Act** (**Government of India Act 1853**).

ne1d8a09c9c0.s: The Act of 1773 made the Governor of Bengal the:
ne1d8a09c9c0.x: The 1773 Act created the Governor-General of Bengal and subordinated Bombay and Madras.
xa: **1784**: **Board of Control**; stricter supervision of the presidencies.
**1793**: greater control over Bombay and Madras; override extended to governors.
**1833**: **GG of India** with **exclusive legislative power** — peak of centralisation.

nc6b559cc145.s: Section 87 of the Charter Act of 1833 provided that no Indian should be barred from office on the grounds of:
o: Province, gender, tribe or political opinion
Religion, place of birth, descent or colour
nc6b559cc145.x: Section 87 declared that religion, place of birth, descent or colour should not bar an Indian from holding office.
nc6b559cc145.tq: Retain the exact four grounds instead of substituting broader modern equality categories.
xs: **Section 87** of the 1833 Act: no Indian barred from office on grounds of **religion, place of birth, descent or colour** — option **(3)**.
Caste, gender, language or property are not the grounds named in Section 87.
xa: **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** first demanded Indians in the services in **1832**.
Open competitive exams came only with the **1853** Act, which abolished the Directors' **patronage**.
APPSC-GS **2018** key: appointments were made exclusively by the Directors **till 1853**.

n1bc13d46d60.s: The territory separated from the Bengal Presidency and placed under the Agra Presidency by the Charter Act of 1833 was renamed in 1836 as the:
n1bc13d46d60.x: The separated territory was placed under the Agra Presidency in 1834 and renamed the North-Western Provinces in 1836.
xa: UPPSC **2021** key: the area placed under Agra Presidency in **1834** was present-day UP.
**Agra** later sent one of the **4** provincial members to the **1853** Central Legislative Council.

n1a45786302c.s: The Macaulay Committee on the Indian Civil Service was constituted in:
n1a45786302c.x: The Macaulay Committee (1854) recommended competitive examinations in place of nomination and favoured graduates.
xa: ⚠ Some notes give the report year as **1855**.
The **1853** Act abolished the Directors' **patronage**; **Trevelyan** and **Robert Lowe** backed open exams.
**Fort William College (1800, Wellesley)** was replaced by **Haileybury (1806)**.

nc3efa679e9a.s: The expression that the Indian territories of the East India Company were held “in trust” is associated with the:
nc3efa679e9a.x: The Charter Act of 1853 continued the Company's authority over its Indian territories in trust for the British Crown, its heirs and successors.
nc3efa679e9a.tq: Discriminate between the Charter Acts by attaching the exact phrase to the correct year.
xs: The **Charter Act of 1853** held the Indian territories "**in trust** for Her Majesty, her heirs and successors" — option **(2)**.
The trust lasted "**until Parliament should otherwise provide**" (APPSC-GS **2018**).
xa: Fill-in-the-blank bait: answer **Charter Act**, not Regulating Act.
Unlike **1813**, the **1853** Act gave **no fixed 20-year term**.
The **1813** Act asserted the **sovereignty of the British Crown** over Indian possessions.

n13b822baa4e.s: John Shore helped Cornwallis plan the:
n13b822baa4e.x: John Shore helped plan the Permanent Settlement; Ryotwari was linked to Read and Munro and Mahalwari to Holt Mackenzie.
xa: Ryotwari began experimentally in **Baramahal (1792)**; general Madras adoption came in **1820**.
**Mountstuart Elphinstone** extended Ryotwari to **Bombay**.
⚠ Mahalwari: **Mackenzie 1822** = proposal; **Bird / Bentinck 1833** = revision.

nf4762aa6699.s: The Permanent Settlement was introduced in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa in:
nf4762aa6699.x: It was introduced in 1793 (not 1795), planned by Cornwallis with John Shore.
xa: It began as a **decennial (10-year)** settlement, made permanent in **1793**.
In Andhra it was applied in **1802**.
APPSC-GS **2024**: Permanent Settlement = **Cornwallis**.

n0f1db3fb2ae.s: Under the Sunset Law associated with the Permanent Settlement, an estate could be auctioned when:
o: the annual revenue was not paid by sunset on the due date
the tenant refused to accept a patta
the zamindar failed to improve the land within ten years
n0f1db3fb2ae.x: If the required revenue was not paid by sunset of the due date, the estate could be auctioned.
n0f1db3fb2ae.tq: Focus on the precise trigger for an estate sale and reject broader consequences.
xs: Under the **Sunset Law**, an estate was auctioned if revenue was **not paid by sunset of the due date** — option **(1)**.
It did not deal with pattas, land improvement or prices.
xa: Permanent vs Ryotwari default: estate **forfeited (Sunset Law)** vs **land auctioned**.
Many old zamindars lost estates to **urban merchants and moneylenders** at auction.
**Haftam (1799)** and **Panjam (1812)** let zamindars seize tenants' property.

nb093fe2a511.s: The first experimental introduction of the Ryotwari system in the Madras Presidency took place in which area?
nb093fe2a511.x: The first experiment was conducted in Baramahal, comprising areas such as Salem, Krishnagiri, Dharmapuri and Tiruvannamalai.
nb093fe2a511.tq: Distinguish the first experimental area from the later area of wider implementation.
xs: Ryotwari was first introduced experimentally in **Baramahal** — option **(1)** (APHQ **2008** key).
It was done by **Captain Alexander Read**, assisted by **Thomas Munro**, in **1792**.
The **Ceded Districts** came later (**1802**) — that is the first in **Andhra**.
xa: Exam angle: "first in Andhra" = **Rayalaseema**; "in the Madras Presidency" = **Baramahal**.
Munro was **Collector of South Canara** in **1799**.

nb9ef4cfa59a.s: The Mahalwari System was proposed in 1822 by:
nb9ef4cfa59a.x: Holt Mackenzie proposed it in 1822; it was revised under Bentinck in 1833 with R.M. Bird.
xa: Mackenzie's law: **Regulation VII of 1822**; Bird's revision: **Regulation IX of 1833**.
**James Thomason** carried on Bird's settlement in the NWP.
⚠ Some notes credit **Bentinck (1833)** as originator — that is only the revision.

na330ec3dd14.s: Baramahal came under Company control after the Third Mysore War in:
na330ec3dd14.x: Baramahal came under the Company in 1792, before the Permanent Settlement was made permanent (1793).
xa: Ryotwari: Rayalaseema **1802**, general Madras **1820**.
**Haftam 1799**, **Panjam 1812**.

nbab7c3e2c20.s: Under the Mahalwari system, the unit of revenue assessment was the:
nbab7c3e2c20.x: Under Mahalwari the mahal (village or estate) was the unit; revenue fixed for it was collected through the headman or village community.
xa: Individual ryots = **Ryotwari**; zamindars = **Permanent Settlement**.
Mahalwari broke village solidarity through **collective liability**.
On default the **village was collectively liable**.

n0a045b03605.s: The Mahalwari system of land revenue was introduced mainly in which of the following regions?
o: North-Western Provinces and parts of Punjab
n0a045b03605.x: Mahalwari covered the North-Western Provinces (Agra-Oudh) and parts of Punjab, plus Central India (APPSC 2018). Bengal, Bihar, Odisha and the Northern Circars were Permanent Settlement areas; Madras and Bombay were Ryotwari areas.
n0a045b03605.tq: Mahalwari = NWP + Punjab; Ryotwari = Madras + Bombay; Zamindari = Bengal.
xs: Mahalwari was mainly in the **North-Western Provinces and parts of Punjab** — option **(2)** (APPSC-GS **2018**).
**Bengal, Bihar**, **Odisha** and the **Northern Circars** were Permanent Settlement areas; **Madras and Bombay** were Ryotwari.
xa: Mahalwari also covered the Gangetic valley and **Central India** — about **30%** of British India.
Proposed by **Holt Mackenzie (1822)**.

naa284a1fbc2.s: The Permanent Settlement introduced by Cornwallis in 1793 was implemented in Andhra in 1802 with which immediate effect?
o: The auction system was abolished and the tax was fixed
The zamindars were replaced by village headmen
Land revenue was remitted during every crop failure
All Zamindari estates were immediately abolished
naa284a1fbc2.x: In Andhra, Cornwallis's 1793 Act was implemented in 1802; it abolished the auction system and fixed the tax. Zamindari abolition occurred much later in 1948.
naa284a1fbc2.tq: Apply the general settlement policy to its Andhra implementation.
xs: When Cornwallis's **1793** settlement was implemented in Andhra in **1802**, **the auction system was abolished and the tax was fixed** — option **(1)**.
Zamindars were not replaced or abolished; abolition came only in **1948**.
There was **no famine remission** under British revenue systems.
xa: Agreements ran for **10** years; farmers were reduced to **tenants**.
Andhra effects: absentee landlordism, **sub-infeudation**, no investment in land.
Some notes give the Andhra split as **9/10** to government, **1/10** to the zamindar.

ne6184b97c95.s: Why did rigid land revenue demands frequently push ryots towards moneylenders?
o: The government accepted revenue only in manufactured goods
Moneylenders alone were authorised to cultivate government land
Revenue had to be paid in cash even when crops failed
Ryots were prohibited from selling agricultural produce
ne6184b97c95.x: The inflexible cash demand continued even during crop failures, forcing ryots to borrow from Mahajans and often mortgage or lose their land.
ne6184b97c95.tq: Trace the cause-effect chain from revenue rigidity to indebtedness.
xs: Revenue had to be **paid in cash even when crops failed** — option **(3)**.
This rigid cash demand drove ryots to **moneylenders (Mahajans)**, then mortgage and eviction.
xa: There was **no famine remission**, unlike the Mughal **zabt**.
Cash revenue forced **cash crops** (indigo, cotton, opium, jute).
Result: rural indebtedness and **land alienation**.

n5798d1eee41.s: The need to pay land revenue in cash encouraged the cultivation of:
o: commercial crops such as indigo, cotton, opium and jute
n5798d1eee41.x: Cash revenue demands pushed peasants to grow commercial crops such as indigo, cotton, opium and jute.
xa: Ryotwari areas: the **American Civil War** cotton slump → defaults → land to moneylenders.
Low investment in agriculture; **overcrowding** as ruined artisans fell back on land.

nd515adfdf82.s: Which pairing of newly strengthened rural classes with the areas in which they emerged is correct?
o: Merchant-landlords — Zamindari areas; moneylender-landlords — Ryotwari and Mahalwari areas
Moneylender-landlords — Zamindari areas; merchant-landlords — Ryotwari areas only
Artisan-landlords — all areas; merchants — no rural areas
Village headmen — Zamindari areas; zamindars — Ryotwari areas only
nd515adfdf82.x: Merchant-landlords became prominent in Zamindari areas, while moneylender-landlords emerged particularly in Ryotwari and Mahalwari areas.
nd515adfdf82.tq: Match each rural class with the revenue system that enabled its rise.
xs: **Merchant-landlords** rose in **zamindari** areas; **moneylender-landlords** in **ryotwari and mahalwari** areas — option **(1)**.
Old zamindars lost estates to **urban merchants and moneylenders** at auction.
xa: The common result: **rural indebtedness + land alienation**.
Land became a **saleable commodity**, concentrated in few hands.

na9081eb5799.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as a major problem of the Ryotwari system?
o: Permanent fixing of revenue at a low and unchangeable rate
na9081eb5799.x: Ryotwari suffered from over-assessment, inadequate records and unclear boundaries. Its revenue was periodically revised and often heavy, not permanently fixed at a low rate.
na9081eb5799.tq: Find the option that contradicts the characteristic weaknesses of the system.
xs: **Permanent fixing at a low, unchangeable rate** was NOT a Ryotwari problem — option **(4)**; Ryotwari was **periodically revised** and high.
Real problems: **over-assessment**, **no proper land records**, **unclear boundaries**, corrupt subordinate officials.
xa: Ryotwari revenue was often **50%+** of produce.
Revision came about **every 30 years**.
The **Permanent Settlement** was the one **fixed forever**.

nb2fc444c5f1.s: Under the Ryotwari and Mahalwari systems, the revenue assessment was:
nb2fc444c5f1.x: Revenue was fixed forever under the Permanent Settlement, but periodically revised under Ryotwari and Mahalwari.
xa: Settlement with: **zamindars** / **individual ryots** / **village community (mahal)**.
Ownership: zamindar as proprietor / cultivator as owner / village jointly.

nfdd06784d6c.s: Under the Mahalwari System, revenue was collected by the:
nfdd06784d6c.x: The lambardar collected under Mahalwari; the zamindar under the Permanent Settlement and the individual farmer under Ryotwari.
xa: Intermediaries: present / absent / limited.
Mahalwari joint ownership: **Bhai Chara** or **Mahali**.

nc8ac4488cb9.s: Under the Mahalwari System, default in revenue payment made:
o: the zamindar's estate liable to auction
nc8ac4488cb9.x: Under Mahalwari the village was collectively liable; under Ryotwari the cultivator's land could be seized.
xa: Zamindari defaults fell under the **Sunset Law**.
Mahalwari's **collective liability** broke village solidarity.

n2bd0d7ea2ea.s: Alice Thorner criticised the Ryotwari system on the ground that it—
o: abolished all direct contact between the state and zamindars
created a permanent landlord class in the Northern Circars
made the village community the sole unit of settlement
destroyed the village system and isolated farmers from the government
n2bd0d7ea2ea.x: Alice Thorner argued that Ryotwari destroyed the village system and isolated individual farmers from the government.
n2bd0d7ea2ea.tq: Associate a named critic with the precise argument attributed to her.
xs: **Alice Thorner** said ryotwari **destroyed the village system and isolated farmers from the government** — option **(4)**.
Making the village the unit is **Mahalwari**; a landlord class in the Circars is **zamindari**.
xa: Another criticism: the state became the **"ultimate landlord"**.
Ryotwari revenue was **as heavy as Zamindari rent**.

nindian-history-110-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Permanent Settlement?
o: It covered Bengal, Bihar, Odisha and Varanasi.
It was associated with Lord Cornwallis.
Zamindars were recognised as proprietors of the land.
It was introduced in Madras and Coorg.
nindian-history-110-2.x: Madras and Coorg came under Ryotwari, not the Permanent Settlement.
n: The Permanent Settlement was associated with Lord Cornwallis. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
The Permanent Settlement mainly covered Bengal, Bihar, Odisha and Varanasi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
The Permanent Settlement recognised zamindars as proprietors or landowners. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
xa: The Permanent Settlement was introduced in **1793** (not **1795**), planned with **John Shore**.
In Andhra it was implemented in **1802** in the **Northern Circars**.
It covered about **19%** of the British-occupied area; Ryotwari **51%**; Mahalwari **30%**.

nindian-history-110-5.s: Under the Mahalwari system, the revenue relationship was between the Government and the:
nindian-history-110-5.x: The Permanent Settlement dealt with the zamindar, Ryotwari with the ryot and Mahalwari with the village or mahal.
n: The Permanent Settlement established a government–zamindar revenue relationship. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
The Ryotwari Settlement established a government–ryot revenue relationship. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
The Mahalwari Settlement established a government–village or mahal revenue relationship. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
xa: Collection: **zamindar** (Permanent), **individual farmer** (Ryotwari), **village headman (lambardar)** (Mahalwari).
Intermediaries: present (Permanent), absent (Ryotwari), limited (Mahalwari).
Revenue: **permanently fixed** vs **periodically assessed** vs **periodically revised**.

nindian-history-110-6.s: The Ryotwari Settlement is associated with Thomas Munro and:
nindian-history-110-6.x: Ryotwari is linked to Thomas Munro and Alexander Read; the Permanent Settlement to Cornwallis.
n: The Permanent Settlement was associated with Lord Cornwallis. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
The Ryotwari Settlement was associated with Thomas Munro and Alexander Read. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
The Mahalwari Settlement was associated with the mahal or village community. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
The Bengal Tenancy Act dealt with the rights of landlords and tenants. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
The village community or collective was the landholder under the Mahalwari Settlement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
xa: The **Bengal Tenancy Act** was enacted in **1885** for **Bengal** and **Bihar**.
**Mahalwari** was devised by **Holt Mackenzie** (**1822**), revised by **R.M. Bird** (**1833**).
**Munro** is called the **Father of Ryotwari**.

nindian-history-110-12.s: The Ryotwari system was first begun, from 1792, in:
nindian-history-110-12.x: Ryotwari began in Baramahal from 1792; its main area was Madras.
n: The Ryotwari Settlement mainly covered Madras, parts of Bombay, Assam and Coorg. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
The first Ryotwari association began in 1792 onward in Baramahal, Tamil Nadu. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
The Ryotwari Settlement also covered Eastern Bengal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
The ryot or peasant was recognised as the proprietor under the Ryotwari Settlement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
The peasant or ryot was the landholder under the Ryotwari Settlement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
xa: **Alexander Read**, assisted by **Thomas Munro**, began it in Baramahal.
**Munro** introduced Ryotwari in **Rayalaseema (Ceded Districts)** in **1802**.
General Madras Presidency adoption came in **1820**; **Elphinstone** extended it to **Bombay**.

nindian-history-110-14.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the first Ryotwari experiment?
o: Alexander Read was assisted by Munro.
The initial demand was 30% of the estimated produce.
nindian-history-110-14.x: The first Ryotwari demand was 50% of the estimated produce, not 30%.
n: The first Ryotwari association began in 1792 onward in Baramahal, Tamil Nadu. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
Alexander Read was assisted by Thomas Munro in the first Ryotwari association. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
The initial Ryotwari revenue demand was 50% of the estimated produce. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #110 · pp 202-205]
xa: **Baramahal** = **Salem, Krishnagiri, Dharmapuri, Tiruvannamalai**; came to the Company after the **Third Mysore War (1792)**.
Ryotwari assessment was revised about **every 30 years**.
⚠ **30%** is the Mahalwari share of the British-occupied area, not the Ryotwari demand.

n8349de27ab7.s: The Permanent Settlement initially began as a ____ settlement.
n8349de27ab7.x: It began as a ten-year (decennial) settlement and was later made permanent.
xa: Zamindars were recognised as **proprietors**.
Reasons for fixity: **assured income**, low collection cost, a **loyal landlord class**, hope of land improvement.
Demand fixed very high → **no share of later growth** to the state.

ne11b7b02289.s: The sale of many old zamindari estates under the Permanent Settlement contributed to the emergence of:
o: a new body of village karanams
a class of hereditary ryot proprietors in Madras
a new landed class of urban merchants and moneylenders
a class of Palegar intermediaries in Rayalaseema
ne11b7b02289.x: Many old zamindars lost their estates for arrears, which were purchased by urban merchants and moneylenders, creating a new landed class.
ne11b7b02289.tq: Trace the ownership change caused by arrears and auction sales.
xs: Estate sales created **a new landed class of urban merchants and moneylenders** — option **(3)**.
Many old zamindars lost estates for **arrears** under the Sunset Law.
xa: Zamindari areas → **merchant-landlords**; ryotwari and mahalwari areas → **moneylender-landlords**.
**Karanams** were village officers under the Collector in Ryotwari — not a new class.
**Palegars** were suppressed by **Munro**, not created.

n646f5dbd57a.s: Absentee landlordism, sub-infeudation and rack-renting were effects of the:
n646f5dbd57a.x: These, along with peasants reduced to tenants-at-will, were effects of the Permanent Settlement.
xa: Andhra effects: absentee landlordism, sub-infeudation, **no investment in land**, loss of estates for arrears.
Land became a **saleable commodity** concentrated in few hands.

n575549a1c11.s: According to the commonly cited distribution of rent under the Permanent Settlement, what share was retained by the zamindar?
n575549a1c11.x: The commonly cited distribution gave the state 10/11 of the rent collected and the zamindar 1/11. Some accounts mention a 9/10 and 1/10 division, but the cited assessment here uses 1/11.
n575549a1c11.tq: Distinguish the zamindar's retained share from the much larger state share.
xs: The zamindar kept **1/11** of the rent — option **(2)**; the state took **10/11**.
Some notes give **9/10** to government and **1/10** to the zamindar in Andhra — the commonly cited split is 10/11 : 1/11.
xa: The demand was fixed at a **very high level** — no share of later growth for the state.
Ryotwari revenue was also high, often **50%+** of produce.

n4ad2371d45f.s: Which of the following was NOT a rationale advanced for making the Permanent Settlement revenue demand fixed?
o: Ensuring that the Company would receive every future increase in agricultural prices
