n: The Battle of Tallikota was fought between the Adil Shahis of Bijapur and Ramaraya. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 17-18]
The capital of Vijayanagara shifted to Penugonda after the Battle of Tallikota. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 17-18]
xa: Tallikota is also called the **Battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi**.
**Raichur** (**1520**) was Krishnadevaraya's greatest battle.
**Palnadu** (**1182**) — **Nagamma** and **Nalagama Raju**.

n9d5b75de83b.s: Which of the following events occurred in 1853?
o: The Residency at Hyderabad was attacked.
n9d5b75de83b.x: Opposition to the Berar assignment occurred in 1853. The Residency attack was in 1857, the Rampa rebellion in 1879, and Mubariz-ud-Daula's imprisonment in 1839.
n9d5b75de83b.tq: Use the year-event pair and reject events belonging to nearby but different dates.
xs: In **1853** the **Berar assignment** was **opposed** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Mubariz-ud-Daula** — **1839**; **Rampa** — **1879**; **Residency attack** — **1857**.
xa: The **1853 Berar treaty** covered **Berar**, **Raichur**, **Osmanabad/Dharashiv**.
It is listed among the **background grievances** of 1857.

n844188b51ab.x: Rammohan Roy, who knew Persian, Arabic, Sanskrit and English, died at Bristol in 1833.
xa: He was influenced by **Vedanta** and **Western rationalism**.
Titles: "**Father of Modern India**", "**Father of the Indian Renaissance**", first "**Modern Man of India**".
He left for England in **1830** as envoy of **Akbar II**.

ne2d0622bb7d.s: Who conferred the title 'Raja' on Rammohan Roy and sent him to England as his envoy?
ne2d0622bb7d.x: The Mughal emperor Akbar II gave Rammohan Roy the title 'Raja' and sent him to England as his envoy.
xa: He left in **1830** and died at **Bristol**, **1833**.
⚠ "**Maharishi**" is **Debendranath Tagore**'s title, not Roy's.

n439ce73757e.s: Which one of the following titles is NOT associated with Raja Rammohan Roy?
n439ce73757e.x: Rammohan Roy is called the Father of Modern India, the Father of the Indian (or Bengal) Renaissance and the first Modern Man of India. 'Maharishi' was the title of Debendranath Tagore. 'Raja' was given to Rammohan Roy by Akbar II.
xs: "**Maharishi**" is **Debendranath Tagore**'s title — so option **(4)** is the answer.
Roy is "**Father of Modern India**", "**Father of the Indian Renaissance**" and the first "**Modern Man of India**".
xa: Also called **Father of Bengal Renaissance** and **Harbinger** of the modern Indian Renaissance.
Title → person: **Lokahitawadi** — **Gopal Hari Deshmukh** (PYQ **2021**).
"Raja" was given by **Akbar II**.

n159d2456e24.s: Raja Rammohan Roy's Vedanta College, which blended Indian and Western learning, was founded in:
n159d2456e24.x: Vedanta College was founded in 1825 to blend Indian and Western learning.
xa: He also protested the **1823 Press Ordinance**.
Hindu College: **1817**, with **David Hare**.

n033ed4d00f8.s: Raja Rammohan Roy protested against the press curbs imposed by the Press Ordinance of:
n033ed4d00f8.x: Rammohan Roy protested the Press Ordinance of 1823 and also demanded fixed maximum rents for peasants.
xa: Other demands: **lower export duties**, **Indianisation of the services**.
Campaigns: against **sati**, **child marriage**, **polygamy**; for **widow remarriage**, **women's property rights**.

n93911fabea5.s: The Brahmo Sabha, founded in Calcutta in 1828 and later renamed the Brahmo Samaj, was founded by:
n93911fabea5.x: Rammohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in August 1828 with Dwarkanath Tagore (APPSC-GS 2018). It grew out of his Atmiya Sabha of 1815. Dayananda founded the Arya Samaj (1875). Ramakrishna was a mystic, not the founder of a Samaj, and Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1897).
xs: **Raja Rammohan Roy** founded the **Brahmo Sabha** (Calcutta, **1828**) — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2018**).
⚠ Not **Vivekananda**, **Dayananda** or **Ramakrishna**: Dayananda founded the **Arya Samaj** (**1875**).
xa: Co-founder: **Dwarkanath Tagore**.
APPSC-G1 **2008** offered **1826/1829/1834/1836** — the correct **1828** was missing (keyed "-").

n4977408eb5d.x: The Brahmo Samaj opposed polygamy and child marriage and supported widow remarriage, women's education and women's property rights.
xa: It was also against **child marriage**, **female infanticide** and **caste**.
Brahmo Samaj = **reformist** (reason), unlike the revivalist **Arya Samaj**.

nf4a7508b77b.s: While respecting the traditional philosophies of the East, Raja Rammohan Roy wanted Indians to adopt:
o: A rejection of all Eastern thought
nf4a7508b77b.x: He drew on the Upanishads and Vedanta while standing for a rational, scientific approach.
xa: Influences: **Vedanta** + **Western rationalism**.
His **Vedanta College** (**1825**) blended Indian and Western learning.

n66e37251073.s: Which of the following reforms was NOT associated with the activities of the Prarthana Samaj?
o: Use of violent confrontation against orthodox groups
n66e37251073.x: Prarthana Samaj promoted widow remarriage, women's education and inter-caste dining through persuasion rather than confrontation. Violent confrontation was not its method.
n66e37251073.tq: Find the option that reverses the organisation's method of gradual persuasion.
xs: **Violent confrontation** was not its method — it used **persuasion** — so option **(2)** is the answer.
It worked for **widow remarriage**, **women's education** and **inter-caste dining**.
xa: Leaders: **M.G. Ranade**, **R.G. Bhandarkar**.
Brahmo + Prarthana Samaj = **reformist**; Arya Samaj, Deoband = **revivalist**.

n72376b0bd9b.s: M.G. Ranade founded the National Social Conference in 1887 along with:
n72376b0bd9b.x: Ranade founded the National Social Conference in 1887 with Raghunath Rao; it was the social wing of the Congress sessions.
xa: Ranade was a leader of the **Prarthana Samaj** (**1867**).
Other leader: **R.G. Bhandarkar**.

nefc260c3613.s: Which region is regarded as the first Indian region to experience a renaissance?
nefc260c3613.x: Bengal is identified as the first Indian region to experience a renaissance. Within Andhra, Rajahmundry is associated with the first renaissance.
nefc260c3613.tq: Distinguish the all-India regional first from the corresponding Andhra location.
xs: **Bengal** was the first Indian region to have a **renaissance** — so option **(4)** is correct.
In **Andhra**, the counterpart centre was **Rajahmundry**.
xa: **Rammohan Roy** is called **Father of Bengal Renaissance** and **Father of the Indian Renaissance**.
He is also the first "**Modern Man of India**".

nindian-history-51-37.x: The Ramakrishna Mission was non-political, non-sectarian and humanitarian; Vivekananda joined pure Vedanta with the truth of all religions.
n: The Ramakrishna Mission was a social movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Ramakrishna Mission was a spiritual movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Ramakrishna Mission was non-political. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Ramakrishna Mission was non-sectarian. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
The Ramakrishna Mission was humanitarian. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Vivekananda's philosophy was associated with Vedanta. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Vivekananda's philosophy emphasized pure Vedanta. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
Vivekananda's philosophy emphasized the truth of all religions. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xa: Vivekananda attended **Chicago** in **1893** and founded the Mission in **1897**.
**Ramakrishna** taught that **Hari, Ram, Allah and Christ** are names of one God.
Vivekananda's thought is called **Neo-Hinduism**.

n8839881fe59.s: Rammohan Roy's Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin, written against idolatry, was in which language?
n8839881fe59.x: Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin ('A Gift to Monotheists') was a Persian work by Rammohan Roy against idolatry.
xa: ⚠ **Tuhfat** + **Mirat-ul-Akhbar** = Persian; **Sambad Kaumudi** = Bengali; **Precepts of Jesus** = English.

n6ccaf8dd6cc.s: Rammohan Roy’s work titled Precepts of Jesus — the Guide to Peace and Happiness was written in:
n6ccaf8dd6cc.x: Precepts of Jesus — the Guide to Peace and Happiness was written in English and presented a rational ethical interpretation of Jesus’s teachings.
n6ccaf8dd6cc.tq: Discriminate among the languages associated with Rammohan Roy’s different books and journals.
xs: **Precepts of Jesus — the Guide to Peace and Happiness** was in **English** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It set out the **rational ethics of Jesus** (**1820**).
xa: **Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin** and **Mirat-ul-Akhbar** — **Persian**.
**Sambad Kaumudi** — **Bengali** weekly.

na38b8a8cf9c.s: The Native Marriage Act of 1872, which legalised inter-caste marriage, is also known as the:
na38b8a8cf9c.x: The Native Marriage Act (Act III of 1872), also called the Brahmo Marriage Act, legalised inter-caste marriage and fixed minimum marriage ages.
xa: It came from **Keshab Chandra Sen**'s efforts.
Ironically, Keshab's **under-age daughter**'s marriage to the **Cooch Behar** prince caused the **1878** split.

nbb6e286fefb.s: After the 1866 split of the Brahmo Samaj, Debendranath Tagore's body came to be known as:
nbb6e286fefb.x: After the 1866 split Debendranath Tagore's body became the Adi Brahmo Samaj, while Keshab Chandra Sen led the Brahmo Samaj of India.
xa: The **Adi Brahmo Samaj** was the **parent body**.
The second split (**1878**) produced the **Sadharan Brahmo Samaj**.

n4b3a65526d8.s: The Sadharan Brahmo Samaj was formed in 1878 primarily because of which development?
o: Debendranath Tagore's rejection of the Upanishads
The introduction of English education by Raja Rammohan Roy
Keshab Chandra Sen's marriage of his under-age daughter to the Cooch Behar prince
Keshab Chandra Sen's opposition to monotheism
n4b3a65526d8.x: The 1878 split followed Keshab Chandra Sen's marriage of his under-age daughter to the Maharaja or prince of Cooch Behar. The Sadharan Brahmo Samaj was associated with Ananda Mohan Bose and Shivnath Shastri.
n4b3a65526d8.tq: Identify the immediate cause of a split rather than confusing it with the ideology of the earlier split.
xs: The **1878** split followed **Keshab**'s **marriage of his under-age daughter** to the **Cooch Behar** prince — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Sadharan Brahmo Samaj** was led by **Ananda Mohan Bose** and **Shivnath Shastri**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly say it was founded "under **Debendranath**".
Keshab's own **Native Marriage Act** (**1872**) had fixed minimum marriage ages.

n1a7c1fb0d7a.s: Who renamed the Brahmo Sabha as the Brahmo Samaj?
n1a7c1fb0d7a.x: Debendranath Tagore renamed it; Rammohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in 1828 with Dwarkanath Tagore.
xa: **Keshab** founded the **Brahmo Samaj of India** (**1866**).
The Atmiya Sabha was the "**Society of Friends**".

n30b6b7a4b07.s: The Sadharan Brahmo Samaj was formed in:
n30b6b7a4b07.x: The Sadharan Brahmo Samaj came in 1878; the Brahmo Samaj of India was formed in 1866, the Prarthana Samaj in 1867 and the Paramahansa Mandali in 1849.
xa: The 1866 body was **Keshab**'s; the 1878 body was led by **Ananda Mohan Bose** and **Shivnath Shastri**.
⚠ **1849** (Mandali) vs **1867** (Prarthana) — the usual swap trap.
The **Prarthana Samaj** reached **Rajahmundry** in **1878**.

nindian-history-58-14.s: Who led the Tattvabodhini Sabha within the Brahmo movement?
nindian-history-58-14.x: Debendranath Tagore led the Tattvabodhini Sabha and the Brahmo movement.
n: Debendranath Tagore is associated with the Tattvabodhini Sabha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Debendranath Tagore is associated with the Brahmo movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Dayanand Saraswati is associated with the Arya Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Ramakrishna Paramahamsa is associated with the unity of religions. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Swami Vivekananda is associated with the Ramakrishna Mission. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
Swami Vivekananda is associated with Vedanta. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 132-134]
xa: Tattvabodhini Sabha was founded in **1839**; its organ the Bengali **Tattvabodhini Patrika**.
Debendranath was called **"Maharishi"**.
Arya Samaj: **1875**, **Mumbai**.

n2fe8e09608a.s: The Bengal Sati Regulation of 1829 was issued as which Regulation of the Bengal Code?
n2fe8e09608a.x: The Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829, was Regulation XVII of the Bengal Code. It declared Sati illegal and punishable.
n2fe8e09608a.tq: Use the exact-number trap by distinguishing the regulation number from nearby legal provisions.
xs: The **Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829** was **Regulation XVII** of the Bengal Code — so option **(3)** is correct.
It declared Sati **illegal and punishable**.
xa: Passed **4 December 1829** under **Lord William Bentinck**.
Exam angle: "Sati was abolished by ..." — **Bentinck**; regulation number **XVII**.

n600d76b30a1.s: The Bengal Sati Regulation of 4 December 1829 was passed under Governor-General:
n600d76b30a1.x: It was passed under Lord William Bentinck and extended to Madras and Bombay in 1830.
xa: ⚠ Trap: not **Munro**, **Minto**, **Curzon**, **Hastings**, **Cornwallis** or **Shore** (APPSC-GS **2019**, **2025**).
**Rammohan Roy**'s long campaign made the ban possible.

nf192ff4d536.s: The orthodox Dharma Sabha, founded in 1830 to oppose the ban on Sati, was set up by:
nf192ff4d536.x: Raja Radhakant Deb founded the Dharma Sabha (1830) against Brahmo propaganda and the Sati ban that Rammohan Roy campaigned for.
xa: The ban: **Regulation XVII**, **4 December 1829**, under **Bentinck**.
The Dharma Sabha opposed both **Brahmo propaganda** and the Sati ban.

nc4fc9e3dc94.s: Keshab Chandra Sen introduced the Nava Vidhan in:
nc4fc9e3dc94.x: Keshab became Acharya in 1862, formed the Brahmo Samaj of India in 1866, founded the Indian Reform Association in 1870 and introduced Nava Vidhan in 1880–81.
xa: The **Native Marriage Act** came in **1872**.
The **Sadharan Brahmo Samaj** broke away in **1878**.

n996767bc86c.s: Who was the first Andhra associated with the Brahmo Samaj?
n996767bc86c.x: Mannava Buchayya Pantulu is identified as the first Andhra associated with the Brahmo Samaj.
n996767bc86c.tq: Distinguish the first Andhra associate from the later Andhra Trinity and organisational promoters.
xs: The first Andhra Brahmo was **Mannava Buchayya Pantulu** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Veeresalingam** and **Desiraju Peda Bapaiah** belong to the Andhra **Trinity**, not the first Brahmo.
xa: Trinity: **Veeresalingam**, **Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu**, **Desiraju Peda Bapaiah**.
Andhra renaissance centre: **Rajahmundry**.

n309d537d158.s: Who among the following formed the Andhra 'Trinity of the Brahma Samaj'?
o: Veeresalingam, Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu and Desiraju Peda Bapaiah
Mannava Buchayya Pantulu, Gurajada Apparao and Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham
Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu, Tanguturi Prakasam and Mannava Buchayya Pantulu
Desiraju Peda Bapaiah, Komarraju Lakshmana Rao and Gurajada Apparao
n309d537d158.x: The Andhra Trinity of the Brahma Samaj was Veeresalingam, Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu and Desiraju Peda Bapaiah, so A. Mannava Buchayya Pantulu was the first Andhra Brahmo but not one of the Trinity. The other names in B, C and D are not part of it.
n309d537d158.tq: Trinity = Veeresalingam, Venkataratnam Naidu, Peda Bapaiah.
xs: The Andhra "**Trinity of the Brahma Samaj**" = **Veeresalingam**, **Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu**, **Desiraju Peda Bapaiah** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Mannava Buchayya Pantulu** was the **first Andhra Brahmo**, not one of the Trinity.
xa: **Veeresalingam** set up the earliest Andhra Prarthana Samaj at **Rajahmundry** (**1878**).
Bengal was the first region to have a renaissance; in Andhra, **Rajahmundry**.

o: The authority of a single scripture
n7a30fe0a970.x: The Brahmo Samaj believed in one formless, eternal God, rejected avatars and treated no scripture as final authority.
xa: It drew on the **Upanishads, Bible and Koran**.
A theistic (**Astika**) reform within Hinduism, not a new religion.

n88c5f72943b.s: Which of the following was banned in the halls of the Brahmo Samaj?
n88c5f72943b.x: Idols and animal sacrifice were banned in Brahmo halls; it rejected priestly ritualism and caste and practised collective prayer.
xa: It held **no heaven or hell**.
**Jivatma** and **Paramatma** are not one.

nindian-history-51-53.s: Ramakrishna Paramahamsa regarded Hari, Ram, Allah and Christ as:
o: Different names for the same God
nindian-history-51-53.x: He saw them as names of one God because he taught the unity behind all religions.
n: Ramakrishna Paramahamsa taught that Hari, Ram, Allah, and Christ are different names for the same God. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 121-126]
xa: His disciple **Swami Vivekananda** founded the **Ramakrishna Mission** (**1897**).
Ramakrishna **provided spiritual inspiration** for Vivekananda.
Brahmo Samaj = **reformist**; Arya Samaj = **revivalist**.

n81b60bf799a.s: The earliest Prarthana Samaj centre in Andhra was set up at Rajahmundry in 1878 by:
n81b60bf799a.x: Veeresalingam set up the first Andhra Prarthana Samaj centre at Rajahmundry in 1878; the Samaj itself was founded in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang.
xa: First Andhra Brahmo: **Mannava Buchayya Pantulu**.
Andhra "Trinity": **Veeresalingam**, **Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu**, **Desiraju Peda Bapaiah**.

n7015629bfcd.s: Which one of the following organisations was founded in Poona in 1849 to oppose caste distinctions and promote women’s education?
n7015629bfcd.x: Paramahansa Mandali was founded by Dadoba Pandurang in 1849 and was associated with opposition to caste distinctions and support for women’s education.
n7015629bfcd.tq: Identify the organisation by combining its place, year and reform objective.
xs: The **Paramahansa Mandali** was founded in **Poona** in **1849** against caste and for women's education — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2023**).
**Tattvabodhini** (**1839**) and **Dharma Sabha** (**1830**) were in **Calcutta**; the **Prarthana Samaj** dates from **1867**.
xa: Founder: **Dadoba Pandurang** (APP: "**Tadoba Panduranga Tarkad**").
**1848**: the **Phules' girls' school**, Pune.

nafd12c9867b.s: Among the following reformers, whose major contributions came earliest?
nafd12c9867b.x: The chronological order is Rammohan Roy, Vidyasagar, Jyotiba Phule and Dayanand Saraswati.
xa: Markers: **Sati** **1829**; **Widow Remarriage Act** **1856**; **Satyashodhak Samaj** **1873**; **Arya Samaj** **1875**.
Phule also ran a **girls' school** in Pune (**1848**).

n67fd300eaa9.s: Which of the following is classed as a revivalist movement?
n67fd300eaa9.x: The Arya Samaj (like Deoband) is classed as revivalist, whereas the Brahmo and Prarthana Samaj were reformist movements based on reason.
xa: The Brahmo Samaj stood for **reason** and **modern ideas**.
It **attacked superstition** and laid the base for **nationalism**.

ne8f8e834467.s: In the context of the Andhra renaissance, which place is identified as its centre?
ne8f8e834467.x: Rajahmundry is identified as the place associated with the first renaissance in Andhra.
ne8f8e834467.tq: Separate the Andhra-specific first from the later Brahmo Samaj centres and dates.
xs: **Rajahmundry** is the Andhra renaissance centre — so option **(2)** is correct.
The earliest Andhra **Prarthana Samaj** came up there in **1878** under **Veeresalingam** (APPSC **2019**).
xa: Andhra "**Trinity of the Brahma Samaj**": **Veeresalingam**, **Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu**, **Desiraju Peda Bapaiah**.
First Andhra Brahmo: **Mannava Buchayya Pantulu**.

nindian-history-97-11.x: Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission; the Prarthana Samaj is linked with Atmaram Pandurang and Ranade.
n: Raja Rammohan Roy is associated with the Brahmo Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Raja Rammohan Roy is associated with the abolition of Sati. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Dayanand Saraswati is associated with the Arya Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan is associated with the Aligarh Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Swami Vivekananda is associated with the Ramakrishna Mission. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
M.G. Ranade is associated with the Prarthana Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
xa: Sati was abolished in **1829** under **Lord William Bentinck** (**Regulation XVII**).
**Jyotiba Phule** — **Satyashodhak Samaj**.
**Shiv Narayan Agnihotri** — **Dev Samaj**.

nindian-history-120-24.x: Shiv Narayan Agnihotri founded the Dev Samaj; Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj.
n: Savitribai Phule was associated with women's education. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
Atmaram Pandurang was associated with the Prarthana Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
Shiv Narayan Agnihotri was associated with the Dev Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was associated with the Aligarh Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
xa: **B.R. Ambedkar** — **Neo-Buddhist/Dalit Buddhist Movement**.
**M.G. Ranade** — **Indian National Social Conference**.
The **Phules' girls' school** in **Pune** dates from **1848**.

n86d9968d3cc.s: The forum associated with the followers of Derozio was the—
n86d9968d3cc.x: The Derozians used the Academic Association as their forum for discussion and intellectual activity.
n86d9968d3cc.tq: Match the movement’s followers with their specific forum.
xs: The Derozians' forum for debate was the **Academic Association** (Calcutta, **1828**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Manav Dharma Sabha** was **Durgaram Mancharam**'s (Surat); the **National Social Conference** and **Poona Sarvajanik Sabha** were **Ranade**'s.
xa: Founder: **Henry Louis Vivian Derozio**.
APPSC-GS **2022** match: **Derozio — Young Bengal**.

n6fda159366f.s: Who among the following was associated with the Prarthana Samaj, Widow Remarriage Association, Poona Sarvajanik Sabha, Deccan Education Society and National Social Conference?
n6fda159366f.x: Justice M.G. Ranade was associated with all the listed reform organisations and bodies. He also advocated the close connection between religious and social reform.
n6fda159366f.tq: Identify the reformer from a cluster of institutional associations.
xs: **Justice M.G. Ranade** links all these bodies — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Widow Remarriage Association** (**1861**), **Poona Sarvajanik Sabha** (**1870**), **National Social Conference** (**1887**).
He supported the **Deccan Education Society** (Pune, **1884**) and led the **Prarthana Samaj**.
xa: His view: **social and religious reform go together**.
**Bhandarkar** joined the Prarthana Samaj but not these other bodies in the notes.

n00e516b5048.s: According to M.G. Ranade, social reform and religious reform should:
o: Be left entirely to the state
n00e516b5048.x: Ranade held that rigid religious belief obstructed progress and that social and religious reform were interrelated and should go together.
xa: He founded the **National Social Conference** (**1887**).
He was linked to **Induprakash**.

n2470cfc8e41.s: The National Social Conference met at the same time and place as the sessions of the:
n2470cfc8e41.x: Founded in 1887 by Ranade with Raghunath Rao, it met alongside the Congress sessions to discuss social reform.
xa: Reason: the INC kept to **political issues**.

n64e6ee0a0ad.s: The Deccan Education Society was founded at Pune by Tilak, Agarkar and Chiplunkar, with Ranade's support, in:
n64e6ee0a0ad.x: The Deccan Education Society was founded in Pune in 1884 with M.G. Ranade's support.
xa: Ranade's other bodies: **Poona Sarvajanik Sabha** (**1870**), **National Social Conference** (**1887**).
**1861** is the **Widow Remarriage Association**.

n30ac815ac85.s: Kandukuri Veeresalingam founded the first Prarthana Samaj in Andhra in 1878 at:
n30ac815ac85.x: Veeresalingam founded it at Rajahmundry in 1878 (APHQ 2019), and K. Seethamma later organised its women's wing. Machilipatnam, Guntur and Visakhapatnam were not the site of the first centre.
xs: **Kandukuri Veeresalingam** founded the first Andhra Prarthana Samaj at **Rajahmundry** in **1878** — so option **(3)** is correct (APHQ **2019**).
**Machilipatnam**, **Guntur** and **Visakhapatnam** were not its site.
xa: **K. Seethamma** organised its **women's wing**.
It held **weekly prayers for women of all castes**.

n3a0716f5c76.s: The Young Bengal Movement stood for:
o: Loyalty to idol worship and caste
Radical rationalism and criticism of social orthodoxy
n3a0716f5c76.x: Young Bengal stood for radical rationalism, opposed idol worship, casteism and decadent customs, and supported women's rights and education.
xa: It was inspired by the **French Revolution**.
Comparative note: **Young Bengal = radical**; Prarthana Samaj = milder.

ne3cb71cf56b.s: The Young Bengal Movement was particularly inspired by the—
ne3cb71cf56b.x: The ideas of the Young Bengal Movement were inspired by the French Revolution and its emphasis on reason and liberty.
ne3cb71cf56b.tq: Link the intellectual movement with its stated historical inspiration.
xs: **Young Bengal** was inspired by the **French Revolution** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its ideas were **radical, rationalist, iconoclastic**.
xa: It attacked **idol worship** and **casteism**.
Leader: **Henry Louis Vivian Derozio**; followers: **Derozians**.

n22df1569d82.s: Henry Vivian Derozio was dismissed from Hindu College in:
n22df1569d82.x: Derozio was dismissed from Hindu College in 1831 and died the same year.
xa: He taught at Hindu College in the **late 1820s**.
The **Academic Association** was set up in **1828**.

o: Secret society that believed in one God
n707ee5f8410.x: It was a secret society believing in one God; its members broke caste rules and supported women's education and widow remarriage.
xa: Founded **1849** by **Dadoba Pandurang**.
⚠ **1849** = Paramahansa Mandali (secret); **1867** = Prarthana Samaj.

n4575f435181.s: Who were associated with the founding of Paramahansa Mandali?
n4575f435181.x: Paramahansa Mandali was founded by Dadoba Pandurang along with Durgaram Mancharam of the Manav Dharma Sabha of Surat.
n4575f435181.tq: Use the paired-founder clue and distinguish it from leaders of other reform movements.
xs: **Dadoba Pandurang** with **Durgaram Mancharam** (Manav Dharma Sabha, **Surat**) founded the **Paramahansa Mandali** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ranade** and **Bhandarkar** led the **Prarthana Samaj**; **Tilak** and **Agarkar** the **Deccan Education Society**.
xa: Founded **1849** in **Bombay**, with branches at **Poona** and **Satara**.
It was a **secret society**.

n4120793e71d.s: The establishment of Prarthana Samaj in Bombay in 1867 was influenced by the visit of—
n4120793e71d.x: Prarthana Samaj was inspired by the visit of Keshab Chandra Sen and was established in Bombay in 1867.
n4120793e71d.tq: Use the inspiration–organisation association rather than confusing different reform leaders.
xs: The **Prarthana Samaj** (**1867**, Bombay) was inspired by **Keshab Chandra Sen**'s visit — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Derozio** led **Young Bengal**; **Dayananda** founded the **Arya Samaj** (**1875**).
xa: Founder: **Dr. Atmaram Pandurang**.
Leaders: **M.G. Ranade**, **R.G. Bhandarkar**.

n7a5087be72f.s: Who were the principal leaders of the Prarthana Samaj in Maharashtra?
n7a5087be72f.x: M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar were prominent leaders of the Prarthana Samaj in Maharashtra.
n7a5087be72f.tq: Identify the correct leadership pair instead of its founder alone.
xs: **M.G. Ranade** and **R.G. Bhandarkar** led the **Prarthana Samaj** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Dadoba Pandurang** and **Durgaram Mancharam** founded the **Paramahansa Mandali**; **Tilak** and **Chiplunkar** the **Deccan Education Society**.
xa: Bhandarkar joined in **1870**.
Founder: **Dr. Atmaram Pandurang** (**1867**).

nd9aad66ebc1.s: The Prarthana Samaj pursued its reform agenda mainly through:
nd9aad66ebc1.x: It worked through persuasion and social work; its aims included raising the age of marriage and uplift of the depressed classes.
xa: Four points: against **caste**; **women's education**; **widow remarriage**; **age of marriage**.
Other aims: **inter-dining**, **inter-marriage**.

nc07545803c7.s: Unlike the Brahmo Samaj, the Prarthana Samaj:
o: Did not outright forbid idol worship or abandon caste practices
Required its members to leave Hindu society
nc07545803c7.x: The Prarthana Samaj focused mainly on social reform and did not outright forbid idol worship or abandon caste as the Brahmos did.
xa: ⚠ p.**83** claims it rejected idol worship — treat p.84 as safe.
Its method: **persuasion and social work**, not confrontation.

n5e09308b603.s: Pandita Ramabai's Sharada Sadan was a:
n5e09308b603.x: Sharada Sadan was a home for widows; the secret society against caste was the Paramahansa Mandali.
xa: **Arya Samaj** — true knowledge of the **Vedas**; **Satyashodhak** — social justice for "**untouchables**".
**Prarthana Samaj** — improvement of **women** and **depressed classes**.

nf3cb2a713ee.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the reform movements of western and eastern India?
o: Paramahansa Mandali functioned as an open public organisation
Prarthana Samaj was influenced by the Brahmo Samaj but followed a milder approach
Young Bengal represented a radical reform tendency
Satyashodhak Samaj focused on anti-Brahmanical reform and the uplift of lower castes
nf3cb2a713ee.x: The Paramahansa Mandali functioned as a secret organisation, not an open one.
xa: Prarthana Samaj worked by **persuasion and social work**.
Young Bengal was **radical, rationalist, iconoclastic**.

n6c2ea9d93b5.s: Who started the Marathi paper Darpan in 1832?
n6c2ea9d93b5.x: Bal Shastri Jambhekar started the Marathi paper Darpan in 1832 and attacked Brahmanical orthodoxy.
n6c2ea9d93b5.tq: Match the journal with its reformer and use the associated year as confirmation.
xs: **Bal Shastri Jambhekar** started the Marathi paper **Darpan** (**1832**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
He attacked **Brahmanical orthodoxy** in **Bombay** (APPSC-G2 **2017**).
xa: **Gopal Hari Deshmukh** = "**Lokahitawadi**"; **Ranade** — **Induprakash**.
**Dnyanodaya** was a Marathi **Christian missionary** journal.

n56cc8f8bfe3.x: Gopal Hari Deshmukh wrote as Lokahitawadi, and his Shatapatre (hundred letters) appeared in the weekly Prabhakar. Jambhekar started Darpan, Ranade was linked to Induprakash, and Bhandarkar was a Sanskrit scholar.
xs: "**Lokahitawadi**" was **Gopal Hari Deshmukh** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2021**, G2 **2008**).
**Jambhekar** started **Darpan**; **Ranade** — **Induprakash**; **Bhandarkar** was a **Sanskrit scholar**.
xa: His **Shatapatre** appeared in the weekly **Prabhakar**.
Jambhekar's **Darpan** dates from **1832**.

nindian-history-95-1.s: The Satyashodhak Samaj primarily aimed at which of the following?
o: Distribution of land to landless farmers
Upliftment of backward classes and liberation of Shudras and Ati-Shudras
nindian-history-95-1.x: Phule's Satyashodhak Samaj aimed to uplift the backward classes and free Shudras and Ati-Shudras from exploitation. Land gifts belong to Bhoodan, and modern Muslim education to Aligarh.
nindian-history-95-1.tq: Recall the aim of each movement.
n: Satyashodhak Samaj aimed to uplift backward classes. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
Satyashodhak Samaj aimed to liberate Shudras and Ati-Shudras. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
Aligarh Movement promoted modern education among Muslims. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
Bhoodan Movement aimed to distribute land to landless farmers. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
Home Rule Movement aimed at self-government for India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
xs: The **Satyashodhak Samaj** aimed at **upliftment of backward classes** and **liberation of Shudras and Ati-Shudras** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Distribution of land to landless farmers** was the **Bhoodan Movement**; **modern education among Muslims** was the **Aligarh Movement**.
xa: The Satyashodhak Samaj worked for **social justice** for the "untouchables" (APPSC-GS **2023**).
**Prarthana Samaj** **opposed** the **caste system** and supported **widow remarriage**.
**Sharada Sadan** (**Pandita Ramabai**) — a home for widows.

nindian-history-95-6.s: Which organisation sought to make the Congress more revolutionary and to organise the common people?
nindian-history-95-6.x: The Workers and Peasants Party sought a more radical Congress; the Radhasoami Satsang stressed one God, the Guru, Satsang and spiritual life.
n: Radhasoami Satsang emphasized belief in one God. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
Radhasoami Satsang emphasized the importance of the Guru and Satsang. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
Radhasoami Satsang emphasized spiritual life. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
Workers and Peasants Party aimed to make the Congress more revolutionary. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
Workers and Peasants Party aimed to organize common people. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
xa: **Bhoodan Movement** — to **distribute land** to **landless farmers**.
**Aligarh Movement** — **modern education** among Muslims.
**Deoband** — **religious education** among Muslims.

n51b4fb2a5de.x: Dayananda Saraswati’s original name was Mool Shankar Tiwari.
n51b4fb2a5de.tq: Discriminate between the original names of Arya Samaj personalities.
xs: Dayananda Saraswati was born as **Mool Shankar Tiwari** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He was born at **Tankara** in **Kathiawar, Gujarat**, and lived **1824-1883**.
xa: His guru was **Swami Virajananda** (Virjanand) of **Mathura**.
He died at **Ajmer** in **1883**.
Titles: **"Martin Luther of India"** (given by **Lala Lajpat Rai**) and **"Grandfather of the Indian Nation"**.

nbd9ea9b7db6.x: He died at Ajmer; Lahore was only the later headquarters of the Arya Samaj, and his guru Virajananda was of Mathura.
xa: His original name was **Mool Shankar** (Tiwari), born at **Tankara**, Kathiawar, **Gujarat**.
He founded the **Arya Samaj** at **Bombay** in **1875**; its strongest base became **Punjab**.
⚠ Trap: Arya Samaj was founded in **Bombay**, not Calcutta or Lahore.

n178be40ead2.s: Who called Dayananda Saraswati the 'Martin Luther of India'?
n178be40ead2.x: Lala Lajpat Rai gave him the title; Dayananda gave the slogan 'India for the Indians' and is credited with first using the term Swaraj.
xa: His other title: **"Grandfather of the Indian Nation"**.
His other slogan: **"Back to the Vedas"** ("Go Back to the Vedas").
He wrote his main work, **Satyarth Prakash**, in **Hindi**.

nadd1eb97f4a.s: The slogan ‘Back to the Vedas’ implied that Dayananda Saraswati regarded the Vedas as:
o: Political documents of the colonial state
Texts limited exclusively to ritual practices
Infallible and the primordial word of God
nadd1eb97f4a.x: The slogan expressed the belief that the four Vedas were infallible and constituted the primordial word of God.
nadd1eb97f4a.tq: Infer the doctrine from the exact meaning of the slogan.
xs: "Back to the Vedas" held the four Vedas **infallible** — the **primordial word of God** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He **rejected** later **Puranic** accretions (myths, rituals, idol worship), so option (2) is the opposite.
xa: He claimed the Vedas contained **all true knowledge, including science**.
This countered the colonial idea of **Western intellectual superiority**.
The slogan is set out in **Satyarth Prakash** (**1875**, **Hindi**).

n01a3ec3efa2.s: The title ‘Satyarth Prakash’ is generally translated as:
n01a3ec3efa2.x: Satyarth Prakash means ‘The Light of Truth’; it is also rendered as ‘The True Exposition’.
n01a3ec3efa2.tq: Choose the precise translation of the title.
xs: **Satyarth Prakash** means **"The Light of Truth"** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is also rendered as **"The True Exposition"**.
xa: Author: **Dayananda Saraswati**, **1875**, in **Hindi**.
It set out his religious and social philosophy and critiqued **Hindu orthodoxy** and other religions.
Its core idea: **"Back to the Vedas"** — Vedas infallible, Puranic accretions rejected.

nc521949c701.s: Arya Samaj was founded at which place in 1875?
nc521949c701.x: Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati at Bombay in 1875. Its headquarters were later shifted to Lahore.
nc521949c701.tq: Distinguish the place of founding from the later headquarters.
xs: The Arya Samaj was founded at **Bombay** in **1875** (April) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Lahore** became its HQ only later; **Calcutta** is a classic trap.
xa: Founding date: some notes give **7 April 1875**; many texts give **10 April 1875**.
Founder: **Swami Dayananda Saraswati**; name means **"Society of Nobles"**.
Strongest base: **Punjab**; also strong in **Rajasthan** and **United Provinces**.
⚠ Statement traps: "founded in Calcutta" (wrong) and "promotes idol worship" (wrong; it rejects it).

n4048e7db62a.s: Which of the following was rejected by the Ten Principles of the Arya Samaj?
n4048e7db62a.x: The Ten Principles emphasised truth, rational thought, moral conduct and the welfare of all; the Arya Samaj rejected caste based on birth.
xa: The **Ten Principles** were drafted by **Dayananda Saraswati** himself.
The Samaj also rejected **idol worship**, **polytheism** and **ritualism**.
It supported **widow remarriage**, **inter-caste marriage** and **women's education**.

nb65abb1cd54.s: Which organisation came to be regarded as a 'nursery of militant nationalists', influencing Lala Lajpat Rai and Swami Shraddhanand?
nb65abb1cd54.x: The Arya Samaj influenced Lala Lajpat Rai, Swami Shraddhanand and Bhagat Singh's family, earning this description.
xa: **Lala Lajpat Rai** called Dayananda the **"Martin Luther of India"**.
**Swami Shraddhanand** led the 1920s **Shuddhi** campaign via the **Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha (1923)**; assassinated in **1926**.
Significance: revivalism + reform; built **Hindu self-confidence**; fed **militant nationalism**.

n6c6ca17a2c8.s: Which of the following subjects was NOT a theme of Satyarth Prakash?
o: Critique of idolatry and caste by birth
Religious and social philosophy of Dayananda
n6c6ca17a2c8.x: Satyarth Prakash presented Dayananda’s religious and social philosophy and criticised Hindu orthodoxy, idolatry, caste by birth and child marriage.
n6c6ca17a2c8.tq: Use the reversal trap involving orthodoxy and reform.
xs: **Advocacy of unquestioned Hindu orthodoxy** was NOT a theme — the book **critiqued** orthodoxy — so option **(4)** is correct.
It did set out his **religious and social philosophy** and attacked **idolatry**, **caste by birth** and **child marriage** — options (1)-(3).
xa: It also critiqued **other religions**.
Written in **Hindi** in **1875**; title means **"The Light of Truth"**.
It rejected the **Puranas'** later accretions — myths, rituals, idol worship.

nbbe0916e50e.s: The Shuddhi movement, to reconvert those who had converted to Islam or Christianity, was started by the:
nbbe0916e50e.x: Shuddhi was started by the Arya Samaj to reconvert converts and admit outsiders into the Hindu fold.
xa: ⚠ "Shuddhi was started by ___" → **Arya Samaj** (not Brahmo Samaj, Satyashodhak Samaj or Ramakrishna Mission).
Later leader: **Swami Shraddhanand**, via the **Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha (1923)**.
Impact: contributed to the **communalisation** of social life.

n50c4fce5060.s: Who led the Shuddhi campaign of the 1920s through the Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha?
n50c4fce5060.x: Swami Shraddhanand led the Shuddhi campaign of the 1920s through the Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha, formed in 1923.
n50c4fce5060.tq: Match the later leader with the specific organisation and campaign.
xs: **Swami Shraddhanand** led the 1920s Shuddhi campaign through the **Bharatiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Sabha was formed in **1923**; Shraddhanand was **assassinated in 1926**.
xa: Shuddhi was started by the **Arya Samaj** — ritual "purification" to reconvert converts to **Islam or Christianity**.
Shraddhanand is among the **"militant nationalists"** the Samaj nurtured, with **Lala Lajpat Rai**.
Impact: Shuddhi fed **communal political consciousness**.

nab05e123184.s: The Arya Samaj satyagraha in Hyderabad State during 1938–39 was directed against:
o: The Nizam’s curbs on religious and civil rights
The educational policies of the Government of India
The abolition of zamindari in coastal Andhra
nab05e123184.x: In 1938–39, Arya Samaj conducted a satyagraha in Hyderabad State against the Nizam’s restrictions on religious and civil rights.
nab05e123184.tq: Link the movement, region, period and immediate grievance.
xs: The **1938-39** Hyderabad satyagraha opposed **the Nizam's curbs on religious and civil rights** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was led by the **Arya Samaj** in **Hyderabad State**.
xa: It ran alongside the **Hyderabad State Congress** satyagraha.
Impact: built **political awakening against Nizam rule** in the **Telangana** region.
AP angle: Arya Samaj had great influence on **women's upliftment in Andhra**.

n3204b320652.s: Ramakrishna Paramahansa was associated as a mystic and priest with the:
n3204b320652.x: Ramakrishna Paramahansa served as a mystic and priest at the Dakshineswar Kali Temple near Calcutta.
n3204b320652.tq: Identify the religious figure through his principal place of association.
xs: Ramakrishna Paramahansa was a mystic and priest of the **Kali Temple at Dakshineswar**, near Calcutta — so option **(4)** is correct.
xa: Original name: **Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya**; wife: **Sarada Devi**.
Gurus: **Bhairavi Brahmani** (Tantra) and **Totapuri** (Advaita).
His saying **"as many faiths, so many paths"** — all religions lead to the same truth.

n5bbef67d4ec.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the teachings of Ramakrishna Paramahansa?
o: Salvation could be pursued through devotion, meditation and renunciation
'As many faiths, so many paths' means all religions lead to the same truth
Salvation was possible only through renunciation and never through devotion
Hari, Ram, Allah and Christ are different names for the same God
n5bbef67d4ec.x: Devotion was itself one of his paths to salvation, alongside meditation and renunciation, so it was not excluded.
xa: Vivekananda's **Practical Vedanta**: serving the poor = serving God (**"Daridra Narayana"**).
RKM motto: **"Atmano Mokshartham Jagat Hitaya Cha"** — for one's own liberation and the welfare of the world.

n267a3b0c261.x: Vivekananda was born Narendranath Datta in Calcutta on 12 January 1863; Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya was Ramakrishna's birth name.
xa: Vivekananda died in **1902**.
His birthday, **12 January**, is **National Youth Day**.
Titles: **"Prophet of Indian Nationalism"**, **"Maker of Modern India"**.

nd10974796d9.s: Swami Vivekananda’s birthday is observed in India as:
nd10974796d9.x: 12 January, the birthday of Swami Vivekananda, is observed as National Youth Day.
nd10974796d9.tq: Link the precise date-based observance with the correct national day.
xs: Vivekananda's birthday, **12 January**, is observed as **National Youth Day** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was born **Narendranath Datta** in **Calcutta** in **1863**.
xa: His ideas stressed **strength, self-confidence, youth** for national regeneration.
Titles: **"Prophet of Indian Nationalism"** and **"Maker of Modern India"**.
He died in **1902**.

n12b94f40235.s: Swami Vivekananda established Vedanta Societies in:
n12b94f40235.x: Vivekananda established Vedanta Societies in the United States of America and Britain.
n12b94f40235.tq: Recall the two-country institutional association given for the reformer.
xs: Vivekananda set up Vedanta Societies in **the USA and Britain** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The first was the **Vedanta Society of New York** (**1894**).
xa: He spoke at **Chicago** in **1893**, representing **Hinduism**.
His Western disciple: **Margaret Noble (Sister Nivedita)**.
On return he founded the **Ramakrishna Mission** (**1897**).

n40c8445fa21.s: Who among the following was the Western disciple of Swami Vivekananda known as Sister Nivedita?
n40c8445fa21.x: Margaret Noble became the well-known Western disciple of Vivekananda under the name Sister Nivedita.
n40c8445fa21.tq: Match the adopted religious name with the original personal name.
xs: **Margaret Noble** was Vivekananda's Western disciple, known as **Sister Nivedita** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Blavatsky** co-founded the Theosophical Society; **Annie Besant** led it; **Sarada Devi** was Ramakrishna's wife.
xa: Vivekananda set up **Vedanta Societies** in the **USA and Britain** (New York, **1894**).
Titles: **"Prophet of Indian Nationalism"**, **"Maker of Modern India"**.
Born **Narendranath Datta** (**1863**); died **1902**.

nfea1d926e2d.s: The expression ‘daridra narayana’, associated with the practical Vedanta of the Ramakrishna Mission, refers to:
nfea1d926e2d.x: ‘Daridra narayana’ expresses the idea that service to the poor is service to God.
nfea1d926e2d.tq: Discriminate between a service-oriented expression and the philosophical doctrines of the Theosophical Society.
xs: **Daridra narayana** means **God manifest in the poor** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It underlies **Practical Vedanta**: **"Service to mankind is service to God"**.
xa: Vivekananda: serving the poor = **serving God**.
⚠ **Rebirth** and **study of ancient religions** are Theosophical beliefs, not this idea.
RKM motto: **"for one's own liberation and the welfare of the world"**.

n223e36ed5c7.s: Swami Vivekananda is described as the:
n223e36ed5c7.x: Vivekananda is called the 'Prophet of Indian Nationalism' and the 'Maker of Modern India'; the other titles belong to other personalities.
xa: His Western disciple: **Margaret Noble (Sister Nivedita)**.
He set up **Vedanta Societies** in the **USA and Britain** — **Vedanta Society of New York (1894)**.
He made **humanitarian relief** a monastic duty.

naca1fe89e5b.s: Who represented Jainism at the Chicago Parliament of Religions?
naca1fe89e5b.x: Virchand Gandhi represented Jainism; Mozoomdar the Brahmo Samaj, Dharmapala Buddhism (Ceylon) and Vivekananda Hinduism.
xa: The event: **World's Parliament of Religions, Chicago, 1893**.
Vivekananda opened with **"Sisters and Brothers of America"** on **11 Sep 1893**.
Before Chicago he meditated on the **Kanyakumari** rock (**Dec 1892**).

ndd1a5bd2760.s: Swami Vivekananda’s opening words at the Chicago Parliament of Religions were:
ndd1a5bd2760.x: Vivekananda began his address with ‘Sisters and Brothers of America’, which received wide acclaim.
ndd1a5bd2760.tq: Recall the exact famous opening phrase instead of a synonymous greeting.
xs: His opening words were **"Sisters and Brothers of America"** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Delivered at the **World's Parliament of Religions, Chicago**, on **11 Sep 1893**; it won wide acclaim.
xa: He represented **Hinduism** there.
Other participants: **P.C. Mozoomdar** (Brahmo Samaj), **Virchand Gandhi** (Jain), **Anagarika Dharmapala** (Buddhist, Ceylon).
In **Feb 1893** he spoke at **Mahboob College, Secunderabad**.

n447d7d2a209.s: Swami Vivekananda regarded humanitarian relief as:
o: The duty of the state alone
n447d7d2a209.x: Vivekananda regarded humanitarian relief as a monastic duty, condemned caste discrimination and condemned empty ritual.
xa: He stressed **strength, self-confidence, youth** for national regeneration.
**Practical Vedanta**: serving the poor = serving God (**"Daridra Narayana"**).

n56e029cd0be.s: Lectures from Colombo to Almora is associated with speeches delivered by Swami Vivekananda after his return in 1897 through:
n56e029cd0be.x: The work is based on speeches delivered after Vivekananda’s 1897 return through Colombo, Ramnad and Madras.
n56e029cd0be.tq: Identify the correct travel route attached to a published work.
xs: **Lectures from Colombo to Almora** are speeches after his **1897** return via **Colombo, Ramnad and Madras** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He had been in the West since the **Chicago** Parliament of **1893**.
xa: Soon after this return he founded the **Ramakrishna Mission** (**1 May 1897**).
His journals: **Prabuddha Bharata** (English) and **Udbodhan** (Bengali).
Other works: **Karma Yoga**, **Raja Yoga**, **Jnana Yoga**, **My Master**.

na296df01c75.s: Ramakrishna Mission has its headquarters at which of the following places?
o: Belur Math on the Hooghly near Howrah
na296df01c75.x: The headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission is at Belur Math, situated on the Hooghly near Howrah.
na296df01c75.tq: Use the location clue to distinguish the headquarters from the founder’s temple and other reform institutions.
xs: The RKM headquarters is **Belur Math on the Hooghly near Howrah** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Adyar** is the Theosophical Society's Indian HQ; **Dakshineswar** was Ramakrishna's temple; the **Central Hindu College** was Besant's.
xa: **Belur Math** was established in **1898**; permanent HQ of the **Ramakrishna Order**.
Its architecture blends **Hindu, Islamic and Christian** motifs → unity of religions.
**Ramakrishna Mission** founded **1 May 1897** at **Belur (Howrah)**.

n388da433b69.s: The motto of the Ramakrishna Mission, ‘Atmano Mokshartham Jagat Hitaya Cha’, signifies:
o: For one’s own liberation and the welfare of the world
n388da433b69.x: The motto means ‘for one’s own liberation and the welfare of the world’.
n388da433b69.tq: Test the exact meaning of a distinctive institutional motto rather than its general theme.
xs: **"Atmano Mokshartham Jagat Hitaya Cha"** means **for one's own liberation and the welfare of the world** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Universal brotherhood** and comparative religion were **Theosophical** aims, not this motto.
xa: RKM's **Practical Vedanta**: **"Service to mankind is service to God"**.
**Daridra narayana** = God in the poor.
⚠ **"Back to the Vedas"** = Arya Samaj slogan, not RKM.

nae0896cbdbf.s: Which of the following forms part of the practical work of the Ramakrishna Mission?
nae0896cbdbf.x: The Mission runs schools, colleges, hospitals and orphanages and provides famine and disaster relief; its work is not exclusively ritualistic.
xa: Two wings: a **monastic order** and **lay disciples** doing preaching, philanthropy, humanitarian work.
Vivekananda made **humanitarian relief** a monastic duty.
Current: RKM's **Vivekananda Human Excellence Centre**, **Vijayawada** (**₹8.5 crore**), inaugurated **1 Feb 2026**.

n3825ddf7ca2.s: In which year did Swami Vivekananda found the Ramakrishna Mission?
n3825ddf7ca2.x: Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897, soon after returning from the West, and named it after his guru. 1879 is a common wrong version of 1897; 1875 is the founding year of the Arya Samaj and the Theosophical Society; 1902 is the year Vivekananda died.
n3825ddf7ca2.tq: RKM = 1 May 1897, not 1879; Belur Math HQ came in 1898.
xs: Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in **1897** (**1 May 1897**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1879** is the classic wrong version; **1875** = Arya Samaj and Theosophical Society; **1902** = Vivekananda's death.
xa: He founded it soon after returning from the West and **named it after his guru**.
Place: **Belur (Howrah)**; **Belur Math** followed in **1898**.
⚠ "Founded the Ramakrishna Mission in **1879**" is a WRONG statement.

n637d2bcb3a2.s: Which of the following were core beliefs of the Theosophical Society?
n637d2bcb3a2.x: Karma and reincarnation were core beliefs; the Society drew on the Upanishads, Samkhya, Yoga and Vedanta and condemned child marriage.
xa: Aims: **universal brotherhood**; comparative religion.
Theosophy led straight into **Home Rule** politics.

nd3f278dd816.s: The Arya Samaj regarded idol worship as:
nd3f278dd816.x: The Arya Samaj considered idol worship useless; it opposed caste by birth and held that all people could read the Vedas.
xa: It believed in **One God** and opposed **child marriage**.
Its **Shuddhi** movement aimed at **reconversion** to Hinduism.
Text: **Satyarth Prakash**; slogan: **"Back to the Vedas"**.

nindian-history-127-5.s: 'Go Back to the Vedas' was the call of the:
nindian-history-127-5.x: The Arya Samaj said 'Go Back to the Vedas'; the Brahmo Samaj stood for worship of one God and the Theosophical Society for universal brotherhood.
n: Arya Samaj used the slogan “Go Back to the Vedas.” [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #127 · pp 230-231]
Brahmo Samaj promoted universal worship of one God. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #127 · pp 230-231]
Ramakrishna Mission used the phrase “Atmano Mokshartham Jagad Hitaya Cha.” [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #127 · pp 230-231]
The Theosophical Society promoted the universal brotherhood of humanity. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #127 · pp 230-231]
xa: The RKM motto means "**for one's own liberation** and for the **welfare** of the **world**".
Arya Samaj also used "**India is for the Indians**".
**Divya Gnana Samajam** is the **Telugu name** of the Theosophical Society.

nindian-history-127-20.s: The motto 'Atmano Mokshartham Jagad Hitaya Cha' belongs to the:
nindian-history-127-20.x: It is the Ramakrishna Mission's motto; the Theosophical Society stood for universal brotherhood and the Servants of India Society for constitutional service.
n: Ramakrishna Mission used the phrase “Atmano Mokshartham Jagad Hitaya Cha.” [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #127 · pp 230-231]
The Theosophical Society promoted the universal brotherhood of humanity. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #127 · pp 230-231]
Satyashodhak Samaj promoted truth-seeking. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #127 · pp 230-231]
Satyashodhak Samaj promoted social equality. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #127 · pp 230-231]
Servants of India Society promoted service of India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #127 · pp 230-231]
Servants of India Society used constitutional methods. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #127 · pp 230-231]
xa: Servants of India Society: **1905**, **Poona**, **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**.
RKM: "**Service to mankind is service to God**" — **daridra narayana**.
Satyashodhak Samaj: **1873**, **Jyotiba Phule**.

nindian-history-132-6.s: The Servants of India Society was founded at Poona in 1905 by:
nindian-history-132-6.x: Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society at Poona in 1905.
n: Ramakrishna Mission was founded at Calcutta in 1897. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
Swami Vivekananda founded Ramakrishna Mission. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
The Aligarh Movement was founded at Aligarh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Aligarh Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
Servants of India Society was founded at Poona in 1905. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded Servants of India Society. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
xa: RKM was founded on **1 May 1897**; ⚠ "**1879**" is a trap.
⚠ Sources differ: other notes say RKM was founded at **Belur (Howrah)**; **Belur Math** dates from **1898**.
Servants of India Society **used constitutional methods**.

n2efdab30a44.s: The Telugu name of the Theosophical Society is:
n2efdab30a44.x: The Theosophical Society is known in Telugu as Divya Gnana Samajam.
n2efdab30a44.tq: Test the exact regional-language equivalent of a well-known organisation.
xs: The Theosophical Society's Telugu name is **Divya Gnana Samajam** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Its Indian HQ at **Adyar (Madras)** put Andhra in the Society's **core area**.
xa: **Krishna Divyajnana Lodge** set up the first public library in **Guntur** district (**1882**).
**Madanapalle** = Theosophy's Andhra centre (**BT College**, **1916**).
**Veeresalingam** set up the **first Theosophical High School** in Andhra.

ndc05737482a.s: The Theosophical Society was founded in 1875 by:
o: Madame H.P. Blavatsky and Col. H.S. Olcott
Annie Besant and Madan Mohan Malaviya
Swami Dayanand Saraswati and Col. H.S. Olcott
ndc05737482a.x: The Theosophical Society was founded at New York in 1875 by the Russian Madame H.P. Blavatsky and the American Col. H.S. Olcott. Annie Besant joined only in 1889 and became President in 1907; Malaviya worked with her on the Central Hindu College; Jiddu Krishnamurti was her adopted son; Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj.
ndc05737482a.tq: Theosophy founders = Blavatsky (Russian) + Olcott (American), New York 1875.
xs: The Theosophical Society was founded by **Madame H.P. Blavatsky** (Russian) and **Col. H.S. Olcott** (American) — option **(1)**.
It was founded at **New York** in **1875**.
**Annie Besant** joined in **1889**; **Malaviya** worked with her on BHU; **Krishnamurti** was her adopted son; **Dayanand** founded the Arya Samaj.
xa: Indian HQ moved to **Adyar, Madras** in **1882**.
Besant became President after Olcott's death (**1907**).
Blavatsky's books: **Isis Unveiled**, **The Secret Doctrine**.

n97db8645dfd.s: In which year did Annie Besant become President of the Theosophical Society?
n97db8645dfd.x: Annie Besant came to India in 1893 and became President of the Theosophical Society in 1907 after Olcott's death.
xa: ⚠ **1889** joined; **1893** came to India; **1907** President; **1916** Home Rule League; **1917** INC President.
**1882** = HQ moved to **Adyar**; **1875** = founding at **New York** by Blavatsky and Olcott.

n86ff7c92673.s: Annie Besant became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress at the session held at:
n86ff7c92673.x: She presided over the 1917 Calcutta Congress; she had launched the Home Rule movement in 1916 and ran New India and Commonweal.
xa: Andhra Home Rule workers: **Konda Venkatappayya**, **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**, **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** (Secretary).
She founded **Central Hindu College** (**1898**) and **BT College, Madanapalle** (**1916**).

nd3b9a2c351d.s: Jiddu Krishnamurti, the adopted son of Annie Besant, wrote:
o: At the Feet of the Master
nd3b9a2c351d.x: Jiddu Krishnamurti, adopted by Annie Besant, wrote At the Feet of the Master (1910). Isis Unveiled and The Secret Doctrine are by H.P. Blavatsky; My Master is by Swami Vivekananda.
nd3b9a2c351d.tq: Krishnamurti = At the Feet of the Master; Blavatsky = Isis Unveiled, Secret Doctrine.
xs: **Jiddu Krishnamurti** wrote **At the Feet of the Master** (**1910**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Isis Unveiled** and **The Secret Doctrine** are by **Blavatsky**; **My Master** is by **Vivekananda**.
xa: Krishnamurti was **Annie Besant's adopted son**.
Besant's papers: **New India**, **Commonweal**.
Vivekananda's journals: **Prabuddha Bharata** (English), **Udbodhan** (Bengali).

n1964897461c.s: The Theosophical Society was founded in 1875 at:
n1964897461c.x: Blavatsky and Olcott founded the Theosophical Society at New York in 1875.
xa: Founders: **Madame H.P. Blavatsky** (Russian) and **Col. H.S. Olcott** (American).
Indian HQ moved to **Adyar, Madras** in **1882**.
Telugu name: **Divya Gnana Samajam**.

nindian-history-126-10.s: Modern education among Muslims was the aim of the:
nindian-history-126-10.x: Modern education among Muslims was the Aligarh Movement's aim, not the Dev Samaj's; Seva Sadan worked for women's welfare.
n: The Theosophical Society was associated with spiritual reform. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
The Theosophical Society was associated with religious reform. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Satyashodhak Samaj was associated with opposition to the caste system. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Satyashodhak Samaj was associated with social equality. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Seva Sadan was associated with women’s welfare. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Seva Sadan was associated with women’s education. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
The Aligarh Movement was associated with modern education among Muslims. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
xa: Seva Sadan is linked with **Ramabai Ranade**.
Theosophical Society promoted the **universal brotherhood** of humanity.
Aligarh Movement was led by **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan**.

nf39ade3af71.s: The College (DAV) party of the Arya Samaj was led by Lala Hansraj and:
nf39ade3af71.x: The DAV party was led by Lala Hansraj and Lala Lajpat Rai; the Gurukul party by Swami Shraddhanand and Pandit Lekh Ram.
xa: DAV wing: **First DAV School, Lahore, 1886**.
Gurukul wing: **Gurukul Kangri, Haridwar (1902)** — traditional Vedic curriculum.
Shraddhanand's earlier name: **Munshi Ram**; **Pandit Gurudutt** also carried on Dayananda's work.

nfac03bf1313.s: The split in the Arya Samaj over Western versus Vedic education and diet took place in:
nfac03bf1313.x: The split came in 1893, after Dayanand's death; 1875 is the founding year of the Arya Samaj at Bombay.
xa: **DAV party**: **Mahatma Hansraj**, **Lala Lajpat Rai** — **First DAV School, Lahore, 1886**.
**Gurukul party**: **Swami Shraddhanand** (Munshi Ram), **Pandit Lekh Ram** — **Gurukul Kangri, Haridwar (1902)**.

n014f3ef022d.s: Gurukul Kangri, which followed a traditional Vedic curriculum, was established at Haridwar in:
n014f3ef022d.x: Gurukul Kangri was set up at Haridwar in 1902 by the Gurukul party of Swami Shraddhanand and Pandit Lekh Ram.
xa: The DAV party's institution: **First DAV School, Lahore, 1886**.
⚠ **Swami Shraddhanand** = **Munshi Ram**.

nindian-history-116-18.s: Vinoba Bhave was associated with the:
nindian-history-116-18.x: Vinoba Bhave led the Sarvodaya Samaj; Agnihotri founded the Dev Samaj and Phule the Satyashodhak Samaj.
n: Dayanand Saraswati is listed as the founder/key person of Arya Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #116 · pp 211-212]
Jyotiba Phule is listed as the founder/key person of Satyashodhak Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #116 · pp 211-212]
Shiv Narayan Agnihotri is listed as the founder/key person of Dev Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #116 · pp 211-212]
Vinoba Bhave is listed as the founder/key person of Sarvodaya Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #116 · pp 211-212]
xa: Sarvodaya Samaj followed **Gandhi's principles** and worked for **refugees**.
**Seva Sadan** — **Ramabai Ranade**.
**Radha Swami Satsang** — **Shivdayal Sahab**.

n7b854b9eb37.s: Udbodhan, a journal of the Ramakrishna movement, was published in:
n7b854b9eb37.x: Udbodhan was a Bengali journal, while Prabuddha Bharata was in English.
xa: ⚠ Classic swap trap: **Prabuddha Bharata = English**; **Udbodhan = Bengali**.
Vivekananda's books: **Karma Yoga**, **Raja Yoga**, **Jnana Yoga**, **My Master**.
Besant's papers, by contrast: **New India** and **Commonweal**.

ncbb67836389.s: Who was the first Principal of the Besant Theosophical College, founded at Madanapalle in 1916?
ncbb67836389.x: Annie Besant founded the Besant Theosophical College at Madanapalle in 1916, and H.J. Cousins was its first Principal.
xa: Founder: **Annie Besant**; also called **Besant Theosophical (National) College**.
There **Rabindranath Tagore** translated **Jana Gana Mana** as **"Morning Song of India"** at Cousins' request.
**Madanapalle** = Theosophy's Andhra centre.

nbca81bdbcc1.s: Who, along with Madan Mohan Malaviya, is regarded as a founder of the Central Hindu College at Benaras?
nbca81bdbcc1.x: Annie Besant founded the Central Hindu College at Benaras in 1898; with Madan Mohan Malaviya it became the nucleus of Banaras Hindu University (1916). Olcott co-founded the Theosophical Society, Sister Nivedita was Vivekananda's disciple, and Shraddhanand led the Gurukul party of the Arya Samaj.
nbca81bdbcc1.tq: Benaras Hindu College + Malaviya -> Annie Besant (APPSC-GS 2025).
xs: **Annie Besant** founded the **Central Hindu College** (**1898**), which with **Malaviya** became BHU — option **(1)**.
**Olcott** co-founded the Theosophical Society; **Sister Nivedita** was Vivekananda's disciple; **Shraddhanand** led the Gurukul party.
xa: APPSC-GS **2025** asked exactly this: answer **Annie Besant**.
Besant's adopted son: **Jiddu Krishnamurti** (**At the Feet of the Master**, **1910**).

nf1b86f57b48.s: At Madanapalle, Rabindranath Tagore translated ‘Jana Gana Mana’ into English under which title?
nf1b86f57b48.x: Tagore translated ‘Jana Gana Mana’ into English at Madanapalle as ‘Morning Song of India’.
nf1b86f57b48.tq: Test the exact translated title rather than a plausible descriptive substitute.
xs: Tagore translated **Jana Gana Mana** into English as **"Morning Song of India"** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He did so at **BT College, Madanapalle**, at **H.J. Cousins'** request.
xa: **BT College** was founded by **Annie Besant** in **1916**; Cousins was first Principal.
**Madanapalle** = Theosophy's Andhra centre.
Other AP Theosophy link: **Krishna Divyajnana Lodge** library, **Guntur** (**1882**).

nindian-history-14-29.s: The foundation stone of Banaras Hindu University, founded by Madan Mohan Malviya, was laid in:
nindian-history-14-29.x: BHU's foundation stone was laid in 1916; Annie Besant, whose Central Hindu School became its nucleus, cooperated in setting it up.
n: Banaras Hindu University was associated with Madan Mohan Malviya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
Banaras Hindu University was located in Varanasi or Banaras. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
Banaras Hindu University was established through the efforts of Madan Mohan Malviya. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
Annie Besant cooperated in the establishment of Banaras Hindu University. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
xa: The stone was laid by **Lord Hardinge II** on **4 February 1916** — **Basant Panchami**.
Besant's **Central Hindu College, Benaras** (**1898**) became the nucleus of BHU.
⚠ **1916** twice: **BHU** and **BT College, Madanapalle**.

nindian-history-14-31.s: Which of the following was the first Central University among the given options?
nindian-history-14-31.x: Banaras Hindu University (1916) was set up by a central Act and is counted as the first Central University among these. Calcutta, Madras and Bombay universities (1857) were affiliating universities.
nindian-history-14-31.tq: Discriminate a central university from the 1857 universities.
n: Banaras Hindu University was the first Central University among the given options. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
xs: **Banaras Hindu University** was the **first Central University** among the given options — so option **(3)** is correct.
BHU was established in **1916** at **Varanasi** through **Madan Mohan Malviya**'s efforts.
xa: Foundation stone laid by **Lord Hardinge II** on **4 February 1916** (**Basant Panchami**).
**Annie Besant** cooperated; her **Central Hindu College** (**1898**) became its nucleus.
Besant became first woman **INC President**, **Calcutta 1917**.

n4274f2a98a9.s: In which year did the Krishna Divyajnana Lodge establish a public library at Guntur?
n4274f2a98a9.x: The Krishna Divyajnana Lodge established the public library in Guntur in 1882, the first public library in Guntur district.
n4274f2a98a9.tq: Use the year attached to a specific regional institutional event.
xs: The **Krishna Divyajnana Lodge** set up the Guntur public library in **1882** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was the **first public library in Guntur district**.
xa: ⚠ **1882** is also when the Theosophical HQ moved to **Adyar**.
**1875** = Society founded at New York; **1893** = Besant came to India; **1916** = BT College / Home Rule League.
Shuddhi in Andhra: **Andhra Shuddhi Samajam, Guntur, Jan 1934**.

n8c3fe19a38e.s: Among the Andhra workers of the Home Rule movement linked to Annie Besant's Madras Home Rule League, who served as Secretary?
n8c3fe19a38e.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was the Secretary among the Andhra Home Rule workers. Konda Venkatappayya and Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao were fellow Home Rule workers but not the Secretary; Veeresalingam is remembered here for the first Theosophical High School in Andhra.
n8c3fe19a38e.tq: Andhra Home Rule Secretary = Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao (Besant's league, not Tilak's).
xs: **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** was the **Secretary** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Konda Venkatappayya** and **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** were fellow Home Rule workers; **Veeresalingam** set up the first Theosophical High School.
xa: Besant's **Madras Home Rule League (1916)** and papers **New India**, **Commonweal** reached Andhra.
Theosophy "led straight into **Home Rule**".
**Madanapalle** = Theosophy's Andhra centre.

n5f56af091b5.s: Who set up the first Theosophical High School in Andhra?
n5f56af091b5.x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam set up the first Theosophical High School in Andhra. Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao and Konda Venkatappayya were Home Rule workers; H.J. Cousins was the first Principal of BT College, Madanapalle.
n5f56af091b5.tq: First Theosophical High School in Andhra = Veeresalingam.
xs: **Kandukuri Veeresalingam** set up the **first Theosophical High School** in Andhra — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Gadicherla** and **Konda Venkatappayya** were Home Rule workers; **H.J. Cousins** was first Principal of **BT College**.
xa: **Krishna Divyajnana Lodge** library, **Guntur** (**1882**) = first public library in Guntur district.
Telugu name of the Society: **Divya Gnana Samajam**.
Arya Samaj branches in **Anantapur and Chittoor** by **1920**.

n735cae246f6.s: The Vivekananda Human Excellence Centre of the Ramakrishna Mission is located at which place in Andhra Pradesh?
n735cae246f6.x: The Ramakrishna Mission's Vivekananda Human Excellence Centre is located at Vijayawada.
n735cae246f6.tq: Use the place-name distinction among the Andhra Pradesh locations.
xs: The **Vivekananda Human Excellence Centre** is at **Vijayawada** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Madanapalle** is Theosophy's Andhra centre; **Anantapur** had Arya Samaj branches; **Guntur** had the Theosophical lodge library.
xa: Built at **₹8.5 crore**; inaugurated **1 Feb 2026**.
Inaugurated by RKM President **Swami Gautamananda**.
**M. Venkaiah Naidu** called the Mission a **"university of values"**.

n2abd701e6bf.s: Which organisation launched the Shuddhi Movement?
n2abd701e6bf.x: The Shuddhi Movement was launched by the Arya Samaj.
n2abd701e6bf.tq: Identify the organisation from a movement–organisation association.
xs: The **Shuddhi Movement** was launched by the **Arya Samaj** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its purpose: **reconversion** to Hinduism and **admission of outsiders**.
xa: The **Brahmo Samaj** (**1828**) was Rammohan Roy's; the **Theosophical Society** (**1875**) Blavatsky and Olcott's; the **RKM** (**1897**) Vivekananda's.
**Keshavdev Gnaneshi**, a disciple of **Shraddhanand**, carried Shuddhi to **Guntur**.
Secretary of the **Andhra Shuddhi Samajam** (**1934**): **Upputuru Venkata Punnarao**.

na002fa98409.s: In Andhra Pradesh, Madanapalle is identified as a centre of:
na002fa98409.x: Madanapalle is identified as an Andhra centre of Theosophy.
xa: There **Tagore** translated **Jana Gana Mana** as **"Morning Song of India"**.
Other AP Theosophy link: **Guntur** Theosophical lodge library (**1882**).
**RKM**'s AP link: **Vijayawada**; Arya Samaj: **Anantapur and Chittoor**.

nindian-history-116-6.x: Rammohan Roy founded the Atmiya Sabha; Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj and Shiv Dayal Sahab the Radha Swami Satsang.
n: Rammohan Roy is listed as the founder/key person of Atmiya Sabha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #116 · pp 211-212]
Atmaram Pandurang is listed as the founder/key person of Prarthana Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #116 · pp 211-212]
Dayanand Saraswati is listed as the founder/key person of Arya Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #116 · pp 211-212]
Shivdayal Sahab is listed as the founder/key person of Radha Swami Satsang. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #116 · pp 211-212]
xa: Atmiya Sabha **1815**; Radha Swami Satsang **1861** (**Satnaam**, **Anami**).
Dayanand was born **Mool Shankar**.
Arya Samaj work later centred in Punjab with HQ at **Lahore**.

nindian-history-116-22.s: Jyotiba Phule's Satyashodhak Samaj was based at:
nindian-history-116-22.x: The Satyashodhak Samaj was based at Pune in Maharashtra; the Arya Samaj was founded at Bombay in 1875.
n: Arya Samaj was located in Bombay. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #116 · pp 211-212]
Satyashodhak Samaj was located in Maharashtra. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #116 · pp 211-212]
xa: ⚠ Arya Samaj was founded in **Bombay**, not Calcutta.
The **Shuddhi Movement** was launched by the **Arya Samaj** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
Satyashodhak Samaj opposed **caste discrimination**.

nindian-history-126-5.s: Who founded the Manav Dharma Sabha?
nindian-history-126-5.x: Durgaram Manchharam founded the Manav Dharma Sabha; Rammohan Roy founded the Atmiya Sabha and Agnihotri the Dev Samaj.
n: Atmiya Sabha was founded by Raja Rammohan Roy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Manav Dharma Sabha was founded by Durgaram Manchharam. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Prarthana Samaj was founded by Atmaram Pandurang. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Dev Samaj was founded by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
xa: Atmiya Sabha **1815**; Manav Dharma Sabha **1844**, **Surat**.
Prarthana Samaj **1867**, **Bombay**.
Dev Samaj **1887**, **Lahore**.

nindian-history-126-16.s: Which of the following was founded in 1875, the same year as the Arya Samaj?
nindian-history-126-16.x: The Theosophical Society was founded at New York in 1875; the Satyashodhak Samaj dates to 1873 and the Prarthana Samaj to 1867.
n: Atmiya Sabha was founded in 1815. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Brahmo Samaj was founded in 1828. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Manav Dharma Sabha was founded in 1844. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Arya Samaj was founded in 1875. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
The Theosophical Society was founded in 1875. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Satyashodhak Samaj was founded in 1873. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Ramakrishna Mission was founded in 1897. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
Dev Samaj was founded in 1887. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
The Aligarh Movement belongs to the 19th century. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
The year of Seva Sadan is not specified in the notes. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #126 · pp 229-230]
xa: ⚠ **1875** twice: **Arya Samaj (Bombay)** and **Theosophical Society (New York)**.
Theosophy moved to **Adyar** in **1882**.
Founders: **H.P. Blavatsky** (Russian) and **H.S. Olcott** (American).

nindian-history-132-3.x: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj; Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj, Rammohan Roy the Brahmo Samaj and Dayanand the Arya Samaj.
n: Raja Rammohan Roy founded Brahmo Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
Atmaram Pandurang founded Prarthana Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
Jyotiba Phule founded Satyashodhak Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded Arya Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
xa: Brahmo Samaj (Brahmo Sabha) **1828**, **Calcutta**.
Arya Samaj text: **Satyarth Prakash** ("Light of Truth").
The Arya Samaj split in **1893** into **DAV** and **Gurukul** factions.

nindian-history-116-10.s: The Manav Dharma Sabha was founded in 1844 at:
nindian-history-116-10.x: The Manav Dharma Sabha was founded at Surat in 1844; the Nadwah-ul-Ulama was founded at Lucknow in 1894.
n: Manav Dharma Sabha was located in Surat. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #116 · pp 211-212]
Nadwah-ul-Ulama was located in Lucknow. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #116 · pp 211-212]
xa: **Dev Samaj** — **Lahore** (**1887**).
**Satyashodhak Samaj** — **Pune** (**1873**).
**Servants of India Society** — **Poona** (**1905**), **Gokhale**.

nindian-history-95-4.s: Which movement aimed to promote modern education among Muslims?
nindian-history-95-4.x: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan's Aligarh Movement promoted modern, Western education among Muslims. The Deoband Movement stood for traditional religious education.
nindian-history-95-4.tq: Discriminate the Aligarh Movement from the Deoband Movement.
n: Aligarh Movement promoted modern education among Muslims. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
xs: The **Aligarh Movement** promoted **modern education** among **Muslims** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was founded/led by **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan** at **Aligarh**.
**Radhasoami Satsang** was about **Satnaam** and **Anami**; the **Brahmo Samaj** stood for **monotheism**.
xa: **MAO College** at Aligarh dates from **1877**.
**Nadwah-ul-Ulama** (**Lucknow**) — **Muslim social reform**.
The **Aligarh Movement** belongs to the **19th century**.

ne406711d78e.s: The chief centre of the anti-British Wahabi movement in India was:
ne406711d78e.x: Syed Ahmad Barelvi's Wahabi movement was anti-British and its chief centre was Patna; Faridpur was the Faraizi base.
xa: Founder in India: **Syed Ahmad Barelvi** (Rae Bareli).
It fought the **Sikhs** in Punjab, then the **British**.
Suppressed **by 1870** after the **Ambala** and **Patna** trials.

n685c3c7c343.s: Who founded the Faraizi Movement in East Bengal in 1818?
n685c3c7c343.x: Haji Shariatullah founded the Faraizi Movement in East Bengal in 1818. Dudu Miyan, his son, later led the movement.
n685c3c7c343.tq: Separate the founder from the later leader while retaining the date.
xs: **Haji Shariatullah** founded the Faraizi movement in **East Bengal**, **1818** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Dudu Miyan** was his **son and successor**; **Syed Ahmad Barelvi** led the Wahabis; **Mirza Ghulam Ahmad** founded the **Ahmadiya**.
xa: Base: **Faridpur**.
Aim: enforce **faraiz** (religious duties), purge un-Islamic practices.
APPSC-GS **2019** asked this pair.

ne52aed7add7.s: Which of the following was the journal associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan's reformist thought?
ne52aed7add7.x: Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq was the journal associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan's reformist and rational interpretation of Islam.
ne52aed7add7.tq: Distinguish a journal from books and publications associated with other reformers.
xs: Sayyid Ahmad Khan's journal was **Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**The Indian Musalmans** is a **1871** book by **W.W. Hunter**, not a journal of Sayyid Ahmad.
xa: His book: **Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind** (**1859**) on the causes of **1857**.
He promoted **Urdu** as a unifying language of Muslims.
Aim: modernisation via **English education** + **rational reading of Islam**.

n4a4f59c171f.s: The Scientific Society, founded by Sayyid Ahmad Khan at Ghazipur in 1864, was later shifted to:
n4a4f59c171f.x: The Society, which translated Western science, history and philosophy into Urdu, was later shifted to Aligarh, not Lucknow.
xa: Some notes give **1863** and Aligarh; **1864 at Ghazipur** is better supported.
⚠ **1863** = **Mohammadan Literary Society** (Calcutta, **Nawab Abdul Latif**).

n06d5801662e.s: The Deoband Movement began at Darul Uloom in 1866 under the leadership of
o: Mirza Ghulam Ahmad and Shibli Numani
