Qasim Nanotavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi
Sayyid Ahmad Khan and Theodore Beck
n06d5801662e.x: Qasim Nanotavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi led the establishment of the Deoband movement at Darul Uloom in 1866.
n06d5801662e.tq: Use the paired-founder clue and avoid mixing Deoband leaders with Aligarh or Ahmadiya figures.
xs: Deoband (Darul Uloom, **1866**) was led by **Qasim Nanotavi** and **Rashid Ahmad Gangohi** — option **(3)**.
**Shariatullah / Dudu Miyan** = Faraizi; **Mirza Ghulam Ahmad** = Ahmadiya; **Sayyid Ahmad / Beck** = Aligarh.
xa: Location: **Deoband, Saharanpur (UP)** — APPSC-GS **2019**: "Darul Uloom Deoband is in" → **Uttar Pradesh**.
Lifespans: **Nanotavi 1832-80**; **Gangohi 1828-1905**.
⚠ Gangohi belongs to **Deoband**, not the **Taiyuni** movement.

ncb16e06f3b4.s: The Muhammadan Literary Society (1863) founded by Nawab Abdul Latif was established at:
ncb16e06f3b4.x: Nawab Abdul Latif founded the Muhammadan Literary Society at Calcutta in 1863. Aligarh was Sayyid Ahmad Khan's centre, Lucknow the seat of the Nadwatul Ulama, and Patna the chief centre of the Wahabis.
xs: **Nawab Abdul Latif's** Muhammadan Literary Society (**1863**) was set up at **Calcutta** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Aligarh** = Sayyid Ahmad Khan; **Lucknow** = **Nadwatul Ulama**; **Patna** = Wahabi centre.
xa: One APPSC key gives **1863**, another **1862** — the place is **Calcutta** in both.
⚠ **1863/1864** = Literary Society / **Scientific Society** (Ghazipur).

nindian-history-14-26.s: Who founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College?
nindian-history-14-26.x: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875. David Hare and Raja Ram Mohan Roy are linked with Hindu College, and Alexander Duff with the Scottish mission college.
nindian-history-14-26.tq: Recall the founder of each institution.
n: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College was founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
xs: **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan** founded the **MAO College** in **1875** at **Aligarh** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Its original name **Madarsatul Uloom Musalmanan-i-Hind** was changed to **Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College** in **1877**.
It promoted **modern Western** and **scientific education** among Indian Muslims.
xa: MAO College became **Aligarh Muslim University** in **1920**.
It was modelled on **Oxford and Cambridge**; principals **Theodore Beck**, then **Theodore Morison**.
Sir Syed wrote **Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind** (**1859**) and ran **Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq**.

n957e6c55f17.s: The MAO Defence Association, formed in 1893, was primarily associated with which of the following positions?
o: Loyalism and opposition to the Congress
n957e6c55f17.x: The MAO Defence Association, associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan and Theodore Beck, was loyalist and anti-Congress in outlook.
n957e6c55f17.tq: Identify the organisation's political stance rather than its educational association.
xs: The **MAO Defence Association** (**1893**) stood for **loyalism** and **opposition to the Congress** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was formed by **Sayyid Ahmad Khan** with **Theodore Beck**.
xa: Earlier, in **1888**, he formed the **United Indian Patriotic Association** to counter the Congress.
**Deoband** issued a **fatwa (1888)** against his associations.
Beck was MAO principal (**1883-99**), followed by **Theodore Morison**.

nbebbf5ced15.s: After 1857, Sayyid Ahmad Khan (1817-1898) promoted the modernisation of Muslims mainly through:
nbebbf5ced15.x: He promoted English education and a rational reading of Islam; his earlier thought had also included Hindu-Muslim unity.
xa: His turn came after the **Hindi-Urdu controversy (1867)**.
He then formed the **United Indian Patriotic Association (1888)** to counter Congress.
Criticism: his later **political conservatism** sowed seeds of communal division.

n0a30f46a6f7.s: The change in Sayyid Ahmad Khan's political outlook, from an earlier emphasis on Hindu-Muslim unity to separate political paths, was associated with the
n0a30f46a6f7.x: The Hindi-Urdu controversy of 1867 contributed to the change in Sayyid Ahmad Khan's political outlook.
n0a30f46a6f7.tq: Link the change in political outlook to the specific earlier controversy, not to later nationalist movements.
xs: His shift followed the **Hindi-Urdu controversy of 1867** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Earlier he called India a bride with Hindus and Muslims as **"her two eyes"**.
xa: Later he held that Hindus and Muslims needed **separate political paths**.
**United Indian Patriotic Association (1888)**; **MAO Defence Association (1893)**.
⚠ **1866** = Deoband; **1867** = Hindi-Urdu controversy.

nc13e0cbd033.s: To counter the Indian National Congress, Sayyid Ahmad Khan formed in 1888 the:
nc13e0cbd033.x: He advised Muslims to stay away from the Congress and formed the United Indian Patriotic Association in 1888.
xa: ⚠ **1888** twice: his **United Indian Patriotic Association** and Deoband's **fatwa** against it.
**MAO Defence Association** (**1893**, with **Theodore Beck**): loyalist, anti-Congress.
Comparative: **Aligarh** opposed Congress; **Deoband** welcomed it.

n34313ea63d5.s: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental school, begun at Aligarh in 1875, was elevated into a college in:
n34313ea63d5.x: The MAO school began in 1875 and became a college in 1877 under Sayyid Ahmad Khan; Theodore Beck was later its principal, not its founder.
xa: Modelled on **Oxford and Cambridge**; became **AMU in 1920**.
Beck (**1883-99**), then **Theodore Morison**, were MAO principals.

n4e048795b0e.s: The Aligarh institution, begun as a school in 1875, became Aligarh Muslim University in:
n4e048795b0e.x: The school began in 1875, college classes in 1877, and it became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.
xa: It was modelled on **Oxford and Cambridge**.
The **Scientific Society** (**1864**) also later shifted to **Aligarh**.
Aligarh built the **modern educated Muslim middle class**.

n79894c64c51.s: Who wrote The Indian Musalmans, published in 1871?
n79894c64c51.x: The Indian Musalmans was written by W.W. Hunter and published in 1871.
n79894c64c51.tq: Match a work with its author and publication year.
xs: **The Indian Musalmans** (**1871**) was written by **W.W. Hunter** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It came a year after the Wahabis were **suppressed by 1870**.
xa: Sayyid Ahmad Khan's book: **Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind** (**1859**).
His journal: **Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq**.
⚠ Don't confuse Hunter's book (**1871**) with Sayyid Ahmad's works.

n6fd3b4e5a7d.s: Sayyid Ahmad Khan established the Muhammadan Educational Conference in:
n6fd3b4e5a7d.x: The Scientific Society came in 1864, the MAO school in 1875, the Muhammadan Educational Conference in 1886 and the United Indian Patriotic Association in 1888.
xa: MAO **college** classes began in **1877**; it became **AMU in 1920**.
**MAO Defence Association** followed in **1893**, with **Theodore Beck**.
⚠ Some notes wrongly give **1866** for the Conference; **1866** = Deoband.

n570decc5113.s: The Deoband Movement, led by orthodox ulema, began at Deoband in which district?
n570decc5113.x: It began at Deoband in Saharanpur district of the United Provinces and opposed foreign rule.
xa: Founded **1866**; nature: orthodox **revivalist**.
It **welcomed the Congress**.

nc5099f4536c.s: Which of the following was NOT an objective of the Deoband Movement?
o: To keep alive the spirit of jihad against foreign rulers
To replace traditional Islamic learning with exclusively Western education
To spread the pure teachings of the Quran and Hadith
nc5099f4536c.x: The Deoband Movement aimed at religious revival, training religious leaders and resistance to foreign rule; replacing Islamic learning with exclusively Western education was not its objective.
nc5099f4536c.tq: Find the option that reverses the movement's traditionalist educational character.
xs: **Replacing traditional Islamic learning with exclusively Western education** was NOT a Deoband aim — option **(3)**.
Deoband aims: spread pure **Koran and Hadis** teachings, keep alive **jihad against foreign rulers**, **train religious leaders**.
xa: Nature: **orthodox revivalist**; traditional Islamic learning, **anti-British**.
⚠ Deoband kept **jihad** alive; **Ahmadiya opposed jihad**.
**Western education** was the **Aligarh** approach.

n96a975b9e24.s: In 1888 the Deoband leadership issued a fatwa against:
o: Sayyid Ahmad Khan's United Indian Patriotic Association
n96a975b9e24.x: Deoband welcomed the Congress and in 1888 issued a fatwa against Sayyid Ahmad Khan's United Indian Patriotic Association and MAO Association.
xa: ⚠ **1888** twice: the **Association** and the **fatwa** against it.
Critics: Deoband backed the Congress more **to oppose Sir Syed** than from a positive creed.
**Mahmud-ul-Hasan** gave Deoband political content → **Jamiat-ul-Ulema**.

n2e717b4a6d0.s: Who gave the Deoband movement political content, leading to the Jamiat-ul-Ulema?
n2e717b4a6d0.x: Mahmud-ul-Hasan gave Deoband political content; Shibli Numani founded the Nadwat al-Ulama at Lucknow and wanted English and European science taught.
xa: Shibli **backed Deoband**.
**Nadwatul Ulama**: Maulana **Muhammad Ali Mungeri**; Shibli prominent; Lucknow, **1894**.

n60938e3e3f7.s: Unlike the Aligarh Movement, the Deoband Movement emphasised:
o: Western education and loyalty to the British
Traditional Islamic learning and opposition to foreign rule
n60938e3e3f7.x: Aligarh promoted Western education and loyalty to the British, while Deoband upheld traditional Islamic learning and opposed foreign rule.
xa: Deoband's **fatwa (1888)** targeted Sayyid Ahmad's anti-Congress associations.
Aligarh built the **modern educated Muslim middle class**; Deoband kept the **anti-colonial** strand alive.
Critics: Deoband backed Congress more to **oppose Sir Syed**.

nbc28289e8de.s: Which movement helped build a modern educated Muslim middle class?
nbc28289e8de.x: Aligarh built a modern educated Muslim middle class, while Deoband kept alive an orthodox and anti-colonial strand.
xa: Aligarh: **Western education**, pro-British, **anti-Congress**.
Deoband: **orthodox**, **anti-British**, **pro-Congress**.
Aligarh's MAO College was modelled on **Oxford and Cambridge**.

n84a5a5dd0cf.s: The Indian founder of the Wahabi Movement was:
n84a5a5dd0cf.x: The movement was named after Abdul Wahab of Arabia, but its Indian founder was Syed Ahmad Barelvi; it was crushed through the Ambala (1864) and Patna (1865) trials.
xa: Indian founder: **Syed Ahmad Barelvi**, inspired by **Shah Waliullah**.
Chief centre: **Patna**; aim: restore **Muslim power**.

n1ac664d0ef5.s: Mubariz-ud-Daula, associated with Wahabi activity in Hyderabad, was:
o: A Parsi reformer who edited Rast Goftar
A brother of the Nizam who resisted British influence in the Deccan
A principal of the Aligarh college
A Sikh mahant who controlled gurdwaras in Punjab
n1ac664d0ef5.x: Mubariz-ud-Daula was the Nizam’s brother. Influenced by Syed Ahmad Barelvi, he attempted to organise resistance to British influence in the Deccan and died in prison after his arrest.
n1ac664d0ef5.tq: Match the regional leader with his family position and political activity.
xs: **Mubariz-ud-Daula** was **a brother of the Nizam** who tried to organise **resistance to British influence in the Deccan** — option **(2)**.
Influenced by **Syed Ahmad Barelvi**, he was arrested under British pressure (**1839**) and **died in prison**.
xa: The **Nawab of Kurnool** was also implicated.
This was **Wahabi** activity in **Hyderabad State** (APPSC G2 **2002**).
Wahabi trials later: **Ambala (1864)**, **Patna (1865)**.

n40172c1616c.s: The Faraizi Movement, founded in East Bengal, primarily aimed at:
o: Enforcing the religious duties known as faraiz and purging un-Islamic practices
n40172c1616c.x: The Faraizi Movement sought to enforce religious duties, or faraiz, and remove un-Islamic practices. It was founded by Haji Shariatullah in East Bengal.
n40172c1616c.tq: Identify the movement from its distinctive objective and religious terminology.
xs: The Faraizi movement sought to **purge un-Islamic practices** and **enforce religious duties (faraiz)** — option **(3)**.
Founder: **Haji Shariatullah**, **East Bengal (Faridpur)**, **1818**.
xa: His son **Dudu Miyan** turned it into a peasant movement against **zamindars** and **indigo planters**.
APPSC-GS **2019** paired **"Faraizi - Haji Shariatullah"**.
⚠ **Promoting Western education** among Muslims was the **Aligarh** / **Ahmadiya** aim.

n48020cb55ff.s: Dudu Miyan transformed the Faraizi Movement into a movement primarily directed against:
o: British missionary institutions and Parsi reformers
n48020cb55ff.x: Dudu Miyan, the son of Haji Shariatullah, converted the Faraizi Movement into a peasant movement against zamindars and indigo planters.
n48020cb55ff.tq: Apply the movement’s social base and immediate opponents to a rural conflict.
xs: **Dudu Miyan** turned the Faraizi movement against **zamindars and indigo planters** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was the **son and successor** of **Haji Shariatullah**.
xa: Faraizi founded in **East Bengal (Faridpur)**, **1818**.
Original aim: enforce **religious duties (faraiz)**.
⚠ Removing corrupt **mahants** was the Sikh **Akali** movement, not Faraizi.

naaaaa8ff5ac.s: Nasaraiah, who was popular among the Madigas, preached:
o: The superiority of zamindars over peasants
The necessity of armed jihad against all Western education
One God and opposition to idol worship
The establishment of Sikh gurdwara committees
naaaaa8ff5ac.x: Nasaraiah, a Sayyid Muslim who died in 1825, preached belief in one God and opposed idol worship. He was associated with the Vinukonda–Narasaraopet region of Guntur.
naaaaa8ff5ac.tq: Connect the regional reformer with his central religious teaching.
xs: **Nasaraiah** preached **one God** and opposed **idol worship** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He was a **Sayyid Muslim** (d. **1825**), popular with **Madigas**.
xa: Region: **Vinukonda-Narasaraopet** (**Guntur**).
Other AP Muslim figure: **Mubariz-ud-Daula** — Wahabi activity in Hyderabad.
**Osmania University (1918)**, Hyderabad, taught in **Urdu**.

neea5e333b13.s: Osmania University, established at Hyderabad in 1918, taught through which language?
neea5e333b13.x: Osmania University was established at Hyderabad in 1918 and taught in Urdu.
xa: It gave **Ambedkar** an honorary **D.Litt in 1953**.
Sayyid Ahmad Khan promoted **Urdu** as a unifying language of Muslims.
**AMU** grew out of the **MAO College** (**1877**).

n7e2a3830096.s: Who is noted as the first to use non-cooperation and boycott of British goods?
n7e2a3830096.x: Ram Singh Kuka is noted as the first to use non-cooperation and boycott of British goods; he was exiled to Rangoon after the 1872 Malerkotla clash.
xa: He led the **Namdhari (Kuka)** movement from **Bhaini, Ludhiana**.
Namdharis wore **white clothes** and gave up meat.
Namdharis were among the **earliest** movements to resist British rule in Punjab.

n545d214809f.s: The Akali movement grew out of the:
n545d214809f.x: The Akali movement grew out of the Singh Sabha movement and later developed into the Akali Dal as a political party.
n545d214809f.tq: Trace institutional succession among closely related Sikh movements.
xs: The Akali movement **grew out of** the **Singh Sabha movement** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Nirankari** movement was **Baba Dayal Das's**, centred on God as **Nirankar**.
xa: **Akali Movement (1920)** removed corrupt **mahants** and became a **political party**.
Its success: **Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925** → gurdwaras under the **SGPC**.
Singh Sabha promoted **Gurmukhi/Punjabi** literature.

n56dbcf44f35.s: The Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925 placed the gurdwaras under the control of the:
n56dbcf44f35.x: The Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925 placed the gurdwaras under the SGPC. The Akali movement later became the political party known as the Akali Dal.
n56dbcf44f35.tq: Distinguish the statutory administrative body from the later political party.
xs: The **Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925** put gurdwaras under the **SGPC** (**Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee**) — option **(3)**.
This was the **Akali movement's** success; it had **removed corrupt mahants**.
xa: The Akali movement (**1920**) grew out of the **Singh Sabha** and became a political party.
Sikh **Anand Marriage Act, 1909**, amended **2012** to allow registration.
Parsi marriages: **Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936**.

n68285be6866.s: The Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha was founded in Bombay in 1851 by:
o: Kartar Singh Jhabbar, Shiv Narain Agnihotri and Behramji Malabari
Naoroji Furdonji, Dadabhai Naoroji and S. S. Bengalee
Baba Dayal Das, Bhagat Jawahar Mal and Ram Singh
Radhakant Deb, Shiv Dayal Singh and Madan Mohan Malaviya
n68285be6866.x: The Parsi Religious Reform Association was founded in Bombay in 1851 by Naoroji Furdonji, Dadabhai Naoroji and S. S. Bengalee.
n68285be6866.tq: Recall the complete founder group and reject groups assembled from other reform movements.
xs: The Sabha was founded by **Naoroji Furdonji**, **Dadabhai Naoroji** and **S.S. Bengalee** — option **(2)**.
**Jhabbar** led the **Akalis**; **Agnihotri** founded **Dev Samaj**; **Dayal Das** the **Nirankaris**; **Radhakant Deb** the **Dharma Sabha**.
xa: Also called the **Parsi Religious Reform Association**, **Bombay, 1851**.
Organ: **Rast Goftar** ("Truth-teller"), edited by **Dadabhai Naoroji**.
Focus: **girls' education** and **reform of marriage customs**.

n4c73a0c7b05.s: The Nirankari movement was founded by:
n4c73a0c7b05.x: Baba Dayal Das founded the Nirankari movement (UPSC dates it to 1855), which worshipped God as Nirankar, the formless. Baba Ram Singh led the Kukas, Kartar Singh Jhabbar the Akalis, and Shiv Dayal Singh founded the Radhasoami Satsang.
n4c73a0c7b05.tq: Distinguish the founder of Nirankari from founders of Namdhari and Radhasoami movements.
xs: The **Nirankari** movement was founded by **Baba Dayal Das** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Ram Singh** led the **Kukas**; **Jhabbar** the **Akalis**; **Shiv Dayal Singh** founded the **Radhasoami Satsang**.
xa: UPSC dates it **1855**.
Core belief: God as **Nirankar (formless)**.
It **cooperated with the British** and became a **separate group** within Sikhism.

naf3f3898f75.s: Rast Goftar ('Truth-teller'), edited by Dadabhai Naoroji, was the organ of the:
naf3f3898f75.x: Rast Goftar was the Parsi reform paper of the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha, not a Sikh paper.
xa: Some notes also name the monthly **Jagat Mithra**.
**Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha** = **Parsi Religious Reform Association**, **Bombay, 1851**.

n0835210deca.s: The campaign against child marriage associated with Behramji M. Malabari led to the enactment of the:
n0835210deca.x: Malabari's campaign against child marriage was associated with the Age of Consent Act of 1891.
n0835210deca.tq: Distinguish the reform law by its exact year from later legislation on a similar subject.
xs: Malabari's campaign led to the **Age of Consent Act, 1891** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925** concerns gurdwaras, not child marriage.
xa: Malabari = **greatest Parsi social reformer** of the **19th** century.
The Parsi **Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha** worked for **girls' education** and **marriage reform**.
Its organ: **Rast Goftar**, edited by **Dadabhai Naoroji**.

nb0931073690.s: The Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha was started to reform which community?
nb0931073690.x: The Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha (Parsi Religious Reform Association, Bombay 1851) aimed at reforming the Parsees. Sikh reform came through the Singh Sabha and Akalis, Muslim reform through Aligarh and Deoband; Jains are not linked to this body.
xs: The **Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha** was started to reform the **Parsees** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC G2 **2017**).
**Sikhs** were reformed by the **Singh Sabha**, **Kukas**, **Nirankaris**, **Akalis**; **Muslims** by **Deoband / Aligarh**.
xa: Founded **Bombay, 1851** — the **Parsi Religious Reform Association**.
Founders: **Naoroji Furdonji**, **Dadabhai Naoroji**, **S.S. Bengalee**.
Organ: **Rast Goftar**.

nd53c6db5fd8.s: Which Sikh movement grew by cooperating with the British and became a separate group within Sikhism?
nd53c6db5fd8.x: The Nirankari movement grew by cooperating with the British and later became a separate group within Sikhism.
xa: They had their own **worship places and priests** and issued **hukamnamas**.
Contrast: the **Namdharis** were **anti-British**.
Founder: **Baba Dayal Das**; UPSC date **1855**.

nbabedbf002e.s: Which one of the following was NOT a characteristic practice of the Kuka or Namdhari followers?
nbabedbf002e.x: Kuka followers rejected Brahmin-led rituals. They commonly wore white clothes, abstained from meat and carried a lathi.
nbabedbf002e.tq: Find the practice that conflicts with the reform movement's stated principles.
xs: **Performing Brahmin-led rituals** was NOT a Kuka practice — they **rejected** them — so option **(4)** is correct.
Kukas wore **white clothes**, gave up **meat** and carried a **lathi** — options (1)-(3).
xa: They also rejected **idol worship** and worship of **tombs, trees and snakes**.
They revived **Guru Gobind Singh's Khalsa** ceremonies.
Region: **Punjab**; centre **Bhaini, Ludhiana**.

n4b8b1c4f848.s: Which movement in Punjab advocated boycott of British goods, English education, law courts and the postal system?
n4b8b1c4f848.x: The Kuka movement advocated boycott of British goods, English education, law courts and the postal system.
xa: The Kuka boycott **anticipated Swadeshi and non-cooperation**.
Suppression: after the **1872 Malerkotla** clash, dozens **blown from cannons**.
APPSC **2025** asked Ram Singh as first to use non-cooperation and boycott.

na833348201c.s: After the 1872 Malerkotla clash, the Kuka leader Baba Ram Singh was deported to:
na833348201c.x: Dozens of Kukas were blown from cannons and Ram Singh was deported to Rangoon in Burma.
xa: ⚠ **Nankana Sahib** (**1921**) is an **Akali** flashpoint, not Kuka.
Kukas boycotted **British goods**, **English education**, **law courts**, **postal system**.
Practices: **white clothes**, no meat, a **lathi**.

n012785f0f1a.s: The principal objective of the Akali or Gurdwara Reform Movement of 1920–25 was to:
o: Establish English education in Punjab courts
Free gurdwaras from corrupt Udasi mahants
Revive worship of trees and snakes
n012785f0f1a.x: The Akali movement sought to free Sikh gurdwaras from corrupt Udasi mahants. It was led by figures including Kartar Singh Jhabbar.
n012785f0f1a.tq: Identify the institutional grievance that gave rise to the movement.
xs: The Akali movement aimed to **free gurdwaras from corrupt Udasi mahants** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was led by **Kartar Singh Jhabbar** (**1920-25**).
xa: It later became a political party — the **Akali Dal**.
**SGPC** formed **1920**.
Flashpoints: **Nankana Sahib (1921)**, **Guru-ka-Bagh (1922)**.

n900d65a3f98.s: The Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) was formed in:
n900d65a3f98.x: The SGPC was formed in 1920 during the Gurdwara Reform Movement.
n900d65a3f98.tq: Distinguish the body's formation year from the later legislation that gave it statutory control.
xs: The **SGPC** was formed in **1920** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1920** is also when the **Akali** movement began; **1902** is the **Bharat Dharma Mahamandal**.
xa: **1921** = **Nankana Sahib** massacre; **1922** = **Guru-ka-Bagh**.
Akali leader: **Kartar Singh Jhabbar**.
Akali aim: free gurdwaras from corrupt **Udasi mahants**.

n83ff17e822d.s: Shiv Dayal Singh (Soamiji Maharaj) founded the Radhasoami Satsang at Agra in:
n83ff17e822d.x: The Radhasoami Satsang was founded at Agra in 1861 and stressed inner realisation through the guru; 1830 is the Dharma Sabha of Radhakant Deb.
xa: The **Dharma Sabha** **opposed abolition of sati**.
**Dev Samaj**: **Shiv Narain Agnihotri**, **Lahore, 1887**.

nf6b4d853888.s: Satyashodhak marriages were significant because they:
o: Were restricted to members of one caste
Required the exclusive participation of Brahmin priests
Could be conducted without priests and permitted inter-caste marriage
Were intended only for upper-caste widows
nf6b4d853888.x: Satyashodhak marriages rejected priestly control and allowed inter-caste marriage.
nf6b4d853888.tq: Apply the movement’s anti-priestly and anti-caste principles to a social institution.
xs: Satyashodhak marriages were **conducted without priests** and allowed **inter-caste marriage** — so option **(3)** is correct.
They date from **1873** (UPSC), the year the **Satyashodhak Samaj** was founded.
xa: Compare **Self-respect marriages** (Periyar) — also without priests, from **1928**.
Samaj aim: free lower castes from **Brahmin priests** and religious exploitation.
Phule also opened a **home for upper-caste widows** (**1854**).

n389916fb389.s: The title ‘Mahatma’ was conferred on Jyotiba Phule by:
n389916fb389.x: Vithalrao Krishnaji Vandekar gave Jyotiba Phule the title ‘Mahatma’ in 1888.
n389916fb389.tq: Match the honorific with the person who conferred it, not with a fellow reformer.
xs: **Vithalrao Krishnaji Vandekar** gave Phule the title **"Mahatma"** in **1888** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Savitribai** was Phule's wife, India's first woman teacher; **Periyar** led the **Self-Respect Movement**.
xa: Phule is also called **"Father of Indian Social Revolution"**.
Phule's **200th birth anniversary** was marked on **11 April 2026**.
⚠ **1888** is also the **Aruvippuram** consecration by Narayana Guru.

n0a4f39977f6.s: Which symbolic pairing did Jyotiba Phule use in his critique of Brahminical dominance?
n0a4f39977f6.x: Phule used King Bali as a symbol representing the oppressed, in opposition to the Brahmanical symbol of Rama.
n0a4f39977f6.tq: Test the distinctive symbolic contrast rather than the general theme of anti-caste reform.
xs: Phule set **King Bali** against the **Brahmanical** symbol of **Rama** — so option **(4)** is correct (UPSC).
King Bali stood for the oppressed.
xa: ⚠ **Phule symbol** = **King Bali**; **Justice Party symbol** = **Scales**.
**Gulamgiri** (**1873**) compared lower castes' condition to **slavery**.
Samaj aim: break **priestly monopoly** over ritual.

neca450fa78d.s: Who wrote Sarvajanik Satyadharma Pustak, Shetkaryacha Asud, Tritiya Ratna and Brahmananche Kasab?
neca450fa78d.x: All four works were written by Jyotiba Phule.
neca450fa78d.tq: Group multiple works under their common author.
xs: All four works are by **Jyotiba Phule** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Ambedkar** wrote **Who Were the Shudras?** and **Annihilation of Caste**; **Jala Rangaswamy** wrote **Nimna Jatula Charitra**; **Periyar** ran **Kudi Arasu**.
xa: Phule's best-known book: **Gulamgiri** (Slavery), **1873**.
**Shetkaryacha Asud** = **The Cultivator's Whipcord**.
⚠ **The Orion** = **Tilak**.

n9c708a85c45.s: In 1848 Jyotiba Phule opened a girls' school at Pune, where the first woman teacher of India taught. Who was she?
n9c708a85c45.x: Savitribai Phule taught at the girls' school opened by Jyotiba Phule at Pune in 1848 and is called India's first woman teacher. Pandita Ramabai and Tarabai Shinde were other Maharashtrian women reformers not named in this context; Sarada Devi was Ramakrishna's wife.
n9c708a85c45.tq: 1848 Pune girls' school -> Savitribai = first woman teacher.
xs: **Savitribai Phule** taught at Phule's girls' school, **Pune**, **1848** — India's **first woman teacher** — option **(2)**.
**Sarada Devi** was **Ramakrishna's** wife (not in this topic).
xa: In **1854** Phule opened a **home for upper-caste widows**.
Phule founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj** in **1873**.
Samaj aim: education for **women, Shudras, Ati-Shudras**.

nea6942f1cf4.s: The SNDP Yogam was founded in:
nea6942f1cf4.x: The SNDP Yogam was founded in 1903; 1906 is the Depressed Classes Mission.
xa: This was the APPSC-GS **2023** year match.
SNDP: **Ezhavas**, Kerala, **Sree Narayana Guru**.

nd9bbf9d7f7c.s: Who founded the journal Vital-Vidhvansak in 1888?
nd9bbf9d7f7c.x: Vital-Vidhvansak was founded in 1888 by Gopal Baba Walangkar.
nd9bbf9d7f7c.tq: Match a journal with its founder rather than with a related social reformer.
xs: **Gopal Baba Walangkar** founded **Vital-Vidhvansak** in **1888** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Din Bandhu** (**1877**) was **Krishnarao Bhalekar's**, later **N.M. Lokhande's**; **V.R. Shinde** founded the **Depressed Classes Mission**.
xa: Walangkar also founded the **Anarya Dosh Pariharak Mandali** (**Mahars**).
⚠ **1888** also = Phule's title **"Mahatma"**.
**Mooknayak** (**1920**) = **Ambedkar**.

nindian-history-22-5.s: Who headed the women's section of the Satyashodhak Samaj?
nindian-history-22-5.x: Savitribai Phule headed its women's section; the Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule for Shudras and Ati-Shudras.
n: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Shudras and Ati-Shudras were the main beneficiaries of the Satyashodhak movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
The Satyashodhak movement sought liberation from exploitation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Savitribai Phule headed the women's section of the Satyashodhak Samaj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
xa: Phule (**1827-1890**) belonged to the **Mali community**.
Phule's girls' school in **Pune**: **1848**; home for upper-caste widows: **1854**.
Title "Mahatma" given by **Vithalrao Krishnaji Vandekar** (**1888**).

nindian-history-22-10.s: Jyotiba Phule's 1873 book comparing caste oppression with slavery is:
nindian-history-22-10.x: Gulamgiri (1873) compared caste oppression with slavery; Sarvajanik Satyadharma Pustak was published posthumously in 1891.
n: Gulamgiri was a work by Jyotiba Phule. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Gulamgiri criticized Brahmanical domination. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Sarvjanik Satyadharm Pustak was a work by Jyotiba Phule. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Sarvjanik Satyadharm Pustak advanced anti-caste thought. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Jyotiba Phule worked for lower-caste upliftment. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
xa: Other Phule works: **Shetkaryacha Asud**, **Tritiya Ratna**, **Brahmananche Kasab**.
**Who Were the Shudras?** and **Annihilation of Caste** (**1936**) are by **B.R. Ambedkar**.
⚠ **The Orion** (**Tilak**) is a regular distractor.
nindian-history-22-10.fixed: stem carried a duplicate, differently ordered option set

nindian-history-22-15.s: Jyotiba Phule, founder of the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873), belonged to which community?
nindian-history-22-15.x: Phule belonged to the Mali community and founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 to uplift the backward classes.
n: Jyotiba Phule belonged to the Mali community. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Satyashodhak Samaj worked for the upliftment of backward classes. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
Jyotiba Phule worked for lower-caste upliftment. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 80-82]
xa: Satyashodhak Samaj = "**Society of Truth Seekers**", founded at **Pune** in **1873**.
Phule is called the "**Father of Indian Social Revolution**".
**Savitribai** was India's first woman teacher (Pune, **1848**).

na843e14cb98.s: The Justice Party's English newspaper 'Justice' began publication in:
na843e14cb98.x: Justice began in February 1917; the party, linked with the South India Peoples Association, was founded by T.M. Nair, P. Theagaraya Chetty and C. Natesa Mudaliar.
xa: Political wing: **South Indian Liberal Federation (SILF)**; symbol **Scales**.
First general meeting: **Coimbatore, 19 Jul 1917** (**Panagal Raja** presiding).

nc76c77394b8.s: Who signed the Non-Brahmin Manifesto of December 1916?
nc76c77394b8.x: The Non-Brahmin Manifesto issued in December 1916 was signed by P. Thyagaraya Chetty.
nc76c77394b8.tq: Use the signatory–document association rather than the founder list.
xs: The **Non-Brahmin Manifesto** (**Dec 1916**) was signed by **P. Thyagaraya Chetty** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**T.M. Nair** and **Natesa Mudaliar** were co-founders; **Panagal Raja** presided over the first general meeting.
xa: Thyagaraya Chetty died on **25 Apr 1925** — a blow to the party.
Founding meeting: **20 Nov 1916**, Victoria Memorial Hall.
Daily **Justice**: **26 Feb 1917**.

n08c70e2b197.s: What was the symbol of the Justice Party?
n08c70e2b197.x: The symbol of the Justice Party was the Scales.
n08c70e2b197.tq: Test a distinctive organisational symbol directly.
xs: The Justice Party's symbol was the **Scales** — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ **Phule's** symbol was **King Bali**.
xa: Political wing: **South Indian Liberal Federation**.
Founders: **T.M. Nair**, **Theagaraya Chetty**, **Natesa Mudaliar**.
It won **63 of 98** elected seats in **1920**.

n77b545c26c9.s: Brahmins constituted approximately what share of the Madras Presidency's population?
n77b545c26c9.x: Brahmins were about 3 per cent of the population though they held over 90 per cent of government jobs.
xa: This base secured the **Communal G.O. (1921)**.
Dalits built a parallel **"Adi"** movement.

n980d182bda5.s: The Communal G.O. of 1921, regarded as a forerunner of reservation policy in South India, was secured by:
o: Intermediate landed castes of the non-Brahmin movement
n980d182bda5.x: It was secured by the intermediate landed castes of the non-Brahmin movement and was not meant exclusively for Dalit organisations.
xa: CDX dates it **Dec 1921**.
Caste-based roster: **50%** of educational seats for non-Brahmins.

n155cc920e44.s: Who became the first Chief Minister of the first Justice Party ministry formed on 17 December 1920?
n155cc920e44.x: A. Subbarayalu Reddiar became the first Chief Minister of the first Justice Party ministry on 17 December 1920; he was later succeeded by the Raja of Panagal.
n155cc920e44.tq: Distinguish the first ministry head from later Justice Party ministers.
xs: **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar** became the first Chief Minister on **17 Dec 1920** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He served until **Jul 1921** (ill health); then **Panagal Raja** (**1921-1926**).
xa: Ministry rested on **63 of 98** seats.
⚠ **17 Dec 1933** = Siddhantam temple entry move.

n81a46366377.s: Which Justice Party Premier served from 1921 to 1926 and headed two ministries?
n81a46366377.x: Panagal Raja, also known as P. Ramarayaningar, served as Premier from 1921 to 1926 and headed two ministries.
n81a46366377.tq: Associate the tenure with the correct premier rather than the party founder.
xs: **Panagal Raja** (**P. Ramarayaningar**) was Premier **1921-1926**, heading **two ministries** — option **(2)**.
**Subbarayalu Reddiar** was first CM; **Munuswamy Naidu** **1930-1932**; **K.V. Reddy Naidu** **Apr-Jul 1937**.
xa: Panagal was **party president**; the **Andhra University Act (1926)** came in his time.
He died on **16 Dec 1928**.
**26 Nov 1923**: no-confidence motion against him by **C.R. Reddy**.

n248cd622ef4.s: The Communal Government Order of 1921 in Madras Presidency gave proportional representation in jobs and education to:
n248cd622ef4.x: The 1921 Communal G.O. provided proportional representation for non-Brahmins in government jobs and education.
xa: Secured by the intermediate landed castes: **Reddys, Kammas, Kapus**.
**Women's franchise resolution** (**1921**) — Madras first province to let women vote.

n07574a9a572.x: Annamalai University was founded in 1929; the Andhra University Act and Madras Hindu Religious Endowments Act were of 1926.
xa: ⚠ **Andhra University 1926** vs **Annamalai University 1929**.
APPSC G2 **2025** asked "Justice Party helped create which university?" → **Andhra University** (three times).
**Periyar** supported the **Hindu Religious Endowments Act** even in his Congress years.

n7ceceb0b903.s: Who was the first Chancellor of Andhra University?
n7ceceb0b903.x: Lord Goschen was the first Chancellor; A.P. Patro, as Education Minister, drove the 1926 Act, and the first headquarters was at Bezawada.
xa: First VC: **C.R. (Kattamanchi Ramalinga) Reddy**.
Act passed in **1926** under **Panagal Raja**.

n0ba9a4a4473.s: The lasting Andhra legacy of the Justice Party was the establishment, in 1926, of:
n0ba9a4a4473.x: Andhra University, established in 1926, is identified as the Justice Party's lasting Andhra legacy.
xa: Act driven by **A.P. Patro**; first VC **C.R. Reddy**.
First HQ **Bezawada**, later **Waltair**.
APPSC G2 **2025** asked it three times.

na354e89a9c8.s: Panagal Raja, President of the Justice Party, served as Premier of Madras from:
na354e89a9c8.x: Panagal Raja was Premier from 1921 to 1926, was associated with Andhra University in 1926 and died on 16 December 1928.
xa: Real name: **Panuganti Ramarayaningar**.
Origin: some notes say Zamindar of **Srikalahasti**; others trace him to **Nalgonda** (Panagal).
He presided over the first general meeting, **Coimbatore, 19 Jul 1917**.

nf2e5f48f245.s: K.V. Reddy Naidu of Eluru, a minister in the first Justice ministry of 1920, became Premier in:
nf2e5f48f245.x: Kurma Venkata Reddy Naidu was a minister in the first Justice ministry (1920) and became Premier in 1937.
xa: He was from **Eluru**; Premier **Apr-Jul 1937** (interim).
He backed an Andhra province only with a **non-Brahmin majority** guaranteed.
SILF founders were **T.M. Nair**, **Theagaraya Chetty**, **Natesa Mudaliar**.

n265704fc71e.s: Who moved the separate Andhra resolution in 1922, which was later withdrawn at A.P. Patro’s urging?
n265704fc71e.x: M. Suryanarayana moved the separate Andhra resolution in 1922, and it was withdrawn at the urging of A.P. Patro.
n265704fc71e.tq: Separate the mover of a resolution from the person who urged its withdrawal.
xs: **M. Suryanarayana** moved the separate Andhra resolution in **1922**, withdrawn at **Patro's** urging — option **(2)**.
**Munukuru Rama Rao** was a **Krishna** organiser; **Koka Appa Rao Naidu** and **P. Ramachandra Reddy** were other leaders.
xa: M. Suryanarayana was from **Visakhapatnam**.
Some notes date a Suryanarayana resolution to **1937**.
The party **opposed the Andhra movement** — a cause of decline.

n332c12a8676.s: The Justice Party lost power to the Congress in the elections of:
n332c12a8676.x: Weakened by lack of a mass base, Andhra–Tamil rifts and the deaths of Theagaraya Chetty and the Raja of Panagal, it lost to the Congress in 1937.
xa: It also **opposed the freedom struggle and the Andhra movement**.
**Natesa Mudaliar** attacked its neglect of the **poor and Harijans**.
After **1937**, **Periyar** turned it into the **Dravidar Kazhagam** (**1944**).

n52221e8584c.s: Who criticised the neglect of the poor and Harijans within the Justice Party?
n52221e8584c.x: C. Natesa Mudaliar criticised the Justice Party for neglecting the poor and Harijans.
n52221e8584c.tq: Distinguish internal criticism from external political opposition.
xs: **C. Natesa Mudaliar** attacked the party's **neglect of the poor and Harijans** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He was himself a co-founder, with **T.M. Nair** and **P. Thyagaraya Chetty**.
xa: **P.T. Rajan** acted as CM **Apr-Aug 1936**.
Decline causes: **Andhra-Tamil rivalry**, **no mass base** in Andhra.
Leaders' deaths: **Thyagaraya Chetty (25 Apr 1925)**, **Panagal Raja (16 Dec 1928)**.

nb342f8e7c72.s: From 1920, the Justice Party formed the government in Madras how many times?
nb342f8e7c72.x: The Justice Party formed the government four times from 1920, won reservations for non-Brahmins and declined by 1937.
xa: Source: The Hindu (**16 Jun 2026**).
Non-Brahmin reservations began in **1920** → shaped Tamil politics.

n41b62c05f12.s: The non-Brahmin movement in the Madras Presidency sought to end Brahmin dominance in:
n41b62c05f12.x: The movement aimed to end Brahmin dominance in jobs, education, politics and religion.
xa: Means: **reservation and representation** in jobs, education, legislatures.
**Communal G.O. (1921)**: proportional representation in jobs and education.
**Temple entry** campaign for non-Brahmins and Dalits.

n6115bf0b560.s: The Justice Party was transformed into the Dravidar Kazhagam under the leadership of Periyar in:
n6115bf0b560.x: Periyar transformed the Justice Party into the Dravidar Kazhagam in 1944.
n6115bf0b560.tq: Distinguish the year of organisational transformation from the year of electoral defeat.
xs: Periyar turned the Justice Party into the **Dravidar Kazhagam** in **1944** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1937** = anti-Hindi agitation and Justice defeat; **1940** = **Dravidistan** demand (Erode); **1947** = Atheist Centre moved to Vijayawada.
xa: **1949**: DK split → **C.N. Annadurai** formed the **DMK** (**17 Sept 1949**).
DMK in power from **1967**.
Periyar's **Self-Respect Movement**: **1925**.

n70756f65fd0.s: Self-respect marriages promoted by the Self-Respect Movement were conducted:
n70756f65fd0.x: Self-respect marriages were conducted without priests; the movement attacked caste hierarchy and priests and supported women's equality and property rights.
xa: Self-respect marriages: from **1928**.
Movement launched **1925** by **Periyar**.

n23396ea6c65.s: Which one of the following sets contains the journals associated with Periyar's Self-Respect Movement?
o: Jai Bheem, Veera Bharati and Adi Hindu
Din Bandhu, Vital-Vidhvansak and Kudi Arasu
n23396ea6c65.x: Periyar was associated with Kudi Arasu and Viduthalai, while Revolt was his English journal.
n23396ea6c65.tq: Separate one reformer's journal group from similarly themed journals.
xs: Periyar's journals were **Kudi Arasu**, **Viduthalai** and **Revolt** (English) — option **(1)**.
**Mooknayak**, **Bahishkrit Bharat** = **Ambedkar**; **Harijan** = **Gandhi**; **Jai Bheem**, **Veera Bharati** = **Jala Rangaswamy**; **Adi Hindu** = **Bhagya Reddy Varma**.
xa: **Din Bandhu** (**1877**) = **Krishnarao Bhalekar**; **Vital-Vidhvansak** (**1888**) = **Gopal Baba Walangkar**.
⚠ **Kudi Arasu** = Periyar; **Mooknayak** = Ambedkar.
**Harijan** weekly: **1933**.

ne790c0bc54d.s: In 1925 Periyar broke with the Congress over communal representation and caste segregation at:
ne790c0bc54d.x: Periyar, who had been president and secretary of the provincial Congress, left in 1925 over communal representation and the Cheranmadevi Gurukulam segregation.
xa: The same year (**1925**) he launched the **Self-Respect Movement**.
Earlier he joined **Vaikom** and was jailed → **"Vaikom Veerar"**.

n541dda249fd.s: Periyar launched the Self-Respect Movement in:
n541dda249fd.x: The Self-Respect Movement began in 1925; the anti-Hindi agitation was in 1937, the Dravidistan demand in 1940 and the DMK in 1949.
xa: **Dravidar Kazhagam** formed from the Justice Party in **1944**.
DMK founded **17 Sept 1949** by **C.N. Annadurai**; in power from **1967**.
**1937** also = Justice Party's defeat.

n39b258d6922.s: The DMK was formed on 17 September 1949, after a split in the Dravidar Kazhagam, by:
n39b258d6922.x: Annadurai formed the DMK in 1949; Periyar had formed the Dravidar Kazhagam from the Justice Party in 1944. The DMK came to power in 1967.
xa: **Dravidistan** demand: Erode, **1940**.
Self-Respect/DK stream **separated religion and caste from politics**.

naa5033baf8b.s: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary's song 'Veeragandhamu techinaramu... veerulevvaro telpudi' is associated with which movement?
naa5033baf8b.x: The song by Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary (Kavi Raju) is linked to the Civil Disobedience Movement, as in the APPSC 2012 key. The other three movements are distractors.
xs: The song "**Veeragandhamu techinaramu... veerulevvaro telpudi**" is linked to the **Civil Disobedience Movement** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2012**).
It is by **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary** (**Kavi Raju**).
xa: His approach: **rationalist** attack on **Puranic** caste stories.
Works: **Kurukshetra Sangramam**, **Sambuka Vadha**, **Suta Puranam**.
Also APPSC **2012**: **Andhra Jana Kendra Sangham** → **Hyderabad**, **1923**.

n94e8948cad9.s: The colonial government used the Justice Party primarily as a counter to:
o: the Swadeshi movement and the Khilafat movement
the Andhra University movement and the Dalit movement
the Round Table Conferences and the Simon Commission
n94e8948cad9.x: The government used the Justice Party against the Home Rule movement and Gandhi’s movements.
n94e8948cad9.tq: Identify the political movements against which an organisation was deployed.
xs: The British used the Justice Party against **Home Rule and Gandhi's movements** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They backed it partly to **weaken Home Rule**.
xa: Criticism: **pro-British**, **landlord-led**, weak among Andhra masses.
It **opposed both the freedom struggle and the Andhra movement**.
Congress **boycotted** the **1920** elections, letting the Justice Party win.

ncd49702f7ff.s: A.K. Gopalan is associated with which satyagraha?
ncd49702f7ff.x: A.K. Gopalan is listed with Guruvayur; T.K. Madhavan, K.P. Kesava Menon and K. Kelappan were associated with Vaikom.
xa: Vaikom was backed by **Narayana Guru**; **Periyar** joined.
**Kelappan** also led **Guruvayur**.
**Gandhi** visited Vaikom in **1925**.

n714fac24f24.s: Periyar E.V. Ramasamy earned the title “Vaikom Veerar” because he:
o: Joined the Vaikom Satyagraha and was jailed
Led the Mahad Satyagraha in Maharashtra
Negotiated the Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation of 1936
n714fac24f24.x: Periyar joined the Vaikom Satyagraha and was imprisoned, after which he became known as “Vaikom Veerar”.
n714fac24f24.tq: Link the title to the specific action and movement rather than to a later reform.
xs: Periyar **joined the Vaikom Satyagraha and was jailed** → **"Vaikom Veerar"** — option **(1)**.
⚠ Vaikom Veerar = **Periyar**, not **Narayana Guru** (Guru only backed Vaikom).
xa: Periyar is also called the **Hero of Vaikom**.
**Mahad** (**1927**) was **Ambedkar's**.
Outcome of Vaikom: **Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation (1936)**.

n956ec7a4fa1.s: The Vaikom Satyagraha eventually helped lead to which development?
o: Establishment of the Independent Labour Party in 1936
Formation of the Nadar Mahajana Sangam in 1910
Formation of the Justice Party in the Madras Presidency
n956ec7a4fa1.x: The Vaikom Satyagraha contributed to the developments culminating in the Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation of 1936.
n956ec7a4fa1.tq: Connect the movement with its later constitutional-social outcome by using the year clue.
xs: Vaikom led on to the **Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation of 1936** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **ILP** (**1936**) was **Ambedkar's** party, unrelated to Vaikom.
xa: Vaikom: **1924-25**, roads around the **Vaikom temple**.
**Gandhi's** **1925** visit brought a compromise.
Later temple entry: **Guruvayur** (**1931-32**), **Siddhantam** (**17 Dec 1933**).

nb8d502dde8c.s: The Mahad Satyagraha led by B.R. Ambedkar asserted the right to draw water from:
nb8d502dde8c.x: Mahad concerned the right to draw water from the Chavdar tank in Maharashtra; Vaikom, in Travancore, concerned access to roads around a temple.
xa: Mahad: **20 March 1927**, organised by the **Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha**.
After Mahad, INC's Anti-Untouchability Subcommittee reconstituted under **Malaviya**.

n28a586c3160.s: The Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25) was associated with the:
n28a586c3160.x: Vaikom in Travancore was a temple-entry and civil-rights struggle for lower castes' use of the roads around the Vaikom temple. Khilafat was a pan-Islamic agitation; the Chavdar tank was the Mahad Satyagraha (1927); self-respect marriages began under Periyar from 1928.
xs: Vaikom (**1924-25**) was associated with the **Temple Entry Movement** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-G2 **2023**).
The **Chavdar tank** struggle was **Mahad** (**1927**); **self-respect marriages** began from **1928** under Periyar.
xa: Issue: lower castes' use of **roads around the Vaikom temple**.
Leaders: **T.K. Madhavan**, **K.P. Kesava Menon**, **K. Kelappan**.
Outcome: **Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation (1936)**.

n53e2f478127.s: Which Madiga leader worked for land rights and seats in local bodies?
n53e2f478127.x: Arige Ramaswamy, a Madiga leader, worked for land rights and representation in local bodies.
xa: Arige Ramaswamy was a **Madiga** leader.
**Kusuma Dharmanna** was an **Adi-Andhra poet**.
**Bhagya Reddy Varma** opposed the **Devadasi system**.

n3c3bb3549fd.s: B.R. Ambedkar agreed to the Poona Pact reluctantly primarily because he wished to:
o: obtain a separate province for Dalits
secure the survival of the Justice Party
n3c3bb3549fd.x: Ambedkar accepted the change from separate electorates to reserved seats in joint electorates reluctantly in order to save Gandhi’s life.
n3c3bb3549fd.tq: Link the political compromise with the immediate circumstance behind it.
xs: Ambedkar accepted the Poona Pact reluctantly to **save Gandhi's life** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The Pact (**24 Sept 1932**) gave **reserved seats in joint electorates** instead of separate electorates.
xa: Seats: **148** vs **71** under the Communal Award.
Comparative: Ambedkar sought caste's **annihilation**, legal rights, **separate electorates**.
Gandhi saw untouchability as a **corruption**; used "**Harijan**".

na3d3c47a5b8.s: Ambedkar's mass conversion to Buddhism at Deeksha Bhoomi, Nagpur on 14 October 1956 was accompanied by how many vows?
na3d3c47a5b8.x: The conversion at Deeksha Bhoomi on 14 October 1956 was accompanied by 22 vows, not 32.
xa: Ambedkar's earlier bodies: **BHS 1924**, **ILP 1936**, **SCF 1942**.
⚠ "**1954**" given in some notes is wrong.

n5577b024614.s: Mooknayak and Bahishkrit Bharat were founded by whom?
n5577b024614.x: Mooknayak and Bahishkrit Bharat were journals founded by B.R. Ambedkar.
n5577b024614.tq: Group two journals under their common founder.
xs: **Mooknayak** and **Bahishkrit Bharat** were founded by **B.R. Ambedkar** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Gandhi** = **Harijan**; **Jala Rangaswamy** = **Jai Bheem**, **Veera Bharati**; **Walangkar** = **Vital-Vidhvansak**.
xa: **Mooknayak** = "Leader of the Silent" (**1920**); **Bahishkrit Bharat** **1927**.
Ambedkar's third journal: **Janata**.
⚠ **Mooknayak** = Ambedkar; **Kudi Arasu** = Periyar.

n263882f60aa.s: The weekly Harijan, started in 1933, was founded by:
n263882f60aa.x: Gandhi founded the weekly Harijan in 1933. Ambedkar founded Mooknayak and Bahishkrit Bharat, Periyar Kudi Arasu, and Walangkar Vital-Vidhvansak.
n263882f60aa.tq: Harijan (1933) = Gandhi; Mooknayak = Ambedkar; Kudi Arasu = Periyar.
xs: **Gandhi** founded the weekly **Harijan** in **1933** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ambedkar** = **Mooknayak**, **Bahishkrit Bharat**; **Periyar** = **Kudi Arasu**; **Walangkar** = **Vital-Vidhvansak**.
xa: **1933** also = League renamed **Harijan Sevak Sangh**.
Gandhi used the term "**Harijan**"; saw untouchability as a **corruption**.
Gandhi's **1932-33** Andhra tour collected **Harijana Bhiksha**.

na30872ff693.s: Who sought the annihilation of caste, legal rights and separate electorates for the depressed classes?
na30872ff693.x: Ambedkar sought caste annihilation, legal rights and separate electorates, whereas Gandhi saw varna as a division of labour and untouchability as a corruption.
xa: **Annihilation of Caste** (**1936**) rebukes **Gandhi's** approach.
**Poona Pact** (**1932**): reserved seats in **joint electorates** replaced separate electorates.

n78da526a84a.s: The demand for reserved seats for non-Brahmins in the Andhra Mahasabha was echoed by Ponaka Pattabhirama Reddy and:
n78da526a84a.x: Pattabhirama Reddy and Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary echoed the demand; Gora and Periyar belong to other rationalist and anti-caste strands.
xa: Tripuraneni = **Kavi Raju**; rationalist attack on **Puranic** caste stories.
His works: **Kurukshetra Sangramam**, **Sambuka Vadha**, **Suta Puranam**.
The demand came at the **Andhra Mahasabha**, **Vijayawada**, **1917**.

nc782e3c2327.s: The term 'Adi-Hindu' referred to the Dalits of:
nc782e3c2327.x: Adi-Hindu referred to Dalits of Hyderabad State, while Adi-Andhra referred to Dalits of the Andhra region, including coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema.
xa: Adi Andhra covers **coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema**.
Both terms were popularised by **Madari Bhagya Reddy Varma**.
Adi-Hindu groups: **Malas, Madigas**.

n637ab5e8eed.s: Who popularised the terms Adi-Andhra and Adi-Hindu and was regarded as the father of the Dalit movement in Hyderabad and Andhra?
n637ab5e8eed.x: Madari Bhagya Reddy Varma popularised both terms and is regarded as the father of the Dalit movement in Hyderabad and Andhra.
n637ab5e8eed.tq: Use the leader-title association to identify the correct personality.
xs: **Madari Bhagya Reddy Varma** popularised both terms and is the **"Father of the Dalit movement"** — option **(4)**.
**Undru Tatayya** held the **1921 Amalapuram** Sadassu; **Jala Rangaswamy** = **Adi Andhra Mahatma**; **Arige Ramaswamy** = Madiga leader.
xa: Born **1888**, Hyderabad; original name **Madari Bagaiah**.
**Manya Sangham** (**1911**) → **Adi Hindu Social Service League**.
Journal: **Adi Hindu**.

n61317a81b08.s: The 1917 resolution of the first Adi-Andhra session sought to replace the term 'Panchama' in Hyderabad by:
n61317a81b08.x: It sought 'Adi Andhra' in the Madras region and 'Adi Hindu' in Hyderabad, along with schools, wells in Dalit wadas and seats in local bodies and councils.
xa: Session: **First Panchama Mahajana Sabha**, **Vijayawada**, **4-6 Nov 1917**.
President: **Bhagya Reddy Varma**.
"Adi Andhra" came into **official use** after it.

n145fdd432b6.s: The first Adi-Andhra session (first Provincial Panchama Mahajana Sabha) of November 1917 was held at:
n145fdd432b6.x: It met at Mailavaram Rajayya Nataka Mandir, Vijayawada, on 4-6 November 1917; the second conference was at Machilipatnam in 1919 and Amalapuram hosted the 1921 Sadassu.
xa: ⚠ APPSC-GS **2025** key: district of the first session = **Krishna**.
**1919** president: **Chilukuri Venkataswamy** — priority to **Dalit education**.

n23a6e88c888.s: The First Adi-Andhra Sadassu was held in 1921 at
n23a6e88c888.x: Undru Tatayya organised the First Adi-Andhra Sadassu at Amalapuram in 1921.
xs: The **First Adi-Andhra Sadassu** was held at **Amalapuram** in **1921** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was led by **Undru Tatayya**.
xa: **Ponnamanda** (Konaseema, **1922**) = Undru Tatayya's Dalit school.
**Kandipappu** (W. Godavari) = **Bojja Appala Swamy's** school.
⚠ Some notes call Amalapuram "first", but the first Adi-Andhra session was **Vijayawada (Krishna)**, **1917**.

n03ada81f327.s: The All India Adi Hindu Conference at Lucknow in 1930, which chose Ambedkar as Dalit representative for the Round Table Conferences, was presided over by:
n03ada81f327.x: Bhagya Reddy Varma presided over the 1930 Lucknow conference.
xa: **1930** also = Ambedkar's **Kalaram Temple Satyagraha**.
Bhagya Reddy Varma also presided over the **1917** Panchama Mahajana Sabha.

nbe11fac944e.s: The journal 'Adi Hindu' was associated with:
nbe11fac944e.x: Adi Hindu was Bhagya Reddy Varma's journal; Jai Bheem and Veera Bharati were Jala Rangaswamy's papers.
xa: ⚠ **Adi Hindu** = Bhagya Reddy Varma; **Kudi Arasu** = Periyar; **Mooknayak** = Ambedkar.
Rangaswamy's titles: **Adi Andhra Mahatma**, **Seva Durandhara**.
**Lakshmi ITI, Ramachandrapuram** (with **Mangamma**).

nbd0929439ee.s: The Arundhatiya Yuvajana Sangham worked for the welfare of the:
nbd0929439ee.x: The Arundhatiya Yuvajana Sangham was the organisation for Madiga welfare in Andhra.
xa: APPSC-GS **2019** asked the **Arundhatiya** – **Madiga** pair.
Adi Andhrapathi Sangham: **1922**.
Undru Tatayya also set up a school at **Ponnamanda** (Konaseema, **1922**).

nf0b687ab95d.s: Which organisation was established by B.R. Ambedkar in 1924 for the welfare of the excluded sections?
nf0b687ab95d.x: Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha was established in 1924 by B.R. Ambedkar for the welfare and advancement of the excluded sections.
xs: Ambedkar set up the **Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha** in **1924** — so option **(1)** is correct.
xa: The Sabha organised the **Mahad Satyagraha (20 March 1927)** at the **Chawdar Tank**.
Chronology: **BHS → Kalaram → ILP → SCF**.
**1924** also = **Vaikom** Satyagraha.

nec644eaacd4.s: Gora founded the Atheist Centre in 1940 at:
nec644eaacd4.x: Gora founded the Atheist Centre at Mudunuru in 1940; it moved to Vijayawada in 1947.
xa: Gora = **Goparaju Ramachandra Rao**.
Other Andhra rationalist: **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary** (**Kavi Raju**).
⚠ **1940** is also the **Dravidistan** demand at Erode.

nb0d5e75e199.s: The Andhra Jana Kendra Sangham was established in 1923 at:
nb0d5e75e199.x: The Andhra Jana Kendra Sangham was founded at Hyderabad in 1923 (APPSC 2012). Vijayawada, Guntur and Madras are distractors.
xs: The **Andhra Jana Kendra Sangham** was founded at **Hyderabad** in **1923** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC **2012**).
**Vijayawada** hosted the **1917** Andhra Mahasabha and Panchama Mahajana Sabha.
xa: Caste journals: **Prabhodini** (**1907**) and **Panchanana** (**1914**) of the **Viswa Brahmana Sangham**.
Other Hyderabad body: **Adi Hindu Social Service League** (**Bhagya Reddy Varma**).
**Adi Hindu** = Dalits of **Hyderabad State**.

n06ebbd7650a.s: Harichand Thakur was associated with the:
n06ebbd7650a.x: Harichand Thakur was associated with the Matua Namashudras of Bengal, not the Nadar movement.
xa: Nadars were in **southern Tamil Nadu / Travancore** (**Nadar Mahajana Sangam**, **1910**).
APPSC **2019** asked the Arundhatiya – Madiga pair.

nb722a2c04d8.x: Ambedkar wrote Annihilation of Caste, Who Were the Shudras? and The Untouchables; Nimna Jatula Charitra was by Jala Rangaswamy.
xa: Ambedkar also wrote **The Problem of the Rupee**.
APPSC-GS **2019** asked **Who Were the Shudras?** → Ambedkar.

n00de277023b.s: Which of the following communities was associated with the SNDP movement?
n00de277023b.x: The SNDP movement in Kerala was associated with the Ezhavas, traditionally toddy-tappers.
n00de277023b.tq: Distinguish the community linked to SNDP from other caste movements in the list.
xs: The **SNDP** movement was associated with the **Ezhavas** (toddy-tappers) of Kerala — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Namashudras** = **Bengal** (Matua); **Mahars** = **Maharashtra**; **Nadars** = southern Tamil Nadu / Travancore.
xa: SNDP Yogam: Kerala, **1903**; inspired by **Sree Narayana Guru**.
Guru's **172nd birth anniversary**: **28 Aug 2026** — "One Caste, One Religion, One God for Man".
**Aruvippuram** Shiva consecration: **1888**.

n498c80beca4.s: Guru Ghasidas, founder of the Satnami movement in Central India, worked among the:
n498c80beca4.x: Guru Ghasidas led the Satnami movement in Chhattisgarh among Chamars, the leatherworkers. Ezhavas were the SNDP base in Kerala, Nadars the community in southern Tamil Nadu, and Namashudras the Matua group of Bengal.
xs: **Guru Ghasidas** worked among **leatherworkers (Chamars)** — the **Satnamis** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2019**).
**Ezhavas** = SNDP (Kerala); **Nadars** = southern Tamil Nadu; **Namashudras** = Bengal (Matua).
xa: Region: **Central India (Chhattisgarh)**.
⚠ **Satnamis** = Guru Ghasidas; **Ezhavas** = SNDP; **Mahars** = Ambedkar.
**Ayyankali** worked among the **Kerala Pulayas**.

nc912af55934.x: Ayyankali founded the Sadhu Jana Paripalana Sangham; Sri Narayana Guru founded the SNDP Yogam and Periyar led the Self-Respect Movement.
xa: SNDP: Kerala, **1903**; Self-Respect: **1925**.
Ayyankali's Sangham was for **Kerala Pulayas** (**1907**).
Self-Respect later became the **Dravidar Kazhagam**.

n027e21d113f.s: Who founded the Depressed Classes Mission at Bombay in 1906?
n027e21d113f.x: The Depressed Classes Mission was founded by V.R. Shinde at Bombay in 1906.
n027e21d113f.tq: Distinguish the founder of the mission from founders of other anti-caste organisations.
xs: **V.R. Shinde** founded the **Depressed Classes Mission** at **Bombay** in **1906** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Phule** founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj** (**1873**); **Ambedkar** the **BHS** (**1924**); **Gandhi** the **Anti-Untouchability League** (**1932**).
xa: **1906** also = **Jagan Mitra Mandali** (Bhagya Reddy Varma).
**All India Depressed Classes Association** = **M.C. Rajah**.
⚠ Gandhi's own body = **Anti-Untouchability League / Harijan Sevak Sangh**.

na354c754420.s: In the 1920s, the Justice Party introduced:
na354c754420.x: The Justice Party introduced a caste-based roster, supported temple entry and promoted schools and scholarships for non-Brahmins.
xa: Also: **Communal G.O. (1921)**; **Andhra University Act (1926)**.
**Bobbili Raja's** ministry amended the **Estate Land Act (1908)** for zamindari tenants.

ndad8d6ede3c.s: Which of the following journals was NOT associated with B.R. Ambedkar?
ndad8d6ede3c.x: Mooknayak, Bahishkrit Bharat and Janata were associated with Ambedkar. Justice was the English newspaper of the Justice Party.
ndad8d6ede3c.tq: Find the odd newspaper from the neighbouring organisational group.
xs: **Justice** was NOT Ambedkar's — it was the **Justice Party's** English daily (**26 Feb 1917**) — option **(1)**.
Ambedkar's journals: **Mooknayak**, **Bahishkrit Bharat**, **Janata**.
xa: **Mooknayak** = "Leader of the Silent" (**1920**).
**Bahishkrit Bharat**: **1927**.
The daily **Justice** gave the **SILF** its popular name.

n5c84255a1cd.s: The Poona Pact, which replaced separate electorates with reserved seats in joint electorates, was signed on:
n5c84255a1cd.x: The Poona Pact was signed on 24 September 1932 and gave 148 seats in place of the 71 under the Communal Award.
xa: Ambedkar agreed **reluctantly** to **save Gandhi's life**.
Gandhi's **Anti-Untouchability League** followed in Sept **1932**.

na7547ed3e6b.s: In 1953 B.R. Ambedkar received an honorary D.Litt from which university?
na7547ed3e6b.x: Osmania University, Hyderabad, conferred an honorary D.Litt on Ambedkar in 1953. Columbia gave him an LL.D in 1952; Andhra University and BHU are not linked to these degrees.
xs: **Osmania University** gave Ambedkar an honorary **D.Litt** in **1953** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2025**).
**Columbia** gave him an **LL.D** in **1952**, not a D.Litt.
xa: The **All India Adi Hindu Conference** (**Lucknow, 1930**) chose Ambedkar as Dalit delegate to the **Round Table Conferences**.
Ambedkar: **Bharat Ratna 1990** (posthumous).
Titles: **"Father of the Indian Constitution"**, **Baba Saheb**.

n3c94eb0f0cd.s: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary was popularly known by which title?
n3c94eb0f0cd.x: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary was popularly known as ‘Kavi Raju’.
n3c94eb0f0cd.tq: Test the exact honorific associated with a regional literary and reform personality.
xs: **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary** was known as **Kavi Raju** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He made a **rationalist attack** on **Puranic** caste stories through drama and poetry.
xa: Works: **Kurukshetra Sangramam**, **Sambuka Vadha**, **Suta Puranam**.
His song "**Veeragandhamu techinaramu**" → **Civil Disobedience Movement** (APPSC **2012**).
He echoed the demand for **reserved seats for non-Brahmins** (Andhra Mahasabha, **1917**).

nc6eac4650e1.s: The proportion of Brahmins in the population of the Madras Presidency and their share in government employment were approximately:
o: 3% of the population and over 90% of government jobs
15% of the population and over 75% of government jobs
10% of the population and 50% of government jobs
25% of the population and 60% of government jobs
nc6eac4650e1.x: Brahmins constituted only about 3% of the Madras Presidency population but held over 90% of government jobs, contributing to the emergence of the non-Brahmin movement.
nc6eac4650e1.tq: Pair the two numerical proportions precisely rather than relying on a general impression.
xs: Brahmins were about **3%** of the Madras Presidency population but held **over 90%** of government jobs — option **(1)**.
This imbalance drove non-Brahmins to meet at **Madras** in **1916**.
xa: The **Justice Party** aimed to protect **non-Brahmin** interests (APPSC **2008**).
It sought **reservation** in jobs, education and legislatures.
Result: the **Communal G.O. (1921)**.

n3b4abe64462.s: Who among the following is associated with the works Paleru, Gudiselu Kalipotunnai, Pilli Shatakam and Paleru Nundi Padmasri Daka?
n3b4abe64462.x: These works are associated with Boyi Bhimanna.
n3b4abe64462.tq: Start from a distinctive work-title cluster and identify its author.
xs: **Paleru**, **Gudiselu Kalipotunnai**, **Pilli Shatakam**, **Paleru Nundi Padmasri Daka** are linked to **Boyi Bhimanna** — option **(2)**.
**Jala Rangaswamy** wrote **Nimna Jatula Charitra**; **Tripuraneni** wrote **Sambuka Vadha**; **Vaddipati Niranjanasastri** ran **Prabhodini**.
xa: Tripuraneni's other works: **Kurukshetra Sangramam**, **Suta Puranam**.
**Gora** wrote **Positive Atheism**.
Prabhodini (**1907**) was the **Viswa Brahmana Sangham** journal.

n6589cc43704.s: Christian mission schools in Andhra admitted:
n6589cc43704.x: Mission schools admitted Sudras and Panchamas, extending education beyond the traditional upper-caste groups.
xa: **London Missionary Society**: **Jammalamadugu, 1805**.
**American Baptists**: Rayalaseema **1835**; schools in Guntur, Gurazala, Palnadu, **Ongole**, Nellore.
**Church Mission Society**: Krishna-Godavari from **1841**; Machilipatnam school became a college in **1864**.
The **Bellary Christian Mission** issued the first Telugu journal, **Satyaduta** (**1835**).

ne6a6fd502b2.s: The London Missionary Society began its work in Andhra in 1805 at:
ne6a6fd502b2.x: The London Missionary Society is associated with Jammalamadugu in Cuddapah, where it began work in Andhra in 1805.
ne6a6fd502b2.tq: Apply the place-and-year pair rather than relying on the organisation alone.
xs: The **London Missionary Society** began at **Jammalamadugu** (Cuddapah) in **1805** — option **(3)**.
**Machilipatnam** was a **Church Mission Society** centre (from **1841**).
**Rajahmundry** was the social-reform base, not an LMS centre.
xa: LMS also worked in **Cuddapah, Kurnool and Bellary**.
⚠ **LMS** = Jammalamadugu **1805**; **CMS** = Krishna-Godavari **1841**.
**North German Mission** = Godavari; **Pennsylvania Synod** = Guntur, Prattipadu, Nallapadu.

n2dc967597f4.s: The widow homes established by Kandukuri Veeresalingam were located at:
n2dc967597f4.x: Veeresalingam established a widow home at Madras in 1897 and another at Rajahmundry in 1905. The Rajahmundry home was called Vitantu Saranalayam.
n2dc967597f4.tq: Use the paired-place and year sequence to eliminate reversed locations.
xs: Veeresalingam's widow homes were at **Madras (1897)** and **Rajahmundry (1905)** — option **(4)**.
The Rajahmundry home, opened **16 Jan 1905**, was the **Sri Victoria Widow Asylum** = **Vitantu Saranalayam**.
Option (1) reverses the places; 1880 and 1909 are the years of the Widow Remarriage Association and the Ram Mohan Roy School.
xa: **Hitakarini Samajam** (**1905**; some notes **1906**) managed all his institutions.
He gave **all his property** (**Rs 50,000**) to it for women's homes and schools.
His wife **Rajyalakshmamma** sheltered widows and couples of the remarriage movement.

n656e5b242c6.s: Which institution was managed through the entire property donated by Kandukuri Veeresalingam?
n656e5b242c6.x: Veeresalingam donated his entire property, valued at Rs. 50,000, to Hitakarini Samajam, which managed all his institutions.
n656e5b242c6.tq: Link the distinctive donation detail with the institution it supported.
xs: Veeresalingam gave **all his property** (**Rs 50,000**) to the **Hitakarini Samajam**, which managed all his institutions — option **(2)**.
It was founded in **1905** (some notes **1906**).
The **Social Reform Association**, **Widow Remarriage Association** (**1880**) and **Prarthana Samaj** (**1878**) were earlier bodies with narrower aims.
xa: The money went to **women's homes and schools**.
**Sri Victoria Widow Asylum** (Vitantu Saranalayam), Rajahmundry, opened **16 Jan 1905**.
Titles: **Andhra Rammohan Roy**, **Gadya Tikkana**, **Yuga Karta**.

n4bb6fadae9d.s: Andhra's first girls' school, started by Kandukuri Veeresalingam in 1874, was located at:
n4bb6fadae9d.x: Veeresalingam opened the first girls' school in Andhra at Dowlaiswaram, near Rajahmundry, in 1874 (some keys say simply 'at Rajahmundry'). Innispeta in Rajahmundry got his second girls' school in 1881. Kakinada and Machilipatnam were later reform centres, not the site of the first school.
xs: Andhra's **first girls' school** (**1874**) was at **Dowlaiswaram** near Rajahmundry — option **(2)**.
**Innispeta** (Rajahmundry) had his **second** girls' school, **1881**.
**Kakinada** and **Machilipatnam** were later reform centres.
xa: ⚠ CDX and APP say **Dowlaiswaram**; APHQ and CDI say "**at Rajahmundry**".
Veeresalingam was the first in Andhra to promote **co-education**.
His **Satihitabodhini** (**1883**) was a monthly for women's education.

ne953ca635ae.s: On 3 August 1879, Kandukuri Veeresalingam delivered a public lecture at Rajahmundry declaring that widow remarriage was
o: a matter solely for colonial courts
ne953ca635ae.x: On 3 August 1879, Veeresalingam publicly argued at Rajahmundry that widow remarriage was sanctioned by Hindu scripture. He was attacked and was protected by his students.
ne953ca635ae.tq: Test the precise claim made in a reform lecture rather than the later marriage event.
xs: On **3 Aug 1879** Veeresalingam declared widow remarriage **scripturally valid** — option **(1)**.
He was attacked at the meeting and **saved by his students**.
xa: The first remarriage followed on **11 Dec 1881** at Rajahmundry.
**Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856** (Act XV) — Vidyasagar's campaign, under **Lord Canning**.
**Vedam Venkataraya Sastri** replied with **Stree Punarvivaha Durvada Nirvaranam** (**1883**), the first major anti-remarriage book.

n59bb3cf6b89.s: The first widow remarriage in Andhra, held at Veeresalingam's house in Rajahmundry, took place on:
n59bb3cf6b89.x: It took place on 11 December 1881 at Ananda Udyana Mandapam; the groom was Gogulapati Sriramulu and the bride Seethamma (Gauramma).
xa: Second remarriage: **15 Dec 1881** (Racharla Ramachandrayya - Ratnamma).
Totals differ: **20** by **1892**; about **53** in all; **61** by **1904**.
At **Kakinada**, **Paidah Ramakrishnayya** funded remarriages and built houses for grooms.

nabaa563cbd8.s: The anti-remarriage work 'Stree Punarvivaha Durvada Nirvaranam' was written by:
nabaa563cbd8.x: Vedam Venkataraya Sastri wrote it; Paidah Ramakrishnayya supported remarriages at Kakinada and Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri was linked with the Aryananda Brundavani Sabha.
xa: Kasibhatta's **Arya Mata Bodhini** drew Veeresalingam's reply **Satyavahini** (**1905**).
Kasibhatta also called **Rajasekhara Charitra** a mere translation.
**Kalpavalli** (Machilipatnam) was another anti-remarriage paper.

nd6166652a8c.s: The first major anti-widow-remarriage book mentioned in connection with Andhra was
nd6166652a8c.x: Vedam Venkataraya Sastri wrote Stree Punarvivaha Durvada Nirvaranam in 1883, described as the first major anti-remarriage book.
nd6166652a8c.tq: Identify the exact title of a polemical work instead of a reformist literary work.
xs: **Stree Punarvivaha Durvada Nirvaranam** (**1883**), by **Vedam Venkataraya Sastri**, was the first major anti-remarriage book — option **(4)**.
**Abala Sachcharitra Ratnamala** is **Bhandaru Acchamamba**'s women's biography series.
**Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu** (from Gulliver's Travels) and **Brahma Vivaham** (satire) are Veeresalingam's pro-reform works.
xa: Other opponents: **Kalpavalli** paper (Machilipatnam) and **Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri** (Aryananda Brundavani Sabha).
**Kokkonda Venkataratnam** of Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini also opposed reform and women's education.
The first remarriage the book opposed took place on **11 Dec 1881**.

n9c727c487a1.s: Which one of the following journals was started as a satirical reply to Kokkonda Venkataratnam's Hasyavardhini?
n9c727c487a1.x: Veeresalingam's Hasyasanjeevani, started in 1876, was a satirical reply to Kokkonda Venkataratnam's Hasyavardhini.
n9c727c487a1.tq: Discriminate between similarly named journals by identifying the direction of the rivalry.
xs: **Hasyasanjeevani** (**1876**), Veeresalingam's satire, replied to Kokkonda's **Hasyavardhini** — option **(4)**.
**Satyasamvardhini** was the Prarthana Samaj monthly; **Satyaduta** the first Telugu journal; **Satihitabodhini** a women's monthly.
xa: It mocked Kokkonda as "**Ko.Ko.Ko...kkonda**".
**Kokkonda Venkataratnam** also edited the orthodox **Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini**.
The rivalry began with Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini vs **Purushartha Pradayini** (Machilipatnam), where Veeresalingam first wrote.

nbb0cb67b54a.x: Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu was based on Gulliver's Travels; Veeresalingam also wrote the first Telugu novel Rajasekhara Charitra and the satire Brahma Vivaham.
xa: Rajasekhara Charitra (**1878**) was modelled on Goldsmith's **The Vicar of Wakefield**.
**Vyavahara Dharmabodhini**: play satirising lawyers.
First to render classical Sanskrit drama into Telugu: **Abhijnana Sakuntalam**, **Malavikagnimitram**, **Ratnavali**.

nd7a4a975403.s: Who among the following founded the Andhra Desa Library Association in 1914?
nd7a4a975403.x: Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah founded the Andhra Desa Library Association in 1914.
nd7a4a975403.tq: Distinguish the founder of the library movement from leaders of the spoken-Telugu movement.
xs: **Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah** founded the **Andhra Desa Library Association** (**1914**) — option **(2)**.
He led the **Library movement**.
**Gidugu** led the vyavaharika movement; **Acchamamba** founded Stree Samajam; **Gurajada** wrote Kanyasulkam.
xa: **Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam**: Hyderabad, **1901**.
**Kavi Club, Kumudavalli** (West Godavari): **1897**.
**Madras Native Association**: **1852**.

n7bad03ee6b8.s: Gurajada Appa Rao worked with which reformer in promoting literary and cultural renaissance in Andhra?
n7bad03ee6b8.x: Gurajada Appa Rao worked alongside Kandukuri Veeresalingam's reform activities, contributing to literary and cultural renaissance.
n7bad03ee6b8.tq: Use the associated-person trap by distinguishing collaborators from other reformers.
xs: Gurajada worked alongside **Kandukuri Veeresalingam**'s reform, focusing on **literary and cultural renaissance** — option **(3)**.
**Vedam Venkataraya Sastri** was an **opponent** of widow remarriage; **Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah** led the Library movement.
xa: His literature attacked **bride-price** and the exploitation of widows.
With **Gidugu**, he championed **vyavaharika** (spoken) Telugu.

n4097983a88a.s: Who among the following was known as the ‘Gadya Tikkana’ and ‘Andhra Vaitalikudu’?
n4097983a88a.x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam was known by several titles, including Gadya Tikkana and Andhra Vaitalikudu.
n4097983a88a.tq: Discriminate among reformers by matching multiple honorific titles to one person.
xs: **Gadya Tikkana** and **Andhra Vaitalikudu** are titles of **Kandukuri Veeresalingam** — option **(1)**.
**Kavi Raju** = **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary**; **Brahmarshi** = **Venkataratnam Naidu**.
xa: Other titles: **Gadya Vajmaya Brahma**, **Yuga Karta**, **Andhra Rammohan Roy**.
He was the **Father of the Andhra Renaissance**.
**Rao Bahadur** (**1893**, British government).

n58a860f41e7.s: The title ‘Vidyasagar of South India’ was conferred on Kandukuri Veeresalingam by:
n58a860f41e7.x: M. G. Ranade called Veeresalingam the ‘Vidyasagar of South India’ in 1898, when Veeresalingam presided over the Indian Social Reform Congress at Madras.
n58a860f41e7.tq: Pair the title with the person who bestowed it, not with the reformer’s own title.
xs: **M.G. Ranade** called Veeresalingam the "**Vidyasagar of South India**" — option **(1)**.
This was in **1898**, when Veeresalingam presided over the **Indian Social Reform Congress, Madras** (PYQ **2019**).
xa: Veeresalingam : Andhra :: **Vidyasagar** : Bengal — widow remarriage, girls' schools.
Bengal's first remarriage **7 Dec 1856**; Andhra's **11 Dec 1881**.
⚠ **Mrs Manning** (willed **50 pounds** to his association) is used as a distractor.

n6e984aa17ea.s: Kandukuri Veeresalingam is popularly known as:
n6e984aa17ea.x: Veeresalingam is called Andhra Rammohan Roy (Raja Ram Mohan Roy of Andhra) and the father of the Andhra renaissance. Andhra Kesari was Tanguturi Prakasam. Andhra Ratna was Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, and Kavi Raju was Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary.
n6e984aa17ea.tq: Andhra Rammohan Roy = Veeresalingam; Andhra Ratna = Duggirala.
xs: Veeresalingam is called **Andhra Rammohan Roy** (Raja Ram Mohan Roy of Andhra) — option **(4)**.
**Andhra Ratna** = **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**; **Kavi Raju** = **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary**.
xa: He is also the **Father of the Andhra Renaissance** and of the Social Reform Movement in Andhra.
Other titles: **Gadya Tikkana**, **Yuga Karta**, **Andhra Vaitalikudu**.
"**Vidyasagar of South India**" — **M.G. Ranade** (**1898**).

n1ef55ca8874.s: Who described Kandukuri Veeresalingam's Rajasekhara Charitra as a mere translation?
n1ef55ca8874.x: Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri criticised Rajasekhara Charitra by calling it a mere translation.
n1ef55ca8874.tq: Apply the author-versus-critic discrimination trap in literary history.
xs: **Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri** called **Rajasekhara Charitra** a mere translation — option **(3)**.
**Kokkonda Venkataratnam** was a different orthodox critic (Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini, Hasyavardhini).
xa: Kasibhatta ran the **Aryananda Brundavani Sabha**, Kakinada; his **Arya Mata Bodhini** drew Veeresalingam's **Satyavahini** (**1905**).
Rajasekhara Charitra (**1878**) was modelled on Goldsmith's **The Vicar of Wakefield**.
It is the **first Telugu novel**.

nap-history-15-12.s: The newspaper Andhra Geeta Svarajya, published from Madras, was started in 1921 by:
nap-history-15-12.x: Andhra Geeta Svarajya was started by Tanguturi Prakasam in 1921 and published from Madras.
n: Andhra Geeta Svarajya is a newspaper. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Andhra Geeta Svarajya was written by Tanguturi Prakasam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Andhra Geeta Svarajya was started in 1921 in Madras. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
xa: **Desha Matha** — edited by **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham**; supported **Home Rule**.
**Rayyat** (**1927**) — an **Urdu daily** edited by **M. Narasinga Rao**.
**Vahini** (**1930**) — Telugu political journal linked with **N. G. Ranga**.

nc3c2897ed1a.s: The earliest phase of Andhra social reform was led mainly by which social group?
nc3c2897ed1a.x: The reform movement began in Rajahmundry under the leadership of the English-educated middle class. It was not an exclusive movement of rulers, soldiers or European missionaries.
nc3c2897ed1a.tq: Identify the social base of a movement rather than its geographical location.
xs: Andhra reform began at **Rajahmundry** under the **English-educated middle class** — option **(4)**.
It was not the work of princely families, a military aristocracy or missionaries alone; zamindari patrons such as the **Pithapuram Raja** only funded later work.
Its first guru was **Atmuri Lakshmi Narasimham**.
xa: Rajahmundry (**Godavari district**, today East Godavari) = Andhra's **first Renaissance centre**.
Peak period: **1870-1935**; other main centre **Kakinada**.
Veeresalingam used the **press, not politics**, for reform; by **1905** about **20** Telugu journals were in print.
Reform became institutional — **samajs, homes, journals** — and so outlived its founders.
