n9f04d19d479.s: Who is identified as the first guru associated with the early social reform movement in Andhra?
n9f04d19d479.x: Atmuri Lakshmi Narasimham is identified as the first guru of the early Andhra social reform movement.
n9f04d19d479.tq: Recall the specific title-holder among several reform-era personalities.
xs: **Atmuri Lakshmi Narasimham** is named the **first guru** of Andhra social reform — option **(1)**.
**Gidugu Ramamurthy** led the **vyavaharika** (spoken Telugu) movement; **Gurajada Apparao** wrote **Kanyasulkam**.
**Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary** was the rationalist poet called **Kavi Raju**.
xa: The early reform was led by the **English-educated middle class** of **Rajahmundry**.
Peak: **1870-1935**; main centres **Rajahmundry** and **Kakinada**.
First organised reform body: **Rajahmundry Social Reform Association** (Veeresalingam).

ncc88c56bacc.s: Which one of the following was the first organised social reform body in Andhra?
ncc88c56bacc.x: The Rajahmundry Social Reform Association was regarded as the first organised reform body in Andhra.
ncc88c56bacc.tq: Distinguish the earliest organisation from later reform bodies by its specific description.
xs: The **Rajahmundry Social Reform Association** was the **first organised reform body** in Andhra — option **(2)**.
Its aim was **widow remarriage** — shelter, legal defence and money for widows.
The **Prarthana Samaj** (**1878**), **Widow Remarriage Association** (**1880**) and **Hitakarini Samajam** (**1905**) came later.
xa: ⚠ Its date varies: **1871** (RPSC key), **1875** (CDX), **1878** (some notes) — learn all three.
Hitakarini Samajam managed all his institutions; he gave it **all his property** (**Rs 50,000**).
Also Veeresalingam's: Andhra's **first night school** and **first Theosophical High School**.

n85654c8b627.s: Which of the following was NOT among the social evils against which reform activities in Andhra were directed?
n85654c8b627.x: Expansion of scientific education was a reform objective, not a social evil. The listed evils included child marriage, nautch or Bhogam and official corruption, among others.
n85654c8b627.tq: Find the item that is a reform measure rather than a social evil.
xs: **Expansion of scientific education** was not a social evil — option **(1)**.
The evils targeted: ban on widow remarriage, **child marriage**, **dowry**, **caste**, bride-price, superstition, **nautch/Bhogam** and **official corruption**.
xa: Methods: **journals and satire**, public lectures, **schools and co-education**, remarriages at his own cost, widow homes.
**Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu** led the **anti-nautch** (Devadasi) campaign.
**Gurajada**'s **Kanyasulkam** attacked **bride-price** and child marriage.

nc59e16e899d.s: Which was the first Telugu political journal?
nc59e16e899d.x: Chintamani was the first Telugu political journal; Satyaduta was the Bellary Christian Mission's, Satyasamvardhini the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj's, and Janana Patrika concerned women's education.
xa: Janana/Zenana Patrika: **1893/1894**; Venkata Siva, later Veeresalingam.
Chintamani was jointly edited by **Veeresalingam** and **Nyapati Subbarao**.
⚠ APPSC 2019 key marks "Telugu Janana - Veeresalingam" as the **wrong pair**.

nf1bbd939953.s: Who, as editor of Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini, led orthodox opposition to spoken Telugu prose?
nf1bbd939953.x: Kokkonda Venkataratnam, the orthodox editor of Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini, opposed the move towards spoken Telugu.
xa: Kokkonda also opposed **women's education**; his **Hasyavardhini** attacked Vivekavardhini.
**Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu** led the classical side through the **Andhra Sahitya Parishad**.
Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini is credited with the **first editorial column**.

nf09cf1e797a.s: Chintamani (1891), regarded as the first Telugu political journal, was jointly edited by:
o: Rayasam Venkata Siva and A.C. Parthasarathi Naidu
nf09cf1e797a.x: Chintamani (1891) was jointly edited by Veeresalingam and Nyapati Subbarao. Kokkonda was an orthodox editor, and Umaranga Nayakulu ran Purushartha Pradayini. Gidugu and Gurajada led the language movement. Rayasam Venkata Siva edited Satyasamvardhini, and Parthasarathi Naidu is linked with Andhra Prakasika.
xs: **Chintamani** (**1891**) was jointly edited by **Veeresalingam** and **Nyapati Subbarao** — option **(3)**.
**Kokkonda** was an orthodox editor; **Umaranga Nayakulu** ran **Purushartha Pradayini**.
**Gidugu** and **Gurajada** led the language movement; **Rayasam Venkata Siva** edited Satyasamvardhini; **Parthasarathi Naidu** is linked with Andhra Prakasika.
xa: ⚠ First political **journal** = **Chintamani**; first political **weekly** (CDX) = **Andhra Prakasika** (**1885**).
First social-reform journal = **Vivekavardhini** (**1874**).
First Telugu journal = **Satyaduta** (**1835**).

nf144b6c3b0f.s: Who wrote Kasiyatra Charitra, an important early modern Telugu travelogue?
nf144b6c3b0f.x: Kasiyatra Charitra was written by Enugula Veeraswamayya.
xa: **Stree Punarvivaha Durvada Nirvaranam** (**1883**) — Vedam Venkataraya Sastri.
Telugu **Brahma Dharmam** — **Chembeti Sridharulu Naidu** (**1875**), published by Mannava Buchayya Pantulu (**1886**).
**Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu** (Veeresalingam) is based on Gulliver's Travels.

n9de40e5c105.s: C. P. Brown is particularly associated with which contribution to Telugu studies?
o: Preparing the first Telugu-English dictionaries and editing Vemana’s verses
n9de40e5c105.x: C. P. Brown, Collector of Cuddapah, prepared the first Telugu-English dictionaries and edited Vemana’s verses.
n9de40e5c105.tq: Combine two distinctive contributions of the same personality.
xs: **C.P. Brown**, Collector of **Cuddapah**, made the **first Telugu-English dictionaries** and edited **Vemana**'s verses — option **(1)**.
**Mutyala Saralu** is **Gurajada**'s; the **first Telugu autobiography** is Veeresalingam's.
The **Navya Sahitya Parishat** was a youth body spreading **Gidugu**'s vyavaharika cause.
xa: **Kasiyatra Charitra** (travelogue) — **Enugula Veeraswamayya**.
Cuddapah also had the **London Missionary Society** (Jammalamadugu, **1805**).
First Telugu journal: **Satyaduta** (**1835**), Bellary.

nc94cf2f9364.s: Who inspired the Vyavaharika Telugu movement?
nc94cf2f9364.x: J. A. Yates inspired the movement for the use of Vyavaharika Telugu.
nc94cf2f9364.tq: Discriminate among the individuals associated with different roles in the language movement.
xs: **J.A. Yates** inspired the vyavaharika movement — option **(3)**.
**P.T. Srinivasa Ayyangar** wrote **Life or Death: A Plea for Vernaculars**.
**Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu** and **Kokkonda Venkataratnam** were **opponents**.
xa: Grammars for vyavaharika: **Malladi Suryanarayana Sastri** (Andhra Bhashanusasanam), **Vadlamudi Gopalakrishnayya** (Vyavaharika Bhasha Vyakaranam).
**Vajjala Venkateswarlu**: Aadhunikapramanikandhra Vyakaranam.
Leaders: **Gidugu** (theory, education), **Gurajada** (literature).

na8a37b98a18.s: Which one of the following places became the centre of Telugu social reform, modern prose, journalism and the novel during the nineteenth century?
na8a37b98a18.x: Rajahmundry emerged as the centre of Telugu social reform and the development of modern prose, journalism and the novel.
na8a37b98a18.tq: Use the significance-based location clue and distinguish the reform centre from other Andhra places.
xs: **Rajahmundry** was the centre of Telugu **social reform, modern prose, journalism and the novel** — option **(4)**.
**Vizianagaram** was a cradle of the **language movement**; **Madanapalle** is the **Theosophy** link; **Kakinada** was the other reform centre.
xa: Rajahmundry (Godavari district) = Andhra's **first Renaissance centre**.
Firsts there: **Prarthana Samaj** (**1878**), first widow remarriage (**11 Dec 1881**).
Dowlaiswaram near it had the **first girls' school** (**1874**).

nae13399e713.s: Which of the following best explains the principal method adopted by Kandukuri Veeresalingam for advancing social reform?
o: Organising armed resistance against colonial rule
Using the press rather than direct political activity
Rejecting all forms of public education
Working exclusively through princely state administrations
nae13399e713.x: Veeresalingam primarily used the press as an instrument of social reform rather than pursuing reform through direct political activity.
nae13399e713.tq: Identify the means of reform from the contrast between press activism and political action.
xs: Veeresalingam used the **press, not politics**, for reform — option **(2)**.
He set up his own **printing press in 1876**; by **1905** about **20** Telugu journals were in print.
xa: His journals: **Vivekavardhini** (**1874**), **Hasyasanjeevani** (**1876**), **Satihitabodhini** (**1883**).
Other methods: public lectures, **schools and co-education**, remarriages at his own cost, widow homes.
He created the Telugu **reading public** and modern prose.

nap-history-15-1.s: Which of the following was the first Telugu journal?
nap-history-15-1.x: Satya Doota, started in 1835 by the Christian Association of Bellary, was the first Telugu journal. Andhra Prakasika was the first political journal, and Vivekavardhini came later in 1874.
nap-history-15-1.tq: Discriminate the first journal from the first political journal.
n: Vivekavardhini is a journal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Satya Doota is the first Telugu journal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Andhra Prakasika is the first political journal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Hasyavardhani is a journal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Satya Doota was started by the Christian Association of Bellary. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Satya Doota was published from Bellary. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
xs: **Satya Doota** (**Satyadoota**) was the **first Telugu journal** (**1835**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was published from **Bellary** by the **Christian Association of Bellary**.
**Andhra Prakasika** was the **first political journal** (**1885**); **Vivekavardhini** and **Hasyavardhani** came in **1874**.
xa: ⚠ First Telugu social-reform journal = **Vivekavardhini**; first Telugu political journal (other notes) = **Chintamani** (**1891**).
**Satihita Bodhini** (**1883**) was Veeresalingam's monthly for women.
By **1905** about **20** Telugu journals were in print.

nap-history-15-11.s: Who was one of the founders and the first editor of the weekly Telugu magazine Krishna Patrika?
nap-history-15-11.x: Konda Venkatappayya was one of Krishna Patrika's founders and its first editor.
n: Krishna Patrika is a weekly Telugu magazine. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Konda Venkatappayya was one of the founders of Krishna Patrika. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Konda Venkatappayya was the first editor of Krishna Patrika. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
xa: It was founded by **A. P. Partha Sarathi Naidu**; ⚠ other notes credit **Mutnuri Krishna Rao**.
It dates from the **early twentieth century**, ⚠ not the eighteenth.
Konda Venkatappaiah is the **father** of the **Andhra State Movement**.

nap-history-15-13.s: Desabhimani commented on the need for which of the following?
nap-history-15-13.x: Desabhimani, a Telugu newspaper, commented on the need for a separate government for Telugu culture, an early voice for a separate Andhra.
nap-history-15-13.tq: Recall the stand of each newspaper.
n: Desabhimani is a Telugu newspaper. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Desabhimani commented on the need for a separate government for Telugu culture. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
xs: **Desabhimani** commented on the need for a **separate government for Telugu culture** — so option **(2)** is correct.
A monthly reform magazine is **Satihita Bodhini**; the first political journal is **Andhra Prakasika**; the weekly Telugu magazine is **Krishna Patrika**.
xa: **Andhra Geeta Svarajya** (**1921**) — **Tanguturi Prakasam**, Madras.
**Nilagiri** was published from **Nalgonda**.
**Desha Matha** backed the **Home Rule Movement**.

nap-history-15-14.s: The Nilagiri journal was published from:
nap-history-15-14.x: Nilagiri, started by Shabnavis Venkata Rama Narasimha Rao, was published from Nalgonda in Telangana.
n: Nilagiri is a journal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Nilagiri was published from Nalgonda. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
xa: **Rayyat** — an **Urdu daily** (**1927**), **M. Narasinga Rao**.
**Andhra Geeta Svarajya** — **Madras**, **1921**.

nap-history-16-16.s: The journal Hasyavardhani was associated with:
nap-history-16-16.x: Hasyavardhani was Kokkonda Venkata Ratnam's journal; Veeresalingam was linked with the Brahmo Samaj in Andhra, Viveka Vardhini and the Vyavaaharikandhra Bhasha Parivartaka Samajam.
n: Brahmo Samaj in the combined Andhra Pradesh was founded by Kandukuri Veeresalingam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 22-23]
Viveka Vardhini was founded by Kandukuri Veeresalingam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 22-23]
Vyavaaharikandhra Bhasha Parivartaka Samajam was founded by Kandukuri Veeresalingam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 22-23]
The Hasyavardhani Journal was founded by Kokkonda Venkata Ratnam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 22-23]
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: other notes credit the Bhasha Parivartaka Samaj to **Gidugu Ramamurthy** (APPSC **2017**).
⚠ Other notes say the first Brahmo Samaj in Andhra was at **Machilipatnam** (**1882**) under Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu.
Veeresalingam founded the **Prarthana Samaj, Rajahmundry** (**1878**).
nap-history-16-16.fixed: Vyavaharika Bhasha Parivartaka Samaj was Gidugu's (APPSC 2017; y5ecee5fcb35), Hasyavardhani was Kokkonda's: only two (I, II) are Veeresalingam's

n2bb1b10d57f.s: Which of the following social evils was directly associated with the term 'Bhogam' in reform discussions in Andhra?
n2bb1b10d57f.x: Nautch, or the Bhogam system, was one of the social evils targeted by reformers in Andhra.
n2bb1b10d57f.tq: Discriminate between a named social practice and other evils in the same reform list.
xs: **Bhogam** refers to the **nautch** (Devadasi) custom — option **(2)**.
**Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu** began the **anti-nautch (Devadasi)** movement in Madras and was the main force behind ending the **Bhogam caste** custom.
xa: APPSC **2019**: Venkataratnam Naidu = main factor in eliminating the **'Bhogam' caste**.
**Desiraju Peda Bapayya**'s **Temperance and Social Purity Sangham** led a boycott of Bhogam melas.
**Devadasi bill**: **Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy** + Chodagam Ammannaraja — bill **1937**, passed **1947**.
Venkataratnam Naidu's **People's Friend** was an anti-Devadasi journal.

n87c4aa099f1.s: The Brahmo Trinity of Andhra comprised Veeresalingam, Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu and:
n87c4aa099f1.x: The Brahmo Trinity of Andhra was Veeresalingam, Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu and Desiraju Peda Bapaiah.
xa: Desiraju Peda Bapayya (**Bapatla**) = **first practising (Anushtanika) Brahmo** in Andhra; discarded the sacred thread.
Comparison: Veeresalingam (**Prarthana Samaj**, widow remarriage) vs Venkataratnam Naidu (**Brahmo Samaj**, anti-nautch, social purity).
Venkataratnam Naidu's **Social Purity Association**: **1891**.

n016bc4bbf19.s: Who among the following was the first practising Brahmo in Andhra and later founded the Temperance and Social Purity Sangham at Rajahmundry?
n016bc4bbf19.x: Desiraju Peda Bapayya of Bapatla was the first practising, or Anushtanika, Brahmo in Andhra. He discarded the sacred thread and founded the Temperance and Social Purity Sangham at Rajahmundry.
n016bc4bbf19.tq: Identify the reformer through two distinctive institutional and personal clues.
xs: **Desiraju Peda Bapayya** of **Bapatla** was the **first practising (Anushtanika) Brahmo** in Andhra — option **(1)**.
He discarded the sacred thread and founded the **Temperance and Social Purity Sangham**, Rajahmundry.
**Pillarisetty Sitaramayya** founded the Guntur Samaj; **Venkataratnam Naidu** founded the **Social Purity Association** (**1891**), a different body.
xa: His Sangham led the **boycott of Bhogam melas**.
He is one of the Andhra **Brahmo Trinity** with Veeresalingam and Venkataratnam Naidu.
⚠ **Temperance and Social Purity Sangham** = Bapayya; **Samajika Shuddhi Samajam** = Venkataratnam Naidu.

n88285612b6d.s: The Brahmo movement in Andhra declined mainly because of splits that followed:
o: Veeresalingam's founding of the Prarthana Samaj at Rajahmundry
Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu joining the Justice Party
the passing of the Vernacular Press Act
the death of Desiraju Pedda Bapayya at Bapatla
n88285612b6d.x: The movement split and declined after Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu joined the Justice Party. The Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj (1878) came at the start of the movement, not its decline. The Vernacular Press Act concerned the press. Bapayya's death is not given as the cause.
n88285612b6d.tq: Decline = Venkataratnam Naidu to the Justice Party.
xs: The Andhra Brahmo movement split and declined after **Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu joined the Justice Party** — option **(2)**.
The Rajahmundry **Prarthana Samaj** (**1878**) marked the movement's start, not its decline.
xa: Brahmo Trinity: **Veeresalingam**, **Venkataratnam Naidu**, **Desiraju Peda Bapayya**.
Reform became institutional (samajs, homes, journals) and so **outlived its founders**.
Venkataratnam Naidu was the **first Andhra Vice-Chancellor of Madras University**.

n25865395fe0.s: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu was inspired to join the Brahmo Samaj by whom?
n25865395fe0.x: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu joined the Brahmo Samaj under the inspiration of Pandit Sivanath Sastri.
xs: Venkataratnam Naidu joined the Brahmo Samaj inspired by **Pandit Sivanath Sastri** — option **(4)**.
**Debendranath Tagore** wrote **Brahma Dharmam**, which Chembeti Sridharulu Naidu translated into Telugu.
xa: He founded the **Brahmo Samaj, Machilipatnam** (**1882**).
His centre was **Kakinada**; he took reform to **North Coastal Andhra**.
Bodies: **Brahmopasana Mandiram**, **Andhra Brahma Dharma Pracharak Nidhi**, **Karunalayam** (with the Pithapuram Maharaja).

n0d268f9ef27.s: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu founded the Samajika Shuddhi Samajam in:
n0d268f9ef27.x: He founded the Samajika Shuddhi Samajam in 1891 and was associated with the anti-nautch movement in Madras.
xa: The Social Purity Association was his **most important** body.
⚠ Similar names: **Social Purity Association** (Venkataratnam Naidu) vs **Temperance and Social Purity Sangham** (Bapayya).
His anti-Devadasi journal: **People's Friend**.

ne8e66909ae8.s: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu received a knighthood in 1924 and was the first person of which category to receive it?
ne8e66909ae8.x: He was the first non-official educator to receive a knighthood, in 1924.
ne8e66909ae8.tq: Use the precise description rather than the associated titles.
xs: Venkataratnam Naidu's **knighthood** (**1924**) made him the **first non-official educator** knighted — option **(3)**.
He was principal of **Pithapuram Raja's College** (**1905-18**) and first Andhra VC of **Madras University**.
xa: His students called him **Brahmarshi** (**1932**).
Other titles: **Rao Bahadur**, **Diwan Bahadur**, **Kulapati**, **Abhinava Socrates**.
⚠ **Rao Bahadur** = Veeresalingam (**1893**) and Venkataratnam Naidu; **Rao Saheb** = Gidugu.

n9f8d196aa5a.s: Gurajada Appa Rao's 'Mutyala Saralu' is noted for:
n9f8d196aa5a.x: Mutyala Saralu introduced a new metre; Kanyasulkam attacked bride-price and Desamunu Preminchumanna is his patriotic song.
xa: **Diddubatu** = first modern Telugu **short story**.
**Saranga Dhara** (**1883**) = English poem, with brother Shyamala Rao.
Other works: **Kalinga Desa Charitra**, Neelagiri Paatalu, Gramina Sabda Vicharam.

nf155c952839.s: Who among the following, along with Gurajada Appa Rao, championed the use of vyavaharika or spoken Telugu?
nf155c952839.x: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy and Gurajada Appa Rao were prominent champions of vyavaharika, or spoken, Telugu.
nf155c952839.tq: Separate leaders of the spoken-Telugu movement from leaders of library and widow-remarriage movements.
xs: **Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy** and Gurajada championed **vyavaharika** (spoken) Telugu — option **(2)**.
Gidugu supplied the **theory and education** side; Gurajada the **literature**.
**Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri** was an orthodox opponent of reform; **Paidah Ramakrishnayya** funded remarriages.
xa: Gidugu = "**Father of the Vyavaharika Bhashodyamam**"; founded the **Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Samstha** (**1910**).
Opponents: **Kokkonda Venkataratnam**, **Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu**.
**Telugu Language Day** = **29 August**, Gidugu's birthday.

n2030206a6b0.s: The first staging of Kanyasulkam was associated with which troupe and place?
n2030206a6b0.x: Kanyasulkam was first staged by the Jagannatha Vilasa Nataka Sangham of Vizianagaram.
n2030206a6b0.tq: Match the literary work with its first staging institution and place.
xs: Kanyasulkam was first staged by the **Jagannatha Vilasa Nataka Sangham**, **Vizianagaram** — option **(1)**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes date the first staging to **1893**.
Characters: **Madhuravani** (reformed courtesan), **Girisham** (educated fraud), **Buchamma** (widow), **Soujanya Rao** (reformer).
Dialect: **Srikakulam dialect**.

n8648d9169cf.s: Gurajada's Kanyasulkam, written in 1890, was first staged in:
n8648d9169cf.x: Kanyasulkam was written in 1890, first staged on 13 August 1892 and published in 1897 by Vavilla.
xa: 2nd edition **1909**, dedicated to **Ananda Gajapati**.
First **vyavaharika** play.
Exam angle (APPSC-GS 2024): a **satirical play on social evils** — true.

o: The first modern Telugu short story
ndeff458ca9a.x: Diddubatu is regarded as the first modern Telugu short story and deals with social reform.
ndeff458ca9a.tq: Test the literary milestone and genre together.
xs: **Diddubatu** is regarded as the **first modern Telugu short story** — option **(1)**.
The **first Telugu social play** in vyavaharika is **Kanyasulkam**; Gurajada's English poem is **Saranga Dhara**.
xa: Diddubatu has a **social reform** theme.
First Telugu **novel**: **Rajasekhara Charitra** (**1878**); first Telugu **autobiography**: Veeresalingam's.
**Mutyala Saralu** introduced a new metre.

ne5c3aa06a5e.s: Telugu Language Day is observed on 29 August in recognition of the contribution of
ne5c3aa06a5e.x: 29 August is observed as Telugu Language Day in recognition of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy, a major champion of vyavaharika Telugu.
ne5c3aa06a5e.tq: Link a commemorative date with the correct movement leader rather than a general reformer.
xs: **Telugu Language Day** (**29 August**) is **Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy**'s birthday — option **(3)**.
He is the only Indian whose birthday is a state language day.
xa: It is called **Telugu Bhasha Dinotsavam**.
Gidugu = "**Father of the Vyavaharika Bhashodyamam**".
Telugu got **classical language status** in **2008** (Government of India).

nbedef231d43.s: Gidugu Ramamurthy was born on 29 August 1863 at which place?
nbedef231d43.x: Gidugu Ramamurthy was born on 29 August 1863 at Ponduru in the Srikakulam region.
nbedef231d43.tq: Use the birthplace and date together to identify the correct personality detail.
xs: Gidugu was born on **29 Aug 1863** at **Ponduru (Srikakulam)** — option **(4)**.
**Parlakimidi** is where he worked as a **Telugu teacher**; he worked mostly from **Vizianagaram**.
xa: He died on **22 Jan 1940**.
**Visakhapatnam** hosted the **1910** meeting that led to his Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Samstha.
He made a script and a **Savara-Telugu dictionary** for the Savara language (Ganjam Agency).

n957dab9b7d7.s: Which of the following was NOT one of Gidugu Ramamurthy’s contributions to Savara studies?
o: Preparing a Savara-Telugu and Telugu-Savara dictionary
n957dab9b7d7.x: Gidugu created a script, prepared bilingual dictionaries and wrote *A Manual of Savara Language*. The Andhra Sahitya Parishad was associated with the classical side of the language debate.
n957dab9b7d7.tq: Separate the individual’s documented linguistic work from an association linked to the opposing camp.
xs: **Establishing the Andhra Sahitya Parishad** was not Gidugu's — option **(3)**; through it **Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu** led the **classical** side.
Gidugu's Savara work: a **script**, a **Savara-Telugu / Telugu-Savara dictionary** and **A Manual of Savara Language**.
xa: Savara is spoken in the **Ganjam Agency**.
Other works: **A Memorandum of Modern Telugu Prose**, Bala Kavi Saranyam.
**Sri Sri** called him "**our recent inspiration**".

n981271ff3b8.s: Which of the following is a work of Gidugu Ramamurthy?
o: A Memorandum of Modern Telugu Prose
n981271ff3b8.x: A Memorandum of Modern Telugu Prose is Gidugu's work; Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini was Kokkonda's journal, Desabhakti is linked with Gurajada and Rajasekhara Charitra with Veeresalingam.
xa: Gidugu's other works: **Bala Kavi Saranyam**, **Andhra Pandita Bhishakkula Bhasha Beshajam**.
He also wrote **A Manual of Savara Language**.
His monthly: **Telugu** (**1919**).

n444be04b91d.s: In which year did Telugu receive classical language status from the Government of India?
n444be04b91d.x: Telugu was granted classical language status by the Government of India in 2008.
n444be04b91d.tq: Test the exact year using closely spaced numerical distractors.
xs: Telugu got **classical language status** in **2008** from the **Government of India** — option **(3)**.
The notes give only **2008**; the other years are distractors.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly say "Government of **Uttar Pradesh**" — a slip.
**Telugu Language Day** = **29 August**, Gidugu's birthday.
Gidugu's monthly **Telugu**: **1919**.

nfa00fa6513c.s: The principal geographical region associated with the cradle of the Telugu language movement was:
o: South Coastal Andhra, especially Nellore and Ongole
North Coastal Andhra, especially Vizianagaram, Srikakulam and Parlakimidi
nfa00fa6513c.x: The language movement had its cradle in North Coastal Andhra, particularly Vizianagaram, Srikakulam and Parlakimidi.
nfa00fa6513c.tq: Use the region-and-example pairing to avoid confusing the cultural zones of Andhra.
xs: The cradle of the language movement was **North Coastal Andhra** — **Vizianagaram**, **Srikakulam**, **Parlakimidi** — option **(2)**.
⚠ The **Rajahmundry-Kakinada** belt was the cradle of social **reform**, not of the language movement.
xa: Gidugu was born at **Ponduru (Srikakulam)** and taught at **Parlakimidi**.
Kanyasulkam uses the **Srikakulam dialect** and was staged at **Vizianagaram** (**1892**).
The Samstha's founding meeting was at **Visakhapatnam** (**1910**).

nc96c1ee7a2e.s: Which of the following did NOT reject idol worship or caste outright, unlike the Brahmo Samaj?
nc96c1ee7a2e.x: The Prarthana Samaj did not reject idol worship or caste outright, whereas the Brahmo Samaj took a categorical position against them.
xa: First Prarthana Samaj in Andhra: **Rajahmundry, 1878** (Veeresalingam).
Brahmo Samaj: **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**, **1828**, Calcutta.
Prarthana Samaj worship was held **without idols**.

nc8f7267d012.s: The principal centres of the Brahmo movement in Andhra were Rajahmundry and:
nc8f7267d012.x: Rajahmundry and Kakinada were the main Brahmo centres in Andhra, where the movement peaked during 1870–1935.
xa: **Trinity of Brahmo Samaj** in Andhra: **Veeresalingam**, **Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu**, **Desiraju Peda Bapayya**.
Samaj timeline: **Machilipatnam 1882**, **Rajahmundry 1887**, **Kakinada 1888**, **Guntur 1898**.
⚠ **1878** = **Prarthana Samaj**, Rajahmundry; **1887** = **Brahmo Samaj**, Rajahmundry.
The movement declined through splits after Venkataratnam Naidu joined the **Justice Party**.

ne5c56645d84.s: Which Telugu journal was orthodox and opposed women's education?
ne5c56645d84.x: Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevani was orthodox and opposed women's education; Vivekavardhini attacked corruption and superstition and Satyasamvardhini printed a biography of Rammohan Roy.
xa: Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini is credited with the **first editorial column**.
Satyasamvardhini was edited by **Rayasam Venkata Siva** for the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj.
⚠ APPSC G2 2025 key names **D. Rangacharyulu** as Vivekavardhini's founder; all notes credit **Veeresalingam**.

n7afebe5fc52.s: Who was the first to render classical Sanskrit drama such as Abhijnana Sakuntalam and Ratnavali into Telugu?
n7afebe5fc52.x: Through translations of Abhijnana Sakuntalam, Malavikagnimitram and Ratnavali, Veeresalingam first rendered classical Sanskrit drama into Telugu.
xa: **Rajasekhara Charitra** (**1878**) = first Telugu novel.
**Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu** ← Swift's **Gulliver's Travels**.
Titles: **Gadya Tikkana**, Gadya Vajmaya Brahma.

nd55d4ba9fe9.s: Karunalayam, established by the Pithapuram Raja, was described as:
o: The first Brahmo Samaj in Andhra
The first girls' school in Andhra
nd55d4ba9fe9.x: Karunalayam was described as the only orphanage in Andhra and also provided vocational education.
nd55d4ba9fe9.tq: Test the distinctive numerical or superlative description.
xs: **Karunalayam** (**1909**), of the **Pithapuram Raja**, was the **only orphanage in Andhra** — option **(1)**.
The first Samaj in Andhra was the **Prarthana Samaj, Rajahmundry** (**1878**); the first girls' school was at **Dowlaiswaram** (**1874**).
xa: Pithapuram Raja: **Rao Venkatakumara Mahipati Suryarao** (**1885-1964**).
He also ran **orphan and vocational schools**; gave **Rs 1 lakh** to the Brahma Dharma Prachara Nidhi.
Karunalayam at **Kakinada** was set up with **Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu**.

nce94984a84e.s: Bhandaru Acchamamba founded the Stree Samajam at Brundavanapuram, Machilipatnam in:
nce94984a84e.x: Acchamamba founded the Stree Samajam in 1902.
xa: ⚠ **1902** = both Stree Samajam (Machilipatnam) and Hindu Sundari (**Kakinada**).
Acchamamba's women's biography series: **Abala Sachcharitra Ratnamala**.
Devadasi bill: **Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy** + Chodagam Ammannaraja (**1937** → passed **1947**).

ne5a06a6bba6.s: Hindu Sundari, associated with the reform activities of Mosalikanti Ramabai and Vempati Shantabai, was published from
ne5a06a6bba6.x: Hindu Sundari was associated with Mosalikanti Ramabai and Vempati Shantabai and was published from Kakinada in 1902.
ne5a06a6bba6.tq: Test a journal-place association using nearby Andhra reform centres as distractors.
xs: **Hindu Sundari** (**1902**) was published from **Kakinada** — option **(3)**.
**Machilipatnam** was the seat of **Acchamamba's Stree Samajam** (also **1902**) — the trap.
xa: Editors: **Mosalikanti Ramabai** + **Vempati Shantabai**.
⚠ **1902** = Stree Samajam (Machilipatnam) and Hindu Sundari (Kakinada).
Kakinada also had the Samaj (**1888**) and **Karunalayam**.

nc64347ceaf0.s: The Devadasi Bill associated with Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy and Chodagam Ammannaraja was passed in
nc64347ceaf0.x: The Devadasi Bill campaign was associated with Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy and Chodagam Ammannaraja; the Bill was passed in 1947.
nc64347ceaf0.tq: Distinguish the year of the reform initiative from the year in which the legislation was passed.
xs: The **Devadasi bill** of **Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy** and **Chodagam Ammannaraja** was passed in **1947** — option **(3)**.
**1937** is the year the bill was introduced, not passed.
xa: The anti-nautch (Devadasi) movement in Madras was begun by **Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu**.
**Desiraju Peda Bapayya** led the **boycott of Bhogam melas**.
Venkataratnam Naidu's anti-Devadasi journal: **People's Friend**.

ne7c58265ea6.s: The Madras Mahajana Sabha was formed in:
ne7c58265ea6.x: The Madras Mahajana Sabha was formed in 1884; the Madras Native Association of Gajula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty dates to 1852.
xa: **Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam** (Hyderabad): **1901**, **Komarraju Lakshmana Rao**.
**Social Purity Association**: **1891**, Venkataratnam Naidu.
**Andhra Desa Library Association**: **1914**.

na0588ab503c.s: The second edition of Kanyasulkam published in 1909 was dedicated to:
na0588ab503c.x: The second edition of Kanyasulkam, published in 1909, was dedicated to Ananda Gajapati.
xs: Kanyasulkam's **2nd edition** (**1909**) was dedicated to **Ananda Gajapati** — option **(1)**.
Gurajada served the **Vizianagaram** court of Ananda Gajapati.
xa: **Saranga Dhara** (**1883**) was written with brother **Shyamala Rao**.
Kanyasulkam was first staged on **13 Aug 1892** by the **Jagannatha Vilasa Nataka Sangham**.
**1909** is also the year of **Karunalayam** (Pithapuram Raja).

n91c98e975a9.s: In Gurajada's Kanyasulkam, written in the Srikakulam dialect, which character is portrayed as a reformer?
n91c98e975a9.x: Soujanya Rao is the reformer, while Ramappa Pantulu is portrayed as a hypocrite.
xa: Other characters: **Madhuravani** (reformed courtesan), **Girisham** (educated fraud), **Buchamma** (widow), **Agnihotravadhanulu**.
Kanyasulkam: written **1890** → staged **1892** → published **1897** → 2nd edn **1909**.
It was the first **vyavaharika** play.

n2b6ba630cf8.x: Gidugu was known as Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Pitamaha and Abhinava Vaganushasanudu and received Rao Saheb and Kaisar-e-Hind; Andhra Kesari is not his title.
xa: He was also **Rao Saheb**; Kaisar-e-Hind came in **1934**.
⚠ **Rao Saheb** = Gidugu; **Rao Bahadur** = Veeresalingam (**1893**) and Venkataratnam Naidu.
**Andhra Ratna** = **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**.

n22a5fa4b860.s: The Telugu journal Janavani was associated with:
n22a5fa4b860.x: Janavani was associated with Tapi Dharma Rao; the monthly Telugu (1919) with Gidugu and the Andhra Sahitya Parishad magazine with Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu.
xa: ⚠ Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu led the **classical (granthika)** side; Gidugu and Tapi Dharma Rao backed **vyavaharika**.
**Andhra Patrika** = **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** (PYQ **2019**).
Gidugu founded the **Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Samstha** (**1910**).

nd4ba1a7c1e7.s: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy led a movement against which literary style in Telugu?
nd4ba1a7c1e7.x: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy led the movement for Vyavaharika Bhasha, opposing the Sanskritised grandhika style. He was allied with Gurajada Apparao.
nd4ba1a7c1e7.tq: Distinguish the spoken-language movement from unrelated literary and religious styles.
xs: Gidugu led the **vyavaharika** movement against the **Sanskritised grandhika** style — option **(2)**.
Granthika = Sanskritised classical Telugu with **archaic grammar**, claimed as the only "pure" literary medium.
xa: Vyavaharika = spoken Telugu (also **Gramya / Janapada bhasha**).
His ally in literature: **Gurajada Apparao**.
Outcome: the **Andhra Mahasabha** endorsed colloquial Telugu for literature, education and administration.

ne0212d4a73c.s: Along with Gurajada Apparao, who led the Vyavaharika (spoken Telugu) movement?
ne0212d4a73c.x: Gidugu and Gurajada led the Vyavaharika cause to narrow the gap between written and spoken Telugu, while orthodox pandits backed Granthika.
xa: Opponents: **Kokkonda Venkataratnam**, **Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu** (Andhra Sahitya Parishad).
Supporters: **Tapi Dharma Rao**, **Navya Sahitya Parishat**.

ne3fa50aa636.s: The classical side in the Telugu language controversy was led through which organisation by Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu?
ne3fa50aa636.x: Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu led the classical side through the Andhra Sahitya Parishad.
ne3fa50aa636.tq: Match the leader with the organisation representing his position.
xs: **Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu** led the classical side through the **Andhra Sahitya Parishad** — option **(4)**.
The **Navya Sahitya Parishat** and **Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Samstha** backed **spoken** Telugu; the **Andhra Mahasabha** finally endorsed it.
xa: **Andhra Sahitya Parishad magazine** — Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu (correct pair, APPSC **2019**).
The other orthodox opponent: **Kokkonda Venkataratnam** (Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini).
⚠ **Parishad** (classical) vs **Parishat** (Navya Sahitya, vyavaharika).

n56f546ecdc0.s: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, which inspired the widow-remarriage campaign in Andhra, was passed in which year and under which Governor-General?
n56f546ecdc0.x: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act (Act XV of 1856) came out of Vidyasagar's campaign and was passed under Lord Canning. 1829 under Bentinck is the Sati Regulation. 1872 is the Native Marriage Act. 1891 under Lansdowne is the Age of Consent Act.
xs: The **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act** (Act XV) was passed in **1856** under **Lord Canning** — option **(2)**.
It came out of **Vidyasagar**'s campaign.
**1829** is the year of the **Sati ban**, not the remarriage Act.
xa: Bengal's first remarriage: **7 Dec 1856**; Andhra's: **11 Dec 1881**.
Exam angle: the year (**1881**) and the Act (**1856**) are asked directly.
Ram Mohan Roy timeline: **Atmiya Sabha 1814**, **Brahmo Sabha 1828**, Sati ban **1829**.

n62732684cba.s: Which one of the following was NOT a method used in the social reform campaigns associated with Veeresalingam?
o: Conducting public lectures and establishing schools
Performing remarriages at his own cost and maintaining widow homes
n62732684cba.x: Veeresalingam's reform methods included journals, satire, public lectures, schools, co-education, remarriages at his own expense and widow homes. Prarthana Samaj worship was conducted without idols.
n62732684cba.tq: Reject the reversed religious practice while retaining the practical reform methods.
xs: **Promoting worship exclusively through idols** was not his method — option **(3)**; **Prarthana Samaj** worship was **without idols**.
His real methods: **journals and satire**, **public lectures**, **schools and co-education**, **remarriages at his own cost**, **widow homes**.
xa: He founded the **Prarthana Samaj, Rajahmundry** (**1878**), the first in Andhra.
⚠ Prarthana Samaj did not reject idol worship or caste outright, unlike the **Brahmo Samaj**.
He used the **press, not politics**; own printing press from **1876**.

n2c7bfaa70db.s: Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was established at Hyderabad in 1901 with the association of which group?
o: Komarraju Lakshmana Rao, Ravichettu Ranga Rao and Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao
Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu, Desiraju Peda Bapayya and Tayi Surya Prakasarao
Gajula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty, Paidah Ramakrishnayya and Atmuri Lakshmi Narasimham
Veeresalingam, Gurajada Apparao and Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy
n2c7bfaa70db.x: Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam at Hyderabad was established in 1901 with Komarraju Lakshmana Rao, Ravichettu Ranga Rao and Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao.
n2c7bfaa70db.tq: Identify the correct founding group from closely related reform-era names.
xs: The **Bhasha Nilayam** (Hyderabad, **1901**) was set up by **Komarraju Lakshmana Rao**, **Ravichettu Ranga Rao** and **Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao** — option **(1)**.
The other groups mix reformers of the Brahmo, remarriage and language movements.
xa: **Varthamana Vyavaharikandhra Bhasha Parivartaka Samaj** — **Gidugu Ramamurthy** (APPSC **2017**).
**Andhra Desa Library Association** (**1914**) — **Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah**, leader of the **Library movement**.
⚠ APPSC-GS 2024: "Kanyasulkam written by **Kommaraju Lakshmana Rao**" is **false** — it is **Gurajada**'s.

n9f8789cf81e.s: Who wrote Kanyasulkam, the satirical social play attacking bride-price and the plight of widows?
n9f8789cf81e.x: Kanyasulkam was written by Gurajada Apparao; Komarraju Lakshmana Rao founded the Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam.
xa: This was asked as an assertion-reason item in **APPSC-GS 2024**.
Kanyasulkam's 2nd edition (**1909**) was dedicated to **Ananda Gajapati**.
It was published in **1897** by **Vavilla**.

nap-history-19-12.s: The American Baptist Mission at Ongole was popularly known by which name?
nap-history-19-12.x: The American Baptist Mission at Ongole, built up by Lyman Jewett and John E. Clough, was known as the Lone Star Mission.
nap-history-19-12.tq: Recall the popular name of the Ongole mission.
n: The American Baptist Mission was known as the “Lone Star” Mission. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
The American Baptist Mission was located in Ongole. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
xs: The **American Baptist Mission** at **Ongole** was the "**Lone Star**" Mission — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was built up by **Lyman Jewett** and **John E. Clough** (**1866**).
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: American Baptist work began in **Rayalaseema** in **1835**.
Mission schools admitted **Sudras and Panchamas**.
**London Missionary Society** — **Jammalamadugu, 1805**.

nap-history-19-20.x: Mahmood Nawaz Khan Qiledar founded the MIM at Hyderabad in 1927. It was later led by Bahadur Yar Jung and Kasim Razvi.
nap-history-19-20.tq: Recall the founder of the MIM.
n: Mahmood Nawaz Khan Qiledar founded MIM. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
MIM was established in 1927. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
Bahadur Yar Jung later led MIM. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
Kasim Razvi later led MIM during the Razakar phase. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
xs: **Mahmood Nawaz Khan Qiledar** founded the **MIM** (**Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen**) in **1927** at **Hyderabad** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was later led by **Bahadur Yar Jung**, and by **Kasim Razvi** in the **Razakar phase**.
xa: **Comrades Association** — **1940**, **Hyderabad**.
**Socialist Party Andhra Branch** — **1934**.
**Jatiya Andhra Mahasabha** — **Ravi Narayana Reddy**.

nap-history-15-3.s: Desha Matha, which strongly supported the Home Rule Movement, was edited by:
nap-history-15-3.x: Desha Matha was edited by Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham and backed the Home Rule Movement.
n: Desha Matha was edited by Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Desha Matha strongly supported the Home Rule Movement. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
xa: Other Home Rule-era supporters: **Andhra Patrika** and **Krishna Patrika**.
Chilakamarti also founded the **Ram Mohan Roy School** (**1909**) for backward-class children.
**Andhra Patrika** — **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.

nap-history-15-24.s: Which of the following publications was an Urdu daily?
nap-history-15-24.x: Rayyat was an Urdu daily edited by M. Narasinga Rao from 1927. Hasyavardhani and Nilagiri were Telugu journals, and Desha Matha was a Telugu newspaper.
nap-history-15-24.tq: Recall the language and format of each publication.
n: Prakasika is a magazine. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
xs: **Rayyat** was an **Urdu daily newspaper** (**1927**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was edited by **M. Narasinga Rao**.
**Hasyavardhani** (**Kokkonda Venkata Ratnam**), **Nilagiri** (**Nalgonda**) and **Desha Matha** were Telugu publications.
xa: **Nilagiri** — **Shabnavis Venkata Rama Narasimha Rao**.
**Desha Matha** — **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham**.
**Desabhimani** — need for a separate government for **Telugu culture**.

ne7cd8d813cc.s: ‘Desamante matti kadoyi, desamante manushuloyi’ conveys the idea that:
o: A country is determined by its religious institutions.
A country is its people, not merely its soil.
A country is defined exclusively by its territory.
A country is identified primarily with its rulers.
ne7cd8d813cc.x: Gurajada's line means that a country is its people, not merely its soil. ⚠ Sources differ on the poem it comes from: Desamunu Preminchumanna / Desabhakti in most notes, while the APPSC 2025 key says Kanyaka.
ne7cd8d813cc.tq: Interpret the central idea of the quoted line rather than relying only on author recall.
xs: "**Desamante matti kadoyi, desamante manushuloyi**" means a country is **its people, not merely its soil** — option **(2)**.
It is **Gurajada**'s line.
xa: ⚠ Source differs: patriotic song **"Desamunu Preminchumanna"** / poem Desabhakti; APPSC **2025** key says **Kanyaka**.
Gurajada's **Mutyala Saralu** introduced a new lyrical metre.
⚠ **Purnamma** (girl married off for money) vs **Kanyaka** — both Gurajada poems.

n20d6f7f0344.s: Which work is the standard answer for the first Telugu novel?
n20d6f7f0344.x: Veeresalingam's Rajasekhara Charitram is the standard answer, though some scholars propose Kokkonda Venkataratnam's Mahasweta.
xa: Rajasekhara Charitram: **Kandukuri Veeresalingam**, **1878**.
Kokkonda was the first Andhra **Mahamahopadhyaya** (**1907**) — "**Andhra Bhasha Johnson**".
First Telugu **social drama**: **Nandaka Rajyam** (Vavilala Vasudeva Sastri).

n9aea3024785.s: Kokkonda Venkataratnam became the first Andhra scholar to receive the title Mahamahopadhyaya in:
n9aea3024785.x: Kokkonda Venkataratnam received the distinction of Mahamahopadhyaya in 1907. He was also known as the Andhra Bhasha Johnson.
n9aea3024785.tq: Use the exact year to distinguish a scholarly honour from institutional founding dates.
xs: **Kokkonda Venkataratnam** became the first Andhra **Mahamahopadhyaya** in **1907** — option **(4)**.
He was called the "**Andhra Bhasha Johnson**".
**1878** is the first Telugu novel and the **Vernacular Press Act**.
xa: He presided over the **Andhra Sahitya Parishat** sessions at Rajahmundry (**23 Apr 1912**, **22 Apr 1913**).
Some scholars call his **Mahasweta** the first Telugu novel.
Veeresalingam's **Vivekavardhini** (from **1874**) attacked Kokkonda's **Sanjeevani**.

n22ca8405279.s: The phrase “Italian of the East” in relation to Telugu was first used by:
n22ca8405279.x: The phrase 'Italian of the East' was first used by Nicolo de Conti; C.P. Brown later applied it to Telugu, which is why Brown is the trap.
n22ca8405279.tq: Separate the originator of a famous phrase from the scholar who popularised Telugu studies.
xs: "**Italian of the East**" was first used by **Nicolo de Conti** — option **(2)**.
**C.P. Brown** later called Telugu the "Italian of the East" — the trap.
xa: Brown was **Collector of Cuddapah** and Honorary Professor of Telugu, **London University**.
**C.P. Brown Memorial Trust Library** = **Kadapa**.
Brown edited **Nannaya, Tikkana, Pothana** and other poets.

n143f4895c74.s: Who first rendered Kalidasa's Shakuntalam and Malavikagnimitram into Telugu?
n143f4895c74.x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam was the first to render Kalidasa's Shakuntalam and Malavikagnimitram into Telugu.
xa: He is the "**Father of the Telugu Renaissance**".
His **Vivekavardhini** began in **1874**.
First Telugu novel: **Rajasekhara Charitram** (**1878**).

ne2600b834d1.s: Which city, Veeresalingam's reform base, has been a cultural capital since Eastern Chalukya times?
ne2600b834d1.x: Rajahmundry was Veeresalingam's reform base and has been regarded as a cultural capital since the Eastern Chalukya period.
xa: Parishat sessions at Rajahmundry: **23 Apr 1912** and **22 Apr 1913**.
**Young Men's Association, Rajahmundry**: Bipin Chandra Pal's visit.
**Vivekavardhini** (from **1874**) was Veeresalingam's journal.

n1c945ee29da.s: Who prepared the systematic Telugu grammar published in 1816?
n1c945ee29da.x: A.D. Campbell prepared the systematic Telugu grammar in 1816.
n1c945ee29da.tq: Match the specific work with its author rather than with another colonial Telugu scholar.
xs: **A.D. Campbell** wrote the **first systematic Telugu Grammar** (**1816**) with a Telugu-English dictionary — option **(4)**.
**Schultze** wrote an earlier Telugu grammar; **C.P. Brown**'s Grammar came in **1840**.
**William Carey** produced the **complete Telugu Bible** at Serampore.
xa: ⚠ First grammar: Schultze (early) vs **Campbell** (first systematic, **1816**).
Brown's dictionaries: **1853**.
Campbell's works were tools for **missionaries and Telugu scholars**.

n767c0e298bf.s: C.P. Brown compiled his Telugu-English and English-Telugu dictionaries in:
n767c0e298bf.x: Brown, Collector of Cuddapah, compiled the dictionaries in 1853 and edited Nannaya, Tikkana and Pothana; 1815 is when Colin Mackenzie became Surveyor General.
xa: Brown collected about **2,000 Vemana** poems; called Telugu the **"Italian of the East"**.
**C.P. Brown Memorial Trust Library** is at **Kadapa**.
⚠ Brown's Grammar **1840**; **A.D. Campbell**'s first systematic grammar **1816**.

n7b7f81c5863.s: Who helped Colin Mackenzie collect the Kaifiyats?
n7b7f81c5863.x: The Kavali brothers (Borraiah, Venkataramaiah, Lakshmaiah) helped Mackenzie, who became the first Surveyor General in 1815.
xa: ⚠ **1797** was his first visit; the stupa marbles reached London decades later.
**C.P. Brown** preserved the Kaifiyats in the **Madras Library**.
**William Carey** of the **Serampore Mission** produced the complete Telugu Bible.

n2f0c382031b.s: Benjamin Schultze's four Telugu books were printed in 1747 at:
n2f0c382031b.x: Schultze, of the Danish-Halle Mission, had his Telugu books printed at Halle in 1747; William Carey's Telugu Bible came from Serampore (1812-19).
xa: Schultze came in **1719** and returned in **1743**.
Carey also made **Telugu typefaces**.
**A.D. Campbell** wrote the first systematic Telugu Grammar (**1816**).

n86fdf7caebd.s: Which colonial scholar kept Telugu as an administrative language?
n86fdf7caebd.x: Thomas Munro kept Telugu as an administrative language.
n86fdf7caebd.tq: Match the administrative policy with the appropriate colonial official.
xs: **Thomas Munro** kept Telugu as an **administrative language** — option **(4)**.
**C.P. Brown** made dictionaries; **Mackenzie** collected Kaifiyats; **A.D. Campbell** wrote the 1816 grammar.
xa: Campbell's grammar (**1816**) was the first systematic one.
Brown's dictionaries: **1853**.
Mackenzie: first **Surveyor General** (**1815**).

na46ddf15e76.s: Telugu Language Day, observed on 29 August, marks the birth anniversary of:
na46ddf15e76.x: Telugu Language Day on 29 August marks Gidugu's birth anniversary and is associated with Telugu Language Awards.
xa: Telugu: **Classical Language** in **2008**.
AP re-introduced **Vemana Suktulu** lessons in schools (Mar **2026**).
A **Telugu Bhavan** is planned in **Mumbai** (Jun **2026**).

ndb37d99712c.s: The last ruler of the Ikshvaku dynasty of Andhra was:
ndb37d99712c.x: The 2019 key names Rudra Purushadatta as the last Ikshvaku ruler. Vasishthiputra Chamtamula founded the line. Virapurushadatta and Ehuvala Chamtamula were earlier rulers who came before him.
xs: The APPSC G2 **2019** key names **Rudra Purushadatta** as the **last Ikshvaku ruler** — option **(4)**.
The notes name no other Ikshvaku ruler, so the other options are distractors.
xa: The same key gives **Penugonda** as the main kshetra of Goddess **Vasavi**.
Telugu: **Classical Language** status **2008**.
