nf8914f381ce.s: Who led the confederacy of the post-Kakatiya liberation movement?
nf8914f381ce.x: Prolaya Nayaka led the post-Kakatiya liberation confederacy.
xa: **Kandukuri Veeresalingam** — father of the **Telugu Renaissance Movement**.
**Konda Venkatappaiah** — father of the **Andhra State Movement**.
**Sidugu Rama Murthy** — father of the **People's Dialect Movement**.

n63c0c8520bb.s: The Adams Regulation of 1823, the Vernacular Press Act of 1878, and the Press Acts of 1908 and 1910 are associated with which aspect of colonial rule?
o: Regulation and curbs on the press
n63c0c8520bb.x: These measures were press regulations or Press Acts used to impose curbs on the press during colonial rule.
n63c0c8520bb.tq: Identify the common administrative purpose linking a sequence of laws.
xs: These were **curbs on the press** — option **(1)**.
**Adams Regulation 1823**, **Vernacular Press Act 1878**, Press Acts **1908** and **1910**.
xa: Early presses: **Bellary** (Satyaduta **1835**), **Madras** (Vrittanti, Dinavartamani), **Masulipatnam** (Hitavadi **1848**).
Veeresalingam used the press for reform from **1874** (Vivekavardhini).

n3966b1ff3cd.s: The author of Asamardhuni Jeevayatra is:
n3966b1ff3cd.x: Asamardhuni Jeevayatra was written by Tripuraneni Gopichand.
n3966b1ff3cd.tq: Directly match a modern Telugu work with its author.
xs: **Asamardhuni Jeevayatra** is by **Tripuraneni Gopichand** — option **(2)** (APPSC G2 **2017** key).
**Gurajada** wrote **Musalamma Maranamu**; **Gurram Jashuva** wrote **Gabbilam**; **Viswanatha Satyanarayana** wrote **Veyi Padagalu**.
xa: Gabbilam (**1941**): a bat carries a Dalit's prayer to God.
⚠ **Tripuraneni Gopichand** (novelist) — don't confuse with Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary.

n1069a168705.s: Jonnavittula Gurunatham was associated with the:
n1069a168705.x: Jonnavittula Gurunatham belonged to the Young Men’s Literary Association and helped promote the Andhra idea through the press.
n1069a168705.tq: Distinguish the literary association from similarly named cultural institutions.
xs: **Jonnavittula Gurunatham** belonged to the **Young Men's Literary Association** — option **(3)**.
He helped **sow the Andhra idea in the press**.
xa: The **Young Men's Association, Rajahmundry**, was active in **Bipin Chandra Pal**'s Rajahmundry visit.
**Brown's College** members: Pattam Parabrahma Sastri, Ravipati Gurumurti Sastri, Juluri Appayya.
**Andhra Sahitya Parishat**: Madras, **1911**.

nd580da5246b.s: The 1912 and 1913 Rajahmundry sessions of the Andhra Sahitya Parishat were presided over by:
nd580da5246b.x: Kokkonda Venkataratnam presided over the Rajahmundry sessions; the Parishat was founded at Madras in 1911 and later based at Kakinada.
xa: Kokkonda was the first Andhra scholar made **Mahamahopadhyaya (1907)** — "**Andhra Bhasha Johnson**".
The **Young Men's Association, Rajahmundry** was active in **Bipin Chandra Pal's** visit.
Rajahmundry has been a cultural capital since **Eastern Chalukya** days.

n6e46a3067f9.s: The Young Men's Association of Rajahmundry played an active role in which event?
o: The first widow remarriage in Andhra
Bipin Chandra Pal's visit to Rajahmundry
The founding of the Andhra Sahitya Parishat
n6e46a3067f9.x: The Young Men's Association, Rajahmundry, played an active role in Bipin Chandra Pal's Rajahmundry visit (APPSC G2 2017 key). The first widow remarriage (1881) and Vivekavardhini (1874) were Veeresalingam's work. The Andhra Sahitya Parishat was founded at Madras in 1911.
n6e46a3067f9.tq: Rajahmundry Young Men's Association: Bipin Chandra Pal.
xs: The **Young Men's Association, Rajahmundry**, was active in **Bipin Chandra Pal's** Rajahmundry visit — option **(2)** (APPSC G2 **2017** key).
**Vivekavardhini** (**1874**) was Veeresalingam's; the **Andhra Sahitya Parishat** was founded at **Madras** (**1911**).
xa: **Jonnavittula Gurunatham** of the Young Men's Literary Association sowed the Andhra idea in the press.
Rajahmundry: cultural capital since **Eastern Chalukya** days.
Parishat sessions at Rajahmundry: **1912-13**.

n97bca88cd7f.s: The C.P. Brown Memorial Trust Library is located at:
n97bca88cd7f.x: The C.P. Brown Memorial Trust Library is at Kadapa (Cuddapah), where Brown served as Collector (APPSC G2 2001 and 2005 keys). Rajahmundry was Veeresalingam's reform base. Machilipatnam and Bellary were missionary and press centres.
n97bca88cd7f.tq: Brown = Collector of Cuddapah; library at Kadapa.
xs: The **C.P. Brown Memorial Trust Library** is at **Kadapa** — option **(1)** (APPSC G2 **2001**, **2005** keys).
Brown was **Collector of Cuddapah** (Kadapa).
**Rajahmundry** was Veeresalingam's base; **Machilipatnam** and **Bellary** were press centres.
xa: Brown (**1798-1884**) learnt Telugu from **Kodandarama Pantulu**.
Dictionaries **1853**; Grammar **1840**.
He called Telugu the "**Italian of the East**".

na785d4ea8c2.s: During the early period of missionary activity, the major contribution to education in Andhra was made by:
na785d4ea8c2.x: Christian missionaries made the major contribution; the Adams Regulation and the Press Acts related to press control.
xa: **Benjamin Schultze** (Danish-Halle Mission) printed the first Telugu books.
**William Carey** (Serampore) gave the complete Telugu Bible and Telugu typefaces.
**A.D. Campbell**'s 1816 grammar served missionaries and Telugu scholars.

n578de7876bc.s: Which was the first Telugu magazine published from Bellary, among the following?
n578de7876bc.x: The 2011 key names Tatvabodhini (1864-70) as the first Telugu magazine from Bellary, although Satyaduta (1835) is also called the first Telugu journal. Hitavadi (1848) was from Masulipatnam. Vrittanti and Dinavartamani were Madras papers.
n578de7876bc.tq: Bellary question in the APPSC key: Tatvabodhini.
xs: The APPSC G2 **2011** key names **Tatvabodhini** (1864-70) the first Telugu magazine from **Bellary** — option **(3)**.
**Hitavadi** (**1848**) was from **Masulipatnam**; **Vrittanti** and **Dinavartamani** were **Madras** papers.
xa: ⚠ Notes call **Satyaduta** (**1835**, Bellary) the first Telugu journal — answer the Bellary question with **Tatvabodhini**, as the key does.
Second Telugu journal: **Vartamana Tarangini** (**1842**).
Hitavadi was run by **J. Edmund Sharky**.
n578de7876bc.fixed: stem cited 'APPSC Group 2 (2011) key' instead of the fact

ne7bb8cbdf3b.s: Under the Sati Regulation (Regulation XVII of 1829) of William Bentinck, participation in sati was treated as:
o: A minor offence punishable by fine
ne7bb8cbdf3b.x: The Regulation made sati illegal and treated participation in it as culpable homicide.
xa: It followed the campaign of **Raja Rammohan Roy**.
Other Bentinck-era steps: **thuggee** suppressed by **Colonel William Sleeman** (**1830s**); **English Education Act, 1835** (Macaulay's Minute).
Exam angle: "Sati was abolished by" → **Bentinck**.

ncbb3fbc0485.s: Bengal Regulations XXI of 1795 and III of 1804 declared ____ to be murder.
ncbb3fbc0485.x: These Regulations declared infanticide, including female infanticide, to be murder.
xa: **Anti-Infanticide Act, 1802** (**Wellesley**): ban on child sacrifice at **Sagar Island**.
**Female Infanticide Prevention Act, 1870** under **Mayo**.
⚠ Some notes wrongly say **1856** under Dalhousie for the infanticide Act.

nccf08d5a07a.s: The Female Infanticide Prevention Act was enacted in:
nccf08d5a07a.x: The Female Infanticide Prevention Act was enacted in 1870. The 1802 reference concerns the ban on child sacrifice at Sagar Island under Wellesley, not this Act.
nccf08d5a07a.tq: Separate the exact Act year from nearby regulations and the Sagar Island measure.
xs: The **Female Infanticide Prevention Act** came in **1870**, under **Mayo** — option **(4)**.
**1795** = Bengal Regulation XXI; **1802** = Sagar Island ban (**Wellesley**).
⚠ **1856** under **Dalhousie**, given in some notes, is wrong.
xa: It curbed the **killing of female infants**.
**1856** is the **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act**.
Regulations **1795** and **1804** had declared infanticide murder.

n3deb5a2acb6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Lex Loci Act (Caste Disabilities Removal Act), 1850?
o: It was passed under Lord Dalhousie
It barred converts from inheriting ancestral property
Orthodox Hindus saw it as an incentive to conversion
It became one of the grievances behind 1857
n3deb5a2acb6.x: The Act did the opposite: it let a Hindu who converted still inherit ancestral property.
xa: Also called the **Caste Disabilities Removal Act** and **Religious Disabilities Act**.
⚠ It did **not** deal with sati, widows or child marriage.
The **Widow Remarriage Act** was also drafted under Dalhousie.

nf695eb266eb.s: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act was enacted in July 1856 under:
nf695eb266eb.x: The bill was prepared under Dalhousie, but the Act was enacted in July 1856 under Canning; it legalised widow remarriage and legitimised the children.
xa: It was **Act XV of 1856**, from **Vidyasagar**'s campaign.
It also **legitimised children** of such marriages.
⚠ Some tables list it under Dalhousie — read the options carefully.

n3f241ad56b2.s: Besides child marriage, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar campaigned against:
n3f241ad56b2.x: Vidyasagar campaigned against child marriage and polygamy; his work was not confined to widow remarriage.
xa: His petitions led to the **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act (Act XV of 1856)**.
He performed Bengal's **first widow remarriage** on **7 Dec 1856**.
He sent support for **Veeresalingam**'s third remarriage.

n987565b1e98.s: The Native (Civil) Marriage Act of 1872 was chiefly associated with the campaign of:
n987565b1e98.x: The Native or Brahmo Marriage Act of 1872 was a product of Keshab Chandra Sen’s campaign. It also barred polygamy and permitted inter-caste marriage.
n987565b1e98.tq: Match the reform legislation with the reformer who campaigned for it.
xs: The **Native (Civil) Marriage Act, 1872** came at **Keshab Chandra Sen**'s urging, for **Brahmo marriages** — option **(3)**.
**Rammohan Roy** = sati campaign (**1829**); **Har Bilas Sarda** = **1929** Act; **Vidyasagar** = **1856** Act.
xa: It set **14 for girls, 18 for boys** (APPSC-GS **2025**), allowed **inter-caste** marriage, barred **polygamy**.
Also called the "**Brahmo Marriage Act**".
⚠ Keshab broke it in **1878** by marrying his minor daughter to the **Cooch Behar** prince.

nf4e5a0b06e7.s: The Brahmo Samaj split in 1878 because Keshab Chandra Sen:
o: opposed the Native Marriage Act of 1872
married his minor daughter to the prince of Cooch Behar, breaking the 1872 Act
joined the Prarthana Samaj at Bombay
supported Tilak's opposition to the Age of Consent Bill
nf4e5a0b06e7.x: Keshab broke the Native Marriage Act he had himself campaigned for by marrying his minor daughter to the Cooch Behar prince, and this split the Samaj in 1878. He did not oppose the 1872 Act; it came from his own campaign. He did not join the Prarthana Samaj. The Age of Consent debate came in 1891.
xs: The **1878** Brahmo split came when Keshab **married his minor daughter to the Cooch Behar prince**, breaking the **1872** Act — option **(2)**.
He did not oppose the 1872 Act — it came from his own campaign.
The **Age of Consent** debate (Tilak) came in **1891**.
xa: The 1872 Act set **14 (girls)** / **18 (boys)**.
It allowed **inter-caste** marriage and barred **polygamy**.

nf139709da7c.s: Kandukuri Rajyalakshmamma, the wife of Veeresalingam, is particularly associated with:
o: Sheltering widows and destitute women and hosting widow and inter-caste marriages
Establishing the Mukti Mission at Kedgaon
nf139709da7c.x: Kandukuri Rajyalakshmamma hosted widow remarriages and inter-caste marriages at her home, which also became a shelter for widows and destitute women.
nf139709da7c.tq: Identify the reformer's distinctive social role rather than assigning her another reformer's institution.
xs: **Kandukuri Rajyalakshmamma** hosted **widow remarriages and inter-caste marriages** at her home and **sheltered widows and destitute women** — option **(1)**.
The **Indian Women's University** was **D.K. Karve**'s; **Stri Purush Tulana** is **Tarabai Shinde**'s; the **Mukti Mission** (Kedgaon) is **Pandita Ramabai**'s.
xa: She married Veeresalingam in **1860**.
Andhra's first widow remarriage: **11 Dec 1881**, Rajahmundry.
Veeresalingam's widow homes: **Madras** (**1897**) and **Rajahmundry** (**1905**).

nfaf1cf8b0e6.s: Who moved the Child Marriage Restraint Bill that became the Sarda Act?
nfaf1cf8b0e6.x: The Sarda Act was moved by Har Bilas Sarda during the period of Lord Irwin.
nfaf1cf8b0e6.tq: Match the legislation with its mover, not with another contemporary reform advocate.
xs: The **Sarda Act** was moved by **Har Bilas Sarda**, under **Irwin** — option **(4)**.
**Keshab Chandra Sen** = **1872** Act; **Behramji Malabari** = **1891** Act; **D.K. Karve** = widows' home and women's university.
xa: Passed **1929**; in force from **1 April 1930**.
Minimum age: **girls 14, boys 18**.
Amended **1978**: **18 (girls) / 21 (boys)**.

nfd6dc48c759.s: The Caste Disabilities Removal Act of 1850 is also known as the:
nfd6dc48c759.x: The Lex Loci Act protected a convert's right to inherit ancestral property; sati was dealt with by the 1829 Regulation.
xa: Also called the **Religious Disabilities Act**; passed under **Dalhousie**.
It became a grievance behind **1857**.

n82dbcc41e3c.s: The Native Marriage Act of 1872 fixed the minimum marriage age for girls at:
n82dbcc41e3c.x: The Act fixed 14 for girls and 18 for boys, allowed inter-caste marriage and barred polygamy.
xa: It was **Act III of 1872**, a product of **Keshab Chandra Sen**'s campaign.
Some notes list it as "Brahma Act (**Anti-Child Marriage Act**)".
⚠ **1891** Act = age of **consent 12**, not a marriage age.

n4901226d841.s: The Age of Consent Act, 1891, enacted under Lord Lansdowne, raised the age of consent for girls from 10 to:
n4901226d841.x: The 1891 Act raised the age of consent from 10 to 12 and regulated consummation rather than the age of marriage.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say it "prohibited marriage below 12" — loosely worded.
**Tilak** opposed it in **Kesari**; the **Moderates** supported it.
Campaigner: **Behramji Malabari**.

nafd4aad85ef.s: In 1925 the age of consent in India was raised to:
nafd4aad85ef.x: The age of consent went from 10 to 12 in 1891, to 14 in 1925, to 16 in 1949 and to 18 in 2012 under POCSO.
xa: ⚠ Age of consent (**18**, POCSO/BNS) ≠ minimum marriage age (**18/21**, **PCMA 2006**).
The **1925** step was an IPC amendment.

n1b5e2fd0ed5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the legal age of marriage in India?
o: The 2021 proposal to raise women's age to 21 had become law by January 2026
The 1978 amendment raised it to 18 for girls and 21 for boys
The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 prescribes 18 for women and 21 for men
In January 2026 the legal age for women remained 18
n1b5e2fd0ed5.x: The 2021 Cabinet proposal had not become law by January 2026, when the legal age for women remained 18.
xa: The original **Sarda Act (1929)** set **14 / 18**.
⚠ Age of consent (**18**, POCSO/BNS) ≠ marriage age (**18/21**, PCMA 2006).

n511c5317cee.s: The Child Marriage Restraint Act (Sarda Act), 1929, passed under Lord Irwin, fixed the minimum marriage age at:
n511c5317cee.x: The Sarda Act fixed 14 for girls and 18 for boys, the same ages as the 1872 Native Marriage Act. 12 was the age of consent set in 1891, not a marriage age. 18 and 21 came only with the 1978 amendment and are now in the PCMA 2006. 16 and 18 is not a pair any of these Acts used.
xs: The **Sarda Act, 1929** set **14 for girls and 18 for boys** — option **(2)**.
**12** was the **1891** age of **consent**, not a marriage age.
**18 and 21** came with the **1978** amendment and the **PCMA 2006**.
xa: ⚠ **14/18** = both the **1872** Act and the **1929** Sarda Act.
In force from **1 April 1930**.
The **AIWC** pressed for the Sarda Act.

n96e4dcb5ad4.s: Under POCSO/BNS, the age of consent in India is:
n96e4dcb5ad4.x: The age of consent is 18 under POCSO/BNS, while the PCMA 2006 fixes the minimum marriage age at 18 for women and 21 for men.
n96e4dcb5ad4.fixed: options 1 and 3 both stated the correct position; made option 3 false

nb2925fbc27c.s: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar's Barnaparichay was a:
nb2925fbc27c.x: Barnaparichay was a Bengali alphabet primer written by Vidyasagar.
xa: Vidyasagar **modernised Bengali prose**.
He founded the **Metropolitan Institution**.
Title "**Vidyasagar**" = Ocean of Learning.

ne8aaebf3632.s: The Bethune School was established with the support of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar and:
ne8aaebf3632.x: Vidyasagar helped J.E.D. Bethune establish the Bethune School in 1849, one of the earliest girls’ schools in India.
ne8aaebf3632.tq: Use the founder–institution association and distinguish it from later women’s education figures.
xs: Vidyasagar helped **J.E.D. Bethune** set up the **Bethune School** (**1849**) — option **(2)**; one of India's earliest girls' schools.
**D.K. Karve** founded the Indian Women's University; **Meherbai Tata** and **Cornelia Sorabji** the National Council of Women (**1925**).
xa: Vidyasagar opened many **girls' schools** in Bengal.
Savitribai Phule taught at the first girls' school in **Pune** (**1848**).
Vidyasagar opposed **child marriage and polygamy**.

n6085daae029.s: The first widow remarriage in Bengal is associated with which date?
n6085daae029.x: Vidyasagar performed the first widow remarriage in Bengal on 7 December 1856. 11 December 1881 is the date of Andhra's first widow remarriage at Rajahmundry, so the options mix the two events' dates.
n6085daae029.tq: Separate closely related regional dates by matching each date with its correct region.
xs: Bengal's first lawful widow remarriage was on **7 December 1856** — option **(3)**, performed by **Vidyasagar**.
**11 Dec 1881** is **Andhra**'s first, at **Rajahmundry** — the options mix the two.
xa: Andhra couple: **Gogulapati Sriramulu** and **Seethamma**/Gauramma.
The **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act** was enacted in **July 1856**.
**M.G. Ranade** called Veeresalingam the "**South Indian Vidyasagar**".

nd66f57ca9e8.s: Who advocated the enactment of the Age of Consent Act of 1891?
nd66f57ca9e8.x: Behramji Malabari, a Parsi reformer from Bombay, advocated the Age of Consent law. The Act was enacted during Lord Lansdowne’s tenure.
nd66f57ca9e8.tq: Use the reformer–Act association rather than the Governor-General association.
xs: **Behramji Malabari** (Parsi reformer) campaigned for the **Age of Consent Act 1891** — option **(1)**.
**Vishnu Shastri Pandit** led the widow-remarriage campaign in **Maharashtra**; **Ramabai Ranade** co-founded the **Poona Seva Sadan**.
xa: Malabari wrote **Notes on Infant Marriage and Enforced Widowhood** (**1884**).
He edited the **Indian Spectator**.
The Act came under **Lansdowne**.

n78fc3cb0ce8.s: Which journal was edited by Behramji Malabari?
n78fc3cb0ce8.x: Behramji Malabari edited the Indian Spectator. Kesari was associated with Tilak, while the other titles are not the journal identified here as his.
n78fc3cb0ce8.tq: Apply the editor–journal association and avoid substituting a journal linked with another reformer.
xs: **Behramji Malabari** edited the **Indian Spectator** — option **(1)**.
**Kesari** was **Tilak**'s; **Sati Hita Bodhini** (**1883**) was **Veeresalingam**'s women's journal.
xa: Malabari's book: **Notes on Infant Marriage and Enforced Widowhood** (**1884**).
His campaign led to the **Age of Consent Act 1891**.
⚠ The APPSC key pairs **Seva Sadan — Malabari**.
n78fc3cb0ce8.fixed: Malabari also edited Voice of India (y29b6f003da5/yb1a588c8d65), so two options were correct

o: A husband's suit for restitution of conjugal rights
n8816f2e7ade.x: Rakhmabai's husband Dadaji sued for restitution of conjugal rights after their child marriage, raising questions of consent and conjugal rights.
xa: Rakhmabai refused to live with the husband she was married to as a child.
She later became one of India's first practising **women doctors**.
The **Phulmoni Dasi** case (**1889-90**) pushed the **1891** Act through.

n820898c3063.s: Who among the following opposed the Age of Consent Bill on the ground that it represented foreign interference in Hindu custom?
n820898c3063.x: Bal Gangadhar Tilak opposed the Bill, including through Kesari, on the ground that it was foreign interference in Hindu custom. The Moderates supported the Bill.
n820898c3063.tq: Use the reformer–position contrast, particularly the opposition of Tilak versus the support of the Moderates.
xs: **B.G. Tilak** opposed the Bill in **Kesari** as **foreign interference in Hindu custom** — option **(1)**.
**Behramji Malabari** campaigned **for** it; the **Moderates** supported it.
xa: The Act raised the age of consent to **12** (**1891**, Lansdowne).
The **Phulmoni Dasi** case (**1889-90**) pushed it through.
The **Rakhmabai** case (**1884-88**) sparked the debate.

n9b72f66f7c6.s: The death of which child bride after forced cohabitation by her adult husband helped push the Age of Consent Act of 1891 through?
n9b72f66f7c6.x: Phulmoni Dasi, a child bride of about 10-11, died after forced cohabitation (1889-90), and her case pushed the 1891 Act through. Rakhmabai refused to live with her husband in the restitution-of-conjugal-rights case. Anandibai Joshi was the first Indian woman with a degree in Western medicine, and Tarabai Shinde wrote Stri Purush Tulana.
xs: **Phulmoni Dasi** (**1889-90**), a child bride of about **10-11**, died after forced cohabitation — option **(3)**; this pushed the **1891** Act through.
**Rakhmabai** refused to live with her husband (restitution of conjugal rights case).
**Anandibai Joshi** = first Indian woman with a Western medical degree; **Tarabai Shinde** wrote **Stri Purush Tulana**.
xa: The Act raised the age of consent from **10 to 12**.
It was passed under **Lansdowne**.

n7531d80bb59.s: Act V of 1843, which made slavery illegal in British India, was passed under:
n7531d80bb59.x: The Charter Act of 1833 directed abolition, Act V of 1843 under Ellenborough made slavery illegal, and the IPC of 1860 made the slave trade an offence.
xa: The IPC of **1860** also set the age of consent at **10**.
Exam angle: **Act-year-Governor-General** matching.

na3857d7a6e6.s: Jyotiba and Savitribai Phule opened a girls' school at Pune in:
na3857d7a6e6.x: The Phules opened the Pune girls' school in 1848 and a home for upper-caste widows in 1854; Savitribai is regarded as India's first woman teacher.
xa: ⚠ Some notes date the first girls' school to **1851**.
Savitribai (**1831-1897**) was born at **Naigaon, Satara**.
Also a **Home for the Prevention of Infanticide** (**1863**).

n484a4a6d985.s: Pandita Ramabai founded the Arya Mahila Samaj at Poona in:
n484a4a6d985.x: The Arya Mahila Samaj was founded in 1882; Sarada Niketan in Guntur (1922) was founded by Unnava Lakshminarayana with his wife Lakshmibayamma.
xa: Ramabai's **Sharada Sadan** (Bombay **1889**, later Poona) was a home for widows.
⚠ **Sharada Sadan** (Ramabai) vs **Sarada Niketan** (Unnava, Guntur).
Lakshmibayamma's widow asylum at **Guntur** (**1902**) later merged into Sarada Niketan.

nc784b9bff43.s: Who founded the Social Service League at Bombay in 1911?
nc784b9bff43.x: N.M. Joshi founded the Social Service League; Kunzru founded the Seva Samiti (Allahabad, 1914) and Pandita Ramabai the Sharada Sadan (1889).
xa: ⚠ The APPSC-G2 **2023** key paired **Deva Samaj — Radhakant Deb**; standard texts say **Agnihotri**.
**Poona Seva Sadan** (**1909**): **Ramabai Ranade** and **G.K. Devadhar**.
**Sarada Niketan** (Guntur, **1922**): **Unnava Lakshminarayana** with Lakshmibayamma.

nindian-history-14-35.s: D.K. Karve's Home for Widows at Hingne near Poona was established in:
nindian-history-14-35.x: Karve set up his Home for Widows near Poona in 1896; in 1916 he founded the first Women's University, now SNDT University, Bombay.
n: The First Women's University was associated with D.K. Karve. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
The First Women's University was located in Bombay. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
D.K. Karve established the Home for Widow. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
The Home for Widow was located in Poona. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
The Home for Widow was established in 1896. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 60-64]
xa: Karve's **Indian Women's University** dates from **1916**; he got the **Bharat Ratna** in **1958**.
He also founded the **Widow Marriage Association (1893)**.
**Pandita Ramabai**'s **Sharada Sadan (1889, Bombay)** — a **home for widows**.

n7617e40af36.s: Poona Seva Sadan was founded by:
o: Shiv Narayan Agnihotri and Hriday Nath Kunzru
n7617e40af36.x: Poona Seva Sadan was founded by Ramabai Ranade and G.K. Devadhar in 1909.
n7617e40af36.tq: Discriminate between institutions with the common name ‘Seva Sadan’.
xs: **Poona Seva Sadan** (**1909**) was founded by **Ramabai Ranade** and **G.K. Devadhar** — option **(2)**.
**Hriday Nath Kunzru** founded the **Seva Samiti**; **Unnava Lakshminarayana** and Lakshmibayamma founded **Sarada Niketan**.
xa: Seva Sadan cared for exploited and abandoned women **across castes** — education, medical help, welfare.
Ramabai Ranade also led the **Ladies' Social Conference** (**1904**, Bombay).
⚠ The APPSC-G2 **2023** key pairs **Seva Sadan — Malabari**.

n0ac45031dfd.s: The Ladies’ Social Conference, also known as Bharat Mahila Parishad, was associated with:
n0ac45031dfd.x: The Ladies’ Social Conference, also called Bharat Mahila Parishad, was associated with Ramabai Ranade in Bombay in 1904 and functioned under the National Social Conference.
n0ac45031dfd.tq: Use the full organisation name, founder and location to avoid confusing similarly themed bodies.
xs: The **Ladies' Social Conference** (Bharat Mahila Parishad) was **Ramabai Ranade**'s, **Bombay**, **1904** — option **(1)**.
It worked under the **National Social Conference**.
**Sarala Devi Chaudhurani** and **Allahabad, 1910** = **Bharat Stree Mahamandal**; **Pandita Ramabai** and **1882** = **Arya Mahila Samaj**.
xa: **National Council of Women in India** (**1925**): **Meherbai Tata**, **Cornelia Sorabji**.
Ramabai Ranade also co-founded the **Poona Seva Sadan** (**1909**).

nb57e2cf146e.s: Bharat Stree Mahamandal, founded at Allahabad in 1910, was established by:
nb57e2cf146e.x: Sarala Devi Chaudhurani founded it in 1910; it is regarded as the first major all-India women's body founded by a woman.
xa: ⚠ Some notes credit it to **D.K. Karve** — the standard answer is Sarala Devi.
**AIWC** pressed for the **Sarda Act (1929)** and the **Hindu Women's Right to Property Act (1937)**.
**National Council of Women in India**: **1925**.

n54e47ce5d87.s: Sarada Niketan, described as a women’s gurukulam, was established at Guntur in 1922 by:
n54e47ce5d87.x: Sarada Niketan was established at Guntur in 1922 by Unnava Lakshminarayana with his wife Lakshmibayamma.
n54e47ce5d87.tq: Test the Andhra-specific institution, place, year and founder together.
xs: **Sarada Niketan** (women's gurukulam, Guntur, **1922**) was founded by **Unnava Lakshminarayana** with **Lakshmibayamma** — option **(1)**.
**Ramabai Ranade** and **G.K. Devadhar** founded the **Poona Seva Sadan**; **N.M. Joshi** the **Social Service League**.
xa: Lakshmibayamma's widow asylum at **Guntur (1902)** later merged into it.
She ran the monthly **Sri Sarada Niketanam**.
Other Andhra bodies: **Vysya Seva Sadanam** (Rajahmundry, **1920**), **Indira Saranalayam** (Vijayawada, **1927**).

n646f7fc8cda.s: Veeresalingam's second girls' school was established at Innispeta, Rajahmundry, in:
n646f7fc8cda.x: His first girls' school dates to 1874 and the Innispeta school to 1881; he was also the first in Andhra to promote co-education.
xa: ⚠ APPSC **2025** key: "first girls' school at **Rajahmundry**".
His women's journal: **Satihita Bodhini** (**1883**).
**M.G. Ranade** called him the "**South Indian Vidyasagar**".

n6426f9af544.s: Bandaru Achamamba is remembered as an early Telugu woman historian and short-story writer. Which of the following was her work?
n6426f9af544.x: Bandaru Achamamba wrote Abala Sachcharitra Ratnamala, dealing with the lives of notable women.
n6426f9af544.tq: Use the exact title to distinguish literary works of women reformers.
xs: **Bandaru Achamamba** wrote **Abala Sachcharitra Ratnamala**, lives of notable women — option **(3)**.
**Sri Sarada Niketanam** was **Unnava Lakshmibayamma**'s monthly; **The High-Caste Hindu Woman** is **Pandita Ramabai**'s; **Sati Hita Bodhini** is **Veeresalingam**'s.
xa: Achamamba was an early Telugu woman **historian** and **short-story writer**.
Lakshmibayamma's widow asylum at **Guntur (1902)** later merged into **Sarada Niketan**.
**Tripura Sundari Samajam** was at **Bapatla**.

nb06ea5fcea1.s: Which of the following was an unintended result of British rule that helped the growth of Indian nationalism?
o: End of racial discrimination in administration
nb06ea5fcea1.x: British rule unified India politically and administratively and linked it by railways, telegraph, post and uniform laws, while ruining many artisans.
xa: Other unintended results: **Western liberal ideas** and a **new educated middle class** (lawyers, journalists, teachers).
Reactions that fed nationalism: **drain**, **racial arrogance** (Lytton, **Ilbert Bill**), foreign inspiration.
**History-writing** — rediscovery of India's past — gave **self-confidence**.

n187dedd5b59.s: Western education contributed to the growth of Indian nationalism by:
o: Helping English function as a link language
Reviving Persian as the court language
n187dedd5b59.x: Western education spread liberal ideas, made English a link language and created an educated middle class; it did not end racial discrimination.
xa: Other factors: **socio-religious reform**, the **press** (Veeresalingam's **Vivekavardhani**, **1874**).
**Foreign inspiration**: **American**, **French** and **Italian** movements.

nc4aeb48a378.s: Which one of the following was NOT a measure of Lord Lytton?
nc4aeb48a378.x: The Ilbert Bill (1883) belonged to Lord Ripon's time. The Vernacular Press Act and the Arms Act (both 1878) and the Delhi Durbar of 1877, which proclaimed Victoria Empress during the famine, were all Lytton's resented measures.
xs: The **Ilbert Bill** was **Ripon**'s, not Lytton's — option **(3)**.
Lytton's measures: **Vernacular Press Act 1878**, **Arms Act 1878**, **Delhi Durbar 1877** and the **Second Afghan War 1878-80**.
xa: The Durbar proclaimed **Queen Victoria** Empress while millions starved (**1876-78**).
The Arms Act disarmed **Indians but not Europeans**.
Both the Ilbert Bill and Lytton's policies are listed as **racial arrogance** that fed nationalism.

ncb6a6265c73.s: The early political associations contributed to the rise of the Indian National Congress chiefly by:
o: Restricting political activity exclusively to princely states
Training the English-educated class in petitions, memorials and all-India coordination
Organising armed revolts against every colonial institution
ncb6a6265c73.x: These associations trained educated Indians in constitutional political methods such as petitions and memorials and promoted all-India coordination, leading to the formation of the INC in 1885.
ncb6a6265c73.tq: Apply the institutional legacy of the associations to the emergence of the INC.
xs: The associations **trained the English-educated class in petitions, memorials and all-India coordination** — option **(3)** — leading straight to the **INC** in **1885**.
They used **constitutional** methods, not armed revolt.
xa: Andhra links: **Madras Native Association (1852)**, **Madras Mahajana Sabha (1884)**, **Krishna District Association (1892)**.
**Indian National Conference** (**1883**, **1885**) merged with the INC.
⚠ They were led by **landlords / urban elite** and were **regional**.

nf349fd820d2.s: The Delhi Durbar of 1877 was significant because it:
o: Announced the end of the Second Afghan War
Proclaimed Queen Victoria as Empress of India
nf349fd820d2.x: The Delhi Durbar of 1877 proclaimed Queen Victoria as Empress of India, even as millions were suffering in the famine of 1876–78.
nf349fd820d2.tq: Match the ceremonial event with its constitutional-symbolic significance.
xs: The **Delhi Durbar** (**1877**) proclaimed **Queen Victoria Empress** of India — option **(3)**.
It was resented because millions were starving in the **1876-78** famine.
The **Second Afghan War** ran **1878-80**; the **Vernacular Press Act** was passed (not repealed) in **1878**.
xa: It was one of **Lytton**'s resented measures (**1876-80**).
The **Arms Act** (**1878**) disarmed Indians but not Europeans.

n66ab7c27a8f.s: Amrita Bazar Patrika was founded in which year, and in which year did it become an English newspaper overnight?
n66ab7c27a8f.x: Amrita Bazar Patrika was founded in 1868 and changed into an English newspaper overnight in 1878 to escape the Vernacular Press Act.
n66ab7c27a8f.tq: Pair the two closely related years instead of treating the later year as the founding year.
xs: **Amrita Bazar Patrika** was founded in **1868** and turned English overnight in **1878** — option **(3)**.
The switch was made to escape **Lytton**'s **Vernacular Press Act** (**1878**).
xa: Founders: **Sisir Kumar Ghosh** and **Motilal Ghosh**.
**The Bengalee** (**1879**) — Surendranath Banerjee; **Swadesamitran** (**1882**) — G. Subramania Iyer.

n4ad3fcadad0.s: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's Anandamath (1882) is set against the background of the:
n4ad3fcadad0.x: Anandamath is set in the Sannyasi Rebellion; its song Vande Mataram was first sung at the INC by Tagore at Calcutta in 1896.
xa: Telugu translation of Vande Mataram: **Y. Doraiswamayya** and **M. Ramarao**.
⚠ **Durgeshnandini** = Bankim's **first novel**; **Anandamath** = Vande Mataram.
Other Bankim novels: **Rajasimha**, **Rajani**, **Indira**.

n9d820d21c51.s: Who wrote Nil Darpan, published in 1860?
n9d820d21c51.x: Dinabandhu Mitra wrote Nil Darpan, which was published in 1860.
n9d820d21c51.tq: Direct author-year recall for nationalist literature.
xs: **Nil Darpan** (**1860**) was written by **Dinabandhu Mitra** — option **(3)**.
**Bankim Chandra Chatterjee** wrote **Anandamath** (**1882**); **Nabin Chandra Sen** and **Hem Chandra Banerjee** were nationalist **poets**.
xa: Bankim's first novel: **Durgeshnandini**.
"**The Cry of Mother India**" (Krishna Patrika, **15 Dec 1905**) = first nationalist song of Andhra.

n2686e4aa184.s: 'The Cry of Mother India', regarded as the first nationalist song in Andhra, appeared in 1905 in:
n2686e4aa184.x: 'The Cry of Mother India' appeared in Krishna Patrika on 15 December 1905.
xa: Krishna Patrika was among about **20** Telugu journals by **1905** that criticised the government.
Others: **Andhra Prakasika**, **Sasilekha**, **Deshabhimani**.
Telugu Vande Mataram: **Y. Doraiswamayya** and **M. Ramarao**.

n9676f8a0e74.s: Andhra Patrika was founded in 1908 by
n9676f8a0e74.x: Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao founded Andhra Patrika in 1908.
n9676f8a0e74.tq: Use the publication year to distinguish Andhra Patrika from earlier Telugu journals.
xs: **Andhra Patrika** (**1908**) was founded by **Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao** — option **(1)**.
**G. Subramania Iyer** founded **Swadesamitran** (**1882**).
xa: Began **9 Sep 1908** as a **Bombay weekly**; daily from **1914**, later at **Madras**.
⚠ Do not confuse with **Andhra Prakasika** = first political journal in Andhra.
English **Swarajya** (**1922**) — **Tanguturi Prakasam**.

n40af8c7e92f.s: The English daily Swarajya, started at Madras in 1922, was founded by:
n40af8c7e92f.x: Tanguturi Prakasam founded the English daily Swarajya at Madras in 1922 (APPSC G2 2011 key). Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao ran a different, Telugu Swarajya at Vijayawada (1907-08), which is the trap. Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded Andhra Patrika, and G. Subramania Iyer founded Swadesamitran.
n40af8c7e92f.tq: English Swarajya = Prakasam; Telugu Swarajya = Harisarvottama Rao.
xs: The English daily **Swarajya** (Madras, **1922**) was founded by **Tanguturi Prakasam** — option **(2)** (APPSC G2 **2011** key).
⚠ **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** ran a different **Telugu Swarajya** at **Vijayawada** (**1907-08**).
**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** founded **Andhra Patrika**; **G. Subramania Iyer** founded **Swadesamitran**.
xa: First Telugu journal: **Satyadoota** (**Bellary**).
Around **20** Telugu journals by **1905**.

n322539b23c1.s: The secretary of the Madras Native Association (1852) was:
n322539b23c1.x: Somasundaram Chettiyar was its secretary; P. Anandacharlu was secretary of the Madras Mahajana Sabha. Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty was founder and first president.
xa: It was the first political body of **Madras** and of **South India**.
It began as an adjunct of the **British Indian Association**.
Chetty was the first to spread national ideas in Andhra.

n4119357d352.s: Surendranath Banerjee toured the country against the reduction of the ICS maximum age from 21 to:
n4119357d352.x: Banerjee, who passed the ICS in 1869 and was dismissed in 1874, campaigned against cutting the maximum age from 21 to 19.
xa: He founded the **Indian Association** (**1876**) with **A.M. Bose**.
Title: "**Rashtraguru**"; paper: **The Bengalee**.

n399c4646930.s: The Indian National Conference, held in 1883 and 1885 and later merged with the INC, was convened by:
n399c4646930.x: Surendranath Banerjee convened the Indian National Conference in 1883 and 1885; it later merged with the INC.
xa: He founded the **Indian Association** (**1876**) with **A.M. Bose**.
He presided over the INC at **Poona 1895** and **Ahmedabad 1902**.
Early associations led straight to the **INC** in **1885**.

n044bc505752.s: The demand for agricultural banks at Angalur in 1900 was made at a conference of the:
n044bc505752.x: Agricultural banks at Angalur were demanded at a Krishna District Association conference in 1900, not by the Madras Native Association.
xa: Krishna District Association conferences: **Guntur 1892**, **Machilipatnam 1893**, **Eluru 1894**, **Angalur 1900**.
⚠ **1900** = Angalur conference, not the Association's founding (**1892**).

n7e2c5b5e2be.s: When the Madras Mahajana Sabha was founded on 16 May 1884, its president was:
n7e2c5b5e2be.x: P. Rangaiah Naidu was president and P. Anandacharlu secretary; the Sabha demanded larger councils and more Indian representation.
xa: Other founders: **M. Viraraghavachariar**, **G. Subramania Iyer**.
APPSC-GS **2025**: **1852** and **1884** are correct.

ne770e444fa0.s: The Kakinada Literary Association submitted memorandums during 1884–85 demanding
o: A lower ICS age limit and separate examinations for Indians
The abolition of the Madras Mahajana Sabha
The introduction of jury trials for Europeans only
A higher ICS age limit and simultaneous examinations
ne770e444fa0.x: The Kakinada Literary Association demanded that the ICS age limit be raised and that the examinations be held simultaneously.
ne770e444fa0.tq: Link a specific association with its distinctive constitutional demand.
xs: The **Kakinada (Coconada) Literary Association** asked (**1884-85**) to **raise the ICS age limit** and hold **simultaneous exams** — option **(4)**.
Option 1 is the opposite — the British had **lowered** the age (**21 to 19**) to keep Indians out.
xa: It handled public affairs in **Godavari**.
**Surendranath Banerjee** toured the country against the age cut.

nf48b492d623.s: The Krishna District Association, founded in 1892, was established by
nf48b492d623.x: Ramaswamy Gupta founded the Krishna District Association in 1892, the first district association in the Madras Presidency.
nf48b492d623.tq: Direct founder recall for a regional association.
xs: The **Krishna District Association** (**1892**) was founded by **Ramaswamy Gupta** — option **(2)**.
**P. Rangaiah Naidu** was Madras Mahajana Sabha president; **Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty** founded the Madras Native Association.
xa: It was the **first district association in the Madras Presidency**.
It was modelled on the **INC's advice** to form district bodies.
⚠ "**1900**" as its year is wrong (APPSC-GS **2021**, **2025**).

ne78227b5924.s: The Krishna District Association, formed in 1892, is significant because it was
o: the first district association in the Madras Presidency
the first provincial government of Madras
the first political association in Bengal
the first newspaper association in Andhra
ne78227b5924.x: The Krishna District Association, formed in 1892 following the INC’s suggestion, was the first district association in the Madras Presidency.
ne78227b5924.tq: Identify the significance attached to a regional organisation rather than its founder.
xs: The **Krishna District Association** (**1892**) was the **first district association in the Madras Presidency** — option **(1)**.
It followed the **INC's advice** to form district bodies.
xa: Founder: **Ramaswamy Gupta**.
⚠ **1852 – 1884 – 1892** = Native Association – Mahajana Sabha – Krishna District Association.

n9d38b617586.s: The Telugu translation of Vande Mataram was made by
o: P. Anandacharlu and G. Subramania Iyer
Rangalal Banerjee and Hem Chandra Banerjee
Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose
n9d38b617586.x: The Telugu translation of Vande Mataram was made by Y. Doraiswamayya and M. Ramarao.
n9d38b617586.tq: Match the translation with its translators.
xs: **Vande Mataram** was translated into Telugu by **Y. Doraiswamayya** and **M. Ramarao** — option **(2)**.
**P. Anandacharlu** and **G. Subramania Iyer** were **Madras Mahajana Sabha** founders; **Rangalal** and **Hem Chandra Banerjee** were Bengal poets.
**Surendranath Banerjee** and **A.M. Bose** founded the **Indian Association** (**1876**).
xa: Vande Mataram became a **nationalist war cry**.
Andhra's first nationalist song: "**The Cry of Mother India**" (Krishna Patrika, **15 Dec 1905**).

nef20de55c23.s: The early pre-Congress political associations were generally:
o: Regional bodies led by landlords or the urban elite
Equally representative of all sections of society
nef20de55c23.x: They were largely led by landlords or the urban elite and were regional in character.
xa: They trained the educated class in **petitions and memorials** → **INC** (**1885**).
The **Madras Native Association** (**1852**) was the first in South India.

nccb8b82d56c.s: Which one of the following was NOT a major factor in the rise of nationalism in nineteenth-century India?
o: Growth of a new middle class
nccb8b82d56c.x: The major factors included Western education, the press, the new middle class, socio-religious reform and economic exploitation. Expansion of hereditary feudal privileges was not identified as a cause.
nccb8b82d56c.tq: Find the option outside the stated cluster of causes.
xs: **Expansion of hereditary feudal privileges** was not a cause of nationalism — so option **(4)** is correct.
The causes were **Western education**, the **press**, a **new middle class**, **socio-religious reform** and **economic exploitation**.
Under economic exploitation, India was reduced to a **raw-material supplier** and a **captive market**.
xa: **Lytton**'s policies — the **Delhi Durbar 1877**, **Vernacular Press Act 1878** and **Arms Act 1878** — fed Indian resentment.
The **Ilbert Bill (1883)** controversy exposed **racial discrimination** (APPSC 2018).
Nationalist literature: **Neel Darpan** (**1860**) and **Anandamath** (**1882**).

n5a7417557fe.s: Which was the first political association in India?
n5a7417557fe.x: The Bangabhasha Prakasika Sabha, established in 1836 by associates of Raja Rammohan Roy, is regarded as the first political association in India.
n5a7417557fe.tq: Direct recall of the earliest organisation in a sequence.
xs: The **Bangabhasha Prakasika Sabha** (**1836**) was the first organised political association — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was founded at **Calcutta** by associates of **Raja Rammohan Roy**.
The **Landholders' Society** came in **1838**, the **Bengal British India Society** in **1843** and the **British Indian Association** in **1851**.
xa: The British Indian Association was a **merger** of the Landholders' Society and the Bengal British India Society.
The **Indian Association** (**1876**) was the most important pre-Congress body.
The **Madras Native Association** was founded on **26 Feb 1852**.

nc9a00760849.s: The British Indian Association was formed at Calcutta in 1851 by merging:
o: The Indian Association and the Landholders' Society
The East India Association and the Bengal British India Society
The Landholders' Society and the Bengal British India Society
The Brahmo Samaj and the Dharma Sabha
nc9a00760849.x: It merged the Landholders' Society (1838) and the Bengal British India Society (1843); the 1866 London body was Naoroji's East India Association.
xa: British Indian Association: President **Radhakanta Deb** (**APPSC 2019**), **Debendranath Tagore** secretary.
The **first organised political association** was the **Bangabhasha Prakashika Sabha** (**1836**), by associates of **Raja Rammohan Roy**.
The **Madras Native Association** (**1852**) began as an adjunct of the British Indian Association.

n64a90df8b01.s: Who was the first president of the British Indian Association?
n64a90df8b01.x: Radhakanta Deb was its first president and Debendranath Tagore its secretary; the Madras Native Association began as its adjunct.
xa: The British Indian Association (**1851**) was a merger of the **Landholders' Society** and the **Bengal British India Society**.
The **Indian Association** (**1876**) was founded by **S.N. Banerjea** and **Ananda Mohan Bose** — the most important pre-Congress body.
Madras Native Association: founded **26 Feb 1852**; first president **Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Setty**.

n67d042f6444.s: Dadabhai Naoroji founded the East India Association in London in:
n67d042f6444.x: Naoroji founded the East India Association in London in 1866.
xa: Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty was the **first to spread national ideas in Andhra**.
Madras Mahajana Sabha (**16 May 1884**): **P. Anandacharlu**, **M. Viraraghavachariar**, **G. Subramania Iyer**.
The Madras Mahajana Sabha (**1884**) was asked in **APPSC 2019**.

n01f83736c27.s: The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha was founded on 2 April 1870 by M.G. Ranade and:
n01f83736c27.x: Ranade and G.V. Joshi founded it; in 1875 it petitioned the House of Commons for Indian representation in Parliament.
xa: The Sabha **nurtured Tilak**.
Some notes add **S.H. Chiplunkar** among its founders.
The **Indian Association** (**1876**) demanded **ICS** exams in India.

nc0408200a34.s: The Indian Association (1876) was founded by S.N. Banerjea and:
nc0408200a34.x: S.N. Banerjea and Ananda Mohan Bose founded the Indian Association; Mehta, Telang and Tyabji founded the Bombay Presidency Association (1885).
xa: Indian Association demanded **ICS** exams in India, opposed the **Arms/Vernacular Press Acts** and held **All-India National Conferences** (**1883, 1885**).
Poona Sarvajanik Sabha petitioned the **House of Commons** in **1875** for Indian representation in the British Parliament.
⚠ **India League (1875)** = **Sisir Kumar Ghosh**; **Indian Association (1876)** = **S.N. Banerjea** + **Ananda Mohan Bose**.

nbaf51167b3b.s: Who was the first person to spread national ideas in Andhra?
nbaf51167b3b.x: Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty is credited with being the first to spread national ideas in Andhra.
nbaf51167b3b.tq: Distinguish the early Andhra propagator from later newspaper and association leaders.
xs: **Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty** was the first to spread national ideas in Andhra — so option **(3)** is correct.
He was the first president of the **Madras Native Association** (**26 Feb 1852**).
**Surendranath Banerjee** made an **Andhra tour** for the Indian Association in **1878**, later than Gazula's work.
xa: The first Andhra/Telugu INC President was **P. Anandacharlu** (**Nagpur 1891**).
**5** Andhra delegates attended the **1885** session.
The **Krishna District Association (1892)** followed the INC's suggestion.

naad38d58d50.s: Which pre-Congress body organised All-India National Conferences in 1883 and 1885?
naad38d58d50.x: The Indian Association, the most important pre-Congress body, organised these conferences and opposed the Arms Act and Vernacular Press Act.
xa: It was founded in **1876** by **S.N. Banerjea** and **Ananda Mohan Bose** — the **most important pre-Congress body**.
**Bipan Chandra** cited it to show Indians were already organising, rejecting the safety-valve myth.
S.N. Banerjea's **Andhra tour** for the Association was in **1878**.

na11fb1b0f99.s: A.O. Hume is popularly known as the
na11fb1b0f99.x: A.O. Hume is known as the Father of Indian Ornithology, in addition to his political role in the formation of the INC.
na11fb1b0f99.tq: Test the less commonly recalled title associated with a well-known political figure.
xs: **A.O. Hume** is known as the **"Father of Indian Ornithology"** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Politically, he was a retired **ICS** officer and the INC's first **General Secretary**.
xa: He was demoted in **1879** after clashing with **Lytton**, retired in **1882** and settled at **Shimla**.
He read **seven volumes of secret reports** at **Simla** in **1878** — the basis of the safety-valve theory.
**Wedderburn**'s biography of Hume (**1913**) first mentioned the safety-valve theory.

n2060a0a5637.s: Kadambini Ganguly, who addressed the 1890 Calcutta session of the INC, was the first woman graduate of:
n2060a0a5637.x: Kadambini Ganguly was Calcutta University's first woman graduate and addressed the 1890 session presided over by Pherozeshah Mehta.
xa: **Pherozeshah Mehta** is called the **Lion of Bombay**.
The **first woman President** was **Annie Besant** (Calcutta **1917**).
The first Indian woman President was **Sarojini Naidu** (Kanpur **1925**).

n7c4f682a1bb.s: Which leader presided over the Indian National Congress three times and is remembered as the Grand Old Man of India?

Eastern Bengal and Assam had **31 million** people.

o: The partition of Bengal was annulled and the capital shifted to Delhi
The partition of Bengal formally took effect as a day of mourning
The boycott resolution was passed at Calcutta Town Hall and Swadeshi was formally proclaimed
The National Council of Education was established
n7813c3d566e.x: On 7 August 1905, the boycott resolution was passed at Calcutta Town Hall and Swadeshi was formally proclaimed.

nc144a9f898d.s: In which year did leadership of the Swadeshi Movement pass from the Moderates to the Extremists?
nc144a9f898d.x: The leadership of the movement passed from the Moderates to the Extremists in 1906.
xa: Extremist methods: **boycott**, **Swadeshi**, **national education**, **passive resistance**.
The **Surat Split** came in **Dec 1907**.
The movement faded by **1908** under repression and the Surat Split.

nc0409f7f9c9.s: Who presided over the Madras Beach students' meeting (September 1905) that began the Swadeshi movement in Andhra?
nc0409f7f9c9.x: The meeting was presided over by G. Subramania Iyer; Mutnuri Krishna Rao arranged Pal's tour in 1907.

The Andhra phase is placed in **1905-1911**.
S.N. Banerjee's arrest (**1906**) triggered protests with the slogan **"Vandemataram - Manade Rajyam"**.

n1dc916cd7c3.s: Who presided over Bipin Chandra Pal's lectures at Kakinada in April 1907?
n1dc916cd7c3.x: Kattiventi Perraju presided at Kakinada; Kompalle Hanumantha Rao was Pal's host at Machilipatnam.

At **Rajahmundry** (**19-24 Apr**) he gave **five lectures**.
The tour was arranged by **Mutnuri Krishna Rao**.

nf45d9fcc387.s: In which year were Osmania University students expelled for singing Vande Mataram in the hostels?
nf45d9fcc387.x: In 1938 Osmania students, including P.V. Narasimha Rao, were expelled for singing Vande Mataram in the hostels.
xa: At Rajahmundry, Principal **Mark Hunter** suspended **138 of 222** students.
The Rajahmundry incident marked the **start of student participation** in Andhra.
Osmania 1938 is a **later echo** of the Vandemataram movement.

nede6581e2ce.s: Which of the following correctly describes the events of December 1906?
o: The National Council of Education was established and Home Rule Leagues began
The Surat Split occurred and Tilak was sent to Mandalay
The partition took effect and the Swadeshi vow was taken
The Muslim League was formed at Dacca and the Calcutta Congress adopted Swaraj
nede6581e2ce.x: In December 1906, the Muslim League was formed at Dacca and the Calcutta Congress under Dadabhai Naoroji adopted Swaraj.
nede6581e2ce.tq: Pair events sharing the same month while rejecting events from neighbouring years.
xs: In **Dec 1906** the **Muslim League** was formed at **Dacca** and the **Calcutta Congress** adopted **Swaraj** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The Calcutta session was presided over by **Naoroji**.
The **National Council of Education** was **15 Aug 1906**; **Home Rule Leagues** **1916**; **Surat Split** **Dec 1907**; Tilak to **Mandalay** **1908**.
xa: ⚠ **Banaras 1905** = Gokhale (Swadeshi); **Calcutta 1906** = Naoroji (Swaraj).
**1908** also saw the **Muzaffarpur bomb**, the **Alipore case** and the **Newspapers Act**.
The partition took effect on **16 Oct 1905**.

n7c469ab059f.s: Which event helped intensify anger against the partition of Bengal?
o: The formation of the Muslim League in 1909
n7c469ab059f.x: Japan’s victory over Russia in 1904–05 inspired Asian and Indian nationalist sentiment and fed anger against the partition (Sumit Sarkar's interpretation).
xa: Japan's influence in Andhra: **Munagala Raja** named his sons **Togo** and **Nogi**.
Andhra youths went to **Japan** for industrial training.
Sarkar used **plays, novels and pamphlets** as sources.

n5984be5e9aa.s: Which one of the following was a major limitation of the Swadeshi movement?
o: It continued unaffected by repression after 1908.
It rejected all forms of national education.
It had no support among intellectuals or urban groups.
It received limited participation from peasants and Muslims.
n5984be5e9aa.x: Peasant and Muslim participation in the movement was limited. The movement also faded by 1908 under repression and after the Surat Split.
n5984be5e9aa.tq: Find the accurately stated limitation while rejecting extreme generalisations.
xs: The movement had **limited participation from peasants and Muslims** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It did not continue unaffected — it **faded by 1908**; and it **promoted** national education.
xa: It is still called the **first mass movement** (UPSC 2016).
The **Muslim League** was formed at **Dacca** in **Dec 1906**.
The **real motive** of partition was to divide **Bengali Hindus from Muslims**.

n8c743dbc7d1.s: The official justification given for the partition of Bengal was:
n8c743dbc7d1.x: Administrative convenience was the stated reason; the real aim was to weaken Bengali nationalism and divide Hindus and Muslims.
xa: **H.H. Risley**: "Bengal united is a power; Bengal divided will pull in several different ways".
**Curzon**: "Bengal is the nerve centre of Indian nationalism".
The partition was annulled on **12 Dec 1911** at the **Delhi Durbar**.

nindian-history-128-5.s: The capital of the new province of Eastern Bengal and Assam (1905) was:
nindian-history-128-5.x: Eastern Bengal and Assam had Dacca as its capital, while Western Bengal kept Calcutta.
n: Eastern Bengal and Assam was the new province. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #128 · pp 231-232]
Dacca (Dhaka) was the capital of Eastern Bengal and Assam. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #128 · pp 231-232]
Calcutta was the capital of Western Bengal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #128 · pp 231-232]
The capital shifted from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #128 · pp 231-232]
xa: Eastern Bengal and Assam had **31 million** people; the rest of Bengal **54 million**.
Rest of Bengal: **18 million** Bengalis, **36 million** Biharis and Oriyas → Bengalis a minority.
Stated motive: administrative convenience; real motive: divide **Bengali Hindus from Muslims**.

n89948322784.s: The Swadesh Bandhab Samiti of Barisal was led by:
n89948322784.x: The Swadesh Bandhab Samiti at Barisal was led by Ashwini Kumar Dutt; K.K. Mitra first advocated boycott in Sanjibani.
xa: ⚠ Boycott first advocated = **K.K. Mitra**; funds raised = **S.N. Banerjee** + **A.M. Bose**.
Ashwini Kumar Dutt is listed among the **Bengal** Extremist leaders.
Mass mobilisation used **jatras**, **folk songs**, **melas** and **volunteer corps**.

n260b1a9cc5d.s: During the Swadeshi Movement, jatras, melas, akharas and lathi clubs were used for:
n260b1a9cc5d.x: Jatras, folk songs, melas, volunteer corps, akharas and lathi clubs were all used for mass mobilisation.
xa: **Samitis** like the **Swadesh Bandhab Samiti** used magic lanterns and arbitration courts.
**Tilak** started **Ganeshotsav** (**1893**) and the **Shivaji festival** (**1895**).
The movement is called the **first mass movement** (UPSC 2016).

o: Colonial self-government within the British Empire
n4be733cc870.x: Extremist Swaraj meant complete freedom, not colonial self-government, pursued through boycott, Swadeshi, national education and passive resistance.
xa: Tilak: **"Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"**.
The **Calcutta 1906** INC under **Naoroji** adopted Swaraj.
⚠ **Banaras 1905** = Gokhale (Swadeshi); **Calcutta 1906** = Naoroji (Swaraj).

n92e62c5bbaf.s: The Swadeshi movement of 1905 is regarded as the first ____ movement in India.
n92e62c5bbaf.x: The Swadeshi movement was regarded as the first mass movement and marked the birth of mass nationalism.
xa: Its limits: **limited peasant and Muslim participation**.
It faded by **1908** under **repression** and the **Surat Split**.
The **National Council of Education** came on **15 Aug 1906**.

nd805d834510.s: Who founded Bengal Chemicals during the Swadeshi Movement?
nd805d834510.x: Bengal Chemicals was founded by Acharya P.C. Ray as a Swadeshi enterprise.

xa: P.C. Ray and **J.C. Bose** represented **Indian scientific achievement**.
**Banga Lakshmi Cotton Mills** came in **1906**.
Swadeshi banks: **Bank of India 1906**, **Indian Bank 1907**.

n65864b70e33.s: The Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company was associated with which of the following persons and places?
n65864b70e33.x: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai established the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company at Tuticorin in 1906.
n65864b70e33.tq: Link the entrepreneur with both the enterprise and its regional centre.
xs: The **Swadeshi Steam Navigation Co.** was **V.O. Chidambaram Pillai**'s, at **Tuticorin** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was founded in **1906**.
**Munagala Raja** ran a textile unit at **Vijayawada**; **P.C. Ray** founded **Bengal Chemicals**; **Guneswara Rao** backed the **Bala Bharati Samiti**.
xa: Chidambaram Pillai led the movement in **Madras**.
The **Swarajya case** (**1908**) arose from an article praising Chidambaram Pillai.
Andhra youths were sent to **Japan** for industrial training.

n6a85f5b7222.s: Who was the first principal of Bengal National College?
n6a85f5b7222.x: Aurobindo Ghosh served as the first principal of Bengal National College.
n6a85f5b7222.tq: Distinguish an institutional office from general political leadership.
xs: **Aurobindo Ghosh** was the first principal of **Bengal National College** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**S.N. Banerjee** led the Moderates; **Bipin Chandra Pal** toured Andhra in **1907**.
xa: The **National Council of Education** came on **15 August 1906** (later **Jadavpur University**).
Aurobindo was tried in the **Alipore case**, acquitted, and retired to **Pondicherry**.
Aurobindo is linked with **Bande Mataram**.

n1e59c468440.s: The National Council of Education was established on:

nbbc57387a29.s: The textile unit established by Munagala Raja at Vijayawada in June 1906 was significant because it was:

the first national college in the Madras Presidency
the first Swadeshi bank in Andhra
nbbc57387a29.x: Munagala Raja’s textile unit at Vijayawada, established in June 1906, was the first of its kind in the Madras Presidency.

xs: **Munagala Raja**'s textile unit at **Vijayawada** (**June 1906**) was **the first such unit in the Madras Presidency** — so option **(2)** is correct.

Andhra youths went to **Japan** for training: **Malladi Venkata Subbarao** (pencils), **S. Ramarao** (glass and clocks).
**Banga Lakshmi Cotton Mills** also date from **1906**.

ndf773c2b241.s: Inspired by Japan's victory over Russia, who named his sons Togo and Nogi?

**Sumit Sarkar** stressed Japan's win in the anger against partition.

nindian-history-111-9.s: What was the principal feature of the Swadeshi and Boycott movement during the period of the Partition of Bengal?

Accept the Nehru Report and begin a mass movement
Adopt Complete Independence as the Congress goal
Draft a constitutional framework for India

n: The Swadeshi and Boycott movement occurred during the period of the Partition of Bengal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Swadeshi and Boycott movement was associated with the Congress and the nationalist movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Swadeshi and Boycott movement promoted the boycott of foreign goods. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Swadeshi and Boycott movement promoted indigenous goods. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Swadeshi and Boycott movement promoted national education. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
xs: The movement's feature was to **boycott foreign goods** and **promote indigenous goods** and **national education** — option **(1)**.
It occurred during the **Partition** of **Bengal**, which nationalists saw as **"Divide and Rule"**.
Boycott covered **foreign cloth**, **salt** and **sugar**, with **bonfires** of cloth, extending to courts, schools and government service.
xa: Formal proclamation: **7 Aug 1905**, boycott resolution at **Calcutta Town Hall**.
**National Council of Education**: **15 August 1906** (later **Jadavpur University**).
**National Handloom Day** is **7 August**, observed since **2015**.

n4d8c3f03d06.s: Who wrote the song ‘Amar Sonar Bangla’, which later became the national anthem of Bangladesh?

**Bankim Chandra Chatterjee** wrote **Bande Mataram**; **Abanindranath Tagore** painted **Bharat Mata**; **Chilakamarti** was a Telugu poet.
xa: ⚠ **Amar Sonar Bangla** = Tagore; **Bande Mataram** = Bankim (**Anandamath**).

n5d5c126f9a8.s: ‘Desher Katha’ was written by S.G. Deuskar primarily to warn Indians against:

the decline of Sanskrit education under the Mughals
the division of Bengal into linguistic provinces
the British ‘hypnotic conquest of the mind’

**Sumit Sarkar** wrote **The Swadeshi Movement in Bengal**.

n58dee1cb667.s: Who was described as the ‘First Telugu national poet’?

**Dasu Narayana Rao** ran **"Jatiya Nataka Rangam"** theatre; **Attili Suryanarayana Rao** wrote **Hindu Desa Daridryam**; **C.Y. Chintamani** was a **Vizag** leader.
xa: Chilakamarti's poem **"Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi yaavu"** is tied to Pal's **Rajahmundry** visit.
Chilakamarti ran the paper **Desamata**.

n206318f3766.s: During his Rajahmundry visit (April 1907), how many lectures did Bipin Chandra Pal deliver?

Kakinada lectures were presided by **Kattiventi Perraju**.

n4cf2b3e09ce.s: Which of the following newspapers was associated with Chilakamarti during the Swadeshi movement in Andhra?

xs: **Chilakamarti** was associated with **Desamata** — so option **(1)** is correct.

His poem **"Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi yaavu"** is tied to Pal's Rajahmundry visit.

ne03015ab73a.s: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was imprisoned for six years at which place?
ne03015ab73a.x: Bal Gangadhar Tilak served a six-year imprisonment at Mandalay.

xs: **Tilak** spent **6 years** in **Mandalay** — so option **(1)** is correct.

**Pondicherry** is where **Aurobindo** retired; **Alipore** was Aurobindo's case; the **Muslim League** was founded at **Dacca**.
xa: Tilak = **"Lokmanya"**; **Valentine Chirol** called him **"Father of Indian Unrest"**.
He ran **Kesari** and **Mahratta** (**1881**).
Slogan: **"Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"**.

n3e77b88c4a3.s: Which Extremist leader undertook an Andhra tour in 1907 and was later arrested?
n3e77b88c4a3.x: Bipin Chandra Pal toured Andhra in 1907 and was subsequently arrested.

n5cd8a208d61.s: The British journalist Valentine Chirol called which leader the Father of Indian Unrest?
n5cd8a208d61.x: Chirol called Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Lokmanya, of Maharashtra) the Father of Indian Unrest. Pal led in Bengal, Lajpat Rai in Punjab (Punjab Kesari), and Aurobindo edited Bande Mataram.
n5cd8a208d61.tq: Chirol -> Tilak = Father of Indian Unrest
xs: **Valentine Chirol** called **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** the **"Father of Indian Unrest"** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Pal** led in Bengal; **Lajpat Rai** in Punjab; **Aurobindo** is linked with **Bande Mataram** and the **Alipore case**.
xa: Tilak = **"Lokmanya"**, of **Maharashtra**.
He spent **6 years** in **Mandalay**.
He was born **23 Jul 1856** at **Ratnagiri**.

n92ef80539c7.s: Which development was associated with Bipin Chandra Pal’s visit to Machilipatnam on 27 April 1907?
o: Formation of the Swadeshi League and Industrial Association
Formation of the Young Men’s Swarajya Samithi and foundation of a national college
Establishment of the Bala Bharati Samiti
Opening of the Godavari Swadeshi Stores
n92ef80539c7.x: The Young Men’s Swarajya Samithi was formed and the foundation for a national college was laid at Machilipatnam during Pal’s visit.
n92ef80539c7.tq: Match the final stop of a tour with the institutional developments recorded there.
xs: At **Machilipatnam** (**27 Apr**) the **Young Men's Swarajya Samithi** was formed and the foundation of a **national college** was laid — so option **(2)** is correct.

The tour ran **16-27 Apr 1907**.
Tour arranged by **Mutnuri Krishna Rao** of **Krishna Patrika**.

nb9164d2b3d0.s: In Andhra, protests at Rajahmundry, Kakinada, Vizianagaram and Gooty, with the slogan Vandemataram - Manade Rajyam, were triggered by
o: the arrest of S.N. Banerjee in 1906
the annulment of the partition of Bengal in 1911
the formation of the Bala Bharati Samiti in 1907
the Madras Beach students' meeting of 1905

nb9164d2b3d0.tq: Trigger in Andhra = S.N. Banerjee's arrest, 1906
xs: The protests were triggered by **the arrest of S.N. Banerjee in 1906** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The slogan was **"Vandemataram - Manade Rajyam"**.
The **Madras Beach** meeting (**Sep 1905**) began the movement; the **Bala Bharati Samiti** came in **Feb 1907**; the annulment in **1911**.

n19c6fddbf10.s: The first criminal case of the Swadeshi movement in Andhra arose from the:
n19c6fddbf10.x: The Kakinada Riot Case of 31 May 1907 was described as the first criminal case of the movement in Andhra.

The **Swarajya case** produced the first **Telugu political prisoners**.

nd1da547da43.s: In the Kakinada Riot Case of 31 May 1907, which building was attacked?
nd1da547da43.x: After Dr Kemp beat Kompelli Krishna Rao for shouting Vande Mataram, the European Club at Kakinada was attacked.

**Nyapati Subbarao** defended the accused.

nfeef60224f6.s: In the Swarajya case (1908), Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao and Bodi Narayana Rao were arrested for an article praising:

He had earlier been expelled after the **Rajahmundry College incident** (**1907**) and barred from government jobs.
**Andhra Kesari** is listed as a separate Andhra paper.

n0a35f82b096.s: Who defended the accused in the Tenali Bomb Case (1909)?
n0a35f82b096.x: Prakasam defended Chukkapalli Ramayya and others in the Tenali case; Nyapati Subbarao defended the Kakinada Riot Case accused.

**Prakasam** was a member of the **Bala Bharati Samiti**.
**Kotappakonda** (**18 Feb 1909**) came shortly before.

nindian-history-119-18.s: Which newspaper is associated with Bal Gangadhar Tilak?
nindian-history-119-18.x: Kesari is linked with Tilak, along with the Ganpati Festival and Gita Rahasya.
n: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was associated with the Ganpati Festival. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Bal Gangadhar Tilak was associated with Kesari. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]

Lala Lajpat Rai suffered a lathi-charge injury during the Simon Commission protest. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Bal Gangadhar Tilak was associated with Swaraj, festivals and newspapers. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
xa: Tilak started **Ganeshotsav** (**1893**) and the **Shivaji festival** (**1895**).
Tilak's other paper: **Mahratta** (**1881**).
Tilak is called "**Lokmanya**".

n92c8f0a51a4.s: The Moderate campaign against the partition of Bengal (1903-1905) relied mainly on:
n92c8f0a51a4.x: The campaign led by S.N. Banerjee, K.K. Mitra and Prithwishchandra Ray used petitions and meetings, and failed to prevent the partition.

**S.N. Banerjee** and **A.M. Bose** raised **Rs 50,000** for funds.
The **Extremists** took control from **1906**.

n4cbc25f6761.s: National Handloom Day has been observed on 7 August since:
n4cbc25f6761.x: National Handloom Day has been observed on 7 August since 2015, commemorating the Swadeshi proclamation at Calcutta Town Hall.
