xs: **National Handloom Day** has been observed on **7 August** since **2015** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The date recalls the Swadeshi proclamation at **Calcutta Town Hall** on **7 Aug 1905** (APPSC 2019).
xa: The mass **Swadeshi vow** was taken on **16 Oct 1905**.
Handloom revival was part of Swadeshi, alongside **Mohini Mills**.
**Munagala Raja**'s textile unit at **Vijayawada** (**June 1906**) was the first in the Madras Presidency.

nfabbf39d6fe.s: The principal targets of the Swadeshi boycott were foreign cloth, foreign salt and foreign:
nfabbf39d6fe.x: The boycott targeted foreign cloth, salt and sugar, while indigenous handloom goods were encouraged.
xa: Boycott extended to **courts, schools, government service**.
Priests refused rituals and marriages using **foreign goods**.
**Swadeshi / Atmashakti** stood for self-reliance.

n702d583479c.s: What name was given in Andhra Pradesh to the movement associated with the Swadeshi upsurge and the use of the Vande Mataram slogan?
n702d583479c.x: In Andhra, the Swadeshi-related agitation was popularly known as the Vandemataram Movement.
n702d583479c.tq: Use the exact regional name instead of a broader national movement label.
xs: In Andhra the Swadeshi upsurge was called the **Vandemataram Movement** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Its Andhra phase is placed in **1906-1911**.
The **Andhra Mahasabha** era and **Home Rule** branches came **later**, led by the same men.
xa: Trigger: **Surendranath Banerjee's arrest** (**1906**) → protests at **Rajahmundry**, **Kakinada**, **Vizianagaram**, **Gooty**.
Slogan: **"Vandemataram - Manade Rajyam"**.
It was the **first mass political awakening** in Andhra.

n317ea9178d6.s: Which slogan was raised during the protests that followed Surendranath Banerjee's arrest in Andhra?
n317ea9178d6.x: The protesters raised the slogan “Vandemataram - Manade Rajyam,” meaning that self-rule belonged to them.
n317ea9178d6.tq: Discriminate the Andhra-specific slogan from other famous nationalist slogans.
xs: The protesters raised **"Vandemataram - Manade Rajyam"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The protests followed **Surendranath Banerjee's arrest** in **1906**.
xa: Protests broke out at **Rajahmundry**, **Kakinada**, **Vizianagaram** and **Gooty**.
**"Vande Mataram"** itself became a greeting; official curbs on it led to the **Rajahmundry** and **Kakinada** incidents.
Pal's line in Andhra: **"Swaraj the goal, boycott the weapon"**.

n572e976bd60.s: In 1906, which two organisations were established in Madras to promote Swadeshi activities?
o: A Swadeshi Store and a National School
A Bala Bharathi Samiti and a Swarajya Samiti
An Industrial Association and a Swadeshi League
A National College and a Young Men's Association
n572e976bd60.x: Madras had an Industrial Association to promote Swadeshi goods and a Swadeshi League in 1906.
n572e976bd60.tq: Identify the paired institutions associated with the same year and place.
xs: In **1906** Madras set up **an Industrial Association and a Swadeshi League** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Industrial Association aimed **to promote Swadeshi goods**.
The **Bala Bharathi Samiti** and the **Godavari Swadeshi Store** were at **Rajahmundry**.
xa: ⚠ **Madras** (**1906**) = Industrial Association + Swadeshi League; **Rajahmundry** (**1907**) = Godavari Swadeshi Store.
**Nyapathi Subbarao** and **K. Venkataramana Rao** toured Andhra for Swadeshi.
Many young Andhras went to **Japan** for industrial training.

n8c602bc3f7a.s: Which Andhra work was inspired by Japan's victory over Russia in 1905?
n8c602bc3f7a.x: Japan's victory over Russia inspired Adipudi Somanatha Rao's Japan Charitra (and the play Japaniyam).
xa: The victory is dated **1905** (some notes say **1908**).
**Munagala Raja** named his sons **Togo and Nogi**.
**Japan Charitra** was written by **Adipudi Somanatha Rao**.

n85a4272873b.s: Official restrictions on the use of 'Vande Mataram' contributed to the incidents at:
n85a4272873b.x: Official restrictions on 'Vande Mataram', which had become a popular greeting, contributed to the Rajahmundry and Kakinada incidents.
xa: At Rajahmundry, **Mark Hunter** banned **Vandemataram badges** and the slogan.
The **Kakinada riots case** was the **first criminal case** of the movement (APPSC 2019 key).
In **1906** Madras set up an **Industrial Association** and a **Swadeshi League**.

n0e9a41542d3.s: What was the title of Bipin Chandra Pal's final speech at Machilipatnam?
n0e9a41542d3.x: Pal delivered his final speech, titled Matru Murthi, at Machilipatnam on 27 April 1907.
n0e9a41542d3.tq: Distinguish the title of a speech from titles of seditious writings and books.
xs: Pal's final speech at **Machilipatnam** was **"Matru Murthi"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was on **27 Apr** **1907**; the **Young Men's Swarajya Samiti** was formed there.
**"Viparita Buddhi"** was Gadicherla's **Swarajya** article; **Japan Charitra** is **Adipudi Somanatha Rao**'s book.
xa: Pal laid the foundation stone of the **National College** there in **1907**.
Host: **Kompalle Hanumantha Rao** (APPSC 2008 key).
Some notes name Brahmo **Ramadasu Naidu** as host.

ndeff30f2bb7.s: Which of the following best represents Bipin Chandra Pal's political message during his Andhra tour?
o: National schools were unnecessary if Swadeshi stores were established.
Swaraj was the goal, boycott was the weapon, and organisation had to reach the village level.
Swaraj could be achieved only through government employment and legislative petitions.
The movement should remain confined to major urban centres.
ndeff30f2bb7.x: Pal presented Swaraj as the goal, boycott as the weapon, and stressed village-level organisation and national schools.
ndeff30f2bb7.tq: Apply the stated programme to identify the option containing the complete and accurate set of principles.
xs: Pal's message was **"Swaraj the goal, boycott the weapon"** with **village-level organisation** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He also called for **national schools**.
xa: At **Kakinada** he spoke on **Vedanta** and **Swadeshi-Swaraj**.
On **23 Apr** at **Rajahmundry** he spoke on **national education**.
His visit to Machilipatnam led to a **national school committee** → **Andhra Jateeya Kalasala**.

nfcb89ff6ce9.s: Who hosted Bipin Chandra Pal at Machilipatnam in April 1907?
nfcb89ff6ce9.x: Kompalle Hanumantha Rao hosted Pal at Machilipatnam (APPSC 2008 key); Perraju presided at Kakinada, Gadicherla at Rajahmundry, Munagala Raja at Vijayawada.
xa: Vijayawada co-host: **Nayani Venkata Rangarao**.
At Rajahmundry Pal stayed at **Madella Sourayya's** house.
Exam angle: pairing a town with its **host** or **organising body**.

n86dab869465.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Vandemataram movement in Andhra?
o: It marked the first mass political awakening in Andhra
Student politics in Andhra began in this context
National education and Swadeshi stores began in this context
It remained confined to elite meetings with no student dimension
n86dab869465.x: The movement was linked with national education, Swadeshi stores and student politics, so it was not confined to elite meetings.
xa: The Rajahmundry incident marked the **active entry of Andhra students**.
It fed into the **Andhra Mahasabha** era and **Home Rule** branches.
The **Andhra Jateeya Kalasala** came up in **1910**.

n50a832bb41a.s: Which of the following is regarded as the first Telugu national song?
n50a832bb41a.x: 'Hinduvulara ennaall ee gati' by Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham, the first Telugu national poet, is the first Telugu national song. 'Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi yaavu' was his poem composed on the spot during Pal's tour; 'Vandemataram - Manade Rajyam' was a protest slogan; Matru Murthi was Pal's final speech at Machilipatnam.
n50a832bb41a.tq: Chilakamarti: first national poet + first national song
xs: **"Hinduvulara ennaall ee gati"** is the **first Telugu national song** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was by **Chilakamarti**, the first Telugu national poet.
**"Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi yaavu"** was his poem during Pal's tour; **"Vandemataram - Manade Rajyam"** was a slogan; **"Matru Murthi"** was Pal's final speech.
xa: Chilakamarti edited **Desamata** and translated Pal's speeches.
Pal gave "Matru Murthi" at **Machilipatnam** (**27 Apr**).
FIRST/LAST: First Telugu national poet — **Chilakamarti**.

n26e00cd94fe.s: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham edited which journal at Rajahmundry?
n26e00cd94fe.x: Chilakamarti edited Desamata at Rajahmundry and translated Bipin Chandra Pal's speeches.
xa: He composed **"Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi yaavu"** on the spot.
**"Hinduvulara ennaall ee gati"** = first Telugu national song.
He is called the **first Telugu national poet**.

n8e8f4fa66ef.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was associated with which of the following combination of roles?
o: Editor of Swarajya, leader at Bandar, and leader of the Rajahmundry student protest
Editor of Krishna Patrika, leader at Vizianagaram, and translator of Pal's speeches
Editor of Desamata, leader at Guntur, and founder of Krishna Patrika
Editor of Andhra Kesari, leader at Vijayawada, and founder of Desamata
n8e8f4fa66ef.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao edited Swarajya, was a leader at Bandar, and led the Rajahmundry student protest.
n8e8f4fa66ef.tq: Keep the three linked roles together and avoid swapping newspapers or regional centres.
xs: Gadicherla was **editor of Swarajya**, a **Bandar** leader and leader of the **Rajahmundry student protest** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Desamata** was **Chilakamarti**'s; **Krishna Patrika** was **Mutnuri Krishna Rao**'s.
xa: He started the Telugu weekly **Swarajya** in **1908**.
His article **"Viparita Buddhi"** brought **3 years' rigorous imprisonment**.
He welcomed **Pal** at **Rajahmundry**.

ne79664acfc2.s: Bipin Chandra Pal's April 1907 tour of Andhra followed an appeal for an Extremist leader made in Krishna Patrika by
ne79664acfc2.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao appealed in Krishna Patrika for an Extremist leader, and standard notes name him as organiser of the tour (the APPSC 2011 key names Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao - know both). Perraju presided at Kakinada, Pal stayed at Madella Sourayya's house in Rajahmundry, and Nayani Venkata Rangarao co-hosted him at Vijayawada.
ne79664acfc2.tq: Krishna Patrika -> Mutnuri Krishna Rao invited Pal
xs: **Mutnuri Krishna Rao** appealed in **Krishna Patrika** for an Extremist leader — so option **(1)** is correct.
Standard notes name him as organiser; the **APPSC 2011 key** names **Gadicherla** — know both.
**Kattiventi Perraju** presided at **Kakinada**; **Madella Sourayya** housed Pal at Rajahmundry; **Nayani Venkata Rangarao** co-hosted at **Vijayawada**.
xa: Some notes say the tour was confirmed by the **Bala Bharathi Samiti**.
The tour ran **16-27 April 1907**.
Pal's line: **"Swaraj the goal, boycott the weapon"**.

n2bd62718575.s: Who wrote the Andhra-related work Japan Charitra?
n2bd62718575.x: Adipudi Somanatha Rao wrote Japan Charitra in the context of the inspiration created by Japan’s victory over Russia.
n2bd62718575.tq: Match the author with the work rather than with a related contemporary.
xs: **Adipudi Somanatha Rao** wrote **Japan Charitra** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Munagala Raja** named his sons **Togo and Nogi**; **Gadicherla** edited **Swarajya**; **Chilakamarti** edited **Desamata**.
xa: The play **Japaniyam** also reflected the Japan link.
Many young Andhras went to **Japan** for **industrial training**.
Munagala Raja co-hosted **Pal** at **Vijayawada**.

ncaadea08bb5.s: Who started the Telugu weekly Swarajya in 1908?
ncaadea08bb5.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao started the Telugu weekly Swarajya in 1908.
ncaadea08bb5.tq: Match the publication with its founder rather than with a political organiser or student leader.
xs: **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** started the Telugu weekly **Swarajya** in **1908** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is placed at **Vijayawada**.
**Adipudi Somanatha Rao** wrote **Japan Charitra**; **Mutnuri Krishna Rao** ran **Krishna Patrika**.
xa: His article **"Viparita Buddhi"** led to a **sedition** charge.
He received **3 years' rigorous imprisonment**.
⚠ **Swarajya** = Gadicherla; **Desamata** = Chilakamarti.

n2770eae9501.s: Who is regarded as the first Telugu national poet of the Vandemataram era?
n2770eae9501.x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham is regarded as the first Telugu national poet.
xs: **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham** is the **first Telugu national poet** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Gadicherla** was an editor and student leader, not the poet.
xa: His **"Hinduvulara ennaall ee gati"** is the **first Telugu national song**.
He composed **"Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi yaavu"** during Pal's visit.
He edited **Desamata** at **Rajahmundry**.

n0f96630a266.s: What was the immediate action taken by Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao in defiance of the Rajahmundry college authorities?
o: He founded the Godavari Swadeshi Store.
He organised a bomb attack on a railway train.
He delivered the final speech Matru Murthi.
He presented an address to Bipin Chandra Pal.
n0f96630a266.x: Gadicherla defied Principal Mark Hunter by presenting an address to Bipin Chandra Pal. J. Ramachandra Rao co-organised the action.
n0f96630a266.tq: Identify the specific act of defiance rather than a later or unrelated movement activity.
xs: Gadicherla defied the college by **presenting an address to Bipin Chandra Pal** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**J. Ramachandra Rao** co-organised it.
The **Godavari Swadeshi Store** was **Karanam Guneswara Rao**'s; **"Matru Murthi"** was **Pal**'s speech.
xa: Gadicherla was **dismissed** and **blacklisted** from government jobs.
The incident marked the **active entry of Andhra students** into the freedom struggle.
He later started **Swarajya** (**1908**).

n5f14982ffd7.s: After the Rajahmundry college Vandemataram incident, 138 students were:
o: debarred from examinations for one year
debarred from examinations for two years
n5f14982ffd7.x: A total of 138 students were debarred from examinations for two years after the incident.
xa: The ban was imposed by Principal **Mark Hunter**.
The only death sentence was **Chinnapa Reddy**'s, at **Kotappakonda**.
The incident marked the **active entry of Andhra students**.

nap-history-46-3.s: Mark Hunter, whose 1907 ban on Vandemataram badges sparked student protest, was Principal of:
nap-history-46-3.x: The 1907 incident took place at Rajahmundry College, whose Principal was Mark Hunter, not at National College, Machilipatnam.
n: An incident in 1907 marked the beginning of student participation in the freedom struggle from Andhra Pradesh. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 57-57]
Mark Hunter was the principal associated with the 1907 student-participation incident. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 57-57]
National College was located in Machilipatnam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 57-57]
xa: Hunter banned **Vandemataram badges**; **138** students were debarred from exams for **two** years.
**Gadicherla Harisarvothama Rao**, a teacher trainee, was dismissed and blacklisted from government jobs.
National College, Machilipatnam: **1910**, president **Konda Venkatappaiah**.

nca3fde641dc.s: Which institution later became Jadavpur University?
nca3fde641dc.x: The National Council of Education, established on 15 August 1906, later became Jadavpur University.
nca3fde641dc.tq: Match an institution with its later institutional identity.
xs: The **National Council of Education** later became **Jadavpur University** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was set up on **15 Aug 1906**.
The **Bengal Technical Institute** (**1906**) was **Taraknath Palit**'s; **Andhra Jateeya Kalasala** is at **Machilipatnam**.
xa: The **Rajahmundry school** was affiliated to the **Bengal national education** body.
Andhra national institutions also came up at **Ongole** and **Kadapa**.
**Vivekananda Vidyalayam**, **Kavali**, was **Oruganti Venkatasubbayya**'s.

n3106f1a70f1.s: Who toured Andhra to popularise Swadeshi activities in the early phase of the movement?
o: Mutnuri Krishna Rao and T. Prakasam
Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao and J. Ramachandra Rao
Nyapathi Subbarao and K. Venkataramana Rao
Karanam Guneswara Rao and Kattiventi Perraju
n3106f1a70f1.x: Nyapathi Subbarao and K. Venkataramana Rao toured Andhra to popularise Swadeshi activities.
n3106f1a70f1.tq: Test the persons associated with propagation, not those associated with later institutions or trials.
xs: **Nyapathi Subbarao and K. Venkataramana Rao** toured Andhra to popularise Swadeshi — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Gadicherla** and **J. Ramachandra Rao** led the **Rajahmundry** student defiance; **Guneswara Rao** and **Kattiventi Perraju** backed national schools.
xa: Nyapati Subbarao was **president** of the **Andhra Jateeya Kalasala** (APPSC 2017 key).
He inaugurated the **Ramachandrapuram** National School.
In **1906** Madras formed an **Industrial Association** and a **Swadeshi League**.

nd408adc148f.s: Who was the president of the Andhra Jateeya Kalasala, Machilipatnam?
nd408adc148f.x: Nyapati Subbarao was president of the Andhra Jateeya Kalasala, set up at Machilipatnam in 1910 on a foundation stone laid by Pal in 1907.
xa: **Kattiventi Perraju** gave land worth **Rs 40,000** for the **Ramachandrapuram** school.
It is also called **"Bandaru National College"**.
Pal's visit led to a **national school committee** → the Kalasala.

n7fcbf04091a.s: The National School of the Swadeshi period in Andhra was located at:
n7fcbf04091a.x: The National School was at Ramachandrapuram; the Godavari Swadeshi Store was at Rajahmundry and the Andhra Jateeya Kalasala at Machilipatnam.
xa: The Store was set up by **Karanam Guneswara Rao** (**1907**) and inaugurated by **Pal**.
The Ramachandrapuram school was inaugurated by **Nyapathi Subbarao** as a true "National School".
The Kalasala came in **1910**, with **Kompalle Hanumantha Rao** as first principal.

n76783e18452.s: Who gave land worth Rs 40,000 for the National School at Ramachandrapuram?
n76783e18452.x: Kattiventi Perraju gave land worth Rs 40,000, while Guneswara Rao donated Rs 1,000.
xa: The school was hailed as a true **"National School"**.
Guneswara Rao also set up the **Godavari Swadeshi Store** (**1907**).
Perraju presided over Pal's lectures at **Kakinada** (**17 Apr**).

nc39263bf1d0.s: Which one of the following leaders belonged to the militant (Extremist) school of nationalism?
nc39263bf1d0.x: Tilak was the militant leader (APPSC-GS 2018 key). Ranade, Gokhale and G.V. Joshi were Moderates - the trap is to mark any of them as militant.
nc39263bf1d0.tq: Militant = Tilak; Ranade, Gokhale, Joshi = Moderates
xs: **B.G. Tilak** belonged to the militant (Extremist) school — so option **(4)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2018).
⚠ Trap: **Ranade**, **Gokhale** and **G.V. Joshi** were **not** militant.
xa: Other Extremists: **Lajpat Rai**, **Pal**, **Aurobindo**.
The Extremist phase is dated **1905-1916**.
Tilak led the Extremists at **Surat 1907** against **Gokhale**.

n828011e0cab.s: Atmashakti, in the context of extremist ideology, referred to:
n828011e0cab.x: Atmashakti meant self-reliance. It was connected with constructive work such as the establishment of cooperatives.
n828011e0cab.tq: Match the indigenous term with its precise ideological meaning.
xs: **Atmashakti** meant **self-reliance** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was expressed through constructive work such as **cooperatives**.
xa: The Extremists' **3 Ss**: **self-reliance, self-sacrifice, strong will**.
Other methods: **boycott**, **Swadeshi**, **national education**.
Extremist base: **students, women, workers, peasants**.

n8c74e6c5418.s: After the Surat Split, the Moderates and Extremists reunited at:
n8c74e6c5418.x: The reunion came at Lucknow in 1916, not in 1908; the split was followed by repression, the Newspapers Act of 1908 and Tilak's imprisonment.
xa: Other 1908 Acts: **Criminal Law Amendment Act** and **Explosive Substances Act**.
Bengal leaders **Ashwini Kumar Dutt** and **K.K. Mitra** were deported in **1908**.
**Gadicherla** was jailed in **1908** in Andhra.

n0f4f6a7604c.s: Tilak's Home Rule League was founded on:
n0f4f6a7604c.x: Tilak began his league on 28 April 1916; Besant's followed in September 1916.
xa: Tilak's league: president **Joseph Baptista**, secretary **N.C. Kelkar**.
**52 Home Rule branches** existed in **Andhra by 1917**.
Besant ran **New India** (the renamed **Madras Standard**) and **Commonweal (Jan 1914)**.
Under the Press Act Besant paid **Rs 2,000** security, then **Rs 10,000** more, to keep publishing.

n6aa9e949ceb.s: The Extremists contributed to the national movement by:
o: turning nationalism into a mass movement and making Swaraj its goal
supporting permanent British control over India
restricting nationalism to educated constitutional petitioners
n6aa9e949ceb.x: The Extremists broadened nationalism into a mass movement and placed Swaraj at the centre of the political goal.
n6aa9e949ceb.tq: Identify the principal historical significance rather than a method or criticism.
xs: The Extremists **turned nationalism into a mass movement** and **made Swaraj the goal** — so option **(1)** is correct.
They took politics to **students, women, workers and peasants**, beyond the Moderates' **urban educated elite**.
They used **Swadeshi, boycott and national education** — so (3) is wrong; and **Swaraj** meant complete freedom, not British control — so (2) is wrong.
Restricting politics to petitions (the **3 Ps**) was the **Moderates'** method — so (4) is wrong.
xa: Extremist methods = **3 Ss**: **self-reliance, self-sacrifice, strong will**; plus mass agitation.
**Spiritual nationalism**: nation as mother goddess (**Bande Mataram**, **Bhavani Mandir**); Hindu festivals for mass contact.
**Atmashakti** (self-reliance): constructive work such as **cooperatives**.
⚠ **3 Ps** (prayers, petitions, protests) = Moderates; **3 Ss** = Extremists.

nindian-history-119-1.s: What was the main objective of the Extremists or Assertive Nationalists?
o: Swaraj or complete independence from English rule
nindian-history-119-1.x: The Extremists, or Assertive Nationalists, aimed at Swaraj, meaning complete independence from British rule. Constitutional agitation, negotiation and gradual self-government were Moderate ideas.
nindian-history-119-1.tq: Discriminate Extremist goals from Moderate goals.
n: The main objective of the Extremists was Swaraj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Swaraj meant complete independence from English rule. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Extremists lacked faith in Moderate negotiations with the British. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Moderate goal was gradual self-government. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Moderate strategy was constitutional agitation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Moderates initially had faith in British liberalism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Extremists were also called Assertive Nationalists. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
xs: The Extremists' main objective was **Swaraj** — **complete independence** from **English rule** — option **(3)**.
**Constitutional agitation**, **negotiations** and **gradual self-government** belong to the **Moderates**.
The Extremists **lacked faith** in Moderate **negotiations** with the British.
xa: Extremists are also called **Assertive Nationalists**; their **influence increased** after **1906**.
Extremist **Swaraj** meant **complete freedom** from British control, not colonial self-government.
Key leaders: **Tilak**, **Lajpat Rai**, **Bipin Chandra Pal**, **Aurobindo Ghosh**.

nindian-history-119-15.x: The Moderates sought gradual self-government through constitutional agitation; the Extremists sought Swaraj.
n: The Moderate goal was gradual self-government. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Moderate strategy was constitutional agitation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]

nindian-history-119-16.x: It was the Extremists who wanted to widen the Swadeshi-Boycott movement; the Moderates were reluctant.
n: The Extremists had increasing distrust of British rule. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Moderates were less willing to extend the Swadeshi–Boycott movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Extremists wanted a wider and extended Swadeshi–Boycott movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Extremists supported Swadeshi and Boycott. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
The Extremists wanted to extend the Swadeshi and Boycott movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
xa: Surat **1907**: Extremists demanded **boycott** extended to all of India; Moderates wanted it kept to **Bengal**.
Moderates initially had **faith** in **British liberalism**.
Extremist attitude: **No faith in British generosity**.

nindian-history-119-30.s: The Moderates and Extremists split at the Surat session of the INC in:
nindian-history-119-30.x: At Surat in 1907 the Moderates and Extremists split over leadership, methods, strategy and the Swadeshi-Boycott programme.
n: Leadership was a major issue in the Surat Split. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Methods were a major issue in the Surat Split. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Congress strategy was a major issue in the Surat Split. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
Swadeshi–Boycott was a major issue in the Surat Split. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #119 · pp 215-218]
xa: Surat **1907** president: **Rash Behari Ghosh** (Moderates' choice).
After the split: **Naram Dal** = Moderates; **Garam Dal** = Extremists.
The split **healed at Lucknow in 1916**.
Cause per UPSC **2016** key: Extremists' lack of faith in Moderates' capacity to negotiate.

n2d8d3ce8c87.s: Which one of the following Acts was enacted in 1908 to deal with incitement to offences through newspapers?
n2d8d3ce8c87.x: The Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act was enacted in 1908. The Indian Press Act followed in 1910.
n2d8d3ce8c87.tq: Distinguish similarly named press and security laws by their exact titles and years.
xs: The **Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act** was passed in **1908** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Explosive Substances Act** was also **1908** but aimed at explosives; the **Seditious Meetings Act** was **1907**; the **Indian Press Act** **1910**.
xa: The **Criminal Law Amendment Act** came in **1908** too.
Tilak was sent to **Mandalay** in **1908**.
**Gadicherla** was jailed in **1908**.

n266091702d5.s: The Indian Press Act was enacted in:
n266091702d5.x: The Indian Press Act was enacted in 1910, following the Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act of 1908.
xa: **By 1910** the Extremist leadership was out of action and the **Moderates dominated**.
Aurobindo retired to **Pondicherry** in **1910**.
Under the Press Act, **Besant** was asked for **Rs 2,000** security, then **Rs 10,000** more.

n453c297cc74.s: On social reform, the Extremists were, compared with the Moderates:
n453c297cc74.x: The Moderates were generally pro-reform while the Extremists were comparatively orthodox; Tilak opposed the Age of Consent Bill.
xa: Criticism: the Extremists' **religious symbolism alienated Muslims**.
Extremists used **Hindu festivals** for mass contact.
The **Surat Split** weakened the Congress.

nac8820a89eb.s: A basic cause of the Surat Split of 1907 was:
o: the Extremists' lack of faith in the Moderates' capacity to negotiate with the British
the annulment of the partition of Bengal
the founding of the Home Rule Leagues
nac8820a89eb.x: The Extremists lacked faith in the Moderates' capacity to negotiate with the British (UPSC 2016). The partition was annulled in 1911 and the Home Rule Leagues came in 1916, after Surat.
xa: ⚠ Order check: **INC 1885 → Bengal partition 1905 → Muslim League 1906 → Surat 1907**.
The printed key "b, d, a, c" was a trap; true order = **d-b-a-c**.
The split healed at **Lucknow in 1916**.

n470fc50ad20.s: Which one of the following events took place in 1911?
o: The Partition of Bengal was annulled
The Tilak Home Rule League was founded
n470fc50ad20.x: The Partition of Bengal was annulled in 1911. Tilak was released in 1914, the Lucknow Pact was concluded in 1916, and the Tilak Home Rule League began in 1916.
n470fc50ad20.tq: Discriminate among closely spaced chronological milestones.
xs: In **1911** the **Partition of Bengal was annulled** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Lucknow Pact** came in **December 1916**.
**Tilak's Home Rule League** was founded on **28 Apr 1916**.
**Tilak was released** from Mandalay on **16 June 1914**.
xa: The Partition itself and the **Swadeshi Movement (7 Aug)** date from **1905**.
**1908**: Tilak to Mandalay and the **Newspapers Act**.
**Besant's Home Rule League** followed in **September 1916**.
The Congress **reunion** at **Lucknow (1916)** healed the **Surat Split** of **1907**.

n1280bbe2f53.s: The Simla Deputation led by Aga Khan III met Lord Minto on:
n1280bbe2f53.x: The Simla Deputation, led by Aga Khan III, met Lord Minto on 1 October 1906.
n1280bbe2f53.tq: Separate two closely connected 1906 dates by linking each to its event.
xs: The **Simla Deputation** led by **Aga Khan III** met **Lord Minto** on **1 October 1906** — option **(2)**.
**30 December 1906** was the founding of the **Muslim League** at **Dacca**.
**12 December 1911** = annulment of partition at the **Delhi Durbar**; **20 August 1917** = **August Declaration**.
xa: It demanded **separate electorates** and **weightage** for Muslims.
⚠ **1 Oct 1906** = Simla Deputation; **30 Dec 1906** = League founded (Dacca).
Aga Khan became the League's **first president**.
The demand was met by the **Indian Councils Act 1909**.

naad3a546ef6.s: The Simla Deputation of 1906 demanded which of the following for Muslims?
naad3a546ef6.x: The deputation demanded separate electorates and weightage, citing the Muslims' contribution to the defence of the Empire.
xa: Led by **Aga Khan (III)** to **Lord Minto** on **1 October 1906**.
**Weightage** = more seats than the community's population share.
The **1909 Act** granted **separate electorates with weightage** — its most critical feature.
The **Muslim League** followed on **30 Dec 1906** at Dacca.

nf05e480d056.s: The formation of the All India Muslim League at Dacca in 1906 was proposed by:
nf05e480d056.x: Nawab Salimullah proposed the League on 30 December 1906; Aga Khan was its first president and Syed Ameer Ali set up the London branch.
xa: Early aims: **loyalty to the British Empire**, safeguarding Muslim interests, keeping Muslims away from the Congress.
**Jinnah** joined the League in **1913**.
The **Simla Deputation (1 Oct 1906)** preceded the League's founding.

nb94676b9623.s: The Congress-League alliance was forged at which Congress session?
nb94676b9623.x: The 1916 Lucknow session saw the Congress-League alliance (Lucknow Pact), the Moderate-Extremist reunion and Tilak's return.
xa: Congress president: **Ambika Charan Majumdar**; League president: **Jinnah**.
Brokers: **Tilak + Jinnah**; Annie Besant also worked for it.
**1916** = high point of **Congress-League unity**.
Limit: the two still held **separate annual sessions**.

n5fbb6c1ea08.s: Muhammad Ali Jinnah joined the All-India Muslim League in
n5fbb6c1ea08.x: Jinnah joined the Muslim League in 1913, although he was also associated with the Congress-League cooperation that culminated in the Lucknow Pact.
n5fbb6c1ea08.tq: Use the close-year discrimination method for a sequence of League milestones.
xs: **Jinnah** joined the Muslim League in **1913** — option **(3)**.
**1906** = League founded; **1909** = Morley-Minto Reforms; **1916** = Jinnah presided the **Lucknow League session**.
xa: Jinnah and **Tilak** brokered the **Lucknow Pact**.
He belonged to the League's **"Young Party"** with the **Ali Brothers**.
**1940**: **Lahore Resolution** demanding independent states for Muslims.

nbd6c9658192.s: Who presided over the Muslim League session held at Lucknow in 1916?
nbd6c9658192.x: Muhammad Ali Jinnah presided over the Muslim League session at Lucknow in 1916.
nbd6c9658192.tq: Match the session with its presiding leader and avoid substituting later ideological figures.
xs: **Muhammad Ali Jinnah** presided the **League's Lucknow 1916** session — option **(3)**.
**Aga Khan** was the League's **first president** (**1906**); **Iqbal** gave the **Allahabad address (1930)**; **Rahmat Ali** coined **"PAKISTAN" (1933)**.
xa: ⚠ Congress president at Lucknow 1916: **Ambika Charan Majumdar**.
Jinnah joined the League in **1913**.
He co-brokered the Pact with **Tilak**.

n18ed953e745.s: The August Declaration relating to India's constitutional development was made on:
n18ed953e745.x: The August Declaration was made on 20 August 1917.
n18ed953e745.tq: Distinguish the date of the declaration from the dates of later mass movements and reforms.
xs: The **August Declaration** was made on **20 August 1917** — option **(2)**.
**12 Dec 1911** = partition annulled; **13 April 1919** = **Jallianwala Bagh**; **1 Jan 1923** = **Swaraj Party**.
xa: **1919**: Rowlatt Act and the **Government of India Act**.
**1920**: Khilafat and Non-Cooperation.
The **1919 Act** introduced **dyarchy in the provinces**.

n3b339110742.s: The annulment of the partition of Bengal was announced at the Delhi Durbar on:
n3b339110742.x: At the Delhi Durbar of 12 December 1911 the annulment was announced through King George V and the capital moved from Calcutta to Delhi.
xa: The partition and **Swadeshi** began in **1905**.
**1907** Surat Split; **1917** August Declaration.
Lord Minto's tenure ended in **1910**.

n6abe18dcbe6.s: An All-India Federation was prescribed by the:
n6abe18dcbe6.x: The 1935 Act prescribed an All-India Federation; the 1919 Act introduced provincial dyarchy and bicameralism at the Centre.
xa: **1935** also gave **provincial autonomy** and **dyarchy at the Centre**.
**1909** introduced **separate electorates** for Muslims.
⚠ Montagu-Chelmsford = **1919**, not 1929 (wrong pair in APPSC-G1 **2019**).
Pitt's India Act = **1784**.

nindian-history-115-11.s: The Muslim League observed Direct Action Day on:
nindian-history-115-11.x: Direct Action Day was observed on 16 August 1946, leading to large riots in Calcutta.
n: The Direct Action Day dates to 1946. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #115 · pp 210-211]
Direct Action Day occurred on 16 August. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #115 · pp 210-211]
xa: **1940** — **Lahore Resolution**, independent states for Muslims.
**1946** — the League also won the Muslim seats.
**1937-39** — League alleged "**Hindu Raj**" under Congress ministries.

nindian-history-115-17.s: In which year did the Muslim League pass the Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution?
nindian-history-115-17.x: The League was founded in 1906, held its first session in 1907, passed the Lahore Resolution in 1940 and observed Direct Action Day in 1946.
n: The Muslim League was established in 1906. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #115 · pp 210-211]
The first session of the Muslim League was held in Karachi in 1907. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #115 · pp 210-211]
The first session of the Muslim League was its first annual session. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #115 · pp 210-211]
The Lahore/Pakistan Resolution dates to 1940. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #115 · pp 210-211]
The Direct Action Day dates to 1946. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #115 · pp 210-211]
xa: **1930** — **Iqbal** proposed a Muslim state in the NW (Allahabad address).
**1933** — **Chaudhry Rahmat Ali** coined "**PAKISTAN**".
Direct Action Day: **16 August 1946**.

nindian-history-115-20.x: The Lahore Resolution of 1940 demanded separate independent states for Muslims, hence the name Pakistan Resolution.
n: The Muslim League was established to protect Muslim political interests. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #115 · pp 210-211]
The Lucknow Pact was a Congress–League agreement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #115 · pp 210-211]
The Lahore/Pakistan Resolution dates to 1940. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #115 · pp 210-211]
The Lahore/Pakistan Resolution involved a separate state demand. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #115 · pp 210-211]
xa: ⚠ Muslim state idea = **Iqbal** (**1930**); the name "PAKISTAN" = **Chaudhry Rahmat Ali** (**1933**).
**Liaquat Ali Khan** — the **Pakistan movement**.
**Direct Action Day** followed on **16 August 1946**.

nindian-history-120-12.s: Who moved the Lahore Resolution at the Muslim League session of March 1940?
nindian-history-120-12.x: A.K. Fazlul Haq, Premier of Bengal, moved the Lahore Resolution in 1940; Jinnah presided over the session. The Aga Khan was the League's first President and Liaquat Ali Khan became Pakistan's first Prime Minister.
nindian-history-120-12.tq: Separate the mover of the resolution from the session's president.
n: Muhammad Ali Jinnah was associated with the Muslim League. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
Muhammad Ali Jinnah was associated with the Lahore Resolution. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
Muhammad Ali Jinnah was associated with the Pakistan demand. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
A.K. Fazlul Haq was associated with the Lahore Resolution. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
xs: The **Lahore Resolution** is associated with **A.K. Fazlul Haq** — option **(4)**.
**Jinnah** is associated with the League, the Lahore Resolution and the **Pakistan demand**.
**Aga Khan** was the League's **first President**; **Liaquat Ali Khan** is linked with the **Pakistan movement**.
xa: The Lahore Resolution (**1940**) demanded **independent states** for Muslims.
**Nawab Salimullah** proposed the formation of the League (**1906**).
**Direct Action Day**: **16 August 1946**.

n49041e70b94.s: Who is associated with the description 'Father of the Communal Electorate'?
n49041e70b94.x: Lord Minto is associated with the title 'Father of the Communal Electorate' because the Morley-Minto Reforms introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
n49041e70b94.tq: Link the popular epithet to the reform and Viceroy of the same period.
xs: **Lord Minto** (Minto II) is called the **"Father of the Communal Electorate"** — option **(3)**.
The **Morley-Minto Reforms (1909)** introduced **separate electorates for Muslims** with **weightage**.
**Montagu-Chelmsford** belong to the **1919** Act, which extended (not began) communal representation.
xa: Minto was **Viceroy (1905-1910)**; **John Morley** was **Secretary of State for India**.
The demand came from the **Simla Deputation (1 Oct 1906)** led by **Aga Khan**.
Exam angle: "Which Act introduced the communal electorate?" → **Morley-Minto 1909**.
⚠ UPSC notes wrongly say Minto expanded the Councils Act in **1919**; the 1919 Act was **Chelmsford's**.

n6f18136fe99.s: In connection with the Indian Councils Act, 1909, John Morley was the:
n6f18136fe99.x: John Morley was the Secretary of State for India and Lord Minto was the Viceroy.
xa: Minto's term as Viceroy: **1905-1910**.
**Gokhale** went to England in **1906** and met Morley to press for self-government like other colonies.
Aim of the reforms: **rally the Moderates** and **reward Muslim loyalty**.
**S.P. Sinha** became the first Indian on the **Viceroy's Executive Council** (Law Member).

n77d40cf4d5d.s: Which one of the following was NOT an aim of the All-India Muslim League in its early phase?
o: Keeping Muslims away from the Congress
Launching an immediate armed revolt against British rule
Promoting loyalty to the British Empire
n77d40cf4d5d.x: The early League aimed at loyalty to the British Empire, protection of Muslim political interests and separation from the Congress; immediate armed revolt was not one of its stated aims.
n77d40cf4d5d.tq: Reject the extreme revolutionary alternative when testing an organisation's declared aims.
xs: **Launching an immediate armed revolt** was **not** an aim — option **(3)**.
The early League's aims were **loyalty to the British Empire**, **safeguarding Muslim political interests** and **keeping Muslims away from the Congress** — options (1), (2), (4).
xa: Founded **30 Dec 1906** at **Dacca**; proposed by **Nawab Salimullah**; first president **Aga Khan**.
**1912-24**: the League was dominated by **younger Muslim nationalists**.
By **1916** it allied with the Congress in the **Lucknow Pact**.
London branch: **Syed Ameer Ali (1908)**.

nf6a10e54159.s: Who was the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council (1909)?
nf6a10e54159.x: S.P. Sinha was the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council (1909), as Law Member.
xa: His appointment came under the **Morley-Minto Reforms (1909)**.
Same reforms: **separate electorates** for Muslims with **weightage**.
Central council enlarged (additional members **to 60**), **official majority** retained.

nf5bba3212b0.s: The Lucknow Pact was negotiated principally by:
nf5bba3212b0.x: The Pact was negotiated by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Muhammad Ali Jinnah with the Muslim League's Young Party.
nf5bba3212b0.tq: Avoid the swapped-leader trap by matching the negotiators with the Pact.
xs: The Lucknow Pact was brokered by **Tilak and Jinnah** — option **(3)**.
**Annie Besant** also worked for it, but with Tilak, not Gokhale.
xa: Tilak's return marked the **reunion of Moderates and Extremists**.
Jinnah led the League's **"Young Party"** with the Ali Brothers.
Key concession: Congress **accepted separate electorates**.
Congress president: **Ambika Charan Majumdar**.

nindian-history-92-3.s: The office of 'Governor-General of India' was created by the:
nindian-history-92-3.x: The Charter Act of 1833 created the Governor-General of India; Pitt's India Act brought dual control and the 1813 Act largely ended the Company's trade monopoly.
n: Pitt's India Act, 1784 introduced dual control. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #92 · pp 174-175]
The Act of 1786 allowed the Governor-General to override the Council. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #92 · pp 174-175]
The Charter Act, 1813 substantially ended the Company's trade monopoly. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #92 · pp 174-175]
The Charter Act, 1833 created the office of Governor-General of India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #92 · pp 174-175]
xa: **Regulating Act, 1773** created the **Governor-General** of **Bengal** and the **first Supreme Court**.
**Charter Act, 1853** was the **last Charter Act**.
**Government of India Act, 1858** **ended Company rule**.

na0a476e0cbc.s: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1909, the Central Legislative Council was enlarged by up to how many additional members?
na0a476e0cbc.x: The 1909 Act enlarged the Central Legislative Council (additional members up to 60) but kept an official majority at the Centre.
xa: Most critical feature: **separate electorates for Muslims** with **weightage**.
Councils could not **vote on the budget** or question **military affairs**.
**S.P. Sinha** joined the Executive Council as **Law Member**.
Aim: **rally the Moderates** + **reward Muslim loyalty**.

nf60b8360774.s: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1909, members could discuss the budget but could not:
nf60b8360774.x: Members could discuss the budget, ask supplementary questions and move resolutions, but could not vote on the budget.
xa: **Official majority** stayed at the Centre.
Provinces had a **non-official majority**, blunted by the **Governor's veto**.
Elections were **indirect, multi-tier**.
Introduced by **John Morley** (Secretary of State) and **Lord Minto** (Viceroy).

n04536036747.s: The Morley-Minto Reforms were introduced mainly to:
o: Rally the Moderates and reward Muslim loyalty
Transfer the capital from Delhi to Calcutta
Abolish princely states and establish a republic
n04536036747.x: Morley and Minto sought to rally the Moderates and reward Muslim loyalty through limited constitutional concessions and separate electorates.
n04536036747.tq: Identify the political purpose behind a constitutional measure.
xs: Morley-Minto Reforms aimed to **rally the Moderates and reward Muslim loyalty** — option **(1)**.
The reward was **separate electorates** with **weightage** for Muslims.
The capital moved **Calcutta → Delhi** (not Delhi → Calcutta) in **1911**; **provincial autonomy** came with the **1935 Act** — (2) and (4) are wrong.
xa: Official majority **retained at the Centre**.
Councils could debate the budget but **could not vote** on it.
**S.P. Sinha** = first Indian on the Viceroy's Executive Council.

n79144aa1843.s: Separate electorates for Muslims were introduced by the:
n79144aa1843.x: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 enlarged the legislative councils and introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
xa: Central council: additional members **to 60**; provincial councils also enlarged.
**Elected** non-official members for the first time; **indirect** elections.
Minto = **"Father of the Communal Electorate"**.
**1919** Act later extended communal representation to **Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans**.

nindian-history-31-13.s: The right to discuss the budget and the indirect election of members came with the:
nindian-history-31-13.x: The 1892 Act brought budget discussion and indirect election; 1909 brought separate Muslim electorates, 1919 dyarchy and 1935 provincial autonomy.
n: The Government of India Act 1919 introduced provincial dyarchy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 97-98]
The Government of India Act 1935 introduced central dyarchy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 97-98]
The 1909 Act introduced a separate Muslim electorate. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 97-98]
Separate Muslim electorates were associated with the Morley-Minto Reforms. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 97-98]
The Government of India Act 1935 introduced constitutional autocracy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 97-98]
xa: The **1909** Act also gave Muslims **weightage** and let councils debate the budget but **not vote** on it.
The **1919** Act extended communal representation to **Sikhs**, **Indian Christians**, **Anglo-Indians** and **Europeans**.
The **1935** Act extended separate electorates to **depressed classes**, **women** and **labour**.

n8f1208f652d.s: Under the Lucknow Pact, the Congress accepted which major concession to the Muslim League?
o: Direct British appointment of Muslim representatives
n8f1208f652d.x: The Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims, which was a major concession under the Lucknow Pact.
n8f1208f652d.tq: Identify the specific concession rather than the general objective of the pact.
xs: The Congress **accepted Muslim separate electorates** — option **(2)**, a **major concession**.
It did not abolish communal representation — so (4) is wrong; it sought an **elected majority** in provincial legislatures — so (3) is wrong.
xa: **Weightage**: Muslims got seats above their population ratio.
**Communal veto**: no bill passed if **three-fourths** of the affected community's members opposed.
Common goal: **self-government**.
Separate electorates first came legally with the **1909** Act.

n0efc653639b.s: Under the Lucknow Pact, a bill affecting a community could not be passed if opposed by ____ of that community's members.
n0efc653639b.x: The Lucknow Pact's communal veto barred a bill if three-fourths of the affected community's members opposed it.
xa: Other terms: **separate electorates** accepted, **weightage**, **self-government** as common goal.
Also: **separation of executive and judiciary**; **elected majority** in provincial legislatures.
Brokers: **Tilak** and **Jinnah** (Dec **1916**).

n119d3279245.s: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 accepted which of the following as the common goal?
n119d3279245.x: The Pact accepted self-government as its goal, with separation of executive and judiciary and elected majorities in provincial legislatures.
xa: Congress **accepted separate electorates** for Muslims.
**Weightage** and the **three-fourths communal veto**.
Limit: **separate annual sessions** continued.

nb23d067fdc1.s: The provision that Muslims should receive more seats than their population share in provinces where they were a minority is known as:
nb23d067fdc1.x: The Lucknow Pact provided weightage to Muslims in minority provinces, giving them representation greater than their population share.
nb23d067fdc1.tq: Discriminate between closely related constitutional terms by their operative meaning.
xs: Seats above population share for a minority community is **weightage** — option **(2)**.
The Lucknow Pact fixed a proportion of seats for Muslims **above their population ratio**.
**Communal veto** was the **three-fourths** rule on bills; **dyarchy** belongs to the **1919** Act.
xa: Weightage was first given with separate electorates in the **1909** Act.
The **Simla Deputation (1906)** had demanded weightage.
Congress **accepted** separate electorates in **1916** — a major concession.

nindian-history-31-11.s: Under Provincial Dyarchy (1919), subjects were divided into:
nindian-history-31-11.x: Provincial Dyarchy under the 1919 Act split subjects into reserved and transferred; the 1935 Act abolished it.
n: The Government of India Act 1919 introduced provincial dyarchy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 97-98]
Provincial dyarchy had reserved subjects. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 97-98]
Provincial dyarchy had transferred subjects. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 97-98]
The Government of India Act 1935 abolished provincial dyarchy. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 97-98]
xa: The **1919** Act also brought **bicameralism and direct elections** at the Centre.
The **1935** Act introduced **central dyarchy**.
⚠ **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms**: **1919**, not **1929**.

n08d36734126.s: The Government of India Act, 1919 extended communal representation to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and:
n08d36734126.x: The 1919 Act extended communal representation to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans; depressed classes, women and labour got it in 1935.
xa: Separate electorates began for **Muslims** in **1909**.
The **1935 Act** extended them to **depressed classes, women, labour**.
1919 also brought **dyarchy in the provinces** and **direct elections** at the Centre.

ne7a04c5b5d1.s: Separate electorates were extended to the depressed classes, women and labour by the:
ne7a04c5b5d1.x: The 1935 Act gave provincial autonomy and extended separate electorates to depressed classes, women and labour.
xa: 1935 also prescribed an all-India **Federation**.
1919 extended communal representation to **Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans**.
1909 began **Muslim separate electorates**.

n440113e47e8.s: The Lucknow Congress Session of December 1916 was presided over by:
n440113e47e8.x: Ambika Charan Majumdar presided over the Lucknow Congress Session of December 1916.
n440113e47e8.tq: Avoid swapping the session president with the principal brokers of the pact.
xs: The **Lucknow Congress session (Dec 1916)** was presided over by **Ambika Charan Majumdar** — option **(4)**.
**Jinnah** presided over the **League's** Lucknow 1916 session — not the Congress.
**Tilak** and **Jinnah** were the **brokers** of the Lucknow Pact; **Annie Besant** also worked for it.
xa: ⚠ Lucknow 1916: Congress president = **Ambika Charan Majumdar**; League president = **Jinnah**.

Bomb thrower: **Basanta Kumar Biswas**.

n9d1bb5eec21.s: The Saunders killing in 1928 was intended as retaliation for the lathi-charge on:
n9d1bb5eec21.x: The Saunders killing was planned in retaliation for the lathi-charge on Lala Lajpat Rai during the anti-Simon Commission protest. The intended target was James A. Scott, while Rajguru fired first.
n9d1bb5eec21.tq: Trace the motive and intended target rather than confusing the person actually killed.
xs: It avenged the lathi-charge on **Lala Lajpat Rai** — option **(3)**.
The intended target was **James A. Scott**; **Rajguru fired first**.
xa: Lajpat Rai died after the **lathi-charge** during the Simon Commission protest.
Saunders killing: **1928**.
Rajguru was born **1908**, **Khed** (now Rajgurunagar).

nb110a40b0a5.s: Which of the following correctly represents the offices in the Provisional Government of India at Kabul?
o: Raja Mahendra Pratap—President; Maulana Barkatullah—Prime Minister
Obaidullah Sindhi—President; Raja Mahendra Pratap—Prime Minister
Raja Mahendra Pratap—Prime Minister; Obaidullah Sindhi—President
nb110a40b0a5.x: Raja Mahendra Pratap was President and Maulana Barkatullah was Prime Minister; Obaidullah Sindhi was also associated with the government.
nb110a40b0a5.tq: Check office–person assignments rather than recognising names alone.
xs: **Raja Mahendra Pratap = President**; **Maulana Barkatullah = Prime Minister** — option **(1)**.
**Obaidullah Sindhi** was the third member.
Formed at **Kabul** in **1915**.
xa: Backers: **Germany and Turkey**, with help from the **Afghan Crown Prince**.
Barkatullah edited **Islamic Fraternity**.
UPPSC **2022** order: Ghadar (**1913**) → Berlin (**1915**) → Assembly bomb (**1929**) → Chittagong (**1930**).

n4f421586086.s: Which pair of leaders was associated with the Berlin Committee?
o: Raja Mahendra Pratap and Obaidullah Sindhi
Gurdit Singh and Sohan Singh Bhakna
Shyamji Krishnavarma and Madan Lal Dhingra
n4f421586086.x: Virendranath Chattopadhyaya and Bhupendranath Dutta were associated with the Berlin Committee.
n4f421586086.tq: Match an organisation with its leading figures.
xs: The **Berlin Committee** = **Virendranath Chattopadhyaya** and **Bhupendranath Dutta** — option **(1)**.
**Mahendra Pratap** and **Obaidullah Sindhi** = **Kabul government**; **Gurdit Singh** = **Komagata Maru**; **Krishnavarma** and **Dhingra** = **India House**.
xa: Berlin, **1915**; sought **German and Turkish** help.
Also called the **Indian Independence Committee**.
Chattopadhyay's paper: **Talwar**.

n448232845e1.s: The revolutionary activities conducted from abroad during the First World War were significant mainly because they:
o: helped internationalise the struggle through arms, funds and foreign support
confined the freedom struggle to constitutional methods within India
restricted revolutionary activities to social reform organisations
ended the activities of Indian revolutionaries outside India
n448232845e1.x: Revolutionary networks abroad gave the Indian freedom struggle an international dimension by arranging arms, funds and support from foreign countries during the First World War.
n448232845e1.tq: Identify the broad significance of the development rather than recalling a single name or date.
xs: They **took the struggle global** — **arms, funds, foreign support** — option **(1)**.
Support came from **Germany, Turkey, Afghanistan** during **WWI**.
They did not confine the struggle to constitutional methods or end revolutionary activity abroad.
xa: Examples: **Berlin Committee (1915)**, **Kabul Provisional Government (1915)**.
**Ghadar Conspiracy**: revolt planned for **21 February 1915**.

nb5bcfb02b9a.s: The word ‘Ghadar’ denotes which of the following?
nb5bcfb02b9a.x: ‘Ghadar’ means mutiny or rebellion, reflecting the revolutionary character of the organisation.
nb5bcfb02b9a.tq: Test the exact meaning of a movement’s name.
xs: **"Ghadar"** means **mutiny/rebellion** — option **(3)**.
The name reflects the party's aim of revolt against British rule.
xa: Founded **1913** in the USA; first meeting in **Oregon**.
HQ: **Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco**.
Members: mostly **Punjabi Sikh immigrants** in North America.
Planned revolt: **21 February 1915**.

nc860cb74af0.s: The members of the Ghadar Party were predominantly drawn from which group?
o: Punjabi Sikh immigrants in North America
nc860cb74af0.x: The Ghadar Party drew most of its members from Punjabi Sikh immigrants living in North America.
nc860cb74af0.tq: Identify the organisation’s principal social base.
xs: Ghadar members were mostly **Punjabi Sikh immigrants in North America** — option **(1)**.
The party was founded in the **USA** in **1913** (first meeting in **Oregon**).
xa: Founders: **Lala Har Dayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, Kartar Singh Sarabha, Bhagwan Singh**.
First president: **Sohan Singh Bhakna**; Har Dayal = moving spirit/secretary.
**Darsi Chenchayya** = first and only **Telugu** member.

ndddca5890df.s: Who was the first president of the Ghadar Party?
ndddca5890df.x: Sohan Singh Bhakna was the first president; Har Dayal was the moving spirit and secretary, not president.
xa: Other founders: **Bhagwan Singh**, **Baba Harnam Singh (Tundilat)**, **Pt. Kanshi Ram**.
**Kartar Singh Sarabha** edited the **Punjabi Ghadar**.
First meeting: **Oregon**, **1913**.

nc1d6c297d2b.s: Which one of the following was actively associated with the Ghadar rising?
nc1d6c297d2b.x: Rash Behari Bose was actively associated with the Ghadar rising (UPSC 2022). Barindra Kumar Ghosh and Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee were not, and Bipin Chandra Pal was associated with the Calcutta Bande Mataram, not the Ghadar.
nc1d6c297d2b.tq: UPSC 2022: only Rash Behari Bose linked to Ghadar.
xs: **Rash Behari Bose** was actively associated with the **Ghadar rising** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **Barindra Kumar Ghosh** and **Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee** were **not** (UPSC **2022**).
**Bipin Chandra Pal** is linked to the Calcutta **Bande Mataram (1906)**.
xa: Rising planned for **21 February 1915** in Punjab.
**Betrayed by informers**; **45 leaders hanged** under the Defence of India Act.
**Kartar Singh Sarabha** executed **16 November 1915**, aged **19**.

n21f661bf00c.s: The Punjabi edition of *Ghadar* was edited by whom?
n21f661bf00c.x: Kartar Singh Sarabha edited the Punjabi edition of *Ghadar*. *Ghadar di Goonj* consisted of poetry associated with the movement.
n21f661bf00c.tq: Distinguish the publication’s editor from the organisation’s founders.
xs: The **Punjabi edition of Ghadar** was edited by **Kartar Singh Sarabha** — option **(3)**.
The paper itself was the **Ghadar Party's** under **Har Dayal**, San Francisco.
xa: **Ghadar di Goonj** = its **poetry**.
Sarabha executed **16 November 1915**, aged **19**.
**Sohan Singh Bhakna** = first president.

ndefcb97e77f.s: India House was founded in London in 1905 by:
ndefcb97e77f.x: Shyamji Krishnavarma founded India House in London in 1905; Cama's Paris Indian Society was a separate body.
xa: India House hub: **Savarkar, Har Dayal, Madan Lal Dhingra**.
Dhingra was hanged at **Pentonville**.
Cama hoisted the first Indian flag at **Stuttgart** (**22 August 1907**).

n8adf998e94a.s: Who among the following was associated with India House along with V.D. Savarkar and Lala Hardayal?
n8adf998e94a.x: Madan Lal Dhingra was associated with India House along with Savarkar and Hardayal. Dhingra killed Curzon Wyllie in 1909.
n8adf998e94a.tq: Identify the India House association without confusing it with the Berlin Committee or Kabul government.
xs: **Madan Lal Dhingra** was the third member of the India House hub — option **(2)**.
**Bhupendranath Dutta** belonged to the **Berlin Committee**; **Mahendra Pratap** and **Obaidullah Sindhi** to the **Kabul government**.
xa: Dhingra shot **Curzon Wyllie** (**1 July 1909**); hanged at **Pentonville**.
India House founder: **Shyamji Krishnavarma** (**1905**).
Har Dayal later founded the **Ghadar Party** (**1913**).

nfff79d05cf5.s: Madame Bhikaji Cama hoisted the first Indian national flag at the International Socialist Congress held at:
nfff79d05cf5.x: Madame Bhikaji Cama hoisted the flag at the International Socialist Congress in Stuttgart, Germany.
nfff79d05cf5.tq: Distinguish the city of the flag event from the city of publication.
xs: Cama hoisted the first Indian flag at **Stuttgart (Germany)** — option **(4)**.
Occasion: the **International Socialist Congress**, **22 August 1907**.
**Paris** was the base of her **Paris Indian Society** and **Bande Mataram**, not the flag venue.
xa: **Paris Indian Society**: **1905**.
Her **Bande Mataram** came out from **Paris** (Paris/Geneva).
⚠ The Calcutta **Bande Mataram (1906)** was **Bipin Chandra Pal's**.

ne86753f49f9.s: The planned date of the Ghadar uprising in the British Indian Army was:
ne86753f49f9.x: The pan-India revolt was planned for 21 February 1915, but informers betrayed the plan and it was crushed.
xa: **45 leaders hanged** under the **Defence of India Act**.
**First Lahore Conspiracy Case**: Sarabha executed with **Vishnu Ganesh Pingle**.
The **Komagata Maru (1914)** had accelerated the movement.

n1b07606d050.s: Kartar Singh Sarabha, executed on 16 November 1915 at the age of 19, was sentenced in which case?
n1b07606d050.x: Sarabha was executed in the First Lahore Conspiracy Case (with Vishnu Ganesh Pingle) after the failed Ghadar rising. The Delhi case (1912) concerned the Hardinge bomb, Kakori (1925) the HRA train action and Alipore (1908) the Maniktala bomb factory.
n1b07606d050.tq: Ghadar 1915 → First Lahore Conspiracy Case → Sarabha hanged at 19.
xs: Sarabha was executed in the **First Lahore Conspiracy Case** — option **(2)**.
Executed **16 November 1915**, aged **19**, with **Vishnu Ganesh Pingle**.
It followed the betrayed **Ghadar rising** of **21 February 1915**.
xa: Sarabha edited the **Punjabi edition of Ghadar**.
Born **24 May 1896**, **Sarabha, Ludhiana**.
Bhakna called him his **"General"**.

n9b63eb17e58.s: The Berlin Committee (1915) sought the help of Germany and ____ to free India.
n9b63eb17e58.x: The Berlin Committee sought German and Turkish help to invade India, not French and Russian support.
xa: Also called the **Indian Independence Committee**.
Chattopadhyay edited **Talwar**.
Har Dayal also joined the **Berlin effort**.

n279e0f8ae8d.s: Madame Bhikaji Cama brought out *Bande Mataram* from:
n279e0f8ae8d.x: Madame Bhikaji Cama brought out *Bande Mataram* from Paris and was associated with the Paris Indian Society.
n279e0f8ae8d.tq: Separate the publication city from the congress city.
xs: Cama brought out **Bande Mataram** from **Paris** — option **(3)**.
She led the **Paris Indian Society (1905)**.
**London** = India House (**Indian Sociologist**); **Berlin** = **Talwar**; **San Francisco** = **Ghadar**.
xa: ⚠ Do not confuse with **Bipin Chandra Pal's** Calcutta **Bande Mataram (1906)**.
Flag at **Stuttgart**, **22 August 1907**.
Other journals abroad: **Islamic Fraternity** (Barkatullah), **Swadesh Sevak** (G.D. Kumar).

nbc617661e95.s: The passengers of the Komagata Maru were denied entry into Canada primarily because of which rule?
nbc617661e95.x: Canada denied entry under racist immigration laws, particularly the ‘continuous journey’ rule.
nbc617661e95.tq: Identify the exact legal or administrative basis of exclusion.
xs: Entry was denied under the **"continuous journey" rule** — option **(3)**.
It was part of Canada's **racist immigration laws**.
xa: Ship: **Japanese**, chartered by **Gurdit Singh**; **376** passengers.
Forced back → **Budge Budge** police firing near Calcutta.
Apology: **Justin Trudeau**, House of Commons, **2016**.

na87e6b204f7.x: Gurdit Singh, a Punjabi businessman, chartered the Japanese ship Komagata Maru.
na87e6b204f7.tq: Separate the organiser of the voyage from later revolutionary leaders.
xs: The ship was chartered by **Gurdit Singh**, a **Punjabi businessman** — option **(2)**.
**Barkatullah** and **Mahendra Pratap** led the **Kabul government**; **Taraknath Das** ran **United India House**, Seattle.
xa: Route: **Singapore** → East Asian ports → **Vancouver** (**1914**).
Impact: radicalised immigrants and **accelerated the Ghadar movement**.
**Budge Budge (Sept 1914)** firing killed **19** passengers.

nc7241705ec7.s: M.N. Roy founded the Communist Party of India in 1920 at:
nc7241705ec7.x: Roy founded the CPI at Tashkent in 1920; the Kanpur formation of 1925 is the date the CPI recognises.
xa: ⚠ **Tashkent 1920** = CPI(M)'s date; **Kanpur 1925** = CPI's date.
Roy also founded the **Communist Party of Mexico**.
Associated with the **Radical Humanist** movement.

n14094664389.s: Besides the Communist Party of India at Tashkent (1920), M.N. Roy is credited with founding the Communist Party of:
n14094664389.x: M.N. Roy founded the Communist Party of Mexico before founding the CPI at Tashkent in 1920. He did not found the communist parties of China, Germany or Indonesia.
xs: Roy also founded the **Communist Party of Mexico** — option **(1)**.
His Indian party: **CPI at Tashkent (1920)**.
xa: CPI recognises the **Kanpur** formation (**26 Dec 1925**).
Newspaper **Vanguard**; book **India in Transition**.
Later: **Radical Democratic Party**.

n19303587d9b.s: Which Canadian Prime Minister apologised in the House of Commons in 2016 for the Komagata Maru episode?
n19303587d9b.x: Prime Minister Justin Trudeau apologised in the Canadian House of Commons in 2016 for the Komagata Maru episode.
xa: **376** passengers were denied entry under the **"continuous journey"** rule.
**Budge Budge (Sept 1914)** firing killed **19** passengers.
The ship was chartered by **Gurdit Singh**.

nindian-history-7-20.s: Vanguard was identified as which of the following?
nindian-history-7-20.x: Vanguard was an émigré Communist journal run by M.N. Roy from abroad. The Free Press Journal was an English daily and Kesari a Marathi paper.
nindian-history-7-20.tq: Recall the nature of each paper.
n: M.N. Roy was associated with Vanguard. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 45-46]
Vanguard was an émigré Communist journal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 45-46]
xs: **Vanguard** was an **émigré Communist journal** — option **(3)**.
It was run by **M.N. Roy** — **India's first communist newspaper**.
xa: M.N. Roy founded the **Communist Party of India at Tashkent (1920)** and the **Communist Party of Mexico**.
His book: **India in Transition**; later the **Radical Democratic Party**.
⚠ CPI founding: **Tashkent 1920** (CPI(M)) vs **Kanpur 26 Dec 1925** (CPI).

n80d6c9707c7.s: The newspaper *Indian Sociologist* was published by Shyamji Krishnavarma from which place?
n80d6c9707c7.x: Shyamji Krishnavarma published *Indian Sociologist* from London, in association with India House.
xs: **Indian Sociologist** was published from **London (India House)** — option **(4)**.
**Paris/Geneva** = Cama's **Bande Mataram**; **Berlin** = **Talwar**.
xa: India House founded **1905** by **Shyamji Krishnavarma**.
APPSC-G1 **2022** matched **Indian Sociologist — Krishnavarma**.
Also linked: the **Indian Home Rule Society**.

nindian-history-8-10.s: Tarak Nath Das published Free Hindustan from which place or region?
nindian-history-8-10.x: Tarak Nath Das published Free Hindustan from Vancouver in North America in 1908 to rally Indian emigrants. Allahabad, Patna and Calcutta were home to other papers.
nindian-history-8-10.tq: Recall the place of each emigrant paper.
n: Tarak Nath Das was associated with Free Hindustan. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 46-50]
Free Hindustan was associated with Vancouver and North America. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 46-50]
xs: **Tarak Nath Das** published **Free Hindustan** from **Vancouver** / **North America** — option **(4)**.
Free Hindustan was an émigré paper for Indians in North America.
xa: Taraknath Das also ran **United India House**, **Seattle**.
**Ghadar Party**: **San Francisco**, **1913**; HQ **Yugantar Ashram**.
**Swadesh Sevak** — **G.D. Kumar**.

n9a67f7803b8.s: Which one of the following descriptions correctly identifies Darsi Chenchayya?
o: The founder of India House in London
The first and only Telugu member of the Ghadar Party
The leader of the Komagata Maru voyage
The first Chairman of the Ghadar Party
n9a67f7803b8.x: Darsi Chenchayya of Kanigiri is identified as the first and only Telugu member of the Ghadar Party.
n9a67f7803b8.tq: Discriminate among persons associated with different revolutionary organisations and episodes.
xs: **Darsi Chenchayya** (Kanigiri) was the **first and only Telugu member of the Ghadar Party** — option **(2)**.
India House was **Krishnavarma's**; the Komagata Maru was **Gurdit Singh's**; the first Ghadar president was **Sohan Singh Bhakna**.
xa: He was **arrested on suspicion**.
Autobiography: **"Nenu Naa Desam"**.
Ghadar founder **Sohan Singh** attended the **Palasa Kisan Sabha (March 1940)**.

n8b90365831b.s: The All India Home Rule League of Annie Besant was founded in:
n8b90365831b.x: Annie Besant's All India Home Rule League was founded in Madras in September 1916. Its headquarters was at Adyar, in Gokhale Hall.
n8b90365831b.tq: Discriminate between the two Leagues by separating their founding places and dates.
xs: Besant's **All India Home Rule League** was founded in **Madras** in **September 1916** — option **(1)**.
HQ: **Adyar** (**Gokhale Hall**).
**Belgaum/Poona, April 1916** = **Tilak's** league.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say **1915** — her self-government campaign began then; the league itself = **Sept 1916**.
Organising secretary: **George Arundale**; ~**200 branches**.
Covered the rest of India, **including Bombay city**.

n3895e61cbd0.s: Tilak's Home Rule League operated in Maharashtra (except Bombay city), Karnataka, Berar and the:
n3895e61cbd0.x: Tilak's League covered Maharashtra except Bombay city, Karnataka, the Central Provinces and Berar; Besant's covered the rest.
xa: Tilak's league: launched at **Belgaum** (Bombay Provincial Conference), based at **Poona**.
President **Joseph Baptista**; Secretary **N.C. Kelkar**.
Tilak's league was **better organised**; Besant's reached a **wider audience**.

nf62a7058254.s: Annie Besant's Home Rule League had approximately how many branches?
nf62a7058254.x: Besant's League covered the rest of India including Bombay city and had about 200 branches.
xa: Allied bodies: **Young Men's India Association**, **Boy Scouts Association**, **Order of Sons of India**.
Tilak's league merged into Besant's.
Andhra had **52 branches by 1917**.

naeb5f516121.s: Who was the President of Tilak's Home Rule League?
naeb5f516121.x: Joseph Baptista was President and N.C. Kelkar Secretary of Tilak's League; Arundale and Wadia were with Besant's League.
xa: Madras League General Secretary: **C.P. Ramaswamy Aiyar**.
⚠ Besant was interned with **Wadia** and **Arundale** at **Ootacamund** (**15 June 1917**).
Some notes give Kelkar's initials as **N.G.**

n4cbca6450c7.s: Annie Besant was styled as the:
n4cbca6450c7.x: Annie Besant was styled the “Iron Lady of Ireland.” She was of Irish origin and later became a prominent Indian nationalist leader.
n4cbca6450c7.tq: Test the title-person association without confusing Besant's title with titles associated with Indian leaders.
xs: Annie Besant was styled the **"Iron Lady of Ireland"** — option **(3)**.
She was born on **1 October 1847** at **Clapham, London**, of **Irish origin**.
xa: In England she was a **Fabian socialist** (Fabian Society).
Joined the **Theosophical Society (1888)**; came to India in **1893**; TS **President in 1907**.
⚠ Tilak = **"Lokmanya"** / **"Father of Indian Unrest"** (Chirol); Besant = **"Iron Lady of Ireland"**.
First woman **INC president (1917)**.

n7739d4fed7b.s: The Central Hindu College founded by Annie Besant in 1898 was located at
n7739d4fed7b.x: Annie Besant founded the Central Hindu College at Varanasi in 1898. It later became the core of Banaras Hindu University under Madan Mohan Malaviya.
n7739d4fed7b.tq: Distinguish the two institutions by their locations.
xs: Besant's **Central Hindu College (1898)** was at **Varanasi** — option **(2)**.
It became the core of **BHU** under **Madan Mohan Malaviya**.
xa: APPSC-GS **2019**: TS President **1907**, first woman INC president **1917**, Central Hindu College **1898** — all correct.
**Madanapalle college** is cited for Home Rule strength in Andhra.
Besant came to India in **1893**.

n216f078cc7f.s: Annie Besant renamed the Madras Standard as New India after purchasing it in:
n216f078cc7f.x: Annie Besant purchased the Madras Standard in July 1914 and renamed it New India. New India was a daily newspaper.
n216f078cc7f.tq: Use the exact month and the newspaper's earlier name as the discriminating clues.
xs: Besant bought the **Madras Standard** in **July 1914** and renamed it **New India** — option **(3)**.
**January 1914** was her English weekly **Common Weal**.
**April/September 1916** were the founding months of the two **Home Rule Leagues**.
xa: APPSC G2 **2025** asked this twice.
⚠ Tilak was released on **16 June 1914** — the same summer.

n4d7fb39524f.s: Who described Bal Gangadhar Tilak as the 'Father of Indian Unrest'?
n4d7fb39524f.x: British journalist Valentine Chirol called Tilak the 'Father of Indian Unrest'. Curzon, Montagu and Minto were British officials who did not coin this title; Minto is called 'Father of the Communal Electorate'.
n4d7fb39524f.tq: Father of Indian Unrest = Tilak, per Valentine Chirol.
xs: British journalist **Valentine Chirol** called Tilak the **"Father of Indian Unrest"** — option **(2)**.
Tilak's popular title was **"Lokmanya"**.
**Montagu** is linked to the **August Declaration (1917)**; **Minto** is the **"Father of the Communal Electorate"**.
xa: Tilak started **Kesari** and **Mahratta** (**1881**).
He made **Ganeshotsav (1893)** and **Shivaji festival (1895)** public.
His Home Rule League: **28 April 1916**.

n775905fa833.s: Annie Besant became the first woman President of the INC in 1917 at the ____ session.
n775905fa833.x: Besant was the first woman INC President at Calcutta in 1917 (APPSC-GS 2019).
xa: Joined the TS in **1888** (**1889** in many texts).
Founded **Central Hindu College (1898)**.
Interned at **Ootacamund**, **15 June 1917**.

n809b41a50ed.s: Annie Besant was interned on 15 June 1917 at which place along with B. P. Wadia and G. S. Arundale?
n809b41a50ed.x: Annie Besant was interned at Ootacamund on 15 June 1917 along with B. P. Wadia and G. S. Arundale.
n809b41a50ed.tq: Use the place-name anchor to distinguish the internment event from other Home Rule centres.
xs: Besant was interned at **Ootacamund** — option **(2)**.
With **B.P. Wadia** and **G.S. Arundale**, on **15 June 1917**.
xa: Released **17 September 1917**.
Montagu's remark: **"Shiva cut his wife into fifty-two pieces..."**.
Andhra reacted with **"Confinement Day"** protests.

ndcf8a03623c.s: What was the effect of Annie Besant's internment on the Home Rule Movement?
ndcf8a03623c.x: Besant's internment aroused public outrage, strengthened the movement and drew several Moderates into it.
xa: Interned at **Ootacamund** on **15 June 1917**.
**Montagu** commented on the folly of the internment.
Tenali and Vijayawada held **"Confinement Day"** protests.

n7031b766606.s: The August Declaration of 20 August 1917 was announced by:
n7031b766606.x: It was announced by Edwin Montagu, the Secretary of State; Chelmsford was the Viceroy.
xa: Date: **20 August 1917**.
Goal: **"progressive realisation of responsible government"**.
Congress split over Mont-Ford proposals at **Bombay (Aug 1918)** under **Hasan Imam**.

nc72777b7a88.s: The central objective expressed in the Montagu Declaration was:
o: Immediate complete independence from British rule
Progressive realisation of responsible government through self-governing institutions
Introduction of separate electorates for all communities
nc72777b7a88.x: The Declaration promised the gradual development of self-governing institutions and the progressive realisation of responsible government by increasing Indian participation in administration.
nc72777b7a88.tq: Choose the precise constitutional objective rather than an extreme or unrelated alternative.
xs: Its objective was the **progressive realisation of responsible government** through **self-governing institutions** — option **(2)**.
Also: **increasing Indian association** in administration.
It did not promise independence; **separate electorates** were a **1909** feature.
xa: Announced by **Edwin Montagu** on **20 August 1917**.
It led to the **1919 Act**.
It raised Andhra's hopes for a **separate province**.

n6c7a2a84acd.s: The Surat split of 1907 between the Moderates and Extremists was healed at:
n6c7a2a84acd.x: The split that occurred at Surat in 1907 was healed at the Lucknow session in 1916.
n6c7a2a84acd.tq: Use the earlier split and later reunion as first-and-last chronological anchors.
xs: The **Surat split (1907)** was healed at **Lucknow in 1916** — option **(2)**.
**Bombay 1918** was the **Hasan Imam** special session where Congress split again over Mont-Ford proposals.
xa: Lucknow also cemented **Congress-League unity**.
Reunion eased by **Tilak and Besant's** efforts.
**Gokhale** and **Pherozeshah Mehta** died in **1915**.

n621cda89895.s: The reunion of the Moderates and Extremists at Lucknow was facilitated mainly by:
o: The formation of the Indian National Liberal Federation alone
Tilak and Besant's efforts, along with the deaths of Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta
n621cda89895.x: Tilak and Besant worked for reunion, while the deaths of Gopal Krishna Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta in 1915 removed important obstacles to reconciliation.
n621cda89895.tq: Match the reunion with its political facilitators, avoiding a later-event trap.
xs: Reunion was eased by **Tilak and Besant's efforts** and the **deaths of Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta** — option **(4)**.
Both deaths came in **1915**.
The **Montagu Declaration** (**1917**) and **1919 Act** came after Lucknow — so (2) is wrong.
xa: Lucknow **1916** reunited **Moderates and Extremists**.
Tilak's remark on the Pact: **"Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers"**.
Congress **accepted separate electorates** for Muslims at Lucknow.

n4aadd39cde2.s: Which of the following correctly describes the later fate of the All India Home Rule League?
o: Besant's League merged into Tilak's League and remained independent.
Tilak's League merged into Besant's League; in 1920 it was renamed Swarajya Sabha under Gandhi and later merged into the Congress.
It was immediately converted into the Indian National Liberal Federation in 1918.
It was dissolved at the Lucknow session in 1916.
n4aadd39cde2.x: Tilak's League merged into Besant's League. In 1920, the All India Home Rule League under Gandhi's presidency was renamed Swarajya Sabha and soon merged into the Congress.
n4aadd39cde2.tq: Track organisational transformation in sequence rather than confusing the League with a contemporary federation.
xs: **Tilak's league merged into Besant's**; in **1920** it was renamed **Swarajya Sabha** under **Gandhi** and soon merged into the Congress — option **(2)**.
So it was not dissolved at Lucknow (**1916**), nor did Besant's merge into Tilak's.
xa: Besant's league HQ: **Adyar** (Gokhale Hall).
**1920**: **Non-Cooperation** launched.
Significance: filled the gap between **Gokhale's death (1915)** and **Gandhi's rise (1920)**.

n2f18a7c8a08.s: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 is significant in the history of communal politics because the Congress:
o: Rejected all forms of communal representation
n2f18a7c8a08.x: Through the Lucknow Pact, the Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
n2f18a7c8a08.tq: Distinguish acceptance from later rejection or extension of a constitutional device.
xs: At Lucknow the Congress **accepted separate electorates for Muslims** — option **(3)**.
It accepted what it had **opposed in 1909** (Morley-Minto).
xa: **Lucknow 1916** also reunited **Moderates and Extremists**.
Tilak: **"Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers"**.
Reunion eased by deaths of **Gokhale** and **Pherozeshah Mehta (1915)**.

ndf226e648f7.s: The newspaper Krishna Patrika was associated with:
ndf226e648f7.x: Krishna Patrika was associated with Mutnuri; Desamata was associated with Chilakamarti.
xa: **Andhra Patrika** — **Kasinathuni**.
