Besant's own papers: **Common Weal** and **New India**.
Andhra was one of the strongest Home Rule regions: **52 branches**.

n159b605ebd2.s: The protests held at Tenali and Vijayawada following Annie Besant's arrest were known as
n159b605ebd2.x: The protests at Tenali and Vijayawada following Besant's arrest were called “Confinement Day” protests.
n159b605ebd2.tq: Recall the exact name of the protest occasion.
xs: The protests at **Tenali** and **Vijayawada** were **"Confinement Day"** protests — option **(4)**.
They followed **Besant's arrest/internment** (**15 June 1917**).
xa: Interned at **Ootacamund** with **B.P. Wadia** and **G.S. Arundale**.
Released **17 September 1917**.
Machilipatnam students wore **"Besant lockets"** (Extremist-phase notes).

n222ca5bb7c0.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao translated Sarojini Naidu's 'Awake Mother' as:
n222ca5bb7c0.x: He translated Awake Mother as Nuthana Haindava Matrigeetham; Swarajya Paramoddesham was a Telugu pamphlet.
xa: He used **libraries as lecture venues**.
Gadicherla = **Secretary** of the Andhra branch.
Andhra had **52 branches by 1917**.

nab80c1d3946.s: Who served as secretary of the Andhra division of the Home Rule League?
nab80c1d3946.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was secretary of the Andhra division, with branches at Guntur, Vijayawada and Kakinada.
xa: **52 branches** in Andhra **by 1917**.
Leaders: **Konda Venkatappayya**, **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**, **K.V. Reddy Naidu**, **Pattabhi Sitaramayya**.
Propaganda via Telugu pamphlets such as **Swarajya Paramoddesham**.

nac131e277eb.s: The demand raised by the Andhra delegation before Montagu in December 1917 primarily concerned:
o: The transfer of the capital to Delhi
The formation of the Swarajya Sabha
nac131e277eb.x: The Montagu Declaration raised hopes of a separate Andhra province, and an Andhra delegation led by Nyapati Subba Rao met Montagu on 20 December 1917 to press that demand.
nac131e277eb.tq: Infer the regional political objective from the delegation's context.
xs: The Andhra delegation sought a **separate Andhra province** — option **(1)**.
Led by **Nyapati Subba Rao**, it met Montagu on **20 Dec 1917**.
The **Montagu Declaration** had raised these hopes.
xa: Declaration date: **20 August 1917**.
**Swarajya Sabha** came only in **1920**.
Andhra had **52 Home Rule branches by 1917**.

n5a2786507f8.s: The remark about Shiva cutting his wife into fifty-two pieces, in the context of Annie Besant's internment, was made by
n5a2786507f8.x: Edwin Montagu used the remark while commenting on the folly of Annie Besant's internment.
n5a2786507f8.tq: Avoid swapping the British official with Indian nationalist leaders.
xs: The Shiva remark was **Edwin Montagu's** — option **(2)**.
It mocked the **folly of Besant's internment**.
xa: Besant interned **15 June 1917**, **Ootacamund**.
Montagu, **Secretary of State**, issued the **August Declaration (20 August 1917)**.
The internment **boosted** the movement.

n4869a3986ce.s: Gandhi returned to India from South Africa on:
n4869a3986ce.x: Gandhi returned on 9 January 1915, the year Gokhale died; Tilak's League came in April 1916.
xa: **Pherozeshah Mehta** also died in **1915**.
**1916**: Besant's league (Sept); **Lucknow Pact** (Dec).
**1914**: Besant's **Common Weal** and **New India**.

n83e0a333359.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the HRA and HSRA?
o: The HRA was founded at Kanpur in 1924
Bhagat Singh reorganised the organisation after Bismil's death
The HSRA stood for socialist revolution
Bhagat Singh is credited with founding the HSRA
n83e0a333359.x: It was Chandrashekhar Azad who reorganised the organisation after Bismil's death.
xa: HRA founders: **Bismil, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee, Sachindra Nath Sanyal** (APPSC-G1 **2024**).
⚠ Bhagat Singh was **not** an HRA founder.
HSRA formed at **Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi** (**1928**).

n9d855796eeb.s: The stated goal of the HSRA was associated with the establishment of a:
o: Federal Republic of United States of India
n9d855796eeb.x: The HSRA envisaged a 'Federal Republic of United States of India' and advocated socialist revolution.
n9d855796eeb.tq: Recall the exact constitutional phrase rather than a broad substitute such as socialist republic.
xs: The HSRA aimed at a **"Federal Republic of United States of India"** — option **(1)**.
Its goal was **socialist** revolution, beyond the HRA's armed revolution for a republic.
xa: HSRA: **1928**, Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi.
Credited to **Bhagat Singh** with **Azad** and **Sukhdev**.
Shift to **socialist** ideology and **mass propaganda** (courtroom, leaflets, hunger strikes).

n1cc57cd7d9a.s: Which one of the following sets contains only those executed in connection with the Kakori Train Action?
o: Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri
Surya Sen, Ananta Singh, Ganesh Ghosh and Lokenath Bal
Jatin Das, Chandrashekhar Azad, Udham Singh and Gopinath Saha
Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru and Batukeshwar Dutt
n1cc57cd7d9a.x: Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were hanged in connection with the Kakori case in December 1927.
n1cc57cd7d9a.tq: Group the correct case participants and exclude revolutionaries belonging to other cases.
xs: Kakori hangings: **Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri** — option **(1)**.
**Surya Sen's** group = Chittagong; **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru** = Lahore case (Dutt got **life**).
xa: Jails: **Bismil (Gorakhpur)**, **Ashfaqullah (Faizabad)**, **Roshan Singh (Allahabad/Naini)**, **Lahiri (Gonda)**.
Hanged in **Dec 1927**.
Bismil born **11 June 1897**.

n4a22945224c.s: The HSRA added ____ to the HRA's objective of establishing a republic through armed revolt.
n4a22945224c.x: The HSRA added socialism to the HRA's aim, an ideological development beyond the HRA.
xa: HSRA goal: **"Federal Republic of United States of India"**.
HSRA also used **mass propaganda** (courtroom, leaflets, hunger strikes).
HRA founders: **Sanyal, Chatterjee, Bismil**.

nindian-history-120-22.s: Bhagat Singh and Chandrashekhar Azad reorganised the HRA in 1928 at Ferozeshah Kotla, Delhi, into which organisation?
nindian-history-120-22.x: In 1928 the HRA was renamed the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) under Bhagat Singh and Azad. Anushilan Samiti was Bengali, Abhinav Bharat was Savarkar's and Khudai Khidmatgar was Ghaffar Khan's.
nindian-history-120-22.tq: Recall the socialist renaming of the HRA in 1928.
n: Bhagat Singh was associated with the HSRA. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
Bhagat Singh was associated with revolutionary nationalism. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #120 · pp 218-221]
xs: In **1928** at **Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi**, the HRA was reorganised into the **HSRA** — option **(2)**.
The HSRA was reorganised under **Chandrashekhar Azad** after Bismil's death; members included **Bhagat Singh**, **Sukhdev**, **Bejoy Kumar Sinha**.
Its goal was a **socialist** revolution — a "Federal Republic of United States of India".
xa: **HRA**: **1924, Kanpur** — **Ram Prasad Bismil**, **Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee**, **Sachindra Nath Sanyal**.
⚠ **Bhagat Singh** was **not** an HRA founder.
**Naujawan Bharat Sabha**: **1926**, **Lahore** — Bhagat Singh, with **Sukhdev**.

ndfc379b214d.s: The Naujawan Bharat Sabha, founded by Bhagat Singh in 1926, was set up at:
ndfc379b214d.x: It was founded at Lahore in 1926 with Sukhdev and Bhagwati Charan Vohra; Delhi 1928 (Feroz Shah Kotla) is the HSRA.
xa: Aim: mobilise **youth, peasants and workers** + fight **communalism**.
Vohra wrote **The Philosophy of the Bomb**.
Sukhdev taught at **National College, Lahore**.

n390855e0ead.s: The principal objective of the Naujawan Bharat Sabha was to
o: mobilise youth, peasants and workers and oppose communalism
establish a princely federation through constitutional reforms
secure separate electorates for revolutionary organisations
organise military assistance for the British during the First World War
n390855e0ead.x: The Sabha sought to mobilise youth, peasants and workers and to fight communalism.
n390855e0ead.tq: Identify the organisation from its distinctive social base and ideological objective.
xs: The Sabha aimed to **mobilise youth, peasants and workers** and **oppose communalism** — option **(1)**.
Founded **1926**, **Lahore**, by **Bhagat Singh** with **Sukhdev** (and **Vohra**).
xa: HSRA (**1928**) added **socialism** to the armed-revolt programme.
Bhagat Singh wrote **Why I am an Atheist (1930)**.
Influences: **Jallianwala Bagh (1919)**, **Nankana Sahib (1921)**, **Chauri Chaura (1922)**.

nce465f4eddf.s: The Kakori Train Action was undertaken primarily to:
o: protest against the Trade Disputes Bill
destroy the railway line between Delhi and Lahore
obtain government treasury funds for the HRA
nce465f4eddf.x: On 9 August 1925, the HRA looted the government treasury carried on a train near Kakori to fund its revolutionary activities.
nce465f4eddf.tq: Identify the motive of an action rather than merely recalling its location or date.
xs: Kakori aimed to **obtain government treasury funds for the HRA** — option **(4)**.
On **9 August 1925** the HRA looted the **government treasury** on a train near **Kakori (Lucknow)**.
The **Trade Disputes Bill** protest was the **1929** Assembly bomb.
xa: **Azad** took part and escaped.
⚠ **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru** were **not** part of Kakori.
Hanged (**Dec 1927**): **Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh, Rajendra Lahiri**.

n2141ae97023.s: J.P. Saunders was killed at Lahore in 1928 because he was mistaken for:
n2141ae97023.x: Saunders was mistakenly killed in place of James A. Scott, associated with the anti-Simon lathi-charge.
xa: Lahore, **Dec 1928**.
⚠ Saunders killed in place of **Scott**; Tegart's would-be killer hit **Ernest Day**.
**Rajguru** fired first.

nd6b328460c6.s: Udham Singh shot Michael O'Dwyer at Caxton Hall, London, on:
nd6b328460c6.x: Udham Singh shot O'Dwyer on 13 March 1940 in revenge for Jallianwala Bagh.
xa: Jallianwala Bagh (**1919**) also turned **Bhagat Singh** towards revolution.
Saunders killing: **Dec 1928**, Lahore.

n45f1c01afc2.s: On 8 April 1929, Bhagat Singh threw smoke bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly along with:
n45f1c01afc2.x: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw non-lethal smoke bombs and leaflets in the Assembly.
xa: Against the **Public Safety Bill** + **Trade Disputes Bill**.
Slogan **"Inquilab Zindabad"**; leaflet: **"To make the deaf hear"**.
Dutt got **life transportation** in the Assembly bomb case.

n39e790b696a.s: The Central Assembly bomb incident was primarily a protest against which Bills?
o: The Government of India Bill and the Rowlatt Bill
The Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill
The Trade Disputes Bill and the Indian Councils Bill
The Rowlatt Bill and the Public Safety Bill
n39e790b696a.x: The action protested against the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill, which were viewed as curbing civil liberties and workers' rights.
n39e790b696a.tq: Match the protest action with the precise legislative targets.
xs: The protest was against the **Public Safety Bill** and **Trade Disputes Bill** — option **(2)**.
These curbed **civil liberties** and **workers**.
xa: Bombs thrown on **8 April 1929** by **Bhagat Singh** and **Batukeshwar Dutt**.
They **courted arrest** to use the court as a platform.
Slogan: **"Inquilab Zindabad"**.

n06ae3474225.s: The leaflet thrown in the Central Assembly in 1929 said the action was 'to make the ____ hear'.
n06ae3474225.x: The leaflet said 'To make the deaf hear'; Bhagat Singh and Dutt then courted arrest to use the court as a platform.
xa: Slogan: **"Inquilab Zindabad"**.
Dutt: **life transportation**; Bhagat Singh tried in the **Lahore Conspiracy Case**.
Dutt died **1965**; cremated at **Hussainiwala**.

n220fdc74b4c.s: The Chittagong Armoury Raid of 18 April 1930 was led by:
n220fdc74b4c.x: The raid was led by Surya Sen, popularly known as Masterda. Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath Bal and Ananta Singh were among his associates.
n220fdc74b4c.tq: Distinguish the principal leader from the named associates in a revolutionary operation.
xs: **Surya Sen ("Masterda")** led the **Chittagong Armoury Raid** (**18 April 1930**) — option **(3)**.
**Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath Bal, Ananta Singh** were his **associates**.
xa: Group name: **Indian Republican Army** (also **Ambika Chakravarty**).
Fight at **Jalalabad Hills**; Surya Sen hanged **1934**.
Women: **Pritilata Waddedar**, **Kalpana Dutt**.

n071620031f5.s: The fighting associated with the Chittagong Armoury Raid took place at the:
n071620031f5.x: The raiders cut telegraph lines, disrupted railways and fought at the Jalalabad Hills.
xa: Leader: **Surya Sen**, **18 April 1930**.
**Pritilata Waddedar** led the **Pahartali European Club** raid.
Surya Sen hanged **1934**.

nbeeb9e32a5a.s: Surya Sen, leader of the Chittagong Armoury Raid, was hanged in:
nbeeb9e32a5a.x: Surya Sen, whose group called itself the Indian Republican Army, was hanged in 1934; the 1931 Lahore executions were of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru.
xa: Associates: **Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath Bal, Ananta Singh, Ambika Chakravarty**.
Known as **"Masterda"**.
Raid: **18 April 1930**.

na189e383a3f.s: Which revolutionary is associated with the Lahore jail hunger strike of 1929?
na189e383a3f.x: The hunger strike for political-prisoner status involved Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Batukeshwar Dutt and Jatin Das.
xa: **Jatin Das** died after a **63-day** hunger strike.
Hunger strikes were part of the HSRA's **mass propaganda**.
Lahore case trial: **1929-1930**.

n0a291d9e3d6.s: The Nankana Sahib incident, which influenced Bhagat Singh, took place in:
n0a291d9e3d6.x: Jallianwala Bagh (1919), Nankana Sahib (1921) and Chauri Chaura (1922) preceded Bhagat Singh's turn to revolutionary politics.
xa: He founded the **Naujawan Bharat Sabha (1926)**.
Credited with founding the **HSRA (1928)**.
Wrote **Why I am an Atheist (1930)**.

n4a9135ca8f9.s: Reservation of forests and restriction of podu cultivation among the Agency tribes followed the Madras Forest Act of:
n4a9135ca8f9.x: The Madras Forest Act, 1882 reserved forests, restricted podu and minor forest produce, and curbed grazing.
xa: **Podu** = shifting cultivation.
**Begar** = forced unpaid labour on roads.
**Tahsildar Bastian's** excesses were the spark.

n4bdd1b76d1f.s: The Rampa or Manyam Rebellion was principally based in which area?
o: The Gudem hills of the East Godavari Agency
n4bdd1b76d1f.x: The rebellion was based in the Gudem hills, located in the Agency area of East Godavari.
n4bdd1b76d1f.tq: Use the location clue to separate the rebellion's operational area from other hill regions of Andhra Pradesh.
xs: The rebellion was based in the **Gudem hills** of the **East Godavari** Agency — option **(3)**.
Area: agency tracts of **East Godavari and Visakhapatnam (Gudem hills)**.
xa: Span: **January 1922 - May 1924**.
First PS attacked: **Chintapalli** (**22 Aug 1922**).
Tribes: **Koya** and other hill tribes.

n8def526aee7.s: An increase in the axe tax during a famine caused the:
n8def526aee7.x: The axe-tax increase caused the Rekapalle rebellion; the 1879-80 Rampa rebellion arose from Madhava Bhupati's exploitation.
xa: Rampa leaders: **Dwarabandala Chandrayya**, **Pulikanta Sambaiah**, **Karu Tammanna Dora**, **Ambul Reddy**.
**Sullivan** removed Madhava Bhupati; revolt crushed **Nov 1880**.
Chandrayya burnt **Addateegala** PS.

n5cc24dd7dae.s: The Rampa rebellion of 1879–80 was brought to an end after:
o: The axe tax was withdrawn and the rebellion ended in July 1879
Madhava Bhupati was removed by Sullivan and the rebellion was crushed in November 1880
The Madras Forest Act was repealed and the rebellion ended in November 1881
Madhava Bhupati was reinstated and the rebellion ended in September 1879
n5cc24dd7dae.x: Sullivan removed Madhava Bhupati, but the rebellion was ultimately crushed in November 1880.
n5cc24dd7dae.tq: Check the complete sequence of administrative action followed by suppression.
xs: **Sullivan removed Madhava Bhupati**, and the revolt was **crushed in Nov 1880** — option **(2)**.
**Sept 1879** is when **Rekapalle** was crushed; the **axe tax** was a Rekapalle grievance.
xa: Rampa revolt span: **1879-80**, Rampachodavaram agency.
Madhava Bhupati was made Munsubdar in **1848**.
The **Madras Forest Act** dates from **1882** — after the revolt.

n632d7c41807.s: Which one of the following was NOT a cause of the Rampa Rebellion?
o: Introduction of permanent settlement in the Gudem hills
Oppressive functioning of the Muttadari system
Loss of forest and podu rights under the Madras Forest Act
n632d7c41807.x: The rebellion was caused by restrictions on forest and podu rights, begar for road building and the oppressive Muttadari system, along with the actions of Tahsildar Bastian. Permanent settlement was not identified as a cause.
n632d7c41807.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated cluster of causes.
xs: **Permanent settlement** was **not** a cause — option **(1)**.
Causes: **Muttadari** oppression, **begar** for roads, loss of **podu/forest** rights under the **Forest Act**, and **Tahsildar Bastian**.
xa: **Madras Forest Act, 1882**.
Bastian's excesses were the **spark**.
Rebellion span: **2 years 5 months**.

na433e996fb8.s: The Rampa Rebellion was an armed tribal rebellion in the:
na433e996fb8.x: It was an armed tribal rebellion in the Agency area, not affiliated with the Congress, and troubled the British more than the Non-Cooperation Movement.
xa: Span: **January 1922 - May 1924**.
**Assam Rifles** and **Gurkhas** reached **Narsipatnam** (**27 Jan 1924**).
Special Commissioner: **Rutherford**.

nde14a5e4f97.s: The first defeat suffered by Alluri Sitarama Raju’s forces at the hands of the Malabar Special Police occurred at:
nde14a5e4f97.x: At Peddagaddapalem on 6 December 1922, the Malabar Special Police inflicted Raju’s first defeat; he was wounded at Lingapuram.
nde14a5e4f97.tq: Separate the sites of the first defeat, the direct battle and the wounding.
xs: The first defeat was at **Peddagaddapalem** (**6 Dec 1922**) — option **(4)**.
Inflicted by the **Malabar Special Police**.
**Lingapuram** = where Raju was **wounded**; **Damanapalli ghat** = ambush; **Panjerighat** = direct battle.
xa: ⚠ **Chintapalli** = first PS attacked; **Panjerighat** = direct battle; **Peddagaddapalem** = first defeat.
**Rutherford** was Special Commissioner.

ncd50a4d0fe2.s: The Rampa rebellion extended approximately from:
ncd50a4d0fe2.x: The rebellion lasted from January 1922 to May 1924, approximately two years and five months, in the Agency tracts of East Godavari and Visakhapatnam.
ncd50a4d0fe2.tq: Use the beginning and ending months together rather than relying only on the commonly remembered year range.
xs: The rebellion ran from **January 1922 to May 1924** — option **(3)**.
About **2 years 5 months**.
xa: Area: **East Godavari and Visakhapatnam (Gudem hills)**.
First raid: **Chintapalli, 22 Aug 1922**.
End: Raju shot **7 May 1924**; **Gantam Dora** killed **7 June 1924**.

nb476cf7449a.s: During the Rampa Rebellion of 1922-24, the direct battle between Alluri Sitarama Raju's forces and the British forces was fought at:
nb476cf7449a.x: The direct battle with British forces was at Panjerighat (Damanghat), September 1922 (APPSC 2012 key). Chintapalli and Krishnadevipeta were police stations raided in August 1922; Koyyuru is where Raju was shot on 7 May 1924.
nb476cf7449a.tq: Panjerighat = direct battle; Chintapalli = first raid; Koyyuru = death.
xs: The direct battle was at **Panjerighat** (Damanghat), **Sept 1922** — option **(2)** (APPSC **2012** key).
**Chintapalli** = first PS raided; **Koyyuru** = where Raju was shot; **Krishnadevipeta** = his tomb.
xa: **Damanapalli ghat** ambush: **Scott Coward and Heiter** killed (**24 Sept 1922**).
First defeat: **Peddagaddapalem**.
Also asked in APPSC G2 **2012**.

n4d793be2652.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju was shot on 7 May 1924 at:
n4d793be2652.x: He was shot at Koyyuru before Major Goodall; last rites were at Krishnadevipeta, and Chintapalli was the first police station he raided.
xa: He was shot **tied to a tree**.
Goodall is also spelt **"Gudal"**, **"Goodman"**.
⚠ Some notes say cremated, others buried; **tomb/samadhi** at Krishnadevipeta.

n69d77e4cb5f.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju, who led the later Rampa rebellion, was born in:
n69d77e4cb5f.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju was born in 1897. Therefore, attributing the 1879–80 Rampa rebellion to him is chronologically incorrect.
n69d77e4cb5f.tq: Use the birth-year check to expose an impossible attribution.
xs: **Alluri Sitarama Raju** was born in **1897** — option **(3)** (**4 July 1897**).
So he could not have led the **1879-80** revolt.
xa: Birthplace: **Pandrangi, near Vizianagaram**; ancestral village **Mogallu**.
**125th birth anniversary**: **30-ft bronze statue** at **Bhimavaram**.
Nickname **Chittibabu**; title **"Manyam Veerudu"**.

nee06cdf1e26.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju was born at which of the following places?
nee06cdf1e26.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju was born on 4 July 1897 at Pandrangi, also referred to as Pandarangipeta, near Vizianagaram. Mogallu was his ancestral village.
nee06cdf1e26.tq: Distinguish the birthplace from the ancestral village and later places associated with the leader.
xs: Alluri was born at **Pandrangi (Pandarangipeta), near Vizianagaram** — option **(4)**.
**Mogallu** (West Godavari) was his **ancestral village** — some notes give it as birthplace.
**Koyyuru** = where he was shot; **Krishnadevipeta** = his tomb.
xa: Born **4 July 1897**.
Parents: **Venkataramaraju** and **Suryanarayana Amma**.
APPSC-GS **2025** asked the village; the key showed no answer.

n350b27c51a8.s: In 1921, Alluri Sitarama Raju visited ____ to meet Bengali revolutionaries.
n350b27c51a8.x: Raju visited Chittagong in 1921; he respected Gandhi but believed force was necessary.
xa: He received **guerrilla training** ideas at Chittagong.
Yet he troubled the British more than the **NCM** in that region.
Unlike Gandhian forest satyagrahas, he used **armed guerrilla war**.

nca5ce4a13e9.s: Which lieutenant of Alluri Sitarama Raju was killed on 7 June 1924?
nca5ce4a13e9.x: Gam Gantam Dora was killed on 7 June 1924; Gam Mallu Dora was arrested in 1923 and later became an MP in 1952.
xa: Mallu Dora arrested at **Nadimpalem** (**17 Sept 1923**) by **Keirns**.
**Aggiraju**: arrested **6 May 1924** at the **Maddaru** river.
⚠ **Gantam Dora** = killed **1924**; **Mallu Dora** = MP **1952**.

nf7168e85220.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju is popularly hailed by which title?
nf7168e85220.x: Alluri is 'Manyam Veerudu' (hero of the forest) (APPSC 2024 key). Andhra Shivaji was Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary and Andhra Ratna was Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya; Andhra Kesari was Tanguturi Prakasam.
xs: Alluri is **"Manyam Veerudu"** (hero of the forest) — option **(2)** (APPSC **2024** key).
**"Andhra Shivaji"** = **Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary**; **"Andhra Ratna"** = **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya**.
xa: Alluri's nickname: **Chittibabu**.
Airport: **Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram**.
Agency district named **Alluri Sitarama Raju district**.

n3788efaae22.s: Which British officer was appointed Special Commissioner to crush the Rampa rebellion?
n3788efaae22.x: Rutherford served as Special Commissioner to crush the revolt and ordered the exile of 55 helpers; warrants were issued for 183 persons.
n3788efaae22.tq: Match the officer with the specific administrative post and action.
xs: **Rutherford** was **Special Commissioner** to crush the revolt — option **(4)**.
He **exiled 55 helpers** and issued **warrants for 183**.
**Goodall** = Major at Raju's shooting; **Scott Coward** = officer killed; **Keirns** = arrested Mallu Dora.
xa: ⚠ **Rutherford** appears thrice: Rampa, **Duggirala's trial** (Srikakulam), **Pedanandipadu**.
His Pedanandipadu plan to ban the **Shanti Sena** was **rejected by the Madras Government**.

n2a3f6c3cd89.s: Which Congress leader urged restraint during the Pedanandipadu campaign?
n2a3f6c3cd89.x: Konda Venkatappayya and Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri backed the campaign, whereas Nyapathi Subbarao urged restraint.
xa: Inquiry committee: **T. Prakasam**, **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**, **Dantu Narayana Raju**.
**Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri** also wrote the song "**Kallumanandoy**".
Withdrawn on **11 Feb 1922** after **Gandhi's message** to Konda Venkatappayya.

ne71e0161d6d.s: The Agency district in Andhra Pradesh was renamed as:
ne71e0161d6d.x: The Agency district was named Alluri Sitarama Raju district in recognition of the revolutionary leader’s legacy.
ne71e0161d6d.tq: Test the official name rather than an honorific or regional description.
xs: The Agency district is named **Alluri Sitarama Raju district** — option **(4)**.
"**Manyam Veerudu**" is Alluri's **title** (APPSC **2024** key), not a district name.
xa: Alluri led the **Rampa / Manyam Rebellion**, **January 1922 - May 1924**.
His **30-ft bronze statue** stands at **Bhimavaram** (**125th birth anniversary**).
The **Bhogapuram** airport (Vizianagaram) is also named after him.

n3f5f530d44b.s: The immediate cause of the Rekapalle rebellion was:
o: The introduction of the Madras Forest Act in the Agency areas
The dismissal of tribal leaders from government service
The increase of the axe tax on podu from 4 annas to 4–12 annas during a famine
The erosion of the authority of the muttadars by Madhava Bhupati
n3f5f530d44b.x: The Rekapalle rebellion was triggered by the increase of the axe tax on podu from 4 annas to 4–12 annas during a famine.
n3f5f530d44b.tq: Distinguish the tax-based cause of Rekapalle from the administrative cause of Rampa.
xs: Rekapalle's cause: the **axe tax on podu** raised from **4 annas to 4-12 annas** during a **famine** — option **(3)**.
**Madhava Bhupati's** erosion of the muttadars caused **Rampa**; the **Forest Act (1882)** came later.
xa: Place: **Rekapalle, Bhadrachalam taluk**, Godavari district.
Leader **Ambul Reddy**; **Vaddagudem** PS attacked **10 July 1879**.
Crushed **Sept 1879**.

n968b9055722.s: Who was associated with both the Rampa and Rekapalle rebellions of the Godavari region?
n968b9055722.x: Ambul Reddy was associated with both; Alluri led the later Rampa rebellion of 1922-24.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly credit Alluri with the 1879-80 revolt.
**1879** = "the year of the Rampa Revolution".
Rampa leaders: **Chandrayya**, **Sambaiah**, **Tammanna Dora**.

n7dbca5d8ced.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju was popularly known by the nickname:
n7dbca5d8ced.x: Chittibabu was his nickname; his ancestral village was Mogallu and his biographer Erramalli Narasimha Rao.
xa: Title: **"Manyam Veerudu"** (APPSC **2024** key).
**1919**: hut at **Kongasingi near Krishnadevipeta**.
Born at **Pandrangi**, near Vizianagaram.

n038de23c725.s: The AICC meeting of 1921 that helped put Gandhi's programme into Andhra was held at:
n038de23c725.x: The Bezawada AICC meeting of 1921 helped put Gandhi's programme into Andhra.
xa: **Delhi AICC (5 Nov 1921)**: provinces could take up **no-tax** → Guntur did.
**1921-22 Guntur** saw the NCM's most original methods in Andhra.

n71c6861959b.s: Who founded the Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi near Chirala?
n71c6861959b.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya founded the Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi near Chirala.
n71c6861959b.tq: Match the institution with its founder while avoiding confusion with other Andhra leaders.
xs: **Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya** founded the **Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi** near **Chirala** — option **(1)**.
He resigned as professor at **Rajahmundry Government College** to promote **national education**.
**Bezawada Gopala Reddy** abolished the Chirala-Perala municipality in **1938**.
xa: Born **2 June**, **Penuganchiprolu (Krishna district)**; **1884-1929**.
Titles: **"Andhra Ratna"**, "Ramadasu".
Volunteer corps: **Ramadandu (1921)**.

n152f84dd0e0.s: Who introduced Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya to Gandhi in London in 1915?
n152f84dd0e0.x: Ananda K. Coomaraswamy introduced Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya to Gandhi in London in 1915 and described him as the coming man of his country.
n152f84dd0e0.tq: Apply the person-introduced-person trap to a specific political meeting.
xs: **Ananda K. Coomaraswamy** introduced him to Gandhi in **London (1915)** — option **(2)**.
He called Duggirala **"the coming man of your country"**.
xa: Duggirala: **M.A. (Hons) Economics, Edinburgh, 1916**.
Later led **Chirala-Perala (1921)**.
Joined the **Swaraj Party** (C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru).

nb0e98b9318e.s: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya's volunteer corps at Chirala-Perala (1921) was called:
nb0e98b9318e.x: His volunteer corps was the Ramadandu (APPSC 2019 key); the Shanti Sena of Pedanandipadu was led by Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **Ramadandu**, not Shanti Sena.
Veeraiah Chowdary = **"Andhra Shivaji"**.
Shanti Sena formation decided by **Guntur DCC, Dec 1921**.

n56d10500860.s: The Chirala-Perala Satyagraha arose primarily because:
o: The British prohibited the Ramadandu from holding public meetings.
The villages were brought under the Forest Act and denied podu rights.
The two villages were converted into a municipality and their annual tax burden increased sharply.
The residents were forced to migrate to the Gudem hills.
n56d10500860.x: Chirala and Perala were made a municipality, and the annual tax rose from Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000, provoking the movement.
n56d10500860.tq: Match the movement with its immediate administrative and fiscal trigger.
xs: Chirala and Perala were made a **municipality**, and the **tax** rose sharply — option **(3)**.
Tax rose from **Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000** a year.
The **Forest Act/podu** grievance and **Gudem hills** belong to the Rampa rebellion.
xa: Municipality proposed **Nov 1919**, formed **Jan 1920**.
Residents: weavers and small farmers, ~**15,000**.
Municipality **abolished in 1938** by **Bezawada Gopala Reddy**.

nd35d7bf0fe5.s: During the Chirala-Perala movement, residents set up a camp outside municipal limits called:
nd35d7bf0fe5.x: The residents set up Ramnagar (Ramanagaram) with a parallel all-caste assembly and arbitration court; it lasted about 11 months.
xa: Exodus on Gandhi's advice: **25 April 1921**.
Failure: **lack of funds**, Congress jealousy, no second line of leaders.
Gandhi wrote in **Young India** that the municipality only meant more taxes.

n82294bf6c0c.s: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was arrested on 1 October 1921 primarily because he:
o: Broke a ban on public speaking after his Berhampur speech
Organised an armed raid in the Gudem hills
Refused to pay the municipal tax
n82294bf6c0c.x: After his Berhampur speech, Duggirala was prohibited from speaking for two months. He defied the ban and was arrested on 1 October 1921.
n82294bf6c0c.tq: Link the arrest to the specific act that violated the colonial order.
xs: Duggirala **broke a ban on public speaking** after his **Berhampur** speech — option **(1)**.
After the **Andhra Mahasabha, Berhampur (Sept 1921)**, he was banned from speaking for **2** months.
Arrested **1 October 1921**.
xa: Tried by **Rutherford** at **Srikakulam**; jailed **1 year**.
⚠ Some notes place the arrest at **Trichinopoly**.
Donations: Srinivasa Ayyangar **Rs 1,000**, APCC **Rs 3,000**, Guntur DCC **Rs 250**.

nf0155861322.s: The municipality of Chirala and Perala was abolished in 1938 during the ministry of:
o: Rajagopalachari, with Bezawada Gopala Reddy as minister concerned
Tanguturi Prakasam, with Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya as minister concerned
P. Subbarayan, with Konda Venkatappayya as minister concerned
Bobbili Raja, with Bezawada Gopala Reddy as minister concerned
nf0155861322.x: The municipality was abolished in 1938 during the Rajaji ministry, when Bezawada Gopala Reddy was the Local Self-Government Minister.
nf0155861322.tq: Match the administrative outcome with the correct ministry and minister instead of swapping office-holders.
xs: The Chirala-Perala municipality was abolished in **1938** under the **Rajagopalachari (Rajaji) ministry**, with **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** as minister — option **(1)**.
Gopala Reddy held the **Local Self-Government** portfolio, which covered municipalities.
**Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya** led the agitation; he was never a minister (he died in **1929**).
xa: The municipality was formed in **Jan 1920**; tax rose from **Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000** a year.
**Gandhi** wrote in **Young India** that the municipality only meant more taxes.
After the movement failed, the **people returned** to their homes.

n3e0858f1586.s: The book *Chirala Perala Vanavasam* was written by:
n3e0858f1586.x: *Chirala Perala Vanavasam* was written by Pisapati Narayana Sastri.
n3e0858f1586.tq: Use the author–work association and reject names linked with other events in the same region.
xs: ***Chirala Perala Vanavasam*** was written by **Pisapati Narayana Sastri** — option **(2)**.
**Erramalli Narasimha Rao** is the biographer of **Alluri Sitarama Raju**, not of Chirala-Perala.
**Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya** led the movement; **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** abolished the municipality in **1938**.
xa: **"Malapalli"** novel — **Unnava Lakshminarayana**; **Desabhakti Geyam** — **Gurajada Apparao**.
"**Kallumanandoy**" — **Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri**; "**Veera gandham tecchinaramu**" — **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy**.
National pledge "**Bharata Desam Naa Matrubhoomi**" — **Paidimarri Venkata Subbarao**.

n55cb36f22be.s: During the Pedanandipadu campaign, Rutherford's proposal to ban which body was rejected by the Madras Government?
n55cb36f22be.x: Rutherford was deployed to deal with the campaign, but his proposal to ban the Shanti Sena was rejected.
xa: Collector **A. Gellatly** blamed **low pay and workload** for the resignations.
As **Special Commissioner** in Rampa, Rutherford **exiled 55 helpers** and issued warrants for **183**.
Rutherford also tried **Duggirala** at **Srikakulam**.

n0c2071732be.s: At which village was Kanneganti Hanumanthu killed in police firing during the Palnadu pullari movement?
n0c2071732be.x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu was killed in police firing at Minchalapadu during the Palnadu pullari movement.
n0c2071732be.tq: Distinguish the leader’s death place from the other villages connected with the same movement.
xs: **Kanneganti Hanumanthu** was killed at **Minchalapadu** — option **(2)**.
The **Palnad pullari (grass tax)** movement covered **Macherla, Veldurthi, Sirigiripadu, Minchalapadu**.
xa: Supported by **Unnava Lakshmi Narayana**.
Palnadu forest satyagraha = local version of the **NCM** call.

n6c955657a3c.s: The Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign was suspended after the Guntur District Congress Committee received Gandhi’s message to Konda Venkatappayya on:
n6c955657a3c.x: Gandhi’s message to suspend the campaign reached the Guntur District Congress Committee on 11 February 1922, after which the campaign ended with the Non-Cooperation Movement.
n6c955657a3c.tq: Match the precise date with the final administrative action in the campaign.
xs: Gandhi's suspension message reached the Guntur DCC on **11 February 1922** — option **(2)**.
**5 Nov 1921** was the **Delhi AICC**, which allowed **no-tax** civil disobedience.
**6 Dec 1922** was Alluri's defeat at **Peddagaddapalem**; **7 May 1924** was **Alluri's** death.
xa: The campaign then **ended with the NCM**.
The **Bezawada AICC (1921)** put Gandhi's programme into Andhra.
Gandhi's message was sent to **Konda Venkatappayya**.

nd6aef4900f8.s: In the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign (1922), how many of the 19 village officers in the firka resigned?
nd6aef4900f8.x: 18 of 19 village officers resigned, and the Shanti Sena was formed.
xa: Resignations were led by Chandavolu karanam **Machiraju Ramamurthy**.
Shanti Sena in the firka was led by **Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary**.
Guntur district saw **29** resignations in all.

n1c0928c0313.s: Which period is called the 'Glorious Decade' of Andhra?
n1c0928c0313.x: 1921-31 is called the 'Glorious Decade' of Andhra.
xa: Local Congress **rivalry** and **money shortage** sank Chirala-Perala.
**Gandhi's halt** ended Pedanandipadu at its peak.
Unlike Gandhian forest satyagrahas, **Alluri** used **armed guerrilla war**, yet respected Gandhi.

nap-history-13-4.s: The Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign was led by:
nap-history-13-4.x: Pedanandipadu in Bapatla taluk, Guntur, ran a no-tax campaign in 1921-22 led by Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary.
n: The no-tax campaign was associated with Pedanandipadu. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 18-19]
Pedanandipadu was located in Bapatla taluka. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 18-19]
Pedanandipadu was located in Guntur district. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 18-19]
Pedanandipadu was associated with Paravataneni Veerayya Chowdary. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 18-19]
xa: Unique feature: **mass resignation of village officers** — **18 of 19** in the firka.
**Shanti Sena** was led by Parvataneni, called "**Andhra Shivaji**".
Withdrawn on **11 Feb 1922** on **Gandhi's message**.

n96ae2fc39be.s: Who was the first editor of Andhra Patrika during 1916–18?
n96ae2fc39be.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao served as the first editor of Andhra Patrika during 1916–18; Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was its founder.
n96ae2fc39be.tq: Distinguish the founder from the first editor of the same newspaper.
xs: The first editor of **Andhra Patrika** (**1916-18**) was **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** — option **(3)**.
**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** was its **founder**, not first editor.
**Mutnuri Krishna Rao** edited **Krishna Patrika**; **Tanguturi Prakasam** ran **Swarajya**.
xa: **Swarajya** daily began on **29 Oct 1921**.
**Desamata** — **Chilakamarti Lakshminarasimham**.
**Zamin Rythu** — **Nellore Venkataramana Naidu**.

na780d958942.s: Which work was written by Unnava Lakshminarayana?
na780d958942.x: Unnava Lakshminarayana wrote the novel Malapalli.
na780d958942.tq: Distinguish literary authors by matching each work with its correct creator.
xs: **Unnava Lakshminarayana** wrote the novel **"Malapalli"** — option **(4)**.
"**Bharata Desam Naa Matrubhoomi**" is by **Paidimarri Venkata Subbarao**; **Desabhakti Geyam** is by **Gurajada Apparao**.
xa: Unnava founded **Sharada Niketan, Guntur** with wife **Lakshmibayamma**.
"**Bharata Khandambu Chakkani Padi Aavu**" — **Chilakamarti Lakshminarasimham**.
***Chirala Perala Vanavasam*** — **Pisapati Narayana Sastri**.

n7a75c409e6e.s: The ‘Desasevikalu’ organisation was associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Promotion of forest administration under the colonial government
Non-violent reform and propaganda for Swaraj
Armed revolutionary training and military recruitment
n7a75c409e6e.x: Desasevikalu was a women’s organisation within the Congress that pledged itself to non-violent reform and Swaraj propaganda.
n7a75c409e6e.tq: Infer the organisation’s purpose from its ideological and organisational setting.
xs: **Desasevikalu** was pledged to **non-violent reform and Swaraj propaganda** — option **(3)**.
It was a **women's organisation within Congress**, not a forest, tax or armed body.
xa: **Andhra Mahila Sabha** was founded by **Durgabai Deshmukh** (Madras, **1937**).
**12 women** were jailed at Chirala-Perala; the first was **Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma**.
**Duvvuri Subbamma** (**Desabandhavi**) was also arrested.

n2bd402c1f0c.s: “Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi aavu” was improvised on which occasion?
o: During the Salt Satyagraha at Dandi in 1930
During Bipin Chandra Pal’s speeches at Rajahmundry in April 1907
During the Home Rule agitation in Madras in 1916
During Gandhi’s visit to Vijayawada in 1921
n2bd402c1f0c.x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham improvised the song during Bipin Chandra Pal’s speeches at Rajahmundry in April 1907.
n2bd402c1f0c.tq: Lock the answer through the distinctive place, speaker and month-year combination.
xs: **"Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi aavu"** was improvised during **Bipin Chandra Pal's speeches at Rajahmundry, April 1907** — option **(2)**.
**Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham** was translating Pal's speeches when he composed it.
The song cast **India as a cow** whose milk the British were taking.
xa: His later verse: "**Bharata khandambe okka pedda bandikhana**".
Chilakamarti is called the **first Telugu national poet**; he edited **Desamata**.
The song was an APPSC **G2 2019** key question.

n1bc6aa48fd3.s: The lines “Desamunu preminchumanna, manchi annadi penchumanna” are associated with which poet and collection?
n1bc6aa48fd3.x: The lines were written by Gurajada Apparao and form part of Mutyala Saralu. The poem was published in Andhra Bharati.
n1bc6aa48fd3.tq: Use the poet–work pair directly; nearby nationalist poets are used as distractors.
xs: "**Desamunu preminchumanna**" is by **Gurajada Apparao**, in ***Mutyala Saralu*** — option **(4)**.
**Harijana Paatalu** is Garimella's; **Andhravali** is Rayaprolu's; **Matru Desa Sankeertanam** is Duvvuri Ramireddy's.
xa: The poem was published in **Andhra Bharati** and called the "**national anthem of Telugu people**".
Same poem: "**Desamante matti kadoi, desamante manushuloi**".
⚠ **Garimella** = "Maakoddee"; **Tripuraneni** = "Veera gandham".

n25204127cfd.s: 'Desamante matti kadoi, desamante manushuloi' was written by:
n25204127cfd.x: Gurajada's line in Mutyala Saralu means a nation is its people, not merely its soil.
xa: The poem was called the "**national anthem of Telugu people**".
Gurajada made **vyavaharika bhasha** (spoken Telugu) normal.
Gurajada also wrote ***Kanyasulkam*** (staged **1893**).

nfda82163c08.s: Garimella Satyanarayana left his studies in response to whose call?
o: Bipin Chandra Pal’s call for Swadeshi
Sri Sri’s call for progressive literature
Rayaprolu Subba Rao’s call for romantic poetry
nfda82163c08.x: Garimella Satyanarayana left his studies in response to Mahatma Gandhi’s call during the freedom movement.
nfda82163c08.tq: Identify the leader associated with the decisive personal action.
xs: **Garimella Satyanarayana** left his studies at **Mahatma Gandhi's call** — option **(2)**.
He was born at **Gonedapadu**, Narasannapeta taluk (**Srikakulam**).
xa: Life: **14 July 1893 to 18 Dec 1952**.
His song "**Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu**" was **praised by Gandhi**.
He is the **first people's poet** of the freedom struggle.

n628f140bed1.s: 'Ma Telugu Talliki mallepoodanda', which later became the AP State song, was written by:
n628f140bed1.x: Sankarambadi Sundarachari wrote it; Garimella wrote Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu and Basavaraju Apparao Kollayi gattithenemi.
xa: ⚠ **Gurajada** = "Desamunu preminchumanna"; **Garimella** = "Maakoddee".
Basavaraju Apparao was also a **Bhava Kavitvam** poet.

ne1544f226f5.s: Why did nationalist songs in spoken Telugu have a wider social reach than pamphlets?
o: They were written exclusively in classical prosody
They avoided political and social themes
They were restricted to educated urban readers
They could reach villagers who could not be reached effectively by pamphlets
ne1544f226f5.x: Songs in spoken Telugu could reach villagers more effectively than pamphlets, thereby widening nationalist communication.
ne1544f226f5.tq: Apply the communication advantage of spoken-language literature to a social situation.
xs: Songs in **spoken Telugu** could **reach villagers that pamphlets could not** — option **(4)**.
They were not bound to **classical prosody** or to urban readers; that is exactly why they spread.
xa: **Gurajada** made **vyavaharika bhasha** normal in literature.
Garimella's "**Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu**" was **cyclostyled a thousand times**.
Progressive writers later widened the attack to **caste and class**.

n04cde23b4f8.s: Who wrote the patriotic lyric “Ye desamegina ... pogadara nee talli bhoomi Bharatini”, commonly known by its title Janmabhoomi?
n04cde23b4f8.x: The patriotic lyric Janmabhoomi was written by Rayaprolu Subbarao.
n04cde23b4f8.tq: Identify the author from a distinctive line and title.
xs: The lyric ***Janmabhoomi*** ("Ye desamegina ... pogadara nee talli bhoomi Bharatini") is by **Rayaprolu Subbarao** — option **(3)**.
**Sankarambadi Sundarachari** wrote "**Ma Telugu Talliki**"; **Basavaraju Apparao** wrote "**Kollayi gattithenemi**".
xa: Rayaprolu was born in **1892**, **Guntur**.
He is the **Father of Telugu Romanticism** and founder of **Bhavakavitvam**.
His works: ***Andhravali***, ***Swatantrya Rathamu***.

n31e024257e2.s: Who is called the Father of Telugu Romanticism?
n31e024257e2.x: Rayaprolu Subba Rao pioneered Bhava Kavitvam, drawing on Shelley and Keats.
xa: Rayaprolu's title: **Abhinava Nannaya** (APPSC **G2 2025** key).
He freed Telugu verse from **rigid prosody**.

n54797f4ab5f.s: Which of the following best describes Rayaprolu Subba Rao’s contribution to Telugu poetry?
o: He restored rigid prosody as the sole basis of Telugu poetry.
He replaced original verse with exclusively devotional compositions.
He moved away from translation of Sanskrit epics and introduced original, emotive verse.
He continued translating Sanskrit epics without alteration.
n54797f4ab5f.x: Rayaprolu broke with the translation of Sanskrit epics and brought original, emotive verse into Telugu. He also helped free Telugu poetry from rigid prosody.
n54797f4ab5f.tq: Choose the option that captures the complete literary change rather than an isolated label.
xs: Rayaprolu **moved away from translating Sanskrit epics** to **original, emotive verse** — option **(3)**.
He **freed** Telugu verse from **rigid prosody**, the opposite of option (1).
xa: New concept: **Amalina Srungaram** (**platonic love**).
⚠ Progressive writers like **Sri Sri** called his romanticism "**escapist**".
Main Bhava poets: **Basavaraju Apparao**, **Duvvuri Ramireddy**, **Devulapalli Krishna Sastri**.

n560002d6f48.x: Bhavakavitvam emphasised romantic and personal emotion, nature and love, and sought freedom from classical prosody.
xa: Founder: **Rayaprolu Subbarao**; key concept **Amalina Srungaram** (platonic love).
**Venkata Parvateeswara Kavulu** — **Ekanta Seva**, the "**Telugu Gitanjali**".

n1fdaa674ae9.s: Garimella Satyanarayana's nationalist song was cyclostyled a thousand times and praised by:
n1fdaa674ae9.x: The song was cyclostyled a thousand times and praised by Mahatma Gandhi.
xa: It grew to **162 lines**.
Garimella was jailed in **1922**, and later served **2.5 years RI**.

nbad786a94e0.s: Garimella Satyanarayana is described as which of the following?
o: The first people’s poet of the freedom struggle
nbad786a94e0.x: Garimella Satyanarayana is called the first people’s poet of the freedom struggle.
nbad786a94e0.tq: Distinguish a popular descriptive title from titles belonging to other Telugu literary figures.
xs: Garimella is called the **first people's poet of the freedom struggle** — option **(1)**.
The **Father of Telugu Romanticism** is **Rayaprolu Subbarao**; the first Telugu Jnanpith went to **Viswanatha**.
xa: Garimella's song: "**Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu**" (Non-Cooperation era).
⚠ **Gurajada** = "Desamunu preminchumanna"; **Tripuraneni** = "Veera gandham".

n77302231eb7.s: Garimella Satyanarayana was jailed in 1922 for his song:
n77302231eb7.x: He was jailed in 1922 for Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu and later served 2.5 years RI.
xa: Life: **14 July 1893 to 18 Dec 1952**.
Other works: **Harijana Paatalu**, **Samajika Navala**, **Palletullalo**.

nf902de69478.x: Unnava wrote Malapalli; Gurajada wrote Kanyasulkam, Viswanatha Veyipadagalu and Rayaprolu Andhravali.
xa: Rayaprolu also wrote ***Swatantrya Rathamu***; Gurajada also ***Mutyala Saralu***, ***Desabhakti Geyam***.
Viswanatha's ***Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu*** won the **Jnanpith**, the first for a Telugu writer.

n2587f4df61c.s: Which literary development is associated with Gurajada in the growth of Telugu nationalist and progressive writing?
o: Banning all patriotic songs from public performance
Making vyavaharika bhasha a normal literary medium
Restoring exclusive dependence on classical prosody
Limiting Telugu literature to court poetry
n2587f4df61c.x: Gurajada helped make vyavaharika bhasha, or spoken Telugu, a normal literary medium.
n2587f4df61c.tq: Identify the specific linguistic contribution rather than a broad political claim.
xs: **Gurajada** made **vyavaharika bhasha** (spoken Telugu) a normal literary medium — option **(2)**.
He moved away from classical diction; he did not restore **classical prosody** or court poetry.
xa: His poem "**Desamunu preminchumanna**" (***Mutyala Saralu***) is the "**national anthem of Telugu people**".
His play ***Kanyasulkam*** was staged in **1893**.
Progressive writers later widened the attack to **caste and class**.

na1afc55982f.s: Which is recognised as the first Telugu national song?
na1afc55982f.x: “Hinduvulara ennaallee gati” by Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham, the first Telugu national poet, is recognised as the first Telugu national song.
xa: **First Telugu national poet**: **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham**.
Often called the first nationalist song: "**The Cry of Mother India**" (**Krishna Patrika**, **15 Dec 1905**).
⚠ Per **C. Narayana Reddy**, the first is "**Melukonumi Bharata Putruda**" (**Andhra Bharati**, Oct **1909**).

nb8e01780bbe.s: Which song, published in Krishna Patrika on 15 December 1905, is often called the first nationalist song in Telugu?
nb8e01780bbe.x: The Cry of Mother India (Krishna Patrika, 15 Dec 1905) is often called the first nationalist song. C. Narayana Reddy instead gave that place to Melukonumi Bharata Putruda (Andhra Bharati, Oct 1909). Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi aavu was Chilakamarti's verse at Bipin Chandra Pal's Rajahmundry speeches (1907), and Desamunu preminchumanna is Gurajada's song in Mutyala Saralu.
nb8e01780bbe.tq: 1905 Krishna Patrika = Cry of Mother India; 1909 Andhra Bharati = Melukonumi (C. Narayana Reddy's choice).
xs: "**The Cry of Mother India**" (**Krishna Patrika**, **15 Dec 1905**) is often called the first nationalist song — option **(1)**.
**C. Narayana Reddy** instead names "**Melukonumi Bharata Putruda**" (**Andhra Bharati**, Oct **1909**).
"**Bharata khandambu**" was Chilakamarti's **1907** song; "**Desamunu preminchumanna**" is **Gurajada's**.
xa: **First Telugu national song**: "**Hinduvulara ennaallee gati**".
**First Telugu national poet**: **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham**.

n22b0e0c5130.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of poets identified as major poets of Bhavakavitvam?
o: Basavaraju Apparao, Duvvuri Ramireddy, Devulapalli Krishna Sastri
Gurajada Apparao, Garimella Satyanarayana, Sri Sri
Bipin Chandra Pal, Rayaprolu Subbarao, Damaraju Pundarikakshudu
Kopparapu Subbarao, Krovvidi Lingaraju, Madduri Annapurnaiah
n22b0e0c5130.x: Basavaraju Apparao, Duvvuri Ramireddy and Devulapalli Krishna Sastri are listed among the main poets of Bhavakavitvam.
n22b0e0c5130.tq: Identify the complete group by separating movement poets from associated nationalist figures and prose contributors.
xs: **Basavaraju Apparao, Duvvuri Ramireddy, Devulapalli Krishna Sastri** are main Bhava Kavitvam poets — option **(1)**.
**Sri Sri** criticised the school as escapist; **Garimella** was the people's poet of the freedom struggle.
**Kopparapu Subbarao** (Roshanara), **Krovvidi Lingaraju** (Veerabali) wrote **proscribed** works.
xa: Another main Bhava poet group: **Venkata Parvateeswara Kavulu** (**Ekanta Seva**).
Basavaraju Apparao also wrote "**Kollayi gattithenemi maa Gandhi**".

n06eddacf175.s: The Venkata Parvateeswara Kavulu are associated with which work, described as the “Telugu Gitanjali”?
n06eddacf175.x: Ekanta Seva, associated with the Venkata Parvateeswara Kavulu, is described as the “Telugu Gitanjali”.
n06eddacf175.tq: Match the literary group with its distinctive work and description.
xs: The **Venkata Parvateeswara Kavulu** wrote **Ekanta Seva**, the "**Telugu Gitanjali**" — option **(2)**.
**Roshanara**, **Tirugubatu** and **Veerabali** are **proscribed** works.
xa: They are among the **main poets** of **Bhava Kavitvam**.
Other main Bhava poets: **Basavaraju Apparao**, **Duvvuri Ramireddy**, **Devulapalli Krishna Sastri**.

n8f8cd263aba.s: Which of the following works was written by Duvvuri Ramireddy?
n8f8cd263aba.x: Matru Desa Sankeertanam was written by Duvvuri Ramireddy. Swatantrya Rathamu is by Rayaprolu, Desabhakti Geyam by Gurajada, and Firdausi by Gurram Jashuva.
n8f8cd263aba.tq: Use direct author–work recall with works from neighbouring poets as distractors.
xs: **Matru Desa Sankeertanam** was written by **Duvvuri Ramireddy** — option **(1)**.
**Firdausi** is **Gurram Jashuva's**; **Swatantrya Rathamu** is **Rayaprolu's**; **Desabhakti Geyam** is **Gurajada's**.
xa: Duvvuri Ramireddy's title: "**Kavi Kokila**".
He was a main poet of **Bhava Kavitvam**.

na60293c1917.s: Who wrote Japaneeyamu, which celebrated Japan’s victory over Russia in 1905?
na60293c1917.x: Japaneeyamu was written by Sriram Veerabrahmam of Bandar and celebrated Japan’s victory over Russia in 1905.
na60293c1917.tq: Match the world event and patriotic work with the correct author.
xs: **Japaneeyamu** was written by **Sriram Veerabrahmam** (Bandar) — option **(4)**.
It celebrated **Japan's victory over Russia (1905)**.
**Adipudi Somanatha Rao** wrote **Japan Charitra**; **Damaraju Pundarikakshudu** wrote **Panchala Parabhavam**; **Umar Alisha** wrote **Mahabharata Kaurava Rangam**.
xa: Japan Charitra was dedicated to the **Raja of Munagala**, who named his sons **Togo and Nogi**.
Japaneeyamu — Sriram Veerabrahmam was asked in the **G2 2025** match.

n4875553048b.s: In the play 'Panchala Parabhavam' on the Jallianwala Bagh tragedy, General Dyer was portrayed as:
n4875553048b.x: Damaraju Pundarikakshudu's play cast Dyer as Duryodhana; 25 Vizag students were arrested for staging it.
xa: The play was **discussed in the British Parliament**.
**Padmavyuham** — **Kallakuri Narayana Rao** (**1919**).
**Mahabharata Kaurava Rangam** — **Umar Alisha** (**1916**).

nd5ea38a77fb.s: Which of the following was the first Telugu play banned by the British?
nd5ea38a77fb.x: Roshanara, authored by Kopparapu Subbarao, was the first Telugu play banned by the British.
nd5ea38a77fb.tq: Use the superlative clue “first” and distinguish the action from later arrests and prosecutions.
xs: ***Roshanara*** by **Kopparapu Subbarao** was the **first play banned** by the British — option **(1)**.
**Veerabali** (Krovvidi Lingaraju, **1931**) and **Chicharapidugu** (**1927-29**) came later.
**Panchala Parabhavam** led to performers' arrest in **Vizag**.
xa: **Tirugubatu** (Muni Manikyam Narasimha Rao) was banned for "**inciting the people**".
**Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu** (Garimella, **1922**) — author jailed.

n0a194a0d57b.s: Chicharapidugu was serialised during which period in Congress, and what consequence followed for its editor?
o: 1907–08; the work was banned as the first Telugu play
n0a194a0d57b.x: Chicharapidugu was serialised in Congress from 1927 to 1929, and its editor Madduri Annapurnaiah was jailed.
n0a194a0d57b.tq: Pair the publication period with the correct person and consequence.
xs: **Chicharapidugu** was serialised **1927-29** in **Congress**; editor **Madduri Annapurnaiah** was jailed — option **(2)**.
Its author was **Ramachandruni Venkatappayya**.
xa: **Veerabali** — **Krovvidi Lingaraju**, **1931**, jailed for sedition (**Sec. 124A**).
***Roshanara*** — **Kopparapu Subbarao**, **first play banned**.

n10b42703ee0.s: Which Telugu poet is known by the title 'Abhinava Nannaya'?
n10b42703ee0.x: The accepted examination answer is Rayaprolu Subbarao. Although another source assigns the title to Viswanatha, the commission’s key and CDI assign it to Rayaprolu.
n10b42703ee0.tq: Resolve a source-sensitive title by remembering the examination-key convention rather than the conflicting attribution.
xs: The commission's key gives "**Abhinava Nannaya**" to **Rayaprolu Subbarao** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Some notes give it to **Viswanatha**, but Viswanatha's title is **Kavi Samrat**.
xa: **Kavi Kokila** — **Duvvuri Ramireddy**.
**Andhra Shelley** — **Devulapalli Krishna Sastri**.
**Telugu Lenka** — **Tummala Sitaramamurthy**.
n10b42703ee0.fixed: odd meta wording about 'commission's key'; y00a6c6b993a

n3e57742e746.s: Which Telugu poet was known as 'Andhra Shelley'?
n3e57742e746.x: Devulapalli Krishna Sastri was Andhra Shelley; Duvvuri Ramireddy was Kavi Kokila and Tummala Telugu Lenka.
xa: **Maha Kavi** — **Sri Sri**; **Boyi Bhimanna** also received "Mahakavi".
**Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti** — **Gurram Jashuva** (**1946**).

nfb3236ed080.s: Who is popularly known by the title 'Maha Kavi' in the context of Telugu progressive literature?
nfb3236ed080.x: Sri Sri is popularly known as 'Maha Kavi'. Boyi Bhimanna also received the title 'Mahakavi'.
nfb3236ed080.tq: Directly associate a popular title with its principal poet.
xs: **Sri Sri** is popularly known as "**Maha Kavi**" — option **(2)**.
**Boyi Bhimanna** also received "**Mahakavi**", but Sri Sri is the standard answer.
**Gurram Jashuva** is **Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti**; **Viswanatha** is **Kavi Samrat**.
xa: Sri Sri wrote **Mahaprasthanam** (**G2 2025** match).
⚠ "**Poet of the Millennium**" is disputed: G2 2025 key — **Jashuva**; APHQ book — **Sri Sri**.

n16289166e5e.s: Which of the following is NOT a work or category associated with Garimella Satyanarayana?
n16289166e5e.x: Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu was written by Viswanatha Satyanarayana. Garimella’s works included Harijana Paatalu, anti-liquor songs, Samajika Navala and Palletullalo.
n16289166e5e.tq: Use the author–work association to reject a famous work belonging to another poet.
xs: **Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu** is not Garimella's — option **(3)**; it is **Viswanatha Satyanarayana's** Jnanpith-winning work.
Garimella's works: **Harijana Paatalu**, **anti-liquor songs**, **Samajika Navala**, **Palletullalo**.
xa: ⚠ Viswanatha's Jnanpith was the **first for a Telugu writer**.
Garimella inspired **Nazar**, **Subbarao Panigrahi** and **Gaddar**.

n934a75ef290.s: The first Jnanpith-winning work by a Telugu writer was:
n934a75ef290.x: Viswanatha's Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu won the Jnanpith, the first for a Telugu writer; Veyipadagalu received Sahitya Akademi recognition.
xa: Viswanatha's title is **Kavi Samrat**.
Viswanatha gave the title "**Madhurakavi**" to **Gurram Jashuva** (**G2 2012** key).

nap-history-15-6.s: Which work is regarded as the first Telugu novel?
nap-history-15-6.x: Rajasekhara Charitram by Kandukuri Veeresalingam is regarded as the first Telugu novel. Vivekavardhini and Satihita Bodhini were his journals, and Asamarthuni Yatra was Gopichand's 1947 novel.
n: Rajasekhara Charitram is a novel. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Rajasekhara Charitram is the first Telugu novel. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
Rajasekhara Charitram was written by Kandukuri Veeresalingam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 20-22]
xs: The first Telugu novel is **Rajasekhara Charitram** — option **(1)**.
It was written by **Kandukuri Veeresalingam**.
**Asamarthuni Jeevitha Yatra** (**1947**) by **T. Gopichand** is the **first psychological novel** in Telugu.
xa: **Kanyasulkam** — **Gurajada Appa Rao**, staged **1893**.
**Veyipadagalu** — **Viswanatha Satyanarayana**; his **Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu** won the first Jnanpith for a Telugu writer.
**Neeti Chandrika** — **Chinnaya Suri**.

n608db78ec7f.s: The Abhyudaya Rachayitala Sangham, popularly known as Arasam, was formed in:
n608db78ec7f.x: Arasam, the Telugu Progressive Writers' Association, was formed in 1943.
n608db78ec7f.tq: Test the founding year of a literary organisation against nearby movement dates.
xs: **Arasam** (**Abhyudaya Rachayitala Sangham**) was formed in **1943** — option **(3)**.
**1936** is the **AIPWA** (Lucknow); **1970** is **Virasam** (Hyderabad).
xa: Arasam was the AIPWA's **Telugu counterpart**.
It organised the **Abhyudaya** current started by **Sri Sri's** poems.
⚠ Arasam = **progressive**; Virasam = **revolutionary** (Viplava).

n86de7202c82.s: The All India Progressive Writers' Association was founded at Lucknow in:
n86de7202c82.x: The All India Progressive Writers' Association was founded at Lucknow in 1936.
n86de7202c82.tq: Pair the organisation's founding venue with its year.
xs: The **AIPWA** was founded at **Lucknow** in **1936** — option **(2)**.
**1943** is **Arasam**, its Telugu counterpart.
xa: The founding session was **presided by Premchand**.
Through the **AIPWA** and the **AISF**, communists spread anti-British revolutionary ideas.

n812db529a20.s: Who presided over the founding session of the All India Progressive Writers' Association?
n812db529a20.x: Premchand presided over the founding session of the All India Progressive Writers' Association at Lucknow.
n812db529a20.tq: Use the presiding-person trap in organisational history.
xs: **Premchand** presided over the AIPWA's founding (**1936, Lucknow**) — option **(2)**.
**Sri Sri** was the **Founding President** of **Virasam** (**1970**), not the AIPWA.
xa: Arasam (**1943**) was the AIPWA's **Telugu counterpart**.
Communists used the **AIPWA** and **AISF** to spread anti-British ideas.

na5822aeb4ac.s: Which sequence correctly represents the broad transition in Telugu progressive and revolutionary literary activity?
o: Virasam — Arasam — nationalist poetry — class struggle
Abhyudaya through Arasam — Viplava through Virasam — class struggle
Class struggle — nationalist poetry — Arasam — Virasam
AIPWA — Praja Natya Mandali — Arasam — nationalist poetry
na5822aeb4ac.x: The broad path ran from Abhyudaya literature through Arasam in the 1930s–40s to Viplava literature through Virasam in 1970, with Telugu poetry moving from nationalism towards class struggle.
na5822aeb4ac.tq: Arrange the movement's ideological development from earlier to later stages.
xs: **Abhyudaya (Arasam) → Viplava (Virasam) → class struggle** — option **(2)**.
Abhyudaya ran in the **1930s-40s** via **Arasam**; Viplava began in **1970** via **Virasam**, after **Srikakulam**.
Telugu poetry turned **from the nationalist to the class struggle**.
xa: Founding Abhyudaya text: ***Mahaprasthanam***; Viplava-phase text: ***Maro Prasthanam***.

nef6366d99f2.s: Which organisation organised the Abhyudaya current associated with the beginning of Sri Sri's progressive poetry?
nef6366d99f2.x: Arasam organised the Abhyudaya current that Sri Sri's poems initiated.
nef6366d99f2.tq: Distinguish the progressive organisation from the later revolutionary writers' organisation.
xs: **Arasam** organised the **Abhyudaya** current started by Sri Sri's poems — option **(1)**.
**Virasam** (**1970**) is the later **Viplava** phase; **Art Lovers** (**1970**) grew into **Jana Natya Mandali**.
**Praja Natya Mandali** was a **communist cultural front** using drama and folk forms.
xa: Arasam was formed in **1943**, as the AIPWA's Telugu counterpart.
The founding text of **Abhyudaya kavitvam** is ***Mahaprasthanam*** (published **1950**).

nfa6461ff48a.s: Who is the author of the Telugu literary work *Mahaprasthanam*?
nfa6461ff48a.x: *Mahaprasthanam* was written by Sri Sri, whose original name was Srirangam Srinivasa Rao.
nfa6461ff48a.tq: Directly identify the author of a major work.
xs: ***Mahaprasthanam*** was written by **Sri Sri** (Srirangam Srinivasa Rao) — option **(3)**.
**Jashuva** wrote ***Gabbilam***; **Gopichand** wrote ***Asamarthuni Jeevayatra***; **Arudra** wrote ***Tvamevaham***.
xa: About **41** poems written **1933-47**, published **1950**; first poem ***Jayabheri*** (**1933**).
Dedicated to **Kompella Janardhana Rao**, preface by **Chalam**.
Founding text of **Abhyudaya kavitvam**.

n0279d49fd77.x: Sri Sri dedicated *Mahaprasthanam* to Kompella Janardhana Rao. Chalam wrote its preface.
n0279d49fd77.tq: Distinguish the person to whom a work was dedicated from its preface writer.
xs: ***Mahaprasthanam*** was dedicated to **Kompella Janardhana Rao** — option **(2)**.
**Chalam** wrote its **preface**; **Puripanda Appalaswamy** co-founded **Sahiti Samiti** with Sri Sri.
xa: It was published in **1950**; first poem ***Jayabheri*** (**1933**).
It is the founding text of **Abhyudaya kavitvam**.

n6f19010b3c6.s: For which song did Sri Sri receive the National Award for Best Lyricist?
n6f19010b3c6.x: Sri Sri received the National Award for Best Lyricist for *Telugu Veera Levara* from the film *Alluri Seetharama Raju*.
n6f19010b3c6.tq: Match the award with the exact song rather than the film title alone.
xs: Sri Sri won the **National Award for best lyricist** for "**Telugu Veera Levara**" (film **Alluri Seetharama Raju**) — option **(3)**.
***Jayabheri*** (**1933**) is the first poem of ***Mahaprasthanam***; **Maa Bhoomi** is a Praja Natya Mandali play.
xa: The award is dated **1974** and called the **first National Award for a Telugu lyricist**.
He was also the **first to dub a film into Telugu** (**Aahuti**).

nf85b2a77952.s: Who translated 'Veera Telangana Viplava Geethalu' from English?
nf85b2a77952.x: Arudra translated Veera Telangana Viplava Geethalu.
xa: **Krovvidi Lingaraju** — **Amma** (Gorky's The Mother), **1934**.
**Narla Venkateswara Rao** — **Neti Russia**.

n749df0b144f.s: The central image in Gurram Jashuva's *Gabbilam* is that of a bat which:
o: carries a Dalit's plea to God
n749df0b144f.x: In *Gabbilam*, a bat carries the plea of a Dalit to God.
n749df0b144f.tq: Identify the central literary image rather than the author alone.
xs: In ***Gabbilam*** the **bat carries a Dalit's plea to God** — option **(1)**.
The work is by **Gurram Jashuva** (**1941**).
The **Telangana struggle** is the theme of Arudra's ***Tvamevaham***.
xa: Jashuva also wrote ***Firdausi***, a **laghu kavyam**.
⚠ Gabbilam is **Jashuva's**, not **Sri Sri's**.

n8623d22959f.x: Gudisale Kalipotunnayi is by Boyi Bhimanna; Arudra's works include Tvamevaham, Cinevali and Samagra Andhra Sahityam.
xa: Arudra = **Bhagavatula Sadasiva Sankara Sastri**, **Sri Sri's nephew**.
Arudra translated **Veera Telangana Viplava Geethalu** from English.

n26e5d4724ab.s: Which work of Tripuraneni Gopichand won the Sahitya Akademi Award?
n26e5d4724ab.x: *Pandita Parameswara Sastri Veelunama* by Tripuraneni Gopichand received the Sahitya Akademi recognition referred to here.
n26e5d4724ab.tq: Distinguish works by the same writer using the associated award detail.
xs: Gopichand's ***Pandita Parameswara Sastri Veelunama*** won the **Sahitya Akademi** — option **(2)**.
***Chaduvu*** is **Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao's**; ***Tvamevaham*** and ***Cinevali*** are **Arudra's**.
xa: Gopichand also wrote ***Asamarthuni Jeevayatra*** (**G2 2017** key).
He was the **first Director of Information of Andhra State** (**1953**).

n3688b58a64d.s: Who wrote *Gudisale Kalipotunnayi*, which won the Sahitya Akademi award in 1975?
n3688b58a64d.x: Boyi Bhimanna wrote *Gudisale Kalipotunnayi*, which won the Sahitya Akademi award in 1975.
n3688b58a64d.tq: Link an award-winning work to its author and year.
xs: ***Gudisale Kalipotunnayi*** (Sahitya Akademi **1975**) was written by **Boyi Bhimanna** — option **(4)**.
Bhimanna was a **praja and abhyudaya poet**.
xa: **Gopichand's** Sahitya Akademi work: ***Pandita Parameswara Sastri Veelunama***.
Arudra's ***Tvamevaham*** (**1948-49**) is on the Telangana struggle.

n97262362783.s: Gorky's *The Mother* was translated into Telugu as *Amma* by:
n97262362783.x: Krovvidi Lingaraju translated Gorky's *The Mother* into Telugu as *Amma* in 1934.
xs: Gorky's **The Mother** was translated as **Amma** by **Krovvidi Lingaraju** (**1934**) — option **(3)**.
**Narla Venkateswara Rao** wrote **Neti Russia**; **Gadde Lingayya** ran **Adarsha Grantha Mandali**.
xa: Amma — Krovvidi Lingaraju was a **GS 2019** key question.
**Arudra** translated **Veera Telangana Viplava Geethalu** from English.

n0db25683a05.s: The play *Maa Bhoomi*, staged by the Praja Natya Mandali, was written by:
o: Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao
n0db25683a05.x: Praja Natya Mandali staged *Maa Bhoomi*, written by Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao.
n0db25683a05.tq: Identify the correct writer pair for a progressive stage work.
xs: **Maa Bhoomi** was written by **Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao** — option **(1)**.
**Gaddar and B. Narsinga Rao** ran **Art Lovers** (**1970**), which became **Jana Natya Mandali** (**1971**).
xa: **Praja Natya Mandali** was a **communist cultural front**; main folk form **Burrakatha**.
Gorky's The Mother → **Amma**, by **Krovvidi Lingaraju** (**1934**).

n40fb1d74ced.s: Praja Natya Mandali was primarily established as which of the following?
o: A constitutional body for local self-government
A communist cultural front for propagating ideas through drama, songs and folk forms
A peasant tribunal for settling tenancy disputes
A journal-editing committee of the CPI
n40fb1d74ced.x: Praja Natya Mandali was a communist cultural front that spread its ideas through drama, songs and folk forms.
n40fb1d74ced.tq: Identify an organisation from its function and method of mobilisation rather than from its name alone.
xs: **Praja Natya Mandali** was a **communist cultural front** spreading ideas through **drama, songs and folk forms** — option **(2)**.
Its main folk form was **Burrakatha**.
xa: Its play **Maa Bhoomi** was by **Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao**.
**Jana Natya Mandali** (**1971**) grew from Gaddar and B. Narsinga Rao's **Art Lovers** (**1970**).

nbeca3ff393f.s: Which folk form constituted the main folk medium of Praja Natya Mandali?
nbeca3ff393f.x: Burrakatha was the main folk form used by Praja Natya Mandali.
nbeca3ff393f.tq: Use the exact traditional art form rather than a broadly related cultural performance.
xs: **Burrakatha** was Praja Natya Mandali's main folk form — option **(1)**.
The body spread communist ideas through **drama, songs and folk forms**.
xa: Its famous play: **Maa Bhoomi**.
⚠ **Arasam** (**1943**) is the progressive **writers'** body; Praja Natya Mandali is the cultural front.

nae3994259d7.s: Which of the following Virasam publications were banned by the government?
nae3994259d7.x: The works *Le* and *March* were banned. *Jhamjha*, *Le* and *Viplavam Vardhillali* were listed as Virasam poetry collections.
nae3994259d7.tq: Distinguish the complete collection list from the separate banned-work list.
xs: **Le** and **March** were **banned** — option **(4)**.
**Jhamjha** (**1970**) and **Viplavam Vardhillali** were Virasam collections but not listed as banned.
**Maa Bhoomi** is a play; **Amma** and **Gabbilam** are a translation and a Jashuva poem.
xa: Virasam collections: **Jhamjha**, **Le**, **Viplavam Vardhillali**.
Virasam's **Founding President** was **Sri Sri**.

n264fb114c88.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Telugu theatre companies and their founders?
o: Hindu Nataka Samajam, Guntur was founded by Kondubhatla Subramanyasastri
Surabhi was founded by Vanarasa Govinda Rao
Sarasa Vinodini Sabha was founded by Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu
Amateur Nataka Sabha was founded by Vanarasa Govinda Rao
n264fb114c88.x: Amateur Nataka Sabha was founded by Erugudipati Gopalakrishnarao; Vanarasa Govinda Rao founded Surabhi.
xa: Kakinada Hindu Nataka Samajam (**1885**) — **Danavahi Hanumantharao**.
**Jaganmitra Samajam** (Vizag) — **Raja Ankitham Jaggara**.
**Hindu Natakajivaka Samajam** (Rajahmundry) — **Vaddadi Subbarayudu**; play **Venisamharam**.

n05c2c85814f.s: Colonial officials watched drama troupes closely during the freedom movement mainly because a troupe could:
o: stage plays only in English for urban elites
reach only a few educated readers through printed scripts
carry a political idea to thousands of illiterate people in one evening
n05c2c85814f.x: Theatre could put a political idea before thousands of illiterate people in a single evening, which made drama companies an influential medium of nationalist mobilisation.
xa: **Viplava Parivartanamu** was **banned during the NCM**.
**Jatiya Nataka Rangam** promoted **swadeshi goods** and **national education**.

n69a80a5210e.s: The first play staged by the Surabhi theatre was:
n69a80a5210e.x: Surabhi's first play was Keechaka Vadham; Venisamharam is linked with Hindu Natakajivaka Samajam, Rajahmundry.
xa: Surabhi is still a **family theatre** about **140 years** on.
Rayalaseema companies: **Surabhi** (Kadapa), **Rama Vilasa Sabha** (Chittoor).

n7c4dfb87141.s: Which event inspired the formation of Guntur’s Hindu Nataka Samajam and Nellore’s Lakshmi Vilasa Nataka Sabha?
o: The inauguration of Lalita Kala Parishad in 1956
The staging of Viplava Parivartanamu during the Non-Cooperation Movement
The first Mahasabha of Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad in 1929
The tour of the Marathi Darwada Nataka Samajam in 1880–81
n7c4dfb87141.x: The Marathi Darwada Nataka Samajam toured and pitched a tent at Rajamahendravaram in 1880–81, inspiring the two theatre organisations.
n7c4dfb87141.tq: Link the triggering event with the organisations it influenced rather than with later theatre milestones.
xs: The tour of the Marathi **Darwada Nataka Samajam** (tent at **Rajamahendravaram**, **1880-81**) inspired them — option **(4)**.
**Lalita Kala Parishad** (**1956**) and the **Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad** Mahasabha (**1929**) came much later.
**Viplava Parivartanamu** was banned during the **NCM**.
xa: Guntur's Hindu Nataka Samajam was founded by **Kondubhatla Subramanyasastri**.
Nellore's **Amateur Nataka Sabha** came in **1896**.

n2c5dabd3cd3.s: Surabhi is regarded as marking which transition in the history of Telugu theatre?
o: From social drama to epic poetry
From sung verse to spoken prose only
From Tholu Bommalata puppets to live Telugu family theatre
From nationalist theatre to court-sponsored performances
n2c5dabd3cd3.x: Surabhi marks the shift from Tholu Bommalata puppets to live Telugu family theatre. This transition is central to its significance in Telugu theatrical culture.
n2c5dabd3cd3.tq: Identify the first-to-last transition by matching the earlier puppetry form with the later live family theatre form.
xs: **Surabhi** marks the shift **from Tholu Bommalata puppets to live Telugu family theatre** — option **(3)**.
A **leather-puppet** family replaced puppets with **live actors**.
xa: First play: **Keechaka Vadham**, at a landlord's wedding.
Founder **Vanarasa Govinda Rao**, **Sorugu** near **Jammalamadugu** (Kadapa).

nd019b04e7a5.s: Hindu Nataka Samajam of Rajahmundry staged plays written by which of the following?
o: Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu and Kolachalam Srinivasa Rao
Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham and Toleti Venkata Subbarao
Kallakuri Narayana Rao and Vedam Venkataraya Sastri
nd019b04e7a5.x: The Rajahmundry Hindu Nataka Samajam staged plays written by Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham and Toleti Venkata Subbarao.
nd019b04e7a5.tq: Identify the correct institutional association rather than matching playwrights merely by fame.
xs: The **Hindu Nataka Samajam, Rajahmundry** staged plays by **Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham** and **Toleti Venkata Subbarao** — option **(2)**.
**Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu** ran his own **Sarasa Vinodini Sabha** at **Bellary**.
xa: The Rajahmundry Samajam dates to **1889**, founded by **Immani Hanumantharao**.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** and **Durga Gopalakrishnayya** acted main roles for it.
⚠ Three Hindu Nataka Samajams: **Guntur 1880-81**, **Kakinada 1885**, **Rajahmundry 1889**.

nf097055e9e1.s: Who was known by the title ‘Andhra Nataka Pitamaha’?
nf097055e9e1.x: Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu was known as Andhra Nataka Pitamaha, meaning ‘Grandfather of Andhra Drama’.
nf097055e9e1.tq: Match the honorific title directly with the person who held it.
xs: "**Andhra Nataka Pitamaha**" (Grandfather of Andhra Drama) was **Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu** — option **(1)**.
**Kolachalam Srinivasa Rao** was a Bellary writer of **historical plays**.
xa: Born **January 1853**, **Dharmavaram (Anantapur)**; died **30 November 1912**.
Wrote **30+ plays**; founded **Sarasa Vinodini Sabha** at **Bellary** (**1886**).
**Bellary Raghava** was his relative.

n3a9aeda80e8.s: Sthanam Narasimha Rao was particularly famous for portraying which of the following roles?
n3a9aeda80e8.x: Sthanam Narasimha Rao was famed for female roles such as Madhuravani in Kanyasulkam and Satyabhama.
n3a9aeda80e8.tq: Associate the stage actor with the characteristic roles for which the actor became famous.
xs: **Sthanam Narasimha Rao** was famed for female roles: **Madhuravani** (Kanyasulkam) and **Satyabhama** — option **(1)**.
**Kondubhatla** and **Danavahi** were founders of Hindu Nataka Samajams, not roles.
xa: **Bellary Raghava** — celebrated stage actor, relative of **Dharmavaram**.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** acted main roles for the Rajahmundry **Hindu Nataka Samajam**.

n2a8ef01fab4.s: Who among the following acted in main roles for Hindu Nataka Samajam of Rajahmundry?
o: Bellary Raghava and Sthanam Narasimha Rao
n2a8ef01fab4.x: Tanguturi Prakasam and Durga Gopalakrishnayya acted main roles for the Hindu Nataka Samajam at Rajahmundry.
n2a8ef01fab4.tq: Match the performers with the theatre company rather than with their unrelated public identities.
xs: **Tanguturi Prakasam and Durga Gopalakrishnayya** acted main roles for Rajahmundry's Hindu Nataka Samajam — option **(1)**.
**Kalluru Subbarao** donated land for **Lalita Kala Parishad**; **Bellary Raghava** and **Sthanam Narasimha Rao** were other actors.
xa: The Rajahmundry Samajam (**1889**) staged plays by **Chilakamarti** and **Toleti Venkata Subbarao**.
Founder: **Immani Hanumantharao**.

nf936cc43119.s: Drama companies became effective vehicles of reform and nationalist messages mainly because they were:
o: the main form of mass entertainment of the time
the main medium of printed propaganda
nf936cc43119.x: Drama companies were the main mass entertainment of the time, and this wide reach let them carry reformist and nationalist messages to the public.
xa: They reached **thousands of illiterate people in one evening**.
They carried **social-reform themes** before nationalist ones.

nb7bfc23d82d.x: Varavikrayam opposes dowry, while Kanyasulkam attacks bride-price.
xa: Kanyasulkam — **Gurajada Apparao**; Varavikrayam — **Kallakuri Narayana Rao**.
Prataparudriyam — **Vedam Venkataraya Sastri**.

nc7400b0aca6.x: Per the APPSC 2024 key, Vyavahara Dharmabodhini is Veeresalingam's reformist drama; Kuliraju is Bhimanna's and Prahlada Charitamu Chilakamarti's.
xa: Exam angle: **four-pair** play-author matching (**APPSC 2024, 2025**).
**Varavikrayam** and **Chintamani** — **Kallakuri Narayana Rao**.

n39e1570430d.x: Padya natakam deals mainly with mythological or epic themes in sung verse; social drama addresses contemporary evils.
xa: Padya natakam examples: **Keechaka Vadham**, **Gayopakhyanam**, **Prahlada Charitamu**.
Social drama examples: **Kanyasulkam**, **Vyavahara Dharmabodhini**, **Varavikrayam**.

nb1082387f1d.s: Before taking up nationalist themes, Andhra drama companies first carried ____ themes.
nb1082387f1d.x: Drama companies initially carried social-reform themes, such as Kanyasulkam and Veeresalingam's drama.
xa: In the **Swadeshi & NCM** years, troupes like **Jatiya Nataka Rangam** promoted swadeshi goods and national education.
Drama companies were the **main mass entertainment** of the time.

na1aed809c9b.s: Land for the Lalita Kala Parishad, Anantapur was donated by freedom fighter:
na1aed809c9b.x: Kalluru Subbarao donated the land; the Parishad was inaugurated by the Governor on 11 February 1956.
xa: **Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad**: first Mahasabha **19-21 June 1929**, **Tenali**.
**Nandi Natakotsavams**: AP government's festival for **Telugu drama**.

n9fc9dc92fc4.s: Who founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha at Madras in 1938?
n9fc9dc92fc4.x: The Andhra Mahila Sabha at Madras was founded by Durgabai Deshmukh in 1938.
