n9fc9dc92fc4.tq: Use direct founder–organisation recall and distinguish the founder from other prominent women leaders.
xs: The **Andhra Mahila Sabha** (Madras, **1938**) was founded by **Durgabai Deshmukh** — option **(3)** (**APPSC 2023** key).
Not **Sarojini Naidu** or **Duvvuri Subbamma**, the usual distractors.
**Unnava Lakshmibayamma** ran **Sri Sarada Niketanam** at Guntur.
xa: The **Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha** ran **parallel** Andhra Mahila Sabha conferences, e.g. **1931 Devarakonda**.
Durgabai later got the **Padma Vibhushan (1975)**.
First chairperson of the **Central Social Welfare Board** (**1953**).

n13445e554bd.s: The Women's Gurukulam of Sarada Niketanam, Guntur was founded in:
n13445e554bd.x: The Gurukulam was founded in 1922; 1902 is the year of the widow asylum where the first widow remarriage was held.
xa: It sheltered widows and destitute girls and became a "**hotbed**" of the freedom movement.
Palnadu forest satyagraha: **8 women** arrested with **28** men.
Lakshmibayamma led women in **Krishna** and **Guntur** in the Salt Satyagraha, **9 April 1930**.

nc9092b50ae0.s: Why did Unnava Lakshmibayamma lead the Guntur hartals during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
o: Her husband was arrested in connection with the Palnadu forest, or pullari, satyagraha
She was arrested for making salt at Chollangi
Her school was closed during the Quit India Movement
She was presiding over the Devarakonda conference
nc9092b50ae0.x: She led the Guntur hartals after her husband was arrested over the Palnadu forest, or pullari, satyagraha.
nc9092b50ae0.tq: Infer the immediate cause of a protest from the person arrested and the movement involved.
xs: She led the **Guntur hartals** after her **husband's arrest** over the **Palnadu forest (pullari) satyagraha** — option **(1)**.
**Chollangi** salt-making was **Duvvuri Subbamma's**; **Devarakonda** was presided by **T. Varalakshmamma**.
xa: The Palnadu forest satyagraha saw **8 women** arrested with **28** men.
On **9 April 1930** she led women in **Krishna and Guntur** in the Salt Satyagraha.

n0f1e0543cd3.s: Who was the first Andhra woman to go to jail in the national movement?
n0f1e0543cd3.x: Duvvuri Subbamma was the first Andhra woman and second woman in India (after Parvati Devi of Punjab) to go to jail.
xa: ⚠ **Rukmini Lakshmipathi** = first woman arrested in Salt Satyagraha; **Subbamma** = first Andhra woman jailed.
Subbamma founded **Sanatana Vidyalayam, Rajahmundry**.
She faced a **lathi charge at Peddapuram** in the **QIM**.

n8b84dc34c8b.s: Duvvuri Subbamma founded which national school at Rajahmundry?
n8b84dc34c8b.x: Duvvuri Subbamma founded the national school called Sanatana Vidyalayam at Rajahmundry.
n8b84dc34c8b.tq: Match the institution and place with its founder.
xs: **Duvvuri Subbamma** founded the national school **Sanatana Vidyalayam, Rajahmundry** — option **(4)**.
**Sarada Niketanam** is the **Unnavas'**; **Andhra Mahila Sabha** is **Durgabai's**; **Desasevikalu** was the Congress women's wing.
xa: She attended the **Vijayawada AICC** in **1921**.
She took part in the **Neil statue satyagraha**.

nea1a1280a3b.s: As a Congress volunteer, Durgabai Deshmukh is remembered for stopping whom at the gate for not having a pass?
nea1a1280a3b.x: As a volunteer, Durgabai stopped Jawaharlal Nehru at the gate because he had no pass; accounts link it to the Vijayawada AICC (1921) or the Kakinada Congress (1923).
xa: At Vijayawada she also **translated Gandhi's Hindi speeches** into Telugu.
In the **CDM** she was prominent in **Madras city**.

nf64dc46c2c5.s: During the Quit India Movement of 1942, Duvvuri Subbamma faced a lathi charge at:
nf64dc46c2c5.x: In 1942 Duvvuri Subbamma faced a lathi charge at Peddapuram.
xa: Subbamma made salt at **Chollangi** on **6 April 1930** and was sent to **Nellore jail**.
Subbamma also led the **Neil statue satyagraha**.

n722a9f79c34.s: Chitturi Annapurna Devi was arrested at the age of seventeen for:
o: Distributing pamphlets during the Quit India Movement
n722a9f79c34.x: Chitturi Annapurna Devi of Guntur was arrested at seventeen during the Quit India Movement for distributing pamphlets.
n722a9f79c34.tq: Test an age-linked distinctive act that can be confused with other forms of protest.
xs: **Chitturi Annapurna Devi** of **Guntur** was arrested at **17** for **distributing pamphlets** in the **QIM** — option **(4)**.
**Chollangi** salt was **Subbamma's**; the anti-zamindari struggle was **Ponaka Kanakamma's**; the first widow remarriage (**1902**) was **Lakshmibayamma's**.
xa: ⚠ In **1942 QIM**: **Peddapuram** = Subbamma (lathi charge); **Guntur** = Chitturi Annapurna Devi.
Other CDM women: **Vallabhaneni Sitamahalakshamma**, **Tallapragada Viswasundaramma**.

n73c4dadd39a.s: Who was the first woman in India to be arrested in the Salt Satyagraha?
n73c4dadd39a.x: Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi, arrested in Madras on 15 May 1930, was the first woman arrested in India in the Salt Satyagraha. Duvvuri Subbamma was the first Andhra woman (second in India) to go to jail in the national movement; Durgabai Deshmukh was prominent in the Madras city Salt Satyagraha; Ponaka Kanakamma led the Nellore anti-zamindari struggle.
n73c4dadd39a.tq: First woman arrested in Salt Satyagraha = Rukmini Lakshmipathi (15 May 1930).
xs: **Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi**, arrested in Madras on **15 May 1930**, was the **first woman arrested in India in the Salt Satyagraha** — option **(1)**.
**Duvvuri Subbamma** was the **first Andhra woman** (**second in India**) to go to jail.
**Durgabai** was prominent in **Madras city**; **Ponaka Kanakamma** led Nellore's **anti-zamindari** struggle.
xa: Rukmini Lakshmipathi led women in **Krishna and Guntur** on **9 April 1930** with Lakshmibayamma.
First woman jailed in India: **Parvati Devi of Punjab**.

n25f91a40ec5.s: Maganti Annapurnamma is remembered as the first Telugu woman to:
o: give her jewellery to the Tilak Swarajya Fund
be arrested in the Salt Satyagraha
go to jail in the national movement
lead the anti-zamindari struggle in Nellore
n25f91a40ec5.x: Maganti Annapurnamma was the first Telugu woman to give her jewellery to the Tilak Swarajya Fund, and she burned foreign cloth during the NCM. Rukmini Lakshmipathi was the first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha, Duvvuri Subbamma the first Andhra woman jailed, and Ponaka Kanakamma led the Nellore anti-zamindari struggle.
n25f91a40ec5.tq: Maganti Annapurnamma = jewellery to Tilak Swarajya Fund (NCM).
xs: **Maganti Annapurnamma** was the **first Telugu woman to give her jewellery to the Tilak Swarajya Fund** — option **(1)**.
She also **burnt foreign cloth** (NCM).
First arrested in Salt Satyagraha: **Rukmini Lakshmipathi**; first Andhra woman jailed: **Duvvuri Subbamma**; Nellore anti-zamindari: **Ponaka Kanakamma**.
xa: Durgabai collected **Rs 5,000** at **Kakinada** (**April 1921**).
**Eluru** was on Gandhi's **1921 coastal tour**.

nc6e72800caa.s: Gandhi's 1921 tour of coastal Andhra is significant mainly because it:
o: launched the Quit India Movement in coastal Andhra
led to the first Congress ministry in Andhra
drew women into the national struggle in Andhra
brought immediate abolition of zamindari in Andhra
nc6e72800caa.x: Gandhi's 1921 coastal tour (Kakinada, Rajahmundry, Eluru, Machilipatnam, Chirala, Nellore) played an important role in drawing Andhra women into the national movement.
xa: At **Kakinada** (**April 1921**) **Durgabai** collected **Rs 5,000** and translated his speech.
**Maganti Annapurnamma** gave her jewellery to the **Tilak Swarajya Fund**.

nf1174339970.s: During the Civil Disobedience Movement, Durgabai Deshmukh was prominent in the Salt Satyagraha at:
nf1174339970.x: Durgabai Deshmukh participated prominently in the Salt Satyagraha in Madras city, alongside K. Nageswara Rao and T. Prakasam.
nf1174339970.tq: Test the place linked to a particular leader rather than a nearby Andhra movement centre.
xs: Durgabai was prominent in the Salt Satyagraha in **Madras city** — option **(2)**.
She worked with **K. Nageswara Rao** and **T. Prakasam**.
**Chollangi** and **Peddapuram** belong to **Duvvuri Subbamma**; **Devarakonda** to the **1931** conference.
xa: ⚠ **Madras city** = Durgabai; **Krishna and Guntur** (**9 April**) = Lakshmibayamma.
Durgabai founded the **Andhra Mahila Sabha** in Madras (**1938**).

n8ef57b8be65.s: On 6 April 1930, Duvvuri Subbamma made salt at:
n8ef57b8be65.x: Duvvuri Subbamma made salt at Chollangi (East Godavari) on 6 April 1930.
xa: Chollangi salt-makers were residents of the **Seethanagaram Ashram** (East Godavari).
After Chollangi, Subbamma was arrested at **Rajahmundry** and sent to **Nellore jail**.

nad76761a337.s: During the Salt Satyagraha, women in Krishna and Guntur districts on 9 April 1930 were led by:
o: Duvvuri Subbamma and Chitturi Annapurna Devi
Durgabai Deshmukh and Chitturi Annapurna Devi
nad76761a337.x: Unnava Lakshmibayamma and Rukmini Lakshmipathi led women in Krishna and Guntur on 9 April 1930. Duvvuri Subbamma was at Chollangi (6 April 1930), Durgabai in Madras city, and Chitturi Annapurna Devi belongs to the 1942 Quit India phase.
xs: **Unnava Lakshmibayamma and Rukmini Lakshmipathi** led women in **Krishna and Guntur** on **9 April 1930** — option **(2)**.
**Duvvuri Subbamma** was at **Chollangi** (**6 April 1930**); **Durgabai** in **Madras city**.
**Chitturi Annapurna Devi** belongs to the **1942 QIM**.
xa: Rukmini Lakshmipathi was arrested in Madras on **15 May 1930**.
She was the **first woman arrested in India in the Salt Satyagraha**.

n504b44a34b5.s: The Devarakonda conference (1931) of the Andhra Mahila Sabha under the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha was presided over by:
n504b44a34b5.x: T. Varalakshmamma presided at Devarakonda in 1931; the 1938 Madras Andhra Mahila Sabha was a separate body founded by Durgabai Deshmukh.
xa: Exam angle: Andhra Mahila Sabha founder = **Durgabai Deshmukh** (**APPSC 2023, 2024**).
**Sri Sarada Niketanam** monthly — **Unnava Lakshmibayamma**.

ndc3b77d3d4e.s: Before turning to public and Congress work, Konda Venkatappayya was a:
ndc3b77d3d4e.x: Konda Venkatappayya, born on 22 February 1866 at Guntur, was a lawyer who gave up his practice for public work.
xa: He was the **first editor** of **Krishna Patrika** (**1902**).
He was **Dictator** of the Andhra **Salt Satyagraha** (**APPSC G2 2008**).
Called the **Father** of the **Andhra State Movement**; wrote **Andhrudyamam**.

ne722297e866.s: During the Civil Disobedience Movement, who was appointed 'Dictator' of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha?
ne722297e866.x: Konda Venkatappayya was appointed Dictator of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha (APPSC G2 2008 key); he was jailed in 1930, 1932 and 1942. Prakasam earned the title Andhra Kesari in the Simon boycott, Sambamurthy toured Andhra for the Simon boycott and became Speaker in 1937, and Pattabhi founded Andhra Bank (1923).
ne722297e866.tq: Andhra Salt Satyagraha Dictator = Konda Venkatappayya (Desabhakta).
xs: **Konda Venkatappayya** was appointed **Dictator** of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha — option **(1)** (**APPSC G2 2008** key).
**Prakasam** earned "**Andhra Kesari**" in the **Simon boycott**; **Sambamurthy** toured Andhra against Simon and became **Speaker** (**1937**).
**Pattabhi** founded **Andhra Bank** (**1923**).
xa: Konda was jailed in **1930, 1932 and 1942**.
He opposed the NC resolution at the **Calcutta special session (1920)**.

n6f967228163.s: Tanguturi Prakasam earned the title ‘Andhra Kesari’ in connection with which event?
o: The Vande Mataram agitation at Osmania University
The Simon Go Back protest at Madras in 1928
n6f967228163.x: Tanguturi Prakasam came to be known as Andhra Kesari for his role in the Simon Go Back protest at Madras in 1928.
n6f967228163.tq: Connect a title with the specific event that earned it, not merely with the person’s general career.
xs: Prakasam became "**Andhra Kesari**" in the **Simon Go Back** protest at **Madras** (**February 1928**) — option **(4)**.
He **defied police firing** during the boycott — not QIM or NCM (**G2 2008** and **2019** keys).
xa: Simon Commission: appointed **November 1927**, arrived **3 February 1928**.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** toured Andhra calling for its boycott.
⚠ Some notes date Prakasam's protest **1927**.

n46359d04abd.s: Tanguturi Prakasam was born in 1872 at:
n46359d04abd.x: Tanguturi Prakasam was born on 23 August 1872 at Vinodarayunipalem, in present-day Prakasam district.
xa: **Prakasam district** is named after him.
He was the **first CM of Andhra State**.

n04400b9b840.s: Swarajya, started by Tanguturi Prakasam in 1921, was a(n):
n04400b9b840.x: Prakasam's Swarajya (1921) was an English daily (APPSC 2011 key); Grama Swarajya was a separate weekly of his.
xa: Some notes say Swarajya came in **English, Telugu and Tamil**.
**Krishna Patrika** (**1902**) — **Konda Venkatappayya** with **Dasu Narayana Rao**.

n7a9c7c096ff.s: Who chaired the Reception Committee of the Indian National Congress session held at Kakinada in 1923?
n7a9c7c096ff.x: Bulusu Sambamurthy was the Chairman of the Reception Committee of the Kakinada Congress session held in 1923.
n7a9c7c096ff.tq: Use the post-person association and distinguish a session organiser from a Congress president.
xs: **Bulusu Sambamurthy** chaired the Reception Committee of the **Kakinada INC session** (**1923**) — option **(3)**.
**Pattabhi** presided at **Jaipur (1948)**; **Konda** was **AICC Secretary (1923)**.
xa: Sambamurthy's title: "**Maharshi**" (ascetic Gandhian life).
He became **Speaker, Madras Legislative Assembly (1937)**.

n9663aeae66d.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over the Congress session of 1948 held at:
n9663aeae66d.x: Pattabhi presided at Jaipur in 1948; at Tripuri (1939) he was Gandhi's candidate but lost to Bose.
xa: Pattabhi founded **Andhra Bank** (**1923**), Machilipatnam.
He was on the **JVP Committee** with Nehru and Patel.
He was **Governor of Madhya Pradesh** (**1952-57**).

n6bff4cd7778.s: What was the initial position of the JVP Committee on the creation of linguistic States?
o: It rejected the idea of linguistic States at the initial stage.
It transferred the decision exclusively to the princely States.
It immediately recommended linguistic States throughout India.
It recommended linguistic States only for the Madras Presidency.
n6bff4cd7778.x: The JVP Committee, comprising Nehru, Patel and Pattabhi, initially rejected the demand for linguistic States.
n6bff4cd7778.tq: Test the committee's initial recommendation rather than its membership or later developments.

n2aca50296eb.s: Which Andhra leader was called 'Maharshi' for his ascetic Gandhian life?
n2aca50296eb.x: Bulusu Sambamurthy was Maharshi; Konda Venkatappayya was Desabhakta and Duggirala Andhra Ratna.

**Desabandhavi** — **Duvvuri Subbamma**.

n64b930349f1.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State?
n64b930349f1.x: Tanguturi Prakasam was the first CM of Andhra State; Bezawada Gopal Reddy was the second and last.

**Konda Venkatappayya** was **AICC Secretary** (**1923**).
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** — **Speaker**, Madras Legislative Assembly (**1937**).

na154f8de14c.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya wrote articles in The Hindu on the need for:
na154f8de14c.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya wrote articles in The Hindu advocating the need for linguistic states.
na154f8de14c.tq: Identify the subject of a leader’s published advocacy.

Yet as a **JVP Committee** member he first **rejected** linguistic states.
xa: **Sambamurthy** as Speaker demanded Andhra state **before** the Constitution.
Pattabhi's **History of the Indian National Congress** came out in **1935**.

n67d8ba5bc4f.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State?
n67d8ba5bc4f.x: Tanguturi Prakasam was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State. Bezawada Gopal Reddy was its second and last CM (28 Mar 1955 - 31 Oct 1956); Pattabhi became Governor of Madhya Pradesh; Sambamurthy was Speaker of the Madras Assembly.
n67d8ba5bc4f.tq: Andhra State CMs: Prakasam (first), Bezawada Gopal Reddy (last).
xs: The **first CM of Andhra State** was **Tanguturi Prakasam** — option **(1)**.
**Bezawada Gopal Reddy** was the **2nd and last** (**28 Mar 1955 - 31 Oct 1956**).
**Pattabhi** became Governor of Madhya Pradesh; **Sambamurthy** was Speaker.
xa: Earlier Prakasam was **Premier** of composite Madras (**1946**).
**Prakasam district** is named after him.

nap-history-26-14.s: Who was described as the Father of the Andhra State Movement and the Dictator of Civil Disobedience?
nap-history-26-14.x: Konda Venkatappayya is called the Father of the Andhra State Movement and was the Dictator of Civil Disobedience in Andhra.
n: Konda Venkatappayya was the Father of the Andhra State Movement. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 37-38]
Konda Venkatappayya was the Dictator of Civil Disobedience. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 37-38]
xs: **Konda Venkatappayya** is the **Father** of the **Andhra State Movement** and **Dictator of Civil Disobedience** — option **(2)**.
He was appointed **Dictator** of the Andhra **Salt Satyagraha** (**APPSC G2 2008**).
**Unnava Lakshminarayana** wrote **Malapalli**; **Gadicherla** is linked with **Home Rule** in Andhra.
xa: ⚠ Other notes call Konda the "**Grandfather** of the Andhra Movement".
Konda was jailed in **1930**, **1932** and **1942**.
He was **Desabhakta**; first president of the **Andhra Congress Circle**.

n36518ebb540.s: Who presided over the fifth Andhra Mahasabha session at Nellore (1917)?
n36518ebb540.x: Konda Venkatappayya presided at Nellore in 1917; he had co-founded Krishna Patrika in 1902 and opposed the Non-Cooperation resolution at Calcutta.
xa: He was **Secretary** of the first session at **Bapatla (1913)**.
Title: "**Desabhakta**".

ne8a6e373b0a.s: In 1951, Tanguturi Prakasam left the Congress with N.G. Ranga and founded the:
ne8a6e373b0a.x: Prakasam and N.G. Ranga left the Congress in 1951 and founded the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party, which was later associated with the Praja Socialist Party.
xa: Prakasam was President of the Andhra Congress Committee **18 times**.
He was **Revenue Minister** in the **Rajaji** ministry (**1937**).

n336d07011dc.s: Tanguturi Prakasam was a coastal signatory to the Sribagh Pact concluded on:
n336d07011dc.x: Tanguturi Prakasam was a coastal signatory to the Sribagh Pact, concluded on 16 November 1937.
n336d07011dc.tq: Match the agreement with its exact date rather than with dates of related movements.
xs: The **Sribagh Pact** was signed on **16 November 1937** — option **(4)**.
Coastal signatories in this topic: **Tanguturi Prakasam** and **Bulusu Sambamurthy**.
**31 Mar 1921** is the **Vijayawada AICC**; **28 Mar 1955** is when **Bezawada Gopal Reddy** became CM.
xa: ⚠ Sribagh Pact = two coastal signatories here: **Prakasam** and **Sambamurthy**.
These leaders steered Andhra through **NCM, CDM, Simon boycott, Sribagh Pact** and **statehood**.

n9f2eb368cf2.s: Pingali Venkayya published his book on national-flag designs in:
n9f2eb368cf2.x: The book came out in 1916; in 1921 he showed the flag to Gandhi at the Vijayawada AICC meeting.
xa: His tricolour was later adopted, with minor changes, as the **National Flag** (**G2 2019** key).
Nicknames: **Patti**, **Japan**, **Diamond Venkayya**.

nbc02f145914.s: Pingali Venkayya showed his design of the national flag to Gandhi at which meeting?
nbc02f145914.x: He showed the flag to Gandhi at the Vijayawada AICC meeting (31 Mar - 1 Apr 1921), held at a venue named Gandhi Nagar; the tricolour was later adopted with minor changes as the National Flag (APPSC G2 2019 key). Kakinada 1923 had Bulusu Sambamurthy as Reception Committee chairman, Calcutta 1920 passed the Non-Cooperation resolution, and Tripuri 1939 saw Bose defeat Pattabhi.
xs: Pingali showed his flag to Gandhi at the **Vijayawada AICC** (**31 Mar - 1 Apr 1921**) — option **(1)**.
The venue was named "**Gandhi Nagar**".
**Kakinada 1923** — Sambamurthy's Reception Committee; **Calcutta 1920** — NC resolution; **Tripuri 1939** — **Bose** beat Pattabhi.
xa: **Bulusu Sambamurthy** also attended the Vijayawada meeting.
The tricolour was adopted with **minor changes** as the National Flag.

n2b500fdc5a3.s: Bulusu Sambamurthy became Speaker of the Madras Legislative Assembly in:
n2b500fdc5a3.x: Sambamurthy became Speaker in 1937; he had toured Andhra calling for a boycott of the Simon Commission.
xa: He was Chairman of the Reception Committee, **Kakinada** session **1923**.
Title: **Maharshi**.
A coastal signatory of the **Sribagh Pact** (**16 Nov 1937**) with **Prakasam**.

nda877ae794f.s: In the Rajaji ministry of 1937, Tanguturi Prakasam held which portfolio?
nda877ae794f.x: Prakasam was Revenue Minister in 1937 and became Premier of composite Madras in 1946.
xa: He was **President** of the Andhra Congress Committee **18 times**.
He was the **first CM** of **Andhra State**.
Title **Andhra Kesari**, from the **Simon Go Back** agitation.

nb51e4374e24.s: 'Naa Jeevita Yatra' is the autobiography of:
nb51e4374e24.x: Naa Jeevita Yatra is Prakasam's four-part autobiography; he wrote three parts and Tenneti Viswanatham the fourth.
xa: Prakasam also wrote **Indian Monetary Systems**.
**Andhrudyamam** — **Konda Venkatappayya**.

nap-history-26-5.s: N.G. Ranga started the first Kisan School at:
nap-history-26-5.x: Ranga started the first Kisan school at Nidubrolu and ran the School of Politics at Kanikapadu in 1939.
n: N.G. Ranga was the first President of the Andhra Socialist Party. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 37-38]
N.G. Ranga started the first Kisan School at Nidubrolu. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 37-38]
N.G. Ranga started the School of Politics at Kanikapadu in 1939. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 37-38]
xa: Ranga's role is listed under the **Kisan movement**.
In **1951** Prakasam left Congress with **N.G. Ranga** to found the **Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party**.
**Konda Venkatappayya** — **Father** of the **Andhra State Movement**.

neec5cdb9d4c.s: Madapati Hanumantha Rao was popularly called:
neec5cdb9d4c.x: Madapati Hanumantha Rao was Andhra Pitamaha; Andhra Bhishma was Nyapathi Subba Rao and Telugu Lenka Tummala Sitarama Murthy.
xa: **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** = **Desoddharaka**, founder of **Andhra Patrika**.
**Pingali Venkayya** = "**Patti Venkayya**", "**Japan Venkayya**", "**Diamond Venkayya**".
**Mahendravarman** = **Vichitrachitta**.

nap-history-20-19.x: Parvataneni Veerayya Choudary was Andhra Sivaji; Nyapathi Subba Rao was Andhra Bhishma and Adibhatla Narayana Dasu Harikatha Pitamaha.
n: Parvataneni Veerayya Choudary is popularly known as Andhra Sivaji. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 29-30]
Nyapathi Subba Rao is popularly known as Andhra Bhishma. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 29-30]

Mahendravarman is known as Vichitrachitta. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 29-30]
xa: **Prakasam** — **Andhra Kesari**; **Duggirala** — **Andhra Ratna**.
**Madapati Hanumantha Rao** — **Andhra Pitamaha**.
**Tummala Sitarama Murthy** — **Telugu Lenka**.

n9c179968e5b.s: 'Feathers and Stones', a prison diary of Ahmednagar Fort, was written by:
n9c179968e5b.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya wrote Feathers and Stones and the History of the INC.
xa: Prakasam wrote **Naa Jeevita Yatra** (3 parts; **Tenneti Viswanatham** wrote the 4th).
Prakasam also wrote **Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae**.
**Pingali Venkayya** wrote a book on national-flag designs, **1916**.

n1e66a5c7609.x: Andhrudyamam is by Konda Venkatappayya; Law Times and the monetary-systems works are linked with Prakasam.
xa: Prakasam also wrote **Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae**.
Pingali Venkayya wrote a book on **national-flag designs** (**1916**).

nb2c8ac69cba.s: 'Nil Darpan' by Dinabandhu Mitra was translated into English by:

The **Indigo Commission (1860)** declared **Tinkathia** illegal.

n00f74fca676.s: After the Deccan Riots of 1875, the Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act was passed in:

xa: ⚠ "Uniform land tax" as cause is incomplete — the **moneylender** was the target.

**Pabna** (**1873-76**) led to the **Bengal Tenancy Act 1885**.

ne850791e279.s: The main grievances of the Oudh Kisan Sabha were directed against which practices of the taluqdars?
ne850791e279.x: The Oudh Kisan Sabha addressed rent increases and begar, or forced labour, imposed by taluqdars.

**Indigo** and **debt bonds** belong to Bengal and the Deccan.
xa: Oudh Kisan Sabha (**Oct 1920**) — **Jawaharlal Nehru** and **Baba Ramchandra**.
**UP Kisan Sabha (1918)** — **Gauri Shankar Mishra** and **Indra Narayan Dwivedi**, backed by **M.M. Malaviya**.

ndd8213a9801.s: The Telangana Peasant Armed Struggle of 1946–1951 was directed primarily against which system of rule?
o: The feudal order of the Nizam in Hyderabad State
The ryotwari system of the Madras Presidency
ndd8213a9801.x: The struggle in Hyderabad State was directed against the Nizam’s feudal order, particularly the power of jagirdars and deshmukhs and the practice of Vetti.
ndd8213a9801.tq: Identify the central authority and the specific system against which the movement was directed.
xs: The Telangana struggle targeted the **Nizam's feudal order** in **Hyderabad State** — option **(2)**.
Its targets: **jagirdars**, **deshmukhs** and **Vetti** (forced labour).
**Permanent Settlement** is Bengal (**1793**); ryotwari is the Madras/Deccan system.
xa: Span: **1946-51**; led by the **CPI/Andhra Mahasabha**.

n0a1af8276fe.s: The Agrarian League of the Pabna Movement (1873-76) was led by Ishan Chandra Roy and:
n0a1af8276fe.x: Ishan Chandra Roy and Shambhu Pal led the Agrarian League; Digambar and Bishnu Biswas led the Indigo Revolt.
xa: ⚠ The UPSC table mislabels Pabna; it also wrongly calls **Sidhu-Kanhu** Bhil leaders (they led the **Santhals**).
Pabna ran **1873-76** in **East Bengal**.

na0812acfd64.s: The Tinkathia system in Champaran (Bihar, 1917) was ended by:
na0812acfd64.x: After the 1917 Champaran movement in Bihar, the Champaran Agrarian Act, 1918 ended Tinkathia there. The Indigo Commission (1860) followed the Bengal Indigo Revolt of 1859-60; the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885 followed the Pabna movement; the Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act, 1879 followed the Deccan Riots.
na0812acfd64.tq: Movement to law: Pabna 1885, Deccan 1879, Champaran 1918, Tebhaga 1950.
xs: **Tinkathia** in **Champaran** (**1917**) was ended by the **Champaran Agrarian Act 1918** — option **(1)**.
**Indigo Commission (1860)** — Bengal; **Bengal Tenancy Act 1885** — Pabna; **1879** Act — Deccan Riots.
xa: Tinkathia: indigo on **3/20** of the land at poor prices.
**Kheda (1918)** in Gujarat followed soon after.

n9c6ddda0c2e.s: Under the Tinkathia system imposed by European indigo planters, peasants were required to cultivate indigo on
n9c6ddda0c2e.x: The Tinkathia system required indigo cultivation on three-twentieths, or 3/20, of the peasants’ land, generally at poor prices.

xs: Under **Tinkathia**, peasants grew indigo on **3/20** of their land — option **(1)**.
European planters forced it at **poor prices**.
xa: The **Indigo Commission (1860)** declared Tinkathia **illegal** in Bengal.
In **Champaran (1917)** Tinkathia was ended by the **Champaran Agrarian Act 1918**.

nd2c468b4dc5.s: What was the effect of the Indigo Commission of 1860 on the Tinkathia system?
o: It expanded the system to all of Bengal
It made the system compulsory for twenty years
It transferred indigo cultivation to zamindars
nd2c468b4dc5.x: The Indigo Commission, appointed in 1860, declared the Tinkathia system illegal.
nd2c468b4dc5.tq: Identify the institutional decision that followed the agrarian protest.
xs: The **Indigo Commission (1860)** **declared the Tinkathia system illegal** — option **(2)**.
It followed the **Indigo Revolt** (**1859-60**, Nadia, Bengal).
xa: Leaders: **Digambar Biswas** and **Bishnu Biswas**.
The play **Nil Darpan** by **Dinabandhu Mitra** exposed the planters.

n58eccd02ee9.s: In the Tebhaga Movement, the bargadars demanded that their share of the crop be raised from one-half to:
n58eccd02ee9.x: 'Tebhaga' means two-thirds, the bargadars' demanded share in place of one-half.
xa: Tebhaga: **1946-47**, **Bengal**, led by **AIKS/CPI**.

**Telangana** struggle (**1946-51**) set up **village soviets**.

n96b65dc4c30.s: Which of the following was an important outcome of the Telangana Peasant Armed Struggle?
o: Land was seized and redistributed, and village soviets were established
The Permanent Settlement was introduced in Hyderabad State
Indigo cultivation was made compulsory in Telangana
The zamindari system was strengthened by the Nizam
n96b65dc4c30.x: The struggle led to the seizure and redistribution of land and the establishment of village soviets in several areas.
n96b65dc4c30.tq: Distinguish movement outcomes from the causes and institutions associated with other agrarian struggles.
xs: Land was **seized and redistributed** and **village soviets** were set up — option **(1)**.
The struggle opposed the Nizam's order; it did not strengthen zamindari.
xa: It was called off in **1951**, with **land reform** promised.
**Vetti** = forced labour under the Nizam's feudal order.

nd20d3e57606.s: Who among the following were associated with the leadership of the Telangana Peasant Armed Struggle on behalf of the Communist Party of India?
o: P. Sundarayya and Chandra Rajeswara Rao

nd20d3e57606.tq: Match the movement with its actual political leaders rather than leaders of similar peasant struggles.
xs: **P. Sundarayya** and **Chandra Rajeswara Rao** led the Telangana struggle for the **CPI** — option **(1)**.
**Biswas** brothers led the Indigo Revolt; **Dodla Ramireddy** and **Vennelakanti Raghavaiah** were Nellore anti-zamindari leaders.
xa: Sundarayya wrote **Telangana People's Struggle and its Lessons**.
**Andhra Mahasabha** President **1941-46**: **M. Suryanarayana** (**G2 2019** key).

n28fcb4be8d7.s: Who was the President of the Andhra Mahasabha during 1941–46?
n28fcb4be8d7.x: The APPSC Group 2 2019 key gives M. Suryanarayana as Andhra Mahasabha President (1941–46), when it had become the CPI's organisational front.
xa: By the 1940s the Mahasabha was the **organisational front of the CPI**.
**Mallu Swarajyam** — leading woman fighter.

n7c8565c7108.s: By the 1940s, the Andhra Mahasabha functioned as the organisational front of the ____ in the Telangana struggle.
n7c8565c7108.x: The Andhra Mahasabha moved from cultural work to leftist agrarian politics and became the CPI's organisational front.
xa: President **1941-46**: **M. Suryanarayana**.
The struggle set up **village soviets** after redistributing land.

nd1163731359.s: Acharya N.G. Ranga’s agricultural labour initiative at Nidubrolu in 1923 was known as the
nd1163731359.x: India’s first Agricultural Labourers’ Mahasabha was held at Nidubrolu in 1923 under the leadership of Acharya N.G. Ranga.
nd1163731359.tq: Use the year and place to identify the correct organisation from closely related peasant bodies.

**Andhra Rythu Vidyalayam, Madanapalle** (**May 1938**) — **T.N. Ramakrishna Reddy**.

nf5821b34f3f.s: In which year did Acharya N.G. Ranga found the Andhra Provincial Ryots’ Association?
nf5821b34f3f.x: The Andhra Provincial Ryots’ Association was founded by N.G. Ranga in 1928.

n04d27d01700.s: Which one of the following was India’s first Kisan School?
n04d27d01700.x: The Peasant Institute, or Ramanayidu Rythu Vidyalayam, at Nidubrolu was India’s first Kisan School. It was established in 1933–34 with Bharathi Devi and Ranga’s brothers.
n04d27d01700.tq: Distinguish the first institution from later schools and political centres.
xs: India's **first Kisan School** was **Ramanayudu Rythu Vidyalayam, Nidubrolu** — option **(1)**.

**Kankipadu** (**1939**), **Kothapatnam** summer school and **Madanapalle** (**May 1938**) came later.

nf40829f3c30.s: The zamindar of the Munagala estate was:
nf40829f3c30.x: Nayani Venkataranga Rao was the Munagala zamindar; Batchala Jagannadh Das was associated with its peasant association.

nf85ddb61ad7.s: The Oudh Kisan Sabha, formed in October 1920, was set up by:

nf85ddb61ad7.x: The Oudh Kisan Sabha (Oct 1920) was set up by Jawaharlal Nehru and Baba Ramchandra against rent hikes and begar. nc030861ce18.s: The Permanent Settlement of 1793 contributed to anti-zamindari struggles because it

created village soviets under peasant control

n667792e492c.s: Who chaired the Zamindari Abolition Committee set up by Rajaji in 1937?

nf3d2d7f3a82.s: The Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill was introduced in which year in the context of land reform demands?

xa: In **1937** **Rajaji** set up a **Zamindari Abolition Committee** chaired by **T. Prakasam**.
Root cause: the **Permanent Settlement** (**1793**).

n5cd18884ca6.s: The Prakasam Committee report (1938) concluded that land belonged to:
o: the tiller, with the zamindar only a tax collector
the zamindar and the tenants jointly
the zamindar, with the tiller only a tenant
n5cd18884ca6.x: The Prakasam Committee held that land belongs to the tiller and that the zamindar is merely a tax collector.
xa: **Prakasam** regretted it did not say outright whether **zamindari should be abolished**.
**Communists** pioneered the **land to the tiller** demand.
n5cd18884ca6.fixed: stem referred to 'the committee' without naming it

na79bfe4a8e6.s: At the time of Independence, approximately what proportion of Andhra’s land remained under zamindars?
na79bfe4a8e6.x: About 40 percent of Andhra’s land was still under zamindars at Independence.
na79bfe4a8e6.tq: Recall the quantitative scale of zamindari persistence at Independence.
xs: About **40 percent** (**40%**) of Andhra's land was still under zamindars at Independence — option **(3)**.
⚠ Don't confuse with **70%** — the share of Madras Presidency zamindari land in Vizag, Nellore, the Godavaris, Krishna and Chittoor.
xa: The **1929-35 Depression** crashed crop prices.
Zamindari was abolished by the **Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948**.

n63056d4af63.s: Who first called for an anti-zamindari struggle in 1920?
n63056d4af63.x: Pattabhi first called for an anti-zamindari struggle in 1920.
n63056d4af63.tq: Distinguish the earliest call from later organisational leadership.
xs: **Pattabhi** first called for an anti-zamindari struggle in **1920** — option **(1)**.
**N.G. Ranga** presided over the **first anti-zamindari conference** (Venkatagiri, **Sept 1931**); **Kala Venkata Rao** introduced the **1947** Bill.
xa: **Gottipati Brahmaiah** was a leader in the **Challapalli/Munagala** struggles.
**Communists** pioneered the demand for **land to the tiller**.

nb054f3d03bf.s: The Vizag Zamindar Rythu Sabha (1929) demanded the amendment of the:
nb054f3d03bf.x: The Sabha (3 Nov 1929) resolved to amend the Estates Land Act of 1908, which itself did not abolish estates.
xa: The Vizag Sabha started **Prajavani** (editor **Garimella Krishnamurthy**).
The **Jameen Ryot Mahasabha** in **1938** demanded a **Zamindari Abolition Act**.

n86c4e94bdfb.s: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, which abolished zamindari in Andhra, bears which year in its name?
n86c4e94bdfb.x: It is the 1948 Act (APPSC G2 2008 PYQ: pick 1948). Trap: some sources call it the 1949 Act because it received assent on 2 April 1949 and came into force on 7 September 1949; estates were taken over from 1950; the Bill was introduced on 11 November 1947.
n86c4e94bdfb.tq: Act year 1948; assent and commencement 1949; takeover 1950.
xs: The Act's name year is **1948** — option **(1)** (**G2 2008** PYQ).
⚠ Some notes call it the "**1949**" Act because assent and commencement fell in **1949**; takeover from **1950**.
**1947** is the year the **Bill** was introduced.
xa: It was the **first law** of independent India to get the GG's assent.
It abolished **zamindari and inamdari estates**.

n45f92c4efe6.s: The rent in Gampalagudem estate was collected primarily:
o: In cash after annual auction of grazing lands
In kind, resulting in excessive extraction
Through a fixed payment of 60 seers per acre
As a renewal fee called nazarana
n45f92c4efe6.x: In Gampalagudem, rent was collected in kind rather than cash, leading to excessive extraction.
n45f92c4efe6.tq: Distinguish the mode of rent collection from other estate grievances and levies.
xs: At **Gampalagudem** rent was collected **in kind instead of cash**, causing **excessive extraction** — option **(2)** (**GS 2023**).
**Grazing-land auction** is Venkatagiri's **Kancha paddhati**; **60 seers** is the Munagala wage cut; **nazarana** is a renewal fee.
xa: **Kalipatnam**: **4,000 acres** grabbed for a project, never returned.
**Munagala** (**1938-39**): wage cut from **80 to 60 seers** per acre.

n44c59256cb6.s: The Palemkota revolt in the Venkatagiri estate took place on:
n44c59256cb6.x: The Palemkota revolt occurred on 20 March 1933 in Venkatagiri, the second largest estate in Coastal Andhra.
xa: **Gandhi** visited Venkatagiri on **20 Dec 1933**.
Leaders: **Ponaka Kanakamma**, **Vennelakanti Raghavaiah**, **Dodla Ramireddy**.

na1e4f109396.s: The zamindar of the Challapalli estate in Krishna district was:
na1e4f109396.x: Yarlagadda Sivarama Prasad was the Challapalli zamindar; the 1930 agitation was against seizure of lanka and waste land and vetti.
xa: Challapalli leaders: **Gorrepati Venkata Subbayya**, **Chandra Rajeswara Rao**.
Munagala zamindar: **Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao**.

n325e1e5a466.s: Ponaka Kanakamma led the anti-zamindari struggle in which area?
n325e1e5a466.x: Ponaka Kanakamma (APPSC G2 2008 key) led the Nellore/Venkatagiri struggle alongside Vennelakanti Raghavaiah and Dodla Ramireddy; Kalipatnam was led by Bhupathiraju Lakshmi Narasimha Raju.
xa: Fellow Nellore leaders: **Vennelakanti Raghavaiah**, **Dodla Ramireddy**, **Yakasiri Chellamma**.
**Gandhi** visited **Venkatagiri** on **20 Dec 1933**.

nc8650efb38f.s: In which year did the Madras Congress Ministry under Rajaji appoint a committee on the zamindari system?
nc8650efb38f.x: The committee was appointed in 1937, with C. Rajagopalachari as Chief Minister and Tanguturi Prakasam as Revenue Minister.
xa: Also called the **Estate Land / Zamindari Enquiry Committee**.
Report completed **7 Nov 1938**.

n87a8cc384a2.s: Who led the yatra from Ichchapuram to submit a petition to the committee on the zamindari system?
o: Gouthu Latchanna and Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao
Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao and C. Rajagopalachari
n87a8cc384a2.x: Gouthu Latchanna and Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao led the yatra from Ichchapuram to petition the committee.
n87a8cc384a2.tq: Match the specific action and starting place with the correct pair of leaders.
xs: The **Ichchapuram** yatra was led by **Gouthu Latchanna and Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao** — option **(2)**.
They petitioned the **Prakasam Committee**.
xa: The committee's report was completed on **7 Nov 1938**.
**Mandasa** (Srikakulam) saw police firing on **1 April 1940**.

ncdd0aee8209.s: Who introduced the Madras Estates Abolition Bill on 11 November 1947?
ncdd0aee8209.x: Revenue Minister Kala Venkata Rao introduced the Bill on 11 November 1947.
ncdd0aee8209.tq: Identify the minister associated with introducing legislation rather than giving assent to it.
xs: Revenue Minister **Kala Venkata Rao** introduced the Bill on **11 Nov 1947** — option **(2)**.
**C. Rajagopalachari**, as **Governor-General**, gave assent on **2 Apr 1949**.
**Pattabhi** called for the struggle in **1920**; **N.G. Ranga** presided at Venkatagiri (**1931**).
xa: The Bill was passed by the **Madras Assembly** in **Nov 1948**.
It came into force on **7 Sept 1949**.

nfe1abf918b6.s: Under the Estates Abolition legislation, the tenants became:
nfe1abf918b6.x: The legislation abolished zamindari and inamdari estates, made tenants direct ryots of the state and compensated zamindars.
xa: The **1st (1951)** and **4th (1955)** Amendments shielded abolition laws.
Estates were taken over from **1950**.

n06c23dbe713.s: Which Constitutional Amendments shielded zamindari abolition laws such as the Madras Act of 1948?
n06c23dbe713.x: The 1st Amendment (1951) and the 4th Amendment (1955) shielded zamindari abolition laws from challenge. The other pairs are not the amendments that gave this protection.
n06c23dbe713.tq: Abolition laws shielded by the 1st (1951) and 4th (1955) Amendments.
xs: The **1st (1951)** and **4th (1955)** Amendments shielded zamindari abolition laws — option **(1)**.
They protected Acts like the **Madras Act of 1948**.
xa: The Madras Act **paid compensation** to zamindars.
Tenants became **direct ryots** of the state.

n2deeec151be.s: In 1938, the Jameen Ryot Mahasabha demanded that the government enact a:
n2deeec151be.x: The Jameen Ryot Mahasabha campaigned for abolition of zamindari and in 1938 demanded a Zamindari Abolition Act.
xa: The **Prakasam Committee** report was completed on **7 Nov 1938**.
The abolition Act finally came in **1948**.

ne54ff43e409.x: Ranga, called Rythu Bandhu and Acharya, received the Padma Vibhushan in 1991, not the Bharat Ratna.
xa: Ranga is also called the **Father of the Indian Peasant Movement**; his full name is **Gogineni Ranganayakulu**.
Ranga's journals: **Praja Bandhu** and **Navayuga**.
Ranga's books: **Credo of World Peasantry**, **Revolutionary Peasantry**, **Fight for Freedom**.
Ranga was the first President of the **Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham (1928)** and Secretary of the **AIKS (1936)**.

naa1d10ed5b7.s: Who among the following authored the Munagala Award?
naa1d10ed5b7.x: Gottipati Brahmaiah authored the Munagala Award. He was also a pioneer of the zamindari ryot movement and Secretary of the APCC.
naa1d10ed5b7.tq: Match the named document with its author, guarding against swapped deeds.
xs: The **Munagala Award** was authored by **Gottipati Brahmaiah** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **Brahmaiah Award** of **15 Jan 1939** settled the Munagala dispute across **142 villages**.
**Kommareddi Satyanarayana** led the 1937 Rythu Yatra; **Nanduri Prasada Rao** led the **Kalukova Satyagraha (1938)**.
xa: Brahmaiah was a pioneer of the **zamindari ryot movement** and **APCC Secretary**.
He led the **1931 Mopidevi no-tax resolution** (Divi taluk Resettlement Mahasabha).
The Award was later broken; **Uppala Ramayya** led land occupations and **350 women** were lathi-charged.
Munagala zamindar: **Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao**.

na858cfa817e.s: Who was the President of the All India Kisan Sabha in 1936?
na858cfa817e.x: The 1936 AIKS President was Swami Sahajanand Saraswati; Kommareddi formed village peasant associations (1935) and led the 1937 Rythu Yatra.
xa: ⚠ Trap: the 1937 yatra was **launched by N.G. Ranga** on **3 July 1937** but **led by Kommareddi**.
The **Ichchapuram-Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra** was compared to the **Dandi March**.
It ended with a memorandum to Speaker **Bulusu Sambamurthy**.
**N.G. Ranga** was the AIKS **Secretary** in 1936.

n669223542d7.s: Which of the following is NOT a book associated with N.G. Ranga?
n669223542d7.x: Credo of World Peasantry, Revolutionary Peasantry and Fight for Freedom are books associated with N.G. Ranga. The Munagala Award was authored by Gottipati Brahmaiah and is not a book of Ranga.
n669223542d7.tq: Find the item that belongs to the neighbouring leader rather than the named author.
xs: The **Munagala Award** is not a Ranga book — option **(4)** is correct; it was authored by **Gottipati Brahmaiah**.
**Credo of World Peasantry**, **Revolutionary Peasantry** and **Fight for Freedom** are **N.G. Ranga's books**.
xa: Ranga's journals: **Praja Bandhu** and **Navayuga**.
⚠ Trap: **Zamin Ryot** = **Nellore**; **Prajavani** = **Vizag** — not Ranga's.
The Brahmaiah (Munagala) Award is dated **15 Jan 1939** and covered **142 villages**.

n6eed05068eb.s: The 1931 Divi Taluk Resettlement Mahasabha movement was led by:
n6eed05068eb.x: Gottipati Brahmaiah led the 1931 Divi Taluk movement; Ranga led the 1935 Guntur anti-resettlement movement.
xa: Ranga also led the **1935 Rythu Rakshana Yatra** and the **1938-39** Ichchapuram-Madras cycle rally.
The cycle rally opposed the **Madras Land Settlement Act**.
The Mopidevi Mahasabha adopted a **no-tax resolution**.

n5fcf47cfd1b.s: At the founding of the All India Kisan Sabha in April 1936 at Lucknow, who were its President and Secretary respectively?
o: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati and N.G. Ranga
N.G. Ranga and Swami Sahajanand Saraswati
Swami Sahajanand Saraswati and Kommareddi Satyanarayana
n5fcf47cfd1b.x: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati (who had founded the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha in 1929) was President and N.G. Ranga was Secretary. Option B reverses the two; Nehru and Baba Ramchandra set up the Oudh Kisan Sabha (1920); Kommareddi Satyanarayana led the 1937 Rythu Yatra.
xs: **Swami Sahajanand Saraswati** was President and **N.G. Ranga** Secretary — option **(1)** is correct.
Option **(2)** reverses the two roles.
**Kommareddi Satyanarayana** led the **1937 Rythu Yatra** and formed village associations in **1935** — he held no AIKS office.
xa: Sahajanand founded the **Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (1929)**.
The AIKS was the **peasant wing of the Congress**.
Sahajanand also presided over the **Palasa session** (**March 1940**).

nf594bd1a73a.s: The Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham was founded in:
nf594bd1a73a.x: The Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham was founded in 1928. It merged into the AIKS in 1936.
nf594bd1a73a.tq: Distinguish the association’s founding year from the years of predecessor bodies and merger.
xs: The **Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham** was founded in **1928** — option **(3)** is correct.
**1915** was the **Krishna District Rythu Sangham**; **1923** the **Guntur and Godavari sanghams** (predecessors).
**1936** was when the Sangham **merged into the AIKS**, founded that year at **Lucknow**.
xa: Founders: **N.G. Ranga**, **Narasimha Devara Satyanarayana** and **Maganti Bapineedu**; based at **Vijayawada**.
First President: **Ranga**; first General Secretary: **B.V. Ratnam**.
It is also called the **Andhra Provincial Ryots Association, 1928**.

n29582f49aec.s: Who was the first General Secretary of the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham?
n29582f49aec.x: B.V. Ratnam was the first General Secretary; Ranga, Narasimha Devara Satyanarayana and Maganti Bapineedu were its founders.
xa: The Sangham was founded in **1928**, based at **Vijayawada**, with **Ranga** as first President.
It **merged into the AIKS in 1936**.
Predecessors: **Krishna District Rythu Sangham (1915)**; **Guntur and Godavari sanghams (1923)**.

na043c646d9e.s: In 1943, N.G. Ranga left the All India Kisan Sabha and founded the:
na043c646d9e.x: When the communist-led AIKS backed the People's War line, Ranga left and founded the Andhra Rashtra Kisan Congress in 1943.
xa: **1940** is the year of the **Palasa AIKS session** (March).
AIKS President: **Swami Sahajanand Saraswati**; Secretary: **N.G. Ranga**.
AIKS demanded **abolition of zamindari** + **debt cancellation**.

n9e020ca087a.s: Munagala paragana was situated in which administrative area at the time of the struggle?
n9e020ca087a.x: Munagala paragana was located in Nandigama taluk of Krishna district at the time. It is now associated with Suryapet/Nalgonda.
n9e020ca087a.tq: Test the historical location rather than the present administrative association.
xs: Munagala paragana lay in **Nandigama taluk**, **Krishna district** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is now in **Suryapet/Nalgonda** (back to **Nalgonda** in **1959**).
xa: The zamindar was **Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao** — a literary patron but harsh landlord.
The struggle ran from **1930** to **1939**.
**Munagala Day** = **11 June 1939**; withdrawn **19 June 1939**.

n53a65bcc203.s: Who was the zamindar of Munagala?
n53a65bcc203.x: Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao was the zamindar of Munagala. Though a literary patron, he was described as a harsh landlord.
n53a65bcc203.tq: Match the estate with its zamindar, avoiding a leader–landlord swap.
xs: The zamindar of Munagala was **Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao** — option **(1)** is correct.
He was a **literary patron** but a **harsh landlord**.
**Uppala Ramayya** led land occupations; **Brahmaiah** authored the Award; **Gorrepati Venkata Subbayya** led the **Challapalli** revolt (June **1930**).
xa: The **Kalukova Satyagraha (1938)** was over a paddy wage of **80 seers per acre**.
The **Brahmaiah Award** of **15 Jan 1939** covered **142 villages**.
Munagala was then in **Nandigama taluk, Krishna district**.

n3ec34b52e88.s: The Kalukova Satyagraha of 1938 over the paddy wage was led by:
n3ec34b52e88.x: The 1938 Kalukova Satyagraha was led by Nanduri Prasada Rao over the 80-seers-per-acre wage; the Sub-Collector made the zamindar pay.
xa: It was part of the **Munagala** paragana struggle (**1930-39**).
The **Brahmaiah Award** followed on **15 Jan 1939**, covering **142 villages**.
⚠ Trap: **Munagala Day** = **11 June 1939**; withdrawn **19 June 1939**.

nf37204994d1.s: The Ichchapuram-Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra (1937) ended with a memorandum to Speaker:
nf37204994d1.x: The memorandum went to Speaker Bulusu Sambamurthy; Prakasam was then Revenue Minister.
xa: The yatra was compared to the **Dandi March**.
Other dating: Ranga's **1,500-mile march** = **1938-39** cycle rally.
**Prakasam** and **Ranga** promised action, leading to withdrawal of the Munagala struggle on **19 June 1939**.

n2e96004f7c7.s: The Ichchapuram–Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra was compared to which national movement?
n2e96004f7c7.x: The Ichchapuram–Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra was compared to the Dandi March. It ended with a memorandum submitted to Speaker Bulusu Sambamurthy.
n2e96004f7c7.tq: Use the stated comparison to identify the model movement.
xs: The **Ichchapuram-Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra** was compared to the **Dandi March** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was launched by **N.G. Ranga** on **3 July 1937** and led by **Kommareddy Satyanarayana**.
xa: It ended with a memorandum to Speaker **Bulusu Sambamurthy**.
The **1938-39** cycle rally from Ichchapuram to Madras opposed the **Madras Land Settlement Act**.
⚠ Trap: **Kommareddi** led the yatra on the ground; **Ranga** launched it.

ncb896be119e.s: The All India Kisan Sabha worked as the peasant wing of the:
ncb896be119e.x: The AIKS worked as the peasant wing of the Congress and demanded abolition of zamindari and cancellation of debts.
xa: Founded **April 1936** at the **Lucknow** INC session; President **Swami Sahajanand Saraswati**, Secretary **N.G. Ranga**.
In **WWII**, the communist-led AIKS backed the **"People's War"**; Ranga left and founded the **Andhra Rashtra Kisan Congress (1943)**.
Ranga's memorandum to the **Whitley Commission (1929)** demanded **minimum wages**.

nadf52d46639.s: The Indian Forest Act of 1878 added to tribal discontent by treating forests as:
nadf52d46639.x: The 1878 Act made forests state property, strengthening state control and hurting tribal customary rights.
xa: The 1879 revolt against forest laws was at **Rekapalli** (APPSC 2017).
At **Rekapalle**, podu tax rose from **4 annas per axe** to **4-12 annas** during a famine.
Common factor of tribal revolts (UPSC 2011): **complete disruption of the old agrarian order**.

nc94a0fec630.s: In the context of tribal revolts, the term ‘dikus’ referred principally to:
nc94a0fec630.x: Dikus were outsiders such as moneylenders, zamindars and traders whose activities contributed to tribal land alienation.
nc94a0fec630.tq: Discriminate between a colonial social category and indigenous administrative institutions.
xs: **Dikus** were outsiders — **moneylenders, zamindars and traders** — option **(3)** is correct.
They caused **land alienation** among tribals.
**Paikas** were Odisha's **traditional militia**; **Munda-Manki** chiefs ran **Kolhan** under **Wilkinson's Rule**.
xa: Oppression by **dikus** and **police** caused the **Santhal Hul**.
**Missionary interference** was another cause of revolts.
Birsa's revolt arose from destruction of **Khuntkatti** by **zamindars, thikadars and missionaries**.

n71ce9883944.s: The Paikas lost their rent-free lands after the British conquest of:
n71ce9883944.x: The Paikas lost rent-free lands after the 1803 conquest and resented salt policy and revenue burdens.
xa: **Paikas** = traditional militia of **Odisha**.
The **Paika Bidroha (1817)** was led by **Bakshi Jagabandhu** at **Khurda**.
⚠ Trap: notes wrongly add **Madhusudan Das** as a Paika leader.

n892df480815.s: An important cause of the Santhal Hul was oppression by:
n892df480815.x: The Santhals rose against oppression by zamindars, moneylenders (the dikus) and the police.
xa: **Damin-i-Koh** = tract for Santhal settlement in the **Rajmahal Hills**.
The British had invited Santhals after failing to control the **Paharias**.
⚠ Trap: **SPT Act** = **1876 / 1949** (Santhals); **CNT Act** = **1908** (Birsa).

n15616e1c647.s: The Rampa Rebellion of 1879–80 was primarily directed against
o: the imprisonment of Jamedar Chida Khan
the disbanding of the Vizianagaram troops
the Permanent Settlement imposed on Narayana Babu
Munsubar Madhava Bhupati Dev and oppressive taxation
n15616e1c647.x: The 1879–80 Rampa Rebellion in the Rampachodavaram Agency opposed Munsubar Madhava Bhupati Dev and oppressive taxes. Madhava Bhupati Dev had been appointed in 1848.
n15616e1c647.tq: Identify the immediate cause and official targeted by the uprising.
xs: The **1879-80 Rampa** rebellion opposed **Munsubar Madhava Bhupati Dev** and **oppressive taxation** — option **(4)**.
Madhava Bhupati Dev was appointed in **1848** and was an **exploitative mansabdar**.
Forest/podu restrictions under the **Madras Forest Act** were another cause.
xa: Rampa lay in **Rampachodavaram** Agency, **Godavari district** (APPSC G2 2011: **1879**).
**Sullivan** of the **Madras Revenue Board** removed the mansabdar.
The rising was suppressed in **Sept 1879** and crushed by **Nov 1880**.

n380c7cf05da.s: The immediate agrarian grievance behind Birsa Munda’s revolt was the destruction of the:
n380c7cf05da.x: The revolt was caused in part by the destruction of the Khuntkatti joint landholding system by zamindars, thikadars and missionaries.
n380c7cf05da.tq: Identify the precise institution affected instead of choosing a general tribal-administration term.
xs: Birsa's revolt arose from destruction of the **Khuntkatti joint landholding system** — option **(3)** is correct.
It was destroyed by **zamindars, thikadars and missionaries**.
**Munda-Manki** was **Wilkinson's** system in Kolhan; **Damin-i-Koh** the Santhal tract.
xa: The **Ulgulan** ran **1899-1900** with about **6,000 Mundas**.
The **Chotanagpur Tenancy Act 1908** recognised Khuntkatti rights.
Birsa was captured **Feb 1900**; died in **Ranchi jail** in **June 1900**.

nindian-history-129-15.s: Which of the following rebellions took place in the Andhra region?
nindian-history-129-15.x: The Rampa Rebellion took place in the Andhra region; the other three are linked with Bengal.
n: The Sanyasi-Fakir Rebellion occurred in Bengal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #129 · pp 232-233]
The Santhal Rebellion occurred in the Bengal/Bihar region. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #129 · pp 232-233]
The Indigo Revolt occurred in Bengal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #129 · pp 232-233]
The Rampa Rebellion occurred in the Andhra region. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #129 · pp 232-233]
xa: Rampa was led by **Alluri Sitarama Raju**.
Santhal Hul began at **Bhognadih** on **30 June 1855**.
**Pabna** (**1873** to **1876**) was also in Bengal.

n486739e4923.s: Which one of the following provided a common factor for tribal revolts in 19th-century India?
o: transfer of Upper Assam to Purandar Singh
complete disruption of the old agrarian order
n486739e4923.x: A common underlying factor was the complete disruption of the old agrarian order through colonial revenue, forest and land policies.
n486739e4923.tq: Move from individual causes to the wider structural explanation.
xs: The common factor (UPSC 2011) was the **complete disruption of the old agrarian order** — option **(3)** is correct.
Upper Assam going to **Purandar Singh** was an outcome of the **Ahom** rebellion only; **Birsait** was Birsa's faith.
xa: Causes: **Indian Forest Act 1878**, **dikus** (land alienation) and **missionary interference**.
**Podu** = shifting cultivation, curbed by forest laws.
The Rampa rebellion (**1879-80**) also targeted **forest/podu restrictions** under the **Madras Forest Act**.
n486739e4923.fixed: odd 'broader interpretation' wording; align with y3eb66daf02f

n94fff88f7d4.s: The Khond rising was led by:
n94fff88f7d4.x: The Khond rising was led by Chakra Bisoi; Budhu Bhagat led the Kol rising and Sidhu and Kanhu the Santhal Hul.
xa: ⚠ Trap: notes (p.125) wrongly say Birsa led the **Kol** rebellion.
**Bhumij (1832-33)** — **Ganga Narayan**, Manbhum.
**Tana Bhagat (1914)** — **Jatra Bhagat (Oraon)**.

n9a3bc69771a.s: The Tamar tribal rising is associated with which one of the following combinations?
o: Oraon tribes and Tamar in Jharkhand
Bhil tribes and Khandesh in Maharashtra
n9a3bc69771a.x: The Tamar rising was associated with the Oraon tribes and the Tamar region of present-day Jharkhand. Its recorded period was 1789–1832.
n9a3bc69771a.tq: Test the tribe–region association rather than relying only on the revolt name.
xs: The **Tamar** rising involved **Oraon tribes** at **Tamar (Jharkhand)** — option **(1)** is correct.
