xa: He presided the Andhra Mahasabha in **1941**, **1944** and **1945**.
He wrote **Veera Telangana (Na Anubhavalu)**.
Communists won **41 of 145** Andhra-region seats in **1952**.

na18f2ab0222.s: What was one political consequence of the CPI’s ‘People’s War’ line and its opposition to the Quit India Movement?
o: It cost the CPI the 1945–46 elections.
It helped the CPI win the 1945–46 elections decisively.
It led immediately to the CPI split in 1964.
It resulted in the formation of Praja Natya Mandali.
na18f2ab0222.x: The CPI’s ‘People’s War’ line and opposition to the Quit India Movement cost it the 1945–46 elections.
na18f2ab0222.tq: Match the political line and wartime position with their stated electoral consequence.
xs: The **"People's War"** line and opposition to **Quit India** **cost the CPI the 1945-46 elections** — option **(1)**.
The **1964** split came much later and was a pro-Soviet vs pro-China divide.
xa: The CPI ban had been lifted on **23 July 1942**.
**Prakasam** arrested communist leaders in **1946**.
The **3rd** conference (**July 1943**) was the first open conference.

n24ccdc32156.s: For purposes of representation, the Communal Award of 1932 divided Indians into how many groups?
n24ccdc32156.x: The Communal Award divided Indians into 11 groups and recognised the Depressed Classes as a minority.
xa: Women got **3%** of seats in all provinces except **NWFP**.
Special-interest seats: **labour, landlords, traders, industrialists**.
UPPSC 2017 A/R: the Award gave each minority seats by **separate electorate** — both true, R explains A.

n4dee5cea450.s: Under the Communal Award, what percentage of seats in all provinces except the North-West Frontier Province was earmarked for women?
n4dee5cea450.x: The Communal Award reserved three per cent of seats for women in all provinces except the North-West Frontier Province.
xa: The Award covered **11 groups**.
Separate electorates: **Muslims, Sikhs, Europeans, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians** + **Depressed Classes**.
Announced **16 Aug 1932** by **Ramsay MacDonald**.

nd1e8b07bbae.s: Under the Communal Award, the Depressed Classes were given:
o: A double vote – one in a separate electorate and one in the general electorate
A single vote in the general electorate only
Two votes, both restricted to the separate electorate
No vote, but nomination to provincial legislatures
nd1e8b07bbae.x: The Depressed Classes received a double vote: one in a separate electorate and another in the general electorate.
xa: **Gandhi** opposed this with a **fast unto death** from **20 September 1932** at **Yerwada Jail, Poona**.
He argued separate electorates for Dalits would **permanently divide Hindu society**.
The Pact replaced this with **reserved seats in a joint electorate**.

nd47dfde6d59.s: Where did Gandhi begin his fast unto death against the Communal Award on 20 September 1932?
nd47dfde6d59.x: Gandhi began his fast unto death in Yerwada Jail, Poona, on 20 September 1932, arguing that separate electorates for Dalits would permanently divide Hindu society.
xa: The Award was announced on **16 Aug 1932** by **Ramsay MacDonald**.
It gave the Depressed Classes a **double vote**.
The Pact's **reserved seats in a joint electorate** became the model for SC reservation.

n5730cbf02a8.s: The term 'Scheduled Castes' was first used by the:
n5730cbf02a8.x: The term was first used by the Simon Commission, fixed by the Government of India Act, 1935, and the first list was issued in 1936.
xa: **Art. 17** later **abolished untouchability**.
The Pact's **joint electorate with reserved seats** = model for constitutional SC reservation.
The Social Justice Ministry began a **2-year** celebration of **Jyotiba Phule's 200th birth anniversary** (Apr **2026**).

ncabe8af4bfd.s: The reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes under the constitutional system is conceptually linked to which feature of the Poona Pact?
o: Nomination by the British Prime Minister
ncabe8af4bfd.x: The Poona Pact's model of joint electorates with reserved seats became the basis for the constitutional approach to SC political reservation.
ncabe8af4bfd.tq: Identify the institutional feature that carried forward into the Constitution.
xs: SC reservation follows the Pact's **reserved seats in a joint electorate** — option **(4)** is correct.
The Communal Award had instead given **separate electorates** with a **double vote**.
xa: **Gandhi's fast** (from **20 Sept 1932**, **Yerwada**) forced the change.
The Award was announced on **16 Aug 1932**.
**Art. 17** abolished **untouchability**.

na376e9e0acc.s: The immediate political pressure that prompted the Montagu Declaration of 20 August 1917 was exerted chiefly by the:
na376e9e0acc.x: The Home Rule Leagues created political pressure that contributed to the British declaration recognising self-government as an objective.
na376e9e0acc.tq: Identify the immediate political force rather than the later constitutional outcome.
xs: The **Montagu Declaration** (**20 August 1917**) was prompted by the **Home Rule Leagues** — option **(2)** is correct.
It was the **first official recognition** of self-government as an aim.
The **Liberal Federation** (**1918**), **Justice Party** and **Swaraj Party** came later.
xa: Aim: **"progressive realisation of responsible government"** in India as an integral part of the British Empire.
**Montagu** + **Chelmsford** toured India in **Dec 1917**.
The **Montagu-Chelmsford Report** was announced in **July 1918**.

nac5d6978ca2.s: The Montagu Declaration of 20 August 1917 announced British policy as the:
o: immediate grant of dominion status to India
progressive realisation of responsible government in India as an integral part of the British Empire
complete independence of India within ten years
provincial autonomy with an All-India Federation
nac5d6978ca2.x: On 20 August 1917 Montagu announced the gradual development of self-governing institutions with a view to the progressive realisation of responsible government in India as an integral part of the Empire - the first official recognition of self-government as an aim. Dominion status as a goal came with the 1929 Deepavali Declaration; complete independence was never promised then; provincial autonomy and federation came with the 1935 Act.
xs: The Declaration aimed at the **progressive realisation of responsible government** in India as an **integral part of the British Empire** — option **(2)**.
It spoke of **gradual development of self-governing institutions**, not immediate dominion status or independence.
**Provincial autonomy** and an **All-India Federation** came with the **1935 Act**.
xa: Made on **20 August 1917**, in Parliament.
Prompted by the **Home Rule Leagues**.
First official recognition of **self-government** as an aim.

n664dd331c98.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the response of the Moderates to the constitutional reforms of 1919?
o: They accepted the reforms and formed the Indian National Liberal Federation in 1918.
They boycotted the reforms and formed the Justice Party.
They joined the Home Rule Leagues and demanded complete independence.
They rejected the reforms and formed the Swaraj Party.
n664dd331c98.x: Surendranath Banerjee and other Moderates accepted the reforms, left the Congress and formed the Indian National Liberal Federation in 1918.
n664dd331c98.tq: Use the founder-group and organisation pairing to avoid confusing Moderates with Swarajists.
xs: The Moderates **accepted the reforms** and formed the **Indian National Liberal Federation (1918)** — option **(1)**.
They were led by **Surendranath Banerjee** and **left the Congress**.
The **Swaraj Party** (**C.R. Das**, **Motilal Nehru**) came later and entered councils to obstruct.
xa: Some notes call it the **"National Liberation Federation"**.
**C.R. Das** + **Tilak** wanted **rejection** at **Amritsar (1919)**.
**Gandhi** + **Malaviya** wanted a **fair trial**.

n777619e6865.s: At the Amritsar Congress of 1919, the reforms were described as:
n777619e6865.x: The Amritsar Congress characterised the reforms as inadequate, unsatisfactory and disappointing.
n777619e6865.tq: Recall the exact three-part political assessment used by the Congress.
xs: The **Amritsar Congress (1919)** called the reforms **"inadequate, unsatisfactory and disappointing"** — option **(4)**.
It was presided by **Motilal Nehru**.
xa: **C.R. Das** and **Tilak** favoured **rejection**.
**Gandhi** and **Malaviya** favoured a **fair trial**.
**Krishna Patrika**: "giving with the right hand, taking with the left".

n2748a3139c4.s: Which Act first introduced direct elections in India?
n2748a3139c4.x: The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced direct elections. The 1909 Act introduced elected non-official members mainly through indirect and separate electorates.
n2748a3139c4.tq: Resolve a close-option ambiguity by distinguishing direct elections from indirect elections.
xs: The **Government of India Act 1919** was the first to introduce **direct elections** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **1909** Act brought **elected** members mostly via **indirect** and **separate electorates**.
xa: ⚠ APPSC GS 2018 key gave **Indian Councils Act 1909** — mark it only if 1919 is absent.
Franchise in 1919 rested on **property, tax and education**.
Assembly: **145** members, **104** elected.
n2748a3139c4.fixed: meta wording ('if an examination question asks...most appropriate') is not exam style

n30e884a157f.s: Jinnah's Fourteen Points of 1929 were formulated as the Muslim League's response to which document?
n30e884a157f.x: Jinnah's Fourteen Points were the Muslim League's answer to the Nehru Report.
n30e884a157f.tq: Discriminate between closely connected constitutional documents.
xs: **Jinnah's Fourteen Points (1929)** were the Muslim League's answer to **the Nehru Report** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Nehru Report (1928)** was drafted by the **All Parties Conference** committee under **Motilal Nehru**.
The **Simon Report** came in **1930**, after the Fourteen Points.
xa: Key demands: **federal constitution**, **residuary powers to provinces**, **one-third** Muslim seats at the Centre and **separate electorates**.
The Nehru Report was discussed at the **Calcutta session (Dec 1928)** with a one-year ultimatum.
The **White Paper** was one basis of the **GoI Act 1935**, along with the Simon Report and three RTCs.

nb12253feace.s: The Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939 mainly because
o: The Muslim League withdrew support from all provincial ministries.
India was involved in the Second World War without the consent of Indian leaders.
The British abolished provincial legislatures without consultation.
The Federal Court rejected provincial autonomy.
nb12253feace.x: The Congress ministries resigned in protest against India being dragged into the Second World War without Indian consent.
nb12253feace.tq: Identify the political cause behind a major institutional action.
xs: The Congress ministries **resigned in Oct-Nov 1939** against **India being dragged into WWII** without Indian consent — so option **(2)** is correct.
The ministries had been formed after the **1937** provincial elections, which the **Congress** won.
The **Muslim League** did not withdraw support; instead it celebrated their exit.
xa: The League observed **"Day of Deliverance"** on **22 Dec 1939**; **Ambedkar** joined.
In **Madras**, the ministry was headed by **C. Rajagopalachari** (APHQ **2011**).
**Provincial autonomy** under the **1935 Act** had begun in **April 1937**.

n3b89db43218.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1919, dyarchy divided provincial subjects into:
n3b89db43218.x: Dyarchy was introduced in the provinces and divided provincial subjects into reserved and transferred subjects.
xa: Subjects were split into **central** and **provincial** lists.
Criticism: ministers got transferred subjects **without finance** (which stayed reserved).
⚠ UPSC notes wrongly call this **"provincial autonomy"** — that came with the **1935** Act.

n7d73bb061d0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about provincial dyarchy under the Government of India Act, 1919?
o: Provincial subjects were divided into reserved and transferred subjects.
Transferred subjects were administered by the Governor with ministers.
Local self-government was a reserved subject.
Reserved subjects were administered by the Governor with the Executive Council.
n7d73bb061d0.x: Local self-government was a transferred subject, administered by the Governor with ministers, not a reserved subject.
xa: Ministers came from the **elected legislature** and answered to it.
Reserved subjects included **law and order**, **finance**, **land revenue**.
In **1935** local self-government became a **provincial subject**.

n11c0b20ac9f.s: Section 63 of the Government of India Act, 1935 dealt with the Governor's:
n11c0b20ac9f.x: Section 63 enabled the Governor to address the provincial legislature in his discretion.
xa: From **1937** the speech was prepared **with ministers**; the **Constituent Assembly** kept that convention.
Today the Governor's address is under **Art. 175/176**.
Other borrowings: **Instrument of Instructions** → **Directive Principles**; **Federal Court** → **Supreme Court**.

n5a3e1d7db3c.s: Dyarchy was criticised because ministers held transferred subjects while finance was a:
n5a3e1d7db3c.x: Ministers controlled transferred subjects, but finance remained a reserved subject, so they lacked financial control.
xa: **Dyarchy** = dual government in the **provinces** under the **GoI Act 1919**.
⚠ APPSC **2019**: "dyarchy = single government" was false.
The **1935 Act** abolished provincial dyarchy and introduced **provincial autonomy**.
Another criticism: **communal electorates** were extended.

n92f8fff0dd4.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1919, the upper chamber of the bicameral central legislature was the:
n92f8fff0dd4.x: The 1919 Act created a bicameral central legislature with the Council of State as the upper chamber and the Legislative Assembly as the lower chamber.
xa: Assembly = **145** members (**104** elected); Council of State = **60**.
Both houses were **mostly elected**.
First President of the Assembly: **Frederick Whyte** (**1921**).

nd880d2ac370.s: The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced direct elections on the basis of:
o: Separate nomination by the Secretary of State
nd880d2ac370.x: The Act introduced direct elections, but the franchise remained limited by property, tax and educational qualifications.
nd880d2ac370.tq: Combine the electoral method with the qualification-based nature of the franchise.
xs: Franchise was limited by **property, tax and educational** qualifications — option **(2)** is correct.
There was no **universal adult franchise**.
xa: The **GoI Act 1919** was the **first Act** to introduce **direct elections**.
**Communal representation** was **extended** (Sikhs etc.).
First elections: **1920**, boycotted by the Congress.

nf443898933f.s: The statutory review provision of the Government of India Act, 1919 required the appointment of a commission after:
nf443898933f.x: The Act required a statutory commission to review its working after ten years. The Simon Commission was appointed two years early under this provision.
nf443898933f.tq: Recall the statutory interval and distinguish it from the actual early appointment.
xs: The Act required a **statutory commission after 10 years** — option **(4) Ten years** is correct.
The **Simon Commission** was appointed **two years early** (**8 November 1927**).
xa: Simon Commission = **Indian Statutory Commission** / "White Commission".
Appointed by the **Conservative (Baldwin)** government.
The Swarajist demand for review led to the **Muddiman Committee (1924)**.

n35c031cc974.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1919, how many members did the Viceroy's Executive Council have apart from the Commander-in-Chief?
n35c031cc974.x: Apart from the Commander-in-Chief, the Viceroy's Executive Council had six members, of whom three were Indians.
xa: Centre: **Council of State** + **Legislative Assembly**.
**Communal representation** was extended (Sikhs etc.).
A **statutory commission** was due after **10 years**.

nacbc3f01bfb.s: Which of the following was a member of the seven-member Simon Commission?
nacbc3f01bfb.x: Clement Attlee was one of the seven British members of the Simon Commission, which was chaired by Sir John Simon.
xa: **No Indian member** was the reason for the boycott.
Also called the **Indian Statutory Commission** / "White Commission".
Second visit: **Oct 1928-Apr 1929**.

n0bb8a54e1a4.s: The Simon Commission arrived at Bombay on:
n0bb8a54e1a4.x: The Simon Commission arrived at Bombay on 3 February 1928.
n0bb8a54e1a4.tq: Separate the appointment year from the year of arrival in India.
xs: The Commission arrived at **Bombay** on **3 February 1928** (APPSC GS 2021) — option **(1)** is correct.
An **all-India hartal** and **black flags** greeted it.
**30 Oct 1928** was the **Lahore** lathi charge on **Lala Lajpat Rai**.
xa: Second visit: **Oct 1928-Apr 1929**.
Slogan **"Simon Go Back"** coined by **Yusuf Meherally** (APPSC GS 2018).
Andhra route: **Tenali - Guntur - Vijayawada - Ongole - Madras**.

nedb55809afa.s: Tanguturi Prakasam acquired the title 'Andhra Kesari' in connection with which incident?
o: Baring his chest before the police during the anti-Simon Commission protest at Madras
Leading the Home Rule League in Andhra
Leading the boycott of the Rowlatt Act in Guntur
nedb55809afa.x: Tanguturi Prakasam bared his chest before the police during the anti-Simon Commission protest at Madras and became known as Andhra Kesari.
nedb55809afa.tq: Link the title to the distinctive action and place associated with it.
xs: **Prakasam** **bared his chest** to the police at the **Madras** anti-Simon protest and was called **"Andhra Kesari"** — option **(1)**.
The **Amritsar Congress (1919)** was presided by **Motilal Nehru**, not Prakasam.
xa: Andhra anti-Simon committee president: **S. Satyamurti**.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** toured Andhra for the boycott.
Tenali/Guntur protest: **G.V. Unnayya Sastri**.

n76f391f55c3.s: The term 'Scheduled Castes' was first used in the:
n76f391f55c3.x: The term 'Scheduled Castes' was first used in the Simon Commission Report.
n76f391f55c3.tq: Match the exact constitutional term with the report in which it first appeared.
xs: **"Scheduled Castes"** was first used in the **Simon Commission Report** — option **(1)** is correct.
The Report came in **1930**.
xa: It recommended **provincial autonomy** and **keeping separate electorates**.
It also proposed separating **Sindh** from Bombay and **Burma** from India.
The **Nehru Report (1928)** was drafted by an **All Parties Conference** committee.

n34b1ff96dac.s: Which of the following did NOT join the boycott of the Simon Commission?
o: Jinnah's faction of the Muslim League
n34b1ff96dac.x: The Justice Party (like Shafi's League faction) did not join the boycott, while Jinnah's faction and the Hindu Mahasabha joined it.
xa: The **Punjab Unionists** also did not join.
The **Madras Congress (Dec 1927)** under **M.A. Ansari** called for boycott.
The Justice Party held office in Madras most of **1920-37**.

nd9d66de82c7.s: The slogan 'Simon Go Back' was coined by:
nd9d66de82c7.x: Yusuf Meherally coined 'Simon Go Back' (APPSC GS 2018). Lajpat Rai led the Lahore protest, Prakasam the Madras protest, and S. Satyamurti headed the Andhra anti-Simon committee.
xs: The slogan **"Simon Go Back"** was coined by **Yusuf Meherally** (APPSC GS **2018**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Lala Lajpat Rai** led the **Lahore** protest and died after the lathi charge of **30 Oct 1928**.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** led the **Madras** protest, baring his chest to police.
**S. Satyamurti** was president of the **Andhra anti-Simon committee**.
xa: Prakasam earned the title **"Andhra Kesari"** for his defiance at Madras.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** toured Andhra for the boycott.
The **Madras session (Dec 1927)** of the INC under **M.A. Ansari** resolved to boycott the Commission "at every stage and in every form".
The Commission is also called the **Indian Statutory Commission** or "White Commission".

na3cd5353260.s: The Nehru Report was primarily prepared in response to which of the following?
o: Lord Birkenhead's challenge to Indians to frame a constitution
The demand for a separate Muslim homeland
The failure of the Cripps Mission
na3cd5353260.x: The Nehru Report was prepared in reply to Secretary of State Lord Birkenhead's challenge to Indians to frame their own constitution.
na3cd5353260.tq: Identify the immediate cause behind a constitutional document.
xs: The **Nehru Report** answered Secretary of State **Lord Birkenhead's challenge** to Indians to frame a constitution — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was drafted by a **9-member** committee of the **All Parties Conference** (**1928**).
The **Cripps Mission** is unrelated here — the report predates it.
xa: **Motilal Nehru** was Chairman and **Jawaharlal Nehru** Secretary of the Nehru Report committee.
It was discussed at the **Calcutta session (Dec 1928)**, which gave the British a **one-year ultimatum**.
The Muslim League's reply to the report was **Jinnah's Fourteen Points (1929)**.

n3eea5c43480.s: The federation proposed under the Government of India Act, 1935 provided for dyarchy at:
o: Both the Centre and the provinces
n3eea5c43480.x: The 1935 Act provided dyarchy at the Centre, while replacing dyarchy in the provinces with provincial autonomy.
xa: ⚠ Dyarchy: **1919** = in the **provinces**; **1935** = provincial dyarchy abolished, Centre dyarchy never operated.
Because the federation failed, the **Centre continued under the 1919 structure**.
The Act had **321 sections and 10 schedules** — the longest Act.

n44f446e38c5.s: The Government of India Act, 1935, the longest British Act on India, contained:
n44f446e38c5.x: The Act contained 321 sections and 10 schedules; some references describe it as having 14 parts and 321 articles.
xa: Basis of the Act: **Simon Report** + three **RTCs** + the **White Paper**.
It is called the largest single source of the **Constitution's structure**.
Borrowed: **Instrument of Instructions** → **Directive Principles** (APPSC **2023**); **Federal Court** → **Supreme Court**.

n48cc706b5c9.s: The Public Service Commission provided for under Section 96(C) of the 1919 Act was set up on 1 October:
n48cc706b5c9.x: The Public Service Commission was set up on 1 October 1926, after the Lee Commission, not in 1921 when the Act came into force.
xa: The **1935** Act provided a **Federal PSC and Provincial PSCs**.
ICS exams were held simultaneously in India from **1922**.
The office of **High Commissioner for India** was created in **London**.

ndb7e1fd202b.s: The Chamber of Princes (Narendra Mandal) was set up by royal proclamation in:
ndb7e1fd202b.x: The Chamber of Princes, a consultative body of Indian rulers, was set up in 1921 under the 1919 reforms, not under the 1935 Act.
xa: The 1935 Act's **All-India Federation** of provinces + princely states **never came into being**.
First Assembly President **Frederick Whyte** also dates to **1921**.
The **Federal Court** at Delhi came in **1937**.

n60282ba14f6.s: Who was the first President of the Legislative Assembly under the 1919 Act?
n60282ba14f6.x: Frederick Whyte was the first President of the Legislative Assembly, with Sachchidananda Sinha as the first Deputy President.
xa: **Vithalbhai Patel** later became Assembly president (Speaker) after **1923**.
The 1919 Act created the posts of **President + Deputy President**.
First Madras CM: **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar** (**Dec 1920**).

n5b0f474e268.s: The Simon Commission (1927) was appointed by the Conservative government of:
n5b0f474e268.x: The Conservative government of Stanley Baldwin appointed the Simon Commission on 8 November 1927, two years early, to review the 1919 Act.
xa: The Act had fixed a review **after 10 years**.
Members: **7**, all British; chairman **Sir John Simon**, incl. **Clement Attlee**.
Arrived at **Bombay** on **3 February 1928**.

n328f64098bc.s: After the Congress ministries resigned, the Muslim League observed the 'Day of Deliverance' on:
n328f64098bc.x: The League observed 22 December 1939 as the Day of Deliverance after the Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939.
xa: **Ambedkar** joined the Day of Deliverance.
The ministries resigned against India being dragged into **WWII**.
Under the **1919** Act, the first Madras Chief Minister was **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar** (**Dec 1920**) of the **Justice Party**.

n9a25293acf2.s: A 27-member Andhra delegation led by Nyapati Subbarao met Montagu at Madras to demand:
o: A separate Muslim province in South India
Abolition of the Madras Legislative Council
n9a25293acf2.x: The Andhra delegation led by Nyapati Subbarao sought the creation of a separate Andhra province.
n9a25293acf2.tq: Connect the delegation leader and its regional constitutional demand.
xs: **Nyapati Subbarao's** **27-member** delegation met Montagu at **Madras** for a **separate Andhra province** — option **(3)**.
p.442 of the notes gives it as **21 members**.
xa: **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** presided the **Special Andhra Mahasabha** at **Guntur** (**17 Aug 1918**).
**Krishna Patrika**: reforms = "giving with the right hand, taking with the left".
Andhra delegations seeking a separate province are a key **AP angle** of the 1919 reforms.

n8b8a7409a11.s: In the Madras elections of 1920, which one of the following combinations is correct?
o: Congress boycotted the elections and the Justice Party won 63 seats
The Justice Party boycotted the elections and Congress won 63 seats
Both Congress and the Justice Party boycotted the elections
n8b8a7409a11.x: The Congress boycotted the 1920 Madras elections as part of the Non-Cooperation movement, while the Justice Party won 63 seats.
n8b8a7409a11.tq: Pair the political action with the correct party and election result.
xs: **Congress boycotted** (Non-Cooperation) and the **Justice Party won 63 seats** — option **(2)** is correct.
The first elections under the Act were in **1920**.
xa: **A. Subbarayalu Reddiar** became the first Chief Minister (**Dec 1920**), then the **Raja of Panagal** (**1921**).
The Justice Party held office most of **1920-37**.
The Justice Party **did not join** the Simon boycott.

n6061c3c1c7d.s: The Muddiman Committee (1924) was the British response to the demand of the ____ for a review of the 1919 Act.
n6061c3c1c7d.x: The Muddiman Committee (1924) was the British response to the Swarajist demand for a review of the Government of India Act, 1919.
xa: Leaders: **C.R. Das** and **Motilal Nehru**.
**V. Ramadas** (Andhra) was elected to the Central Legislative Assembly in **1923**.
**Vithalbhai Patel** became Assembly president.

n874131d0d70.s: Who became the President, or Speaker, of the Central Legislative Assembly after the Swarajist success in 1923?
n874131d0d70.x: Vithalbhai Patel became the President, commonly described as the Speaker, of the Central Legislative Assembly.
n874131d0d70.tq: Use the office-holder trap by distinguishing the legislative leaders from the presiding officer.
xs: **Vithalbhai Patel** became **president (speaker)** of the Central Legislative Assembly — option **(1)**.
**M.A. Ansari** presided the **Madras Congress (Dec 1927)**; **C.R. Das** and **Motilal Nehru** led the Swaraj Party.
xa: First Assembly President: **Frederick Whyte** (**1921**).
Swarajists won about **40%** of seats in **1923**.
**Muddiman Committee**: **1924**.

n394e1928b13.s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Government of India Act, 1919?
o: Direct elections to the central legislature
Creation of the office of High Commissioner for India in London
Separation of provincial budgets from the central budget
Provincial autonomy in place of dyarchy
n394e1928b13.x: Provincial autonomy was associated with the Government of India Act, 1935. The 1919 Act introduced dyarchy in the provinces, along with the other listed features.
n394e1928b13.tq: Use the later 1935 feature as the chronological trap in a NOT question.
xs: **Provincial autonomy in place of dyarchy** was not a 1919 feature — option **(4)**; it came with the **1935 Act** (from **April 1937**).
The 1919 Act gave **direct elections**, the **High Commissioner** in **London** and **separate provincial budgets**.
xa: The **Simon Report (1930)** first recommended abolishing provincial dyarchy for **provincial autonomy**.
⚠ **Dyarchy**: **1919** = in the provinces; **1935** = provincial dyarchy abolished, Centre dyarchy never operated.
The 1935 Act also abolished the **India Council**.

n7bf4df4be8c.s: The dyarchy scheme of the Government of India Act, 1919 is named after Edwin Montagu and:
n7bf4df4be8c.x: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms are named after Secretary of State Edwin Montagu and Viceroy Lord Chelmsford.
xa: Dyarchy was in the **provinces**, not the Centre.
The **1935** Act abolished provincial dyarchy; **Centre dyarchy** never operated.
⚠ UPSC notes wrongly call 1919 **"provincial autonomy"**.

n410de35809f.s: The Simon Commission Report (1930) recommended replacing provincial dyarchy with:
o: Complete responsible government at the Centre
n410de35809f.x: The Simon Commission Report recommended abolishing provincial dyarchy in favour of provincial autonomy.
xa: The Report (**1930**) first used the term **"Scheduled Castes"**.
The **1935 Act** drew on the **Simon Report**, three **RTCs** and the **White Paper**.
Provincial autonomy began in **April 1937**.

n1770222ff48.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents important features of Jinnah's Fourteen Points?
o: Unitary constitution, joint electorates and abolition of provincial autonomy
Federal constitution, residuary powers to provinces and separate electorates
Dominion status, nominated legislatures and universal adult franchise
Presidential government, one-third provincial seats and communal veto at all levels
n1770222ff48.x: Jinnah's Fourteen Points demanded a federal constitution with residuary powers to the provinces and separate electorates.
n1770222ff48.tq: Split the options by testing the distinctive features of a constitutional demand.
xs: The Fourteen Points demanded a **federal constitution**, **residuary powers to provinces** and **separate electorates** — so option **(2)** is correct.
They also sought **one-third** Muslim seats at the **Centre**.
A **unitary** constitution with **joint electorates** is the opposite of these demands.
xa: The Fourteen Points (**1929**) were the Muslim League's answer to the **Nehru Report (1928)**.
The Nehru Report was drafted by a **9-member** committee of the **All Parties Conference** under **Motilal Nehru**.
⚠ Do not confuse "one-third **provincial** seats" — the demand was one-third Muslim seats **at the Centre**.

nc997afd2928.s: Provincial autonomy under the Government of India Act, 1935 began in:
nc997afd2928.x: Provincial autonomy, which replaced dyarchy in the provinces, began in April 1937.
xa: The Act also created bicameral legislatures (**Vidhan Parishads**) in some provinces.
**Local self-government** became a **provincial subject** (under 1919 it was a **transferred** subject).
Provincial autonomy was a recommendation of the **Simon Report (1930)**.

nc5518c18ade.s: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in:
nc5518c18ade.x: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in March 1931; 'March 1930' is a known trap (March 1930 was the start of the Dandi March). December 1929 was the Lahore session and August 1932 the Communal Award.
xs: The **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** was signed in **March 1931** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ "March **1930**" is the known trap (APPSC **2018** context) — wrong year.
xa: APPSC **2018** chronology: **Partition of Bengal**, **Rowlatt Act**, **Simon Commission**, **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** (b, d, a, c).
**1929**: Jinnah's Fourteen Points; **1928**: Nehru Report.

n0a60508781d.s: Tanguturi Prakasam earned the title ‘Andhra Kesari’ because he
o: drafted the Nehru Report in Andhra
bared his chest and dared the police to shoot during the Simon protest
organised the first Round Table Conference
led the boycott resolution at the Madras Congress session
n0a60508781d.x: During the Simon protest, Prakasam bared his chest and challenged the police to shoot, earning the title ‘Andhra Kesari’.
n0a60508781d.tq: Connect an honorific with the specific incident that produced it.
xs: During the **Madras** anti-Simon protest (**1928**), **Tanguturi Prakasam** **bared his chest and dared the police to shoot** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Police firing had killed **Parthasarathi**; Prakasam's defiance earned him the title **"Andhra Kesari"**.
The **Nehru Report** was drafted by **Motilal Nehru's** committee, and the RTCs were held in **London** — not Prakasam's work.
xa: Date of the Madras protest: **26 Feb 1928** (a printed **"2028"** is a typo); asked in APPSC GS **2022**.
**S. Satyamurthy** was President of the **Andhra Boycott Committee**.
Prakasam's moment and the Simon report's neglect of Andhra fuelled the **separate-Andhra** demand.

nffeed07c2c1.s: The All Parties Muslim Conference held at Delhi (from 31 December 1928), under the Aga Khan,
o: drafted the Government of India Act, 1935
resolved to boycott the Simon Commission at every stage
accepted the Nehru Report without modification
nffeed07c2c1.x: The All Parties Muslim Conference at Delhi in January 1929, presided over by the Aga Khan, rejected the Nehru Report.
nffeed07c2c1.tq: Distinguish the Muslim Conference's reaction from the earlier All Parties Conference.
xs: The **All Parties Muslim Conference** (**Delhi, Jan 1929**) under the **Aga Khan** **rejected the Nehru Report** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **GoI Act 1935** came from the Simon report + RTCs, not from this conference.
The boycott "at every stage" was not this conference's work.
xa: **Jinnah's Fourteen Points** followed in **March 1929** at the **Muslim League session in Delhi**.
The **Muslim League** also rejected the Nehru Report.
The **Nehru Report** proposed **joint electorates**, unacceptable to these Muslim bodies.

n4aa28a4ec17.s: Jinnah's Fourteen Points were presented in March 1929 at the
o: Indian National Congress session at Lahore
Second Round Table Conference at London
n4aa28a4ec17.x: Jinnah presented the Fourteen Points in March 1929 at the Muslim League session in Delhi.
n4aa28a4ec17.tq: Match a constitutional document with its organisation, venue and date.
xs: Jinnah presented the **Fourteen Points** in **March 1929** at the **Muslim League session in Delhi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Lahore** session (**1929**) of Congress declared **Purna Swaraj** — not the Fourteen Points.
The **2nd RTC** came later, in **Sep-Dec 1931**.
xa: Demands: **federal constitution**, **residuary powers to provinces**, **one-third** Muslim seats at the centre, **separate electorates**, Muslim-majority safeguards.
⚠ **Delhi Proposals (1927)** = drop separate electorates; **Fourteen Points (1929)** = keep them.
The **All Parties Muslim Conference** (**Jan 1929**) under the **Aga Khan** had already rejected the Nehru Report.

ncea40c63d1f.s: The Deepavali Declaration of 1929 was issued by:
ncea40c63d1f.x: Lord Irwin issued the Deepavali Declaration in 1929, promising a Round Table Conference after the Simon Commission report.
xa: It declared **dominion status** the natural goal of India's constitutional progress.
The **Simon report** followed in **May 1930**.
**Ramsay MacDonald** was British PM during all three RTCs (**1930-32**).

ne76bbd37689.s: During the Simon Commission protest in Madras, the person killed by police firing was
ne76bbd37689.x: Police firing during the Madras protest killed Parthasarathi.
ne76bbd37689.tq: Identify the individual associated with a specific regional incident.
xs: Police firing during the **Madras** Simon protest killed **Parthasarathi** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**G.V. Unnayya Sastri** led protests at **Tenali and Guntur**; **Bulusu Sambamurti** toured Andhra for the boycott.
**S. Satyamurthy** was President of the **Andhra Boycott Committee**.
xa: After the firing, **Tanguturi Prakasam** bared his chest → title **"Andhra Kesari"**.
The protest was on **26 Feb 1928** (APPSC GS **2022**).
**Guntur and Ongole** showed **black flags** to the Commission.

nbae5fb4b949.s: Black flags were shown against the Simon Commission at
nbae5fb4b949.x: Black flags were shown at Guntur and Ongole. G. V. Unnayya Sastri led protests at Tenali and Guntur.
nbae5fb4b949.tq: Distinguish locations of black-flag demonstrations from locations of organised leadership.
xs: **Black flags** were shown at **Guntur and Ongole** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Eluru, Srikakulam, Tirupati, Kurnool** instead passed **municipal resolutions**.
At **Vijayawada**, chairman **Kaleswara Rao** sent the "Simon Go Back" cover; **Tenali** saw G.V. Unnayya Sastri's protest.
xa: **G.V. Unnayya Sastri** led the protest at **Tenali and Guntur**.
**Bulusu Sambamurti** toured Andhra for the boycott.
**S. Satyamurthy** presided over the **Andhra Boycott Committee**.

n77f20d64178.s: The challenge issued by Birkenhead in 1927, which led to the formation of the committee for the Nehru Report, was that Indians
o: could not organise a boycott of the Simon Commission
could not agree on a constitutional scheme
n77f20d64178.x: Birkenhead challenged Indians to prepare an agreed constitutional scheme, leading to the All Parties Conference and the Nehru Report committee.
n77f20d64178.tq: Identify the cause behind the formation of a constitutional committee.
xs: **Birkenhead's** challenge (**1927**) was that Indians **could not draft an agreed constitution** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The answer was the **Nehru Report** (**August 1928**), drafted by a committee of the **All Parties Conference**.
Far from opposing **linguistic provinces** or **dominion status**, the Nehru Report itself recommended both.
xa: **Dr M.A. Ansari** presided the **All Parties Conference (1928)**.
**Motilal Nehru** chaired the **7-member committee**; **Jawaharlal Nehru** was secretary.
⚠ Trap: "**10 Aug 1929**" is wrong — the report is of **1928**.

n12b3248d4ed.s: The Nehru Report, drafted by a committee chaired by Motilal Nehru, was published in:
n12b3248d4ed.x: The Nehru Report came out in August 1928; 1929 is a known trap.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "**10 Aug 1929**" is wrong; **1928** is correct.
⚠ **Ansari** presided the All Parties Conference; **Motilal** chaired its drafting committee.
The committee had **7 members**.

nf2c4cc52c10.s: Who served as secretary of the committee that drafted the Nehru Report?
nf2c4cc52c10.x: Jawaharlal Nehru was the secretary; the report recommended a Supreme Court and proposed ending dyarchy.
xa: **Motilal Nehru** chaired the **7-member committee**.
It recommended **linguistic provinces** (incl. **Andhra**) and **joint electorates**.
Report date: **August 1928**.

n3dc59edc1f3.s: On electorates, the Simon Commission report recommended:
n3dc59edc1f3.x: The report recommended continuing separate communal electorates, along with abolition of dyarchy and provincial autonomy.
xa: Report date: **May 1930**.
It separated **Sindh** from Bombay and **Burma** from India, and created an **Orissa** province.
Report + RTCs → **Government of India Act 1935**.

n4ce5f9f8f31.s: On the question of electorates, the Delhi Proposals supported:
n4ce5f9f8f31.x: The Delhi Proposals supported joint electorates subject to safeguards such as the separation of Sindh and one-third Muslim representation at the Centre.
xa: ⚠ **Delhi Proposals (1927)** = drop separate electorates; **Fourteen Points (1929)** = keep separate electorates.
**Jinnah's Fourteen Points** came in **March 1929** at the **Muslim League session in Delhi**.
The **All Parties Muslim Conference** (**Delhi, Jan 1929**) under the **Aga Khan** rejected the Nehru Report.

nd777eff1996.s: Jinnah's Fourteen Points demanded what share of Muslim representation at the Centre?
nd777eff1996.x: Jinnah's Fourteen Points demanded one-third Muslim representation at the Centre, along with provincial residuary powers, separate electorates and safeguards for Muslim-majority provinces.
xa: Presented in **March 1929** at the **Muslim League session in Delhi**.
⚠ The **Delhi Proposals (March 1927)** had offered to **drop** separate electorates for joint electorates.
The Delhi Proposals also sought **separation of Sindh** and reforms in **NWFP and Baluchistan**.

n2ddabee418c.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Nehru Report?
o: Universal adult suffrage and fundamental rights
Separate electorates as the permanent basis of representation
A federal structure with a bicameral central legislature
n2ddabee418c.x: The Nehru Report recommended joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities, not separate electorates as a permanent arrangement.
n2ddabee418c.tq: Use the central distinction between joint electorates and separate electorates.
xs: The Nehru Report did **not** recommend **separate electorates** — so option **(3)** is the answer.
It proposed **joint electorates + reserved seats** for minorities.
It did recommend **dominion status**, a **bicameral** centre and **universal adult suffrage + fundamental rights**.
xa: Other recommendations: end of **dyarchy**, **responsible government**, a **Supreme Court**, **linguistic provinces** (incl. **Andhra**).
The **Muslim League** rejected it; **Jinnah's amendments** failed at the **Calcutta All Parties Convention (Dec 1928)**.
⚠ Separate electorates were kept by the **Simon report** and demanded by the **Fourteen Points**.

n04630fd37e0.s: The Simon Commission report recommended the creation of which new province?
n04630fd37e0.x: The report recommended creating Orissa as a province (and separating Sindh and Burma), but ignored Andhra's demand for a separate province.
xa: Contrast: **Oriyas lobbied** the Commission; **Andhras boycotted** it.
This neglect, along with Prakasam's **"Andhra Kesari"** moment, fuelled the **separate-Andhra** demand.
Report date: **May 1930**.

ne5a586f38f7.s: The Simon Commission's neglect of Andhra's demand, with Prakasam's 'Andhra Kesari' moment, fuelled the demand for:
o: restoration of dyarchy in the provinces
ne5a586f38f7.x: The Simon Commission's neglect of Andhra's demand and Prakasam's role fuelled the demand for a separate Andhra Province.
xa: **Oriyas lobbied** the Commission; **Andhras boycotted** it.
**Prakasam** became **"Andhra Kesari"** at the **Madras** protest (**26 Feb 1928**).
The **Nehru Report** had backed **linguistic provinces** including **Andhra**.

n42671327c04.s: Which group lobbied the Simon Commission and saw its provincial demand supported in the report?
n42671327c04.x: The Oriyas lobbied the Simon Commission and the report supported the creation of Orissa; the Andhras boycotted it and their demand was ignored.
xa: Andhra boycott: **Prakasam** in Madras, **black flags** at **Guntur and Ongole**, **Kaleswara Rao's** cover at Vijayawada.
**S. Satyamurthy** was President of the **Andhra Boycott Committee**.
The **Nehru Report** had backed **linguistic provinces** including **Andhra**.

na1b61e78afa.s: The three Round Table Conferences in London were held under which British Prime Minister?
na1b61e78afa.x: All three Round Table Conferences were held in London under Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald to discuss the Simon Report and a federal constitution.
xa: Congress attended only the **2nd** RTC; **Ambedkar** attended all three.
The 1st RTC agreed on a **federal structure**.

nbbd77d01687.s: After returning from the Second Round Table Conference, Mahatma Gandhi:
o: attended the Third Round Table Conference
resumed the Civil Disobedience Movement and was jailed in Yerwada
nbbd77d01687.x: After the Second Conference, Gandhi resumed the Civil Disobedience Movement and was imprisoned in Yerwada; the Communal Award followed in August 1932.
xa: The 2nd RTC failed on **minority representation**.
3rd RTC: **17 Nov-24 Dec 1932**, only **46** delegates.
Gandhi was the **sole INC representative** at the 2nd RTC.

n908011aedb2.s: How many subjects did the Federal List contain under the Government of India Act, 1935?
n908011aedb2.x: The Federal List had 59 subjects, the Provincial List 54 and the Concurrent List 36.
xa: **Residuary powers** were with the **Governor-General**.
The **Governor** had discretionary powers, e.g. the **Sec. 63** address.
The **federal scheme** is among the features borrowed into the Constitution.

na01d787b930.s: Which one of the following sets contains only features borrowed from the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: Concurrent List, joint sitting and freedom of trade
Fundamental Rights, judicial review, impeachment and Vice-President
Federal scheme, office of Governor, judiciary and Public Service Commissions
Fundamental Duties, Five-Year Plans and ideals of justice
na01d787b930.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 contributed the federal scheme, office of Governor, judiciary and Public Service Commissions, among other administrative features.
na01d787b930.tq: Group the administrative and institutional provisions before considering ideological or federal borrowings from other countries.
xs: **Federal scheme, office of Governor, judiciary and PSCs** all come from the **1935 Act** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Act also gave **emergency provisions** and administrative details.
xa: **Instrument of Instructions** → model for the **Directive Principles** (APPSC **2023**).
**1919 Act** → **bicameralism**, **direct elections**, **separate provincial budget**.
Large parts of the Constitution's structure come from the 1935 Act — hence "**blueprint**".

na255c144721.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, residuary powers were vested in the:
na255c144721.x: Residuary powers were vested in the Governor-General, not in the provinces.
xa: Three lists: **Federal (59)**, **Provincial (54)**, **Concurrent (36)**.
**Separate electorates** were extended to **depressed classes, women and labour**.
The **Governor** had discretion too, e.g. the **Sec. 63** address.

n9ded92b02d4.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 further extended the system of separate electorates to include which of the following groups?
o: Workers, soldiers and civil servants only
n9ded92b02d4.x: The separate electorate system was extended further to depressed classes, women and labour.
n9ded92b02d4.tq: Test the exact membership of a statutory category through a closely related group-list option.
xs: Separate electorates were extended to **depressed classes, women and labour** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The 1935 Act extended the communal scheme **further** rather than ending it.
xa: The Act was called a **"Charter of Slavery"** by **Nehru**.
**Residuary powers** went to the **Governor-General**.
Congress rejected the Act and demanded a **Constituent Assembly** on **adult franchise**.

n19d342c9975.s: The idea behind Section 63 of the Government of India Act, 1935, on the Governor's address to the provincial legislature, is carried in which Article of the Constitution of India?
n19d342c9975.x: Article 175 (the Governor's address) carries the idea of Section 63 of the 1935 Act. Today the speech reflects the elected ministry's policy rather than the Governor's own discretion.
xs: **Section 63** (Governor's address) is carried by **Article 175** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Under Sec. 63 the Governor addressed the provincial legislature "**in his discretion**".
Today the speech reflects the **elected ministry's policy**.
xa: Rows over **Governors' addresses** in **Opposition-ruled States** are traced to Sec. 63 and Art. 175 (**26 Jan 2026**).
The **office of Governor** itself is a **1935** borrowing.
The **Instrument of Instructions** became the model for the **Directive Principles**.

n50b6c2c77e3.s: The Sri Bagh Pact (November 1937) was concluded at the house of:
n50b6c2c77e3.x: The pact, which sought to close the Coastal-Rayalaseema rift, was concluded at Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's house 'Sreerbagh', not Prakasam's.
xa: **Prakasam** led the Madras **1937** campaign as **APCC President**.
First Congress government in Madras (**1937**, **Rajaji**) ended Justice Party rule of **1920-37**.
Andhra ministers in **1937**: **Prakasam**, **Gopala Reddy**, **V.V. Giri**; **Bulusu Sambamurthy** Speaker.
n50b6c2c77e3.fixed: Sri Bagh Pact was 16 Nov 1937, after the Feb 1937 polls, not before

n507927d292b.s: Who first raised the demand for a Constituent Assembly in 1934?
n507927d292b.x: M.N. Roy first raised the Constituent Assembly demand in 1934; the Congress adopted it officially in 1935.
xa: The demand was for an Assembly elected on **adult franchise**.
The elections were held in winter **1936-37** in **11** provinces.
**Jinnah** called the Act "thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable".

n07005a4cefd.s: Who described the Government of India Act, 1935 as “thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable”?
n07005a4cefd.x: Muhammad Ali Jinnah used the description “thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable” for the Act.
n07005a4cefd.tq: Discriminate between two well-known but different criticisms of the same Act.
xs: **Jinnah** called the Act "**thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable**" — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Nehru** called it a **"Charter of Slavery"** and "a machine with **strong brakes but no engine**".
**M.N. Roy** is known for first raising the **Constituent Assembly** demand (**1934**).
xa: Congress officially demanded a Constituent Assembly in **1935**.
The **Muslim League** later **did poorly** even in Muslim seats in the **1937** elections.
⚠ **Lucknow 1936** rejected the Act; **Faizpur 1936** decided to contest.

n0a60cdae9e2.s: Who described the Government of India Act, 1935 as a 'Charter of Slavery' and as 'a machine with strong brakes but no engine'?
n0a60cdae9e2.x: Jawaharlal Nehru used both descriptions. Jinnah called the Act 'thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable'; M.N. Roy first raised the Constituent Assembly demand (1934).
n0a60cdae9e2.tq: Charter of Slavery / brakes no engine = Nehru; 'rotten' = Jinnah.
xs: **Jawaharlal Nehru** used both phrases — **"Charter of Slavery"** and "a machine with **strong brakes but no engine**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Jinnah** called it "**thoroughly rotten**, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable".
**M.N. Roy** first raised the **Constituent Assembly** demand (**1934**).
xa: Nehru presided the **Lucknow (1936)** session, which rejected the Act.
**Faizpur (1936)** decided to contest the elections.
Congress demanded a **Constituent Assembly** on **adult franchise** (official in **1935**).

n869f606043a.s: In how many of the eleven provinces did the Congress form ministries after the 1937 elections?
n869f606043a.x: Congress formed ministries in eight of the eleven provinces, including Bombay, Madras, Central Provinces, Orissa, Bihar, UP, NWFP and Assam.
xa: The 5: **Madras, UP, CP, Bihar, Orissa**.
**Gandhi's advice**: hold office "**lightly, not tightly**", a "**crown of thorns**".
The ministries **resigned in Oct-Nov 1939**.

ndebd008e9ca.s: Which Act is correctly associated with the introduction of dyarchy in the provinces, bicameralism at the Centre and direct elections?
ndebd008e9ca.x: These three features were introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919, also known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
ndebd008e9ca.tq: Recognize the characteristic three-feature combination of the 1919 Act.
xs: **Dyarchy in the provinces**, **bicameralism at the Centre** and **direct elections** came with the **Government of India Act, 1919** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **1935 Act** instead brought **provincial autonomy**, three lists and the **Instrument of Instructions**.
xa: The **1919** Act also gave a **Public Service Commission** and a **separate provincial budget**.
**1935** borrowings: **federal scheme**, **office of Governor**, **judiciary**, **emergency provisions**.
⚠ Do not confuse: **1919** = bicameralism and direct elections; **1935** = federal scheme.

n78d0832dbfe.s: Which party formed the ministry in the Madras Presidency after the 1937 elections?
n78d0832dbfe.x: The Congress formed the Madras ministry, while the Justice Party was almost wiped out and the People's Party lost all its seats.
xa: The ministry was formed on **14 July 1937** under **C. Rajagopalachari** (APHQ **2011**).
It ended **Justice Party** rule of **1920-37**.
The campaign was led by **Tanguturi Prakasam** and **Bulusu Sambamurthy**.

n1689815fd3c.s: The Congress ministry formed in Madras on 14 July 1937 was headed by:
n1689815fd3c.x: C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji) became Premier of Madras on 14 July 1937 (APHQ 2011). Prakasam was Revenue Minister, V.V. Giri Labour and Industries Minister, and Bulusu Sambamurthy the Speaker.
xs: The Madras Congress ministry of **14 July 1937** was headed by **C. Rajagopalachari** — so option **(3)** is correct (APHQ **2011**).
**Prakasam** was **Revenue Minister**, **V.V. Giri** handled **Labour and Industries**, **Bulusu Sambamurthy** was **Speaker**.
xa: **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** held **Local Self-Government**.
It ended **Justice Party** rule (**1920-37**).
Rajaji's Hindi policy → **Periyar's anti-Hindi agitation** → withdrawn.

n55abe8fdba7.s: 'Begar', abolished by the Congress ministries of 1937-39, was:
n55abe8fdba7.x: Begar was forced labour, not a salt tax; the Congress ministries abolished it.
xa: **Debt relief** was another agrarian measure.
Labour: **Industrial Disputes Act (1938)**.
Civil liberties: political prisoners released, **press freedom** restored.

nfaadbff7e52.s: The provision of the Government of India Act, 1935 that served as a model for the Directive Principles of State Policy was the:
nfaadbff7e52.x: The Instrument of Instructions under the Government of India Act, 1935 served as the model for the Directive Principles of State Policy.
xs: The **Instrument of Instructions** of the 1935 Act was the model for the **Directive Principles** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC **2023**).
The **Federal Court** and **separate provincial budget** are other borrowings, not the DPSP model.
xa: Other 1935 borrowings: **federal scheme**, **office of Governor**, **judiciary**, **PSCs**, **emergency provisions**.
From the **1919** Act: **bicameralism** and **direct elections** at the Centre, **separate provincial budget**.
The Act is called the **blueprint** of the Constitution.

n0bbb1257a51.s: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 accepted separate electorates along with:
o: Universal adult franchise and linguistic provinces
Complete independence and abolition of legislatures
Reserved seats only for depressed classes in joint electorates
Weightage and a communal veto based on a three-fourths rule
n0bbb1257a51.x: The Lucknow Pact accepted separate electorates, weightage and a communal veto requiring a three-fourths rule.
n0bbb1257a51.tq: Test the additional conditions attached to a familiar constitutional arrangement.
xs: The **Lucknow Pact (1916)** accepted separate electorates with **weightage** and a **communal veto** (**three-fourths rule**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Weightage** = more seats than the community's population share.
Reserved seats in **joint electorates** for depressed classes came later, with the **Poona Pact**.
xa: Separate electorates for **Muslims** began with the **Indian Councils Act 1909** (Morley-Minto).
**Minto** is called the "**Father of Communal Electorate**".
The **GoI Act 1919** extended them to **Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans**.

n3bc325674c5.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 gave Muslims what share of seats in the Federal Legislature?
n3bc325674c5.x: The 1935 Act gave Muslims 33% of the seats in the Federal Legislature, extending separate electorates further.
xa: The 1935 Act extended them to **depressed classes (SCs), women and labour**.
The **Communal Award 1932** extended them to depressed classes; the **Poona Pact** replaced that with reserved seats.
**1909**: separate electorates for **Muslims** + **weightage**.

n5502831a2e0.s: What was the principal change introduced by the Poona Pact in relation to the Communal Award?
o: The Muslim League was given a communal veto
Separate electorates for Muslims were abolished
Reserved seats in joint electorates replaced separate electorates for the depressed classes
Separate electorates were extended to all Europeans
n5502831a2e0.x: The Poona Pact replaced separate electorates for the depressed classes with reserved seats in joint electorates.
n5502831a2e0.tq: Compare the original constitutional arrangement with its replacement.
xs: The **Poona Pact** replaced the Award's separate electorates for the **depressed classes** with **reserved seats in joint electorates** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Communal Award 1932** had extended separate electorates to the **depressed classes**.
Muslims kept their separate electorates — they continued **till the Constituent Assembly**.
xa: The **GoI Act 1935** extended them further to **depressed classes (SCs), women and labour**.
**1919**: extended to **Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans**.
**1916 Lucknow Pact**: Congress accepted them, with **weightage**.

n6a4a07cd4bf.s: Which one of the following best describes the long-term political consequence of the Indian Councils Act, 1909?
o: It abolished communal representation in legislatures.
It legally institutionalised communalism and contributed to the growth of the Two-Nation Theory.
It established complete responsible government at the Centre.
It introduced universal adult franchise in British India.
n6a4a07cd4bf.x: The 1909 Act legally institutionalised communal representation, thereby strengthening communal politics and contributing to the emergence of the Two-Nation Theory.
n6a4a07cd4bf.tq: Identify the precise consequence rather than being distracted by extreme constitutional claims.
xs: The **1909** Act "**legally institutionalised communalism**" — the **seed of the Two-Nation Theory** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It gave **Muslims** separate electorates plus **weightage**; only Muslims voted for Muslim candidates.
It did not abolish communal representation — later Acts **extended** it.
xa: **Minto** = "**Father of Communal Electorate**".
The **Muslim League (1906)** came up in the run-up to 1909.
APPSC-G2 **2025**: "Which Act introduced the communal electorate?" = **Morley-Minto Reforms**.

nc1f95f21888.s: Which one of the following Acts first introduced separate (communal) electorates for Muslims in British India?
nc1f95f21888.x: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) introduced separate electorates for Muslims, with weightage; Minto is called the Father of Communal Electorate. The 1892 Act did not create them; the 1919 Act extended them to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans; the 1935 Act extended them further to depressed classes, women and labour.
xs: The **Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms)** first gave **Muslims** separate electorates — so option **(2)** is correct.
It added **weightage**; **Minto** is called the **"Father of Communal Electorate"**.
The **1919** Act **extended** them to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans; the **1935** Act to **depressed classes, women and labour**.
xa: APPSC-G2 **2025** asked exactly this: answer **Morley-Minto Reforms**.
The **Shimla Deputation** (**1906**) under the **Aga Khan** demanded separate electorates.
The **Lucknow Pact 1916**: Congress accepted them.

n8144a67e4c6.s: Who among the following was associated with the early advocacy of keeping Muslims away from the Indian National Congress in 1887?
n8144a67e4c6.x: Sayyid Ahmad Khan, along with Raja Shiv Prasad of Bhinga, promoted an anti-Congress front in 1887.
n8144a67e4c6.tq: Link the early stage of an idea with its initial advocate.
xs: In **1887**, **Sayyid Ahmad Khan** with **Raja Shiv Prasad of Bhinga** was propped up as an **anti-Congress front** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Dufferin** used him to keep **Muslims out of Congress**.
**Iqbal** (**1930**) and **Rahmat Ali** (**1933**) came much later; **Ambedkar** wrote on Pakistan.
xa: **1906**: **Shimla Deputation** (Aga Khan) → separate electorates demanded; **League** founded.
**1930**: **Iqbal's Allahabad address** — consolidated Muslim state in the North-West.
**1940**: **Lahore Resolution** — demand formalised by **Jinnah**.

n3fd44b02d22.s: The 1930 Allahabad address of Muhammad Iqbal is associated with the proposal for:
o: Immediate withdrawal of the British from India
A federation of all princely states
A consolidated Muslim state in north-western India
n3fd44b02d22.x: In his 1930 Allahabad address, Iqbal advocated a consolidated Muslim state in the north-western region.

xs: **Iqbal's 1930 Allahabad address** (League session) proposed a **consolidated Muslim state in the North-West** — so option **(4)** is correct.

xa: **1933**: **Chaudhry Rahmat Ali** coined **"PAKISTAN"** in **"Now or Never"**.
**1940**: **Lahore Resolution**, adopted **23 March 1940**.
**1928-29**: Nehru Report vs Jinnah's **14 Points** — "parting of the ways".

n2d22617c1d3.s: The Shimla Deputation of 1906 is associated with which of the following developments?
o: Acceptance of complete independence by the Congress
Demand for separate electorates and the founding of the Muslim League
Replacement of reserved seats by joint electorates
n2d22617c1d3.x: The 1906 Shimla Deputation, led by Aga Khan, demanded separate electorates, and the Muslim League was founded in the same year.
n2d22617c1d3.tq: Connect a deputation with its immediate constitutional and organisational consequences.
xs: The **Shimla Deputation (1906)**, led by the **Aga Khan**, **demanded separate electorates**, and the **League was founded** the same year — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Lahore Resolution** came in **1940**; reserved seats in joint electorates came via the **Poona Pact**.
xa: The demand was met by the **Indian Councils Act 1909**.
The **Muslim League (1906)** came up in the run-up to 1909.
**1887**: **Sayyid Ahmad Khan** used as an anti-Congress front.

n851cde3668f.x: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the word 'Pakistan' in 1933.

n41f606c2271.s: The Muslim League observed 'Deliverance Day' on 22 December 1939 to celebrate:
o: The adoption of the Lahore Resolution
The resignation of the Congress provincial ministries
The announcement of the Communal Award
The publication of the Pirpur Report
n41f606c2271.x: Deliverance Day ('Day of Deliverance and Thanksgiving'), 22 December 1939, celebrated the resignation of the Congress ministries. The Lahore Resolution came in March 1940, the Communal Award in 1932 and the Pirpur Report in 1938.
