**Kochrab Ashram**, Ahmedabad: **1915**; Sabarmati: **1917**; Sevagram: **1936**.
**Songs from Prison** were made in **Yerwada** jail.

n6aaa220f6bd.s: Gandhi returned his Kaisar-i-Hind gold medal in:
n6aaa220f6bd.x: Gandhi returned the medal (awarded in 1915 for his South African ambulance work) in 1920 during the Khilafat and Non-Cooperation campaign.
xa: Gandhi returned to India on **9 January 1915** — now **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas**.
**Mahatma** — **Rabindranath Tagore**; **Father of the Nation** — **Subhas Chandra Bose**.
**Half-naked fakir** — **Winston Churchill**, **1931**.

n323e99fa070.s: Who called Gandhi a 'half-naked fakir' in 1931?
n323e99fa070.x: Winston Churchill, not Lord Irwin, called Gandhi a 'half-naked fakir' in 1931.
xa: APPSC **2019** key accepts "Mahatma given in **1914**".
⚠ Mahatma = **Tagore**; Father of the Nation = **Bose**; half-naked fakir = **Churchill**.
The **Kaisar-i-Hind** medal (**1915**) came from the **British Government**.

n4043c2b293c.s: Which one of the following correctly associates the early Indian satyagrahas with their principal issues?
n4043c2b293c.x: Champaran concerned indigo, Ahmedabad concerned mill wages, and Kheda concerned remission of land revenue.
n4043c2b293c.tq: Start from the sure issue–movement pair and eliminate swapped associations.
xs: **Champaran — indigo**; **Ahmedabad — mill wages**; **Kheda — revenue remission** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Champaran 1917** = first **civil disobedience**; **Ahmedabad 1918** = first **hunger strike**; **Kheda 1918** = first **non-cooperation**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **C – A – K** = civil disobedience – hunger strike – non-cooperation.
First satyagraha overall = **Transvaal 1906**.
First in India = **Champaran 1917**.

ndd965c680e2.s: The journals Indian Opinion, Navajivan and Harijan are associated with:
ndd965c680e2.x: Indian Opinion, Navajivan and Harijan are associated with Gandhi's journalistic work.
xa: **Indian Opinion** had **English and Gujarati** editions.
**Navajivan** serialised his autobiography.
**Young India** was an **English weekly**.
ndd965c680e2.fixed: stem 'listed in this context' is odd; APPSC 2019 asks it plainly

n0960ad27292.s: In Gandhian thought, the relationship between truth and non-violence is that
o: truth is the end and non-violence is the means
non-violence is needed only when truth cannot be established
truth is the means and non-violence is the end
n0960ad27292.x: Gandhi regarded truth as the ultimate end and non-violence as the means for realising it.
xs: In Gandhian thought **truth is the end** and **non-violence is the means** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Gandhi: "**Means are after all everything**. As the means so the end" — means-ends purity.
xa: "My religion is based on **truth and non-violence**. Truth is my God."
"**Wrong means never take us to right ends**" (UPPSC **2015**).
Satyagraha = **satya (truth) + agraha (insistence)**.

n4d53bde9af3.s: When the only alternatives were cowardice and violence, Gandhi said he would prefer:
n4d53bde9af3.x: Gandhi preferred violence to cowardice when those were the only alternatives; for him ahimsa was a quality of the strong, not of the weak.
xa: He contrasted non-violence of the **brave** with that of the **weak**.
"Non-violence is not a **garment** to be put on and off at will."
"**Poverty is the worst form of violence**" (UPPSC **2015**: persistence of poverty).

n47fea7e2d25.s: The early English rendering of 'Satyagraha' was:
n47fea7e2d25.x: Satyagraha, born in 1906 in the Transvaal, was early rendered in English as 'passive resistance'.
xa: Satyagraha = **satya + agraha** (insistence on truth).
Rules for satyagrahis: no **anger or hatred**, no retaliation, never **insult** the opponent.
⚠ It is not "weak" passive resistance — ahimsa belongs to the **strong**.

nd2006bf5157.s: Gandhi's concept of Swaraj is wider than political independence because it includes
o: self-rule, self-control and the capacity of the masses to govern themselves without coercion
freedom only from foreign economic competition
centralised rule by a single national authority
rule by a hereditary political class
nd2006bf5157.x: For Gandhi, Swaraj meant not merely political freedom but also self-rule, self-control and the ability of people to govern themselves without coercion.
nd2006bf5157.tq: Distinguish the broad conceptual meaning from the narrow constitutional meaning.
xs: Swaraj meant **self-rule, self-control** and the capacity of masses to **govern themselves without coercion** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was not only political freedom, and it opposed centralisation in favour of **decentralisation**.
xa: Swaraj has **eight interrelated principles**, incl. **swadeshi** and **education for all**.
Real Swaraj = capacity to **resist authority when abused**.
Gandhian individualism: **self-rule before State rule**.

ncbc3016a5d9.s: According to Gandhi, the nature of the end is determined by the nature of the:
ncbc3016a5d9.x: Gandhi held that means are everything and that the end reflects the means used to attain it.
xa: **Means-ends purity** is a Gandhian core value.
"What is **morally wrong** can never be **politically right**".
Truth is the **end**, non-violence the **means**.

n32b797de5ec.s: Gandhi held that politics bereft of religion is a ____.
n32b797de5ec.x: Gandhi said politics bereft of religion (meaning morality based on truth and non-violence) is a death-trap.
xa: "What is **morally wrong** can never be **politically right**".
Real Swaraj = **capacity of all to resist authority when abused**.
He saw the **State** as **violence in concentrated form**.

n57f825bf38c.s: Gandhi's Talisman asks a person, before taking a step, to recall the face of:
n57f825bf38c.x: Gandhi's Talisman requires one to consider the poorest and weakest person before taking a step.
xa: "**Means are after all everything**."
Ahimsa is in **thought, word and deed**.
**Poverty** = the worst form of violence.

nd34b288fa21.s: The Rowlatt Satyagraha of 1919 is significant as Gandhi's first:
nd34b288fa21.x: The Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919) was Gandhi's first all-India mass movement; Champaran was his first civil disobedience, Ahmedabad his first hunger strike and Kheda his first non-cooperation.
xa: Some notes call the **NCM (1920)** the "first nationwide mass movement".
⚠ Keep "first mass movement by Gandhi" = **Champaran** apart from "first all-India" = **Rowlatt/NCM**.
**Champaran 1917** = first **civil disobedience**; **Kheda 1918** = first **non-cooperation**.
nd34b288fa21.fixed: 'in this classification' refers to app-internal table; reworded

n70e0b8be5c1.s: Which one of the following is inconsistent with the rules prescribed for a Satyagrahi?
o: Insulting the opponent to expose injustice
n70e0b8be5c1.x: A Satyagrahi must never insult the opponent. The rules require non-retaliation, submission to arrest and observance of jail discipline.
n70e0b8be5c1.tq: Find the option that directly violates a stated rule of conduct.
xs: **Insulting the opponent** breaks the satyagrahi's rules — so option **(3)** is the answer.
A satyagrahi must **never insult** the opponent and must have no **anger or hatred**.
He must bear assaults **without retaliation**, **submit to arrest** and follow **jail rules** — options 1, 2, 4 are rules.
xa: Ahimsa must be in **thought, word and deed**.
Satyagraha = **soul force** in place of physical force.
Gandhi's **Talisman**: recall the face of the **poorest and weakest**.

nb99ad4303bd.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the interrelated principles included in Gandhi's concept of Swaraj?
nb99ad4303bd.x: Swadeshi, ahimsa, Satyagraha, decentralisation and education for all are included among the interrelated principles of Swaraj. Class dictatorship is not a Gandhian principle.
nb99ad4303bd.tq: Identify the ideological outsider in a list of principles.
xs: **Class dictatorship** is not a Swaraj principle — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Swaraj's **eight interrelated principles** include **swadeshi**, **ahimsa**, **satyagraha**, **decentralisation**, **education for all**.
xa: **Decentralisation**: power close to the people; local communities decide.
Gandhi's method is **change of heart**, not **class struggle**.
The unit of Gandhian individualism is the **individual and his conscience**.

n1260056cd85.s: 'Trusteeship' as the basis of property relations is a concept of:
n1260056cd85.x: Trusteeship is Gandhian; Marxism seeks the abolition of private property.
xa: Marxist method: **class struggle**, **revolution**.
Gandhism's basis: **moral/spiritual**.
They share only the **stateless end**; they differ on **means**.

n195d5847b6f.s: Gandhi is called a philosophical anarchist because of his ideal of:
n195d5847b6f.x: His ideal of 'enlightened anarchy' and his view of the State as violence in concentrated form make Gandhi a philosophical anarchist.
xa: Final goal: a **stateless society**, shared with Marxism.
**Decentralisation**: power close to the people.
Gandhian method: **non-violence**, **change of heart**.

n04cad2a3e5b.s: The term 'Sarvodaya' signifies which of the following?
o: Welfare or uplift of all, including the last person
Exclusive economic development of rural areas
n04cad2a3e5b.x: Sarvodaya means the welfare, uplift or progress of all, with attention reaching the last person.
n04cad2a3e5b.tq: Choose the precise meaning rather than a related but narrower social idea.
xs: **Sarvodaya** means the **welfare/uplift of all**, "**progress for all**", reaching the **last person** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The term was used by **M.K. Gandhi** (APPSC **2019**), from his paraphrase of **Ruskin's Unto This Last**.
xa: **Sarvodaya Day**: **30 January** (Martyrs' Day).
**Vinoba Bhave** made Sarvodaya the cornerstone of his work → **Bhoodan**.
**JP's Sarvodaya Plan**: **1950**.

n5f3fb356d80.s: Swadeshi and khadi were intended, among other things, to:
n5f3fb356d80.x: Swadeshi and khadi promoted rural employment, self-reliance and a bridge between towns and villages. Gandhi popularised the charkha and khadi for these purposes.
n5f3fb356d80.tq: Infer the practical social and economic objective from the policy pair.
xs: **Swadeshi and khadi** aimed at **rural employment** and **self-reliance** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They also formed a **bridge between town and village**.
**Gandhi** popularised the **charkha and khadi**.
xa: **All India Spinners' Association**: **1925**.
**Ponduru** (Srikakulam) — the **finest khadi** in India.
**Prakasam's** Khadi Development Centre at **Guravareddypalem** got **Rs 10,000** from the AISA.

n26d1a0511fc.s: Who wrote *Unto This Last*, which Mahatma Gandhi paraphrased into Gujarati as *Sarvodaya* in 1908?
n26d1a0511fc.x: *Unto This Last* was written by John Ruskin. Gandhi's Gujarati paraphrase was titled *Sarvodaya* and influenced his ideas on labour and social welfare.
n26d1a0511fc.tq: Use the author–work association and distinguish it from nearby literary distractors.
xs: **Unto This Last** was written by **John Ruskin**; Gandhi paraphrased it into Gujarati as **"Sarvodaya"** (**1908**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Trap: the Sarvodaya paraphrase = **Ruskin**, not **Tolstoy** or **Carlyle** (APPSC G1 **2022**).
**Thomas Carlyle** (Heroes and Hero Worship) was the **distractor** in APPSC **2022**; **Tolstoy** wrote **The Kingdom of God is Within You**.
xa: Unto This Last inspired **dignity of labour** + **Sarvodaya** and was a source of **bread labour**.
**Sarvodaya** = **welfare/uplift of all**, reaching the **last person**.
**Sarvodaya Day**: **30 January** (**Martyrs' Day**).

nd3b376bee99.s: Which one of the following correctly represents Gandhi’s stated influence from The Kingdom of God is Within You?
o: The right to break unjust laws
nd3b376bee99.x: Gandhi took the ideas of love and non-violence from Leo Tolstoy’s The Kingdom of God is Within You.
nd3b376bee99.tq: Distinguish closely related influences by matching each text with its specific idea.
xs: **Tolstoy's The Kingdom of God is Within You** influenced Gandhi on **love and non-violence** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Dignity of labour and Sarvodaya** came from **Ruskin's Unto This Last**.
Gandhi made **no translation** of Tolstoy's book.
xa: **Bread labour**: the term came via **Tolstoy** from **T.M. Bondaref**.
Gandhi's paraphrase "**Sarvodaya**" was of **Ruskin**, not Tolstoy.
**Carlyle's Heroes and Hero Worship** was an APPSC **2022** distractor.

n598c440374f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Gandhian trusteeship?
o: It sought class harmony rather than class struggle.
It was applied only to zamindars and not to capitalists.
Its roots lay in the Gita's idea of non-possession and the English law of trusts.
It was applied to mill owners such as those of Ahmedabad.
n598c440374f.x: Trusteeship was applied to both capitalists and zamindars (e.g. the Ahmedabad mill owners), not only to zamindars.
xa: The 1918 strike involved a **fast** and a **35%** wage rise.
**Textile Labour Association 1920**: based on **arbitration** + non-violence.
Wealthy are **not expropriated** as in Marxism.

nde18ef571c0.s: Which organisations were established in 1925 and 1934 respectively?
o: All India Village Industries Association and All India Spinners' Association
All India Spinners' Association and All India Village Industries Association
Textile Labour Association and All India Spinners' Association
All India Spinners' Association and Constructive Programme Committee
nde18ef571c0.x: The All India Spinners' Association was established in 1925, while the All India Village Industries Association was established in 1934.
nde18ef571c0.tq: Use the two dates to place the similarly named organisations in the correct order.
xs: **1925** = **All India Spinners' Association**; **1934** = **All India Village Industries Association** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option 1 reverses the two; the **TLA** dates from **1920**.
xa: The AISA gave **Rs 10,000** to **Prakasam's** centre at **Guravareddypalem**.
**Constructive Programme** booklet: **1941**.
Gandhian priority: **village/cottage industries** over heavy industry.

n2711e1fea24.s: Vinoba Bhave's Bhoodan movement began in 1951 at:
n2711e1fea24.x: Bhoodan began at Pochampalli (now in Telangana) in 1951.
xa: Pochampalli is now in **Telangana**.
Sarvodaya = welfare of all, reaching the **last person**.

n26d158d04ed.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's criticism of the Gandhian village ideal was based mainly on his view that the village was:
o: A seat of caste domination and localism
A unit without any social organisation
n26d158d04ed.x: Ambedkar viewed the village as a seat of caste domination and described it as a sink of localism, ignorance and communalism. He preferred the individual as the basic unit.
n26d158d04ed.tq: Identify the precise basis of the disagreement between two political thinkers.
xs: **Ambedkar** saw the village as a **seat of caste domination** and "**a sink of localism**, a den of ignorance and communalism" — so option **(2)** is correct.
He preferred the **individual** as the unit.
xa: The compromise: **Article 40** (**DPSP**) — organise **village panchayats**.
Article 40 is **non-justiciable**.
Gandhian thought later shaped the **73rd Amendment's** panchayat idea.

n30ab0b85147.s: Who wrote *Sarvodaya Ganam* and translated Gandhi's autobiography into Telugu?
n30ab0b85147.x: Tummala Sitaramamurthy wrote *Sarvodaya Ganam*, inspired by Vinoba, and translated Gandhi's autobiography into Telugu.
n30ab0b85147.tq: Use the author–work–language combination to identify the Andhra cultural association.
xs: **Tummala Sitaramamurthy** wrote **Sarvodaya Ganam** and translated Gandhi's **autobiography** into **Telugu** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Sarvodaya Ganam** was inspired by **Vinoba**.
**Vinoba Bhave** led **Bhoodan**; **J.P. Narayan** gave the **Sarvodaya Plan (1950)**.
xa: Bhoodan began at **Pochampalli** (**1951**).
**Ponduru** (Srikakulam) — **finest khadi**.
**Prakasam's** Khadi Development Centre — **Guravareddypalem** (Guntur).

n4b2c366fbbd.s: Which of the following represents Gandhi's route for the uplift of communities subjected to untouchability?
o: Separate electorates, political boycott and armed resistance
Exclusive reliance on litigation and legislative vetoes
Moral persuasion, temple entry, funds, schools and hostels, and constructive work
Economic isolation of orthodox Hindu groups
n4b2c366fbbd.x: Gandhi's approach combined moral persuasion, temple entry, funds, schools and hostels, and constructive work.
n4b2c366fbbd.tq: Identify the complete constructive programme rather than a single method.
xs: Gandhi's route: **moral persuasion**, **temple entry**, **funds**, **schools + hostels**, **constructive work** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He sought reform **from within** Hindu society, not through separate electorates or boycott.
xa: He called untouchability "**a blot on Hinduism**".
He founded the **Harijan Sevak Sangh** in **1932**.
The **Harijan tour** (**November 1933 - July 1934**) collected funds for the Sangh.

n87fd74719a9.s: What was Gandhi's stand on the remarriage of child widows?
o: He left it to caste panchayats
n87fd74719a9.x: Gandhi opposed purdah, child marriage and dowry but supported the remarriage of child widows.
xa: Andhra women formed **Desasevikalu**, a women's wing.
Andhra women gave **jewellery** for the **Tilak Fund**.
**Durgabai** met Gandhi at **Kakinada** (**1921**) and raised **Rs 5,000**.

o: Separation of religion from all public prayer
The superiority of one religion over all others
Acceptance of only reformist Hindu sects
n8c7867649d8.x: Sarva dharma samabhava means equal respect for all religions. Gandhi's ashram prayers drew upon several faiths.
n8c7867649d8.tq: Test the exact meaning of the Sanskrit expression.
xs: **Sarva dharma samabhava** = **equal respect for all religions** — so option **(4)** is correct.
His **ashram prayers** drew on **many faiths**.
xa: **Hindu-Muslim unity** was the **bedrock of nationalism** for Gandhi.
He backed the **Khilafat** movement.
He fasted during riots at **Calcutta and Noakhali** (**1946-47**).

nab0e8a128b9.s: Gandhi's fasts during the communal riots of 1946-47 were held at Calcutta and:
nab0e8a128b9.x: His riot-time fasts of 1946-47 were at Calcutta and Noakhali, not Vaikom or Guruvayur.
xa: **Sarva dharma samabhava**: equal respect for all religions.
His ashram prayers drew on **many faiths**.
Untouchability = "**a blot on Hinduism**".

n86b58d5f94e.s: Which of the following was NOT among the activities associated with the Harijan Sevak Sangh?
o: Introducing separate electorates for the Depressed Classes
Promoting entry into wells and temples
n86b58d5f94e.x: The Sangh worked for access to wells, schools and temples, and promoted schools, hostels, cooperatives, inter-dining and inter-caste marriage. Separate electorates were a political demand associated with the Poona Pact debate, not its activity.
n86b58d5f94e.tq: Find the option belonging to the political debate rather than the organisation's constructive work.
xs: **Introducing separate electorates** was not a Sangh activity — so option **(2)** is the answer.
The Sangh worked for entry to **wells, schools, temples**, ran **schools, hostels, cooperatives**, and promoted **inter-dining** and **inter-caste marriage**.
It was founded **after** the **Poona Pact**, which settled the depressed-class electorate question.
xa: Founder: **Gandhi**, **1932**; president **G.D. Birla**, secretary **Thakkar Bapa**.
AP branches: **Hyderabad and Vijayawada (1932)**.
**Bhagya Reddy Varma** called it **paternalistic** and weak on **civil rights**.

n130456bfa55.s: Who was the first president of the Harijan Sevak Sangh (1932)?
n130456bfa55.x: G.D. Birla was its first president and Amritlal Thakkar (Thakkar Bapa) its secretary; Gandhi founded it after the Poona Pact.
xa: Former name: **All India Anti-Untouchability League**.
Date: **September 1932**, while Gandhi was **in prison**; some notes give **30 October 1932, Mumbai**.
Asked in UPPSC **2014**, **2017** and BPSC **2022**.

o: A matter for the State alone
n8631d951a06.x: Gandhi called untouchability 'a blot on Hinduism' and sought reform from within Hindu society.
xa: **Ambedkar** and Dalit leaders rejected "**Harijan**" and caste-Hindu **paternalism**.
Gandhi's route: **moral persuasion**, **temple entry**, **schools + hostels**, **constructive work**.
Untouchability was abolished by **Article 17**.

nc8cca7b5b55.s: In Andhra, the Desasevikalu functioned as a:
nc8cca7b5b55.x: Desasevikalu was a women's wing; Durgabai met Gandhi at Kakinada in 1921 and Andhra women donated jewellery to the Tilak Fund.
xa: **Kolla Tayaramma** — Harijan schools + hostels, **Tenali**.
**Alladi Annapurna Devi** — Harijan schools + hostels, **Nellore**.
Gandhi drew women into **picketing liquor shops** and **making salt**.

ne7a5da2c73e.s: Which of the following correctly describes Gandhi's Harijan tour?
o: November 1933 to July 1934, covering about 20,000 km from Wardha Ashram
August 1934 to March 1935, covering about 10,000 km from Sabarmati
January 1933 to December 1933, covering about 5,000 km from Poona
November 1932 to July 1933, covering about 20,000 km from Mumbai
ne7a5da2c73e.x: Gandhi's Harijan tour ran from November 1933 to July 1934, covered about 20,000 km, began from the Wardha Ashram and collected funds for the Harijan Sevak Sangh. Orthodox groups disrupted some meetings.
ne7a5da2c73e.tq: Combine the duration, distance, starting point and purpose instead of relying on a single date.
xs: The **Harijan tour** ran **November 1933 - July 1934**, about **20,000 km**, from the **Wardha** ashram — so option **(1)** is correct.
It collected funds for the **Harijan Sevak Sangh**; **orthodox groups** disrupted meetings.
xa: The **Harijan weekly** began in **1933**, first issue from **Poona**.
In Andhra he toured to **collect funds** and campaign **against untouchability**.
He also visited **Machilipatnam** for **Swaraj Nidhi**.

nf613a3432ae.s: Gandhi's weekly 'Harijan' was started in which year, with its first issue brought out from which place?
nf613a3432ae.x: Harijan was started in 1933 (January 1933 in some sources), with the first issue from Poona. 1919 is when Gandhi began editing Young India; 1903 at Durban is Indian Opinion; 1936 is the founding of Sevagram at Wardha.
xs: The **Harijan** weekly started in **1933**, first issue from **Poona** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Some notes give **January 1933**.
xa: The name "Harijan" (children of God) came from **Narsi Mehta**.
The **Harijan tour** followed from **November 1933**.
The **Harijan Sevak Sangh** dates from **1932**.

n84c18638d65.s: Nai Talim, or Basic Education, primarily aimed at:
o: Replacing manual work with purely literary education
Providing higher education exclusively in English
Training students only for government employment
Making villages self-sufficient through vocational and craft-centred education
n84c18638d65.x: Gandhi's Basic Education was vocational and craft-centred, sought to make villages self-sufficient and aimed to dignify manual labour.
n84c18638d65.tq: Identify the educational philosophy from its practical social objective.
xs: **Nai Talim** was **vocational**, **craft-centred** education to make **villages self-sufficient** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It aimed to **dignify manual labour**, not replace it with literary education.
xa: Propounded by **Gandhi** (APPSC **2019**).
Adopted at the **Wardha Educational Conference, 1937**; drawn up by the **Zakir Hussain Committee**.
**Free + compulsory** education for **7 years** (age **7-14**), **mother tongue** medium.

nf3652532350.s: Which term used by Gandhi was rejected by Ambedkar and Dalit leaders, who criticised caste-Hindu paternalism?
nf3652532350.x: Ambedkar and Dalit leaders rejected the term 'Harijan' and criticised what they saw as caste-Hindu paternalism.
xa: "Harijan" came from **Narsi Mehta**.
Gandhi sought reform **from within** Hindu society.
The **Harijan Sevak Sangh** was founded in **1932** after the **Poona Pact**.

n6840b7ffb93.s: Which event is regarded as the precursor to the Champaran indigo movement?
n6840b7ffb93.x: The Bengal Indigo Revolt of 1859 preceded and served as an important precursor to the later indigo-related mobilisation in Champaran.
n6840b7ffb93.tq: Identify the earlier related movement rather than the later Gandhian campaign.
xs: The **Bengal Indigo Revolt of 1859** is the precursor of Champaran — option **(1)**.
It was a Bengal peasant refusal to grow indigo; Champaran came nearly **60 years** later.
xa: The "**Indigo blue**" story (Jan **2026**) called Champaran Gandhi's "**launch pad**" for a new anti-colonial method.
Champaran (**1917**) was the **first satyagraha in India**.
⚠ Trap: dating Champaran to **1915** is wrong; the correct year is **1917**.

n433e4509567.s: The Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918 abolished:
n433e4509567.x: Based on the Enquiry Committee's recommendations, the Act abolished Tinkathia and secured a 25 per cent refund of illegal exactions.
xa: Committee chair: **F.G. Sly**; Gandhi was a member for the **ryots**.
**Tinkathia**: indigo on **3/20th** of land for **European planters**.
Appointed by the **Bihar and Orissa government** in **1917**.

ne60a7b6d8fb.s: In the Ahmedabad Mill Strike, the workers’ demand and the mill owners’ offer were, respectively:
o: 20 per cent wage increase and 35 per cent increase
50 per cent wage increase and 20 per cent increase
35 per cent wage increase and 50 per cent increase
50 per cent wage increase and complete withdrawal of wages
ne60a7b6d8fb.x: The workers demanded a 50 per cent wage increase because of wartime inflation, while the mill owners offered only 20 per cent.
ne60a7b6d8fb.tq: Match the two competing numerical demands without reversing them.
xs: Workers demanded a **50 per cent wage increase**; owners offered a **20 per cent increase** — option **(2)**.
The demand arose from **wartime inflation** after owners withdrew the **"plague bonus"**.
**35%** was Gandhi's advice and the tribunal's award, not the owners' offer.
xa: Gandhi undertook his **first hunger strike in India** here → **tribunal awarded 35%**.
The strike was in **Feb-Mar 1918**, Gujarat.
⚠ Trap: **Anusuya Sarabhai** backed the workers; her brother **Ambalal Sarabhai** led the owners.

nd03f6ecf292.s: The immediate agrarian cause of the Kheda Satyagraha was:
o: Demand for a 50 per cent increase in industrial wages
Crop failure due to drought or famine and refusal of revenue remission
nd03f6ecf292.x: The Kheda peasants suffered crop failure caused by drought or famine and sought remission or suspension of land revenue, which the government initially refused.
nd03f6ecf292.tq: Separate agrarian grievances from industrial labour disputes.
xs: Kheda's cause was **crop failure** (drought/famine) and refusal of **revenue remission** — option **(4)**.
The **plague bonus** and **50%** wage demand belong to the **Ahmedabad Mill Strike**; compulsory indigo to **Champaran**.
xa: Peasants refused to pay despite threats of **land confiscation**.
Settlement: revenue **recovered only from those able to pay** (APPSC **2023** key); confiscated property returned.
**Vallabhbhai Patel** was field commander; Kheda = **first non-cooperation**.

n92bc965004e.s: The Kheda Satyagraha was called off after the government agreed to:
o: Abolish the Tinkathia system throughout Gujarat
Collect revenue only from those able to pay, suspend it for poor peasants and return confiscated property
Appoint Gandhi as the sole member of a revenue commission
Grant a 50 per cent wage increase to agricultural labourers
n92bc965004e.x: The settlement provided that revenue would be collected only from those able to pay, revenue would be suspended for poor peasants, and confiscated property would be returned.
n92bc965004e.tq: Distinguish the settlement terms from the original grievance.
xs: Kheda was called off when revenue was to be **recovered only from those able to pay**, suspended for poor peasants, and **confiscated property returned** — option **(2)**.
Abolition of **Tinkathia** was the Champaran result (**1918** Act), not Gujarat.
The **50%** wage figure was the Ahmedabad workers' demand.
xa: This settlement is the APPSC **2023** key.
Cause: **crop failure** and refusal of **remission of land revenue**.
Kheda began the **Gandhi-Patel alliance**.

nafcbd19283b.s: Who provided field leadership to the Kheda Satyagraha of 1918?
nafcbd19283b.x: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel gave field leadership as Kheda peasants refused to pay land revenue despite threats of confiscation.
xa: **Mohanlal Pandya** was co-leader at Kheda.
Kheda is called the **first non-cooperation**.
Viceroy at the time: **Lord Chelmsford (1916-21)**.

n7f892b24bd9.s: Which of the following took place first?
n7f892b24bd9.x: Champaran (1917) came first, followed by the Ahmedabad Mill Strike (Feb-Mar 1918), Kheda (1918) and the Rowlatt Satyagraha (April 1919).
xa: Next in sequence: **Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22)**, then **Civil Disobedience (Dandi, 1930)**.
Gandhi returned to India in **1915**.

n48bd592d27f.s: The year of Mahatma Gandhi’s Champaran pro-ryot movement was
n48bd592d27f.x: The Champaran pro-ryot movement took place in 1917. The year 1915 is an incorrect attribution sometimes made in secondary material.
n48bd592d27f.tq: Use the confusable-year trap by distinguishing the correct date from a nearby but incorrect year.
xs: Champaran was in **1917** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Dating it to **1915** is WRONG, though some notes say so; 1915 is Gandhi's return to India.
**1918** is the year of Ahmedabad and Kheda.
xa: Champaran = **first satyagraha in India**, in **Bihar**.
Gandhi met **Rajkumar Shukla** at the **Lucknow Congress, 1916**.
Result: **Champaran Agrarian Act (1918)**.

nindian-history-95-10.s: Which movement demanded the immediate end of British rule?
nindian-history-95-10.x: The Quit India Movement demanded the immediate end of British rule; Non-Cooperation was non-violent non-cooperation.
n: Non-Cooperation Movement promoted non-violent non-cooperation with the colonial government. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
Quit India Movement aimed at the immediate end of British rule. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
Swadeshi Movement promoted the boycott of foreign goods. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
Swadeshi Movement promoted indigenous goods. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #95 · pp 178-179]
xa: NCM was adopted at the **Calcutta Congress**.
**Civil Disobedience** (**1930**) went from **Sabarmati** to **Dandi**.
Quit India's key organisation: the **INC**, at **Bombay**.

nindian-history-132-11.s: In which year did the Champaran Satyagraha take place in Bihar?
nindian-history-132-11.x: Champaran was in 1917; Kheda and the Ahmedabad Mill Strike followed in 1918.
n: Champaran Satyagraha was started at Champaran, Bihar, in 1917. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
Kheda Satyagraha was started at Kheda, Gujarat, in 1918. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
Ahmedabad Mill Strike was started at Ahmedabad in 1918. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
The Non-Cooperation Movement was started at the Calcutta Congress in 1920. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
xa: ⚠ **C – A – K** = civil disobedience – hunger strike – non-cooperation.
Kheda: **Gandhi** and **Sardar Patel**.
Rowlatt Satyagraha followed on **6 April 1919**.

nindian-history-132-17.s: Where was the 'Do or Die' call of the Quit India Movement given in 1942?
nindian-history-132-17.x: The Quit India Movement began with the 'Do or Die' call at Bombay in 1942.
n: Annie Besant and Bal Gangadhar Tilak founded the Home Rule Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
Gandhi and Sardar Patel were key personalities in Kheda Satyagraha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
Mahatma Gandhi and the Indian National Congress were key personalities or organisations in the Non-Cooperation Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
The Indian National Congress was the key organisation in the Quit India Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #132 · pp 235-236]
xa: Patel was Kheda's **field commander** — start of the **Gandhi-Patel alliance**.
**Mohanlal Pandya** was Kheda's co-leader.
Quit India demanded the **immediate end** of British rule.

nindian-history-100-4.s: Under the Tinkathia system in Champaran, peasants were forced to grow indigo on what portion of their land?
nindian-history-100-4.x: The Tinkathia system forced peasants to grow indigo on 3/20 of their land.
n: The Champaran Satyagraha was associated with indigo cultivation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #100 · pp 185-188]
The Tinkathia system was associated with indigo cultivation in Champaran. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #100 · pp 185-188]
xa: Result: **25% refund**; Champaran was the **first civil disobedience**.
**Teen Kathiya** = **three-twentieths** of land.
⚠ **C – A – K** = civil disobedience – hunger strike – non-cooperation.

nindian-history-100-26.s: Gandhi first used a hunger strike as a weapon during the:
nindian-history-100-26.x: Gandhi's fast at Ahmedabad in 1918, during the mill workers' dispute, was his first hunger strike used as a weapon.
n: Gandhi used a fast unto death in Ahmedabad in 1918. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #100 · pp 185-188]
The Ahmedabad fast was Gandhi’s first hunger strike used as a weapon. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #100 · pp 185-188]
xa: The strike **lasted 21 days**.
**Ambalal Sarabhai** and **Anasuya Behn** were important associates.
Kheda (**1918**) was the **first non-cooperation**.

nindian-history-100-28.s: The main condition behind the Kheda Satyagraha (1918) was:
nindian-history-100-28.x: Crop failure in Kheda in 1918 made revenue payment hard, so peasants demanded remission or suspension of land revenue.
n: The Kheda Satyagraha involved peasants affected by crop failure. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #100 · pp 185-188]
The Kheda Satyagraha demanded revenue remission or suspension. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #100 · pp 185-188]
xa: **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel** was the **field commander**.
Kheda was the **first non-cooperation**.
Champaran (**1917**) was the **first civil disobedience**.

nb5c50596a55.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Gandhi’s method during the Champaran Satyagraha?
o: He began an armed resistance against the European planters.
He accepted the order to leave the district and confined his work to petitions.
He called upon peasants to stop cultivating all food crops.
He defied the order to leave and, with his lawyers, recorded peasants’ complaints in the villages.
nb5c50596a55.x: Gandhi defied the official order to leave Champaran and toured villages with his lawyers to record complaints against forced indigo cultivation. This compelled the government to order an inquiry.
nb5c50596a55.tq: Apply the principle of non-violent civil disobedience to the historical situation.
xs: Gandhi **defied the order to leave the district** and, with lawyers, **recorded peasants' complaints** in villages — option **(4)**.
This forced a government (**official**) **inquiry** — so he neither accepted the order nor limited himself to petitions.
Champaran was a **non-violent** satyagraha, not armed resistance, and was about indigo, not food crops.
xa: The defiance took place at **Motihari**.
His lawyers included **Rajendra Prasad**, **Brajkishore Prasad** and **Anugrah Narayan Sinha**.
The inquiry led to the **Champaran Agrarian Committee** under **F.G. Sly**, with Gandhi as a member.

n4792af99387.s: Who chaired the Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee (1917), on which Gandhi represented the ryots?
n4792af99387.x: F.G. Sly chaired the committee, appointed by the Bihar and Orissa government.
xa: Result: **Champaran Agrarian Act (1918)**, which **abolished the Tinkathia system**.
Refund of **25%** of illegal exactions.
It was set up after Gandhi's village inquiry with his lawyers.

n77b240d1184.s: The Champaran Satyagraha was directed mainly against:
o: Forced indigo cultivation and illegal exactions by European planters
n77b240d1184.x: European planters compelled peasants to grow indigo and, when indigo became unprofitable, demanded illegal dues and enhanced rents; forest tax was not the issue.
xa: Later exactions: **Sharahbeshi** (enhanced rent) and **Tawan** (lump-sum compensation).
Outcome: **Champaran Agrarian Act (1918)** abolished **Tinkathia**; **25%** of illegal exactions refunded.
Precursor: the **Bengal indigo revolt of 1859**.

o: Lump-sum compensation demanded when indigo lost its value
ne6721a7fba5.x: Tawan was lump-sum compensation extracted when indigo became less valuable; sharahbeshi was enhanced rent.
xa: Indigo lost value because of **synthetic dyes**.
**Tinkathia**: indigo on **3/20th** of land for **European planters**.
The **Champaran Agrarian Act (1918)** refunded **25%** of illegal exactions.

n149dc584caa.s: The Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association, also known as Majoor Mahajan Sangh, was founded in 1920 by:
o: Ambalal Sarabhai with Vallabhbhai Patel's guidance
J.B. Kripalani with Anugrah Narayan Sinha's guidance
n149dc584caa.x: The Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association, or Majoor Mahajan Sangh, was founded in 1920 by Anusuya Sarabhai with Gandhi’s guidance.
n149dc584caa.tq: Distinguish the labour organisation’s founder from the mill-owner representative.
xs: The TLA was founded by **Anusuya Sarabhai with Gandhi's guidance** — option **(4)**.
**Ambalal Sarabhai**, her brother, led the **mill owners**; **Patel** was Kheda's field commander.
**Rajendra Prasad**, **Anugrah Narayan Sinha** (lawyers) and **J.B. Kripalani** (teacher) were Champaran associates.
xa: The TLA grew out of the **Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918)** over the **plague bonus**.
The tribunal awarded the workers **35%**.
n149dc584caa.fixed: UPSC key ybca83dd7bc3/ya0dc34ad97b: TLA founded by Gandhi

nindian-history-23-17.s: The Teen Kathiya system at Champaran forced peasants to cultivate indigo on:
nindian-history-23-17.x: Under the Tinkathia system, Champaran peasants had to grow indigo on 3 out of every 20 parts (3/20th) of their land.
nindian-history-23-17.tq: Recall the share fixed under Tinkathia.
n: Teen Kathiya forced indigo cultivation on three-twentieths of the land. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Teen Kathiya was associated with indigo cultivation in Champaran. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
xs: Teen Kathiya forced indigo on **3/20th** of the land — option **(2)**.
**Tinkathia**: tenants bound to grow indigo on **three-twentieths** of holdings for **European planters**.
xa: The **Champaran Agrarian Committee** was chaired by **F.G. Sly**, with Gandhi a member.
The system was **abolished** by the **Champaran Agrarian Act (1918)**.
Precursor: the **Bengal indigo revolt** of **1859**.

n88ff21b936e.x: Gopal Krishna Gokhale was Gandhi's political mentor; Tolstoy, Ruskin and Thoreau were his intellectual influences.
xa: On **Gokhale's** advice, Gandhi spent a year touring India without taking political positions after returning in **1915**.
**Tolstoy Farm (1910, near Johannesburg)** was named after Tolstoy.
Gandhi's own writings: **Hind Swaraj** (**1909**) and **The Story of My Experiments with Truth**.

n23555206bf8.s: Rajkumar Shukla, who persuaded Mahatma Gandhi to visit Champaran, was a:
o: Lawyer of the Bihar High Court
n23555206bf8.x: Rajkumar Shukla was a local indigo cultivator and agriculturist of Champaran who persuaded Gandhi to investigate the peasants’ condition. Rajendra Prasad was an associate, not the inviter.
n23555206bf8.tq: Distinguish the inviter from the prominent associate.
xs: **Rajkumar Shukla** was a **local indigo cultivator** (agriculturist) of Champaran — so option **(2)** is correct.
He **persuaded Gandhi to come** to Champaran after meeting him at the **Lucknow Congress, 1916**.
The **lawyers (vakils)** of Bihar were **Rajendra Prasad**, **Brajkishore Prasad** and **Anugrah Narayan Sinha**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **Rajendra Prasad** was an associate, not the inviter.
**J.B. Kripalani** was a teacher; **Mahadev Desai** was Gandhi's **secretary**.
Champaran (**1917**) was in **Bihar**, not Gujarat — Gandhi's **first civil disobedience** in India.

n26f726c1b53.s: What wage rise did the tribunal award the workers in the Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918)?
n26f726c1b53.x: The workers had demanded 50%; Gandhi advised 35% and the tribunal awarded 35%.
xa: Owners had offered only **20%**.
Gandhi's **first hunger strike in India** was in this strike.
Anusuya founded the **TLA (Majoor Mahajan Sangh)** in **1920**.

ncc3d4a52fbf.s: In the Kheda campaign of 1918, which of the following combinations is correct?
o: Gandhi — spiritual head; Patel, Mohanlal Pandya and Narahari Parikh — mobilisation
Patel — spiritual head; Gandhi, Rajendra Prasad and Nehru — mobilisation
Nehru — spiritual head; Patel and Subhas Bose — mobilisation
Gandhi — spiritual head; Sarojini Naidu and Annie Besant — mobilisation
ncc3d4a52fbf.x: Gandhi acted as the spiritual head, while Patel, Mohanlal Pandya and Narahari Parikh led the mobilisation among the peasants.
ncc3d4a52fbf.tq: Avoid swapping the overall guide with the local organisers.
xs: **Gandhi** was the spiritual head; **Patel**, **Mohanlal Pandya** and **Narahari Parikh** handled mobilisation — option **(1)**.
Patel was the **field commander** at Kheda; Mohanlal Pandya was **co-leader**.
**Rajendra Prasad** belonged to Champaran (Bihar), not Kheda.
xa: Kheda started the **Gandhi-Patel alliance**.
Cause: **crop failure** and refused **remission of land revenue**.
Settled when revenue was **recovered only from those able to pay**.

n842b818ee75.s: Which of the following leaders was associated with the Kheda Satyagraha and became an important partner in the Gandhi–Patel alliance?
n842b818ee75.x: Vallabhbhai Patel provided field leadership in Kheda and thereby began the important Gandhi–Patel alliance. The other names were associated mainly with the Champaran work.
n842b818ee75.tq: Match the leader with the correct satyagraha rather than the associate group.
xs: **Vallabhbhai Patel** led Kheda and began the **Gandhi-Patel alliance** — option **(4)**.
**J.B. Kripalani** (teacher), **Mahadev Desai** (secretary) and **Brajkishore Prasad** (lawyer) were associated with **Champaran**.
xa: Patel was **field commander**; **Mohanlal Pandya** was co-leader.
Kheda (**1918**): **crop failure**, refused **remission of land revenue**.

n13df60b4716.s: The Champaran, Ahmedabad and Kheda struggles took place during the viceroyalty of:
n13df60b4716.x: All three struggles occurred during the viceroyalty of Lord Chelmsford, who served from 1916 to 1921.
n13df60b4716.tq: Use the common chronological frame to identify the viceroy.
xs: The Viceroy during all three struggles was **Lord Chelmsford (1916-21)** — option **(3)**.
Champaran (**1917**), Ahmedabad and Kheda (**1918**) all fall within his term.
xa: Chelmsford was also Viceroy at the **Jallianwala Bagh** massacre (**13 April 1919**).
Punjab's Lt. Governor then was **Sir Michael O'Dwyer**.

nf170e2e9202.s: Gandhi's return to India on 9 January 1915 is now observed as:
nf170e2e9202.x: 9 January, the day Gandhi returned in 1915, is observed as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.
xa: **Tolstoy Farm** was founded in **1910** near **Johannesburg**.
After return he founded the **Satyagraha Ashram (1915)** at **Kochrab**, then **Sabarmati (1917)**.
His first struggle in India was **Champaran (1917, Bihar)**.

nb80747a5dda.s: Gandhi's Satyagraha Ashram, established in 1915, was at:
nb80747a5dda.x: The Satyagraha Ashram at Kochrab was set up in 1915, followed by Sabarmati (1917) and Sevagram (1936).
xa: In South Africa: **Phoenix Settlement (1904, near Durban)** and **Tolstoy Farm (1910, near Johannesburg)**.
Gandhi returned to India on **9 January 1915**, the year the Kochrab ashram was founded.

nindian-history-122-3.s: The crowd at Jallianwala Bagh on 13 April 1919 had gathered on the occasion of:
nindian-history-122-3.x: The crowd gathered on Baisakhi, 13 April 1919, amid the Rowlatt Satyagraha protests and arrests of local leaders.
n: The occasion of the Jallianwala Bagh incident was Baisakhi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
The immediate context of the Jallianwala Bagh incident was the Rowlatt Satyagraha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
xa: **Viceroy**: **Lord Chelmsford**.
**Dyer** fired for about **10 minutes**, **1,650 rounds**, blocking the **only exit**.
Official toll: **379 dead**, **1,100 injured**.

n426c1f77b9e.s: Who is credited with giving Gandhi the title ‘Mahatma’?
n426c1f77b9e.x: Rabindranath Tagore is credited with giving Gandhi the title ‘Mahatma’. Subhas Chandra Bose is associated with the title ‘Father of the Nation’ for Gandhi.
n426c1f77b9e.tq: Distinguish the persons associated with Gandhi’s two well-known titles.
xs: The title "**Mahatma**" is credited to **Rabindranath Tagore** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Subhas Chandra Bose** called Gandhi "**Father of the Nation**", not Mahatma.
**Gokhale** was Gandhi's **political mentor**, not the giver of the title.
xa: APPSC **2019** accepted "Mahatma given in **1914**".
APPSC **2019** also accepted that Gandhi was absent at Nehru's "**Tryst with Destiny**" speech.
Tagore later renounced his **Knighthood** after the **Jallianwala Bagh** massacre (**1919**).

n9297eccbb8d.s: According to the official figures, the casualties in the Jallianwala Bagh firing were approximately:
n9297eccbb8d.x: The official figures recorded 379 deaths and 1,100 injuries, although the Indian National Congress estimated a higher death toll.
n9297eccbb8d.tq: Keep official figures separate from alternative estimates and firing-round data.
xs: Official figures: **379 dead, 1,100 injured** — option **(3)**.
**1,650** is the number of rounds fired, not the injured.
The **INC** estimated **over 1,000** dead.
xa: Firing lasted about **10 minutes**; Dyer blocked the **only exit**.
Date: **13 April 1919 (Baisakhi)**.
The **Hunter Committee** condemned Dyer; the **House of Lords** backed him.

n5a67e88b9e6.s: After the Hunter Committee condemned General Dyer's conduct, which body backed him?
n5a67e88b9e6.x: The Hunter Committee, appointed after the massacre, condemned Dyer, but the House of Lords supported him.
xa: Aftermath included **martial law**, the **crawling order** and **floggings**.
Official toll: **379 dead, 1,100 injured**.
⚠ Trap: **O'Dwyer** = Lt. Governor; **Dyer** = Brigadier-General who fired.

n2269387be3b.s: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
n2269387be3b.x: Lord Chelmsford was the Viceroy when the massacre took place at Amritsar.
xa: O'Dwyer handed Amritsar to **Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer**.
⚠ Trap: **O'Dwyer** = Lt. Governor; **Dyer** = officer who fired.
Chelmsford's term: **1916-21**.

nindian-history-122-8.s: Which Amritsar leader was arrested in April 1919, before the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
nindian-history-122-8.x: Dr Saifuddin Kitchlew was the Amritsar leader arrested on 9 April 1919, before the massacre.
n: Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal were the Punjab leaders who were arrested. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered the firing at Jallianwala Bagh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
Lord Chelmsford was the Viceroy during the Jallianwala Bagh incident. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
xa: Kitchlew and Satyapal were symbols of **Hindu-Muslim unity**.
On **10 April** troops fired on a crowd demanding their release.
⚠ **O'Dwyer** = Lt. Governor; **Dyer** = Brigadier-General who fired.
nindian-history-122-8.fixed: Kitchlew and Satyapal were arrested on 10 April 1919, not 9 April

nindian-history-122-10.s: Who was the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab at the time of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
nindian-history-122-10.x: Michael O'Dwyer was Lieutenant Governor of Punjab; Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered the firing.
n: Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered troops to open fire. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
Dyer was associated with the firing, while O'Dwyer was associated with Punjab administration. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
xa: O'Dwyer handed Amritsar to Dyer, who **banned assemblies**.
Aftermath: **martial law**, **crawling order**, **floggings**.
The **Hunter Committee** condemned Dyer; the **House of Lords** backed him.

nfed29f2151c.s: Which one of the following was NOT a journal associated with Mahatma Gandhi?
nfed29f2151c.x: Mathrubhumi was not associated with Gandhi. Young India, Navajivan and Harijan were among his journals.
nfed29f2151c.tq: Eliminate the outsider from a closely related list of publications.
xs: **Mathrubhumi** was not Gandhi's journal — so option **(3)** is the answer (an APPSC **2019** trap).
**Young India**, **Navajivan** and **Harijan** were Gandhi's journals in India.
xa: In South Africa he ran **Indian Opinion**.
His writings: **Hind Swaraj** (**1909**) and **The Story of My Experiments with Truth**.
The title "**Mahatma**" is credited to **Tagore**; "**Father of the Nation**" to **Subhas Chandra Bose**.

na87e78982fb.s: The Rowlatt Act (Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, 1919) was repealed during the viceroyalty of:
na87e78982fb.x: It was repealed under Lord Reading, along with the Press Act of 1910.
xa: Passed on **10 March 1919**; popularly the **"Black Act"**.

Slogan against it: "**No Vakil, No Dalil, No Appeal**".

nffe988e4653.s: The Rowlatt Act was passed on:
nffe988e4653.x: The Rowlatt Act was passed on 10 March 1919. 6 April was the date of the Rowlatt Satyagraha hartal, while 13 April was the date of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
nffe988e4653.tq: Separate the dates of enactment, hartal and massacre rather than treating them as one event.
xs: The Rowlatt Act was passed on **10 March 1919** — option **(4)**.
**6 April 1919** was the **hartal**; **13 April 1919** was the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre**.
xa: Gandhi had **warned** against it on **24 Feb 1919**.
Gandhi **withdrew** the satyagraha on **18 April 1919**.
⚠ Trap: passed **10 March 1919**; **repealed** under **Lord Reading** with the **Press Act 1910**.

ncc694e8794e.s: Under the Rowlatt Act, in-camera trials were held by a High Court panel of how many judges?
ncc694e8794e.x: The Rowlatt Act provided in-camera trials by a three-judge High Court panel, with no right of appeal.
xa: It also provided **special tribunals** and **press curbs**.
It extended **Defence of India Act (1915)** powers.
All Indian members of the **Imperial Legislative Council** opposed it.

nfa6237a96e9.s: The Rowlatt Act came into existence as an extension of the:
nfa6237a96e9.x: The Rowlatt legislation extended the extraordinary powers earlier provided under the Defence of India Act, 1915.
nfa6237a96e9.tq: Distinguish the parent wartime legislation from the later Rowlatt enactment.
xs: The Rowlatt Act extended the powers of the **Defence of India Act, 1915** — option **(3)**.
The **Press Act, 1910** was repealed along with the Rowlatt Act under **Lord Reading**, not extended by it.
xa: Official name: **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, 1919**.
Based on the **Sedition Committee** report of Justice **Sidney Rowlatt**.
Passed on **10 March 1919**.

nindian-history-122-5.s: Which Act was popularly described as 'No Vakil, No Appeal, No Daleel'?
nindian-history-122-5.x: The Rowlatt Act was called 'No Vakil, No Appeal, No Daleel' because it allowed detention without trial; Gandhi responded with the Rowlatt Satyagraha.
n: The Rowlatt Act was popularly described as “No Vakil, No Appeal, No Daleel.” [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
Gandhi responded to the Rowlatt Act through the Rowlatt Satyagraha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
xa: Official name: **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act**, **1919**; passed **10 March 1919**.
Based on the **Sedition Committee** of Justice **Sidney Rowlatt**.
Repealed under **Lord Reading**, with the **Press Act 1910**.

nbb6de5e2458.s: The Satyagraha Sabha was established in:
nbb6de5e2458.x: The Satyagraha Sabha was formed in Bombay in February 1919, using the networks of the Home Rule League.
nbb6de5e2458.tq: Combine the organisation’s location and date to distinguish it from later events.
xs: The **Satyagraha Sabha** was formed in **Bombay** in **February 1919** — option **(2)**.
It was built on **Home Rule League** networks to run the anti-Rowlatt agitation.
xa: Gandhi **warned** the government on **24 Feb 1919**; the Act was passed on **10 March 1919**.
The **6 April 1919** hartal followed.
It was Gandhi's **first all-India campaign**.

n3c8aada0bcb.s: The hartal called by Gandhi against the Rowlatt Act was observed on
n3c8aada0bcb.x: Gandhi called a nationwide hartal for 6 April 1919, involving fasting, prayer and protest against the Act.
n3c8aada0bcb.tq: Separate the dates of the warning, Act, hartal and withdrawal of the Satyagraha.
xs: The hartal was on **6 April 1919** — option **(2)**.
**10 March** = Act passed; **24 Feb** = Gandhi's warning; **18 April** = withdrawal.
xa: The hartal involved **fasting, prayer** and a day of **national humiliation**.
AP: peaceful hartals at **Vizag, Rajahmundry, Guntur, Vijayawada, Nellore**.
It was the **first all-India mass strike**.

n7f9b8448044.s: Gandhi withdrew the Rowlatt Satyagraha on 18 April 1919 because of:
o: Acceptance of Congress demands by the Hunter Committee
Advice of the Home Rule League
n7f9b8448044.x: The movement turned violent in Punjab and Ahmedabad, so Gandhi called it a Himalayan blunder and withdrew it on 18 April 1919.
xa: The **Jallianwala Bagh massacre** occurred on **13 April 1919**.
**Martial law** was imposed in **Amritsar** and **Lahore** after **13 April**.

nc47f2616cac.s: The Hunter Committee was appointed by the British Government in October 1919 primarily to inquire into
o: the Chauri Chaura incident and withdrawal of Non-Cooperation
the constitutional reforms proposed by the Home Rule Leagues
the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and disturbances in Punjab
the causes of the Swadeshi Movement in Bengal
nc47f2616cac.x: The committee was appointed to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the disturbances in Punjab.
nc47f2616cac.tq: Identify the exact event and regional disturbances associated with the committee.
xs: It probed the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre and Punjab disturbances** — option **(3)**.
Appointed by the government in **Oct 1919**; chairman **Lord William Hunter**.
xa: Indian members: **Chimanlal Setalvad**, **Jagat Narayan**, **Sultan Ahmed Khan**.
⚠ Trap: **Hunter** = official; **Punjab Sub-Committee** = Congress, non-official.

nindian-history-122-9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the events of April 1919 in Punjab?
o: Kitchlew and Satyapal were arrested on 13 April 1919
The Jallianwala Bagh crowd had gathered for a protest and Baisakhi
A country-wide strike took place on 6 April 1919
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919
nindian-history-122-9.x: Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal were arrested on 9 April 1919, not 13 April; 13 April was the day of the massacre.
n: The country-wide strike took place on 6 April 1919. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
The crowd gathered for a protest and to celebrate Baisakhi. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal were the Punjab leaders who were arrested. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal were arrested on 9 April 1919. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
xa: Gandhi reached **Vijayawada** on **8 April 1919**.
Gandhi **withdrew** the satyagraha on **18 April 1919** — a "**Himalayan blunder**".
**Martial law** in **Amritsar** and **Lahore** after **13 April**.

nindian-history-122-15.s: How did Rabindranath Tagore protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
o: Resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council
Resigned from the Imperial Legislative Council
nindian-history-122-15.x: Tagore gave up his knighthood on 31 May 1919 in protest; it was Shankaran Nair who resigned from the Viceroy's Council.
n: Rabindranath Tagore renounced or returned his Knighthood. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
xa: **Montagu** called the action "**Preventive Murder**".
**Udham Singh** killed **Michael O'Dwyer** on **13 March 1940**.
The **Amritsar Congress Session** met in **December 1919**.

n7a78dedc524.s: Which of the following was an Indian member of the Hunter Committee?
n7a78dedc524.x: Chimanlal Setalvad, Jagat Narayan and Sultan Ahmed Khan were the Indian members; their minority report was more critical of Dyer.
xa: Dyer was censured and **relieved of command**, but no real punishment.
Gandhi called the findings a **"whitewash"**.

n1375d63009c.s: What was the outcome of the Hunter Committee inquiry for General Dyer?
o: He was fully exonerated and retained in command
He was censured and relieved of command but received no real punishment
He was sentenced to life imprisonment
He was promoted to Lieutenant Governor of Punjab
n1375d63009c.x: Dyer was censured and relieved of command but not really punished; the House of Lords backed him and Gandhi called the findings a whitewash.
xa: Gandhi called the findings a **"whitewash"**.
The Indian members' **minority report** was more critical of Dyer.
The Hunter Committee was appointed in **Oct 1919**.

nbe5af635e61.s: Who among the following was a member of the Congress's Punjab Sub-Committee that inquired into the Punjab events?
nbe5af635e61.x: The Punjab Sub-Committee comprised Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das, Abbas Tyabji, M.R. Jayakar and Gandhi; the other three were Indian members of the official Hunter Committee.
xa: It was the Congress's own **non-official** inquiry.
It called Dyer's firing **inhuman** and martial law **disproportionate**.

nindian-history-122-12.s: The report of the Congress's non-official inquiry into the Jallianwala Bagh incident was drafted by:
nindian-history-122-12.x: Gandhi drafted the report of the Congress Inquiry Committee; the Hunter Committee, chaired by Lord William Hunter, was the official inquiry.
n: The official inquiry into the Jallianwala Bagh incident was the Hunter Committee, also called the Disorders Inquiry Committee. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
Lord William Hunter was the chairman of the Hunter Committee. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
C.H. Setalvad was an Indian member of the Hunter Committee. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
Sultan Ahmad Khan was an Indian member of the Hunter Committee. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
xa: Hunter Committee: **seven members** — **four British**, **three Indian** (**Setalvad**, **Jagat Narayan**, **Sultan Ahmad Khan**).
Congress committee members: **Motilal Nehru**, **C.R. Das**, **Abbas Tyabji**, **M.R. Jayakar**, **Gandhi**.
Gandhi called Hunter's findings a **"whitewash"**.

nindian-history-122-23.s: The Hunter Committee described General Dyer's action as:
nindian-history-122-23.x: The Hunter Committee criticised Dyer by calling his action an 'error of judgement'; 'preventive murder' was Montagu's phrase.
n: The Hunter Committee criticised Dyer's actions. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
The Hunter Committee described Dyer's action as an “Error in judgement.” [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
xa: The Indian members wrote a **minority report** more critical of Dyer.
It was appointed in **Oct 1919** — also called the **Disorders Inquiry Committee**.
⚠ **Hunter** = official; **Punjab Sub-Committee** = Congress, non-official.

n3bc5d9344e2.s: Mahatma Gandhi visited Vijayawada on 8 April 1919, and his speech there was translated by
n3bc5d9344e2.x: Gandhi visited Vijayawada on 8 April 1919, and Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao translated his speech.
n3bc5d9344e2.tq: Use the place-date-person combination to avoid swapping a regional associate with another Andhra leader.
xs: **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao** translated Gandhi's speech at **Vijayawada** — option **(3)**.
Gandhi reached Vijayawada on **8 April 1919**.
xa: **Prakasam** demanded **fundamental rights** at the **Nellore** meeting, **Sept 1919**.
**Andhra Patrika** and **Krishna Patrika** opposed the Rowlatt Act.
**Ganjam, Godavari** and **Krishna** district conferences condemned the massacre.

nbf7b671167a.s: Martial law in Amritsar and Lahore after 13 April 1919 included public floggings, aircraft strafing and the humiliating ____ order.
nbf7b671167a.x: Martial law included public floggings, aircraft strafing of protestors and the crawling order.
xa: The crawling order applied to the **Amritsar** lane where **Marcella Sherwood** was assaulted.
Gandhi was stopped from entering **Punjab**.
The Congress inquiry called martial law **disproportionate**.

nindian-history-122-18.s: Udham Singh assassinated Michael O'Dwyer on 13 March 1940 at:
nindian-history-122-18.x: Udham Singh killed Michael O'Dwyer at Caxton Hall, London, on 13 March 1940.
n: Udham Singh killed Michael O'Dwyer. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
Michael O'Dwyer was assassinated on 13 March 1940. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
Michael O'Dwyer was assassinated at Caxton Hall in London. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
xa: O'Dwyer was **Lt. Governor** of Punjab during the massacre.
Under O'Dwyer's regime: public **floggings** and **aircraft strafing**.
**Sir C. Sankaran Nair** later lost **O'Dwyer's libel suit**, **11-1**.

nindian-history-122-17.s: Who resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
nindian-history-122-17.x: Sir Sankaran Nair resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council in protest; Montagu called the firing 'preventive murder'.
n: Shankaran Nair resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
Montagu described the action as “Preventive Murder.” [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #122 · pp 223-225]
xa: Sankaran Nair was the **only Indian** on the Executive Council.
**Jinnah**, **Malaviya**, **Mazhar-ul-Haq** resigned from the **Imperial Legislative Council** over the Rowlatt Act.
**Tagore** returned his **Knighthood** on **31 May 1919**.

nindian-history-26-2-18.s: The Chauri Chaura violence of February 1922 led Gandhi to withdraw the:
nindian-history-26-2-18.x: The Chauri Chaura violence of February 1922 made Gandhi withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement.
n: Chauri Chaura was associated with violence and the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Bardoli was associated with the Bardoli Satyagraha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
Vallabhbhai Patel was associated with the Bardoli Satyagraha. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #26-2 · pp 90-93]
xa: **Bengal** — the **Tebhaga Movement** (**Kisan Sabha**).
**Dandi March**: **1930**.

n7f6070af9d3.s: The Khilafat Movement sought primarily to secure which of the following?
o: Restoration of the Ottoman Sultan as Khalifa and protection of his territories
Abolition of the zamindari system in India
Withdrawal of British troops from Afghanistan
Establishment of a separate Muslim state in India
n7f6070af9d3.x: The movement aimed to restore the Ottoman Sultan as Khalifa and preserve the territorial integrity of the Ottoman Empire after the First World War.
n7f6070af9d3.tq: Identify the precise objective rather than a related political demand.
xs: Khilafat aimed at **restoration of the Ottoman Sultan as Khalifa and protection of his territories** — option **(1)**.
It sought to protect the **Ottoman Empire**'s territorial integrity after its defeat in **WWI**.
xa: Trigger: Treaty of **Sevres, May 1920**; the British PM had promised Turkey would not be humiliated.
Organisation: **Khilafat Committee (1919)**.
It lost relevance when Turkey **abolished the Caliphate (1924)**.
Leaders: **Ali Brothers (Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali)**, **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**, Hakim Ajmal Khan, Hasrat Mohani, Dr. M.A. Ansari.

n759c568bfbc.s: The Khilafat leaders opposed which treaty imposed on the Ottoman Empire after the First World War?
n759c568bfbc.x: The Treaty of Sevres (May 1920) threatened the territorial integrity of the Ottoman Empire and intensified the Khilafat agitation.
xa: The **Khilafat Committee** was formed in **1919**.
Turkey abolished the Caliphate in **1924**.
The NCM was launched on **1 August 1920**, months after Sevres.

nffbcf047a6e.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the Khilafat Movement?
nffbcf047a6e.x: Tej Bahadur Sapru was not a Khilafat leader; he is known as a mediator of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931). Hakim Ajmal Khan, Hasrat Mohani and Dr. M.A. Ansari were Khilafat leaders along with the Ali brothers and Abul Kalam Azad.
nffbcf047a6e.tq: Find the outsider in a group of closely associated leaders.
xs: **Tej Bahadur Sapru** was not a Khilafat leader — option **(1)**.
**Hakim Ajmal Khan**, **Hasrat Mohani** and **Dr. M.A. Ansari** were Khilafat leaders.
xa: Other Khilafat leaders: the **Ali Brothers** and **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**.
Gandhi presided over the **All-India Khilafat Conference (Delhi, Nov 1919)**.
**Ajmal Khan** later was a Swarajist; **M.A. Ansari** a No-changer.

n422a604690a.s: The Khilafat agitation lost its relevance when Turkey abolished the Caliphate in:
n422a604690a.x: Turkey abolished the Caliphate in 1924, removing the central issue around which the Khilafat agitation had developed.
xa: Aim: protect the **Ottoman Sultan/Khalifa** after WWI.
After the NCM, the Khilafat issue died, Hindu-Muslim unity broke, and communal riots followed in **1921-27**.

n24cec715d65.s: At which of the following did Gandhi preside and first propose non-violent non-cooperation over the Khilafat issue?
n24cec715d65.x: Gandhi presided over the All-India Khilafat Conference at Delhi in November 1919 and first proposed non-violent non-cooperation there. The Allahabad conference (June 1920) endorsed the boycott and asked him to lead; Nagpur (Dec 1920) formally adopted the NCM; the Karachi conference (July 1921) urged Muslims to quit the Army.
n24cec715d65.tq: Delhi Khilafat Conference, Nov 1919 = Gandhi presides, proposes non-cooperation.
xs: The **All-India Khilafat Conference, Delhi, November 1919** — option **(2)**.
**Allahabad (June 1920)** endorsed boycott and asked Gandhi to lead; **Nagpur (Dec 1920)** ratified the NCM; **Karachi (July 1921)** urged Muslims to quit the Army.
xa: The **Calcutta special session (Sept 1920)**, under **Lala Lajpat Rai**, passed Gandhi's resolution **1886 to 884**.
Gandhi's only Congress presidency was **Belgaum (1924)**.

n9c53a1e1536.s: Which of the following was a background factor behind the launch of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
n9c53a1e1536.x: The Khilafat issue, along with the Rowlatt Act and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, was a cause of the movement; the Simon Commission Report was not.
xa: The **Amritsar session (1919)**, under **Motilal Nehru**, called the reforms inadequate and disappointing.
Viceroys during NCM: **Chelmsford**, then **Lord Reading**.

n5376427d04e.s: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched on 1 August 1920, the day of the death of:
n5376427d04e.x: The movement was launched on 1 August 1920, the day Tilak died; the Calcutta special session approved it in September 1920.
xa: ⚠ Gandhi launched on **1 Aug 1920**; the Khilafat Committee on **31 Aug 1920**.
Calcutta president: **Lala Lajpat Rai**; Nagpur: **C. Vijayaraghavachariar**.

n8a271665eab.s: Who presided over the Nagpur session of the Indian National Congress in December 1920?
n8a271665eab.x: C. Vijayaraghavachariar presided over the Nagpur session of the Congress in December 1920.
n8a271665eab.tq: Match the session with its presiding president rather than with the president of the Calcutta session.
xs: **C. Vijayaraghavachariar** presided at **Nagpur, Dec 1920** — option **(4)**.
**Lala Lajpat Rai** presided the **Calcutta special session**; **C.R. Das** presided **Gaya (Dec 1922)**.
xa: Nagpur **ratified the NCM unanimously** and adopted a new constitution.
⚠ Calcutta = **Lajpat Rai**; Nagpur = **Vijayaraghavachariar**; Gaya = **C.R. Das**; Belgaum = **Gandhi**.

n6378b5b9c21.s: At the Calcutta special session, which of the following Andhra leaders initially opposed the Non-Cooperation resolution but later resigned from the Madras Legislature?
n6378b5b9c21.x: Konda Venkatappayya initially opposed the resolution but subsequently resigned from the Madras Legislature. Pattabhi Sitaramayya, Duggirala, A. Kaleswara Rao and Peta Bapayya were also among the Andhra participants.
n6378b5b9c21.tq: Identify the individual through the unusual change in stance and subsequent action.
xs: **Konda Venkatappayya** initially opposed, then **resigned from the Madras Legislature** — option **(3)**.
**Pattabhi Sitaramayya**, **A. Kaleswara Rao** and **Peta Bapayya** were other Andhras at Calcutta, without this record.
xa: Calcutta passed Gandhi's resolution **1886 to 884**.
Gandhi's post-Chauri Chaura message to Konda Venkatappayya suspended the Guntur no-tax campaign on **11 February 1922**.

n669cc981718.s: Which Congress session is associated with Mahatma Gandhi’s only presidency of the Indian National Congress?
n669cc981718.x: Mahatma Gandhi presided over the Belgaum Session in 1924, which was his only presidency of the Indian National Congress.
n669cc981718.tq: Distinguish the unique presidency from the other NCM-period sessions.
xs: Gandhi's only presidency was **Belgaum Session, 1924** — option **(1)**.
**Calcutta (1920)** = **Lala Lajpat Rai**; **Gaya (1922)** = **C.R. Das**; **Nagpur (1920)** = **C. Vijayaraghavachariar**.
xa: Gandhi was released from prison in **1924** on health grounds.
Gandhi presided over the **All-India Khilafat Conference (Delhi, Nov 1919)** — not a Congress session.

n3ac432ba3ad.s: Which of the following gave up legal practice during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
n3ac432ba3ad.x: T. Prakasam was among the lawyers who gave up practice, along with Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das, Rajagopalachari, Patel and others; Ambedkar was not.
xa: **Saifuddin Kitchlew** (Punjab) also gave up practice.
Urban groups: **students, teachers**, **lawyers**, **merchants**.

n78556e1c470.s: During the Non-Cooperation Movement, tribals and forest users participated through opposition to:
n78556e1c470.x: Tribals and forest users joined the movement by opposing pullari, while peasants joined no-tax campaigns.
xa: The **Palnadu** satyagraha refused the **pullari (grazing) tax**.
**12** women were jailed in **Chirala-Perala**.

ne966df63f27.s: The Akali Movement for gurdwara reform led to the Sikh Gurdwaras Act of:
ne966df63f27.x: The Akali Movement (1920–25) against corrupt mahants culminated in the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925.
xa: The Akali movement spanned **1920-25**.
The **Moplah uprising (1921)** in Malabar was another parallel struggle.

nffcdcc3af6e.s: Gandhi's visit to Kakinada in April 1921 inspired which later national leader?
nffcdcc3af6e.x: Gandhi's Kakinada visit in April 1921 inspired Durgabai Deshmukh.
nffcdcc3af6e.tq: Connect a place-specific visit with its stated personal influence.
xs: **Durgabai Deshmukh** — option **(3)**.
Gandhi's **Kakinada visit (Apr 1921)** inspired her.
xa: Women entered the NCM in numbers; **'Desasevikalu'** in Andhra.
Women's jewellery for the Tilak Fund: **Maganti Annapurnamma**, **Yamini Purna Tilakam**.

n7daebbb62d9.s: Who led the Palnadu forest satyagraha?
n7daebbb62d9.x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu led the Palnadu forest satyagraha, which involved boycotting forest officials and refusing the grazing tax.
xa: Issue: refusal of **pullari (grazing) tax**.
**Unnava Lakshminarayana** and **Madabhushi Vedanta Lakshmi Narasimhachari** were arrested.
⚠ **Pedanandipadu** = **Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary** (**'Shanti Sena'**).

nb48db856a01.s: The Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn through the Bardoli resolution adopted on
nb48db856a01.x: The Bardoli resolution of 11–12 February 1922 turned the Congress towards constructive work after the movement was withdrawn.
nb48db856a01.tq: Distinguish the withdrawal resolution date from the date of the Chauri Chaura incident and Gandhi’s arrest.
xs: The **Bardoli resolution** was adopted on **11-12 Feb 1922** — option **(3)**.
**4 February 1922** was **Chauri Chaura**; **March 1922** was Gandhi's arrest.
xa: Congress turned to **constructive work** after Bardoli.
Gandhi fasted **3 days** before calling off the movement.
Gandhi was arrested on **10 March 1922** at **Sabarmati**.

n0b08df628b0.s: The Chauri Chaura incident occurred in which district of the United Provinces?
n0b08df628b0.x: Chauri Chaura is in Gorakhpur district, where a crowd burnt the police station after police action against a procession in February 1922.
xa: **22 policemen** were killed (some notes say **21**).
**Bhagwan Ahir** was among those beaten.
Of **172** sentenced to death, **19** were finally hanged.

na99b673d562.s: Who provided legal defence to the accused in the Chauri Chaura case?
na99b673d562.x: Madan Mohan Malaviya defended the accused persons in the Chauri Chaura case.
na99b673d562.tq: Use the lawyer–case association rather than confusing the defence counsel with prominent Congress lawyers.
xs: **Madan Mohan Malaviya** defended the accused — option **(1)**.
Of **172** sentenced to death, **19** were finally hanged.
xa: Chauri Chaura was in **Gorakhpur district, UP**.
It led to the **Bardoli resolution (11-12 Feb 1922)**.

n063f85d8c7a.s: Who called the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement after Chauri Chaura a 'national calamity'?
n063f85d8c7a.x: Subhas Chandra Bose called the withdrawal a national calamity; M.N. Roy described it as weak leadership.
xa: Bose also said "**sprinkling cold water**".
**C.R. Das** also criticised the sudden withdrawal.
Result: Hindu-Muslim unity broke; communal riots **1921-27**.

n663e6240975.s: How many policemen were killed when a crowd burnt the police station at Chauri Chaura in February 1922?
n663e6240975.x: At Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district (4 February 1922), the crowd burnt the police station and 22 policemen were killed; the NCM was then withdrawn by the Bardoli resolution.
xa: Withdrawal: **Bardoli resolution (11-12 Feb 1922)**.
The NCM **made nationalism a mass movement** — a commonly paired true statement.

n3a224c8c5e5.s: In April 1919, while on his way to Punjab, Gandhi was stopped and detained by the British at:
n3a224c8c5e5.x: In April 1919 Gandhi was stopped and detained at Palwal while proceeding towards Punjab; the incident contributed to riots.
n3a224c8c5e5.tq: Separate the place of the first detention from the place of the later sedition trial.
xs: Gandhi was detained at **Palwal** — option **(2)**.
In **April 1919** he was stopped on his way to **Punjab**, which sparked riots.
xa: His later arrest was on **10 March 1922** at **Sabarmati, Ahmedabad**.
Trial: **18 March 1922**, Ahmedabad, before Judge **C.N. Broomfield**.
n3a224c8c5e5.fixed: Palwal detention was not a sedition arrest; his sedition arrest was March 1922

nb54f82a40ae.s: In the Great Trial at Ahmedabad (March 1922), Gandhi was sentenced to:
nb54f82a40ae.x: Charged with sedition under Section 124A for his Young India articles, Gandhi received a six-year sentence.
xa: Articles included "**Tampering with Loyalty**" and "**Shaking the Manes**".
Released in **1924** on health grounds.
Judge: **C.N. Broomfield**.

n2218e19a6ef.s: Gandhi's Great Trial of 1922 was presided over by Judge:
n2218e19a6ef.x: Judge C.N. Broomfield presided over the Great Trial on 18 March 1922, where Gandhi pleaded guilty and asked for the highest penalty.
xa: Gandhi said "**affection cannot be manufactured or regulated by law**".
Charge: **Sedition (Sec. 124A IPC)**; sentence **6 years**.

n2de897939e2.s: Which of the following periodicals was NOT edited by Gandhi?
n2de897939e2.x: The Bengalee was not Gandhi's paper; it was Surendranath Banerjea's. Gandhi's papers were Young India, Navajivan, Indian Opinion and Harijan.
n2de897939e2.tq: Identify the odd publication among a list of known Gandhi-edited periodicals.
xs: **The Bengalee** was not Gandhi's — option **(4)**.
Gandhi's papers: **Young India**, **Navajivan**, **Indian Opinion**, **Harijan**.
xa: His **1922** sedition charge arose from three **Young India** articles.
Articles included "**Tampering with Loyalty**" and "**Shaking the Manes**".

n0f06cbce841.s: The Delhi special session of the Indian National Congress held in September 1923 permitted the Swarajists to
o: withdraw from the Central Legislative Assembly
n0f06cbce841.x: The Delhi special session in September 1923 allowed the Swarajists to contest elections. They made substantial gains in the elections held later in 1923.
n0f06cbce841.tq: Link the special session with its specific organisational and electoral decision.
xs: It allowed Swarajists to **contest** elections — option **(4)**.
In the **1923 elections** they made **large gains**.
xa: **V. Ramadas** won a **Central Legislative Assembly** seat from Madras.
Strategy: "**End or Mend**".

nfb9b91b41a9.s: The Bardoli resolution was adopted on:
nfb9b91b41a9.x: The Bardoli resolution was adopted on 11–12 February 1922; the Prince of Wales boycott was on 17 November 1921 and the Treaty of Sevres in May 1920.
xa: NCM launched **1 Aug 1920**; **Chauri Chaura** on **4 Feb 1922**.
**Moplah rebellion**: **Aug 1921**.

n61e42dc8c18.s: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched on 1 August 1920, the same day on which which of the following leaders died?
n61e42dc8c18.x: Bal Gangadhar Tilak died on 1 August 1920, the day the Non-Cooperation Movement was launched.
xs: **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** died on **1 August 1920** — option **(3)**.
Gandhi launched the NCM that day and returned his **Kaiser-i-Hind** medal.
xa: The Khilafat Committee began non-cooperation on **31 August 1920**.
The fund named after him: **Tilak Swaraj Fund**, **₹1 crore**.

nfa1e2ace7a5.s: The Marxist interpretation of Gandhi’s withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement held that it was intended to prevent:
o: A radical anti-landlord turn of the movement
The expansion of council entry by Swarajists
The formation of the Akali Dal
nfa1e2ace7a5.x: The Marxist interpretation argued that Gandhi halted the movement to prevent it from taking a radical anti-landlord direction.
nfa1e2ace7a5.tq: Link an ideological interpretation with the political-economic development it claims Gandhi sought to prevent.
xs: To prevent a **radical anti-landlord turn** — option **(1)**.
That is the **Marxist view** of the post-Chauri Chaura withdrawal.
xa: Others criticising: **Bose, M.N. Roy and C.R. Das**.
Withdrawal: **Bardoli resolution (11-12 Feb 1922)**.

n2380d3288ac.s: Under the Non-Cooperation programme, the November 1920 legislative elections were:
n2380d3288ac.x: The November 1920 elections were boycotted; surrender of titles and non-payment of taxes (as the final stage) were part of the programme.
xa: Other boycotts: **law courts**, government **schools/colleges**, durbars, **foreign cloth**.
The boycott let the **Justice Party** win **63 of 98** seats in Madras.

nc4d62388ba7.s: The Tilak Swaraj Fund associated with the Non-Cooperation Movement had a target of
nc4d62388ba7.x: The Tilak Swaraj Fund had a target and collection of one crore rupees.
nc4d62388ba7.tq: Test the exact fund target with nearby monetary distractors.
xs: The **Tilak Swaraj Fund** target was **₹1 crore** — option **(1)**.
The **1 crore** was also collected.
xa: The **Vijayawada AICC (1921)** set targets: **Rs 1 crore** fund, **1 crore members**, **20 lakh charkhas**.
