Andhra women gave jewellery: **Maganti Annapurnamma**, **Yamini Purna Tilakam**.

na006b887bb4.s: Which of the following was part of the constructive programme of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
o: Promotion of khadi and the charkha
na006b887bb4.x: Promotion of khadi and the charkha was constructive work; boycott of foreign cloth was a boycott measure.
xa: Constructive items also included prohibition and **removal of untouchability**.
Merchants joined through the **foreign-cloth boycott**.

nd2e05e68b0f.s: The Moplah uprising of 1921 occurred in Malabar, Kerala, and primarily involved:
o: Tribal forest users against British forest officials
nd2e05e68b0f.x: The Moplah uprising took place in Malabar, Kerala, and began as an agrarian conflict involving Muslim tenants and Hindu landlords before turning communal.
nd2e05e68b0f.tq: Separate the Moplah agrarian conflict from the parallel Akali and forest struggles.
xs: **Muslim tenants against Hindu landlords** — option **(3)**.
It took place in **Malabar, Kerala, 1921**, and turned communal.
**Sikh** reform against **corrupt mahants** was the **Akali movement**.
xa: Moplah rebellion: **Aug 1921** in the NCM chronology.
Akali movement led to the **Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925**.

n5496f08b529.s: The Khilafat–Non-Cooperation phase is regarded as the high point of:
n5496f08b529.x: The Khilafat–Non-Cooperation phase represented the high point of Hindu-Muslim unity during the national movement.
xa: After withdrawal, unity broke and communal riots followed (**1921-27**).
Ali Brothers toured India with Gandhi.

n4e278240f18.s: Which of the following institutions was founded at Aligarh in 1920 and later shifted to Delhi?
n4e278240f18.x: Jamia Millia Islamia was founded at Aligarh in 1920 and later shifted to Delhi.
n4e278240f18.tq: Distinguish the institution’s original location from its later well-known location.
xs: **Jamia Millia Islamia** — founded **1920**, **Aligarh**, later Delhi — option **(4)**.
**AMU** grew from **MAO College** (**1875**, Sir Syed), becoming a university in **1920** by Act.
xa: **Gujarat Vidyapith (1920, Ahmedabad)** was founded by Gandhi.
**Kashi Vidyapith** — **1921**, Varanasi.
Leaders linked to national education: **Zakir Hussain**, Acharya **Narendra Dev**, **Subhas Bose**.

n5bc25397e43.s: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan established the MAO College, from which Aligarh Muslim University developed, in:
n5bc25397e43.x: The MAO College was established in 1875; the university got legal status in 1920 but was not a Non-Cooperation national institution.
xa: APPSC **2023**: only **Jamia** and **Kashi Vidyapith** are NCM-era of the three.
⚠ **Besant Theosophical College, Madanapalle** (**1915**) is also not NCM-era.

n98690c3dd11.s: Gujarat Vidyapith, a national institution of the Non-Cooperation era, was founded in:
n98690c3dd11.x: Gujarat Vidyapith was founded in 1920, while Kashi and Bihar Vidyapiths came in 1921.
xa: **Jamia Millia Islamia** (**1920**, Aligarh) was also NCM-era.
About **800 national schools and colleges** opened.

nap-history-25-8.s: The Home Rule League, whose Andhra branches were started under Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao, was founded by:
nap-history-25-8.x: Annie Besant founded the Home Rule Movement in 1916; its Andhra branches were started under Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.
n: Gadicherla Hari Sarvothama Rao led the starting of branches of the Home Rule Movement. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
Annie Besant was the overall founder of the Home Rule Movement. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
xa: The **Swadeshi Movement** in Andhra was started by the **youth of Rajahmundry**, who founded the **Bala Bharathi Samiti** in **1907**.
**Bipin Chandra Pal** toured Andhra during the **Vandemataram Movement**.
The **Wahabi Movement** in **Hyderabad** was led by **Mubariz-ud-Daulah**.
nap-history-25-8.fixed: original stem oddly worded ('overall founder associated with the branches')

n210f01a4a9e.s: The Palnadu satyagraha involved refusal to pay which tax?
n210f01a4a9e.x: The Palnadu forest satyagraha involved refusal to pay the pullari, or grazing, tax and a boycott of forest officials.
n210f01a4a9e.tq: Discriminate between the similarly placed tax issues of Andhra movements.
xs: The **Pullari or grazing tax** — option **(2)**.
Peasants also **boycotted forest officials**.
The **municipal tax** was the Chirala-Perala issue.
xa: The **forest satyagraha first started in Palnadu**.
Leader: **Kanneganti Hanumantarao**; **28** men and **8** women arrested.

nap-history-25-5.s: Who led the Kisan (agrarian) movement in Andhra?
nap-history-25-5.x: N.G. Ranga led the Kisan movement; Veerayya Chowdary led the No-Tax Campaign and Kanneganti Hanumanthu the Palnadu forest satyagraha.
n: Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary led the No-Tax Campaign. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
Kannuganti Hanumanthu led the Forest Satyagraha in Palnadu. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
The Forest Satyagraha first started in Palnadu. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
N.G. Ranga led the Kisan or Agrarian Movement in Andhra. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
xa: Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary was called **Andhra Shivaji** and founded the **'Shanti Sena'**.
The Palnadu struggle was a refusal of the **pullari (grazing) tax**; **28** men and **8** women were arrested.
**Unnava Lakshminarayana** visited Palnadu in **1921** to study the forest satyagraha.
⚠ **Ramadandu** = Chirala-Perala (**Duggirala**); **Shanti Sena** = Pedanandipadu (**Parvataneni**).

nap-history-25-22.s: The Chirala-Perala Movement opposed the formation of which of the following?
nap-history-25-22.x: The Chirala-Perala Movement opposed turning Chirala into a municipality, which brought heavy taxes. Under Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah, residents moved out to Ramnagar.
nap-history-25-22.tq: Recall what the Chirala people protested.
n: The Chirala-Perala Movement opposed the formation of the Chirala municipality. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
xs: The **Chirala-Perala Movement** opposed the **formation** of the **Chirala municipality** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was **started** by **Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah** in **Bapatla taluka**, **Guntur** (now Bapatla district).
The **Bala Bharathi Samiti** was founded by the youth of **Rajahmundry** in **1907** during the **Swadeshi Movement** — unrelated.
xa: Chirala-Perala ran in **1921-22**; its volunteer force was **"Ramadandu"** and **12** women were jailed.
⚠ Sources differ: one note calls the force **"Ramanandu"**; the other notes say **"Ramadandu"**.
The **Pedanandipadu** no-tax campaign was led by **Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary**, founder of the **'Shanti Sena'**.

nap-history-25-23.x: Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary, who led the No-Tax Campaign at Pedanandipadu in Guntur, was called Andhra Shivaji.
n: Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary was known as Andhra Shivaji. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
Pedanandipadu in Guntur was associated with the No-Tax Campaign. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
xa: He founded the volunteer body **'Shanti Sena'**.
The Guntur no-tax campaign was **suspended on 11 February 1922** after Gandhi's message to **Konda Venkatappayya** (post-Chauri Chaura).
⚠ **Shanti Sena** = Pedanandipadu; **Ramadandu** = Chirala-Perala (**Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah**).

nap-history-26-16.s: Which police station was attacked first during the Rampa Rebellion?
nap-history-26-16.x: The Rampa Rebellion began on August 22, 1922, when Alluri Sitarama Raju's men raided the Chintapalli police station. Kanikapadu and Nidubrolu are linked with N.G. Ranga.
nap-history-26-16.tq: Recall the first station raided in 1922.
n: The first police station attacked during the Rampa Rebellion was at Chintapalli. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 37-38]
xs: The **first police station attacked** in the **Rampa Rebellion** was at **Chintapalli** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The rebellion (**1922-24**) was led by **Alluri Sitarama Raju** in the **Godavari agency**.
**Palnadu** was the site of the **forest (pullari) satyagraha** led by **Kannuganti Hanumanthu**, not a Rampa police station.
xa: The tribes associated with Rampa were the **Koyas and Konda Doras**.
Alluri Sitarama Raju was killed on **7 May 1924**.
The **forest satyagraha first started in Palnadu**, linked with the **Non-Cooperation Movement**.

nd568e8e128d.s: The AICC meeting at Vijayawada (1921) set a target of how many charkhas?
nd568e8e128d.x: The Vijayawada targets were one crore rupees for the Tilak Swaraj Fund, one crore members and twenty lakh charkhas.
xa: The AICC met at **Vijayawada, 31 March-1 April 1921**, under Gandhi.
⚠ **Ramadandu** = Chirala-Perala; **Shanti Sena** = Pedanandipadu.

n6b07cf78f7d.s: Who presented a design for the national flag at the AICC meeting held at Vijayawada in 1921?
n6b07cf78f7d.x: Pingali Venkayya presented his flag design at the Vijayawada AICC meeting.
n6b07cf78f7d.tq: Match the symbolic contribution with its Andhra contributor.
xs: **Pingali Venkayya** presented his flag design — option **(2)**.
**Duggirala** led Chirala-Perala; **Konda Venkatappayya** and **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** were Andhras at Calcutta.
xa: Venue: **Gandhinagar**; reception chairman **Addepati Ramaseshaiah**.
Dates: **31 March-1 April 1921**.

nf6d10c44529.s: After the Congress boycotted the November 1920 elections in Madras Presidency, the first ministry was formed by:
nf6d10c44529.x: The Justice Party won 63 of 98 seats and the first ministry was formed under A. Subbarayalu Reddiar on 17 December 1920.
xa: The boycott of legislatures (**Nov 1920**) was part of the NCM programme.
In **1923**, **V. Ramadas** won a **Central Legislative Assembly** seat from Madras.

nb9d3a1c0631.s: Which leader of the Non-Cooperation era was associated with Madras and later became a No-Changer?
nb9d3a1c0631.x: Rajagopalachari (Madras) became a No-Changer; C.R. Das (Bengal) and Motilal Nehru (UP) became Swarajists.
xa: Swaraj Party: **C.R. Das (president)**, **Motilal Nehru (secretary)**.
Lajpat Rai presided the **Calcutta special session**.

nbd8962aec83.s: After the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement, the pro-changers favoured:
nbd8962aec83.x: The pro-changers, or Swarajists, sought to enter the councils to 'end or mend' them; the no-changers preferred constructive work and continued boycott.
xa: Pro-changers: **C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru, Ajmal Khan, Vithalbhai Patel**.
No-changers: **C. Rajagopalachari, Vallabhbhai Patel, Rajendra Prasad, M.A. Ansari**.
Swarajists called the councils "**sham parliaments**".

n8abb6504ee7.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Andhra branch of the Swaraj Party?
o: Pithapuram Raja was president and C.R. Das was secretary.
V. Ramadas was president and Motilal Nehru was secretary.
Unava Lakshmi Narayana was president and Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was secretary.
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was president and Unava Lakshmi Narayana was secretary.
n8abb6504ee7.x: The Andhra branch had Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao as president and Unava Lakshmi Narayana as secretary.
n8abb6504ee7.tq: Keep the regional office-bearers distinct from the central Swaraj Party founders.
xs: President **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao**, secretary **Unava Lakshmi Narayana** — option **(4)**.
Option (3) reverses the two posts.
xa: The **Pithapuram Raja** formed the **People's Party** to back the Swarajists.
**V. Ramadas** won a **Central Legislative Assembly** seat from Madras in **1923**.

n707c34e8e19.s: Who founded the Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party along with C.R. Das?
n707c34e8e19.x: C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru were the principal founders of the Swaraj Party; Jawaharlal Nehru was not a founder.
xa: ⚠ "C.R. Das and Jawaharlal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party" is WRONG (APPSC **2023**).
It formed after the **suspension of the NCM** (APPSC **2018**).

na363516bf80.s: The expression “End or Mend” was associated with the Swarajists’ strategy of
o: forming a separate party outside the Congress permanently
entering councils and obstructing colonial governance from within
na363516bf80.x: The Swarajists entered the councils to expose them as sham parliaments and obstruct their functioning from within, a strategy expressed as “End or Mend.”
na363516bf80.tq: Apply the slogan to the practical political strategy rather than treating it as a general objective.
xs: "**End or Mend**" meant **entering councils and obstructing from within** — option **(3)**.
Swarajists aimed to expose the councils as **"sham parliaments"**.
Permanent boycott of councils was the No-changers' stance.
xa: The **Delhi special session (Sept 1923)** allowed Swarajists to contest.
Swarajists made **large gains** in **1923**.

nap-history-25-4.s: The Salt Satyagraha centre Mypadu was located in the region of:
nap-history-25-4.x: Mypadu was in Nellore; Chinnapuram was near Machilipatnam and Devarampadu near Ongole.
n: Salt Satyagraha centres emerged at Chinnapuram in Machilipatnam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
Salt Satyagraha centres emerged at Mypadu in Nellore. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
Salt Satyagraha centres emerged at Devarampadu in Ongole. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
T. Prakasam broke the salt laws in Madras city. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
Durgabai broke the salt laws in Madras city. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
xa: **Konda Venkatappayya** was the **dictator** of the Civil Disobedience / Salt Satyagraha in Andhra.
The **Kisan / Agrarian Movement** was led by **N.G. Ranga**; the **Anti-Zamindari Movement** in **Nellore** by **Vennelakanti Raghavayya**.
**Prativadi Bhayankarachari** is closely associated with the **Kakinada Conspiracy Case**.

n663c35f2750.s: The AICC meeting held at Vijayawada in 1921 is particularly associated with which decision?
o: Acceptance of Gandhi's leadership of the national struggle
Formation of the Swaraj Party at Gaya
Approval of council entry as the sole Congress programme
n663c35f2750.x: At the 1921 AICC meeting at Vijayawada, political leaders accepted Gandhi's leadership of the national struggle.
n663c35f2750.tq: Distinguish a conference decision from later developments such as suspension and council entry.
xs: At the **1921 Vijayawada AICC**, leaders **accepted Gandhi's leadership** of the national struggle — option **(1)**.
The NCM was suspended only at **Bardoli (11-12 Feb 1922)**, and council entry was set aside at **Gaya (Dec 1922)**.
xa: Targets (by **30 June 1921**): **1 crore members**, **Rs 1 crore** for the **Tilak Swaraj Fund**, **20 lakh charkhas**.
**Pingali Venkayya**'s flag design (with the charkha) was endorsed by Gandhi there.
⚠ APCC meeting **January 1921** ≠ AICC session **1921** (APPSC **2023** key).

n2024bf8c846.s: The flag design of Pingali Venkayya endorsed by Gandhi at the Vijayawada AICC meeting (1921) carried the:
n2024bf8c846.x: Pingali Venkayya's design endorsed by Gandhi at Vijayawada had the charkha.
xa: Deadline for targets: **30 June 1921**.
Leaders there **accepted Gandhi's leadership**.
PM paid tribute to Pingali Venkayya on his **150th birth anniversary** (**3 Aug 2026**).

n05c8a845827.s: At the Gaya Session of the Congress in December 1922, the resolution relating to council entry was:
n05c8a845827.x: C.R. Das’s resolution supporting council entry was defeated at Gaya in December 1922, leading to the subsequent formation of the Swaraj Party.
n05c8a845827.tq: Connect the decisive session outcome with the later organisational split.
xs: C.R. Das's council-entry resolution was **defeated** (set aside) at **Gaya (Dec 1922)** — option **(2)**.
This led to the council-entry fight between Swarajists and No-Changers.
xa: NCM had been suspended at **Bardoli** (**11-12 Feb 1922**) after **Chauri Chaura**.
Bose called the suspension a national tragedy; **M.N. Roy** blamed **weak leadership**.

n8feca22086e.s: Which group of women leaders emerged prominently in Andhra during Gandhi's Non-Cooperation tour?
o: Duvvuri Subbamma, Ponaka Kanakamma and Unnava Lakshmibayamma
Durgabai, Annie Besant and Sarojini Naidu
Ponaka Kanakamma, Konda Venkatappayya and Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
Unnava Lakshmibayamma, Garimella Satyanarayana and Durgabai
n8feca22086e.x: Duvvuri Subbamma, Ponaka Kanakamma and Unnava Lakshmibayamma emerged as women leaders during this phase of the movement.
n8feca22086e.tq: Identify the complete group of women leaders without mixing them with male organisers or other national leaders.
xs: **Duvvuri Subbamma, Ponaka Kanakamma and Unnava Lakshmibayamma** — option **(1)**.
**Konda Venkatappayya** and **Duggirala** were male Congress leaders, not part of this group.
xa: **Durgabai** translated Gandhi's Kakinada speech (**April 1921**) and gave **Rs 5,000**.
Unnava Lakshmi Narayana wrote **Nayakuralu** in jail.

ne635a06310e.s: During Gandhi's April 1921 tour of coastal Andhra, who translated his speech at Kakinada and donated Rs 5,000?
ne635a06310e.x: At Kakinada (April 1921) Durgabai translated Gandhi's speech and gave Rs 5,000. Duvvuri Subbamma, Ponaka Kanakamma and Unnava Lakshmibayamma were women leaders who emerged in the same phase, but the Kakinada translation is linked to Durgabai.
xs: **Durgabai** translated Gandhi's **Kakinada** speech and gave **Rs 5,000** — option **(1)**.
**Duvvuri Subbamma**, **Ponaka Kanakamma** and **Unnava Lakshmibayamma** emerged as women leaders on the tour, but not for the Kakinada translation.
xa: The **April 1921** coastal tour also covered Rajahmundry, Eluru, Machilipatnam, Chirala, Nellore.
In **October 1921** Gandhi toured **Kurnool, Kadapa, Tirupati, Tadipatri**.

n616d6238f18.s: Who wrote the play *Nayakuralu* while in jail in connection with the Palnadu agitation?
n616d6238f18.x: Unnava Lakshmi Narayana wrote the play *Nayakuralu* while he was in jail.
n616d6238f18.tq: Associate the literary work with the activist who produced it during imprisonment.
xs: **Unnava Lakshmi Narayana** wrote **Nayakuralu** in jail — option **(1)**.
He studied and backed the Palnadu struggle with **Madabhushi Vedantam Narasimhachari**.
xa: Unnava was also **secretary** of the Andhra Swaraj branch.
**Konda Venkatappayya** tried to dilute the struggle.

n0120d6849c1.s: Which of the following places was covered in Gandhi's October 1921 tour of Andhra?
n0120d6849c1.x: In October 1921 Gandhi toured Kurnool, Kadapa, Tirupati and Tadipatri; Kakinada, Eluru and Machilipatnam were on his April coastal tour.
xa: At **Kakinada**, **Durgabai** translated Gandhi's speech and gave **Rs 5,000**.
Women leaders who emerged: **Duvvuri Subbamma, Ponaka Kanakamma, Unnava Lakshmibayamma**.

n8f351ca7fd6.s: During the Palnadu Pullari satyagraha, the 300 cattle driven into the forest without paying the tax were impounded at:
n8f351ca7fd6.x: The cattle were impounded at Minchalapadu; Macherla was where officials were socially boycotted.
xa: ⚠ **Macherla** = social boycott; **Minchalapadu** = cattle impounded, Hanumanthu shot.
**28 men and 8 women** arrested; normalcy by **March 1922**.

nbd0d2223cad.s: Kanneganti Hanumanthu, hero of the Palnadu Pullari satyagraha (1921-22), was born in which district?
nbd0d2223cad.x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu was born in Guntur district, where Palnadu, the site of Andhra's first forest satyagraha, lies.
xa: Some notes date the Pullari rebellion from **Sept 1921**.
Hanumanthu was shot on **26 Feb 1922**.

n3a474c0f678.s: Kanneganti Hanumanthu was killed in police firing during which incident?
o: The boycott of the Prince of Wales at Vijayawada
n3a474c0f678.x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu was shot dead during the cattle-rescue action at Minchalapadu on 26 February 1922.
n3a474c0f678.tq: Identify the leader by associating him with the specific event rather than the wider movement.
xs: Hanumanthu was shot in the **cattle-rescue at Minchalapadu** — option **(4)**.
**Macherla** was the social boycott site, not the firing.
xa: He was born in **Guntur district** (APPSC **2022** key).
The Palnadu satyagraha was the **first forest satyagraha** in Andhra (APPSC **2023** key).

n34129a7a520.s: Who reacted to the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement with 'amazement and consternation'?
n34129a7a520.x: Jawaharlal Nehru reacted with 'amazement and consternation'; Bose called it a national tragedy and M.N. Roy blamed weak leadership.
xa: Reason for suspension: violence at **Chauri Chaura**.
In Andhra, withdrawal dismayed satyagrahis at **Pedanandipadu** and **Palnadu**.

ndf8b7c903ea.s: Pingali Venkayya was born at which place?
ndf8b7c903ea.x: Pingali Venkayya was born at Bhatlapenumarru.
ndf8b7c903ea.tq: Test the birthplace directly and distinguish it from other Andhra locations associated with the movement.
xs: **Bhatlapenumarru** — option **(4)**.
The PM recalled this on his **150th birth anniversary** (**3 Aug 2026**).
xa: His flag design had the **charkha**.
Gandhi endorsed it at the **1921 Vijayawada session**.

n2c67085b81e.s: Who became the first elected Indian President of the Legislative Assembly in 1925?
n2c67085b81e.x: Vithalbhai Patel became the first elected Indian President of the Legislative Assembly in 1925.
n2c67085b81e.tq: Distinguish the first office-holder from the first elected Indian holder of the office.
xs: **Vithalbhai Patel** — option **(3)**.
Elected (first Indian) **Speaker/President** of the Central Legislative Assembly in **1925**.
xa: He was a pro-changer (Swarajist).
The Swarajists did poorly in **1926**.

n57c81bfea53.s: Which bill of 1928 did the Swarajists oppose in the Central Legislative Assembly?
n57c81bfea53.x: The Swarajists opposed the Public Safety Bill of 1928; earlier, their demand for review of the 1919 Act led to the Muddiman Committee.
xa: They walked out of the councils in **1930** after **Lahore**.
The **Nationalist Party** blocked the **Finance Bill**.

nd654707ed87.s: At which Congress session, held in Andhra in 1923, did local women serve as executive members and volunteers?
nd654707ed87.x: The 1923 Congress session was held at Kakinada in Andhra, where local women served as executive members and volunteers. Gaya (1922) was in Bihar, Belgaum (1924) in Karnataka and Nagpur (1920) in central India.
xs: Local women served as **executive members and volunteers**.
**Belgaum 1924** is known instead as the only session presided by **Gandhi**.
xa: The **Nationalist Party** formed in **1924**.
Women in Andhra also did **picketing and prohibition** work.

n9f3e155bf6b.s: Who was the President of the Swarajist party organisation in Andhra?
n9f3e155bf6b.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was President, Unnava Lakshminarayana Secretary and Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao Treasurer.
xa: ⚠ **Kaleswara Rao** (president) - **Unnava** (secretary) - **Gadicherla** (treasurer).
Madras council: **B. Venkataratnam, P. Anjaneyulu, P.V. Venkatapathiraju**.

n1f33d81bac3.s: The Nationalist Party formed in the Central Legislative Assembly in 1924 consisted principally of
o: Swarajists, Jinnah’s Independents and Malaviya’s group
Congress socialists, revolutionaries and trade unions
Swarajists, British officials and Simon Commission members
n1f33d81bac3.x: The Nationalist Party brought together the Swarajists, Jinnah’s Independents and Malaviya’s group. It had about 70 members.
n1f33d81bac3.tq: Use the composition of the legislative bloc to distinguish it from other Congress groupings.
xs: **Swarajists**, **Jinnah's Independents** and **Malaviya's group** — option **(1)**.
It was the **Nationalist Party (1924)**, about **70** members.
xa: It **outvoted the government** and blocked the **Finance Bill**.
**Malaviya** later joined the **Responsivists**.

naf0f4b060d9.s: The Responsivists within the Swarajist movement favoured
o: the immediate abolition of the Congress
exclusive emphasis on spinning and khadi
complete withdrawal from all legislative activity
naf0f4b060d9.x: The Responsivists favoured cooperation with the government. Lajpat Rai, Malaviya and N.C. Kelkar were associated with this tendency.
naf0f4b060d9.tq: Test the precise meaning of a faction label instead of relying on its general political impression.
xs: **Co-operation with the government** — option **(3)**.
Responsivists: **Lajpat Rai, Malaviya, N.C. Kelkar**.
xa: They emerged after C.R. Das's death in **June 1925** split the party.
The Swarajists opposed the **Public Safety Bill (1928)**.

n7166bb839d6.s: Which of the following was a part of the constructive programme of the 1920s national movement?
n7166bb839d6.x: The constructive programme included khadi and spinning, removal of untouchability, Hindu-Muslim unity, prohibition, national schools and village panchayats.
xa: **Ponduru (Srikakulam)** khadi was famed nationally.
Women did **picketing** and **prohibition** work.

n7c871cba611.s: Which of the following activities was particularly associated with women’s participation in Andhra during the constructive programme?
n7c871cba611.x: Women in Andhra participated in picketing and prohibition work as part of the constructive programme.
n7c871cba611.tq: Link a social activity with the relevant regional participant group.
xs: **Picketing and prohibition work** — option **(1)**.
The **Muddiman Committee** and blocking the **Finance Bill** were Swarajist legislative actions.
xa: At the **Kakinada Congress (1923)** women served as executive members and volunteers.
**Ponduru (Srikakulam)** khadi was famous.

n0469708a636.s: The Belgaum session of the Indian National Congress (1924) is notable because:
o: It was the only Congress session presided over by Mahatma Gandhi
It adopted the Purna Swaraj resolution
It approved the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement
It was the first session presided over by a woman
n0469708a636.x: Belgaum 1924 was the only INC session presided over by Gandhi, and it reunited the Swarajists and No-Changers. Purna Swaraj was adopted at Lahore (1929); the NCM was suspended at Bardoli (1922); the first woman President was Annie Besant (1917).
xs: **Belgaum 1924** was the **only INC session presided by Gandhi** — option **(1)**.
It is the notes' **FIRST/LAST** fact for Belgaum; the other options are not linked to it in the notes.
xa: Belgaum reunited the **Swarajists** and **No-Changers**.
Council work and constructive work proved **complementary**.

nbd4a78842b6.s: The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared by the committee of the All Parties Conference under the chairmanship of:
nbd4a78842b6.x: The committee that prepared the Nehru Report was chaired by Motilal Nehru. Jawaharlal Nehru served as its secretary.
nbd4a78842b6.tq: Distinguish the chairman from the secretary in a committee-based question.
xs: The Nehru Report committee was chaired by **Motilal Nehru** — option **(2)**.
**Jawaharlal Nehru** was its **secretary**, not chairman.
It was an **All Parties Conference** committee and asked for **dominion status**.
xa: The **Calcutta 1928** session accepted the Report with a **one-year ultimatum**.
When it lapsed, **Lahore (Dec 1929)**, under **Jawaharlal Nehru**, adopted **Purna Swaraj**.
⚠ Trap: crediting **Calcutta 1928** with Purna Swaraj is WRONG.

n72497c7f876.s: The Lahore Session of the Congress (December 1929) adopted:
n72497c7f876.x: With the one-year Calcutta ultimatum expired, the Lahore Session rejected Dominion Status and adopted Purna Swaraj.
xa: Lahore resolved that **26 January** be observed every year as **Independence Day**.
CWC was authorised to launch **Civil Disobedience**; the **RTC** was boycotted.

n3faedbdc636.s: Who presided over the Lahore session of the Congress in December 1929?
n3faedbdc636.x: Jawaharlal Nehru presided at Lahore and hoisted the tricolour on the banks of the Ravi; Motilal Nehru chaired the Nehru Report committee.
xa: First Independence Day: **26 January 1930**.
CWC was authorised to launch **Civil Disobedience**.

na7a5a9b84f5.s: Who was the first woman arrested in Nellore in connection with the national movement?
na7a5a9b84f5.x: Paturi Balasaraswatamma was the first woman arrested in Nellore in connection with the national movement.
na7a5a9b84f5.tq: Match the specific Andhra district with its associated woman activist.
xs: **Paturi Balasaraswatamma** — option **(2)**.
**Maganti Annapurna** gave her jewellery; **Palakojeti Shyamalamba** was from E. Godavari.
xa: Women jailed: **Bharati Devi Ranga**, **Digumarti Janakamma**, **Khammampati Manikyamba** (with a six-month-old baby).
**Duvvuri Subbamma** (East Godavari) was jailed in the CDM.

nd80657fdfb2.s: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact, also called the Delhi Pact, was signed on:
nd80657fdfb2.x: The Pact was signed on 5 March 1931; dating it to March 1930 is a known trap (the Dandi March was then just beginning). 23 March 1931 is the execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru; 24 September 1932 is the Poona Pact.
xs: Signed **5 March 1931** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Dating it to March **1930** is WRONG.
**23 March 1931** = execution of **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru**; **24 Sept 1932** = **Poona Pact**.
xa: Also called the **Delhi Pact**; the CWC authorised Gandhi.
Gandhi then attended the **2nd RTC** (**1931**).

n4a66d8f4e20.s: The Poona Pact was signed in:
n4a66d8f4e20.x: The Poona Pact was signed in September 1932; the Communal Award was announced in August 1932.
xa: The Simon Commission arrived on **3 Feb 1928**.
First RTC: **Nov 1930**.

n5e602f33864.s: The second phase of the Civil Disobedience Movement, covering 1932–1934, failed mainly because of
o: Lack of any participation by peasants
Acceptance of the Communal Award by Gandhi
The absence of a Karachi Congress Session
n5e602f33864.x: The second phase of the Civil Disobedience Movement, from 1932 to 1934, failed under repression.
n5e602f33864.tq: Match the phase with its stated cause of failure.
xs: **Repression** — option **(4)**.
The second phase (**1932-34**) began when the CDM resumed in **Jan 1932** and Gandhi was arrested.
xa: **1934**: CDM crushed and withdrawn.
The Pact was also attacked for not saving **Bhagat Singh**.

nindian-history-111-5.s: On which date was the national flag hoisted on the Ravi as part of the Complete Independence declaration?
nindian-history-111-5.x: Jawaharlal Nehru hoisted the tricolour on the banks of the Ravi at Lahore at midnight on 31 December 1929. 26 January 1930 was the later Purna Swaraj Day.
nindian-history-111-5.tq: Discriminate the flag hoisting from Purna Swaraj Day.
n: The flag-hoisting and Complete Independence declaration occurred on 31 December 1929. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The flag-hoisting and Complete Independence declaration occurred at Lahore. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The national flag was hoisted on the Ravi during the Complete Independence declaration. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
Purna Swaraj Day was observed on 26 January 1930. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
xs: The national flag was hoisted on the **Ravi** on **31 December 1929** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Jawaharlal Nehru**, president of the **Lahore Session**, hoisted it with the **Complete Independence** declaration.
**26 January 1930** was the later **Purna Swaraj Day** — the **first Independence Day**, not the flag-hoisting date.
xa: The Lahore Session also authorised the CWC to launch **Civil Disobedience** and boycotted the **RTC**; Viceroy was **Lord Irwin**.
The **Calcutta 1928** session had accepted the **Nehru Report** with a **one-year ultimatum**.
⚠ **Purna Swaraj** was adopted only at **Lahore** — crediting Calcutta 1928 is wrong.
AP angle: **Bulusu Sambamurthy** (East Godavari) passed a Purna Swaraj resolution at district level first.

n35be1fa9e36.s: Which of the following was central among Gandhi's demands addressed to Viceroy Irwin before the Dandi March?
o: Acceptance of the Nehru Report without change
Immediate convening of the Third Round Table Conference
n35be1fa9e36.x: Abolition of the salt tax was a central demand in Gandhi's eleven-point letter to Viceroy Irwin. Irwin did not accept the demands.
n35be1fa9e36.tq: Identify the policy demand directly connected with the chosen symbol of protest.
xs: **Abolition of the salt tax** was central — option **(1)**.
It was part of Gandhi's **11 demands** to **Irwin** (letter of **30 Jan 1930**); Irwin refused.
xa: The ultimatum was sent/ignored on **2 March 1930**.
Why salt: a **universal necessity** of rich and poor; the salt tax was the most visible face of colonial exploitation.

n07e9ed350d6.s: Who was the only Telugu marcher among Gandhi's followers in the Dandi March?
n07e9ed350d6.x: Yerneni, also written Erneni, Subrahmanyam of Krishna district was the only Telugu marcher among Gandhi's followers in the Dandi March.
n07e9ed350d6.tq: Distinguish the Telugu participant in the march from Andhra leaders associated with other activities.
xs: **Yerneni (Erneni) Subrahmanyam** of **Krishna district** — option **(3)**.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** led Kakinada; **Thota Narsayya** hoisted the flag at Machilipatnam; **Maganti Annapurna** gave her jewellery.
xa: He later founded an ashram at **Komaravolu**.
The march had **78** followers.

nd5f078bdf33.s: Why did Gandhi choose salt as the central symbol of the Civil Disobedience Movement?
o: It was produced exclusively in Gujarat.
It was used only by the urban middle classes.
It was a universal necessity and the salt tax visibly represented colonial exploitation.
It was connected with the demand for separate electorates.
nd5f078bdf33.x: Salt was consumed by both rich and poor, and the salt tax and monopoly made it a visible symbol of colonial economic exploitation.
nd5f078bdf33.tq: Choose the option that combines the social reach and political significance of salt.
xs: Salt was a **universal necessity** and the salt tax visibly represented **colonial exploitation** — option **(3)**.
It was used by **rich and poor** alike, and the **salt tax/monopoly** was the most visible face of colonial taxation.
xa: Abolition of the salt tax was central to the **11 demands**.
The CDM was the **first mass law-breaking**.

n110a3dbff18.s: Gandhi named which person as the first successor to lead the movement after his arrest during the Salt Satyagraha?
n110a3dbff18.x: Abbas Tyabji was designated as Gandhi's first successor after his arrest. Sarojini Naidu was named the second successor.
n110a3dbff18.tq: Read the sequence carefully when two leaders are both associated with succession.
xs: **Abbas Tyabji** was the first successor — option **(2)**.
**Sarojini Naidu** was second, and led the **Dharasana** raid.
xa: **Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay** led women into the Salt Satyagraha.
**Kasturba Gandhi** joined protests and was imprisoned.

nddd8622e225.s: The first Indian woman to preside over the Indian National Congress was:
nddd8622e225.x: Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President of the Congress. She presided over the Kanpur session in 1925.
nddd8622e225.tq: Separate nationality from gender by comparing the first woman president with the first Indian woman president.
xs: **Sarojini Naidu at Kanpur in 1925** — option **(4)**.
She was the **first Indian woman INC president**, and also led the **Dharasana** raid.
xa: She was Gandhi's **second** successor, after **Abbas Tyabji**.
⚠ **Aruna Asaf Ali** = **Quit India (1942)**.

n589bb3b1719.s: Why did the Salt Satyagraha in Rayalaseema take place at Bellary under Kalluri Subbarao?
o: The Madras Government permitted salt manufacture there
Bellary was the headquarters of the Congress
The Andhra Salt Committee was based there
n589bb3b1719.x: Rayalaseema had no coast, so Kalluri Subbarao led the activity at Bellary instead of a coastal salt-making centre.
n589bb3b1719.tq: Apply the geographical condition to explain the choice of centre.
xs: **Rayalaseema had no coast** — option **(3)**.
So **Kalluri Subbarao** led it at **Bellary**.
xa: Coastal centres: **Machilipatnam**, **Kakinada**, **Mylapadu**, **Devarampadu**.
**Pedaganjam-Chinaganjam** was a famous salt coast.

n8198cf628f7.s: Who reported the beatings at the Dharasana Salt Works to the international public?
n8198cf628f7.x: The beatings at Dharasana were reported by Webb Miller, a United States journalist.
n8198cf628f7.tq: Test the eyewitness separately from the political leader.
xs: **Webb Miller**, a US journalist — option **(1)**.
The beatings were at the **Dharasana Salt Works** raid led by **Sarojini Naidu**.
xa: She led it after **Abbas Tyabji**'s arrest.
Other centres: **Peshawar** (Red Shirts), **Sanikatta** (Karnataka coast).

n9f57392f4ee.s: The Khudai Khidmatgars organised their Civil Disobedience protests particularly in
n9f57392f4ee.x: The Khudai Khidmatgars, or Red Shirts, led non-violent protests in Peshawar and the North-West Frontier Province. The Qissa Khwani firing occurred there in April 1930.
n9f57392f4ee.tq: Associate the organisation with its regional field of action.
xs: **Peshawar and the NWFP** — option **(2)**.
**Khudai Khidmatgars / Red Shirts** were founded by **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan** among Pathans.
xa: **Qissa Khwani** firing: **April 1930**.
**Garhwal Rifles** refused to fire on the Peshawar crowd (**1930**).

n4ccd9d59b5f.s: Who among the following was known as the ‘Frontier Gandhi’?
n4ccd9d59b5f.x: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was popularly known as the ‘Frontier Gandhi’ and was associated with the Khudai Khidmatgars.
xs: **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan** — option **(2)**.
He founded the **Khudai Khidmatgars (Red Shirts)** in the **NWFP**.
xa: **Konda Venkatappayya** was the Andhra salt satyagraha dictator.
**Qissa Khwani** firing, **April 1930**.

nfb1074554ca.s: The Garhwal Rifles became notable during the Civil Disobedience Movement because they
o: refused to fire on the crowd at Peshawar
led the salt march at Vedaranyam
nfb1074554ca.x: The Garhwal Rifles, associated with Chandra Singh Garhwali, refused to fire on the crowd at Peshawar in 1930.
nfb1074554ca.tq: Identify the distinctive action rather than the unit’s location alone.
xs: They **refused to fire** on the **Peshawar** crowd — option **(2)**.
They are linked to **Chandra Singh Garhwali** (**1930**).
xa: The Peshawar protests were by the **Khudai Khidmatgars**; **Qissa Khwani** firing, **April 1930**.
**Sarojini Naidu** led the **Dharasana** raid.

n040d9cb59d0.s: Sarojini Naidu led the raid at:
n040d9cb59d0.x: Sarojini Naidu led the raid at the Dharasana Salt Works after Gandhi's arrest.
n040d9cb59d0.tq: Separate the Civil Disobedience role from the Quit India role of the same leader.
xs: **Dharasana Salt Works** — option **(2)**.
She led it after **Abbas Tyabji**'s arrest.
**Gowalia Tank** is linked to **Aruna Asaf Ali** (**1942**).
xa: Beatings were reported by **Webb Miller**.
Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman INC president (**Kanpur 1925**).

ne5f823cc12d.s: The ‘Kattera Udyamam’ in Andhra was associated with
o: the formation of the Red Shirts
increased participation of women in the Salt Satyagraha
a campaign against the Cunningham Circular
the boycott of the Round Table Conference
ne5f823cc12d.x: The ‘Kattera Udyamam’, or scissors movement, helped raise women’s participation in the Andhra movement.
ne5f823cc12d.tq: Distinguish a local term by the social participation it promoted.
xs: **"Kattera Udyamam"** (scissors movement) **raised women's participation** — option **(2)**.
The **Red Shirts** were Ghaffar Khan's; the **Cunningham Circular** protests were in **Assam**.
xa: CDM was the first time women joined **in massive numbers**.
**Maganti Annapurna** gave all her jewellery.

ndb02fbadf1b.s: Who was designated as the dictator of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha?
ndb02fbadf1b.x: Konda Venkatappayya was the dictator of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha and had met Gandhi at Jambusar.
ndb02fbadf1b.tq: Distinguish the overall dictator from district-level leaders.
xs: **Konda Venkatappayya** — option **(2)**.
He met Gandhi at **Jambusar**.
**Pattabhi Sitaramayya** proposed the district camps; **Kaleswara Rao** led Machilipatnam; **Prakasam** led Madras/Devarampadu.
xa: Each district had its own dictator, war council and **sibiram**.
Konda Venkatappayya also led in **Guntur villages** with **Unnava Lakshminarayana**.

n337a54e6288.s: Which Salt Satyagraha camp was called the 'Andhra Dandi'?
n337a54e6288.x: Seethanagaram Ashram (Brahmajosyula Subrahmanyam), the East Godavari camp, was the 'Andhra Dandi'; Devarampadu was the 'Dakshina Dandi'.
xa: Vizag's camp: **Vizianagaram**; Krishna's: **Andhraratna Bhavan** and **Machilipatnam**.
⚠ **"Mecca"** = Machilipatnam.

n4368ca18763.s: Who conducted the first Salt Satyagraha at Machilipatnam?
n4368ca18763.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao conducted the first Salt Satyagraha at Machilipatnam. Pattabhi Sitaramayya called Machilipatnam his ‘Mecca’.
n4368ca18763.tq: Distinguish the first local satyagrahi from associated leaders.
xs: **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao** — option **(2)**.
Pattabhi called Machilipatnam his **"Mecca"**.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** = Kakinada; **Oruganti Venkatasubbayya** = Mylapadu; **Kalluri Subbarao** = Bellary.
xa: **Thota Narsayya ("Jenda Narsayya")** hoisted the flag at Machilipatnam.
Krishna district camps: **Andhraratna Bhavan** and **Machilipatnam**.

ne3a589a0d35.s: Under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, Gandhi agreed to attend which Round Table Conference?
ne3a589a0d35.x: Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and attend the Second Round Table Conference.
xa: Irwin also refused a **public inquiry** into police excesses.
Irwin agreed: release of non-violent prisoners; coastal villagers may make **salt for own use**.

n58e01b9607c.s: Who wrote the patriotic song ‘Bharata Swarajya Yuddham’?
n58e01b9607c.tq: Match the literary work with its author.
xs: **Jagganna Sastri** — option **(2)**.
**Adavi Bapiraju** wrote songs in jail; **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary** wrote "**Veeragandhamu**".
xa: Veeragandhamu — APPSC **2012** key: **CDM**.
⚠ An APPSC **2019** question tied Veeragandhamu to NCM.

nfd4f756d271.s: Who were the mediators associated with the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
o: Madan Mohan Malaviya and Jawaharlal Nehru
Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar
nfd4f756d271.x: Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar acted as mediators in the negotiations leading to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
xs: **Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar** — option **(3)**.
**V.S. Srinivasa Sastri** also mediated.
xa: Signed **5 March 1931** (**Delhi Pact**).
⚠ Dating it to March **1930** is WRONG.

nc9584ab6bc9.s: The Karachi Session of the Indian National Congress held in March 1931 was presided over by
nc9584ab6bc9.x: Vallabhbhai Patel presided over the Karachi Session of the Congress in March 1931.
nc9584ab6bc9.tq: Link the session with its presiding president.
xs: **Vallabhbhai Patel** — option **(3)**.
The **Karachi session (March 1931)** endorsed the pact.
xa: It passed resolutions on **Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme**.
Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru were executed on **23 Mar 1931**.

n71cf874e9b1.s: Who was the first to pass a Purna Swaraj resolution at the district level in Andhra Pradesh?
n71cf874e9b1.x: Bulusu Sambamurthy of East Godavari was associated with the first district-level Purna Swaraj resolution in Andhra Pradesh.
n71cf874e9b1.tq: Use the place-name clue to identify the associated Andhra leader.
xs: **Bulusu Sambamurthy** (East Godavari) passed a Purna Swaraj resolution at district level first — option **(4)**.
He got it passed at a district meeting **before Lahore**.
**Yerneni Subrahmanyam** was the only Telugu Dandi marcher; **Thota Narsayya** hoisted the flag at Machilipatnam.
xa: Sambamurthy also led the salt satyagraha at **Kakinada** (**Chollangi**).
**Lahore** passed the Purna Swaraj resolution on **31 Dec 1929**.

n702ef681b21.s: The patriotic song 'Veeragandhamu Techhinaramu... Veerulevvaro Telpudee' by Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary is associated with which movement?
n702ef681b21.x: The APPSC 2012 key ties the song to the Civil Disobedience Movement. Linking it to the NCM (as an APPSC 2019 question did) is the known trap; Quit India and Vandemataram are unrelated to this song.
xs: **Civil Disobedience Movement** — option **(2)** (APPSC **2012** key).
⚠ An APPSC **2019** question tied it to NCM — a known trap.
xa: Author: **Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary**.
Other CDM songs: **Bharata Swarajya Yuddham** (**Jagganna Sastri**); jail songs by **Adavi Bapiraju**.

n926e6318657.s: In which year did the Cripps Mission come to India?
n926e6318657.x: The Cripps Mission came in 1942, after Chauri Chaura (1922), the Lahore Session (1929) and the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931).
xa: This mirrors the APPSC G2 **2025** order (with **Poona Pact, 1932**).
NCM was withdrawn in **Feb 1922** after Chauri Chaura.

n5ef0f63697f.s: Who was appointed by the Andhra Congress Committee as the Dictator for Andhra during the Civil Disobedience Movement?
n5ef0f63697f.x: Konda Venkatappaiah was appointed as the Dictator for Andhra and became the first leader of the Civil Disobedience Movement in Andhra.
n5ef0f63697f.tq: Use the leader–role association and distinguish the regional dictator from district-level leaders.
xs: The Andhra Congress Committee made **Konda Venkatappaiah** the **Dictator** — option **(4)**.
He was the **first leader of CDM in Andhra** (APPSC **2008** and **2017** keys).
**Kaleswara Rao** led at **Machilipatnam**; **Kalluri Subbarao** at **Bellary**; **Bulusu Sambamurthy** at **Chollangi**.
xa: Each district had its own dictator, **war council** and camp (**shibiram**).
Camps: **Guntur**, **Pallepadu Ashram** (Nellore), **Bellary** (Rayalaseema), **Vedavanam** (Madras).

nb84541d7b48.s: Each district during the Civil Disobedience Movement in Andhra had its own:
nb84541d7b48.x: Every district had its own dictator, war council and camp, known as a shibiram.
nb84541d7b48.tq: Test the distinctive organisational structure rather than a prominent individual.
xs: Each district had its own **dictator, war council and camp** — option **(3)**.
The camp was called a **shibiram**.
xa: Overall Andhra Dictator: **Konda Venkatappaiah**.
Programme: make salt, raid salt depots, **picket foreign-cloth shops**, **cut toddy palms**.

ndcb1f8b9be9.s: Which of the following was part of the Civil Disobedience programme in Andhra villages?
ndcb1f8b9be9.x: The programme included making salt, picketing foreign-cloth and toddy shops, cutting toddy palms and raiding salt depots.
xa: Also **picketing toddy and arrack shops**.
**Eluru National School** volunteers joined in **May 1930**.

nindian-history-23-13.s: Which tax was the main target of the Civil Disobedience Movement launched in 1930?
nindian-history-23-13.x: The salt tax was the main target of the Civil Disobedience Movement, launched with Gandhi's Dandi March in 1930.
n: Salt Tax was a major target of Gandhian protest. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
Gandhian protest against the Salt Tax was associated with the Civil Disobedience Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 82-84]
xa: **C. Rajagopalachari** led the **Vedaranyam Satyagraha** (Trichinopoly to Vedaranyam, **April 1930**).
**Dharasana**: **Sarojini Naidu** led the march on the salt works; **Webb Miller** (United Press) reported it.
Other salt leaders: **K. Kelappan** (Malabar), **Gopabandhu Chaudhuri** (Odisha), **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan** (NWFP).

n4467ecf896a.s: Who led the Salt Satyagraha at Visakhapatnam and Bhimunipatnam?
n4467ecf896a.x: Tenneti Viswanatham led the Salt Satyagraha at Visakhapatnam and Bhimunipatnam.
n4467ecf896a.tq: Match the leader to the pair of coastal centres, not merely to a district.
xs: **Tenneti Viswanatham** — option **(3)**.
**Bezawada Gopal Reddy** = **Mylapadu**; **Dandu Narayana Raju** = **Mattapalem**; **Ravi Narayana Reddy** = **Ramachandrapuram**.
xa: First Andhra salt satyagraha: **Machilipatnam, 6 Apr 1930**.
**Kasi Viswanadham** led at **Vadarevu** (Guntur coast).

n5b9b5a5d8ea.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya described which centre as his “Mecca” in connection with the Salt Satyagraha?
n5b9b5a5d8ea.x: Machilipatnam was associated with Pattabhi Sitaramayya, who referred to it as his “Mecca”.
n5b9b5a5d8ea.tq: Test the distinctive epithet attached to a specific centre.
xs: **Machilipatnam** — option **(4)**.
It was the **first** Andhra salt satyagraha, **6 Apr 1930** (Krishna district).
**Chollangi** = Bulusu; **Vadarevu** = Kasi Viswanadham; **Mylapadu** = Bezawada Gopal Reddy.
xa: Other leaders there: **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao**, **Mutnuri Krishna Rao**.
**Puranam Suri Sastry** bought the auctioned salt.

n5c7e4b6432c.s: Which was the first Salt Satyagraha centre in Andhra, beginning on 6 April 1930?
n5c7e4b6432c.x: Machilipatnam was the first Andhra Salt Satyagraha centre, beginning on 6 April 1930.
xa: Chollangi's satyagraha was also on **6 Apr 1930**.
Leaders: **Pattabhi Sitaramayya**, **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao**, **Mutnuri Krishna Rao**.

n1e441a27c96.s: At Machilipatnam, who was injured while raising the flag at Tilak Chowk?
n1e441a27c96.x: Thota Narsayya, popularly known as “Jenda Narsayya”, was injured while raising the flag at Tilak Chowk in Machilipatnam.
n1e441a27c96.tq: Distinguish the person injured during flag-hoisting from those arrested or involved in the salt auction.
xs: **Thota Narsayya** ("**Jenda Narsayya**") — option **(3)**.
He was hurt raising the flag at **Tilak Chowk**, Machilipatnam.
**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** was arrested; **Puranam Suri Sastry** bought the auctioned salt.
xa: He had hoisted the flag at Machilipatnam on **26 Jan 1930**.
**Venneti Satyanarayana** faced a lathi charge at **Rajahmundry**.

nac8ad3c62fd.s: Who led twenty women to make salt at the High Court beach in Madras?
nac8ad3c62fd.x: Durgabai Deshmukh led twenty women in making salt at the High Court beach in Madras.
nac8ad3c62fd.tq: Use the specific numerical detail to distinguish this action from other women's roles.
xs: **Durgabai Deshmukh** — option **(1)**.
She led **20 women** to make salt at the **High Court beach, Madras**.
**Rukmini Lakshmipathi** was the first woman arrested; **Unnava Lakshmibayamma** ran the **Swarajya Lakshmi Vratam**.
xa: **Duvvuri Subbamma** was among the first at Chollangi; jailed in Nellore.
National CDM women: **Kamaladevi**, **Kasturba**, **Maniben Patel**.

n2650a83ba1e.s: Which of the following describes women's role in the Andhra Civil Disobedience Movement?
o: They took part only in symbolic gatherings
They joined in large numbers, making salt, picketing and courting imprisonment
Their role was confined to national leaders outside Andhra
n2650a83ba1e.x: The Civil Disobedience Movement brought women into the Andhra struggle in large numbers, including salt-making, picketing and imprisonment.
xa: First woman arrested: **Rukmini Lakshmipathi**.
**Duvvuri Subbamma** was jailed in **Nellore**.

n2d83202d642.s: Who led the Khudai Khidmatgar-linked Salt Satyagraha in the North-West Frontier Province?
n2d83202d642.x: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan led the movement in the NWFP through the Khudai Khidmatgar organisation.
n2d83202d642.tq: Connect the regional movement with its associated organisation and leader.
xs: **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan** — option **(4)**.
He led through the **Khudai Khidmatgar**.
**Gopabandhu Chaudhuri** = Odisha; **K. Kelappan** = Malabar; **Abbas Tyabji** = first declared satyagrahi.
xa: **Sarojini Naidu** led **Dharasana**.
**Rajaji** led **Vedaranyam**.

ncef49c5370c.s: The non-violent march on the Dharasana Salt Works was led by ____ and reported to the world by ____.
ncef49c5370c.x: Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana march, where volunteers took unarmed beatings, and Webb Miller of United Press reported it. Abbas Tyabji had been arrested before it; Kamaladevi led women into the Salt Satyagraha elsewhere; Louis Fischer was not the reporter.
xs: **Sarojini Naidu; Webb Miller** — option **(2)**.
Volunteers took **unarmed beatings**; **Webb Miller** (**United Press**) reported it.
**Abbas Tyabji** was the first declared satyagrahi, not the Dharasana leader.
xa: Sarojini Naidu was the **second** declared satyagrahi.
National CDM women: **Kamaladevi**, **Kasturba**, **Maniben Patel**.

n521a082da33.s: How many followers accompanied Gandhi on the Dandi March (12 March–6 April 1930)?
n521a082da33.x: Gandhi marched with 78 followers, covering about 240 miles.
xa: Only Telugu marcher: **Yerneni Subramanyam**.
Gandhi's letter with **11 demands** to **Irwin**: **2 Mar 1930**.

nc0590991fd8.s: Who was identified as the only Telugu marcher in the Dandi March?
nc0590991fd8.x: Yerneni Subramanyam was identified as the only Telugu marcher in the Dandi March.
nc0590991fd8.tq: Test the regional identity attached to a participant in a national event.
xs: **Yerneni Subramanyam** — option **(4)**.
**Thota Narsayya** hoisted the flag at Machilipatnam; **Kalluri Subbarao** led at Bellary; **Venneti Satyanarayana** was lathi-charged at Rajahmundry.
xa: Dandi: **78** followers, **240 miles**.
Machilipatnam's salt satyagraha came on **6 Apr 1930**, the day Dandi ended.

n1b14a3c7ca3.s: Which Viceroy was associated with the repression of the Civil Disobedience Movement during 1932–34?
n1b14a3c7ca3.x: Lord Willingdon was the Viceroy during the repression of the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1932–34. Lord Irwin was associated with the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
n1b14a3c7ca3.tq: Discriminate between the Viceroy associated with the pact and the Viceroy associated with repression.
xs: **Lord Willingdon** — option **(4)**.
**Irwin** is linked with the **pact** (**1931**).
xa: ⚠ Some notes date the pact "March **1930**" — the pact was **1931**.
CDM revived **Jan 1932**; **Berhampore firing**, **15 Jan 1932**.

na4f1d2ea4fd.s: Which of the following was included in the Karachi resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme?
o: Separate electorates for the depressed classes
na4f1d2ea4fd.x: The Karachi resolution included civil liberties, universal adult franchise, religious neutrality and free primary education.
xa: Economic side of the same resolution: **rent/revenue cuts**, **debt relief**, **state control of key industries**.
Karachi was presided over by **Vallabhbhai Patel** and endorsed the **Gandhi-Irwin (Delhi) Pact**.
The resolution foreshadowed **Part III** (Fundamental Rights) and the **Directive Principles** of the Constitution.

nd76064e1a88.s: The Karachi Congress Session was held shortly after the execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru. The Congress leadership at the session
o: withdrew the resolution on Fundamental Rights
celebrated political violence as the official method of struggle
admired their bravery while disapproving of political violence
nd76064e1a88.x: The Congress admired the courage of the three revolutionaries but disapproved of political violence as a method.
nd76064e1a88.tq: Separate admiration for individual bravery from endorsement of a method of struggle.
xs: At Karachi the Congress **admired the bravery** of **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru** while **disapproving of political violence** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It neither celebrated violence (3) nor withdrew the Fundamental Rights resolution (1) — that resolution was in fact adopted there.
xa: The session (**March 1931**) was held days after their execution; president **Vallabhbhai Patel**.
Karachi endorsed the **Gandhi-Irwin (Delhi) Pact** and reiterated **Purna Swaraj**.
The **Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme** resolution was drafted by **Jawaharlal Nehru**.

n599cbd58158.s: The Karachi resolution of 1931 foreshadowed which parts of the Constitution of India?
n599cbd58158.x: The Karachi resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme foreshadowed Part III (Fundamental Rights) and Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy).
xa: The resolution was drafted by **Jawaharlal Nehru**; the session was presided over by **Vallabhbhai Patel** (**March 1931**).
Similar constitutional link: the **Poona Pact** = root of reserved seats (**Arts. 330, 332**).

nindian-history-111-18.s: 'Purna Swaraj', adopted as the Congress goal, meant:
nindian-history-111-18.x: Purna Swaraj meant Complete Independence as the Congress goal.
n: The Purna Swaraj Resolution adopted Complete Independence as the Congress goal. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Fundamental Rights resolution addressed civil liberties. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Fundamental Rights resolution addressed citizens' rights. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Economic Programme addressed labour welfare. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Economic Programme addressed economic justice. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Swadeshi and Boycott movement promoted the boycott of foreign goods. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
The Swadeshi and Boycott movement promoted indigenous goods. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #111 · pp 205-207]
xa: The **Karachi Session** (**1931**) was presided by **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**; **Jawaharlal Nehru** drafted the resolution.
It was held days after the execution of **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru** and endorsed the **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**.
Political provisions included **universal adult franchise** and **free primary education**.
The Karachi resolution foreshadowed **Part III** and the **Directive Principles**.

n44e17db3228.s: Who was the sole representative of the Congress at the Second Round Table Conference (1931)?
n44e17db3228.x: Gandhi was the sole Congress representative; Sarojini Naidu represented Indian women and Malaviya also attended.
xa: **V.V. Jogayya Pantulu** went from Andhra to assist Gandhi; the **separate-Andhra resolution** was handed to Gandhi there.
The conference ended in deadlock; **MacDonald** threatened a **unilateral award**.
⚠ Trap: the 2nd RTC was in **1931**, not 1932; it was the **only RTC Gandhi attended**.

nab7318355a1.s: Which Andhra leader went to the Second Round Table Conference (1931) to assist Gandhi, where a resolution for a separate Andhra was handed to Gandhi?
nab7318355a1.x: V.V. Jogayya Pantulu went to assist Gandhi at RTC-2, and the separate-Andhra resolution was handed to Gandhi there. Konda Venkatappayya, Pattabhi Sitaramayya and Prakasam were Andhra leaders of the CDM but are not named for RTC-2.
xs: **V.V. Jogayya Pantulu** went to the Second RTC to assist Gandhi — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **separate-Andhra resolution** was handed to Gandhi there; Andhra leaders used RTC-2 to press for a **separate Andhra province**.
xa: Gandhi was the **sole Congress representative** at RTC-2 (**1931**).
Other participants: **Sarojini Naidu** (Indian women), **Muhammad Iqbal** (Muslims), **Malaviya**, **Ambedkar**, **Jinnah**, **Aga Khan**.
Post-CDM Telugu works: **Bharat Swarajya Yuddham** (**Jagannadh Shastry**), **Navayuga Gandhi** (**Damaraju Pundarikakshudu**).

n616c786bc5f.s: The Second Round Table Conference failed primarily because of disagreement over
o: separate electorates for minorities and the depressed classes
the venue of the Third Round Table Conference
n616c786bc5f.x: The conference ended in a deadlock over separate electorates for minorities and the depressed classes. MacDonald subsequently threatened to make a unilateral award.
n616c786bc5f.tq: Identify the central issue rather than a peripheral conference topic.
xs: RTC-2 broke down in **deadlock** over **separate electorates for minorities and the depressed classes** — so option **(2)** is correct.
After the deadlock **MacDonald** threatened a **unilateral award**.
xa: **Gandhi** was the **sole Congress representative**; **Muhammad Iqbal** spoke for the **Muslims**, **Sarojini Naidu** for **Indian women**.
Gandhi returned **empty-handed** in **Jan 1932**; Viceroy **Lord Willingdon** struck first and Gandhi was arrested.
The **Poona Pact** is the root of reserved seats in **Arts. 330, 332**.

n294f7e34321.s: The only Round Table Conference that Gandhi attended was the:
n294f7e34321.x: Gandhi attended only the Second RTC, held in 1931. Listing the Second RTC under 1932 is a known trap; the First RTC (1930) was boycotted by the Congress and Gandhi did not attend the Third (1932).
xs: Gandhi attended only the **Second RTC, 1931** — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Option (3) is the trap: listing the 2nd RTC under **1932** is wrong — it was **1931**.
At RTC-2 Gandhi was the **sole Congress representative**.
xa: Other participants: **Sarojini Naidu** (Indian women), **Muhammad Iqbal** (Muslims), **Malaviya**, **Ambedkar**, **Jinnah**, **Aga Khan**.
The conference ended in **deadlock**; **MacDonald** threatened a **unilateral award**.
Gandhi returned empty-handed in **Jan 1932** and the CDM was resumed.

n03a658be114.s: After mass Civil Disobedience was suspended on 14 July 1933, the movement was formally withdrawn in:
n03a658be114.x: The movement was formally withdrawn in April 1934, and the Congress then contested the 1934 Central Assembly elections.
xa: Resumption: **Jan 1932**, after Gandhi returned empty-handed from RTC-2; Viceroy **Lord Willingdon** arrested him and banned the Congress.
**15 Jan 1932**: firing on satyagrahis at **Berhampur**.
Post-CDM Telugu works: **Bharat Swarajya Yuddham** (**Jagannadh Shastry**), **Navayuga Gandhi** (**Damaraju Pundarikakshudu**).

n8b40eedc653.s: Who joined the Muslim League's observance of the 'Day of Deliverance' in Bombay on 22 December 1939?
n8b40eedc653.x: B.R. Ambedkar joined the observance of the Muslim League's Day of Deliverance in Bombay on 22 December 1939.
n8b40eedc653.tq: Match the participant with the specific political observance.
xs: **B.R. Ambedkar** joined the League's **"Day of Deliverance"** event in **Bombay** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The League observed it on **22 December 1939**, celebrating the resignation of the **Congress ministries** (**Oct-Nov 1939**).
xa: The ministries resigned because India was dragged into the war **without consultation**.
Next on the timeline: **Ramgarh** Congress session (**March 1940**), then the **August Offer** (**August 1940**).

nb658a944c6d.s: The August Offer of 1940 was made by:
nb658a944c6d.x: The August Offer was made by Viceroy Lord Linlithgow in August 1940.
nb658a944c6d.tq: Match the constitutional proposal with the Viceroy who announced it.
xs: The August Offer was made by Viceroy **Lord Linlithgow** in **August 1940** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It came when **Britain was losing in Europe**; **Sir Stafford Cripps** (3) led the separate mission of **March 1942**.
xa: Proposals: a **constitution-making body after the war**, more Indians in the **Viceroy's Executive Council**, a **War Advisory Council**.
It answered **Ramgarh** (**March 1940**) — ⚠ Ramgarh came BEFORE the Offer.
**Nehru** called Dominion Status **"dead as a doornail"**; Congress **rejected** the Offer.

n0190dd4710a.s: Individual Satyagraha was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on:
n0190dd4710a.tq: Distinguish the exact launch date from nearby wartime dates.
xs: Individual Satyagraha began on **17 October 1940** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**22 December 1939** (1) was the League's **Day of Deliverance**; **8 August 1942** (2) the **Quit India resolution**; **August 1940** (4) the **August Offer**.
xa: Gandhi launched it from **Paunar**, Wardha (also spelt "Palner").
Order of satyagrahis: **Vinoba Bhave** first, **Jawaharlal Nehru** second, **Brahma Dutt** third.
In **Bihar (1940)** it was led by **Shyam Narayan Singh**.

na5e38be8f10.s: From which place did Vinoba Bhave commence Individual Satyagraha?
na5e38be8f10.x: Vinoba Bhave commenced Individual Satyagraha from Paunar in Wardha.
na5e38be8f10.tq: Match the movement's starting place with its associated district.
xs: Individual Satyagraha was launched from **Paunar in Wardha** (also spelt **"Palner"**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Acharya Vinoba Bhave** was the **first satyagrahi**; launch date **17 October 1940**.
**Ramgarh in Bihar** (4) was the venue of the Congress session of **March 1940**, not of the satyagraha.
xa: Second satyagrahi: **Jawaharlal Nehru**; third: **Brahma Dutt**.
Aim: assert **freedom of speech against the war**, not mass mobilisation.
The government arrested **Vinoba**, **Nehru** and **Patel**.

n7f375b13c91.s: The failure of the Cripps Mission was followed directly by which major movement?
n7f375b13c91.x: The failure of the Cripps Mission directly contributed to the launch of the Quit India Movement in August 1942.
n7f375b13c91.tq: Link the failed constitutional negotiation with its immediate political outcome.
xs: The failure of Cripps led directly to the **Quit India Movement (August 1942)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Individual Satyagraha** (2) came earlier, from **17 October 1940**.
xa: The **Quit India resolution** was passed at **Bombay** on **8 Aug 1942**.
Talks broke down over Cripps's **"take it or leave it"** attitude and **Churchill's sabotage**.
Both Congress and League **rejected** the plan.

n98c1c8ec440.s: The Ramgarh session of the Congress, held between the resignation of the ministries and the August Offer, took place in:
n98c1c8ec440.x: The ministries resigned in October–November 1939, the Ramgarh session was in March 1940, the August Offer in August 1940 and the Cripps Mission in March–April 1942.
xa: Next: **Quit India resolution**, **8 Aug 1942**, Bombay; **Desai-Liaquat Pact**, **1945**.
**Cabinet Mission**: **March 1946**.

na3886a92e01.s: Which Viceroy declared India a party to the Second World War without consulting Indian leaders?
na3886a92e01.x: Lord Linlithgow's declaration led to the resignation of the Congress ministries in 1939.
xa: The Congress ministries resigned in **October-November 1939** in protest.
**B.R. Ambedkar** joined the Day of Deliverance event in **Bombay**.

nb10e779a01d.s: The Quit India resolution was passed on 8 August 1942 at:
nb10e779a01d.x: The Quit India resolution was passed at Bombay on 8 August 1942.
xs: The **Quit India resolution** was passed at **Bombay** on **8 Aug 1942** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Wardha** (1) is linked to **Paunar**, where Gandhi launched **Individual Satyagraha** in **1940**.
xa: The failure of the **Cripps Mission** led directly to Quit India.
Gandhi had used "Quit India" in **Harijan** in **April 1942**, amid rumours of Japanese bombing of **Vizag** and **Kakinada**.

nbc4374dea6a.s: The August Offer was significant because it constituted the first official British acceptance that:
o: Indians would frame their own constitution
Congress ministries could continue without wartime restrictions
The Muslim League alone represented Indian Muslims
nbc4374dea6a.x: The August Offer was the first official acceptance that Indians would frame their own constitution. The demand had been raised by M.N. Roy in 1934 and officially adopted by Congress in 1935.
nbc4374dea6a.tq: Identify the constitutional principle represented by the offer.
xs: The August Offer was the **first official acceptance** that **Indians would frame their own constitution** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It proposed a representative **constitution-making body after the war**.
**M.N. Roy** had raised the Constituent Assembly demand in **1934**; Congress made it official in **1935**.
xa: Other proposals: more Indians in the **Viceroy's Executive Council**; a **War Advisory Council**; Dominion Status as goal; **minority veto**.
Contrast: the **Cripps Mission** first conceded the **provincial opt-out** — germ of Partition.
Congress **rejected** the Offer; Nehru: Dominion Status **"dead as a doornail"**.

n53abf1c3604.s: The August Offer was made in response to which earlier Congress position?
o: Demand for a separate Muslim homeland
Demand for the immediate abolition of all provincial legislatures
Support for the war if a provisional national government were formed at the Centre
n53abf1c3604.x: The August Offer responded to the Ramgarh Congress position that support for the war could be extended if a provisional national government were formed at the Centre.
n53abf1c3604.tq: Connect the offer with the political demand it was intended to answer.
xs: The August Offer answered **Ramgarh**'s offer of **support for the war if a provisional national government were formed at the Centre** — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ **Ramgarh (March 1940)** came BEFORE the **August Offer (August 1940)**; the Cripps proposals (2) came only in **1942**.
xa: Ramgarh session was held in **Bihar**.
The Offer was made by Viceroy **Lord Linlithgow**; Congress **rejected** it.
Proposals: post-war **constitution-making body**, more Indians in the **Executive Council**, **War Advisory Council**.

n7c7198e4a17.s: The immediate objective of Individual Satyagraha was to:
o: Mobilise the entire population for an armed revolt
Establish a provisional government at the Centre
Assert freedom of speech against assisting the British war effort
n7c7198e4a17.x: The movement aimed to assert freedom of speech and oppose the view that India should help the British war effort with men or money. Selected individuals made anti-war speeches and courted arrest successively.
n7c7198e4a17.tq: Apply the stated objective to distinguish limited protest from mass mobilisation.
xs: The aim was to **assert freedom of speech against the war** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was **not mass mobilisation** (1): selected individuals made **anti-war speeches** and courted arrest one after another.
Gandhi's line: **"It is wrong to help the British war effort with men or money."**
xa: Launched **17 October 1940** from **Paunar**, Wardha.
Satyagrahis in order: **Vinoba Bhave**, **Jawaharlal Nehru**, **Brahma Dutt**.
Exam angle: assertion-reason on why it was **"limited"** (**October 1940**).

nd8da0a72351.s: In the Individual Satyagraha of 1940, the first, second and third satyagrahis were respectively:
o: Jawaharlal Nehru, Vinoba Bhave, Brahma Dutt
Vinoba Bhave, Jawaharlal Nehru, Brahma Dutt
Vinoba Bhave, Vallabhbhai Patel, Jawaharlal Nehru
Brahma Dutt, Vinoba Bhave, Jawaharlal Nehru
nd8da0a72351.x: Acharya Vinoba Bhave was the first satyagrahi, Jawaharlal Nehru the second and Brahma Dutt the third (chosen for moral conviction, not political prominence). Patel was arrested but was not among the first three; the other options reorder the sequence.
xs: First **Vinoba Bhave**, second **Jawaharlal Nehru**, third **Brahma Dutt** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Brahma Dutt** was chosen to show **moral conviction, not political prominence**.
**Patel** (3) was arrested along with Vinoba and Nehru but was not one of the first three.
xa: Launch: **17 October 1940** from **Paunar**, Wardha.
**Ongole Municipality** condemned the arrests of **Vinoba, Nehru and Patel**.
Nehru was also a **Cripps negotiator** and called Dominion Status **"dead as a doornail"**.

nfd35ae299b5.s: Which of the following was NOT included in the August Offer?
o: Immediate transfer of defence to an Indian national government
An increase in Indian membership of the Viceroy's Executive Council
A representative constitution-making body after the war
nfd35ae299b5.x: The August Offer did not provide for immediate transfer of defence. It proposed a post-war constitution-making body, more Indians in the Executive Council and a War Advisory Council.
nfd35ae299b5.tq: Find the option that turns a limited proposal into an immediate transfer of power.
xs: **Immediate transfer of defence to an Indian national government** was not in the August Offer — so option **(1)** is correct.
The Offer proposed a representative **constitution-making body after the war** (4), more Indians in the **Viceroy's Executive Council** (3) and a **War Advisory Council** (2).
It kept **Dominion Status** as the goal with a **minority veto** — nothing on handing over defence.
xa: Made by **Lord Linlithgow** in **August 1940**, answering the **Ramgarh** offer.
⚠ Even the later **Cripps** plan kept **defence** and the army with **the British** in the interim.
Significance: **first official acceptance** that Indians would frame their own constitution.

ne4b842b248b.s: The Cripps proposals promised India ____ after the war.
ne4b842b248b.x: The proposals promised dominion status after the war and allowed the Indian Union the power to secede.
xa: Constitution-making body: a **Constituent Assembly after the war**.
**Provincial option** to stay out — Pakistan conceded in principle, the **"fatal flaw"**.
A **treaty** was to protect racial/religious minorities; **Governor-General's powers retained**.

n987cb670141.s: Which provision of the Cripps proposals was regarded as the 'fatal flaw' because it could lead to the formation of separate unions by provinces?
o: The retention of the Governor-General's powers
The provincial option to remain outside the proposed Indian Union
The creation of a War Advisory Council
n987cb670141.x: The proposal allowing unwilling provinces to form separate unions conceded the principle that later supported the demand for Pakistan and created the risk of balkanisation.
n987cb670141.tq: Link a constitutional provision with its political consequence.
xs: The **provincial option to remain outside the proposed Indian Union** was the **"fatal flaw"** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Any unwilling province/princely state could stay out and **form separate unions**, conceding **Pakistan in principle**.
Congress saw in it a **risk of Balkanisation**; it is called the **germ of Partition**.
xa: The **War Advisory Council** (3) belonged to the **August Offer**, not Cripps.
The **minority-protection treaty** (4) and the retained **Governor-General's powers** (1) were separate Cripps provisions.
⚠ The League still **rejected** Cripps: it wanted Pakistan conceded **explicitly**.

nbc7b04aafd7.s: Under the Cripps proposals, defence and control of the army during the interim period were to remain with:
nbc7b04aafd7.x: Defence and the army were to stay with Britain in the interim, and the Governor-General's powers were retained.
xa: Promise: **Dominion Status** with power to **secede**, after the war.
**Provincial option** to stay out — the "fatal flaw".
Congress objected to **no immediate transfer of power**.

nee5d6ca8cf3.s: Who were the Congress negotiators with the Cripps Mission?
nee5d6ca8cf3.x: Nehru and Azad negotiated for the Congress, which objected to the right to secede and to the absence of an immediate transfer of power.
xa: Congress also feared **Balkanisation** through the provincial option.
Gandhi called the offer a **"post-dated cheque"**; Nehru added **"on a crashing bank"**.
Failure led directly to the **Quit India Movement (August 1942)**.

nindian-history-130-18.s: What was the outcome of the Cripps proposals of 1942?
o: They led to an immediate interim government
They were accepted by the Congress
They were rejected and the negotiations failed
They were accepted by the Muslim League alone
nindian-history-130-18.x: The Cripps proposals, which offered post-war Dominion Status and let provinces opt out of the Union, were rejected and the talks failed.
n: The Cripps Mission offered Dominion Status after the war. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #130 · pp 233-234]
The Cripps Mission proposed that provinces could opt out of the proposed Union. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #130 · pp 233-234]
The Cripps Mission proposals were rejected. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #130 · pp 233-234]
The Cripps Mission negotiations failed. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #130 · pp 233-234]
xa: The constitution-making body was to be a **Constituent Assembly after the war**.
**Defence** and control of the army were to stay with **the British** in the interim.
⚠ Both **Congress** and the **League** rejected Cripps — for opposite reasons (no immediate power vs no explicit **Pakistan**).
The provincial opt-out was the "**fatal flaw**" — germ of **Partition**.

n4ba348419d5.s: The Cripps Mission was sent to India by the British Government primarily under pressure from which combination of leaders?
n4ba348419d5.x: The mission was sent by Winston Churchill's Government under pressure from United States President Franklin Roosevelt and China's Chiang Kai-shek.
n4ba348419d5.tq: Match the political pressure with the correct international leaders.
xs: Churchill sent Cripps under pressure from US President **Roosevelt** and China's **Chiang Kai-shek** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Winston Churchill** (2) was the PM who sent the mission and was later **accused of sabotage**; **Linlithgow** made the 1940 August Offer.
**Maulana Azad** and Nehru (3, 4) were the **Congress negotiators**, not those who pressed for the mission.
xa: Trigger: **Pearl Harbor 1941**; Malaya, Singapore overrun; **Rangoon fell March 1942**.
Cripps: **Labour Party**, member of Churchill's War Cabinet, **"take it or leave it"** attitude.

n229a9178a5b.s: Sir Stafford Cripps was a member of the
o: Labour Party and Churchill's War Cabinet
Liberal Party and Wavell's Executive Council
Communist Party and Churchill's War Cabinet
n229a9178a5b.x: Cripps was a Labour member of Churchill's War Cabinet. Churchill sent him to India in 1942 under international and military pressure.
n229a9178a5b.tq: Test the exact party and cabinet association instead of relying on the person's later political reputation.
xs: Cripps belonged to the **Labour Party** and was a member of **Churchill's War Cabinet** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He was criticised for a **"take it or leave it"** attitude.
xa: **Churchill** sent him under pressure from **Roosevelt** and **Chiang Kai-shek**; Churchill was accused of sabotage.
Cripps reached Delhi **22-23 March 1942**; returned **mid-April**.
Congress negotiators: **Nehru** and **Maulana Azad**.

ne3907255afe.s: The Muslim League rejected the Cripps proposals because they:
o: provided for an explicit and immediate Pakistan
transferred all defence powers to the League
accepted the idea of a single Indian Union and did not explicitly concede Pakistan
abolished the right of provinces to remain outside the Union
ne3907255afe.x: The Muslim League opposed the proposed single Indian Union and wanted Pakistan to be explicitly conceded rather than left as an indirect possibility through the provincial option.
ne3907255afe.tq: Distinguish the League's objection from the Congress objections to the same proposals.
xs: The League rejected Cripps because it **opposed a single Indian Union** and **wanted Pakistan conceded explicitly** — option **(3)** is correct.
The plan only conceded Pakistan **in principle** through the **provincial option**, not explicitly (1).
**Defence** stayed with **the British** in the interim, not with the League (2).
xa: ⚠ Both Congress AND League rejected Cripps — Congress for **no immediate power**, the League for **no explicit Pakistan**.
At the **August Offer** the League had welcomed the **minority veto** but wanted partition.

n9338857c393.s: The immediate failure of the Cripps Mission contributed to the Quit India Movement mainly because the Mission offered
o: A separate province for every linguistic group
n9338857c393.x: The Cripps Mission failed to satisfy Indian demands because it did not offer immediate self-government. Its failure in March–April 1942 became a major cause of the Quit India Movement.
n9338857c393.tq: Identify the precise deficiency in a political proposal rather than its general historical association.
xs: The Cripps Mission offered **no immediate self-government** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its failure in **March-April 1942** became a direct cause of Quit India (UPSC 2013: launched in response to the **Cripps Proposals**).
xa: Other causes: the **Japanese advance** (Malaya, Singapore overrun; **Rangoon** fell **March 1942**) and **economic distress** (rising prices, wartime shortages).
**14 July 1942**: CWC resolution at **Wardha**; **8 August 1942**: AICC ratified it at **Gowalia Tank Maidan**, Bombay.
**9 August 1942**: leaders arrested in **Operation Zero Hour**.
