nb393b1c5b87.s: Rangoon, whose fall formed part of the wartime background to Quit India, fell to Japan in:
nb393b1c5b87.x: Rangoon fell in March 1942 as the Japanese advance brought the war close to India's eastern frontier.
xa: Other causes: failure of the **Cripps Mission** (no immediate self-government) and **economic distress**.
Economic distress meant **rising prices** and **wartime shortages**.

nc04c434da36.s: The Quit India resolution adopted by the Congress Working Committee at Wardha on 14 July 1942 was proposed by:
nc04c434da36.x: The Wardha resolution was proposed by Nehru and seconded by Patel; the AICC ratified it at Bombay on 8 August 1942.
xa: Hence the names **"Wardha Resolution"** and **"August Resolution"**.
**9 August 1942**: pre-dawn arrests in **Operation Zero Hour**.
The Wardha resolution empowered **Gandhi** to lead a **non-violent mass movement**.

n4782a5f81e3.s: Which of the following was NOT a demand or feature of the resolution ratified by the AICC in August 1942?
o: Mass civil disobedience under Gandhi’s leadership
Continuation of British rule until the end of the Second World War
Formation of a provisional government after the British withdrawal
n4782a5f81e3.x: The resolution demanded the immediate end of British rule, envisaged a provisional government after withdrawal and authorised mass civil disobedience under Gandhi. It did not support continuation of British rule until the war ended.
n4782a5f81e3.tq: Reject the option that reverses the central demand of the resolution.
xs: **Continuation of British rule until the end of the war** was never demanded — so option **(3)** is the odd one out.
The AICC, Bombay demanded the **immediate end of British rule**, a **provisional government after the British left**, and **mass civil disobedience under Gandhi**.
xa: The AICC met on **8 August 1942** at **Gowalia Tank Maidan**.
It ratified the CWC's **Wardha** resolution of **14 July 1942**.
Gandhi's speech there: **"Do or Die"** ("Karo ya Maro").

nedbef80e794.s: The coinage of the slogan 'Quit India' is generally credited to:
nedbef80e794.x: Yusuf Meherally is generally credited with coining 'Quit India'; Gandhi suggested the phrase in Harijan in April 1942.
xa: The Harijan use came amid rumours of Japanese bombing of **Vizag** and **Kakinada**.
**"Do or Die"** ("Karo ya Maro") was Gandhi's slogan at **Gowalia Tank**, **8 Aug 1942**.

n0e56fbdefc0.s: In 1942, when Gandhi gave the 'Do or Die' call, his paper was:
n0e56fbdefc0.x: Gandhi's paper in 1942 was Harijan; Young India had ceased publication in 1932.
xa: Same speech: **"We shall either free India or die in the attempt"** (BPSC 2025).
"Quit India" was suggested by Gandhi in **Harijan** (**April 1942**); coinage credited to **Yusuf Meherally**.

n71deaa6af70.s: Operation Zero Hour during the Quit India Movement referred to
o: The pre-dawn arrest of Congress leaders on 9 August 1942
The imposition of a 21-day fast by Gandhi
The formation of Jatiya Sarkar at Tamluk
n71deaa6af70.x: Operation Zero Hour was the pre-dawn operation through which Congress leaders were arrested on 9 August 1942.
n71deaa6af70.tq: Match an operation name with its precise action and date.
xs: **Operation Zero Hour** was the **pre-dawn arrest of Congress leaders on 9 August 1942** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **fall of Rangoon** (1) was in **March 1942**; **Gandhi's 21-day fast** (3) was in **February 1943**; **Jatiya Sarkar** (4) was at **Tamluk**.
xa: After the arrests the movement became **leaderless and spontaneous**.
**CWC members** were held at **Ahmednagar Fort**.

nindian-history-112-4.s: Who said, 'Partition fell on us like a bomb'?
nindian-history-112-4.x: Surendranath Banerjee said the partition fell like a bomb; 'Swaraj is my birthright' was Tilak's and 'Do or Die' Gandhi's.
n: Bal Gangadhar Tilak said, “Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it.” [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #112 · pp 207-208]
Mahatma Gandhi said, “Do or Die.” [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #112 · pp 207-208]
Rabindranath Tagore said, “Political symptom of our social disease.” [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #112 · pp 207-208]
Surendranath Banerjee said, “Partition fell on us like a bomb.” [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #112 · pp 207-208]
xa: The **Partition of Bengal** occurred in **1905**.
"Back to the Vedas" — **Swami Dayanand Saraswati**; "Give me blood… freedom" — **Subhas Chandra Bose**.
"Swaraj should be for **common people**" — **C.R. Das**.

n18af581dcad.s: During the Quit India Movement, Gandhi instructed government servants to:
o: Stay in service but pledge loyalty to the Congress
n18af581dcad.x: Government servants were told to stay in service but pledge loyalty to the Congress; soldiers were not to fire on Indians.
xa: **Students** were told they **may leave studies**.
The instructions accompanied the **AICC, Bombay** resolution of **8 August 1942**.

nfb1286b35d2.s: The Quit India Movement of 1942 was Gandhi's:
o: Movement that won immediate transfer of power
nfb1286b35d2.x: The Quit India Movement was Gandhi's final mass movement and showed that Indian independence could not be postponed after the war.
xa: Viceroy **Linlithgow**: the most serious rebellion since **1857**.
AP angle: **"final, decisive event of the freedom struggle in Andhra"**.

nindian-history-113-16.s: Who said, 'Library Movement in Andhra is Swayambhu'?
nindian-history-113-16.x: The line on the Andhra Library Movement is Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah's.
n: The slogan “Swaraj should be for common people…” relates to Swaraj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #113 · pp 208-209]
The line “Library Movement in Andhra is Swayambhu” relates to the Andhra Library Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #113 · pp 208-209]
The line “Everything could wait but not agriculture” relates to agriculture. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #113 · pp 208-209]
The line “Political symptom of our social disease” relates to British rule. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #113 · pp 208-209]
xa: I.V. Ramanaiah is **Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah**.
Nehru's agriculture line belongs to **post-Independence agriculture**.
**"Back to the Vedas"** — **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** (**Arya Samaj**).

n15f074049a4.s: Who among the following organised sabotage and formed the Azad Dasta during the Quit India Movement?
n15f074049a4.x: Jayaprakash Narayan organised sabotage and formed the Azad Dasta during the Quit India Movement.
n15f074049a4.tq: Match a named underground organisation with its organiser.
xs: **Jayaprakash Narayan** organised sabotage and formed the **Azad Dasta** — so option **(2)** is correct (BPSC 2025 key).
**Ram Manohar Lohia** (1) was an underground leader who broadcast on the **Congress Radio**.
**Biju Patnaik** and **Achyut Patwardhan** (3, 4) were other underground figures.
xa: ⚠ **Azad Dasta** = **JP**; **Congress Radio** = **Usha Mehta**.
**Aruna Asaf Ali**: flag-hoisting and underground network.
Sabotage hit bridges, rail tracks, telegraph lines — especially **UP** and **Bihar**.

nindian-history-97-24.s: Who hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank during the Quit India Movement?
nindian-history-97-24.x: Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank; Kanaklata Barua was shot at Gohpur and Matangini Hazra fell at Tamluk.
n: Jayaprakash Narayan is associated with Quit India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Jayaprakash Narayan is associated with the Hazaribagh Jail escape. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Aruna Asaf Ali is associated with Quit India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Aruna Asaf Ali is associated with the Gowalia Tank flag hoisting. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Kanaklata Barua is associated with Quit India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Kanaklata Barua is associated with Gohpur, Assam. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Matangini Hazra is associated with Quit India. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
Matangini Hazra is associated with Tamluk. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #97 · pp 181-183]
xa: JP organised sabotage and formed the **Azad Dasta**.
**Usha Mehta** ran the **Congress Radio**; **Ram Manohar Lohia** broadcast on it.
⚠ **Azad Dasta** = **JP**; **Congress Radio** = **Usha Mehta**.
**Tamluk** later had the parallel **Jatiya Sarkar** (Dec 1942 - Sept 1944).

n6737a466941.s: Who led the parallel government at Ballia in August 1942?
n6737a466941.x: Chittu Pandey led the Ballia parallel government, which lasted about a week; Nana Patil and Y.B. Chavan were associated with Satara.
xa: Ballia (**Aug 1942**) **freed Congress leaders**.
⚠ **Ballia** = shortest; **Satara** = longest.

n99d8d71240a.s: Jatiya Sarkar, which undertook cyclone relief, school grants and paddy distribution, was established at
n99d8d71240a.x: Jatiya Sarkar was formed at Tamluk in Midnapore, Bengal. Its activities included cyclone relief, school grants and distribution of paddy.
n99d8d71240a.tq: Match a distinctive programme of activities with its place of operation.
xs: **Jatiya Sarkar** was set up at **Tamluk in Midnapore**, Bengal — option **(4)** is correct.
It ran **Dec 1942 - Sept 1944**, with cyclone relief, school grants, paddy distribution and **Vidyut Vahinis**.
**Satara** (1) had the **"Prati Sarkar"**; **Ballia** (3) was under **Chittu Pandey**.
xa: Satara (**Y.B. Chavan**, **Nana Patil**) was the longest, mid-**1943** to **1945**.
**Talcher** (Odisha) also had a parallel government in **1942**.

n0683b85d002.s: The Jatiya Sarkar parallel government (December 1942 – September 1944) was set up at:
n0683b85d002.x: Jatiya Sarkar was at Tamluk; the Satara Prati Sarkar, linked to Y.B. Chavan and Nana Patil, was the longest-lasting.
xa: Satara ran **Nyayadan Mandals** (people's courts), village libraries, prohibition, **"Gandhi marriages"**.
APPSC 2016 asked where **"Prati Sarkar"** was formed — **Satara**.

na781255a54e.s: Who was the Viceroy of India during the Quit India Movement?
na781255a54e.x: Lord Linlithgow was the Viceroy of India during the Quit India Movement and directed the colonial response to it.
na781255a54e.tq: Use the office-holder trap by distinguishing neighbouring Viceroy tenures.
xs: The Viceroy was **Lord Linlithgow** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He called Quit India the **most serious rebellion since 1857**.
xa: Repression: about **10,000 deaths**, floggings, **collective fines**, military control of cities.
Gandhi's **21-day fast** (**February 1943**) at the **Aga Khan Palace** led three members of the **Viceroy's Executive Council** to resign.

nebd412e1f0e.s: Gandhi's fast at the Aga Khan Palace from February 1943 lasted:
nebd412e1f0e.x: Gandhi undertook a 21-day fast against state violence, and three members of the Viceroy's Executive Council resigned in this context.
xa: **Kasturba Gandhi** died in detention at **Poona** (**1944**).
**CWC members** were held at **Ahmednagar Fort**.

n0f736878c72.s: The Kurnool (Andhra) Circular, issued on 29 July 1942 during the Quit India Movement, was drafted by whom?
n0f736878c72.x: The Kurnool (Andhra) Circular was drafted by Kala Venkat Rao on 29 July 1942. It was subsequently seized by the police at Kurnool.
n0f736878c72.tq: Use the author–document trap by distinguishing the drafter from other Andhra leaders.
xs: The **Kurnool (Andhra) Circular** (**29 July 1942**) was drafted by **Kala Venkat Rao** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was **seized by police at Kurnool**.
**Mamidipudi Venkatrangayya** (1) led the **Andhra University** resolution; **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** (3) presided over the **APCC meeting at Machilipatnam**.
xa: Pattabhi was jailed at **Ahmednagar Fort** and wrote **"Feathers and Stones"**.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** emerged as Andhra's leading figure.

n37e14db2a85.s: During the Quit India Movement, where was the Madras–Puri passenger train burnt after police firing on 12 August 1942?
n37e14db2a85.x: Tenali saw firing on 12 August 1942 and the burning of the Madras–Puri train; Guntur had firing on 13 August and Bhimavaram on 17 August.
xa: **Bapatla** railway station burnt; **Chirala** signal wires cut; **Tadepalligudem** post office burnt.
Rail lines between **Guntur and Vijayawada** torn up.

n902aefd92a8.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya was jailed at which place during the Quit India Movement, where he wrote the diary titled ‘Feathers and Stones’?
n902aefd92a8.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya was imprisoned at Ahmednagar Fort and wrote ‘Feathers and Stones’ there.
n902aefd92a8.tq: Use the place–work pairing and avoid confusing different colonial prisons.
xs: **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** was jailed at **Ahmednagar Fort**, where he wrote **"Feathers and Stones"** — option **(1)** is correct.
**CWC members** were held at Ahmednagar Fort.
xa: Pattabhi presided over the **APCC meeting** at **Machilipatnam**.
Gandhi was held at the **Aga Khan Palace**; **Kasturba** died at **Poona** (**1944**).

n9079dd8912b.s: Why did the Communist Party of India oppose the Quit India Movement in 1942?
o: It considered the movement an exclusively provincial movement in Andhra.
It supported the Muslim League’s demand for Pakistan from the beginning of the war.
It supported the British war effort after Nazi Germany attacked the Soviet Union.
It had already withdrawn from Indian politics after the Civil Disobedience Movement.
n9079dd8912b.x: The Communists opposed the Quit India Movement because, after the Nazi attack on the Soviet Union, they backed the British war effort.
n9079dd8912b.tq: Identify the cause–attitude link rather than confusing Communist policy with the position of the Muslim League.
xs: The **Communists** backed the British war effort after the **Nazi attack on the USSR** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **CPI ban** was lifted on **23 July 1942**.
xa: The CPI then **lost heavily** in the **1945-46 elections**.
Also stayed away: **Muslim League**, **Hindu Mahasabha** and princely states.

nc0af044d4fe.s: Who emerged as a leading figure in Andhra during the Quit India Movement?
nc0af044d4fe.x: Tanguturi Prakasam emerged as a leading figure in Andhra during the Quit India Movement.
nc0af044d4fe.tq: Distinguish the prominent regional figure from leaders associated with particular documents or underground work.
xs: **Tanguturi Prakasam** emerged as Andhra's leading figure during Quit India — option **(4)** is correct.
**Mamidipudi Venkatrangayya** (1) led the **Andhra University** resolution; **Kala Venkat Rao** (3) drafted the **Kurnool Circular**.
xa: **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** presided over the **APCC** at **Machilipatnam**, then was jailed at **Ahmednagar Fort**.
Quit India was the **"final, decisive event of the freedom struggle in Andhra"**.

ncf36ff06b7e.s: Which of the following stayed away from the Quit India Movement?
ncf36ff06b7e.x: The Muslim League, the Hindu Mahasabha and the princely states stayed away from the movement.
xa: The **Communists** opposed the movement; **CPI ban lifted 23 July 1942**.
Muslims were also **exempted** from the Andhra collective fines.

n2859adbb5c6.s: Who said, "We shall either free India or die in the attempt"?
n2859adbb5c6.x: Mahatma Gandhi said it in his Gowalia Tank speech of 8 August 1942, the same speech in which he gave the call "Do or Die".
n2859adbb5c6.tq: It is just "Do or Die" spelt out in full.
xs: **Mahatma Gandhi** said it in his **Gowalia Tank** speech of **8 Aug 1942** — so option **(4)** is correct (BPSC 2025).
In the same speech he gave the call **"Do or Die"** ("Karo ya Maro").
xa: The **AICC, Bombay** ratified the Quit India resolution that day.
The Wardha resolution was **proposed by Nehru**, **seconded by Patel**.

nf3696279fdf.s: During the Quit India Movement, sabotage was especially directed against
o: Bridges, railway tracks and telegraph lines
Universities, courts and municipal libraries only
nf3696279fdf.x: Underground activists sabotaged bridges, railway tracks and telegraph lines, particularly in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
nf3696279fdf.tq: Identify the infrastructure targets that disrupted colonial administration and communication.
xs: Sabotage targeted **bridges, rail tracks and telegraph lines** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was strongest in **UP** and **Bihar**.
xa: **Jayaprakash Narayan** organised sabotage through the **Azad Dasta**.
Andhra: lines between **Guntur and Vijayawada** torn up; **Chirala** signal wires cut.
Tenali: the **Madras-Puri passenger train** burnt at the station.

ne158baee2fc.s: How did the Communist Party of India fare in the 1945–46 elections after opposing the Quit India Movement?
o: It did not contest owing to a ban
It formed the government in Andhra
ne158baee2fc.x: The CPI lost heavily in 1945–46, against the background of its opposition to Quit India and support for the British war effort.
xa: **Muslim League**, **Hindu Mahasabha** and princely states also stayed away.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** emerged as Andhra's leading figure.

nindian-history-112-14.s: The slogan 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' is associated with:
nindian-history-112-14.x: 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' is Shastri's slogan; 'Do or Die' is Gandhi's.
n: Mahatma Gandhi said, “Do or Die.” [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #112 · pp 207-208]
Mahatma Gandhi’s quote “Do or Die” is associated with the Quit India Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #112 · pp 207-208]
Mahatma Gandhi wrote “Hind Swaraj.” [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #112 · pp 207-208]
Mahatma Gandhi’s “Hind Swaraj” expresses his conception of Swaraj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #112 · pp 207-208]
Lal Bahadur Shastri said, “Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan.” [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #112 · pp 207-208]
xa: Hind Swaraj expresses Gandhi's **conception of Swaraj**.
Tagore called British rule a "**political symptom of our social disease**".
"Quit India" was hinted by Gandhi in **Harijan** (**April 1942**); the coinage is usually credited to **Yusuf Meherally**.

nindian-history-100-34.s: Which slogan did Gandhi give in association with the Quit India Movement?
nindian-history-100-34.x: At the Quit India session in August 1942, Gandhi gave the call "Do or Die". "Swaraj is my birthright" was Tilak's slogan and "Inquilab Zindabad" was linked with revolutionaries.
nindian-history-100-34.tq: Match each slogan with its leader.
n: Gandhi gave the “Do or Die” call during the Quit India Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #100 · pp 185-188]
The Quit India Resolution represented Gandhi’s call. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #100 · pp 185-188]
xs: Gandhi's Quit India slogan was **"Do or Die"** ("Karo ya Maro") — so option **(1)** is correct.
He gave it in the **Gowalia Tank** speech, Bombay, **8 Aug 1942**.
**"Swaraj is my birthright"** was **Tilak**'s; **"Two Mahatmas"** was **Sarojini Naidu**'s description of Gandhi and **Irwin**.
xa: Same speech: "We shall either **free India or die** in the attempt".
The AICC resolution was ratified at **Gowalia Tank Maidan**; arrests followed on **9 August 1942** (**Operation Zero Hour**).
⚠ "Do or Die" was not in **Young India** — Gandhi's paper in **1942** was **Harijan**.

nindian-history-112-3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Tilak said, “Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it.”
Tagore said, “Freedom is within our reach and we should hold it very tight.”
Gandhi gave the call “Do or Die” in August 1942
Gandhi's words “Freedom is within our reach and we should hold it very tight” belong to the Quit India Movement
nindian-history-112-3.x: “Freedom is within our reach and we should hold it very tight” was said by Gandhi during Quit India, not by Tagore.
n: Bal Gangadhar Tilak said, “Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it.” [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #112 · pp 207-208]
Mahatma Gandhi said, “Freedom is within our reach and we should hold it very tight.” [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #112 · pp 207-208]
Mahatma Gandhi’s quote about freedom is associated with the Quit India Movement. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #112 · pp 207-208]
xa: Tagore's line: "**Political symptom of our social disease**" — on **British rule** in India.
Gandhi's Quit India call: **"Do or Die"** ("Karo ya Maro") at **Gowalia Tank**, **8 Aug 1942**.
**Hind Swaraj** was written by **Mahatma Gandhi** — his conception of Swaraj.

n5cf30684cc5.s: During the Quit India Movement, the Congress Working Committee members were detained at:
n5cf30684cc5.x: CWC members were held at Ahmednagar Fort, while Gandhi was detained at the Aga Khan Palace, Pune.
xa: The arrests came on **9 Aug** **1942**, the day after the **Gowalia Tank** AICC.
**Pattabhi Sitaramayya**, a CWC member, was jailed with the CWC.

n4695cb75d76.s: The AICC session that adopted the Quit India resolution and gave the call 'Do or Die' was held at:
n4695cb75d76.x: The AICC met at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 August 1942 and gave the call 'Do or Die'. Wardha (14 July 1942) was the earlier CWC meeting; 6 August is a wrong date found in some sources; Ahmednagar Fort was where CWC members were detained after the 9 August arrests.
n4695cb75d76.tq: CWC Wardha 14 July -> AICC Bombay 8 Aug -> arrests 9 Aug
xs: The AICC met at **Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 Aug 1942**, with the call **"Do or Die"** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Wardha** (**14 July 1942**) (2) was the earlier **CWC** meeting.
⚠ Option (3): some notes date the AICC to **6 Aug** — use **8 Aug**; option (4): **Ahmednagar Fort** is where CWC members were held after **9 Aug**.
xa: The **Andhra Circular** (**29 July 1942**) came **before** the Bombay AICC.
⚠ Some notes say "Young India" — the paper was **Harijan**.

nd16599c43f1.s: The Andhra Circular, dated 29 July 1942, was seized by the police at:
nd16599c43f1.x: The Andhra Circular, prepared before the Bombay AICC meeting, was seized by the police at Kurnool.
xa: Author: **Kala Venkata Rao** (APPSC 2019 key).
The **APCC** met at **Machilipatnam** under **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** in the same phase.

na5511a3fdb2.s: The Andhra Circular was also known as the:
na5511a3fdb2.x: The Andhra Circular was also called the Kurnool Circular because it was seized by the police at Kurnool.
na5511a3fdb2.tq: Distinguish the official alternative name from associated Andhra locations.
xs: The Andhra Circular is also called the **Kurnool Circular** — option **(2)** is correct.
It was **seized by police at Kurnool**.
**Machilipatnam** (3) was where the **APCC** met; **Guntur** (1) saw police firing on **13 Aug**.
xa: Author: **Kala Venkata Rao**; dated **29 July 1942**.
It carried **directives for the coming movement**.

nec2c1dc7cbc.s: At which place did police firing on 12 August 1942 reportedly result in about nine deaths during the Quit India Movement in Andhra?
nec2c1dc7cbc.x: Police firing at Tenali railway station on 12 August 1942 reportedly caused about nine deaths.
nec2c1dc7cbc.tq: Fix the date and match it with the corresponding town rather than relying on the event alone.
xs: Police firing at **Tenali** on **12 Aug** killed about **nine** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Guntur** (4) saw firing on **13 Aug**; **Bhimavaram** (3) on **17 Aug**.
xa: The Tenali firing came three days after Gandhi's arrest on **9 Aug**.
The CWC members were held at **Ahmednagar Fort**.

ncb0d71de94f.s: The Andhra Circular (Kurnool Circular) of July 1942, giving directives for the coming Quit India Movement, was prepared by:
ncb0d71de94f.x: Kala Venkata Rao authored the Andhra Circular dated 29 July 1942 (APPSC 2019 key). Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over the APCC meeting at Machilipatnam; Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah of Kurnool stayed underground; Chandra Rajeswara Rao was secretary of the 1943 Communist conference.
ncb0d71de94f.tq: Circular - Kala Venkata Rao; seized at Kurnool
xs: The **Andhra Circular** was prepared by **Kala Venkata Rao** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2019 key).

**Pattabhi Sitaramayya** (1) presided over the **APCC at Machilipatnam**; **Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah** (3) stayed **underground**; **Chandra Rajeswara Rao** (4) was **Communist Conference** secretary.
xa: Dated **29 July 1942**; **seized by police at Kurnool**.
It came before the **AICC** at **Gowalia Tank** on **8 Aug 1942**.

n46de21055ce.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra leaders during the Quit India Movement?
o: Unnava Lakshmi Narayana was jailed for the first time in 1942.
Pattabhi Sitaramayya, a CWC member, was jailed along with the CWC.
Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah of Kurnool stayed underground throughout.
The secret paper 'Quit India' spread the pamphlet 'Rahasya Udyamam Saginchandi'.
n46de21055ce.x: Unnava Lakshmi Narayana was jailed again in 1942, not for the first time.
xa: **Mamidipudi Venkatarangayya** led the **Andhra University** protest demanding Gandhi's release.
**Chitturi Annapurna Devi** (**17**) was arrested in **Guntur** for pamphlets and picketing.

nef4ab744589.s: The Quit India protest of Andhra University students demanding Gandhi's release was associated with:
nef4ab744589.x: The Andhra University protest was associated with Mamidipudi Venkatarangayya; Kakinada lawyers passed a similar resolution.
xa: **Chitturi Annapurna Devi** (**17**) was arrested in **Guntur**.
**Duvvuri Subbamma** faced a **lathi charge at Peddapuram**.

n61eb31e2e50.s: Who among the following groups led the underground movement nationally during the Quit India Movement as Congress Socialists?
o: Chandra Rajeswara Rao, N.G. Ranga, Duvvuri Subbamma and Karunasree
Pattabhi Sitaramayya, Chitturi Annapurna Devi, Unnava Lakshmi Narayana and Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah
Jayaprakash Narayan, Rammanohar Lohia, Aruna Asaf Ali and Usha Mehta
Vinoba Bhave, Jawaharlal Nehru, Pattabhi Sitaramayya and Kala Venkata Rao
n61eb31e2e50.x: The Congress Socialist leaders associated with the national underground were Jayaprakash Narayan, Rammanohar Lohia, Aruna Asaf Ali and Usha Mehta.
n61eb31e2e50.tq: Group people by political role and eliminate names belonging to other organisations or regional activities.
xs: The national underground was led by Congress Socialists **Jayaprakash Narayan**, **Rammanohar Lohia**, **Aruna Asaf Ali** and **Usha Mehta** — option **(3)**.
**Usha Mehta** ran the **secret radio**.
**Chandra Rajeswara Rao** (1) was a Communist; **Vinoba** and **Nehru** (4) were Individual Satyagraha's first two satyagrahis.
xa: Andhra's **Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah** (Kurnool) stayed **underground** throughout.
The **CPI** opposed Quit India, backing the British war effort.

n10f1602e5fd.s: Subhas Chandra Bose was born on 23 January 1897 at:
n10f1602e5fd.x: Subhas Chandra Bose was born on 23 January 1897 at Cuttack.
n10f1602e5fd.tq: Test the date–birthplace combination directly, a common modern-history factual pair.
xs: Subhas Chandra Bose was born on **23 January 1897** at **Cuttack** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Pithapuram** (1) is linked to **Madduri Annapurnaiah** ("Andhra Netaji"); **Singapore** (3) is where Bose arrived in **July 1943**; **Calcutta** (4) is where he studied and was under house arrest.
xa: Education: **Presidency College Calcutta**, then **Cambridge**.
Cleared the **ICS** in **1920**, resigned in **1921** to join Congress.
Political guru: **C.R. Das**.

n81ff32ee318.s: Subhas Chandra Bose resigned from the Indian Civil Service to join the Congress in:
n81ff32ee318.x: Bose qualified for the ICS in 1920 and resigned in 1921 to join the Congress.
xa: He published **"The Indian Struggle"** in **1935**.
Re-elected at **Tripuri** in **1939**, then resigned and founded the **Forward Bloc**.

n01b4d5e46a2.s: The book 'The Indian Struggle', an account of the national movement, was published by Subhas Chandra Bose in:
n01b4d5e46a2.x: Bose's account of the national movement, titled 'The Indian Struggle', was published in 1935.
n01b4d5e46a2.tq: Use the middle chronological value while rejecting nearby movement and organisational years.
xs: **"The Indian Struggle"** was published in **1935** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1939** (4) is the year of **Tripuri** and the **Forward Bloc**.
xa: **1938**: Congress president at **Haripura**.
**January 1941**: escape from house arrest in **Calcutta**.

nc22d97b456b.s: Who is regarded as the political guru of Subhas Chandra Bose?
nc22d97b456b.x: After resigning from the ICS in 1921, Bose joined the Congress and worked under C.R. Das, his political guru. Bose differed with Gandhi (e.g. at Tripuri); Tilak was an earlier Extremist leader; Rash Behari Bose was linked to the IIL and the first INA.
xs: Bose's political guru was **C.R. Das** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He differed with **Gandhi** at **Tripuri** ("Pattabhi's defeat is my defeat"); **Rash Behari Bose** (4) was linked to the **IIL** and the first INA.
xa: Bose resigned the ICS in **1921** to join Congress.
⚠ **Rash Behari Bose** (IIL, Japan) ≠ **Rash Behari Ghosh** (Moderate).

n34d40c0e887.s: At the Tripuri session of the Indian National Congress in 1939, Mahatma Gandhi reacted to the defeat of his preferred presidential candidate by stating that:
o: The Congress must immediately suspend its session
The defeat of Bose is the defeat of Congress
The defeat of Pattabhi is my defeat
The victory of the left wing is my victory
n34d40c0e887.x: Gandhi stated, “Pattabhi's defeat is my defeat,” after Dr. Pattabhi Sitaramayya lost the presidential election to Subhas Chandra Bose.
n34d40c0e887.tq: Use the exact leader–reaction association rather than relying only on the election result.
xs: Gandhi said **"Pattabhi's defeat is my defeat"** — so option **(3)** is correct.
At **Tripuri, 1939**, Bose defeated Gandhi-backed **Dr. Pattabhi Sitaramayya** (**1,580** to **1,377**).
xa: APPSC 2018 asked whom Bose defeated at Tripuri — **Pattabhi Sitaramayya**.
The **Working Committee** deadlock led Bose to resign (**April 1939**); **Dr. Rajendra Prasad** became President.
The **Pant Resolution** asked Bose to name the Working Committee in line with **Gandhi's wishes**.

n4da042ac899.s: The National Planning Committee established during Subhas Chandra Bose's Congress presidentship was chaired by:
n4da042ac899.x: The National Planning Committee was set up by the Congress in 1938 under Bose, with Jawaharlal Nehru as its chairman.
n4da042ac899.tq: Match an organisation with its chairman, avoiding confusion among major Congress leaders.
xs: The **National Planning Committee** (**1938**) was chaired by **Jawaharlal Nehru** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ It was set up **under Bose**, but the chairman was **Nehru** — the forerunner of planning.
**Dr. Rajendra Prasad** (2) became Congress President after Bose resigned in **April 1939**.
xa: APPSC 2022 key: **National Planning Committee: 1938**.
Bose presided over **Haripura**, the **51st** session.

n7f794144a8c.s: Subhas Chandra Bose escaped from house arrest in Calcutta in:
n7f794144a8c.x: Bose escaped from Calcutta in January 1941, travelled via Kabul and Moscow to Berlin, and reached Singapore in July 1943.
xa: In Germany he set up the **Free India Centre** and **Azad Hind Radio**.
Supreme Commander of the INA from **25 Aug 1943**.

n3f554925594.s: The INA anthem was a Hindustani version of 'Jana Gana Mana' translated by:
n3f554925594.x: Abid Hasan 'Safrani' translated the Hindustani version of 'Jana Gana Mana' that served as the INA anthem.
n3f554925594.tq: Match the cultural contribution with its precise individual contributor.
xs: The INA anthem — Hindustani **Jana Gana Mana** — was translated by **Abid Hasan 'Safrani'** — option **(3)**.
**Lakshmi Sahgal** (1) led the Rani of Jhansi Regiment; **Dhillon** and **Sehgal** (2, 4) were Red Fort accused.
xa: INA motto: **"Ittefaq, Itmad, Qurbani"**.
Bose's call: **"Tum mujhe khoon do, main tumhe azadi dunga"**.

n780866c585a.s: Subhas Chandra Bose was reportedly killed in a plane crash at Taipei on:
n780866c585a.x: Bose was reportedly killed in a plane crash at Taipei on 18 August 1945. The circumstances of his death later became the subject of official inquiries.
n780866c585a.tq: Differentiate closely spaced dates in a disputed historical event.
xs: Bose was reportedly killed in a **plane crash at Taipei, 18 August 1945** — option **(2)**.
Inquiries: **Shah Nawaz Committee** and **Khosla Commission** — died in the crash.
xa: The **Mukherjee Commission** found he **did not die** in the crash; its report was rejected.
"Netaji" was given by the **people of Germany**.

n6f1df57b760.s: After the Tripuri session, the Pant Resolution required Subhas Chandra Bose to form the Working Committee according to the wishes of:
n6f1df57b760.x: The Pant Resolution required Bose to form the Working Committee in accordance with Gandhi's wishes.
xa: Bose had defeated **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** (**1,580** to **1,377**).
**Dr. Rajendra Prasad** succeeded Bose as President.

nbe479519504.s: At the Tripuri Congress (1939), Subhas Chandra Bose was re-elected president by defeating the Gandhi-backed candidate ______; after Bose resigned, ______ became president.
nbe479519504.x: Bose defeated Dr. Pattabhi Sitaramayya (1,580 to 1,377) at Tripuri, 1939 (APPSC 2018). The Working Committee deadlock led Bose to resign in April 1939 and Dr. Rajendra Prasad became President. Nehru and Patel were not the candidate or successor here.
nbe479519504.tq: Tripuri: Bose beat Pattabhi; Prasad succeeded
xs: Bose defeated **Pattabhi Sitaramayya**; after he resigned, **Rajendra Prasad** became President — option **(1)** is correct.
The vote was **1,580** to **1,377**; Bose resigned in **April 1939** over the **Working Committee** deadlock.
Option (2) swaps the two; **Nehru** (3) chaired the **National Planning Committee**.
xa: Gandhi: **"Pattabhi's defeat is my defeat."**
Bose then founded the **Forward Bloc**.

n271c103bfdc.x: Madduri Annapurnaiah, a Forward Bloc member jailed for the article 'Chicharapidugu', was called Andhra Netaji.
xa: Title: **"Andhra Netaji"**; born **1899**, **Pithapuram** taluk.
He led the Andhra Forward Bloc with **Peta Bapayya**.

n5eb8c0e9e45.s: The August Offer of 1940 accepted ____ as the goal for India.
n5eb8c0e9e45.x: The August Offer accepted dominion status as the goal, proposed an expanded Executive Council and a war advisory council, and was rejected by the Congress.
xa: It was announced by Viceroy **Linlithgow** on **8 Aug 1940**.
It also offered a **veto for minorities**.
Congress answered with **Individual Satyagraha** (**17 October 1940**).

nbbdba5100ed.s: Which of the following was associated with the underground leadership of the Quit India Movement?
nbbdba5100ed.x: Lohia, with Jayaprakash Narayan, Sucheta Kripalani and Biju Patnaik, was part of the underground network; Desai and Sapru were linked to the INA trial defence.
xa: **Usha Mehta** ran the secret **Congress Radio**.
INA trial defence also had **Nehru**, **Asaf Ali**, **K.N. Katju**.

n83271053487.s: Matangini Hazra, shot while leading a flag procession during the Quit India Movement, was associated with:
n83271053487.x: Matangini Hazra was associated with Tamluk in Bengal; Kanaklata Barua was from Assam.
xa: Both were shot while leading **flag processions**.
After **9 August 1942** the movement turned leaderless and violent.
n83271053487.fixed: Kanaklata Barua (b. Dec 1924, shot Sept 1942) was 17, not 15

nd5ad9144968.s: The immediate political objective behind the formation of the Forward Bloc by Subhas Chandra Bose in 1939 was to:
o: Support the British war effort during the Second World War
Create a purely provincial party in Bengal
Replace the Indian National Congress with a princely federation
Unite radical, left-wing and anti-imperialist forces within the Congress
nd5ad9144968.x: The Forward Bloc was initially formed within the Congress to unite radical, left-wing and anti-imperialist forces after Bose's resignation.
nd5ad9144968.tq: Infer the organisation's purpose from its political context and avoid an unrelated organisational objective.
xs: The Forward Bloc was first a bloc within Congress to **unite radical, left-wing and anti-imperialist forces** — option **(4)** is correct.
Bose founded it in **1939** (some notes say **April 1939**) after resigning the presidency.
xa: Andhra branch: **Madduri Annapurnaiah** (first Andhra leader to join) and **Peta Bapayya**.
July 2026: **AIFB** demanded an apology after Forward Bloc members were called "goons".

n898e9559dcf.s: Which leaders were associated with the Andhra branch of the Forward Bloc?
o: Kala Venkata Rao and Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah
n898e9559dcf.x: Madduri Annapurnaiah and Peta Bapayya were associated with the Andhra branch of the Forward Bloc.
xa: Annapurnaiah was titled **"Andhra Netaji"**; born **1899**, **Pithapuram** taluk.
He spent **4 years** in jail as a Forward Bloc member during **WWII**.

n3c16733597e.s: The Free India Centre established by Subhas Chandra Bose during his stay in Europe was located in:
n3c16733597e.x: Bose established the Free India Centre in Berlin during his stay in Germany.
n3c16733597e.tq: Match an organisation with its location, a frequent place-association trap in modern history.
xs: The **Free India Centre** was set up by Bose in **Germany** — option **(2) Berlin** is correct.
**Azad Hind Radio** was also started in Germany, broadcasting from **Berlin**.
**Moscow** (1) was only a stop on his escape route.
xa: The **Indian Legion** was raised from POWs captured by **Rommel** in **North Africa**.
He left Germany early **1943** by submarine.

n83f47c04d0c.s: The Indian Legion, also known as the Free Indian Legion, was formed in Germany mainly from:
o: Indian sailors of the Royal Indian Navy
Members of the Congress Volunteer Corps
Indian prisoners of war captured by Rommel in North Africa
n83f47c04d0c.x: The Free Indian Legion was recruited from Indian prisoners of war captured by Rommel's forces in North Africa.
n83f47c04d0c.tq: Connect the military formation with its source of recruitment rather than with Bose's later INA base.
xs: The **Indian Legion** came from **POWs captured by Rommel in North Africa** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was raised in **Germany**, alongside the **Free India Centre**.
xa: The first INA, by contrast, came from Indian POWs in **South-East Asia**, under **Capt. Mohan Singh**.
**Azad Hind Radio** broadcast from **Berlin** (APPSC 2018).

n1693bd27e6d.s: Azad Hind Radio, which broadcast from Berlin, was started in:
n1693bd27e6d.x: Azad Hind Radio was started in Germany and broadcast from Berlin.
n1693bd27e6d.tq: Separate the location of a propaganda broadcast from the later headquarters of the INA.
xs: **Azad Hind Radio** was started in **Germany** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2018).
It broadcast from **Berlin**.
xa: Other German ventures: **Free India Centre** and the **Indian Legion** (Rommel's POWs).
"Netaji" was given by the **people of Germany** (UPSC notes).

n02b9c472237.s: Usha Mehta is particularly associated with which activity during the Quit India movement?
o: Organising the Prati Sarkar in Satara
Running the secret Congress Radio in Bombay
n02b9c472237.x: Usha Mehta ran the secret Congress Radio in Bombay during the Quit India movement.
n02b9c472237.tq: Identify a participant through her distinctive underground activity.
xs: **Usha Mehta** ran the secret **Congress Radio** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Matangini Hazra** (2) was the **Tamluk** martyr shot leading a flag procession.
xa: Underground leadership: **Jayaprakash Narayan**, **Rammanohar Lohia**.
Underground network: **Sucheta Kripalani**, **Biju Patnaik**.

n61ca5daff79.s: The Rani of Jhansi Regiment of the INA was:
o: An all-women combat unit under Captain Lakshmi Sahgal
A women's medical unit under Aruna Asaf Ali
A civilian relief organisation under Sucheta Kripalani
A mixed military unit under Rash Behari Bose
n61ca5daff79.x: The Rani of Jhansi Regiment was an all-women combat unit commanded by Captain Lakshmi Sahgal.
n61ca5daff79.tq: Match the unit's character and commander rather than selecting a well-known woman freedom fighter at random.
xs: The **Rani of Jhansi Regiment** was an **all-women combat unit** under **Capt. Lakshmi Sahgal** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Sucheta Kripalani** (3) was in the **Quit India** underground network.
xa: The **IIL** was the INA's political wing.
INA motto: **"Ittefaq, Itmad, Qurbani"** (Unity, Faith, Sacrifice).

nindian-history-101-2.s: The Indian National Army was also known as:
nindian-history-101-2.x: The Indian National Army was called the Azad Hind Fauj. The Azad Hind Government was the provisional government set up in 1943, a separate body.
nindian-history-101-2.tq: Discriminate the army from the government.
n: INA is also known as Azad Hind Fauj. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #101 · pp 188-189]
xs: The Indian National Army was also known as the **Azad Hind Fauj** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Azad Hind Government** was a separate body — the **Provisional Government** proclaimed at **Singapore** on **21 October 1943**.
The INA was the brainchild of **Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon** and **Major Iwaichi Fujiwara**.
xa: **Captain Mohan Singh** was the **first operational commander**; his INA was formed in **July 1942**.
**Rash Behari Bose** handed over INA command to **Subhas Chandra Bose**, who took command in **July 1943**.
⚠ **Rash Behari Bose** (IIL, Japan) ≠ **Rash Behari Ghosh** (Moderate).

nf92829d697b.s: Subhas Chandra Bose described the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922 as:
o: A new dawn for constitutional politics
Sprinkling cold water on the spirits of the people
A necessary preparation for the Cripps Mission
nf92829d697b.x: Bose criticised the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement as 'sprinkling cold water on the spirits of the people'.
nf92829d697b.tq: Identify the exact quotation associated with the correct critic and event.
xs: Bose called the NCM withdrawal (**1922**) **"sprinkling cold water on the spirits of the people"** — option **(2)** is correct.
He had resigned the **ICS** in **1921** to join Congress, working under **C.R. Das**.
xa: His account of the national movement: **"The Indian Struggle"** (**1935**).
At **Tripuri** (**1939**) he again clashed with the Gandhian old guard.

nf4017f98a83.s: Subhas Chandra Bose became the Supreme Commander of the Indian National Army on:
nf4017f98a83.x: Bose assumed the position of Supreme Commander of the INA on 25 August 1943.
nf4017f98a83.tq: Distinguish closely related dates connected with Bose's command, government and INA campaigns.
xs: Bose became **Supreme Commander of the INA** on **25 Aug 1943** — option **(3)** is correct.
**21 October 1943** (4) is the **Azad Hind** proclamation; **14 April 1944** (1) the **Moirang** flag; **18 August 1945** (2) the reported death.
xa: He had taken over the **IIL** and INA in **July 1943**.
HQ: **Singapore**, later **Rangoon**.

na5449b8f1e8.s: Who among the following were associated with the formation of the first INA?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru and Rash Behari Ghosh
Subhas Chandra Bose and C.R. Das
Capt. Mohan Singh and Rash Behari Bose
Mahatma Gandhi and Capt. Lakshmi Sahgal
na5449b8f1e8.x: The first INA was formed under Capt. Mohan Singh with the political association of Rash Behari Bose. Subhas Chandra Bose took over and revived it in its second phase in 1943.
na5449b8f1e8.tq: Apply the founder-versus-later-commander distinction instead of choosing the most famous associated person.
xs: The first INA was formed by **Capt. Mohan Singh** with **Rash Behari Bose** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **Rash Behari Ghosh** (1) was the **Moderate**, not the IIL leader.
**Capt. Lakshmi Sahgal** (4) led the **Rani of Jhansi Regiment**.
xa: **June 1942**: IIL leaders met the Japanese to set up the INA.
Second phase (**1943**): **Subhas Bose** revived the INA as Supreme Commander.

nb4d8069b4d0.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the headquarters of the INA under Subhas Chandra Bose?
nb4d8069b4d0.x: The INA headquarters was at Singapore under Bose and was later shifted to Rangoon.
nb4d8069b4d0.tq: Watch for the reversal of the initial and later locations.
xs: INA HQ was at **Singapore**, later **Rangoon** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (3) reverses the order.
xa: Bose took over the IIL and INA in **July 1943**.
**Imphal-Kohima campaign (1944)** ended in retreat after Japanese defeats + supply shortages.

nc4e3cf86a14.s: The Individual Satyagraha Movement was formally launched on 17 October 1940 from:
nc4e3cf86a14.x: Individual Satyagraha began on 17 October 1940 from Paunar in Wardha.
nc4e3cf86a14.tq: Test the exact launch place rather than the residence or prison of a leader.
xs: Individual Satyagraha began on **17 October 1940** from **Paunar, Wardha** (some notes: **"Palner"**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Ahmednagar Fort** (1) is where the **CWC** was held in **1942**.
xa: First satyagrahi **Vinoba Bhave**; second **Jawaharlal Nehru**.
**Ongole** municipality condemned their arrests.

n2c19e445190.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind)?
o: It declared war on Britain and the USA.
It was recognised by Japan, Germany and Italy.
Its proclamation guaranteed religious liberty and equal rights.
It was proclaimed at Rangoon on 21 October 1943.
n2c19e445190.x: The government was proclaimed at Singapore on 21 October 1943; Rangoon was where the INA headquarters later moved.
xa: Allies recognising it: **Burma**, **Thailand**, **Philippines**, **Manchukuo**.
**Rangoon** was the INA's later HQ.

n8c497c5faaa.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Andaman and Nicobar Islands under the Azad Hind Government?
o: The Andaman Islands were renamed Shaheed Dweep.
The islands were handed over to the Azad Hind Government by Germany.
The Nicobar Islands were renamed Swaraj Dweep.
Bose hoisted the tricolour at Port Blair on 30 December 1943.
n8c497c5faaa.x: The islands were handed over by Japan, not Germany.
xa: ⚠ **Shaheed** = Andaman; **Swaraj** = Nicobar.
**Jan 2026**: PM marked the **82nd anniversary** of the Port Blair flag-hoisting.

n427c7d74730.s: The INA hoisted its flag at Moirang in Manipur during the Imphal campaign on:
n427c7d74730.x: The INA hoisted its flag at Moirang, Manipur, on 14 April 1944 during the Imphal campaign, before retreating.
n427c7d74730.tq: Link a military campaign site with its precise date while separating it from Port Blair events.
xs: The INA hoisted its flag at **Moirang, Manipur, 14 April 1944** — option **(4)** is correct.
**30 December 1943** (2) was Bose's flag at **Port Blair**; **21 October 1943** (1) the Azad Hind proclamation.
xa: The **Imphal-Kohima campaign (1944)** ended in retreat after Japanese defeats + supply shortages.
INA war cry: **"Dilli Chalo"**.

n8001154505e.s: Who led the defence at the Red Fort INA trials (1945)?
n8001154505e.x: Bhulabhai Desai led the defence; Sapru, Nehru, Asaf Ali and K.N. Katju assisted.
xa: Defence team also had **Nehru**, **Asaf Ali**, **K.N. Katju**.
INA trials + the **RIN mutiny** broke the loyalty of the Indian armed forces.

n9e455989d30.s: Which development immediately triggered the Quit India Movement?
o: The conclusion of the Shimla Conference in 1945
The resignation of Congress ministries in November 1939 alone
Failure of the Cripps Mission in March 1942
The formation of the INA in 1943
n9e455989d30.x: The failure of the Cripps Mission (March 1942), which offered no immediate self-government, was the immediate trigger for Quit India. Gandhi called the Cripps offer a 'post-dated cheque' (Nehru is credited with adding 'on a crashing bank'). Shimla 1945 and the INA's 1943 revival came later, and the 1939 ministry resignations were only background.
n9e455989d30.tq: Distinguish the immediate trigger from earlier background developments and later events.
xs: The trigger was the **failure of the Cripps Mission (March 1942)** — option **(3)** is correct.
Gandhi called Cripps a **"post-dated cheque"** (on a failing/crashing bank).
Ministries' resignation in **Nov 1939** (2) was only background.
xa: AICC at **Gowalia Tank Maidan**, **8 August 1942**.
**9 August 1942**: leaders arrested.

n142a31738f8.s: Who coined the phrase 'Quit India', while Gandhi gave the call for the movement?
n142a31738f8.x: The phrase 'Quit India' was coined by Yusuf Meherally. Gandhi subsequently gave the call for the movement.
n142a31738f8.tq: Separate the person who coined a phrase from the leader who popularised or gave the call.
xs: The phrase **"Quit India"** was coined by **Yusuf Meherally** — option **(1)** is correct.
Gandhi gave the call, having hinted it in **Harijan** in **April 1942**.
**Lohia** and **JP** (2, 3) were **underground leaders** after the arrests.
xa: Gandhi's **"Do or Die"** came at **Gowalia Tank**, **8 Aug 1942**.
**Usha Mehta** ran the secret **Congress Radio**.

n4253fabed72.s: Which greeting did Subhas Chandra Bose popularise in place of 'Bande Mataram'?
n4253fabed72.x: Bose popularised 'Jai Hind'; 'Dilli Chalo' was the INA war cry.
xa: INA motto: **"Ittefaq, Itmad, Qurbani"**.
⚠ **"Do or Die"** is **Gandhi**'s, not Bose's (APPSC 2018, 2025).

ne79c55d8beb.s: The call 'Do or Die' was given in 1942 by:
ne79c55d8beb.x: 'Do or Die' was Gandhi's call at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 August 1942; Meherally coined 'Quit India' and Bose's war cry was 'Dilli Chalo'.
xa: Exam angle: asked repeatedly (**APPSC 2018, 2025**) — answer **Gandhi**, not Bose.
Leaders were arrested the next day, **9 August 1942**.

n33737ae9315.s: INA Day was observed on which date?
n33737ae9315.x: INA Day was observed on 12 November 1945.
n33737ae9315.tq: Distinguish the commemorative date from the dates of later protests and the naval revolt.
xs: **INA Day** was **12 November 1945** — option **(3)** is correct (UPPSC 2013 key).
**21 November 1945** (1) = Calcutta student protest; **11 February 1946** (2) = Rashid Ali protests; **18 February 1946** (4) = RIN mutiny.
xa: The Red Fort trials ran **November 1945 - May 1946**.
The Calcutta firing on **21 November** killed **two**.

neceb87eeba3.s: The Royal Indian Navy Mutiny began on 18 February 1946 among the ratings of:
neceb87eeba3.x: The mutiny began on 18 February 1946 among the ratings of HMIS Talwar in Bombay.
neceb87eeba3.tq: Link the date, naval vessel and city precisely.
xs: The RIN mutiny began on **18 February 1946** at **HMIS Talwar, Bombay** — option **(4)** is correct.
It spread to about **20,000 personnel**, **78 ships**, **20 shore establishments**, and also **Karachi**.
xa: ⚠ It came one day before Attlee's **Cabinet Mission** announcement (**19 Feb 1946**).
**M.S. Khan** headed the **Naval Central Strike Committee**.

na035867976c.s: When did Attlee announce the Cabinet Mission?
na035867976c.x: Attlee announced the Cabinet Mission on 19 February 1946; the Mission arrived in India on 24 March 1946.
na035867976c.tq: Separate the announcement date from the arrival and plan dates.
xs: Attlee announced the **Cabinet Mission** on **19 Feb 1946** — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ That was **one day after** the **RIN mutiny** began (**18 Feb 1946**).
**20 February 1947** (4) was the declaration that the British would leave by **June 1948**.
xa: The RIN mutiny began at **HMIS Talwar, Bombay**.
Attlee saw the loss of military loyalty as decisive.

nbb087e28f2d.s: On 20 February 1947, Attlee declared that the British would leave India by:
nbb087e28f2d.x: Attlee's statement of 20 February 1947 set June 1948 as the deadline for British withdrawal. August 1947 is when power was actually transferred; March 1947 and January 1950 are unrelated to this announcement.
xs: On **20 February 1947** Attlee declared the British would leave by **June 1948** — option **(2)** is correct.
**August 1947** (1) is not the date in the declaration.
xa: Earlier: **19 Feb 1946**, Attlee announced the **Cabinet Mission**.
Attlee called Gandhi's role in the immediate transfer of power **"minimal"**.

n48b48570a27.s: The sentence of transportation for life in the first INA trial was remitted in January 1946 by:
n48b48570a27.x: Commander-in-Chief Auchinleck remitted the sentences of Sahgal, Shah Nawaz Khan and Dhillon, who had been found guilty of waging war.
xa: **Rashid Ali**'s later **7-year sentence** sparked protests (**11 February 1946**).
UPSC 2021: the three were **INA officers**.

ne4b58eb8423.s: The INA Defence Committee was set up by:
ne4b58eb8423.x: The INA Defence Committee was established by the Congress to defend the accused INA officers.
xa: Lead counsel: **Bhulabhai Desai** — his last major contribution.
Other lawyers: **Sapru**, **Asaf Ali**, **Sarat Chandra Bose**, **K.N. Katju**, **Jawaharlal Nehru**.

n2b3a27b1b88.s: Who served as the lead counsel of the INA Defence Committee?
n2b3a27b1b88.x: Bhulabhai Desai was the lead counsel of the INA Defence Committee, and this was regarded as his last major contribution.
n2b3a27b1b88.tq: Distinguish the lead counsel from the other lawyers who assisted the defence.
xs: **Bhulabhai Desai** was lead counsel — option **(4)** is correct; it was his **last major contribution**.
**Sapru**, **K.N. Katju** and **Asaf Ali** (1-3) were other defence lawyers.
xa: ⚠ BPSC 2020: of **Rajendra Prasad**, **Bhulabhai Desai**, **K.M. Munshi**, **Patel** — only **Bhulabhai Desai** was counsel.
APPSC 2018: Bhulabhai Desai was **counsel, not an accused**.

n83d58501062.s: Who was the president of the Naval Central Strike Committee during the RIN revolt?
n83d58501062.x: M.S. Khan served as president of the Naval Central Strike Committee.
n83d58501062.tq: Distinguish the strike committee leader from the political leaders who negotiated surrender.
xs: **M.S. Khan** was president of the **Naval Central Strike Committee** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Patel** and **Jinnah** (2, 4) persuaded the ratings to surrender; **Aruna Asaf Ali** (3) backed them.
xa: Strike began at **HMIS Talwar, Bombay**, **18 February 1946**.
Congress and **Muslim League flags** were hoisted together.

ne25d2904650.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the RIN revolt of 1946?
o: Aruna Asaf Ali and the Communists backed the ratings.
Congress and Muslim League flags were hoisted together.
Bombay mill workers, railway workers and students joined the ratings.
Patel and Jinnah backed the continuation of the revolt.
ne25d2904650.x: Patel and Jinnah persuaded the ratings to surrender; they did not back the revolt's continuation.
xa: Grievances: **poor food**, **low pay**, **racial discrimination**.
Events of **18-22 February**; leaders did not back a **violent revolt**.

n3f7d0fb71a7.s: The 80th anniversary of the Royal Indian Navy revolt was observed on:
n3f7d0fb71a7.x: The 80th anniversary of the RIN revolt was observed on 18 February 2026, marking eight decades since the revolt began in 1946.
n3f7d0fb71a7.tq: Calculate the anniversary from the original revolt year and distinguish the current commemorative date.
xs: The **80th anniversary** was observed on **18 February 2026** — option **(2)** is correct.
The revolt began on **18 February 1946** at **HMIS Talwar, Bombay**.
xa: It was revisited at India's **80th Independence Day** (**Aug 2026**) as a factor that hastened British withdrawal.
Debate: **"mutiny or revolt"**.

n73c042e1fff.s: The INA trials and the RIN revolt alarmed the British mainly because they showed that:
o: The Cabinet Mission had already failed
The Muslim League had merged with the Congress
The princely states had turned against Britain
The Indian Army could no longer be fully trusted
n73c042e1fff.x: The British depended on the 2.5-million-strong Indian Army; the INA trials and RIN revolt showed its loyalty could no longer be assumed.
xa: The RIN mutiny "destroyed the loyalty" of the British Indian armed forces.
**Attlee** called Gandhi's role in the immediate transfer of power **"minimal"** by comparison.

n22f40f8a801.s: According to Attlee's later assessment, which factor was more important than Gandhi's role in the immediate transfer of power?
o: The expansion of British territorial control
The success of the Simon Commission
The formation of the Indian Civil Service
n22f40f8a801.x: Attlee regarded Gandhi's role in the immediate transfer of power as minimal compared with the loss of loyalty in the armed forces.
n22f40f8a801.tq: Test the comparison between political influence and military loyalty directly.
xs: Attlee rated **the loss of military loyalty** above Gandhi's role — option **(4)** is correct.
He called Gandhi's role in the immediate transfer of power **"minimal"**.
xa: The INA trials + RIN revolt showed the **2.5-million** Indian Army could no longer be trusted.
Attlee announced the **Cabinet Mission** on **19 Feb 1946**.

n694ff02c935.s: Mannathu Padmanabhan, known as Bharatha Kesari, founded the:

**K. Kelappan**, the **"Kerala Gandhi"**, is also linked to the **Guruvayur** satyagraha.

naab8d96cb3f.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was 'Andhra Ratna'; Prakasam was 'Andhra Kesari' and Konda Venkatappayya 'Deshabhakta'.
xa: ⚠ Don't confuse **Deshabhakta** (Konda Venkatappayya) with **Deshbandhu** (**C.R. Das**).
Konda Venkatappayya was **dictator** of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha.
Prakasam became the **first CM of Andhra State (1953)**.

ne219d43d2d6.s: Who invited Gandhi on his 1920 Chhattisgarh tour?
ne219d43d2d6.x: Pandit Sundarlal Sharma invited Gandhi; Shaukat Ali accompanied him on the tour.
xa: **C.F. Andrews** — "**Deen Bandhu**", a title given by **Gandhi**.
Andrews lived with Gandhi at **Phoenix Farm** and accompanied him to the **Round Table Conference**.
**Tagore** called Gandhi "**Mahatma**"; **Bose** called him "**Father of the Nation**".

n46870910644.s: Gandhi gave C.F. Andrews the title:
n46870910644.x: Gandhi called C.F. Andrews 'Deen Bandhu'; Andrews lived with Gandhi at Phoenix and accompanied him to the Round Table Conference.
xa: On the **1920 Chhattisgarh tour**, **Sundarlal Sharma** invited Gandhi and **Shaukat Ali** accompanied him.
**Gokhale** was "**Socrates of Maharashtra**" and **Gandhi's political mentor**.

ndf7fbdb0a06.s: Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India' in:
ndf7fbdb0a06.x: Nehru wrote The Discovery of India in Ahmednagar Fort jail; Gandhi's 'Songs from Prison' came from Yerwada.
xa: **Songs from Prison** — **Gandhi**, translations of Sanskrit hymns made in **Yerwada** jail.
**Sarvodaya** — Gandhi's Gujarati rendering of **John Ruskin's "Unto This Last"**.
**Jana Gana Mana** — **Rabindranath Tagore**; **Saare Jahan se Achcha** — **Muhammad Iqbal**.
**Annihilation of Caste** — **B.R. Ambedkar** (**1936**).

ncc7fc742b77.s: Gandhi's 'Sarvodaya' was a Gujarati rendering of:
o: Tolstoy's The Kingdom of God Is Within You
ncc7fc742b77.x: Sarvodaya was Gandhi's Gujarati rendering of Ruskin's Unto This Last.
xa: Gandhi's other works: **Hind Swaraj**, **The Story of My Experiments with Truth**, **Songs from Prison**.
**Pattabhi**: **History of the Indian National Congress**, **Feathers and Stones**.

n5cb53a0a754.s: The song 'Jana Gana Mana' was composed by
n5cb53a0a754.x: Jana Gana Mana was written by Rabindranath Tagore (APPSC 2025). Iqbal wrote 'Saare Jahan se Achcha'; Sarojini Naidu wrote 'The Golden Threshold'; Bankim Chandra is a distractor not linked to this song.
n5cb53a0a754.tq: Jana Gana Mana = Tagore; Saare Jahan se Achcha = Iqbal.

**Muhammad Iqbal** (1) wrote **Saare Jahan se Achcha**; **Sarojini Naidu** (4) wrote **The Golden Threshold**.
xa: Tagore called Gandhi **"Mahatma"**.
⚠ **Saare Jahan se Achcha** = **Iqbal**; **Jana Gana Mana** = **Tagore**.

nf035b57e3fb.s: Gandhi's 'Sarvodaya' was a Gujarati rendering of which work?
o: Leo Tolstoy's 'The Kingdom of God is Within You'

Gandhi founded the **Harijan Sevak Sangh (1932)**.

n55fbb4ee473.s: Who paid the tribute to Gandhi: 'Generations to come... will scarce believe that such a one... walked upon this earth'?

nf985023d58d.s: Vallabhbhai Patel got the title 'Sardar' after the:

n13795d6b5b1.s: Gandhi compared the Cripps offer to a:

n1d5c82217e8.x: Gandhi took the term 'Harijan' from Narsi Mehta, not Kabir.

xa: Gokhale = **"Socrates of Maharashtra"**, Gandhi's political mentor.
**Indira Gandhi** founded the **Bal Charkha Sangh**.

nf4f956bff78.s: The Moderates who formed the National Liberal Federation left the Congress in:

Surendranath Banerjee is associated with the Indian National Liberal Federation. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #118 · pp 213-215]

**M.G. Ranade** — social reform and **gradual reform**.
The Liberal Federation dates to **1918**; Sapru and **V.S. Srinivasa Sastri** were among its presidents.

nindian-history-118-18.s: Which of the following belonged to the Extremist rather than the Moderate tradition?

xa: Other Moderates: **Pherozeshah Mehta**, **M.G. Ranade**, **Surendranath Banerjee**, **V.S. Srinivasa Sastri**.
The Liberal Federation (**1918**) was formed by Moderates who left Congress.

Motilal Nehru was a founder or key personality of the Independent Party. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #114 · pp 209-210]

Inayatullah Mashriqui was a founder or key personality of the Khaksars. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #114 · pp 209-210]
xa: The Khaksars were founded in **1931**.
The **National Liberation Federation** (**1919**) is linked with **Tej Bahadur Sapru**.
⚠ **1934** also gave the **Socialist Party** of **Jayaprakash Narayan**.

n0408ca6edd9.s: Who was the first political prisoner of the Madras Presidency?

n4dacd066afa.s: Who led the Vedaranyam salt march?

**Subramania Siva** was the **Madras Presidency**'s first political prisoner.

nc549e63972b.s: Who founded the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company at Tuticorin?

n778bca605dc.s: Rani Gaidinliu of the Zeliangrong Heraka movement was given the title 'Rani' by:

n9a1ab9b64d9.s: Who was the first president of the All India Kisan Sabha (1936)?

**Birsa Munda** led the Munda **Ulgulan** (Chotanagpur).

nbb4112364cd.s: The Rampa movement is associated with:

Sahajanand was first president of the **All India Kisan Sabha (1936)**.

nde382ac4075.s: Who presided over the Belgaum session of the Congress in 1924?

**Calcutta 1917**: **Annie Besant**; **Calcutta special 1920**: **Lajpat Rai**.

n7dce6df560e.s: Who became the first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh?
n7dce6df560e.x: Sarojini Naidu, associated with Hyderabad and the Dharasana raid of 1930, became the first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh.

n6b2f5ef3fcd.s: Durgabai Deshmukh stopped Jawaharlal Nehru without a pass at which place and event?

ned9403e36b2.s: Who became the first Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953?

nf54591bc057.s: Pingali Venkayya, whose flag design Gandhi endorsed at Vijayawada in 1921, was born at:

nc037fa71a23.s: Potti Sriramulu died on 15 December 1952 after a fast for Andhra State lasting:

n8420dfce729.s: Who served as the 'dictator' of the Salt Satyagraha in Andhra?

xa: **Prakasam** led salt satyagraha in **Madras** and at **Devarampadu**.
