n386fe644499.s: Who called Gandhi the 'Father of the Nation'?
n386fe644499.x: Subhas Chandra Bose called Gandhi the 'Father of the Nation'; Tagore called him 'Mahatma'.
xa: **"Socrates of Maharashtra"** = **Gokhale**, also **Gandhi's political mentor**.
**C.F. Andrews** got the title **"Deen Bandhu"** from **Gandhi**.
"Jhanda Venkayya" and "Diamond Venkayya" = **Pingali**.

n5fb23c41922.s: Who founded the Servants of the People Society?
n5fb23c41922.x: Lala Lajpat Rai founded the Servants of the People Society; Mashriqi founded the Khaksars and Nehru the Independence for India League.
xa: ⚠ Servants of **India** Society (**1905**) = **Gokhale**; Servants of the **People** Society = **Lajpat Rai**.
Khaksars: **1931**; Independence for India League: **1928** (with Bose).

n1bcf4f586fe.s: Who presided over the Indian National Congress session held at Calcutta in 1917?
n1bcf4f586fe.x: Annie Besant presided over the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1917.
n1bcf4f586fe.tq: Match the leader with the correct Congress session and year.
xs: **Annie Besant** presided at **Calcutta 1917** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ **Lajpat Rai** (3) also presided at **Calcutta** — the **special session of 1920**.
xa: **Belgaum 1924**: **Gandhi**; **Kanpur 1925**: **Sarojini Naidu**.
Sarojini Naidu was the first **Indian** woman Congress president.

n3a9067edbce.s: The cut of the revenue increase to about 6 per cent after the Maxwell-Broomfield inquiry was the outcome of the:
n3a9067edbce.x: The 6 per cent cut belongs to Bardoli (1928); Kheda ended with revenue suspended for poor peasants and confiscated property returned.
xa: Kheda outcome: **revenue suspended for poor peasants**; confiscated property returned.
Bardoli hike was about **30%** → cut to **6%**.

nf78cdda60ec.s: Which of the following satyagrahas was led by Vallabhbhai Patel rather than Gandhi?
nf78cdda60ec.x: The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was led by Patel; Champaran, the Ahmedabad Mill Strike and the Dandi March were led by Gandhi.
xa: Patel's other campaigns: **Sarabandi (1922)**, **Borsad (1923)**.
At **Kheda**, Gandhi was spiritual head while **Patel** led mobilisation.

n0cd85c47689.s: The Maxwell-Broomfield inquiry, associated with the Bardoli Satyagraha, resulted in which of the following?
o: Reduction of the proposed increase to about 6 per cent after a fresh survey
Recognition of complete tax exemption for all peasants
Transfer of Bardoli taluk to a princely state
Withdrawal of the entire land revenue system
n0cd85c47689.x: The government suspended the enhanced assessment and ordered a fresh survey; the Maxwell-Broomfield inquiry reduced the increase to about 6 per cent.
n0cd85c47689.tq: Test the inquiry and its quantitative outcome together.
xs: The **Maxwell-Broomfield inquiry** cut the increase to about **6%** after a **fresh survey** — option **(1)**.
The government first **suspended the hike** and ordered the survey.
xa: The original enhancement was about **30%**, despite floods and famine.
Bardoli (**1928**) gave Patel the title **"Sardar"**.

nb77358b45c0.s: The description of the Indian civil service as the ‘steel frame’ of India was used by Patel to emphasise that
o: it was intended only for military administration
it could function without constitutional safeguards
if it bends, the whole structure will collapse
it should be replaced entirely by provincial services
nb77358b45c0.x: Patel stated that if the civil service steel frame bends, the whole structure will collapse, stressing its importance to national administration.
nb77358b45c0.tq: Complete the distinctive metaphor with its stated consequence.
xs: Patel's **"steel frame"**: **"If it bends, the whole structure will collapse"** — option **(3)**.
He **created** the All India Services (**IAS/IPS**).
xa: He addressed the first IAS probationers at **Metcalfe House, Delhi**, **21 April 1947** — now **Civil Services Day**.
Hence the title **"Patron Saint of Indian Civil Servants"**.

n86a7753570e.s: The popular title ‘Iron Man of India’ is chiefly associated with Vallabhbhai Patel’s role in
o: Leading the Civil Disobedience Movement in Gujarat
Drafting the Karachi Resolution on Fundamental Rights
n86a7753570e.x: Patel is popularly called the Iron Man of India for his role in integrating approximately 565 princely states.
n86a7753570e.tq: Match a title with the achievement that explains it.
xs: **"Iron Man of India"** is for **integrating about 565 princely states** — option **(1)**.
⚠ **"Iron Man"** = princely states; **"Patron Saint"** = All India Services.
xa: He ran the **States Department** with **V.P. Menon**.
**"Sardar"** came from **Bardoli (1928)**.

n5107d3776ba.s: Why has Vallabhbhai Patel been described as the ‘Patron Saint of Indian Civil Servants’?
o: He abolished the civil services after independence.
He served as the first Governor-General of India.
He created and defended the All India Services.
He introduced provincial elections under the Government of India Act, 1935.
n5107d3776ba.x: The description refers to Patel’s role in creating the All India Services and supporting their importance in administration.
n5107d3776ba.tq: Infer the title from the institutional contribution associated with it.
xs: Patel **created** the **All India Services** (**IAS/IPS**) — hence **"Patron Saint of Indian Civil Servants"** — option **(3)**.
He called the service the **"steel frame"**: "If it bends, the whole structure will collapse."
He ran the **1937** elections (4) as head of the **Congress Parliamentary Board** — a separate role.
xa: **21 April 1947** Metcalfe House speech → **Civil Services Day**.
⚠ **"Patron Saint"** = All India Services; **"Iron Man"** = princely states.

n44b848e1eed.s: Who headed the Congress Parliamentary Board that ran the 1937 provincial elections?
n44b848e1eed.x: As head of the Congress Parliamentary Board, Patel ran the 1937 elections and supervised the Congress ministries' discipline, elections and finances.
xa: He was **Gujarat PCC** president for **over two decades**.
Assessment: **"While Gandhi gave the moral vision, Patel was the machine"**.

n8ee70ad69a8.s: Who was the first Deputy Prime Minister of India?
n8ee70ad69a8.x: Patel was the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister and handled the States Department.
xa: He **created** the All India Services (**IAS/IPS**).
Earlier, in the **Interim Government** (**2 September 1946**): Home + I&B.

nindian-history-104-1.s: Who was the temporary Chairman of the Constituent Assembly when it first met on 9 December 1946?
nindian-history-104-1.x: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member, was temporary Chairman; Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 December 1946.
n: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the Temporary Chairman of the Constituent Assembly. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #104 · pp 193-194]
Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the first President of the Constituent Assembly. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #104 · pp 193-194]
xa: **Sardar Patel** chaired the **Advisory Committee** and the **Provincial Constitution Committee**.
Patel was the **First Deputy Prime Minister** and **Home Minister**; **V.P. Menon** was Secretary of the **States Department**.
In the **Interim Government** (**2 September 1946**) Patel held **Home** + Information & Broadcasting.

nindian-history-104-17.s: The chairmanship of which committee was held by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel?
nindian-history-104-17.x: Sardar Patel chaired the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights and Minorities. Nehru chaired the Union Powers and Union Constitution Committees and Ambedkar the Drafting Committee.
nindian-history-104-17.tq: Recall the chairman of each committee.
n: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #104 · pp 193-194]
Jawaharlal Nehru was the Chairman of the Union Powers Committee. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #104 · pp 193-194]
Jawaharlal Nehru was the Chairman of the Union Constitution Committee. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #104 · pp 193-194]
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was the Chairman of the Advisory Committee. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #104 · pp 193-194]
xs: **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel** chaired the **Advisory Committee** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was the **Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, Tribal and Excluded Areas**.
**Nehru** chaired the **Union Powers** and **Union Constitution** Committees; **Ambedkar** the **Drafting Committee**.
xa: Patel also chaired the **Provincial Constitution Committee**.
**Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha** = Temporary Chairman; **Dr. Rajendra Prasad** = Permanent President.
Patel addressed the first IAS probationers at **Metcalfe House** on **21 April 1947** — now **Civil Services Day**.
He called the civil service the "**steel frame**".

n7d460fefb77.s: Who referred the Kashmir issue to the United Nations?
n7d460fefb77.x: Nehru referred the issue to the UN, influenced by idealism and Mountbatten's advice, while Patel was sceptical and preferred a military solution.
xa: **Hyderabad**: Patel ordered **Operation Polo** (**Sept 1948**).
**China**: Patel warned Nehru after **Tibet** (**7 November 1950**).

n9ef75713065.s: Patel warned Nehru about China in a letter dated
n9ef75713065.x: Patel warned Nehru about China after Tibet in his letter of 7 November 1950.
n9ef75713065.tq: Use the exact date associated with a diplomatic warning.
xs: Patel warned Nehru about **China** after **Tibet** in his letter of **7 November 1950** — option **(1)**.
**26 January 1950** and **15 August 1947** are unrelated to the letter; Patel's birth anniversary is **31 October**.
xa: Other Patel–Nehru issues: **Kashmir** (UN vs military solution), **Hyderabad** (**Operation Polo**, **Sept 1948**).
Patel was the **first Deputy Prime Minister** and **Home Minister**.

n6f15cb41c94.s: Patel addressed the first IAS probationers at Metcalfe House, Delhi, on
n6f15cb41c94.x: Patel addressed the first IAS probationers at Metcalfe House, Delhi, on 21 April 1947; the date is now observed as Civil Services Day.
n6f15cb41c94.tq: Use the exact date to distinguish the speech from later national commemorations.
xs: Patel addressed the first IAS probationers at **Metcalfe House** on **21 April 1947** — option **(2)**.
This date is now **Civil Services Day**.
⚠ **21 April** is not Patel's birthday — that is **31 October** (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas).
xa: Patel **created** the **IAS/IPS**.
The civil service was his **"steel frame"**.

n632a7e8715a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Statue of Unity?
o: It was sculpted by Ram V. Sutar
n632a7e8715a.x: The Statue of Unity is in Gujarat (facing the Sardar Sarovar Dam), not Hyderabad.
xa: ⚠ **2018** = Statue unveiled; **2019** = Unity Award instituted.
The **150th birth anniversary** commemoration was launched there on **31 Oct 2024**.

nf771fee44b6.s: Rashtriya Ekta Diwas is observed on 31 October because it marks
o: the unveiling of the Statue of Unity
the formation of the Interim Government
nf771fee44b6.x: National Unity Day is observed on 31 October, the birth anniversary of Vallabhbhai Patel, who was born on 31 October 1875 at Nadiad.
nf771fee44b6.tq: Connect the observance with the person and the exact birth date.
xs: **31 October** is **Patel's birth anniversary** (born **31 October 1875, Nadiad**) — option **(3)**.
The Statue of Unity (1) was unveiled in **2018**, not tied to this date.
xa: ⚠ **21 April** = Civil Services Day, not Patel's birthday.
**Sardar Patel National Unity Award** instituted **2019**.

n6e17e913cd7.s: Who was the Secretary and chief negotiator of the States Department headed by Sardar Patel?
n6e17e913cd7.x: V.P. Menon was Secretary and chief negotiator of the States Department, which Patel headed.
xa: Patel was **Deputy PM and Home Minister**, called the "**Iron Man of India**".
Menon wrote "**The Story of the Integration of the Indian States**".
Menon's four phases: **Extinction**, **Consolidation into unions**, **Democratisation**, **Abolition of privy purses**.

n9ecb0533ef5.s: Under the Indian Independence Act, 1947, a princely state could:
o: Transfer its decision to the United Nations
Join India, join Pakistan or remain independent
n9ecb0533ef5.x: The Indian Independence Act, 1947, allowed princely states to join India, join Pakistan or remain independent.
n9ecb0533ef5.tq: Test the complete three-way choice instead of confusing legal options with the later political outcome.
xs: Under the **Indian Independence Act 1947**, a princely state could **join India, join Pakistan or remain independent** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The Act gave all three choices, so "India only" or "Pakistan only" is wrong.
xa: About **562** princely states were involved.
Accession was through the **Instrument of Accession**, ceding **Defence, External Affairs and Communications**.
Hold-outs on **15 August 1947**: **Kashmir, Hyderabad and Junagadh**.

n98e9c50b16f.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the subjects ceded to the Centre through the Instrument of Accession?
n98e9c50b16f.x: The Instrument of Accession initially transferred Defence, External Affairs and Communications to the Centre. Internal autonomy was retained by the rulers at that stage.
n98e9c50b16f.tq: Find the exception by separating the three ceded subjects from the retained internal autonomy.
xs: **Internal administration** was NOT ceded: rulers kept **internal autonomy** at first — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Instrument of Accession** ceded only **Defence, External Affairs and Communications** to the Centre.
xa: In return the rulers received **privy purses**, guaranteed annual payments for accession.
Privy purses and royal titles were abolished by the **26th Amendment Act (1971)**, which omitted **Articles 291 and 362**.
**Kashmir** signed its IoA on **26 Oct 1947** after the tribal invasion.

n72f846c50ad.s: The accession of Jammu and Kashmir in the context of the first India–Pakistan conflict took place on:
n72f846c50ad.x: Jammu and Kashmir acceded to India on 26 October 1947. The UN ceasefire in the conflict came into effect later, on 1 January 1949.
n72f846c50ad.tq: Separate the date of accession from the later date of the UN ceasefire.
xs: **Jammu and Kashmir** signed the **Instrument of Accession** on **26 October 1947** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Sequence: **tribal invasion** → **IoA** → troops airlifted to **Srinagar** → **First Indo-Pak war** → **UN ceasefire Jan 1949**.
**15 August 1947** was when Kashmir was still a hold-out, with **Hyderabad and Junagadh**.
xa: Ruler: Maharaja **Hari Singh**.
**Nehru** took Kashmir to the **UN**; **Patel** preferred a military solution.
The **Delhi Agreement (1952)** concerned Kashmir.

nf299e53f654.s: Before Operation Polo, the Nizam of Hyderabad sought:
nf299e53f654.x: Mir Osman Ali Khan wanted Hyderabad to stay independent or accede to Pakistan.
xa: The Nizam banned **Indian currency** and imported arms from **Pakistan**.
The **Standstill Agreement** was signed on **29 November 1947** for **one year**.
**Moin Nawaz Jung** led the Nizam's delegation to the **UN Security Council (1948)**.

n71f916d7c7b.s: The integration of Junagadh was resolved through:
o: An Instrument of Accession followed by war
n71f916d7c7b.x: Junagadh was resolved by a plebiscite, Hyderabad by police action, and Kashmir by an Instrument of Accession followed by war.
xa: These three had not signed by **15 August 1947**.
Kashmir war ended with the **UN ceasefire Jan 1949**.
**Nehru** took Kashmir to the **UN**; **Patel** preferred a military solution.

nc88f0e387d6.s: At the time of integration, Hyderabad was regarded as the ____ princely state.
nc88f0e387d6.x: Hyderabad was regarded as the largest and richest princely state and ranked first in population.
xa: Last Nizam: **Mir Osman Ali Khan**, the **7th Nizam**.
Asaf Jahi dynasty founded by **Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I** in **1724**.
On **1 November 1956** it was split: Telugu districts to **Andhra Pradesh**, **Marathwada** to **Bombay**, **Raichur/Gulbarga** to **Mysore**.

na2f2de10e0a.s: The Standstill Agreement between Hyderabad and the Government of India was intended primarily to:
o: Maintain existing arrangements for one year while negotiations continued
Transfer all administrative powers to the Indian Army
Create the Dominion of Hyderabad as an independent country
Provide for the immediate abolition of the Nizam’s office
na2f2de10e0a.x: The Agreement was for one year and maintained existing arrangements with India while discussions regarding Hyderabad’s future continued.
na2f2de10e0a.tq: Identify the practical purpose of an agreement instead of confusing it with the final accession arrangement.
xs: The **Standstill Agreement** kept **existing arrangements with India** for **one year** while talks went on — so option **(1)** is correct.
It did not create a "**Dominion of Hyderabad**" — that was the Nizam's own aim in defiance of it.
xa: Signed **29 November 1947** (APPSC G2 2012 key); the Nizam's defiance continued.
Violations: banning **Indian currency** and importing arms from **Pakistan**.
The deadlock ended with **Operation Polo** (**13-17 September 1948**).

n6aaedce6bfd.s: Operation Polo, also known as the Hyderabad Police Action, was conducted during which period?
n6aaedce6bfd.x: Operation Polo was conducted from 13 to 17 September 1948, ending with the surrender and accession of the Nizam.
n6aaedce6bfd.tq: Use the exact date range to distinguish the operation from the Standstill Agreement and later reorganisation.
xs: **Operation Polo** ran from **13-17 September 1948** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It lasted about **four to five days** and ended with the Nizam's surrender and accession on **17 September 1948**.
**29 November 1947** was the **Standstill Agreement**; **1 November 1956** was the dissolution of Hyderabad State.
xa: Indian commander: **Maj. Gen. J.N. Chaudhuri**, later **Military Governor**.
**17 September 1948** ended Nizam rule over **Telangana**.
⚠ **Operation Polo** (Hyderabad 1948) vs **Operation Vijay** (Goa 1961).

n277efcb4c9d.s: The movement in Hyderabad demanding merger with the Indian Union was led by:
n277efcb4c9d.x: Swami Ramananda Theertha led the Join Indian Union movement through the Hyderabad State Congress.
n277efcb4c9d.tq: Use the state-specific leader association to separate Hyderabad from other Praja Mandal movements.
xs: The "**Join Indian Union**" movement in Hyderabad was led by **Swami Ramananda Theertha** through the **Hyderabad State Congress** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Vijay Singh Pathik** led the **Bijolia** movement in **Rajasthan**; **Sewa Singh Thikriwala** led the **Riyasti Praja Mandal** in **Punjab (Patiala)**.
**Sarangadhar Das** led the **Dhenkanal Praja Mandal** in **Orissa**.
xa: The **Hyderabad State Congress** was formed in **1938**.
⚠ **1927** = **AISPC** founded **and** **Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen** emerged; **1938** = Hyderabad State Congress.
The **Razakars**, led by **Kasim Razvi**, were the militia of the **MIM**; their violence forced **Operation Polo (1948)**.

n60ace5e9392.x: Laik Ali, the last Prime Minister of Hyderabad, wrote Hyderabad in Retrospect; V.P. Menon wrote The Story of the Integration of the Indian States.
xa: V.P. Menon was **Secretary and chief negotiator** of the **States Department** under **Sardar Patel**.
Hyderabad questions (**Standstill Agreement**, **Razvi**, **Laik Ali**, **Moin Nawaz Jung**) recur in APPSC.
**Burgula Ramakrishna Rao** became the **first elected CM** of Hyderabad State in **1952**.

n40f8893f104.s: Who led the Nizam’s delegation to the United Nations Security Council in 1948?
n40f8893f104.x: Moin Nawaz Jung led the Nizam’s delegation to the United Nations Security Council in 1948.
n40f8893f104.tq: Distinguish the Hyderabad diplomat from the Prime Minister, Dewan and Indian negotiator names.
xs: **Moin Nawaz Jung** led the Nizam's delegation to the **UN Security Council** in **1948** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**V.P. Menon** was India's chief negotiator; **Laik Ali** was the **last Prime Minister of Hyderabad**; **Shah Nawaz Bhutto** was **Dewan of Junagadh**.
xa: This is an **APPSC G2 2012** key.
Laik Ali wrote "**Hyderabad in Retrospect**".
The Nizam's army chief was **Maj. Gen. El Edroos**.

n2177d58b582.s: Who was the first elected Chief Minister of Hyderabad State (1952)?
n2177d58b582.x: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao became the first elected CM of Hyderabad State in 1952. J.N. Chaudhuri was the Military Governor after Operation Polo; Prakasam was the first CM of Andhra State (1953); Ramananda Tirtha led the Hyderabad State Congress.
n2177d58b582.tq: Hyderabad State CM 1952 = Burgula; Andhra State CM 1953 = Prakasam.
xs: **Burgula Ramakrishna Rao** became the **first elected CM** of Hyderabad State in **1952** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**J.N. Chaudhuri** was **Military Governor** after Operation Polo; **Swami Ramananda Tirtha** led the **Hyderabad State Congress**.
xa: Hyderabad was a **Part B state (1950-56)** with the Nizam as **Rajpramukh**.
The State was dissolved on **1 November 1956**.
Hyderabad ranked **1st in population** among princely states (**1,63,38,534** in **1951**).

n15118474ac8.s: The Haripura Congress (1938) declared that Purna Swaraj covered:
n15118474ac8.x: Moving away from non-interference, the Haripura Congress (1938) declared that Purna Swaraj covered the states; Tripuri (1939) openly backed state movements.
xa: **Nehru** became president of the **AISPC** in **1939**, the same year as Tripuri.
The **Indian Independence Act 1947** let princely states join India, join Pakistan or stay independent.
The **Hyderabad State Congress** was founded in **1938**, the Haripura year.

na3665544a73.s: The Telangana armed struggle (1946-51) was withdrawn in:
na3665544a73.x: The struggle, led by the Communists and the Andhra Mahasabha, was withdrawn in October 1951, not right after Operation Polo.
xa: Trigger: killing of **Doddi Komaraiah (1946)**.
Unrest + Razakar violence → **Operation Polo (1948)**.
The Razakars were the MIM militia led by **Kasim Razvi**.

n5c690e96b3e.s: The immediate incident that set off the Telangana armed struggle was the killing of:
n5c690e96b3e.x: The killing of Doddi Komaraiah in 1946 helped set off the Telangana armed struggle.
n5c690e96b3e.tq: Match the triggering incident with the individual involved rather than a later political leader.
xs: The killing of **Doddi Komaraiah** in **1946** set off the **Telangana armed struggle** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Moin Nawaz Jung** led the Nizam's UN delegation; **Laik Ali** was the last PM of Hyderabad.
xa: The revolt (**1946-51**) was led by the **Communists and the Andhra Mahasabha**.
It was against the **Nizam**, the **deshmukhs** and later the **Razakars**.
Withdrawn in **October 1951**.

n179085fd6c8.s: Privy purses and royal titles were abolished by the:
n179085fd6c8.x: The 26th Amendment Act, 1971 abolished privy purses and titles, omitting Articles 291 and 362; the Rajpramukh office ended with the 7th Amendment.
xa: ⚠ **26th (1971)** = privy purses; **7th (1956)** = Rajpramukhs.
Privy purses were guaranteed annual payments to rulers for accession.
Abolition of privy purses was Menon's **fourth phase**.

n37e62fc8a29.s: Yanam, a French-origin enclave inside Andhra Pradesh, is administered as part of:
n37e62fc8a29.x: Yanam lies inside Andhra Pradesh's Godavari delta but is administered as part of the Puducherry Union Territory.
xa: Portuguese possessions came by **Operation Vijay** (**December 1961**), led by **Maj. Gen. K.P. Candeth**.
**Goa, Daman and Diu (1961)** = last European possessions freed; **Goa** became a full state in **1987**.
AP angle: Hyderabad's Telugu districts joined **Andhra State** in **1956** to form Andhra Pradesh.

nda63c9ebd29.s: Mir Osman Ali Khan, the ruler of Hyderabad at the time of integration, was which Nizam of the Asaf Jahi dynasty?
nda63c9ebd29.x: Mir Osman Ali Khan was the seventh Nizam of the Asaf Jahi dynasty, founded by Asaf Jah I in 1724.
xa: Hyderabad was the **largest and richest** princely state, **1st in population** (**1,63,38,534** in **1951**).
⚠ Exam trap: **Asaf Jahi** vs **Qutb Shahi**.
After **1950** Hyderabad was a **Part B state** with the Nizam as **Rajpramukh**.

na1379796f96.s: The Razakars, the militant volunteer force of the Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen, were led by:
na1379796f96.x: The Razakars were led by Kasim (Qasim) Razvi; Laik Ali was the last Prime Minister of Hyderabad.
xa: ⚠ **1927** = AISPC founded **and** Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen emerged.
Razakar violence forced military action (APHQ 2011 key).
They also targeted the **Telangana armed struggle**.

nee757316dc7.s: In the 1950 classification of states, Part D consisted of:
nee757316dc7.x: Part D was the Andaman and Nicobar Islands; Part A were former Governor's provinces, Part B princely unions with Rajpramukhs and Part C Chief Commissioners' provinces.
xa: Hyderabad was a **Part B state (1950-56)** with the Nizam as Rajpramukh.
The **7th Amendment (1956)** ended the office of **Rajpramukh**.
Unions like **Saurashtra**, **Rajasthan Union**, **PEPSU**, **Madhya Bharat** were consolidated princely states.

n11b0272ace1.s: Operation Vijay (December 1961), which liberated Goa, was led by:
n11b0272ace1.x: Operation Vijay was led by Maj. Gen. K.P. Candeth; J.N. Chaudhuri led Operation Polo in Hyderabad.
xa: The Portuguese surrender marked the **end of European colonial rule in India**.
Portugal also held **Dadra and Nagar Haveli**.
French possessions were handed over in **1954**.

naf546f09393.s: On 1 November 1956, the Marathwada region of Hyderabad State was transferred to:
naf546f09393.x: Marathwada went to Bombay State, the Telugu districts to Andhra Pradesh, and Raichur and Gulbarga to Mysore.
xa: Before that, Hyderabad was a **Part B state (1950-56)** with the Nizam as **Rajpramukh**.
Hyderabad's Telugu districts joined **Andhra State** in **1956** to form Andhra Pradesh.
**Yanam** (**Puducherry**) sits inside AP.

n88678c240ca.s: The Portuguese surrender in December 1961 marked the:
o: end of European colonial rule in India
integration of Hyderabad into the Indian Union
beginning of French rule in India
n88678c240ca.x: The Portuguese surrender in December 1961 marked the end of European colonial rule in India.
n88678c240ca.tq: Identify the significance of an event rather than merely recalling its date.
xs: The **Portuguese surrender (December 1961)** marked the **end of European colonial rule in India** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It came through **Operation Vijay**, led by **Maj. Gen. K.P. Candeth**, freeing **Goa, Daman and Diu**.
Hyderabad was integrated by **Operation Polo (1948)**.

**Sir Cyril Radcliffe** chaired both the **Punjab and Bengal** boundary commissions; award on **17 August 1947**.
The **Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947)** set out partition into two dominions.

nindian-history-105-1.s: The First Interim Government of India was formed on:
nindian-history-105-1.x: The first Interim Government took office on 2 September 1946. Wavell invited Nehru on 12 August, its composition was announced on 24 August, and Attlee's announcement came on 20 February 1947.
nindian-history-105-1.tq: Recall the dates in the Interim Government process.
n: The Interim Government of India was first formed on 2 September 1946. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #105 · pp 194-197]
Lord Wavell invited Congress President Jawaharlal Nehru to form the Interim Government on 12 August 1946. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #105 · pp 194-197]
The Congress announced the formation of the Interim Government under Jawaharlal Nehru on 24 August 1946. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #105 · pp 194-197]
Clement Attlee announced on 20 February 1947 the transfer of power to Indian hands before June 1948. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #105 · pp 194-197]
xs: The First Interim Government was **formed on 2 September 1946** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**12 August 1946**: **Lord Wavell** invited **Nehru** to form it.
**24 August 1946**: the **Congress announced** its formation under Nehru.
xa: The **Muslim League** joined in **October 1946** with **5** nominees.
It was envisaged by the **Cabinet Mission Plan (1946)**.
⚠ **Abul Kalam Azad** was **not** a member of the Interim Government in **1946**.

ne38bd2d366e.s: The Radcliffe Award announcing the partition boundaries was published on
ne38bd2d366e.x: Although independence took place on 15 August 1947, the Radcliffe Award was announced two days later, on 17 August 1947.
ne38bd2d366e.tq: Distinguish the boundary announcement date from the date of independence.
xs: The **Radcliffe Award** was announced on **17 August 1947** — so option **(2)** is correct.
That was **after** independence on **15 Aug 1947**; **3 June 1947** was the **Mountbatten Plan**.
xa: **Sir Cyril Radcliffe** chaired both the **Punjab and Bengal** commissions.
Referendum provinces were only **NWFP** and **Sylhet (Assam)**.
**Sindh**'s own assembly decided its future.

n33cf3db42f2.s: The C.R. Formula was authored by:
n33cf3db42f2.x: The C.R. Formula was proposed by C. Rajagopalachari in 1944. It was not a proposal of Lord Wavell.
n33cf3db42f2.tq: Use the author–proposal association and reject the look-alike attribution.
xs: The **C.R. Formula (1944)** was authored by **C. Rajagopalachari** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes wrongly credit **Lord Wavell**; Wavell's own proposal was the **Wavell Plan (1945)**.
**Bhulabhai Desai** is linked to the **Desai-Liaquat Pact (1945)**; **Maulana Azad** led the Congress at **Simla**.
xa: It proposed a post-war **plebiscite** in contiguous Muslim-majority areas (NW and NE).
**Gandhi-Jinnah talks** in Bombay (**9-27 Sept 1944**) on its basis failed.
Rejected by both Congress and League: **Jinnah** wanted only Muslims to vote and **no common centre**.

nb3198a30e78.s: The Muslim League joined the Interim Government in:
nb3198a30e78.x: The Muslim League entered the Interim Government in October 1946.
nb3198a30e78.tq: Distinguish the date of the original formation from the month of League participation.
xs: The **Muslim League** joined the Interim Government in **October 1946** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Government itself had been formed on **2 September 1946** without it.
xa: It came in with **5** nominees; **Sarat Chandra Bose**, **Shafaat Ahmed Khan** and **Syed Ali Zaheer** made way.
The League still **refused to attend** the Constituent Assembly.
**Liaquat Ali Khan** became **Finance** Member.

nindian-history-105-15.s: The first Interim Government headed by Nehru took office on:
nindian-history-105-15.x: Wavell invited Nehru on 12 August 1946 and the Interim Government took office on 2 September 1946.
n: The Interim Government of India was first formed on 2 September 1946. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #105 · pp 194-197]
Lord Wavell invited Congress President Jawaharlal Nehru to form the Interim Government on 12 August 1946. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #105 · pp 194-197]
Clement Attlee announced on 20 February 1947 the transfer of power to Indian hands before June 1948. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #105 · pp 194-197]
The Mountbatten Plan was issued on 3 June 1947. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #105 · pp 194-197]
xa: The **Mountbatten (June 3) Plan** partitioned India into two dominions and advanced the date to **15 Aug 1947**.
**Mountbatten replaced Wavell** as Viceroy in **March 1947**.
**Direct Action Day** — **16 August 1946**.

nindian-history-105-20.s: Who among the following was NOT a member of the Interim Government formed in 1946?
nindian-history-105-20.x: Liaquat Ali Khan (Finance), Baldev Singh (Defence) and Asaf Ali (Railways and Transport) were members of the Interim Government; B.R. Ambedkar was not.
n: Baldev Singh held the Defence portfolio in the Interim Government. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #105 · pp 194-197]
Asaf Ali held the Railways and Transport portfolio in the Interim Government. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #105 · pp 194-197]
Liaquat Ali Khan held the Finance portfolio in the Interim Government. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #105 · pp 194-197]
Abul Kalam Azad was not a member of the Interim Government in 1946. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #105 · pp 194-197]
xa: At the **Simla Conference** (**1945**), Congress was led by **Maulana Azad**.
Other members: **Nehru** (External Affairs), **Patel** (Home), **Rajendra Prasad** (Food and Agriculture).
The League joined in **October 1946** with **5** nominees.
nindian-history-105-20.fixed: Azad joined the Interim Government as Education Member (Jan 1947) per APPSC key y571a35c6f72; Ambedkar was never a member (y8090b4fe0f8)

ne743b6bc31b.s: The League’s call for ‘Direct Action’ was issued after it
o: accepted the Mountbatten Plan without reservation
accepted the Cabinet Mission Plan and joined the interim government
withdrew its acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan
ne743b6bc31b.x: The Muslim League called for Direct Action on 29 July 1946 after withdrawing its acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan.
xs: The League called for **Direct Action** on **29 July 1946** after it **withdrew its acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Mountbatten Plan** (**3 June 1947**) and the **Indian Independence Act** came a year later.
xa: Jinnah also condemned **Wavell's invitation to Congress** to form the interim government.
**Direct Action Day**: **16 August 1946**, a "bandh" call to press for **Pakistan**.
Riots began in **Calcutta** — the "**Great Calcutta Killings**".

n4811282710d.s: In March 1947, Gandhi went to ____ to calm riots against Muslims.
n4811282710d.x: After his Noakhali mission (Nov 1946 - Mar 1947), Gandhi went to Bihar in March 1947 to calm anti-Muslim riots.
xa: On **15 August 1947** he was in **Calcutta (Beliaghata)**, fasting and praying.
**Mountbatten** called him a "**one-man boundary force**".
Assassinated by **Nathuram Godse** in New Delhi on **30 January 1948**.

naf70610b4ff.s: On 15 August 1947, Mahatma Gandhi was fasting and praying at:
naf70610b4ff.x: Gandhi spent 15 August 1947 at Beliaghata in Calcutta, fasting and praying, rather than attending the Delhi celebrations.
xa: **Mountbatten** called him a "**one-man boundary force**".
**Nehru** gave the "**Tryst with Destiny**" midnight speech.
Gandhi was assassinated on **30 January 1948** in **New Delhi**.

na9ed150bb70.s: Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated on 30 January 1948 at
na9ed150bb70.x: Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated by Nathuram Godse in New Delhi on 30 January 1948.
xs: Gandhi was assassinated by **Nathuram Godse** in **New Delhi** on **30 January 1948** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Beliaghata, Calcutta** is where he spent **15 August 1947**; **Noakhali** was his **Nov 1946 - March 1947** peace mission.
xa: **Nehru**: "**The light has gone out of our lives**".
It happened while **Mountbatten** was **Governor-General**.
In **March 1947** he went to **Bihar** to calm riots.

n9f256bb7450.s: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 is best described as the law that
o: gave legal force to the Mountbatten Plan
gave legal force to the Cabinet Mission Plan
replaced the Government of India Act, 1935 with a new constitution
n9f256bb7450.x: The Act (introduced 4 July, royal assent 18 July, effective 15 August 1947) legalised the Mountbatten (3 June) Plan. The Cabinet Mission Plan and C.R. Formula were earlier schemes; the GoI Act 1935, as adapted, continued as interim law and was not replaced by a constitution.
n9f256bb7450.tq: 3 June Plan -> Indian Independence Act (assent 18 July) -> 15 Aug 1947.
xs: The **Indian Independence Act** **gave legal force to the Mountbatten Plan** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Cabinet Mission Plan** and the **C.R. Formula** were earlier schemes.
The **GoI Act 1935** (as adapted) continued as interim law; the Act did not replace it with a constitution.
xa: Introduced **4 July**, royal assent **18 July**, effective **15 August 1947**.
Most distinctive feature: an **Act without a constitution** (APPSC-G2 2017).
It abolished the offices of **Viceroy** and **Secretary of State for India**.

n349edabedeb.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Mountbatten Plan?
o: Princely states were given a third option of remaining completely independent.
Sindh was to decide on partition through its own legislative assembly.
The Punjab and Bengal assemblies were to vote on partition in two parts.
Referendums were provided for in NWFP and Sylhet district.
n349edabedeb.x: No third option was provided: paramountcy lapsed and the states could join India or Pakistan.
xa: A **Boundary Commission** was set up for Punjab and Bengal.
**NWFP** joined Pakistan despite the **Khudai Khidmatgar** boycott.
Armed forces were divided; power transferred under the **GoI Act 1935**.

n420d901bc09.s: The transfer of power originally contemplated for June 1948 was advanced to
n420d901bc09.x: The Mountbatten Plan advanced the transfer of power from June 1948 to 15 August 1947.
n420d901bc09.tq: Compare the originally proposed date with the advanced date.
xs: The **Mountbatten Plan** advanced the transfer from **June 1948** to **15 August 1947** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**17 August 1947** was when the **Radcliffe award** was published; **3 June 1947** was the plan's announcement.
xa: ⚠ Attlee deadline **30 June 1948** → advanced to **15 August 1947**.
The **Indian Independence Act** got **royal assent** on **18 July 1947** and took effect on **15 August 1947**.
Criticism: the **haste** of the advanced date worsened the violence.

nf5c0e24a06d.s: Under the Indian Independence Act, 1947, the princely states were given the option to
o: form a single federation under the British Crown
accede to either India or Pakistan
nf5c0e24a06d.x: With the lapse of paramountcy, the 565 princely states were free to accede to India or Pakistan. Independence for the princely states was not the intended constitutional arrangement.
nf5c0e24a06d.tq: Apply the legal effect of lapse of paramountcy to the position of princely states.
xs: With **British paramountcy lapsed**, the **565** princely states were free to **accede to India or Pakistan** — so option **(4)** is correct.
There was **no third option** of independence, and paramountcy did not continue.
xa: **Boundary Commissions** for **Punjab and Bengal**; armed forces divided.
Referendums in **NWFP and Sylhet**.
Kashmir's accession came in **Oct 1947**, under **Mountbatten** as GG.

na0cf3dd32a1.s: Plan Balkan, an earlier scheme of Lord Mountbatten (May 1947), was rejected by:
na0cf3dd32a1.x: Nehru rejected Plan Balkan because it could lead to the Balkanisation of India.
xa: Some notes credit Plan Balkan to **Wavell**; the standard attribution is **Mountbatten**.
It gave way to the **Mountbatten (3 June) Plan, 1947**.
The United Bengal plan was rejected by **Congress and League**.

n242a9b9f110.s: Who suggested immediate transfer of power on dominion status, thereby avoiding the need to frame a new constitution before the transfer?
n242a9b9f110.x: V.P. Menon suggested immediate transfer of power on dominion status without waiting for a new constitution.
xs: **V.P. Menon** suggested immediate transfer on **dominion status**, bypassing a new constitution first — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Cyril Radcliffe** chaired the **Boundary Commissions**; **J.B. Kripalani** was **INC President**; **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan** led the **Khudai Khidmatgar** boycott in NWFP.
xa: Significance: dominion status let India and Pakistan become **free before writing constitutions**.
The **Indian Independence Act** is "an **Act without a constitution**" (APPSC-G2 2017).
Power was transferred on the basis of the **GoI Act 1935**.

n0155d63a734.s: The Congress accepted partition in 1947 mainly to:
o: avoid Balkanisation, secure a strong Centre and end communal bloodshed
retain British paramountcy over the princely states
prevent the formation of two dominions
n0155d63a734.x: Congress accepted partition to avoid Balkanisation, establish a strong Centre and bring an end to communal bloodshed.
xa: **Nehru** had already rejected **Plan Balkan** as **Balkanisation** of India.
The plan itself accepted Pakistan to avoid **civil war and administrative collapse**.
**INC President** at independence: **J.B. Kripalani**.

nb4907c3dc64.s: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 received the Royal Assent on
nb4907c3dc64.x: The Act received Royal Assent on 18 July 1947. It came into effect on 15 August 1947.
nb4907c3dc64.tq: Discriminate between the date of Royal Assent and the date on which the Act became effective.
xs: The **Indian Independence Act** received **Royal Assent** on **18 July 1947** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It came into effect on **15 August 1947**; **3 June 1947** was the **Mountbatten Plan**.
xa: Bill introduced in the **House of Commons** on **4 July 1947** (APPSC G1 2022).
⚠ Trap: "passed on 4 July" is wrong (introduced then); "passed on 18 July" was royal assent.
APPSC-GS 2007 keyed "**3 July**" for introduction; the standard date is **4 July**.

n8a3bf934df8.s: The Indian Independence Bill was introduced in the House of Commons on
n8a3bf934df8.x: The Indian Independence Bill was introduced in the House of Commons on 4 July 1947.
n8a3bf934df8.tq: Distinguish closely related dates in sequence.
xs: The Bill was introduced in the **House of Commons** on **4 July 1947** — so option **(4)** is correct (APPSC G1 2022).
**18 July 1947** = **royal assent**; **3 June 1947** = **Mountbatten Plan**; **15 August 1947** = effective date.
xa: ⚠ APPSC-GS 2007 keyed "**3 July**"; the standard date is **4 July**.
Passed by the Commons / Lords on **15 July / 16 July 1947**.
The Act **legalised the Mountbatten Plan**.

nfe6afd403f8.s: Until new constitutions were framed, governance in India and Pakistan was to be carried on under the
o: Government of India Act, 1935, as adapted
nfe6afd403f8.x: The Government of India Act, 1935, as adapted, continued to govern the dominions until their new constitutions were framed.
xs: Each dominion was governed by the **Government of India Act 1935, as adapted**, until its new constitution — so option **(4)** is correct.
The Mountbatten Plan's transfer of power was also on the basis of the **GoI Act 1935**.
xa: The **Constituent Assemblies** also acted as **dominion legislatures**.
They could repeal any British law, including the Independence Act.
Hence the Act is called "an **Act without a constitution**".

n4fa6aa8b8f1.s: Under the Indian Independence Act, 1947, the Constituent Assemblies of the two dominions were given ____ power to frame any Constitution.
n4fa6aa8b8f1.x: The Act gave the Constituent Assemblies sovereign power, including the power to repeal any British law, even the Independence Act itself.
xa: They also acted as **dominion legislatures**.
Interim law: **GoI Act 1935** (as adapted).
An "**Act without a constitution**" (APPSC-G2 2017).

n55845851cc8.s: Which of the following offices was ended by the Indian Independence Act, 1947?
o: Chief Justice of the Federal Court
n55845851cc8.x: The Act ended the offices of the Viceroy and the Secretary of State, lapsed paramountcy and provided for boundary commissions.
xa: Two **dominions** with the right to **leave the British Commonwealth**.
Each dominion got a **Governor-General** as constitutional head.
**Mountbatten** = last Viceroy **and** first GG of free India.

n216be042347.s: Transfer of power to India and Pakistan as dominions enabled them to:
o: become free before framing their constitutions
remain provinces under the British Parliament
n216be042347.x: Dominion status let India and Pakistan become free before their constitutions were written, giving an interim constitutional position during the transition.
xa: **V.P. Menon** suggested immediate transfer on **dominion status**, bypassing a new constitution first.
The **Indian Independence Act** is "an **Act without a constitution**" (APPSC-G2 2017).
Dominions had the right to **leave the British Commonwealth**.

n3670b33c6c2.s: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress on 15 August 1947?
n3670b33c6c2.x: J.B. Kripalani was the Congress President at the time of Indian independence.
n3670b33c6c2.tq: Separate the office of Congress President from the offices of Prime Minister and Governor-General.
xs: **J.B. Kripalani** was **INC President** on **15 August 1947** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Jawaharlal Nehru** was **Prime Minister** ("**Tryst with Destiny**" speech).
xa: British PM: **Clement Attlee**; British monarch: **George VI**.
**Mountbatten** = last Viceroy and first GG.
First GG of Pakistan: **M.A. Jinnah**.

n44f64ea8705.s: Who was the last Governor-General of India and the only Indian to hold that office?
n44f64ea8705.x: C. Rajagopalachari (June 1948 - Jan 1950) was the last and only Indian Governor-General. Mountbatten was the last Viceroy and first GG of free India; Rajendra Prasad became the first President in 1950; Jinnah was the first GG of Pakistan.
n44f64ea8705.tq: First GG = Mountbatten; last and only Indian GG = Rajaji.
xs: **C. Rajagopalachari** (**June 1948 - Jan 1950**) was the **last and only Indian Governor-General** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Mountbatten** was the **last Viceroy** and **first GG**; **Jinnah** was the first GG of **Pakistan**.
xa: AP angle: as GG, Rajaji gave assent (**2 April 1949**) to the **Madras Estate Abolition Act**.
It was the **first law in free India** to receive the GG's assent.
⚠ **Mountbatten** = last Viceroy **and** first GG; **Rajaji** = last and only Indian GG.

nindian-history-105-32.s: Clement R. Attlee, British Prime Minister at the time of Indian independence, belonged to the:
nindian-history-105-32.x: Clement Attlee led the British Labour Party and was Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.
n: Clement Attlee belonged to the Labour Party. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #105 · pp 194-197]
xa: On **20 February 1947** Attlee announced the transfer of power to Indian hands before **June 1948**.
In **1947** **Mountbatten replaced Lord Wavell** as Viceroy.
Mountbatten's **3 June 1947** plan advanced independence to **15 August 1947**.

n1a93bceb8f2.s: Who described Mahatma Gandhi as a 'one-man boundary force'?
n1a93bceb8f2.x: Lord Mountbatten called Gandhi a 'one-man boundary force' because of his efforts to restrain communal violence.
xa: On **15 August 1947** Gandhi was fasting and praying at **Beliaghata, Calcutta**.
Mountbatten was the **last Viceroy** and **first Governor-General** of free India.
**C. Rajagopalachari** was the **last and only Indian GG**.

n4deb4410201.s: The 1947 referendum in the North-West Frontier Province was boycotted by the:
n4deb4410201.x: The Khudai Khidmatgar movement boycotted the referendum, and the North-West Frontier Province joined Pakistan.
xa: The other referendum: **Sylhet** → **East Pakistan**.
**Sindh** decided on its own.
Princely states had **no third option** of independence.

n7c342b7914a.s: The Radcliffe Line award was announced on:
n7c342b7914a.x: The Radcliffe award was announced on 17 August 1947, after independence.
xa: The delay was so Britain would **not be blamed for the violence**.
**Radcliffe** chaired both; a British lawyer with **no knowledge of Indian conditions** (APPSC 2019).
Criticism: the **late-announced award** worsened the violence.

n9ad15beeae8.s: At Partition, what share of the assets and liabilities went to Pakistan?
n9ad15beeae8.x: The Partition Council gave Pakistan 17.5 per cent of the assets and liabilities, not 25 per cent.
xa: Services and assets were also split between the two dominions.
**Boundary Commissions** fixed the **Punjab and Bengal** borders.
About **10-15 million** people crossed the new borders.

n52c7e34225e.s: The number of people estimated to have crossed the newly created borders during the Partition of India was approximately:
n52c7e34225e.x: An estimated 10–15 million people crossed the new borders during Partition. The movement was accompanied by widespread communal violence in which hundreds of thousands were killed.
n52c7e34225e.tq: Distinguish the stated migration range from larger or smaller approximate figures.
xs: An estimated **10-15 million** people crossed the new borders — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Hundreds of thousands** were killed in communal violence.
xa: The Government set up a **Ministry of Relief and Rehabilitation**.
It ran **refugee camps**, **resettlement** and **evacuee property**.
Pakistan took **17.5%** of assets and liabilities.

n44f377b47eb.s: Which of the following was set up by the Government of India to deal with the refugee crisis after Partition?
n44f377b47eb.x: The Government of India established the Ministry of Relief and Rehabilitation. Its responsibilities included refugee camps, resettlement and the management of evacuee property.
n44f377b47eb.tq: Apply the ‘which ministry would perform this function?’ method to distinguish the official institutional name.
xs: The Government of India set up a **Ministry of Relief and Rehabilitation** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It handled **refugee camps**, **resettlement** and **evacuee property**.
xa: About **10-15 million** crossed the new borders.
Hundreds of thousands were killed in communal violence.
The **Partition Council** divided assets; Pakistan took **17.5%**.

n911c5d536ac.s: Who was the first Governor-General of Pakistan after the partition of British India?
n911c5d536ac.x: M.A. Jinnah became the first Governor-General of Pakistan in August 1947.
xs: **M.A. Jinnah** was the **first Governor-General of Pakistan** — so option **(3)** is correct.
A **common GG** was permitted, but Pakistan chose Jinnah; **Mountbatten** became India's first GG.
**Rajagopalachari** was India's **last and only Indian GG**; **Kripalani** was **INC President**.
xa: Mountbatten was GG of India **1947-48**.
Rajaji was GG from **June 1948 - Jan 1950**.
⚠ **Mountbatten** = last Viceroy **and** first GG.

nf015577fad8.s: Why is the Indian Independence Act, 1947 described as an ‘Act without a constitution’?
o: It transferred power but left constitution-making to the Indians.
It imposed a permanent British constitution on both dominions.
It abolished both Constituent Assemblies before independence.
It prevented the dominions from repealing British laws.
nf015577fad8.x: The Act transferred power to the two dominions but left the framing of their constitutions to their respective Constituent Assemblies.
nf015577fad8.tq: Conceptual interpretation of a distinctive feature.
xs: It **transferred power but left constitution-making to Indians** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-G2 2017).
The **Constituent Assemblies** were made **sovereign**, could frame any constitution and **repeal any British law**, including this Act.
xa: The **GoI Act 1935** (as adapted) was interim law.
**V.P. Menon** suggested transfer on **dominion status** to bypass a new constitution first.
Significance: India and Pakistan became **free before writing constitutions**.

nb6c062a6235.s: Sir Cyril Radcliffe, who chaired the Boundary Commissions in 1947, was:
o: a British lawyer with no knowledge of Indian conditions beyond the map
the Governor-General who supervised the partition
an Indian judge experienced in provincial administration
a Muslim League nominee on the Boundary Commission
nb6c062a6235.x: Radcliffe was a British lawyer who lacked knowledge of Indian conditions beyond the map when he chaired the Boundary Commissions.
xa: ⚠ Award ready **12 August**, published **17 August 1947**.
About **10-15 million** crossed the new borders.
The **Partition Council** divided assets and liabilities.

nc891b6efdec.x: India Divided was written by Rajendra Prasad; Azad wrote India Wins Freedom and Khushwant Singh Train to Pakistan.
xa: **Pakistan or the Partition of India** — **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**.
**Guilty Men of India's Partition** — **Ram Manohar Lohia**.
⚠ Don't mix **India Divided** (Prasad) with **India Wins Freedom** (Azad).

n1ea5dddc784.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was born on 14 April 1891 at:
n1ea5dddc784.x: Ambedkar was born on 14 April 1891 at Mhow (now Dr. Ambedkar Nagar, Madhya Pradesh) in a Mahar family.
xa: He was one of the first Dalit students at **Elphinstone High School**, Bombay.
Titles: "**Modern Manu**", "**Messenger of Dalits**".
Slogan: "**Educate, Agitate, Organise**".

nfecbc1aa62c.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was conferred an honorary D.Litt in 1953 by which university?
nfecbc1aa62c.x: Osmania University, Hyderabad, conferred the honorary D.Litt in 1953. Columbia gave him an MA, PhD and an honorary LL.D (1952); Bombay University gave his BA (1912); LSE gave the MSc and DSc.
xs: **Osmania University**, Hyderabad, conferred the **honorary D.Litt in 1953** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2025).
**Columbia** gave his **MA, PhD** and an **honorary LL.D (1952)**; **Bombay University** his **BA (1912)**; **LSE** his **MSc and DSc**.
xa: ⚠ Honorary **LL.D** = **Columbia** (1952); honorary **D.Litt** = **Osmania** (1953).
LSE thesis: **The Problem of the Rupee**.
**Gray's Inn**, London: **Barrister-at-law**.

n0efcf6f5558.s: Who founded the journal titled ‘Mooknayak’, meaning ‘Leader of the Voiceless’ or ‘Leader of the Silent’?
n0efcf6f5558.x: Mooknayak was founded by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in 1920. It was his first paper and addressed the concerns of the voiceless.
n0efcf6f5558.tq: Use the founder–publication association and distinguish the exact title from similar social-reform journals.
xs: **Mooknayak** ("**Leader of the Voiceless/Silent**") was founded by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** in **1920** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2012).
It was **his first paper**.
xa: **Bahishkrit Bharat (1927)**: Dalit rights and social reform (BPSC 2022).
**Janata** was renamed **Prabuddha Bharat** (**1956**) after his conversion to Buddhism.
**Gandhi** founded the **Harijan Sevak Sangh (1932)**.

n0af836797b9.s: Which journal founded by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was associated with Dalit rights and social reform and was started in 1927?
n0af836797b9.x: Bahishkrit Bharat was founded by Ambedkar in 1927 and focused on Dalit rights and social reform.
n0af836797b9.tq: Match the publication’s purpose with its year and founder.
xs: **Bahishkrit Bharat** (**1927**) focused on **Dalit rights and social reform** — so option **(2)** is correct (BPSC 2022).
**Mooknayak** was his first paper (**1920**); **Janata** dates to **1930**; **Prabuddha Bharat** to **1956**.
xa: **1927** also saw the **Mahad Satyagraha**, **Manusmriti Dahan** and **Samata Samaj**.
