On **26 Jan 1950** India would enter "**a life of contradictions**".
Constitutional morality "**has to be cultivated**" (**4 Nov 1948**).

nf75c25aa6e1.s: During the debates on its making, the Indian Constitution was criticised as a copy of the:
nf75c25aa6e1.x: Critics called it a 'copy of the Government of India Act, 1935' and a 'lawyers' paradise'.
xa: His reply came in the speech of **4 Nov 1948** (UPPSC 2015).
Same speech: **constitutional morality** "has to be cultivated".
The Draft had **315 Articles and 13 Schedules**.

n7408f72f81e.s: Who was originally the only Congress member of the Drafting Committee?
n7408f72f81e.x: K.M. Munshi, who also chaired the Order of Business Committee, was originally the only Congress member of the Drafting Committee.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **Jawaharlal Nehru** was **not a member** (UPPSC 2012).
Chairman: **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**; set up on **29 August 1947**.
**Syed Mohammad Saadullah** was the member from **Assam**.

n5cc761ede5f.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described which provision as the ‘heart and soul’ of the Constitution?
n5cc761ede5f.x: Article 32, which guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies, was described by Ambedkar as the ‘heart and soul’ of the Constitution.
n5cc761ede5f.tq: Match the famous phrase with the constitutional provision, not with the related social-justice articles.
xs: **Article 32** (**Right to Constitutional Remedies**) is the "**heart and soul**" of the Constitution — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Art. 356** he hoped would stay a "**dead letter**"; **Art. 17** abolishes untouchability; **Art. 46** is **SC/ST welfare**.
xa: ⚠ "Heart and soul" = **Art. 32**; "dead letter" = **Art. 356**.
**Arts. 330 and 332**: reserved seats.
**Arts. 15-16**: non-discrimination, equal opportunity.

n8e504de9000.s: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability?
n8e504de9000.x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and makes it punishable; Articles 15-16 cover non-discrimination and Article 46 the welfare of SCs/STs.
xa: **Article 32** = "**heart and soul**".
**Art. 356** = hoped to be a "**dead letter**".
These embedded a "**social revolution**" — rights, reservation, abolition of untouchability.

ne272a57c657.s: Ambedkar hoped that the emergency provisions under Article 356 would remain a:
o: Source of the Union’s power to secede
ne272a57c657.x: Ambedkar expressed the hope that Article 356 would remain a ‘dead letter’, indicating that it would not be used routinely.
ne272a57c657.tq: Match the distinctive quotation with the correct emergency provision.
xs: Ambedkar hoped **Art. 356** would remain a "**dead letter**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
States have **no right to secede**, so "power to secede" is wrong.
xa: ⚠ "Heart and soul" = **Art. 32**; "dead letter" = **Art. 356**.
India is a "**Union of States**", able to work as **unitary or federal**.
He favoured a **strong Centre** to protect weaker sections.

nf463b71d0df.s: Ambedkar borrowed the term 'constitutional morality' from:
nf463b71d0df.x: Ambedkar took the term from George Grote and said constitutional morality has to be cultivated.
xa: Same speech: **no need to apologise** for borrowing from the **GoI Act 1935**.
Final speech: **25 November 1949**.
Warning against **bhakti or hero-worship** in politics.

n727d405e916.s: Ambedkar’s reference to India entering ‘a life of contradictions’ on 26 January 1950 pointed to the coexistence of:
o: Federalism with the right of secession
Political equality with social and economic inequality
n727d405e916.x: The contradiction lay in political equality coexisting with inequality in social and economic life. Ambedkar urged that political democracy be transformed into social democracy.
n727d405e916.tq: Match each side of the contrast without reversing the domains of equality and inequality.
xs: "**A life of contradictions**" meant **political equality** alongside **social and economic inequality** — so option **(4)** is correct.
India would enter it on **26 Jan 1950**; he urged turning **political democracy into social democracy**.
Option (2) reverses the two.
xa: "Political democracy cannot last unless there lies at the base of it **social and economic democracy**."
Final speech: **25 November 1949**.
States have **no right to secede**, so option (1) is also wrong.

n92cdeb37b0f.s: Which of the following best expresses Ambedkar's critique of caste in Annihilation of Caste?
o: Only untouchability needed to be removed while the caste system could remain.
Caste had no connection with religious texts and could be reformed through charity alone.
The caste system as a whole had to be destroyed because it possessed religious sanction in the Shastras and Vedas.
Caste was an ideal division of labour that required only greater efficiency.
n92cdeb37b0f.x: Ambedkar argued that caste had religious sanction in the Shastras and Vedas and that reform limited to untouchability was inadequate; the entire caste system had to go.
n92cdeb37b0f.tq: Choose the option that captures both the source of caste sanction and the scope of the remedy.
xs: In **Annihilation of Caste**, the **caste system as a whole had to be destroyed** because it had **religious sanction in the Shastras and Vedas** — option **(3)** is correct.
Since the sanction was religious, Ambedkar held **reform within Hinduism futile**.
Removing only **untouchability** was not enough — the **whole caste system** must go, so option (1) is wrong.
Varna as an ideal **division of labour** was **Gandhi's** view, not Ambedkar's.
xa: The book was a **direct rebuke of Gandhi's approach**.
⚠ Gandhi: varna a **division of labour**; Ambedkar: caste a **division of labourers**.
"Nothing can emancipate the outcaste except the **destruction of the caste system**" — Ambedkar (**APPSC-G1 2018**).
Remedy prescribed: **inter-caste marriage**.

n37637db5504.s: Gandhi and Ambedkar differed fundamentally on:
o: Whether the whole caste system should be annihilated
n37637db5504.x: Both sought uplift of the marginalised and stressed education, but differed on whether the whole caste system should be annihilated.
xa: Gandhi called **untouchability a corruption** of varna.
Ambedkar's education slogan: "**Educate, Agitate, Organise**".
Ambedkar founded the **People's Education Society (1945)**.

nf7a7d010e5a.s: Who described caste as “not just a division of labour, but a division of labourers”?
nf7a7d010e5a.x: The statement that caste is a division of labourers, rather than merely a division of labour, was made by B.R. Ambedkar.
nf7a7d010e5a.tq: Use author-quotation matching, a common history question pattern.
xs: **B.R. Ambedkar** described caste as "not just a **division of labour**, but a **division of labourers**" — option **(3)** is correct.
**Gandhi** held the opposite: **varna** was an ideal **division of labour** and only untouchability a corruption.
**B.S. Moonje** and **Malaviya** appear in the notes only in the debate on Ambedkar's turn to **Sikhism** (Moonje for, Malaviya against).
xa: ⚠ Classic trap: Gandhi = division of **labour**; Ambedkar = division of **labourers**.
Ambedkar: "Nothing can emancipate the outcaste except the **destruction of the caste system**" (**APPSC-G1 2018**).
His remedy: **inter-caste marriage**, the "**real remedy**".

nd6c88bd2535.s: The term 'Harijan' for the depressed classes was used by:
nd6c88bd2535.x: Gandhi used the term 'Harijan'; Ambedkar rejected it in favour of Dalit/Scheduled Castes.
xa: **Poona Pact (1932)**: Ambedkar accepted joint electorates with **147** reserved seats to save Gandhi's life.
Religion: Gandhi reformed Hinduism from within; Ambedkar left it for **Buddhism (1956)**.
Governance: Gandhi — decentralised **Gram Swaraj**; Ambedkar — a **strong Centre**.

nfc802358810.s: Ambedkar later felt that the Poona Pact made the Dalits:
o: independent of caste Hindus in political matters
nfc802358810.x: Ambedkar later felt the Pact made Dalits dependent on caste Hindus, although he had accepted joint electorates during the negotiations.
xa: **Poona Pact (1932)** followed Gandhi's **fast** against separate electorates.
Ambedkar accepted it to **save Gandhi's life**.
His underlying view: **political power** is necessary for the depressed classes to protect themselves (**APPSC GS 2016**).

n102c9c1f3f1.s: Rejecting Gandhi's Gram Swaraj and trusteeship, Ambedkar advocated:
n102c9c1f3f1.x: Ambedkar rejected Gram Swaraj and trusteeship, favouring a strong, centralised constitutional democracy to protect minorities.
xa: He called the village a "**sink of localism**" (Constituent Assembly, **4 Nov 1948**).
He preferred the **individual** as the unit.
He also criticised **Congress** for refusing to treat caste as a political issue.

n8eb84c708d9.s: What was a major criticism made by Ambedkar against the Indian National Congress?
o: It opposed all constitutional safeguards for minorities.
It supported separate electorates for the Scheduled Castes.
It refused to treat caste as a political issue.
It treated caste exclusively as an economic issue.
n8eb84c708d9.x: Ambedkar criticised Congress for refusing to recognise caste as a political issue. His work What Congress and Gandhi Have Done to the Untouchables was published in 1945.
n8eb84c708d9.tq: Identify the specific criticism rather than a broader political accusation.
xs: Ambedkar criticised Congress because it **refused to treat caste as a political issue** — option **(3)** is correct.
He set this out in "**What Congress and Gandhi Have Done to the Untouchables**" (**1945**).
Congress did not support separate electorates — **Gandhi opposed** them and fasted in **1932**.
xa: The **SCF** constitution declared its members **distinct from Hindus**.
**States and Minorities (1947)** was a memorandum to the Constituent Assembly for the **Scheduled Castes Federation**.
**Who Were the Shudras?** came in **1946** (**APPSC-GS 2019**).

n6f4a3a46a65.s: According to Ambedkar's argument in Who Were the Shudras?, the Shudras were originally:
o: A Kshatriya community degraded after conflict with Brahmins
An occupational group created by British legislation
A group formed exclusively from foreign invaders
n6f4a3a46a65.x: Ambedkar argued that the Shudras were originally Kshatriyas who were degraded after conflict with Brahmins, who denied them the upanayana.
n6f4a3a46a65.tq: Test the proposed social origin and the specific cause of degradation together.
xs: The Shudras were originally a **Kshatriya community degraded after conflict with Brahmins** — option **(2)** is correct.
The Brahmins **denied them the upanayana**, causing the degradation.
The book appeared in **1946** (asked in **APPSC-GS 2019**).
xa: ⚠ Shudras = degraded **Kshatriyas**; Untouchables = "**broken men**" (The Untouchables, **1948**).
**The Buddha and His Dhamma** (**1957**) is the basis of **Navayana** — not about the Shudras.
**States and Minorities** came the next year, **1947**.

na1567a3a39d.s: Which work of Ambedkar advanced the “broken men” theory regarding the origin of untouchability?
o: What Congress and Gandhi Have Done to the Untouchables
na1567a3a39d.x: The Untouchables, published in 1948, dealt with the origin of untouchability and advanced the theory of “broken men.”
na1567a3a39d.tq: Match the distinctive theory with the correct title.
xs: **The Untouchables** (**1948**) advanced the "**broken men**" theory of the origin of untouchability — option **(3)** is correct.
**Who Were the Shudras?** (**1946**) dealt with the origin of the **Shudras**, not untouchables.
**What Congress and Gandhi Have Done** (**1945**) attacked Congress; **The Buddha and His Dhamma** (**1957**) reread Buddhism.
xa: ⚠ Shudras = degraded **Kshatriyas**; Untouchables = "**broken men**".
**Thoughts on Linguistic States** — **1955**.
**Annihilation of Caste** — **1936**.

na9b21027bfb.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar suggested which city as a second capital of India?
na9b21027bfb.x: Ambedkar suggested Hyderabad as a second capital; he also proposed dividing Maharashtra and warned against huge states.
xa: He proposed splitting **UP, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh**.
Source: **Thoughts on Linguistic States (1955)**.
Principle: "**one state, one language**", not "one language, one state".

nb84cd7943d3.s: States and Minorities was submitted to the Constituent Assembly in 1947 on behalf of:
nb84cd7943d3.x: States and Minorities was a 1947 memorandum submitted to the Constituent Assembly on behalf of the Scheduled Castes Federation.
nb84cd7943d3.tq: Match the memorandum with the organisation that submitted it.
xs: **States and Minorities** was submitted on behalf of the **Scheduled Castes Federation** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was a **1947** memorandum to the **Constituent Assembly**.
The **Jat-Pat Todak Mandal** was linked to **Annihilation of Caste (1936)**; the **Independent Labour Party** was founded in **1936**.
xa: It set out **state socialism**: state ownership of **key industries** and **agricultural land**.
Land to be let to village collectives for **collective farming**; **nationalised insurance**.
State socialism to be written into the **Constitution** so a legislative majority could not undo it.

nc33b21ac837.s: Ambedkar set out his proposals for State socialism in:
nc33b21ac837.x: States and Minorities proposed State ownership of key industries and agricultural land and nationalised insurance.
xa: **States and Minorities (1947)** was submitted for the **Scheduled Castes Federation**.
State socialism was to be written into the **Constitution** so a legislative majority could not undo it.

n5231217d2db.s: Why did Ambedkar propose that State socialism should be written into the Constitution?
o: To ensure that a legislative majority could not undo it
To place economic policy exclusively under local bodies
To permit every village to frame a separate economic constitution
To prevent all state ownership of industries
n5231217d2db.x: Ambedkar wanted State socialism entrenched in the Constitution so that a temporary legislative majority could not reverse it.
n5231217d2db.tq: Link the constitutional method with its intended protection against ordinary majorities.
xs: So that **a legislative majority could not undo it** — option **(1)** is correct.
The proposal is in **States and Minorities (1947)**.
It called for **state ownership of key industries**, so option (4) is the reverse of his plan.
xa: Also: state ownership of **agricultural land**, let out for **collective farming**.
**Nationalised insurance**.
He favoured a **strong Centre**, not local bodies, so option (2) is wrong.

naaf89b4b94f.s: Ambedkar's reinterpretation of Buddhism is known as:
naaf89b4b94f.x: Ambedkar's reinterpretation of Buddhism is called Navayana, meaning Neo-Buddhism. It gave rise to the Dalit Buddhist Movement.
naaf89b4b94f.tq: Distinguish Ambedkar's modern reinterpretation from the established Buddhist sects.
xs: His reinterpretation is **Navayana** ("**Neo-Buddhism**") — option **(4)** is correct.
**CGPSC 2019** asked it as Neo-Buddhism = Ambedkar.
Its basis is **The Buddha and His Dhamma** (posthumous, **1957**), a rational, social reading of Buddhism.
xa: It gave rise to the **Dalit Buddhist Movement**.
Conversion: **14 October 1956**, **Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur**, with **22 vows**.
Buddhists were added for SC status in **1990**.

n46d7368aa3a.s: Ambedkar called the Indian village 'a sink of localism, a den of ignorance, narrow-mindedness and communalism' in the Constituent Assembly on:
n46d7368aa3a.x: He said this on 4 November 1948, preferring the individual, not the village, as the basic unit.
xa: He **rejected Gram Swaraj** and trusteeship, favouring a **strong, centralised constitutional democracy**.
Gandhi stood for decentralised **Gram Swaraj**; Ambedkar for a **strong Centre**.
The strong Centre was meant to **protect minorities**.

n051684d47fa.s: Ambedkar's resignation in 1951 was closely associated with the stalling of the:
o: Constitution of the Scheduled Castes Federation
n051684d47fa.x: Ambedkar resigned in 1951 when the Hindu Code Bill, which dealt with inheritance, marriage and divorce, stalled.
n051684d47fa.tq: Link the resignation to the legislative measure rather than to a constitutional memorandum.
xs: His **1951** resignation followed the stalling of the **Hindu Code Bill** — option **(3)** is correct.
The Bill covered **inheritance, marriage and divorce**.
The **Poona Pact** dates from **1932** and **States and Minorities** from **1947**.
xa: He measured a community's progress by its **women's progress**.
He supported **women's votes** from the start.
As **Labour Member (1942-46)** he backed the **8-hour working day**.

nbd2d09906f5.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar founded the Independent Labour Party in:
nbd2d09906f5.x: He founded the ILP in 1936 and was Labour Member during 1942-46.
xa: He resigned in **1951** when the **Hindu Code Bill** stalled.
**People's Education Society (1945)**; **Siddharth College, Bombay (1946)**.
⚠ **1936** is also the year of **Annihilation of Caste**.

n085ec7453e9.s: According to the Supreme Court ruling of 24 March 2026, conversion out of which of the following religions results in the immediate loss of Scheduled Caste status under Clause 3 of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950?
n085ec7453e9.x: The ruling held that conversion out of Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism leads to immediate loss of Scheduled Caste status under Clause 3 of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950.
n085ec7453e9.tq: Identify the exact religious categories and the constitutional provision involved.
xs: Converting out of **Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism** brings immediate loss of SC status — option **(1)** is correct.
The basis is **Clause 3** of the **Constitution (SC) Order 1950**, per the SC ruling of **24 March 2026**.
The bench: Justices **P.K. Mishra** and **Manmohan**.
xa: **Buddhists** were added in **1990**; **Sikhs** in **1956**.
The case, **Chinthada Anand**, came from **Andhra Pradesh**.
It arose from an AP pastor's case under the **SC/ST Atrocities Act**.

n23591003016.s: "Nothing can emancipate the outcaste except the destruction of the caste system." Who said this?
n23591003016.x: The statement is B.R. Ambedkar's (APPSC-G1 2018), in line with Annihilation of Caste (1936).
xa: Ambedkar also said caste is a "**division of labourers**", not just of labour.
"Turn in any direction you like, caste is the **monster** that crosses your path" — Ambedkar.
At **Yeola** (**13 October 1935**): "born a Hindu... will **not die a Hindu**".

n4154edcdfc1.s: Which of the following best represents Ambedkar's position regarding political power for the Depressed Classes?
o: Political power was necessary to protect their interests.
Political power could be secured only through religious conversion.
Political power should remain exclusively with caste Hindus.
Political power was irrelevant because social reform alone was sufficient.
n4154edcdfc1.x: Ambedkar held that political power was necessary for the Depressed Classes to protect themselves and secure their rights.
n4154edcdfc1.tq: Test the central argument associated with a political thinker.
xs: Ambedkar held that **political power was necessary** for the depressed classes **to protect themselves** — option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC GS 2016**).
This is why he **demanded separate electorates**, against Gandhi.
He did not see social reform alone as enough: his method was **legal, constitutional, political rights** and state action.
xa: **Poona Pact (1932)**: he settled for joint electorates with **147** reserved seats.
Later he felt the Pact made Dalits **dependent on caste Hindus**.
He founded the **Independent Labour Party (1936)**.

n086bfae591b.s: Which one of the following best represents Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's position on the relationship between language and states?
o: He accepted “one state, one language” but not “one language, one state”.
He supported “one language, one state” but rejected “one state, one language”.
He supported both “one state, one language” and “one language, one state”.
He rejected both linguistic principles in favour of administrative states.
n086bfae591b.x: Ambedkar accepted the principle of one state, one language, but did not accept the principle of one language, one state.
n086bfae591b.tq: Distinguish the two similar-sounding linguistic principles instead of reversing their order.
xs: He accepted "**one state, one language**" but not "**one language, one state**" — option **(1)** is correct.
The view is in **Thoughts on Linguistic States (1955)**.
He did not reject linguistic principles outright, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: He **warned against huge states**.
Split **UP, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh**; divide **Maharashtra** into smaller units.
**Hyderabad** as a second capital of India.

n47c1c1dd871.s: Who first put forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India in 1934?
n47c1c1dd871.x: M.N. Roy proposed it in 1934; the INC made it an official demand in 1935 and the August Offer accepted it in 1940.
xa: **1938**: Nehru — constitution by an Assembly elected on **adult franchise**.
**1942**: carried forward in the **Cripps Proposals**; **1946**: Assembly set up under the **Cabinet Mission Plan**.
⚠ **1934** = M.N. Roy; **1935** = INC demand; **1940** = August Offer.

n2f3c971d094.s: Who is generally credited with first putting forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly in 1934?
n2f3c971d094.x: M.N. Roy first put forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly in 1934. The idea had earlier been attributed to Bal Gangadhar Tilak in 1895 by some sources.
n2f3c971d094.tq: Separate the earlier attribution to Tilak from the specific 1934 formulation by M.N. Roy.
xs: **M.N. Roy** first put forward the idea in **1934** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was the **first formal proposal** for a Constituent Assembly.
**Tilak** gets early credit only in some sources, for his **1895** Swaraj Bill; **Nehru** spoke of an elected Assembly in **1938**.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** **APPSC-GS 2019** framed it as "first in 1935"; the key was still **M.N. Roy**.
**1935**: it became an **official INC demand**.
**1940**: British acceptance in principle in the **August Offer**.

nf2d06b5d77d.s: The demand for a Constituent Assembly was accepted in principle in the August Offer of
nf2d06b5d77d.x: The demand was accepted in principle in the August Offer of 1940.
nf2d06b5d77d.tq: Use the chronological progression from INC demand to August Offer to avoid year substitution.
xs: The **August Offer** was of **1940** — option **(3)** is correct.
It gave **British acceptance in principle** of a Constituent Assembly.
**1935** = official INC demand; **1938** = Nehru's adult-franchise statement; **1942** = **Cripps Proposals**.
xa: **1934**: **M.N. Roy**'s first formal proposal.
**1946**: set up under the **Cabinet Mission Plan**.

n077691a21af.s: Under the Cabinet Mission scheme, provincial members of the Constituent Assembly were elected by:
o: Proportional representation by single transferable vote
n077691a21af.x: Each community's members in the provincial assembly elected its representatives by PR-STV, with seats divided broadly by population.
xa: **Princely states**: members **nominated** by rulers; seats initially unfilled.
Nature: **partly elected, partly nominated**.
It was **not elected on adult franchise** — a main criticism.

nde82c81b58a.s: Which two prominent leaders were NOT members of the Constituent Assembly?
nde82c81b58a.x: Nearly every leader was a member except Gandhi and Jinnah. Nehru, Patel, Prasad, Ambedkar, Sarojini Naidu and Hansa Mehta were all members.
nde82c81b58a.tq: Not in the CA: Gandhi and Jinnah.
xs: **Mahatma Gandhi and M.A. Jinnah** were not members — option **(2)** is correct.
Nearly every other leader was a member.
**Ambedkar** chaired the Drafting Committee; **Prasad** chaired the Assembly as constitution-maker; **Sarojini Naidu** and **Hansa Mehta** were among the **15 women**.
xa: The **Muslim League boycotted** the first sitting on **9 December 1946**.
**211** members attended the first sitting.
After partition strength fell from **389** to **299**.

n5edc7b99bf8.s: At the first sitting of the Constituent Assembly, the number of members who attended was
n5edc7b99bf8.x: The first sitting, held on 9 December 1946, was attended by 211 members. The Muslim League boycotted the sitting.
n5edc7b99bf8.tq: Distinguish attendance at the first sitting from the total strength before and after partition.
xs: **211** members attended the first sitting — option **(1)** is correct.
The first sitting was on **9 December 1946**; the **Muslim League boycotted** it.
**389** was the original strength and **299** the strength after League members withdrew.
xa: ⚠ **211** attended; **389** → **299** after partition.
**Vice-President**: **H.C. Mukherjee** (later also **V.T. Krishnamachari**).
**Constitutional Adviser**: **B.N. Rau**.

nc55d572c1b9.s: The strength of the Constituent Assembly fell from 389 to 299 mainly because of the:
o: withdrawal of Muslim League members from areas that went to Pakistan
nc55d572c1b9.x: After Partition, Muslim League members from territories that became part of Pakistan withdrew, reducing the strength from 389 to 299.
xa: The Assembly was set up under the **Cabinet Mission Plan** (**1946**).
Seats split among **General, Muslim, Sikh** in proportion to population.
**15 women** members.

n0d982609b81.s: Jawaharlal Nehru accepted the Andhra demand in the Constituent Assembly on:
n0d982609b81.x: Nehru accepted it on 27 November 1947; Andhra was dropped from the Draft Constitution on 21 February 1948 and the Dhar Commission named on 17 June 1948.
xa: Andhra members: **B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya**, **Durgabai Deshmukh**, **M. Ananthasayanam Ayyangar**.
Pattabhi was INC President at **Jaipur** in **1948**.
AP angle: the **Andhra state demand** was raised in the Assembly.

n4054668d2e1.s: Which member of the Constituent Assembly founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha?
n4054668d2e1.x: Durgabai Deshmukh founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha; Pattabhi Sitaramayya chaired the House Committee and Ranga was a peasant leader.
xa: Pattabhi was INC President at **Jaipur** in **1948**.
Durgabai was among the **15 women** members.
AP angle: **Pingali Venkayya** designed the flag (**1921**).

n3a00e3932c9.s: Which political organisation demanded the dissolution of the Constituent Assembly and its re-election on the basis of adult suffrage?
n3a00e3932c9.x: The Socialist Party demanded dissolution of the Constituent Assembly and its re-election through adult suffrage.
n3a00e3932c9.tq: Identify the organisation associated with the specific constitutional criticism.
xs: The **Socialist Party** demanded its **dissolution and re-election on adult suffrage** — option **(4)** is correct (**RPSC 2024**).
The charge: it was **not elected on adult franchise** but indirectly under the **1935 Act**.
The **Muslim League** instead **boycotted** the first sitting.
xa: Other charges: **Congress dominance** ("Congress Assembly Party").
Also: **Hindu and lawyer dominance**; slow.
Counter-view: its **broad inclusion of views**.

n9a3ccf8b0e4.s: The National Flag of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on
n9a3ccf8b0e4.x: The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Flag on 22 July 1947.
n9a3ccf8b0e4.tq: Distinguish the earlier flag-adoption date from the cluster of January 1950 decisions.
xs: The National Flag was adopted on **22 July 1947** — option **(3)** is correct.
**27 December 1911** is when **Jana Gana Mana** was first sung at the Calcutta INC session.
**Pingali Venkayya** designed the tricolour in **1921**.
xa: Gandhi added the **charkha**; the Assembly replaced it with the **Ashoka Chakra**.
The design was shown to Gandhi at the AICC session at **Bezwada (Vijayawada)**.
Venkayya's **150th birth anniversary** (b. **1876**) was marked in **2026**.

nb1b5675cba4.s: Pingali Venkayya showed his 1921 tricolour design to Gandhi at the AICC session held at:
nb1b5675cba4.x: Venkayya presented the design at the Bezwada AICC session; Gandhi added the charkha, later replaced by the Ashoka Chakra.
xa: Flag adopted on **22 July 1947**.
Venkayya: born **1876**, **Bhatlapenumarru**, called "**Jhanda Venkayya**".
AP angle: Venkayya's flag; **Pattabhi**, **Ranga**, **Durgabai**, **Ananthasayanam** in the Assembly.

nb4c930432b7.tq: Recall the exact characterization used in a regional debate.
xs: At **Mahanandi** (Kurnool), **April 1913**, **Guthi Kesava Pillai** called separation **impractical** and a "**Brahmin movement**" — option **(1)** is correct.
This meeting came **before Bapatla**.
xa: Later, Rayalaseema and Nellore leaders saw the movement as **Circars/Brahmin-led** → the **1917** district-wise vote.
Guthi Kesava Pillai attended the **1885 Bombay** INC session.
The Mahanandi meeting is listed among the causes of Rayalaseema's **distrust** of coastal leadership.

nap-history-1-18.s: Where did the Forest Satyagraha first start?
nap-history-1-18.x: The Forest Satyagraha during the Non-Cooperation Movement first started in Palnadu in Guntur district. Chintapalli belongs to Alluri's revolt and Bapatla to the first Andhra Mahasabha.
nap-history-1-18.tq: Link each place to its movement.
n: The Forest Satyagraha first started in Palnadu, Guntur. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
xs: The **Forest Satyagraha** first started in **Palnadu in Guntur** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Chintapalli** was the first police station attacked by **Alluri Sitarama Raju**.
**Bapatla** hosted the **first Andhra Mahasabha** (**1913**); **Machilipatnam** is not linked with the forest satyagraha in these notes.
xa: The **Kakinada Riot Case** — the **first criminal case** in the **Vandemataram Movement**.
**Nyapati Subba Rao** — first lawyer in Andhra to **boycott British courts**.
**Vallabhaneni Sitamahalakshmi** — first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha.

ncc6deeea78c.s: The Swarajya associated with the Vandemataram era was published at Vijayawada, with which person as editor?
ncc6deeea78c.x: The Vijayawada Swarajya of the Vandemataram era had Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao as its editor.
ncc6deeea78c.tq: Distinguish two newspapers with the same title by place and period.
xs: **Swarajya**, Vijayawada, was edited by **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham** ran **Desamata** (Rajahmundry).
**Mutnuri Krishna Rao** edited **Krishna Patrika**.
xa: Gadicherla presided the **7th session** (**1919**, Guntur).
He proposed **district-wise voting** at Nellore (**1917**).
**Navayuga**, Chilakaluripet — **Srinivasa Rao**.

nccf44706f49.s: The joint conference of the Guntur, Krishna and Godavari districts held at Nidadavolu in 1912 is significant because it:
o: Opposed the formation of any linguistic province
Demanded a separate Rayalaseema state with Madras as capital
Passed the first formal resolution for a separate province
nccf44706f49.x: The Nidadavolu conference of 1912 passed the first formal resolution demanding a separate province. The resolution was moved by Gurunatham.
nccf44706f49.tq: Identify the significance of an early conference rather than its venue alone.
xs: **Nidadavolu (1912)** **passed the first formal resolution for a separate province** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was a joint conference of **Guntur, Krishna, Godavari** districts (in **West Godavari**).
It was moved by **Jonnavittula Gurunatham**; a standing committee was formed with **Konda Venkatappayya** as secretary.
xa: Opposed by **K.V. Reddy Naidu** and **Peddada Sambasiva Rao**.
⚠ Nidadavolu **1912** = first formal resolution; Bapatla **1913** = first numbered conference.
A separate Rayalaseema state with Madras as capital was asked only before the **Dhar Commission** (**1948**).

nb9049f1860c.s: The demand for a separate Andhra university was first raised at the first session of the Andhra Mahasabha in:
nb9049f1860c.x: The university demand was first raised at the first session in 1913; Telugu as medium of instruction was demanded at the third session in 1915.
xa: Exam angle: "Which session first demanded a separate Telugu university?" = **First** (**APPSC 2022**).
Reason: Tamil-dominated **Madras University** neglected Telugu.
**Andhra University** established **26 April 1926**.

nf78883f8c8e.s: Who moved the early proposal for a separate Andhra province, which Nyapati Subba Rao opposed?
nf78883f8c8e.x: The proposal was moved by Vemavarapu Ramadasu Pantulu; Krishna Rao moved the amendment and a committee under Pattabhi Sitaramayya followed.
xa: Krishna and Guntur delegates were **disappointed** by the deferment.
President **B.N. Sarma**: "**First we are Indians, then we are Andhras.**"
The resolution passed at **Vijayawada** in **1914**.

n4cd0e44420c.s: What was the principal position taken by B.N. Sarma regarding the demand for a separate Andhra province at the first Andhra Mahasabha?
o: It should be achieved only through armed struggle.
It should be pursued immediately through constitutional agitation.
It was essential before any work for Andhra uplift could begin.
It might do more harm than good at that time.
n4cd0e44420c.x: B.N. Sarma cautioned that the demand for a separate province might do more harm than good at that stage.
n4cd0e44420c.tq: Identify the precise qualification in a political leader’s stand.
xs: **B.N. Sarma** felt the demand **might do more harm than good** at that time — option **(4)** is correct.
He saw it as a **premature demand**.
He urged **loyalty to the British** and joint work for Andhra's uplift — not immediate agitation.
xa: Exam angle: "president of the first Mahasabha opposed a separate state" = **B.N. Sarma** (**APPSC G2 2017**).
His motto: "**First we are Indians, then we are Andhras.**"
He later moved a linguistic-provinces resolution in the **Imperial Legislative Council** (**6 Feb 1918**).

n3d68117d01c.s: Who was the secretary of the first Andhra Mahasabha at Bapatla (1913)?
n3d68117d01c.x: Konda Venkatappayya was secretary (APPSC 2022 key) of the Bapatla Mahasabha of 26 May 1913.
xa: President: **B.N. Sarma**.
Exam angle: venue **Bapatla**, president **B.N. Sarma**, secretary **Konda Venkatappayya**.
Bapatla is now HQ of **Bapatla district**.

n6e77e8b5efc.s: At the Nellore session of 1917, 480 of the 740 delegates came from Nellore. Voting was therefore conducted:
n6e77e8b5efc.x: Since 480 of the 740 delegates came from Nellore, voting was conducted district-wise to avoid domination by one district.
xa: The same session **rejected the demand to include Madras city**.
⚠ Some notes place the **5th** session at **Pikkavolu** under **V. Venkatarama Rao**.
District-wise voting answered **Circars/Brahmin-led** suspicion in Rayalaseema and Nellore.

n478060b7380.s: Who presided over the first Andhra Mahasabha at Bapatla on 26 May 1913?
n478060b7380.x: B.N. Sarma presided at Bapatla; the province resolution was deferred, not passed, there.
xa: Bapatla **demanded a separate university**.
Bapatla "**sowed the seeds**" of the Andhra movement.
It was the first **numbered** Andhra Conference.

n8febc47f80f.s: The resolution demanding a separate Andhra province was passed at the second Andhra Mahasabha session held at:
n8febc47f80f.x: The second session, held at Vijayawada on 11 April 1914, passed the resolution demanding a separate Andhra province.
n8febc47f80f.tq: Directly pair the resolution with its session venue and year.
xs: The province resolution passed at the **2nd** session, **Vijayawada** — option **(4)** is correct.
Date: **11 April 1914**; president **Nyapati Subba Rao**.
**Bapatla (1913)** had deferred it; **Visakhapatnam (1915)** and **Kakinada (1916)** came later.
xa: Moved by **Manda Suryanarayana**, seconded by **Vemavarapu Ramadasu**; passed by **overwhelming majority**.
Vijayawada **1914** = first session called "**Andhra Mahasabha**".
It also asked for an **engineering college**.

nf0651cc97ea.s: The demand for a separate Andhra Congress circle was made at the fourth Andhra Mahasabha session held at:
nf0651cc97ea.x: The fourth session was held at Kakinada in May 1916 and demanded that the AICC create a separate Andhra Congress circle.
nf0651cc97ea.tq: Link the organisational demand to the correct venue and session.
xs: The separate Andhra Congress circle was demanded at the **4th session**, **Kakinada** — option **(2)** is correct.
It was held in **May 1916** under **Mocherla Ramachandra Rao**.
**Nellore** hosted the **5th** (**1917**), **Kadapa** the **6th** (**1918**), **Guntur** the **7th** (**1919**).
xa: **C.V. Narasimha Raju** moved a **fully autonomous province** there.
A women's session (**8 May 1916**) under **Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi**.
The **AICC** at **Lucknow 1916** examined the demand but took no decision.

n4f58054766c.s: The special Andhra Sabha held at Guntur on 17 August 1918 protested that:
o: The Montagu-Chelmsford proposals did not provide for an Andhra province
The AICC had rejected Telugu as a medium of instruction
The Andhra Provincial Congress Conference had been dissolved
Madras city had been included in the Andhra province
n4f58054766c.x: The Guntur special session protested that the Montagu-Chelmsford proposals made no provision for an Andhra province.
n4f58054766c.tq: Identify the precise grievance associated with the special session.
xs: The special **Guntur** session (**17 Aug 1918**) protested that the **Montagu-Chelmsford proposals had no Andhra province** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was presided by **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.
The **Montagu-Chelmsford Report** (**July 1918**) had no Andhra provision.
xa: There **Pattabhi** proposed an **All-India Linguistic States Conference**.
**Krishna Patrika** mocked the scheme as "digging a mountain to catch a mouse" (**13 July 1918**).
**Dec 1918**: a delegation went to **London**; **Mocherla Ramachandra Rao** submitted a memorandum.

n6423ba4143b.s: Who presided over the fourth Andhra Mahasabha at Kakinada (1916) and was called the 'Gokhale of South India'?
n6423ba4143b.x: Mocherla Ramachandra Rao, the 'Gokhale of South India', presided at Kakinada; a women's session was held there under Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi.
xa: **C.V. Narasimha Raju** moved a **fully autonomous province** at Kakinada.
Kakinada sought a separate **Andhra Congress circle** from the AICC.
⚠ Mocherla had **opposed** the province resolution at **Bapatla (1913)**.

na483d5a4382.s: The Congress session held at Kakinada in 1923 was presided over by:
na483d5a4382.x: Maulana Mohammed Ali presided over the Congress session held at Kakinada in 1923.
na483d5a4382.tq: Match the Andhra venue and year with its presiding president.
xs: The **Kakinada session, 1923** was presided by **Maulana Mohammed Ali** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was one of the Congress sessions held in Andhra.
**Pattabhi** presided only in **1948** (Jaipur).
xa: **AICC at Bezawada (Vijayawada), 1921**: **Tilak Swaraj Fund**.
⚠ Kakinada also hosted the **4th Andhra Mahasabha** (**1916**).
**1921-35**: "**Swarajya within Swarajya**".

n459855763c6.s: In which year did the Madras session block the Andhra resolution?
n459855763c6.x: Madras blocked it in 1914, the provincial conference refused it in 1915, Lucknow took no decision in 1916 and a committee followed in 1918.
xa: The **Calcutta Congress (1917)** accepted the demand.
First president **Nyapati Subba Rao**; first secretary **Konda Venkatappayya**.
It was the **first major victory** of the Andhra movement.

ne69e74ab30e.s: Who moved the separate-province resolution in 1917?
ne69e74ab30e.x: B.N. Sarma moved the separate-province resolution in 1917.
ne69e74ab30e.tq: Use the action-person association rather than the later memorandum and deputation links.
xs: **B.N. Sarma** moved the separate-province resolution in **1917** — option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC 2017** key).
It followed Montagu's declaration of **20 Aug 1917**.
**Kaleswara Rao** spoke in **1928**; **Jogayya Pantulu** went to London in **1931**; **Guthi Kesava Pillai** opposed separation.
xa: ⚠ At **Bapatla (1913)** Sarma had called the demand premature.
He moved a linguistic-provinces resolution in the **Imperial Legislative Council**, **6 Feb 1918**.
He founded the **Andhra Rajakeeya Samiti** (**1917**).

n99c94052c42.s: In 1931, the Andhra resolution was handed to Gandhi for the Second Round Table Conference. Who went to London to press it?
n99c94052c42.x: V.V. Jogayya Pantulu went to London in 1931, while Bobbili Raja and Mocherla Ramachandra Rao attended the Second Round Table Conference.
xa: **Oct 1931, Madras**: **Kalluri Subbarao** sought separate representation for Rayalaseema.
Kadapa Koti Reddy also presided the **1937 Silver Jubilee** session.
**1928**: **A. Kaleswara Rao** raised the delay in the Madras Council.

n14a06d2b615.s: Who remarked, in connection with the 1918 resolution on linguistic provinces, that “the time has not come”?
n14a06d2b615.x: Surendranath Banerjee stated that the time had not come for the proposed linguistic reorganisation.
n14a06d2b615.tq: Test an exact quotation against the associated political figure.
xs: **Surendranath Banerjee** said "**the time has not come**" — option **(4)** is correct.
**Jinnah** opposed the resolution outright; **Sapru** would back it **for Andhra only**.
**Ramadasu Pantulu** was a mover of later resolutions (**1925-27**), not a critic.
xa: The resolution was **B.N. Sarma**'s, in the **Imperial Council**, **1918**.
Supported by **K.V. Rangaswami Ayyangar**.
Also opposed by **V.S. Srinivasa Sastri**.

n561b8dc0931.s: Who led the Andhra delegation that met Edwin Montagu in Madras on 20 December 1917?
n561b8dc0931.x: Nyapati Subba Rao led the delegation that met Montagu in Madras on 20 December 1917 to press for an Andhra province.
xa: Montagu's declaration on self-governing institutions came on **20 Aug 1917**.
The **July 1918** Montagu-Chelmsford Report had **no Andhra provision**.
At the Guntur special session, **Pattabhi** proposed an **All-India Linguistic States Conference**.
**Venkatapati Raju** moved a matching resolution in the **Madras Legislative Council**.

n72f5ac81e90.s: Which one of the following leaders initially opposed the Andhra demand in 1916 but later supported it at Cuddapah in 1918?
n72f5ac81e90.x: Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao of Cuddapah initially opposed the demand in 1916 but changed his position and supported it at Cuddapah in 1918.
n72f5ac81e90.tq: Track the change in a leader’s position across two dates.
xs: **Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao** opposed the Andhra demand in **1916** but switched to support it at **Cuddapah in 1918** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Jinnah** opposed in the **Imperial Council, 1918**; **Ekambaram Ayyar** opposed in **1917**; **N.M. Sastry** opposed in **1938** — none switched.
xa: ⚠ He then presided the **6th session, Kadapa 1918**, where the province resolution passed **unanimously**.
He also presided the **1st Rayalaseema Mahasabha** (**28 January 1934**, Madras), which demanded a university at **Tirupati**.
The **Andhra Provincial Congress Conference** met alongside the Kadapa session.

ne92b7f6b09b.s: The demand for a separate university for the Telugu people was first raised at the Andhra Mahasabha session held at:
ne92b7f6b09b.x: The separate-university demand was first raised at the first session at Bapatla in 1913, because Madras University neglected Telugu; Vijayawada (1914) only reiterated it.
xa: Reason: the Tamil-dominated **Madras University** neglected Telugu.
Bapatla (**26 May 1913**) was presided by **B.N. Sarma**, with **Konda Venkatappayya** as secretary.
Exam angle: "Which session first demanded a separate Telugu university?" = **First** (APPSC 2022).

n077c80e1bc4.s: Who introduced the Andhra University Bill on 20 August 1925?
n077c80e1bc4.x: Education Minister A.P. Patro of the Justice Party introduced the Andhra University Bill on 20 August 1925.
n077c80e1bc4.tq: Test the person associated with the legislative action rather than the later university administration.
xs: Education Minister **A.P. Patro** (Justice Party) introduced the Andhra University Bill on **20 Aug 1925** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Dr. Subbaroyan's** ministry decided the seat (**Dec 1928**); **P. Ramarayaningar** (Raja of Panagal) was CM; **C.R. Reddy** was the first VC.
xa: Governor's assent **15 Dec 1925**; Governor-General's assent **13 Jan 1926** — Madras **Act II of 1926**.
Established **26 April 1926**, HQ **Vijayawada**, teaching centre **Rajahmundry**.
First university for **Telugu-speaking people**; oldest in today's AP.

n827994299bd.s: The first Rayalaseema Mahasabha (28 January 1934) demanded a separate university at:
n827994299bd.x: Presided over by Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao, it opposed inclusion in Andhra University and demanded a separate university at Tirupati.
xa: ⚠ First session venue: notes give **Madras**; the APPSC G2 2008 key says **Anantapur**.
**2nd** Rayalaseema Mahasabha: **September 1935, Kadapa**, under **T.N. Ramakrishna Reddy**.
Pre-history: **Mahanandi, April 1913**, under **Guthi Kesava Pillai**.

n9ba5bcfd0b5.s: Sir Vijayanand ('Sir Vijaya') presided over the Andhra Mahasabha session held in November 1941 at:
n9ba5bcfd0b5.x: He presided at Visakhapatnam in November 1941 and met Stafford Cripps on 2 April 1942.
xa: **M. Suryanarayana** was Andhra Mahasabha president **1941-46** (PYQ).
**1921-35**: moderates (**Radhakrishnan**, **Sir Vijaya**, **C.R. Reddy**) kept the Mahasabha going.
From **1946**, Congress in office in Madras took over the demand.

n0fef22276b6.s: Who wrote “Maa Telugu Talliki,” recognised as the State song of Andhra Pradesh?
n0fef22276b6.x: “Maa Telugu Talliki” was written by Sankarambadi Sundarachari and is the State song of Andhra Pradesh.
n0fef22276b6.tq: Use the author-work association, a common culture-paper pattern.
xs: "**Maa Telugu Talliki**", the State song, was written by **Sankarambadi Sundarachari** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao** founded **Andhra Kesari** (**1904**) and wrote **Andhrula Charitra**; **C.R. Reddy** was AU's first VC.
xa: **Andhra Abhyudaya Dinam**: Ugadi, **24 March 1936**.
**Diwali 1937**: Andhra State Day.
**Konda Venkatappayya**'s title: **Deshabhakta**.

n436bfcf01ab.s: Who proposed the Cooum river as the boundary between the Andhra and Tamil areas in the early 1920s?
n436bfcf01ab.x: Panaganti Ramarayaningar, popularly known as the Raja of Panagal and Madras Chief Minister in the early 1920s, proposed the Cooum as the boundary.
n436bfcf01ab.tq: Use the office-and-proposal association to identify the correct person.
xs: **Panaganti Ramarayaningar (Raja of Panagal)**, Madras CM in the early **1920s**, proposed the **Cooum river** as the boundary — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kadapa Koti Reddy** wanted **Madras as Andhra capital** (**1933**); **Rajaji** opposed any sharing; **Prakasam** wrote "**Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae**".
xa: Cooum plan: **north to Andhras**, **south to Tamils** (APPSC 2022).
The **Andhra Congress** wanted **half of Madras town**.
**Sriramulu (1952)**: Madras city as a **Chief Commissioner's (C-class) state**.

nc60afd5f23a.s: The Andhra Mahasabha demanded that Andhra State be formed by:
nc60afd5f23a.x: The Andhra Mahasabha demanded the formation of Andhra State by 26 January 1950.
nc60afd5f23a.tq: Distinguish the movement's demanded deadline from later actual reorganisation dates.
xs: The **Andhra Mahasabha** demanded the state by **26 January 1950** — option **(1)** is correct.
**1 October 1953** = Andhra State formed; **1 November 1956** = Andhra Pradesh.
xa: The **Partition Committee** too agreed on **26 Jan 1950** — not implemented.
**Swami Sitaram's** fast (**1951**) demanded the state by **2 October 1951**.
**1949**: the **Visalandhra Mahasabha** was formed for all Telugu areas.

n26f714a60a2.s: In which year was Nellore district renamed Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District?
n26f714a60a2.x: Nellore district was renamed Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District in 2008 by the government headed by Chief Minister Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy.
n26f714a60a2.tq: Test a renaming year with closely spaced alternatives.
xs: Nellore was renamed **"Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District"** in **2008** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The renaming was done under CM **Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy**.
xa: Sriramulu's ancestral village was **Gajula Dinne**, in Nellore district; he was born in Madras on **16 March 1901**.
**Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University** (Hyderabad) is also named after him.
His titles: **Amarajeevi** (Immortal Martyr) and "Andhra Martyra Martanda".

n7dabe4c3838.s: On 6 February 1918, B. N. Sarma moved a resolution in the Imperial Legislative Council relating to which of the following?
n7dabe4c3838.x: B. N. Sarma moved the resolution for the creation of linguistic provinces in the Imperial Legislative Council on 6 February 1918.
n7dabe4c3838.tq: Use the date–mover–subject combination to identify the correct resolution.
xs: On **6 Feb 1918**, **B.N. Sarma** moved a resolution for **linguistic provinces** in the Imperial Legislative Council — so option **(3)** is correct.
Supported by **K.V. Rangaswami Ayyangar**; opposed by **Jinnah** and **V.S. Srinivasa Sastri**.
**Surendranath Banerjee** said "the time has not come"; **Tej Bahadur Sapru** would back it for Andhra only.
xa: B.N. Sarma (Visakhapatnam) presided the **1st Andhra Conference, Bapatla 1913**, where he called the province demand premature.
He founded the **Andhra Rajakeeya Samiti** (**1917**).
Later Council of State bids: **1925** (Dr. Ramarao, amended by Ramadasu Pantulu) and **1926** — both failed.

n0a56c417e8f.s: The Nizam Andhra Mahasabha, distinct from the Andhra Mahasabha of the Madras Presidency, began in 1930 at:
n0a56c417e8f.x: The Nizam Andhra Mahasabha began at Jogipet in 1930 under Suravaram Pratapa Reddy; the Madras Presidency body began at Bapatla in 1913 under B.N. Sarma.
xa: Nizam Andhra Mahasabha later sessions: **1931 Devarakonda** (Burgula Ramakrishna Rao), **1934 Khammam**, **1935 Siricilla** (Madapati Hanumantha Rao).
Andhra Mahasabha later sessions: **Vijayawada**, **Visakhapatnam**, **Kakinada**, **Nellore**.
The Nizam body's sessions also held women's conferences (**Andhra Mahila Sabha**).

ncd4616f32aa.s: The Visalandhra Mahasabha, formed in 1949, was intended to represent the demand for a state comprising:
o: The Telugu and Tamil-speaking areas jointly
ncd4616f32aa.x: The Visalandhra Mahasabha was formed to advocate the integration of all Telugu-speaking areas.
ncd4616f32aa.tq: Distinguish the geographical scope of an organisation from the narrower regional demands.
xs: The **Visalandhra Mahasabha** (**1949**) stood for a state of **all Telugu-speaking areas** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was formed after the **Dar Commission** and **JVP Committee** (**1948**).
xa: In the APPSC G2 2025 order: **Dhar → Visalandhra Mahasabha → Sitaram's fast → SRC**.
The Andhra State of **1 Oct 1953** had only **11** districts (7 coastal + 4 Rayalaseema) — not all Telugu areas.
**B. Ramakrishna Rao** shifted to favour merger in **1954**.

nap-history-1-6.s: Who was the first President of the Hyderabad State Congress?
nap-history-1-6.x: Govinda Rao Nanal was the first President of the Hyderabad State Congress.
n: The first Andhra Mahasabha or Andhra Conference was held on 26 May 1913 at Bapatla. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
Govinda Rao Nanal was the first President of the Hyderabad State Congress. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
xa: Bapatla was the **first Telugu session** and **demanded a separate university**.
⚠ Some notes date Bapatla **20 May 1913**; the keys give **26 May 1913**.
**Konda Venkatappayya** was the Bapatla **secretary**; the province resolution was **deferred**.
**B. Ramakrishna Rao** was the **first elected Chief Minister** of Hyderabad State.

nap-history-1-16.s: Which case was the first criminal case in the Vandemataram Movement?
nap-history-1-16.x: The Kakinada Riot Case (1907) was the first criminal case of the Vandemataram Movement in Andhra. Chintapalli is linked with Alluri Sitarama Raju and Palnadu with the Forest Satyagraha.
nap-history-1-16.tq: Link each place to its movement.
n: The Kakinada Riot Case was the first criminal case in the Vandemataram Movement. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
xs: The **Kakinada Riot Case** was the **first criminal case** of the **Vandemataram Movement** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Chintapalli** was the first police station attacked by **Alluri Sitarama Raju**.
**Palnadu** (Guntur) is where the **Forest Satyagraha** first started.
xa: **Vallabhaneni Sitamahalakshmi** — **first woman arrested** in the **Salt Satyagraha**.
**Nyapati Subba Rao** — **first lawyer** in Andhra to **boycott British courts**.
The **Vande Mataram movement (1905-11)** politicised Andhra youth.

nap-history-1-28.s: Who was the first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha in Andhra?
nap-history-1-28.x: Vallabhaneni Sitamahalakshmi was the first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha in Andhra.
n: Vallabhaneni Sitamahalakshmi was the first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
Nyapati Subba Rao was the first lawyer in Andhra to boycott British courts. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
xa: Nyapati Subba Rao was the **first President** of the **Andhra Congress Circle** (**1918**).
He presided the **2nd Mahasabha, Vijayawada 1914**, and led the delegation to **Montagu** (**20 Dec 1917**).
⚠ The APPSC G2 2011 key names **Konda Venkatappayya** as first APCC president (he was first **secretary**).

nap-history-40-6.s: The Vandemataram Struggle of 1938 was associated with which university?
nap-history-40-6.x: The 1938 Vandemataram Struggle took place at Osmania University, when students sang Vandemataram against the Nizam's ban.
nap-history-40-6.tq: Recall the university linked with the struggle.
n: The Vandemataram Struggle took place at Osmania University in 1938. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 51-52]
xs: The **Vandemataram Struggle of 1938** took place at **Osmania University** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Osmania University was established in **1918**.
**Sri Venkateswara University** dates to **1954** (Tirupathi); **Andhra University** to **1926**.
xa: **Andhra University Act** was passed under the **Justice Party** government; bill introduced **20 Aug 1925** by **A.P. Patro**.
**S. Radhakrishnan** was AU VC **1931-1936**.
**C.R. Reddy** coined "**City of Destiny**" for Visakhapatnam.

nap-history-17-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Third Andhra Mahasabha?
o: It was held at Visakhapatnam in 1915.
It demanded a separate Andhra Province.
It was presided over by the Raja of Panagal.
nap-history-17-2.x: The Third Andhra Mahasabha met at Visakhapatnam in 1915, not Bellary. It was presided over by the Raja of Panagal and demanded a separate Andhra Province.
n: The third Andhra Mahasabha was held in 1915. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
The third Andhra Mahasabha was held at Visakhapatnam. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
Panuganti Ramarayaningar, the Raja of Panagal, presided over the third Andhra Mahasabha. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
The third Andhra Mahasabha demanded the creation of a separate Andhra Province, or Andhra Rashtram. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
xa: **Bellary** hosted the **1936 Convention** under **Vijayanagar Gajapati**.
The **1915** session declared a separate state of **11 Telugu districts** just and necessary.
Session order: **Bapatla, Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Nellore, Kadapa**.

nap-history-17-10.s: Who was the president of the Andhra Mahasabha during 1941–46?
nap-history-17-10.x: Sir Gajapathi Vijayananda was president of the Andhra Mahasabha during 1941–46. Ravi Narayana Reddy and Suravaram Pratapa Reddy led the Andhra Mahasabha of Hyderabad State, a different body, and Konda Venkatappayya was an earlier organiser.
nap-history-17-10.tq: Discriminate the Coastal Andhra Mahasabha from the Telangana one.
n: Sir Gajapathi Vijayananda was president of the Andhra Mahasabha from 1941 to 1946. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
xs: **Sir Gajapathi Vijayananda** was president of the Andhra Mahasabha during **1941–46** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The Mahasabha was then based at **Visakhapatnam**; he met **Stafford Cripps** on **2 April 1942**.
**Ravi Narayana Reddy** and **Suravaram Pratapa Reddy** led the Andhra Mahasabha of the **Nizam's** state; **Konda Venkatappayya** presided the **5th** session (**1917**).
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: other notes name **M. Suryanarayana** as president **1941-46**.
At **Bellary (1943)** Sir Vijaya asked the Mahasabha to back pro-Andhra candidates.
The **1936** Bellary Convention was under **Vijayanagar Gajapati**.

nap-history-17-14.s: The Andhra Jana Sangham, formed in Hyderabad in 1921 and later renamed the Andhra Mahasabha, was led by:
nap-history-17-14.x: Madapati Hanumantha Rao led the Andhra Jana Sangham, later restructured as the Andhra Mahasabha.
n: The Andhra Jana Sangham was formed in 1921 under Madapati Hanumantha Rao. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
The Andhra Jana Sangham was formally restructured and renamed as the Andhra Mahasabha. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
xa: The **first Andhra Nizam Mahasabha** met at **Jogipet** in **1930** under **Suravaram Pratap Reddy**.
Later Nizam sessions: **1931 Devarakonda**, **1934 Khammam**, **1935 Siricilla**.
The **11th Bhongir session (1944)** under **Ravi Narayana Reddy** saw the **Communist** faction take control.

nap-history-17-23.s: Besides a separate Andhra Province, the Third Andhra Mahasabha (Visakhapatnam, 1915) demanded:
o: Madras as the capital of Andhra
the mother tongue as the medium of instruction in secondary schools
nap-history-17-23.x: The 1915 Visakhapatnam session demanded a separate Andhra Province (Andhra Rashtram) and the mother tongue as the medium in secondary schools.
n: The third Andhra Mahasabha demanded that the mother tongue be the medium of instruction in secondary schools. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
xa: The **1915** session declared a state of **11 Telugu districts** just and necessary; speeches were in Telugu.
Opposition to a separate Andhra state came from the **1935** Kadapa Rayalaseema Mahasabha.
**Swadesamitran**, a Tamil daily, backed the Telugu-medium resolution of **1915**.

nap-history-34-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Rayalaseema Mahasabha?
o: The Second Rayalaseema Mahasabha was presided over by Nemali Pattabhirama Rao.
The First Rayalaseema Mahasabha was held at Madras in January 1934.
The Second Rayalaseema Mahasabha was held at Kadapa in 1935.
The Second Rayalaseema Mahasabha opposed a separate Andhra state.
nap-history-34-2.x: Nemali Pattabhirama Rao presided over the first session at Madras in 1934; the second, at Kadapa in 1935, was under K. Subrahmanyam.
n: The First Rayalaseema Mahasabha was held on 28-1-1934 at Madras. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 45-46]
Nemali Pattabhirama Rao was the president of the First Rayalaseema Mahasabha. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 45-46]
The Second Rayalaseema Mahasabha was held in 1935 at Kadapa. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 45-46]
The Second Rayalaseema Mahasabha opposed a separate Andhra state. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 45-46]
xa: The first session was **organized** by **K. Subrahmanyam** and demanded a university at **Tirupati**.
**Pappuri Ramacharyulu**, Koti Reddy and Gadicherla stayed away from the Kadapa session.
**1938**: R. Suryanarayana Rao + N.M. Sastry formed a new Rayalaseema Mahasabha opposing an Andhra province.

nfce5136f13a.s: At Lucknow in 1916, the All-India Congress Committee, while examining the Andhra demand,
o: rejected the demand as harmful to national unity
referred the demand to the Montagu-Chelmsford Committee
examined the demand but took no decision
accepted the demand and immediately formed Andhra Province
nfce5136f13a.x: The AICC examined the demand at Lucknow in 1916 but took no decision. Pattabhi Sitaramayya pressed the demand there with Tilak’s support.
nfce5136f13a.tq: Distinguish examination of a proposal from its acceptance or rejection.
xs: At **Lucknow 1916** the AICC **examined the demand but took no decision** — option **(3)** is correct.
Some notes say **Pattabhi** pressed it there with **Tilak's** support.
It was then referred to provincial bodies in **December 1916**.
xa: The **Calcutta Congress (1917)** accepted the demand.
The **Andhra Congress Committee** was formed on **22 January 1918**.
Stance timeline: **1915** provincial conference refused; **1916** Lucknow no decision; **1918** separate committee.

n7e65ed5b368.s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Nagpur Congress session of 1920?
o: The membership fee was reduced to four annas.
Provincial Congress Committees were reorganised on a linguistic basis.
An AICC of 350 members and a Congress Working Committee were provided for.
The goal of complete independence by armed means was adopted.
n7e65ed5b368.x: The Nagpur session changed the goal to Swaraj by peaceful and legitimate means, not complete independence through armed struggle. The other three features belonged to the reorganisation adopted at Nagpur.
n7e65ed5b368.tq: Find the one statement that reverses the session’s constitutional and political programme.
xs: **Complete independence by armed means** was NOT a Nagpur feature — option **(4)** is correct.
Nagpur (**December 1920**) cut the membership fee to **4 annas**.
It reorganised **PCCs on linguistic lines**.
It created an **AICC of 350** + a **Congress Working Committee**.
xa: Nagpur was presided by **C. Vijayaraghavachariar**.
The Andhra PCC (formed **1918**) became a **regular linguistic unit**.
The **Calcutta special session (September 1920)** accepted non-cooperation.

ncdd85f67c4e.s: The opposition of R. Suryanarayana Rao and N.M. Sastry in 1938 was mainly based on the fear of:
ncdd85f67c4e.x: The new Rayalaseema Mahasabha leaders R. Suryanarayana Rao and N.M. Sastry opposed the demand because they feared Circars domination.
ncdd85f67c4e.tq: Connect the opposition with the regional interest behind it.
xs: **R. Suryanarayana Rao** and **N.M. Sastry** (**1938**) opposed the Andhra province fearing **Circars domination** over Rayalaseema — option **(2)** is correct.
They formed a **new Rayalaseema Mahasabha** for this purpose.
xa: **1937**: **Rajaji's** cabinet had **no Rayalaseema minister** → deepened the rift.
**1948**: the Rayalaseema Mahasabha told the **Dhar Commission** it wanted a separate Rayalaseema state with **Madras** as capital.
Causes of distrust: **1913 Mahanandi**, the **1934** and **1935** Mahasabhas, and the Andhra University seat going to **Waltair**.

n0f4d41862de.s: Who drafted the Andhra University Bill?
n0f4d41862de.x: Kattamanchi Ramalinga Reddy drafted the Andhra University Bill.
n0f4d41862de.tq: Identify the person associated with the specific legislative task rather than the broader Andhra movement.
xs: The **Andhra University Bill** was drafted by **Kattamanchi Ramalinga Reddy** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Vemavarapu Ramadasu Pantulu** is known for moving the separate-province resolution at **Bapatla (1913)**; **V. Satyanarayana** supported it.
xa: **K.V. Reddy Naidu** proposed the name "**Telugu Viswavidyalayam**".
The Bill was introduced on **20 Aug 1925** by Education Minister **A.P. Patro** (Justice Party).

n0df3111882d.s: Who proposed the name “Telugu Viswavidyalayam” for the proposed university?
n0df3111882d.x: K.V. Reddy Naidu proposed the name “Telugu Viswavidyalayam.”
n0df3111882d.tq: Discriminate the proposer from other persons associated with the university demand.
xs: **K.V. Reddy Naidu** proposed the name "**Telugu Viswavidyalayam**" — option **(4)** is correct.
**Venkatapathi Raju** moved a resolution in the Madras Legislative Council (**Feb 1917**); **M. Suryanarayana's** resolution was accepted on **2 Sept 1921**; **C. Natesa Mudaliar** opposed it.
xa: The Bill was drafted by **Kattamanchi Ramalinga Reddy**.
**Oct 1920**: Madras University Senate accepted **linguistic universities**.
**1923**: the **Stout Commission**.

ne6afe9d1121.s: Andhra University was inaugurated at Waltair on:
ne6afe9d1121.x: After Subbaroyan's ministry fixed the seat at Visakhapatnam (December 1928), it was inaugurated at Waltair on 5 September 1930.
xa: The shift to Visakhapatnam followed **C.R. Reddy's report** (APPSC 2019), chosen for its **climate and setting**.
**C.R. Reddy** coined "**City of Destiny**" for Visakhapatnam.
The Andhra University Act of **1925** was passed under the **Justice Party**.

nfa231e61dc6.s: C.R. Reddy selected Waltair for the university seat primarily because of its:
o: Political importance and proximity to Madras
nfa231e61dc6.x: C.R. Reddy chose Waltair for its climate and setting. He also coined the expression “City of Destiny” for Visakhapatnam.
nfa231e61dc6.tq: Identify the practical basis of an institutional-location decision rather than its political consequences.
xs: **C.R. Reddy** chose **Waltair** for its **climate and setting** — option **(1)** is correct.
The shift to **Visakhapatnam** followed **C.R. Reddy's report** (APPSC 2019).
xa: He coined "**City of Destiny**" for Visakhapatnam.
Seat fixed **Dec 1928** by **Dr. Subbaroyan's** ministry; inaugurated at Waltair on **5 Sept 1930**.
The **Waltair Andhra Varotsavalu** (Dec **1937**) — Andhra Week by students under VC **C.R. Reddy**.

n61bef445d57.s: When an amendment excluded Rayalaseema from Andhra University's jurisdiction, its colleges went back to:
n61bef445d57.x: The amendment excluded Rayalaseema from Andhra University's jurisdiction, and its colleges returned to Madras University.
xa: **Sri Venkateswara University, Tirupati** was founded in **1954** for Rayalaseema.
The **Sri Bagh Pact (1937)** promised AU centres at **Waltair and Anantapur**.
The **Anantapur** claim had won a Senate vote of **35-20**.

n64fb3b15dbf.s: The first Rayalaseema Mahasabha demanded a separate university at:
n64fb3b15dbf.x: The first Rayalaseema Mahasabha opposed inclusion in Andhra University and demanded a separate university at Tirupati.
xs: The **1st Rayalaseema Mahasabha** demanded a separate university at **Tirupati** — option **(3)** is correct.
It **opposed** inclusion in **Andhra University**.
xa: Held **28 January 1934**, presided by **Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao**.
**Sri Venkateswara University, Tirupati** came in **1954**.
⚠ **Anantapur** was the Rayalaseema **seat claim** for AU (Senate vote **35-20**), and a Sri Bagh university centre.

nc17a6a4ae8e.s: The second Rayalaseema Mahasabha, held in September 1935, adopted which of the following resolutions?
o: Opposition to a separate Andhra state
Demand for immediate merger with Telangana
Demand for a separate Andhra province without safeguards
Demand for Madras as the capital of Andhra State
nc17a6a4ae8e.x: The second Rayalaseema Mahasabha held at Kadapa in September 1935 opposed the creation of a separate Andhra state.
nc17a6a4ae8e.tq: Test the precise resolution rather than the general regional demand.
xs: The **2nd Rayalaseema Mahasabha** (**September 1935, Kadapa**) **opposed a separate Andhra state** — option **(1)** is correct.
It did not demand a province without safeguards; it opposed separate Andhra **without safeguards** (APPSC 2017).
xa: Presided by **T.N. Ramakrishna Reddy**.
**Koti Reddy**, **Pappuri Ramachari** and **Gadicherla** stayed away.
This opposition led to the **Sri Bagh Pact** (**1937**).

n31123fc3882.s: The 1935 opposition of the Rayalaseema Mahasabha to a separate Andhra state eventually contributed to the:
n31123fc3882.x: The 1935 resolution opposing a separate Andhra state led to the Sri Bagh Pact, which addressed Rayalaseema safeguards.
n31123fc3882.tq: Test the cause-and-effect link between a regional resolution and its outcome.
xs: The **1935** Rayalaseema opposition (no separate Andhra **without safeguards**) led to the **Sri Bagh Pact** — option **(2)** is correct.
**JVP** and **Dhar** were **1948** bodies on linguistic states; **Nagpur 1920** reorganised **PCCs** on linguistic lines.
xa: Sri Bagh Pact: **16 November 1937**, at **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's** house in Madras.
Purpose: allay Rayalaseema fears of **coastal domination**.
Trigger: the **Silver Jubilee session** (**1937**) asked for safeguards.

nd1efb18cb83.s: What position did the Rayalaseema Mahasabha communicate to the Dhar Commission in 1948?
o: A united Andhra province with Vijayawada as capital
Immediate merger with the Hyderabad State
A separate Rayalaseema state with Madras as capital
Continuation of the Madras Presidency without reorganisation
nd1efb18cb83.x: In 1948, the Rayalaseema Mahasabha told the Dhar Commission that it wanted a separate Rayalaseema state with Madras as its capital.
nd1efb18cb83.tq: Discriminate between a regional demand and the proposed capital.
xs: In **1948**, the Rayalaseema Mahasabha told the **Dhar Commission** it wanted a **separate Rayalaseema state with Madras as capital** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Vijayawada** was the **Communists'** choice for Andhra's capital in **1953**.
xa: **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy**, for **20** Rayalaseema MLAs, opposed linguistic states or asked that **Sribagh** terms be written in.
**Kadapa Koti Reddy** (**1933**) wanted **Madras as Andhra capital**.
The **Dhar Commission** (**17 June 1948**) reported **against linguistic states**.

n1ffe04f8030.s: The Sreebagh Pact was concluded on:
n1ffe04f8030.x: The Sreebagh Pact of 16 November 1937 put the capital and High Court in different regions and gave Rayalaseema first choice.
xa: Irrigation priority to Rayalaseema in **Krishna, Tungabhadra, Pennar** waters for **10 years**.
Implemented in **1953**: capital **Kurnool**, High Court **Guntur**.
⚠ **Sri Bagh** = **1937**, Coastal–Rayalaseema; **Gentlemen's Agreement** = **1956**, Andhra–Telangana.

n074e0427ab1.s: The Sri Bagh Pact primarily sought to:
o: End the demand for a separate Andhra province
Establish Hyderabad as the permanent capital of Andhra
Allay Rayalaseema fears of Coastal Andhra domination
Create a separate university for Telangana
n074e0427ab1.x: The pact was designed to remove Rayalaseema's fears of domination by Coastal Andhra and thereby facilitate a common Andhra demand.
n074e0427ab1.tq: Identify the underlying political purpose rather than a specific clause.
xs: The pact sought to **allay Rayalaseema fears of Coastal Andhra domination** — option **(3)** is correct.
It aimed to **unite** the regions before a common Andhra demand — not to end it.
xa: It united Telugu Congress leaders for the **1937 elections**.
It set the "gentlemen's agreement" pattern used in **1956**.
Its capital, High Court and irrigation terms are **still cited** in Rayalaseema debates.

na3dbfb4501d.s: The Sri Bagh Pact of 1937 promised Andhra University centres at Waltair and:
na3dbfb4501d.x: The Sri Bagh Pact of 1937 promised Andhra University centres at Waltair and Anantapur.
xa: Capital and High Court in **separate regions**, Rayalaseema choosing first.
Irrigation **priority to Rayalaseema** for **10 years**.
Legislature seats allotted **district-wise on an equal basis**.

n473e2941db2.s: The Sri Bagh Pact was signed on 16 November 1937 at Sri Bagh, the residence of:
n473e2941db2.x: The pact was signed at Sri Bagh, the residence of (Kasinathuni) Nageswara Rao of Andhra Patrika.
xa: ⚠ "K. Koteswara Rao" as owner — wrong (APPSC G2 2017 key = Kasinathuni).
Kasinathuni founded **Andhra Patrika** (**1908**); title **Desoddharaka**.
He presided the special **Guntur** session, **17 Aug 1918**.

n086f50cc5ec.s: Who presided over the Silver Jubilee session of the Andhra Mahasabha at Vijayawada in 1937?
n086f50cc5ec.x: Kadapa Koti Reddy presided over the 1937 session (and the 1931 Special Andhra Sabha); H.M. Sitaram Reddy only inaugurated it.
xa: Both were **Rayalaseema** leaders.
Koti Reddy was Andhra Mahasabha president at the time of **Sri Bagh** and a Rayalaseema signatory.
In **1933** he proposed **Madras** as the Andhra capital.

n44e447c13b3.s: In the Madras city question, who proposed the Cooum river as the boundary?
n44e447c13b3.x: Panaganti Ramarayaningar proposed the Cooum boundary in the early 1920s; Kadapa Koti Reddy proposed Madras as capital in 1933.
xa: **1952**: **Sriramulu's** demand — Madras as a **Chief Commissioner's (C-class) state**.
**19 December 1952**: Andhra announced, **excluding Madras city**.
**Prakasam's** book: "**Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae**".

ne5bcf5fec1d.s: The provisions of the Sri Bagh Pact continue to be cited particularly in contemporary debates concerning:
o: the status of the Telugu language in the Union List
the creation of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council
the merger of Andhra with Maharashtra
Rayalaseema’s capital, High Court and irrigation concerns
ne5bcf5fec1d.x: The Sri Bagh terms concerning capital, High Court and irrigation remain important in Rayalaseema-related debates.
ne5bcf5fec1d.tq: Group the three linked provisions under the region whose interests they addressed.
xs: The **Sri Bagh** terms on **capital, High Court and irrigation** are still cited in Rayalaseema debates — option **(4)** is correct.
The pact (**16 Nov 1937**) put **Capital and High Court in separate regions**, Rayalaseema choosing first.
xa: Irrigation clause: **priority to Rayalaseema** in Krishna, Tungabhadra and Pennar waters for **10 years**.
University clause: AU centres at **Waltair and Anantapur**.
Signed at **'Sri Bagh', Madras**, the house of **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.
⚠ **Sri Bagh** = **1937**, Coastal-Rayalaseema; **Gentlemen's Agreement** = **1956**, Andhra-Telangana.

nap-history-33-18.s: Gandhi visited Hyderabad on 9 March of which year?
nap-history-33-18.x: Gandhi's Hyderabad visit was on 9 March 1934, the same year as the first Rayalaseema Mahasabha (28 January).
n: The first Andhra Mahasabha was held in 1913. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
The first Rayalaseema Mahasabha was held on January 28, 1934. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
The Sribagh Agreement was signed on November 16, 1937. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
Gandhi visited Hyderabad on March 9, 1934. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
xa: The **second Rayalaseema Mahasabha** (**Kadapa**, **1935**) opposed a separate Andhra state.
The **Gentlemen's Agreement** came on **20 February 1956**.

nap-history-17-5.s: The second session of the Vishalandhra Mahasabha, held at Hyderabad in 1954, was presided over by:
nap-history-17-5.x: K.V. Ranga Reddy presided over the 1954 session; Swamy Ramananda Tirtha strongly supported Vishalandhra.
n: The second Vishalandhra Mahasabha session was held in 1954. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
The second Vishalandhra Mahasabha session was held at Hyderabad. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
Sri K. V. Ranga Reddy presided over the second Vishalandhra Mahasabha session. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
Swamy Ramananda Tirtha strongly supported Vishalandhra. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
xa: The **Visalandhra Mahasabha** was formed in **1949** for all Telugu areas.
K.V. Rangareddy was later the **first Deputy CM** of Andhra Pradesh.
The **Gentlemen's Agreement** (**20 February 1956**) set Telangana safeguards on merger.

nap-history-17-9.s: The 1936 Andhra Mahasabha convention, which sought to bridge the trust deficit between Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema leaders, was held at:
nap-history-17-9.x: The 1936 convention met at Bellary and paved the way for the Sribagh Pact of 1937.
n: The 1936 Andhra Mahasabha Convention was held at Bellary. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
The 1936 Andhra Mahasabha Convention aimed to bridge trust deficits between Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema leaders. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
xa: The rift led to the **Sri Bagh Pact** (**16 November 1937**).
The **1937 Silver Jubilee session** (Vijayawada) under **Kadapa Koti Reddy** sought safeguards in **Cabinet, Irrigation and Capital**.
The **1935** Rayalaseema Mahasabha opposed a separate Andhra state.

nap-history-17-15.s: Who presided over the first session of the Nizam Mahasabha Andhra?
nap-history-17-15.x: Suravaram Pratapa Reddy presided over the first Nizam Andhra Mahasabha at Jogipet in 1930. Madapati Hanumantha Rao led the earlier Andhra Jana Sangham.
nap-history-17-15.tq: Recall the president of the Jogipet session.
n: Suravaram Pratap Reddy presided over the first Andhra Nizam Mahasabha. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
xs: **Suravaram Pratapa Reddy** presided the **first** Nizam Andhra Mahasabha — so option **(4)** is correct.
It met at **Jogipet** (Medak) in **1930**.
**Madapati Hanumantha Rao** led the earlier **Andhra Jana Sangham** (**1921**); **Ravi Narayana Reddy** presided at **Bhongir** (**1944**).
xa: **Burgula Ramakrishna Rao** presided the **1931 Devarakonda** session.
⚠ Do not confuse with the Madras Presidency Andhra Mahasabha — begun at **Bapatla**, **1913**, first president **B.N. Sarma**.
The **Andhra Jatiya Mahasabha** (**1930**) was helped by **Suravaram Pratapa Reddy** and **Burgula Ramakrishna Rao**.

nap-history-17-16.s: Who founded the Jatiya Mahasabha Andhra?
o: Madapati Hanumantha Rao and B.N. Sharma
Ravi Narayana Reddy and K. Subrahmanyam
Suravaram Pratapa Reddy and Burgula Ramakrishna Rao
Konda Venkatappayya and Nemali Pattabhirama Rao
nap-history-17-16.x: Suravaram Pratapa Reddy and Burgula Ramakrishna Rao founded the Jatiya Andhra Mahasabha. The other pairs mix coastal and Rayalaseema leaders.
nap-history-17-16.tq: Recall the founders of the Jatiya Mahasabha.
n: The Andhra Jatiya Mahasabha was founded in 1930. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
Suravaram Pratapa Reddy helped found the Andhra Jatiya Mahasabha. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
Burgula Ramakrishna Rao helped found the Andhra Jatiya Mahasabha. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 23-25]
xs: The **Jatiya Mahasabha Andhra** (**1930**) was founded with the help of **Suravaram Pratapa Reddy and Burgula Ramakrishna Rao** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Madapati Hanumantha Rao** led the **Andhra Jana Sangham** (**1921**); **B.N. Sharma** presided at **Bapatla**.
**Konda Venkatappayya** and **Nemali Pattabhirama Rao** belong to the Andhra and Rayalaseema Mahasabhas.
xa: Suravaram Pratap Reddy presided the first Nizam Andhra Mahasabha at **Jogipet**, **1930**, and edited **Golconda Patrika**.
Burgula presided the **1931 Devarakonda** session.
**Ravi Narayana Reddy** presided the **11th Bhongir session (1944)**.

n04962f32204.s: Konda Venkatappayya came to prominence among the Andhra Moderates after:
n04962f32204.x: Konda Venkatappayya rose among Andhra Moderates after 1908, so he was not an Andhra delegate at the first INC session of 1885.
xa: **P. Anandacharlu** and **Nyapathi Subbarao** (**Rajahmundry**) attended the 1st session.
**B.N. Sarma** rose alongside Venkatappayya after 1908.
**Kesava Pillai** is listed among the early Andhra leaders.

nf9037a36302.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over the session of the Indian National Congress held in 1948 at:
nf9037a36302.x: He presided at Jaipur in 1948; at Tripuri (1939) he had lost to Subhas Bose despite Gandhi's backing.
xa: ⚠ The **APPSC G2 2011** key named Pattabhi "first Telugu person" — read the wording.
Pattabhi was president of the **JVP Committee**'s **Jaipur** AICC session (**Dec 1948**).
**N. Sanjiva Reddy**: INC president **1960-62**.

n0d072f5516e.s: The reorganisation of the Provincial Congress Committees on linguistic lines was undertaken at the:
n0d072f5516e.x: The Congress reorganised its Provincial Congress Committees on linguistic lines at the Nagpur session in 1920. Linguistic provinces had therefore been a Congress commitment since the 1920s.
