n0d072f5516e.tq: Distinguish the organisational decision at Nagpur from later constitutional debates.
xs: PCCs were reorganised on linguistic lines at the **Nagpur session, 1920** — option **(2)** is correct.
Linguistic states had thus been a **Congress commitment since the 1920s**.
**Jaipur** hosted the **Dec 1948** AICC session that set up the **JVP Committee**.
xa: "PCCs after **1920** were based on linguistic regions" (**APPSC 2016**).
The **Nehru Report (1928)** advocated linguistic provinces in line with this.
Andhra (**1953**) was the first to claim the promise.

n95d27523b79.s: The Nehru Report of 1928 advocated linguistic provinces in accordance with the:
n95d27523b79.x: The Nehru Report advocated linguistic provinces in line with the reorganisation of Provincial Congress Committees undertaken in 1920.
n95d27523b79.tq: Link a constitutional recommendation to the earlier organisational precedent it followed.
xs: The **Nehru Report (1928)** advocated linguistic provinces in line with the **1920 reorganisation of PCCs** — option **(1)** is correct.
The PCCs were reorganised at **Nagpur, 1920**.
Linguistic states were thus a Congress promise **since the 1920s**.
xa: **1928**: **A. Kaleswara Rao** reminded the Madras Council of the delay.
The **Simon Commission** toured in **1928**, boycotted by Congress.
The **Montagu-Chelmsford Report** (**July 1918**) had no Andhra provision.

n502b290b7e2.s: The Andhra Provincial Congress Committee was formed in:
n502b290b7e2.x: The Andhra PCC was formed in 1918 and became a regular linguistic unit after the Nagpur session.
xa: The Andhra Congress Committee was formed on **22 January 1918**.
This showed early **Congress commitment to linguistic provinces**.
**6th Mahasabha** (Kadapa, **1918**): the **Andhra Provincial Congress Conference** met alongside.

nf181a7e8027.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Montagu-Chelmsford Report of July 1918?
o: It accepted the All-India Linguistic States Conference proposal.
It made no provision for Andhra.
It provided for a separate Andhra province.
nf181a7e8027.x: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report of July 1918 made no provision for Andhra.
nf181a7e8027.tq: Test the precise omission in the reform report rather than assuming that the deputation succeeded.
xs: The **Montagu-Chelmsford Report** (**July 1918**) **made no provision for Andhra** — option **(2)** is correct.
In response, the special **Guntur** session (**17 Aug 1918**) protested.
There **Pattabhi** proposed an **All-India Linguistic States Conference** — the report did not accept it.
xa: **Krishna Patrika** mocked the scheme as "digging a mountain to catch a mouse".
**Venkatapati Raju** moved a matching resolution in the **Madras Legislative Council**.
**Dec 1918**: a delegation to **London**; **Mocherla Ramachandra Rao** submitted a memorandum.

n03a8fcec1fe.s: At the special Mahasabha at Guntur in 1918, Pattabhi Sitaramayya proposed
o: a deputation to the Round Table Conference
the transfer of Bellary to Madras
a boycott of the Simon Commission
n03a8fcec1fe.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya proposed an All-India Linguistic States Conference at the special Guntur Mahasabha.
n03a8fcec1fe.tq: Match the proposal with the meeting at which it was made.
xs: At the special **Guntur** Mahasabha (**17 Aug 1918**) **Pattabhi** proposed an **All-India Linguistic States Conference** — option **(4)** is correct.
The session was presided by **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.
The **Simon Commission** boycott (**1928**) and the **RTC** deputation (**1931**) came later.
xa: It protested that **Montagu-Chelmsford** had no Andhra province.
**Dec 1918**: Vijayawada APCC under **Pattabhi** sent a delegation to **London**.
Pattabhi chaired a committee to collect opinion after **Bapatla (1913)**.

nd977f46e403.s: When Andhra University was established in 1926, its headquarters was at:
nd977f46e403.x: At its establishment on 26 April 1926, Andhra University had its headquarters at Vijayawada and its teaching centre at Rajahmundry.
xa: ⚠ APPSC G2 2012 key answered **Kakinada** for "first established in which town"; G2 2008 key + notes give **Vijayawada**.
Inaugurated at **Waltair** on **5 Sept 1930**.
The **Anantapur** claim won a Senate vote of **35-20**.

n5f1d1311d74.s: Which book argued the Telugu claim over Madras by declaring that Madras was an Andhra city?
o: The Telugu People and Madras Presidency
On the Present Position of the Telugu People
n5f1d1311d74.x: Tanguturi Prakasam's book “Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae” argued that Madras was an Andhra city.
n5f1d1311d74.tq: Identify the work through its distinctive title and claim.
xs: **Tanguturi Prakasam's** book "**Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae**" declared **Madras an Andhra city** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ "**On the present position of the Telugu people**" was **Jonnavittula Gurunatham's** series in **The Hindu** (**1911**).
xa: **Andhra Congress** wanted **half of Madras town**.
Telugu demand: Madras as **capital** or a **shared Union Territory**.
**Nehru (25 March 1953)**: "**No question**" of Madras as the capital.

nda428f3f48b.s: Which leader, and later Kamaraj, opposed sharing Madras city with the Andhras?
nda428f3f48b.x: Rajaji and later Kamaraj opposed sharing Madras; the JVP formula required the Andhras to drop their claim to it.
xa: Nellore **1917**: province passed by **district-wise voting**, proposed by **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**.
**CWC** recommendation: Andhra **without Madras city**.
**Sriramulu's** 1952 condition: Madras → **C-class state** by agreement.

n9770692d449.s: The Dar Commission (June 1948) was appointed by the:
n9770692d449.x: It was appointed by the President of the Constituent Assembly in June 1948, with S.K. Dhar as chairman.
xa: Members: **Dr. Panna Lal** and **Jagat Narayan Lal**.
Report **10 Dec 1948**, published **13 Dec** — **against linguistic states**.
⚠ **Dar** = appointed by **Constituent Assembly**; **JVP** = by **Congress**.

n5d7cd2d6a3b.s: The principal mandate of the Dar Commission was to examine the formation of which group of provinces and their boundaries and consequences?
o: Karnataka, Gujarat, Kerala and Tamil Nadu
n5d7cd2d6a3b.x: The Dar Commission examined the formation of Andhra, Karnataka, Kerala and Maharashtra, including their boundaries and consequences.
n5d7cd2d6a3b.tq: Recall the complete named set; do not replace the listed provinces with later state names.
xs: The Dar Commission's mandate: formation of **Andhra, Karnataka, Kerala and Maharashtra** — boundaries and consequences — option **(3)** is correct.
It was appointed on **17 June 1948** by the **Constituent Assembly**.
xa: Chairman **S.K. Dhar**; members **Dr. Panna Lal**, **Jagat Narayan Lal**.
It favoured **administrative convenience** over language.
APCC under **N.G. Ranga** gave it a memorandum on **10 Sep 1948**.

nc9a851066c3.s: The Dar Commission recommended that provinces should be reorganised primarily on the basis of:
nc9a851066c3.x: The Dar Commission recommended administrative convenience rather than language as the primary basis for reorganisation.
nc9a851066c3.tq: Use the central recommendation and distinguish it from the linguistic principle later adopted.
xs: The Dar Commission recommended reorganisation on **administrative convenience** — option **(4)** is correct.
It rejected **linguistic identity** as the basis, warning of a threat to **national unity**.
xa: Criteria: geographical contiguity, financial self-reliance, administrative viability, development potential.
Appointed **17 June 1948** by the **Constituent Assembly**.
The **JVP** report (**April 1949**) reaffirmed Dhar.

nf8683694f4d.s: The Dar Commission warned that the creation of linguistic states could threaten:
nf8683694f4d.x: The Commission warned that linguistic states threatened national unity and thereby rejected the linguistic basis at that stage.
nf8683694f4d.tq: Link the distinctive warning directly with the Commission that issued it.
xs: The Dar Commission warned that linguistic states threatened **national unity** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Financial self-reliance** and **administrative viability** were its **criteria**, not the threatened values.
xa: This was the **first official rejection** of the linguistic basis.
Exam angle: APPSC G2 2025 — "**1948, Justice S.K. Dhar**".
The **JVP** Committee also put **security, unity, economic prosperity** first.

n73a24f07f55.s: During his 1948 visit to ____, Nehru promised a committee on the Andhra/linguistic province issue.
n73a24f07f55.x: Nehru promised a committee during his 1948 Visakhapatnam visit, part of the background to the Dar Commission and JVP Committee.
xa: Andhra was **dropped** from the Draft Constitution published **21 Feb 1948** after Tamil and Kannada objections.
The Centre went slow, fearing for **national unity** after Partition.
The **Dar Commission** followed on **17 June 1948**.

n781ed493fb6.s: After 1947, the Central Government went slow on linguistic states mainly because it feared:
o: a constitutional bar on language-based states
n781ed493fb6.x: With Partition, Kashmir and the princely-state question still unsettled, the Government feared linguistic reorganisation could endanger national unity.
xa: Government **accepted the principle in 1947** but delayed acting.
The **Dar** report (**Dec 1948**) warned of a threat to **national unity**.
**Delay** is blamed on Centre caution + **Andhra factionalism**.

nb1d12e9e27e.s: Which one of the following was NOT a member of the Linguistic Provinces Commission appointed in 1948?
nb1d12e9e27e.x: The Commission consisted of S.K. Dhar, Dr Pannalal and Jagat Narayan Lal. Pattabhi Sitaramayya was a member of the later JVP Committee.
nb1d12e9e27e.tq: Find the person belonging to the neighbouring committee rather than the named body.
xs: **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** was **not** on the Dhar Commission — he was on the **JVP** Committee — option **(4)** is the answer.
The Commission: **S.K. Dhar** (chair), **Dr. Panna Lal**, **Jagat Narayan Lal**.
xa: JVP = **Jawaharlal Nehru**, **Vallabhbhai Patel**, **Pattabhi Sitaramayya**.
⚠ **N. Sanjiva Reddy** was **not** a JVP member (APPSC 2021).
⚠ **Dar** = Constituent Assembly; **JVP** = Congress.

nf8d8d4f66d1.s: The JVP Committee was constituted in December 1948 at the AICC session held at:
nf8d8d4f66d1.x: It was constituted at the Jaipur AICC session (December 1948) with Pattabhi Sitaramayya as president and reported in 1949.
xa: Members: **Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi** ("Three Ministers Committee").
Report: Andhra possible **if Madras city was given up**.
Some questions say "**Jaipur, 1949**".

n029f97cb622.s: Which one of the following best reflects the recommendation of the JVP Committee regarding the creation of new provinces?
o: Creation of provinces solely on financial criteria
Postponement of the creation of new provinces
Merger of all Telugu areas with Hyderabad
Immediate creation of all provinces on a linguistic basis
n029f97cb622.x: The JVP Committee recommended postponing the creation of new provinces, while allowing Andhra's claim to be considered subject to giving up the claim to Madras city.
n029f97cb622.tq: Identify the committee's cautious recommendation rather than the later outcome of Andhra State formation.
xs: The JVP Committee recommended **postponing the creation of new provinces** — option **(2)** is correct.
It rejected **immediate linguistic reorganisation**, putting **security, unity and economic prosperity** first.
xa: It **reaffirmed the Dhar** report.
Exception: **Andhra** could be formed if the Madras claim was dropped.
**CWC** then recommended Andhra **without Madras city**.

n10e56a9febf.s: The JVP Committee's report reaffirmed the general approach of the:
n10e56a9febf.x: The JVP report reaffirmed the Dhar approach, putting security, unity and economic prosperity above immediate linguistic reorganisation.
xa: Report submitted **April 1949** to the **CWC**.
**T.T. Krishnamachari**: neighbouring states would also have to consent.
Madras government + **Tamil Nadu Congress** agreed to Andhra without Madras.

na1e92dbd631.s: What did the Congress Working Committee recommend after the JVP report regarding the creation of Andhra State?
o: No linguistic state should be formed until after the States Reorganisation Commission.
Andhra should be merged with Rayalaseema and Hyderabad immediately.
Andhra should be formed without Madras city.
Andhra should be formed with Madras city as its capital and half the city shared with Tamil areas.
na1e92dbd631.x: The Congress Working Committee recommended forming Andhra without Madras city. The Madras government and Tamil Nadu Congress accepted this position, while Andhra Congress wanted half of Madras town.
na1e92dbd631.tq: Test the exact institutional recommendation and avoid confusing it with the Andhra Congress demand.
xs: The **CWC** recommended Andhra **without Madras city** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **Madras government** and **Tamil Nadu Congress** agreed; the **Andhra Congress** wanted **half of Madras town**.
xa: This followed the **JVP** report of **April 1949**.
The Madras **Partition Committee** followed (Cabinet decision **7 Dec 1949**).
**P.S. Kumaraswamy Raja's** government accepted Andhra on **JVP terms**.

n2e8455b04cc.s: The committee formed by the Madras Government under Chief Minister P.S. Kumaraswami Raja was primarily concerned with:
o: Selecting the first Governor of Andhra State
Dividing the assets and liabilities between Madras and Andhra
Drafting a constitution for Andhra State
n2e8455b04cc.x: The committee was constituted to divide assets and liabilities between the proposed Andhra region and Madras. It failed because Madras leaders refused to surrender Madras city to Andhra.
n2e8455b04cc.tq: Identify the purpose of the committee before examining why it failed.
xs: The **Partition Committee** under CM **P.S. Kumaraswami Raja** was formed to **divide assets and liabilities** — option **(3)** is correct.
It also handled **administrative arrangements** and the **six Bellary taluks**.
xa: Madras Cabinet decided on it on **7 Dec 1949**.
Report **4 Jan 1950**; **Prakasam** wrote a separate report.
It **failed**: Madras leaders refused to let **Madras city** go to Andhra.

nf0588f5e086.s: Which Madras Chief Minister chaired the Partition Committee constituted in 1949?
nf0588f5e086.x: P.S. Kumaraswamy Raja, Chief Minister of Madras from 1949 to 1952, chaired the Partition Committee.
nf0588f5e086.tq: Use the office-holder trap by separating the committee chairman from the committee members.
xs: **P.S. Kumaraswamy Raja** (Madras CM **1949-52**) chaired the Partition Committee — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes say **T.T. Krishnamachari** — wrong (APPSC G2 2025 key = Kumaraswamy Raja).
xa: Andhra members: **T. Prakasam**, **Kala Venkatrao**, **Bezawada Gopala Reddy**, **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy**.
Tamil members: **T.T. Krishnamachari**, **C. Rajagopalachari**, **Madhava Menon**.
Report: **4 Jan 1950**.

n7189ad75bc7.s: The committee headed by Justice K.N. Wanchoo was appointed on:
n7189ad75bc7.x: Justice K.N. Wanchoo was appointed on 7 February 1953 to report on the implications of the proposed Andhra State.
n7189ad75bc7.tq: Use exact-date discrimination among closely related Andhra movement events.
xs: **Justice K.N. Wanchoo** was appointed on **7 February 1953** — option **(2)** is correct.
**19 December 1952** = Nehru's announcement; **19 October 1952** = start of Sriramulu's fast.
xa: Wanchoo was **Chief Justice, Rajasthan HC**; a **single-member** committee.
He reported on the **implications** of forming Andhra.
Report dated **25 Mar 1953** (some notes **23 March 1953**).

nf390dcb5a1e.s: The Wanchoo inquiry was conducted during:
nf390dcb5a1e.x: The Wanchoo inquiry was held in February–March 1953, after the Dhar Commission, JVP Committee and the Madras Partition Committee (1949–50).
xa: Partition Committee chairman: **Kumaraswamy Raja**, Madras CM (APPSC G2 2025 key).
**Justice K.N. Wanchoo** (Chief Justice, Rajasthan HC) was a **single-member** committee.
⚠ **Dar** = appointed by the **Constituent Assembly**; **JVP** = appointed by **Congress**.

nb5fe3bac815.s: The formation of Andhra State in 1953 is commonly described as the “Andhra exception” because it:
o: allowed Madras to become the capital of a separate Andhra State
created a state without any elected legislature
reversed the decision to use language as a basis for state formation
opened the way for the States Reorganisation Commission and nationwide linguistic reorganisation
nb5fe3bac815.x: Although the Dhar Commission and JVP Committee were cautious about linguistic states, the Andhra exception paved the way for the SRC and broader linguistic reorganisation.
nb5fe3bac815.tq: Identify the historical consequence rather than merely recalling the event itself.
xs: The "**Andhra exception**" opened the way to the **SRC** and nationwide **linguistic reorganisation** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Dhar** and **JVP** both rejected language as a basis, yet JVP's Andhra exception (**minus Madras**) became the formula used in **1953**.
So it did not hand Madras to Andhra, nor reverse the linguistic principle.
xa: **Potti Sriramulu's death** forced the Centre's hand → Andhra → **SRC (Dec 1953)** → **States Reorganisation Act 1956**.
JVP's report (**April 1949**): Andhra could be formed **if Andhras gave up Madras city**.
SRC members: **Fazl Ali**, **Kunzru**, **Panikkar**.

naa8b60903f4.s: Which body, set up in 1953, dealt specifically with the formation of Andhra State?
naa8b60903f4.x: The sequence was Dhar (1948), JVP (1948-49), Wanchoo (1953, for Andhra) and Fazal Ali SRC (1953-55, all India).
xa: SRC members: **H.N. Kunzru** and **K.M. Panikkar**.
**Justice K.N. Wanchoo** was appointed on **7 Feb 1953**; report dated **25 Mar 1953**.
⚠ **Dar** = appointed by the **Constituent Assembly**; **JVP** = by **Congress** at **Jaipur**.

n79c6ee320ea.s: The States Reorganisation Commission announced on 22 December 1953 was headed by:
n79c6ee320ea.x: The SRC was headed by Fazal Ali, with H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar as members.
xa: The SRC led to the **States Reorganisation Act 1956**.
Its path was opened by the formation of **Andhra State** on **1 Oct 1953**.
⚠ **N. Sanjiva Reddy was not a member** of the JVP Committee either (APPSC 2021).

nap-history-1-13.s: Who was the first Telugu President of the Indian National Congress?
nap-history-1-13.x: P. Anandacharyulu was the first Telugu President of the Indian National Congress, presiding over the 1891 Nagpur session. Nyapati Subba Rao and Govinda Rao Nanal are linked with Andhra and Hyderabad bodies, not the INC presidency.
n: P. Anandacharyulu was the first Telugu President of the Indian National Congress. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
P. Anandacharyulu became the first Telugu President of the Indian National Congress in 1891 at Nagpur. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
xs: **P. Anandacharyulu** was the **first Telugu President** of the INC — so option **(3)** is correct.
He presided the **7th session**, **Nagpur, 1891**; earlier he was Secretary of the **Madras Mahajana Sabha** (**1884**).
**Nyapati Subba Rao** was the first president of the **Andhra Congress Circle**; **Govinda Rao Nanal** of the **Hyderabad State Congress**.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** a key named **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** "first Telugu person" — he presided the **Jaipur session, 1948**.
**N. Sanjiva Reddy** was INC president **1960-62**.
Andhra delegates at the **1885 Bombay** session included **P. Anandacharlu** and **Nyapati Subba Rao**.

nap-history-1-14.s: Who was the first Muslim leader from Hyderabad to join the Indian National Congress?
nap-history-1-14.x: Mulla Abdul Qayyum was the first Muslim leader from Hyderabad to join the Indian National Congress. B. Ramakrishna Rao was Hyderabad's first elected Chief Minister, and Anandacharyulu was the first Telugu INC President.
n: Mulla Abdul Qayyum was the first Muslim leader from Hyderabad to join the Indian National Congress. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
xs: **Mulla Abdul Qayyum** was the **first Muslim leader** from Hyderabad to **join the INC** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**P. Anandacharyulu** was the first Telugu **INC President** (**1891**, **Nagpur**).
**B. Ramakrishna Rao** was the **first elected Chief Minister** of Hyderabad State.
xa: **Govinda Rao Nanal** was the **first President** of the **Hyderabad State Congress**.
In **1954** **B. Ramakrishna Rao** shifted to favour the merger.
**Andhra State** and **Hyderabad State** merged in **1956**.

nap-history-33-5.s: N.T. Rama Rao founded the Telugu Desam Party on:
nap-history-33-5.x: NTR founded the TDP on 29 March 1982, not 29 May.
n: Christian Association of Bellary published the first Telugu journal. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
The Telugu Desam Party was founded by NTR on May 29, 1982. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
Pingali Venkayya was inspired for the national flag in 1906. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
The inspiration for the national flag associated with Pingali Venkayya occurred at an AICC session. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
Dadabhai Naoroji was associated with the 1906 AICC session. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 44-45]
xa: The **first widow remarriage** in Andhra was on **11 December 1881** at **Rajahmundry**.
**Gandhi visited Hyderabad** on **9 March 1934**.
The **Sribagh Agreement** was signed on **16 November 1937**.

n96491ee1ced.s: Andhra Patrika was originally founded in:
n96491ee1ced.x: Andhra Patrika was founded in Bombay, moved to Madras and became a daily in 1914.
xa: Founder: **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** ("**Desoddharaka**").
Its reply to Tamil opposition: "Tamils separating from Telugus will not harm **national unity**".
The **Sri Bagh Pact** (**1937**) was signed at Kasinathuni's Madras house.

ncca1b9ba599.s: Manda Suryanarayana, who presided over the Vizag district meeting of June 1913, was the municipal chairman of:
ncca1b9ba599.x: Manda Suryanarayana was Vizianagaram's municipal chairman; Guntur's first was Vinjamuri Bhavanacharyulu. The meeting started the weekly Andhra Advocate.
xa: Manda Suryanarayana moved the province resolution at **Vijayawada (1914)**.
He was **Andhra Mahasabha president 1941-46** (PYQ).
His **2 Sept 1921** university resolution was accepted.

n10c8bc94a4f.s: Ramadasu Pantulu moved an Andhra state proposal in the Council of State in:
n10c8bc94a4f.x: Ramadasu Pantulu moved the Andhra state proposal in 1926; in 1925 he had amended Dr. Ramarao's resolution to seek linguistic states.
xa: **1927**: **Vemavaram Ramadasu** moved linguistic states in the **State Council**.
**Pillalamarry Anjaneyulu** moved it in the **Madras Council**.
All were in the **Council of State**, the Central upper house.

n17b0145f38f.s: Andhra was dropped from the Draft Constitution published on:
n17b0145f38f.x: Andhra, first in the Draft's First Schedule, was omitted from the Draft of 21 February 1948 after Tamil and Kannada objections.
xa: The **Constituent Assembly** kept only the pre-Independence provinces.
The Dar Commission came on **17 June 1948**.
The Constitution of **26 January 1950** had **no Andhra state**.

nc0766e993be.s: Apart from Jawaharlal Nehru and Vallabhbhai Patel, the third member of the JVP Committee was:
nc0766e993be.x: The three members were Nehru, Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya; N. Sanjiva Reddy was not a member.
xa: Called the "**Three Ministers Committee**".
Set up by **Congress** at **Jaipur**, **December 1948**.
⚠ The **Dar Commission** members were **S.K. Dhar**, **Panna Lal**, **Jagat Narayan Lal**.

nf2cff202e9e.s: Swami Sitaram, who undertook a fast for a separate Andhra State in 1951, was also known as
nf2cff202e9e.x: Swami Sitaram was the popular name of Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri, a Gandhian associated with the Andhra movement.
nf2cff202e9e.tq: Use the direct identity link between a popular name and the full name.
xs: **Swami Sitaram** was **Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri (Sastry)**, a Gandhian — option **(3)** is correct.
**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** founded **Andhra Patrika**; **Konda Venkatappayya** co-founded **Krishna Patrika**; **Jonnavittula Gurunatham** wrote the **1911** series in **The Hindu**.
xa: His fast: **15 August to 20 September 1951**, **35 days**.
He led the **palm-tree cutting** campaign in the **Civil Disobedience Movement**.
⚠ **Swami Sitaram** = **35 days** (1951, ended by **Vinoba Bhave**); **Potti Sriramulu** = **58 days** (1952, died).

nac2b658fff3.s: Swami Sitaram's fast for a separate Andhra State in 1951 lasted:
nac2b658fff3.x: Swami Sitaram fasted for 35 days in 1951 for a separate Andhra State.
xa: Demand: Andhra state by **2 October 1951**.
Madras city's status to be settled within **three** years.
It ended on **Acharya Vinoba Bhave's** appeal — empty assurances, no gain.

ndcce7aeac3f.s: Which one of the following was NOT a demand associated with Swami Sitaram's 1951 fast?
o: Settlement of Madras city's status within three years
Immediate merger of Telangana with Andhra State
Formation of Andhra State by 2 October 1951
Neither Andhra nor Tamil interests controlling Madras city during the interim
ndcce7aeac3f.x: The demands concerned the formation of Andhra State, settlement of Madras city's status, and an interim arrangement over the city. Merger of Telangana was not one of the stated demands.
ndcce7aeac3f.tq: Find the option outside the specific demand set.
xs: **Immediate merger of Telangana** was **not** one of Swami Sitaram's demands — option **(2)** is the answer.
His demands: Andhra State by **2 October 1951**; Madras city's status settled within **three years**; **neither side** to control Madras meanwhile.
xa: Fast: **35 days**, **15 August to 20 September 1951**.
Ended on the appeal of **Vinoba Bhave**.
**Nehru criticised** the fast.

n447ce84f2c4.s: In the April 1951 APCC election, Sanjiva Reddy defeated N.G. Ranga by a margin of:
n447ce84f2c4.x: Sanjiva Reddy won by five votes, after which Prakasam and Ranga formed the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party.
xa: The split (**Prakasam and Ranga vs Pattabhi and Sanjiva Reddy**) **delayed the state**.
Swami Sitaram fasted **15 August to 20 September 1951**.
**Leadership splits** — **Circars vs Rayalaseema**, **Prakasam vs Pattabhi** — repeatedly slowed the movement.

n465b085bb35.s: On whose appeal did Swami Sitaram end his fast in 1951?
n465b085bb35.x: Swami Sitaram ended his fast on the appeal of Vinoba Bhave.
n465b085bb35.tq: Test who intervened in ending the fast.
xs: Swami Sitaram ended his fast on the appeal of **Acharya Vinoba Bhave** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Nehru** criticised the fast rather than ending it.
xa: The fast gave only **empty assurances**, no gain.
It lasted **35 days** (**1951**).
⚠ **Potti Sriramulu** did not end his fast — he died on the **58th day** (**15 December 1952**).

n52ff0a85897.s: Potti Sriramulu was born on 16 March 1901 in a family belonging to which community?
n52ff0a85897.x: Potti Sriramulu was born on 16 March 1901 in an Arya Vysya family. His ancestral village was Gajula Dinne in Nellore.
n52ff0a85897.tq: Test a precise biographical detail carried in the heading and introductory account.
xs: Potti Sriramulu was born in an **Arya Vysya** family on **16 March 1901** — option **(4)** is correct.
Born in **Madras**; ancestral village **Gajula Dinne**, Nellore district.
xa: Some notes give **15 March**; older notes **15 March 1901 or 1911**.
125th birth anniversary: **16 March 2026** — **58-foot** "**Statue of Sacrifice**", **Sakhamuru Park, Amaravati**.
Titles: **Amarajeevi**; "**Andhra Martyra Martanda**".

n6c1817d285a.s: The earlier fasts of Potti Sriramulu were primarily undertaken for which cause?
o: Demand for prohibition in Madras Presidency
n6c1817d285a.x: His earlier fasts were undertaken for Harijan causes, including temple entry and Harijan welfare. The 1952 fast was his only fast for statehood.
n6c1817d285a.tq: Separate the earlier Harijan fasts from the later statehood fast.
xs: His earlier fasts were for **Harijan causes** — including **temple entry** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **1952** fast was his **only fast for statehood**, so (3) is wrong for the earlier ones.
xa: **1946**: Nellore **Venugopala Swamy temple** — Harijan entry.
**1948**: **29 days**, **Wardha** — Harijan Day.
**1949**: **28 days** (January) — **Gandhi Smarak Din**.

nf4cd85af249.s: Potti Sriramulu's 29-day fast at Wardha in 1948 was associated with which combination?
o: Harijan Day and a grant of one crore rupees
Temple entry and the formation of Andhra State
Gandhi Smarak Din and the creation of Rayalaseema
Prohibition and the establishment of Andhra University
nf4cd85af249.x: The Wardha fast in 1948 was associated with the observance of Harijan Day and a grant of one crore rupees. Madras also marked Harijan Welfare Day on the thirtieth of every month.
nf4cd85af249.tq: Match the duration and place of a fast with its distinctive outcome.
xs: The **1948 Wardha** fast of **29 days** led Nehru to declare a **Harijan Day** and **₹1 crore** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Gandhi Smarak Din** came from the **1949** fast; **temple entry** from **1946**.
xa: **Madras** marks **Harijan Welfare Day** on the **30th** of every month (APP).
**1946**: **19 days** — temple-entry law for Harijans.

n280a53f077f.s: On 19 December 1952, Jawaharlal Nehru announced that Andhra State would be formed from:
o: Telangana and the coastal districts of Madras Presidency
The undisputed Telugu-speaking areas, excluding Madras city
All Telugu-speaking areas including Madras city
The entire Madras Presidency excluding Rayalaseema
n280a53f077f.x: Nehru announced that Andhra State would be formed from the undisputed Telugu areas, while Madras city would be excluded.
n280a53f077f.tq: Separate the accepted Telugu areas from the specifically excluded Madras city.
xs: On **19 December 1952**, Nehru told Parliament Andhra would be formed from the **undisputed Telugu areas, excluding Madras city** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Telangana** joined only in **1956** (Andhra Pradesh); Madras city was never included.
xa: ⚠ **19 December** is often misgiven as Sriramulu's death — he died on **15 December 1952**.
**25 March 1953**: Nehru — "**No question**" of Madras as the capital.
Andhra State formed **1 October 1953**.

n0cfcb8a904e.s: Potti Sriramulu began his final fast at the house of:
n0cfcb8a904e.x: Although the fast initially began at the St. George's Fort gate, Bulusu Sambamurthy moved Sriramulu to his house in Mylapore, which is generally given as the venue.
n0cfcb8a904e.tq: Distinguish the initial location from the recognised venue of the fast.
xs: Sriramulu fasted at **Bulusu Sambamurthy's** house in **Mylapore** — option **(3)** is correct.
He first began at the **St. George's Fort gate** (CDX); Sambamurthy then moved him to his house — the venue in most notes.
xa: Start: **19 October 1952**, Madras.
Plan disclosed to friend **V. Lakshminarayana** in **September 1952**.
**Bulusu Sambamurthy** was a **coastal signatory** of the **Sri Bagh Pact**.

na3b574c15a6.s: After Potti Sriramulu's death, riots and police firing broke out. How many persons died in the firing?
na3b574c15a6.x: Sriramulu's death was followed by riots and police firing in which seven people died; Nehru then announced Andhra State in Parliament on 19 December 1952.
xa: **Hartals, demonstrations, riots**; railway stations, post offices attacked.
MLA **Tenneti Viswanatham** and MLC **P. Sitaramayya** resigned.
Announcement in Parliament: **19 December 1952**.

n664e23e899f.s: Which one of the following was NOT one of the three conditions associated with Potti Sriramulu's demand?
o: Madras city should become a Chief Commissioner's State by agreement
The Andhra State should include the whole of the Madras Presidency
The Centre should announce the formation of Andhra State immediately
n664e23e899f.x: The three conditions concerned immediate announcement, unity among Andhra leaders and making Madras a Chief Commissioner's State by agreement. Inclusion of the entire Madras Presidency was not a condition.
n664e23e899f.tq: Find the option that goes beyond the precise three-condition formulation.
xs: Inclusion of **the whole Madras Presidency** was **not** a condition — option **(2)** is the answer.
The **three conditions**: Centre to **announce Andhra State at once**; Andhra leaders to **stay united**; **Madras city** → **Chief Commissioner's (C-class) state** by agreement.
xa: The C-class arrangement was also called a "**free state**".
On the **50th day**, Nehru offered Andhra **without Madras** if all parties agreed.
He died on the **58th day**.

na5b6166da9c.s: Potti Sriramulu, honoured with the title 'Amarajeevi', died on the 58th day of his fast. The date of his death was:
na5b6166da9c.x: Sriramulu began his fast on 19 October 1952 and died on its 58th day, 15 December 1952, earning the title 'Amarajeevi'. 19 December 1952 is the date of Nehru's announcement in Parliament (a common trap), and 1 October 1953 is the formation of Andhra State.
na5b6166da9c.tq: 19 Oct start - 15 Dec death - 19 Dec announcement - 1 Oct 1953 state.
xs: **Amarajeevi** Potti Sriramulu died on **15 December 1952**, the **58th day** — option **(2)** is correct.
**19 October 1952** = fast began; **19 December 1952** = **Nehru's announcement** (common trap); **1 October 1953** = Andhra State formed.
xa: Some notes say **56** days.
Exam angle: **19 Oct** start, **15 Dec** death, **19 Dec** announcement, "**58 days**".
Venue: **Bulusu Sambamurthy's** house, **Mylapore**.

nf41eb010143.s: Potti Sriramulu died during his fast for Andhra State on:
nf41eb010143.x: He began fasting on 19 October 1952 and died on 15 December 1952; Nehru announced Andhra State on 19 December 1952.
xa: Wanchoo report: **25 Mar 1953** (some notes **23 March 1953**).
Act introduced **10 Aug 1953**; President's assent **14 Sept 1953**.
Andhra State formed **1 October 1953**.

n0ccf0c8db4f.s: The Andhra State Bill received assent on:
n0ccf0c8db4f.x: Introduced on 10 August 1953, the Bill received assent on 14 September 1953, and Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953.
xa: Passage: **Madras Assembly → Lok Sabha → Rajya Sabha**.
Andhra = **first linguistic state** of independent India.
⚠ **1 Oct 1953** (Andhra State) vs **1 Nov 1956** (Andhra Pradesh).

n7cef12e893c.s: Who inaugurated Andhra State at Kurnool?
n7cef12e893c.x: Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated Andhra State at Kurnool.
n7cef12e893c.tq: Distinguish the inaugurating national leader from the constitutional authorities associated with state reorganisation.
xs: **Jawaharlal Nehru** inaugurated Andhra State at **Kurnool** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Rajendra Prasad** was President of the **Constituent Assembly**; **Rajagopalachari** was Madras CM (**1952-54**) and anti-Andhra.
xa: Formed **1 October 1953**, carved out of **Madras State**.
First CM **T. Prakasam**; Governor **C.M. Trivedi**.
Capital path: **Kurnool (1953) → Hyderabad (1956) → Amaravati**.

n66e4cc12ecc.s: Andhra State, the first state of independent India formed on a linguistic basis, came into existence on:
n66e4cc12ecc.x: Andhra State was carved out of Madras State on 1 October 1953 as the first linguistic state, with Kurnool as capital. 15 December 1952 is Potti Sriramulu's death; 26 January 1950 is when the Constitution came into force without an Andhra State; 1 November 1956 is the formation of Andhra Pradesh.
n66e4cc12ecc.tq: 1 Oct 1953 = Andhra State; 1 Nov 1956 = Andhra Pradesh.
xs: **Andhra State**, the first linguistic state, was formed on **1 October 1953** — option **(2)** is correct.
**15 December 1952** = Sriramulu's death; **26 January 1950** = Constitution, with no Andhra; **1 November 1956** = **Andhra Pradesh**.
xa: Carved out of **Madras State**; capital **Kurnool**.
It opened the way to the **SRC** (**Dec 1953**).
Firsts: CM **Prakasam**, Governor **C.M. Trivedi**, Speaker **N. Venkatramayya**.

nee17ecd71e5.s: Which of the following is a title associated with Potti Sriramulu?
nee17ecd71e5.x: Potti Sriramulu is known by the title Amarajeevi, meaning Immortal Martyr. He is also associated with the title “Andhra Martyra Martanda.”
nee17ecd71e5.tq: Test an exact honorific while using titles associated with other Andhra leaders as traps.
xs: Potti Sriramulu is known as **Amarajeevi** (Immortal Martyr) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Andhra Ratna** = **Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah**; **Desoddharaka** = **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**; **Andhra Kesari** = **Tanguturi Prakasam**.
xa: His other title: **"Andhra Martyra Martanda"**.
He got the title after dying on the **58th day** of his fast, **15 December 1952**.
⚠ **Andhra Kesari** is also the name of **Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao's** paper (**1904**).
**Deshabhakta** = Konda Venkatappayya; **Swami Sitaram** = Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri.

n4a933e2296b.s: The 58-foot 'Statue of Sacrifice' of Potti Sriramulu at Amaravati was unveiled on 16 March 2026, his:
n4a933e2296b.x: Born 16 March 1901, Sriramulu's 125th birth anniversary fell on 16 March 2026, when CM Chandrababu Naidu unveiled the statue.
xa: Memorial park of **6.80 acres**, about **₹150 crore**; **26 t** bronze + **42 t** iron.
Built by the **Amarajeevi Potti Sriramulu Memorial Trust**; phase 2 adds a **museum, auditorium** and skill centre.
The 58-foot height echoes his **58-day** fast of **1952**.

na8648655ebf.s: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 is associated with which provision?
o: Abolition of the statutory concept of a state capital
Affirmation of Amaravati’s permanent statutory position as the capital
Transfer of Andhra Pradesh’s capital to Hyderabad
Recognition of Kurnool as the permanent capital of Andhra Pradesh
na8648655ebf.x: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 affirms Amaravati’s permanent statutory position as the capital of Andhra Pradesh.
na8648655ebf.tq: Use the exact statutory effect instead of confusing historical and current capitals.
xs: The **AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026** affirms **Amaravati's** permanent statutory position as capital — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kurnool** was the temporary capital of Andhra State (**1953**) and **Hyderabad** came in **1956**.
xa: The **58-foot** "Statue of Sacrifice" of Potti Sriramulu stands at **Sakhamuru Park, Amaravati**.
Deputy CM **Pawan Kalyan**: A.P. still grapples with its capital question.
The **Central University of AP** at **Anantapur** followed the **AP Reorganisation Act 2014**.

n130e78c805e.s: The first Vice-Chancellor of Andhra University was:
n130e78c805e.x: C.R. Reddy was the first VC of Andhra University, set up under the 1925 Act passed by the Justice Party government.
xa: Seat decided **Dec 1928**: **Visakhapatnam**, by **Dr. Subbaroyan's** ministry.
Inaugurated at Waltair on **5 Sept 1930**.
⚠ APPSC 2023 trap: 1926 inauguration at **Guntur** — wrong.

n9978401203e.s: Rayalaseema's grievance at exclusion from Andhra University was answered in 1954 by the founding of:
n9978401203e.x: Sri Venkateswara University at Tirupati was founded in 1954, answering Rayalaseema's grievance after it had been excluded from Andhra University.
xa: An amendment had excluded Rayalaseema from AU; its colleges went back to **Madras University**.
The **1st Rayalaseema Mahasabha (1934)** had demanded a university at **Tirupati**.
Later Rayalaseema institutions: **Yogi Vemana University, Kadapa (2006)**; **Central University of AP, Anantapur**.

nc9a4b159e3e.s: When the Sri Bagh Pact was implemented in 1953, Kurnool became the capital and the High Court was located at:
nc9a4b159e3e.x: When the pact was put into effect in 1953, Kurnool became the capital and Guntur the seat of the High Court.
xa: Rayalaseema had the **first choice** under the pact → chose the capital.
Madras Assembly vote: **Kurnool 79** vs **Vijayawada 53**; Kurnool = **temporary** capital.
The Guntur High Court was set up on **5 July 1954**; until then the **Madras High Court** served Andhra.

nb19900e799b.s: Who among the following was an Andhra member of the Madras Partition Committee of 1949?
nb19900e799b.x: The Andhra members were T. Prakasam, Kala Venkatrao, Bezawada Gopala Reddy and Neelam Sanjiva Reddy; the others named belonged to the Tamil side.
xa: Chairman: **Kumaraswamy Raja**.
**Kala Venkatarao** drafted the "**Kurnool Circular**" (APPSC 2018).
**Prakasam** wrote a **separate report**.

nbdef91518f4.s: Potti Sriramulu sought the formation of a state comprising which of the following areas?
o: The Telugu-speaking districts along with the entire Madras city area
The Telugu-speaking districts of Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema
nbdef91518f4.x: Potti Sriramulu demanded a separate state consisting of both Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema. The question of Madras city was left for later negotiation.
nbdef91518f4.tq: Test the territorial scope directly and distinguish the core demand from the disputed city question.
xs: Sriramulu sought a state of the Telugu districts of **Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Madras city** was left to **later negotiation** (APPSC 2019).
xa: His condition on Madras: a **Chief Commissioner's (C-class) state** by agreement.
Andhra State (**1953**): **Coastal Andhra (7)** + **Rayalaseema (4)** districts.
⚠ **Swami Sitaram's** 1951 demand: Madras's status settled within **three years**.

n7154157fb5b.s: At its formation in 1953, Andhra State had how many districts?
n7154157fb5b.x: Andhra State had 11 districts: 7 in Coastal Andhra and 4 in Rayalaseema.
xa: Plus the **Bellary taluks** (some notes say "**12 districts**").
**Vizianagaram** and **Prakasam** districts did not exist yet.
Exam angle: **1 Oct 1953** and the **7 + 4** split.

nf3f330da716.s: Which one of the following was NOT included among the districts of Andhra State at the time of its formation?
nf3f330da716.x: Vizianagaram district did not exist at the time of Andhra State formation. Nellore, Kurnool and Chittoor were included.
nf3f330da716.tq: Find the later-created district among the districts belonging to the 1953 arrangement.
xs: **Vizianagaram** did not exist when Andhra State was formed — option **(4)** is the answer.
**Nellore** (Coastal), **Chittoor** and **Kurnool** (Rayalaseema) were among the **11** districts.
xa: **Prakasam** district too did not exist yet.
Coastal Andhra **7** + Rayalaseema **4**.
**Rayadurg** joined **Anantapur**; **Adoni and Alur** joined **Kurnool**.

n4e546ab4758.s: In the Madras Assembly vote on the capital of Andhra State, Kurnool defeated Vijayawada by:
n4e546ab4758.x: Kurnool won 79 to 53, helped by five non-Andhra votes; Prakasam did not vote.
xa: Kurnool was a **temporary** capital.
High Court went to **Guntur** under the **Sreebagh** balance.
**Communists** backed **Vijayawada**.

n955895352f7.s: Who became Chief Minister of Andhra State after the 1955 mid-term election?
n955895352f7.x: Prakasam (CM from 1 October 1953) fell in November 1954; after the 1955 poll Bezawada Gopala Reddy became CM.
xa: **President's rule** was imposed after Prakasam's ministry fell in **Nov 1954**.
⚠ Some notes put the fall of Prakasam's government in **1955**; the no-confidence defeat was **Nov 1954**.
Prakasam's title was **"Andhra Kesari"**; the first Deputy CM was **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** (later President of India).
Andhra State had **no Legislative Council**; its members had been elected to the Madras Assembly in **1952**.

n7a85a5893d9.s: The 1955 mid-term election in Andhra State followed the fall of the ministry headed by:
n7a85a5893d9.x: It followed the fall of Prakasam's ministry; the United Congress front (Congress, Krishikar Lok Party, PSP) contested against the Communists.
xa: After the win, **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** became CM.
**N.G. Ranga's Krishikar Lok Party** had backed **Tirupati** as capital in 1953; the **Communists** (Puchalapalli Sundarayya) backed **Vijayawada / Guntur**.
Prakasam's government lost its majority over the **liquor-prohibition** controversy.

n70c9a362a10.s: The High Court of Andhra State at Guntur was set up on:
n70c9a362a10.x: It was set up on 5 July 1954; until then the Madras High Court served Andhra State.
xa: The **Sri Bagh Pact (16 Nov 1937)** put the **Capital and High Court in separate regions**, with Rayalaseema getting first choice.
Exam pair: **"capital Kurnool, High Court Guntur"** (APPSC G2 2008 and 2025).
In the Madras Assembly vote on the capital, **Kurnool 79** beat **Vijayawada 53**; Kurnool was a **temporary** capital.

n51b8aac8a04.s: Who presented the 1955-56 budget of Andhra State?
n51b8aac8a04.x: Bezawada Gopala Reddy presented the 1955-56 budget of Andhra State (APPSC GS 2021 key); he became CM after the 1955 mid-term poll. Prakasam was the first CM, Sanjiva Reddy the Deputy CM, and Tenneti Viswanatham sat on Trivedi's advisory committee.
xs: **B. (Bezawada) Gopala Reddy** presented the **1955-56** budget of Andhra State (APPSC GS 2021 key) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**T. Prakasam** was the first CM; **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** was the Deputy CM.
**Tenneti Viswanatham** sat on Trivedi's advisory committee (with Sanjiva Reddy) and later resigned as MLA over Sriramulu's death.
xa: Gopala Reddy became CM after the **1955 mid-term poll**, won by the **United Congress front**.
Gopala Reddy was also an Andhra member of the **1949** Madras **Partition Committee**, and a coastal signatory of the **Sri Bagh Pact**.
First Governor: **C.M. Trivedi**; first Speaker: **N. Venkatramayya**.

n8f4c5b1eeff.s: Which of the following best explains why the Andhra movement was repeatedly slowed before 1953?
o: The immediate acceptance of the Andhra demand by the Central Government
Leadership and regional splits, including Circars–Rayalaseema and Prakasam–Pattabhi divisions
The unanimous opposition of all Telugu-speaking districts to a separate state
The absence of any demand for linguistic organisation within Congress
n8f4c5b1eeff.x: Factional divisions between regions and leaders, notably Circars versus Rayalaseema and Prakasam versus Pattabhi, repeatedly weakened the movement.
n8f4c5b1eeff.tq: Identify the internal political cause rather than an absolute or externally imposed explanation.
xs: Leadership and regional splits — **Circars vs Rayalaseema**, **Prakasam vs Pattabhi** — repeatedly slowed the movement — option **(2)** is correct.
The Centre was **cautious**, not accepting: **Dhar** and **JVP** both rejected language as a basis.
Congress had promised linguistic PCCs since **1920**, and Telugu districts were divided, not unanimous.
xa: Delay was blamed on Centre caution after **Partition** + Andhra factionalism.
**April 1951**: **N. Sanjiva Reddy** beat **N.G. Ranga** for APCC by **5** votes → Prakasam and Ranga left to form the **Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party**.
The university seat/jurisdiction row left lasting **Rayalaseema** resentment → the **Sri Bagh Pact**.

nap-history-1-11.s: The Andhra Pradesh Legislature became bicameral for the first time in:
nap-history-1-11.x: The Legislative Council was created in 1958, making the legislature bicameral.
n: Bezawada Gopala Reddy was the last Chief Minister of Andhra State. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
The Andhra Pradesh Legislature became bicameral for the first time in 1958. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
xa: Gopala Reddy became CM after the **1955 mid-term poll**, won by the **United Congress front** (Congress + **Krishikar Lok Party** + **Praja Socialist Party**).
**Prakasam**'s ministry fell over **liquor prohibition**; no-confidence defeat **Nov 1954**.
Gopala Reddy also presented the **1955-56** budget.

nap-history-1-15.s: Who was the first elected Chief Minister of Hyderabad State?
nap-history-1-15.x: B. Ramakrishna Rao became the first elected Chief Minister of Hyderabad State in 1952. Prakasam and Gopala Reddy headed Andhra State, and Sanjiva Reddy was the first CM of Andhra Pradesh.
nap-history-1-15.tq: Discriminate Hyderabad State from Andhra State leaders.
n: B. Ramakrishna Rao was the first elected Chief Minister of Hyderabad State. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-5]
xs: **B. Ramakrishna Rao** was the **first elected Chief Minister** of **Hyderabad State** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Tanguturi Prakasam** and **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** were the first and last CMs of **Andhra State**.
**Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** was the **first CM of Andhra Pradesh** (**1956**).
xa: **Govinda Rao Nanal** — first President of the **Hyderabad State Congress**.
**Mulla Abdul Qayyum** — first Muslim leader from Hyderabad to join the INC.
In **1954** Ramakrishna Rao shifted to favour the merger.

nap-history-19-5.s: Who was the first Chief Justice of the High Court of Andhra State at Guntur?
nap-history-19-5.x: Koka Subba Rao was the first Chief Justice of the Andhra High Court, set up at Guntur in 1954.
n: The High Court of Andhra State was located in Guntur. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
Koka Subba Rao was the first Chief Justice of the High Court of Andhra State. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
xa: ⚠ Pair: capital at **Kurnool** (Rayalaseema), High Court at **Guntur** (Coastal) — the **Sri Bagh Pact** balance.
Until then the **Madras High Court** served Andhra.
The **APPSC** was established on **1 November 1956** under **Article 315**.

n4088de8c2e0.s: The agenda of the Bapatla session of 1913 included lifting the ban on the entry of Telugus into the:
n4088de8c2e0.x: The Bapatla agenda included removal of the ban on Telugus entering the Army, an English paper and a fund for technical training abroad.
xa: Bapatla also **demanded a separate university**.
Attendance: about **800 delegates and 2,000 visitors**.
Delegates came from **Hyderabad, Warangal, Nagpur**.

n8b2a3779c2b.s: Who among the following supported B.N. Sarma's 1918 resolution?
n8b2a3779c2b.x: K.V. Rangaswami Ayyangar supported it, while Jinnah and V.S. Srinivasa Sastri opposed it.
xa: **Surendranath Banerjee**: "the time has not come".
**Tej Bahadur Sapru**: would back it **for Andhra only**.
⚠ Opponents table: **Jinnah** + **V.S. Srinivasa Sastri**, **Imperial Council, 1918**.

n9fd4cabb3dd.s: In 1937, the regional rift deepened because Rajaji's Madras cabinet had no minister from:
n9fd4cabb3dd.x: The absence of a Rayalaseema minister in Rajaji's 1937 cabinet deepened the existing regional rift.
xa: The **1937 Silver Jubilee session** demanded safeguards in **Cabinet, Irrigation and Capital**.
The **Sri Bagh Pact** (**16 Nov 1937**) followed to allay Rayalaseema fears.
**1938**: **R. Suryanarayana Rao** and **N.M. Sastry** formed a new anti-Andhra Rayalaseema Mahasabha.

n0bb57b5a90d.s: At the 1937 Silver Jubilee session, Rayalaseema leaders demanded safeguards relating to:
o: Separate army recruitment and the capital
Cabinet representation, irrigation and the capital
Cabinet representation and separate army recruitment
n0bb57b5a90d.x: The 1937 safeguards concerned Cabinet representation, irrigation and the capital; separate army recruitment was not among them.
xa: The session set up a **committee** to examine the safeguards.
Presided by **Kadapa Koti Reddy**; inaugurated by **H.M. Sitaram Reddy** (both Rayalaseema).
⚠ Rajaji's **1937** cabinet had **no Rayalaseema minister**.

n5772a7624de.s: The Sri Bagh Pact later served as a model for the:
n5772a7624de.x: The Sri Bagh Pact established a pattern of regional safeguards that was later used in the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956.
n5772a7624de.tq: Connect an earlier regional arrangement with the later agreement that followed its pattern.
xs: The **Sri Bagh Pact** set the pattern later used in the **Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Dhar (1948)**, **Wanchoo (1953)** and the **Partition Committee (1949)** were inquiry/administrative bodies, not regional pacts.
xa: Gentlemen's Agreement: **Cabinet ratio 60:40** (Andhra : Telangana).
It also created a **Telangana Regional Committee**.
Safeguards in **jobs and education**; Telangana **surplus funds** protected.

n88b4d684556.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Sri Bagh Pact?
o: Irrigation priority for Rayalaseema for ten years
Andhra University centres at Waltair and Anantapur
A cabinet ratio of 60:40 between Andhra and Telangana
n88b4d684556.x: The 60:40 cabinet ratio was a provision of the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956. The other provisions belonged to the Sri Bagh Pact.
n88b4d684556.tq: Separate provisions of two regional agreements by identifying the borrowed provision.
xs: The **60:40 cabinet ratio** (Andhra : Telangana) was the **Gentlemen's Agreement (1956)**, not Sri Bagh — option **(4)** is the answer.
Sri Bagh did provide **irrigation priority** for **10 years**, **equal district-wise** legislature seats and AU centres at **Waltair and Anantapur**.
xa: Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 — Gentlemen's Agreement ratio **60:40**.
Sri Bagh also put **Capital and High Court** in separate regions.
⚠ **Sri Bagh** = **1937**; **Gentlemen's Agreement** = **1956**.

n1f04ee553e1.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement provided for an Andhra–Telangana cabinet ratio of:
n1f04ee553e1.x: It provided a 60:40 cabinet ratio, a Telangana Regional Committee, protection of surplus funds and job/education safeguards.
xa: Purpose: safeguards for **Telangana** on merger to form **AP** (**1956**).
Exam angle: APPSC-G2 2025 — cabinet ratio **60:40**.
⚠ **Sri Bagh** = **1937**, Coastal–Rayalaseema; **Gentlemen's Agreement** = **1956**, Andhra–Telangana.

nf0b8374effa.s: As Premier of Madras in 1937, C. Rajagopalachari:
o: included Rayalaseema in his cabinet and backed Andhra separation
left Rayalaseema out of his cabinet
nf0b8374effa.x: Rajaji left Rayalaseema out of his cabinet as Premier in 1937 and later made anti-Andhra statements.
xa: He was Madras CM **1952-54**.
He opposed sharing **Madras** (later **Kamaraj** too).
The 1937 cabinet snub **deepened** the regional rift.

nce17deda7ea.s: Who founded Andhra Kesari at Rajahmundry in 1904 and wrote Andhrula Charitra?
nce17deda7ea.x: Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao did both; Andhra Patrika is associated with Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
xa: He founded the **Vijnana Chandrika Mandali** (**1906**) with **Komarraju Lakshmana Rao**.
He also founded the **Balabharati Samithi** (**Feb 1907**).
⚠ **Andhra Kesari** is also the title of **Tanguturi Prakasam**.

nc6fa40fcbe3.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was 'Andhra Ratna'; 'Deshabhakta' was Konda Venkatappayya.
xa: ⚠ **Andhra Kesari** = Tanguturi Prakasam — do not confuse with Punjab Kesari.
Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded **Andhra Patrika** (**1908**); the **Sri Bagh Pact** was signed at his Madras house.
Lala Lajpat Rai presided the **Calcutta special session (September 1920)**, which accepted non-cooperation.

n0fde3dcff40.s: The Wanchoo Committee (1953) was appointed to deal with:
o: Determining the permanent capital of India
Reorganisation of all Indian states on linguistic lines
Boundaries, finances, assets and administration of the new Andhra State
n0fde3dcff40.x: Its terms covered boundary division, financial settlement, asset distribution and administrative arrangements, not the capital of India.
xa: Wanchoo = **single member**, **Chief Justice, Rajasthan High Court**; appointed **7 Feb 1953**.
On the capital, it only suggested Andhra work temporarily from **Madras city for 3-5 years** — rejected by Nehru.
The earlier **Partition Committee** (**1949-50**, **Kumaraswamy Raja**) had first been asked to work out the asset split.

n5ad412568ed.s: The Wanchoo Committee submitted its report on:
n5ad412568ed.x: Appointed on 7 February 1953, it reported on 23 March 1953; Nehru announced the capital on 25 March 1953.
xa: ⚠ Some notes give **25 March** as the report date — that was really Nehru's announcement.
The **25 March** announcement: capital inside Andhra, temporary capital to be decided **before 1 July 1953**.
Result: **Kurnool** became the temporary capital.

na47cd95b24f.s: The decision to assign Bellary taluk to Mysore was based on the report of:
o: Kumaraswamy Raja, Chairman of the Partition Committee
M. Trivedi, Special Officer of Andhra State
Justice Mishra, Chief Justice of the Hyderabad High Court
Justice Wanchoo, Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court
na47cd95b24f.x: Bellary taluk was assigned to Mysore on the basis of Justice Mishra’s report. Justice Mishra was the Chief Justice of the Hyderabad High Court.
na47cd95b24f.tq: Use the wrong-person-for-the-deed trap by matching the report with its author and office.
xs: **Bellary taluk** went to **Mysore** on the report of **Justice Mishra**, **Chief Justice, Hyderabad High Court** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Wanchoo** (Rajasthan HC), **Kumaraswamy Raja** (Partition Committee) and **C.M. Trivedi** (Special Officer) did not decide Bellary taluk.
xa: Mishra's hearings: **1-15 May 1953**.
**Rayadurg** → Anantapur; **Adoni, Alur** → Kurnool.
The **Tungabhadra Board** was set up under the **Andhra State Act 1953**.

n724d6288ee6.s: The Wanchoo Committee recommended that the Andhra Government function temporarily, for three to five years, from:
n724d6288ee6.x: As Andhra lacked capital infrastructure, Wanchoo recommended working from Madras city for three to five years.
xa: The Centre **did not accept** this: Nehru (**25 March 1953**) ruled out Madras as capital.
⚠ **Wanchoo** = Madras for **3-5 years**; **Nehru** = capital inside Andhra → **Kurnool**.
The Andhra **PCC** had wanted **half of Madras town**.

ne58018bd425.s: Which description best reflects the financial and administrative position of the newly formed Andhra State?
o: It had no need for an asset division with residual Madras.
It possessed a developed capital and a major commercial centre.
It was administratively and economically orphaned, lacking a developed capital and commercial centre.
It had inherited the entire financial surplus of residual Madras.
ne58018bd425.x: The new state lacked both developed capital infrastructure and a commercial centre and was described as administratively and economically orphaned.
ne58018bd425.tq: Choose the precise combined description rather than an exaggerated or reversed financial claim.
xs: Without a capital or commercial centre, Andhra was "**administratively and economically orphaned**" — option **(3)** is correct.
It **did** need an asset division: assets and administration were split between **Andhra** and **residual Madras**.
xa: For lack of capital infrastructure, Wanchoo proposed **Madras city for 3-5 years**; Nehru chose a capital inside Andhra (**Kurnool**).
The **Partition Committee** (**1949-50**) first worked on the asset split.
⚠ Compare **2014**: assets split by **location**, debts by **population** → AP carried a heavy debt share.

n3f9c0099e8a.s: In 1954, the Andhra High Court was established at:
n3f9c0099e8a.x: The Andhra High Court was set up at Guntur in 1954; the Madras High Court retained jurisdiction until then.
xa: **Bellary district court** was to serve **Adoni, Alur and Rayadurg** for the time being (Nehru, **25 Mar 1953**).
Capital: **Kurnool** (temporary); High Court: **Guntur**.

ne7dd4cf1aab.s: After Bellary was divided, the Tungabhadra Board for the works shared by Andhra and Mysore was set up under the:
ne7dd4cf1aab.x: The Tungabhadra Board was established under the Andhra State Act, 1953 to manage the shared works.
xa: **Bellary taluk** and **Hospet** etc. went to **Mysore**; **Adoni, Alur, Rayadurg** to Andhra.
On **26 Jun 2026**, **C.R. Patil** opened **33 new gates** of the **Tungabhadra dam** with three CMs present.
A **high-level committee** is planned for **AP, Telangana and Karnataka** water disputes.

n80419c199c2.s: The Sreebagh Pact of 1937 promised priority for irrigation in Rayalaseema and Nellore on which rivers?
o: Krishna, Godavari and Pennar only in coastal Andhra
n80419c199c2.x: The Sreebagh Pact promised priority for irrigation in Rayalaseema and Nellore on the Tungabhadra, Krishna and Penna for ten years or as needed.
n80419c199c2.tq: Recall the exact three-river combination instead of selecting a nearby river group.
xs: The **Sreebagh Pact** (**1937**) gave **Rayalaseema** and **Nellore** irrigation priority on the **Tungabhadra, Krishna and Penna** — option **(2)** is correct.
Godavari, Vamsadhara, Bhima and Kaveri were not in the pact's clause.
xa: The priority was for **10 years** or as needed.
The **Andhra State Act 1953** set up the **Tungabhadra Board** to manage the works.
Today the Centre plans a **high-level committee** on Tungabhadra disputes among **AP, Telangana and Karnataka**.

nac3ebe04c10.s: In the 2014 bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, the allocation of employees was handled by the:
nac3ebe04c10.x: The Kamalanathan Committee dealt with employees, the Sheela Bhide Committee with Schedule IX institutions and the Section 6 committee with the capital.
xa: In **2014**, assets were split by **location** and debts by **population** → AP carried a heavy debt share.
⚠ For **1953**, the matching panels were the **Partition Committee** (**1949-50**) and the **Wanchoo Committee**.

nabf2a3da236.s: Which was the first Telugu newspaper, established in 1835 at Bellary and run by Christian missionaries?
nabf2a3da236.x: Satyadoota, established in Bellary in 1835, was the first Telugu newspaper and was run by Christian missionaries.
nabf2a3da236.tq: Recall the earliest publication through its year, place and institutional association.
xs: **Satyadoota** (**1835, Bellary**), run by **Christian missionaries**, was the first Telugu newspaper — option **(4)** is correct.
**Vrutantini** came in **1838** (Mandigala Venkataraya Sastri); **Hitavadi** in **1841** (Edmund Park).
**Vartamana Tarangini** (**1842**, Madras) was the first Telugu paper started by a Muslim (**Syed Rahamatullah**).
xa: ⚠ **Satyadoota** = first Telugu paper (Bellary); **Hitavadi** = first **printed in Andhra**.
**Andhra Prakasika** (**1885**) = first **political** journal in Telugu.
**Desabhimani** = the **only Telugu daily** in British Andhra.

n5d3325fedb5.s: Which Telugu newspaper was the first to be printed in Andhra?
n5d3325fedb5.x: Hitavadi, associated with Edmund Park and dated 1841, was the first Telugu newspaper printed in Andhra.
n5d3325fedb5.tq: Distinguish the first Telugu newspaper from the first one printed in Andhra.
xs: **Hitavadi** (**1841**, **Edmund Park**) was the first Telugu newspaper **printed in Andhra** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Satyadoota** (**1835**) was the first Telugu paper overall, but at **Bellary**.
**Vartamana Tarangini** (**1842**) and **Tattvabodhini** (**1864**) were both from **Madras**.
xa: ⚠ **Satyadoota** = first Telugu paper; **Hitavadi** = first printed in Andhra.
**Vrutantini** (**1838**) — Mandigala Venkataraya Sastri.

n73cdeceb878.s: Vartamana Tarangini, the first Telugu paper started by a Muslim, was begun at Madras in 1842 by:
n73cdeceb878.x: Syed Rahamatullah began the weekly at Madras on 8 June 1842; after 1843 it passed to Puvvada Seshagiri Rao.
xa: It was a **weekly**.
Earlier papers: **Satyadoota** (**1835**), **Vrutantini** (**1838**), **Hitavadi** (**1841**).
**Tattvabodhini** (**1864**, Madras) came from the **Madras Veda Samaj**.

nf959df1545b.s: The first political journal in Telugu (1885) was:
nf959df1545b.x: Andhra Prakasika (1885) was the first Telugu political journal; Satyadoota (1835) was the first Telugu newspaper.
xa: Andhra Prakasika's editor: **A.P. Parthasarathy Naidu**.
Desabhimani's founder: **Devaguptam Seshachalapati Rao**; it began as **Krishnavrittantini**.
**Hitavadi** (**1841**) = first Telugu paper printed in Andhra.

n456840ff696.s: Tattvabodhini, which supported widow remarriage, was published at Madras in 1864 by the:
n456840ff696.x: Tattvabodhini was published by the Madras Veda Samaj in 1864 and supported widow remarriage.
xa: **Veeresalingam's** journals included **Vivekavardhani (1874)** and **Sati Hitabodhini (1883)**.
Women's-cause papers: **Hindu Sundari** (**1902**) and **Sri Savitri** (**1904**).

n8e561ccbd4e.s: Andhra Patrika was initially published from which place and in which year?
n8e561ccbd4e.x: Andhra Patrika was started at Bombay on 9 September 1908 by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
n8e561ccbd4e.tq: Separate the original publication place and year from the later shift and change to a daily.
xs: **Andhra Patrika** began at **Bombay** on **9 Sept 1908** — option **(3)** is correct.
It moved to **Madras** later, and became a **daily in 1914** — so options 1 and 4 mix up the facts.
**Vijayawada, 1907** is Gadicherla's **Swarajya**.
xa: Founder: **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**; it **promoted Gandhian ideas**.
He also ran the literary monthly **Bharati** (**1924**).
APPSC GS 2025 pair: **Andhra Patrika – Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao**.

nfefaf0a7913.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao started the Telugu paper Swarajya in 1907 at:
nfefaf0a7913.x: Gadicherla's Swarajya began at Vijayawada in 1907; Prakasam's Swarajya was a separate English daily from Madras.
xa: Gadicherla's Swarajya was **militant nationalist**; he was jailed for editorials such as **"Veerabali"**.
APPSC GS 2025 pair: **Swarajya – Gadicherla**.

n1bc64dcb928.s: Krishna Patrika was founded at Machilipatnam on 1 February 1902 by which pair?
o: Konda Venkatappaiah and Dasu Narayana Rao
Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham and C.Y. Chintamani
Mutnuri Krishna Rao and Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao and Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao
n1bc64dcb928.x: Krishna Patrika was founded on 1 February 1902 by Konda Venkatappaiah and Dasu Narayana Rao at Machilipatnam.
n1bc64dcb928.tq: Combine the date with the founder pair rather than relying on the later editor’s name.
xs: **Konda Venkatappaiah and Dasu Narayana Rao** founded **Krishna Patrika** (**1 Feb 1902**, Machilipatnam) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Mutnuri Krishna Rao** was its later, most famous editor; **Gadicherla** founded **Swarajya**.
**Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham** ran **Manorama** and **Desamata**; **Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao** ran **Andhra Kesari**.
xa: APPSC GS 2025 pair: **Krishna Patrika – Konda Venkatappayya**.
**30 Nov 1912**: Krishna Patrika wrote that strengthening the nation begins with the Andhra movement.

nbadac1073fd.s: Who is regarded as the second and most famous editor of Krishna Patrika, largely responsible for its success?
nbadac1073fd.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao was Krishna Patrika's second and most famous editor and was largely responsible for its success (APPSC GS 2024). Konda Venkatappayya and Dasu Narayana Rao founded it in 1902; Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded Andhra Patrika.
nbadac1073fd.tq: Founders of Krishna Patrika = Konda + Dasu; famous editor = Mutnuri.
xs: **Mutnuri Krishna Rao** was Krishna Patrika's **second and most famous editor**, "largely responsible for its success" — option **(2)** (APPSC GS 2024).
**Konda Venkatappayya** and **Dasu Narayana Rao** were its **founders** (**1902**).
**Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** founded **Andhra Patrika** (**1908**).
xa: Krishna Patrika's office was a meeting point for freedom fighters.
It backed the **Vandemataram / Swadeshi** movement.
Its **11 Apr 1914** editorial and **19 Jul 1913** iceberg cartoon backed the Andhra movement.

n8eb04974d3f.s: Which of the following groups consisted entirely of publications that supported the movement for a separate Andhra?
o: Andhra Patrika, Krishna Patrika, Desabhimani, Desamata and Darbar
The Hindu, Viswamitra, Swadesamitran and Desamata
Krishna Patrika, The Hindu, Modern Review and Viswamitra
Desabhimani, Zamin Ryot, The Hindu and Hindusthan Review
n8eb04974d3f.x: Andhra Patrika, Krishna Patrika, Desabhimani, Desamata and Darbar were listed as supporters of the separate Andhra movement.
n8eb04974d3f.tq: Screen each group for a known opposing paper or publication not listed as a supporter.
xs: **Andhra Patrika, Krishna Patrika, Desabhimani, Desamata and Darbar** all supported a separate Andhra — option **(1)** is correct.
The **"Viswamitra"** letter in The Hindu (**29 Aug 1912**) **opposed** the demand, so options 2 and 3 fail.
**Zamin Ryot** is not among the listed supporters.
xa: Outside support: **The Modern Review**, **Hindusthan Review**, **London Review of Reviews**.
**Janmabhumi** (**25 Aug 1920**): the Andhra movement strengthens national unity.

n09fcc5da3fc.s: Which Telugu newspaper is associated with the Home Rule movement in Andhra?
n09fcc5da3fc.x: Andhra Mata was the paper of the Home Rule movement (APPSC G2 2017 key). Zamin Ryot wrote on peasant issues, Navasakthi was the first fully socialist Telugu journal, and Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal after independence.
xs: **Andhra Mata** was the **Home Rule** paper (APPSC G2 2017 key) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Zamin Ryot** = peasant issues; **Navasakthi** = socialist; **Jaya Bharat** = first Telugu journal after independence.
xa: **Vandemataram / Swadeshi** papers: Krishna Patrika, Swarajya, Desamata, Andhra Kesari, Navayuga.
**Prajasakthi** = first communist Telugu journal.

n17c2d9dc3c2.s: The article 'Are Telugu people backward?' reported the ratio of non-Andhras to Andhras in the civil services as:
n17c2d9dc3c2.x: The article reported 56 non-Andhras to 8 Andhras in the civil services, and 19 non-Andhras to no Andhras in the judiciary.
xa: It appeared in **The Hindu** on **15 Apr 1911**, by **Jonnavittula Gurunatham**.
He wrote **6** articles in **1911**; Telugu papers demanded a separate state from **1911**.
Opposing view: the **"Viswamitra"** letter in The Hindu (**29 Aug 1912**) asked where Andhra would find officers.

n3b4c83474ae.s: Which newspaper stated on 30 November 1912 that strengthening the nation begins with the Andhra movement?
n3b4c83474ae.x: Krishna Patrika made this statement on 30 November 1912 in support of the Andhra movement.
n3b4c83474ae.tq: Link a dated editorial statement to the correct newspaper.
xs: **Krishna Patrika** wrote on **30 Nov 1912** that strengthening the nation begins with the Andhra movement — option **(3)** is correct.
**Janmabhumi's** similar article (national unity) came on **25 Aug 1920**.
xa: Krishna Patrika's **19 Jul 1913** cartoon showed **Rayalaseema** as an **iceberg** blocking the ship.
Its **11 Apr 1914** editorial also backed the movement.
**The Hindu** ran both Gurunatham's articles and the opposing **"Viswamitra"** letter.

n57e164342e9.s: Who was the editor associated with Bharati, the literary monthly started in 1924?
n57e164342e9.x: Bharati, a literary monthly started in 1924, was associated with Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
n57e164342e9.tq: Match a journal with its editor while separating literary journals from political newspapers.
xs: **Bharati** (**1924**), a literary monthly, was run by **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Suravaram Pratapa Reddy** ran **Golconda Patrika**; **Jayanti Ramayya** the **Andhra Sahitya Parishad Patrika**; **Kokkonda Venkataratnam** **Andhra Bhasa Sanjivani**.
xa: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao also founded **Andhra Patrika** (**9 Sept 1908**, Bombay).
**Manorama** (**1906**) and **Desamata** (**1910**) — Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham.

ncd3715a3dd6.s: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878, popularly called the 'Gagging Act', was repealed in 1882 by:
ncd3715a3dd6.x: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was repealed by Lord Ripon in 1882.
xa: This was the background to the growth of Telugu nationalist papers.
Gadicherla was jailed with a heavy sentence for **Swarajya** editorials such as **"Veerabali"**.

n3b47fdd3301.s: The Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu consisted of Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, Ayyanki and:
n3b47fdd3301.x: The Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu included Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, Ayyanki and Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.
n3b47fdd3301.tq: Complete the named triad by identifying the missing member from the same movement.
xs: The **Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu** = Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, **Ayyanki** and **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Gante Laxmanna** co-founded the **Bala Bharati Samithi**; **Dasu Narayana Rao** and **Konda Venkatappayya** are not in the trio.
xa: **Gadicherla** founded the **Edward Corporation Library**, **Nandyal**, with Kaderbad Narasinga Rao.
Kasinathuni gave free papers and books to village libraries set up by **10 youths**.

n43db382e509.s: The newspaper Zamin Ryot was edited by:
n43db382e509.x: Venkatarama Naidu edited Zamin Ryot; Mutnuri edited Krishna Patrika, Nageswara Rao Bharati, and Chilakamarti Desamata and Manorama.
xa: Kasinathuni also founded **Andhra Patrika** (**1908**).
**Gadicherla** edited **Swarajya** (**1907**) and also Navayugam, Matru Seva, Panchayati Rajyam.

nea7efb03dc2.s: The newspaper 'Swarajya' (1907) of the Andhra movement was edited by:
nea7efb03dc2.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao edited Swarajya (1907). Nageswara Rao edited Andhra Patrika and Bharati, Venkatarama Naidu edited Zamin Ryot, and Chilakamarti edited Desamata and Manorama.
nea7efb03dc2.tq: Swarajya 1907 = Gadicherla, the Vande Mataram year paper.
xs: **Swarajya** (**1907**) was edited by **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kasinathuni** = Andhra Patrika, Bharati; **Venkatarama Naidu** = Zamin Ryot; **Chilakamarti** = Desamata, Manorama.
xa: Gadicherla was arrested and heavily sentenced for Swarajya editorials such as **"Veerabali"**.
His other papers: **Navayugam**, **Andhra Patrika**, **Matru Seva**, **Panchayati Rajyam**.
He founded the **Edward Corporation Library**, Nandyal.

n9e8936a388b.s: Mutnuri Krishna Rao transformed which paper into a political weekly and a hub of freedom fighters?
n9e8936a388b.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao made Krishna Patrika a political weekly and a centre of political awakening.
xa: In **1907**, Mutnuri called extremist leaders to visit Andhra.
**Bipin Chandra Pal** toured Andhra in **April 1907** — Kakinada (**17** Apr) and **five** lectures at Rajahmundry (**19-24** Apr).
Editors made journalism a tool of political awakening that also publicised the **library movement**.

n03f572dcedf.s: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao (1867-1947) was known by the title:
n03f572dcedf.x: Nageswara Rao was titled 'Desoddharaka'; he used his Amrutanjan wealth for public work in the spirit of trusteeship.
xa: Other titles: **"Udattamati"** (noble-minded) and **"Library Protector"**.
With Ayyanki and Gadicherla he made up the **Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu**.
Film **Viswadata** marks his **160th birth anniversary**.

n1478567e826.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao founded the Edward Corporation Library (now the Victoria Reading Room) at:
n1478567e826.x: He founded it at Nandyal with Kaderbad Narasinga Rao, not at Kurnool.
xa: The Nandyal library is now the **Victoria Reading Room**.
Gadicherla's **Swarajya** dates from **1907**.
⚠ The **G2 2011 key** credits Gadicherla with organising **Bipin Chandra Pal's** tour.

nd92bc3c9ed5.s: Which extremist leader toured Andhra in April 1907, lecturing at Kakinada and delivering five lectures at Rajahmundry?
nd92bc3c9ed5.x: Bipin Chandra Pal toured Andhra in April 1907 (Kakinada on 17 April, Rajahmundry 19-24 April) after Andhra leaders invited extremist leaders. Tilak, Lajpat Rai and Aurobindo did not make this tour. Some sources credit Mutnuri Krishna Rao with organising it; the APPSC G2 2011 key credits Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.
nd92bc3c9ed5.tq: 1907 Andhra tour = Bipin Chandra Pal; organiser per G2 2011 key = Gadicherla.
xs: **Bipin Chandra Pal** toured Andhra in **April 1907** — option **(4)** is correct.
He spoke at **Kakinada** (**17** Apr) and gave **five** lectures at **Rajahmundry** (**19-24** Apr), at **Mutnuri's** invitation.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes say Mutnuri organised the tour; the **G2 2011 key** credits **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao**.
The **1907 Rajahmundry College** incident got Gadicherla blacklisted from government jobs.
**Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao** co-founded the **Bala Bharati Samithi**, Rajahmundry, **Feb 1907**.

n5976768a11c.s: Sreebagh, the Madras house where the Sreebagh Pact was signed in 1937, belonged to:

Gadicherla's papers: **Swarajya (1907)**, **Navayugam**, Andhra Patrika, **Matru Seva**, **Panchayati Rajyam**.
xa: He was imprisoned for Swarajya editorials such as **"Veerabali"**.
He renamed the Ceded Districts **"Rayalaseema"** in **1928**.

n9d966b5e1be.x: Sarvottama Bhavan was named in honour of Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.
n9d966b5e1be.tq: Identify the person commemorated by a memorial building.
