The building was bought via **Komma Sitaramayya's** gift, through the **Andhra Granthalaya Dharma Samstha (1946)**; opened **1949**.
xa: Gadicherla was **president of the library association** in **1946**.
⚠ **1928** = "Rayalaseema" name; **1946** = library president; **1949** = Sarvottama Bhavan opened.
Gadicherla lived **1883-1960**.

n39ed5b93a16.s: Who renamed the Dattamandalam (Ceded Districts) as "Rayalaseema" in 1928?
n39ed5b93a16.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao renamed the Ceded Districts "Rayalaseema" in 1928 (APPSC G2 2011, 2012); he also signed the Sreebagh Pact for Rayalaseema. Nageswara Rao, Ayyanki and Paturi were library leaders not credited with the renaming.
xs: **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** renamed the **Dattamandalam (Ceded Districts) "Rayalaseema"** in **1928** — option **(2)** (APPSC G2 2011, 2012).
**Kasinathuni**, **Ayyanki** and **Paturi** were library leaders not credited with the renaming.
xa: Gadicherla signed the **Sreebagh Pact** for Rayalaseema.
He linked the movement to the **Home Rule League**.

nbd682dfdfee.s: Who started the Bala Saraswati Bhandaramu library as a schoolboy?
nbd682dfdfee.x: Paturi Nagabhushanam started the Bala Saraswati Bhandaramu library in his village while he was still a schoolboy.
nbd682dfdfee.tq: Directly identify the person associated with a distinctive initiative.
xs: **Paturi Nagabhushanam** started **Bala Saraswati Bhandaramu** as a schoolboy — option **(2)** is correct.
It later served **40 villages**, with branches at **Pedavadlapudi** and **Duggirala**.
xa: As Secretary of the **Guntur Library Association** he set up libraries in about **160 villages**, new buildings for **28**.
Title: **Andhra Desa Granthalayodyama Roopasilpi**.

nfad89838cf8.s: A boat library service operated on passenger boats on the Bank Canal for which period?
nfad89838cf8.x: Paturi Nagabhushanam operated the boat library service on passenger boats on the Bank Canal for seven years, from 1935 to 1942.
nfad89838cf8.tq: Match the distinctive activity with its exact time span.
xs: Paturi's **boat library** ran on passenger boats on the **Bank Canal** for **7** years, **1935-42** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is in the APPSC GS 2019 key ("boat library service").
xa: He also made a **Buckingham Canal** tour for the **Pedapalem Sevakrama Vani Mandiram**.
The **library pilgrimage** was **Ayyanki's** idea.

n4eea3902ecb.s: Paturi Nagabhushanam was a member of the committee that drafted which legislation?
n4eea3902ecb.x: Paturi Nagabhushanam was a member of the committee that drafted the AP Public Libraries Act.
n4eea3902ecb.tq: Identify the legislation from the person connected with its drafting.
xs: Paturi was on the committee that drafted the **AP Public Libraries Act** — option **(4)** is correct.
The **Sreebagh Pact** was signed by Gadicherla (for Rayalaseema), not drafted by Paturi.
xa: Paturi got **Kala Prapoorna** from **Andhra University** in **1975**.
Karunasri called him **"University of Humanity"** and **"Walking Library"**.

o: Nehru, Rajendra Prasad and B. R. Ambedkar
Patel, Fazl Ali and K. M. Panikkar
Pattabhi Sitaramayya, P. S. Kumaraswamy Raja and Prakasam
ne2250c58664.x: The JVP Committee comprised Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
ne2250c58664.tq: Start from the sure membership pair and eliminate substituted personalities.
xs: The **JVP Committee** = **Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Fazl Ali** and **K.M. Panikkar** were on the **SRC** (**Dec 1953**), not JVP.
xa: JVP (**Dec 1948-1949**) rejected language as the basis and advised **postponement**.
⚠ **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** = JVP, **not** SRC.
Before JVP: **S.K. Dhar Commission** (June-Dec **1948**) — administrative convenience over language.

n01c4b1c5660.s: The JVP Committee advised that the demand for linguistic states should be
o: referred only to the Supreme Court
n01c4b1c5660.x: The JVP Committee rejected language as the immediate basis of reorganisation and advised postponement.
n01c4b1c5660.tq: Test the recommendation rather than the composition of the committee.
xs: JVP advised that linguistic states be **postponed** — option **(3)** is correct.
It **rejected language** as the basis for reorganisation for the time being.
xa: Members: **Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya**.
It followed the **S.K. Dhar Commission** (**1948**), which preferred **administrative convenience**.
**Wanchoo** (**1953**) then reported on the financial and administrative issues of Andhra's separation.

n9122a5e5fe8.s: Which of the following demands was NOT accepted by the States Reorganisation Commission?
o: Separate Hyderabad State for the Telugu districts
n9122a5e5fe8.x: The Punjabi Suba demand was not accepted. The Commission did recommend a separate Vidarbha, bilingual Bombay and a separate Hyderabad State for the Telugu districts.
n9122a5e5fe8.tq: Use the recommendation list to identify the rejected demand rather than a transferred territory.
xs: The **Punjabi Suba** demand was **not accepted** — option **(3)** is the answer.
The SRC did recommend a **bilingual Bombay**, a separate **Vidarbha** and a separate **Hyderabad State** for the Telugu districts.
xa: SRC total: **16 states and 3 Union Territories**.

n3dab4c3bbec.s: Tenneti Viswanatham criticised the States Reorganisation Commission's report for being
o: opposed to the use of Hyderabad as a capital
favourable only to a separate Telangana
n3dab4c3bbec.x: Tenneti Viswanatham described the report as self-contradictory.
n3dab4c3bbec.tq: Directly identify the criticism associated with a particular political leader.
xs: **Tenneti Viswanatham** called the SRC report **self-contradictory** — option **(3)** is correct.
It was the **Special-Telangana advocates**, not he, who welcomed the report; **T. Prakasam** dissented over **Madras city**.
xa: **Special-Telangana advocates** welcomed the report.
CM **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** moved the Andhra Assembly resolution on **Telangana safeguards**.
**T. Prakasam** dissented over **Madras city**.

nfa7b658e6e7.s: The Congress sub-committee of November 1955 on the Andhra–Telangana question comprised Nehru, G.B. Pant and:
nfa7b658e6e7.x: The sub-committee comprised Nehru, Maulana Azad and G.B. Pant; Azad continued to oppose the merger.
xa: In **Nov 1955**, Nehru was greeted with **Visalandhra slogans** in Hyderabad.
**22 Oct 1955**: the two CMs agreed to merge at **Hyderabad House**.
⚠ The **JVP** Committee (**1948-49**) = **Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi** — a different body.

nap-history-40-1.s: What was the opinion of the Dhar Commission in 1948 regarding the creation of linguistic states?
o: It opined that they were a threat to unity
It supported the formation of Andhra State in 1953
It recommended a separate Telugu University
It considered them essential for national unity
nap-history-40-1.x: The Dhar Commission of 1948 opposed linguistic states, saying their creation was a threat to national unity.
nap-history-40-1.tq: Recall the stand of the Dhar Commission.
n: The Dhar Commission opined that the creation of linguistic states was a threat to unity. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 51-52]
xs: The **Dhar Commission (1948)** opined that creating **linguistic states** was a **threat to unity** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It advised reorganisation on **administrative convenience**, not language.
It did not support Andhra State: **Andhra State** was formed only on **1 October 1953**, after **Potti Sriramulu**'s **58-day** fast.
xa: The **JVP Committee** (**Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya**) also rejected language as the basis and advised postponement.
**Justice K.N. Wanchoo** (**1953**) reported on the financial and administrative issues of separation.
The **SRC** (**Dec 1953**): **Fazl Ali**, **Kunzru**, **Panikkar**.

nap-history-40-19.s: The Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission was established in:
nap-history-40-19.x: The APPSC came in 1956, after the Dhar Commission (1948) and the SRC (1953).
n: The Dhar Commission was constituted in 1948. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 51-52]
The States Reorganisation Commission was set up on 22 December 1953. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 51-52]
The Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission was established in 1956. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 51-52]
xa: **Andhra State** was formed on **1 October 1953**; **Andhra Pradesh** on **1 November 1956**.
The AP Legislature became **bicameral** for the first time in **1958**.
⚠ **Andhra State (1953)** = first state formed on a linguistic basis; **Orissa (1936)** = first province on linguistic lines.

nap-history-40-20.s: During the boycott of which commission did Prakasam receive the title “Andhra Kesari”?
nap-history-40-20.x: Tanguturi Prakasam earned the title "Andhra Kesari" in 1928 when he bared his chest to police guns during the boycott of the Simon Commission in Madras.
nap-history-40-20.tq: Recall the event behind the title.
n: Prakasam received the title “Andhra Kesari” during the boycott of the Simon Commission. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 51-52]
xs: **Prakasam** received the title "**Andhra Kesari**" during the **boycott of the Simon Commission** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Dhar Commission** (**1948**) and **SRC** (**1953**) came long after; the **APPSC** was set up in **1956**.
Prakasam also **dissented over Madras city**.
xa: **Tenneti Viswanatham** criticised the SRC report as self-contradictory.
**Swami Sitaram**'s fast (**1951**) kept the Andhra demand alive.
Nehru called the Visalandhra movement "**Andhra imperialism**" (**Oct 1953**).

n6eaf14728c8.s: Which of the following was an argument in favour of linguistic states?
o: It would let people be governed in their own language
It would impose one language for all administration
n6eaf14728c8.x: Governance in the people's language, preservation of cultural identity and easier administration were the arguments for linguistic states.
xa: Arguments against: fear for **unity after Partition**, **regionalism**, **border and minority disputes**.
Border disputes remain, e.g. **Belgaum** (Maharashtra-Karnataka).

n68140702fcb.s: Andhra State, the first state formed on a linguistic basis after independence, was carved out of:

xa: ⚠ **Orissa (1936)** = first linguistic **province**.
Andhra's creation set off similar demands → the **SRC**.

nd1fd9df75f2.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State (1953)?
nd1fd9df75f2.x: Tanguturi Prakasam was the first CM of Andhra State; N. Sanjiva Reddy was the first CM of Andhra Pradesh (1956).
xa: Andhra State was formed on **1 October 1953** from Madras State.
Andhra Pradesh (**1 November 1956**) had its capital at **Hyderabad**.

nef0a29bdea8.s: The States Reorganisation Commission was formally constituted by a Home Ministry Resolution on:
nef0a29bdea8.x: Announced on 22 December 1953, it was formally constituted on 29 December 1953 and reported in 1955.
xa: The report was made public on **9 Oct 1955**.
⚠ APHQ keys the appointment as **20 Dec 1953**; APPSC G2 2017 key = **22 December**.

n33da93be190.s: The appointment of the States Reorganisation Commission was primarily necessitated by which development?
o: The creation of Andhra State leading to similar demands in other regions
The acceptance of the Punjabi Suba demand
The merger of Hyderabad with Mysore
The demand for a separate Pakistan after Partition
n33da93be190.x: The creation of Andhra State in 1953 intensified similar demands elsewhere, prompting the appointment of the Commission.
n33da93be190.tq: Link the institutional response to its immediate historical trigger.
xs: The creation of **Andhra** (**1953**) — the "**Andhra exception**" — set off similar demands everywhere → Nehru appointed the SRC — option **(1)** is correct.
The **Punjabi Suba** demand was in fact **not accepted** by the SRC.
xa: Announced **22 Dec 1953**; constituted **29 Dec 1953**.
Members: **Fazl Ali**, **Kunzru**, **Panikkar**.
Trigger chain: Andhra State → SRC → its **Hyderabad chapter** decided the Andhra-Telangana question.

nb9334336433.s: The States Reorganisation Commission regarded language as:
o: The sole basis for forming states
An important factor but not the only factor
A factor only for southern states
nb9334336433.x: The SRC treated language as important but not the only factor, rejecting 'one language, one state' and weighing national unity.
xa: It split same-language areas into more than one state — not a "Linguistic States Commission".
It kept **Bombay** bilingual and proposed a separate **Vidarbha**.

n4de4014edd8.s: Which one of the following correctly illustrates the SRC’s rejection of the idea that every language should have only one State?
o: It prohibited the formation of all linguistic States.
It made language irrelevant in every case.
It converted all linguistic regions into Union Territories.
It divided same-language areas into more than one State where other factors warranted it.
n4de4014edd8.x: The SRC was not solely a Linguistic States Commission; it could divide areas sharing a language into more than one State when other considerations required it.
n4de4014edd8.tq: Use the example-based interpretation of a general principle.
xs: The SRC **split same-language areas into more than one state** where other factors warranted — option **(4)** is correct.
It did not ban linguistic states or make language irrelevant — language stayed a **major** factor.
xa: Example: a separate **Vidarbha** state, apart from Marathi areas of Bombay.
Example: Telugu **Telangana** kept as a separate **Hyderabad State** for now (para **386**).

n1966fc85599.s: The States Reorganisation Commission recommended that Bombay should be:
o: Divided immediately into Gujarat and Maharashtra
Retained as a bilingual state comprising Gujarati and Marathi areas
n1966fc85599.x: The Commission recommended retaining Bombay as a bilingual state consisting of Gujarati- and Marathi-speaking areas.
n1966fc85599.tq: Watch for later developments being projected backward onto the 1955 recommendation.
xs: The SRC kept **Bombay** as a **bilingual** state (**Gujarati + Marathi** areas) — option **(3)** is correct.
It did not divide Bombay into Gujarat and Maharashtra or make it a Union Territory.
xa: It proposed a separate **Vidarbha** state.
The **SR Act 1956** also kept a **bilingual Bombay**.
**Marathwada** districts of Hyderabad went to **Bombay State**.

n318b505f984.s: The States Reorganisation Commission report (1955) recommended the creation of:
n318b505f984.x: The 1955 report proposed 16 states and 3 Union Territories and abolition of the Part A, B and C classification.
xa: The **7th Amendment (1956)** did abolish the Part A/B/C/D distinction → **states and Union Territories**.
The **SR Act** created **14 states and 6 Union Territories**.

n9ae7ec0f4c1.s: The Belgaum border dispute, which continued after linguistic reorganisation, is between:
n9ae7ec0f4c1.x: Border disputes such as Belgaum between Maharashtra and Karnataka continued after reorganisation.
xa: For linguistic states: **administration becomes easier** (APPSC 2024).
Against: **regionalism**; **border and minority disputes**.
The SRC rejected "**one language, one state**".

nap-history-40-17.s: In which year was the States Reorganisation Commission set up?
nap-history-40-17.x: The SRC was set up in December 1953; Kailashnath Wanchoo was not a member.
n: The States Reorganisation Commission was set up on 22 December 1953. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 51-52]
Kailashnath Wanchoo was not a member of the States Reorganisation Commission. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 51-52]
xa: Members: **Syed Fazl Ali** (Chairman, Governor of Odisha), **H.N. Kunzru**, **K.M. Panikkar**.
It was formally constituted on **29 Dec 1953** by Home Ministry **Resolution No. 53/69/53**.
⚠ **Trap:** "August 1953" and "1954" are wrong for the SRC; **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** = JVP, not SRC.

n104c0c3dde8.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision associated with the Sri Bagh Pact?
o: Immediate merger of Telangana with Andhra
Establishment of university centres in Rayalaseema
n104c0c3dde8.x: The pact provided for irrigation priority, university centres and equal legislative representation for Rayalaseema, but it did not provide for the immediate merger of Telangana with Andhra.
n104c0c3dde8.tq: Find the option belonging to a later Hyderabad-Telangana debate rather than the pact.
xs: **Immediate merger of Telangana** was not a Sri Bagh term — option **(1)** is the answer.

xa: It also let **Rayalaseema choose** between the capital and the High Court.
The Telangana merger came with the **Gentlemen's Agreement** (**20 Feb 1956**).
⚠ Sri Bagh = Coastal Andhra + Rayalaseema; Gentlemen's Agreement = Andhra + Telangana.

n1d0501a162f.s: The idea of Visalandhra began in 1937 in the
n1d0501a162f.x: The Visalandhra idea began in the Circar districts in 1937.
n1d0501a162f.tq: Distinguish the geographical origin of an idea from its later venue of organisation.
xs: The **Visalandhra** idea began in **1937** in the **Circar** districts — option **(4)** is correct.

xa: **Visalandhra Mahasabha** was formed in **1949**.
**Oct 1953**: Nehru called the Visalandhra movement "**Andhra imperialism**".
**Nov 1955**: Nehru was greeted with **Visalandhra slogans** in Hyderabad.

n0104e36b2e8.s: Under the SRC's review mechanism (para 386), unification of Telangana with Andhra after 1961 required the support of ____ of the elected members of the Telangana Assembly.
n0104e36b2e8.x: The SRC required two-thirds of the elected members, not three-fourths.

nc06103ca2b6.s: One objection to the immediate merger of Telangana with Andhra was that it might affect Telangana's local-employment safeguards known as the:
nc06103ca2b6.x: The Telangana case feared that the Mulki rules and local jobs might be affected, along with diversion of its revenue surplus.
xa: The SRC gave weight to these grievances in **finance and education**.

nf8a8a651d96.s: Jawaharlal Nehru compared the merger of Andhra and Telangana to a
o: temporary administrative arrangement imposed by Parliament
military treaty between two sovereign states
matrimonial alliance with a provision for divorce
federal compact without any provision for separation
nf8a8a651d96.x: In 1956 Nehru likened the merger to a matrimonial alliance, adding that there could be a provision for divorce if the partners could not get along.
nf8a8a651d96.tq: Recall the exact metaphor used for a politically significant arrangement.
xs: Nehru likened the merger to a **matrimonial alliance with a provision for divorce** if partners could not get along — option **(3)** is correct.

xa: The merger was made **against SRC advice**, resting on **safeguards**.
It was later cited by **separate-Telangana advocates**.
⚠ Nehru in **Oct 1953** had called Visalandhra "**Andhra imperialism**".

nca9bf32c8aa.s: The later political significance of Nehru's matrimonial-alliance remark was that it was cited by
o: supporters of the abolition of linguistic states
the advocates of a permanently centralised India
the proponents of retaining the Part A-D classification
nca9bf32c8aa.x: Separate-Telangana advocates later invoked the remark as evidence that the merger was conditional rather than irrevocable.
nca9bf32c8aa.tq: Connect a historical statement with the later group that used it politically.
xs: Nehru's remark was later cited by **advocates of a separate Telangana** — option **(2)** is correct.
They read the "**provision for divorce**" as showing the merger was conditional.
xa: The **para 386** departure was the core grievance of the Telangana movements (**1969**, **2001-14**).
The 1956 safeguards (**Regional Council**, **Mulki rules**) fed the later Telangana movement.
**K.T. Rama Rao** (Jan **2026**) cited the **Fazal Ali Commission** to blame Congress for the merger.

n90a10bd28d8.s: The Centre's political handling of the Andhra-Telangana question differed from the SRC's formula because the Centre
o: referred the matter back to the Hyderabad Assembly indefinitely
overrode the recommendation to wait until 1961 and settled the issue through a political agreement
accepted the SRC plan of permanent separation without modification
waited until 1961 before considering any merger
n90a10bd28d8.x: The Centre did not follow the SRC's wait-till-1961 formula; it proceeded through a political agreement that resulted in the 1956 merger.
n90a10bd28d8.tq: Compare the Commission's proposed timing with the Centre's eventual political decision.
xs: The Centre **overrode the SRC's "wait till 1961" formula** and settled the issue by a **political agreement** — option **(2)** is correct.

xa: SRC condition: merger if **two-thirds** of Telangana's legislators voted for it.
The **Gentlemen's Agreement** (**20 Feb 1956**) led to immediate merger.
This departure fed later **Telangana movements**.

nad18bc0c90b.s: The departure from which paragraph of the States Reorganisation Commission's approach remained a core grievance of later Telangana movements?
nad18bc0c90b.x: The departure from paragraph 386 was identified as a central grievance in the Telangana movements of 1969 and 2001-14.

xs: The departure from **Paragraph 386** stayed the core grievance of the Telangana movements (**1969**, **2001-14**) — option **(4)** is correct.

**Chapter 5** = Hyderabad State; **Chapter 6** = Andhra State.

n610705ee238.s: In the Hyderabad Assembly vote on Visalandhra, how many members voted in favour of the proposal?

n192991f52c3.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 provided for a Telangana:

n8c8480e8d7f.s: The Gentlemen’s Agreement between the leaders of Andhra and Telangana was concluded on:

xs: The **Gentlemen's Agreement** was concluded on **20 February 1956** at **Hyderabad House, New Delhi** — option **(1)** is correct.

xa: Safeguards: **Telangana Regional Council**; Telangana's **surplus revenues** spent there; **Mulki rules** kept.

nd41bc7303f1.s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh formed on 1 November 1956?
nd41bc7303f1.x: N. Sanjiva Reddy became the first Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh after its formation on 1 November 1956.

xa: **Burgula Ramakrishna Rao** was the Hyderabad CM who worked to allay Telangana's fears.

Andhra Pradesh's capital: **Hyderabad**; Andhra State's: **Kurnool**.

n025f5a43cd7.s: For Telangana, the States Reorganisation Commission had originally recommended:
n025f5a43cd7.x: The SRC initially recommended keeping Telangana separate; the 1956 merger followed the Gentlemen's Agreement.

nfb289eb1698.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement was concluded on:
nfb289eb1698.x: The Agreement came on 20 February 1956, after the CMs agreed to merge (22 October 1955) and before AP's formation (1 November 1956).
xa: **Nov 1955**: Congress sub-committee of **Nehru, Maulana Azad, G.B. Pant**.
**1949**: Visalandhra Mahasabha formed.
**1937**: the Visalandhra idea starts in the **Circar** districts.

n654d70d502c.s: The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 came into force on:
n654d70d502c.x: The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 came into force on 1 November 1956.
n654d70d502c.tq: Use the exact commencement date rather than the year of enactment alone.
xs: The **SR Act 1956** came into force on **1 November 1956** — option **(4)** is correct.

xa: Outcome: **14 states and 6 Union Territories**.
**Andhra Pradesh** was formed the same day.
The **7th Amendment Bill** was introduced on **10 Aug 1956**.

n1b08660082c.s: Which was the first state formed under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
n1b08660082c.x: Andhra Pradesh was the first state formed under the SR Act, 1956, not Mysore.
xa: ⚠ **Andhra State (1953)** = first linguistic state; **Orissa (1936)** = first linguistic province.
In force **1 November 1956**.
Hyderabad's Kannada districts (**Raichur, Gulbarga**) went to **Mysore**.

ne86c9684d8b.s: Which Articles were inserted by the Seventh Constitutional Amendment to deal with mother-tongue instruction and linguistic minorities?
ne86c9684d8b.x: Articles 350A and 350B concern mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage and the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, respectively.
ne86c9684d8b.tq: Discriminate between closely numbered constitutional provisions.
xs: The **7th Amendment** inserted **Articles 350A-350B** — option **(4)** is correct.
**350A**: **mother-tongue instruction**; **350B**: **Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities**.
xa: It also abolished the **Rajpramukh** office.
It dealt with **new High Courts** and High Court judges.
It made **Part C and D** units into **Union Territories**.

n85337d35962.s: The Seventh Constitutional Amendment (1956) abolished the office of:
n85337d35962.x: It abolished the office of Rajpramukh and replaced the Part A/B/C/D classification with states and Union Territories.
xa: Gave effect to SRC recommendations: **14** states + **6** UTs.
Inserted **Articles 350A-350B**.
⚠ The **SRC** had itself proposed abolishing the **Part A/B/C** classification.

nf9db4433feb.s: The States Reorganisation Act, 1956, read with the Seventh Constitutional Amendment, reorganised India into:
nf9db4433feb.x: The SR Act 1956 and the Seventh Amendment gave effect to 14 states and 6 Union Territories (UPSC). 16 states and 3 UTs was the SRC's own recommendation of 1955; the other combinations mix the two.
xs: The SR Act 1956 with the 7th Amendment gave **14 states and 6 Union Territories** — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ **16 states and 3 UTs** was the **SRC's** own recommendation (**1955**).
xa: UTs: **Delhi, Manipur, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, Andaman & Nicobar, Laccadive-Minicoy-Amindivi**.
SRC report submitted **30 Sep 1955**, made public **9 Oct 1955**.
SRC's states included **Hyderabad** and **Vidarbha**.

naaa104a95e5.s: Who was the chairman of the States Reorganisation Commission (1953)?
naaa104a95e5.x: Syed Fazl Ali (then Governor of Odisha) chaired it; H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar were members.
xa: ⚠ **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** = JVP, not SRC.
The SRC report (**1955**) recommended **16 states and 3 Union Territories**.

nd53578f4c5f.s: Hyderabad State was classified as a Part B State during which of the following periods?
nd53578f4c5f.x: Hyderabad State was a Part B State from 1950 until 31 October 1956, immediately before the formation of Andhra Pradesh.
nd53578f4c5f.tq: Use the exact constitutional period and distinguish the final date from the appointed day.
xs: **Hyderabad State** was a **Part B state** from **1950 to 31 October 1956** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It ceased to exist the day before **Andhra Pradesh** was formed on **1 November 1956**, so dates ending "1 November 1956" are wrong.
**1952** is the year of its first elected ministry (**Burgula**), not the start of Part B status.
xa: Population of Hyderabad State: **18.7 million**.
Language shares: **Telugu 47.8%**, **Marathi 24.3%**, **Urdu 11.6%**, **Kannada 10.5%**.
On reorganisation its **Kannada** areas went to **Mysore** and **Marathi** areas to **Bombay**; the **9** Telangana districts joined Andhra.

nd748d27806e.s: The Nizam Andhra Mahasabha developed out of which organisation founded in 1921?
nd748d27806e.x: The Nizam Andhra Mahasabha grew out of the Andhra Jana Sangham, which was founded in 1921.
nd748d27806e.tq: Use the organisation-to-successor relationship rather than confusing it with later political bodies.
xs: The Nizam Andhra Mahasabha grew out of the **Andhra Jana Sangham (1921)** — option **(4)**.
It became the vehicle for **Telugu cultural and political awakening** in the Nizam's State.
xa: **First Andhra Mahasabha:** **Jogipet (1930)**, presided by **Suravaram Pratapa Reddy**.
It later split along **moderate** and **Communist** lines.
⚠ Jogipet **1930** (Andhra Mahasabha) is different from the **Visalandhra Mahasabha** founded at **Vijayawada, 1949**.

nc0616a27461.s: Who, along with Jonnavittula Gurunatham, sketched the idea of a united Andhra in 1912?
nc0616a27461.x: Unnava Lakshminarayana and Jonnavittula Gurunatham sketched it in 1912; Nyapati Subbarao proposed one rule for all Telugu areas in 1914.
xa: **1936:** **Andhra Congress Swaraj Party** manifesto.
**1946:** the **Communist Party** first demanded Visalandhra.
**1954:** **Madapati Hanumantha Rao** called the idea **50 years** old, as old as the Andhra Movement.

n802fd420128.x: Sundarayya's book was published in 1946, after the 1912 and 1914 proposals and the 1936 Swaraj Party manifesto.
xa: **Visalandhralo Prajarajyam** ("People's Rule in Greater Andhra") was written by **Puchalapalli Sundarayya**.
**1949:** Visalandhra Mahasabha founded at **Vijayawada**.
APHQ 2025 order: **Dhar Commission (1948) → Visalandhra Mahasabha (1949) → Swami Sitaram's fast (1951) → SRC (1953)**.

n2e0b0d04a21.s: Who coined the expression ‘Visalandhra’ and wrote Visalandhralo Prajarajyam?
n2e0b0d04a21.x: Puchalapalli Sundarayya coined the expression ‘Visalandhra’ and authored Visalandhralo Prajarajyam.
n2e0b0d04a21.tq: Directly associate the slogan-related publication with its author and campaigner.
xs: **Puchalapalli Sundarayya** first used the word "Visalandhra" and wrote **Visalandhralo Prajarajyam** (**1946**) — option **(3)**.
**Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao** wrote **pamphlets**; **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao** founded the Visalandhra Mahasabha; **Prakasam** gave the "mother's right" slogan.
xa: Sundarayya later became the **first General Secretary of CPI(M) (1964)**.
The daily **Visalandhra** started in **June 1952** on **Sundarayya**'s initiative.
He was the first **Leader of Opposition** in Andhra Pradesh.
**The Emergence of Andhra Pradesh** = **K.V. Narayana Rao**.

n932d0ba3a13.s: Which party started the Visalandhra movement, won many seats in both regions in 1952 and expected a majority in a united state?
n932d0ba3a13.x: The Communist Party started the movement and expected a majority in a united Telugu state.
xa: CPI demand dates from **1946**, spread through **songs, poems, books, pamphlets** and press.
**PDF (People's Democratic Front)**: the Communists' electoral front in Hyderabad State, **1952**.
⚠ Trap (APPSC G2 2025): "Communists opposed integrated linguistic states" = the **only incorrect** statement.
The Congress was initially cold to the idea, fearing a **Communist majority**.

n956998e5006.s: Who wrote 'The Emergence of Andhra Pradesh'?
n956998e5006.x: K.V. Narayana Rao wrote the book; Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao contributed pamphlets for Visalandhra.
xa: **Nilgiri** magazine was published from **Nalgonda** (APPSC G2 2012).
Other papers: **Kakatiya**, **Andhra Janata**, **Andhra Patrika**, **Telugu Desam**.
Poems on the 1956 formation: **Dasarathi** ("Enni Naalla Swapnamidi") and **Kaloji** ("Emaanandam ... Eenadu").

nf814cc80287.s: Who started the Visalandhra paper and became the first General Secretary of the CPI(M) in 1964?
nf814cc80287.x: P. Sundarayya started the Visalandhra paper and became the CPI(M)'s first General Secretary in 1964.
xa: Sundarayya first used the word Visalandhra and wrote **Visalandhralo Prajarajyam** (**1946**).
He was the first **Leader of Opposition** in Andhra Pradesh.
The **1950** Warangal session was presided by **Hayagreevachari**.

ncd1e2944b3b.s: The first Visalandhra Mahasabha at Warangal demanded that Hyderabad State be divided into three linguistic parts, with ____ as the capital.
ncd1e2944b3b.x: The first Mahasabha called for Hyderabad as the capital and for Hyderabad State to be divided into three linguistic parts.
xa: President of the Warangal session: **Hayagreevachari**.
Attendees: **Tanguturi Prakasam**, **Kodati Rajalingam**, **T.S. Murthy**; opposed by **Marri Chenna Reddy, K.V. Ranga Reddy**.
The **June 1953** Hyderabad Congress Committee also backed a three-way split: Visalandhra, United Maharashtra, United Karnataka.

ndf698253bcf.s: Who presided over the 1950 session of the Visalandhra Mahasabha?
ndf698253bcf.x: Hayagreevachari presided over the 1950 session of the Visalandhra Mahasabha.
ndf698253bcf.tq: Separate the session president from the founder and the president of the later session.
xs: The **1950** (Warangal) session was presided by **Hayagreevachari** — option **(3)**.
**Sri Sri** presided over the **1954** session; **Kaleswara Rao** was the founder (**1949**); **Harishchandra Heda** backed a separate Telangana.
xa: Session dates: **12-13 Feb 1950, Warangal**.
It demanded **Hyderabad** as capital and Hyderabad State split into three linguistic parts.
Opposed by **Marri Chenna Reddy** and **K.V. Ranga Reddy**.

n09c7f6cdab0.s: The Congress was initially cold towards the Visalandhra proposal mainly because the idea had been advanced by the:
n09c7f6cdab0.x: The idea came from the Communists, and the Congress feared a united state might give them a majority.
xa: Congress later backed it: APCC **Madras (Jan 1950)** and **Kurnool (30 Sep 1953)** with **Hyderabad** as capital.
**Nehru** called it "**Andhra imperialism**" (**Oct 1953**).
**Rajagopalachari (1949)** preferred keeping Hyderabad a **multilingual state**.

n87eba5f8fd6.s: Who described the Visalandhra movement as “Andhra imperialism” in October 1953?
n87eba5f8fd6.x: Jawaharlal Nehru referred to the Visalandhra movement as “Andhra imperialism” in October 1953.
n87eba5f8fd6.tq: Match the political remark with its speaker and time.
xs: **Jawaharlal Nehru** called it "**Andhra imperialism**" in **Oct 1953** — option **(2)**.
The remark **strengthened** the separate-Telangana camp.
xa: Nehru announced the **SRC** in the Lok Sabha on **22 Dec 1953**.
Nehru inaugurated **Andhra Pradesh** on **1 Nov 1956** with **Hyderabad** as capital.
⚠ **Rajagopalachari (1949)** = Hyderabad as a **multilingual state**.

n794105de8bb.s: Which Chief Minister was in office when the Telugu Desam Party was founded on 29 March 1982?
n794105de8bb.x: The Telugu Desam Party was founded on 29 March 1982 during the tenure of Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy.
n794105de8bb.tq: Place the party’s founding date within the correct Chief Ministerial tenure.
xs: The TDP was founded on **29 March 1982** during **Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy**'s tenure — option **(1)** (APPSC G2 2019).
Bhavanam was CM **24 Feb-20 Sep 1982**; **Kotla** followed, and **NTR** came only in **Jan 1983**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes print **29 May 1982** — wrong.
TDP won **202** seats in **1983**, within about **nine months** of founding.
**T. Anjaiah** preceded Bhavanam (**1980-82**).

nd6a5f8e79ce.s: Who headed the first elected ministry of Hyderabad State that took office in 1952?
nd6a5f8e79ce.x: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao headed the first elected ministry of Hyderabad State, which assumed office in 1952.
nd6a5f8e79ce.tq: Apply the wrong-person-with-the-deed trap by separating Hyderabad leaders from Andhra leaders.
xs: **Burgula Ramakrishna Rao** headed the first elected ministry of Hyderabad State (**1952-56**) — option **(3)**.
He was both the **first** and the **last** elected CM of Hyderabad State.
**Bezawada Gopala Reddy** was CM of **Andhra State** (after the **1955** mid-term polls); **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** was the first CM of **Andhra Pradesh**.
xa: Burgula, initially for a separate **Telangana**, backed **early merger** with Andhra in **1954** (key answer).
On **22 Oct 1955** at **Hyderabad House, New Delhi**, the CMs of Andhra and Hyderabad agreed to merge.
The **Mulki agitation (1952)** and City College firing took place under the **Burgula** ministry.
He signed the **Gentlemen's Agreement** (**20 Feb 1956**) as Hyderabad CM.

n018d98e3fb3.s: The first Andhra Mahasabha in the Nizam's Hyderabad State was held at which place in 1930, and who presided over it?
n018d98e3fb3.x: The first Andhra Mahasabha met at Jogipet in 1930 under Suravaram Pratapa Reddy. Warangal and Hayagreevachari belong to the 1950 Visalandhra Mahasabha session; Vijayawada and Kaleswara Rao to the founding of the Visalandhra Mahasabha (1949); Burgula did not preside at Jogipet.
xs: The first Andhra Mahasabha met at **Jogipet** in **1930**, presided by **Suravaram Pratapa Reddy** — option **(1)**.
**Warangal** and **Hayagreevachari** belong to the **1950** Visalandhra Mahasabha session.
**Vijayawada** and **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao** belong to the founding of the Visalandhra Mahasabha (**1949**); **Burgula** did not preside at Jogipet.
xa: The Nizam Andhra Mahasabha grew out of the **Andhra Jana Sangham (1921)**.
It later split along **moderate** and **Communist** lines.
⚠ **Jogipet 1930** = first Andhra Mahasabha; **Mulki** rules = **1888**, tightened **1919**.

n37a376b2930.s: In the 1954 Visalandhra discussions, who warned that a separate Telangana would be weak and vulnerable to suppression of democratic forces?
n37a376b2930.x: Swami Ramananda Tirtha strongly supported Visalandhra and gave this warning.
xa: Ramananda Tirtha was **President, Hyderabad Congress** (APPSC G2 2017).
The **1st** Mahasabha session was at **Warangal (1950)**.
The **2nd** Mahasabha (**13-14 Jun 1954**) was presided by **Sri Sri**.

n03bb9c4b863.s: Swami Ramananda Tirtha, Burgula Ramakrishna Rao, Mandumula Narsing Rao and Pandit Narendraji all supported the:
n03bb9c4b863.x: All four supported the Visalandhra movement.
xa: Educated Muslim support: **Mir Mohammed Ali Khan**, **Makhdoom Mohiuddin**, **Mehdi Nawaz Jung**.
Opponents: **Marri Chenna Reddy**, **Mahadev Singh** (**PSP**).
**Kaloji** first supported, later opposed the merger.

n51fd8734b71.s: Which one of the following was NOT an argument advanced in favour of Visalandhra?
o: Combination of Andhra agriculture and coastline with Telangana minerals and industry
Integrated planning of the Krishna and Godavari basins
Permanent protection of separate Telangana political institutions
n51fd8734b71.x: Protection of separate Telangana political institutions was not a pro-Visalandhra argument. The other three were arguments advanced in favour of unification.
n51fd8734b71.tq: Find the option belonging to the opposing camp rather than the pro-merger arguments.
xs: **Permanent protection of separate Telangana political institutions** was not a pro-Visalandhra argument — option **(4)**.
Arguments for: **Hyderabad** as capital, Andhra's **agriculture and coastline** + Telangana's **minerals and industry**, and integrated planning of the **Krishna and Godavari** basins.
Protection of Telangana institutions was a Telangana **safeguard** demand (the Regional Council), not an argument for union.
xa: Linguistic-cultural argument: one language, one culture; **Satavahana-Kakatiya** legacy.
Communist agrarian argument: unification to push **land reform** and weaken **feudal structures**.
**Ramananda Tirtha**: Telangana would **develop** in Visalandhra; a separate Telangana would be weak.

n6f0170f1283.s: Who preferred retaining Hyderabad as a multilingual state in 1949?
n6f0170f1283.x: C. Rajagopalachari preferred retaining Hyderabad as a multilingual state in 1949.
n6f0170f1283.tq: Match the position with the correct national leader and year.
xs: **Rajagopalachari (1949)** preferred keeping Hyderabad a **multilingual state** — option **(2)**.
**Nehru** is linked with "**Andhra imperialism**" (**Oct 1953**); **Kaleswara Rao** founded the Mahasabha; **Burgula** switched to merger in **1954**.
xa: ⚠ "Andhra imperialism" = **Nehru**; "multilingual state" = **Rajagopalachari**.
Hyderabad State languages: **Telugu 47.8%**, **Marathi 24.3%**, **Urdu 11.6%**, **Kannada 10.5%**.
Nehru's remark **strengthened** the separate-Telangana camp.

n4edb7d8af2d.s: In 1954, B. Ramakrishna Rao changed his earlier stand and advocated:
o: Continuation of Hyderabad as a multilingual State
Early merger of Telangana with Andhra
n4edb7d8af2d.x: B. Ramakrishna Rao, who had initially backed a separate Telangana, changed his position in 1954 and advocated early merger of Telangana with Andhra.
xa: ⚠ One scanned key reads **1955**; the APHQ key answer is **1954**.
After the SRC report he allayed Telangana fears on **High Command** orders.
He was the **first** and **last** elected CM of Hyderabad State (**1952-56**).

nccf22ab2b78.s: The argument that Telangana could exist as a separate State rested on its higher ____ compared with Andhra State.
nccf22ab2b78.x: Telangana's higher per capita income and revenue than Andhra State made it economically viable on its own.
xa: Telangana's revenue surplus fear led to the clause: **surplus spent only in Telangana**.
SRC: merger only with **two-thirds** of the Telangana legislature.
Nehru's "**Andhra imperialism**" remark (**Oct 1953**) boosted the separate-Telangana camp.

n36e50d421f2.s: Under paragraph 386 of the SRC report, Telangana could merge with Andhra after the 1961 elections only if its legislature approved it by a:
n36e50d421f2.x: The SRC recommended a separate Telangana initially, with merger after the 1961 elections only on a two-thirds majority of the Telangana legislature.
xa: SRC members: **Fazl Ali** (chair), **H.N. Kunzru, K.M. Panikkar**.
Also: **Raichur, Gulbarga** → Mysore; **Marathwada** detached.
The wait-till-**1961** formula foreshadowed later separate-Telangana demands.

nae1a92e3420.s: The dismissal of N.T. Rama Rao's government in 1984 is a textbook example of the alleged misuse of the discretion of the:
nae1a92e3420.x: The 1984 dismissal is cited as a classic misuse of gubernatorial discretion and fed into the later Sarkaria Commission debates.
xa: Governor: **Ram Lal**; NTR was in the **US** for treatment.
Nadendla's **31 days** (**16 Aug-16 Sep 1984**).
It led to the **52nd Amendment, 1985** (anti-defection law).

n008be9c537d.s: At the time of the Gentlemen's Agreement, the Chief Minister of Hyderabad State was:
n008be9c537d.x: Burgula was CM of Hyderabad State, K.V. Ranga Reddy its Deputy CM, and Bezawada Gopala Reddy CM of Andhra State.
xa: Other Andhra signatories: **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** (Deputy CM), **Gouthu Latchanna**.
Other Telangana signatory: **Marri Chenna Reddy** (minister).
⚠ **Tanguturi Prakasam** was **not** a signatory (APPSC GS 2018).

ncd214b9257e.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 adapted the model of which earlier pact for settling regional apprehensions?
ncd214b9257e.x: Like the Sribagh Pact, the Gentlemen's Agreement addressed regional fears through a moral and political understanding rather than a constitutional settlement.
xa: It was the written basis of the **1956** merger.
Later settlements: **1969 Eight-Point**, **1973 Six-Point**, **371D**.
**Kurnool** was chosen as Andhra State's capital in the spirit of the **Sri Bagh Pact**.

n82235425a55.s: The Mulki rules of Hyderabad State originated in:
n82235425a55.x: The Mulki rules date from 1888 and were tightened by the Nizam's farman of 1919.
xa: The **Mulki agitation (1952)** under the **Burgula** ministry saw police firing near **City College, Hyderabad**.
⚠ Domicile: Mulki rules = **15 years**; Agreement = **12 years** (some notes say 15).
Hyderabad State was a **Part B** state from **1950 to 31 Oct 1956**.

nf74b3c5d598.s: The Mulki agitation of 1952 took place under the ministry of:
nf74b3c5d598.x: It occurred under the Burgula ministry; police firing near City College, Hyderabad, killed students.
xa: Mulki rules: from **1888**, tightened by the Nizam's farman of **1919**; residence of about **15 years**.
Agreement domicile rule: residence of **12 years** for recruitment in Telangana.
Alleged later violation: Mulki rules bypassed by reclassifying local posts as "**state-cadre**" or "**unreserved**".

n8f5e5baf958.s: The term ‘Visalandhra’, meaning ‘Greater Andhra’, referred to the proposal for:
o: A separate Telangana state under Hyderabad
One state for all Telugu-speaking people of the Madras and Hyderabad regions
A federation of all southern Indian states
The merger of Andhra with the Madras Presidency without Hyderabad
n8f5e5baf958.x: Visalandhra, or Greater Andhra, envisaged one state for Telugu-speaking people living in the Madras region and Nizam’s Hyderabad.
n8f5e5baf958.tq: Identify the exact meaning of the movement rather than confusing it with later Telangana movements.
xs: **Visalandhra ("Greater Andhra")** meant **one state for all Telugu people** split between **Madras** and **Nizam's Hyderabad** — option **(2)**.
A **separate Telangana** was the opposite demand, raised by leaders like **Marri Chenna Reddy**.
xa: First to use the word: **Puchalapalli Sundarayya**.
First demand by a party: the **Communist Party**, in **1946**.
APPSC-GS 2024: the united-Telugu-state movement = **Visalandhra Movement**.
The Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded at **Vijayawada** on **26 Nov 1949**.

n1130f113b9d.s: Before the 1956 merger, Telangana's employment apprehension was that the ____ might be weakened.
n1130f113b9d.x: The employment concern was weakening of the Mulki Rules; other fears concerned the revenue surplus and regional disparities.
xa: Education fear: Coastal Andhra's advanced educational and administrative position would dominate public services.
Agreement answer to revenue fear: **surplus spent only in Telangana**, reviewed after **5 years**.
Argument for separate Telangana: higher **per capita income** and **revenue** than Andhra State.

n5386a7603f1.s: The Warangal Congress meeting connected with the merger discussions was held on:
n5386a7603f1.x: The Warangal meeting was on 8 July 1954; the CMs met at Hyderabad House on 22 October 1955 and the Agreement came on 20 February 1956.
xa: At Warangal the Hyderabad government had **no official opinion** before the SRC; ministers gave personal views.
⚠ Both **22 Oct 1955** and **20 Feb 1956** events were at **Hyderabad House, New Delhi**.
The Agreement was signed by **8 leaders** — **4** from each region.

n5ca37666dae.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement was signed at which of the following places?
n5ca37666dae.x: The agreement was signed at Hyderabad House in New Delhi. Some accounts refer to the venue as Hyderabad Guest House, Delhi, but the commonly recorded venue is Hyderabad House.
n5ca37666dae.tq: Use location-based recall while distinguishing the venue from the place represented by the agreement.
xs: The Gentlemen's Agreement was signed at **Hyderabad House, New Delhi** — option **(4)**.
Some notes call it "**Hyderabad Guest House, Delhi**".
xa: Date: **20 February 1956**.
The CMs had agreed to merge at the same venue on **22 Oct 1955**.
Signed by **8 leaders** — **4** from Andhra and **4** from Telangana.

n166c9cd81c6.s: How many leaders signed the Gentlemen's Agreement of 20 February 1956?
n166c9cd81c6.x: Eight leaders signed it, four from Andhra and four from Telangana.
xa: Venue: **Hyderabad House, New Delhi**.
Not a signatory: **Tanguturi Prakasam**.

n069968df0eb.s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement, Telangana students were assured admission priority or at least ____ of the seats in technical institutions, whichever was more favourable.
n069968df0eb.x: The agreement gave Telangana students admission priority or at least one-third of the seats in technical institutions, whichever was more favourable.
xa: Fear: Coastal Andhra's more advanced educational position would dominate.
Domicile rule for recruitment: **12 years** of residence.
Later, **Article 371D** (**32nd Amendment, 1973**) gave equitable opportunities in public employment and education.

n241a2a3b159.s: The domicile safeguard associated with recruitment in Telangana required residence for how many years?
n241a2a3b159.x: The agreed safeguard referred to Mulki or domicile rules requiring 12 years of residence for recruitment in Telangana.
n241a2a3b159.tq: Separate the exact numerical requirement from nearby duration figures used in related provisions.
xs: The domicile safeguard required **12 years** of residence — option **(3)**.
⚠ Some notes say **15 years**; the original **Mulki rules** required about **15 years**.
**5 years** is the Urdu/finance review period; **10 years** the Regional Committee review.
xa: Mulki rules: from **1888**, tightened by the Nizam's farman of **1919**.
Alleged violation: posts reclassified as "**state-cadre**" or "**unreserved**".
The local-cadre system under **Art. 371D** descends from this domicile clause.

n6f040834442.s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956), Urdu was to be kept in Telangana's administration and courts for:
n6f040834442.x: Urdu was retained for five years (then reviewed by the Regional Council), not ten.
xa: After 5 years the Urdu clause was to be reviewed by the **Regional Council**.
Finance clause also reviewed after **5 years**.
Regional Committee itself was to be reviewed after **10 years**.

n21a3b8ca0d9.s: The cabinet composition agreed under the Gentlemen's Agreement was based on which ratio between Andhra and Telangana?
n21a3b8ca0d9.x: The finally agreed cabinet share was 60:40 between Andhra and Telangana. It was also provided that at least one Muslim minister would be included from Telangana.
n21a3b8ca0d9.tq: Prefer the precise percentage ratio when both a simplified ratio and a rounded formulation may appear in sources.
xs: The cabinet share was **60:40** (Andhra:Telangana) — option **(4)**.
⚠ Older notes print **3:1**; keyed answer = **60:40** (APPSC G2 2025).
xa: Also put as "Telangana at least **40%**".
At least **one Muslim** minister from Telangana.
At least **two** of Home, Finance, Revenue, Planning & Development, Commerce & Industry to Telangana.

nea85fa7eb21.s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement, at least how many of the portfolios of Home, Finance, Revenue, Planning and Development, and Commerce and Industry were to go to Telangana?
nea85fa7eb21.x: At least two of these portfolios were to go to Telangana, and the CM and Deputy CM were to be from different regions.

Report: **March 1953**; it fixed the new state's districts.
Trigger: **Potti Sriramulu**'s death (**Dec 1952**).

nddc344d4cbf.s: Who among the following was NOT a member of the States Reorganisation Commission?
nddc344d4cbf.x: Fazl Ali, H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar were the members of the States Reorganisation Commission. Harishchandra Heda was associated with Telangana political resolutions, not with the Commission.
nddc344d4cbf.tq: Identify the person outside the formal membership list.
xs: **Harishchandra Heda** was not an SRC member — option **(3)**.
SRC members: **Fazl Ali** (chair), **H.N. Kunzru, K.M. Panikkar**.
Heda was in the Hyderabad PCC delegation to the SRC and backed separate Telangana (**Nov 1955**).
xa: SRC announced **22 Dec 1953**, constituted **29 Dec 1953**, report **1955**.
⚠ **Fazl Ali** = SRC; **Wanchoo** = Andhra State problems; **Pataskar** = Andhra-Madras border.
BRS leader **K.T. Rama Rao** (**Jan 2026**) cited the **Fazal Ali Commission**'s recommendation.

ncdd798799b9.s: Which of the following territorial changes was recommended in relation to Hyderabad State by the States Reorganisation Commission?
o: Raichur and Gulbarga to Andhra, and Marathwada to Mysore
Marathwada to Andhra, and the Kannada areas to Telangana
Raichur and Gulbarga to Mysore, and Marathwada to be detached
ncdd798799b9.x: The Commission recommended that Raichur and Gulbarga go to Mysore and that Marathwada be detached from Hyderabad State.
ncdd798799b9.tq: Test the direction of territorial transfers without reversing the recipient regions.
xs: SRC: **Raichur and Gulbarga to Mysore**, and **Marathwada** to be **detached** — option **(3)**.
Telangana was to continue initially as a **separate state**.
xa: Reconsider after **1961** elections; merger only with **two-thirds** of the Telangana legislature.
On **1 Nov 1956**, Kannada areas of Hyderabad went to **Mysore** and Marathi areas to **Bombay**.
Telugu, Kannada and Marathi areas of Hyderabad State agreed to partition.

n4580d84764d.s: Which of the following persons was NOT a signatory associated with the Gentlemen's Agreement?
n4580d84764d.x: Tanguturi Prakasam was not a signatory. Gouthu Latchanna, Alluri Satyanarayana Raju and J.V. Narsing Rao were among the listed signatories.
n4580d84764d.tq: Find the one outsider in a list of regional signatories.
xs: **Tanguturi Prakasam** was not a signatory — option **(3)** (APPSC GS 2018).
**Gouthu Latchanna** and **Alluri Satyanarayana Raju** signed for Andhra; **J.V. Narsing Rao** for Telangana.
xa: Andhra: **Bezawada Gopala Reddy**, **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy**, Gouthu Latchanna, Alluri Satyanarayana Raju.
Telangana: **Burgula**, **K.V. Ranga Reddy**, **Marri Chenna Reddy**, J.V. Narsing Rao.
Signed **20 February 1956**, **Hyderabad House, New Delhi**.

n71f156492ca.s: P.V. Narasimha Rao first became Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in:
n71f156492ca.x: The order was Sanjivayya (1960), Kasu Brahmananda Reddy (1964), P.V. Narasimha Rao (1971), T. Anjaiah (1980).
xa: Brahmananda Reddy's 2nd term began **6 Mar 1967**.
President's Rule: **18 Jan-10 Dec 1973**, after PVNR.
Anjaiah: **11 Oct 1980-Feb 1982**.
n71f156492ca.fixed: remove '(PYQ 2025)' tag from stem; matches y72a291a29f7

nap-history-25-10.s: The Join Indian Union Movement in Hyderabad was launched on:
nap-history-25-10.x: It began on 7 August 1947 against the Nizam's plan to keep Hyderabad independent; 17 September 1948 is the date of integration after Operation Polo.
n: The Join Indian Union Movement was launched on August 7, 1947. [AP History · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 35-37]
xa: **Swamy Ramananda Tirtha** was a **key personality** of the movement.
He later, as **President, Hyderabad Congress**, strongly backed **Visalandhra** at the **Second Mahasabha (Hyderabad, 1954)**.
The **Visalandhra Mahasabha** was founded on **26 Nov 1949** at **Vijayawada** under **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao**.

ndf71f80a1fc.x: Dasarathi wrote 'Enni Naalla Swapnamidi', while Kaloji wrote 'Emaanandam ... Eenadu'.
xa: ⚠ **Kaloji** first supported, later opposed the merger.
**Visalandhralo Prajarajyam** (**1946**) = **Sundarayya**.
**The Emergence of Andhra Pradesh** = **K.V. Narayana Rao**.

n08eda4952fa.s: Bombay State was bifurcated into Maharashtra and Gujarat in 1960 mainly following the:
o: Akali Dal and Punjabi Suba movements
n08eda4952fa.x: The Samyukta Maharashtra and Mahagujarat movements led to the division of Bombay State into Maharashtra and Gujarat on 1 May 1960.
n08eda4952fa.tq: Match a reorganisation outcome with the movements that demanded it.
xs: Bombay was split into **Maharashtra and Gujarat** (**1960**) after the **Samyukta Maharashtra and Mahagujarat** movements — option **(1)**.
The law was the **Bombay Reorganisation Act 1960**.
xa: It was a **linguistic** reorganisation, like Andhra **1953**.
**1966:** **Punjab Reorganisation Act** created **Haryana**.
**1963:** **Nagaland**, first NE state with full statehood.

nb5ccf3c27af.s: Under the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966, Chandigarh became:
o: A Union Territory and the shared capital of Punjab and Haryana
nb5ccf3c27af.x: The 1966 Act created Punjab and Haryana and made Chandigarh a Union Territory serving as their shared capital.
xa: ⚠ HP became a **state** only in **1971**, not **1966**.
**Gujarat** came from Bombay in **1960**, not from Punjab.
Ascending order (APPSC 2018 key): AP (**1953/56**) → Haryana (**1966**) → Chhattisgarh (**2000**) → Telangana (**2014**).

nc91d2016ec3.s: Which one of the following states was created in 1963 and was the first North-Eastern state to receive full statehood?
nc91d2016ec3.x: Nagaland became a state in 1963 and was the first North-Eastern state granted full statehood. The State of Nagaland Act was enacted in 1962.
nc91d2016ec3.tq: Separate the year of the Act from the year of state inauguration.
xs: **Nagaland** (**1963**) was the first NE state to get full statehood — option **(4)**.
Its Act is the **State of Nagaland Act 1962**; some notes date it to 1962.
**Manipur, Tripura, Meghalaya** came in **1972**; **Mizoram** in **1987**.
xa: Nagaland was the first NE state carved out of **Assam** (APPSC 2025).
It was formed on an **ethnic/tribal** basis.
**1971** NE Areas (Reorganisation) Act made **Mizoram** and **Arunachal** UTs.

n05149952bb9.s: Manipur, Tripura and Meghalaya attained statehood in 1972 under which enactment?
n05149952bb9.x: Manipur, Tripura and Meghalaya became states in 1972 under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971.
n05149952bb9.tq: Start from the sure law-state association.
xs: **Manipur, Tripura and Meghalaya** became states in **1972** under the **North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971** — option **(2)**.
The same Act made **Mizoram** and **Arunachal** UTs.
xa: Mizoram and Arunachal became states in **1987** (Acts of **1986**).
**Meghalaya** = ethnic/tribal basis.
**Nagaland Act 1962** → statehood **1963**.

n559844b63d3.s: The states created in 2000 were formed mainly on grounds of:
n559844b63d3.x: The 2000 states were created on grounds of tribal and regional backwardness, not language.
xa: Other ethnic/tribal states: **Meghalaya**, **Jharkhand**, **Chhattisgarh**.
Linguistic: Andhra **1953**, the **1956** wave, Maharashtra-Gujarat **1960**.
Newer basis: **size + governance** (mega-states like **UP**, **240 million+**).

n74bf503e2cf.s: Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Uttarakhand were formed in:
n74bf503e2cf.x: The three States were formed in 2000, between AP (1956) and Telangana (2014).
xa: J&K and Ladakh became UTs from **31 October 2019** under the **J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019**.
J&K's **Legislative Council** was abolished; **Ladakh** has no legislature.
Common **High Court of J&K and Ladakh**.

ncffd4125b0d.s: Telangana came into existence as the 29th State of India on
ncffd4125b0d.x: Telangana was formed on 2 June 2014 under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, as the 29th State. The other dates are distractors: 1 November is the old AP formation day and 2 October is Gandhi Jayanti.
xs: Telangana became the **29th state** on **2 June 2014** — option **(2)**.
**1 November** is AP's old formation day (**1956**).
xa: President's assent to APRA: **1 March 2014** (APPSC 2025 key).
⚠ Trap: "came into effect **2 March 2014**" is wrong.
**Section 10**: First Schedule entry **"29. Telangana"**.

n47be921b086.s: Sakala Janula Samme, associated with the separate Telangana movement, was:
o: An eight-point formula announced in April 1969
A parliamentary resolution adopted in July 2013
A one-day march at Tank Bund during March 2011
A general strike lasting approximately 42 days during September–October 2011
n47be921b086.x: Sakala Janula Samme was a general strike that lasted approximately 42 days during September–October 2011. The Tank Bund march was the Million March, held in March 2011.
n47be921b086.tq: Distinguish the prolonged general strike from the one-day Million March.
xs: **Sakala Janula Samme** was a **general strike** of about **42 days** in **Sep-Oct 2011** — option **(4)**.
The **Tank Bund** march of **Mar 2011** was the **Million March**.
The **8-point formula** was Indira Gandhi's of **11 Apr 1969**; **July 2013** was a **CWC resolution**.
xa: The **TRS** was formed in **2001** by **K. Chandrasekhar Rao**.
The **Srikrishna Committee** reported on **30 Dec 2010** with **six options**.
Telangana was born on the appointed day, **2 June 2014**.

n1c00ee44ea7.s: Which rivers constitute the principal subject of dispute between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana after bifurcation?
n1c00ee44ea7.x: The Krishna and Godavari are the principal rivers involved in post-bifurcation water-sharing disputes between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
n1c00ee44ea7.tq: Use direct identification of the central factual pair.
xs: The most contentious rivers are the **Krishna and Godavari** — option **(3)** (**APPSC 2025**).
They are managed by the **KRMB and GRMB** under an **Apex Council**.
xa: The **Apex Council** is chaired by the **Union Water Resources Minister** with both CMs.
The **Polavaram-Banakacherla link** (Godavari → Krishna → Penna) is opposed by Telangana.
Boards are provided under **Sec 84-85** of the Act.

nf5f56425d00.s: The objection raised by Telangana to the Polavaram–Banakacherla link is that it allegedly violates which of the following?
o: The River Boards Act and the Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal Award, 1973
The Inter-State Water Disputes Act and the Sarkaria Commission Report
The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act and the GWDT Award, 1980
The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 and the Bachawat Commission Award
nf5f56425d00.x: Telangana has argued that the link violates the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act and the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal Award of 1980.
nf5f56425d00.tq: Match the dispute with the exact legal instruments named in it.
xs: Telangana says the link violates the **AP Reorganisation Act** and the **GWDT Award, 1980** — option **(3)**.
The link carries water **Godavari → Krishna → Penna** (**Jul 2025**).
xa: The **Apex Council** is chaired by the **Union Water Resources Minister** with both CMs.
Telangana wants time-bound closure of Act issues and its **Krishna** rights.
Deputy CM **Bhatti Vikramarka** raised this with the Centre (**Aug 2026**).

n06278a37a5d.s: After the J&K Reorganisation of 2019 and the merger of Dadra & Nagar Haveli with Daman & Diu (January 2020), India has:
n06278a37a5d.x: After Jammu and Kashmir ceased to be a State and became a Union Territory in 2019, India has 28 States and 8 Union Territories.
n06278a37a5d.tq: Account for the change in status of Jammu and Kashmir before selecting the present total.
xs: After J&K became a UT in **2019**, India has **28 states and 8 UTs** — option **(2)**.
The **J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019** split it into two UTs — **Jammu and Kashmir** and **Ladakh**.
xa: The split took effect from **31 October 2019**.
It followed a presidential order under **Art. 370** revoking special status.
Telangana (**2014**) was the **29th state** at its formation.
n06278a37a5d.fixed: In Oct 2019 the count was 28 States + 9 UTs; 8 UTs only after the Jan 2020 merger, so the stem as worded is ambiguous

n62826a23f2c.s: A major criticism of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 is that it was passed without the consent of the:
n62826a23f2c.x: The Act was passed without the consent of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.
xa: Under **Art. 3**, the state legislature's views are **not binding**.
Telangana wants time-bound closure of pending Act issues and its **Krishna** rights.
**Sec 108** and the expert committees have **no deadlines or binding force**.

n981b3550ed2.s: Prof. K. Jayashankar, associated with the Telangana movement, was a former Vice-Chancellor of:
n981b3550ed2.x: Prof. K. Jayashankar was a former Vice-Chancellor of Kakatiya University and was widely regarded as the ideologue of the Telangana movement.
n981b3550ed2.tq: Use the person–institution association to distinguish prominent regional figures.
xs: **Prof. K. Jayashankar** was a former VC of **Kakatiya University** — option **(2)**.
He was active in the **1952** and **1969** agitations and is widely called the **ideologue** of the Telangana movement.
xa: He came up in the **'Jatipita'** title debate (**Feb 2026**).
The **1969** agitation began with a **student strike in Khammam**.
Telangana (**2014**) = youngest (**29th**) state.

n27c1a3274fa.s: Under which Article can Parliament by law form a new State or alter the area, boundaries or name of a State?
n27c1a3274fa.x: Article 3 empowers Parliament to form new States and change their area, boundaries or names.
xa: **Article 2** = admission of new states/territory from outside (e.g., **Sikkim**, **36th Amendment**).
**Article 4**: such a law is **not an amendment** under **Article 368**.
The **AP Reorganisation Act 2014** was made under **Article 3**.

n67eaf55c123.s: A Bill under Article 3 can be introduced in Parliament only on the recommendation of the:
n67eaf55c123.x: It needs the President's recommendation; the State legislature's views are sought but not binding, and it passes by simple majority.
xa: Time limit for views: **5th Amendment 1955**.
No reference is needed for a **UT**.
Criticism of APRA 2014: passed **without the state assembly's consent**.

n96e95b87df5.s: The provision requiring the State Legislature to express its views on an Article 3 Bill within a period specified by the President was added by the
n96e95b87df5.x: The time limit for the affected State Legislature to express its views on an Article 3 Bill was added by the 5th Amendment, 1955. The 1st Amendment (1951) dealt with other matters, the 7th Amendment (1956) implemented the States reorganisation, and the 36th Amendment (1975) made Sikkim a State.
n96e95b87df5.tq: Art 3 reference time limit = 5th Amendment 1955; views are still not binding.
xs: The time limit for the state's views was added by the **5th Amendment, 1955** — option **(2)**.
The **36th Amendment** relates to **Sikkim** (Art. 2 admission), not Article 3 procedure.
xa: The views remain **not binding** on Parliament.
No fresh reference is needed for each amendment to the bill.
**Article 4**: such laws are not Art. 368 amendments.

n6d1e396072c.s: Section 10 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 added Telangana as entry number ____ in the First Schedule.
n6d1e396072c.x: Section 10 added Telangana as entry 29; the Act was made under Articles 3 and 4, needing no Article 368 amendment.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes say **Article 2** — wrong; Art. 2 = admitting new states/territory from outside (e.g., **Sikkim**).
An Art. 3 bill needs the **President's recommendation** and passes by **simple majority**.
The state legislature's views are **not binding**.

n1bdc82666be.s: Which Article of the Constitution was amended in relation to the Legislative Council of Telangana?
n1bdc82666be.x: Article 168 was changed in relation to the Legislative Council of Telangana. Article 371D was extended to Telangana separately.
n1bdc82666be.tq: Distinguish the constitutional provision concerning State legislatures from those concerning Assembly delimitation and High Courts.
xs: **Article 168** was amended for the **Telangana Legislative Council** — option **(2)**.
**Art. 371D** was extended to Telangana by **Sec 97**; **Art. 170** governs the Assembly seat increase; **Art. 214** concerns AP's separate High Court.
xa: Legislative Council seats: AP **58** (some notes: **50**), Telangana **40**.
Amendment of **Articles 371D and 168** is in **Part XII** (**APPSC 2022**).
Assembly seats: AP **175**, Telangana **119**.

n745c789ef2f.s: Under the original Mulki rules of 1888, an outsider could be appointed to a State post only with the permission of the:
n745c789ef2f.x: The 1888 rules reserved State posts for local residents, while an outsider required the permission of the Prime Minister, or Diwan, for appointment.
n745c789ef2f.tq: Use the authority-holder trap in an administrative-history question.
xs: An outsider needed the permission of the **Prime Minister (Diwan)** — option **(1)**.
From **1919** the stricter rule required the **Nizam's personal permission**.
xa: Purpose: local residents to get **State posts**.
Origin: **1888**, **Salar Jung II** era.
The **1919** Farman aimed to curb **unemployment among locals**.

nfb5317555fc.s: The 1919 Nizam's Farman made the Mulki rules stricter by requiring outsiders to obtain:
o: A certificate from the Girglani Commission
The personal permission of the Nizam
The approval of the Hyderabad Legislative Council
The permission of the Prime Minister of India
nfb5317555fc.x: The 1919 Farman required outsiders to obtain the Nizam's personal permission, strengthening the protection of local employment.
nfb5317555fc.tq: Separate the 1888 Diwan-permission rule from the stricter 1919 requirement.
xs: The **1919 Nizam's Farman** required outsiders to get the **Nizam's personal permission** — option **(2)**.
The **Girglani Commission** came only in **2001**.
xa: Under the **1888** rules, the **Prime Minister (Diwan)** gave permission.
Aim: curb **unemployment among locals**.
Mulki = **15 years** continuous residence (Nizam's rules).

na6d89196153.s: The Nizam's Mulki rules required how many years of continuous residence?
na6d89196153.x: The Nizam's rules required 15 years' continuous residence, whereas the 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement suggested 12 years.
xa: ⚠ Some notes give **15 years** for the Agreement too.
Gentlemen's Agreement signed **20 Feb 1956**.
**1969 Jai Telangana** sought implementation of Mulki safeguards.

nce330c5d98b.s: The Telangana agitation of 1969 was led by which organisation, whose convener was A. Madan Mohan?
nce330c5d98b.x: The 1969 Jai Telangana agitation was led by the Telangana Praja Samithi, with A. Madan Mohan as its convener.
nce330c5d98b.tq: Identify the organisation through its associated office-bearer.
xs: The **1969** agitation was led by the **Telangana Praja Samithi**, convener **A. Madan Mohan** — option **(4)**.
**TRS** came much later (**2001**).
xa: TPS formed **February 1969**; president **Marri Channa Reddy**; symbol **spade**.
TPS won **10 of the 14** seats it contested in the **1971** Lok Sabha poll.
TPS later **merged with the Congress** after agreement with **Indira Gandhi**.

n85b578b2ae5.s: The Telangana agitation began as a student strike at:
n85b578b2ae5.x: The agitation began as a student strike in Khammam in January 1969.
n85b578b2ae5.tq: Test the movement’s place of origin directly, using nearby regional locations as distractors.
xs: The agitation began as a **student strike in Khammam** (**January 1969**) — option **(3)**.
It was led by student leaders such as **Mallikarjun** and intensified by **March 1969**.
xa: First hunger strike: student **Ravindranath** at Khammam.
Over **360** students and agitators were killed in police firings.
They are remembered as the **Telangana martyrs of 1969**.

n31e3c23ea9c.s: Who undertook the first hunger strike during the Telangana agitation of 1969?
n31e3c23ea9c.x: The first hunger strike was undertaken by the student Ravindranath at Khammam in January 1969.
n31e3c23ea9c.tq: Distinguish the student hunger-strike participant from the political leaders and organisers of the movement.
xs: Student **Ravindranath** began the first hunger strike at **Khammam** (**January 1969**) — option **(3)**.
**Mallikarjun** led the student strike; **Madan Mohan** was TPS convener; **Marri Channa Reddy** TPS president.
xa: The movement grew from students into a political movement under the **TPS**.
Police firings killed **over 360** students and agitators.
**Eight-Point Formula** announced **11 April 1969**.

n53e8f4226cc.s: The Telangana Praja Samiti was formed in:
n53e8f4226cc.x: The Telangana Praja Samiti was formed in February 1969. It was renamed in December 1970.
n53e8f4226cc.tq: Distinguish the organisation’s formation date from its later renaming and merger-related developments.
xs: The **Telangana Praja Samiti** was formed in **February 1969** — option **(1)**.
It was **renamed** in **December 1970**; **September 1971** is the merger date in some notes.
xa: Convener **A. Madan Mohan**; president **Marri Channa Reddy**; symbol **spade**.
Won **10 of the 14** seats contested (**1971** Lok Sabha).
Merger opponents formed the **Complete Telangana Praja Samithi** (**B. Satyanarayana Reddy**).

n52e631637b8.s: Who was the president of the Telangana Praja Samiti?
n52e631637b8.x: Marri Channa Reddy was president of the Telangana Praja Samiti; B. Satyanarayana Reddy later led the Complete Telangana Praja Samiti.
xa: TPS was formed **February 1969**.
It merged with the Congress (**September 1971**; some notes **Sep 1972**).
Demand lay dormant until **TRS (2001)**.

n31adab40722.s: The Telangana martyrs of 1969 are associated with the death of approximately how many students and agitators in police firings?
n31adab40722.x: Severe police firings during the 1969 movement resulted in the death of over 360 students and agitators, remembered as the Telangana martyrs.
n31adab40722.tq: Retain the specific casualty figure and distinguish it from nearby numerical distractors.
xs: Police firings in **1969** killed **over 360 students and agitators** — option **(2)** is correct.
They are remembered as the **Telangana martyrs of 1969**.
xa: The agitation began with a **student strike in Khammam**, **January 1969** (leaders such as **Mallikarjun**).
First hunger strike: student **Ravindranath** at **Khammam** (**January 1969**).
It grew from a students' agitation into a statehood movement under the **TPS**.

n28b84184d1c.s: The Eight-Point Formula relating to Telangana was announced by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on:
n28b84184d1c.x: The Eight-Point Formula was announced by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi at a special meeting in Delhi on 11 April 1969.
n28b84184d1c.tq: Use the exact date associated with the formula and distinguish it from the later Five-Point and Six-Point arrangements.
xs: **PM Indira Gandhi** announced the **Eight-Point Formula** on **11 April 1969** at a special meeting in **Delhi** — option **(2)** is correct.
**27 November 1972** = **Five-Point Formula**; **21 September 1973** = Six-Point Formula proposed; **1 October 1973** = Jai Andhra called off.
xa: Clause 1: a high-level committee headed by a sitting/retired **Supreme Court judge**.
Clause 2: special committee on **Telangana surplus funds**.

nb9944c4e6a8.s: In A.V.S. Narasimha Rao v. State of Andhra Pradesh, decided in 1969, the Supreme Court:
o: Struck down the Telangana residence clause of the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957
Upheld the Mulki Rules as applicable to all public posts in Andhra Pradesh
Repealed the Mulki Rules under the Six-Point Formula
nb9944c4e6a8.x: In A.V.S. Narasimha Rao v. State of Andhra Pradesh, the Supreme Court struck down the Telangana residence requirement in the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957, invoking Article 16(3).
nb9944c4e6a8.tq: Match the case name with its specific law and judicial outcome rather than with the later Mulki ruling.
xs: In **A.V.S. Narasimha Rao v. State of AP** (**1969**), the SC **struck down the Telangana residence clause** of the **1957** Act — option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ The SC **upheld** the Mulki Rules later, in **October 1972**; the **TRC** was dissolved on **1 Jan 1974**.
xa: Reason: under **Art. 16(3)**, Parliament cannot prescribe a residence condition for **only part** of a State.
⚠ **1969** ruling = **1957** residence law; **1972** ruling = older **Mulki Rules**.
Mulki Rules were repealed in **1973** under the **Six-Point Formula**.

n750f20f1b6e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Supreme Court judgment of October 1972?
o: It permitted non-locals to be barred from public posts in Hyderabad and Telangana.
It concerned the residence clause of the 1957 Public Employment Act.
It immediately contributed to the Jai Andhra Movement.
n750f20f1b6e.x: The 1972 ruling concerned the older Mulki Rules; the 1957 Act's residence clause had been struck down in 1969.
xa: Mulki origin: **1888**, Hyderabad State; outsiders needed the **Diwan's** permission.
**1919 Nizam's Farman**: outsiders needed the **Nizam's personal permission**.
⚠ **1969** = Telangana **for** Mulki rules; **1972** = Andhra **against**.

n45954159138.s: The Mulki Rules were repealed in 1973 under the Six-Point Formula and were replaced by the:
n45954159138.x: The Mulki Rules were repealed in 1973 under the Six-Point Formula and replaced by the zonal system. The Telangana Regional Committee was dissolved on 1 January 1974.
n45954159138.tq: Identify the institutional replacement, not merely the date of repeal.
xs: The Mulki Rules, repealed in **1973** under the Six-Point Formula, were replaced by the **zonal system** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **Presidential Order 1975** set up **6 zones** and **local cadres**.
xa: The **Telangana Regional Committee** was dissolved on **1 Jan 1974**.
**Zones I-III** Coastal Andhra; **Zone IV** Rayalaseema; **Zones V-VI** Telangana.
Constitutional basis: **Art. 371D** (**32nd Amendment**).

naa5f38d6842.s: Who became the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh on 10 December 1973 after the end of President’s Rule?
naa5f38d6842.x: Jalagam Vengala Rao became Chief Minister on 10 December 1973 after President’s Rule ended.
naa5f38d6842.tq: Apply the successor trap to closely connected political figures.
xs: **Jalagam Vengala Rao** became CM on **10 December 1973** after President's Rule — option **(4)** is correct.
**P.V. Narasimha Rao** had resigned on **18 Jan 1973**; **Marri Chenna Reddy** led the **1969** TPS; **A. Madan Mohan** was TPS convener.
xa: President's Rule: **18 Jan 1973 to 10 Dec 1973** (about **11 months**).
It was the **first President's Rule** in AP.
The **Six-Point Formula** was approved on **18 Dec 1973**.

n558b2d8bd76.s: Indira Gandhi announced the Eight-Point Formula on 11 April 1969 during the:
n558b2d8bd76.x: The Eight-Point Formula belongs to the Jai Telangana agitation; the Five-Point Formula of 27 November 1972 belongs to the Jai Andhra phase.
xa: The Five-Point Formula brought **Assistant Surgeons** and **Assistant Engineers** under Mulki rules.
The Eight-Point Formula led to the **Bhargava**, **Lalit** and **Wanchoo** committees.

n3674ebd89e7.s: Who among the following spearheaded the Jai Andhra agitation as a prominent Congress leader?
n3674ebd89e7.x: Kakani Venkataratnam was the prominent Congress leader who spearheaded the Jai Andhra agitation. B.V. Subba Reddy was another Congress leader associated with it.
n3674ebd89e7.tq: Test the leader-role association directly, a common history-paper trap.
xs: **Kakani Venkataratnam**, a prominent Congress leader, **spearheaded** Jai Andhra — option **(2)** is correct.
**Jalagam Vengala Rao** was the CM after President's Rule; **J.M. Girglani** headed the **2001** commission.
xa: **B.V. Subba Reddy**: another Congress leader in the agitation.
**M. Venkaiah Naidu** took part as a **student leader**.
**Students** formed the core of the movement.

n0fe808819b4.s: The President's Rule imposed in Andhra Pradesh on 18 January 1973 is significant because it was
o: the first President's Rule in the State since its formation
imposed under Article 360 for a financial emergency
the second spell of President's Rule after one in 1969
imposed to implement the Eight-Point Formula
n0fe808819b4.x: After P.V. Narasimha Rao resigned on 18 January 1973 amid a breakdown of law and order during Jai Andhra, President's Rule lasted until 10 December 1973 - the first in AP since the State was formed. Article 360 concerns financial emergency; there was no President's Rule in 1969; the Eight-Point Formula (1969) is unrelated.
n0fe808819b4.tq: First PR in AP = 18 Jan 1973 to 10 Dec 1973 (~11 months), Jai Andhra.
xs: President's Rule from **18 January 1973** was the **first in AP since its formation** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was imposed for a **breakdown of law and order** during Jai Andhra — not a financial emergency, and there was none in **1969**.
xa: It lasted till **10 Dec 1973** (about **11 months**).
CM **P.V. Narasimha Rao** resigned the same day.
The **Eight-Point Formula** belongs to **1969** — unrelated.

nf4c5e2d13bb.s: The Six-Point Formula provided for backward-area development through:
o: An Administrative Tribunal with zonal committees
A State Planning Commission with local sub-committees
A Central University with local sub-committees
The Telangana Regional Committee with district committees
nf4c5e2d13bb.x: Backward-area development was to be addressed through a State Planning Commission with local sub-committees.
nf4c5e2d13bb.tq: Distinguish planning institutions from tribunals and regional bodies.
xs: Point 4: backward-area development through a **State Planning Commission with local sub-committees** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **Administrative Tribunal** dealt with service disputes; the **Central University** with education (**Art. 371E**); the **TRC** was **abolished**.
xa: Point 5: local preference in **admissions** → **Central University, Hyderabad**.
Point 6: constitutional amendment → **32nd Amendment**, **Presidential Order 1975**.
Proposed **21 Sep 1973**; approved **18 Dec 1973**.

nb2712f4135e.s: Article 371E, associated with the Six-Point Formula, provides for:
o: Local cadres and six administrative zones
A State Planning Commission for backward areas
