nb2712f4135e.x: Article 371E provides for the establishment of a Central University at Hyderabad. Local cadres and zones are associated with Article 371D.
nb2712f4135e.tq: Separate the closely related constitutional articles 371D and 371E.
xs: **Article 371E** provides for a **Central University** at **Hyderabad** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Local cadres**, **zones** and the **AP Administrative Tribunal** come under **Art. 371D**.
xa: Both were inserted by the **32nd Amendment** (in force **1 July 1974**).
**State Planning Commission** = Six-Point Formula's backward-area body.
Exam angle: which article gave the Central University — **371E**.

n5a86d0eb16b.s: The Jai Andhra agitation of 1972-73 was finally brought to an end by
o: the abolition of the Mulki Rules alone
the Six-Point Formula proposed by the Central Government
the Eight-Point Formula of Indira Gandhi
n5a86d0eb16b.x: Jai Andhra ended with the Six-Point Formula proposed by the Centre on 21 September 1973. Neither repression nor the abolition of the Mulki Rules by itself ended it (the PYQ trap); the Eight-Point Formula belongs to the 1969 Telangana agitation.
n5a86d0eb16b.tq: Jai Andhra ended by = Six-Point Formula (21 Sep 1973), not repression or Mulki abolition.
xs: Jai Andhra was ended by the **Six-Point Formula proposed by the Central Government** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ PYQ trap: **neither repression nor abolition of the Mulki Rules** alone ended it; the **Eight-Point Formula** was for **1969**.
xa: Proposed **21 Sep 1973**; agitation called off **1 Oct 1973**.
It got constitutional backing via the **32nd Amendment** (**Art. 371D, 371E**).
It still governs AP's **local cadres**.

neca7af0ab57.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, existing admission quotas under Article 371D were continued for:
neca7af0ab57.x: The Act continued the existing Article 371D admission quotas for ten years and extended Article 371D to Telangana.
xa: **Part XII** covers amendment of **Articles 371D and 168** (APPSC 2022).
**Art. 168**: Telangana's Legislative Council.
AP's **Public Employment Order-2025** rebuilt the 371D system as **6 zones and 2 multi-zones**.

n1882341b135.s: Articles 371D and 371E relating to Andhra Pradesh were inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
n1882341b135.x: The Thirty-second Amendment of 1973 gave effect to the Six-Point Formula and inserted Articles 371D and 371E.
n1882341b135.tq: Reject the nearby but incorrect 33rd Amendment and recall the exact amendment number.
xs: **Articles 371D and 371E** were inserted by the **32nd Amendment** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes say **33rd** — wrong; **36th** Amendment admitted **Sikkim** under **Article 2**.
xa: It gave effect to the **Six-Point Formula** (APHQ PYQ 2019).
In force **1 July 1974**.
Exam angle: amendment number (**32nd**), President's Rule (**Jan 1973**), **371E** for the Central University.

n6e4a40dd7e1.s: After the reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh in 2014, which zones of the undivided State were retained by Andhra Pradesh for its 13 districts?
n6e4a40dd7e1.x: After 2014, Andhra Pradesh retained Zones I to IV for its 13 districts; Zones V and VI related to the Telangana region.
n6e4a40dd7e1.tq: Test the boundary of the retained range rather than recalling an individual district.
xs: After **2014**, AP kept **Zones I-IV** for its **13 districts** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Zones V and VI** were the **Telangana** zones.
xa: **Zones I-III** = Coastal Andhra; **Zone IV** = Rayalaseema.
New system: **6 zones and 2 multi-zones** (Cabinet, **April 2026**).

o: Introduce the Mulki rules in Hyderabad State
Repatriate non-local employees appointed in violation of the Presidential Order and restore posts to Telangana locals
Create six local zones for the first time
n3fd5873ea0a.x: GO 610 sought to repatriate non-local employees appointed contrary to the 1975 Presidential Order and restore local posts to Telangana candidates.
n3fd5873ea0a.tq: Test the purpose of an executive order through the action it required.
xs: **GO 610** was issued to **repatriate non-local employees** appointed in violation of the **1975 Presidential Order** to their own zones and **restore local posts to Telangana** candidates — option **(2)**.
The **Mulki rules** go back to **1888** in **Hyderabad State**, not to GO 610.
**Six zones** were created by the **Presidential Order, 1975**; the **University at Hyderabad** came from **Art. 371E** (32nd Amendment).
xa: GO 610 was issued on **30 December 1985** by the **N.T. Rama Rao** (TDP) government.
Its **weak implementation** led to the one-man **Girglani Commission** (**2001**, report **2004**).
The **1975 Order** set **Zones V-VI** for Telangana, with **Hyderabad in Zone VI**.

na6d59bed0f7.s: GO 610 (30 December 1985), to repatriate non-locals appointed in violation of the 1975 Presidential Order, was issued by the government of:
na6d59bed0f7.x: GO 610 was issued by the NTR (TDP) government; the Girglani Commission (2001) was set up by the Chandrababu Naidu government.
xa: The Girglani report (**2004**) found large-scale violations, especially in **Zone VI - Hyderabad**.
PYQ order: **Jai Telangana → Jai Andhra → 32nd Amendment → GO 610 → Girglani Report**.

nf582b28fd16.s: The one-man Girglani Commission examined violations of GO 610 and the:
nf582b28fd16.x: J.M. Girglani examined violations of GO 610 and the 1975 Presidential Order, finding many non-local appointments, especially in Zone VI.
xa: Constituted in **2001** by the **Chandrababu Naidu** government; report in **2004**.
**GO 610** was issued on **30 December 1985** by the **N.T. Rama Rao** government.
After **2014**, disputes over Mulki rules and GO 610 complicated the **division of employees** between AP and Telangana.

n830cb9c7631.s: The Telangana Rashtra Samithi was formed in:
n830cb9c7631.x: The TRS was formed in 2001, before the Centre's December 2009 announcement, the Srikrishna report (2010) and the Million March (2011).
xa: **Sakala Janula Samme**, a general strike of about **42 days**, followed in **Sep-Oct 2011**.
The **CWC resolution** for Telangana came in **July 2013**.
The Srikrishna Committee's report (**30 Dec 2010**) gave **six options**.

n870fdef797c.s: The Committee on Telangana (2010), which gave six options in its report, was chaired by:
n870fdef797c.x: Justice B.N. Srikrishna chaired the 2010 Committee, which reported on 30 December 2010 with six options.
xa: The committee studied the **separate-Telangana demand**.
⚠ Srikrishna report = **2010**; **2001** = **TRS** founded by **K. Chandrasekhar Rao**.
The **Million March** (**Mar 2011**) and **Sakala Janula Samme** (**Sep-Oct 2011**) came after the report.

n5b8948425e9.s: Which one of the following was a consequence faced by the residuary State of Andhra Pradesh after reorganisation?
o: It lost Hyderabad and faced revenue deficits.
It became responsible for the entire Telangana public debt.
It acquired all districts of the former State of Hyderabad.
It retained Hyderabad and obtained a revenue surplus.
n5b8948425e9.x: The residuary State of Andhra Pradesh lost Hyderabad, a major revenue-generating centre, and faced revenue deficits after bifurcation.
n5b8948425e9.tq: Apply the territorial and fiscal consequences together rather than treating them as separate facts.
xs: Residual AP **lost Hyderabad** and **faced revenue deficits** — option **(1)**.
**Debt** was split by **population ratio**, so AP did not take all of Telangana's debt; Hyderabad went to Telangana.
xa: AP with **58%** of the population got about **46%** of revenue and power.
AP's loss on tax refunds was about **₹3,900 crore** (**14th FC**).
**Special Category Status** was a PM's assurance in the **Rajya Sabha**, not in the Act.

n3d212e1dea6.s: The 32nd Constitutional Amendment was enacted in:
n3d212e1dea6.x: The order was Jai Telangana (1969), Jai Andhra (1972), 32nd Amendment (1973), GO 610 (1985) and Girglani Report (2004).
xa: The **1975 Presidential Order** on local cadres came between the 32nd Amendment and GO 610.
**GO 610** = **NTR**; **Girglani** = **Chandrababu Naidu**.
The **Srikrishna Committee** report followed in **Dec 2010**.

n0b40688c928.s: The Telangana Praja Samiti merged with the Congress after reaching an agreement with:
n0b40688c928.x: The Telangana Praja Samiti merged with the Congress after an agreement with Indira Gandhi. Those opposing the merger formed the Complete Telangana Praja Samiti under B. Satyanarayana Reddy.
n0b40688c928.tq: Apply the ‘agreement with’ trap by identifying the national leader associated with the merger.
xs: The **TPS merged with the Congress** after an agreement with **Indira Gandhi** — option **(2)** is correct.
Opponents formed the **Complete Telangana Praja Samithi** under **B. Satyanarayana Reddy**.
xa: Merger date: **September 1971** (some notes **Sep 1972**).
TPS had won **10 of the 14** seats it contested in the **1971 Lok Sabha** election.
Indira Gandhi **refused to split** the State; the demand lay dormant until **TRS (2001)**.

n7374396fc8f.s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Six-Point Formula of 1973?
o: Continuation of the Telangana Regional Committee
Local preference in non-gazetted posts and admissions
n7374396fc8f.x: The Six-Point Formula abolished the Telangana Regional Committee. It provided for a Central University at Hyderabad, an Administrative Tribunal and local preference in specified posts and admissions.
n7374396fc8f.tq: Watch for the reversal of an institution that was abolished rather than continued.
xs: **Continuation of the TRC** was **not** a feature — the Six-Point Formula **abolished** it — option **(3)** is the answer.
It did provide an **Administrative Tribunal**, a **Central University** at Hyderabad and **local preference** in non-gazetted posts and admissions.
xa: TRC dissolved on **1 Jan 1974**.
Mulki Rules abolished with the **TRC's consent**.
The formula ended **Jai Andhra** and brought about **two decades** of relative peace.

n41f96fb6a45.s: Who founded the Gorkha National Liberation Front and coined the term 'Gorkhaland'?
n41f96fb6a45.x: Subhash Ghisingh founded the GNLF in 1980 and coined the term 'Gorkhaland'.
xa: **Gorkhaland** is one of the active demands, with **Vidarbha**, **Bodoland** and **Bundelkhand**.
**1988:** **Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council**.
**2011:** **Gorkhaland Territorial Administration** (GTA).

n7c502c0431d.s: The Central University at Hyderabad is associated with Article:
n7c502c0431d.x: The Central University is under Article 371E; Article 371D concerns local cadres and the AP Administrative Tribunal.
xa: Art. 371D: **equitable opportunities** in public employment and education.
Under it, the **Presidential Order 1975** created **6 zones**.
**APRA 2014 Sec 97** extended **Art. 371D** to Telangana.

n3cc3afeb0c4.s: Under Article 371D, service disputes in Andhra Pradesh were placed under:
o: The exclusive jurisdiction of the High Court
n3cc3afeb0c4.x: Article 371D provided an Administrative Tribunal for service disputes, taking them out of the High Court's jurisdiction.
xa: The President acts through a **Presidential Order**.
Inserted by the **32nd Amendment**.

n42346b37ee7.s: Under Article 16(3), residence requirements for public employment can be prescribed by:
n42346b37ee7.x: Article 16(3) empowers only Parliament; Article 371D is a special route for Andhra Pradesh.
xa: Art. 371D works through a **Presidential Order** (**1975**).
⚠ **1969 vs 1972**: residence law struck down vs **Mulki Rules** upheld.

n421618cf224.s: Under the 1975 zonal system of undivided Andhra Pradesh, Hyderabad was included in Zone:
n421618cf224.x: Hyderabad was in Zone VI; Zones I-III were Coastal Andhra, Zone IV Rayalaseema and Zones V-VI Telangana.
xa: Zone V: **Adilabad, Karimnagar, Warangal, Khammam**.
**Girglani** found large violations especially in **Zone VI - Hyderabad**.
The zones came from the **Presidential Order, 1975**.

nefe713ce155.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the broad population ratio used for apportionment of assets and liabilities between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana was:
nefe713ce155.x: The broad population ratio used for apportionment was 58.32:41.68 between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana respectively.
nefe713ce155.tq: Read ratio options in the stated order—Andhra Pradesh first and Telangana second—before comparing the figures.
xs: The population ratio was **58.32 : 41.68** (AP : Telangana), from **Census 2011** — option **(3)**.
It is defined in **Part I** (Preliminary) of the Act.
xa: **Liabilities/debt** are divided by this **population ratio**; **assets** by **location**.
The same ratio was used for the **judges' salaries** of the common High Court.
**Power** was split by the **last 5 years' average consumption**.
**Outcome:** AP with **58%** of population got about **46%** of revenue and power.

n92467ac49ff.s: The President gave assent to the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 on:
n92467ac49ff.x: Assent was given on 1 March 2014; the appointed day, when Telangana was formed, was 2 June 2014.
xa: Lok Sabha / Rajya Sabha passed the Bill on **18 / 20 Feb 2014**.
⚠ Some notes give "in force from **2 March 2014**" — treated as a trap.
The Act has **12 Parts, 108 Sections** and **13 Schedules**.

na4271f1bc6e.s: Which Part of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 deals with the High Court?
na4271f1bc6e.x: Part IV deals with the High Court; Parts III, VI and VIII cover legislatures, assets and liabilities, and services.
xa: **Part V** = Authorisation of Expenditure and Distribution of Revenues; **Part VII** = Certain Corporations.
**Part IX** = Water Resources (**84-91**); **Part X** = Infrastructure and Special Economic Measures.
**Part XI** = Access to higher education; **Part XII** = Legal and miscellaneous.

n18e00e33683.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 consists of
n18e00e33683.x: The Act has 12 Parts, 108 Sections (Section 108 is the removal-of-difficulties clause) and 13 Schedules (the Thirteenth lists the institutions and infrastructure promised to AP). The other combinations alter one or more of these numbers.
xs: The Act has **12 Parts, 108 Sections and 13 Schedules** — option **(1)**.
**Sec. 108** is the **removal of difficulties** clause.
xa: The **Thirteenth Schedule** (Sec. 93) lists central institutions and infrastructure promised to AP.
**Ninth** Schedule = PSUs/corporations; **Tenth** = State institutions; **Eleventh** = irrigation projects; **Twelfth** = coal, oil & gas, power.
**Part II** (Sections **3-11**) is the reorganisation itself.

n115aa55adc2.s: Which Section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 extended Article 371D to Telangana?
n115aa55adc2.x: Section 97 extended Article 371D to Telangana; Section 10 added Telangana as Entry 29 in the First Schedule.
xa: **Sec 5** = Hyderabad **common capital** for up to **10 years**; **Sec 7** = **Common Governor**.
**Sec 90** = **Polavaram** a **national project**.
**Sec 94** = fiscal support, special development package and **Central support for the new capital**.

n97d621de1f2.s: The Apex Council and the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards are provided for under which sections of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
n97d621de1f2.x: Sections 84 and 85 provide for the Apex Council and the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards respectively.
n97d621de1f2.tq: Use paired-number recall for consecutive statutory provisions dealing with related water-management institutions.
xs: The **Apex Council** and the **Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards** are under **Sections 84-85** — option **(4)**.
**Sec 90** = Polavaram; **Sec 94** = fiscal support; **Sec 95** = higher education; **Sec 97** = Art. 371D extended.
xa: Part IX (Water Resources) covers Sections **84-91**.
The **Apex Council** is chaired by the **Union Water Resources Minister** with both CMs.
**Krishna and Godavari** are the most contentious rivers (**APPSC 2025**).

n16b32aa8b21.s: Which Section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 made Hyderabad the common capital?
n16b32aa8b21.x: Section 5 dealt with Hyderabad as common capital; Section 3 formed Telangana, Section 6 the capital expert committee and Section 8 the Governor's security role.
xa: ⚠ **Sec 3** = **10 districts** in one note, **9 districts** in another.
**Sec 7** = **Common Governor**; **Sec 10** = Telangana as entry **29**.
The Sec 6 committee was chaired by **K.C. Sivaramakrishnan** (report **Aug 2014**).

n37e90d2eb85.s: Under Section 5 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, Hyderabad was to be the common capital for a period not exceeding:
n37e90d2eb85.x: Section 5 made Hyderabad the common capital for not more than ten years.
xa: The **AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026** amends **Section 5** → **Amaravati** sole, permanent capital, **with effect from 2 June 2024**.
It followed the AP Assembly resolution of **28 Mar 2026**.
**Amaravati** was chosen in **2015** (~**33,000 acres** land pooling).

ncb9be3d84f1.s: Provisions for IIT, NIT, IIM, AIIMS and a new railway zone for Andhra Pradesh are in which Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
ncb9be3d84f1.x: The Thirteenth Schedule lists these institutions, central and tribal universities and infrastructure such as a railway zone, steel plant, port and metros.
xa: The railway zone is now **South Coast Railway** — **18th zone**, HQ **Visakhapatnam**.
**Sec 94** separately gives **Central support for the new capital** and a backward-area package.
**Ninth** Schedule = PSUs; **Tenth** = State institutions.

n4c966bcb142.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, liabilities and debt are apportioned according to:
n4c966bcb142.x: Liabilities and refunds go by population ratio, assets by location and tax arrears by place of assessment.
xa: **Power** was split by the **average consumption of the previous five years**.
AP's loss on refunds: about **₹3,900 crore** (**14th FC**).
Schedule IX companies (**Sec 53**): units by location, HQ by population ratio.

n5d9a77f68cb.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 made Amaravati the sole, permanent capital with effect from:
n5d9a77f68cb.x: It took effect from 2 June 2024, when Hyderabad's 10-year common-capital term ended, not 2 June 2014.
xa: Original **Sec 5**: Hyderabad common capital for **not more than 10 years**; that period ended in **June 2024**.
**Amaravati** was chosen in **2015** (~**33,000 acres** land pooling).
The **AP High Court** (order of **3 March 2022**) struck down the **CRDA Repeal Act** and upheld Amaravati as the only legal capital.

na05e7eb4bb9.s: After the 2019 reorganisation, which Union Territory was provided no legislature?
na05e7eb4bb9.x: Ladakh has no legislature, while the UT of Jammu and Kashmir has a Legislative Assembly.
xa: The two UTs exist from **31 October 2019**.
Judiciary: a common **High Court of J&K and Ladakh**.
All constitutional amendments apply w.e.f. **5 Aug 2019**.

nd1b3b31ae52.s: The South Coast Railway, operational from 1 June 2026, has its headquarters at:
nd1b3b31ae52.x: South Coast Railway became operational on 1 June 2026 as India's 18th railway zone, with headquarters at Visakhapatnam.
nd1b3b31ae52.tq: Separate the headquarters from the listed divisions, which include Guntakal, Guntur, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam.
xs: **South Coast Railway** has its HQ at **Visakhapatnam** — option **(4)**.
**Vijayawada**, **Guntur** and **Guntakal** are its **divisions** (with Visakhapatnam).
xa: It became fully operational as the **18th zone** from **1 June 2026**.
It was promised in the **APRA** (**13th Schedule**).
The 13th Schedule also promised a **steel plant**, **port** and **metros**.

n69ad4d8dfd4.s: Hyderabad's period as the joint capital of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana ended in:
n69ad4d8dfd4.x: The ten-year joint-capital period of Hyderabad ended in June 2024.
n69ad4d8dfd4.tq: Distinguish the fixed duration from the date on which the period actually ended.
xs: Hyderabad's **10-year** joint-capital period ended in **June 2024** — option **(4)**.
**Sec 5** made Hyderabad the common capital for **not more than 10 years** from **2 June 2014**.
xa: The **2026 Amendment Act** made **Amaravati** sole capital **with effect from 2 June 2024**.
**Sec 8** gave the Governor **special responsibility** in the common capital.
**Amaravati** was chosen in **2015**.

nbe48201e624.s: The number of districts in Andhra Pradesh changed in which of the following sequence between 2014 and 2025?
nbe48201e624.x: Andhra Pradesh had 13 districts in 2014, 26 in 2022 and 28 in 2025.
nbe48201e624.tq: Arrange successive administrative changes in their time sequence.
xs: The new districts in **2025**: **Polavaram** and **Markapuram**.
xa: After **2014**, AP kept **Zones I-IV** for its **13 districts**.
Current local-cadre system: **6 zones and 2 multi-zones** (**AP Public Employment Order-2025**).
AP area: **1,60,205 sq km**; coastline **974 km**.

n0cfe216f826.s: How many Assembly seats were initially allocated to Telangana under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
n0cfe216f826.x: Telangana got 119 seats and Andhra Pradesh 175; 225 and 153 are the proposed future increases under Section 26.
xa: Lok Sabha: AP **25**, Telangana **17**; Rajya Sabha: AP **11**, Telangana **7**.
Legislative Council: AP **58**, Telangana **40**.
**Art. 168** was amended for the **Telangana Council**.

ne95f61c48b8.s: Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh was an assurance given by the Prime Minister in the:
ne95f61c48b8.x: It was an assurance given by the Prime Minister in the Rajya Sabha and was not a provision of the Reorganisation Act.
xa: The **Polavaram Ordinance, 2014** dealt with transfer of Khammam villages, not SCS.
The **Srikrishna Committee** (Dec 2010) gave **six options** on Telangana.
**Sec 94** of the Act gives tax incentives and a **special development package** for backward areas.

ne72a626013b.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 was enacted primarily under which Article of the Constitution of India?
ne72a626013b.x: The Act was enacted under Article 3, which empowers Parliament to form a new State out of an existing State. Article 2 deals with admission or establishment of new States.
ne72a626013b.tq: Distinguish the closely related constitutional provisions rather than relying on the subject of the legislation alone.
xs: APRA 2014 was enacted under **Article 3** — option **(1)**.
With **Arts. 3 and 4**, **no Art. 368 amendment** was needed.
⚠ **Article 2** deals with admitting new states/territory from outside — a common wrong answer.
xa: President's assent: **1 March 2014**; appointed day **2 June 2014**.
Telangana became the **29th state**.
Structure: **12 Parts, 108 Sections, 13 Schedules**.

n7fff76aed53.s: Who were the Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh during the 1969 Telangana agitation and the 1972 Jai Andhra agitation respectively?
o: P.V. Narasimha Rao and Kasu Brahmananda Reddy
Kasu Brahmananda Reddy and P.V. Narasimha Rao
Kasu Brahmananda Reddy and Jalagam Vengala Rao
Marri Channa Reddy and P.V. Narasimha Rao
n7fff76aed53.x: Kasu Brahmananda Reddy was CM in 1969 and was forced to resign by the agitation; P.V. Narasimha Rao was sworn in on 30 September 1971 and was CM during Jai Andhra. Option A reverses them; Jalagam Vengala Rao became CM only on 10 December 1973; Marri Channa Reddy led the TPS and was not CM in 1969.
n7fff76aed53.tq: 1969 = Brahmananda Reddy; 1972 Jai Andhra = PVN; after PR (Dec 1973) = Vengala Rao.
xs: CMs: **Kasu Brahmananda Reddy** (**1969**) and **P.V. Narasimha Rao** (**1972** Jai Andhra) — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses them; **Jalagam Vengala Rao** became CM only on **10 Dec 1973**; **Marri Channa Reddy** led the TPS.
xa: P.V. Narasimha Rao: CLP leader **25 Sep 1971**, sworn in **30 Sep 1971**.
He **resigned on 18 Jan 1973** → **President's Rule**.
Brahmananda Reddy was forced to **resign** by the 1969 agitation.

n0e143d4b29b.s: During the Jai Andhra Movement, protesters hoisted a separate Andhra State flag on:
n0e143d4b29b.x: The flag was hoisted on 10 December 1972, after the October 1972 Supreme Court judgment upholding the Mulki Rules.
xa: Demand: **repeal of the Mulki Rules** or a **separate Andhra State**.
Grievance: Andhra people treated as "**outsiders**" in **Hyderabad**.
⚠ **10 Dec** twice: flag **10 Dec 1972**; President's Rule ended **10 Dec 1973**.

nc096a3c9b75.s: The provisions relating to amendments of Articles 168 and 371D of the Constitution are contained in:
nc096a3c9b75.x: Part XII contains legal and miscellaneous provisions and amends Articles 168 and 371D.
nc096a3c9b75.tq: Match the constitutional amendment with the appropriate concluding Part of the Act.
xs: Amendments of **Articles 168 and 371D** are in **Part XII** (Legal and miscellaneous) — option **(4)** (**APPSC 2022** key).
**Part IX** = Water Resources; **Part X** = Infrastructure and Special Economic Measures; **Part XI** = Access to higher education.
xa: Part XII also holds **Sec. 108** — removal of difficulties.
**Art. 168** change concerns the **Telangana Legislative Council**.
**Sec 97** extended **Art. 371D** to Telangana.

n2ce6b07db0c.s: Which Part of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 deals with the formation of Telangana, the common capital and the common Governor?
n2ce6b07db0c.x: Part II (Sections 3-11) covers the reorganisation itself; Part I is preliminary, Part VI deals with assets and liabilities and Part XII with legal and miscellaneous provisions.
xa: **Sec 3** = formation of Telangana; **Sec 5** = Hyderabad common capital up to **10 years**.
**Sec 6** = Expert Committee on new capital; **Sec 7** = **Common Governor**.
**Sec 8** = Governor's **special responsibility** in the common capital.

n37cdefa0ab8.s: The Polavaram project, proposed by Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy, was originally known as:
n37cdefa0ab8.x: The original name was Ramapada Sagaram, proposed by Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy.
xa: **Sec 90** declared **Polavaram** a **national project**.
The **Polavaram Ordinance, 2014** moved **seven mandals** of **Khammam** to AP.
**Polavaram** is one of AP's new districts in the **2025** count (with **Markapuram**).

n04a79156d51.s: Which slogan was associated with the Naxalbari uprising?
n04a79156d51.x: “Land to the tiller” was the slogan associated with the Naxalbari peasant uprising.
n04a79156d51.tq: Recall the movement-specific slogan rather than a general nationalist slogan.
xs: The slogan of the Naxalbari uprising was "**Land to the tiller**" — option **(3)** is correct.
Its related line "**Ballot to Bullet**" rejected the **CPI(M)'s parliamentary path**, so "Inquilab through elections" is the opposite of its stand.
xa: Causes of Naxalbari: **land concentration**, **failed land reforms** (zamindari abolition, ceilings, tenancy) and **exploitation of tribals**.
The movement later put **land to the tiller** and **tribal land alienation** at the centre of AP politics.
Naxalbari: **Siliguri** sub-division, **Darjeeling**, **West Bengal**, **March-May 1967**.

neb0fbae85e0.s: The Naxalbari peasant uprising of March-May 1967 was led by
o: Tarimela Nagi Reddy and Chandra Pulla Reddy
neb0fbae85e0.x: Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal led the Naxalbari uprising in Darjeeling district. Nagi Reddy, Pulla Reddy, Venkaiah and Patnaik led the 1967 Andhra extremist wing; Kondapalli Seetharamaiah founded the PWG in 1980; Vempatapu Satyam is linked with Srikakulam.
xs: The Naxalbari uprising (**March-May 1967**) was led by **Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Tarimela Nagi Reddy**, **Chandra Pulla Reddy**, **Kolla Venkaiah** and **Nagabhushana Patnaik** led the **AP extremist CPI(ML) wing** (1967 split).
**Kondapalli Seetharamaiah** founded the **PWG** in **1980**.
xa: **Kanu Sanyal** with **Tarimela Nagi Reddy** also spread the **Srikakulam** struggle.
⚠ Some notes misprint Kanu Sanyal as "**Kasu Sanyal**".
Charu Majumdar went on to found the **CPI(ML)** in **1969**.

n9a696b4ad79.s: The Srikakulam Girijan struggle is generally placed in the period:
n9a696b4ad79.x: The Srikakulam Girijan struggle is generally dated to 1968–70, although 1968–69 is also used in some references.
n9a696b4ad79.tq: Distinguish the standard period from nearby movement and Emergency dates.
xs: The Srikakulam Girijan struggle is placed in **1968-70** — option **(4)** is correct (PYQ key).
⚠ Some notes give **1968-69**; **1975-77** is the **Emergency**, when Naxalite cadres were killed in alleged encounters.
xa: It took place in the **Srikakulam Agency** against landlords, moneylenders and forest officials.
Tribes involved: **Savaras (Soras)** and **Jatapus**.
It began under the **CPI(M)** and shifted to the **CPI(ML)** in **1969**.

nc96f8d76539.s: Which of the following tribal communities were associated with the Srikakulam Girijan struggle?
nc96f8d76539.x: The principal tribal communities associated with the struggle were the Savaras, also called Soras, and the Jatapus.
nc96f8d76539.tq: Discriminate between the named Srikakulam tribes and other tribal groups of India.
xs: The tribes of the Srikakulam struggle were the **Savara (Sora) and Jatapu** — option **(3)** is correct.
The notes name only these two tribes for Srikakulam.
xa: The struggle was in the **Srikakulam Agency**, **1968-70**.
Leaders who spread it: **Kanu Sanyal** and **Tarimela Nagi Reddy**.
Target: **landlords, moneylenders and forest officials**.

n0f6a89fadd8.s: The expression “Ballot to Bullet” indicated the rejection of:
o: The Chinese model of guerrilla warfare
n0f6a89fadd8.x: The “Ballot to Bullet” line rejected the CPI(M)’s parliamentary path and favoured armed revolutionary struggle.
n0f6a89fadd8.tq: Distinguish the rejected parliamentary route from the alternative guerrilla strategy.
xs: "**Ballot to Bullet**" rejected the **CPI(M)'s parliamentary path** — option **(1)** is correct.
The movement in fact embraced the **Chinese-model protracted guerrilla war** and **land redistribution** ("Land to the tiller"), so options (2) and (4) are wrong.
xa: The **CPI(ML)** was formed in **1969** and saw the Indian state as **semi-feudal**.
Its founder was **Charu Majumdar** (with **Kanu Sanyal**), based in **West Bengal**.
⚠ **Srikakulam** began under the **CPI(M)** and shifted to the **CPI(ML)** in **1969**.

na39f3456150.s: The People's War Group (PWG) was banned in Andhra Pradesh in:
na39f3456150.x: The PWG was banned in Andhra Pradesh in 1992.
na39f3456150.tq: Fix the year by distinguishing the ban from the formation and policing milestones.
xs: The **PWG was banned** in Andhra Pradesh in **1992** — option **(2)** is correct.
**1989** = Greyhounds raised; **1996** = start of H.J. Dora's term as DGP; **2004** = Hyderabad peace talks / CPI (Maoist).
xa: The PWG was founded by **Kondapalli Seetharamaiah** in **1980**.
PWG merged with MCC to form the **CPI (Maoist)** in **2004**.
Peace talks: **October 2004**, Hyderabad, **YSR** government.

n9b745421f30.s: The Revolutionary Writers’ Association, popularly known as Virasam, was founded on:
n9b745421f30.x: Virasam was founded on 4 July 1970 in Hyderabad.
n9b745421f30.tq: Distinguish the founding date from the February 1970 pamphlet episode and later cultural organisations.
xs: **Virasam** was founded on **4 July 1970** in **Hyderabad** — option **(4)** is correct.
**1-2 Feb 1970** was **Sri Sri's 60th-birthday** celebration at **Vizag**, where the seed pamphlet was distributed — not the founding.
xa: The pamphlet challenging writers was distributed by **Andhra University** students.
Founding president: **Sri Sri**; vice-presidents: **Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao** and **Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry**.
First meeting: **Khammam (1970)**; first revolutionary poetry collection: **Jhamjha (1970)**.

nc4e1da80c33.s: Who were the founding vice-presidents of Virasam?
o: Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry
Sri Sri and Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao
nc4e1da80c33.x: Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry were the founding vice-presidents; Sri Sri was president.
xa: Virasam was founded on **4 July 1970**, **Hyderabad**.
Seed: pamphlet at **Sri Sri's 60th-birthday** celebrations (**1-2 Feb 1970, Vizag**).
First meeting at **Khammam (1970)**.

nf86b15b7d68.s: The first meeting of Virasam was held in 1970 at:
nf86b15b7d68.x: The first Virasam meeting was held at Khammam in 1970.
xa: Virasam: founded **4 July 1970**, **Hyderabad**; president **Sri Sri**.
Vice-presidents: **Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao** and **Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry**.
Seed pamphlet by **Andhra University** students at Sri Sri's **60th-birthday** (Vizag).

ne280c9c2adc.s: Who was the founding president of the Revolutionary Writers' Association (Virasam), formed in Hyderabad on 4 July 1970?
ne280c9c2adc.x: Sri Sri was Virasam's founding president; the seed was a pamphlet handed out by Andhra University students at his 60th-birthday celebrations in Vizag in 1970. Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry were vice-presidents; Gaddar was with Art Lovers / Jana Natya Mandali.
ne280c9c2adc.tq: Virasam: president Sri Sri; VPs KoKu + Ravi Sastry; JNM = Gaddar.
xs: **Sri Sri** was Virasam's founding president — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao** and **Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry** were vice-presidents; **Gaddar** co-founded **Art Lovers** (later Jana Natya Mandali).
xa: The seed was a pamphlet distributed by **Andhra University** students at **Sri Sri's 60th-birthday** celebrations (**1-2 Feb 1970, Vizag**).
First meeting: **Khammam (1970)**; first collection: **Jhamjha (1970)**.
Through Virasam and **Jana Natya Mandali**, Srikakulam reshaped **Telugu literature**.

n76179c5a70f.s: Besides Virasam, the Srikakulam movement reshaped Telugu culture through which troupe?
n76179c5a70f.x: Srikakulam made AP a core base of Indian Maoism and influenced Telugu literature through Virasam and Jana Natya Mandali.
xa: **Virasam** was founded on **4 July 1970**, Hyderabad; president **Sri Sri**.
**Art Lovers (1970)** → **Jana Natya Mandali (1971)** (B. Narsinga Rao and Gaddar).
AP angle: the **Greyhounds** base at **Anandapuram** secures the **ASR** and **Parvathipuram Manyam** LWE corridor.

n2a3968b8e97.x: The CPI(ML) was formed in 1969, viewed India as semi-feudal and followed the Chinese-model protracted guerrilla war.
xa: CPI(ML) founder: **Charu Majumdar** (with **Kanu Sanyal**); base **West Bengal**.
The **AP extremist CPI(ML) wing** (1967 split) was led by **Tarimela Nagi Reddy**, Chandra Pulla Reddy, Kolla Venkaiah and Nagabhushana Patnaik.
**People's War Group (PWG)**: **Kondapalli Seetharamaiah**, **1980**; **CPI (Maoist)**: PWG-MCC merger, **2004**.

n65bb3803573.s: Integrated Tribal Development Agencies (ITDAs) were set up under the Tribal Sub-Plan from:
n65bb3803573.x: ITDAs were set up under the Tribal Sub-Plan from the Fifth Plan, beginning in 1974–75.
n65bb3803573.tq: Link the institutional arrangement with the correct Five-Year Plan and starting year.
xs: **ITDAs** were set up under the **Tribal Sub-Plan** from the **Fifth Plan (1974-75)** — option **(3)** is correct.
ITDA = **Integrated Tribal Development Agency**, for tribal development.
xa: **AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation** was tightened in **1970** (**Regulation 1 of 1970**) to stop tribal land passing to non-tribals.
**Girijan Cooperative Corporation (GCC)**, **Visakhapatnam**, procures minor forest produce and supplies essentials.
These measures followed the movement putting **tribal land alienation** at the centre of politics.

n92b35055b6c.s: The AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation was tightened in 1970 (Regulation 1 of 1970) mainly to
o: stop land in Scheduled Areas passing from tribals to non-tribals
set up Integrated Tribal Development Agencies
allow procurement of minor forest produce by the GCC
abolish zamindari in the Srikakulam Agency
n92b35055b6c.x: Regulation 1 of 1970, a response to the tribal unrest, barred transfer of land in Scheduled Areas from tribals to non-tribals. ITDAs came under the Tribal Sub-Plan from the Fifth Plan (1974-75); minor forest produce procurement is the Girijan Cooperative Corporation's work; zamindari abolition was not the Regulation's purpose.
n92b35055b6c.tq: Regulation 1 of 1970 = no tribal-to-non-tribal land transfer (LTR).
xs: **Regulation 1 of 1970** was meant to **stop land in Scheduled Areas passing from tribals to non-tribals** — option **(1)** is correct.
**ITDAs** came under the Tribal Sub-Plan from the **Fifth Plan (1974-75)**; procuring minor forest produce is the **GCC's** work.
xa: The **GCC** is at **Visakhapatnam** and frees tribals from moneylenders.
The movement made **tribal land alienation** a central political issue.
Srikakulam tribes: **Savaras (Soras)** and **Jatapus**.

ne59c05c6300.s: The Greyhounds, raised in 1989, is an elite anti-Naxal force of the:
ne59c05c6300.x: Greyhounds is an elite anti-Naxal special police force of the Andhra Pradesh Police, raised in 1989.
xa: Under DGP **H.J. Dora** (**1996-2002**) it neutralised top Naxalite leaders; **over 1,200 cadres** surrendered (**1998-2001**).
Post-bifurcation **Greyhounds Training Centre**: **Anandapuram** (near Visakhapatnam), under **Sec. 9** of the AP Reorganisation Act, **2014**.
The **PWG was banned** in AP in **1992**.

nb2d7c959009.s: Government–Maoist peace talks were held in Hyderabad in October 2004 during the tenure of which government?
nb2d7c959009.x: Government–Maoist talks were held in Hyderabad in October 2004 during the YSR government.
nb2d7c959009.tq: Match the event, place, month and government rather than relying on the year alone.
xs: Government-Maoist peace talks in Hyderabad in **October 2004** were held under the **YSR government** — option **(3)** is correct.
2004 was also the year the **CPI (Maoist)** formed from the **PWG-MCC** merger.
xa: The **PWG was banned** in AP in **1992**.
Earlier, under DGP **H.J. Dora** (**1996-2002**), **over 1,200 cadres** surrendered (**1998-2001**).
National toolkit includes **rehabilitation** for surrendering cadres + **dialogue**.

nd6eb524ff4d.s: The Bhargava Commission was set up in 1977 to inquire into:
o: The reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh districts
Alleged encounter killings of Naxalite cadres in Andhra Pradesh
The procurement activities of the Girijan Cooperative Corporation
nd6eb524ff4d.x: The Bhargava Commission, headed by Justice Vashist Bhargava, was set up in 1977 to inquire into alleged encounter killings during the Emergency.
nd6eb524ff4d.tq: Match the commission with its subject of inquiry and its historical context.
xs: The **Bhargava Commission (1977)** inquired into **alleged encounter killings of Naxalite cadres in Andhra Pradesh** — option **(2)** is correct.
The killings took place during the **Emergency (1975-77)**.
xa: It was headed by **Justice Vashist Bhargava**.
The **CPI(ML)** was formed in **1969**, under **Charu Majumdar**.
The **GCC** (Visakhapatnam) procures minor forest produce — unrelated to the commission.

nf0df4eff353.s: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation, headquartered at Visakhapatnam, primarily:
o: Procures minor forest produce and supplies essentials to tribals
nf0df4eff353.x: The GCC procures minor forest produce and supplies essential goods, freeing tribals from moneylenders.
xa: **ITDAs** came under the **Tribal Sub-Plan** from the **Fifth Plan (1974-75)**.
**Regulation 1 of 1970** tightened the AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation.
Srikakulam was directed against **landlords, moneylenders and forest officials**.

n046608c63a2.s: Kaka Kalelkar is known for chairing the:
n046608c63a2.x: Kaka Kalelkar chaired the First National Backward Class Commission; he is not a figure of modern Dalit assertion in AP.
xa: **Katti Padmarao** founded the **AP Dalit Mahasabha** (**1985**).
**Bojja Tarakam** was also a founder of the AP Dalit Mahasabha.
The **MRPS** is named among the bodies of caste assertion that reshaped AP politics.

n0ff97d5c6bb.s: Who founded the Andhra Pradesh Dalit Mahasabha in 1985, after Karamchedu?
n0ff97d5c6bb.x: Katti Padmarao is identified as its founder, with Bojja Tarakam also recognised as a founder.
xa: It was founded in **1985**, after the **Karamchedu** massacre (**Prakasam**).
Precursors: **Bhagya Reddy Varma** (Machilipatnam, **1919**) and **Kusuma Dharmanna** (Vizianagaram, **1936**).
AP's Adi-Andhra leaders were inspired by Phule's **Satyashodhak Samaj (1873)** and Periyar's **Self-Respect Movement**.

nf48c0558b15.s: Kusuma Dharmanna's Adi-Andhra Mahasabha of 1936 was held at:
nf48c0558b15.x: The 1936 Mahasabha was at Vizianagaram; Bhagya Reddy Varma's 1919 conference was at Machilipatnam.
xa: The **1919 Machilipatnam** conference demanded abolition of the **Jogini and Devadasi** systems.
⚠ **1936** = Kusuma Dharmanna (Vizianagaram) **and** the **All India Kisan Sabha**.
These two Adi-Andhra bodies are the **precursors** of the AP Dalit Mahasabha (**1985**).

ndadd9b9cf7b.s: The principal objective of Bhu Poratam was to occupy and distribute which land to the landless?
ndadd9b9cf7b.x: Bhu Poratam sought the occupation and distribution of government and surplus land to landless people.
ndadd9b9cf7b.tq: Identify the precise scope of land targeted by the campaign.
xs: Bhu Poratam aimed to occupy and distribute **government and surplus land** to the landless — option **(1)** is correct.
The notes name no forest, temple or private land as its target.
xa: Launched jointly by the **CPI and CPI(M)** in **2007**.
It continued the Communist **tenancy and land campaigns of 1956-69**.
The **AIKS** (founded **1936**) was one of the mass organisations the CPI worked through.

nb43aab9454d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about N.G. Ranga and the peasant movement?
o: Ranga founded the Indian Peasants' Institute in 1933.
The Institute was located at Nidubrolu.
Ranga was a founder of the All India Kisan Sabha in 1936.
The All India Kisan Sabha was a mass organisation of the Congress.
nb43aab9454d.x: The AIKS was a mass organisation of the CPI, not the Congress.
xa: ⚠ **1933** = Nidubrolu institute; **1936** = Kisan Sabha — both **N.G. Ranga**.
**1936** was also the year of **Kusuma Dharmanna's** Adi-Andhra Mahasabha at **Vizianagaram**.
N.G. Ranga is described as a **peasant leader**.

n561ae071d85.s: The power tariff agitation of 2000 was directed against which issue?
o: Auction of arrack shops under prohibition policy
Hikes in electricity tariffs under power-sector reforms
n561ae071d85.x: Left parties and farmers protested electricity tariff hikes introduced under power-sector reforms during the 2000 agitation.
n561ae071d85.tq: Connect the agitation with the policy issue that triggered it.
xs: The **2000** power tariff agitation was against **hikes in electricity tariffs under power-sector reforms** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was led by **Left parties + farmers** in **Hyderabad**.
xa: Police opened fire at **Bashir Bagh, Hyderabad**, on **28 Aug 2000**.
Another Left-led campaign was **Bhu Poratam** (**CPI and CPI(M)**, **2007**).
Arrack auctions were the target of the separate **anti-arrack movement** (**1991**).

nfc3f9ae525c.s: The anti-arrack movement in Andhra Pradesh began in 1991 at which place?
nfc3f9ae525c.x: The movement began in 1991 at Dubagunta village in Nellore district.
xs: The anti-arrack movement began in **1991** at **Dubagunta village in Nellore district** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Nidubrolu** is linked with **N.G. Ranga's** Indian Peasants' Institute (**1933**); **Chunduru** is the **1991** massacre site in **Guntur**.
xa: Leader: **Vardhineni Rosamma**, with rural women.
It grew out of **"Aksharajyothi"** adult-literacy classes.
1930s precursor: **Kallur Subbarao's** anti-liquor and Swadeshi movements in the **Dattamandalas** (**Rayalaseema**).

nd033be2754b.s: The Anti-arrack movement is regarded as one of India’s most successful movements led by which group?
nd033be2754b.x: The anti-arrack movement began in Dubagunta (Nellore) in 1991, led by rural women from the Aksharajyothi literacy classes, and is regarded as one of India's most successful women-led movements.
nd033be2754b.tq: Match the movement’s significance with its principal social constituency.
xs: The anti-arrack movement was led by **rural women** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is regarded as one of India's most successful **women-led movements**.
xa: The women came from **Aksharajyothi** adult-literacy classes.
Their methods: **broomsticks and chilli powder** to close shops and stop auctions.
Leader: **Vardhineni Rosamma** of **Dubagunta**, **Nellore**.

n00fca9b1656.s: The anti-arrack agitation of 1991 emerged primarily from discussions held in which programme?
o: Workers' education classes under the Kisan Sabha
n00fca9b1656.x: Women discussed the effects of men's arrack drinking during Aksharajyothi adult-literacy classes, which helped initiate the agitation.
n00fca9b1656.tq: Identify the immediate institutional origin of a movement.
xs: The agitation grew out of **"Aksharajyothi"** **adult-literacy classes** — option **(1)** is correct.
The lessons led women to discuss men's **arrack drinking**, **debt**, **domestic violence** and men missing work.
xa: Origin: **1991**, **Dubagunta**, **Nellore**.
Methods: women closed arrack shops and stopped auctions using **broomsticks and chilli powder**.
Outcome: **arrack prohibited** in AP on **1 Oct 1993**.

n941bfcd4bdb.s: The Karamchedu massacre of Dalits took place in which district?
n941bfcd4bdb.x: The Karamchedu massacre occurred in Prakasam district on 17 July 1985.
xs: The **Karamchedu** massacre of Dalits took place in **Prakasam** district — option **(4)** is correct.
It is dated **17 July 1985** (one source says **1982**).
**Guntur** is the district of the **Chunduru** massacre (**6 Aug 1991**); **Nellore** is linked with the anti-arrack movement.
xa: After Karamchedu, Dalits broke away from the **Congress and Communist parties** and formed **independent Dalit Mahasabhas**.
The **AP Dalit Mahasabha** was founded in **1985** by **Katti Padmarao** (Bojja Tarakam also a founder).
⚠ **Karamchedu** = **Prakasam**, 1985; **Chunduru** = **Guntur**, 1991.

n4ae2f5182a1.s: The Chunduru massacre occurred on 6 August 1991 in which district?
n4ae2f5182a1.x: The Chunduru massacre occurred on 6 August 1991 in Guntur district.
n4ae2f5182a1.tq: Combine the date with the correct district to avoid event-location reversal.
xs: The **Chunduru** massacre (**6 Aug 1991**) occurred in **Guntur** district — option **(3)** is correct.
**Prakasam** is the district of the **Karamchedu** massacre (**17 July 1985**).
xa: ⚠ **Karamchedu** = **Prakasam**, 1985; **Chunduru** = **Guntur**, 1991.
1991 was also the year the **anti-arrack movement** began at **Dubagunta**, **Nellore**.
Leaders of modern Dalit assertion include **Katti Padmarao**, **Gaddar**, **Manda Krishna Madiga** and **Jupudi Prabhakar Rao**.

nfabed0e711e.s: The first Andhra Pradesh Backward Class Commission, which grouped BCs into A–D categories, was the:
nfabed0e711e.x: The Anantharaman Commission (1968–70) was the first AP Backward Class Commission and grouped BCs into A–D categories.
xa: ⚠ FIRST AP BC Commission = **Anantharaman**, not Muralidhar Rao.
Muralidhar Rao combined BC, ST and religious-group populations as **29.08%**, leading to a big rise in the reservation quota.
**86 castes** are recognised as BCs in Andhra; Telangana has a separate list.

nc34e4948c03.s: Which of the following developments followed the Karamchedu incident?
o: Dalits formed independent Dalit Mahasabhas after breaking away from Congress and Communist parties.
Total prohibition was imposed across Andhra Pradesh.
The Mandal Commission was immediately constituted.
The MRPS was founded at Eedumudi.
nc34e4948c03.x: After Karamchedu, Dalits broke away from the Congress and Communist parties and formed independent Dalit Mahasabhas.
nc34e4948c03.tq: Identify the political consequence directly linked to the event.
xs: After Karamchedu, **Dalits broke away from the Congress and Communist parties** and **formed independent Dalit Mahasabhas** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Total prohibition** came only in **1995**, after the anti-arrack movement — not a result of Karamchedu.
xa: Karamchedu: **Prakasam** district, **17 July 1985**.
The **AP Dalit Mahasabha** (**1985**) was founded by **Katti Padmarao**; **Bojja Tarakam** was also a founder.
Precursors: **Bhagya Reddy Varma's** Adi-Andhra conference (**1919**) and **Kusuma Dharmanna's** Adi-Andhra Mahasabha (**1936**).

nd289ea99631.s: Which pair of movements influenced the Adi-Andhra leaders in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Bhu Poratam and Power Tariff Agitation
nd289ea99631.x: Phule’s Satyashodhak Samaj, founded in 1873, and Periyar’s Self-Respect Movement influenced the Adi-Andhra leaders.
nd289ea99631.tq: Match the ideological influences with the social movement they inspired.
xs: Phule's **Satyashodhak Samaj** (**1873**) and Periyar's **Self-Respect Movement** inspired AP's Adi-Andhra leaders — option **(1)** is correct.
**Bhu Poratam** (**2007**) and the **power tariff agitation** (**2000**) came long after the Adi-Andhra bodies.
xa: The **200th birth anniversary of Jyotirao Phule** was commemorated on **11 April 2026**.
Adi-Andhra leaders: **Bhagya Reddy Varma** (Machilipatnam, **1919**) and **Kusuma Dharmanna** (Vizianagaram, **1936**).
These bodies were the **precursors** of the Dalit movement.

n260f6240bc5.s: Which function was associated with the Muralidhar Rao Commission?
o: It introduced the A–B–C–D categorisation of Scheduled Castes.
It examined whether minorities were included in the Backward Class list.
It imposed prohibition throughout Andhra Pradesh.
It conducted the first national survey of OBC population.
n260f6240bc5.x: The Muralidhar Rao Commission examined whether minorities were included in the Backward Class list.
n260f6240bc5.tq: Match the commission with its precise terms of reference.
xs: The **Muralidhar Rao Commission** **examined whether minorities were included in the Backward Class list** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **A-D** grouping of BCs was the **Anantharaman Commission's** work (the first AP BC Commission, **1968-70**).
xa: Muralidhar Rao took charge on **27 Jan 1982**.
It combined BC, ST and religious-group populations as **29.08%**.
Its report led to a big rise in the State's **reservation quota**.

n16c767adba2.s: The Progressive Organisation of Women (POW) was founded in:
n16c767adba2.x: POW was founded in 1974; the Stree Shakti Sanghatana followed in 1978.
xa: Andhra Mahila Sabha founder: **Durgabai Deshmukh**.
Stree Shakti Sanghatana: **Vasantha Kannabiran**, **K. Lalita** and others, Hyderabad.
Mahila Dakshata Samiti: **Suman Krishnakant**, branches in **Vizag** and **Chittoor**.
⚠ **1964** = two Communist women's bodies after the CPI split.
n16c767adba2.fixed: Mahila Dakshata Samiti was founded in 1977 (Suman Krishnakant, Delhi), not 1990

n57e5d0aad5d.s: The Andhra Mahila Sabha was founded by:
n57e5d0aad5d.x: The Andhra Mahila Sabha was founded by Durgabai Deshmukh.
xa: **POW** (**1974**) was formed by radical-Left women activists in Hyderabad.
**Stree Shakti Sanghatana** (**1978**): **Vasantha Kannabiran** and **K. Lalita**.
Durgabai Deshmukh was the first chairperson of the **Central Social Welfare Board (1953)**.

n4bcef00d742.s: Who was the editor of the Telugu feminist magazine Bhumika, founded in 1993?
n4bcef00d742.x: Bhumika was founded in 1993 and its editor was Kondaveeti Satyavathi.
n4bcef00d742.tq: Distinguish a journal’s editor from activists, reformers and political leaders listed in the same field.
xs: **Bhumika** (**1993**) was edited by **Kondaveeti Satyavathi** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kandukuri Veeresalingam** ran the earlier journals **Janana** and **Satihita Bodhini**; **Pratibha Bharati** was the first woman Speaker; **Vasantha Kannabiran** co-founded Stree Shakti Sanghatana.
xa: Bhumika is a **Telugu feminist magazine**.
Veeresalingam's journals promoted **women's education** and **widow remarriage**.
Feminist bodies of the time: **POW (1974)**, **Stree Shakti Sanghatana (1978)**.

ne4cbdfc64e4.s: Who became the first woman Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly in 1999?
ne4cbdfc64e4.x: Pratibha Bharati became the first woman Speaker of the AP Legislative Assembly in 1999. Sharda Mukherjee was the first woman Governor (1977).
xa: **Pratibha Bharati** was the first woman **Speaker** of the AP Assembly (**1999**).
The **1986** AP Act gave daughters **coparcenary rights** — well before the Central amendment of **2005**.
Durgabai Deshmukh also founded the **Andhra Mahila Sabha** (**1937**).

n6c6908457ac.s: Following Muthulakshmi Reddy's campaign, Ammannaraja moved an anti-dedication (Devadasi) bill in the Madras Assembly in:
n6c6908457ac.x: Ammannaraja's anti-dedication bill came in the Madras Assembly in 1937, after Muthulakshmi Reddy's campaign.
xa: **Madras Devadasis (Prevention of Dedication) Act**: **1947**.
**AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act**: **1988**.
**Bhagya Reddy Varma's** **1919** conference demanded abolition of the **Jogini and Devadasi** systems.

n3dbacab9bfe.s: The AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act was enacted in:
n3dbacab9bfe.x: The AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act is of 1988; the earlier Madras Act is of 1947.
xa: NCRB **2023**: about **15,000 dowry cases** and **6,100 dowry deaths**.
**Ammannaraja's** **1937** anti-dedication bill followed **Muthulakshmi Reddy's** campaign.
The **1919 Machilipatnam** Adi-Andhra conference demanded abolition of the **Jogini and Devadasi** systems.

n35e87133e9c.s: What was the principal significance of the Hindu Succession (AP Amendment) Act, 1986?
o: It reserved one-third of Assembly seats for women.
It established the Central Social Welfare Board.
It abolished the Devadasi system in Andhra Pradesh.
It gave daughters coparcenary rights in joint family property.
n35e87133e9c.x: The 1986 Andhra Pradesh amendment gave daughters coparcenary rights in joint family property, well before the Central amendment of 2005.
n35e87133e9c.tq: Match a legislation with its precise legal effect and distinguish it from reservation laws.
xs: The **Hindu Succession (AP Amendment) Act, 1986** **gave daughters coparcenary rights in joint family property** — option **(4)** is correct.
One-third reservation came from the **73rd and 74th Amendments (1992)**, for local bodies, not Assemblies; the Devadasi system was dealt with by the **1988** AP Act.
xa: ⚠ AP acted in **1986** — well before the Central amendment of **2005**.
The **Central Social Welfare Board** dates from **1953** (first chairperson **Durgabai Deshmukh**).
The first woman Speaker of the AP Assembly, **Pratibha Bharati**, came in **1999**.

nd673ca35378.s: Which Article reserves at least one-third of seats for women in Panchayats?
nd673ca35378.x: Article 243D(3), added by the 73rd Amendment (1992), covers Panchayats; Article 243T covers Municipalities.
xa: They reserve **at least one-third** of seats for women.
The **Constitution (131st) Amendment Bill, 2026** on women's reservation was **defeated** in **April 2026**.
As of **Aug 2026**, the women's reservation Act is still not in force — tied to **delimitation**.

n1f4fa3cee88.s: The journals Janana and Satihita Bodhini, which promoted women's education and widow remarriage, were associated with:
n1f4fa3cee88.x: Janana and Satihita Bodhini were Kandukuri Veeresalingam's journals promoting women's education and widow remarriage.
xa: Veeresalingam's journals are the **earlier model** of feminist publishing.
The **Central Social Welfare Board** (**1953**) had **Durgabai Deshmukh** as its first chairperson.
SHG economics in AP: **DWCRA** and **IKP**.

n8986aa35e11.s: The 1919 Machilipatnam Adi-Andhra conference demanded the abolition of which systems?
n8986aa35e11.x: The 1919 Machilipatnam Adi-Andhra conference, associated with Bhagya Reddy Varma, demanded abolition of the Jogini and Devadasi systems.
n8986aa35e11.tq: Link a conference with its specific reform demand rather than with later legislation.
xs: The **1919 Machilipatnam** Adi-Andhra conference demanded abolition of the **Jogini and Devadasi systems** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was led by **Bhagya Reddy Varma**.
xa: **Muthulakshmi Reddy** campaigned against Devadasi dedication; **Ammannaraja** followed with a **1937** bill in the Madras Assembly.
Laws: **Madras Devadasis** Act (**1947**); **AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act** (**1988**).
⚠ Same **1919** conference, two names: **Bhagya Reddy Varma** led it, at **Machilipatnam**.

n8a087d66119.s: Which initiative was launched to build the leadership skills of women elected representatives?
n8a087d66119.x: Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan was launched to build leadership skills among women elected representatives.
n8a087d66119.tq: Match a programme with its stated target group and purpose.
xs: **Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan** was launched to build the leadership skills of **women elected representatives** (**Jun 2026**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Mahila Dakshata Samiti** is a women's body (**Suman Krishnakant**, **1990**); **Aksharajyothi** was the adult-literacy programme behind the anti-arrack movement.
xa: Women's-quota implementation was still disputed in **Aug 2026**.
**73rd and 74th Amendments (1992)** reserved at least **one-third** of local-body seats for women.
AP: **One Stop Centres** in all **26 districts** (**22,692** cases handled).

nc70c767bd9e.s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, which now covers all 26 districts of Andhra Pradesh, was launched in
nc70c767bd9e.x: BBBP was launched in 2015. The AP Socio-Economic Survey wrongly dates it from 2006 - the exam trap. 2011 is a Census year and 2016 is when the 181 Women Helpline began in AP.
xs: **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** was launched in **2015** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **Trap:** the AP Socio-Economic Survey (APSES) dates it from **2006**.
**2016** is when AP's **181 Women Helpline** began.
xa: BBBP covers all **26 districts** of AP.
AP has **28 Shakti Sadans**.
**One Stop Centres** in all 26 districts have handled **22,692** cases.

n884907801ac.s: Ravindra Bharathi, Hyderabad (1961), was built to mark the birth centenary of:
n884907801ac.x: Ravindra Bharathi was built in 1961 for Tagore's birth centenary, not Gandhi's.
xa: ⚠ Ravindra Bharathi's inaugurator: **APPSC G2 2017 key** gives **Dr S. Radhakrishnan**; a PYQ book gives **Jawaharlal Nehru** — follow the official key.
**AP Sahitya Akademi** was set up in **1957**.
**1975** is also the year of the **first World Telugu Conference** at **Hyderabad**.

nf0ac263ccc4.s: The Andhra Pradesh Sahitya Akademi, set up to promote Telugu literature, translation and awards, was established in
nf0ac263ccc4.x: The AP Sahitya Akademi was set up in 1957. The national Sahitya Akademi was inaugurated in 1954; Ravindra Bharathi was built in 1961; the International Telugu Institute dates from 1975.
nf0ac263ccc4.tq: AP Sahitya Akademi 1957; merged into Telugu University 1985.
xs: The **AP Sahitya Akademi** was set up in **1957** — option **(2)** is correct (PYQ).
**1954** = national Sahitya Akademi inaugurated; **1961** = Ravindra Bharathi; **1975** = International Telugu Institute.
xa: ⚠ Sahitya Akademi: set up **1952**, inaugurated **1954**; AP Sahitya Akademi = **1957**.
In **1985** the NTR government merged the State akademis into the **Telugu University**.
The national **Sahitya Akademi** is a **society**, not a statutory body.

n5e1ce9a4d76.s: The Sangeet Natak Akademi, the first national arts academy, was inaugurated by:
n5e1ce9a4d76.x: The Sangeet Natak Akademi, the first national arts academy, was inaugurated by Rajendra Prasad.
xa: Sahitya Akademi was set up in **1952** but inaugurated on **12 March 1954**.
**Lalit Kala Akademi**: **1954**.
⚠ The State-level **AP Sahitya Akademi** came in **1957**.

n50ca62729fb.s: Which one of the following is NOT listed among the Andhra Pradesh cultural awards?
n50ca62729fb.x: Ugadi Kala Ratna, Kandukuri, Telugu Language and Gurram Jashuva awards are listed among Andhra Pradesh cultural awards. Lalit Kala Akademi is a national cultural academy, not one of the listed Andhra Pradesh awards.
n50ca62729fb.tq: Distinguish a state award list from the name of a national academy.
xs: **Lalit Kala Akademi Award** is NOT among the listed AP cultural awards — option **(3)** is correct.
**Lalit Kala Akademi** (**1954**) is a **national** academy.
The AP awards (**Jul 2026**) are **Ugadi Kala Ratna**, **Kandukuri**, **Telugu Language** and **Gurram Jashuva** awards.
xa: The **Kandukuri Awards** were revived by the coalition government after lapsing under the **YSRCP** government.
The **Nandi Awards** (**1964**) are AP's film, TV and drama awards.
National akademis: Sahitya (**1952**), Sangeet Natak (**1953**), Lalit Kala (**1954**).

n97f7fdca3b6.s: The Second World Telugu Conference was held at:
n97f7fdca3b6.x: The Second World Telugu Conference was held at Kuala Lumpur; the First was at Hyderabad, the Third in Mauritius and the Fourth at Tirupati.
xa: The first conference was called **Prapancha Telugu Mahasabhalu**.
Its year **1975** is asked repeatedly — also the year of the **International Telugu Institute**.
Kuala Lumpur is in **Malaysia**.

ncc582430f09.s: The first communist Telugu journal was:
ncc582430f09.x: Prajasakti was the first communist Telugu journal; Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal after Independence.
xa: Post-1956 papers: **Andhra Jyothi (1960)**, **Eenadu (1974)**, **Udayam (1984)**, **Sakshi (2008)**.
**Eenadu** was launched from **Visakhapatnam** by **Ramoji Rao**.
⚠ FIRST communist = Prajasakti; FIRST after Independence = Jaya Bharat.

n43631b50b81.s: Rayaprolu Subbarao received the Sahitya Akademi Award for which work?
n43631b50b81.x: Rayaprolu Subbarao received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1965 for Misra Manjari.
n43631b50b81.tq: Match the author with the specific award-winning work rather than with a better-known Telugu title.
xs: **Rayaprolu Subbarao** won the **Sahitya Akademi** award in **1965** for **Misra Manjari** — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ **Gabbilam** is **Gurram Jashuva's** work, and his award was **not** for Gabbilam (PYQ 2025).
xa: **Gurram Jashuva**: Sahitya Akademi **1964**; **Padma Bhushan 1970**; nominated **MLC 1964**.
Other awardees: **C. Narayana Reddy** and **Ravuri Bharadwaja**.
Sahitya Akademi Award now: **Rs 1 lakh**, **24 languages**.

nb8ed468343f.s: The Sahitya Akademi Award currently carries which combination of languages and prize amount?
nb8ed468343f.x: The Sahitya Akademi Award covers 24 languages—22 Eighth Schedule languages along with English and Rajasthani—and carries Rs 1 lakh.
nb8ed468343f.tq: Distinguish the language count and prize amount from figures associated with other awards.
xs: The Sahitya Akademi Award now covers **24 languages** and carries **Rs 1 lakh** — option **(4)** is correct.
The 24 = **22** Eighth Schedule languages + **English** + **Rajasthani**.
**Rs 15 lakh** is the **Dadasaheb Phalke** prize money.
xa: The Sahitya Akademi was set up in **1952** and inaugurated on **12 March 1954**.
It is a **society**, not a statutory body.
Telugu winners: **Gurram Jashuva** (**1964**), **Rayaprolu Subbarao** (**1965**, Misra Manjari).

nfed258e8a7e.s: Gurram Jashuva received the Padma Bhushan in:
nfed258e8a7e.x: Jashuva received the Padma Bhushan in 1970; his Sahitya Akademi Award came in 1964.
xa: Jashuva was also a nominated **MLC** in **1964**.
⚠ **1964** = Nandi Awards instituted **and** Jashuva's Sahitya Akademi + MLC.
A **Gurram Jashuva award** is among AP's cultural awards (**Jul 2026**).

n8297aa2823d.s: The Nandi Awards of the Andhra Pradesh Government for films, television and drama were instituted in:
n8297aa2823d.x: Nandi Awards are AP Government awards for films, television and drama, instituted in 1964.
xa: The previous **YSRCP** government let the Nandi and **Kandukuri Veeresalingam** Awards lapse.
The coalition government announced revival of Nandi Awards and **Nandi Natakotsavams** (**Mar 2026**).
⚠ **1964** = Nandi Awards **and** Jashuva's Sahitya Akademi + MLC.

n9575e7947bc.s: Which of the following Telugu film directors received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award?
n9575e7947bc.x: K. Viswanath is among the Telugu recipients of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, along with B.N. Reddy and Akkineni Nageswara Rao.
xa: Phalke prize: **Swarna Kamal**, shawl + **Rs 15 lakh**.
The cash was raised from **Rs 10 lakh** in **2024**.
The State's own film awards are the **Nandi Awards** (**1964**).

nefde1da3701.s: Along with an annual Telugu Mahotsavam, Andhra Pradesh has proposed to revive the:
nefde1da3701.x: Andhra Pradesh announced an annual Telugu Mahotsavam to revive folk and theatre forms, and the Nandi Natakotsavams are also proposed to be revived.
xa: Telugu Mahotsavam: announced at **Undavalli Caves**, **July 2026**, Minister **Kandula Durgesh**.
The **Nandi Awards** (films, TV, drama; **1964**) are also to be revived.
The previous **YSRCP** government had let the Nandi and Kandukuri Awards lapse.

n4db83d0b403.s: The Digambara kavulu, the anti-establishment movement of 'naked poets', began in:
n4db83d0b403.x: The Digambara movement began in 1965; 1970 is when several Digambaras moved to Virasam.
xa: In **1970** several Digambaras (**Cherabandaraju**, **Jwalamukhi**, **Nikhileswar**) moved to **Virasam**.
The six Digambara pen names: **Nagnamuni**, **Nikhileswar**, **Cherabandaraju**, **Jwalamukhi**, **Mahaswapna**, **Bhairavayya**.
⚠ **1965** = Digambaras; **1969** = Srikakulam struggle; **1970** = Virasam.

nf560293f3ac.s: Who was the first president of the Viplava Rachayitala Sangham (Virasam), founded in 1970?
nf560293f3ac.x: Virasam, founded on 4 July 1970, had Sri Sri as its first president, not Gaddar.
xa: Context: the **Srikakulam peasant struggle (1969)** under **Vempatapu Satyam** spread Naxalism in Andhra.
Digambaras **Cherabandaraju**, **Jwalamukhi** and **Nikhileswar** joined Virasam in **1970**.
Virasam = **Viplava Rachayitala Sangham**.

nc342c2b9a83.s: The Karamchedu incident referred to in the context of the Dalit movement took place in:
nc342c2b9a83.x: The Karamchedu incident took place in 1985. The 1982 reference is an erroneous date appearing in one compilation and is not the year of the incident.
nc342c2b9a83.tq: Discriminate between closely placed year options.
xs: The **Karamchedu** incident took place in **1985** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ **Trap:** some notes print **1982**; **1969** is the Srikakulam struggle and **1970** is Virasam.
xa: After Karamchedu, Dalits formed independent **Dalit Mahasabhas**.
Dalit literature has its roots in **Gurram Jashuva**.
Later Dalit voices: **Katti Padmarao**, **Gaddar**, **Endluri Sudhakar**, **Boyi Bhimanna**.

o: G. Lakshmi Narasaiah and Tripuraneni Srinivas
n7bbf328bf73.x: Neeli Meghalu was edited by Volga and others.
n7bbf328bf73.tq: Test the editor of an anthology directly, using editors of nearby anthologies as distractors.
xs: **Neeli Meghalu** (**1993**) was edited by **Volga and others** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Khadar Mohiuddin** wrote **Puttumacha**; **Ditta Pullayya** ran **Adi Andhra Patrika**; **Lakshmi Narasaiah and Tripuraneni Srinivas** edited **Chikkanavutunna Pata**.
xa: Poets of Neeli Meghalu: **Jayaprabha**, **Vimala**, **Kondepudi Nirmala**.
It is the landmark of **feminist poetry**.
Feminist and Dalit fiction rest on the **Gidugu-Gurajada** spoken-Telugu revolution.

o: A collection of three Digambara volumes
An anthology of Telugu Muslim minority poetry of the 1990s
A 1993 anthology of Telugu feminist poetry
n3bc97a28a6b.x: Jaljala is an anthology of Telugu Muslim minority poetry of the 1990s.
n3bc97a28a6b.tq: Distinguish literary anthologies by stream and decade.
xs: **Jaljala** is **an anthology of Telugu Muslim minority poetry of the 1990s** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **1995** Dalit anthology is **Chikkanavutunna Pata**; the **1993** feminist anthology is **Neeli Meghalu**; the three Digambara volumes are **Digambara Kavitvam**.
xa: **Khadar Mohiuddin's** **Puttumacha** is a long poem on Muslim identity.
Digambara Kavitvam appeared in **1965-68**.
Neeli Meghalu was edited by **Volga** and others.

n8ee26b9c1d4.x: Baddam Bhaskara Reddy wrote as Cherabandaraju; Mahaswapna was the pen name of Kammisetti Venkateswara Rao.
xa: **Nikhileswar** = **Kumbham Yadava Reddy**.
**Jwalamukhi** = **Veeravalli Raghavacharyulu**.
**Sri Sri** = **Srirangam Srinivasa Rao** (not a Digambara).

nd981cb29d05.s: Several Digambara poets joined Virasam in 1970. Which of the following group contains only such poets?
nd981cb29d05.x: Cherabandaraju, Jwalamukhi and Nikhileswar moved on to Virasam in 1970.
nd981cb29d05.tq: Separate the subgroup that changed from one literary movement to another.
xs: **Cherabandaraju, Jwalamukhi and Nikhileswar** moved from the Digambaras to **Virasam** in **1970** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Volga**, **Jayaprabha** and **Vimala** are feminist poets of **Neeli Meghalu**; **Sri Sri** was Virasam's first president, not a Digambara.
xa: Cherabandaraju = **Baddam Bhaskara Reddy**; Jwalamukhi = **Veeravalli Raghavacharyulu**; Nikhileswar = **Kumbham Yadava Reddy**.
Virasam was founded on **4 July 1970**.
The Digambaras began in **1965**.

n8af7ad2032c.s: Which work of Sri Sri is associated with breaking Telugu prosody and issuing a call to the oppressed?
n8af7ad2032c.x: Maha Prasthanam broke conventional Telugu prosody and presented a call to the oppressed.
n8af7ad2032c.tq: Match the work with its distinctive literary function.
xs: **Maha Prasthanam** by **Sri Sri** broke **Telugu prosody** and issued a **call to the oppressed** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Khadga Srushti** (Sri Sri) is on **armed struggle**; **Firdausi** is **Gurram Jashuva's** poem.
xa: **Siri Siri Muvvalu** is another work of Sri Sri.
Sri Sri won the first National Award for a Telugu lyricist ("**Teluguveera Levara**", **Alluri Seetharamaraju**).
Sri Sri (**Srirangam Srinivasa Rao**) was Virasam's first president.

nf0ef68f7512.s: Gurram Jashuva is regarded as the first modern Telugu poet associated with which literary stream?
nf0ef68f7512.x: Gurram Jashuva is regarded as the first modern Telugu Dalit poet.
nf0ef68f7512.tq: Test the identity of a pioneering literary figure directly.
xs: **Gurram Jashuva** is the first modern Telugu **Dalit** poet — option **(1)** is correct.
Dalit literature has its roots in Jashuva.
xa: His works: **Gabbilam (1941)**, **Firdausi**, **Kandiseekudu**, **Kreesthu Charitra**.
Later Dalit voices: **Katti Padmarao**, **Gaddar**, **Endluri Sudhakar**, **Boyi Bhimanna**.
**Ditta Pullayya** ran the magazine **Adi Andhra Patrika**.

nc7a726c5680.s: Firdausi, a poem about a Persian poet cheated of his promised reward by Sultan Mahmud, was written by:
nc7a726c5680.x: Firdausi is Jashuva's poem on the Persian poet cheated by Sultan Mahmud, presented as a rebel against patronage.
xa: Jashuva's other works: **Gabbilam**, **Kandiseekudu**, **Kreesthu Charitra**.
Jashuva = first modern Telugu **Dalit** poet.
Gabbilam is modelled on **Meghaduta**.

n01495d1fdaf.s: 'Nallapoddu', a collection of Dalit women's writings, was edited by
n01495d1fdaf.x: Nallapoddu was edited by Gogu Syamala (APPSC G2 2017 key; the 'Mallepoddu' version of the question has the same answer). Volga edited the feminist anthology Neeli Meghalu; G. Lakshmi Narasaiah edited Chikkanavutunna Pata and Padunekkina Pata; Kondaveeti Satyavathi edits Bhumika.
xs: **Nallapoddu** is by **Gogu Syamala** — option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2017** key).
**Volga** co-edited **Neeli Meghalu**; **G. Lakshmi Narasaiah** edited **Chikkanavutunna Pata** and **Padunekkina Pata**.
xa: ⚠ "**Mallepoddu / Mallapoddu**" in one version of the **2017** paper is the same question — answer **Syamala**.
Chikkanavutunna Pata (**1995**) was co-edited with **Tripuraneni Srinivas**.
First modern Telugu Dalit poet: **Gurram Jashuva**.

nf951f3ebd0c.s: Puttumacha, meaning ‘Birthmark’, is a long poem by:
nf951f3ebd0c.x: Puttumacha, meaning ‘Birthmark’, is a long poem by Khadar Mohiuddin on Muslim identity.
nf951f3ebd0c.tq: Use the title’s meaning and subject to identify the poet.
xs: **Puttumacha** ("Birthmark") is a long poem by **Khadar Mohiuddin** on **Muslim identity** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Kondepudi Nirmala** is a **Neeli Meghalu** feminist poet; **Jashuva** and **Sri Sri** wrote Gabbilam and Maha Prasthanam.
xa: Muslim minority poetry anthology of the **1990s**: **Jaljala**.
The post-**1956** streams turned Telugu literature towards caste, class, gender and **minority identity**.
Feminist anthology: **Neeli Meghalu (1993)**.

n5d4d4579f9d.s: Post-1956 Telugu literature shifted its focus from classical and romantic themes towards:
o: Caste, class, gender and minority identity
n5d4d4579f9d.x: Post-1956 Telugu literary streams broadened literature to take in caste, class, gender and minority identity.
xa: Feminist landmark: **Neeli Meghalu (1993)**; Muslim minority: **Jaljala** (**1990s**).
First modern Telugu Dalit poet: **Gurram Jashuva**.
Comparative note: Bengali Dalit poet **Kalyani Thakur Charal's** anthology won the **A.K. Ramanujan Prize** (**Feb 2026**).

n167962b2192.s: In Gabbilam, what is the central function of the bat?
o: It announces the beginning of the Srikakulam struggle.
It carries a hungry Dalit’s message to Lord Shiva.
It symbolises the founding of Virasam.
It represents a Persian poet seeking royal patronage.
n167962b2192.x: In Gabbilam, a bat carries the message of a hungry Dalit to Lord Shiva. Its life outside the temple and in darkness symbolises the condition of the untouchable.
n167962b2192.tq: Identify the central image and its social symbolism in a protest poem.
xs: In **Gabbilam**, a **bat** **carries a hungry Dalit's message to Lord Shiva** — option **(2)** is correct.
The bat, outside the temple and in the dark, stands for the **untouchable**.
A Persian poet cheated of reward is the theme of Jashuva's **Firdausi**, not Gabbilam.
xa: Gabbilam (**1941**) is modelled on Kalidasa's **Meghaduta**.
⚠ **Trap:** Gabbilam did **not** win the Akademi award (PYQ 2025).
Jashuva = first modern Telugu **Dalit** poet.

nb1377e51cc7.s: Who among the following authored the novel Jakkadona?
nb1377e51cc7.x: Jakkadona was written by R.C. Krishnaswamy Raju.
xs: **Jakkadona** was written by **R.C. Krishnaswamy Raju** — option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC 2023** key).
**Yandamuri Veerendranath** wrote **Tulasidalam**; **Kesava Reddy** wrote **Athadu Adavini Jayinchadu**; **Ranganayakamma** wrote **Ramayana Vishavruksham**.
xa: **Veyi Padagalu** is by **Viswanatha Satyanarayana**.
It was translated as **Sahasraphan** by **P.V. Narasimha Rao** (**APPSC 2022**).
Exam angle: author-work matching with distractors **Tulasidalam**, **Mahaprasthanam**, **Vennello Aadapilla**.

n1e41ce149a9.s: Who translated Veyi Padagalu into Hindi as Sahasraphan?
n1e41ce149a9.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao translated Veyi Padagalu into Hindi as Sahasraphan.
n1e41ce149a9.tq: Test the translator separately from the author of the original work.
xs: **P.V. Narasimha Rao** translated **Veyi Padagalu** into Hindi as **Sahasraphan** — option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC 2022**).
The novel is by **Viswanatha Satyanarayana**.
xa: ⚠ Viswanatha's Jnanpith work = **Ramayana Kalpavrukshamu**; Veyi Padagalu = his novel translated by PVNR.
Viswanatha was the **first Telugu Jnanpith** awardee and wrote over **100** works.
He is called "**Abhinava Nannaya**".

nc603195d961.s: C. Narayana Reddy received the Jnanpith Award in:
nc603195d961.x: C. Narayana Reddy received the Jnanpith in 1988; Viswanatha Satyanarayana in 1970 and Ravuri Bharadwaja in 2012.
xa: Viswanatha was the **first Telugu Jnanpith** awardee.
CM Naidu recalled all three at the **World Telugu Mahasabhalu** (**Jan 2026**).
Telugu is one of India's **six classical languages**.

n1bbc28f5f75.s: Viswanatha Satyanarayana, author of over 100 works, was known as:
n1bbc28f5f75.x: Viswanatha Satyanarayana was known as 'Abhinava Nannaya' and wrote over 100 works.
xa: Viswanatha won the Jnanpith in **1970** for **Ramayana Kalpavrukshamu**.
He was the **first Telugu Jnanpith** awardee.
Veyi Padagalu's Hindi title: **Sahasraphan**.

n94320e7387d.s: The first Telugu talkie, Bhakta Prahlada, was directed by:
n94320e7387d.x: Bhakta Prahlada was directed by H.M. Reddy, not C. Pullaiah.
xa: H.M. Reddy is called the "**godfather of the Telugu talkie**".
He assisted **Ardeshir Irani** on **Alam Ara** and also made **Gruha Lakshmi**.
Years: silent **1921**, talkie **1931**, colour **1963**.

n94d71b1d0b5.s: The Nandi Awards of the Andhra Pradesh Government are given in the fields of:
n94d71b1d0b5.x: The Nandi Awards cover films, television and drama, including the Nandi Natakotsavam for drama.
xa: Instituted by the **Government of AP** in **1964**.
They lapsed under the previous government; revival announced (**Feb, Mar and Jul 2026**).
⚠ Phalke = Centre, **1969**; Nandi = AP, **1964**.

n54faae35881.s: Who was the first recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, instituted in 1969?
n54faae35881.x: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award was instituted in 1969 and Devika Rani was its first recipient.
xa: It is presented by the **President** with the National Film Awards.
First South Indian awardee: **B.N. Reddy**.
Telugu awardees include **Akkineni Nageswara Rao** and **K. Viswanath**.

n6d94f599446.s: The Nandi Awards were instituted in 1964 by:
n6d94f599446.x: The Nandi Awards were instituted by the Government of Andhra Pradesh in 1964; NFDC administers the National Film Awards.
xa: Categories: **films, television and drama**.
⚠ Phalke = Centre, **1969**; Nandi = AP, **1964**.
Revival of Nandi Awards and **Nandi Natakotsavams** announced in **2026**.

n079f1e58f0c.s: Doordarshan Kendra Hyderabad was established in:
n079f1e58f0c.x: Doordarshan Kendra Hyderabad was established in 1977.
n079f1e58f0c.tq: Differentiate the public broadcaster’s regional-centre year from private-channel years.
xs: **Doordarshan Kendra Hyderabad** was set up in **1977** — option **(2)** is correct.
**1995** is the year of the private Telugu satellite channels **Gemini TV** and **ETV**; **1982** is the TDP's founding.
xa: **ETV** was founded by **Ramoji Rao**.
**Doordarshan** and **Akashvani** come under **Prasar Bharati**.
⚠ **Ramoji Rao** = ETV (**1995**) + **Ramoji Film City** (**1996**).

n6689f3d1817.s: Who is hailed as the 'godfather of the Telugu talkie'?
n6689f3d1817.x: H.M. Reddy, who assisted Ardeshir Irani on Alam Ara, is hailed as the godfather of the Telugu talkie.
xa: H.M. Reddy directed **Bhakta Prahlada** (**1931**), the first Telugu talkie, and **Gruha Lakshmi**.
He is called "the first Telugu cinema's director".
New biography: "**H.M. Reddy - Telugu Cinema Pitamahudu**" by **H. Ramesh Babu** (**Mar 2026**).

n0ee4eb353fd.s: Which Telugu film-maker, known for the social-lyrical film Malliswari, was the first South Indian to receive the Dadasaheb Phalke Award?
n0ee4eb353fd.x: B.N. Reddy (Malliswari) was the first South Indian Phalke awardee, in 1974. K.V. Reddy made mythological-folklore classics such as Pathala Bhairavi and Mayabazar; L.V. Prasad got the Phalke Award later, in 1982; H.M. Reddy directed the first Telugu talkie Bhakta Prahlada and is not among the Telugu Phalke awardees listed.
n0ee4eb353fd.tq: First South Indian Phalke = B.N. Reddy (1974), maker of Malliswari.
xs: **B.N. Reddy** (**Malliswari**) was the **first South Indian** Phalke awardee (**1974**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**K.V. Reddy** made **Pathala Bhairavi** and **Mayabazar**; **L.V. Prasad** got the Phalke later (**1982**); **H.M. Reddy** directed **Bhakta Prahlada**.
xa: The Phalke Award was instituted in **1969**; first awardee **Devika Rani**.
