Telugu awardees after B.N. Reddy: **L.V. Prasad**, **B. Nagi Reddy**, **Akkineni Nageswara Rao**, **D. Ramanaidu**, **K. Viswanath**.
It is presented by the **President** with the National Film Awards.

n49cab3c10c1.s: Bapu, the painter-director, is associated in films with:
n49cab3c10c1.x: Bapu made films in association with Mullapudi Venkata Ramana.
n49cab3c10c1.tq: Identify the creative collaborator linked with the personality.
xs: **Bapu** (**Sattiraju Lakshminarayana**), painter-director, made films with **Mullapudi Venkata Ramana** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Ardeshir Irani** made **Alam Ara** (assisted by H.M. Reddy); **Aluri Chakrapani** co-founded **Vijaya Vauhini Studios**.
xa: Bapu's real name: **Sattiraju Lakshminarayana**.
**K. Viswanath**: classical-arts social films (**Sankarabharanam**).
**K.V. Reddy**: **Pathala Bhairavi**, **Mayabazar**.

nbd71dd6238c.s: Ramoji Film City is recognised by Guinness as the world’s largest:
nbd71dd6238c.x: Guinness lists Ramoji Film City as the world’s largest film studio complex.
nbd71dd6238c.tq: Separate a studio complex from related film institutions.
xs: **Guinness** lists **Ramoji Film City** as the world's largest **film studio complex** — option **(3)** is correct.
It was founded by **Ramoji Rao** in **1996** (APPSC 2018 key).
xa: Ramoji Rao also founded **ETV** (**1995**), a private Telugu satellite channel.
Other Hyderabad studios: **Annapurna** and **Ramanaidu Studios**.
The studio belt grew after the industry's move from **Madras to Hyderabad** after **1956**.

n75f64036f91.s: N.T. Rama Rao, who founded the TDP in March 1982, became Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in:
n75f64036f91.x: NTR became Chief Minister in 1983, within a year of founding the TDP on 29 March 1982.
xa: The TDP was founded when **Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy** was CM (**APPSC G2 2019**).
TDP slogan: **Telugu Vari Atma Gauravam**.
NTR's TDP ended the **Congress monopoly** in **1983**.

nc3987b01585.s: In 2011, Chiranjeevi's Praja Rajyam Party merged with the:
nc3987b01585.x: The Praja Rajyam Party (founded 2008) merged with the Congress in 2011, not the TDP.
xa: **NTR** ("Andhra MGR") founded the **TDP** (**29 March 1982**) and became CM in **1983**.
**K. Pawan Kalyan** (**Jana Sena**) is **Deputy CM** of AP.
Cinema made the Telugu film star a **political force**.

nb7fb3582c71.s: K. Pawan Kalyan, who became Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, leads which party?
nb7fb3582c71.x: K. Pawan Kalyan is associated with the Jana Sena Party and became Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.
xa: Praja Rajyam (**2008**) merged with the Congress (**2011**).
**NTR** founded the **TDP** on **29 March 1982**.
NTR became CM in **1983**.

nadc004e9190.s: Who received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2023 at the 71st National Film Awards?
nadc004e9190.x: Mohanlal received the Phalke Award for 2023 at the 71st National Film Awards; Anant Nag was named for 2024.
xa: Anant Nag's award was at the **72nd** NFA (**Sep 2026**).
The award carries the President's presentation along with the **National Film Awards**.
First awardee: **Devika Rani** (**1969**).

n4b10ff33e04.s: When N.T. Rama Rao founded the Telugu Desam Party on 29 March 1982, who was the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
n4b10ff33e04.x: The TDP was founded when Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy was Chief Minister (APPSC Group 2, 2019). Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy is associated with the 1993 arrack ban, Chandrababu Naidu with lifting prohibition in 1997, and P.V. Narasimha Rao was CM in 1971-73 (land reforms) - none was CM in March 1982.
n4b10ff33e04.tq: TDP founded 29 March 1982 under CM Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy; NTR became CM in 1983.
xs: When NTR founded the TDP (**29 March 1982**), the CM was **Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy** — option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2019**).
NTR himself became CM only in **1983**.
xa: TDP slogan: **Telugu Vari Atma Gauravam**.
NTR's mass image came from playing screen **Rama/Krishna**.
NTR's TDP ended the **Congress monopoly** in 1983.

n4558c8bf0cc.s: Which of the following is a component of Prasar Bharati?
n4558c8bf0cc.x: Prasar Bharati comprises Akashvani and Doordarshan. NFDC and CBFC are separate institutions, while the National Film Awards are administered by NFDC.
n4558c8bf0cc.tq: Separate an institution’s components from associated film bodies and awards.
xs: **Akashvani** (with **Doordarshan**) is a component of **Prasar Bharati** — option **(4)** is correct.
**NFDC** and **CBFC** are separate bodies; the **National Film Awards** are administered by **NFDC**.
xa: These form the Centre's **Mass Communication** set-up.
**Doordarshan Kendra Hyderabad**: **1977**.
Private Telugu satellite TV: **Gemini TV** and **ETV** (**1995**).

n86e9c374661.s: In Ugadi 2012, Bapu received the State's ____ award for painting.
n86e9c374661.x: Bapu, known for line drawings of epic characters, received the State's Telugu Velugu award for painting in Ugadi 2012.
xa: Bapu's birth name: **Sattiraju Lakshminarayana** (**APPSC G2 2017**).
His film partner: **Ramana** (**Mullapudi Venkata Ramana**).
PYQ distractors for Bapu's name: **Ramana**, **Paidi Raju**, **Sanjeeva Dev**.

n0937ed37678.s: Who is regarded as the 'Father of Modern Contemporary Art' in Andhra Pradesh?
n0937ed37678.x: Nandikolla Gopala Rao is called the Father of Modern Contemporary Art in AP (APPSC 2018 key). Adivi Bapiraju was a painter, poet and novelist; Vaddadi Papaiah illustrated Chandamama and Yuva covers; Bapu was known for line drawings and as a film director - these three were the distractors in the PYQ.
n0937ed37678.tq: Father of Modern Contemporary Art (AP) = Nandikolla Gopala Rao.
xs: **Nandikolla Gopala Rao** is the "**Father of Modern Contemporary Art**" in AP — option **(3)** is correct (**APPSC 2018** key).
**Adivi Bapiraju** was a painter-poet-novelist; **Vaddadi Papaiah** a magazine-cover illustrator; **Bapu** a line-drawing artist and film director — the PYQ's distractors.
xa: **Damerla Rama Rao** = pioneer of modern Andhra painting, **Rajahmundry**.
Bapu = **Sattiraju Lakshminarayana**.
Vapa = **Vaddadi Papaiah**.

n15d505768c7.s: The real name of the painter and film director popularly known as 'Bapu' is:
n15d505768c7.x: Bapu's birth name is Sattiraju Lakshminarayana (APPSC Group 2, 2017). Mullapudi Venkata Ramana is 'Ramana', Bapu's film partner; Paidi Raju and Sanjeeva Dev were the distractors in the PYQ and are not Bapu's name.
n15d505768c7.tq: Bapu = Sattiraju Lakshminarayana; Ramana = Mullapudi Venkata Ramana.
xs: Bapu's real name is **Sattiraju Lakshminarayana** — option **(4)** is correct (**APPSC G2 2017**).
**Mullapudi Venkata Ramana** is "**Ramana**", Bapu's film partner; **Paidi Raju** and **Sanjeeva Dev** were PYQ distractors.
xa: Bapu: line drawings of **Ramayana-Mahabharata** characters; illustrator and film director.
He won the **Telugu Velugu** award for painting (Ugadi **2012**).
⚠ **Vapa** = Vaddadi Papaiah, not Bapu.

n263a6bb4b9c.s: Lepakshi was placed on UNESCO's tentative list of World Heritage Sites in:
n263a6bb4b9c.x: Lepakshi, including the Veerabhadra temple and monolithic Nandi, was placed on the tentative list in 2022; Andhra Pradesh has no inscribed World Heritage Site.
xa: Lepakshi: **Veerabhadra** temple + monolithic **Nandi**.
"**Discover Andhra**" promotes a **Buddhist heritage circuit** — **Amaravati, Bavikonda, Thotlakonda** (**Feb 2026**).
**ASI** was founded in **1861** by **Alexander Cunningham**.

n4979de6009f.s: The Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act was enacted in:
n4979de6009f.x: The AMASR Act is of 1958; the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act is of 1972 and ICOMOS was founded in 1965.
xa: **ASI**: **1861**, **Alexander Cunningham**.
**Hyderabad State Archaeological Department** (**1914**) is the origin of the AP Department of Archaeology and Museums.
AP has **no inscribed World Heritage Site**; **Lepakshi** is on the tentative list (**2022**).

n5fdb99d3774.s: The AP Department of Archaeology and Museums traces its origin to the Hyderabad State Archaeological Department, established in:
n5fdb99d3774.x: It traces its origin to the Hyderabad State Archaeological Department of 1914; 1861 is the founding of the ASI.
xa: Its present HQ: Commissioner's office at **Vijayawada** (**2026**).
Central laws: **AMASR Act 1958**; **Antiquities and Art Treasures Act 1972**.
AP's share of antiques is being transferred under the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014**.

n4f180a44005.s: The Archaeological Survey of India was founded in 1861 by:
n4f180a44005.x: Alexander Cunningham founded the ASI in 1861; Ranganatha Saraswati found Nagarjunakonda (1926) and Longhurst dug it (1927).
xa: The ASI rebuilt Nagarjunakonda monuments at **Anupu** and on the island — "**Transplanted Monuments**".
ASI began scientific conservation at **Mangalagiri's** Panakala Narasimha Swamy Temple (**Jul 2026**).

n4828e3e1b38.s: Nagarjunakonda was first found in 1926 by whom?
n4828e3e1b38.x: Nagarjunakonda was found in 1926 by A. Ranganatha Saraswati. Later excavation work involved Longhurst, Ramachandran and R. Subrahmanyam.
n4828e3e1b38.tq: Distinguish the initial discoverer from later excavators.
xs: **Nagarjunakonda** was found in **1926** by **A. Ranganatha Saraswati** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Longhurst** dug it in **1927**; **Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy** discovered **Salihundam**; **Cunningham** founded the ASI.
xa: Later excavators: **Ramachandran** and **R. Subrahmanyam** — **salvage archaeology** before submergence.
Site is in **Palnadu** district.
⚠ Found **1926**, dug **1927**; submerged after **1960**.

n72519b421d9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Nagarjunakonda?
o: It has an acoustic building and an amphitheatre.
It shows habitation from the Palaeolithic to 1960 CE.
It has Santamula's Ashvamedha altar and a Sati sculpture.
It has fewer than ten stupas.
n72519b421d9.x: Nagarjunakonda has more than 30 stupas, so 'fewer than ten' is false; the other three features are all associated with the site.
xa: Submerged after **1960** by the **Nagarjunasagar Dam**.
The ASI rebuilt monuments at **Anupu** and on **Nagarjunakonda island** — "**Transplanted Monuments**".
Rescued **Ikshvaku-Buddhist** finds are in the **Nagarjunakonda island museum**.

n4a0ed206dc9.s: Monuments at Anupu and on Nagarjunakonda island were rebuilt on higher ground because of submergence by the:
n4a0ed206dc9.x: The area was submerged after 1960 by the Nagarjunasagar Dam, so the ASI dismantled and rebuilt the monuments ('transplantation of monuments').
xa: They are called "**Transplanted Monuments**".
The excavation before submergence was **salvage archaeology**.
Rescued finds are in the **Nagarjunakonda island museum** in the **Nagarjuna Sagar** reservoir.

nc5e94cb9e39.s: The Buddhist site of Salihundam was discovered by:
nc5e94cb9e39.x: Salihundam was discovered by Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy; A. Ranganatha Saraswati found Nagarjunakonda in 1926.
xa: Thotlakonda also has a **stupa** and **apsidal chaityas**.
Salihundam: **Mahayana-Vajrayana** port town with **Tara** bronzes and a Buddha footprint.
Bavikonda and Thotlakonda were dug by the **AP State Archaeology Dept**.

n4b9c7d795d3.s: The Salar Jung Museum, Hyderabad, houses the collection of:
o: Mir Osman Ali Khan, Nizam VII
Mir Turab Ali Khan, Salar Jung I
Mir Mahbub Ali Khan, Nizam VI
Nawab Mir Yousuf Ali Khan, Salar Jung III
n4b9c7d795d3.x: The museum holds the collection gathered over 40 years by Nawab Mir Yousuf Ali Khan, Salar Jung III.
xa: Its "**Veiled Rebecca**" marble statue was bought in **Rome**, **1876**.
The **AP State Museum**, Hyderabad, is now the **Telangana State Museum**.
AP formed a committee (chair **Tejaswi Podapati**) to take its share of antiques.

ne9696f3c7fd.s: Which museum is situated on an island in the Nagarjuna Sagar reservoir and houses rescued Ikshvaku-Buddhist remains?
ne9696f3c7fd.x: The Nagarjunakonda island museum, located in the Nagarjuna Sagar reservoir, houses archaeological material rescued from the submerged area, including Ikshvaku-Buddhist finds.
ne9696f3c7fd.tq: Use the location–collection combination to identify the museum.
xs: The **Nagarjunakonda island museum**, in the **Nagarjuna Sagar** reservoir, holds rescued **Ikshvaku-Buddhist** finds — option **(2)** is correct.
The **Bapu Museum** is at **Vijayawada**, **Baudhasree** at **Guntur**, and the **Amaravati** site museum shows Amaravati School sculpture.
xa: Monuments were rebuilt at **Anupu** and on the island — "**Transplanted Monuments**".
Nagarjunakonda finds include **Santamula's Ashvamedha** altar and **30+** stupas.
The site was submerged after **1960**.

n395e6fb2b49.s: Which museum is chiefly associated with the Mahachaitya and the white limestone sculpture of the Amaravati School?
n395e6fb2b49.x: The Amaravati site museum is associated with the Amaravati Mahachaitya and the white limestone sculptures of the Amaravati School.
xa: Many Amaravati relics went to **London and Madras** museums.
"**Discover Andhra**" promotes a Buddhist circuit — **Amaravati, Bavikonda, Thotlakonda**.
**Baudhasree Archaeological Museum** is at **Guntur**.

nc043f9416ae.s: Which one of the following was identified as an unfinished item of the 2014 bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Reconstruction of the 153-foot gopuram at Mangalagiri
Transfer of all temple conservation functions to the Archaeological Survey of India
nc043f9416ae.x: The division of museum antiques remained one of the unfinished items arising from the 2014 bifurcation.
nc043f9416ae.tq: Apply the institutional consequence to the specific unresolved bifurcation issue.
xs: The **division of museum antiques** is an unfinished item of the **2014** bifurcation — option **(4)** is correct.
AP formed a committee under the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014** to identify and transfer its share.
xa: G.O. of **31 Dec 2025**; chair **Tejaswi Podapati**.
The former **AP State Museum**, Hyderabad, is now the **Telangana State Museum**.
The **Salar Jung Museum** (Hyderabad) is a museum of national importance.

n3fee15049d6.s: Which committee of 1949 helped set the agenda for land reform in India?
n3fee15049d6.x: The Kumarappa Committee of 1949 set the land reform agenda; Phase I of land reform covered 1947-70.
xa: **Prakasam Committee (1938)** had recommended **abolition of intermediaries**.
**Raj Krishna** classified reforms as **liberative, distributive, organisational and developmental**.
Ceilings came in two rounds — **1950s** and **early 1970s**.

n01b4cadd17a.s: Which land reform brought about two crore tenants into direct contact with the State?
n01b4cadd17a.x: Abolition of intermediaries, regarded as the most successful reform, brought about two crore tenants into direct contact with the State.
xa: It covered about **40%** of cultivated area.
⚠ Critics: abolition **only changed the revenue hierarchy**.
**Consolidation** succeeded in **Punjab, Haryana, western UP**.

n5acc41f9dc7.s: Operation Barga (1977), the notable exception to failed tenancy reform, was carried out in:
n5acc41f9dc7.x: Operation Barga (1977) was carried out in West Bengal, not Kerala.
xa: **Oral leases**, **benami transfers** and **exemptions** defeated tenancy and ceiling laws.
Failure on ceilings and tenancy fed the **Naxalbari (1967)** revolt.
Tenancy/ceiling reforms are Raj Krishna's **"distributive"** type.

n6238bf3eec6.s: Under the land-ceiling guidelines of 1972, the unit for applying the ceiling was the:
n6238bf3eec6.x: From 1972 the family, not the individual landholder, was made the unit for ceilings.
xa: AP's first ceiling law: **AP Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings Act, 1961**.
AP's **1973** Act set **10-27 acres wet** or **35-54 acres dry** per family unit.
⚠ Max retainable under the 1973 Act = **54 acres of 'K' grade** land.

o: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
n36a0fcaa582.x: Land consolidation achieved notable success in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.
n36a0fcaa582.tq: Match the reform with the geographical region where it succeeded.
xs: **Consolidation** succeeded in **Punjab, Haryana and western UP** — option **(4)**.
It is one of the land-reform measures alongside abolition, tenancy reform and ceiling.
xa: **Operation Barga (1977)** in **West Bengal** was the exception for tenancy reform.
Other components: **cooperative farming** and **computerisation of land records**.
Raj Krishna's classes: **liberative, distributive, organisational, developmental**.

n162d85bbba8.s: After the abolition of intermediaries in Telangana, Jagir and Sarfekhas lands became:
n162d85bbba8.x: Jagir and Sarfekhas lands became Diwani, or ryotwari, lands after the abolition measures.
xa: The **Hyderabad Jagirdari Abolition** Regulation (**1949**) abolished intermediaries in Telangana.
Andhra's estates went under the **Madras Estates** Act (**1948**).
Background: **Prakasam Committee (1938)** and the Madras **Zamindari Abolition Bill**, **1947**.

n00ac450c19c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Telangana inams legislation?
o: The Telangana Inams Act was enacted in 1955.
The 1967 extension of the Andhra Inams Act to Telangana was upheld by the High Court.
Religious and charitable inams were exempted.
The Act was stalled in courts.
n00ac450c19c.x: The 1967 extension of the Andhra Inams Act to Telangana was struck down, not upheld, by the High Court.
xa: The **Andhra Inams** Act is of **1956**.
Telangana's jagirs were abolished by the **Hyderabad Jagirdari Abolition** Regulation, **1949**.
**Jagir and Sarfekhas** lands became **Diwani (ryotwari)**.

nff8c478ed5a.s: The Prakasam Committee, constituted in 1938, recommended:
o: Declaration of Telugu as a Classical Language
nff8c478ed5a.x: The Prakasam Committee of 1938 recommended the abolition of intermediaries.
nff8c478ed5a.tq: Match the committee with its reform recommendation.
xs: The **Prakasam Committee (1938)** recommended **abolition of intermediaries** — option **(3)**.
It formed the background, with the Madras Assembly's **Zamindari Abolition Bill** (**1947**), to the **Madras Estates** Act (**1948**).
xa: The **Kumarappa Committee** (**1949**) was Congress's agenda-setter for land reforms.
The **Subba Rao Committee** report led to the **AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956**.
Abolition covered about **40%** of cultivated area.

n8eec6e9b796.s: The AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956, prescribed a minimum lease period of:
n8eec6e9b796.x: The Act required written lease deeds and leases of at least six years; it came into force in 1961.
xa: It was passed in **1956** on the **Subba Rao Committee** report.
⚠ Passed **1956**, in force **1961** — same year as the first ceiling Act.
**AP New Tenancy Act, 2024 (planned):** tenants get rights on the crop, **not the land**.

n8faf809ca18.s: The first residential school in Andhra Pradesh (1971) was set up at:
n8faf809ca18.x: The first residential school was set up at Sarvail in Nalgonda district in 1971, under P.V. Narasimha Rao.
xa: PVNR (CM **1971-73**) also had the AP Cabinet pass the **Land Reforms Bill**.
NTR's scheme: **Rs 2 per kg rice** (**1983**).
AP universities: **Nagarjuna** and **Kakatiya** (**1976**).

n39d022dc1a8.s: The First Constitutional Amendment was significant for land reforms because it:
o: abolished all tenancy arrangements throughout India
shielded zamindari abolition measures from legal challenge
n39d022dc1a8.x: The First Amendment provided constitutional protection to zamindari abolition measures, helping shield them from legal challenge.
n39d022dc1a8.tq: Connect a constitutional amendment with its land-reform consequence.
xs: The **First Amendment** **shielded zamindari abolition** — option **(3)**.
Its **75th anniversary** fell on **18 June 2026**.
xa: **First State to abolish zamindari:** **UP (1950)**; ⚠ Madras's **1948** Act was earlier.
Abolition of intermediaries was the **most successful** reform (about **2 crore** tenants).
**Art. 371D** came by the **32nd Amendment**, not the First.

nbb2bd518315.s: The failure of land reforms to overcome ceiling and tenancy problems contributed to the emergence of the:
nbb2bd518315.x: The failure of land reforms, particularly regarding ceilings and tenancy, contributed to the Naxalbari revolt of 1967.
nbb2bd518315.tq: Link a policy failure to its stated historical consequence.
xs: Failure on ceilings and tenancy fed the **Naxalbari (1967)** revolt — option **(2)**.
**Bhoodan (1951)** was a voluntary land-gift movement, not a revolt.
xa: **Oral leases, benami transfers and exemptions** defeated tenancy and ceiling laws.
Abolition **only changed the revenue hierarchy**.
**Operation Barga (1977)** in **West Bengal** was the tenancy exception.

n53d65c6717e.s: Transfers of land in others' names to defeat ceiling laws are known as:
n53d65c6717e.x: Benami transfers helped defeat the objectives of ceiling laws; oral leases and exemptions also weakened land reforms.
xa: AP's **1961** ceiling Act was weak due to **benami transfers** and exemptions.
Tenancy reform was also defeated by **"voluntary surrenders"**.
The failure fed the **Naxalbari (1967)** revolt.

n89685cda11c.s: Under the planned Andhra Pradesh New Tenancy Act, 2024, tenants get rights over:
o: The land after six years of cultivation
n89685cda11c.x: Tenants get rights on the crop, not the land, along with entitlement cards and access to crop loans.
xa: AP's earlier **Andhra Area Tenancy Act** (**1956**) required written lease deeds and a lease of at least **6 years**.
Telangana's **1950** Act made **6 years'** cultivators **protected tenants**.

n33971aa44ab.s: The Hyderabad Jagirdari Abolition Regulation was enacted in:
n33971aa44ab.x: The Hyderabad Jagirdari Abolition Regulation was enacted in 1949 to abolish intermediaries in Telangana.
n33971aa44ab.tq: Use the adjacent-year distinction among the early Hyderabad and Andhra land laws.
xs: The **Hyderabad Jagirdari Abolition Regulation** dates to **1949** (PYQ) — option **(2)**; it abolished **intermediaries in Telangana**.
**1948** = Madras Estates Act (Andhra); **1950** = Hyderabad Tenancy Act; **1956** = Andhra Inams Act.
xa: ⚠ Andhra = **Estates** Act **1948**; Telangana = **Jagirdari** Regulation **1949**.
**Jagir and Sarfekhas** lands became **Diwani (ryotwari)** lands.
**Abolition of Telangana Inams Act**: **1955**.

ne5aed249e8e.s: Intermediaries (zamindari estates) in the Andhra area were abolished mainly by the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act of:
ne5aed249e8e.x: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act is of 1948. 1938 is the Prakasam Committee that recommended abolition; 1955 is the Abolition of Telangana Inams Act; 1967 is the extension of the Andhra Inams Act to Telangana, struck down by the High Court.
ne5aed249e8e.tq: Andhra: Madras Estates Act 1948; Telangana: Jagirdari Abolition Regulation 1949.
xs: Andhra's zamindari estates were abolished by the **Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act**, **1948** — option **(2)**.
**1938** = **Prakasam Committee**; **1955** = **Telangana Inams Act**; **1967** = Andhra Inams Act extension to Telangana, **struck down**.
xa: APP gives **1949**, in force **1950**.
Andhra inams: **Andhra Inams Act**, **1956**.
⚠ Andhra = **Estates** Act **1948**; Telangana = **Jagirdari** Regulation **1949**.

n535debf98b5.s: The AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956 was based on the report of the:
n535debf98b5.x: The AP Andhra Area Tenancy Act, 1956 was based on the report of the Subba Rao Committee.
n535debf98b5.tq: Match the committee with the legislation it influenced.
xs: The **AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956** was based on the **Subba Rao Committee** report — option **(1)**.
The **Kumarappa Committee** (**1949**) set Congress's national agenda; it was not behind this Act.
xa: The Act required **written lease deeds** and a lease of **at least 6 years**.
It came into force in **1961**.
⚠ **1961** is also the year of AP's first **ceiling** Act.

n218c9fb511f.s: The maximum area retainable under the 1973 AP Land Reforms Act was:
n218c9fb511f.x: The maximum retainable area was 54 acres of ‘K’ grade, the lowest-grade, land.
n218c9fb511f.tq: Match the maximum ceiling with the specific land-grade classification.
xs: Maximum retainable = **54 acres of 'K' grade land** (the lowest grade) — option **(2)** (PYQ key).
**27** acres is the top of the **wet** range and **35** acres the bottom of the **dry** range, not the maximum.
xa: Ceiling per family unit: **10-27 acres wet** or **35-54 acres dry**.
The Act is of **1973** (PYQ), under **CM P.V. Narasimha Rao**.
AP's first ceiling law was of **1961**.

n35cee7c0884.s: The raising of the BC reservation in Andhra Pradesh to 44% in 1986 was based on the report of the:
n35cee7c0884.x: The Muralidhar Rao Commission (1982) led to NTR raising the BC quota to 44% in 1986, later struck down by the High Court. The Subba Rao Committee was behind the AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act 1956; the Prakasam Committee (1938) recommended abolition of intermediaries; the Kumarappa Committee (1949) set the land-reform agenda.
n35cee7c0884.tq: BC 44% (1986) = Muralidhar Rao Commission (1982), NTR; struck down by HC.
xs: The **44%** BC quota (**1986**) followed the **Muralidhar Rao Commission** (**1982**) — option **(1)**.
**Subba Rao Committee** → **Andhra Area Tenancy Act, 1956**; **Prakasam Committee (1938)** → abolition of intermediaries; **Kumarappa Committee** (**1949**) → land-reform agenda.
xa: The **High Court** struck down the raised quota.
Backward Muslims got **4%** (**BC-E**) in **2007**.
**Art. 371D** gives local-cadre reservation in jobs and education.

n20464331d0f.s: A major limitation of the abolition of zamindari and jagirdari was that it:
o: Changed the revenue hierarchy but left tenancy and landholding inequalities
n20464331d0f.x: Abolition mainly altered the revenue hierarchy; it did not by itself resolve tenancy problems and unequal landholding.
xa: Abolition still was the **most successful** reform, covering about **40%** of cultivated area.
**Jagir and Sarfekhas** lands became **Diwani (ryotwari)**.
Tenancy reform was defeated by **"voluntary surrenders"**.

n825980de08e.x: Mangroth in Hamirpur, Uttar Pradesh, became the first Gramdan village in 1952; Bhoodan began at Pochampalli.
xa: Bhoodan began on **18 April 1951** under **Acharya Vinoba Bhave**.
Gramdan = whole village gifted to the community.
⚠ **54 acres** is the 'K' grade ceiling under AP's **1973** Act, not the Bhoodan gift.

naf08d74b1bf.s: The AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation 1/1959, amended by 1/1970, primarily:
o: Barred transfer of land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals
Created the National Land Reforms Council
Permitted unrestricted transfer of tribal land to non-tribals
Abolished all tenancy in the Andhra area
naf08d74b1bf.x: The Regulation barred the transfer of land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals.
naf08d74b1bf.tq: Apply the protective purpose of a tribal-area land-transfer regulation.
xs: **Regulation 1/1959** (amended **1/1970**) **bars transfer of land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals** — option **(1)**.
It applies to **Agency (tribal) areas**.
xa: The **Eluru agency land dispute** under **APSALT Regulation 1/59 and 1/70** is still in court (**17 Jan 2026**).
**Fifth Schedule** covers Scheduled Areas outside the North-East; **PESA 1996** applies there.
**Elwin** argued for **limits on land alienation**.

n7f863bd7d59.s: Which approach to tribal policy was favoured by Jawaharlal Nehru over both isolation and forced assimilation?
o: Forced assimilation into the dominant society
n7f863bd7d59.x: Nehru rejected both the museum approach of isolation and forced assimilation, favouring integration while respecting tribal identity and institutions.
n7f863bd7d59.tq: Directly distinguish between two rejected approaches and the preferred policy.
xs: Nehru chose **integration** respecting tribal identity — option **(1)**.
He **rejected isolation** (the **"museum"** approach) and **forced assimilation**.
xa: **Tribal Panchsheel:** develop along their **own genius**; respect rights in **land and forests**.
Encourage **tribal languages**; train tribes to **run their own administration**; **avoid over-administration**.
**Verrier Elwin** wrote **A Philosophy for NEFA**.

n9bc3d0ab22c.s: Which of the following is NOT a principle of the Tribal Panchsheel?
o: Tribes should develop along the lines of their own genius.
Tribal areas should be subjected to maximum administrative control.
Tribal languages should be encouraged and preserved.
Tribal communities should be trained to run their own administration.
n9bc3d0ab22c.x: The Tribal Panchsheel advocated avoiding over-administration, so 'maximum administrative control' is not one of its principles.
xa: It also says respect tribal rights in **land and forests**.
Some notes credit its formulation to **Elwin**, under Nehru's influence.
Nehru's policy: **integration**, not the **"museum"** approach.

nab874977cfc.s: Verrier Elwin's work titled A Philosophy for NEFA primarily argued for which of the following?
o: Cultural autonomy and limits on land alienation
Complete assimilation and unrestricted land transfer
Expansion of commercial farming in tribal areas
nab874977cfc.x: A Philosophy for NEFA argued for cultural autonomy and limitations on the alienation of tribal land.
nab874977cfc.tq: Link the author and work with its central argument.
xs: **A Philosophy for NEFA** argued for **cultural autonomy + limits on land alienation** — option **(2)**.
NEFA was a **policy laboratory** for **Elwin's** approach.
xa: Some notes credit the **Tribal Panchsheel** to **Elwin**, under Nehru's influence.
NEFA (now **Arunachal Pradesh**) was run through the **Governor of Assam**.
AP's **Regulation 1/1959** likewise bars land transfer to non-tribals in Scheduled Areas.

ned2ba7175a5.s: The formulation of the Tribal Panchsheel, under Nehru's influence, is credited to:
ned2ba7175a5.x: The Tribal Panchsheel is credited to Verrier Elwin, under the influence of Jawaharlal Nehru.
xa: Elwin wrote **A Philosophy for NEFA** — cultural autonomy + limits on land alienation.
Panchsheel: **avoid over-administration**; train tribes to run their own administration.
Nehru rejected the **"museum"** approach.

n34a666aabfc.s: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 applies to:
o: All urban areas in the North-East
Scheduled Areas covered by the Fifth Schedule
Only Union Territories with tribal populations
Autonomous districts under the Sixth Schedule only
n34a666aabfc.x: PESA 1996 applies to Scheduled Areas in states covered by the Fifth Schedule; it does not apply to the Sixth Schedule autonomous district areas.
n34a666aabfc.tq: Separate PESA's Fifth Schedule coverage from Sixth Schedule autonomous councils.
xs: **PESA 1996** applies only to **Fifth Schedule** Scheduled Areas — option **(2)**.
The Fifth Schedule covers Scheduled Areas in **states other than the North-East**.
xa: **Tana Bhagats** cited **PESA** and the **CNT Act 1908** against a Bharatmala highway (**4 Jun 2026**).
AP's **APSALT Regulation 1/59 and 1/70** bars land transfer to non-tribals.
Tribal Panchsheel: respect tribal rights in **land and forests**.

ncc19d4d0e43.s: Goa, Daman and Diu were integrated into India through:
ncc19d4d0e43.x: Goa, Daman and Diu were integrated through Operation Vijay; Dadra and Nagar Haveli was freed separately in 1954.
xa: Goa became a UT under the **12th Amendment, 1962**; full state in **1987**.
Pondicherry: de facto transfer **1 Nov 1954**; UT by the **14th Amendment, 1962**.
⚠ **10th** = Dadra; **12th** = Goa; **14th** = Pondicherry.

n17664343af8.s: Dadra and Nagar Haveli was freed in 1954 and subsequently made a Union Territory by which Constitutional Amendment?
n17664343af8.x: The Tenth Amendment Act of 1961 made Dadra and Nagar Haveli a Union Territory.
n17664343af8.tq: Match the territory with the correct Constitutional Amendment.
xs: **Dadra & Nagar Haveli** was made a UT by the **10th Amendment, 1961** — option **(1)**.
**12th Amendment, 1962** = **Goa**; **14th Amendment, 1962** = **Pondicherry**.
xa: Dadra & Nagar Haveli was **freed in 1954**.
Goa was taken by **Operation Vijay**, **18-19 Dec 1961**.
Goa became a full state in **1987**.

n5244ba1f6e2.s: NEFA, which is now known as Arunachal Pradesh, was administered initially through the:
n5244ba1f6e2.x: NEFA was run through the Governor of Assam and served as a policy laboratory for Elwin's approach.
n5244ba1f6e2.tq: Test the administrative authority associated with a former regional name.
xs: **NEFA** was run through the **Governor of Assam** — option **(3)**.
It was a **policy laboratory** for **Elwin's** approach.
xa: NEFA became a UT in **1972** and a state in **1987**.
**Verrier Elwin** wrote **A Philosophy for NEFA**.
⚠ **1987** = Arunachal **and** Goa statehood.

nec466868c93.s: The Centre responded to the Naga question in 1963 principally by granting:
o: Sixth Schedule status to the whole of Assam
nec466868c93.x: The Centre addressed the Naga question in 1963 by creating the state of Nagaland. The demand for Greater Nagalim associated with the NSCN continued thereafter.
nec466868c93.tq: Distinguish the actual constitutional response from the continuing political demand.
xs: The Centre answered the **Naga National Council** by granting **statehood to Nagaland** in **1963** — option **(1)**.
Nagaland got **full statehood**, not UT status; independence was **not** granted.
xa: The **Greater Nagalim** demand (**NSCN**) continues.
NNC was led by **A.Z. Phizo**.

n8649edc3542.s: The Madras Devadasi (Prevention of Dedication) Act of December 1947 was piloted by:
n8649edc3542.x: The Act was piloted by Muthulakshmi Reddy; Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu was a reformer who campaigned against the Bhogam system.
xa: The **AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act** came in **1988**.
It also covers **Jogini, Basivi, Matangi** dedication.
**Dubagunta (Nellore)** women's anti-arrack movement: **1992**.

n751d79afb41.s: Which of the following practices were also covered by the Andhra Pradesh Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1988?
n751d79afb41.x: The 1988 Act also covered Jogini, Basivi and Matangi forms of dedication.
n751d79afb41.tq: Recall the complete group of practices covered by the legislation.
xs: The **1988** AP Act also covers **Jogini, Basivi and Matangi** dedication — option **(4)**.
**Jagir, Sarfekhas, Inam**, **Ryotwari, Zamindari, Diwani** are land-tenure terms, not forms of dedication.
xa: The **Madras** Act (**December 1947**) was piloted by **Muthulakshmi Reddy**.
**Bhogam** is another name for the Devadasi system.
**Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu** campaigned against it.

n3af7a9ab3b9.s: Total prohibition was introduced in Andhra Pradesh under N.T. Rama Rao in:
n3af7a9ab3b9.x: Total prohibition came in 1995, after the Dubagunta movement (1992) and the arrack ban (1993); it was lifted in 1997.
xa: Dubagunta is in **Nellore**.
NTR also launched the **Rs 2 per kg rice** scheme (**1983**).
Chandrababu Naidu also launched **Janmabhoomi** (**1997**).

naf3ad7dc012.s: Article 371D, which implemented the Six-Point Formula, was inserted by the:
naf3ad7dc012.x: The Six-Point Formula of 1973 was implemented through Article 371D, inserted by the 32nd Constitutional Amendment in 1973.
xa: **Muralidhar Rao Commission** (**1982**) → BC quota **44%** (**1986**), struck down by the High Court.
**4%** reservation for backward Muslims (**BC-E**): **2007**.
Nehru's **NIC** (**1961**) was another integration tool.

n32501c468bd.s: Backward Muslims in Andhra Pradesh were given a 4% quota under the category:
n32501c468bd.x: Backward Muslims got 4% reservation under BC-E, introduced in 2007.
xa: The **44%** quota followed the **Muralidhar Rao Commission** (**1982**) and was **struck down by the High Court**.
**Art. 371D** (**32nd Amendment, 1973**) gives local-cadre reservation.
The **Six-Point Formula** is of **1973**.

n262bd910556.s: Raj Krishna classified land reforms into which four categories?
n262bd910556.x: Raj Krishna classified land reforms as liberative, distributive, organisational and developmental.
n262bd910556.tq: Recall the complete four-part classification without substituting broader policy categories.
xs: **Raj Krishna** classified land reforms as **liberative, distributive, organisational and developmental** — option **(1)**.
**Abolition** = **"liberative"**; tenancy/ceiling = **"distributive"**.
xa: These reforms broke the **zamindari-jagirdari** order.
The **Kumarappa Committee** (**1949**) set the reform agenda.
**Prakasam Committee (1938)** recommended abolition of intermediaries.

ne8a67de945b.s: The National Integration Council was set up in 1961 by Jawaharlal Nehru after the:
ne8a67de945b.x: The National Integration Council was established by Nehru in 1961 after the National Integration Conference.
ne8a67de945b.tq: Link the institution to its immediate constitutional-political origin.
xs: **Nehru** set up the **National Integration Council** in **1961** after the **National Integration Conference** — option **(1)**.
The Conference addressed **communalism, casteism, regionalism and linguism**.
xa: Other tools vs regionalism: **Art. 44**, **Art. 51A**, the **Fifth, Sixth and Eighth Schedules**.
**Anti-Hindi agitations in Tamil Nadu (1937, 1965, 1986)** → **two-language formula**.
Nehru's tribal policy was **integration**.

n936fcc6ed12.s: Which institution was the first open university in India?
o: Andhra Pradesh Open University, now Dr B.R. Ambedkar Open University
n936fcc6ed12.x: The Andhra Pradesh Open University, now named Dr B.R. Ambedkar Open University, was the first open university in India and was established in 1982.
n936fcc6ed12.tq: Identify the institution by its distinctive national distinction.
xs: India's first open university was the **AP Open University**, now **Dr B.R. Ambedkar Open University** (**1982**) — option **(4)**.
**Telugu University** = **1985**; **Nagarjuna** and **Kakatiya** = **1976**.
xa: ⚠ First health university = **NTR UHS (1986)** — do not confuse.
First residential school: **Sarvail (Nalgonda)**, **1971**.
**Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University**: **1985**.

nd956019e7ed.s: Who described a tribe as a 'segmental organisation' of equivalent multi-family groups?
nd956019e7ed.x: Marshall Sahlins described a tribe as a segmental organisation of equivalent multi-family groups.
xa: Scheduled Tribes are notified by the **President** after consulting the **Governor**.
Scheduled Areas fall under the **Fifth Schedule**.

n35019cc9b69.s: Who can amend the notified list of Scheduled Tribes under Article 342(2)?
n35019cc9b69.x: Only Parliament can amend the list (Art. 342(2)); the President only notifies it after consulting the Governor.
xa: Tribe = **"segmental organisation"** of multi-family groups (**Marshall Sahlins**).
ST = **8.6%** of India (**Census 2011**).
**MP** has the largest tribal population.

n34949a24a6c.s: Chenchu social organisation is best described as:
n34949a24a6c.x: The Chenchus are an endogamous tribe with exogamous clans (kulams/gothrams); they are patriarchal and patrilineal.
xa: Village offices: **Raju** (Bhoomani), **Mantri** (Kumakula), **Kolagadu** (Dasari / Uttaluri / Mandla).
These three, from different clans, **officiate marriages**.
Youth dormitory example: **Ghotul** of the **Muria** (Chhattisgarh).

n5de1d13a2e7.s: Idital wall paintings are associated with which tribal community?
n5de1d13a2e7.x: Idital wall paintings are associated with the Savara, also known as Sora, community.
n5de1d13a2e7.tq: Match a distinctive art form with its tribal community.
xs: **Idital** wall paintings belong to the **Savara (Sora)** — option **(3)**.
**Gond** art is from **MP**; **Pithora** is of the **Rathwa** (Gujarat-MP).
xa: Other tribal arts: **Warli** (Maharashtra), **Bhil**.
Dhimsa is also danced by the **Savara** (per CDCA).
Agency crafts include **bamboo work**.

n690d8cf645b.s: Pithora painting is particularly associated with the
o: Rathwa of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh
n690d8cf645b.x: Pithora is associated with the Rathwa community of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.
n690d8cf645b.tq: Identify the community and region linked with a named art tradition.
xs: **Pithora** is the art of the **Rathwa** (**Gujarat-MP**) — option **(2)**.
**Warli** is Maharashtra's art; the **Savara** paint **Idital**; the **Koya** are known for the **Kommu** dance.
xa: **Gond** art is from **MP**.
**Bhil** art is another comparison form.
**MP** has the largest tribal population.

ne52028a684c.s: The agency economy of the Araku belt rests on:
o: Podu, minor forest produce, coffee and horticulture
Tea plantations, jute mills and inland shipping
Marine fishing, salt production and shipbuilding
ne52028a684c.x: The agency economy combines podu (shifting cultivation) and minor forest produce with coffee and horticulture in the Araku belt.
xa: Agency crafts: **bamboo work**.
**Idital** wall paintings of the **Savara (Sora)**.
Araku tribes' spring festival: **Eetela Panduga (Chaitrapurab)**.

nb3107e85358.s: Eetela Panduga, also known as Chaitrapurab, is associated with
o: the harvest festival of the Lambadas
the birth ceremony of Koya boys
the spring festival of the Araku tribes
nb3107e85358.x: Eetela Panduga or Chaitrapurab is the spring festival of the Araku tribes, during which Dhimsa is danced.
nb3107e85358.tq: Link a regional festival with its tribe and season.
xs: **Eetela Panduga (Chaitrapurab)** is the **spring festival of the Araku tribes** — option **(3)**.
**Dhimsa** is danced at it (**Aug 2026**).
Newborn-son rites are **Heli Panduga** (Lambadi); **Modakondamma** is a separate **Paderu** jatara.
xa: **Seethala Panduga** (Ashada) is the Lambadi cattle festival.
Lambadi Deepavali = **Kalimas**.
Dhimsa region: **ASR** and **Parvathipuram Manyam**.

na853696f553.s: Deepavali is called ____ by the Lambadis.
na853696f553.x: The Lambadis call Deepavali Kalimas; Jari Gundu is another name for Heli Panduga.
xa: Seethala Panduga falls in **Ashada**; **Seethala Mata** guards against **smallpox**.
**Lambadi** dance: Lambada/Sugali (Banjara) **women**.
Araku tribes' spring festival: **Eetela Panduga**.

n6bb285c5991.s: Modakondamma, in whose honour an annual tribal jatara is held, is the goddess of the:
n6bb285c5991.x: Modakondamma is regarded as the goddess of the Paderu agency, where an annual tribal jatara is held.
xa: Araku tribes celebrate **Eetela Panduga (Chaitrapurab)** in spring.
**Dhimsa** belongs to **ASR** and **Parvathipuram Manyam**.
Lambadi festivals: **Seethala Panduga**, **Heli Panduga**, **Kalimas**.

nebc365dca8b.s: The Guinness World Record for the largest Dhimsa dance (July 2026) was set at:
o: Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram
nebc365dca8b.x: Over 13,000 tribal women and girl students danced at the Bhogapuram airport in Vizianagaram; the certificate went to the AP Tribal Welfare Department.
xa: Dhimsa: **15-20 women** per circle, hands on shoulders.
**World Adivasi Day** festival: **Tummalapalli Kalakshetram, Vijayawada** (**11 Aug 2026**).
Dhimsa origin traced to **Koraput**.

n2b97c855fef.s: Who led the Rampa Rebellion of 1922–24 in the Eastern Ghats?
n2b97c855fef.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa Rebellion in the Eastern Ghats from 1922 to 1924.
xa: The **Bhogapuram (Vizianagaram)** airport is named after him; it hosted the **Guinness** Dhimsa record.
The **ASR** district is a Dhimsa region, with **Parvathipuram Manyam**.
Agency economy: **Podu** and **minor forest produce**.

n5f163fbac97.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Scheduled Tribe profile (Census 2011)?
o: Odisha has the largest tribal population.
n5f163fbac97.x: Madhya Pradesh, not Odisha, has the largest tribal population; the other three statements are correct.
xa: **Gond** art is from **MP**; **Gussadi** is the Gond dance on the Telangana side.
Tribe = **"segmental organisation"** (**Marshall Sahlins**).
STs are notified by the **President** after consulting the **Governor**.

n12cd0482584.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Regulating Act, 1773?
o: It abolished the Court of Directors.
It made the Presidencies of Bombay and Madras subordinate to Bengal.
It was based on the report of a committee under Lord North.
It was the British Parliament's first step to control the East India Company.
n12cd0482584.x: The Regulating Act did not abolish the Court of Directors, which survived until the 1858 Act.
xa: ⚠ "Regulating Act abolished the Court of Directors" was the **incorrect statement** in **APPSC-GS 2019**.
The Act made **Warren Hastings** the **Governor-General of Bengal** and set up a **4-member Executive Council**.
It provided for the **Supreme Court at Calcutta**, set up in **1774**; first Chief Justice **Sir Elijah Impey**.
It **banned private trade** and **bribes**; the trigger was the Company's financial crisis and a loan of about **£1 million** (**1772**).

nfbd01009858.s: Under the Regulating Act, 1773, the Governor-General of Bengal was assisted by an Executive Council of:
nfbd01009858.x: The Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings) had a four-member Executive Council; Pitt's India Act later reduced it to three.
xa: The Charter Act **1793** extended the override power to all future GGs and presidency Governors.
**Pitt's India Act 1784** reduced the GG's council to **3**.
The Regulating Act was based on the report of a committee under **Lord North**; it was the **first parliamentary control** over the EIC.
⚠ The Regulating Act did **NOT abolish the Court of Directors** — it survived until **1858** (the "incorrect statement" in APPSC-GS 2019).

n0e80025ea17.s: The Act of 1767 required the East India Company to pay the British Government an annual sum of:
n0e80025ea17.x: The Act of 1767 fixed an annual payment of £400,000.
xa: Under Pitt's India Act, the **Board of Control** handled **political** affairs and the **Court of Directors** **commercial** affairs.
Pitt's India Act reduced the **GG's council** to **3** members.
The **Act of 1786** let the Governor-General **override his Council**; **Lord Cornwallis** first used this power.

nf6d9eb3849c.s: Under the Charter Act of 1793, the salaries of the Board of Control were charged to:
nf6d9eb3849c.x: The Charter Act of 1793 charged the Board of Control's salaries to Indian revenues and increased the Governor-General's control over Bombay and Madras.
xa: The 1793 Act **extended the trade monopoly** for **20 years**.
It extended the **override power** (first given by the Act of **1786** to Cornwallis) to all future GGs.
Charter renewals: **1793, 1813, 1833**; the **1853** Act fixed no term.

n85c822fa315.s: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly except in:
n85c822fa315.x: The 1813 Act did not end the monopoly completely: tea and the China trade remained exceptions. It also permitted missionaries to enter India.
xa: The 1813 Act gave **Rs 1 lakh** a year for literature, science and education.
Evangelical pressure — **Charles Grant**, **William Wilberforce** — made 1813 a turning point.
⚠ **1833** = all trade ended, Company **purely administrative**.

n7309bca1b62.s: The Charter Act of 1833, the final step towards centralisation, made the East India Company:
o: A trading body with its monopoly restored
A Crown department under the India Office
n7309bca1b62.x: The 1833 Act ended the Company's commercial functions and made it purely administrative, while centralising legislation in the Governor-General-in-Council.
xa: The GG of Bengal became the **Governor-General of India** (**William Bentinck**).
A **Law Commission** under **Macaulay** was set up — origin of the **Law Ministry**.
No Indian was to be debarred from office by **religion, birth, descent or colour**; open competition was attempted (not implemented).
The 1833 Act is also called the **Saint Helena Act**.

n60f72cc2a4b.s: How many legislative members did the Charter Act of 1853 add to the Governor-General's Council?
n60f72cc2a4b.x: The 1853 Act added six legislative members, separating legislative from executive functions of the Council.
xa: Territories were held **"in trust for Her Majesty... until Parliament should otherwise provide"** (APPSC-GS **2018**).
It created a functioning central **Indian Legislative Council** (mini-parliament).
Open competition was given effect by the **Macaulay Committee (1854)**.
**1853** was the **last Charter Act**.

n9bbca231ab3.s: Under the Charter Act of 1853, the Company's territories were held:
o: For a fixed period of twenty years only
As independent territories under the Governor-General
As permanent private property of the Court of Directors
In trust for the Crown until Parliament otherwise provided
n9bbca231ab3.x: The Act declared that the territories were held in trust for Her Majesty until Parliament otherwise provided.
n9bbca231ab3.tq: Focus on the legal status phrase rather than the administrative changes surrounding it.
xs: Under the **Charter Act 1853**, territories were held **in trust for the Crown until Parliament otherwise provided** — option **(4)**.
The words were **"in trust for Her Majesty... until Parliament should otherwise provide"** (APPSC-GS **2018**).
Option 1 is wrong: the 1853 Act fixed **no period** — earlier renewals ran **20 years**.
xa: The 1853 Act **separated legislative and executive functions** and added **6 legislative members**.
It introduced **open competition** for the civil services.
The **GoI Act 1858** then ended Company rule; the **Crown** took over.

n845821bb735.s: The Law Commission headed by Macaulay, regarded as the origin of the present Law Ministry, was set up under which Act?
n845821bb735.x: The Charter Act of 1833 (Saint Helena Act) created a Law Commission under Macaulay, the origin of the Law Ministry. The Regulating Act 1773 set up the Supreme Court at Calcutta, the 1813 Act admitted missionaries and gave Rs 1 lakh for education, and the 1853 Act separated the legislative and executive functions of the GG's Council.
n845821bb735.tq: 1833 = GG of India + Macaulay Law Commission + end of all trade.
xs: The **Law Commission** under **Macaulay** came under the **Charter Act 1833** — option **(3)**.
IYB **2026** dates the **Ministry of Law and Justice**'s origin to the Charter Act **1833**.
**1773** set up the Supreme Court at Calcutta; **1813** admitted missionaries; **1853** separated legislative and executive functions.
xa: 1833 made **William Bentinck** the first **Governor-General of India**.
It centralised legislative power in the **GG-in-Council** — the "final step towards centralisation".
**Macaulay** also led the **Macaulay Committee (1854)** on open competition.

nf71f69358a2.s: The British Parliament intervened in the Company's affairs in Bengal in 1772 mainly because of:
o: The appointment of the first Viceroy
The Carnatic Wars and the Mysore conflict
The famine, falling revenue and the Company's financial crisis
The transfer of Bombay and Madras to Parliament
nf71f69358a2.x: The Bengal famine, declining revenue and the Company's financial crisis compelled Parliament to intervene in 1772.
xa: The Company sought a loan of about **£1 million** (**1772**).
The result was the **Regulating Act 1773** — the first parliamentary control over the EIC.
It was based on a committee report under **Lord North**.

ne48cbf7b2d0.s: Pitt's India Act, 1784 described the Company's territories in India as:
ne48cbf7b2d0.x: The Act described the territories as British possessions in India and made the Company subordinate to the State.
xa: This was **dual control / double government**.
The GG's council was reduced to **3**.
The Board of Control had **6 members**, incl. a **Secretary of State** + **Chancellor of the Exchequer**.

n051038d44e3.s: The Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774) initially had one Chief Justice and how many other judges?
n051038d44e3.x: It had one Chief Justice (Sir Elijah Impey) and three other judges.
xa: Later: **Madras Supreme Court 1801**; Madras High Court in the Charter Act **1853** era.
The **Federal Court** (**1935** Act) was set up at **Delhi** in **1937** — forerunner of the Supreme Court.
The Regulating Act also made **Bombay and Madras** subordinate to Bengal.

n6aa163d0dd3.s: The Governor-General's power to override his Council was first given to Lord Cornwallis by the Act of:
n6aa163d0dd3.x: The Act of 1786 gave the override power to Cornwallis; the Charter Act of 1793 extended it to all future Governors-General and Presidency Governors.
xa: Under the 1786 Act Cornwallis was also made **Commander-in-Chief**.
The 1793 Act said the C-in-C was **not ordinarily** a council member.
The Regulating Act **1773** gave the GG a **4-member** council.

n8921fafe840.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Indians' share in administration?
o: The Charter Act of 1833 said no Indian would be debarred from office by religion, birth, descent or colour.
The Charter Act of 1853 introduced open competition for the civil services.
The Macaulay Committee (1854) was set up to give effect to open competition.
The Charter Act of 1833 put open competition into actual operation.
n8921fafe840.x: The 1833 Act only attempted open competition, which was not implemented; open competition came with the 1853 Act.
xa: Under the **1861** Act the Viceroy **nominated Indians** — Raja of Benaras, Maharaja of Patiala, Sir Dinkar Rao.
**1909**: **Satyendra Sinha** became the first Indian on the Viceroy's Executive Council.
**1919**: **3 of 6** Executive Council members were Indian.

nd476f5e723d.s:
Under the Indian Councils Act, 1892, recommendations for nomination came from which of the following?
1. Universities
2. Municipalities
3. Chambers of commerce
Which of the above is/are correct?
nd476f5e723d.x: The 1892 Act's indirect system worked through recommendations from universities, municipalities and chambers of commerce.
xa: The practice began in **1892** (APPSC GS **2019** key).
1892 allowed **budget discussion** and questions, but **no vote**.
**1909** brought the first **formal** election and **separate electorate for Muslims**.

ne94193dce33.s: The Simon Commission, chaired by Sir John Simon, was appointed in:
ne94193dce33.x: The Simon Commission was appointed in 1927, two years before the scheduled review; all seven members were British and it was boycotted in India.
xa: The statutory commission was a provision of the **GoI Act 1919**.
1919 also provided a **Public Service Commission** (set up **1 October 1926**).
1919 created a **High Commissioner for India** in London.

nd936f6aa2fb.s: The principle of indirect election was introduced by the Indian Councils Act of:
nd936f6aa2fb.x: Indirect election began with the 1892 Act; nomination of Indians began in 1861 and separate electorates in 1909.
xa: **1909** = first **formal** election; **1892** = indirect start (APPSC GS **2019**).
First **Supreme Court at Calcutta** (**1774**: CJ + **3** judges) = Regulating Act **1773**.

n6bfcfa90caf.s: Which one of the following was the last Charter Act enacted by the British Parliament for the East India Company?
n6bfcfa90caf.x: The Charter Act of 1853 was the last Charter Act. The Government of India Act, 1858 subsequently transferred the governance of India from the East India Company to the Crown.
n6bfcfa90caf.tq: Distinguish the final Charter Act from the later Act that ended Company rule.
xs: The last Charter Act was the **Charter Act of 1853** — option **(2)**.
Renewals came every **20 years** (1793, 1813, 1833); **1853** fixed **no term**.
The **GoI Act 1858** is not a Charter Act: it ended Company rule and the **Crown** took over.
xa: 1853 held territories **"in trust for Her Majesty"**.
1853 separated **legislative and executive functions** and added **6 legislative members**.
It introduced **open competition** for civil services.

nindian-polity-22-5.s: Which of the following about the Charter Act, 1813 is INCORRECT?
o: It permitted Christian missionaries to work in India.
It completely abolished the Company's trade monopoly in India.
It retained the Company's monopoly over the tea and China trade.
It provided an annual grant of ₹1 lakh for education.
nindian-polity-22-5.x: The 1813 Act ended the Company's monopoly only partly, keeping the tea and China trade; complete abolition came in 1833.
n: The Charter Act was enacted in 1813. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Charter Act of 1813 abolished the Company’s trade monopoly in India except for the tea trade. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Charter Act of 1813 retained the Company’s monopoly over China trade. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Charter Act of 1813 permitted Christian missionaries to operate in India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Charter Act of 1813 allocated an annual grant of ₹1 lakh for Indian education. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The trade monopoly in India was partially abolished in 1813. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The tea trade monopoly was retained in 1813. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The China trade monopoly was retained in 1813. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
xa: The monopoly was **completely abolished** by the **Charter Act 1833**.
⚠ Trap: some notes say 1833 kept "tea and China" trade — that was the **1813** position.
The 1813 Act also asserted **Crown sovereignty** over Company territories (**UPSC 2019** key).
**Charles Grant** and **William Wilberforce** applied evangelical pressure → the **1813 turning point** (missionaries).

nindian-polity-22-13.x: Pitt's India Act, 1784 introduced Dual Control; the Regulating Act set up the Supreme Court at Calcutta.
n: The Supreme Court was established at Calcutta under the Regulating Act. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Supreme Court at Calcutta was established in 1774. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
Pitt’s India Act established the system of Dual Control. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Charter Act of 1813 abolished the Company’s trade monopoly in India except for the tea trade. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Charter Act of 1833 ended the Company’s commercial status entirely. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The trade monopoly in India was partially abolished in 1813. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The trade monopoly in India was completely abolished in 1833. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
xa: Dual Control: **Board of Control** (politics) + **Court of Directors** (commerce).
Charters were renewed every **20 years** (**1793, 1813, 1833**); the **1853** Act fixed no term.
**Last Charter Act** = **1853**.

nindian-polity-22-50.s: The Company’s trade monopoly in India was completely abolished by the:
nindian-polity-22-50.x: The Charter Act, 1833 ended the Company's trade monopoly completely and made it a purely administrative body. The 1813 Act ended it only partly, keeping tea and China trade.
n: The Charter Act of 1833 ended the Company’s commercial status entirely. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The trade monopoly in India was completely abolished in 1833. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
xs: The **Charter Act, 1833** completely abolished the trade monopoly — option **(2)**.
The Company's **commercial** functions ended entirely and it became **purely administrative**.
The **Charter Act, 1813** had ended the monopoly only partly, keeping **tea** and **trade with China**.
The **GoI Act 1858** transferred power to the **Crown**; the **1861** Act restored the legislative powers of Bombay and Madras.
xa: The 1833 Act created the **Governor-General of India** — first holder **Lord William Bentinck**.
It centralised legislative power in the **GG-in-Council**, calling it the "final step towards centralisation".
IYB 2026 dates the **Ministry of Law and Justice**'s origin to the **Charter Act 1833**.

nindian-polity-43-19.s: Which British Act created the office of Governor-General of India and added a Law Member to the Governor-General’s Council?
nindian-polity-43-19.x: The Charter Act, 1833 created the office of Governor-General of India and added a Law Member (Macaulay) to the Council. The 1853 Act separated legislative and executive functions.
nindian-polity-43-19.tq: Link the Law Member and the new title to 1833.
n: The Charter Act of 1833 created the office of Governor-General of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Charter Act of 1833 added a Law Member. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
Macaulay was the Law Member added under the Charter Act of 1833. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
xs: The **Charter Act, 1833** created the office of **Governor-General of India** and added a **Law Member** — option **(1)**.
The first Law Member was **Macaulay**, the **fourth member** of the GG's Council.
The **Charter Act 1853** separated **legislative and executive functions**; the **1813** Act partly ended the monopoly; the **1858** Act transferred power to the **Crown**.
xa: First Governor-General of India: **Lord William Bentinck**.
The 1833 Act set up the **Law Commission** under Macaulay — origin of the **Law Ministry**.
**Section 87** opened Company service to Indians for the first time.

nindian-polity-43-20.s: Under the Dual Control set up by Pitt's India Act, 1784, political affairs were assigned to the:
nindian-polity-43-20.x: Dual Control gave political functions to the Board of Control and commercial functions to the Court of Directors.
n: Pitt’s India Act was enacted in 1784. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
Pitt’s India Act introduced Dual Control. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Board of Control handled political affairs under Dual Control. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Court of Directors handled commerce under Dual Control. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
xa: Company territories became **"British possessions in India"**; the Company became a subordinate department of the State.
The **Board of Control** had **6 members**, including a Secretary of State and the **Chancellor of the Exchequer**.
Both the **Board of Control** and the **Court of Directors** were abolished by the **GoI Act 1858**.

nd24c1584728.s: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1861, an ordinance issued by the Viceroy could remain in force for at most:
nd24c1584728.x: An ordinance under the 1861 Act lasted at most six months, not twelve.
xa: The **1861 Act** restored the legislative powers of **Bombay** and **Madras** (decentralisation).
It was passed on **1 August 1861**; the **High Courts Act, 1861** set up High Courts at **Calcutta, Bombay and Madras** in **1862**.
New provincial councils: **Bengal (1862)**, **Punjab (1897)**.
Indian participation marked the beginning of **representative institutions**.

n298d4b95a13.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1858, the Crown's powers over India were exercised through the:
n298d4b95a13.x: The 1858 Act vested the Crown's powers in the Secretary of State for India, assisted by a 15-member Council of India; the Board of Control and Court of Directors were abolished.
xa: The **Council of India** was **abolished** by the **GoI Act 1935**; the Secretary of State was given advisers.
First Viceroy = **Canning**; last Viceroy = **Mountbatten**.
Double government (**1784**) = Court of Directors + Board of Control.

n90e18be2d89.s: The absence of Indians in the legislative council, as a lesson of the Revolt of 1857, was particularly criticised by
n90e18be2d89.x: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan attributed part of the crisis to the absence of Indian opinion in the council, a concern addressed through later expansion and nomination of Indian members.
n90e18be2d89.tq: Match the criticism of an institutional defect with its associated thinker.
xs: **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan** blamed the **absence of Indians in the council** — option **(2)**.
**Link to 1857**: rulers must know Indian opinion → the **1861** Act.
**Sir Dinkar Rao**, **Maharaja of Patiala** and **Raja of Benaras** were the Indians the Viceroy **nominated** in 1861.
xa: The 1861 Act was the beginning of **representative institutions**.
It gave the Viceroy **ordinance** power (**6 months**).
It recognised **Canning**'s **portfolio system** (**1859**).

n1c2b3343159.s: Who among the following was NOT one of the first three Indians nominated by Canning to the expanded legislative council?
n1c2b3343159.x: The first three Indians nominated by Canning were the Raja of Benaras, the Maharaja of Patiala and Sir Dinkar Rao. Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was not one of these three nominees.
n1c2b3343159.tq: Find the outsider in a short list of named nominees.
xs: **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan** was NOT a 1861 nominee — option **(4)**.
The Viceroy **nominated** the **Raja of Benaras**, **Maharaja of Patiala** and **Sir Dinkar Rao**.
Syed Ahmad Khan was the critic who blamed the **absence of Indians** in the council after **1857**.
xa: The 1861 Act was passed on **1 August 1861**.
⚠ Indians **nominated** = 1861; indirect election = **1892**; formal election = **1909**.
First Indian on the Viceroy's Executive Council = **Satyendra Sinha** (**1909**).

nindian-polity-22-4.s: Which Act transferred the rule of India from the Company to the British Crown?
nindian-polity-22-4.x: The Government of India Act, 1858 transferred rule from the Company to the Crown and made the Governor-General the Viceroy. The 1861 and 1919 Acts reformed councils; 1947 ended British rule.
nindian-polity-22-4.tq: Link the end of Company rule to the Act after the 1857 revolt.
n: The Government of India Act was enacted in 1858. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Government of India Act of 1858 transferred rule from the Company to the British Crown. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Government of India Act of 1858 designated the Governor-General as Viceroy. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
xs: The **Government of India Act, 1858** transferred rule from the Company to the **British Crown** — option **(3)**.
The **1861** Act restored provincial legislative powers and the **1919** Act brought **dyarchy**; neither transferred power.
xa: The Governor-General was designated **Viceroy**; **Lord Canning** was the **first Viceroy**.
The 1858 Act abolished the **Board of Control** and the **Court of Directors**.
It created the **Secretary of State for India**, assisted by a **15-member Council of India**.
Last Viceroy = **Mountbatten**.

n3a1fb0fa04d.s: The practice of indirect election to legislative councils was first introduced by the
n3a1fb0fa04d.x: The Indian Councils Act, 1892 began the practice of indirect election through nominations made on the recommendation of bodies such as universities, municipalities and chambers of commerce.
n3a1fb0fa04d.tq: Distinguish the beginning of indirect election in 1892 from the first formal elected representation under 1909.
xs: **Indirect election** began with the **Indian Councils Act 1892** — option **(2)**.
Nomination on the recommendation of **universities, municipalities, chambers** (APPSC GS **2019** key).
**1861** only nominated Indians; **1909** brought **formal** election and separate electorate.
xa: ⚠ Indirect election = **1892**; separate electorate + formal election = **1909**.
APP notes say 1909 "first introduced elected members".
1892 allowed **budget discussion** and questions, **no vote**.

n14fb65bdd0a.s: Under the Indian Councils Act, 1909, the additional members of the Central Legislative Council were raised to:
n14fb65bdd0a.x: The 1909 Act raised the additional members to 60 (total 69), though the Centre kept an official majority.
xa: 1909 introduced a **separate electorate for Muslims**.
**Satyendra Sinha** became the first Indian on the Viceroy's Executive Council.
The Act that allowed some **elected representation** = **1909** (**2018** key).

n75af0835a86.s: At the time of the Morley-Minto Reforms (1909), Morley and Minto respectively were:
o: Governor of Bombay and Secretary of State
Secretary of State and Governor of Bengal
n75af0835a86.x: John Morley was Secretary of State for India and Lord Minto was the Viceroy when the Indian Councils Act, 1909 was passed.
xa: 1909 introduced a **separate electorate for Muslims**.
Central council: **69** — **37 officials, 32 non-officials**.
The 1917 declaration came from **Montagu** → **1919** Act (with Chelmsford).

n2b0e54d305f.s: Which Act introduced a separate electorate for Muslims and is regarded as the Act that allowed some elected representation in the legislative councils?
n2b0e54d305f.x: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto) introduced separate electorates for Muslims and formal elected representation. The 1861 Act only nominated Indians, the 1892 Act began indirect election through recommendations, and the 1919 Act extended communal representation and set up a bicameral Centre.
xs: The **Indian Councils Act 1909** gave **separate electorate for Muslims** and formal elected representation — option **(3)**.
**1861** only **nominated** Indians; **1892** began **indirect election**.
**1919** extended communal representation and set up a **bicameral** Centre.
xa: Elected representation = **1909** (the **2018** key).
⚠ Indirect election = **1892**; separate electorate + formal election = **1909**.
**1935** extended communal representation to **depressed classes, women and labour**.

nindian-polity-1-24.s: Who is known as the 'Father of Communal Electorate'?
nindian-polity-1-24.x: Lord Minto, of the Morley-Minto reforms (Indian Councils Act, 1909), which introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
n: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Lord Minto was called the Father of Communal Electorate. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xa: **Morley** was the **Secretary of State**; **Minto** the **Viceroy**.
⚠ **Indirect election** = **1892**; **separate electorate** + formal election = **1909**.
The Central Council's additional members rose to **60**; total **69** — **37 officials, 32 non-officials**.

nindian-polity-43-39.s: Which Act provided an annual grant of Rs 1 lakh for education in India?
nindian-polity-43-39.x: The Charter Act of 1813 provided the annual education grant of Rs 1 lakh.
n: The Charter Act was enacted in 1813. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Charter Act of 1813 provided an annual education grant of ₹1 lakh. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Indian Councils Act was enacted in 1861. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Indian Councils Act of 1861 introduced the Portfolio System. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Morley-Minto Reforms were introduced in 1909. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Morley-Minto Reforms introduced separate electorates for Muslims. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Government of India Act was enacted in 1935. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Government of India Act of 1935 created the Federal Court. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Federal Court was established on 1 October 1937. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
xa: The 1813 grant was the **first** provision for the education of Indians.
**Lord Canning** began the portfolio system in **1859**.
First Chief Justice of the Federal Court: **Sir Maurice Gwyer**.

nindian-polity-43-23.s: Provincial autonomy was introduced by the:
nindian-polity-43-23.x: The 1935 Act introduced provincial autonomy; the 1919 Act had introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
n: The Morley-Minto Reforms were introduced in 1909. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Morley-Minto Reforms introduced separate electorates for Muslims. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms were introduced in 1919. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms introduced dyarchy in the provinces. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Government of India Act was enacted in 1935. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Government of India Act of 1935 introduced provincial autonomy. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Indian Independence Act was enacted in 1947. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Indian Independence Act created two independent Dominions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
xa: Under provincial autonomy, provinces were run by **ministers answerable to their legislatures**.
The 1935 Act abolished provincial dyarchy; responsible governments came into force from **April 1937**.
The GoI Acts **1919** and **1935** redefined legislative power until the **Indian Independence Act 1947**.

n08577211175.s: The office of the High Commissioner for India in London was created by the:
n08577211175.x: The 1919 Act provided for a High Commissioner for India in London, a Public Service Commission and separate provincial budgets.
xa: ⚠ PSC: **provided** 1919, **set up 1 October 1926**.
1919 brought **dyarchy in provinces** and a **bicameral** central legislature with **direct elections**.
A **statutory commission** after **10 years** → Simon Commission (**1927**).

nef6891bd31d.s: Montagu's declaration on the gradual introduction of responsible government in India was made on 20 August:
nef6891bd31d.x: Montagu's declaration of 20 August 1917 formed the basis of the Government of India Act, 1919.
xa: 1919 brought **dyarchy in provinces** — **transferred** and **reserved** subjects.
Central legislature: **Council of State** + **Legislative Assembly**, mostly **directly elected**.
Franchise was limited by **property, tax, education**.

n59002ce6d89.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of reserved subjects under the provincial dyarchy introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919?
n59002ce6d89.x: Police, finance and land revenue were reserved subjects administered by the Governor with the assistance of the Executive Council. Education, agriculture, public health and local self-government were transferred subjects.
n59002ce6d89.tq: Separate the two columns of the dyarchy table before evaluating the set.
xs: **Police, finance and land revenue** were all **reserved subjects** — option **(4)**.
Reserved subjects (Governor + **Executive Council**): **law and order, police, land revenue, irrigation, finance**.
**Education, agriculture, public health** and **local self-government** were **transferred** (Governor + Indian Ministers), so options 1–3 each contain a transferred subject.
xa: **Dyarchy** = subjects split into **reserved** and **transferred** (**1919**, provinces).
**Local self-government** was a **transferred subject** under an Indian minister.
⚠ Dyarchy: **1919** = provinces; **1935** = Centre (never worked).
Provincial dyarchy was ended by the **1935** Act → **provincial autonomy**.

nd95f217adb6.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1919, the upper house of the central legislature was the:
nd95f217adb6.x: The 1919 Act made the Centre bicameral: the Council of State (upper) and the Legislative Assembly (lower).
xa: The 1919 Act introduced **dyarchy in the provinces** and first used the term **"responsible government"**.
It set up the **Chamber of Princes** (**120** members) and the **Public Accounts Committee** (**1921**).

n1abbf33ea6e.s: Which of the following provinces was NOT among the six provinces provided with bicameral legislatures under the Government of India Act, 1935?
n1abbf33ea6e.x: Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Bihar, Assam and the United Provinces had bicameral legislatures. Punjab was not included in this group.
n1abbf33ea6e.tq: Test the exception within a compact memorisation list.
xs: **Punjab** was NOT one of the six bicameral provinces — option **(4)**.
The six: **Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Bihar, Assam, United Provinces**.
xa: Bihar's Legislative Council came from the **1935 Act** (BPSC **2024** key).
Punjab got a provincial council under the 1861 scheme in **1897**.
⚠ Bicameral: **centre 1919**; **provinces (6) 1935**.

nindian-polity-1-29.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, in whom were the residuary powers vested?
nindian-polity-1-29.x: Under the 1935 Act residuary powers were vested in the Governor-General — not in the Federal Court, the Executive Council or the provincial Governors. (Under the Constitution they lie with Parliament.)
nindian-polity-1-29.tq: Remember who held residuary powers before the Constitution.
n: The Government of India Act of 1935 vested residuary powers in the Governor-General. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xs: Under the **1935 Act**, residuary powers were vested in **the Governor-General** — option **(1)**.
They lay neither with the **Federal Court**, the Executive Council nor the provincial Governors.
xa: The Act created **three lists**: **Federal, Provincial, Concurrent**.
**Central executive** was vested in the **Governor-General** (**APPSC 2007** key: "Governor-General in Council").
**Defence and foreign affairs** were **reserved subjects** under the GG, not the federal legislature.

n28fe9c75572.s:
The Government of India Act, 1935 contained:
1. 321 sections
2. 14 parts
3. 10 schedules
Which of the above is/are correct?
n28fe9c75572.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 had 321 sections, 14 parts and 10 schedules.
xa: It created an **All-India Federation**, **provincial autonomy** and dyarchy at the **Centre**.
It set out **three Lists**: Federal, Provincial, Concurrent; residuary powers with the **Governor-General**.
It provided the **RBI**, **Federal Court** and PSCs; **Council of India abolished**.
Basis: **3rd Round Table Conference and the White Paper**.

n71d595c1b39.s: Which provision of the Government of India Act, 1935 was never implemented?
o: Federal and Provincial Public Service Commissions
n71d595c1b39.x: Dyarchy at the Centre was never implemented because the Federation did not come into operation; provincial autonomy and the Federal Court were implemented.
xa: Joining the Federation was **optional for the states**.
The **Council of India** was abolished (implemented).
Federal Court = forerunner of the **Supreme Court**.

ne643f048b2b.s: Responsible governments in the provinces under the Government of India Act, 1935 came into force from:
ne643f048b2b.x: The 1935 Act abolished provincial dyarchy, and ministries answerable to the legislatures took office from April 1937.
xa: PYQ: responsible provincial governments after ending dual rule = **GoI Act 1935** (APPSC-GS **2025**).
At the Centre, **Defence and foreign affairs** were **reserved subjects under the GG**.
Provincial dyarchy had been introduced by **1919**.

nc1286dc818d.s: Dyarchy in the provinces was introduced by the:
nc1286dc818d.x: Provincial dyarchy came with the 1919 Act; provincial autonomy and the proposed central dyarchy belonged to the 1935 Act.
xa: ⚠ Dyarchy: **1919** = provinces; **1935** = Centre (never worked).
1919 dyarchy split subjects into **transferred** (Governor + Ministers) and **reserved** (Governor + Executive Council).
Central dyarchy under **1935**: reserved + transferred subjects under the GG.

nf25ad982f52.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 was based primarily on the discussions of the:
o: First Round Table Conference and the Simon Commission Report
Third Round Table Conference and the White Paper
Second Round Table Conference and the Nehru Report
Cabinet Mission and the Cripps Proposals
nf25ad982f52.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 was based on the Third Round Table Conference and the White Paper.
nf25ad982f52.tq: Match the constitutional enactment with its immediate source documents.
xs: The **1935** Act was based on the **3rd Round Table Conference and the White Paper** — option **(2)**.
The **Simon Commission** (**1927**) was the statutory review of the **1919** Act.
