xa: The 1935 Act had **14 parts, 321 sections, 10 schedules**.
It proposed an **All-India Federation** and gave **provincial autonomy**.
It abolished the **Council of India**.

n62057d4fb55.s: The All India Federation proposed by the Government of India Act, 1935 never came into existence because:
o: The Federal Court declared it invalid
n62057d4fb55.x: Accession of the princely states was optional, and since no princely state joined, the Federation never came into operation.
xa: UPSC **2024**: "All India Federation" (correct) paired with "Defence and Foreign Affairs under the federal legislature" (wrong).
**Dyarchy at the Centre** also never came into operation.
Residuary powers were with the **Governor-General**.

n74214746fc9.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, Defence and Foreign Affairs were:
o: Federal subjects under the federal legislature
n74214746fc9.x: Defence and foreign affairs were reserved subjects under the Governor-General, not the federal legislature.
xa: The Federation never came into being — **none of the states joined**.
Dyarchy at the Centre never came into operation.
Residuary powers were also with the **Governor-General**.

nc3bbd12defc.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, the central legislature was to consist of the Federal Assembly and the:
nc3bbd12defc.x: The 1935 Act's bicameral Centre was the Federal Assembly plus the Council of States; communal representation was also extended to depressed classes, women and labour.
xa: Bicameral legislatures in **6 provinces**: Bengal, Bombay, Madras, **Bihar**, Assam, United Provinces.
Bihar's Legislative Council came from the **1935 Act** (BPSC **2024** key).

n350222ac172.s:
Which of the following territorial changes were associated with the Government of India Act, 1935?
1. Separation of Burma from India
2. Separation of Sindh from Bombay
3. Separation of Orissa from Bihar
Which of the above are correct?
n350222ac172.x: The 1935 Act provided for the separation of Burma from India, Sindh from Bombay and Orissa from Bihar.
xa: 1935 also gave bicameral legislatures to **6 provinces**.
It provided the **Federal Court**, the **RBI** and **Federal, Provincial and Joint PSCs**.
It extended communal representation to **depressed classes, women and labour**.

ne84b0d4540b.s: Which one of the following provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935 was borrowed into the Constitution of India in substantially corresponding form?
o: The separate colonial status of Burma
The compulsory accession of princely states
ne84b0d4540b.x: The federal scheme, office of Governor, judiciary, Public Service Commissions, emergency provisions and administrative details were among the features carried into the Constitution. Compulsory accession and non-operational dyarchy were not borrowed as constitutional arrangements.
ne84b0d4540b.tq: Identify a continuing constitutional feature rather than a colonial arrangement that failed or ended.
xs: The **federal scheme** was carried into the Constitution — option **(3)**.
Features taken from **1935**: federal scheme, office of **Governor**, judiciary, PSCs, **emergency provisions**, administrative details.
**Central dyarchy** never came into operation, and state accession was **optional**, not compulsory.
xa: Example: Sec. **63** (Governor's address) → **Art. 175**.
The **Federal Court** (**1937**) was the forerunner of the Supreme Court.
GoI Acts **1919** and **1935** redefined legislative power until the **Indian Independence Act 1947** (IYB **2026**).

n6763e97a1c4.s: The Reserve Bank of India was formed on 1 April 1935 under the:
n6763e97a1c4.x: The 1935 Act provided for the RBI, but the bank was formed on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934.
xa: ⚠ PSC: **provided** by the **1919** Act, **set up** **1 October 1926**.
The **Federal Court** was the forerunner of the Supreme Court; first Chief Justice **Sir Maurice Gwyer**.
The 1935 Act also **abolished the Council of India** created in **1858**.

n8deab8e3fc1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Governor's address to a provincial/State legislature?
o: Section 63 of the GoI Act, 1935 dealt with the Governor's address.
Provincial ministries drafted the speech from April 1937.
Article 175 of the Constitution provides for the Governor's address.
Article 175 makes the Governor's address absolutely mandatory in every circumstance.
n8deab8e3fc1.x: Article 175 provides for the Governor's address, but does not make it mandatory in every circumstance.
xa: Rows over the Governor's address in **Opposition-ruled States** trace to Sec. 63.
The office of **Governor** was among features borrowed from the 1935 Act.
Responsible provincial governments came into force from **April 1937**.

nindian-polity-1-27.s: The first Chief Justice of the Federal Court (inaugurated on 1 October 1937) was:
nindian-polity-1-27.x: Sir Maurice Gwyer was the first Chief Justice of the Federal Court, which the Supreme Court replaced in 1950.
n: The Government of India Act of 1935 abolished dyarchy in the provinces. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
The Government of India Act of 1935 established the Federal Court. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Sir Maurice Gwyer was the first Chief Justice of the Federal Court. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
The Government of India Act of 1935 separated Burma from India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xa: The Federal Court sat at **Delhi** and was the **forerunner of the Supreme Court**.
The 1935 Act **proposed Central Dyarchy**, which was **never implemented**.
Provincial autonomy: responsible governments in force from **April 1937**.

n94e1c005c17.s: Which of the following correctly describes India's status on 15 August 1947?
o: A sovereign republic with no constitutional link to the Crown
A federation of independent princely states
A Dominion with the British monarch as nominal head
A colony governed directly by the British Parliament
n94e1c005c17.x: India became a Dominion on 15 August 1947, with the British monarch as its nominal head.
n94e1c005c17.tq: Separate Dominion status from republican status.
xs: On **15 August 1947** India became a **Dominion** with the **British monarch as nominal head** — option **(3)**.
Pakistan became a Dominion too; the Crown lost its **veto** over dominion laws.
Option 1 is wrong: India became a **Republic** only on **26 January 1950**.
xa: Each dominion got its own **Governor-General**, acting on **dominion ministers' advice**.
**Paramountcy lapsed**: about **565** princely states were in theory free.
Congress accepted dominion status for a **quick, peaceful transfer** + strong Centre.

n2d64672f28d.s: After independence, the Governor-General of each Dominion was to act on the advice of the:
n2d64672f28d.x: The Governor-General, common or separate for each Dominion, was to act on the advice of the Dominion ministers.
xa: Last Viceroy & first GG = **Mountbatten**; last GG = **Rajagopalachari**.
**C. Rajagopalachari** (**June 1948-Jan 1950**) was the last and **only Indian GG**.
Dominion status ended with the **Republic on 26 January 1950**.

n71bf00fea44.s: Approximately how many princely states were theoretically free after the lapse of paramountcy?
n71bf00fea44.x: About 565 princely states were theoretically free after paramountcy lapsed, although in practice they were expected to join India or Pakistan.
n71bf00fea44.tq: Use the stated approximate figure and reject adjacent-number traps.
xs: About **565** princely states were in theory free after **paramountcy lapsed** — option **(3)**.
In practice they were expected to join **India or Pakistan** (APP says no independence option).
xa: Accession ceded **defence, external affairs and communications** to the dominion.
**Kashmir** acceded **26 October 1947** after the tribal invasion.
Princely states had **93** of the **389** planned Constituent Assembly seats.

nd46c30c4486.s: Under the Instrument of Accession (1947), a princely state ceded defence, external affairs and ____ to the Dominion.
nd46c30c4486.x: The Instrument of Accession ceded defence, external affairs and communications, not finance.
xa: **Kashmir** acceded on **26 October 1947**; UN-arranged ceasefire **1 January 1949**.
**Paramountcy lapsed**: about **565** states in theory free.
Representatives of **6 princely states** joined the Assembly on **28 April 1947**.

n4fe2d945f59.x: Kashmir acceded to India on 26 October 1947 after the tribal invasion.
n4fe2d945f59.tq: Separate the accession date from the later ceasefire date.
xs: **Kashmir** acceded on **26 October 1947**, after the **tribal invasion** — option **(4)**.
**1 January 1949** was the **UN-arranged ceasefire**, not the accession.
xa: Accession ceded **defence, external affairs and communications**.
**Hyderabad** signed a **Standstill Agreement** in **November 1947**.
About **565** states were in theory free when **paramountcy lapsed**.

nb4eb00b0ee0.s: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on
nb4eb00b0ee0.x: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949. It came into full effect on 26 January 1950.
nb4eb00b0ee0.tq: Distinguish the adoption date from the signing date and the commencement date.
xs: The Constitution was **adopted on 26 November 1949** — option **(1)**.
It came into force (**commenced**) on **26 January 1950**; members signed on **24 Jan 1950**.
xa: "Adopted on?" → **26 Nov 1949** (APPSC G2 **2025**).
**Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas)** = **26 November**, observed **since 2015**.
Some provisions (citizenship, elections, provisional Parliament) commenced on **26 Nov 1949** itself.

nc88bf2fcd11.s: How many of the 299 members signed the Constitution on 24 January 1950?
nc88bf2fcd11.x: 284 of the 299 members signed the Constitution at the final session on 24 January 1950.
xa: APP dates the signing to **26 Nov 1949**; UPSC notes place it at the last sitting.
On **24 January 1950** Prasad was elected **first President**; the **Anthem** and **National Song** were settled.
Strength fell from **389** to **299** after partition.

nca3f4375ec3.s: The Constitution of India came into force on 26 January 1950 because this date was associated with:
o: The Purna Swaraj declaration associated with the Lahore Congress of 1929
The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly in 1946
The adoption of the Objectives Resolution in 1947
The publication of the Draft Constitution in 1948
nca3f4375ec3.x: 26 January was chosen to commemorate Purna Swaraj Day, following the Lahore Congress decision of 1929 and its observance in 1930.
nca3f4375ec3.tq: Link a constitutional date with its historical nationalist significance.
xs: 26 January was **Purna Swaraj Day** (**1930**, **Lahore Congress 1929** decision) — option **(1)**.
The first meeting was **9 December 1946**; the Objectives Resolution adopted **22 January 1947**; the Draft published **21 February 1948**.
xa: On 26 January 1950 India became a **Republic**, ending dominion status.
⚠ **Adopted** 26 Nov 1949 / **commenced** 26 Jan 1950.
Total time: **2 years, 11 months, 18 days**.

n28124a23151.s: After the Indian Independence Act, 1947, the Constituent Assembly performed which of the following functions?
o: It functioned only as the provincial legislature of the newly formed Union
It functioned as the legislature of British India under the control of the Viceroy
It functioned only as the constitution-making body until 26 January 1950
It functioned both as a sovereign constitution-making body and as the Dominion legislature
n28124a23151.x: The Act made the Constituent Assembly fully sovereign in its constitution-making role and also made it the Dominion legislature. The Central Legislative Assembly consequently ceased to function.
n28124a23151.tq: Distinguish the Assembly’s dual constitutional and legislative roles.
xs: It was both a **sovereign constitution-making body** and the **Dominion legislature** — option **(4)**.
The Act made it **fully sovereign** + **Dominion legislature**; the **Central Legislative Assembly** ended.
xa: As constitution-maker it was chaired by **Dr Rajendra Prasad**; as legislature by **G.V. Mavalankar**.
It sat as Dominion Legislature from **17 November 1947**.
After **26 January 1950** it continued as **Provisional Parliament**.

n9eb27a2f27e.s: The strength of the Constituent Assembly declined from 389 to 299 primarily because
o: the nominated members resigned before the commencement of the Constitution
members representing the areas that became part of Pakistan withdrew from the Assembly
the British Government dissolved the provincial representation
the princely states refused to send their representatives
n9eb27a2f27e.x: The representatives from the territories that went to Pakistan withdrew from the Constituent Assembly, reducing its strength from 389 to 299.
n9eb27a2f27e.tq: Identify the direct cause of an institutional numerical change.
xs: Strength fell from **389** to **299** because **members from areas going to Pakistan withdrew** — option **(2)**.
**389** = **296** British India + **93** princely states (planned).
xa: **284 of 299** members signed the Constitution.
Representatives of **6 princely states** joined on **28 April 1947**.
The **Muslim League** had boycotted the first meeting (**9 December 1946**).

nae8015f504c.s: The Constituent Assembly continued after 26 January 1950 as the
nae8015f504c.x: After the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, the Constituent Assembly functioned as the Provisional Parliament until the first general elections held in 1951–52.
nae8015f504c.tq: Use the constitutional transition sequence to identify the successor institution.
xs: After **26 January 1950** the Assembly continued as the **Provisional Parliament** — option **(1)**.
It lasted until the first elections (**1951-52**).
xa: It ceased on **17 April 1952**; the new Parliament came in **May 1952**.
It had been the **Dominion Legislature** from **17 November 1947**.
The **Constitution** itself had commenced on **26 January 1950**, the date of **Purna Swaraj Day**.

ne186a2a1d1f.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar warned against the “grammar of anarchy” in his closing speech delivered on:
ne186a2a1d1f.x: Ambedkar used the expression “grammar of anarchy” in his closing speech on 25 November 1949.
ne186a2a1d1f.tq: Discriminate between closely related Constitution-making dates.
xs: Ambedkar's **"grammar of anarchy"** line came in his **closing speech, 25 Nov 1949** — option **(2)**.
In the same speech: India entering **"a life of contradictions"**.
**26 November 1949** was adoption; **24 January 1950** signing; **26 January 1950** commencement.
xa: On **4 Nov 1948** Ambedkar said **constitutional morality** "has to be cultivated".
He borrowed the term from **George Grote**.
Ambedkar chaired the **Drafting Committee**.

nebb67713402.s: Critics who called the Indian Constitution a 'patchwork' meant that it was:
o: Drafted without any debate in the Constituent Assembly
Framed by a body elected on adult franchise
Largely borrowed from various other constitutions and sources
Written only by the British Parliament
nebb67713402.x: The Constitution was called 'borrowed' or a 'patchwork' because it drew heavily on provisions from various constitutions and sources.
nebb67713402.tq: Patchwork = patches borrowed from many constitutions.
xs: **"Patchwork"** meant **largely borrowed from various other constitutions** — option **(3)**.
Critics called it **"borrowed"** or a **"patchwork"**; about **60** constitutions were consulted.
Option 2 is wrong: the Assembly had **no adult franchise**.
xa: Other criticisms: **not sovereign**, **Congress-dominated**, **took too long**.
Draft discussed **114 days**; **2,473** amendments discussed.
**B.N. Rau** prepared the initial draft.

n176eef543d6.s: Before Indian independence, the Madras Assembly had resolved to divide the Presidency into which four units?
n176eef543d6.x: The Madras Assembly resolved to divide the Presidency into Andhra, Tamil, Karnataka and Kerala four months before independence.
n176eef543d6.tq: Recall the complete four-part geographical list without substituting later State names.
xs: The Madras Assembly resolved to divide the Presidency into **Andhra, Tamil, Karnataka, Kerala** — option **(1)**.
This came **four months before independence**.
xa: **Nehru** accepted the Andhra demand on **27 Nov 1947**.
Andhra was dropped from the **Draft of 21 Feb 1948** → **Dar Commission**.
The demand continued until **Andhra State of 1953**.

nb68c09d793f.s: The immediate historical significance of the Indian Independence Act, 1947 was that it
o: ended provincial autonomy and restored direct British rule over India
combined sovereignty with partition and enabled a quick transfer of power under dominion status
abolished the Constituent Assembly and transferred power to the princely States
created a unitary republic with universal adult franchise
nb68c09d793f.x: The Act gave sovereignty to India in the context of partition. Congress accepted dominion status to facilitate a quick and peaceful transfer of power and to support a strong Centre.
nb68c09d793f.tq: Select the option that combines the Act’s constitutional consequence with its political context.
xs: The Act **gave sovereignty with partition**; dominion status allowed a **quick transfer** — option **(2)**.
Congress accepted dominion status for a **quick, peaceful transfer** + **strong Centre**.
It made the Constituent Assembly **fully sovereign**; it did not abolish it.
xa: India became a **Dominion** on **15 August 1947**.
**Paramountcy lapsed** for about **565** princely states.
Dominion status ended with the **Republic** (**26 January 1950**).

n67d794d5b9a.s: The Cabinet Mission that proposed the scheme for forming the Constituent Assembly consisted of:
o: Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander
A.V. Alexander, Rajendra Prasad and Stafford Cripps
n67d794d5b9a.x: The Cabinet Mission consisted of Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander. It arrived in India in 1946 to work out the constitutional and political arrangements.
n67d794d5b9a.tq: Use the complete membership combination and reject substitutions by other contemporary figures.
xs: The **Cabinet Mission** = **Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, A.V. Alexander** — option **(2)**.
It came on **24 Mar 1946**; the Assembly was formed under the **Cabinet Mission Plan (1946)**.
xa: Planned strength **389**: **296** British India + **93** princely states.
Seats were roughly **1 per million** population.
⚠ **389** planned; **299** after partition.

n34e16bde47a.s: The continuing demand for a separate Andhra ultimately resulted in the creation of Andhra State in
n34e16bde47a.x: The Dhar Commission and the JVP Committee rejected linguistic States at the time, but the Andhra demand continued and resulted in the Andhra State of 1953.
n34e16bde47a.tq: Connect an earlier committee recommendation with the later political outcome.
xs: The demand ended in **Andhra State** in **1953** — option **(4)**.
**Dhar Commission** and **JVP Committee** rejected linguistic states, but the **Andhra** demand continued.
xa: **Nehru** accepted the Andhra demand on **27 Nov 1947**.
Madras Assembly had resolved on **Andhra, Tamil, Karnataka, Kerala** four months before independence.
APPSC GS **2025** asked for the Linguistic Provinces Committee chairman → **S.K. Dar**.

nindian-polity-1-30.s: Who first put forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India in 1934?
nindian-polity-1-30.x: M.N. Roy first put forward the idea in 1934; the Swaraj Party made the first formal demand at Ranchi in May 1934.
n: M.N. Roy first put forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly in 1934. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
The Swaraj Party made the first formal demand for a Constituent Assembly at its Ranchi conference in May 1934. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
The Constituent Assembly was constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xa: The **Congress** officially demanded it at **Patna**.
**1938**: **Jawaharlal Nehru**'s clear statement of support; **1940**: the **August Offer** accepted the principle.
**1942**: the **Cripps Mission** gave the final proposal for an **elected** Constituent Assembly.
Cabinet Mission (**24 Mar 1946**): **Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, A.V. Alexander**.

n6314fe97e55.s: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, the total strength of the Constituent Assembly was to be:
n6314fe97e55.x: The total strength was 389: 296 from British India and 93 from the princely states.
xa: Provincial members were **indirectly elected** by **proportional representation (single transferable vote)**.
Princely representatives were **nominated** by rulers.
After partition the strength fell to **299**.

na57c645514f.s: The representatives of the princely States in the Constituent Assembly were:
o: Elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies
na57c645514f.x: Princely representatives were nominated by the rulers; only the provincial members were elected by the Provincial Assemblies.
xa: On **28 April 1947**, representatives of **6 princely states** — **Baroda, Bikaner, Jaipur, Patiala, Rewa, Udaipur** — joined.
Planned seats: **389** = **296** (British India) + **93** (Princely States).
The Assembly was **partly elected, partly nominated**; there was no adult franchise.

nba56db116f2.s: The Constituent Assembly of India was:
o: Wholly nominated by the British Government
Wholly nominated by the princely rulers
nba56db116f2.x: The Assembly was partly elected and partly nominated; it was not based on adult franchise.
xa: Criticism: **not representative** — no adult franchise; **not sovereign** — a British creation.
**Granville Austin**: "a one-party body in an essentially one-party country".
**Viscount Simon**: "A body of Hindus"; **lawyer-politician dominated**.

na84a41d3336.s: Members of the Constituent Assembly from the provinces were:
o: Indirectly elected by Provincial Assembly members by proportional representation (single transferable vote)
na84a41d3336.x: Each community's members in the Provincial Assembly elected their representatives by proportional representation with single transferable vote; there was no adult franchise.
xa: Seats were roughly **1 per million** population.
The Assembly was **partly elected, partly nominated**.
**Gandhi and Jinnah** were not members.

n7781e5dc44b.s: Sir B.N. Rau, who prepared the initial draft of the Constitution, later served as a judge of the:
n7781e5dc44b.x: B.N. Rau prepared the initial draft and later served as a judge of the International Court of Justice.
xa: Rau was the **Constitutional Adviser**, named on **11 December 1946**.
He was the first permanent Indian judge of the **International Court of Justice**.
APP credits him with the **1948** draft.
n7781e5dc44b.fixed: B.N. Rau sat on the ICJ Feb 1952 - Nov 1953 (elected late 1951)

n9be878ab240.s: The original Preamble of the Constitution was illuminated by:
n9be878ab240.x: The original Preamble was illuminated by Beohar Rammanohar Sinha. This is distinct from the persons associated with handwriting or other artwork in the original Constitution.
n9be878ab240.tq: Apply confusable-person discrimination among artists and contributors associated with the original Constitution.
xs: The original Preamble was illuminated by **Beohar Rammanohar Sinha** — option **(3)**.
The notes say nothing on the other names.

n268feb5cc26.s: Which one of the following was NOT a member of the seven-member Drafting Committee?

n7404ef309d4.s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Munshi-Ayyangar formula?

xs: **Immediate discontinuation of English** was NOT a feature — option **(4)**.

n82d340b60b1.s: Who presided over the Constituent Assembly when it functioned as the constitution-making body and who presided over it as the legislature, respectively?

n744ac637079.s: Who stated that constitutional morality “is not a natural sentiment. It has to be cultivated”?

n480de799f99.s: Which of the following is true of both the Dhar Commission and the JVP Committee?

xs: The **Drafting Committee** under **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** was constituted on **29 August 1947** — option **(1)**.

nindian-polity-5-4.s: The Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal Areas was chaired by:

Sardar Patel chaired the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal Areas. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 14-16]

nindian-polity-5-7.s: The ad-hoc Flag Committee of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by:

nindian-polity-52-21.s: The Union Powers Committee of the Constituent Assembly dealt with:

xa: Union Powers and Functions Committees: **Jawaharlal Nehru**; Provincial Constitution: **Sardar Patel**; Order of Business: **K.M. Munshi**.

nindian-polity-52-39.s: The 1931 Karachi Congress Flag Committee was chaired by:

xs: The **1931 Karachi** Congress Flag Committee was chaired by **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel** — option **(1)**.

nindian-polity-35-14.s: Who chaired both the Union Constitution Committee and the Union Powers Committee?

The Union Constitution Committee covered Union powers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Union Constitution Committee covered the central constitutional structure. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
Jawaharlal Nehru chaired the Union Powers Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]

xa: Nehru also chaired the **States Committee** and the **Constituent Assembly Functions Committee**.

n3a112e15957.s: On 24 January 1950, which song was declared the national song of India and accorded equal honour with the National Anthem?

nindian-polity-43-17.s: What was adopted at the final meeting of the Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950?

xs: On **24 January 1950** the Assembly adopted the **National Anthem** — option **(2)**.

n34743e4ceaa.s: The Constituent Assembly took approximately how long to complete its work?

ne7aa1ee7995.s: The Constituent Assembly sat for a total of:

nc27e4ebc6c8.s: The Draft Constitution had 315 Articles. How many Articles did the Constitution contain as adopted?

**Direct Action Day** (**16 August 1946**) came just before it was formed.
Nehru held **External Affairs and Commonwealth Relations**.

n82338237de6.s: Who were the two Vice-Presidents of the Constituent Assembly?
n82338237de6.x: H.C. Mukherjee and V.T. Krishnamachari served as the Vice-Presidents of the Constituent Assembly.
n82338237de6.tq: Distinguish the two Vice-Presidents from the provisional president, constitutional adviser and legislative chair.
xs: The Vice-Presidents were **H.C. Mukherjee** and **V.T. Krishnamachari** — option **(3)**.

xa: ⚠ **V.T.** Krishnamachari = Vice-President; **T.T.** Krishnamachari = Drafting Committee.

n53d87199a0b.s: Which of the following provisions came into force on 26 November 1949?

⚠ **Adopted** 26 Nov 1949 / **commenced** 26 Jan 1950.

ndcdd7f558cd.s: The Drafting Committee, chaired by Dr B.R. Ambedkar, sat for:
ndcdd7f558cd.x: The seven-member Drafting Committee chaired by Ambedkar sat for 141 days.

**Naziruddin Ahmed** called it the "Drifting Committee".

n797b8e3bf1b.s: The three Lists under the Government of India Act, 1935 became which of the following in the Constitution of India?
o: Union List, Residuary List and Concurrent List
Central List, Provincial List and Local List
Union List, State List and Concurrent List
Federal List, Provincial List and State List
n797b8e3bf1b.x: The Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists of the 1935 Act developed into the Union, State and Concurrent Lists of the Constitution.
n797b8e3bf1b.tq: Map the older statutory terminology to its constitutional successor.
xs: The 1935 Lists became the **Union, State and Concurrent Lists** — option **(3)**.
**Federal, Provincial, Concurrent** (1935) → **Union, State and Concurrent** (Constitution).
There is no "Residuary List" or "Local List"; **residuary powers** lie with **Parliament** (**Art. 248**).
xa: **Seventh Schedule today**: **Union 98, State 59, Concurrent 52** subjects.
The framers followed the **Canadian scheme** for dividing subjects but **added** the Concurrent List from **Australia**.
GoI Act 1935 = the **single largest source**.

n217502c0bfd.s: Which of the following is regarded as the single largest source of the provisions of the Indian Constitution?
o: The Constitution of the United States of America
n217502c0bfd.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 is regarded as the single largest source, particularly for the federal scheme, Governor's office, judiciary, Public Service Commissions, emergency provisions and administrative details.
n217502c0bfd.tq: Distinguish the largest overall institutional source from countries supplying individual concepts.
xs: The **Government of India Act 1935** is the **single largest source** — option **(3)**.
It gave the **federal scheme**, **office of Governor**, **judiciary**, **PSCs**, **emergency provisions**, **administrative details**.
**France** gave the Republic and **liberty, equality, fraternity**; **Ireland** the DPSPs; **USA** the FRs.
xa: Its three Lists became the **Union, State and Concurrent Lists**.
**Integrated judiciary**, with the **Federal Court** as model, also came from 1935.
Structure largely from the 1935 Act; philosophical part (**FRs, DPSPs**) borrowed from abroad.

n621f6dee71a.s: The Indian Constitution is criticised as a 'bag of borrowings' mainly because it:
o: Drew many provisions from foreign constitutions
n621f6dee71a.x: The criticism refers to the large number of provisions drawn from foreign constitutions and earlier laws; length is the 'elephantine' criticism and legal detail the 'lawyers' paradise' one.
xa: Examples of India's own: **DPSP** as a "novel feature", the **federal-unitary switch**.
Sources: most of the world's constitutions + **GoI Act 1935**.
**Art. 324** (**Election Commission**) is not traced to any foreign constitution in the notes.

nindian-polity-3-5.s: The language of the Preamble was borrowed from the Constitution of:
nindian-polity-3-5.x: The language of the Preamble came from Australia, while the GoI Act, 1935 gave the Constitution its structural and administrative backbone.
n: The Government of India Act, 1935 provided the structural and administrative backbone. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 12-14]
The language of the Preamble was borrowed from Australia. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 12-14]
The Government of India Act, 1935 is the main blueprint. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 12-14]
xa: The 1935 Act is the **single largest source**; its influence explains the Constitution's **bulk**.
Its **three Lists** (Federal, Provincial, Concurrent) became the Union, State and Concurrent Lists.
The idea of the Preamble came from the **USA**.

n6db31abb04d.s: Suspension of Fundamental Rights during an Emergency is a feature associated with:
n6db31abb04d.x: Suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency is associated with Weimar Germany; the general emergency scheme is associated with the 1935 Act.
xa: ⚠ UPSC and CDI notes tie Emergency Arts. **352, 356, 360** to Germany ("German Reich").
APPSC-G2 **2023** key: **Emergency provisions → GoI Act 1935**; **Suspension of FRs → Weimar Germany**.
FRs can be suspended in a National Emergency **except Articles 20 and 21**.

nd685d15457b.s: India borrowed the parliamentary system and its conventions from:
nd685d15457b.x: The parliamentary system and its conventions came from Britain, even though Britain has no single written Constitution.
xa: British borrowings: **parliamentary government**, **rule of law**, **single citizenship**, **cabinet system**, **bicameralism**.
The **nominal head** (President like the Crown) is also British.
APPSC asks "from Britain?" — distractors are **USA** and **Canada**.

n4eed3f31ac5.s: Single citizenship in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
n4eed3f31ac5.x: Single citizenship, like bicameralism and the cabinet system, came from Britain; the USA has dual citizenship.
xa: Other British: **rule of law**, **prerogative writs**, **parliamentary privileges**, office of **Speaker**.
⚠ Trap: Concurrent List is **Australia, not Canada**.
APPSC-G2 **2023** key: **Single citizenship → Britain**.

n31ec1b1c93c.s: A joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament under Article 108 is presided over by the:
o: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
n31ec1b1c93c.x: A joint sitting under Article 108, itself an Australian borrowing, is presided over by the Speaker.
xa: **Joint sitting** itself is also an **Australian** borrowing.
**Concurrent** List today: **52** subjects.
The trap: Concurrent List (**Australia, not Canada**).

nbff32f90f3c.s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of features borrowed from the Constitution of the United States of America?
o: Judicial review, parliamentary system, independence of judiciary and single citizenship
Fundamental Rights, judicial review, independence of judiciary and impeachment of the President
Fundamental Rights, procedure established by law, joint sitting and impeachment of the President
Impeachment of the President, Directive Principles of State Policy, removal of judges and joint sitting
nbff32f90f3c.x: Fundamental Rights, judicial review, independence of the judiciary and impeachment of the President are among the features borrowed from the United States. Procedure established by law is associated with Japan, while joint sitting is associated with Australia.
nbff32f90f3c.tq: Group features by their source and reject options containing a feature associated with another country.
xs: **FRs, judicial review, independence of judiciary, impeachment of the President** — all **USA** — option **(2)**.
Others mix in **parliamentary system** and **single citizenship** (Britain), **procedure established by law** (Japan), **joint sitting** (Australia), **DPSPs** (Ireland).
xa: USA also gave **removal of SC/HC judges** and the **Vice-President's post**.
Indian judicial review is **narrower than in the USA**.
USA has **dual citizenship**; India **single**.

n0834d21b049.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about features borrowed from Australia and the USSR?
o: Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse came from Australia.
The Concurrent List came from Australia.
The ideals of social, economic and political justice in the Preamble came from Australia.
Fundamental Duties came from the USSR.
n0834d21b049.x: The ideals of social, economic and political justice in the Preamble were borrowed from the USSR, not Australia.
xa: Australia also gave the **joint sitting**.
USSR also gave **Five-Year Plans / Planning Commission**.
Fundamental Duties were added by the **42nd Amendment (1976)**.

n1d7738bdeec.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about borrowed features of the Constitution?
o: Election of Rajya Sabha members and the amendment procedure came from South Africa.
The method of election of the President came from Ireland.
Nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha came from Ireland.
Residuary powers with the Centre came from South Africa.
n1d7738bdeec.x: Residuary powers with the Centre were borrowed from Canada, not South Africa.
xa: In India residuary powers lie with **Parliament** (**Art. 248**).
Ireland also gave the **DPSPs**.
⚠ Election vs nomination is the standard trap.

na00f8b5559b.s: Ireland, from which India took the Directive Principles, had itself taken the idea from:
na00f8b5559b.x: Ireland took the idea of Directive Principles from Spain; India adapted it as a novel feature of its Constitution.
xa: The criticism "**bag of borrowings**" is answered by this adaptation.
DPSPs + FRs form the **philosophical part**.
Ireland also gave **nomination to Rajya Sabha**.

nindian-polity-3-1.s: The idea of a federation with a strong Centre was borrowed from:
nindian-polity-3-1.x: A federation with a strong Centre came from Canada; the Concurrent List came from Australia.
n: The parliamentary form of government was borrowed from Britain. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 12-14]
The Directive Principles of State Policy were borrowed from Ireland. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 12-14]
The federation with a strong Centre was borrowed from Canada. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 12-14]
The Concurrent List was borrowed from Australia. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 12-14]
xa: Ireland itself took the DPSPs from **Spain**; Ambedkar called them a "**novel feature**".
⚠ Traps: **residuary powers** = Canada (not USA); **Concurrent List** = Australia (not Canada).
The makers followed the **Canadian scheme** for dividing subjects but **added a third list**, the Concurrent List.

nindian-polity-3-4.s: The idea of the Preamble in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
nindian-polity-3-4.x: The idea of the Preamble came from the USA; France gave liberty, equality, fraternity and the Republic.
n: Judicial review was borrowed from the USA. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 12-14]
The post of Vice-President was borrowed from the USA. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 12-14]
The removal of judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts was borrowed from the USA. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 12-14]
The idea of the Preamble was borrowed from the USA. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 12-14]
xa: **France** gave the **republic** and **liberty, equality and fraternity**; **Australia** the **language** of the Preamble.
India's judicial review is **narrower than in the USA** — Art. 21 uses "procedure established by law", not "due process".
The USA also gave **Fundamental Rights**, **independence of judiciary** and **impeachment of the President**.

nindian-polity-3-11.s: The provision for a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament was borrowed from:
nindian-polity-3-11.x: The joint sitting, freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse, and the language of the Preamble came from Australia.
n: The joint sitting of both Houses was borrowed from Australia. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 12-14]
The freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse was borrowed from Australia. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 12-14]
xa: The **Concurrent List** also came from **Australia**.
APPSC-G2 2023 key: **Concurrent List → Australia**; **Suspension of FRs → Weimar Germany**.

nindian-polity-3-13.s: The ideal of a Republic in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
nindian-polity-3-13.x: The ideal of a Republic, like liberty, equality and fraternity, was borrowed from France.
n: The ideals of liberty, equality and fraternity in the Preamble were borrowed from France. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 12-14]
xa: The ideals of **social, economic and political justice** came from the **USSR**.
The idea of the **Preamble** came from the **USA**; its **language** from **Australia**.

nd57d10c4b60.s: The eleventh Fundamental Duty was added by the:
nd57d10c4b60.x: Fundamental Duties were introduced by the 42nd Amendment (1976); the eleventh duty was added by the 86th Amendment.
xa: Source: **USSR**.
The USSR also gave the ideal of **justice (social, economic, political)** and **Five-Year Plans / Planning Commission**.
**Fundamental Rights** (Part III, Arts. **12-35**) came from the **USA**.

n6b7af0236f5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about residuary powers?
o: In India, residuary powers lie with Parliament under Article 248.
In India, residuary powers lie exclusively with the States.
In the USA and Australia, residuary powers lie with the States.
India's arrangement of residuary powers was borrowed from Canada.
n6b7af0236f5.x: In India residuary powers lie with Parliament (Article 248), following the Canadian model.
xa: Under the **1935** Act, residuary powers were with the **Governor-General**.
**Seventh Schedule today**: **Union 98, State 59, Concurrent 52**.
Canada also gave the **advisory jurisdiction** of the SC (**Art. 143**).

nd78cc03eed1.s: Which one of the following is correct about Article 21?
o: It uses 'procedure established by law', borrowed from Japan
It was borrowed from the Government of India Act, 1935
It uses 'procedure established by law', borrowed from Ireland
It uses 'due process of law', borrowed from the USA
nd78cc03eed1.x: Article 21 uses 'procedure established by law', an expression borrowed from Japan; it does not use 'due process of law'.
xa: ⚠ Trap: UPSC notes also list it under **Britain**; standard answer = **Japan**.
Art. **21** (with Art. 20) cannot be suspended in a National Emergency.
**Judicial review** itself came from the **USA**.

n9f80135bf2d.s: A system in which a single hierarchy of courts enforces both Central and State laws is called:
n9f80135bf2d.x: India has an integrated judiciary with one hierarchy of courts for both Central and State laws, unlike the separate federal and State courts of the USA.
xa: The **integrated judiciary** with the **Federal Court** as model came from the **GoI Act 1935**.
**Independence of judiciary** and **judicial review** came from the **USA**.
**Advisory jurisdiction** of the SC (**Art. 143**) came from **Canada**.

n9b2346d9eb8.s: During a National Emergency, the enforcement of which of the following Articles cannot be suspended?
n9b2346d9eb8.x: Most Fundamental Rights can be suspended during a National Emergency, an idea borrowed from Weimar Germany, but Articles 20 (protection in respect of conviction for offences) and 21 (life and personal liberty) cannot. Article 19 is in fact the right most readily suspended in an Emergency, and Articles 14 and 32 are not the protected pair, so A, B and D are wrong.
n9b2346d9eb8.tq: Emergency: everything can go except 20 and 21.
xs: **Articles 20 and 21** cannot be suspended in a National Emergency — option **(3)**.
**Most FRs** can be suspended, an idea from **Weimar Germany**; the other pairs are not the protected ones.
xa: **Art. 21** uses **"procedure established by law"** — from **Japan**.
Emergency articles: **352, 356, 360**.
General emergency provisions → **GoI Act 1935** (APPSC-G2 **2023** key).

n97311d5ff9d.s: New provisions are usually inserted into the Constitution without renumbering by:
o: Adding them only as new Schedules
Using lettered Articles such as 21A and 51A
n97311d5ff9d.x: New provisions are inserted as lettered Articles such as 21A and 51A, so the original numbering still ends at Article 395.
xa: Original: Preamble + **395 Articles, 22 Parts, 8 Schedules**.
Today about **470 Articles** (CDI; older notes say **448**).
**Art. 51A** holds the **Fundamental Duties** (Part **IVA**, **42nd**, **1976**).

n90575ca5c55.s: Part IXB was added to the Constitution by the:
n90575ca5c55.x: Part IXB was added by the 97th Amendment in 2011; Part IXA came by the 74th Amendment in 1992.
xa: **XIVA** (Tribunals) was also added by the **42nd** in **1976**.
The **73rd** and **74th** Amendments (**1992**) added the **local government** tier.
Net result: **25** Parts.

n3619ac1cebb.s: Who described the size of the Indian Constitution as 'elephantine'?
n3619ac1cebb.x: H.V. Kamath used the expression 'elephantine size' for the Constitution (APPSC 2018 key). Granville Austin called the Constituent Assembly 'a one-party body in an essentially one-party country', Viscount Simon called it 'a body of Hindus', and Naziruddin Ahmed mocked the Drafting Committee as the 'Drifting Committee'.
xs: **H.V. Kamath** called it **"elephantine size"** — option **(2)** (APPSC **2018** key).
The notes say nothing on the other names in this topic.
xa: Other criticisms: "**borrowed constitution**", "**carbon copy of the 1935 Act**", "**un-Indian**", "**lawyers' paradise**".
Reasons for bulk include the **1935 Act** and **administrative detail**.
Original: **395 Articles, 22 Parts, 8 Schedules**.

n4f2623651da.s: The collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers in India is primarily associated with responsibility to the
n4f2623651da.x: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha under the parliamentary system.
n4f2623651da.tq: Direct identification of the House to which the executive is responsible.
xs: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the **Lok Sabha** — option **(1)**.
This is under **Art. 74(1)** and **Art. 75**.
xa: Ministers are **members of the legislature**.
The **lower House** can be **dissolved**.
The model is **British**, not the American presidential one.

nbb0294a9769.s: The framers of the Constitution preferred the parliamentary system partly because
o: India had no experience of representative institutions before 1950
it was familiar through the Government of India Acts of 1919 and 1935
it guarantees a fixed-term executive in every situation
it completely separates the executive from the legislature
nbb0294a9769.x: The parliamentary system was familiar to India through the Government of India Acts of 1919 and 1935. It was also considered suitable for India's size and diversity and for avoiding executive–legislature conflict.
nbb0294a9769.tq: Connect the institutional choice with its historical and practical justification.
xs: It was **familiar through the 1919 and 1935 Acts** — option **(2)**.
Also suited to India's **size and diversity**.
It has no fixed-term executive or full separation — that is the **presidential (USA)** model.
xa: Under the **1919 and 1935** Acts the parliamentary pattern had already operated in the provinces.
Parliamentary system = **cooperation and coordination** between legislature and executive.
**Collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha** (Art. **74(1)**, Art. **75**).

nb4a50bc36d2.s: The Indian Constitution describes India as a:
nb4a50bc36d2.x: India is described as a Union of States with a parliamentary system of government.
xa: The **head of state is elected**.
**Single citizenship** — unlike the **dual citizenship** of the USA.
India is called **"quasi-federal"**.

n165749a6e09.s: Which doctrine limits the amending power of the Indian Parliament?
n165749a6e09.x: Parliament is a creature of the Constitution, and its amending power is limited by the basic structure doctrine.
xa: Other limits: written constitution, **FRs (Art. 13)**, **judicial review**, federal division of powers.
Britain = **sovereignty of Parliament**.
APPSC GS **2019** keyed "Indian Parliament is not sovereign" as correct.

n9dea8a330b1.s: India follows which form of democracy?
o: Direct democracy through referendum and recall
n9dea8a330b1.x: India follows representative or indirect democracy; referendum, initiative and recall are not part of its national system.
xa: Ultimate authority is with the **people** ("**We, the people**").
**Universal adult franchise**: voting age cut from **21** to **18** (**61st Amendment, 1988**).
India is a **sovereign democratic republic** — elected head of state.

n7cd9d2cc0ce.s: India is described as a 'Republic' primarily because:
o: Its head of state is elected and not hereditary
n7cd9d2cc0ce.x: India is a sovereign democratic republic because its head of state, the President, is elected rather than hereditary; ultimate authority rests with the people.
xs: India is a **Republic** because its **head of state is elected**, not hereditary — option **(1)**.
Parliamentary executive, written constitution and independent judiciary are other features, not what "Republic" means.
xa: **Hereditary head of state** is a **non-feature** (odd one out).
APPSC GS **2019**: "India's head of state is elected" correct; "**Britain's head is elected**" wrong.
Ultimate authority with the **people** ("We, the people").

n6974eb8880f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Indian and British parliamentary systems?
o: India's head of state is elected.
The Indian Parliament is sovereign in the British sense.
The British system rests on the sovereignty of Parliament.
The Indian Parliament is bound by a written Constitution and judicial review.
n6974eb8880f.x: The Indian Parliament is not sovereign in the British sense: it is bound by a written Constitution, Fundamental Rights and judicial review.
xa: India follows the **British pattern but with basic differences**.
Parliament = **"a creature of the Constitution"**.
**Hereditary head of state** is not a feature of India.

n9dd82955e03.s: Judicial review in India is narrower than in the USA because Article 21 uses the phrase:
n9dd82955e03.x: Article 21 uses 'procedure established by law', which makes judicial review in India narrower than in the USA.
xa: Inconsistent laws are void — **Art. 13**.
**Judicial review** is a **basic-structure** element.
**Single integrated judiciary** for Union and States.

n500883732c9.s: In India, both Central and State laws are enforced by:
o: Separate federal and State court systems
n500883732c9.x: India has an integrated judiciary in which one court system administers both Union and State laws.
xa: Independence: **tenure**, **salary protection**, **no discussion of judges' conduct**, **bar on post-retirement practice**, **contempt powers**.
US states have their own constitutions; Indian states do not.
**Independence of judiciary** is a basic-structure feature.

nd9ff86ca259.s: The Right to Property is now protected as a constitutional legal right under:
nd9ff86ca259.x: The Right to Property was moved out of the Fundamental Rights chapter and is now protected by Article 300A.
xa: All FRs are suspendable in a National Emergency **except Arts. 20 and 21**.
**DPSPs**: **socialist, Gandhian, liberal-intellectual**; **non-justiciable**.
**Fundamental Duties**: **11**.

n0dad1c0affe.s: The emergency provisions (Articles 352-360) are contained in:
n0dad1c0affe.x: Part XVIII (Arts. 352-360) provides for National, State (President's Rule) and Financial Emergencies.
xa: FRs are suspendable **except Arts. 20 and 21**.
This flexibility is why India is called **"quasi-federal"**.
The federal-unitary switch is one of India's own features.

n52884b2e87f.s: The voting age in India was reduced from 21 to 18 years by which Constitutional Amendment?
n52884b2e87f.x: The 61st Amendment (1988) lowered the voting age under universal adult franchise from 21 to 18. The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Fundamental Duties and Parts IVA and XIVA, and the 73rd Amendment (1992) added Panchayats; the 44th Amendment (1978) did not change the voting age.
xs: The **61st Amendment, 1988** cut the voting age from **21** to **18** — option **(3)**.
**42nd (1976)** added Fundamental Duties; **73rd (1992)** added Panchayats.
xa: **Universal adult franchise** existed from the start — not property/education-based.
India is a **representative (indirect) democracy**.
**ECI** is listed among the **independent bodies**.

ne8e3b609726.s: Which one of the following best expresses the meaning of constitutionalism?
o: Unrestricted sovereignty of the legislature in all matters
Government limited by a written and supreme Constitution
Government by the personal will of the ruler without legal restraint
Government in which courts cannot examine executive action
ne8e3b609726.x: Constitutionalism means that governmental power is limited by a supreme Constitution and exercised according to established rules rather than the personal will of the ruler.
ne8e3b609726.tq: Contrast limited government with absolute rule.
xs: **Constitutionalism** = government **limited by a written, supreme constitution** — option **(2)**.
Power is by **rules, not the ruler's will** (absolute rule).
xa: In India the limits are: **written constitution**, **FRs (Art. 13)**, **judicial review**, federal division, **basic structure**.
**Basic structure** limit: **Kesavananda Bharati, 1973**.
Parliament is **not sovereign in the British sense**.

n0af2e2d92b7.s: Which of the following is an element of the basic structure of the Constitution?
o: Absolute precedence of DPSPs over Fundamental Rights
n0af2e2d92b7.x: Supremacy of the Constitution is a basic-structure element, along with rule of law, separation of powers, judicial review and limited amending power.
xa: Features forming the base of the basic structure: **federalism**, **secularism**, **parliamentary system**, **independence of judiciary**.
Basic structure: **Kesavananda Bharati, 1973**.
Parliament = "**a creature of the Constitution**".

nfccdb21f4ef.s: The original Constitution of India contained how many Schedules?
nfccdb21f4ef.x: The original Constitution had 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules; there are 12 Schedules now.
xa: Now: about **470 Articles, 25 Parts, 12 Schedules** (**2026**); APP gives about **448** Articles.
⚠ Old UPSC notes also say **397** Articles — wrong; original was **395**.
"How many Articles in the original Constitution?" → **395**.

nf039025cfa8.s: The Preamble of the Constitution is described as a modified version of the:
nf039025cfa8.x: The Preamble is a modified version of the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru and adopted by the Constituent Assembly.
nf039025cfa8.tq: Identify the direct constitutional source instead of a general colonial constitutional instrument.
xs: The Preamble is a **modified version** of the **Objectives Resolution** — option **(1)**.
The Objectives Resolution was moved by **Jawaharlal Nehru** on **13 Dec 1946** and adopted unanimously on **22 Jan 1947**.
It laid down the **philosophy and guiding principles** of the Constitution.
xa: Sources: **Justice** — **Russian Revolution (1917)**; **Liberty, Equality, Fraternity** — **French Revolution (1789)**.
**Idea of a preamble** — **US Constitution**; **language** — **Australia**.
The Preamble was **enacted after the rest of the Constitution** so that it matched the text.

n4e64be5b3bb.s: The date mentioned in the Preamble as ‘this twenty-sixth day of November, 1949’ refers to the date of:
o: Election of the first Lok Sabha
First meeting of the Constituent Assembly
n4e64be5b3bb.x: 26 November 1949 was the date on which the Constitution was adopted. It commenced on 26 January 1950.
n4e64be5b3bb.tq: Separate the closely associated adoption date from the commencement date.
xs: **26 November 1949** is the date of **adoption** of the Constitution — option **(2)**.
The Constitution **commenced** on **26 Jan 1950**, so option (1) is wrong.
xa: The Preamble ends: "IN OUR CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY this **twenty-sixth day of November, 1949**, do HEREBY ADOPT, ENACT AND GIVE TO OURSELVES THIS CONSTITUTION."
**Constitution Day** is observed on **26 Nov** (since **2015**).
The Objectives Resolution was moved on **13 Dec 1946**.

nf2ef0c766ce.s: The Preamble of the Constitution was enacted:
o: Before the rest of the Constitution
After the rest of the Constitution
Along with the Objectives Resolution in 1946
After the commencement of the Constitution
nf2ef0c766ce.x: The Preamble was enacted after the rest of the Constitution so that it would conform to the constitutional text.
xa: Objectives Resolution: moved **13 Dec 1946**, adopted **22 Jan 1947**.
The Preamble's date — **26 November 1949** — is the date of **adoption**.
Commencement: **26 Jan 1950**.

n07b6747ac6c.s: Constitution Day in India is observed on which date, and since which year has it been observed in this form?
n07b6747ac6c.x: Constitution Day is observed on 26 November, and it has been observed since 2015.
n07b6747ac6c.tq: Pair the date with the year rather than selecting a familiar national day or constitutional milestone.
xs: **Constitution Day** is observed on **26 Nov**, since **2015** — option **(2)**.
**26 November 1949** is the date the Constitution was **adopted**.
xa: **26 Jan 1950** is the date of **commencement**.
The Preamble has been amended **only once** (**42nd, 1976**).

nindian-polity-14-1.s: The Objectives Resolution, on which the Preamble was based, was adopted on:
nindian-polity-14-1.x: Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946 and it was adopted on 22 January 1947; 26 November 1949 is the date of adoption of the Constitution.
n: Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
The Objectives Resolution was adopted on 22 January 1947. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
The Preamble is based on the Objectives Resolution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
xa: Its **modified version** became the **Preamble**.
The idea of a preamble came from the **USA**; its **language** from **Australia**.
Liberty, Equality, Fraternity came from the **French Revolution (1789)**; Justice from the **Russian Revolution (1917)**.

nindian-polity-14-5.s: The date mentioned in the Preamble is:
n: The date mentioned in the Preamble is 26 November 1949. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
The word “Federal” is not mentioned in the Preamble. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
The Preamble can be amended under Article 368. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
The Preamble does not confer any power by itself. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
The Preamble does not create any right by itself. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
The date mentioned in the Preamble is the date of adoption. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
xa: The Preamble is **non-justiciable** — it cannot be **enforced in a court of law**.
It is used as an **aid to interpretation** of ambiguous provisions.
It has been amended **only once** — **42nd Amendment, 1976**.

nindian-polity-14-12.s: According to the Preamble, the Constitution was given to the people of India by:
nindian-polity-14-12.x: The Preamble says 'We, the people of India ... give to ourselves this Constitution', so the people are its source.
n: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
The Constituent Assembly enacted the Constitution on 26 November 1949. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
The Constituent Assembly gave the Constitution to itself on 26 November 1949. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
xa: The date in the Preamble is the date of **adoption**, not commencement (**26 Jan 1950**).
At commencement India was a **"Sovereign Democratic Republic"**.
**Constitution Day** is observed on **26 Nov** (since **2015**).

nindian-polity-14-18.s: The Preamble reflects the philosophy, the ideals and the ____ of the Constitution.
nindian-polity-14-18.x: The Preamble reflects the philosophy, ideals and objectives of the Constitution.
n: The Preamble reflects the philosophy of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
The Preamble reflects the ideals of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
The Preamble reflects the objectives of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
xa: It is **non-justiciable** and is **neither a source of power nor a limit on power**.
It is called the **Key to the Constitution** and the **Soul of the Constitution**.
Its basis is the **Objectives Resolution**, which laid down the philosophy and guiding principles.

n80d918de94e.s: The idea of Fraternity in the Preamble is possibly drawn from which Article of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
n80d918de94e.x: Fraternity, a sense of brotherhood promoted by single citizenship, is possibly drawn from Article 1 of the UDHR (1948), not Article 29.
xa: The Preamble's Fraternity assures **dignity of the individual** and **unity and integrity of the Nation**.
**Liberty, Equality, Fraternity** as a set come from the **French Revolution (1789)**.
The word **"Integrity"** in the Fraternity clause was added by the **42nd Amendment, 1976**.

n8693bdda2f7.s: The original Preamble of 1949 described India as a:
n8693bdda2f7.x: The 1949 Preamble described India as a 'Sovereign Democratic Republic' and referred to the 'unity of the Nation'.
xa: Present order: **Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic**.
At **commencement (26 Jan 1950)** India was described as a **"Sovereign Democratic Republic"**.
The Preamble has been amended **only once** — by the **42nd Amendment**.

n9275e52683b.s: The 42nd Amendment inserted 'Socialist' and 'Secular' into the Preamble between the words:
n9275e52683b.x: They were inserted between 'Sovereign' and 'Democratic', so the Preamble now reads 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic'.
xa: The **42nd Amendment** also added **"Integrity"** — "unity **and integrity** of the Nation".
The Preamble has been amended **only once**.
**Republic** means an **elected head of state**; no hereditary office.

nc43950c2645.s: A secular State in the Indian constitutional sense is one that:
o: Is hostile to all religious practices
Has an official religion but tolerates others
nc43950c2645.x: A secular State has no State religion and gives equal respect to all religions; it is not hostile to religion.
xa: **S.R. Bommai (1994)** reaffirmed secularism as **basic structure**.
Secularism was part of the basic structure **even before 1976**.

n559cd451f36.s: Before the insertion of the word ‘Secular’ in the Preamble, the word appeared in the Constitution in which context?
o: Article 25(2)(a) relating to regulation of secular activities associated with religious practice
Article 44 relating to a uniform civil code
Article 14 relating to equality before law
n559cd451f36.x: Before 1976, the word ‘secular’ appeared in Article 25(2)(a), which refers to secular activities associated with religious practice.
n559cd451f36.tq: Distinguish the specific Article from nearby Fundamental Rights and Directive Principle provisions.
xs: Before **1976**, the word "secular" appeared only in **Art. 25(2)(a)** — option **(1)**.
Secularism is linked to **Arts. 25-28**, not to Art. 44, 32 or 14.
xa: **Secular** was inserted in the Preamble by the **42nd Amendment, 1976**.
**S.R. Bommai (1994)**: a state government acting against secularism could be dismissed.
Secular = equal respect for all religions; **no state religion**.

n191f2bac169.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the terms used in the Preamble?
o: 'Democratic' covers political, social and economic democracy.
'Republic' means the head of state is elected.
'Republic' means no public office is hereditary.
n191f2bac169.x: 'Democratic' is not limited to political democracy; it covers social and economic democracy as well.
xa: Republic also means **public offices open to all**.
PYQ (APPSC G1 **2024**): "'democratic' is a mix of **British Fabian Socialism** and **American Populism**" — marked **not valid**.
**Republic** as an ideal is traced to the **French Revolution (1789)**.

n3214c5c8742.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the terms in the Preamble?
o: 'Socialist' denotes democratic socialism with public and private sectors co-existing.
Indian socialism is a blend of Marxism and Gandhism.
Indian socialism leans towards Gandhian socialism.
'Democratic' in the Preamble is a mix of British Fabian Socialism and American Populism.
n3214c5c8742.x: Describing 'Democratic' as a mix of Fabian Socialism and American Populism is not valid; the APPSC G1 2024 key treated it as wrong.
xa: **Democratic**: supreme power with the people; government responsible to the people.
**Socialist** was added by the **42nd Amendment, 1976**, along with Secular and Integrity.

nindian-polity-14-11.s: In the Indian context, secularism means:
o: A State religion with tolerance of others
nindian-polity-14-11.x: Secularism in India means equal respect for all religions.
n: Secularism means equal respect for all religions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
Democracy means government of the people. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
Democracy means government by the people. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
Democracy means government for the people. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
xa: ⚠ **APPSC G1 2024**: "'democratic' is a mix of British Fabian Socialism and American Populism" was marked **not valid**.
**Republic** = **elected** head of state; public offices open to all.

n2d6d483a031.s: Which of the following expressions is found in the Preamble?
n2d6d483a031.x: 'Dignity of the individual' is in the Preamble (fraternity assuring it); 'Federal', 'Fundamental Duties' and 'adult franchise' are not.
xa: "**Welfare state**" is also absent from the Preamble.

n70192500fde.x: The Preamble assures equality of status and opportunity, along with liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship.
xa: Liberty = **absence of restraints** + **opportunities** to develop one's personality.
Fraternity assures **dignity of the individual** and **unity and integrity of the Nation**.

n0275f2b6c15.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the objectives in the Preamble?
o: Economic justice means removing economic discrimination and glaring inequality.
Liberty means the complete absence of every restraint on individual activity.
Political justice means equal political rights and access to office.
Equality has civic, political and economic dimensions.
n0275f2b6c15.x: Liberty means absence of restraints plus opportunities to develop one's personality, not freedom from every restraint.
xa: **Social** justice = equal treatment without social distinction.
Liberty in the Preamble is of **thought, expression, belief, faith and worship**.
**Fraternity** is promoted by **single citizenship**.

n0735060a69a.s: In the Berubari Union case, the Supreme Court held that the Preamble:
o: was an integral part of the Constitution and could be amended under Article 368
formed the basic structure and could not be referred to for interpretation
was not a part of the Constitution, but could guide interpretation where an Article was ambiguous
was enforceable by constitutional courts as a source of legislative power
n0735060a69a.x: In the Berubari Union case (1960), the Preamble was held not to be a part of the Constitution, although it was regarded as a key to the minds of the framers and an aid to interpretation in cases of ambiguity.
n0735060a69a.tq: Separate the case’s holding on constitutional status from its limited interpretative use.
xs: **Berubari Union (1960)** held the Preamble is **NOT part** of the Constitution, but can **guide interpretation** where an article is **ambiguous** — option **(3)**.
"Integral part, amendable under **Art. 368**" is the later **Kesavananda Bharati (1973)** view — option (1) wrong.
xa: Berubari called the Preamble the **"key to the minds of the makers"**.
**Kesavananda Bharati** overruled Berubari; **LIC of India (1995)** called it an **integral part**.
The Preamble is **non-justiciable** — no court can enforce it.

n96addc89ca3.s: The 42nd Amendment's clauses giving Parliament unlimited amending power and excluding judicial review were struck down in:
n96addc89ca3.x: Those clauses of the 'Mini-Constitution' were struck down in Minerva Mills (1980); Kesavananda Bharati came before the 1976 amendment.
xa: Other changes: **Fundamental Duties**, new **DPSPs**, curbs on **judicial review**.
It added **Socialist, Secular, Integrity** to the Preamble.
Enacted during the **Emergency (1975-77)** under **Indira Gandhi**.

nc1a9eb84c61.s: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) is known for:
o: Holding that the Preamble is not part of the Constitution
Striking down absolute precedence of DPSPs over Fundamental Rights
Reaffirming secularism as part of the basic structure
Upholding 'Socialist' and 'Secular' in the Preamble in 2024
nc1a9eb84c61.x: S.R. Bommai (1994) reaffirmed secularism as part of the basic structure; Berubari, Minerva Mills and Balram Singh are the cases behind the other options.
xa: **Kesavananda Bharati (1973)**: Preamble amendable under **Art. 368**, but not its basic features.
**Waman Rao (1981)**: review applies to amendments after **24 Apr 1973**.
**Dr Balram Singh (25 Nov 2024)** upheld **'Socialist'** and **'Secular'**.

nb6920727187.s: In Dr Balram Singh v. Union of India, decided on 25 November 2024, the Supreme Court is stated to have—
o: struck down the insertions made in the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment.
upheld the words ‘Socialist’ and ‘Secular’ in the Preamble and rejected challenges to their insertion.
directed Parliament to conduct a fresh referendum on the Preamble.
held that the Preamble could never be reviewed by the judiciary.
nb6920727187.x: On 25 November 2024, the Supreme Court upheld ‘Socialist’ and ‘Secular’ in the Preamble and rejected challenges to the 42nd Amendment insertions.
nb6920727187.tq: Use the case-name and date to distinguish the latest judicial position from earlier constitutional debates.
xs: In **Dr Balram Singh (25 Nov 2024)** the SC **upheld 'Socialist' and 'Secular'** and **rejected challenges** to the 42nd Amendment insertions — option **(2)**.
So it did not strike down the insertions — option (1) wrong.
xa: The case came in the **75**-years-of-the-Constitution debate.
Criticism: the words were inserted during the **Emergency** without a fresh popular mandate.
Counter-view: secularism was always inherent in **Art. 25-28**.

ne67b2d95fe1.s: In the Berubari case, the Supreme Court described the Preamble as the:
o: Key to the minds of the makers of the Constitution
ne67b2d95fe1.x: In the Berubari case, the Supreme Court referred to the Preamble as the ‘key to the minds of the makers’ of the Constitution.
ne67b2d95fe1.tq: Distinguish a judicial description from the quotations attributed to individual scholars.
xs: **Berubari (1960)** described the Preamble as the **"key to the minds of the makers"** — option **(2)**.
The Preamble is **not a source of power** to the legislature — option (1) wrong.
xa: Berubari held the Preamble **NOT part** of the Constitution — overruled by **Kesavananda Bharati (1973)**.
**"Identity card"** — **N.A. Palkhivala**; **"Key-note"** — **Ernest Barker**.
**"Political horoscope"** — **K.M. Munshi**.

nindian-polity-14-7.s: The Golaknath case was decided in:

n: The Berubari Union Case was decided in 1960. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
The Golaknath Case was decided in 1967. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
The Kesavananda Bharati Case was decided in 1973. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]

xa: Berubari: Preamble is a **key to the framers' minds**, guiding interpretation where an article is ambiguous.

**S.R. Bommai** (**1994**) reaffirmed **secularism** as basic structure.

nindian-polity-14-8.s: Which case held that the Preamble is part of the Constitution and can be amended, but its basic structure cannot be destroyed?

The Kesavananda Bharati Case held that the Preamble can be amended. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
The Preamble can be amended under Article 368. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
The basic structure cannot be altered. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]

xa: **Secularism** was part of the basic structure **even before 1976**.
**Dr Balram Singh v. Union of India** (**25 Nov 2024**): SC **upheld 'Socialist' and 'Secular'** in the Preamble.

nindian-polity-14-15.tq: Link 'Preamble is part of the Constitution' to the basic-structure case.
n: The Golaknath Case held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 36-38]
xs: The **Kesavananda Bharati Case** held that the Preamble is part of the Constitution — option **(3)**.

nfb6351cf74e.s: In which case did the Supreme Court call the Preamble a key to the minds of the framers?

n88f3fa41185.s: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 was enacted during the Emergency under the leadership of:

n54b28db43a5.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?

Freezing of delimitation of parliamentary seats
Addition of new Directive Principles of State Policy

n343b7b378c5.s: Which child born in India between 26 January 1950 and 30 June 1987 could NOT acquire citizenship by birth?
