Both the UK and Indian Prime Ministers must be members of the lower House.
Neither the UK nor the Indian Prime Minister may be a member of the upper House.
n0bdc0557043.x: The UK Prime Minister must belong to the House of Commons, while the Indian Prime Minister may be a member of either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.
n0bdc0557043.tq: Use the House-membership distinction to separate the British and Indian parliamentary arrangements.
xs: The **UK PM** must belong to the **House of Commons**, while the **Indian PM** may belong to **either House** — so option **(2)** is correct.
India has had Rajya Sabha PMs: **Indira Gandhi** (first, **1966**), **Deve Gowda**, **I.K. Gujral**, **Manmohan Singh** — so options (1), (3), (4) fail.
xa: A **non-member** can be PM for **six months** (**Art 75(5)**).
By convention the PM is the leader of the **Lok Sabha majority**.
The PM is appointed by the **President** under **Art 75(1)**.

nindian-polity-9-9.s: What is the maximum period for which the Vice-President may act as President when the office of President falls vacant or the President is unable to discharge functions?
nindian-polity-9-9.x: The Vice-President can act as President for at most six months, within which a new President must be elected.
n: The maximum period for which the Vice-President acts as President is six months. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 25-27]
An election for a new President must be held within six months when the Vice-President acts as President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 25-27]
The Vice-President acts as President under Article 65 when the office of the President falls vacant. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 25-27]
The Vice-President acts as President when the President is unable to discharge the President’s functions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 25-27]
xs: The VP can act as President for a maximum of **six months** — option **(1)**.
A new President must be **elected within six months** of the vacancy (**Article 65** context; Art 62).
He acts on **death, resignation, removal**, or when the President is **unable to discharge functions** (absence, illness).
xa: While acting as President he **ceases to be RS Chairman** → the **Deputy Chairman** presides.
He draws the **President's salary, allowances and privileges**, not the Chairman's.
As Chairman of the RS his salary is **not charged** on the **Consolidated Fund of India**.

nindian-polity-46-33.s: Which Article gives Ministers the right to speak in both Houses of Parliament?
nindian-polity-46-33.x: Article 88 gives Ministers the right to speak in both Houses; 75(2) is pleasure tenure, 75(3) collective responsibility and 75(5) the six-month rule.
n: Union Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President under Article 75(2). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
A non-member Minister must become a member of either House within six consecutive months. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
A Union Minister can speak and participate in the proceedings of both Houses. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
A Union Minister can speak and participate in joint sittings of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible only to the Lok Sabha under Article 75(3). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
The Council of Ministers is not collectively responsible to Parliament as a whole. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
The Council of Ministers is not collectively responsible to the President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
xa: The President removes a Minister only **on the PM's advice**.
**S.R. Chaudhuri v. State of Punjab (2001):** a non-member **cannot be re-appointed** repeatedly without election.

nindian-polity-7-5.s:
Which of the following bodies are chaired by the Prime Minister?
1. NITI Aayog
2. National Development Council
3. Inter-State Council
nindian-polity-7-5.x: The Prime Minister chairs all three, as well as the National Integration Council.
n: The Prime Minister is the Chairman of NITI Aayog. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
The Prime Minister is the Chairman of the National Development Council. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
The Prime Minister is the Chairman of the National Integration Council. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
The Prime Minister is the Chairman of the Inter-State Council. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
xa: The PM also chairs the **National Disaster Management Authority**.
He chairs key Cabinet Committees: **ACC**, **CCS**, **CCPA** and **CCEA**.
Under **Article 78** the PM is the **link** between the President and the Council of Ministers.

nindian-polity-7-13.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the duties of the Prime Minister towards the President?
o: The PM communicates to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers.
These duties are laid down in Article 74.
The PM submits a Minister's decision for the Council's consideration when the President so requires.
The PM furnishes information sought by the President.
nindian-polity-7-13.x: These duties of the PM are laid down in Article 78; Article 74 provides for the Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President.
n: The Prime Minister acts as the link between the President and the Council of Ministers under Article 78. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
The Prime Minister communicates all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
The Prime Minister furnishes information required by the President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
The Prime Minister submits matters for reconsideration of the Council of Ministers if the President so requires. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
xa: The matter submitted for reconsideration is one **decided by an individual Minister**.
**Article 74:** Council of Ministers to **aid and advise** the President; advice binding after one reconsideration.

nindian-polity-7-16.s:
The Prime Minister advises the President on which of the following?
1. Appointment of other Ministers
2. Dissolution of the Lok Sabha
3. Appointment of the Chief Justice of India
nindian-polity-7-16.x: The PM advises the President on appointing Ministers and dissolving the Lok Sabha. The CJI is appointed through the collegium process, not on the PM's advice.
n: The Prime Minister advises the President on the appointment of other Ministers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
The Prime Minister advises the President on the summoning of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
The Prime Minister advises the President on the prorogation of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
The Prime Minister advises the President on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
The Prime Minister advises the President on the declaration of Emergency through the recommendation of the Cabinet. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
xa: PM chairs **NITI Aayog**, **NDC**, **National Integration Council**, **Inter-State Council** and **NDMA**.
⚠ The President does **not** acquire discretionary powers during a **National Emergency** — advice stays binding.

n82eeaab72fd.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the removal of the Vice-President of India?
o: The resolution must originate in the Rajya Sabha.
The resolution needs a majority of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha.
The Lok Sabha must agree to the resolution by a simple majority.
The Constitution specifies the grounds for removal.
n82eeaab72fd.x: The Constitution does not state any grounds for removing the Vice-President; the other three statements describe the procedure correctly.
xa: **14 days' notice** is needed before the resolution is moved.
⚠ The President is removed by **impeachment** (**Art 61**), in **either House**, by **2/3**.
"Where can the removal resolution first be moved" → **Rajya Sabha** is a stock exam angle.

n0204774e030.s: Article 75(2) was referred to in the acceptance of a Minister's resignation because that Article relates to
o: collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha
the President's pleasure regarding the tenure of Ministers
the Prime Minister's duty to furnish information
n0204774e030.x: Article 75(2) provides that Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President, which operates in practice on the advice of the Prime Minister.
n0204774e030.tq: Link a constitutional clause to its operative subject instead of to a neighbouring Article.
xs: **Art 75(2)** says ministers hold office **during the pleasure of the President** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The President removes a minister only **on the PM's advice**; collective responsibility, authentication (**Art 77(2)**) and the PM's duty to inform (**Art 78**) are other provisions.
xa: MoS **Ravneet Singh Bittu**'s resignation was accepted "under clause (2) of Article 75" (**Jul 2026**).
**George Kurian** resigned on **23 Jun 2026**; both left after their **Rajya Sabha** terms ended on **21 Jun 2026**.
The PM has **no fixed tenure** — he too holds office during the President's pleasure.

n3a3eeb78383.s: Under Article 74(1), the advice of the Council of Ministers becomes binding on the President after the President
o: secures approval from the Election Commission
refers the matter to the Supreme Court
obtains the consent of the Rajya Sabha
n3a3eeb78383.x: The President may require the Council of Ministers to reconsider its advice once, but must act in accordance with the advice tendered after such reconsideration.
n3a3eeb78383.tq: Focus on the one permitted reconsideration rather than an unlimited presidential discretion.
xs: Under **Art 74(1)**, the CoM's advice is **binding after one reconsideration** — so option **(4) has it reconsidered once** is correct.
No **Election Commission**, **Supreme Court** or **Rajya Sabha** step is involved.
xa: **Art 74(2):** the advice is **not inquired into** by any court.
⚠ Even in a **National Emergency**, the President gets **no discretionary powers** — advice stays binding (PYQ).
The CoM is **headed by the PM**.

n74969792cf4.s: Which Article provides that the advice tendered by Ministers to the President shall not be inquired into by any court?
n74969792cf4.x: Article 74(2) bars courts from inquiring into ministerial advice; Article 77 deals with executive action in the President's name, authentication of orders and business rules.
xa: **Art 78:** PM's duty to **communicate** all CoM decisions to the President.

n3b967908902.s: Under Article 77(3), the President makes rules for the convenient transaction of the business of the Government of India and for its allocation among Ministers. These rules are known as the
o: Union Executive Rules and Ministerial Responsibility Rules
Allocation of Business Rules and Transaction of Business Rules
Conduct of Government Rules and Delegation Rules
Rules of Procedure of Parliament and Cabinet Manual
n3b967908902.x: Article 77(3) is implemented through the Allocation of Business Rules, 1961 and the Transaction of Business Rules, 1961.
n3b967908902.tq: Identify the precise official titles associated with a constitutional rule-making power.
xs: Art 77(3) rules are the **Allocation of Business Rules, 1961** and **Transaction of Business Rules, 1961** — so option **(2)** is correct.
They are often called the **AoB and ToB Rules, 1961**.
xa: **Art 77(1):** executive action **in the President's name**; **77(2):** **authentication** of orders.
**Art 78:** PM must **communicate** all CoM decisions and furnish information called for.
**Art 74(2):** advice **not inquired into** by any court.

n2adab80b6eb.s: When Manmohan Singh, a Rajya Sabha member, was Prime Minister, who was named Leader of the House in the Lok Sabha?
n2adab80b6eb.x: The Leader of the House is not a constitutional office; a PM who is not a Lok Sabha member nominates a minister, and Pranab Mukherjee was named under Manmohan Singh.
xa: First Leader of the House: **Nehru**.
**Manmohan Singh** was a **Rajya Sabha** PM, like **Deve Gowda** and **I.K. Gujral**.
Other non-constitutional posts: **Deputy PM** and the **PMO**.

n5fa1681944b.s: P.V. Narasimha Rao, who became Prime Minister in 1991 without being an MP, later entered the Lok Sabha from:
n5fa1681944b.x: Narasimha Rao, the first PM from South India, entered the Lok Sabha from Nandyal.
xa: AP angle: **M. Venkaiah Naidu** (Nellore) was VP **2017-22**.
**1956 Gentlemen's Agreement** fixed the united AP cabinet at **60% Andhra : 40% Telangana**.

n01536151771.s: Under the 130th Constitution Amendment Bill, 2025, a Minister detained for 30 consecutive days for an offence punishable with five or more years would be removed on the:
n01536151771.x: The Bill provides for removal on the 31st day after 30 consecutive days of detention; it touches Articles 75, 164 and 239AA.
xa: The Bill covers the **PM, CM and ministers** alike.
**Art 75** covers Union ministers; **Art 164** State ministers.
**Art 75(1B):** a member disqualified for **defection** cannot be a minister until **re-elected**.

nindian-polity-46-20.s: Which body is the core decision-making body of the Union Government?
nindian-polity-46-20.x: The Union Cabinet, the top tier of the ministerial hierarchy, is the core decision-making body, not the whole Council of Ministers.
n: The four-tier classification of Ministers is a practical convention or tradition. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
The Constitution does not classify Ministers into four tiers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
The Union Cabinet is the highest executive category within the ranking hierarchy. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
The Council of Ministers is a collective constitutional entity. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
The Union Cabinet is the core decision-making body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
The Union Cabinet is the apex policy-formulation body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
xa: Four ranks: **Cabinet Ministers**, **Ministers of State (Independent Charge)**, **Ministers of State**, **Deputy Ministers**.
**MoS (independent charge)** hold a ministry/department on their own; **MoS** are attached to Cabinet Ministers.
Council size **60–80**; Cabinet size **15–20**.

nindian-polity-7-6.s: Which Article provides for a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President?
nindian-polity-7-6.x: Article 74 provides for the Council of Ministers to aid and advise; Article 75 covers appointment and tenure, and Article 78 the PM's duties.
n: Article 74 provides for a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
Article 74 provides for the Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
Article 75 deals with the appointment, tenure, responsibility and other provisions relating to Ministers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
Article 75 provides for other provisions relating to Ministers, including appointment and responsibility. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
Article 78 deals with the duties of the Prime Minister. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
The Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha under Article 75(3). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
xa: "All work of the GoI is done in the **name of the President**" — **Art 77**.

nff5f643de4e.s: Under Article 75(1A), the Union Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, cannot exceed ____ of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
nff5f643de4e.x: The 91st Amendment (2003) inserted Article 75(1A), capping the Council of Ministers including the PM at 15 per cent of the Lok Sabha's total strength.
xa: At **543** seats the cap is **81** ministers.
**Art 75(1B):** a member disqualified for **defection** cannot be a minister until **re-elected**.
States: **Art 164(1A)** — not over **15%** of the Assembly and **not less than 12**.

n043fffea491.s: A member of Parliament disqualified for defection under the Tenth Schedule is, by virtue of Article 75(1B),
o: eligible only after approval by the Election Commission
permanently barred from becoming a Union Minister
ineligible to be appointed Union Minister until re-elected to Parliament
eligible to be appointed Union Minister immediately after disqualification
n043fffea491.x: Article 75(1B), inserted by the 91st Amendment, prevents a member disqualified for defection from being appointed a minister until re-elected to Parliament.
n043fffea491.tq: Test the duration and condition of disqualification instead of treating it as a permanent bar.
xs: Under **Art 75(1B)**, a member disqualified for **defection** cannot be a minister **until re-elected** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is not a **permanent** bar, not immediate eligibility, and needs no **Election Commission** approval.
xa: Both **Art 75(1A)** and **75(1B)** came with the **91st Amendment Act, 2003**.
**Art 75(1A):** total ministers including the PM ≤ **15%** of the Lok Sabha.
At **543** seats the cap is **81**.

n41c47e78c3b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the size of a State Council of Ministers under Article 164(1A)?
o: Ministers, including the CM, cannot exceed 15% of the Assembly's strength.
The number of ministers cannot be less than 12.
In a 294-member Assembly the maximum, including the CM, is 45.
The limit was inserted by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.
n41c47e78c3b.x: 15% of 294 is 44.1, so the maximum is 44 (e.g. West Bengal), not 45.
xa: Union equivalent: **Art 75(1A)** — **15%** of the **Lok Sabha**, i.e. **81** at **543** seats.
The State limit was asked in **APPSC-G2 2017**; the Union limit in **APPSC G2 2025**.
⚠ The Union has **no minimum** like the State floor of **12**.

na87818cb0dd.s: The classification of Union Ministers into different ranks is based on:
o: convention and the choice of the Prime Minister
the Third Schedule of the Constitution
na87818cb0dd.x: The Constitution does not classify ministers into ranks; the ranks, including Deputy Minister, rest on convention and the PM's choice.
xa: The four ranks: **Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State (Independent Charge), Ministers of State, Deputy Ministers**.
**Deputy Ministers** assist Cabinet Ministers/MoS.
**Deputy PM** is **not mentioned in the Constitution** and takes oath as an ordinary minister.

n46a5e3896bb.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the categories of Union Ministers?
o: A Deputy Minister heads an important ministry and attends Cabinet meetings.
A Cabinet Minister heads an important ministry and attends Cabinet meetings.
A Minister of State with independent charge holds a ministry on his or her own.
A Minister of State is attached to a Cabinet Minister.
n46a5e3896bb.x: A Deputy Minister only assists a senior Minister; it is the Cabinet Minister who heads an important ministry and attends Cabinet meetings.
xa: The **Constitution does not classify ministers** into ranks — the ranking is **by convention**, by the PM's choice.
Total ministers incl. the PM ≤ **15%** of the **Lok Sabha** (**Art 75(1A)**).
**Deputy PM** is not a rank in the Constitution; first Deputy PM: **Sardar Patel**.

n34123f973a8.s: The 1956 Gentlemen’s Agreement relating to the united Andhra Pradesh cabinet provided for the proportion of Andhra and Telangana representation as
n34123f973a8.x: The 1956 Gentlemen’s Agreement fixed the united Andhra Pradesh cabinet proportion at 60% Andhra and 40% Telangana.
n34123f973a8.tq: Retain the direction of the comparison as well as the two percentages.
xs: The **1956 Gentlemen's Agreement** fixed the united AP cabinet at **60% Andhra : 40% Telangana** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Options (2), (3), (4) misstate the agreed ratio.
xa: AP angle: **P.V. Narasimha Rao**, first **PM from South India**, entered the LS from **Nandyal** (**1991**).
**M. Venkaiah Naidu** (Nellore) was **Vice-President 2017-22**.
⚠ State ministries are capped at **15%** of the Assembly and **not less than 12** (**Art 164(1A)**).

o: the PM and Cabinet-rank Ministers only
the PM, Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers
the PM and Ministers of State only
the PM, Cabinet Ministers and Deputy Ministers
nindian-polity-46-10.x: The Cabinet (about 15–20) is the PM and Cabinet-rank Ministers; the wider Council (about 60–80) also includes Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers.
n: The Council of Ministers is a wider constitutional body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
The Council of Ministers has 60–80 members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
The Union Cabinet has 15–20 members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]

The Council of Ministers consists of the Prime Minister, Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State with independent charge, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
The Union Cabinet consists only of the Prime Minister and Cabinet-rank Ministers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
xa: The Council is the **wider** collective constitutional body; the Cabinet is the **inner core** of policy-making.
The four-tier classification is a **convention** — the Constitution does **not** classify Ministers.

nindian-polity-46-11.s: The word referring to the Union Cabinet was inserted into Article 352(3) by which amendment?
nindian-polity-46-11.x: The word 'Cabinet' was absent from the original Constitution and was inserted into Article 352(3) by the 44th Amendment (1978), requiring the Cabinet's written advice for an Emergency.
n: The original constitutional text lacked the word “Cabinet.” [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
The word “Cabinet” was inserted into Article 352(3) by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 123-125]
xs: The word "Cabinet" was inserted into **Article 352(3)** by the **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978** — option **(2)**.
It was **not in the original text** of the Constitution.
The **91st Amendment Act, 2003** instead capped the ministry at **15%** of the Lok Sabha.
xa: Under **Article 352(3)** an Emergency is proclaimed only on the **written** advice of the Union Cabinet.
The **Council of Ministers** itself rests on **Articles 74 and 75**.
⚠ **44th** (Cabinet word) vs **91st** (15% cap on Ministers).

nindian-polity-12-12.s: What is the quorum of the Lok Sabha?
nindian-polity-12-12.x: The quorum of the Lok Sabha is one-tenth of its total membership. One-fifth and one-third are distractors.
nindian-polity-12-12.tq: Recall the quorum fraction for either House of Parliament.
n: The quorum of the Lok Sabha is one-tenth of its total membership. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 32-34]
xs: The quorum of the Lok Sabha is **one-tenth of its total membership** — option **(1)**.
The notes list the **quorum** as **one-tenth** of the total membership; one-fifth, one-third and one-half are distractors.
xa: **91st Amendment Act, 2003:** Ministers capped at **15%** of the **total strength of the Lok Sabha** — **81** at **543** seats.
States (**Article 164(1A)**): **15%** of the Assembly, **minimum 12** Ministers.
A member disqualified for **defection** cannot be a minister until re-elected (**Art 75(1B)**).

nindian-polity-7-12.s:
Which of the following are powers of the Prime Minister as head of the Council of Ministers?
1. Selecting Ministers
2. Allocating portfolios to Ministers
3. Asking any Minister to resign
nindian-polity-7-12.x: As head of the Council, the PM selects Ministers, allocates portfolios and can ask any Minister to resign.
n: The Prime Minister selects Ministers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
The Prime Minister allocates portfolios to Ministers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
The Prime Minister can ask any Minister to resign. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 20-22]
xa: **Article 78:** PM **communicates** all Council decisions to the President and **furnishes information** he requires.
The PM advises on **summoning** and **prorogation** of Parliament and **dissolution** of the Lok Sabha.
PM's **death/resignation** **dissolves** the Council.

nd745458bbef.s: Which one of the following Vice-Presidents also served two full terms?
nd745458bbef.x: Hamid Ansari served two full terms as Vice-President from 2007 to 2017. Dr. S. Radhakrishnan was the other Vice-President associated with two terms.
nd745458bbef.tq: Distinguish the two-term office-holders from Vice-Presidents who served only one term.
xs: **Hamid Ansari** served **two full terms** as VP (**2007-17**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**R. Venkataraman** (1987), **K.R. Narayanan** (1997) and **V.V. Giri** (1969) are remembered as VPs who **became President**.
xa: **S. Radhakrishnan**, the **first VP**, also held **two terms** (**1952-62**).
**M. Venkaiah Naidu** (Nellore) was VP **2017-22**.
⚠ **S. Radhakrishnan** = first VP; **C.P. Radhakrishnan** = present VP (2025).

n433bf34b68f.s: The Prime Minister’s Office is best described as a/an
o: parliamentary committee of the Lok Sabha
statutory body headed by the President
extra-constitutional staff agency of the Prime Minister
n433bf34b68f.x: The Prime Minister’s Office is not mentioned in the Constitution; it is an extra-constitutional staff agency assisting the Prime Minister.
n433bf34b68f.tq: Distinguish constitutional, statutory and extra-constitutional institutions by their legal source.
xs: The **PMO** is **not mentioned in the Constitution** — it is an **extra-constitutional staff agency of the PM** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is not created by **Art 77**, not a parliamentary committee and not a statutory body.
xa: Other non-constitutional posts: **Deputy PM** and **Leader of the House (LS)**.
**Art 77(3)** rules (**AoB and ToB Rules, 1961**) allocate government business.
First Deputy PM: **Sardar Patel**; rank **5A** in the Table of Precedence.

nb23c1672a2e.s: Who was the first Prime Minister of India and also holds the record for the longest overall tenure as Prime Minister?
nb23c1672a2e.x: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India and had the maximum aggregate tenure as Prime Minister, from 1947 to 1964.
nb23c1672a2e.tq: Directly identify the office-holder associated with two linked firsts.
xs: **Jawaharlal Nehru** was the first PM and holds the **longest overall tenure** (**1947-64**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Narendra Modi** became the longest **continuously serving elected** PM on **10 June 2026**, but **Nehru keeps the aggregate record**.
xa: Modi passed **Indira Gandhi's** continuous tenure in **July 2025**.
Modi cannot exceed Nehru's **unbroken 1947-64** term — the 2026 record is likely his combined **CM + PM** time.
First acting PM: **Gulzarilal Nanda** (twice: **1964, 1966**).

n886da302b8c.s: Who was the first acting Prime Minister of India (in 1964 and 1966)?
n886da302b8c.x: Gulzarilal Nanda was the first acting Prime Minister, in 1964 and again in 1966.
xa: Nanda acted in **1964** and **1966**.
Other RS PMs: **H.D. Deve Gowda, I.K. Gujral, Manmohan Singh**.
**P.V. Narasimha Rao** (**1991**) became PM **without being an MP**.

nf10481d5310.s: Which one of the following was NOT a Prime Minister of India who came from the Rajya Sabha?
nf10481d5310.x: The Prime Ministers from the Rajya Sabha were Indira Gandhi (the first, 1966), H.D. Deve Gowda, I.K. Gujral and Manmohan Singh. Charan Singh was a Lok Sabha member, not a Rajya Sabha PM (he is noted as the PM who never faced the Lok Sabha).
nf10481d5310.tq: Find the odd office-holder by comparing the complete list of Rajya Sabha Prime Ministers.
xs: **Charan Singh** was NOT a Rajya Sabha PM — he is noted as the PM who **never faced the Lok Sabha** (**1979**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**H.D. Deve Gowda**, **I.K. Gujral** and **Manmohan Singh** are the other PMs from the **Rajya Sabha**.
xa: The **first PM from the Rajya Sabha** was **Indira Gandhi** (**1966**).
The Indian PM **may belong to either House**; the **UK PM** must belong to the **House of Commons**.
**P.V. Narasimha Rao** (**1991**) became PM **without being an MP** and later won **Nandyal**.

nindian-polity-9-18.s: Who was the first President of India to die in office?
nindian-polity-9-18.x: Dr Zakir Husain was the first President to die in office; V.V. Giri then acted as President in 1969.
n: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan was the longest-serving Vice-President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 25-27]
Dr. S. Radhakrishnan served two terms as Vice-President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 25-27]
Mohammad Hamid Ansari is the only person to serve two full terms as Vice-President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 25-27]
xa: VPs who became President: **Radhakrishnan (1962)**, **Zakir Husain (1967)**, **V.V. Giri (1969)**, **R. Venkataraman (1987)**, **S.D. Sharma (1992)**, **K.R. Narayanan (1997)**.
**Jagdeep Dhankhar** resigned in July **2025** — the **third mid-term vacancy** after **V.V. Giri** (1969) and **Krishan Kant** (2002, died).
Present VP: **C.P. Radhakrishnan** (September **2025**).

n035b588a334.s: The existence of nominal and real executives is a feature of the:
n035b588a334.x: Nominal and real executives and dissolution of the lower House are parliamentary features; separation of powers marks the presidential system.
xa: Parliamentary: **majority party rule**, **collective responsibility**, **political homogeneity**, **secrecy of procedure**.
Presidential: **fixed-term executive**, **no legislative responsibility** of the executive.
Ministers in India are MPs — **double membership**.

n411d5b2a95b.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the feature that most clearly marks India as a parliamentary system?
o: Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers
n411d5b2a95b.x: Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the elected House is the characteristic feature distinguishing the parliamentary system.
n411d5b2a95b.tq: Identify the defining institutional feature rather than a general constitutional feature.
xs: India is parliamentary because of **collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers** — so option **(4)** is correct (APPSC **2025**).
It is **not separation of powers or judicial review**; the other options (indirect election, written Constitution, federalism) do not define the parliamentary form.
xa: **Art 75(3):** the CoM is collectively responsible to the **Lok Sabha**.
Ministers **"sink or swim together"**.
Underlying principle of Cabinet form: ensuring **collective responsibility of the Government to the people** (UPSC **2017**).

n45442414735.s: The underlying principle of the Cabinet form of government in India is:
o: Collective responsibility of the Government to the people
Supremacy of the President over Parliament
Complete separation of the executive from the legislature
n45442414735.x: The Cabinet form is a mechanism of parliamentary democracy for ensuring collective responsibility of the Government to the people (UPSC 2017 key).
xa: India's defining feature = **collective responsibility** (APPSC **2025**).
The **Cabinet** is the **nucleus** that meets regularly and takes policy decisions.

ne02e6d090e6.s: Which body generally meets regularly and takes the policy decisions of the Union Government?
o: The Council of Ministers as a whole
ne02e6d090e6.x: The wider Council of Ministers (Articles 74 and 75) rarely meets as a body; the Cabinet meets regularly and takes policy decisions.
xa: CoM ranks: **Cabinet Ministers, MoS (independent charge), MoS, Deputy Ministers**.
The Cabinet **directs and supervises** the Council.
The word "Cabinet" appears only in **Art. 352**.

n3a8e1188a02.s: The expression 'ministers sink or swim together' means that:
o: Each minister answers only for his own department
All ministers must defend Cabinet decisions or resign
Ministers may publicly oppose Cabinet decisions
Only Cabinet Ministers share responsibility for policy
n3a8e1188a02.x: Collective responsibility requires all ministers to support Cabinet decisions publicly; a minister unwilling to defend such a decision must resign.
xa: **Political homogeneity** and **secrecy** → differences ironed out behind closed doors, a **public show of unity**.

n33a3be6c9a5.s: The kitchen cabinet is criticised mainly because it:
o: Is a constitutional body with a fixed membership
Is an extra-constitutional power centre that may bypass the Cabinet
Is directly answerable to the Lok Sabha
n33a3be6c9a5.x: The kitchen cabinet is criticised as an extra-constitutional power centre because it may shape decisions while bypassing the formal Cabinet.
xa: Example: **Indira Gandhi's advisers**.
**GoMs/EGoMs** were criticised for **delay** and **diluting collective responsibility**.
**PMO** and cabinet committees are also criticised for concentrating power.

nfcc87391c51.s: A no-confidence motion against the Union Council of Ministers can be moved in:
o: a joint sitting of both Houses
nfcc87391c51.x: Under Article 75(3) the Council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, so a no-confidence motion lies only there; even Rajya Sabha ministers are responsible to the Lok Sabha.
xa: Responsibility is **not to both Houses**, and **not to the President**.

n105d43128a8.s: The death or resignation of the Prime Minister results in:
o: The Council of Ministers going out of office
Automatic dissolution of the Lok Sabha
The senior-most minister automatically becoming Prime Minister
Only the Prime Minister's office falling vacant
n105d43128a8.x: The Prime Minister heads the Council of Ministers, so his death or resignation means the Council of Ministers as a whole goes out of office.
xa: **Loss of LS confidence** (no-confidence motion, defeat on a money bill/major policy) → **whole ministry resigns**.
Defeat in the **Rajya Sabha** does **not** bring down the government.

n709be685f8e.s: The oaths of office and secrecy to Union Ministers are administered by the
n709be685f8e.x: The President administers the oaths of office and secrecy to Union Ministers in accordance with the Third Schedule.
n709be685f8e.tq: Identify the constitutional authority associated with administering the oath.
xs: Oaths of **office and secrecy** to Union Ministers are administered by the **President** (**Third Schedule**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **PM**, **CJI** or **Speaker** play no part in ministers' oaths.
xa: The **oath of secrecy** ensures the **secrecy** of Cabinet deliberations.
Ministers hold office at the **President's pleasure** (**Art. 75(2)**).
**Arts. 74-75** create the Council of Ministers.

n53b72cf7f02.s: In the States, the constitutional provision corresponding to Article 75(3) on collective responsibility is:
n53b72cf7f02.x: Article 164(2) provides that the Council of Ministers in a State is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.
n53b72cf7f02.tq: Discriminate between neighbouring constitutional provisions by matching the subject with the exact Article.
xs: The State counterpart of **Art 75(3)** is **Article 164(2)** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Under it the State CoM is collectively responsible to the **Legislative Assembly**.
xa: **Art 75(3):** Union CoM collectively responsible to the **Lok Sabha**.
⚠ **75(3)** = collective; **75(2)** = individual responsibility.
A **no-confidence motion** at the Union lies **only in the Lok Sabha**.

ne3e5d9379c8.s: Which of the following does NOT, by itself, require the whole Union ministry to resign?
o: Passage of a no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha
Defeat on a money bill in the Lok Sabha
Defeat on a major policy measure in the Lok Sabha
Defeat of the Government in the Rajya Sabha
ne3e5d9379c8.x: Only loss of Lok Sabha confidence can lead the ministry to resign; defeat in the Rajya Sabha does not by itself compel resignation.
xa: The no-confidence motion lies **only in the Lok Sabha**.
**PM's death/resignation** dissolves the Council.
RS ministers are also responsible to the **Lok Sabha**.

nf1e13b63a28.s: The secrecy of Cabinet deliberations is principally ensured by the:
nf1e13b63a28.x: The oath of secrecy ensures confidentiality of Cabinet deliberations and supports the public presentation of a united government.
nf1e13b63a28.tq: Distinguish the oath connected with confidentiality from the general oath of office.
xs: Secrecy of Cabinet deliberation is ensured by the **oath of secrecy** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Differences are **ironed out behind closed doors**, with a **public show of unity**.
xa: Oaths of **office and secrecy** are in the **Third Schedule**, administered by the **President**.
Cabinet decisions **bind all ministers** even if they differed inside.
**Secrecy of procedure** is a parliamentary-system feature.

n0f1ae9f0a24.s: Under Article 75(2), a Union Minister holds office during the pleasure of the:
n0f1ae9f0a24.x: Article 75(2) provides that a Union Minister holds office during the pleasure of the President; in practice the Prime Minister may ask a minister to resign or advise his dismissal.
xa: The **PM** can ask a minister to resign or **advise the President to dismiss** him (UPSC).
A resigned minister may make a **personal statement** in the House with the **Speaker's consent**.

ne024c502f6e.s: As of April 2025, how many Cabinet Committees function in India?
ne024c502f6e.x: There are eight: Appointments, Security, Political Affairs, Economic Affairs, Parliamentary Affairs, Accommodation, Investment and Growth, and Employment and Skill Development.
xa: The **2019** committees: **Investment and Growth** + **Employment and Skill Development**.
Not PM-chaired: **Parliamentary Affairs** + **Accommodation**.
They work under the **ToB Rules, 1961**.

n2de13198db5.s: Which of the following Cabinet Committees is NOT chaired by the Prime Minister?
n2de13198db5.x: The Accommodation Committee is chaired by a senior minister; the PM chairs the Appointments, Security and Political Affairs Committees.
xa: The PM also chairs the **CCEA**.
⚠ Not PM-chaired = **Parliamentary Affairs** + **Accommodation**.

nc3014f731d8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Cabinet Committees?
o: The decision on caste enumeration in the Census was taken by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs.
The Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs is described as a 'super cabinet'.
The Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs handles Centre-State and political issues.
The Committees on Investment and Growth and on Employment and Skill Development were set up in 2019.
nc3014f731d8.x: Caste enumeration in the Census was decided by the Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs, not the CCEA.
xa: The **CCEA** handles economic and infrastructure projects.
The **PM** chairs both the CCPA and CCEA.

o: A Cabinet Committee formed under the Transaction of Business Rules
An informal inner circle of the Prime Minister's trusted colleagues and friends
The Cabinet Secretariat headed by the Cabinet Secretary
The Cabinet Ministers within the Council of Ministers
n6c0447a337b.x: A kitchen cabinet is an informal inner circle of the Prime Minister's trusted colleagues and friends, including some senior ministers and non-ministers.
xa: Criticism: an **extra-constitutional** power centre that **bypasses the Cabinet**.
**GoMs/EGoMs** are ad hoc groups reporting to the Cabinet; abolished in **2014**.
Cabinet committees are **extra-constitutional** bodies under the **ToB Rules, 1961**.

nde7185555f6.s: During single-party majority eras, the dominance of the Union Cabinet over Parliament led to the criticism of a:
nde7185555f6.x: In single-party majority eras the Prime Minister and Cabinet generally dominated Parliament, leading to the criticism that the system resembled a 'cabinet dictatorship'.
xa: **Coalition era (1989-2014):** allies' demands weakened Cabinet cohesion.
**Kitchen cabinet** criticism: an extra-constitutional power centre.
⚠ **Shadow Cabinet** (UK) has no formal counterpart in India.

n48bfd796bf3.s: Who is regarded as the State equivalent of the Cabinet Secretary?
n48bfd796bf3.x: The Chief Secretary is regarded as the State equivalent of the Cabinet Secretary. G. Sai Prasad took charge as Andhra Pradesh Chief Secretary in February 2026.
n48bfd796bf3.tq: Apply the Union–State administrative equivalent pairing.
xs: The State equivalent of the Cabinet Secretary is the **Chief Secretary** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Advocate General** is the State counterpart of the **AG**, not the Cabinet Secretary.
xa: **G. Sai Prasad** took charge as AP Chief Secretary (**Feb 2026**).
The Cabinet Secretary is the **senior-most civil servant**, **11th** in precedence.
Cabinet Secretary tenure: **2 years**, extendable up to **4 years**.

n10d8744bf8f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Department of Personnel?
o: It originated from the Administrative Reforms Commission of 1966.
The N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar report recommended it to provide a minister and secretary solely for administrative reform.
It was placed under the Prime Minister.
n10d8744bf8f.x: The Ayyangar report did not suggest a minister and secretary solely for administrative reform; the Department came in 1970 out of the 1966 ARC and was placed under the PM.
xa: The **N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar report (1949)** dealt with **reorganising the machinery** of Central Government.
It recommended **grouping ministries** and **cabinet committees**.
**AoB** and **ToB Rules** date from **1961**.

nfcdbe4ab161.s: The N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar report on the reorganisation of the machinery of government dates from:
nfcdbe4ab161.x: The 1949 Ayyangar report dealt with reorganising the machinery of government, including grouping of ministries and Cabinet Committees.
xa: ⚠ It did **not** suggest a minister and secretary solely for administrative reform (UPSC **2021** key).
**ARC (1966)** → **Department of Personnel (1970)**, under the **PM**.

n2395dd033cb.s: Cabinet Committees in India are formed under the:
n2395dd033cb.x: Cabinet Committees are extra-constitutional bodies formed under the Transaction of Business Rules, 1961, framed under Article 77(3).
xa: Criticism: power concentrated in the **PMO and cabinet committees** dilutes collective Cabinet decision-making.

n43bd5c2ad15.s: In which year were the existing Groups of Ministers (GoMs) and Empowered GoMs abolished?
n43bd5c2ad15.x: The existing GoMs and EGoMs, criticised for delay and diluting collective responsibility, were abolished in 2014.
xa: The **kitchen cabinet** is the PM's **informal inner circle**.
Coalition era (**1989-2014**): coordination committees weakened Cabinet cohesion.

n93bfd64371b.s: During 1989–2014, Cabinet cohesion and collective responsibility were weakened mainly by:
o: Direct exercise of Cabinet powers by the President
Coordination committees and demands of alliance partners
Frequent dissolution of the Rajya Sabha
n93bfd64371b.x: Coalition governments had to accommodate coordination committees and the demands of alliance partners, which weakened Cabinet cohesion and collective responsibility.
xa: In **single-party majority eras**, PM and Cabinet dominate → **"cabinet dictatorship"** charge.
**GoMs/EGoMs** were criticised for delay and diluting collective responsibility.

ne509ae39309.s: The Cabinet Secretariat functions directly under the:
ne509ae39309.x: The Cabinet Secretariat, which serves the Cabinet and its committees and administers the Business Rules, functions directly under the PM.
xa: It coordinates ministries via **Committees of Secretaries**.
It sends a **monthly summary** of ministries' work to the President, VP and ministers.
Wings: **Civil, Military, Intelligence**.

o: The Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs
The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet
nd1e55b22f93.x: The ACC appoints the Cabinet Secretary, the senior-most civil servant, for two years extendable up to four.
xa: He is **ex officio Chairman** of the **Civil Services Board** and heads the **National Crisis Management Committee**.
He is **11th** in the order of precedence.
**T.V. Somanathan:** **one-year extension** beyond **30 Aug 2026**.
The Cabinet Secretariat works **directly under the Prime Minister** — ⚠ not under the VP.

n56ad280a58b.s: Who heads the National Crisis Management Committee?
n56ad280a58b.x: The Cabinet Secretary, first among equals among Secretaries and eleventh in the Table of Precedence, heads the NCMC.
xa: He is **ex officio Chairman of the Civil Services Board**.
Tenure: **2 years**, extendable up to **4 years**.
⚠ The **AG** also has precedence **11**; the **SG** has **23**.

n2b284642d21.s: By convention, the Attorney General of India resigns when:
o: The Chief Justice of India retires
n2b284642d21.x: The Constitution fixes no term for the Attorney General, but by convention he resigns when the government changes.
xa: First AG: **M.C. Setalvad**; first SG: **C.K. Daphtary**.
⚠ The **Solicitor General** has a **3-year** term.
The AG is **constitutional** (**Art 76**); the SG is **statutory**.

n95cfa6ac770.s: Who was the first Attorney General of India?
n95cfa6ac770.x: M.C. Setalvad was the first Attorney General of India. C.K. Daphtary was the first Solicitor General.
n95cfa6ac770.tq: Discriminate between the first holders of two closely related law offices.
xs: The first Attorney General of India was **M.C. Setalvad** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **C.K. Daphtary** was the **first Solicitor General**.
xa: The AG is a **constitutional** office under **Art 76**; the SG is **statutory**.
The AG is the **first law officer** (precedence **11**); the SG the **second** (precedence **23**).
The AG's **term and removal are not fixed**; he holds office during the **President's pleasure**.

nc5f206f285a.s: Which Article, among the following, specifically deals with the Attorney General's right to speak and participate in Parliament without voting rights?
nc5f206f285a.x: Article 88 confers the Attorney General's right to speak and take part in parliamentary proceedings without the right to vote. Article 78 concerns the duties of the Prime Minister in relation to the President.
nc5f206f285a.tq: Reject the look-alike Article number and identify the precise constitutional provision.
xs: **Article 88** lets the AG **speak** in either House, joint sittings and committees **without vote** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ Some practice questions give **"Art. 78"** — that is wrong; **Art 105(4)** gives an MP's **privileges**, and **Art 76** creates the office.
xa: He may take part in any **committee** of which he is named a member.
He has **audience in all courts** in India.
State parallel: the **Advocate General** speaks in the legislature under **Art 177**.

nindian-polity-31-10.s: Who is the highest law officer of the Government of India?
nindian-polity-31-10.x: The Attorney General is India's highest law officer; the Solicitor General assists the Attorney General.
n: The Attorney General of India is the highest law officer of the Government of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
The Attorney General of India serves the Union Government at the national level. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
The Advocate General serves the State Government. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
The Solicitor General of India serves the Union Government and assists the Attorney General of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
xa: The AG has precedence **11**; the SG, the **second law officer**, precedence **23**.
The SG gives **no advice** to the government — he only appears in courts.
**First AG:** **M.C. Setalvad**; **first SG:** **C.K. Daphtary**.

nindian-polity-31-13.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Attorney General of India?
o: He advises the Government of India on legal matters
He performs legal duties referred to him by the President
He holds office during the pleasure of the President
He performs legal duties referred to him by a State Governor
nindian-polity-31-13.x: The Attorney General performs legal duties referred by the President, not by a Governor; the State's legal adviser is the Advocate General.
n: The Attorney General of India advises the Government of India on legal matters. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
The Attorney General of India performs other legal duties referred by the President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
xa: The AG is a **constitutional** post under **Article 76**.
**First AG:** **M.C. Setalvad**.
The AG is **not debarred from private practice** but must not hold a brief **against GoI**.

nindian-polity-31-14.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Advocate General of a State is appointed by the Governor.
The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
The Solicitor General's term is fixed at appointment, usually three years.
The Advocate General of a State is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet.
nindian-polity-31-14.x: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet appoints the Solicitor General of India; the Advocate General is appointed by the Governor.
n: The Advocate General of a State is appointed by the Governor of the State. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
The Solicitor General of India is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
The Advocate General of a State holds office during the pleasure of the Governor. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
The Solicitor General of India has a fixed statutory term. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: other notes say the **ACC recommends** SG/ASGs → the **President appoints**.
The **AG** holds office at the **pleasure of the President**; term not fixed.
The SG has **no floor rights** in Parliament.

n84497b50ecd.s: Experience under which Acts influenced India's adoption of the parliamentary form of government?
o: Government of India Acts of 1919 and 1935
Regulating Act of 1773 and Pitt's India Act of 1784
n84497b50ecd.x: India chose the parliamentary form because of experience under the Acts of 1919 and 1935 and to avoid a personality cult.
xa: Defining feature of India's system = **collective responsibility** (APPSC **2025**).
Necessary features: **majority party rule**, **collective responsibility**, **PM as centre of power** (APPSC **2019**).
Parliamentary system has **nominal (President)** and **real (PM)** executives.

n0f4df986727.s: Which of the following is a necessary feature of the parliamentary form of government in India?
o: Complete separation of the executive from the legislature
n0f4df986727.x: Majority party rule, collective responsibility and the PM as the centre of power are its necessary features; complete separation of powers belongs to the presidential system.
xa: India chose the system from experience under the **1919 and 1935 Acts** and to avoid a **personality cult**.
⚠ Separation of powers = **USA** feature.

n2d871a6489d.s: The word 'Cabinet' was inserted into Article 352 of the Constitution by the:
n2d871a6489d.x: The 44th Amendment, 1978 inserted it; Article 352(3) is the only place the word 'Cabinet' appears.
xa: **Arts. 74-75** create the **Council of Ministers**; the Cabinet otherwise rests on **convention**.

naa1a494fdcb.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Parliament of India?
naa1a494fdcb.x: Parliament consists of the President, the Council of States and the House of the People; State Legislative Councils are not part of it.
xa: Large and diverse countries prefer **two Houses** to represent all sections and regions.
Unicameral: **China**, **Israel**, **New Zealand**, **Sweden**, **Denmark**.
AP is **bicameral**.

n8fce548c6c7.s: Israel's unicameral national legislature is called the:
n8fce548c6c7.x: Israel, like China, New Zealand, Sweden and Denmark, has a unicameral legislature; it is the Knesset.
xa: India's Parliament is **bicameral**: **Rajya Sabha + Lok Sabha**.
Bicameral examples: **UK**, **USA**, **Japan**, **Russia**, **Australia**.
**Bangladesh** voted in **Feb 2026** for a **bicameral** Parliament.

nindian-polity-62-4.s: Bicameralism was first introduced at the Centre in India by the:
nindian-polity-62-4.x: The Government of India Act, 1919 first brought bicameralism to the Centre (Council of State and Central Legislative Assembly); the 1935 Act brought it to some provinces.
n: Bicameralism was first introduced in India at the Central level by the Government of India Act, 1919. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The Government of India Act, 1919, created the Council of State and the Central Legislative Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
xa: India's Parliament: **Council of States (Rajya Sabha)** + **House of the People (Lok Sabha)**.
Large and diverse countries prefer **two Houses** to represent all sections and regions.
Unicameral examples: **China**, **Israel**, **New Zealand**, **Sweden**, **Denmark**.

nindian-polity-62-20.s: Which of the following can be abolished under Article 169 of the Constitution?
nindian-polity-62-20.x: A State Legislative Council, though a permanent House, can be abolished under Article 169; the Rajya Sabha cannot be abolished.
n: The State Legislative Council can be abolished. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The State Legislative Council can be abolished under Article 169. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The Council of States cannot be abolished. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The Council of States is a permanent body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The Legislative Council cannot be dissolved on the recommendation of the Governor. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
xa: Pre-condition: **Assembly resolution** by a **majority of total membership** and **two-thirds** of members **present and voting**.
AP's Council was abolished in **1985** and revived in **2007**.
A **2020** resolution to abolish it again was withdrawn in **2021**.

n76f3a527f3f.s: The Parliament of Russia is officially known as the
n76f3a527f3f.x: Russia's Parliament is the Federal Assembly. The Federation Council is its upper house and the State Duma is its lower house.
n76f3a527f3f.tq: Distinguish the name of the complete legislature from the names of its two chambers.
xs: Russia's Parliament is the **Federal Assembly** — so option **(1)** is correct (UPSC **2005**).
⚠ The **Federation Council** is its **upper** house and the **State Duma** its **lower** house — not the Parliament's name.
xa: Japan's Parliament: **Diet**; USA's: **Congress**.
China's legislature: **National People's Congress** (unicameral).
Israel's: **Knesset** (unicameral).

n02ee91632a7.s: Which one of the following is NOT an argument advanced in favour of a second chamber?
o: States, regions and diverse interests receive representation.
It necessarily makes the legislative process faster.
Experts can be brought into the legislature through nomination.
Every Bill receives a second examination.
n02ee91632a7.x: A second chamber is argued to provide a double check, regional representation and expert participation. Delay and duplication are generally cited as arguments against it, not in its favour.
n02ee91632a7.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated advantage into a consequence of bicameral delay.
xs: A second chamber does **not** make legislation faster — **delay** is an argument **against** it — so option **(2)** is correct.
Arguments for: **double check** (every bill discussed twice), representation of **states/regions**, **experts** through nomination.
xa: Against: **duplication**; **not directly elected**, less democratic.
**Abbé Sieyès**: "If it agrees it is superfluous, if it dissents it is mischievous".
**N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar** defended the RS as a House for **dignified debate**.

n41c22714a80.s: 'If it agrees it is superfluous, if it dissents it is mischievous' — this criticism of a second chamber is attributed to:
n41c22714a80.x: This criticism of a second chamber is attributed to Abbé Sieyès.
xa: Ayyangar saw the RS as able to **delay hasty legislation** passed in the passion of the moment.
Against a second chamber: **delays**, **duplication**, **not directly elected**.
For: a **double check** on hasty decisions.

n1f83229ad75.s: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar defended the Rajya Sabha mainly as a forum for:
o: Dignified debate and delaying hasty legislation
n1f83229ad75.x: Ayyangar regarded the Rajya Sabha as a forum for dignified debate that could delay legislation passed in the passion of the moment.
xa: ⚠ **Abbé Sieyès** criticised second chambers as **"superfluous"** or **"mischievous"**.
**Nehru** cautioned against the judiciary becoming a **"third chamber"**.
The RS also **brings experts** in through nomination (**12** nominated members).

nef83f733b0e.s: Within how many days must the Rajya Sabha return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha?
nef83f733b0e.x: A Money Bill must be returned within 14 days, showing the Rajya Sabha is weaker than the Lok Sabha in financial matters.
xa: The **Speaker** certifies money bills and presides over **joint sittings**.
The RS has **12** nominated members; the US Senate none.
RS members are elected by **elected MLAs** by **STV**.

n14db45eda9f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Rajya Sabha can initiate a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers.
The Speaker certifies whether a Bill is a Money Bill.
The Speaker presides over a joint sitting of Parliament.
The Rajya Sabha has no vote on Demands for Grants.
n14db45eda9f.x: A no-confidence motion is a device of the Lok Sabha alone, not the Rajya Sabha.
xa: Money bills are introduced **only in the LS**; the RS must return them in **14 days**.
A larger LS would **dilute the RS's weight in joint sittings** (**Apr 2026**).
RS seats are by **population** (**Fourth Schedule**).

n4b4b4c632c1.s: For creating or abolishing a Legislative Council under Article 169, the State Assembly must pass a resolution by:
o: A majority of total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting
A two-thirds majority of the total membership
A simple majority of members present and voting
A majority of the total membership alone
n4b4b4c632c1.x: The resolution must be passed by a majority of the total membership and by not less than two-thirds of members present and voting.
xa: **Art. 171:** Council size not more than **one-third** of the Assembly; at least **40**.
AP's Council was **abolished in 1985** and **revived in 2007**.
Unicameral States: **Goa**, **Mizoram**, **Sikkim**.

nb40c7604217.s: The minimum strength of a State Legislative Council is:
nb40c7604217.x: A Legislative Council must have at least 40 members and cannot exceed one-third of the Assembly's strength.
xa: Pre-condition: **Assembly resolution** by **majority of total membership** and **two-thirds** present and voting.
AP's **2020** abolition resolution was **withdrawn in 2021**.
Older notes listed six/seven bicameral states including **J&K**.

nindian-polity-62-3.s: Which State has the largest Legislative Council, with 100 seats?
nindian-polity-62-3.x: Uttar Pradesh has the largest Legislative Council, with 100 seats, among the six bicameral States.
nindian-polity-62-3.tq: Recall the largest of the six State Legislative Councils.
n: Uttar Pradesh has the largest Legislative Council, with 100 seats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
India currently has 6 bicameral States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
Uttar Pradesh is a bicameral State. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
xs: **Uttar Pradesh** has the largest Legislative Council, with **100** seats — option **(3)**.
UP is one of the **six** bicameral States.
**Maharashtra**, **Bihar** and **Andhra Pradesh** are also bicameral but have smaller Councils.
xa: Other bicameral States: **Telangana** and **Karnataka**.
**Art. 171:** Council not more than **one-third** of the Assembly; at least **40** members.
**Art. 169:** Parliament creates or abolishes a Council **by law**.

nindian-polity-62-37.s:
Which of the following States have bicameral legislatures?
1. Telangana
2. Bihar
3. Karnataka
nindian-polity-62-37.x: All three are bicameral. With Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh they make up the six bicameral States.
n: Telangana is a bicameral State. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
Bihar is a bicameral State. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
Maharashtra is a bicameral State. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
Karnataka is a bicameral State. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
India currently has 6 bicameral States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
xa: Largest Council: **Uttar Pradesh**, **100** seats.
Older notes list six/seven bicameral states including **J&K**.
Unicameral examples: **Goa**, **Mizoram**, **Sikkim**.

n7881026a795.s: Besides its 30 elected members, the Puducherry Assembly can have:
n7881026a795.x: Puducherry has 30 elected members and up to 3 nominated members; Delhi has 70 seats and Jammu and Kashmir 90 elected seats.
xa: Bases: Delhi **Art. 239AA**; Puducherry **Art. 239A**; J&K the **J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019**.
These three are the **only UTs** with elected members in the **Rajya Sabha**.
The **UT Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026** extends **women's reservation** to these legislatures.

ne72a7f21ae1.s: Which Union Territories have elected members in the Rajya Sabha?
o: Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir
Delhi, Daman and Diu and Dadra and Nagar Haveli
ne72a7f21ae1.x: Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir are the three Union Territories having elected members in the Rajya Sabha.
ne72a7f21ae1.tq: Use the complete three-member list and reject Union Territories without elected Rajya Sabha representation.
xs: **Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir** are the only UTs with elected RS members — so option **(2)** is correct.
These are the three UTs with legislatures.
xa: Delhi: **Art. 239AA**, **70** seats.
Puducherry: **Art. 239A**, **30** elected + up to **3** nominated.
J&K: **J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019**, **90** elected seats.

n75d07308797.s: The Legislative Council of Andhra Pradesh, abolished in 1985, was revived in:
n75d07308797.x: The AP Legislative Council was abolished in 1985 and revived in 2007; the 2020 resolution to abolish it again was withdrawn in 2021.
xa: Councils are created/abolished by Parliament **by law** under **Art. 169**.
Council size: ≤ **one-third** of the Assembly, at least **40** (**Art. 171**).
Unicameral States: **Goa**, **Mizoram**, **Sikkim**.

nd0c4d844c83.s: The Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was introduced with the objective of extending women's reservation to the legislatures of
o: All Union Territories having no Legislative Assembly
Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir
nd0c4d844c83.x: The Bill introduced in 2026 sought to extend women's reservation to the legislatures of Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir.
nd0c4d844c83.tq: Match the current legislative proposal with the exact set of affected Union Territories.
xs: The **Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026** extends **women's reservation** to **Delhi, Puducherry and J&K** (**17 Apr 2026**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
These are the three UTs **with legislatures**; Chandigarh, Ladakh and Lakshadweep have none in the notes.
xa: They are also the **only UTs** with elected **Rajya Sabha** members.
⚠ **239AA** = Delhi; **239A** = Puducherry.
J&K Assembly: **90** elected seats.

na782ceb2ac0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the President as a component of Parliament?
o: The President is a part of Parliament but not a member of either House.
No Bill passed by Parliament becomes law without the President's assent.
The President summons and prorogues the Houses of Parliament.
The President sits in Parliament as a member while addressing the Houses.
na782ceb2ac0.x: The President is a component of Parliament but never sits as a member of either House.
xa: He also **dissolves** the Lok Sabha and issues **ordinances**.
**Art. 86:** may address either House or both.
Comparison: **Crown-in-Parliament** (UK).

n2003beefe86.s: Under Article 87, the President makes a special address to both Houses at the commencement of:
o: the first session after each general election and the first session of each year
only the first session after each general election
only the first session of each year
n2003beefe86.x: The Article 87 special address is made at the first session after each general election and the first session of each year; Article 86 is the general power to address either or both Houses.
xa: The President **summons** and **prorogues** Parliament and **dissolves** the Lok Sabha.
He **nominates 12** members to the Rajya Sabha.
Parliament = **President + Rajya Sabha + Lok Sabha** (**Art. 79**) — no bill becomes law without his **assent**.

n6d89fe3390a.s: The present composition of the Rajya Sabha is correctly represented by which one of the following?
o: 238 representatives of States and Union Territories and 7 nominated members
225 representatives of States, 12 representatives of Union Territories and 8 nominated members
225 representatives of States, 8 representatives of Union Territories and 12 nominated members
238 representatives of States and Union Territories and 12 nominated members
n6d89fe3390a.x: The present strength is 245: 225 representatives of States, 8 representatives of Union Territories and 12 nominated members.
n6d89fe3390a.tq: Separate present composition from the constitutional maximum.
xs: The present RS (**245**) = **225** States + **8** UTs + **12 nominated** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The 8 UT seats come from **Delhi, Puducherry and J&K**.
xa: The **12** nominees come under **Art. 80(1)(a)** and **80(3)**.
⚠ RS: **250** max / **245** present.
n6d89fe3390a.fixed: option 4 (233 elected + 12 nominated) was also correct; replaced with the maximum-strength figure

n9f358e61db5.s: The representatives of a State in the Rajya Sabha are elected by:
o: all members of the State Legislative Assembly, including nominated members
the elected members of the State Legislative Assembly
the elected members of both Houses of the State Legislature
the people of the State directly
n9f358e61db5.x: Under Article 80(4) they are elected by the elected MLAs through PR-STV; nominated MLAs do not take part.
xa: UT members are chosen as **Parliament provides by law**.
**Kuldip Nayar v. UoI (2006)** upheld the **open ballot** in RS elections.
Lok Sabha: **direct election**, adult suffrage (**Art. 326**), **first past the post**.

nc7a0bf724a7.s: The present strength of the Lok Sabha is composed of
o: 530 members from States and 13 from Union Territories
524 members from States and 19 from Union Territories
525 members from States and 18 from Union Territories
nc7a0bf724a7.x: The present strength is 543, comprising 524 members from the States and 19 from the Union Territories.
nc7a0bf724a7.tq: Split the total into its State and Union Territory components.
xs: The present Lok Sabha (**543**) = **524** from States + **19** from UTs — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **530** States + **20** UTs is the **maximum** (**550**).
xa: **Art. 81** governs LS composition.
Older figure **552** included **2** nominated **Anglo-Indians**.
Seats: **Delhi 7**, **J&K 5**.

n2c405a7220b.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the maximum and present strength of the Lok Sabha?
n2c405a7220b.x: The constitutional maximum is 550, while the present strength is 543. The older figure of 552 included two nominated Anglo-Indian members.
n2c405a7220b.tq: Compare the current figure with the historical figure instead of treating them as interchangeable.
xs: LS **maximum 550**, **present 543** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The older figure **552** counted **2** nominated **Anglo-Indians**.
xa: Anglo-Indian nomination was ended by the **104th Amendment, 2019**.
⚠ RS: **250** max / **245** present.

n6baa4f0559c.s: The voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 years by the:
n6baa4f0559c.x: The 61st Amendment lowered the voting age under Article 326 from 21 to 18 years (in force 1989).
xa: **33rd Amendment (1974):** streamlined acceptance of **resignation**.
**84th Amendment (2001):** froze LS seat allocation on the **1971 census** till the first census **after 2026**.
**104th Amendment (2019):** ended **Anglo-Indian** nomination.
n6baa4f0559c.fixed: 61st Amendment Act is of 1988 (in force 1989); ye61be0c88ab, y3def781bd24

n928374dd039.s: Nominated members of the Rajya Sabha can vote in the election of the:
o: both the President and the Vice-President
neither the President nor the Vice-President
n928374dd039.x: Nominated members vote in the Vice-Presidential election but not in the Presidential election.
xa: After **6 months**, joining a party attracts disqualification under the **Tenth Schedule**.
They **take full part in debates**.
No nominated member has so far been in the **Council of Ministers**.

n71ae71792ca.s: In which year was Sachin Tendulkar nominated to the Rajya Sabha?
n71ae71792ca.x: Sachin Tendulkar was nominated in 2012 and Mary Kom in 2016.
xa: ⚠ Sport is **not a listed field**: **literature, science, art, social service**.
**12** members are nominated by the **President**.
Nominees **cannot vote** in the Presidential election.

n71d762870e8.s: Seats in the Rajya Sabha are allotted to the States under the:
n71d762870e8.x: Seats are allotted by population under the Fourth Schedule (Arts. 4 and 80(2)), not equally as in the US Senate; UP has the most (31).
xa: Order: **UP 31**, Maharashtra **19**, Tamil Nadu **18**, West Bengal **16**, Bihar **16**.
AP has **11** RS seats (APPSC **2023**).
Single-seat States include **Goa**, **Sikkim**, **Tripura**.

nb7f10a39f72.s: Which one of the following groups consists only of States having one seat each in the Rajya Sabha?
o: Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Manipur and Tripura
nb7f10a39f72.x: Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura each have one Rajya Sabha seat. The group in option a contains only such States.
nb7f10a39f72.tq: Check every member of the group against the single-seat condition.
xs: **Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Manipur and Tripura** each have **one** RS seat — so option **(1)** is correct.
Each other group includes a State not on the single-seat list.
xa: Full single-seat list: **Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura** (+ UT **Puducherry**).
⚠ **Tripura** has **1** RS seat but **2** LS seats.
**UP** has the most RS seats: **31**.

n069a4ff84b7.s: How many Lok Sabha seats does Telangana have?
n069a4ff84b7.x: Telangana has 17 Lok Sabha seats; Andhra Pradesh has 25 and Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir 5 each.
xa: RS seats: AP **11**, Telangana **7**, Uttarakhand **3**, J&K **4**.
Assemblies: AP **175**, Telangana **119**, Uttarakhand **70**, J&K **90**.
**UP** has the most LS seats: **80**.

ndd272db4da4.s: How many Lok Sabha seats does Tripura have?
ndd272db4da4.x: Tripura has 2 Lok Sabha seats (and one Rajya Sabha seat); Sikkim, Mizoram and Nagaland have one Lok Sabha seat each.
xa: Other single-seat UTs: **A&N Islands**, **Chandigarh**, **Puducherry**.
**Ladakh** is the largest LS constituency by area; **Lakshadweep** the smallest by electors.
Delhi has **7** LS seats.

nf2794f45b9d.s: The President dissolves the Lok Sabha before its term on the advice of the:
nf2794f45b9d.x: Early dissolution is on the PM's advice, not the Speaker's, and cannot be challenged in court; the five-year term runs from the first meeting (Art. 83(2)).
xa: **18 Lok Sabhas** constituted so far.

o: dissolved along with the Lok Sabha
a permanent House not subject to dissolution
dissolved by the President on the PM's advice
n2414d16c71e.x: The Rajya Sabha is permanent and never dissolved; its members retire by rotation.
xa: A member's term is **6 years**, fixed by the **RPA 1951**.
In **1952**, who retired first was decided by **lottery**.
Only the **LS** is dissolved.

n6410a8cec46.s: The term of a member of the Rajya Sabha is six years. This term is fixed by the
o: Rules of Procedure of the Rajya Sabha
n6410a8cec46.x: The six-year term of a Rajya Sabha member is fixed by the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and not directly by the Constitution.
n6410a8cec46.tq: Use the statutory-versus-constitutional distinction to avoid an authority trap.
xs: The RS member's **6-year** term is fixed by the **Representation of the People Act, 1951**, not the Constitution — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ A classic trap: the Constitution itself does not fix it.
xa: The RS is **never dissolved**; **one-third retire every second year**.
First RS (**1952**): terms curtailed, retirees chosen by **lottery**.
The LS term (**5 years**) is in **Art 83(2)**.

n919c20bace3.s: In the first Rajya Sabha constituted in 1952, the members who were to retire first were selected by
o: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
n919c20bace3.x: To initiate the one-third retirement cycle, the terms of the initial members were curtailed and the members retiring first were decided by lottery.
n919c20bace3.tq: Use a precise institutional detail rather than a general feature of rotation.
xs: In the **first Rajya Sabha (1952)**, those retiring first were chosen by **lottery** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The President curtailed initial terms to start the **one-third** cycle.
xa: About **one-third retire every second year**.
Member's term: **6 years** (**RPA 1951**).
**Art. 83(1):** RS is **not subject to dissolution**.

neae7fbebb7c.s: The minimum age for membership of the Rajya Sabha is:
neae7fbebb7c.x: The minimum age is 30 for the Rajya Sabha and 25 for the Lok Sabha; no educational qualification is prescribed.
xa: Both need **citizenship** and an oath before an **EC-authorised person**.
Candidates must be **electors** in a parliamentary constituency (**RPA 1951**).
RS **domicile** requirement was **removed in 2003**.

nc6c1f520bae.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about disqualification on the ground of defection?
o: A member who voluntarily gives up membership of his party is liable to disqualification.
An independent member who joins a party after election is liable to disqualification.
A nominated member who joins a party after six months from taking his seat is liable to disqualification.
The President decides every question of disqualification under the Tenth Schedule.
nc6c1f520bae.x: Under the Tenth Schedule the Speaker of the Lok Sabha or the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha decides such questions, subject to judicial review.
xa: Voting/abstaining against the whip, unless condoned within **15 days**, is another ground.
Subject to **judicial review** — **Kihoto Hollohan (1992)**.
⚠ **Art. 102** grounds → **President** (on EC opinion).

n4eecb9ef37b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about women's reservation under the 106th Constitutional Amendment?
o: It applies to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
Its operation is governed by Article 334A.
It reserves one-half of the seats in these legislatures.
It is initially meant to operate for fifteen years and may be extended.
n4eecb9ef37b.x: The 106th Amendment reserves one-third of the seats, not one-half.
xa: It is the **106th Amendment, 2023** (**Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam**).
Operative only **after the next Census and delimitation**.

n28a0fe76ad3.s: Which Article allows the business of Parliament to be transacted in Hindi or English?
n28a0fe76ad3.x: Article 120 recognises Hindi and English and lets a member use his mother tongue with the presiding officer's permission.
xa: Quorum: **one-tenth** (**Art. 100**).
Rules of procedure: **Art. 118**.

n67f6017a070.s: No tax can be imposed without the approval of the:
n67f6017a070.x: No tax can be levied without Lok Sabha approval; questions and motions are other tools of control over the executive.
xa: Ministers are **collectively responsible** to the Lok Sabha.
The **RS cannot remove the Council of Ministers**.

n3efe888d8e1.s: Which one of the following is NOT an electoral function of Parliament?
o: Participating in the election of the President
Electing the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha
n3efe888d8e1.x: A is the answer: Parliament's electoral functions are electing the Vice-President, taking part in the President's election and electing its presiding officers (the Lok Sabha elects the Speaker and Deputy Speaker). The Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the President, not elected by Parliament, so A is not an electoral function.
n3efe888d8e1.tq: Find the item that is an appointment function rather than an electoral function of Parliament.
xs: **Appointing the Chief Election Commissioner** is NOT an electoral function of Parliament — so option **(1)** is correct.
Electoral functions: **elects the VP**, **takes part in the President's election**, **elects presiding officers** (Speaker and Deputy Speaker).
Parliament only **recommends removal** of the **CEC** — a judicial function.
xa: The **Rajya Sabha** elects only the **Deputy Chairman** (VP is ex officio Chairman).
Election laws: **RPA 1950 and 1951**; **Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952**.

nffa4bf616b2.s: Which Article protects the freedom of speech of members in Parliament?
nffa4bf616b2.x: Article 105 bars court proceedings for anything said or any vote given in Parliament or its committees; it does not cover statements made outside.
xa: **Sita Soren (2024)**: no privilege for a **bribe**.

n8fdf33ff085.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sita Soren case (2024)?
o: It was decided by a seven-judge Bench.
It held that privilege does not protect a legislator who takes a bribe to vote or speak.
It held that every speech made by a legislator outside the House is protected by Article 105.
It overruled the protection recognised in P.V. Narasimha Rao (1998) on this point.
n8fdf33ff085.x: Sita Soren held no such thing; it held that parliamentary privilege does not protect bribery for voting or speaking.
xa: **Kihoto Hollohan (1992)**: Tenth Schedule decisions subject to judicial review.
**Kuldip Nayar (2006)**: upheld **open ballot** in RS elections.

nd72053ba9a5.s: The right to be informed of a member's arrest, detention or release is:
o: an individual privilege of the member
a Fundamental Right of the member under Article 22
a collective privilege of the House
a privilege of the Presiding Officer alone
nd72053ba9a5.x: Being informed of a member's arrest, detention or release is a collective privilege of the House.
xa: Individual privilege: freedom from **civil** arrest **40 days** before and after a session.
Both collective and individual privileges exist.

nf1def5a64e7.s: Besides members, parliamentary privileges also extend to the:
nf1def5a64e7.x: Privileges extend to ministers, the Attorney-General and others who speak in the House; the House also has collective privileges.
xa: Individual: **freedom of speech**, **jury service** exemption.

nd57bd0502b1.s: Under the proposal to enlarge the Lok Sabha by about 50% once the 1971 freeze lifts, its strength would rise to about:
nd57bd0502b1.x: The House would grow to about 815, and the 15% ministerial ceiling would rise from 81 to 122 (133 by another source).
xa: The **84th Amendment (2001)** froze LS seat allocation on the **1971 census** till the first census **after 2026**.
The **Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026** sought a maximum of **850** seats.

n42655f5dbae.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026?
o: It was introduced along with the Delimitation Bill, 2026.
