It sought to raise the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850.
It was passed by the Lok Sabha with the required special majority.
The proposed 850 seats comprised 815 for the States and 35 for the Union Territories.
n42655f5dbae.x: The Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha and so did not secure the required special majority.
xa: It also sought to **fast-track women's reservation**.
It fell short of the **Art. 368** special majority.

n18fbbfabd42.s: The Tamil Nadu Assembly resolution on Lok Sabha delimitation sought to freeze the Lok Sabha at:
n18fbbfabd42.x: The Tamil Nadu Assembly resolved to retain the Lok Sabha at 543 seats and preserve the approximate 2.2:1 Lok Sabha–Rajya Sabha ratio.
xa: Southern States fear losing share to **UP, Bihar and Rajasthan**.
Present LS strength: **543** (**524** States + **19** UTs).

nindian-polity-2-42.s: Which Article deals with the composition of the Lok Sabha?
nindian-polity-2-42.x: Article 81 covers the Lok Sabha; 79 the constitution of Parliament, 80 the Rajya Sabha and 83 the duration of the Houses.
n: Article 79 concerns the constitution of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 80 concerns the composition of the Rajya Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 81 concerns the composition of the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 83 concerns the duration of the Houses of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
xa: **Article 85:** **sessions, prorogation and dissolution**.
**Article 87:** **special address** by the President.
Parliament is covered in **Arts. 79-122**, **Part V**.

nindian-polity-12-13.s: What was the elected strength of the First Lok Sabha?
nindian-polity-12-13.x: The First Lok Sabha had 489 elected seats; the present elected strength is 543.
n: The Lok Sabha has 19 elected members from the Union Territories (524 from the States). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 32-34]
The first Lok Sabha had 489 elected members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 32-34]
Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of Lok Sabha seats, with 80 seats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 32-34]
xa: Maximum strength: **550** — up to **530** from States + up to **20** from UTs.
Seats: **Delhi 7**, **J&K 5**.

nindian-polity-13-12.s: What proportion of Rajya Sabha members retire every two years?
nindian-polity-13-12.x: A member serves six years and about one-third retire every two years; a casual vacancy is filled only for the rest of the term.
n: The term of a Rajya Sabha member is six years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 34-36]
Approximately one-third of Rajya Sabha members retire every two years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 34-36]
A casual vacancy in the Rajya Sabha is filled for the remainder of the term. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 34-36]
xa: ⚠ The member's **6 years** is fixed by the **RPA 1951**, not by the Constitution.
In **1952** the first members' retirement order was decided by **lottery**.

nindian-polity-45-11.s: The maximum sanctioned strength of the Rajya Sabha is:
nindian-polity-45-11.x: The maximum is 250: 238 from States and UTs and 12 nominated members.
n: The minimum age for a Rajya Sabha member is 30 years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 120-123]
The maximum sanctioned strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 120-123]
The Rajya Sabha has 238 members representing States and Union Territories. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 120-123]
The President nominates 12 Rajya Sabha members for expertise in literature, science, art, and social service. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 120-123]
The minimum age for membership of the Legislative Council is 30 years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 120-123]
xa: Present strength **245** — **233** elected + **12** nominated.
⚠ RS: **250** max / **245** present.

ne6d05edbb8c.s: Which Article provides for the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
ne6d05edbb8c.x: Article 89(2) provides for the Deputy Chairman, chosen from among Rajya Sabha members; the Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman under Articles 64 and 89(1), and Article 93 is the Lok Sabha Speaker.
xa: The Chairman (VP) is **not** a member of the Rajya Sabha.
The **Lok Sabha** elects the **Speaker and Deputy Speaker**; the **Rajya Sabha** only the **Deputy Chairman**.
Removal notice for the Deputy Chairman: **fourteen days** — **Article 90(c)**.

nindian-polity-36-32.s: Who among the following can vote in Rajya Sabha elections?
nindian-polity-36-32.x: Rajya Sabha elections are indirect, by elected MLAs; nominated MLAs and MLCs cannot vote.
n: Elected Members of the Legislative Assemblies of the respective States elect Rajya Sabha members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
The Rajya Sabha is elected indirectly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
Nominated Members of Legislative Assemblies cannot vote in Rajya Sabha elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
Members of Legislative Councils cannot vote in Rajya Sabha elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
xa: RS seats are allocated by **population** (**Fourth Schedule**) — **not** equally.
**Kuldip Nayar v. UoI (2006):** upheld **open ballot** and removal of the **domicile** requirement.
AP has **11** RS seats; Telangana **7**.

n890ab4fb617.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019?
o: It ended the reservation of Lok Sabha seats for SCs and STs.
The discontinuance took effect from 25 January 2020.
It discontinued the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha.
Before it, Article 331 enabled the President to nominate up to two Anglo-Indians.
n890ab4fb617.x: The 104th Amendment extended SC/ST reservation by ten years, till 2030; it ended only Anglo-Indian nomination.
xa: SC/ST reservation (**Article 330**) was initially for **10 years** and repeatedly extended.
LS maximum is now **550**; the older **552** included **2** nominated Anglo-Indians.
The Lok Sabha now has **no nominated members**.

n27efb90d04a.s: Which of the following is NOT a field listed in Article 80(3) for nomination to the Rajya Sabha?
n27efb90d04a.x: Article 80(3) lists literature, science, art and social service; sports is not among them.
xa: Notable: **Lata Mangeshkar** (art); **Sachin Tendulkar** (**2012**), **Mary Kom** (**2016**).
**No nominated member has so far been in the Council of Ministers**.

nindian-polity-13-19.s: Who was the first film actress nominated to the Rajya Sabha (1980)?
nindian-polity-13-19.x: Nargis Dutt, nominated in 1980, was the first film actress in the Rajya Sabha.
n: The first nominated woman member of the Rajya Sabha was Nargis Du in 1980. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 34-36]
Uttar Pradesh has the highest number of Rajya Sabha seats, with 31 seats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 34-36]
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha decides questions concerning anti-defection. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 34-36]
xa: Nominated fields: **literature, science, art and social service** — ⚠ sport is not listed.
Other nominees: **Lata Mangeshkar**, **Sachin Tendulkar** (**2012**), **Mary Kom** (**2016**).
Nominated members may **join a party within 6 months**, after which the **Tenth Schedule** applies.

n12e0a386324.s: The gap between two sessions of Parliament cannot exceed:
n12e0a386324.x: Two sessions cannot be more than six months apart; this keeps legislative business going and the government accountable, though it fixes no minimum sitting days.
xa: This was an **APPSC-GS 2025** question.
There is **no fixed calendar**; normally **three sessions**.

ne0e2c67844a.s: Rules of procedure and conduct of business in Parliament are dealt with under:
ne0e2c67844a.x: Article 118 empowers each House to make rules for regulating its procedure and conduct of business.
ne0e2c67844a.tq: Link the procedural subject directly to Article 118 and distinguish it from quorum and language provisions.
xs: Rules of procedure are under **Article 118** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Art. 100** = quorum; **Art. 120** = language.
xa: **Art. 86**: President's right to address / send messages.
**Art. 98**: separate secretariats for each House.

n31d9fdb7c27.s: Under Article 122, courts cannot inquire into parliamentary proceedings on the ground of:
n31d9fdb7c27.x: Article 122 bars courts from questioning parliamentary proceedings on the ground of alleged procedural irregularity.
xa: The House may also make its **own rules** and punish **breach of privilege**.
No arrest within the precincts without the **Presiding Officer's permission**.

nddcbf7dd112.s: The Andhra State Act of 1953 and the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act of 2014 were enacted under which Article of the Constitution?
nddcbf7dd112.x: Both the creation of Andhra State in 1953 and the reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh in 2014 were carried out under Article 3, which concerns the formation and alteration of States.
nddcbf7dd112.tq: Use the common constitutional provision rather than the different years of enactment.
xs: **Andhra State (1953)** and the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014** were both made under **Article 3** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Art. 3** covers forming new states and altering areas, boundaries, names; the bill needs the **President's recommendation**.
xa: The **2014** Act amended the **Fourth Schedule**: undivided AP's **18** RS seats = **AP 11 + Telangana 7**.
AP has **25 LS** and **11 RS** seats; Assembly **175**.

nindian-polity-2-12.s: Which Article of the Constitution defines a Money Bill?
nindian-polity-2-12.x: Article 110 defines a Money Bill; Article 109 lays down the special procedure for it. Article 108 is joint sitting, 111 assent to Bills and 117 Financial Bills.
nindian-polity-2-12.tq: Recall the Article that defines a Money Bill.
n: Article 108 concerns a joint sitting of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Articles 109 and 110 concern the special procedure for Money Bills. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 110 defines a Money Bill. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 111 concerns assent to Bills. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 117 concerns special provisions for Financial Bills. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
xs: **Article 110** defines a Money Bill — option **(2)**.
**Articles 109 and 110** lay down the **special procedure** for Money Bills.
**Article 108** is **joint sitting**, **111** **assent to Bills**, and **117** **Financial Bills**.
xa: The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill within **14 days**, else it is **deemed passed**.
The **Speaker** certifies what is a Money Bill.
The President can return a Bill only **once** — **except** a **Money Bill**.

nindian-polity-38-1.s: Under which Article does the President summon each House of Parliament, with the maximum gap between two sessions limited to six months?
nindian-polity-38-1.x: Under Article 85, the President summons each House, and no more than six months may pass between sessions. Article 123 is about ordinances.
n: The President summons each House of Parliament under Article 85. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
The maximum gap between two parliamentary sessions cannot exceed six months. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
xs: The President summons each House under **Article 85** — option **(2)**.
The maximum gap between two sessions is **six months**.
**Article 112** is the **Budget**, **Article 100** **quorum** and **Article 123** **Ordinances**.
xa: **Art. 85(1):** Houses need not be summoned together.
The six-month rule sets **no minimum number of sitting days**.
**No fixed calendar**; normally **three sessions** — **Budget, Monsoon, Winter**.

nindian-polity-78-6.s: Which of the following minimum age requirements is NOT correct?
o: Prime Minister or Chief Minister – 25 years
nindian-polity-78-6.x: The Governor's minimum age is 35 years, not 30 (Article 157). The President and Vice-President need 35, and a PM or CM from the lower House 25.
n: A Prime Minister must be at least 25 years old if the Prime Minister heads the lower chamber. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
A Chief Minister must be at least 25 years old if the Chief Minister heads the lower chamber. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
Twenty-five years is the minimum possible age for becoming Prime Minister or Chief Minister when heading the lower chamber. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
The President of India must be at least 35 years old. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
The Vice-President of India must be at least 35 years old. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
The Governor of a State must be at least 35 years old. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
Article 157 governs the minimum age for a State Governor. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
Thirty-five years is the highest entry age required in the Indian Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
xa: **35** is the **highest entry age** in the Constitution.
**30:** Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council members.
**21:** Panchayat and Municipality contestants.

nindian-polity-78-15.s: Which Article provides for elections on the basis of universal adult suffrage?
nindian-polity-78-15.x: Adult suffrage is under Article 326; Article 84(b) deals with Lok Sabha membership.
n: Universal adult suffrage provides voter eligibility from 18 years of age. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
Article 326 governs universal adult suffrage and voter eligibility. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
A Panchayat member or chairperson must be at least 21 years old. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
Article 243F(1)(a) governs the minimum age for Panchayat membership and chairpersonship. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
A Member of the Lok Sabha must be at least 25 years old. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
Article 84(b) governs the minimum age for Lok Sabha membership. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
The Governor of a State must be at least 35 years old. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
Article 157 governs the minimum age for a State Governor. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
xa: **173(b):** Vidhan Sabha (**25**) and Vidhan Parishad (**30**).

nindian-polity-78-29.s: Which Article lays down the minimum age qualification for the Governor of a State?
nindian-polity-78-29.x: Article 157 covers the Governor; 58(1)(b) the President, 66(3)(b) the Vice-President and 84(b) members of Parliament.
n: Article 84(b) governs the minimum age for Lok Sabha membership. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
Article 84(b) governs the minimum age for Rajya Sabha membership. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
Article 58(1)(b) governs the minimum age for the President of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
Article 66(3)(b) governs the minimum age for the Vice-President of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
Article 157 governs the minimum age for a State Governor. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
xa: **173(b):** Vidhan Sabha and Vidhan Parishad.
**35** is the highest entry age in the Constitution.

nindian-polity-78-34.s: The 61st Amendment, which lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years, came into effect in:
nindian-polity-78-34.x: The 61st Amendment (1988) lowered the voting age to 18, and it took effect in 1989.
n: The voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
The reduction of the voting age became effective in 1989. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
xa: ⚠ The amendment table lists the **61st Amendment** under **1987**.
**18** years = **universal adult suffrage**.
**21** remains the minimum for **Panchayat** and **Municipality** contestants.

nc6c4b59b7e6.s: The constitutional position of the Indian President in relation to Parliament is most closely comparable to
o: The Governor of a State in relation to its Legislative Assembly only
The President of France in relation to its Senate
The President of the United States in relation to Congress
The Crown-in-Parliament in the United Kingdom
nc6c4b59b7e6.x: The inclusion of the President as a component of Parliament resembles the Crown-in-Parliament principle in the United Kingdom. It differs from the United States, where the President is separate from Congress.
nc6c4b59b7e6.tq: Apply the comparative constitutional analogy and distinguish the UK model from the US model.
xs: The President's place in Parliament is like the **Crown-in-Parliament** in the **UK** — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ The **US President** is **separate from Congress** — the opposite model.
xa: **Art. 79:** Parliament = **President + RS + LS**.
**No bill becomes law without his assent**.
He **summons**, **prorogues** and **dissolves** (LS only).

ndf570beef46.s: In which case (2006) did the Supreme Court uphold the open ballot and the removal of the domicile requirement for Rajya Sabha elections?
o: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Sita Soren v. Union of India
Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India
Krishna Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar
ndf570beef46.x: Kuldip Nayar (2006) upheld both the removal of the domicile requirement and the open-ballot system.
xa: The domicile requirement was **removed in 2003**.
⚠ **Kuldip Nayar** = RS domicile case; **Kuldip Singh** = Delimitation Commission.
**Kihoto Hollohan (1992):** Tenth Schedule decisions are subject to **judicial review**.

nd9dd2e18411.s: Before taking his seat, a Member of Parliament makes the oath or affirmation before:
o: The President or a person appointed by him
The Election Commission or a person authorised by it
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha only
nd9dd2e18411.x: Per the original's explanation, the oath or affirmation (Third Schedule form) is made before the Election Commission or a person authorised by it.
xa: This applies to candidates for **both Houses**.
Minimum age: **25** (LS), **30** (RS).
No **minimum educational qualification**.
nd9dd2e18411.fixed: Art. 99: oath on taking seat is before the President or person appointed by him; EC-authorised oath is for candidature (Art. 84(a))

nfd049486ac5.s: Which one of the following is NOT a ground of disqualification under Article 102 of the Constitution?
o: Being declared of unsound mind by a competent court
Holding an office of profit under the Union or a State, subject to exemptions by law
nfd049486ac5.x: Article 102 includes office of profit, unsoundness of mind declared by a court, undischarged insolvency, loss or absence of Indian citizenship and disqualification under a parliamentary law. Lack of a university degree is not a ground of disqualification.
nfd049486ac5.tq: Identify the option that is outside the constitutional list of disqualifications.
xs: **Lacking a university degree** is not an Art. 102 ground — there is **no minimum educational qualification** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Art. 102 grounds include **office of profit**, **unsound mind** declared by a court, **undischarged insolvent**.
xa: Other grounds: **not a citizen**, disqualified by a law of Parliament (**RPA 1951**), **defection**.
**Art. 103:** the **President** decides, on the **EC's opinion**.
Parliament can **exempt** offices of profit by law.

na60df275cf1.s: Parliament may exempt a particular office from the disqualification relating to office of profit by
o: A notification issued by the President alone
A direction of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
An order of the Election Commission
na60df275cf1.x: Parliament can exempt specified offices from the office-of-profit disqualification by enacting a law.
na60df275cf1.tq: Ask which authority has legislative power rather than merely administrative power.
xs: Parliament exempts offices from office-of-profit disqualification **by law** — so option **(3)** is correct.
No presidential notification, Speaker's direction or EC order can do it.
xa: Office of profit under the **Union/a state** is an **Art. 102** ground.
**Art. 103:** disqualification questions → **President**, on **EC's opinion**.
Defection questions → **Speaker / Chairman**.

n5e47bf3ffe6.s: Under Article 103, a question of disqualification of an MP (other than under the Tenth Schedule) is decided by the:
o: Election Commission, after consulting the President
Supreme Court, on a reference by the President
Speaker or Chairman of the House concerned
President, acting on the opinion of the Election Commission
n5e47bf3ffe6.x: Under Article 103, the President decides the question after obtaining the opinion of the Election Commission and acts according to that opinion.
xa: **Art. 102** grounds: office of profit, unsound mind, insolvency, non-citizenship, RPA **1951**.
Tenth Schedule decisions are subject to **judicial review** (**Kihoto Hollohan, 1992**).
Parliament can **exempt** offices of profit by law.

n1efc963a45c.s: A vote against the party whip does not attract disqualification if the party condones it within:
n1efc963a45c.x: A vote or abstention contrary to the party whip attracts disqualification unless permitted or condoned by the party within 15 days.
xa: Other grounds: **voluntarily giving up** party membership; **independent joining a party**.
A **nominated member** joining a party after **6 months** is disqualified.
Decided by the **Speaker / Chairman**.

nf7d7d0b257d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about vacation of seats under Article 101?
o: If a sitting member of one House is elected to the other, his seat in the first House falls vacant.
If a person elected to both Houses does not choose within 10 days, his Lok Sabha seat falls vacant.
If a person elected to two seats in the same House does not choose one, both seats fall vacant.
A House may declare a seat vacant if a member is absent without permission for 60 days.
nf7d7d0b257d.x: In that case it is the Rajya Sabha seat that falls vacant, not the Lok Sabha seat.
xa: Parliament + state legislature: resign the state seat within **14 days**, else the **Parliament** seat goes.
Absence for **60 days** without permission → House may declare the seat vacant.
⚠ **10 days** = both Houses; **14 days** = Parliament + state; **60 days** = absence.

n92c902a422f.s: A person elected to both Parliament and a State Legislature must resign the State seat within ____ days, failing which the Parliament seat falls vacant.
n92c902a422f.x: Under the Prohibition of Simultaneous Membership Rules, 1950, the State seat must be resigned within 14 days, otherwise the seat in Parliament becomes vacant.
xa: ⚠ **10 days** applies to election to **both Houses** of Parliament.
The **33rd Amendment (1974)** lets a resignation be rejected if **not voluntary or genuine**.

n86b37f42add.s: Who orders an adjournment sine die of a House of Parliament?
o: The Speaker or Chairman of the concerned House
The Prime Minister after consulting the Cabinet
The President in respect of both Houses
n86b37f42add.x: An adjournment sine die is ordered by the Speaker in the Lok Sabha or the Chairman in the Rajya Sabha, without fixing a date for the next sitting.
n86b37f42add.tq: Use the office-and-function matching method for parliamentary terminology.
xs: **Adjournment sine die** is ordered by the **Speaker or Chairman** of the House — so option **(1)** is correct.
It ends the sitting **without fixing a date** for the next; then the **President prorogues**.
xa: **Prorogation** (by the President) ends the **session**.
**Dissolution** ends the life of the **Lok Sabha** only.

nd9d37bbc083.s: The Rajya Sabha Secretariat functions under the control of the:
nd9d37bbc083.x: The parliamentary Secretariats are independent of the executive: the Rajya Sabha Secretariat is under the Chairman and the Lok Sabha Secretariat under the Speaker.
xa: **Art. 98** provides separate secretarial staff for each House.
The **VP** is ex officio Chairman of the RS.

nindian-polity-44-1.s: For calculating the continuous absence of a Member of Parliament under Article 101(4), which period is excluded from the 60-day limit?
o: The period between two sessions of Parliament
Adjournments exceeding four consecutive days and periods of prorogation
Only adjournments of two consecutive days
nindian-polity-44-1.x: Under Article 101(4), the 60 days of absence leave out prorogation and adjournments of more than four consecutive days.
nindian-polity-44-1.tq: Recall what is excluded from the 60-day count.
n: Adjournments exceeding four consecutive days are excluded when calculating the sixty-day limit for continuous absence of a Member of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
Periods of prorogation are excluded when calculating the sixty-day limit for continuous absence of a Member of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
Article 101(4) governs the calculation of continuous absence of a Member of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
xs: Excluded are **adjournments exceeding four consecutive days** and periods of **prorogation** — option **(3)**.
**Article 101(4):** an MP's seat may be declared vacant if **absent** from all meetings for **sixty days** **without permission**.
xa: **Member of both Houses:** must choose within **10 days**, else the **RS seat** falls vacant.
**Parliament + State Legislature:** resign the State seat within **14 days**, else the **Parliament** seat goes.
⚠ **10 days** = both Houses; **14 days** = Parliament + state; **60 days** = absence.

n2ad6f4445f3.s: The allocation of seats in the Lok Sabha to the States remains frozen on the basis of the 1971 Census until
o: the completion of the 2031 Census only
n2ad6f4445f3.x: The 84th Amendment Act, 2001 froze the allocation of Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 Census until the first Census after 2026.
n2ad6f4445f3.tq: Read the endpoint of a constitutional freeze precisely.
xs: The **84th Amendment (2001)** froze LS seat allocation on the **1971 census** till the first census **after 2026** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **87th Amendment** readjusted constituencies on the **2001** census, without changing the allocation.
xa: Debate: raising LS strength by **50% (to ~815)** once the freeze lifts.
The **131st Amendment Bill, 2026** sought an LS max of **850**; it was defeated (**298 for, 230 against**).
Tamil Nadu resolved to freeze the LS at **543**.

n221eef07c90.s: The readjustment of Lok Sabha constituencies on the basis of the 2001 Census was done by the Delimitation Commission headed by:
n221eef07c90.x: The 87th Amendment enabled readjustment on the 2001 Census; the work was done by the Delimitation Commission under Justice Kuldip Singh.
xa: ⚠ **Kuldip Singh** = Delimitation Commission; **Kuldip Nayar** = RS domicile case.
Largest LS constituency by electors: **Malkajgiri** (Telangana).
Largest by area: **Ladakh**.

nindian-polity-39-9.s: Which is the second-largest Lok Sabha constituency by geographical area?
nindian-polity-39-9.x: Ladakh is the largest, Barmer the second-largest and Kachchh the third; Chandni Chowk is the smallest.
n: Ladakh is the largest Lok Sabha constituency by geographical area. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
The area of the Ladakh Lok Sabha constituency is 173,266 square kilometres. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
Barmer is the second-largest Lok Sabha constituency by geographical area. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
The area of the Barmer Lok Sabha constituency is 55,074 square kilometres. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
Kachchh is the third-largest Lok Sabha constituency by geographical area. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
The area of the Kachchh Lok Sabha constituency is 41,414 square kilometres. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
Chandni Chowk in Delhi is the smallest Lok Sabha constituency by geographical area. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
xa: Fourth- and fifth-largest: **Arunachal East** and **Arunachal West**.
Largest by electors: **Malkajgiri** (Telangana); smallest: **Lakshadweep**.
⚠ **Kuldip Singh** = Delimitation Commission; **Kuldip Nayar** = RS domicile case.

nd2d2ae5c306.s: Which Lok Sabha was extended during the National Emergency of 1975–1977?
nd2d2ae5c306.x: The Fifth Lok Sabha, constituted for the period 1971–1977, was extended during the 1975–1977 Emergency.
nd2d2ae5c306.tq: Discriminate between closely numbered Lok Sabhas and their distinct events.
xs: The **5th Lok Sabha** (**1971-77**) was extended during the **1975-77** Emergency — so option **(4) Fifth Lok Sabha** is correct.

xa: Extension is **by law**, **1 year at a time**, not beyond **6 months** after the emergency.
**6th LS (1977)** had the **lowest share** of women MPs.
**18 Lok Sabhas** constituted so far.

n3cd546322b9.s: In which Lok Sabha did women members cross 10 per cent of the total membership for the first time?
n3cd546322b9.x: Women members crossed 10 per cent of the total strength of the House for the first time in the 15th Lok Sabha, elected in 2009.
n3cd546322b9.tq: Link the threshold event with the correct Lok Sabha number and election period.
xs: Women crossed **10%** for the first time in the **15th Lok Sabha** (**2009**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
xa: This was an **APPSC-G2 2023** key.
⚠ FIRST above 10% = **15th**; highest = **17th** (**78**); lowest share = **6th** (**1977**).

nb2379103d1e.s: In which year was the first Women's Reservation Bill introduced?
nb2379103d1e.x: The first Bill came in 1996 and was passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010; the 106th Amendment was enacted in 2023.
xa: It reserves **33%** (one-third) of seats in the Lok Sabha and state Assemblies (**Art. 334A**).
The reservation lasts **15 years**, extendable.
It is called the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam**.

nindian-polity-12-11.s: Reservation of Lok Sabha seats for SCs and STs was initially provided for:
nindian-polity-12-11.x: Seats are reserved for SCs and STs in proportion to their population; the reservation was first given for ten years.
n: Seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes in the Lok Sabha in proportion to their population. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 32-34]
Seats are reserved for Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha in proportion to their population. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 32-34]
Reservation of Lok Sabha seats was initially provided for 10 years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 32-34]
xa: The **104th** Amendment extended it until **2030**.
The same Amendment ended **Anglo-Indian** nomination from **25 Jan 2020**.
**87th Amendment:** constituencies readjusted on the **2001** census.

nindian-polity-76-19.s: The lowest representation of women, only 19 MPs, was recorded in which Lok Sabha?
nindian-polity-76-19.x: The 6th Lok Sabha (1977) had the fewest women members, only 19 MPs.
n: The 6th Lok Sabha had the lowest representation of women among the stated electoral milestones. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
The 6th Lok Sabha was elected in 1977. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
The 6th Lok Sabha had 19 women Members of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
xa: **15th** LS (**2009**): **59** women — first time above **10%**.

nd955df17d0e.s: Parliament in India normally holds which three sessions in a year?
nd955df17d0e.x: There is no fixed constitutional calendar, but Parliament normally has Budget, Monsoon and Winter sessions.
xa: **Art. 85** sets **no minimum number of sitting days**.
Monsoon Session **2026** ran from **20 July** and was adjourned sine die on **13 Aug**.

n7af571a485c.s: A Member of Parliament enjoys freedom from arrest in civil cases during the session and:
n7af571a485c.x: The privilege covers civil arrest during the session and forty days before and after it; it does not cover criminal cases or preventive detention.
xa: Members are also exempt from **jury service**.
Privileges are **co-terminous with membership**.

nindian-polity-2-44.s: Which Article deals with Appropriation Bills?
nindian-polity-2-44.x: Article 114 covers Appropriation Bills; 100 is voting and quorum, 105 privileges and 113 the procedure for estimates.
n: Article 100 concerns voting and quorum in Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 105 concerns the powers and privileges of the Houses of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 113 concerns the procedure for estimates. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 114 concerns Appropriation Bills. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
xa: Quorum under **Article 100** is **one-tenth** of the total membership.
**Article 112:** **Annual Financial Statement (Budget)**.
**Article 123:** President's power to promulgate **Ordinances**.

nindian-polity-8-12.s: Under Article 123, the President can promulgate an Ordinance when:
o: A National Emergency is in operation
The Rajya Sabha rejects a Bill
nindian-polity-8-12.x: The President issues Ordinances under Article 123 only when Parliament (either House) is not in session.
n: The President promulgates Ordinances when Parliament is not in session under Article 123. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-25]
The President’s Ordinance-making power is co-extensive with the legislative power of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-25]
xa: **Prorogation** ends a **session**, not the House; **dissolution** applies **only to the Lok Sabha**.
The President **summons** each House under **Article 85**.
Maximum gap between two sessions: **six months**.

nindian-polity-38-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: A sitting is a daily meeting of the House during a session.
Prorogation terminates the House itself but not its session.
Dissolution ends the life of the House and applies only to the Lok Sabha.
Adjournment terminates a sitting for a specified period.
nindian-polity-38-2.x: Prorogation ends the session, not the House; only dissolution ends the House, and only the Lok Sabha can be dissolved.
n: A sitting is a daily meeting of a House during a session. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
Adjournment terminates a daily sitting for a specified time. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
Prorogation terminates a session of the House. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
Prorogation does not terminate the House itself. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
Dissolution ends the life of the House entirely. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
Dissolution applies only to the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]

The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
Prorogation terminates a session and may be effected by the President or Governor. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
Dissolution terminates a House and may be effected by the President or Governor. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
xa: **Adjournment sine die** ends a sitting **without fixing a date** for reassembly.
Adjournment is by the **Presiding Officer**; prorogation by the **President**.
The **Rajya Sabha** is permanent and cannot be dissolved.

nindian-polity-38-26.s: Termination of a session of a House, without ending the life of the House, is called:
nindian-polity-38-26.x: Prorogation ends the session; adjournment ends a sitting for a set time, adjournment sine die ends it without a date, and dissolution ends the House.
n: Adjournment terminates a daily sitting for a specified time. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
Adjournment sine die terminates a sitting without assigning a day for reassembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
Prorogation terminates a session of the House. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
Dissolution ends the life of the House entirely. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
The specified period of an adjournment may be hours, days, or weeks. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
Prorogation terminates a session and may be effected by the President or Governor. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
Dissolution terminates a House and may be effected by the President or Governor. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
xa: Prorogation usually follows **adjournment sine die**.
**Recess:** period between **prorogation** and a new session.
Adjournment may be for **hours, days or weeks**.

nindian-polity-38-50.s: The quorum for conducting official business in a House of Parliament is what fraction of its total membership?
nindian-polity-38-50.x: Under Article 100, the quorum is one-tenth of the House's total membership.
n: Quorum is the minimum number of members required to conduct official business. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
The quorum under Article 100 is one-tenth of the total membership of the House. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 97-101]
xs: The quorum is **one-tenth** of the total membership — option **(1)**.
**Article 100** deals with **voting and quorum**; the same fraction applies to the **Rajya Sabha**.
xa: **Art. 98:** separate secretarial staff for each House.
**Art. 118:** rules of procedure; **Art. 120:** language — **Hindi or English**.
Lok Sabha Secretariat is under the **Speaker**; Rajya Sabha Secretariat under the **Chairman**.

n9c99cd94be5.s: The provision that the Speaker or Chairman may refuse to accept a member's resignation if satisfied that it is not voluntary or genuine was introduced by the
n9c99cd94be5.x: The 33rd Amendment Act, 1974 amended Article 101(3)(b) so that a resignation takes effect only on acceptance, and the presiding officer may reject it if it is not voluntary or genuine. The 24th Amendment concerned Parliament's amending power, the 42nd was the 'mini-Constitution' of the Emergency, and the 52nd added the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection).
n9c99cd94be5.tq: 33rd Amendment (1974) = resignation must be voluntary and genuine; 52nd (1985) = anti-defection.
xs: The **33rd Amendment Act, 1974** streamlined acceptance of resignation — it **may be rejected if not voluntary or genuine** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Resignation is **subject to acceptance** under **Art 101(3)(b)**, unlike judges or the President.
xa: **61st Amendment (1987)**: voting age **18 years**.
**84th Amendment (2001)**: froze LS seat allocation on the **1971 census**.

n2c162a2782c.s: A Financial Bill of category I:
o: Can be introduced in either House of Parliament
Can be introduced only in the Rajya Sabha
Can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and both Houses have equal powers in its passage
Can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha must return it within 14 days
n2c162a2782c.x: A Financial Bill of category I can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, but unlike a Money Bill both Houses have equal powers in its passage.
xa: A Money Bill must be returned by the RS within **14 days**.
The President may return **Financial Bills (I) and (II)** for reconsideration.

nad676950432.s: If the two Houses of Parliament disagree on a constitutional amendment bill, which one of the following is the consequence?
o: The bill fails because no joint sitting is permitted for such a bill.
The Lok Sabha may pass the bill by a simple majority in a second sitting.
The Supreme Court decides which version of the bill shall prevail.
The President convenes a joint sitting under Article 108.
nad676950432.x: There is no provision for a joint sitting in respect of a constitutional amendment bill. Failure to secure the required approval in either House causes the bill to fall.
nad676950432.tq: Ask whether the ordinary deadlock mechanism applies; Article 108 does not apply here.
xs: For a **constitutional amendment bill** there is **no joint sitting**, so the bill fails — option **(1)**.
It needs a **special majority in each House**.
xa: ⚠ A **joint sitting** is presided by the **Speaker**; LS numbers prevail.
Amendments are made under **Art. 368**.

nindian-polity-13-14.s: The powers of the Rajya Sabha are restricted in the case of:
nindian-polity-13-14.x: The Rajya Sabha has equal powers on Constitutional Amendment Bills and can introduce Ordinary and Amendment Bills; it is restricted only for Money Bills.
n: The Rajya Sabha has equal powers with the Lok Sabha in Constitutional Amendment Bills. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 34-36]
The Rajya Sabha can introduce Ordinary Bills. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 34-36]
The Rajya Sabha can introduce Constitutional Amendment Bills. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 34-36]
xa: **Article 249:** authorises Parliament to legislate on a **State List** subject — **two-thirds** present and voting.
**Article 312:** initiates new **All-India Services**.
**Art. 67(b):** removal of the **Vice-President** can be moved **only in the Rajya Sabha**.

nindian-polity-44-4.s: Which Article deals with the procedure for impeachment of the President?
nindian-polity-44-4.x: Impeachment is under Article 61; Article 109 covers the Rajya Sabha's 14 days on Money Bills and 90(c) the Deputy Chairman's removal.
n: Fourteen days is the prior-notice period for the impeachment of the President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
Article 61 governs the prior notice for the President's impeachment. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
Fourteen days is the period for consideration of a Money Bill by the Rajya Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
Article 109 governs the Rajya Sabha's consideration of a Money Bill. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
Fourteen days is the period for resolving simultaneous membership of Parliament and a State Legislature. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 governs simultaneous membership resignation. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
Fourteen days is the notice period for removing the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
Article 90(c) governs the removal notice for the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
xa: All four carry a **fourteen-day** limit.
Simultaneous membership is also governed by the **Prohibition of Simultaneous Membership Rules, 1950**.

nd059d983a0d.s: How many Rajya Sabha seats does Andhra Pradesh have?
nd059d983a0d.x: Andhra Pradesh has 11 Rajya Sabha seats; Telangana has 7, Uttarakhand 3 and Tripura 1.
xa: APPSC **2023** asked AP's RS seats → **11**.
AP: **25** Lok Sabha seats, Assembly **175**.
Telangana: **17** LS, **119** Assembly.

n13fdea688b7.s: During a National Emergency, the term of the Lok Sabha can be extended by law for:
n13fdea688b7.x: The term can be extended one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ends.
xa: The **5th Lok Sabha** (**1971-77**) was extended during the **1975-77** Emergency.
Only the LS can resolve to **discontinue a National Emergency**.

n85bee2a9317.s: An existing law made by Parliament can be changed only by:
n85bee2a9317.x: Only Parliament can change an existing law it has made (APPSC-GS 2024); it legislates on the Union and Concurrent Lists and reviews delegated legislation.
xa: **Art. 249**: RS resolution lets Parliament legislate on a **State List** subject.
**Art. 253**: laws to implement **international treaties** on any subject.

n4a6d1144a8a.s: Which of the following is a judicial function of Parliament?
n4a6d1144a8a.x: Impeachment of the President, removal of the Vice-President, recommending removal of judges and punishing breach of privilege are Parliament's judicial functions.
xa: **Constituent** function: amends the Constitution under **Art. 368**, but cannot alter the **basic structure**.
**Electoral** function: elects the VP and presiding officers.

nabe239e1115.s: Parliamentary privileges in India, which remain uncodified, continue under:
nabe239e1115.x: Parliamentary privileges have not been comprehensively codified; they continue under Article 105(3), historically based on those of the British House of Commons.
xa: Codification is urged to protect **press freedom** and **citizens' rights**.
**Art. 122** bars courts from inquiring into proceedings; it codifies nothing.

n8fdaa1d2256.s: On which of the following matters do the two Houses of Parliament NOT have equal powers?
o: Passing a resolution to discontinue a National Emergency
Approval of an Ordinance promulgated by the President
Removal of a Judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court
n8fdaa1d2256.x: Only the Lok Sabha can pass a resolution to discontinue a National Emergency; the Houses are equal on the other three.
xa: **No-confidence motion** — only in the LS.
Also equal: **constitutional amendment bills** — special majority in each House, no joint sitting.

n0cddc1733a9.s: If the Rajya Sabha approves a National Emergency while the Lok Sabha is dissolved, the new Lok Sabha must approve it within ____ of its first sitting.
n0cddc1733a9.x: The Rajya Sabha may approve the proclamation for the time being; the newly constituted Lok Sabha must approve it within thirty days of its first sitting.
xa: This covers Emergencies under **Arts. 352, 356, 360**.
RS special powers: **Art. 249**, **Art. 312**, **Art. 67(b)**.

n43599e6a690.s: A Bill under Article 3 to form a new State can be introduced in Parliament only on the recommendation of the:
n43599e6a690.x: Such a Bill needs the President's recommendation; the State Legislature's views are sought but are not binding on Parliament.
xa: **Andhra State (1953)** and the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014** were both made under **Art. 3**.
**Art. 253**: law to implement **international treaties** on any subject.

n21ab69350f2.s: Under which Article can the Rajya Sabha authorise the creation of new All-India Services?
n21ab69350f2.x: Article 312 covers new All-India Services; 249 deals with State List legislation in the national interest and 67(b) with initiating the Vice-President's removal.
xa: ⚠ **APPSC-G1 2017** trap: RS does **not** "authorise State Assemblies" to legislate.
Returning a **money bill with recommendations** is also an RS power.

nac312301d57.s: A Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249 must be supported by:
o: a simple majority of members present and voting
two-thirds of members present and voting
a majority of the total membership
nac312301d57.x: It needs two-thirds of members present and voting, is valid for one year and can be renewed one year at a time.
xa: **Art. 250**: State List law during a **National Emergency**.
**Art. 356-357**: during President's Rule, Parliament legislates for the state.

n3355272df24.s: The Law Commission's 170th Report, submitted in 1999, proposed which of the following alternatives in the context of parliamentary representation?
o: A 50 per cent reduction in Rajya Sabha seats
A 25 per cent increase in seats through a party-list system
Direct election of the President by the people
Abolition of reserved seats in the Lok Sabha
n3355272df24.x: The Law Commission's 170th Report of 1999 proposed increasing representation by 25 per cent through a party-list system.
n3355272df24.tq: Link the institutional proposal with the report number and year.
xs: The Law Commission's **170th Report (1999)** proposed **25%** more seats via a **party list** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was an alternative in the LS expansion debate; it did not seek RS cuts, direct presidential elections or abolition of reserved seats.
xa: The current proposal: raise LS strength by **50% (to ~815)**.
The LS-RS ratio would go from **2.2:1 to 3.3:1**.

n9ccaa64610a.s: The resolution to remove Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, rejected by voice vote on 11 March 2026, was moved under:
n9ccaa64610a.x: The removal resolution against Speaker Om Birla was moved under Article 94(c) and rejected by voice vote on 11 March 2026.
xa: The **Speaker** presides over a **joint sitting** and certifies **Money Bills**.
The **Lok Sabha** elects the **Speaker and Deputy Speaker**.

n667c0a6688c.s: Which one of the following is NOT an individual parliamentary privilege of a member?
o: Freedom from arrest in civil cases during the prescribed period
Freedom of speech in the House
Power to prohibit publication of the House's proceedings
n667c0a6688c.x: The power to publish or prohibit publication of the House's reports and proceedings is a collective privilege of the House, not an individual privilege.
n667c0a6688c.tq: Find the option that belongs to the opposite classification.
xs: **Power to prohibit publication of the House's proceedings** is a **collective** privilege, not individual — so option **(4)** is correct.
Individual privileges: **freedom of speech**, freedom from arrest in **civil** cases, exemption from **jury service**.
xa: Other collective privileges: **exclude strangers**, hold **secret sittings**, punish for **contempt**.
⚠ "Only individual privileges exist" is **wrong** (**APPSC-G2 2017**).

nfdf120a4d24.s: Which one of the following matters is within the equal powers of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha?
o: Initiation of a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers
Consideration of the report of the Comptroller and Auditor-General
nfdf120a4d24.x: Both Houses have equal powers in considering the reports of the CAG, UPSC and Finance Commission. The other matters are associated with the superiority of the Lok Sabha.
nfdf120a4d24.tq: Distinguish an equal parliamentary function from a power exclusively associated with the Lok Sabha.
xs: **Consideration of the CAG's report** is an equal power of both Houses — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Demands for grants** — RS cannot vote; **no-confidence motion** — LS only; **Money Bill certification** — the **Speaker**.
xa: **APPSC G1 2024**: equal status = **CAG's report** + approval of Emergency.
Also equal: **UPSC** and **Finance Commission** reports.

n2c7ac6c7acf.s: Articles 79 to 122 of the Constitution occur in
n2c7ac6c7acf.x: Parliamentary provisions in Articles 79 to 122 are contained in Part V of the Constitution.
n2c7ac6c7acf.tq: Link the article range with the correct constitutional Part.
xs: **Arts. 79-122** on Parliament are in **Part V** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Art. 79** opens it: Parliament = **President + RS + LS**.
xa: **Art. 86:** President may address either House or both.
**Art. 87:** special address at the **first session after each general election** and the **first session of each year**.
Procedural Articles in this Part: **Art. 98** (secretariats), **Art. 100** (quorum), **Art. 118** (rules), **Art. 120** (language).

n8fc688297c4.s: A resolution to remove the Speaker of the Lok Sabha requires advance notice of at least:
n8fc688297c4.x: Under Article 94 removal needs a majority of all the then members after 14 days' notice; the Speaker resigns to the Deputy Speaker.
xa: ⚠ Speaker → resigns to Deputy Speaker; Deputy Speaker → to Speaker; Deputy Chairman → to Chairman.
Removal motions against **Mavalankar (1954)**, **Hukum Singh (1966)**, **Jakhar (1987)** all **failed**.

n6a1385ec964.s: The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha addresses his resignation to the:
n6a1385ec964.x: The Deputy Chairman resigns to the Chairman and can be removed by an effective majority after 14 days' notice.
xa: **Harivansh**'s term as Deputy Chairman ended **9 Apr 2026**.
When the VP acts as President, the **Deputy Chairman** presides (**Art 91**).

nca3fe95b268.s: When the Vice-President acts as President, the duties of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha are performed by the:
o: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
senior-most member of the Rajya Sabha
Leader of the House in the Rajya Sabha
nca3fe95b268.x: The Deputy Chairman performs the Chairman's duties when the Vice-President acts as President.
xa: ⚠ The **Speaker** in that situation **can vote** in the first instance.
The Chairman is removed **only when removed as VP**.

n7bbd329f7bd.s: In which Lok Sabha did the office of Deputy Speaker remain vacant throughout?
n7bbd329f7bd.x: The Deputy Speaker's post remained vacant through the 17th Lok Sabha, and also through the 18th.
xa: It has been **vacant since June 2019**.
State office (**Art 178**) vacant in **8 State Assemblies**.

nindian-polity-57-11.s: Under which Article is the Speaker removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Lok Sabha?
nindian-polity-57-11.x: Article 94(c) requires an effective majority, after 14 days' notice; a simple majority is not enough.
n: The Speaker is removed only by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Lok Sabha under Article 94(c). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
The majority required to remove the Speaker is an effective majority. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
At least 14 days’ advance written notice is required before moving the Speaker’s removal resolution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
xa: Removal motions against **Mavalankar (1954)**, **Hukum Singh (1966)** and **Balram Jakhar (1987)** all failed.
A motion against **Om Birla** was signed by **118** Opposition MPs (**9 Mar 2026**).
The Speaker resigns in writing to the **Deputy Speaker** — **Article 94(b)**.

nindian-polity-56-7.s: Removal of which of the following requires NO advance notice?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
nindian-polity-56-7.x: The President removes a Governor at pleasure without notice; the other three removals need 14 days' notice.
n: The President removes a Governor at pleasure under Article 156. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 150-153]
The removal of the President requires at least 14 days’ advance written notice. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 150-153]
The removal of the Lok Sabha Speaker requires at least 14 days’ advance written notice. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 150-153]
The removal of the Lok Sabha Deputy Speaker requires at least 14 days’ advance written notice. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 150-153]
The removal of the Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman requires at least 14 days’ advance written notice. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 150-153]
The Governor of a State is removed without impeachment. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 150-153]
The removal of the Lok Sabha Speaker requires 14 days’ notice. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 150-153]
The removal of the Lok Sabha Deputy Speaker requires 14 days’ notice. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 150-153]
The removal of the Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman requires 14 days’ notice. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 150-153]
xa: Speaker and Deputy Speaker: removed by an **effective majority** — **Article 94**.
Deputy Chairman: **RS resolution** by an **effective majority** — **Article 90**.
The RS **Chairman** is removed only when removed as **Vice-President**.

nindian-polity-56-36.s: On assuming office, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha takes:
o: only the oath as a Member of Parliament
a separate oath administered by the President
a separate oath administered by the Chief Justice of India
a separate oath administered by the Pro-Tem Speaker
nindian-polity-56-36.x: The Speaker and Deputy Speaker take only the oath as MPs; there is no separate oath as presiding officer.
n: The Speaker and Deputy Speaker take oath only as ordinary Members of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 150-153]
The Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha is removed by a Lok Sabha resolution passed by an effective majority. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #56 · pp 150-153]
xa: The RS **Deputy Chairman** also takes oath only as an ordinary MP.
Removal needs **14 days'** notice.
The Deputy Chairman resigns to the **Chairman** of the Rajya Sabha.

nb35faef9aef.s: The salary and allowances of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha are charged on the:
nb35faef9aef.x: The salaries and allowances of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 97.
nb35faef9aef.tq: Use the constitutional funding source rather than a general parliamentary budget description.
xs: The Speaker's salary is **charged on the Consolidated Fund** of India (**Art 97**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
Being charged, it is not voted upon — the Public Account and Contingency Fund are wrong.
xa: On **dissolution**, the Speaker continues till immediately before the **first meeting of the new LS**.
The **Speaker Pro Tem** is the senior-most member, sworn in by the **President**.

n4b133cccd9f.s: Who is usually appointed Speaker Pro Tem of a newly elected Lok Sabha?
o: The senior-most member of the House
n4b133cccd9f.x: The Speaker Pro Tem is the senior-most member, sworn in by the President; the outgoing Speaker only stays in office until just before the new House first meets.
xa: The Pro Tem Speaker **presides and conducts the new Speaker's election**.
The Speaker's salary is charged on the **Consolidated Fund** (**Art 97**).

nindian-polity-57-34.s: Who administers the oath to newly elected members of the Lok Sabha?
nindian-polity-57-34.x: The Pro-Tem Speaker swears in the new MPs and conducts the election of the regular Speaker.
n: The regular Speaker administers the oath to newly elected Members of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
The Pro-Tem Speaker enables the election of the regular Speaker. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
xa: Presiding officers take **no separate oath** — only the oath as **ordinary MPs**.
The President fixes the **date** of the Speaker's election.

nindian-polity-58-6.s: The date of election of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is fixed by the:
nindian-polity-58-6.x: The President fixes the Speaker's election date and the Speaker fixes the Deputy Speaker's.
n: The date of election of the Deputy Speaker is fixed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha under Rule 8(1). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 156-158]
The President fixes the date of election of the Speaker. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 156-158]
The Deputy Speaker addresses resignation to the Speaker under Article 94(b). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 156-158]
The Speaker addresses resignation to the Deputy Speaker under Article 94(b). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 156-158]
xa: The **Secretary-General** communicates the Deputy Speaker's election date.
⚠ Neither resigns to the **President**.
RS **Deputy Chairman** resigns to the **Chairman**.

nindian-polity-57-7.s: In normal sittings of the Lok Sabha, the Speaker:
o: does not vote in the first instance but has a casting vote in a tie
votes in the first instance and also has a casting vote
votes in the first instance like any member
nindian-polity-57-7.x: Under Article 100 the Speaker does not vote in the first instance but gives a casting vote when votes are tied.
n: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is covered by Article 100. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
During normal parliamentary sittings, the Speaker does not vote in the first instance. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
During normal parliamentary sittings, the Speaker exercises a casting vote under Article 100 upon an equality of votes. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
xa: During his **own removal resolution** (**Article 96**) he cannot preside, but **can vote** in the first instance — **no casting vote**.
⚠ Removal pending: Speaker **can vote**; the RS **Chairman cannot vote**.

nindian-polity-58-13.s: When not in the Chair, the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
o: can only give a casting vote
can debate, move motions and vote in the first instance
nindian-polity-58-13.x: Out of the Chair the Deputy Speaker is an ordinary member who can debate, move motions and vote in the first instance, unlike the Speaker.
n: The Deputy Speaker sits as an ordinary member of the House during normal proceedings when not in the Chair. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 156-158]
The Deputy Speaker can participate in debates during normal proceedings. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 156-158]
The Deputy Speaker can move motions during normal proceedings. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 156-158]
The Deputy Speaker can vote in the first instance during normal proceedings. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 156-158]
xa: In his **own removal** resolution (**Article 96**) he **cannot preside** and has **no casting vote**.
The **Speaker** does **not** vote in the first instance in normal sittings.
The Deputy Speaker presides when the Speaker is **absent** or the office is **vacant**.

n36eafca7d20.s: Which Article provides for the election of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
n36eafca7d20.x: Article 93 provides that the House of the People shall choose two members to be Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
n36eafca7d20.tq: Match the constitutional article with the office it creates.
xs: **Article 93**: the LS elects the **Speaker and Deputy Speaker** from its members — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Art. 89** is about the RS **Chairman and Deputy Chairman**; **Art. 100** = quorum / casting vote; **Art. 85** = sessions.
xa: **Art. 94**: Speaker resigns to the **Deputy Speaker**; removal by a **majority of all the then members** after **14 days'** notice.
The **Deputy Speaker** is elected **after the Speaker**.

n86bba541116.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the powers of the Speaker?
o: The Speaker recognises the Leader of the Opposition, subject to the party-strength requirement.
The Speaker's decisions under the Tenth Schedule are beyond judicial review.
The Speaker appoints chairmen of parliamentary committees.
Rulings of the Speaker are protected by Article 122.
n86bba541116.x: The Speaker decides Tenth Schedule cases, but those decisions remain subject to judicial review.
xa: LoP recognition needs at least **one-tenth** of the House's strength.
The LoP became statutory under the **1977 Act**.

n237145bf6fe.s: The party seeking recognition of the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is required, according to the Speaker’s direction, to have at least:
n237145bf6fe.x: Recognition of the Leader of the Opposition requires the party to have at least one-tenth of the strength of the House, according to the Speaker’s direction. The office has statutory status since the 1977 Act.
n237145bf6fe.tq: Distinguish the one-tenth threshold from other parliamentary fractions.
xs: The party needs at least **one-tenth of the House's strength** — so option **(1)** is correct.
This comes from the **Speaker's direction**; the LoP is **statutory since the 1977 Act**.
xa: Quorum is also **one-tenth** of total members (**Art 100(3)**).
The Speaker also decides **Tenth Schedule** cases.

nb4c56bdbfb2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
o: The Deputy Speaker is elected after the election of the Speaker.
The Deputy Speaker resigns by writing to the Speaker.
The Deputy Speaker is subordinate to the Speaker in exercising the office's functions.
The Deputy Speaker presides over a joint sitting when the Speaker is absent.
nb4c56bdbfb2.x: The Deputy Speaker is not subordinate to the Speaker while exercising the functions of the office.
xa: By convention he is from the **Opposition**.
He becomes **chairman of any committee** he is appointed to.

ne622f8dcf0f.s: Under which Article may the President send messages to either House of Parliament regarding a pending Bill?
ne622f8dcf0f.x: Article 86 lets the President address either or both Houses, require members' attendance and send messages on pending Bills.
xa: **Art 87**: **special address** at the **first session after each general election** and the **first session of each year**.
The address is debated on a **Motion of Thanks**.

nindian-polity-58-12.s: A ruling given by the Deputy Speaker while in the Chair:
o: can be appealed to the Speaker
must be ratified by the Speaker
cannot be appealed to the Speaker
can be appealed to the President
nindian-polity-58-12.x: While presiding, the Deputy Speaker has the Speaker's powers, and his rulings cannot be appealed to the Speaker.
n: The Deputy Speaker exercises the same powers as the Speaker when presiding over a sitting of the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 156-158]
There is no appeal to the Speaker against a ruling given by the Deputy Speaker while the Deputy Speaker is in the Chair. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 156-158]
The Deputy Speaker presides over joint sittings of Parliament when the Speaker is absent under Article 118(4). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 156-158]
The Deputy Speaker automatically becomes the chairman of any Parliamentary Committee to which the Deputy Speaker is appointed. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 156-158]
xa: After him, the **Deputy Chairman** of the Rajya Sabha presides at a joint sitting.
The Speaker's **Panel of Chairpersons** has up to **10** members.
RS equivalent: **Panel of Vice-Chairpersons** nominated by the **Chairman**.

nindian-polity-57-13.s: If both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are absent from a joint sitting of Parliament, it is presided over by the:
o: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
senior-most member of the Lok Sabha
nindian-polity-57-13.x: The Speaker presides over a joint sitting (Art. 118(4)), then the Deputy Speaker, then the Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman.
n: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is covered by Article 110. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is covered by Article 118. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
The Speaker is the sole and final authority to certify whether a Bill is a Money Bill under Article 110(4). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
The Speaker presides over joint sittings of both Houses of Parliament under Article 118(4). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
In the absence of the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker presides over a joint sitting before the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
xa: Joint sitting is provided in **Art 108**.
The Speaker's certificate is **final** when the Bill goes to the **Rajya Sabha** and the **President**.

nindian-polity-57-23.s: The constitutional provisions governing the Speaker of the Lok Sabha are contained in which one of the following groups of Articles?
nindian-polity-57-23.x: The Speaker is covered by Articles 93–96 (election, vacation, removal), 100 (casting vote), 110 (Money Bill certificate) and 118 (joint sitting rules).
n: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is governed under Part V of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is covered by Article 93. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is covered by Article 94. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is covered by Article 95. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is covered by Article 96. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is covered by Article 100. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is covered by Article 110. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is covered by Article 118. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
xs: The Speaker is governed by **Articles 93–96, 100, 110 and 118** — option **(3)**.
**Article 93:** election; **94:** resignation and removal; **96:** own removal resolution.
**100:** casting vote; **110:** Money Bill certification; **118:** joint sitting.
xa: **Art 97:** salary charged on the **Consolidated Fund**.
**Art 122:** the Speaker's rulings are **protected**.
**Kihoto Hollohan (1992):** Tenth Schedule decisions subject to **judicial review**.

nindian-polity-57-37.s: Who appoints the Pro-Tem Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
nindian-polity-57-37.x: The President appoints the Pro-Tem Speaker; adjourning sine die, Tenth Schedule decisions and fixing the Deputy Speaker's election date are the Speaker's.
n: The Speaker exercises adjournment sine die. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
The Speaker decides questions of member disqualification arising out of defection under the Tenth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
The Speaker fixes the date for the election of the Deputy Speaker under Rule 8(1). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
The Pro-Tem Speaker is appointed by the President under Article 95(1). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
xa: The Speaker recognises the **Leader of the Opposition** — party needs **one-tenth** of the House.
He **appoints committee chairmen**.
He adjourns or suspends a sitting when there is **no quorum** (**one-tenth**).

na07b41aa122.s: In January 2026, the Supreme Court upheld the Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman's power under Article 91 to decide a judge-removal motion (Chairman's office vacant) in the:
na07b41aa122.x: In the Justice Varma case (January 2026), the Supreme Court upheld the Deputy Chairman's power under Article 91 to decide a judge-removal motion while the Chairman's office was vacant.
xa: **Harivansh**'s term as Deputy Chairman ended **9 Apr 2026**.
Under **Art 91** the Deputy Chairman also presides when the VP acts as President.

n906b367d1cf.s: As of 2026, who is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
n906b367d1cf.x: C.P. Radhakrishnan, as Vice-President, is the ex officio Chairman; Harivansh was Deputy Chairman (term ended 9 April 2026) and S. Radhakrishnan was the first Chairman (1952-62).
xa: The Chairman has a **casting vote only**.
RS has a **Panel of Vice-Chairpersons** nominated by the Chairman.

n19b0f1c46e2.s: Until Parliament makes a law regulating recruitment and conditions of service of the secretarial staff of the Houses, rules may be made by the President after consultation with the:
o: Chief Justice of India and Attorney-General of India
Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha and Secretary-General of the Rajya Sabha
Prime Minister and Union Home Minister
Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
n19b0f1c46e2.x: In the absence of a law by Parliament, the President may make rules after consulting the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
n19b0f1c46e2.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish the constitutional consultees from parliamentary officials and ministers.
xs: Until Parliament legislates, the **President** makes rules **after consulting the Speaker/Chairman** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Not the CJI, the Secretaries-General or the PM.
xa: **Art 98** provides each House a **separate secretarial staff**.
Each Secretariat is headed by a **Secretary-General**.

nindian-polity-57-5.s: The Lok Sabha Secretariat functions directly under the control and guidance of the:
o: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
nindian-polity-57-5.x: The Lok Sabha Secretariat works directly under the Speaker's control and guidance, not under the executive, which keeps the House independent.
nindian-polity-57-5.tq: Recall who controls each House's secretariat.
n: The Lok Sabha Secretariat functions directly under the control and guidance of the Speaker. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #57 · pp 153-156]
xs: The **Lok Sabha Secretariat** works under the **Speaker of the Lok Sabha** — option **(2)**.
It functions under the Speaker's **control and guidance**, **independent of the executive**.
The **Rajya Sabha Secretariat** is under the **Chairman**.
xa: **Art 98:** each House has a **separate secretarial staff**; posts **common to both Houses** may be created.
Head: the **Secretary-General**, appointed by the presiding officer.
Until Parliament legislates, recruitment rules are made by the **President** after consulting Speaker/Chairman.

n7fa8bd8a093.s: The period between prorogation of Parliament and the commencement of its next session is known as:
n7fa8bd8a093.x: The period from prorogation to the next session is called a recess. It is different from adjournment, which interrupts a sitting within a session.
n7fa8bd8a093.tq: Discriminate between a break within a session and the interval between two sessions.
xs: The period from **prorogation to the next session** is a **recess** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Adjournment sine die** ends a sitting; **dissolution** ends the life of the LS.
xa: **Session** = first sitting → prorogation/dissolution.
**Prorogation** is ordered by the **President** (**Governor** in States).

ne49b2e3e197.s: A quorum in either House of Parliament is ordinarily:
o: One-half of the total membership, including the presiding officer
One-tenth of the total membership, including the presiding officer
One-fourth of the elected membership, excluding nominated members
One-twentieth of the total membership, excluding the presiding officer
ne49b2e3e197.x: Under Article 100(3), the quorum is one-tenth of the total number of members of the House, including the presiding officer.
ne49b2e3e197.tq: Check both the fraction and whether the presiding officer is included.
xs: Quorum is **one-tenth of total members, including the presiding officer** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The provision is **Art 100(3)**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes list it as **Art 100(1)**, but **100(1)** actually carries the **casting vote**.
State Assemblies averaged only **24 sittings** in **2025** (**Odisha 43**, **Nagaland 7**).

n8e58d71e9da.s: Which of the following does NOT lapse on the prorogation of Parliament?
n8e58d71e9da.x: Bills do not lapse on prorogation, although pending notices generally lapse except notices to introduce bills.
xa: On **dissolution**, many bills **lapse**.
In States, prorogation is by the **Governor**.

nindian-polity-64-13.s: The President's power to dissolve the Lok Sabha is provided in:
nindian-polity-64-13.x: Article 85(2)(b) covers dissolution and 85(2)(a) prorogation; Article 123 is about ordinances.
n: Article 85 governs the summoning of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 170-172]
The President of India exercises prorogation under Article 85(2)(a). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 170-172]
The President of India exercises dissolution under Article 85(2)(b). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 170-172]
The maximum interval between two Parliamentary sessions is six months under Article 85. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 170-172]
The maximum validity of an Ordinance after reassembly is six weeks under Article 123. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 170-172]
Six months cannot intervene between the last sitting of one session and the date appointed for the first sitting of the next session. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 170-172]
The Constitution mandates only the maximum six-month gap between parliamentary sessions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 170-172]
xa: **Article 86:** President may address either House and send **messages**.
**Article 87:** **special address** at the first session after each **general election** and of each year.
The President's address is debated on a **Motion of Thanks**.

nindian-polity-64-24.s: The lapse of pending bills on dissolution of the Lok Sabha is subject to the rules in:
nindian-polity-64-24.x: Dissolution ends the Lok Sabha and its pending business lapses, subject to Article 107; the Rajya Sabha is permanent.
n: Dissolution ends the very life of the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 170-172]
The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 170-172]
Dissolution causes pending bills to lapse, subject to Article 107 rules. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 170-172]
Dissolution causes pending motions to lapse, subject to Article 107 rules. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 170-172]
Dissolution causes pending resolutions to lapse, subject to Article 107 rules. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 170-172]
xa: **Prorogation** ends only the **session**; pending bills are unaffected.
The **Speaker** continues after dissolution till the new House's **first meeting**.

n690f2a8fefa.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Secretary-General of a House of Parliament?
o: Each House has a Secretary-General as head of its secretarial staff.
The Secretary-General is appointed by the Union Government.
The parliamentary secretariat is independent of the executive.
The Secretary-General holds rank equal to the Cabinet Secretary.
n690f2a8fefa.x: The Secretary-General is appointed by the presiding officer of the House concerned, keeping the secretariat independent of the executive.
xa: **Posts common to both Houses** may be created (**Art 98**).
Recruitment: Parliament may regulate **by law**.

n26c1178800a.s: The six-month maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament is counted from:
o: the last sitting of one session to the first sitting of the next
the first sitting of one session to the first sitting of the next
the date of prorogation to the date of the next summons
the date of summons to the date of prorogation
n26c1178800a.x: The rule runs from the last sitting of one session to the first sitting of the next; the Budget, Monsoon and Winter names are only conventions.
xa: Hence at least **two sessions a year**.
States follow the same six-month rule under **Art 174**.

n1adc5ef2690.s: The President's special address at the first session after each general election and the first session of each year is made under:
n1adc5ef2690.x: Article 87 provides for this special address; it is not required after every prorogation.
xa: It **outlines government policy**, debated on a **Motion of Thanks**.
**Art 86** covers addresses **at any time** and **messages**.

n81fe194938e.s: The address of the President outlining the policies of the Government is debated in Parliament through a:
n81fe194938e.x: The President’s address outlining Government policy is debated through a Motion of Thanks in Parliament.
n81fe194938e.tq: Match the constitutional address with the parliamentary motion that follows it.
xs: The President's address is debated through a **Motion of Thanks** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The address **outlines government policy**.
xa: The **special address** is under **Art 87**.
The **Budget** session (**Feb-May**) is the longest.

n1eaeaaec92b.s: Which of the following is correct about the summoning of Parliament?
o: The President may summon the two Houses separately.
The Vice-President summons the Rajya Sabha.
Both Houses must always be summoned together.
n1eaeaaec92b.x: The President need not summon both Houses together, but each must meet within six months of its last sitting.
xa: The gap runs from the **last sitting** of one session to the **first sitting** of the next.
States: same rule under **Art 174**.

nindian-polity-58-22.s: Who communicates the date of election of the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha to all members?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha
nindian-polity-58-22.x: The Speaker fixes the Deputy Speaker's election date under Rule 8(1), and the Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha communicates it to all members.
nindian-polity-58-22.tq: Discriminate who fixes the date from who communicates it.
n: The Secretary-General communicates the Deputy Speaker’s election date to all members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 156-158]
xs: The **Secretary-General** of the Lok Sabha communicates the date — option **(4)**.
The date of the Deputy Speaker's election is **fixed by the Speaker** under **Rule 8(1)**.
The **Speaker's** own election date is fixed by the **President**.
