xa: The **Secretary-General** heads each House's Secretariat; rank = **Cabinet Secretary**.
He is appointed by the **presiding officer** and is **independent of the executive**.
**Art 98:** each House has **separate secretarial staff**.

nindian-polity-64-6.s: The Budget, Monsoon and Winter sessions of Parliament are based on:
nindian-polity-64-6.x: The three-session pattern is a convention, and the Constitution prescribes no minimum number of sitting days.
n: Having Budget, Monsoon, and Winter sessions is a parliamentary convention. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 170-172]
The Constitution does not prescribe a minimum number of sitting days in a year. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 170-172]
The Constitution does not mandate three sessions named Budget, Monsoon, and Winter. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 170-172]
xa: **Article 85:** gap between sessions **not more than 6 months**.
The six-month gap runs from the **last sitting** of one session to the **first sitting** of the next.
**Monsoon** (Jul-Sep); **Winter** (Nov-Dec).

nindian-polity-29-17.s: Under Rule 8(1), the date of the Deputy Speaker's election is fixed by the ____ and notified by the Secretary-General.
nindian-polity-29-17.x: The Speaker fixes the date of the Deputy Speaker's election and the Secretary-General notifies it to members.
n: The date for the election of the Deputy Speaker is fixed by the Speaker. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 72-75]
The date for the election of the Deputy Speaker is notified by the Secretary-General. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 72-75]
xa: The **Speaker's** own election date is fixed by the **President**.
The Deputy Speaker is elected from the House's **sitting members** (**Article 93**).
From the **Opposition** only by **convention**.

nfc9af76f954.s: To raise a matter during Zero Hour, a member:
o: intimates the Presiding Officer on the same day
gives the same notice as for an ordinary question
needs the consent of the Minister concerned
nfc9af76f954.x: Zero Hour needs no ordinary-question notice; members intimate the Presiding Officer the same day, and it has no fixed duration in the Rules.
xa: Zero Hour is an **Indian innovation** in use since **1962**, not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure.
Ministers are **not bound to reply**.
Follow-up: the **Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs** sends extracts of the Chair's directions to the ministry concerned for action.

n9a9997cd978.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of matters raised during Zero Hour?
o: The Presiding Officer decides which members may be allowed to raise them
Members may raise them without the prior notice required for a question
Ministers are constitutionally bound to give an immediate reply
They concern urgent matters of public importance
n9a9997cd978.x: Ministers are not bound to reply to matters raised during Zero Hour. The other features correctly describe the procedure.
n9a9997cd978.tq: Find the single statement that reverses a procedural limitation.
xs: **Ministers constitutionally bound to give an immediate reply** is NOT a feature — so option **(3)** is correct; ministers are **not bound to reply** in Zero Hour.
The rest are true: members raise matters **without prior notice**, and the **Presiding Officer decides** whom to allow.
xa: Zero Hour starts **immediately after Question Hour** in the Lok Sabha.
It is informal and **not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure**; in use since **1962**.
Chair's directions / assurances → **Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs** forwards them to the ministry concerned.

n82bfaa1424b.s: In the Lok Sabha, the time immediately after Question Hour, when members raise urgent matters without prior notice, is called:
n82bfaa1424b.x: Zero Hour begins immediately after Question Hour; members raise matters with only same-day intimation to the Presiding Officer.
xa: Exam angle: this exact stem appeared in **APPSC-GS 2025** and **G2 2023, 2025**.
Zero Hour is an **Indian innovation** (**1962**), not in the Rules of Procedure.
Ministers are **not bound to reply**; the Presiding Officer decides whom to allow.

nbf95831bbe0.s: The Calling Attention procedure, an Indian innovation included in the Rules of Procedure, dates from:
nbf95831bbe0.x: Calling Attention is an Indian innovation dating from 1954 and is provided for in the Rules of Procedure.
xa: It draws a minister's attention to a matter of **urgent public importance** and seeks an **authoritative statement**.
Used in **both Houses**.
⚠ **1953** short-duration – **1954** calling attention – **1962** Zero Hour.

n7438c07cc20.s: The office of Whip in the Indian parliamentary system derives its authority primarily from:
o: The Rules of Procedure of Parliament
A specific provision of the Constitution
n7438c07cc20.x: The office of Whip is not mentioned in the Constitution, the Rules of the House or any parliamentary statute. It is based on conventions of parliamentary government.
n7438c07cc20.tq: Distinguish a conventional office from a constitutional, statutory or rule-based office.
xs: The Whip rests on **parliamentary conventions** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is **not mentioned in the Constitution, the Rules of the House or any statute** — so options (2), (3) and (4) are wrong.
xa: ⚠ Only the convention statement was valid in **APPSC-G1 2024**.
Defying the whip on a vote can attract **Tenth Schedule** disqualification.
Whips: **one-line** informative, **two-line** attendance, **three-line** strict voting direction.

nindian-polity-55-46.s: Asking and answering questions addressed to Ministers takes place during:
nindian-polity-55-46.x: Question Hour is for questions to Ministers; Zero Hour is informal and needs no notice.
n: Parliamentary hours are primary mechanisms through which Parliament enforces executive accountability. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Procedural motions are primary mechanisms through which Parliament scrutinizes government policies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Question Hour involves asking questions addressed to Ministers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Zero Hour is used for raising urgent matters of public importance without prior notice. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Zero Hour is an informal convention. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
xa: Zero Hour is **not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure**.
Question Hour is codified in the **Rules**.
Zero Hour is an **Indian innovation** (**1962**).

nindian-polity-55-48.s: A Confidence Motion can be moved in:
o: a joint sitting of both Houses
nindian-polity-55-48.x: Confidence motions are admissible only in the Lok Sabha.
n: Zero Hour is an informal convention. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Supplementary questions are allowed for Short Notice Questions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
A Confidence Motion is admissible only in the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Rule 184 of the Lok Sabha permits discussion on a matter of public interest accompanied by a formal motion and voting. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
xa: **Rule 193** = short-duration discussion, max **2 hours**.
**Rule 198** = no-confidence motion.

nindian-polity-33-2.s: Since 2014, the Rajya Sabha begins its day at 11 AM with:
nindian-polity-33-2.x: Since 2014 the Rajya Sabha has Zero Hour at 11 AM and Question Hour from noon to 1 PM; the Lok Sabha has Question Hour first.
n: Question Hour in the Lok Sabha runs from 11:00 AM to 12:00 Noon. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
Question Hour in the Rajya Sabha runs from 12:00 Noon to 1:00 PM. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
Rajya Sabha Question Hour was shifted to 12:00 Noon–1:00 PM after 2014. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
Question Hour in the Lok Sabha runs from 11:00 AM to 12:00 Noon. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
Zero Hour immediately follows Question Hour in the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
xa: Question Hour lasts a maximum of **one hour**.
In the RS, urgent matters are raised in the **first hour**.
Zero Hour follow-up: the **Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs** sends extracts to ministries.

nindian-polity-33-11.s: Which device lets members raise urgent matters of public importance without prior notice?
nindian-polity-33-11.x: Zero Hour, an Indian innovation, is for raising urgent matters without notice; Question Hour is a formal procedure for questioning Ministers.
n: Question Hour is a formal procedure under Parliamentary Rules. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
Zero Hour is an Indian parliamentary innovation. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
The core purpose of Question Hour is questioning Ministers on administrative actions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
The core purpose of Zero Hour is raising urgent matters of public importance without prior notice. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
xa: Question Hour is the most effective **vigil** on the executive.
**Calling attention** (**1954**) is the other indigenous device.
⚠ **1953 – 1954 – 1962** = short-duration – calling attention – Zero Hour.

nindian-polity-29-6.s: Which of the following parliamentary devices is informal and not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure?
nindian-polity-29-6.x: Zero Hour, which follows Question Hour, is informal; Question Hour is formal and provided in the Rules.
n: Question Hour is the first hour of every sitting. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 72-75]
Zero Hour immediately follows Question Hour. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 72-75]
Question Hour is a formal parliamentary procedure under the Rules. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 72-75]
Zero Hour is used for raising urgent matters of great public importance. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 72-75]
The day-to-day proceedings of Lok Sabha are governed by the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 72-75]
Question Hour is provided under the Rules of Procedure. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 72-75]
xa: Question Hour: **11 AM to 12 Noon**; Zero Hour **12 Noon to 1 PM** (LS).
Ministers are **not bound to reply** in Zero Hour.
Questions in Question Hour are **classified questions**.

n70d47f5cec7.s: A short-notice question differs from an ordinary question in that it may be admitted when notice is given:
o: Only on the day of the sitting
At least 15 clear days in advance
n70d47f5cec7.x: A short-notice question is one for which notice is given less than 10 days in advance. Ordinary questions require at least 15 clear days' notice.
n70d47f5cec7.tq: Discriminate between the two notice thresholds instead of treating all questions alike.
xs: A short-notice question may be admitted on notice of **less than 10 days** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**At least 15 clear days'** notice is for **ordinary** questions, so option (2) is wrong.
xa: A short-notice question must be on a matter of **urgent public importance** and gets an **oral answer**.
It is printed on **light pink** paper; supplementaries are allowed.
**Zero Hour** matters need **no prior notice** of the kind a question needs — only same-day intimation to the Presiding Officer.

nf93ea734334.s: An Adjournment Motion in Parliament can be admitted only when it concerns:
o: A demand for grant requiring reduction by one rupee
Any matter raised without prior notice
A matter of definite and urgent public importance
nf93ea734334.x: An Adjournment Motion sets aside the normal business of the House to discuss a definite matter of urgent public importance.
nf93ea734334.tq: Match the motion with its defining procedural condition rather than with a related device.
xs: An Adjournment Motion concerns **a definite matter of urgent public importance** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It sets aside the House business to discuss that matter.
Reducing a demand to **Re 1** is a **policy cut**; matters raised without prior notice belong to **Zero Hour**.
xa: It is moved **only in the Lok Sabha** with **50 members'** support.
It carries an **element of censure**; debate lasts at least **2 h 30 min**.
⚠ Adjournment and no-confidence are both **Lok Sabha only** and both need **50 members**.

n4d5b188874f.s: Private Members’ Resolutions in Parliament are generally taken up on:
o: The last sitting day of every month
n4d5b188874f.x: Private Members’ Resolutions are taken up on alternate Fridays during the afternoon.
n4d5b188874f.tq: Match the device with its distinctive day-and-time arrangement.
xs: Private members' resolutions are taken up on **alternate Fridays in the afternoon** — so option **(3)** is correct.
They are not a Monday, Wednesday or month-end item; the slot is **alternate Fridays**.
xa: A **government resolution** is moved by a minister, e.g., approving **treaties**.
A **statutory resolution** is moved under a constitutional/statutory provision.
A resolution is a **self-contained proposal**; same subject barred for **one year**.

nac8fe9172ef.s: When a member who is speaking gives way to another member or to the Chair, the procedure is known as:
nac8fe9172ef.x: Yielding the floor occurs when the member speaking gives way to another member or to the Chair.
nac8fe9172ef.tq: Match the ordinary procedural action with its precise parliamentary term.
xs: A member giving way to another member or the Chair is **yielding the floor** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Simple closure** ends debate and puts the matter to vote; **point of order** is raised when proceedings depart from rules; **calling attention** seeks a minister's statement.
xa: **Kangaroo closure**: only important clauses debated, others taken as passed.
**Guillotine**: all pending clauses put to vote when time ends.
**Three-line whip** = strict voting direction.

nindian-polity-55-3.s: Question Hour, supplementary questions and adjournment motions together are described as the:
nindian-polity-55-3.x: Together they let Parliament question the government, follow up and raise urgent matters, forming the 'accountability triangle'.
n: The Parliamentary Accountability Triangle comprises Question Hour, Supplementary Questions, and Adjournment Motions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
The Parliamentary Accountability Triangle directly ensures executive responsibility to the legislature. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Question Hour involves asking questions addressed to Ministers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Zero Hour is used for raising urgent matters of public importance without prior notice. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
xa: **Question Hour** = most effective **day-to-day** vigil on the executive.
**No-confidence motion** = **most powerful weapon** of executive accountability.
**Zero Hour** and **Calling Attention Motion** are **indigenous Indian** contributions.

nindian-polity-55-4.s: A question that gets a written answer, with no supplementary questions allowed, is a:
nindian-polity-55-4.x: Unstarred questions get written answers without supplementaries; starred questions get oral answers with supplementaries.
n: Zero Hour is used for raising urgent matters of public importance without prior notice. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Starred Questions are taken during Question Hour. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Starred Questions require oral answers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Supplementary questions are allowed for Starred Questions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Unstarred Questions are taken during Question Hour. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Unstarred Questions require written answers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Supplementary questions are not allowed for Unstarred Questions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Short Notice Questions are taken during Question Hour. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Short Notice Questions concern urgent matters of public importance. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Short Notice Questions require oral answers with shorter notice. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Supplementary questions are allowed for Short Notice Questions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
xa: ⚠ Starred = oral + **green**; unstarred = written + **white**; short notice = **light pink**.
Short notice = less than **10 clear days**; ordinary questions need **15 clear days'** notice.
At most **20** starred questions listed per day.

nindian-polity-34-16.s: At most how many starred questions are listed per day for oral answer?
nindian-polity-34-16.x: Starred questions are limited to 20 a day for oral answer; unstarred questions have no such limit.
n: A Short Notice Question is identified by a shorter notice period. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 85-87]
A maximum of 20 Starred Questions are listed for oral answer per day. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 85-87]
There is no strict limit of 20 Unstarred Questions per day. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 85-87]
A Short Notice Question is accepted with a shorter notice duration than ordinary questions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 85-87]
xa: Standard notice: at least **15 clear days**.
Short notice: less than **10 clear days**.
Short-notice daily listing: **discretion** of the **Speaker or Chairman**.

nindian-polity-34-19.s: Which type of question deals with matters of urgent public importance?
nindian-polity-34-19.x: Short notice questions concern urgent matters; starred and unstarred questions concern matters of general public importance.
n: The subject matter of Starred Questions is of general or ordinary public importance. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 85-87]
The subject matter of Unstarred Questions is of general or ordinary public importance. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 85-87]
A Short Notice Question concerns a matter of urgent public importance. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 85-87]
xa: Starred = **oral**; unstarred = **written**.
Short notice questions get an **oral** answer and allow **supplementaries**.
⚠ Starred = oral + green; unstarred = written + white.

ncfb21291e09.s: In the Lok Sabha, a short-duration discussion without voting is held under:
ncfb21291e09.x: Rule 193 is a discussion without voting, Rule 184 a discussion followed by voting, and Rule 377 is for matters not raisable under any other device.
xa: **Rule 198 (LS)** = no-confidence motion.
Privilege motion = **Rule 222 (LS)**, **Rule 187 (RS)**.
Short-duration discussion: max **2 hours**; Indian innovation (**1953**).

n139c0d59bc1.s: In which year was the Calling Attention device introduced?
n139c0d59bc1.x: Calling Attention dates from 1954; the short-duration discussion is from 1953 and Zero Hour is associated with 1962.
xa: All three are **Indian innovations**; Zero Hour was not borrowed from any other country.
Short-duration discussion is under **Rule 193**, max **2 hours**, no voting.
Calling attention is **in the Rules of Procedure**; Zero Hour is **not**.

nbeafecbc175.s: The short-duration discussion, an Indian parliamentary innovation, was introduced in:
nbeafecbc175.x: The short-duration discussion dates from 1953; it is limited to two hours and involves no vote.
xa: ⚠ **Rule 184** = discussion followed by a vote.
**Half-an-hour discussion**: matter sufficiently debated needing factual elucidation; no formal motion or vote.
Next Indian innovations: calling attention **1954**, Zero Hour **1962**.

nindian-polity-33-1.s: The primary purpose of Question Hour in Parliament is to:
o: Discuss only matters of urgent public importance
Enforce accountability of the Council of Ministers
nindian-polity-33-1.x: Question Hour and related hours exist to enforce executive accountability and control over the Council of Ministers.
n: Question Hour and related hours are primary parliamentary instruments for enforcing executive accountability. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
Question Hour and related hours are instruments for exercising control over the Council of Ministers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
xa: Accountability triangle: **Question Hour + Supplementary Questions + Adjournment Motions**.
Other tools: **half-an-hour discussion**, **short-duration discussion**, **calling attention**, **censure**, **no-confidence**.
Committees: **Government Assurances**, **Petitions**, **Subordinate Legislation**, **PAC**, **Estimates**.

nindian-polity-55-18.s: Since 2015, the maximum number of matters that can be raised daily under Rule 377 is:
nindian-polity-55-18.x: Up to 30 matters a day can be raised under Rule 377 since 2015; Zero Hour lasts at most one hour.
n: A maximum of 20 Starred Questions may be listed for oral answer per day. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
A No-Confidence Motion requires the support of 50 members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
The number of matters that could be raised daily under Rule 377 increased from 20 to 30 in 2015. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
A maximum of 30 matters may be raised daily under Rule 377 after 2015. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
The minimum number of members required to support admission of a No-Confidence Motion is 50. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
Zero Hour has a maximum duration of one hour. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
The maximum duration of Zero Hour in the Lok Sabha is one hour. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
xa: **Short-duration discussion** (Rule 193) is the one with max **2 hours**.
Adjournment Motion debate: at least **2 h 30 min**.
⚠ Some notes say Zero Hour duration is **not fixed**.

nindian-polity-33-29.s: Historically, the operational scope of which parliamentary motion was restricted by Calling Attention notices?
nindian-polity-33-29.x: Calling attention notices narrowed the scope of adjournment motions by offering a milder way to raise urgent matters. Question Hour and Zero Hour were not affected.
nindian-polity-33-29.tq: Recall which motion calling attention notices replaced.
n: Calling Attention Motion restricted the scope of Adjournment Motion. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
Calling Attention notices historically restricted the operational scope of Adjournment Motions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
Calling Attention notices did not restrict the operational scope of Question Hour. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
Calling Attention notices did not restrict the operational scope of Zero Hour. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
xs: Calling Attention notices restricted the scope of the **Adjournment Motion** — option **(3)**.
They did **not** restrict **Question Hour** or **Zero Hour**.
The Calling Attention Motion **resembles** an Adjournment Motion but has **no censure** element.
xa: Calling attention: **Indian** innovation, since **1954**.
It seeks an **authoritative statement** from the minister.
The Adjournment Motion is a **traditional** parliamentary device.

nindian-polity-33-30.s: An Adjournment Motion is admissible only when which condition is satisfied?
o: Other tools, such as a Short Duration discussion, are too late
The matter concerns a question of privilege
A matter has already been fully debated in Question Hour
The scheduled daily agenda has been completed
nindian-polity-33-30.x: An adjournment motion is admitted only when other routes, such as a short duration discussion, would come too late. Questions of privilege cannot be raised this way.
nindian-polity-33-30.tq: Recall the condition for admitting an adjournment motion.
n: An Adjournment Motion is admissible only when other tools, such as Short Duration discussions, are too late. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
xs: An Adjournment Motion is admissible only when **other tools**, such as a **Short Duration** discussion, are **too late** — option **(1)**.
It **cannot** raise a **question of privilege**.
It must be a **single**, **definite**, **specific** matter of **recent** occurrence; only **one** per sitting.
xa: Needs the **Presiding Officer's** consent and **50 members**' support.
Debate lasts at least **2 h 30 min**.
It is **Lok Sabha only**.

n2dde54a6d12.s: The day-to-day proceedings of the Lok Sabha are governed mainly by the:
o: Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha
n2dde54a6d12.x: The Constitution gives only the broad framework; devices such as the No-Confidence Motion and Rule 377 come from the Rules of Procedure.
xa: **Zero Hour** also derives from **convention**.
No-confidence motion: **Rule 198**; **written notice** to the **Secretary-General**.
The **Whip** is not in the Constitution, the Rules or any statute — only **conventions**.

nindian-polity-29-16.s: A matter that cannot be raised through questions, calling attention or other motions is raised in the Lok Sabha under:
nindian-polity-29-16.x: Rule 377 covers such matters; it requires written notice and the Speaker's consent.
n: Matters raised under Rule 377 cannot be raised under the rules governing Questions, Calling Attention, or other formal Motions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 72-75]
A matter under Rule 377 requires written notice. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 72-75]
A matter under Rule 377 requires the Speaker's consent. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 72-75]
xa: Daily limit raised from **20 to 30** in **2015**.
Written notice goes to the **Secretary-General**.
RS equivalent: **Special Mention** (**Rule 180A-E**).

n837a4ff818f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about an Adjournment Motion?
o: The debate on it lasts not less than two hours and thirty minutes.
It needs the support of 50 members for admission.
It can be moved in either House of Parliament.
It must relate to a single, definite matter of recent occurrence.
n837a4ff818f.x: An Adjournment Motion can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
xa: It **interrupts / suspends** normal business and involves **censure** of the Government.
It is admissible only when other tools, e.g. **Short Duration** discussions, are too late.
⚠ Adjournment and no-confidence motions → both **Lok Sabha only**, both need **50 members**.

na5c48fbdf31.s: Leave to move a no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha requires the support of at least:
na5c48fbdf31.x: It needs 50 members' support; the motion is not expressly in the Constitution but flows from Article 75(3) and lies only in the Lok Sabha.
xa: Moved under **Rule 198**; **no reasons need be stated**.
If passed, the whole **Council of Ministers must resign**.
First instance: against **Nehru** (**1963**) by **J.B. Kripalani**.

ndd1d2bd6b0c.s: Which is regarded as the most powerful weapon for enforcing the accountability of the executive?
ndd1d2bd6b0c.x: The no-confidence motion is the most powerful weapon of accountability and need not state reasons; Question Hour is the most effective day-to-day vigil.
xa: ⚠ **Question Hour** = most effective **day-to-day** vigil; no-confidence = most powerful weapon.
The **Speaker** has discretion to admit or reject a no-confidence motion.
Censure can be against a **minister or a group**; no-confidence only the **entire** Council.

nfff31d19856.s: Who rules on a point of order raised in the House?
nfff31d19856.x: A point of order, raised when proceedings depart from the Rules or the Constitution, is not debated; the Presiding Officer rules on it.
xa: **Yielding the floor**: member speaking gives way to another member or the Chair.
**Simple closure**: "matter sufficiently discussed; be put to vote".
**Rule 377 (LS)** matters are those that are **not points of order** ("special mention").

nee7cf8fcba1.s: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is the ex-officio Chairperson of the:
nee7cf8fcba1.x: The Speaker is ex-officio Chairperson of the Business Advisory, Rules and General Purposes Committees.
xa: **Standing committees** are permanent (e.g., Business Advisory, Petitions, Privileges, Rules); **ad hoc** ones end when the task is done.
Committee of Privileges (LS): **15** members nominated by the **Speaker**.
**Committee on Petitions** = **"Ombudsman"** of Parliament (APPSC-GS 2025).

n177b5de3d9f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the removal of the Speaker under Article 94(c)?
o: A notice of fourteen days is required.
The procedure is governed by Rules 200–203 of the Lok Sabha Rules of Procedure.
The notice must be supported by at least fifty members.
The resolution needs only a simple majority of members present and voting.
n177b5de3d9f.x: Removal needs a majority of all the then members of the House (an effective majority); a simple majority is not enough.
xa: A resolution against Speaker **Om Birla** was **dismissed by voice vote** (**Mar 2026**).
The Speaker has **discretion to admit or reject** a no-confidence motion.
⚠ A no-confidence motion (vs the government) also needs **50 members**, under **Rule 198**.

nindian-polity-34-4.s: Which of the following is not one of the three primary categories of Parliamentary Questions?
nindian-polity-34-4.x: The three kinds of parliamentary question are starred, unstarred and short notice. There is no 'adjournment question'; adjournment is a motion.
nindian-polity-34-4.tq: Discriminate kinds of question from kinds of motion.
n: The three primary categories of parliamentary questions are Starred Questions, Unstarred Questions, and Short Notice Questions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 85-87]
xs: **Adjournment Question** is not a category — option **(1)**.
The three primary categories are **Starred**, **Unstarred** and **Short Notice** questions.
**Adjournment** is a **motion**, not a type of question.
xa: All three are taken up during **Question Hour**.
Questions **to a private member** (on his bill/resolution) are on **yellow** paper.
Starred: at most **20** listed for oral answer daily.

nindian-polity-55-28.s: A privilege motion is referred to the:
nindian-polity-55-28.x: A privilege motion goes to the Committee of Privileges.
n: A No-Confidence Motion is admissible only in the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
A Censure Motion is admissible only in the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
A Calling Attention Motion is admissible in either House of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
An Adjournment Motion is admissible only in the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
A Privilege Motion is admissible in either House of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
xa: The Adjournment Motion also needs **50 members**' support.
Calling attention may be admitted in **either House**.
No-confidence: **Rule 198**; no **reasons** required.

nindian-polity-33-28.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: A Calling Attention Motion does not disrupt the scheduled daily agenda.
An Adjournment Motion interrupts normal parliamentary business.
A Calling Attention Motion involves censure of the Government.
An Adjournment Motion involves an element of censure of the Government.
nindian-polity-33-28.x: A Calling Attention Motion has no element of censure; it is the Adjournment Motion that implies censure.
n: A Calling Attention Motion does not disrupt the scheduled daily agenda. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
An Adjournment Motion interrupts normal parliamentary business. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
An Adjournment Motion suspends normal parliamentary business. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
A Calling Attention Motion has no element of condemnation or censure. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
An Adjournment Motion involves censure or condemnation of the Government. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 82-85]
xa: Calling Attention: **either House**; Adjournment Motion: **Lok Sabha only**.
Adjournment needs **50 members**' support.
Adjournment debate lasts at least **2 h 30 min**.

nindian-polity-35-9.s: Which parliamentary committee regulates the timetable of the House's business?
nindian-polity-35-9.x: The Business Advisory Committee sets the timetable; the Rules Committee proposes rule changes and the Assurances Committee tracks Ministers' promises.
n: The Committee on Government Assurances tracks the fulfillment of promises given by Ministers on the floor of the House. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Committee on Government Assurances tracks the fulfillment of undertakings given by Ministers on the floor of the House. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Committee on Government Assurances tracks the fulfillment of assurances given by Ministers on the floor of the House. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Committee on Government Assurances reports on the fulfillment of promises, undertakings, and assurances given by Ministers on the floor of the House. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Committee on Petitions examines petitions submitted to the House. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Committee on Petitions examines representations submitted to the House. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Business Advisory Committee regulates the official parliamentary timetable. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Business Advisory Committee regulates the programme of House business. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Rules Committee recommends amendments to the Rules of Procedure. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Rules Committee recommends additions to the Rules of Procedure. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Rules Committee recommends procedural adjustments to the Rules of Procedure. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
xa: Petitions Committee is the "**Ombudsman**" of Parliament.
**Committee on Subordinate Legislation:** checks **delegated** rule-making stays within **statutory limits**.
**Consultative Committees** are formed by the **Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs** — not parliamentary committees per se.

nindian-polity-39-15.s: What is the constitutional quorum for a House of Parliament?
nindian-polity-39-15.x: Under Article 100, the quorum of either House is one-tenth of its total membership.
n: The constitutional quorum of a House is one-tenth of its total membership. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
The constitutional quorum is provided under Article 100. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
xs: The quorum is **one-tenth** of the **total membership** — option **(1)**.
It is laid down in **Article 100**.
One-half, one-third and one-twentieth are distractors.
xa: **Article 85:** maximum gap of **six months** between sessions.
First Speaker of the Lok Sabha: **G.V. Mavalankar**.
Estimates Committee (**30**, LS only) is the **largest** Parliamentary Committee.

nde870ae0321.s: A privilege motion, moved when a member feels that a minister or member has committed a breach of privilege, is raised in the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha respectively under
nde870ae0321.x: A privilege motion is governed by Rule 222 of the Lok Sabha rules and Rule 187 of the Rajya Sabha rules. Rule 184 (LS) is a discussion followed by a vote, Rule 193 (LS) is a short-duration discussion without a vote, Rule 180A-E (RS) covers Special Mentions, and Rule 198 (LS) is the no-confidence motion.
xs: A privilege motion is under **Rule 222** (LS) and **Rule 187** (RS) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Rule 184** = discussion with vote; **Rule 193** = short-duration discussion; **Rule 180A-E** = Special Mentions (RS); **Rule 198** = no-confidence motion.
xa: A privilege motion concerns a **breach of privilege** by a minister or member and is available in **both Houses**.
A privilege notice was given in the Rajya Sabha against the **Union Education Minister** (**May 2026**).
Committee of Privileges: **15** members (LS, by the Speaker); **10** (RS, by the Chairman).

n381ed5a22ac.s: The first no-confidence motion against the Union Council of Ministers was moved against Jawaharlal Nehru in 1963 by:
n381ed5a22ac.x: The first no-confidence motion against Jawaharlal Nehru was moved in 1963 by J.B. Kripalani.
n381ed5a22ac.tq: Link the event, year and mover rather than relying on the event alone.
xs: The first no-confidence motion, against **Nehru** in **1963**, was moved by **J.B. Kripalani** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Gouthu Latchanna** moved the motion against the **Prakasam** ministry in **Andhra State** (Nov **1954**).
xa: The Andhra motion was carried **69 for, 68 against**; the ministry fell after **13 months**.
President's Rule followed: **16 Nov 1954 - 27 Mar 1955**.
No-confidence is moved under **Rule 198** with **50 members'** support.

n329b57a7249.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: A Censure Motion may be directed against a Minister, a group of Ministers or the whole Council.
A No-confidence Motion is directed against the entire Council of Ministers.
Passing a Censure Motion compels the Council of Ministers to resign.
Passing a No-confidence Motion requires the Council of Ministers to resign.
n329b57a7249.x: A passed Censure Motion does not compel resignation; a passed No-confidence Motion does.
xa: Censure **must state reasons**; no-confidence needs **no reasons**.
Censure seeks **disapproval of a policy**.
No-confidence: **only in Lok Sabha**, **50 members**, **Rule 198**.

nf929b390acc.s: A resolution moved under a constitutional or statutory provision is called a:
nf929b390acc.x: Such a resolution is a statutory resolution; a Government resolution is one moved by a minister, e.g. to approve a treaty.
xa: Private member's resolutions: **alternate Fridays**, afternoon.
The mover cannot withdraw a resolution **without leave of the House**.
Same subject barred for **one year**.

nindian-polity-55-6.s: A motion raised against a Minister for withholding or distorting facts is a:
nindian-polity-55-6.x: A privilege motion targets a Minister who withheld or distorted facts; a censure motion disapproves of specific policies.
n: A No-Confidence Motion tests the majority support of the Council of Ministers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
A Confidence Motion proves majority floor support. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
A Censure Motion expresses strong disapproval of specific policies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
A Censure Motion expresses criticism of specific policies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
A Privilege Motion is raised against a Minister for withholding facts. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
A Privilege Motion is raised against a Minister for distorting facts. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
xa: Censure motion: **reasons must be stated**; does **not** force resignation.
Privilege motion goes to the **Committee of Privileges** — **Rule 222 (LS)**, **Rule 187 (RS)**.
No-confidence needs **50** members and is **Lok Sabha only**.

nindian-polity-55-24.s: If a Confidence Motion moved by the Government is defeated in the Lok Sabha:
o: The Lok Sabha is automatically dissolved
The motion is referred to the Committee of Privileges
nindian-polity-55-24.x: Defeat of a confidence motion shows the Government has lost the Lok Sabha's support, so it falls.
n: If a Confidence Motion is defeated, the Government falls. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #55 · pp 146-150]
xa: A passed **No-Confidence Motion** also forces the **whole Council** to resign.
The **Speaker** decides the admissibility of a no-confidence motion.

n734fac6257a.s: Who appoints the Chairpersons of Department-related Standing Committees?
o: The Prime Minister for Lok Sabha committees and the Vice-President for Rajya Sabha committees
The respective ministers heading the departments concerned
The Speaker for Lok Sabha committees and the Chairman for Rajya Sabha committees
n734fac6257a.x: The Speaker appoints the Chairpersons of Lok Sabha DRSCs, while the Chairman appoints the Chairpersons of Rajya Sabha DRSCs.
n734fac6257a.tq: Apply the authority-to-House distinction instead of attributing all appointments to one presiding officer.
xs: DRSC chairs are appointed by **the Speaker for Lok Sabha committees and the Chairman for Rajya Sabha committees** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Not the Prime Minister, ministers or the President — options (1), (2) and (3) are wrong.
xa: **24** DRSCs: **16** under Lok Sabha, **8** under Rajya Sabha; set up in **1993**.
Each DRSC: **31 members = 21 LS + 10 RS**; quorum **11**.
The Speaker is **ex-officio chair** of the Business Advisory, Rules and General Purposes Committees.

nb5d06d384e1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Public Accounts Committee?
o: A Minister can be a member of the Committee.
It has 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.
Its members are elected annually by PR-STV.
Its Chairperson is appointed by the Speaker.
nb5d06d384e1.x: Ministers cannot be members of the Public Accounts Committee.
xa: Chair from the **Opposition since 1967**.
It examines **CAG audit reports**; its recommendations are **not binding**.
PAC for **2026-27** held its first meeting under **K.C. Venugopal**.

n7e10758a5d8.s: The Committee on Public Undertakings (1964) was created on the recommendation of the:
n7e10758a5d8.x: COPU came from the Krishna Menon Committee's recommendation; John Mathai's recommendation gave the Estimates Committee its present form in 1950.
xa: The **PAC** was set up in **1921** under the **Government of India Act, 1919**.
Estimates Committee: **30** members, **Lok Sabha only** — the **largest** committee.
CPU: **22** members — **15** LS + **7** RS.

n0f18645f3ea.s: The Public Accounts Committee was first set up in:
n0f18645f3ea.x: The PAC was set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919; it examines the CAG's audit reports.
xa: ⚠ PAC chair = **Opposition**; Estimates chair = **ruling party**.
Its recommendations are **not binding**; it examines execution, not policy.
**22** members = 15 LS + **7 RS**.

n40eb01540cf.s: Which committee is described as the “Continuous economy committee”?
n40eb01540cf.x: The Estimates Committee is known as the “Continuous economy committee.”
n40eb01540cf.tq: Match the nickname with the committee concerned with economies and efficiency.
xs: The **Estimates Committee** is the "Continuous economy committee" — so option **(2)** is correct.
It suggests **economies, efficiency, administrative reform** and alternative policies.
xa: **30** members, all from the **Lok Sabha**.
Present form in **1950** on **John Mathai**'s recommendation.
⚠ The **Committee on Petitions** is the **"Ombudsman"** of Parliament.

na5a31ca13a9.s: Biometric attendance for MLAs in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly was introduced from the:
na5a31ca13a9.x: Andhra Pradesh introduced biometric attendance for MLAs from its Budget Session in 2026.
xa: The **AP Legislature** uses the same devices as Parliament.
The **AP Legislative Council** was adjourned amid a row on the **Tirumala laddu** issue (**Feb 2026**).
Andhra State: **Prakasam** ministry fell by one vote (**69 for, 68 against**) in Nov **1954**.

nindian-polity-52-10.s: Which parliamentary committee has 30 members drawn from the Lok Sabha only and is the largest parliamentary committee?
nindian-polity-52-10.x: The Estimates Committee is the largest parliamentary committee, with 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha. The PAC and Public Undertakings Committee have 22 members each.
nindian-polity-52-10.tq: Discriminate the 30-member Estimates Committee from the 22-member committees.
n: The Estimates Committee has 30 members in total. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 137-141]
The Estimates Committee consists only of Lok Sabha members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 137-141]
The Estimates Committee is the largest parliamentary committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 137-141]
xs: The **Estimates Committee** has **30** members, all from the **Lok Sabha** — option **(3)**.
It is the single **largest** parliamentary committee and the **only** one with no Rajya Sabha members.
The **PAC** and the **Committee on Public Undertakings** have **22** members each (**15** LS + **7** RS).
xa: Its chairman is appointed by the **Speaker**, traditionally from the **ruling party**.
It examines **budget estimates** and suggests **economy** and **efficiency** in administration.
Nickname: "**Continuous economy committee**".

nindian-polity-35-19.s: Ministers are barred from the PAC, the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Petitions mainly because these committees:
o: consist only of Rajya Sabha members
meet only when Parliament is not in session
nindian-polity-35-19.x: These committees, along with COPU and the Subordinate Legislation Committee, scrutinise the government, so Ministers are kept out.
n: Ministers cannot be elected or nominated to the Public Accounts Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
Ministers cannot be elected or nominated to the Estimates Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
Ministers cannot be elected or nominated to the Committee on Public Undertakings. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
Ministers cannot be elected or nominated to the Committee on Subordinate Legislation. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
Ministers cannot be elected or nominated to the Committee on Petitions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
xa: Subordinate Legislation: **15** members in **each House**.
Petitions: **15** (LS), **10** (RS) — the "**Ombudsman**" of Parliament.
**Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs:** **30** members; no minister can be a member.

nindian-polity-35-26.s: Since 1967, the Chairman of which committee has been appointed from the Opposition?
nindian-polity-35-26.x: The Speaker has appointed the PAC Chairman from the Opposition since 1967; the Estimates Committee Chairman comes from the ruling party.
n: The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee has been appointed from the Opposition since 1967. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Chairman of the Estimates Committee is appointed by the Speaker. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Chairman of the Estimates Committee is appointed from the ruling party. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
The Chairman of the Committee on Public Undertakings is appointed by the Speaker. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
xa: ⚠ PAC chair = **Opposition**; Estimates chair = **ruling party**.
PAC for **2026-27** met under **K.C. Venugopal**.
**Speaker** is ex-officio chair of the **Business Advisory**, **Rules** and **General Purposes** Committees.

n6638803569e.s: After a resolution has been moved in Parliament, a resolution on the same subject is barred for:
n6638803569e.x: A resolution on the same subject is barred for one year; a resolution is always a substantive motion, must be put to vote, and cannot be withdrawn without the House's leave.
xa: **Private member's** resolutions are taken up on **alternate Fridays**, afternoon.
**Government** resolutions are moved by a minister (e.g. approving treaties).
**Statutory** resolutions are moved under a constitutional/statutory provision.

nbcaec177ef1.s: Which Union Minister maintains close contact with the Chief Whips of political parties in both Houses of Parliament?
o: Minister of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
nbcaec177ef1.x: The Minister of Parliamentary Affairs keeps close contact with the Chief Whips of parties in both Houses.
nbcaec177ef1.tq: Use the functional association between parliamentary coordination and the concerned ministry.
xs: The **Minister of Parliamentary Affairs** keeps close contact with the chief whips — so option **(3)** is correct.
This liaison covers the chief whips of parties in **both Houses**.
xa: The same ministry sends extracts of the Chair's **Zero Hour** directions/assurances to the ministry concerned for action.
Whips ensure **attendance and voting** per party line.
Defiance can bring **Tenth Schedule** disqualification.

n47a26cd7bf3.s: Department-related Standing Committees (DRSCs) were set up in:
n47a26cd7bf3.x: DRSCs were set up in 1993; there are 24 (16 Lok Sabha and 8 Rajya Sabha), each with 31 members and a quorum of 11.
xa: Chairs are appointed by the **Speaker** (LS committees) and the **Chairman** (RS committees).
⚠ DRSC **31 = 21 + 10**; SC/ST Welfare Committee **30 = 20 + 10**.
DRSCs are among Parliament's **"watchdogs"** over the executive.

n1773a432295.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ad hoc committees of Parliament?
o: Inquiry committees may be set up by a motion or by the Speaker or Chairman.
The Committee on MPLADS is an example of an inquiry committee.
They continue permanently after completing their assigned task.
Select and Joint Committees on Bills are ad hoc committees.
n1773a432295.x: Ad hoc committees end when their assigned task is completed.
xa: Another inquiry-type ad hoc example: the **Railway Convention Committee**.
**Standing committees** are permanent: Business Advisory, Petitions, Privileges, Rules.
Select = one House; Joint = **both Houses**, formed on a motion adopted in the House.

n271a20f5d5b.s: Committees such as the PAC, the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings are described as:
n271a20f5d5b.x: These committees, along with the Department-related Standing Committees, are described as watchdogs over the executive.
xa: **Committee on Subordinate Legislation**: checks rule-making (delegated) powers.
**Committee on Government Assurances**: tracks ministers' promises till implemented.
**Committee on Petitions** = **"Ombudsman"** of Parliament.

n3d0a4479928.s: Which parliamentary committee is described as the 'Ombudsman' of Parliament, examining petitions on bills and on matters of general public interest?
n3d0a4479928.x: The Committee on Petitions examines petitions on bills and matters of public interest and is called Parliament's 'Ombudsman'. The Committee on Government Assurances tracks ministers' promises, the Committee on Subordinate Legislation checks the exercise of delegated rule-making powers, and the Committee of Privileges examines breaches of privilege.
xs: The **Committee on Petitions** is the **"Ombudsman"** of Parliament — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2025 key).
**Government Assurances** tracks ministers' promises; **Subordinate Legislation** checks delegated rule-making.
xa: It is a **standing** (permanent) committee.
**Estimates Committee** = "Continuous economy committee".
Committee of Privileges: LS **15** (Speaker), RS **10** (Chairman).

n1578e61f5dc.s: Which body's recommendations are associated with a code of ethics, the Right to Public Services and e-governance?
n1578e61f5dc.x: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2nd ARC) is linked with a code of ethics, the Right to Public Services and e-governance. Shanta Kumar dealt with FCI/PDS, Ashok Dalwai with farmers' income and Kasturirangan with education.
xs: Code of ethics, **Right to Public Services** and **e-governance** = the **Second Administrative Reforms Commission** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Shanta Kumar** = FCI/PDS; **Ashok Dalwai** = farmers' income; **Kasturirangan** = education.
xa: Shanta Kumar: **DBT for food**, decentralised procurement.
Kasturirangan: **NEP 2020**, **5+3+3+4**.
Urjit Patel: inflation targeting (**4% +/- 2%**).

n7fa3a65d088.s: In the 17th Lok Sabha, what proportion of Bills were referred to parliamentary committees?
n7fa3a65d088.x: Only 16% of Bills in the 17th Lok Sabha were referred to committees; the corresponding figure for the 15th Lok Sabha was 71%.
n7fa3a65d088.tq: Separate the figures belonging to the 17th and 15th Lok Sabhas instead of selecting the larger comparison value.
xs: Only **16%** of Bills went to committees in the 17th Lok Sabha — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **71%** was the 15th Lok Sabha's figure.
xa: Question Hour ran only **60%** of its scheduled time.
UK comparison: every Bill examined by committees of both Houses; India: **under one-fifth** referred.
Ad hoc **Select / Joint Committees on Bills** examine Bills referred to them.

nindian-polity-35-10.s: The Lok Sabha Ethics Committee was first constituted as an ad-hoc committee in:
nindian-polity-35-10.x: It was first set up as an ad-hoc committee on 16 May 2000 and made permanent in 2015.
n: The Lok Sabha Ethics Committee was first constituted as an Ad-hoc Committee on 16 May 2000. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
xa: **Rajya Sabha** Ethics Committee: constituted **4 March 1997**.
**Committee on Empowerment of Women:** **29 April 1997**.
PAC chair from the Opposition since **1967**.

ndff73d322ef.s: A half-an-hour discussion in Parliament is held on:
o: A matter of urgent public importance requiring adjournment of the House
A matter already sufficiently debated but requiring factual elucidation
ndff73d322ef.x: A half-an-hour discussion is held on a matter sufficiently debated that needs further factual elucidation; it involves no formal motion or vote.
xa: **Short-duration discussion** (Rule **193**): max **2 hours**, no vote, Indian innovation of **1953**.
**Rule 184** discussion ends in a vote.
**Rule 377 (LS)** covers matters not raisable under any other device.

n114ccea83eb.s: Defiance of a party Whip can attract disqualification under the:
n114ccea83eb.x: The Whip enforces attendance and voting on party lines, and defiance can attract disqualification under the Tenth Schedule.
xa: The Whip rests on **conventions** — not in the Constitution, Rules or any statute.
The **Minister of Parliamentary Affairs** keeps close contact with chief whips of both Houses.
**Three-line** whip = strict voting direction.

nbfa9da20d73.s: The recommendations of the Public Accounts Committee are:
o: binding once approved by the Speaker
nbfa9da20d73.x: PAC recommendations are not binding; the PAC checks spending within the scope of the demand and examines execution, not policy.
xa: It examines **CAG audit reports** and points out **waste, loss, nugatory expenditure**.
Chair from the **Opposition since 1967**.
PAC and Estimates Committee are quoted for **financial discipline and accountability**.

nc05098b9939.s: Inflation targeting at 4% with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2% is associated with the committee headed by:
nc05098b9939.x: The Urjit Patel committee is linked with 4% ± 2% inflation targeting; Nachiket Mor is associated with financial inclusion and Shanta Kumar with FCI/PDS reform.
xa: **2nd ARC**: code of ethics, **Right to Public Services**, e-governance.
**Ashok Dalwai**: doubling farmers' income — value addition, land leasing.

nindian-polity-29-23.s: The form of closure in which all remaining clauses or demands are put to vote at once when the allotted time expires is called:
nindian-polity-29-23.x: The guillotine is the form of closure applied when the allotted time runs out, putting all remaining clauses or demands to vote at once.
n: A Closure Motion is moved to cut short debate. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 72-75]
A Closure Motion puts the question to vote. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 72-75]
A Guillotine is a form of closure applied when the allotted time expires. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 72-75]
Under the Guillotine, all remaining discussed and undiscussed clauses or demands are immediately put to vote. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 72-75]
xa: Closure / guillotine is **Lok Sabha only**.
**Simple closure:** "matter sufficiently discussed; be put to vote".
**Kangaroo closure:** only important clauses debated.

n1c112242c03.s: The no-confidence motion carried against the Prakasam ministry of Andhra State in November 1954 was moved by:
n1c112242c03.x: Gouthu Latchanna's motion was carried by 69 votes to 68 in November 1954, and the Prakasam ministry fell.
xa: President's Rule in Andhra State: **16 Nov 1954 - 27 Mar 1955**.
A passed no-confidence motion forces the whole **Council of Ministers** to resign.

nindian-polity-35-43.s: Consultative Committees of MPs for particular ministries are constituted by the:
nindian-polity-35-43.x: Consultative Committees are set up by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs and are not parliamentary committees in the strict sense.
n: Consultative Committees are constituted by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
Consultative Committees are not parliamentary committees per se. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
Members of Consultative Committees are MPs from specific zones or ministries. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 87-91]
xa: **Standing committees** are permanent (e.g. **Business Advisory**, **Petitions**, **Privileges**, **Rules**).
**Ad hoc committees** end when the task is done (e.g. **Select / Joint Committees on Bills**).
The **Minister of Parliamentary Affairs** keeps close contact with **chief whips** of parties.

ncc704077bc3.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the recognised tools of parliamentary control over the executive?
o: Judicial review by the Supreme Court
ncc704077bc3.x: Judicial review is a constitutional function of the judiciary, not a parliamentary device listed among the tools of legislative control over the executive.
ncc704077bc3.tq: Separate parliamentary control devices from mechanisms belonging to another constitutional organ.
xs: **Judicial review by the Supreme Court** is NOT a tool of parliamentary control — so option **(4)** is correct.
The recognised tools include **Question Hour**, **Zero Hour**, **half-an-hour discussion**, short-duration discussion, **calling attention**, adjournment, censure and no-confidence motions.
**Budget approval** and the **Motion of Thanks** are also listed tools, so options (1), (2) and (3) are all genuine devices.
xa: The **committee system** is also a tool: Government Assurances, Petitions, Subordinate Legislation, **PAC** and **Estimates**.
⚠ Order of Indian firsts: **1953** short-duration discussion – **1954** calling attention – **1962** Zero Hour.
**States** use the same devices plus estimates and public accounts committees.

n888fc066916.s: The Committee on Papers Laid on the Table primarily checks whether:
o: The estimates contain alternative taxation policies
Public sector undertakings follow commercial principles
Papers laid by ministers, other than statutory orders, comply with the relevant requirements
n888fc066916.x: The Committee on Papers Laid on the Table checks papers laid by ministers, other than statutory orders, for compliance.
n888fc066916.tq: Distinguish documentary scrutiny from assurance-tracking and financial scrutiny.
xs: It checks **papers laid by ministers, other than statutory orders**, for compliance — so option **(3)** is correct.
Commercial principles of PSUs = **CPU**; ministers' assurances = **Government Assurances** committee.
xa: **Committee on Subordinate Legislation**: whether rule-making (delegated) powers are properly exercised.
**Committee on Petitions** = **"Ombudsman"** of Parliament.
**Estimates Committee** = **"Continuous economy committee"**.

n9d725c0c05b.s: The reform area associated with the Ashok Dalwai Committee includes:
o: DBT for food and decentralised procurement under the PDS
Value addition and land leasing in the context of doubling farmers’ income
Inflation targeting and monetary policy independence
n9d725c0c05b.x: Ashok Dalwai’s reform area concerns doubling farmers’ income, including value addition and land leasing.
n9d725c0c05b.tq: Identify the policy package that belongs to the specified reform objective.
xs: **Ashok Dalwai** = **value addition and land leasing** for **doubling farmers' income** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**5+3+3+4** = Kasturirangan; **DBT for food** = Shanta Kumar; **inflation targeting** = Urjit Patel.
xa: **2nd ARC**: code of ethics, Right to Public Services, e-governance.
Kasturirangan's area is linked to **NEP 2020**.
Urjit Patel: inflation target **4% +/- 2%**.

n6b4119515f0.s: A Government Bill in Parliament ordinarily requires what period of notice before introduction, whereas a Private Member's Bill requires what period?
n6b4119515f0.x: A Government Bill requires seven days' notice, while a Private Member's Bill requires one month's notice before introduction.
n6b4119515f0.tq: Compare the two notice periods directly and watch for their reversal in the options.
xs: A Government Bill needs **7 days'** notice and a Private Member's Bill **1 month's** notice — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option (4) reverses the two; **14 days** is the Rajya Sabha's limit for returning a Money Bill, not a notice period.
xa: A Government Bill is introduced by a **minister**; a Private Member's Bill by any MP who is **not a minister**.
Rejection of a Government Bill signals **loss of confidence**; defeat of a private bill does not affect the government.
Only **14** private members' bills have become law, the last in **1970**.

n59b3767a915.s: A Government Bill is normally drafted by the:
o: Concerned department in association with the Law Ministry
n59b3767a915.x: A Government Bill is drafted by the concerned department with the Law Ministry; a Private Member's Bill is drafted by the member.
xa: Notice: Government Bill **7 days**; Private Member's Bill **1 month**.
The LS **Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions** classifies them and allots time.
Defeat of a Private Member's Bill has **no bearing** on the government.

n2e3a9d9e946.s: The last Private Member's Bill to become law was enacted in:
n2e3a9d9e946.x: Only 14 Private Members' Bills have become law, the last in 1970.
xa: A Private Member's Bill is introduced by any MP who is **not a minister**, with **1 month's** notice.
Its defeat does **not affect** the government.
The LS **Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions** classifies them and allots time.

n666aa5f5ac9.s: After an ordinary Bill is passed by one House, the other House may:
o: Return it only to the President
Pass it, amend it, reject it, or keep it pending for six months
Certify it as a Money Bill
n666aa5f5ac9.x: The second House may pass, amend or reject an ordinary Bill, or keep it pending for six months, potentially creating a deadlock.
n666aa5f5ac9.tq: Choose the option that lists the complete range of legislative responses rather than an exclusive power.
xs: The second House may **pass, amend, reject, or keep it pending for six months** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Only the **Speaker certifies** Money Bills, so option (3) is wrong.
xa: A deadlock leads to a **joint sitting** (**Art. 108**).
Joint sitting ground: not passed for **more than six months**, excluding prorogation/adjournment over **4 consecutive days**.
An ordinary bill may be introduced in **either House**.

n0a74fa6de76.s: Which one of the following is included within the scope of a Money Bill under Article 110(1) of the Constitution?
o: Fees for licences issued by local authorities
Taxes imposed by a municipality for local purposes
Imposition of fines by a criminal court
Imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax
n0a74fa6de76.x: A Money Bill may deal with the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of a tax. Fines, licence fees and local taxes are not, by themselves, matters of a Money Bill.
n0a74fa6de76.tq: Identify the exact constitutional subject instead of selecting nearby revenue-related terms.
xs: **Imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax** is an **Art. 110(1)** matter — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Fines/penalties**, **fees for licences**, and **taxes by local bodies for local purposes** are not money-bill matters — options (1), (2) and (3) are wrong.
xa: Other Art. 110(1) matters: **borrowing by GoI**; custody of the **Consolidated/Contingency Fund**.
Also: appropriation from the **CFI** and declaring expenditure **charged**.
A Money Bill deals **only** with Art. 110(1) matters.

n89eb477cfe5.s: A Money Bill can be introduced only:
o: In either House by any member with the Speaker's consent
In the Rajya Sabha by a minister on the President's recommendation
In the Lok Sabha by a private member with the Rajya Sabha's approval
In the Lok Sabha by a minister on the President's recommendation
n89eb477cfe5.x: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, only by a minister, and only on the President's recommendation.
xa: The Rajya Sabha must return it within **14 days** (**Art. 109**).
**No joint sitting** on a Money Bill.

n3c07f83dcfd.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the role of the Rajya Sabha on a Money Bill?
o: It must return the Bill within 14 days, with or without recommendations.
A deadlock over a Money Bill can be resolved through a joint sitting.
The Lok Sabha may accept or reject the Rajya Sabha's recommendations.
If not returned within 14 days, the Bill is deemed passed by both Houses.
n3c07f83dcfd.x: There is no joint sitting for a Money Bill (Article 109 governs it).
xa: The AP Legislative Council too can only recommend on money bills within **14 days**.
Monsoon Session 2026: the RS **returned several money bills** to the Lok Sabha.
Joint sittings are barred for **Money Bills** and **constitutional amendment bills**.

ne65194361ae.s: Which case upheld the Aadhaar Act as a Money Bill, while the Money-Bill issue was subsequently referred to a larger bench in another case?
ne65194361ae.x: The Aadhaar Act was upheld as a Money Bill in K.S. Puttaswamy (2018). The Money-Bill question was later referred to a seven-judge bench in Rojer Mathew (2019).
ne65194361ae.tq: Anchor the judicial developments by matching the case names with their years and sequence.
xs: **K.S. Puttaswamy (2018)** upheld the Aadhaar Act as a Money Bill; **Rojer Mathew (2019)** referred the question to a larger bench — so option **(1)** is correct.
Options (2) and (3) swap the years.
xa: Rojer Mathew referred it to a **7-judge** bench.
The **Speaker's** certificate on a Money Bill is **final** under **Art. 110(3)**.
A Money Bill deals **only** with **Art. 110(1)** matters.

n3ef95e177f6.s: Can a joint sitting be summoned for a Bill that has lapsed on dissolution of the Lok Sabha?
o: No, a joint sitting cannot be held for a lapsed Bill
Yes, within six months of dissolution
Yes, if the Rajya Sabha so requests
n3ef95e177f6.x: A joint sitting cannot be summoned for a Bill that has already lapsed; dissolution can end the Bill before the deadlock procedure operates.
xa: But a bill for which the President has **notified a joint sitting before dissolution** does not lapse.
Bills passed by both Houses pending **assent** do not lapse.
⚠ "Passed by LS but not yet taken up in RS does not lapse" is **false** (APPSC-G1 2024).

n433a2373bbe.s: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council, in relation to a Money Bill, can
o: refer it to a joint sitting within fourteen days
amend it finally within fourteen days
n433a2373bbe.x: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council can only make recommendations on a Money Bill within fourteen days. It cannot reject or amend the Bill finally.
n433a2373bbe.tq: Apply the special limitation on the Upper House of a State Legislature to a Money Bill.
xs: The AP Legislative Council can only **make recommendations within 14 days** on a money bill — so option **(1)** is correct.
It cannot reject, amend finally or seek a joint sitting.
xa: The Rajya Sabha's position is the same: return within **14 days** (**Art. 109**); LS may accept or reject.
**Andhra State Bill**: introduced **10 Aug 1953**; assent **14 Sep 1953**.
There is **no joint sitting** for Money Bills.

n9403271632d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about timelines for assent to State Bills?
o: The April 2025 Tamil Nadu Governor judgment laid down fixed timelines for Governors.
The November 2025 opinion upheld the deemed assent granted in the Tamil Nadu case.
In November 2025, a five-judge Bench advised on a Presidential Reference that courts cannot fix such timelines.
n9403271632d.x: The November 2025 advisory opinion held that courts cannot fix timelines or declare deemed assent, so it did not uphold the Tamil Nadu deemed assent.
xa: ⚠ APPCA dates the Tamil Nadu judgment to **2023**; the notes give **April 2025**.
Governor's options under **Art. 200**: assent, withhold, **return non-Money Bill**, reserve.
The President's options on reserved bills are under **Art. 201**.

nindian-polity-21-16.s: Under Article 110(2), a Bill is NOT a Money Bill merely because it deals with:
nindian-polity-21-16.x: A Bill only about fines or penalties is not a Money Bill; taxes, borrowing and the Consolidated Fund are Money Bill matters.
n: A Money Bill may be introduced only in the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 49-52]
A Money Bill requires the President’s prior recommendation for introduction. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 49-52]
A Money Bill includes provisions relating to taxes. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 49-52]
A Money Bill includes provisions relating to borrowings. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 49-52]
A Money Bill includes provisions relating to the custody of the Consolidated Fund of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 49-52]
A Money Bill includes provisions relating to withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 49-52]
A Bill dealing merely with fines or penalties is not a Money Bill. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 49-52]
A Money Bill requires the President’s recommendation before introduction. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 49-52]
xa: Also not money bills: **fees for licences or services**, taxes by **local bodies** for local purposes.
**Joint Sitting** is **not** possible for a Money Bill.

n0dfbd6cd4ba.s: In the Rajya Sabha, time for Private Members' Bills is allotted by its:
o: Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions
n0dfbd6cd4ba.x: The Rajya Sabha has no Committee on Private Members' Bills; its Business Advisory Committee allots the time.
xa: A **private member's bill** needs **1 month's** notice; a **government bill** **7 days'**.
Only **14** private members' bills have become law, the last in **1970**.
Defeat of a private member's bill has **no bearing** on the government.

n9b3d69c93d5.s: In the Lok Sabha, time for Private Members' Bills is allotted by the:
o: Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions
n9b3d69c93d5.x: The Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions allots the time; defeat of such a Bill has no bearing on the government.
xa: In the **Rajya Sabha**, the **Business Advisory Committee** allots time.
Notice for a Private Member's Bill: **1 month**.
Only **14** have become law, the last in **1970**.

n6ce1fac92b8.s: Under Article 110(3), the final decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill rests with the:
n6ce1fac92b8.x: The Speaker's decision is final, and the certificate is endorsed on the Bill sent to the Rajya Sabha and presented to the President.
xa: The Rajya Sabha must return it within **14 days**, with or without recommendations.
The President may assent or withhold but **cannot return** it.
The **Finance Bill** is usually certified a Money Bill.

n82b8b21117b.s: A Financial Bill-I under Article 117(1) can be introduced:
n82b8b21117b.x: It is introduced only in the Lok Sabha on the President's recommendation; the Rajya Sabha may amend or reject it.
xa: FB-I contains Art. 110 matters **partially, plus other matters**; no Speaker's certificate.
A **joint sitting** is allowed for FB-I.
Amendments **reducing/abolishing** a tax need no recommendation; those **increasing** a tax do.

n6a53e868919.s: The Bill that gives effect to the tax proposals of the Budget is the:
n6a53e868919.x: The Finance Bill gives effect to the Budget's tax proposals; every Money Bill is a Financial Bill, but not every Financial Bill is a Money Bill.
xa: The Finance Bill is **usually certified a Money Bill**.
⚠ Trap: some notes reverse the definitions.

n660eac43b34.s: In counting the six-month period for a joint sitting under Article 108, adjournments of more than ____ consecutive days are excluded.
n660eac43b34.x: Periods of prorogation and adjournment over four consecutive days are excluded; rejection or final disagreement on amendments are the other grounds.
xa: The President "**notifies his intention**" → neither House proceeds with the bill.
Decision by **simple majority of members present and voting** of both Houses together.
Quorum: **one-tenth** of total members.

n135a27f7527.s: At a joint sitting of the two Houses under Article 108, if both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha are absent, who presides?
o: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Vice-President)
The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
The senior-most member of the Lok Sabha
n135a27f7527.x: The order is: Speaker, then Deputy Speaker, then the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, and failing all three, a member chosen by those present. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (the Vice-President) does not preside over a joint sitting, the President only summons it, and there is no rule for the senior-most Lok Sabha member.
n135a27f7527.tq: Joint sitting chair: Speaker > Deputy Speaker > RS Deputy Chairman; never the VP/Chairman.
xs: With the Speaker and Deputy Speaker absent, the **Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha** presides — so option **(2)** is correct.
Order: **Speaker** → **Deputy Speaker** → **Deputy Chairman of RS** → a member chosen by those present.
⚠ The **VP/Chairman does not preside**; the President only **summons** it.
xa: Decision: **simple majority** of members present and voting.
Quorum: **one-tenth** of total members.
The President "notifies his intention"; neither House then proceeds with the bill.

nd97f4234d7a.s: On dissolution of the Lok Sabha, which of the following Bills lapses?
o: A Bill returned by the President for reconsideration
A Bill passed by both Houses and awaiting the President's assent
A Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha that the Lok Sabha has not passed
A Bill passed by the Lok Sabha but pending in the Rajya Sabha
nd97f4234d7a.x: A Bill passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha lapses; the other three survive dissolution.
xa: A bill with a joint sitting **notified before dissolution** also survives.
⚠ APPSC-G1 2024 treated "passed by LS but not yet taken up in RS does not lapse" as **false**.
A bill passed by RS, pending in LS lapses.

n4f5209a7def.s: A proposed amendment to a Financial Bill-I seeks to abolish an existing tax. Is the President's recommendation required for such an amendment?
o: No, because Financial Bills-I never require recommendation
Yes, because every amendment to a tax requires recommendation
No, an amendment reducing or abolishing a tax does not require such recommendation
Yes, but only when the Bill is pending in the Rajya Sabha
n4f5209a7def.x: An amendment reducing or abolishing a tax does not require the President's recommendation. An amendment increasing a tax requires such recommendation.
n4f5209a7def.tq: Distinguish the direction of the tax change; reducing or abolishing tax is treated differently from increasing it.
xs: No — an amendment **reducing or abolishing** a tax needs **no** President's recommendation — so option **(3)** is correct.
An amendment **increasing** a tax **does** need it — so option (1) "never" and option (2) "every amendment" are wrong.
xa: FB-I itself needs the President's recommendation **at introduction** and starts **only in LS**.
The RS can **amend or reject** FB-I.
FB-I can go to a **joint sitting**.

na4db53cf80e.s: If the President does not summon a joint sitting after a deadlock under Article 108, the Bill:
o: Automatically becomes law after six months
Is deemed to have been rejected by the Rajya Sabha only
Must be referred to the Supreme Court
na4db53cf80e.x: If the President does not summon the joint sitting, the Bill comes to an end. It does not automatically become law or receive judicial certification.
na4db53cf80e.tq: Apply the consequence of non-summoning instead of assuming that a deadlocked Bill remains permanently pending.
xs: If the President does not summon it, the bill **comes to an end** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-G2 2017).
It does not become law automatically — option (1) is wrong.
xa: The joint sitting is **summoned by the President**.
Presided by the **Speaker** → Deputy Speaker → **Deputy Chairman of RS**.
A joint sitting **cannot be summoned** for a bill that has already lapsed.

n5e7991c92b5.s: A decision at a joint sitting is taken by:
o: A unanimous vote of the presiding officers of both Houses
A simple majority of members present and voting in both Houses together
A special majority of the total membership of both Houses
A two-thirds majority of members present and voting in each House separately
n5e7991c92b5.x: The Bill is decided by a simple majority of the members of both Houses present and voting together at the joint sitting.
n5e7991c92b5.tq: Distinguish the voting threshold and the combined body voting from special-majority procedures.
xs: Decided by a **simple majority of members present and voting** of both Houses together — so option **(2)** is correct.
No two-thirds or special majority, and the Houses do not vote separately.
xa: Quorum: **one-tenth** of total members.
⚠ The **VP/Chairman does not preside**; the Speaker does.
**Money bills** and **constitutional amendment bills** are excluded.

nf2809e0f2a6.s: Which one of the following sets contains only the categories of Bills excluded from a joint sitting?
o: Private Members' Bills and Government Bills
Money Bills and Constitution Amendment Bills
nf2809e0f2a6.x: Money Bills and Constitution Amendment Bills cannot be referred to a joint sitting. Financial Bills of types I and II can go to a joint sitting.
nf2809e0f2a6.tq: Identify the two express exclusions and avoid treating every financial measure as excluded.
xs: **Money Bills and Constitution Amendment Bills** are excluded from a joint sitting — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Financial bills (I) and (II)** and ordinary bills can go to a joint sitting.
xa: Joint sitting is under **Art. 108**.
Decision by **simple majority** of members present and voting.

n44dcd1f263e.s: The joint sitting of Parliament in 2002 was held on the:
n44dcd1f263e.x: Joint sittings were held in 1961 (Dowry Prohibition), 1978 (Banking Service Commission Repeal) and 2002 (Prevention of Terrorism).
xa: ⚠ **1961 – 1978 – 2002** = Dowry – Banking Service Commission – POTA.
The joint sitting is **presided by the Speaker**.
Grounds: rejection, final disagreement on amendments, or delay of **more than six months**.

n436a143bf0f.s: A joint sitting of Parliament has already been notified before the dissolution of the Lok Sabha. What is the position of the bill concerned?
o: It does not lapse merely because of dissolution
It must be returned to the Rajya Sabha for fresh introduction
It becomes a Money Bill automatically
n436a143bf0f.x: A bill for which a joint sitting has been notified before dissolution does not lapse merely on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
n436a143bf0f.tq: Look for the specific exception to the general rule that dissolution causes bills to lapse.
xs: It **does not lapse** merely because of dissolution — so option **(2)** is correct.
The President had **notified a joint sitting before dissolution**.
xa: A joint sitting **cannot** be summoned for a bill that has already lapsed.
Bills passed by both Houses pending **assent** also do not lapse.
The joint sitting would be presided over by the **Speaker**.
