xa: After **2019**, President's Rule ran under the **Reorganisation Act** until **Oct 2024**.
Under Art 356 generally: **6 months** at a time, maximum **3 years**.
**Art. 360** is the **Financial Emergency**, not J&K Governor's Rule.

n37ba9630dc8.s: President's Rule was first imposed in the Telugu region in Andhra State during:
n37ba9630dc8.x: Andhra State came under President's Rule in 1954-55. 1951 is the first-ever instance (Punjab); 1973 was the Jai Andhra spell in Andhra Pradesh; 1984 was the Nadendla Bhaskara Rao episode, not President's Rule.
n37ba9630dc8.tq: Andhra State PR = 1954-55; AP 1973 Jai Andhra.
xs: **Andhra State** had President's Rule in **1954-55** — option **(2)** is correct.
**1951** was the first-ever use (**Punjab**); **1973** was the **Jai Andhra** spell in AP.
xa: **C.M. Trivedi** was the first Governor of **Andhra State (1953)** and of **Andhra Pradesh (1956)**.
**2020**: the AP High Court "**breakdown**" episode — the Supreme Court **stayed** it.
⚠ **Punjab** = first use (**1951**); **Kerala** = first dismissal (**1959**).

n7a297da7f96.s: Which case held that an Assembly should not be dissolved before Parliament approves a proclamation under Article 356?
n7a297da7f96.x: Bommai protected the Assembly pending parliamentary approval, allowed restoration of a displaced ministry and treated secularism as a basic feature.
xa: Bommai: proclamations **judicially reviewable**; Centre must show **relevant material**.
Bommai upheld the **MP, Rajasthan, HP** dismissals after **Ayodhya (Dec 1992)**.
**Punchhi** wanted the **Bommai guidelines** written into **Art 356**.

n186a5e1f865.s: The Sarkaria Commission recommended that Article 356 be used:
o: As the first response to political instability
n186a5e1f865.x: Sarkaria recommended Article 356 only as a last resort, along with a mandatory floor test and a politically neutral outsider as Governor.
xa: The outsider should be **not a recent active politician** and chosen **after consulting the CM**.
⚠ **Punchhi** = **localised emergency** and **fixed tenure**; **Sarkaria** = **outsider** + **last resort**.
**Rameshwar Prasad** cited Sarkaria on misuse of **Art. 356 reports**.

n75424f7b42e.s: The First ARC study team on Centre-State relations recommended an Inter-State Council under Article:
n75424f7b42e.x: The study team recommended an Inter-State Council under Article 263, along with non-partisan Governors, delegation of powers and more resources for States.
xa: It also proposed deployment of **central armed forces** in States, on their request or otherwise.
The study team was headed by **Setalvad** (**1969**).
The First ARC (**1966**) was chaired by **Morarji Desai**, later **K. Hanumanthaiya**.

n54a0567c6cc.s: Who became Governor of Andhra Pradesh in February 2023?
n54a0567c6cc.x: S. Abdul Nazeer has been Governor of Andhra Pradesh since February 2023.
xa: AP Governors since 2014: **E.S.L. Narasimhan**, **Biswabhusan Harichandan**, **S. Abdul Nazeer**.
**K. Pawan Kalyan** (**Jana Sena**) is Deputy CM (**2026**).
The **2019-24** government had **five** Deputy CMs.

n471397685e8.s: Who was the first Governor of Andhra State (1953) and of Andhra Pradesh (1956)?
n471397685e8.x: C.M. Trivedi was the first Governor of both Andhra State (1953) and Andhra Pradesh (1956). E.S.L. Narasimhan was the common Governor of AP and Telangana (2014-19); Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was the first CM and K.V. Ranga Reddy the Deputy CM of united AP.
xs: **C.M. Trivedi** was the first Governor of **Andhra State (1953)** and of **Andhra Pradesh (1956)** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** was the first CM and **K.V. Ranga Reddy** the Deputy CM of united AP; **E.S.L. Narasimhan** was common Governor **2014-19**.
xa: **Andhra State** had President's Rule in **1954-55**.
AP's present Governor: **S. Abdul Nazeer** (from **Feb 2023**).
First woman Governor: **Sarojini Naidu** (UP, **1947**).

n286c6774973.s: Which of the following correctly identifies an Andhra Pradesh-specific Article 356-related reference?
o: President’s Rule in 1984 during the Telugu Desam Party formation and a 2019 Supreme Court dissolution
President’s Rule in 1992 following the dissolution of the Tamil Nadu Assembly
President’s Rule in 1973 during the Jai Andhra movement and the 2020 High Court ‘breakdown’ episode
Governor’s Rule in 1973 under Section 92 of the J&K Constitution
n286c6774973.x: The Andhra Pradesh references are President’s Rule in 1973 during the Jai Andhra movement and the 2020 Andhra Pradesh High Court episode concerning constitutional breakdown.
n286c6774973.tq: Separate the State-specific examples from similarly worded events in Jammu and Kashmir and other States.
xs: AP angle: **President's Rule in 1973** (**Jai Andhra**) and the **2020 AP High Court "breakdown"** episode — option **(3)** is correct.
The Supreme Court **stayed** the AP High Court episode.
xa: **Andhra State** had President's Rule earlier, in **1954-55**.
**Sec 92** Governor's Rule belongs to the former **J&K**, not AP.
Never used in **Telangana** or **Chhattisgarh**.

nindian-polity-74-14.s: Who may withdraw an ordinance, and when?
o: Only Parliament may withdraw it after six weeks.
Only the State Legislature may withdraw it.
Neither the President nor the Governor may withdraw it once issued.
The President or Governor may withdraw it at any time, as applicable.
nindian-polity-74-14.x: The President or the Governor can withdraw their ordinance at any time (Article 123(2)(b) / 213(2)(b)).
nindian-polity-74-14.tq: Recall that withdrawal is open at any time.
n: The President can withdraw an ordinance at any time. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #74 · pp 201-204]
The Governor can withdraw an ordinance at any time. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #74 · pp 201-204]
The statement that the President cannot repeal or withdraw an ordinance once issued is false. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #74 · pp 201-204]
The President can withdraw an ordinance at any time under Article 123(2)(b). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #74 · pp 201-204]
xs: **The President or Governor may withdraw** an ordinance **at any time**, as applicable — so option **(4)** is correct.
For the President this is **Article 123(2)(b)**; the Governor also may withdraw **any time**.
Option (1) confuses withdrawal with **lapse** — an ordinance ceases **six weeks** after the legislature **reassembles**.
xa: President's ordinances need approval by **Parliament**; Governor's by the **State Legislature**.
President: **Union and Concurrent List**; Governor: **State and Concurrent List**.
Governor's ordinance is issued during **recess** under **Article 213**.

n0888a1cd35c.s: Which of the following is a constitutional duty of the Chief Minister under Article 167?
o: Reserving Bills for the consideration of the President
Communicating Cabinet decisions to the Governor
n0888a1cd35c.x: Under Article 167, the Chief Minister must communicate the decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor and furnish information the Governor seeks.
xa: Seeking information from the CM (**Art. 167**) is a **constitutional discretion** of the Governor.
**Loss of majority:** CM must **resign or be dismissed**.
Governors are appointed by the **President** (**Art. 155**), not by the CM.

ncf83cefaf26.s: In the Tamil Nadu 2026 hung Assembly situation, the Governor invited C. Joseph Vijay after receiving letters of support from 120 members, following which convention?
o: Appointment of the leader of the single largest party without a floor test
Appointment by the President under Article 356
Selection by the Legislative Council under Article 169
The Sarkaria-Punchhi order, followed by an early floor test
ncf83cefaf26.x: The Governor invited C. Joseph Vijay on the basis of 120 letters of support, following the Sarkaria-Punchhi order and requiring an early floor test.
ncf83cefaf26.tq: Apply the convention for government formation in a hung Assembly.
xs: The Governor followed the **Sarkaria-Punchhi order**, with an **early floor test** — option **(4)** is correct.
**C. Joseph Vijay** was invited under **Art. 164** on **120** letters of support and sworn in as CM.
xa: **TVK** = single largest party with **108** seats, **10 short**.
**Sarkaria (1987)** and **Punchhi (2010)** Commissions give the guidelines.
Hung Assembly appointment = **situational discretion**.

n4d1d15c9437.s: The Venkatachaliah Commission recommended that the Governor should be appointed by a committee consisting of:
o: The Prime Minister, Union Home Minister, Lok Sabha Speaker and the State Chief Minister
The President, Vice-President, Chief Justice of India and the State Chief Minister
The Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India, Governor and State Speaker
The Union Home Minister, Rajya Sabha Chairman, State Governor and Chief Minister
n4d1d15c9437.x: The recommended committee comprised the Prime Minister, Union Home Minister, Lok Sabha Speaker and the Chief Minister of the State concerned.
n4d1d15c9437.tq: Check each appointing authority rather than relying on a familiar constitutional appointment pattern.
xs: **NCRWC (Venkatachaliah)** proposed a committee of the **Prime Minister, Union Home Minister, Lok Sabha Speaker and the State Chief Minister** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **President, Vice-President** or **Chief Justice of India** were not part of the proposed committee.
xa: NCRWC worked during **2000-02**; it suggested assent within about **4 months**.
**Sarkaria:** an **outsider**, chosen **after consulting the CM**.
**First ARC:** persons of long experience and a **non-partisan** attitude.

n15cde251e18.s: The Punchhi Commission recommended a localised emergency in a district for up to:
n15cde251e18.x: Punchhi recommended a localised district emergency for up to three months, codification of Bommai guidelines and fixed tenure for Governors.
xa: Punchhi was set up in **2007** and reported in **2010**.
It also urged **time-bound disposal of bills** and no misuse of discretion.
⚠ **Sarkaria** = **outsider** + Art. 356 as **last resort**.

n76a8d818afa.s: The Rajamannar Committee was constituted in:
n76a8d818afa.x: The Rajamannar Committee was constituted in 1969, before Sarkaria (1983), NCRWC (2000) and Punchhi (2007).
xa: **Sarkaria** reported in **1988**; **Punchhi** in **2010**.
The **First ARC** came earlier, in **1966**.
The **Kurian Joseph Committee (TN, 2026)** proposes a **new Schedule** on Governor's discretion.

n6ba4f81330e.s: To which of the following bodies is the Governor constitutionally answerable in the ordinary discharge of the office?
o: The Council of Ministers of the State alone
n6ba4f81330e.x: The Governor is not answerable to either House of Parliament, to the State Legislature, or to the State Council of Ministers.
n6ba4f81330e.tq: Use the institutional-accountability trap and select the option covering all three excluded bodies.
xs: The Governor is **not answerable** to either House of Parliament, the state legislature, or the **Council of Ministers** — **None of the above**, option **(4)**.
This was asked as a PYQ in **2019**.
xa: **Art. 361:** not answerable to any **court** for official acts.
He holds office **during the pleasure of the President** (**Art. 156**).
"Pleasure of the President" makes the office **structurally dependent on the Centre**.

n6cd51501bd0.s: In which of the following circumstances does the Governor require instructions from the President before promulgating an ordinance?
o: Whenever the State Legislature has two Houses
When a Bill containing the same provisions would require the President's prior sanction or would have to be reserved for his consideration
Whenever the ordinance concerns any State List subject
Whenever the ordinance concerns any Concurrent List subject
n6cd51501bd0.x: The Governor requires the President's instructions where a Bill containing the same provisions would require prior sanction of the President or would have to be reserved for his consideration.
n6cd51501bd0.tq: Apply the prior-sanction test rather than treating every State or Concurrent List subject alike.
xs: The Governor needs **President's instructions** when a bill with the same provisions would need the President's **prior sanction** or would have to be **reserved** — option **(2)** is correct.
The mere subject (**State** or **Concurrent List**) or having **two Houses** does not trigger it.
xa: The **President's** ordinance (**Art. 123**) needs no such prior instruction.
Governor's ordinance under **Art. 213** lapses **6 weeks** after the legislature reassembles.
Prior sanction example: bills restricting **inter-state trade** — **Art. 304(b)**.

n7238bacfc86.s: In which of the following groups of States is the appointment of a Minister for Tribal Welfare mandatory?
o: Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal
Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra and Odisha
Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh
n7238bacfc86.x: A Minister for Tribal Welfare is mandatory in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha. Bihar was removed from the list by the 94th Amendment Act, 2006.
n7238bacfc86.tq: Start with the sure State names and identify the set containing no substituted State.
xs: A **Minister for Tribal Welfare** is mandatory in **Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Bihar** was dropped by the **94th Amendment, 2006**, so options (1) and (4) are wrong.
xa: The minister may also handle **SC and backward class** welfare.
⚠ **94th** (2006) = Bihar dropped; **91st** (2003) = **15%** cap and minimum **12**.
**Art. 164(1):** the CM is appointed by the **Governor**.

na7550149757.s: Who was the common Governor of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana during the period 2014 to July 2019?
na7550149757.x: E.S.L. Narasimhan served as the common Governor of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana from 2014 to July 2019.
na7550149757.tq: Use the tenure and office combination to distinguish the common Governor from later separate Governors.
xs: **E.S.L. Narasimhan** was the **common Governor** of AP and Telangana, **2014 to July 2019** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Biswabhusan Harichandan** followed as AP's separate Governor; **C.M. Trivedi** was the first Governor (**1953/1956**); **S. Abdul Nazeer** is the present one.
xa: A common Governor is possible under the **7th Amendment Act, 1956**.
Cost of a common Governor is shared among states as the **President** decides.
Under **Sec. 8**, he had special responsibility for **law and order** in **Hyderabad**.

nindian-polity-10-6.s: Who was the first woman Chief Minister in India?
nindian-polity-10-6.x: Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister; E.M.S. Namboodiripad was the first non-Congress Chief Minister.
n: The oath of the Chief Minister is administered by the Governor. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 27-29]
Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 27-29]
E. M. S. Namboodiripad was the first non-Congress Chief Minister. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 27-29]
The Chief Minister of Delhi is appointed by the President under Article 239AA. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 27-29]
The Chief Minister of Puducherry is appointed by the President under Article 239AA. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 27-29]
Sucheta Kripalani was the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 27-29]
E. M. S. Namboodiripad became Chief Minister of Kerala in 1957. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 27-29]
xa: The CM's **resignation** is addressed to the **Governor**.
First CM of united AP: **Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy**; first cabinet of **13** ministers.
First Speaker of the united AP Assembly: **Nallapati Venkata Ramaiah**.

nf68b382a5ce.s: Under which Article of the Constitution is the Chief Minister of a State appointed by the Governor?
nf68b382a5ce.x: Article 164(1) provides that the Governor appoints the Chief Minister. Article 163(1) concerns aid and advice, Article 167 the CM's duties towards the Governor, and Article 174 sessions of the legislature.
xs: The Governor appoints the CM under **Article 164(1)** — option **(2)** (APPSC-GS **2021**).
**Art. 167** is about the **CM's duties towards the Governor**, not appointment.
xa: ⚠ Clauses of **Art. 164**: (1) appointment, (2) **collective responsibility**, (3) **oath**, (4) **6 months** rule, (5) **salaries**.
Usually the **leader of the majority party** is appointed.
In a **hung Assembly** the Governor uses discretion.

n1733e5f37f9.s: The term of office of the Chief Minister is:
n1733e5f37f9.x: The Constitution does not fix the Chief Minister's term.
xa: The CM is the **chief link** between Governor and Council (**Art. 167**).
The CM stays only while he has the **Assembly's confidence**.

nc1855be2546.s: Under Article 167, who is the chief link between the Governor and the State Council of Ministers?
nc1855be2546.x: Article 167 makes the Chief Minister the link, communicating Council decisions to the Governor and placing matters before the Council when required.
xa: Seeking information under **Art. 167** is a **constitutional discretion** of the Governor.
CM mirrors the **PM** (**Arts. 74-75**).

ne74a4fe04b3.s: Under Article 164(2), the State Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the:
o: Both Houses of the State Legislature
ne74a4fe04b3.x: Article 164(2) makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly alone. Ministers hold office at the Governor's pleasure but are not collectively responsible to him; the Council is not responsible to the Legislative Council.
xs: The State Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the **Legislative Assembly** — option **(3)**.
This is **Art. 164(2)** (BPSC **2022**); not to the Governor or the Legislative Council.
xa: The CM stays only while he has the **Assembly's confidence**.
**Art. 164(3)**: oath by the **Governor**; **Art. 164(5)**: salaries by the **state legislature**.
The Union parallel lies in **Arts. 74-75**.

n628d720ccfa.s: The office of Deputy Chief Minister in a State is:
o: A political arrangement not specifically mentioned in the Constitution
n628d720ccfa.x: The Constitution does not specifically mention the office; the incumbent is sworn in as a minister and the post is a political arrangement.
xa: Precedence: ranks with **Union Ministers of State** at **No. 10**.
Likewise, a State has **no counterpart of the Vice-President**.

n3d9a2253c9f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sarkaria and Punchhi order of preference for inviting a group to form the government in a hung Assembly?
o: A post-poll coalition comes before the single largest party with support
A post-poll alliance with outside support comes last
A pre-poll alliance gets first preference
The single largest party with support of others comes second
n3d9a2253c9f.x: The order is pre-poll alliance, single largest party with support, post-poll coalition, then post-poll alliance with outside support.
xa: The Constitution gives **no criteria** for a hung Assembly — it is the Governor's discretion.
An **early floor test** follows (May **2026**).

nfa540617c99.s: A Chief Minister continues in office constitutionally so long as he or she enjoys the confidence of the
nfa540617c99.x: The Chief Minister must retain the confidence of the Legislative Assembly. Loss of majority may lead to resignation or dismissal of the government after the position is established.
nfa540617c99.tq: Distinguish the formal pleasure of the Governor from the actual requirement of legislative confidence.
xs: The CM stays in office only while he has the **confidence of the Legislative Assembly** — option **(3)**.
If he loses it, the Governor can **ask him to resign** or **dismiss** the government.
A literal "**pleasure**" reading (Governor alone) was cautioned against in the **Constituent Assembly**.
xa: Collective responsibility is to the **Legislative Assembly** (**Art. 164(2)**).
The CM's **term is not fixed**.
The CM can **advise dissolution** of the Assembly.

n7e1687d7d8c.s: Seeking information from the Chief Minister under Article 167 is regarded as a constitutional discretion of the
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
n7e1687d7d8c.x: Under Article 167, the Governor can call on the Chief Minister for information about administration and legislative proposals, and this is a constitutional discretion of the Governor. The CM is the chief link between the Governor and the Council of Ministers.
n7e1687d7d8c.tq: Match the information-seeking discretion with the constitutional office to which the duty is addressed.
xs: Seeking information under **Art. 167** is a constitutional discretion of the **Governor** — option **(1)**.
The CM must **communicate** all Council decisions on administration and legislative proposals to him.
xa: The CM is the **chief link** between Governor and Council.
The Governor can require a single minister's decision to be **placed before the Council**.
By contrast, choosing a CM in a **hung Assembly** is discretion without constitutional criteria.

n4ed8d98fd41.s: The first Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of united Andhra Pradesh was
n4ed8d98fd41.x: Nallapati Venkata Ramaiah was the first Speaker of the united Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.
n4ed8d98fd41.tq: Distinguish the first presiding officer of the Assembly from the first Chief Minister of the State.
xs: **Nallapati Venkata Ramaiah** was the first Speaker of the united AP Assembly — option **(3)**.
**Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy** was the first **CM** of united AP, not the Speaker.
xa: Sanjeeva Reddy's first cabinet had **13** ministers (**1956-60**).
First CM of residuary AP (**2014**): **N. Chandrababu Naidu**.

n6bb8fbc0908.s: Under the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025, a PM, CM or Minister in custody for 30 consecutive days for an offence punishable with five years or more is removed on the:
n6bb8fbc0908.x: The Bill (amending Articles 75, 164 and 239AA) provides removal on the 31st day after 30 consecutive days in custody.
xa: **West Bengal (May 2026)**: a defeated CM said she would not resign; BJP won **207/294**.
**NITI Aayog**: the **11th** Governing Council saw all **28** CMs present for the first time.
The CM mirrors the PM (**Arts. 74-75**); the state has no counterpart of the **Vice-President**.

ncdf457dba32.s: The Legislative Assembly of Andhra Pradesh has 175 seats. On the stated maximum-size rule for a State Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, the maximum number of ministers would be:
ncdf457dba32.x: The stated maximum is 15 percent of the Assembly strength. Fifteen percent of 175 is 26.25, giving a maximum of 26 ministers when expressed as the applicable whole-number limit.
ncdf457dba32.tq: Apply the percentage limit to the Assembly strength and use the applicable whole-number maximum.
xs: For AP's **175**-seat Assembly, the maximum Council of Ministers is **26** — option **(2)**.
The cap is a share of **Assembly strength**, which works out to **26** for **175** seats; options (1), (3) and (4) do not match it.
xa: The **Governor appoints** the CM, and ministers on the CM's advice; the CM **recommends portfolios**.
The CM **can drop ministers**.
United AP's first cabinet (**1956**) had **13** ministers.

n5958aa9e23c.s: The membership of a State Legislative Council cannot exceed ____ of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly.
n5958aa9e23c.x: A Council cannot exceed one-third of the Assembly's strength nor be less than 40; Parliament fixes its actual strength.
xa: Creation/abolition by **Art. 169**: Assembly special majority + Parliament law.
AP Assembly has **175** seats.
Council is a **permanent body**.

n59723214fd2.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the tenure of the State Legislative Council?
o: It is a permanent body, and one-sixth of its members retire every year.
It is a permanent body, and one-third of its members retire every second year.
It is dissolved every five years along with the Assembly.
It has a fixed tenure of six years as a whole House.
n59723214fd2.x: The Legislative Council is a permanent House. One-third of its members retire every second year, while each member has a six-year term.
n59723214fd2.tq: Separate the tenure of an individual member from the continuity of the House.
xs: The Council is a **permanent body**; **one-third** of members retire **every second year** — option **(2)**.
Each member serves **6 years**; the Council itself is **not dissolved**, unlike the Assembly's **5**-year term.
xa: Minimum age: **30** (**Art. 173**).
Size: min **40**, max **1/3** of the Assembly.
Its existence depends on the **will of the Assembly** (**Art. 169**).

nae26c7c997d.s: In a State Legislature, the certificate that a Bill is a Money Bill is issued by the
nae26c7c997d.x: Under Article 199(3), the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly certifies whether a Bill is a Money Bill.
nae26c7c997d.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to the certification power.
xs: The **Speaker of the Legislative Assembly** certifies a Money Bill — option **(1)**.
His decision is **final** (**Art. 199(3)**).
A Money Bill is **introduced only in the Assembly** on the **Governor's recommendation** — the Governor recommends, not certifies.
xa: Council must return a Money Bill within **14 days**; cannot reject or amend.
Speaker also decides **Tenth Schedule** disqualification.
Speaker has a **casting vote** on a tie (**Art. 189**).

n0491ffdf31e.s: The Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly can be removed by a resolution of a majority of all the then members after a notice of:
n0491ffdf31e.x: Under Article 179, removal requires a resolution by a majority of all the then members after fourteen days' notice.
xa: During removal (**Art. 181**) he **does not preside**.
The **Deputy Speaker** resigns to the Speaker.
Council: **Chairman** resigns to the **Deputy Chairman**.

ndd39d7e8a40.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly?
o: The Speaker addresses the resignation to the Governor
The Speaker can be removed by a majority of all the then members after 14 days' notice
On dissolution, the Speaker continues until just before the new Assembly first meets
The Deputy Speaker acts with full powers when the Speaker's office is vacant
ndd39d7e8a40.x: Under Article 179 the Speaker resigns by writing to the Deputy Speaker, not the Governor.
xa: **Deputy Speaker** post vacant in **8** states; **Jharkhand** had none for **21 years**.
Removal: **majority of all the then members**, **14 days' notice**.

n4c30edd659c.s: In a bicameral State Legislature, the presiding officers are:
o: Speaker and Deputy Speaker – Assembly; Chairman and Deputy Chairman – Council
n4c30edd659c.x: The Legislative Assembly has a Speaker and Deputy Speaker, while the Legislative Council has a Chairman and Deputy Chairman.
xa: Council: the **Chairman** resigns to the **Deputy Chairman**.
Assembly: the **Speaker** resigns to the **Deputy Speaker**.
**Telangana Council** Chairman = **Gutha Sukender Reddy**.

n0f5dbcff789.s: Under Article 190(3)(b), the resignation of a member of a State Legislative Assembly takes effect only when—
o: It is accepted by the Speaker
It is accepted by the Governor
It is published in the official gazette
It is accepted by the Election Commission
n0f5dbcff789.x: The resignation of an MLA takes effect only upon acceptance by the Speaker. For a member of the Legislative Council, acceptance is by the Chairman.
n0f5dbcff789.tq: Match the resignation with the presiding officer of the concerned House.
xs: An MLA's resignation takes effect only on **acceptance by the Speaker** — option **(1)**.
For a member of the Council, the **Chairman** accepts it (**Art. 190(3)(b)**).
xa: **Art. 190(4)**: seat vacated after **60 days'** absence without permission.
The **Speaker** himself resigns to the **Deputy Speaker**.
Disqualification under **Art. 191** is decided by the **Governor** on the **EC's opinion**.

n212f6a264d2.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Legislative Assembly from the Legislative Council in relation to a Money Bill?
o: A Money Bill may originate in either House, but the Council has the final decision.
The Council may reject a Money Bill if two-thirds of its members so decide.
A Money Bill can originate only in the Council on the Governor's recommendation.
A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Assembly, and the Council may make recommendations within 14 days.
n212f6a264d2.x: A Money Bill is introduced only in the Legislative Assembly on the Governor's recommendation. The Council can only recommend changes and must return it within 14 days; it cannot reject or amend it.
n212f6a264d2.tq: Identify who introduces, who recommends and who has the final word.
xs: A Money Bill is introduced **only in the Assembly**; the Council may only **recommend** within **14 days** — option **(4)**.
It is introduced by a minister on the **Governor's recommendation** (**Art. 207**).
The Council **cannot reject or amend** it (**Art. 198**); its recommendations may be rejected.
xa: The **Speaker** certifies a Money Bill (**Art. 199(3)**).
⚠ Council delay: **14 days** (Money Bill); **3 months** + **1 month** (ordinary Bill).
Demands for grants are **voted only in the Assembly**.

n8fee094ddc9.s: A Bill originating in the Legislative Council and rejected by the Legislative Assembly:
o: Is referred to a joint sitting
Returns to the Council for reconsideration
n8fee094ddc9.x: Such a Bill ends; the Council has no second chance and State Legislatures have no joint sitting.
xa: For Assembly Bills, the Council can delay **3 months** then **1 month**.
The Council has **no role in ratifying** constitutional amendments.

na758d0f88e0.s: MLAs elect what fraction of the members of a State Legislative Council?
na758d0f88e0.x: MLAs elect one-third of the Council's members; they also vote in Presidential and Rajya Sabha elections.
xa: ⚠ **Vice-President**: **No** — only MPs vote (APPCA **2026**).
Council members are elected by **PR-STV**.

n81ddf2fa71a.s: The Governor's right to address and send messages to the House or Houses of the State Legislature is under Article:
n81ddf2fa71a.x: Article 175 covers the address and messages; 174 deals with sessions and dissolution and 176 with the special address.
xa: Art. 174 rule: no more than **6 months** between sittings.
**Art. 172** = duration (**5 years**); **Art. 173** = qualifications (**25 / 30**).

na626b604ee5.s: Which Article bars discussion in the State Legislature of the conduct of a High Court judge in the discharge of duties?
na626b604ee5.x: Article 211 bars such discussion; Article 208 covers rules of procedure and Article 212 bars courts inquiring into proceedings.
xa: **Art. 194** = **privileges** of MLAs and committees.
**Art. 210** = language: **Hindi/English** or the state's official language.
**Art. 187** = **secretariat** of the state legislature.

nec3214bae40.s: Who is the Chairman of the Telangana Legislative Council?
nec3214bae40.x: Gutha Sukender Reddy is the Council Chairman; Gaddam Prasad Kumar is the Speaker of the Assembly.
xa: ⚠ Assembly = **Speaker**; Council = **Chairman**.
**Telangana** Assembly has **119** seats and is one of **six states** with a Council.
Council: the **Chairman** resigns to the **Deputy Chairman**.

ndb5b4ef956b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about State Legislative Councils?
o: A Council gives a place to experts who cannot face elections
Its existence depends on the ruling party in the Assembly, as in Andhra Pradesh
A Council can permanently veto an ordinary Bill passed by the Assembly
ndb5b4ef956b.x: The Council has only a delaying power (3 months, then 1 month), after which the Assembly's will prevails.
xa: Criticism: a costly "**delaying chamber**".
Under **Art. 169** its existence depends on the **will of the Assembly**.
Money Bill: Council must return it within **14 days**.

nindian-polity-62-17.s: The Legislative Council must return a State Money Bill with its recommendations within:
nindian-polity-62-17.x: The Council must return a Money Bill within 14 days, failing which it is deemed passed by both Houses.
n: The Legislative Council receives a Money Bill only for recommendations. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The Legislative Council must return a Money Bill within 14 days. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
A Money Bill is deemed to have been passed upon expiry of 14 days if the Legislative Council does not return it. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
xa: The Council **cannot amend or reject** a Money Bill; the Assembly has **final authority** (**Art. 198**).
Money Bills are introduced **only in the Assembly**, on the **Governor's prior recommendation** (**Article 207**).
⚠ Council delay: **14 days** (Money Bill); **3 months** + **1 month** (ordinary bill).

nindian-polity-62-18.s: On first passage, the Legislative Council can delay an ordinary Bill passed by the Assembly for a maximum of:
nindian-polity-62-18.x: The Council can delay an ordinary Bill three months, then one month after it is repassed; it has no veto.
n: The Legislative Council has no veto power over ordinary bills. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The Legislative Council cannot permanently block legislation passed by the Legislative Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The Legislative Council can delay an ordinary bill for a maximum of 3 months after its first passage. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The Legislative Council can delay a re-passed ordinary bill for a maximum of 1 month. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The Legislative Assembly can re-pass an ordinary bill after its first passage through the Legislative Council. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
xa: The Assembly is the **originating and overriding** chamber (**Article 197**).
A bill **originating in the Council** and rejected by the Assembly **ends**.
There is **no joint sitting** in states, unlike Parliament (**Art. 108**).

nindian-polity-60-5.s: The minimum age for membership of a State Legislative Council is:
nindian-polity-60-5.x: The minimum age is 30 for the Council (Article 171) and 25 for the Assembly (Article 170).
n: The Constitutional basis of the Legislative Assembly is Article 170. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The Constitutional basis of the Legislative Council is Article 171. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The minimum age for membership of the Legislative Assembly is 25 years under Article 173. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The minimum age for membership of the Legislative Council is 30 years under Article 173. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
xa: Assembly: maximum **500**, minimum **60**.
Council: maximum **one-third** of the Assembly, minimum **40**.
**Rajya Sabha** minimum age is also **30**.

nindian-polity-60-7.s: The term of a member of a State Legislative Council is:
nindian-polity-60-7.x: Council members serve six years, with one-third retiring every two years; the Council is a permanent body.
n: The normal term of the Legislative Assembly is five years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The Legislative Council is a permanent body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
One-third of the Legislative Council members retire every two years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The term of a Legislative Council member is six years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
xa: The Council **cannot be dissolved**, not even on the Governor's recommendation.
The **Rajya Sabha** follows the same pattern: **six** years, one-third retire every **two** years.
The Council is called the **Upper House** / **House of Elders**.

nindian-polity-40-37.s: The Legislative Council's power to delay ordinary Bills is provided under Article:
nindian-polity-40-37.x: Article 197 covers the Council's delay of ordinary Bills; 176 is the Governor's address and 207 the recommendation for Money Bills.
n: The Governor addresses the Legislative Assembly at the commencement of the first session after each general election under Article 176. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The Governor addresses the Legislative Assembly at the first session of each year under Article 176. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
Introduction of a Money Bill requires the Governor's prior recommendation under Article 207. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The Legislative Council can delay an ordinary Bill for three months on the first occasion under Article 197. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The Legislative Council can delay an ordinary Bill for one month on the second occasion under Article 197. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The Governor can reserve a Bill for the President's consideration under Articles 200 and 201. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
xa: **Article 175** = optional address/messages; **176** = **mandatory** address at the first session of the year.
**Article 200** = Governor's assent / reservation.
**Articles 198-199** = State Money Bills.

nindian-polity-40-56.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about a State Money Bill?
o: The Speaker's certification of a Money Bill is final
The Legislative Council may keep it for 14 days
The Governor's recommendation is required before its introduction
The Legislative Council may permanently block it
nindian-polity-40-56.x: The Council cannot block a Money Bill; it can only keep it for 14 days.
n: The Legislative Council cannot amend or reject a Money Bill. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
Introduction of a Money Bill requires the Governor's prior recommendation under Article 207. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The Speaker's certification of a Money Bill is final. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The Legislative Council has 14 days to consider a Money Bill. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
xa: After **14 days**, the Bill is **deemed passed**.
The Assembly may accept or reject the Council's **recommendations** (**Art. 198**).
Money Bills are introduced **only in the Assembly**, by a minister.

nindian-polity-60-17.s: In a bicameral State Legislature, a Money Bill can be introduced only in:
nindian-polity-60-17.x: Money Bills start only in the Legislative Assembly; the Assembly is dissolvable with a five-year term, while the Council is permanent.
n: The Legislative Assembly is dissolvable and temporary. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The normal term of the Legislative Assembly is five years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The Legislative Council is a permanent body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
A State Money Bill can be introduced only in the Legislative Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
When the Legislative Assembly re-passes an ordinary Bill, the Legislative Council can delay it for up to one month in the second instance. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]

The Legislative Council can delay an ordinary Bill for a maximum of four months, consisting of three months the first time and one month the second time. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The total maximum delay of an ordinary Bill by the Legislative Council is four months. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
xa: First-time delay on an ordinary bill: **three months** — **four months** in all.
Money Bill delay: **14 days**.
The Assembly is the **originating and overriding** chamber.

ne0eb96fbc5e.s: The Legislative Assemblies of Goa and Mizoram have how many seats each?
ne0eb96fbc5e.x: Goa and Mizoram have 40 seats each, and Sikkim has 32 under Article 371F.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly list Arunachal as below **60**.
Normal range under **Art. 170**: **60-500**.
**AP 175**; **Telangana 119**.

n8b11d459a3f.s: Which one of the following correctly presents the present strength of the Legislative Assemblies of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh respectively?
n8b11d459a3f.x: The Legislative Assemblies of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh have 175, 119 and 403 seats respectively.
n8b11d459a3f.tq: Read the three figures as a fixed sequence and reject near-value substitutions.
xs: Option (4) wrongly gives AP **176**; options (1) and (2) misstate Telangana and UP.
xa: AP's Council exists today; **six states** have Councils.

ndeda19e9781.s: Which of the following is NOT a power or function of the Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly?
o: Approving the creation of a Legislative Council in the State
Giving the final decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill
Deciding disqualification under the Tenth Schedule, subject to judicial review
Adjourning or suspending the House in case of lack of quorum
ndeda19e9781.x: The Speaker performs the first three functions. Creation or abolition of a Legislative Council involves an Assembly resolution followed by parliamentary law; it is not approved by the Speaker.
ndeda19e9781.tq: Find the option assigning a constitutional function to the wrong authority.
xs: **Approving the creation of a Legislative Council** is not the Speaker's power — option **(1)**.
Creation needs an **Assembly special-majority resolution** and a **Parliament** law (**Art. 169**).
The Speaker does: decide **Money Bill** status, **Tenth Schedule** disqualification, and adjourn for **lack of quorum**.
xa: Tenth Schedule decisions are **subject to judicial review** (**Kihoto Hollohan 1992**).
Other powers: allows a **secret sitting**, appoints committee chairmen.
Chairs the **Business Advisory**, **Rules** and **General Purposes** Committees.

n8815c0492e5.s: A person elected to both Houses of a State Legislature is required to vacate one of the memberships because—
o: The Constitution prohibits simultaneous membership of both Houses of the same State Legislature
An MLA cannot become an MLC under any circumstances
The Council is a nominated body and cannot have elected members
The Governor alone may permit only one membership
n8815c0492e5.x: Article 190 prevents a person from being a member of both Houses of the Legislature of a State at the same time. It also bars simultaneous membership of legislatures of two States.
n8815c0492e5.tq: Use the constitutional incompatibility rule to eliminate explanations based on the composition of the Council.
xs: **Art. 190** bars membership of **both Houses** of the same State Legislature — option **(1)**.
It also bars membership of **two states'** legislatures.
MLAs do elect **1/3** of MLCs, so the Council is not wholly nominated (option 3 wrong).
xa: **Art. 190(4)**: seat vacated after **60 days'** absence without permission.
**Art. 190(3)(b)**: resignation effective on **Speaker's/Chairman's acceptance**.

nindian-polity-40-7.s: Which State has the smallest Legislative Assembly?
nindian-polity-40-7.x: Sikkim has the smallest State Assembly with 32 members; Puducherry has the smallest UT Assembly (33).
n: Sikkim has the smallest State Legislative Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The Sikkim Legislative Assembly has 32 members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
Puducherry has the smallest Union Territory Legislative Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The Puducherry Legislative Assembly has 33 members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
Sikkim's 32-member Legislative Assembly is a special constitutional exception. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
xa: Largest Assembly: **Uttar Pradesh** (**403**).
**Goa** and **Mizoram** have **40** seats each.
**AP** has **175** seats; **Telangana** **119**.
⚠ **Arunachal** has a minimum of **30** under **Art. 371H** but actually has **60**.

nindian-polity-60-30.s: Which of the following has a Legislative Assembly of 40 seats or fewer but is NOT a State?
nindian-polity-60-30.x: Puducherry (33 seats) is a Union Territory; Goa and Mizoram (40 each) and Sikkim (32) are States.
n: Sikkim has the smallest State Legislative Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The Sikkim Legislative Assembly has 32 seats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The Goa Legislative Assembly has 40 seats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The Mizoram Legislative Assembly has 40 seats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
Puducherry has the smallest Union Territory Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The Puducherry Assembly has 33 seats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
xa: Sikkim is a special exception (**Art. 371F**) below the standard minimum of **60**.
Puducherry = **30** elected + **3** nominated.
Largest Assembly: **Uttar Pradesh** (**403**).

nindian-polity-39-4.s: The maximum strength of a State Legislative Assembly is:
nindian-polity-39-4.x: An Assembly can have at most 500 and at least 60 members; Uttar Pradesh has the largest and Sikkim the smallest.
n: The maximum prescribed strength of a general State Legislative Assembly is 500 members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
The constitutional floor for the strength of a State Legislative Assembly is 60 members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
Uttar Pradesh has the largest State Legislative Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
Sikkim has the smallest State Legislative Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
The minimum prescribed strength of a State Legislative Assembly is 60 members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
xa: Sikkim's **32** is a special exception under **Art. 371F**.
Smallest UT Assembly: **Puducherry** (**33**).
**AP** has **175** seats; **Telangana** **119**.

n48a6495bf7b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the composition of a State Legislative Council?
o: One-sixth are elected by registered graduates
One-twelfth are elected by teachers of three years' standing
One-third are elected by local bodies
One-sixth are nominated by the Governor
n48a6495bf7b.x: Registered graduates elect one-twelfth; the one-sixth share is nominated by the Governor.
xa: ⚠ **1/3 – 1/12 – 1/12 – 1/3 – 1/6** = **local bodies – graduates – teachers – MLAs – Governor**.
**1/3** elected by **MLAs** from among non-members of the Assembly.
Mode of election: **PR-STV**.

n2664a67c42d.s: The Governor nominates what fraction of the members of a State Legislative Council?
n2664a67c42d.x: The Governor nominates one-sixth of the Council from literature, science, art, co-operative movement and social service, on Cabinet advice.
xa: Other shares: **1/3** local bodies, **1/12** graduates, **1/12** teachers, **1/3** MLAs.
Council size: max **1/3** of the Assembly, min **40** (**Art. 171**).
Significance: gives a place to **experts who cannot face elections**.

nindian-polity-45-15.s: The minimum strength of a State Legislative Council is:
nindian-polity-45-15.x: A Council must have at least 40 members; one-third are elected by MLAs, one-twelfth by graduates and one-sixth nominated.
n: One-third of the members of a State Legislative Council are elected by MLAs. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 120-123]
One-third of the members of a State Legislative Council are elected by local authorities. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 120-123]
One-twelfth of the members of a State Legislative Council are elected by graduates. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 120-123]
One-twelfth of the members of a State Legislative Council are elected by teachers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 120-123]
One-sixth of the members of a State Legislative Council are nominated by the Governor. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 120-123]
xa: **Local bodies** elect **one-third**; **teachers** elect **one-twelfth**.
⚠ **1/3 – 1/12 – 1/12 – 1/3 – 1/6** = **local bodies – graduates – teachers – MLAs – Governor**.
Maximum size: **one-third** of the Assembly; **Uttar Pradesh** has the largest Council (**100**).
Graduates and teachers need at least **3 years** of standing.

nindian-polity-62-14.s: Which of the following is NOT a field for nomination by the Governor to the State Legislative Council?
nindian-polity-62-14.x: The valid fields are literature, science, art, the co-operative movement and social service; industrial activity is not one.
n: Literature is a nomination field for the Governor’s nominees to a State Legislative Council. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
Science is a nomination field for the Governor’s nominees to a State Legislative Council. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
Art is a nomination field for the Governor’s nominees to a State Legislative Council. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The co-operative movement is a nomination field for the Governor’s nominees to a State Legislative Council. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
Social service is a nomination field for the Governor’s nominees to a State Legislative Council. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
Industrialists are not valid nomination categories for a State Legislative Council. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The Governor’s five nomination fields for a State Legislative Council are literature, science, art, the co-operative movement, and social service. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
xa: The Governor nominates **one-sixth** of the Council, on **Cabinet advice**.
⚠ The **co-operative movement** is a ground under **Article 171** but **not** for the Rajya Sabha (**Article 80**).
Other Council members are elected by **PR-STV**, by **secret ballot**.

nc6d0e21fe86.s: A law of Parliament under Article 169 creating or abolishing a Legislative Council is passed by:
o: Two-thirds of members present and voting
A special majority with ratification by half the States
nc6d0e21fe86.x: Parliament uses a simple majority, and such a law is not deemed an amendment under Article 368.
xa: Assembly resolution: **majority of total membership** + **2/3 of members present and voting**.
The **Governor has no role** in the resolution.
⚠ Assembly = **special majority**; Parliament = **simple majority**.

nf6cf8ef682f.s: Under Article 169, the resolution of a State Legislative Assembly for the creation or abolition of its Legislative Council must be passed by—
o: A simple majority of members present and voting
A majority of the total membership of the Assembly and at least two-thirds of the members present and voting
Two-thirds of the total membership of the Assembly
A majority of the total membership of both Houses sitting jointly
nf6cf8ef682f.x: Article 169 needs a special majority: a majority of the total membership of the Assembly plus not less than two-thirds of members present and voting. A simple majority is what Parliament then uses for its law; two-thirds of total membership is not the test; States have no joint sitting.
nf6cf8ef682f.tq: Assembly = special majority; Parliament = simple majority; not an Art 368 amendment.
xs: The resolution needs a **majority of total membership** and **at least two-thirds of members present and voting** — option **(2)**.
A **simple majority** is what **Parliament** uses for the follow-up law.
There is no joint sitting in State legislatures.
xa: The law is **not deemed an amendment** under **Art. 368**.
The **Governor has no role**.
APPSC-GS **2018** asked on **Art. 169**.

nindian-polity-62-11.s: A State Assembly resolution for creation or abolition of a Legislative Council must be passed by:
o: A simple majority of members present
A majority of total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting
Three-fourths of members present and voting
nindian-polity-62-11.x: It needs a special majority (majority of total membership and two-thirds present and voting), but only requests and does not compel the Union.
n: The State Legislative Assembly resolution for creating or abolishing a Legislative Council requires a special majority. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The special majority requires at least 50 percent of the total membership of the State Legislative Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The special majority requires at least two-thirds of the members present and voting in the State Legislative Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The State Legislative Assembly resolution for creating or abolishing a Legislative Council is recommendatory. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The State Legislative Assembly resolution does not legally compel the Union Government to introduce a bill in Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The State Legislative Assembly initiates the creation or abolition of a Legislative Council by passing a resolution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
xa: **Parliament** then acts by **simple majority**; the law is **not deemed an amendment** under **Art. 368**.
The **Governor has no role** in the resolution.
⚠ Assembly = **special majority**; Parliament = **simple majority**; Governor = **no role**.

n49125378737.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of States having Legislative Councils at present?
o: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Kerala, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Goa
Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh
Telangana, Mizoram, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Sikkim
Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh
n49125378737.x: The six States with Legislative Councils are Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh.
n49125378737.tq: Check every member of the six-State list; a single unicameral State makes the option wrong.
xs: The six states: **AP, Telangana, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra and UP** — option **(4)**.
**Goa**, **Kerala**, **Mizoram** and **Sikkim** have no Councils, so options (1), (2) and (3) fail.
xa: **J&K's** Council was abolished in **2019**.
**Tamil Nadu** abolished its Council in **1986**.
**Karnataka Council (2026)**: **Saleem Ahmed** elected Chairperson (**38-30**).
**Telangana Council** Chairman: **Gutha Sukender Reddy**.

ndbb5c24714d.s: In which of the following years or periods did Andhra Pradesh illustrate the politically fluctuating status of the Legislative Council?
ndbb5c24714d.x: Andhra Pradesh abolished its Legislative Council in 1985 (NTR government) and revived it in 2007; in January 2020 the Assembly resolved to abolish it again, but withdrew that resolution in November 2021. These swings show that the Council's fate depends on state politics.
ndbb5c24714d.tq: Recall the distinctive three-point chronology rather than selecting a sequence of unrelated years.
xs: AP's Council fate swung in **1985, 2007 and 2020-21** — option **(3)**.
AP **abolished** its Council in **1985** and **revived** it in **2007**.
xa: Criticism: a costly "**delaying chamber**" whose existence depends on the ruling party in the Assembly.
**Tamil Nadu** abolished its Council in **1986**.
Significance: checks **hasty legislation**.

n1796fbd0d51.s: The interval between the last sitting in one session of a State Legislature and the first sitting in the next session cannot exceed:
n1796fbd0d51.x: Article 174 requires that not more than six months intervene between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next.
n1796fbd0d51.tq: Test the constitutional time limit directly and distinguish it from other legislative periods.
xs: The gap cannot exceed **six months** — option **(1)**.
This is the **Art. 174** rule: no more than **6 months** between the last sitting of one session and the first of the next.
xa: Many Assemblies met only to satisfy this **Art. 174** rule.
PRS **2025**: Assemblies sat an average of **24 days** (**Odisha 43**, **Nagaland 7**).
About **33%** of Bills passed in a single sitting.

n043f0688d8e.s: Who among the following was the first woman legislator in India?
n043f0688d8e.x: Muthulakshmi Reddy was India’s first woman legislator and served in the Madras Legislative Council.
n043f0688d8e.tq: Use the first-in-history clue and distinguish legislative office from executive office.
xs: **Muthulakshmi Reddy** was India's **first woman legislator** — option **(2)**.
She sat in the **Madras Legislative Council**.
xa: The Council gives a place to **experts who cannot face elections**.
**Tamil Nadu** later abolished its Council in **1986**.
Governor nominates **1/6** of a Council from literature, science, art, cooperation and social service.

nindian-polity-40-55.s: The minimum strength of a State Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, is:
nindian-polity-40-55.x: The 91st Amendment (2003) caps a State ministry at 15% of the Assembly with a minimum of 12.
n: The Council of Ministers is capped at a maximum of 15 percent of the Assembly's strength under Article 164. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act of 2003 provides the 15-percent cap on the Council of Ministers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The minimum size of the Council of Ministers is 12 ministers, including the Chief Minister. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
xa: The cap is in **Article 164** (**164(1A)**).
A **non-member** minister may serve only **six consecutive months**.

n727e046aabb.s: In a Legislative Assembly consisting of 70 members, the quorum for a sitting would be—
n727e046aabb.x: Quorum is 10 members or one-tenth of the total membership, whichever is greater. For a 70-member House, 10 is greater than 7.
n727e046aabb.tq: Apply the ‘whichever is greater’ rule rather than simply calculating one-tenth.
xs: Quorum is **10 members**, which is greater than one-tenth of **70** (= **7**) — option **(2)**.
Rule (**Art. 189(3)**): **10 members or one-tenth** of the House, **whichever is greater**.
So option (1), **7**, is only the one-tenth figure; **35** and **70** are not the rule.
xa: The **Speaker** adjourns or suspends the House for **lack of quorum**.
**Art. 189** also: the Speaker has a **casting vote** on a tie.
Normal Assembly strength: **60-500** (**Art. 170**).

n564908b7c41.s: Which one of the following is NOT a ground of disqualification under Article 191 of the Constitution?
o: Being absent from the House for 60 days without permission
Being of unsound mind as declared by a competent court
n564908b7c41.x: Absence for 60 days without permission results in vacation of the seat under Article 190(4), not disqualification under Article 191.
n564908b7c41.tq: Distinguish disqualification under Article 191 from vacation of seat under Article 190.
xs: **Absence for 60 days without permission** is not an **Art. 191** ground — option **(3)**.
It vacates the seat under **Art. 190(4)**.
**Insolvency**, **office of profit** and **unsound mind** are Art. 191 grounds.
xa: Other Art. 191 grounds: **not a citizen**, Parliament's law (**RPA 1951**), **Tenth Schedule** defection.
**Art. 190**: no one can be a member of **both Houses** or of **two states'** legislatures.
**Art. 190(3)(b)**: MLA's resignation takes effect only on the **Speaker's acceptance**.

n0137b8e1e71.s: With reference to the Governor's address to the State Legislature, which one of the following is correct?
o: It is delivered before every sitting of the Legislative Assembly.
It is delivered on the first day of the first session of each year and is followed by discussion.
It is delivered on the last day of every annual session.
It is delivered only when the Legislative Council demands it.
n0137b8e1e71.x: The Governor addresses the Legislature on the first day of the first session of each year, and the address is followed by discussion in the House.
n0137b8e1e71.tq: Use the time phrase ‘first day of the first session’ as the key discriminator.
xs: The Governor's address is on the **first day of the first session of each year**, followed by **discussion** — option **(2)**.
It is not before every sitting or on the last day.
xa: **Art. 175** = Governor's address and messages; **Art. 176** = special address (mandatory at the first session).
Then **general discussion** → **voting on demands**.
**Art. 208**: each House makes its **rules of procedure**.

nindian-polity-40-8.s: Which Constitutional Amendment ended the nomination of Anglo-Indian members under Article 333?
nindian-polity-40-8.x: The 104th Amendment Act, 2020 ended Anglo-Indian nomination; the 106th (2023) provides about one-third reservation for women.
n: Article 332 mandates reservation of Legislative Assembly seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Legislative Assembly reservations are based on population ratios. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2020 ended the nomination of Anglo-Indian members under Article 333. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2023 provides approximately one-third reservation for women in directly elected Assembly seats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The women's reservation under the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act becomes effective after post-census delimitation. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
xa: Minimum age (**Article 173**): **Assembly 25**, **Council 30** years.
The Assembly is **directly elected** by **First-Past-the-Post**.
Maximum **500**, minimum **60** seats (**Article 170**).

nindian-polity-39-31.s: The term of office of a Governor is:
nindian-polity-39-31.x: The Governor's term is five years, subject to the President's pleasure, and continues until a successor takes over.
n: The Governor has a five-year term. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
The Governor continues in office until the successor assumes office. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 101-104]
xa: **Five years** is also the tenure of the **President**, **Lok Sabha**, a **State Legislative Assembly**, a **Panchayat** and a **Municipality**.
**Six years**: **Rajya Sabha** and **Legislative Council** members.
The Assembly can be extended **1 year at a time** during a National Emergency.

nindian-polity-60-11.s: An extension of a State Assembly's term during a National Emergency cannot continue beyond ____ after the Emergency ceases.
nindian-polity-60-11.x: Parliament may extend the term a year at a time during an Emergency, but not beyond six months after it ceases.
n: The normal term of the Legislative Assembly is five years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The normal term of the Legislative Assembly is five years under Article 172. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
During a National Emergency under Article 352, Parliament may extend the Legislative Assembly’s duration by law for one year at a time. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The Legislative Assembly’s duration may be extended only up to six months after the National Emergency ceases. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
xa: The Assembly may be **dissolved** earlier but cannot be **abolished**.
**Art. 174**: no more than **6 months** between sittings.

n9a62b075815.s: The members of a State Legislative Council are elected by which method?
o: Cumulative voting by the Legislative Assembly alone
First-past-the-post system by direct universal suffrage
Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote
n9a62b075815.x: Members of a State Legislative Council are elected indirectly through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
n9a62b075815.tq: Discriminate between the electoral system and the appointing authority.
xs: Council members are elected indirectly by **PR-STV** — **proportional representation by single transferable vote** — option **(4)**.
It is not direct election by universal suffrage; only **1/6** are **nominated** by the Governor.
xa: **Rajya Sabha** members are also elected by MLAs by **PR-STV**.
MLAs elect **1/3** of MLCs.
Members serve **6 years**; **1/3** retire every **second year**.

nindian-polity-62-9.s: Who presides over the State Legislative Council?
o: The Chairman elected by the Council from among its members
The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
nindian-polity-62-9.x: Under Article 182, the Council elects its Chairman from among its own members. The Governor does not nominate the Chairman, and the Vice-President chairs only the Rajya Sabha.
nindian-polity-62-9.tq: Discriminate the Council's Chairman from the Rajya Sabha's ex-officio Chairman.
n: The Chairman of the State Legislative Council is elected by the Council from among its members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The Chairman of the Legislative Council is chosen by the Council members from among themselves under Article 182. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The Governor does not nominate the Chairman of the Legislative Council. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
xs: The Council is presided over by **the Chairman elected by the Council from among its members** — so option **(1)** is correct.
This is under **Article 182**; the Chairman is **not nominated by the Governor**.
The **Speaker** presides over the **Legislative Assembly**, not the Council.
xa: The **Chairman** resigns to the **Deputy Chairman**.
The Assembly's **Speaker and Deputy Speaker** are elected under **Article 178** and resign to each other (**Article 179**).
Defection cases in the Council are decided by the **Chairman**.

nindian-polity-40-15.s: The Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly can vote:
o: Only a casting vote in case of a tie
In the first instance and also a casting vote
nindian-polity-40-15.x: The Speaker has only a casting vote when votes are tied, not a first vote.
n: The Speaker does not vacate office immediately when the Assembly is dissolved. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The Speaker continues in office until immediately before the first meeting of the newly elected Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The Speaker cannot vote in the first instance. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The Speaker exercises a casting vote when votes are equally divided. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
xa: Exception: during a **removal resolution** (**Art. 181**) the Speaker **does not preside** but may vote in the first instance.
Removal needs a **majority of all the then members**, after **14 days' notice**.
The Speaker's certificate decides whether a bill is a **Money Bill**.

n9951f8c9d7d.s: Disqualification of a State legislator on grounds other than defection is decided by:
o: The Governor, bound by the Election Commission's opinion
n9951f8c9d7d.x: Under Articles 191–192 the Governor decides according to the Election Commission's opinion; defection goes to the Speaker or Chairman.
xa: **Art. 191** grounds: **office of profit**, **unsound mind**, **undischarged insolvent**, **not a citizen**, Parliament's law (**RPA 1951**), defection.
⚠ Governor (EC opinion) = **Art. 191** grounds; Speaker/Chairman = **Tenth Schedule**.

nindian-polity-40-57.s: Under the Tenth Schedule, defection cases arising in a State Legislative Council are decided by the:
nindian-polity-40-57.x: The Chairman decides defection cases in the Council under the Tenth Schedule.
n: The Legislative Assembly cannot be abolished. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The Chairman decides defection cases under the Tenth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
xa: Other disqualifications (**Article 191**) are decided by the **Governor** on the **Election Commission's binding opinion** (**Article 192**).
⚠ **Governor** = Art. 191 grounds; **Speaker/Chairman** = **Tenth Schedule** defection.
**Kihoto Hollohan 1992** made the Speaker's decision subject to judicial review.

nindian-polity-25-7.s: Under Article 103, the President decides the disqualification of a Member of Parliament on the opinion of the:
nindian-polity-25-7.x: The President acts on the ECI's binding opinion (Article 103); the Governor does the same for State legislators (Article 192).
n: The Election Commission of India advises the President on the disqualification of Members of Parliament under Article 103. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India advises the Governor on the disqualification of State legislators under Article 192. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The President decides questions of disqualification of Members of Parliament under Article 103. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The President's decision under Article 103 is based on the opinion of the Election Commission of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The opinion of the Election Commission of India under Article 103 is binding. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Governor decides questions of disqualification of Members of Legislative Assemblies and Councils under Article 192. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Governor's decision under Article 192 is based on the opinion of the Election Commission of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The opinion of the Election Commission of India under Article 192 is binding. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xa: Grounds under **Article 191**: **office of profit**, **unsound mind**, **undischarged insolvent**, **not a citizen**.
⚠ **Tenth Schedule** defection is decided by the **Speaker/Chairman**, not the Governor.
**Art. 190**: no one can be a member of **both Houses** or of two states' legislatures.

n8c20f49bc2b.s: Which one of the following correctly states the relative position of a State Legislative Council and the Rajya Sabha?
o: The State Council's power is essentially a delaying power and is weaker than that of the Rajya Sabha.
The State Council can dissolve the Legislative Assembly during a constitutional deadlock.
The State Council alone can ratify constitutional amendments.
The State Council has the same power as the Rajya Sabha to veto an ordinary Bill of the Assembly.
n8c20f49bc2b.x: The State Legislative Council can delay legislation but cannot permanently veto an Assembly Bill. Its powers are considerably weaker than those of the Rajya Sabha in comparable matters.
n8c20f49bc2b.tq: Avoid transferring the Rajya Sabha's powers to the State Council.
xs: The Council's power is **only delaying** — much **weaker than the Rajya Sabha's** — option **(1)**.
It cannot veto an Assembly Bill: delay **3 months** + **1 month**, then the Bill is **deemed passed**.
It has **no role in ratifying** constitutional amendments, and cannot dissolve the Assembly.
xa: Money Bill: return within **14 days**.
No joint sitting in states.
Criticism: a costly "**delaying chamber**".

n41418c135b9.s: Elected members of a State Legislative Assembly take part in the election of:
o: Both the President and the Vice-President
n41418c135b9.x: Elected MLAs are in the President's electoral college (Article 54); the Vice-President is elected only by MPs.
xa: MLAs also elect **Rajya Sabha** members (**PR-STV**).
MLAs elect **1/3** of MLCs.

nindian-polity-45-12.s: The representatives of a State in the Rajya Sabha are elected by:
nindian-polity-45-12.x: Elected MLAs choose them by PR-STV through secret ballot; nominated MLAs cannot vote.
n: State representatives in the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected MLAs of State Legislative Assemblies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 120-123]
The electoral system for State representatives in the Rajya Sabha is proportional representation by means of the Single Transferable Vote. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 120-123]
Rajya Sabha elections for State representatives are conducted by secret ballot. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 120-123]
Nominated MLAs cannot vote in the election of State representatives to the Rajya Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 120-123]
xa: Elected MLAs also vote in the **President's** election (**Art. 54**).
MLAs do **not** vote in the **Vice-President's** election — only MPs.
MLAs elect **one-third** of the **Legislative Council** (**Art. 171**).
nindian-polity-45-12.fixed: Rajya Sabha elections use open ballot (RPA amended 2003), not secret ballot; only I and II correct

nindian-polity-62-43.s: Which field is valid for nomination to a State Legislative Council but not to the Rajya Sabha?
nindian-polity-62-43.x: Under Article 80 the Rajya Sabha fields are literature, science, art and social service; the co-operative movement applies only to the Council.
n: The co-operative movement is a nomination field for the Governor’s nominees to a State Legislative Council. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The co-operative movement is not a nomination ground for the Rajya Sabha under Article 80. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
The Governor’s five nomination fields for a State Legislative Council are literature, science, art, the co-operative movement, and social service. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 164-167]
xa: Council nomination fields: **literature, science, art, co-operative movement, social service**.
**Industrialists** are **not** an electoral or nomination category.
The Governor nominates **one-sixth** of the Council.

nindian-polity-21-27.s: State Money Bills are governed by Articles 198, 199 and:
nindian-polity-21-27.x: State Money Bills come under Articles 198, 199 and 207; Articles 200 and 201 concern reservation of Bills.
n: The Governor can reserve a State Bill for the President under Article 200. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 49-52]
The President considers a State Bill reserved by the Governor under Article 201. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 49-52]
Articles 200 and 201 deal with Governor’s and President’s assent to State Bills. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 49-52]
xa: **Article 207**: Money Bill only on the **Governor's prior recommendation**.
**Article 197**: the Council's delay of **ordinary Bills**.
**Article 213**: the Governor's **Ordinances**.

nindian-polity-40-1.s: The State Legislature is governed under which Part and range of Articles of the Constitution?
nindian-polity-40-1.x: State Legislatures are in Part VI, Articles 168–212. Parliament is in Part V, Articles 79–122.
nindian-polity-40-1.tq: Discriminate Part V (Parliament) from Part VI (State Legislatures).
n: The State Legislative Assembly is governed under Part VI of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
Articles 168 to 212 govern the State Legislative Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
xs: The State Legislature is in **Part VI, Articles 168–212** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Article 168** covers composition; **169** creation/abolition of Councils; **170/171** composition of the Assembly/Council.
**Article 213** (Ordinances) lies just after this range, so option (3) is wrong.
xa: **Article 208**: each House makes **rules of procedure**.
**Article 194**: powers and **privileges** of MLAs.
**Article 211**: no discussion of a **HC judge's conduct**; **212**: courts not to inquire into proceedings.

nindian-polity-40-2.s: Under Article 168, the State Legislature consists of the Governor and the Legislative Assembly, along with which additional body in bicameral States?
nindian-polity-40-2.x: Under Article 168, a State Legislature is the Governor plus the Assembly, and in bicameral States also the Legislative Council.
nindian-polity-40-2.tq: Remember that the Governor is part of every State Legislature.
n: Article 168 provides that the State Legislature consists of the Governor and the Legislative Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The State Legislature also includes a Legislative Council in bicameral States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
xs: In bicameral States the legislature also includes the **Legislative Council** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Article 168**: **unicameral** = **Governor + Legislative Assembly**; **bicameral** = Governor + Assembly + **Legislative Council**.
The **Council of Ministers** is part of the executive, not the legislature.
xa: **Six** bicameral States: **Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh**.
J&K's Council was abolished by the **J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019**.
The Governor is part of the legislature **without being a member**.

nindian-polity-36-35.s: Teachers elect what fraction of the members of a State Legislative Council?
nindian-polity-36-35.x: Teachers and graduates each elect one-twelfth; one-sixth are nominated by the Governor.
n: One-twelfth of the members of a Legislative Council are elected by graduates. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
One-twelfth of the members of a Legislative Council are elected by teachers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
One-sixth of the members of a Legislative Council are nominated by the Governor. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
Industrialists are not an electoral category for Legislative Council elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
The Legislative Council is constituted through indirect election categories and gubernatorial nomination. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
xa: **MLAs** elect **one-third** (from among **non-MLAs**); **local bodies** elect **one-third**.
Teachers must be in institutions of at least **secondary-school** level.
Election is by **PR-STV**, by **secret ballot**.

n2ed07996f15.s: When Andhra Pradesh was formed in 1956, its Legislature was unicameral with a Legislative Assembly of how many members?
n2ed07996f15.x: In 1956 the AP Legislature was unicameral with an Assembly of 301 members. 175 is the present strength of residual AP (Sec. 17, AP Reorganisation Act); 294 and 245 are distractors not supported for 1956.
xs: In **1956** AP's legislature was **unicameral**, with **301** members — option **(3)** (APPSC-GS **2022** key).
**175** is residual AP's present strength (**Sec. 17**).
xa: The **Council** was created only in **1958**.
First Speaker (**1956**): **Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao**.
The **1956** Assembly: **Congress** held a large majority.

nfd5aa0de05e.s: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council, abolished in 1985, was revived in:
nfd5aa0de05e.x: The Council was created in 1958, abolished in 1985, revived in 2007, and an abolition resolution was passed in January 2020.
xa: The **Jan 2020** resolution was **withdrawn in Nov 2021**; the Council continues.
⚠ Trap: revival Act is of **2005**, revival in **2007**.
**2015**: Council raised to **58**.

nd3c1af07293.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2015 raised the strength of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council to:
nd3c1af07293.x: The 2015 Amendment Act raised the strength of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council from 50 to 58 members.
nd3c1af07293.tq: Separate the original statutory figure from the later amended figure.
xs: The **2015** amendment raised AP's Council to **58** — option **(3)** (APPSC-GS **2021** key).
**50** was the original cap under **Sec. 22(1)** of the **2014** Act.
xa: Still **58** members (Jan **2026**).
Composition: **20** local authorities, **20** MLAs, **5** graduates, **5** teachers, **8** nominated.
Telangana's Council: **40**.

n5b6edbaa785.s: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council was revived in 2007 under the:
n5b6edbaa785.x: The Council was revived in 2007 under the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council Act, 2005.
