Financial Emergency requires a simple majority in both Houses of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
A National Emergency has no maximum continuation limit. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
xa: Financial Emergency continues until **revoked** by the President.

nindian-polity-50-16.s: The last National Emergency was formally withdrawn on 21 March:
nindian-polity-50-16.x: Emergencies were declared in 1962, 1971 and 1975; the last was lifted on 21 March 1977.
n: National Emergencies were invoked in 1962, 1971, and 1975. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
The National Emergency of 1975 was proclaimed on 25 June 1975. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
The 1975 National Emergency was formally withdrawn on 21 March 1977. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
xa: The **1975** Emergency was on the ground of **Internal Disturbance**.
The **44th Amendment, 1978** replaced "internal disturbance" with "**armed rebellion**".
**Samvidhan Hatya Diwas** (**25 June**) recalls the **1975** Emergency.

n683da91c356.s: The coalition era of Indian federalism, with more negotiated Centre-State relations, broadly spanned:
n683da91c356.x: Congress dominance (1952–67), confrontation (1967–77), the Janata interlude (1977–89) and the coalition era (1989–2014).
xa: **Rajamannar Committee (1969)** — phase C; **Sarkaria Commission (1983)** — phase D.
**ISC (1990)** and **Bommai (1994)** — phase A.
Phase C ended with the **1975 Emergency**.

nc59217d5877.s: 'Samvidhan Hatya Diwas', which recalls the Emergency of 1975, is observed on:
nc59217d5877.x: Samvidhan Hatya Diwas is observed on 25 June, recalling the Emergency proclaimed in 1975. 26 January is Republic Day, 26 November is Constitution Day, and 15 August is Independence Day.
xs: **Samvidhan Hatya Diwas** is observed on **25 June**, recalling the **1975 Emergency** — option **(3)**.
Source: LENSD **26 Jun 2026**.
xa: National Emergencies: **1962, 1971, 1975**.
After 1975, the **44th Amendment (1978)** replaced "internal disturbance" with **"armed rebellion"**.
The **1967-77** phase ended in re-centralisation up to the **1975 Emergency**.

n2a400982fda.s: Which of the following is NOT a financial consequence of a National Emergency?
o: Transfers to States may be reduced or cancelled, subject to Parliament's approval
An obligatory increase in transfers of funds to States
The President may modify the distribution of revenues between the Union and States
The Union may issue directions affecting its financial relations with States
n2a400982fda.x: The President may modify revenue distribution and reduce or cancel transfers to States; an increase in transfers is not a specified consequence.
xa: Financial Emergency (**Art. 360**): **reduce salaries** of State employees and **SC/HC judges**; State **money bills reserved** for the President.
Financial Emergency has **never been declared**.
⚠ "**Art. 311** - Financial Emergency" is a mismatch; it is **Art. 360**.

ne857c7ecba1.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated federal consequence of a Financial Emergency under Article 360?
o: The Union may direct States regarding financial propriety.
The Union may direct reduction of salaries and allowances.
The Union automatically assumes all legislative powers of State Legislatures.
Money Bills of States may be required to be reserved for the President's consideration.
ne857c7ecba1.x: Article 360 can enable directions concerning State finances, salary reductions and reservation of State Money Bills. It does not automatically transfer all legislative powers of State Legislatures to the Union.
ne857c7ecba1.tq: Find the overbroad claim that exceeds the financial scope of Article 360.
xs: The Union does NOT **automatically assume all legislative powers** of State Legislatures under **Art. 360** — option **(3)**.

Under Financial Emergency the Centre can **direct financial propriety**, order **reduction of salaries and allowances** of State employees, and require State **money bills to be reserved** for the President.
It can also reduce salaries of Union employees and **SC/HC judges**.
xa: Ground of **Art. 360**: threat to the **financial stability or credit** of India.
Approval within **2 months**, **simple majority**.
Financial Emergency has **never been declared**.
⚠ "**Art. 311** - Financial Emergency" is a mismatch; it is **Art. 360**.

nindian-polity-50-18.s: The 44th Amendment replaced 'internal disturbance' in Article 352 with:
nindian-polity-50-18.x: It substituted 'armed rebellion', cut approval to one month, protected Articles 20–21 and required the Cabinet's written advice.
n: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 replaced “Internal Disturbance” with “Armed Rebellion” under Article 352. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 reduced parliamentary approval time for a National Emergency from 2 months to 1 month. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 guaranteed that enforcement of Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended under Article 359. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
The President can proclaim a National Emergency only upon the written advice of the Union Cabinet. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
War, external aggression, or armed rebellion are the grounds for National Emergency under Article 352. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended during a National Emergency. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act established the non-suspendability of Articles 20 and 21 under Article 359. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
xa: ⚠ Trap: "internal disturbance" is no longer a ground (APPSC-GS 2018).
**Special sitting:** notice by **1/10th of Lok Sabha** members → sitting within **14 days**.
The **38th Amendment** barred judicial review of Emergency; **Minerva Mills** reopened it.

nindian-polity-50-43.s: During a National Emergency, the President may modify the distribution of revenues between the Union and States under Article:
nindian-polity-50-43.x: Article 354 allows it; the change lasts until the end of the financial year in which the Emergency ends.
n: Article 354 empowers the President to modify the constitutional distribution of revenues between the Union and the States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
Modification of revenue distribution under Article 354 remains valid up to the end of the financial year in which the proclamation ceases. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
xa: The President can **reduce or cancel** transfers to States, subject to Parliament's approval.
⚠ "**Increase** the transfer" is the wrong statement (APPSC-G2 2017).
Parliament's State-List laws (**Art. 250**) **cease 6 months** after the Emergency is **revoked**.

n0a4b7d44ed6.s: Under Article 255, an Act passed without the required previous sanction but later assented to by the Governor or President is:
o: not invalid merely for want of that sanction
valid only if upheld by the Supreme Court
n0a4b7d44ed6.x: Article 255 treats the recommendation or previous sanction as procedural; subsequent assent prevents invalidity on that ground alone.
xa: **Art. 254**: **repugnancy** — Union law prevails; State law with **President's assent** prevails in that State.
State bills restricting **inter-state trade** need the **President's previous sanction** (Part XIII, **Arts. 301-305**).
**Art. 253**: laws to implement **international agreements**.

nb1689335247.s: Repugnancy between Union and State laws is dealt with by Article:
nb1689335247.x: Article 254 deals with repugnancy; Article 255 concerns recommendations and previous sanctions as procedural matters, and Article 248 with residuary powers.
xa: **246A** (**101st CAA**): both Parliament and States make **GST** laws; only Parliament for **IGST**.
**252** = law for **two or more States by consent**; **253** = **international agreements**.
**251** = inconsistency with laws under **249/250**.

n99162de7391.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the territorial extent of laws?
o: Parliament may make laws for the whole or any part of India
A parliamentary law is not invalid merely because it has extra-territorial operation
A State Legislature may ordinarily legislate for another State's territory without any territorial connection
A State law needs a sufficient territorial nexus for extra-territorial reach
n99162de7391.x: A State law requires a sufficient territorial nexus for any extra-territorial reach, so the last statement is false.
xa: ⚠ **Extra-territorial** laws = Parliament only; State needs **territorial nexus**.
**President's regulations** for **Andaman & Nicobar** and **Lakshadweep** have the force of Parliament's Acts.
The **Governor** can bar or modify Parliament's Acts for **Scheduled Areas**.

nefd1d111edb.s: A State law on a State List subject conflicts with a valid Parliamentary law under the Concurrent List. Which ordinarily prevails?
o: The later of the two laws
The law approved by the Governor
nefd1d111edb.x: The Concurrent List has precedence over the State List, so a valid Parliamentary law on a Concurrent matter ordinarily prevails over an inconsistent State law.
xa: **Art. 251**: a law under **Art. 249/250** prevails over a conflicting State law.

nd6c6f5eaf22.s: Under Article 246(4), Parliament may legislate for areas not included in a State (Union Territories) on matters in:
o: The Union and Concurrent Lists only
nd6c6f5eaf22.x: Article 246(4) lets Parliament legislate for areas not included in a State on matters in all three Lists, not merely the Union List.
xa: **President's regulations** for **Andaman & Nicobar** and **Lakshadweep** have the force of Parliament's Acts.

n6364bc70e7c.s: Article 246A was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
n6364bc70e7c.x: Article 246A was introduced by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, which established the constitutional framework for GST.
n6364bc70e7c.tq: Match the distinctive constitutional article with the amendment that introduced it.
xs: **Art. 246A** was inserted by the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act** — option **(1)**.
Under it, **both** Parliament and States make **GST** laws; only Parliament for **inter-state supply (IGST)**.
xa: **Art. 246**: three lists in the **Seventh Schedule**.
**Art. 248** + **Entry 97** = residuary power, including **taxation**.

nf32479758df.s: In India, the residuary power of legislation is vested in Parliament by which combination?
o: Article 248 and Entry 97 of the Union List
Article 249 and Entry 97 of the State List
Article 250 and Entry 98 of the Concurrent List
Article 253 and Entry 97 of the Concurrent List
nf32479758df.x: Article 248 and Entry 97 of the Union List together confer residuary legislative power on Parliament.
nf32479758df.tq: Link the constitutional article with the corresponding Seventh Schedule entry.
xs: Residuary power: **Article 248** and **Entry 97 of the Union List** — option **(1)**.
Parliament has **exclusive** power over any matter not in the State or Concurrent List.
**Art. 249** = Rajya Sabha resolution; **Art. 250** = Emergency; **Art. 253** = treaties.
xa: Covers residuary **taxation** as well.
⚠ **97** is also the **original** Union List count.
Borrowed from **Canada**.

n315d7b4d5d2.s: Articles 301 to 303 principally restrict Parliament from doing which of the following in relation to trade and commerce?
o: Making any law concerning inter-State trade
n315d7b4d5d2.x: Articles 301 to 303 restrict discriminatory or preferential treatment between States in laws relating to trade and commerce.
n315d7b4d5d2.tq: Distinguish a restriction against discrimination from a complete prohibition on regulation.
xs: **Arts. 301-303** stop Parliament from **preferring or discriminating between States** in trade laws — option **(1)**.
Discrimination is allowed only in **scarcity**.
xa: State restrictions on **inter-state trade**: reasonable, in **public interest**, with **President's previous sanction** (Part XIII, **Arts. 301-305**).
**Inter-state trade** is a **Union** subject; trade **within** a State is a State subject.

n0c7c6fd984f.s: Under Article 251, if a Parliamentary law made under Article 249 or 250 conflicts with a State law:
o: both laws become void to the extent of conflict
n0c7c6fd984f.x: Article 251 provides that a Parliamentary law made under Article 249 or 250 prevails over an inconsistent State law.
xa: The **State legislature's power is not suspended** under Art. 249 or 250.
**Art. 249** law ceases **6 months after the resolution lapses**; **Art. 250** law **6 months** after the emergency.

n82f814b8d04.s: While an Article 249 resolution is in force, the State Legislature:
o: may legislate only with the Rajya Sabha's consent
loses its power, which passes to the Governor
may still legislate, but the Parliamentary law prevails in a conflict
stands dissolved for the duration of the resolution
n82f814b8d04.x: An Article 249 resolution does not suspend the State Legislature's power, but the Parliamentary law prevails if the two conflict.
xa: **Art. 251**: the State law is **inoperative only while** the Union law lasts.
Same for **Art. 250** during an Emergency.
Art. 249 resolution: **2/3 present and voting**, **up to 1 year**.

nf354af8c197.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 252?
o: Two or more State Legislatures must pass resolutions requesting parliamentary legislation
Any other State may adopt the law later by a resolution of its legislature
The requesting State Legislatures may independently repeal the law
Only Parliament can amend or repeal a law made under it
nf354af8c197.x: Only Parliament can amend or repeal a law enacted under Article 252; the requesting States cannot repeal it on their own.
xa: ⚠ **252** needs consent of **two or more states**; **253** needs **no state consent**.
Art. 252 Acts: **Prize Competition (1955)**, **Wild Life (1972)**, **Water (1974)**, **Urban Land Ceiling (1976)**, **Human Organs (1994)**.
"Art. 252 laws cannot be changed by states" is cited as a **centralising tool**.

n533387cb0ba.s: A law made for a State during President’s Rule continues after the Proclamation ends until:
o: the State Legislature alters, repeals or re-enacts it
the Supreme Court declares it permanent
the Governor issues an ordinance replacing it
n533387cb0ba.x: Such a law does not automatically lapse when President’s Rule ends. It continues until the State Legislature alters, repeals or re-enacts it.
n533387cb0ba.tq: Test the post-emergency effect instead of confusing continuation with automatic repeal.
xs: A President's Rule law continues until the **State Legislature alters, repeals or re-enacts** it — option **(1)**.
It does not lapse automatically when the Proclamation ends.
xa: Such laws are made by **Parliament** or the **President by delegation** (**Art. 356**).
Contrast: **Art. 250** laws lapse **6 months** after the emergency; **Art. 249** laws **6 months** after the resolution lapses.

n5e7997b62ef.s: A Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249 remains in force for a period not exceeding:
n5e7997b62ef.x: An Article 249 resolution lasts up to one year and may be renewed any number of times, one year at a time.
xa: Majority: **2/3 of members present and voting** (APPSC-GS 2025).
Laws **cease 6 months after** the resolution lapses.
State power is **not suspended** but the Union law prevails (**Art. 251**).

nd0eb72fa667.s: Parliament can legislate on a State List subject to implement an international convention under:
nd0eb72fa667.x: Article 253 empowers Parliament to make laws implementing treaties, agreements and conventions, even on State List subjects.
xa: Applies to the **whole or any part of India**; includes decisions of **international bodies** (APPSC-GS 2018).
⚠ **252** = consent of **two or more states**; **253** = **no state consent**.

n804117c3a04.s: The Supreme Court's advisory opinion of November 2025 was reported in connection with which issue?
o: Deemed assent and timelines for Governors and the President
Allocation of residuary powers to States
Transfer of forests to the Union List
n804117c3a04.x: The advisory opinion rejected deemed assent and fixed timelines concerning Governors and the President.
n804117c3a04.tq: Identify the constitutional controversy from the paired concepts rather than from a general federalism label.
xs: The SC advisory opinion (**Nov 2025**) rejected **deemed assent** and **fixed timelines** for **Governors/President** — option **(1)**.
It concerns assent to State bills, linked to **Art. 254(2)** reservation by the Governor.
xa: Under **254(2)**, the Governor may reserve a bill as an exception to **aid-and-advice**.
A State law with **President's assent** prevails **in that State**.
Parliament can later **override** it with a fresh law.

nindian-polity-68-51.s: Parliament exercises the legislative powers of a State Legislature during President's Rule under Article:
nindian-polity-68-51.x: Under Article 356 Parliament exercises the State Legislature's powers; Article 250 applies during a National Emergency and Article 252 on request of two or more States.
n: Article 250 permits Parliament to legislate on State List subjects during the operation of a National Emergency under Article 352. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
Article 252 permits Parliament to legislate on State List subjects following requests by at least two State Legislatures through resolutions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
Article 356 permits Parliament to legislate on State List subjects following a proclamation of President’s Rule in a State. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
Under Article 356, Parliament exercises the legislative powers of the State Legislature. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
xa: The five special circumstances: **Art. 249, 250, 252, 253** and **356**.
**President's Rule laws** stay in force after PR ends until the state legislature repeals, alters or re-enacts them.
⚠ A request by **one** state is **not** valid under Art. 252.

nindian-polity-68-12.s: A law made by Parliament under Article 249 remains in force for what period after the Rajya Sabha resolution lapses?
nindian-polity-68-12.x: A law under Article 249 ceases six months after the Rajya Sabha resolution lapses (each resolution lasts one year and can be renewed).
nindian-polity-68-12.tq: Separate the one-year resolution from the six-month grace period.
n: A law enacted under Article 249 remains in force for one year. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
A law enacted under Article 249 ceases six months after the related Rajya Sabha resolution lapses. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
xs: A law made under **Article 249** ceases **six months** after the Rajya Sabha resolution lapses — option **(4)**.
The resolution needs **two-thirds of members present and voting** and is in force **not exceeding 1 year**.
xa: The resolution is **renewable** any number of times, **1 year at a time**.
The State's power to legislate on the same matter is **not suspended**.
**Art. 251:** on conflict with a law under **249/250**, the **Union** law prevails.

nindian-polity-68-13.s: A law made by Parliament on a State List subject under Article 250 ceases to have effect ____ after the National Emergency ends.
nindian-polity-68-13.x: Laws made under Article 250 lapse six months after the Emergency ends.
n: Article 250 permits Parliament to legislate on State List subjects during the operation of a National Emergency under Article 352. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
Article 250 legislation ceases six months after the National Emergency ends. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
xa: The law can extend to the **whole or any part of India**.
During an Emergency, State List laws are made by **Parliament**, not any minister (APPSC-GS 2023).
**Art. 251:** the State law is inoperative only while the Union law lasts.

nindian-polity-68-54.s: Under Article 249, a Rajya Sabha resolution authorising Parliament to legislate on a State List subject in the national interest must be passed by:
o: The unanimous vote of all Rajya Sabha members
A majority of members present and voting
At least two-thirds of the total membership of the Rajya Sabha
At least two-thirds of members present and voting
nindian-polity-68-54.x: Under Article 249 the Rajya Sabha resolution needs two-thirds of the members present and voting — not two-thirds of total membership.
n: Article 249 permits Parliament to legislate on State List subjects through a Rajya Sabha resolution in the national interest. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
An Article 249 resolution requires at least two-thirds of the members present and voting in the Rajya Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
xs: The **Article 249** resolution needs **two-thirds of members present and voting** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is **not** two-thirds of total membership, a simple majority, or unanimity.
xa: The resolution is valid **up to 1 year**, renewable.
Laws made under it **cease 6 months** after the resolution lapses.
It allows Parliament to legislate on a **State List** subject in the **national interest**.

n2f89acafa00.s: Regulations having the force of Acts of Parliament for Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep are made by the:
o: Chief Secretary of the Union Territory
n2f89acafa00.x: Regulations made by the President for Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep have the force and effect of an Act of Parliament.
xa: The **Governor** can bar/modify Parliament's Acts for **Scheduled Areas**.
The **Governor of Assam** has a similar role for Assam tribal areas.

nd4a7821504e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 254(2)?
o: A repugnant State law on a Concurrent List subject prevails in that State if it receives the President's assent
The State law must be reserved for the consideration of the President
Parliament can later amend or repeal such a State law by a fresh law
Such a State law, once assented to, prevails throughout India
nd4a7821504e.x: A State law assented to under Article 254(2) prevails only in that State, not throughout India.
xa: Repugnancy applies to the **Concurrent List** field.

nea64dff636d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about preservation of livestock (cow slaughter)?
o: Parliament can legislate on it through Articles 249, 250 or 252
Preservation of livestock is a State List subject
Article 48 is relevant to constitutional policy on preservation of livestock
Parliament may legislate on it only through the ordinary Union List power
nea64dff636d.x: Being a State subject, Parliament can legislate on it through routes such as Articles 249, 250 or 252, not through the ordinary Union List power.
xa: **Prevention of cruelty to animals** is a separate **Concurrent** subject (**Entry 17**).
Parliament can reach State subjects only via **Arts. 249, 250, 252, 253, 356**.

nindian-polity-68-7.s: Which of the following is INCORRECT about repugnancy on Concurrent List subjects?
o: Repugnancy is dealt with under Article 250.
In a conflict, the Central law generally prevails.
The Central-law rule has an exception relating to Presidential assent.
A reserved State law that gets Presidential assent may prevail under Article 254(2).
nindian-polity-68-7.x: Repugnancy on Concurrent subjects is dealt with by Article 254, not Article 250 (Emergency legislation).
n: Article 254 governs repugnancy between Central and State legislation on a Concurrent List subject. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
Central legislation prevails when it conflicts with State legislation on a Concurrent List subject. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]

A State law can prevail over conflicting Central legislation when the State law was reserved for the President’s assent and received that assent under Article 254(2). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
Article 250 permits Parliament to legislate on State List subjects during the operation of a National Emergency under Article 352. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
xa: **Proviso:** Parliament can later **override** such a State law with a **fresh law**.
**Article 250** = Parliament on the State List during an **Emergency**.

n3a41e23a204.s: Article 248 is located in which Part of the Constitution?
n3a41e23a204.x: Article 248 is located in Part XI, which deals with relations between the Union and the States and extends from Articles 245 to 263.
n3a41e23a204.tq: Match the article with its constitutional Part, not merely with its subject.
xs: **Article 248** (residuary powers) lies in **Part XI** — option **(3)**.
Part XI covers **Relations between the Union and the States**, **Art. 245-263** (APPSC-GS 2023).
Its Chapter I (**Arts. 245-255**) deals with legislative relations.
xa: **245** = territorial extent; **246** = subject-matter (three lists); **247** = additional courts.
**248** + **Entry 97 of the Union List** = Parliament's exclusive residuary power, including **taxation**.
**249 / 250** = State List — national interest / Emergency; **254** = repugnancy.

nb2f85a20b0d.s: Which case upheld a State prohibition law under the doctrine of pith and substance?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Prafulla Kumar Mukherjee v. Bank of Commerce
State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara
K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo v. State of Orissa
nb2f85a20b0d.x: In State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara (1951), the prohibition law was upheld under pith and substance; its incidental encroachment did not change its true character.
xa: ⚠ **Balsara (1951)** = pith and substance; **Gajapati Narayan Deo (1953)** = colourable legislation.
**Harmonious construction**: entries read together so both operate.
**Repugnancy (Art. 254)**: Union law prevails in the **Concurrent** field.

nb4982bbb9b5.s: Which doctrine requires legislative entries to be read together so that each can operate harmoniously?
nb4982bbb9b5.x: Harmonious construction requires apparently overlapping entries to be interpreted together so that both retain operative effect.
nb4982bbb9b5.tq: Discriminate among neighbouring doctrines by their operative principle.
xs: **Harmonious construction** reads entries together so that **both operate** — option **(2)**.
**Pith and substance** looks at a law's **true nature**; **repugnancy** (**Art. 254**) makes Union law prevail; **colourable legislation** bars doing indirectly what cannot be done directly.
xa: Pith and substance case: **State of Bombay v F.N. Balsara (1951)**.
Colourable legislation case: **K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo v State of Orissa (1953)**.
Under **254(2)**, a State law with **President's assent** prevails in that State.

nindian-polity-67-4.s: What is the effect of the Doctrine of Severability?
o: The whole statute is declared void
Only the unconstitutional part is declared void, if separable
A law is tested only by its title
Parliament must re-enact the entire law
nindian-polity-67-4.x: Under severability, only the unconstitutional part of a law is struck down if it can be separated; the rest survives.
n: Only the offending or unconstitutional portion of a statute is declared void under the Doctrine of Severability. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 178-181]
The valid portion of a statute remains intact under the Doctrine of Severability if it can be separated from the offending portion. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 178-181]
xa: Cases: **A.K. Gopalan (1950)** and **State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara (1951)**.
⚠ **Eclipse** concerns **pre-constitutional** laws, which stay **dormant**, not permanently void.
Most doctrines are **judicially evolved**, not written in the Constitution.

nindian-polity-67-7.s: A pre-Constitution law that conflicts with a Fundamental Right stays dormant and revives if that right is amended. This is the Doctrine of:
nindian-polity-67-7.x: Under the doctrine of eclipse such a law is not dead ab initio but only overshadowed, and it revives when the right is amended.
n: Pre-constitutional laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are not dead ab initio under the Doctrine of Eclipse. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 178-181]
Pre-constitutional laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights remain overshadowed or dormant under the Doctrine of Eclipse. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 178-181]
A pre-constitutional law eclipsed by Fundamental Rights becomes active if the relevant Fundamental Right is amended. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 178-181]
xa: **Severability:** only the **offending portion** is void.
**Basic Structure:** **Kesavananda Bharati (1973)**, **Article 368**.

nindian-polity-67-13.s: Judicial review by the higher judiciary tests the constitutional validity of:
o: Both legislative acts and executive actions
nindian-polity-67-13.x: Judicial review is the higher judiciary's power to test both laws and executive action.
n: Most constitutional doctrines in India are not expressly defined in the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 178-181]
Most constitutional doctrines in India are not written in the text of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 178-181]

The higher judiciary, comprising the Supreme Court and High Courts, can adjudicate the constitutional validity of legislative acts and executive actions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 178-181]
xa: Origin: **Marbury v. Madison (1803)** — **John Marshall** (USA).
**Colorable legislation:** **Kameshwar Singh v. State of Bihar (1952)**.

nindian-polity-67-25.s: 'What cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly' is the principle behind the Doctrine of:
nindian-polity-67-25.x: This maxim underlies the doctrine of colourable legislation, which checks whether a legislature crosses its competence under a permissible guise.
n: The principle of Colorable Legislation is that what cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 178-181]
The Doctrine of Colorable Legislation concerns transgression of legislative competence masked under a permissible guise. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 178-181]
xa: Case: **Kameshwar Singh v. State of Bihar (1952)**; basis **Article 246**.
⚠ Other notes cite **K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo v. State of Orissa (1953)**.
⚠ **Balsara (1951)** = pith and substance; **Gajapati Narayan Deo (1953)** = colourable legislation.

n8fe80c73dbb.s: The Union List and Concurrent List originally had 97 and 47 subjects. How many do they have today?
n8fe80c73dbb.x: The Union List now has 98 subjects (97 originally) and the Concurrent List 52 (47 originally).
xa: Some notes (UPSC) give the present counts as **100 / 61 / 52**.
⚠ **Safe exam fact:** original **97/66/47**.
**Entry 97** of the Union List is also the **residuary** entry.

ndf27be28d84.s: Which of the following examples has been cited in debates concerning use of the Concurrent List to reach State subjects?
o: Farm Laws through Concurrent List Entry 33
Currency regulation through State List Entry 15
Foreign affairs through Concurrent List Entry 3
ndf27be28d84.x: Farm Laws were discussed as an example of Concurrent List Entry 33 being used in a field associated with agriculture, which is State List Entry 14.
ndf27be28d84.tq: Match the debated law with the relevant Concurrent List entry and the associated State subject.
xs: **Farm Laws** were made via **Concurrent List Entry 33** — option **(2)**.
Critics say this reached a **State** subject, as agriculture is **State List Entry 14**.
**Census**, **currency** and **foreign affairs** are **Union** subjects, so the other options are wrong.
xa: The **NEP** and **NMC Act** are also cited in the Concurrent List encroachment debate.
Other centralising tools: **Art. 254(2)** override; **Art. 249/252** use.
**Frequent ordinances** and **Union List dominance** are also criticised.

nindian-polity-68-5.s: Education was moved from the State List to the Concurrent List by the:
nindian-polity-68-5.x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) moved Education from the State List to the Concurrent List.
n: Railways are a Union List subject. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
Police is a State List subject. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
Education is a Concurrent List subject. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
Education was shifted to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
Marriage is a Concurrent List subject. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
Divorce is a Concurrent List subject. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
Adoption is a Concurrent List subject. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
Railways belong to the Union List. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
Police belongs to the State List. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
xa: Entry counts: Union **97** → **98**; State **66** → **59**; Concurrent **47** → **52**.
The Concurrent List follows the **Government of India Act 1935** tradition; the scheme is borrowed from **Canada**.
⚠ Original counts **97/66/47** are the safe exam fact.

ncd63d15e6ff.s: The scheme of distribution of legislative powers in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the constitution of:
ncd63d15e6ff.x: India's scheme of legislative distribution follows the Canadian model.
xa: **Residuary power** with the Centre also follows **Canada** (strong Centre).
USA and Australia leave the residue with the **states**.
Original counts: **97/66/47**.

nb798a6a3543.s: What did the Sarkaria Commission recommend regarding residuary powers, apart from taxation?
o: Giving residuary taxation exclusively to the States
Moving all residuary powers except taxation to the Concurrent List
Transferring all residuary powers to the State List
nb798a6a3543.x: The Sarkaria Commission in 1988 recommended moving all residuary powers other than taxation to the Concurrent List.
nb798a6a3543.tq: Identify the precise exception in a commission recommendation.
xs: The **Sarkaria Commission (1988)** recommended **moving all residuary powers except taxation to the Concurrent List** — option **(3)**.
Residuary **taxation** would stay with **Parliament**.
xa: At present **Art. 248** + **Entry 97** give **Parliament** exclusive residuary power.
The model is **Canada**; USA and Australia leave residue with the **states**.
Original Concurrent List count: **47**; now **52**.

nindian-polity-68-4.s: Under Article 246, legislative competence over the Concurrent List rests with:
o: Parliament only during a National Emergency
nindian-polity-68-4.x: Under Article 246, Parliament alone legislates on the Union List, States on the State List, and both on the Concurrent List.
n: Parliament has exclusive legislative competence over List I, the Union List, under Article 246(1). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
State Legislatures have exclusive legislative competence over List II, the State List, under Article 246(3). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
Both Parliament and State Legislatures have concurrent legislative competence over List III, the Concurrent List, under Article 246(2). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
xa: **Precedence:** **Union List > Concurrent List > State List**.
**Article 246A** (**101st Amendment, 2016**) gives **simultaneous** GST power to Parliament and States.

n7679943c96c.s: In Scheduled Areas, who may bar or modify the application of Acts of Parliament?
n7679943c96c.x: The Governor may bar or modify the application of Acts of Parliament in Scheduled Areas.
xa: The **Governor of Assam** has a similar power for **Assam tribal areas**.
**President's regulations** for **Andaman & Nicobar** and **Lakshadweep** carry the force of Parliament's Acts.
⚠ **Extra-territorial** laws = Parliament only.

na39eaff4055.s: Which one of the following is NOT an example of legislation enacted under Article 252?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
na39eaff4055.x: The Prize Competition Act, 1955, the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 were enacted under Article 252 on resolutions of two or more States. The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is not an Article 252 law; it was enacted to implement an international (Stockholm) commitment, i.e. under Article 253.
na39eaff4055.tq: Find the option outside the specified group of Article 252 examples.
xs: The **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** is NOT in the list of **Art. 252** Acts — option **(2)**.
Art. 252 Acts: **Prize Competition (1955)**, **Wild Life (Protection) (1972)**, **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) (1974)**.
xa: Others: **Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976**; **Transplantation of Human Organs Act, 1994**.
**Art. 253** covers **environment treaties** — no State consent needed.
⚠ **252** = consent of **two or more States**; **253** = treaties.

nd4f74c455da.s: The Transplantation of Human Organs Act, 1994 was enacted by Parliament under Article:
nd4f74c455da.x: It is an example of a law made by Parliament under Article 252 following resolutions by two or more State Legislatures.
xa: Also under Art. 252: **Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972** and **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974**.
Only **Parliament** can amend/repeal these; the requesting States lose that power.
Other States may **adopt** the law by resolution.

n9426404df55.s: The MMDR (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was reported as restricting the States' power to tax which subject?
n9426404df55.x: The Bill was reported as restricting State taxation power over mineral rights and mineral-bearing land. Kerala viewed this as encroachment on State List Entries 18 and 50.
n9426404df55.tq: Match the legislative development with the precise fiscal subject affected.
xs: The **MMDR (Amendment) Bill, 2026** restricts States' power to tax **mineral rights and mineral-bearing land** — option **(3)**.
**Kerala** called it an encroachment on State **Entries 18 and 50** and may go to court (**15 Aug 2026**).
xa: Preventive detention: **Union Entry 9** + **Concurrent Entry 3**.
**Sarkaria Commission (1988)** recommended moving non-tax residuary powers to the **Concurrent List**.

nf32c35ac389.s: The constitutional basis for Parliament enacting the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act is primarily found in which entry?
nf32c35ac389.x: Prevention of cruelty to animals is placed in Concurrent List Entry 17, enabling Parliament to enact central legislation on the subject.
nf32c35ac389.tq: Distinguish the Concurrent List entry on animal cruelty from the State entry on preservation of livestock.
xs: **Prevention of cruelty to animals** is **Concurrent List Entry 17** — the basis of the central **Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act** — option **(1)**.
**State Entry 15** is **preservation of livestock**; **Concurrent Entry 33** was used for the **Farm Laws**.
xa: Cow slaughter: preservation of livestock = **State** subject (**Entry 15**) + DPSP **Art. 48**.
Other Concurrent subjects: **criminal law**, **civil procedure**, **succession**, **marriage and divorce**.

nindian-polity-68-47.s: Under Article 250, laws made by Parliament on State List subjects may extend to:
o: Only the State where the emergency originated
The whole or any part of India
nindian-polity-68-47.x: Under Article 250, during a National Emergency, Parliament's laws on State subjects can extend to the whole or any part of India. 'Only consenting States' describes Article 252.
n: Article 250 permits Parliament to legislate on State List subjects during the operation of a National Emergency under Article 352. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
Article 250 legislation can extend to the whole or any part of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #68 · pp 181-185]
xs: Under **Article 250**, laws on State List subjects may extend to **the whole or any part of India** — option **(2)**.
"Only the consenting States" describes **Article 252**, not 250.
xa: Such laws cease **six months** after the Emergency ends.
**Art. 252** laws can be amended or repealed **only by Parliament**; other states may adopt them by resolution.
**Art. 253** laws can also cover the **whole or any part of India**.

ne2bfb82a0c9.s: Under Article 73, the executive power of the Union extends to matters on which ____ can make laws.
ne2bfb82a0c9.x: Article 73 extends Union executive power to matters on which Parliament can legislate and to rights and authority under treaties or agreements.
xa: On **Concurrent** subjects, executive power **stays with the states** unless the Constitution or a Parliamentary law expressly gives it to the Centre.
**Territorial spread** of executive power follows that of **legislative** power.

n944f4d09c7f.s: Article 154 of the Constitution vests the executive power of a State in the
n944f4d09c7f.x: Article 154 vests the executive power of the State in the Governor, who may exercise it directly or through subordinate officers.
n944f4d09c7f.tq: Discriminate between the constitutional vesting authority and the holder of real political power.
xs: **Art. 154** vests the State's executive power in the **Governor**, exercised directly or through subordinate officers — option **(4)**.
⚠ UPSC notes place it in the **Council of Ministers** — that is where **real power** lies, but the Article vests it in the Governor.
xa: **Art. 163(1)**: Council of Ministers aids and advises the Governor, except in **discretionary** matters.
**Art. 162**: extent — matters in the **State List**, within the State.
Union counterpart: **Art. 53** — vests in the **President**.

ncf6f14c2da6.s: The executive power of a State under Article 162 ordinarily extends to matters on which the
o: State Legislature can legislate within the territory of the State
Union Parliament can legislate throughout India
ncf6f14c2da6.x: Article 162 extends State executive power to matters on which the State Legislature has power to make laws, within the State's territory.
ncf6f14c2da6.tq: Match the extent of executive power with the corresponding legislative competence.
xs: **Art. 162**: State executive power extends to matters on which the **State Legislature can legislate**, within the **State's territory** — option **(1)**.
Union counterpart: **Art. 73** — matters on which **Parliament** legislates, across **the whole of India**.
xa: Concurrent subjects: executive power **stays with the states**, unless the Constitution or a Parliamentary law expressly provides (**proviso to Art. 73 and Art. 162**).
**Territorial spread** of executive power follows **legislative** power.

nde070d0a7a5.s: In a Union Territory, executive power is ordinarily exercised by the:
o: Chief Secretary of the Union Territory
Union Home Minister in every matter
Lieutenant Governor or Administrator, as the President's representative
nde070d0a7a5.x: The Lieutenant Governor or Administrator exercises executive power in a Union Territory as the President's representative.
xa: **LGs**: **Delhi**, **Puducherry**, **J&K**, **Ladakh**, **Andaman & Nicobar**.
**Administrators**: **Chandigarh** (Punjab Governor), **Lakshadweep**, **Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu**.
**Delhi — Art. 239AA (69th Amendment, 1991)**: Legislative Assembly + Council of Ministers; **public order, police and land** outside its power.

n7db25aaccd0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the executive power of the Union?
o: The President's power as Supreme Commander is not subject to regulation by law
It may be exercised through subordinate officers
It may be exercised directly by the President
The President is the Supreme Commander of the armed forces
n7db25aaccd0.x: The President's power as Supreme Commander of the armed forces is regulated by law.
xa: The President is the **constitutional (formal) head**; real power lies with the Council, **collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha**.
State counterpart: **Art. 154** vests executive power in the **Governor**.

na19d77143ab.s: In relation to remission under Article 161, the Supreme Court has held that the Governor is bound by the advice of the
na19d77143ab.x: The Governor must act on the advice of the State Cabinet while exercising the remission power under Article 161.
na19d77143ab.tq: Identify the correct advising authority in a State executive function.
xs: The SC held the Governor **bound by State Cabinet advice** — the **State Council of Ministers** — when granting **remission** under **Art. 161** (**Apr 2026**) — option **(3)**.
**Art. 163(1)**: the Council aids and advises the Governor, except in **discretionary** matters.
xa: Governors skipping the **address to the legislature** test constitutional limits (Jan 2026).
Precedents: **Shamsher Singh (1974)**, **Nabam Rebia (2016)**.

n5158d33693b.s: Executive power over Concurrent List subjects ordinarily rests with:
o: the States, subject to constitutional or statutory exceptions
n5158d33693b.x: By default, executive power over Concurrent subjects stays with the States; the Centre exercises it only where the Constitution or a Parliamentary law expressly provides.
xa: **Art. 73**: Union executive covers matters in the **Union List** + **treaties**.
**Art. 162**: State executive covers matters in the **State List**.

n71adeeef80c.s: How does Article 258(2) differ from Article 258(1)?
o: It applies only during a National Emergency
It concerns inter-State agreements on river-valley projects
It lets Parliament by law confer duties on State officers without State consent
It lets the Governor transfer State functions to the Union
n71adeeef80c.x: Under Article 258(2), Parliament may by law confer powers or duties on State officers without State consent; Article 258(1) involves Presidential entrustment with State consent.
xa: **258A** = State entrusting functions to the **Union** (APPSC-GS 2023).

nad3b4604607.s: Failure of a State to comply with Union directions may be treated as a breakdown of constitutional machinery under Article:
nad3b4604607.x: Article 365 allows such non-compliance to be treated as a breakdown of constitutional machinery, opening the way to action under Article 356.
xa: Under **Art. 356**, the President takes over the State's executive functions; **High Court powers untouched**.

nfd72795a82f.s: Article 258A of the Constitution deals with:
o: Agreements between States on river valley projects
Power of a State, with the consent of the Union Government, to entrust its functions to the Union
Entrustment of Union functions to States by Parliament without State consent
Directions of the Union to States during a Financial Emergency
nfd72795a82f.x: Article 258A lets a State entrust its functions to the Union (APPSC-GS 2023). Calling it 'agreements between States on river valley projects' is a known wrong statement. Entrustment by Parliament without consent is Article 258(2), and Financial Emergency directions fall under Article 360.
xs: **Art. 258A**: a **State** entrusts its **functions to the Union** — option **(2)** (APPSC-GS 2023).
⚠ UPSC notes call 258A "agreements between states on **river valley projects**" — **WRONG**.
**258(2)** (not 258A) lets Parliament confer duties on State officers without consent.
xa: **258(1)**: President, **with the state's consent**, entrusts Union functions to the State.
Financial Emergency directions come under **Art. 360**, not 258A.

n4f3f7ffd1c4.s: Under Article 356, the powers of which of the following remain untouched when President's Rule is imposed in a State?
n4f3f7ffd1c4.x: Article 356 expressly leaves the powers of the State High Court untouched; the President takes over the executive and the Council of Ministers is dismissed.
xa: Non-compliance with Union directions (**Art. 365**) can lead to **Art. 356**.
Contrast: National Emergency (**Art. 353**) does **not suspend** State governments.

n855c942247c.s: Under Article 353, what is the effect of a National Emergency on executive relations?
o: State governments are suspended and replaced by administrators
The Union may direct States on any matter, but State governments are not suspended
The State Council of Ministers is dismissed in every State
The powers of the High Courts pass to the Union executive
n855c942247c.x: During a National Emergency the Union's power of direction expands under Article 353, but State governments continue and are not suspended.
xa: ⚠ National Emergency = state governments **not suspended**; President's Rule = Council **dismissed**.
**Art. 360**: Centre directs **financial propriety**; **Money and Financial Bills** may be reserved for the President.

n2008b52f71a.s: Which of the following is a possible effect of a Financial Emergency under Article 360?
o: The Union automatically assumes all State legislative powers
State Money and Financial Bills may be reserved for the President
n2008b52f71a.x: During a Financial Emergency, the Centre may require Money Bills and other Financial Bills of States to be reserved for the President's consideration.
xa: National Emergency (**Art. 353**): directions to **any state on any matter**.
President's Rule (**Art. 356**): State Council of Ministers **dismissed**; **High Court powers untouched**.

ne6832244be9.s: Article 239AA, giving Delhi a Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers, was inserted by the:
ne6832244be9.x: The 69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991 inserted Article 239AA.
xa: **Public order**, **police** and **land** are outside the Assembly's power.
Delhi is headed by an **LG**.
**Art. 239**: UTs administered by the **President through an Administrator**.

nf6b10dca97d.s:
Under Article 239AA, which of the following are outside the legislative competence of the Delhi Legislative Assembly?
1. Public order
2. Land
3. Public health
Which of the above is/are correct?
nf6b10dca97d.x: Public order, police and land are excluded from the Delhi Assembly's competence under Article 239AA; public health is not among them.
xa: **Art. 239AA** inserted by the **69th Amendment, 1991**.
Delhi has a **Legislative Assembly** + **Council of Ministers**.
⚠ In States, **public order** and **police** are State List subjects.

naab9b70ade8.s: Which Article requires that the executive power of every State be exercised so as to ensure compliance with the laws made by Parliament?
naab9b70ade8.x: Article 256 requires State executive power to ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament and permits the Union to issue directions for that purpose.
naab9b70ade8.tq: Discriminate between the two adjacent Articles dealing with Union directions to States.
xs: **Article 256**: states must exercise executive power **in compliance with Parliament's laws**; Union may direct — option **(1)**.
**Art. 257** = do **not impede the Union**; **Art. 365** = failure to follow directions; **Art. 258** = delegation.
xa: Under **Art. 257** the Centre directs on **means of communication** and protection of **railways**.
**Art. 365** → **President's Rule (Art. 356)**.
During **National Emergency**, directions may be on **any matter**.

nc115cb7b266.s: If a State fails to comply with Union directions, which Article lets the President hold that its government cannot be carried on per the Constitution?
nc115cb7b266.x: Article 365 lets the President draw that conclusion when a State fails to comply with Union directions, which can open the way to action under Article 356.
xa: Asked in **PYQ 2017, 2018**.
**Art. 256**: compliance with **Parliament's laws**.

nb3743ec04bb.s: Grants under Article 275 are specifically associated with:
o: discretionary grants for any public purpose
compensation to States for GST revenue loss
Scheduled Tribe welfare and administration of Scheduled Areas
nb3743ec04bb.x: Article 275 provides grants for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes and the administration of Scheduled Areas; discretionary grants for any public purpose fall under Article 282.
xa: **Art. 339**: Union directions on **welfare schemes for STs**.
**Art. 261**: **full faith and credit** to public acts, records, judicial proceedings.
Constitutional devices: **ISC (Art. 263)**, **Art. 262**, **Art. 307**.

nc791e41f0a2.s:
Under Article 257, the Union may issue directions to a State regarding:
1. Means of communication of national or military importance
2. All matters of public order in the State
3. Protection of railways within the State
Which of the above is/are correct?
nc791e41f0a2.x: Article 257 covers communications of national or military importance and protection of railways; public order is not among its direction powers.
xa: Art. 257: state executive must **not impede the Union**.
**Art. 339**: welfare schemes for **STs**; **Art. 350A**: **mother-tongue** instruction.
Non-compliance → **Art. 365** → **Art. 356**.

nbae0746b85e.s:
The Administrative Reforms Commission recommended:
1. Establishment of an Inter-State Council
2. Appointment of non-partisan Governors
3. Abolition of all advisory bodies
Which of the above is/are correct?
nbae0746b85e.x: The ARC urged an Inter-State Council and non-partisan Governors; it did not recommend abolishing all advisory bodies.
xa: ARC (**1966**): **Morarji Desai**, then **K. Hanumanthaiya**; **M.C. Setalvad** study team (1969).
**Sarkaria** too recommended a **permanent ISC**.
**ISC** today **meets rarely**.

n3a625a337e5.s: Under Article 312 of the Constitution, Parliament may create a new All India Service when the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by:
o: A majority of the members present and voting
A simple majority of the total membership
Two-thirds of the members present and voting
n3a625a337e5.x: Article 312 requires a Rajya Sabha resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting before Parliament can create a new All India Service.
n3a625a337e5.tq: Check the exact constitutional majority instead of confusing present-and-voting with total membership.
xs: **Art. 312** needs a **Rajya Sabha** resolution by **2/3 of members present and voting** — option **(4)**.
Only then may Parliament create a new All India Service, including an **All India Judicial Service**.
xa: Existing AIS: **IAS, IPS, IFoS** (Indian Forest Service).
Governed by the **All India Services Act, 1951**.
Suggestion: create new AIS for **health and education**.

nba1bcb3066d.s: Which one of the following services is specifically mentioned in Article 312 as capable of being created as an All India Service?
nba1bcb3066d.x: Article 312 expressly includes the possibility of creating an All India Judicial Service.
nba1bcb3066d.tq: Identify the constitutionally named service rather than an existing Central Service.
xs: **Art. 312** expressly allows an **All India Judicial Service** — option **(4)**.
The **Indian Foreign Service** is a **Central Service**, not an AIS.
xa: Creation needs a **Rajya Sabha** resolution by **2/3 of members present and voting**.
Existing AIS: **IAS, IPS, IFoS**; **Indian Forest Service** created **1966**.
⚠ **IFoS** = Indian Forest Service (AIS); **IFS** = Indian Foreign Service (Central Service).

n22bb7496cb5.s: The Indian Forest Service, an All India Service, was created in:
n22bb7496cb5.x: The Indian Forest Service was created in 1966; it is an All India Service along with the IAS and IPS.
xa: ⚠ **IFoS** = Indian Forest Service (AIS); **IFS** = Indian Foreign Service (Central Service).
**ICS** restructured as **IAS in 1947**.
**Indian Revenue Service (IRS)** is also a **Central Service** — Union subjects only.

nf5da0c320d0.s: Officers of the All India Services are recruited on an all-India basis by the:
nf5da0c320d0.x: UPSC recruits them; the Centre trains them and they serve in State cadres.
xa: Governed by **All India Services Act, 1951**.
Federal critique: officers governed by **Central rules**; states lack full control.
**UPSC** replaced the Federal PSC in **1950**.

nfa0bf0ed416.s: Who described the All India Services as the 'Steel Frame' of India?
nfa0bf0ed416.x: Sardar Patel championed the All India Services and called them the 'Steel Frame' of India.
xa: **ICS** restructured as **IAS in 1947**.
**UPSC** replaced the **Federal PSC** in **1950**.
**Indian Forest Service** created **1966**.

n8e1aece6650.s: Why are All India Services sometimes criticised from the federal perspective?
o: Their officers are governed by Central rules and States lack full control over them.
They are confined entirely to local government administration.
They are recruited exclusively by State Public Service Commissions.
They have no connection with the Union Government.
n8e1aece6650.x: The federal criticism is that Central rules govern the officers and States do not exercise full control over them, thereby restricting State autonomy.
n8e1aece6650.tq: Apply the federal-autonomy principle to identify the institutional source of friction.
xs: AIS officers are governed by **Central rules** and **states lack full control** — option **(1)**.
So they are a **unitary feature** restricting state autonomy.
xa: **APPSC-G2 2025**: A and R both true, R explains A.
Removal only by the **Union government** (PYQ 2017, 2019).
**IAS (Cadre) Rules, 1954** amendments: central deputation **without state or officer consent**.

n30063c15aa3.s: The proposed amendments to the All India Services (Cadre) Rules, 1954 were associated with which issue?
o: Compulsory retirement of all AIS officers by State Governments
Central deputation without the consent of the State or the officer
Replacement of UPSC recruitment by direct State recruitment
Abolition of State cadres for All India Services
n30063c15aa3.x: The proposed amendments would enable the Centre to order central deputation without the consent of the State Government or the officer, with the Centre's order becoming final after a prescribed time.
n30063c15aa3.tq: Focus on the authority and consent issue in the cadre-rule proposal.
xs: **IAS (Cadre) Rules, 1954** amendments let the Centre order **central deputation without state or officer consent** — option **(2)**.
The Centre's order becomes **final after a set time**.
xa: Criticism: **unilateral** central deputation hurts state bureaucracy's **morale**.
AIS are a **unitary feature**; states lack full control.
Removal only by the **Union government**.

n1b41eecce65.s: A member of an All India Service serving in a State cadre can be dismissed or removed from service only by:
o: The State Government in whose cadre the officer serves
The Governor on the advice of the State Public Service Commission
n1b41eecce65.x: An All India Service officer can be dismissed or removed only by the Union Government, even though he serves under the State. The State Government and the Governor cannot remove him, and the UPSC only recruits; it is not the removing authority.
n1b41eecce65.tq: Serves the State, removed only by the Union.
xs: An AIS officer can be **dismissed or removed only by the Union Government** — option **(2)**.
Not by the **state** whose cadre he serves; **UPSC** only recruits.
xa: Asked in **PYQ 2017, 2019** and **APPSC-G1 2019**.
The **Centre recruits and trains**; officers serve in **state cadres**.
Federal critique: states **lack full control**.

nbf2ce1eaf30.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about inter-State water disputes?
o: The Mullaperiyar dam is located on the Godavari river
The Mahanadi dispute is between Odisha and Chhattisgarh
The Mullaperiyar dam is situated in Kerala
The Mullaperiyar dam is operated by Tamil Nadu under a lease
nbf2ce1eaf30.x: Mullaperiyar is on the Periyar, not the Godavari.
xa: Mullaperiyar dam dates to **1895**.
SC-directed **Supervisory Committee** involves the **National Dam Safety Authority** (**Dam Safety Act, 2021**).
**Godavari** is one of the tribunals AP is party to, with **Krishna** and **Vansadhara**.

n00bec134a3e.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes All India Services from Central Services?
o: Central Services serve in State cadres; All India Services only in Union ministries
All India Services are confined to Union subjects; Central Services are common to Union and States
All India Services are common to Union and States; Central Services relate to Union subjects only
Both are recruited only by State Public Service Commissions
n00bec134a3e.x: All India Services are common to the Union and the States, while Central Services relate to Union subjects only.
xa: AIS: **IAS, IPS, IFoS**; Central Services: e.g. **Indian Foreign Service**, **IRS**.
State civil and police services = **State Services**.
PYQ 2007 asked this "common to Union and states" point.

n3c42b7d5717.s: A Joint State Public Service Commission is created by ____, and its members are appointed by ____.
o: an Act of Parliament; the President
a State law; the Chief Ministers concerned
the UPSC; the Union Home Minister
n3c42b7d5717.x: A Joint State Public Service Commission is created by an Act of Parliament, and its members are appointed by the President.
xa: Art. 315 also provides **UPSC** and an **SPSC** for each state.
⚠ JSPSC = **Act of Parliament**; CAT = **Art. 323A**.
**UPSC** replaced the **Federal PSC** in **1950**.

n5747c95dcc4.s: Article 323A, inserted by which Constitutional Amendment, deals with administrative tribunals for the Union and the States?
n5747c95dcc4.x: Article 323A was inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, to provide for administrative tribunals.
n5747c95dcc4.tq: Match the constitutional provision with its exact amendment year.
xs: **Art. 323A** was inserted by the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976** — option **(3)**.
It provides tribunals for Union and states, individually or **jointly**.
xa: **CAT**: **Administrative Tribunals Act 1985**.
CAT: principal bench **New Delhi** + **18 benches**; **69 members**.
The **42nd CAA** also inserted **Entry 2A** of the Union List.

nf12dac7cba9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sarkaria Commission?
o: It recommended a temporary Inter-State Council convened only during emergencies
It was set up in June 1983 under Justice R.S. Sarkaria
It recommended that Article 356 be used sparingly
nf12dac7cba9.x: The Sarkaria Commission recommended a permanent Inter-State Council, not a temporary one.
xa: Other members: **B. Sivaraman**, **S.R. Sen**.
**ARC (1966)** had also urged an **Inter-State Council**.
**ISC** = constitutional device under **Art. 263**.

n8e700c93d77.s: The authority that may be established under Article 307 is associated with
n8e700c93d77.x: Article 307 provides for an authority to carry out the purposes of the constitutional provisions relating to trade, commerce and intercourse within India.
n8e700c93d77.tq: Link the Article number with the specific federal function it supports.
xs: **Art. 307** provides an **inter-state trade authority** — option **(1)**.
It is a **constitutional device** of cooperation, with **Art. 263** and **Art. 262**.
xa: **Inter-State Council** = **Art. 263**; **water disputes** = **Art. 262**.
Extra-constitutional devices: **NDC**, **NE Council**, **Governors' Conference**, **CMs' Conference**.
Administrative tribunals = **Art. 323A**.

n0cfb9604883.s: Article 261 of the Constitution provides for which of the following?
o: Uniformity of service conditions in All-India Services
Distribution of financial resources between the Union and the States
Full faith and credit throughout India to public acts, records and judicial proceedings
Adjudication of inter-State river water disputes
n0cfb9604883.x: Article 261 requires full faith and credit throughout India to public acts, records and judicial proceedings of the Union and every State.
n0cfb9604883.tq: Directly match the Article with its constitutional principle.
xs: **Art. 261**: **full faith and credit** throughout India to **public acts, records and judicial proceedings** — option **(3)**.
Water disputes = **Art. 262**; asked in **APPSC-GS 2023**.
xa: **Art. 261(3)**: final civil court judgments can be **executed anywhere** in India.
**Integrated judiciary**: HC judges appointed by the President consulting **CJI + Governor**.
A **common HC** for 2+ states is possible.

nb38b844ce00.s: Which one of the following extra-constitutional devices of Centre-State cooperation is presided over by the President?
nb38b844ce00.x: The Governors' Conference is presided over by the President. The Chief Ministers' Conference is presided over by the Prime Minister; the Chief Secretaries' Conference and the Central Council for Local Government are other extra-constitutional devices not chaired by the President.
nb38b844ce00.tq: Governors meet the President; CMs meet the PM.
xs: The **Governors' Conference** is chaired by the **President** — option **(2)**.
⚠ The **CMs' Conference** is chaired by the **PM**.
xa: Other extra-constitutional devices: **NDC**, **Central Council of Health**, **Central Council for Local Government**, **NE Council**, **Chief Secretaries' Conference**.
Constitutional devices: **ISC (Art. 263)**, **Art. 262**, **Art. 307**.
**ISC** meets rarely.

nd0f85f9375c.s: Article 258A was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
nd0f85f9375c.x: Article 258A was inserted by the Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956.
nd0f85f9375c.tq: Link the Article with the specific amendment year while avoiding the nearby 42nd Amendment association.
xs: **Art. 258A** was inserted by the **Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956** (7th CAA) — option **(3)**.
It lets the **Governor** entrust state functions to the Union with **GoI consent**.
xa: **42nd CAA, 1976** inserted **Art. 323A** and **Entry 2A** of the Union List.
**States Reorganisation Act** was passed in **November 1956**.
**258(1)** notification is a **legislative act**, specific or general.

n329a000feba.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five Zonal Councils established under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
n329a000feba.x: The five councils are Northern, Central, Eastern, Western and Southern. The North-Eastern Council was created separately under the North-Eastern Council Act, 1971.
n329a000feba.tq: Find the body created under a separate law rather than under the 1956 Act.
xs: There is **no North-Eastern Zonal Council** — option **(1)**.
The **5 councils** are **Northern, Central, Eastern, Western, Southern**; the **NEC** came under a separate **NEC Act, 1971**.
xa: NEC **2002 amendment** added **Sikkim** and made it a **regional planning body**.
Since **2018** the **Union Home Minister** is ex-officio NEC Chairman.
Zonal Councils were proposed by **Nehru** in **1956**.

nacdae97669c.s: Zonal Councils are best described as:
o: statutory advisory bodies whose recommendations are not binding
executive bodies that allocate State finances
constitutional bodies that can dissolve State Legislatures
judicial bodies whose decisions bind the States
nacdae97669c.x: Zonal Councils are statutory, deliberative and advisory bodies; their recommendations do not bind the States.
xa: ⚠ Zonal Councils = **statutory**, not constitutional; **NEC** = separate Act (**1971**).
**5 councils**, all chaired by the **Union Home Minister**.
**31st Southern Zonal Council** met **20 Aug 2026** near **Mamallapuram**.

n7068a302628.s: Which one of the following is correct about the chairmanship of the Zonal Councils?
o: The Chief Minister of the largest State chairs each council permanently
The President chairs them; the Union Home Minister is vice-chairman
The Union Home Minister chairs all five; vice-chairmanship rotates annually among member Chief Ministers
The Prime Minister chairs them; Governors are permanent vice-chairpersons
n7068a302628.x: The Union Home Minister is the common Chairman of all five Zonal Councils, and the vice-chairmanship rotates annually among the Chief Ministers of member States.
xa: **31st Southern Zonal Council**: chaired by **Amit Shah**; vice-chairman TN CM **C. Joseph Vijay**.
Southern Zonal Council: **AP, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana, Puducherry**.
⚠ Older APP table leaves out **Telangana**.

n6385fb2811e.s: Which one of the following is NOT a member of the Southern Zonal Council?
n6385fb2811e.x: The Southern Zonal Council comprises Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana and the UT of Puducherry. Telangana (often left out of older tables) and Puducherry are members, as is Kerala; Goa is not among the members.
n6385fb2811e.tq: South = AP, TN, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana + Puducherry.
xs: **Goa** is not in the **Southern Zonal Council** — option **(3)**.
Members: **Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana, Puducherry**.
xa: ⚠ Older APP table leaves out **Telangana**.
**31st Southern Zonal Council**: **20 Aug 2026** near **Mamallapuram, Tamil Nadu**.
**5 councils**: Northern, Central, Eastern, Western, Southern — proposed by **Nehru** in 1956.

nf2cc934d2f2.s: The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 reorganised India into:
nf2cc934d2f2.x: The States Reorganisation Act, passed in November 1956, created 14 States and 6 Union Territories. The other combinations are incorrect. The same Act set up the five Zonal Councils in its Part III.
xs: The **States Reorganisation Act, 1956** (passed **November 1956**) created **14 states and 6 Union Territories** — option **(1)**.
This was the **MPPSC 2025** key.
xa: Its **Part III** set up the **5 Zonal Councils**.
**Andhra Pradesh (1 Nov 1956)**: Telangana merged with Andhra State.
**Kerala**: **Travancore-Cochin + Malabar**.

nee6b4fe7365.s: In discharging its duty under Article 355, the Union may deploy armed or central forces in a State:
o: only with the State Government's consent
with or without the State's consent
only when the State Legislature authorises it
only after a National Emergency is proclaimed
nee6b4fe7365.x: The Union may deploy armed or central forces with or without State consent in discharge of its Article 355 duty.
xa: Basis: **Entry 2A, Union List** (**42nd CAA**).
**ARC (1966)** backed deployment "**on their request or otherwise**".
~**13,000** CAPF officers in the CAPF dispute.

n16771f1404e.s: The constitutional basis associated with Union deployment of armed or central forces in States is:
o: Entry 2A of the Union List, inserted through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment
Entry 97 of the Concurrent List, inserted through the First Amendment
Entry 1 of the State List, inserted through the Seventh Amendment
Entry 2 of the State List, inserted through the 44th Amendment
n16771f1404e.x: Entry 2A of the Union List, associated with the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, provides the relevant Union List basis for deployment.
n16771f1404e.tq: Match the entry, list and amendment together instead of relying on the general subject of policing.
xs: **Entry 2A, Union List**, inserted by the **42nd CAA**, is the basis — option **(1)**.
**Public order** and **police** are **State List Entries 1, 2**.
xa: Deployment is for the Centre's **Art. 355** duty, **with or without state consent**.
**ARC (1966)**: "on their request or otherwise".
The **42nd CAA, 1976** also inserted **Art. 323A**.

n1672e303f15.s: Why do States object to Union deployment of armed or central forces without their consent?
o: Public order and police are Union List subjects
Police is a Concurrent List subject
Public order and police are State List subjects
Defence is a State List subject
n1672e303f15.x: Public order and police are Entries 1 and 2 of the State List, so deployment without consent touches State authority.
xa: Centre deploys under **Entry 2A, Union List** for its **Art. 355** duty.
**ARC (1966)** backed deployment "**on their request or otherwise**".
Under **Art. 257** the Centre may direct states on protection of **railways**.

nfd060695697.s: Which of the following sets contains only taxes or levies associated with the State domain?
o: Land revenue, agricultural income tax, State excise on alcohol and taxes on vehicles
Customs duty, corporation tax, Union excise duty and income tax
Goods and Services Tax, customs duty, wealth tax and corporation tax
Surcharge on Union taxes, customs duty, export duty and corporation tax
nfd060695697.x: Land revenue, agricultural income tax, State excise on alcohol and taxes on vehicles are included among taxes associated with the State domain. The other sets consist predominantly of Union taxes.
nfd060695697.tq: Separate the State tax field from familiar Union taxes by checking every item in the set.
xs: **Land revenue, agricultural income tax, state excise on alcohol, vehicle taxes** are all **state-only** taxes — option **(1)**.
**Customs**, **corporation tax**, **income tax** and **surcharges** are **Union** taxes.
xa: Other state-only taxes: **stamp duties and registration**, taxes on **land and buildings**, **mineral rights**, **electricity** consumption, **professions**.
**Agricultural income tax**: **States** only (UPPSC 2009).
**Excise on liquor**: **States** (UPPSC 2014).

nac1dfd5ce72.s: Which of the following is a power of the Union during a Financial Emergency under Article 360?
o: To direct States on financial propriety and require Money Bills to be reserved for the President
To automatically assume all State legislative powers
nac1dfd5ce72.x: During a Financial Emergency, the Centre may direct States on financial propriety and require Money and Financial Bills to be reserved for the President.
xa: ⚠ **Art. 354** = **National Emergency** power to modify distribution of revenues.
Art. 354's effect lasts until the **end of the financial year** in which the emergency ends.

n10c0888cc7f.s: Under Article 268 (e.g. stamp duties on specified instruments), duties are:
o: Levied, collected and appropriated exclusively by the Union
Levied and collected by the States but appropriated by the Union
Levied by the States and collected jointly by the Union and the States
Levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States
n10c0888cc7f.x: Article 268 covers duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States.
xa: ⚠ **269** = Union collects, **assigned to states**; **271** surcharges = **Centre only**.
Excise on **medicinal/toilet preparations** under 268 ended with GST.
**268A** (service tax, **88th Amendment, 2003**) was **omitted by the 101st Amendment, 2016**.

n9b83026e556.s: Under Article 269, taxes on inter-State sale or purchase of goods (other than newspapers) are:
o: Levied and collected by the States and appropriated by them
Levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States
Levied, collected and appropriated exclusively by the Union
Levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States
n9b83026e556.x: Under Article 269 the Union levies and collects these taxes (including taxes on consignment of goods) and assigns them to the States.
xa: ⚠ Collected and appropriated by states = **Art. 268** (stamp duties).
**Art. 269A**: **IGST** on inter-state supplies.
**Art. 271** surcharges: **exclusively for the Union**.

n3b1038ffff4.s: Which one of the following was NOT folded into the Article 270 pool by the 80th Constitutional Amendment?
o: Taxes on stock-exchange transactions other than stamp duty
n3b1038ffff4.x: Pre-2000 taxes on stock-exchange transactions, estate duty, railway fares and newspapers were folded into the Article 270 pool. Surcharges remain exclusively for the Union under Article 271.
n3b1038ffff4.tq: Identify the item expressly excluded from the divisible pool.
xs: **Surcharges** were not folded in — they stay **exclusively for the Union** under **Art. 271** — option **(1)**.
The **80th CAA** folded pre-2000 Art. 269 taxes — **stock-exchange transactions**, **estate duty**, **railway fares**, newspapers — into the **Art. 270** pool.
xa: PYQ trap: surcharges under Art. 271 are **not shared** with states (APPSC-G1 2024).
Art. 270 excludes **268, 269, 269A** taxes, **surcharges** and **cesses**.
Non-shareable cesses ~**18%** of Centre's gross tax revenue.

nf0b7c079072.s: A surcharge levied on a tax covered by Article 270 is:
o: automatically divided between the Union and States
collected and kept by the State concerned
distributed on the GST Council's recommendation
nf0b7c079072.x: Under Article 271, surcharges on Article 269 and 270 taxes are for Union purposes and are not shared with the States.
xa: Art. 271 surcharges are on **Art. 269/270** taxes.
Non-shareable **cesses and surcharges** cut effective devolution to near **31-32%** vs the **41%** award.
Art. 270 pool is shared on **FC** recommendation.

n5c1841ee5d5.s: Corporation tax, levied and collected by the Union, has been shared with the States since the:
n5c1841ee5d5.x: Since the 80th Constitutional Amendment, corporation tax is part of the shareable pool of Union taxes.
xa: 80th CAA effective **1 April 1996**; enacted the **10th FC's** scheme.
**Customs duty** too is now in the divisible pool (**Art. 270**).
Net proceeds certified by the **CAG**.

n671e99f44c4.s: The proceeds of IGST on inter-State supply are apportioned between the Centre and the States on the advice of the:
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
n671e99f44c4.x: Article 269A provides for apportionment of IGST on inter-State supply between the Centre and the States on the advice of the GST Council.
n671e99f44c4.tq: Identify the constitutional body associated with the specific tax-distribution mechanism.
xs: **IGST** proceeds are shared as Parliament provides on **GST Council** advice (**Art. 269A**) — option **(1)**.
Revenue goes to the **destination state**.
xa: **GST Council** = **Art. 279A**; chaired by the **Union Finance Minister**.
Art. 270 pool includes the **Centre's share of IGST**.
GST components: **CGST, SGST, IGST, UTGST**.

o: all Union List taxes without exception
only customs duties and Union excise duties
all State List taxes collected by the Union
Union taxes shared via the Finance Commission, excluding specified taxes, surcharges and cesses
na60e3e1bfab.x: Article 270 covers Union List taxes shared as recommended by the Finance Commission, excluding Article 268, 269 and 269A taxes, Article 271 surcharges and cesses.
xa: States' share: **41%** of the divisible pool (**15th FC**; retained by **16th FC**).
**Customs duty** is now in the divisible pool.
Net proceeds certified by the **CAG**.

n4d632a423b5.s: Under Article 246A, the power to make GST laws on inter-State supplies rests exclusively with:
n4d632a423b5.x: Article 246A gives concurrent GST power to Parliament and State Legislatures, but Parliament alone legislates on inter-State supplies.
xa: **Art. 269A**: **IGST** on inter-state supplies.
**Art. 279A**: **GST Council**.
**AP HC (May 2026)**: Central and state GST authorities must decide who proceeds — **no dual action**.

n4d7fe0ccee6.s: Which of the following was NOT a parameter traditionally associated with special category status?
o: Strategic location along an international border
High per-capita income and commercially viable State finances
Low population density or a sizeable tribal population
n4d7fe0ccee6.x: Special category parameters included difficult terrain, low population density or sizeable tribal population, strategic border location, economic and infrastructural backwardness, and non-viable State finances. High per-capita income and commercially viable finances were not such parameters.
n4d7fe0ccee6.tq: Find the reversed economic condition among otherwise recognised special-category characteristics.
xs: **High per-capita income and commercially viable State finances** was NOT a parameter — option **(3)** is the answer.
The NDC parameters were the opposite: **economic and infrastructural backwardness** and **non-viable state finances**.
**Strategic border location**, **hilly/difficult terrain** and **low population density or sizeable tribal population** were genuine parameters.
