xa: Special category States had the first charge on central plan assistance on **90% grant : 10% loan**.
Andhra Pradesh has demanded **special category status** since **2014**.
The Plan-grant system ended with the **Planning Commission's abolition (2015)**.

n836b77989c2.s: The ceiling on profession tax was raised from ₹250 to ₹2,500 by the:
n836b77989c2.x: The Sixtieth Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 raised the profession-tax ceiling under Article 276 from ₹250 to ₹2,500 per annum.
n836b77989c2.tq: Match the amendment number and year with the specific monetary change.
xs: The **60th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988** raised the ceiling from **₹250** to **₹2,500** — option **(3)**.
It amended **Art. 276(2)**; asked in **PYQ 2017**.
xa: **80th CAA, 2000**: **10th FC's** "Alternative Scheme of Devolution".
**88th Amendment, 2003**: added **Art. 268A** (service tax).
**101st Amendment, 2016**: inserted **246A, 269A, 279A** (GST).

n3b62b8243aa.s: Which of the following is correct about Article 131 and the Finance Commission?
o: Article 131 abolishes the Finance Commission's advisory role
Every Finance Commission matter must be decided under Article 131
Article 131 applies only to disputes between private persons and States
Matters referred to the Finance Commission are excluded from Article 131
n3b62b8243aa.x: Matters referred to the Finance Commission are excluded from Article 131, which covers original Union-State and inter-State legal disputes.
xa: **Art. 280** = Finance Commission; **281** = its recommendations.
**16th FC (2026-31)** retained **41%**; the Centre **accepted** its devolution recommendations.
**Kerala v UoI (2024)** challenged the **Net Borrowing Ceiling**.

n429d3969b6d.s: Under which Article can the President modify the distribution of revenues between the Union and States during a National Emergency?
n429d3969b6d.x: Article 354 allows this modification until the end of the financial year in which the emergency ends. Article 360 is Financial Emergency, 280 the Finance Commission and 293 State borrowing.
xa: Art. 360: directions on **financial propriety** + **Money and Financial Bills** reserved for the President.
**Arts. 268-281**: distribution of revenues.
Disputes: **Art. 131** original suit; FC matters **excluded**.

n3adf862190c.s: Who certifies the net proceeds relevant to the divisible pool?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
n3adf862190c.x: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India certifies the net proceeds used in determining the divisible pool.
n3adf862190c.tq: Use the institutional-responsibility approach: identify who certifies rather than who recommends devolution.
xs: **Net proceeds** are certified by the **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)** — option **(4)**.
The FC recommends the sharing; the CAG certifies the proceeds.
xa: Divisible pool = **Art. 270** taxes.
**CAG's State Finances 2023-24** report is in current relevance.

nindian-polity-26-1.s: The Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial constitutional body established under which Article of the Constitution?
nindian-polity-26-1.x: The Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial constitutional body under Article 280, in Part XII. Article 275 deals with grants and 282 with discretionary grants.
n: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body under Article 280. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
Article 280 concerns the Finance Commission. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
Article 280 is located in Part XII of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The Finance Commission has a quasi-judicial character. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The Union Finance Commission is governed by Article 280. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
Article 280 belongs to Part XII. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
xs: The **Finance Commission** is set up under **Article 280** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Article 281** deals with its **report / recommendations**; **Article 275** = **grants-in-aid**; **Article 282** = **discretionary grants**.
xa: **Article 275** grants: **principles** recommended by the Finance Commission.
⚠ Statutory grants are **not** on **NITI Aayog's** advice (APPSC-GS 2019).

n85037fa03a7.s: Service tax was associated with Article 268A before that Article was omitted by which Constitutional Amendment?
n85037fa03a7.x: Article 268A was introduced for service tax by the 88th Amendment in 2003 and was omitted by the 101st Amendment in 2016 with the introduction of GST.
n85037fa03a7.tq: Pair the provision with the amendment that removed it, not the amendment that introduced it.
xs: **Art. 268A** (service tax) was **omitted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016** — option **(3)**.
It had been added by the **88th Amendment, 2003**; service tax was replaced by **GST**.
xa: 101st Amendment inserted **246A, 269A, 279A**.
**80th CAA, 2000** omitted **Art. 272**.
GST from **1 July 2017**.

n036948567f9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 80th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000?
o: It gave effect to the Tenth Finance Commission's 'Alternative Scheme of Devolution'
It was made effective from 1 April 2000
It omitted Article 272 on sharing of Union excise duties
It made the States share the gross proceeds of all Union taxes
n036948567f9.x: Though enacted in 2000, the 80th Amendment was made effective from 1 April 1996.
xa: Share: IYB = **26%** of gross Union taxes; APP = **29%** (26% + 3% in lieu of additional excise duties).
It folded old **Art. 269** taxes into the **Art. 270** pool.
**Corporation tax** shared since the **80th Amendment**.

n11eafa9668a.s: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 inserted which set of provisions in connection with GST?
n11eafa9668a.x: The 101st Amendment inserted Articles 246A, 269A and 279A for the GST framework and the GST Council.
n11eafa9668a.tq: Recall the distinctive cluster of GST-related Articles.
xs: The **101st Amendment, 2016** inserted **Articles 246A, 269A and 279A** — option **(2)**.
**246A** = concurrent GST law; **269A** = **IGST**; **279A** = **GST Council**.
xa: It **omitted 268A** (service tax).
It amended Arts **248-250**, **268-271**, **286**, **366**, **368** + Sixth/Seventh Schedules.
GST from **1 July 2017**.

nab62fe2b8f3.s: Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India with effect from which date?
nab62fe2b8f3.x: GST came into effect on 1 July 2017 pursuant to the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016.
nab62fe2b8f3.tq: Use the precise implementation date rather than the year of constitutional amendment.
xs: GST came into effect on **1 July 2017** — option **(2)**.
It followed the **101st CAA, 2016**.
xa: GST is **destination-based** and subsumed ~**17** taxes.
"**GST 2.0**": effective **September 2025**.
Compensation cess guaranteed revenue for **5 years (2017-22)**.

n0e2ce4b95e6.s: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) is a ____-based tax.
n0e2ce4b95e6.x: GST is a destination-based tax that subsumed about 17 earlier taxes.
xa: GST from **1 July 2017** (**101st CAA**).
**IGST** revenue goes to the **destination state** (**Art. 269A**).
**Art. 246A**: **only Parliament** legislates on inter-state supply.

n2058c7cfbb7.s: Why can neither the Union nor the States alone carry a decision in the GST Council?
o: Because the Union Finance Minister does not vote in the Council
Because the States have a veto over all GST matters
Because the Council requires unanimous approval in every matter
Because the Centre has one-third and the States together have two-thirds of the weighted votes, while three-fourths is required
n2058c7cfbb7.x: A GST Council decision needs three-fourths of the weighted votes. The Centre holds only one-third and all States together only two-thirds, so neither side can reach three-fourths alone; options A-C misstate the voting rules.
n2058c7cfbb7.tq: Apply the voting weights and threshold instead of recalling either figure in isolation.
xs: **Centre one-third**, **states together two-thirds**; decisions need **three-fourths** of weighted votes — option **(4)**.
So **neither side** can carry a decision alone.
xa: ⚠ **1/3 – 2/3 – 3/4** = **Centre – states – majority needed**.
Chair: **Union Finance Minister**.
**Mohit Minerals (2022)**: recommendations **not binding**.

n59ff1e219d7.s: The Supreme Court's decision in Union of India v. Mohit Minerals (2022) held that the recommendations of the GST Council are:
o: Binding only when supported by a unanimous vote
Binding on Parliament and State Legislatures in every matter
Persuasive and not binding on Parliament and State Legislatures
n59ff1e219d7.x: The Court held that GST Council recommendations have persuasive value but are not binding on Parliament or State Legislatures.
n59ff1e219d7.tq: Distinguish persuasive constitutional coordination from binding legislative authority.
xs: **Mohit Minerals (2022)**: GST Council recommendations are **not binding**, only **persuasive** — option **(3)**.
They bind neither **Parliament** nor **state legislatures**.
xa: GST Council: **Art. 279A**; chair **Union Finance Minister**.
Members: Union **MoS (Finance)** + **State Finance Ministers**.
Decisions need **3/4 of weighted votes**.

o: the Union Home Minister, State Home Ministers and the RBI Governor
the Finance Commission Chairman and State Chief Secretaries
the Union Finance Minister, Union Minister of State for Finance and State Finance Ministers
the Prime Minister, Union Finance Minister and all Chief Ministers
nf65e2040219.x: The GST Council comprises the Union Finance Minister (Chairperson), the Union Minister of State in charge of Finance and the State Finance Ministers.
xa: Votes: **Centre one-third**, **all states together two-thirds**.
Decisions need **three-fourths** of weighted votes.
**Mohit Minerals (2022)**: recommendations **not binding**.

n43a24c195a5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: It retained the vertical share of States in the divisible pool at 41%
The Union Government accepted this recommendation in Budget 2026–27
Vertical share refers to distribution of the divisible pool among individual States
Distribution of the divisible pool among individual States is inter se devolution
n43a24c195a5.x: Vertical devolution concerns the Centre–State share; distribution among individual States is inter se (horizontal) devolution.
xa: Non-shareable cesses (~**18%** of gross tax revenue) cut effective devolution to about **31-32%**.
The **16th FC** caps state fiscal deficit at **3% of GSDP**.

nc0265126b0e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about grants-in-aid?
o: Statutory grants under Article 275 are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Statutory grants are made on the recommendation of NITI Aayog
Discretionary grants under Article 282 may be made for any public purpose
Statutory grants are made on the recommendation of the Finance Commission
nc0265126b0e.x: Statutory grants under Article 275 are made on the recommendation of the Finance Commission, not NITI Aayog.
xa: **NITI Aayog has no financial powers**.
Discretionary grants were earlier via the **Planning Commission**; now **Union ministries**.
Art. 275 grants meet **state-specific needs** formulas cannot capture.

o: are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
may be made for any public purpose
are meant only for Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Areas
n26a59aa5e33.x: Article 282 permits discretionary grants for any public purpose; historically they were largely routed through the Planning Commission and are not charged on the Consolidated Fund.
xa: Historically discretionary grants were the **larger** share of Central grants.
Now given by **Union ministries**; the **Planning Commission was abolished (2015)**.
**Gadgil formula (1969)** distributed **Central Plan assistance** among states.

nc093a3c1d86.s: Compensation Cess under the GST system was primarily imposed on which category of goods?
nc093a3c1d86.x: Compensation Cess on luxury and sin goods was used to fund compensation to States for GST-related revenue loss.
nc093a3c1d86.tq: Use the purpose-and-base combination rather than confusing cess with a general GST levy.
xs: **Compensation cess** was imposed on **luxury/"sin" goods** — option **(4)**.
It funded **states' compensation** promised by the **101st Amendment**.
xa: It guaranteed revenue for **5 years (2017-22)**.
Kerala lists "**cessation of GST compensation**" as a fiscal stress.
Luxury/sin goods kept **existing rates** + compensation cess.

naf4b4c0ea13.s: A shift in the composition of transfers from grants-in-aid to tax devolution generally results in:
o: A reduction in unconditional transfers to States
An increase in unconditional or untied transfers to States
An increase in the Central parameters attached to every transfer
naf4b4c0ea13.x: Tax devolution is formula-based and generally untied. Therefore, shifting from grants to tax devolution increases the share of unconditional transfers available to States.
naf4b4c0ea13.tq: Apply the distinction between untied tax devolution and conditional grants to identify the consequence of a compositional shift.
xs: Shifting transfers from grants to **tax devolution** causes **an increase in unconditional or untied transfers to States** — option **(3)** is correct.
Tax devolution is **formula-based and untied**, whereas **CSS** grants carry **central parameters** and **matching shares**.
The **14th FC's "compositional shift"** raised devolution and cut grants — the **APPSC-G1 2017** answer was "increases the share of unconditional transfers".
xa: **14th FC** set the states' share at **42%**; the **15th FC** at **41%** (2021-26).
The **16th FC** (2026-31) retained **41%**, and the Centre **accepted** its devolution recommendations.
Tax devolution was **₹12.87 lakh crore** in **2024-25** (BE ₹12.47 lakh crore).

n0a1395a8a9e.s: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended what share of the divisible pool for the States?
n0a1395a8a9e.x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended 41 percent; 42 percent was the Fourteenth Finance Commission's figure.
xa: Non-shareable cesses are about **18%** of the Centre's gross tax revenue.
The **10th FC** gave the "**Alternative Scheme of Devolution**", enacted by the **80th CAA, 2000**.
Under that scheme the states' share was **29%** = **26%** + **3%** in lieu of additional excise duties.
**Art. 280** creates the Finance Commission; **Art. 281** deals with its recommendations.

n5a6c1bcc1db.s: The Gadgil formula was introduced in 1969 for the distribution of Central Plan assistance during the:
n5a6c1bcc1db.x: The Gadgil formula, associated with D. R. Gadgil, was introduced in 1969 during the Fourth Five Year Plan for distributing Central Plan assistance among States.
n5a6c1bcc1db.tq: Link the formula to its year and Plan period rather than to the later Gadgil–Mukherjee formula.
xs: The **Gadgil formula** (**1969**) distributed Central Plan assistance in the **Fourth Five Year Plan** — option **(2)** is correct.
It was devised by **D.R. Gadgil**; the **Eighth Plan** saw the later **Gadgil-Mukherjee** formula, not the original.
xa: Gadgil weights: **population 60**, per-capita income **10**, tax effort **10**, ongoing irrigation/power **10**, special problems **10**.
**Gadgil-Mukherjee** weights: population **60%**, per capita income **25%**, fiscal management **7.5%**, special problems **7.5%**.
⚠ Sources differ on Gadgil-Mukherjee: **1991** with population **55** vs **1990** with population **60%**.
**APPSC-G2 2017** answer: Gadgil formula = "**devolution of funds**".

nc4dede8a438.s: Special category States traditionally received Central Plan assistance on which terms?
o: 100 percent grant without any loan component
nc4dede8a438.x: Special category States had the first charge on Central Plan assistance and received it on the favourable terms of 90 percent grant and 10 percent loan.
nc4dede8a438.tq: Recall the grant–loan ratio and reject the more familiar but incorrect rounded alternatives.
xs: Special category States got the first charge on central plan assistance on **90 percent grant and 10 percent loan** — option **(4)** is correct.
The **90 : 10** grant-loan ratio was their favourable term; none of the other ratios applied.
xa: Parameters (**NDC**): **hilly/difficult terrain**, low population density or sizeable **tribal population**, **strategic border location**.
Also: **economic and infrastructural backwardness** and **non-viable state finances**.
**AP angle:** post-**2014** demand for **special category status**.

na57f9507da8.s: The 2024 “Chalo Delhi” protest by southern States was primarily associated with opposition to
o: the replacement of grants by cesses
the abolition of State Development Loans
conditionality attached to Centrally Sponsored Schemes only
na57f9507da8.x: The protest concerned the perceived adverse effect of population-heavy or population-based criteria on the devolution share of southern States.
na57f9507da8.tq: Identify the policy issue represented by the protest instead of confusing it with other fiscal criticisms.
xs: The **2024 "Chalo Delhi"** protest by southern states was against **population-based criteria in devolution** — option **(3)** is correct.
Southern states objected to **population-heavy** devolution criteria.
xa: Gadgil-type formulas weighted **population** at **60%**.
Other debates: **vertical fiscal imbalance**, **CSS conditionality**, and **non-shareable cesses**.
AP's memorandum to the **16th FC** sought extra weight for **capital-city and infrastructure costs** (**Feb 2026**).

ncc428f73e0f.s: The post-2014 demand specifically associated with Andhra Pradesh in the context of Centre–State relations is for
o: separate representation in the Finance Commission
transfer of all Union taxes to the State
ncc428f73e0f.x: Andhra Pradesh has continued its post-2014 demand for special category status.
ncc428f73e0f.tq: Identify the State-specific demand without extending it into an absolute fiscal claim.
xs: Andhra Pradesh's post-**2014** demand is for **special category status** — option **(2)** is correct.
Special category states got central plan assistance on **90% grant : 10% loan**.
xa: Parameters: **hilly terrain**, low population density/**tribal population**, **strategic border location**, **backwardness**, **non-viable finances**.
AP's memorandum to the **16th FC** sought extra weight for **capital-city and infrastructure costs** after bifurcation (**Feb 2026**).
**AP net borrowings** were **Rs. 60,485.40 Cr** in 2024-25.

n5f3cbec623d.s: Under Article 292, the Union Government may borrow:
o: On the security of the Consolidated Fund of India, within limits fixed by Parliament by law
Only on the security of State Consolidated Funds
Only from foreign sources without parliamentary limits
Without reference to any law made by Parliament
n5f3cbec623d.x: Article 292 authorises Union borrowing on the security of the Consolidated Fund of India, subject to limits fixed by Parliament by law.
n5f3cbec623d.tq: Identify the borrowing authority, security and statutory limit together.
xs: **Art. 292**: the Union borrows **on the security of the Consolidated Fund of India, within limits fixed by Parliament by law** — option **(1)** is correct.
State Consolidated Funds secure **state** borrowing under **Art. 293(1)**, not Union borrowing.
Union borrowing is never free of **Parliament's** law-fixed limits, so options 3 and 4 fail.
xa: **Art. 293(1):** a state borrows **only within India**, on its own Consolidated Fund.
**Art. 293(2):** the **Union can lend to states** or guarantee their loans (**APPSC-G2 2025**).
**Art. 266:** the **Consolidated Fund of India** receives all Union revenues, loans raised and loan repayments.

o: Supreme Court to fix the borrowing limit of every State
States to guarantee Union loans without limit
Union to lend to States or guarantee their loans
Finance Commission to sanction State loans
ne14bc0fc811.x: Article 293(2) empowers the Union to make loans to States and to guarantee loans raised by them.
xa: This clause was asked in **APPSC-G2 2025**.
**Art. 292:** the Union borrows on the security of the **Consolidated Fund of India**.

neb74a7087d0.s: Under Article 293(3), a State with an outstanding Union loan or guarantee needs what to raise a fresh loan?
o: Only the approval of the Reserve Bank of India
The Union's consent, which may carry conditions
No consent, if the loan is raised within India
neb74a7087d0.x: While a Union loan or guarantee is outstanding, the State needs the Union's consent for a further loan, and conditions may be attached.
xa: **State of Kerala v UoI (2024)** challenged it by an original suit under **Art. 131**.
The **16th FC** caps state fiscal deficit at **3% of GSDP** and calls for ending off-budget borrowing.

n3e29135bc35.s: Kerala v. Union of India (2024) concerned a suit under Article 131 challenging—
o: The appointment of the Governor under Article 156
The distribution of river waters under Article 262
The Net Borrowing Ceiling imposed under Article 293(3)
The validity of GST under Article 279A
n3e29135bc35.x: Kerala's 2024 suit under Article 131 challenged the Net Borrowing Ceiling imposed under Article 293(3).
n3e29135bc35.tq: Match the case, constitutional jurisdiction and disputed fiscal provision.
xs: **Kerala v UoI (2024)** was an original suit under **Art. 131** against the **Net Borrowing Ceiling imposed under Article 293(3)** — option **(3)** is correct.
The NBC is fixed by **GoI**, counts **off-budget borrowings**, and limits a state's market borrowing.
xa: **Art. 131** suits exclude matters **referred to the Finance Commission**.
**Art. 293(3):** a state indebted to the Centre needs the **Centre's consent** for a new loan.
Kerala also lists "**cessation of GST compensation**" as a fiscal stress (**11 May 2026**).

n0d5eef0fd38.s: Which one of the following is associated with the recommendations of the Sixteenth Finance Commission regarding State finances?
o: A fiscal deficit ceiling of 3% of GDP for the Union alone
A fiscal deficit ceiling of 5% of GSDP and expansion of off-budget borrowing
A fiscal deficit ceiling of 3% of GSDP and ending off-budget borrowing
A prohibition on all State borrowing from domestic sources
n0d5eef0fd38.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission caps the State fiscal deficit at 3% of GSDP and calls for ending off-budget borrowing.
n0d5eef0fd38.tq: Match the numerical ceiling with the correct level of government and fiscal practice.
xs: The **16th FC** caps the state fiscal deficit at **3% of GSDP** and calls for **ending off-budget borrowing** — option **(3)** is correct.
It concerns **State** finances, not the Union alone; it seeks to end, not expand, off-budget borrowing.
xa: The **16th FC** (**2026-31**) retained the states' share at **41%**; the Centre **accepted** its devolution recommendations.
The **Net Borrowing Ceiling** already **counts off-budget borrowings**.
AP's memorandum to the 16th FC sought extra weight for **capital-city and infrastructure costs** after bifurcation (**Feb 2026**).

n4e8c29d507a.s: Part XI of the Constitution deals with:
o: elections and special provisions for certain classes
legislative and administrative relations between the Union and the States
emergency provisions and amendment of the Constitution
financial relations and trade within India
n4e8c29d507a.x: Part XI contains legislative relations (Articles 245-255) and administrative relations (Articles 256-263) between the Union and the States.
xa: **Part XII** covers **financial relations** in **Arts 268-293**.
UKPSC 2024 keyed **Part XI** as the Part on Centre-State legislative and administrative relations.
Shaping factors of Centre-State relations: **constitutional provisions, conventions, judicial interpretation** and **mechanisms for dialogue** (UPPSC 2009: all four).

n9e54252cd17.s: Part XII of the Constitution primarily deals with—
o: Emergency relations between the Union and the States
Financial relations between the Union and the States
Administrative relations between the Union and the States
n9e54252cd17.x: Part XII deals with financial relations, including Articles 268 to 293.
n9e54252cd17.tq: Direct Part-subject recall with a Part XI subject as the principal trap.
xs: Part XII primarily deals with **financial relations** between the Union and the States — so option **(2)** is correct.
It spans **Arts 268-293**.
**Administrative relations** (option 3) sit in **Part XI** (**Arts 256-263**), along with legislative relations.
xa: **Part XI** = legislative (**Arts 245-255**) + administrative (**Arts 256-263**) relations.
During a National Emergency, the President can **reduce or cancel** financial transfers under **Art 354**.
⚠ Fiscal friction: cesses and surcharges are excluded, so the divisible pool is only about **81%** of gross tax revenue.

n46c9004a15b.s: Which one of the following is a unitary feature of the Indian Constitution?
o: A constitutional prohibition on Union directions to States
Separate and independent judicial systems for the Union and each State
Dual citizenship for Union and State citizens
All India Services serving both the Union and the States
n46c9004a15b.x: All India Services are a unitary feature because they provide a common administrative structure serving both the Union and the States. India has single citizenship and an integrated judiciary.
n46c9004a15b.tq: Identify the one genuine unitary feature among reversed or non-existent federal features.
xs: **All India Services** serving both the Union and the States are a **unitary feature** — so option **(4)** is correct.
India has **single citizenship**, not dual citizenship (option 3).
India has an **integrated judiciary**, not separate Union and State judicial systems (option 2).
The Union can in fact give **directions** to States (e.g. **Art 353** in an emergency; defying them counts as a breakdown under **Art 365**), so option 1 is wrong.
xa: Unitary features listed together: **single citizenship**, **integrated judiciary**, **AIS**, **emergency powers**.
**AIS** is also an area of friction because of **central control of officers**.
Planning process and party politics also shape Centre-State relations (**UKPSC 2002**).

n20948c6588d.s: During a National Emergency, India's federal structure becomes:
o: more strongly federal, with State powers protected
confederal, with States gaining international personality
unchanged in the legislative, executive and financial spheres
quasi-unitary, with increased powers for the Union
n20948c6588d.x: A National Emergency strengthens the Union, so the system operates in a unitary or quasi-unitary manner.
xa: Parliament can legislate on **any State List subject** (**Art 250**); such laws lapse **6 months** after the emergency.
The **Lok Sabha term** can be extended by **1 year at a time**.
Other unitary features: **single citizenship**, **integrated judiciary**, **AIS**, **emergency powers**.

nindian-polity-72-19.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the IMDT Act?
o: It was upheld as strengthening the Union's duty under Article 355.
It was struck down in Sarbananda Sonowal v. Union of India (2005).
The Supreme Court held that it violated Article 355.
nindian-polity-72-19.x: The IMDT Act (1983) was struck down, not upheld, in Sarbananda Sonowal (2005) for violating Article 355.
n: The Illegal Migrants (Determination by Tribunals) Act was enacted in 1983. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #72 · pp 196-199]
The Supreme Court struck down the IMDT Act as unconstitutional in Sarbananda Sonowal v. Union of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #72 · pp 196-199]
The Supreme Court decided Sarbananda Sonowal v. Union of India in 2005. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #72 · pp 196-199]
The IMDT Act violated Article 355. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #72 · pp 196-199]
Article 355 imposes a duty on the Union to protect States against external aggression. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #72 · pp 196-199]
Article 355 imposes a duty on the Union to protect States against internal disturbance. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #72 · pp 196-199]
xa: **Art. 355** is the basis/justification for **Art. 356**.
**Art. 365:** defying Union directions counts as a breakdown of constitutional machinery.
Art. 355 also requires governance of every state per the Constitution.

ne9dcb2003a5.s: What is the effect of Article 353 during a National Emergency?
o: State Governments are suspended and Parliament administers the States.
The Supreme Court assumes the executive functions of the States.
The Union may direct a State on any matter, but State Governments are not suspended.
The Governor alone exercises all executive power of the State.
ne9dcb2003a5.x: Article 353 enlarges the Union's executive authority to direct a State on any matter; it does not suspend State Governments.
xa: ⚠ **250 – 353 – 354** = **legislative – executive – financial** effects of a National Emergency.
**Art 250**: Parliament can legislate on **any State List subject**; such laws lapse **6 months** after the emergency ends.
**Art 354**: the President can **reduce or cancel** transfers until the end of that financial year.

n68b3abdb086.s: Under Article 354, during a National Emergency the President may:
o: transfer all State taxes to the Consolidated Fund of India
suspend tax distribution without laying the order before Parliament
reduce or cancel certain transfers to States until the end of the financial year
n68b3abdb086.x: Article 354 lets the President modify or reduce financial transfers to States, generally until the end of the financial year; the order must be laid before Parliament.
xa: ⚠ **250 – 353 – 354** = **legislative – executive – financial**.
**Art 353**: Centre can direct a State on **"any" matter**; State governments are **not suspended**.
Part XII (**Arts 268-293**) governs financial relations in normal times.

nfad5e74d6a7.s: Laws made by Parliament on State List matters under Article 250 cease to have effect:
o: One year after the Emergency ends
Only after repeal by every State Legislature
Six months after the Emergency ends
nfad5e74d6a7.x: Such laws do not become void immediately; they cease to have effect six months after the National Emergency ends.
nfad5e74d6a7.tq: Distinguish the post-emergency sunset period from immediate expiry.
xs: Laws made by Parliament on State List subjects under **Art 250** lapse **6 months after the emergency ends** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They do not lapse **immediately**, nor need repeal by State Legislatures.
xa: **Art 250** = legislative effect; **353** = executive; **354** = financial.
⚠ **One year at a time** is the Lok Sabha term extension during emergency, not the lapse period.
During an emergency the Constitution becomes **unitary rather than federal**.

n4b131f1cdf3.s: Article 355 imposes on the Union the duty to:
o: appoint State ministers during political instability
protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance
permit States to maintain their own armed forces
ensure every State follows the same economic policy
n4b131f1cdf3.x: Article 355 requires the Union to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance and to ensure each State is governed according to the Constitution.
xa: The Art 355 duty is the **justification for Art 356** (President's Rule).
**Art 365**: a State **defying Union directions** counts as a breakdown of constitutional machinery.
Asked in **UPSC 2003** and **UPPSC 2001**.

n8e87dd7b26c.s: President's Rule under Article 356 has been imposed in India approximately:
n8e87dd7b26c.x: Article 356 has been used over 125 times, often against opposition-led governments, causing Centre-State friction.
xa: The constitutional justification for Art 356 is the Union's duty under **Art 355**.
**Art 365**: defying Union directions counts as a **breakdown**.
Other friction areas: **Governor** (Art 156), **fiscal** (divisible pool ~**81%**), **CBI** consent, **Art 262** river disputes.

na1a495c59ff.s: With cesses and surcharges excluded, the divisible pool is about what share of gross tax revenue?
na1a495c59ff.x: Excluding cesses and surcharges leaves the divisible pool at about 81% of gross tax revenue, shrinking the base shared with States.
xa: States now demand **50%** devolution (**3 Feb 2026**).
**GST compensation** ended in **June 2022**.
Borrowing limits led to litigation — **Kerala v.** the Union.

n0fbd7652465.s: Which one of the following is correct about GST compensation to States?
o: It began only after the 16th Finance Commission.
It was abolished before GST commenced.
n0fbd7652465.x: The compensation promised to States under the GST framework ended in June 2022.
xa: States demand **50%** devolution (**3 Feb 2026**).
**Borrowing** limits: **Kerala v.** the Union.
Divisible pool is only about **81%** of gross tax revenue because **cesses and surcharges** are excluded.

n62c297caa86.s: Which of the following are AP Reorganisation Act assurances that the opposition claims remain unmet?
o: Kadapa steel plant, Dugarajapatnam port and metro rail
Visakhapatnam airport, Kurnool dam and inland waterways
Amaravati High Court, Sriharikota port and a national university
Polavaram barrage, Hyderabad metro and a new Parliament building
n62c297caa86.x: The cited unmet assurances include the Kadapa steel plant, Dugarajapatnam port and metro rail, valued by the opposition at about Rs 5 lakh crore.
xa: **SCS** was promised by PM **Manmohan Singh** but **not written into APRA 2014**; it would mean **90%** CSS funding.
**Polavaram**: national project under **Sec 90 of APRA 2014**.
**SCS + APRA promises** are AP's main federal grievances.

n1a4ec15ef4d.s: Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh was promised in Parliament by Prime Minister:
n1a4ec15ef4d.x: Manmohan Singh promised SCS in Parliament, but the promise was never written into the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.
xa: SCS would have meant **90%** central funding for CSS.
Unmet APRA assurances (~**₹5 lakh crore**): **Kadapa steel plant**, **Dugarajapatnam port**, metro rail.
**SCS + APRA** promises are AP's main federal grievances; **Polavaram** is the flagship central commitment.

nddc22e1dcde.s: Which committee has been associated with the call for a “structural reset” of federalism?
o: Kurian Joseph Committee of Tamil Nadu
nddc22e1dcde.x: The Tamil Nadu Kurian Joseph Committee was associated with the call for a structural reset of federalism.
nddc22e1dcde.tq: Direct committee-identification question using familiar Centre-State committees as distractors.
xs: Tamil Nadu's **Kurian Joseph Committee** calls for a **"structural reset"** of federalism — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its **Part I** report came on **16 Feb 2026**.
xa: Recent friction: Governors delaying bills in **TN and Kerala** (**23 Mar 2026**).
States demand **50%** devolution (**3 Feb 2026**).
**GST compensation** ended in **June 2022**.
nddc22e1dcde.fixed: Rajamannar Committee was set up by Tamil Nadu, not Andhra Pradesh

n1a78129ded3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about parliamentary approval of a National Emergency?
o: Approval requires only a simple majority in each House
Both Houses must approve the proclamation within one month
Once approved, it continues for six months
It can be extended indefinitely with approval every six months
n1a78129ded3.x: Approval of a National Emergency needs a special majority in each House; simple majority applies to a Financial Emergency.
xa: President's Rule: **6 months** per approval, maximum **3 years**.
Financial Emergency has **no maximum period** — continues till revoked.

n2693e86d7b8.s: In which case did the Supreme Court affirm that a proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352 is reviewable?
n2693e86d7b8.x: Minerva Mills affirmed reviewability, reversing the 38th Amendment's attempt to make the President's satisfaction non-justiciable.
xa: **S.R. Bommai (1994)**: a proclamation under **Art. 356** is subject to **judicial review** (mala fide or irrelevant grounds).
**ADM Jabalpur (1976)** held even the right to life unenforceable; rejected in **Puttaswamy (2017)**.
**Rameshwar Prasad (2006)** struck down the **Bihar Assembly** dissolution.

n764cc85a0dc.s: Article 358 automatically suspends Article 19 when a National Emergency is proclaimed on the ground of:
n764cc85a0dc.x: Article 358 operates only for an Emergency based on war or external aggression, not armed rebellion.
xa: **Lasting protection**: acts done under Art. 358 cannot be challenged even after the emergency.
⚠ **359** needs a **Presidential order** and can never suspend **Arts. 20 and 21**.

n963bc545aae.s: Under Article 356, the President may impose President's Rule in a State:
o: Only on the report of the Governor
Only with the consent of the State Legislature
On the report of the Governor or otherwise
Only on a resolution of the Rajya Sabha
n963bc545aae.x: The President may act on the Governor's report or otherwise; State Legislature consent is not a precondition.
xa: Art. 356 is also deemed under **Art. 365** (non-compliance with Union directions).
Basis: **Art. 355** — the Union's duty to ensure constitutional governance in states.
Approval: **6 months** per approval; maximum **3 years**.

n9b854467e23.s: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar expressed the hope that Article 356 would remain a:
n9b854467e23.x: Ambedkar hoped that the emergency provision under Article 356 would remain a “dead letter” and be used only in exceptional circumstances.
n9b854467e23.tq: Recall the exact phrase associated with a constitutional provision.
xs: **Ambedkar** hoped Art. 356 would remain a "**dead letter**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
In practice it has been among the **most controversial provisions** (PYQ **2025**), with partisan Governor reports.
xa: **S.R. Bommai (1994)** subjected it to **judicial review**.
**First PR in India**: **Punjab, 1951**.
⚠ Art. 356 is also deemed under **Art. 365**.

n0f1edb8b4b6.s: The first instance of President’s Rule in India occurred in:
n0f1edb8b4b6.x: Punjab witnessed the first imposition of President’s Rule in India in 1951.
n0f1edb8b4b6.tq: Combine the correct State and year to defeat swapped-location options.
xs: The first President's Rule in India was in **Punjab, 1951** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Andhra Pradesh** had its first spell only in **January 1973**, so option 4 is wrong.
xa: **First PR in AP**: **January 1973** (PYQ **2019/2021**), after the **Jai Andhra** agitation.
**Ambedkar** hoped Art. 356 would remain a "**dead letter**".
Art. 356 is among the **most controversial provisions** (PYQ **2025**).

nindian-polity-44-9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about parliamentary approval of emergencies?
o: A National Emergency must be approved within one month.
The 44th Amendment, 1978 cut the National Emergency period from two months to one.
A Financial Emergency must be approved within two months.
President's Rule must be approved within one month.
nindian-polity-44-9.x: President's Rule must be approved within two months, like a Financial Emergency; only a National Emergency has one month.
n: Parliamentary approval of a National Emergency must be obtained within one month. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
Article 352 governs parliamentary approval of a National Emergency. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
The time for parliamentary approval of a National Emergency was reduced from two months to one month by the Forty-Fourth Amendment of 1978. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
President's Rule under Article 356 has a two-month parliamentary approval period. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
Financial Emergency under Article 360 has a two-month parliamentary approval period. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
xa: National Emergency approval is by **special majority**.
⚠ Sources differ: other notes give President's Rule a **6 months** window.
An Emergency continues **six months at a time**.

nindian-polity-44-19.s: The maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament is governed by Article:
nindian-polity-44-19.x: Article 85 governs the session gap; Article 62(2) deals with a Presidential vacancy and Article 352 with National Emergency.
n: Parliamentary approval of a National Emergency must be obtained within one month. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
Article 352 governs parliamentary approval of a National Emergency. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
Article 62(2) governs the filling of a Presidential vacancy. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
The maximum gap between sessions of Parliament is six months. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
Article 85 requires Parliament to meet at least twice a year. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
State laws on State List subjects have a six-month post-Emergency timeframe under Article 250. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 117-120]
xa: All four involve a **six-month** time limit.
**Article 356** and **360** approvals need **two months**.
⚠ **1 month – 2 months – 6 months** = **352 – 360 – 356** approval windows (per the mnemonic).

n58769ea75a4.s: Both the emergency provisions and the ordinance power of the Indian Constitution are drawn from the:
n58769ea75a4.x: The emergency provisions and the ordinance power (Articles 123 and 213) are relics of the Government of India Act, 1935; the Weimar Constitution is the source of suspending Fundamental Rights in an emergency.
xa: Three emergencies: **National (Art. 352)**, **President's Rule (Art. 356)**, **Financial (Art. 360)**.
⚠ Approval windows: **1 month – 2 months – 6 months** = **352 – 360 – 356**.
**Art. 355** (Union's duty to protect states) is the basis for **Art. 356**.

n61a863af946.s: Written advice of the Union Cabinet for proclaiming a National Emergency was made mandatory by the:
n61a863af946.x: Article 352(3), inserted by the 44th Amendment, makes written advice of the Union Cabinet mandatory.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** some UPSC notes wrongly say "new **Article 352A**".
Approval by both Houses within **1 month** by **special majority**.
Notice by **1/10 of Lok Sabha members** → special sitting within **14 days** to consider disapproval.

n726940484ad.s: The 39th Constitutional Amendment Act, enacted during the Emergency period, placed which disputes beyond the jurisdiction of courts?
o: Disputes relating to elections of the President and Vice-President only
All disputes concerning State Legislative Assemblies
Election disputes concerning the Prime Minister and the Speaker
Disputes relating to the proclamation of Financial Emergency
n726940484ad.x: The 39th Amendment placed election disputes concerning the Prime Minister and the Speaker beyond the courts.
n726940484ad.tq: Match the amendment with the particular constitutional office affected, not a neighbouring office.
xs: The **39th CAA** put **election disputes of the PM and the Speaker** beyond courts — so option **(3)** is correct.
It followed the **Allahabad HC** voiding **Indira Gandhi's 1971 election**.
xa: **38th CAA (1975)**: made satisfaction **non-justiciable** (later reversed).
**42nd CAA (1976)**: "mini-constitution"; terms raised to **6 years**.
**44th CAA, 1978**: "internal disturbance" → "**armed rebellion**"; written Cabinet advice.

n4f752c0677f.s: During a National Emergency, the President may modify the distribution of revenues between the Union and the States. Such modification may continue until:
o: The date on which the Emergency is proclaimed
The end of the financial year in which the Emergency ends
Six months after Parliament approves the Emergency
n4f752c0677f.x: The President may modify revenue distribution during the Emergency, and the modification can continue until the end of the financial year in which the Emergency ends.
n4f752c0677f.tq: Focus on the precise terminal time attached to a financial consequence.
xs: The President can modify revenue distribution **till the end of the financial year in which the emergency ends** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This is the **financial** effect of a National Emergency.
xa: Executive effect: the Centre can direct states on **any matter**.
Terms of the Lok Sabha and Assemblies extendable **1 year at a time**, not beyond **6 months** after it ends.
⚠ Don't confuse with a **Financial Emergency (Art. 360)**, which has never been declared.

nf87bdd7400e.s: While a proclamation of National Emergency is in operation, the term of the Lok Sabha may be extended by law:
o: By one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ceases to operate
By six months at a time, but not beyond one year after the Emergency ceases to operate
By one year at a time, without any limit after the Emergency ends
By two years in total, with the approval of the Supreme Court
nf87bdd7400e.x: Parliament may extend the term of the Lok Sabha (and of State Assemblies) by law for one year at a time during a National Emergency, but the extension cannot continue beyond six months after the Emergency ceases. The six-month unit, the absence of any limit and Supreme Court approval are all incorrect.
nf87bdd7400e.tq: 1 year at a time; 6 months after it ends.
xs: Terms extendable by law **one year at a time**, **not beyond six months** after the emergency ends — so option **(1)** is correct.
The unit is **1 year**, not six months, and the six-month outer limit rules out "without any limit".
xa: The **42nd CAA (1976)** had raised Lok Sabha/Assembly terms to **6 years**.
Financial effect: revenue distribution modified **till the end of the financial year** in which the emergency ends.
Executive effect: Centre can direct states on **any matter**.

n47ef9d986ec.s: President's Rule under Article 356 can be continued beyond one year only if:
o: A National Emergency is in operation or the Election Commission certifies that elections cannot be held
The Governor recommends it and the State Legislature consents
A National Emergency is in operation and the Election Commission certifies that elections cannot be held
Parliament approves it by a special majority every three months
n47ef9d986ec.x: Beyond one year, President's Rule needs both conditions together: a National Emergency in operation AND an Election Commission certificate that elections cannot be held. The 'or' version is the common trap. Governor's recommendation or state consent are not conditions, and approval is every six months (maximum three years), not every three months by special majority.
n47ef9d986ec.tq: Beyond 1 year: Emergency AND EC certificate - both.
xs: Beyond **1 year**, PR continues only if a **National Emergency is in operation and the Election Commission certifies** elections cannot be held — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Both conditions are needed — option 1's "**or**" is the trap.
Approval is every **6 months** (maximum **3 years**), not every three months by special majority.
xa: ONOE critique: deferred state polls could prolong PR, clashing with **Art. 356(5)** (**9 Mar 2026**).
PR can be revoked by the President **at any time**.

nbbf05c58b26.s: Which of the following is NOT a principle laid down in S.R. Bommai v. Union of India?
o: A proclamation under Article 356 is subject to judicial review
The Governor's opinion is the conclusive test of majority in the Assembly
The floor test in the Assembly is the proper test of majority
A court can restore a dismissed State government in an appropriate case
nbbf05c58b26.x: Bommai held that the Governor's opinion is not conclusive; majority must ordinarily be tested on the floor of the Assembly.
xa: Bommai: **9-judge bench**, **1994**.
**Secularism** and **federalism** are basic features; a state government acting against secularism can be dismissed.

n56805b534fd.s: Which amendment ensured that an order under Article 359 cannot suspend the enforcement of Articles 20 and 21?
n56805b534fd.x: The 44th Amendment, 1978 protected Articles 20 and 21 from suspension under Article 359, even during a National Emergency.
xa: ⚠ LENS Jul **2026** MCQ: "Arts 20 and 21 can be suspended under Art. 359" is **wrong**.
⚠ **358** = **Art. 19**, automatic; **359** = Presidential order, never Arts. 20 and 21.
The 44th CAA also barred Art. 358 when the ground is **armed rebellion**.

nindian-polity-50-38.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Articles 358 and 359?
o: Article 358 automatically suspends the freedoms under Article 19
Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended
Article 359 requires a specific, separate Presidential Order
Article 358 operates when the Emergency is proclaimed on the ground of armed rebellion
nindian-polity-50-38.x: Article 358 does not apply to an Emergency proclaimed on the ground of armed rebellion.
n: Article 358 automatically suspends the 6 basic freedoms under Article 19. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
Article 358 operates only on the grounds of war or external aggression. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
Suspension under Article 359 requires a specific and separate Presidential Order. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
Article 358 does not operate during a proclamation based on armed rebellion. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended under any circumstances under Article 359. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended during a National Emergency. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
Article 358 applies during an external emergency. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 131-135]
xa: These changes came from the **44th Amendment, 1978**.
**Lasting protection (Art. 358):** acts done during the emergency cannot be challenged even afterwards.
⚠ **358** = Art. 19, automatic; **359** = Presidential order, never Arts. 20 and 21.

n56d9cf949cc.s: Which constitutional amendment substituted the expression “internal disturbance” with “armed rebellion” as a ground for National Emergency under Article 352?
n56d9cf949cc.x: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 replaced “internal disturbance” with “armed rebellion” in Article 352.
n56d9cf949cc.tq: Discriminate between closely numbered Constitutional Amendments and their specific changes.
xs: The **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978** replaced "**internal disturbance**" with "**armed rebellion**" in Art. 352 — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **38th CAA (1975)** made satisfaction non-justiciable; the **39th** shielded PM/Speaker election disputes; the **42nd (1976)** raised terms to **6 years**.
xa: The 44th CAA also made **written Cabinet advice** mandatory — **Art. 352(3)**.
It barred **Art. 358** for **armed rebellion**, and stopped **Art. 359** from touching **Arts. 20 and 21**.
⚠ The **1975** emergency was declared on "**internal disturbance**" — the ground before the 44th CAA.

n147edb5dde1.s: Which one of the following is correct about the National Emergency of 25 June 1975?
o: It was proclaimed by President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed on the ground of internal disturbance.
It was proclaimed by the Union Cabinet on the ground of armed rebellion.
It was proclaimed by the President on the ground of external aggression.
It was proclaimed after the 44th Amendment on the ground of internal disturbance.
n147edb5dde1.x: President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed proclaimed the Emergency on 25 June 1975 on the ground of internal disturbance.
xa: The **1st** emergency was in **1962** (**Chinese aggression**).
**25 June** is now "**Samvidhan Hatya Diwas**".

nd5af82829af.s: Which judgment overruled the approach of ADM Jabalpur concerning the right to life and personal liberty?
o: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
nd5af82829af.x: The K.S. Puttaswamy judgment of 2017 overruled the approach taken in ADM Jabalpur concerning the suspension of Article 21 protections.
nd5af82829af.tq: Distinguish the later corrective privacy judgment from the earlier Article 21 cases.
xs: **ADM Jabalpur (1976)** was rejected in **K.S. Puttaswamy (2017)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
ADM Jabalpur had held even the **right to life** unenforceable during the emergency; it is now effectively overruled.
xa: The **44th CAA** ensures **Art. 359** can never suspend **Arts. 20 and 21**.
**Minerva Mills (1980)**: emergency proclamation **reviewable**.
**S.R. Bommai (1994)**: **9-judge bench**, landmark on **Art. 356**.

na82e9530042.s: Which case is associated with the striking down of the dissolution of the Bihar Legislative Assembly on partisan grounds in 2006?
o: K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
S. R. Bommai v. Union of India
Rameshwar Prasad v. Union of India
na82e9530042.x: In Rameshwar Prasad (2006), the Supreme Court struck down the dissolution of the Bihar Assembly on partisan grounds.
na82e9530042.tq: Use the case-name and judicial action as a paired identification test.
xs: **Rameshwar Prasad (2006)** struck down the **Bihar Assembly dissolution** on partisan grounds — so option **(4)** is correct.
**S.R. Bommai (1994)** is the 9-judge Art. 356 landmark; **ADM Jabalpur (1976)** is on the right to life; **Puttaswamy (2017)** rejected ADM Jabalpur.
xa: Bommai: no **arbitrary dissolution**; Assembly may only be **suspended** until Parliament approves.
Bommai: **floor test** is the only test of majority.

n7124705243c.s: The decision in S.R. Bommai v. Union of India was delivered by a Bench comprising:
n7124705243c.x: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India was decided by a nine-judge Constitution Bench.
n7124705243c.tq: Test a precise judicial composition figure using nearby Constitution Bench sizes as distractors.
xs: **S.R. Bommai (1994)** was decided by a **9-judge bench** (nine judges) — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is the landmark case on **Art. 356**.
xa: Principles: **judicial review** of proclamation; **floor test**; Assembly only **suspended** until Parliament approves; court can **restore** a government.
**Secularism + federalism** are basic features.

n803aab89e11.s: In S.R. Bommai v. Union of India, the Supreme Court recognised which as basic features of the Constitution?
n803aab89e11.x: The Bommai judgment recognised secularism and federalism as basic features of the Constitution.
xa: A state government acting **against secularism** can be dismissed.
Bommai: **9-judge bench**, **1994**.
Proclamation under 356 is subject to **judicial review**.

nda7b700ee52.s: Which event immediately preceded the proclamation of the National Emergency in June 1975 and formed an important background to it?
o: The Allahabad High Court voided Indira Gandhi’s 1971 election.
The Lok Sabha passed a resolution of no confidence against the Union Cabinet.
The Supreme Court struck down the 42nd Amendment.
The Election Commission postponed the general election indefinitely.
nda7b700ee52.x: The Allahabad High Court judgment voiding Indira Gandhi’s 1971 election formed the immediate political background to the 1975 Emergency.
nda7b700ee52.tq: Link a constitutional event to its immediate triggering political development.
xs: The trigger was the **Allahabad HC voiding Indira Gandhi's 1971 election** (**Indira Nehru Gandhi v Raj Narain**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
The emergency followed on **25 June 1975** on the ground of "**internal disturbance**".
xa: The **39th CAA** then put the **PM's and Speaker's election disputes** beyond courts.
The **42nd CAA (1976)** — the "**mini-constitution**" — raised Lok Sabha/Assembly terms to **6 years**.
**ADM Jabalpur (1976)** held even the right to life unenforceable.

n28613318c9b.s: Failure by a State to comply with directions given by the Union may be treated as a ground for President’s Rule under:
n28613318c9b.x: Article 365 provides that failure to comply with, or give effect to, Union directions can justify the conclusion that the State government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.
n28613318c9b.tq: Use the article-number distinction among emergency provisions.
xs: **Article 365** deems non-compliance with **Union directions** a ground for President's Rule — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Art. 355** is the Union's duty to protect states (basis for 356); **Art. 360** is Financial Emergency; **Art. 352** is National Emergency.
xa: President's Rule can come on the **Governor's report or otherwise**.
⚠ **1 month – 2 months – 6 months** = **352 – 360 – 356** approval windows.

n86aad0bfb0b.s: During President's Rule, the State is administered on behalf of the President by the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
n86aad0bfb0b.x: The Governor administers the State on behalf of the President, Parliament legislates for it, and the High Court is unaffected.
xa: **Ambedkar** hoped Art. 356 would remain a "**dead letter**".
**Manipur**: PR imposed **Feb 2025**; second extension till **Feb 2026**.

n17552066572.s: The first and longest spell of President’s Rule in Andhra Pradesh extended from:
n17552066572.x: The first and longest spell in Andhra Pradesh began on 18 January 1973 and ended on 10 December 1973.
n17552066572.tq: Match both endpoints of a constitutional time period, not merely its starting year.
xs: The first and longest AP spell ran from **18 January 1973 to 10 December 1973** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It followed the **Jai Andhra** agitation and ended when **Jalagam Vengala Rao** became CM.
**1 March – 8 June 2014** (option 4) was the **second** spell.
xa: **First PR in AP**: **January 1973** (PYQ **2019/2021**).
The 1973 spell ended after the **Six-Point Formula**, validated by the **32nd CAA, 1973** (**Art. 371D**).
**First PR in India**: **Punjab, 1951**.

n6a6045cfd4a.s: In December 2020, the AP High Court asked whether it could record a breakdown of constitutional machinery in the State. This relates to:
n6a6045cfd4a.x: A breakdown of constitutional machinery in a State is the ground for President's Rule under Article 356.
xa: PR is on the **Governor's report or otherwise**.
**First PR in AP**: **January 1973**.

n0f07d2cea5e.x: 25 June is observed as “Samvidhan Hatya Diwas” in remembrance of the proclamation of the 1975 Emergency.
n0f07d2cea5e.tq: Test the exact official commemorative expression rather than a near-synonym.
xs: **25 June** is observed as "**Samvidhan Hatya Diwas**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
It marks the emergency proclaimed on **25 June 1975** on the ground of "**internal disturbance**".
xa: It was proclaimed by President **Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed**.
Earlier emergencies: **1962** (Chinese aggression) and **1971** (Indo-Pak war).
Background: **Allahabad HC** voided Indira Gandhi's **1971** election.

n15f59f2fe62.s: The Six-Point Formula relating to the 1973 Andhra Pradesh episode was validated through the:
n15f59f2fe62.x: The Six-Point Formula was validated by the 32nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1973, which inserted Article 371D. The 33rd Amendment concerned resignation of legislators.
n15f59f2fe62.tq: Distinguish the closely numbered 32nd and 33rd Amendments by their subject matter.
xs: The **Six-Point Formula** was validated by the **32nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1973** (**Art. 371D**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ The **33rd CAA** (option 2) concerns **resignation of legislators**, not the Six-Point Formula.
xa: The **1973** AP spell of President's Rule ended after the Six-Point Formula.
That spell ran **18 Jan 1973 - 10 Dec 1973**, after the **Jai Andhra** agitation; it ended when **Jalagam Vengala Rao** became CM.
AP's 2nd spell: **1 Mar 2014 - 8 Jun 2014**, after CM **Kiran Kumar Reddy** resigned over bifurcation.

ndd15f2f8938.s: Article 263 empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council primarily to
o: investigate and discuss subjects of common interest between the Union and States or among States
audit the accounts of State Governments
ndd15f2f8938.x: Article 263 contemplates an Inter-State Council for investigating and discussing subjects of common interest between the Union and States or among States, and for making recommendations on such matters.
ndd15f2f8938.tq: Focus on the exact constitutional functions instead of assigning judicial or executive powers to the Council.
xs: Under **Art. 263**, the **President** may set up an ISC to **investigate and discuss subjects of common interest** and coordinate policy — so option **(1)** is correct.
Adjudication of disputes is not its role; river disputes go under **Art. 262**.
xa: ⚠ **Art. 262** = river water disputes; **Art. 263** = Inter-State Council; **Art. 131** = original jurisdiction (excludes water disputes).
The ISC was set up in **1990** under Art 263 (APPSC-G1 **2017** key).
Its **Chairman** is the **Prime Minister**; its Standing Committee is chaired by the **Union Home Minister**.

n72cd2de799a.s: The Sarkaria Commission proposed constitutional status for a renamed National Economic and Development Council under Article:
n72cd2de799a.x: The NEDC was to get status under Article 263; Article 280 deals with the Finance Commission.
xa: The **ISC** was set up in **1990** under Art 263.
Earlier backers: **ARC (1966-69)** and **Rajamannar Committee (1969)**.

n7fd43d98886.s: Which Article guarantees freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India?
n7fd43d98886.x: Article 301 declares freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse throughout India, subject to the provisions that follow.
n7fd43d98886.tq: Match the article number with its central principle before considering exceptions.
xs: **Article 301** guarantees **freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse** throughout India — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Art 302** lets Parliament restrict it in **public interest**; **Art 304** covers state restrictions; **Art 307** provides an authority.
xa: **Art 303**: no **preference/discrimination** by Union or states.
**Art 305**: saving of existing laws and **state monopolies**.
**Art 306** (Part B states) is **repealed**.

n1fb64a76b33.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Articles 301 to 307?
o: Article 306 continues to operate as the principal provision for Part B States
Article 303 deals with preference or discrimination by the Union or States
Article 305 saves existing laws and State monopolies
Under Article 302, Parliament may restrict trade, commerce and intercourse in the public interest
n1fb64a76b33.x: Article 306, relating to Part B States, has been repealed.
xa: **Art 304(b)**: a State bill needs the **President's previous sanction**.
**Art 307**: authority for Arts 301-304, e.g. an **Inter-State Commerce Commission**.

n7a9a192b343.s: A State Legislature proposes a bill imposing restrictions on trade, commerce or intercourse with other States under Article 304(b). What constitutional requirement applies before the bill is introduced?
o: Previous consent of the Supreme Court
n7a9a192b343.x: A bill imposing reasonable restrictions in the public interest under Article 304(b) requires the previous sanction of the President before its introduction in the State Legislature.
n7a9a192b343.tq: Ask which constitutional authority must act first in a State trade-restriction scenario.
xs: A bill under **Art 304(b)** needs the **President's previous sanction** — so option **(3)** is correct.
PYQ **2018**: a bill restricting goods from other states needs the **President's** previous sanction.
xa: **Art 301**: freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse.
**Art 302**: Parliament may restrict in **public interest**.
**Art 307**: authority such as an **Inter-State Commerce Commission**.

n58a4b5e8259.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about inter-State river water disputes?
o: The Supreme Court's original jurisdiction under Article 131 covers all such disputes
The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 provides for tribunals
Under Article 262, Parliament may exclude the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts
Article 131 does not cover inter-State water disputes
n58a4b5e8259.x: Article 131 does not cover inter-State water disputes, since Article 262(2) lets Parliament bar court jurisdiction over them.
xa: **River Boards Act 1956**: **no board** ever set up.
⚠ **Art. 262** = river disputes; **Art. 263** = Inter-State Council.

n9518a1cc295.s: The Standing Committee of the Inter-State Council is chaired by the:
n9518a1cc295.x: The Prime Minister chairs the Council, while the Union Home Minister chairs its Standing Committee.
xa: ⚠ Zonal Council vice-chairman = a **CM by annual rotation**.
Members include **6 Union Cabinet ministers** nominated by the PM.

nf522e4e7d6c.s: The Inter-State Council under Article 263 is:
o: a recommendatory body for consultation on inter-governmental matters
an extra-constitutional body created by executive resolution
a recommendatory body whose decisions legally bind all States
a judicial body whose awards bind like Supreme Court judgments
nf522e4e7d6c.x: The Inter-State Council is a constitutional, recommendatory body under Article 263; it is neither judicial nor created by mere executive resolution.
xa: Questions are decided by **consensus**; the **Chairman's view** on consensus is final.
Its secretariat is the **Inter-State Council Secretariat** (**MHA**).
Set up in **1990** on the **Sarkaria** recommendation.

nbb830ae68a7.s: The Inter-State Council under Article 263 was set up in 1990 on the recommendation of the:
nbb830ae68a7.x: The Council was established in 1990 following the Sarkaria Commission; the ARC and Rajamannar Committee had earlier supported it, and Punchhi came later.
xa: Set up under **Art 263** (APPSC-G1 **2017** key).
Sarkaria's term was a permanent "**Inter-Governmental Council**".
It is **recommendatory**, deciding by **consensus**.

ne48459c1ca2.s: Which one of the following States is included in the Southern Zonal Council according to the current composition?
ne48459c1ca2.x: The Southern Zonal Council includes Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana and Puducherry.
ne48459c1ca2.tq: Use regional grouping to distinguish Southern members from Central, Eastern and Northern members.
xs: **Telangana** is a member of the **Southern Zonal Council** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Southern members: **AP, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana, Puducherry**.
**Chhattisgarh** is in the **Central** Council and **Rajasthan** in the **Northern** Council.
xa: ⚠ APP's list omits Telangana; **IYB 2026** and LENS include it.
The **31st Southern Zonal Council** met on **20 Aug 2026** at **Mamallapuram** (TN), chaired by **Amit Shah**.

n0bc12957a31.s: The Vansadhara Water Disputes Tribunal was constituted in:
n0bc12957a31.x: The Vansadhara Tribunal dates from 2010; the Godavari and First Krishna Tribunals from 1969 and the Second Krishna Tribunal from 2004.
xa: ⚠ Tribunals involving AP: **Godavari**, **Krishna-II**, **Vansadhara** (with Odisha).
Other tribunals: **Narmada 1969**, **Ravi-Beas 1986**, **Cauvery 1990**, **Mahadayi 2010**.
Tribunals are set up under the **ISRWD Act, 1956**.

n220002a3a28.s: The Mahadayi Water Disputes Tribunal (2010) involves Goa, Karnataka and:
n220002a3a28.x: The Mahadayi Tribunal involves Goa, Karnataka and Maharashtra.
xa: Years: Narmada **1969**, Ravi-Beas **1986**, Cauvery **1990**, Mahadayi **2010**.
⚠ **Mullaperiyar** dam (**1895**, Periyar) is in Kerala but run by TN under a lease.

na086629b2dc.s: Under Section 3 of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, a State having a river-water dispute complains to the:
na086629b2dc.x: Section 3 of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 provides for a State to make a complaint to the Central Government regarding an inter-State river-water dispute.
na086629b2dc.tq: Apply the “who receives the complaint?” test before identifying the adjudicatory body.
xs: Under **Section 3** of the ISRWD Act, a State complains to the **Central Government** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The Supreme Court can be barred under **Art. 262(2)**, so a State does not go to it directly.
xa: In **Aug 2026**, Telangana planned to raise **Karnataka's unauthorised Krishna projects** under **Section 3**.
The ISRWD Act provides for **tribunals**.

nc12fb9e0b9a.s: The Krishna River Management Board (KRMB) and Godavari River Management Board (GRMB) were set up under the:
nc12fb9e0b9a.x: KRMB and GRMB come from the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 and work with an Apex Council.
xa: AP-Telangana disputes: control of boards, **Rayalaseema Lift**, hydel generation.
**Jan 2026**: first **CWC-chaired** inter-state committee meeting.

n4379f9487ff.s: At the January 2026 CWC-chaired inter-State meeting, Andhra Pradesh said Telangana's 50:50 Krishna water demand:
o: is contrary to the KWDT awards and Apex Council decisions
should be settled jointly through the Zonal Council
should be referred to the Supreme Court
n4379f9487ff.x: Andhra Pradesh rejected the 50:50 demand as contrary to the KWDT awards and the Apex Council's decisions.
xa: AP also objected to **968 tmcft** of Godavari water for Telangana projects not quantified under the **GWDT award**.
Framework: **KRMB**, **GRMB**, **Apex Council** under APRA **2014**.

n31f87331dac.s: The coalition era, giving the States a greater say in Centre-State relations, began in the:
n31f87331dac.x: Congress dominance marked the 1950s and early 1960s, opposition State governments rose from the mid-1960s, and the coalition era began in the 1990s.
xa: In the first phase, states **relied on grants**; calm except **new-state demands**.
Planning grants overlapped the FC until **NITI Aayog, 2015**.

n3d0ebd81449.s: The decision in S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) is particularly associated with which of the following propositions?
o: The Governor has unlimited discretion in all matters
Article 356 action is completely beyond judicial scrutiny
The GST Council has binding legislative authority
Article 356 action is subject to judicial review
n3d0ebd81449.x: S.R. Bommai established that the exercise of power under Article 356 is reviewable by the courts.
n3d0ebd81449.tq: Match the landmark case with its distinctive constitutional principle.
xs: **S.R. Bommai (1994)** held **Art. 356** action **subject to judicial review** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Option 2 ("beyond judicial scrutiny") is the opposite of the ruling.
xa: Courts are one of the **drivers** of Centre-State relations, along with constitutional design, planning and party politics.
**Sarkaria** wanted Art. 356 used **very sparingly, as a last resort**.
**Rajamannar** wanted **complete elimination of Art. 356**.

n2aaed8273a5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the State autonomy debate in India?
o: Autonomy demands grew after the Congress lost power in many States in the mid-1960s
Coalition politics after the 1990s led towards more cooperative federalism
The Punjab militancy of the 1980s is cited in favour of greater State autonomy
The Punjab militancy of the 1980s is cited to stress national unity
n2aaed8273a5.x: The Punjab militancy is cited against greater autonomy, stressing unity.
xa: Arguments against autonomy: **unity and integrity**; **regional disparities** need a strong redistributive Centre.
Arguments for: states **lack resources** (UPPSC **2007** key); **linguistic and cultural identity**.

n6c028eb4f53.s: The demand to restrict the Centre to defence, foreign affairs, currency and communications was specifically associated with:
n6c028eb4f53.x: This four-subject demand is associated with Punjab and West Bengal; Tamil Nadu's position sought deletion of Article 356 and abolition of the All India Services and Planning Commission.
xa: The Rajamannar Committee was appointed in **1969** (report **1971**); TN Assembly resolution **1974**.
⚠ AIS: **Rajamannar = abolish**; **Sarkaria = strengthen**.

n54f7b5e46a8.s: A principal argument for greater State autonomy is that States:
o: have surplus revenue beyond their needs
lack adequate resources for the duties assigned to them
have no role in delivering public services
n54f7b5e46a8.x: A major argument for State autonomy is that States often lack sufficient resources to perform their constitutionally assigned duties.
xa: Another argument for: **linguistic and cultural identity**, e.g. **resistance to Hindi in TN**.
Arguments against: **unity and integrity**, **regional disparities**, the **Punjab militancy** of the **1980s**.
Devolution: **16th FC** keeps **41%**; states want **50%**.

nf445b6ecc82.s: A commission on Centre-State relations was constituted by the Union Government in June 1983 under a retired Supreme Court judge. It is:
nf445b6ecc82.x: The Sarkaria Commission was set up by the Centre in June 1983 under Justice R.S. Sarkaria, a retired Supreme Court judge, and reported in 1988 with 247 recommendations. The Rajamannar Committee (1969) was appointed by Tamil Nadu, the ARC dates to 1966, and the Punchhi Commission came later (2007).
xs: It is the **Sarkaria Commission** — appointed by the Centre in **June 1983** under **Justice R.S. Sarkaria**, a **retired SC judge** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Rajamannar (1969)** was appointed by **Tamil Nadu**; **ARC** dates to **1966**; **Punchhi** came in **2007**.
xa: Sarkaria reported in **1988** with **247 recommendations**.
Its advice led to the **Inter-State Council** in **1990**.
Sarkaria favoured **strengthening** the All India Services.

n6b1b894ac40.s: Which one of the following was a recommendation of the Rajamannar Committee?
o: Appointment of Governors as recent active politicians
A four-month period for assent to every Bill
Strengthening of the All India Services
n6b1b894ac40.x: The Rajamannar Committee recommended abolishing the Planning Commission, eliminating Article 356 and establishing an Inter-State Council under Article 263.
n6b1b894ac40.tq: Use the commission-specific recommendation and reject proposals belonging to other bodies.
xs: Rajamannar recommended **abolishing the Planning Commission** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Strengthening AIS** (option 3) was **Sarkaria**; Rajamannar wanted AIS **abolished**.
The **four-month assent** period (option 2) was **NCRWC**; Sarkaria wanted Governors **not recent active politicians** (option 1 is the reverse).
xa: Rajamannar also wanted **complete elimination of Art. 356** and an **Inter-State Council** under Art. 263.
The Planning Commission was criticised for making states "**suppliants for aid**" (Rajamannar).

n2f5ae442ebd.s: On residuary powers, the Sarkaria Commission proposed that:
o: all residuary powers go to the States
residuary taxation stay with Parliament and other residuary matters go to the Concurrent List
all residuary powers, including taxation, go to the Concurrent List
all residuary powers remain exclusively with Parliament
n2f5ae442ebd.x: Sarkaria proposed keeping residuary taxation with Parliament and placing the remaining residuary matters in the Concurrent List.
xa: Sarkaria also proposed **time-bound cesses**.
It wanted states **consulted** on **Concurrent List** laws.
It made **247 recommendations** (report **1988**).

n25c03cd1fe8.s: In the federal context, the Planning Commission was criticised as:
o: a statutory body collecting taxes on behalf of States
a judicial body adjudicating disputes between States
an extra-constitutional body that made States dependent on the Union for aid
a constitutional body controlling State Legislatures
n25c03cd1fe8.x: Critics called the Planning Commission an extra-constitutional institution that made States 'suppliants for aid'.
xa: Rajamannar wanted the Planning Commission **abolished**.
Plan grants overlapped the FC until **NITI Aayog, 2015**.
Other criticised institutions: **Governor**; **Arts 356, 256, 257, 365**; **cesses and CSS**.

na511993e6d5.s: The study team on Centre-State relations of the Administrative Reforms Commission (1966) was headed by:
na511993e6d5.x: M.C. Setalvad headed the study team; the ARC itself was chaired first by Morarji Desai and later by K. Hanumanthaiya.
xa: ARC recommended an **Inter-State Council** under **Art. 263**, **non-partisan Governors**, more delegation and finances to states.
Order: State first (**1969**, Rajamannar), then Centre (**1983**, **2007**).

na5efa37ac49.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission?
o: Abolition of the All India Services
Use of Article 356 very sparingly and as a last resort
Consultation with States on laws relating to the Concurrent List
na5efa37ac49.x: The Sarkaria Commission favoured strengthening the All India Services, not abolishing them.
xa: Sarkaria's Governor: an **eminent outsider**, not a recent active politician, with the **CM consulted**.
Also: **floor test**; bills decided within a set period; **247 recommendations**.

n08c955f7549.s: Which of the following was recommended by the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution regarding the Governor's handling of Bills?
o: The Governor should decide Bills only after a referendum
Every Bill should be reserved for the President
Assent should be withheld indefinitely in case of disagreement with the State Cabinet
Assent should be given within about four months
n08c955f7549.x: The NCRWC recommended that assent to Bills should be given within about four months. It also suggested safeguards concerning Article 356 and an order of preference in a hung Assembly.
n08c955f7549.tq: Identify the precise time-bound recommendation and reject extreme alternatives.
xs: **NCRWC** wanted assent **within about four months** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It did not ask that every bill be reserved for the President or that assent be withheld indefinitely.
xa: NCRWC hung-assembly order: **pre-poll alliance**, **largest party**, **post-poll coalition**.
It also proposed **Art. 356 safeguards** and an **All India Judicial Service**.
⚠ **Punchhi** wanted **time-bound disposal** of bills; Sarkaria wanted bills decided within a set period.

nae19c3d11bf.s: Which body proposed the concept of a 'localised emergency'?
nae19c3d11bf.x: The Punchhi Commission proposed the localised emergency; Rajamannar sought deletion of Article 356 and Sarkaria treated it as a last resort.
xa: **NCRWC** proposed **Art. 356 safeguards**.
**S.R. Bommai (1994)** made Art. 356 **reviewable**.

n2c827bc11e8.s: Which commission recommended that Governors be removed only through a procedure similar to the impeachment of the President?
n2c827bc11e8.x: The Punchhi Commission recommended a fixed tenure for Governors and a President-like (impeachment) removal procedure (APPSC-G1 2024 key), along with time-bound disposal of Bills and the localised emergency idea. Sarkaria wanted an eminent outsider as Governor, Rajamannar sought deletion of Article 356, and the ARC urged non-partisan Governors.
xs: **Punchhi** recommended a **President-like removal (impeachment) procedure** for Governors — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-G1 **2024** key).
**Sarkaria** wanted an **eminent outsider** as Governor; **Rajamannar** sought deletion of **Art. 356**; **ARC** urged **non-partisan Governors**.
xa: Punchhi also wanted a **fixed tenure** for Governors.
Punchhi: Art. 356 as a **localised emergency**; **regular PM-CM meetings**.

ne3ddd23e46b.s:
Which of the following were recommended by the Administrative Reforms Commission?
1. An Inter-State Council under Article 263
2. Non-partisan Governors
3. Complete deletion of Article 356
ne3ddd23e46b.x: The ARC recommended an Inter-State Council and non-partisan Governors; deleting Article 356 was the Rajamannar Committee's demand.
xa: ARC was appointed in **1966**; study team under **M.C. Setalvad**.
Chaired by **Morarji Desai**, later **K. Hanumanthaiya**.

n92e40acd617.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about central agencies and State consent?
o: The Enforcement Directorate needs a State's general consent to enforce PMLA and FEMA there
