The NIA can investigate scheduled offences without State consent
The NIA functions under the NIA Act, 2008
Under Section 6 of the DSPE Act, 1946, the CBI needs State consent to act in a State
n92e40acd617.x: The ED enforces PMLA, 2002 and FEMA, 1999 nationwide with no State consent needed.
xa: ⚠ Only the **CBI** needs state consent; **NIA** and **ED** do not.
Withdrawing **general consent** forces **case-by-case** consent.

n6bb53fa874e.s: If a State withdraws general consent to the CBI, then:
o: its cases pass automatically to the NIA
the CBI must obtain consent case by case
the CBI is permanently barred from all cases in the State
the CBI may investigate on Union direction without approval
n6bb53fa874e.x: Withdrawal of general consent means the CBI must seek the State's consent separately for each case.
xa: ⚠ **NIA** and **ED** need **no state consent**.
NIA investigates **scheduled offences** anywhere in India.

n41fe2d98580.s: State autonomy demands in India have mainly sought:
o: more powers, greater own revenue and less central administrative control
transfer of defence and foreign affairs to local bodies
a uniform language policy for all States
abolition of State legislatures and central taxation
n41fe2d98580.x: Autonomy demands sought more powers for States, more control over own revenue and reduced central administrative control.
xa: Main documents: **Rajamannar (1969)**, **Anandpur Sahib (1973)**, **West Bengal memorandum (1977)**.
For autonomy: states **lack resources** for their duties.
Against: **unity and integrity**; **regional disparities**.

n3ad9f89cc01.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about All India Services and State autonomy?
o: All India Services have no role in Centre-State coordination
Officers are governed in important respects by Central rules
States cannot fully discipline or remove such officers
Officers are recruited by the UPSC but serve in the States
n3ad9f89cc01.x: All India Services are also defended as promoting Centre-State coordination.
xa: APPSC-G2 **2025**: AIS **violate the federal principle** — **A and R both true, R explains A**.
In favour: **high standards**, **uniformity**, coordination.

ncc41ed85a80.s: Articles 256, 257, 365 and ____ are criticised in federalism debates as instruments of Union overreach.
ncc41ed85a80.x: Articles 356, 256, 257 and 365 are identified as provisions that may enable excessive Union intervention.
xa: Other criticised institutions: the **Planning Commission** (extra-constitutional), the **Governor** (appointed by the Centre).
**Cesses and CSS**: cesses (about **18%** of gross tax revenue) are not shared.
**S.R. Bommai (1994)** made Art. 356 reviewable.

n914a42bb187.s: The defeat of the 131st Amendment Bill, 2026 on Lok Sabha expansion sharpened which debate?
o: The debate on abolishing local governments
n914a42bb187.x: The defeat of the 131st Amendment Bill on Lok Sabha expansion sharpened the North–South debate.
xa: TN Assembly passed a unanimous resolution for a **fair share of tax devolution** (**Aug 2026**).
**Kurian Joseph Committee** (TN) Part I, **16 Feb 2026**, seeks a "**structural reset**".
States want **50%** devolution vs the **16th FC's 41%**.

n9ea65602ba5.s: Which one of the following explains fiscal centralisation after GST?
o: GST abolished the divisible pool of Union taxes.
State taxes expanded and all cesses entered the divisible pool.
Cesses and surcharges automatically joined the divisible pool.
GST subsumed several State taxes, while cesses and surcharges stayed outside the divisible pool.
n9ea65602ba5.x: GST subsumed several State taxes, while cesses and surcharges remain outside the divisible pool.
xa: The divisible pool is about **81%** of the Centre's gross tax revenue in **2025-26**.
Cesses are about **18%** of gross tax revenue.
States want **50%** devolution vs the **16th FC's 41%**.

n7aef1e99e6e.s: Special Category Status, not provided for in the Constitution, was granted to States by the:
n7aef1e99e6e.x: SCS was granted by the National Development Council using the Gadgil formula criteria.
xa: Benefit: **90%** Central funding of plan spending.
**14th FC** removed the special/general distinction, meeting gaps via **42%** devolution + **revenue deficit grants**.

nea8ca8f5b48.s: What did the Union Government provide to Andhra Pradesh instead of granting the promised Special Category Status?
o: A separate Finance Commission for Andhra Pradesh
nea8ca8f5b48.x: The Centre subsequently provided a special assistance package in 2016 instead of granting SCS.
nea8ca8f5b48.tq: Separate the assurance of SCS from the substitute measure actually provided.
xs: The Centre gave AP a **special assistance package (2016)** instead of SCS — so option **(2)** is correct.
The SCS promise was **not written into APRA 2014**.
xa: The PM's assurance in the **Rajya Sabha** (**20 Feb 2014**) was SCS for **5 years**.
The Centre's main reason for denial: the **14th FC** (**42%** devolution + revenue deficit grants).
The demand is still alive (**2026**).

n9a0e578e30c.s: Under Special Category Status, the Central share in funding of plan spending was:
n9a0e578e30c.x: SCS involved 90 per cent Central funding of plan spending; the 14th Finance Commission instead raised devolution to 42 per cent and used revenue deficit grants.
xa: The 14th FC formula was the Centre's **main reason for denying SCS** to AP.
SCS criteria: **hilly terrain**, low density or tribal share, **border location**, backwardness, **weak finances**.
SCS is **not in the Constitution**.

nbac55bed984.s: Which of the following is NOT cited as contributing to centralisation in contemporary federalism debates?
nbac55bed984.x: State Finance Commissions strengthen local fiscal devolution; cesses, CSS and GST are cited in the centralisation critique.
xa: Cesses are about **18%** of gross tax revenue and are **not shared**.
Divisible pool = about **81%** of Centre's gross tax revenue in **2025-26**.
Also criticised: **Arts 356, 256, 257, 365** as tools of Union overreach.

n56574b11101.s: Which one of the following is the odd one out among bodies associated with reviewing Centre-State relations?
n56574b11101.x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) dealt with State funding of elections (partial funding in kind to recognised parties), not Centre-State relations. The Rajamannar Committee (1969), the Sarkaria Commission (1983) and the ARC (1966, Setalvad study team) all reviewed Centre-State relations.
n56574b11101.tq: Indrajit Gupta = election funding, not federalism.
xs: The **Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998)** is the odd one out — so option **(3)** is correct.
It dealt with **State funding of elections** (partial funding in kind to recognised parties), not Centre-State relations.
**Rajamannar (1969)**, **Sarkaria (1983)** and **ARC (1966)** all reviewed Centre-State relations.
xa: Sarkaria made **247 recommendations**.
ARC's study team on Centre-State relations: **M.C. Setalvad**.

n2c3eaeecda5.s: Dr. P.V. Rajamannar, chairman of the Centre-State Relations Inquiry Committee (1969), was a former Chief Justice of the ____ High Court.
n2c3eaeecda5.x: P.V. Rajamannar was a former Chief Justice of the Madras High Court; the committee was appointed in 1969 and reported in 1971.
xa: Members: **A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar** and **P. Chandra Reddy** (three in all).
Also spelt "**Rajmannar**", including in the Group-II syllabus.
⚠ P.V. Rajamannar also chaired the **4th Finance Commission**.

nd618c01435c.s: Besides its Chairman, the members of the Rajamannar Committee were A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar and:
nd618c01435c.x: A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar and P. Chandra Reddy were the other two members; R.S. Sarkaria chaired a later commission.
xa: Chairman: **Dr. P.V. Rajamannar**, former CJ of the **Madras High Court**.
The committee had **three members** in all.
Set up by the **DMK** government under **Karunanidhi** in **1969**.

n65d366a99e3.s: The Rajamannar Committee is significant as the:
o: first Union-appointed commission on Centre-State relations
first committee on Centre-State relations appointed by a State
first committee to recommend abolishing the Finance Commission
first committee formed after the Inter-State Council was set up
n65d366a99e3.x: The Rajamannar Committee was the first committee on Centre-State relations appointed by a State.
xa: Appointed **1969** (report **1971**), chaired by **Dr. P.V. Rajamannar**.
Its intellectual legacy: the **Anandpur Sahib Resolution** and the **West Bengal memorandum**.
TN's **Kurian Joseph Committee** (**April 2025**) consciously follows Rajamannar.

n429992e4ff4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Rajamannar Committee?
o: It was to identify the causes of unitary tendencies in the working of the Constitution
It was to suggest measures securing the utmost autonomy for the States
It was to strengthen the Centre's control over education and health
n429992e4ff4.x: The committee sought to reduce central control, including over subjects such as education and health.
xa: Finding: the states had become "**administrative units of the Centre**".
Arts **256, 257 and 365** enabled this overreach.
It took forward **C.N. Annadurai's 1967** view that the Union need not control health and education.

nad43318d9ab.s: The Rajamannar Committee recommended the immediate setting up of a permanent Inter-State Council under Article:
nad43318d9ab.x: Rajamannar wanted a permanent Inter-State Council under Article 263 at once, along with a revitalised Finance Commission.
xa: It also sought to **delete Art 356** and **abolish IAS, IPS and IFS**.
It wanted the **Planning Commission** abolished.
Exam angle: in "NOT a Rajamannar recommendation", pick the option that **strengthens the Centre or the Governor**.

n6c4ad1c4792.s: With reference to Article 356, the Rajamannar Committee recommended:
o: Its complete deletion from the Constitution
Its wider application during constitutional emergencies
Its transfer from the Constitution to ordinary law
Its use only with the approval of the Inter-State Council
n6c4ad1c4792.x: The committee recommended the complete elimination of Article 356 as part of reducing central control over the States.
n6c4ad1c4792.tq: Use a direct constitutional-provision question with nearby but reversed recommendations as distractors.
xs: Rajamannar recommended **complete deletion** of **Article 356** from the Constitution — option **(1)** is correct.
It sought to cut central control — wider use or ISC-gated use was not its proposal.
xa: With Arts **256, 257 and 365** also gone, the Centre's override would end.
⚠ Contrast: **Sarkaria** wanted Art 356 used **very sparingly, as a last resort** — not deleted.
It also recommended **abolishing** the All-India Services and the **Planning Commission**.

n9359c90170f.s: The Rajamannar Committee viewed the Planning Commission as an extra-constitutional body because it:
o: controlled the recruitment to All-India Services
appointed the Governors of the States
alone decided grants to the States
n9359c90170f.x: The committee criticised the Planning Commission as an extra-constitutional body that alone decided grants to the States and recommended its abolition.
n9359c90170f.tq: Identify the specific institutional function attached to the body rather than its general description.
xs: Rajamannar called the **Planning Commission** extra-constitutional because it **alone decided grants to the States** — option **(4)** is correct.
It recommended **abolishing** it.
xa: It wanted the **Finance Commission** revitalised and revenue devolution **widened**.
It wanted the **All-India Services** (IAS, IPS, IFS) abolished to cut central administrative control.
It wanted a permanent **Inter-State Council** under **Art 263**.

n33d72449acb.s: The Rajamannar Committee recommended abolition of the All-India Services primarily to:
o: Reduce central administrative control over State governments
Transfer recruitment to the Planning Commission
Create a separate service for each district
Increase the control of the Union over State governments
n33d72449acb.x: Abolition of the All-India Services was recommended to reduce central administrative control over State governments.
n33d72449acb.tq: Link the institutional recommendation with its stated federal objective.
xs: Abolition of the **IAS, IPS and IFS** was to **reduce central administrative control over State governments** — option **(1)** is correct.
It aimed at less Union control, not more — so option 4 is the reverse.
xa: ⚠ **UPSC 1993** key: ending IAS and IPS = **Rajamannar**; the **Dhebar, Kalelkar and Kher** commissions did not.
It also recommended deleting **Art 356** and abolishing the **Planning Commission**.
It was the **first state-level** committee on Centre-State relations.

nd224f05b240.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the examples of subjects proposed for transfer to the State List?
nd224f05b240.x: Inland waterway navigation, industrial disputes, and oil fields regulation and development were cited examples. Foreign affairs was not among them.
nd224f05b240.tq: Identify the unrelated Union subject inserted into a specific transfer list.
xs: **Foreign affairs** was NOT among the subjects proposed for transfer — option **(3)** is the answer.

The examples were **inland waterway navigation**, **industrial disputes**, **oil fields** (regulation and development), **stock exchanges**, **trade unions**, **factories**, **electricity**, **publishing**.
xa: Subjects were to move from the **Union and Concurrent Lists** to the **State List**.
Central control over **education and health** was to end.
**Residuary powers** were to go to the **states**.

n9b6fa5f63dc.s: On residuary powers, the Rajamannar Committee and the Sarkaria Commission respectively favoured:
o: the States; the Concurrent List for non-tax residuary matters
n9b6fa5f63dc.x: Rajamannar wanted residuary powers given to the States; Sarkaria placed residuary powers other than taxation in the Concurrent List.
xa: Rajamannar also wanted more **Concurrent** subjects moved to the **State List**.
Sarkaria: **1983** (report **1988**), chaired by **R.S. Sarkaria**.
⚠ The **Inter-State Council (1990)** came through **Sarkaria**, not Rajamannar.

n49b2faca5c0.s: The Inter-State Council was established in 1990 through the influence of the:
n49b2faca5c0.x: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 through the Sarkaria Commission's influence.
xa: Sarkaria: appointed by the **Centre**, **1983** (report **1988**), chaired by **R.S. Sarkaria**.
**Punchhi**: Centre, **2007** (report **2010**), **M.M. Punchhi**.
**Kurian Joseph**: **Tamil Nadu**, **Apr 2025** (Part I, **16 Feb 2026**).

n4a4488d654a.s: The Rajamannar Committee recommended ending central control over which pair of subjects?
n4a4488d654a.x: The committee sought to end central control over education and health and to move more Concurrent subjects to the State List.
n4a4488d654a.tq: Test the exact subject pair associated with devolution of powers.
xs: Rajamannar sought to end the Centre's control over **education and health** — option **(3)** is correct.
This echoed **C.N. Annadurai's 1967** view that the Union need not control such subjects.
xa: It recommended moving more **Concurrent subjects** to the **State List**.
Examples for transfer: **stock exchanges**, **oil fields**, **trade unions**, **industrial disputes**, **electricity**.
**Residuary powers** were to go to the **states**.

n032bbcd4efe.s: The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly adopted a State autonomy resolution on the basis of the Rajamannar report in:
n032bbcd4efe.x: The Tamil Nadu Assembly adopted the State autonomy resolution in April 1974 on the basis of the report.
n032bbcd4efe.tq: Distinguish the resolution year from the committee’s appointment and report years.
xs: The TN Assembly adopted a **state autonomy resolution in April 1974** based on the report — option **(2)** is correct.
**1969** is when the committee was appointed and **1971** when it reported; **1983** is the **Sarkaria** year.
xa: The **Centre ignored** the report; no action was taken.
Its value: it put **state autonomy on the national agenda**.
DMK slogan: "**autonomy for the States, federalism at the Centre**".

nc914803d7a9.s: What was the immediate response of the Union Government to the Rajamannar Committee report?
o: It ignored the report and took no action on it.
It accepted the recommendations on Article 356 but rejected all others.
It referred the report to the Finance Commission for implementation.
It implemented all its recommendations through a constitutional amendment.
nc914803d7a9.x: The Centre ignored the report and took no action on its recommendations.
nc914803d7a9.tq: Test the actual governmental response, not the report’s later influence.
xs: The **Centre ignored** the report and **took no action** on it — option **(1)** is correct.
No Rajamannar recommendation was implemented — not Art 356, not via amendment or the Finance Commission.
xa: Its value: it put **state autonomy on the national agenda**.
The **Inter-State Council (1990)** came through **Sarkaria**, not Rajamannar.
The TN Assembly passed its **autonomy resolution** in **April 1974**.

nc12d7b88639.s: The Kurian Joseph Committee on Centre-State relations was appointed in:
nc12d7b88639.x: The Kurian Joseph Committee was appointed in April 2025, after Rajamannar (1969), Sarkaria (1983) and Punchhi (2007).
xa: Memory chain: **State**, then **Centre twice**, then a **state again** in **2025**.
Rajamannar and Kurian Joseph were set up by **Tamil Nadu**; Sarkaria and Punchhi by the **Centre**.
Report years: **1971**, **1988**, **2010**, and Kurian Joseph Part I on **16 Feb 2026**.

n499144acb01.s: Justice R.S. Sarkaria, who chaired the Commission on Centre-State relations, was a retired judge of the:
n499144acb01.x: Justice Rajinder Singh Sarkaria was a retired Supreme Court judge; his report made 247 recommendations.
xa: Its objective: examine the **balance of power** between Centre and states and suggest changes **within the constitutional framework** (**APPSC 2018** key).
The **Inter-State Council (1990)** is the main recommendation implemented.
Report submitted in **1988**.

n11db59633fd.s: With reference to the tenure of a Governor, which one of the following reflects the Sarkaria recommendation?
o: A six-year term co-terminus with the Legislative Assembly
A secure five-year term, cut short only for extremely compelling reasons
A tenure determined exclusively by the Chief Minister
A fixed three-year term, extendable without limitation
n11db59633fd.x: The Commission recommended a secure five-year tenure, which should not be cut short except for extremely compelling reasons.
n11db59633fd.tq: Test the exact tenure and the qualification attached to premature removal.
xs: Sarkaria recommended a **secure five-year term**, **cut short only for extremely compelling reasons** — option **(2)** is correct.
No six-year, three-year or CM-determined tenure was proposed.
xa: ⚠ **Punchhi** (Centre, **2007**) later proposed **fixed tenure** for Governors.
The CM must be **effectively consulted** on the appointment.
Appointments **strictly non-partisan**.

nf886c4a0aee.s: The Sarkaria Commission recommended that a Governor should decide on Bills:
nf886c4a0aee.x: Sarkaria recommended strictly non-partisan appointment of Governors and decision on Bills within a specified period.
xa: Governor: an **eminent person** **from outside the state**.
Tenure: secure **5-year term**.
The **Chief Minister** must be effectively consulted.

n5e2471a1a97.s: Which of the following was NOT a Sarkaria Commission recommendation on Article 356?
o: It should be used very sparingly, as a last resort
Loss of majority should be decided by the Governor's own assessment rather than a floor test
The State should be given a warning before it is invoked
Majority should be tested on the floor of the Assembly
n5e2471a1a97.x: Sarkaria wanted the majority tested by a floor test in the Assembly, not by the Governor's own assessment.
xa: **Hung Assembly:** invite parties in a **set order of preference** — later endorsed by **Punchhi (2010)**.
**Bommai (1994)** drew on Sarkaria to separate proper from improper uses.
⚠ Contrast **Rajamannar**: **abolish** Art 356.

n584724d5aed.s: The courts relied on the Sarkaria report in S.R. Bommai (1994) and in:
n584724d5aed.x: Bommai and Rameshwar Prasad relied on Sarkaria; Kesavananda Bharati came a decade before the Commission.
xa: Bommai drew on Sarkaria to separate **proper from improper** uses of Art 356.
Sarkaria: Art 356 as a **last resort**, after a **warning**, with a **floor test**.

nbd734e103a5.s: Before Parliament legislates on a subject in the Concurrent List, the Sarkaria Commission recommended that the Union should:
o: Consult the States through an institutionalised process
Seek permission from the Supreme Court
Obtain approval from every State Legislature
Refer the matter exclusively to the Finance Commission
nbd734e103a5.x: The Centre should consult the States before legislating on a Concurrent List subject, preferably through an institutionalised process of prior consultation.
nbd734e103a5.tq: Identify the recommended consultation mechanism without converting consultation into a veto.
xs: Sarkaria said the Centre should **consult the States** through an **institutionalised process** of prior consultation — option **(1)** is correct.
Concurrent List laws need no Supreme Court permission or approval of every State Legislature.
xa: Residuary powers (**Art 248**): **taxation** stays with **Parliament**.
⚠ Contrast Rajamannar: **residuary powers** to the **states**.
The main implemented Sarkaria idea: the **Inter-State Council (1990)**.

n3ad5615ca7c.s: Which of the following best reflects the Sarkaria recommendation on cesses and surcharges?
o: They should be collected exclusively by State governments.
They should be abolished immediately in all circumstances.
They should be kept to a minimum and be time-bound, after which they should merge into the shareable tax pool.
They should be unlimited and permanently excluded from the divisible pool.
n3ad5615ca7c.x: The Commission recommended that cesses and surcharges be kept to a minimum and made time-bound, with their subsequent merger into the shareable tax pool.
n3ad5615ca7c.tq: Identify the complete policy recommendation rather than an extreme alternative.
xs: Cesses and surcharges should be **kept to a minimum** and **time-bound**, then **merged into the shareable tax pool** — option **(3)** is correct.
Sarkaria neither demanded their immediate abolition nor made them permanent and unlimited.
xa: Current status (**2025-26**): about **18%** of gross tax revenue is in **non-shareable cesses**.
Actual devolution is therefore nearer **31-32%**.

n38feed4bb9d.s: With reference to residuary powers (Article 248), the Sarkaria Commission recommended that the residuary power of taxation should:
o: be placed in the Concurrent List
be shared equally through the Finance Commission
n38feed4bb9d.x: Sarkaria wanted the residuary power of taxation to remain with Parliament; only residuary powers other than taxation were to go to the Concurrent List. Transfer to the States was Rajamannar's view, and equal sharing through the Finance Commission was never proposed.
n38feed4bb9d.tq: Sarkaria: residuary tax stays with Parliament; non-tax residuary to Concurrent.
xs: Under **Art 248**, Sarkaria kept the residuary power of **taxation** with **Parliament** — option **(2)** is correct.
Residuary powers **other than taxation** were to go to the **Concurrent List**; transfer to the states was **Rajamannar's** view.
xa: Before Concurrent List laws, the Centre should **consult states** through an **institutionalised process**.
Sarkaria made **247 recommendations** (report **1988**).

n297e9d3341c.s: The Inter-State Council of 1990 implemented which Sarkaria recommendation?
o: A permanent intergovernmental forum under Article 263
Transfer of residuary taxation to the States
Mandatory dissolution of Assemblies under Article 356
n297e9d3341c.x: The Inter-State Council, set up in 1990 under Article 263, is regarded as the main implemented Sarkaria recommendation.
xa: Of the **247** recommendations, the ISC is the main one implemented.
Sarkaria: set up **June 1983**, report **1988**.
Its objective was change **within the constitutional framework**.

n90d72cfcd1a.s: Who served as the Chairman of the Commission on Centre-State Relations appointed in 2007?
n90d72cfcd1a.x: Justice Madan Mohan Punchhi, a former Chief Justice of India, chaired the Commission on Centre-State Relations appointed in 2007.
n90d72cfcd1a.tq: Discriminate between the chairmen of successive Centre-State relations commissions.
xs: The 2007 Commission on Centre-State Relations was chaired by **Justice Madan Mohan Punchhi**, former **Chief Justice of India** — option **(2)** is correct.
**N.R. Madhava Menon** was only a **member**; **Sarkaria** headed the earlier **1983-88** commission.
xa: Other members: **Dhirendra Singh**, **V.K. Duggal**, **N.R. Madhava Menon**.
Set up by the **UPA government** in **April 2007**; report **2010**, **7 volumes**.

na041d295d17.s: The Punchhi Commission on Centre-State relations was set up in:
na041d295d17.x: The UPA government set it up in April 2007; 2010 is the year of its report.
xa: It also covered the **distribution of legislative and administrative powers**.
Report: **2010**, **7 volumes**.
Members: **Dhirendra Singh**, **V.K. Duggal**, **N.R. Madhava Menon**.

ncd241793086.s: The Punchhi Commission recommended that a Governor's tenure should be:
o: rotated among States every two years
a fixed five years, insulated from Central pressure
limited to three years by Parliament
at the pleasure of the Union Cabinet
ncd241793086.x: Punchhi recommended a fixed five-year tenure so that Governors are insulated from Central pressure.
xa: Governors should **not be Chancellors** of universities.
A **six-month deadline** to decide on bills, by constitutional amendment.
Removal only by **impeachment by the State Legislature** (Art 156 amendment).

nfcce7a52f4e.s: On State universities, the Punchhi Commission recommended that Governors:
o: be Chancellors only during President's Rule
not be made Chancellors or given other statutory university roles
compulsorily remain Chancellors of all State universities
nfcce7a52f4e.x: To avoid clashes with State Governments, Punchhi recommended that Governors not be made Chancellors or given statutory university roles.
xa: Status: Governors **still act as Chancellors** — not implemented.
Fixed **5-year** tenure; removal by **impeachment**.
A **six-month deadline** for decisions on bills.

n4f2272e1737.s: On Articles 355 and 356, the Punchhi Commission recommended that:
o: they be retained unamended and used freely
they be amended, with Article 356 used sparingly as a last resort
Article 356 be the normal remedy for State political disputes
n4f2272e1737.x: Punchhi recommended amending Articles 355 and 356 and using Article 356 sparingly, only as a last resort and never in a partisan manner.
xa: ⚠ "No need to amend Articles 355 and 356" is the **wrong** statement (**APPSC-G2 2017**).
"**Localised emergency**": a district or part of a district, for a **limited period**.
**Communal violence**: central forces **suo motu** for a short period.

nec4af006e62.s: A 'localised emergency' under Articles 355 and 356 would let the Centre:
o: take over the whole country indefinitely
take over a district or part of a district for a limited period
permanently suspend local governments in the State
dissolve every State Legislature during public disorder
nec4af006e62.x: A localised emergency would let the Centre take over a specific troubled area, such as a district, for a limited period instead of the whole State.
xa: Punchhi wanted **Arts. 355 and 356** amended.
Art 356 only **sparingly**, as a **last resort**, never partisan.
**Communal violence**: deploy central forces **without the State's consent** for a short period.

n49314c624b5.s: In the event of communal violence in a State, the Punchhi Commission recommended that the Centre may deploy central forces:
o: only after obtaining prior consent from the State Government
only after the approval of the Inter-State Council
suo motu, without prior State consent, for a short period, with consent obtained afterwards
permanently, without any subsequent consultation with the State
n49314c624b5.x: The recommendation permitted the Centre to deploy central forces suo motu without the State's prior consent for a short period; the State's consent would be obtained afterwards.
n49314c624b5.tq: Track the sequence of action first and consent afterwards.
xs: The Centre may deploy central forces **suo motu, without prior State consent, for a short period**, with **consent obtained afterwards** — option **(3)** is correct.
This was the **correct statement** in the **2018 PYQ**; permanent deployment was not proposed.
xa: Origin: the **1st ARC** — central armed forces "**either on their request or otherwise**".
"**Localised emergency**" for a troubled district.
Arts. **355 and 356** to be amended.

n6cb50d3ec46.s: Before Parliament legislates on a subject in the Concurrent List, the Punchhi Commission recommended that the Union should:
o: refer the matter exclusively to the Finance Commission
consult only the Governor of each State
obtain approval from every State Legislature as a constitutional prerequisite
reach broad agreement with the States through the Inter-State Council
n6cb50d3ec46.x: The Commission recommended that the Centre should reach broad agreement with the States through the Inter-State Council before legislating on Concurrent List subjects.
n6cb50d3ec46.tq: Identify the cooperative consultation mechanism linked to Concurrent List legislation.
xs: The Centre should **reach broad agreement with the States through the Inter-State Council** before Parliament legislates on Concurrent List subjects — option **(4)** is correct.
No approval of every State Legislature or Finance Commission reference was proposed.
xa: New **Union List** entry: **environment, ecology and climate change**.
ISC to meet **at least thrice a year**.
**National Water Resources Council** to play a bigger role.

nba363f44ab1.s: Which of the following was recommended as a new entry in the Union List?
nba363f44ab1.x: The Commission recommended adding a specific Union List entry on environment, ecology and climate change.
nba363f44ab1.tq: Distinguish the proposed Union List entry from subjects associated with State or local government.
xs: Punchhi proposed a new Union List entry on **environment, ecology and climate change** — option **(3)** is correct.
No Union List entry on health, agriculture or local government was proposed.
xa: Concurrent List laws need **broad agreement with the States** via the **ISC**.
**National Water Resources Council**: a bigger role.
**Arts. 243G and 243W** to be amended for local-body devolution.

n8b630104f44.s: Which of the following was NOT a financial recommendation of the Punchhi Commission?
o: Time periods of the Finance and Planning Commissions should be synchronised with the Five Year Plans
Backward States should get higher central transfers with an area-specific strategy
Cesses and surcharges should be left unlimited
Cesses and surcharges should be limited
n8b630104f44.x: Punchhi wanted cesses and surcharges limited, not left unlimited.
xa: CDI model answer: "**capping cesses at 5%**".
**National Water Resources Council** to play a bigger role.
Outside the divisible pool, the pool was about **81%** of gross tax revenue in **2025-26**.

n73a8ac3b52c.s: Which one of the following is correct about judicial rulings on Governors' timelines for Bills?
o: The 8 April 2025 Tamil Nadu case fixed timelines, but the 20 November 2025 Presidential Reference held courts cannot impose fixed timelines or deemed assent.
The 2025 Presidential Reference abolished judicial review of Governors.
The 8 April 2025 Tamil Nadu case let Governors withhold assent indefinitely.
The 2025 Presidential Reference made deemed assent mandatory.
n73a8ac3b52c.x: The Tamil Nadu case (8 April 2025) fixed timelines, but the Presidential Reference opinion (20 November 2025) held that courts cannot impose fixed timelines or deemed assent.
xa: ⚠ APPCA calls it a "**2023 Tamil Nadu case**" giving timelines "binding force" — **outdated**.
Punchhi proposed a **six-month deadline** on bills by constitutional amendment.

n8f427351325.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The 11th Inter-State Council meeting was the first in about a decade
The 11th Inter-State Council meeting (16 July 2016) took up the Punchhi recommendations
Article 156 has been amended to remove the words 'during the pleasure of the President'
In State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to the Governor (2023), the Supreme Court held a Governor cannot keep Bills pending indefinitely
n8f427351325.x: Article 156 is unchanged, so Governors still hold office during the pleasure of the President.
xa: **Tamil Nadu case (8 April 2025)**: fixed timelines.
**Presidential Reference (20 Nov 2025)**: no fixed timelines or "deemed assent" by courts.

n91420ebeb45.s: The Committee of Governors, set up in 1970 to study the role of Governors, was headed by:
n91420ebeb45.x: Bhagwan Sahay headed the Committee of Governors (set up 1970, reported 1971). R.S. Sarkaria headed the 1983 Commission on Centre-State relations, M.N. Venkatachaliah the NCRWC (2002), and P.V. Rajamannar the Tamil Nadu committee of 1969.
xs: The **Committee of Governors** (**1970**) was headed by **Bhagwan Sahay** — option **(2)** is correct.
**M.N. Venkatachaliah** chaired the **NCRWC** (report **2002**), a different body.
xa: It reported in **1971**.
It defined the Governor as the State's **constitutional head** and a **link with the Centre**.
The **2nd ARC** was chaired by **M. Veerappa Moily**, later **V. Ramachandran**.

nf631da28dab.s: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC) was chaired by:
nf631da28dab.x: M.N. Venkatachaliah chaired the NCRWC, which reported in 2002 after reviewing the Constitution's first 50 years.
xa: It also wanted greater **fiscal autonomy for States** and a stronger **third tier**.
Judiciary: **All India Judicial Service** + **National Judicial Commission**.

nf570d889e0c.s: The Bhagwan Sahay Committee of Governors described the Governor as:
o: the Union's political agent in the State
only the State's executive head, with no Union role
the presiding officer of the State Legislature
both the State's constitutional head and a link with the Centre
nf570d889e0c.x: The Committee saw the Governor as both the State's constitutional head and a link with the Centre, keeping watch and reporting to the Centre.
xa: The Committee of Governors was set up in **1970** and reported in **1971**.
**NCRWC** (**M.N. Venkatachaliah**, report **2002**) sought **safeguards against misuse of Art. 356**.
The **2nd ARC** stressed **restrained use of emergency powers**.

nceaf938297b.s: In relation to Article 356, the NCRWC recommended:
o: Its use only on a Rajya Sabha resolution
nceaf938297b.x: The NCRWC sought safeguards against misuse of Article 356 (along with greater fiscal autonomy and a stronger third tier); deletion was Rajamannar's demand.
xa: ⚠ NCRWC = **National Judicial Commission**; 2nd ARC = **National Judicial Council** (**2007-08**).
NCRWC: chaired by **M.N. Venkatachaliah**; report **2002**, reviewing the first **50** years.

n441b36f5441.s: A Code of Ethics, Right to Public Services laws and a Department of E-Governance were recommended by the:
n441b36f5441.x: The Second ARC recommended these, along with financial autonomy for PRIs and ULBs.
xa: Federal matters: **cooperative federalism**, restrained use of **emergency powers**, better **Centre-State coordination**.
Judiciary: a **National Judicial Council** (**2007-08**).

nindian-society-11-6.s: The National Integration Council is chaired by whom?
o: The Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission
The Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities
nindian-society-11-6.x: The Prime Minister chairs the National Integration Council, which works to fight communalism, casteism and regionalism.
n: The National Integration Council is chaired by the Prime Minister. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
xs: The **National Integration Council** is chaired by **the Prime Minister** — option **(2)** is correct.
Its focus is **national integration**.
xa: **Sri Krishna Commission** — **B. N. Srikrishna** — **Mumbai riots**.
**Liberhan Commission** — **M. S. Liberhan** — **Babri Masjid demolition**.
The **Inter-State Council** is also chaired by the **PM**.

nindian-society-11-14.s: The Sri Krishna Commission, chaired by B.N. Srikrishna, inquired into the:
nindian-society-11-14.x: The Sri Krishna Commission inquired into the 1992–93 Mumbai riots.
n: The Sri Krishna Commission was chaired by B. N. Srikrishna. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
The Sri Krishna Commission investigated the Mumbai riots. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
xa: **Liberhan Commission** (**M. S. Liberhan**) inquired into the **Babri Masjid demolition**.
Both are linked to **communalism** and **national integration**, and laid guidelines for **police accountability** and **riot prevention**.
**National Integration Council** is chaired by the **Prime Minister**.

n042ce93682a.s: The Indrajit Gupta Committee dealt with:
n042ce93682a.x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee dealt with electoral reform and State funding of elections, not Centre-State relations.
xa: **Kurian Joseph**: a **3-member** High-Level Committee, appointed **2025**.
Its Part I was tabled in the TN Assembly by CM **M.K. Stalin** (**19 Feb 2026**).
⚠ Kurian Joseph got **little attention** compared with Sarkaria (**2 Sep 2026**).

nindian-society-11-17.s: Which commission reviewed the Constitution, including issues related to social justice?
o: National Commission to Review Working of Constitution
nindian-society-11-17.x: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (Venkatachaliah, 2000) reviewed the Constitution, including social justice.
n: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution reviewed the Constitution, including social justice. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
xs: The **National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution** reviewed the Constitution including **social justice** — option **(1)**.
It was established in **2000**, chaired by **M.N. Venkatachaliah**, and reported in **2002**.
xa: It reviewed the Constitution's first **50** years.
NCRWC recommended greater **fiscal autonomy for States** and **safeguards against misuse of Art. 356**.
⚠ NCRWC = **National Judicial Commission**; 2nd ARC = **National Judicial Council**.

nf13400ca617.s: The description of NITI Aayog’s approach as “marble-cake federalism” refers primarily to
o: the working together of the Centre and States on a common platform through a bottom-up approach
the complete separation of Union and State functions
the financial control of States by the Union
the replacement of State governments by regional councils
nf13400ca617.x: NITI Aayog uses the expression “marble-cake federalism” for cooperative federalism, in which the Centre and States work together through a bottom-up approach.
nf13400ca617.tq: Translate the distinctive label into its underlying institutional meaning.
xs: **"Marble-cake federalism"** is NITI Aayog's name for **cooperative federalism**: the Centre and States **working together on a common platform** through a **bottom-up approach** — option **(1)**.
It is the opposite of a **complete separation** of Union and State functions, and does not mean Union financial control or replacing States with councils.
Under this model, planning starts with credible **village-level plans aggregated upwards**.
xa: **Cooperative federalism** was **first recommended by** the **Sarkaria Commission** (APPSC Group 1 **2017**).
**Competitive federalism** = competition **among States** for investment and citizens; driven by NITI's **performance rankings**.
**Usual pairing:** **GST Council = cooperative federalism**; NITI Aayog rankings = competitive federalism.

nf47a55f7525.s: The idea of cooperative federalism, in which the Centre and the States work together on a common platform, was first recommended by the:
nf47a55f7525.x: The Sarkaria Commission first recommended cooperative federalism (APPSC-G1 2017 key). Rajamannar sought state autonomy, the First ARC dealt with administrative matters, and NITI Aayog (2015) later put cooperative federalism into practice through its bottom-up approach.
nf47a55f7525.tq: Cooperative federalism: first recommended by Sarkaria.
xs: The idea of **cooperative federalism** was **first recommended by** the **Sarkaria Commission** — option **(2)** (APPSC Group 1 **2017** key).
**NITI Aayog** (**1 January 2015**) came much later and put cooperative federalism into practice through its **bottom-up** approach; it did not first recommend the idea.
xa: The **Inter-State Council** (**Art. 263**) was set up in **1990** on **Sarkaria's** recommendation; its chairman is the **PM**.
NITI's version of cooperative federalism is called **"marble-cake federalism"**.
⚠ **Competitive federalism** = States compete; **competitive sub-federalism** = **local bodies** compete.

n60b859048a1.s: The GST Council and NITI Aayog's State rankings are usually cited, respectively, as examples of:
n60b859048a1.x: The GST Council is a model of cooperative federalism, whereas NITI Aayog rankings promote competitive federalism.
xa: Competitive federalism is driven by NITI's **performance rankings** — **SDG**, **Health**, **Fiscal Health**.
Cooperative federalism was **first recommended by** the **Sarkaria Commission**.
⚠ Competitive **sub-federalism** = local bodies compete, e.g. ADP **"Champions of Change"** district rankings.

o: among States, and between States and the Centre in policy, to attract investment and improve outcomes
only between the two Houses of Parliament over financial legislation
among courts over the interpretation of federal provisions
only among municipalities for constitutional status
nd8ad0b8423f.x: Competitive federalism involves States competing with one another and with the Centre through policy initiatives to attract investment and improve outcomes.
nd8ad0b8423f.tq: Distinguish the level of competition and its policy objective instead of treating all inter-governmental relations as federal competition.
xs: **Competitive federalism** = competition **among States** (and between States and the Centre in policy) **to attract investment** and **improve outcomes** — option **(1)**.
Its tool is **better policies and services**; its driver is NITI's **performance rankings**.
xa: ⚠ **Competitive sub-federalism** = competition **among local bodies**.
**Cooperative federalism** = Centre and States on a **common platform**, first recommended by **Sarkaria**.
Usual pairing: **NITI rankings = competitive**; **GST Council = cooperative**.

ncb8666ccb31.s: A competition among district administrations or other local bodies to improve performance is best described as
ncb8666ccb31.x: Competitive sub-federalism means competition among local bodies. District rankings under the Aspirational Districts Programme provide an example.
ncb8666ccb31.tq: Identify the governmental level first: competition below the State level indicates sub-federalism.
xs: Competition **among local bodies** (e.g., districts) is **competitive sub-federalism** — option **(3)** (APPSC-G1 **2017** key).
**Cooperative federalism** is Centre and States working together; competitive federalism is competition **among States**.
xa: Example: **district rankings** on the ADP **"Champions of Change"** dashboard.
AP angle: **Alluri Sitharama Raju** district ranked **1st** in India in ADP **Basic Infrastructure** (March **2026**).
⚠ Competitive federalism = **States** compete; competitive sub-federalism = **local bodies** compete.

n72e603f3ed1.s: Under NITI Aayog's approach to cooperative federalism, planning is meant to proceed by:
o: Allocating plan funds from the Centre to States through a single national Five Year Plan
Leaving all planning to the Union Ministries with States only implementing schemes
Assigning planning exclusively to State Finance Commissions
Formulating credible plans at the village level and aggregating them progressively upwards
n72e603f3ed1.x: NITI Aayog follows a bottom-up approach in which credible village-level plans are formulated and aggregated at higher levels of government, unlike the top-down Planning Commission model.
n72e603f3ed1.tq: NITI plans grow from the village up, not from Delhi down.
xs: Under NITI's cooperative federalism, planning proceeds by **formulating credible plans at the village level and aggregating them upwards** — option **(4)**, a **bottom-up** approach.
A single national plan with Central allocation of plan funds belongs to the old **Planning Commission** model; NITI has **no financial powers** (no plan grants).
xa: NITI's version of cooperative federalism brings states together on a **single platform** — **"marble-cake federalism"**.
**NITI Aayog** replaced the **Planning Commission** by a **Union Cabinet resolution** of **1 January 2015**.
With NITI giving no plan grants, the **Finance Commission's** domain was restored.

nindian-polity-65-1.s: A Constitutional Body is one that is:
o: created by an Act of Parliament
created by a State Legislature alone
nindian-polity-65-1.x: A constitutional body is set up and empowered by the Constitution itself, such as the ECI or the CAG; bodies created by law are statutory.
n: A constitutional body is an authority or institution directly established within the text of the Constitution of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
A constitutional body is empowered within the text of the Constitution of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
A constitutional body is anchored within the text of the Constitution of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xa: Constitutional examples: **Election Commission**, **Finance Commission**, **CAG**, **Attorney General**, Public Service Commissions.
Statutory examples: **NHRC**, **Lokpal**, **NGT**.
Extra-constitutional: **NITI Aayog**, **Planning Commission**, **NDC**.

nindian-polity-65-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Planning Commission was a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament.
The National Development Council was set up by an executive order in 1952.
NITI Aayog was set up by a Cabinet resolution in 2015.
The Planning Commission was set up by a Cabinet resolution in 1950.
nindian-polity-65-2.x: The Planning Commission (1950) was created by a Cabinet resolution, so it was extra-constitutional and non-statutory.
n: The Planning Commission was established in 1950. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Planning Commission is an extra-constitutional body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Planning Commission is not a constitutional body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Planning Commission is not a statutory body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
NITI Aayog was established in 2015. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
NITI Aayog was established through a Cabinet Resolution dated 1 January 2015. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Planning Commission was established through a Cabinet Resolution dated 15 March 1950. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The National Development Council was established through an Executive Order dated 6 August 1952. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
An extra-constitutional or non-statutory body is established through an executive order or cabinet resolution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
NITI Aayog is an example of an extra-constitutional or non-statutory body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Planning Commission is an example of an extra-constitutional or non-statutory body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
NITI Aayog is not a constitutional body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
NITI Aayog is not a statutory body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xa: NITI Aayog is **non-constitutional, non-statutory**, with **no financial powers**.
NDC is now **inactive**; its role is taken by NITI's **Governing Council**.
The Planning Commission was **abolished** and replaced by NITI.

n21dc83675ab.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the structure of NITI Aayog?
o: The Prime Minister is its Chairperson and appoints the Vice-Chairperson
Its CEO is a Union Cabinet Minister with no fixed tenure
It can have at most two part-time members, by rotation
It can have at most four Union Ministers as ex-officio members
n21dc83675ab.x: The CEO of NITI Aayog is a Secretary-rank officer with a fixed tenure.
xa: Current Vice-Chairperson: **Ashok Kumar Lahiri** (**April 2026**), replacing **Suman K. Bery**.
Full-time members: **K.V. Raju**, **M. Srinivas**, **Abhay Karandikar**, **Gobardhan Das**, **Rajiv Gauba**.
The **Governing Council** (PM chairs) includes **CMs of all States** and of UTs with legislatures.

ne83966c3150.s: The Chief Ministers of which Union Territories are members of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog?
o: Puducherry, Lakshadweep, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Puducherry
Delhi, Chandigarh, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
ne83966c3150.x: The Governing Council includes the Chief Ministers of Union Territories having legislatures: Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Puducherry.
ne83966c3150.tq: Use the legislature-based classification to distinguish Union Territories represented by Chief Ministers.
xs: CMs of **UTs with legislatures** — **Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Puducherry** — sit on the Governing Council — option **(3)**.
Other UTs (like **Chandigarh**, **Lakshadweep**, **Ladakh**) are represented by their **Lt Governors**, not CMs.
xa: The Council is chaired by the **PM** and includes **CMs of all States**.
Also members: **ex-officio members**, the **Vice-Chairperson**, **full-time members** and **special invitees**.
It took over the role of the **NDC**, now inactive.

nf620d5dc52b.s: The State Support Mission of NITI Aayog is intended to help States
o: replace their elected local bodies with nominated bodies
obtain constitutional status for their planning departments
receive plan grants directly from NITI Aayog
nf620d5dc52b.x: The State Support Mission helps States build State Institutions for Transformation. GRIT in Gujarat and MITRA in Maharashtra are examples.
nf620d5dc52b.tq: Link the mission name to its institutional capacity-building function and reject the financial-power trap.
xs: The **State Support Mission** helps States build **State Institutions for Transformation** — option **(3)**.
Examples: **GRIT** (Gujarat) and **MITRA** (Maharashtra).
NITI cannot give **plan grants** — it has **no financial powers**, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: The Mission falls under NITI's mandate area "**NITI for States**" (cooperative and competitive federalism).
**Team India Hub** leads the States' engagement with the Centre (APPSC-GS **2018**).
**Regional Councils** handle issues spanning States, jointly headed by a **CM (by rotation)** and a **Union Minister**.

n8240096a399.s: Regional Councils of NITI Aayog are constituted primarily to deal with:
o: Allocation of funds to individual districts
Issues affecting more than one State
n8240096a399.x: Regional Councils address issues that affect more than one State.
n8240096a399.tq: Match the council type with the geographical scope of the issues it handles.
xs: **Regional Councils** deal with **issues affecting more than one State** — option **(4)**.
They are **jointly headed** by a **CM (by rotation)** and a **Union Minister**.
xa: ⚠ **Governing Council** = **PM** chairs; Regional Councils = CM by rotation + Union Minister.
NITI's two hubs: **Team India Hub** and **Knowledge and Innovation Hub**.
**DMEO** handles NITI's monitoring and evaluation mandate.

n308a1c178de.s: Which of the two hubs at the core of NITI Aayog leads the engagement of the States with the Centre?
n308a1c178de.x: NITI Aayog has two hubs: the Team India Hub, which leads State engagement with the Centre (APPSC-GS 2018), and the Knowledge and Innovation Hub, its think-tank arm. DMEO is the monitoring and evaluation office, and there is no 'Regional Council Hub'; Regional Councils are separate forums for issues spanning States.
xs: The **Team India Hub** leads the **States' engagement with the Centre** — option **(2)** (APPSC-GS **2018**).
The **Knowledge and Innovation Hub** is the other hub; **DMEO** is the monitoring and evaluation office, not a hub.
There is no "Regional Council Hub"; **Regional Councils** are forums for issues spanning States.
xa: NITI's four mandate areas: knowledge and innovation, **NITI for States**, transformational change, monitoring and evaluation (**DMEO**).
**State Support Mission** → **State Institutions for Transformation** (e.g., **GRIT**, **MITRA**).
NITI is called a "**directional and policy dynamo**".

n864c58f6103.x: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission; it follows a bottom-up approach and has no power to allocate plan grants.
xa: Legal status: **non-constitutional, non-statutory**, created by **Union Cabinet resolution**.
Its lack of financial powers is a common **criticism**: advice is **not binding**.
The **Finance Commission's** domain over grants was restored once plan grants ended.

n7ffc783880f.s: The usual Centre-State funding ratio for core Centrally Sponsored Schemes is:
n7ffc783880f.x: The usual ratio is 60:40; for North-Eastern and Himalayan States it is 90:10.
xa: CSS form a **large part of Centre-State transfers** and need **matching State contributions**.
Debate: CSS **squeeze State priorities** since the Centre decides parameters.
2015 classification: **core of the core**, **core**, **optional**.

nd109930e08a.s: Which of the following has been advanced as a criticism of Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
o: They eliminate all State contributions to development programmes
They make State Governments responsible for designing all national schemes
They can squeeze State priorities because programme parameters are decided by the Centre
They prevent the Centre from transferring funds to States
nd109930e08a.x: A major criticism is that CSS may squeeze State priorities because the Centre determines important programme parameters and States must provide matching contributions.
nd109930e08a.tq: Apply the financing structure to the federal-priorities debate.
xs: A key criticism: CSS can **squeeze State priorities** because **programme parameters are decided by the Centre** — option **(3)**.
CSS actually **require matching State contributions** and are a **large part of Centre-State transfers**, so options (1) and (4) are wrong.
xa: Suggested fixes: **revisit CSS**, **greater State say in GST design**, **regular ISC meetings**.
Funding pattern: **60:40**; **90:10** for North-Eastern & Himalayan States.
**GST critique**: curtailed States' taxation powers, plus **compensation disputes**.

nc6df32c90fb.s: The proposal for establishing Zonal Councils is associated with:
nc6df32c90fb.x: The proposal for Zonal Councils was made by Jawaharlal Nehru.
nc6df32c90fb.tq: Match the institutional proposal with its associated statesman.
xs: The **Zonal Councils** were **proposed by Jawaharlal Nehru** — option **(1)**.
They were set up under **Part III of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956**, as **statutory** bodies.
xa: Chair of **all five**: the **Union Home Minister**.
Each State: **CM + 2 ministers**; councils are **advisory only**.
**Inter-State Council** (**Art. 263**, **1990**) is chaired by the **PM**.

n1dfcd383119.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation
River boards are set up under the Inter-State Council Order, 1990
All five Zonal Councils are chaired by the Union Home Minister
Zonal Councils are statutory and advisory bodies
n1dfcd383119.x: River boards are set up under the River Boards Act, 1956.
xa: Zonal Councils are **statutory** under **Part III of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956**, proposed by **Nehru**.
The Inter-State Council is **recommendatory**; Zonal Councils are **advisory only**.
**GST Council** rests on **Art. 279A**.

n2a0ab5ad67a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about State-ranking indices?
o: Swachh Survekshan is released by NITI Aayog
NITI Aayog prepares the Export Preparedness Index with the Institute for Competitiveness
The SDG India Index of NITI Aayog is now localised to districts
Export infrastructure and export performance are pillars of the Export Preparedness Index
n2a0ab5ad67a.x: Swachh Survekshan is released by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, not NITI Aayog.
xa: ⚠ **Ease of Doing Business (BRAP)** = **DPIIT**, not NITI.
**State Health Index** = NITI with **MoHFW and World Bank**; **SEQI** = NITI with **MHRD**.
AP has **~70% of India's shrimp exports** → helps its EPI rank.

nf36d035777d.s: The Ease of Doing Business State Business Reform Action Plan is published by
nf36d035777d.x: The State Business Reform Action Plan rankings are associated with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).
nf36d035777d.tq: Match the index with its exact publishing institution and avoid substituting NITI Aayog.
xs: The **Ease of Doing Business** (**State Business Reform Action Plan**) is published by **DPIIT** — option **(3)**.
It is **not a NITI Aayog** index; **MoHFW** partners NITI on the State Health Index.
xa: ⚠ **Swachh Survekshan** = **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs** — also not NITI.
NITI indices: **SDG India Index**, **EPI**, **State Health Index**, **SEQI**, **Fiscal Health Index**.
AP in the **Fiscal Health Index 2023-24**: **17th**.

n7ec07434ab8.s: The State Health Index is also known by the title:
o: Progressive Health and Human Capital Index
n7ec07434ab8.x: NITI Aayog’s State Health Index is titled “Healthy States, Progressive India.”
n7ec07434ab8.tq: Discriminate between a formal title and a plausible reversal of its words.
xs: The **State Health Index** is titled "**Healthy States, Progressive India**" — option **(3)**.
Option (4) reverses the words — a trap.
xa: It is prepared by **NITI Aayog with MoHFW and World Bank**.
Health rankings are part of NITI's **competitive federalism** tools with **SDG** and **Fiscal Health** rankings.
**SEQI** = NITI with **MHRD**.

nd360ed04148.s: The 2015 sub-group of Chief Ministers classified Centrally Sponsored Schemes into which categories?
o: Core of the core, core and optional
nd360ed04148.x: The 2015 sub-group divided CSS into core of the core, core and optional schemes.
xs: The **2015 CM sub-group** classified CSS into **core of the core, core and optional** schemes — option **(3)**.
This sub-group on **Rationalisation of CSS** was convened by **Shivraj Singh Chouhan** (MP).
xa: Core schemes funding: **60:40** usually; **90:10** for **North-Eastern & Himalayan States**.
CSS need **matching State contributions**, with parameters set by the Centre.
Suggested fixes: **revisit CSS**, greater State say in **GST design**, regular **ISC meetings**.

n2ea872d3f21.s: In the SDG India Index 2023-24, Andhra Pradesh's score and category were:
n2ea872d3f21.x: Andhra Pradesh scored 74 out of 100 and was classified as a Frontrunner.
xa: The SDG India Index is by **NITI Aayog**, built to encourage **competitive federalism**, and now **localised to districts**.
**ASR district** ranked **1st** in ADP **Basic Infrastructure** (March **2026**).

nfacc3e2ed2a.s: Approximately what share of India’s shrimp exports is contributed by Andhra Pradesh?
nfacc3e2ed2a.x: Andhra Pradesh contributes approximately 70 percent of India’s shrimp exports, a factor associated with its EPI ranking.
nfacc3e2ed2a.tq: Recall the approximate percentage rather than confusing it with a rounded half or majority figure.
xs: Andhra Pradesh contributes **~70% of India's shrimp exports** — option **(2)**, about 70 percent.
This export strength **helps AP's rank** in the **Export Preparedness Index (EPI)**.
xa: The **EPI** is prepared by **NITI Aayog** with the **Institute for Competitiveness**.
EPI pillars: **export policy**, **business environment**, **export infrastructure**, **export performance**.
Other AP angles: **ASR district 1st** in ADP **Basic Infrastructure** (March **2026**); showcased for **Real Time Governance** and **AWARE**.

nf76873ee377.s: Transfer of work to field officers within the bureaucracy, without transfer to elected local bodies, is called:
nf76873ee377.x: Administrative delegation or deconcentration keeps functions within the bureaucracy, whereas democratic decentralisation transfers power to elected local bodies.
xa: Order of depth: **deconcentration → delegation → devolution**.
Three dimensions: **political** (decide), **administrative** (implement), **fiscal** (raise and spend).
**Vertical devolution** = States' share of the **divisible pool**; **horizontal** = allocation **among States** by formula.

n8d1502dea36.s: Which of the following represents the increasing order of depth of decentralisation?
n8d1502dea36.x: The order of increasing depth is deconcentration, delegation and devolution. Devolution transfers the greatest degree of authority to the receiving institution.
n8d1502dea36.tq: Arrange concepts by depth rather than by alphabetical order.
xs: The increasing order of depth is **deconcentration → delegation → devolution** — option **(3)**.
**Devolution** is the deepest: power moves to **elected** local bodies; deconcentration only shifts work to **field officers** within the bureaucracy.
xa: **Democratic decentralisation** is **Balwant Rai Mehta's** term.
Three dimensions of decentralisation: **political**, **administrative**, **fiscal**.
The **73rd Amendment** gave panchayats **constitutional status**, but **no independent taxing power**.

n572fc475024.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes vertical and horizontal devolution?
o: Vertical devolution is between Union and States; horizontal devolution is among the States
Vertical devolution concerns taxes; horizontal devolution concerns borrowing alone
Vertical devolution is among States; horizontal devolution is between Union and States
Both terms refer only to grants to local bodies
n572fc475024.x: Vertical devolution divides the divisible pool between the Union and States, while horizontal devolution distributes the States' share among the States.
n572fc475024.tq: Discriminate between two closely related fiscal terms by their direction of distribution.
xs: **Vertical devolution** = share of the **divisible pool** going from the **Union to States**; **horizontal devolution** = allocation of that share **among States** by a formula — option **(1)**.
Option (3) reverses the two terms.
xa: ⚠ The divisible pool (**Art. 270** taxes) **excludes cesses and surcharges**.
Vertical shares: **13th FC 32%**, **14th FC 42%**, **15th FC 41%**.
Highest horizontal weight in every FC: **income distance**.

nfa273800b99.s: Vertical fiscal imbalance in India arises mainly because:
o: Some States have higher per capita income than others
The States have the more buoyant taxes while the Union carries heavier spending duties
The Union has the more buoyant taxes while States carry heavier spending duties
The Union and the States have identical tax bases
nfa273800b99.x: The Centre controls the more buoyant taxes, while States bear major spending duties such as health, education, agriculture and police.
xa: Vertical devolution of the **divisible pool** corrects this imbalance.
⚠ Divisible pool **excludes cesses and surcharges** — a "shrinking divisible pool" is a criticism.
**18 states** had sought **50%** (Aug **2026**).

n0be8dd7d7a0.s: Which one of the following is excluded from the divisible pool of Central taxes?
n0be8dd7d7a0.x: Cesses and surcharges are excluded from the divisible pool. The divisible pool was approximately 81 per cent of gross tax revenue in 2025-26.
n0be8dd7d7a0.tq: Test the exact composition of a fiscal pool through exclusion.
xs: **Cesses and surcharges** are **excluded** from the divisible pool — option **(1)**.
The divisible pool is made up of **Art. 270** taxes, excluding cesses and surcharges.
xa: Vertical devolution = States' share of this pool; horizontal = its allocation **among States**.
Criticism: a **shrinking divisible pool**.
16th FC kept the States' share at **41%**.

n81d6dd21b75.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the legal position of the Eleventh Schedule after the 73rd Constitutional Amendment?
o: It contains subjects exclusively reserved for municipalities.
It automatically transferred all 29 subjects to Panchayats.
It provides a menu of 29 subjects that may be entrusted under Article 243G.
It abolished the discretionary role of the States in Panchayat functions.
n81d6dd21b75.x: The Eleventh Schedule contains 29 subjects that may be entrusted to Panchayats under Article 243G. It is a menu of possible functions and does not itself automatically transfer every subject.
n81d6dd21b75.tq: Distinguish a constitutional enabling provision from an automatic transfer of powers.
xs: The **Eleventh Schedule** (**29 subjects**) is **only a menu** that **may** be entrusted to panchayats under **Art. 243G** — option **(3)**.
It does **not automatically transfer** all 29 subjects; the word in 243G is "**may**", so States keep discretion.
xa: Mandatory features of the 73rd Amendment: constitutional status, **three tiers**, direct elections, **5-year term**, reservation, **SEC (243K)**, **SFC (243I)**.
**Art. 243H**: own taxes, duties, tolls, fees only if the **State Legislature authorises**.
**Art. 243X** is the **municipal equivalent** of 243H.

nc659fea3920.s: Under Part IX of the Constitution, the State Finance Commission and the State Election Commission for Panchayats are provided for, respectively, in:
nc659fea3920.x: Article 243I provides for the State Finance Commission and Article 243K for the State Election Commission, both mandatory under the 73rd Amendment. The reverse pairing is wrong; 243H (taxing powers) and 243G (powers and functions) deal with other matters; Articles 280 and 324 concern the Union Finance Commission and the Election Commission of India.
xs: The **SFC** is in **Article 243I** and the **State Election Commission** in **Article 243K** — option **(1)**.
**243H** covers panchayat taxing powers and **243G** the Eleventh Schedule menu; **Art. 280** is the **Union Finance Commission**.
xa: Under **243I**, grants-in-aid come from the **State Consolidated Fund** on **SFC** advice.
Comparative note: **Union FC (Art. 280, President)** vs **SFC (Art. 243I, Governor)**.
**243J / 243Z**: State legislature provides for maintenance and **audit** of LB accounts.

ne5ab22def67.s: The Technical Guidance and Support provided by the Comptroller and Auditor General over the audit of local bodies was recommended by which Finance Commission?
ne5ab22def67.x: CAG Technical Guidance and Support over local-body audits was recommended by the Eleventh Finance Commission.
ne5ab22def67.tq: Discriminate between closely related Finance Commission numbers.
xs: **CAG's Technical Guidance and Support (TGS)** over local body audit was recommended by the **11th FC** — option **(3)**, the Eleventh Finance Commission.
The 14th and 16th FCs are known for other things: **42%** share and the **GDP criterion** respectively.
xa: Audit of LB accounts is provided by State law under **Art. 243J / 243Z**.
15th FC performance conditions: **audited accounts** and **property-tax floor rates**.
**Weak accrual accounting** keeps most LBs out of the bond market.

nba14a9cdca5.s: Panchayats may levy taxes, duties, tolls and fees only when authorised by the State Legislature under Article:
nba14a9cdca5.x: Under Article 243H Panchayat taxing power depends on State legislative authorisation; property tax is a major own-source revenue.
xa: Other own revenue: **markets, fairs, water, lighting**.
**Assigned taxes** = State-levied taxes handed over to panchayats; **shared taxes** = share of State taxes as per SFC.
**SVAMITVA** drone maps create a **rural property-tax baseline**.

necbcc4fb7bd.s: Who among the following chaired the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
necbcc4fb7bd.x: Dr Arvind Panagariya chaired the Sixteenth Finance Commission. Y.V. Reddy and N.K. Singh chaired the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Finance Commissions respectively.
necbcc4fb7bd.tq: Use a chairperson-to-Commission association instead of relying on the numerical order alone.
xs: The **16th FC** was chaired by **Dr Arvind Panagariya** — option **(2)**.
**Y.V. Reddy** chaired the **14th FC** and **N.K. Singh** the **15th FC**.
xa: 16th FC constituted **31 Dec 2023**; report tabled **1 Feb 2026**; award **1 Apr 2026 – 31 Mar 2031**.
The 14th FC was constituted on **2 Jan 2013**.
16th FC added **contribution to GDP** (**10**) and dropped **revenue deficit grants**.

n244db23d27f.s: Under the Fourteenth Finance Commission, the weight given to income distance was:
n244db23d27f.x: Income distance carried 50 per cent; population 1971 had 17.5, area 15 and forest cover 7.5 per cent.
xa: Income distance carried the highest weight in **every FC** (13th FC: **47.5**, called fiscal capacity distance).
The 14th FC used **1971** population plus the change since; FC-15 used **2011**.
14th FC chair: **Y.V. Reddy**; vertical share **42%**.

n4eb17277134.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Fifteenth Finance Commission's tax devolution criteria?
o: Population, 2011 carried a weight of 15 per cent
Tax and fiscal effort carried a weight of 2.5 per cent
Demographic performance carried a weight of 12.5 per cent
Contribution to GDP was included as a criterion
n4eb17277134.x: Contribution to GDP was introduced by the Sixteenth Finance Commission, not the Fifteenth.
xa: 15th FC: **income distance 45**, **area 15**, **forest and ecology 10**.
The 16th FC's **GDP contribution replaces tax effort**.
15th FC demographic performance used **change in TFR**.

nd60b210abbf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sixteenth Finance Commission (2026–31) devolution criteria?
o: Income distance has a weight of 42.5%
Tax and fiscal effort has been retained with a weight of 2.5%
Contribution to GDP has been introduced with a weight of 10%
nd60b210abbf.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission dropped the 2.5% tax and fiscal effort criterion.
xa: Area and forest each carry **10** under the 16th FC; demographic performance **10**.
16th FC award period: **1 Apr 2026 – 31 Mar 2031**.
The GDP criterion **helped AP's share** rise to **4.217%**.

n471497412cd.s: Which new criterion of the 16th Finance Commission, carrying 10% weight, helped Andhra Pradesh's share?
n471497412cd.x: The new contribution-to-GDP criterion carried a 10% weight and helped Andhra Pradesh's share by recognising its economic contribution.
xa: AP's share rose to **4.217%** from **4.05%**; Karnataka **4.131%**, TN **4.097%**.
Formula: **square root of State GSDP** over the sum of square roots.
⚠ **Prosperity paradox**: AP's above-average PCI hurts it under income distance.

nbe1db2c3ede.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a change introduced by the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: Demographic performance was measured by total fertility rate alone.
Income distance was calculated from the average of the three largest States.
Forest cover excluded open forests from consideration.
Tax and fiscal effort replaced contribution to GDP.
nbe1db2c3ede.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission calculated income distance from the average of the top three large States. Its demographic-performance measure was population growth from 1971 to 2011; forest included open forests; and contribution to GDP replaced tax effort.
nbe1db2c3ede.tq: Discriminate between closely related criteria by matching each change with the correct Commission.
xs: The **16th FC** measured **income distance** from the **average of the top three large States'** per capita GSDP — option **(2)**.
Others are wrong: demographic performance = **population growth 1971-2011** (not TFR); forest **includes open forests**; **GDP contribution replaced tax effort**, not the reverse.
xa: 16th FC weights: income distance **42.5**, population 2011 **17.5**, area **10**, forest **10**, demographic performance **10**, GDP **10**.
Forest also counts the **increase in forest area (2015-2023)**.
GDP criterion = **square root of State GSDP** over the sum of square roots.

n987ccff8a91.s: Andhra Pradesh's 'prosperity paradox' in tax devolution arises under which criterion?
n987ccff8a91.x: Income distance gives greater weight to States with lower per capita GSDP, so Andhra Pradesh's above-average per capita income works against it.
xa: The 16th FC measures income distance from the **average of the top three large States**.
The new **GDP-contribution** criterion helped AP's share rise.
AP's 16th FC share: **4.217%**; tax share in **AP Budget 2026-27**: **4.22%**.

n58292e62629.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated feature of the Sixteenth Finance Commission grants-in-aid framework?
o: Limitation of grants-in-aid to local bodies and disaster management
An overall grants-in-aid figure of ₹9.47 lakh crore for the specified categories
Continuation of revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants
n58292e62629.x: Under the stated Sixteenth Finance Commission framework, revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants were dropped. Grants-in-aid were limited to local bodies and disaster management, with total grants-in-aid of ₹9.47 lakh crore.
n58292e62629.tq: Spot the reversed policy change: the discontinued grant categories are presented as if they continued.
xs: **Continuation of revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants** is NOT a feature — the 16th FC **dropped** them — option **(4)**.
Its grants-in-aid total **₹9.47 lakh crore**, limited to **local bodies + disaster management**, with **basic and performance-linked** components.
xa: Grants-in-aid share fell from **19.4% to 8.3%** of FC transfers.
Criticism: "**tyranny of the base year**" after RDGs ended.
Local bodies get **₹7.91 lakh crore**; urban share raised to **45%**.

n79d14c5a324.s: Which change is associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission award for 2026–31?
o: GDP criterion added; revenue-deficit grants continued
Tax-effort criterion added; revenue-deficit grants dropped
GDP criterion added; revenue-deficit grants dropped
GDP criterion dropped; revenue-deficit grants doubled
n79d14c5a324.x: The 2026–31 award adds a GDP criterion and drops revenue-deficit grants.
xa: GDP contribution (weight **10**) **replaces tax effort**.
Grants-in-aid of **₹9.47 lakh crore** are limited to **local bodies + disaster management**.
16th FC chair: **Dr Arvind Panagariya**.

n624746ac406.s: Under the Fourteenth Finance Commission, the basic-to-performance grant ratio for Gram Panchayats was:
n624746ac406.x: The Fourteenth FC used 90:10 for Gram Panchayats and 80:20 for Municipalities.
xa: ⚠ PYQ trap: do **not mix** the 90:10 and 80:20 ratios.
14th FC panchayat total: **Rs 2,00,292 crore**; overall **Rs 2,87,436 crore**.

nb2addba0a6f.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Fifteenth Finance Commission provision for rural local bodies during 2021–26?
o: ₹2.36 lakh crore, with tied and untied components in a 60:40 ratio for rural bodies
₹4.40 lakh crore, with the urban share fixed at 45 per cent
₹2.00 lakh crore, with no conditions relating to accounts or property tax
nb2addba0a6f.x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission provided ₹2.36 lakh crore for rural local bodies, with tied and untied components in a 60:40 ratio. Performance-linked conditions included audited accounts and property-tax floor rates.
nb2addba0a6f.tq: Match the Commission period with its amount and distinguish its tied-untied structure from the Fourteenth and Sixteenth Commissions.
xs: The **15th FC** (**2021-26**) gave rural local bodies **₹2.36 lakh crore**, with **tied and untied** components in **60:40** — option **(2)**.
**₹1.18 lakh crore** was the 14th FC comparison figure; **45% urban share** belongs to the **16th FC**.
xa: Part of the tied grant goes to **drinking water and sanitation**.
Performance conditions: **audited accounts** and **property-tax floor rates**.
Urban LBs got roughly **Rs 1.2-1.3 lakh crore**.

n671a48f2d83.s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission (2026-31), local body grants of about ₹7.91 lakh crore were recommended. What share of these grants goes to urban local bodies?
n671a48f2d83.x: The 16th FC raised the urban share of local body grants to 45% (about ₹3.6 lakh crore urban against about ₹4.4 lakh crore rural). 36% was the earlier urban share, 41% is the States' share of the divisible pool, and 60 per cent is not the urban share.
n671a48f2d83.tq: 16th FC: ₹7.91 lakh crore to local bodies, urban share 45%.
xs: The 16th FC raised the **urban share** of local body grants to **about 45 per cent** — option **(3)**.
Of **₹7.91 lakh crore**: rural about **Rs 4.4 lakh crore**, urban about **Rs 3.6 lakh crore**.
**41%** is the **States' share** of the divisible pool, not the urban share.
xa: Some notes give urban as **~Rs 3.56 lakh crore**.
**Revenue-deficit grants** were discontinued.
AP: **₹28,785 crore** local body grants over **2026-31**.

n662140df410.s: The Fourteenth Finance Commission recommended vertical devolution of ____ of the divisible pool to the States.
n662140df410.x: The Fourteenth FC recommended 42 per cent; the Fifteenth and Sixteenth recommended 41 per cent.
xa: Chairs: **14th Y.V. Reddy**, **15th N.K. Singh**, **16th Dr Arvind Panagariya**.
**18 states** had sought **50%**.

n0dbbe237ee9.s: The Fifteenth Finance Commission assigned the highest weight among the following to which criterion?
n0dbbe237ee9.x: Income distance received the highest weight under the Fifteenth Finance Commission, at 45 per cent. Demographic performance, forest and ecology, and Population (2011) received 12.5 per cent, 10 per cent and 15 per cent respectively.
n0dbbe237ee9.tq: Compare the principal weight with the three moderately weighted criteria.
xs: **Income distance** got the highest weight under the 15th FC, at **45** — option **(1)**.
Others: **population 2011 – 15**, **demographic performance – 12.5**, **forest and ecology – 10**.
xa: Income distance was the highest weight in **every FC** (16th: **42.5**).
15th FC also used **area 15** and **tax and fiscal effort 2.5**.
15th FC chair: **N.K. Singh**; vertical share **41%**.

naa272ca523c.s: The Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program is a component of the:
naa272ca523c.x: The Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program and Training of Trainers on own-source revenue are associated with the revamped RGSA.
xa: RGSA trained **35 lakh+** participants in **FY25**.
**AMRUT 2.0 (2021)** rewards **property-tax reform** and **municipal bonds**.
**SVAMITVA** drone maps create a **rural property-tax baseline**.

n4c2ccbad8f9.s: Which one of the following best describes the standard condition of 3F devolution in practice?
o: Staff are answerable to local bodies, while functions and funds are retained by the Union.
Functions, funds and functionaries are fully transferred to local bodies in an untied form.
Funds are untied, but functions remain exclusively with State departments.
Functions are devolved on paper, funds arrive tied to schemes, and staff report to State line departments.
