n4c2ccbad8f9.x: The standard finding is that functions exist on paper, funds are commonly tied to schemes, and functionaries continue to report to State line departments.
n4c2ccbad8f9.tq: Compare the formal position with the operational reality across all three Fs.
xs: In practice, **functions are devolved on paper**, **funds arrive tied to schemes**, and **staff report to State line departments** — option **(4)**.
The ideal — **untied** funds and staff answerable to the local body — is what is missing, so option (2) is wrong.
xa: Result: PRIs are **reduced to implementing agencies**.
ULBs **depend on tied grants**; own revenue only **~0.3% of GDP**.
**Roadmap for Panchayati Raj** lists weak 3F devolution, **bureaucratic control**, **tied funds**, **dependence on grants**, **reluctance to tax**.

n7e06744a694.s: The constitutional planning bodies intended to integrate plans at the district and metropolitan levels are, respectively:
o: DPC under Article 243ZD and MPC under Article 243ZE
MPC under Article 243ZD and DPC under Article 243ZE
DPC under Article 243G and MPC under Article 243W
DPC under Article 280 and MPC under Article 281
n7e06744a694.x: The District Planning Committee is provided under Article 243ZD, while the Metropolitan Planning Committee is provided under Article 243ZE.
n7e06744a694.tq: Match the planning body, territorial level and Article number in sequence.
xs: **DPC under Article 243ZD** (district) and **MPC under Article 243ZE** (metropolitan) — option **(1)** is correct; both exist for **integration of plans**.
Option 2 swaps them; **243G/243W** cover devolution of functions, not planning committees.
xa: **243K / 243ZA**: **SEC** for panchayats / municipalities.
**243E/243U**: **5-year term**; elections within **6 months** of dissolution.
**243D**: women's reservation floor of **one-third**.

n6542f0e53cd.s: Article 243D sets a constitutional floor for the reservation of seats for women in Panchayats. Andhra Pradesh, like many other States, reserves:
n6542f0e53cd.x: Article 243D guarantees at least one-third of seats for women, but many States, Andhra Pradesh included, give 50%. One-third is only the constitutional minimum; 40% and 25% are not the AP figure.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** reserves **50 per cent of the seats** for women — option **(3)**.
**One-third** is only the constitutional floor under **Art. 243D**; many States give **50%**.
xa: Proxy problem: "**sarpanch pati**"; it **falls markedly in a second term**.
AP Cabinet (**18 Aug 2026**): **34%** BC reservation rural, **33⅓%** urban.

n5ccbf6e8fee.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about constitutional devolution to local bodies?
o: The Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules transfer subjects automatically without legislative action
These Articles say the State Legislature 'may' devolve powers and responsibilities
n5ccbf6e8fee.x: The Schedules do not transfer subjects automatically; Articles 243G and 243W use the discretionary 'may'.
xa: Likewise **243H/243X** (taxing powers) use "**may**".
This discretion is the **root cause** of weak devolution.
**DPC (243ZD)** and **MPC (243ZE)** are meant to **integrate plans**.

nf910dc18ae4.s: Which one of the following is the single most important source of own revenue for Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)?
nf910dc18ae4.x: Property tax is the main own-source revenue of ULBs, although it remains under-assessed and under-collected.
nf910dc18ae4.tq: Directly identify the principal own-source revenue item.
xs: **Property tax** is the **single most important own revenue** of ULBs — option **(3)**.
It is **under-assessed** and **under-collected**, and property registers are **outdated**.
xa: ULB own revenue is only **~0.3% of GDP**.
**GST** cost ULBs ~**19%** of own revenue (**octroi**, **entry tax**).
**SVAMITVA** gives a **property-tax baseline** for rural homes.

nafd95413a0d.s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission grants for 2026–31, the urban share increased from 36% to:
nafd95413a0d.x: The urban share rises to 45%, with grants split 80% basic and 20% performance.
xa: 16th FC (**2026-31**): rural **₹4.4 lakh crore**, urban **₹3.6 lakh crore** (~**₹75,000 crore** a year).
15th FC urban: about **₹1.2-1.3 lakh crore** (about **0.12-0.13%** of GDP).
Grant conditions: **properly constituted** LBs, **audited accounts**, **timely SFCs**.

nc6db5c3f6dd.s: In debates on local devolution, Janmabhoomi committees and secretariats are criticised as:
o: Constitutional planning bodies integrating local plans
Parallel bodies weakening the centrality of PRIs
nc6db5c3f6dd.x: The criticism is that PRIs act mainly as implementing agencies, while parallel bodies such as Janmabhoomi committees and secretariats reduce their centrality.
xa: Other parallel bodies: **DRDAs**, **SHGs**, **MPLADS/MLA LADS**, **parastatals/SPVs**.
**DPC (243ZD)** and **MPC (243ZE)** are meant for **integration of plans**.

nf3a90d65bb0.s: Village and ward secretariats and volunteers were introduced in Andhra Pradesh in:
nf3a90d65bb0.x: They were introduced in 2019, after the Janmabhoomi committees of 2014-19; both were criticised as parallel to gram panchayats and wards.
xa: When terms lapse, AP local bodies are run by **Special Officers**.
AP gives **50%** women's reservation (Art. **243D** floor is **one-third**).
AP was showing a **local-body poll push** with **direct Mayor elections**.

n82bc522749a.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated condition associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission’s local-body grants?
o: Timely constitution of State Finance Commissions
Permanent appointment of Special Officers in place of elected bodies
n82bc522749a.x: The conditions include properly constituted local bodies, published audited accounts and timely State Finance Commissions. Permanent replacement of elected bodies by Special Officers is not a condition.
n82bc522749a.tq: Find the institutional arrangement that contradicts the grant conditions.
xs: **Permanent Special Officers** is NOT a condition — option **(4)**; the 16th FC wants **properly constituted** (elected) bodies.
The conditions are: **properly constituted local bodies**, **audited accounts published**, **timely SFCs**.
xa: Problem: **SFC reports** are often **ignored**.
This is why AP is **rushing polls** — **₹12,150 crore** at stake.
16th FC: **80% basic / 20% performance**; urban share **45%**.

n017a85fc267.s: Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), begun in 2018-19, strengthens Panchayati Raj Institutions mainly for achieving:
n017a85fc267.x: RGSA aims to strengthen PRIs so that they can contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals.
xa: Focus on **117 aspirational districts** + convergence with **Mission Antyodaya**.
**Revamped RGSA: 1 April 2022 – 31 March 2026**, co-terminus with the **XV FC**.
**BRGF** was merged into RGSA (APPSC-GS **2018**).

n520836f08f1.s: The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet decision of 18 August 2026 provided ____ reservation for Backward Classes in rural local bodies.
n520836f08f1.x: It provided 34% BC reservation in rural local bodies and 33⅓% in urban local bodies, with direct election of Mayors and chairpersons.
xa: ⚠ BC reservation **34%** rural vs **33⅓%** urban — do not swap.
AP **Mandal and Zilla Parishads** were due by **23 Sep 2026**.
AP gives **50%** reservation for women.

nf1fa9f42cae.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about proxy representation of elected women in Panchayats?
o: 'Sarpanch pati' refers to a male relative exercising power in the elected woman's name
Proxy behaviour falls markedly in a second term
Online trolling and intimidation are other problems faced by women leaders
Proxy behaviour increases markedly when the woman enters a second term
nf1fa9f42cae.x: Proxy behaviour falls markedly, not increases, when the woman representative enters a second term.
xa: Responses: **capacity building**, **Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan**, **Model Women-Friendly GPs**.
**Sushil Kumar** committee (report **2025**) recommended **exemplary penalties** in proven proxy cases.

n29ccdf45af9.s: Which measure is identified as a response to proxy participation by male relatives in women-led Panchayats?
o: Conducting Panchayat meetings without elected representatives
Appointing Special Officers to run Panchayats
Exemplary penalties in proven proxy cases
n29ccdf45af9.x: Capacity building of elected women and exemplary penalties in proven proxy cases were identified as responses.
xa: The penalties came from the **MoPR advisory committee** chaired by **Sushil Kumar** (report **2025**).
Proxy behaviour **falls markedly in a second term**.
Other responses: **Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan**, **Model Women-Friendly GPs**.

n9d17d16f0b8.s: The Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan is aimed at:
o: Strengthening participation of elected women representatives
n9d17d16f0b8.x: Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan and Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats strengthen participation of elected women representatives.
xa: **Capacity building** is the third response listed.
Constitutional floor **one-third** (**243D**); AP gives **50%**.

n76d2d445e13.s: Which programme was merged into the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan?
n76d2d445e13.x: The Backward Regions Grant Fund (BRGF) was merged into RGSA (APPSC-GS 2018). RGSA converges with Mission Antyodaya rather than absorbing it; SVAMITVA and MPLADS are separate schemes.
n76d2d445e13.tq: Use the programme-merger relationship to distinguish RGSA from associated initiatives.
xs: The **Backward Regions Grant Fund (BRGF)** was **merged into RGSA** — option **(2)** (APPSC-GS **2018**).
RGSA only **converges with Mission Antyodaya**; **SVAMITVA** and **MPLADS** are separate.
xa: RGSA covers **non-Part IX** areas too.
Focus on **117 aspirational districts**.

nd7c6a048a4c.s: The funding pattern under RGSA is correctly represented by which one of the following?
o: Centre:State is 40:60, with 90:10 for Union Territories
Centre:State is 75:25, with no separate pattern for Union Territories
Centre:State is 60:40, 90:10 for North-Eastern and hilly States, and 100% Central funding for Union Territories
nd7c6a048a4c.x: The normal Centre-State ratio is 60:40; it is 90:10 for North-Eastern and hilly States, while Union Territories receive 100% Central funding.
nd7c6a048a4c.tq: Separate the normal ratio from the special ratios for difficult terrain and Union Territories.
xs: RGSA funding: **Centre:State 60:40** for general States, **90:10 for North-Eastern and hilly States**, **100% Central** for **Union Territories** — option **(4)** is correct.
The other options give ratios (50:50, 40:60, 75:25) that are not the RGSA pattern.
xa: RGSA aims to strengthen **PRIs** to achieve the **SDGs**.
Revamped RGSA runs **1 April 2022 – 31 March 2026**, co-terminus with the **XV Finance Commission**.
FY25: **35 lakh+** trained; **Training of Trainers** on **own-source revenue**.

nb0b089a86d9.s: The revamped RGSA is co-terminus with which period?
o: The Fifteenth Finance Commission period, from 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026
The Fourteenth Finance Commission period, from 2015 to 2020
The Sixteenth Finance Commission period, from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2027
The Fifteenth Finance Commission period, from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2026
nb0b089a86d9.x: The revamped RGSA runs from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2026 and matches the period of the Fifteenth Finance Commission. The 1 April 2021 starting date is incorrect.
nb0b089a86d9.tq: Discriminate between the close starting dates 1 April 2021 and 1 April 2022.
xs: The **revamped RGSA** runs **1 April 2022 – 31 March 2026**, co-terminus with the **Fifteenth Finance Commission** — option **(4)**.
⚠ "**1 April 2021** to 31 March 2026" (option 1) is the known wrong date (UPSC **2026** trap).
xa: Phase 1 of RGSA launched **2018-19**.
**BRGF** was merged into RGSA.

ne1ca7836e9f.s: Which one of the following correctly describes eGramSwaraj?
o: It provides only online auditing of Panchayat accounts.
It executes works recommended under MPLADS.
It combines Panchayat planning, accounting and reporting.
It prepares property records for rural homes.
ne1ca7836e9f.x: eGramSwaraj integrates Panchayat planning, accounting and reporting. Online auditing is the specific function of AuditOnline, while property records are associated with SVAMITVA.
ne1ca7836e9f.tq: Distinguish the complementary digital platforms by their precise functions.
xs: **eGramSwaraj** integrates panchayat **planning, accounting and reporting** — option **(3)**.
**Online audit** is **AuditOnline**; property records come from **SVAMITVA**.
xa: eGramSwaraj was launched with SVAMITVA on **24 April 2020**.
**SVAMITVA** is implemented by the **Survey of India**.

ndd2d72c26d9.s: A major concern about State Finance Commission reports is that they are:
o: Prepared by the Union Finance Commission
ndd2d72c26d9.x: State Finance Commission reports are often ignored, which weakens fiscal devolution to local bodies.
xa: Other conditions: **properly constituted** local bodies and **published audited accounts**.
The SEC (not the SFC) conducts local polls, **appointed by the Governor**.

n47b65bf2779.s: The recommendation to establish a Local Body Ombudsman was made by the:
o: First Administrative Reforms Commission in its Sixth Report
Second Finance Commission in its Local Finance Report
Second Administrative Reforms Commission in its Sixth Report
n47b65bf2779.x: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended a Local Body Ombudsman in its Sixth Report, titled Local Governance, published in 2007.
n47b65bf2779.tq: Discriminate between the First and Second ARC, a standard institutional trap.
xs: The **Local Body Ombudsman** was recommended by the **Second Administrative Reforms Commission**, **6th Report "Local Governance"** (**2007**) — option **(4)**.
⚠ The **UKPSC 2012** key marked the **First ARC**; the standard answer is the **Second ARC**.
The **V. Ramachandran** Committee (**2013**) dealt with delivery of public goods through panchayats.
xa: **Sushil Kumar** committee (report **2025**): ending **proxy participation**.
**Devolution Index** report: **Ministry of Panchayati Raj** with **IIPA**.

n822ed8fb56a.s: The report titled “Status of Devolution to Panchayats in States” is published by the:
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, prepared with the National Institute of Urban Affairs
Ministry of Panchayati Raj, prepared with IIPA
Ministry of Rural Development, prepared with NIRDPR
Ministry of Finance, prepared with the Finance Commission
n822ed8fb56a.x: The Devolution Index report is published by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj and is prepared with the Indian Institute of Public Administration.
n822ed8fb56a.tq: Identify the publishing ministry and distinguish it from related rural-development institutions.
xs: "**Status of Devolution to Panchayats in States**" (Devolution Index) is published by the **Ministry of Panchayati Raj**, **prepared with IIPA** — option **(2)** is correct.
**NIRDPR** (Hyderabad) is the national **training** institute, not the publisher.
xa: Devolution concerns the **3Fs** — **functions, funds, functionaries**.
Root cause of weak devolution: Art. **243G/243W** say the State "**may**" devolve.
**Eleventh Schedule**: **29** subjects; **Twelfth Schedule**: **18**.

n5c42066acdd.s: Article 324, which provides for the Election Commission of India, lies in Part ____ of the Constitution.
xa: The ECI was **set up on 25 January 1950**; its seat is **Nirvachan Sadan, New Delhi**.
Its training arm is **IIIDEM**, New Delhi.
**25 January** is also **National Voters' Day**, observed since **2011**.

n91ad708832f.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners?
o: The CEC and the ECs have equal powers and differences are settled by majority
The CEC has a permanent veto over the decisions of the ECs
The CEC alone takes all substantive decisions of the Commission
The ECs can overrule the CEC only with the President's approval
n91ad708832f.x: The CEC and the other Election Commissioners have equal powers, and differences are resolved by majority decision.
n91ad708832f.tq: Discriminate between the chairing role of the CEC and unequal voting power.
xs: **The CEC and the ECs have equal powers** and **differences are settled by majority** — option **(1)** is correct.
So the CEC has no veto and cannot decide alone; the CEC only **presides**.
xa: **T.N. Seshan v Union of India (1995)** upheld the **multi-member body + majority rule**.
Salaries: **CEC and ECs equal**, on a par with a **Supreme Court judge**.
⚠ But removal differs: CEC like an **SC judge**; ECs only on the **CEC's recommendation**.

n543c2596969.s: The CEC and Election Commissioners receive equal salaries on a par with:
o: a judge of a High Court
a judge of the Supreme Court
n543c2596969.x: They are paid on a par with a Supreme Court judge, and their service conditions cannot be varied to their disadvantage.
xa: Tenure: **6 years or 65**; **no reappointment** under the 2023 Act.
**CEC and ECs have equal powers**; differences settled by **majority**.

nabf2e8c7053.s: Under Article 324(1), the ECI's superintendence does NOT extend to elections to:
nabf2e8c7053.x: Article 324(1) covers Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President; Panchayat and municipal polls come under the State Election Commissions.
xa: ECI does not conduct the elections of **Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Deputy Chairman** — the House elects them.
**Art. 71**: President/VP election disputes go to the **Supreme Court**.
The **State Election Commissioner** is appointed by the **Governor**.

na6c9837451c.s: The Model Code of Conduct rests on which provision, and applies from when?
o: Article 324; from the announcement of the election schedule
Article 324; from the start of polling
Representation of the People Act, 1951; from the announcement of the schedule
Representation of the People Act, 1951; from the declaration of results
na6c9837451c.x: The MCC is not a statute; it rests on Article 324 and applies from the announcement of the election schedule (Harbans Singh Jalal, 1997).
xa: The start date comes from **Harbans Singh Jalal (1997)**.
**T.N. Seshan** enforced the MCC strictly in **1991**.
A petition said the PM's broadcast during Assembly polls violated **Part VII of the MCC** (conduct of the party in power).

n73532628ae2.s: The 2022 delimitation of Jammu and Kashmir was conducted by a Commission headed by Justice:
n73532628ae2.x: The J&K delimitation (2022) was done by a Commission under Justice Ranjana Desai, while Assam was delimited by the ECI.
xa: The ECI decides constituencies under the **Delimitation Commission Act**.
**Art. 329(a)**: delimitation laws cannot be questioned in court.

nf3725943f85.s: Which body decides every step of the election process, from the announcement of the schedule to the declaration of results?
nf3725943f85.x: The ECI decides every step from announcement to results; Panchayat and municipal polls belong to the State Election Commissions.
xa: It can **cancel polls** for rigging or booth capturing.
It **recognises parties** and **allots symbols**.

n8bb45ed2a59.s: National Voters' Day, observed since 2011, falls every year on:
n8bb45ed2a59.x: National Voters' Day is 25 January, the ECI's foundation day (25 January 1950).
xa: **V.S. Ramadevi** (**1990**) was the first and only woman CEC.
**T.N. Seshan** was the **10th CEC** (**1990-96**); he enforced the MCC strictly in **1991**.
The opposition's removal motion against **Gyanesh Kumar** is the first against a CEC appointed under the **2023 Act**.

n752c7ae678e.s: There is a demand that the expenses of the Election Commission of India be charged on the:
n752c7ae678e.x: Critics note the ECI's dependence on DoPT, Law and Home Ministries and demand its expenses be charged on the Consolidated Fund.
xa: Listed flaws: the Constitution prescribes **no qualifications** and **no term** for members.
**Salary equal to a Supreme Court judge**; service conditions cannot be varied to their disadvantage.

n68ccff7b654.s: Two Election Commissioners were added in 1989 after which Amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18?
n68ccff7b654.x: The 61st Amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18, after which two Election Commissioners were added in 1989.
xa: **Jan 1990**: EC posts abolished; single-member again.
**Oct 1993 onwards**: multi-member (**CEC + 2 ECs**), decisions by majority.
From **1950** to **Oct 1989**, the ECI was a **single-member** body (CEC only).

nd753e0154fc.s: V.S. Ramadevi, the first woman Chief Election Commissioner of India, served in:
nd753e0154fc.x: V.S. Ramadevi served as CEC in 1990; T.N. Seshan was the tenth CEC.
xa: First CEC: **Sukumar Sen**.
Current CEC: **Gyanesh Kumar**, the **26th CEC**.

n53f9876a9c7.s: The reservoir of power under Article 324 may be used by the Election Commission primarily when:
o: A State Election Commission requests it in every case
No law holds the field on the matter concerned
A law already completely occupies the field
The President delegates legislative power to it
n53f9876a9c7.x: Article 324 operates as a reservoir where no law holds the field; it cannot ordinarily override an existing law governing the matter.
n53f9876a9c7.tq: Apply the condition attached to residual constitutional power.
xs: Art. 324's "**reservoir of power**" is usable only where **no law holds the field** — option **(2)** is correct.
This was held in **Mohinder Singh Gill v. CEC (1978)**; where a law occupies the field, the ECI must follow it.
xa: The **MCC is not a statute** — it rests on **Art. 324**.
**SIR** of rolls is ordered under **Art. 324** + **Section 21, RPA 1950**.
**T.N. Seshan v UoI (1995)** upheld the **multi-member** Commission.

nf35b5f5ca66.s: The constitutional validity of the multi-member Election Commission and the majority rule was upheld in which case?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner
ADR v. Election Commission of India
T.N. Seshan v. Union of India
nf35b5f5ca66.x: The Supreme Court upheld the multi-member structure and majority rule in T.N. Seshan v. Union of India (1995).
nf35b5f5ca66.tq: Use the case-name association to distinguish institutional-structure litigation from election-process cases.
xs: **T.N. Seshan v Union of India (1995)** upheld the **multi-member body + majority rule** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Mohinder Singh Gill (1978)** is the "**reservoir of power**" case, not this one.
xa: The ECI has been **multi-member since Oct 1993**.
**Anoop Baranwal (2023)**: interim panel of **PM + LoP + CJI**.
**Harbans Singh Jalal (1997)**: MCC applies from the day the schedule is announced.

ne69c4dc3ea2.s: In Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India (2023), the interim selection panel directed by the Constitution Bench consisted of:
o: Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India
Prime Minister, Law Minister and Chief Justice of India
President, Prime Minister and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India
ne69c4dc3ea2.x: Until Parliament enacted a law, the Constitution Bench directed selection by a panel comprising the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition or leader of the largest opposition party in the Lok Sabha, and the Chief Justice of India.
ne69c4dc3ea2.tq: Separate the interim judicial mechanism from the later statutory mechanism.
xs: **Anoop Baranwal (2023)**: **PM + Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha + CJI** — option **(1)** is correct.
This was a **Constitution Bench** order, to apply **until Parliament legislates**.
xa: Where there is no LoP, the **largest opposition party leader** sits.
⚠ The **2023 Act** replaced the **CJI** with a **Union Cabinet Minister**.
**May 2026**: SC said the CJI's place was **only temporary**, pending a law.

nc6c28762219.s: Which one of the following was the principal change made by the 2023 Act in relation to the interim mechanism in Anoop Baranwal?
o: The entire Selection Committee was replaced by the Search Committee.
The Prime Minister was replaced by the President.
The Leader of Opposition was replaced by the Law Minister.
The Chief Justice of India was replaced by a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
nc6c28762219.x: The 2023 Act replaced the Chief Justice of India on the selection panel with a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
nc6c28762219.tq: Discriminate between the CJI in the interim panel and the Cabinet Minister in the statutory panel.
xs: The 2023 Act replaced **the Chief Justice of India** with **a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister** — option **(4)** is correct.
The **PM** and the **LoP** stay on the panel.
xa: Criticism: the government now has a **2-1 majority**.
**Jaya Thakur v UoI (2024)** challenges the Act — **pending** as of May 2026.
SC (May 2026) questioned the lack of "**one absolutely neutral person**".

n16a6ceae621.s: The Election Commission recognises political parties and allots election symbols under the:
n16a6ceae621.x: Party recognition and symbol allotment are governed by the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968, issued under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 and Article 324.
n16a6ceae621.tq: Match a power with its exact legal instrument and year.
xs: Parties are recognised and symbols allotted under the **Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968** — option **(2)** is correct.
The Order was issued under the **RPA 1951** + **Art. 324**.
xa: The ECI settles **symbol and recognition disputes** like a court — a **quasi-judicial** function.
It **cannot review a result** and **does not try election petitions**.

necc3f676a93.s: The Search Committee for Election Commissioners under the 2023 Act is headed by the:
necc3f676a93.x: The Search Committee is headed by the Law Minister, has two Secretary-rank members and shortlists five names.
xa: The **Selection Committee** — **PM (chair)**, **LoP**, a **Union Cabinet Minister** — may pick names **outside the shortlist**.
The **President** appoints on the Selection Committee's recommendation.
The Act is **Act No. 49 of 2023**, replacing the **1991 Act**.

n8703fc8116d.s: The Tarkunde Committee on electoral reforms was set up by:
n8703fc8116d.x: Jayaprakash Narayan set up the Tarkunde Committee, which proposed a three-member Election Commission.
xa: **Anoop Baranwal (2023)** adopted the same **PM + LoP + CJI** panel as an interim measure.
The ECI became a **three-member** body from **Oct 1993**.

ne84a03eb682.s: The Election Commission advises the Governor on disqualification of members of State Legislatures under Article:
ne84a03eb682.x: The ECI advises the Governor under Article 192 and the President under Article 103; anti-defection cases go to the Speaker or Chairman.
xa: This is the ECI's **advisory** function.
⚠ Disqualification (Art. 103/192) → ECI advises; anti-defection → Speaker/Chairman.

n1761cb19f4f.s: At the district level, Returning and Presiding Officers are appointed by the:
n1761cb19f4f.x: Each State has a Chief Electoral Officer, while at district level the Collector/District Election Officer appoints Returning and Presiding Officers.
xa: The CEO is appointed by the **ECI** from **senior civil servants** of the state.
⚠ CEO appointment: APP says **by the CEC**; IYB says **by the Commission**.

n8f1f73d9db3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Chief Electoral Officer is removed like a High Court judge
The State Election Commission functions under Articles 243K and 243ZA
The Chief Electoral Officer functions under the Representation of the People Act, 1950
The State Election Commissioner is removable only like a High Court judge
n8f1f73d9db3.x: The Chief Electoral Officer is removed by the Election Commission; only the State Election Commissioner has High Court judge-like protection.
xa: The SEC is appointed by the **Governor**; the CEO by the **ECI**.
AP SEC: **Anil Chandra Punetha**, for local-body polls.

n45801048b27.s: The challenged composition of the Selection Committee under the 2023 Election Commission law gives the government a majority of:
n45801048b27.x: Petitions by ADR and Jaya Thakur challenge the 2:1 government majority; the Supreme Court said the CJI's place had been only temporary, pending a law.
xa: **Anoop Baranwal v Union of India** (**2023**): until Parliament legislates, **PM + LoP + CJI** choose the CEC and ECs.
The **2023 Act** (**Act No. 49 of 2023**) replaced the **CJI with a Union Cabinet Minister**.
A **Search Committee** headed by the **Law Minister** shortlists **5** names; the Selection Committee may pick from outside it.
**Jaya Thakur v Union of India** (**2024**) was still **pending** as of May 2026.

nindian-polity-25-20.s: Which of the following elections is NOT conducted by the Election Commission of India?
nindian-polity-25-20.x: Panchayat elections at all three tiers are conducted by the State Election Commission.
n: The Election Commission of India conducts elections to the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections to the Rajya Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections to State Legislative Assemblies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections to State Legislative Councils. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections for the President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections for the Vice-President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India does not conduct local body elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The State Election Commission conducts Panchayat elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The State Election Commission conducts Municipal elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections to the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections to State Legislative Assemblies and Councils. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections for the President and Vice-President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The State Election Commission conducts elections to Gram Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The State Election Commission conducts elections to Panchayat Samitis. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The State Election Commission conducts elections to Zilla Parishads. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xa: SEC basis: **Articles 243K and 243ZA**.
⚠ ECI also does **not** conduct elections of **Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Deputy Chairman** (chosen by the House itself).
SECs operate under the respective **State Panchayati** and **State Municipal** laws.

n3e10331c7fe.s: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office:
o: In the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge
In the same manner as a High Court judge
By the President on the advice of the Prime Minister
On the recommendation of the Union Law Minister
n3e10331c7fe.x: The CEC is removable like a Supreme Court judge; Election Commissioners and Regional Commissioners only on the CEC's recommendation.
xa: CEC grounds: **proven misbehaviour or incapacity**; **special majority** in both Houses.

n16495e47b08.s: A motion for removal of the Chief Election Commissioner must be supported by at least how many signatures when initiated in the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha, respectively?
n16495e47b08.x: The motion requires the signatures of at least 100 members in the Lok Sabha or 50 members in the Rajya Sabha.
n16495e47b08.tq: Keep the House-wise numerical requirements in their correct order.
xs: A CEC removal motion needs **100** Lok Sabha or **50** Rajya Sabha signatures — option **(1)** is correct.
This mirrors the procedure for a **Supreme Court judge**.
xa: Grounds: **proven misbehaviour or incapacity**; **special majority** in both Houses.
The Opposition's removal motion against **Gyanesh Kumar** was the first against a CEC appointed under the 2023 Act.
ECs are removed only **on the CEC's recommendation** (**Section 11** of the 2023 Act).

n5c715ac13fd.s: Which of the following does the Constitution NOT prescribe for members of the Election Commission?
o: Removal of the CEC in the manner of a Supreme Court judge
Superintendence of elections vested in the Commission
n5c715ac13fd.x: The Constitution prescribes no qualifications and no fixed term for members of the Election Commission.
xa: The **2023 Act** fills the gap: **Secretary to GoI** rank; **6 years or 65**.
Criticism: ECI depends on **DoPT, Law and Home Ministries**; no power over **inner-party democracy** or **party finances**.
Demand: charge its expenses on the **Consolidated Fund**.

nindian-polity-25-16.s: An Election Commissioner holds office for six years or until attaining the age of ____, whichever is earlier.
nindian-polity-25-16.x: The ECI has one CEC and two ECs, appointed by the President, each serving six years or until age 65.
n: The Election Commission of India consists of one Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The President of India appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners is six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xa: **CEC and ECs have equal powers**; differences settled by **majority**.
The **2023 Act** bars **reappointment**.
**Salary** equals that of a **Supreme Court judge**.

nindian-polity-25-18.s: The removal safeguard for the Chief Election Commissioner is provided under which provision of the Constitution?
nindian-polity-25-18.x: Article 324(5) protects the CEC: they can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge.
n: Article 324(5) provides the removal safeguard for the Chief Election Commissioner. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xs: The CEC's removal safeguard is in **Article 324(5)** — option **(3)** is correct.
The CEC is removed only in the **same manner** and on the **same grounds** as a **Supreme Court judge**.
**Art. 324(1)** vests **superintendence, direction and control** of elections; **243K/243ZA** concern **State Election Commissions**.
xa: Removal motion needs **100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha** signatures; **special majority** in both Houses.
Other ECs are removed by the **President** only **on the CEC's recommendation**.
⚠ CEC like an **SC judge**; SEC like an **HC judge**.

nindian-polity-25-21.s: The head of a State Election Commission can be removed only in the manner of a:
nindian-polity-25-21.x: A State Election Commissioner is removed like a High Court judge, while the CEC is removed like a Supreme Court judge.
n: The State Election Commission conducts elections to Municipalities. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The State Election Commission conducts elections to Municipal Corporations. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The head of the Election Commission of India is removed like a Supreme Court Judge. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The head of the State Election Commission is removed like a High Court Judge. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xa: **AP SEC:** **Anil Chandra Punetha**.
SEC head is appointed by the **Governor**; ECI members by the **President**.
President/VP election disputes go to the **Supreme Court** (**Art. 71**).

n98a78ed5080.s: Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls is ordered under:
o: Article 280 and Section 21 of the Delimitation Act, 2002
Article 324 and Section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950
Article 243K and Section 11 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
Article 326 and Section 62 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
n98a78ed5080.x: Special Intensive Revision is ordered under Article 324 and Section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
n98a78ed5080.tq: Match the electoral exercise with both its constitutional and statutory bases.
xs: **SIR** is ordered under **Article 324** and **Section 21 of the RPA 1950** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Art. 243K** is the **SEC** (local bodies), and **Art. 280** is unrelated to rolls.
xa: The ECI **prepares and revises electoral rolls**.
AP angle: **ASR district's 100% SIR digitalisation**.

n783fee3baee.s: An election petition on a Parliamentary or State Legislature election is tried by the ____, with appeal to the ____.
n783fee3baee.x: Such election petitions are tried by the High Court, and an appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
xa: ⚠ **President/VP** disputes go straight to the **Supreme Court** (**Art. 71**).
By convention, courts **do not interfere once the poll process begins**.

n692d7c3902a.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the election reforms of the T.N. Seshan era?
o: Transfer of election petitions from High Courts to the Election Commission
Strict enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct in 1991
Introduction of Electors Photo Identity Cards
n692d7c3902a.x: Election petitions were not transferred to the Election Commission; they are tried by the High Courts in the case of Parliamentary and State Legislature elections. The other three measures were associated with the Seshan era.
n692d7c3902a.tq: Find the institutional power wrongly transferred to the Election Commission.
xs: **Transfer of election petitions from High Courts to the Election Commission** was never a Seshan-era reform — so option **(1)** is the answer.
**Art. 329(b)** petitions are tried by the **High Court**, with appeal to the **Supreme Court**; the **ECI does not try election petitions**.
Seshan era: **strict MCC enforcement in 1991**, arrest of violators and **removal of partisan police officers**.
**Electors Photo Identity Cards** were also introduced in the Seshan era.
xa: **T.N. Seshan** was the **10th CEC** (**1990-96**), the reform-era CEC.
The **MCC is not a statute**; it rests on **Art. 324** and applies from the day the schedule is announced (**Harbans Singh Jalal, 1997**).
**T.N. Seshan v Union of India** (**1995**) upheld the **multi-member body** and majority rule.
⚠ **ECI cannot review a result**; it decides **party and symbol disputes** and advises on disqualification.

n941056bc010.s: The Opposition's removal motion against which Chief Election Commissioner was described as the first such motion against a CEC appointed under the 2023 Act?
n941056bc010.x: The removal motion was moved against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and was described as the first such motion against a CEC appointed under the 2023 Act.
n941056bc010.tq: Use the current-affairs association between the office-holder and the specific constitutional controversy.
xs: The removal motion was against CEC **Gyanesh Kumar** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He is the **26th CEC** and the first CEC appointed under the **2023 Act** to face such a motion.
**Anil Chandra Punetha** is the **AP SEC**; **Sukumar Sen** was the **first CEC**; **V.S. Ramadevi** the first woman CEC.
xa: **Removal of CEC:** only like a **Supreme Court judge**, on proven misbehaviour or incapacity, by special majority in both Houses.
The motion needs **100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha** signatures.
⚠ ECs are removed only **on the CEC's recommendation**; an SEC is removed like an **HC judge**.

n7685c768c75.s: Under first-past-the-post in Lok Sabha elections, a candidate wins by securing:
o: At least two-thirds of the valid votes
More than half of the valid votes
At least one-third of the valid votes
n7685c768c75.x: FPTP needs only a plurality in a single-member constituency, not a majority.
xa: FPTP (territorial, single-member) is used for the **Lok Sabha** and **Assemblies**.
PR was rejected for Lok Sabha as hard for voters and prone to **fragmentation and unstable** governments.
**Security deposit** is forfeited below **one-sixth** of valid votes.

n9119d5fdc21.s: Which type of revision rebuilds the electoral roll comprehensively?
n9119d5fdc21.x: A Special Intensive Revision rebuilds the electoral roll, whereas summary revision is conducted annually.
xa: **Bihar SIR** removed about **70 lakh names**.
Four qualifying dates: **1 January, 1 April, 1 July, 1 October**.

nindian-polity-60-33.s: The State Legislative Assembly is elected from which type of constituencies?
nindian-polity-60-33.x: Assembly members are directly elected from single-member territorial constituencies, by first-past-the-post.
n: The Legislative Assembly is elected from single-member territorial constituencies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The Legislative Assembly is directly elected by the people. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
xs: The Assembly is elected from **single-member territorial constituencies** — option **(4)**.
It is **directly elected** by citizens using **First-Past-the-Post**.
xa: It rests on **universal adult suffrage** — **Article 326**.
Conducted by the **Election Commission of India** (**Article 324**).
Assembly is under **Article 170**.

nindian-polity-66-27.s: NOTA is NOT applicable in which of the following elections?
nindian-polity-66-27.x: NOTA does not apply to Rajya Sabha or Legislative Council elections.
n: NOTA is an electoral option provided on ballot papers. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
NOTA is an electoral option provided on Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
NOTA enables voters to formally reject all contesting candidates in secret. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
NOTA is a symbolic expression only. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
NOTA does not determine the election outcome by itself. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
NOTA is not applicable in Rajya Sabha elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
NOTA is not applicable in Legislative Council elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
xa: NOTA came from **PUCL v. Union of India** (**2013**).
NOTA first Lok Sabha use: **2014** — **1.1%** of votes.
⚠ NOTA is not **abstention**.

nindian-polity-36-7.s: The Vice-President of India is elected by:
nindian-polity-36-7.x: The Vice-President is elected by all MPs, elected and nominated, by single transferable vote; the President by elected MPs and MLAs.
n: The President is elected through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
The Vice-President is elected through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
Citizens directly elect Lok Sabha members from territorial electoral rolls. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
The Lok Sabha uses the first-past-the-post system. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
Elected Members of the Legislative Assemblies of the respective States elect Rajya Sabha members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
The Rajya Sabha is elected indirectly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
The Rajya Sabha uses proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
The President is elected by elected Members of Parliament and elected Members of Legislative Assemblies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
The Vice-President is elected by all Members of Parliament, both elected and nominated. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
Elected Members of Parliament form part of the Presidential electoral college. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
Elected Members of State Legislative Assemblies form part of the Presidential electoral college. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
All Members of Parliament form the Vice-Presidential electoral college. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
Elected Members of Parliament form part of the Vice-Presidential electoral college. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
Nominated Members of Parliament form part of the Vice-Presidential electoral college. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
xa: Articles: President **54**; Vice-President **66**; Lok Sabha **81**; Rajya Sabha **80**.
Delhi and Puducherry MLAs join the presidential electoral college (**70th Constitutional Amendment Act**).
**Legislative Councils** also use PR-STV.

nindian-polity-36-36.s: The Vice-President is elected under Article:
nindian-polity-36-36.x: The Vice-President is elected under Article 66; the President under Article 54.
n: The President is elected under Article 54. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
The Vice-President is elected under Article 66. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
The Lok Sabha is constituted under Article 81. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
The Legislative Assembly is provided for under Article 170. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
The Legislative Council is provided for under Article 171. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
xa: **Rajya Sabha** = **Article 80**.
**Lok Sabha** and **Assembly** use **FPTP**; the rest use **PR-STV**.
Panchayat/municipal members: minimum age **21**.

n632b445cc98.s: Under Article 326, a citizen aged 18 or above may be disqualified from voting on grounds of:
o: Non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime or corrupt practice
n632b445cc98.x: Article 326 grants adult suffrage subject to disqualifications such as non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime and corrupt or illegal practice.
xa: Voting age was cut from **21 to 18** by the **61st Amendment Act, 1988**.
Right to vote is a **statutory right**, not a Fundamental Right.

n1ca9211269e.s: A candidate's security deposit is forfeited when the candidate secures less than:
n1ca9211269e.x: The security deposit is forfeited if the candidate obtains less than one-sixth of the valid votes.
n1ca9211269e.tq: Recall the exact fractional threshold and distinguish it from common one-fourth and one-third distractors.
xs: The **security deposit** is forfeited below **one-sixth** of valid votes — option **(2)**.
One-third, one-tenth and one-fourth are not the stated threshold.
xa: FPTP winner = candidate with the **most votes (plurality)**, not a majority.
**NOTA** has no electoral effect: even if NOTA leads, the **highest-scoring candidate** wins.

na35ee22756c.s: The constitutional principle underlying delimitation is best expressed as:
o: One State, one vote, one value
One district, one representative, one value
One party, one constituency, one value
One person, one vote, one value
na35ee22756c.x: Delimitation rests on the principle of ‘one person, one vote, one value’, associated with uniformity of representation under Article 81(2).
na35ee22756c.tq: Discriminate among similar-looking formulations of the electoral equality principle.
xs: Delimitation rests on **"one person, one vote, one value"** — option **(4)**.
It flows from **Art. 81(2)** uniformity of representation.
xa: Also phrased as **one citizen-one vote-one value** (UPSC; APPSC-G1 **2024**).
Readjustment after each census: **Art. 82** (Lok Sabha) and **Art. 170** (Assemblies).

n6136f19f4e3.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the qualifying dates for revision of electoral rolls?
n6136f19f4e3.x: The four qualifying dates are 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October. 1 December is not a qualifying date.
n6136f19f4e3.tq: Find the date outside the four-date set.
xs: **1 December** is not a qualifying date — option **(3)**.
The four dates: **1 January, 1 April, 1 July, 1 October** (Election Laws (Amendment) Act **2021**).
xa: **Summary revision** = annual; **SIR** rebuilds the roll.
Roll revision rests on **Sec. 21, RPA 1950**.

nd675e8fe33d.s: An overseas Indian elector may enrol in the electoral roll at:
o: the address of the Indian embassy in the foreign country
any address selected by the elector
the last place of employment in India only
the address of the Indian passport
nd675e8fe33d.x: Under Section 20A of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, an overseas elector may enrol at the address given in the Indian passport.
nd675e8fe33d.tq: Apply the special registration rule to the overseas-elector scenario.
xs: An overseas elector enrols at the **address of the Indian passport** — option **(4)**.
This is under **Sec. 20A, RPA 1950** (**2010**).
xa: RPA 1950 also covers **Sec. 19** voter eligibility and **Sec. 21** roll revision.
**Postal ballot** is for service voters, special voters, electors on election duty and those in preventive detention.

n40a422f21ab.s: The 'Sahulat' app, launched to facilitate voting, was associated with which of the following?
o: Jammu and Kashmir, for elderly voters
Sikkim, for Buddhist monks in the Sangha seat
n40a422f21ab.x: The Sahulat app was a Jammu and Kashmir initiative for elderly voters (APPSC 2019). Meghalaya was the first State to provide Braille-enabled ballot papers at all booths; overseas electors enrol under Sec 20A at their passport address; the Sangha seat in Sikkim is a floating constituency. None of these is the Sahulat app.
n40a422f21ab.tq: Sahulat = J&K elderly; Braille ballots = Meghalaya.
xs: The **Sahulat** app was for **elderly voters** in **Jammu and Kashmir** — option **(2)** (APPSC **2019**).
**Meghalaya** is linked to **Braille-enabled ballot papers**; **Sangha (Sikkim)** is the floating monks' seat.
xa: **Saksham** is the app for voters with disabilities.
**SVEEP** partnered **Indian Railways** (APPSC 2019).

nindian-polity-40-3.s: The constitutional authority for conducting State Legislative Assembly elections is the:
nindian-polity-40-3.x: Assembly elections are direct, use first-past-the-post and are run by the Election Commission of India.
n: Citizens directly elect the State Legislative Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
State Legislative Assembly elections are conducted on the basis of universal adult suffrage under Article 326. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
State Legislative Assembly elections use the First-Past-the-Post system. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections to the State Legislative Assembly under Article 324. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 104-108]
xa: ⚠ Assembly polls are run by the ECI, **not** the State Election Commission.
Members come from **single-member territorial constituencies**.
FPTP needs no absolute majority over **50 percent**.

nindian-polity-25-8.s: In the Kuldip Nayar case (2006), the Supreme Court held the right to vote to be a:
nindian-polity-25-8.x: Kuldip Nayar held the right to vote statutory, not fundamental.
n: Article 325 provides for a single general electoral roll. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Article 325 prohibits discrimination in electoral rolls on the basis of religion. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Article 325 prohibits discrimination in electoral rolls on the basis of race. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Article 325 prohibits discrimination in electoral rolls on the basis of caste. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Article 325 prohibits discrimination in electoral rolls on the basis of sex. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Article 326 provides universal adult suffrage for Lok Sabha elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Article 326 provides universal adult suffrage for Legislative Assembly elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Kuldip Nayar case described the right to vote as a legal or statutory right. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The right to vote is not a Fundamental Right. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xa: Every citizen aged **18+** may vote unless disqualified.
Voting age cut from **21** to **18** by the **61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988**.
President/VP disputes go **exclusively** to the **Supreme Court** (**Article 71**).

nindian-polity-25-33.s: Article 83, which may need amending for simultaneous elections, deals with the:
o: Duration of the Houses of Parliament
nindian-polity-25-33.x: Articles 83 and 85 concern Parliament's term and sessions, 172 and 174 the States', and 356 President's Rule; all may need amending.
n: Simultaneous elections may require amendment of Article 83. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Simultaneous elections may require amendment of Article 85. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Simultaneous elections may require amendment of Article 172. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Simultaneous elections may require amendment of Article 174. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Simultaneous elections may require amendment of Article 356. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xa: The first four general elections (**1951-52, 1957, 1962, 1967**) were **simultaneous** with Assembly polls.
**Bypolls** must be held within **6 months** of a vacancy.
Universal adult suffrage: **Article 326**.

nindian-polity-36-16.s: The voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 years by the:
nindian-polity-36-16.x: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 lowered the voting age to 18.
n: The voting age was lowered from 21 years to 18 years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988, lowered the voting age. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
The minimum age for membership of a Legislative Council is 30 years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
The minimum age for Panchayat and Municipality elections is 21 years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
xa: The change became effective in **1989** (some notes say 1987).
Right to vote is a **statutory right** (**Kuldip Nayar, 2006**).
**Article 326** = universal adult suffrage.

nindian-polity-66-8.s: Under the old Rule 49-O, a voter:
o: Entered the booth but refused to vote before the Presiding Officer
Voided the result by majority rejection
Pressed the NOTA button on the EVM
nindian-polity-66-8.x: Old Rule 49-O meant refusing to vote before the presiding officer; NOTA means pressing a button on the EVM.
n: A NOTA voter presses the NOTA button on the EVM. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
Under old Rule 49-O, an abstaining voter entered the polling booth. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
Under old Rule 49-O, an abstaining voter refused to vote before the Presiding Officer. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
Under the full international right to reject, voters reject all candidates. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
Under the full international right to reject, rejection is made via the ballot or EVM. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
xa: Rule 49-O was recorded in **Form 17-A** — secrecy **violated**; struck down as **ultra vires**.
NOTA **preserves** secrecy.
⚠ The **50%** re-election threshold is **not applicable** in India.

nindian-polity-66-10.s: A candidate forfeits the security deposit on securing not more than ____ of the valid votes.
nindian-polity-66-10.x: A candidate with one-sixth or less of the valid votes forfeits the deposit.
n: NOTA does not determine the election outcome by itself. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
Under NOTA, the candidate with the highest valid votes among the contestants is declared elected. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
Abstention under old Rule 49-O did not affect the winning tally. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
Under the international right to reject, re-election is mandated if rejection crosses a threshold of more than 50%. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
xa: ⚠ Trap: "election cancelled if NOTA gets the highest votes" is **false**.
NOTA applies only to **direct Lok Sabha** and **Assembly** elections.
**PUCL** judgment: **27 September 2013**.

nindian-polity-66-23.s: Former Rule 49-O was struck down because recording a voter's refusal to vote in Form ____ compromised secrecy.
nindian-polity-66-23.x: Recording the refusal in Form 17-A broke the secrecy of the vote.
n: Abstention under old Rule 49-O violated secrecy. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
Abstention under old Rule 49-O was recorded in Form 17-A. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
Old Rule 49-O was struck down as ultra vires. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
xa: Rule 49-O did **not affect** the **winning tally**.
**NOTA** replaced it with a **secret** button on the EVM.
**PUCL v. Union of India** — **27 September 2013**.

nindian-polity-36-18.s: Which additional areas are included in the Presidential electoral college through the 70th Constitutional Amendment Act?
o: Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
nindian-polity-36-18.x: The 70th Amendment (1992) added the elected MLAs of Delhi and Puducherry to the electoral college for the President.
n: Elected Members of the Delhi Legislative Assembly form part of the Presidential electoral college through the 70th Constitutional Amendment Act. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
Elected Members of the Puducherry Legislative Assembly form part of the Presidential electoral college through the 70th Constitutional Amendment Act. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
Elected Members of State Legislative Assemblies form part of the Presidential electoral college. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]
xs: The **70th Constitutional Amendment Act** added **Delhi and Puducherry** to the President's electoral college — option **(1)**.
Their **elected** MLAs vote with **elected** MPs and **elected** members of State Assemblies.
xa: President is elected under **Article 54** by **PR-STV**, **secret ballot**.
**Nominated** members do not vote for the President but do vote for the **Vice-President**.
Vice-President: **Article 66**.

ne2d7382b775.s: Elections to panchayats and municipalities in India are conducted by which body?
o: The Election Commission of India under Article 324
State Election Commissions under Articles 243K and 243ZA
The Chief Electoral Officer of the State under Article 325
ne2d7382b775.x: Panchayat and municipal polls are run by the State Election Commissions under Articles 243K (panchayats) and 243ZA (municipalities), not by the ECI. Article 324 vests control of Parliament, State legislature, President and VP elections in the ECI; Article 325 provides one general electoral roll; Article 329 bars courts in electoral matters. The CEO and Delimitation Commission do not conduct local polls.
xs: **State Election Commissions** under **Articles 243K and 243ZA** conduct **panchayat and municipal** polls — option **(2)**.
The **ECI** (Art. 324) does **not** run local polls; the **CEO** only assists the ECI in a State/UT.
The **Delimitation Commission** fixes seats and boundaries; it conducts no elections.
xa: **Article 325** = one general electoral roll; **Article 329** = bar on courts in electoral matters.
**Art. 243K** covers **panchayats**; **Art. 243ZA** covers **municipalities**.

n8801c761f9e.s: Under the Delimitation Act of 1972, the Delimitation Commission was constituted in:
n8801c761f9e.x: The Delimitation Acts were enacted in 1952, 1962, 1972 and 2002; the Commissions were constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002.
xa: There have been **four** Commissions so far.
Chairs: **1952** N. Chandrasekhara Aiyar; **1963** and **1973** J.L. Kapur; **2002** Kuldip Singh.
Readjustment is under **Art. 82** (Lok Sabha) and **Art. 170** (Assemblies) after each census.

n38f2118ecaa.s: The 84th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001 permitted rationalisation of constituencies on the basis of the ____ Census.
n38f2118ecaa.x: The 84th Amendment extended the freeze on inter-State seat allocation and allowed rationalisation using the 1991 Census.
xa: The original freeze: **42nd (1976)**, on the **1971 Census**, till **2000**.
Per-State Lok Sabha numbers unchanged since **1976**.

n882da9f9158.s: The present number of elected Lok Sabha seats, as distinguished from the constitutional ceiling mentioned, is:
n882da9f9158.x: The Lok Sabha has 543 elected seats against a ceiling of 550, comprising 530 seats for States and 20 for Union Territories in the stated allocation framework.
n882da9f9158.tq: Distinguish the existing elected strength from the maximum ceiling.
xs: The Lok Sabha has **543 elected seats** against a ceiling of **550** — option **(1)**.
The ceiling is **530** for States + **20** for UTs.
xa: ⚠ **Stale value**: "maximum 552 including 2 Anglo-Indians" — Anglo-Indian seats ended in **2020**.
**131st Amendment Bill, 2026** proposed raising the ceiling from **550 to 850** on the **2011 Census**; it was defeated.

nf983c037c26.s: Readjustment of State Legislative Assembly constituencies after each census is provided under:
nf983c037c26.x: Article 170 provides for readjustment of Assembly constituencies; Article 82 does so for the Lok Sabha and Article 81(2) embodies uniformity of representation.
xa: Principle: **"one person, one vote, one value"**.
Readjustment takes place **after each census** through a **Delimitation Commission** set up under an Act of Parliament.

n29794564d63.s: The freeze on the inter-State allocation of Lok Sabha seats on the basis of the 1971 Census was first imposed by which Amendment, and until when?
n29794564d63.x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) froze inter-State seat allocation on the 1971 Census till 2000 to encourage population control. The 84th Amendment (2001) extended the freeze till the first census after 2026, and the 87th (2003) switched boundary redrawing to the 2001 Census. The 44th Amendment did not deal with the freeze.
n29794564d63.tq: 42nd froze (1971 Census, till 2000); 84th extended (till 2026); 87th = 2001 Census boundaries.
xs: The **42nd Amendment, 1976** first froze allocation on the **1971 Census**, **till 2000** — option **(1)**.
The **84th (2001)** later extended it to the first census after **2026**; the **87th (2003)** switched boundaries to the **2001 Census**.
xa: Purpose of the freeze: **population control**.
**106th Amendment (2023)**: women's quota begins only after the next census (**2027 Census**) and delimitation.

n9163be7803c.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 proposed raising the Lok Sabha ceiling from 550 to:
n9163be7803c.x: The Bill proposed 850 seats with delimitation on the 2011 Census, but it was defeated.
xa: The Delimitation Bill 2026 was **withdrawn**.
EAC-PM (2026) suggested splitting **170** oversized seats to reach **824**.

n7eb91dd8d9b.s: The increase in Andhra Pradesh–Telangana seats under Section 26 awaits:
n7eb91dd8d9b.x: The seat increase under Section 26 awaits the census conducted after 2026.
xa: AP's reserved Lok Sabha seats: **4 SC, 1 ST**.
**84th (2001)** froze seats till the **first census after 2026**.

nindian-polity-53-23.s: Recognition of political parties and reservation of symbols is governed by the:
nindian-polity-53-23.x: The 1968 Order recognises parties and reserves symbols; the RPA 1950 covers seats and rolls, and the RPA 1951 nomination, scrutiny and counting.
n: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 provides the pre-election framework and deals with voter rolls. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides for the operational conduct of elections and candidature. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides nomination procedures. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides scrutiny procedures. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides counting procedures. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Representation of the People Act, 1950 provides for the preparation of electoral rolls. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Representation of the People Act, 1950 provides seat quotas. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Representation of the People Act, 1950 provides the delimitation framework. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with the actual conduct of elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
xa: The **87th Amendment (2003)** switched boundaries to the **2001 Census**.
**84th (2001)** extended the seat freeze to the first census after **2026**.

nindian-polity-53-29.s: The Delimitation Commission is headed by a:
nindian-polity-53-29.x: It is set up under an Act of Parliament, headed by a retired Supreme Court judge, with the CEC and State Election Commissioners as members.
n: The Delimitation Commission is constituted by the Central Government under an Act of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Delimitation Commission is headed by a retired Supreme Court Judge. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Chief Election Commissioner is a member of the Delimitation Commission. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
State Election Commissioners are members of the Delimitation Commission. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
xa: Basis: **Art. 82** (Lok Sabha) + **Art. 170** (Assemblies).
Orders **cannot be challenged in court** (**Article 329**).
**J&K** Commission: **Justice Ranjana Desai** (**2022**).

nindian-polity-53-43.s: Disqualifications for membership of Parliament are dealt with in Article:
nindian-polity-53-43.x: Article 102 covers disqualifications for Parliament; 84 its qualifications, 173 and 191 those for State Legislatures.
n: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 is connected with Articles 84, 102, 173, 191, 324, and 329 of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with the qualifications of candidates. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with the disqualifications of candidates. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
xa: All four are linked to the **RPA 1951**, along with **324** and **329**.
Disqualification on conviction: sentence of at least **two years**; lasts **six years** after release.
RPA 1951 **Sec. 8** lists disqualifications on conviction.

nc9063fecb4a.s: Which Article of the Constitution vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India?
nc9063fecb4a.x: Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India.
nc9063fecb4a.tq: Identify the constitutional provision from its distinctive power.
xs: **Article 324** vests the **superintendence, direction and control** of elections in the **ECI** — option **(3)**.
**Article 325** = one general electoral roll; **Article 327** = Parliament's power to make election laws; **Article 329** = bar on courts.
xa: SC in **Mohinder Singh Gill v CEC (1978)**: Art. 324 is a "**reservoir of power**" where Parliament has not legislated.
The **Model Code of Conduct** draws its authority from the ECI's **plenary power under Art. 324**.
ECI constituted in **1950** — a permanent independent constitutional body.

n179c12cb096.s: Election expense accounts are dealt with in which Sections of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
n179c12cb096.x: Sections 77–78 of the 1951 Act cover election expenses; Section 8 covers disqualifications.
xa: Expense accounts reach the **District Election Officer** within **30 days** (**Sec. 78**).
**Sec. 29A, RPA 1951** = registration of political parties.
**Sec. 126** bars opinion polls in the **48 hours** before close of poll; **Sec. 126A** governs exit polls.

n90789c4cecc.s: An election held after a legislature is dissolved before the expiry of its normal term is called a:
n90789c4cecc.x: A mid-term election follows premature dissolution; a by-election fills a single vacancy, ordinarily within six months.
xa: Bypoll exceptions: remaining term **under one year**, or ECI (consulting the Centre) certifies difficulty.
The first four general elections (**1951-52, 1957, 1962, 1967**) were **simultaneous** with Assembly polls.

n417d9aa690e.s: The Delimitation Commission is constituted under:
o: A notification of the Election Commission
A resolution of the Rajya Sabha
An executive order of the President
n417d9aa690e.x: It is constituted under parliamentary legislation, works with the ECI, and its orders cannot be modified by the Lok Sabha or Assemblies.
xa: Its orders also **cannot be challenged in court**.

n584fd7ea925.s: Reservation of one-third of seats for women, under the 106th Amendment, is linked to Article:
n584fd7ea925.x: Article 334A relates to the women's one-third reservation; Article 330 covers SC/ST seats in the Lok Sabha and 331 the former Anglo-Indian nomination.
xa: ⚠ **330 / 332** = SC/ST seats; **331 / 333** = Anglo-Indians (ended).
**Art. 334** originally set **10 years** (till **1960**), repeatedly extended.

n16eb65cf256.s: Which Lok Sabha constituency in Andhra Pradesh is reserved for Scheduled Tribes?
n16eb65cf256.x: Araku is the ST-reserved constituency; Amalapuram and Tirupati are SC-reserved.
xa: AP's **4** SC seats: **Amalapuram, Bapatla, Chittoor, Tirupati**.
⚠ **AP** = 4 SC + 1 ST; **Telangana** = 3 SC + 2 ST (**Adilabad, Mahabubabad** ST).

n96fea97b16a.s: In a constituency reserved for Scheduled Castes, who can vote?
o: Only voters belonging to Scheduled Castes
Only voters belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
Only voters belonging to Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes
n96fea97b16a.x: Reserved constituencies have a common electorate: all voters, not merely those of the reserved community, may vote.
xa: AP has **4** SC + **1** ST Lok Sabha seats; Telangana **3** SC + **2** ST.
SC/ST reservation runs to **2030** (**104th Amendment**).

n845ce618199.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about women's reservation under the 106th Amendment?
o: It provides one-third reservation of seats
It operates immediately, irrespective of census and delimitation
n845ce618199.x: Its operation begins only after the next census and delimitation.
xa: Tamil Nadu's resolution sought the women's quota from **2029** without linking it to delimitation.
SC/ST reservation is under **Arts. 330 / 332**, extended to **2030**.

n2f91d4c5244.s: The number of Scheduled Caste-reserved seats in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly is:
n2f91d4c5244.x: Andhra Pradesh has 29 SC and 7 ST Assembly seats; Telangana has 19 SC and 12 ST.
xa: AP's ST Lok Sabha seat: **Araku**; Telangana's: **Adilabad, Mahabubabad**.
Telangana's SC Lok Sabha seats: **Peddapalle, Warangal, Nagarkurnool**.

nd626580c72a.s: Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies under Article 334 has been extended up to 2030 by which Amendment?
nd626580c72a.x: The 104th Amendment (Act of 2019, in force January 2020) extended SC/ST seat reservation under Article 334 to 2030 and ended Anglo-Indian nomination. Article 334 originally set 10 years (till 1960). The 95th Amendment gave the previous extension; the 106th introduced one-third women's reservation (Art 334A); the 84th dealt with the delimitation freeze.
nd626580c72a.tq: 104th: SC/ST seats to 2030 + Anglo-Indian nomination ended.
xs: The **104th Amendment** extended SC/ST reservation to **2030** — option **(2)**.
Act of **2019**, in force **Jan 2020**; it also **ended** Anglo-Indian nomination.
The **106th** gave women one-third (**Art. 334A**); the **84th** extended the delimitation freeze.
xa: **Art. 334** originally provided **10 years** (till **1960**).
⚠ IYB also calls it the "Act of **2020**".

nd41691c82f4.s: Under Section 78 of the RPA 1951, election expense accounts must be filed with the District Election Officer within:
nd41691c82f4.x: Section 78 requires expense accounts to reach the DEO, usually the Collector, within 30 days.
xa: **Observers** (general, police, expenditure) are appointed by the ECI under **Sec. 20B**.
**BLOs** now carry standard photo ID cards (IYB **2026**).

n3334f7418d0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the election machinery?
o: Booth Level Officers now carry standard photo identity cards
The Chief Electoral Officer assists the Election Commission in each State or UT
Electoral Registration Officers and Booth Level Officers are associated with electoral rolls
The Election Commission has no control over officers deployed on poll duty
n3334f7418d0.x: The Election Commission controls officers on poll duty and may transfer them or act against partisan conduct.
xa: **Returning Officer** conducts the poll and declares results.
**DEO** (usually the Collector) receives expense accounts within **30 days**.

na5e4dcc1c47.s: For State Party recognition on seat share, a party needs three per cent of Assembly seats or ____ seats, whichever is more.
na5e4dcc1c47.x: One alternative criterion is three per cent of Assembly seats or three seats, whichever is more.
xa: A fifth route: **1** Lok Sabha seat for every **25** from the state.
Recognition is under the **Election Symbols Order, 1968**; registration under **Sec. 29A**.

ncbc22496fc5.s: A party is eligible for National Party recognition if it is recognised as a State party in at least ____ States.
ncbc22496fc5.x: State-party recognition in four or more States is one of the alternative criteria under the Election Symbols Order, 1968.
xa: PYQ APPSC-G2 **2025**: all listed national-party conditions were valid → key "**None of the above**".
State Party routes include **8%** of valid votes, and **1** Lok Sabha seat for every **25** from the state.
Recognition is under the **Election Symbols Order, 1968** (an ECI order, not an Act).

nfd928c56503.s: For a Lok Sabha general election, the notification under Section 14 of the RPA 1951 is issued by the:
nfd928c56503.x: The President notifies Lok Sabha polls on the ECI's recommendation; the ECI fixes the schedule and nomination dates.
xa: ⚠ **Sec. 14** = President (Lok Sabha); **Sec. 15** = Governor (Assembly).
**Bypolls** must be held within **6 months** of a vacancy.

nc81d76bcee0.s: The authority of the Model Code of Conduct is associated with the Election Commission's plenary power under Article:
nc81d76bcee0.x: The Model Code is a set of ECI guidelines supported by Article 324, not a statute enacted by Parliament.
xa: SC in **Mohinder Singh Gill v CEC (1978)**: Art. 324 = "**reservoir of power**".
MCC comes into force **from the announcement of the schedule** (**Harbans Singh Jalal v UoI (1997)**).

nf8cb10f42a1.s: Persons in preventive detention may vote through:
o: A special booth in the jail
nf8cb10f42a1.x: Persons in preventive detention, along with service voters, special voters and electors on election duty, are covered by postal-ballot provisions.
xa: Absentee voters: seniors **85+** (raised from **80**), **benchmark disability (40%+)**, essential-service staff on duty.
Overseas electors enrol at their **passport address** (**Sec. 20A**).

nda83e987de1.s: The age threshold for senior citizens in the absentee-voter postal ballot category is:
nda83e987de1.x: The senior-citizen threshold is 85 years or above, raised from 80 years.
xa: Persons with **benchmark disability (40%+)** and **essential-service staff** on duty also qualify.
Postal ballot also covers **service voters** and those in **preventive detention**.

n199802edea4.s: The grounds for declaring an election void are listed in which Section of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
n199802edea4.x: Section 100 lists grounds such as disqualification of the returned candidate, corrupt practice and improper rejection of a nomination.
xa: Petition tried by the **High Court** (**Sec. 80A**), filed within **45 days** (**Sec. 81**).
Electoral offences now sit in **BNS Chapter IX (Sections 169-177)**.

n6a9b6eeb6f4.s: The 17th Lok Sabha was elected in:
n6a9b6eeb6f4.x: The 17th Lok Sabha was elected in 2019; 2014 elected the 16th and 2024 the 18th.
xa: First general election: **1951-52**.
NOTA first used in a Lok Sabha poll in **2014**.

nea61087cef0.s: Southern States fear population-based delimitation would shift Lok Sabha seats towards States such as:
nea61087cef0.x: Population-based delimitation would shift representation towards more populous States such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan.
xa: **Tamil Nadu** resolution (**17 Aug 2026**): permanent freeze at **543** + **2.2:1** Lok Sabha-Rajya Sabha ratio.
The freeze on inter-State seats dates from the **42nd Amendment (1976)** on the **1971 Census**.

nc0739af5e1e.s: IIIDEM, which trains election managers, is an institute of the:
nc0739af5e1e.x: IIIDEM belongs to the Election Commission, a permanent independent constitutional body constituted in 1950.
xa: SC in **State of Karnataka v Prathik Parasrampuria (2026)**: removing black money from elections = **core ECI duty**.
**Art. 324** vests superintendence, direction and control of elections in the ECI.

nindian-polity-22-43.s: Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the disqualification for conviction continues for how long after release?
nindian-polity-22-43.x: Under the RPA 1951 the disqualification continues for six years after release. Three, five and ten years are distractors.
nindian-polity-22-43.tq: Recall the six-year period after release.
n: The disqualification for conviction continues for six years after release. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
xs: Under the **RPA 1951**, disqualification continues for **six years** after release — option **(2)**.
It applies to one convicted and sentenced to at least **two years**, during imprisonment and **six years** after.
xa: RPA 1951 **Sec. 8** deals with **disqualifications**.
RPA 1951 also covers **corrupt practices** and **election petitions**.
**Sec. 77-78** = expense accounts.

ncb99b5c45d0.s: The Model Code of Conduct was first drafted and used in the 1960 Assembly election of:
ncb99b5c45d0.x: The Code was first used in Kerala in 1960, formalised by the ECI in 1968 and strictly enforced by T.N. Seshan in 1991.
xa: The MCC was revised in **1974**.
