n6b067c34191.s: Which one of the following is NOT a restriction under Part VII of the Model Code of Conduct?
o: Introducing new schemes or grants after announcement of polls
Using official machinery or transport for campaigning
Continuing ordinary official visits without combining them with electioneering
n6b067c34191.x: Part VII (party in power) bars combining official visits with electioneering, using official machinery or transport, and announcing new schemes or grants once polls are announced (options A, B, C). Ordinary official visits not combined with electioneering are not restricted, so D is the answer.
n6b067c34191.tq: Find the option that does not describe a prohibited act under the specific part of the Code.
xs: **Ordinary official visits not combined with electioneering** are not barred — option **(4)**.
**Part VII** curbs: no **official visits with electioneering**, no use of **official machinery/transport**, no **new schemes or grants** once polls are announced.
xa: **Part VII** on the "**party in power**" was added in **1979**.
Sanctions go up to **suspension/withdrawal of recognition** under **Para 16A** of the Symbols Order.
A 2026 petition alleged the **PM's national broadcast** breached MCC Part VII.

nddae4891aca.s: In which case did the Supreme Court describe Article 324 as a “reservoir of power”?
o: Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
nddae4891aca.x: In Mohinder Singh Gill v. CEC (1978), the Supreme Court described Article 324 as a reservoir of power.
nddae4891aca.tq: Match the constitutional principle with the case that established or described it.
xs: **Mohinder Singh Gill v CEC (1978)** called Art. 324 a "**reservoir of power**" — option **(1)**.
It lets the ECI act where **Parliament has not legislated**.
xa: The **MCC**'s authority rests on this **plenary power under Art. 324**.
**Kuldip Nayar**: right to vote = **statutory right**; **PUCL (2013)**: **NOTA** on EVMs.

ne9833f9e6b5.s: Under which provision can the Election Commission suspend or withdraw the recognition of a political party for violating the Model Code of Conduct?
o: Paragraph 16A of the Election Symbols Order, 1968
ne9833f9e6b5.x: Sanctions for MCC violations range from censure up to suspension or withdrawal of recognition under Paragraph 16A of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968. Section 29A deals with party registration, Section 126A with exit polls, and Article 329 bars courts in electoral matters.
xs: **Paragraph 16A of the Election Symbols Order, 1968** allows suspension/withdrawal of recognition — option **(2)**.
**Sec. 29A** = party registration; **Sec. 126A** = exit polls; **Art. 329** = bar on courts.
xa: Sanctions under the MCC range from **censure** up to **suspension/withdrawal of recognition**.
The Symbols Order is an **ECI order, not an Act**.

nindian-polity-53-18.s: When does the Model Code of Conduct come into force?
o: Immediately upon the formal announcement of the election schedule by the ECI
After the completion of nomination and scrutiny
After Parliament approves the election schedule
When the election results are declared
nindian-polity-53-18.x: The Model Code of Conduct takes effect as soon as the ECI announces the election schedule, and lasts until the results.
nindian-polity-53-18.tq: Recall when the Model Code starts.
n: The Model Code of Conduct comes into force immediately upon the ECI's formal announcement of the election schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
xs: The **Model Code of Conduct** comes into force **immediately upon the formal announcement of the election schedule** by the ECI — option **(1)**.
Held in **Harbans Singh Jalal v UoI (1997)**, **P&H HC**; it is lifted once **results are declared**.
xa: The MCC is **not statutory**; it rests on the ECI's plenary power under **Art. 324**.
First drafted by **Kerala** (**1960**); formalised by the ECI in **1968**; **Part VII** (party in power) added **1979**.
Enforced with rigour by CEC **T.N. Seshan** in **1991**.

n3bd92866223.s: The indelible election ink used in India is manufactured by which organisation and is based on which substance?
o: Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd; silver nitrate
n3bd92866223.x: Indelible election ink is manufactured by Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd and is based on silver nitrate.
n3bd92866223.tq: Use the manufacturer–ingredient pair to avoid a two-part factual trap.
xs: Indelible ink is made by **Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd** and is **silver nitrate** based — option **(1)**.
India Security Press, Government Printing Press and Bharat Electronics are not named in the notes as its maker.
xa: Formula from the **National Physical Laboratory**; applied on the **left forefinger**.
First used in the **1962** general election.

n8a567566d37.s: The key chemical in the indelible ink used in Indian elections is:
n8a567566d37.x: Silver nitrate is the key chemical; the formula comes from the National Physical Laboratory and it is applied on the left forefinger.
xa: Manufacturer: **Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd** (Karnataka).
First used in **1962**.

n4fb3db765b1.s: Indelible ink was first used in the Indian general election of:
n4fb3db765b1.x: Indelible ink was first used in the 1962 general election. The claim that it was first used in Mysore in 1960 is incorrect.
n4fb3db765b1.tq: Reject the nearby but incorrect preliminary-use year.
xs: Indelible ink was first used in the **1962** general election — option **(3)**.
**1952** is the 1st Lok Sabha; **1957** and **1967** were other early general elections.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "first used in **1960** in Mysore" is wrong — **1960** = MCC in **Kerala**.
Made by **Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd**; **silver nitrate** based.

n70a64276eb3.s: The Supreme Court directed the inclusion of a NOTA option on all Electronic Voting Machines in:
o: Harbans Singh Jalal v Union of India, 1997
Mohinder Singh Gill v Chief Election Commissioner, 1978
Kuldip Nayar v Union of India, 2006
n70a64276eb3.x: In PUCL v Union of India on 27 September 2013, the Supreme Court directed that a NOTA button be provided on all EVMs.
n70a64276eb3.tq: Match the election-related judicial direction with the correct case and year.
xs: **PUCL v Union of India (27 September 2013)** ordered a **NOTA** button on all EVMs — option **(1)**.
**Harbans Singh Jalal** = MCC from schedule announcement; **Mohinder Singh Gill** = Art. 324 "reservoir of power"; **Kuldip Nayar** = vote a statutory right.
xa: PUCL (2013) also linked the **secret vote** to **Art. 19(1)(a)**.
NOTA symbol: ballot with a **black cross**, designed by **NID, Ahmedabad**.

n2633ea1c843.s: The NOTA symbol, a ballot paper with a black cross, was designed by:
o: The National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad
n2633ea1c843.x: The NOTA symbol was designed by NID Ahmedabad; it was first used in a Lok Sabha election in 2014.
xa: In 2014 NOTA took **1.1%** of votes (over **6 million**).
⚠ NOTA was ordered in **2013** (PUCL); first used in a Lok Sabha poll in **2014**.

nb4afc0e5df4.s: From 1 July 2024, electoral offences such as bribery, undue influence and personation are contained in:
nb4afc0e5df4.x: From 1 July 2024 these offences are in Chapter IX of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (Sections 169–177); earlier they were in IPC Chapter IXA.
xa: **Corrupt practice** is a **Section 100** ground for voiding an election.
**Art. 329(b)** is the constitutional base of the election-petition bar.

nindian-polity-60-3.s: A candidate can win a State Assembly election without obtaining more than 50 per cent of the votes because Assembly elections follow the:
o: Proportional representation by single transferable vote
nindian-polity-60-3.x: Under first-past-the-post, the candidate with the most valid votes wins even without 50 per cent.
n: The Legislative Assembly election uses the First-Past-the-Post system. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
A candidate does not need an absolute majority of more than 50 percent to win under the First-Past-the-Post system. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
The candidate securing the highest number of valid votes wins under the First-Past-the-Post system. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 158-161]
xa: FPTP is used for the **Lok Sabha** and **Assemblies**.
**PR-STV** is used for **Rajya Sabha**, **Legislative Councils**, **President** and **Vice-President**.
PR was rejected for the Lok Sabha due to **fragmentation and unstable** governments.

nindian-polity-66-3.s: The right to register a secret negative vote (NOTA) was linked by the Supreme Court to Article:
nindian-polity-66-3.x: The Court linked a secret negative vote to freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a).
n: The Supreme Court linked the right to register a negative vote in secrecy with the Freedom of Speech and Expression. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
The right to register a negative vote in secrecy is linked with Article 19(1)(a). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
xa: The judgment directed the **mandatory introduction** of the **NOTA button** on EVMs.
NOTA symbol designed by **NID, Ahmedabad**.
NOTA first used in the Lok Sabha in **2014** → **1.1%** of votes.

nindian-polity-73-3.s: An Electronic Voting Machine is best described as:
o: A judicial mechanism for resolving election disputes
An electoral system based on proportional representation
An electronic vote recording and counting apparatus
nindian-polity-73-3.x: An EVM is a machine that records and counts votes. It is not an electoral system; first-past-the-post is the system.
nindian-polity-73-3.tq: Discriminate a voting machine from an electoral system.
n: An EVM is an electronic vote-recording apparatus. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
An EVM is an electronic vote-counting apparatus. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
An EVM is not an electoral system. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
xs: An **EVM** is an **electronic vote-recording and vote-counting apparatus** — option **(4)**.
⚠ It is **not** an **electoral system**; India's system for direct elections is **First-Past-the-Post**.
xa: EVMs are used for **Lok Sabha** and **State Assembly** elections.
Deployed under the **superintendence, direction and control** of the **ECI**.
First EVM: **Parur 1982**; VVPAT: **Noksen 2013**.

na36bcd3e362.s: Which of the following is NOT a category of observer appointed by the Election Commission under Section 20B?
na36bcd3e362.x: The listed observer categories are general, police and expenditure observers. Judicial observer is not among them.
na36bcd3e362.tq: Find the role outside the three-member observer set.
xs: **Judicial observer** is not a Sec. 20B category — option **(1)**.
The ECI appoints **general, police and expenditure** observers (**Sec. 20B**).
xa: During elections the **ECI controls officers** on poll duty and can transfer them.
The **CEO** verifies non-compliant **RUPPs**; ECI **delisted 808** of them.

nac6a9260616.s: Recognition of political parties under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968 is distinct from registration under which provision?
o: Section 19 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950
Paragraph 16A of the Election Symbols Order, 1968
Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
nac6a9260616.x: Recognition is governed by the Election Symbols Order, 1968, whereas registration of political parties is under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
nac6a9260616.tq: Separate the similar-looking concepts of registration and recognition by identifying the governing provision.
xs: Registration is under **Section 29A of the RPA, 1951** — option **(3)**; recognition is under the **Election Symbols Order, 1968**.
**Sec. 19, RPA 1950** = voter eligibility; **Para 16A** = sanctions under the Symbols Order; **Art. 324** = ECI's powers.
xa: The Symbols Order is an **ECI order, not an Act**.
Under **Para 16A** the ECI can **suspend/withdraw recognition** for MCC breaches.

ncc134ca5534.s: The six-month requirement for holding a by-election does NOT apply when:
o: The vacancy arises in a reserved constituency
The vacancy arises from the resignation of the member
The vacancy arises during a session of the House
The remaining term is less than one year
ncc134ca5534.x: The exceptions are a remaining term of less than one year, or the Election Commission certifying difficulty after consulting the Central Government.
xa: By-election = **single vacancy**, within **6 months** (**Sec. 151A RPA**).
A polling station may have at most **1,200 electors**.

n94ce82a61b4.s: An exit poll is best described as:
o: A survey conducted before the election notification to assess voter intention
A poll of voters taken immediately after they leave the polling station
A survey conducted only among political party workers
A statistical report prepared after the declaration of results
n94ce82a61b4.x: An exit poll is conducted among voters immediately after they leave the polling station; it is different from an opinion poll.
n94ce82a61b4.tq: Separate the timing of an exit poll from that of an opinion poll.
xs: An **exit poll** is a poll of voters taken **immediately after they leave** the polling station — option **(2)**.
It is **not the same as an opinion poll**, which is taken before voting.
xa: APPSC **2018** key: a, c, d correct.
**Sec. 126A, RPA 1951** restricts exit polls during multi-phase polling.

n0cf5faef09c.s: The bar on opinion polls during the 48 hours before the close of poll is provided under which Section of the RPA, 1951?
n0cf5faef09c.x: Section 126 bars opinion polls in the 48 hours before the close of poll; Section 126A governs the longer restriction on exit polls.
xa: Exit-poll ban runs till **half an hour** after the close of the last phase.
Opinion-poll ban is under **Sec. 126**.

n1e9a19471c0.s: The High Court should endeavour to decide an election petition within:
n1e9a19471c0.x: The High Court should try to decide an election petition within six months, and an appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
xa: **President/VP** election disputes go to the **SC** (**Art. 71**).
**Sec. 80**: no election questioned except by petition; base = **Art. 329(b)**.

naeaabc3ac7c.s: The first general election to the Lok Sabha in India was held in:
naeaabc3ac7c.x: India's first general election was held in 1951-52 (the 1st Lok Sabha is dated 1952); it and the next three (1957, 1962, 1967) were held simultaneously with Assembly polls.
naeaabc3ac7c.tq: Distinguish the first election period from the year in which the First Lok Sabha was constituted.
xs: The first general election was held in **1951-52** — option **(1)**.
The first four (**1951-52, 1957, 1962, 1967**) were **simultaneous** with Assembly polls.
xa: The 1st Lok Sabha is dated **1952**.
**18** general elections so far; the **18th Lok Sabha** was elected in **2024**.

n4935c2a80ac.s: A constituency having no fixed geographical boundary, such as the Sangha seat in Sikkim, is known as a:
n4935c2a80ac.x: A floating constituency has no fixed geographical boundary. The Sangha constituency in Sikkim is an example in which only registered Buddhist monks vote and contest.
n4935c2a80ac.tq: Identify the exact electoral term from its defining geographical feature.
xs: A seat with no fixed geographical boundary is a **floating constituency** — option **(4)**.
Example: **Sangha (Sikkim)** — only **registered Buddhist monks** vote and contest.
xa: PYQ: APPSC-G2 **2023, 2025** — both statements on floating constituency were correct.
**Delimitation** fixes the **number of seats and boundaries** of territorial constituencies.

n7720bc60e02.s: The NETA app, which lets voters rate their elected representatives, was built by:
o: The Ministry of Law and Justice
n7720bc60e02.x: The NETA app was built by a private start-up; it was not conceptualised by the Election Commission of India.
xa: APPSC-GS **2019** key: only statement b true.
⚠ **NETA** = private start-up; **cVIGIL** = ECI, **100 minutes**.

nindian-polity-53-22.s: Corrupt practices in elections are dealt with in the:
nindian-polity-53-22.x: Corrupt practices and disqualifications are in the RPA, 1951; voter registration is in the 1950 Act.
n: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 provides for the registration of electors. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides disqualifications for holding membership. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides for corrupt practices. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with the disqualifications of candidates. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
xa: RPA 1950 also covers **allocation of seats** and **preparation of electoral rolls**.
RPA 1951 also covers **election petitions** and **registration of political parties** (**Section 29A**).
RPA 1951 **Sec. 8** = disqualifications.

ned0ca584baf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Tarkunde Committee on electoral reforms?
o: It was appointed in 1974 and reported in 1975
It was set up by Jayaprakash Narayan
It proposed a selection panel of the Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chief Justice of India
It recommended a three-member Election Commission and a voting age of 18
ned0ca584baf.x: The proposed panel was the PM, the Leader of the Opposition and the CJI, not the Speaker.
xa: ⚠ The **CEC and ECs Act 2023** dropped the **CJI**, unlike Tarkunde's proposal.
2023 panel: **PM, a Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM, Leader of the Opposition**.

n29ed009c4ee.s: The Vohra Committee, constituted in 1993, primarily examined:
o: The financing of political parties by the State
The nexus between crime and politics
n29ed009c4ee.x: The Vohra Committee examined the nexus between criminals and politicians, or the crime-politics nexus.
n29ed009c4ee.tq: Discriminate between committees by their central subject rather than their common electoral-reform setting.
xs: The **Vohra Committee (1993)** examined the **nexus between crime and politics** — option **(4)**.
**State funding** = Indrajit Gupta; **internal party democracy** = Law Commission 170th Report.
xa: Vohra = crime-politics is the **most repeated** exam pair.
APPSC-G2 **2023** asked a matching of **Vohra/Gupta/Goswami/Verma**.

n2d416038b69.s: The Law Commission report that recommended giving the ECI a limited power to deregister non-compliant parties is the:
n2d416038b69.x: The 255th Report (2015) sought limited deregistration power; the 170th Report (1999) dealt with internal party democracy and partial list seats.
xa: The 255th also recommended the **Totaliser** and **one candidate, one seat**.
170th: full state funding desirable only if parties are **barred from other sources**.

n234f9f52c74.s: Which one of the following committees/commissions was NOT concerned with Centre-State relations?
n234f9f52c74.x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) dealt with state funding of elections (an electoral reform), so it is the odd one out (APPSC-G2 2025, UPPSC 2015). The Rajamannar Committee (Tamil Nadu, 1969-71), Sarkaria Commission (1983-88) and Punchhi Commission (2007-10) all examined Centre-State relations.
n234f9f52c74.tq: Indrajit Gupta = state funding of elections, not Centre-State.
xs: The **Indrajit Gupta Committee** dealt with **state funding of elections**, not Centre-State relations — option **(4)**.
**Rajamannar, Sarkaria** and **Punchhi** all examined **Centre-State relations**.
xa: PYQs: APPSC-G2 **2025**, UPPSC **2015**.
Gupta (1998) proposed partial funding **in kind**; still **not adopted**.

n95a0bbaf615.s: Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the ban on exit polls is provided in:
n95a0bbaf615.x: Section 126A of the RPA, 1951 concerns the ban on exit polls.
xa: Liquor ban **48 hours** before poll = **Sec. 135C**.
Paid holiday on poll day = **Sec. 135B**.

na96026b9b52.s: Disqualification under the Tenth Schedule is decided by the Speaker or Chairman, subject to which limitation?
o: Approval by the President in all cases
A referendum among members of the House
Approval by the Election Commission before every decision
na96026b9b52.x: The Speaker or Chairman decides disqualification under the Tenth Schedule, but the decision remains subject to judicial review, as recognised by the Supreme Court in 1992.
na96026b9b52.tq: Ask who exercises the power and then identify the constitutional check on that power.
xs: **Tenth Schedule** decisions by the **Speaker/Chairman** are subject to **judicial review** — option **(2)** (SC **1992**).
No presidential approval, referendum or ECI approval is required.
xa: Anti-defection amendments: **52nd (1985)**, **91st (2003)**.
Goswami (**1990**) also dealt with anti-defection.

nb995aabceb8.s: The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) recommended State funding of elections in the form of:
o: Partial funding in kind to recognised parties and candidates
Full funding in cash to every candidate
Full funding in kind to every candidate
Partial cash funding to independents only
nb995aabceb8.x: It suggested partial funding in kind to recognised parties and candidates; the recommendation is still not adopted.
xa: ⚠ "Which is NOT on Centre-State relations?" → **Indrajit Gupta**.
APPSC **2025**: Indrajit Gupta = electoral reforms.

n1e274c1f30c.s: The Law Commission's 170th Report found full state funding of elections desirable only if:
o: Only recognised parties were allowed to contest
Parties were barred from taking funds from other sources
Independent candidates were excluded from funding
n1e274c1f30c.x: The Law Commission considered full state funding desirable only if parties were barred from receiving funds from other sources.
xa: The **170th Report** also backed **simultaneous elections**, **internal party democracy** and partial **list (PR) seats**.
**Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998)**: partial funding **in kind** to recognised parties/candidates; still **not adopted**.
**Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990)** and the **2nd ARC** also recommended public funding.
Countries with public funding: **Germany, Sweden, Japan** (and **Canada** in another list).

nc857cc77580.s: The 'level field for resource-poor candidates' argument for State funding of elections rests on equality under Article:
nc857cc77580.x: The level-field argument rests on equality under Article 14; curbing black money is another argument in favour, while the fiscal burden is an argument against.
xa: Another objection: it does **not stop off-book cash** spending.
SC (**2026**): eliminating black money is a **core ECI responsibility**.

nc68a7055cf2.s: According to the Supreme Court decision in State of Karnataka v. Prathik Parasrampuria (2026), eliminating black money from elections is primarily whose core responsibility?
nc68a7055cf2.x: The Supreme Court described elimination of black money from elections as a core responsibility of the Election Commission of India.
nc68a7055cf2.tq: Ask which constitutional institution has the responsibility, avoiding a swap with an auditing or fiscal body.
xs: In **State of Karnataka v Prathik Parasrampuria (2026)**, the SC called eliminating black money from elections a **core responsibility** of the **Election Commission of India** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The case is on the **state funding** page; the CAG, Parliament Secretariat and Finance Commission are not named for this role.
xa: Yet the ECI still **lacks power to deregister** parties for **financial non-compliance**.
The **Law Commission 255th Report (2015)** sought **limited power to deregister** non-compliant parties.
Arguments for state funding: curbs **black money** and quid-pro-quo funding; levels the field (**Art. 14**).
Against: **heavy fiscal burden**; does not stop **off-book cash** spending.

n242b09ddcba.s: A totaliser, which combines the counting of several EVMs, is intended to:
n242b09ddcba.x: A totaliser combines several EVM counts to hide booth-wise trends; the ECI stated no legal framework for it exists.
xa: Recommended by the **Law Commission 255th Report (2015)**.
SC **sought the Centre's response** on totalisers as a "fall-back option" (**Sep 2026**).

n9e9eb74e937.s: The use of 'totalisers' in counting votes was recommended by:
n9e9eb74e937.x: The Law Commission's 255th Report (2015) recommended totalisers, which pool the count of several control units so booth-wise voting patterns stay hidden. The Indrajit Gupta Committee dealt with state funding, the Vohra Committee with the crime-politics nexus, and the 2nd ARC with ethics in governance.
xs: **Totalisers** were recommended by the **Law Commission's 255th Report, 2015** — option **(2)**.
**Indrajit Gupta** = state funding; **Vohra** = crime-politics; **2nd ARC** = Ethics in Governance.
xa: The 255th also urged **one candidate, one seat** and a **collegium** for appointing the CEC.
It sought **limited power to deregister** non-compliant parties.

n377a64cc072.s: Simultaneous Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections were held from 1951-52 up to:
n377a64cc072.x: Simultaneous polls were held from 1951-52 to 1967; both the 170th Law Commission Report and the 2018 draft report backed them.
xa: Proposed safeguard: **constructive no-confidence motion** (German model).
Criticism: weakens **federalism**.

n46020bbc32f.s: The High-Level Committee on simultaneous elections (2023-24) was chaired by:
n46020bbc32f.x: Former President Ram Nath Kovind chaired it; Amit Shah and N.K. Singh were members, and Dinesh Goswami headed the 1990 electoral reform committee.
xa: Other members: **N.K. Singh, Subhash C. Kashyap, Harish Salve, Sanjay Kothari**.
Recommendation: **phased rollout**.

nindian-polity-25-31.s: A candidate forfeits the security deposit when the candidate fails to secure more than which proportion of the total valid votes polled?
nindian-polity-25-31.x: A candidate loses the security deposit if they win no more than one-sixth of the valid votes.
n: A candidate forfeits the security deposit if the candidate fails to secure more than one-sixth of the total valid votes polled. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xs: The deposit is forfeited if the candidate fails to get more than **one-sixth** of the **total valid votes** — option **(4)**.
**Sec. 34** deposits: **₹25,000** (Lok Sabha), **₹10,000** (Assembly), half for SC/ST.
xa: The **1996** RP (Amendment) Act brought **higher security deposits**.
It also required more proposers for independents/unrecognised parties.
Election petition: within **45 days** (**Sec. 81**).

nindian-polity-53-27.s:
Which of the following were recommended by the Dinesh Goswami Committee?
1. State funding of elections
2. Use of Electronic Voting Machines
3. Allocation of State Legislative Council seats
Select the correct answer:
nindian-polity-53-27.x: The Goswami Committee recommended State funding of elections and EVMs, leading to the 1996 RPA amendment; Council seat allocation was not its subject.
n: The Dinesh Goswami Committee recommended state funding of elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Dinesh Goswami Committee recommended the use of electronic voting machines. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The Dinesh Goswami Committee recommended measures subsequently enacted in the 1996 amendment to the Representation of the People Act, 1951. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
xa: Goswami was the **broadest review**: time limits for bye-elections, strengthening the EC, anti-defection; flagged **musclemen**.
**Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998)** = **State funding of elections**, partial funding **in kind**.
⚠ **Vohra (1993)** = **crime–politics nexus**.

n239f32561b3.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the corrupt practices covered by Section 123 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
o: Failure to file an election expenditure account within 30 days
Appeal on the grounds of religion or caste
n239f32561b3.x: Section 123 covers corrupt practices such as bribery, undue influence and appeals based on religion or caste. Filing the expenditure account within 30 days is governed by Section 78.
n239f32561b3.tq: Find the provision belonging to a neighbouring compliance area rather than the corrupt-practices list.
xs: **Failure to file an expense account within 30 days** is not a Sec. 123 corrupt practice — option **(1)**; it falls under **Sec. 78**.
**Sec. 123** covers **bribery, undue influence, appeal on religion/caste**.
xa: Failure to file accounts can lead the **ECI** to **disqualify** the candidate.
Bribery and undue influence are now offences in **BNS** too.

neba772ed4bf.s: The reform principle 'one candidate, one seat' addresses:
o: Candidates contesting from more than one constituency
neba772ed4bf.x: The Law Commission proposed 'one candidate, one seat' for candidates contesting from more than one constituency; the ECI proposed the vacating candidate bear by-election costs.
xa: Winner of both must vacate one within **14 days**.

n3014713e66a.s: Which one of the following was a major provision of the Representation of the People (Amendment) Act, 1996?
o: Removal of the limit on constituencies from which a candidate may contest
Reduction of security deposits and proposers for independent candidates
Abolition of by-elections within six months
Capping a candidate’s contest to two constituencies and increasing security deposits
n3014713e66a.x: The 1996 amendment capped contests at two constituencies, increased security deposits, and required more proposers for independents and unrecognised parties.
n3014713e66a.tq: Identify the option that combines the principal nomination-related changes without reversing them.
xs: The **RP (Amendment) Act, 1996** capped contests at **two constituencies** and raised **security deposits** — option **(4)**.
It increased (not reduced) deposits and proposers, and it kept bypolls within **6 months** (**Sec. 151A**).
xa: It limited **countermanding** to the death of a **recognised-party** candidate.
It added a **paid holiday** (**Sec. 135B**) and **liquor ban** (**Sec. 135C**).
Offences under the **Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971** became a disqualification.

na6776d883fb.s: A person elected from two constituencies must vacate one of them within:
na6776d883fb.x: Under Section 70 one seat must be vacated within 14 days; the two-constituency cap in Section 33(7) came with the 1996 amendment.
xa: **30 days** is the deadline for filing expense accounts (**Sec. 78**).

n1fe38e89a68.s: Under Section 8 of the RPA 1951, conviction resulting in imprisonment of ____ or more attracts disqualification.
n1fe38e89a68.x: Section 8 disqualifies on conviction with two years' imprisonment or more; Lily Thomas removed protection during pendency of an appeal.
xa: Period: **term plus 6 years** after release.

ne2203077099.s: Section 77 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, is criticised in the context of party expenditure because it:
o: Prohibits all expenditure on election campaigns
Places a ceiling only on the expenditure of candidates, not on the election expenditure incurred directly by political parties
Places a ceiling only on political parties, not on candidates
Requires all campaign expenditure to be incurred in cash
ne2203077099.x: The perceived loophole is that Section 77 caps candidate expenditure while not imposing a comparable ceiling on the parties’ own election spending.
ne2203077099.tq: Ask who bears the statutory ceiling to expose the candidate-party distinction.
xs: **Sec. 77** caps only **candidate** spending, not **parties'** own election spending — option **(2)**.
It does not ban campaign spending or require cash; it does not cap parties.
xa: Travel of **20 star campaigners** is excluded from the candidate's limit.
Unfinished agenda: a **party spending cap**.

nindian-polity-25-13.s: A candidate contesting an election to the Lok Sabha or a State Assembly can contest from a maximum of how many constituencies under Section 33 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
nindian-polity-25-13.x: Under Section 33(7) of the RPA, 1951, a candidate can contest from at most two constituencies, a limit added in 1996.
n: Section 33 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, limits a candidate to contesting from a maximum of two constituencies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
A candidate can contest from a maximum of two Lok Sabha constituencies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
A candidate can contest from a maximum of two State Assembly constituencies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xs: A candidate can contest from at most **two** constituencies — option **(4)** — under **Section 33(7), RPA 1951**.
The cap was added by the **1996** amendment after **Devi Lal** contested **three Lok Sabha seats** in **1991**.
xa: A winner of both seats must vacate one within **14 days** (**Sec. 70**).
Reform proposal: **one candidate, one seat** (**Law Commission 255th report**).
ECI proposal: the vacating candidate pays for the bypoll.

nc0475c8910d.s: The judgment in Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013) is associated with which of the following conclusions?
o: Disqualification of legislators was transferred from Parliament to the Election Commission.
Only a sitting legislator can be disqualified after a three-month period.
A convicted legislator remains protected until the disposal of the appeal.
A convicted legislator is disqualified immediately, without protection during the pendency of an appeal.
nc0475c8910d.x: The Lily Thomas judgment held that conviction leads to immediate disqualification and that an appeal does not provide protection against that disqualification.
nc0475c8910d.tq: Test the holding of a landmark judgment against closely related but reversed legal effects.
xs: **Lily Thomas (July 2013)**: a convicted legislator is **disqualified immediately**, with **no protection while appeal pending** — option **(4)**.
It struck down **Sec. 8(4)**, the **3-month appeal buffer** for sitting members.
xa: Disqualification follows conviction with **2+ years** (**Sec. 8**).
**Ramesh Dalal (2005)**: sitting MP/MLA convicted with 2+ years barred from contesting.

nf872a3ef75d.s: Mandatory disclosure by candidates of criminal cases, assets, liabilities and education was laid down in:
o: Public Interest Foundation v. Union of India
Lily Thomas v. Union of India
Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India
nf872a3ef75d.x: ADR (2002) made such disclosure mandatory; PUCL placed the voter's right to know in Article 19(1)(a).
xa: **PUCL (2013)** ordered the **NOTA** option.

nce5aaf2c38d.s: In ADR v Union of India (2024), the Supreme Court struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme mainly because it violated:
o: The right to equality under Article 14
The voters' right to information under Article 19(1)(a)
The right to life under Article 21
The freedom of association under Article 19(1)(c)
nce5aaf2c38d.x: The five-judge bench unanimously held that donor anonymity violated voters' right to information, part of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a). Articles 14, 21 and 19(1)(c) were not the ground stated for striking the scheme down.
nce5aaf2c38d.tq: Bonds struck down = Art 19(1)(a) right to information (15 Feb 2024).
xs: The scheme violated voters' **right to information under Art. 19(1)(a)** — option **(2)**.
Articles **14**, **21** and **19(1)(c)** were not the stated ground.
xa: **PUCL (2003)**: voter's **right to know** is part of Art. 19(1)(a).
**PUCL (2013)**: right to reject (NOTA) also flows from Art. 19(1)(a).

nbb92f07bf72.s: ECIL, one of the two public sector undertakings that manufacture EVMs, is headquartered in:
nbb92f07bf72.x: BEL is based in Bengaluru and ECIL in Hyderabad.
xa: BEL and ECIL also make **VVPATs**.
AP angle: **ECIL** is the EVM maker based in **Hyderabad**.

naae0157627d.s: Under ADR v. ECI (2024), symbol-loading units are to be sealed and preserved for:
naae0157627d.x: The Court rejected ballot papers and 100% VVPAT counting, but ordered SLUs preserved for 45 days and allowed runners-up to seek checking of 5% of EVMs.
xa: The check is of the EVMs' **burnt memory**.
**N. Chandrababu Naidu (2019)** raised the VVPAT tally to **5** polling stations per segment.

n166a336c569.s: Which case held that VVPAT is necessary for free and fair elections and directed its introduction in phases?
o: State of Karnataka v Prathik Parasrampuria
n166a336c569.x: In Subramanian Swamy v ECI (2013), the Supreme Court held that VVPAT was needed for free and fair polls and required phased introduction.
n166a336c569.tq: Match the judicial case with its distinctive electoral reform.
xs: **Subramanian Swamy v ECI (2013)** held VVPAT needed for free and fair polls, to be brought **in phases** — option **(1)**.
**ADR v ECI** = 2024 EVM/VVPAT safeguards; **PUCL** = NOTA; **Prathik Parasrampuria** = black money.
xa: VVPAT debuted at **Noksen**, **2013**.
**N. Chandrababu Naidu (2019)**: tally from **1 to 5** polling stations per segment.

n24d2424602b.s: Which of the following correctly describes the phased rollout recommended by the Ram Nath Kovind High-Level Committee?
o: Local-body elections first, followed by Lok Sabha elections after five years
All elections to be held on the same day without any transitional phase
Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council elections together first, followed by Assembly elections
Lok Sabha and Assembly elections together first, followed by local-body elections within 100 days
n24d2424602b.x: The committee recommended holding Lok Sabha and Assembly polls together initially, followed by local-body elections within 100 days.
n24d2424602b.tq: Track the sequence and the specific 100-day interval in the proposed phased model.
xs: The **Kovind Committee** recommended a **phased rollout**: **Lok Sabha and Assembly** polls together first, then **local-body elections within 100 days** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It did not propose a same-day poll without transition, nor local bodies first.
xa: Committee chair: ex-President **Ram Nath Kovind** (**2023-24**); members included **Amit Shah** and **Ghulam Nabi Azad**.
The **129th Amendment Bill, 2024** inserts **Art. 82A** and amends **Arts. 83, 172 and 327**.
Lok Sabha + Assembly polls were held together **1951-52 to 1967**.
JPC still examining the Bill (**Feb 2026**).

n5b0a369112f.s: Under Section 34 of the RPA 1951, the security deposit for a general-category Lok Sabha candidate is:
n5b0a369112f.x: It is ₹25,000 for the Lok Sabha and ₹10,000 for an Assembly; SC/ST candidates pay half.
xa: Deposit is forfeited below **one-sixth** of valid votes.
The **1996** amendment raised security deposits.

nb6ab69977e5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about judgments on criminalisation of politics?
o: In Public Interest Foundation (2018), the Court itself imposed disqualification on framing of charges
Public Interest Foundation (2018) ordered publicity of candidates' criminal records
Public Interest Foundation (2018) left disqualification on framing of charges to Parliament
Lily Thomas removed protection from disqualification during pendency of an appeal
nb6ab69977e5.x: The Court did not itself impose disqualification on framing of charges; it left the issue to Parliament.
xa: ECI (**Sep 2025**) also requires **reasons for selecting** such candidates.
Law Commission **244th Report (2014)** urged barring candidates once charges are framed.

nc191234fd0c.s: Under the ECI's requirement, political parties fielding candidates with criminal records must publish the details of those records and:
o: An undertaking to resign if convicted
The reasons for selecting such candidates
nc191234fd0c.x: Parties must publish the criminal-record details and the reasons for selecting such candidates; withdrawal is not required.
xa: Affidavits on criminal cases, assets, liabilities, education date from **2002**.
ADR data: **31%** of MPs and **29%** of MLAs face serious charges.

n613e2fbb641.s: Barring candidates upon framing of charges in serious offences was recommended by which Law Commission report?
n613e2fbb641.x: The recommendation was made in the Law Commission's 244th Report of 2014.
xa: ⚠ LENS cites it as "Law Commission, **2015**".
**Public Interest Foundation (2018)** left this question to **Parliament**.

nc36f21173b7.s: The current election expenditure limit for a Lok Sabha candidate in a larger State is:
nc36f21173b7.x: The limit is ₹95 lakh (earlier ₹70 lakh), raised by the Conduct of Elections (Amendment) Rules, 2022; ₹40 lakh is the Assembly limit.
xa: Smaller States: **Rs 75 lakh** (LS), **Rs 28 lakh** (Assembly).
Earlier: Rs **70** lakh (LS) and Rs **28** lakh (Assembly) for larger States.

na1a2131bd07.s: For a political party to retain tax exemption under the stated provisions, which combination is relevant?
o: No donation above ₹2,000 in any form and no record of larger donations
No cash donation above ₹20,000 and records only of donations above ₹2,000
No cash donation above ₹2,000 and proper records of donations above ₹20,000
Acceptance of unlimited cash donations provided they are reported after the election
na1a2131bd07.x: The stated conditions include no cash donation above ₹2,000 and maintenance of records for donations above ₹20,000. These are referred to under Section 12 of the Income Tax Act, 2025, replacing the earlier reference to Section 13A of the 1961 Act.
na1a2131bd07.tq: Keep the two monetary thresholds separate instead of reversing their functions.
xs: **No cash donation above Rs 2,000** and **records of donations above Rs 20,000** — option **(3)**.
Option (2) swaps the two thresholds.
xa: ⚠ **Rs 2,000** = cash cap; **Rs 20,000** = record threshold.
Now under **Sec. 12, Income Tax Act 2025**; earlier **Sec. 13A**, IT Act **1961**.

n1b498c25970.s: The Supreme Court's decision in Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India also invalidated which change associated with electoral political funding?
o: Abolition of political party registration under the RPA
Removal of the corporate donation cap under the Companies Act
Compulsory disclosure of all cash donations by parties
Restriction on donations by individual citizens
n1b498c25970.x: The Court struck down the removal of the corporate donation cap from the Companies Act.
n1b498c25970.tq: Identify the allied legal provision affected by the judgment, not merely the main scheme.
xs: It also struck down the **removal of the corporate donation cap** from the **Companies Act** — option **(2)**.
The notes record no ruling on party registration, cash disclosure or individual donations.
xa: Ground: violation of voters' **right to information under Art. 19(1)(a)**.
ADR: **60% (₹19,083 cr)** of party funds in **2004-23** came from undisclosed sources.

n2f16eafe3b6.s: The decision in N. Chandrababu Naidu v Union of India (2019) changed the random VVPAT-EVM tally from:
o: Two to five polling stations per district
One to five polling stations per Assembly segment
One to ten polling stations per parliamentary constituency
Five to ten polling stations per Assembly segment
n2f16eafe3b6.x: The 2019 decision raised the random VVPAT-EVM tally from one to five polling stations per Assembly segment.
n2f16eafe3b6.tq: Remember both sides of the judicially ordered numerical increase.
xs: **N. Chandrababu Naidu v UoI (2019)** raised the random VVPAT–EVM tally from **one to five polling stations** per **Assembly segment** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The tally unit is the **Assembly segment**, not a district or parliamentary constituency.
xa: **ADR v ECI (Apr 2024)** rejected **100% slip counting** and a **return to paper ballots**.
In that case, symbol-loading units are sealed for **45 days**; runners-up can seek a check of **5% of EVMs**.
**Subramanian Swamy v ECI (2013)**: VVPAT is needed for free and fair polls; introduce it **in phases**.

n75f7b40d113.s: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended:
o: Full state funding and a lifetime ban on convicted legislators
Simultaneous elections and a constructive no-confidence motion
Partial state funding and barring persons charged with serious offences
n75f7b40d113.x: The Second ARC recommended partial state funding and barring persons charged with serious offences.
xa: Its report was titled "**Ethics in Governance**" (chair **Veerappa Moily**).
**Indrajit Gupta (1998)** and **Goswami (1990)** also backed public funding.

nb41759dfdba.s: A political party could encash electoral bonds only if it had secured at least what percentage of votes in the last election?
nb41759dfdba.x: Only a registered political party that had secured at least 1% of the votes in the last election could encash electoral bonds.
nb41759dfdba.tq: Recall the statutory eligibility threshold rather than the general registration requirement.
xs: A party could encash electoral bonds only with at least **1 per cent** (**1% of the vote**) in the last election — so option **(2)** is correct.
Only **registered parties** meeting this **1%** threshold could encash; the bonds were sold only by **SBI** as **bearer bonds**.
xa: Denominations: **₹1,000 to ₹1 crore**; each bond was valid for **15 days**.
The scheme was notified in **2018** via **Finance Act 2017** amendments.
Struck down as **unconstitutional** by a unanimous **five-judge Constitution Bench** in **ADR v UoI** (**15 Feb 2024**) — it violated the **right to information under Art. 19(1)(a)**.
⚠ Donor anonymity was hailed in older notes as a "**transparency**" gain.

nf2842a71a56.s: In the 2024 electoral bond judgment, the Supreme Court directed ____ to provide donor data to the Election Commission.
nf2842a71a56.x: A five-judge Constitution Bench unanimously struck down the scheme and directed SBI to provide donor data to the ECI.
xa: Case: **ADR v Union of India, 15 Feb 2024**.
⚠ **ADR v UoI** 2002 = disclosure; **ADR v ECI** 2024 = EVM/VVPAT.

n25cf1d6ee5a.s: A State funding model in which the State bears all legitimate costs and private donations are banned is:
n25cf1d6ee5a.x: Bearing all legitimate costs while banning private donations describes full funding; funding may be full or partial, in cash or in kind.
xa: Countries with public funding: **Germany, Sweden, Japan** (+ **Canada**).
Against: **heavy fiscal burden**; does not stop **off-book cash**.

n29377d1a6ab.s: VVPAT slips must be counted in which of the following circumstances?
o: Whenever EVM data and Form 17C do not match
Whenever postal ballots exceed the number of EVM votes
Only in constituencies using postal ballots
Only when the winning candidate requests it after the declaration of results
n29377d1a6ab.x: VVPAT slips are required to be counted wherever the EVM data and Form 17C do not match.
n29377d1a6ab.tq: Apply the verification rule to a specific discrepancy rather than to a general recount demand.
xs: **VVPAT slips must be counted wherever EVM data do not match Form 17C** — so option **(1)** is correct.
This is one of the **new ECI rules** on counting; postal ballots relate to a different rule (below).
xa: The **penultimate EVM/VVPAT round** is counted only after **postal ballots** are finished.
**ADR v ECI (April 2024)**: candidates placed **2nd and 3rd** can seek a check of **5% of EVMs' burnt memory** within **7 days**.
ECI objects that **totalisers** would make **EVM, VVPAT and Form 17C** checks harder.

nbfff8799655.s: A proposed safeguard for maintaining governmental accountability under simultaneous elections is based on which model?
o: The Westminster model of an unelected executive
The American model of judicial review
The German model of a constructive vote of no-confidence
nbfff8799655.x: The proposed safeguard is a constructive no-confidence motion modelled on the German system.
nbfff8799655.tq: Match the institutional safeguard with the country model specifically associated with it.
xs: The proposed safeguard is a **constructive no-confidence motion** on the **German model** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is meant to keep a government accountable without breaking the **simultaneous-election** cycle.
xa: The **Law Commission 170th Report (1999)** and the **2018 draft report** backed simultaneous polls.
Lok Sabha + Assembly polls were held together from **1951-52 to 1967**.
Criticism: simultaneous polls weaken **federalism** and need huge numbers of **EVMs and forces**.
The **Kovind Committee** (**2023-24**) recommended a **phased rollout**: local bodies within **100 days** of LS + Assembly polls.

nead2e136a32.s: The expression “bahubali culture” in the context of electoral politics refers primarily to the erosion of trust in legislatures through:
nead2e136a32.x: The expression refers to the use of muscle power and its adverse effect on trust in legislatures.
nead2e136a32.tq: Decode the contextual meaning of a politically significant phrase.
xs: "**Bahubali culture**" refers to **muscle power** eroding trust in legislatures — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is a **criminalisation** issue, unrelated to VVPATs, postal ballots or digital enumeration.
xa: **ADR data**: **31% of MPs and 29% of MLAs** face serious criminal charges.
MPs' share rose from **14% (2009) to 31% (2024)**.
The **Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990)** flagged **musclemen**; the **Vohra Committee (1993)** studied the **crime–politics nexus**.
**12 special courts** handle cases against MPs/MLAs.

n54bbd019382.s: Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 relates to:
o: Corrupt practices during an election campaign
The maintenance of election expenditure accounts
Election petitions presented in the High Court within 45 days of the result
n54bbd019382.x: Section 81 concerns election petitions, which are presented in the High Court within 45 days of the election result.
n54bbd019382.tq: Separate the post-result election-petition provision from campaign and nomination provisions.
xs: **Sec. 81** = **election petition** in the **High Court** within **45 days** — option **(4)**.
Registration = **29A**; corrupt practices = **123**; expense accounts = **77-78**.
xa: **Sec. 100** lists grounds for declaring an election **void**.

ne20abd4ef6b.s: Which State was the first to conduct its entire Assembly election using EVMs?
ne20abd4ef6b.x: Goa conducted the first whole-State Assembly election using EVMs in 1999. Gujarat was not the first State to do so.
ne20abd4ef6b.tq: Separate pilot use from the first whole-State use.
xs: **Goa, 1999** was the first whole-State Assembly election on EVMs — option **(2)**.
⚠ **Gujarat** was **not** the first; **Kerala** (**Parur 1982**) was the first pilot; **Nagaland** (Noksen) = first **VVPAT**.
xa: APPSC-G2 **2025** key: the Goa 1999 statement is true.
**2004** = first nationwide (all-India) EVM use.

na44b6c2c3f9.s: The Electors' Photo Identity Card (EPIC) was introduced in:
na44b6c2c3f9.x: EPIC was introduced in 1993 and its number stays valid for life despite a change of address; it did not come through the 61st Amendment.
xa: PYQ order: **EVM → photo ID → VVPAT → NOTA** (**UPPSC 2025**).
**Election Laws (Amendment) Act 2021**: **Aadhaar linking** of rolls to stop multiple enrolment.
EVMs were first used in **1982** (**Parur, Kerala**) — before EPIC.

n7fdda51ac60.s: Linking of electoral rolls with Aadhaar to check multiple enrolment was provided by the:
o: Representation of the People Act, 1950 as originally enacted
n7fdda51ac60.x: The Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 provided Aadhaar linking, multiple qualifying dates, gender-neutral wording and requisition of premises.
xa: **2022**: spending limit raised to **₹95 lakh (LS) / ₹40 lakh (Assembly)** for bigger States.
**2025**: **ECINET**, one platform for **40+ apps**; **100% webcasting**; **Special Intensive Revision (SIR)** of rolls.
**Overseas electors**: RP (Amendment) Act **2010**, in force **Feb 2011**.

n9b85de079cf.s: Under the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, the selection panel consists of:
o: The Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Union Home Minister
The Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition
The President, the Prime Minister and the Chief Justice of India
The Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India and the Leader of the Opposition
n9b85de079cf.x: The 2023 Act provides for a panel comprising the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition. The Chief Justice of India was dropped from the panel.
n9b85de079cf.tq: Use the composition trap by identifying the authority omitted from the final arrangement.
xs: The **2023 Act** panel = the **Prime Minister**, a **Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM** and the **Leader of the Opposition** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **CJI was dropped**; a panel of **PM, LoP and CJI** was the **Tarkunde Committee**'s **1975** proposal.
xa: ⚠ **Tarkunde (1975)** panel had the **CJI**; the **2023 Act** dropped the CJI.
Criticism: the Act gives the **executive a majority** on the panel that picks the election referee.
The **Law Commission 255th Report (2015)** proposed a **collegium** for appointing the CEC.

nindian-polity-73-4.s: The nationwide rollout of Electors Photo Identity Cards was initiated in 1993 under CEC:
nindian-polity-73-4.x: The nationwide EPIC rollout began in 1993 under Chief Election Commissioner T.N. Seshan.
n: Electors Photo Identity Cards (EPICs) had their nationwide rollout initiated in 1993. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
The nationwide rollout of EPICs was initiated under Chief Election Commissioner T. N. Seshan. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
xa: EPIC was introduced to prevent **bogus voting** and **impersonation**.
An EPIC number, once issued, is **valid for life**.
PYQ order: **EVM → photo ID → VVPAT → NOTA** (UPPSC 2025).

n147b8bc01c6.s: An M3 EVM control unit can connect up to how many ballot units?
n147b8bc01c6.x: An M3 system can take up to 24 ballot units (384 candidates including NOTA), whereas M2 supports four ballot units and 64 candidates.
xa: EVMs are to show **colour photos** of candidates.
First pilot: **70-Parur, Kerala, 1982**.

n6243d9bfbba.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about VVPAT?
o: The slip is handed over to the voter for personal custody
It prints a slip with the serial number, name and symbol of the selected candidate
The voter can see the printed slip for seven seconds
It is attached to the Electronic Voting Machine
n6243d9bfbba.x: The voter only views the slip through the VVPAT window; it is not handed over.
xa: Generations: **M1, M2, M3** (current).
First used at **51-Noksen, Nagaland, 2013**.

n6bee87787b2.s: What is the principal purpose of a Remote Voting Machine (RVM) prototype?
o: To permit domestic migrants to vote for up to 72 constituencies from one remote polling station
To count postal ballots together with EVM votes
To enable overseas citizens to vote in all constituencies without registration
To conceal booth-wise voting patterns by pooling control units
n6bee87787b2.x: The ECI's RVM prototype is intended to enable domestic migrants to vote for up to 72 constituencies from one remote polling station.
n6bee87787b2.tq: Distinguish remote voting from totaliser-based secrecy of booth results.
xs: The **RVM** lets **domestic migrants** vote for up to **72 constituencies** from one remote polling station — option **(1)**.
Pooling control units to hide booth-wise trends is the **totaliser**, not the RVM.
xa: RVM was demonstrated to parties in **Jan 2023**.
**Overseas electors** were enabled by the RP (Amendment) Act **2010**.

n7ec8b7d2178.s: Which Article is NOT among those the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 proposes to amend?
n7ec8b7d2178.x: The Bill proposes amendments to Articles 83, 172 and 327, not Article 280.
xa: Debate also named **85, 174 and 356**.
**U.U. Lalit** and **Sanjiv Khanna** raised Basic Structure doubts.

n2e5a965ec94.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024?
o: It seeks to synchronise Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections and inserts a new Article 82A
It raises the Lok Sabha ceiling from 550 to 850 and inserts Article 334A
It provides one-third reservation for women and amends Article 330
It extends the delimitation freeze beyond 2026 and amends Article 81
n2e5a965ec94.x: The 129th Amendment Bill (introduced December 2024, referred to a JPC) aims at simultaneous Lok Sabha and Assembly elections (APPSC 2024 key); it inserts Art 82A and amends Arts 83, 172 and 327. Raising the ceiling to 850 was the 131st Amendment Bill, 2026; women's reservation (Art 334A) came via the 106th Amendment; the delimitation freeze was extended by the 84th Amendment.
xs: The **129th Amendment Bill, 2024** seeks to **synchronise Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections** and inserts **Art. 82A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It also amends **Art. 83** (duration of Parliament), **Art. 172** (duration of State Legislatures) and **Art. 327** (Parliament's power over elections).
It does not deal with the Lok Sabha ceiling, women's reservation or the delimitation freeze.
xa: Introduced in the Lok Sabha in **Dec 2024** and referred to a **Joint Parliamentary Committee**.
The JPC was still examining the Bill in **Feb 2026**.
Others named in debate: **Arts. 85, 174 and 356** (dissolution, President's Rule).
Aim of simultaneous elections was the **APPSC 2024** key.

n4d43c7d2230.s: The Election Commission capped the number of electors per polling station at:
n4d43c7d2230.x: The Election Commission capped electors per polling station at 1,200 and delisted 808 RUPPs.
xa: There are over **2,800 RUPPs**, of which only ~**750** contested **2024**.
**Sec. 29A** of RPA 1951 deals with **registration of political parties** with the ECI.
The **Law Commission 255th Report** sought **limited power to deregister** non-compliant parties.

n6b7561ebc16.s: The Communist Party of India formally took shape at which conference?
n6b7561ebc16.x: Although the CPI dates its initial association with M.N. Roy and others at Tashkent in 1920, it was formally established at the Kanpur conference in 1925.
n6b7561ebc16.tq: Separate the preliminary formation at Tashkent from the formal establishment at Kanpur.
xs: The CPI formally took shape at the **Kanpur** conference in **1925** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Tashkent** (**1920**) was where **M.N. Roy** and others first formed it, but the exam year is **1925** (Kanpur).
xa: ⚠ **CPI**: **Tashkent (1920)** vs **Kanpur (1925)**.
The **CPI(M)** broke away from the CPI in **1964**.
The CPI marked its **100th foundation day** on **26 Dec 2025**.
**Puchalapalli Sundarayya** was secretary of the **Andhra Communist Party** (**Kakinada, 1936**).

n7376a011299.s: The Republican Party of India was planned by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and formed
o: during the Constituent Assembly period in 1950
after the formation of the BSP in 1984
n7376a011299.x: The Republican Party of India was planned by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and formed after his death in 1956–57.
n7376a011299.tq: Discriminate between the year of planning and the period of actual formation.
xs: The **Republican Party of India** was planned by **Dr B.R. Ambedkar** and formed **after his death** in **1956-57** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was not formed in his lifetime, and it predates the **BSP** (**1984**).
xa: Exam angle: the party founded by Ambedkar is the **Republican Party of India** (**APPSC-GS 2025**).
The **BSP** was founded by **Kanshi Ram** in **1984**.
**Swatantra Party** (**1959**) was founded by **C. Rajagopalachari**.

n142ee1b4605.s: The Bahujan Samaj Party was founded in 1984 by:
n142ee1b4605.x: Kanshi Ram founded the BSP (1984); Mulayam Singh Yadav founded the Samajwadi Party (1992).
xa: **Akhilesh Yadav** is the **SP chief** (**28 Feb 2026**).
After the **2023** NCP split, **Sharad Pawar and Supriya Sule** lead the **NCP-SP**.
**Jana Sangh**'s first president was **S.P. Mookerjee** (**1951**).

neefcb1f3f6c.s: The YSRCP emerged in 2011 from a split in which party?
neefcb1f3f6c.x: The YSRCP emerged from a Congress split in 2011; the TDP was founded by NTR in 1982.
xa: The TDP took power within **9 months** on "**Telugu atma gauravam**".
**N. Chandrababu Naidu** leads the TDP, now an **NDA** partner.
The **Justice Party** held its first Andhra session at **Pikkavolu** (East Godavari) in **1917**.

nindian-polity-54-4.s: The Communist Party of India was founded in:
nindian-polity-54-4.x: The CPI dates from 1925; the CPI(M) emerged after the 1964 split.
n: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The Communist Party of India was formed in 1925. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The Bharatiya Jana Sangh was formed in 1951. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The Communist Party of India split in 1964. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The 1964 split of the Communist Party of India led to the formation of the Communist Party of India (Marxist). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
xa: ⚠ CPI: **Tashkent** (**1920**) vs **Kanpur** conference (**1925**) — exam year is **1925**.
**CPI(M)** came from the **1964** split of the CPI.
Other dates: **DMK 1949**, **Swatantra 1959**, **BJP 1980**.

naf6b9741b01.s: In 1969, the Indian National Congress split into
naf6b9741b01.x: The Congress split of 1969 produced Congress (Organisation) and Congress (Requisitionists), commonly abbreviated as Congress (O) and Congress (R).
naf6b9741b01.tq: Distinguish the 1969 Congress factions from later factional labels.
xs: In **1969** the INC split into **Congress (O) and Congress (R)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Congress (O)** later joined the **Janata Party** merger of **1977**.
xa: **Congress for Democracy** (**1977**) was formed by **Jagjivan Ram, H.N. Bahuguna, Nandini Satpathy**.
**Congress(S)** joined the **Janata Dal** in **1988**.
The **Kamaraj Plan (1963)** had senior Congress ministers resign to work in the party organisation.

nc21421d6b34.s: Which of the following groups merged to form the Janata Party in 1977?
o: Congress (O), Jana Sangh, BLD and Socialists
Jana Sangh, CPI(M), Congress (S) and Lok Dal
Congress for Democracy, NCP, BLD and Socialists
nc21421d6b34.x: The Janata Party was formed in 1977 through the merger of Congress (O), Jana Sangh, the Bharatiya Lok Dal and the Socialists.
nc21421d6b34.tq: Test merger composition by identifying the correct parent-party set.
xs: The **Janata Party** (**1977**) was formed by merger of **Congress (O), Jana Sangh, BLD and Socialists** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Congress for Democracy** was a separate **1977** breakaway from the INC; the NCP came only in **1999**.
xa: The Janata Party gave the **first non-Congress (and first coalition) government** at the Centre under **Morarji Desai**.
Party-system phase: **1977-89** = transition and first alternation.
The **BJP** was formed in **1980**, with **A.B. Vajpayee** as first president.

nd57c473f27b.s: The Janata Dal was formed on 11 October 1988 through the coming together of
o: Congress(R), Janata Party, CPI and Lok Dal
Jan Morcha, Congress(S), Janata and Lok Dal
Jan Morcha, Congress(O), DMK and Socialists
Congress(O), Jana Sangh, BLD and Socialists
nd57c473f27b.x: The Janata Dal was formed on 11 October 1988 through the merger of Jan Morcha, Congress(S), Janata and Lok Dal.
nd57c473f27b.tq: Combine the exact date with the constituent organisations to avoid a partial merger match.
xs: The **Janata Dal** (**11 Oct 1988**) united **Jan Morcha, Congress(S), Janata and Lok Dal** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Congress (O), Jana Sangh, BLD and Socialists** formed the **Janata Party** in **1977** — a different merger.
xa: **RJD, JD(U), JD(S), BJD** all trace back to the **1988** Janata Dal.
**Lalu Prasad Yadav** leads the **RJD** (**APPSC-GS 2019**).
The **1989** election began the multi-party **coalition era**, lasting until **2014**.

n604ea0a1ea5.s: With reference to the split in the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) in 2023, which one of the following is correct?
o: The Sharad Pawar faction retained the NCP name, and the Ajit Pawar faction formed the NCP-SP
The Ajit Pawar faction retained the NCP name, upheld by the top court, and the Sharad Pawar group formed the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar)
Both factions merged into the Indian National Congress
The Election Commission froze the NCP name and neither faction could use it
n604ea0a1ea5.x: In the 2023 split the Ajit Pawar faction kept the NCP name, which the top court upheld, while Sharad Pawar's group became the NCP-SP (Sharadchandra Pawar). Option A reverses the factions; there was no merger with the INC and the name was not frozen.
n604ea0a1ea5.tq: NCP 1999 from INC; 2023 split: Ajit = NCP, Sharad = NCP-SP.
xs: After the **2023** split the **Ajit Pawar** faction kept the **NCP** name (upheld by the top court); **Sharad Pawar**'s group formed the **NCP-SP** (**Sharadchandra Pawar**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the factions; there was no merger with the INC and the name was not frozen.

n0d4af91705a.s: Political parties were not mentioned in the original Constitution. They entered the constitutional framework through the:

**Defections** are listed among the problems of Indian parties.
Recognition comes under the **Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968**.

nd2e08da442c.s: Who founded the Indian National Congress in 1885?

n5806c6b30c0.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated route for recognition as a State party?

Securing 10 per cent of votes alone
Securing 6 per cent of votes and two Assembly seats
Securing 6 per cent of votes in a Lok Sabha election and one Lok Sabha seat

na461f71bab7.s: The first national party from the North-East is the:

n7fcde3f3617.s: The electoral bond scheme was struck down in which case and on what date?

n28febb0e3a2.x: The TDP rapidly gained power by mobilising the sentiment of “Telugu atma gauravam”, or Telugu self-respect.

n1c350449942.s: N.T. Rama Rao founded the Telugu Desam Party in 1982 on the plank of:
