The **DMK** formed the Tamil Nadu government in **1967**, one of those simultaneous elections.
Regional parties' negatives: **parochialism**, **instability**.

n8bef71a9bdf.s: In coalition politics, regional parties have often acted as ____, supplying Speakers, Union Ministers and survival votes.
n8bef71a9bdf.x: Regional parties have acted as coalition kingmakers, supplying Speakers and Union Ministers and providing votes for government survival.
xa: Positive: **backward-region representation**, **balanced development**.
Negative: **parochialism**, **instability**.
The TDP left the **NDA** in **2018** over **special category status**.

nbc897b30c83.s: Which of the following is the correct list of the six National Parties referred to in the current classification?
o: BJP, INC, CPI, NCP, AITC and AAP
BJP, INC, CPI(M), NCP, AITC and NPP
BJP, INC, DMK, BSP, NPP and AAP
BJP, INC, CPI(M), BSP, NPP and AAP
nbc897b30c83.x: The six listed National Parties are the BJP, INC, CPI(M), BSP, NPP and AAP.
nbc897b30c83.tq: Direct list recall with nearby recognised and derecognised parties as distractors.
xs: The six national parties are **BJP, INC, CPI(M), BSP, NPP and AAP** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**CPI, NCP, AITC** and **DMK** are not in the list; **DMK** and **AITC** are State parties in the IYB list.
xa: All others in the IYB **2026** list — **TDP, YSRCP, JSP, DMK, AITC, BJD, SP, SS, BRS** — are State or unrecognised parties.
The **BSP** was founded in **1984**.
The BJP defeated **AAP** in **Delhi** in **2025**.

ncf1594f401c.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the Telugu Desam Party leads the ruling coalition with the support of the:
ncf1594f401c.x: The TDP leads the ruling coalition in Andhra Pradesh with support from the BJP.
xa: The TDP left the **NDA** in **2018** over **special category status**.
The TDP was founded by **NTR** in **1982** on **Telugu atma gauravam**.
A regional party can hold power alone or **dominate a coalition**.

n6c19077b952.s: The DMK originally demanded which of the following and later formed the Tamil Nadu government in 1967 under C. N. Annadurai?
n6c19077b952.x: The DMK began with anti-Brahmin, anti-North and anti-Hindi positions and demanded Dravidanadu; it later scaled back these demands and formed the Tamil Nadu government in 1967 under Annadurai.
n6c19077b952.tq: Connect the original demand with the party’s later electoral transition.
xs: The DMK originally demanded **Dravidanadu** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its origin was **anti-Brahmin, anti-North, anti-Hindi**; it scaled back and formed the Tamil Nadu government in **1967** under **Annadurai**.
"**Bombay for Maharashtrians**" was the **Shiv Sena**'s slogan, not the DMK's.
xa: The DMK was founded by **C.N. Annadurai** in **1949**.
The **AIADMK** (**M.G. Ramachandran**, **1972**) is the other Tamil Nadu regional party.
APPSC-G2 **2025** keyed order: **DMK, TDP, BSP, SP**.

n8bdaa0754e9.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three statuses through which a political party may be classified?
n8bdaa0754e9.x: The three relevant states are unregistered, registered but unrecognised—commonly referred to as an RUPP—and recognised.
n8bdaa0754e9.tq: Direct classification recall using the legally distinct middle category.
xs: A party is **unregistered**, **registered but unrecognised (RUPP)**, or **recognised** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Registration** comes under **Section 29A, RPA 1951**; **recognition** under the **Symbols Order, 1968**.
**Reserved** and **free** are kinds of **symbols**, not statuses of a party.
xa: Registration: apply within **30 days** of formation.
The party constitution must pledge allegiance to the Constitution and to **socialism, secularism, democracy** and national integrity.
Only about **750 of 2,800+ RUPPs** contested **2024**.

n499494a5a98.s: Which authority is responsible for registration of a political party under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and for recognition under the Symbols Order, respectively?
o: Election Commission of India and Parliament
Election Commission of India and Election Commission of India
President of India and Governor of the concerned State
Ministry of Law and Justice and Election Commission of India
n499494a5a98.x: The Election Commission handles both processes: registration under Section 29A of the RPA, 1951, and recognition under the Election Symbols Order, 1968.
n499494a5a98.tq: Compare the two legal steps while keeping the authority constant.
xs: The **Election Commission of India** does both: it registers and it recognises — so option **(2)** is correct.

**Registration** is under **Section 29A, RPA 1951**; **recognition** (National/State) is under the **Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968** — the authority for both is the **ECI**.
**Parliament**, the **President**, the **Governor** and the **Ministry of Law** play no part in either step.
xa: The **1968 Order** is a **statutory order of the ECI** under **RPA 1951** and **Article 324**.
In recognition and symbol disputes the ECI acts as a **court**.
Three states of a party: **Unregistered** → **registered but unrecognised (RUPP)** → **recognised**.

n84f07111bd1.s: In a dispute between factions of a recognised political party over its name and election symbol, the Election Commission acts under which provision and applies which test?
o: Paragraph 15 and the Sadiq Ali majority test
n84f07111bd1.x: Paragraph 15 deals with split disputes. The ECI applies the Sadiq Ali test, principally examining the majority support of the rival factions.
n84f07111bd1.tq: Pair the correct paragraph with the correct judicially developed test.
xs: Split disputes go under **Paragraph 15**, using the **Sadiq Ali (1971)** majority test — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Para 6B** is the **National party** criteria; **Section 29A** is **registration**; **Para 16A** is about the **Model Code of Conduct**.
xa: In such disputes the ECI acts as a **court**.
Current relevance: **Trinamool rebel MPs** chose a **merger** over a Para 15 claim.
Criticism: **long factional litigation** over symbols.

n06c67b7c6b2.s: Under paragraph 16A of the Election Symbols Order, the Election Commission may suspend or withdraw recognition of a party for:
o: Using a free symbol in another State
Failing to win a Lok Sabha seat in every election
Defying the Model Code of Conduct
Changing the party constitution after registration
n06c67b7c6b2.x: Paragraph 16A empowers the ECI to suspend or withdraw recognition for defiance of the Model Code of Conduct.
n06c67b7c6b2.tq: Identify the specific regulatory ground instead of a general electoral failure.
xs: Under **Para 16A**, the ECI may **suspend or withdraw recognition** for **defying the Model Code of Conduct** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is a power over **recognition**, not about free symbols, seat wins or constitution changes.
xa: **Para 15**: split disputes, **Sadiq Ali (1971)** test.
**Deregistration** is limited (**INC v Institute of Social Welfare, 2002**): fraud, ceasing allegiance, unlawful declaration.
The **1968 Order** is a statutory order under **RPA 1951** and **Article 324**.

n942786d4ac2.s: Under Section 29A, a party's constitution must pledge allegiance to the Constitution and to:
n942786d4ac2.x: It must pledge allegiance to the Constitution and to socialism, secularism, democracy and national integrity; a reserved symbol comes only with recognition.
xa: Common symbol for RUPPs: if they contest **2 Lok Sabha seats** or **5% of Assembly seats**.
Latest free symbols list: **May 2025 - 184 symbols**.
Recognition is a separate step under the **Election Symbols Order, 1968**.

n7554468f756.s: Under the Election Symbols Order, 1968, free symbols are meant for:
n7554468f756.x: Reserved symbols go only to recognised parties; free symbols are for registered unrecognised parties and independents.
xa: Latest free list: **May 2025 - 184 symbols**.
**Common symbol** for RUPPs if they contest **2 Lok Sabha seats or 5% of Assembly seats**.
Symbol disputes between factions: **Para 15**, **Sadiq Ali (1971)** test.

nindian-polity-53-42.s: Under one route to National Party status, a party must win 2% of Lok Sabha seats (11 seats) from at least ____ States.
nindian-polity-53-42.x: The MPs must come from at least three States, not four.
n: A political party can satisfy an alternative National Party criterion by winning at least 2% of the total seats in the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The 2%-of-Lok-Sabha-seats National Party criterion equals 11 seats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
Members elected under the 2%-of-Lok-Sabha-seats criterion must come from at least three different States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
xa: Other routes: **State party in four or more States**; or **6%** votes in **four States** + **4 Lok Sabha seats**.
Distractors like "**2 or more States**" or "**4% / 10% / 15%**" of votes are wrong.

nindian-polity-54-16.s: Under Route 2, which combination is specified as mandatory for national party recognition?
o: At least 4% votes in four States and four Lok Sabha seats
At least 6% votes in two States and six Lok Sabha seats
At least 6% votes in four States and four Lok Sabha seats
At least 10% votes in two States and two Lok Sabha seats
nindian-polity-54-16.x: Under the second route to national-party status, a party needs both 6% of votes in four States and four Lok Sabha seats.
n: The National Party recognition route mentioned in the notes requires at least 6% of votes in four states. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The National Party recognition route mentioned in the notes requires four Lok Sabha seats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
The two National Party recognition conditions under Route 2 are both mandatory. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 144-146]
xs: Under **Route 2**, a party needs **6%** votes in **four States** and **four Lok Sabha seats** — option **(3)**.
Both conditions under Route 2 are **mandatory**.
xa: Route 3: **2%** of Lok Sabha seats (**11 of 543**) from **three** States.
AAP got national status in **2023**; **CPI, NCP and AITC** derecognised.
**NPP** = first **North-East** national party.

nb6adc8019f4.s: One route to State-party recognition is at least 6% of valid votes in the Assembly election plus ____ Assembly seats.
nb6adc8019f4.x: The route is 6% plus 2 Assembly seats (or 6% in the Lok Sabha poll plus 1 Lok Sabha seat); '6% + 4 Lok Sabha seats' belongs to the National-party criterion.
xa: Other State routes: **3% of Assembly seats or 3 seats**, whichever is more; **1 Lok Sabha seat for every 25** allotted.
**8%** of valid votes in the State — **no seat needed**; the route candidates forget.
A party qualifies through **any one** route.

n4ec63fb7321.s: Under the seat-based route, a party becomes a State Party by winning one Lok Sabha seat for every ____ seats allotted to the State.
n4ec63fb7321.x: A party qualifies by winning one Lok Sabha seat for every 25 seats allotted to the State.
xa: **6%** Lok Sabha votes **+ 1 Lok Sabha seat** from the State is another route.
**3% of Assembly seats or 3 seats**, whichever is more.
**8%** of valid votes in the State, **no seat needed** — added later.

n883a08b76a7.s: For State-party recognition, the 8% valid-vote route requires the party to win:
n883a08b76a7.x: The 8% route requires no seat; any one of the prescribed routes suffices.
xa: The **8% route** was added later; candidates forget it.
Seat-linked vote routes: **6% + 2 Assembly seats**; **6% + 1 Lok Sabha seat**.
**1 Lok Sabha seat for every 25** allotted to the State.

n4136e099569.s: Which one of the following changes was associated with the Election Commission's April 2023 review of National Party status?
o: DMK, RSP and AIFB were recognised as National Parties
CPI, NCP and AITC were derecognised and AAP was recognised
BSP, NPP and AAP were derecognised and CPI was recognised
INC and BJP were derecognised and AAP was recognised
n4136e099569.x: The April 2023 review derecognised CPI, NCP and AITC and recognised AAP as a National Party.
n4136e099569.tq: Use the date and separate recognition from derecognition.
xs: The **April 2023** review **derecognised CPI, NCP and AITC** and **recognised AAP** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**DMK, RSP and AIFB** are not National parties; **INC** and **BJP** were not derecognised.
xa: AAP got national status in **2023**.
In **May 2020** there were **eight** national parties.
**NPP (Meghalaya)** was the **first North-East party** with national status.
⚠ The ECI reviews status after each general election — always quote the list with a date.

na738564c62e.s: Which party was the first party from the North-Eastern region to obtain National Party status?
na738564c62e.x: The National People's Party (NPP), based in Meghalaya, was the first North-Eastern party to obtain National Party status.
na738564c62e.tq: Direct identity recall based on region and status.
xs: The **NPP (Meghalaya)** was the **first North-East party** with national status — so option **(4)** is correct.
**AAP** won national status in **2023**; **AITC** lost it in the **April 2023** review.
xa: April 2023: **CPI, NCP and AITC** derecognised; **AAP** recognised.
**Eight** national parties as of **May 2020** (APPSC 2019 key).
National status needs any one of: **State party in 4 States**, **6% in 4 States + 4 LS seats**, or **2% LS seats from 3 States**.

nbac5ee225d9.s: Which of the following combinations consists entirely of parties that are not National Parties?
o: DMK, Revolutionary Socialist Party, All India Forward Bloc and Peasants and Workers Party
nbac5ee225d9.x: DMK, Revolutionary Socialist Party, All India Forward Bloc and Peasants and Workers Party are not National Parties in the classification referred to here.
nbac5ee225d9.tq: Separate the complete non-National group from the recognised list.
xs: **DMK, Revolutionary Socialist Party, All India Forward Bloc and Peasants and Workers Party** are not National parties — so option **(3)** is correct (**APPSC 2018**).
**NPP** and **AAP** hold national status; **BJP** and **INC** are national parties.
xa: **AAP** was recognised in **April 2023**; **CPI, NCP, AITC** were derecognised then.
**NPP** = first **North-East** national party.
AP angle: **TDP** and **YSRCP** are recognised **State parties**; neither is National.

n30dee88ff8b.s: Which of the following is an additional benefit available to recognised political parties?
o: Automatic recognition as a National Party
Exclusive use of every free symbol in the State
Automatic exemption from all election expenditure limits
Two free sets of electoral rolls and broadcast or telecast time on Akashvani and Doordarshan
n30dee88ff8b.x: Recognised parties receive two free sets of electoral rolls, broadcast or telecast time on Akashvani and Doordarshan, and consultation by the ECI.
n30dee88ff8b.tq: Separate concrete institutional benefits from powers not conferred by recognition.
xs: Recognised parties get **two free sets of electoral rolls** and **broadcast/telecast time on Akashvani and Doordarshan** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Recognition does not make a party **National** automatically, and **free symbols** are for RUPPs and independents.
xa: Also: **consultation by the ECI**.
Nomination needs **one** proposer instead of **ten**.
Up to **40** star campaigners vs **20** for an RUPP.

n9ba2b46549d.s: The Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968 is best described as:
o: An Act of Parliament dealing exclusively with National Parties
An executive notification issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs
A constitutional provision contained in the Election Commission chapter
A statutory order of the Election Commission issued under the RPA, 1951 and Article 324
n9ba2b46549d.x: The 1968 Order is a statutory order of the Election Commission under the RPA, 1951 and Article 324. It is neither an Act of Parliament nor a constitutional provision.
n9ba2b46549d.tq: Use the legal-status distinction to reject the familiar but incorrect labels.
xs: The 1968 Order is a **statutory order of the Election Commission** issued under the **RPA, 1951** and **Article 324** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is **not an Act of Parliament** and **not a constitutional provision**.
It is the ECI's own order, not a notification of the **Ministry of Home Affairs**, and it covers both National and State parties.
xa: **Para 15** of the Order: the ECI decides split disputes using the **Sadiq Ali (1971)** majority test.
**Para 16A**: the ECI may **suspend or withdraw recognition** for defying the **Model Code of Conduct**.
**Para 6B** lays down the **National party** criteria.

n3435cb4149e.s: Which one of the following is NOT a valid criterion for recognition as a National Party under paragraph 6B of the Symbols Order?
o: Recognition as a State party in four or more States
At least 2% of Lok Sabha seats, won from not fewer than three States
At least 6% of valid votes in four or more States and four Lok Sabha seats
At least 15% of valid votes in two States, without any Lok Sabha seat
n3435cb4149e.x: The 15%-in-two-States route is not a National Party criterion. The valid alternatives are the four-State recognition route, the 6% plus four-seat route, and the 2% Lok Sabha-seat route.
n3435cb4149e.tq: Find the one percentage-and-seat combination absent from the recognised alternatives.
xs: **15% of valid votes in two States without any seat** is not a criterion — so option **(4)** is correct.
The three valid routes: **State party in four or more States**; **6% votes in four States + 4 Lok Sabha seats**; **2% of Lok Sabha seats** from **three States**.
The notes flag "**2 or more States**" and "**4% / 10% / 15%** of votes" as standard wrong distractors.
xa: **2%** of Lok Sabha seats = **11 of 543**.
⚠ The vote-only (no seat) route — **8%** of valid votes — exists only for a **State party**, not a National party.
**APPSC-G2 2025**: all listed conditions were valid, so the key was "**None of the above**".

n10ced97f45b.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the TDP and the YSRCP are both:
n10ced97f45b.x: TDP and YSRCP are recognised State Parties in Andhra Pradesh; neither has National Party status.
xa: National status needs, e.g., recognition as a **State party in four or more States**.
State routes include **6% votes + 2 Assembly seats** and **8% votes with no seat**.
**NPP** was the **first North-East party** with national status.

ndd0511a3791.s: On the Lee Commission's recommendation, a Public Service Commission was first set up in India on:
ndd0511a3791.x: The Lee Commission recommended it in 1924 and it was set up on 1 October 1926; the Federal PSC became the UPSC on 26 January 1950.
xa: First chairman of the 1926 PSC: **Sir Ross Barker**.
Members continued into UPSC under **Art. 378**.
Simultaneous **ICS** exams in India from **1922** (**Montagu-Chelmsford**).

nc4c5de12666.s: The headquarters of the Union Public Service Commission is located at:
nc4c5de12666.x: The headquarters of the UPSC is Dholpur House in New Delhi.
nc4c5de12666.tq: Test the exact location, not merely the city.
xs: The UPSC is headquartered at **Dholpur House, New Delhi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is the **central recruiting agency** and an **independent constitutional body**.
xa: First chairman of the PSC (**1 Oct 1926**): **Sir Ross Barker**.
The Federal PSC became UPSC on **26 Jan 1950**.
Provisions: **Articles 315-323**, **Part XIV**.

n55032f48d4c.s: Who was the first Chairman of the Public Service Commission set up in India on 1 October 1926?
n55032f48d4c.x: Sir Ross Barker was the first Chairman of the Public Service Commission set up on 1 October 1926 on the Lee Commission's advice. Satyendranath Tagore was the first Indian to clear the ICS (1864). Lord Lee headed the 1924 Commission that recommended the PSC but did not chair it. Sir Samuel Hoare was not its chairman.
n55032f48d4c.tq: 1926 PSC: Lee recommended, Ross Barker chaired.
xs: **Sir Ross Barker** was the first chairman of the PSC set up on **1 Oct 1926** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Satyendranath Tagore** was the first Indian to clear the ICS (**1864**).
The **Lee Commission** (**1924**) only recommended the PSC.
xa: **GoI Act 1919** first provided for a PSC.
**GoI Act 1935**: **Federal PSC** + provincial PSCs.
UPSC HQ: **Dholpur House, New Delhi**.

n2593cf120df.s: The report of a Joint State Public Service Commission is laid before each concerned State Legislature by the:
n2593cf120df.x: A JSPSC reports to each concerned Governor, who lays the report before the relevant State Legislature.
xa: UPSC → **President** → **both Houses**.
SPSC → **Governor** → **State Legislature**.
JSPSC members **resign to the President**.

n2eb2b1ab942.s: Which one of the following functions is performed by the Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission in addition to recruitment to State services?
o: Conducting examinations for the lower judicial service
Auditing the accounts of the State Government
Appointing judges of the High Court
n2eb2b1ab942.x: The APPSC conducts recruitment examinations for State services and examinations for the lower judicial service under Article 234.
n2eb2b1ab942.tq: Distinguish a recruitment function from constitutional appointments and auditing.
xs: APPSC also conducts **lower judicial service examinations** (**Art. 234**) — option **(1)**.
Audit, appointing High Court judges and local-body elections are not PSC functions.
xa: Main function: **State service recruitment**.
APPSC is an **SPSC** under **Art. 315**.
SPSC = "**watchdog of the merit system**".

nindian-polity-52-12.s: The Lokpal Selection Committee is chaired by the:
nindian-polity-52-12.x: The Prime Minister chairs the Lokpal Selection Committee; the President appoints the UPSC Chairman and the Governor the SPSC Chairman.
n: The President of India appoints the UPSC Chairperson under Article 315. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 137-141]
The Governor of the State appoints the State Public Service Commission Chairperson. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 137-141]
The President of India appoints the Finance Commission Chairperson under Article 280. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 137-141]
The Prime Minister is the Chairperson of the Lokpal Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 137-141]
xa: ⚠ SPSC chairman: **Governor appoints, President removes**.
FC qualifications: **Finance Commission Act, 1951**.
UPSC removal for **misbehaviour** needs a **Supreme Court** inquiry (**Article 317**).

nf94dc3e274c.s: Under Article 320, the Union Public Service Commission conducts examinations primarily for appointment to
o: only Group B and Group C posts
nf94dc3e274c.x: UPSC conducts examinations for appointment to All-India services, Central services and Group-A services. Group B and C posts and the highest diplomatic posts are outside the stated purview.
nf94dc3e274c.tq: Distinguish the principal examination mandate from categories expressly excluded from consultation.
xs: UPSC conducts exams for **All-India, Central and Group-A services** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Group B/C posts** and the **highest diplomatic posts** are outside UPSC's purview; State services are for the **SPSC**.
xa: Consulted on **methods of recruitment**, **promotion and transfer**, **suitability of candidates**.
Consulted on **disciplinary matters** and temporary appointments of **more than one year**.
Functions are in **Art. 320**.

na4ef2d55a3f.s: The strength of the UPSC and of a State PSC is determined, respectively, by the:
na4ef2d55a3f.x: The Constitution does not fix the strength; the President decides it for the UPSC and the Governor for an SPSC.
xa: **Half** the members must have held government office for at least **10 years**.
**Acting Chairman** is appointed by the President when the Chairman's post is vacant.
UPSC term: **6 years or age 65**; SPSC: **6 years or age 62**.

n35b3653a69a.s: A member of a State Public Service Commission addresses the resignation to the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
n35b3653a69a.x: An SPSC member resigns to the Governor; UPSC and JSPSC members resign to the President. Removal is only by the President.
xa: ⚠ "Governor appoints, President removes" is the favourite trap (**APPSC 2019**).
For misbehaviour, the SC's advice is **binding**.
SPSC term: **6 years or age 62**.

n7491ce24878.s: The Chairman of a State Public Service Commission is appointed by ______ and can be removed by ______.
n7491ce24878.x: The Chairman of an SPSC is appointed by the Governor but can be removed only by the President, a favourite exam trap (APPSC 2019).
xs: SPSC Chairman: appointed by **the Governor**, removed by **the President** — option **(4)**.
**APPSC 2019** asked exactly this; it is the favourite trap.
xa: SPSC members **resign to the Governor**.
Term: **6 years or age 62**.
Removal grounds under **Art. 317**: insolvency, outside paid employment, infirmity, misbehaviour (via **Supreme Court**).

n117b5a028cd.s: A constitutional requirement relating to the background of members of a Public Service Commission is that
o: all members must have held office under the Union Government
at least one-fourth of the members must have served in Parliament
at least half the members must have held government office for at least ten years
all members must have served in the judiciary for ten years
n117b5a028cd.x: At least half of the members must have held office under the Government of India or a State Government for a minimum of ten years.
n117b5a028cd.tq: Watch the quantifier and the alternative government levels in a composition requirement.
xs: **At least half** the members must have held office under **GoI/State Govt** for **at least 10 years** — so option **(3)** is correct.
No rule requires all members to be Union officers, MPs or judges.
xa: Strength is **not fixed by the Constitution**; UPSC usually **9-11** members.
**Acting Chairman** is appointed by the **President**.
**No second term** in the same office.

n107869a4a10.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about removal of members of Public Service Commissions?
o: Misbehaviour can be established by the President without referring the matter to the Supreme Court
Insolvency is a ground for removal
Paid employment outside the duties of office is a ground for removal
Infirmity of mind or body is a ground for removal
n107869a4a10.x: In a case of misbehaviour, the President must first refer the matter to the Supreme Court.
xa: Removal only if the SC upholds the cause; its advice is **binding**.
President (Governor for SPSC) may **suspend** the member during the inquiry.

nf8a40a3676c.s: Which of the following is included within the meaning of misbehaviour for the purpose of Article 317?
o: Failure to secure unanimous decisions in the Commission
Refusal to accept a temporary appointment
Disagreement with a recommendation of the Commission
Being interested in a government contract or sharing in its profit
nf8a40a3676c.x: Misbehaviour includes being interested in a government contract or sharing in its profit under Article 317(4).
nf8a40a3676c.tq: Discriminate the specific statutory example from general administrative disagreements.
xs: Misbehaviour includes **being interested in a government contract or sharing in its profit** — option **(4)**, under **Art. 317(4)**.
Misbehaviour is proved only after reference to the **Supreme Court**.
xa: Other grounds: **insolvency**, **paid outside employment**, **infirmity of mind or body**.
The SC's advice is **binding**.
The member may be **suspended** during the SC inquiry.

n5fc83360e90.s: In the case of alleged misbehaviour by a member of a Public Service Commission, which procedure is constitutionally required?
o: The Governor conducts the inquiry and gives the final decision in every case
The Union Cabinet conducts the inquiry and recommends removal to the concerned Commission
The President refers the matter to the Supreme Court, and removal follows only if the Court upholds the charge
Parliament must pass an impeachment resolution by special majority
n5fc83360e90.x: For misbehaviour, the President refers the matter to the Supreme Court. The member may be removed only when the Supreme Court upholds the cause, and its advice is binding.
n5fc83360e90.tq: Follow the constitutional sequence: reference, judicial examination and binding outcome.
xs: The **President refers** the matter to the **Supreme Court**, and removal follows **only if the Court upholds** it — option **(3)**.
The SC's advice is **binding**; there is no **impeachment** or Cabinet/Governor inquiry.
xa: President (Governor for SPSC) may **suspend** the member during the inquiry.
Misbehaviour includes interest in a **government contract** (**Art. 317(4)**).
Even SPSC members are **removed by the President**, not the Governor.

n734a647956b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about a Joint State Public Service Commission?
o: A member submits resignation to the concerned Governor
Their service conditions and number are fixed by the President
Its Chairman and members are appointed by the President
The term is six years or until the age of 62, whichever is earlier
n734a647956b.x: A member of a Joint Commission resigns to the President, not to the Governor.
xa: Created by an **Act of Parliament** on request of **two or more state legislatures** — **statutory** body.
Report goes to **each concerned Governor**.
Example: **Punjab and Haryana** after **1966**.

n116a998f1ab.s: Which one of the following is NOT permissible for a member of a State Public Service Commission after ceasing to hold office?
o: Becoming Chairman of the same or another State Public Service Commission
Accepting any other employment under the Government of India
Becoming a member of the UPSC
n116a998f1ab.x: A former SPSC member may become UPSC Chairman or member, or Chairman of the same or another SPSC, but cannot accept any other government employment.
n116a998f1ab.tq: Use the post-office bar to eliminate the broadly worded employment option.
xs: An ex-SPSC member **cannot take any other employment under the Government of India** — so option **(2)** is the answer.
He may become **chairman/member of UPSC** or **chairman of that/another SPSC** (**Art. 319**).
xa: **UPSC Chairman**: no further employment under GOI or any State.
**UPSC member**: may become **UPSC Chairman** or **SPSC Chairman**, nothing else.
⚠ An SPSC member may become **UPSC member**; a UPSC member may not become an SPSC member.

n82cebf74fd6.s: Which of the following is ordinarily subject to consultation with the UPSC?
o: Temporary appointments for more than one year
Temporary appointments for less than one year
Group B and Group C posts
Claims of SCs and STs to services and posts
n82cebf74fd6.x: Temporary appointments exceeding one year are ordinarily subject to consultation; the other three are excluded.
xa: Also excluded: **reservations** of posts and the **highest diplomatic posts**.
Consulted on **disciplinary matters**: censure, withholding increments, demotion, compulsory retirement, removal.
Consulted on **extension of service/re-employment**.

n5313ec5d2b7.s: Which one of the following is outside the principal concern of a State Public Service Commission?
o: Classification, pay and training of government employees
Advice on promotion and transfer principles
n5313ec5d2b7.x: An SPSC is not concerned with classification, pay or training. Its principal concerns include recruitment, promotion, transfer and candidate suitability.
n5313ec5d2b7.tq: Identify the administrative personnel subjects expressly placed outside the Commission's concern.
xs: PSCs are **not concerned with classification, pay or training** — option **(3)** is the answer.
**Recruitment**, **suitability** of candidates and **promotion and transfer** principles are core consultation matters.
xa: Excluded: **reservations**, temporary appointments of **less than a year**.
Functions extendable only by an **Act** (**Art. 321**).
Advice is **advisory**, consultation **directory, not mandatory**.

n9b4d2b9d3dc.s: The provisions on Public Service Commissions (Articles 315-323) are in Part ____ of the Constitution.
n9b4d2b9d3dc.x: Articles 315-323 are in Part XIV; the UPSC is a constitutional body, not a statutory one.
xa: UPSC is the **central recruiting agency**.
JSPSC is created by an **Act of Parliament** on request of **two or more state legislatures**.
The Federal PSC became UPSC on **26 Jan 1950**.

nbd9d09173c7.s: Under Article 321, the functions of the UPSC can be extended by:
o: An executive order of the President
A resolution of the Rajya Sabha
nbd9d09173c7.x: Functions are extended only by an Act of Parliament (State Legislature for an SPSC), which may cover local bodies, corporate bodies and public institutions.
xa: Posts may be **excluded** by **regulations**, laid before Parliament for **14 days**.
Advice is only **advisory**.
**Art. 322**: expenses on the **Consolidated Fund**.

n824c6eae955.s: Regulations excluding posts from consultation with a Public Service Commission must be laid before the legislature for at least:
n824c6eae955.x: The President (Governor for an SPSC) may exclude posts by regulations, which are laid for 14 days, not 30.
xa: Functions are **extendable** only by an **Act** (**Art. 321**).
Excluded anyway: **reservations**, temporary appointments of **less than a year**, **Group B/C** posts.
PSCs are not concerned with **classification, pay or training**.

n44e59058f0b.s: The State Public Service Commission is commonly described as the watchdog of the
n44e59058f0b.x: The SPSC is described as the watchdog of the merit system in public services.
n44e59058f0b.tq: Recall the distinctive institutional description without confusing it with financial or electoral oversight.
xs: The SPSC is the "**watchdog of the merit system**" — option **(4)**.
It guards merit-based **recruitment**, **promotion and transfer** in State services.
xa: SC in **TNPSC v A. Balasubramaniam (1994)**: PSC **independence** is essential to fair administration.
Current concern: **crisis of trust** in State PSCs — **paper leaks**, flawed evaluation, delays, litigation.
SPSC: **Governor appoints**, **President removes**.

nf931399f032.s: Which authority must approve every case in which the advice of the UPSC is not accepted?
o: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet
The Union Public Service Commission itself
nf931399f032.x: Every case of non-acceptance of UPSC advice must be approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet; an individual ministry cannot reject the advice on its own.
nf931399f032.tq: Ask which authority would perform the specific approval function.
xs: The **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet** must approve every non-acceptance — option **(3)**.
A **ministry cannot reject** UPSC advice on its own.
xa: Non-accepted cases are listed in a **memorandum** laid before **both Houses**.
Advice is **advisory**; consultation **directory, not mandatory**.
Reports: **Art. 323**.

n8ec345d861e.s: The annual report of a State Public Service Commission is submitted to the:
n8ec345d861e.x: An SPSC reports to the Governor, who lays it before the State Legislature; the UPSC reports to the President.
xa: **JSPSC** → **each concerned Governor** → his Legislature.
Non-acceptance needs the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet**.
Provision: **Art. 323**.

nd4625da9a21.s: A Joint State Public Service Commission can be established only when which of the following conditions is fulfilled?
o: The Governors of two or more States issue a joint notification.
The Parliament passes an Act on the request of two or more State Legislatures.
The President issues an executive order on his own initiative.
The UPSC recommends its establishment to the Union Cabinet.
nd4625da9a21.x: A Joint State Public Service Commission is created by an Act of Parliament following a request from the legislatures of two or more States.
nd4625da9a21.tq: Ask which authority performs the job and identify the required initiating condition.
xs: A JSPSC is created by an **Act of Parliament** on request of **two or more State Legislatures** — option **(2)**.
It is a **statutory**, not constitutional, body.
xa: Chairman and members are **appointed, suspended and removed by the President**.
Term: **6 years or 62**.
Example: **Punjab and Haryana**, briefly after **1966**.

n6f6fa187634.s: The APPSC came into existence on 1 November 1956 by merging the Andhra PSC (1953) with the ____ PSC.
n6f6fa187634.x: APPSC merged the Andhra PSC (1953) with the Hyderabad PSC; after 2014 it continues for residuary AP, while Telangana got the TSPSC.
xa: APPSC chairman/members are appointed by the **Governor**; removed by the **President**.
Term: **6 years** / age **62**.
APPSC also holds lower judicial service exams (**Art. 234**).

n81e9167a97d.s: The ICS examinations began to be held simultaneously in India from 1922 in the context of the:
n81e9167a97d.x: ICS examinations began to be held simultaneously in India from 1922 in the context of the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms.
n81e9167a97d.tq: Link the date with the reform framework rather than the later statutory Act.
xs: Simultaneous ICS exams in India began in **1922** under the **Montagu-Chelmsford** reforms — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Lee Commission** (**1924**) recommended a PSC; the **GoI Act 1935** created the **Federal PSC** — neither started simultaneous exams.
xa: The simultaneous exams were held at **Allahabad**.
**Satyendranath Tagore** was the first Indian to clear the ICS (**1864**).
**GoI Act 1919** first provided for a Public Service Commission.

n9f02d4d3158.s: Under Article 281, the President is required to place before each House of Parliament:
o: Only the report of the Comptroller and Auditor General
The recommendations along with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken
The recommendations after approval by the Supreme Court
n9f02d4d3158.x: Article 281 requires the President to lay the Finance Commission’s recommendations together with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken before each House of Parliament.
n9f02d4d3158.tq: Test the constitutional procedure and watch for the omission of the explanatory memorandum.
xs: Under **Art. 281**, the President lays **the recommendations along with an explanatory memorandum on action taken** before **each House of Parliament** — option **(3)**.
No role for the **CAG** or **Supreme Court** here.
xa: Recommendations are **advisory, not binding**.
**P.V. Rajamannar** (**4th FC**): should not be rejected without very compelling reasons.
**16th FC** report was tabled in Parliament on **1 Feb 2026**.

nfe31c23eeb7.s: The recommendations of the Finance Commission are generally:
o: Judicial orders enforceable without further governmental action
Legally binding in every respect on the Union Government
Binding only on State Governments and never considered by the Union
Advisory and not binding, though they are ordinarily not rejected without compelling reasons
nfe31c23eeb7.x: Finance Commission recommendations are not legally binding. However, the Rajamannar view emphasises that they should not ordinarily be rejected without compelling reasons.
nfe31c23eeb7.tq: Distinguish constitutional recommendation from binding adjudication and note the convention of reasoned acceptance.
xs: FC recommendations are **advisory and not binding**, but not to be rejected **without compelling reasons** — option **(4)**.
This is the view of **P.V. Rajamannar** (**4th FC**).
xa: The President lays them with an **explanatory memorandum** before **each House** (**Art. 281**).
**16th FC** devolution was **accepted** by the Centre in the **Budget 2026-27** speech.
**14th FC** report: accepted on **24 Feb 2015**.

nindian-polity-52-14.s: The first Chairman of the Finance Commission was:
nindian-polity-52-14.x: K.C. Neogy was the first Chairman of the Finance Commission (1951). Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar and Ambedkar were Constituent Assembly figures.
nindian-polity-52-14.tq: Recall the first Finance Commission chairman.
n: K.C. Neogy was the first Finance Commission Chairperson. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 137-141]
xs: The first FC Chairman was **K.C. Neogy** — option **(1)** is correct.
The first FC was set up on **6 April 1952** (**1952 to 1957**).
xa: **P.V. Rajamannar** (4th FC): recommendations should not be rejected without very compelling reasons.
**14th FC** raised the vertical share to **42%** (from **32%**).

n2f30372e163.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the qualifications of Finance Commission members under the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951?
o: The Chairman should have experience in public affairs
One member should have special knowledge of government finance and accounts
One member should be a High Court judge or qualified to be one
One member must be an expert in monetary policy operations
n2f30372e163.x: The Act names no expert in monetary policy operations; the other members are experts in government finance and accounts, financial matters and administration, and economics.
xa: Members are **eligible for reappointment**.
Recommendations are **advisory, not binding**.

nfa3df5d9730.s: The memorandum submitted by Andhra Pradesh in connection with horizontal devolution sought, among other things, criteria for which of the following?
o: Exclusion of infrastructure expenditure from Finance Commission consideration
Abolition of horizontal devolution among States
Capital-city and infrastructure costs arising from post-bifurcation imbalances
Only coastal protection costs unrelated to bifurcation
nfa3df5d9730.x: Andhra Pradesh sought higher vertical devolution and criteria addressing capital-city and infrastructure costs resulting from post-bifurcation imbalances.
nfa3df5d9730.tq: Identify the specific post-bifurcation demand rather than a general fiscal claim.
xs: AP sought criteria for **capital-city and infrastructure costs** from **post-bifurcation imbalances** — option **(3)**.
It also sought **higher vertical devolution** (**Feb 2026**).
xa: **Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam** eligible for up to **₹5,000 crore each** for wastewater.
Special Category Status: promised in **2014**, not in the AP Reorganisation Act.

n7d4b3be57a1.s: The award period of the 15th Finance Commission was:
n7d4b3be57a1.x: The 15th FC gave a first report for 2020-21 and a main report for 2021-26. '2020-25' is the trap figure that appears in some sources. 2015-20 was the 14th FC's period and 2026-31 is the 16th FC's. The 15th FC cut the share to 41% because of J&K's change of status.
xs: The 15th FC covered **2020-21 (first report) and 2021-26** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **2020-25** is a trap figure in APP notes; **2015-20** is the **14th FC**; **2026-31** is the **16th FC**.
xa: 15th FC constituted in **Nov 2017**.
It used **2011** population.
It cut the vertical share to **41%**.

n4ce8f01657f.s: The 15th Finance Commission was the first Finance Commission to:
o: cut the States' vertical share from 42 per cent to 41 per cent
recommend a 50 per cent share to the States
n4ce8f01657f.x: The 15th Finance Commission was the first to reduce the vertical share from 42 per cent to 41 per cent, largely in the context of the change in Jammu and Kashmir's status.
n4ce8f01657f.tq: Test a first-in-series fact against nearby but unsupported reforms.
xs: The **15th FC** was the **first to cut** the vertical share, **42 to 41%** — option **(1)**.
The cut reflected **J&K's change of status**.
xa: **14th FC**: largest increase ever (**32 → 42%**).
**16th FC**: first to use **Contribution to GDP** (**10%**).
15th FC added **demographic performance** and **tax effort**.

n3e3721b28ac.s: Which criteria were newly added by the 15th Finance Commission?
o: Contribution to GDP and forest cover
n3e3721b28ac.x: The 15th Finance Commission added demographic performance and tax effort as new criteria.
xa: 15th FC weights: demographic performance **12.5**, tax and fiscal effort **2.5**.
15th FC was the **first to cut** the vertical share (**42 to 41%**), due to **J&K's change of status**.
16th FC **dropped** tax and fiscal effort.

nd512330ee5e.s: Which criterion received the highest weight under the 16th Finance Commission’s award for 2026–31?
nd512330ee5e.x: Income distance received the highest weight under the 16th Finance Commission, at 42.5%.
nd512330ee5e.tq: Compare the largest weights rather than relying on the presence of a new criterion.
xs: **Income distance** has the highest weight, **42.5** — option **(3)**.
Population (2011) is **17.5**; **Contribution to GDP** and **forest and ecology** are **10** each.
xa: Income distance under the **15th FC** was **45**.
Area fell from **15** to **10**.
**Tax and fiscal effort** was **dropped**.

nbe3bb4fb847.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the devolution criteria of the 15th and 16th Finance Commissions?
o: The weight for area declined from 15% to 10%
The 16th Finance Commission retained tax and fiscal effort as a criterion
The weight for forest and ecology remained at 10% under both
The weight for demographic performance was reduced from 12.5% to 10%
nbe3bb4fb847.x: The 16th Finance Commission dropped tax and fiscal effort as a criterion; the other three changes are correct.
xa: **Income distance**: **45 → 42.5**.
New: **Contribution to GDP**, **10%**.

o: A Chairman and four members appointed by the President
A Chairman and three members appointed by Parliament
A Chairman and four members appointed by the Prime Minister
n8aee89f1203.x: The Finance Commission comprises a Chairman and four other members appointed by the President.
n8aee89f1203.tq: Test composition and appointing authority in the same question.
xs: The FC has **a Chairman and four members appointed by the President** — so option **(1)** is correct (**Art. 280(1)**).
Members are neither elected nor appointed by **Parliament** or the **Prime Minister**; Parliament only fixes **qualifications**.
xa: Qualifications: **Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951**.
Term: as the **President** specifies; members are **eligible for reappointment**.
Constituted **every fifth year or earlier**.

nf07d8906640.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the local-body grants recommended by the 16th Finance Commission for 2026-31?
o: The total grant for local bodies is ₹7.91 lakh crore
Rural local bodies get about ₹4.35 lakh crore
The urban share of local-body grants is 45%
Urban local bodies get about ₹4.35 lakh crore
nf07d8906640.x: The figures are the other way round: urban local bodies get about ₹3.56 lakh crore and rural local bodies about ₹4.35 lakh crore.
xa: Urbanisation premium: **₹10,000 crore**.
Some figures put urban at **₹3.5 lakh crore**.
A **duly constituted ULB** is needed to draw 16th FC grants.

nc5a08f459a7.s: The 16th Finance Commission recommended that State deficits be capped at what percentage of GSDP?
nc5a08f459a7.x: State deficits were recommended to be capped at 3% of GSDP.
nc5a08f459a7.tq: Test the fiscal-limit percentage directly against close alternatives.
xs: State deficits are capped at **3% of GSDP** — option **(2)**.
This is a **fiscal cap** recommended by the **16th FC**.
xa: **Revenue-deficit grants** were discontinued.
AP's **2026-27** Budget shows a revenue deficit of **1.1%**.
Total 16th FC grants: **₹9.47 lakh crore**.

n5f9cb11bdcf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the population data used by Finance Commissions?
o: The 15th Finance Commission used only the 1971 population
The 14th Finance Commission used both the 1971 and 2011 population
The 16th Finance Commission used the 2011 population
The 16th Finance Commission measured demographic performance against the 1971 population
n5f9cb11bdcf.x: The 15th Finance Commission used the 2011 population, not the 1971 figure.
xa: 14th FC distribution: **2011 population (90%)** + **area (10%)**.
16th FC demographic performance weight: **10**.

n18a3a3f8c09.s: Which of the following States was specifically associated with fiscal stress because the 16th Finance Commission provided neither revenue deficit grants nor State-specific grants?
n18a3a3f8c09.x: Kerala was identified as facing fiscal stress because the 16th Finance Commission gave it neither revenue deficit grants nor State-specific grants.
n18a3a3f8c09.tq: Match the State with the specific fiscal consequence.
xs: **Kerala** faces fiscal stress as the 16th FC gives it **no revenue deficit or state-specific grants** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Andhra Pradesh** is linked to the **₹38,000 crore** loss; **Karnataka** to complaints about its **4.13%** share.
xa: Kerala's horizontal share still rose to **2.382%** from **1.92%**.
**Revenue-deficit grants** were **discontinued** by the 16th FC.
State deficits are capped at **3% of GSDP**.

n8ab3c7ebaa7.s: The qualifications of the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission are prescribed by Parliament under the:
n8ab3c7ebaa7.x: Parliament prescribed the qualifications through the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, also referred to in abbreviated form as the Finance Commission Act, 1951.
n8ab3c7ebaa7.tq: Distinguish the exact statutory title from plausible but nonexistent titles.
xs: Parliament fixed qualifications in the **Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The APP notes call it the **Finance Commission Act, 1951**; the other names are invented.
xa: Chairman: **experience in public affairs**.
Members: a **High Court judge** (or qualified to be one), an expert in **government finance and accounts**, one with **financial matters and administration** experience, one with **economics**.
Recommendations are **advisory, not binding**.

n04636e45c35.s: Which Finance Commission recommended a National Disaster Response Reserve (NDRR)?
n04636e45c35.x: The 13th Finance Commission recommended the National Disaster Response Reserve (APPSC-GS 2023 key); it also set the States' share at 32%. The 14th FC is known for raising the share to 42%. The 15th FC is known for adding demographic performance and tax effort. The 12th FC is not linked to the NDRR.
xs: The **13th Finance Commission** (13th FC) recommended the **National Disaster Response Reserve (NDRR)** — option **(2)** (**APPSC-GS 2023** key).
The **14th FC** is known for the **42%** share; the **15th FC** for **demographic performance** and **tax effort**.
xa: 13th FC vertical share: **32%**.
**16th FC disaster corpus**: **₹2.04 lakh crore**; sharing **90:10** NE/Himalayan, **75:25** others.
16th FC proposed **heatwaves and lightning** as new notified disasters.

n34c34f36c5a.s: Which two phenomena were proposed as new national disasters by the 16th Finance Commission?
n34c34f36c5a.x: Heatwaves and lightning were proposed as new notified national disasters.
n34c34f36c5a.tq: Recall the paired additions and reject familiar but unstated disaster categories.
xs: The 16th FC proposed **heatwaves and lightning** as new notified/national disasters — option **(2)**.
These sit alongside its **disaster corpus** recommendations.
xa: Disaster corpus: **₹2.04 lakh crore**.
Sharing: **90:10** for NE/Himalayan states; **75:25** for others.
AP's disaster grant: **₹6,125 crore**.

ne58d1cd024a.s: The divisible pool of Central taxes is calculated by deducting which of the following from gross tax revenue?
o: Cesses, surcharges and cost of collection
States’ share and Finance Commission grants
Only customs duties and Union excise
ne58d1cd024a.x: The divisible pool is gross tax revenue minus cesses, surcharges and the cost of collection. The net proceeds are certified by the Comptroller and Auditor General.
ne58d1cd024a.tq: Apply the formula by identifying the deductions rather than the items included in the pool.
xs: The divisible pool excludes **cesses, surcharges and cost of collection** — option **(1)**.
The **16th FC**'s **41%** applies only to this divisible pool.
xa: Criticism: rising **cesses and surcharges** shrink the divisible pool.
After the 14th FC's **42%**, the Centre increased **non-shareable cesses**.
FM: total transfers **₹25.44 lakh crore** for 2026-27.

n515fc48a186.s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission, the shares of the five southern States in the States' pool:
o: Rose only for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
n515fc48a186.x: All five southern States gained under the Sixteenth Finance Commission, e.g. Karnataka 4.131% and Tamil Nadu 4.097%.
xa: Karnataka's share: **4.13%** (15th: **3.64%**; 14th: **4.71%**) — called unfair.
**UP 17.619%** and **Bihar 9.948%** fell but stay top two.

nd91d0228dab.s: The rising use of cesses and surcharges is criticised because it:
o: shrinks the divisible pool available for sharing
raises the States' vertical share automatically
increases the divisible pool available for tax devolution
nd91d0228dab.x: Cesses and surcharges are not generally part of the divisible pool, so their increasing use shrinks the pool available for devolution.
nd91d0228dab.tq: Trace the fiscal cause-and-effect relationship in a policy scenario.
xs: Rising **cesses and surcharges** **shrink the divisible pool** available for sharing — so option **(1)** is correct.
The divisible pool **excludes cesses, surcharges and cost of collection**, so more cesses mean less to share with states.
They do not raise the states' share or enlarge the pool; the **16th FC** kept the share at **41%**.
xa: After the **14th FC** raised the share to **42%**, the Centre increased **non-shareable cesses**.
FM: states got the **full 41%**; total transfers **₹25.44 lakh crore** for 2026-27.
Southern states call their shares unfair — Karnataka **4.13%** (15th: **3.64%**; 14th: **4.71%**).

nafbbe6373ec.s: The oath of office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is administered by the President in the form prescribed in the
nafbbe6373ec.x: The CAG takes the oath before the President, in the form prescribed in the Third Schedule.
nafbbe6373ec.tq: Separate the Schedule dealing with oath from the Schedule dealing with salary and service conditions.
xs: The CAG takes the oath before the **President** in the form in the **Third Schedule** — option **(3)**.
⚠ The **Second Schedule** holds his **salary**, not the oath.
xa: Appointed by the **President** by **warrant under his hand and seal** (**Art. 148**).
Resigns to the **President**.
Term: **6 years or age 65**.

n38e6246cbf8.s: The salary of the CAG of India, charged on the Consolidated Fund, is equal to that of a:
n38e6246cbf8.x: The CAG gets a salary equal to a Supreme Court judge's, charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and not subject to vote.
xa: Salary, **leave**, pension and retirement age cannot be varied to his disadvantage.
Office expenses, allowances and pensions are also **charged** on the CFI.
**Leave** is granted by the **President**.

n29217955ed3.s: After the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh in 2014, CAG audit reports relating to the accounts of the undivided State were submitted to:
o: the President only, for laying before Parliament
the Governor of Andhra Pradesh only
the Governors of both Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament directly
n29217955ed3.x: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, CAG reports on the undivided State's accounts went to each successor State, so they were submitted to the Governors of both AP and Telangana. State audit reports go to the Governor under Article 151(2), not to the President, which rules out A. B leaves out Telangana. D is wrong because reports never go straight to the PAC.
n29217955ed3.tq: Art 151(2): State reports go to the Governor; pre-2014 reports went to both successor States.
xs: Pre-bifurcation reports went to **the Governors of both Andhra Pradesh and Telangana** — option **(3)**.
Under the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014**, they go **to each successor State**; State reports go to the **Governor** (**Art. 151(2)**).
xa: Current AP reports go to the **Governor of AP**.
Union reports go to the **President**.

nindian-polity-80-1.s: The constitutional framework governing the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is contained in:
nindian-polity-80-1.x: The CAG is in Part V, Chapter V, Articles 148–151. Part XII is finance, and Chapter VI is not the CAG chapter.
nindian-polity-80-1.tq: Recall Part V Chapter V for the CAG.
n: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is governed under Part V, Chapter V of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
Articles 148 to 151 deal with the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
xs: The CAG is in **Part V, Chapter V, Articles 148–151** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is an **independent constitutional authority**; Part XII and Chapter VI are wrong.
xa: **148** = appointment; **149** = duties and powers; **150** = form of accounts; **151** = audit reports.
Full name: **Comptroller and Auditor-General of India** (not "Controller").
Governing Act: **CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971**.

nindian-polity-80-10.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the audit reports of the Union and the States?
nindian-polity-80-10.x: Article 151 deals with audit reports; 148 provides for the CAG, 149 his duties and powers, and 150 the form of accounts.
n: Article 148 deals with the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
Article 149 deals with the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor General. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
Article 150 deals with the form of accounts of the Union and the States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
Article 151(1) deals with the audit reports of the Union. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
Article 151(2) deals with the audit reports of the States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
xa: **Article 150:** form prescribed by the **President** on the CAG's **advice**.
Ultimate action rests with **Parliament** / **State Legislature**.

nindian-polity-80-28.s: The form of accounts of the Union and the States is prescribed by the President on the advice of the:
nindian-polity-80-28.x: Under Article 150, the President prescribes the form of accounts on the CAG's advice.
n: The President prescribes the form of Union and State accounts on the advice of the Comptroller and Auditor General. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
The Comptroller and Auditor General advises on the form of accounts but does not prescribe it unilaterally. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
The Union and State accounts are kept in the form prescribed by the President upon the advice of the Comptroller and Auditor General. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
xa: The CAG does **not** prescribe it unilaterally.
**Article 149** = duties and powers; **Article 151** = audit reports.
The **1976** reform separated accounting from auditing.

n4417b715432.s: The salary and service conditions of the CAG are provided in which Schedule of the Constitution?
n4417b715432.x: The CAG's salary and service conditions are provided in the Second Schedule, and they cannot be varied to his disadvantage after appointment.
xa: Salary **equal to an SC judge**.
Expenses **charged** on the **Consolidated Fund of India** — not votable.
**No minister** represents the CAG in Parliament.

n3b3a3480a76.s: Who represents the CAG in Parliament?
n3b3a3480a76.x: No Minister represents the CAG in Parliament; audit reports reach it through the constitutionally prescribed channel.
xa: The CAG is the PAC's "**friend, philosopher and guide**".
Executive accountability to Parliament works mainly through **CAG reports**.
Not eligible for **further office** under GOI or any State after retirement.

n4a80819c827.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India?
o: He holds office for six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier
After ceasing to hold office, he is not eligible for further office under the Union or any State
He is removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge
He holds office during the pleasure of the President
n4a80819c827.x: The CAG does not hold office at the President's pleasure; he can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge.
xa: Removal: address by both Houses with **special majority** for proved **misbehaviour or incapacity**.
Resignation: to the **President**.
Salary **equal to an SC judge**.

nindian-polity-80-4.s: The CAG’s (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act was enacted in:
nindian-polity-80-4.x: The CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act was passed in 1971. 1976 is the year accounting was separated from audit.
n: The Comptroller and Auditor General’s (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act was enacted in 1971. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
xs: The **CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act** was enacted in **1971** — option **(2)**.
**1976** is the year **accounting** was separated from **auditing** (CAG relieved of **Union accounts** from **1 March 1976**).
xa: Union accounts are now compiled by the **Central Government Accounts** authority under the **Ministry of Finance**.
The CAG still keeps accounts of **most States**.
Tenure under the **1971** Act and **Art. 148(3)**: **6 years or 65**.

nindian-polity-80-7.s: The CAG can be removed on an address by both Houses of Parliament, passed by special majority, on the ground of:
o: An adverse report of the Public Accounts Committee
nindian-polity-80-7.x: Like a Supreme Court judge, the CAG is removed for proved misbehaviour or incapacity on an address by both Houses passed by special majority.
n: The Comptroller and Auditor General is removed on the same grounds and in the same manner as a Supreme Court Judge. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
Removal of the Comptroller and Auditor General requires an address by both Houses of Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
The removal address must be passed by a special majority. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
Proved misbehaviour or incapacity is required for removal of the Comptroller and Auditor General. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
xa: Tenure: **six years** or **65 years**, whichever is earlier.

nindian-polity-80-37.s: From which date was the CAG relieved of the duty of compiling Union accounts?
nindian-polity-80-37.x: The CAG stopped compiling Union accounts from 1 March 1976, when accounting was separated from audit; Union accounts are now compiled by the CGA under the Ministry of Finance.
n: The 1976 departmentalization reform separated accounting from auditing. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
The Comptroller and Auditor General was relieved of the responsibility of preparing Union accounts from 1 March 1976. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
The Comptroller and Auditor General continues to compile and maintain the accounts of most States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
The Central Government Accounts authority handles Union account compilation under the Ministry of Finance. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
xa: The governing Act: **CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971**.
CAG heads the **Indian Audit and Accounts Department**.
Current CAG: **K. Sanjay Murthy**.

nindian-polity-78-9.s: Which Constitutional Amendment raised the retirement age of High Court judges from 60 to 62 years?
nindian-polity-78-9.x: The 15th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1963 raised the retirement age of High Court judges from 60 to 62.
n: A High Court Judge retires at 62 years of age. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
The retirement age of High Court Judges was raised from 60 to 62 years by the 15th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1963. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
xa: **SPSC** members: **6 years or 62**.

nindian-polity-78-16.s: The Chairman and members of a State Public Service Commission hold office for six years or until the age of:
nindian-polity-78-16.x: State PSC members serve six years or until 62, whichever is earlier; UPSC members serve six years or until 65.
n: A High Court Judge retires at 62 years of age. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
A Supreme Court Judge retires at 65 years of age. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
A Supreme Court Judge has no fixed tenure in years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
A Supreme Court Judge retires upon turning 65 years of age. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
The Chairman and Members of the UPSC have a tenure of 6 years or until 65 years of age, whichever is earlier. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
The UPSC Chairman and Members retire at 65 years of age. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
The Chairman and Members of an SPSC have a tenure of 6 years or until 62 years of age, whichever is earlier. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
The SPSC Chairman and Members retire at 62 years of age. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #78 · pp 212-215]
xa: HC age raised from **60 to 62** by the **15th Amendment, 1963**.
The **CAG** also has **6 years or 65**.

n6bd8833440c.s: Who was the first Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
n6bd8833440c.x: V. Narahari Rao was the first Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
xa: K. Sanjay Murthy is the **15th** CAG (as of **May 2026**).

**Ambedkar**: CAG = "most important officer under the Constitution".

n4f1fd55bf8a.s: Who is the Comptroller and Auditor General of India in 2026?
n4f1fd55bf8a.x: K. Sanjay Murthy is the CAG of India in 2026.
xa: He is the **15th** CAG.
**Vinod Rai** wrote "**When Audit Matters**" (**2026**).
India hosted the **5th BRICS SAI Leaders' Summit** in 2026.

ne3c1d36baea.s: Who authored the book titled “When Audit Matters”?

xa: **V. Narahari Rao**: first CAG (**1948**).
**K. Sanjay Murthy**: current, **15th** CAG.

nindian-polity-80-19.s: In relation to the Public Accounts Committee, the CAG functions as its:

n: The Comptroller and Auditor General acts as the Friend, Philosopher and Guide of the Public Accounts Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]

xs: The CAG is the PAC's **Friend, Philosopher and Guide** — option **(4)**.

xa: PAC chairperson is appointed by the **Speaker**; currently **K.C. Venugopal**.
PAC members are elected annually by **STV**; **no minister**.
PSU reports go to the **Committee on Public Undertakings**.

n1bb516007bb.s: Which of the following audits conducted by the CAG are obligatory?
o: Financial attest audit and performance audit
Compliance audit and financial attest audit
n1bb516007bb.x: Compliance and financial attest audits are obligatory, while performance audit is discretionary.
xa: **Propriety audit** is also discretionary: **wisdom, economy** of expenditure.

n3d3f9d6b317.s: Which audit checks whether money was legally available and spent as the rules require?

nc1e1736bf87.s: Which audit examines the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of government schemes?
nc1e1736bf87.x: Performance audit tests economy, efficiency and effectiveness; propriety audit examines wisdom, faithfulness and economy in expenditure.
xa: Propriety audit **flags extravagance**.

nindian-polity-80-15.s: The CAG’s performance audit evaluates which three dimensions of government schemes and outlays?
nindian-polity-80-15.x: A performance audit checks the 3 Es: economy, efficiency and effectiveness of schemes and spending.
n: Performance audits by the Comptroller and Auditor General evaluate economy, efficiency and effectiveness. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
xs: Performance audit tests **Economy, Efficiency and Effectiveness** — option **(3)**.
It is a **discretionary** audit of schemes and outlays.
xa: **Propriety** audit is also discretionary — wisdom, faithfulness, economy.
**Obligatory** audits: **legal and regulatory** and **financial attest**.

n23e30b19f05.s: The official constitutional name of the office is:

First CAG: **V. Narahari Rao** (**1948**).

nb7a270099a7.s: Among the following, whose normal constitutional term is the longest in duration?

xa: **CEC** and **UPSC member** also have **6 years or 65**.

Removal: like a **Supreme Court judge**.

n5ff53bdecd4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the audit jurisdiction of the CAG?
o: He audits the Consolidated Fund of India
He audits the Consolidated Funds of States and of UTs having legislatures
He audits the Contingency Funds and Public Accounts
He audits only expenditure and not receipts

nc1903adcb6e.s: Which of the following falls within the audit jurisdiction of the CAG?
o: Local bodies automatically in every case
Government companies and bodies substantially financed by the government
Secret service expenditure, in the same manner as ordinary expenditure
Day-to-day control over the issue of money from the treasury

nbbbee734b84.s: In relation to secret service expenditure, the CAG:
o: Audits it in the same manner as ordinary expenditure
Audits it only on the request of the President
Audits it in a closed session with the Public Accounts Committee
Accepts a certificate from the competent authority
nbbbee734b84.x: The CAG cannot audit secret service expenditure; he accepts a certificate from the competent authority instead.

xa: PSU reports → **Committee on Public Undertakings**.

Landmark reports: **2G (2010)**, **Coal (2012)**, **Rafale (2019)**.

nfdb2c0dc4e8.s: Which of the following is the correct sequence for Union audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General?

nfdb2c0dc4e8.x: Union reports are submitted by the CAG to the President, laid before both Houses, and then examined by the Public Accounts Committee.

nc0dde1f11ba.s: Which technological approach is being used by the CAG to detect fraud in welfare schemes?

Artificial intelligence and machine learning-based audits

xa: **Social audits** feed CAG performance audits.
Auditing **101 cities** for ease of living.

nindian-polity-80-5.s: Who appoints the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?

The Public Accounts Committee does not appoint the Comptroller and Auditor General. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
xs: The CAG is appointed by **the President of India** — option **(1)** — by **warrant under his hand and seal** (**Article 148(1)**).
⚠ Not the **Prime Minister**, **Finance Minister** or **Public Accounts Committee**.
xa: **Oath** before the President, form in the **Third Schedule**.

nindian-polity-80-13.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the CAG?
o: Auditing expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India
Day-to-day control over the issue of money from the treasury
Auditing Contingency Funds and Public Accounts
Auditing stores, stocks and government companies
nindian-polity-80-13.x: The CAG does not control treasury issues day to day; the other three are within his audit.

The Comptroller and Auditor General audits all transactions relating to the Contingency Funds of the Union and the States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]

Prescribing the form of accounts of the Union
nindian-polity-80-14.x: Performance audit is a CAG function; he cannot prosecute or control treasury withdrawals, and the form of accounts is prescribed by the President on his advice.
n: The Comptroller and Auditor General audits public sector undertakings. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
The Comptroller and Auditor General conducts performance audits. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
The Comptroller and Auditor General does not control the issue or drawal of money from the treasury. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
The Comptroller and Auditor General has no power to initiate criminal prosecutions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
xa: No power to **disallow expenditure** or **enforce recovery**.

nindian-polity-80-34.s: The CAG of India does not control the issue of money from the treasury because he functions only as:

n: The Comptroller and Auditor General does not exercise day-to-day control over the exchequer. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
The Comptroller and Auditor General does not control the issue or drawal of money from the treasury. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]
The Comptroller and Auditor General is an Auditor General and not a Comptroller in the Indian system. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #80 · pp 218-221]

xa: In **Britain** the C&AG does control issue.

nindian-polity-80-57.s: The removal of the CAG is governed by Article 148(1) read with which Article?

ndfe5404f39a.s: Reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General relating to public sector undertakings are examined by the

n10ae68046ad.s: The Public Accounts Committee that pulled up the Railways in relation to CAG Report No. 31 of 2026 was chaired by:

nc44cafdcc6c.s: The recommendations of the Public Accounts Committee are:

naad70046e6f.s: The presumptive loss figure associated with the CAG's 2G spectrum report of 2010 was approximately:

n0f0f65f7bab.s: Which one of the following is NOT a duty of the Attorney General of India?

First SG: **C.K. Daphtary**.

n7b5d2e59b9a.s: The right of the Attorney General to speak in Parliament and the right of the Advocate General to speak in the State Legislature are provided, respectively, by:
n7b5d2e59b9a.x: Article 88 gives the AG the right to speak in Parliament, and Article 177 gives the Advocate General the same right in the State Legislature; neither can vote. Articles 76 and 165 create the two offices. Articles 105(4) and 194(4) extend legislative privileges to them. D reverses the correct pair.
xs: **Article 88** (AG in Parliament) and **Article 177** (Advocate General in State Legislature) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Arts. 76 and 165** create the offices; **Arts. 105(4) and 194(4)** give privileges.
Option (4) reverses the correct pair.
xa: The Advocate General may speak in either House and its **committees**, but has **no right to vote**.
AG qualification: **SC judge**; Advocate General: **HC judge**.
AG precedence **11**; Advocates General **25**.

nc41fe9a9b0d.s: The legislative privileges available to the Attorney General and to the Advocate General are provided, respectively, by:
nc41fe9a9b0d.x: Article 105(4) extends parliamentary privileges to the Attorney General and Article 194(4) extends State legislative privileges to the Advocate General. Articles 88 and 177 give the right to speak, and Articles 76 and 165 create the offices.
nc41fe9a9b0d.tq: Privileges follow the House: 105 for Parliament, 194 for the State.
xs: **Article 105(4)** (AG) and **Article 194(4)** (Advocate General) give legislative privileges — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Arts. 88 and 177** give the right to **speak**; **Arts. 76 and 165** create the offices.
Option (2) reverses the pair.
xa: Neither law officer has a **right to vote** in the legislature.
AG: appointed by the **President**; Advocate General: by the **Governor**.
AG must be qualified to be an **SC judge**; Advocate General an **HC judge**.

nindian-polity-32-4.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Advocate General of a State?
nindian-polity-32-4.x: The Advocate General is provided for under Article 165 (Part VI); the Attorney General under Article 76 (Part V).
n: The Advocate General of the State is provided for under Part VI of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
Article 165 concerns the Advocate General of the State. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
The constitutional basis of the Advocate General of the State is Article 165 in Part VI. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
The constitutional basis of the Attorney General of India is Article 76 in Part V. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
The Solicitor General of India assists the Attorney General of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
Article 76 concerns the Attorney General of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
Article 165 concerns the Advocate General of the State. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
The pairing of Article 76 with Article 165 represents the Attorney General of India and the Advocate General of the State, respectively. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
xa: The SG has **no** constitutional basis — **statutory**.
SG is appointed by the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet**.
First SG: **C.K. Daphtary**.

nindian-polity-32-6.s: The Advocate General of a State holds office during the pleasure of the:
nindian-polity-32-6.x: The Advocate General serves at the Governor's pleasure, not that of the Cabinet or the Chief Minister.
n: The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor under Article 165(3). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
The Advocate General does not hold office during the pleasure of the State Cabinet. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
The Advocate General does not hold office during the pleasure of the Chief Minister. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
A claim that the Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the State Cabinet is false. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
A claim that the Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Chief Minister is false. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
The correct tenure formulation for the Advocate General is pleasure of the Governor. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
xa: By convention the AG changes with the state government.
Floor rights: **Article 177** — may speak, **no right to vote**.

nindian-polity-32-10.s: Who appoints the Solicitor General of India?
nindian-polity-32-10.x: The Solicitor General is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet, while the President appoints the Attorney General.
n: The President of India appoints the Attorney General of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet appoints the Solicitor General of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
The Attorney General of India requires the qualification of a Supreme Court Judge. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
The Solicitor General of India must be a distinguished senior advocate. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
xa: SG and ASGs are **statutory** posts under the **Law Officers (Terms and Conditions) Rules, 1987**.
**Tushar Mehta** reappointed SG for **3** years from **1 July 2026**.
First AG **M.C. Setalvad**; first SG **C.K. Daphtary**.

nindian-polity-32-11.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Attorney General and the Solicitor General of India?
o: The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President
The Attorney General has rights in Parliament under Article 88
The Solicitor General has rights in Parliament under Article 88
The Solicitor General has a fixed statutory term
nindian-polity-32-11.x: The Solicitor General has no floor rights in Parliament; Article 88 rights belong to the Attorney General.
n: The Attorney General of India holds office during the pleasure of the President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
The Solicitor General of India has a fixed statutory term. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
The Attorney General of India has legislative floor rights in Parliament under Article 88. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
The Solicitor General of India has no floor rights in Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 80-82]
