xa: **Advocate General** floor rights: **Article 177**.
Order of precedence: AG **11**, SG **23**.

nb4f7417abeb.s: Which of the following is correct about the removal of the Attorney General of India?
o: He can be removed only on an order of the Supreme Court
He can be removed only by impeachment by both Houses of Parliament
The Constitution lays down specific grounds and a special procedure for his removal
He holds office during the pleasure of the President; no grounds or procedure for removal are specified
nb4f7417abeb.x: The Constitution prescribes no grounds or special procedure for removing the Attorney General; he holds office during the pleasure of the President.
xa: **Term not fixed** by the Constitution.
The AG resigns to the **President**; by convention, also when the **Council of Ministers** goes.
⚠ The **Advocate General** likewise holds office during the **Governor's pleasure**.

n49c08be7a94.s: Who is the highest law officer of India?
n49c08be7a94.x: The Attorney General is the first law officer of India; he is not a member of the Union Cabinet.
xa: ⚠ "**Fixed five-year term**" is a repeated trap (**APPSC-G2 2025**; **LENS Oct 2025**).
The AG must be **qualified to be a Supreme Court judge**.
Current AG: **R. Venkataramani**, reappointed for **2 years** (Oct **2025**).

nindian-polity-31-11.s: The Attorney General of India submits his resignation to the:
nindian-polity-31-11.x: The Attorney General resigns to the President and, by convention, quits when the Council of Ministers changes.
n: The Attorney General of India submits their resignation to the President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
The Attorney General of India traditionally resigns when the Council of Ministers changes. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
xa: The AG is appointed on the Council of Ministers' advice.
**Current AG: R. Venkataramani**, reappointed for **2 years** (Oct 2025).
First AG: **M.C. Setalvad**.

nindian-polity-31-12.s: To qualify as Attorney General of India, an advocate must have practised in a High Court for at least:
nindian-polity-31-12.x: The Attorney General needs Supreme Court judge qualifications: a High Court judge for 5 years, a High Court advocate for 10 years, or an eminent jurist in the President's opinion.
n: The qualifications for the Attorney General of India are equivalent to those for a Supreme Court judge. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
The Attorney General of India must be a citizen of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
A person qualified to be the Attorney General of India must have been a High Court judge for at least five years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
A person qualified to be the Attorney General of India must have been an advocate of a High Court for at least ten years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
A person qualified to be the Attorney General of India may be a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 78-80]
xa: **Advocate General** needs **High Court judge** qualifications (**Article 217**).
**Solicitor General** must be a **distinguished senior advocate**.

nf786fcd43ed.s: The Attorney General is consulted through the Ministry of Law primarily on:
o: All administrative matters of the Union Government
nf786fcd43ed.x: References to the Attorney General are made through the Ministry of Law, and consultation is confined to legal matters of real importance.
nf786fcd43ed.tq: Watch for the overbroad word 'all' and identify the carefully limited scope of consultation.
xs: The AG is consulted through the **Ministry of Law** only on **legal matters of real importance** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The AG does not handle all administrative matters; the **Law Minister** handles legal matters at government level.
xa: Duties: advise GoI on legal matters referred by the **President**; appear for GoI in all **Supreme Court** cases.
The AG represents GoI in **Art. 143** references and may appear in any **High Court**.
The AG is the **chief legal adviser** to GoI.

n649f1e34b36.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional status of the Solicitor General of India?
o: He is a constitutional authority appointed by the President under Article 165
He is a statutory law officer governed by the Law Officers (Terms and Conditions) Rules, 1987
He is created under Article 76 of the Constitution
He is an ex officio member of the Union Cabinet
n649f1e34b36.x: The Solicitor General is not mentioned in the Constitution. The post is statutory and is governed by the Law Officers (Terms and Conditions) Rules, 1987.
n649f1e34b36.tq: Distinguish the constitutional Attorney General from the statutory Solicitor General.
xs: The SG is a **statutory** law officer under the **Law Officers (Terms and Conditions) Rules, 1987** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**SG and ASGs are not mentioned in the Constitution**; **Art. 76** creates only the AG, and **Art. 165** the Advocate General.
The SG is not a Cabinet member.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes wrongly say the Constitution governs the SG.
The SG has a **3-year term**, appointed through the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet**.
**Tushar Mehta** was reappointed SG for **3 years** from **1 July 2026**.

n3b31e4ef63c.s: The Attorney General of India and the Solicitor General of India are ex officio members of the:
n3b31e4ef63c.x: Under the Advocates Act, 1961, the Attorney General and Solicitor General are ex officio members of the Bar Council of India.
n3b31e4ef63c.tq: Recall the statutory body associated with the two principal Union law officers.
xs: The AG and SG are **ex officio members** of the **Bar Council of India** (**Advocates Act, 1961**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
The notes link this membership to the **Advocates Act, 1961**; nothing ties them to the UPSC, NHRC or Law Commission.
xa: The **AG** is a **constitutional** office (**Art. 76**); the **SG** is **statutory**.
AG must be qualified to be a **Supreme Court judge**.
The SG has a **3-year term**; **Tushar Mehta** reappointed from **1 July 2026**.

nf3a8cdaf37b.s: The remuneration of the Advocate General of a State is determined by the:
nf3a8cdaf37b.x: The Governor appoints the Advocate General, who holds office at the Governor's pleasure and receives remuneration the Governor determines.
xa: By convention he changes with the **state government**.
Order of precedence: **No. 25**.
Duties: advises the State Government and performs duties assigned by the **Governor**.

n32a472397e2.s: The right of audience of the Advocate General extends to:
o: Only the High Court of the State
n32a472397e2.x: The Advocate General has the right of audience in any court within the State. The Attorney General has the corresponding right of audience in all courts in India.
n32a472397e2.tq: Use the territorial scope of the office to distinguish the State law officer from the Union law officer.
xs: The Advocate General's right of audience extends to **any court in the State** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is not confined to the **High Court** alone.
xa: **Art. 177**: right to **speak and take part** in either House of the state legislature; **no right to vote**.
**Art. 194(4)**: privileges of a member of the state legislature.
The **AG** may appear in any **High Court** when required.

nf84af622bef.s: Who was the first Attorney General of India?
nf84af622bef.x: M.C. Setalvad was India's first Attorney General.
xa: **Mukul Rohatgi** was AG just before **K.K. Venugopal**.
R. Venkataramani was **reappointed** for **2 years** in Oct **2025**.
First SG: **C.K. Daphtary**.

n2058d7ccab1.s: Who is the present Attorney General of India?
n2058d7ccab1.x: R. Venkataramani is the current Attorney General of India as stated for September 2026. He was first appointed in 2022 and was reappointed for a two-year term in 2025.
n2058d7ccab1.tq: Apply the current-affairs date carefully and distinguish the present office-holder from earlier Attorneys General.
xs: **R. Venkataramani** is the AG as of **Sep 2026** — so option **(2)** is correct.
He was first appointed in **2022** and **reappointed** for a **two-year term** (Oct **2025**).
**K.K. Venugopal** (**2017-2022**), **Mukul Rohatgi** and **M.C. Setalvad** (first AG) are earlier AGs.
xa: The SC asked him to relay directions to all **Advocates General** on **senior-citizen facilities** (**8 Sep 2026**).
SG: **Tushar Mehta**, reappointed for **3 years** from **1 July 2026**.

ne10f4dd65c5.s: Who was the first Solicitor General of India?
ne10f4dd65c5.x: C.K. Daphtary was the first Solicitor General of India.
ne10f4dd65c5.tq: Apply the FIRST/LAST approach to closely related law-officer posts.
xs: The first **Solicitor General** was **C.K. Daphtary** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**M.C. Setalvad** was the first **Attorney General**.
**Vikramjit Banerjee** and **K.M. Nataraj** are among the **5 ASGs** for the SC reappointed recently.
xa: The SG is the **second law officer**, with a **3-year term**.
Current SG: **Tushar Mehta** (from **1 July 2026**).
SG and ASGs are **not mentioned in the Constitution**.

na0f0b43d55e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Attorney General and the Advocate General?
o: The Attorney General is qualified to be a Supreme Court judge
The Advocate General's remuneration is determined by the President
The Advocate General is qualified to be a High Court judge
The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor
na0f0b43d55e.x: The Advocate General's remuneration is determined by the Governor; only the Attorney General's is fixed by the President.
xa: AG appointed under **Art. 76** by the President; Advocate General under **Art. 165** by the Governor.
Legislature rights: **Art. 88** (Parliament) vs **Art. 177** (State Legislature).

n214ca0f0476.s: The National Commission for Backward Classes is provided for under:
n214ca0f0476.x: The NCSC, NCST and NCBC fall under Articles 338, 338A and 338B respectively.
xa: The original **Art. 338** provided a **Special Officer (Commissioner) for SCs and STs**.
The **Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities** is under **Art. 350B**.
APPSC **2022**: the NCBC got constitutional status by the **102nd** Amendment.

n7fda902472a.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, as a combined commission, was created by the
n7fda902472a.x: The 65th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1990 created the combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes under Article 338.
n7fda902472a.tq: Use the amendment-number trap by distinguishing the original provision from the later bifurcation.
xs: The combined **National Commission for SCs and STs** was created by the **65th Amendment, 1990** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **89th Amendment, 2003** created the separate **NCST** (**Art. 338A**), not the combined body.
xa: It replaced the **Special Officer** and the commission set up by the **1987 Resolution**.
Its first chairperson was **S.H. Ramdhan** (**1992**).
Earlier, **1978 & 1987** resolutions set up **non-statutory** commissions.

n530aefcf95e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 65th Constitutional Amendment?
o: It replaced the original Special Officer for SCs and STs
It created the separate National Commission for STs under Article 338A
It replaced the commission established by the 1987 Resolution
The separate NCST under Article 338A came later, through the 89th Amendment
n530aefcf95e.x: The separate NCST under Article 338A came through the 89th Amendment, not the 65th.
xa: The NCST was set up on **19 Feb 2004**; a separate NCSC also from **2004**.
A separate **Ministry of Tribal Affairs** (**1999**) paved the way for the NCST.
First chairpersons: **Suraj Bhan** (NCSC) and **Kunwar Singh** (NCST).

n72dcedadcd4.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the National Commissions for the protected communities?
o: Inquiring into specific complaints of deprivation of rights
Investigating and monitoring constitutional and legal safeguards
Adjudicating criminal cases and awarding punishment to offenders
Advising on socio-economic planning and evaluating progress
n72dcedadcd4.x: The Commissions investigate safeguards, inquire into complaints and advise on development; they do not function as criminal courts or award criminal punishment.
n72dcedadcd4.tq: Find the institutionally impossible power by asking which function belongs to a court rather than a commission.
xs: **Adjudicating criminal cases and awarding punishment** is not a function — so option **(3)** is the answer.
The commissions **investigate and monitor safeguards**, **inquire into specific complaints**, and **advise on socio-economic planning**.
They have **civil court** powers only while investigating.
xa: Reports go to the **President** **annually** (⚠ **not the Prime Minister**, APPSC **2022**).
Criticism: recommendations are **advisory only**.
Mandatory consultation: **Art. 338(9)** (SCs), **Art. 338A(9)** (STs).

n3ead3b64f11.s: The annual and special reports of the National Commissions for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Backward Classes are submitted to the:
n3ead3b64f11.x: The annual and special reports of these constitutional commissions are submitted to the President. The President lays them before Parliament along with an action-taken memorandum.
n3ead3b64f11.tq: Apply the ‘who receives the report?’ method to distinguish the reporting authority from the laying authority.
xs: Reports go to the **President of India** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **Not the Prime Minister** — the **APPSC 2022** trap.
The **President lays them before Parliament**; state-related reports go to the **Governor**.
xa: Reports are submitted **annually** or when the Commission deems fit.
The **NCBC** follows the same pattern — annual report to the President.
Members are appointed by the **President by warrant**.

na6d1de3bf9c.s: Under Article 338(9), which one of the following is required of the Union and every State Government?
o: They must transfer their powers over Scheduled Caste lists to the Commission.
They must consult the National Commission for Scheduled Castes on major policy matters affecting Scheduled Castes.
They must obtain the Commission's prior approval for every welfare expenditure.
They must consult the Commission only on matters concerning Union Territories.
na6d1de3bf9c.x: Article 338(9) requires the Union and every State Government to consult the National Commission for Scheduled Castes on all major policy matters affecting Scheduled Castes. It does not confer prior approval or list-alteration powers on the Commission.
na6d1de3bf9c.tq: Identify the exact nature of the constitutional duty—consultation—not approval or transfer of power.
xs: **Art. 338(9)**: the Union and every State Government must **consult** the **NCSC** on all **major policy matters** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It gives no list-transfer, prior-approval or UT-only role.
xa: For STs the same rule is **Art. 338A(9)**.
The NCSC also **advises on socio-economic planning** and evaluates progress.
Reports go to the **President**, who lays them before **Parliament**.

n130725686e3.s: Which one of the following was a consequence of the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018?
o: Bifurcation of the NCSC and NCST
Insertion of Article 338B and constitutional status for the NCBC
Insertion of Article 350B and creation of the Linguistic Minorities Officer
Creation of the first statutory NCBC
n130725686e3.x: The 102nd Amendment inserted Article 338B and gave constitutional status to the NCBC. The other developments belong to different constitutional provisions or earlier enactments.
n130725686e3.tq: Match the amendment with its article and institutional result, avoiding chronology traps.
xs: The **102nd Amendment Act, 2018** inserted **Art. 338B** and gave the **NCBC constitutional status** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Bifurcation of NCSC/NCST came via the **89th Amendment, 2003**; **Art. 350B** is from the **7th Amendment, 1956**; the first statutory NCBC came from the **1993 Act**.
xa: APPSC **2022**: NCBC got constitutional status by the **102nd** Amendment.
It also let the **President notify SEBCs** and removed backward classes from the **NCSC's purview**.
Composition: Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson + **3** members appointed by the President.

n570603a1de9.s: The creation of a separate Ministry of Tribal Affairs in 1999 paved the way for a separate:
n570603a1de9.x: The separate Ministry of Tribal Affairs set up in 1999 paved the way for a separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes.
xa: The **NCST** came under **Art. 338A** via the **89th Amendment, 2003**, set up on **19 Feb 2004**.
NCST extra work: **minor forest produce ownership**, mineral and water rights, rehabilitation of displaced tribals.
First NCST chairperson: **Kunwar Singh**.

na33ab7126c2.s: Before a proposal for de-reservation of posts is implemented, it must first be examined by the concerned:
o: NCSC, NCST or NCBC, as applicable
na33ab7126c2.x: Proposals for de-reservation of posts must first be examined by the relevant NCSC, NCST or NCBC, depending on the category concerned.
na33ab7126c2.tq: Ask which authority would perform the specialised constitutional safeguard in a practical administrative situation.
xs: **De-reservation** proposals must first be examined by the **NCSC, NCST or NCBC**, as applicable — so option **(4)** is correct.
In **2026** the NCSC began a full review of de-reservation (**13 Aug 2026**).
xa: Union and State Governments must **consult** the commissions on all major policy matters.
Commissions have **civil court** powers while investigating.
Criticism: recommendations are **advisory only**.

n3d9b0a9d275.s: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment also had the effect of:
o: Transferring all SEBC-list powers to State Governors
Removing Scheduled Tribes from the purview of the NCST
Removing backward classes from the purview of the NCSC
n3d9b0a9d275.x: The 102nd Amendment removed backward classes from the purview of the NCSC while constitutionalising the NCBC under Article 338B.
n3d9b0a9d275.tq: Look for the precise change in jurisdiction rather than a general statement about reservation.
xs: The **102nd Amendment** also **removed backward classes from the NCSC's purview** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The creamy layer remained (from **Indra Sawhney**), and STs stayed with the **NCST**.
xa: It inserted **Art. 338B** and let the **President notify SEBCs**.
The **105th Amendment, 2021** restored the **States' power** to prepare SEBC lists.
⚠ Statutory NCBC (**1993**) = **5** members; constitutional NCBC = Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson + **3**.

nindian-society-1-19.s: Which Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes?
nindian-society-1-19.x: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018 gave the NCBC constitutional status.
n: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission was the first Backward Class Commission in 1953. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
B. P. Mandal was the first Mandal Commission Chairman. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Mandal Commission was the first Commission to recommend 27% reservation. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The NCBC received constitutional status through the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 2018. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xa: Kalelkar Commission: **1953**.
**Indra Sawhney (16 Nov 1992)** upheld **27%** OBC reservation and introduced the **creamy layer**.
NCBC was first set up in **1993**.

nindian-society-1-69.s: The first Backward Classes Commission, set up in 1953, was headed by:
nindian-society-1-69.x: Kaka Kalelkar chaired the first Backward Classes Commission (1953); B.P. Mandal chaired the second.
n: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission was the first Backward Class Commission in 1953. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
Kaka Kalelkar was the first Chairman of the Backward Classes Commission. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
B. P. Mandal was the first Mandal Commission Chairman. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xa: The **Mandal Commission** first recommended **27%** reservation.
**NCBC** got constitutional status by the **102nd Amendment, 2018**.
Current NCBC chair: **Niranjan Jyoti** (**2026**).

nbe5773d8e20.s: In Indra Sawhney v. Union of India, decided on 16 November 1992, the Supreme Court, among other things, upheld:
o: 27 per cent reservation for OBCs and the concept of the creamy layer
50 per cent reservation exclusively for economically weaker sections
The abolition of all reservation in public employment
The exclusive power of States to notify all SEBCs without constitutional limitation
nbe5773d8e20.x: The judgment upheld 27 per cent reservation for OBCs, introduced the creamy-layer principle and directed the creation of a permanent body concerning inclusion and exclusion from the OBC list.
nbe5773d8e20.tq: Combine the date with the judgment’s distinct holdings instead of confusing it with later amendments.
xs: **Indra Sawhney v UoI** (**16 Nov 1992**) upheld **27 per cent** OBC reservation and introduced the **creamy layer** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It also directed a **permanent body** for OBC-list inclusion/exclusion.
xa: That direction led to the **NCBC Act, 1993** (in force **2 April 1993**), with **5 members**.
**102nd Amendment Act, 2018** made the NCBC **constitutional** (**Art. 338B**).
**105th Amendment, 2021** restored the **States' power** to prepare their own SEBC lists.

n14b9c006691.s: Which one of the following correctly states the effect of the 102nd and 105th Constitutional Amendments in relation to SEBCs?
o: The 102nd Amendment created the creamy layer, while the 105th Amendment abolished it.
The 102nd Amendment gave the President power to notify SEBCs, while the 105th Amendment restored the States’ power to prepare their own lists.
The 102nd Amendment restored State lists, while the 105th Amendment gave the President the first power to notify SEBCs.
Both amendments abolished the power of the President to notify SEBCs.
n14b9c006691.x: The 102nd Amendment enabled the President to notify SEBCs. The 105th Amendment, 2021 restored the States’ power to prepare their own SEBC lists.
n14b9c006691.tq: Compare the two amendments by assigning one distinct constitutional effect to each.
xs: The **102nd Amendment** let the **President notify SEBCs**; the **105th Amendment** (**2021**) **restored the States' power** to prepare their own lists — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **creamy layer** came from **Indra Sawhney** (**1992**), not from these amendments.
xa: The 105th came after the **Maratha quota judgment**.
The 102nd also inserted **Art. 338B** and **removed backward classes from the NCSC's purview**.
AP aligned its definitions with the **central thresholds** (APPCA Apr **2026**).

nb8e9ece84e7.s: The direction in Indra Sawhney concerning a permanent body for inclusion and exclusion from the OBC list led to the establishment of the:
o: National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under the 89th Amendment
National Commission for Women under the 1990 Act
Statutory National Commission for Backward Classes under the 1993 Act
National Commission for Minorities under the 1992 Act
nb8e9ece84e7.x: The direction in Indra Sawhney led to the NCBC Act, 1993 and the establishment of the statutory NCBC. It was intended to advise on inclusion and exclusion from the OBC list.
nb8e9ece84e7.tq: Trace the judicial direction to the institution created to perform the specified function.
xs: The **permanent body** direction led to the **statutory NCBC** under the **NCBC Act, 1993** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **NCST** came from the **89th Amendment** — unrelated to Indra Sawhney.
xa: The 1993 statutory NCBC had **5 members**, headed by a retired SC/HC judge.
The **102nd Amendment Act, 2018** made it **constitutional** under **Art. 338B**.
**Indra Sawhney** (**16 Nov 1992**) upheld **27%** OBC reservation.

nd04d5ad5e88.s: Which one of the following is specifically associated with the functions of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
o: Appointment of State Human Rights Commissioners
Protection of minor forest produce ownership and tribal mineral and water rights
nd04d5ad5e88.x: The NCST deals, among other matters, with ownership of minor forest produce, mineral and water rights, and rehabilitation of displaced tribal communities.
nd04d5ad5e88.tq: Identify the commission from a distinctive cluster of subject-specific responsibilities.
xs: The NCST's extra work includes **minor forest produce ownership** and **mineral and water rights** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It also covers **rehabilitation of displaced tribals**.
xa: NCST: **Art. 338A**, **89th Amendment, 2003**, set up **19 Feb 2004**.
First NCST chairperson: **Kunwar Singh**.
Governments must **consult** the NCST on major policy matters (**Art. 338A(9)**).

ndcb9c3afc95.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the civil-court powers of the National Commission while investigating a matter?
o: It can summon and examine a person on oath
It can require the discovery and production of documents
It can requisition public records from a court or office
It cannot issue commissions for the examination of witnesses
ndcb9c3afc95.x: The Commission can issue commissions for examining witnesses, along with summoning persons, requiring documents, receiving affidavits and requisitioning records.
xa: APPSC-G1 **2022** keyed "all of these".
**NHRC** and **NCM** also have civil-court powers in inquiries.
⚠ APPCA (**Jun 2026**) says NCM has "no automatic civil-court powers"; the **NCM Act** does give them.

nf9d728a2244.s: Who was the first chairperson of the separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes constituted in 2004?
nf9d728a2244.x: Kunwar Singh was the first NCST chairperson (2004); Suraj Bhan headed the first separate NCSC and S.H. Ramdhan the combined commission (1992).
xa: The combined commission came from the **65th Amendment, 1990**.
Separate bodies: **NCST** w.e.f. **19 Feb 2004**, separate NCSC also from **2004**.
Current **NCBC** chair: **Niranjan Jyoti** (**2026**).

nba327471ab2.s: Which body was set up in 2007 under a law enacted in 2005?
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
nba327471ab2.x: The NCPCR was set up in 2007 under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005.
xa: The NCPCR is one of the **WCD Ministry's** three statutory bodies, with the **NCW** and **CARA**.
It monitors the **RTE Act 2009**, **POCSO Act 2012** and **JJ Act 2015**.
The **NHRC** came under the **Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993** on **12 October 1993**.

n09a88a381a2.s: The National Commission for Women was constituted in:
n09a88a381a2.x: The NCW was constituted in January 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.
xa: First NCW chairperson: **Jayanti Patnaik** (**1992**); present: **Vijaya Rahatkar**.
⚠ **Rekha Sharma** was the chairperson in July **2023** (G2-GS 2023 key).
The NCW is one of the **WCD Ministry's** three statutory bodies, with **NCPCR** and **CARA**.

nfffbb64cfe6.s: The NCPCR is a statutory body established under the
o: Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
nfffbb64cfe6.x: The NCPCR was established under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, although it monitors the implementation of several other child-related laws.
nfffbb64cfe6.tq: Match the institution with its constituting statute rather than a law it monitors.
xs: The NCPCR is a statutory body under the **Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005** — option **(2)**.
It was set up in **2007**.
The **JJ Act 2015**, **POCSO Act 2012** and **RTE Act 2009** are Acts it monitors, not its parent Act.
xa: **SCPCRs** also come under the **CPCR Act 2005**.
The NCPCR checks laws against the **UNCRC**; India acceded in **1992**.
It is one of the **WCD Ministry's** statutory bodies with **NCW** and **CARA**.

n54f6a3e7604.s: State Human Rights Commissions are established under the:
o: Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
n54f6a3e7604.x: SHRCs are set up under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; human-rights functions in Delhi remain with the NHRC.
xa: SHRC jurisdiction covers only **State List and Concurrent List** subjects.
⚠ SHRC members are **appointed by the Governor** but **removed only by the President**.
After **2019**, an SHRC chair may be a former **Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court**.

n38ec88f1434.s: After the 2019 amendment, the term of office of the NHRC Chairperson and members is:
o: Five years or until the age of 70
Three years or until the age of 70
Three years or until the age of 65
Five years or until the age of 65
n38ec88f1434.x: Since 2019 the term is three years or until 70, whichever is earlier; earlier it was five years.
xa: Before 2019: chair only an **ex-CJI**, **2** human-rights members, term **five years** or age 70.
Removal is by the **President** after an **SC inquiry** for misbehaviour or incapacity.
The 2019 amendment added the **NCBC**, **NCPCR** chairs and the **Chief Commissioner for PwD** as deemed members.

n958c7529447.s: Which of the following was NOT added as a deemed member of the NHRC by the 2019 amendment?
o: Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes
Chairperson of the National Commission for Women
Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
n958c7529447.x: The NCW chairperson was already a deemed member before 2019; the amendment added the NCBC and NCPCR chairpersons and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities.
xa: Post-2019 NHRC: Chair + **3** members + deemed members; **3 years** or **70**.
The chair may now be a former **CJI or a Judge of the Supreme Court**.
At least **one** of the human-rights members must be a **woman**.

n53e4eb95998.s: In which year was CEDAW adopted?
n53e4eb95998.x: CEDAW was adopted in 1979; the Convention against Torture followed in 1984.
xa: The **UN Convention on the Rights of the Child** dates from **1989**; India acceded in **1992**.
**10 Dec** is **Human Rights Day**, marking the UDHR.
The **Paris Principles** (Oct **1991**) were endorsed by the UNGA on **20 Dec 1993**.

n322bb44a099.s: Under the 2019 amendment relating to State Human Rights Commissions, the Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission may be:
o: A former Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court
Only a serving Chief Justice of India
n322bb44a099.x: After the 2019 amendment, the Chairperson may be a former Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court.
n322bb44a099.tq: Watch the qualifying words ‘former’ and ‘High Court’ in eligibility questions.
xs: After the **2019** amendment an SHRC chair may be a **former Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court** — option **(2)**.
Earlier only a former **Chief Justice** of a High Court could chair it.
The parallel change for the **NHRC**: former **CJI or a Judge of the Supreme Court**.
xa: SHRC members are appointed by the **Governor** and removed only by the **President**.
The selection committee: **CM**, Speaker, Home Minister, Leader of Opposition (+ Council Chairman and LoP where a Council exists).
SHRCs take only **State List and Concurrent List** matters.

nb0b97654345.s: Who chairs the selection committee for appointing the NHRC Chairperson and members?
nb0b97654345.x: The Prime Minister chairs the six-member committee, which includes the Union Home Minister and the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
xa: Other members: the **Lok Sabha Speaker** and the **Leaders of Opposition in both Houses**.
The NHRC is appointed by the **President**; the **NCW** and **NCM** by the **Central Government**.
For an **SHRC**, the **Governor** appoints on a committee of the **CM**, Speaker, Home Minister and Leader of Opposition.

n7e719e7f114.s: The NHRC cannot inquire into a matter after what period from the date of the alleged violation?
n7e719e7f114.x: The NHRC cannot inquire into a complaint after one year from the date of the alleged violation.
xa: In inquiries the NHRC has **civil court** powers: summon witnesses, call for documents.
Recommendations are **not binding**; the government must respond.
Limited role over the **armed forces**.

n3e8dbb8a289.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the removal of the Chairperson or a member of the NHRC on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity?
o: Removal by the Prime Minister on the advice of the selection committee
Removal by the President after an inquiry by the Supreme Court
Removal by Parliament through a special-majority resolution only
Removal by the Central Government by a simple order
n3e8dbb8a289.x: For misbehaviour or incapacity, the President removes an NHRC member after the Supreme Court inquires into the charge. A is wrong because the PM chairs the selection committee but does not remove anyone. C is wrong because no parliamentary resolution is needed. D describes the NCW, whose members the Centre can remove.
n3e8dbb8a289.tq: NHRC: President appoints and removes (after SC inquiry); NCW and NCM: Centre.
xs: An NHRC member is removed **by the President after an inquiry by the Supreme Court** for **misbehaviour or incapacity** — option **(2)**.
The **PM** only chairs the selection committee; he does not remove anyone.
Removal **by the Centre** is the rule for the **NCW**, not the NHRC.
xa: NHRC: Chair + **3** members + deemed members; **3 years** or **70**.
⚠ **SHRC** members are appointed by the **Governor** but removed only by the **President**.
The selection committee includes the **Lok Sabha Speaker**, **Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman**, both **LoPs** and the **Home Minister**.

nindian-polity-65-39.s: Who is the common Chairman of the Zonal Councils?
nindian-polity-65-39.x: The Union Home Minister chairs all the Zonal Councils.
nindian-polity-65-39.tq: Recall who chairs the Zonal Councils.
n: The Home Minister is the common Chairman of the Zonal Councils. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xs: The **Union Home Minister** is the **common Chairman** of the **Zonal Councils** — option **(1)**.
The Zonal Councils are **statutory** bodies under the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**, **Section 15**.
xa: Other statutory bodies: **NHRC** (PHRA **1993**), **Lokpal** (Act of **2013**), **NGT** (Act of **2010**), **CIC** (RTI Act **2005**).
The **Finance Commission** is **constitutional** (**Art. 280**), unlike the Zonal Councils.
The **Union Home Minister** also sits on the **NHRC** appointment committee chaired by the **PM**.

n5d553b7cbfd.s: A State Human Rights Commission may inquire into a matter only when it relates to
o: Any matter regardless of its legislative list
The State List or the Concurrent List and is not already before the NHRC or another statutory commission
Only matters already decided by a court
n5d553b7cbfd.x: The jurisdiction of an SHRC extends to matters in the State List and Concurrent List, but it cannot inquire into a matter already pending before the NHRC or another statutory commission.
n5d553b7cbfd.tq: Apply both jurisdictional limits: legislative list and prior institutional consideration.
xs: An SHRC may inquire only into **State List or Concurrent List** matters **not already before the NHRC or another statutory commission** — option **(2)**.
So the **Union List** alone or "any matter" are wrong.
It also will not take a case already pending elsewhere.
xa: SHRCs are set up under the **PHRA 1993**.
The **2019 amendment** lets the Centre give **UT** functions to SHRCs; **Delhi** stays with the NHRC.
⚠ SHRC: **appointed by the Governor**, **removed by the President**.

nc41fd3d4015.s: The Chairperson and members of a State Human Rights Commission are appointed by ______ but can be removed only by ______.
nc41fd3d4015.x: The Governor appoints SHRC members on the recommendation of a committee of the Chief Minister, Speaker, Home Minister and Leader of Opposition (plus the Council Chairman and its LoP where a Council exists). Only the President can remove them. A reverses the two roles. The Chief Minister chairs the committee but does not appoint, and the State Legislature has no power to remove.
nc41fd3d4015.tq: SHRC: Governor appoints, President removes (like SPSC).
xs: SHRC members are appointed by **the Governor** but removed only by **the President** — option **(2)**.
The Governor acts on a committee of the **CM**, **Speaker**, **Home Minister** and **Leader of Opposition**.
The CM only sits on the committee; the **State Legislature** has no removal role.
xa: Where a Council exists, the **Council Chairman** and its **LoP** join the committee.
For the **NHRC**, the **President** appoints on a committee chaired by the **PM**.
After **2019** the SHRC chair is a former **Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court**.

n2d4777736a5.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Human Rights Commission functions from:
n2d4777736a5.x: The Andhra Pradesh State Human Rights Commission works from Kurnool.
n2d4777736a5.tq: Use location discrimination among major Andhra Pradesh cities.
xs: The **AP State Human Rights Commission** works from **Kurnool** — option **(3)**.
It is an SHRC under the **PHRA 1993**.
Its members are appointed by the **Governor** and removed only by the **President**.
xa: The **AP Commission for Backward Classes** rests on the **AP Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993** and is a permanent body.
The NHRC sought reports from the AP DGP, Chief Secretary and **AP SHRC** on **Gade Sai Krishna's** custodial death (**28 Jun 2026**).
SHRCs take only **State List and Concurrent List** matters.

n56318fe4904.s: Reports of State commissions constituted under State laws are submitted to the:
o: Governor and laid before the State Legislature
Chief Minister and laid before the Union Cabinet
High Court and laid before the Legislative Council only
n56318fe4904.x: Reports of State commissions go to the Governor and are laid before the State Legislature.
n56318fe4904.tq: Apply the State-level reporting chain and reject the Union-level authority trap.
xs: Reports of State commissions go to the **Governor** and are **laid before the State Legislature** — option **(2)**.
These commissions are created by **State laws**, so their reports stay within the State.
The President, Parliament and Union Cabinet have no role in the notes for State commission reports.
xa: ⚠ **Art 338(9)** and **338A(10)** do not create State commissions; they make the **Union and States consult** the national commission.
AP: the **AP State Commission for SCs and STs Act, 2003**; the body was **reconstituted in 2016**.
AP State SC Commission chairman **K.S. Jawahar** took **196 petitions** in SPSR Nellore (**28 Aug 2026**).

n34f2eea6156.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the National Commission for Women?
o: Suggesting amendments to laws affecting women
Taking suo motu notice where women’s rights are denied
Commissioning special studies on discrimination and atrocities against women
Enforcing criminal sentences imposed by courts
n34f2eea6156.x: The NCW reviews laws, suggests amendments, takes suo motu notice and commissions special studies; it does not enforce criminal sentences imposed by courts.
xa: It reviews constitutional and **legal safeguards** for women and advises on policy.
The **Central Government must consult the NCW** on all major policy matters affecting women.
**Jan Sunwai**: the NCW's public hearings of women's grievances.

nf8adb123569.s: In the context of women’s rights, ‘Jan Sunwai’ refers to:
o: An annual financial audit of women’s commissions
A public hearing of women’s grievances
A legislative session on gender budgeting
nf8adb123569.x: Jan Sunwai refers to public hearings held to hear and address women’s grievances.
xa: The AP zones included **Nellore**, **Guntur**, **Vijayawada** and **Rajamahendravaram**.
AP Mahila Commission chairperson: **Rayapati Sailaja**.
The NCW takes **complaints and suo motu notice** under **Section 10** of its Act.

n536a94e137b.s: The NCPCR’s mandate includes examining whether laws and policies are in conformity with the
o: Paris Agreement and the Constitution alone
Convention against Torture and the Geneva Conventions
Constitution of India and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights alone
n536a94e137b.x: The NCPCR keeps laws and policies in line with the Constitution and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. India acceded to the UNCRC in 1992.
n536a94e137b.tq: Identify the paired domestic and international foundations of the child-rights mandate.
xs: The NCPCR keeps laws and policies in line with the **Constitution** and the **UN Convention on the Rights of the Child** — option **(3)**.
The **CRC** dates from **1989**; India acceded in **1992**.
The **Convention against Torture** (**1984**) and **ICCPR** (**1966**) are not its benchmark.
xa: The NCPCR monitors the **RTE**, **POCSO** and **JJ** Acts.
It was set up in **2007** under the **CPCR Act, 2005**.
**POCSO monitoring** is shared with the State Commissions (**SCPCRs**).

n31531e57c82.s: India acceded to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child in
n31531e57c82.x: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child was adopted in 1989, and India acceded to it in 1992.
n31531e57c82.tq: Distinguish the year of adoption of an international convention from India’s accession year.
xs: India acceded to the **UN Convention on the Rights of the Child** in **1992** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **1989** is the year of the **CRC** itself, not India's accession.
The NCPCR checks Indian laws against the **UNCRC**.
xa: **CEDAW** — **1979**; **Convention against Torture** — **1984**.
Child-rights Acts: **RTE 2009**, **POCSO 2012**, **JJ 2015**.

n4b901da7d15.s: The NCPCR monitors the implementation of which of the following Acts?
o: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
n4b901da7d15.x: The NCPCR monitors the POCSO Act, 2012, along with the RTE Act, 2009 and the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015.
xa: The NCPCR itself rests on the **CPCR Act, 2005** (set up **2007**).
**SCPCRs** share POCSO monitoring.

n0ae62cebce0.s: The number of communities notified as minorities by the Government of India is
n0ae62cebce0.x: Six communities are notified as minorities: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis, with Jains added on 27 January 2014 as the latest notified minority.
n0ae62cebce0.tq: Count the notified communities and avoid omitting the later-listed Jain community.
xs: **Six** communities are notified minorities — option **(1)**.
They are **Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis** and **Jains**.
**Jains** were the latest, notified on **27 Jan 2014**.
xa: **15** States have State Minorities Commissions, including **AP**.
The statutory **NCM** came under the **NCM Act, 1992** (set up **1993**).
NCM: **5 including the chair** must be from minorities; term **3 years**.

n8db32c34cff.s: Which of the following functions is associated with the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis?
o: Monitoring the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013
Conducting the census of urban households
Appointing municipal commissioners in every State
n8db32c34cff.x: The NCSK monitors implementation of the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 and reports to the Government.
xa: Foundation day **23 August**: a **missed-call grievance line** for sanitation workers was launched (**2026**).
**NAMASTE** (**2022**) is linked to the **NSKFDC**.
Tenure runs to **31 March 2028**.

nd43a30b02ce.s: Jains were notified as a minority community at the national level in:
nd43a30b02ce.x: Jains were the latest community to be notified as a national minority, in 2014.
nd43a30b02ce.tq: Use the first/latest distinction and select the precise year rather than a nearby milestone year.
xs: **Jains** were notified as a minority in **2014** (**27 Jan 2014**) — option **(3)**.
They are the latest notified minority.
The others: **Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis** — six in all.
xa: **15** States have State Minorities Commissions, including **AP**.
The statutory **NCM** came under the **NCM Act, 1992**.
A non-statutory Minorities Commission existed from **1978** (MHA resolution).

n9d01118e78c.s: Who is the Chairperson of the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Women according to the 2026 information?
n9d01118e78c.x: Rayapati Sailaja is the Chairperson of the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Women.
n9d01118e78c.tq: Separate a State Commission appointment from the Chairpersons of the National Commission for Women.
xs: **Rayapati Sailaja** chairs the **AP State Commission for Women** (Mahila Commission) — option **(4)**.
**Vijaya Rahatkar** is the present **NCW** chairperson; **Rekha Sharma** was NCW chair in **2023**; **Jayanti Patnaik** was the first NCW chair.
State Commissions for Women come under **State Acts**.
xa: The AP Mahila Commission probed **281 abortion registrations** in **Eluru** Agency mandals (Feb-Mar **2026**).
It held a five-day **Jan Sunwai** in five zones, **9-13 March 2026**, on NCW directions.
AP State SC Commission chairman: **K.S. Jawahar**.

n43993adb55f.s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Women?
n43993adb55f.x: Jayanti Patnaik was the first NCW Chairperson; Vijaya Rahatkar is the present one.
xa: First chair of the combined NCSC-ST (1990s): **Ram Dhan**.
First chair of the constitutional **NCBC**: **Bhagwan Lal Sahni**.
The **89th Amendment (2003)** split the NCSC and NCST; separate bodies from **2004**.

n91cb11a77c7.s: Which of the following is NOT a statutory body under the Ministry of Women and Child Development?
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
n91cb11a77c7.x: NCW, NCPCR and CARA are statutory bodies under the Ministry of Women and Child Development. The NCSK is under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and has been non-statutory since 2004.
xa: The NCSK was created under the **NCSK Act 1993**; its tenure is now extended by government resolution.
It monitors the **Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013**.
The **NCW** dates from the **NCW Act, 1990** (constituted **January 1992**); the **NCPCR** from the **CPCR Act 2005** (set up **2007**).

nc53fe7a7459.s: In January 2022, the Union Cabinet extended the tenure of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis beyond 31 March 2022 by:
nc53fe7a7459.x: The Cabinet extended the NCSK for three years beyond 31 March 2022, i.e., up to 31 March 2025.
xa: The NCSK Act **1993** lapsed in **2004**; the body continues by resolution.
It monitors the **Manual Scavengers Act, 2013**.
A **missed-call grievance line** for sanitation workers was launched on NCSK's foundation day, **23 August** (**2026**).

nd4cdafa2a3c.s: Which of the following correctly explains the relevance of Articles 338(9) and 338A(10)?
o: They directly establish all State commissions.
They empower the President to appoint all State commission members.
They transfer the reports of State commissions to Parliament.
They require the Union and States to consult the concerned National Commission on policy matters affecting the communities concerned.
nd4cdafa2a3c.x: Articles 338(9) and 338A(10) concern consultation with the National Commissions on major policy matters; they do not create State commissions.
nd4cdafa2a3c.tq: Reject the wrong institutional function by distinguishing consultation clauses from establishment provisions.
xs: **Art 338(9)** and **338A(10)** require the **Union and States to consult** the national commission on policy matters — option **(4)**.
⚠ The claim that they empower the creation of State commissions is wrong.
State commissions are created by **State laws** and report to the **Governor**.
xa: **Art. 338** = **NCSC**; **Art. 338A** = **NCST** (inserted by the **89th Amendment 2003**).
**Art. 338B** = **NCBC**, by the **102nd Amendment 2018**.
Only the **NCSC, NCST and NCBC** are constitutional commissions.

nab680475a0a.s: Who was the Chairperson of the National Commission for Women in July 2023?
nab680475a0a.x: Rekha Sharma was the NCW Chairperson in July 2023 (the G2-GS 2023 key). Vijaya Rahatkar is the present NCW Chairperson (2026). Jayanti Patnaik was the first NCW Chairperson (1992). Rayapati Sailaja chairs the AP State Commission for Women.
nab680475a0a.tq: NCW: Jayanti Patnaik (first), Rekha Sharma (2023), Vijaya Rahatkar (now).
xs: **Rekha Sharma** was the NCW chairperson in **July 2023** (G2-GS 2023 key) — option **(3)**.
**Vijaya Rahatkar** is the present NCW chair; **Jayanti Patnaik** was the first (**1992**).
**Rayapati Sailaja** chairs the **AP Mahila Commission**, not the NCW.
xa: The NCW was constituted in **January 1992** under the **NCW Act, 1990**.
NCW: Chairperson + **5 members** + Member-Secretary, nominated by the **Central Government**.
NCW term: **3 years**.

n0cc9aa79e04.x: The word ‘Lokpal’ was coined by Dr. L.M. Singhvi.
n0cc9aa79e04.tq: Test the person associated with the exact origin of a term.
xs: The term **Lokpal** was coined by **Dr. L.M. Singhvi** in **1963** — option **(3)**.
Lokpal is the Indian equivalent of the **Ombudsman** at the Union; the State equivalent is the **Lokayukta**.
The Ombudsman itself began in **Sweden in 1809**.
xa: The **first Lokpal Bill** was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** in **1968**.
The **First ARC (1966-70)** recommended a **Lokpal** for the Union and a **Lokayukta** in every State.
⚠ **1809** Sweden ombudsman ≠ **1766** Sweden RTI law.

nfca4c3862b7.s: The institution of Ombudsman was first established in which country in 1809?
nfca4c3862b7.x: The Ombudsman institution was first set up in Sweden in 1809. Sweden’s 1766 law is associated with the right to information, not the origin of the Ombudsman institution.
nfca4c3862b7.tq: Use the date-place pair and distinguish it from the nearby 1766 Swedish fact.
xs: The **Ombudsman** was first set up in **Sweden in 1809** — option **(1)**.
⚠ Sweden's **1766** law is about RTI, not the Ombudsman.
India's equivalents are the **Lokpal** (Union) and **Lokayukta** (State).
xa: The term Lokpal was coined by **Dr. L.M. Singhvi** (**1963**).
First Lokayukta in India: **Maharashtra, 1971**; first State law: **Odisha, 1970**.
First Lokpal Bill: **1968**.

n72c0a49e57c.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the Indian equivalents of the Ombudsman at the Union and State levels respectively?
n72c0a49e57c.x: Lokpal is the Ombudsman institution at the Union level, while Lokayukta performs the corresponding role at the State level.
n72c0a49e57c.tq: Discriminate between the two similar terms by matching them with Union and State levels.
xs: The Union and State equivalents of the Ombudsman are the **Lokpal and Lokayukta** — option **(1)**.
The **Lokpal** works at the Union level; the **Lokayukta** in the States.
The **CVC** came from the **Santhanam Committee**; it is not the Ombudsman.
xa: The **First ARC** recommended this two-tier model in **1966**.
The term Lokpal was coined by **Dr. L.M. Singhvi**.
Every State had to set up a Lokayukta within **one year** under **Section 63** of the **2013** Act.

n6def444bacd.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the First Administrative Reforms Commission from the Santhanam Committee?
o: The First ARC recommended the CVC, whereas the Santhanam Committee recommended the Lokpal.
The First ARC recommended a two-tier Lokpal-Lokayukta system, whereas the Santhanam Committee recommended the CVC and the CBI.
The Santhanam Committee recommended the Lokayukta for States, whereas the First ARC recommended only the CBI.
Both bodies recommended only the Lokpal at the Union level.
n6def444bacd.x: The First ARC recommended Lokpal at the Union level and Lokayukta in the States. The Santhanam Committee was associated with the CVC and the CBI, not the Lokpal.
n6def444bacd.tq: Separate closely associated anti-corruption bodies by assigning each recommendation to the correct committee.
xs: The **First ARC** recommended a **two-tier Lokpal-Lokayukta** system; the **Santhanam Committee** recommended the **CVC and the CBI** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **Santhanam** → CVC + CBI; **First ARC** → Lokpal + Lokayukta.
The Santhanam Committee did not recommend the Lokpal.
xa: Santhanam Committee: **1962-64**, chaired by **K. Santhanam**.
The ARC's interim report "**Problems of Redressal of Citizens' Grievances**" (**1966**) carried the two-tier idea.
The **Second ARC (2007)** strongly reiterated the Lokpal recommendation.

n7fcb40604ff.s: In which year did the First Administrative Reforms Commission recommend a two-tier Lokpal-Lokayukta system?
n7fcb40604ff.x: The First ARC made the recommendation in 1966; the Second ARC reiterated it in 2007.
xa: Santhanam recommended the **CVC** and **CBI**, not the Lokpal.
First ARC chair: **Morarji Desai**, later **K. Hanumanthaiya**.
The first Lokpal Bill followed in **1968**.

n1135d5f5914.s: In which year did the Lok Sabha pass the First Lokpal Bill?
n1135d5f5914.x: The First Lokpal Bill, introduced in the Lok Sabha, was passed by it in 1969 and lapsed on the dissolution of that Lok Sabha.
xa: Exam angle: options mix **1968** (introduced) with **1969** (passed by the Lok Sabha) — read the verb.
Final passage came in **December 2013**, after the **Anna Hazare** movement.

n146a2fb1ea8.s: In which year did Parliament pass the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill?
n146a2fb1ea8.x: Parliament passed the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill in December 2013, after the Bill's re-introduction in 2008.
xa: The Rajya Sabha passed it on **17 December 2013** and the Lok Sabha on **18 December 2013**.
President's assent: **1 January 2014**; in force: **16 January 2014**.
The Lokpal began functioning on **27 March 2019**.

n95252309f93.s: The India Against Corruption movement was led by
n95252309f93.x: India Against Corruption was led by Anna Hazare and was central to the 2011 civil society campaign for the Jan Lokpal Bill.
n95252309f93.tq: Distinguish the movement’s leader from members of the later drafting committee.
xs: **India Against Corruption (IAC)** was led by **Anna Hazare** — option **(1)**.
It began in **2011** and pushed the civil-society **Jan Lokpal Bill**.
**Shanti Bhushan** and **Prashant Bhushan** sat on the civil-society side of the drafting panel; **Pranab Mukherjee** chaired it for the Government.
xa: Fasts: **Jantar Mantar (April 2011)** and **Ramlila Maidan (August 2011)**.
Civil-society members also included **Arvind Kejriwal** and **Justice N. Santosh Hegde**.
The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill was passed in **December 2013**.

n987dd961d0c.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the dates associated with the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013?
o: Assent was given on 1 January 2014 and the Act came into force on 16 January 2014.
Assent was given on 16 January 2014 and the Act came into force on 1 January 2014.
Both assent and commencement took place on 1 January 2014.
Both assent and commencement took place on 16 January 2014.
n987dd961d0c.x: The President gave assent on 1 January 2014, while the Act came into force on 16 January 2014.
n987dd961d0c.tq: Discriminate between two closely related dates by matching each date with its legal event.
xs: **Assent** came on **1 January 2014** and the Act **came into force** on **16 January 2014** — option **(1)**.
⚠ TH (**23 Mar 2026**) wrongly gives 1 January 2014 as commencement — that is the assent date.
**16 January 2014** is the APPSC key (APPSC **2019**, G2 **2025**).
xa: Parliament passed it on **17 December 2013** (Rajya Sabha) and **18 December 2013** (Lok Sabha).
The Lokpal actually began functioning on **27 March 2019**.
The Lokpal is a **statutory body**, not constitutional.

n0d81873414e.s: The Inquiry Wing of the Lokpal conducts preliminary inquiry into offences under the:
n0d81873414e.x: The Inquiry Wing conducts preliminary inquiries into offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
n0d81873414e.tq: Use the statutory subject of the inquiry rather than the name of the investigating wing alone.
xs: The Inquiry Wing makes preliminary inquiries into offences under the **Prevention of Corruption Act** (PCA) — option **(2)**.
It is headed by a **Director of Inquiry** (**Section 11**).
Its report after a reference is due in **60 days**.
xa: SC **split verdict** on **Section 17A** of the PCA (prior approval before investigation), **22 Jan 2026**.
Justice **K.V. Viswanathan** upheld 17A only with a **binding opinion of the Lokpal/Lokayukta**; Justice **B.V. Nagarathna** held it unconstitutional.
AP's **ACB** investigates **Prevention of Corruption Act** offences.

nb0048b78db2.s: Which one of the following is the principal role of the Anti-Corruption Bureau in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Receiving complaints and submitting recommendations to the Governor
Investigating offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, including trap and disproportionate-assets cases
Advising departments on disciplinary matters without investigating offences
Exercising superintendence over the Central Bureau of Investigation in all cases
nb0048b78db2.x: The Anti-Corruption Bureau is a police investigating agency that investigates Prevention of Corruption Act offences, including trap and disproportionate-assets cases.
nb0048b78db2.tq: Match the agency with its operational function rather than its broad anti-corruption label.
xs: The ACB's main role is **investigating offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act**, including **trap** and **disproportionate-assets** cases — option **(2)**.
Receiving complaints and recommending to the Governor is the **Lokayukta's** role.
Advising departments is the **State Vigilance Commission's** role.
xa: AP ACB head (IG level): **R. Jayalakshmi** (Apr **2026**).
Many Lokayuktas depend on the **state police/ACB** for investigation.
The State Vigilance Commission dates from **1964**.

o: Body created by a Constitutional Amendment
n3e01cc2ad03.x: The Lokpal is established by statute and is not a constitutional body.
xa: **50%** of members are **judicial**; at least **50%** from **SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women**.
CDI suggests **constitutional status** and a **model Lokayukta Act**.
The Act came into force on **16 January 2014**.

nb1baf100318.s: An eminent person may be appointed Chairperson of the Lokpal if he or she has at least ____ years' experience in specified fields.
nb1baf100318.x: Besides a former CJI or Supreme Court judge, an eminent person with 25 years' relevant experience may be Lokpal Chairperson.
xa: Members: up to **8**, **50%** judicial (former SC judges or former HC Chief Justices).
Bar: cannot be an **MP or MLA**.
Present chair: **Justice A.M. Khanwilkar**, a retired SC judge.

n9695871069a.s: The term of office of the Chairperson or a member of the Lokpal is
o: six years irrespective of age, with one reappointment
eight years or until attaining 70 years of age, whichever is later
five years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is later, with reappointment permitted
five years or until attaining 70 years of age, whichever is earlier, with no reappointment
n9695871069a.x: The term is five years or until the age of 70, whichever is earlier, and reappointment is not permitted. A member may become Chairperson within the total five-year period.
n9695871069a.tq: Watch the reversed comparison words 'earlier' and 'later' and the reappointment trap.
xs: The term is **five years or age 70**, whichever is **earlier**, with **no reappointment** — option **(4)**.
A member may become Chairperson within a **5-year** total.
The other options' terms do not match the Act.
xa: Bar: a Chairperson or member **cannot be an MP or MLA**.
The **Rajasthan** Lokayukta's tenure was cut from **8** years to **5** years (APPSC G1 **2018** key).
AP's new Lokayukta has a **5-year term** (**20 Aug 2026**).

n9c008a15563.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Selection Committee of the Lokpal?
o: The Prime Minister is its Chairperson
The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is a member
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is an ex officio member
An eminent jurist is nominated by the President on the other members' recommendation
n9c008a15563.x: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is not a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee.
xa: Others: **Speaker of the Lok Sabha**; **CJI** or an SC judge nominated by the CJI.
A **Search Committee** of at least **seven** persons prepares the panel.
At least **half** of the Search Committee must be from SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women.

nindian-polity-22-47.s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee?
nindian-polity-22-47.x: The Rajya Sabha Chairman is not a member; the PM chairs the committee, and the Speaker and the CJI (or a Supreme Court judge he nominates) are members.
n: The Prime Minister is the Chair of the Lokpal Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court nominee is a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Rajya Sabha Chairman is not a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
xa: The other members: the **Leader of the Opposition** in the Lok Sabha and **one eminent jurist**.
The **President** appoints the Lokpal on the **Selection Committee**'s recommendation.
The Selection Committee sets up a **Search Committee** of at least **seven** persons, at least **half** from SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women.

n8f1d524a2e8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the declaration of assets under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas law?
o: The original law covered the public servant, spouse and dependent children
The 2016 amendment placed the form and manner of declaration in the Constitution
The declaration was required within 30 days of entering office
After 2016, the form and manner are prescribed by the Central Government
n8f1d524a2e8.x: The 2016 amendment left the form and manner to be prescribed by the Central Government, not by the Constitution.
xa: The **2016** amendment filled "a small gap" in the Act (UPSC Governance).
The **2013** Act also amended the **DSPE Act** (CBI Director's committee; a **Directorate of Prosecution**).
The Lokpal is a **statutory body**.

n93ff31f4183.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Search Committee for the Lokpal?
o: It prepares a panel for consideration
It is constituted by the Selection Committee
It may have fewer than seven persons
At least half its members must be from SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women
n93ff31f4183.x: The Search Committee must have at least seven persons.
xa: The Selection Committee is chaired by the **PM**.
The **President** makes the appointment.
The Lokpal bench itself must be at least **50%** from these groups.

n4d7e264a239.s: The Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and not more than ____ members.
n4d7e264a239.x: The Lokpal has a Chairperson and up to eight members, at least half of whom must be judicial members.
xa: At least **50%** must also be from **SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women** — the two 50% rules apply together.
Present bench: **6 members** against a sanctioned **8** (Jun **2026**).
Term: **5 years or age 70**.

nf8b71ef37c6.s: Which of the following categories of organisations comes within the Lokpal’s jurisdiction when the stated condition is fulfilled?
o: Only organisations receiving domestic donations above ₹10 lakh
Only constitutional bodies receiving no government funding
Every private company, irrespective of funding
NGOs, trusts and societies receiving foreign contributions above ₹10 lakh
nf8b71ef37c6.x: NGOs, trusts and societies receiving foreign contributions above ₹10 lakh come within the stated jurisdiction of the Lokpal.
nf8b71ef37c6.tq: Focus on both the organisation category and the exact monetary threshold.
xs: **NGOs, trusts and societies** receiving **foreign contribution above ₹10 lakh** (FCRA) are covered — option **(4)**.
The test is **foreign** contribution, not domestic donations.
Bodies set up by an **Act of Parliament** or **funded by government** are also covered.
xa: Central officials of **Groups A, B, C and D** are covered.
**Union Ministers** and **MPs** are covered.
Public servants **in and outside India** are covered.

n5f9e6dd46a4.s: Allegations against the Prime Minister relating to which of the following are excluded from the Lokpal's jurisdiction?
o: International relations, security, public order, atomic energy and space
n5f9e6dd46a4.x: All these areas, namely international relations, security, public order, atomic energy and space, are excluded from the Lokpal's jurisdiction over the Prime Minister.
xa: An inquiry against the PM needs the **full bench** and a **two-thirds** majority.
It is held **in camera**.
Complaints are barred **after seven years**.

n3fa00014a2d.s: An allegation against the Prime Minister relates to a matter not covered by the statutory exclusions. Which condition is required for an inquiry by the Lokpal?
o: Approval by the Union Cabinet through an open hearing
Prior approval of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha alone
Approval by the full Bench with at least a two-thirds majority, with the proceedings held in camera
Approval by a simple majority of any two members, in public proceedings
n3fa00014a2d.x: An inquiry against the Prime Minister requires approval of the full Bench by at least a two-thirds majority, and the inquiry is held in camera.
n3fa00014a2d.tq: Apply the special procedural safeguards to a concrete jurisdictional situation.
xs: An inquiry against the PM needs the **full Bench** with at least a **two-thirds majority**, held **in camera** — option **(3)**.
Neither the **Cabinet** nor the **Rajya Sabha Chairman** has a role.
A simple majority or public proceedings would not satisfy the safeguard.
xa: Excluded subjects: **international relations**, **security**, **public order**, **atomic energy and space**.
Lokpal: Chairperson + up to **8** members.
The Lokpal has **civil court** powers: summon persons, requisition records.

n4add6b2fcbd.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the jurisdiction of the Lokpal?
o: It applies to Indian public servants both within and outside India
It extends to Union Ministers and Members of Parliament
It covers anything said or any vote given by an MP in Parliament
It covers bodies set up by an Act of Parliament or funded by the government
n4add6b2fcbd.x: Anything said or any vote given by an MP in Parliament is outside the Lokpal's jurisdiction.
xa: NGOs with **foreign contribution above ₹10 lakh** are covered.
⚠ UPSC **2025** key marks the "not posted abroad" statement wrong.
Groups **A, B, C and D** officials are covered.

n92463e43c30.s: A preliminary inquiry under the Lokpal framework is ordinarily to be completed within:
n92463e43c30.x: A preliminary inquiry ordinarily takes 90 days, extendable by 90 more days for reasons recorded in writing.
xa: Inquiry Wing report: **60 days**.
Investigation: **6 months** + **6 months**.
Trial: **1 year**, extendable up to **2 years**.

n8eb80861522.s: Under the Lokpal framework, a trial by the Special Court is ordinarily to be completed within
o: six months, extendable by six months
one year, extendable up to two years
n8eb80861522.x: The Special Court trial has a one-year limit extendable up to two years. Six months plus six months is the investigation limit; 90 plus 90 days is the preliminary inquiry; 60 days is the Inquiry Wing's report.
n8eb80861522.tq: 60 days report, 90+90 inquiry, 6+6 months investigation, 1-2 years trial.
xs: A Special Court trial takes **one year**, extendable up to **two years** — option **(2)**.
**Six months + six months** is the investigation limit.
**90 + 90 days** is the preliminary inquiry; **60 days** the Inquiry Wing's report.
xa: The **Prosecution Wing** files cases before the **Special Court**.
It is headed by a **Director of Prosecution**.
The Lokpal can attach property even while **prosecution is pending**.

n195b6bb33cc.s: The recommendations of Lokayuktas are binding in:
n195b6bb33cc.x: Lokayukta recommendations are advisory in many States and binding only in some, not in every State.
xa: Weakness: many Lokayuktas have **no independent investigating wing**.
Karnataka is an exception with its own **Lokayukta Police** wing.
Criticism: executive attempts to **dilute powers** (e.g. **Delhi**).

n3f729c0e5ec.s: Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act is associated with the issue of:
o: Publication of the Corruption Perceptions Index
Appointment of the Central Vigilance Commissioner
General consent of States for all CBI investigations
Prior approval before investigating certain decisions or recommendations by public servants
n3f729c0e5ec.x: Section 17A concerns prior approval for investigation in specified circumstances involving decisions or recommendations of public servants. Its interpretation has been the subject of a Supreme Court split verdict and debate over 'sanction paralysis'.
n3f729c0e5ec.tq: Distinguish prior approval under the PCA from State general consent under the DSPE Act.
xs: **Section 17A** of the PC Act concerns **prior approval before investigation** of public servants — option **(4)**.
It was the subject of an SC **split verdict** (**22 Jan 2026**).
Justice **K.V. Viswanathan** upheld it only with a **binding opinion of the Lokpal/Lokayukta**.
xa: Justice **B.V. Nagarathna** held 17A unconstitutional.
The Lokpal's **Inquiry Wing** handles preliminary inquiries into **PCA** offences.
Criticism: the Lokpal has **no power of prior sanction**.

nc3c0ef29301.s: The Lokpal actually began functioning on:
nc3c0ef29301.x: Although the Act came into force in 2014, the Lokpal began functioning on 27 March 2019 after its Chairperson and members were appointed.
nc3c0ef29301.tq: Distinguish commencement of an Act from the date on which an institution began functioning.
xs: The Lokpal actually began functioning on **27 March 2019** — option **(2)**.
This was after the chairperson and members were appointed.
**16 January 2014** is commencement, **1 January 2014** assent and **17 December 2013** Rajya Sabha passage.
xa: First Lokpal: **Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose**, appointed **17 March 2019** (UPSC notes: **19** March).
Criticism: the **2013** Act → first Lokpal only in **2019** shows delay.
Second chair: **Justice A.M. Khanwilkar** since **10 March 2024**.

n6d5e279a886.s: Section 11 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, requires the establishment of
o: a vigilance wing headed by the CVC and an audit wing headed by the CAG
an inquiry wing headed by a Director of Inquiry and a prosecution wing headed by a Director of Prosecution
a judicial wing headed by the Chief Justice of India and a police wing headed by the CBI Director
a parliamentary wing headed by the Speaker and a prosecution wing headed by the Attorney General
n6d5e279a886.x: Section 11 requires an inquiry wing headed by a Director of Inquiry and a prosecution wing headed by a Director of Prosecution.
n6d5e279a886.tq: Match each statutory wing with its specifically designated head.
xs: **Section 11** requires an **inquiry wing** headed by a **Director of Inquiry**; a **prosecution wing** is headed by a **Director of Prosecution** — option **(2)**.
The prosecution wing files cases before the **Special Court**.
Both wings were **still being staffed** (parliamentary standing committee, **23 Mar 2026**).
xa: The Inquiry Wing was recently set up with **3 SPs** (general, economic/banking, cyber).
The Lokpal has **superintendence and direction** over the **CBI** in cases it refers.
It can **attach and confiscate** corruptly acquired property.

n2fd1637255a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the powers associated with the Lokpal?
o: Its Prosecution Wing files cases before the Special Court
It exercises superintendence and direction over the CBI in cases it refers
Tainted property can be attached only after the prosecution is over
It may summon persons and requisition records like a civil court
n2fd1637255a.x: Property acquired by corrupt means can be attached and confiscated even while the prosecution is pending.
xa: It can also direct protection of documents and recommend **transfer/suspension** and disciplinary action.
⚠ The **CVC Act 2003** gives the CVC superintendence over the CBI in PCA cases generally; the Lokpal only in cases it refers.
Criticism: **dependence on the CBI**.

na32bdbd64ee.s: Who has been the second Chairperson of the Lokpal since 10 March 2024?
na32bdbd64ee.x: Justice Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar, a retired Supreme Court judge, became the second Chairperson of the Lokpal on 10 March 2024.
na32bdbd64ee.tq: Distinguish the Chairperson from the judicial members of the bench.
xs: **Justice A.M. Khanwilkar** (**Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar**) has been the second Lokpal chair since **10 March 2024** — option **(4)**.
He is a retired **SC judge**, appointed after a gap of nearly two years (UPPSC **2024** key).
**Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose** was the first; **Ritu Raj Awasthi** and **Lingappa Narayana Swamy** are judicial members.
xa: Ghose was appointed **17 March 2019** and left on **27 May 2022**.
Present bench: **6 members** against a sanctioned **8**.
Non-judicial members: **Sushil Chandra**, **Pankaj Kumar**, **Ajay Tirkey**.

n998746da18b.s: Who was appointed the first Lokpal of India in March 2019?
n998746da18b.x: Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose, a retired Supreme Court judge, became the first Lokpal in March 2019. Khanwilkar is the present (second) Chairperson since 2024; Santosh Hegde was Karnataka Lokayukta; Ritu Raj Awasthi is a judicial member.
n998746da18b.tq: First Lokpal = P.C. Ghose (2019); second = Khanwilkar (2024).
xs: **Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose**, a retired **Supreme Court judge**, became the first Lokpal in **March 2019** — option **(3)**.
**Justice A.M. Khanwilkar** is the present (second) chair since **2024**.
**Justice N. Santosh Hegde** gave Karnataka's **Bellary** report; **Ritu Raj Awasthi** is a judicial member.
xa: APPSC answer for the first Lokpal's year: **2019** (APPSC **2018** key).
The Lokpal **started work** on **27 Mar 2019**.
Ghose left office on **27 May 2022**.

n086de4cabd0.s: Which of the following correctly states the distinction between the Central Vigilance Commission and the Lokpal in relation to the Central Bureau of Investigation?
o: The CVC has superintendence over the CBI generally in Prevention of Corruption Act cases, whereas the Lokpal has it only in cases referred by the Lokpal.
The Lokpal has general superintendence, while the CVC acts only in cases referred by the Lokpal.
The Lokpal has superintendence over the CBI in every Prevention of Corruption Act case.
Neither the CVC nor the Lokpal has any relationship with the CBI.
n086de4cabd0.x: The CVC Act, 2003 gives the CVC superintendence over the CBI in Prevention of Corruption Act cases generally. The Lokpal exercises such a role only in cases referred by it.
n086de4cabd0.tq: Compare the scope words ‘generally’ and ‘only in cases it refers’.
xs: The **CVC** has superintendence over the **CBI** in **PCA cases generally**; the **Lokpal** only in **cases it refers** — option **(1)**.
The CVC's power comes from the **CVC Act 2003**.
So options 2-4 misstate the split.
xa: The **Santhanam Committee (1962-64)** recommended the **CVC** and **CBI**.
**Group C and D** complaints go from the Lokpal to the **CVC**, which reports back.
The 2013 Act amended the **DSPE Act** (CBI Director's committee; Directorate of Prosecution).

n9a7f986666f.s: A complaint is made more than seven years after the alleged offence. Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the Lokpal:
o: can inquire only if the complaint concerns a Union Minister
cannot inquire into it after the statutory seven-year period
can inquire only after approval of the Rajya Sabha Chairman
must inquire into it because there is no limitation period
n9a7f986666f.x: The Lokpal cannot inquire into a complaint made after seven years from the alleged offence.
n9a7f986666f.tq: Apply the statutory time limit to a filing scenario.
xs: The Lokpal **cannot inquire** into a complaint made **after seven years** from the alleged offence — option **(2)**.
So there is a limitation period; it is not a Union Minister or Rajya Sabha Chairman exception.
The bar is **7 years** from the alleged offence.
xa: Inquiry Wing report after reference: **60 days**.
Preliminary inquiry: **90 days**, plus **90 days** with **reasons in writing**.
Investigation: **6 months**, extendable by **6 months**.
n9a7f986666f.fixed: bar applies after expiry of seven years; 'seven years after' is ambiguous

n1b5cdd16c3b.s: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act required every State to establish a Lokayukta within:
o: Six months of the Act’s assent
Two years of the first Lokpal appointment
One year of the commencement of the Act
Five years of the establishment of the Central Vigilance Commission
n1b5cdd16c3b.x: Every State was required to set up a Lokayukta within one year of the commencement of the Act.
n1b5cdd16c3b.tq: Test the exact time limit and its starting point.
xs: Every State had to set up a Lokayukta within **one year of commencement** of the Act — option **(3)**.
This is **Section 63** of the **2013** Act.
Each State does so by **its own State law**.
xa: By **2013**, **21 States and 1 UT (Delhi)** already had Lokayuktas.
There is **no uniform model**; CDI asks the Centre to encourage a **uniform, robust model**.
The Act came into force on **16 January 2014**.

n87ad817e349.s: The annual consolidated report of a State Lokayukta is submitted to the
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
n87ad817e349.x: The Lokayukta submits an annual consolidated report to the Governor.
n87ad817e349.tq: Test the reporting relationship by identifying the constitutional recipient.
xs: The Lokayukta submits an **annual consolidated report to the Governor** — option **(1)**.
The Governor is also the appointing authority.
In AP the Lokayukta/Upa-Lokayukta **reports to the Governor**.
xa: AP annual report **2025**: **7,431** cases handled, **3,654** disposed.
Recoveries facilitated: **₹15.29 crore**.
Nearly half the disposals concerned the **Revenue Department**.

neb0cb82eb29.s: Which State reduced the tenure of its Lokayukta from 8 years to 5 years?
neb0cb82eb29.x: Rajasthan cut its Lokayukta's tenure from eight to five years (APPSC G1 2018 key). Maharashtra, Karnataka and Bihar are not cited for this change.
xs: **Rajasthan** cut its Lokayukta's tenure from **8 years to 5 years** — option **(3)**.
This is the APPSC G1 **2018** key.
Rajasthan's Lokayukta Act dates from **1973**.
xa: Rajasthan's **Section 7** keeps sexual harassment, caste discrimination and violence outside the Lokayukta's investigation.
Rajasthan has a **Lokayukta + Upa-Lokayukta** but needs **no judicial qualification**.
AP's new Lokayukta has a **5-year term**.

nd94ddb2933e.s: The Bellary illegal iron ore mining report of 2011 was associated with:
nd94ddb2933e.x: The Bellary illegal iron ore mining report was prepared under Justice N. Santosh Hegde in 2011.
nd94ddb2933e.tq: Match the report with its author while avoiding confusion with other Lokayukta-related names.
xs: The **Bellary** illegal iron ore mining report (**2011**) was by **Justice N. Santosh Hegde** — option **(3)**.
**Chandru Lamani** was caught in a **₹5 lakh** trap case; **Morarji Desai** chaired the First ARC; **Dr. L.M. Singhvi** coined "Lokpal".
Hegde was then the **Karnataka** Lokayukta.
xa: The report led to the **CM's resignation** and the arrest of **G. Janardhana Reddy**.
Mining leases were cancelled and thousands of crores recovered.
