Hegde was also on the civil-society side of the **April 2011** Joint Drafting Committee.

nde4b1ec0441.s: The Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act was enacted in
nde4b1ec0441.x: The governing law is the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1983.
nde4b1ec0441.tq: Discriminate between the founding State Act and later central anti-corruption legislation.
xs: The **AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act** was enacted in **1983** — option **(2)**.
It was amended by the **AP Lokayukta (Amendment) Act, 2024**.
**1973** is Rajasthan's Act; **2013** the central Lokpal Act.
xa: First Lokayukta of integrated AP: **Justice A. Sambasiva Rao** (APPSC **2018** key).
Present Lokayukta: **Justice (Retd) T. Mallikarjuna Rao** (Aug **2026**).
AP covers the **Chief Minister** and **MLAs**.

n1f48a93ac7d.s: A major institutional weakness of many Lokayuktas is that they
o: have no independent investigating wing and depend on the State police or Anti-Corruption Bureau
submit all reports directly to Parliament
have no statutory basis in any State
n1f48a93ac7d.x: Many Lokayuktas lack an independent investigating wing and therefore depend on the State police or the Anti-Corruption Bureau for investigation.
n1f48a93ac7d.tq: Apply the institutional-design distinction between inquiry, investigation and prosecution.
xs: Many Lokayuktas have **no independent investigating wing** and **depend on state police/ACB** — option **(1)**.
Reports go to the **Governor**, not Parliament.
They do take **citizens' complaints** and rest on **State Acts**.
xa: Other criticisms: **no uniformity**, **advisory powers**, executive attempts to **dilute powers** (e.g. **Delhi**).
Karnataka is an exception with its own **Lokayukta Police**.
CDI suggests **constitutional status** and a **model Lokayukta Act**.

n7258b9625a3.s: Who was the first Lokayukta of the integrated State of Andhra Pradesh?
n7258b9625a3.x: Justice A. Sambasiva Rao was the first Lokayukta of the integrated State of Andhra Pradesh.
n7258b9625a3.tq: Discriminate between the first office-holder, the present office-holder and other anti-corruption personalities.
xs: **Justice A. Sambasiva Rao** was the first Lokayukta of integrated AP — option **(2)**.
This is the APPSC **2018** PYQ key.
**T. Mallikarjuna Rao** is the present Lokayukta; **P. Rajani** is Upa-Lokayukta; **N. Santosh Hegde** was Karnataka's.
xa: AP's law: **AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1983**.
Mallikarjuna Rao was appointed by **Governor S. Abdul Nazeer** in **Aug 2026**.
AP requires a **judicial qualification** for the Lokayukta.

ndf44577db93.s: In August 2026, Justice (retd.) T. Mallikarjuna Rao was appointed Lokayukta of Andhra Pradesh by the:
o: Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh High Court
ndf44577db93.x: Governor S. Abdul Nazeer appointed him under Section 3(1) on the recommendation of the Selection Committee.
xa: Term: **five years** under **Section 5** (G.O. MS No.**157**, **20 Aug 2026**).
Mallikarjuna Rao is a former **AP High Court** judge.
Before him, **Upa-Lokayukta P. Rajani** held all functions during **2025**.

n7ad6fba5d28.s: The State Vigilance Commission in Andhra Pradesh was set up, on the pattern of the CVC, from:
n7ad6fba5d28.x: The AP State Vigilance Commission was set up from 1964 on the CVC pattern; trap cases are handled by the Anti-Corruption Bureau.
xa: The ACB investigates **Prevention of Corruption Act** offences, incl. **disproportionate-assets** cases.
AP ACB is headed at IG level by **R. Jayalakshmi** (Apr **2026**).
The **Lokayukta** is the statutory ombudsman under the **1983 Act**.

n8cbd8ed6eb0.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the Lokayukta in Andhra Pradesh?
n8cbd8ed6eb0.x: The AP Lokayukta offers informal procedure, easy access, almost free and prompt service, and independence from executive control. Interpreting the Constitution is not one of its features (APPSC 2019 PYQ).
n8cbd8ed6eb0.tq: Lokayukta is an ombudsman, not a constitutional interpreter.
xs: **Interpreting the Constitution** is NOT a feature of the AP Lokayukta — option **(3)**.
Its features: **informal procedure**, **easy access**, **almost free and prompt service**, **independence from executive control**.
This is the APPSC **2019** PYQ.
xa: It is a **statutory ombudsman** under the **1983 Act**.
It takes citizens' complaints, inquires and **recommends**; reports to the **Governor**.
It covers the **Chief Minister** and **MLAs**.

nbdf4a1ce922.s: In the January 2026 split verdict of the Supreme Court on Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, which judge held Section 17A unconstitutional?
nbdf4a1ce922.x: Justice B.V. Nagarathna held Section 17A unconstitutional. Justice K.V. Viswanathan upheld prior approval only if based on a binding opinion of the Lokpal/Lokayukta. Khanwilkar is the Lokpal Chairperson and Surya Kant the CJI; neither was part of the split.
nbdf4a1ce922.tq: 17A split: Nagarathna struck it; Viswanathan read it down via Lokpal opinion.
xs: Justice **B.V. Nagarathna** held **Section 17A** unconstitutional — option **(2)**.
Justice **K.V. Viswanathan** upheld prior approval only on a **binding opinion of the Lokpal/Lokayukta**.
**A.M. Khanwilkar** is the Lokpal chair, not on this bench.
xa: The verdict came on **22 Jan 2026**.
Section 17A is in the **Prevention of Corruption Act**.
The **Mahua Moitra** matter also raised the sanction procedure; the SC agreed to clarify it (**14 Mar 2026**).

nade2b2af75f.s: The Central Bureau of Investigation was set up in 1963 on the recommendation of the
o: Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption
nade2b2af75f.x: The CBI was set up in 1963 following the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption, constituted during 1962–64.
nade2b2af75f.tq: Link an executive agency to the committee whose recommendation led to its creation.
xs: The CBI was set up in **1963** on the **Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption** recommendation — option **(3)**.
The committee sat in **1962-64** (APPCA says **1962-63**).
The **Second ARC (2007)** proposed a new law to replace the DSPE Act; the **Vohra Committee (1993)** looked at the criminal-politician nexus.
xa: The **CVC** was also set up on Santhanam's recommendation, in **1964**.
⚠ **CBI = 1963**, executive resolution, still non-statutory; **CVC = 1964**, statutory only in **2003**.
The CBI was set up on **1 April 1963**.

n1bcb19b1ada.s: The Central Vigilance Commission, set up in 1964 by executive resolution, became a statutory body under the:
n1bcb19b1ada.x: The CVC became statutory under the CVC Act, 2003; it is the apex vigilance body but not a constitutional body.
xa: It was set up on the **Santhanam Committee's** recommendation.
Composition: **Central Vigilance Commissioner + up to 2 Vigilance Commissioners**.
Term: **4 years or age 65**.

n548ed03cd50.s: Which of the following is NOT a recognised criticism or debate about the functioning of the CBI?
o: The ‘caged parrot’ description due to executive control
A constitutional bar on the CBI investigating economic offences
n548ed03cd50.x: No constitutional bar stops the CBI from investigating economic offences; it does handle them. The other three are recognised criticisms or debates.
xa: **Over 9 States** have withdrawn general consent.
**5.4 crore** cases are pending in courts (**25 Jul 2026**).
The CBI is **neither constitutional nor statutory**; its powers come from the **DSPE Act, 1946**.

nc073479aa4f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Central Bureau of Investigation?
o: It is an attached office under the Department of Personnel and Training
It derives its powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946
It was initially set up by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs
nc073479aa4f.x: The CBI is not a constitutional body; it was set up by an MHA resolution and draws its powers from the DSPE Act, 1946.
xa: Precursor: the **Special Police Establishment (1941)**.
Founder Director: **D.P. Kohli** (APPSC **2018** key).
Critics call it a **"caged parrot"** over executive control.

nfdca2eb5cf9.s: In which year was the Central Bureau of Investigation set up?
nfdca2eb5cf9.x: The CBI was set up in 1963, after the Special Police Establishment (1941) and the DSPE Act (1946), and a year before the CVC (1964).
xa: The CVC became statutory under the **CVC Act, 2003**.
The SPE probed bribery and corruption in **war-time supplies**.
The **Vineet Narain** case (**1997**) led to the **2003** DSPE revision.

n1bbb6926092.s: The decision in Vineet Narain v. Union of India (1997) is associated with which of the following changes concerning the CBI?
o: Transfer of CBI control to the Ministry of Finance and a five-year tenure
Transfer of all CBI investigations to the Enforcement Directorate
Abolition of State consent and appointment of the Director by the Lokpal
Superintendence by the CVC and a fixed two-year tenure for the CBI Director
n1bbb6926092.x: The 1997 Vineet Narain judgment gave the CVC superintendence over the CBI and prescribed a fixed two-year tenure for the CBI Director. The DSPE Act was revised accordingly in 2003.
n1bbb6926092.tq: Match the landmark case with its specific institutional consequences rather than later reforms.
xs: **Vineet Narain (1997)** gave the **CVC superintendence** over the CBI and a **fixed two-year tenure** for the Director — option **(4)**.
It also quashed the **"Single Directive"**.
The DSPE Act was revised accordingly in **2003**.
xa: The CBI stays under the **Ministry of Personnel**, not Finance.
The CVC became statutory under the **CVC Act, 2003**.
The **2021** amendments let the tenure run up to **five years**.

n9a33e8dac3b.s: The BHARATPOL portal, launched in January 2025 for real-time Interpol assistance requests, was developed by the:
n9a33e8dac3b.x: BHARATPOL was developed by the CBI for central and State agencies to send Interpol assistance requests.
xa: It puts State and central police on **one platform**.
It uses **Big Data and AI** for fugitive tracking.
The CBI is India's **National Central Bureau** for Interpol.

n0f55e704d9e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's investigating agencies?
o: The Enforcement Directorate enforces the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002
The Enforcement Directorate enforces the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999
The CBI handles only corruption cases and has no role in economic or special crimes
The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence is mainly concerned with anti-smuggling and customs evasion
n0f55e704d9e.x: Apart from corruption cases, the CBI also investigates economic and special crimes.
xa: ⚠ **ED and DRI = Finance**; **CBI = Personnel**.
The ED attaches and confiscates **proceeds of crime**.
The DRI is under the Dept of Revenue (**CBIC**).

nde10be15a0d.s: The Director of the CBI is appointed by the Central Government on the recommendation of a committee comprising the
o: Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Attorney General of India
Union Home Minister, Leader of the largest opposition party and CVC
Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and CVC
Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India or his nominee
nde10be15a0d.x: The committee consists of the Prime Minister as Chairperson, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha or leader of the largest opposition party, and the Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court judge nominated by the CJI.
nde10be15a0d.tq: Split the options by identifying the required judicial member and the chairperson.
xs: The CBI Director is picked by the **PM**, the **Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha** and the **CJI or his nominee** — option **(4)**.
The appointment is made by the **Central Government**.
⚠ **CVC panel = Home Minister**; **CIC panel = PM-nominated Cabinet Minister**; **CBI panel = CJI or SC judge**.
xa: If there is no LoP, the **leader of the largest opposition party** sits.
Tenure: minimum **2 years**, extendable to **5 years** (**2021**).
In **May 2026** the LoP recorded **dissent** over the new Director's selection.

nafe54118b85.s: The Central Vigilance Commissioner is appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee consisting of the
o: Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India
Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India
Union Home Minister, Union Law Minister and Cabinet Secretary
nafe54118b85.x: The CVC panel is PM, Union Home Minister and LoP in the Lok Sabha. Option B mixes in the Lokpal panel's Speaker and CJI; option C is the CBI Director panel; option D is not any statutory panel.
nafe54118b85.tq: CVC: PM + Home Minister + LoP; CBI: PM + LoP + CJI.
xs: The CVC panel is the **PM**, **Union Home Minister** and **LoP in the Lok Sabha** — option **(1)**.
The **Speaker** and **CJI** belong to the **Lokpal** panel; **PM, LoP and CJI** is the **CBI Director** panel.
⚠ **CVC panel = Home Minister**; **CIC panel = PM-nominated Cabinet Minister**.
xa: The **President** appoints the CVC.
CEC and ECs: **PM**, a Union Cabinet Minister and LoP (**2023** Act).
State ICs: **CM**, **LoP in the Assembly** and a CM-nominated minister; the **Chief Justice is not a member**.

n56f0258a0b7.s: The Chief Information Commissioner at the Centre is appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee comprising the
o: Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Union Home Minister
Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
n56f0258a0b7.x: The CIC panel is PM, LoP in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM; the CJI is not a member. Option D is the CVC panel; options A and C mix in members of other panels.
n56f0258a0b7.tq: CIC: PM + LoP + PM's minister; no CJI.
xs: The CIC panel is the **PM**, the **LoP in the Lok Sabha** and a **Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM** — option **(2)**.
The **CJI** is not a member.
**PM, Home Minister and LoP** is the **CVC** panel.
xa: ⚠ **CVC panel = Home Minister**; **CIC panel = PM-nominated Cabinet Minister**; **CBI panel = CJI or SC judge**.
The CIC has Chief IC + **up to 10 ICs**; constituted **12 Oct 2005**.
Under the **2019** Rules the term is **3 years**.

n80f869da1f3.s: Under the 2023 Act, the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners are appointed by the President on the recommendation of
o: the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
the Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chief Justice of India
n80f869da1f3.x: The 2023 Act panel is the PM, a Union Cabinet Minister and the LoP in the Lok Sabha. The CJI is not a member (option B is the CBI Director panel pattern); option C wrongly adds the Speaker and CJI; the Cabinet alone does not recommend.
xs: Under the **2023 Act**, the CEC and ECs are recommended by the **PM**, a **Union Cabinet Minister** and the **LoP in Lok Sabha** — option **(1)**.
The **CJI** is not on this panel; **PM, LoP and CJI** is the **CBI Director** pattern.
The **Speaker** and CJI sit on the **Lokpal** panel.
xa: The **President** appoints the CEC and ECs.
A **State Election Commissioner** is appointed by the **Governor** under State law.
Earlier, the CIC's pay equalled the **CEC**'s.

ne5321b1d1f0.s: Who was the founder Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation?
ne5321b1d1f0.x: D.P. Kohli was the founder Director of the CBI (APPSC 2018 key); an annual memorial lecture is held in his name. K. Santhanam headed the committee that recommended the CBI; Vineet Narain was the petitioner in the 1997 case; Vohra headed the 1993 committee on the criminal-politician nexus.
xs: **D.P. Kohli** was the founder Director of the CBI (APPSC **2018** key) — option **(1)**.
**K. Santhanam** headed the committee that recommended the CBI; **Vineet Narain** was the **1997** petitioner.
**Vohra** headed the **1993** committee on the criminal-politician-bureaucrat nexus.
xa: The **22nd** D.P. Kohli Memorial Lecture was given by CJI **Surya Kant** (**22 Apr 2026**).
The CBI was set up by an **MHA resolution** in **1963**.
It is now an **attached office** under the **Ministry of Personnel**.

nc5778e8d90f.s: Under Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946, the Central Bureau of Investigation requires the consent of a State Government primarily because:
o: The CBI is constitutionally subordinate to State Governments
Criminal law is exclusively a Union subject
Police is a subject in the State List
The Lokpal Act prohibits investigation without State approval
nc5778e8d90f.x: Section 6 of the DSPE Act requires general or specific consent of the State concerned because police is included in Entry 2 of the State List.
nc5778e8d90f.tq: Identify the constitutional subject behind the statutory requirement instead of confusing it with the CBI's administrative control.
xs: The CBI needs State consent because **police is a State List** subject (**Entry 2**) — option **(3)**.
**Section 6** of the DSPE Act requires the State's **general or specific consent**.
The CBI is not subordinate to the States, and the Lokpal Act is not the source.
xa: **Over 9 States** have withdrawn general consent, among them **Tamil Nadu, Telangana and Punjab**.
The Centre increasingly uses the **ED** under the **PMLA** instead.
**AP** withdrew consent in **Nov 2018** and restored it in **June 2019**.

n4b401017db1.s: In which year was Vineet Narain v. Union of India decided?
n4b401017db1.x: Vineet Narain was decided in 1997; the DSPE Act was revised in 2003 in response to its directions.
xa: Vineet Narain quashed the **"Single Directive"**.
The **CVC** also became statutory in **2003**.
**Tamil Nadu, Telangana and Punjab** are among States that withdrew consent.

necaa9fb4218.s: The present procedure for selection of the CBI Director through a committee headed by the Prime Minister was introduced through the
necaa9fb4218.x: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 amended the DSPE framework and introduced the present three-member selection committee. Until 2014, the process operated under the DSPE Act alone.
necaa9fb4218.tq: Use the legal-amendment trap by separating the original statute from the later reforming Act.
xs: The PM-led committee came through the **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013**, which amended the **DSPE Act** — option **(2)**.
Before **2014**, the Director was chosen on a committee headed by the **CVC**, under the DSPE Act alone.
The **CVC Act, 2003** gave the CVC superintendence, not this committee.
xa: Committee: **PM (chair)**, **LoP in Lok Sabha**, **CJI or an SC judge nominated by the CJI**.
Director's minimum tenure: **2 years**.
The **Vineet Narain** case had fixed a **two-year tenure** for the Director.

ne1d19155e6f.s: With reference to the Central Vigilance Commission, which one of the following is NOT correct?
o: It recommends the Director of Prosecution of the CBI.
It directly conducts the trial of all corruption cases investigated by the CBI.
Its committee recommends CBI officers of the rank of Superintendent of Police and above.
It exercises superintendence over the CBI in cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
ne1d19155e6f.x: The CVC exercises specified superintendence and makes recommendations, but it does not conduct the trials of CBI corruption cases.
ne1d19155e6f.tq: Find the option that assigns a judicial trial function to a vigilance body.
xs: The CVC does NOT **directly conduct the trial** of CBI corruption cases — option **(2)**.
It **recommends** the CBI's **Director of Prosecution** and leads the committee choosing officers of **SP rank and above**.
It has **superintendence over the CBI** for **Prevention of Corruption Act** cases.
xa: The Director of Prosecution is not below **Joint Secretary** rank and serves **2 years**.
The CVC is the competent authority under the **Whistle Blowers Act**.
CVC annual report (**2 Sep 2026**): **755** corruption cases pending investigation, including **13 Lokpal references**.

ndfd35a6f067.s: Which of the following correctly describes the composition and tenure of the Central Vigilance Commission?
o: One Central Vigilance Commissioner and exactly four Vigilance Commissioners; five years without an age limit
One Central Vigilance Commissioner and up to two Vigilance Commissioners; four years or until attaining 65 years, whichever is earlier
A Chairperson and up to eight members; six years or until 70 years
The CVC consists only of the Home Minister and the Cabinet Secretary
ndfd35a6f067.x: The Commission consists of the Central Vigilance Commissioner and up to two Vigilance Commissioners. Their tenure is four years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
ndfd35a6f067.tq: Combine institutional composition with tenure and age limits.
xs: The CVC is a **Central Vigilance Commissioner + up to two Vigilance Commissioners**, for **4 years or age 65** — option **(2)**.
They are appointed by the **President**.
A Chairperson + up to eight members describes the **Lokpal**, not the CVC.
xa: The panel: **PM**, **Union Home Minister** and **LoP in Lok Sabha**.
The CVC has superintendence over the CBI in **PC Act** cases.
It became statutory in **2003**.

n5d25a7eb6ae.s: The Central Vigilance Commissioner is appointed by the:
n5d25a7eb6ae.x: The Central Vigilance Commissioner is appointed by the President, not the Prime Minister.
xa: The CVC panel: **PM**, **Union Home Minister**, **LoP in Lok Sabha**.
APPSC **2025** keyed "CIC by President, SIC by Governor" as correct pairs.
The **CBI Director** is appointed by the **Central Government**.

nf33838bd596.s: An RTI application concerns a person’s life or liberty. The information should ordinarily be provided within
nf33838bd596.x: When the application concerns life or liberty, information must be provided within 48 hours. The ordinary time limit is 30 days.
nf33838bd596.tq: Apply the special exception to the ordinary statutory time limit.
xs: Information concerning **life or liberty** must be given within **48 hours** — option **(2)**.
This is **Section 7** of the RTI Act.
The normal reply period is **30 days**.
xa: **BPL applicants** get information free.
**Public Information Officers** are designated by each public authority (**Section 5**).
The CIC was constituted under **Section 12**.

nb639015758e.s: Which of the following best describes the amendment made to Section 8(1)(j) of the Right to Information Act by the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023?
o: It transferred RTI appeals involving personal data to the CVC
It restricted exemption only to information held by private companies
It made all personal information mandatorily disclosable
It exempted personal information outright and removed the public-interest override
nb639015758e.x: The DPDP Act, 2023 amended Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act to exempt personal information outright, thereby removing the earlier public-interest override.
nb639015758e.tq: Distinguish an outright exemption from the earlier balancing approach involving public interest.
xs: The **DPDP Act 2023** made **Section 8(1)(j)** exempt **personal information outright**, removing the **public-interest override** — option **(4)**.
It did not make personal information disclosable or move appeals to the CVC.
The Congress president said it "**diluted** the RTI Act's public interest clause" (**31 Jan 2026**).
xa: The **Economic Survey 2025-26** called for a **"re-examination"** of the RTI Act.
It floated a possible **"ministerial veto"**.
Criticism of RTI: **backlogs and vacancies**, misuse of **Section 8**, attacks on RTI activists (**100+ killed**).

ne40ed5af66f.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 is associated with which of the following in relation to the RTI Act?
o: A call for its 're-examination', including a possible 'ministerial veto'
A proposal to extend RTI to all private companies
Restoration of the public-interest override in Section 8(1)(j)
Making the CIC a constitutional body
ne40ed5af66f.x: The Survey called for a re-examination of the RTI Act, suggesting exemptions for confidential service records and draft policy discussions and floating a possible ministerial veto. It did not propose extension to private companies, restoration of the override (removed by the DPDP Act) or constitutional status.
xs: The **Economic Survey 2025-26** called for a **'re-examination'** of the RTI Act, including a possible **'ministerial veto'** — option **(1)**.
It suggested exemptions for **confidential service records** and **draft policy discussions**.
The public-interest override was **removed** by the **DPDP Act 2023**, not restored.
xa: The DPDP change was to **Section 8(1)(j)**.
The CIC is a **statutory**, not constitutional, body.
The **RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019** let the Centre fix tenure and salaries.

na048af319d1.s: The anti-corruption work of the CBI is mainly concerned with
o: Central Government and Union Territory employees and their public sector undertakings
Foreign diplomatic personnel stationed in India
Only elected representatives of State Legislatures
na048af319d1.x: The CBI’s anti-corruption mandate mainly covers Central Government and Union Territory employees and their public sector undertakings.
na048af319d1.tq: Use the scope of jurisdiction to distinguish the correct category of officials.
xs: CBI anti-corruption work mainly covers **Central Government** and **UT employees** and their **PSUs** — option **(1)**.
State matters need **State consent** under **Section 6** of the DSPE Act.
Its wider mandate: **corruption, economic offences and conventional crime**.
xa: "Police" is a **State List** subject (**Entry 2**).
**Over 9 States** have withdrawn general consent.
For **PC Act** cases, superintendence lies with the **CVC**.

nc45d92172d3.s: Under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, the Director of the Enforcement Directorate may:
o: Attach property believed to be proceeds of crime
Grant general consent to CBI investigations in a State
Appoint the Director of the CBI
nc45d92172d3.x: Under the PMLA, the ED Director may attach property believed to be proceeds of crime.
xa: The ED enforces **PMLA 2002** and **FEMA 1999**.
It is under **Finance - Dept of Revenue**.
The Centre increasingly uses the ED where States withdraw **CBI consent**.

nd171f99e319.s: The Enforcement Directorate functions under which Ministry/Department?
o: Ministry of Finance, Department of Revenue
nd171f99e319.x: The ED is under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance. The CBI is under the Ministry of Personnel (DoPT); the Home Ministry and Law Ministry do not control the ED.
xs: The ED is under the **Ministry of Finance, Department of Revenue** — option **(3)**.
The **CBI** is under the **Ministry of Personnel** (DoPT).
⚠ **ED and DRI = Finance**; **CBI = Personnel**.
xa: The ED enforces **PMLA 2002** and **FEMA 1999**.
The **DRI** handles anti-smuggling and customs evasion.
The ED and CBI Directors' tenure can run to **five years** (**2021**).

n1e5760cc2fa.s: The Anti-Corruption Bureau in Andhra Pradesh is best described as:
o: A Union agency operating only under the FEMA
A State police agency dealing with offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act
A statutory commission appointed by the President
A judicial body hearing appeals against the State Vigilance Commission
n1e5760cc2fa.x: The Andhra Pradesh ACB is a State police agency that deals with offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
n1e5760cc2fa.tq: Distinguish a State police agency from a commission, court or Union enforcement agency.
xs: The **AP ACB** is a **State police agency** for **PC Act** offences — option **(2)**.
It is not a Union FEMA agency or a commission.
It is headed by **IGP R. Jayalakshmi**.
xa: The **State Vigilance Commission (1964)** changed the **SPSC's** disciplinary role.
**AP** withdrew CBI consent in **Nov 2018** and restored it in **June 2019**.
The ED, not the ACB, enforces **FEMA**.

o: the nexus between criminals, politicians and bureaucrats
the setting up of the Central Bureau of Investigation
the creation of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas
the tenure of the CBI Director
ncf9f428bd18.x: The Vohra Committee (1993) dealt with the criminal-politician-bureaucrat nexus. The CBI came from the Santhanam Committee; Lokpal/Lokayukta from the First ARC; the CBI Director's tenure from Vineet Narain and later amendments.
xs: The **Vohra Committee (1993)** examined the **nexus between criminals, politicians and bureaucrats** — option **(1)**.
The CBI came from the **Santhanam Committee (1962-64)**.
The CBI Director's **two-year tenure** came from **Vineet Narain (1997)**.
xa: The **Second ARC (2007)** proposed a new law to replace the DSPE Act.
The CBI was set up on **1 April 1963** by an **MHA resolution**.
The Director's tenure was made extendable to **5 years** in **2021**.

n9e55278410f.s: SETUs, supported by NITI Aayog under the State Support Mission, are intended to help States prepare:
n9e55278410f.x: NITI Aayog assists States in setting up State Economic and Transformation Units, or SETUs, to prepare State Vision@2047 plans.
n9e55278410f.tq: Expand the acronym and link the institutional support to its stated planning output.
xs: **SETUs** help States prepare **"State Vision@2047"** plans — option **(2)**.
SETU = **State Economic and Transformation Unit**.
NITI helps set them up under the **State Support Mission** (**2026**).
xa: ⚠ **Team India Hub** = States–Centre engagement; **Knowledge and Innovation Hub** = think-tank.
Criticism: NITI is an **advisory body** whose influence depends on **persuasion**.
CM Naidu attended the **11th Governing Council** (June **2026**).

n2d436d93355.s: Which NITI Aayog vertical leads the engagement of States with the Centre?
n2d436d93355.x: The Team India Hub is responsible for leading engagement between the States and the Centre.
n2d436d93355.tq: Match the functional description with the correct named vertical.
xs: The **Team India Hub** leads the engagement of States with the Centre — option **(4)**.
This was asked in APPSC **2018**.
The **Knowledge and Innovation Hub** builds think-tank capacity; the **Atal Innovation Mission** promotes innovation.
xa: **Regional Councils** are chaired by the **PM or his nominee**.
The **State Support Mission** helps States set up **SETUs**.
The **Governing Council** usually meets **once a year**.

n09dacbf5487.s: Which institution runs the Aspirational Districts Programme?
n09dacbf5487.x: The Aspirational Districts Programme is run by NITI Aayog.
xs: The **Aspirational Districts Programme** is run by **NITI Aayog** — option **(4)**.
It was launched in **January 2018**.
It covers **112 districts** with **49 indicators** in **5 themes**.
xa: Strategy: **3 Cs - Convergence, Collaboration, Competition**.
**Monthly delta ranking** on the **Champions of Change** dashboard.
The **Aspirational Blocks Programme** followed in **Jan 2023**.

nfa0e5ba1d3a.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the five themes of the Aspirational Districts Programme?
nfa0e5ba1d3a.x: The five themes include Health and Nutrition, Education, Agriculture and Water Resources, Financial Inclusion and Skill Development, and Basic Infrastructure. Urban Transport and Housing is not listed as a theme.
nfa0e5ba1d3a.tq: Find the option outside the official thematic list.
xs: **Urban Transport and Housing** is NOT an ADP theme — option **(4)**.
The five themes: **Health and Nutrition**, **Education**, **Agriculture and Water Resources**, **Financial Inclusion and Skill Development**, **Basic Infrastructure**.
Together they carry **49 indicators**.
xa: Weights: **Health and Nutrition 30%**; **Agriculture and Water Resources 20%**.
**Financial Inclusion and Skill Development 10%**; **Basic Infrastructure 10%**.
The **Aspirational Blocks Programme** follows the same theme model.

n62d57803f35.s: The Aspirational Districts Programme, launched in January 2018, covers:
o: 112 districts using 49 indicators across five themes
112 districts using 49 indicators across ten themes
n62d57803f35.x: The Aspirational Districts Programme was launched in January 2018 and covers 112 districts, using 49 indicators grouped under five themes.
n62d57803f35.tq: Separate the programme’s coverage, indicator count and thematic structure.
xs: The ADP covers **112 districts** with **49 indicators** across **five themes** — option **(1)**.
It was launched in **January 2018**.
⚠ **513** is the **Aspirational Blocks** count; ABP uses about **40** indicators.
xa: ⚠ **112 districts / 49 indicators** (ADP) vs **513 blocks / about 40 indicators** (ABP).
Strategy: **3 Cs**.
AP's ADP districts now: **Alluri Sitharama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam, YSR Kadapa**.

na759f4de9a4.s: The Aspirational Blocks Programme was launched in January 2023 for:
o: 329 blocks in 513 districts across all States
513 districts in 329 blocks across 27 States and 4 Union Territories
513 blocks in 329 districts across 27 States and 4 Union Territories
na759f4de9a4.x: The Aspirational Blocks Programme, launched in January 2023, covers 513 blocks in 329 districts across 27 States and 4 Union Territories.
na759f4de9a4.tq: Check the direction of the block-district relationship and the exact coverage figures.
xs: The ABP (**Jan 2023**) covers **513 blocks in 329 districts** across **27 States, 4 UTs** — option **(4)**.
Option 3 swaps blocks and districts.
The earlier figure was "**500**" blocks; **513** is from the NITI Annual Report **2025-26**.
xa: It follows the **ADP** theme model.
It tracks about **40 key indicators**.
**Sampoornata Abhiyan 2.0** targets **6 KPIs** in the blocks.

ncca7c55209a.s: The strategy of the Aspirational Districts Programme is based on which of the following?
ncca7c55209a.x: The programme uses the three-dimensional strategy of Convergence, Collaboration and Competition.
ncca7c55209a.tq: Discriminate between similar alliterative policy terms.
xs: The ADP strategy is the **3 Cs — Convergence, Collaboration, Competition** — option **(3)**.
Competition runs through the **monthly delta ranking**.
Rankings appear on the **Champions of Change** dashboard.
xa: ADP: **112 districts**, **49 indicators**, **5 themes**.
Highest weight: **Health and Nutrition 30%**.
**Sampoornata Abhiyan 2.0** saturates **5 KPIs** in ADs and **6 KPIs** in ABs.

n25e2fbdadd7.s: The SDG India Index primarily measures:
o: States’ progress towards Sustainable Development Goals
Multidimensional poverty through only health indicators
n25e2fbdadd7.x: The SDG India Index assesses the progress of States and Union Territories towards the Sustainable Development Goals.
n25e2fbdadd7.tq: Match the index with its subject rather than with another NITI Aayog index.
xs: The **SDG India Index** measures **States' progress** on the **Sustainable Development Goals** — option **(1)**.
Its **4th edition 2023-24** (July **2024**) used **113 indicators**.
Poverty is the **National MPI**; e-mobility the **India Electric Mobility Index**; export readiness the **EPI**.
xa: AP scored **74**, a **"Front Runner"**.
AP ranks **1st** on **SDG 7** and **2nd** on **SDG 14**.
The National MPI covers **health, education, standard of living**.

n96451712f77.s: In the Export Preparedness Index 2024, released in January 2026, Andhra Pradesh was ranked
n96451712f77.x: Andhra Pradesh was ranked fifth among large States in the Export Preparedness Index 2024.
n96451712f77.tq: Distinguish the specific index, edition and category before selecting the rank.
xs: In **EPI 2024** (released **Jan 2026**) AP ranked **fifth among large States** — option **(2)**.
Earlier it was **8th** in **EPI 2022**.
EPI 2024 is the **4th edition**; the first came in **2020**.
xa: The EPI is made with the **Institute for Competitiveness**.
AP scored **74** ("**Front Runner**") in the SDG India Index **2023-24**.
AP ranks **1st** on **SDG 7**.

n5112899ace0.s: Which body is now the nodal agency for poverty estimation in India?
n5112899ace0.x: NITI Aayog (earlier the Planning Commission) is the nodal agency for poverty estimation and also brings out the National MPI. The Finance Commission, RBI and Rural Development Ministry are not the nodal agency.
n5112899ace0.tq: Poverty estimation: Planning Commission -> NITI Aayog.
xs: **NITI Aayog** is the **nodal agency for poverty estimation** — option **(2)**.
Earlier this was the **Planning Commission**.
NITI also brings out the **National MPI** (health, education, standard of living).
xa: Vizianagaram's **poverty headcount** is **8.66%**.
NITI also publishes the **SDG India Index** and **EPI**.
NITI is an **advisory body** without funds or statutory backing.

nfdfec1e3837.s: In the 4th edition (2023-24) of NITI Aayog's SDG India Index, Andhra Pradesh
o: scored 74 and was placed in the 'Front Runner' category
was not ranked because it used only 49 indicators
nfdfec1e3837.x: The 2023-24 edition (released July 2024) used 113 indicators; AP scored 74 and was a 'Front Runner'. The other options give wrong scores or categories, and 49 is the ADP indicator count, not the SDG Index's.
nfdfec1e3837.tq: SDG Index 2023-24: 113 indicators; AP 74, Front Runner.
xs: In the **4th edition (2023-24)** AP **scored 74** and was a **'Front Runner'** — option **(1)**.
That edition (July **2024**) used **113 indicators**.
**49** is the **ADP** indicator count, not the SDG Index's.
xa: AP ranks **1st** on **SDG 7** and **2nd** on **SDG 14**.
AP is **5th** among large States in **EPI 2024**.
The SDG India Index measures **States' progress on SDGs**.

nacdadcb9ee4.s: Which of the following districts constituted the original group of Aspirational Districts in Andhra Pradesh?
nacdadcb9ee4.x: The original aspirational districts of Andhra Pradesh were Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam and YSR Kadapa.
nacdadcb9ee4.tq: Recall the exact state-specific district combination.
xs: AP's original aspirational districts were **Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam and YSR Kadapa** — option **(3)**.
Visakhapatnam's agency area now lies in **ASR district**.
⚠ Lists naming **Kurnool** and **Anantapur** are WRONG.
xa: Current list (**2025-26**): **Alluri Sitharama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam, YSR Kadapa**.
Vizianagaram's poverty headcount: **8.66%**.
ASR's literacy is the lowest at **44.67%**.

n1c3c8cf7610.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the forms of decentralisation?
o: Delegation transfers powers to elected local governments with their own revenue
Deconcentration shifts work to field offices of the same government
Delegation entrusts tasks to semi-autonomous bodies
Devolution transfers powers to elected local governments with their own mandate and revenue
n1c3c8cf7610.x: Delegation entrusts tasks to semi-autonomous bodies; transferring powers to elected local governments with their own mandate and revenue is devolution.
xa: Under deconcentration the Centre keeps **full control** — the weakest form.
Delegated power **can be withdrawn at will**; devolved power cannot.
Devolution was attempted by the **73rd and 74th Amendments**.

nef14ecf3fb5.s: A State has regularly elected local bodies, but they lack adequate funds to perform their assigned functions. Which conclusion most accurately follows from the principle of decentralisation?
o: Without fiscal decentralisation, elected local bodies may remain powerless.
Fiscal decentralisation necessarily eliminates the role of State Governments.
Local bodies become constitutionally invalid if they lack sufficient funds.
Election alone automatically ensures effective local self-government.
nef14ecf3fb5.x: Political decentralisation through elections is insufficient by itself. Local bodies require fiscal decentralisation and adequate financial powers to exercise their responsibilities effectively.
nef14ecf3fb5.tq: Apply the distinction between elected institutions and the financial capacity required to make decentralisation effective.
xs: **Without fiscal decentralisation, elected local bodies may remain powerless** — option **(1)**.
Election gives **political** decentralisation but not the power to **spend and raise** funds.
India transferred the **least fiscal** power.
xa: The **3Fs**: **Funds, Functions, Functionaries**.
Incomplete devolution leaves PRIs as **implementing agencies**.
Devolving taxes and grants is **voluntary** for States.

n5bc9084c8ed.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of decentralisation?
n5bc9084c8ed.x: Autonomy, people's participation and empowerment of local communities are features of decentralisation. Instilling non-confidence among local communities is not a feature.
n5bc9084c8ed.tq: Find the one negative formulation that does not belong to the standard features.
xs: **Instilling non-confidence among local communities** is NOT a feature — option **(4)**.
The features are **autonomy**, **people's participation** and **empowerment of local communities**.
This trap appeared in BPSC **2020**.
xa: Arguments for decentralisation: **proximity and information**, **participation**, **accountability and speed**, **political education**.
**Participation** turns subjects into citizens.
Decentralisation transfers authority **downward**.

nded9a6f6844.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principle of subsidiarity?
o: Every function must be performed by the Union Government for uniformity
Local bodies may perform only those functions expressly delegated temporarily by the Centre
A function should be performed at the lowest level competent to do so and move upward only when that level cannot perform it
The highest tier should decide all functions and lower tiers should implement them
nded9a6f6844.x: Subsidiarity assigns a function to the lowest competent level and permits movement to a higher level only when the lower level cannot perform it adequately.
nded9a6f6844.tq: Apply the lowest-competent-level test to the institutional scenario.
xs: **Subsidiarity**: a function is done at the **lowest level competent to do it**, moving up only if that level cannot — option **(3)**.
The **2nd ARC** used it to divide functions among the **three tiers**.
Options giving everything to the Union or the top tier are the opposite.
xa: The **3Fs** are **Funds, Functions, Functionaries**.
Incomplete devolution leaves PRIs as **implementing agencies**.
⚠ Power that can be withdrawn at will is **delegation**, not devolution.

ndd1c206501c.s: In the context of Panchayati Raj Institutions, the three Fs stand for:
ndd1c206501c.x: The three Fs are Funds, Functions and Functionaries. Effective devolution requires all three rather than merely assigning responsibilities on paper.
ndd1c206501c.tq: Use the standard acronym expansion as a direct institutional recall question.
xs: The **3Fs** are **Funds, Functions, Functionaries** — option **(2)**.
Incomplete devolution of these leaves PRIs as **implementing agencies**.
The other expansions are not used.
xa: **Subsidiarity**: function at the **lowest competent level**.
India transferred the **least fiscal** power.
Devolving subjects, taxes and grants is **voluntary** for States.

nindian-polity-37-11.s: Which of the following is NOT a functional area of local government?
nindian-polity-37-11.x: Public health, sanitation and water supply are local functions; judicial review belongs to the higher courts.
n: Local self-government includes public health. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Local self-government includes sanitation. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Local self-government includes water supply. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Judicial Review is not a local-government function. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xa: **Rural development** is another listed local function.
⚠ Maintenance of **public order** is **not** a local-government function either.
⚠ Instilling **non-confidence** among local communities is **not** a feature of decentralisation (BPSC 2020).
Test: if the transferring authority can take power back at will → **delegation, not devolution**.

n04dad558d25.s: The Gandhian conception of village self-government is best represented by which one of the following?
o: A centralised planned state based on heavy industry
A republic of self-sufficient villages with decentralised economic and political power
A system of village administration controlled by departmental headquarters
A local-government system limited to implementation of centrally prepared plans
n04dad558d25.x: Gandhi advocated Gram Swaraj, conceived as a republic of self-sufficient villages with decentralised economic and political power.
n04dad558d25.tq: Use the direct contrast between the Gandhian and Nehruvian models.
xs: Gandhi's **Gram Swaraj** was a **republic of self-sufficient villages** with **decentralised economic and political power** — option **(2)**.
A **centralised planned state with heavy industry** was the **Nehruvian** view.
Gandhi wanted **self-contained villages**, cottage industry, **swadeshi, sarvodaya and trusteeship**.
xa: The **Gandhian Plan (1944)** by **Sriman Narayan Agarwal** reflected Gram Swaraj.
**Art. 40** was a compromise between **Gandhi** and **Ambedkar**.
⚠ **Ambedkar** saw the village as a seat of **caste domination**.

nbaa06fe3026.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Nehruvian approach to state and development?
o: A centralised planned state with emphasis on heavy industry
A state without central planning or national industrial priorities
A republic of self-sufficient villages based on cottage industries
Complete fiscal autonomy for village panchayats from the beginning of planning
nbaa06fe3026.x: The Nehruvian approach favoured a centralised planned state with heavy industry, as reflected in the National Planning Committee and the Bombay Plan.
nbaa06fe3026.tq: Use the ideology-based contrast and connect Nehruvian planning with heavy industry.
xs: The Nehruvian approach was a **centralised planned state** with **heavy industry** — option **(1)**.
It was like the **NPC** and **Bombay Plan**.
A republic of self-sufficient villages is **Gandhi's** Gram Swaraj.
xa: The **Community Development Programme (1952)** was run **top-down**.
Yet Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at **Nagaur (Rajasthan)** on **2 Oct 1959**.
In the **1960s** planning grew more centralised.

nf8c1cf2b5b1.s: On 4 November 1948, B.R. Ambedkar described the Indian village as which of the following?
o: The primary constitutional unit protected from all central authority
A seat of caste domination and a sink of localism, ignorance, narrow-mindedness and communalism
A model of decentralised economic and political power
nf8c1cf2b5b1.x: Ambedkar criticised the village as a seat of caste domination and called it a sink of localism, a den of ignorance, narrow-mindedness and communalism on 4 November 1948.
nf8c1cf2b5b1.tq: Use the exact descriptive expression and the associated date as the recall cue.
xs: Ambedkar called the village a seat of **caste domination** and "a **sink of localism**, a **den of ignorance, narrow-mindedness and communalism**" — option **(3)**.
He said this in the Constituent Assembly on **4 Nov 1948**.
A republic of self-sufficient villages is **Gandhi's** view.
xa: Ambedkar preferred **the individual** as unit of the republic.
**Art. 40** reconciled the two views: panchayats **named but non-justiciable**.
Gandhi's model: **Gram Swaraj**.

ne5abf1cd92d.s: Article 40, on organising village panchayats, is a:
ne5abf1cd92d.x: Article 40 is a Directive Principle in Part IV; it is non-justiciable.
xa: Art. 40 asks the State to **organise village panchayats** as **units of self-government**.
The **73rd Amendment** gave it practical shape.
It balanced **Gandhi's** Gram Swaraj with **Ambedkar's** reservations.

nb8aa8ddd962.s: Article 40 is generally regarded as a compromise between which two perspectives?
o: The Gandhian advocacy of panchayats and Ambedkar's reservations about the village
The Union List and the State List
The Nehruvian advocacy of heavy industry and the Gandhian advocacy of cottage industry
nb8aa8ddd962.x: Article 40 represented a compromise: panchayats were named as an objective, reflecting the Gandhian position, but the provision was made non-justiciable, accommodating Ambedkar's reservations.
nb8aa8ddd962.tq: Identify the constitutional compromise by linking the institutional provision with the two contrasting viewpoints.
xs: **Art. 40** is a compromise between **Gandhian advocacy of panchayats** and **Ambedkar's reservations about the village** — option **(1)**.
Panchayats were **named** (Gandhi) but made **non-justiciable** (Ambedkar).
Heavy industry vs cottage industry is the **Nehru-Gandhi** contrast, not Art. 40.
xa: Ambedkar: village = **caste domination**; preferred unit = **the individual**.
Gandhi: **Gram Swaraj**.
The **73rd Amendment** gave Art. 40 its practical shape.

na6bbf2b0e78.s: Despite favouring a centralised planned state, Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at
na6bbf2b0e78.x: Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at Nagaur in Rajasthan on 2 October 1959. Andhra Pradesh followed on 1 November 1959; 1952 is the Community Development Programme year; January 1957 is when the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was appointed.
na6bbf2b0e78.tq: Nagaur, 2 Oct 1959 - Rajasthan first, AP next.
xs: Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at **Nagaur, Rajasthan, on 2 October 1959** — option **(1)**.
This was despite his preference for a **centralised planned state**.
**1952** is the **Community Development Programme** year.
xa: The CDP was run **top-down**.
The Nehruvian model resembled the **NPC** and **Bombay Plan**.
**Rajiv Gandhi's 64th Amendment Bill** came in **1989**.

n8753d307951.s: Why did the 64th Amendment Bill of 1989 fail to become law?
o: It passed the Lok Sabha but failed in the Rajya Sabha amid fears of centralisation
It was rejected by the Supreme Court for violating Article 40
It failed to secure passage in the Lok Sabha because it opposed decentralisation
It lapsed because the State legislatures refused to ratify it unanimously
n8753d307951.x: The 64th Amendment Bill, associated with Rajiv Gandhi, passed the Lok Sabha but failed in the Rajya Sabha because of fears that it would promote centralisation.
n8753d307951.tq: Track the legislative chamber and the specific reason for failure rather than merely recalling the year.
xs: The **64th Amendment Bill (1989)** **passed the Lok Sabha but failed in the Rajya Sabha** amid **fears of centralisation** — option **(1)**.
⚠ It failed in the **Rajya Sabha**, not the Lok Sabha.
It was **Rajiv Gandhi's** Bill.
xa: The **V.P. Singh Bill (1990)** lapsed.
The **73rd and 74th Amendments** finally attempted devolution.
**Art. 40** got practical shape from the 73rd Amendment.

nindian-polity-37-1.s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to organise Village Panchayats as units of self-government?
nindian-polity-37-1.x: Article 40, a Directive Principle, tells the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government. Articles 243A, 243B and 243G came much later with the 73rd Amendment.
nindian-polity-37-1.tq: Discriminate Article 40 (directive) from Part IX (the 73rd Amendment).
n: Article 40 of the Directive Principles of State Policy directs the State to organize Village Panchayats as units of self-government. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243A deals with the Gram Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243B provides for a three-tier system and exemption. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243G deals with the powers and responsibilities of Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xs: **Article 40** (DPSP) directs the State to organise **Village Panchayats** as units of self-government — option **(1)**.
It sits in **Part IV** and is **non-justiciable** — a compromise between **Gandhi** and **Ambedkar**.
The **73rd Amendment** gave Article 40 its **practical shape**.
xa: The **64th Amendment Bill (1989)** passed the Lok Sabha but **failed in the Rajya Sabha**.
The **V.P. Singh Bill (1990)** lapsed.
Ambedkar called the village "a sink of localism, a den of ignorance" (**4 Nov 1948**) and preferred **the individual**.
Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at **Nagaur** (Rajasthan) on **2 Oct 1959**.

ncc9149dfd8d.s: Which of the following was an argument advanced in favour of centralisation in India after Independence?
o: Local bodies possess complete knowledge of local needs
Nation-building after Partition required unity and security
ncc9149dfd8d.x: Nation-building after Partition, along with the requirements of unity and security, was an argument for centralisation. The other options are arguments for decentralisation.
ncc9149dfd8d.tq: Use the for-versus-against comparison and identify the nation-building rationale.
xs: **Nation-building after Partition**, unity and security was an argument for centralisation — option **(4)**.
Accountability and speed, participation, and local knowledge are arguments **for decentralisation**.
Other centralising arguments: a **single command** for heavy industry and food security, weak local **capacity**, **elite capture**.
xa: In the **1960s** planning grew more centralised and people's participation was diluted.
The **Community Development Programme (1952)** was run **top-down**.
The **Nehruvian** model was a **centralised planned state** with heavy industry.

ndc6e9ae6b62.s: The power to take back an entrusted authority at will is the decisive test distinguishing which of the following?
ndc6e9ae6b62.x: If the transferring authority can withdraw the power at will, the arrangement is delegation rather than devolution. Devolved powers are not ordinarily withdrawable at will by the transferring authority.
ndc6e9ae6b62.tq: Apply the confusable-pair test by focusing on the power of withdrawal.
xs: The power to take authority back **at will** separates **devolution from delegation** — option **(1)**.
If it can be withdrawn at will → **delegation, not devolution**.
Devolution, the **strongest form**, cannot be withdrawn at will.
xa: Devolution goes to **elected local governments** with their own mandate and revenue.
The three dimensions: **political** (decide), **administrative** (implement), **fiscal** (spend and raise).
⚠ **Weakest = deconcentration**.

n9d579dc2b88.s: What is the principal consequence of incomplete devolution of the three Fs to Panchayati Raj Institutions?
o: They remain primarily implementing agencies rather than planning units
They replace the State legislature in rural areas
They become fully autonomous planning governments
They acquire complete control over State taxation
n9d579dc2b88.x: Without adequate funds, functions and functionaries, Panchayati Raj Institutions remain implementing agencies instead of becoming effective planning units.
n9d579dc2b88.tq: Trace the institutional consequence of an incomplete transfer of resources, responsibilities and personnel.
xs: With incomplete 3Fs, PRIs remain **implementing agencies**, not **planning units** — option **(1)**.
The 3Fs: **Funds, Functions, Functionaries**.
They do not replace the State legislature or control State taxes.
xa: Local bodies can be elected but **powerless without fiscal decentralisation**.
India gave **political** power, some **administrative** and **least fiscal** power.
The **2nd ARC** invoked **subsidiarity** for the three tiers.

n5f3eeb2964e.s: Which of the following best illustrates historical village autonomy in the Andhra Pradesh region?
o: The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 under Article 253
The 12-Ayagar village administration associated with the Kakatiyas and Vijayanagara
The transfer of all local functions to the Union Government
The Justice Kurian Joseph committee on Union-State relations
n5f3eeb2964e.x: The traditional 12-Ayagar village administration under the Kakatiyas and Vijayanagara is cited as an example of historical village autonomy in the Andhra region.
n5f3eeb2964e.tq: Identify the historical institution by linking the distinctive administrative term with the dynasties associated with it.
xs: The **12-Ayagar** village administration of the **Kakatiyas** and **Vijayanagara** shows historical village autonomy — option **(2)**.
The **SWM Rules, 2026** are criticised as centralising.
The **Justice Kurian Joseph committee** dealt with Union-State relations.
xa: SWM Rules: in force **1 Apr 2026**, under **Art. 253**.
Gandhi's **Gram Swaraj** also idealised self-sufficient villages.
⚠ **Ambedkar** saw the village as a seat of **caste domination**.

n55633224ffe.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of local self-government?
o: Election by and accountability to local people
A defined local area and functions
n55633224ffe.x: Local self-government does not possess sovereignty or legislative supremacy. Its features include local accountability, defined functions, own funds and autonomy within State law.
n55633224ffe.tq: Locate the constitutional attribute that belongs to the sovereign State rather than a local body.
xs: **Sovereignty or legislative supremacy** is NOT a feature of local self-government — option **(2)**.
Its features: elected by and **accountable to local people**, a **defined local area and functions**, **own funds and taxing powers**, **autonomy within State law**.
It acts within **State law**, so it cannot be sovereign.
xa: **Judicial powers** are also not a feature — **Nyaya Panchayats** are separate.
**Control by a central department** is deconcentration, not local self-government.
Definition: transfer of power to **elected local bodies**.

n0f83e13e352.s: Which one of the following was NOT a recommendation associated with the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee?
o: Constitutional status for Panchayati Raj Institutions
n0f83e13e352.x: The committee recommended a three-tier system, genuine transfer of power and adequate resources. Constitutional status for PRIs was associated with later recommendations, particularly those of the L.M. Singhvi Committee.
n0f83e13e352.tq: Find the recommendation belonging to a later committee rather than the committee under examination.
xs: **Constitutional status for PRIs** was NOT a Balwant Rai Mehta recommendation — option **(4)**.
Mehta recommended a **three-tier PRI**, **genuine transfer of power** and **adequate resources**.
Constitutional status came from the **Committee on Policy and Programmes (1988)**.
xa: That 1988 committee also sought a **5-year term**, **direct elections** and **State Finance and Election Commissions**.
The Mehta Committee was appointed **Jan 1957** and reported **Nov 1957**.
The **NDC** accepted it in **Jan 1958**.

ne7bfa31be50.s: In the context of the Ashok Mehta Committee, the provision concerning supersession of a local body was that:
o: Elections should be held only after five years of supersession
There should be no supersession, or elections should be held within six months
Supersession could continue indefinitely without elections
Supersession should be decided by the Union Cabinet
ne7bfa31be50.x: The committee recommended no supersession, or that polls should be conducted within six months if supersession occurred.
ne7bfa31be50.tq: Focus on the precise time limit and the alternative safeguard in a recommendation.
xs: **Ashok Mehta** sought **no supersession**, or **polls within 6 months** — option **(2)**.
He also wanted **compulsory taxation powers** and **social audit**.
He made the **district** the first point of decentralisation.
xa: The Ashok Mehta Committee sat in **1977-78**.
⚠ **Dantwala (1978) = block**; **Hanumantha Rao (1984) = district**.
**G.V.K. Rao (1985)**: "**grass without roots**".

n3deca7592e7.s: The expression “grass without roots” was used in the context of which observation?
o: Development had become bureaucratised, requiring restoration of the Zila Parishad’s role
Municipal corporations had become financially autonomous
Village communities had acquired excessive judicial powers
n3deca7592e7.x: The G.V.K. Rao Committee observed that development had become bureaucratised—described as “grass without roots”—and called for restoration of the Zila Parishad’s role.
n3deca7592e7.tq: Match the distinctive phrase with the correct committee diagnosis.
xs: "**Grass without roots**" meant **development had become bureaucratised**, so the **Zila Parishad's** role should be restored — option **(1)**.
This was the **G.V.K. Rao (1985)** committee.
The other options do not match.
xa: **Ashok Mehta** made the **district** the first point of decentralisation.
**Hanumantha Rao (1984)**: **district planning** with the **Collector** coordinating.
The **1988** committee sought **constitutional status** for PRIs.

n4827cc24746.s:
The Committee on Policy and Programmes (1988) recommended which of the following?
1. Constitutional status for PRIs
2. A five-year term for PRIs
3. State Finance Commissions and State Election Commissions
n4827cc24746.x: The 1988 Committee recommended constitutional status, a five-year term, direct elections, and State Finance and Election Commissions.
xa: **Balwant Rai Mehta (1957)**: **adequate resources** and genuine transfer of power.
**Ashok Mehta (1977-78)**: **no supersession** or polls within **6 months**.
**G.V.K. Rao (1985)**: "**grass without roots**".

n5e020598760.s: The Hanumantha Rao Committee (1984) recommended district planning coordinated by the:
n5e020598760.x: The Hanumantha Rao Committee wanted the Collector to coordinate district planning.
xa: **Art. 243ZD** now provides a **District Planning Committee**.
**Ashok Mehta** made the **district** the first point of decentralisation.
**G.V.K. Rao (1985)**: restore the **Zila Parishad's** role.

nb24979eaa7b.s: Which committee recommended block-level planning in 1978?
nb24979eaa7b.x: The Dantwala Committee (1978) recommended block-level planning. The Hanumantha Rao Committee (1984) recommended district planning with the Collector coordinating it; G.V.K. Rao (1985) spoke of 'grass without roots'; Ashok Mehta (1977-78) made the district the first point of decentralisation.
xs: The **Dantwala Committee (1978)** recommended **block-level** planning — option **(2)**.
**Hanumantha Rao (1984)** recommended **district planning** with the Collector.
**G.V.K. Rao (1985)** spoke of "**grass without roots**"; **Ashok Mehta** made the **district** the first point.
xa: Both Dantwala and Hanumantha Rao put the basic planning function at the **district** level (UPSC).
**Art. 243ZD**: District Planning Committee.
Ashok Mehta sat in **1977-78**.

n745ec5acae3.s: SabhaSaar, in the context of Gram Sabha functioning, is associated with:
o: Conduct of elections to Jammu and Kashmir DDCs
Collection of property tax by Zilla Parishads
Preparation of Gram Sabha minutes using an artificial intelligence tool
n745ec5acae3.x: SabhaSaar is an AI tool associated with Gram Sabha minutes.
n745ec5acae3.tq: Use the function of a named digital tool to distinguish it from unrelated Panchayati Raj activities.
xs: **SabhaSaar** is an **AI tool** for **Gram Sabha minutes** — option **(4)**.
It was noted in the **ES 2025-26** with **e-GramSwaraj**.
The Survey also discussed PRI **own-source revenue**.
xa: A report flagged **low Gram Sabha participation** (**1 Jul 2026**).
J&K **DDCs'** term ended **24 Feb 2026**.
**RGSA** trains PRI members.

na0b4588214e.s: Local self-government can be best explained as an exercise in
na0b4588214e.x: UPSC 2017 keyed 'democratic decentralisation': power is transferred to elected local bodies. Federalism is about Union-State division; delegation can be withdrawn at will; direct democracy is citizens deciding without representatives.
xs: Local self-government is best explained as an exercise in **democratic decentralisation** (UPSC **2017**) — option **(2)**.
It means transferring power to **elected local bodies** for people's participation.
It is not **federalism** or **delegation**; local bodies have **autonomy within State law**.
xa: The term was coined by the **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee**.
PRIs were adopted to **decentralise the power of democracy** (UPPSC **2016**).
The fundamental objects: **people's participation in development** + **democratic decentralisation**.

n6c88730d0cd.s: Panchayati Raj Institutions brought which significant change in village governance?
o: Abolition of local participation in development
Direct control by Parliament over village decisions
n6c88730d0cd.x: PRIs brought formal representation of weaker sections in village governance and were adopted to decentralise democratic power.
n6c88730d0cd.tq: Test the social consequence of an institution rather than its organisational structure.
xs: PRIs brought **formal representation of the weaker sections** in village governance (APPSC **2019**) — option **(4)**.
They were adopted to **decentralise the power of democracy** (UPPSC **2016**).
They widened participation rather than abolishing it.
xa: Fundamental objects: **people's participation in development** + **democratic decentralisation** (UPSC **2015**).
Post-73rd needs: decentralisation of **decision-making**, **the system as a whole** and **administrative powers**.
⚠ **Not judicial powers** (BPSC **2022**).

n9f9c9636504.s: The constitutional trace of the idea of Gram Swaraj is found in:
n9f9c9636504.x: The constitutional trace of Gram Swaraj is found in Article 40, a Directive Principle of State Policy concerning village panchayats.
n9f9c9636504.tq: Distinguish the Article associated with village self-government from nearby decentralisation provisions.
xs: The constitutional trace of Gram Swaraj is **Article 40** (DPSP) — option **(4)**.
**Art. 243ZD** is the **District Planning Committee**.
Gram Swaraj = a **self-reliant village republic**.
xa: The **1988** Committee on Policy and Programmes sought **constitutional status** for PRIs.
The **RGSA** was revamped for **1 Apr 2022 to 31 Mar 2026**.
**SVAMITVA** launched on **24 Apr 2020**.

nd33154db6b3.s: Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan, which trains members of Panchayati Raj Institutions, is implemented by the:
nd33154db6b3.x: RGSA is implemented by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj from 2018-19 to train PRI members.
xa: Revamped for **1 Apr 2022 to 31 Mar 2026**.
Funding: **60:40**; NE and hill States **90:10**.
ES **2025-26** noted **e-GramSwaraj** and **SabhaSaar**.

na37a4651d9b.s: The District Planning Committee is constitutionally recognised as a coordinating body under:
na37a4651d9b.x: The District Planning Committee is a constitutional coordinating body under Article 243ZD.
na37a4651d9b.tq: Match the institution with its exact constitutional Article rather than a related Panchayati Raj provision.
xs: The **District Planning Committee** is a constitutional coordinating body under **Article 243ZD** — option **(2)**.
**Art. 40** is the DPSP trace of Gram Swaraj.
District planning was recommended by **Hanumantha Rao (1984)**.
xa: **Dantwala (1978)** wanted **block-level** planning.
J&K **DDCs'** term ended **24 Feb 2026** with no fresh polls.
AP has **13 Zilla Parishads**.

n9a13413d504.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Scandinavian model of local government?
o: Strong municipalities delivering most welfare services with high local taxes
Local councils functioning only through parliamentary committees
Village bodies exercising judicial supremacy over the State
Weak municipalities dependent mainly on central grants
n9a13413d504.x: The Scandinavian model is characterised by strong municipalities, delivery of most welfare services and high local taxes; it is treated as a benchmark for fiscal decentralisation.
n9a13413d504.tq: Identify the model through its combination of municipal strength, welfare delivery and local taxation.
xs: The **Scandinavian** model has **strong municipalities** delivering most **welfare services** with **high local taxes** — option **(1)**.
It is the benchmark for **fiscal decentralisation**.
Councils as **creatures of Parliament** with committees is the **British** model.
xa: British councils follow the **ultra vires** rule.
India's municipal model derives from the **British** (Ripon's boards).
Kerala devolved about **35-40%** of plan funds to local bodies.

n9e260a79ec4.s: Which one of the following is a characteristic of the British model of local government?
o: Local bodies deliver most welfare services through high local taxes
Municipalities possess complete sovereignty independent of Parliament
Local councils are creatures of Parliament and operate under the ultra vires rule
All local councils are governed through Gram Panchayats
n9e260a79ec4.x: In the British model, local councils are creatures of Parliament and are subject to the ultra vires rule; the model also uses a committee system.
n9e260a79ec4.tq: Distinguish parliamentary creation and ultra vires from the fiscal characteristics of the Scandinavian model.
xs: In the **British** model, local councils are **creatures of Parliament** under the **ultra vires** rule — option **(3)**.
It also uses a **committee system**.
High local taxes and welfare delivery mark the **Scandinavian** model.
xa: India's municipal model derives from the British (**Ripon's boards**).
Local self-government has no **sovereignty or legislative supremacy**.
The Scandinavian model is the benchmark for **fiscal decentralisation**.

n8279ba9e9f8.s: Which phase of the Five Year Plan framework gave Panchayati Raj Institutions a new lease of life, although it did not become an official Plan of India?
n8279ba9e9f8.x: The Sixth Five Year Plan, associated with the Janata Government’s 1978-1983 plan, gave Panchayati Raj a new lease of life but was dropped after 1980 and did not become an official Plan of India.
n8279ba9e9f8.tq: Use the unusual qualification about an unofficial Plan to identify the correct Plan phase.
xs: The **Sixth Five Year Plan** gave PRIs a new lease of life but "could not become an official plan of India" — option **(2)** (APPSC-G2 2017 key).
It was the Janata government's **1978-83** plan, dropped after **1980**.
xa: It matches the Ashok Mehta report of **1978**.
Post-1977 panchayats on Ashok Mehta lines = "**Second Generation Panchayats**".
The **1978-83** revival phase was shaped by this committee.

nae0834b17dd.s: The Grow More Food Inquiry Committee, constituted in 1952, was chaired by:
nae0834b17dd.x: V.T. Krishnamachari chaired the Grow More Food Inquiry Committee constituted in 1952.
nae0834b17dd.tq: Apply the wrong-person trap by distinguishing the committee chairman from later Panchayati Raj committee chairmen.
xs: The Grow More Food Inquiry Committee (**1952**) was chaired by **V.T. Krishnamachari** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-G2 2008 key).
**Balwant Rai Mehta** (1957), **Ashok Mehta** (1977-78) and **G.V.K. Rao** (1985) headed later Panchayati Raj committees — they are the keyed distractors.
The committee found the campaign **too narrow** and called for an **integrated village-development** approach.
xa: It recommended a nationwide **extension organisation**, which led to the **CDP (1952)** and the **NES (1953)**.
V.T. Krishnamachari is also linked with the **Baroda** rural project of **1932**.
The **Grow More Food campaign** itself began in **1943**.

n432e63deba7.s: The principal recommendation of the Grow More Food Inquiry Committee was to establish:
o: A separate constitutional court for villages
n432e63deba7.x: The Committee found the campaign too narrow and recommended an integrated village-development approach supported by a nationwide extension organisation.
n432e63deba7.tq: Identify the institutional recommendation that connects the inquiry with the later rural extension system.
xs: The Grow More Food Inquiry Committee's principal recommendation was a **nationwide extension organisation** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It found the Grow More Food campaign **too narrow** and wanted an **integrated village-development approach**.
That extension organisation took shape as the **Community Development Programme (1952)** and the **National Extension Service (1953)**.
xa: Chairman: **V.T. Krishnamachari** (APPSC-G2 2008 key); distractors were Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta, G.V.K. Rao.
The **NES** was a lighter, extension-staff version that spread the CDP pattern (**block, BDO, VLW**) nationwide.
The CDP was launched on **2 October 1952**, in the **First Five Year Plan (1951-56)**.

nbd0aeae271b.s: The Community Development Programme represented a step towards implementing which provision of the Directive Principles of State Policy?
o: Article 50 relating to separation of judiciary from executive
Article 44 relating to a Uniform Civil Code
nbd0aeae271b.x: The programme was viewed as a step towards implementing Article 40 of the Constitution, which directs the State to organise village panchayats.
nbd0aeae271b.tq: Apply the article-subject association and distinguish the relevant Directive Principle from neighbouring provisions.
xs: The CDP was a step towards the Directive Principles (**Part IV**), especially **Article 40** on village panchayats — option **(2)**.
It aimed at **public participation** in village development, putting the DPSP into practice.
xa: PR evolution: CDP's development schemes → self-government; **Art. 40** (DPSP) → justiciable **Part IX**.
The **73rd Amendment, 1992** added **Part IX** (**Art. 243-243O**) and the **Eleventh Schedule** (**29** items).
The 73rd Amendment came into force on **24 April 1993**.

nd6e0435404e.s: The Community Development Programme was launched in India in which year?
nd6e0435404e.x: The CDP was launched on 2 October 1952 (Gandhi Jayanti) during the First Five Year Plan. 1950 is the Constitution/Planning Commission year, 1957 the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee and 1959 the launch of Panchayati Raj.
xs: The CDP was launched in **1952** (2 October, Gandhi Jayanti) — option **(2)**.
⚠ **1957** = Balwant Rai Mehta Committee; **1959** = Panchayati Raj launched; **1953** = NES.
xa: It came during the **First Five Year Plan (1951-56)**, starting with **55 community projects**.
The **IADP** came in **1960** (pilot in **7** districts).
Exam angle: the year is asked directly — **1952**, not 1950/1957/1959.

n1b5efdc262d.s: The basic aim of the Community Development Programme was:
o: Development of villages through public participation
Establishment of Nyaya Panchayats in every village
A two-tier system of rural government
n1b5efdc262d.x: The CDP aimed to develop villages and raise rural living standards through public participation.
xa: Objective in full: raise the **standard of living of the rural population** through **public participation**.
Its lack of real people's participation later led to the **Balwant Rai Mehta** review (**1957**).
Unit: the **block**, with a **BDO** and **Village Level Workers**.

n07cd2e5a2bb.s: The Village Level Worker, also known as the Gram Sevak, is best described as a:
o: Political representative elected to the Panchayat Samiti
Single-purpose revenue official for one village
Multipurpose extension worker for a group of villages
Judicial officer appointed to a Nyaya Panchayat
n07cd2e5a2bb.x: A Village Level Worker or Gram Sevak served as a multipurpose extension worker for a group of villages.
n07cd2e5a2bb.tq: Discriminate between the administrative, developmental and judicial roles associated with village institutions.
xs: The **Village Level Worker (Gram Sevak)** was a **multipurpose extension worker for a group of villages** — option **(3)**.
He was not elected, not a single-purpose revenue official, and not a judicial officer of a **Nyaya Panchayat**.
xa: The **BDO** headed the block team of extension officers.
**Block** = unit of planning and development (about **100 villages**).
The block later became the base of the **Panchayat Samiti** in the Rajasthan-AP pattern.

n899d9951a11.s: Under the Community Development Programme, the unit of planning and development headed by the Block Development Officer was the:
n899d9951a11.x: The block, covering about 100 villages, was the CDP’s unit of planning and development, headed by the BDO.
xa: The block later became the base of the **Panchayat Samiti** in the Rajasthan-AP pattern.
**Dantwala (1978)** reported on **Block-Level Planning**; **Hanumantha Rao (1984)** on **District Planning**.
Gram Sabha = "**embodiment of direct democracy**" (Singhvi).

n58dabfebd55.s: What was the principal finding of the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee regarding rural development?
o: Public participation was indispensable for development
District-level bureaucracy alone could ensure development
Administrative centralisation was indispensable for development
Private agencies should replace local bodies in development
n58dabfebd55.x: The committee’s main finding was that public participation is indispensable for development.
n58dabfebd55.tq: Identify the central principle rather than a structural detail of the committee’s recommendations.
xs: The committee's main finding: **public participation was indispensable for development** — option **(1)**.
Its remedy was **democratic decentralisation** — transfer of power and resources to elected bodies, the opposite of centralisation or bureaucratic control.
xa: The CDP and NES were seen as **imposed by government** with little people's participation.
The decentralisation scheme "later came to be known as **Panchayati Raj**".
Balwant Rai Mehta first used the term "**democratic decentralisation**" (APPSC 2019).

n35e38bf52e0.s: A major criticism of the Community Development Programme was that it:
o: Was implemented without any administrative unit
Was confined exclusively to urban municipalities
Had no agricultural or social components
Was imposed by the government with inadequate people’s participation
n35e38bf52e0.x: The programme was criticised for being government-imposed and for involving the people insufficiently. This weakness contributed to the review by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee.
n35e38bf52e0.tq: Link the criticism of implementation with the later institutional review it prompted.
xs: The CDP was criticised as **imposed by the government with inadequate people's participation** — option **(4)**.
The other options are false: it had a unit (the **block**), was rural, and had **agricultural** and **social education** components.
xa: This weakness led to the **Balwant Rai Mehta** review in **January 1957**.
The committee's remedy: **democratic decentralisation** through three-tier elected bodies.
Later decline causes: **bureaucratisation**, poor finances, irregular elections, weak devolution.

nbae04ae69c7.s: The G.V.K. Rao Committee dealt primarily with:
o: Administrative arrangements for rural development and poverty alleviation programmes
Election disputes of urban local bodies
nbae04ae69c7.x: The full title associated with the G.V.K. Rao Committee was ‘Administrative Arrangements for Rural Development and Poverty Alleviation Programmes’.
nbae04ae69c7.tq: Match the committee with its distinctive official subject rather than a general Panchayati Raj theme.
xs: G.V.K. Rao reviewed "**Administrative Arrangements for Rural Development and Poverty Alleviation Programmes**" — option **(1)**.
**Panchayat statistics** = **V.R. Rao (1960)**; constitutional recognition = **L.M. Singhvi**.
xa: Set up in **1985** by the **Planning Commission**.
Finding: PRIs had become "**grass without roots**".
CGPSC 2021: "G.V.K. Rao - administrative arrangements" is a correct pair.

na43d288344f.s: Under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, which of the following is the correct constitutional range dealing with Panchayati Raj Institutions?
na43d288344f.x: Panchayats are dealt with in Part IX of the Constitution, covering Articles 243 to 243O.
