na43d288344f.tq: Use the constitutional Part and Article-range distinction.
xs: Panchayats: **Part IX**, **Articles 243–243O** — option **(3)**.
Added by the **73rd Amendment, 1992**, in force **24 April 1993**.
xa: It also added the **Eleventh Schedule** with **29** items.
Thungon (**1988**) first proposed a list of PR subjects in the Constitution.
Part IX made PRIs **justiciable**, replacing reliance on **Art. 40** (DPSP).

nindian-polity-1-60.s: Which of the following was the first major rural development programme after independence?
nindian-polity-1-60.x: The Community Development Programme (1952) was the first major rural development programme after independence; the National Extension Service followed in 1953 and Panchayati Raj in 1959.
nindian-polity-1-60.tq: Pick the earliest programme in the rural-development sequence.
n: The Community Development Programme of 1952 was the first major rural development programme after independence. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xs: The **Community Development Programme** (**1952**) was the first major rural development programme after independence — option **(4)**.
It was launched on **2 October 1952**, during the **First Five Year Plan**.
The **National Extension Service** came later, in **1953**; **Panchayati Raj** was launched in **1959**.
xa: The CDP began with **55 community projects**; its unit was the **block**.
It is called the "**Mother of social development programmes**".
**Social education** was a CDP component — ⚠ not part of NAEP, IRDP or National Literacy Mission (APPSC 2019).
Its objective: **development of village through public participation** (APPSC 2018 key).

n9102f5ea940.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee?
o: It examined the working of the Integrated Rural Development Programme
It examined the working of the Community Development Programme
It examined the working of the National Extension Service
n9102f5ea940.x: It examined the Community Development Programme (1952) and the National Extension Service (1953); IRDP was outside its terms of reference.
xa: Appointed by the **Government of India** in **January 1957**; report **November 1957**.
Main finding: **local people's participation** is indispensable.
Remedy: **democratic decentralisation** → three-tier elected bodies, later called **Panchayati Raj**.

n9247ec2bfb5.s: The democratic decentralisation recommended by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee consisted essentially of:
n9247ec2bfb5.x: The recommended remedy was democratic decentralisation through elected three-tier local bodies, which later came to be known as Panchayati Raj.
n9247ec2bfb5.tq: Link the remedy proposed by the reviewing committee with its institutional form.
xs: Democratic decentralisation meant **three-tier elected local bodies** — option **(4)**.
Tiers: **Gram Panchayat** (village), **Panchayat Samiti** (block), **Zila Parishad** (district), "organically linked" by **indirect elections**.
xa: It meant genuine transfer of **power and responsibility** with **adequate resources**.
The scheme "later came to be known as **Panchayati Raj**".
⚠ **Nyaya Panchayat** is NOT one of the three tiers (UPPSC 2024).

n716b44114d3.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the election pattern recommended by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee?
o: Indirect elections at all three levels
Direct elections at all three levels
Direct election to the Gram Panchayat and indirect elections to the Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad
Direct elections to the Gram Panchayat and Zila Parishad, with indirect election to the Panchayat Samiti
n716b44114d3.x: The committee recommended direct election to the village Panchayat, while the Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad were to be constituted through indirect elections.
n716b44114d3.tq: Discriminate between direct election at the base and indirect election at the higher tiers.
xs: Balwant Rai Mehta: **direct** election to the **Gram Panchayat**, **indirect** elections to the **Panchayat Samiti** and **Zila Parishad** — option **(3)**.
⚠ "Direct elections to both village panchayat and Zila Parishad" is a keyed **false** statement (APPSC 2019).
xa: The three tiers were "**organically linked**" through indirect elections (UPSC).
**Gadgil (1988)** later proposed **direct elections at all levels**.
**Ashok Mehta** wanted **political parties** to take part at all levels.

n82f9aded846.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the roles assigned by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee?
o: Panchayat Samiti—supervisory body; Zila Parishad—village-level implementation body
Panchayat Samiti—advisory body; Zila Parishad—executive body
Panchayat Samiti—executive body; Zila Parishad—advisory, coordinating and supervisory body
Panchayat Samiti—judicial body; Zila Parishad—legislative body
n82f9aded846.x: The Panchayat Samiti was recommended as the executive body, whereas the Zila Parishad was assigned advisory, coordinating and supervisory functions.
n82f9aded846.tq: Use role-based comparison to distinguish the executive Samiti from the coordinating Zila Parishad.
xs: **Panchayat Samiti — executive body**; **Zila Parishad — advisory, coordinating and supervisory body** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Making the **Zila Parishad the executive body** was something the committee did **NOT** recommend (APPSC 2019).
xa: The block was the **basic unit of planning and development** for the Panchayat Samiti.
The **District Collector** was to chair the **Zila Parishad**.
Under **Ashok Mehta** the roles flipped: **Zila Parishad** = executive body.

neefc82155dc.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee's recommendations?
o: The transfer of functions should come with adequate resources
The District Collector should chair the Zila Parishad
Planning and development functions should go to Panchayati Raj bodies
The Zila Parishad should be the executive body
neefc82155dc.x: The Committee made the Panchayat Samiti, not the Zila Parishad, the executive body.
xa: APPSC 2019 keyed "**c and d only**": all planning and development to these bodies + Collector as ZP chairman.
⚠ **Collector as ZP chairman** = BRM; **Collector as ZP CEO** = **Thungon**; **DDC as ZP CEO** = **G.V.K. Rao**.

n341593c41d0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee's recommendations?
o: Direct election to the Zila Parishad
The Panchayat Samiti as the executive body
The District Collector as chairman of the Zila Parishad
n341593c41d0.x: The Committee did not recommend direct election to the Zila Parishad; it recommended three tiers with the Panchayat Samiti as the executive body.
xa: Two tiers came from **Ashok Mehta (1978)** — Zila Parishad + **Mandal Panchayat**.
⚠ **3 – block – Collector chairman** = BRM; **2 – district – parties** = Ashok Mehta.

nf247d60e415.s:
Which of the following contributed to the decline of Panchayati Raj Institutions?
1. Poor finances
2. Irregular elections and supersession
3. Excessive independence from the development administration
nf247d60e415.x: Poor finances and irregular elections/supersession were causes. Excessive independence was not; the problem was bureaucratic detachment from Panchayati Raj.
xa: **Ashok Mehta** set a **six-month** limit for elections after supersession.
**Thungon (1988)**: fixed **5-year** term; supersession at most **6 months**.

nf279cf702da.s: The V.R. Rao Committee of 1960 is associated with:
nf279cf702da.x: Although its name may suggest a statistical body outside the Panchayati Raj field, the V.R. Rao Committee was associated with Panchayat Statistics and was a Panchayati Raj committee.
nf279cf702da.tq: Resolve the look-alike committee trap by recalling its specific Panchayat-related subject.
xs: The **V.R. Rao Committee (1960)** dealt with the **Rationalisation of Panchayat Statistics** — option **(1)**.
⚠ It sounds statistical but **IS** a PR committee (CGPSC 2021: "V.R. Rao - statistics" is a correct pair).
**Centre-State relations** = **Sarkaria**; **electoral reforms** = **Dinesh Goswami** and **Tarkunde** — not PR committees.
xa: **S.D. Mishra (1961)** — Working Group on Panchayats and Cooperatives.
**Vishwa Raman (1961)** — PR Administration.
**C. Rangarajan** headed the **National Statistical Commission** — not a PR committee.

n2f6ba13a936.s: According to the Ashok Mehta Committee, the first point of decentralisation below the State level was to be the:
n2f6ba13a936.x: The Committee treated the district as the first point of decentralisation under popular supervision below the State level.
n2f6ba13a936.tq: Separate the district-based recommendation from the commonly associated block-level structure.
xs: The **District** was the first point of decentralisation below the State — option **(2)**.
⚠ UPPSC 2023 trap: Ashok Mehta made the **district**, **not the block**, the unit.
xa: The block (Samiti executive) was the unit under **Balwant Rai Mehta**.
**G.V.K. Rao (1985)** also made the **district** the basic unit of planning.
**Dantwala (1978)** = **block**-level planning; **Hanumantha Rao (1984)** = **district** planning.

nee62bd50d23.s: The Ashok Mehta Committee on Panchayati Raj (1977) was appointed by the Janata Government headed by Prime Minister:
nee62bd50d23.x: The Janata Government of Morarji Desai appointed the Ashok Mehta Committee in December 1977 (APPSC-G2 2008 key). Rajiv Gandhi's government appointed the L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986); Indira Gandhi and Charan Singh are distractors.
nee62bd50d23.tq: Ashok Mehta = Janata / Morarji Desai; Singhvi = Rajiv Gandhi.
xs: The Janata Government of PM **Morarji Desai** appointed the Ashok Mehta Committee (**December 1977**) — option **(2)** (APPSC-G2 2008 key).
**Rajiv Gandhi's** government appointed the **L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986)**.
xa: The report came in **August 1978** with **132 recommendations**.
The **Sixth Five Year Plan** (Janata's **1978-83** plan) gave PRIs a new lease of life.
It was dropped after **1980** and "could not become an official plan of India" (APPSC-G2 2017).

n50aa089e920.s: If a Panchayati Raj body was superseded under the Ashok Mehta Committee's recommendation, elections were to be held within:
n50aa089e920.x: The Committee recommended that elections should be conducted within six months if a Panchayati Raj body was superseded.
n50aa089e920.tq: Distinguish the prescribed election deadline from other common constitutional time limits.
xs: Elections within **six months** of supersession — option **(4)**.
This six-month limit was Ashok Mehta's answer to **irregular elections + supersession**.
xa: **Thungon (1988)** also set supersession at most **6 months**, with a fixed **5-year** term.
Ashok Mehta also wanted a **Minister for Panchayati Raj** in the state cabinet.
Elections run by the **Chief Electoral Officer** of the state.

n6bd0970792b.s: Panchayats formed after 1977 broadly on the lines suggested by the Ashok Mehta Committee are known as:
n6bd0970792b.x: Panchayats formed after 1977 on the lines of the Ashok Mehta recommendations are referred to as Second Generation Panchayats.
n6bd0970792b.tq: Discriminate between the generation label and descriptive institutional terms.
xs: Post-1977 panchayats on Ashok Mehta lines are "**Second Generation Panchayats**" — option **(3)**.
They followed the Ashok Mehta report (**August 1978**).
xa: **West Bengal** adopted Ashok Mehta's model.
"**Grass without roots**" = **G.V.K. Rao's** phrase for PRIs.
Gram Sabha = "**embodiment of direct democracy**" (Singhvi).

n2f3dc92c925.s:
Which of the following was/were associated with the Gadgil Committee (1988)?
1. Constitutional status for Panchayati Raj Institutions
2. Reservations in Panchayati Raj Institutions
3. Serving as the model for the 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill
n2f3dc92c925.x: The Gadgil Committee recommended constitutional status, direct elections and reservations, and its ideas were the model for the 64th Amendment Bill.
xa: Gadgil: **Congress Party** Committee on Policy and Programmes (**1988**).
It also proposed a **State Finance Commission** + **State Election Commission**.
PRIs to **levy taxes**.

n91ab7a85384.s: Which one of the following expressions is most closely associated with the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee?
n91ab7a85384.x: Democratic decentralisation was the central idea associated with the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee, along with the recommendation of a three-tier system.
n91ab7a85384.tq: Discriminate between closely related committee slogans and subjects.
xs: **Democratic decentralisation** is the BRM hallmark — option **(4)** (first used the term, APPSC 2019).
**Revitalisation for democracy and development** = **L.M. Singhvi**; **administrative arrangements** = **G.V.K. Rao**; **district planning under the Collector** = **Hanumantha Rao**.
xa: The scheme "later came to be known as **Panchayati Raj**".
BRM's structure: **three tiers**, organically linked by **indirect elections**.

na457340da9c.s: Which one of the following sets contains only recommendations associated with the Ashok Mehta Committee?
o: Constitutional recognition, free and fair elections and viable Gram Panchayats
Three tiers, indirect elections above the village level and Collector as Zila Parishad chairman
Two tiers, four-year term and participation of political parties in Panchayat elections
Zila Parishad as pivotal body, decentralised field administration and District Development Commissioner as its Chief Executive Officer
na457340da9c.x: Two tiers, a four-year term and party participation in panchayat elections are all Ashok Mehta recommendations. Option A belongs to L.M. Singhvi, option B to Balwant Rai Mehta and option D to G.V.K. Rao.
na457340da9c.tq: Identify the committee by a cluster of recommendations rather than by one isolated fact.
xs: **Two tiers, four-year term, party participation** — all **Ashok Mehta** — option **(3)**.
Option 1 = **L.M. Singhvi**; option 2 = **Balwant Rai Mehta**; option 4 = **G.V.K. Rao**.
xa: Ashok Mehta also: **compulsory taxation**, **social audit**, **Minister for Panchayati Raj**.
Superseded PRIs → elections **within six months**.
Mandal Panchayat population: **15,000-20,000**.

nbf07df33694.s: The Ashok Mehta Committee envisaged regular social audit by:
o: A district-level agency and a committee of legislators
The Gram Sabha and the Supreme Court jointly
nbf07df33694.x: The Committee proposed regular social audit by a district-level agency together with a committee of legislators.
nbf07df33694.tq: Identify the combination of bodies assigned the audit function.
xs: Regular social audit by **a district-level agency and a committee of legislators** — option **(2)**.
It was one of Ashok Mehta's **132 recommendations** (August 1978).
xa: Other points: **compulsory taxation**, **party participation**, **Minister for Panchayati Raj**.
**SC/ST reservation by population**.
Superseded body → elections within **6 months**.

n969647c89a1.s: Which one of the following committees was concerned with block-level planning?
n969647c89a1.x: The Dantwala Committee, appointed in 1978, dealt with block-level planning.
n969647c89a1.tq: Match the planning level with the committee specifically associated with it.
xs: The **Dantwala Committee (1978)** reported on **Block-Level Planning** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **Hanumantha Rao (1984)** = **district** planning; **G.V.K. Rao (1985)** = administrative arrangements; **L.M. Singhvi (1986)** = revitalising PRIs.
xa: Hanumantha Rao kept the **Collector** as primary coordinator of district planning.
Dantwala too kept the Collector central to district planning.
The block was the CDP's unit (about **100 villages**).

neca32392788.s: The phrase ‘grass without roots’ was used in the context of Panchayati Raj Institutions by the:
neca32392788.x: The G.V.K. Rao Committee observed that Panchayati Raj Institutions had become ‘grass without roots’.
neca32392788.tq: Use the distinctive quotation to separate committees with overlapping rural-development concerns.
xs: "**Grass without roots**" was the phrase of the **G.V.K. Rao Committee** — option **(1)**.
It meant development had become **bureaucratised** and cut off from PR.
xa: Remedy: **Zila Parishad** pivotal; **district** = basic unit of planning.
**District Development Commissioner** = ZP CEO.
It also urged **regular elections** to PRIs.

nfddf42172b6.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the G.V.K. Rao Committee from the L.M. Singhvi Committee?
o: G.V.K. Rao focused on Gram Sabhas, while L.M. Singhvi focused on district bureaucracy
G.V.K. Rao focused on administrative arrangements, while L.M. Singhvi focused on revitalising PRIs for democracy
G.V.K. Rao focused on constitutional recognition, while L.M. Singhvi focused on taxation powers
Both committees had identical objectives and key units
nfddf42172b6.x: G.V.K. Rao examined the administrative set-up for rural development, whereas L.M. Singhvi focused on revitalising Panchayati Raj Institutions as instruments of democracy.
nfddf42172b6.tq: Separate committees by focus rather than by their common connection with Panchayati Raj.
xs: G.V.K. Rao = **administrative arrangements** for rural development; L.M. Singhvi = **revitalising PRIs for democracy** — option **(2)**.
Key unit: G.V.K. Rao = **district / Zila Parishad**; Singhvi = **Gram Sabha** and viable gram panchayats.
xa: Big idea: G.V.K. Rao = **DDC as ZP CEO**; Singhvi = **constitutional recognition**.
G.V.K. Rao **1985** (Planning Commission); Singhvi **1986** (Rajiv Gandhi government).

ne338f6e66c3.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation associated with the L.M. Singhvi Committee?
o: Abolition of the Gram Sabha as an institution of direct democracy
Regular, free and fair elections to Panchayati Raj Institutions
Constitutional recognition of Panchayati Raj Institutions
Nyaya Panchayats for clusters of villages
ne338f6e66c3.x: The Singhvi Committee supported the Gram Sabha as the embodiment of direct democracy; it did not recommend its abolition. It also supported constitutional recognition, regular elections and Nyaya Panchayats for clusters of villages.
ne338f6e66c3.tq: Find the option that reverses a stated recommendation while the other three retain the committee’s approach.
xs: **Abolition of the Gram Sabha** was not Singhvi's idea — option **(1)**: he called the Gram Sabha the "**embodiment of direct democracy**".
He did recommend **constitutional recognition**, **regular, free and fair elections** and **Nyaya Panchayats** for **clusters of villages**.
xa: He wanted villages reorganised to make **gram panchayats viable**, with more money for them.
**Judicial tribunals** in each state for PR election and dissolution disputes.
**R.R. Diwakar (1963)** studied the **Gram Sabha**.

nc54347d9234.s: The Gadgil Committee of 1988 was set up by the:
nc54347d9234.x: The Gadgil Committee was set up by the Congress party in 1988 and its recommendations fed into the draft constitutional amendment proposals.
nc54347d9234.tq: Identify the political origin of the committee instead of confusing it with a governmental commission.
xs: The **Gadgil Committee (1988)** was set up by the **Congress Party** (Committee on Policy and Programmes) — option **(3)**.
The **Planning Commission** set up **G.V.K. Rao (1985)**.
xa: Gadgil "**fed into draft amendment proposals**" — model for the **64th Amendment Bill**.
It proposed **direct elections at all levels** and a **State Election Commission**.
**Thungon (1988)** was a sub-committee of Parliament's Consultative Committee.

ndf7a233aed3.s: The principal objection raised by opponents to the 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill was that it would
o: remove the system of reservation in local bodies
centralise power and bypass the States
ndf7a233aed3.x: Opponents feared that the 64th Bill would centralise power and bypass the States in matters relating to Panchayati Raj.
ndf7a233aed3.tq: Identify the specific political objection rather than the broad objective of the Bill.
xs: Opponents feared the 64th Bill would **centralise power and bypass the States** — option **(3)**.
The Centre would deal directly with local bodies over the states' heads, though "**Local Government**" is a **State List** subject.
xa: Moved by **Rajiv Gandhi** govt, **July 1989**; **passed Lok Sabha**, **defeated in Rajya Sabha** (October 1989).
No special majority → it **lapsed**.
The 64th Bill = **legislative origin of the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992** (BPSC 2020 key).

n4ad7c6553f8.s: Which combination of committees is associated with the principal blueprint of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment?
o: Balwant Rai Mehta, Hanumantha Rao and Dantwala
G.V.K. Rao, K. Santhanam and R.R. Diwakar
Ashok Mehta, S.D. Mishra and Rajagopalan
n4ad7c6553f8.x: The L.M. Singhvi, Thungon and Gadgil Committees collectively contributed to the blueprint of the 73rd Amendment, including constitutional status, election and financial institutions, tenure and reservation.
n4ad7c6553f8.tq: Start from the distinctive three-committee combination linked with constitutionalisation.
xs: **L.M. Singhvi, Thungon and Gadgil** = blueprint of the **73rd Amendment** — option **(2)**.
They gave **constitutional status**, **SEC**, **SFC**, **5-year term** and **reservation**.
xa: Singhvi **1986**; Thungon and Gadgil **1988**.
Gadgil was the model for the **64th Amendment Bill**.
**Balwant Rai Mehta (1957)** gave **three tiers**; **Hanumantha Rao** and **Dantwala** were planning committees.

nca7092678a1.s: Which Bill was the first attempt to provide constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions?
nca7092678a1.x: The Constitution (64th Amendment) Bill was the first attempt to confer constitutional status on Panchayati Raj Institutions. It failed in the Rajya Sabha in 1989.
nca7092678a1.tq: Distinguish the first failed constitutional attempt from the later successful amendment.
xs: The **64th Amendment Bill** was the **first attempt** at constitutional status for PRIs — option **(4)**.
Moved **July 1989** by **Rajiv Gandhi**; passed Lok Sabha, **defeated in Rajya Sabha** (October 1989).
xa: It was the **legislative origin of the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992** (BPSC 2020 key).
The **131st Amendment Bill, 2026** was defeated in the **Lok Sabha** on **17 April 2026** — special majority still decisive.

nafbb79e3bd6.s: Andhra Pradesh adopted the three-tier Panchayati Raj system at Shadnagar on:
nafbb79e3bd6.x: Andhra Pradesh, the second State to adopt the system, introduced three-tier Panchayati Raj at Shadnagar on 1 November 1959.
nafbb79e3bd6.tq: Test the exact date and location of the second State's adoption.
xs: AP adopted three-tier PR at **Shadnagar** on **1 November 1959** — option **(4)**.
**2 October 1959** was **Rajasthan's** date (Nagaur), the first state.
xa: AP was the **second state** but the **first to implement PR across the entire state** (APPSC 2019 key).
It came under CM **N. Sanjiva Reddy's** government.
Law: **AP Panchayat Samithis and Zilla Parishads Act, 1959**.

nd98e6121e34.s: Andhra Pradesh is credited with being the first State to:
o: Implement Panchayati Raj across the entire State in 1959
Give 50 per cent reservation to women in local bodies
nd98e6121e34.x: AP was the second State to adopt Panchayati Raj (1 November 1959, Shadnagar) but the first to implement it across the whole State. Rajasthan was the first to adopt it.
xa: Exam angle: "first state" = **Rajasthan**; "first across the entire state" = **Andhra Pradesh**.
AP's law today: **AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994** (implements the 73rd Amendment).
AP's intermediate tier is the **Mandal Parishad**, not a block Panchayat Samiti.

n8eb79a3aae9.s: In the constitutional distribution of legislative subjects, ‘Local Government’ is included in the:
n8eb79a3aae9.x: Local Government is a subject in the State List, which formed the basis of the States' objection to greater direct Central involvement with local bodies.
n8eb79a3aae9.tq: Distinguish the federal list containing local government from the Union and Concurrent Lists.
xs: "**Local Government**" is in the **State List** — option **(3)**.
This was the basis of the objection that the **64th Bill** would let the Centre **bypass the States**.
xa: The 64th Bill (**1989**) passed the Lok Sabha but was **defeated in the Rajya Sabha**.
The **1992 Acts** made PRIs justiciable + put a **constitutional obligation** on states.

nindian-polity-43-10.s: Where was the three-tier Panchayati Raj system first launched on 2 October 1959?
nindian-polity-43-10.x: Nehru launched three-tier Panchayati Raj at Nagaur, Rajasthan, on 2 October 1959. Andhra Pradesh followed at Shadnagar on 1 November 1959.
n: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was established in 1957. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee recommended a three-tier model. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
Panchayati Raj was first launched on 2 October 1959. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
Panchayati Raj was first launched at Nagaur in Rajasthan. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
xa: **Andhra Pradesh** was **second**, on **1 November 1959** at **Shadnagar**, and first to implement PR **across the entire state**.
The **NDC** accepted the Mehta scheme in **January 1958**, letting States vary the structure.
State patterns: **Rajasthan-AP** — Panchayat Samiti most powerful; **Tamil Nadu** 2-tier; **West Bengal** 4-tier.
Phases: Ascendancy **1959-1964**, Stagnation **1965-1969**, Decline **1969-1983**, Revival **1983** onwards.

n294c4967b26.s: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 emerged after the controversial portions of the earlier proposal were dropped during the tenure of
n294c4967b26.x: The P.V. Narasimha Rao Government during 1991–92 dropped the controversial portions and enacted the revised proposal as the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.
n294c4967b26.tq: Discriminate between the governments associated with the successive stages of one reform.
xs: The **P.V. Narasimha Rao** government dropped the controversial parts — option **(4)**.
Modified Panchayat and Municipality bills, **September 1991** → **Joint Parliamentary Committee** → passed **December 1992**.
**Rajiv Gandhi** moved the 64th Bill (**1989**); **V.P. Singh** moved fresh bills in **September 1990**.
xa: The 73rd Amendment came into force on **24 April 1993**.
It added **Part IX** (**Art. 243-243O**) and the **Eleventh Schedule** (**29** items).
**National Panchayati Raj Day**: **24 April**.

nd833059e985.s: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment came into force on:
nd833059e985.x: The 73rd Amendment, which grew out of the Narasimha Rao Bill, came into force on 24 April 1993.
xa: The 64th Bill = **legislative origin of the 73rd Amendment** (BPSC 2020 key).
The 1990 bill lapsed when the **Lok Sabha was dissolved**.
The Narasimha Rao bills passed through a **Joint Parliamentary Committee**.

nd9c0601092e.s: Which State adopted the model associated with the Ashok Mehta Committee?
nd9c0601092e.x: West Bengal adopted the Ashok Mehta recommendations and strengthened its PRIs (Karnataka also followed). Rajasthan had pioneered the Balwant Rai Mehta three-tier model in 1959, and Tamil Nadu is cited only for a two-tier pattern.
nd9c0601092e.tq: Associate the distinctive committee model with the State specifically linked to its adoption.
xs: **West Bengal** adopted the Ashok Mehta recommendations and strengthened its PRIs — option **(1)**.
**Rajasthan** pioneered the **Balwant Rai Mehta** model (**2 Oct 1959**); **Tamil Nadu** had a **2-tier** pattern.
xa: **Karnataka** also followed Ashok Mehta.
**AP**: NTR replaced Panchayat Samithis with **Mandal Praja Parishads** (**1986**), in the Ashok Mehta mould.
West Bengal: Panchayat Act **1973**; first panchayat elections **June 1978**.

nb54928b6ae6.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the reform introduced by N.T. Rama Rao in 1985?
o: Enactment of the AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994
Creation of the first open university in India
Abolition of the hereditary Patel-Patwari system and introduction of the Mandal system
Introduction of the three-tier Panchayati Raj system in Andhra Pradesh
nb54928b6ae6.x: In 1985, N.T. Rama Rao abolished the hereditary village officer Patel-Patwari system and introduced the Mandal system.
nb54928b6ae6.tq: Match the reform, year and political leader while rejecting later milestones.
xs: In **1985** NTR **abolished the hereditary Patel-Patwari system** and **introduced the Mandal system** — option **(3)**.
The **AP Panchayat Raj Act** is of **1994**; three-tier PR in AP came in **1959**.
xa: ⚠ **Mandal system 1985** (NTR) vs **Mandal Praja Parishads Act 1986**.
The **1986** Act replaced block Panchayat Samithis with smaller **Mandal Praja Parishads**.
This followed the **Ashok Mehta** mandal idea.

n89e586dab07.s: After the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act was enacted in:
n89e586dab07.x: The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act was enacted in 1994 following the 73rd Constitutional Amendment.
n89e586dab07.tq: Connect the constitutional amendment with the subsequent State legislation.
xs: The **AP Panchayat Raj Act** was enacted in **1994** — option **(3)**.
It is **Act 13 of 1994**, dated **21 April 1994**, implementing the **73rd Amendment**.
xa: It has **278 sections** in **8 Parts**.
Tiers: **Gram Panchayat**, **Mandal Parishad**, **Zilla Parishad**.
**1986** = Mandal Praja Parishads Act; **1992** = 73rd Amendment passed.

n0eb35c2475f.s: The Andhra Pradesh Mandal Praja Parishads reform of 1986 primarily aimed to
o: transfer all Panchayat functions to municipalities
replace smaller Mandal Praja Parishads with larger district bodies
replace block Panchayat Samithis with smaller Mandal Praja Parishads
n0eb35c2475f.x: The 1986 reform under the NTR Government replaced block-level Panchayat Samithis with smaller Mandal Praja Parishads, reflecting the mandal idea associated with the Ashok Mehta approach.
n0eb35c2475f.tq: Apply the institutional reform to identify which tier was replaced and by what.
xs: The **1986** reform **replaced block Panchayat Samithis with smaller Mandal Praja Parishads** — option **(3)**.
It followed the **Ashok Mehta** mandal idea; the Zilla Parishad stayed (as **Zilla Praja Parishad**).
xa: It was enacted by the **NTR** government.
Erstwhile **13** Zilla Praja Parishads were reorganised into **28**.
AP's intermediate tier today: **Mandal Parishad**, not a block Panchayat Samiti.

naee16e9eaf9.s: In the Panchayati Raj structure of Andhra Pradesh, which institution occupies the intermediate tier?
naee16e9eaf9.x: The distinctive intermediate-level institution in Andhra Pradesh is the Mandal Praja Parishad. It is not called a block Panchayat Samiti as in the conventional model.
naee16e9eaf9.tq: Discriminate between the general block-level terminology and the Andhra Pradesh-specific institution.
xs: AP's intermediate tier is the **Mandal Praja Parishad** — option **(3)**, not a **block Panchayat Samiti**.
NTR's **1986** Act replaced Panchayat Samithis with smaller Mandal Praja Parishads.
xa: AP has Mandal Praja Parishads for its **588** mandals.
The **Firka Development Scheme** was the Madras Presidency's **1946** scheme.
**AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994** tiers: Gram Panchayat, **Mandal Parishad**, Zilla Parishad.

na491031731a.s: The National Development Council accepted the recommendations of the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee in:
na491031731a.x: The National Development Council accepted the recommendations in January 1958. It allowed States to vary the structure, but required the basic principles to remain the same.
na491031731a.tq: Distinguish the committee’s appointment and report dates from the later NDC acceptance date.
xs: The **NDC** accepted the recommendations in **January 1958** — option **(2)**.
**January 1957** = committee appointed; **November 1957** = report; **October 1959** = PR launched in Rajasthan.
xa: The NDC allowed **no rigid single pattern** — states could vary structure, basic principles same.
Origin chain: CDP → NES → Mehta Committee → **NDC (Jan 1958)** → Rajasthan and AP (**1959**).
Most states had PRIs by the **mid-1960s**.

ncd11869ba0e.s: The term ‘Panchayati Raj’ was significantly promoted in association with which idea?
o: M.K. Gandhi’s concept of Gram Swaraj
The industrial policy of the Janata Government
The colonial system of district administration
The judicial reforms of the Nyaya Panchayats
ncd11869ba0e.x: The term is credited in this context to M.K. Gandhi’s promotion of Gram Swaraj, which placed villages at the centre of governance.
ncd11869ba0e.tq: Use the associated concept, Gram Swaraj, to identify the person linked with the name Panchayati Raj.
xs: The term 'Panchayati Raj' was promoted with **M.K. Gandhi's** idea of **Gram Swaraj** — option **(1)**.
Gram Swaraj placed **villages at the centre** of governance; UPPSC 2017 key credits the name to **Gandhi**.
xa: Some notes credit **Nehru**, who **inaugurated** the scheme in **1959**.
⚠ **Architect** = **Balwant Rai Mehta**; **name** = **Gandhi**; **inauguration** = **Nehru**.
**Sevagram** (Wardha, 1930s) was Gandhi's rural project.

na47442163d2.s: Who is popularly regarded as the architect or father of Panchayati Raj in India?
na47442163d2.x: Balwant Rai Mehta is popularly called the architect or father of Panchayati Raj because of his Committee’s recommendations on democratic decentralisation.
na47442163d2.tq: Distinguish the person associated with the name from the committee chairman regarded as the system’s architect.
xs: **Balwant Rai Mehta** is the **architect / father of Panchayati Raj** — option **(2)**.
**Gandhi** is credited with the **name** (UPPSC 2017); **L.M. Singhvi** urged **constitutional recognition (1986)**; **G.V.K. Rao** called PRIs "**grass without roots**" (1985).
xa: His committee (**1957**) recommended **democratic decentralisation** and **three tiers**.
Chain of committees: **BRM → Ashok Mehta → G.V.K. Rao → L.M. Singhvi → Thungon/Gadgil**.

n09abb0e75f5.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the decision of the National Development Council regarding the Panchayati Raj pattern?
o: Only Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh were permitted to establish Panchayats.
The Council rejected elected local bodies in favour of nominated bodies.
States could adopt different patterns, but the basic principles were to remain common.
Every State was required to adopt an identical institutional pattern.
n09abb0e75f5.x: The NDC did not insist on one rigid pattern for all States; however, the basic principles of Panchayati Raj were to be the same everywhere.
n09abb0e75f5.tq: Read the distinction between uniform structure and common basic principles carefully.
xs: The **NDC** let **states adopt different patterns** with **common basic principles** — option **(3)**.
It accepted the report in **January 1958** without a rigid single pattern, so options 1, 2 and 4 are false.
xa: Patterns: **Rajasthan-AP** (3-tier, Panchayat Samiti strongest); **Maharashtra-Gujarat** (Zila Parishad dominant).
**Tamil Nadu** = 2-tier; **West Bengal** = 4-tier.
Most states had PRIs by the **mid-1960s**.

n0213bf8f1d9.s: Which one of the following was identified as a major cause of the decline of Panchayati Raj Institutions?
o: Regular elections being held without interruption
Excessive transfer of functions and staff to local bodies
Development work becoming bureaucratised and detached from Panchayati Raj
Complete financial autonomy of Panchayati Raj Institutions
n0213bf8f1d9.x: Development work became bureaucratised and was increasingly cut off from Panchayati Raj Institutions, weakening their role.
n0213bf8f1d9.tq: Identify the causal statement and reject options that describe the opposite condition.
xs: A major cause of decline: **development work became bureaucratised and detached from Panchayati Raj** — option **(3)**.
The other options are the opposite of the real causes: **irregular** elections, **weak** devolution, **poor** finances.
xa: **G.V.K. Rao (1985)** described this as PRIs being "**grass without roots**".
Poor finances were noted by **Santhanam (1963)**.
Decline phase: **1969-1983**.

nf9f4457e795.s: Why did the Ashok Mehta Committee recommend compulsory taxation powers for Panchayati Raj Institutions?
o: To transfer all Union taxes to local bodies
To impose taxes without legislative authority
To enable them to raise their own financial resources
To abolish grants from the State governments
nf9f4457e795.x: Compulsory taxation powers were recommended so that Panchayati Raj Institutions could raise their own money and become financially capable.
nf9f4457e795.tq: Link the recommended power with its stated institutional purpose.
xs: Compulsory taxation powers were meant **to enable PRIs to raise their own financial resources** — option **(3)**.
The notes say PRIs were to **raise own money**; nothing about transferring Union taxes or abolishing grants.
xa: **Poor finances** (Santhanam, **1963**) were a cause of PR decline.
**Gadgil (1988)** also wanted PRIs to **levy taxes**.
Thungon and Gadgil proposed a **State Finance Commission**.

ncdd6e410d26.s: Which of the following was the title of the L.M. Singhvi Committee report?
o: Working Group on Panchayats and Cooperatives
Revitalisation of Panchayati Raj Institutions for Democracy and Development
ncdd6e410d26.x: The L.M. Singhvi Committee was associated with the title ‘Revitalisation of Panchayati Raj Institutions for Democracy and Development’.
ncdd6e410d26.tq: Match the exact title with the committee instead of relying on a broad subject similarity.
xs: Title: "**Revitalisation of Panchayati Raj Institutions for Democracy and Development**" — option **(4)** (APPSC 2018, G2 2008).
**Administrative Arrangements** = **G.V.K. Rao**; **Panchayats and Cooperatives** = **S.D. Mishra (1961)**; **District Planning** = **Hanumantha Rao (1984)**.
xa: Chairman: **L.M. Singhvi**; **1986**; **Rajiv Gandhi** government.
Singhvi = the committee that "**first suggested constitutional status**" (APPSC 2018).
It proposed **judicial tribunals** in each state for PR election and dissolution disputes.

n299a359965b.s: Which committee recommended constitutional status for Panchayati Raj Institutions as its principal precondition?
n299a359965b.x: The L.M. Singhvi Committee of 1986 recommended constitutional status for Panchayati Raj Institutions.
n299a359965b.tq: Discriminate between committees by pairing each with its signature recommendation.
xs: The **L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986)** is keyed as the one that "first suggested **constitutional status**" — option **(2)** (APPSC 2018).
⚠ Older notes say **Ashok Mehta** also recommended it; **Balwant Rai Mehta** did **not** propose it.
xa: Singhvi proposed recognition through a **new chapter** in the Constitution.
**Singhvi + Thungon + Gadgil** = blueprint of the **73rd Amendment**.
**Dantwala (1978)** = **block-level planning**.

n7cc5dea72b2.s: Which one of the following was specifically associated with the Thungon sub-committee's recommendations?
o: A constitutional list of subjects for Panchayati Raj Institutions, later reflected in the Eleventh Schedule
Direct elections only at the village level
Transfer of Panchayat taxation to the Election Commission
n7cc5dea72b2.x: Thungon recommended placing a list of Panchayati Raj subjects in the Constitution; this was later reflected in the Eleventh Schedule.
n7cc5dea72b2.tq: Connect the committee recommendation with its later constitutional institutionalisation.
xs: Thungon wanted a **list of PR subjects in the Constitution**, later the **Eleventh Schedule** — option **(2)**.
He supported reservation for **women** (not abolition) and three tiers.
xa: The **Eleventh Schedule** has **29** items; added by the **73rd Amendment, 1992**.
The 73rd Amendment came into force on **24 April 1993**.
Thungon also proposed a **State Finance Commission**.

n2b00c2d6545.s: The committee associated with training centres for Panchayati Raj was the:
n2b00c2d6545.x: The G. Ramachandran Committee of 1969 dealt with training centres. A.S. Trivedi is not the committee associated with this subject in the given classification.
n2b00c2d6545.tq: Resolve the look-alike distractor by matching the exact subject with the correct committee name.
xs: PR **training centres** = **G. Ramachandran Committee (1969)** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **CGPSC 2021 trap:** "PR Training - **A.S. Trivedi**" is the WRONG pair.
**V.R. Rao** = Panchayat Statistics (**1960**); **S.D. Mishra** = Panchayats and Cooperatives (**1961**).
xa: **R.K. Khanna (1966)** — Audit and Accounts.
**Daya Choubey (1976)** — reviewed CD and PR.

n53e9e490856.s: Which one of the following is the odd one out with reference to committees that inquired into Panchayati Raj Institutions?
n53e9e490856.x: Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta and G.V.K. Rao were associated with Panchayati Raj inquiries. Dinesh Goswami was associated with electoral reforms.
n53e9e490856.tq: Group the committees by subject and identify the electoral-reforms committee.
xs: **Dinesh Goswami** is the odd one out — option **(3)**: it dealt with **electoral reforms**.
**Balwant Rai Mehta**, **Ashok Mehta**, **G.V.K. Rao** (and L.M. Singhvi) all inquired into PRIs (JPSC 2023 key).
xa: **Tarkunde** — also electoral reforms.
**Sarkaria** — Centre-State relations.
**C. Rangarajan** — National Statistical Commission.

n1fb0d7559ad.s: In which year was Panchayati Raj implemented in Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh?
n1fb0d7559ad.x: After the NDC accepted the Balwant Rai Mehta model in January 1958, Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh implemented Panchayati Raj in 1959.
xa: The Mehta Committee itself: appointed **January 1957**, report **November 1957**.
The NDC allowed states to vary the structure with common basic principles.

n86166380141.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the implementation history of the Ashok Mehta Committee's two-tier model?
o: It was adopted uniformly by all States
It was adopted nationally through the 73rd Amendment
It was adopted only in Andhra Pradesh
n86166380141.x: The Ashok Mehta Committee's two-tier model was never adopted nationally. The 73rd Amendment subsequently retained a three-tier framework, subject to the population-based exception.
n86166380141.tq: Find the historically accurate exception to an apparently influential committee recommendation.
xs: The two-tier model was **never adopted nationally** — option **(2)**.
The **73rd Amendment (1992)** went back to **three tiers**.
xa: Two tiers are allowed only in states under **20 lakh** population.
States like **West Bengal** and **Karnataka** followed Ashok Mehta's ideas.
The Janata government fell before acting on the report.

n4fa9b343569.s: Under the constitutional framework introduced by the 73rd Amendment, a two-tier Panchayati Raj structure may exist in:
o: States with a population below 20 lakh
States with a population above 20 lakh only
All Union Territories irrespective of population
States with a population below 10 lakh only
n4fa9b343569.x: The general constitutional model is three-tiered, but states with a population below 20 lakh may have only two tiers.
n4fa9b343569.tq: Focus on the population threshold that creates the constitutional exception.
xs: Two tiers are allowed in **states with a population below 20 lakh** — option **(1)**.
Otherwise the **73rd Amendment (1992)** prescribes **three tiers**.
xa: ⚠ **Ashok Mehta's** nationwide two-tier plan was never adopted.
**Tamil Nadu** once had a **2-tier** pattern; **West Bengal** a **4-tier** one.

n08ac64773b4.s: Which development best explains the significance of the 1992 constitutional changes concerning Panchayati Raj?
o: They made Panchayati Raj Institutions justiciable and imposed a constitutional obligation on States
They transferred all rural development functions to the Union Government
They converted Panchayati Raj into a non-justiciable administrative experiment
They abolished the three-tier system throughout India
n08ac64773b4.x: The 1992 constitutional changes transformed Panchayati Raj from a largely policy-based arrangement into a constitutionally protected and justiciable system, creating obligations for the States.
n08ac64773b4.tq: Identify the legal consequence of constitutionalisation rather than merely its institutional form.
xs: The **1992 Acts** made PRIs **justiciable** and put a **constitutional obligation** on states — option **(1)**.
They kept **three tiers** (two only under **20 lakh** population) — they did not abolish the system or centralise it.
xa: Earlier, PRIs rested on **Art. 40** (DPSP), which is non-justiciable.
Part IX: **Art. 243-243O**; **Eleventh Schedule** with **29** items.
In force **24 April 1993**.

n8eb200f7c04.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional changes introduced by the 73rd Amendment?
o: Part VIII containing 16 Articles and the Eleventh Schedule containing 18 subjects
Part IX containing 16 Articles and the Eleventh Schedule containing 29 subjects
Part IX containing 18 Articles and the Twelfth Schedule containing 29 subjects
Part IX-A containing 18 Articles and the Twelfth Schedule containing 18 subjects
n8eb200f7c04.x: The 73rd Amendment inserted Part IX, comprising Articles 243 to 243O, and the Eleventh Schedule containing 29 subjects.
n8eb200f7c04.tq: Split the options by matching the correct Part, number of Articles and Schedule.
xs: The 73rd added **Part IX** (**16 Articles**, Art. **243-243O**) and the **Eleventh Schedule** (**29 subjects**) — option **(2)**.
**Part IXA** (**243P-243ZG**, **18** Articles) and the **Twelfth Schedule** (**18** subjects) came from the **74th**.
xa: Part IX is titled "**The Panchayats**".
**Art. 243G** links panchayat functions to the Eleventh Schedule.
⚠ "**18** functional items for Panchayats" is a wrong statement (APPSC 2023) — 18 = Twelfth Schedule.

n3f7a336f039.s: Which of the following is NOT a compulsory provision under the 73rd Amendment?
o: Devolution of all 29 subjects in the Eleventh Schedule to Panchayats
Fresh elections within six months of dissolution
A minimum age of 21 years for membership of a Panchayat
n3f7a336f039.x: Actual devolution of the 29 Eleventh Schedule subjects is voluntary for the States. The minimum age, five-year term and election within six months of dissolution are compulsory provisions.
n3f7a336f039.tq: Find the provision involving actual transfer of functions, which is distinct from constitutional listing.
xs: **Devolution of the 29 Eleventh Schedule subjects** is **voluntary** — option **(1)**.
Compulsory: **minimum age 21**, **five-year** term, fresh elections within **six months** of dissolution.
xa: The Eleventh Schedule is "a **menu, not a transfer**" — the State "**may**" devolve.
Funds, functions and functionaries are devolved **unevenly** across states.

n0d9e1023bea.s: In which State does reservation of SC seats in Panchayats not apply, because the State has no Scheduled Caste population?
n0d9e1023bea.x: Arunachal Pradesh has no SC population, so SC reservation does not apply there, though the rest of Part IX does.
xa: SC/ST reservation is in proportion to **population** (**243D**).
Exempted areas also include **hill areas of Manipur** and the **Darjeeling hills**.

n7cdc81d49fb.s: Which Ministry oversees Part IX, PESA and District Planning Committees?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
n7cdc81d49fb.x: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj oversees Part IX, PESA and District Planning Committees.
n7cdc81d49fb.tq: Identify the responsible ministry by matching it with the cluster of decentralisation functions.
xs: The **Ministry of Panchayati Raj** oversees **Part IX**, **PESA** and **District Planning Committees** — option **(2)**.
**MoHUA** runs urban schemes such as **AMRUT 2.0 (2021)**.
xa: It was created on **27 May 2004**.
Its newer tool: **Panchayat Advancement Index** (**2.5 lakh+ GPs**).
Apps: **Meri Panchayat** for citizens; **SabhaSaar**, its first AI tool for Gram Sabha minutes.

nb36e82ebb2f.s: How many subjects are listed in the Eleventh Schedule?
nb36e82ebb2f.x: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects that the State may devolve to Panchayats; it does not transfer them automatically.
xa: Devolving the **29** subjects is a **voluntary** provision.
Result: funds, functions and functionaries devolved **unevenly**.

nf362bb5bc15.s: Which of the following is NOT a subject in the Eleventh Schedule?
nf362bb5bc15.x: Fire services is a Twelfth Schedule (municipal) subject. Rural housing, drinking water and rural electrification are Eleventh Schedule subjects.
xa: **Urban planning** is also Twelfth Schedule.
Infrastructure items: **roads, culverts, bridges, ferries, waterways**.

n3551c35d9a3.s: Urban planning is a subject listed in which Schedule of the Constitution?
n3551c35d9a3.x: Urban planning is a Twelfth Schedule subject; fuel and fodder, rural roads and non-conventional energy are in the Eleventh.
xa: Industry and energy items: **small-scale industries**, **khadi, village and cottage industries**, **rural electrification**.
Twelfth Schedule also has **slaughterhouses**, **burial grounds**, **fire services**.

nc9faf1f31b9.s: Which of the following is a subject in the Eleventh Schedule?
nc9faf1f31b9.x: The public distribution system is an Eleventh Schedule subject; slaughterhouses, burial grounds and urban planning are Twelfth Schedule subjects.
xa: Other health and welfare items: **women and child development**, **family welfare**.
Twelfth Schedule = **18** subjects; Eleventh = **29**.

nc75e71e78a2.s: The SVAMITVA scheme for drone-based mapping of rural inhabited areas was launched on:
nc75e71e78a2.x: SVAMITVA was launched on 24 April 2020, National Panchayati Raj Day, with the Survey of India and NICSI preparing Records of Rights through drone mapping. The other dates are distractors.
nc75e71e78a2.tq: 24 April = National PR Day: 73rd in force (1993), SVAMITVA (2020), Panchayat Awards.
xs: **SVAMITVA** was launched on **24 April 2020** — option **(1)** — National Panchayati Raj Day.
It uses **drone mapping** with the **Survey of India** and **NICSI**.
xa: Its output: **Record of Rights** for rural inhabited areas.
⚠ **e-GramSwaraj** was also launched in **2020**.

n4b59fe79d42.s: The National Panchayat Awards are given on
n4b59fe79d42.x: The National Panchayat Awards are given on 24 April.
n4b59fe79d42.tq: Separate the award date from other nationally significant dates used in governance schemes.
xs: National Panchayat Awards are given on **24 April** — option **(3)**.
**21 April** is when the **AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994** was enacted.
xa: 24 April is **National Panchayati Raj Day** (73rd in force **24 April 1993**).
Judged on **9 LSDG themes** under **RGSA**, using the **PAI**.

nfd020b7d891.s: AMRUT 2.0 was launched in 2021 by the
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
nfd020b7d891.x: AMRUT 2.0 was launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
nfd020b7d891.tq: Use the implementing ministry as the key discriminator among neighbouring schemes.
xs: **AMRUT 2.0** (**2021**) belongs to the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)** — option **(3)**.
The **Ministry of Panchayati Raj** handles rural Part IX matters, not this urban mission.
xa: Aims: **universal water supply**, **sewerage**, **water-body rejuvenation**.
**238 lakh** new connections.

na98dc056592.s: The 74th Constitutional Amendment is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Part X, Articles 244–244A and Fifth Schedule with 29 subjects
Part IXB, Articles 243ZH–243ZT and Ninth Schedule with 18 subjects
Part IX, Articles 243A–243O and Eleventh Schedule with 29 subjects
Part IXA, Articles 243P–243ZG and Twelfth Schedule with 18 subjects
na98dc056592.x: The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA, comprising Articles 243P to 243ZG, and the Twelfth Schedule containing 18 subjects.
na98dc056592.tq: Use the Part–Article range–Schedule combination to identify the correct constitutional amendment.
xs: 74th Amendment: **Part IXA**, **Art. 243P–243ZG**, **Twelfth Schedule** with **18** subjects — option **(4)**.
Option 3 is the **73rd**: Part IX, **243-243O**, Eleventh Schedule (**29**).
xa: 74th came into force on **1 June 1993**; 73rd on **24 April 1993**.
Part IXA has **18 Articles**; Part IX has **16**.
⚠ **243ZC** = Part IXA exemption.

n6317a4fba54.s: Which Article deals with disqualifications for membership of a Panchayat, including the minimum age of 21 years?
n6317a4fba54.x: Article 243F deals with disqualifications for membership of Panchayats, including the minimum age requirement of 21 years.
n6317a4fba54.tq: Track the sequence: reservations in 243D, duration in 243E and disqualifications in 243F.
xs: **Article 243F** covers **disqualifications**, including the **minimum age of 21** — option **(1)**.
**243D** = reservation; **243E** = duration; **243G** = powers and Eleventh Schedule.
xa: Disqualification follows laws for **State Legislature** elections + State laws.
Minimum age **21** is a **compulsory** provision.

o: The powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats, including matters linked to the Eleventh Schedule
The bar on judicial interference in electoral matters
The application of Part IX to Union Territories
nedee04488fb.x: Article 243G concerns the powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats and connects these functions with the Eleventh Schedule.
nedee04488fb.tq: Match the broad functional provision with the Eleventh Schedule rather than with election or audit provisions.
xs: **Art. 243G**: **powers, authority and responsibilities** of panchayats, linked to the **Eleventh Schedule** — option **(1)**.
Court bar = **243O**; UTs = **243L**; audit = **243J**.
xa: 243G is the Article the Eleventh Schedule (**29** subjects) hangs on.
The schedule is a **menu, not a transfer**.

na5cda22110f.s: In K. Krishna Murthy v. Union of India (2010), the Constitution Bench upheld the constitutional validity of provisions enabling reservation for backward classes in local bodies under:
na5cda22110f.x: K. Krishna Murthy upheld the provisions contained in Articles 243D(6) and 243T(6), while distinguishing political backwardness from social and educational backwardness.
na5cda22110f.tq: Match the case with the precise constitutional provisions involved.
xs: **K. Krishna Murthy (2010)** upheld **Articles 243D(6) and 243T(6)** — option **(2)**.
It was a **Constitution Bench**; it held **political backwardness ≠ social/educational backwardness**.
xa: Total vertical reservation should normally stay within **50%**.
⚠ **Krishna Murthy 2010** = upheld OBC quota; **Gawali 2021** = **triple test**.
**Art. 280(3)(bb)** is about the Union Finance Commission and panchayats.

nb805552aa67.s: The report of the State Finance Commission is submitted to the Governor, who is required to:
o: Reject it before placing it before the State Legislature
Place it only before the Legislative Council
Forward it directly to the Union Finance Commission for approval
Lay it before the State Legislature along with an action-taken memorandum
nb805552aa67.x: The Governor lays the State Finance Commission report before the State Legislature together with a memorandum explaining the action taken on its recommendations.
nb805552aa67.tq: Test the constitutional procedure by identifying the authority responsible for laying the report and the accompanying document.
xs: The Governor **lays it before the State Legislature with an action-taken memorandum** — option **(4)**.
The report is **advisory**, not sent to the Union Finance Commission for approval.
xa: The **Governor** constitutes the SFC every **five years**.
The Union FC acts **on the basis of the SFC's recommendations**.

n571aae75f7e.s: Which one of the following best describes Kerala's People's Plan Campaign?
o: Exclusive financing of urban infrastructure through municipal bonds
Centralisation of all plan funds at the State secretariat
Replacement of Gram Sabhas by municipal corporations
Devolution of a large share of plan funds and preparation of plans from Gram Sabhas upwards
n571aae75f7e.x: The campaign devolved a large share of plan funds and encouraged planning from Gram Sabhas upwards.
n571aae75f7e.tq: Identify the governance model from its functional characteristics rather than its name alone.
xs: Kerala's campaign = **large share of plan funds devolved** + plans made **from Gram Sabhas up** — option **(4)**.
**Municipal bonds** are used by only a few large cities — unrelated.
xa: Launched in **1996**.
The national version (**2 Oct 2018**) prepares **GPDPs** through Gram Sabhas.

nindian-polity-26-15.s: The Finance Commission may deal with which of the following matters?
o: Any other matter referred to it by the President in the interest of sound public finance
Resolution of legal disputes between the Centre and States
Distribution between the State and local bodies only
Constitution of the State Finance Commission every five years
nindian-polity-26-15.x: Besides sharing taxes and grants, the Finance Commission handles any other matter the President refers to it in the interest of sound finance. It does not settle legal disputes.
nindian-polity-26-15.tq: Recall the Finance Commission's residual function.
n: The Finance Commission deals with any other matter referred to it by the President in the interest of sound public finance. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
xs: The Finance Commission may deal with **any other matter referred by the President** in the interest of **sound public finance** — option **(1)**.
Settling **legal disputes** between the Centre and States is not among its functions.
Distribution between the **State and local bodies** is the **State Finance Commission**'s job, and the SFC is constituted by the **Governor**.
xa: Core functions: share of **divisible Union taxes**, allocation among **States**, principles of **grants-in-aid** (**Article 275**).
It supplements **Panchayats** and **Municipalities** through the State's Consolidated Fund — **Art. 280(3)(bb)** and **(c)**.
Panchayats get Central money only as **FC grants routed through the state**.
Karnataka's **5th SFC** asked for **5% of urban GST revenue** for ULBs.

nb64a997bf33.s: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave effect to which Directive Principle of State Policy?
o: Article 39(b) on distribution of material resources
Article 44 on a Uniform Civil Code
Article 40 on organisation of village panchayats
Article 48 on agriculture and animal husbandry
nb64a997bf33.x: Article 40 directs the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government; the 73rd Amendment put it into effect through Part IX. Articles 39(b), 44 and 48 deal with resources, a common civil code and agriculture/animal husbandry.
nb64a997bf33.tq: Art. 40 -> CDP was a step towards it; 73rd Amendment gave it effect.
xs: The 73rd gave effect to **Article 40** (DPSP) on organising **village panchayats** — option **(3)**.
It put Art. 40 into effect through **Part IX**, making PRIs **justiciable**.
xa: States are now **constitutionally obliged** to hold panchayat elections.
Part IX has **16 Articles** (**243-243O**).

n68b3499d033.s: Which one of the following is a VOLUNTARY provision under the 73rd Amendment?
o: Direct election to all seats at all levels
Reservation of one-third of seats for women
Constitution of a State Election Commission
n68b3499d033.x: Reservation for backward classes is left to the discretion of the States. Direct elections, women’s reservation and the State Election Commission are compulsory provisions.
n68b3499d033.tq: Separate the constitutionally compulsory provisions from the expressly optional ones.
xs: **Reservation for backward classes** is **voluntary** — option **(3)**.
**Direct election** to all seats, **one-third for women** and the **State Election Commission** are **compulsory**.
xa: Other voluntary items: representation of **MPs and MLAs**, devolving the **29** subjects, financial powers.
**Art. 243D** covers reservation (SC/ST, women, chairpersons; **BCs optional**).
⚠ **Gawali (2021)**: SC+ST+OBC total not above **50%**.

ncbd857434eb.s: Which Article of Part IX provides for the State Election Commission?
ncbd857434eb.x: Article 243K provides for the SEC; 243A covers the Gram Sabha, 243B the three tiers and 243I the State Finance Commission.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** some UPSC notes list Gram Sabha, three tiers or SEC as "voluntary" — **WRONG**.
APPSC-G2 2025 answered "**All of the above**" for the mandatory list.
Intermediate tier is optional where population is **20 lakh** or less.

n76113d149ba.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about membership of Panchayats?
o: All members at the three levels are directly elected from territorial constituencies
The Constitution prescribes a uniform method for choosing every village chairperson
Intermediate and district chairpersons are elected by and from among the elected members
The method of choosing the village chairperson is left to State law
n76113d149ba.x: The Constitution leaves the method of choosing a village chairperson to State law; it prescribes no uniform method.
xa: ⚠ IYB 2026 speaks of direct election of chairpersons (quoting the original Bill) — follow the Article as enacted.
Minimum age to be a member: **21** (**Art. 243F**).

nc6fa46f671d.s: If a Panchayat is dissolved before the expiry of its normal term, elections to reconstitute it shall ordinarily be completed within:
o: The remaining period of the original term only
nc6fa46f671d.x: Elections must ordinarily be completed within six months of dissolution. No election is necessary when the remainder of the Panchayat's term is less than six months.
nc6fa46f671d.tq: Separate the six-month election deadline from the exception concerning the remaining term.
xs: After early dissolution, elections within **six months** — option **(2)**.
No election is needed if **less than six months** of the term remain.
xa: The reconstituted panchayat serves only the **remainder** of the term.
Normal term: **5 years** (**Art. 243E**).

n7943254252e.s: Which one of the following is correct regarding a Panchayat constituted after an early dissolution?
o: It serves only for the remainder of the original term.
It always enjoys a fresh five-year term.
It continues until the next general election to the State Legislature.
It serves for six months only.
n7943254252e.x: A Panchayat constituted after an early dissolution continues only for the remainder of the period for which the dissolved Panchayat would have continued.
n7943254252e.tq: Reject the tempting but incorrect assumption that every newly elected Panchayat gets a fresh full term.
xs: A panchayat formed after early dissolution serves **only the remainder** of the original term — option **(1)**.
It does not get a fresh **five-year** term.
xa: Elections must be held within **six months** of dissolution.
No election if the remaining term is **under six months**.

n8790405a810.s: Reservation of not less than one-third of the total number of offices of chairpersons in Panchayats for women is provided under:
n8790405a810.x: Article 243D(4) provides reservation of not less than one-third of the offices of chairpersons in Panchayats for women.
n8790405a810.tq: Discriminate between adjacent constitutional clauses dealing with seats and chairperson posts.
xs: **Article 243D(4)**: **one-third** of seats and **chairperson** posts for women — option **(1)**.
**243E** is about duration; **243C** about composition.
xa: The one-third is a **floor**; many states raised it to **50%**.
**Bihar** was first to give **50%**, in **2006**.
Reserved seats **rotate**.

nbffa375a2e3.s: Which of the following initiatives is intended to counter token representation of women in Panchayati Raj institutions?
o: Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan and Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats
PESA and the Sixteenth Finance Commission grants
nbffa375a2e3.x: The Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan and Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats are intended to promote substantive women’s leadership and counter token representation.
nbffa375a2e3.tq: Match the initiative with its stated social-governance objective.
xs: **Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan** and **Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats** counter token representation — option **(2)**.
**SabhaSaar** (on **Bhashini**) is an AI tool for Gram Sabha minutes; **OWMS** monitors AP water projects.
xa: Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan trains **women elected representatives**.
At least **one** Model Women-Friendly GP per district.
**Bokkasampalem** (Tirupati) won **1st** for women-friendly panchayat (**2026**).

n86104896dc8.s: The State Finance Commission is constituted every five years by the:
n86104896dc8.x: The Governor constitutes the SFC every five years to review local-body finances; its recommendations are advisory.
xa: Its report goes to the Governor, who lays it before the Legislature with an **action taken report**.
APPSC-G1 2022: set up **once in five years**.

nindian-polity-37-12.s: Under Article 243B, the intermediate tier of Panchayati Raj is optional for States with a population of:
nindian-polity-37-12.x: Under Article 243B, States with a population of 20 lakh or less need not have the intermediate tier.
n: Article 243B provides for a three-tier system and exemption. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The intermediate tier is optional for States with a population of 20 lakh or less. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The population threshold at which the intermediate tier is optional is 20 lakh. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xs: Under **Article 243B**, the intermediate tier is optional for States with a population of **20 lakh or less** — option **(2)**.
The **three-tier** system itself is **mandatory**: village, intermediate and district.
xa: The intermediate tier is called **Mandal Parishad** in **Andhra Pradesh**; **Panchayat Samiti** in most States.
⚠ UPSC match: **Mandal Praja Parishad** → AP; tribal councils → **Meghalaya**; no village panchayats → **Mizoram**.
Members at all levels are **directly elected**; intermediate and district chairpersons **indirectly** (**Art. 243C**).
**Minimum age 21** (**Art. 243F**); term **5 years** (**Art. 243E**).

nindian-polity-26-7.s: The Union Finance Commission is constituted by the President of India:
o: Only once during the President's term
Every five years or earlier as deemed necessary
Every ten years or earlier as decided by Parliament
nindian-polity-26-7.x: The President sets up a Finance Commission every five years, or earlier if needed. The interval is not rigidly fixed.
nindian-polity-26-7.tq: Recall the 'five years or earlier' rule.
n: The President of India constitutes the Finance Commission every five years or earlier when necessary. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The Finance Commission is not constituted strictly every five years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The Union Finance Commission is constituted every five years or earlier. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The President of India appoints the Union Finance Commission. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
xs: The Union Finance Commission is constituted **every five years or earlier** — option **(2)**.
It is appointed by the **President of India** under **Article 280** (**Part XII**).
xa: The **State Finance Commission** (**243-I and 243-Y**) is appointed by the **Governor** every **five years**.
Union FC deals with the **Union–States** split; SFC with the **State–local bodies** split.
The SFC report goes to the **Governor** and the **State Legislature**, with an **action taken report**.
The SFC is **advisory**, not binding.

o: Only the elected Panchayat members and the Sarpanch
Persons registered in the electoral rolls of villages within the Panchayat area
Members of the Panchayat Samiti from the village
Persons nominated by the State Election Commission
nba12ef5c29e.x: The Gram Sabha comprises persons on the village electoral rolls of the Panchayat area; its powers are left to State law.
xa: In **Fifth Schedule** areas under **PESA 1996**, the **Gram Sabha is supreme**.
GS NIRNAY (**2023**) is an app on Gram Sabha decisions.

n68f8fa1c787.s: The People's Plan Campaign 'Sabki Yojana Sabka Vikas' has been run since:
n68f8fa1c787.x: The campaign has run since 2 October 2018, preparing Gram Panchayat Development Plans through Gram Sabhas.
xa: ⚠ **Kerala People's Plan Campaign 1996** vs national "**Sabki Yojana Sabka Vikas**" **2 Oct 2018**.
**e-GramSwaraj**: **2.54 lakh GPs** uploaded GPDP for FY25.

na068ee9b140.s: PESA, 1996 was enacted following the recommendations of which committee?
na068ee9b140.x: PESA followed the recommendations of the Bhuria Committee, constituted in 1995.
na068ee9b140.tq: Avoid the common committee-name trap by linking PESA with the Bhuria Committee.
xs: **PESA 1996** came from the **Bhuria Committee** (**1995**) — option **(2)**.
**Sarkaria** and **Punchhi** are not linked to PESA in the notes.
xa: PESA extends Part IX to **Fifth Schedule** areas in **ten States, including AP**.
It was done under **Art. 243M(4)(b)**.
**30 years of PESA** were marked in **2026**.

nac494e262fb.s: In Scheduled Areas, the Gram Sabha under PESA must be consulted before:
nac494e262fb.x: PESA requires consultation with the Gram Sabha before land acquisition in Scheduled Areas.
nac494e262fb.tq: Apply the consultation requirement to a land-related administrative decision.
xs: Under PESA the Gram Sabha must be consulted before **land acquisition** — option **(3)**.
This applies in **Fifth Schedule** (Scheduled) areas under **PESA 1996**.
xa: In Fifth Schedule areas the **Gram Sabha is supreme**.
It owns **minor forest produce** and controls village markets and **liquor**.
PESA came from the **Bhuria Committee (1995)**.

nffe68f7eaa8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Gram Sabha in Fifth Schedule areas under PESA, 1996?
o: It approves plans and identifies beneficiaries
It is regarded as supreme and may settle disputes in the customary way
It has only an advisory role, with village markets and liquor under the State Excise Department
It controls village markets and liquor
nffe68f7eaa8.x: Under PESA the Gram Sabha is not merely advisory; it controls village markets and liquor.
xa: It owns **minor forest produce** and must be consulted before **land acquisition**.
PESA covers **ten States**, including AP.

n8f8ed0ecd26.s: PESA, 1996 extends Part IX of the Constitution, with exceptions, to:
n8f8ed0ecd26.x: PESA applies only to Fifth Schedule Areas, recognising governance through customary law; it does not apply to Sixth Schedule areas.
xa: Sixth Schedule areas of **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram** are exempted under **243M**.
**Bhuria Committee 1995** → **PESA 1996**.

nb4a319561b4.s: Parliament extended Part IX to the Fifth Schedule (Scheduled) Areas, with modifications, through the PESA Act, 1996 under:
nb4a319561b4.x: Article 243M(4)(b) lets Parliament extend Part IX to Scheduled Areas with exceptions and modifications, which it did through PESA, 1996. Article 243ZC is the parallel exemption in Part IXA, 244A concerns an autonomous State in Assam, and 243D(6) enables backward-class reservation.
xs: **Article 243M(4)(b)** lets Parliament extend Part IX to **Scheduled Areas** — done by **PESA 1996** — option **(1)**.
**243ZC** is the parallel exemption in **Part IXA**.
xa: PESA came from the **Bhuria Committee, 1995**.
It covers Fifth Schedule areas in **ten States**, including AP.

n9df4bf1d4ce.s: Which of the following is NOT an Eleventh Schedule subject?
n9df4bf1d4ce.x: Land improvement, minor irrigation and fisheries are Eleventh Schedule subjects; public order is not.
xa: Other agri items: **animal husbandry, dairying, poultry**; **social and farm forestry**; **minor forest produce**.
Not in it: **defence**, **railways**.

n8d60d020661.s: The People's Plan Campaign associated with Kerala was launched in
n8d60d020661.x: Kerala's People's Plan Campaign was launched in 1996.
n8d60d020661.tq: Use the year as the decisive discriminator among Panchayati Raj milestones.
xs: Kerala's **People's Plan Campaign** began in **1996** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Don't confuse it with the national "**Sabki Yojana Sabka Vikas**" from **2 Oct 2018**.
xa: It devolved a large share of plan funds; plans were made **from Gram Sabhas up**.
**1973** = West Bengal Panchayat Act; **1978** = its first polls.

nbb7fe632558.s: The National Panchayat Awards use which index in their assessment?
nbb7fe632558.x: The awards, including the theme-wise Deen Dayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas Puraskar, are assessed using the Panchayat Advancement Index.
xa: AP's PR Department won the Deen Dayal Upadhyay awards for a **second consecutive year** (**2026**).
**Chittoor DPRC**: **1st**, Panchayat Capacity Building Institution Award **2026**.

n1f2f53e9d71.s: Under Article 243M, Part IX of the Constitution does NOT apply to which of the following States?
n1f2f53e9d71.x: Part IX does not apply to Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram, the Fifth and Sixth Schedule areas, or the hill areas of Manipur that have District Councils.
xa: Also exempted: **district-level** panchayats in the **Darjeeling hills**.
⚠ Parallel exemption for municipalities: **243ZC** (Part IXA).
Parliament extended Part IX to Fifth Schedule areas by **PESA 1996**.

n1e57c9feb37.s: Part IX is not applicable to which of the following areas in West Bengal?
o: All coastal districts of West Bengal
The entire State of West Bengal
n1e57c9feb37.x: Article 243M excludes the hill council area of Darjeeling district from the application of Part IX.
n1e57c9feb37.tq: Identify the area-specific exemption rather than treating the exclusion as State-wide.
xs: Part IX does not apply to the **Darjeeling hill council area** — option **(4)**.
Precisely: **district-level** panchayats in the **Darjeeling hills** are exempted (**243M**).
xa: Other exemptions: **Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram**; **hill areas of Manipur**.
**West Bengal** was a pioneer of the three-tier system (**1973** Act, **1978** polls).

n543551da46c.s: The 13 Zilla Parishads of Andhra Pradesh are being reorganised into how many Zilla Parishads?
n543551da46c.x: The cited reorganisation proposes increasing the number of Zilla Parishads from 13 to 28.
n543551da46c.tq: Test the before-and-after figures in a current-affairs numerical comparison.
xs: AP's **13** Zilla Parishads are being reorganised into **28** — option **(3)**.
The **13** ZPPs date from the older district count (May 2026); **28** is the new figure (Sep 2026).
xa: AP has ~**15,000+** GPs and **588** mandals.
AP tiers: Gram Panchayat — **Mandal Parishad** — Zilla Parishad.
**2026** local body polls are under SEC **Punetha**.

nb0592276c86.s: Which State was the first to launch Panchayati Raj Institutions, and when did Andhra Pradesh launch them?
o: Andhra Pradesh first on 1 November 1959; Rajasthan second on 2 October 1959
Rajasthan first on 2 October 1959; Andhra Pradesh second on 1 November 1959
Rajasthan first on 1 November 1959; Andhra Pradesh second on 2 October 1959
Andhra Pradesh first on 2 October 1959; Rajasthan second on 1 November 1959
nb0592276c86.x: Rajasthan was the first State to launch PRIs on 2 October 1959, while Andhra Pradesh was the second on 1 November 1959.
nb0592276c86.tq: Anchor the sequence with the first and second States and verify both dates.
xs: **Rajasthan** first (**2 October 1959**), **AP** second (**1 November 1959**) — option **(2)**.
The other options swap the states or the dates.
xa: ⚠ **First to implement the 73rd** = **Madhya Pradesh**, not Rajasthan.
**Bihar** was first to give women **50%**, in **2006**.
**West Bengal** = pioneer three-tier system (**1973** Act, **1978** polls).

nd50c4fe0f08.s: Which State was the first to provide 50 per cent reservation for women in local bodies?
nd50c4fe0f08.x: Bihar was the first State mentioned as having raised reservation for women in local bodies to 50 per cent, in 2006.
nd50c4fe0f08.tq: Test the first-adopter trap among States that subsequently provided 50 per cent reservation.
xs: **Bihar** was first to give **50%** reservation to women, in **2006** — option **(3)**.
**Madhya Pradesh** was first to **implement the 73rd** (MPPSC 2015 key).
xa: **AP**, **Himachal Pradesh**, **Madhya Pradesh** and **Sikkim** meet **50%** exactly.
Women = **12.14 lakh (49.75%)** of **24.41 lakh** elected panchayat representatives.

n286d47178a3.s: According to Ministry of Panchayati Raj data (April 2026), women make up approximately what share of the elected representatives of Panchayati Raj Institutions?
n286d47178a3.x: Of 24.41 lakh elected panchayat representatives, 12.14 lakh (49.75%) are women, well above the constitutional floor of one-third (33%). 40% and 60% do not match the data.
n286d47178a3.tq: One-third is the floor; actual share is near 50%.
xs: Women are **about 49.75 per cent** of elected panchayat representatives — option **(3)** (MoPR, **23 Apr 2026**).
Of **24.41 lakh** representatives, **12.14 lakh** are women — far above the **one-third** floor of **Art. 243D(4)**.
xa: Women increasingly win **unreserved** seats too.
**AP, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Sikkim** meet the **50%** quota exactly.
Short of 50%: **Gujarat 49.9%**, **Haryana 42.12%**, **Tripura 45.25%**.

n04adce0240a.s: Which of the following is NOT part of the triple test laid down in Vikas Kishanrao Gawali v. State of Maharashtra (2021)?
o: A dedicated commission conducting a rigorous empirical inquiry
Keeping aggregate SC, ST and OBC reservation within 50 per cent
Fixing local-body-wise reservation based on the findings
Automatic reservation of 50 per cent for OBCs in every local body
n04adce0240a.x: The judgment provides for no automatic 50 per cent OBC reservation; the other three make up the triple test.
xa: AP: a **34%** BC quota plus SC/ST shares must pass Gawali's **50%** ceiling.
AP's **G.O. Rt. No. 1065** notified a **33.33%** BC quota for ULB polls.

ncc9b5902fb9.s: Which legislation gives effect to Article 243I for Panchayats in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The Andhra Pradesh Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2005
The Andhra Pradesh Land Revenue Act, 1990
The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994
The Andhra Pradesh Municipal Corporations Act, 1955
ncc9b5902fb9.x: Part VI of the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 gives effect to Article 243I for Panchayats.
ncc9b5902fb9.tq: Match the constitutional provision with its State-level implementing law.
xs: **Part VI** of the **AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994** gives effect to **Art. 243I** — option **(3)**.
It is AP's conformity law — **Act No. 13 of 1994**.
xa: It has **278 sections** in **8 Parts**.
Enacted on **21 April 1994**.

n09c5c17c90d.s: Which State was the first to implement the 73rd Constitutional Amendment by holding panchayat elections under it?
n09c5c17c90d.x: Madhya Pradesh was the first State to implement the 73rd Amendment (MPPSC 2015 key). Rajasthan was first to adopt Panchayati Raj in 1959; Andhra Pradesh was second in 1959 and passed its conformity Act on 21 April 1994; Kerala is known for the 1996 People's Plan Campaign.
n09c5c17c90d.tq: Pre-1993 first = Rajasthan; post-73rd first = Madhya Pradesh.
xs: **Madhya Pradesh** was first to implement the 73rd Amendment — option **(1)** (MPPSC 2015 key).
**Rajasthan** was first to launch PRIs in **1959**; **AP** second; **Kerala** is known for the **1996** People's Plan Campaign.
xa: AP passed its conformity Act on **21 April 1994**.
MP also meets the **50%** women quota exactly.

n908e7313f9d.s: The e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project was introduced under
n908e7313f9d.x: The e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project was undertaken under the National e-Governance Plan, launched in 2006.
n908e7313f9d.tq: Match a digital governance project with its parent programme and year.
