xs: The **e-Panchayat MMP** came under the **National e-Governance Plan** (NeGP, **2006**) — option **(2)**.
**AMRUT 2.0** (**2021**) is a MoHUA urban mission.
xa: Its apps: **PriaSoft**, **PlanPlus**, **AuditOnline**.
**e-GramSwaraj** came in **2020**.

naa16337747b.s: The issue concerning the 34 per cent BC reservation in Andhra Pradesh local bodies is that the BC quota together with SC/ST shares must remain within the:
o: Fifty per cent ceiling associated with the Gawali principle
naa16337747b.x: Under the Vikas Kishanrao Gawali triple test (2021), total SC+ST+OBC reservation must not exceed 50 per cent, so the 34 per cent BC quota plus SC/ST shares must stay within that 50 per cent ceiling.
naa16337747b.tq: Add the reservation components conceptually and identify the applicable ceiling.
xs: AP's **34%** BC quota plus SC/ST shares must stay within the **fifty per cent** ceiling of **Gawali** — option **(1)**.
Gawali (**2021**) triple test: dedicated commission, local-body-wise proportion, **SC+ST+OBC** not above **50%**.
xa: **K. Krishna Murthy (2010)** had set **50%** as the normal cap.
**G.O. Rt. No. 1065** notified a **33.33%** BC quota for AP ULB polls.

nee57df82ec1.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional provisions relating to the State Finance Commission?
o: Article 243I concerns the Union Finance Commission and Article 243Y concerns State Budgets
Article 243I concerns Municipalities and Article 243Y concerns Panchayats
Article 243I concerns Panchayats and Article 243Y extends the role to Municipalities
Both Articles 243I and 243Y concern only the distribution of Union taxes
nee57df82ec1.x: Article 243I provides for the State Finance Commission to review Panchayat finances, while Article 243Y applies the corresponding review to Municipalities.
nee57df82ec1.tq: Discriminate between the closely related Articles 243I and 243Y by matching each Article with its local-body level.
xs: **243I** = SFC for **Panchayats**; **243Y** = the same Commission for **Municipalities** — option **(3)**.
The Union Finance Commission is under **Art. 280**, not 243I.
xa: It recommends sharing **State taxes, duties, tolls and fees**, assigned taxes and **grants-in-aid**.
APPSC-G2 2025: it examines finances **and** reviews revenue distribution between state and local bodies.

n65ee3ad9a61.s: Under Article 280(3)(bb) and Article 280(3)(c), the Union Finance Commission recommends measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State for supplementing the resources of:
o: Panchayats under clause (bb) and municipalities under clause (c)
Municipalities under clause (bb) and Panchayats under clause (c)
State Legislatures under clause (bb) and municipalities under clause (c)
n65ee3ad9a61.x: Article 280(3)(bb) concerns panchayats and was inserted through the 73rd Amendment. Article 280(3)(c) concerns municipalities and was inserted through the 74th Amendment.
n65ee3ad9a61.tq: Discriminate between neighbouring constitutional clauses and the local bodies covered by them.
xs: **280(3)(bb)** = **panchayats** (73rd); **280(3)(c)** = **municipalities** (74th) — option **(1)**.
The **Central Finance Commission** recommends measures to augment a **State's Consolidated Fund** for these.
xa: It acts **on the basis of the SFC's recommendations**.
⚠ "Union FC has no role in LB assistance" is **false** (UPPSC 2011).

nfb6a4a4b316.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Union Finance Commission's role in local-body finance?
o: It recommends measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State
Its local-body recommendations draw on those of the State Finance Commission
Central tax devolution is paid directly to Panchayats rather than to the States
Panchayats receive Central assistance through Finance Commission grants
nfb6a4a4b316.x: Central tax devolution goes to the States; Panchayats get Central assistance through Finance Commission grants.
xa: Clause **(bb)** came with the 73rd; clause **(c)** with the 74th.
AP local bodies stand to lose **₹12,150 crore** of Central funds if elections are not held by October 2026.

nb57c67a58ac.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the State Finance Commission?
o: Distribution of net proceeds of State taxes, duties, tolls and fees between the State and local bodies
Appointment of the State Election Commissioner
Grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of the State
Measures to improve the finances of Panchayats and Municipalities
nb57c67a58ac.x: The SFC recommends on fiscal distribution, grants-in-aid and local finances; appointing the State Election Commissioner is not its function.
xa: The **State Election Commission** is under **Art. 243K**.
The SFC also handles any matter the **Governor** refers.

nindian-polity-26-5.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Finance Commission?
o: Recommending the distribution of divisible Union taxes between the Centre and States
Recommending the allocation of the States' share among the States
Recommending principles for grants-in-aid out of the Consolidated Fund of India
Resolving Centre-State legal disputes under Article 131
nindian-polity-26-5.x: Article 131 disputes go to the Supreme Court; the other three are Finance Commission functions.
n: The Finance Commission deals with the distribution of the net proceeds of divisible Union taxes between the Centre and the States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The Finance Commission deals with the allocation of the net proceeds of divisible Union taxes among the States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The Finance Commission recommends principles governing grants-in-aid of State revenues from the Consolidated Fund of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
Legal and constitutional disputes between the Centre and the States are resolved by the Supreme Court. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The Supreme Court resolves Centre–State legal and constitutional disputes under its Original Jurisdiction. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
Article 131 provides for the Supreme Court's Original Jurisdiction. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The Finance Commission does not resolve legal or constitutional fiscal disputes between the Centre and the States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The Finance Commission recommends the allocation of tax proceeds among the States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
Article 275 provides for grants-in-aid of State revenues from the Consolidated Fund of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The Union Finance Commission deals with fiscal distribution between the Union and the States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The Finance Commission recommends the principles for statutory grants-in-aid under Article 275. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
xa: It also suggests measures to **augment the Consolidated Fund of a State** to supplement **Panchayats** and **Municipalities**, based on **SFC** recommendations.
⚠ "Union FC has no role in local-body assistance" is **false** (UPPSC 2011).
Report goes to the **President**, then **Parliament** (**Article 281**).

n8d1f1570314.s: In Andhra Pradesh, which of the following correctly represents the three Panchayati Raj tiers?
o: Gram Panchayat, Mandal Parishad and Zilla Parishad
Gram Sabha, Municipal Council and Zilla Parishad
Village Council, Taluk Board and District Council
Gram Panchayat, Nagar Panchayat and Zilla Parishad
n8d1f1570314.x: The Andhra Pradesh structure comprises Gram Panchayats, Mandal Parishads or Mandal Praja Parishads, and Zilla Parishads.
n8d1f1570314.tq: Match the State-specific names with the three constitutional levels.
xs: AP tiers: **Gram Panchayat**, **Mandal Parishad** (Mandal Praja Parishad), **Zilla Parishad** — option **(1)**.
**Municipal Council** and **Nagar Panchayat** are urban bodies, not PR tiers.
xa: AP has **588** mandals and ~**15,000+** GPs.
**13** ZPPs are being reorganised into **28**.
PESA applies in AP's **agency areas**.

nindian-polity-37-46.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional position of the three-tier Panchayati Raj structure?
o: It is applicable only to urban areas
It is applicable only where the intermediate tier is compulsory
It is merely an administrative arrangement
nindian-polity-37-46.x: The three-tier structure is compulsory under Article 243B, though States under 20 lakh may skip the middle tier. It is a constitutional requirement, not just an administrative choice.
nindian-polity-37-46.tq: Recall that three tiers are compulsory, with one exemption.
n: The three-tier Panchayati Raj structure is mandatory. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xs: The three-tier structure is **mandatory** under **Article 243B** — option **(2)**.
Only the **intermediate tier** may be skipped, by States with a population of **20 lakh** or less.
It is a **compulsory** provision of **Part IX**, not a mere **administrative** arrangement and not limited to **urban** areas.
xa: Other compulsory provisions: **Gram Sabha**, **direct election**, **minimum age 21**, **one-third** seats for women, **State Election Commission**.
Voluntary: representation of **MPs and MLAs**, reservation for **backward classes**, devolving the **29** subjects.
⚠ Some UPSC notes wrongly list the Gram Sabha, three tiers and SEC as voluntary.

n584c311ed3a.s: The Municipal Corporations of Bombay and Calcutta were established in:
n584c311ed3a.x: The Municipal Corporations of Bombay and Calcutta were established in 1726.
n584c311ed3a.tq: Use the distinct early-municipality dates to distinguish 1726 from the later decentralisation milestones.
xs: The Municipal Corporations of **Bombay** and **Calcutta** came in **1726** — option **(2)**.
**1688** = **Madras** (first corporation); **1870** = **Lord Mayo**; **1882** = **Lord Ripon**.
xa: Madras charter dated **30 Dec 1687**; corporation began **29 Sep 1688**.
⚠ **Mayo 1870** = financial decentralisation; **Ripon 1882** = "**Magna Carta**".
UP's **KAVAL towns** got corporations in **1953**.

n84826614a12.s: The Bill introduced in September 1991 that became the 74th Constitutional Amendment was introduced by the government of:
n84826614a12.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao's Bill of September 1991 became the 74th Amendment and inserted Part IXA; the 1989 Municipalities Bill had lapsed.
xa: Passed by both Houses **December 1992**; in force **1 June 1993**.
Part IXA: **Art. 243P to 243ZG**, **18** Articles.

n2e3d7f81ff6.s: Which resolution is described as the 'Magna Carta' of local self-government in India?
o: The UP Municipal Corporations Act of 1959
n2e3d7f81ff6.x: Lord Ripon's resolution of 1882 is called the Magna Carta of local self-government. Lord Mayo's 1870 resolution dealt with financial decentralisation. The 1687 charter created the Madras corporation, and the 1959 UP Act followed the KAVAL towns corporations; neither is the Magna Carta.
n2e3d7f81ff6.tq: Ripon 1882 = Magna Carta; Mayo 1870 = financial decentralisation.
xs: **Lord Ripon's resolution of 1882** is the "**Magna Carta**" of local self-government — option **(2)**.
**Lord Mayo's 1870** resolution was on **financial decentralisation**.
The **1687** charter set up the Madras corporation; the **1959** UP Act followed the KAVAL corporations.
xa: Madras corporation began **29 Sep 1688**.
**Bombay** and **Calcutta** corporations: **1726**.

nefd9bf81497.s: Local Government is a subject in which List of the Seventh Schedule?
nefd9bf81497.x: Local Government remains in the State List; the 74th Amendment did not move it to the Union List.
xa: **243ZF** also lets existing laws continue for one year.
The 74th = **Nagarpalika Act**, in force **1 June 1993**.

n528f73753f2.s: Which one of the following matters is voluntary and may be decided by the State legislature under the 74th Amendment?
o: The five-year term of a municipality
The manner of electing the municipal Chairperson
Ward Committees in municipalities with a population of three lakh or more
State Election Commission supervision of municipal elections
n528f73753f2.x: The manner of electing the Chairperson or Mayor is left to the State legislature. The other three are compulsory constitutional provisions.
n528f73753f2.tq: Use the compulsory-versus-voluntary table to identify the discretionary provision.
xs: **The manner of electing the municipal Chairperson** is left to the state — option **(2)**.
The **5-year term**, **Ward Committees** (**3 lakh+**) and **SEC** supervision are compulsory.
xa: AP Cabinet (**18 Aug 2026**) approved **direct election of Mayors** and chairpersons, replacing the indirect system.
Other voluntary items: **BC reservation**, **MP/MLA representation**.

n63669e6c348.s: Cantonment Boards come under which Union Ministry?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
n63669e6c348.x: Cantonment Boards are under the Ministry of Defence; MoHUA is the main ministry for ULBs, and Home Affairs handles ULBs in UTs.
xa: ULBs in AP come under the **MA&UD** department.
MoHUA is the **main** ministry; Defence handles only **cantonment boards**.

n2e2072b5d5e.s: The constitutional provisions relating to District Planning Committees and Metropolitan Planning Committees were inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
n2e2072b5d5e.x: DPCs and MPCs are part of Part IXA and were inserted through the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992. The 73rd Amendment concerns Panchayats under Part IX.
n2e2072b5d5e.tq: Discriminate between the 73rd rural-local-body Amendment and the 74th urban-local-body Amendment.
xs: DPCs and MPCs were inserted by **the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992** — option **(1)**.
⚠ The DPC sits in **Part IXA** — the **74th**, not the 73rd (APPSC-GS 2018).
xa: DPC = **Art. 243ZD**; MPC = **Art. 243ZE**.
The 74th came into force on **1 June 1993**.

nf89f55a26d0.s: Critics of urban governance have described Urban Local Bodies as the ____ of federalism.
nf89f55a26d0.x: ULBs, which spend less than 1 per cent of GDP and employ about 10 per cent of the public workforce, have been called the 'stepchild' of federalism.
xa: **Property tax** is the key own revenue but is chronically **under-collected**.
Cities house **~36%** of India's population.

ncad629a993f.s: Which one of the following is identified as the key own-source revenue of Urban Local Bodies but is chronically under-collected?
ncad629a993f.x: Property tax is the key own-source revenue of Urban Local Bodies, but it is chronically under-collected.
ncad629a993f.tq: Identify the principal own-revenue source rather than a shared tax.
xs: **Property tax** is the ULBs' key own revenue, chronically under-collected — option **(2)**.
The notes name no other tax (stamp duty, motor vehicle or entertainment) as the ULBs' key own revenue.
xa: ULBs spend **less than 1%** of GDP.
Their taxing powers and grants (**243X**) are left to state legislatures.
They are the "**stepchild**" of federalism.

n24ca8b1bf62.s: Which committee (1984) gave the District Collector a central role in district planning?
n24ca8b1bf62.x: The Hanumantha Rao Committee (1984) made the Collector central to district planning. The Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta and G.V.K. Rao committees (along with ARC-I) instead reduced the Collector's role.
n24ca8b1bf62.tq: Hanumantha Rao = Collector central; the rest reduced the Collector's role.
xs: The **Hanumantha Rao Committee (1984)** kept the **Collector central** to district planning — option **(3)**.
**Balwantrai Mehta**, **ARC-I**, **Ashok Mehta** and **G.V.K. Rao** reduced the Collector's role.
xa: In **AP**, the **District Collector** still chairs the District Plan and Development Committee.
In **Kerala** the Collector is only **member-secretary** of the DPC.

nindian-polity-37-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the history of local self-government in India?
o: Charles Metcalfe called Indian village communities 'Little Republics'.
Madras was the first Municipal Corporation, set up in 1688.
The Government of India Act, 1919 made local self-government a Reserved Subject.
Lord Ripon is called the Father of Local Self-Government in India.
nindian-polity-37-2.x: The 1919 Act made local self-government a transferred subject under dyarchy, run by elected Ministers, not a reserved one.
n: Charles Metcalfe described Indian village communities as “Little Republics.” [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Lord Ripon’s 1882 Resolution recognized Lord Ripon as the Father of Local Self-Government in India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The Government of India Act, 1919 made Local Self-Government a Transferred Subject under provincial dyarchy. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Madras established the first Municipal Corporation. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The first Municipal Corporation was established in Madras in 1688. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xa: Ripon's **1882** resolution is the "**Magna Carta**" of local self-government.
⚠ **Mayo 1870** = financial decentralisation; **Ripon 1882** = "Magna Carta".
**Bombay and Calcutta** got Municipal Corporations in **1726**.
The Madras charter was dated **30 Dec 1687**; the corporation began **29 Sep 1688**.

nindian-polity-37-24.s: How many functional subjects are listed in the Twelfth Schedule?
nindian-polity-37-24.x: The Twelfth Schedule lists 18 subjects for municipalities; the Eleventh lists 29 for Panchayats.
n: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act concerns rural local self-government. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act concerns urban local self-government. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act contains the 11th Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The 11th Schedule contains 29 functional subjects. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act contains the 12th Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The 12th Schedule contains 18 functional subjects. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xa: The 11th Schedule came by the **73rd Amendment, 1992**; the 12th by the **74th Amendment, 1992**.
**9th Schedule** — **1st Amendment, 1951** (land reforms); **10th Schedule** — **52nd Amendment, 1985** (Anti-Defection).
**Part IV-A** (Fundamental Duties, **Article 51A**) — **42nd Amendment, 1976**.
**Part IX-B** (Co-operative Societies) — **97th Amendment, 2011**.

nindian-polity-37-30.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about reservation for women in local bodies?
o: Article 243D deals with reservation in Panchayats.
Article 243T deals with reservation in Municipalities.
The minimum reservation for women is less than one-third of total seats.
Reservation for women also applies to chairpersons' posts.
nindian-polity-37-30.x: At least one-third of seats and chairpersons' posts must be reserved for women under Articles 243D and 243T.
n: Article 243D deals with reservations in Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243T deals with reservations in Municipalities. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Reservation for women must be not less than one-third of the total seats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Reservation for women must be not less than one-third of the chairperson positions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
One-third reservation is at least 33 percent. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xa: Composition: **243C** / **243R**, regulated by the **State Legislature**; minimum age **21** years.
**243G / 243W**: economic development, social justice, sanitation, public health.
**243J / 243Z**: audit laws by the **State Legislature**.
**243K / 243ZA**: State Election Commission — superintendence, direction and conduct of local elections.

n11bee1188c2.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the three types of municipalities specifically recognised under Article 243Q?
n11bee1188c2.x: Article 243Q recognises Nagar Panchayats for transitional areas, Municipal Councils for smaller urban areas and Municipal Corporations for larger urban areas. Cantonment Boards are other forms of urban local bodies outside this classification.
n11bee1188c2.tq: Find the one institution outside the constitutional three-fold classification.
xs: The **Cantonment Board** is not one of the **243Q** types — option **(1)**.
243Q types: **Nagar Panchayat** (transitional), **Municipal Council** (smaller), **Municipal Corporation** (larger).
xa: Cantonment Boards come under the **Ministry of Defence**.
Also outside 243Q: notified area committee, town area committee, township, port trust, special purpose agency.

na871b9191ad.s: A Municipal Corporation generally comprises which three principal authorities?
o: Mayor, State Finance Commission and Commissioner
Council, District Collector and Standing Committee
na871b9191ad.x: The three principal authorities of a Municipal Corporation are the Council headed by the Mayor, the Standing Committees and the Commissioner.
na871b9191ad.tq: Match the institutional structure rather than individual office-holders.
xs: A Municipal Corporation has a **Council** (headed by the Mayor), **Standing Committees** and a **Commissioner** — option **(2)**.
The **Governor**, the **SFC** and the **District Collector** are not corporation authorities.
xa: The **Municipal Commissioner** (IAS, appointed by the State) is the chief executive.
The **Mayor** (assisted by a Deputy Mayor) presides over the Council.

n5ee1f056c1f.s: Under the Community Participation Law, an Area Sabha consists of:
o: All elected councillors of the municipality
Members of the Wards Committee only
All voters in a polling-booth area
Members of Parliament from the urban area
n5ee1f056c1f.x: An Area Sabha consists of all voters in a polling-booth area and sits below the Wards Committee.
xa: The **Community Participation Law** was a **JNNURM** mandatory reform.
Wards Committees: **243S**, mandatory at **3 lakh+**.

n857969550c7.s: Who is the chief executive of a Municipal Corporation and is ordinarily appointed by the State Government?
n857969550c7.x: The Municipal Commissioner is the chief executive of a Municipal Corporation and is appointed by the State Government, commonly from the IAS.
n857969550c7.tq: Apply the “who would do this job?” method to separate political leadership from administration.
xs: The **Municipal Commissioner** (IAS, appointed by the State) is the chief executive — option **(3)**.
The **Mayor** presides over the Council; the **Chairperson** heads a Municipal Council / Nagar Panchayat.
xa: **GVMC** has **zonal commissioners** under the Municipal Commissioner.
Corporation = **Council** + **Standing Committees** + **Commissioner**.

o: State-appointed chief executive of a Municipal Corporation
Elected head of a Municipal Corporation
Elected head of a Gram Panchayat
ndb7302dbf47.x: The Municipal Commissioner is the State-appointed chief executive of a Municipal Corporation; the Mayor heads the Corporation and the Sarpanch the Gram Panchayat.
xa: AP rural: Sarpanch, **Mandal Parishad President (MPP)**, Zilla Parishad Chairperson.
AP urban: **Mayor** (Corporation), **Chairperson** (Municipality/Nagar Panchayat).

nindian-polity-37-8.s: Which body governs an area in transition from rural to urban?
nindian-polity-37-8.x: A Nagar Panchayat governs a transitional area; the Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad work at village, block and district level.
n: The village-level institution under the 73rd Amendment is the Gram Panchayat. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The block-level institution under the 73rd Amendment is the Panchayat Samiti. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The district-level institution under the 73rd Amendment is the Zila Parishad. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The institution for a transitional urban area under the 74th Amendment is the Nagar Panchayat. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xa: Under the 74th: **Municipal Council** for a smaller urban area; **Municipal Corporation** for a larger urban area.
The 73rd covers rural local government; the 74th urban.
Both systems are interlinked with district planning bodies — **DPC (Article 243ZD)** and **MPC (Article 243ZE)**.

n6a067ce6884.s: The Constitution (Seventy-Fourth Amendment) Act, 1992 inserted which Schedule?
n6a067ce6884.x: The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA (Articles 243P-243ZG) and the Twelfth Schedule; the Eleventh Schedule came with the 73rd.
xa: The Twelfth Schedule is linked to **Art. 243W**.
In force **1 June 1993**.

nc27e09e52d3.s: Which one of the following is NOT a compulsory provision under the 74th Amendment?
o: Reservation for backward classes in every municipality
Ward Committees in municipalities having a population of three lakh or more
Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to population
nc27e09e52d3.x: Reservation for backward classes is voluntary and is left to the State legislature. Ward Committees for municipalities with a population of three lakh or more, five-year terms, and SC/ST reservation are compulsory provisions.
nc27e09e52d3.tq: Find the provision expressly left to State legislative discretion among otherwise mandatory features.
xs: **Reservation for backward classes** is **voluntary** — option **(1)**.
Compulsory: **Ward Committees** (**3 lakh or more**), **SC/ST reservation** by population, **5-year** term.
xa: Other voluntary items: representation of **MPs, MLAs, MLCs**; manner of electing the **Chairperson**.
Devolving the Twelfth Schedule subjects (**243W**) is also voluntary.

n440070414e8.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for Ward Committees?
n440070414e8.x: Article 243S provides for Ward Committees; 243Q covers types of municipalities, 243R their composition and 243T reservation.
xa: **243U** — duration (**5 years**); **243V** — disqualifications (age **21**).
**243W** — powers and the **Twelfth Schedule**.

n4cfcae4341e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about municipal tenure and elections?
o: An election must be held within one year of the dissolution of a municipality
A municipality has a five-year term
The State Election Commission conducts municipal elections
The State Finance Commission reviews the financial position of municipalities
n4cfcae4341e.x: An election must be held within six months of dissolution, not one year.
xa: ⚠ **243K / 243ZA** = SEC; **243I / 243Y** = SFC — one body each for panchayats and municipalities.
The term runs from the **first meeting**.

n3e923606665.s: Which Article provides for the powers, authority and responsibilities of municipalities, including matters in the Twelfth Schedule?
n3e923606665.x: Article 243W deals with the powers, authority and responsibilities of municipalities and links them with the Twelfth Schedule.
n3e923606665.tq: Test the Article by its functional subject instead of its numerical proximity.
xs: **Article 243W** covers municipal powers and the **Twelfth Schedule** — option **(4)**.
**243Z** = audit; **243V** = disqualifications; **243Y** = Finance Commission.
xa: The Twelfth Schedule has **18** functional items.
Its panchayat counterpart is **243G** (Eleventh Schedule, **29**).

nbb46df591b4.s: Under Article 243ZA, municipal elections are conducted by the:
nbb46df591b4.x: Under Article 243ZA, municipal elections are conducted by the State Election Commission, not the Election Commission of India.
xa: The SEC under 243ZA is the same as under **243K**.
**243ZG** bars courts in electoral matters.

nc2f713924f0.s: Where an industrial establishment provides municipal services, the Governor may under Article 243Q specify the area as a(n):
nc2f713924f0.x: Under the proviso to Article 243Q the Governor may specify such an area as an industrial township, and a municipality need not be constituted there.
xa: The Governor specifies area types by **public notification**.
Criteria: population, density, revenue, non-agricultural employment, economic importance.

n9f94e552797.s: The term of a municipality under Article 243U is calculated from the date of its:
n9f94e552797.x: A municipality continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless dissolved earlier according to law.
n9f94e552797.tq: Distinguish the constitutional starting point from election and notification dates.
xs: The term runs **five years** from the **first meeting** — option **(3)** (**243U**).
Not from the election result, budget session or Governor's notification.
xa: After dissolution, polls within **six months**.
The municipality is **heard** before dissolution.
Panchayat term is also **5 years** (**243E**).

n537e33d4b6c.s: Under Article 243U, before a municipality is dissolved it must be given:
o: A reasonable opportunity of being heard
Approval of the State Election Commission
n537e33d4b6c.x: Article 243U requires that a municipality be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard before its dissolution.
xa: Fresh polls within **six months** of dissolution.
Polls are run by the **SEC** (**243ZA**).

n46ae70925c6.s: Under Article 243R, which persons may be represented in a municipality but without the right to vote in its meetings?
o: Officials of the State Election Commission
Persons with special knowledge or experience in municipal administration
Members of the State Finance Commission
n46ae70925c6.x: State law may provide for representation of persons with special knowledge or experience in municipal administration, but they cannot vote in municipal meetings.
xa: State law may add **Lok Sabha/Assembly** members for the area.
**Rajya Sabha/Council** members **registered as electors** there may be added.

n6e420cf8b87.s: Under Article 243S of the Constitution, a Wards Committee is mandatory in a municipality having a population of:
n6e420cf8b87.x: Article 243S makes Wards Committees mandatory in municipalities having a population of three lakh or more.
n6e420cf8b87.tq: Identify the constitutional population threshold precisely.
xs: Wards Committees are mandatory in municipalities of **three lakh or more** — option **(3)** (**243S**).
It is a **compulsory** provision of the 74th; other committees are voluntary.
xa: A committee may cover **one or more wards**.
⚠ **Wards committee** = Constitution (**243S**); **Area Sabha** = **Model Nagara Raj Bill 2008**.
**MPC** threshold: **10 lakh** population.

nc6dd2f90293.s: Which of the following is NOT a Twelfth Schedule subject?
o: Street lighting, parking, bus stops and public conveniences
nc6dd2f90293.x: Technical and vocational education is an Eleventh Schedule subject; the other three are Twelfth Schedule municipal subjects.
xa: Twelfth also covers **burial and cremation grounds**, electric crematoria.
And **water supply** (domestic, industrial, commercial), **roads and bridges**.

n6ae61d0f62e.s: Which one of the following best describes the present status of District Planning Committees in most States?
o: They have been abolished by subsequent constitutional amendments.
They are generally weak, and operationalising them remains a continuing mandate of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.
They function exclusively under the Union Ministry of Finance.
They have been replaced by Metropolitan Planning Committees in all districts.
n6ae61d0f62e.x: District Planning Committees remain weak in most States, and operationalising them continues to be listed among the mandates of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.
n6ae61d0f62e.tq: Distinguish constitutional existence from effective institutional functioning.
xs: DPCs are **weak in most States**; **operationalising** them is still an **MoPR** mandate — option **(2)**.
They have not been abolished or replaced by MPCs.
xa: It is one of the **three** mandates of the **Ministry of Panchayati Raj**.
⚠ Proposed **District Development Councils** were criticised as parallel bodies bypassing Zila Panchayats and ULBs.

naea4a498ceb.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the eight types of urban local bodies listed for India?
naea4a498ceb.x: The eight listed types are Municipal Corporation, Municipality or Municipal Council, Notified Area Committee, Town Area Committee, Cantonment Board, Township, Port Trust and Special Purpose Agency. Zonal Development Authority is not in the list.
naea4a498ceb.tq: Check every option against the complete named classification.
xs: **Zonal Development Authority** is not among the **eight** types — option **(2)**.
The eight: Municipal Corporation, Municipality, Notified Area Committee, Town Area Committee, **Cantonment Board**, Township, **Port Trust**, **Special Purpose Agency**.
xa: Only the first type groups appear in **243Q**; the rest lie outside it.
Cantonment Boards = **Ministry of Defence**.

n4f9915c5fb3.s: Under Article 243V, disqualifications for membership of a municipality are determined primarily with reference to:
o: Only rules framed by the Union Government
The law made by the municipal council itself
Only the Representation of the People Act, 1951
The law applicable to elections to the State Legislature or a State law
n4f9915c5fb3.x: A person may be disqualified under the law applicable to elections to the State Legislature or under a law made by the State Legislature.
n4f9915c5fb3.tq: Identify the correct level of law governing disqualification.
xs: Disqualifications follow **the law for State Legislature elections or a State law** — option **(4)** (**243V**).
Not Union rules, nor the municipal council's own law.
xa: Minimum age: **21 years**.
Same pattern as panchayats under **243F**.

n4891c2cfe9a.s: Which authority is responsible for electoral rolls and all municipal elections under Article 243ZA?
n4891c2cfe9a.x: Article 243ZA places the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of municipal elections under the State Election Commission, the same constitutional authority associated with Article 243K.
n4891c2cfe9a.tq: Ask who would do this job and reject the similarly named Union body.
xs: The **State Election Commission** handles electoral rolls and all municipal polls under **243ZA** — option **(1)**.
It is the **same SEC** as under **Art. 243K**.
xa: AP SEC Commissioner **Anil Chandra Punetha** notified ward-wise photo rolls for **41 ULBs**.
Rolls due **22 Sep 2026**; qualifying date **1 Jan 2026**.

nc8d4b1cc92e.s: A Metropolitan Planning Committee is constituted for every metropolitan area with a population of:
nc8d4b1cc92e.x: An MPC is mandatory for every metropolitan area of ten lakh or more under Article 243ZE, and such an area may span more than one district.
xa: The 10 lakh definition is in **Art. 243P**.
The **DPC** is under **243ZD**.
⚠ **DPC four-fifths** elected vs **MPC two-thirds** elected.

n43991a4f947.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the composition of a Metropolitan Planning Committee?
o: Not less than two-thirds of its members are elected
Elected members are chosen from municipal members and panchayat chairpersons in the area
Elected representation reflects the ratio of urban and rural population
Elected representation is in proportion to the geographical area of urban and rural parts
n43991a4f947.x: Elected representation in the MPC follows the urban-rural population ratio, not area.
xa: ⚠ DPC: **four-fifths** elected, from district panchayat and municipal members.
The MPC prepares a **draft development plan** for the whole metropolitan area.

nc2315d26eb5.s: The Constitution requires not less than ____ of the members of a District Planning Committee to be elected.
nc2315d26eb5.x: At least four-fifths of DPC members must be elected; the rest are decided by State law, so the DPC is not wholly elected.
xa: ⚠ APPSC-GS 2018: "**all members elected**" is the false statement.
The elected share is in proportion to the district's **rural-urban population**.

n6d98056646d.s: Which of the following is correct about the plans of the DPC and the MPC?
o: The DPC prepares a plan for the metropolitan area; the MPC prepares the district plan.
The DPC consolidates panchayat and municipal plans; the MPC prepares a plan for the whole metropolitan area.
Both committees prepare plans only for rural areas.
Neither committee is concerned with local plans.
n6d98056646d.x: The DPC consolidates panchayat and municipal plans into a draft district plan, while the MPC prepares a draft plan for the entire metropolitan area.
xa: The MPC also considers **Union/State objectives and investments**.
Both chairpersons **forward** the plan to the **State Government**.

nindian-polity-37-33.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the tenure and dissolution of Panchayats?
nindian-polity-37-33.x: Article 243E covers tenure; 243D covers reservations, 243G powers and 243-I the State Finance Commission.
n: Article 243D deals with reservations in Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243E deals with the tenure of Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
If a Panchayat or Municipality is dissolved prematurely, elections must be held within six months. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243G deals with the powers and responsibilities of Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243-I deals with the State Finance Commission for Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xa: Municipal counterparts: **243T**, **243U**, **243W**, **243-Y**.
**243J** → accounts and audit; **243K** → State Election Commission.
The SFC is constituted by the **Governor** every **five years**.

nindian-polity-37-40.s: Which Article provides for the Metropolitan Planning Committee?
nindian-polity-37-40.x: Article 243ZE provides for the MPC; 243W covers municipal powers, 243Y the Finance Commission and 243Z audit.
n: The Metropolitan Planning Committee is associated with Article 243ZE. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243W deals with the powers and responsibilities of Municipalities. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243-Y deals with the State Finance Commission for Municipalities. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243Z deals with accounts and audit of Municipalities. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xa: Panchayat counterparts: **243G**, **243-I**, **243J**.
**243ZD** → District Planning Committee.
**243ZA** → State Election Commission for municipal elections.

ne9ebdbb2e21.s: Which one of the following is included in the Twelfth Schedule?
o: Cattle pounds and prevention of cruelty to animals
ne9ebdbb2e21.x: Cattle pounds and prevention of cruelty to animals are Twelfth Schedule subjects. Non-conventional energy, small-scale industries and technical and vocational education are Eleventh Schedule subjects used as distractors.
ne9ebdbb2e21.tq: Separate municipal Twelfth Schedule functions from Panchayat Eleventh Schedule distractors.
xs: **Cattle pounds and prevention of cruelty to animals** are Twelfth Schedule items — option **(3)** (APPSC-G2 2025).
⚠ **Small-scale industries**, **technical and vocational education** and **non-conventional energy** are **Eleventh** Schedule distractors.
xa: Only in Twelfth: **fire services**, **slum improvement**, **slaughter houses and tanneries**, **vital statistics**, **burial grounds**.
Twelfth has **18** items.

n1df5aea4b5e.s: Which one of the following is NOT a subject in the Twelfth Schedule?
o: Regulation of slaughter houses and tanneries
n1df5aea4b5e.x: Libraries and markets and fairs are listed under the Eleventh Schedule, not the Twelfth Schedule. Urban poverty alleviation, urban forestry and environmental protection, and regulation of slaughter houses and tanneries are Twelfth Schedule subjects.
n1df5aea4b5e.tq: Use the municipal-versus-Panchayat list distinction to identify the excluded subject.
xs: **Libraries and markets and fairs** are **Eleventh** Schedule (panchayat) items — option **(1)**.
**Urban poverty alleviation**, **urban forestry and environment** and **slaughter houses and tanneries** are Twelfth Schedule items.
xa: Other Eleventh-only items: **PDS**, **small-scale industries**, **non-conventional energy**.
Twelfth also has **public health, sanitation, solid waste management**.

nedcdff2fe68.s: As per the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26, how many of the State's 123 urban local bodies are Municipal Corporations?
nedcdff2fe68.x: The Survey 2025-26 lists 17 Municipal Corporations, 76 Municipalities and 30 Nagar Panchayats among AP's 123 ULBs.
xa: Year-specific keys: APPSC 2018 = **71** municipalities; G1 2019 = **17** corporations.
APPCA May 2026 gives "**113** municipalities, **7** cantonment boards" — use the Survey split.

n0f1f78d79ee.s: Under G.O. Rt. No. 1065 dated 19 August 2026, the reservation provided for Backward Classes in Andhra Pradesh Urban Local Bodies is:
n0f1f78d79ee.x: G.O. Rt. No. 1065 provides 33.33 percent reservation for Backward Classes in Urban Local Bodies.
n0f1f78d79ee.tq: Distinguish the urban reservation figure from the rural reservation figure.
xs: **G.O. Rt. No. 1065** gives **33.33 percent** BC reservation in AP ULBs — option **(2)**.
**34%** is the figure for **rural** bodies.
xa: It is implemented under both municipal laws.
Approved by the AP Cabinet on **18 Aug 2026**.

n9458df3ddfd.s: The nodal department for Urban Local Bodies in Andhra Pradesh is the:
o: Municipal Administration and Urban Development Department
Panchayat Raj and Rural Development Department
n9458df3ddfd.x: The Municipal Administration and Urban Development (MA&UD) Department is the nodal department for ULBs in AP.
xa: Laws: **AP Municipalities Act, 1965** + corporations law.
AP has **123** ULBs.

n7664382c8a2.s: Which pair of laws governs municipalities and municipal corporations in Andhra Pradesh respectively?
o: AP Municipalities Act, 1994 and AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1965
AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1956 and AP Municipalities Act, 2001
AP Municipalities Act, 1965 and AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994
Andhra Pradesh Panchayats Act, 1965 and AP Municipalities Act, 1994
n7664382c8a2.x: Municipalities (and Nagar Panchayats) in AP are governed by the AP Municipalities Act, 1965, and Municipal Corporations by the AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 (as CDCA cites it; some 2026 reports name a 1955 Corporations Act). Options A and B swap or misdate the two Acts, and D names a Panchayats Act.
n7664382c8a2.tq: Distinguish the two enactments by both subject and year.
xs: **AP Municipalities Act, 1965** and **AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994** — option **(3)**.
Options 1 and 2 swap or misdate the Acts; option 4 names a **Panchayats** Act.
xa: ⚠ CDCA cites the **1994** Corporations Act; TH cites a **1955** Act.
33.33% BC reservation is applied under **both** laws.

n2ed4ca6eb5e.s: Who is the State Election Commissioner of Andhra Pradesh who notified ward-wise photo electoral rolls for 41 urban local bodies in 2026?
n2ed4ca6eb5e.x: Anil Chandra Punetha is the AP State Election Commissioner who notified ward-wise photo rolls for 41 ULBs (12 corporations and 29 municipalities/nagar panchayats). The other names are not the current SEC.
xs: AP SEC **Anil Chandra Punetha** notified ward-wise photo rolls for **41 ULBs** — option **(2)**.
These cover **12** Corporations + **29** municipalities/NPs.
xa: Corporations include **GVMC**, **Vijayawada**, **Guntur**, **Tirupati**, **Kurnool**.
Rolls due **22 Sep 2026**; qualifying date **1 Jan 2026**.

n28f94fc479c.s: In August 2026, the AP Cabinet approved which method for choosing Mayors and municipal or Nagar Panchayat chairpersons?
n28f94fc479c.x: The Cabinet approved direct election of Mayors and municipal or Nagar Panchayat chairpersons, replacing the indirect system.
xa: Under the 74th, the manner of electing the chairperson is **left to the state**.
The same meeting approved **33.33%** BC quota in ULBs.

n14e1933538b.s: In Rajasthan, the District Planning Committee is chaired by the:
o: Mayor of the largest Municipal Corporation
n14e1933538b.x: In Rajasthan the DPC is chaired by the Zila Pramukh, the head of the Zila Parishad (RPSC 2024 key). A Collector-chaired body is the Andhra Pradesh pattern, and in Kerala the Collector is only member-secretary. Neither a Mayor nor the Divisional Commissioner chairs it.
n14e1933538b.tq: Rajasthan = Zila Pramukh; AP = Collector; Kerala = District Panchayat President.
xs: In Rajasthan the DPC is chaired by the **Zila Pramukh** — option **(2)** (RPSC 2024 key).
The **Collector** chairs in **AP**; in **Kerala** he is only member-secretary.
xa: Kerala: **District Panchayat President** chairs.
DPC = **Art. 243ZD**.

n7d00e4f8086.s: The Community Participation Law was identified as a mandatory reform under which programme?
n7d00e4f8086.x: The Community Participation Law was a mandatory reform under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM).
n7d00e4f8086.tq: Match the reform with the programme under which it was made mandatory.
xs: The **Community Participation Law** was a **JNNURM** mandatory reform — option **(3)**.
The notes link the law only to **JNNURM**, not to the other schemes listed.
xa: It provides for **Area Sabhas** below Wards Committees.
Model Nagara Raj Bill: **2008**.

ndb07ed0d7d0.s: Who notifies the Scheduled Tribes for a State or Union Territory under Article 342?
o: The Union Council of Ministers by executive order
The Parliament after consultation with the Governor
The President after consultation with the Governor
The Governor after consultation with the President
ndb07ed0d7d0.x: Under Article 342 the President, after consultation with the Governor, notifies the Scheduled Tribes of a State or UT (the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950). Parliament only includes or excludes communities later by law; the Governor and the Council of Ministers do not notify the list.
ndb07ed0d7d0.tq: Ask who performs the constitutional notification function and who is consulted.
xs: Under **Article 342**, **the President after consultation with the Governor** notifies the STs of a State/UT — option **(3)** is correct.
The first list was the **Constitution (ST) Order, 1950**; later inclusion or exclusion is made only by **Parliament by law**, not by the Governor or the Council of Ministers.
xa: ST status is **religion-neutral**; SC status is limited to **Hindu/Sikh/Buddhist** persons.
The **Lokur Committee (1965)** gave the five traits for identifying STs: **primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact, backwardness**.
**705** ethnic groups are notified as STs; **Bhil** is the largest tribe and **MP** has the largest tribal population.

n9072b58785e.s: After the initial notification under Article 342, inclusion in or exclusion from the list of Scheduled Tribes can be made only by:
o: The President through a fresh notification
The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes by recommendation
n9072b58785e.x: Subsequent inclusion or exclusion of communities from the Scheduled Tribe list requires a law made by Parliament.
n9072b58785e.tq: Distinguish the original notifying authority from the authority competent to alter the list later.
xs: After the first notification, a community can be included in or excluded from the ST list only by **Parliament by law** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **President** notifies the list only once (with the Governor's consultation) under **Art. 342**; a fresh Presidential notification cannot alter it.
xa: The original list is the **Constitution (ST) Order, 1950**.
**Art. 338A** (inserted by the **89th Amendment Act, 2003**) created the **NCST**, set up in **2004** — it does not add or drop tribes.
Parliament also amends the **Fifth and Sixth Schedules** by **ordinary law**, not under **Art. 368**.

nd553ada3710.s: Scheduled Tribes have not been notified in which of the following groups of States and Union Territories?
o: Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, Puducherry and Chandigarh
Punjab, Gujarat, Haryana, Goa and Chandigarh
Delhi, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Puducherry and Chandigarh
Delhi, Rajasthan, Haryana, Puducherry and Chandigarh
nd553ada3710.x: No Scheduled Tribe has been notified in Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, Puducherry or Chandigarh.
nd553ada3710.tq: Test an exact exclusion list and trap it with neighbouring regions having tribal populations.
xs: No Scheduled Tribe has been notified in **Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, Puducherry and Chandigarh** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh** and **Rajasthan** are all **Fifth Schedule States** with Scheduled Areas, so options (2), (3) and (4) are wrong.
xa: **705** ethnic groups are notified as STs.
Largest tribal population: **MP**; largest tribe: **Bhil**.
Notification is by the **President** after consulting the Governor (**Art. 342**).

n1caec3582b9.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338A was created by which Constitutional Amendment?
n1caec3582b9.x: The 89th Amendment Act, 2003 inserted Article 338A, and the NCST was set up in 2004. The 73rd Amendment dealt with Panchayats. The 65th and 102nd Amendments are not the source of Article 338A.
n1caec3582b9.tq: 89th (2003) split off the NCST; it was set up in 2004.
xs: **Article 338A** (**NCST**) was inserted by the **89th Amendment Act, 2003** — option **(3)** is correct.
The NCST was actually set up in **2004**.
xa: NCST extra focus: **minor forest produce**, **mineral and water rights**, **rehabilitation** of displaced tribals.
**Art. 342**: President notifies STs; **Art. 244(1)**: Fifth Schedule; **Art. 244(2) and 275(1)**: Sixth Schedule.
**Art. 243M(1)** keeps Scheduled and Tribal Areas out of **Part IX** (Panchayats).

na487b3e453d.s: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for declaring an area a Scheduled Area?
o: Compactness and reasonable size of the area
na487b3e453d.x: The criteria are tribal preponderance, compactness and reasonable size, a viable administrative unit and economic backwardness; industrial development is not one.
xa: Scheduled Areas are declared by the **President**, **in consultation with the Governor**.
Purpose of the Schedules: **area-based protection** of tribal land and culture, since STs live in contiguous areas.

nca53eb183a6.s: Regulations for the peace and good government of a Scheduled Area under Paragraph 5 of the Fifth Schedule are made by the:
nca53eb183a6.x: The Governor makes these regulations after consulting the Tribes Advisory Council, and they need the President's assent.
xa: Regulations may **prohibit/restrict land transfer** by or among STs and regulate **allotment of land** and **money-lending**.
They may also **repeal Acts**; the Governor may direct that an **Act of Parliament or the State legislature** does not apply to a Scheduled Area.
⚠ "Governor is NOT authorised to direct that an Act does not apply" was the false statement (APPSC-G2 2017).
The TAC has **not more than 20 members**, about **three-fourths ST MLAs**.

n373451c1824.s: The Tribes Advisory Council shall have not more than ____ members.
n373451c1824.x: The TAC has not more than 20 members, about three-fourths of them ST members of the State Legislative Assembly.
xa: Exam angle: TAC size "**up to 20**" (**G2 2017** — the key was left blank; the Constitution says not more than 20).
TAC is mandatory in every State with **Scheduled Areas**.
Criticism: **TACs rarely meet**; Governors rarely use Fifth Schedule powers.

na2609bde105.s: The President may direct the establishment of a Tribes Advisory Council in a State which:
o: Has neither Scheduled Tribes nor Scheduled Areas
Has Scheduled Areas but no Scheduled Tribes
Has Scheduled Tribes but no Scheduled Areas
na2609bde105.x: The President may direct the establishment of a Tribes Advisory Council in a State having Scheduled Tribes but no Scheduled Areas.
na2609bde105.tq: Distinguish the mandatory case from the exceptional case requiring a Presidential direction.
xs: The President may direct a TAC in a State that **has Scheduled Tribes but no Scheduled Areas** — option **(4)** is correct.
In States **with Scheduled Areas**, the TAC is already **mandatory**.
xa: TAC: **up to 20** members, about **three-fourths** ST MLAs.
It advises only on matters **referred by the Governor**.
AP **TAC** members attended a Tribal Cultural Research and Training Mission event (**11 Aug 2026**).

n7c79af104cc.s: How may Parliament amend the Fifth and Sixth Schedules to the Constitution?
o: Only by the special procedure under Article 368
By an executive order of the President
Only through a constitutional amendment ratified by all States
n7c79af104cc.x: Parliament may amend the Fifth and Sixth Schedules by an ordinary law; such amendment is not required to follow the procedure under Article 368.
n7c79af104cc.tq: Test the distinction between an ordinary law and a formal constitutional amendment.
xs: Parliament can amend the **Fifth and Sixth Schedules** **by an ordinary law** — option **(1)** is correct.
Such amendment is **not** made under **Art. 368**.
xa: Likewise, a law under **Art. 243M(4)(b)** extending Part IX is **not an amendment under Art. 368**.
Inclusion/exclusion from the ST list is also by **Parliament by law** (**Art. 342**).

n7a028135582.s: The Governor reports to the President on the administration of Scheduled Areas:
o: Annually or whenever the President requires
Only when the State Legislature requests
n7a028135582.x: The Governor reports annually or whenever required; the Union may also give the State directions on administering Scheduled Areas.
xa: In the **Sixth Schedule**, administration is within the State's executive authority.
The Governor may direct that an Act **does not apply** or applies with modifications (**Para 5**).

ne34c3c8b197.s: The Sixth Schedule of the Constitution derives its constitutional basis primarily from which of the following combinations of provisions?
ne34c3c8b197.x: The Sixth Schedule operates in conjunction with Article 244(2), while Article 275(1) provides for grants-in-aid for the administration of Scheduled and Tribal Areas.
ne34c3c8b197.tq: Identify the exact constitutional provisions instead of choosing nearby tribal-area articles.
xs: The Sixth Schedule rests on **Articles 244(2) and 275(1)** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Art. 275(1)** provides **grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of India**.
**Art. 371A** concerns **Nagaland**, which it keeps out of the Sixth Schedule.
xa: **Art. 244(1)** is the base of the **Fifth Schedule** (Scheduled Areas).
Sixth Schedule covers tribal areas of **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**.
**10** ADCs: Assam **3**, Meghalaya **3**, Tripura **1**, Mizoram **3**.

nacffb8ce473.s: The areas listed in Parts I, II, IIA and III of the table to paragraph 20 of the Sixth Schedule are known as
nacffb8ce473.x: The areas specified in the table to paragraph 20 are constitutionally referred to as Tribal Areas.
nacffb8ce473.tq: Distinguish the exact Sixth Schedule term from the related expression Scheduled Areas.
xs: Areas in **Parts I, II, IIA and III** of the table to **para 20** are **Tribal Areas** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Scheduled Areas** is the Fifth Schedule term.
xa: ⚠ **Scheduled Areas** = Fifth = **TAC**; **Tribal Areas** = Sixth = **District/Regional Councils**.
Tribal areas are constituted as **autonomous districts**, organised by the **Governor**.
An **autonomous region** is a unit **within** an autonomous district (**APPSC-G2 2017**).

nabb2ca3b08d.s: Under the Sixth Schedule, every autonomous region within an autonomous district has a:
nabb2ca3b08d.x: The Governor may divide an autonomous district into autonomous regions, each with a Regional Council; the region lies within the district.
xa: ⚠ Key (**APPSC-G2 2017**): **autonomous region is a unit within an autonomous district**.
**Tribal Areas** are those in **Parts I, II, IIA and III** of the table to **para 20**.

n30b920f101a.s: Autonomous district councils are provided for under the Sixth Schedule in which group of states?
o: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Sikkim
Meghalaya, Sikkim, Tripura and Arunachal Pradesh
n30b920f101a.x: The Sixth Schedule provides for autonomous district councils in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
n30b920f101a.tq: Use the complete four-state list to distinguish the Sixth Schedule from other North-Eastern arrangements.
xs: ADCs exist under the Sixth Schedule in **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Nagaland** (**Art. 371A**), **Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh** and **Sikkim** are NOT under the Sixth Schedule.
xa: **10** ADCs: Assam **3**, Meghalaya **3**, Tripura **1**, Mizoram **3**.
**Ladakh**: Sixth Schedule demands (**Sep 2025**).
PESA does **not** apply in these four States.

n29ef15a8aa5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the application of laws to Sixth Schedule areas?
o: Acts of Parliament and State Legislatures apply only with the prescribed direction or modification
In Meghalaya, the direction is given by the President
In Tripura and Mizoram, the direction is given by the President
In Assam, the direction is given by the President
n29ef15a8aa5.x: In Assam the direction is given by the Governor; in Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram it is given by the President.
xa: In the **Fifth Schedule**, the **Governor** may exclude or modify any Act (**Para 5**).
ADCs get **grants-in-aid** under **Art. 275** and assess **land revenue**.

n07f9d36a167.s: The Sixth Schedule applies to the tribal areas of which States?
o: Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh
n07f9d36a167.x: The Sixth Schedule covers tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram; Nagaland has its own provisions under Article 371A.
xa: The Sixth Schedule covers only **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**.
**Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh** and **Sikkim** are also NOT under it.
⚠ Trap: "All states with ST above **40%**" is WRONG.

n1458203b7c8.s: The exclusion of Scheduled Areas and Tribal Areas from Part IX of the Constitution is provided under which Article?
n1458203b7c8.x: Article 243M excludes Scheduled Areas and Tribal Areas from the operation of Part IX relating to Panchayats.
n1458203b7c8.tq: Identify the constitutional provision directly linked with the exclusion.
xs: **Article 243M** (clause **(1)**) keeps Scheduled and Tribal Areas out of **Part IX** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Art. 275** is about **grants-in-aid**; **Art. 244** deals with the Fifth and Sixth Schedules themselves.
xa: **Art. 243M(4)(b)** lets Parliament extend Part IX with modifications — this enabled **PESA 1996**.
PESA extends **Part IX (Panchayats)** to **Fifth Schedule Areas** only.

n9e7cc0948a7.s: Article 243M(4)(b) enables Parliament to extend the provisions of Part IX to Scheduled Areas and Tribal Areas with modifications. Such a law is treated as:
o: A constitutional order issued by the President
An ordinary law not constituting an amendment under Article 368
A regulation made by the Governor under the Fifth Schedule
An amendment requiring the procedure under Article 368
n9e7cc0948a7.x: Article 243M(4)(b) permits Parliament to extend Part IX with modifications, and such legislation is not deemed to be a constitutional amendment under Article 368.
n9e7cc0948a7.tq: Distinguish an ordinary enabling law from a formal constitutional amendment.
xs: A law under **Art. 243M(4)(b)** extending Part IX with modifications is **an ordinary law, not an amendment under Article 368** — option **(2)** is correct.
**PESA 1996** was made using this enabling clause.
xa: **Art. 243M(1)** bars Part IX in **Scheduled and Tribal Areas**.
The **Fifth and Sixth Schedules** too are amended by **ordinary law**.
PESA was enacted on **24 Dec 1996**, after the **Bhuria Committee** report (**1995**).

n275dafc1e9e.s: Which of the following States is NOT among the ten Fifth Schedule States covered by PESA?
n275dafc1e9e.x: The ten PESA States are AP, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha and Rajasthan; Kerala is not one of them.
xa: PESA covers all **10** Fifth Schedule States.
**Odisha**: only **draft rules** (Apr **2026**).
Largest tribal population: **MP**.

ndeb0cfcabd8.s: The Alluri Sitharama Raju district was carved out of which erstwhile district?
ndeb0cfcabd8.x: Alluri Sitharama Raju district was carved from the erstwhile Visakhapatnam district.
ndeb0cfcabd8.tq: Test the old-district and new-district relationship directly.
xs: **Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR)** district was carved from old **Visakhapatnam** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is **tribal-majority** with **PVTGs**.
xa: ASR ITDAs: **Paderu** (tribal medical college), **Rampachodavaram** (Rampa), **Chintoor** (Godavari Koya belt).
**Tribal Medical College at Paderu** opened **2024-25** with **50** seats.
ST Lok Sabha seat: **Araku**.

nad256fa9538.s: The tribal-majority Alluri Sitharama Raju district is noted for the presence of:
nad256fa9538.x: Alluri Sitharama Raju district is tribal-majority and has Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs).
xa: ASR ITDAs: **Paderu, Rampachodavaram, Chintoor**.
**Srisailam** ITDA serves the **Chenchus** of the Nallamala.
AP has **34 ST communities** in its scheduled areas.

nc9783ebe660.s: Scheduled Tribes constitute approximately what proportion of India's population as per Census 2011?
nc9783ebe660.x: PESA covers Scheduled Tribe populations constituting approximately 8.6 percent of India's population.
nc9783ebe660.tq: Identify the precise percentage rather than relying on approximate scale comparisons.
xs: PESA covers the ST population, about **8.6 percent** of India — option **(2)** is correct.
For this population PESA makes the **Gram Sabha**, not the Panchayat, the nucleus of self-rule.
xa: **705** ethnic groups are notified as STs.
Largest tribal population: **MP**; largest tribe: **Bhil**.
STs are notified by the **President** under **Art. 342**.
nc9783ebe660.fixed: 8.6% is the national ST share (Census 2011), not the population 'covered by PESA'

nindian-polity-49-1.s: The administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes are governed by which of the following?
o: Part X, Article 244(2) and the Sixth Schedule
Part X, Article 244(1) and the Fifth Schedule
nindian-polity-49-1.x: Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes come under Part X, Article 244(1) and the Fifth Schedule. Tribal areas of the North-East come under Article 244(2) and the Sixth Schedule.
n: Scheduled Areas are governed under Part X of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
Article 244(1) governs Scheduled Areas. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Fifth Schedule governs the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Fifth Schedule relates to Scheduled Areas. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
xs: Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes are governed by **Part X, Article 244(1)** and the **Fifth Schedule** — option **(2)**.
**Article 244(2)** with **275(1)** relates to the **Sixth Schedule** — the **Tribal Areas** of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
xa: Scheduled Areas are **declared by the President** in consultation with the Governor.
Declaring a Scheduled Area does **not** make it a **Union Territory**; the State's executive power continues, subject to the Fifth Schedule.
The **Governor** reports on Scheduled Areas **directly to the President**, annually and when required.
**Art. 275(1)** provides **grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of India**.

n8bc403c7038.s: In a Scheduled Area, the Governor may direct that an Act of Parliament or of the State Legislature shall:
o: Apply only after approval of every Gram Sabha
Not apply, or apply with specified modifications
Apply only after approval of the Tribes Advisory Council
Stand repealed for that area by executive order
n8bc403c7038.x: Under the Fifth Schedule the Governor may direct that such an Act shall not apply, or shall apply with specified modifications, to a Scheduled Area.
xa: Exam angle (**APPSC-G2 2017**): "Governor is NOT authorised to direct that an Act does not apply" is the **false** statement.
The Governor's regulations may **repeal Acts**, but need the **President's assent**.
In the Sixth Schedule, laws apply as directed by the **Governor** (Assam) or **President** (Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram).

nf52afd68894.s: Under PESA, a Gram Sabha in a Scheduled Area may be constituted at the level of a:
o: Habitation such as a para, majra or tola
nf52afd68894.x: PESA recognises habitation-level Gram Sabhas, including units such as a para, majra or tola.
xa: Its meeting is presided over by an **ST member elected by the Gram Sabha**, not the Sarpanch (**CGPSC 2015**).
AP has **2,038 notified PESA Gram Sabhas** being strengthened.
**19 model GPs** covering **43 Gram Sabhas** are being developed in AP.

n6be1582c53d.s: If a State law is inconsistent with PESA, the inconsistent provision generally ceases to operate after:
o: Two years from publication in the Gazette
One year from the date of assent
n6be1582c53d.x: Under PESA, any provision of a State Panchayat law inconsistent with it ceases to operate one year from the date PESA received assent (24 December 1996), unless amended earlier. Six months, two years and five years are not the stated period.
n6be1582c53d.tq: Recall the statutory time limit and distinguish it from nearby constitutional periods.
xs: A State law inconsistent with PESA lapses **one year from the date of assent** — option **(4)** is correct.
PESA received assent on **24 Dec 1996**; six months, two years and five years are not the stated period.
xa: PESA was enacted after the **Bhuria Committee** report (**1995**).
AP followed with an amending Act in **1998** and the **AP PESA Rules 2011**.
Enabling clause: **Art. 243M(4)(b)**.

nindian-polity-49-7.s: Under Paragraph 5 of the Fifth Schedule, the Governor may make regulations for which of the following purposes?
o: Establishing Autonomous District Councils in all States
Prohibiting or restricting transfer of tribal land to non-tribals and regulating money-lending to STs
Creating new Union Territories and regulating elections to Parliament
Transferring executive power over Scheduled Areas to the President
nindian-polity-49-7.x: Under paragraph 5 of the Fifth Schedule, the Governor can make regulations to stop or limit tribal land passing to non-tribals and to control money-lending to Scheduled Tribes.
nindian-polity-49-7.tq: Recall the Governor's regulation powers under the Fifth Schedule.
n: The Governor may make regulations prohibiting the transfer of tribal land to non-tribals. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Governor may make regulations restricting the transfer of tribal land to non-tribals. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Governor may make regulations regulating money-lending to Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
xs: Under **Paragraph 5**, the Governor may make regulations **prohibiting or restricting transfer of tribal land** to non-tribals and **regulating money-lending** to STs — option **(2)**.
These are **regulations for peace and good government** of a Scheduled Area (G2 2017 key).
**Autonomous District Councils** belong to the **Sixth Schedule**, not the Fifth; and a Scheduled Area does **not** become a **Union Territory**.
xa: Regulations may also regulate the **allotment of land**.
They are made after consulting the **TAC** and need the **President's assent**.
The Governor may direct that any Act **does not apply**, or applies with modifications, to a Scheduled Area.
AP's **Land Transfer Regulation 1 of 1959** (amended by Regulation **1 of 1970**) bars land transfers to non-tribals in Scheduled Areas.

n32724517896.s: With reference to the Sixth Schedule, which one of the following is correct regarding the composition of an Autonomous District Council?
o: Twenty-eight members are elected and two are nominated by the Governor
Twenty-four members are elected and six are nominated by the Governor
All 30 members are nominated by the Governor
Twenty-six members are elected and four are nominated by the Governor
n32724517896.x: A District Council may have 30 members, of whom 26 are elected by adult franchise and four are nominated by the Governor.
n32724517896.tq: Split the total strength into elected and nominated components.
xs: An ADC has up to **30 members**: **twenty-six elected** by adult franchise and **four nominated by the Governor** — option **(4)** is correct.
Elected members serve **5 years**.
xa: There are **10** ADCs: Assam **3**, Meghalaya **3**, Tripura **1**, Mizoram **3**.
Each **autonomous region** has its own **Regional Council**.
ADCs legislate on land, forests, **shifting cultivation**, inheritance, marriage, social customs — with the **Governor's assent**.

nefddfb1e352.s: Which one of the following is NOT a subject within the legislative sphere of an Autonomous District Council under the Sixth Schedule?
nefddfb1e352.x: District Councils may legislate on inheritance, village administration and social customs, among other local tribal matters. Citizenship is not included in this field.
nefddfb1e352.tq: Find the outside subject among a cluster of genuine Sixth Schedule powers.
xs: **Citizenship of India** is not in an ADC's legislative sphere — option **(2)** is correct.
ADCs legislate on **land, forests, canal water, shifting cultivation, village administration, inheritance, marriage, social customs** — covering options (1), (3) and (4).
xa: Such laws need the **Governor's assent**.
Judicial: **village councils/courts** for suits between tribals.
Financial: assess **land revenue** and levy specified taxes; **grants-in-aid** under **Art. 275**.

n3ce70920194.s: To be eligible under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must show residence for:
n3ce70920194.x: OTFDs must prove three generations, taken as 75 years, of residence before 2005. One or two generations is too short, and 1980 and 1950 are the wrong cut-off years.
xs: **OTFDs** must show residence for **three generations (75 years) before 2005** — option **(3)** is correct.
One or two generations is too short, and **1980/1950** are the wrong cut-offs.
xa: **FRA 2006** gives individual + community rights over forest land + **ownership of MFP**.
Forest land for public utilities needs **Gram Sabha** recommendation.
NCST requisitioned FRA reports from **MoEFCC**.

nd5f6897a933.s: Under which Schedule does the Union's executive power extend to giving directions to a State on the administration of its tribal areas?
nd5f6897a933.x: Under the Fifth Schedule the Union may give directions to the State regarding Scheduled Areas; under the Sixth, administration stays within the State's executive authority.
xa: In the Fifth Schedule, the **Governor** reports to the President **annually or when required**.
Fifth: **President declares** areas; Sixth: **Governor organises** districts.
PESA applies only to the **Fifth Schedule** areas.

nindian-polity-49-21.s: The Sixth Schedule does NOT apply to which of the following States?
nindian-polity-49-21.x: Manipur is not covered by the Sixth Schedule (it has hill-area committees under Article 371-C), and neither is Nagaland. Only Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram are.
nindian-polity-49-21.tq: Recall the four Sixth Schedule States.
n: Assam is covered by the Sixth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
Meghalaya is covered by the Sixth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
Mizoram is covered by the Sixth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Sixth Schedule applies only to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Sixth Schedule does not apply to Manipur. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Sixth Schedule covers four North-Eastern States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
xs: The Sixth Schedule does **not** apply to **Manipur** — option **(2)**.
It covers **four North-Eastern States only**: **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**.
xa: **Nagaland** is also out (**Art. 371A**); so are **Arunachal Pradesh** and **Sikkim**.
Sixth Schedule bodies: **Autonomous District Councils** and **Autonomous Regional Councils**.
Application of Acts: **Assam** → Governor; **Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram** → President.
The Sixth Schedule is **not population-based** — no ST-share threshold decides coverage (APPSC-G2 2025).

nbef8d67cecb.s: Which of the following is NOT an area of special focus associated with the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
o: Regulation of inter-State trade in agricultural commodities
nbef8d67cecb.x: The Commission focuses on minor forest produce, mineral and water rights, and rehabilitation of displaced tribals. Regulation of inter-State agricultural trade is not listed as this special focus.
nbef8d67cecb.tq: Identify the unrelated function among several functions linked to tribal safeguards.
xs: **Regulation of inter-State trade in agricultural commodities** is not an NCST focus area — option **(4)** is correct.
The NCST's extra focus is **ownership of minor forest produce**, safeguarding **mineral and water rights** and **rehabilitation** of displaced tribals — options (1), (2) and (3).
xa: The NCST (**Art. 338A**) was inserted by the **89th Amendment Act, 2003** and set up in **2004**.
It used its powers to requisition **FRA** implementation reports from **MoEFCC**.
Under **PESA**, Gram Sabhas/Panchayats get **ownership** of minor forest produce.

nc5140eb51f0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Gram Sabha under PESA?
o: It can settle local disputes according to local practice.
It is the nucleus of village governance.
It can protect traditions and manage common property resources.
Higher-level Panchayats may take over its powers.
nc5140eb51f0.x: PESA seeks to prevent higher-level Panchayats from taking over the powers of Gram Sabhas.
xa: Seats in PESA panchayats: STs get at least **50%**; **all Chairperson posts** go to STs.
Inconsistent State laws lapse **one year** after assent.
At district level, States should follow the **Sixth Schedule pattern**.

nindian-polity-49-8.s: What was held by the Supreme Court in Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997)?
o: The Fifth Schedule did not apply to tribal land used for mining.
All tribal land in Scheduled Areas could be freely transferred to private parties for mining.
Transfer or lease of tribal land in Scheduled Areas to private parties for mining was null, void and inoperative.
Only money-lending regulations in Scheduled Areas were unconstitutional.
nindian-polity-49-8.x: In Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997), the Supreme Court held that transferring or leasing tribal land in Scheduled Areas to private companies for mining is void under the Fifth Schedule.
n: Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh was decided in 1997. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh is a landmark ruling. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]

The Supreme Court held in Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh that the transfer of tribal land in Scheduled Areas to private parties for mining operations is null, void, and inoperative under the Fifth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
xs: In **Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997)**, transfer or lease of tribal land in Scheduled Areas to **private parties** for **mining** was held **null, void and inoperative** — option **(3)**.
The **Supreme Court** held such leasing violates the **Fifth Schedule** and the AP Land Transfer Regulation.
The State itself was treated as a "**person**" under the Regulation.
xa: ⚠ **Niyamgiri / Orissa Mining Corporation case** (SC, **2013**): **Gram Sabhas** decided on bauxite mining.
The Niyamgiri Gram Sabhas rejected the **Vedanta** project.
**FRA 2006**: forest land for public utilities only on **Gram Sabha** recommendation.
**CNT Act 1908** was breached by the **Bharatmala** highway without PESA consent.

nindian-society-42-6.s: Which committee formulated the classic five criteria for scheduling Scheduled Tribes?
nindian-society-42-6.x: The Lokur Committee (1965) set the five classic tests for listing a group as a Scheduled Tribe: primitive traits, distinct culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact and backwardness.
n: The Lokur Committee formulated five criteria for scheduling Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Lokur Committee concerned Scheduled Tribes (STs). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xs: The **Lokur Committee** (**1965**) formulated the five criteria for scheduling STs — option **(2)**.
The criteria: **primitive traits**, **distinct culture**, **geographical isolation**, **shyness of contact**, **backwardness**.
**Xaxa** reviewed tribal development and **Bhuria** laid the basis for PESA.
xa: **Kalelkar Commission**: tribes may belong to **any religion**.
⚠ ST status is **religion-neutral**; SC status = Hindu/Sikh/Buddhist only.
STs are notified by the **President** under **Art. 342** → **Constitution (ST) Order, 1950**; later changes only by **Parliament by law**.
**705** ethnic groups notified as STs; largest tribe **Bhil**; largest tribal population **MP**.

nindian-society-11-21.s: Who chaired the Xaxa Committee, established for reviewing tribal development?
nindian-society-11-21.x: Virginius Xaxa chaired the 2013 committee reviewing tribal development. Dhebar (1960) and Bhuria (1995) were earlier tribal bodies.
nindian-society-11-21.tq: Match each tribal committee to its chair.
xs: **Virginius Xaxa** chaired the Xaxa Committee on **tribal development** — option **(1)**.
**U. N. Dhebar** chaired the **1960** commission; **Dilip Singh Bhuria** the **1995** committee.
xa: The Xaxa Committee was set up by the **Prime Minister's Office** (**2013**).
It recommended **preventing tribal land alienation** and **strictly enforcing** the **FRA, 2006**.
**Lokur (1965)** set the five ST criteria.
Bhuria laid the basis of **PESA, 1996**.

n27dd3a42c99.s: In a PESA area, a Gram Sabha meeting is presided over by:
o: An ST member elected by the Gram Sabha
n27dd3a42c99.x: The presiding officer is an ST member elected by the Gram Sabha; the Sarpanch does not automatically preside.
xa: The detail is fixed by each State's PESA rules — AP: **AP PESA Rules 2011**.
AP framework: **PESA Act 1996** → AP amending Act **1998** → **AP PESA Rules 2011**.
Gram Sabha level: **para, majra, tola**.

na64e9e12dbf.s: Under PESA, the power of the Gram Sabha or Panchayat over tribal land is to:
o: Transfer tribal land to private companies
Prevent alienation and restore unlawfully alienated land
na64e9e12dbf.x: PESA empowers these bodies to prevent alienation of tribal land and restore unlawfully alienated land.
xa: **Samatha v. State of AP** (SC, **1997**): Scheduled Area land cannot be leased to **non-tribals or private companies**.
**AP Land Transfer Regulation 1 of 1959** bars transfers between tribals and non-tribals.
They also control **money-lending to STs**.

n390f9ea6b30.s: A Ministry of Panchayati Raj assessment found that more than what proportion of elected representatives in PESA panchayats could not explain what a Gram Sabha is?
n390f9ea6b30.x: More than 40 per cent of elected representatives in PESA panchayats could not explain what a Gram Sabha is.
n390f9ea6b30.tq: Select the stated threshold rather than treating it as an exact percentage.
xs: Over **40 per cent** of elected representatives in PESA panchayats could not explain a Gram Sabha — option **(3)** is correct.
This came from an **MoPR** assessment of **Dec 2025**.
xa: **30 years of PESA**: **PESA Mahotsav** in **Visakhapatnam**; MoPR set up a **PESA Cell** and launched the **PESA-GPDP portal**.
