MoPR trained **1 lakh+** representatives.
⚠ The same "**40%**" figure is the G2 2025 Sixth Schedule trap (coverage is not population-based).

n2b764e03042.s: The allegation by Tana Bhagats concerning a Bharatmala highway primarily relates to which implementation problem?
o: Failure to obtain PESA consent of the Gram Sabha
Non-payment of forest rights titles by the Union Government
Failure to conduct elections to the State Legislative Assembly
Failure to constitute a Sixth Schedule autonomous district council
n2b764e03042.x: Tana Bhagats in Jharkhand stated that PESA consent was not taken for the Bharatmala highway. The issue was also described as breaching the CNT Act, 1908.
n2b764e03042.tq: Identify the governance failure from the facts of the situation.
xs: The **Tana Bhagats** (Oraon, Jharkhand) said **PESA consent** of the Gram Sabha was not obtained for the **Bharatmala** highway — option **(1)** is correct.
The highway was also said to breach the **CNT Act 1908**.
xa: Suggested fix: merge **PESA + FRA 2006 + LARR 2013** consent into one binding Gram Sabha clearance.
Criticism: in land acquisition, **Gram Sabha consent** is often ignored.
Over **40%** of PESA representatives could not explain a Gram Sabha (**MoPR, Dec 2025**).

ne4026b7a0e7.s: In the Niyamgiri (Orissa Mining Corporation) case, 2013, Gram Sabhas decided whether bauxite mining affected their:
ne4026b7a0e7.x: The Gram Sabhas were to decide whether the mining affected their religious and forest rights; they rejected the Vedanta project.
xa: **Samatha v. State of AP** (SC, **1997**): Scheduled Area land cannot be leased to **non-tribals or private companies**.
**FRA 2006** gives individual + community rights over forest land.
Criticism: "**consultation is not consent**".

n3fc37886e09.s: Diversion of forest land for public utilities under the Forest Rights Act, 2006 requires recommendation of which body?
n3fc37886e09.x: Forest land may be diverted for public utilities only on the recommendation of the Gram Sabha.
n3fc37886e09.tq: Identify the institution legally associated with the specific approval function.
xs: Under **FRA 2006**, forest land for public utilities is diverted only on the **Gram Sabha**'s recommendation — option **(4)** is correct.
The **TAC** advises the Governor only; the State Assembly and District Mineral Foundation have no such role.
xa: FRA recognises individual + community rights over forest land + **ownership of MFP**.
**OTFD**: **3 generations (75 years)** before **2005**.
**Niyamgiri** (**2013**): **Gram Sabhas** decided on bauxite mining.

n0a4fd84eb03.s: A Tribal Medical College with 50 seats opened at Paderu during:
n0a4fd84eb03.x: The Tribal Medical College at Paderu opened in 2024–25 with 50 seats.
n0a4fd84eb03.tq: Separate the opening year from the current analysis year and the seat count.
xs: The **Tribal Medical College at Paderu** opened in **2024-25** with **50** seats — option **(2)** is correct.
**Paderu** is the ITDA in **ASR** district noted for this tribal medical college.
xa: **Paderu** ITDA is in **ASR** district.
Multi-specialty hospitals sanctioned at **Seethampeta, Parvathipuram, Rampachodavaram, Buttaigudem, Dornala** (**Rs 482 cr**).
ASR was carved from old **Visakhapatnam**.

n1e8b353ee6e.s: Under PESA, the nucleus of tribal self-rule in Scheduled Areas is the:
n1e8b353ee6e.x: PESA places the Gram Sabha at the centre of self-rule; autonomous district councils belong to the Sixth Schedule.
xa: PESA covers the ST population (**8.6%** of India).
Gram Sabha level: **para, majra, tola**.
Objective: an administrative framework consistent with **traditional practice**.

n9f4e5966cb9.s: Which of the following is correct about the implementation of PESA?
o: Provisions on minor minerals and minor forest produce are among the least implemented
Gram Sabha consent is always obtained before land acquisition in PESA areas
Provisions on minor forest produce are the most fully implemented
Consultation is accepted as fully protecting tribal decision-making
n9f4e5966cb9.x: Minor minerals and minor forest produce provisions are among the least implemented; Gram Sabha consent has reportedly been ignored in some land acquisitions.
xa: Over **40%** of PESA representatives could not explain a Gram Sabha.
**TACs rarely meet**; Governors rarely use Fifth Schedule powers.

nindian-society-40-4.s: Under PESA, 1996, Gram Sabhas in Schedule V areas are given authority over:
o: Natural resources, minor forest produce, dispute resolution and project approvals
nindian-society-40-4.x: PESA gives Gram Sabhas authority over natural resources, minor forest produce, dispute resolution and project approvals.
n: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act was passed in 1996. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
PESA gives Gram Sabhas authority over natural resources in Schedule V areas. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
PESA gives Gram Sabhas authority over minor forest produce in Schedule V areas. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
PESA gives Gram Sabhas authority over dispute resolution in Schedule V areas. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
PESA gives Gram Sabhas authority over project approvals in Schedule V areas. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
xa: Gram Sabhas get **ownership** of minor forest produce and must be **consulted** before land acquisition (consultation, not consent).
They also control **money-lending to STs**, intoxicants and village markets.
The Gram Sabha works at habitation level — **para, majra, tola**.
⚠ Its presiding officer is an **ST member elected by the Gram Sabha**, not the Sarpanch (CGPSC 2015).

nd73bb269040.s: Under PESA, Scheduled Tribes must get at least what share of Panchayat seats in Scheduled Areas?
nd73bb269040.x: Seats are reserved in proportion to population, with STs getting at least 50%; all Chairperson posts at every level go to STs.
xa: Higher-level panchayats **must not usurp** Gram Sabha powers.
At district level, States should follow the **Sixth Schedule pattern**.
State laws inconsistent with PESA lapse **one year** after assent.

n8f951b10cc6.s: In Scheduled Areas, the Zila Panchayat may perform which of the following functions?
o: Planning for minor water bodies only
Planning for minor water bodies, control of social-sector institutions and control of Tribal Sub-Plans
n8f951b10cc6.x: The Zila Panchayat in Scheduled Areas may do all three, along with other functions the State confers.
xa: At district level, States should follow the **Sixth Schedule pattern** for Zila Panchayat arrangements.
Gram Sabhas/Panchayats also manage **village markets** and local plans.
**All Chairperson posts** at every level go to STs.

n2dfdfd5f302.s: Which Act recognises individual and community rights over forest land and ownership rights over minor forest produce?
n2dfdfd5f302.x: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 recognises individual and community forest rights and ownership of minor forest produce.
xa: Forest land for public utilities only on **Gram Sabha** recommendation.
**OTFD** eligibility: **3 generations (75 years)** of residence before **2005**.
AP FRA (2024-25): **2,26,651** individual titles and **1,822** community titles distributed.

n2bd34f4ee9f.s: The Scheduled Areas of Andhra Pradesh are primarily located in the agency tracts of which geographical region?
n2bd34f4ee9f.x: The Scheduled Areas of Andhra Pradesh lie in the Eastern Ghats agency tracts.
n2bd34f4ee9f.tq: Use the geographical-location clue to distinguish the agency tracts.
xs: AP's Scheduled Areas lie in the **Eastern Ghats** agency tracts — option **(4)** is correct.
They span erstwhile **Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, East and West Godavari** districts.
xa: Coverage: **3,512 villages** in **Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalli, Eluru**.
**12.9 lakh** STs live in AP's scheduled areas; **34 ST communities**.
**7 ITDAs** cover **76 mandals**.

ne3eb1d6408c.s: Srisailam ITDA is primarily associated with:
ne3eb1d6408c.x: Srisailam ITDA is associated with the Chenchus of the Nallamala region.
ne3eb1d6408c.tq: Use the tribe–habitat association to distinguish the ITDAs.
xs: **Srisailam** ITDA serves the **Chenchus of the Nallamala** — option **(4)** is correct.
Its **Dornala** hospital unit is in **Prakasam**.
xa: Dornala is one of the multi-specialty hospital sites (**Rs 482 cr**).
**Chintoor**: Godavari **Koya** belt.
**Seethampeta, Parvathipuram**: Srikakulam agency / Parvathipuram Manyam.

n484bdb58501.s: The Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Area Land Transfer Regulation, which prohibits land transfers between tribals and non-tribals and among non-tribals in Scheduled Areas, is:
o: Regulation 1 of 1959, amended by Regulation 1 of 1970
Regulation 2 of 1970, amended by Regulation 1 of 1996
Regulation 1 of 2011, under the AP PESA Rules
n484bdb58501.x: The AP Scheduled Area Land Transfer Regulation is Regulation 1 of 1959, amended by Regulation 1 of 1970. It bars transfers between tribals and non-tribals and also among non-tribals. 1996 is the PESA year and 2011 is the AP PESA Rules year; neither is the land transfer regulation.
xs: The AP Scheduled Area Land Transfer Regulation is **Regulation 1 of 1959, amended by Regulation 1 of 1970** — option **(1)** is correct.
It bars transfers **between tribals and non-tribals and among non-tribals**.
**1996** is the PESA year and **2011** the AP PESA Rules year, so options (2)–(4) are wrong.
xa: **Samatha** (SC, **1997**) held leasing to non-tribals violates the **Fifth Schedule** + **LTR**.
Draft amendments are being prepared to curb **non-tribal infiltration**.

n4203518991f.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the legislative and regulatory framework for PESA in Andhra Pradesh?
o: PESA Act, 1996 → AP amending Act, 1998 → AP PESA Rules, 2011
AP amending Act, 1996 → PESA Act, 1998 → AP PESA Rules, 2001
PESA Act, 1998 → AP amending Act, 2011 → Rules, 2014
PESA Act, 1996 → AP PESA Rules, 1998 → amending Act, 2011
n4203518991f.x: The sequence is the PESA Act of 1996, the Andhra Pradesh amending Act of 1998, and the AP PESA Rules of 2011.
n4203518991f.tq: Arrange the legal instruments by year and distinguish the central Act from the State measures.
xs: The sequence is **PESA Act, 1996 → AP amending Act, 1998 → AP PESA Rules, 2011** — option **(1)** is correct.
The other options jumble these years; **1998** is the AP Act and **2011** the Rules.
xa: PESA was enacted on **24 Dec 1996**.
AP has **2,038 notified PESA Gram Sabhas** being strengthened.
**19 model GPs** covering **43 Gram Sabhas** are being developed.

n7b0c4798756.s: In which year were the Andhra Pradesh PESA Rules issued?
n7b0c4798756.x: The AP PESA Rules came in 2011; AP's amending Act dates to 1998.
xa: AP has **2,038 notified PESA Gram Sabhas** being strengthened.
**PESA Mahotsav** (30th anniversary) was held in **Visakhapatnam**.

n0ef5f94792d.s: The 30th anniversary of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996, was marked by which event hosted in Andhra Pradesh?
n0ef5f94792d.x: The 30th anniversary of PESA was marked by the PESA Mahotsav hosted in Visakhapatnam.
n0ef5f94792d.tq: Use the event-location association to distinguish closely related tribal-governance programmes.
xs: PESA's **30th** anniversary was marked by the **PESA Mahotsav in Visakhapatnam** (**Dec 2025**) — option **(1)** is correct.
It was part of **MoPR**'s **30 years of PESA** observance (**2025-26**).
xa: MoPR set up a **PESA Cell**, trained **1 lakh+** representatives and launched the **PESA-GPDP portal**.
AP is strengthening **2,038** PESA Gram Sabhas.
PESA was enacted on **24 Dec 1996**.

nb7a667bd10a.s: Which of the following is a Scheduled Tribe-reserved Lok Sabha constituency in Andhra Pradesh?
nb7a667bd10a.x: Araku is an ST Lok Sabha seat; AP is one of the ten Fifth Schedule States, with Scheduled Areas in the old Agency tracts.
xa: PESA governs panchayats in AP's **agency areas**.
**Rampachodavaram**: a **PESA Committee** approves middlemen for **annatto seeds** (**17 Apr 2026**).

n66bb41cfb0a.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Scheduled Tribe status from Scheduled Caste status?
o: ST status is limited to Hindus; SC status is religion-neutral
ST status is religion-neutral; SC status is limited to Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists
Both statuses are limited to Hindus
n66bb41cfb0a.x: ST status is religion-neutral, while SC status is restricted to Hindu, Sikh or Buddhist communities under the constitutional orders.
xa: STs are notified by the **President** (in consultation with the Governor) under **Art. 342** — **Constitution (ST) Order, 1950**.
Identification traits came from the **Lokur Committee, 1965**.
⚠ Trap: ST = **any religion**; SC = **Hindu/Sikh/Buddhist** only.

n1ab49ac2dd3.s: Which one of the following is NOT an objective associated with the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996?
o: Preventing higher-level Panchayats from taking over the powers of Gram Sabhas
Providing a framework consistent with traditional tribal practices
Creating autonomous regions with legislative powers
n1ab49ac2dd3.x: Creation of autonomous regions is associated with the Sixth Schedule, not an objective of PESA. PESA focuses on extending Panchayati Raj with modifications and protecting tribal self-governance.
n1ab49ac2dd3.tq: Find the objective belonging to the neighbouring constitutional arrangement.
xs: **Creating autonomous regions with legislative powers** is not a PESA objective — it belongs to the **Sixth Schedule** — option **(4)** is correct (**UPSC 2013**).
PESA objectives include stopping **higher-tier panchayats** from taking over lower-tier powers, safeguarding **customs and traditions**, and a framework consistent with **traditional practice**.
xa: Other objectives: **self-rule** for tribals; Gram Sabha as the **nucleus** of village governance.
PESA extends **Part IX** to **Fifth Schedule** areas with modifications.
PESA does **not** apply to Sixth Schedule areas.

nf77a458e3bb.s: Which of the following States is NOT among the ten Fifth Schedule States covered by PESA?
nf77a458e3bb.x: Tamil Nadu is not among the ten Fifth Schedule States covered by PESA and is a State without Scheduled Areas. The listed covered States include Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Rajasthan.
nf77a458e3bb.tq: Find the State outside the stated Fifth Schedule coverage list.
xs: **Tamil Nadu** is not a Fifth Schedule/PESA State — it has **no Scheduled Areas** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Rajasthan, Maharashtra** and **Andhra Pradesh** are among the **10** Fifth Schedule States.
xa: ⚠ Key (**RPSC 2016**): PESA not covered — **Assam-Meghalaya-Tamil Nadu**.
The Sixth Schedule States (**Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**) are also outside PESA.
**Odisha** has only **draft rules** (Apr **2026**).

n1f68508ae54.s: On which date did Andhra Pradesh introduce Panchayati Raj?
n1f68508ae54.x: AP introduced Panchayati Raj on 1 November 1959 following the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee; Rajasthan was first and AP second.
xa: ⚠ Trap (**APPSC 2019**): **1961, 1965 and 1960** are offered as distractors.
First AP laws: **AP Panchayat Samithis and Zilla Parishads Act, 1959** and **AP Gram Panchayats Act, 1964**.
The first AP polls triggered **village and caste clashes**.

n9698a2082f1.s: Panchayati Raj was first inaugurated in India by Jawaharlal Nehru on:
n9698a2082f1.x: Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj on 2 October 1959 in Nagaur district, Rajasthan. Andhra Pradesh came second, on 1 November 1959. Years such as 1960, 1961 and 1965 are the usual distractors (APPSC 2019), and Jaipur was not the venue.
n9698a2082f1.tq: Nagaur, 2 Oct 1959 first; AP second, 1 Nov 1959.
xs: **Jawaharlal Nehru** inaugurated Panchayati Raj on **2 October 1959** in **Nagaur** district, Rajasthan — option **(1)** is correct.
**1 November 1959** is when **AP** (the second State) introduced it.
⚠ **1960, 1961** and **1965** are the usual distractors (**APPSC 2019**); Jaipur was not the venue.
xa: Basis: **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee** (**1957**); report accepted by NDC in **January 1958**.
Its scheme: **3 tiers** linked by indirect election.

n5d34a45e59d.s: Under the AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, the minimum age for contesting a Gram Panchayat election is:
n5d34a45e59d.x: The minimum contesting age is 21; ward members and the Sarpanch are directly elected for five years.
xa: **Art. 243C** leaves the village chairperson's election mode to the **State legislature**.
The **Panchayat Secretary** convenes GP meetings and implements resolutions.

nbd8ad361e10.s: The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 was enacted on 21 April 1994 mainly to:
o: Introduce Mandal Praja Parishads for the first time
Give effect to the 73rd Constitutional Amendment
Give effect to the 74th Constitutional Amendment
Extend Panchayats to Scheduled Areas under PESA
nbd8ad361e10.x: The AP Panchayat Raj Act (Act No. 13 of 1994) was enacted on 21 April 1994 to give effect to the 73rd Amendment. Mandal Praja Parishads came earlier, in 1986. The 74th Amendment concerns municipalities, and AP's PESA amending Act came in 1998.
nbd8ad361e10.tq: AP PR Act 1994 (Act 13) = 73rd Amendment; 278 sections, 8 Parts.
xs: **Act No. 13 of 1994** was enacted on **21 April 1994** to **give effect to the 73rd Amendment** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Mandal Praja Parishads** came earlier, in **1986**; AP's PESA amending Act came in **1998**.
xa: The Act has **278 sections in 8 Parts**.
Part VI (**Finance Commission**) gives effect to **Art. 243I**.
MPTC/ZPTC rolls are prepared under the **AP PR Act 1994**.

n18fcb00afd1.s: After bifurcation, the State Election Commission for the residuary State of Andhra Pradesh was constituted by the Governor on:
n18fcb00afd1.x: After bifurcation, the Governor constituted the State Election Commission for the residuary State of AP on 30 January 2016 (APPSC-GS 2022 key). 2 June 2014 is the bifurcation date, 1 November 2014 is not linked to the SEC, and 24 April 1994 is close to the AP Panchayat Raj Act (21 April 1994) and the 73rd Amendment's anniversary, not the SEC.
xs: The Governor constituted AP's SEC on **30 January 2016** (**APPSC-GS 2022** key) — option **(3)** is correct.
It was set up post-bifurcation for the **residuary state**.
xa: Present Commissioner: **Anil Chandra Punetha** (appointed Apr **2026**).
**21 April 1994** is the **AP Panchayat Raj Act**'s date, not the SEC's.

nf7aff89d972.s: The e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj mainly aims to:
o: Digitise Panchayat planning, budgeting and service delivery
nf7aff89d972.x: e-Panchayat digitises Panchayat planning, budgeting and service delivery through the e-Gram Swaraj portal.
xa: **Mee Seva**: single-window counter for citizen services (since **2011**).
AP's digitised bill processing cut payment time from **20-25** days to about a week.

ne2ff5affd0c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the recent reorganisation of Panchayati Raj institutions in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The terms of the Mandal Praja Parishads end on 23 September 2026
The erstwhile 13 Zilla Praja Parishads have been reorganised into 26
The terms of the Zilla Praja Parishads end on 24 September 2026
The number of Zilla Praja Parishads now stands at 28
ne2ff5affd0c.x: The former 13 Zilla Praja Parishads have been reorganised into 28, not 26.
xa: These are AP's **second ordinary MPTC/ZPTC** elections.
Rolls are prepared under the **AP PR Act 1994**.
**16th FC** grants require **duly constituted** local bodies.

n6facba042ec.s: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee envisaged which body as the executive body of Panchayati Raj?
n6facba042ec.x: The Panchayat Samiti was to be executive and the Zilla Parishad advisory, with the Collector as its Chairman; the two-tier model was Ashok Mehta's.
xa: Balwant Rai Mehta (**1957**) proposed **3 tiers linked by indirect election**.
⚠ **Balwant Rai Mehta** = 3 tiers; **Ashok Mehta** = 2 tiers.
**Thungon (1988)** made the **ZP the pivot of planning**.

nc9f0b386d80.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Thungon Committee recommendations?
o: A State Finance Commission in each State
Constitutional status for Panchayati Raj Institutions
Zilla Parishad as the pivot of planning
A maximum one-year period for supersession of Panchayats
nc9f0b386d80.x: The Thungon Committee recommended a maximum supersession period of six months, not one year.
xa: **L.M. Singhvi (1986)** also urged **constitutional recognition** and Gram Sabha as **direct democracy**.
Today **Art. 243I** has the Governor constitute an **SFC every five years**.
**Balwant Rai Mehta (1957)**: Collector as ZP chairman.

n30add1c76a5.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the Mandal Parishad President is elected:
o: Indirectly from among the MPTC members
Directly by all voters of the mandal
Indirectly from among the ZPTC members
n30add1c76a5.x: MPTC members are directly elected, and the Mandal Parishad President is elected indirectly from among them.
xa: **Art. 243C**: intermediate and district chairpersons are elected **indirectly**.
Every tier: **5 years** term; minimum age **21**.
⚠ AP's intermediate tier is the **Mandal Parishad**, not a Panchayat Samiti.

nb5b703fa656.s: Which of the following is classified as an obligatory function of a Gram Panchayat?
nb5b703fa656.x: Maintaining burial grounds is an obligatory or essential function of a Gram Panchayat. Libraries, mother-child welfare homes and promotion of modern agricultural practices are discretionary functions.
nb5b703fa656.tq: Separate essential civic duties from discretionary developmental activities.
xs: **Maintaining burial grounds** is an obligatory (essential) function — option **(3)** is correct (**APPSC 2018**).
**Libraries and reading rooms**, **mother-child welfare homes** and **modern agricultural practices** are **discretionary** functions.
xa: Obligatory functions are compulsory under the Act: **sanitation, drinking water, drains, street lighting, village roads**.
Discretionary functions **depend on funds**; also **tree planting** and **markets**.

n8d5a1c3bf01.s: In Andhra Pradesh, who in a Gram Panchayat has been appointed by the Governor as the Marriage Officer?
n8d5a1c3bf01.x: The Panchayat Secretary of the Gram Panchayat is the Marriage Officer appointed by the Governor (APPSC-GS 2018). The Sarpanch is the elected political head. The Mandal Parishad President heads the intermediate tier, and ward members are elected representatives; none of them holds this office.
n8d5a1c3bf01.tq: Convenes / implements / Marriage Officer = Secretary, not Sarpanch.
xs: The **Panchayat Secretary** is appointed by the Governor as **Marriage Officer** — option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC-GS 2018**).
The **Sarpanch** is the elected political head; the **Mandal Parishad President** heads the intermediate tier.
xa: The Secretary also **convenes** GP meetings and **implements** its resolutions (**APPSC-GS 2019**).
Exam angle: these answers are the **Secretary**, not the Sarpanch.

n002386ca25a.s: Who implements the resolutions of a Gram Panchayat and its committees in Andhra Pradesh?
n002386ca25a.x: The Panchayat Secretary, the executive functionary of the GP, implements its resolutions (APPSC-GS 2019). The Sarpanch presides as political head but is not the implementer. The MPDO works at mandal level and the Collector at district level.
xs: The **Panchayat Secretary** implements the resolutions of the GP and its committees — option **(3)** is correct (**APPSC-GS 2019**).
The **Sarpanch** is only the **political head**; the Collector and MPDO are not GP functionaries.
xa: The Secretary is the **executive functionary** appointed to run GP administration.
The Secretary is the Governor-appointed **Marriage Officer** (**APPSC-GS 2018**).

nb06609d7786.s: Ward Secretariats and the Volunteer system in Andhra Pradesh function as service-delivery arms under the:
nb06609d7786.x: Ward Secretariats and the Volunteer system operate under the Municipal Administration Department as service-delivery mechanisms.
nb06609d7786.tq: Use the department-function relationship to reject neighbouring administrative departments.
xs: **Ward Secretariats + Volunteer system** are service-delivery arms under the **Municipal Administration department** — option **(2)** is correct.
Their **urban role** is delivering services in **ULBs**, which fall under Municipal Administration.
xa: The Village/Ward Secretariat system was launched on **2 October 2019**.
**2024-25** target: quality, accountable urban services "through **Ward Secretariat and Volunteer Systems**" across all **ULBs**.
**Mee Seva**: single-window counter for citizen services (since **2011**).

nfda9e403981.s: The 14th and 15th Finance Commission grants to local bodies gave priority to:
nfda9e403981.x: The 14th and 15th Finance Commission grants to local bodies prioritised drinking water and sanitation.
xa: **16th Finance Commission (2026-31)**: AP Rural Local Bodies get **Rs 16,627 crore** (AP Budget **2026-27**).
Its guidelines make a **duly constituted** local body a condition for grants.
The State-level counterpart is the **SFC**, every **five years**.

n1a2125bb099.s: The main own-source revenue of a Gram Panchayat is:
n1a2125bb099.x: Property (house) tax is the main own-source revenue of a Gram Panchayat. Finance Commission grants and a share of GST are transfers from above, not own revenue. Stamp duty is a State tax.
n1a2125bb099.tq: Own-source revenue = house/property tax; grants are not own revenue.
xs: The main GP own-source revenue is **property (house) tax** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Finance Commission** grants and a share of GST are transfers from above, not own revenue.
xa: **Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program**: GPs with own-source revenue ≥ **Rs 50 lakh**.
**16th FC**: AP Rural Local Bodies get **Rs 16,627 crore**.
⚠ The **3Fs** (Funds, Functions, Functionaries) are incompletely devolved, leaving PRIs as implementing agencies.

n6c4441b2ea6.s: Under Article 243C, the mode of election of the chairperson at the village level is left to the:
n6c4441b2ea6.x: Article 243C leaves the mode of election of the village-level chairperson to the State Legislature. Chairpersons at the intermediate and district levels are elected indirectly.
n6c4441b2ea6.tq: Identify which constitutional authority is empowered to determine the election method.
xs: Under **Art. 243C**, the mode of electing the village-level chairperson is left to the **State Legislature** — option **(2)** is correct.
Intermediate and district chairpersons are elected **indirectly** (**73rd Amendment**).
xa: In AP the **Sarpanch** is **directly elected**.
**Mandal Parishad President** is elected indirectly from **MPTCs**; **ZP Chairperson** from **ZPTCs**.
Minimum age to contest: **21 years** (**Art. 243F**).

n90f54c5eb04.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the State Finance Commission?
o: It is constituted every five years
It reviews the finances of Panchayats and Municipalities
It recommends the sharing of taxes, duties, tolls, fees and grants
It is constituted by the State Election Commission
n90f54c5eb04.x: The State Finance Commission is constituted by the Governor.
xa: Part VI of the **1994 Act** gives effect to **Art. 243I**.
**Thungon (1988)** recommended an **SFC in each state**.
**16th FC (2026-31)**: AP Rural Local Bodies get **Rs 16,627 crore**.

n59f43e24b9c.s: Under the Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program, a Gram Panchayat must have own-source revenue of at least:
n59f43e24b9c.x: The threshold is Rs 50 lakh for a Gram Panchayat and Rs 1 crore for a Block Panchayat, with three years' tenure left and written Gram Sabha consent.
xa: The programme is run by **MoPR** under **RGSA**.
It is a challenge for **revenue-generating projects**.
⚠ Criticism: incomplete devolution of **3Fs** — Funds, Functions, Functionaries.

n48c6102a560.s: The State Election Commissioner can be removed only in the manner and on the grounds applicable to a:
o: Member of a State Public Service Commission
n48c6102a560.x: Removal follows the procedure for a High Court judge; the Governor cannot remove the Commissioner at will.
xa: ⚠ Appointed by the **Governor**, removed like a **HC judge**.
**Art. 243K** (panchayats) + **243ZA** (municipalities).

na7463df7037.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the State Election Commission?
o: Controlling electoral rolls for Panchayat elections
Directing rearrangement and republication of Gram Panchayat electoral rolls
na7463df7037.x: The SEC controls Panchayat electoral rolls and conducts municipal elections, but it does not conduct cooperative elections.
xa: It has **superintendence, direction and control** of all local body elections.
AP SEC ordered photo rolls for **MPTC/ZPTC** polls (**8 Sep 2026**).

n2cbe0904791.s: In local bodies, seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes are reserved:
o: At exactly one-third of total seats
In proportion to their population, allotted by rotation
n2cbe0904791.x: SC/ST seats are reserved in proportion to population and allotted by rotation; the one-third floor applies to women.
xa: **AP Cabinet (18 Aug 2026)**: **34%** reservation for **BCs** in rural local bodies.
Urban: **33.33%** BC quota under the Municipalities and Corporations Acts.

n1b472c4f98a.s: The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet approved what reservation for Backward Classes in rural local bodies on 18 August 2026?
n1b472c4f98a.x: The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet approved 34 percent reservation for Backward Classes in rural local bodies on 18 August 2026.
n1b472c4f98a.tq: Test a current numerical provision against nearby reservation figures.
xs: On **18 Aug 2026** the AP Cabinet approved **34 percent** reservation for **BCs** in rural local bodies — option **(4)** is correct.
**33.33 percent** is the BC quota in **urban** local bodies.
xa: Polls were expedited to secure **central funds**.
The same Cabinet approved **direct election** of Mayors and Municipal Chairpersons.
SC/ST quotas stay **unchanged**; women get not less than **one-third**.

n9c7bdfd1a5c.s: The Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965 primarily governs which of the following?
n9c7bdfd1a5c.x: The Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965 governs Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats.
n9c7bdfd1a5c.tq: Match the statute with the exact category of local bodies governed by it.
xs: The **AP Municipalities Act, 1965** governs **Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Municipal Corporations** come under the **AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994**; GPs and Zilla/Mandal Parishads under the **AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994**.
xa: The 1965 Act came into effect on **2 April 1965** (**APPSC-GS 2021**).
⚠ Sources differ on the Corporations Act year: **1994** vs **1955**.
The **33.33%** BC quota in ULBs is implemented under the 1965 Act and the Corporations Act.

na48e9c318b5.s: The correct order of municipal grades under the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act is:
o: Special, Grade I, Selection, Grade II, Grade III
Grade I, Grade II, Grade III, Selection, Special
Special, Selection, Grade I, Grade II, Grade III
Selection, Special, Grade II, Grade I, Grade III
na48e9c318b5.x: The grades are Special, Selection, Grade I, Grade II and Grade III.
xa: A **Nagar Panchayat** is an area in transition from rural to urban (**Art. 243Q**).
UDAs are **special-purpose (functional) agencies**.
The **AP Municipalities Act, 1965** governs Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats.

n9a483a70f3f.s: Under Article 243Q, which factors does the Governor take into account when classifying areas as municipal bodies?
o: Population, density and revenue for local administration only
Revenue and percentage of non-agricultural employment only
Population, density, revenue for local administration and percentage of non-agricultural employment
n9a483a70f3f.x: All four factors (population, density, revenue for local administration and non-agricultural employment) are considered.
xa: A **Nagar Panchayat** is for an area in transition from rural to urban.
Municipal grades: **Special, Selection, Grade I, II, III** (by annual income).
**74th Amendment**: Part IX-A, **Art. 243P-243ZG**, **18** Twelfth Schedule items.

nd1ec109f1b9.s: The Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965 came into force on:
nd1ec109f1b9.x: The Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965 has been in force from 2 April 1965.
nd1ec109f1b9.tq: Directly test the precise commencement date of an enactment.
xs: The **AP Municipalities Act, 1965** came into effect on **2 April 1965** — option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC-GS 2021**).
It governs **Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats**.
xa: **AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994** governs Municipal Corporations (**1955** in some sources).
**Third Amendment Bill 2026** adds a **Uniform Mutation Fee**, since neither the 1965 Act nor the 1955 Act allowed one.

n601f076e617.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the AP Cabinet decision of 18 August 2026 on electing local body heads?
o: Until now, Mayors have been elected indirectly from among the corporators
It approved direct election of Mayors of Municipal Corporations
It approved direct election of Chairpersons of Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats
It also provided for direct election of Mandal Parishad Presidents
n601f076e617.x: The decision covered urban heads only; Mandal Parishad Presidents remain indirectly elected.
xa: The same Cabinet approved **34%** BC reservation in rural local bodies.
Direct Mayor polls + **33.33%** BC quota + roll revision lead to AP's **second ordinary ULB polls**.

n84939209367.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated feature of Urban Development Authorities in Andhra Pradesh?
o: They are subordinate administrative wings of Urban Local Bodies.
They may be established by executive resolution.
They may be established by a State Act.
n84939209367.x: Urban Development Authorities are not subordinate to ULBs; their separate and autonomous functioning can fragment urban governance.
n84939209367.tq: Find the institutional relationship that reverses the correct position.
xs: UDAs are **not subordinate** to ULBs, so option **(1)** is the false feature.
They are **autonomous special-purpose (functional) agencies**, set up by **State Act or executive resolution** — options (2), (3), (4).
xa: Their separateness **fragments urban governance**.
Major UDAs: **APCRDA** (Amaravati, **APCRDA Act 2014**) and **VMRDA** (Visakhapatnam).
A **three-level uniform mechanism** for building checks covers UDAs too.

nbda846b8cd5.s: Part IX-A, inserted by the 74th Constitutional Amendment, comprises Articles:
nbda846b8cd5.x: Part IX-A on municipalities runs from Article 243P to 243ZG and is linked to the 18 Twelfth Schedule subjects.
xa: It is in force from **1 June 1993**.
**Art. 243ZA** gives the same SEC municipal elections; **243Y** the SFC for municipalities.
**Art. 243Q**: Nagar Panchayat for transitional areas.

n3a7d529bfd4.s: Which was the first Municipal Corporation in India?
n3a7d529bfd4.x: Madras got the first Municipal Corporation in 1688. Bombay and Calcutta followed later, in 1726. Delhi was not the first.
xs: India's first municipal corporation was **Madras (1688)** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Bombay** and **Calcutta** followed in **1726**.
xa: **74th Amendment**: in force from **1 June 1993**.
AIIB-aided AP Urban Water Supply Project: **Rs 300 crore**, **3.3 million** people, **50** ULBs.

nbd582591613.s: The Village/Ward Secretariat system in Andhra Pradesh was launched on:
nbd582591613.x: The system was launched on 2 October 2019, with a secretariat intended for each village or ward cluster.
nbd582591613.tq: Distinguish the 2019 launch date from Panchayati Raj foundation dates.
xs: The Village/Ward Secretariat system was launched on **2 October 2019** — option **(2)** is correct.
**1 November 1959** is when AP introduced Panchayati Raj.
xa: A secretariat serves each village or ward cluster, delivering services **alongside the Gram Panchayat**.
Urban Ward Secretariats work under the **Municipal Administration** department.

n25db92e77ba.s: National Panchayati Raj Day, on which the National Panchayat Awards are presented, is observed on:
n25db92e77ba.x: National Panchayati Raj Day is 24 April, when the 73rd Amendment came into force; five AP panchayats won National Panchayat Awards in 2026. 2 October is the 1959 Nagaur inauguration date and Gandhi Jayanti. 1 November is AP's Panchayati Raj start date, and 26 November is Constitution Day.
n25db92e77ba.tq: 24 April = Panchayati Raj Day (73rd in force 24 Apr 1993).
xs: **National Panchayati Raj Day** is **24 April** — option **(2)** is correct.
**2 October** (1959) is the Nagaur inauguration; **1 November** (1959) is AP's start date.
xa: **National Panchayat Awards 2026**: **five AP panchayats** won.
**Deendayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas** awards: AP won for the **2nd** year running.
**Bokkasam Palem** (Srikalahasti, Tirupati) → 1st for **women-friendly** panchayats; **Sringavaram** (Visakhapatnam) topped **governance**.

ne090e8de780.s: Which one of the following best represents the working definition of public policy?
o: A systematic course of action adopted by the state to address public issues, achieve development goals and regulate behaviour
A judicial determination applicable only to an individual dispute
A temporary administrative order issued only during emergencies
A set of private decisions taken by market participants without state intervention
ne090e8de780.x: Public policy is a systematic state course of action addressing public issues, pursuing development goals and regulating behaviour; it bridges political intent and administrative action.
ne090e8de780.tq: Choose the precise comprehensive definition over narrower alternatives.
xs: Public policy is **a systematic course of action adopted by the state to address public issues, achieve development goals and regulate behaviour** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is the **bridge between political intent and administrative action** — not a court ruling, an emergency order or a private market decision.
xa: Simply put: **government actions, laws and rules** to address specific problems.
Indian bases: **Preamble + DPSPs**, judicial interpretation, international commitments, **NITI Aayog** agendas, Budget, Economic Survey.
**Dye**: "whatever governments choose to do or not to do".

n8d946a0cda2.s: Which type of public policy creates or reorganises institutions?
n8d946a0cda2.x: Constitutive policy creates or reorganises institutions; regulatory policy limits individual or firm behaviour.
xa: Distributive: **farm input subsidies, PM-KISAN**; redistributive: **land reforms, progressive income tax**.
Regulatory: **licensing**, food-safety standards; constitutive: **NITI Aayog**, **delimitation**.

n0489e379a2e.s: Who defined public policy as “whatever governments choose to do or not to do”?
n0489e379a2e.x: Thomas Dye defined public policy as whatever governments choose to do or not to do, thereby treating governmental inaction also as policy.
xs: **Thomas Dye** defined public policy as "**whatever governments choose to do or not to do**" — option **(4)** is correct.
So for Dye, **inaction is also policy**.
**Easton** = "authoritative allocation of values"; **Lasswell** = "projected programme of goals, values and practices"; **Anderson** = "purposive course of action".
xa: Dye also gave **elite theory** with **Zeigler**.
⚠ **Lasswell** = founder of "**policy sciences**"; **Dye** = "do or not to do".
**Easton** also gave the **systems model** (inputs, conversion, outputs, feedback).

n7cac45667cd.s: Who defined public policy as the 'authoritative allocation of values for the whole society'?
n7cac45667cd.x: Easton gave this definition; Lasswell called policy a projected programme of goals, values and practices.
xa: **Lasswell** is the founder of the "**policy sciences**".
⚠ **Easton** = both a definition and the **systems model**.
**Thomas Dye**: "whatever governments choose to do or not to do".

n55bbbe92b39.s: The optimal model of policy-making is associated with:
n55bbbe92b39.x: Dror proposed the optimal model; Easton is linked to the systems model, Bentley to group theory and Mills to elite theory.
xa: Easton's systems model: **inputs, conversion, outputs, feedback**.
**Etzioni** = mixed scanning; **Lindblom** = incrementalism.

n74ca035b70b.s: The concept of nudges in public policy is associated with:
n74ca035b70b.x: Behavioural nudges and their use in policy design are associated with Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein.
n74ca035b70b.tq: Match the behavioural policy concept with its proponents.
xs: **Nudges** (behavioural design) come from **Thaler and Sunstein** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Pressman and Wildavsky** = "Implementation" (**1973**); **Bentley and Truman** = group theory; **Lindblom and Simon** = incrementalism/satisficing.
xa: Hood's tools: **Nodality, Authority, Treasure, Organisation**.
Information instruments: **RTI Act Sec. 4** disclosure, public campaigns.

nc700120eeea.s: Which one of the following correctly gives Hood’s NATO policy tools?
nc700120eeea.x: Hood’s NATO framework consists of Nodality, Authority, Treasure and Organisation.
nc700120eeea.tq: Reject look-alike expansions of a well-known policy acronym.
xs: **Hood's "NATO" tools** are **Nodality, Authority, Treasure, Organisation** — option **(2)** is correct.
The other options invent words (Negotiation, Accountability, Technology etc.) for the acronym.
xa: Indian instruments: **regulation**, **taxes and subsidies**, **direct provision**, **information**, **nudges**.
**Nudges** = **Thaler and Sunstein**.

n2b1b9742470.s: In the public policy cycle, which stage immediately follows formulation?
n2b1b9742470.x: The sequence is agenda-setting, formulation, adoption, implementation and evaluation.
xa: Last stage: **termination or revision**; **policy learning** feeds back to agenda setting.
**Communication + transparency** run through every stage.
Example: **Draft National Policy for Women 2016** (**Pam Rajput Committee**).

nede16c50cee.s: At which stage of the policy cycle are research, stakeholder consultation, cost-benefit analysis and impact assessment of options undertaken?
nede16c50cee.x: These activities are characteristic of policy formulation, when alternative courses of action are developed and assessed.
nede16c50cee.tq: Match the activity cluster with its stage.
xs: Research, stakeholder consultation, **cost-benefit analysis** and impact assessment belong to **formulation** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Agenda setting** only identifies the problem; **adoption** is formal approval; **implementation** is planning and resource allocation.
xa: ⚠ **Cost-benefit analysis** = formulation; **policy learning** = termination/revision.
AP live case: a Group of Ministers framing new **excise policy** with stakeholder feedback (2024-26 policy expires **30 Sep 2026**).

nbdbeae93efd.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the public policy cycle?
o: Agenda setting brings an identified problem onto the policy agenda
Communication and transparency are confined to the evaluation stage
Media, advocacy and expert analysis can place an issue on the agenda
Monitoring and evaluation give feedback that may lead to policy adjustment
nbdbeae93efd.x: Communication and transparency run through every stage of the cycle, not just evaluation.
xa: **Formulation**: research, consultation, **cost-benefit analysis**.
**Termination or revision**: **policy learning** feeds back to agenda setting.

n03f26ad7efb.s: Ending or revising an ineffective policy, with lessons fed back into agenda setting, is called:
n03f26ad7efb.x: Termination or revision deals with ineffective policies and lets policy learning feed back into agenda setting.
xa: **Monitoring and evaluation**: data and metrics test whether goals are met.
⚠ **Policy learning** = termination/revision; **cost-benefit analysis** = formulation.

na45698cd7dd.s: The bottom-up approach to policy implementation stresses the role of:
na45698cd7dd.x: The bottom-up approach recognises that front-line officials shape actual outcomes; central direction and faithful execution mark the top-down approach.
xa: Top-down: **Pressman and Wildavsky**, "Implementation" (**1973**) — chains of clearances derail programmes.
Bottom-up: **Lipsky** "street-level bureaucracy" (**1980**); **Elmore** "backward mapping".

n42eb2867415.s: The concept of “street-level bureaucracy” is associated with:
n42eb2867415.x: Michael Lipsky developed the concept of street-level bureaucracy in 1980, referring to front-line officials who shape policy outcomes.
n42eb2867415.tq: Separate the proponents of related implementation concepts.
xs: "**Street-level bureaucracy**" (**1980**) is **Michael Lipsky**'s concept — option **(4)** is correct.
It is a **bottom-up** view: front-line officials shape outcomes.
xa: **Richard Elmore**: "**backward mapping**" (also bottom-up).
**Pressman and Wildavsky** (**1973**): the top-down classic.
**Simon**: satisficing; **Easton**: systems model.

n61812827b2f.s: “Backward mapping” in policy implementation is associated with:
n61812827b2f.x: Richard Elmore is associated with the bottom-up implementation concept of backward mapping.
n61812827b2f.tq: Discriminate between the two bottom-up implementation scholars.
xs: "**Backward mapping**" is **Richard Elmore**'s idea — option **(2)** is correct.
It belongs to the **bottom-up** approach, like **Lipsky**'s street-level bureaucracy.
xa: **Dror** = optimal model; **Lindblom** = incrementalism.
Top-down: **Pressman and Wildavsky** (**1973**).

n3c44cc09a7d.s: The top-down study 'Implementation' (1973), which showed how chains of clearances derail programmes, was written by:
n3c44cc09a7d.x: Pressman and Wildavsky wrote 'Implementation' (1973), the classic top-down study. Lipsky (street-level bureaucracy, 1980) and Elmore (backward mapping) belong to the bottom-up approach. Thaler and Sunstein are linked with nudges.
xs: '**Implementation**' (**1973**) was written by **Pressman and Wildavsky** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is the **top-down** classic: chains of clearances derail programmes.
**Lipsky** (street-level bureaucracy, **1980**) and **Elmore** (backward mapping) are **bottom-up**; **Thaler and Sunstein** = nudges.
xa: Top-down: policy set at the centre and carried out **faithfully**.
Bottom-up: **front-line officials** shape real outcomes.

nba4859d7e26.s: Judicial interpretation as a basis of Indian public policy is illustrated by the Right to Food under Article:
nba4859d7e26.x: Courts read the Right to Food into Article 21, which makes judicial interpretation one of the bases of public policy.
xa: Public policy bridges **political intent and administrative action**.
Setting up **NITI Aayog** is itself a **constitutive** policy (Lowi).

n123fafc80c6.s: Proactive disclosure under Section 4 of the RTI Act illustrates which policy instrument?
n123fafc80c6.x: Section 4 proactive disclosure is an information instrument; regulation uses licensing and standards, and direct provision means services like schools and PHCs.
xa: Regulation example: **Delhi EV policy** — e-three-wheelers/N1 trucks from **1 Jan 2027**, e-two-wheelers from **1 Apr 2028**.
**Hood's "NATO" tools**: Nodality, Authority, Treasure, Organisation.
**Nudges**: behavioural design (**Thaler and Sunstein**).

nbc27cda5069.s: Which of the following is NOT a recognised cause of policy failure or an implementation gap?
nbc27cda5069.x: Weak coordination, resource shortfalls and poor targeting are causes of policy failure. Real-time public outcome tracking is a remedy.
nbc27cda5069.tq: Find the option that represents a remedy rather than a cause.
xs: **Real-time public outcome tracking** is a **remedy**, not a cause of failure — option **(2)** is correct.
Causes include **weak inter-departmental coordination**, **resource shortfalls** and **poor targeting**.
xa: Other causes: **political change**, **capacity gaps**, bypassing of citizens by **parastatals and SPVs**.
Remedies: **phased roll-out with milestones** + real-time monitoring.
AP: **Action Taken Reports** against **seven sector white papers** (**22 Jun 2026**).

n2cbb3fc828d.s: The Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO) is the apex monitoring and evaluation office under:
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
n2cbb3fc828d.x: DMEO works under NITI Aayog, evaluating Central schemes suo motu or at a ministry's request and advising States.
xa: ATRs + DMEO evaluations → "**outcome-based**" governance.
NITI Aayog (with **WRI India**) launched the **second India Electric Mobility Index** (**17 Sep 2026**).
Its weights: **50:30:20** across transport electrification, charging and R&D.

n3be1f45f09e.s: Gender budgeting in India and the Outcome Budget both began in:
n3be1f45f09e.x: Gender budgeting was adopted in 2005-06, and the Outcome Budget also began in 2005-06.
n3be1f45f09e.tq: Identify the common year attached to two budgetary initiatives.
xs: **Gender budgeting** and the **Outcome Budget** both began in **2005-06** — option **(1)** is correct.
The other years (2001-02, 2003-04, 2007-08) are distractors; only 2005-06 appears for both.
xa: **6th Plan (1980-85)**: women's policy moved from welfare to **development**.
**8th-9th Plans**: **empowerment**.
**MWCD** became a separate ministry in **2006-07**.

nc463cf2c42e.s: Under Section 17 of MGNREGA, social audit is conducted by the:
nc463cf2c42e.x: Section 17 of MGNREGA provides for social audit of works by the Gram Sabha.
xa: AP pioneered statewide NREGS social audits (**2006**) through independent **SSAAT (2009)**.
NREGA guarantee: **100 days** (**125** under the VB-G RAM G Bill **2025**).

n5c1a8da536d.s: Andhra Pradesh pioneered statewide NREGS social audits in:
n5c1a8da536d.x: AP began statewide NREGS social audits in 2006; the independent SSAAT was set up later, in 2009.
xa: ⚠ AP social audits began **2006**; **SSAAT** set up **2009**.
Social audit is under MGNREGA **Sec. 17**, done by the **Gram Sabha**.

n958964bcbaa.s: The shift from announcement-based to outcome-based governance is linked with:
n958964bcbaa.x: Outcome-based governance is linked with Action Taken Reports (ATRs) and Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO) evaluations.
xa: **DMEO** is the apex M&E office under **NITI Aayog**.
Remedies for implementation gaps: **real-time monitoring** and **public outcome tracking**.

n9c81bd81415.s: The Draft National Policy for Women, 2016, was based on the recommendations of which committee?
n9c81bd81415.x: The Draft National Policy for Women, 2016, was based on the Pam Rajput Committee.
n9c81bd81415.tq: Test the policy-document and committee association directly.
xs: The **Draft National Policy for Women 2016** was based on the **Pam Rajput Committee** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is the notes' example of the **policy cycle** in action.
xa: Policy cycle: **agenda-setting → formulation → adoption → implementation → evaluation**.
**6th Plan (1980-85)** shifted women's policy from welfare to **development**.
**Gender budgeting** was adopted in **2005-06**.

n195b6bd73f9.s: In which Five-Year Plan did India's approach to women shift from welfare to development?
n195b6bd73f9.x: The welfare-to-development shift came in the Sixth Plan; the empowerment approach marked the Eighth and Ninth Plans.
xa: Now: "**New welfarism**" — targeted, technology-driven **DBT** benefits rather than legal rights.
**Central Social Welfare Board**: **1953**.

n80cde62d641.x: New welfarism is targeted and technology-driven, relying on DBT benefits rather than primarily on legal rights.
xa: Criticism: it **weakens rights**; social protection spending is only **4.0% of GDP**.
Social protection covers **64.3%** of population, up from **22%** in **2016**.
**DBT** from **1 Jan 2013**; drawback: excludes people without digital access.

n5ee7e7bf236.s: In which year was the Ministry of Welfare renamed the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment?
n5ee7e7bf236.x: The Ministry of Welfare was renamed the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in 1998.
n5ee7e7bf236.tq: Recall the precise year of renaming among closely related administrative dates.
xs: The Ministry of Welfare was renamed **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment** in **1998** — option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC-G2 2008** key).
**1999** is the formation of the **Ministry of Tribal Affairs**; **1985** saw the split of the Ministry of Welfare.
xa: ⚠ **1998** = MoSJE renamed; **1999** = Tribal Affairs formed.
MoSJE departments now: **Social Justice and Empowerment** + **Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan)**.

nbf3c45ff3e8.s: Which of the following is a department of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment?
o: Department of School Education and Literacy
Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan)
nbf3c45ff3e8.x: The Ministry's present departments are Social Justice and Empowerment, and Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan).
xa: MoSJE got its name in **1998** (**APPSC-G2 2008** key).
**Ministry of Tribal Affairs** formed in **1999**.

nindian-society-7-1.s: In which year was the Ministry of Welfare renamed the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment?
nindian-society-7-1.x: The Ministry of Welfare (1985) was renamed in 1998; Tribal Affairs split off in 1999 and Minority Affairs in 2006.
n: The Ministry of Welfare was established in 1985. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 28-30]
The Ministry of Welfare was renamed as the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in 1998. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 28-30]
Tribal Affairs functions were separated from the Ministry of Welfare in 1999 to create the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 28-30]
Minority welfare functions were transferred to the Ministry of Minority Affairs in 2006. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 28-30]
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: Minority Affairs/MWCD created **Jan 2006** vs transfer **2007** (IYB).
MoSJE now has two departments: Social Justice and Empowerment + **Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan)**.
⚠ **1998** = MoSJE renamed; **1999** = Tribal Affairs formed.

nindian-society-7-2.s: Matters relating to the Parsi community come under which Union Ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Women and Child Development
nindian-society-7-2.x: Minority Affairs handles the Parsis and other minorities; Social Justice handles transgender welfare.
n: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment deals with transgender welfare. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 28-30]
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs deals with the Forest Rights Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 28-30]
The Ministry of Minority Affairs deals with Parsis. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 28-30]
The Ministry of Women and Child Development deals with Poshan initiatives. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 28-30]
xa: MoSJE also handles **SC** and **OBC** welfare, **senior citizens** and **persons with disabilities**.
Tribal Affairs also handles **PESA implementation** and **tribal education**.
WCD also runs **ICDS** and **child protection**.

nc0a66ec4add.s: Which one of the following is NOT generally regarded as a social welfare service?
nc0a66ec4add.x: General health services for all are not classified as targeted social welfare services, whereas the other three serve vulnerable groups.
nc0a66ec4add.tq: Separate targeted welfare services from universal public services.
xs: **General health services for all** are **not** a social welfare service — option **(3)** is correct (**APPSC-GS 2019**).
Welfare services are **targeted** at the vulnerable: **disabled persons, destitute children, widows**.
xa: **Social welfare** = services for **weaker and vulnerable sections**.
Welfare is **short-term, consumption-oriented**; development is **long-term, production-oriented**.

ne2a55e0c52e.s: Which one of the following is NOT a social development programme?
ne2a55e0c52e.x: The Mid-Day Meal, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and the Rural Health Mission are social development programmes. The Look East Policy is a foreign policy, not a social development programme (UPPSC 2015).
ne2a55e0c52e.tq: Look East = foreign policy, the odd one out.
xs: The **Look East Policy** is **not** a social development programme — option **(4)** is correct (**UPPSC 2015**).
**Mid-Day Meal**, **SSA** and the **Rural Health Mission** are social development programmes.
xa: Development is **long-term, production-oriented**.
⚠ Similar trap: **general health services for all** is not a welfare service (**APPSC-GS 2019**).

na05fbde60f5.s: The Central Social Welfare Board was established in:
na05fbde60f5.x: The Central Social Welfare Board was established in 1953 during the state-led planned development and welfare phase.
na05fbde60f5.tq: Recall the specific institutional milestone within the early welfare phase.
xs: The **Central Social Welfare Board** was set up in **1953** — option **(2)** is correct.
It belongs to the **1950s-70s** phase of state-led planned development and welfare.
xa: **6th Plan (1980-85)**: welfare → **development**.
**2000s**: **rights-based** laws.

n18784c76fc2.s: The principal aim of social legislation is to:
o: Protect vulnerable persons and set minimum conditions for a dignified life
Replace public assistance with private charity
n18784c76fc2.x: Social legislation protects vulnerable groups and sets minimum floors for a dignified life, moving from freedom of contract to fairness in contract.
xa: ⚠ Key: "**all of the above**" (**APPSC-GS 2019**).
Protective: **Factories Act 1948**, **Bonded Labour Act 1976**; regulatory: **Minimum Wages Act 1948**, **Dowry Prohibition Act 1961**.

n27e2689ffc8.s: Social legislation that creates entitlements is called:
n27e2689ffc8.x: Enabling legislation creates entitlements; protective legislation guards against exploitation and regulatory legislation governs conduct.
xa: Protective: **Factories Act 1948**, Child Labour Act, **Bonded Labour Act 1976**.
Regulatory: **Minimum Wages Act 1948**, **Dowry Prohibition Act 1961**.

nb07bfc8d136.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, social protection in India covers approximately what share of the population?
nb07bfc8d136.x: As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, social protection covers about 64.3% of India's population, up from 22% in 2016. The 22% figure is the 2016 level, not the current one.
nb07bfc8d136.tq: Distinguish the current coverage figure from the earlier benchmark of 22%.
xs: Social protection covers **64.3%** of the population — option **(3)** is correct (**ES 2025-26**).
**22%** was the level in **2016**, not today's.
xa: Spending is only **4.0% of GDP**.
"New welfarism" relies on targeted **DBT** benefits.

n25177aaabdb.s: Media organisations are generally regarded as stakeholders of governance under which category?
n25177aaabdb.x: Media organisations are counted among civil society stakeholders involved in governance.
n25177aaabdb.tq: Test institutional classification through a nearby-category distinction.
xs: Media organisations are stakeholders under **civil society** — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ **Media** = civil society, not State.
xa: Stakeholders: **State** (legislature, judiciary, executive, bureaucracy), **Market**, **Civil Society**.
Civil society: **NGOs, VOs, media, trade unions, religious + pressure groups**.

n30dfdd18ee6.s: Pressure groups, trade unions and NGOs belong to which set of governance stakeholders?
n30dfdd18ee6.x: State, Market and Civil Society are the three broad stakeholder sets, and pressure groups, trade unions and NGOs belong to civil society.
xa: **Media** is also civil society.
Civil society also includes **VOs** and **religious** groups.

ne486b43b654.s: Which body, headed by the Cabinet Secretary, administers the Transaction of Business Rules?
ne486b43b654.x: The Cabinet Secretariat, headed by the Cabinet Secretary, works directly under the PM and administers the Transaction of Business Rules; the PMO is the PM's policy office.
xa: **NITI Aayog** (**2015**) is the apex public policy think tank, chaired by the **PM**.
AP CM's **two-month review cycle** for **₹50,999 crore** of Amaravati contracts resembles the Centre's **PRAGATI** model.

n56107112876.s: Who was appointed Vice Chairperson of NITI Aayog in 2026?
n56107112876.x: A is correct: Ashok Kumar Lahiri was appointed Vice Chairperson of NITI Aayog in 2026. B and C are earlier Vice Chairpersons, not the 2026 appointee. D, Amitabh Kant, was NITI Aayog's CEO, a different post. The Chairperson is the Prime Minister.
n56107112876.tq: NITI Aayog: Chair = PM; VC (2026) = Ashok Kumar Lahiri.
xs: **Ashok Kumar Lahiri** was appointed **Vice Chairperson** of NITI Aayog in **2026** — option **(1)** is correct.
NITI Aayog itself is **chaired by the PM**.
xa: NITI Aayog (**2015**) replaced the **Planning Commission** (**1950**).
It is **non-constitutional + non-statutory**.
NITI Aayog (with **WRI India**) launched the **second India Electric Mobility Index**.

nfad9fdd0afe.s: Which of the following is identified as an accountability gap in governance?
o: Rising referral of Bills to parliamentary committees
Delays by Governors and Speakers in assent and Tenth Schedule decisions
nfad9fdd0afe.x: Delays by Governors and Speakers on assent and Tenth Schedule matters are an accountability gap, along with an RTI backlog and fewer committee referrals.
xa: Other gaps: **RTI backlog** (over **4 lakh**); **fewer committee referrals** (**16%** in 17th LS).
Sri Lanka's proposed **22nd Amendment**: SC judges' retirement age from **65 to 67**.

n0ed52fa1d8b.s: In the legislative process, government Bills are generally drafted by the:
n0ed52fa1d8b.x: Parliament is the chief law-making body and the Cabinet decides the substance and timing of Bills, but the bureaucracy generally drafts them.
xa: Controls on the executive: **Question Hour** (most effective), **Zero Hour**, adjournment motions, financial control.
Committee referrals fell from **71%** (15th Lok Sabha) to **16%** (17th Lok Sabha).

n811cd2a25d3.s: Which of the following is regarded as the most effective parliamentary control over the executive among the listed devices?
n811cd2a25d3.x: Question Hour is identified as the most effective among the listed parliamentary controls over the executive.
n811cd2a25d3.tq: Recall the relative effectiveness of a parliamentary control device.
xs: **Question Hour** is the **most effective** parliamentary control over the executive — option **(2)** is correct.
Constitutional amendment and private members' bills are law-making, not executive controls.
xa: Other controls: **Zero Hour**, **half-an-hour discussions**, **adjournment motions**, **financial control**, ratification of laws.
Without a **Rajya Sabha** majority, governments must concede (**Prevention of Terrorism Bill 2002** was rejected there).

n5e17b906f33.s: The share of Bills referred to parliamentary committees fell from about 71% in the 15th Lok Sabha to about what share in the 17th Lok Sabha?
n5e17b906f33.x: C is correct: referral of Bills to committees fell from 71% in the 15th Lok Sabha to 16% in the 17th Lok Sabha, showing falling committee scrutiny. A, B and D are not the figures given; the drop was much steeper.
xs: Bills referred to committees fell from **71%** (**15th Lok Sabha**) to **16%** (**17th Lok Sabha**) — option **(3)** is correct.
This shows **falling committee scrutiny** (**30 Jul 2026**).
xa: ⚠ **71%** = 15th Lok Sabha; **16%** = 17th Lok Sabha.
"Fewer committee referrals" is listed as an **accountability gap**.

ne0a1c4e1ddd.s: The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2018 was enacted by Parliament to overturn the effect of which Supreme Court decision?
ne0a1c4e1ddd.x: B is correct: the SC/ST (PoA) Amendment 2018 followed the Subhash Kashinath Mahajan judgment. A, Shah Bano, led to the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act 1986. C, Kesavananda Bharati, laid down the basic structure limit on amendments. D, Vishaka, gave workplace sexual-harassment guidelines.
ne0a1c4e1ddd.tq: Shah Bano gave the 1986 Act; Subhash Kashinath Mahajan gave the PoA Amendment 2018.
xs: The **SC/ST (PoA) Amendment 2018** overturned the **Subhash Kashinath Mahajan** decision — option **(2)** is correct.
**Shah Bano** led to the **Muslim Women Act 1986**; **Kesavananda Bharati** set the **basic structure** limit; **Vishaka** gave workplace harassment guidelines.
xa: A validating law must remove the **basis** of a judgment.

n3c109ff5c56.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the options available against a Supreme Court decision?
o: A review or curative petition is heard by the same Court
Parliament may amend the law to remove the basis of a judgment but cannot simply overrule it
A constitutional amendment under Article 368 must respect the basic structure
A Presidential reference under Article 143 produces a binding judgment on the dispute
n3c109ff5c56.x: A Presidential reference under Article 143 yields only an advisory opinion, not a binding judgment.
xa: Examples: **Muslim Women Act 1986** after **Shah Bano**; **SC/ST (PoA) Amendment 2018** after **Subhash Kashinath Mahajan**.
**Kesavananda Bharati** is the source of the **basic structure** limit.

nf2543943f80.s: In which year did Public Interest Litigation begin in India, with a case filed on behalf of prisoners?
nf2543943f80.x: PIL began in 1979 with a case filed on behalf of prisoners; its basis lies in Articles 32, 226 and 142.
xa: Criticism: **Upendra Baxi's** typology of fears — ideological, epistemic, management, legitimation, democratic.
PIL misuse for **publicity or political ends** draws criticism.

n86e0edc4764.s: Which one of the following is NOT included in Upendra Baxi's typology of fears concerning judicial activism?
n86e0edc4764.x: Upendra Baxi's typology includes ideological, epistemic, management, legitimation and democratic fears. Electoral fear is not included in the listed typology.
n86e0edc4764.tq: Use the complete named classification to identify the outsider.
xs: **Electoral fear** is not in **Upendra Baxi's** typology — option **(4)** is correct.
His fears are **ideological, epistemic, management, legitimation, democratic** — covering options (1)–(3).
xa: Ignored **police-reform orders** → **legitimation** risk.
Overreach → **policy paralysis + backlog**.

nfaa348a2c10.s: The Vishaka guidelines continued to operate in a legislative vacuum until the enactment of which law?
o: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
nfaa348a2c10.x: The Vishaka guidelines on workplace sexual harassment operated until the POSH Act was enacted in 2013.
nfaa348a2c10.tq: Link the judicial guideline with the later legislation that occupied the legislative field.
xs: The **Vishaka** guidelines (**1997**) filled the vacuum until the **POSH Act, 2013** — option **(1)** is correct.
They are an example of court guidelines that **acted as law**.
xa: Similar cases: **Prakash Singh (2006)** on police; **T.S.R. Subramanian (2013)** on civil servants.

n49f4b48df83.s: The MKSS right-to-information movement led to which law?
n49f4b48df83.x: The MKSS movement led to the RTI Act, 2005; Right to Work advocacy to MGNREGA and the Right to Food campaign to the NFSA.
xa: Right to Food rested on the **PUCL v. Union of India** PIL, **2001**.

n5c8d552c30f.s: The permanent executive in India includes:
o: All-India Services, State services, local staff and PSU staff
n5c8d552c30f.x: The permanent executive comprises All-India Services, State services, local staff and PSU staff, who help ministers formulate and implement policy.
xa: Recruitment: **UPSC + State PSCs**.
Accountability tools: **Vigilance, conduct rules, CAG, CVC, Lokpal**.

n50fe499f545.s: The 33.33% Backward Classes quota in Andhra Pradesh urban local bodies originated as:
n50fe499f545.x: The 33.33% BC quota in AP urban local bodies was an NDA 2024 poll promise, later implemented through G.O. Rt. No. 1065.
xa: It shows **manifesto → policy** in agenda setting.
Delivery tracking: **Action Taken Reports** against **seven sector white papers**.

n087996820eb.s: From which date has Andhra Pradesh published Action Taken Reports on its seven sectoral white papers?
n087996820eb.x: AP has published Action Taken Reports from 22 June 2026, so manifesto delivery can be tracked publicly.
xa: Manifesto example: **33.33% BC quota** (NDA **2024** promise).
ATRs + **DMEO** evaluations mark a shift to "**outcome-based**" governance.

n79e8af2247d.s: In which year was the National Innovation Council established as a Government body?
n79e8af2247d.x: The National Innovation Council was set up in 2010; CPR, NCAER, PRS and ORF are independent bodies.
xa: Party-linked: **Syama Prasad Mookerjee Research Foundation** (BJP), **Rajiv Gandhi Foundation** (Congress).
Newer channels: **policy labs, hackathons, idea competitions**.

n594442f56c4.s: NITI Aayog is chaired by the:
n594442f56c4.x: The Prime Minister chairs NITI Aayog, a non-constitutional, non-statutory policy think tank working on cooperative federalism.
xa: ⚠ **NITI Aayog** = **2015**; **Planning Commission** = **1950**.
It is a **Government** think tank, together with **DMEO**.
Vice Chairperson: **Ashok Kumar Lahiri** (**2026**).

n4de31fc91e5.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a concern relating to bureaucracy?
n4de31fc91e5.x: Frontline implementation discretion is itself a concern, so 'complete absence of discretion' is not.
xa: **Lipsky**'s "street-level bureaucracy" is about front-line officials shaping outcomes.
Accountability tools: **Vigilance, conduct rules, CAG, CVC, Lokpal**.

n31d8b15909b.s: Which of the following is correct about the image-building role of mass media?
o: The ideology of a media outlet can influence its treatment of news
Mass media play no part in shaping the identity of political personalities
Media treatment has no bearing on the public image of political personalities
A media outlet's ideology is irrelevant to how it treats news
n31d8b15909b.x: Mass media shape the image of political personalities, and an outlet's ideology can colour its treatment of news.
xa: ⚠ Key (**APPSC-GS 2018**): **(A) true, (R) the correct explanation**.
Free press is necessary for a **vibrant democracy**.

nc4cb15ce391.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the World Bank's definition of governance?
o: The manner in which power is exercised in managing a country's economic and social resources for development
The distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States
The exclusive exercise of authority by the executive branch
The process by which elections are conducted at regular intervals
nc4cb15ce391.x: The World Bank defines governance as the manner in which power is exercised in managing a country's economic and social resources for development.
nc4cb15ce391.tq: Match the exact institutional definition with the correct body.
xs: The **World Bank** defines governance as "**the manner in which power is exercised in the management of a country's economic and social resources for development**" — option **(1)** is correct.
It stresses **accountability, transparency, rule of law**.
xa: The World Bank first brought "**good governance**" into development discourse — **1989** report on **Sub-Saharan Africa**.
**UNDP (1997)**: exercise of **economic, political and administrative** authority.
**UNESCAP** stresses efficiency, effectiveness, equity, sustainability.

nd61614ce5af.s: Which institution first brought the concept of 'good governance' into development discourse?
nd61614ce5af.x: B is correct: the World Bank first brought 'good governance' into development discourse through its 1989 report on Sub-Saharan Africa (APPSC-GS 2018 key). A, UNDP, gave its own definition later (1997). C and D are not credited with introducing the term.
nd61614ce5af.tq: Good governance term: World Bank, 1989, Sub-Saharan Africa.
xs: The **World Bank** first brought "**good governance**" into development discourse — option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC-GS 2018**).
It did so in its **1989** report on **Sub-Saharan Africa**; **UNDP** gave its definition later, in **1997**.
xa: World Bank stresses **accountability, transparency, rule of law**.
The World Bank's **WGI** cover **200+** countries since **1996**.

nf174dd9ff0f.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the eight attributes of good governance identified in the UN/UNDP list?
nf174dd9ff0f.x: Administrative centralisation is not one of the eight attributes. The list includes consensus orientation, participation, rule of law, effectiveness and efficiency, accountability, transparency, responsiveness, and equity and inclusiveness.
nf174dd9ff0f.tq: Find the odd feature that is absent from the recognised list.
xs: **Administrative centralisation** is not one of the **8 attributes** — option **(3)** is correct.
The 8: **consensus oriented, participatory, rule of law, effective and efficient, accountable, transparent, responsive, equitable and inclusive**.
xa: Exam angle: in "NOT a feature" questions look for **centralisation, secrecy, discretion** or **majoritarian rule**.
Most critical three (UNDP): **transparency, accountability, responsiveness**.

n949fcaba17f.s: Which department is identified as India's nodal department for the World Bank's Worldwide Governance Indicators?
o: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
n949fcaba17f.x: The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, or DARPG, is India's nodal department for the WGI.
n949fcaba17f.tq: Use the institutional-responsibility approach: identify which department handles the governance indicator.
xs: **DARPG** (**Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances**) is India's nodal department for the WGI — option **(4)** is correct.
**DPIIT** publishes **BRAP** rankings; **NITI Aayog** the **SDG India Index**.
xa: DARPG also publishes the **Good Governance Index** and **GRAI**.
DARPG tools: **NeSDA** (**2019**), **Citizen's Charter** portal, **CPGRAMS**.

n552ec08be99.s: The National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG) was established by upgrading the:
n552ec08be99.x: The NCGG was established by upgrading the National Institute of Administrative Research associated with LBSNAA.
n552ec08be99.tq: Identify the predecessor institution rather than the parent organisation by association.
xs: **NCGG** was set up by upgrading the **National Institute of Administrative Research** (LBSNAA) — option **(4)** is correct.
It is an **autonomous** institute.
xa: Head office **New Delhi**; branch **Mussoorie**.
⚠ **CGG** (Centre for Good Governance) is in **Hyderabad**, set up **2001**.

nd3cf490c840.s: According to the indicated UNDP emphasis, the three most critical characteristics of good governance are:
o: Rule of law, security and decentralisation
nd3cf490c840.x: Transparency, accountability and responsiveness are identified as the three most critical characteristics.
nd3cf490c840.tq: Recall the specifically emphasised subset within a larger list.
xs: UNDP's three most critical traits are **transparency, accountability and responsiveness** — option **(3)** is correct.
They come from the **8 attributes** of good governance.
xa: Other attributes: **consensus oriented**, **participatory**, **rule of law**, **effective and efficient**, **equitable and inclusive**.
Four pillars: **Ethos, Ethics, Equity, Efficiency**.

n89e5cae414a.s: Among the pillars of good governance, 'Ethos' stands for:
n89e5cae414a.x: Ethos means service; ethics means honesty and integrity, equity means empathy for weaker sections, and efficiency means speedy ICT-based delivery.
xa: Tools: **people's participation**, **RTI**, **Sevottam**, **Citizen Charters**, **e-governance**.
Second ARC's **4th Report**: "**Ethics in Governance**" (**2007**).

n51449f090f3.s: The Worldwide Governance Indicators have been available since:
n51449f090f3.x: The WGI cover more than 200 countries since 1996, with dimensions including Government Effectiveness and Rule of Law.
xa: **DARPG** is India's nodal department.
Criticism: WGI **relies on perception data**.

n6ef8d1f4a6e.s: The Good Governance Index of DARPG, launched on Good Governance Day 2019, is to be revised every:
n6ef8d1f4a6e.x: The GGI, which ranks States, UTs and districts, is to be revised every two years.
xa: GGI covers **10 sectors**.
⚠ **BRAP** = DPIIT; **GGI/GRAI** = DARPG.

n856d32afdcb.s: The Worldwide Governance Indicators and V-Dem indices are mainly criticised because they:
o: Rely substantially on expert opinion and perceptions
Measure only economic growth and fiscal deficit
n856d32afdcb.x: WGI and V-Dem are contested because, as perception-based indices, they rely substantially on expert opinion.
xa: V-Dem 2026: India **106th of 179**, "**electoral autocracy**".
India in **WGI 2023**: moderate effectiveness, **low political stability**.

n5a6c376f6ae.s: Which one of the following is NOT a dimension of the World Bank's Worldwide Governance Indicators?
n5a6c376f6ae.x: Human Development Index is not a WGI dimension. The WGI dimensions include Voice and Accountability, Political Stability, Government Effectiveness, Regulatory Quality, Rule of Law and Control of Corruption.
n5a6c376f6ae.tq: Identify the item that belongs to another index rather than the six WGI dimensions.
xs: The **Human Development Index** is not a WGI dimension — option **(3)** is correct.

The **six** WGI dimensions: **Voice and Accountability**, **Political Stability and Absence of Violence/Terrorism**, **Government Effectiveness**, **Regulatory Quality**, **Rule of Law**, **Control of Corruption**.
xa: WGI cover **200+** countries since **1996**.
⚠ **WGI** = **6** dimensions; **GGI** = **10** sectors.

nf0d17dd1855.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the ten sectors of the Good Governance Index?
nf0d17dd1855.x: Foreign affairs and diplomacy is not one of the ten GGI sectors. The sectors include citizen-centric governance, environment, public health, agriculture and allied sectors, and others.
nf0d17dd1855.tq: Find the sector outside the prescribed domestic-governance framework.
xs: **Foreign affairs and diplomacy** is not a GGI sector — option **(4)** is correct.
The **10 sectors** include **environment**, **citizen-centric governance** and **public health**.
xa: Others: agriculture and allied, commerce and industry, human resource development, public infrastructure and utilities, economic governance, social welfare and development, judicial and public security.
GGI launched **2019**; revised every **two years**.

na39928dabd4.s: The Good Governance Index is published by:
na39928dabd4.x: DARPG publishes the Good Governance Index; NITI Aayog publishes the SDG India Index, DPIIT the BRAP rankings and PAC the Public Affairs Index.
xa: ⚠ **BRAP** = DPIIT, not NITI Aayog.
**GRAI** is also by **DARPG**.
NITI Aayog's first **Investment Friendliness Index 2026**: **Gujarat** 1st.

n33694a6b6a3.s: According to the 2026 V-Dem assessment, India was placed at:
o: 100th among 179 countries and classified as an electoral democracy
106th among 154 countries and classified as a liberal democracy
106th among 179 countries and classified as an electoral autocracy
16th among 179 countries and classified as an electoral autocracy
n33694a6b6a3.x: The 2026 V-Dem assessment placed India 106th out of 179 and described it as an “electoral autocracy.”
n33694a6b6a3.tq: Keep the country rank, total number and classification together to avoid mixing editions.
xs: **V-Dem 2026** placed India **106th of 179**, an "**electoral autocracy**" — option **(3)** is correct.
India was **100th** in **2025**; **16th of 154** is the **Responsible Nations Index** rank.
xa: V-Dem is by the **University of Gothenburg**.
