Criticism: perception-based indices (**WGI, V-Dem**) rely on expert opinion.

nfefecc6469c.s: In the Responsible Nations Index 2026, India ranked:
nfefecc6469c.x: India ranked 16th out of 154 countries in the Responsible Nations Index 2026; Singapore ranked first.
xa: The index is by **WIF, JNU and IIM Mumbai**.
**Investment Friendliness Index 2026**: **Gujarat** 1st.

n08de0ec5a3a.s: The Second ARC's 12th Report, which covered Citizen's Charters, grievance redress and the Sevottam model, was titled:
o: Promoting e-Governance – The SMART Way Forward
Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance
n08de0ec5a3a.x: The 12th Report (2009), 'Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance', covered Citizen's Charters, grievance redress, Sevottam and people's participation.
xa: The **Second ARC** was set up in **2005** and gave **15 reports**.
**4th Report** (**2007**): "**Ethics in Governance**".

n544279454b0.s: Which of the following is regarded as the most foundational tool for implementing good governance?
n544279454b0.x: People's participation is identified as the most foundational tool for implementing good governance; other tools include RTI, Sevottam, Citizen Charters and e-governance.
n544279454b0.tq: Identify the foundational element rather than a supporting administrative instrument.
xs: **People's participation** is the **most foundational** good-governance tool — option **(2)** is correct.
**Secrecy, discretion** and **centralisation** run against good governance.
xa: Other tools: **RTI**, **Sevottam**, **Citizen Charters**, **e-governance**.
Democracy aids development by **encouraging citizen participation** (**APPSC-GS 2025**).

n27ec7848d7a.s: The Centre for Good Governance, set up by undivided Andhra Pradesh in 2001, is based in:
n27ec7848d7a.x: The CGG, set up with DFID (UK) and the World Bank, is in Hyderabad; New Delhi and Mussoorie are the locations of the National Centre for Good Governance.
xa: The CGG is a governance-reform **think tank**: administrative reforms, e-governance, research, training.
**NCGG** was set up by upgrading the National Institute of Administrative Research (**LBSNAA**).
The **World Bank** first brought "good governance" into development discourse — **1989** report on Sub-Saharan Africa.
DARPG tools: **NeSDA** (**2019**), **CPGRAMS**, **Citizen's Charter** portal.

nba59d1aa441.s: Which one of the following best distinguishes governance from government?
o: Governance is confined to the state, whereas government includes civil society.
Governance refers only to judicial administration.
Governance is broader and involves the market and civil society, not merely the state.
Government and governance are identical in scope and meaning.
nba59d1aa441.x: Governance is broader than government because it involves the state together with the market and civil society.
nba59d1aa441.tq: Focus on the scope comparison and reject the reversed relationship.
xs: **Governance is broader** — it involves the **market and civil society**, not just the state — option **(3)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses this; option (4) treats the two as identical.
xa: Stakeholders of governance: **State, Market, Civil Society**.
**UNDP (1997)**: governance manages a country's affairs **at all levels**.

n77910af256f.s: Democracy aids development mainly because it encourages:
n77910af256f.x: Democracy aids development by encouraging citizen participation and accountability.
n77910af256f.tq: Apply the cause-effect relationship rather than choosing a general democratic feature.
xs: Democracy aids development as it **encourages citizen participation and accountability** — option **(4)** is correct (**APPSC-GS 2025**).
**Centralisation, secrecy, discretion** and **majoritarian rule** are the odd ones out in good-governance questions.
xa: **People's participation** is the **most foundational** good-governance tool.
UN/UNDP attributes include **participatory** and **accountable**.

n3916e9471d8.s: The Centre for Good Governance (CGG) in Andhra Pradesh functions primarily as a:
o: Statutory commission for recruitment to public services
Governance-reform think tank advising the government
n3916e9471d8.x: The CGG is a governance-reform think tank that advises the government on administrative reforms, e-governance, research and training.
n3916e9471d8.tq: Identify the institution by its mandate rather than by its location.
xs: AP's **CGG** is a **governance-reform think tank** advising on **administrative reforms, e-governance, research, training** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is not a regulator, recruitment commission or constitutional authority.
xa: Set up by undivided AP in **2001** with **DFID (UK) and the World Bank**.
Based in **Hyderabad**.

naa31f137ec8.s: Who is associated with the five models of e-governance comprising broadcasting, critical flow, comparative analysis, e-advocacy and interactive service?
naa31f137ec8.x: The five models listed are attributed to Arie Halachmi.
naa31f137ec8.tq: Match the named theorist with the distinctive classification of models.
xs: The five models — broadcasting, critical flow, comparative analysis, e-advocacy and interactive service — are those of **Arie Halachmi**, so option **(3)** is correct.
Each model is a distinct way of using ICT in government, from **public-domain information** (broadcasting) to **two-way G2C services** (interactive service).
xa: **Critical flow** channels critical information to a targeted audience, e.g. corruption data to an **ombudsman**.
**Comparative analysis** means learning from **best practices** elsewhere.
**E-advocacy / mobilisation and lobbying**: online **civil-society networks** influence decisions.
⚠ Corruption data → ombudsman is **critical flow**, not broadcasting.

nd8484fb93b7.s: Information on corruption is channelled electronically to an ombudsman. This illustrates which model of e-governance?
nd8484fb93b7.x: Critical flow channels critical information to a targeted audience, such as corruption data sent to an ombudsman.
nd8484fb93b7.tq: Identify whether information is disseminated broadly or targeted to a specific recipient.
xs: Channelling corruption data to an **ombudsman** is the **critical flow** model, so option **(4)** is correct.
Critical flow sends **critical information** to a **targeted audience**.
**Broadcasting** puts information in the **public domain** for all; **comparative analysis** learns from **best practices**; **e-advocacy** uses **civil-society networks**.
xa: The model belongs to **Arie Halachmi's** five models of e-governance.
**Interactive service** = two-way **G2C** services like filing, payments and feedback.
⚠ The notes flag this trap: corruption data → ombudsman = **critical flow**, not broadcasting.

nf122bbd973d.s: A citizen applies online for an income certificate through UMANG or MeeSeva. This interaction is best classified as:
nf122bbd973d.x: G2C means Government to Citizen interaction. Online birth, income and caste certificates are examples of G2C services.
nf122bbd973d.tq: Identify the recipient of the service before classifying the interaction type.
xs: Applying online for an income certificate is a **G2C** (Government to Citizen) service, so option **(4)** is correct.
The notes list **online birth/income/caste certificates**, **UMANG** and **MeeSeva** as G2C examples.
**G2B** serves businesses (GSTN), **G2G** links departments (NIC, SWAN), **G2E** serves employees (HR tools).
xa: **UMANG** is a single app for central/state services such as tax, **EPF**, gas and passport.
**MeeSeva** ("At your service", **2011**) is AP's single-window G2C service centre.
Halachmi's **interactive service** model is also described as two-way **G2C** service.

n1330ab9b6a3.s: Which of the following is an example of G2B interaction?
o: GSTN and e-Procurement services for businesses
Online HR tools for government employees
Online birth certificate services for citizens
n1330ab9b6a3.x: G2B means Government to Business interaction; MCA portal, GSTN and e-Procurement are examples.
n1330ab9b6a3.tq: Use the beneficiary category—businesses—to distinguish G2B from citizen, employee and inter-government services.
xs: **GSTN and e-Procurement** services for businesses are **G2B** (Government to Business), so option **(1)** is correct.
**e-Office** between departments is **G2G**; online HR tools for employees are **G2E**; online birth certificates are **G2C**.
xa: The **MCA portal** is another G2B example.
⚠ **GSTN** = G2B, while **NIC**, **SWAN** and **e-Office** = G2G.
AP's **e-Procurement** (**2003**) brought online tendering to stop collusion.

nb5558ffbeef.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about types of e-governance interaction?
o: G2G refers to interaction between departments or governments
G2E refers to interaction between different governments
NIC solutions, SWAN and e-Office are G2G examples
Online HR and administrative tools are G2E examples
nb5558ffbeef.x: G2E means services from government to its employees; interaction between governments is G2G.
xa: **G2C** examples: online certificates, **UMANG**, **MeeSeva**.
**G2B** examples: **MCA portal**, **GSTN**, **e-Procurement**.
**e-Taal** is by **NIC**; AP's **APSWAN** is the state's data backbone.

n73e8641a2b0.s: Which one of the following is the correct expansion of UMANG?
o: Universal Mobile Application for National Governance
Universal Mechanism for Administrative and New Governance
Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance
Unified Management Application for New Government
n73e8641a2b0.x: UMANG stands for Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance.
n73e8641a2b0.tq: Test the exact official expansion rather than a look-alike phrase.
xs: UMANG stands for **Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance**, so option **(3)** is correct.
It is a **single app** for central and state services such as tax, **EPF**, gas and passport.
xa: UMANG is accessible through **web, SMS and IVR**.
**DigiLocker** is a cloud locker for documents and certificates, a key **Digital India** initiative.
**MeghRaj** is the GI Cloud (Government of India cloud) hosting government applications.

nd7e4b6c7ee9.s: Which single application gives access to Central and State Government services such as tax, EPF, gas and passport services through web, SMS and IVR?
nd7e4b6c7ee9.x: UMANG offers multiple Central and State services through web, SMS and IVR.
xa: UMANG = **Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance**.
UMANG is a **G2C** example, alongside **MeeSeva** and online certificates.
**DigiLocker** (documents) and **MyGov** (citizen engagement) are other national platforms.

n23e1179a11a.s: Participative governance is most directly associated with which platform?
n23e1179a11a.x: MyGov is a citizen-engagement platform intended to promote participative governance.
n23e1179a11a.tq: Match the governance objective with the platform designed for citizen engagement.
xs: Participative governance is most directly associated with **MyGov**, a citizen-engagement platform, so option **(4)** is correct.
**CSC** are village-level service outlets; **e-Taal** is by **NIC**; **ERSS** is the emergency system on **112**.
xa: **DigiLocker** is a cloud locker for documents and certificates.
**GI Cloud "MeghRaj"** hosts government applications.
Halachmi's **e-advocacy** model also concerns citizen voice: online **civil-society networks** influence decisions.

nc54bbfdb5f6.s: Aadhaar was launched in ____ and the Aadhaar Act was enacted in ____.
nc54bbfdb5f6.x: Aadhaar was launched in 2009; the Aadhaar Act was enacted in 2016 and amended in 2019.
xa: Aadhaar is the **biometric identity** platform.
⚠ Sequence to remember: **2009** launch → **2016** Act → **2019** amendment.
**UPI** (by **NPCI**) is another key national platform; BHIM on UPI came on **30 Dec 2016**.

nf8a69864076.s: In which year were the National Awards for e-Governance (NAeG) started?
nf8a69864076.x: NAeG, instituted by DARPG, began in 2003 and are presented at the National Conference on e-Governance.
xa: The **2025** awards (with **MoPR**) had a first-ever dedicated category for **Gram Panchayats**.
**NAeG 2026**: **17 projects in 7 categories**.
⚠ **28th** NCeG = **Visakhapatnam** (2025); **29th** = **Jaipur** (2026).

n9759ee3b4be.s: Andhra Pradesh's Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) was established in:
n9759ee3b4be.x: RTGS, AP's flagship digital-governance platform using a Data Lake and real-time dashboards, was set up in 2017.
xa: RTGS has a **Command & Control Centre**.
A **Singapore** delegation reviewed RTGS (Jul 2026).
**Mana Mitra** WhatsApp Governance came in Jan **2026**.

nc32773ecf4a.s: The objective of e-Pragati is most closely associated with:
o: A unified state service portal and state enterprise architecture
A network limited to district treasuries
nc32773ecf4a.x: e-Pragati is a unified state service portal and state enterprise architecture. It aims at faceless, paperless and cashless governance.
nc32773ecf4a.tq: Match the broad architecture-level function with the appropriate state initiative.
xs: **e-Pragati** is a **unified state service portal / state enterprise architecture**, so option **(1)** is correct.
A national consumer grievance platform is **e-Jagriti**, not e-Pragati.
xa: **45 more citizen services** were added to e-Pragati.
Its aim: "**faceless, paperless, cashless**" governance.
**APSWAN** is the separate data backbone linking state, district and mandal offices.

nef933affdce.s: The primary purpose of e-Procurement in Andhra Pradesh was to:
o: Register births and deaths through village offices
Conduct online tendering and help stop collusion
Monitor consumer grievances at the national level
nef933affdce.x: The e-Procurement initiative, introduced in 2003, enabled online tendering with the objective of stopping collusion.
nef933affdce.tq: Infer the governance outcome from the service mechanism described.
xs: AP's **e-Procurement** (**2003**) was for **online tendering to stop collusion**, so option **(2)** is correct.
Cloud documents are **DigiLocker**; national consumer grievances are **e-Jagriti** — neither is e-Procurement.
xa: e-Procurement is also a **G2B** example nationally, with **GSTN** and the **MCA portal**.
⚠ AP sequence: **eSeva 2001** → **e-Procurement 2003** → **MeeSeva 2011** → **RTGS 2017**.

n1584786ec2b.s: MeeSeva, meaning “At your service”, was introduced in Andhra Pradesh in:
n1584786ec2b.x: MeeSeva was introduced in 2011 as a single-window G2C service centre initiative.
n1584786ec2b.tq: Distinguish the later single-window service initiative from earlier eSeva and CARD projects.
xs: **MeeSeva** ("At your service") was introduced in **2011**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**2001** was **eSeva** and **2003** was **e-Procurement**.
xa: MeeSeva provides **single-window G2C** service centres.
⚠ Order: **eSeva 2001** → **e-Procurement 2003** → **MeeSeva 2011** → **RTGS 2017**.

ncf73dedcf1c.s: The Jaipur Declaration of the 29th National Conference on e-Governance mainly dealt with:
o: DPI, AI-enabled governance, cybersecurity and data governance
Extension of NeSDA to low-connectivity areas
Launch of the National e-Governance Plan
ncf73dedcf1c.x: The 29th NCeG in Jaipur adopted the Jaipur Declaration on DPI, AI-enabled governance, cybersecurity and data governance. NeSDA extension was in the Visakhapatnam Declaration.
xa: Theme: "**Viksit Bharat 2047: AI-enabled, Data-driven and Secure Digital Governance**".
NAeG 2026: **e-Jagriti** got **Silver** in Category I; **Rohini Gram Panchayat** (Dhule) got **Gold**.

nc61a327d321.s: Which State enacted India's first Right to Services law?
nc61a327d321.x: Madhya Pradesh's Lok Sewa Guarantee Act, 2010 was the first; Bihar followed in 2011.
xa: ⚠ First RTS = **MP 2010**, not Bihar (2011); first social audit law = **Meghalaya 2017**.
RTS features: notified services within **fixed time**, **appeal** on delay, **penalty** on the official.

nb7fa3935231.s: Which State passed the first law making social audit of government programmes mandatory?
nb7fa3935231.x: Meghalaya passed the first state law making social audit of government programmes mandatory in 2017.
nb7fa3935231.tq: Distinguish the first state law from Andhra Pradesh's pioneering implementation institution.
xs: **Meghalaya** (**2017**) passed the first state law making social audit of government programmes mandatory, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Andhra Pradesh** pioneered state-wide **MGNREGA social audits**, but not the first law; **MP** and **Bihar** are linked with RTS laws.
xa: ⚠ First RTS = **MP 2010**; first social audit law = **Meghalaya 2017**.
The **2nd ARC** wanted social audits in **all major welfare schemes**.

nebfb8c2843f.s: The Second ARC recommended that social audits be:
o: Institutionalised in all major welfare schemes
nebfb8c2843f.x: The Second ARC recommended institutionalising social audits in all major welfare schemes, beyond MGNREGA alone.
xa: MGNREGA's social audit is under **Section 17**, conducted by the **Gram Sabha**.
**Meghalaya** (**2017**) passed the first state law on social audit.

n53ae62c35ae.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the First Administrative Reforms Commission?
o: Morarji Desai was associated with it
It recommended a Lokpal in each State and Lokayuktas at the Union level
It recommended a Lokpal at the Union level
n53ae62c35ae.x: It recommended a Lokpal for the Union and Lokayuktas for the States, not the other way round.
xa: The term "Lokpal" was coined by **L.M. Singhvi**.
First Lokayukta: **Maharashtra** (**1971**).
Ombudsman origin: **Sweden, 1809**.

nf3ba875d90f.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six principles of the Citizens' Charter?
nf3ba875d90f.x: The six principles are quality, choice, standards, value, accountability and transparency; participation is not one. The Charter began in the UK in 1991 under John Major.
xa: India adopted the Citizens' Charter in **1997**.
⚠ **Sweden 1809** = ombudsman; **UK 1991** = Citizens' Charter.
The Right to Services idea grew out of the **UK Citizens' Charter**.

nfc95bbcb900.s: A Citizens' Charter is best described as a:
o: Constitutional guarantee enforceable in every court
Statutory code that penalises every service delay
Written commitment on service standards, time-bound delivery and grievance redress
nfc95bbcb900.x: A Citizens' Charter records commitments on service standards, time-bound delivery and grievance redress; it is not by itself legally enforceable.
xa: The **2nd ARC** recommended **statutory status** for charters.
Basic elements: **service standards**, **information about services**, **grievance redress mechanism**, **contact details** of officers.
Exam angle: its main purpose is **time-bound service delivery and grievance redress**.

nfc8f35044a6.s: India adopted the Citizens' Charter in:
nfc8f35044a6.x: India adopted it in 1997; 1991 is its UK origin. DARPG coordinates the charters (goicharters.nic.in).
xa: DARPG also runs **CPGRAMS** (**2007**) and designs **Sevottam**.

n429112fec7f.s: What happened to the Citizens Charter Bill, 2011, on time-bound delivery of services and grievance redress?
o: It lapsed with the dissolution of the Lok Sabha in 2014
It was withdrawn by the Government in 2012
n429112fec7f.x: The Bill never became law; it lapsed when the Lok Sabha was dissolved in 2014.
xa: India adopted Citizens' Charters in **1997**; they remain **non-justiciable**.
The **2nd ARC** recommended statutory backing for charters.

n32f91b037cd.s: The word “Sevottam” is formed from which combination?
n32f91b037cd.x: Sevottam is derived from “Seva” and “Uttam”, conveying excellence in service.
n32f91b037cd.tq: Use the exact word derivation rather than translating the general objective alone.
xs: Sevottam = **Seva + Uttam**, meaning **excellence in service**, so option **(1)** is correct.
It was suggested in the **2nd ARC's 12th report** (Citizen Centric Administration).
xa: Implementation in departments began in **2009**.
It has **3** modules: Citizen's Charter, Public Grievance Redress, Service Delivery Capability.
Certification follows **IS 15700:2005**; **DARPG** designs and promotes the framework.

n573194ac82f.x: Sevottam-compliant certification follows Indian Standard IS 15700:2005.
n573194ac82f.tq: Identify the exact standard number rather than substituting a familiar quality or information-security standard.
xs: Sevottam-compliant certification follows **IS 15700:2005**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**DARPG** designs and promotes the Sevottam framework.
xa: Sevottam was suggested in the **2nd ARC's 12th report**; departmental implementation began in **2009**.
⚠ Sevottam = **3** modules; chairman **Veerappa Moily**.

n0edaf62b480.s: Implementation of the Sevottam model in government departments began in:
n0edaf62b480.x: Sevottam, suggested in the Second ARC's 12th Report and promoted by DARPG, was implemented from 2009; 2005 is when the Second ARC was set up.
xa: Sevottam certification follows **IS 15700:2005**.
The 12th report's chairman was **Veerappa Moily**.

n9b160ba431c.s: Among the following States, which enacted its Right to Services law earliest?
n9b160ba431c.x: The order of enactment among these is Punjab, Assam, Gujarat and Maharashtra.
xa: The first RTS law overall was the **Madhya Pradesh Lok Sewa Guarantee Act, 2010**.
RTS laws provide **appeal** on delay and a **penalty on the responsible official**.

nefaeeae07d8.s: A circular of DARPG dated 23 August 2024 reduced the maximum disposal time for CPGRAMS grievances from:
nefaeeae07d8.x: The DARPG circular dated 23 August 2024 reduced the maximum disposal time from 30 days to 21 days.
nefaeeae07d8.tq: Retain both the original and revised limits; the reduction pair is the tested fact.
xs: The **23 Aug 2024** DARPG circular cut the maximum disposal time from **30 days to 21 days**, so option **(3)** is correct.
It applies to **CPGRAMS** grievances.
xa: Over **71,000** grievances were pending on CPGRAMS (Sep 2025).
**GRAI** ranks ministries on **11 indicators, 4 dimensions**.
CPGRAMS was launched in **2007** by **DARPG**.

n5b5fd1e982e.s: Which of the following is NOT a dimension of the Grievance Redressal Assessment & Index (GRAI)?
n5b5fd1e982e.x: GRAI's four dimensions (11 indicators) are efficiency, feedback, domain and organisational commitment; transparency is not one.
xa: GRAI = **Grievance Redressal Assessment & Index**.
⚠ Disposal limit **30 → 21 days** (**23 Aug 2024**).

n9a5a0fa3b49.s: CPGRAMS, the online grievance platform run by DARPG, stands for:
o: Central Public Grievance Registration and Management System
Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System
Citizen Public Grievance Resolution and Monitoring Scheme
Centralised Pension and Grievance Redress Monitoring System
n9a5a0fa3b49.x: B is the correct expansion: Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System, launched in 2007 by DARPG. A, C and D are invented expansions; D also mixes in pensions, which have a separate platform, CPENGRAMS.
n9a5a0fa3b49.tq: CPGRAMS: Centralised Public Grievance Redress And Monitoring System (2007, DARPG).
xs: CPGRAMS = **Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System**, so option **(2)** is correct.
It was launched in **2007** by **DARPG**; pensioners use the separate **CPENGRAMS**.
xa: Access **24x7** via web, app and **UMANG**; grievances also through **5.1 lakh CSCs**.
**CPGRAMS 7.0** works in many Indian languages.
⚠ CPGRAMS handles **service grievances** (executive); **Lokpal** handles **corruption** (statutory).

ndab4de947c5.s: Which one of the following Andhra Pradesh initiatives provided web-based online receipt, reply and monitoring of grievances at District Collectorates?
ndab4de947c5.x: Prajavani was an earlier Andhra Pradesh initiative for online receipt, reply and monitoring of grievances at District Collectorates.
ndab4de947c5.tq: Match the distinctive operational function with the correct platform rather than the later statewide portals.
xs: **Prajavani** gave web-based online receipt, reply and monitoring of grievances at **District Collectorates**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Meekosam** (**2015**) was a single-window portal; **Spandana** (**2019**) a one-stop grievance platform; **People First** was a distractor in APPSC 2018.
xa: This Prajavani description is from **APPSC 2018**.
AP sequence: **Prajavani → Meekosam → Spandana**.

ne963e106168.s: Meekosam in Andhra Pradesh is a:
o: Single-window portal to lodge grievances and suggestions and track their status
Portal for social audits of MGNREGA works
ne963e106168.x: Meekosam let citizens lodge grievances and suggestions through a single window and track their status.
xa: Meekosam = "**For You**", **2015**, TDP government.
**Data analytics** was added to it.

n773a582c658.s: Spandana was launched in Andhra Pradesh in 2019 during the government of:
n773a582c658.x: Spandana was associated with the YSRCP Government in 2019 and served as a one-stop public grievance redressal platform.
n773a582c658.tq: Discriminate between the two major AP grievance platforms by matching year and government.
xs: **Spandana** was launched in **2019** under the **YSRCP** government, so option **(2)** is correct.
**TDP** is linked with **Meekosam** (**2015**).
xa: Spandana is a **one-stop public grievance redressal** platform.
**APPSC 2021** and **2018** both keyed Spandana as the AP grievance platform.

na758483e742.s: Which of the following is NOT a normal feature of Right to Services legislation?
o: Automatic abolition of all departmental grievance mechanisms
A penalty on the responsible official
A right of appeal in case of delay
Notification of services to be delivered within a fixed time
na758483e742.x: Right to Services laws provide notified services within fixed time limits, appeals against delay and penalties for responsible officials. They do not automatically abolish all other grievance mechanisms.
na758483e742.tq: Identify the option that goes beyond the stated legal features and uses an absolute institutional claim.
xs: **Automatic abolition of all departmental grievance mechanisms** is not an RTS feature, so option **(1)** is the answer.
RTS laws provide **notified services within fixed time**, **appeal on delay** and **penalty on the responsible official**.
xa: The RTS idea grew out of the **UK Citizens' Charter**.
AP too has laws mandating **time-bound delivery** of notified services with appeal and penalty.

n07d3afc1777.s: Under Section 17 of MGNREGA, 2005, social audit of all works is conducted by the:
n07d3afc1777.x: Section 17 makes the Gram Sabha audit all works; social audit is MGNREGA's accountability tool, not a CVC function.
xa: AP's **SSAAT** was set up in **2009** as an independent society.
AP pioneered **state-wide MGNREGA social audits**.

n8cf7c48490a.s: The AP Society for Social Audit, Accountability and Transparency (SSAAT) was set up in:
n8cf7c48490a.x: SSAAT, an independent society, was set up in 2009; 2005 is the year of MGNREGA. AP pioneered state-wide MGNREGA social audits.
xa: SSAAT = **AP Society for Social Audit, Accountability and Transparency**.
Social audit is mandated by **Section 17** of MGNREGA.

nf8f5d75fcf3.s: Sweden's Freedom of the Press Act, regarded as the world's first freedom-of-information law, dates to:
nf8f5d75fcf3.x: Sweden's 1766 Freedom of the Press Act was the first such law; UDHR Article 19 (1948) later recognised the right to seek information.
xa: Order (APPSC 2025): **Sweden → UN → FOI Act → RTI Act**.
⚠ **1766** = Sweden (world first); **1997** = **Tamil Nadu + Goa** (Indian state first).

nb4744cafcd0.s: The Right to Information Act, 2005 received Presidential assent and came fully into force, respectively, on:
nb4744cafcd0.x: B is correct: assent was given on 15 June 2005 and the Act came fully into force on 12 October 2005. A gives the Rajya Sabha passage date as assent; C gives the Lok Sabha passage date as assent; D gives a wrong commencement date.
nb4744cafcd0.tq: RTI: LS 11 May, RS 12 May, assent 15 June, in force 12 Oct 2005.
xs: Assent came on **15 June 2005** and full commencement on **12 October 2005**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**11 May** and **12 May 2005** are the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha passage dates.
xa: ⚠ **11 May** LS → **12 May** RS → **15 June** assent → **12 October** in force.
The Act replaced the **Freedom of Information Act, 2002**.

n1cb51d63d36.s: Under the Right to Information framework, information is provided free of cost to applicants belonging to which category?
o: All applicants below 25 years of age
All applicants belonging to rural areas
n1cb51d63d36.x: Applicants belonging to the below-poverty-line category are entitled to information without payment of the prescribed fee.
n1cb51d63d36.tq: Recall the specific beneficiary category attached to fee exemption.
xs: Information is free / fee waived for **BPL** applicants (**persons below the poverty line**), so option **(4)** is correct.
Only **citizens** can apply.
xa: Requests may be in **Hindi, English or the local official language**.
**Section 6(2)**: **no reason need be given**.

nc3de6d996b5.s: Under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act, which of the following is included within the meaning of ‘information’?
o: Information personally generated by an applicant after filing a request
Only physical records maintained by public authorities
Material in any form, including records, e-mails, opinions, contracts, samples and electronic data
Only final judicial decisions published in the Gazette
nc3de6d996b5.x: Section 2(f) covers material in any form, including records, documents, e-mails, opinions, advice, contracts, samples, models and electronic data.
nc3de6d996b5.tq: Choose the option reflecting the broad statutory wording ‘material in any form’.
xs: Under **Section 2(f)**, information is **material in any form**, including **records, e-mails, opinions, contracts, samples and electronic data** — option **(3)**.
It is not limited to physical records or judicial decisions.
xa: The list also covers **advices, press releases, circulars, orders, logbooks, models**.
It includes information on a **private body accessible to a public authority under law**.
**CBSE v Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011)**: evaluated **answer sheets** are "information".

n181b6c9daaa.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the organisations generally covered by the exemption under Section 24 and the Second Schedule of the Right to Information Act, 2005?
n181b6c9daaa.x: The IB, R&AW and CRPF are among the intelligence and security organisations covered by Section 24. The Central Information Commission is the appellate information body and is not a Section 24 exempt organisation.
n181b6c9daaa.tq: Identify the odd institutional category instead of confusing an exempt security body with the appellate authority.
xs: The **Central Information Commission** is not a Second Schedule body, so option **(2)** is the answer.
The Second Schedule lists **IB, R&AW**, DRI, ED, NCB, BSF, **CRPF**, NSG.
xa: The **CBI** was added in **2011**.
Exception: information on **corruption and human-rights violations** must still be given.

n71a4b732953.s: Which of the following is NOT a permissible ground associated with removal of a State Information Commissioner?
o: Conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude
Disagreement with a decision of the State Government
Proved incapacity after the prescribed inquiry
n71a4b732953.x: Disagreement with a State Government decision is not a stated ground for removal. Insolvency, conviction involving moral turpitude and proved incapacity are recognised grounds.
n71a4b732953.tq: Reject the plausible-sounding ground that is not a statutory basis.
xs: **Disagreement with a decision of the State Government** is not a removal ground, so option **(2)** is the answer.
Valid grounds: proved **misbehaviour/incapacity** (after SC inquiry), **insolvency**, **conviction (moral turpitude)**, **paid employment**, **infirmity**.
xa: Removal is by the **Governor** (Section **17**).
⚠ CIC/SIC = **up to 10** ICs; CVC = **two** Vigilance Commissioners, **4 years or age 65**.

naa10388b885.s: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended that the RTI framework should be linked firmly with
naa10388b885.x: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended firmly linking RTI with whistle-blower protection to prevent victimisation of those who disclose information.
naa10388b885.tq: Identify the protection mechanism that directly addresses victimisation of information-seekers.
xs: The 2nd ARC wanted RTI linked firmly with **whistle-blower protection law**, to prevent victimisation — option **(4)**.
It also asked to **narrow Section 8** and **maximise Section 4** disclosure.
xa: The **Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014** is not operationalised.
The call was repeated on **30 Jul 2026**.

neb41a7b7dbd.s: Which was the first Indian State to enact a Right to Information law (1997)?
neb41a7b7dbd.x: Tamil Nadu enacted the first Indian State RTI law in 1997. Sweden had the world's first RTI law (1766), and Wajahat Habibullah was the first CIC.
xa: **Goa** passed its law the same year as Tamil Nadu (**1997**).
Order: **Sweden → UN → FOI Act → RTI Act**.

nca6b0ff6c16.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or institutional concern relating to the functioning of the RTI regime?
o: Excessive speed in disposal of all RTI applications
nca6b0ff6c16.x: The identified concerns include appeal backlogs, vacancies, misuse of Section 8 and threats to activists. Excessive speed in disposal is not listed as a criticism.
nca6b0ff6c16.tq: Find the option that reverses the documented governance problem.
xs: **Excessive speed in disposal of all RTI applications** is not a concern — the problem is delay — so option **(3)** is the answer.
The listed criticisms are **backlog of appeals/delays**, **vacancies in Commissions**, misuse of **Section 8** and **threats/attacks on activists**.
xa: Over **4 lakh** appeals/complaints were pending (Jul 2026).
Another criticism: **weakened autonomy** after **2019**.
The **Satark Nagrik Sangathan 2025** report flagged gaps as the Act turns **20**.

n5198e49e8a2.s: The right to know has been judicially read into which Article of the Constitution?
n5198e49e8a2.x: Courts have read the right to know into Article 19(1)(a), and also Article 21, in cases like State of U.P. v. Raj Narain and S.P. Gupta.
xa: The RTI Act gives a **statutory right** giving effect to this fundamental right.
**CBSE v Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011)**: evaluated **answer sheets** are "information".

nc852fcce156.s: The Preamble of the RTI Act links an informed citizenry and transparency mainly with:
o: Containing corruption and holding governments accountable
Making every document public without exception
nc852fcce156.x: The Preamble ties informed citizenship and transparency to containing corruption and ensuring accountability, harmonised with other public interests.
xa: Other listed aims: participation and **better service delivery**.
Exemptions under **Section 8** carry out this balance.

ne8e73f73335.s: Section 11 of the RTI Act, 2005 deals with:
o: Constitution of the State Information Commission
ne8e73f73335.x: Section 11 covers third-party information; Section 19 covers appeals and Section 15 the SIC.
xa: Third-party information has a time limit of **40 days**.
**Section 20** = penalties on PIOs.

n5824edc4bd7.s: Under Section 2(h) of the RTI Act, public authorities include:
o: Only bodies created directly by the Constitution
Only bodies established by an Act of Parliament
Bodies set up by law or government notification, and bodies substantially financed or controlled by government
n5824edc4bd7.x: Section 2(h) covers bodies set up by law or notification and those substantially financed or controlled by government, not just constitutional bodies.
xa: NGOs **substantially financed** by government are public authorities (**DAV College Trust, 2019**).
⚠ The CIC held **BCCI is not a public authority** (May 2026).

n8ac107a5fd8.s: Under Section 6(2) of the RTI Act, an applicant seeking information:
o: Must state the reasons for seeking it
Need not give any reason for seeking it
n8ac107a5fd8.x: No reasons are needed; applications may be made by post, in person or by e-mail, in Hindi, English or the local official language.
xa: ⚠ The **Madras High Court (2014)** remark that an applicant should state a reason was later **withdrawn**.
Normal reply time under **Section 7**: **30 days**.

n4f4802dbc0c.s: Which Section of the RTI Act, 2005 provides for the constitution of the Central Information Commission?
n4f4802dbc0c.x: Section 12 constitutes the CIC; Section 15 the SIC, Section 5 covers PIOs and Section 9 copyright-based rejection.
xa: PIOs are designated by each **public authority**, not by the President or Governor.
**Section 11** deals with third-party information.

n5279b672cc0.s: Under Section 24 of the RTI Act, listed intelligence and security organisations are still not excluded from disclosing information on:
n5279b672cc0.x: Section 24 generally excludes listed organisations, but information on corruption and human-rights violations is not excluded.
xa: Human-rights information from such bodies: **45 days**, with **Commission approval**.
The **CBI** was added to the Second Schedule in **2011**.

n4d5c5abf3b8.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the ‘right to information’ under Section 2(j)?
o: Compelling an authority to create a new explanation or opinion
Taking notes, extracts or certified copies
Inspection of works, documents and records
n4d5c5abf3b8.x: Section 2(j) includes inspection, notes, extracts, certified copies, certified samples and electronic information. It does not require an authority to create a new explanation or opinion.
n4d5c5abf3b8.tq: Find the option that demands creation of information rather than access to existing information.
xs: **Compelling an authority to create a new explanation or opinion** is not part of **Section 2(j)**, so option **(1)** is the answer.
2(j) covers **inspection** of work, documents, records; **notes, extracts or certified copies**; **certified samples**; and electronic information.
xa: ⚠ **2(f)** = "information"; **2(h)** = "public authority"; **2(j)** = "right to information".
**CBSE v Aditya Bandopadhyay** also warned that impractical demands should not **clog administration**.

ncaaafb9290d.s: Under the RTI Act, a second appeal to the Central or State Information Commission is ordinarily filed within:
ncaaafb9290d.x: The second appeal lies within ninety days; the first appeal is filed within thirty days.
xa: Appeals are under **Section 19**: First Appellate Authority, then Information Commission.
Life or liberty requests: **48 hours**.

nacf8ba41b3e.s: Under Section 8(3) of the RTI Act, most exempt information becomes disclosable after:
nacf8ba41b3e.x: The Section 8(3) rule is 20 years, with exceptions such as cabinet deliberations; Section 8(2) is the public-interest override.
xa: **Section 9**: copyright of a person other than the State.

nf89b7c6a883.s: The CIC has ruled that which of the following is NOT a public authority under Section 2(h) of the RTI Act?
o: Office of the Chief Justice of India
An NGO substantially financed by Government
nf89b7c6a883.x: The CIC ruled that the BCCI is not a public authority under Section 2(h); the CJI's office and substantially financed NGOs are.
xa: BCCI is not **substantially financed** by government, per the CIC.
**Zee Telefilms v. UoI (2005)**: BCCI performs public functions but is not "State" under **Art. 12**.

n7b79d0d82a2.s: The demand to bring political parties under the RTI Act is intended to:
o: Check corruption and crony capitalism and scrutinise illegal foreign contributions
n7b79d0d82a2.x: Activists cite checking corruption and crony capitalism, scrutiny of illegal foreign contributions and parties' state privileges such as free Doordarshan airtime.
xa: The **CIC (June 2013)** cited indirect government funding: land, bungalows, free airtime.
**2026 demand**: a **transparent, auditable electoral-funding system**.

n28fda1b62ce.s: How many political parties were declared public authorities by the CIC under the RTI Act?
n28fda1b62ce.x: The CIC declared six parties public authorities; they did not comply, and the 2005 Act does not name political parties.
xa: ⚠ No final **2018** SC ruling made parties disclose funding under RTI.
The RTI (Amendment) Bill **2013** to exclude parties **lapsed**.

n2a4feafc279.s: Which of the following cannot be appointed a State Information Commissioner?
o: A person of eminence in public life with knowledge of law
A person of eminence in public life with knowledge of journalism
A person of eminence in public life with knowledge of administration
n2a4feafc279.x: A sitting MP cannot be appointed; the appointee must be eminent in public life and hold no office of profit.
xa: They also cannot be connected with a **political party** or carry on a business or profession.
Term now **3 years** under the **2019** Rules.

n95c1d68895a.s: The Central and State Information Commissions are:
o: Statutory bodies under the RTI Act
Bodies under the Protection of Human Rights Act
n95c1d68895a.x: Both are statutory bodies under the RTI Act, with civil-court powers, hearing second appeals and complaints.
xa: Composition: Chief IC + **up to 10** ICs at both levels.
The **2019 amendment** let the Centre fix tenure and salaries, raising **autonomy** concerns.

nf60b1fd8d82.s: In penalty proceedings under Section 20 of the RTI Act, the burden of proof lies on the:
nf60b1fd8d82.x: The PIO bears the burden of proof and must be heard before a penalty; the Commission may also recommend disciplinary action.
xa: Penalty: **₹250 per day**, up to **₹25,000**.

n5185f14b5e5.s: Under Section 19(8)(b) of the RTI Act, the Information Commission may require the public authority to:
o: Compensate the applicant for any loss or detriment suffered
Pay a penalty directly to the Information Commissioner
n5185f14b5e5.x: Section 19(8)(b) lets the Commission require the public authority to compensate the applicant for any loss or other detriment suffered.
xa: **Section 19** deals with **appeals** (two-tier).

n059100a39ea.s: Before the 2019 amendment, the salary of a State Information Commissioner was linked to that of the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
n059100a39ea.x: A State IC's salary was linked to the Chief Secretary's, while the CIC's equalled the Chief Election Commissioner's.
xa: After **2019**, salaries are fixed by the **Central Government**.
The term is now **3 years** under the **2019** Rules.

ne2b3dc57d96.s: In CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011), the Supreme Court held that evaluated answer sheets are:
o: Held in a fiduciary capacity and hence exempt
Accessible only through a court order
ne2b3dc57d96.x: Evaluated answer sheets are information that examinees can inspect, and the examining body does not hold them in a fiduciary capacity.
xa: In **Jun 2026** the CIC rejected CBSE's fiduciary plea on answer-book procurement data.
⚠ Answer sheets = information (**2011**); service record/tax returns = personal information (**2012**).

n21651cd0626.s: Under Section 6(2) of the RTI Act, an applicant seeking information:
o: Must state the reason for the request
Need not give any reason for the request
n21651cd0626.x: Section 6(2) says no reason need be given; a 2014 Madras High Court observation requiring reasons was withdrawn for this reason.
xa: This was a **UPPSC 2014** key.
Requests may be by post, in person or e-mail, in **Hindi, English** or the local official language.

nc5f6018b597.s: The violation identified during the Andhra Pradesh Information Commission’s statewide inspection primarily related to
o: Section 7 and payment of RTI fees
nc5f6018b597.x: The inspection found violations of Section 4(1)(b), which concerns proactive or suo motu disclosure of information.
nc5f6018b597.tq: Match the section number with its exact RTI subject.
xs: The AP inspection found **Section 4(1)(b)** (**proactive disclosure**) violations — option **(1)**.
It covered **258 offices in 18 districts** over two days.
xa: It was led by AP Chief Information Commissioner **Vajja Srinivasa Rao** (Jul 2026).
Police denied him entry at **Medikonduru** police station.

neb873b27e57.s: Section 4 of the Right to Information Act, 2005 is primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Imposition of penalty on every delayed applicant
Compulsory adjudication of all RTI appeals by courts
Exemption of personal information from disclosure
Suo motu disclosure by public authorities
neb873b27e57.x: Section 4 mandates proactive or suo motu disclosure by public authorities, reducing the need for citizens to file separate applications.
neb873b27e57.tq: Match the statutory section with its distinctive function.
xs: **Section 4** mandates **suo motu disclosure** by public authorities, so option **(4)** is correct.
Personal information exemption is **8(1)(j)**; penalties are **Section 20** and fall on PIOs, not applicants.
xa: **4(1)(b)** lists what must be published.
The **2nd ARC** wanted maximum information **automatically in the public domain**.

n8c74b5521d4.s: The Second ARC recommended that the Section 8 exemptions of the RTI Act be interpreted:
n8c74b5521d4.x: The Second ARC wanted Section 8 exemptions read narrowly and maximum information placed in the public domain automatically.
xa: It also asked to **protect activists** and link RTI with **whistle-blower protection law**.

n39e5d403aa8.s: Under the RTI Act, information concerning the life or liberty of a person must be supplied within:
n39e5d403aa8.x: Life or liberty cases must be answered within 48 hours; routing through an APIO gives 35 days and third-party cases 40 days.
xa: Normal reply by PIO: **30 days**.
⚠ "Reply in **45 days**" is the standard wrong pair (APPSC 2025).

n97bf86e8b7d.s: Section 44(3) of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 altered Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act by
o: making personal information a blanket exemption and dropping the earlier public-interest override
transferring all RTI appeals to the Data Protection Board
requiring every applicant to disclose the reason for seeking personal information
removing all exemptions relating to personal information
n97bf86e8b7d.x: Section 44(3) rewrote Section 8(1)(j) to exempt personal information outright, dropping the earlier test concerning relationship to public activity, unwarranted invasion of privacy and the public-interest override.
n97bf86e8b7d.tq: Contrast the original conditional privacy exemption with the amended blanket exemption.
xs: **Section 44(3)** of the DPDP Act **made personal information a blanket exemption** and **dropped the public-interest override** — option **(1)**.
It also dropped the "**no relationship to public activity**" test.
xa: The original 8(1)(j) withheld personal information only if unrelated to public activity or an **unwarranted invasion of privacy**.
The **Supreme Court** referred the challenge to a **Constitution Bench** (Feb 2026).

n7c12805222e.s: When did the Supreme Court refer the challenge to the DPDP amendment of the RTI Act to a Constitution Bench?
n7c12805222e.x: The amendment was notified in November 2025 and the challenge was referred to a Constitution Bench in February 2026; on 7 August 2026 the Court agreed to examine repugnancy.
xa: The SC noted its "**constitutional sensitivity**".

n3993fa4fffb.s: The right created by the Right to Information Act, 2005 is a:
o: Fundamental Right under a separate Article
Constitutional right of public officials only
n3993fa4fffb.x: The Act creates a statutory right; separately, the Supreme Court has read the right to know into Article 19(1)(a).
xa: Only **citizens** can apply under the Act (**Section 3**).
Judicial roots: **Raj Narain** and **S.P. Gupta** cases; Art. 21 is also cited.

n33beadc1e90.s: A State Information Commissioner can be removed by the Governor for proved misbehaviour only after an inquiry by the:
n33beadc1e90.x: Removal for proved misbehaviour or incapacity is by the Governor after a Supreme Court inquiry on the Governor's reference.
xa: At the Centre, the **President** removes after a Supreme Court inquiry.
The **CVC** is also removed by the President after a **Supreme Court inquiry**.

nadf6f618712.s: Besides the Chief Information Commissioner, an Information Commission may have up to how many Information Commissioners?
nadf6f618712.x: Both the Central and State Information Commissions have a Chief Information Commissioner and up to ten Information Commissioners.
xa: The **President** appoints the CIC (**Section 12**); the **Governor** appoints the SIC (**Section 15**).
⚠ CIC/SIC = **up to 10** members; CVC = **two** Vigilance Commissioners.
Both are **statutory bodies** with **powers of a civil court**.

n9be1bc6e645.s: Under the original RTI Act, the term of an Information Commissioner was:
o: Three years or until the age of 65
Five years or until the age of 62
Six years or until the age of 65
Five years or until the age of 65
n9be1bc6e645.x: The original term was five years or age 65, with no reappointment; since 2019 the Centre notifies it, and the 2019 Rules fix three years.
xa: The **2019 amendment** also let the Centre fix salaries.
Critics say this **weakens the Commissions' autonomy**.

n087f034070e.s: Which one of the following is NOT a member of the committee that recommends appointment of the State Chief Information Commissioner?
o: Leader of Opposition in the Legislative Assembly
A State Cabinet Minister nominated by the Chief Minister
Chief Justice of the High Court
n087f034070e.x: D is correct: the Chief Justice of the High Court is not on the SIC selection committee (the trap in the G2 2025 key). The committee is the Chief Minister (chair) (A), the Leader of Opposition in the Assembly (B) and a State Cabinet Minister nominated by the CM (C). The Governor then appoints.
n087f034070e.tq: SIC panel: CM + LoP + Minister; no judge.
xs: The **Chief Justice of the High Court** is **not** on the SIC selection committee, so option **(4)** is the answer.
The committee is the **Chief Minister (chair)**, the **Leader of Opposition** in the Assembly and a **State Cabinet Minister** nominated by the CM.
xa: This was a **G2 2025** key.
At the Centre: **PM (chair)**, **Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha**, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM.
The **Governor** appoints the SIC (**Section 15**).

n91b889ab49f.s: Members of the Central Vigilance Commission hold office for:
o: 5 years or until the age of 65
4 years or until the age of 65
3 years or until the age of 65
6 years or until the age of 65
n91b889ab49f.x: The CVC term is 4 years or age 65; 5 years or 65 was the original Information Commission term.
xa: ⚠ CIC/SIC = **up to 10** ICs, term now **3 years**.
CVC members can also be removed on grounds like **insolvency**.

nff1d04ab3c7.s: The penalty that may be imposed on a Public Information Officer under Section 20 is
nff1d04ab3c7.x: Section 20 provides for a penalty of ₹250 per day, subject to a maximum of ₹25,000, along with possible disciplinary action.
nff1d04ab3c7.tq: Retain both parts of a statutory penalty: the daily rate and the maximum ceiling.
xs: Section 20 penalty is **₹250 per day**, **subject to** a maximum of **₹25,000**, so option **(3)** is correct.
It runs until the application is received or the information furnished.
xa: It is imposed by the **CIC/SIC** on the PIO.
The Commission can also recommend **disciplinary action**.

n99598db4293.s: The principal criticism of the 2019 changes relating to the tenure and salaries of Information Commissions is that they
o: removed the power of the Commissions to impose penalties
weakened the autonomy of the Commissions by placing tenure and pay in executive hands
made all decisions of the Commissions subject to approval by political parties
n99598db4293.x: The criticism is that executive control over tenure and remuneration may weaken the institutional autonomy of the Information Commissions.
n99598db4293.tq: Connect the institutional design change with its governance consequence.
xs: The 2019 changes **weakened the Commissions' autonomy by placing tenure and pay in executive hands**, so option **(2)** is correct.
They did not remove penalty powers or abolish the CIC.
xa: Original term: **5 years** or age **65**; now **3 years** under the 2019 Rules.
"Weakened autonomy after **2019**" is listed among the Act's criticisms.

n069eaebd860.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the six national political parties declared public authorities by the Central Information Commission in June 2013?
n069eaebd860.x: The six parties were INC, BJP, CPI, CPI(M), NCP and BSP. The Aam Aadmi Party was not included in that CIC order.
n069eaebd860.tq: Find the odd name by recalling the complete six-party list.
xs: The **Aam Aadmi Party** was not among the six, so option **(2)** is the answer.
The six were **INC, BJP, CPI, CPI(M), NCP, BSP**.
xa: The CIC declared them **public authorities** under **2(h)** in **June 2013**.
The parties **did not comply**; the issue is pending before the Supreme Court.

nd1b9131e1f6.s: In the Zee Telefilms case, the Supreme Court held that the BCCI:
o: Performs public functions but is not 'State' under Article 12
Is 'State' and a public authority under the RTI Act
nd1b9131e1f6.x: Zee Telefilms held that BCCI performs public functions but is not State under Article 12; a later CIC ruling held it is not a public authority under Section 2(h).
xa: By contrast, NGOs **substantially financed** by government are public authorities (**DAV College Trust, 2019**).
The **CJI's office** is a public authority (**2019**).

nb137efd65dd.s: As of July 2026, the approximate number of RTI appeals and complaints pending across Information Commissions was reported to be
nb137efd65dd.x: More than 4 lakh RTI appeals and complaints were reported to be pending across Information Commissions as of July 2026.
nb137efd65dd.tq: Use the exact numerical figure rather than being distracted by nearby order-of-magnitude options.
xs: Over **4 lakh** RTI appeals/complaints were pending across commissions (Jul 2026), so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Do not mix with **26,000** — the figure cited by the Congress president for 2025.
xa: The **massive backlog of appeals** causes long delays.
**Chronic vacancies** in CIC/SICs add to pendency.

n2cc458d9e0e.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 suggested re-examination of the RTI framework mainly in the context of exempting which of the following categories of information?
o: Only information supplied by private bodies
All information held by local authorities
All records relating to public expenditure and contracts
Confidential service records and draft or exploratory policy discussions
n2cc458d9e0e.x: The Economic Survey suggested considering exemptions for confidential service records and draft or exploratory policy discussions, along with a possible ministerial veto.
n2cc458d9e0e.tq: Match the policy proposal with the specific categories named in it.
xs: The **Economic Survey 2025-26** sought to exempt **confidential service records and draft/exploratory policy discussions** — option **(4)**.
It floated a possible "**ministerial veto**".
xa: It called India's RTI regime "**uniquely broad**", with a **chilling effect** on honest decision-making.
The **Opposition** called it dilution of accountability.

n13cd950a3be.s: More than how many RTI activists were reported to have been killed by July 2026?
n13cd950a3be.x: Reports cited that more than 100 RTI activists had been killed by July 2026.
n13cd950a3be.tq: Recall the reported threshold and avoid confusing it with lower estimates.
xs: **More than 100** RTI activists have been killed, so option **(4)** is correct.
Threats include **harassment, legal intimidation and physical attacks**.
xa: The **Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014** is not operationalised; a **2015** amendment bill sought to dilute it.
The call to implement the 2nd ARC whistle-blower recommendations was repeated on **30 Jul 2026**.

ncbdae6ce529.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the Doctrine of Pleasure in relation to services?
ncbdae6ce529.x: Article 310 embodies the Doctrine of Pleasure.
xs: The **Doctrine of Pleasure** is in **Article 310**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Article 311** = safeguards; **312** = All India Services; **309** = recruitment and conditions of service.
xa: ⚠ **310** = pleasure; **311** = safeguards; **312** = AIS.
Article 311: no dismissal by an authority **subordinate** to the appointing one; **inquiry and hearing** required.

n86612ebe33b.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the All India Services?
n86612ebe33b.x: Article 312 concerns All India Services; 309 covers recruitment, 311 safeguards and 320 PSC functions.
xa: **Article 315** = PSCs for Union and States; **316** = appointment and term; **317** = removal and suspension.
**Article 323** = reports of PSCs.

n233eba7d1ab.s: A member of a Public Service Commission is proposed to be removed for misbehaviour. Which procedure is constitutionally relevant?
o: Removal by the Chief Minister after consultation with the State Cabinet
An inquiry by the Supreme Court before removal for misbehaviour
Removal by the Governor without any inquiry
Removal by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha after a simple majority vote
n233eba7d1ab.x: B is correct: a member of a Public Service Commission can be removed for misbehaviour only after an inquiry by the Supreme Court. A, C and D are wrong because neither the Chief Minister, nor the Governor without inquiry, nor the Lok Sabha Speaker by a vote can remove a PSC member.
n233eba7d1ab.tq: Apply the constitutional safeguard by asking which authority performs the inquiry.
xs: A PSC member can be removed for misbehaviour only after **an inquiry by the Supreme Court**, so option **(2)** is correct.
Removal and suspension of members is under **Article 317**.
xa: **Article 316** covers appointment and term of members.
UPSC began in **1950**, from the **Federal PSC** under the **GoI Act 1935**.

nbd338103c78.s: A member of the Union Public Service Commission holds office for:
o: 5 years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier
6 years or until the age of 62, whichever is earlier
6 years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier
4 years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier
nbd338103c78.x: C is correct: a UPSC member serves 6 years or until 65. B is the limit for State and Joint PSC members (6 years or 62). A was the original Information Commissioner term; D is the CVC term.
xs: A UPSC member serves **6 years or until 65**, whichever earlier, so option **(3)** is correct.
**62** is the age limit for **SPSC/JSPSC** members.
xa: ⚠ UPSC **65** vs SPSC/JSPSC **62**.
The **JSPSC** is a **statutory** body.
UPSC came in **1950**, succeeding the Federal PSC of the **GoI Act 1935**.

n9ae7ec2e135.s: The tenure system under the Central Staffing Scheme refers to:
o: Permanent transfer of every State officer to the Union Government
A fixed term of service at the Centre followed by return to the State cadre
Rotation only among district offices within a State
Appointment of Central officers exclusively to local governments
n9ae7ec2e135.x: Under the tenure system, State-cadre officers serve a fixed term at the Centre and then return to their State cadre.
n9ae7ec2e135.tq: Distinguish a fixed central deputation followed by return from permanent transfer.
xs: The tenure system means **a fixed term at the Centre followed by return to the State cadre**, so option **(2)** is correct.
It runs under DoPT's **Central Staffing Scheme**.
xa: The **split system** separates **policy** (Secretariat) from **implementation** (field agencies).
⚠ IAS cadre control = **DoPT**, not MHA.

n69ac5ade99d.s: The split system in civil administration refers to the separation of:
o: Policy formulation in the Secretariat from implementation through field agencies
n69ac5ade99d.x: The split system separates policy functions performed by the Secretariat from implementation carried out by field agencies.
n69ac5ade99d.tq: Discriminate between policy and implementation functions.
xs: The split system separates **policy formulation in the Secretariat** from **implementation through field agencies**, so option **(2)** is correct.
This was a **BPSC 2021** question.
xa: The **tenure system**: state-cadre officers serve a fixed term at the Centre, then return.
Civil servants act as **policy advisers, implementers and stabilisers**.

ndfa1965c85d.s: The cadre-controlling authority for the Indian Police Service is the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
ndfa1965c85d.x: MHA controls the IPS cadre; DoPT controls the IAS and MoEFCC the Indian Forest Service.
xa: ⚠ IAS = **DoPT**, not MHA.
All India Services are under **Article 312**.

nc926ec83769.s: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Max Weber’s ideal-type bureaucracy based on legal-rational authority?
o: Personal patronage as the primary basis of appointment
nc926ec83769.x: Weber’s ideal-type bureaucracy is based on hierarchy, rules, impersonality, specialisation, merit and written files. Personal patronage is not its defining basis.
nc926ec83769.tq: Identify the option that belongs to a contrasting patronage system.
xs: **Personal patronage as the primary basis of appointment** is not a Weberian feature, so option **(1)** is the answer.
Weber's ideal-type bureaucracy rests on **legal-rational authority**: **hierarchy**, rules, **impersonality**, specialisation, **merit**, **written files**.
xa: **Patronage** bureaucracy is one of **F. Morstein Marx's** four types, with guardian, caste and merit.
Morstein Marx wrote **The Administrative State**.

na170373f111.s: Which of the following sets correctly represents the types of bureaucracy identified by F. Morstein Marx?
na170373f111.x: F. Morstein Marx identified guardian, caste, patronage and merit bureaucracies in The Administrative State.
na170373f111.tq: Recall the exact four-part typology without confusing it with Weber’s authority types.
xs: **F. Morstein Marx** classified bureaucracies as **guardian, caste, patronage and merit**, so option **(2)** is correct.
"Legal, traditional, charismatic" are types of authority, not his bureaucracy types.
xa: His book: **The Administrative State**.
**Max Weber** gave the **ideal-type** bureaucracy based on **legal-rational authority**.

nb4a74e0fb91.s: The B.S. Baswan Committee, constituted in 2016, examined issues relating to:
o: The introduction of the essay paper alone
Age limit, number of attempts and examination pattern
The three-stage examination system introduced in 1979
nb4a74e0fb91.x: The B.S. Baswan Committee examined the age limit, number of attempts and examination pattern for the Civil Services Examination.
nb4a74e0fb91.tq: Beware of the word “only” and identify the option that captures all the stated areas of review.
xs: The **Baswan** Committee (**2016**) examined CSE **eligibility, age limit, attempts and syllabus**, so option **(3)** is correct.
The essay paper came from **Satish Chandra** (**1989**); the three-stage exam from **Kothari**.
xa: **P.C. Hota** (**2004**): domain expertise, **lateral entry**, appraisal.
Baswan is the latest in the list: Kothari → Satish Chandra → Alagh → Hota → Baswan.

nf1f5c3ffe9a.s: The committee set up by the UPSC in July 2000 to review the Civil Services Examination scheme was headed by:
nf1f5c3ffe9a.x: Standard sources identify the July 2000 committee set up by the UPSC with Y.K. Alagh. Sukhadeo Thorat is named in a conflicting examination key, but the standard identification is Alagh.
nf1f5c3ffe9a.tq: Resolve a look-alike attribution by focusing on the standard committee-chairman association.
xs: The UPSC's **July 2000** committee is named after **Y.K. Alagh** in standard sources, so option **(1)** is correct.
It reviewed the **CSE scheme** (**2000-01**).
xa: ⚠ An **MPPSC 2023** key names **Sukhadeo Thorat** — the Thorat vs Alagh trap.
**Satish Chandra** (**1989**) and **Kothari** (**1976**) were earlier.

n16f3aa90574.s: Lateral entry into the civil services was supported by:
o: Neither the Second ARC nor the Hota Committee
Both the Second ARC and the Hota Committee
n16f3aa90574.x: Both the Second ARC and the P.C. Hota Committee supported lateral entry; a UPSC-led, merit-based process has been suggested for domain experts.
xa: **Hota** (**2004**) also covered domain expertise and appraisal.
There is a parallel case for **dedicated scientific cadres**.

ncf020b495b5.s: Fixed tenure and Civil Services Boards to insulate civil servants from political pressure were recommended in which case?
ncf020b495b5.x: Fixed tenure and Civil Services Boards are associated with the T.S.R. Subramanian case and the Second ARC.
xa: Neutrality is required by the **AIS (Conduct) Rules 1968** and **CCS (Conduct) Rules 1964**.
The **Chhattisgarh** circular (**21 Apr 2026**) reopened the neutrality debate.

nfcd205d87b2.s: Who chaired the Second Administrative Reforms Commission constituted in 2005?
nfcd205d87b2.x: M. Veerappa Moily chaired the 2nd ARC (31 August 2005), which gave 15 reports, the first on RTI as the 'Master Key to Good Governance'.
xa: Moily was later succeeded by **V. Ramachandran**.
It is called the "**Bible**" of administrative reform.

na6935528758.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation associated with the Second Administrative Reforms Commission?
o: Lateral entry at the Joint Secretary level
Abolition of right to public services laws
na6935528758.x: The Commission recommended right to public services laws, not their abolition. It also supported lateral entry, performance-based appraisal and rotational postings.
na6935528758.tq: Find the option that reverses a recorded recommendation.
xs: **Abolition of right to public services laws** was not recommended — the 2nd ARC backed such laws — so option **(4)** is the answer.
It recommended **lateral entry** at Joint Secretary level, **performance-based appraisal** and **rotational postings**.
xa: Other recommendations: a **code of ethics** + a **Public Service Bill**, and a **Department of e-Governance**.
Chairman: **M. Veerappa Moily**; **15 reports**.

n9b89ed41572.s:
Civil servants perform which of the following roles in public administration?
1. Policy advisers
2. Implementers of public policy
3. Stabilisers of the administrative system
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
n9b89ed41572.x: Civil servants serve as policy advisers, implementers and stabilisers in public administration; therefore, all three statements are correct.
n9b89ed41572.tq: Recognise the complementary roles of civil servants instead of treating advice, implementation and stability as mutually exclusive.
xs: All three roles are correct, so option **(4)** is correct.
Civil servants act as **policy advisers**, **implementers** and **stabilisers**.
xa: Sardar Patel called the civil services the **"steel frame of India"** (**1947**).
The **split system** separates policy (Secretariat) from implementation (field agencies).

n07c7db8fcc2.s: Which rules require political neutrality and integrity from the concerned civil servants?
o: Civil Services Examination Rules, 1968 and Election Rules, 1964
All India Services Act, 1935 and CCS Rules, 1947
n07c7db8fcc2.x: The AIS (Conduct) Rules, 1968 and CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 require political neutrality and integrity.
n07c7db8fcc2.tq: Discriminate between conduct rules and recruitment or constitutional provisions.
xs: The **AIS (Conduct) Rules, 1968** and **CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964** require political neutrality and integrity, so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ AIS Conduct Rules **1968**; CCS Conduct Rules **1964**; AP CCA Rules **1991**.
xa: An AP section officer was dismissed under **Rule 9, AP CCA Rules 1991** for campaigning in the **2024** elections.
A **Chhattisgarh** circular (**21 Apr 2026**) barring party membership was quickly withdrawn.

n9c8b1d2be78.s: Civil Services Day is observed on 21 April because on 21 April 1947:
o: The Federal Public Service Commission was renamed UPSC
Sardar Patel addressed the first probationers at Metcalfe House, Delhi
The first All India Service was created
The UPSC was established in New Delhi
n9c8b1d2be78.x: On 21 April 1947, Sardar Patel addressed the first probationers at Metcalfe House in Delhi and described civil servants as the “steel frame of India.”
n9c8b1d2be78.tq: Link the observance date to its historical origin and speaker.
xs: On **21 Apr 1947**, **Sardar Patel addressed the first probationers at Metcalfe House, Delhi**, so option **(2)** is correct.
He called them the **"steel frame of India"**.
xa: The **17th CSD** was held on **21 Apr 2025** at **Vigyan Bhawan**.
UPSC itself came in **1950**.

n801263a3d30.s: The Santhanam Committee was the Committee on:
n801263a3d30.x: The Santhanam Committee was the Committee on Prevention of Corruption; the CBI followed in 1963 and the CVC in 1964.
xa: The CVC is now statutory under the **CVC Act 2003**.
The CBI rests on the **DSPE Act 1946**.

n754bb7c7d4a.s: The Whistle Blowers Protection Act was enacted in which year?
n754bb7c7d4a.x: The Whistle Blowers Protection Act was enacted in 2014. The reference to 2011 relates to the year in which the Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha.
n754bb7c7d4a.tq: Distinguish the year of enactment from the year associated with the Bill.
xs: The Whistle Blowers Protection Act was enacted in **2014** (assent **9 May 2014**), so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Older notes call it the "**2011** Act" — the year the Bill passed the Lok Sabha.
xa: A **2015** Amendment Bill passed the Lok Sabha but **lapsed in 2019**.
Complaints must be made within **7 years**.

n90cc37e7e83.s: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is a:
o: Non-constitutional, non-statutory body linked to the DSPE Act, 1946
Statutory body under the CVC Act, 2003
Judicial body under the Ministry of Law
n90cc37e7e83.x: The CBI is a non-constitutional, non-statutory body whose legal basis is linked to the DSPE Act, 1946.
xa: CBI is under the **Ministry of Personnel**.
It needs state **consent** under **Sec 6 DSPE Act**.

n065db2b659b.s: The selection committee for the Director of the CBI includes the:
o: Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India or nominee, and Leader of Opposition
President, Vice-President and Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and Chief Ministers of all States
Chief Justice of India, Attorney General and Cabinet Secretary
n065db2b659b.x: The Director of the CBI is chosen by a committee comprising the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India or the Chief Justice’s nominee, and the Leader of Opposition.
n065db2b659b.tq: Ask who performs the appointment function and avoid swapping constitutional offices.
xs: The CBI Director is chosen by the **PM, CJI (or nominee) and LoP**, so option **(1)** is correct.
The CBI rests on the **DSPE Act 1946**, under the **Ministry of Personnel**.
xa: The CBI was set up in **1963** on **Santhanam Committee** advice.
It needs state **consent** under **Sec 6 DSPE Act**.

nb0c1d1e5fd6.s: The Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 came into force on:
nb0c1d1e5fd6.x: The Prevention of Money Laundering Act came into force on 1 July 2005.
nb0c1d1e5fd6.tq: Distinguish the year of enactment from the date on which the law came into force.
xs: The **PMLA 2002** came into force on **1 July 2005**, so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ PMLA enacted **2002**, in force **2005**.
xa: The ED uses PMLA to **attach proceeds of crime**.
The **FEOA 2018** threshold is **₹100 crore**.

n5fb614f0ef4.s: In the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta framework, the Lokayukta primarily deals with:
o: International relations, while the Upa-Lokayukta deals with public order
Only judicial officers, while the Upa-Lokayukta deals with private citizens
Higher functionaries, while the Upa-Lokayukta deals with the rest
Only Group C and D employees, while the Upa-Lokayukta deals with Ministers
n5fb614f0ef4.x: The Lokayukta has jurisdiction over higher functionaries, whereas the Upa-Lokayukta deals with the remaining categories covered by the state law.
n5fb614f0ef4.tq: Discriminate between two closely related offices by their functional jurisdiction.
xs: Under the **AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1983**, the Lokayukta handles **higher functionaries** and the **Upa-Lokayukta** the rest — option **(3)**.
The other options misassign the two bodies' jurisdiction.
xa: The **2013** Act obliged every state to set up a Lokayukta within a year.
The first Lokayukta was in **Maharashtra** (**1971**).

n46ac332e852.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2018 amendment to the Prevention of Corruption Act?
o: Bribe-giving became a direct offence punishable with up to seven years
It sought to align Indian law with the UN Convention against Corruption
Commercial organisations are liable for bribes offered on their behalf
A coerced bribe-giver is protected only if the matter is reported within 30 days
n46ac332e852.x: A coerced bribe-giver must report within 7 days, not 30.
xa: **Sec 17A**: government approval before inquiry/investigation into official decisions.
Trial within **2 years**, extendable to a maximum of **4**.

nf6d20fa7be2.s: Under the amended Prevention of Corruption Act, a public servant convicted of taking a bribe faces imprisonment of:
nf6d20fa7be2.x: The amended Act prescribes three to seven years' imprisonment and a fine; trials should end within two years, extendable to four.
xa: Bribe-giving: up to **7 years**.
Commercial organisations are liable for bribes offered on their behalf.

ncec20346422.s: In which year did India ratify the United Nations Convention against Corruption?
ncec20346422.x: The Convention was adopted in 2003, India signed it in 2005 and ratified it in 2011.
xa: The **PCA (Amendment) Act, 2018** aimed to align Indian law with UNCAC.
⚠ UNCAC **2003** adopted → **2005** signed → **2011** ratified.

n3b82af81b76.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about proceedings under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018?
o: An arrest warrant must have been issued
Property can be confiscated only after conviction
The person has fled from India
The value involved is ₹100 crore or more
n3b82af81b76.x: On the ED's application, the Special Court may confiscate property even before conviction.
xa: ED has declared **21** Fugitive Economic Offenders in seven years.
⚠ FEOA threshold **₹100 crore**; PMLA in force **2005**.

n7b24b0b5633.s: In the split verdict on Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, who struck it down as violating Article 14?
n7b24b0b5633.x: Justice Nagarathna struck Section 17A down under Article 14; Justice Viswanathan upheld it subject to a binding Lokpal or Lokayukta opinion.
xa: The matter is pending before a **larger Bench**.
Proposed middle path: let **Lokpal/Lokayuktas** grant approval.
Debate: "**sanction paralysis**" vs guarding honest officers from a "**play-it-safe syndrome**".

na0abff03272.s: Which section of the Prevention of Corruption Act requires prior sanction before a court takes cognizance of an offence?
na0abff03272.x: Section 19 requires prior sanction before cognizance; Section 17A requires government approval before inquiry or investigation.
xa: Since **2018**, Sec 19 also covers **retired** public servants.
General protection: **Sec 218 BNSS** (earlier **Sec 197 CrPC**).

n980834ca830.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about sanction for prosecution of public servants?
o: Section 19 of the PC Act requires government approval before a police inquiry begins
Section 218 of the BNSS, corresponding to Section 197 CrPC, came into force on 1 July 2024
Since 2018, Section 19 sanction under the PC Act also covers retired public servants
Approval before an inquiry or investigation is governed by Section 17A of the PC Act
n980834ca830.x: Prior approval before inquiry or investigation is Section 17A; Section 19 concerns sanction for prosecution.
xa: Sec 19 applies **before a court takes cognizance**.
⚠ **17A** (approval before investigation) and **19** (sanction before prosecution) are often swapped.

n37478fb1546.s: Under Section 2(c) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, which of the following does NOT correctly describe a 'public servant'?
o: An employee of a local authority
Only a permanent employee of the Union Government
A person whose office requires performance of a public duty
n37478fb1546.x: The definition covers local-authority employees, Judges and persons performing public duties; it is not limited to permanent Union employees.
xa: PCA offences: **bribery**, **undue advantage**, **criminal misconduct**.
The **2018** amendment aligned the PCA with **UNCAC**.

nc4a89cf4b4c.s: Under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014, a whistleblower may be
o: only a Member of Parliament making a complaint to the Lokpal
only a government employee of the Union Government
a public servant or another person, including an NGO, making a public interest disclosure
nc4a89cf4b4c.x: A whistleblower includes any public servant or other person, including an NGO, who makes a public interest disclosure of specified wrongdoing to the Competent Authority.
nc4a89cf4b4c.tq: Test the inclusive definition against options that wrongly restrict the eligible complainant.
xs: A whistle-blower is **any public servant or other person, including an NGO**, making a **public interest disclosure** — option **(4)**.
The disclosure may go to the public or a higher authority (APPSC 2019 key).
xa: It may concern **corruption, wilful misuse of power/discretion or a criminal offence**.
The Act **protects the complainant's identity**.

n80b54926d0f.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the protection available under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014?
o: Acceptance of anonymous complaints as a general rule
Punishment for knowingly false or frivolous complaints
n80b54926d0f.x: Anonymous complaints are not accepted as a general rule. The complainant’s identity is disclosed to the competent authority but is required to be kept confidential; protection against victimisation is also provided.
n80b54926d0f.tq: Find the exception by distinguishing confidentiality from anonymity.
xs: **Acceptance of anonymous complaints** is not a feature — **no anonymous complaints** are allowed — so option **(2)** is the answer.
The Act keeps the **identity confidential**, protects against **victimisation** and punishes **false or frivolous** complaints.
xa: Revealing identity: up to **3 years** + **₹50,000**.
Knowingly false complaint: up to **2 years** + **₹30,000**.

nc6cda0de92e.s: Which of the following categories is specifically excluded from the stated whistleblower rules?
nc6cda0de92e.x: The Special Protection Group (SPG) is excluded from the stated rules.
nc6cda0de92e.tq: Test the statutory exception rather than the general coverage rule.
xs: The **Special Protection Group (SPG)** is excluded, so option **(4)** is correct.
State Ministers, MPs and central employees all have named competent authorities.
xa: Union Ministers → **Prime Minister**; State Ministers → **Chief Minister**.
A weakness: "**victimisation**" is not defined.

n16fe964641c.s: The Whistle Blowers Protection (Amendment) Bill, 2015 lapsed with the dissolution of the:
n16fe964641c.x: The Bill would have barred disclosures in Section 8(1)-type categories; it lapsed with the 16th Lok Sabha in 2019.
xa: It passed the **Lok Sabha** in **May 2015**.
Weakness of the parent Act: "**victimisation**" not defined.

n05f34b83fa0.s: The 2013 central law on Lokpal and Lokayuktas required every State to set up a Lokayukta within:
