n05f34b83fa0.x: The 2013 Act obliged every State to establish a Lokayukta within one year of its commencement; States then framed widely differing laws. Six months, two years and five years are not the stated period.
n05f34b83fa0.tq: 2013 Act: Lokayukta in every State within 1 year.
xs: The **2013** Act required every state to set up a Lokayukta **within a year**, so option **(2)** is correct.
States still differ widely in their Lokayukta laws.
xa: AP's law: **AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1983**.
First Lokayukta: **Maharashtra (1971)**.

n497f707b937.s: The Enforcement Directorate functions primarily under which combination of laws?
o: RTI Act, 2005 and Official Secrets Act, 1923
n497f707b937.x: The Enforcement Directorate operates under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, and the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.
n497f707b937.tq: Match the agency with its paired economic-enforcement statutes.
xs: The ED works under the **PMLA 2002** and **FEMA 1999**, so option **(2)** is correct.
The **DSPE Act** governs the CBI; the **CVC Act 2003** the CVC.
xa: The ED Director can **attach "proceeds of crime"** (APPSC-G1 2022).
PMLA came into force on **1 July 2005**.

n11caf8b2222.s: The Central Vigilance Commission is best described as an:
o: Department of the Ministry of Finance under the PMLA
Independent statutory body established under the CVC Act, 2003
n11caf8b2222.x: The CVC is an independent statutory body established under the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.
n11caf8b2222.tq: Distinguish a statutory oversight body from a constitutional body and an international organisation.
xs: The CVC is an **independent statutory body** under the **CVC Act 2003**, so option **(4)** is correct.
The CPI is published by **Transparency International**, not the CVC.
xa: CVC has **superintendence over CBI** in corruption cases.
The CVC was first set up in **1964** after the **Santhanam Committee**.

n0c15252362d.s: Which body exercises superintendence over the CBI in corruption cases?
n0c15252362d.x: The CVC supervises the CBI in corruption cases; the CBI rests on the DSPE Act, 1946, and the ED on the PMLA and FEMA.
xa: CVC annual report (**2 Sep 2026**): **7,229** PC Act cases pending trial; **400+** over **20** years.

nae07a98dfb3.s: Before the CBI can investigate a case within a State's territory, it needs the consent of that State government under which provision?
o: Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946
Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
Section 8 of the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003
nae07a98dfb3.x: The CBI draws its powers from the DSPE Act, 1946, and Section 6 of that Act requires the State's consent. Section 17A PCA is government approval before investigating a public servant's official decisions; Section 19 PCA is sanction before a court takes cognizance; the CVC Act is about the CVC's superintendence, not State consent.
nae07a98dfb3.tq: CBI in a State = Sec 6 DSPE consent.
xs: The CBI needs state **consent** under **Section 6 of the DSPE Act, 1946**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sec 17A** and **Sec 19** PCA concern government approval and prosecution sanction, not state consent.
xa: The CBI is a **non-constitutional, non-statutory** body.
Director chosen by **PM, CJI (or nominee), LoP**.

ne0a324bcf2a.s: The Corruption Perceptions Index is published by:
o: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
ne0a324bcf2a.x: The Corruption Perceptions Index is published by Transparency International, headquartered in Berlin.
ne0a324bcf2a.tq: Identify the publisher rather than confusing the index with a World Bank or United Nations product.
xs: The CPI is published by **Transparency International (Berlin)**, so option **(1)** is correct.
It has been published **yearly since 1995**.
xa: It measures **perceived public-sector corruption** (APPSC-G2 2017).
Scale: **0 (highly corrupt) to 100 (very clean)**; covers about **180 countries**.

nf49355f2596.s: On the Corruption Perceptions Index scale of 0 to 100, a score of 0 denotes:
nf49355f2596.x: The CPI measures perceived public-sector corruption on a 0-100 scale, where 0 denotes highly corrupt conditions.
xa: ⚠ **0** = highly corrupt; **100** = very clean.
Publisher: **Transparency International**, yearly since **1995**.

nd6b38672f64.s: Citizen Report Cards were pioneered in Bengaluru in the 1990s by the:
o: Central Vigilance Commission associated with K. Santhanam
Public Affairs Centre associated with Samuel Paul
Planning Commission associated with B. R. Ambedkar
Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan associated with Aruna Roy
nd6b38672f64.x: Citizen Report Cards were developed by the Public Affairs Centre in Bengaluru in the 1990s under the leadership of Samuel Paul.
nd6b38672f64.tq: Recall the institution, person, place and decade as a single civil-society initiative.
xs: Citizen Report Cards come from the **Public Affairs Centre, Bengaluru**, associated with **Samuel Paul** (**1990s**) — option **(2)**.
**Aruna Roy's MKSS** is linked with **Jan Sunwai**, not report cards.
xa: **Jan Sunwai**: MKSS public hearings in Rajasthan, **1990s**.
**Social audit**: AP's **SSAAT**.

n50d2b0a2b0f.s: Jan Sunwai, as a method of citizen oversight, is most closely associated with:
o: Lokpal inquiries in Maharashtra during the 2000s
CVC hearings in Delhi during the 1980s
MKSS public hearings in Rajasthan during the 1990s
SSAAT audits in Andhra Pradesh during the 1970s
n50d2b0a2b0f.x: Jan Sunwai refers to public hearings associated with the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan in Rajasthan during the 1990s.
n50d2b0a2b0f.tq: Distinguish the similarly public-facing mechanisms by organisation, place and decade.
xs: **Jan Sunwai** means the **MKSS public hearings in Rajasthan during the 1990s**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**SSAAT** is AP's social audit society, and the first Lokayukta was in **Maharashtra** in **1971** — neither is Jan Sunwai.
xa: **Citizen Report Cards**: **Public Affairs Centre, Bengaluru** (**Samuel Paul**, **1990s**).
**Social audit** in AP is done by **SSAAT**.

nae261ae7b48.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Industrial Policy Resolutions?
o: The 1948 Resolution adopted a mixed economy with four categories of industries
Under the 1956 Resolution, Schedule C industries were left to the private sector
Under the 1956 Resolution, Schedule A listed 17 industries for the public sector
Under the 1956 Resolution, Schedule B listed 12 industries reserved exclusively for the private sector
nae261ae7b48.x: Schedule B's 12 industries were mixed (public and private); it was Schedule C that was left to the private sector.
xa: **1980 IPS**: technology upgrading and **export orientation**.
**1977 IPS** (Janata): small/cottage sector, **District Industries Centres**.

n87d8ab0b5a7.s: After the 1991 reforms, industrial licensing was retained for:
o: Every industry employing more than 100 workers
Alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals and industrial explosives
n87d8ab0b5a7.x: Licensing was largely abolished but retained for alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, industrial explosives, electronic aerospace and defence, and drugs.
xa: Public-sector reservation is now only **atomic energy and railway operations**.
Import licensing was abolished except hazardous/environmentally sensitive items.

n77b56921fb4.s: During the 1991 balance of payments crisis, about how many tonnes of gold were pledged with the Bank of England and UBS?
n77b56921fb4.x: About 67 tonnes of gold were pledged with the Bank of England and UBS in 1991.
xa: The trigger was **NRI deposit flight**.
The **IMF** was approached for **$7 billion**.

necad5f20ea2.s: In the 1991 crisis, India approached the IMF for about how much assistance, with structural-adjustment conditions?
necad5f20ea2.x: India approached the IMF for about $7 billion, which came with structural-adjustment conditions.
xa: Reserves had fallen to **$975 million** (June **1991**).
The rupee was devalued about **20%** towards a **market-determined** rate.

n846ff49affd.s: Which short-term reform measure targets the balance of payments, inflation and the fiscal deficit?
n846ff49affd.x: Stabilisation is short-term and corrects macroeconomic imbalances; structural adjustment is medium- or long-term and seeks efficiency and competitiveness.
xa: Stabilisation measures: **devaluation**, fiscal deficit cuts.
Structural adjustment: **delicensing**, trade, financial, tax and PSU reforms.
⚠ Devaluation = **stabilisation**; delicensing = **structural adjustment**.

n00ab640a70a.s: Navratna public sector undertakings were given greater autonomy in:
n00ab640a70a.x: Nine PSUs were given Navratna status and greater autonomy in 1997 (NCERT-based sources give 1996). 1991 is the year of the reforms, not of the Navratna scheme.
n00ab640a70a.tq: Distinguish the Navratna date and count from nearby PSU reform figures.
xs: **Navratnas** — nine PSUs — got autonomy in **1997**, so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ NCERT-based notes say **1996**.
xa: There are **97** **Miniratnas**.
The **New PSE Policy (2021)** favours strategic disinvestment.

ne2174c4131a.s: In 1991, automatic approval was given for FDI up to ____ per cent in 34 priority industries.
ne2174c4131a.x: The 1991 reforms allowed automatic approval for FDI up to 51 per cent in 34 priority industries.
xa: **100% FDI in insurance** is a recent extension.
**Capital account** convertibility was never fully adopted.

n5d127fa8f5f.s: The conversion of FERA into FEMA took place in:
n5d127fa8f5f.x: The Foreign Exchange Regulation Act framework was replaced by the Foreign Exchange Management Act in 1999.
n5d127fa8f5f.tq: Distinguish the year of a legal successor from the year of the broader reform package.
xs: **FERA** was converted into **FEMA** in **1999**, so option **(3)** is correct.
It is listed as part of the LPG reforms.
xa: The ED works under **FEMA 1999** and PMLA.
Current account convertibility: **1994**.

n8b10d269688.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's generations of economic reforms?
o: First-generation reforms (1991-2000) included industrial delicensing and tariff cuts
First-generation reforms were mainly concerned with factor markets such as labour, land and power
First-generation reforms introduced the automatic FDI route
Second-generation reforms addressed fiscal rules and PSU disinvestment
n8b10d269688.x: Factor markets (labour, land, power) belong to the second-generation reforms of the 2000s, not the first generation.
xa: **Reforms 2.0** (**2014** on): DPI, Aadhaar, UPI, Jan Dhan, DBT.
Average tariffs fell from about **125%** to about **30%**.

nf82159584bf.s: Which of the following was a prescription of the Washington Consensus?
o: Import licensing to protect domestic industry
Higher trade barriers on foreign investment
nf82159584bf.x: The Washington Consensus advocated trade and FDI liberalisation, privatisation and deregulation, along with fiscal discipline and tax reform.
xa: It was framed by **John Williamson** (**1989**) with **10 prescriptions**.
Its **one-size-fits-all** approach is now questioned.

n4e860edc5f0.s: The New Public Sector Enterprise Policy for Atmanirbhar Bharat (2021) favours:
n4e860edc5f0.x: The New PSE Policy, 2021 favours strategic disinvestment.
xa: Above **51%** private stake transfers ownership and management.
**Navratnas** got autonomy in **1997**.

nba398535497.s: The term ‘Washington Consensus’ is associated with which one of the following economists and years?
nba398535497.x: The Washington Consensus was formulated by John Williamson in 1989.
nba398535497.tq: Use the direct author–year association without being distracted by economists linked with other economic doctrines.
xs: The **Washington Consensus** is linked with **John Williamson**, **1989** — option **(1)**.
It had **10 prescriptions** and is now seen as **outdated**.
xa: Prescriptions: **fiscal discipline**, **tax reform**, **trade + FDI liberalisation**, **privatisation**, **deregulation**, **property rights**.
Its **one-size-fits-all** approach is now questioned.

nf97feb4708c.s: Which set contains only instruments of the enabler State?
o: State ownership, licensing and price controls
Industrial licensing, MRTP controls and public-sector reservation
Commanding heights, state ownership and production controls
nf97feb4708c.x: PPPs, DBT, GeM and UMANG are instruments through which the State enables delivery by private or civil-society actors.
xa: E-governance tools like **Aadhaar, DBT, GeM, UMANG** reduce **discretion and middlemen**.
AP's **Deepam-2** (free LPG via **DBT**) is an enabler example.

nc851b8b264d.s: Deepam-2 illustrates the State's shift from:
nc851b8b264d.x: By supporting BPL families through DBT for LPG cylinders, Deepam-2 shows a shift from the State as direct provider to the State as enabler.
xa: Enabler state instruments: **PPPs, DBT, GeM, UMANG**.
Housing too: State moved from direct provider to **enabler of private real estate**.

nd9e0030e264.s: Abolition of asset limits under the MRTP Act removed curbs on:
o: Concentration, entry, expansion, mergers and acquisitions
nd9e0030e264.x: Abolition of MRTP asset limits removed curbs on concentration, entry, expansion, mergers and acquisitions.
xa: The **CCI** is the competition regulator.

nf6e7fe5eda7.s: The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) regulates:
nf6e7fe5eda7.x: CERC regulates power tariffs and inter-state transmission; TRAI regulates telecom, IRDA insurance and SEBI the securities market.
xa: **PNGRB** (**2006**) regulates petroleum and gas pipelines.

n3144fd07f31.s: Which one of the following was NOT cited as an aspect of government failure that justified the economic reforms of 1991?
o: Low efficiency and profitability of public sector undertakings
Complete autonomy of public sector undertakings from political influence
Mounting losses of public sector undertakings
n3144fd07f31.x: Lack of autonomy and political interference, rather than complete autonomy, were cited as features of government failure. Low efficiency, losses, labour problems and project delays were also identified.
n3144fd07f31.tq: Find the option that reverses the direction of a stated institutional problem.
xs: **Complete autonomy of PSUs from political influence** was not cited — the problem was **political interference** and **no autonomy** — so option **(2)** is the answer.
The listed PSU problems: **low efficiency + profitability**, **mounting losses**, **labour problems**, **project delays**.
xa: PSU autonomy came later via **MoUs** and **Navratna/Maharatna** status.
The intellectual basis: **public choice theory** (**James Buchanan**).

nc97816b3857.s: The intellectual basis for the argument that government failure necessitated the 1991 reforms was provided by which of the following?
o: Embedded autonomy theory associated with Peter Evans
Developmental-state theory associated with Chalmers Johnson
Public choice theory associated with James Buchanan
Flailing-state theory associated with Lant Pritchett
nc97816b3857.x: Public choice theory, associated here with James Buchanan, supplied the intellectual basis for the government-failure critique of the pre-1991 system.
nc97816b3857.tq: Use the author–theory association to distinguish closely related governance concepts.
xs: **Public choice theory** of **James Buchanan** gave the intellectual basis for the government-failure case, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Evans** = embedded autonomy; **Johnson** = developmental state; **Pritchett** = flailing state.
xa: ⚠ **Pritchett** = flailing state (India); **Johnson** = developmental state (Japan); **Evans** = embedded autonomy.
**John Williamson** coined "Washington Consensus" in **1989**.

n39081829f10.s: Public sector enterprises were given greater autonomy through:
o: MoUs and Navratna or Maharatna status
Transfer of PSUs to local governments
n39081829f10.x: PSEs received greater autonomy through Memoranda of Understanding and Navratna or Maharatna status.
xa: Disinvestment began in **1991-92** with a **Rs 2,500 crore** target.
Public-sector reserved list: **17 → 8 → 3**.

n7a08dc599b7.s: Who used the term “flailing state” in 2009 in relation to India?
n7a08dc599b7.x: Lant Pritchett used the concept of the “flailing state” in 2009 in relation to India.
xs: **Lant Pritchett** used "**flailing state**" in **2009** about India, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Johnson** = developmental state; **Evans** = embedded autonomy; **Williamson** = Washington Consensus.
xa: Flailing state: the "**head**" (elite institutions) works but is not connected to its "**limbs**" (field delivery).
⚠ **Pritchett** = India; **Johnson** = Japan.

n191e244cf29.s:
Which of the following are market failures that justified the planning-era role of the State?
1. Public goods
2. Externalities
3. Information asymmetry
n191e244cf29.x: Public goods, externalities, monopoly and information asymmetry are all market failures that justified an active planning-era State.
xa: The 1991 shift rested instead on **government failure**.
**James Buchanan's public choice theory** gave the government-failure case.

nc14c97af9f5.s:
The Washington Consensus policy package was associated with which institutions?
1. International Monetary Fund
2. United States Treasury
3. World Trade Organization
nc14c97af9f5.x: The package was associated with the IMF, World Bank and US Treasury; the WTO is not part of the formulation.
xa: Term coined by **John Williamson** in **1989**; it has **10** prescriptions.
Critique: **one template** ignores country conditions.

nfa97d467f78.s: The number of industries reserved for the public sector changed in which sequence?
nfa97d467f78.x: The public-sector reservation list was reduced in phases from 17 industries under Schedule A in 1956 to 8 in 1991 and later to 3.
nfa97d467f78.tq: Track the direction and stages of numerical reduction instead of treating the figures as isolated facts.
xs: The reserved list went **17 in 1956**, **8 in 1991** and **3 subsequently**, so option **(1)** is correct.
The **17** were in **Schedule A** of the 1956 IPR.
xa: Many notes now list **2** (atomic energy + railway operations).
Defence production was opened to the private sector in **2001**.

n37cdc4bcb60.s: Defence production, earlier among the industries reserved for the public sector, was opened to the private sector in which year?
n37cdc4bcb60.x: Defence production was opened to the private sector in 2001, leaving atomic energy and railway operations as the reserved areas in many lists. 1991 is when the reserved list was cut to 8 (defence still in it); 1997 is the Navratna year; 2015 is when the last SSI items were de-reserved.
xs: **Defence production** was opened to the private sector in **2001**, so option **(3)** is correct.
That is why many notes now list only **2** reserved sectors: **atomic energy + railway operations**.
xa: SSI de-reservation ended in **2015**.

n0004c01d4b1.s: In the Washington Consensus, market-determined interest rates fall under which prescription?
n0004c01d4b1.x: Market-determined interest rates are part of financial liberalisation; a competitive exchange rate is the exchange-rate prescription.
xa: India's interest-rate deregulation followed the **Narasimham Committee**.
India adopted a **market-determined exchange rate** in **1993**.

n0479eb8a0bd.s: Interest-rate deregulation in India's 1991 reform package followed the recommendations of which committee?
n0479eb8a0bd.x: Interest rates were deregulated on the Narasimham Committee line; tax cuts followed the Chelliah Committee.
xa: ⚠ **Narasimham** = interest rates; **Chelliah** = tax cuts.
The package also shifted to export promotion and removed **import quotas**.

n0db21e5960d.s: A State that sets rules and uses independent regulators to police markets is called a:
n0db21e5960d.x: The regulatory state sets rules and polices markets through independent regulators; the provider state owns and runs production.
xa: ⚠ **SEBI** (**1992**) = regulatory state; **PPPs, DBT, GeM, UMANG** = enabler state.
In the enabler model the private sector becomes the "**engine of growth**".

n5f7cc0d8049.s: Which of the following was identified as a criticism of the economic reforms?
o: Expansion of public investment in agricultural infrastructure
Fall in public investment in agricultural infrastructure
Rise in revenue available for welfare due to tax incentives
n5f7cc0d8049.x: Critics pointed to falling public investment in agricultural infrastructure, welfare revenue lost to tax incentives and curtailed social-sector spending.
xa: Disinvestment critique: PSU assets **undervalued**; proceeds plugged revenue gaps.
Regulatory overlap (e.g. **TRAI vs MIB** on TV ratings) is another concern.

nbb72403d175.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Economic Survey 2025-26's observations on regulators?
o: It recommended relying mainly on retired bureaucrats to staff regulators
It noted that regulators exercise legislative, executive and judicial powers
It recommended balancing regulatory independence with accountability
It suggested statutory timelines for clearances, with penalties for delay
nbb72403d175.x: The Survey proposed dedicated regulatory careers for younger professionals instead of relying mainly on retired bureaucrats.
xa: The chapter: "**Refining the Regulatory Touch**" (Ch. **3**, **31 Jan 2026**).
**RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA** are moving to **anticipatory** governance.

n38323515501.s: Which of the following best expresses the meaning of “Minimum Government, Maximum Governance”?
o: A leaner State that does less itself but governs better through rules, technology and accountability
A State that directly provides every service through public enterprises
A State that withdraws from all regulation and public accountability
A State that replaces all public institutions with private companies
n38323515501.x: The expression refers to a leaner State that performs fewer activities directly but governs more effectively through rules, technology and accountability.
n38323515501.tq: Reject extreme interpretations of “minimum government” and select the balanced meaning.
xs: It means **a leaner State that does less itself but governs better through rules, technology and accountability** — option **(1)**.
It does not mean withdrawal from regulation or full privatisation.
xa: Instruments: **RTI Act 2005**, e-governance (**Aadhaar, DBT, GeM, UMANG**), **right-sizing** the bureaucracy.
The slogan dates from **2014**.

nf3f1ad01933.s: Which of the following is NOT an instrument associated with e-governance for reducing discretion and middlemen?
nf3f1ad01933.x: Aadhaar, DBT and GeM are e-governance instruments that can reduce discretion and middlemen. Navratna status concerns autonomy for public sector enterprises, not e-governance.
nf3f1ad01933.tq: Separate digital governance tools from public-enterprise autonomy measures.
xs: **Navratna status** is a PSU autonomy measure, not an e-governance tool, so option **(3)** is the answer.
E-governance tools that cut discretion and middlemen: **Aadhaar, DBT, GeM, UMANG**.
xa: PSU autonomy came via **MoUs** + **Navratna/Maharatna** status.
**Deepam-2** uses **DBT** for free LPG cylinders.

nd5b9071bf4f.s: The 1991 reforms shifted the Indian economy from:
nd5b9071bf4f.x: The LPG reforms under P.V. Narasimha Rao and Dr. Manmohan Singh shifted the economy from state-controlled to market-oriented.
xa: The State shifted from direct provider to **facilitator, regulator and catalyst**.
The case for 1991 rested on **government failure**; the planning era rested on **market failure**.

nb4ddb4810de.s: A major criticism of disinvestment was that:
o: PSU assets were undervalued and proceeds plugged revenue gaps
Proceeds were used only for social infrastructure
It prevented all private participation in PSUs
nb4ddb4810de.x: Critics held that PSU assets were undervalued and proceeds filled revenue gaps instead of developing PSUs or social infrastructure.
xa: Disinvestment started in **1991-92** to bridge the fiscal deficit.
"Undervalued asset sales" are also listed among current criticisms.

nfa49b2d94cb.s: Which of the following is primarily a growth and external-sector measure rather than a measure to reduce the size of the State?
nfa49b2d94cb.x: Downsizing, disinvestment and privatisation shrink the State's direct role; encouraging FDI is mainly a growth and external-sector measure.
xa: ⚠ This keyed set (downsizing, disinvestment, privatisation of higher education) was asked by **UPSC in 2010**.
**Economic Survey 2025-26** proposed redefining "Government Company" so the State can hold **less than 51%** — a new disinvestment paradigm.
Public-sector employment fell from **19.6 million (1991)** to **17.5 million (2008)** as uncompetitive PSUs were closed or downsized.

n9b3754534d1.s: The sale of part of a PSU's equity to the public is called:
n9b3754534d1.x: Disinvestment is selling part of a PSU's equity to the public; it need not transfer ownership or management.
xa: Disinvestment is one of the LPG-era measures to cut the **size and cost of the State**, along with **downsizing** and **privatising** higher educational institutions.
**Economic Survey 2025-26:** a "Government Company" may be redefined so the State holds **less than 51%** — a new disinvestment paradigm.
⚠ **FDI inflows** are a growth measure, not a downsizing measure.

n64ce5daf9a4.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 proposed redefining a Government Company in a manner that would permit the State to hold
n64ce5daf9a4.x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 proposed a definition under which the State could hold less than 51%, indicating a new paradigm for disinvestment.
n64ce5daf9a4.tq: Focus on the changed ownership threshold rather than the conventional controlling-share figure.
xs: The **Economic Survey 2025-26** proposed redefining a "Government Company" so the State can hold **less than 51%** — option **(1)**.
This is described as a **new disinvestment paradigm**.
xa: **Disinvestment** = sale of part of a PSU's equity to the public; **privatisation** = shedding government ownership/management.
LPG-era measures to cut State size: **downsizing** the bureaucracy, **disinvestment**, **privatising** higher educational institutions.
⚠ **FDI inflows** are a growth and external-sector measure, not a cut in State size.

n622cb8c70aa.s: Hiring external sources for services such as legal, IT and security work earlier done in-house is called:
n622cb8c70aa.x: Outsourcing means hiring external sources for services previously performed in-house.
xa: Since **1991**, many organised-sector workers have **no direct employer relation**, weakening union mobilisation.
Contract labour rose from **20% (1999)** to **40.7%** of the manufacturing workforce (**2022-23**).
AP's **APCOS** (**2020**) recruits outsourced staff and pays them directly, cutting out contractor middlemen.

ncb3bd963425.s: Contractualisation in public administration is criticised for causing:
o: Higher job security and stronger unions
Lower job security but stronger unions
Higher job security but weakened unions
Lower job security and weakened unions
ncb3bd963425.x: Contractualisation lowers job security and weakens unions, and may also hurt productivity.
xa: Contract labour rose from **20% (1999)** to **40.7%** of manufacturing workers (**2022-23**).
Since **1991**, many organised-sector workers have **no direct employer relation**, weakening union mobilisation.
Only **6.3%** of the workforce is unionised; **1.8%** in the private sector.

ncb313569f6c.s: In the Reinventing Government framework, moving from hierarchy to participation and teamwork is the meaning of which principle?
ncb313569f6c.x: The decentralised principle seeks to move from hierarchy to participation and teamwork.
ncb313569f6c.tq: Match the organisational contrast with the corresponding principle.
xs: **Decentralised** government means moving from **hierarchy to participation and teamwork** — option **(2)**.
**Mission-driven** = rules to mission; **Market-oriented** = leverage change through the market; **Catalytic** = steer rather than row.
xa: These are among the **ten principles** of Osborne and Gaebler's **Reinventing Government** (**1992**).
**Results-oriented** = fund outcomes, not inputs; **Enterprising** = earn rather than spend.
**Anticipatory** = prevent rather than cure; **Community-owned** = empower rather than serve.

n841af60e527.s: 'Serve, not steer' is the central prescription of which approach?
n841af60e527.x: New Public Service emphasises democratic citizenship and public interest, and holds that administrators should serve, not steer.
xa: ⚠ Trap: Osborne-Gaebler = "steering, not rowing"; Denhardt = **"serve, not steer"**.
**Mark Moore's Public Value** also rejects the citizen-as-customer view, stressing **legitimacy and trust**.
Critique of NPM: a citizen has **rights**, not just purchasing power.

nb1f7802bf09.s: The core claim of Public Value theory is that:
o: Public managers should pursue efficiency alone
Citizens should be treated only as customers
Public managers create value for the public, including legitimacy and trust
nb1f7802bf09.x: Public Value theory holds that managers create value for the public, including legitimacy and trust, not merely efficiency.
xa: Public Value is associated with **Mark Moore**, Creating Public Value (**1995**).
**New Public Service** (Denhardt and Denhardt) shares the critique: **"serve, not steer"**.
Both reject NPM's reduction of the State to a **service seller**.

nb7658ddc987.s:
Which of the following are features of New Public Management?
1. Performance auditing
2. Contracting out non-core services
3. Rejection of all performance measures
nb7658ddc987.x: NPM promotes performance auditing, contracting out and a customer view of citizens; it does not reject performance measurement.
xa: Other Hood doctrines: **hands-on professional management**, **disaggregation** into agencies, **competition** in the public sector, **discipline and parsimony** in resources.
**Christopher Hood** popularised the term NPM in **1991**.
Pioneering NPM countries: **UK** (Thatcher), **New Zealand**, **Australia**, **USA**.

nbd49e748d4e.s:
Which of the following were pioneering countries of New Public Management?
1. United Kingdom
2. New Zealand
3. Australia
nbd49e748d4e.x: The UK under Thatcher, New Zealand, Australia and the USA are identified as NPM pioneers.
xa: The term NPM was popularised by **Christopher Hood** in **1991**.
NPM's core idea: **private-sector techniques** in government — performance auditing, contracting out, citizen as **"customer"**.
Critics: **New Public Service** and **Public Value** both reject reducing the citizen to a customer.

nb9909f346b2.s: Which of the following is a doctrine of Christopher Hood's New Public Management?
o: Complete elimination of competition in the public sector
Emphasis on process and input controls
nb9909f346b2.x: Hood's NPM doctrines include hands-on professional management, explicit performance standards, output controls and competition in the public sector.
xa: Other Hood doctrines: **disaggregation into smaller units (agencies)**, **private-sector management styles**, **discipline and parsimony** in resource use.
**Christopher Hood** popularised the term NPM in **1991**.
Osborne and Gaebler's **Competitive** principle likewise means "inject competition into service delivery".

n21941fb5269.s: In Reinventing Government, the principle 'steer rather than row' describes ____ government.
n21941fb5269.x: Catalytic government steers rather than rows; community-owned government empowers, competitive injects competition, mission-driven moves from rules to mission.
xa: **Results-oriented** = fund outcomes, not inputs; **Customer-driven** = meet the needs of the customer, not the bureaucracy.
**Enterprising** = earn rather than spend; **Anticipatory** = prevent rather than cure.
**Decentralised** = hierarchy to participation and teamwork; **Market-oriented** = leverage change through the market.

n8771741f288.s: The recommendations of the Seventh Pay Commission (Justice A.K. Mathur) became effective from:
n8771741f288.x: The Seventh Pay Commission reported in 2015, but its recommendations were effective from 2016.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **5th–6th–7th** = **Pandian–Srikrishna–Mathur**.
Fifth: staff strength cut by about **30%**, freeze on new posts; Sixth: **Group D merged into Group C**, running pay bands.
Seventh: **pay matrix** replaced pay bands; performance-linked pay; rationalised allowances.

n9b6e8655850.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about unionisation and contract labour in India?
o: Only about 6.3% of the workforce is unionised
Unionisation in the private sector is about 1.8%
The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 requires 10% or 100 workers to form a union
Since 1991, all organised-sector workers have maintained a direct relation with their employer
n9b6e8655850.x: Contractualisation has weakened the direct employer relationship for many organised-sector workers.
xa: Contract labour share rose from **20% (1999)** to **40.7%** of manufacturing workers (**2022-23**), per the **Annual Survey of Industries**.
Contract-labour-intensive firms show **31%** lower productivity.
Public-sector employment fell from **19.6 million (1991)** to **17.5 million (2008)**.

n65b82d3f850.s: APCOS, which recruits outsourced staff and pays them directly, was set up by the Andhra Pradesh Government in:
n65b82d3f850.x: APCOS was set up in 2020 to recruit outsourced staff and pay them directly, cutting out contractor middlemen.
xa: **APSRTC** has about **8,000** outsourced employees paid via contractors → irregularities in wages, PF, ESI; they demand equal pay.
**NEDCAP** staff recruited after **1987** are kept only as contract/outsourced workers.
**Outsourcing** = hiring regular services (legal, IT, advertising, security) from external sources.

ndaa446867c8.s: Which recommendation is associated with the Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2005–09)?
o: Merger of Group D into Group C
Replacement of pay bands by a pay matrix
Lateral entry at the level of Joint Secretary
ndaa446867c8.x: The Second ARC recommended lateral entry at Joint Secretary level with performance-based appraisal and promotion; the others are Pay Commission features.
xa: The first lateral-entry Joint Secretaries joined in **2019**.
In **Aug 2024** the Centre asked UPSC to cancel an advertisement for **45** lateral posts after a reservation debate.
**NITI Aayog Action Agenda:** wider lateral entry at middle and senior levels, career pathways, longer stable tenures.

n8d536817a50.s: Joint Secretary and Director posts at the Centre are ordinarily filled by tenure deputation under the:
n8d536817a50.x: These posts are filled through tenure deputation under the Central Staffing Scheme administered by DoPT.
xa: The first lateral-entry Joint Secretaries joined in **2019**.
The **Second ARC** (**2005-09**) recommended lateral entry at **joint secretary level**.
In **Aug 2024** UPSC was asked to cancel an advertisement for **45** lateral posts after a reservation debate.

nce34c9d5d0d.s: The first lateral-entry Joint Secretaries at the Union level joined in:
nce34c9d5d0d.x: The first lateral-entry Joint Secretaries joined in 2019.
nce34c9d5d0d.tq: Recall the exact year from the sequence of lateral-entry developments.
xs: The first lateral-entry Joint Secretaries joined in **2019** — option **(3)**.
**2024** is when the Centre asked UPSC to cancel an advertisement for **45** lateral posts; the **2009** date is of the Results Framework Document.
xa: Lateral entry was recommended by the **Second ARC** (**2005-09**) at **joint secretary level**.
Normal route: **tenure deputation** under the **Central Staffing Scheme** (DoPT).
Debates: domain expertise vs **no reservation for single posts**, conflict of interest, demotivation of career officers.

n015ccd7b826.s: Which of the following is NOT cited as a debate associated with lateral entry into senior civil services?
o: Automatic enhancement of reservation in every single post
Access to domain expertise and fresh ideas
n015ccd7b826.x: The lateral-entry debate weighs domain expertise and fresh ideas against concerns that single posts carry no reservation, possible conflict of interest and demotivation of career officers. Option B inverts the reservation concern: the criticism is the absence of reservation in single-post recruitment, not any automatic enhancement of it.
n015ccd7b826.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated advantages and concerns.
xs: **Automatic enhancement of reservation in every single post** is NOT a debate — the actual concern is **no reservation for single posts** — so option **(2)** is the answer.
**Demotivation of career officers** and **conflict of interest** are cited criticisms of lateral entry.
**Domain expertise and fresh ideas** is the argument in its favour.
xa: In **Aug 2024** the Centre asked UPSC to cancel the advertisement for **45** lateral posts after the **reservation debate**.
The first lateral-entry Joint Secretaries joined in **2019**.
The **Second ARC** (**2005-09**) recommended lateral entry at **joint secretary level**.

n9bb10319683.s: The New Public Service response to treating the citizen merely as a customer is expressed as:
n9bb10319683.x: New Public Service answers the citizen-as-customer view with 'serve, not steer', stressing citizenship rights, equity and accountability.
xa: **Public Value** (Mark Moore) also rejects reducing citizen → customer and State → service seller.
⚠ Trap: Osborne-Gaebler = **"steering, not rowing"**.
NPM instruments: **Citizens' Charters**, service standards, grievance redressal.

ncc3268bc9d4.s: The Civil Services Board in Andhra Pradesh was created primarily to:
o: Regulate online grievance disposal by central ministries
ncc3268bc9d4.x: The Civil Services Board was created to curb political interference in postings.
ncc3268bc9d4.tq: Ask which institutional mechanism addresses the administrative problem described.
xs: AP's **Civil Services Board** was created to **curb political interference in postings** — option **(4)**.
The **Central Staffing Scheme** is a DoPT arrangement for JS/Director posts; **GRAI** ranks central ministries on CPGRAMS — neither is this Board's role.
xa: AP raised the upper age limit for non-uniform services **42 → 44** years until **30 Sep 2027** (G.O. Ms. No. **187**).
**Gram/Ward Sachivalayams (2019)**: **10,000+** secretariats, **500+** services.
**APCOS** (**2020**) pays outsourced staff directly.

ne491a4f27f2.s: Which of the following is generally regarded as a symbol of cooperative federalism?
ne491a4f27f2.x: The GST Council, where the Centre and States decide jointly, is generally regarded as a symbol of cooperative federalism.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **NITI Aayog** = competitive; **GST Council** = cooperative.
NITI Aayog replaced the **Planning Commission's** planning-era allocation role.
DPIIT's **Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP)** ranks states on ease of doing business; **AP topped the 2019** ranking.

nea420dd64e6.s: The 16th Finance Commission’s introduction of a GDP-contribution criterion is intended to promote which form of federalism?
nea420dd64e6.x: The GDP-contribution criterion rewards efficiency and has been described as part of a framework for competitive and accountable federalism.
nea420dd64e6.tq: Infer the institutional objective from the stated incentive mechanism.
xs: The **16th Finance Commission's** new **GDP-contribution** criterion promotes **"competitive and accountable federalism"** — option **(4)**.
It **rewards efficiency** of states that contribute more to GDP.
xa: The 16th FC (Arvind Panagariya, **2026-31**) retained a **41%** states' share.
It capped state deficits at **3% of GSDP** and ended off-budget borrowing.
⚠ Trap: **NITI Aayog** = competitive federalism; **GST Council** = cooperative federalism.

nindian-polity-26-18.s: The 14th Finance Commission covered which period?
nindian-polity-26-18.x: The 14th Finance Commission, under Y.V. Reddy, covered 2015–20.
n: The 14th Finance Commission covered the period 2015–20. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
xs: The **14th Finance Commission** covered **2015–20** — option **(2)**.
It raised the **States' share** of net divisible taxes from **32%** to **42%** — **10 percentage points**.
**2020–26** was the **15th** FC's period; **2020–21** was the 15th FC's first report.
xa: 14th FC chairman: **Y.V. Reddy**.
**15th FC** (**N.K. Singh**): States' share **41%**.
**16th FC** (**2026-31**, **Arvind Panagariya**): **41%** retained.

n9bbd3721277.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about recent figures on cesses and tax devolution?
o: Actual devolution in 2025-26 was close to the full 41% share
About 18% of gross tax revenue was in cesses in 2025-26
These cesses are not shareable with the States
The 16th Finance Commission kept the devolution share at 41% for 2026-31
n9bbd3721277.x: Because about 18% of gross tax revenue was in non-shareable cesses, actual devolution was nearer 31-32%, not 41%.
xa: **Budget 2026-27** accepted the 16th FC's 41% vertical share.
A **growing cess pool** is listed among the main criticisms of fiscal federalism.

nbd9bda1d23b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the FRBM Act targets (as amended in 2018)?
o: Central government debt of not more than 60% of GDP by 31 March 2025
Fiscal deficit of not more than 3% of GDP by 31 March 2021
The FRBM Act was enacted in 2003
General government debt of not more than 60% of GDP by 31 March 2025
nbd9bda1d23b.x: The Central government debt target is 40% of GDP; 60% is the target for general government debt.
xa: FRBM Act **2003**, amended **2018**.
Four statements laid in Parliament: **Medium-term Fiscal Policy**, **Fiscal Policy Strategy**, **Macro-economic Framework**, **Medium-term Expenditure Framework**.
Economic Survey 2025-26: general government debt fell **7.1 percentage points** since **2020**.

n5ad5e01f872.s: Under Article 293(3) of the Constitution, a State indebted to the Centre requires whose consent to borrow further?
o: Consent of the President acting alone
n5ad5e01f872.x: A State that is indebted to the Centre requires the consent of the Union Government to borrow under Article 293(3).
n5ad5e01f872.tq: Ask which authority exercises the borrowing-control power.
xs: Under **Art. 293(3)**, a state in debt to the Centre needs the **consent of the Union Government** (the Centre) to borrow — option **(2)**.
The **Finance Commission** and **Supreme Court** have no such consent role.
xa: **State of Kerala v. Union of India (2024)**: Kerala's **Art. 131** suit against the Centre's **Net Borrowing Ceiling**.
The ceiling counts **off-budget borrowings** against the state's cap.
The **16th FC** capped state deficits at **3% of GSDP** and ended off-budget borrowing.

nbb702fd308f.s: The Centre steers State capital expenditure through which mechanism mentioned in the Economic Survey 2025-26?
nbb702fd308f.x: The Centre steers State capital expenditure through SASCI.
nbb702fd308f.tq: Identify the fiscal instrument from a set of nearby scheme acronyms.
xs: The Centre steers state capital expenditure through **SASCI** — option **(1)**, per the **Economic Survey 2025-26**.
**PMMVY** is a **60:40** CSS; **NSAP** is a core-of-the-core scheme; **BRAP** is DPIIT's ease-of-doing-business ranking.
xa: The Survey found debt **sustainable** on **Bohn's fiscal response test**.
Markets **do not price State Development Loans** on fiscal health.
CSS have grown **26.5% a year** since **2016-17**.

nfcb1d432d52.s: In State of Kerala v. Union of India (2024), Kerala filed a suit under which Article to challenge the Centre's Net Borrowing Ceiling?
nfcb1d432d52.x: Kerala used the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction in Centre-State disputes under Article 131 to challenge the Net Borrowing Ceiling, which counts off-budget borrowings against the State's cap. Article 32 is for enforcing Fundamental Rights; Article 226 is High Court writ jurisdiction; Article 293 is the borrowing provision itself (293(3) needs Central consent), not the route to sue.
nfcb1d432d52.tq: Centre-State dispute suit = Art 131; State borrowing = Art 293.
xs: Kerala filed a suit under **Article 131** in **State of Kerala v. Union of India (2024)** — option **(2)**.
It challenged the **Net Borrowing Ceiling**, which counts **off-budget borrowings** against the state cap.
**Art. 293(3)** is the borrowing-consent provision itself, not the route to sue.
xa: Under **Art. 293(3)**, a state in debt to the Centre needs its **consent to borrow**.
The **16th FC** asked that **off-budget borrowing** be ended and capped state deficits at **3% of GSDP**.
Most states have their **own FRBM Acts**.

n960d673a5e1.s: The 16th Finance Commission recommended that State fiscal deficits be capped at:
n960d673a5e1.x: The 16th FC capped State deficits at 3% of GSDP, ended off-budget borrowing and asked for subsidy rationalisation.
xa: The 16th FC (**2026-31**) retained a **41%** states' share.
It introduced a **GDP-contribution** criterion — "competitive and accountable federalism".

ndc002752dff.s: Which of the following is included in the ‘core of the core’ category of Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
ndc002752dff.x: MGNREGA is included in the core-of-the-core category, along with NSAP and umbrella schemes for vulnerable groups.
ndc002752dff.tq: Identify a scheme from the correct CSS category.
xs: **MGNREGA** is in the **"core of the core"** CSS group — option **(3)**.
The group also includes **NSAP** and umbrella schemes for **SCs, STs, minorities** and other vulnerable groups.
**BRAP** is a state ranking and **SASCI** a capex mechanism — not CSS categories.
xa: The **2015 NITI Aayog Sub-Group of Chief Ministers** split CSS into **core of the core**, **core** and **optional** schemes.
**Core schemes:** mostly **60:40** Centre:State; **90:10** for NE and Himalayan states.
MGNREGA (**2005**) is funded roughly **90:10** Centre:state.

n82530491c30.s: PMMVY and ICDS follow which Centre-State sharing ratio?
n82530491c30.x: PMMVY and ICDS follow a 60:40 Centre-State sharing pattern.
xa: After **2015**, most CSS moved to **higher state shares**.
⚠ Trap: **60:40** = core schemes; **90:10** = NE + Himalayan states.
**Core of the core:** MGNREGA, NSAP and umbrella schemes for SCs, STs, minorities.

n0f308e50e77.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2015 rationalisation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
o: The 90:10 ratio applies to North-Eastern and Himalayan States
It followed a NITI Aayog Sub-Group of Chief Ministers
Schemes were grouped as core of the core, core and optional
Core schemes are funded 90:10 by the Centre and States for all States
n0f308e50e77.x: Core schemes are mostly funded 60:40; the 90:10 ratio applies only to North-Eastern and Himalayan States.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **60:40** = core schemes; **90:10** = NE + Himalayan states.
**Core of the core:** **MGNREGA**, **NSAP** and umbrella schemes for SCs, STs, minorities.
After 2015, **PMMVY** and **ICDS** moved to **60:40**.

o: Direct transfer of fertiliser subsidy to farmers
Direct transfer of LPG subsidy through Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts
Guaranteed wage employment in rural areas
n9891138c697.x: PAHAL is a DBT mechanism for LPG subsidy using Aadhaar-seeded accounts.
xa: DBT began on **1 Jan 2013** under the **JAM trinity**.
Critique: JAM creates **new exclusion** for those without digital access/documents.
The Centre steers state capex through **SASCI** (Economic Survey 2025-26).

ncc0ef18b934.s: Since 2016-17, Centrally Sponsored Schemes have grown at about ____ a year.
ncc0ef18b934.x: CSS grew about 26.5% a year since 2016-17, while State plan allocations fell by nearly 30%.
xa: After **2015**, most CSS moved to higher state shares — PMMVY and ICDS = **60:40**.
**CSS conditionality** is a listed criticism of current fiscal federalism.
States now bear **75.2%** of school education spending.

n767f86564c5.s: Excessive expenditure on unconditional cash schemes by some states is criticised primarily because it may crowd out spending on which sectors?
o: Defence, foreign affairs and space research
n767f86564c5.x: Some states reportedly spend over 200% of their health budget on cash schemes, raising concern that health, education and nutrition spending may be crowded out.
n767f86564c5.tq: Link the stated fiscal trade-off with the specific social sectors affected.
xs: Heavy spending on cash schemes **crowds out health, education and nutrition** — option **(1)**.
Some states spend **over 200%** of their health budget on cash schemes.
xa: States spent **₹4.14 lakh crore** on **unconditional cash transfers** (16th FC report).
This trend is called **"new welfarism"**.
Social protection spending is just **4.0% of GDP**.

n8b4ee3d5ddd.s: The shift from enforceable welfare rights to discretionary transfers is criticised on the ground that it:
o: transfers all welfare functions to local governments
makes all welfare benefits universal and automatic
n8b4ee3d5ddd.x: The criticism is that discretionary transfers can transform citizens who hold enforceable rights into passive beneficiaries.
n8b4ee3d5ddd.tq: Identify the precise conceptual contrast between rights-holders and beneficiaries.
xs: The shift from enforceable **rights** to **discretionary transfers** turns **rights-holders into passive beneficiaries** — option **(3)**.
This is the main welfare critique of the post-reform model.
xa: **JAM** streamlines delivery but creates **new exclusion** for people without digital access/documents.
**"New welfarism"** (cash transfers) crowds out **health, education, nutrition**.
Some states spend over **200%** of their health budget on cash schemes.

nc0eed1d78c8.s: Which one of the following best represents the divergence view of regional disparities after the 1991 reforms?
o: Richer and industrialised States attracted most post-1991 private investment, widening regional gaps.
Transfers completely eliminated differences between States.
Poorer States automatically caught up because private investment was evenly distributed.
Infrastructure investment was concentrated only in poorer States.
nc0eed1d78c8.x: The divergence view holds that richer, industrialised States attracted a larger share of post-1991 private investment, causing regional gaps to widen.
nc0eed1d78c8.tq: Separate the divergence explanation from the competing convergence expectation.
xs: The **divergence** view: **richer, industrialised states** attracted most **post-1991 private investment**, so regional gaps **widened** — option **(1)**.
The **convergence** view says poorer states catch up via **transfers and infrastructure**.
xa: **Transfers** try to correct regional imbalances, but **horizontal criteria** spark disputes.
Corrective tools: **Golden Quadrilateral**, **NS-EW corridors**, **PMGSY**, **UDAN**.
The **M. Govinda Rao High-Power Committee** framework tracks internal regional imbalances.

nb38d239a262.s: Southern States protested in 2024 that population weights in devolution:
o: Rewarded States with better performance disproportionately
nb38d239a262.x: Southern States argued that population weights punish good performance in the devolution formula.
nb38d239a262.tq: Identify the direction of the grievance rather than the existence of the protest.
xs: The **Southern states' protest (2024)** argued that **population weights punish good performance** — option **(1)**.
States that controlled population growth feel they lose share in devolution.
xa: **Transfers** aim to correct regional imbalances, but **horizontal criteria** spark disputes.
The **16th FC** added a **GDP-contribution** criterion that rewards efficiency.
The **16th FC** retained the **41%** vertical share for **2026-31**.

o: The government pays a fixed annuity and bears the revenue risk
The private player bears the revenue risk
The private player owns the asset permanently
Toll rights on an already-built highway are transferred
n554e2d7ae9f.x: In BOT (Annuity) the government pays a fixed annuity and bears revenue risk; in BOT (Toll) the private player bears it.
xa: **HAM** blends **EPC + BOT-Annuity**: government pays **40%** during construction.
In **EPC** the **government funds entirely**; the private player only constructs.
**BOO** (Build-Own-Operate) has **no transfer back** to government.

n0e02dd7da39.s: In which PPP model does the private player own the asset during the concession period and subsequently transfer it to the government?
n0e02dd7da39.x: BOOT stands for Build-Own-Operate-Transfer; the private player owns the asset during the concession and transfers it thereafter.
n0e02dd7da39.tq: Expand the acronym and use the final word to identify the ownership outcome.
xs: In **BOOT** (Build-Own-Operate-Transfer) the private player **owns the asset during the concession**, then **transfers** it — option **(4)**.
**BOO** has **no transfer back**; **EPC** is fully government-funded; **TOT** transfers toll rights on built highways.
xa: **BOLT** = Build-Own-Lease-Transfer: the asset is leased to government, then transferred.
**DBFO(T)**: the private player also **designs and finances**.
⚠ Trap: BOOT transfers the asset; **BOO** never does.

n1d8ddf869a6.s: Under the Hybrid Annuity Model, the government pays what share of the project cost during construction?
n1d8ddf869a6.x: Under HAM the government pays 40% during construction; the developer's 60% is repaid through annuities over about 15 years.
xa: ⚠ Trap: HAM **40 – 60** = government – developer.
HAM blends **EPC + BOT-Annuity**.
**Stricter HAM norms (May 2026):** developer net worth **20%** of project cost (up from **15%**).

nffcf2fbfa9e.s: Toll rights on already-built highways are transferred to private players under
nffcf2fbfa9e.x: TOT means Toll-Operate-Transfer and involves transferring toll rights on already-built highways to private players.
nffcf2fbfa9e.tq: Distinguish a brownfield toll-rights arrangement from construction-based PPP models.
xs: **TOT** (Toll-Operate-Transfer) transfers **toll rights on already-built highways** to private players — option **(4)**.
**BOT (Toll)** involves building new projects; **EPC** is government-funded construction.
xa: **Revised BOT guidelines (May 2026):** sovereign wealth funds, pension/infrastructure funds and private equity may now bid for **BOT** (earlier only **TOT**).
**BOT (Annuity):** government pays fixed annuity, **bears revenue risk**.
**BOT (Toll):** private player **bears revenue risk**.

n5078f789150.s: Which of the following was NOT among the recommendations associated with the Vijay Kelkar Committee report on revisiting and revitalising PPP?
o: A renegotiation mechanism for concession agreements
Creation of an Infrastructure PPP Adjudication Tribunal headed by a former Supreme Court or High Court judge
A prohibition on all private participation in toll PPPs
n5078f789150.x: The report proposed discouraging PSUs from bidding for toll PPPs, not prohibiting all private participation. It also recommended renegotiation, periodic review, an IPRC and an IPAT.
n5078f789150.tq: Find the option that reverses a recommendation into an extreme prohibition.
xs: A **prohibition on all private participation in toll PPPs** was NOT recommended — option **(4)**.
Kelkar only wanted to **discourage PSUs** from bidding for **toll PPPs**.
It did recommend a **renegotiation mechanism**, **periodic review** of concession agreements and an **IPAT** headed by a former **SC/HC judge**.
xa: It also proposed an **Infrastructure PPP Project Review Committee (IPRC)**.
The Kelkar Committee (**2015**) **discouraged the Swiss challenge** (information asymmetry).
Stalled PPPs arise from **aggressive bidding** (winner's curse), revenue shortfalls and land/clearance delays.

n59cd725b12c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme?
o: It provides a capital grant for commercially viable PPP projects
The sponsoring authority may add up to a further 20%
The Centre may provide up to 20% of the project cost
For social-sector projects, the limits may rise to 30% each
n59cd725b12c.x: VGF is a capital grant for PPP projects that are economically justified but commercially unviable.
xa: **Draft AP PPP Policy-2026:** **₹1,500 crore** earmarked for VGF plus a proposed bridge fund.
**PPPAC** appraises central-sector PPPs (chaired by Secretary, DEA).
**IIFCL (2006)** gives long-term infrastructure debt.

ncd5f586d351.s: Which of the following is a major cause of stalled PPP projects?
o: Aggressive bidding, revenue shortfalls, and land or clearance delays
Automatic transfer of all risks to the Government
Guaranteed traffic growth and absence of land issues
Exclusive reliance on dividend income from CPSEs
ncd5f586d351.x: Aggressive bidding, often producing the winner's curse, traffic and revenue shortfalls, and land or clearance delays can leave PPP projects stalled.
ncd5f586d351.tq: Apply the risk chain from bidding assumptions to implementation failure.
xs: PPP projects stall due to **aggressive bidding** (winner's curse), **traffic/revenue shortfalls** and **land/clearance delays** — option **(1)**.
Such contracts then need **renegotiation**.
xa: The **Kelkar Committee** wanted a **built-in renegotiation mechanism**.
It proposed **IPAT** (adjudication tribunal) and **IPRC** (project review committee).
**Swiss challenge** is criticised for **information asymmetry**.

n3b1676f4c5a.s: Which pair of institutions was proposed to expedite dispute resolution and project review in PPPs?
n3b1676f4c5a.x: The Kelkar Committee (2015) proposed IPAT, the Infrastructure PPP Adjudication Tribunal headed by a former SC/HC judge, and IPRC, the Infrastructure PPP Project Review Committee, to speed up dispute resolution and project review. The ETFs are disinvestment instruments, DIPAM/DPE are departments, and NMP/VGF are monetisation and funding schemes.
n3b1676f4c5a.tq: Distinguish the two proposed PPP institutions by their functions.
xs: **IPAT** (adjudication tribunal) and **IPRC** (project review committee) were proposed for faster dispute resolution and project review — option **(4)**.
**CPSE ETF / Bharat-22 ETF** are disinvestment methods; **DIPAM/DPE** are departments; **NMP/VGF** are monetisation and funding schemes.
xa: They were proposed by the **Vijay Kelkar** Committee (**2015**) on revitalising PPP.
IPAT is to be headed by a **former SC/HC judge**.
Kelkar also wanted a **built-in renegotiation** mechanism.

nbce400fe5cf.s: The AP Infrastructure Development Enabling Act, 2001 primarily provides:
o: The constitutional basis for privatisation of all State enterprises
The statutory framework for Union disinvestment of CPSEs
The legal framework exclusively for municipal bonds
The legal framework for PPP projects in Andhra Pradesh, including Swiss-challenge proposals
nbce400fe5cf.x: The AP Infrastructure Development Enabling Act, 2001 provides the legal framework for PPP projects in Andhra Pradesh and includes Swiss-challenge proposals.
nbce400fe5cf.tq: Match the State statute with its specific institutional purpose.
xs: The **AP Infrastructure Development Enabling Act, 2001** gives the **legal framework for PPP projects in AP**, including **Swiss-challenge proposals** — option **(4)**.
It is a state PPP law, not a central disinvestment statute.
xa: **Draft AP PPP Policy-2026** approved by AP Cabinet on **6 Aug 2026**, with **₹1,500 crore** for VGF.
**Krishnapatnam Port** (Nellore) → **Adani Ports** (**2020**); **Gangavaram Port** (Visakhapatnam) → **Adani Ports** (**2021**).
⚠ The **Kelkar Committee (2015)** discouraged the Swiss challenge for **information asymmetry**.

n3508278b380.s: Asset monetisation involves transfer of rights for a limited period through:
n3508278b380.x: Asset monetisation transfers rights for a limited period by lease or licence, and the assets ordinarily return to the government.
xa: **APPSC-G1 2024** trap: public asset owners using new structures — **not private assets** or **indefinite leases**.
**NMP 1.0** launched **Aug 2021** by NITI Aayog; **NMP 2.0** covers **FY26-FY30**.
Structures used: **InvITs and REITs**.

n642dbbb1d63.s: The National Monetisation Pipeline (NMP) 1.0 was launched by NITI Aayog in:
n642dbbb1d63.x: NITI Aayog launched NMP 1.0 in August 2021 with a size of about ₹6 lakh crore.
xa: NMP 2.0 = **Asset Monetisation Plan 2025-30**, announced in **Budget 2025-26**.
NMP 2.0 includes **₹5.8 lakh crore** of private investment across **12** sectors.
NMP 1.0 covered **FY22-FY25**.

n0b965196908.s: Disinvestment revenue has fallen every year except for a surge in:
n0b965196908.x: Apart from a surge in 2022-23, disinvestment revenue has fallen, while dividends have grown every year.
xa: Criticism: **undervaluation** of assets; monetisation seen as sale **"by another name"**.
**LIC IPO** (**17 May 2022**) was India's biggest issue at the time.
**1991-98** disinvestment raised only **₹17,557 crore**.

n67cbd4eb19e.s: Which of the following represents a criticism of asset monetisation and disinvestment?
o: Assets may be undervalued, and monetisation may be viewed as a sale by another name.
Strategic sales always increase Government ownership and control.
Dividends have disappeared completely from public enterprises.
Asset monetisation eliminates all concerns about valuation.
n67cbd4eb19e.x: Criticisms include possible undervaluation of assets and the perception that monetisation is a sale by another name. The shift from disinvestment towards dividends is also debated.
n67cbd4eb19e.tq: Choose the option expressing the stated criticism rather than an absolute claim.
xs: Critics warn of **undervaluation** of assets and see monetisation as a **sale "by another name"** — option **(1)**.
The **shift from disinvestment to dividends** is also debated.
Strategic sales transfer **management control** away from government, so option 2 is wrong; dividends have **grown every year**, so option 3 is wrong.
xa: **Asset monetisation** transfers rights for a **limited period**; assets return to government and are **not sold**.
Disinvestment revenue **fell every year** except a **2022-23** surge.

n380440f4599.s: A disinvestment transaction in which both a stake and management control are transferred is known as:
n380440f4599.x: A strategic sale involves the transfer of a stake together with management control. The other methods do not necessarily transfer control.
n380440f4599.tq: Distinguish a strategic sale from ordinary share-sale methods by using the control element.
xs: A **strategic sale** transfers a block of shares **plus management control** to a strategic partner — option **(2)**.
**Buyback**, **OFS** and **IPP** do not transfer management control.
xa: **Minority disinvestment:** government keeps **>51%** and control.
**Complete privatisation:** sells **100%** ownership and control.
**Modern Foods (2000)** was the **first strategic sale** (to Hindustan Lever, **74%**).

nc988a9c0f6a.s: The Vijay Kelkar Committee (2012) was associated with recommendations for
o: exclusion of CPSE subsidiaries from performance agreements
replacement of the MoU system by annual budgeting
nc988a9c0f6a.x: The Vijay Kelkar Committee recommended faster disinvestment and governance reforms.
nc988a9c0f6a.tq: Test the committee’s distinctive reform emphasis rather than its date alone.
xs: The **Vijay Kelkar Committee (2012)** recommended **faster disinvestment and corporate governance reforms** — option **(2)**.
It also gave a **fiscal consolidation roadmap**.
xa: ⚠ A separate **Kelkar Committee (2015)** dealt with **revisiting and revitalising PPP**.
**Rangarajan (1993):** disinvestment up to **49%**; **Ramakrishna (1996):** strategic sale.
DIPAM was renamed from the Department of Disinvestment in **2016**.

n0e7a6c1b77b.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the New Public Sector Enterprise Policy, 2021?
o: Maintaining a bare-minimum presence in strategic sectors
Retaining a Government enterprise in every non-strategic sector
n0e7a6c1b77b.x: The policy envisages exit from non-strategic sectors, not retention of a Government enterprise in every such sector. It retains only a bare-minimum presence in strategic sectors.
n0e7a6c1b77b.tq: Find the option that reverses the policy direction.
xs: **Retaining an enterprise in every non-strategic sector** is NOT a feature — the policy **exits non-strategic sectors** — option **(4)**.
It keeps only a **bare-minimum presence** in **strategic** sectors.
xa: The **New PSE Policy 2021** is part of **Atmanirbhar Bharat**.
Four strategic groups: atomic energy/space/defence; transport/telecom; power/petroleum/coal/minerals; banking/insurance/financial services.
**DPE** handles closure/privatisation proposals for the non-strategic sector with **DIPAM**.

n64069ebac9c.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the four strategic sector groups under the New PSE Policy, 2021?
o: Power, petroleum, coal and other minerals
n64069ebac9c.x: The four groups are atomic energy, space and defence; transport and telecommunications; power, petroleum, coal and other minerals; and banking, insurance and financial services.
n64069ebac9c.tq: Recall the complete classified list and identify the outside group.
xs: **Agriculture, textiles and retail trade** is NOT a strategic sector group — option **(3)**.
The four groups: **atomic energy, space and defence**; **transport and telecommunications**; **power, petroleum, coal and other minerals**; **banking, insurance and financial services**.
xa: **New PSE Policy 2021** (Atmanirbhar Bharat): **exit non-strategic** sectors, **bare-minimum** presence in strategic ones.
**DPE** and **DIPAM** handle closure/privatisation proposals.
Trend: focus shifted **from selling PSUs to earning dividends** from them.

n1e006835e40.s: The LIC Initial Public Offer of 17 May 2022 was significant because it was:
o: the first complete privatisation of a CPSE
India's biggest issue at that time
the first OFS conducted by DIPAM
n1e006835e40.x: The LIC IPO on 17 May 2022 was India's biggest issue at that time.
n1e006835e40.tq: Identify the significance attached to the dated transaction.
xs: The **LIC IPO** (**17 May 2022**) was **India's biggest issue at the time** — option **(2)**.
The **first strategic sale** was **Modern Foods (2000)**, not LIC.
xa: **GIC Re OFS:** **3.39%** sold on 4-5 Sept **2024**, raising about **₹2,345.55 crore**.
**General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act** amended in **2021**.
**IPO** = first-time public issue; **FPO** = further issue by a listed PSE.

n6ec689b9ec9.s: Which institution appraises central-sector public-private partnership projects and is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs?
n6ec689b9ec9.x: The PPP Appraisal Committee appraises central-sector PPP projects and is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs.
n6ec689b9ec9.tq: Match the institutional role with the correct authority and chairing arrangement.
xs: **PPPAC** (PPP Appraisal Committee) appraises central-sector PPP projects, chaired by the **Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs** — option **(2)**.
**IPAT** is an adjudication tribunal; **IIFCL** gives long-term debt; **NIIF** is a quasi-sovereign wealth fund.
xa: **VGF scheme (2006):** capital grant up to **20%** from the Centre + **20%** from the sponsoring authority.
**IIFCL (2006):** long-term debt for infrastructure.
**NIIF (2015):** Centre holds **49%**; co-invests with global investors.

nd1f2ae8e79e.s: The Kelkar Committee recommended that PPP contracts should have:
o: A mandatory Swiss challenge in every project
A complete prohibition on any contractual modification
nd1f2ae8e79e.x: Because unforeseen financial and implementation problems can arise, the Kelkar Committee wanted a built-in mechanism for renegotiation of PPP contracts.
nd1f2ae8e79e.tq: Identify the institutional remedy proposed for a known PPP problem.
xs: The **Kelkar Committee** wanted a **built-in mechanism for renegotiation** in PPP contracts — option **(1)**.
It **discouraged** the Swiss challenge, so option 2 is wrong.
xa: Kelkar (**2015**) also proposed **periodic review** of concession agreements, **IPRC** and **IPAT** (headed by a former SC/HC judge).
It discouraged **PSUs** from bidding for **toll PPPs**.
⚠ Trap: **Rangarajan 1993** = up to **49%**; **Ramakrishna 1996** = strategic sale; **Kelkar 2015** = PPP.

na2a9714334b.s: The Disinvestment Commission headed by G.V. Ramakrishna was established in
na2a9714334b.x: The Disinvestment Commission, headed by G.V. Ramakrishna, was established in 1996.
na2a9714334b.tq: Separate the commission’s year from the years of the other disinvestment-related committees.
xs: The **Disinvestment Commission** headed by **G.V. Ramakrishna** was set up in **1996** — option **(4)**.
It recommended **strategic sale** of selected PSUs and a **privatisation roadmap**.
**1993** is the **C. Rangarajan** Committee; **1991** is the announcement of **20%** disinvestment.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **Rangarajan 1993** = up to **49%**; **Ramakrishna 1996** = strategic sale; **Kelkar 2015** = PPP.
**1999-2004** saw the shift to **strategic sales** (VSNL, BALCO).
**Modern Foods (2000)** was the **first strategic sale**.

nd2d28d8bbf9.s: Asset monetisation lets public asset owners use which financial structures?
nd2d28d8bbf9.x: Asset monetisation enables use of Infrastructure Investment Trusts and Real Estate Investment Trusts; the others are disinvestment methods.
xa: Strategic objective: unlock value of **brownfield public-sector assets** by tapping institutional + long-term capital.
**APPSC-G1 2024** asked this "strategic objective" angle.
Rights are transferred for a **limited period**; assets return to government.

na3bbac4758c.s: Which department manages the Centre's equity in CPSEs and conducts disinvestment?
o: Department of Investment and Public Asset Management
na3bbac4758c.x: DIPAM, under the Ministry of Finance, manages the Centre's equity in CPSEs and conducts disinvestment.
xa: DIPAM began as the **Department of Disinvestment** in **1999**, later a Ministry, renamed DIPAM in **2016**.
**OFS** has been used widely since **2012**.
ETFs used: **CPSE ETF** and **Bharat-22 ETF**.

nf21a87c6709.s: The draft AP PPP Policy-2026 earmarks how much for Viability Gap Funding?
nf21a87c6709.x: The draft AP PPP Policy-2026 earmarks ₹1,500 crore for VGF and proposes a bridge fund.
xa: It also proposes a **bridge fund**.
Central **VGF scheme (2006):** up to **20%** of project cost from the Centre + **20%** from the sponsoring authority.
For **social-sector** projects, central VGF can go up to **30% + 30%**.

n659c2b6c998.s: The Sarkaria Commission recommended that the National Development Council should be given constitutional status under Article 263 and renamed as the:
n659c2b6c998.x: The Sarkaria Commission recommended constitutional status for the NDC under Article 263 and proposed the name National Economic and Development Council.
n659c2b6c998.tq: Match a commission recommendation with the precise proposed institutional name and Article.
xs: The **Sarkaria Commission** proposed renaming the NDC the **"National Economic and Development Council"** with **constitutional status under Art. 263** — option **(4)**.
Art. **263** is the basis of the **Inter-State Council**.
xa: The **NDC** was created by executive resolution in **August 1952**.
Members: **PM**, all Union Cabinet ministers (since **1967**), all CMs, UT administrators.
The **Inter-State Council** was set up by **Presidential order** in **1990**.

n3cc8e382251.s: The Water Disputes Tribunals derive their statutory basis from the
n3cc8e382251.x: Water Disputes Tribunals are statutory bodies established under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, in the context of Article 262.
n3cc8e382251.tq: Match the specialised tribunal with its specific enabling statute.
xs: River **Water Disputes Tribunals** are statutory, under the **Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Art. **262** enables them, but the tribunals themselves are **statutory**.
The **States Reorganisation Act 1956** created the **Zonal Councils**, not the tribunals.
xa: **North Eastern Council** — statutory, **NEC Act 1971**.
**Inter-State Council** — constitutional, Art. **263**.
**National Security Council** — extra-constitutional, executive order **1998**.

n1955fb607a4.s: The North Eastern Council is a statutory body established under the:
n1955fb607a4.x: The North Eastern Council was established as a statutory body under the North Eastern Council Act, 1971.
n1955fb607a4.tq: Match the institution with its specific establishing statute.
xs: The **North Eastern Council** is statutory under the **NEC Act 1971** — option **(4)**.
The **States Reorganisation Act 1956** created the **Zonal Councils**; the **Inter-State Council** rests on Art. **263**, not an Act.
xa: River water tribunals: **Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956** under Art. **262**.
**National Security Council:** executive order, **1998**.
⚠ Statutory = changeable by **amending the Act**.

n0f419ad6225.s: The National Security Council of India is best described as:
o: A statutory body set up under an Act of Parliament in 1998
An extra-constitutional body set up by an executive order in 1998
A statutory body under the North Eastern Council Act, 1971
n0f419ad6225.x: The National Security Council is an extra-constitutional body created by an executive order in 1998; it has neither constitutional nor statutory basis.
n0f419ad6225.tq: NSC 1998: born of an executive order, not law.
xs: The **National Security Council** is **extra-constitutional**, set up by an **executive order in 1998** — option **(3)**.
It has no constitutional (Art. **263** is the Inter-State Council) or statutory basis.
xa: **Planning Commission (1950)** and **NDC (1952)** were also created by executive resolution.
**NEC** is statutory under the **NEC Act 1971**.
**Inter-State Council:** Presidential order, **1990**.

nb969c292117.s: Which one of the following is NOT a quasi-judicial body?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
nb969c292117.x: NITI Aayog is an advisory body and is not quasi-judicial. NHRC, SEBI and CIC are examples of bodies having quasi-judicial features.
nb969c292117.tq: Remove the advisory institution from the group of bodies that apply law or adjudicate statutory matters.
xs: **NITI Aayog** is an **advisory** body, NOT quasi-judicial — option **(1)**.
**SEBI**, **CIC** and **NHRC** are listed examples of quasi-judicial bodies.
xa: Definition: a **non-judicial** body that can interpret and apply law, **summon**, and impose sanctions.
The **Law Commission** is also advisory and **not quasi-judicial**.
NITI Aayog is the **odd one out** among NCBC, CAG, Finance Commission (**APPSC-GS 2025**).

n44f9cfea118.s: Which of the following bodies has civil court powers such as summoning witnesses and requisitioning records?
n44f9cfea118.x: The NCBC has powers of a civil court, including summoning witnesses and requisitioning records, particularly after it received constitutional status in 2018.
n44f9cfea118.tq: Use the ‘civil court powers’ clue to distinguish commissions from advisory bodies.
xs: The **NCBC** has **civil court powers** (summon witnesses, requisition records) since **2018** — option **(3)**.
The **NDC**, **Law Commission** and **NITI Aayog** are executive/advisory and lack such powers.
xa: Others with civil court powers: **NHRC**, **NCM**, **NCSC and NCST**, **NCW**, **CIC** (RTI Act).
NCBC got Art. **338B** via the **102nd Amendment (2018)**.
Quasi-judicial examples: **SEBI**, **Mental Health Review Commission**.

ncd04baf4cf6.s: Zonal Councils were set up under:
ncd04baf4cf6.x: Zonal Councils derive from the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, whereas the NDC and Planning Commission came from executive resolutions.
xa: NCBC's Article came from the **102nd Amendment, 2018**.
NCBC has **civil court powers**.
NDC — **August 1952**; Planning Commission — **March 1950**.

nindian-polity-65-26.s: Which of the following is an extra-constitutional or non-statutory body?
nindian-polity-65-26.x: The Law Commission is set up from time to time by executive order, so it is extra-constitutional. The SC Commission, Finance Commission and State Election Commission are constitutional.
nindian-polity-65-26.tq: Classify a body by where its power comes from: Constitution, statute or order.
n: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body under Article 280. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is a constitutional body under Article 338. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Law Commission of India is constituted periodically by executive order. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The State Election Commission is a constitutional body under Article 243-K. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
An extra-constitutional or non-statutory body is established through an executive order or cabinet resolution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xs: The **Law Commission of India** is an extra-constitutional, non-statutory body — option **(1)**.
It is constituted **periodically** by **executive order** — a Department of Legal Affairs notification **every 3 years**.
The others are **constitutional**: **NCSC** (**Art. 338**), **Finance Commission** (**Art. 280**), **State Election Commission** (**243-K** and **243-ZA**).
xa: The Law Commission is **advisory**, **not quasi-judicial**, and reports to the **Ministry of Law and Justice**.
The **23rd Law Commission** runs **1 Sep 2024 - 31 Aug 2027**.
⚠ APPSC-G1 2024 keyed "All incorrect" for statements calling it a quasi-judicial body advising the President.
First Law Commission of independent India: **M.C. Setalvad**, **1955**.

n42502eb850f.s: The National Commission for Backward Classes (Article 338B) got constitutional status through which Amendment?
n42502eb850f.x: NCBC came from the 102nd Amendment, 2018; the 89th created NCST and the 101st the GST Council.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **101st (2016)** = GST Council; **102nd (2018)** = NCBC.
**NCSC** is under Art. **338**.
NCBC has **civil court powers** since **2018**.

ncd3d86d43e0.s: The Law Commission of India reports to which ministry?
ncd3d86d43e0.x: The Law Commission is an advisory research body that recommends to the Government and reports to the Ministry of Law and Justice.
xa: ⚠ **APPSC-G1 2024** keyed "All incorrect" for statements calling it a quasi-judicial body advising the President.
It is constituted by a **Department of Legal Affairs** notification **every 3 years**.
The **23rd Law Commission** runs **1 Sep 2024 - 31 Aug 2027**.

n27da9bb175f.s: The report of a Joint State Public Service Commission is submitted to:
n27da9bb175f.x: A JSPSC reports to each Governor concerned, and the report is laid before each State Legislature.
xa: **CAG (State accounts)** → Governor; State Legislature.
**Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities** → President; Parliament; also **sent to the states** (Art. **350B**).
**UPSC** → President; Parliament with a memorandum on non-acceptance (Art. **323**).

nbe66a094d21.s: The report of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is submitted to the President and:
o: submitted to the Inter-State Council for approval
laid only before the Lok Sabha
laid before Parliament and sent to the States
laid only before the concerned State Legislatures
nbe66a094d21.x: Under Article 350B, the report of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is submitted to the President, laid before Parliament and also sent to the concerned States.
nbe66a094d21.tq: Remember the additional transmission to the States as the distinguishing feature.
