xs: The **Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities**' report goes to the **President**, is **laid before Parliament** and **sent to the states** — option **(3)**.
This is under **Art. 350B**.
xa: ⚠ Linguistic minorities are **not notified** under the **NCM Act** — the Art. 350B officer oversees them.
The Special Officer is the **only constitutional** body among NITI Aayog, NCM, Special Officer, NHRC (**APPSC-G2 2023**).
**NCSC/NCST/NCBC** also report to the **President**, laid before **Parliament**.

n787f5786ff8.s: Which of the following is a constitutional body?
n787f5786ff8.x: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is under Article 350B; NITI Aayog is executive and the NCM and NHRC are statutory.
xa: This count question was asked in **APPSC-G2 2023**.
⚠ **NCM** = statutory; **Special Officer** = constitutional.
The NHRC was set up on **12 Oct 1993** under the Protection of Human Rights Act.

n885804f6676.s: In the order of precedence, which of the following groups is placed at rank 9A?
o: Chairperson of UPSC, Chief Election Commissioner and Comptroller and Auditor General
Chairpersons of NCM, NCSC and NCST
Chairperson of the Finance Commission, Attorney General and Cabinet Secretary
Chairpersons of the State Election Commission and State Finance Commission
n885804f6676.x: The Chairperson of the UPSC, the Chief Election Commissioner and the CAG are placed at rank 9A in the order of precedence. The Chairpersons of NCM, NCSC and NCST are placed at rank 17.
n885804f6676.tq: Compare the two stated rank groups instead of relying on the constitutional status of the bodies.
xs: **UPSC Chairperson**, **Chief Election Commissioner** and **CAG** are at rank **9A** — option **(1)**.
The chairpersons of **NCM, NCSC and NCST** are at rank **17**, so option 2 is wrong.
xa: UPSC (Art. **315**), Election Commission (Art. **324**) and CAG (Art. **148**) are **constitutional** bodies.
NCM is **statutory**; NCSC (Art. **338**) and NCST (Art. **338A**) are constitutional.
Both Houses consider annual reports of constitutional bodies — **Rajya Sabha** has equal status.

nindian-polity-65-4.s: The Advocate General of a State is provided for under Article:
nindian-polity-65-4.x: Article 165 covers the Advocate General; 76 is the Attorney General, 148 the CAG and 280 the Finance Commission.
n: The office of the Attorney General of India is governed by Article 76. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The office of the Advocate General of a State is governed by Article 165. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The office of the Comptroller and Auditor General is governed by Article 148. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Finance Commission of India is governed by Article 280. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Comptroller and Auditor General is a constitutional body under Article 148. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Advocate General is a constitutional body under Article 165. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xa: The AG holds office during the **pleasure of the President**; the Advocate General during the **pleasure of the Governor**.
The CAG's tenure is **six years** or until age **65**.
The AG must be qualified to be a **Supreme Court judge**; the Advocate General a **High Court judge**.

nindian-polity-65-7.s: The CAG holds office for six years or up to the age of ____, whichever is earlier.
nindian-polity-65-7.x: The CAG (Article 148) serves six years or until age 65, and is removed like a Supreme Court judge.
n: The office of the Comptroller and Auditor General is governed by Article 148. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The President appoints the Comptroller and Auditor General. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Comptroller and Auditor General is removed on the same grounds and in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The tenure of the Comptroller and Auditor General is six years or until the age of 65 years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Comptroller and Auditor General is a constitutional body under Article 148. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xa: CAG (Union accounts) reports go to the **President** → Parliament (**Art. 151**).
CAG (State accounts) reports go to the **Governor** → State Legislature.
In the order of precedence, the **CAG**, **CEC** and **UPSC Chairperson** share rank **9A**.

nindian-polity-65-8.s: State Election Commissions are provided for under which Articles?
nindian-polity-65-8.x: State Election Commissions fall under Articles 243-K and 243-ZA; 243-I and 243-Y cover State Finance Commissions.
n: The State Finance Commission is governed by Articles 243-I and 243-Y. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The State Election Commission is governed by Articles 243-K and 243-ZA. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Election Commission of India is governed by Article 324. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is governed by Article 338. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
Local body elections are conducted solely by the State Election Commission under Article 243-K. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
Local body financial devolution is recommended by the State Finance Commission under Article 243-I. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xa: ⚠ The **ECI** does **not** conduct local body elections — only the **State Election Commission** does.
The State Election Commissioner is removed like a **High Court judge**.
The SFC is appointed by the **Governor**, every **five years**.
The **NCST** is under **338-A**; the **NCBC** under **338-B**.

nindian-polity-65-9.s: Under Article 317, both the UPSC and SPSC members are removed only by the:
nindian-polity-65-9.x: Under Article 317, members of both the UPSC and State PSCs can be removed only by the President, after a Supreme Court inquiry. The Governor appoints State PSC members but cannot remove them.
nindian-polity-65-9.tq: Discriminate who appoints a State PSC member from who removes them.
n: The members of both the Union Public Service Commission and State Public Service Commissions are removed only by the President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
Removal of members of the Union Public Service Commission and State Public Service Commissions is carried out under Article 317. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
Removal of members of the Union Public Service Commission and State Public Service Commissions involves a Supreme Court inquiry. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xs: Under **Article 317**, members of both the **UPSC** and **SPSCs** are removed **only by the President** — option **(1)**.
Removal follows a **Supreme Court inquiry**.
The **Governor** appoints SPSC members but cannot remove them.
xa: PSCs are provided under **Article 315** (Arts **315-323**).
⚠ A **JSPSC** is **statutory** — created by Parliament at the request of 2+ states, though Art. **315** provides for it.
The PSC system began in **1926**; UPSC in **1950**.
UPSC reports go to the **President** (**Art. 323**); SPSC reports to the **Governor**.

nindian-polity-65-36.s: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
nindian-polity-65-36.x: The 7th Amendment (1956) inserted the linguistic minorities officer; the 65th set up the joint SC/ST Commission and the 89th split off the NCST.
n: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes was bifurcated from the National Commission for Scheduled Castes through the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The National Commission for Backward Classes received full constitutional status through the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The office of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities was inserted by the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The National Commission for Backward Classes received constitutional status under Article 338-B through the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The National Commission for Backward Classes is a constitutional body under Article 338-B. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xa: ⚠ The **NCBC** is **not merely** a statutory body under the **1993 Act** — it is constitutional under **338-B**.
All these bodies submit reports to the **President**.
The **GST Council** (**279A**) came by the **101st Amendment, 2016**.

nindian-polity-26-12.s: The qualifications of members of the Finance Commission are determined by:
nindian-polity-26-12.x: The President appoints the members, but Parliament determines their qualifications by law.
n: The President appoints the members of the Finance Commission. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The President does not determine the qualifications of Finance Commission members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The Union Cabinet does not determine the qualifications of Finance Commission members. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
xa: The Commission has **five** members — **one Chairman** and **four other members**.
Its report goes to the **President**, laid before Parliament with an **explanatory memorandum** (**Art. 281**).
First Finance Commission: **1951**, chaired by **K.C. Neogy**.

nindian-polity-65-46.s: Who appoints the State Election Commissioner?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
nindian-polity-65-46.x: The Governor appoints the State Election Commissioner and the Advocate General; the President appoints the Attorney General and the Finance Commission.
n: The President appoints the Attorney General of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Advocate General of a State holds office during the pleasure of the Governor. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Governor appoints the State Election Commission. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The President appoints the Finance Commission of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xa: The Governor also appoints the **State Finance Commission** (**243-I**).
The AG serves at the **pleasure of the President**; the Advocate General at the **pleasure of the Governor**.
⚠ The Governor appoints SPSC members, but only the **President** can remove them (**Art. 317**).

n408b8f78638.s: Besides a chairperson and a vice-chairperson, the National Commission for Minorities has how many members?
n408b8f78638.x: The NCM has a chairperson, a vice-chairperson and five members; five of the seven must be from notified minorities.
xa: NCM is **statutory** (NCM Act **1992**), under **Minority Affairs**.
Precursor: **Minorities Commission**, **1978** MHA resolution.
**Harjit Singh Grewal** was appointed NCM chairperson in Jul 2026 for a full **3-year** term.

n92371e32c34.s: The National Commission for Minorities functions under which ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
n92371e32c34.x: The NCM is a statutory body that functions under the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
xa: ⚠ **NCM** = statutory; **Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities** = constitutional (Art. **350B**).
NCM has **civil court powers** (summon witnesses, requisition records).
NCM chairperson ranks **17** in the order of precedence.

nd7c7c213658.s: The National Human Rights Commission was set up on 12 October ____ under the Protection of Human Rights Act.
nd7c7c213658.x: The NHRC was set up on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; it is a statutory body.
xa: NHRC is under the **Home Affairs** ministry.
NHRC is a **quasi-judicial** body with **civil court powers**.
Other quasi-judicial examples: **SEBI**, **CIC**, **Mental Health Review Commission**.

n8627b9aabe3.s: All Union Cabinet Ministers became members of the National Development Council from:
n8627b9aabe3.x: The NDC was created by executive resolution; all Union Cabinet Ministers became members from 1967.
xa: **Sarkaria Commission:** give the NDC **constitutional status under Art. 263** and rename it **"National Economic and Development Council"**.
The NDC is an executive body, like the **Planning Commission** and **NITI Aayog**.
The Planning Commission (**March 1950**) had **no state representation**.

nefe41ac203a.s: State Commissions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes are established under:
nefe41ac203a.x: State SC and ST Commissions are set up under State laws; they are not directly created by Articles 338 and 338A.
xa: **K.S. Jawahar** is AP **State SC Commission** chairman.

n87b5e7226b9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about State-level bodies?
o: State Finance Commissions are provided for under Articles 243I and 243Y
A Joint State Public Service Commission is created by Parliament at the request of two or more States
A Joint State Public Service Commission is a statutory body
State Information Commissions are constitutional bodies under Article 315
n87b5e7226b9.x: State Information Commissions are statutory bodies under the RTI Act, 2005, not constitutional bodies.
xa: ⚠ Art. **315** provides for a JSPSC, but the JSPSC itself is statutory.
A JSPSC reports to **each Governor concerned**, laid before **each State Legislature**.
State Finance Commissions are set up **every 5 years**.

na1bc54df433.s: Which one of the following bodies was established first?
o: Public Service Commission at the central level
na1bc54df433.x: The predecessor of the UPSC, the Public Service Commission, was established in 1926. The Federal Public Service Commission followed under the Government of India Act, 1935, and the UPSC came into existence in 1950.
na1bc54df433.tq: Use the earliest date to eliminate the later constitutional bodies.
xs: The **Public Service Commission** (UPSC's predecessor) came first, in **1926** — option **(3)**.
**Election Commission** — **1950**; first **Finance Commission** — **1951**; **NDC** — **1952**.
The **Federal PSC** followed under the **GoI Act 1935**, and the **UPSC** in **1950**.
xa: **Inter-State Council** — **1990**; **NHRC** — **1993**.
⚠ UPSC and ECI both date to **1950**, but the PSC predecessor dates to **1926**.

n15a28a9c6a5.s: In which year was the Inter-State Council set up?
n15a28a9c6a5.x: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990; the ECI dates from 1950, the First Finance Commission 1951 and the NDC 1952.
xa: UPSC's predecessor **Public Service Commission** — **1926**.
The Inter-State Council is **constitutional** under Art. **263**; the NDC is **executive**.

n0716ab5c0ee.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the establishment years of the Inter-State Council, NCM and NHRC?
n0716ab5c0ee.x: The Inter-State Council was established in 1990, the NCM in 1992 and the NHRC in 1993.
n0716ab5c0ee.tq: Arrange the institutions by their establishment years.
xs: The sequence is **1990, 1992, 1993** — option **(1)**.
xa: NCM precursor: **Minorities Commission**, **1978** MHA resolution.
NHRC was set up on **12 Oct 1993** under the Protection of Human Rights Act.
⚠ Inter-State Council is constitutional (Art. **263**); NCM and NHRC are **statutory**.

nf7f231ea758.s: Under Section 6 of the DSPE Act, the CBI generally requires which of the following to act in a State?
o: Sanction of the Governor of the State
Prior consent of the concerned State Government
Approval of the concerned High Court
Consent of the Supreme Court in every case
nf7f231ea758.x: Section 6 of the DSPE Act requires the consent of the concerned State Government; several States have withdrawn general consent.
xa: The CBI draws its powers from the **DSPE Act 1946** and is itself **non-statutory**.
CBI origin: **Santhanam Committee (1962-63)**; it is under **Personnel (DoPT)**.
CBI Director selection: **PM, CJI (or nominee), Leader of Opposition**.

nindian-polity-1-47.s: Who was the first Chairman of the Finance Commission?
nindian-polity-1-47.x: The First Finance Commission was constituted in 1951 with K.C. Neogy as Chairman.
n: The First Finance Commission was set up in 1952, according to some sources. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
K.C. Neogy was the first Chairman of the Finance Commission. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Chairman of the Planning Commission in an ex-officio capacity. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Arvind Panagariya was the first Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xa: ⚠ Some sources say the Finance Commission was set up in **1952**.
The Planning Commission came by a **Cabinet Resolution** of **15 March 1950**; NITI Aayog by a **Cabinet Resolution** of **1 January 2015**.
The Finance Commission (**Art. 280**) has **five** members — a Chairman and **four** others.

nindian-polity-1-49.s: The Inter-State Council is set up by the President under Article:
nindian-polity-1-49.x: Article 263 empowers the President to set up the Inter-State Council, first set up in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation.
n: The Inter-State Council was first established in May or December 1990. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xa: ⚠ First establishment is given as **May or December 1990**.
It is a **constitutional** inter-state body, unlike river water tribunals (**statutory**, **1956** Act) and the **North Eastern Council** (**NEC Act 1971**).
The **National Security Council** is **extra-constitutional** (executive order, **1998**).
Sarkaria also proposed renaming the NDC "**National Economic and Development Council**" with status under **Art. 263**.

nindian-polity-65-43.s: NITI Aayog was established through a Cabinet Resolution dated:
nindian-polity-65-43.x: NITI Aayog was set up by a Cabinet Resolution of 1 January 2015; the Planning Commission by one of 15 March 1950.
n: The Law Commission of India is constituted periodically by executive order. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The National Development Council was established through an Executive Order dated 6 August 1952. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Planning Commission was established through a Cabinet Resolution dated 15 March 1950. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
NITI Aayog was established through a Cabinet Resolution dated 1 January 2015. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
An extra-constitutional or non-statutory body is established through an executive order or cabinet resolution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
NITI Aayog is an example of an extra-constitutional or non-statutory body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Planning Commission is an example of an extra-constitutional or non-statutory body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
NITI Aayog is not a constitutional body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
NITI Aayog is not a statutory body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xa: ⚠ Other notes call the Planning Commission's instrument a "Government resolution" and the NDC's an "Executive resolution".
The NDC includes the PM, all Union Cabinet ministers (since **1967**), all CMs and UT administrators.
NITI Aayog's **Governing Council** has all CMs and LGs.

n36769c30fcd.s: The origin of the Central Bureau of Investigation is associated with which committee and period?
n36769c30fcd.x: The origin of the CBI is associated with the Santhanam Committee of 1962–63.
n36769c30fcd.tq: Match the institution with the committee and period specifically linked to its origin.
xs: The CBI originated from the **Santhanam Committee (1962-63)** — option **(2)**.
The **Sarkaria Commission** is linked with the NDC proposal under Art. **263**, not the CBI.
xa: The CBI draws powers from the **DSPE Act 1946** and is **non-statutory**.
CBI Director selection: **PM, CJI (or nominee), Leader of Opposition**.
Federal flashpoint: **CBI general-consent withdrawals** (2026).

n2be70231f6f.s: Who chaired the first Law Commission of India constituted in 1834?
n2be70231f6f.x: The first Law Commission, constituted in 1834, was chaired by Lord Macaulay.
n2be70231f6f.tq: Associate the earliest commission with its chairperson and distinguish it from the first post-Independence commission.
xs: The first Law Commission (**1834**) was chaired by **Lord Macaulay** — option **(2)**.
**M.C. Setalvad** chaired the **first post-Independence** commission (**1955**); **K.C. Neogi** is linked to the **Advisory Planning Board (1946)**.
xa: The Law Commission is constituted **every 3 years** by Department of Legal Affairs notification.
The **23rd Law Commission**: **1 Sep 2024 - 31 Aug 2027**.
It is advisory — **not quasi-judicial**.

nindian-polity-1-54.s: Which Constitutional Amendment lowered the voting age to 18?
nindian-polity-1-54.x: The 61st Amendment lowered the voting age to 18; it was first exercised in the 1989 general election.
n: Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Sukumar Sen served as Chief Election Commissioner from 1950 to 1958. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
V.S. Ramadevi was the first woman Chief Election Commissioner. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
The voting age was lowered to 18 by the 61st Amendment. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
The voting age of 18 was first exercised in the 1989 General Election. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xa: **VVPAT** was first used at **Noksen**, **Nagaland** (**4 September 2013**).
The **Election Commission** (**Art. 324**) was set up in **1950**.
The **CEC** is removed in the same manner as a **Supreme Court judge**.

nindian-polity-1-55.s: VVPAT was first used in 2013 in which election?
nindian-polity-1-55.x: VVPAT was first used in the Noksen Assembly by-election in Nagaland on 4 September 2013.
n: VVPAT was first used in the Noksen Assembly by-election in Nagaland on 4 September 2013. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xa: First CEC: **Sukumar Sen** (**1950 to 1958**); first woman CEC: **V.S. Ramadevi**.
**Estimates Committee** first constituted in **1950**.
Ethics Committees: **Rajya Sabha (1997)**, **Lok Sabha (2000)**.
First Classical Language: **Tamil**.

nd443f422830.s: Which one of the following is the odd one out on the basis of constitutional status?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
nd443f422830.x: The NCBC, CAG and Finance Commission are constitutional bodies. NITI Aayog is an executive, non-statutory body created by Cabinet resolution.
nd443f422830.tq: Spot the executive body placed among constitutional bodies; status, not subject matter, is the basis of grouping.
xs: **NITI Aayog** is the odd one out — it is an **executive** body, not constitutional — option **(2)**.
**Finance Commission** (Art. **280**), **NCBC** (Art. **338B**) and **CAG** (Art. **148**) are constitutional.
xa: This was asked in **APPSC-GS 2025**.
NITI Aayog was created by **Cabinet resolution** on **1 Jan 2015**.
Other executive bodies: **Planning Commission**, **NDC**, **Law Commission**.

ne9f720e0512.s: The headquarters of the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) is located at:
ne9f720e0512.x: IFSCA is headquartered at GIFT City, Gandhinagar. It functions under the Ministry of Finance.
ne9f720e0512.tq: Use the distinctive headquarters location to separate IFSCA from the Mumbai- and Delhi-based regulators.
xs: **IFSCA** is headquartered at **GIFT City, Gandhinagar** — option **(4)**.
**Hyderabad** is IRDAI; **Mumbai** is RBI and SEBI; **New Delhi** is PFRDA and IBBI.
xa: IFSCA was set up on **27 Apr 2020** under the **IFSCA Act 2019**.
It promotes **FinTech** and **regulatory and innovation sandboxes**.
It comes under the **Ministry of Finance**.

n817ec0599ca.s: The establishment of IRDAI was recommended by which committee?
n817ec0599ca.x: The Malhotra Committee recommended IRDAI, set up in April 2000 at Hyderabad under the IRDA Act, 1999.
xa: ⚠ Classic trap: "NOT correct about IRDAI" = the **Gadgil Committee** statement.
Malhotra Committee: set up **1993**, reported **1994**.
IRDAI is the apex regulator of **insurance and reinsurance** companies.

n349979e515f.s: The Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority is a statutory authority under the Companies Act, 2013, functioning under the:
n349979e515f.x: IEPF Authority is a statutory authority under the Companies Act, 2013, under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
n349979e515f.tq: Distinguish the parent ministry from financial regulators with related functions.
xs: The **IEPF Authority** is statutory under the **Companies Act 2013**, under the **Ministry of Corporate Affairs** — option **(4)**.
It is not an RBI body (unlike **DICGC**).
xa: **NFRA** (Companies Act **2013**) oversees auditing and accounting standards.
**IBBI** is also under **Corporate Affairs**.
IRDAI's **Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund** is a separate fund under **Sec. 16A**.

n2e0dd648db6.s: SEBI, first set up by a resolution in 1988, acquired statutory status in:
n2e0dd648db6.x: SEBI became a statutory body under the SEBI Act, 1992.
xa: ⚠ The **APPSC-GS 2018** key gives **12 Apr 1992** for autonomous/statutory status.
SEBI HQ **Mumbai**; regional offices in **New Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, Ahmedabad**.
SEBI replaced the **Controller of Capital Issues**.

nc215dbde799.s: External members of the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee are appointed by the Centre for:
nc215dbde799.x: The six-member MPC has three external members appointed by the Centre for 4 years; the Governor chairs it with a casting vote.
xa: The MPC fixes the **repo rate**.
RBI members: **Governor + a Deputy Governor + one officer**.
Objectives: **price stability** primary; growth secondary.

n046d15f009d.s: Under Section 45ZA of the RBI Act, 1934, the Centre, in consultation with the RBI, sets the inflation target every:
n046d15f009d.x: Section 45ZA lets the Centre, consulting the RBI, set the inflation target every five years.
xa: Inflation targeting was adopted in **2016**, on the **Urjit Patel Committee** (**2014**) recommendation.
Target: **4% CPI-Combined ±2%**; nominal anchor **headline CPI (base year 2024)**.
The **MPC** is a **six-member** statutory body that fixes the **repo rate** — **3** from the RBI, **3** external members for **4 years**.
The **Governor** chairs the MPC with a **casting vote**; **price stability** is the primary objective.

n6d2f6f2328b.s: The inflation target under India's flexible inflation-targeting framework is:
o: 6% headline CPI with no tolerance band
4% CPI-Combined with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%
2% CPI-Combined with a tolerance band of plus or minus 4%
4% WPI with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%
n6d2f6f2328b.x: The target is 4% CPI-Combined with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%. The framework uses CPI-Combined, not WPI, as the specified measure.
n6d2f6f2328b.tq: Check both the central target and the inflation measure before accepting the option.
xs: The target is **4% CPI-Combined** with a band of **±2%** — option **(2)**.
It uses **CPI-Combined**, not WPI, and does have a tolerance band.
xa: Inflation targeting was **adopted in 2016** on the **Urjit Patel Committee (2014)** recommendation.
The target is set **every 5 years** under **Sec. 45ZA**.
Nominal anchor: **headline CPI (base year 2024)**.

n58c9df64d4b.s: Which of the following correctly states the hierarchy of objectives under the inflation-targeting framework?
o: Price stability is primary and growth is secondary
Growth is primary and price stability is secondary
Fiscal consolidation is primary and price stability is optional
Exchange-rate stability is primary and growth is excluded
n58c9df64d4b.x: Price stability is the primary objective, while growth is treated as a secondary objective.
n58c9df64d4b.tq: Identify the stated priority rather than selecting a neighbouring macroeconomic objective.
xs: Under inflation targeting, **price stability is primary** and **growth is secondary** — option **(1)**.
Option 2 reverses the order.
xa: The **MPC** (**six** members) fixes the **repo rate**.
Target: **4% CPI-Combined ±2%**, adopted **2016**.
**Urjit Patel Committee (2014)** recommended inflation targeting.

n94ebaafce05.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the Reserve Bank of India?
o: Regulating and supervising banks and NBFCs
Issuing the one-rupee note and coins
n94ebaafce05.x: The Ministry of Finance issues the one-rupee note and coins. RBI functions include monetary authority, foreign-exchange management under FEMA, and regulation and supervision of banks and NBFCs.
n94ebaafce05.tq: Find the exception by separating RBI's currency function from the one-rupee and coin issuing authority.
xs: **Issuing the ₹1 note and coins** is NOT an RBI function — the **Ministry of Finance** issues them — option **(3)**.
The RBI is the **monetary authority**, regulator of **banks and NBFCs**, and forex manager under **FEMA 1999**.
xa: RBI is also **banker and debt manager** to the government via its **Public Debt Office**.
RBI was set up on **1 Apr 1935** under the **RBI Act 1934**.
A **Public Debt Management Cell** was set up to reduce RBI's conflict of interest.

n2bfa10c688a.s: India's flexible inflation-targeting framework, adopted in 2016, was based on the recommendation of which committee?
n2bfa10c688a.x: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014) recommended inflation targeting, adopted in 2016 with a 4% CPI-Combined target. The Narasimham Committee dealt with banking reforms, the Malhotra Committee with insurance reforms, and the Raghuram Rajan Committee with financial-sector reforms, not the inflation-targeting framework.
xs: Inflation targeting (adopted **2016**) came from the **Urjit Patel Committee** (**2014**) — option **(2)**.
The **Malhotra Committee** dealt with **insurance reforms** (private entry → IRDA Act).
xa: Target: **4% CPI-Combined ±2%**; set **every 5 years** (Sec. **45ZA**).
Malhotra Committee: set up **1993**, reported **1994**.
⚠ Critique: **a decade** of inflation targeting shows mixed evidence on output and jobs.

nde755b3acb6.s: The Securities and Exchange Board of India replaced which of the following authorities?
o: Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
nde755b3acb6.x: SEBI replaced the Controller of Capital Issues in the regulation of the capital market.
nde755b3acb6.tq: Use the predecessor-successor relationship to eliminate nearby regulatory bodies.
xs: SEBI replaced the **Controller of Capital Issues** — option **(4)**.
The **Forward Markets Commission** was **merged into** SEBI (Sep **2015**) — it was not what SEBI replaced.
**BIFR** was dissolved in **2016** with cases going to NCLT/NCLAT; **NHB** is the housing refinancer.
xa: SEBI serves **issuers, investors and intermediaries**.
SEBI has **quasi-judicial** powers: investigates, summons, passes orders and penalties.
SEBI Act **1992**; HQ **Mumbai**.

n754eadc4610.s: The Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC), set up in 2010, is chaired by:
n754eadc4610.x: The non-statutory FSDC is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and handles financial stability and inter-regulatory coordination.
xa: FSDC: **non-statutory**, set up **2010**, chaired by the **Union Finance Minister**.
Its sub-committee is chaired by the **RBI Governor**.
Economic Survey 2025-26 ("Refining the Regulatory Touch"): regulators moving to **anticipatory regulation**.

n73bbaa9f98d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about SEBI?
o: SEBI can investigate, summon persons and impose penalties
Appeals against SEBI's orders lie first to the NCLAT
Appeals against SEBI's orders lie to the Securities Appellate Tribunal and then to the Supreme Court
Since 2014, orders of IRDAI and PFRDA are also appealable to the SAT
n73bbaa9f98d.x: Appeals against SEBI's orders go to the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) and then to the Supreme Court, not the NCLAT.
xa: SEBI: non-statutory from **12 Apr 1988**; statutory powers **30 Jan 1992**; **SEBI Act 1992**.
SEBI replaced the **Controller of Capital Issues**; HQ **Mumbai**.
The **Forward Markets Commission** merged into **SEBI** in Sep **2015**.
FSLRC (**B.N. Srikrishna**) proposed expanding SAT into a **Financial Sector Appellate Tribunal**.

ne963643d052.s: In 2015, the FDI cap in the insurance sector was raised to:
ne963643d052.x: The insurance FDI cap rose from 26% (2000) to 49% (2015), 74% (2021) and 100% (2025-26).
xa: The **100%** cap came from the **Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha** Act, passed **17 Dec 2025**.
The same Act inserted **Sec. 16A** (Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund).
The **IRDA Act 1999** first opened insurance to private participation.

n67cf82f085e.s: Section 16A, inserted in the IRDA Act by the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha Act, 2025, creates the:
n67cf82f085e.x: The 2025 Act inserted Section 16A in the IRDA Act to create the Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund; it also allows up to 100% FDI in insurers.
xa: PEPF package (operationalised **Jul 2026**): salesperson tagging, **perpetual licensing**, revised actuarial and investment rules.
IRDAI's regulation-making power: **Sec. 114A**, Insurance Act **1938**.

n804f6d7ae05.s: The Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission was chaired by:
n804f6d7ae05.x: The Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission was chaired by Justice B.N. Srikrishna.
n804f6d7ae05.tq: Test the chairperson of a commission against plausible judicial names.
xs: The **FSLRC** was chaired by **Justice B.N. Srikrishna** — option **(4)**.
It was set up in **2011** and reported in **2013**.
xa: Proposals: a single **Indian Financial Code** and a **Unified Financial Agency** merging SEBI, FMC, IRDA and PFRDA.
Also: **Financial Redress Agency**, **Public Debt Management Agency**, **Resolution Corporation**.
RBI keeps **banking and payments**; SAT to become a **Financial Sector Appellate Tribunal**.

n345597a6caf.s: Which one of the following was NOT a key proposal of the Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission?
o: A Unified Financial Agency merging SEBI, FMC, IRDA and PFRDA
A separate constitutional court for financial disputes
n345597a6caf.x: The Commission proposed a single Indian Financial Code, a Unified Financial Agency, a Public Debt Management Agency and other reforms, but not a separate constitutional court.
n345597a6caf.tq: Find the proposal that does not belong to the commission’s reform package.
xs: A **separate constitutional court for financial disputes** was NOT an FSLRC proposal — option **(2)**.
FSLRC did propose a single **Indian Financial Code**, a **Unified Financial Agency** (SEBI, FMC, IRDA, PFRDA) and a **Public Debt Management Agency**.
xa: Other proposals: **Financial Redress Agency**, **Resolution Corporation**, and SAT expanded into a **Financial Sector Appellate Tribunal**.
FSLRC was chaired by Justice **B.N. Srikrishna**; set up **2011**, report **2013**.
Under FSLRC, the **RBI keeps banking and payments**.

n25c2e66e829.s: The Forward Markets Commission was merged into SEBI in:
n25c2e66e829.x: The Forward Markets Commission, which regulated commodities, was merged into SEBI in September 2015.
n25c2e66e829.tq: Use the exact month-year to distinguish the merger from later regulatory shifts.
xs: The **Forward Markets Commission** (commodities) merged into **SEBI** in **September 2015** — option **(2)**.
**2019** is when HFC regulation moved from NHB to the **RBI**.
xa: ⚠ FMC → **SEBI**; HFCs → **RBI** (not NHB); chit funds → **state governments**.
**FSLRC** had proposed a **Unified Financial Agency** merging SEBI, FMC, IRDA and PFRDA.
**BIFR** was dissolved on **1 Dec 2016**.

nc1792ee935b.s: Which body oversees auditing and accounting standards under the Companies Act, 2013?
nc1792ee935b.x: The National Financial Reporting Authority oversees auditing and accounting standards under the Companies Act, 2013.
nc1792ee935b.tq: Match the statutory body with its technical oversight function.
xs: **NFRA** oversees **auditing and accounting standards** under the **Companies Act 2013** — option **(3)**.
**IEPF Authority** protects investors; **DICGC** insures deposits; **FSDC** is the apex coordination council.
xa: IEPF Authority is under **Corporate Affairs** (Companies Act **2013**).
Insurers now use **Ind AS 117 and 109**, enforced by **IRDAI**.
**FSDC** was set up in **2010**.

n3f25315827a.s: PFRDA’s NPS e-Shramik is intended to extend pension coverage to:
n3f25315827a.x: NPS e-Shramik extends pension coverage to informal workers.
n3f25315827a.tq: Infer the target beneficiary from the scheme’s name and stated purpose.
xs: PFRDA's **NPS e-Shramik** extends pensions to **informal workers** — option **(3)**.
**FPIs** are linked to SEBI's **SWAGAT-FI**, not NPS.
xa: **PFRDA**: interim body by resolution in **2003**; statutory from **2014** under the **PFRDA Act 2013**.
PFRDA is headquartered in **New Delhi**.
Since **2014**, PFRDA orders are appealable to **SAT**.

n3141658df6a.s: SWAGAT-FI, in the context of SEBI’s recent initiatives, is associated with:
o: A single-window framework for trusted FPIs and FVCIs
A pension scheme for informal workers
n3141658df6a.x: SWAGAT-FI is a single-window framework for trusted Foreign Portfolio Investors and Foreign Venture Capital Investors.
n3141658df6a.tq: Test the exact expansion and target group of a similarly named initiative.
xs: **SWAGAT-FI** is SEBI's **single-window framework for trusted FPIs and FVCIs** — option **(1)**.
It came with an **India Market Access Portal** (Sep **2025**).
xa: ⚠ LENS (Sep 2025) prints it as **"SWAFAT-FI"**.
SEBI extended **IPO approval validity** to **30 Sep 2026** due to geopolitical tensions.
Off-market sale of unlisted shares to **≤200** buyers a year is not a deemed public issue.

n49507b2f4eb.s: Which accounting standards replaced IGAAP for insurers?
n49507b2f4eb.x: Ind AS 117 and Ind AS 109 replaced IGAAP for insurers, and IRDAI enforces their adoption.
n49507b2f4eb.tq: Pair the exact accounting standards with the insurance-sector transition.
xs: **Ind AS 117 and 109** replace **IGAAP** for insurers — option **(2)**.
**IRDAI** enforces their adoption.
**45ZA/45ZN** are RBI Act sections, not accounting standards.
xa: **D-SIIs** (FY 2025-26): **LIC, GIC Re, New India Assurance**.
**NFRA** oversees auditing and accounting standards under the **Companies Act 2013**.
IRDAI regulates under **Sec. 114A** of the Insurance Act **1938**.

n8bfc222da7b.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the Domestic Systemically Important Insurers for FY 2025–26?
o: General Insurance Corporation of India Re
n8bfc222da7b.x: The Domestic Systemically Important Insurers for FY 2025–26 are LIC, GIC Re and New India Assurance. HDFC Bank is listed among the D-SIBs, not the D-SIIs.
n8bfc222da7b.tq: Separate systemically important insurers from systemically important banks.
xs: **HDFC Bank** is NOT a Domestic Systemically Important Insurer — option **(1)**.
The **D-SIIs** for FY **2025-26** are **LIC**, **GIC Re** and **New India Assurance**.
xa: IRDAI is headquartered in **Hyderabad**.
Insurers now report under **Ind AS 117 and 109**, replacing IGAAP.
Insurance FDI cap is now **100%** (2025-26).

nae52b67a8d3.s: The Economic Survey 2025–26 described RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA as moving towards:
nae52b67a8d3.x: The Economic Survey 2025–26, under the theme ‘Refining the Regulatory Touch’, stated that these regulators are moving towards anticipatory regulation.
nae52b67a8d3.tq: Identify the precise policy direction from the stated current-affairs formulation.
xs: The **Economic Survey 2025-26** ("Refining the Regulatory Touch") says **RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA** are moving to **anticipatory regulation** — option **(2)**.
It is regulating ahead of problems, not only after market failure.
xa: RBI's **regulation-making framework (May 2025)** stresses transparency, consultation, periodic review.
Insurance law amendments (Dec **2025**) allow **100% FDI**.
Criticism: **overlapping mandates** among regulators.

nd94b2c2704a.x: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India was set up on 20 February 1997 under the TRAI Act, 1997.
nd94b2c2704a.tq: Discriminate between the establishment dates of different sectoral regulators.
xs: **TRAI** was set up on **20 February 1997** — option **(1)**.
**24 August 2004** is **APTEL**; **14 October 2003** is the **CCI**.
xa: **APPSC 2018** asked TRAI's year of establishment (**1997**).
TRAI regulates **tariffs**, **interconnection** and **quality of service**.
TRAI Chairperson: **Anil Kumar Lahoti**.

neea7d5a5d2b.s: Under the DPDP Rules, 2025, the Data Protection Board of India is a board of how many members?
neea7d5a5d2b.x: The DPDP Rules, 2025 provide for a four-member Data Protection Board, set up under the DPDP Act, 2023.
xa: DPBI is an **independent adjudicatory body**; DPDP Act enacted **August 2023**.
Penalties up to **₹250 crore**; **no imprisonment**.
Appeals: **TDSAT within 60 days**, then the **Supreme Court**.

ncd187d43764.s: Which of the following is a statutory body under the Ministry of Power?
o: Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board
ncd187d43764.x: CEA, APTEL and CERC are statutory bodies under the Ministry of Power.
xa: CERC is also the **regulator of carbon trading** under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme.
**SERCs** handle intra-state tariffs and consumer protection.
**PNGRB** is under **Petroleum & Natural Gas**, not Power.

n32e77e11979.s: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, the maximum penalty the Data Protection Board can impose is:
o: Rs 50 crore, with imprisonment up to 3 years
Rs 500 crore, with imprisonment up to 7 years
n32e77e11979.x: The Board can impose penalties of up to Rs 250 crore, and the Act provides no imprisonment. So the options with imprisonment are wrong, and Rs 50 crore or Rs 25 crore understate the ceiling.
n32e77e11979.tq: DPDP: up to Rs 250 crore, civil only.
xs: The DPBI can impose penalties up to **Rs 250 crore**, with **no imprisonment** — option **(2)**.
Options with imprisonment are wrong; lower figures understate the ceiling.
xa: The DPBI has **civil-court powers** under the **CPC, 1908**.
It can order **urgent remedial action** after a **data breach**.
DPDP Act **2023**: consent-based processing of digital personal data.

n71f7abf9b24.s: From 26 May 2017, appeals against orders of the Competition Commission of India lie to the:
o: High Court directly in every case
n71f7abf9b24.x: NCLAT became the appellate forum for CCI matters from 26 May 2017. Earlier, appeals lay to COMPAT, and a further appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
n71f7abf9b24.tq: Use the date to distinguish the present appellate forum from its predecessor.
xs: From **26 May 2017**, appeals against CCI orders go to the **NCLAT** — option **(3)**.
Earlier they went to the **Competition Appellate Tribunal (COMPAT)**.
A further appeal lies to the **Supreme Court**.
xa: **CERC/SERC** and **PNGRB** orders go to **APTEL**, then the Supreme Court.
**TRAI** matters go to **TDSAT**.
NCLAT upheld CCI's **abuse finding** against **Meta/WhatsApp**.

nb445ed74e51.s: An order of the Data Protection Board of India can be challenged in appeal before:
o: The TDSAT within 60 days, with a further appeal to the Supreme Court
nb445ed74e51.x: Appeals against the Board's orders go to the TDSAT within 60 days, and from there to the Supreme Court. The claim that appeals go directly to the Supreme Court is a known wrong statement. The High Court and NCLAT are not the appellate forums under the DPDP Act.
xs: DPBI orders can be appealed to **TDSAT within 60 days**, with a further appeal to the **Supreme Court** — option **(3)**.
⚠ "Appeals go **directly to the Supreme Court**" is a known **wrong** statement for the DPBI.
**NCLAT** is the appeal forum for **CCI**, not the DPBI.
xa: TDSAT has wider jurisdiction over **IT Act 2000** and **DPDP Act** matters.
Feb **2026**: **Delhi HC** issued notice on a plea calling the Board and its appellate tribunal **"Executive-controlled"**.
Criticism: the DPDP Act amends **RTI Section 8(1)(j)**, widening the personal-information exemption.

o: Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 and CCI
Companies Act, 1956 and Company Law Board
n01d84516da4.x: The Competition Act, 2002 replaced the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969 and its MRTP Commission.
n01d84516da4.tq: Match the replacing law with the predecessor law and institution.
xs: The **Competition Act 2002** replaced the **MRTP Act, 1969** and its **MRTP Commission** — option **(3)**.
**COMPAT** was the CCI's old appellate tribunal, replaced by **NCLAT** from **26 May 2017**.
xa: The Act was amended by the **Competition (Amendment) Act, 2007**.
The CCI was set up on **14 October 2003**.
CCI is under the **Ministry of Corporate Affairs**.

nce4605cc733.s: Which one of the following was among the laws or orders consolidated by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006?
nce4605cc733.x: The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was among the eight laws and orders consolidated by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
nce4605cc733.tq: Identify the food-sector predecessor law among statutes belonging to different regulatory fields.
xs: The **Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954** was among the **eight** laws consolidated by the **FSS Act 2006** — option **(4)**.
The **MRTP Act 1969** was replaced by the **Competition Act 2002**, not the FSS Act.
xa: Others consolidated: **Fruit Products Order 1955**, **Meat Food Products Order 1973**.
FSSAI was set up in **2008**, under **Health & Family Welfare**.
**Eat Right India** — launched **2018**.

nb44ecefe92a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan (VBSA) Bill, 2025?
o: It would repeal the AICTE Act, 1987 and the NCTE Act, 1993
It is the current form of the Higher Education Commission of India proposal
It would repeal the UGC Act, 1956
It was introduced in the Rajya Sabha and passed in December 2025
nb44ecefe92a.x: The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2025 and referred to a Joint Committee of Parliament; it was not passed.
xa: It proposes three councils: **Regulatory**, **Accreditation** and **Standards**.
⚠ Trap: **Lok Sabha**, not Rajya Sabha; **referred**, not passed.

nd1f1d8a4fb8.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three councils proposed under the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025?
nd1f1d8a4fb8.x: The proposed Bill provides for Regulatory, Accreditation and Standards Councils. A Funding Council is not among the three councils listed.
nd1f1d8a4fb8.tq: Use the complete three-member institutional list to identify the added distractor.
xs: A **Funding Council** is NOT one of the three — option **(4)**.
The VBSA Bill proposes **Regulatory**, **Accreditation** and **Standards** councils.
xa: It would repeal the **UGC Act 1956**, **AICTE Act 1987** and **NCTE Act 1993**.
Introduced in the **Lok Sabha** in **Dec 2025**; referred to a **Joint Committee of Parliament**.
It is the current form of the **HECI** proposal.

n25970f780e8.s: The CCI's action against WhatsApp's 2021 privacy policy was taken on the ground of:
n25970f780e8.x: The WhatsApp case concerned abuse of dominant position; combinations means reviewing mergers and acquisitions.
xa: CCI fined **Meta/WhatsApp** **₹213.14 crore** for abuse of dominance.
**NCLAT** upheld the abuse finding; appeal is before an SC Bench headed by **CJI Surya Kant**.
Combinations: a **₹2,000 crore** deal-value threshold targets **"killer acquisitions"**.

n3a5adc83aaf.s: The proposed Digital Competition Bill seeks to pre-regulate:
o: Digital enterprises registered outside India alone
All online platforms irrespective of their size
n3a5adc83aaf.x: The proposed Digital Competition Bill would pre-regulate Systemically Significant Digital Enterprises.
n3a5adc83aaf.tq: Recall the exact defined category rather than broadening it to all digital platforms.
xs: The **Digital Competition Bill** would pre-regulate **Systemically Significant Digital Enterprises** — option **(2)**.
It targets significant players, not all platforms regardless of size.
xa: The CCI has set up a **Digital Markets Division**.
A **₹2,000 crore** deal-value threshold targets "killer acquisitions" of start-ups.
CCI fined **Meta/WhatsApp ₹213.14 crore** for abuse of dominance.

n0cea8a55755.s: The CCI imposed a penalty of ₹213.14 crore on Meta/WhatsApp for:
n0cea8a55755.x: The CCI fined Meta/WhatsApp ₹213.14 crore for abuse of dominance.
xa: **NCLAT** upheld the abuse finding; the appeal is before an SC Bench headed by **CJI Surya Kant**.
CCI's other areas: **anti-competitive agreements** (cartels, bid-rigging) and **combinations** (M&A).
Appeals from CCI go to **NCLAT** since **26 May 2017**.

n3026e887268.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the appointment of chairpersons of regulators?
o: Chairpersons are appointed by the Central Government
Chairpersons of regulators are elected by Parliament
For the CCI, the committee is headed by the Chief Justice of India or the CJI's nominee
Appointment is usually on the recommendation of a search-cum-selection committee
n3026e887268.x: Regulatory chairpersons are appointed by the Central Government, usually on a search-cum-selection committee's recommendation.
xa: **DPBI** members are also appointed by the Centre on a **Selection Committee**'s recommendation.
Removal: by the Centre, only on grounds in the **parent Act** and **after a hearing**.
CCI: **Chairperson + 2 to 6** other members.

n11b221363f9.s: The Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT) was set up in:
n11b221363f9.x: TDSAT was set up in May 2000 and also hears appeals under the IT Act, 2000 and the DPDP Act.
xa: Appeals against the **Data Protection Board** go to TDSAT **within 60 days**, then the **Supreme Court**.
⚠ TDSAT was created by the **TRAI (Amendment) Act**, not a "TDSAT Act, 2000".
TRAI = regulator; TDSAT = adjudicator.

nac278c28605.s: Under the current composition described for the Competition Commission of India, it consists of:
o: A Chairperson and two to six other members appointed by the Central Government
A Chairperson and exactly six members appointed by the Supreme Court
Only a Chairperson and one member appointed by the President
A Chairperson and two to six members appointed by the State Governments
nac278c28605.x: The current composition is a Chairperson and two to six other members, all appointed by the Central Government.
nac278c28605.tq: Check both the numerical range and the appointing authority; both are common sources of traps.
xs: The **CCI** has a **Chairperson + 2 to 6 other members**, all appointed by the **Central Government** — option **(1)**.
⚠ Older notes say "Chairperson and six Members"; the original **2002** Act allowed up to **10** members.
xa: CCI's selection committee is headed by the **CJI or a nominee**.
CCI was set up on **14 October 2003**.
Appeals: **NCLAT** (from **26 May 2017**), then the **Supreme Court**.

na33cac37249.s: From 1 July 2019, food businesses are prohibited from wrapping food in:
na33cac37249.x: From 1 July 2019, recycled plastics and newspaper may not be used to wrap food.
xa: This FSSAI packaging rule was asked in **APPSC 2019**.
**Eat Right India** (**2018**): safe, healthy and sustainable food.
FSSAI is under the **Ministry of Health & Family Welfare**.

n59e28c94006.s: The Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT), set up in May 2000, was created by:
n59e28c94006.x: TDSAT was created in May 2000 by the TRAI (Amendment) Act, which separated adjudication from TRAI's regulatory role. There is no separate 'TDSAT Act, 2000'; that is a common trap. The IT Act, 2000 only adds appeals that TDSAT hears, and the Telegraph Act, 1885 is the old telegraph law.
xs: **TDSAT** (May **2000**) was created by the **TRAI (Amendment) Act** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Some notes cite a **"TDSAT Act, 2000"** — that is the trap; no such Act created it.
The **IT Act 2000** only adds appeals that TDSAT hears.
xa: TRAI = **regulator**; TDSAT = **adjudicator**.
DPBI appeals: TDSAT **within 60 days**, then the **Supreme Court**.
TRAI itself was set up on **20 February 1997**.

nbcd970da18c.s: The Securities Appellate Tribunal was set up under the:
o: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999
nbcd970da18c.x: The Securities Appellate Tribunal was established under the SEBI Act, 1992.
nbcd970da18c.tq: Identify the parent statute rather than one of the regulators whose orders it reviews.
xs: The **Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT)** has its legal basis in the **SEBI Act, 1992** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Though SAT also hears appeals against **IRDAI** and **PFRDA**, it is set up under the **SEBI Act**, not their Acts.
xa: SAT hears appeals against orders of **SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA**.
Further appeal from SAT lies to the **Supreme Court on points of law** (asked by **UPSC**).

n09f1b08fa0a.s: An appeal against a decision of the Securities Appellate Tribunal to the Supreme Court lies on:
n09f1b08fa0a.x: A SAT decision can be appealed to the Supreme Court on points of law.
n09f1b08fa0a.tq: Identify the legally limited ground of further appeal.
xs: An appeal from the **Securities Appellate Tribunal** lies to the **Supreme Court on points of law** — so **questions of law only**, option **(3)**, is correct.
This is the **UPSC**-asked fact on SAT's further appeal; there is no appeal on facts, policy or general grievances.
xa: SAT was set up under the **SEBI Act, 1992**.
SAT's jurisdiction: appeals against **SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA** orders.
SC ordered a report on **5.7 lakh** pending consumer cases before the **NCDRC** (**Aug 2026**).

ndfaee99790c.s: The National Green Tribunal’s order relating to rat-hole mining in Meghalaya was principally concerned with:
o: Air pollution caused by diesel vehicles
ndfaee99790c.x: The 2014 ban on rat-hole mining in Meghalaya addressed unscientific and unsafe coal mining.
ndfaee99790c.tq: Use the issue rather than the date to identify the landmark order.
xs: The NGT's ban on **rat-hole mining** in **Meghalaya** (**2014**) addressed **unscientific and unsafe coal mining** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Tree felling for road works** was the issue behind the **BRO** order in **Uttarakhand** (**Aug 2023**), not Meghalaya.
**Yamuna floodplain** damage relates to the **Art of Living** fine (**2016**); **diesel vehicle** curbs targeted **air pollution** in **Delhi-NCR**.
xa: This rat-hole mining question was asked in **APPSC 2024**.
The **BRO** was told to plant **at least 10,000 trees** in Uttarakhand within **two months**.
⚠ The **NGT lacks an IT division** (a criticism in the notes).

ncfe3094536c.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 describes regulators as “mini-states” primarily because they combine which of the following functions?
o: Judicial, electoral and administrative functions only
ncfe3094536c.x: Regulators are described as “mini-states” because they combine rule-making, investigation and adjudication, corresponding broadly to legislative, executive and judicial functions.
ncfe3094536c.tq: Identify the functions combined by the institution rather than focusing on the metaphor.
xs: The **Economic Survey 2025-26** calls regulators **"mini-states"** because they combine **legislative, executive and judicial** functions — option **(2)** is correct.
Rule-making = **legislative**, investigation = **executive**, adjudication = **judicial**; electoral, military or diplomatic powers are not part of it.
Such concentrated power needs **internal checks** built into the design.
xa: ES 2025-26: regulation is a key point where the **State meets the economy**, so regulatory capacity is part of **State capacity**.
ES 2025-26 noted **no dedicated cadre** trained in regulation and proposed a **School for Regulations**.
Sanctions should be **proportional** to intent, scale and harm (ES 2025-26).

ne2c1100b2fa.s: Regulatory capture refers to a situation in which:
o: A regulator serves the industry it regulates rather than the public interest
A regulator transfers all functions to a ministry
A regulated industry is controlled directly by the judiciary
A regulator is abolished by the legislature
ne2c1100b2fa.x: Regulatory capture occurs when a regulator comes to serve the interests of the regulated industry instead of the public.
ne2c1100b2fa.tq: Use the precise meaning of the paired term rather than its ordinary meaning.
xs: **Regulatory capture** is when a regulator **serves the industry it regulates rather than the public** — option **(1)** is correct.
The theory is associated with **George Stigler** (**1971**).
xa: After the **SHANTI Act, 2025**, commentators urged more autonomy for **AERB** "to avoid **regulatory capture** risks".
**Conflict of interest**: a board member acquires an interest that may **prejudice duties**.
Independence safeguards: **fixed tenure**, **selection-committee** appointment, removal only on **statutory grounds**.

n655967abc29.s: The theory of regulatory capture is associated with:
n655967abc29.x: The theory of regulatory capture is associated with George Stigler, particularly his 1971 work.
xa: Regulatory capture = regulator serves the **industry** it regulates rather than the **public**.
**L. Chandra Kumar (1997)**: HC judicial review of tribunals is part of the **basic structure**.
**FSLRC** reported in **2013** with a draft **Indian Financial Code**.

nb5db9b89278.s: The Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission, which proposed moving from area-based to task-based financial regulation, was headed by:
nb5db9b89278.x: FSLRC was headed by Justice B.N. Srikrishna and reported in 2013 with a draft Indian Financial Code. Y.V. Reddy was an RBI Governor, Urjit Patel headed the committee on inflation targeting, and R.N. Malhotra headed the committee on insurance reforms.
xs: The **FSLRC** was headed by **Justice B.N. Srikrishna** — option **(1)** is correct.
It reported in **2013** with a draft **Indian Financial Code** (UPSC).
xa: FSLRC proposed **"area-based" → task-based** regulation.
It proposed a **Unified Financial Agency**, a **Financial Redressal Agency** and a **Financial Sector Appellate Tribunal**.

nb0cf30db050.s: Which one of the following is NOT regarded as a standard safeguard for regulatory independence?
o: Removal only on grounds stated in the statute
Unrestricted removal at the discretion of the parent ministry
nb0cf30db050.x: Fixed tenure, selection-committee appointment and statutory grounds for removal are standard safeguards. Unrestricted removal by a parent ministry weakens independence.
nb0cf30db050.tq: Find the option that reverses the institutional safeguard.
xs: **Unrestricted removal at the discretion of the parent ministry** is NOT a safeguard; it weakens independence — option **(2)** is correct.
The standard safeguards are **fixed tenure**, **selection-committee appointment** and **removal only on statutory grounds** — options (1), (3), (4).
xa: **Accountability**: annual reports and accounts are laid before **Parliament** and examined by **Departmentally Related Standing Committees**.
**Parent ministries** fund and administer most tribunals, e.g. **NGT** by **MoEFCC**.
**Regulatory capture** = regulator serving the industry rather than the public (**George Stigler, 1971**).

n97ec32c07fe.s: Annual reports and accounts of regulators are laid before Parliament and examined primarily by:
n97ec32c07fe.x: Regulators’ annual reports and accounts are laid before Parliament and examined by the Departmentally Related Standing Committees.
n97ec32c07fe.tq: Identify the parliamentary scrutiny mechanism linked to annual reports and accounts.
xs: Regulators' **annual reports and accounts** are laid before **Parliament** and examined by **Departmentally Related Standing Committees** — option **(2)** is correct.
This is a standard **accountability mechanism** for regulators; the Finance Commission, ECI or Inter-State Council have no such role in the notes.
xa: ES 2025-26: regulators are accountable to Parliament through **periodic reviews and published orders**.
Governing **boards** hold executive management to account.
Independence safeguards: **fixed tenure**, **selection committee**, removal on **statutory grounds**.

na27954b30c2.s: Under the Securities Markets Code Bill, 2025, board members must disclose:
na27954b30c2.x: The Bill requires disclosure of direct, indirect and family interests, and a member may be removed for a prejudicial interest.
xa: The Bill also provides **inter-regulatory coordination** on instruments overseen by several regulators.
**Conflict of interest** = a board member acquiring a financial/other interest that may prejudice duties.
The **SEBI-IRDAI law** (**2010**) placed **ULIPs** under **IRDAI** with a joint dispute mechanism.

n975f9e673c4.s: In the Madras Bar Association case (2025), the Supreme Court gave the government four months to set up which body?
n975f9e673c4.x: In Madras Bar Association (2025) the Supreme Court gave the government four months to set up a National Tribunals Commission to address tribunal capacity problems. The School for Regulations is an Economic Survey 2025-26 proposal, and the Unified Financial Agency and Financial Sector Appellate Tribunal are FSLRC proposals.
n975f9e673c4.tq: Madras Bar Assn 2025 -> National Tribunals Commission.
xs: In **Madras Bar Association (2025)**, the SC gave the government **four months** to set up the **National Tribunals Commission** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **School for Regulations** is an **ES 2025-26** proposal; **Unified Financial Agency** and **Financial Sector Appellate Tribunal** are **FSLRC** proposals.
xa: **L. Chandra Kumar (1997)**: HC judicial review of tribunals is part of the **basic structure**.
Most tribunals are funded and administered by **parent ministries**, e.g. **NGT** by **MoEFCC**.

nbb3b112934a.s: The decision in L. Chandra Kumar (1997) established that:
o: All tribunal decisions are immune from judicial review
Tribunals are superior to constitutional courts
Only the Supreme Court may review tribunal decisions
High Court judicial review of tribunals survives as part of the basic structure
nbb3b112934a.x: L. Chandra Kumar held that High Court judicial review of tribunals survives as part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
nbb3b112934a.tq: Identify the constitutional consequence rather than confusing judicial review with appellate jurisdiction.
xs: **L. Chandra Kumar (1997)** held that **High Court judicial review of tribunals** is part of the **basic structure** — option **(4)** is correct.
So tribunal decisions are not immune from review, and tribunals are not superior to constitutional courts.
xa: **Madras Bar Association (2025)**: SC gave **four months** to set up the **National Tribunals Commission**.
Appeals from **TDSAT, SAT, APTEL, NCLAT** lie to the **Supreme Court**.

n412224aa10c.s: The Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) works under the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
n412224aa10c.x: AERB (1983, under the Atomic Energy Act, 1962) works under the DAE through the Atomic Energy Commission; since DAE both promotes and regulates, an NSRA Bill has been proposed.
xa: After the **SHANTI Act, 2025**, commentators urged more **autonomy for AERB** to avoid **regulatory capture** risks.
⚠ **MoEFCC** funds and administers the **NGT**, not the AERB.

na91731d145a.s: In the context of regulatory overlap, the Financial Stability and Development Council mainly:
na91731d145a.x: The FSDC coordinates financial regulators and helps address overlap among them.
xa: **CCI vs sector regulators**: CCI penalised **WhatsApp**; **DPDP Act** separately restricts cross-use of data.
**TRAI vs MIB** overlap was resolved by the **TV Ratings Policy, 2026**.
The **2010** ULIP law placed **ULIPs** under **IRDAI** with a joint dispute mechanism.

nb5ff923130f.s: Which of the following was NOT a proposal of the FSLRC’s draft Indian Financial Code?
o: A Unified Financial Agency for core regulatory tasks
Moving from area-based to task-based regulation
A Financial Redressal Agency for consumer complaints
Abolishing the Financial Sector Appellate Tribunal
nb5ff923130f.x: The FSLRC proposed a Financial Sector Appellate Tribunal for appeals; it did not propose abolishing such a tribunal.
nb5ff923130f.tq: Find the option that reverses a specific reform proposal.
xs: **Abolishing the Financial Sector Appellate Tribunal** was NOT an FSLRC proposal — it proposed **creating** one for appeals — option **(4)** is correct.
FSLRC did propose a **Unified Financial Agency**, **task-based** regulation and a **Financial Redressal Agency** — options (1), (2), (3).
xa: FSLRC was headed by **Justice B.N. Srikrishna** and reported in **2013** (UPSC).
It produced a draft **Indian Financial Code**.

n3d3c7f7f3fe.s: Which one of the following best describes a pressure group?
o: A constitutional body that supervises the conduct of elections
A temporary administrative committee constituted by the government
An organised group that seeks to influence public policy without contesting elections or seeking office
An organised group that contests elections to capture political power
n3d3c7f7f3fe.x: A pressure group seeks to influence public policy but does not contest elections or seek governmental office.
n3d3c7f7f3fe.tq: Distinguish influence on policy from contesting elections and holding office.
xs: A **pressure group** is an organised group that **influences public policy without contesting elections or seeking office** — option **(3)** is correct.
Contesting elections to **capture power** is the mark of a **political party** — option (4) is wrong.
xa: It represents a **particular section** (farmers, industrial workers) and presses government, legislators, bureaucracy.
**Almond and Powell**: institutional, associational, non-associational, anomic.
Pressure groups are called the **"Anonymous Empire"**.

n9e4bdcefd10.s: The Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (MKSS) is associated with which one of the following combinations?
n9e4bdcefd10.x: MKSS emerged in Rajasthan in 1990 and is associated with Aruna Roy. Its campaign contributed to the enactment of the Right to Information Act, 2005.
n9e4bdcefd10.tq: Match the organisation with its year, location and associated personality.
xs: **MKSS** — **1990**, **Rajasthan**, **Aruna Roy** — option **(1)** is correct.
**2011 / Anna Hazare** is **India Against Corruption**; **1985 / Medha Patkar** is **Narmada Bachao Andolan**.
**1992 / Nellore** is the **anti-arrack movement**; **Gaura Devi** belongs to **Chipko**.
xa: MKSS (with **Nikhil Dey**) demanded **minimum wages** and **right to information** via **jan sunwai**.
Its campaign led to the **RTI Act, 2005**.
⚠ **MKSS** (Aruna Roy) → **RTI**; **India Against Corruption** (Anna Hazare) → **Lokpal**.

n6308fba39dd.s: The Anti-arrack movement of 1992 began at which place?
n6308fba39dd.x: The Anti-arrack movement began in 1992 at Dubagunta village in Nellore. It resulted in an arrack ban and later prohibition in Andhra Pradesh.
n6308fba39dd.tq: Test the exact place associated with a regional movement.
xs: The **anti-arrack movement** (**1992**) began at **Dubagunta village, Nellore** — option **(2)** is correct.
It led to an **arrack ban** and later **prohibition in AP**.
**Uttarakhand** belongs to **Chipko** (**1973**); **Rajasthan** belongs to **MKSS** (**1990**).
xa: **MKSS** campaign led to the **RTI Act, 2005**.
**India Against Corruption** (**2011**, Anna Hazare) demanded **Jan Lokpal**.

n72f3611adb5.s: The Narmada Bachao Andolan was mainly a movement against the:
n72f3611adb5.x: The Narmada Bachao Andolan opposed the Sardar Sarovar dam and the displacement it caused.
xa: **Chipko** (**1973**, Uttarakhand Himalayas): stop **tree-felling**.
**MKSS** (**1990**, Rajasthan): minimum wages and **RTI**.

n82f44634a3a.s: The Chipko Movement is correctly associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Uttarakhand, formerly Uttar Pradesh — Sunderlal Bahuguna, Chandi Prasad Bhatt and Gaura Devi — 1973
n82f44634a3a.x: The Chipko Movement is associated with Uttarakhand, then part of Uttar Pradesh, and with Sunderlal Bahuguna, Chandi Prasad Bhatt and Gaura Devi in 1973.
n82f44634a3a.tq: Match the movement with its state, leaders and year; reject the swapped movement details.
xs: **Chipko** — **Uttarakhand Himalayas**, **Sunderlal Bahuguna, Chandi Prasad Bhatt and Gaura Devi**, **1973** — option **(2)** is correct.
Its demand: **stop tree-felling** and protect forests.
xa: **Narmada Bachao Andolan** (**1985**): Medha Patkar, Baba Amte, against **Sardar Sarovar**.
**MKSS** (**1990**, Rajasthan): Aruna Roy, **RTI**.
**Anti-arrack movement** (**1992**): **Dubagunta**, Nellore.

ncbcf048b8d1.s: An NGO receiving foreign funds must, in addition to its applicable legal-form registration, also register under:
o: The Representation of the People Act, 1951
ncbcf048b8d1.x: Any NGO receiving foreign funds must also register under the FCRA.
ncbcf048b8d1.tq: Apply the additional-registration rule to the condition of receiving foreign funds.
xs: An NGO receiving foreign funds must also register under the **Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA)** — option **(3)** is correct.
This is in addition to its legal-form registration (society, trust or **Section 8** company).
The **Trade Unions Act, 1926** gave legal recognition to trade unions, not NGOs' foreign funding.
xa: FCRA is administered by the **MHA**; **FEMA 1999** by **RBI + ED**.
FCRA registration is valid for **5 years**.
Since **2020**, all foreign contributions must first go to the **FCRA account at SBI, New Delhi**.

ndb29cc95e6b.s: The Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) was first enacted in which year?
ndb29cc95e6b.x: The FCRA was first enacted in 1976 and was later replaced by the FCRA, 2010.
ndb29cc95e6b.tq: Use the direct year-recall method for a foundational statute.
xs: The **FCRA** was first enacted in **1976** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was replaced by **FCRA 2010**; **1999** is the year of **FEMA**.
xa: **2016** amendment (retrospective): Indian subsidiaries of foreign firms no longer **"foreign sources"**.
**2020** amendment: designated SBI account, **20%** admin cap, **sub-granting ban**.
FCRA is administered by the **MHA**.

n04bf8df22de.s: The retrospective 2016 FCRA amendment followed which court's 2014 ruling on donations received by the BJP and Congress?
n04bf8df22de.x: The 2016 amendment followed the Delhi High Court's 2014 ruling and excluded Indian subsidiaries of foreign firms from 'foreign source'.
xa: The **2020** amendment brought a designated account, admin cap and **sub-granting ban**.
FCRA first enacted in **1976**, replaced by **FCRA 2010**.

n6c52c71ae8b.s: The FCRA 2020 amendment reduced the ceiling on administrative expenses from 50 per cent to:
n6c52c71ae8b.x: The 2020 amendment cut the ceiling from 50% to 20% and prohibited sub-granting to other NGOs.
xa: FCRA registration is valid for **5 years**.
**FCRA Amendment Rules, 2026**: at least **75%** of an instalment used before the next is sought.

n54b87b1f1fe.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated ground or administrative basis associated with cancellation of FCRA registration?
o: Failure to file returns or seek renewal on time
Breach of the Act, rules or registration conditions
Having a registered office in a State other than New Delhi
n54b87b1f1fe.x: Cancellation may arise from breach of the law or conditions, non-functioning, or administrative defaults such as non-filing of returns or delayed renewal. Location of the registered office in another State is not a stated ground.
n54b87b1f1fe.tq: Find the unrelated location-based option among genuine cancellation grounds.
xs: **Having a registered office in a State other than New Delhi** is not a ground for cancellation — option **(4)** is correct.
Stated grounds: **breach of the Act/rules/registration conditions** and **non-functioning** — options (1) and (3).
Many grounds are **administrative**, e.g. **returns not filed** or **renewal not sought on time** — option (2).
xa: ⚠ Only the **FCRA account** must be at **SBI, New Delhi** — not the NGO's office.
**18,000+** NGOs' registrations cancelled since **2015**.
2024-25: **16,200** associations received **₹22,963 crore**.

n29f4a2e0d78.s: The FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026, introduced in the Lok Sabha on 25 March 2026, proposed to:
o: Create an authority to take over assets of NGOs whose registration is cancelled or suspended
Transfer FCRA administration from MHA to RBI
Abolish FCRA registration for all NGOs
n29f4a2e0d78.x: The Bill proposed an authority empowered to take over the assets of NGOs whose registration was cancelled or suspended. Its passage was deferred after protests.
n29f4a2e0d78.tq: Identify the proposed institutional power rather than confusing it with existing FCRA rules.
xs: The **FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026** proposed an authority to **take over assets of NGOs with cancelled/suspended registration** — option **(2)** is correct.
It was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** on **25 March 2026**; **passage deferred after protests**.
⚠ FCRA stays with the **MHA**; **sub-granting** remains banned since **2020**.
xa: ⚠ **Bill** = **25 March 2026** (deferred); **Rules** = **22 June 2026** (notified).
**K.C. Venugopal** and **John Brittas** wrote seeking withdrawal of the **2026 Rules**.
Critics: FCRA moving from regulating foreign funds to **State control of civil society**.

n66f9a84959b.s: Civil society organisations are described as development partners and democratic watchdogs forming the:
o: First sector alongside the judiciary and legislature
Fourth sector alongside government and courts
Third sector alongside government and market
Second sector alongside government and market
n66f9a84959b.x: Civil society organisations are described as the third sector, alongside government and the market, while functioning as development partners and democratic watchdogs.
n66f9a84959b.tq: Discriminate among sector classifications by using the government-market comparison.
xs: Civil society is the **"third sector"**, alongside the **State (first)** and the **market (second)** — option **(3)** is correct.
CSOs are seen as **development partners and democratic watchdogs**.
The State is the first sector and the market the second, so "first", "second" or "fourth" sector labels are wrong.
xa: **Civil society** = pressure groups + trade unions + NGOs.
India has an estimated **1.5-3.3 million** NGOs.
⚠ **APPSC 2019** key called NGOs **"observationalists in development"**; standard texts call them **partners** of government.

n8acc814efda.s: The focus of NGOs in India has shifted from welfare delivery towards:
n8acc814efda.x: The focus of NGOs has shifted from welfare delivery to rights and empowerment.
xa: Example of watchdog work: **ADR** on candidate disclosure.
Constraints: **project-tied short-term funding**, digital divide, regulatory curbs.
Rights secured by civil society: work (**MGNREGA**), education (**RTE**), food, information (**RTI**).

n590e15658f3.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the National Policy on the Voluntary Sector, 2007?
o: Partnership between voluntary organisations and government
Creation of an enabling environment for voluntary organisations
Complete subordination of voluntary organisations to government departments
n590e15658f3.x: The 2007 policy seeks an enabling environment, resource mobilisation and partnership, not subordination to government.
xa: Adopted in **2007** by the **Planning Commission**.
It prefers **transparency, self-regulation and codes of conduct** over tight government control.

ndb42aea10a8.s: An FCRA registration is ordinarily valid for:
ndb42aea10a8.x: FCRA registration is valid for five years.
ndb42aea10a8.tq: Recall the statutory validity period using the distinct year options.
xs: FCRA registration is valid for **5 years** — **five years**, option **(3)**, is correct.
Renewal must be sought on time; delay is a common **administrative** ground for cancellation.
xa: **2026 Rules**: renewal needs at least **₹10 lakh** foreign funds spent over **two years**.
**18,000+** NGOs' registrations cancelled since **2015**.
**14,538** FCRA NGOs active as on **15 Apr 2026**.

n15de6a7a9ab.s: The Public Health Foundation of India was placed under the FCRA prior-permission category in 2017 primarily on the ground of:
o: Failure to maintain a designated SBI account
Employing foreign citizens as key functionaries
n15de6a7a9ab.x: The Public Health Foundation of India was placed under the FCRA prior-permission category in 2017 for lobbying with parliamentarians.
n15de6a7a9ab.tq: Apply the who-and-why trap by linking the organisation with the specific cancellation reason.
xs: The **Public Health Foundation of India** was placed under FCRA **prior permission** (**2017**) for **lobbying with parliamentarians** — option **(1)** is correct.
This was asked in **APPSC 2017**.
xa: **Lobbying** = dealing with legislators and officials to promote or defeat legislation (**APPSC 2019**).
Cancellation grounds: **breach** of Act/rules/conditions + **non-functioning**.
**2026 Rules**: ineligible if **foreign citizens** (other than **PIOs**) are key functionaries.

nd18436935b5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the FCRA Amendment Rules, 2026?
o: Foreign funds cannot be used for proselytisation
At least 75% of an instalment must be used before the next is sought
An NGO with a Person of Indian Origin as a key functionary is ineligible
nd18436935b5.x: Ineligibility applies to foreign citizens other than PIOs as key functionaries; PIOs are excluded from it.
xa: The Rules were notified on **22 June 2026**.
Renewal needs at least **₹10 lakh** foreign funds spent over **two years**.
NGOs must disclose **websites + social-media handles**; no **"political content"**.

n8c31d4ff91d.s: Beyond service delivery, civil society organisations increasingly undertake:
o: Advocacy, policy formulation and watchdog functions
n8c31d4ff91d.x: CSOs have moved beyond service delivery to advocacy, policy formulation and watchdog roles, helping secure rights to work, education, food and information.
xa: Focus shift: **welfare delivery → rights and empowerment**.
Constraints: **project-tied** short-term funding, **digital divide**, regulatory curbs.

n2cbfeff50d2.s: Which of the following is a professional pressure group?
n2cbfeff50d2.x: IMA is a professional group; FICCI is a business group, AITUC a trade union and BKU a peasant organisation.
xa: Other trade unions: **INTUC, CITU, BMS, HMS**.
**AITUC** (**1920**) is India's oldest central trade union; **N.M. Joshi** a co-founder.
Student groups: **ABVP, NSUI, SFI, AISF**.

nfe9f26e4741.s: Which of the following is a feature of a political party rather than a pressure group?
o: Being answerable primarily to its members
nfe9f26e4741.x: Pressure groups represent sectional interests and do not contest elections; seeking to form the government marks a political party.
xa: Pressure groups are the **"Anonymous Empire"**.
**Almond and Powell**: institutional, associational, non-associational, anomic.

n3c8424ba52d.s: Which of the following is a constitutional authority and NOT a pressure group?
n3c8424ba52d.x: The AP NGOs' Association and farmers' associations, including rythu sanghams, are pressure groups; the ECI is a constitutional authority.
xa: **Amaravati farmers' agitation** began in **Dec 2019** against the **three-capitals plan**.
Pressure group test: does **not seek office** + lobbies on a **specific interest**.

n61e85e90355.s: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh mainly lends to:
o: Individual women borrowers directly, without intermediaries
Intermediary NGOs and microfinance bodies, which on-lend to poor women and SHGs
