Commensality restrictions = **cultural** theory (**Sarat Chandra Roy**); Brahmin device = **Brahminical** theory (**Abbé Dubois**); occupations becoming guilds = **occupational** theory (**Nesfield**).
xa: Brahmins from the **head**, Kshatriyas from the **arms**, Vaishyas from the **thighs**, Shudras from the **feet**.
The Purusha Sukta is considered a **late addition** to the Rig Veda.
**Racial** theory: **Herbert Risley**.

n78c32f1a429.s: The occupational theory of the origin of caste is associated with:
n78c32f1a429.x: Nesfield gave the occupational theory; Risley the racial, Dubois the Brahminical/political and S.C. Roy the cultural theory.
xa: Racial theory: Aryans kept apart from the original inhabitants (**Pratiloma** bar).
Occupational: hereditary occupations became **guilds**, then castes.
**Divine** theory: the **Purusha Sukta** (RV **10.90**).

n393b35b0152.s: Which of the following is NOT a cultural trait associated with caste?
n393b35b0152.x: Universal inter-caste commensality is contrary to the commensal taboos associated with caste. Pollution by touch, untouchability and Sanskritic rituals are recognised traits.
n393b35b0152.tq: Identify the option that reverses a central prohibition.
xs: **Universal inter-caste commensality** is **not** a caste trait — option **(1)** — it contradicts **commensal taboos**.
**Commensal taboos**, **untouchability** and **pollution-by-touch** are all listed traits.
xa: The fourth trait is **Sanskritic rituals**.
Ghurye's list includes restrictions on **feeding and social intercourse**.
**Marriott**: castes ranked by exchange of food, water and services.

n9c778dde22d.s: The post-Maurya and Gupta period is particularly associated with which development in the history of caste?
o: Emergence of the Manu Smriti and rigid caste divisions
Transfer of caste councils’ judicial powers to courts
n9c778dde22d.x: The post-Maurya and Gupta period saw the Manu Smriti and the development of a more rigid caste system.
n9c778dde22d.tq: Associate the named historical period with its specific institutional development.
xs: The **post-Maurya/Gupta** period saw the **Manu Smriti** and **rigid caste** — option **(2)**.
The Purusha Sukta belongs to the Vedic texts; the transfer of caste councils' powers to courts came in the **British** period.
xa: **Later Vedic**: four varnas + hereditary divisions crystallise.
**Medieval**: more rigidity, moderated by **Bhakti**.
**APPSC 2007** asked when caste "began"; the notes date the crystallisation to the **Later Vedic** age.

ne7312411af9.s: According to S.V. Ketkar, caste membership is primarily determined by
o: birth and prohibition of marriage outside the group
ne7312411af9.x: S.V. Ketkar emphasised membership by birth and the prohibition on marrying outside the caste.
ne7312411af9.tq: Combine the two elements in the definition instead of selecting only one.
xs: **S.V. Ketkar** defined caste by **membership by birth** plus a **ban on marrying outside** — option **(3)**.
His book: **History of Caste in India (1909)**.
xa: **Risley**: families with a common name, a claimed mythical ancestor, the same hereditary calling.
**Bouglé**: hereditary specialisation, hierarchy, **repulsion**.
**A.W. Green**: ideally, **no mobility** up or down the status ladder.

n545398582aa.s: Which of the following was NOT included among G.S. Ghurye’s six features of caste?
o: Civil and religious disabilities and privileges
n545398582aa.x: Ghurye identified lack of free choice of occupation, not free choice of occupation, as a feature of caste. Segmental division, marriage restrictions and civil and religious disabilities or privileges were included in his list.
n545398582aa.tq: Watch for the reversal of a precisely worded feature.
xs: **Free choice of occupation** is not a Ghurye feature — he listed the **lack** of it — option **(3)**.
**Segmental division**, **restriction on marriage** and **civil and religious disabilities and privileges** are among his six.
xa: The other three: **hierarchy**, restrictions on **feeding and social intercourse**, lack of free choice of occupation.
Source: **Caste and Race in India (1932)**.
**Dimensions** of caste: **vertical** (ranking) + **horizontal** (grouping).

nac460f54a93.s: Caste possesses which two dimensions in relation to social organisation?
nac460f54a93.x: Caste has a vertical dimension expressed through ranking and a horizontal dimension expressed through grouping into separate communities.
nac460f54a93.tq: Recall the paired dimensions and distinguish ranking from grouping.
xs: Caste has a **vertical** dimension (**ranking**) and a **horizontal** dimension (**grouping**) — option **(2)**.
Ranking reflects **hierarchy**; grouping reflects separate, **endogamous** communities.
xa: **Ghurye**'s **segmental division** and **hierarchy** match these two dimensions.
**Dumont**: hierarchy rests on **pure vs impure**.
**Dipankar Gupta**: castes = **discrete communities**; "difference" ≠ "hierarchy".

na74c97cf53f.s: The concept of the opposition between purity and impurity is central to the analysis of caste by
na74c97cf53f.x: Louis Dumont analysed caste through the opposition of purity and impurity in Homo Hierarchicus, published in 1966.
na74c97cf53f.tq: Link the distinctive conceptual pair with its principal scholar.
xs: **Louis Dumont** built caste hierarchy on **pure vs impure** — option **(2)**.
**Risley** gave the **racial** theory; **A.W. Green** stressed no mobility; **Ketkar** stressed birth and endogamy.
xa: Dumont's book: **Homo Hierarchicus (1966)**; Homo Hierarchicus vs **Homo Aequalis**.
For Dumont the **religious status encompasses power**.
⚠ **Pure vs impure** = Dumont; **coded substances** = Marriott; **continuum** = Bailey.

na3ae0416e4f.s: McKim Marriott’s interactional approach explains caste ranking through the exchange of
o: coded substances such as food, water and services
na3ae0416e4f.x: McKim Marriott explained caste interaction and ranking through the exchange of coded substances, including food, water and services.
na3ae0416e4f.tq: Associate the interactional approach with its concrete exchange items.
xs: **McKim Marriott**'s **interactional** approach ranks castes by the exchange of **coded substances** — **food, water, services** — option **(3)**.
Coins, contracts, texts or land are not the substances in his model.
xa: ⚠ **Coded substances** = **Marriott**; **pure vs impure** = **Dumont**.
**Dipankar Gupta** (vs Dumont): castes = **discrete communities**.
**William Wiser**: The Hindu Jajmani System (**1936**).

n35359b70b26.s: Who studied the Jajmani system in the work titled The Hindu Jajmani System?
n35359b70b26.x: William Wiser studied the system in The Hindu Jajmani System, published in 1936.
n35359b70b26.tq: Combine the author, title and year to avoid confusing scholars of caste.
xs: **William Wiser** wrote **The Hindu Jajmani System (1936)** — option **(1)**.
**Risley** gave the racial theory; **Ghurye** wrote Caste and Race in India; **Marriott** gave the interactional approach.
xa: Jajmani = **socio-economic and ritual** arrangement between **jajman** and **kamin**.
Andhra equivalent: **Ayagar (Ayagadu)** — **12** hereditary functionaries.
**UPPSC 2020** matched the regional pairs.

n4203fe593e9.s: In Andhra, the village service system consisting of twelve hereditary functionaries was known as the
n4203fe593e9.x: The Ayagar or Ayagadu system was the Andhra village service arrangement. Its twelve hereditary functionaries were paid through Manyam land or a share of the harvest.
n4203fe593e9.tq: Use the regional-specific term instead of the wider North Indian label.
xs: Andhra's **Ayagar (Ayagadu)** system had **12 hereditary functionaries** — option **(1)**.
They were paid by **Manyam land** or a **harvest share**.
**Jajmani** = North India; **Bara Balute** = Maharashtra; **Mirasi** = Tamil Nadu.
xa: **Adade** = Karnataka.
**Satavahanas** organised the **18 (Ashta-dasha) professions**.
**Kakatiya** era = "**Age of Shudras**".

n0189f106de8.s: The 1931 Census recorded how many castes?
n0189f106de8.tq: Recall the exact census figure and distinguish it from nearby numerical distractors.
xs: The **1931 Census** recorded **4,147 castes** — option **(3)**.
The other figures are not in the record.
xa: The **colonial Census** ranked castes from **1871**.
**Susan Bayly** and **Nicholas Dirks** see caste as a **colonial construct** shaped by the Census.
**Census 2027** will enumerate caste.

n7dc899f65c3.s: The word ‘caste’ is derived from the Portuguese word
n7dc899f65c3.x: The term caste is derived from the Portuguese casta, meaning race or breed.
n7dc899f65c3.tq: Test the exact foreign-language source and spelling of the term.
xs: "Caste" comes from the **Portuguese casta**, meaning **race, breed** — option **(4)**.
One source (CDX) calls the word **Spanish**, but the standard derivation is Portuguese.
xa: **Varna** = theoretical **4**-fold scheme from the Vedas (**Chaturvarna**); **jati** = thousands of real local groups.
The **1931 Census** recorded **4,147 castes**.
Each varna is sub-divided into **jatis**.

n675fa7ef203.s: The four varnas and hereditary divisions crystallised during the:
n675fa7ef203.x: The Early Vedic period lacked a rigid varna system; the four-fold hereditary divisions crystallised in the Later Vedic period.
xa: **Post-Maurya/Gupta**: **Manu Smriti** + rigid caste.
**Medieval**: more rigidity, moderated by **Bhakti**.
**British**: caste councils' judicial powers transferred to **courts**.

nd6732449c49.s: The Jajmani system was primarily a system of
o: socio-economic and ritual interdependence among castes
nd6732449c49.x: The Jajmani system was a socio-economic and ritual arrangement in which the landholding jajman received hereditary services from kamin castes.
nd6732449c49.tq: Identify the institutional relationship rather than a superficial occupational label.
xs: The **Jajmani** system was a **socio-economic and ritual** arrangement among castes — option **(1)**.
The landholding **jajman** received hereditary services from **kamin** castes.
xa: ⚠ **Jajman** = landholder receiving services; **kamin** = service castes.
In the **Pallava** era villages used it as **barter of services**.
Regional names: **Bara Balute** (Maharashtra), **Mirasi** (Tamil Nadu), **Adade** (Karnataka).

na4470ff8bca.s: Which Sikh group constitutes the largest Scheduled Caste component among the groups mentioned?
na4470ff8bca.x: Mazhabi Sikhs are identified as the largest Scheduled Caste component among the Sikh groups mentioned.
na4470ff8bca.tq: Distinguish the Scheduled Caste component from the other named Sikh communities.
xs: **Mazhabi Sikhs** are the **largest SC component** among Sikhs — option **(1)**.
**Khatri**, **Arora** and **Jat** are listed Sikh castes but not the SC component.
xa: The fourth listed Sikh caste: **Ramgarhia**.
Sikhs were added to the **SC Order** in **1956**.
⚠ **1956** = Sikhs; **1990** = Buddhists.

n84f85d484fc.s: Surajit Sinha's idea of 'secondary state formation' refers to:
o: Tribe and caste as poles of a continuum
The Hindu method of tribal absorption
n84f85d484fc.x: Sinha's secondary state formation is tribal chiefs adopting Raja titles; he read the tribal little tradition in relation to the Hindu great tradition.
xa: **F.G. Bailey**: tribe and caste = poles of a **continuum** (**1960**).
**N.K. Bose**: The Hindu Method of Tribal Absorption (**1941**).

nc1ed3abc1ad.s: In the colonial period, caste groups formed associations and pressed upward status claims mainly because:
o: The Census from 1871 ranked castes, encouraging groups to seek higher classification
The Minto-Morley Reforms gave each caste a separate electorate
The Communal G.O. of 1921 abolished caste ranking
Land reforms transferred land to caste councils
nc1ed3abc1ad.x: The colonial Census, beginning in 1871, ranked castes, so groups formed associations and petitioned for higher status.
xa: A **caste association** is a voluntary, membership-based **pressure group**.
**Kakatiya**-era caste associations were called "**Samayas**".

nb159075f445.s: A caste association is best defined as a
o: religious institution open only to twice-born castes
voluntary membership-based body acting as a pressure group
hereditary state department exercising judicial power
nb159075f445.x: A caste association is a voluntary, membership-based organisation of a caste that acts as a pressure group.
nb159075f445.tq: Choose the precise institutional definition rather than a related but incorrect body.
xs: A **caste association** is a **voluntary, membership-based body** of a caste acting as a **pressure group** — option **(2)**.
It is not hereditary or state-run, and judicial powers of caste councils went to **courts** under the British.
xa: Colonial **Census** (from **1871**) ranking prompted associations to claim higher status.
**Rudolphs**: caste associations = agents of **democratisation** (Nadars, Vanniyars).
"**Samayas**" = Kakatiya-era caste associations.

n43e048f7e6a.s: The caste associations known as 'Samayas' are associated historically with the
n43e048f7e6a.x: Samayas were caste associations associated with the Kakatiya era.
n43e048f7e6a.tq: Match a distinctive institutional name with its historical period.
xs: "**Samayas**" were caste associations of the **Kakatiya period** — option **(4)**.
**Mandal** and **Minto-Morley** belong to the modern era.
xa: A **caste association** = voluntary, membership-based **pressure group**.
Medieval Andhra: **Nayankara** system Kshatriyaised Reddys, Kammas, Velamas, Kapus.

nc9a836c5840.s: In medieval Andhra, the Kshatriyaisation of Reddys, Kammas, Velamas and Kapus was associated with the
nc9a836c5840.x: In medieval Andhra, these groups were Kshatriyaised through the Nayankara system.
nc9a836c5840.tq: Distinguish the political-military system from other caste-related institutions.
xs: **Reddys, Kammas, Velamas, Kapus** were Kshatriyaised through the **Nayankara system** — option **(2)**.
"**Samayas**" were **Kakatiya**-era caste associations; **Minto-Morley** brought separate electorates; **Mandal** concerns OBC reservation.
xa: These four are the **martial and agrarian** dominant castes of **AP**.
**Kayasthas** = the administrative elite.
**Kshatriyaisation** is **Kulke**'s term.

neeeadd5e1a2.s: The concept of 'dominant caste' was developed by
neeeadd5e1a2.x: The concept of dominant caste is associated with sociologist M.N. Srinivas.
neeeadd5e1a2.tq: Directly identify the originator of a sociological concept.
xs: **M.N. Srinivas** developed the concept of **dominant caste** — option **(1)**.
He drew it from his study of **Rampura** village, Mysore (**1955**).
**Kothari** edited Caste in Indian Politics; **Jaffrelot** wrote India's Silent Revolution; **Béteille** wrote Caste, Class and Power.
xa: Srinivas also gave **Sanskritisation**.
His books: **Social Change in Modern India**, **The Remembered Village**.
⚠ **Rampura** = Srinivas; **bullock capitalists** = Rudolphs; **hali** = Breman.

n9ce0a811915.s: Which of the following is NOT a traditional criterion of a dominant caste?
o: Exclusive control over urban industrial capital
n9ce0a811915.x: The traditional criteria are sizeable arable land, numerical strength and high ritual status.
xa: Later additions: **Western education**, **administrative jobs**, **urban income**.
Originator: **M.N. Srinivas**, from **Rampura**, Mysore (**1955**).
Bihar (pre-independence): **Bhumihar, Rajput, Kayastha** were dominant.

nf199464b4eb.s: Which of the following was a later addition to the criteria of a dominant caste?
nf199464b4eb.x: Western education, administrative jobs and urban income were later additions to the traditional criteria of land, numbers and ritual status.
xa: Original criteria: **sizeable arable land**, **numerical strength**, **high ritual status**.
Concept by **M.N. Srinivas** (Rampura, **1955**).
AP dominant castes: **Reddys, Kammas, Velamas, Kapus**.

n51bfdbe9bb8.s: Which one of the following was NOT a dominant caste in Bihar in the pre-independence period?
n51bfdbe9bb8.x: In pre-independence Bihar the dominant castes were the Bhumihar, Rajput and Kayastha; the Kurmi were not a dominant caste then (BPSC 2004 PYQ). So Kurmi is the answer.
n51bfdbe9bb8.tq: Bihar pre-1947 dominant: Bhumihar, Rajput, Kayastha; not Kurmi.
xs: The **Kurmi** were **not** a dominant caste in pre-independence **Bihar** — option **(4)**.
**Bhumihar, Rajput, Kayastha** were the dominant castes (**BPSC 2004 PYQ**).
xa: Criteria: **sizeable arable land**, **numerical strength**, **high ritual status**.
**Bihar survey (2022-23)**: OBC+EBC = **63%**.
Concept by **M.N. Srinivas**.

na5e5005e1b3.s: M.N. Srinivas developed the concept of 'dominant caste' from his study of which village?
na5e5005e1b3.x: Srinivas formulated the concept of dominant caste from his study of Rampura village in Mysore (1955). Mahuva is the site of I.P. Desai's study of joint family jointness; Kishangarhi and Senapur are not linked to the concept.
xs: Srinivas drew the dominant-caste idea from **Rampura** village, **Mysore** (**1955**) — option **(2)**.
**Mahuva**, **Kishangarhi** and **Senapur** are not linked to this concept.
xa: ⚠ **Rampura** = **Srinivas**.
Srinivas's books: **The Remembered Village**, **Social Change in Modern India**.
Later criteria additions: Western education, administrative jobs, urban income.

n287d47e1574.s: The Justice Party was primarily based on the mobilisation of which combination of intermediate castes?
n287d47e1574.x: The Justice Party rested on intermediate-caste mobilisation involving Kammas, Reddys and Naidus.
n287d47e1574.tq: Identify the sure regional caste combination rather than a broader list of dominant groups.
xs: The **Justice Party** rested on the intermediate castes **Kammas, Reddys and Naidus** — option **(1)**.
**Marathas, Gujjars, Patels** are groups now seeking OBC status, not the Justice Party base.
xa: Its non-Brahmin mobilisation led to the **Communal G.O. of 1921**.
**AP** dominant castes: **Reddys, Kammas, Velamas, Kapus**.

nf923a23dbf6.s: André Béteille described the transformation of caste inequality as a movement from
nf923a23dbf6.x: Béteille described a movement from cumulative inequality to dispersed inequality.
nf923a23dbf6.tq: Watch for the reversed comparison in a paired sociological formulation.
xs: **André Béteille** traced inequality from **cumulative** to **dispersed** — option **(4)**.
Option (2) reverses the direction.
xa: His book: **Caste, Class and Power (1965)**.
Béteille (born **1934**) passed away in **Feb 2026**.
**Dipankar Gupta**: difference vs hierarchy.

nc0dcb29d40e.x: Dipankar Gupta wrote 'Interrogating Caste'; Beteille wrote 'Caste, Class and Power' and Srinivas 'The Remembered Village'.
xa: Béteille's book: **1965**; Gupta's: **2000**.
Breman studied **hali** bonded labour in south Gujarat.

n3cd0440f9c0.s: Dipankar Gupta’s analysis of caste is particularly associated with the distinction between:
n3cd0440f9c0.x: Dipankar Gupta’s work Interrogating Caste is associated with the distinction between difference and hierarchy.
n3cd0440f9c0.tq: Test the precise wording of a paired theoretical distinction.
xs: **Dipankar Gupta** is known for **difference vs hierarchy** — option **(3)**.
His book: **Interrogating Caste (2000)**.
xa: Gupta argued, against **Dumont**, that castes are **discrete communities**.
Béteille: inequality **cumulative → dispersed**.

nf67ac42cdae.s: Reservation and the Mandal process affected caste identity by:
o: Reinforcing it, with OBCs computed at over 52 percent
Weakening it, with OBCs computed at under 10 percent
Confining it to the Scheduled Tribes
nf67ac42cdae.x: Reservation and the Mandal process reinforced caste identity; OBCs were computed at 52 percent or more.
xa: **Modern education** weakened caste and led to the decline of Brahmin supremacy.
**Marathas, Gujjars and Patels** seek OBC status.
Census debate: data for **sub-categorisation** and the **50% cap**.

n16fd8c39216.s: The introduction of separate electorates in colonial India is associated with which of the following?
n16fd8c39216.x: The Minto-Morley Reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates and formed an important colonial background to later vote-bank politics.
n16fd8c39216.tq: Discriminate between nearby constitutional milestones by matching the reform with its year.
xs: Separate electorates came with the **Minto-Morley Reforms 1909** — option **(2)**.
They laid the colonial roots of **vote-bank politics** built on caste associations.
The **Communal G.O. of 1921** came from **non-Brahmin mobilisation** in Madras.
xa: Present caste conflict is for **power, not ritual status**.
The **Justice Party** rested on intermediate castes (Kammas, Reddys, Naidus).

n30487a37d96.s: The Communal G.O. of 1921 in the Madras Presidency was associated with
o: the formation of the Mandal Commission
n30487a37d96.x: Non-Brahmin mobilisation led to the Communal Government Order of 1921.
n30487a37d96.tq: Connect a historical order with the social movement that produced it.
xs: The **Communal G.O. of 1921** grew out of **non-Brahmin mobilisation** — option **(1)**.
The first **digital** Census is **Census 2027**; separate electorates came in **1909**.
xa: The **Justice Party** rested on **Kammas, Reddys, Naidus**.
**Modern education** led to the decline of **Brahmin supremacy**.

nf7cb4b36b9b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Census 2027?
o: Caste enumeration was approved on 30 April 2025
It is projected to be the first digital Census
It will be the first caste count since 1951
Population Enumeration is due in February 2027
nf7cb4b36b9b.x: Census 2027 is projected to be the first caste count since 1931, not 1951.
xa: The **SC upheld** the caste count.
The Centre dropped OBC lists as "**classes, not castes**".
Since **1951** only SCs and STs had been counted.

n3ec5ccd3fe0.s:
Which of the following rose as martial and agrarian (landholding) castes in Andhra Pradesh?
1. Reddys
2. Kammas
3. Velamas
n3ec5ccd3fe0.x: Reddys, Kammas and Velamas (along with Kapus) rose as martial and agrarian castes in Andhra Pradesh.
xa: **Kayasthas** = the administrative elite.
**Justice Party** rested on **Kammas, Reddys, Naidus**.
The **EWS Welfare Department** clubs Reddy, Kamma, **Kapu** and other corporations.

na486e1e702a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Scheduled Tribes under Article 342?
o: The President specifies STs after consultation with the Governor
The Scheduled Tribe list is identical for the whole of India
The first order was the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950
Only Parliament can include or exclude communities from the list by law
na486e1e702a.x: Scheduled Tribe lists are State- or UT-specific.
xa: **Art. 366(25)** defines STs by reference to **Article 342**.
**Banchhada**, once a "criminal tribe", is listed as **SC** in MP and Rajasthan — showing state-specific lists.

n7c00136d73a.s: Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes by reference to:
n7c00136d73a.x: Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes with reference to the communities notified under Article 342.
n7c00136d73a.tq: Match the definitional provision with the notification provision.
xs: **Art. 366(25)** defines STs as communities "deemed under **Article 342**" — option **(3)**.
The notes link none of the other Articles to this definition.
xa: **Art. 342(1)**: President notifies after consulting the Governor; first order **1950**.
**Art. 342(2)**: only **Parliament by law** can include/exclude.
The term took shape under the **GoI Act 1935** and the Constitution.

n659e412acf7.s: After the Criminal Tribes Act, 1871 was repealed in ____, the communities it branded came to be called 'Denotified' tribes.
n659e412acf7.x: The Act was repealed on 31 August 1952 and replaced by State Habitual Offenders Acts.
xa: Repealed **31 August 1952** on the **All India Criminal Tribes Inquiry Committee (1949)** report.
Amended in **1924**.

n4fd044a9050.s: Marshall Sahlins described a tribe as which of the following?
o: A territorial unit administered directly by Parliament
A segmental organisation of equivalent, unspecialised multi-family groups, clans or bands
A religious association restricted to urban occupations
A centralised state based exclusively on hereditary monarchy
n4fd044a9050.x: Marshall Sahlins described a tribe as a segmental organisation of equivalent, unspecialised multi-family groups, clans or bands.
n4fd044a9050.tq: Recall the precise definitional wording and reject broader administrative descriptions.
xs: **Marshall Sahlins** saw a tribe as a **segmental organisation of equivalent, unspecialised multi-family groups, clans or bands** — option **(2)**.
A tribe is not centralised, so a hereditary monarchy or Parliament-run unit (options 1, 4) contradicts the definition.
xa: "Tribe" comes from Latin **"tribus"**.
ST criteria: **primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact, backwardness**.
The criteria are **not in the Constitution**.

n7a46e596e11.s: Which committee of 1965 is a source of the criteria for identifying Scheduled Tribes?
n7a46e596e11.x: The ST criteria draw on the 1931 Census, the Kalelkar Committee (1955), the Lokur Committee (1965) and the Chanda Committee (1969).
xa: Five criteria: **primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact, backwardness**.
⚠ **Renke (2008)** and **Idate (2017)** dealt with denotified and nomadic tribes, not ST criteria.

nef9351c1eeb.s: The economic classification of Indian tribes is associated with:
nef9351c1eeb.x: Vidyarthi and Rai gave the economic classification; Risley and Guha gave racial classifications.
xa: Economic types: food-gatherers/hunters (**Chenchu**), shifting cultivators, settled agriculturists, artisans, pastoralists, industrial labour.
Linguistic groups: **Austro-Asiatic**, **Dravidian**, **Tibeto-Burman**.

n70dc0f85676.s: The 'Ghotul' youth dormitory is associated with the:
n70dc0f85676.x: Ghotul belongs to the Gond (Muria), Morung to the Nagas and Dhumkuria to the Oraon.
xa: ⚠ Memory chain: **Ghotul – Morung – Dhumkuria** = **Gond – Naga – Oraon**.
**Oraon** speak **Kurukh** (Dravidian); **Gond** are Dravidian too.
**Totemism** goes with **clan exogamy**.

n57d23c3a931.s: The concept of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups originated from the:
n57d23c3a931.x: The PVTG concept is associated with the Dhebar Commission (1960-61); India has 75 PVTGs.
xa: The **PTG** category followed (dated **1973**); renamed **PVTGs in 2006**.
The 75 are spread over **18 states + 1 UT (A&N)**.
⚠ CDX wrongly dates the Commission itself to **1973**.

n7b16ece58bd.s: How many PVTGs are included in the Ministry’s combined list for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
n7b16ece58bd.x: The combined Ministry list for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana contains 12 PVTGs.
n7b16ece58bd.tq: Test the exact count using closely spaced numerical options.
xs: The Ministry's combined list for **AP and Telangana** has **12** PVTGs — option **(3)**.
**13** is **Odisha** (highest); **7** groups remain in residual AP (APP notes).
xa: ⚠ **12** = AP + Telangana together; **7** = residual AP.
**Kolam and Thoti** belong to the **Telangana** side; the list was never split after **2014**.
The list includes **Chenchu, Konda Reddi, Konda Savara, Kutia Khond, Bodo Gadaba**.

ndd0ce61f5fd.s: Which of the following correctly states the distribution of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) in India?
o: 75 PVTGs in 18 States and one Union Territory
75 PVTGs in 28 States and no Union Territory
33 PVTGs in 18 States and two Union Territories
62 PVTGs in 18 States and one Union Territory
ndd0ce61f5fd.x: There are 75 PVTGs distributed across 18 States and one Union Territory, namely the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
ndd0ce61f5fd.tq: Keep the total, number of States and number of Union Territories together as one factual unit.
xs: There are **75 PVTGs** in **18 States and 1 UT (A&N)** — option **(1)**.
The count is **75**, not 33 or 62, and there is one UT, so (2), (3), (4) are wrong.
xa: **Odisha 13** (highest); AP with Telangana **12**; Bihar **9**.
Population ~**27.68 lakh** (**2001**); **Sahariyas** largest.
Sentinelese and Andamanese are the smallest.

nad71af88c2d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)?
o: Andhra Pradesh including Telangana has more PVTGs than Odisha
Irular and Konda Reddi are included in the PVTG list
nad71af88c2d.x: Odisha has 13 PVTGs against 12 in Andhra Pradesh including Telangana.
xa: **75 PVTGs** in **18 states + 1 UT**.
APP notes: **7** groups in residual AP.

n89d7c8b1f64.s: In which year were Primitive Tribal Groups (PTGs) renamed Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups?
n89d7c8b1f64.x: The Dhebar Commission flagged the least-developed groups in 1960-61, the PTG category followed in 1973 and the renaming to PVTGs came in 2006.
xa: ⚠ CDX wrongly dates the Dhebar Commission itself to **1973**.
MoTA sought **separate PVTG enumeration** in **Census 2027**.

ndf7209b63d2.s: Which one of the following sets contains only groups included in the list of 12 PVTGs of undivided Andhra Pradesh?
o: Bodo Gadaba, Gutob Gadaba, Bondo Poraja and Chenchu
Konda Reddi, Irular, Kolam and Thoti
Jarawa, Onge, Chenchu and Konda Savaras
ndf7209b63d2.x: Bodo Gadaba, Gutob Gadaba, Bondo Poraja and Chenchu are all included in the 12-group list of undivided Andhra Pradesh.
ndf7209b63d2.tq: Check every member of the set against the State-specific list.
xs: **Bodo Gadaba, Gutob Gadaba, Bondo Poraja and Chenchu** are all in undivided AP's **12** — option **(1)**.
**Irular, Sahariya, Sentinelese, Jarawa, Onge** are PVTGs or tribes outside the AP list.
**Kolam and Thoti** are on the list but option (3) includes **Irular**.
xa: Variant spellings: **Parangiperja**, **Kuttiya Kondhs**, **Kondareddis**, **Konda Savaras**.
**Jarawa, Onge** = **Negrito** (B.S. Guha).

n0580d8e8b30.s: Which was the first PVTG to receive habitat rights under Section 3(1)(e) of the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
n0580d8e8b30.x: The Bharia of Madhya Pradesh were the first PVTG to get habitat rights under FRA Sec. 3(1)(e). Sahariyas are the largest PVTG by population; Chenchu is on the AP-Telangana PVTG list; the Shompen are protected by the A&N Aboriginal Tribes Regulation, 1956. None of these three was the first to get habitat rights.
xs: The **Bharia** (**Madhya Pradesh**) were the first PVTG to get **habitat rights** under **FRA Sec. 3(1)(e)** — option **(3)**.
**Sahariyas** are the largest PVTG; **Chenchu** is on the AP-Telangana list; the **Shompen** are protected by the **1956** A&N Regulation.
xa: ⚠ First PVTG with habitat rights = **Bharia**.
The **Shompen** issue relates to the **Great Nicobar** project.

nb151a397297.s: The Shompen controversy over the Great Nicobar project concerns protection under:
o: The A&N (Protection of Aboriginal Tribes) Regulation, 1956 and habitat rights under Section 3(1)(e) of the FRA
The Sixth Schedule and the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act
The NCBC Act and urban land rights
The Criminal Tribes Act, 1871 and the Habitual Offenders Acts
nb151a397297.x: The Shompen area is protected by the A&N (Protection of Aboriginal Tribes) Regulation, 1956, and the dispute also raises habitat rights under Section 3(1)(e) of the Forest Rights Act.
xa: The Shompen speak an **Austro-Asiatic** language.
First PVTG with habitat rights: **Bharia** (MP).

nd9c5b56f62f.s: Who among the following wrote ‘The Baiga’ and ‘A Philosophy for NEFA’?
nd9c5b56f62f.x: ‘The Baiga’ and ‘A Philosophy for NEFA’ were written by Verrier Elwin.
xs: **Verrier Elwin** wrote **The Baiga** and **A Philosophy for NEFA** — option **(2)**.
**Ghurye** wrote The Scheduled Tribes; **Raizada** Tribal Development in M.P.; **T.B. Naik** The Bhils.
xa: **MPPSC 2025** matched Russell-Hiralal / Raizada / Naik / **Elwin**.
**Fürer-Haimendorf**: The Chenchus; The Reddis of the Bison Hills.

n132cdfcbc49.s: ‘The Chenchus’ and ‘The Reddis of the Bison Hills’ are associated with
n132cdfcbc49.x: Both works are associated with C. von Fürer-Haimendorf.
n132cdfcbc49.tq: Use the paired-title clue to identify the single author.
xs: **The Chenchus** and **The Reddis of the Bison Hills** are by **C. von Fürer-Haimendorf** — option **(3)**.
**Naik** wrote The Bhils; **Russell and Hira Lal** the Central Provinces volume; **Elwin** The Baiga.
xa: **Chenchu** and **Konda Reddi** are PVTGs on the **AP-Telangana** list.
Chenchus are food-gatherers/hunters (**Vidyarthi and Rai**).

nindian-society-1-76.s: Which was the first tribal university in India?
o: Central Tribal University of Andhra Pradesh
nindian-society-1-76.x: Indira Gandhi National Tribal University (Amarkantak, 2007) was India's first tribal university.
xs: **Indira Gandhi National Tribal University** was the **first Tribal University in India** — option **(4)**.
The **Ministry of Tribal Affairs** (**1999**) was the first ministry exclusively for tribal affairs — not a university.
xa: **Verrier Elwin**: first anthropologist to **study Indian tribes extensively**.
**Tilka Manjhi**: first tribal freedom fighter against the **British**.
**Droupadi Murmu**: first **Scheduled Tribe President** of India.
**National Tribal Policy**: **first drafted 2006**.

nfa9fee72693.x: Anderson wrote 'Imagined Communities'; Barth wrote 'Ethnic Groups and Boundaries' and Jaffrelot 'India's Silent Revolution'.
xa: **T.K. Oommen**: Citizenship, Nationality and Ethnicity.
**Primordialist**: Clifford Geertz, Edward Shils.

n7c7e5ce6c08.s: Longpi pottery is associated with the:
n7c7e5ce6c08.x: The Tangkhul Naga of Manipur make Longpi pottery; the Nyishi hold the Pakke Paga Hornbill Festival.
xa: **Nyishi** = largest tribe of **Arunachal**; **Apatani** live in the **Ziro valley**.
**Tangkhul Naga** are of **Manipur**; two Tangkhul Nagas were killed in Ukhrul (**Apr 2026**).

n3bfbdd157aa.s: Which of the following best defines an ethnic group?
o: People residing only within a constitutionally recognised State
People belonging exclusively to the same religious denomination
People identified solely by their common occupation
People who identify with one another through common language, history, society, culture or nation
n3bfbdd157aa.x: An ethnic group consists of people who identify with one another through common language or dialect, history, society, culture or nation. Ethnicity is not confined to occupation, territory or religion alone.
n3bfbdd157aa.tq: Choose the comprehensive definition rather than an exclusive single-marker definition.
xs: An **ethnic group** is people who **identify with one another** through common **language/dialect, history, society, culture or nation** — option **(4)**.
Ethnicity is not limited to one religion, one occupation or residence in one State.
xa: Ethnic **markers**: **language, religion, race, region, culture**.
**Intra-ethnic** conflict is within a group; **inter-ethnic** is between groups.
**T.K. Oommen** is India's foremost scholar on ethnicity.

n312922a518d.s: The 2011 Census recorded 121 languages and how many mother tongues?
n312922a518d.x: The 2011 Census recorded 121 languages and 270 mother tongues; India has 22 Scheduled Languages.
xa: ⚠ **121** languages vs **270** mother tongues vs **22** scheduled vs **19,500+** returned.
Linguistic stocks: **Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Austro-Asiatic, Tibeto-Burman**.

nd662ac4b90e.s: T.K. Oommen is particularly known for which contribution to the study of ethnicity?
o: Formulating the concept of Greater Nagalim
Separating nation, nationality, ethnicity and citizenship
Classifying Indian tribes exclusively by race
nd662ac4b90e.x: T.K. Oommen is regarded as a foremost Indian scholar on ethnicity and distinguished nation, nationality, ethnicity and citizenship in Citizenship, Nationality and Ethnicity.
nd662ac4b90e.tq: Identify the scholar through his distinctive conceptual contribution and work.
xs: **T.K. Oommen** separates **nation, nationality, ethnicity and citizenship** — option **(2)**.
**Greater Nagalim** is the Naga demand; racial classification follows **S.S. Sarkar**.
xa: Oommen's book: **Citizenship, Nationality and Ethnicity**.
He is India's **foremost scholar on ethnicity**.
**Barth**: Ethnic Groups and Boundaries.

n2ca1531863f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the official languages of Meghalaya?
o: Khasi and Garo were made official languages alongside English
Khasi belongs to the Austro-Asiatic Mon-Khmer group
Khasi and Garo are included in the Eighth Schedule
Garo belongs to the Bodo group of the Sino-Tibetan family
n2ca1531863f.x: Khasi and Garo are official languages of Meghalaya, but neither is in the Eighth Schedule.
xa: India has **22** scheduled languages.
**Sixth Schedule** autonomous district councils exist in **Meghalaya** too.

n9dd0cc7789d.s: According to Arnold Rose, a minority is a group that is set apart by
o: economic class alone and is recognised only by the State
race, nationality, religion or language, and is regarded as different by itself and by others
territorial concentration alone, irrespective of identity
n9dd0cc7789d.x: Arnold Rose describes a minority as a group set apart by race, nationality, religion or language that sees itself, and is seen by others, as different, with negative connotations.
n9dd0cc7789d.tq: Select the option containing the complete definition rather than a partial attribute.
xs: **Arnold Rose**: a minority is set apart by **race, nationality, religion or language** and is **seen as different by itself and others** — option **(3)**.
The difference carries **negative connotations**.
xa: **Giddens**: minority marked by **disadvantage**, **group solidarity**, physical/social **isolation**.
**National minority**: a term from **European minority-rights law**.
NCM Act **1992** notifies India's minorities.

nf0c7148c80d.s: Which community was notified as a minority under the NCM Act, 1992 in 2014?
nf0c7148c80d.x: Jains were the 2014 addition to the notified minorities.
xa: "**National minority**" is a term from European minority-rights law.
**Giddens**: minority = disadvantage, group solidarity, isolation.

o: A sovereign Assam for ethnic Assamese
naa64875b0d0.x: ULFA sought a sovereign Assam; the Bodo movement sought Bodoland, the Naga movement Greater Nagalim, and Khalistan a Sikh state.
xa: **ULFA** was formed in **April 1979**; **ABSU** in **1967**.
Khalistan leader: **Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale**.

nd021ac8e76d.s: The GNLF is associated with which movement?
nd021ac8e76d.x: GNLF led the Gorkhaland movement; MNF the Mizo, ABSU/NDFB the Bodo and NNC/NSCN the Naga movement.
xa: **ABSU** was formed in **1967**.
Gorkhaland responses: **DGHC 1988**; **Gorkhaland Territorial Administration 2012**.

na9740dc23dc.s: Operation All Clear (2003) against ULFA was conducted in:
na9740dc23dc.x: Operation All Clear was in Bhutan (2003), after Operations Bajrang (1990) and Rhino (1991).
xa: **ULFA** (April **1979**) sought a **sovereign Assam** for ethnic Assamese.
The pro-talks ULFA faction **disbanded** after the **Dec 2023** settlement.

n27ad4dd672b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Bodo accords?
o: The 1993 accord was associated with the Bodoland Autonomous Council
Organisations such as ABSU, BLT and NDFB were involved
The 2020 accord was associated with the Bodoland Territorial Region
The 2003 accord created the Bodoland Territorial Region
n27ad4dd672b.x: The 2003 accord led to the Bodoland Territorial Council; the Bodoland Territorial Region came with the 2020 accord.
xa: **ABSU (1967)** first demanded **Udayachal**, then **Bodoland** (**1987**).
ABSU revived the Bodoland demand after the **Assam Accord (1985)**.

nb94e7500c11.s: The States Reorganisation Commission (1953) was headed by:
nb94e7500c11.x: Fazl Ali headed the SRC constituted in 1953; the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 followed.
xa: **Andhra State (1953)** = first state on language lines, after **Potti Sriramulu**'s fast.

ncfed5677c82.s: Which of the following groups correctly represents the States formed in 1987?
ncfed5677c82.x: Goa, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram became States in 1987.
ncfed5677c82.tq: Test a complete named list, with distractors formed by swapping neighbouring north-eastern States.
xs: **Goa, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram** became states in **1987** — option **(2)**.
**Nagaland** became a state in **1963**, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: Mizoram statehood followed the **Mizo Accord 1986**.
**1960**: Bombay split into **Maharashtra** and **Gujarat**; **1966**: **Punjab/Haryana**.
**2014**: **Telangana**; **2019**: J&K and Ladakh UTs.

n532f249d671.s: Which was the first state in India formed on linguistic lines, following the fast of Potti Sriramulu?
n532f249d671.x: Andhra State, formed in 1953 after Potti Sriramulu's fast, was the first state formed on language lines. Andhra Pradesh was formed later, on 1 Nov 1956, under the States Reorganisation Act. Maharashtra was carved out of Bombay in 1960, and Nagaland (1963) was formed in response to Naga aspirations, not on language lines.
n532f249d671.tq: First linguistic state: Andhra State 1953 (Potti Sriramulu).
xs: **Andhra State (1953)** was the **first state on language lines**, after **Potti Sriramulu**'s fast — option **(1)**.
**AP** was formed later, on **1 Nov 1956**; **Maharashtra (1960)** came from Bombay; **Nagaland (1963)** met Naga aspirations.
xa: **SRC (Fazl Ali, 1953)** → **States Reorganisation Act 1956**.
**371D** gives AP special provisions on public employment and education.

neb10ca429fe.s: The ethnic conflict in Manipur since May 2023 centres on:
o: Meitei demand for ST status and Kuki demand for separate administration
Naga demand for statehood and Kuki demand for ST status
Meitei demand for separate administration and Naga demand for ST status
Kuki demand for statehood and Bodo demand for autonomy
neb10ca429fe.x: The Manipur conflict involves the Meitei demand for Scheduled Tribe status and the Kuki demand for separate administration, continuing since May 2023.
xa: **Meitei vs Kuki** was asked in **APPSC 2024**.
Manipur shutdowns hit **12 of 16 districts** (**Apr 2026**).
**371C** = Manipur.

nb42dc3c111f.s: The Assam Movement was primarily associated with conflict between which communities and over which issue?
o: Meitei and Kuki communities over ST status
Mizo and Bru communities over the Eighth Schedule
Assamese and Bengali communities over illegal migration
Tribes and Bengali settlers over demographic change in Tripura
nb42dc3c111f.x: C is right: the Assam Movement (led by AASU) was an Assamese-Bengali conflict over illegal migration. A is the Manipur Meitei-Kuki conflict over ST status, B the Mizo-Bru conflict (not about the Eighth Schedule), and D the Tripura tribes-vs-Bengali-settlers conflict.
nb42dc3c111f.tq: Pair the conflict communities with the correct underlying cause.
xs: The **Assam Movement** (**AASU**) was an **Assamese-Bengali** conflict over **illegal migration** — option **(3)**.
(1) is the **Manipur** conflict; (2) refers to the **Mizo-Bru** clash; (4) is the **Tripura** conflict.
xa: It ended in the **Assam Accord 1985** — cut-off **24 March 1971**.
The **ABSU** revived the Bodoland demand after the Accord.

nc5917e0979e.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Tripura ethnic conflict?
o: Conflict between Meitei and Kuki communities over separate administration
Conflict between indigenous tribes and Bengali settlers following demographic change
Conflict between Nagas and Mizos over Greater Nagalim
Conflict between Assamese and Bengali communities over illegal migration
nc5917e0979e.x: The Tripura conflict developed between indigenous tribes and Bengali settlers after demographic change. The Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council provides local self-rule.
nc5917e0979e.tq: Distinguish the Tripura conflict from the similar ethnic conflicts of Manipur and Assam.
xs: **Tripura**: **indigenous tribes vs Bengali settlers** after **demographic change** — option **(2)**.
(1) is **Manipur**; (4) is **Assam**; Greater Nagalim is the **Naga** demand.
xa: The **Tripura Tribal Areas ADC** gives local self-rule.
Regionalism aids **democratisation** (Tripura ADC) but can feed secessionism.

nf5fc4bad687.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the evolutionary or linear theory of social change?
o: Herbert Spencer explained change as a transition from mechanical to organic solidarity
Auguste Comte is associated with the theory of three stages
Durkheim explained change as a transition from mechanical to organic solidarity
L.H. Morgan is associated with the evolutionary approach
nf5fc4bad687.x: Mechanical to organic solidarity is Durkheim's idea; Spencer explained evolution as movement from simple to complex forms.
xa: **Cyclical** theory: **Spengler, Toynbee, Sorokin, Pareto**.
**Conflict**: **Karl Marx**, Dahrendorf, Coser.
**Technological**: Veblen, **Ogburn**.

n9f33de64c6e.s: The idea of 'challenge and response' is associated with:
n9f33de64c6e.x: Toynbee gave challenge and response; Spengler the decline of the West, Sorokin sensate and ideational cultures, Pareto the circulation of elites.
xa: **Evolutionary (linear)**: Comte, **Spencer**, L.H. Morgan, Durkheim.
**Conflict**: Karl Marx (class struggle), Dahrendorf, Coser.

n77177a70f97.s: Elliot Smith is associated with which theory of social change?
n77177a70f97.x: Elliot Smith is a diffusionist; Veblen and Ogburn are associated with the technological theory.
xa: **Ogburn** originated **cultural lag** in Social Change (**1922**).
Diffusion: Elliot Smith, Perry, **Boas**.

n9c9fb8a04d7.s: M.N. Srinivas coined the term 'Sanskritisation' in which work?
o: Religion and Society among the Coorgs of South India
n9c9fb8a04d7.x: The term was coined in the Coorgs study (1952), after Srinivas first called it 'Brahminisation'; Social Change in Modern India developed it later.
xa: Coined by **M.N. Srinivas** (**APPSC 2019**).
Reference groups: **Brahmins**, **Kshatriya, Vaishya** and the local **dominant caste**.

n0d1d091f03b.s: De-sanskritisation refers to a process in which groups:
o: Reject Sanskritic norms and assert their own identity
Replace non-material culture with material culture
Adopt only Western technology and institutions
Merge completely with a dominant culture
n0d1d091f03b.x: De-sanskritisation involves rejecting Sanskritic norms and asserting one's own identity, as illustrated by the non-Brahmin or Dravidian movement.
n0d1d091f03b.tq: Use the reversal of Sanskritisation carefully; rejection and identity assertion are the key clues.
xs: **De-sanskritisation**: groups **reject Sanskritic norms** and **assert their own identity** — option **(1)**.
Example: the **non-Brahmin/Dravidian movement**.
Full merger with a dominant culture is **assimilation**.
xa: **Sanskritisation**: positional, not structural change.
**Acculturation**: influenced by another culture but distinct.

n6d383919406.s:
According to M.N. Srinivas, Westernisation operates at which of the following levels?
1. Technology
2. Institutions
3. Values
n6d383919406.x: Srinivas identified technology, institutions, ideology and values as levels at which British rule produced Westernisation.
xa: Srinivas treated Westernisation as **ethically neutral**.
Westernisation has a **specific source**; modernisation is **universal**.

n0dd8e1f041b.x: Max Weber used the expression “disenchantment of the world” in relation to secularisation.
n0dd8e1f041b.tq: Match the distinctive phrase with the correct sociological thinker.
xs: **Weber** called secularisation the "**disenchantment of the world**" — option **(4)**.
**Psychic mobility** is **Lerner**'s; **culture circles** the German-Austrian school's; **great tradition** relates to **Singer**.
xa: Srinivas's secularisation: differentiation and **rationalisation**.
Sociological secularisation = decline of religion's hold on social life.

ned222cd4ace.s: In Daniel Lerner's sequence of modernisation, which stage comes first?
ned222cd4ace.x: Lerner's sequence runs urbanisation, literacy, media exposure, then participation.
xa: Lerner linked "**Empathy**" with **psychic mobility**.
His book: **The Passing of Traditional Society (1958)**.

n6ff1b8ea945.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about sources of social change?
o: The spread of modern education illustrates education as a source of change
Reform and Dalit movements are examples of social movements
Street plays under Nasha Mukt Bharat illustrate behaviour-change communication
The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 illustrates behaviour-change communication through media
n6ff1b8ea945.x: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 illustrates the role of law, not media communication.
xa: Dalit change came through **state policy, reform movements, and Sanskritisation and Westernisation**.
⚠ **Seasonal nomad migration** = routine cycle, NOT social change.

nad5cd629292.s: Who propounded the concept of cultural lag?
nad5cd629292.x: W.F. Ogburn propounded the concept of cultural lag in Social Change, published in 1922.
nad5cd629292.tq: Match the concept with its originator, not with a scholar associated with another process of change.
xs: **W.F. Ogburn** originated **cultural lag** in **Social Change (1922)** — option **(2)**.
**Daniel Lerner** gave the modernisation sequence; **Weber** called secularisation the "disenchantment of the world".
xa: Ogburn is a **technological** theorist, with **Veblen**.
Lagging factors: **religion, law, tradition**; **politics is not** one (**UPPSC 2014**).

nd3e1fea778a.s: According to Ogburn, cultural lag occurs because:
o: Non-material culture changes faster than material culture
Material culture, especially technology, changes faster than non-material culture
Religion and law are entirely unaffected by technological change
Both material and non-material culture always change at the same rate
nd3e1fea778a.x: Ogburn held that material culture, particularly technology, changes faster, while beliefs, norms and other non-material elements lag behind.
nd3e1fea778a.tq: Check the direction of the comparison; the material–non-material order is the central trap.
xs: In Ogburn's **cultural lag**, **material culture** (technology) changes **faster** than **non-material culture** (beliefs, norms) — option **(2)**.
Option (1) reverses it; (3) and (4) contradict the idea of a lag.
xa: Lagging factors: **religion, law, tradition**.
Example: digital spread vs slow norms on children's online safety (**DPDP Act 2023**).
Ogburn: Social Change (**1922**).

n56ad7381b21.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a lagging factor in cultural lag?
n56ad7381b21.x: Religion, law and tradition are identified as lagging factors. Politics is not included in that list.
n56ad7381b21.tq: Find the outsider in the short list rather than selecting a familiar social institution automatically.
xs: **Politics** is **not** a lagging factor — option **(3)** (**UPPSC 2014**).
**Religion, law and tradition** are the lagging factors.
xa: ⚠ Cultural lag: **politics** is NOT a lagging factor.
Material culture (technology) changes faster than non-material culture.
Concept by **W.F. Ogburn** (**1922**).

n53c1fa0eb40.s: The rapid spread of digital technology accompanied by slower changes in norms concerning children's online safety illustrates:
n53c1fa0eb40.x: The example illustrates cultural lag because technological change is faster than the adjustment of social norms. The reference also mentions parental consent for persons under 18 under the DPDP Act, 2023.
n53c1fa0eb40.tq: Apply the material-versus-non-material distinction to a contemporary example.
xs: Fast **digital spread** with **slow change in norms** on children's online safety is **cultural lag** — option **(1)**.
Technology moves ahead; norms lag behind.
xa: The **DPDP Act 2023** requires **parental consent** for under-**18**s.
India has **820 million+** internet users.
Concept by **W.F. Ogburn**.

nindian-society-4-8.s: Delay in adjustment to change is called:
nindian-society-4-8.x: Cultural lag is delay in adjusting to change; xenophobia is fear of foreigners.
n: Ethnicity is shared cultural identity. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 17-21]
Cultural lag is delay in adjustment to change. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 17-21]
Xenophobia is fear of foreigners. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 17-21]
Regionalism is loyalty to a region. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 17-21]
An ethnic group is a group sharing a common culture. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 17-21]
xa: **Communalism** = loyalty to a **religious group**.
In cultural lag, **material culture** changes faster than **non-material culture**, which lags (**Ogburn**).
**Cultural relativism** = understanding a culture on its **own terms**.

nindian-society-4-33.s: A group sharing a common culture is known as a/an:
nindian-society-4-33.x: An ethnic group shares a common culture. A clan, lineage and sapinda are kinship or descent groups.
nindian-society-4-33.tq: Discriminate cultural groups from kinship groups.
xs: A group sharing a **common culture** is an **ethnic group** — option **(2)**.
**Ethnicity** means a **shared cultural identity**.
**Clan**, **lineage** and **sapinda** are kinship/descent groups, not cultural ones.
xa: **Cultural pluralism** = coexistence of different cultures.
**Ethnocentrism** = viewing one's own culture as **superior**.
**Communalism** = loyalty to a **religious group**.

n71bb53a68a7.s: Cultural change through sustained contact, in which one group is influenced by another culture, is called:
n71bb53a68a7.x: Acculturation is change through sustained contact with another culture (APPSC 2019); assimilation goes further, with the minority merging fully and losing its identity.
xa: ⚠ Acculturation = influenced but distinct.
**Westernisation**: changes from **150+ years** of British rule.

nindian-society-4-26.s: Understanding a culture on its own terms is called:
nindian-society-4-26.x: Cultural relativism means understanding a culture on its own terms; cultural diffusion is the spread of culture.
n: Cultural diffusion is the spread of culture. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 17-21]
Cultural relativism means understanding a culture on its own terms. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 17-21]
Multiculturalism is the coexistence of multiple cultures. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 17-21]
Communalism is loyalty to a religious group. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 17-21]
xa: **Regionalism** = loyalty to a **region**; **xenophobia** = **fear of foreigners**.
**Ethnocentrism** = viewing one's own culture as **superior**.
**Integration** = participation while **retaining identity**.

n37b26e9255e.s: Milton Singer's When a Great Tradition Modernizes argues that:
o: Tradition and modernity can continue together in Madras temple culture
Modernity always destroys every traditional institution
Caste groups can change only through legislation
n37b26e9255e.x: Singer showed that tradition and modernity can coexist, using Madras temple culture as an example.
n37b26e9255e.tq: Choose the precise coexistence argument and reject extreme claims about modernity destroying tradition.
xs: **Milton Singer** showed **tradition and modernity continue together** in **Madras temple culture** — option **(1)**.
So modernity need not destroy tradition (option 2 is the opposite).
xa: Book: **When a Great Tradition Modernizes**.
**Lerner**: The Passing of Traditional Society (**1958**).

n8bf45483533.s: Which one of the following is NOT a source of social change?
o: Migration of nomads in a particular season
Legislation such as the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955
n8bf45483533.x: Seasonal migration of nomads is a routine, recurring cycle and does not alter social structure, so it is not a source of social change (APPSC 2019). Modern education, legislation like the Untouchability (Offences) Act 1955, and industrialisation/urbanisation are all recognised sources of social change.
n8bf45483533.tq: Routine seasonal cycles = not social change.
xs: **Migration of nomads in a particular season** is **not** a source of social change — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2019**).
It is a **routine cycle** that recurs without altering society.
**Modern education**, the **Untouchability (Offences) Act 1955** and **industrialisation/urbanisation** are all recognised sources.
xa: ⚠ Seasonal nomad migration = routine cycle, NOT social change.
**Technology**: **820 million+** internet users.
**Planning**: Green Revolution (**3rd Plan**).

n4f7fb7c1c51.s: The idea of 'culture circles' was developed by which diffusionist school?
n4f7fb7c1c51.x: Graebner and Schmidt (German-Austrian) gave culture circles; the British school saw Egypt as the source and the American school gave culture areas.
xa: ⚠ Culture **circles** = German-Austrian; culture **areas** = American.
Indus debate: **Mackay** (migration), **Wheeler** (diffusion of ideas).

n5df71ea88dd.s: Besides Brahmins, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas, which of the following may act as a reference group in Sanskritisation?
n5df71ea88dd.x: Reference groups in Sanskritisation may be Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas or the locally dominant caste.
xa: Srinivas first called the process "**Brahminisation**".
Coined in the **Coorgs** study (**1952**).

n15187e95acb.s: Constitutional secularism, as distinct from sociological secularisation, concerns:
o: Complete removal of religion from public life
Changes in social beliefs and practices
n15187e95acb.x: Constitutional secularism is about state neutrality and equal respect; sociological secularisation is about changing beliefs and practices.
xa: Sociological secularisation = **decline of religion's hold** on social life.
Srinivas: less "religious" meaning, differentiation, **rationalisation**.

n1c539d95e21.s: Sanskritisation may give a caste upward mobility, but it:
n1c539d95e21.x: Sanskritisation gives positional mobility to a caste but does not change the hierarchy itself.
xa: Sanskritisation = **positional, not structural** change.
Srinivas preferred Westernisation as **ethically neutral**.

nindian-society-4-36.s: Regionalism refers to which of the following?
nindian-society-4-36.x: Regionalism is loyalty to one's region. Loyalty to a religious group is communalism, to a caste casteism, and fear of foreigners xenophobia.
xs: **Regionalism** is **loyalty to a region** — option **(3)**.
**Fear of foreigners** is **xenophobia**; loyalty to a **religious group** is **communalism**.
Loyalty to one's own **caste** is **casteism**.
xa: **Ethnicity** = shared cultural identity.
**Cultural diffusion** = spread of culture; **cultural relativism** = understanding a culture on its own terms.

n6d7d8c2da23.s: According to Melvin Tumin, which of the following is NOT a characteristic of social stratification?
o: It affects the life chances of individuals
It is social rather than biological
It is a recent phenomenon of industrial societies
n6d7d8c2da23.x: Tumin regarded stratification as ancient and universal, not as a recent phenomenon limited to industrial societies.
n6d7d8c2da23.tq: The extreme time claim in the option is the trap; compare it with the characteristic of being ancient.
xs: For **Tumin**, stratification is **ancient**, so "a **recent phenomenon of industrial societies**" is not a characteristic — option **(3)**.
His list: **social (not biological)**, **ancient**, **universal**, diverse in form, **consequential** (decides **life chances**).
xa: Tumin also **criticised Davis-Moore**: stratification **wastes talent** and passes inequality on.
In India, **Harappan** society showed differentiation (citadel vs lower town).

n673adda0ebd.s: The functionalist theory of stratification is associated with:
n673adda0ebd.x: Davis and Moore gave the functionalist approach; Marx the conflict, Weber the multi-dimensional and Dumont the ideological caste approach.
xa: ⚠ Davis-Moore = functionalist; **Tumin** = its critic; Weber = **class, status, party**.
Dumont's book: **Homo Hierarchicus** (purity and pollution).

nb73a58b386b.s: According to Davis and Moore, stratification is functionally necessary because it:
o: Ensures equal rewards for all positions
Draws scarce talent into functionally important positions through higher rewards
nb73a58b386b.x: Davis and Moore argued that unequal rewards attract scarce talent to functionally important positions.
xa: The theory dates from **1945**.
**Melvin Tumin** countered that it **wastes talent** and passes inequality to the next generation.

n3b57ba47b29.s: Who criticised functionalism by arguing that stratification wastes talent and transmits inequality to the next generation?
n3b57ba47b29.x: Melvin Tumin criticised the functionalist view, arguing that stratification can waste talent and reproduce inequality across generations.
n3b57ba47b29.tq: Link the critique to the critic rather than to the original functionalist theorists.
xs: **Melvin Tumin** argued stratification **wastes talent** and **passes inequality to the next generation** — option **(4)**.
**Thorner** classified agrarian classes; **Beteille** studied Sripuram; **Sorokin** set out vertical and horizontal mobility.
xa: Tumin critiqued the **functionalist** theory of **Davis and Moore** (**1945**).
Tumin's characteristics: social, ancient, universal, diverse, consequential.

n8158e3fe853.s: Max Weber's three dimensions of stratification are class, status and:
n8158e3fe853.x: Weber's three dimensions are class, status and party; class position and market situation decide life chances.
xa: Weber saw caste as a **closed status group**.
**Status group**: people sharing a **lifestyle and social honour**.

n399f99a10ca.s: The demand of Marathas, Gujjars and Patels for OBC status is explained mainly as a pursuit of:
n399f99a10ca.x: Dominant peasant castes such as Marathas, Gujjars and Patels seek OBC status in pursuit of greater life chances.
xa: **Life chances** (**Weber**): ability to get the necessities and opportunities for a better life.
Marathas also figure in **Kshatriyaisation** claims.

nindian-society-5-8.s: 'Homo Hierarchicus', on the purity-pollution principle, was written by:
nindian-society-5-8.x: Dumont wrote Homo Hierarchicus; Ghurye listed the features of caste and Srinivas coined Sanskritisation and dominant caste.
n: G. S. Ghurye stated that caste is characterized by hierarchy, endogamy and social restrictions. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 21-24]
The class system is based on wealth and occupation. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 21-24]
xa: **Max Weber**: **class, status, party**; class decides **life chances**.
For **Marx**, class depends on ownership of the **means of production**.
⚠ **Davis-Moore** = functionalist; **Tumin** = its critic.

nindian-society-5-13.s: The estate system of stratification is associated with:
nindian-society-5-13.x: Estates belong to medieval feudal Europe; caste to traditional India, slavery to ancient Greece and Rome, class to industrial societies.
n: Ancient Greece is an example associated with slavery. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 21-24]
Rome is an example associated with slavery. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 21-24]
America is an example associated with slavery. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 21-24]
The estate system was found in medieval Europe. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 21-24]
xa: Estates were **clergy**, **nobility** and **commoners**.
Slavery meant **extreme inequality** — the person was **property**, with **no freedom**.
The class system is **open**; the caste system **closed**.

nindian-society-19-19.s: Which of the following is a hereditary caste occupation?
nindian-society-19-19.x: Blacksmith, like potter and weaver, is an inherited caste occupation; IAS officer, doctor and scientist are achieved positions.
xa: Other caste occupations: **potter**, **carpenter**, **weaver**.
Caste status is **linked with occupation** and **determines social prestige**.

n5cf620ef0d9.s: In the caste system, vertical and horizontal classification respectively refer to:
o: Ranking by birth; division into separate caste groups
Division into separate caste groups; ranking by birth
Ritual ranking; rural and urban residence
n5cf620ef0d9.x: Vertical classification is hierarchical ranking by birth; horizontal classification is division into many separate caste groups.
xa: Caste basis: **birth and hereditary status**.
Muslim strata: **Ashraf, Ajlaf, Arzal**.

ne9ef5c2f079.s: According to M. N. Srinivas, a dominant caste combines numerical strength, sizeable arable land and:
ne9ef5c2f079.x: Srinivas's dominant caste has numerical strength, sizeable arable land and a fairly high ritual rank.
xa: Caste dominance now rests increasingly on **secular factors**.
Group mobility: **Sanskritisation** (Srinivas), **Kshatriyaisation** (Kulke).

n674e93bc9f6.s: A change in status within the lifetime of one individual is called:
n674e93bc9f6.x: Intra-generational mobility occurs within a single person's lifetime; inter-generational mobility occurs across generations.
xa: **ES 2025-26** defines mobility as inter- and intra-generational change in status.
**Structural** mobility comes from changes in the economy's occupational structure.

nd9a21410049.s: Kshatriyaisation (Kulke) refers to martial or landholding groups claiming:
nd9a21410049.x: Kshatriyaisation refers to claims by martial or landholding groups to warrior or Kshatriya status.
xa: It brings mobility but **reproduces the hierarchy**.
**Sanskritisation** (Srinivas) is the other route of caste group mobility.

nd83cbcf1111.s: Kshatriyaisation among Marathas, Jats and Yadavs is criticised because it:
o: Brings mobility but reproduces the caste hierarchy
Blocks all mobility for these castes
nd83cbcf1111.x: Kshatriyaisation gives mobility and higher status claims, but it reproduces the hierarchy rather than eliminating it.
xa: **Kshatriyaisation** was named by **Kulke**: martial/landholding groups claim **warrior (Kshatriya)** status.
**Sanskritisation** (**M.N. Srinivas**) is the parallel route: copying rituals and lifestyle of higher castes.
Dominant peasant castes (**Marathas, Gujjars, Patels**) now seek **OBC status** for "greater life chances".
**Pitirim Sorokin** first set out **vertical and horizontal** mobility (book **Social Mobility**, **1927**).

nindian-society-5-17.s: A farmer's son becoming an IAS officer is an example of which type of mobility?
nindian-society-5-17.x: A farmer's son becoming an IAS officer rises above his father's position, which is upward (vertical) mobility. Being a change across generations, it is not intragenerational, and it is not horizontal or downward.
nindian-society-5-17.tq: Ask whether the move is up, down or level, and within or across generations.
n: A farmer's son becoming an IAS officer is an example of upward mobility. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 21-24]
xs: A **farmer's son becoming an IAS officer** is the notes' example of **upward mobility** — option **(4)**.
**Vertical** mobility is **upward or downward** movement in the hierarchy; this is a rise.
**Horizontal** mobility is change with the **same status**; **intragenerational** is change **within one lifetime**.
xa: **Intergenerational** mobility = change between **parents and children**.
**Structural** mobility comes from changes in the occupational structure (e.g., **industrialisation**).
**Pitirim Sorokin** first set out **vertical and horizontal** mobility.

nindian-society-17-1.s: Caste status refers to which of the following?
o: The level of education attained by an individual
The social position occupied by an individual within the caste hierarchy
The economic position occupied within an urban society
The occupation obtained through personal effort
nindian-society-17-1.x: Caste status is a person's position in the caste hierarchy, fixed by birth. Education and occupation are bases of achieved status.
nindian-society-17-1.tq: Recall the meaning of caste status.
n: Caste status refers to the social position occupied by an individual within the caste hierarchy. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 50-51]
xs: **Caste status** is the **social position occupied by an individual within the caste hierarchy** — option **(2)**.
It is **determined by birth** and is a **fixed social position**.
Education and an occupation gained by **personal effort** belong to **achieved status**.
xa: Caste status is **linked with occupation** and **determines social prestige**.
**Ascribed status** (by birth): **caste**, **gender**, **family background**.
Inter-caste conflicts today are about **power, not ritual status**.

nindian-society-19-12.s: Occupational mobility, which lets people take up work other than their family's, is associated with the weakening of:
nindian-society-19-12.x: Occupational mobility lets people leave inherited occupations, which weakens hereditary occupations.
xa: Other weakening forces: **education**, **industrialization**, **urbanization**.
**Ezhavas** of Kerala moved from **toddy tapping** to tailoring and cottage industries.

nindian-society-17-4.s: A clerk moving to an equal-rank job in another office is an example of:
nindian-society-17-4.x: Moving to an equal-rank position is horizontal mobility; a labourer's son becoming an engineer is intergenerational mobility.
n: Caste is an example of ascribed status. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 50-51]
Gender is an example of ascribed status. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 50-51]
An IAS Officer is an example of achieved status. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 50-51]
A Doctor is an example of achieved status. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 50-51]
xa: Achieved status is obtained through **personal effort**: **IAS officer**, **doctor**, **scientist**.
**Intragenerational** mobility = change **within one lifetime**.
Achieved status grew with **education**, **urbanization**, **industrialization**, **reservation**, **globalization**.

nindian-society-17-16.s: The adoption of upper-caste customs by a lower caste is called:
nindian-society-17-16.x: Sanskritisation is adopting upper-caste customs; Westernisation is adopting Western values and ways.
xa: **M. N. Srinivas** coined **Sanskritisation**; group mobility via caste.
**Kshatriyaisation** (**Kulke**): martial/landholding groups claim warrior status.

n5deafe8889d.s: Daniel Thorner’s agrarian classes are primarily differentiated according to:
o: Nature of land rights and type of income
n5deafe8889d.x: Thorner’s classification is based on the nature of land rights and the type of income derived from agriculture.
n5deafe8889d.tq: Select the structural economic basis rather than a cultural basis of classification.
xs: **Thorner**'s agrarian classes follow the **nature of land rights** and **type of income** — option **(4)**.
They are **Maliks**, **Kisans** and **Mazdoors**.
xa: ⚠ **Maliks** = landlords on rent; **Kisans** = own-and-cultivate; **Mazdoors** = landless.
Source: **UPSC** Post-Independence notes p.**91**.

n8974e1dbac2.s: Social stratification refers to the ranking of groups in a hierarchy based on unequal distribution of which of the following?
n8974e1dbac2.x: Social stratification is the hierarchical ranking of groups according to unequal wealth, prestige and power.
n8974e1dbac2.tq: Use the precise definition rather than selecting a related social characteristic.
xs: **Stratification** ranks groups in a hierarchy of unequal **wealth, prestige and power** — option **(1)**.
Language, religion, region or residence are not the unequal rewards in the definition.
xa: Bases: **caste, class, gender, age, race, ethnicity**.
⚠ **Language is NOT a basis** of stratification (**APPSC-GS 2019**).
**Melvin Tumin**: stratification is social, ancient, universal, diverse in form, consequential.

n0e3412cf45d.s: Andre Beteille's 'Caste, Class and Power' (1965) was based on fieldwork in:
n0e3412cf45d.x: Beteille studied Sripuram village in Thanjavur and argued that caste, class and power can diverge.
xa: Land ownership and political authority moved away from the old ritual hierarchy.
Beteille also wrote **Studies in Agrarian Social Structure**.

n68b35218354.s: Who defined caste as a system in which mobility up and down the status ladder, at least ideally, may not occur?
n68b35218354.x: A. W. Green defined caste as a system of stratification in which status mobility, at least ideally, may not occur.
xa: One APP note prints "**A.R. Green**".
Caste is a **closed** system with **cumulative** inequality.

n90b730adcdd.s: Which of the following works is associated with Andre Beteille?
o: The Division of Labour in Society
n90b730adcdd.x: Studies in Agrarian Social Structure is associated with Andre Beteille. He also wrote Caste, Class and Power.
n90b730adcdd.tq: Match the title with the sociologist associated with agrarian social structure.
xs: **Studies in Agrarian Social Structure** is by **Andre Beteille** — option **(2)**.
**Social Mobility** is **Sorokin**'s (**1927**); **Homo Hierarchicus** is **Dumont**'s.
xa: Beteille also wrote **Caste, Class and Power (1965)**.
Beteille's fieldwork: **Sripuram**, Thanjavur.

n7a2cb04d9b9.s: Who first systematically set out the distinction between vertical and horizontal social mobility?
n7a2cb04d9b9.x: Pitirim Sorokin first set out the distinction between vertical and horizontal mobility in Social Mobility, published in 1927.
n7a2cb04d9b9.tq: Link the paired mobility concepts with their original theorist and work.
xs: **Pitirim Sorokin** first set out **vertical and horizontal mobility** — option **(4)**.
His book: **Social Mobility (1927)**.
xa: **Srinivas** gave **Sanskritisation**; **Thorner** agrarian classes; **Davis** functionalism.
Horizontal example: **one clerical job to another**.

nindian-society-4-19.s: Viewing one's own culture as superior is called:
nindian-society-4-19.x: Ethnocentrism is seeing one's own culture as superior; casteism is loyalty to one's own caste.
n: Untouchability is social exclusion based on caste. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 17-21]
Casteism is loyalty to one's own caste. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 17-21]
Social mobility is movement between social positions. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 17-21]
Ethnocentrism is viewing one's own culture as superior. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 17-21]
xa: **Dominant caste** = an **economically and politically powerful** caste.
**Vertical** mobility = upward or downward; **horizontal** = change **without status change**.
Muslim stratification: **Ashraf, Ajlaf, Arzal**.

nindian-society-17-17.s: Which of the following is a feature of caste status?
nindian-society-17-17.x: A fixed social position is a feature of caste status; education, urbanisation and globalisation widen achieved status.
xa: Other such factors: **industrialization** and **reservation policies**.
Caste status is **determined by birth** and **determines social prestige**.

nindian-society-2-4.s: 'Modernization of Indian Tradition' was written by:
nindian-society-2-4.x: Yogendra Singh wrote it; Ghurye wrote 'Caste and Race in India' and Desai 'Social Background of Indian Nationalism'.
n: Caste and Race in India was written by G. S. Ghurye. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 13-15]
A. R. Desai wrote Social Background of Indian Nationalism. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 13-15]
Yogendra Singh wrote Modernization of Indian Tradition. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 13-15]
Andre Beteille wrote Caste, Class and Power. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 13-15]
Modernization of Indian Tradition was written by Yogendra Singh. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 13-15]
xa: Beteille's **Caste, Class and Power** (**1965**) is based on **Sripuram** village, Thanjavur.
**Louis Dumont** wrote **Homo Hierarchicus** (purity and pollution).
**Pitirim Sorokin** wrote **Social Mobility** (**1927**).

nffc18b17fd5.s: The ranking principle of the caste system is:
nffc18b17fd5.x: Caste ranking rests on ritual purity and pollution.
xa: Varna crystallised in the **Later Vedic** period.
**Dumont** read caste through **purity and pollution** (Homo Hierarchicus).

n2369bf17cd5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about caste and class?
o: Caste is based on birth and hereditary status
Inequality in caste is cumulative, whereas in class it is dispersed
Class is associated with achievement, wealth, education and occupation
Mobility is generally more restricted in class than in caste
n2369bf17cd5.x: The comparison is reversed: mobility is more restricted in caste and more allowed in class.
xa: Caste = **closed**; class = **open**.
Agrarian hierarchy broadly **matches the caste hierarchy**.

n96e4064c605.s: India's middle class is projected to reach what share of the population by 2047?
n96e4064c605.x: India's middle class was about 43.2 crore (31%) in 2021 and is projected to reach 61% by 2047.
xa: Definitions: **World Bank** $10-50/day (PPP); **NCAER** ₹2-10 lakh; **PRICE** ₹5-30 lakh.
It emerged from **English education** after **Macaulay's Minute (1835)**.

n3aacfee75cc.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, low social mobility:
n3aacfee75cc.x: The Survey says low mobility entrenches historical inequality; health, education, technology and institutions drive mobility.
xa: **Intra-generational** = within one lifetime; **inter-generational** = between parents and children.

n76fbbf9aa0a.s: Southern backward classes demanded reservation in government jobs through which movement?
n76fbbf9aa0a.x: They demanded reservation through Periyar's Self-Respect Movement; reservation led to group mobility and broadened the urban middle class.
xa: **Mandal Commission**: OBCs **over 52%**.
Mandal used **11 indicators** = **4 social + 4 economic + 3 educational**.

nc1b5f5f9428.s: The shift of the Ezhavas of Kerala from toddy tapping to tailoring and cottage industries is an example of:
nc1b5f5f9428.x: Moving from toddy tapping to tailoring and cottage industries illustrates occupational mobility among the Ezhavas.
xa: Other routes: **education**, **reservation**, **migration and urbanisation**.
Dalit change: **state policy, reform movements, Sanskritisation/Westernisation**.

n2555ea2c9df.s: Which of the following can weaken caste identity in cities?
o: City anonymity and caste-blind public spaces
n2555ea2c9df.x: Anonymity and caste-blind public spaces can weaken caste identity, though migrants may carry caste networks and prejudices into cities.
xa: The Gen Z "**horizontal**" category cuts across vertical caste loyalties.
**Ezhavas** of Kerala show **occupational mobility** (toddy tapping → tailoring).

n63ad7b4bd16.s: The Mandal Commission identified OBCs as constituting over what proportion of the population and used how many indicators for their identification?
n63ad7b4bd16.x: The Mandal Commission estimated OBCs at over 52 per cent of the population and used 11 indicators: four social, four economic and three educational.
n63ad7b4bd16.tq: Pair the population estimate with the total number of indicators, not with unrelated percentages.
xs: **Mandal Commission**: OBCs **over 52 per cent**, identified by **11 indicators** — option **(2)**.
The **11** = **4 social + 4 economic + 3 educational**.
**31%** and **43.2** are middle-class figures; **67%** is from the Telangana survey.
xa: OBCs = communities **not on SC/ST lists**.
⚠ Mandal **11** indicators = **4 + 4 + 3**.

n2d91c6422b9.s: The Telangana caste survey ranked how many castes?
n2d91c6422b9.x: The survey ranked 242 castes; 135 castes (67% of the population) scored above the State average on backwardness.
xa: It showed backward classes are **not one block**.
Mandal: OBCs **over 52%**.

n022a0cb2298.s: As per the Economic Survey estimate cited, poverty fell from 21.9 per cent in 2011–12 to what level in 2023–24?
