n022a0cb2298.x: The estimate places poverty at 2.3 per cent in 2023–24, down from 21.9 per cent in 2011–12.
xa: Key determinants of mobility per the Survey: **health, education, technology, institutions**; low mobility **entrenches historical inequality**.
India's middle class was **43.2 crore (31%)** in **2021**, projected to reach **61% by 2047**.
⚠ **31%** is the middle-class share in 2021, not a poverty figure.
**OECD**: India will have the world's **largest middle class by 2035**, overtaking **China**.

nindian-society-19-18.s:
How many of the following are listed as modern changes that have weakened hereditary occupations?
1. Education
2. Industrialization
3. Urbanization
4. Occupational mobility
nindian-society-19-18.x: All four weaken hereditary occupations: education, industrialisation, urbanisation and occupational mobility.
xs: **All four** — **education**, **industrialization**, **urbanization** and **occupational mobility** — weaken hereditary occupations: option **(4)**.
Hereditary characteristics, occupations, rights and positions pass **from one generation to another** until these modern changes break the chain.
xa: Hereditary occupations: **traditional occupations**, **family businesses**.
**Kingship** is a **hereditary position**; **property ownership** a **hereditary right**.
The **Jajmani system has weakened**.

n11d1804427a.s: Which one of the following is NOT generally recognised as a basis of social stratification?
n11d1804427a.x: Caste, gender and ethnicity are recognised bases of social stratification. Language is not treated as a basis in this context.
n11d1804427a.tq: Find the odd term among the recognised bases of stratification.
xs: **Language** is **not** a basis of social stratification — option **(1)** (**APPSC-GS 2019**).
**Ethnicity**, **gender** and **caste** are all bases, along with class, age and race.
xa: Stratification = ranking by unequal **wealth, prestige and power**.
Caste has **vertical** (ranking by birth) and **horizontal** (separate groups) classification.
Among **Muslims**: **Ashraf, Ajlaf, Arzal**.

nc04337f5d0e.s: Among non-Hindu communities, the categories Ashraf, Ajlaf and Arzal are associated with:
nc04337f5d0e.x: Ashraf, Ajlaf and Arzal are status categories found among Muslims, illustrating that stratification is not confined to Hindus.
nc04337f5d0e.tq: Match the named internal categories with the community to which they belong.
xs: **Ashraf, Ajlaf, Arzal** are strata among **Muslims** — option **(2)**.
They show stratification is not confined to Hindus.
xa: Bases of stratification: caste, class, gender, age, race, ethnicity.
Caste ranking principle = **purity and pollution**.

n022341664df.s: The emergence of the English-educated middle class in India is most directly associated with which of the following?
n022341664df.x: Macaulay's Minute of 1835 promoted English education, which contributed to the emergence of an English-educated middle class that later participated in the freedom struggle.
n022341664df.tq: Identify the historical document directly associated with the emergence of the class.
xs: **Macaulay's Minute** (**1835**) spread **English education**, producing the English-educated middle class — option **(1)**.
That middle class **led the freedom struggle**.
xa: Middle class size: **43.2 crore (31%)** in **2021**; projected **61% by 2047**.
Occupational base: **salaried professionals**, white-collar and service jobs, business.

n12ec5343d9b.s: Which set correctly describes a typical village, as against a town or city?
o: Agricultural; large and dense; heterogeneous; formal control
Agricultural; small and sparse; homogeneous; informal control
Non-agricultural; small and sparse; homogeneous; informal control
Non-agricultural; large and dense; heterogeneous; formal control
n12ec5343d9b.x: Villages are mainly agricultural, small and sparse, homogeneous, built on primary face-to-face relations and governed by informal control.
xa: Village informal control works through **family, caste, custom**; city formal control through **law, police**.
Wirth: **size, density, heterogeneity** produce urbanism.
⚠ **Homogeneity** is a rural element; **cultural diversity** is NOT (UPPSC 2021).

nd782d8a8006.s: Which one of the following is NOT an element of a rural community?
nd782d8a8006.x: The elements of a rural community are territory, we-feeling (community sentiment), relative self-sufficiency, small size and homogeneity. Cultural diversity is not an element (UPPSC 2021); a rural community is marked by homogeneity, while diversity and heterogeneity are urban traits.
nd782d8a8006.tq: Rural = homogeneous, so diversity is the odd one out.
xs: **Cultural diversity** is NOT an element of a rural community — so option **(3)** is correct (**UPPSC 2021**).
Elements are **territory, we-feeling (community sentiment), relative self-sufficiency**, small size and **homogeneity**.
Diversity/**heterogeneity** is a trait of the town or city.
xa: Urban life features: **competition, impersonal relationships, loss of humanistic values**, anonymity, weak social control.
⚠ **Informal ties** are NOT an urban feature (JPSC 2021).
**Metcalfe** called villages "**little republics**" — self-reliant units.

nac7c7a87adc.s: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic feature of urban life?
o: Informal ties as the dominant feature
nac7c7a87adc.x: Urban life is associated with competition, impersonal relationships, anonymity and weak social control. Informal ties are not identified as a characteristic feature in this context.
nac7c7a87adc.tq: Find the feature belonging more closely to rural primary relations than to urban life.
xs: **Informal ties as the dominant feature** is NOT a feature of urban life — so option **(3)** is correct (**JPSC 2021**).
Urban features: **competition, impersonal relationships**, loss of humanistic values, **anonymity, weak social control**.
xa: Informal control (family, caste, custom) belongs to the **village**; city control is **formal** (law, police).
**Urbanism** = social, cultural, behavioural side of urban life; **urbanisation** = population shifting to urban areas.
Urban problems include **lack of social control**, maladjustment, **environmental degradation**, alienation.

n15f39afec04.s: Who described Indian villages as ‘little republics’?
n15f39afec04.x: Charles Metcalfe described Indian villages as ‘little republics’, referring to their character as relatively self-reliant units.
n15f39afec04.tq: Test the thinker associated with a distinctive description.
xs: **Charles Metcalfe** called Indian villages "**little republics**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
He saw them as **self-reliant units** (asked as "**Village republics**", MPPSC 2020).
**Louis Wirth** wrote on **urbanism**; **Robert Redfield** gave the **Little Community** and folk-urban continuum; **M.N. Srinivas** studied **Rampura**.
xa: ⚠ **Redfield** = folk-urban continuum + Little Community; **Wirth** = urbanism; **Metcalfe** = little republics.
Elements of a rural community: **territory, we-feeling, relative self-sufficiency**, small size, homogeneity.
**Milton Singer** studied Hinduism in urban **Madras** — continuity between tradition and modernity.

n7bb9a7617a9.s: McKim Marriott's concepts of universalisation and parochialisation describe the two-way flow between:
n7bb9a7617a9.x: Marriott used universalisation and parochialisation for the two-way flow between the Great and Little traditions.
xa: Marriott studied **Kishan Garhi** (UP) — book **Village India**.
**Primary urbanisation** is **orthogenetic**: folk culture is carried forward into a **Great Tradition** (UPPSC 2013).
**Milton Singer** — When a Great Tradition Modernizes — found continuity between tradition and modernity in **Madras**.

ned5dc7d8ad7.s: According to the folk-urban continuum, settlements:
o: Fall into two separate categories, village and city
Are classified solely by population size
Lie along a gradual scale from folk to urban forms
ned5dc7d8ad7.x: The folk-urban continuum places settlements along a gradual scale from folk to urban forms rather than in two separate categories.
xa: It was based on his studies in **Mexico (Yucatan)** (UPPSC 2013).
**Louis Wirth**: **size, density, heterogeneity** produce urbanism ("Urbanism as a Way of Life", **1938**).
A-R (**UPPSC 2009**): the village-town dividing line begins to be passed with **traders and manufacturers**.

n7826236d1e1.s: The term ‘footloose labour’, as used by Jan Breman, refers to:
o: Circular migrant workers moving among seasonal, casual and informal jobs
Highly skilled workers employed permanently by multinational firms
Permanent agricultural labourers tied to one village
n7826236d1e1.x: Jan Breman’s Footloose Labour (1996) describes circular migrant workers who move between seasonal, casual and informal employment.
n7826236d1e1.tq: Match the author and title with the exact labour-mobility concept.
xs: **Jan Breman**'s "**footloose labour**" means **circular migrants** moving among **seasonal, casual and informal jobs** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is not permanent or skilled employment.
xa: Breman's book **Footloose Labour** appeared in **1996**.
Main migrant **source States: UP and Bihar**.
**Milton Singer** — When a Great Tradition Modernizes (urban **Madras**).

n852d53fbec1.s: Who among the following was also associated with the study of Senapur in Jaunpur district?
n852d53fbec1.x: Senapur in Jaunpur was associated with Morris Opler, R.D. Singh and Bernard Cohn.
n852d53fbec1.tq: Test the additional scholar attached to a familiar village-study location.
xs: **Senapur** (Jaunpur, UP) was studied by **Morris Opler and R.D. Singh**, and also by **Bernard Cohn** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Louis Wirth** wrote on urbanism, **Robert Redfield** on the folk-urban continuum (Mexico) and **Milton Singer** studied urban **Madras** — none studied Senapur.
xa: **Rampura** = **M.N. Srinivas**; **Shamirpet** = **S.C. Dube**.
**Kishan Garhi** = **McKim Marriott** (Village India); **Sripuram** = **Andre Beteille**.
⚠ Shamirpet (near Hyderabad) is the Telugu-region village study — by **Dube**.

n02f873fe585.s: The criteria for identifying Census towns have remained unchanged since:
n02f873fe585.x: Census towns are administratively villages meeting population, male non-farm workforce and density tests; the criteria are unchanged since 1981.
xa: Census town tests: population **≥5,000**, **≥75% of male workers** in non-farm work, density **≥400/sq km**.
The **RGI** is keeping the criteria for **Census 2027**.
**MoHUA** told a parliamentary panel (headed by **Magunta Sreenivasulu Reddy**) the definition is outdated.

nd212bd4a090.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the criteria for a census town?
o: At least 75% of male workers engaged in non-agricultural activities
Population density of at least 400 persons per square kilometre
At least 60% of male workers engaged in non-agricultural activities
nd212bd4a090.x: A census town must have at least 75%, not 60%, of its male workers engaged in non-agricultural activities, in addition to the population and density criteria.
nd212bd4a090.tq: Target the close numerical trap in a three-condition definition.
xs: **60% of male workers** is NOT a census-town criterion — the test is **≥75%** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The three tests are population **≥5,000**, **≥75%** male workers in non-farm work and density **≥400/sq km**.
xa: Criteria unchanged since **1981**; retained for **Census 2027**.
**Statutory towns** are notified by States and run by **ULBs**.

n4b844613b41.s: The urban share of India’s population increased in which of the following sequences?
n4b844613b41.x: India’s urban population share rose from 11% in 1901 to 27.81% in 2001 and 31.16% in 2011.
n4b844613b41.tq: Read the figures in chronological order and reject reversed percentage trends.
xs: India's urban share rose **11% in 1901, 27.81% in 2001 and 31.16% in 2011** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Urban centres rose from **1,827 (1901)** to **7,935 (2011)**.
xa: "Hidden urbanisation": satellite data (DEGURBA) put India about **63%** urban in **2015** (EAC-PM).
**16th Finance Commission** projects urbanisation of **41% by 2031**.
**AP** was **29.47%** urban in 2011 — below India's **31.16%**.

nf30a62595b2.s: The concept of ‘hidden urbanisation’ refers to the finding that satellite and built-up data placed India’s urban population at approximately what level in 2015?
nf30a62595b2.x: Satellite and built-up data using DEGURBA placed India’s urbanisation at about 63% in 2015, more than double the Census figure of 31%.
nf30a62595b2.tq: Compare alternative measurement methods rather than confusing the Census and satellite estimates.
xs: Satellite/built-up data (**DEGURBA**) put India at about **63%** urban in **2015** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This is more than double the Census figure of **31%** (**EAC-PM**).
**41%** is the 16th FC's projection for **2031**; **68.8%** is the Census 2011 rural share.
xa: Census 2011 urban share: **31.16%**; urban centres **7,935**.
Criticism: the rural-urban binary leaves fast-urbanising areas under **panchayats** with little fiscal power.
MoHUA called the **Census Town** definition outdated; **RGI** keeps it for **Census 2027**.

n11fe084bf62.s: Which of the following is a problem associated with urbanisation?
o: End of segregation between rich and poor
n11fe084bf62.x: Urban problems include crime with high density, maladjustment, rich-poor segregation and alienation.
xa: Other problems: **lack of social control** and **environmental degradation**.
Caste persists in cities via **slum concentration**, residential segregation and caste job networks.
ES 2025-26: informality is a **structural outcome** of rapid urbanisation.

ne6898884707.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 treats urban informality such as slums and informal labour as:
o: A temporary aberration to be eradicated
A structural outcome of urbanisation to be integrated
A result of excess fiscal autonomy of cities
ne6898884707.x: The Survey sees informality as a structural outcome of rapid urbanisation to be integrated; cities lack fiscal autonomy due to institutional fragmentation.
xa: Informality = **slums, informal labour, unregistered firms**.
**16th FC** raised the ULB share of local-body grants from **36% to 45%**.
ES 2025-26: urban wages **1.7-2 times** rural.

n20ae1b328e5.s: The motto "rural soul, urban amenities", aimed at checking distress migration, is associated with which initiative?
n20ae1b328e5.x: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission (SPMRM, 2016) follows the idea of 'rural soul, urban amenities'. PMEGP is a KVIC-run employment programme. The Smart Cities Mission is an urban scheme. A Census Town is a Census category, not a policy.
xs: "**Rural soul, urban amenities**" is the motto of the **Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission (SPMRM, 2016)** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**PMEGP** is an employment programme run through **KVIC**; a **Census Town** is a Census category, not a policy.
xa: Both SPMRM and PMEGP target **distress migration**.
AP: **359 panchayats** classified under the **Rurban** cluster scheme.
Push factors of migration: **monsoon failure**, **rural unemployment**.

nc27bf23fd2d.s: Which of the following is a noted institutional feature of tribal society?
nc27bf23fd2d.x: Tribal society may have a common name and dialect, animism or totemism, youth dormitories and a simple economy.
xa: Other features: territorial community, **claim of common ancestor**, hereditary chieftainship, **clan system**.
**Imperial Gazetteer**: common name, dialect and territory; originally **endogamous**.
Tribe vs peasant: tribe = **subsistence economy**, common control of land and forest.

nc72e237de79.s: As per 2011 data, Andhra Pradesh's urban population share was:
nc72e237de79.x: Andhra Pradesh's urban share was 29.47% in 2011, up from 24.13% in 2001, leaving about 70.5% rural.
xa: AP urban population: **173.5 lakh**, projected **190.9 lakh by 2029**.
**AP has 123 ULBs**.
Urbanisation concentrated in **Visakhapatnam** and **Krishna**.
⚠ **40.81%** is Krishna district's urban share, not the State's.

nce1cf14bbb7.s: Which district was the most urbanised in Andhra Pradesh as per the 2011 figures?
nce1cf14bbb7.x: Visakhapatnam (47.45%) was the most urbanised district, followed by Krishna (40.81%); Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and West Godavari were below India's 1991 level.
xa: Least urbanised: **Srikakulam 16.16%**, **Prakasam 19.56%** (APSES 2024-25 p.182).
28 districts: highest **Visakhapatnam 89.69%**, lowest **Polavaram 2.84%**.
CDI suggests Tier-2 cities (**Kurnool, Ongole, Rajahmundry**) to absorb migration.

ne5e8ee60c75.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Scheduled Tribes in Andhra Pradesh (2011 data)?
o: They formed 5.53% of the State's population
The entire Scheduled Tribe population lived within Scheduled Areas
ne5e8ee60c75.x: Only about 12.9 lakh of the 27.39 lakh tribals lived in the Scheduled Areas.
xa: Scheduled Areas: **16,267.63 sq km (~10.15%)** with **3,512 villages**.
Districts: **Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Anakapalli, Eluru**.
India's ST sex ratio is **990** against the all-India **940**.

n338f38cedc4.s: Which of the following districts of Andhra Pradesh has Scheduled Areas?
n338f38cedc4.x: Scheduled Areas in Andhra Pradesh lie in Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Anakapalli and Eluru districts.
xa: Scheduled Areas: **16,267.63 sq km (~10.15%)** with **3,512 villages**.
About **12.9 lakh** tribals live in them (APSES 2024-25 p.251).
AP STs: **27.39 lakh = 5.53%**; **34 ST communities**.

n32f1b043864.s:
Which of the following districts were less urbanised in 2011 than India was in 1991?
1. Visakhapatnam
2. Srikakulam
3. West Godavari
Select the correct answer:
n32f1b043864.x: Srikakulam and West Godavari (with Vizianagaram) were below India's 1991 urbanisation level of 22.87%; Visakhapatnam was not.
xa: ⚠ By APSES figures, **Prakasam** (19.56%) was also below it.
Least urbanised: **Srikakulam 16.16%**.
Largest rural population in absolute numbers: **East Godavari** (APPSC-G2 2017).

o: A form of occupational specialisation without social hierarchy
A system of universal brotherhood cutting across caste groups
A hereditary social group with a traditional occupation
Discrimination and prejudice against people because of their caste
n6adcdf40330.x: Casteism is the evil form of the caste system involving discrimination and prejudice based on caste, along with concentration of power, money and prestige in a few castes.
n6adcdf40330.tq: Distinguish the attitude and practice of casteism from the institution of caste.
xs: **Casteism** is **discrimination and prejudice against people because of their caste** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is the **evil form** of the caste system: power, money and prestige **concentrate in a few castes**.
A **hereditary group with a traditional occupation** (option 3) describes **caste** the institution, not casteism.
xa: ⚠ Caste = institution (may exist **without hostility**); casteism = **partisan attitude and practice**.
**Kaka Kalelkar**: casteism = "an overriding, blind and supreme group loyalty".
Casteism produces **discrimination, conflict and vote-bank politics**.

n4983a9dbe13.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes caste from casteism?
o: Caste is a social structure, whereas casteism is partisan loyalty to one's own caste against others
Caste and casteism are identical terms for hereditary endogamy
Caste rests on political mobilisation, whereas casteism rests on hereditary occupation
Casteism is a social structure, whereas caste is partisan loyalty to one's own caste
n4983a9dbe13.x: Caste is a social structure of hereditary, endogamous identity; casteism is the attitude of partisan loyalty and using caste for gain.
xa: **Kaka Kalelkar**: casteism = "blind and supreme group loyalty".
Casteism hinders **national integration** and excludes castes from the economy.
**Rajni Kothari** (Caste in Indian Politics, **1970**): politics **politicises** caste.

nd9d8b0e06e8.s: Which of the following has contributed to the persistence of casteism in electoral politics?
o: Prohibition of caste associations from acting as pressure groups
Complete separation of elections from social identities
Decline of caste-based vote banks and caste associations
Political mobilisation through caste-based vote banks and caste politics
nd9d8b0e06e8.x: Caste-based vote banks and caste politics have increased, and caste associations may act as pressure groups in electoral politics.
nd9d8b0e06e8.tq: Identify the causal factor rather than an absolute reversal of the trend.
xs: **Political mobilisation through caste-based vote banks and caste politics** keeps casteism alive — so option **(4)** is correct.
Caste-based vote banks have **increased**, and caste associations act as **pressure groups**.
xa: Origin of caste in electoral politics: **Minto-Morley Reforms, 1909** (separate electorates).
**Samajwadi Party** and **RJD** grew out of backward-caste mobilisation.
**Rajni Kothari**: politics **politicises** caste.
TN: **Gounders, Mukkulathors and Vanniyars** used caste solidarity to enter the legislature.

n83e842056f3.s: Which one of the following is NOT a manifestation of caste prejudice in urban areas?
o: Caste associations continuing to operate in cities
Complete disappearance of caste identity among migrants
Caste networks deciding access to informal jobs
n83e842056f3.x: Migrants may carry caste prejudice into cities. Caste networks, caste associations and caste stickers on vehicles may persist, so caste identity does not completely disappear.
n83e842056f3.tq: Find the option using an absolute claim that contradicts the limits of urban anonymity.
xs: **Complete disappearance of caste identity among migrants** is NOT a manifestation — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Migrants carry caste prejudice into cities**; caste networks decide **informal jobs**.
Caste associations and **caste stickers on vehicles** persist (UPSC).
xa: Housing: upper-caste **landlords refuse tenants**; workplace discrimination.
**Caste-based matrimonial sites** are another manifestation.
**UP** banned caste rallies and caste signboards after an **Allahabad HC** directive.

o: A division of labour based on hereditary occupation
A system of political representation for disadvantaged groups
A voluntary association based on economic interests
An overriding, blind and supreme group loyalty
na8cf6c42a2b.x: Kaka Kalelkar described casteism as “an overriding, blind and supreme group loyalty” that ignores justice, fair play and universal brotherhood.
na8cf6c42a2b.tq: Use the exact wording of a thinker’s definition to avoid look-alike interpretations.
xs: **Kaka Kalelkar** defined casteism as "**an overriding, blind and supreme group loyalty**" — so option **(4)** is correct.
Such loyalty ignores **justice, fair play and universal brotherhood**.
xa: **Ambedkar**: caste is "not just a division of labour, but also a **division of labourers**".
**Rajni Kothari**: politics does not just use caste, it **politicises** it.
Casteism = **partisan loyalty** to one's own caste against others.

n70a9de063fc.s: According to B.R. Ambedkar, caste is not merely a division of labour but also a:
n70a9de063fc.x: Ambedkar stated that caste is “not just a division of labour, but also a division of labourers.” He argued that it splits the working class and blocks collective bargaining.
n70a9de063fc.tq: Test the precise completion of a well-known quotation.
xs: **Ambedkar**: caste is "not just a division of labour, but also a **division of labourers**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
It **splits the working class** and **blocks collective bargaining**.
xa: Ambedkar wrote **Annihilation of Caste (1936)**, Who Were the Shudras? and **Mooknayak**.
He founded the **Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924)**.
He embraced **Buddhism** on **14 Oct 1956** at **Nagpur**.

n9cdd2793621.s: Rajni Kothari’s central observation in Caste in Indian Politics (1970) was that:
o: Politics does not just use caste; it politicises caste
Politics merely reflects caste without changing it
Caste has no role in electoral mobilisation
n9cdd2793621.x: Rajni Kothari argued that politics does not merely use caste but also politicises it, thereby transforming caste into a political resource.
n9cdd2793621.tq: Test the precise distinction between using a social identity and politicising it.
xs: **Rajni Kothari** held that politics **does not just use caste; it politicises caste** — so option **(1)** is correct.
His book **Caste in Indian Politics** appeared in **1970**.
xa: **Kaka Kalelkar**: casteism = "blind and supreme group loyalty".
Political manifestation: **caste-based voting** + caste associations as **pressure groups**.
Parties court caste leaders at every level (**caste arithmetic**).

nb8c0af1e5ba.s: Periyar E.V. Ramasamy was jailed in 1924 in connection with the:
nb8c0af1e5ba.x: Periyar was jailed during the Vaikom Satyagraha (1924) and led the Self-Respect Movement from 1925.
xa: ⚠ **Vaikom (1924)** = Periyar jailed; **Self-Respect Movement** = **1925**.
**Jyotiba Phule**'s **Satyashodhak Samaj** dates to **1873**.
**Sree Narayana Guru**: "**One Caste, One Religion, One God for Man**".

ne8e417478b0.s: The casteist element in electoral politics in India is traced back to the:
ne8e417478b0.x: The casteist element in electoral politics is traced to the Minto-Morley Reforms of 1909, particularly their provision for separate electorates.
ne8e417478b0.tq: Distinguish between closely associated constitutional and electoral milestones by year.
xs: The casteist element in electoral politics goes back to the **Minto-Morley Reforms, 1909** — so option **(1)** is correct.
They introduced **separate electorates**.
xa: ⚠ **Communal G.O.** = **1921** (Justice Party), not 1909.
Caste enumeration returns in **Census 2027**; **Bihar caste survey** (2022-23) cited as model.
**Samajwadi Party** and **RJD** grew out of backward-caste mobilisation.

n302c5264152.s: Which pair of political parties grew out of backward-caste mobilisation?
o: Samajwadi Party and Rashtriya Janata Dal
Bahujan Samaj Party and Telugu Desam Party
Justice Party and Communist Party of India
Indian National Congress and Bharatiya Janata Party
n302c5264152.x: The Samajwadi Party and the Rashtriya Janata Dal grew out of backward-caste mobilisation.
n302c5264152.tq: Match the political parties with the social mobilisation from which they emerged.
xs: The **Samajwadi Party** and **RJD (Rashtriya Janata Dal)** grew out of backward-caste mobilisation — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Justice Party** mobilised Reddys, Kammas, Kapus and Velamas against Brahmin dominance in Andhra.
xa: TN: **Gounders, Mukkulathors and Vanniyars** used caste solidarity to enter the legislature.
Origin of caste in elections: **Minto-Morley, 1909**.
Post-**Karamchedu**, Dalits formed independent **Dalit Mahasabhas**.

n3b224c1b5f8.s: The debate over counting caste in the Census centres on whether it would:
o: Ossify caste identities or expose existing inequity
End reservations or extend them to all castes
Weaken caste associations or ban them
Replace the Census or merge it with the SECC
n3b224c1b5f8.x: The debate is whether caste enumeration would ossify caste identities or instead expose existing inequities for corrective policy.
xa: The **2022-23 Bihar caste survey** is cited as a model.
**Rajni Kothari**: politics **politicises** caste.
Article **17** abolished untouchability.

n23a950cb571.s: In Ghurye's features of caste, the exception to endogamy is:
n23a950cb571.x: Caste involves restricted occupational choice and endogamy, with hypergamy (anuloma) as the exception.
xa: The exception to endogamy is **hypergamy (anuloma)**.
Only about **5%** of Indian marriages are inter-caste (Aug 2025).
⚠ Caste may exist without hostility; **casteism** is the partisan practice.

n1b07b7ec408.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the UGC Promotion of Equity in Higher Educational Institutions Regulations, 2026?
o: The Supreme Court upheld the Regulations without any stay
They defined caste-based discrimination as discrimination against SC, ST and OBC members
The case arose in the context of student suicides
The case is titled Abeda Salim Tadvi v. Union of India
n1b07b7ec408.x: The Supreme Court stayed the Regulations in the interim.
xa: Criticism: the SC/ST/OBC-only definition **excluded general-category students**.
National Helpline **14566** for FIRs under the Atrocities Act.

n54551a76516.s: In Shakti Vahini v. Union of India (2018), the Supreme Court directed safe houses for couples to be set up in:
n54551a76516.x: The Court held khap interference illegal, laid down preventive, remedial and punitive measures, and directed safe houses in every district.
xa: **Tamil Nadu** announced a safe house in each district "in line with" Shakti Vahini.
⚠ **Lata Singh** = **2006**; **Shakti Vahini** = **2018**.
Spouse choice is protected by **Art. 21**.

neefda889e01.s: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability?
neefda889e01.x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability; Article 14 gives equality before law and Article 15 bars caste discrimination.
xa: **PCR Act 1955** and **SC/ST (PoA) Act 1989** penalise untouchability and atrocities.
Spouse choice across caste is protected by **Art. 21**.
Haldwani "**purification**" ritual after Kharge's rally was attacked as **untouchability**.

n65adf4d5c46.s: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 primarily provide for:
o: Promotion of inter-caste marriages through financial incentives
n65adf4d5c46.x: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 provide penal safeguards against untouchability and atrocities.
n65adf4d5c46.tq: Link each statute to its central legal purpose rather than its year alone.
xs: The **PCR Act 1955** and **SC/ST (PoA) Act 1989** **penalise untouchability and atrocities** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Inter-caste marriage incentives come from the **Dr. Ambedkar Scheme** (**₹2.5 lakh**), not these Acts.
xa: National Helpline **14566** handles FIRs under the **Atrocities Act**.
**Art. 17** abolished untouchability.
UP's caste-rally ban **exempted PoA cases**.

n2c99e0fa7a5.s: Under the Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages, the incentive provided per couple is:
n2c99e0fa7a5.x: The scheme provides an incentive of ₹2.5 lakh per couple. It seeks to weaken the practice of endogamy through inter-caste marriages.
n2c99e0fa7a5.tq: Use direct numerical recall and distinguish closely spaced monetary figures.
xs: The **Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages** gives **₹2.5 lakh** per couple — so option **(3)** is correct.
Its aim is to **weaken endogamy**.
xa: Only about **5%** of Indian marriages are inter-caste.
**PM-DAKSH** = skilling; **Venture Capital Fund for SCs** (2 Sep 2026).
National Helpline **14566** — FIRs under the Atrocities Act.

n555156fe327.s: The Supreme Court has held that choosing a spouse, including across caste lines, is protected under:
n555156fe327.x: The choice of a spouse, including the choice to marry across caste, is protected as part of personal liberty under Article 21.
n555156fe327.tq: Match the constitutional protection with the precise Article rather than a neighbouring fundamental right.
xs: The Supreme Court held that **choosing a spouse**, including across caste, is protected by **Article 21** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Lata Singh v. State of UP (2006)**: no bar on inter-caste marriage; police must protect such couples.
xa: **Shakti Vahini (2018)**: khap interference in marriage of consenting adults is **illegal**.
**Art. 17** abolishes untouchability; **Art. 15(2)** bars denial of access to shops and public places.
⚠ **Lata Singh** = **2006**; **Shakti Vahini** = **2018**.

n3f4875b2726.s: Which one of the following best distinguishes religious fundamentalism from communalism?
o: Fundamentalism is mainly doctrinal and seeks a return to literal scripture, whereas communalism politically mobilises religious identity against other communities.
Fundamentalism is always directed against another community, whereas communalism reforms one's own community.
Communalism is concerned only with religious doctrine and is unrelated to power or resources.
Fundamentalism and communalism both necessarily involve inter-group conflict.
n3f4875b2726.x: Religious fundamentalism is mainly doctrinal, emphasising a return to fundamentals and literal scripture. Communalism is political mobilisation of religious identity against other communities to seek power and resources.
n3f4875b2726.tq: Discriminate between look-alike concepts by comparing their direction, objective and method.
xs: **Fundamentalism** is mainly **doctrinal** (return to literal scripture); **communalism** is **political mobilisation of religious identity against other communities** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Fundamentalism is aimed at **reforming one's own community**; communalism at **other communities**, seeking power and resources.
Fundamentalism **can exist without inter-group conflict**, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: Communalism is **always relational** — "us vs them".
Fundamentalism is often **anti-modern**.
**Political** communalism uses religion for **votes**.

nf95a4393942.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about religious fundamentalism and communalism?
o: Religious fundamentalism is often directed at reforming one's own community.
Communalism constructs an 'us versus them' relationship.
Religious fundamentalism cannot exist without inter-group conflict.
nf95a4393942.x: Fundamentalism can exist without inter-group conflict, so this statement is false; the others are correct.
xa: Fundamentalism = return to "**fundamentals**" and literal scripture.
Communalism seeks **power and resources**.
**Ram Ahuja**: "communal persons" practise politics through religion.

nindian-society-30-5.s:
Which of the following are causes of religious fundamentalism?
1. Identity crisis
2. Group exclusiveness
3. Social insecurity
Select the correct answer:
nindian-society-30-5.x: Identity crisis and social insecurity (with globalisation) are causes; group exclusiveness is a feature of fundamentalism, not a cause.
n: Identity crisis is a cause of religious fundamentalism. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 64-65]
Religious fundamentalism involves group exclusiveness. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 64-65]
Globalization is a cause of religious fundamentalism. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 64-65]
Social insecurity is a cause of religious fundamentalism. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 64-65]
xa: Other causes: **political mobilization** and **economic inequalities**.
Other features: **literal interpretation** of scriptures, **religious conservatism**, **resistance to change**.
**Communalism** = political mobilisation of religious identity **against other communities**.

needf02d7c5d.s: Ram Ahuja described communalism as which of the following?
o: An ideology that society is divided into religious communities whose interests differ and often oppose each other
A movement for the complete separation of religion from politics
A constitutional arrangement providing separate electorates to minorities
A process through which all religious communities assimilate into one nation
needf02d7c5d.x: Ram Ahuja viewed communalism as an ideology in which religious communities are considered to have differing and often opposing interests. He also associated communal persons with practising politics through religion.
needf02d7c5d.tq: Match the precise definition with its scholar rather than selecting a related institutional concept.
xs: **Ram Ahuja**: communalism is an **ideology that society is divided into religious communities whose interests differ and often oppose** each other — so option **(1)** is correct.
"**Communal persons**" practise **politics through religion**.
Separate electorates are a colonial device (**1909** Act), not Ahuja's definition.
xa: **Bipan Chandra**: a religious group has **common social, political and economic interests**.
**Melson and Wolpe**: political assertiveness of a community in a **plural society undergoing modernisation**.
**Asghar Ali Engineer** wrote **Communalism in India**.

n0cb8fe0d773.s: Communalism has been defined as "the political assertiveness of a community to maintain its identity in a plural society undergoing modernisation". This definition is given by:
n0cb8fe0d773.x: The definition is by Robert Melson and Howard Wolpe (asked in APPSC-G2 2025). Bipan Chandra defined communalism as the belief that followers of one religion share common social, political and economic interests. Ram Ahuja saw it as an ideology of religious communities with differing, often opposing, interests. T.K. Oommen gave its six dimensions.
xs: "**Political assertiveness of a community** to maintain its identity in a plural society undergoing modernisation" is by **Robert Melson and Howard Wolpe** — so option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC-G2 2025**).
**Bipan Chandra**: a religious group has **common social, political and economic interests**.
**Ram Ahuja**: communities with interests that **differ and often oppose**; **T.K. Oommen**: **six dimensions**.
xa: Bipan Chandra also gave **three stages** of communalism.
**Asghar Ali Engineer**: leading scholar of communal harmony.
Exam angle: **definition → scholar** matching.

nd75081d041f.s: Who is known as the “Father of the Communal Electorate” in British India?
nd75081d041f.x: Lord Minto is known as the Father of the Communal Electorate because the reforms associated with him introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
nd75081d041f.tq: Use the person–policy association and distinguish Minto from other Viceroys.
xs: **Lord Minto** is the "**Father of the Communal Electorate**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
He received the **Simla Deputation (1906)** demanding separate electorates; the **1909** Act gave the first legal separate electorate.
xa: ⚠ Ideological father of the two-nation theory = **Syed Ahmad Khan**.
**Ramsay MacDonald** gave the **Communal Award (1932)**.
**Lord Dufferin** used Syed Ahmad Khan in **1887** to keep Muslims from Congress.

n08c1c17a079.s: Which scholar defined communalism as the belief that a group following a particular religion also has common social, political and economic interests?
n08c1c17a079.x: Bipan Chandra defined communalism as the belief that followers of a particular religion have common social, political and economic interests.
n08c1c17a079.tq: Use scholar-definition matching and distinguish closely related formulations.
xs: **Bipan Chandra** defined communalism as the belief that a religious group also has **common social, political and economic interests** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ram Ahuja** saw interests that **differ and often oppose**; **T.K. Oommen** gave **six dimensions**; **Asghar Ali Engineer** is a scholar of communal harmony.
xa: Bipan Chandra also gave the **three stages**: communal nationalism → liberal → extreme communalism.
⚠ **T.K. Oommen** = six dimensions; **Bipan Chandra** = three stages.
**Melson and Wolpe**: "political assertiveness of a community" (APPSC-G2 2025).

nde23ce25f52.s: According to Bipan Chandra, the final stage of communalism is:
nde23ce25f52.x: Bipan Chandra's sequence is communal nationalism, liberal communalism and then extreme communalism.
xa: Stage 1: common **secular** interests, still nationalist.
Stage 2: interests **different** but reconcilable within one nation.
Stage 3: **mutually antagonistic** — politics of **fear, hatred and violence**.
After the **1937** elections the Muslim League turned to extreme communalism.

n7ce2714b55d.s: In Bipan Chandra's scheme, the stage in which community interests are seen as different but reconcilable within one nation is:
n7ce2714b55d.x: In liberal communalism, interests are different but reconcilable within one nation; 'mutually antagonistic' interests mark extreme communalism.
xa: Extreme communalism = politics of **fear, hatred and violence**.
Muslim League turned extreme after the **1937** elections; echoed by **Hindu Mahasabha** and **RSS**.
⚠ **Bipan Chandra** = three stages; **Oommen** = six dimensions.

n1761f43b8f3.s: After the elections of 1937, the Muslim League turned towards extreme communalism based mainly on
o: cooperation with the Congress on joint electorates
n1761f43b8f3.x: After the 1937 elections, the Muslim League adopted extreme communalism based on fear, hatred and violence. This approach was echoed by the Hindu Mahasabha and the RSS.
n1761f43b8f3.tq: Link the political turning point with its stated ideological characteristics.
xs: After the **1937** elections the Muslim League turned to extreme communalism "based on **fear, hatred and violence**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was echoed by the **Hindu Mahasabha and RSS**.
xa: Extreme communalism sees interests as **mutually antagonistic** (Bipan Chandra's stage 3).
**Lahore ("Pakistan") Resolution** followed on **24 Mar 1940**.
**Allama Iqbal** proposed a consolidated Muslim state in **1930**.

nb06f7a1cb7b.s: Who among the following were associated with the founding of the All-India Muslim League at Dacca in 1906?
o: Aga Khan and Nawab Salimullah of Dacca
nb06f7a1cb7b.x: The Muslim League was founded at Dacca under the leadership of Aga Khan and Nawab Salimullah of Dacca.
nb06f7a1cb7b.tq: Use the founder–organisation association rather than the later reform association.
xs: The Muslim League was founded under the **Aga Khan and Nawab Salimullah of Dacca** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Minto** received the Simla Deputation; he did not found the League.
xa: The **Aga Khan** led the **Simla Deputation** (Oct 1906).
Lord **Minto** = "**Father of the Communal Electorate**".
⚠ **1906** = Muslim League; **1909** = first legal separate electorate.

n0ed7c3bf625.s: The Simla Deputation to Lord Minto, which preceded the formation of the Muslim League, took place in:
n0ed7c3bf625.x: The Simla Deputation to Minto took place in October 1906, before the Muslim League was founded later in 1906.
n0ed7c3bf625.tq: Separate closely related events by their month and year.
xs: The **Simla Deputation** to **Lord Minto** was in **October 1906** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Led by the **Aga Khan**, it demanded **separate electorates**.
xa: The **Muslim League** was founded later in **1906** at **Dacca**.
**1905**: Partition of Bengal; **1909** Act: first legal separate electorate.
Minto = "**Father of the Communal Electorate**".

n5244fc96bf5.s: The Poona Pact of 1932 was concluded between Mahatma Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar at
n5244fc96bf5.x: The Poona Pact was concluded in 1932 between Gandhi and Ambedkar at Yerwada Jail.
n5244fc96bf5.tq: Distinguish the exact venue from other locations associated with the freedom movement.
xs: The **Poona Pact (1932)** between **Gandhi and Ambedkar** was concluded at **Yerwada Jail** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It replaced Dalit separate electorates with **reserved seats in joint electorates** (**71 → 148**).
xa: It followed the **Communal Award** (**16 Aug 1932**) of **Ramsay MacDonald**.
The Award was based on the **Lothian Committee**.
⚠ Communal Award separate electorates were for **20 years**.

nc0c9f4df2b2.s: The Lahore or Pakistan Resolution of the Muslim League was adopted on
nc0c9f4df2b2.x: The Lahore, also called Pakistan, Resolution of the Muslim League was moved on 23 March and adopted on 24 March 1940; 23 March 1956 is when Pakistan became a republic.
nc0c9f4df2b2.tq: Distinguish the exact date of the resolution from nearby dates associated with other events.
xs: The **Lahore ("Pakistan") Resolution** was adopted on **24 March 1940** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**16 August 1932** is the date of the **Communal Award**.
xa: After the **1937** elections the League turned to **extreme communalism**.
**Allama Iqbal** proposed a consolidated Muslim state in **1930**.
Syed Ahmad Khan = **ideological father** of the two-nation theory.

n267bf098b26.s: Which one of the following correctly states the difference between the Communal Award and the Poona Pact regarding representation of the depressed classes?
o: The Award provided separate electorates with 71 seats, while the Pact retained joint electorates and reserved 148 seats.
The Award provided joint electorates with 148 seats, while the Pact introduced separate electorates with 71 seats.
Both provided separate electorates with 148 seats in the provincial legislatures.
Both provided joint electorates with 71 seats in the provincial legislatures.
n267bf098b26.x: The Communal Award provided separate electorates and 71 seats for the depressed classes. The Poona Pact retained joint electorates and provided 148 reserved seats in provincial legislatures.
n267bf098b26.tq: Compare the paired figures and the reversed electoral arrangements.
xs: The **Award** gave **separate electorates with 71 seats**; the **Pact** kept **joint electorates with 148 reserved seats** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Poona Pact** replaced Dalit separate electorates with reserved seats in joint electorates (**71 → 148**).
xa: ⚠ Poona Pact: **71 → 148**; Communal Award separate electorates were for **20 years**.
Award by **Ramsay MacDonald** (**16 Aug 1932**), based on the **Lothian Committee**.
Pact between **Gandhi and Ambedkar** at **Yerwada Jail**.

nc5bd3297e24.s: Which one of the following correctly states the firsts associated with communal politics in India?
o: 1976 saw the first legal separate electorate, while 1994 saw the first communal political party.
1906 saw the first legal separate electorate, while 1976 saw the first communal political party.
1906 saw the first communal political party, while 1909 saw the first legal separate electorate.
1909 saw the first communal political party, while 1906 saw the first legal separate electorate.
nc5bd3297e24.x: The Muslim League, identified as the first communal political party, was formed in 1906. The 1909 Act introduced the first legal separate electorate.
nc5bd3297e24.tq: Use the first/last-style date contrast and avoid reversing the two closely placed milestones.
xs: **1906** saw the **first communal political party**, and **1909** the **first legal separate electorate** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The 1906 party was the **Muslim League**; option (4) reverses the years.
xa: **1976** is the **42nd Amendment** adding "Secular" — not a first of communal politics.
**Simla Deputation** (Oct **1906**) to **Lord Minto** demanded separate electorates.
Lord Minto = "**Father of the Communal Electorate**".

n4390dd087f6.s: The first census in which caste and religion were recorded, contributing to communal consciousness, was conducted in
n4390dd087f6.x: The recording of caste and religion in the first census of 1871-72 is identified as a historical or colonial factor contributing to communalism.
n4390dd087f6.tq: Retain the exact census range and reject nearby-looking dates.
xs: Caste and religion were recorded in the **first census (1871-72)** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is listed among the **historical/colonial** causes of communalism.
xa: Other colonial causes: British **divide and rule**, **separate electorates**, **revivalist movements**.
**1909** Act = first legal separate electorate.
**1905 Partition of Bengal**: Muslim-majority East, Hindu-majority West.

n35042c9b836.s: In the 1920s, which pair of movements represented contrasting mobilisation efforts among Hindus and Muslims respectively?
o: Swadeshi and Home Rule; Khilafat and Non-Cooperation
Shuddhi and Sangathan; Tabligh and Tanzim
Tabligh and Tanzim; Shuddhi and Sangathan
Brahmo and Arya Samaj; Aligarh and Deoband
n35042c9b836.x: The Arya Samaj promoted Shuddhi and Sangathan, while Muslim organisations promoted Tabligh and Tanzim in the 1920s.
n35042c9b836.tq: Discriminate between similarly placed religious mobilisation movements by community association.
xs: **Shuddhi and Sangathan** (Arya Samaj, Hindu) vs **Tabligh and Tanzim** (Muslim) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option (3) reverses the two.
xa: ⚠ **Shuddhi and Sangathan** = Arya Samaj; **Tabligh and Tanzim** = Muslim.
**Hindu Mahasabha** founded **1915** (Maharaja of **Kasim Bazar**).
Revivalist movements are a **historical/colonial** cause.

ne50ce610fe0.s: T.K. Oommen identified how many dimensions of communalism?
ne50ce610fe0.x: T.K. Oommen identified six dimensions of communalism, ranging from assimilationist to secessionist.
xa: Six dimensions: assimilationist, welfarist, retreatist, **retaliatory**, **separatist**, **secessionist**.
⚠ **Separatist** = state **within** India (Gorkhaland, Bodoland); **secessionist** = state **outside** India (Khalistan).
⚠ **Bipan Chandra** = three stages, not six dimensions.

nc5f98b39195.s: Which law bars the use of religious places for political or communal ends?
nc5f98b39195.x: The Religious Institutions (Prevention of Misuse) Act, 1988 bars such use; the 1991 Places of Worship Act is a separate law.
xa: The **Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act, 1991** is a separate statutory safeguard.
Bodies: **National Integration Council**, **National Foundation for Communal Harmony**.
**Art. 51A(e)**: promote harmony.

ncf742fde0c9.s: The word 'Secular' was added to the Preamble of the Constitution of India by which Amendment?
ncf742fde0c9.x: 'Secular' was inserted in the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment, 1976. The 24th Amendment concerned Parliament's power to amend the Constitution, the 44th Amendment (1978) undid parts of the 42nd, and the 52nd Amendment (1985) is the anti-defection law.
xs: "**Secular**" was added to the Preamble by the **42nd Amendment, 1976** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is part of the constitutional safeguards against communalism.
xa: **Art. 25-28**: freedom of religion; **Art. 29-30**: minority rights.
**Art. 51A(e)**: promote harmony.
**Sec. 123(3)**, RP Act 1951: religious appeal = **corrupt practice**.

nd73dbfe42a6.s: The Direct Action Day and Noakhali violence of 1946 took place in:
nd73dbfe42a6.x: Direct Action Day and the Noakhali violence (1946) occurred in Bengal.
xa: Partition: **14-18 million** crossed the borders; deaths estimated **2 lakh to 20 lakh** (most historians near **10 lakh**).
The **Srikrishna Commission** probed the **Bombay riots, 1992-93**.
The **Liberhan Commission** probed the demolition on **6 Dec 1992**.

n1880ec3b322.s: The Ahmedabad communal riots took place in:
n1880ec3b322.x: The Ahmedabad riots were in 1969; Jabalpur was 1961, Moradabad 1980 and Bhagalpur 1989.
xa: Jabalpur = **MP**; Ahmedabad = **Gujarat**; Moradabad = **UP**; Bhagalpur = **Bihar**.
Between them: **anti-Sikh riots 1984** (Delhi) and **Meerut 1987** (UP).
⚠ CDX prints Ahmedabad as **1967**.

n5a8a5b9b6a9.s: Which commission was appointed to inquire into the demolition of the disputed structure at Ayodhya on 6 December 1992?
n5a8a5b9b6a9.x: The Liberhan Commission investigated the demolition of the disputed structure at Ayodhya on 6 December 1992.
n5a8a5b9b6a9.tq: Directly identify the commission from the matter it was constituted to probe.
xs: The **Liberhan Commission** probed the **demolition of the disputed structure** at Ayodhya on **6 Dec 1992** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Jain** = Rajiv Gandhi assassination conspiracy; **Nanavati** = **1984 anti-Sikh riots**; **Srikrishna** = **Bombay riots 1992-93**.
xa: Liberhan was a **one-man commission** set up on **16 Dec 1992**.
Justice **M.S. Liberhan** died at **87** in **Aug 2026**.
Exam angle: **commission → matter** matching (UPSC 2002, 2005).

n62cd6f1198b.s: The Srikrishna Commission primarily investigated which of the following?
n62cd6f1198b.x: The Srikrishna Commission investigated the Bombay, now Mumbai, riots of 1992–93 and found failure of state administration.
n62cd6f1198b.tq: Use the commission–riot pair rather than confusing it with other inquiry commissions.
xs: The **Srikrishna Commission** probed the **Bombay riots of 1992-93** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It found **failure of state administration**.
**1984 riots** = **Nanavati**; **Gujarat 2002** = **Nanavati-Mehta**; **Ayodhya demolition** = **Liberhan**.
xa: Liberhan: **one-man** commission, set up **16 Dec 1992**.
Administrative failure is itself a cause: police **inaction and biased intelligence**.
**Home Guards** were first raised in **Dec 1946** to help control communal riots.

n20b3532cfa1.s: The murder of missionary Graham Staines in Odisha (1999) was inquired into by which commission?
n20b3532cfa1.x: The Wadhwa Commission probed the murder of Graham Staines (UPSC 2002 PYQ). The Jain Commission probed the conspiracy behind Rajiv Gandhi's assassination. The Srikrishna Commission probed the Bombay riots of 1992-93, and the Liberhan Commission probed the Babri Masjid demolition.
xs: The **Wadhwa Commission** probed the murder of missionary **Graham Staines** (Odisha, **1999**) — so option **(2)** is correct (UPSC **2002** PYQ).
**Jain** = **Rajiv Gandhi** assassination conspiracy; **Srikrishna** = **Bombay riots 1992-93**; **Liberhan** = **Babri demolition**.
xa: **Nanavati** = **1984** anti-Sikh riots; **Nanavati-Mehta** = Gujarat **2002**.
**Ranganath Misra** (NCRLM): religious and linguistic minorities, report **2007**.
Exam angle: **commission → matter** matching.

n66d170fc468.s: The Sachar Committee (2005) found that Muslims in India were:
o: Ahead of other communities in education
Under-represented in public employment, including the police
n66d170fc468.x: The Sachar Committee found Muslims lagging in education and employment and under-represented in public employment, including the police.
xa: **Ranganath Misra** (NCRLM) studied backward sections among **religious and linguistic minorities** (report **2007**).
⚠ **Ranganath Misra (1985)** is a different commission — on the **1984** riots.
Exam angle: commission → matter (UPSC **2002, 2005**).

n7dcb4ae6c77.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Prakash Singh v. Union of India (2006)?
o: It mandated a State Security Commission.
It directed district nodal officers to prevent mob violence.
It mandated a Police Complaints Authority.
It directed separation of investigation from law-and-order duties.
n7dcb4ae6c77.x: District nodal officers against mob violence came from Tehseen Poonawalla (2018), not Prakash Singh.
xa: **Ramji Lal Modi** upheld **Sec. 295A**.
**Pravasi Bhalai Sangathan (2014)**: SC asked the **Law Commission** to define hate speech.
Police inaction and **biased intelligence** are causes of riots.

nb8943934347.s: The Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025 provides for imprisonment ranging from:
nb8943934347.x: The Bill, described as the first State-level law to define hate speech, provides for two to ten years' imprisonment and covers organisational liability.
xa: Hate speech is **not specifically defined** in central law.
**Law Commission 267th Report** (**2017**) on hate speech.
The **2011** Communal Violence Bill was **never passed**.

n7db8289f12b.s: How many people, mostly kar sevaks, were burnt on the Sabarmati Express near Godhra on 27 February 2002?
n7db8289f12b.x: The Godhra train burning killed 59 people, mostly kar sevaks; it was investigated by a Supreme Court-appointed SIT.
xa: **1,169** were killed in the riots that followed.
The **Nanavati-Mehta Commission** (2002) was set up by the **Gujarat govt**.
⚠ **Nanavati** = 1984 anti-Sikh riots; **Nanavati-Mehta** = Gujarat 2002.

n7c3892bd532.s: Ghettoisation following communal riots refers to the
o: temporary migration of workers to industrial areas
legal segregation of citizens by the State
movement of communities into religiously segregated neighbourhoods
division of a district into administrative wards
n7c3892bd532.x: Ghettoisation is the movement of communities into religiously segregated neighbourhoods after communal violence.
n7c3892bd532.tq: Distinguish a social consequence from formal legal or administrative segregation.
xs: **Ghettoisation** = **communities move into religiously segregated neighbourhoods** after riots — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is a social consequence of riots, not legal or administrative division.
xa: **Displacement**: Partition = **largest forced migration in history**.
**Polarisation**: weaker **social capital**, threat to unity in diversity.
**Loss of trust**: guilty of **1984** and **2002** not brought to book.

nb5555c410f9.s: Which one of the following is NOT a consequence of communal violence?
o: Loss of faith in the police and courts
Harm to India's global image and diaspora
nb5555c410f9.x: Communal violence causes polarisation and weakens social capital; it does not strengthen it.
xa: **Ghettoisation** follows riots.
**Veena Das** analysed gendered violence in **Critical Events**.
Low conviction and case withdrawals **weaken deterrence**.

nc1dccf61d55.s: Who analysed the impact of Partition and communal riots on women in Critical Events?
nc1dccf61d55.x: Veena Das analysed the impact of Partition and communal riots on women in her work Critical Events.
xa: Partition = **largest forced migration in history**.
Consequences include **ghettoisation**, **displacement**, **polarisation**.
**National Foundation for Communal Harmony** supports **child victims** of violence.

nb1546afd152.s: The Prevention of Communal and Targeted Violence Bill, 2011 was drafted by the:
nb1546afd152.x: The National Advisory Council drafted the Bill, which was never passed.
xa: **Congress** promised a similar law in **Assam** (2 Apr 2026).
The draft was attacked as **one-sided**.
**Karnataka's 2025 Bill** is the first State-level law to **define** hate speech.

n0d0e6f1b6f6.s: Home Guards were first raised in December 1946 primarily to
o: help the police control civil disturbance and communal riots
replace the regular police in all districts
n0d0e6f1b6f6.x: Home Guards were first raised in December 1946 to assist the police in controlling civil disturbance and communal riots.
n0d0e6f1b6f6.tq: Match the organisation’s origin date with its original operational purpose.
xs: **Home Guards** were first raised in **Dec 1946** to **help the police control civil disturbance and communal riots** — so option **(3)** is correct.
They assist, not replace, the regular police.
xa: **1946** was also the year of **Direct Action Day** and **Noakhali** (Bengal).
**National Integration Council**: chaired by the **PM**.
**NFCH** supports **child victims** and **inter-faith dialogue**.

nb644d4f0efb.s: Who began the construction of Mecca Masjid in Hyderabad in 1614?
nb644d4f0efb.x: Construction of Mecca Masjid was begun by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah in 1614; it was completed in 1693.
xa: **Mecca Masjid blast**: **18 May 2007** — tension and police firing.
Hyderabad old city riots: **1978** (Rameeza Bee case) and **1990**.
**Sanjeev Balyan** figures in the **Muzaffarnagar** riot case, not Hyderabad.

n336ba1f37a7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the consequences of regionalism?
o: Balanced development is a negative consequence.
Giving backward regions a voice through regional parties is a positive consequence.
The Tripura TTAADC is cited as an example of intergroup solidarity.
Openings for extremists is a negative consequence.
n336ba1f37a7.x: Balanced development is listed as a positive consequence of regionalism, not a negative one.
xa: Other positives: cultural pride, **local innovation, accountability**.
Other negatives: **law-and-order breakdowns**, political exploitation, **inter-state disputes**, new linguistic minorities.
Hostility to migrants: **Shiv Sena, MNS**.

n49e417bd21e.s: Which one of the following correctly states the linguistic diversity figures associated with demands for linguistic States?
o: 14 official languages and about 1,635 mother tongues
28 official languages and about 2,635 mother tongues
22 official languages and about 1,635 mother tongues
22 official languages and about 635 mother tongues
n49e417bd21e.x: The linguistic diversity figures cited are 22 official languages and approximately 1,635 mother tongues. Emotional attachment to language contributed to demands for linguistic States.
n49e417bd21e.tq: Check both figures together; changing either the language count or the mother-tongue count makes the option incorrect.
xs: India has **22 official languages and about 1,635 mother tongues** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This **linguistic identity** fed demands for linguistic states.
xa: First linguistic state: **Andhra State**, **1 October 1953**, capital **Kurnool**.
**SR Act 1956**: **14 states + 6 UTs**.
⚠ **14** is the number of states under the 1956 Act, not of official languages.

n6d029e0f2f3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the causes of regionalism?
o: The sons-of-the-soil feeling is strongest where migrants compete with local agricultural labourers for farm work.
Neglect of sub-regions led to demands for Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Telangana.
Regional kingdoms and British divide-and-rule fed historical memory.
The sons-of-the-soil feeling is strongest where migrants and local educated youth compete for middle-class jobs.
n6d029e0f2f3.x: The sons-of-the-soil feeling is strongest where migrants and local educated youth compete for middle-class jobs, not farm work.
xa: The sons-of-the-soil doctrine grew out of the **job shortage of the 1960s-70s**.
Uneven industrialisation: **Bombay and West Bengal** held **59%** of capital (1948).
UPPSC 2008: all such causes — "**all the above**".

n602f6363836.s: The Dravida Nadu demand is an example of which form of regionalism?
n602f6363836.x: Dravida Nadu represents secessionism; Telangana represents a demand for a separate State within the Union.
xa: River disputes: **Cauvery** (TN, KA, KL), **Krishna, Narmada, Ravi**.
⚠ **Secessionism** = out of India; **separatism** = new state inside the Union.
Earlier full-statehood cases: **Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim**.

n72831e12281.s: Which of the following represents a demand for a new State within the Indian Union rather than secession?
n72831e12281.x: Uttarakhand sought a new State within the Union; Dravida Nadu, Khalistan and Greater Nagaland were secessionist demands.
xa: Dates: **Dravida Nadu (1960s)**, **Khalistan (1980s)**, **Greater Nagaland (NSCN, 1980)**.
Other separatist cases: **Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Telangana**.
**Autonomy** demands: Tamil Nadu, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal (since the **1960s**).

n9d3f7fdd58c.s: In 1948, Bombay and West Bengal together held about what share of India's industrial capital?
n9d3f7fdd58c.x: Bombay and West Bengal held 59% of capital in 1948, an example of the uneven industrialisation that feeds regionalism.
xa: Exam angle (**UPPSC 2008**): uneven development, fear of losing cultural identity and political prominence are **all** causes.
Neglected sub-regions demanded new states: **Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Telangana**.
Industrialised states now resent acting as **net fiscal donors**.

n3877ae00559.s: The Dar Commission was appointed in:
n3877ae00559.x: The Dar Commission came in 1948, followed by the Visalandhra Mahasabha (1949), Swami Sitaram's fast (1951) and the SRC (1953).
xa: The Dhar Commission (**S.K. Dhar**) **rejected language** as the basis.
**Andhra State** formed **1 October 1953**; this "**Andhra exception**" forced the SRC.
SRC report **1955**: **16 states + 3 territories**.

n5671b5ef8a4.s: Which one of the following correctly states the recommendation of the Dhar Commission?
o: It rejected language as the basis and preferred administrative convenience.
It recommended the immediate creation of states strictly on a linguistic basis.
It recommended the merger of Andhra State with Telangana.
It recommended the creation of 16 states and 3 territories.
n5671b5ef8a4.x: The Dhar Commission rejected language as the basis for reorganising provinces and preferred administrative convenience.
n5671b5ef8a4.tq: Discriminate between the recommendations of the Dhar Commission, SRC and the States Reorganisation Act.
xs: The **Dhar Commission** **rejected language as the basis** and preferred **administrative convenience** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**16 states + 3 territories** was the **SRC** (1955); the merger of Andhra State with Telangana came from the **SR Act 1956**.
xa: Dhar Commission: **1948**, headed by **S.K. Dhar**.
The SRC also **rejected "one language, one state"**.
⚠ SRC report = **16 + 3**; SR Act 1956 = **14 states + 6 UTs**.

n7dab123aeaa.s: Who was the Chairman of the States Reorganisation Commission appointed in December 1953?
n7dab123aeaa.x: Fazl Ali chaired the SRC; K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru were its members.
xa: SRC report: **16 states + 3 territories**; rejected "one language, one state".
SR Act 1956: **14 states + 6 UTs**.
The **Andhra exception** (Andhra State, 1953) forced the SRC.

nd8db97402d8.x: The 1956 Act created 14 states and 6 UTs; the SRC (1955) had recommended 16 states and 3 territories.
xa: The Act **merged Andhra State with Telangana** → Andhra Pradesh.
SRC: **Fazl Ali**, **K.M. Panikkar**, **H.N. Kunzru**.

n6d3034d7b4a.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the effect of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 on Andhra Pradesh?
o: It created Telangana as a separate state along with Andhra State.
It divided Andhra State into Andhra and Telangana.
It merged Andhra State with Telangana to form Andhra Pradesh.
It merged Andhra State with Tamil Nadu to form Andhra Pradesh.
n6d3034d7b4a.x: The Act merged Andhra State with Telangana to form Andhra Pradesh.
n6d3034d7b4a.tq: Use the merger relationship and reject the split or wrong-state alternatives.
xs: The **SR Act 1956** **merged Andhra State with Telangana to form Andhra Pradesh** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It did not divide the State; Telangana became separate only in **2014**.
xa: SR Act 1956: **14 states + 6 UTs**.
Andhra State (**1953**) had its capital at **Kurnool**.
**Telangana movements**: **1969** agitation and the **2009-14** phase.

ne723370567a.s: Andhra State, formed on 1 October 1953 as India's first linguistic State, had its capital at:
ne723370567a.x: Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953 with Kurnool as its capital. Hyderabad became the capital only after the 1956 merger with Telangana formed Andhra Pradesh; Guntur and Visakhapatnam were never its capital.
xs: **Andhra State** (formed **1 October 1953**) had its capital at **Kurnool** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Hyderabad** became the capital only after the **1956** merger with Telangana.
xa: It was India's **first linguistic state**.
The **SR Act 1956** merged it with Telangana → **Andhra Pradesh**.
**Swami Sitaram's fast** (**1951**) preceded it.

nce031f68884.s: Which of the following is NOT listed among government steps to contain regionalism?
nce031f68884.x: The Eleventh Schedule (panchayats) is not among the listed measures; the NIC, Articles 44 and 51A, and the Fifth, Sixth and Eighth Schedules are.
xa: Regionalism's negatives include **inter-state disputes** and **new linguistic minorities**.
India has **22** official languages.
SR Act 1956: **14 states + 6 UTs**.

n28f6e7ddb5a.s: In the North-South debate after the defeat of the 131st Amendment Bill, 2026, southern states feared lifting the seat freeze based on the Census of:
n28f6e7ddb5a.x: Southern states feared lifting the seat freeze based on the 1971 Census; industrialised states also resented being net fiscal donors.
xa: The debate followed the **131st Amendment Bill, 2026**'s defeat in the **Lok Sabha**.
**Autonomy** demands from TN, Punjab, AP, WB date from the **1960s**.
Regional parties add **political diversity** to federalism.

n02729176c85.s: The sons-of-the-soil doctrine holds that a State belongs to:
o: All its residents, irrespective of language
Only those born in the State before 1950
Its main linguistic group, with others treated as outsiders however long they have lived there
The Union, which alone decides its cultural identity
n02729176c85.x: The doctrine treats the main linguistic group as locals and others as outsiders; it grew with the job shortages of the 1960s and 1970s.
xa: **Shiv Sena** (1960s) targeted **South Indians**; **MNS** targeted **North Indians** (**2008**).
**Assam Movement** (**1979-85**) against **illegal immigrants**.
Feeling is strongest where migrants and **local educated youth** compete for **middle-class jobs**.

n38f916b16dc.s: In the 1960s, the Shiv Sena's sons-of-the-soil campaign in Maharashtra initially targeted:
n38f916b16dc.x: The Shiv Sena of the 1960s targeted South Indians; the MNS targeted North Indians in 2008.
xa: ⚠ **Shiv Sena** = South Indians (1960s); **MNS** = North Indians (2008).
**Mulki rules** — local-residence preference in **Hyderabad/Telangana** jobs.
Anti-Hindi agitations → **two-language formula**.

n861920457a7.s: The Mulki rules were primarily associated with:
o: Reservation of jobs for Scheduled Tribes in Agency areas
Use of Telugu as the official language
Preference for local residents in jobs in Hyderabad/Telangana
Restriction of land transfers in Scheduled Areas
n861920457a7.x: The Mulki rules gave local residents preference in jobs in Hyderabad/Telangana and fed the agitations of 1969 and 1972–73.
xa: **Telangana movements**: **1969** agitation and **2009-14** phase → statehood in **2014**.
Sons-of-the-soil doctrine: state belongs to its **main linguistic group**.

n794e3aeffc1.s: The Anti-Hindi agitations in Tamil Nadu are associated with which outcome?
n794e3aeffc1.x: The Anti-Hindi agitations of 1937, 1965 and 1986 in Tamil Nadu led to the two-language formula.
n794e3aeffc1.tq: Distinguish the policy outcome of the language movement from outcomes of other regional movements.
xs: TN's **anti-Hindi agitations** led to the **two-language formula** — so option **(2)** is correct.
They took place in **1937, 1965, 1986**.
The **Mulki rules** are Hyderabad's; **Chandigarh** is a capital dispute; **Greater Nagaland** is secessionist.
xa: **Dravida Nadu** (**1960s**) was a secessionist demand from the same region.
**Autonomy** demands came from TN, Punjab, AP, WB (since the 1960s).
**M.G. Ramachandran** — regional party leader of TN.

n3d67427ad98.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about State laws reserving private jobs for locals?
o: AP's 2019 Act reserved 75% of private industrial jobs for locals.
Haryana's 2020 Act was struck down by the Punjab and Haryana High Court in November 2023.
Jharkhand's 2021 Act reserved 75% of lower-salary private jobs.
Haryana's 2020 Act was the first such law in India.
n3d67427ad98.x: Andhra Pradesh's 2019 Act was the first such law; Haryana's came in 2020.
xa: Haryana's Act was **struck down by the Punjab & Haryana High Court (Nov 2023)**.
AP's Act was **challenged in the AP High Court**.
⚠ First 75% law = **AP (2019)**; struck down = **Haryana**.

n5616b5dc959.s: The Haryana State Employment of Local Candidates Act, 2020 was struck down in November 2023 by which court?
n5616b5dc959.x: The Punjab and Haryana High Court struck down the Haryana law in November 2023 as unconstitutional.
n5616b5dc959.tq: Discriminate between the State concerned and the court that delivered the ruling.
xs: The **Punjab and Haryana High Court** struck down Haryana's **2020** Act in **Nov 2023** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It held the law **unconstitutional**.
xa: **APPSC-G2 2025** asked which state's 75% quota was struck down — **Haryana**.
Objection: it contradicts **Articles 14, 15, 16 and 19**.

n7e3a0c7636d.s: Under Article 16(3) of the Constitution, a residence requirement for employment under a State may be prescribed only by:
n7e3a0c7636d.x: Article 16(3) allows only Parliament to prescribe a residence requirement (it did so through the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957). The State Legislature, Governor and State PSC have no such power; Article 16(2) otherwise bars discrimination by place of birth or residence.
xs: Under **Art. 16(3)**, only **Parliament** can prescribe a residence requirement — so option **(3)** is correct.
Parliament did so via the **Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957**.
xa: **Art. 16(2)** bars discrimination in public employment on **place of birth and residence**.
States' 75% laws: **AP 2019**, **Haryana 2020**, **Jharkhand 2021**.
**Mulki rules** were a local-residence preference in **Hyderabad/Telangana**.

n064ffe81073.s: Under the pre-2022 public-employment zonal grouping, Zone II comprised:
o: East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna
n064ffe81073.x: Zone II comprised East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna; Zone I was North Andhra, Zone III Guntur-Prakasam-Nellore and Zone IV Rayalaseema.
xa: **Zones V and VI** went to **Telangana**.
Coastal Andhra (esp. **Krishna-Guntur**) is historically more developed than North Andhra and Rayalaseema.
The **Wanchoo Committee (1969)** examined **Mulki (employment) safeguards**.

n70b70637007.s: NITI Aayog monitors how many Aspirational Districts?
n70b70637007.tq: Direct numerical recall with nearby-value distractors.
xs: NITI Aayog monitors **112** Aspirational Districts — so option **(2)** is correct (Jan 2026).
It is one of the indicators of regional disparity.
xa: AP Cabinet tracked **₹8.55 lakh crore** of investment for North Andhra and Rayalaseema.
Defunct **BRGF** → **AP Industrial Policy 2023**.
AP's backward districts package covers **7 districts**.

n5f3cc4bd53b.s: In Rayalaseema's industrial growth, a JSW steel plant is located in:
n5f3cc4bd53b.x: The JSW steel plant is in Kadapa; Royal Enfield has a facility in Tirupati.
xa: Rayalaseema also has a **Kia plant**, **defence units** and **renewable parks** (CDCA, Jul 2026).
**₹8.55 lakh crore** investment aimed at jobs in **North Andhra and Rayalaseema**.
JSP MP sought an **AIIMS** in **Rayalaseema** and one in the north coastal districts.

nb85ab869391.s: Which of the following was set up under the 8-Point Formula of 1969?
o: Expert committee for locating the new capital of AP
nb85ab869391.x: The 8-Point Formula set up a high-level committee under a judge and a special committee on Telangana surpluses; the capital-location committee came under the 2014 Act.
xa: **Bhargava Committee (1969)**: Telangana surplus funds.
**Wanchoo Committee (1969)**: Mulki safeguards.
**Srikrishna Committee (2010)**: report with **six options**.

nb3d6477c215.s: The appointed day under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 was:
nb3d6477c215.x: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 took effect on the appointed day, 2 June 2014.
nb3d6477c215.tq: Direct date recall with close-date distractors.
xs: The **appointed day** of the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014** was **2 June 2014** — so option **(2)** is correct.
From that day **Hyderabad** became the common capital for up to **10 years**.
xa: PM promised **SCS** in the Rajya Sabha in **Feb 2014**.
**Sections 46(2)-(3)**: backward-areas package; **Section 94**: tax incentives.
**Sivaramakrishnan Committee** under the Act located the **new capital**.

n8bcfb01d38f.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, Hyderabad was made the common capital for up to:
n8bcfb01d38f.x: Hyderabad was the common capital for up to ten years; Sections 46(2)-(3) give the backward-areas package.
xa: Package: **7 districts**, **₹50 crore per district per year** (KBK/Bundelkhand model).
Appointed day: **2 June 2014**.

n7118aa96c15.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Special Category Status debate for Andhra Pradesh?
o: The Prime Minister promised SCS in the Rajya Sabha in February 2014.
The Fourteenth Finance Commission ended the general-versus-special distinction for devolution.
The SCS demand has ceased to be a political issue.
A special assistance measure was offered instead.
n7118aa96c15.x: The SCS demand still remains a political issue in Andhra Pradesh.
xa: Backward districts package: **₹50 crore per district per year**.
**Section 94**: tax incentives.
Comparison: **Kalyana Karnataka** has **Art. 371J** status (since **2013**).

n46acb0a2c27.s: Which committee was constituted under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 as an expert committee for locating the new capital of Andhra Pradesh?
n46acb0a2c27.x: The Sivaramakrishnan Committee, headed by K.C. Sivaramakrishnan, was the expert committee under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, for locating the new capital of Andhra Pradesh.
n46acb0a2c27.tq: Who would perform this specific statutory task?
xs: The **Sivaramakrishnan Committee** (**K.C. Sivaramakrishnan**, **2014**) located AP's **new capital** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was an expert committee under the **AP Reorganisation Act**.
**Srikrishna** = Telangana question (**2010**); **Bhargava** = surplus funds; **Wanchoo** = Mulki safeguards (both **1969**).
xa: Three-capitals plan (**2020**): **Visakhapatnam** executive, **Amaravati** legislative, **Kurnool** judicial.
Both 2020 laws were withdrawn in **Nov 2021**.
Hyderabad was common capital for up to **10 years**.

n1e438a8ffdf.s: Both the AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020 and the APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2020 were withdrawn in:
n1e438a8ffdf.x: Both laws were withdrawn in November 2021.
n1e438a8ffdf.tq: Discriminate between the year of enactment and the year of withdrawal.
xs: Both three-capitals laws were withdrawn in **2021** (**Nov 2021**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**APPSC-GS 2022** asked exactly this.
xa: The laws: **AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020** + **APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2020**.
After **2024**, the coalition is pushing a **central law** to protect **Amaravati**.
Coalition fear: three-capital plan revived in **2029**.

n0df80cef1a5.s: Under the AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020, which city was proposed as the executive capital?
n0df80cef1a5.x: The 2020 Act proposed Visakhapatnam as executive, Amaravati as legislative and Kurnool as judicial capital.
xa: ⚠ Three capitals: **Visakhapatnam** = executive; **Amaravati** = legislative; **Kurnool** = judicial.
Repealed in **Nov 2021** along with the **APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2020**.
After 2024 the coalition aims to complete **Amaravati within three years**.

n67196b0a3e1.s: Kalyana Karnataka has special status under which Article of the Constitution?
n67196b0a3e1.x: Kalyana Karnataka has special status under Article 371J since 2013, although disparities continue.
xa: AP's backward districts package: **7 districts**, **₹50 crore per district per year**.
AP's **SCS** demand remains a political issue.
NITI Aayog monitors **112** Aspirational Districts.

ncb8cffb5537.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra sub-regional accords?
o: The Sri Bagh Pact (1937) was the first Coastal-Rayalaseema accord.
Poor implementation of such safeguards fed agitations.
Such agreement-based safeguards are criticised for institutionalising sub-regional fault lines.
The Gentlemen's Agreement was concluded in 1969.
ncb8cffb5537.x: The Gentlemen's Agreement was in 1956, not 1969.
xa: **1969** is the year of the **8-Point Formula**, **Bhargava** and **Wanchoo** Committees.
**Srikrishna Committee (2010)** reported with **six options**.
Public-employment **Zones V and VI** went to **Telangana**.

n8d7536de593.s: In the life cycle of a youth agitation, which stage comes first?
n8d7536de593.x: The sequence is discontent, initiation, formalisation, public support and official action.
xa: Signs of youth unrest: **shared dissatisfaction**, **public attention**, **desire for change**.
Types: **Persuasive**, **Resistance**, **Revolutionary**.
