**Resource mobilisation** theory: **tactics and leadership** matter more than grievances.

n05b07c9f883.s: The relative deprivation theory of youth unrest is associated with:
n05b07c9f883.x: Relative deprivation theory is associated with Stouffer; personal maladjustment is another listed theory.
xa: ⚠ **Relative deprivation = Stouffer** — a favourite matching trap.
Life cycle of an agitation: **Discontent → initiation → formalisation → public support → official action**.
Revolutionary unrest aims to **overthrow the system** — e.g. **AASU, Bodo**.

n8822c295368.s: The Dalit Panthers emerged as a militant movement in:
n8822c295368.x: The Dalit Panthers emerged in 1972 in Maharashtra and are associated with militancy.
n8822c295368.tq: Link the movement with its year and location.
xs: The **Dalit Panthers** emerged in **1972** in **Maharashtra** as a **militant** form of youth unrest — option **(2)**.
**1974 Gujarat** is the **Nav Nirman** movement; **1979 Assam** is **AASU**; **1990 North India** is the **Anti-Mandal** agitation.
xa: Regional/secessionist forms: **Naga, Assam, Khalistan**.
Deviance form: **drug abuse**.
New pattern: **leaderless, digital** protests — Bangladesh **2024**, **Nepal Gen Z 2025**.

ncca44b35941.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the new pattern of youth protest?
o: The Bangladesh 2024 protests were over job quotas.
Protests are organised on encrypted apps.
Such protests are typically led by a formally constituted central committee.
ncca44b35941.x: The new pattern is leaderless, digital protest, so a formal central committee contradicts it.
xa: Another example: **Nepal Gen Z 2025**.
A wave of youth-led protests also hit **Bangladesh, Nepal and Kenya**.
Older forms: regional/secessionist (**Naga, Assam, Khalistan**), militancy (**Dalit Panthers**, 1972), deviance (**drug abuse**).

n5c1230956ac.s: According to MoSPI 2022, the youth unemployment rate was:
n5c1230956ac.x: For youth aged 15–29 years, the reported unemployment rates were 13.0% for males and 12.5% for females.
n5c1230956ac.tq: Keep the sex-wise percentages in their correct order.
xs: Option (1) reverses the two figures; **17.5% / 22.7%** are AP's overall and urban youth rates (**PLFS 2023-24**).
**13.1% vs 27.4%** are the ILO 2026 global rates for **men vs women**.
xa: AP youth unemployment **17.5%** — well **above the national rate**; rural **15.5%**, urban **22.7%**.
AP **urban female youth**: **29.1%** — the highest figure in the table.
**ILO 2026**: global youth unemployment **12.4%** (**67 M**); **NEET 20%**.

n0a1baf66992.s: Youth unemployment in Andhra Pradesh is reported as:
n0a1baf66992.x: Youth unemployment in Andhra Pradesh is reported as 17.5%, higher than the national rate.
xa: AP break-up: **rural 15.5%**, **urban 22.7%**, **urban female youth 29.1%**.
AP skilling: **APSSDC** trained **2,57,575** people in **2024-25**.

n6101ba62378.s: The motto of the National Service Scheme (NSS) is:
n6101ba62378.x: The NSS motto is 'Not Me But You'; the scheme, started in 1969, rests on the idea of 'Education through Service'.
xa: **MY Bharat** (**31 Oct 2023**) replaced **NYKS** under **MoYAS**.
**National Young Leaders Programme** (**Dec 2014**) includes the **Neighbourhood Youth Parliament**.
**PMKVY (Skill India)** — **2015** — skill training for new entrants to the job market.

o: A temporary disagreement between students and teachers over examinations
Individual frustration of a young person over personal failure
Organised violence carried out only by youth wings of political parties
Collective frustration among young people when social norms appear ineffective or harmful
n4c17039af77.x: Youth unrest is collective frustration among young people when society's norms seem ineffective or harmful.
xa: Types: **Persuasive** (exam postponement), **Resistance** (against attendance rules), **Revolutionary** (overthrow the system — **AASU, Bodo**).
Life cycle: **Discontent → initiation → formalisation → public support → official action**.
Theories: discontent, **personal maladjustment**, **relative deprivation (Stouffer)** and **resource mobilisation**.

n567a4dad252.x: The Anti-Mandal movement opposed 27% reservation for OBCs.
xa: **AASU** is also cited as a **revolutionary** type of agitation, with the **Bodo**.
**Nav Nirman** (Gujarat) and **JP movement** (Bihar) — both **1974**.
**Jai Andhra** (**1972-73**) followed the SC upholding the **Mulki Rules**; ended by the **Six-Point Formula (1973)**.

ne60f67833aa.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the student movements of 1974?
o: The Nav Nirman movement forced Chief Minister Chimanbhai Patel to resign.
The JP movement in Bihar fed into the Emergency of June 1975.
The Nav Nirman movement was a Gujarat student agitation.
The Nav Nirman movement was led by Jayaprakash Narayan in Bihar.
ne60f67833aa.x: JP led the Bihar movement; Nav Nirman was a separate student agitation in Gujarat.
xa: ⚠ **Nav Nirman = Gujarat**; **JP = Bihar** — both **1974**.
**AASU** (**1979-85**, Assam) against illegal migrants → **Assam Accord 1985**.
**Telangana students** (**1969; 2009-14**) — **Osmania University** — separate statehood.

n3f941188627.s: The Jai Andhra agitation (1972–73) followed the Supreme Court's decision upholding the:
n3f941188627.x: The Jai Andhra agitation arose after the Supreme Court upheld the Mulki Rules and ended with the Six-Point Formula in 1973.
xa: Jai Andhra was ended by the **Six-Point Formula (1973)**.
Visakha Ukku: **T. Amrutha Rao's** fast; deaths in police firing.
Latest: YSRCP student and youth wings protested over alleged **Mega DSC** recruitment irregularities (**29 Jul 2026**).

nb535c5acd06.s: The 'Visakha Ukku – Andhrula Hakku' agitation for a steel plant at Visakhapatnam took place in:
nb535c5acd06.x: The agitation took place in 1966, with T. Amrutha Rao undertaking a fast.
xa: **Jai Andhra** (**1972-73**) followed the SC upholding the **Mulki Rules**.
**Special Category Status** agitation — **after 2014** — for the SCS promised at bifurcation.
**Mega DSC** recruitment protests by YSRCP youth wings (**29 Jul 2026**).

n92aedbb1a04.s: Under the National Youth Policy 2014, the term ‘youth’ refers to persons in which age group?
n92aedbb1a04.x: The National Youth Policy 2014 defines youth as persons aged 15–29 years. The National Youth Policy 2003 used the age group 13–35 years.
n92aedbb1a04.tq: Separate the age group in NYP 2014 from the earlier NYP 2003 definition.
xs: **NYP 2014** defines youth as **15-29 years** — option **(1)**.
**13-35 years** was the age group of the earlier **NYP 2003** — a classic trap.
xa: NYP 2014 has **5 objectives** and **11 priority areas**.
The same **15-29** band is used for **MoSPI 2022** youth unemployment data.

na02ad0fc144.s: The National Youth Policy 2014 has how many priority areas?
na02ad0fc144.x: NYP 2014 has 5 objectives and 11 priority areas, including participation in politics and governance and sports.
xa: Other priority areas: **education**, **employment and skills**, **entrepreneurship**, **health**, **social values**, **community engagement**, **inclusion**, **social justice**.
Youth = **15-29 years** under NYP 2014.
A Bill seeks a constitutional **National Commission for Youth**; the last, non-statutory one ran **2002-04**.

nc9a488a6ffa.s: MY Bharat, launched on 31 October 2023, replaced which organisation?
nc9a488a6ffa.x: MY Bharat was launched on 31 October 2023 and replaced NYKS under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
nc9a488a6ffa.tq: Identify the predecessor organisation from the institutional relationship.
xs: **MY Bharat** (**31 Oct 2023**) replaced **NYKS** — option **(3)**; it is under the **MoYAS**.
**NSS** (1969) continues; **PMKVY** is a Skill India scheme; the **National Youth Advisory Council** is part of the National Young Leaders Programme.
xa: **NSS** motto: **"Not Me But You"**; idea: **"Education through Service"**.
**National Young Leaders Programme** — **Dec 2014**.
**PMKVY** — **2015** — skill training for new job-market entrants.

n715cef99e66.s: The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana under Skill India was launched in:
n715cef99e66.x: PMKVY under Skill India was launched in 2015 and provides skill training for new entrants to the job market.
n715cef99e66.tq: Distinguish the launch year from the year of the National Young Leaders Programme.
xs: **PMKVY** under **Skill India** began in **2015** — option **(4)**; it gives skill training to new entrants to the job market.
**1969** is **NSS**; **2003** the earlier **NYP**; **2014** the current **NYP** and the National Young Leaders Programme.
xa: AP skilling: **APSSDC** trained **2,57,575** people in **2024-25**.
**MY Bharat** — **31 Oct 2023** — replaced **NYKS**.
Unemployment backdrop: about **9.7 million** join the working-age group each year (**2021-31**).

n6a269a38912.s: The protests over the NEET paper leak began at:
n6a269a38912.x: The protests began at Jantar Mantar and later spread nationwide.
xa: A **ministerial resignation** followed (**5 Aug 2026**).
Comparative note: youth-led protests in **Bangladesh, Nepal and Kenya**.
New pattern: **leaderless, digital** protests on encrypted apps.

n92e400e1091.s: Which is the correct sequence of developments in the NEET paper leak protests?
o: Ministerial resignation – nationwide protests – Jantar Mantar protests
Jantar Mantar protests – nationwide protests – ministerial resignation
Nationwide protests – ministerial resignation – Jantar Mantar protests
Jantar Mantar protests – ministerial resignation – nationwide protests
n92e400e1091.x: The protests began at Jantar Mantar, turned nationwide and were followed by the ministerial resignation.
xa: The trigger was the **NEET paper leak**.
Life cycle of agitation: **Discontent → initiation → formalisation → public support → official action**.
Wave of youth-led protests in **Bangladesh, Nepal and Kenya**.

n4eba5d03fde.s: The National Institute of Social Defence functions under the
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
n4eba5d03fde.x: NISD works under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
xs: The **National Institute of Social Defence (NISD)** works under the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MoSJE)** — option **(1)**.
NISD implements the **Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan** and trains officials (e.g. on **children who beg**).
**MoYAS** runs the 2026 **Nasha Mukt Yuva** campaign through **MY Bharat**; the **NCB** is under the **MHA**.
xa: **NMBA** — launched **15 Aug 2020** by **MoSJE**; first in **272** vulnerable districts, now in all.
**SMILE** (MoSJE, **2022**) — sub-scheme for **comprehensive rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging**.
Social defence scope: **drug and alcohol abuse**, **beggary**, **destitute elderly**, **transgender persons**.

nbbead4aca2b.s: The Anti-Arrack Movement in Andhra Pradesh was led by:
nbbead4aca2b.x: Dubagunta Rosamma led the Anti-Arrack Movement among neo-literate women of the literacy campaign.
xa: The movement began in **1992** in **Dubagunta** village, **Nellore** district.
It spread among **neo-literate women** of the **literacy campaign**.
⚠ Anti-Arrack = **Dubagunta (Nellore), 1992**; temperance precedent = **Social Purity Association (1891)**.

n5514fa04d5a.s: The Anti-Arrack Movement of 1992 began in Dubagunta village of which district?
n5514fa04d5a.x: The movement began in 1992 in Dubagunta village of Nellore district, led by Dubagunta Rosamma.
xa: ⚠ Precedent: **Social Purity Association** (**1891**) of **R. Venkataratnam Naidu**.
**Chittoor Police** ran **"Dharya Sparsa - Operation Flush-Out"** against drugs and illegal liquor (Jul 2026).
**Art. 47** — State to try to **prohibit intoxicating drinks** and harmful drugs.

n055365c816c.s: Which city was declared the first beggar-free city in 2025?
n055365c816c.x: Indore was declared the first beggar-free city in 2025.
n055365c816c.tq: Separate the city-level distinction from State-level beggar statistics.
xs: **Indore** was declared the **first beggar-free city** (**2025**) — option **(1)**.
It is listed as a **FIRST** under social defence, whose scope includes **beggary**.
xa: **West Bengal** tops the state list of beggars.
**SMILE** (**2022**) — rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging.
**Delhi HC (2018, Harsh Mander)** decriminalised begging in Delhi.

ne712332bc22.s: Which one of the following best describes the changing approach towards social problems such as suicide, drug abuse and beggary?
o: From statutory regulation towards complete absence of regulation
From health and rehabilitation towards punishment alone
From punishment towards health and rehabilitation
ne712332bc22.x: The approach is moving from punishment, including Section 309 and anti-begging laws, towards health and rehabilitation through measures such as MHCA, SMILE and NMBA.
ne712332bc22.tq: Identify the direction of change by comparing the earlier punitive approach with the newer rehabilitative approach.
xs: The approach is shifting **from punishment towards health and rehabilitation** — option **(4)**.
Punishment: **Sec. 309** and **anti-begging laws**; health and rehabilitation: **MHCA**, **SMILE**, **NMBA**.
xa: **P. Rathinam (1994)** called Sec. 309 invalid; **MHCA 2017 Sec. 115** bars trial or punishment.
**SC (2021)** treated begging as a **socio-economic problem**.
**NMBA** (**2020**) is implemented by **NISD** with a focus on campuses.

n00d1c06a660.s: Article 47 directs the State to endeavour to prohibit, except for medicinal purposes, the consumption of:
o: Intoxicating drinks and drugs injurious to health
n00d1c06a660.x: Article 47, a Directive Principle, refers to prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs injurious to health, except for medicinal purposes.
xa: **NDPS Act, 1985** — **Sec. 71** provides for **treatment centres**.
Drug enforcement: **Police**, **NCB (1986, MHA)**, **Customs**, **DRI**.
Temperance precedent: **R. Venkataratnam Naidu's Social Purity Association (1891)**.

n5fb7cee0389.s: India lies between which two major drug-producing regions?
n5fb7cee0389.x: India lies between the Golden Crescent and the Golden Triangle, two major drug-producing regions.
xa: Drug enforcement: **Police**, **NCB (1986, MHA)**, **Customs**, **DRI**.
**NDPS Act, 1985** — **Sec. 71** treatment centres.
**Anti-drug day**: **26 June**.

n36865227240.s: The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan is implemented by the:
n36865227240.x: NMBA, launched by MoSJE on 15 August 2020, is implemented by the National Institute of Social Defence (NISD).
xa: NMBA focuses on **campuses**.
⚠ **NMBA = MoSJE (2020)**; **Nasha Mukt Yuva = MoYAS through MY Bharat (2026)**.
**Anti-drug day**: **26 June**.

n3ddb6b3c641.s: Tele-MANAS is a tele-mental-health helpline launched on 10 October 2022. Its toll-free number is
n3ddb6b3c641.x: Tele-MANAS was launched on 10 October 2022 and can be accessed through the toll-free number 14416.
n3ddb6b3c641.tq: Combine the launch-date and service-number clues without confusing other helplines.
xs: **Tele-MANAS** (launched **10 Oct 2022**) has the toll-free number **14416** — option **(4)**.
It is a **tele-mental-health helpline**.
xa: **Sec. 115**, **MHCA 2017** — presumes severe stress; no trial or punishment for attempted suicide.
ADSI 2024: **1,70,746** suicides; **daily wagers** about **31%**.
AP ran **463** school and **308** college suicide-prevention programmes (**2023-25**).

nea98c3ff3d5.s: SMILE, launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in 2022, includes a sub-scheme for
o: Construction of prisons for habitual beggars
Removal of beggars from all urban areas
Comprehensive rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging
nea98c3ff3d5.x: SMILE includes a sub-scheme for comprehensive rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging and shifts towards rights-based rehabilitation.
nea98c3ff3d5.tq: Choose the precise welfare objective rather than a punitive substitute.
xs: **SMILE** (**MoSJE, 2022**) has a sub-scheme for **comprehensive rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging** — option **(4)**.
It marks a shift from **punitive laws** to **rights-based rehabilitation** — not institutionalisation, prisons or removal.
xa: **SMILE-Beggary Survey App** — **Chandigarh Chintan Shivir** (**24-26 Apr 2026**).
**NISD** trains officials, e.g. on **children who beg**.
**Indore** — **first beggar-free city** (**2025**).

n825a9f6eb7f.s: According to the National Survey on Extent and Pattern of Substance Use (2019), the most-used substance in India was:
n825a9f6eb7f.x: Alcohol (14.6%) was the most-used substance, followed by cannabis (2.8%) and opioids (2.1%).
xa: **Art. 47** asks the State to try to prohibit intoxicating drinks and harmful drugs.
ADSI 2024 drug-overdose deaths: **978** (up **50%**).
**NMBA** — **15 Aug 2020** — **272** districts first, now all.

n9614187b136.s: As per ADSI 2015, the leading cause of farmer suicides was
n9614187b136.x: Bankruptcy or indebtedness ranked first among the causes of farmer suicides in ADSI 2015, followed by farming-related issues.
n9614187b136.tq: Identify the first-ranked cause rather than a related secondary cause.
xs: In **ADSI 2015**, **bankruptcy/indebtedness** ranked first among causes of farmer suicides — option **(1)**.
**Farming-related issues** came second; this was the **APPSC-G1 2017** key.
xa: ADSI 2024: **1,70,746** suicides; **daily wagers** about **31%**.
**Tele-MANAS** helpline — toll-free **14416**.
**Sec. 115**, Mental Healthcare Act **2017**: presumes **severe stress** — no trial or punishment.

n7c7ca173661.s: Who propounded the concept of the “culture of poverty” in 1959?
n7c7ca173661.x: The concept of the “culture of poverty” was propounded by Oscar Lewis in 1959.
xa: ⚠ **René Lenoir** (France, **1974**) coined **social exclusion** — do not confuse with Lewis.
**Absolute poverty**: below the **minimum needed to survive**.
**STs** have the highest poverty, then **SCs** — the cause is **discrimination and exclusion**.

n096555b2422.s: Which one of the following is NOT generally treated as a social indicator of poverty?
n096555b2422.x: Illiteracy, malnutrition, poor health care and lack of safe water and sanitation are the listed social indicators of poverty. Size of the house is not one; UPPSC 2025 keyed it as the NOT-a-social-indicator option.
n096555b2422.tq: Find the item outside the established social-indicator group.
xs: **Size of the house** is not a social indicator of poverty — option **(3)**; **UPPSC 2025** keyed it as the NOT option.
The social indicators are **illiteracy**, **malnutrition**, **poor health care** and lack of **safe water and sanitation** — so options (1), (2), (4) are indicators.
xa: **Absolute poverty**: below the minimum needed to survive.
**National MPI** standard-of-living indicators include **cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, housing, electricity, assets, bank accounts**.
The MPI has **3 equally weighted dimensions** and **12 indicators**.

n4e46cabd441.s: The term ‘social exclusion’ was coined by
n4e46cabd441.x: The term was coined by René Lenoir in France in 1974.
n4e46cabd441.tq: Combine the person, country and year to avoid author substitution.
xs: **René Lenoir** coined **social exclusion** in **France** in **1974** — option **(2)**.
Social exclusion is the **process** that shuts people out of **facilities, benefits and opportunities** others enjoy.
xa: ⚠ **Oscar Lewis (1959)** — **culture of poverty**.
Bases of exclusion: **caste, gender, disability, religion, region**.
First state employment guarantee scheme: **Maharashtra EGS (1972)**.

n1fea3a229a2.s: The Union opposes a creamy layer for SCs and STs mainly on the view that:
o: Caste exclusion exists only in urban areas
Income alone does not end caste-based exclusion
Economic criteria cannot be used in any welfare policy
n1fea3a229a2.x: The stated position is that income does not eliminate caste exclusion, so economic advancement alone does not end caste-based discrimination.
xa: **STs** and **SCs** have the highest poverty, caused by **discrimination and exclusion**.
Practices of exclusion: **untouchability**, **segregation**, denied access to land, water and jobs.
Debate on **VB-G RAM G** funding: critics say budget caps and **cost-sharing** hurt poor states.

n9a9f18649b4.s: The Y.K. Alagh Committee’s poverty estimation method was based on calorie requirements of
o: 2,700 calories in rural areas and 2,400 calories in urban areas
2,400 calories in rural areas and 2,100 calories in urban areas
2,100 calories in rural areas and 2,400 calories in urban areas
2,200 calories in both rural and urban areas
n9a9f18649b4.x: The Y.K. Alagh Committee, formed in 1979, used a calorie norm of 2,400 calories for rural areas and 2,100 calories for urban areas. The corresponding expenditure was treated as the poverty line.
n9a9f18649b4.tq: Use the rural–urban comparison to distinguish the calorie norms.
xs: The **Y.K. Alagh Committee** (**1979**) used **2,400 calories rural** and **2,100 calories urban** — option **(2)**.
The poverty line was the **spending needed** to buy those calories; option (3) reverses the figures.
xa: ⚠ **Alagh** = calories only; **Tendulkar** = dropped the calorie anchor; **Rangarajan** = food plus non-food.
**Lakdawala** (report **1993**) kept the calorie base with **state-specific** lines.
**Tendulkar** (report **2009**) used **MRP** and an urban basket for both sectors.

n2cd6949dae3.s: Which of the following was a significant departure introduced by the Tendulkar Committee methodology?
o: It used only rural consumption baskets for both sectors.
It excluded non-food expenditure from the poverty line.
It restored the calorie anchor as the sole basis of poverty estimation.
It dropped the calorie anchor and included health and education expenditure.
n2cd6949dae3.x: The Tendulkar Committee (report 2009) dropped the calorie anchor, used the Mixed Reference Period (MRP), applied the urban basket to both sectors and included health and education spending. The other options are wrong: it did not use a rural-only basket, exclude non-food spending or restore the calorie anchor.
n2cd6949dae3.tq: Identify the methodological change rather than the older calorie-based approach.
xs: **Tendulkar** **dropped the calorie anchor** and **included health and education** spending — option **(4)**.
It used **MRP** and the **urban basket for both** sectors — so a rural-only basket (1) is wrong.
It did not restore the calorie anchor; **Alagh** was the calorie-only method.
xa: **Rangarajan** (**2014**) added **food plus non-food** items (housing, clothing, education, health, transport).
⚠ **₹972/₹1,407** a month are **Rangarajan's**, not Tendulkar's.

n5cd9fb90bcd.s: The Rangarajan poverty lines for 2011–12 were:
o: ₹32 per day rural and ₹47 per day urban
₹32 per day urban and ₹47 per day rural
₹47 per day in both rural and urban areas
₹27 per day rural and ₹33 per day urban
n5cd9fb90bcd.x: Rangarajan estimated ₹32 per day for rural and ₹47 per day for urban areas (₹972 and ₹1,407 per month).
xa: ⚠ Trap: APSES and CDI wrongly give ₹972/₹1,407 as **Tendulkar's** — the **APPSC-GS 2025** key confirms **₹32** as Rangarajan's.
Rangarajan used **food plus non-food** (housing, clothing, education, health, transport).
**Oct 2025**: RBI updated the Rangarajan line with **HCES 2022-23**.

nindian-society-11-20.s: Who chaired the Rangarajan Committee, which dealt with poverty measurement?
nindian-society-11-20.x: C. Rangarajan chaired the 2012 committee on poverty measurement. Tendulkar (2005) came before it, and Hashim and Saxena (2009) dealt with BPL lists and rural poverty.
nindian-society-11-20.tq: Match each poverty committee to its chair.
xs: **C. Rangarajan** chaired the **Rangarajan Committee** (**2012**, report **2014**) on **poverty measurement** — option **(1)**.
**Suresh Tendulkar** chaired the **2005** committee on poverty estimation.
**S. R. Hashim** (BPL identification) and **N. C. Saxena** (rural poverty) headed **2009** bodies.
xa: Rangarajan used **food plus non-food** (housing, clothing, education, health, transport).
Rangarajan's 2011-12 line: **₹32 rural / ₹47 urban a day** (₹972/₹1,407 a month).
RBI updated the **Rangarajan** line with **HCES 2022-23** (Oct **2025**).
⚠ **Alagh** = calories only; **Tendulkar** = dropped calorie anchor.

n35468bda4fc.s: The nodal agency for poverty estimation, using NSSO data, is
n35468bda4fc.x: NITI Aayog is the nodal agency for poverty estimation; it replaced the Planning Commission and uses NSSO data.
n35468bda4fc.tq: Apply the institutional succession trap: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission.
xs: **NITI Aayog** (earlier the **Planning Commission**) is the **nodal agency** for poverty, using **NSSO** data — option **(4)**.
The **Finance Commission**, **NDC** and **RBI** are not the nodal poverty agency, though the RBI updated the Rangarajan line in **Oct 2025**.
xa: **NSO (MoSPI)** runs the **HCES** about every **5 years**; **MPCE** sets the line.
**National MPI**: **NITI Aayog** with **UNDP** and **OPHI**.
**PLFS** of the NSO is the standard for **unemployment**.

n943c9d8ccc4.s: The National Multidimensional Poverty Index has three equally weighted dimensions and how many indicators?
n943c9d8ccc4.x: The National MPI, prepared by NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI, has 3 dimensions and 12 indicators.
xa: Other standard-of-living indicators: **cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, housing, electricity, assets**.
**NITI MPI 2023**: **Bihar** highest (**33.76%**), **Kerala** lowest.
AP MPI headcount **6.06%** vs India's **14.96%**.

nbbc4dbead24.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, poverty in 2023-24 measured by the Tendulkar line was
nbbc4dbead24.x: Poverty measured by the Tendulkar line was stated to have fallen from 21.9 percent in 2011–12 to 2.3 percent in 2023–24.
nbbc4dbead24.tq: Distinguish the Tendulkar-line estimate from the MPI and World Bank estimates.
xs: Poverty on the **Tendulkar line** was **2.3 percent** in **2023-24** — option **(1)** (ES 2025-26).
**21.9%** was the earlier **2011-12** figure.
xa: Tendulkar 2004-05 estimate: **37.2%**.
Critics say the Tendulkar line is **too low**.
Income inequality is **rising** (World Inequality Database).

n16ae74ff6bf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about poverty by social group in India?
o: Scheduled Tribes have the highest incidence of poverty.
Discrimination contributes to poverty among these groups.
Scheduled Tribes rank below Scheduled Castes in poverty incidence.
Social exclusion is a cause of poverty among these groups.
n16ae74ff6bf.x: Scheduled Tribes have the highest poverty incidence, with Scheduled Castes next, so STs do not rank below SCs.
xa: Bases of exclusion: **caste, gender, disability, religion, region**.
Practices: **untouchability**, **segregation**, denied access to **land, water and jobs**.
The Union opposes a **creamy layer** for SC/STs since **income does not end caste exclusion**.

n420266fa8d5.s: According to the NITI Multidimensional Poverty Index for 2023, which State recorded the highest poverty level?
n420266fa8d5.x: Bihar recorded the highest multidimensional poverty level in the NITI MPI 2023, at 33.76%.
n420266fa8d5.tq: Match the precise percentage with the State rather than confusing the MPI ranking with the Rangarajan poverty-line estimates.
xs: **Bihar** recorded the highest MPI in **NITI MPI 2023** — **33.76%**, option **(3)**.
**Kerala** recorded the lowest.
xa: AP district extremes: **West Godavari (2.42%)** lowest, **Kurnool (12.84%)** highest.
The National MPI is prepared by **NITI Aayog** with **UNDP** and **OPHI**.

n84517f5c840.s: The process that shuts people out of facilities, benefits and opportunities that others enjoy is called:
n84517f5c840.x: This is the standard definition of social exclusion, whose bases include caste, gender, disability, religion and region.
xa: Term coined by **René Lenoir** (France, **1974**).
**STs** then **SCs** have the highest poverty — due to discrimination and exclusion.
⚠ **Oscar Lewis (1959)** = culture of poverty, not social exclusion.

n378f1fb9c01.s: As per PLFS 2023–24, the unemployment rate of Andhra Pradesh was:
n378f1fb9c01.x: PLFS 2023–24 shows 4.1 per cent unemployment for Andhra Pradesh against 3.2 per cent for India.
xa: India's UR fell from **6.0% (2017-18)**.
AP **rural informal employment**: **62.3%**.
Female LFPR (India) rose **23.3% → 41.7%**.

n7c3a86d3445.s: The Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) was introduced in:
n7c3a86d3445.x: SGSY came in 1999, after IRDP (1978–80) and before NREGA (2005–06) and DAY-NRLM (2011).
xa: ⚠ **SGSY** merged **IRDP**; **DAY-NRLM** restructured **SGSY**.
**JRY (1989)** merged **NREP** and **RLEGP**.
**PMEGP (2008)** merged **PMRY** and **REGP**.

n5de88f14820.s: The first state-level employment guarantee scheme in India was the
o: Andhra Pradesh Rural Employment Scheme of 1978
n5de88f14820.x: The Maharashtra Employment Guarantee Scheme, introduced in 1972, was the first state scheme of this kind.
n5de88f14820.tq: Combine the state, name and year instead of selecting a later national programme.
xs: The **Maharashtra Employment Guarantee Scheme (1972)** was the first state scheme — option **(1)**.
It preceded the national **NREGA** (passed **2005**) by decades.
xa: **NREGA** passed **2005**; in force **2 Feb 2006**.
Renamed **MGNREGA** on **2 Oct 2009**.
**VB-G RAM G Bill, 2025** passed on **18 Dec 2025**.

n2705288bfd4.s: The VB-G RAM G Bill, 2025 raises the rural employment guarantee to
n2705288bfd4.x: The VB-G RAM G Bill, 2025, passed on 18 December 2025, proposed raising the guarantee from 100 to 125 days and changing the funding pattern.
n2705288bfd4.tq: Distinguish the updated figure from the original MGNREGA guarantee.
xs: The **VB-G RAM G Bill, 2025** raises the guarantee to **125 days** — option **(3)**.
**100 days** is the original **MGNREGA** guarantee.
xa: It was passed on **18 Dec 2025** and also **changes the funding pattern**.
Critics: **budget caps** and **cost-sharing** hurt poor states.
⚠ **100 days = MGNREGA**; **125 days = VB-G RAM G**.

nf558e8c60a2.s: The three-generation classification of human rights was proposed in 1977 by:
nf558e8c60a2.x: Karel Vasak proposed the three generations in 1977, mapped to liberty, equality and fraternity.
xa: Second generation (equality): **work, education, health**, **eradication of social discrimination**.
Generations **overlap** — e.g. **education** is both second- and third-generation.
⚠ **1st – 2nd – 3rd = liberty – equality – fraternity**.

nf336695b4b0.s: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights covers which rights?
o: Civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights
Only economic, social and cultural rights
nf336695b4b0.x: The UDHR covers all five categories of rights, though it is not a treaty and is not legally binding as one.
xa: Binding covenants came later: **ICCPR** and **ICESCR** (adopted **16 Dec 1966**).
**International Bill of Human Rights** = **UDHR + ICCPR + ICESCR** + optional protocols.
Adopted by the **UNGA** on **10 December 1948**.

n09d2fefb620.s: In India, the right to vote is best described as a:
o: Statutory right under Section 62 of the Representation of the People Act
n09d2fefb620.x: The right to vote is only a statutory right, conferred by Section 62 of the Representation of the People Act. It is not a Fundamental Right (Art. 19 lists freedoms of speech, movement etc.), a Directive Principle (Art. 47 concerns nutrition, health and prohibition) or a Fundamental Duty. This shows that not every human right is a Fundamental Right.
n09d2fefb620.tq: Vote = statutory right (Sec. 62 RP Act), not an FR.
xs: The **right to vote** is only a **statutory right** under **Section 62** of the **Representation of the People Act** — option **(2)**.
It is not a Fundamental Right, DPSP or Fundamental Duty — showing that **not every human right is an FR**.
xa: Voting is a **first-generation** (liberty) right in Vasak's scheme, with life, speech and fair trial.
Every **Fundamental Right** is a human right.
Human rights are **inherent and inalienable**, held because one is human.

n318c74cdf59.s: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights contains how many articles?
n318c74cdf59.x: The UDHR, adopted on 10 December 1948 with Eleanor Roosevelt chairing its drafting, has 30 articles.
xa: **Human Rights Day**: **10 December**.
The UDHR is **not a treaty** → **not legally binding**.
Its **80th anniversary** falls in **Dec 2028**.

n1d65d71dd8b.s: Which one of the following is NOT specifically included among the rights recognised in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
o: Right to an adequate standard of living
n1d65d71dd8b.x: The listed UDHR rights include dignity, liberty, equality, life, an adequate standard of living and education. A right to universal basic income is not included.
n1d65d71dd8b.tq: Find the entitlement that falls outside the stated UDHR list.
xs: A **right to universal basic income** is not in the UDHR — option **(1)** (JPSC **2023**).
Included: **dignity, liberty and equality**, **life**, an **adequate standard of living** and **education**.
xa: UDHR: **30 articles** covering civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights.
⚠ Privacy is protected by UDHR **Art. 12** and ICCPR **Art. 17**, though a JPSC **2016** key treated it as not UN-listed.
Adopted **10 December 1948**; drafting chaired by **Eleanor Roosevelt**.

n6389bd79d8c.s: The right to privacy is protected under which articles of the UDHR and the ICCPR respectively?
n6389bd79d8c.x: The UDHR protects privacy under Article 12 and the ICCPR under Article 17.
xa: ⚠ A **JPSC 2016** key treated privacy as not a UN-listed human right — expect this only in badly set questions.
Other ICCPR articles: **life (Art. 6)**, **no torture (Art. 7)**, **fair trial (Art. 14)**.
UDHR does not include a **right to universal basic income** (JPSC **2023**).

nindian-society-32-15.s: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on:
nindian-society-32-15.x: The UN General Assembly adopted the UDHR on 10 December 1948, now marked as Human Rights Day. The UN came into being on 24 October 1945, and India's Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949.
nindian-society-32-15.tq: Discriminate the UDHR date from other famous dates.
xs: The **UNGA** adopted the **UDHR** on **10 December 1948** — option **(3)**.
**10 December** is observed as **Human Rights Day**.
xa: Drafting was chaired by **Eleanor Roosevelt**.
The UDHR is **not a treaty**, so **not legally binding**.
It has a **preamble** and **30 articles**, with **human dignity** at its core.
**ICCPR** and **ICESCR** were adopted on **16 Dec 1966**.

nindian-society-32-18.s: Which of the following is identified as an economic and social right under the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
nindian-society-32-18.x: The right to work is an economic and social right in the UDHR. Free speech, freedom of religion and equality before law are civil and political rights.
nindian-society-32-18.tq: Sort the rights as civil-political or economic-social.
xs: The **right to work** is an **economic and social** (second-generation) right — option **(2)**.
**Freedom of speech** is a **civil and political** (first-generation) right, alongside life, fair trial and vote.
xa: **Karel Vasak (1977)** mapped three generations to **liberty, equality and fraternity**.
Second generation also covers **education**, **health** and **eradication of social discrimination**.
Third generation: **healthy environment**, **development**, **peace**.
**ICESCR** covers work, social security, health, education — realised **progressively**.

n3d329417b1e.s: The International Bill of Human Rights comprises:
o: The ICCPR, ICESCR and the Vienna Declaration only
Only the UDHR and the ICCPR
The UDHR, UN Charter and International Court of Justice Statute
The UDHR, ICCPR, ICESCR and the optional protocols
n3d329417b1e.x: The International Bill of Human Rights consists of the UDHR, the ICCPR, the ICESCR and the optional protocols.
n3d329417b1e.tq: Test the complete composition of a named international instrument group.
xs: The **International Bill of Human Rights** = **UDHR + ICCPR + ICESCR + optional protocols** — option **(4)**.
The **Vienna Declaration** (1993) affirmed indivisibility; it is not part of the Bill.
xa: **ICESCR** in force **3 Jan 1976**; **ICCPR** in force **23 Mar 1976**.
**ICCPR First OP** (**1966**) — individual complaints; **Second OP** (**1989**) — abolition of the death penalty.
**ICESCR OP** (**2008**) — complaints.

nac54125d23c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about optional protocols in the International Bill of Human Rights?
o: The Optional Protocol to the ICESCR was adopted in 1976.
The First Optional Protocol to the ICCPR (1966) provides for individual complaints.
The Second Optional Protocol to the ICCPR (1989) aims at abolition of the death penalty.
The two Covenants entered into force in 1976.
nac54125d23c.x: The ICESCR Optional Protocol was adopted in 2008; 1976 is when the Covenants entered into force.
xa: India has **not signed the First Optional Protocol**.
So Indians cannot take complaints to the UN after exhausting domestic remedies.
⚠ ICESCR in force **Jan 1976**, ICCPR **Mar 1976**.

ndf2042fd018.s: India's position on the ICCPR and its First Optional Protocol is:
o: Not a party to the ICCPR at all
Party to the ICCPR since 1979 but has not signed the First Optional Protocol
Party to the ICCPR since 1979 and signatory to the First Optional Protocol
Party only to the Second Optional Protocol, not the ICCPR
ndf2042fd018.x: India has been a party to the ICCPR since 1979 but has not signed its First Optional Protocol, so its individual complaints procedure is unavailable.
xa: First OP (**1966**) — **individual complaints**; Second OP (**1989**) — **death penalty** abolition.
India has also **not ratified CAT** (signed **1997**).
ICCPR rights: **life (Art. 6)**, **fair trial (Art. 14)**, **privacy (Art. 17)**, **expression (Art. 19)**.

n1ec621ff0c5.s: The UN convention known as CPED deals with:
n1ec621ff0c5.x: CPED concerns enforced disappearance; CMW covers migrant workers, CRPD persons with disabilities and CAT torture.
xa: India: **CMW not signed**; **CPED signed 2007, not ratified**.
**CRPD** ratified **2007** → **RPwD Act, 2016**.
**CAT** (**1984**) — India **signed 1997, not ratified**.

nad699a3ccd7.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India’s position concerning CMW, CRPD and CPED?
o: CMW was ratified in 1990, CRPD was signed in 2007, and CPED was not signed.
CMW was not signed, CRPD was ratified in 2007, and CPED was signed in 2007 but not ratified.
CMW was acceded to in 1992, CRPD was ratified in 1993, and CPED was ratified in 2006.
CMW was signed in 1990, CRPD was not ratified, and CPED was acceded to in 2007.
nad699a3ccd7.x: India has not signed CMW; it ratified CRPD in 2007; and it signed CPED in 2007 but has not ratified it.
nad699a3ccd7.tq: Separate the statuses not signed, ratified and signed but not ratified.
xs: **CMW not signed**, **CRPD ratified 2007**, **CPED signed 2007 but not ratified** — option **(2)**.
The other options invent dates: CMW is from **1990** and CPED from **2006**, but India neither signed CMW nor ratified CPED.
xa: ⚠ Signed but not ratified: **CAT** and **CPED**; not signed: **CMW**.
**CRPD** gave rise to the **RPwD Act, 2016** — disabilities raised from **7 to 21**.
**CEDAW** (**1979**) — India **ratified 1993**.

n5d0cfcb389e.s: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 is associated with which treaty and what change in the number of recognised disabilities?
n5d0cfcb389e.x: The CRPD concerns persons with disabilities and gave rise to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, which raised recognised disabilities from 7 to 21.
n5d0cfcb389e.tq: Link the treaty, implementing legislation and numerical change as one factual chain.
xs: The **RPwD Act, 2016** flows from the **CRPD** and raised recognised disabilities **from 7 to 21** — option **(4)**.
**CPED** is on **enforced disappearance** and **CEDAW** on **discrimination against women**; option (1) reverses the numbers.
xa: CRPD adopted **2006**; India **ratified 2007**.
**CPED** (**2006**) — India **signed 2007, not ratified**.
**CMW** (**1990**, migrant workers) — India **not signed**.

nbca751cd3d6.s: How many seats does the Eastern European group hold in the UN Human Rights Council?
nbca751cd3d6.x: Eastern Europe has 6 seats; Africa and Asia-Pacific have 13 each and Latin America and the Caribbean 8.
xa: **Western Europe & Others**: **7** seats; total **47**.
**APPSC 2018** asked the **Asia-Pacific** seat count (**13**).
Members serve **3-year terms**, at most **two consecutive**.

n6b318ea81ba.s: Which 1993 document affirmed the indivisibility and interdependence of human rights?
n6b318ea81ba.x: The Vienna Declaration of 1993 affirmed that civil-political and socio-economic rights are indivisible and interdependent.
xa: Example: the **right to vote** is only a **statutory right** (**Sec 62, RP Act**).
**OHCHR** was set up in **1993**, after the **Vienna Conference**.
Human rights rest on **human dignity** and are **universal** across cultures.

nb3735c8ba04.s: The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights was set up in 1993 following the:
nb3735c8ba04.x: The OHCHR was established in 1993 after the Vienna Conference.
nb3735c8ba04.tq: Match the institution with the conference that preceded its establishment.
xs: **OHCHR** was set up in **1993**, after the **Vienna Conference** — option **(2)**.
The **Vienna Declaration, 1993** affirmed that rights are **indivisible and interdependent**.
xa: ⚠ **1993** = **OHCHR** + **Paris Principles** (UNGA) + **NHRC** (**12 Oct**).
**OHCHR 2026** convened the **Global Alliance for Human Rights** (Imagine-Dialogue-Act).
It looks ahead to the **UDHR's 80th anniversary (Dec 2028)**.

n767faa7fde7.s: The Paris Principles relating to national human rights institutions were adopted by the UN General Assembly in:
n767faa7fde7.x: The Paris Principles were adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1993.
n767faa7fde7.tq: Distinguish the adoption year of the institutional standards from treaty years.
xs: The **Paris Principles** were adopted by the **UNGA** in **1993** — option **(3)**.
**1968** is the start of the **UN Human Rights Prize**; **1977** is Vasak's generations; **2006** the **HRC**.
xa: ⚠ **1993** = OHCHR + Paris Principles + **NHRC (12 Oct)**.
Contents: **broad mandate in law**, **independence**, **pluralist composition**, **adequate resources**, **powers to investigate**.
**GANHRI** accredits NHRIs: **"A"** = fully compliant.

n5bfc5e61b61.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Paris Principles?
o: Exclusive dependence on the executive for investigations
A broad mandate set out in law
n5bfc5e61b61.x: The Paris Principles require independence and autonomy from government and powers to investigate; exclusive dependence on the executive is contrary to these requirements.
n5bfc5e61b61.tq: Find the option that reverses the institutional-independence requirement.
xs: **Exclusive dependence on the executive** is not a feature — option **(2)**.
The Paris Principles demand **independence and autonomy from government** and **powers to investigate**.
**Pluralist composition**, **adequate resources** and a **broad mandate set out in law** are features.
xa: Adopted by the **UNGA** in **1993**.
India's **NHRC** (**12 Oct 1993**) was set up in conformity with them.
**GANHRI**'s **Sub-Committee on Accreditation** grades NHRIs **"A"** or **"B"**.

nf12da1e86c6.s: The Magna Carta was issued in:
nf12da1e86c6.x: The Magna Carta dates to 1215, before the event of 1688, the Declaration of Independence (1776) and the French Revolution (1789).
xa: The **UDHR** followed much later — **10 December 1948**.
**Karel Vasak (1977)** later mapped rights to **liberty, equality and fraternity**.
**Vienna Declaration, 1993** — rights are **indivisible and interdependent**.

n442a3f1eb0b.x: CEDAW came in 1979, after the UDHR (1948) and ICCPR (1966).
xa: ICCPR in force **23 Mar 1976**; **ICESCR** in force **3 Jan 1976**.
India ratified **CEDAW** in **1993**.
India has been a **party to the ICCPR since 1979**.

nd6c6523acce.s: The National Human Rights Commission is a statutory body set up under the:
nd6c6523acce.x: The NHRC is a statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, set up in conformity with the Paris Principles; it is not a constitutional body.
xa: **2019 amendment**: term cut to **3 years**.
Three human-rights members required, **including a woman**.
⚠ **1993** = OHCHR + Paris Principles + NHRC.

n72ef83d388f.s: Amnesty International was founded in 1961 in:
n72ef83d388f.x: Amnesty International was founded in London in 1961 and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977; the New York-based body is Human Rights Watch.
xa: Amnesty focuses on **prisoners of conscience**.
Amnesty called Afghanistan's new police law **"a sweeping assault on human rights"**.
HRW criticised the **Taliban's ban on all protests**.

n4233d6bbcd8.s: In Karel Vasak's classification, the eradication of social discrimination falls under which generation of rights?
n4233d6bbcd8.x: Eradication of social discrimination is grouped with work, education and health as a second-generation (equality) right.
xa: ⚠ **1st – 2nd – 3rd = liberty – equality – fraternity**.
Generations **overlap** — **education** is both second- and third-generation.
Classification by **Karel Vasak (1977)**.

n36fae71c8fe.s: Article 21 of the Indian Constitution corresponds to which Article of the UDHR?
n36fae71c8fe.x: Article 21 corresponds to UDHR Article 3; Article 14 matches UDHR Article 7, Article 32 Article 8 and Article 23 Article 4.
xa: **Art. 19** freedoms parallel UDHR **Arts. 13, 19, 20, 23**.
**Art. 23** also bans **bonded labour**.

ncf3922cb765.s: Which one of the following Fundamental Rights is available to both citizens and foreigners?
o: Article 30 right of minorities to establish educational institutions
Article 29 protection of language and script of citizens
Article 21 protection of life and personal liberty
ncf3922cb765.x: Articles 14, 20, 21, 23 and 25 to 28 are available to citizens and foreigners alike. Article 19 is available only to citizens.
ncf3922cb765.tq: Separate citizen-specific freedoms from rights available to every person.
xs: **Art. 21** (life and personal liberty) is available to **citizens and foreigners alike** — option **(4)**.
Arts. **14, 20, 21, 23, 25-28** cover foreigners too; **Arts. 19, 29, 30** are not in that list.
xa: Art. 21 parallels **UDHR Art. 3**.
**Art. 23** bans traffic in human beings, begar and forced labour — also for foreigners.
SC: "a person does not become a **non-person** after going to jail".

nb92c8c8f382.s: Bonded labour is constitutionally prohibited under:
nb92c8c8f382.x: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings, begar and other similar forms of forced labour, including bonded labour.
nb92c8c8f382.tq: Distinguish the constitutional prohibition of forced labour from neighbouring Articles concerning life, child labour and remedies.
xs: **Bonded labour** is prohibited under **Article 23** — option **(3)**.
Art. 23 bans **traffic in human beings, begar and forced labour**; it parallels **UDHR Art. 4**.
**Art. 24** bars child labour below **14**; **Art. 21** is life and liberty; **Art. 32** is constitutional remedies.
xa: Art. 23 is available to **foreigners** too.
**Art. 24** parallels UDHR **Arts. 4, 25(2)**.
**Art. 43** (DPSP): **living wage**.

n9a53bacd16b.s: Under the stated Transgender Persons Amendment Act, 2026, the identity certificate is issued by the:
n9a53bacd16b.x: The District Magistrate issues the certificate on a medical board's recommendation; self-perceived identity is excluded.
xa: Another group-specific law: the **Manual Scavengers Act, 2013**.
Human rights under **PHRA** relate to **life, liberty, equality and dignity**.
**Art. 14**: equality before law and equal protection.

nindian-polity-2-7.s:
1. Article 14
2. Article 32
3. Article 40
Which of the above Articles deal with Fundamental Rights?
nindian-polity-2-7.x: Articles 14 and 32 are Fundamental Rights in Part III; Article 40 (village panchayats) is a Directive Principle in Part IV.
n: Article 14 provides equality before law. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 21 protects life and personal liberty. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 32 provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 40 concerns the organisation of Village Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
xa: **Article 14**: **equality before law**; **Article 21**: **life and personal liberty**.
**Article 32**: **Right to Constitutional Remedies**.
**Article 21A** (**86th Amendment**): **Right to Education**.

nindian-polity-27-7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the mechanisms under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993?
o: The NHRC functions at the State level.
The NHRC functions at the national level.
SHRCs function at the State level.
Human Rights Courts provide a district-level mechanism for speedy trials.
nindian-polity-27-7.x: The NHRC is a national body; State-level work is done by the SHRCs.
n: The NHRC operates at the national level under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) operates at the state level under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
Human Rights Courts provide a district- or trial-level mechanism for speedy trials. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
xa: **Sec. 31**: an advocate of **not less than 7 years** may be a **Special Public Prosecutor**.
Human Rights Courts are notified by the State Govt **with concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court**.

nindian-polity-16-6.s: Abolition of Untouchability is provided under which Article?
nindian-polity-16-6.x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability; Article 14 is equality before law and Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings.
n: Article 14 provides equality before law. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 40-42]
Article 17 abolishes untouchability. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 40-42]
Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 40-42]
Article 28 provides freedom from attending religious instruction in certain educational institutions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 40-42]
xa: **Article 18** abolishes **titles**.
Citizens and foreigners alike enjoy Arts. **14, 20, 21, 23, 25-28**.
**Articles 29 and 30**: minorities' cultural and educational rights.

nindian-society-32-17.s:
1. Right to work
2. Right to education
3. Right to social security
Which of the above are economic and social rights in the UDHR?
nindian-society-32-17.x: Work, education and social security (along with health) are all economic and social rights in the UDHR.
xa: Other rights recognized: **right to life**, **freedom of speech**, **freedom of religion**, **equality before law**.
**Art. 41** (DPSP): work, education, public assistance; **Art. 43**: **living wage**.
⚠ **42** = maternity relief; **43** = living wage.

nindian-polity-2-18.s: Which Article of the Constitution defines the 'State' for the Fundamental Rights?
nindian-polity-2-18.x: Article 12 defines 'State'; Article 15 prohibits discrimination and Article 18 abolishes titles.
n: Article 12 defines “State” for the purpose of Fundamental Rights. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 15 prohibits discrimination. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 16 provides equality of opportunity in public employment. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
Article 18 abolishes titles. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 6-12]
xa: **Article 17** abolishes **untouchability**.

n07f1fef4a4f.s: Which Directive Principle provides for a living wage for workers?
n07f1fef4a4f.x: Article 43 provides for a living wage; 39(a) covers livelihood, 39(d) equal pay and 42 humane work conditions and maternity relief.
xa: ⚠ **42 = maternity relief**; **43 = living wage**.
**Art. 41** — **work, education, public assistance**.
These DPSPs reflect the **social-economic rights of the ICESCR**.

n0f146d391f9.s: Which Fundamental Duty is specifically related to protecting the dignity of women?
n0f146d391f9.x: Article 51A(e) requires citizens to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
n0f146d391f9.tq: Distinguish the women’s-dignity duty from environmental and education-related duties.
xs: **Article 51A(e)** requires citizens to **renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women** — option **(1)**.
It is a **Fundamental Duty** (FD), one of the places where **UDHR** values are reflected.
xa: UDHR principles are reflected in the **Preamble, DPSPs and Fundamental Duties** (UPSC **2020**).
**Vishaka (1997)** relied on **CEDAW** for workplace harassment guidelines.
**Art. 42** provides **maternity relief**.

nf748ecec0ef.s: Which Article empowers Parliament to make laws for implementing international treaties and agreements?
nf748ecec0ef.x: Article 253 empowers Parliament to legislate for implementing treaties; Article 51(c) only directs respect for international law.
xa: ⚠ **253 = treaty laws**.
**Guruvayur Devaswom (2003)**: courts may rely on **international conventions**.
**Vishaka (1997)** relied on **CEDAW**.

n924c1f6202d.s: The Vishaka guidelines on workplace sexual harassment relied substantially on:
n924c1f6202d.x: In Vishaka (1997), the Supreme Court relied on CEDAW to frame workplace-harassment guidelines.
xa: ⚠ **1997** = **Vishaka** (CEDAW) and **D.K. Basu** (arrest safeguards).
**Guruvayur Devaswom (2003)**: PIL principles let courts rely on international conventions.
**Art. 253**: Parliament may legislate to implement treaties.

n796b083a612.s: In which 2003 case did PIL principles enable courts to rely on international conventions?
n796b083a612.x: The principles of public interest litigation enabled courts to rely on international conventions in Guruvayur Devaswom (2003).
xa: **Art. 253**: **Parliament** legislates to implement treaties.
**D.K. Basu (1997)** — arrest safeguards.
India is a party to the **ICCPR since 1979**.

ncb8ba62632c.s: The NCPCR, set up in 2007, works in line with which international instrument?
ncb8ba62632c.x: The NCPCR was set up in 2007 and works in line with the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC).
xa: **CEDAW** — relied on in **Vishaka (1997)**.
India has **not signed the ICCPR First Optional Protocol**.
**Art. 24**: no child below **14** in factories, mines, hazardous work.

nd6e4690f3cd.s: The expression ‘International Covenants’ under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 refers to
nd6e4690f3cd.x: The Act defines International Covenants as the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights.
nd6e4690f3cd.tq: Discriminate between covenants, declaration and institutional principles.
xs: Under **Sec. 2(1)(f)**, "International Covenants" = the **ICCPR and ICESCR** — option **(1)**.
The **UDHR** is a declaration, not a covenant; the **Paris Principles** guide NHRIs.
xa: Both were adopted by the UNGA on **16 Dec 1966**.
**Sec. 2(1)(d)**: human rights = rights to **life, liberty, equality and dignity**.
India is party to the **ICCPR since 1979**.

nadb3c2aecda.s: The arrest safeguards laid down in D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal relate primarily to:
o: Recognition of the right to livelihood
Protection of persons during arrest and custodial detention
nadb3c2aecda.x: D.K. Basu (1997) laid down safeguards intended to prevent custodial abuse and protect persons during arrest and detention.
nadb3c2aecda.tq: Associate the case with its precise subject instead of the broader category of human-rights litigation.
xs: **D.K. Basu (1997)** laid down **arrest safeguards** — protection of persons during **arrest and custodial detention**, option **(4)**.
**CEDAW** guidelines came from **Vishaka**; manual scavengers are covered by the **2013** Act.
xa: ⚠ **1997** = **Vishaka** and **D.K. Basu**.
SC: a person does not become a **non-person** after going to jail.
**Guruvayur Devaswom (2003)** — courts may rely on international conventions.

n670d0a5f9cf.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the dates associated with the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993?
n670d0a5f9cf.x: The Ordinance was issued on 28 September 1993, while the NHRC was constituted on 12 October 1993.
n670d0a5f9cf.tq: Separate closely related dates by placing the event against its proper sequence.
xs: **Ordinance: 28 Sept 1993**; **NHRC constituted: 12 October 1993** — option **(2)**.
Option (1) swaps the two; **20 Dec 1993** is the **UNGA endorsement** of the Paris Principles.
xa: The Act is deemed in force from **28 September 1993**.
⚠ Ordinance/in force **28 Sept**; NHRC **12 Oct 1993**.
Objective: **NHRC + SHRCs + Human Rights Courts**.

n6ed5f2d693c.s: The National Human Rights Commission was constituted in conformity with the Paris Principles, which were adopted in Paris in
n6ed5f2d693c.x: The Paris Principles were adopted in Paris in October 1991. They were endorsed by the UN General Assembly on 20 December 1993.
n6ed5f2d693c.tq: Distinguish adoption of an international standard from its later UN endorsement.
xs: The **Paris Principles** were adopted in **Paris** in **October 1991** — option **(1)**.
The **UNGA** endorsed them on **20 Dec 1993**; September 1993 is the PHRA Ordinance date.
xa: The **NHRC** (**12 October 1993**) was set up in conformity with them.
**16 Dec 1966** — adoption of the **ICCPR and ICESCR**.
**NHRC advice is non-binding** — a criticism.

nindian-polity-27-3.s: The National Human Rights Commission of India is a:
o: Executive body set up by Cabinet resolution
nindian-polity-27-3.x: The NHRC is statutory, not constitutional, because it was created by the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
n: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) is a statutory and independent body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The NHRC was established under the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The NHRC is a statutory body and not a constitutional body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The NHRC and the SHRC are governed by the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
xa: The PHRA was effective **28 September 1993**; NHRC set up on **12 October 1993**.
It conforms to the **Paris Principles**.
The Act also created **SHRCs** and **Human Rights Courts**.

n2dfea873264.s: Under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, Human Rights Courts are provided for in:
n2dfea873264.x: Section 30 deals with Human Rights Courts; Section 31 covers Special Public Prosecutors, Section 3 the NHRC and Section 21 the SHRC.
xa: Public servant: **Sec. 21 IPC** → now **Sec. 2(28) BNS** (from **1 July 2024**).
Sec. 31: advocate in practice for **not less than 7 years**.

n0e1aabe57e2.s: Under the PHRA, 1993, 'human rights' are rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity that are:
o: Recognised only as civil and political rights in the UDHR
Guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in International Covenants and enforceable by Indian courts
n0e1aabe57e2.x: The statutory definition covers rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in International Covenants and enforceable by Indian courts.
xa: International Covenants = **ICCPR and ICESCR**.
NHRC constituted **12 October 1993**.

n6485e3d1c38.s: Under Section 2(1)(a) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, which of the following is NOT included in the expression 'armed forces'?
o: Other armed forces of the Union
n6485e3d1c38.x: The Act defines armed forces as the naval, military and air forces and includes any other armed forces of the Union. State armed police are expressly not included, so complaints against them fall under the Commission's ordinary jurisdiction.
n6485e3d1c38.tq: Armed forces = Union forces only; State armed police excluded.
xs: **State armed police** are **not included** in "armed forces" — option **(4)**.
**Sec. 2(1)(a)**: armed forces = **naval, military and air forces**, including **other armed forces of the Union**.
xa: **Sec. 2(1)(d)** defines human rights — **life, liberty, equality and dignity**.
**Sec. 39**: members and officers deemed **public servants**.
**Sec. 3 / 21**: constitution of **NHRC / SHRC**.

n7b627dc4d1e.s: A Court of Session is notified as a Human Rights Court by the State Government with the concurrence of the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
n7b627dc4d1e.x: Under Section 30, the State Government needs the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court, not the Chief Justice of India.
xa: **Sec. 31**: **Special Public Prosecutor** — a Public Prosecutor or advocate of **not less than 7 years**.
The Act's objective: **NHRC + SHRCs + Human Rights Courts**.
Commission has **civil court powers under CPC 1908**.

n0777190ee51.s: During an inquiry, the Human Rights Commission has the powers of a civil court under the CPC, 1908 for:
o: Reviewing judgments of the High Courts
Awarding imprisonment to guilty public servants
n0777190ee51.x: The Commission has civil-court powers such as summons, requiring documents, receiving affidavits and requisitioning public records; it has no sentencing powers.
xa: Proceedings are deemed **judicial** for false evidence (**s.193**) and insulting a public servant (**s.228**).
Since **1 July 2024** these read as the corresponding **BNS/BNSS** provisions.
**NHRC advice is non-binding** — a common criticism.

n033e6bed586.s: Proceedings of a Human Rights Commission are deemed judicial proceedings for offences relating to:
o: Bribery and criminal breach of trust
False evidence and insulting a public servant in judicial proceedings
n033e6bed586.x: They are deemed judicial proceedings for false evidence (IPC 193) and insulting a public servant in judicial proceedings (IPC 228); corresponding BNS provisions apply from 1 July 2024.
xa: **Civil court powers under CPC 1908**: summons, documents, affidavits, public records.
**Sec. 39**: members and officers are **public servants** (**Sec. 2(28) BNS**).
**Sec. 30**: **Human Rights Courts** for speedy trial.

nfad483ed2ec.s: Under the Manual Scavengers Act, 2013, local bodies must survey and build sanitary latrines within:
nfad483ed2ec.x: Local bodies must do so within three years; the Act also bans cleaning sewers and septic tanks without protective gear.
xa: **Art. 23** bans **traffic in human beings, begar and forced labour**.
Transgender persons **Amendment Act 2026**: **District Magistrate** issues certificate on a **medical board's** recommendation.
FD **51A(e)**: renounce practices derogatory to women's dignity.

nindian-polity-27-8.s: Under the statutory procedure concerning the armed forces, what does the NHRC do?
o: It calls for an independent report from the Central Government and makes recommendations based on that report
It transfers every complaint to the SHRC for investigation
It directly imposes criminal sentencing on members of the armed forces
It directly investigates all complaints without restriction
nindian-polity-27-8.x: For the armed forces, the NHRC cannot investigate directly. It asks the Central Government for a report and makes recommendations on it.
nindian-polity-27-8.tq: Recall the NHRC's limited role over the armed forces.
n: The NHRC does not directly execute criminal sentencing. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The NHRC does not have direct or unrestricted investigative powers over the armed forces. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
Under the statutory procedure, the NHRC calls for an independent report from the Central Government regarding the armed forces. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The NHRC makes recommendations based on the report from the Central Government. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
xs: For the **armed forces**, the NHRC **calls for an independent report from the Central Government** and **makes recommendations** — option **(1)**.
It has **no direct or unrestricted investigative** powers over them.
It does **not** execute **criminal sentencing**; its recommendations are **advisory**.
xa: **Armed forces** = **naval**, **military** and **air** forces and other Union armed forces.
⚠ Sources differ on the section: **Section 2(m)** vs **Sec. 2(1)(a)**.
**State armed police** are **not included** in "armed forces".

nindian-society-32-3.s: Which value lies at the core of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
nindian-society-32-3.x: The UDHR was drafted after the atrocities of the Second World War to protect human dignity, which is at its core.
n: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was prepared after the atrocities of World War II. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 67-70]
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was prepared to safeguard human dignity. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 67-70]
Human dignity is at the core of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 67-70]
xa: Adopted by the **UNGA** on **10 December 1948**; **30 articles**.
UDHR is reflected in India's **Preamble, DPSPs and Fundamental Duties** (**UPSC 2020**).

nindian-polity-22-46.s: The Right to Information Act came into force on:
nindian-polity-22-46.x: The RTI Act got assent on 15 June 2005 and took effect on 12 October 2005, after 120 days.
n: The Right to Information Act received assent on 15 June 2005. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Right to Information Act became effective on 12 October 2005. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Namit Sharma Case was decided in 2012 in relation to the Right to Information Act. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Right to Information Act is rooted in the MKSS movement. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
xa: RTI supports **transparency** and **accountability**.
**Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act**: **2005**, enforced **26 October 2006**.
**National Green Tribunal Act**: **2010**.

n286b354ccd0.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the legal status of the National Human Rights Commission?
o: A statutory body created under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
A constitutional body established directly under Part III of the Constitution
A judicial body created by the Supreme Court in 1993
An executive body created by a resolution of the Union Cabinet in 1994
n286b354ccd0.x: The NHRC is a statutory body created under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; it is not a constitutional body.
n286b354ccd0.tq: Distinguish statutory status from constitutional status and identify the enabling legislation.
xs: The **NHRC** is a **statutory body** created under the **Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993** — option **(1)**.
It is **not a constitutional body**, nor a judicial or Cabinet-created body; "constitutional body" and "established 1994" are both wrong (**APPSC 2023**).
xa: It conforms to the **Paris Principles**.
⚠ NHRC (statutory) vs **UPSC/CAG** (constitutional) — the most repeated classification question.
The **NCM** is also statutory (**NCM Act 1992**).

n33f8c46f906.s: The establishment of the NHRC conforms to the
n33f8c46f906.x: The NHRC was established in conformity with the Paris Principles relating to national institutions for the promotion and protection of human rights.
n33f8c46f906.tq: Match the institution with the exact international principles associated with its status and functioning.
xs: The NHRC conforms to the **Paris Principles** — option **(2)**.
They are UNGA (**1993**) standards of **independence, pluralism and broad mandate** for national human-rights institutions.
xa: The **PHRA, 1993** was framed in their light.
**GANHRI** accredits NHRIs as **"A"** (fully compliant) or **"B"** based on conformity with them.
NHRC constituted **12 October 1993**.

n7d8f47bf80c.s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission?
n7d8f47bf80c.x: Justice Ranganath Misra was the first Chairperson of the NHRC, constituted on 12 October 1993.
xa: Ordinance: **28 Sept 1993**.
Present Chairperson: **Justice V. Ramasubramanian**.
⚠ "NHRC is a **constitutional body**" is also false (**APPSC-GS 2023**).

n0c0b27f2564.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Paris Principles?
o: They prescribe the procedure for prosecuting custodial deaths before Human Rights Courts.
They prescribe standards of independence, pluralism and a broad mandate for national human-rights institutions.
They establish the jurisdiction of State Human Rights Commissions over Union Territories.
They classify national human-rights institutions as A or B categories.
n0c0b27f2564.x: The Paris Principles, adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1993, set standards of independence, pluralism and a broad mandate for national human-rights institutions.
n0c0b27f2564.tq: Match the international principles with their institutional purpose, not with accreditation labels or domestic jurisdiction.
xs: The **Paris Principles** prescribe standards of **independence, pluralism and a broad mandate** for **national human-rights institutions** — option **(2)**.
They were adopted by the **UN General Assembly** in **1993**; the **A/B** grading is done by **GANHRI**, not the Principles.
xa: The **PHRA, 1993** was framed in their light.
**GANHRI** accredits NHRIs as **"A"** (fully compliant) or **"B"**.
UT functions of SHRCs are conferred by the **Central Government** (**2019**) — unrelated to the Principles.

n417cdd6136f.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the constitutional status of the institutions listed below?
o: NHRC is statutory, whereas UPSC and CAG are constitutional bodies.
NHRC and UPSC are constitutional, whereas CAG is statutory.
NHRC, UPSC and CAG are all statutory bodies.
NHRC is constitutional, whereas UPSC and CAG are statutory.
n417cdd6136f.x: The NHRC is a statutory body, while the Union Public Service Commission and the Comptroller and Auditor General are constitutional bodies.
n417cdd6136f.tq: Split the options by classification and watch for the statutory–constitutional reversal.
xs: The **NHRC is statutory**, whereas **UPSC and CAG** are **constitutional** — option **(1)**.
This is the **most repeated classification question**.
xa: The NHRC was created by the **PHRA, 1993**.
"NHRC is a constitutional body" was keyed **false** in **APPSC-GS 2023**.
The **NCM** is also statutory (**NCM Act 1992**).

na8162bb1143.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the composition of the NHRC?
o: It includes one former or serving Judge of the Supreme Court.
At least one woman must be among its human-rights experts.
It includes one former or serving Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court.
It includes two persons having knowledge of human rights.
na8162bb1143.x: The NHRC includes three persons with knowledge of human rights, at least one of whom must be a woman.
xa: Chairperson: former **CJI or SC Judge**.
Deemed members: chairpersons of **NCM, NCSC, NCST, NCW** + (2019) **NCBC, NCPCR, CCPD**.
Appointment by the **President** on a **PM-led six-member committee's** recommendation.

neade652781c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about deemed members of the NHRC?
o: The NCSC and NCST Chairpersons became deemed members through the 2006 amendment.
Only the Chairpersons of the commissions concerned are deemed members.
A deemed member is identical in status to an ordinary NHRC member.
The NCBC Chairperson was added as a deemed member in 2019.
neade652781c.x: The deemed-member provision does not convert the Chairpersons into ordinary NHRC members.
xa: Before 2019: **4** deemed members; after 2019: **7**.
2019 additions: **NCBC**, **NCPCR**, **Chief Commissioner for PwDs**.
The 2006 amendment also cut SHRC size from **five to three**.

n26c6030c25b.s: A sitting Judge of the Supreme Court or a sitting Chief Justice of a High Court can be appointed to the NHRC only after consultation with the
n26c6030c25b.x: Appointment of a sitting Supreme Court Judge or a sitting High Court Chief Justice requires consultation with the Chief Justice of India.
n26c6030c25b.tq: Test the mandatory consultation requirement by asking which authority is specifically associated with judicial appointments.
xs: A sitting **SC judge** or **HC Chief Justice** is appointed only **after consulting the Chief Justice of India** — option **(1)**.
The CJI is consulted but is **not** on the selection committee.
xa: For an SHRC, a sitting HC judge or district judge needs consultation with the **Chief Justice of the High Court**.
Selection committee: **PM** (chair), **Speaker**, **Deputy Chairman of RS**, **LoPs** of both Houses, **Home Minister**.
Appointment is by the **President** (APPSC **2025**).

nd2614e83c39.s: A member of the NHRC submits a written resignation during the tenure of office. To whom should it be addressed?
nd2614e83c39.x: A Chairperson or member of the NHRC resigns by writing addressed to the President of India.
nd2614e83c39.tq: In an authority-based scenario, ask who receives the formal resignation rather than who recommends the appointment.
xs: An NHRC member resigns in writing **to the President of India** — option **(1)**.
SHRC members resign **to the Governor** (both under the **2006 amendment**).
xa: The **President** also appoints and removes NHRC members.
Term: **3 years or age 70**, whichever earlier.
After office: **ineligible for further employment** under Centre or States.

n60d1a2cb165.s: For removal of the NHRC Chairperson on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, the President refers the matter to the:
n60d1a2cb165.x: The President refers such cases to the Supreme Court for inquiry; grounds like insolvency allow direct removal by the President.
xa: SHRC members too are **removable only by the President** on the same grounds.
Resignation: NHRC → **President**; SHRC → **Governor**.
Appointment: **President** on a **PM-led** committee's recommendation.

n48837ee3ece.s: After demitting office, the Chairperson or a member of the NHRC is
o: eligible for employment under either the Central or State Government without restriction
ineligible for further employment under the Central or any State Government
eligible for any post under the Central Government but not under a State Government
eligible only for judicial employment under the Central Government
n48837ee3ece.x: The Chairperson and members are not eligible for further employment under the Central Government or any State Government after leaving office.
n48837ee3ece.tq: Watch for the reversed distinction between post-tenure ineligibility and eligibility for government employment.
xs: After office the Chairperson or member is **ineligible for further employment** under the **Central or any State Government** — option **(2)**.
However, they are **eligible for reappointment** to the Commission.
xa: Term: **3 years or age 70** (since **2019**).
⚠ "Member is not eligible for re-appointment" is the **wrong** statement (MPPSC).
The **5-year reappointment limit** was removed in 2019.

na6648b72c37.s: The Chairperson and members of the NHRC are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee headed by the Prime Minister. Which one of the following is NOT a member of that committee?
o: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
na6648b72c37.x: The six-member committee is the Prime Minister (chair), Speaker of the Lok Sabha, Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, Leaders of Opposition in both Houses and the Union Home Minister. The Chief Justice of India is not a member; he is only consulted before a sitting SC Judge or HC Chief Justice is appointed.
na6648b72c37.tq: Appointed by President; PM-led 6-member committee; CJI only consulted.
xs: The **Chief Justice of India** is not a member of the committee — option **(4)**.
The committee: **PM** (chair), **Speaker of Lok Sabha**, **Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha**, **Leaders of Opposition** in both Houses, **Union Home Minister**.
The CJI is only **consulted** before a sitting SC judge or HC Chief Justice is appointed.
xa: SHRC committee: **CM** (chair), Assembly **Speaker**, **State Home Minister**, **LoP**; plus Council Chairman and LoP in bicameral States.
A **vacancy** in the committee does not invalidate its decisions.
Members are **removed by the President**.

ncd75ca7a4b1.s: The Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission can be removed only by the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
ncd75ca7a4b1.x: The Governor appoints the SHRC Chairperson, but only the President can remove them.
xa: Resignation is addressed **to the Governor** (**2006**).
Selection committee is headed by the **Chief Minister**.
⚠ Both NHRC and SHRC chairs are **removed by the President**.

nefe56dc419b.s: The selection committee for a State Human Rights Commission is headed by the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
nefe56dc419b.x: The Chief Minister chairs it, with the Speaker, State Home Minister and Leader of Opposition; the High Court Chief Justice is only consulted.
xa: SHRC members are **appointed by the Governor**.
On a vacancy, the **Governor** may authorise a member to act as Chairperson.
A **vacancy** in a committee does not invalidate its decisions.

n01de553b8bd.s: After the 2006 amendment, a State Human Rights Commission consists of how many members, including the Chairperson?
n01de553b8bd.x: The 2006 amendment reduced it from five to three: the Chairperson, a judicial member and a person with human-rights knowledge or experience.
xa: SHRC chair: former **HC Chief Justice or Judge** (since **2019**).
The 2006 amendment also enabled the NHRC to **transfer complaints** to SHRCs.
SHRCs in rich States get only **80 paisa per capita**; several have **over 40% vacancies**.

n246a16f4a29.s: A State Human Rights Commission inquires into violations relating to subjects in the:
n246a16f4a29.x: An SHRC covers the State and Concurrent Lists; the NHRC covers all subjects.
xa: **UTs (2019)**: the **Central Government may confer** a UT's functions on an SHRC; **Delhi** is handled by the NHRC.
An SHRC will **not inquire** into a case already before the NHRC or another statutory commission.
The **2006 amendment** lets the NHRC **transfer complaints** to SHRCs.

n67a54ee4dc3.s: Which of the following is correct about overlapping complaints before the NHRC and an SHRC?
o: An SHRC may inquire into a case already pending before the NHRC.
The NHRC may take up a matter pending before an SHRC.
The NHRC and an SHRC may inquire simultaneously into the same matter.
An SHRC will not inquire into a case already being inquired into by another statutory commission.
n67a54ee4dc3.x: The arrangement bars simultaneous inquiry by the SHRC, NHRC or another statutory commission into the same pending matter.
xa: The **2006 amendment** enabled the NHRC to **transfer complaints** to the concerned SHRC.
Matters **sub judice** are not taken up.
The NHRC's purview is limited to violations by **public servants**.

n79e4c068c0a.s: The NHRC cannot inquire into a matter after how long from the date of the alleged act?
n79e4c068c0a.x: The NHRC is barred after one year from the alleged act; a review committee wanted this relaxed where sufficient cause exists.
xa: The **SHRC** is subject to the same **one-year bar**.
⚠ Action taken: **one month** (general) vs **three months** (armed forces).
The time bar is part of the "**toothless tiger**" criticism.
