nb75785dd2d5.x: GANHRI accredits national human-rights institutions ('A' for fully compliant, 'B' for others), based on independence and effectiveness.
xa: Paris Principles: UNGA, **1993**.
The **NHRC** was set up in conformity with the Paris Principles.
The NHRC is a **statutory body** under the **PHRA, 1993**.

n61b8585149e.s: In the Gade Sai Krishna custodial-death case, the NHRC directed which combination of authorities to submit a report?
o: The Union Home Ministry, DGP and District Collector
The State Election Commission, DGP and Chief Justice of the High Court
The Governor, Speaker and Advocate-General of Andhra Pradesh
The Andhra Pradesh SHRC, DGP and Chief Secretary
n61b8585149e.x: In the Gade Sai Krishna case, the NHRC directed the Andhra Pradesh SHRC, the Director General of Police and the Chief Secretary to report.
n61b8585149e.tq: Use the authority-and-function trap by distinguishing reporting authorities from constitutional offices.
xs: The NHRC directed the **AP SHRC**, **DGP** and **Chief Secretary** to report — option **(4)**.
It took cognisance of the alleged **custodial death** of **Gade Sai Krishna** (**28 Jun 2026**).
xa: Reports were sought **within a week**.
Custodial deaths must be reported to the NHRC within **24 hours**.
Other safeguards: **post-mortem videography**, **independent investigation**.

nb07896552c3.s: Under the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019, reappointment of NHRC members:
o: is limited to the Chairperson for one further term
is barred after the first term
is permitted, the earlier five-year limit having been removed
needs a compulsory gap of five years
nb07896552c3.x: The 2019 amendment removed the earlier five-year limit, so members remain eligible for reappointment, subject to the 3-year/70 term.
xa: Term after 2019: **3 years or 70**.
⚠ "Member is not eligible for re-appointment" is the wrong statement (MPPSC).
After office: **ineligible for further government employment**.

nd397821f71e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019?
o: It reduced the term of NHRC members to three years or the age of 70.
It allowed a former High Court Judge to be SHRC Chairperson.
It raised the deemed members of the NHRC from four to seven.
It made members ineligible for reappointment.
nd397821f71e.x: The 2019 amendment removed the five-year limit on reappointment, so members remain eligible for reappointment.
xa: The **2019** amendment also raised human-rights members to **three**, at least **one woman**.
NHRC chair: former **CJI or SC Judge** (earlier only former CJI).
The **2006** amendment cut SHRC size from **five to three**.

ne6f8bf0cff8.s: The NHRC can intervene in court proceedings involving human-rights allegations with the approval of the:
ne6f8bf0cff8.x: It needs the approval of the court concerned, not the Central Government.
xa: Since 2006 it may also recommend **interim relief even during inquiry**.
2006 also enabled the NHRC to **transfer complaints** to the concerned SHRC.
Custodial deaths must be reported within **24 hours**.

n804b54c0087.s: With reference to the Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission, which one of the following is correct?
o: He resigns by writing addressed to the Governor and holds office for 3 years or till 70, whichever is earlier.
He resigns by writing addressed to the President and holds office for 5 years or till 65.
He resigns by writing addressed to the Chief Minister and holds office for 3 years or till 70.
He resigns by writing addressed to the Chief Justice of the High Court and holds office for 5 years or till 70.
n804b54c0087.x: Since 2006 the SHRC Chairperson resigns in writing to the Governor, and since 2019 the term is 3 years or 70, whichever is earlier. The President only removes (and receives NHRC resignations); the Chief Minister heads the selection committee; the High Court Chief Justice is only consulted on sitting judges.
n804b54c0087.tq: SHRC: appointed by Governor, resigns to Governor, removed by President.
xs: The SHRC chair resigns **in writing to the Governor** and holds office for **3 years or till 70**, whichever earlier — option **(1)**.
The **President** receives **NHRC** resignations; **5 years** was the pre-**2019** term.
xa: Resignation rule from the **2006 amendment**; term rule from **2019**.
Removal of the SHRC chair is **only by the President**.
The **CM** heads the selection committee; the HC Chief Justice is only consulted.

n8d51c348a48.s: The 2006 amendment to the Protection of Human Rights Act enabled the NHRC to:
o: Convert every district court into a Human Rights Court
Transfer all NHRC members to State service
Transfer complaints to the concerned SHRC
n8d51c348a48.x: The 2006 amendment enabled the NHRC to transfer complaints to the concerned State Human Rights Commission.
n8d51c348a48.tq: Identify the precise transfer power and reject broader institutional powers not stated in the law.
xs: The **2006 amendment** enabled the NHRC to **transfer complaints** to the concerned **SHRC** — option **(4)**.
It gave no power to dissolve SHRCs or move members; **Human Rights Courts** are notified by the State Govt under the PHRA.
xa: Other 2006 changes: **NCSC and NCST** chairs as deemed members; jail visits **without intimating the State Govt**.
Also: **interim relief** even **during inquiry**; SHRC cut from **five to three**.
Resignation: NHRC → **President**, SHRC → **Governor**.

nindian-polity-27-5.s: Which of the following is a power of the NHRC?
o: Visiting jails to study inmates' living conditions
Unrestricted investigation of the armed forces
nindian-polity-27-5.x: The NHRC may visit jails and has civil-court powers, but its recommendations are advisory and it cannot directly investigate the armed forces.
n: The NHRC has all the powers of a civil court while inquiring into complaints. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The NHRC visits jails and detention centres to study the living conditions of inmates. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The recommendations of the NHRC are advisory in nature. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The recommendations of the NHRC are recommendatory in nature. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The NHRC does not directly execute criminal sentencing. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The NHRC does not have direct or unrestricted investigative powers over the armed forces. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The NHRC suggests reforms based on its study of jail and detention-centre conditions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
The NHRC does not act as a regular court of law. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 68-70]
xa: **Time bar**: no inquiry **after one year** from the alleged act.
⚠ Action taken: **one month** (general) vs **three months** (armed forces).
Since **2006**, NHRC may visit jails **even without intimating the State Govt**.

n8107517521e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about how the NHRC may take up an inquiry?
o: It may take suo motu cognisance.
It may inquire into a complaint solely against a private individual with no public servant involved.
It may act on a petition presented to it.
It may act on a direction of a court.
n8107517521e.x: The NHRC's jurisdiction concerns violations or negligence by public servants, so a purely private complaint is outside it.
xa: It may **intervene** in court proceedings with the **court's approval**.
Time bar: no inquiry **after one year** from the alleged act.
Sub judice matters are not taken up.

n8252e514389.s: While inquiring into complaints, the NHRC has the powers of a:
n8252e514389.x: The NHRC has civil-court powers such as summoning persons, examining them on oath, requiring documents and requisitioning public records.
xa: It can also **receive evidence on affidavit**.
The **SHRC** has the same inquiry powers.
Yet it has **no power to punish** violators.

n8bc0c7bc4f6.s: With respect to relief, the National Human Rights Commission may:
o: Grant relief only after a criminal court records conviction
Recommend compensation and interim relief, including during the inquiry
Punish the public servant and recover the amount directly
Award final compensation in every case without recommendation
n8bc0c7bc4f6.x: The NHRC may recommend compensation, prosecution and interim relief. Since the 2006 amendment, it may recommend interim relief even during the inquiry.
n8bc0c7bc4f6.tq: Apply the distinction between recommending relief and directly awarding or enforcing it.
xs: The NHRC may **recommend compensation and interim relief**, including **during the inquiry** — option **(2)** (since **2006**).
It cannot itself **punish** or award final compensation; it only recommends.
xa: It may also recommend **prosecution**.
Government must inform it of **action taken within one month**.
Armed forces: Centre informs it of action within **three months**.

n500a0069020.s: The Supreme Court entrusted the NHRC with monitoring the implementation of which law in 1997?
o: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
n500a0069020.x: In 1997, the Supreme Court entrusted the NHRC with monitoring the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976.
n500a0069020.tq: Pair the judicial direction with the exact statute rather than a neighbouring social-justice law.
xs: In **1997** the SC entrusted the NHRC with monitoring the **Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976** — option **(3)**.
It is one of the NHRC's **specialised mandates**, alongside custodial and encounter deaths.
xa: **Custodial deaths**: report within **24 hours**; post-mortem videography.
**Encounter deaths**: reporting + magisterial inquiry per **PUCL v Maharashtra (2014)**.
**Transgender welfare**: **Advisory 2.0** (May **2026**).

ncc4f57c546b.s: In cases of custodial death, information is required to be reported to the NHRC within what period?
ncc4f57c546b.x: Custodial deaths are to be reported to the NHRC within 24 hours; post-mortem videography and independent investigation are also associated safeguards.
ncc4f57c546b.tq: Test the exact reporting deadline using nearby but distinct time intervals as distractors.
xs: Custodial deaths must be reported to the NHRC within **24 hours** — option **(3)**.
Other safeguards: **post-mortem videography** and **independent investigation**.
xa: **Gade Sai Krishna** case: NHRC directed the **AP SHRC**, DGP and Chief Secretary to report within a week (**28 Jun 2026**).
**Encounter deaths**: magisterial inquiry (**PUCL v Maharashtra, 2014**).
SC (**1997**): NHRC monitors the **Bonded Labour** Act, **1976**.

n37f82f2542a.s: After the NHRC sends its inquiry report with recommendations, the Government concerned must inform the Commission of the action taken within:
n37f82f2542a.x: The Government must inform the Commission of the action taken on its report within one month. Three months is the period for the Central Government to report action in armed-forces cases; six months and one year are not the prescribed periods (one year is the time bar for inquiry).
xs: The Government must inform the NHRC of **action taken within one month** — option **(1)**.
**Three months** applies to the Centre in **armed-forces** cases; **one year** is the **time bar** for inquiries.
xa: ⚠ Action taken: **one month** (general) vs **three months** (armed forces); time bar **one year**.
Recommendations are **advisory**.
NHRC annual report is laid before **each House of Parliament** with a memorandum of action taken.

n154cc983feb.s: Which of the following correctly describes the position regarding Union Territories after the 2019 change?
o: Every Union Territory must constitute an independent SHRC, including Delhi.
The Central Government may confer the human-rights functions of a Union Territory on an SHRC, while Delhi’s functions are handled by the NHRC.
Only the concerned State Government may confer Union Territory functions on an SHRC.
The NHRC has no role in the human-rights functions of Union Territories.
n154cc983feb.x: The Central Government may confer the human-rights functions of a Union Territory on an SHRC. Delhi’s human-rights functions are handled by the NHRC itself.
n154cc983feb.tq: Ask who holds the power and then distinguish Delhi’s special position from the general rule.
xs: The **Central Government may confer** a **UT's** human-rights functions on an **SHRC**; **Delhi's** functions are handled by the **NHRC** — option **(2)** (**2019**).
So UTs need not set up their own SHRC, and the NHRC does have a role.
xa: SHRC jurisdiction: **State List** and **Concurrent List** subjects.
SHRCs are **optional** — a State Government "may" constitute one.
No overlap: SHRC and NHRC do not inquire into the same pending matter.

naa23742dc9f.s: While dealing with complaints of human-rights violations by members of the armed forces, the NHRC may:
o: Order the State Government to prosecute the personnel compulsorily
Directly punish the personnel concerned after a summary trial
Transfer the matter to any private tribunal for final adjudication
Seek a report from the Central Government and make recommendations
naa23742dc9f.x: In armed-forces cases, the NHRC may seek a report from the Central Government and make recommendations. Its powers are more restricted than in ordinary public-servant cases.
naa23742dc9f.tq: Ask which authority supplies the report and avoid attributing direct punitive power to the Commission.
xs: In **armed-forces** cases, the NHRC may only **seek a report from the Central Government** and **make recommendations** — option **(4)**.
It cannot punish, order prosecution or send matters to a private tribunal.
The **Centre** informs it of action within **three months**.
xa: "Armed forces" = **naval, military and air forces**, incl. other armed forces of the Union (**Sec. 2**).
The armed-forces limit is part of the "**toothless tiger**" criticism.
In ordinary cases, the action-taken report is due within **one month**.

n1c615452fb9.s: In cases concerning the armed forces, the Central Government is required to inform the NHRC of the action taken within:
n1c615452fb9.x: In armed-forces cases, the Central Government must inform the NHRC of the action taken within three months.
n1c615452fb9.tq: Distinguish the armed-forces response period from the general one-month reporting period.
xs: In **armed-forces** cases the Centre must inform the NHRC of action taken within **three months** — option **(2)**.
**One month** is the general action-taken period; **one year** is the time bar for inquiries.
xa: ⚠ Action taken: **one month** (general) vs **three months** (armed forces); time bar **one year**.
In armed-forces cases the NHRC may only **seek a report from the Central Government** and recommend.
"Armed forces" = **naval, military and air forces**, incl. other armed forces of the Union (**Sec. 2**).

ne20e09a407f.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the legal effect of recommendations made by the NHRC?
o: They can be ignored without any communication to the Commission.
They are advisory, although the Government must respond to the Commission.
They are binding decrees enforceable as judgments of a civil court.
They automatically impose criminal liability on the public servant.
ne20e09a407f.x: NHRC recommendations are advisory and cannot be compelled as binding orders. The Government is required to inform the Commission of the action taken.
ne20e09a407f.tq: Distinguish an advisory recommendation from an enforceable judicial order.
xs: NHRC recommendations are **advisory**, though the **Government must respond** — option **(2)**.
They are **not binding** decrees and impose no criminal liability; the Government **cannot be compelled**.
xa: Government must inform the Commission of **action taken within one month**.
The NHRC has **no power to punish** violators — it only **recommends** compensation or prosecution.
Non-binding advice is part of the "**toothless tiger**" criticism.

n4855c9a5c7c.s: The annual report of a State Human Rights Commission is submitted to the State Government and thereafter laid before the:
o: Parliament with a memorandum of action taken
State Legislature with a memorandum of action taken
n4855c9a5c7c.x: The SHRC submits its annual report to the State Government, which lays it before the State Legislature along with a memorandum of action taken.
n4855c9a5c7c.tq: Track the reporting chain and distinguish the State Legislature from Parliament.
xs: The SHRC's **annual report** goes to the **State Government** and is laid before the **State Legislature** with a **memorandum of action taken** — option **(3)**.
**Parliament** receives the **NHRC** report, not the SHRC's.
xa: NHRC report goes to the **Central Govt** (and State Govt concerned) and is laid before **each House of Parliament**.
Older notes say the NHRC report goes "to the **President**".
SHRC powers mirror the NHRC's — **civil court** powers, **one-year** bar, **advisory** nature.

n26d1af3c999.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Human Rights Commission is constituted by:
o: Parliament under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014
The Andhra Pradesh Government under the PHRA, 1993
n26d1af3c999.x: The AP SHRC is constituted by the Andhra Pradesh Government under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
xa: Constituting an SHRC is **optional** — a State Government "**may**" constitute one.
SHRC chair: former **HC Chief Justice or Judge**; appointed by the **Governor**.
SHRC jurisdiction: **State List** and **Concurrent List** subjects.

n550d1891535.s: The NHRC is criticised as a 'toothless tiger' mainly because:
o: It lacks civil-court powers during inquiries
It is not a statutory body
n550d1891535.x: The criticism rests on its non-binding advice, along with the one-year bar and limits on armed-forces complaints.
xa: The NHRC has **no power to punish** violators.
**Allahabad HC** said the NHRC exceeded its mandate by directing an EOW probe into **558** aided madrasas (**30 Apr 2026**).
SHRCs are weakened by **optional creation**, **advisory powers** and **vacancies**.

nbdbbc24fa86.s: Which of the following is NOT a mandatory safeguard associated with D.K. Basu v State of West Bengal?
o: Automatic arrest in every offence punishable up to seven years
nbdbbc24fa86.x: D.K. Basu required safeguards such as an arrest memo, identification of officers, informing kin and medical examination. Automatic arrest for offences up to seven years is contrary to the safeguard approach associated with Arnesh Kumar.
nbdbbc24fa86.tq: Find the one proposition that reverses the arrest-safeguard principle.
xs: **Automatic arrest in every offence up to seven years** is not a D.K. Basu safeguard — option **(3)**.
**D.K. Basu (1997)** mandated an **arrest memo**, **ID of officers**, **informing kin** and a **medical check**.
In fact **Arnesh Kumar (2014)** barred **automatic arrest** for offences up to **7 years**.
xa: **Joginder Kumar (1994)**: arrest must be justified, not routine.
**Nilabati Behera (1993)**: compensation for custodial death.
**PUCL v Maharashtra (2014)**: **16-point** encounter guidelines.

n87038ead028.s: How many directives on police reform did the Supreme Court issue in Prakash Singh v Union of India (2006)?
n87038ead028.x: Prakash Singh (2006) issued seven directives: State Security Commission, DGP from a UPSC panel with a 2-year tenure, 2-year tenure for field officers, separation of investigation from law and order, Police Establishment Board, National Security Commission and Police Complaints Authorities. Five, six and ten are wrong counts.
xs: **Prakash Singh v UOI (2006)** issued **seven** directives — option **(3)**.

They are: **State Security Commission**; **DGP from UPSC panel** (**2-year** tenure); **2-year** tenure for field officers; separate investigation; **Police Establishment Board**; **National Security Commission**; **PCAs**.
xa: ⚠ **PUCL (2014)** has **16** points; Prakash Singh has **7** directives.
**Arnesh Kumar (2014)**: no automatic arrest up to **7 years**.
PCAs exist at **State and district levels**.

n01b4830bfe7.s: The guidelines in PUCL v State of Maharashtra (2014) concerning encounter deaths consisted of how many points?
n01b4830bfe7.x: PUCL v State of Maharashtra (2014) laid down 16-point guidelines for encounter deaths.
n01b4830bfe7.tq: Recall the exact count attached to the leading encounter-death guidelines case.
xs: **PUCL v Maharashtra (2014)** laid down guidelines of **16 points** on **encounter deaths** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Do not confuse with the **7 directives** of **Prakash Singh (2006)** on police reform.
xa: Key points: record the **tip-off**, register an **FIR**, independent probe by **CID or another police station**, **magisterial inquiry**.
Also: inform **NHRC/SHRC**, medical aid, inform kin, **forensic check of weapons**.
**No out-of-turn promotion or gallantry award** until cleared.

nec8c71a66c3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the directives in Prakash Singh v. Union of India (2006)?
o: A State Security Commission was envisaged.
Field officers were to get a two-year tenure.
The DGP was to get a five-year tenure.
nec8c71a66c3.x: The DGP was to be selected from a UPSC panel and given a two-year tenure, not five years.
xa: Also: **separate investigation from law and order**, **National Security Commission**, **PCAs**.
Total: **7 directives**.
The colonial **Police Act 1861** still remains in force.

n33ab1bc5f57.s: Under the Prakash Singh framework, the State Police Complaints Authority is headed by a:
n33ab1bc5f57.x: The State PCA is headed by a retired judge and handles serious misconduct such as custodial death; PCAs exist at State and district levels.
xa: There is a call for **PCAs with statutory backing**.
Prakash Singh (**2006**) issued **7 directives**.
⚠ PCAs are a Prakash Singh directive, not a creation of the **Police Act 1861**.

n127f44a35e8.s: Under the PUCL guidelines on encounter deaths, which of the following is barred until the officers involved are cleared?
n127f44a35e8.x: The guidelines require recording the tip-off, an FIR and an independent probe, and prohibit out-of-turn promotion or gallantry awards until clearance.
xa: A **magisterial inquiry** is also required.
Inform **NHRC/SHRC**; **forensic check** of weapons.
PUCL (**2014**) has **16** points.

nf1441084b65.s: Which of the following correctly states the position of the NHRC regarding encounter deaths?
o: They are treated as serious violations requiring mandatory reporting, post-mortem videography and independent investigation.
They can be investigated only by the armed forces.
They require only an internal police report and no post-mortem.
They are treated as routine police actions requiring no special reporting.
nf1441084b65.x: The NHRC treats encounter deaths as serious violations and requires mandatory reporting, post-mortem videography and independent investigation.
nf1441084b65.tq: Match the rights-protection body with its prescribed procedural safeguards.
xs: The **NHRC** treats encounter deaths as **serious violations** needing **mandatory reporting, post-mortem videography and independent investigation** — option **(1)**.
They are not routine police actions and are not left to internal reports or the armed forces.
xa: **PUCL (2014)**: **16-point** guidelines, including a **magisterial inquiry**.
Way forward: **body-worn cameras** (Delhi Police) and better **forensic capacity**.
Only **3 convictions** for **2,253** custody deaths.

na705fcbf81e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Shatrughan Chauhan v. Union of India (2014)?
o: Solitary confinement before rejection of a mercy petition is illegal.
Delay in deciding a mercy petition can never justify commutation.
At least 14 days should ordinarily separate rejection of mercy and execution.
Unexplained delay may justify commuting death to life imprisonment.
na705fcbf81e.x: The Court held that inordinate, unexplained delay may justify commutation of a death sentence.
xa: **Art. 72** (President) and **Art. 161** (Governor) are the mercy powers.
**Epuru Sudhakar (2006)**: limited **judicial review** of pardon.
**Bachan Singh (1980)**: **life is the rule**, death the exception.

naeb954eac87.s: The decision in Epuru Sudhakar v. Government of Andhra Pradesh (2006) is associated with which proposition?
o: Mercy powers are completely immune from judicial scrutiny.
Pardon and remission are open to limited judicial review.
Only the Supreme Court may decide mercy petitions.
A Governor may pardon every death sentence.
naeb954eac87.x: Epuru Sudhakar (2006) established that the exercise of pardon or remission powers is subject to limited judicial review.
naeb954eac87.tq: Identify the precise extent of judicial review without confusing limited review with complete judicial control.
xs: **Epuru Sudhakar v Govt of AP (2006)**: **pardon and remission** are open to **limited judicial review** — option **(2)**.
So mercy powers are not immune; the **Governor** still cannot pardon a death sentence (**Art. 161**).
xa: **Art. 72**: the **President** can pardon a death sentence.
**Shatrughan Chauhan (2014)**: unexplained delay → **commute to life**.
**Machhi Singh (1983)**: categories of rarest cases.

nd5df8ce4dff.s: A death sentence passed by a Sessions Court must be confirmed by the:
nd5df8ce4dff.x: A death sentence passed by a Sessions Court requires confirmation by the High Court.
xa: Appeal to SC under **Arts 132, 134, 136**.
**Art. 72**: the **President** can pardon a death sentence.
**Art. 161**: the **Governor** cannot pardon a death sentence but can commute/remit/suspend.

ne107967e32e.s: An appeal against a death sentence may reach the Supreme Court under which combination of constitutional provisions?
ne107967e32e.x: Appeals in such matters may lie to the Supreme Court under Articles 132, 134 and 136.
ne107967e32e.tq: Recall the exact constitutional Article cluster instead of nearby judicial provisions.
xs: Appeals reach the Supreme Court under **Articles 132, 134 and 136** — option **(1)**.
First the Sessions Court sentence needs **High Court confirmation**.
xa: **Nilabati Behera** compensation is under **Arts 32/226** — writ jurisdiction, not appeals.
**Art. 72** (President) can pardon death sentences and **court-martial** cases.
Capital offences now in the **BNS** (murder **s.103**).

nc3b64a1fb94.s: Which provision made a judicial inquiry mandatory in cases of custodial death, and what is its present BNSS equivalent?
nc3b64a1fb94.x: CrPC Section 176(1A) made judicial inquiry mandatory in custodial deaths; the corresponding BNSS provision is Section 196.
nc3b64a1fb94.tq: Match the old and new procedural section numbers without confusing arrest and sanction provisions.
xs: **CrPC s.176(1A)** made a **judicial inquiry mandatory in custodial deaths**; it is now **BNSS s.196** — option **(1)**.
**BNSS s.218** is government sanction for prosecuting public servants; **CrPC s.41** became **BNSS s.35** (arrest checklist); **BNSS s.479** is undertrial relief.
xa: Only **3 convictions** for **2,253** police-custody deaths (**1999-2023**).
NHRC norms: custodial/encounter deaths need **mandatory reporting** and **post-mortem videography**.
**Bihar** records the most police-custody deaths.

n7f378be3cce.s: During 1999–2023, police-custody deaths and convictions reported were:
n7f378be3cce.x: The reported data recorded 2,253 police-custody deaths and only three convictions during 1999–2023.
xa: **Bihar** records the most custody deaths, then **Rajasthan** and **UP**.
Debate: the custodial-death **conviction rate near zero**.
**CrPC s.176(1A)** / **BNSS s.196**: mandatory judicial inquiry.

n84339a6b246.s: India signed the UN Convention against Torture (UNCAT), which it has not ratified, in:
n84339a6b246.x: India signed UNCAT in 1997 but has not ratified it; the 2010 Prevention of Torture Bill lapsed.
xa: **Law Commission 273rd Report (2017)** recommended **UNCAT ratification** and a draft Bill.
Way forward: **standalone law** + **PEACE model** of interviewing.
⚠ **262nd** = death penalty; **273rd** = torture.

n114594568b2.s: Under the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India, prisons are included in which of the following?
n114594568b2.x: Prisons are a State subject under Entry 4 of the State List in the Seventh Schedule.
n114594568b2.tq: Test the exact List and Entry instead of relying on the general subject classification.
xs: **Prisons** are in the **State List, Entry 4** of the Seventh Schedule — option **(4)**.
They are not a Union or Concurrent subject.
xa: Prisons are governed by the **Prisons Act 1894** and **State jail manuals**.
**BPR&D** issues **advisory** guidelines.
**Model Prisons Act 2023** — prepared by **MHA** as a guide for States.

nddf766ad176.s: The Model Prisons Act, 2023 guides States in replacing the colonial Prisons Act of:
nddf766ad176.x: The MHA's Model Prisons Act, 2023 is meant to replace the Prisons Act, 1894; it is not automatically binding on States.
xa: Prisons = **State List, Entry 4**.
**BPR&D** issues advisory guidelines.
Justice **Amitava Roy Committee** (**2018**): overcrowding, undertrials, legal aid, speedy trial.

n6349c3fca11.s: Under BNSS Section 479, an undertrial is generally eligible for release after serving what part of the maximum term?
n6349c3fca11.x: BNSS Section 479 provides release after one-half of the maximum term, reduced to one-third for first-time offenders, subject to statutory conditions.
xa: Undertrials are **~73%** of inmates; **9,028** held over **5 years** (NCRB **2024**).
The **Justice Amitava Roy Committee** (**2018**) addressed undertrials and speedy trial.
The **Mulla Committee** wanted **separate undertrials**.

nb292ad25eac.s: The 273rd Law Commission Report recommended which of the following?
o: Replacement of the Seventh Schedule by a new prison list
Ratification of UNCAT and a draft Prevention of Torture Bill, 2017
Confirmation of all death sentences by the Supreme Court
nb292ad25eac.x: The 273rd Law Commission Report (2017) recommended ratification of UNCAT and proposed a draft Prevention of Torture Bill, 2017.
nb292ad25eac.tq: Match the Law Commission report number with its specific subject and recommendation.
xs: The **273rd Report (2017)** recommended **UNCAT ratification** and a draft **Prevention of Torture Bill, 2017** — option **(3)**.
Prison manuals, the Seventh Schedule and death-sentence confirmation were not its subject.
xa: ⚠ **262nd (2015)** = death penalty; **273rd** = torture.
India **signed UNCAT in 1997**, not ratified.
The **2010** torture Bill **lapsed** after passing the Lok Sabha.

na30aaf0ad6d.s: Which State records the highest number of deaths in police custody?
na30aaf0ad6d.x: Bihar records the most police-custody deaths, followed by Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.
xa: Only **3 convictions** for **2,253** custody deaths (**1999-2023**).
**Delhi** has the highest prison occupancy (**194.6%**).
AP case: **Gade Sai Krishna** (**Krishnalanka** police, **Vijayawada**).

n710de7738af.s: According to NCRB Prison Statistics 2024, undertrials constituted approximately what share of inmates?
n710de7738af.x: Undertrials were about 73% of inmates; women were 4.14% and there were only 34 women's prisons.
xa: **21** States/UTs lack a women's prison.
Prisons **1,333**; inmates **5.11 lakh** against ~**4.53 lakh** capacity.
About **37%** of staff posts vacant; **122 suicides**.

nd5071230893.s: According to NCRB Prison Statistics 2024, the prison occupancy rate and the proportion of undertrials were respectively:
nd5071230893.x: NCRB Prison Statistics 2024 reported prison occupancy at 112.7%, with undertrials constituting 73% of the prison population.
nd5071230893.tq: Keep the percentage pair together and reject options that alter one figure while retaining the other.
xs: NCRB **2024**: occupancy **112.7%** and undertrials **73%** — option **(4)**.
**112.7%** is a **decade-low**; the other percentages are not in the data.
xa: **Delhi** highest occupancy **194.6%**, **Meghalaya** **163.5%**.
**9,028** undertrials held over **5 years**.
Released on **3 Jun 2026**.

nad11d0b16a7.s: With reference to parole and furlough, which one of the following is correct?
o: They are available only to undertrial prisoners.
They are governed by identical Central rules applicable to every State.
They are not absolute rights, and each State has its own prisoner-release rules.
They constitute an absolute constitutional right available uniformly throughout India.
nad11d0b16a7.x: Parole and furlough are not absolute rights. Each State frames its own prisoner-release or parole rules.
nad11d0b16a7.tq: Distinguish a non-absolute release facility from a uniform constitutional entitlement.
xs: Parole and furlough are **not absolute rights**, and **each State has its own prisoner-release rules** — option **(3)** (UPSC **2021**: the only correct statement).
They are not uniform Central rules, not limited to undertrials and not constitutional rights.
xa: Prisons are a **State List (Entry 4)** subject.
**BNSS s.479**: undertrial release after **half** the maximum term (**one-third** for first-time offenders).
SC (**Aug 2025**): immediate release of prisoners held beyond sentence completion.

ncd671d8c1bd.s: According to Amnesty International, which country is the world's biggest state executioner?
ncd671d8c1bd.x: China was identified as the world’s biggest state executioner.
ncd671d8c1bd.tq: Test the named country directly without importing unrelated current ranking figures.
xs: **China** was named the **world's biggest state executioner** by **Amnesty International** — option **(1)** (UPPSC **2014**).
India, Iran and the USA are not named as the biggest executioner in the notes.
xa: India: **Bachan Singh (1980)** "**rarest of rare**" doctrine.
**Law Commission 262nd (2015)**: abolish death penalty except for **terrorism and waging war**.
Debate: **retributive** vs **reformative** justice.
ncd671d8c1bd.fixed: odd wording 'ranking referred to here'; ya9279f6e17c

n0827c225dbc.s: Gade Sai Krishna’s custodial-death case in Andhra Pradesh was associated with which police station and city?
n0827c225dbc.x: The case concerned the Krishnalanka police station in Vijayawada.
n0827c225dbc.tq: Match the incident with its precise local jurisdiction instead of the wider State alone.
xs: The **Gade Sai Krishna** custodial death involved the **Krishnalanka police station, Vijayawada** — option **(1)**.
It is the **AP angle** of custodial violence; Tirupati figures only because the **Tirupati MP** was later summoned.
xa: NHRC sought reports (**Jun 2026**).
SC gave the SIT (IGP **M. Ravi Prakash**) **7-day** custody of suspended CI **Nagaraju** (**31 Jul 2026**).
A Vijayawada court summoned the **Tirupati MP** to record his statement (**11 Aug 2026**).

n0d9c5997fd7.s: Who founded the first Women’s Studies Centre at SNDT?
n0d9c5997fd7.x: Neera Desai founded the first Women’s Studies Centre at SNDT.
n0d9c5997fd7.tq: Discriminate among women’s movement leaders by their specific institutional contribution.
xs: **Neera Desai** founded the first **Women's Studies Centre** at **SNDT** — option **(4)**.
**Vina Mazumdar** founded **CWDS**; **Madhu Kishwar** founded **Manushi**; **Margaret Cousins** was in **WIA** and **AIWC**.
xa: These belong to the **post-1970s autonomous movement**, after **Towards Equality (1974)**.
**Chipko (1973)**: women of **Chamoli** hugged trees.
**Anti-Arrack Movement** began **1992** at **Dubagunta (Nellore)**.

ne512b2e1fc0.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for special provisions for women and children?
ne512b2e1fc0.x: Article 15(3) enables the State to make special provisions for women and children.
ne512b2e1fc0.tq: Identify the specific sub-clause rather than the broader equality provision.
xs: **Article 15(3)** permits **special provisions for women and children** — option **(3)**.
**Art. 14**: equality; **Art. 15(1)**: no discrimination on ground of **sex**; **Art. 16(2)**: no sex discrimination in **public employment**.
xa: **Art. 42**: just and humane work conditions, **maternity relief**.
**Art. 44**: **Uniform Civil Code**.
**Arts. 243D / 243T**: at least **one-third** seats for women in Panchayats / Municipalities.

n473165d09d7.s: Reservation of seats for women in Panchayats is provided under Article:
n473165d09d7.x: Article 243D covers Panchayats; 243T covers Municipalities and 330A/332A cover the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.
xa: The **33%** quota came into effect in the **J&K and Puducherry** Assemblies on **17 Apr 2026**.
The **131st Amendment Bill, 2026** (to speed up the quota) was defeated on **17 Apr 2026**.
**Art. 44**: Uniform Civil Code.

n0811677835c.s: Which of the following correctly describes women's reservation in Andhra Pradesh local bodies?
o: 50% only in municipalities and 33⅓% in panchayats
50% in panchayats and municipalities, above the one-third floor
33⅓% in panchayats and municipalities, equal to the constitutional floor
One-third in panchayats and 50% only in nominated posts
n0811677835c.x: Andhra Pradesh provides 50% reservation for women in panchayats and municipalities, which is above the one-third floor.
n0811677835c.tq: Compare the State share with the constitutional minimum instead of confusing the two percentages.
xs: AP gives **50%** to women in **panchayats and municipalities**, above the **1/3** floor — option **(2)**.
The Constitution's **Arts. 243D / 243T** require only **at least one-third**.

nfb1d270401f.s: The Devadasi system was prohibited in Andhra Pradesh by the

both the Madras Act, 1947 and the AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1988

nb5022360467.s: The Child Marriage Restraint Act, commonly known as the Sarda Act, was enacted in
nb5022360467.x: The Child Marriage Restraint or Sarda Act was enacted in 1929 and dealt with the minimum marriage age.

xs: The **Child Marriage Restraint (Sarda) Act** was enacted in **1929** — option **(4)**; it fixed a **minimum marriage age**.
**1917** = **WIA**; **1925** = **NCWI**; **1927** = **AIWC** — organisations, not this Act.
xa: **Female Infanticide Prevention Act**: **1870** (APPSC **2018**).

n79989407236.s: The UN Decade for Women covered the period
n79989407236.x: The UN Decade for Women extended from 1976 to 1985.

n52c305782fd.s: The Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act, which bans sati and its glorification, was enacted in:

n7ba859f4502.s: The Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act was enacted in:

n0f8fe278045.s: Which one of the following is correct about the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956?

xs: The **ITPA 1956** penalises **brothel keeping, soliciting, living on earnings** — **not prostitution itself** — option **(2)**.

nef40f515417.s: Which Act provides for monogamy and grounds of divorce under Hindu personal law?

n1a957133e8e.s: The Code on Wages, 2019 subsumes the:

o: Members of Scheduled Tribes, unless the Central Government directs otherwise
nf7424dff25b.x: Section 2(2) excludes notified Scheduled Tribes unless the Centre directs otherwise; the Supreme Court (8 Oct 2025) upheld this exclusion.
xa: HSA **1956**: equal inheritance; limited estate abolished.
**2005 amendment**: daughters equal coparceners.
**Vineeta Sharma (2020)**: daughter a **coparcener by birth**.
nf7424dff25b.fixed: exclusion covers ST members as a whole, not only ST women

na79ffe81829.s: Which State had already made unmarried daughters coparceners through its amendment before the national Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005?
na79ffe81829.x: Andhra Pradesh made unmarried daughters coparceners through an earlier amendment. The Andhra Pradesh Assembly passed the relevant Act on 24 September 1985 under NTR.
na79ffe81829.tq: Identify the State-level precursor to the later central reform.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** made **unmarried daughters coparceners** well before **2005** — option **(1)**.
The AP Assembly passed its Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act on **24 Sept 1985** under **NTR**.
xa: The AP amendment is dated **1986**.
Central **2005 amendment**: daughters = **equal coparceners**.
**Vineeta Sharma (2020)**: daughter a **coparcener by birth**.

n93eae8a3b16.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021?
o: A woman can be a surrogate only once.
The couple requires certificates of essentiality and eligibility.
Sex selection is permitted if the surrogate gives written consent.
n93eae8a3b16.x: Sex selection is prohibited and cannot be permitted merely through the surrogate's consent.
xa: **Altruistic** surrogacy allowed (medical costs, insurance only).
**Abandoning the child** is also prohibited.
⚠ "Abortion of surrogate child prohibited" was **NOT** in the **2019 Bill** (APPSC **2018**).

n0753a530c4f.s: A foetus carried through surrogacy may be aborted under the applicable law only when
o: the intending couple alone gives consent
the ART clinic recommends it without further approval
the surrogate gives written consent and authorisation is obtained under the MTP Act
the surrogate’s consent is specifically excluded
n0753a530c4f.x: Abortion of a surrogate foetus is not prohibited outright. It requires the surrogate’s written consent and authorisation under the MTP Act.
n0753a530c4f.tq: Apply the exception to a general prohibition instead of treating abortion as absolutely banned.
xs: A surrogate foetus may be aborted with the **surrogate's written consent** + **authorisation under the MTP Act** — option **(3)**.
It is **not banned outright**, and the couple's or clinic's say alone is not enough.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "abortion of the surrogate child is prohibited" was NOT in the **2019 Bill** (APPSC **2018**).
**MTP (Amendment) Act, 2021**: up to **20 weeks** on one doctor's opinion.
A woman can be a surrogate only **once**.

n0f66a27c844.s: The National Commission for Women, created under the NCW Act, 1990, was constituted in:
n0f66a27c844.x: The NCW is a statutory body under the 1990 Act and was constituted in 1992.
xa: Composition: Chairperson + **5 members** (at least one **SC**, one **ST**) + Member-Secretary.
Functions: review laws, complaints and **suo motu** notice, inspect jails/remand homes, police gender sensitisation.
⚠ NCW **Act 1990** but **set up Jan 1992**.
First women's court: **West Bengal**, **Malda, 2013** (APPSC **2019**).

n01c41397e70.s: Under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990, the Commission consists of a Chairperson, a Member-Secretary and:
o: three members, at least one from the Scheduled Castes
five members, at least one each from the SCs and the STs
seven members, all nominated by the Chief Justice of India
five members, all of whom must be retired judges
n01c41397e70.x: The NCW has a Chairperson, five members (at least one SC and one ST) and a Member-Secretary. The counts of three and seven are wrong, and there is no requirement that members be retired judges or nominated by the CJI.
xs: The NCW has a Chairperson, **five members (at least one SC, one ST)** and a Member-Secretary — option **(2)**.
Three or seven members, CJI nomination or retired judges are not in the **NCW Act 1990**.
xa: NCW functions: review safeguards and laws, take complaints and **suo motu** notice.
It inspects **jails/remand homes**, does research and **police gender sensitisation**.
⚠ NCW **Act 1990**, but **set up Jan 1992**.

nbc9c8a3c0b9.s: Which of the following correctly represents the sex ratio figures reported by NFHS-4 and NFHS-5 respectively?
nbc9c8a3c0b9.x: The sex ratio was 991 in NFHS-4 and increased to 1020 in NFHS-5.
nbc9c8a3c0b9.tq: Read the direction of change and distinguish survey figures from census figures.
xs: Sex ratio: **NFHS-4: 991**, **NFHS-5: 1020** — option **(3)**.
Option (1) reverses them; **904 and 917** are **sex ratio at birth** figures from MoSPI.
xa: Sex ratio at birth rose from **904 (2017-19)** to **917 (2021-23)** (**Women and Men in India 2025**, **27th edition**).
NFHS-5 also records **32%** spousal violence.
Causes of low ratio: **son preference**, female foeticide/infanticide, dowry, neglect of girls.

n5216667859b.s: Which of the following correctly describes the regional pattern of sex ratio in India?
o: Kerala and the North-East are the most male-skewed, while Punjab has the best sex ratio
Haryana and Punjab are the most male-skewed, while Kerala and the North-East have the best sex-ratio balance
Haryana and Punjab are the most female-skewed, while Kerala and the North-East are male-skewed
There is no marked regional variation in the sex ratio between northern and southern India
n5216667859b.x: Haryana and Punjab are identified as the most male-skewed region, whereas Kerala and the North-East, including Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya and Mizoram, have the best sex-ratio balance.
n5216667859b.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap by distinguishing the north-western pattern from the southern and north-eastern pattern.
xs: **Haryana and Punjab** are most **male-skewed**; **Kerala and the North-East** have the **best** sex ratio at birth — option **(2)**.
Options (1) and (3) reverse the pattern; (4) denies a pattern that the data show.
xa: North-East best: **Arunachal, Meghalaya, Mizoram** (CRS **2024**).
NFHS-5 sex ratio: **1020** (NFHS-4: **991**).

nd11d51f06a9.s: The Female Infanticide Prevention Act was enacted during British rule in the year:
nd11d51f06a9.x: The Female Infanticide Prevention Act was passed in 1870 (APPSC 2018). 1829 is the abolition of Sati, 1856 the Widow Remarriage Act and 1929 the Sarda (Child Marriage Restraint) Act.
xs: The **Female Infanticide Prevention Act** dates from **1870** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2018**).
**1829** = abolition of **Sati**; **1856** = **Widow Remarriage Act**; **1929** = **Sarda Act**.
xa: The Phules ran a **Home for Prevention of Infanticide** (**1863**).
**PCPNDT Act 1994** bans sex selection and pre-natal sex determination.
Low sex ratio causes: **son preference**, female foeticide/infanticide, dowry.

n44bd90a66d5.s: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 is associated with which of the following reforms?
o: Abolition of the female heir’s limited estate and equal inheritance for women
Mandatory registration of every inter-faith marriage under one uniform law
n44bd90a66d5.x: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 gave women equal inheritance and abolished the female heir’s limited estate. Civil marriage irrespective of religion is associated with the Special Marriage Act.
n44bd90a66d5.tq: Distinguish personal-law reform from marriage and labour legislation.
xs: The **HSA 1956** gave **equal inheritance** to women and **abolished the female heir's limited estate** — option **(1)**.
**Civil marriage irrespective of religion** = **Special Marriage Act 1954**; **equal pay** = **Equal Remuneration Act 1976**.
xa: **2005 amendment**: daughters = **equal coparceners**.
**AP amendment (1986)** made unmarried daughters coparceners well before 2005.
STs are excluded under **s.2(2)**.

n7e9d2a64a56.s: India's first exclusive women's court was set up in which State?
n7e9d2a64a56.x: The first women's court was set up in West Bengal, at Malda in 2013 (APPSC 2019). Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra are distractors.
n7e9d2a64a56.tq: First women's court: Malda, West Bengal, 2013.
xs: India's first women's court was set up in **West Bengal**, at **Malda** in **2013** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2019**).
Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra are not linked with the first women's court in the notes.
xa: **Family Courts Act 1984**: **953** Family Courts in **29** States/UTs (as of **31 Jul 2025**).
**NCW Act 1990**; NCW set up **Jan 1992**.
Kerala instead stands out for the **best sex ratio at birth**, with the North-East.

n7f4c46c99fb.s: The 0 to 1 scale in which 0 denotes equality and 1 denotes the worst outcome belongs to the
n7f4c46c99fb.x: The 0-to-1 scale, where 0 represents equality and 1 the worst outcome, belongs to the Gender Inequality Index, not the GDI.
n7f4c46c99fb.tq: Correct a commonly confused index-scale association.
xs: The **0 (equal) to 1 (worst)** scale belongs to the **Gender Inequality Index** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Notes that give this scale for the **GDI** are wrong.
xa: The GII was **proposed to fix GDI's gaps**.
**GDI**: female-to-male comparison on health, education, command over resources.
**Global Gender Gap Index** is the **WEF's**.

ne8ad722fe35.s: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act was originally known as SITA and was amended in:
ne8ad722fe35.x: The law was enacted in 1956 as the Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act (SITA) and was renamed the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act by the 1986 amendment. 1986 is the amendment year, not the enactment year; 1961, 1994 and 2003 relate to the Dowry Act, PNDT Act and its renaming.
ne8ad722fe35.tq: Distinguish the original enactment year from the amendment year.
xs: The law was **renamed ITPA by the 1986 amendment** — option **(2)**; it began in **1956** as the **Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act (SITA)**.
**1961** = **Dowry Prohibition Act**; **1994** = **PCPNDT (PNDT) Act**; **2003** = PNDT's renaming.
xa: ⚠ ITPA is a **1956** law; "ITPA 1986" refers only to its **amendment year**.
It gives effect to the **1950 UN Convention**.
It does **not criminalise prostitution itself**; **protective homes** are run by states.

n7056858b0c7.s: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 came into force on:
n7056858b0c7.x: The Dowry Prohibition Act came into force on 1 July 1961 (APPSC-G2 2025). The other dates are distractors; 26 October is the date the Domestic Violence Act came into force, in 2006.
xs: The **Dowry Prohibition Act** came into force on **1 July 1961** — option **(2)** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
**26 October** is the **DV Act's** commencement, in **2006**.
xa: It penalises **giving, taking or abetting** dowry.
Offences: **cognisable, non-bailable, non-compoundable**.
IPC → BNS also took effect on **1 July** (**2024**).

nfcd1cc45557.s: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 came into force on:
nfcd1cc45557.x: The PWDVA, though enacted in 2005, came into force on 26 October 2006 (UPPSC 2015). 1 July is the Dowry Act's commencement date (1961), December 2013 is when the POSH Act came into force, and 26 January 2006 is a distractor.
xs: The **PWDVA** came into force on **26 October 2006** — option **(2)** (UPPSC **2015**).
**1 July** is the **Dowry Act's** date (**1961**); **Dec 2013** is when the **POSH Act** came into force.
xa: The Act is a **civil law**.
**Protection Officers** are appointed by the State Govt.
AP: **51,581** PWDVA cases (AP SES 2025-26).

o: Criminalises prostitution itself in every circumstance
Only regulates registration of protective homes
Penalises brothel-keeping, soliciting and living on prostitution earnings, but not prostitution itself
na640ef89ba7.x: The ITPA does not criminalise prostitution itself; it penalises brothel-keeping, living on prostitution earnings, soliciting and detaining persons.
xa: Selling/buying minors for prostitution: **BNS 98/99** (IPC **372/373**).
**Shakti Sadan** (Mission Shakti) houses trafficked and destitute women.
**Ujjawala** is now part of Shakti Sadan.

nc35f8c26e2c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Monitoring under the Indecent Representation law excludes digital and AI-generated content.
The Indecent Representation of Women Act bans denigrating depiction of women in advertisements and publications.
The Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act punishes attempt, abetment and glorification of sati.
A District Magistrate may seize property used for glorification of sati.
nc35f8c26e2c.x: As of 2025, monitoring under the Indecent Representation law extends to digital and AI-generated content.
xa: Sati Act: **1987**, in force **1988**.
**ITPA 1956** began as **SITA**.
**PCPNDT Act 1994** (renamed **2003**).

n3143a109c3f.s: Under Section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, the term ‘dowry’ refers to:
o: Only property demanded by the bride’s family before marriage
Property or valuable security given or agreed to be given, directly or indirectly, in connection with a marriage
Any gift exchanged between the spouses after marriage, including mahr
Only cash or movable property given after marriage
n3143a109c3f.x: Dowry includes property or valuable security given or agreed to be given directly or indirectly, before, at or any time after marriage, in connection with the marriage. Dower or mahr under Muslim personal law is excluded.
n3143a109c3f.tq: Test the exact statutory definition and distinguish the excluded term.
xs: **Dowry (s.2)** = property or valuable security given or agreed to be given, **directly or indirectly**, in connection with marriage — option **(2)**.
It covers **before, at or any time after marriage**, not just one stage or only cash.
**Dower/mahr** under Muslim personal law is **excluded**.
xa: The Act came into force on **1 July 1961** (APPSC **2025**).
It penalises **giving, taking or abetting** dowry.
Amendments of **1984 and 1986**.

nbe678ca3f35.s: Under Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, demanding dowry is punishable with imprisonment of:
nbe678ca3f35.x: Demanding dowry attracts six months to two years; giving or taking dowry (s.3) carries a minimum of five years.
xa: ⚠ Notes saying "up to five years" are wrong.
s.3 fine: at least **₹15,000** or the dowry's value, whichever is more.
s.4 fine: up to **Rs 10,000**.

n0efc42ce16c.s: Under Section 8A of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, the burden of proof lies on the:
n0efc42ce16c.x: Section 8A places the burden of proof on the accused; the offences are also cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable.
xa: Courts may act on their **own knowledge** or on complaints by **recognised welfare bodies**.
**s.8B**: **Dowry Prohibition Officers** appointed by the State Govt.
~**20** dowry deaths a day, **6,000+** a year.

nfde2848a610.s: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is primarily classified as a:
nfde2848a610.x: The Act is a civil law protecting women from domestic violence, although other criminal provisions may also apply to related conduct.
nfde2848a610.tq: Discriminate between the civil character of the Act and criminal provisions dealing with particular offences.
xs: The **DV Act 2005** is a **civil law** (only civil) — option **(4)**.
⚠ CDI's list of criminal laws wrongly includes it.
xa: It protects women **irrespective of the relationship's status** with the respondent.
In force **26 October 2006** (UPPSC **2015**).
Reliefs: protection (**s.18**), residence (**s.19**), monetary (**s.20**), custody (**s.21**), compensation (**s.22**).

n13b4b7a5537.s: Section 3 of the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 covers which forms of abuse?
o: Physical, sexual and verbal or emotional abuse only
Physical, sexual, verbal or emotional, and economic abuse
Physical, verbal and economic abuse only
n13b4b7a5537.x: Section 3 covers physical, sexual, verbal or emotional, and economic abuse.
xa: The Act is a **civil law**.
Authorities: **Protection Officers**, registered **Service Providers**, the **Magistrate**.
Disposal within **60 days**.

n36fdc6971dc.s: Which of the following correctly states the time limits under the POSH Act?
o: Complaint within 6 months, inquiry within 60 days and employer action within 90 days
Complaint within 3 months, inquiry within 90 days and employer action within 60 days
Complaint within 90 days, inquiry within 3 months and employer action within 6 months
Complaint within 3 months, inquiry within 60 days and employer action within 30 days
n36fdc6971dc.x: The complaint is ordinarily filed within three months, the inquiry is to be completed within 90 days, and the employer is to act within 60 days.
n36fdc6971dc.tq: Keep the three separate statutory periods distinct instead of swapping their order.
xs: Complaint within **3 months**, inquiry within **90 days**, employer acts within **60 days** — option **(2)**.
The other options jumble these limits.
xa: The complaint period is **extendable by 3** months.
AP: **86 of 88** POSH cases resolved.
**SHe-Box 2.0** tracks ICs/LCs online.

nf9248d46fd4.s: SHe-Box 2.0, under Mission Shakti, is best described as:
o: A fund exclusively providing maternity benefits
An employment exchange for women in rural areas
A single-window online system for complaint and tracking of Internal and Local Committees
A criminal investigation portal for dowry deaths
nf9248d46fd4.x: SHe-Box 2.0 is a single-window online complaint and tracking system for Internal and Local Committees under Mission Shakti.
nf9248d46fd4.tq: Match the digital platform with its operational function rather than its broad women-welfare context.
xs: **SHe-Box 2.0** (MWCD, **Mission Shakti**) is a **single-window online complaint** and **tracking** system for **ICs/LCs** — option **(3)**.
It covers **public, private, organised and unorganised** sectors.
xa: **SHINE app**: launched by **Railways** for staff.
**One Stop Centres (Sakhi)**: medical, legal, counselling, shelter under one roof.
**Women Helpline 181**: emergency help and counselling.

nd84a262958f.s: For the purpose of the offence of dowry death, death occurring within what period from the date of marriage is specifically relevant?
nd84a262958f.x: BNS Section 80, corresponding to IPC Section 304B, concerns dowry death where the death occurs within seven years of marriage, subject to the other legal requirements.
nd84a262958f.tq: Use the statutory time-limit as the decisive numerical clue.
xs: Dowry death covers death **within seven years** (**7 years**) of marriage — option **(2)**.
It is **BNS s.80**, the old IPC **304B**.
xa: Presumption: **BSA s.118** (Evidence Act **113B**).
The **1986** amendment brought in dowry death.
**Guntur** special court gave **life imprisonment** in a **2020** dowry-death case (**2026**).

n44b6e59549c.s: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, stalking is dealt with under:
n44b6e59549c.x: Stalking is BNS 78 (IPC 354D); voyeurism is 77, sexual harassment 75 and outraging modesty 74.
xa: **BNS 80**: dowry death; **85-86**: cruelty.
IPC → BNS from **1 July 2024**.

nb3814307dfd.s: Cruelty by a husband or his relatives is covered under which provision of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
nb3814307dfd.x: Cruelty by a husband or relatives is covered under BNS Sections 85-86, corresponding to IPC Section 498A.
nb3814307dfd.tq: Distinguish the cruelty provision from the nearby dowry-death provision by section number.
xs: **Cruelty by husband or relatives** = **BNS sections 85-86** (IPC **498A**) — option **(4)**.
**80** is dowry death; **77-78** voyeurism and stalking; **143** trafficking.
xa: Debate: **misuse claims against 498A** vs heavy under-reporting.
The **1986** amendment linked this framework with **dowry death** (304B).

n396f82947b8.s: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, acid attack is covered by:
n396f82947b8.x: Acid attack is Section 124; rape is 63-64, trafficking 143 and selling or buying minors for prostitution 98-99.
xa: Acid attack: minimum **10 years**, extendable to life; attempt **5-7 years**.
Old IPC: trafficking **370**; minors **372/373**; acid **326A/326B**.
**RPwD Act 2016** lists acid-attack injuries as a **disability**.

n6a45eabe523.s: According to UNODC trafficking findings, which one of the following countries is identified as both a high origin country and a high destination country?
n6a45eabe523.x: Bangladesh, India, Nepal and Pakistan are identified as high origin countries, while India and Pakistan are also identified as high destination countries.
n6a45eabe523.tq: Separate the overlapping origin-and-destination category from countries listed only as origins.
xs: **India** is both a high **origin** and a high **destination** country — option **(1)**.
**Bangladesh** and **Nepal** are origin countries only; **Sri Lanka** is not listed.
xa: High origin: **Bangladesh, India, Nepal, Pakistan**.
High destination: **India, Pakistan**.
**GLOTIP 2016**: traffickers and victims often share the same national or ethnic background.

n13947aea200.s: Under BNS Section 124, the punishment for an acid attack and for its attempt is respectively:
o: Minimum ten years to life; five to seven years
Maximum three years; seven to ten years
Minimum seven years to life; five to seven years
Minimum ten years to life; one year
n13947aea200.x: BNS Section 124 provides a minimum of ten years extending to life for acid attack, while attempt attracts five to seven years.
xa: Introduced by **CLA 2013**.
**RPwD Act 2016** treats acid-attack injuries as a disability.

nba60b251376.s: Under the POSH Act, showing pornography is:
o: Outside the Act's definition of harassment
Harassment only if accompanied by physical contact
Itself a form of sexual harassment
Harassment only if a demand for sexual favours is also made
nba60b251376.x: Showing pornography is itself listed as a form of sexual harassment, along with unwelcome contact and demands for sexual favours.
xa: **Sexually coloured remarks** are also covered.
Internal Committee: **1 external NGO member**; half the members women.
Employer's penalty for non-compliance: up to **₹50,000**.

o: Prosecution and conviction of traffickers only
Prevention, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of trafficking victims
Overseas employment and migration of women
n628c7d7f484.x: Ujjawala covered prevention, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of trafficking victims.
xa: Ujjawala is now part of **Shakti Sadan** under **Mission Shakti (Samarthya)**.
AP has **26 Shakti Sadans** sheltering **950** women (AP SES 2025-26).
**Cri-MAC** gives real-time trafficking alerts across states.

n37c1c177237.s: Ujjawala is now part of which institutional framework under Mission Shakti?
o: Legal Services Authorities, through Women Helpline 181
n37c1c177237.x: Ujjawala is now part of Shakti Sadan under the Samarthya component of Mission Shakti, providing integrated relief homes for trafficked and destitute women.
n37c1c177237.tq: Distinguish the rehabilitation framework from emergency response, judicial and legal-aid mechanisms.
xs: Ujjawala is now part of **Shakti Sadan** under **Mission Shakti (Samarthya)** — option **(2)**.
**Cri-MAC** is an alert system; **Helpline 181** gives emergency help; **FTSCs** include **POCSO** courts — none absorbed Ujjawala.
xa: Shakti Sadans are **integrated relief homes** for trafficked and destitute women.
**SHe-Box 2.0** also falls under **Mission Shakti**.
AP: **26 Shakti Sadans**, **950** women sheltered.

nc3c62347d25.s: What minimum compensation was directed for victims of acid attacks in Laxmi v. Union of India?
nc3c62347d25.x: Victims of acid attacks were directed to receive compensation of at least ₹3 lakh.
nc3c62347d25.tq: Use the statutory minimum rather than confusing it with a higher discretionary amount.
xs: **Laxmi v Union of India (2013)** directed compensation of **at least ₹3 lakh** — option **(3)**.
The case also regulated **acid sale** and ensured **free treatment**.
xa: Sale only against a **photo ID** + stated purpose; sellers keep a **sales register**.
**No sale to under-18s**.
Acid attack: **BNS s.124**, minimum **10 years**, extendable to life.

na670531b7fe.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the directions relating to the sale of acid in Laxmi v Union of India?
o: Maintenance of a register by sellers
No sale to persons below 18 years
Sale without recording the purchaser’s purpose
na670531b7fe.x: The purchaser’s stated purpose had to be recorded; sale without recording it was not permitted. The directions also included photo identification, a register and prohibition of sale to persons below 18 years.
na670531b7fe.tq: Find the option that reverses a specific regulatory safeguard.
xs: **Sale without recording the purpose** was not allowed — option **(4)**: acid is sold only against a **photo ID + stated purpose**.
**Sales register**, **photo ID** and **no sale to under-18s** were all directed.
xa: The **Laxmi** case also ordered at least **₹3 lakh** compensation.
Victims get **free treatment**.
Acid attack was added by **CLA 2013**.

n2f0bc1d6db5.s: Under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, Protection Officers are appointed by the:
n2f0bc1d6db5.x: The State Government appoints them; in AP, DWCDA Project Directors and RDOs act as Protection Officers, while 55 NGOs are Service Providers.
xa: AP SES 2025-26: **51,581** cases addressed; **₹9 crore** relief to **2,207** victims.
APSES 2024-25: **47,734** petitions; **23,644** Domestic Incident Reports; **7,307** final orders.

n198e89a51f2.s: Which of the following States are identified as leading in the incidence of dowry deaths?
o: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan
Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand
n198e89a51f2.x: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan are identified as the leading States in the cited assessment.
n198e89a51f2.tq: Test the exact membership of a named group rather than a single State.
xs: **UP, Bihar, MP, Rajasthan** lead in dowry deaths — option **(2)**.
The southern, western and north-western groups are not named.
xa: About **20** dowry deaths a day, **6,000+** a year.
Laws are ineffective due to **poor enforcement** and **faulty FIRs**.
The **Dowry Prohibition Act** came into force on **1 July 1961**.

n981b46162be.s: The guidelines laid down in Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997) were primarily concerned with:
o: Sexual harassment of women at the workplace
n981b46162be.x: In Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan, the Supreme Court laid down guidelines concerning sexual harassment of women at the workplace.
n981b46162be.tq: Use the case-name and subject association to distinguish closely related women-centric laws.
xs: **Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997)** laid down guidelines on **sexual harassment of women at the workplace** — option **(2)**.
They stood until a law was enacted, leading to the **POSH Act, 2013**.
xa: **Laxmi v Union of India (2013)**: acid sale regulation, compensation, free treatment.
POSH **Local Committee** is set up by the **District Officer**.
Complaint within **3 months**; inquiry within **90 days**.

n70c07bb9c81.s: Which information system shares real-time alerts on trafficking across States?
n70c07bb9c81.x: Cri-MAC is the Ministry of Home Affairs information technology initiative that shares real-time crime and trafficking alerts across States and supports inter-State coordination.
n70c07bb9c81.tq: Use the function-based distinction between an alert-sharing system, an emergency number and a global report.
xs: **Cri-MAC** gives **real-time alerts on trafficking across states** — option **(3)** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
**SHe-Box** handles workplace harassment complaints; **GLOTIP** is a UNODC report.
xa: Cri-MAC is an **MHA** IT initiative for inter-state coordination.
**GLOTIP 2016**: traffickers and victims often share the **same national or ethnic background**.
**Women Help Desks** in police stations; **Nirbhaya Fund** for safety projects.

xs: **Safe City** projects and **ERSS-112** are funded by the **Nirbhaya Fund** — option **(2)**.
The Nirbhaya Fund also pays for **FTSCs**.
xa: It is a **non-lapsable corpus** created after the **2012** case.
Safe City covers **8 major cities** with CCTV and AI-based safety.

n140c2c59866.s: Under the POCSO Act, which court may be designated as the Special Court in each district?
o: Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate
n140c2c59866.x: The POCSO Act permits a Sessions Court to be designated as the Special Court in each district.
xa: **394 exclusive POCSO** courts within the FTSCs.
Critique: disposals rising while **POCSO conviction rates fall**.
n140c2c59866.fixed: stem said 'designated by' a Sessions Court; Sessions Court is the court designated

n499e26aa281.s: In which State was India's first women's court set up?
n499e26aa281.x: The first women's court was set up in West Bengal (APPSC-GS 2019). Kerala had the first all-women police station (Kozhikode, 1973), Odisha announced 45 fast-track courts in 2019, and Andhra Pradesh is linked to the Disha model, so those options are traps.
n499e26aa281.tq: First women's court = West Bengal; first all-women police station = Kozhikode.
xs: The first women's court was set up in **West Bengal** — option **(3)** (APPSC-GS **2019**).
**Kerala** had the first **all-women police station** (**Kozhikode, 1973**); **Odisha** announced **45** fast-track courts (Dec **2019**).
xa: **AP** is linked with the **Disha** model.
AP's **Disha police stations**: **18** dedicated women's police stations.

n4e2322e342f.s: The first all-women police station in India was established at:
n4e2322e342f.x: The first all-women police station was established at Kozhikode in Kerala in 1973.
n4e2322e342f.tq: Use the exact place and year rather than substituting a prominent State capital.
xs: The first all-women police station: **Kozhikode, Kerala (1973)** — option **(3)**.
Not New Delhi, Vijayawada or Hyderabad.
xa: First women's court: **West Bengal**.
AP's **Disha police stations**: **18**.
Women are only **11.7%** of the police.

ncae63a320a2.s: Which Articles of the Constitution provide for equal franchise in the context of women voters?
ncae63a320a2.x: Articles 325 and 326 provide the constitutional basis for equal electoral franchise.
ncae63a320a2.tq: Distinguish voting rights provisions from provisions concerning eligibility to contest elections.
xs: **Articles 325 and 326** provide **equal franchise** for women voters — option **(1)** is correct.
**Articles 84 and 173** only allow women to **contest** elections to Parliament and State Legislatures.
**Articles 330A and 332A** are the women's seat quotas inserted by the **106th Amendment**.
xa: The reservation Bill was needed because women were historically **under-represented in legislatures**.
**Art. 330A** = Lok Sabha quota; **Art. 332A** = State Assemblies quota.
⚠ Women's turnout exceeded men's first in **2019** and again in **2024**.

ne5ea228e03c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023?
o: It provides one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha.
It provides one-third reservation in State Legislative Assemblies.
It includes one-third of the seats reserved for SCs and STs.
It provides reservation for women in the Rajya Sabha.
ne5ea228e03c.x: The Act does not provide reservation in the Rajya Sabha.
xa: **No OBC/BC sub-quota**.
Duration **15 years**, extendable by Parliament.

nbb659caf412.s: Which Article inserted by the 106th Amendment provides the women's quota in the Lok Sabha?
nbb659caf412.x: Article 330A covers the Lok Sabha; 332A the State Assemblies, 239AA(2)(ba) the Delhi Assembly and 334A commencement and duration.
xa: **Art. 334A** also provides **rotation** after each delimitation.
⚠ **Art. 368** = the special majority that the **131st Bill** missed.
The Act is the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam**, passed as the **128th Amendment Bill**.

n18d67b05b36.s: Which State is exempt from reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes in Panchayats because it has no Scheduled Caste population?
n18d67b05b36.x: Arunachal Pradesh is exempt from SC reservation because it has no Scheduled Caste population.
n18d67b05b36.tq: Test the specific constitutional exception rather than the general reservation rule.
xs: **Arunachal Pradesh** is exempt because it has **no SC population** — option **(4)** is correct.
Elsewhere, SC/ST seats are reserved at every level **in proportion to population**.
**Bihar** is known instead as the first State with **50%** for women in local bodies (**2006**).
xa: **73rd Amendment** in force: **24 April 1993**.
**243D(2)**: one-third of SC/ST seats go to **SC/ST women**.
SC/ST reservation ends with the **Art. 334** period, now **2030** (**104th Amendment**).

nb474518d5b5.s: Under Article 243D(3) of the Constitution, the minimum reservation for women in seats of Panchayats is:
o: One-half of the total seats, excluding SC/ST seats
One-third of the total seats, including one-third of the seats reserved for SCs and STs
nb474518d5b5.x: Article 243D(3) provides that not less than one-third of the total seats in every Panchayat, including one-third of the seats reserved for SCs and STs, shall be reserved for women.
nb474518d5b5.tq: Test the constitutional minimum against the higher reservation adopted by some States.
xs: **Art. 243D(3)**: not less than **one-third** of total seats, **including one-third of SC/ST seats** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is not one-half or one-fourth, and it is not limited to unreserved seats.
**243D(2)**: one-third of the SC/ST seats go to **SC/ST women**.
xa: **243D(4)** = one-third of **chairperson offices** for women.
**19 States/UTs** give women **50%** (**2026**); **Bihar** first (**2006**).
The same rule for municipalities is **Art. 243T(3)**.

nab8ce72f1cf.s: Bokkasam Palem, located in Srikalahasti mandal of Tirupati, is associated with which achievement?
o: It received the first national award for tribal self-governance
It became the first girls’ Panchayat in India
It was ranked first nationally among women-friendly Panchayats
It was the first Panchayat to introduce a BC-women sub-quota
nab8ce72f1cf.x: Bokkasam Palem in Srikalahasti mandal of Tirupati ranked first nationally among women-friendly Panchayats under the Deendayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas Awards.
nab8ce72f1cf.tq: Link the place, administrative location and award-related achievement precisely.
xs: **Bokkasam Palem** (Srikalahasti mandal, Tirupati) ranked **1st nationally** among **women-friendly panchayats** — option **(3)** is correct.
The ranking was under the **Deendayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas Awards, 2026**.
India's first girls' panchayat (**Balika Panchayat**) was in **Kutch, Gujarat**, not here.
xa: MoPR's **Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats**: at least **one per district**, with **SHG alignment**.
**AP** gives **50%** reservation to women in local bodies.
First woman **AP Assembly Speaker**: **Pratibha Bharati** (**2004**, undivided AP).

n74175aa376b.s: Mahila Sabha is best described as:
o: A meeting of women officers of the Election Commission
A statutory committee of the National Commission for Women
A meeting of women members of Parliament before a joint sitting
A women-only meeting held before the Gram Sabha
n74175aa376b.x: Mahila Sabha refers to a women-only meeting conducted before the Gram Sabha, as exemplified in Maharashtra.
n74175aa376b.tq: Discriminate between a grassroots women-only forum and statutory or parliamentary bodies.
xs: **Mahila Sabha** is a **women-only meeting held before the Gram Sabha** — option **(4)** is correct.
It brings **women's issues to the Gram Sabha**; **Maharashtra** is an example.
It is not an ECI body, an NCW committee or a meeting of MPs.
xa: **Balika Panchayat** (Kutch, Gujarat, **June 2022**) trains girls in local governance.
**NCW** is a statutory body (**1992**) under the **NCW Act 1990**.
**ECI's SVEEP** targets women voters.

na9759fe3190.s: Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats are envisaged at the rate of at least one per:
na9759fe3190.x: At least one per district is envisaged, providing safe spaces and gender-responsive governance aligned with SHGs.
xa: They are an initiative of the **Ministry of Panchayati Raj**.
**Bokkasam Palem** (Tirupati) ranked **1st nationally** among women-friendly panchayats.
Nearly **10 crore women** are in over **90 lakh SHGs**.

n38ed6474003.s: Which of the following correctly states the relationship between the 2023 Women's Reservation Bill and the Constitution?
o: The 108th Amendment Bill was enacted as the 106th Amendment Act in 2023.
The 106th Amendment Bill was enacted as the 128th Amendment Act.
The 81st Amendment Bill was revived and enacted without modification.
The 128th Amendment Bill was enacted as the 106th Amendment Act.
n38ed6474003.x: The 2023 Bill was introduced as the 128th Amendment Bill and was enacted as the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023.
n38ed6474003.tq: Keep the Bill number and enacted Amendment number distinct.
xs: The **128th Amendment Bill** was enacted as the **106th Amendment Act** — option **(4)** is correct.
It passed on **21 Sept 2023** and got assent in **2023**.
The **108th** Bill (**2008**) only passed the Rajya Sabha and **lapsed** in **2014**; the **81st** Bill (**1996**) lapsed with the 11th Lok Sabha.
xa: The 106th Amendment is called the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam**.
Articles inserted: **330A** (Lok Sabha), **332A** (State Assemblies), **239AA(2)(ba)** (Delhi), **334A** (commencement and duration).
Commencement only after the **first Census after the Act** and the delimitation that follows.

nda2accb745f.s: From 17 April 2026, the women's reservation under the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act was stated to be in force for the Assemblies of:
nda2accb745f.x: The reservation was stated to be in force for the Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry Assemblies from 17 April 2026.
nda2accb745f.tq: Match the effective date with the exact pair of Assemblies named.
xs: The quota was in force for the **J&K and Puducherry** Assemblies from **17 April 2026** — option **(2)** is correct.
For the Delhi Assembly the quota comes through **Art. 239AA(2)(ba)**, but the notes list only **J&K and Puducherry** as in force.
xa: Nationally, commencement waits for the **2027 Census** and delimitation (not before **2034**).
The same day, **17 April 2026**, the **131st Amendment Bill** was defeated in the Lok Sabha.
The quota includes **one-third of SC/ST reserved seats**.

n13d6a93aa05.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 was defeated in the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026 because:
o: It got fewer votes in favour than against
It got 298 votes in favour against 230, short of the 352 needed for the Article 368 special majority
The Rajya Sabha had rejected it first
It needed ratification by half the States, which was refused
n13d6a93aa05.x: It won a simple majority (298 for, 230 against, of 528 present and voting) but fell short of the 352 votes needed for the special majority under Article 368. It was not defeated on a simple vote, the Rajya Sabha did not vote first, and State ratification was not the reason.
xs: It got **298 for and 230 against**, short of the **352** needed for the **Art. 368** special majority — option **(2)** is correct.
It actually had **more votes in favour** than against, so option (1) is wrong.
**528** members were present and voting.
xa: ⚠ **Art. 368** = special majority; **Art. 334A** = rotation and duration of the 106th quota.
The Bill aimed at a quota **from 2029** with a Lok Sabha of **850** (**815** States, **35** UTs).
Defeated on **17 April 2026**.

n29009dec6be.s: Under Article 334A, the reservation of seats for women is to be rotated:
o: Every five years irrespective of delimitation
n29009dec6be.x: Article 334A provides for rotation of the reserved seats after each delimitation.
n29009dec6be.tq: Distinguish the constitutional trigger for rotation from the ordinary election cycle.
xs: Under **Art. 334A**, reserved seats **rotate after each delimitation** — option **(4)** is correct.
Rotation is tied to delimitation, not to every general election, a fixed five-year cycle or a referendum.
**Art. 334A** also covers the **commencement and duration** of the quota.
xa: Duration: **15 years**, **extendable by Parliament**.
⚠ **Art. 334A** = rotation + duration of the 106th quota; **Art. 368** = the special majority the **131st Bill** missed.
In panchayats, reserved seats and chairperson offices are also allotted **by rotation**.

n594f8a1306d.s: Women's reservation under the 106th Amendment will commence after delimitation based on the:
n594f8a1306d.x: The reservation commences only after delimitation based on the first Census after the Act, i.e. the 2027 Census.
xa: Seats **rotate** after each delimitation (**Art. 334A**).
Duration: **15 years**, extendable by Parliament.
