Critics see bundling the quota with delimitation as **political cover** for reallocating seats.

n0799ba0ccdc.s: Which of the following is NOT provided under the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023?
o: An OBC or BC sub-quota within the women's reservation
One-third reservation in the Delhi Legislative Assembly
Rotation of reserved seats after delimitation
One-third reservation in State Legislative Assemblies
n0799ba0ccdc.x: The Act does not provide an OBC or BC sub-quota. It provides reservation in the specified legislatures and provides for rotation after delimitation.
n0799ba0ccdc.tq: Look for the specific exclusion among otherwise correct features of the amendment.
xs: The Act provides **no OBC/BC sub-quota** — option **(1)** is the one NOT provided.
It does provide one-third in the **Delhi Assembly** (**Art. 239AA(2)(ba)**) and in **State Assemblies** (**Art. 332A**).
It does provide **rotation** after each delimitation (**Art. 334A**).
xa: It also excludes the **Rajya Sabha** and **State Legislative Councils**.
**AP angle:** AP Congress and BC groups demand a **BC-women sub-quota**.
In local bodies, reservation for **backward classes** is **voluntary** for States.

n3dcb9e3900f.s: The reservation for women under the 106th Amendment is provided for:
n3dcb9e3900f.x: The reservation is provided for 15 years and may be extended by Parliament.
xa: Seats **rotate** after each delimitation.
⚠ In panchayats, **SC/ST reservation** ends with the **Art. 334** period (**2030**), but **women's reservation has no such sunset**.
Commencement only after the **next Census and delimitation**.

n6e2b34bd726.s: The principal legal shield against atrocities and discrimination targeting Dalit and tribal communities is:
o: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976
Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 and Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976
SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
n6e2b34bd726.x: The safeguards identified are the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.
xa: SC/ST seats in panchayats are reserved **in proportion to population**.
SC/ST reservation ends with the **Art. 334** period, now **2030** (**104th Amendment**).

n1a47a61361e.s: Women’s groups demanded the removal of which condition attached to women’s legislative reservation?
o: The condition of reservation only in urban local bodies
The condition of approval by all State Legislatures
The condition of prior approval by the Election Commission
n1a47a61361e.x: Women’s groups demanded removal of the Census-delimitation condition, including during the Monsoon Session.
n1a47a61361e.tq: Identify the specific procedural condition under debate rather than a general approval requirement.
xs: Women's groups demand removing the **Census-delimitation condition** — option **(1)** is correct.
The demand is for the **Monsoon Session**, after the **131st Bill** was defeated (Apr **2026**).
xa: Under current law the quota waits for the **2027 Census** and is not enforceable before **2034**.
The 131st Bill got **298** for, **230** against — short of **352**.
Critics call bundling with delimitation **political cover** for reallocating seats.

nindian-polity-76-37.s: The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023 is also known as:
nindian-polity-76-37.x: The 106th Amendment Act, 2023, the women's reservation law, is called the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam.
n: The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act was enacted in 2023. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act is known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
xs: The **106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023** is the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam** — option **(4)**.
It extends **not less than one-third** reservation to the **Lok Sabha**, **State Assemblies** and the **Delhi** Assembly.
xa: It passed as the **128th Amendment Bill** (**21 Sept 2023**).
Local-body reservation came earlier via the **73rd and 74th Amendments, 1992**.
The **131st Amendment Bill, 2026** to fast-track it was **defeated** (**17 Apr 2026**).

n6d98b8623a1.s: Which of the following measures came first in empowering women politically in India?
o: Setting up the National Commission for Women
Reserving seats for women in local bodies
Introducing the Women's Reservation Bill for legislatures
n6d98b8623a1.x: Reserving seats for women in local bodies came first (73rd/74th Amendments) and is the APPSC 2007 key. The NCW, SHGs and a Reservation Bill for legislatures came after, so they are not the answer.
n6d98b8623a1.tq: Local-body reservation first; legislature quota (106th) came much later.
xs: **Reserving seats for women in local bodies** came first — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC **2007** key).
The **NCW**, women's **SHGs** and the **Reservation Bill** for legislatures came after it.
Local-body reservation came through **Art. 243D(3)** (panchayats) and **Art. 243T(3)** (municipalities).
xa: The **73rd Amendment** came into force on **24 April 1993**.
**NCW** was set up in **1992** under the **NCW Act 1990**.
**Bihar** was the first State to give women **50%** in local bodies (**2006**).

ncc2cb35dedd.s: The Constitution (73rd Amendment) Act, which introduced one-third reservation for women in Panchayats, came into force on:
ncc2cb35dedd.x: The 73rd Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993, which is why 24 April is National Panchayati Raj Day. The other dates are not its commencement date.
xs: The **73rd Amendment** came into force on **24 April 1993** — option **(2)** is correct.
It introduced not less than **one-third** of seats for women in Panchayats (**Art. 243D(3)**).
xa: The municipal counterpart is the **74th Amendment** (**Art. 243T(3)**).
Not applicable to **Arunachal Pradesh** for SC reservation (no SC population).
SC/ST reservation ends with the **Art. 334** period (**2030**); women's has no sunset.

n77479c51ecf.s: What percentage of seats is reserved for women in Andhra Pradesh local bodies?
n77479c51ecf.x: Andhra Pradesh provides 50 per cent reservation for women in local bodies.
xa: **19 States/UTs** give women **50%** (**2026**); **Bihar** was first (**2006**).
**AP 2026:** Cabinet approved **34% BC** reservation in rural and **33.33%** in urban local bodies.
AP Congress and BC groups demand a **BC-women sub-quota**.

n03613185fa2.s: Which was the first State to raise the reservation for women in Panchayati Raj Institutions to 50%, and in which year?
n03613185fa2.x: Bihar was the first State to give women 50% in PRIs, in 2006. Many States followed, and 19 States/UTs now give 50%, including Andhra Pradesh. The other pairs are not the first.
n03613185fa2.tq: 50% for women in PRIs: Bihar first (2006).
xs: **Bihar** was the first State to give women **50%** in local bodies, in **2006** — option **(3)** is correct.
Many States followed; **19 States/UTs** now give **50%** (**2026**), including **Andhra Pradesh**.
xa: Women are **~46%** of PRI representatives (Republic Day address, **2026**).
Only **10** States/UTs exceed the quota; **4** fall short (Centre, **23 Apr 2026**).
APPSC **2019** key: "**1/2** of the seats" in PRIs.

n3cc5a5d9356.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about women's reservation?
o: Local bodies have a constitutional one-third floor for women's reservation.
Half reservation for women in local bodies exists in 19 States and UTs.
Half reservation for women in local bodies is constitutionally mandatory in every State.
In legislatures, one-third reservation is to operate only after delimitation.
n3cc5a5d9356.x: The constitutional floor is one-third; half reservation exists only in 19 States and UTs that chose it.
xa: **Bihar** was first with **50%** (**2006**).
The legislature quota is linked to the **2027 Census**, not enforceable before **2034**.
**AP** has legislated **50%** for women in local bodies.

n2926436bada.s: Who was the first woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
n2926436bada.x: Meira Kumar was the first woman Lok Sabha Speaker; Pratibha Patil was the first woman President.
xa: ⚠ Both **Naidu** and **Kripalani** were firsts in **UP**.
**Pratibha Bharati** = first woman **AP Assembly Speaker** (**2004**).
Women's turnout exceeded men's first in **2019**.

n96a86c67b6a.s: Who was the first woman Speaker of the (undivided) Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly?
n96a86c67b6a.x: Pratibha Bharati became the first woman Speaker of the undivided AP Assembly in 2004. Meira Kumar was the first woman Lok Sabha Speaker, Sucheta Kripalani the first woman Chief Minister (UP), and Sarojini Naidu the first woman Governor (UP).
n96a86c67b6a.tq: AP Assembly first woman Speaker = Pratibha Bharati (2004).
xs: **Pratibha Bharati** became the first woman **AP Assembly Speaker** in **2004** (undivided AP) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Meira Kumar** was the first woman **Lok Sabha Speaker** (**2009**).
**Sucheta Kripalani** was the first woman **CM** (UP, **1963**); **Sarojini Naidu** the first woman **Governor** (UP, **1947**).
xa: **Pratibha Patil** = first woman **President** (**2007**).
**AP** gives women **50%** reservation in local bodies.
**Bokkasam Palem** (Tirupati) ranked **1st nationally** among women-friendly panchayats.

nindian-society-1-4.s: Who was the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress?
nindian-society-1-4.x: Sarojini Naidu (1925) was the first Indian woman INC president; Annie Besant (1917) was the first woman president.
n: Annie Besant was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress in 1917. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress in 1925. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
Indira Gandhi was the first woman Prime Minister. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xa: ⚠ **Sarojini Naidu** was also the first woman **Governor** (UP, **1947**) — both firsts tied to UP.
**Pratibha Patil** (**2007**): first woman **President of India**.
**Meira Kumar** (**2009**): first woman **Lok Sabha Speaker**.

nindian-society-1-44.s: Who was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court?
nindian-society-1-44.x: M. Fathima Beevi (1989) was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court. Kiran Bedi was the first woman IPS officer and Pratibha Patil the first woman President.
nindian-society-1-44.tq: Match each first to the woman who holds it.
n: M. Fathima Beevi was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xs: **M. Fathima Beevi** was the **first woman judge of the Supreme Court** — option **(4)**.
**Kiran Bedi** was the first woman **IPS officer**; **Pratibha Patil** the first woman **President**.
**Sarojini Naidu** was the first woman **Governor**.
xa: **Jayanti Patnaik**: first **Chairperson** of the **National Commission for Women**.
**Pratibha Bharati**: AP Assembly Speaker (**2004**).
Women's turnout first exceeded men's in **2019**, and again in **2024**.

nindian-polity-1-44.s: Who was the first woman Governor of an Indian State?
nindian-polity-1-44.x: Sarojini Naidu became Governor of the United Provinces in 1947; Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman CM (UP, 1963).
n: Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of any State. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Sarojini Naidu was the Governor of Uttar Pradesh. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister of any State. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Sucheta Kripalani was the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xa: **Annie Besant** (**1917**): first woman INC President.
**Pratibha Patil** (**2007**): first woman President of India.
**M. Fathima Beevi**: first woman Supreme Court judge.

n741a412751e.s: The Gender Development Index primarily measures the ratio of female to male achievement in which of the following dimensions?
o: Economic participation, educational attainment, health and political empowerment
Reproductive health, political empowerment and labour market participation
Health, education and command over economic resources
n741a412751e.x: GDI compares female and male HDI achievements in life expectancy, education and earned income or command over economic resources.
n741a412751e.tq: Distinguish the dimensions of GDI from the sub-indices of GII and GGGI.
xs: GDI compares women and men in **health**, **education** and **command over economic resources** — option **(3)** is correct.
Indicators: **life expectancy**, **expected and mean years of schooling**, **earned income**.
Option 1 lists the **GGGI** sub-indices; option 2 is the **GII**; option 4 is the **WPS Index**.
xa: GDI is the **ratio of female to male HDI**, published by **UNDP**.
GDI parity is near **1**.
⚠ The 0-to-1 "loss" scale (1 = women fare worst) is the **GII**'s.

n55600e590a4.s: The 0-to-1 scale on which 1 denotes the worst position for women belongs to the:
n55600e590a4.x: This loss scale belongs to the GII; the GDI is read as female-to-male parity, with a value near 1 indicating parity.
xa: Both GDI and GII are published by **UNDP**.
GII dimensions: **reproductive health**, **empowerment**, **labour market**.
India's GII lags its overall HDI rank.

nda9e8e653fc.s: Which of the following indicators is included under the reproductive health dimension of the Gender Inequality Index?
o: Maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rate
Mean years of schooling and earned income
Share of women in parliamentary seats only
nda9e8e653fc.x: The reproductive health dimension of GII includes maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rate.
nda9e8e653fc.tq: Link each indicator to the correct index dimension.
xs: GII's **reproductive health** dimension = **maternal mortality ratio (MMR)** and **adolescent birth rate** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Parliamentary seats** belong to the **empowerment** dimension; **female LFPR** to the **labour market** dimension.
Mean years of schooling and earned income are **GDI** indicators.
xa: GII was introduced by **UNDP** in **2010**.
Empowerment also includes **secondary education**.
⚠ **GDI** and **GII** = **UNDP**; **GGGI** = **WEF**.

n43b11d1e101.s: The Global Gender Gap Index is published by the:
n43b11d1e101.x: The Global Gender Gap Index is published by the World Economic Forum.
n43b11d1e101.tq: Use publisher-index matching to avoid confusing GGGI with UNDP indices.
xs: The **GGGI** is published by the **World Economic Forum** — option **(3)** is correct.
**UNDP** publishes the GDI and GII; the **Georgetown Institute with PRIO** publishes the WPS Index.
xa: GGGI has existed **since 2006**.
Four sub-indices: **Economic Participation & Opportunity**, **Educational Attainment**, **Health & Survival**, **Political Empowerment**.

n5453ebf3cf9.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four sub-indices of the Global Gender Gap Index?
n5453ebf3cf9.x: The four GGGI sub-indices are Economic Participation and Opportunity, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, and Political Empowerment. Reproductive Health is associated with GII.
n5453ebf3cf9.tq: Eliminate the GII dimension inserted into the GGGI list.
xs: **Reproductive Health** is NOT a GGGI sub-index — option **(1)**; it is a **GII** dimension.
GGGI's four sub-indices: **Economic Participation & Opportunity**, **Educational Attainment**, **Health & Survival**, **Political Empowerment**.
xa: GGGI is published by the **World Economic Forum** (since **2006**).
GII reproductive health = **MMR** and **adolescent birth rate**.
India's economic participation parity was only **36.7%** (**2023**).

n7a5957b966b.s: India's lower position in the Gender Inequality Index relative to its overall Human Development Index rank is attributed particularly to:
o: Low female labour-force participation and low political representation
High female labour-force participation and high political representation
Low male literacy and high maternal mortality alone
High educational enrolment and low life expectancy of men
n7a5957b966b.x: India's GII position is pulled down especially by low female labour-force participation and low political representation.
n7a5957b966b.tq: Identify the stated cause-effect relationship rather than substituting unrelated development indicators.
xs: India's GII lags its HDI rank because of **low female labour-force participation** and **low political representation** — option **(1)** is correct.
These map to GII's **labour market** (female LFPR) and **empowerment** (parliamentary seats) dimensions.
xa: GII also has **reproductive health** (MMR, adolescent birth rate).
GII was introduced by **UNDP** in **2010**.
The **106th Amendment** reserves **one-third** of Lok Sabha and Assembly seats for women.

nc3a90e13905.s: The Balika Panchayat initiative, India's first of its kind, was launched in June 2022 in which of the following places?
nc3a90e13905.x: The first Balika Panchayat was established in villages of Kutch, Gujarat, in June 2022.
nc3a90e13905.tq: Use the state-location association to distinguish the initiative from other grassroots programmes.
xs: India's first **Balika Panchayat** was set up in villages of **Kutch, Gujarat**, in **June 2022** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is a **girls' panchayat** that trains girls in local governance (APPSC **2021** key).
xa: **Mahila Sabha**: a women-only meeting before the Gram Sabha (e.g. **Maharashtra**).
**Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan** builds the capacity of **Women Elected Representatives**.
**Bokkasam Palem** (Tirupati) ranked **1st** among women-friendly panchayats.

nca364c8242b.s: The initiative 'Nirbhay Raho - Nirbhay Chetna' is associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Training girls exclusively for urban municipal administration
Providing legal aid only to women prisoners
Increasing women's turnout through electronic voting
nca364c8242b.x: Nirbhay Raho - Nirbhay Chetna gender-sensitises male panchayat representatives.
nca364c8242b.tq: Identify the programme from its target group and objective.
xs: **Nirbhay Raho - Nirbhay Chetna** **gender-sensitises male panchayat representatives** — option **(2)** is correct.
It covers **~17.5 lakh male** representatives through **~28,500 master trainers**.
It is a **Ministry of Panchayati Raj** initiative.
xa: ⚠ **Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan** trains women (**EWRs**).
**Proxy representation** ("sarpanch-pati") is a key barrier; it **declines markedly in a second term**.
**Balika Panchayat** trains girls (Kutch, Gujarat).

n5e159b88ef3.s: According to the findings associated with the Chattopadhyay-Duflo study, women leaders invested more in which of the following?
o: Military infrastructure and border roads exclusively
Goods and facilities requested by women, including drinking water and roads
Only administrative buildings and police infrastructure
n5e159b88ef3.x: Women leaders invested more in public goods that women specifically requested, notably drinking water and roads.
n5e159b88ef3.tq: Apply the study’s finding to the type of public goods selected by women leaders.
xs: Women leaders invested more in **goods women asked for**, such as **drinking water** and **roads** — option **(2)** is correct.
The study was **Chattopadhyay & Duflo (2004)**, using random reservation in **West Bengal and Rajasthan**.
xa: Barriers to women leaders: **proxies**, **intimidation**, **online trolling**.
Legal shield for Dalit and tribal representatives: **SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989** and **Protection of Civil Rights Act 1955**.
Women are **over 49.7%** of elected panchayat representatives nationally.

n5437f22cea0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about reservation in local bodies?
o: SC/ST reservation of seats and chairperson offices is proportionate to population.
Reservation for backward classes is constitutionally compulsory in every State.
Chairperson offices are reserved as provided by State law and allotted by rotation.
Local bodies have a constitutional one-third floor for women's reservation.
n5437f22cea0.x: Reservation for backward classes in local bodies is left to the States; it is not compulsory everywhere.
xa: **Women's one-third** is **compulsory**, a **floor, not a ceiling**.
**AP 2026:** Cabinet approved **34% BC** reservation in rural and **33.33%** in urban local bodies.
**Arunachal Pradesh** has no SC reservation (no SC population).

n98a9c76ea4c.s: India's Global Gender Gap Index rank in 2018 was:
n98a9c76ea4c.x: India was ranked 108th among 149 countries in the 2018 Global Gender Gap Index.
n98a9c76ea4c.tq: Match the rank with the correct year and denominator.
xs: India ranked **108th out of 149 countries** in the **2018** GGGI — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC **2019** key).
xa: GGGI is published by the **World Economic Forum**.
Four sub-indices include **Political Empowerment** and **Health & Survival**.
Economic participation parity: only **36.7%** (**2023**).

neb11d453d2c.s: From 1 April 2022, the schemes of the Ministry of Women and Child Development were placed under how many umbrella missions?
neb11d453d2c.x: From 1 April 2022, MWCD schemes were organised under three umbrella missions: Mission Shakti, Mission Vatsalya, and Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0.
neb11d453d2c.tq: Use the exact count and identify the three umbrella missions together.
xs: Since **1 April 2022**, MWCD schemes sit under **three** umbrella missions — option **(1) Three** is correct (APPSC **2021** key).
The three: **Mission Shakti**, **Mission Vatsalya**, **Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0**.
xa: **Mission Poshan 2.0** = Anganwadi Services, Poshan Abhiyaan, Scheme for Adolescent Girls.
**Mission Vatsalya** = child protection services (subsumed **ICPS**).
**Mission Shakti** has two sub-schemes: **Sambal** (safety) and **Samarthya** (empowerment).

nc9fee334c3c.s: From 1 April 2022, which component is included under Mission Poshan 2.0?
o: One Stop Centre and Women Helpline 181
Anganwadi Services, Poshan Abhiyaan and Scheme for Adolescent Girls
Shakti Sadan, Sakhi Niwas and PMMVY
Child Protection Services and the Juvenile Justice system
nc9fee334c3c.x: Mission Poshan 2.0 comprises Anganwadi Services, Poshan Abhiyaan and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls.
nc9fee334c3c.tq: Identify the umbrella mission from its component-scheme cluster.
xs: **Mission Poshan 2.0** = **Anganwadi Services, Poshan Abhiyaan and Scheme for Adolescent Girls** — option **(2)** is correct.
**OSC** and **Helpline 181** are under **Sambal**; **Shakti Sadan, Sakhi Niwas, PMMVY** under **Samarthya**.
**Child protection** is **Mission Vatsalya**.
xa: Full name: **Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0**.
**SABLA** (Scheme for Adolescent Girls) is now part of **Poshan 2.0**.
Umbrella missions came into effect on **1 April 2022**.

n3565dbdc003.s: Under Mission Shakti, the 'Sambal' vertical concerns:
n3565dbdc003.x: Sambal concerns women's safety and Samarthya women's empowerment.
xa: Sambal: **OSC**, **Helpline 181**, **BBBP**, **Nari Adalat**, SHe-Box 2.0.
Samarthya: **Shakti Sadan**, **Sakhi Niwas**, **Palna**, **PMMVY**, SANKALP-Hub, Gap Funding.
**Mission Vatsalya** outlay: **₹10,916 crore**.

n059fa87b68c.s: SABLA (Scheme for Adolescent Girls) is now part of:
n059fa87b68c.x: SABLA, covering nutrition, life-skills and health of adolescent girls, is now part of Poshan 2.0, not Samarthya.
xa: **Mission Poshan 2.0** = Anganwadi Services, Poshan Abhiyaan, **Scheme for Adolescent Girls**.
**Kishori Shakti Yojana** (**2000**) was the ICDS-based forerunner for adolescent girls.
**Samarthya** holds Shakti Sadan, Sakhi Niwas, Palna, PMMVY.

nfd15ae95617.s: NAVYA (2025-26) gives vocational training through PMKVY 4.0 to girls aged:
nfd15ae95617.x: NAVYA, an MSDE-MWCD initiative, trains girls aged 16-18 in 27 aspirational districts in 19 States.
xa: NAVYA is a **2025-26** initiative (VIS **2026**).
**Kishori Shakti** (**2000**) and **SABLA** also target adolescent girls.
**STEP** (**1986-87**) = skills for gainful employment of women.

n8431a31ab85.s: STEP, introduced during 1986–87, was designed to promote which of the following?
o: Fast-track trials of crimes against women
Skills for gainful employment of women
n8431a31ab85.x: STEP, or Support to Training and Employment Programme for Women, was introduced in 1986–87 to develop skills for women’s gainful employment.
n8431a31ab85.tq: Link the programme’s historical period with its employment-oriented purpose.
xs: **STEP** (**1986-87**) promotes **skills for gainful employment of women** — option **(4)** is correct.
Fast-track trials were the aim of AP's **Disha** Bill (**2019**); post-birth grants = **Balika Samriddhi**.
xa: **DWCRA** (**1982-83**): groups of rural BPL women, sub-scheme of IRDP.
**Working Women Hostel** (**1972-73**) → now **Sakhi Niwas**.
**NAVYA** gives vocational training to girls **16-18**.

nindian-society-35-35.s: Mission Saksham Anganwadi & POSHAN 2.0 is administered by the Ministry of:
nindian-society-35-35.x: POSHAN 2.0, covering ages 0–6 with Poshan Tracker and Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi, comes under WCD.
n: Mission Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0 includes the Poshan Tracker. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi focuses on early childhood care and education. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Mission Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0 covers the 0–6 age group. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
The nodal ministry for Mission Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0 is the Ministry of Women and Child Development. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Mission Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0 is a key scheme for children. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
xa: Components: **Anganwadi Services**, **Poshan Abhiyaan**, **Scheme for Adolescent Girls**.
The three umbrella missions: **Mission Shakti**, **Mission Vatsalya**, **Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0**.

n8c8db6a18ac.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Sambal sub-scheme?
n8c8db6a18ac.x: One Stop Centre, Women Helpline 181 and Nari Adalat are components of Sambal. Palna is a component of Samarthya.
n8c8db6a18ac.tq: Separate the safety components of Sambal from the empowerment components of Samarthya.
xs: **Palna** is NOT under Sambal — option **(1)**; it is under **Samarthya** (ex-**National Creche Scheme**).
**Nari Adalat**, **Women Helpline 181** and **One Stop Centre** are all **Sambal** (safety) components.
xa: **BBBP** and **SHe-Box 2.0** are also under Sambal.
**OSC** and **181** are funded through the **Nirbhaya Fund**.
⚠ **Sambal** = safety; **Samarthya** = empowerment.

n2afa65bdbb5.s: Shakti Sadan was formed by merging which two earlier schemes?
o: Working Women Hostel and National Creche Scheme
n2afa65bdbb5.x: Shakti Sadan was created by merging Swadhar Greh and Ujjawala under Samarthya.
n2afa65bdbb5.tq: Test the merger relationship while distinguishing it from renamed or reclassified schemes.
xs: **Shakti Sadan** merged **Swadhar Greh and Ujjawala** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Working Women Hostel** became **Sakhi Niwas**; the **National Creche Scheme** became **Palna**.
**Mahila Shakti Kendra** was **discontinued**; **BBBP** sits under Sambal.
xa: **Ujjawala** (**2007**) = anti-trafficking, rescue and rehabilitation.
**Swadhar Greh** = women in difficult circumstances.
AP: **26 Shakti Sadans** sheltered **950** women (AP SES 2025-26).

na5448478800.s: One Stop Centre (Sakhi) provides which services under one roof?
o: Medical, legal, counselling and shelter support
na5448478800.x: One Stop Centre provides medical, legal, counselling and shelter support under one roof and is funded from the Nirbhaya Fund.
xa: **Women Helpline 181**: 24x7, in **34** States/UTs, **84 lakh+** calls till Dec **2022**; being integrated with **ERSS-112**.
AP: OSCs in **all 26 districts**, served **3,590 women**.
Calls exist for **national minimum standards** for OSCs and shelters.

n425e8fadc12.s: Nari Adalat under Mission Shakti is intended primarily for:
o: Alternative grievance redressal in petty cases such as harassment and denial of entitlements
Selection of beneficiaries for LPG connections
Distribution of maternity benefits to government employees
Trial of serious criminal offences by regular courts
n425e8fadc12.x: Nari Adalat provides an alternative grievance-redressal mechanism for petty cases, including harassment and denial of entitlements.
n425e8fadc12.tq: Distinguish alternative local grievance redressal from formal criminal adjudication.
xs: **Nari Adalat** is an **alternate grievance redressal** forum for **petty cases** (harassment, denial of entitlements) — option **(1)** is correct.
It is a **new** component under **Sambal**.
xa: Other Sambal components: **OSC**, **Women Helpline 181**, **BBBP**, **SHe-Box 2.0**.
⚠ Discontinued: **Mahila Shakti Kendra** and **Mahila Police Volunteers**.

nf8d40ce14ac.s: Swadhar Greh is intended primarily for which target group?
nf8d40ce14ac.x: Swadhar Greh is meant for women in difficult circumstances and has now been brought within Shakti Sadan.
nf8d40ce14ac.tq: Identify the target group before considering the scheme’s institutional location.
xs: **Swadhar Greh** is for **women in difficult circumstances** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is now within **Shakti Sadan** (with **Ujjawala**).
Hostels for working women = **Working Women Hostel**/**Sakhi Niwas**; rural savings = **Mahila Samriddhi**; ICDS nutrition = **Kishori Shakti**.
xa: AP: **26 Shakti Sadans** sheltered **950** women; earlier figure **28**.
Shakti Sadan sits under **Samarthya**.

nindian-society-35-16.x: Palna runs crèches; Sakhi Niwas runs working-women hostels and PMMVY gives maternity benefit.
n: Mission Shakti has the Samarthya component. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Samarthya includes the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana maternity benefit. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Samarthya includes Sakhi Niwas working women hostels. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Samarthya includes Palna creches. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Samarthya focuses on empowerment. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
xa: **Sambal** (safety): **One Stop Centres**, **Women Helpline 181**, **BBBP**, **Nari Adalat**.
**Shakti Sadan** merged **Swadhar Greh** and **Ujjawala**.
⚠ **Mahila Shakti Kendra** and **Mahila Police Volunteers** were **discontinued**.

n8475bddafd2.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
o: Ensuring survival, protection and education of the girl child
Arresting the decline in Child Sex Ratio
n8475bddafd2.x: BBBP focuses on the Child Sex Ratio, preventing gender-biased sex selection and the survival, protection and education of girls; legal assistance is not its stated objective.
xa: Launched **2015**, **100% centrally funded**.
**Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana** (**2015**) came under BBBP.
Began in **100** districts, now **all districts**.

n8b3c311adc1.s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao operates under which vertical of Mission Shakti?
n8b3c311adc1.x: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is included under the Sambal vertical, which deals with women’s safety.
n8b3c311adc1.tq: Match the scheme with the correct Mission Shakti vertical.
xs: **BBBP** runs under **Sambal** of Mission Shakti — option **(3)** is correct.
**Samarthya** is the empowerment vertical; **Mission Vatsalya** and **Saksham Anganwadi** are separate umbrella missions.
xa: Sambal also has **OSC**, **181**, **Nari Adalat**, **SHe-Box 2.0**.
BBBP nodal ministry: **Women and Child Development**.
BBBP is **100% centrally funded**.

nf9b31a75fea.s: Which of the following Ministries is NOT involved in implementing Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
nf9b31a75fea.x: BBBP is a joint scheme of MWCD (nodal), Health and Family Welfare, and Education (then HRD). Social Justice and Empowerment is not involved, which was the APPSC 2022 key.
nf9b31a75fea.tq: BBBP: MWCD (nodal) + Health + Education; NOT Social Justice.
xs: **Social Justice & Empowerment** is NOT involved in BBBP — option **(4)** (APPSC **2022** key).
Nodal: **Women and Child Development**; jointly with **Health & Family Welfare** and **Education (then HRD)**.
xa: Launched **2015**; **100% centrally funded**.
Objective: arrest the decline in the **Child Sex Ratio**.
Runs under **Sambal**.

n57ba529c930.s: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (2015), introduced under Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, is:
o: A vocational training scheme for adolescent girls
A post-birth grant for girls of BPL families
A pension scheme for women above 60 years
A small-savings account for a girl below 10 years
n57ba529c930.x: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana, introduced in 2015 under BBBP, is a small-savings account for girls below 10 years, mainly for education and marriage.
xa: ⚠ **Sukanya** (**2015**, savings) vs **Balika** (**1997**, grant) vs **Mahila Samriddhi** (**1993**, rural women's savings).
**Dhanalakshmi** (**2008**): conditional cash transfer incl. delaying marriage beyond **18**.
BBBP was launched in **2015**.

nindian-society-32-6.s: Allocating resources for gender-sensitive programmes is called:
nindian-society-32-6.x: Gender budgeting allocates resources; analysis assesses impacts, planning brings gender into policy and monitoring evaluates outcomes.
n: Gender analysis assesses gender impacts. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 67-70]
Gender planning incorporates gender concerns into policymaking. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 67-70]
Gender budgeting allocates resources for gender-sensitive programmes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 67-70]
Gender monitoring evaluates gender outcomes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 67-70]
xa: Examples: **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao**, **Gender Budget Statements**, **Mission Shakti**, women reservation initiatives.
**BBBP** (**2015**) is **100% centrally funded**, nodal ministry **MWCD**.
⚠ **Social Justice & Empowerment** is **NOT** involved in BBBP (**APPSC 2022**).

n1b086159051.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with the Dhanalakshmi scheme?
o: 1997 – Post-birth grant and scholarships for BPL girls
2008 – Conditional cash transfer for the girl child
n1b086159051.x: Dhanalakshmi (2008) was a conditional cash transfer linked to birth registration, immunisation, schooling and delaying marriage beyond 18.
xa: **SABLA** = nutrition, life-skills, health of adolescent girls; now in **Poshan 2.0**.
**NAVYA** (**2025-26**) trains girls **16-18** via **PMKVY 4.0**.

n2d6f8a2406c.s: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan provides free antenatal check-ups on:
o: The first day of every month
The fifteenth day of every month
The fifth day of every month
The ninth day of every month
n2d6f8a2406c.x: PMSMA provides free antenatal check-ups for all pregnant women on the ninth day of every month.
n2d6f8a2406c.tq: Recall the fixed monthly date associated with PMSMA.
xs: **PMSMA** gives free antenatal check-ups on the **ninth day of every month** — option **(4)** is correct (APPSC **2022** key).
It started in **2016**, for all pregnant women.
xa: ⚠ **PMSMA** = **9th** of every month check-up; **PMMVY** = cash for the first child.
**JSY** (**2005**) = **100%** centrally sponsored cash for institutional delivery under NHM.

n86849d48344.s: Balika Samriddhi Yojana, launched in 1997, provides which of the following benefits?
o: A savings account for girls below 10 years of age
Post-birth grants and annual scholarships for girls belonging to BPL families
Nutrition and life-skills training for adolescent girls under ICDS
Conditional cash transfers for immunisation and delayed marriage
n86849d48344.x: Balika Samriddhi Yojana provides a post-birth grant and annual scholarships to girls from families living below the poverty line.
n86849d48344.tq: Use the scheme-year and benefit together to avoid confusing similar girl-child schemes.
xs: **Balika Samriddhi Yojana** (**1997**) gives a **post-birth grant** and **annual scholarships** to girls of **BPL** families — option **(2)** is correct.
The girl-below-**10** savings account is **Sukanya Samriddhi**; ICDS life-skills = **Kishori Shakti**; conditional cash for immunisation = **Dhanalakshmi**.
xa: ⚠ **Mahila Samriddhi Yojana** (**1993**) = savings habit among rural women.
**Kishori Shakti Yojana** dates from **2000**.
**Dhanalakshmi** dates from **2008**.

nef564cb5725.s: Mahila e-Haat is best described as:
o: A credit scheme exclusively for SC/ST entrepreneurs
An online marketing platform for women entrepreneurs and Self-Help Groups
A maternity cash-transfer programme for pregnant women
A residential shelter for women in distress
nef564cb5725.x: Mahila e-Haat is an MWCD online marketing platform for women entrepreneurs and Self-Help Groups. It was started in 2016 and is run by Rashtriya Mahila Kosh.
nef564cb5725.tq: Identify the function of the platform before associating it with its implementing institution.
xs: **Mahila e-Haat** is an **online marketing platform** for **women entrepreneurs and SHGs** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is an **MWCD** platform from **2016**, run by **Rashtriya Mahila Kosh**.
Credit for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs is **Stand-Up India**.
xa: **RMK** (**1993**) lends to intermediary **NGOs/MFIs**.
**Lakhpati Didi** = SHG member earning at least **₹1 lakh a year**.
About **70% of MUDRA loans** go to women.

nf9673e53fe7.s: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana was launched on 1 May 2016 at:
nf9673e53fe7.x: PMUY, under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, was launched at Ballia (UP) to give LPG connections to women of BPL households.
xa: **Ujjwala 2.0** (Aug **2021**, **Mahoba**): free first refill + hotplate.
Reach: over **10.5 crore households** (**2026**).
⚠ **Ujjwala** (**2016**) = LPG; **Ujjawala** (**2007**) = anti-trafficking.

n10fe1917c66.s: Ujjwala 2.0, launched in August 2021 at Mahoba, provided which additional features?
o: Antenatal care and maternity cash assistance
Free second LPG cylinder and permanent housing for migrants
Free first refill and hotplate, with self-declaration of address for migrant families
Interest-free loans for LPG distributors only
n10fe1917c66.x: Ujjwala 2.0 provided a free first refill and hotplate. Migrant families were permitted to self-declare their address.
n10fe1917c66.tq: Use the launch location and the two distinctive benefits to identify Ujjwala 2.0.
xs: **Ujjwala 2.0** gave a **free first refill and hotplate**, and **migrant families** can **self-declare** address — option **(3)** is correct.
It was launched in **Aug 2021** at **Mahoba**.
xa: The original PMUY was launched on **1 May 2016** at **Ballia (UP)**.
Ministry: **Petroleum & Natural Gas**.
Reach: over **10.5 crore households**.

n82ad12731b3.s: Mahila Samriddhi Yojana, introduced in 1993, seeks to promote which one of the following among rural women?
n82ad12731b3.x: Mahila Samriddhi Yojana was introduced in 1993 to encourage the savings habit among rural women.
n82ad12731b3.tq: Use the beneficiary group and the single core objective to avoid scheme substitution.
xs: **Mahila Samriddhi Yojana** (**1993**) promotes the **habit of saving** among rural women — option **(2)** is correct.
Shelter = **Swadhar Greh**; ICDS nutrition = **Kishori Shakti**; PMKVY training = **NAVYA**.
xa: ⚠ **Mahila Samriddhi** (**1993**) vs **Balika Samriddhi** (**1997**) vs **Sukanya Samriddhi** (**2015**).
**Rashtriya Mahila Kosh** also dates from **1993**.

n9a696354b4b.s: The Rashtriya Mahila Kosh (1993) is a registered society under the:
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Women and Child Development
n9a696354b4b.x: RMK is under the Ministry of WCD and lends to NGOs/MFIs that on-lend micro-credit to poor women; Finance runs Stand-Up India.
xa: ⚠ **Stand-Up India** = **Ministry of Finance**; **Ujjwala** = Petroleum; **DAY-NRLM** = Rural Development.
**Mahila e-Haat** (**2016**) is run by Rashtriya Mahila Kosh.
**Lakhpati Didi**: SHG member earning at least **₹1 lakh a year**.

n4329760a04f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Stand-Up India?
o: It is restricted to existing enterprises only.
It is associated with the Ministry of Finance.
It provides bank loans from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore.
Each bank branch must support at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower.
n4329760a04f.x: Stand-Up India is for new (greenfield) enterprises, not existing ones.
xa: Non-individual firms need **51%** holding by the SC/ST or woman borrower.
**SIDBI** provides handholding.
Launched **2016**.

ned8f737cc5d.s: DAY-NRLM is administered by which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of Women and Child Development
ned8f737cc5d.x: DAY-NRLM is a Ministry of Rural Development programme. It was launched as Aajeevika in 2011 and renamed in 2016.
ned8f737cc5d.tq: Identify the implementing ministry from the rural livelihoods character of the programme.
xs: **DAY-NRLM** is run by the **Ministry of Rural Development** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was launched in **2011 as Aajeevika**, renamed **2016**.
xa: ~**10 crore women** in **90 lakh SHGs** (TH **10 Apr 2026**).
**Lakhpati Didi** = SHG member earning at least **₹1 lakh a year**.
⚠ **Ujjwala** = Petroleum & Natural Gas; **Stand-Up India** = Finance; **RMK** = MWCD.

n30d3cff85a1.s: A woman who is an SHG member and earns at least ₹1 lakh in a year is described under DAY-NRLM as a:
n30d3cff85a1.x: Under DAY-NRLM, an SHG member earning at least ₹1 lakh annually is termed a Lakhpati Didi.
n30d3cff85a1.tq: Use the income threshold and SHG membership to identify the programme label.
xs: An SHG member earning at least **₹1 lakh a year** is a **Lakhpati Didi** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is under **DAY-NRLM** (Ministry of Rural Development).
**Nari Adalat** is a Sambal grievance forum; **Sakhi Niwas** is a women's hostel.
xa: DAY-NRLM: ~**10 crore women** in **90 lakh SHGs**.
**Mahila e-Haat** (**2016**) markets products of women entrepreneurs and SHGs.
About **70% of MUDRA loans** go to women.

n1b1f3f4cefd.s: Stree Mano Raksha, launched in March 2022 for the mental health of women, is a project of the Ministry of Women and Child Development with:
n1b1f3f4cefd.x: Stree Mano Raksha is an MWCD project with NIMHANS, Bengaluru for the mental health of women (APPSC 2021 key). AIIMS and ICMR are not the partners, and NLSIU is the partner in Nirbhay Raho, not this project.
n1b1f3f4cefd.tq: Stree Mano Raksha = MWCD + NIMHANS (mental health).
xs: **Stree Mano Raksha** (Mar **2022**) is MWCD + **NIMHANS, Bengaluru** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC **2021** key).
It is for **women's mental health**.
xa: **OSC (Sakhi)** offers medical, legal, counselling and shelter support.
**Women Helpline 181** is being integrated with **ERSS-112**.
⚠ **Sambal** = safety; **Samarthya** = empowerment.

n16d3b14974c.s: Which of the following initiatives has been discontinued?
o: Mahila Shakti Kendra and Mahila Police Volunteers
One Stop Centre and Women Helpline 181
n16d3b14974c.x: Mahila Shakti Kendra and Mahila Police Volunteers have been discontinued. The other options refer to continuing schemes or sub-schemes.
n16d3b14974c.tq: Identify the discontinued pair rather than choosing active Mission Shakti components.
xs: **Mahila Shakti Kendra and Mahila Police Volunteers** were **discontinued** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Sambal** and **Samarthya** are the live sub-schemes of Mission Shakti.
**OSC**, **181**, **PMMVY** continue (PMMVY completed **nine years** in **2026**).
xa: **Nari Adalat** is a **new** Sambal component.
**Swadhar** and **Ujjawala** continue only within **Shakti Sadan**.

n8cadf3a868f.s: Ujjawala, the women’s welfare scheme, primarily dealt with:
o: Deposit-free LPG connections for poor households
Prevention of trafficking, rescue and rehabilitation
n8cadf3a868f.x: Ujjawala was concerned with prevention of trafficking, rescue and rehabilitation. Deposit-free LPG connections belong to PM Ujjwala Yojana, a separate scheme.
n8cadf3a868f.tq: Separate two look-alike scheme names by comparing their ministry purpose and beneficiary service.
xs: **Ujjawala** (**2007**) dealt with **prevention of trafficking** and **rescue/rehabilitation** of victims — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Free LPG is **Ujjwala** (**2016**), a different scheme.
It is now within **Shakti Sadan**.
xa: **Swadhar Greh** also merged into Shakti Sadan.
**Balika Samriddhi** (**1997**) gives scholarships to BPL girls.
**Sakhi Niwas** = former Working Women Hostel.

nindian-society-35-4.s: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam is which Constitutional Amendment Act?
nindian-society-35-4.x: It is the 106th Amendment, reserving 33% of Lok Sabha and State Assembly seats for women.
n: Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam is the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam provides 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam provides 33% reservation for women in State Legislative Assemblies. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
xa: It is linked to the **Ministry of Law and Justice**.
**Mission Shakti** has two components: **Sambal** (safety) and **Samarthya** (empowerment).

ne75d82b786b.s: Which of the following is NOT a form of untouchability?
o: The two-tumbler system in tea shops
ne75d82b786b.x: Temple-entry denial, residential segregation and the two-tumbler system are forms of untouchability; reservation of seats is a protective measure, not such a practice.
xa: **Manual scavenging** = "the **worst surviving symbol of untouchability**".
PCR offences include barring entry to places of **public worship** and **justifying untouchability**.

naedea5e572b.s: In the context of untouchability, "structural violence" refers to:
naedea5e572b.x: Structural violence, a concept associated with Johan Galtung, is harm built into social structures.
xa: UPPSC **2019** A-R: "Untouchability is the worst form of structural violence" (A) + "practised in the name of religious sanction" (R) → **both true, R explains A**.
Two angles of untouchability: **ritual pollution** + society's "protective" practices.
**Two-tumbler system** = separate tumblers in tea shops.

na3e3d11efcc.s: Article 244A of the Constitution provides for:
o: Reservation in posts for backward classes
na3e3d11efcc.x: Article 244A, inserted by the 22nd Amendment in 1969, provides for an Autonomous State within Assam; 244(1) and 244(2) cover the Fifth and Sixth Schedules.
xa: Sixth Schedule States: **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**.
⚠ Scheduled Areas are declared under the **Fifth Schedule (para 6)**, not Art. 339.

n7fc86f034cf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Article 15(5) permits admission quotas in minority educational institutions.
Article 15(4) provides special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs.
Article 16(4) concerns reservation of posts for inadequately represented backward classes.
n7fc86f034cf.x: Article 15(5) excludes minority educational institutions from its scope.
xa: **16(4A)** = reservation in **promotion** (**77th**, **1995**).
**16(4B)** = carry-forward vacancies outside the **50% ceiling** (**81st**).

nd0de20a9d5f.s: Reservation of seats for SCs and STs in State Legislative Assemblies is provided under Article:
nd0de20a9d5f.x: Article 332 covers State Assemblies and Article 330 the Lok Sabha; there is no SC/ST reservation in the Rajya Sabha.
xa: Seats are in proportion to population; **no separate electorates**.
**Art. 334**: time limit, now till **2030** (**104th Amendment**).
Lok Sabha SC/ST seats: **79/41** (**1971** Census) → **84/47** after the **2008** delimitation.

n028a8cf9499.x: Scheduled Areas are declared under paragraph 6 of the Fifth Schedule; Article 339 provides for Union control and a Commission on their administration.
xa: Art. 339 also lets the Union give **directions to States** on ST schemes.
⚠ **NCST** is under **338A**, not 338.

n17cc3233c46.s: Which of the following constitutional provisions deals with reservation of seats and chairperson posts for SCs and STs in local bodies?
n17cc3233c46.x: Articles 243D and 243T provide for reservation of seats and chairperson posts for SCs and STs in Panchayats and Municipalities, respectively.
n17cc3233c46.tq: Distinguish local-body reservations from Parliament and State Assembly reservations.
xs: **Articles 243D and 243T** reserve SC/ST seats and chairperson posts in **Panchayats/Municipalities** — option **(3)** is correct.
**330/332** are Lok Sabha/Assemblies; **341/342** are the SC/ST lists; **244/275** concern Scheduled Areas and grants.
xa: **244** = Scheduled Areas (Fifth Schedule) and Tribal Areas (Sixth Schedule).
**275(1)** = grants-in-aid for ST welfare.
**Art. 334** time limit now till **2030**.

na8b8f4d285b.s: The number of seats reserved for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha was refixed on the basis of the
o: 1971 Census and 1981 Census through the 42nd and 44th Amendments
1981 Census and 1991 Census through the 73rd and 74th Amendments
1991 Census and 2001 Census through the 84th and 87th Amendments
2001 Census and 2011 Census through the 87th and 91st Amendments
na8b8f4d285b.x: The 84th Amendment refixed the seat numbers on the basis of the 1991 Census, and the 87th Amendment did so on the basis of the 2001 Census.
na8b8f4d285b.tq: Match the Census years with the corresponding amendment numbers.
xs: Seats were refixed on the **1991 Census** (**84th**) and the **2001 Census** (**87th**) — option **(3)** is correct.
The **73rd/74th** are local-body amendments; the **42nd/44th** are not listed for seat refixing.
xa: Lok Sabha SC/ST seats: **79/41** (**1971** Census) → **84/47** after the **2008** delimitation on **Census 2001**.
**51st Amendment (1984)**: ST seats for **Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal, Mizoram**.
⚠ **85th** = consequential seniority, not seat refixing.

nfa2ca50ec31.s: The 51st Constitutional Amendment, 1984, provided for ST seats in the Lok Sabha for
o: Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram
nfa2ca50ec31.x: The 51st Amendment, 1984, provided ST representation in the Lok Sabha for Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram.
nfa2ca50ec31.tq: Test the exact four-State grouping and avoid substituting neighbouring north-eastern States.
xs: The **51st Amendment (1984)** gave ST Lok Sabha seats to **Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram** — option **(3)** is correct.
Assam, Tripura, Manipur, Sikkim and Goa are not in the 51st Amendment list.
xa: Sixth Schedule (**244(2)**) States: **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**.
**244A** = Autonomous State within Assam (**22nd Amendment, 1969**).

n84512b89284.s: Article 16(4A), permitting reservation in promotion for SCs and STs, was inserted by the 77th Amendment (1995) mainly in response to which judicial position?
o: Indra Sawhney (1992) confining reservation under Article 16(4) to initial appointment
E.V. Chinnaiah (2004) treating SCs as a homogeneous class
n84512b89284.x: Indra Sawhney (1992) held that reservation under Article 16(4) applies only at initial appointment, not promotion; the 77th Amendment (1995) responded by inserting Article 16(4A). M. Nagaraj came later and upheld the 77th; Chinnaiah concerns SC sub-classification; Janhit Abhiyan concerns EWS.
xs: The **77th Amendment (1995)** responded to **Indra Sawhney (1992)**, which confined **Art. 16(4)** to **initial appointment** — option **(1)** is correct.
**M. Nagaraj (2006)** came later and upheld the 77th; **E.V. Chinnaiah (2004)** concerns SC sub-classification.
xa: Indra Sawhney also set the **50% ceiling**.
**85th** added consequential seniority w.e.f. **17 June 1995**.
**Davinder Singh (2024)** overruled **Chinnaiah**.

na5bc27c85c6.s: The 89th Amendment (2003) created the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article:
na5bc27c85c6.x: The 89th Amendment split the joint commission into the NCSC (Article 338) and NCST (Article 338A); the Commissions report to the President.
xa: Functions: investigate safeguards, inquire into complaints, **advise on planning**.
Powers: **civil-court powers** while inquiring.
Original Art. 338 had a **Special Officer**.

n0384dd763b7.s: In 2017, the NCRB added a separate crime head for SCs relating to:
o: Being forced to leave residence or facing social boycott
Denial of reservation in educational institutions
n0384dd763b7.x: The 2017 NCRB crime head covered persons forced to leave their residence or facing social boycott. Uttar Pradesh recorded 57 cases under this head that year.
n0384dd763b7.tq: Recall the exact wording of a newly introduced crime category.
xs: The **2017** NCRB head: SCs **forced to leave residence / facing social boycott** — option **(1)** is correct.
**UP** recorded **57** cases that year.
xa: Dalit labourers depend on dominant-caste landowners and **hide complaints** for fear of boycott.
⚠ **Mysore HC**: social boycott of a few individuals is **not** untouchability under Art. 17.

n55f6a9a4995.s: The 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill (April 2026) sought to enlarge the Lok Sabha to how many members?
n55f6a9a4995.x: The Bill sought to amend Articles 330, 332 and 334A and enlarge the Lok Sabha to 850; it was not passed.
xa: The Bill was **not passed** (Apr **2026**).
⚠ **334A** = women's reservation (**106th**, **2023**).

n9d812bee068.s: In the Sabarimala reference, Justice B.V. Nagarathna observed that Article 17 cannot be applied:
o: After the commencement of the Constitution
Only during the annual pilgrimage season
n9d812bee068.x: Justice B.V. Nagarathna stated that Article 17 cannot apply “for three days a month” in the Sabarimala reference.
n9d812bee068.tq: Recall the precise time-related phrase rather than replacing it with a broader limitation.
xs: Justice **B.V. Nagarathna** said Art. 17 cannot apply "**for three days a month**" — option **(2)** is correct.
It was in the **Sabarimala reference** (**8 Apr 2026**).
xa: Art. 17 binds **private persons** too (**PUDR v Union of India**, **1982**).
Haldwani "shuddhikaran" row: **32** SC/ST Congress MPs petitioned the **President** (**8 Sep 2026**).

nd0bb7dc8e1b.s: Article 17 (abolition of untouchability) belongs to which group of Fundamental Rights?
nd0bb7dc8e1b.x: Article 17 is in the Right to Equality group and operates against private persons too; the Constitution does not define 'untouchability'.
xa: Only **Parliament** can prescribe punishment for Art. 17 offences (**Art. 35(a)(ii)**).
**Mysore HC:** untouchability means the practice **as it developed historically**, not the literal sense.
First law enforcing Art. 17: **Untouchability (Offences) Act 1955**, renamed **Protection of Civil Rights Act** in **1976**.

n4e2952cb0e4.s: Who is associated with ensuring that Article 17 made untouchability a punishable offence?
n4e2952cb0e4.x: B.R. Ambedkar ensured that Article 17 constitutionally treated untouchability as a punishable offence.
n4e2952cb0e4.tq: Match the constitutional contribution with the principal figure associated with it.
xs: **B.R. Ambedkar** ensured Art. 17 made untouchability a **punishable offence** — option **(3)** is correct.
He called caste "**a division of labourers**" and preferred the term **Dalit** over 'Harijan'.
xa: ⚠ **Gandhi** coined **'Harijan'** and called untouchability "**a blot on Hinduism**".
Ambedkar led the **Mahad (Chavdar Tank) Satyagraha** on **20 Mar 1927**.
Ambedkar wrote **Annihilation of Caste** (**1936**).

n064de46b480.s: Under Article 35(a)(ii) of the Constitution of India, the power to prescribe punishment for offences under Article 17 belongs to
o: Both Parliament and State Legislatures concurrently
n064de46b480.x: Article 35(a)(ii) gives Parliament, and not the State Legislatures, the power to prescribe punishment for offences relating to Article 17.
n064de46b480.tq: Ask which authority would do this job, while distinguishing Parliament from State Legislatures.
xs: Under **Art. 35(a)(ii)**, only **Parliament** — not State legislatures — can prescribe punishment for Art. 17 offences: option **(1) Parliament alone**.
So the power is not concurrent and not with the courts.
xa: Art. 17 abolishes untouchability; its practice in any form is **forbidden** and **punishable by law**.
Laws enforcing Art. 17: **PCR Act** (**1955**/**1976**) and **SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989**.
Conviction for untouchability offences disqualifies from elections under **Sec. 8, RPA 1951**.

n0c582e8e111.s: The Mysore High Court interpreted 'untouchability' under Article 17 as:
o: The practice as defined in the 1955 Act
Including social boycott of a few individuals
The practice as it developed historically
n0c582e8e111.x: The Mysore HC read it as the historically developed practice, which excludes social boycott of a few individuals.
xa: **Neither the Constitution nor any Act** defines "untouchability".
Critics: because it is undefined, **new indirect forms escape penalty** (**2 Sep 2026**).
Two angles: stigma of **ritual pollution** + practices society uses to "protect" itself from it.

nfc6cf489254.s: Which one of the following is correct about the list of Scheduled Castes of a State?
o: The President notifies it after consulting the Governor.
The State Legislature notifies it by resolution.
The Governor notifies it with the State Legislature's approval.
The National Commission for Scheduled Castes notifies it by order.
nfc6cf489254.x: Under Article 341, the President specifies the Scheduled Castes of a State after consulting the Governor; later inclusion or exclusion can be made only by Parliament by law.
xa: **SC (July 2024)** struck down **Bihar's 2015** resolution merging **Tanti-Tantwa** into the SC list.
First SC list after the Constitution: **Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950**.
⚠ "Article **344**" (CDX) is wrong — 344 is the Official Language Commission.

n425acc2e4ff.s: In Chinthada Anand v. State of Andhra Pradesh, the Supreme Court held that a Scheduled Caste person who converts to Christianity:
o: Cannot claim SC status merely on the basis of earlier caste identity
Can claim SC status on the State Government's recommendation alone
Retains SC status because religion is irrelevant to the SC list
n425acc2e4ff.x: A Christian convert cannot claim SC status merely on earlier caste identity; reconversion requires proof of original SC status, bona fide reconversion and acceptance by the community.
xa: ⚠ By contrast, **ST status is religion-neutral**.
**K.G. Balakrishnan Commission**: SC status for Dalit converts to **Christianity and Islam**, extended to **10 June 2026**.
The Chinthada Anand ruling was in the news in **Jun 2026**.

n7145b46a2b5.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional position regarding Scheduled Tribes?
o: Scheduled Tribe status is decided exclusively by the State Legislature.
Scheduled Tribe status is religion-neutral and the list for a State or Union Territory is specified under Article 342.
Scheduled Tribe status is confined to Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists.
Scheduled Tribe status is determined by the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes without Presidential notification.
n7145b46a2b5.x: Article 342 concerns the specification of Scheduled Tribes, and ST status is not restricted by religion.
n7145b46a2b5.tq: Combine the correct Article with the key SC–ST distinction instead of choosing a familiar but misplaced authority.
xs: ST status is **religion-neutral** and the list is specified under **Article 342** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is not decided by the State Legislature or the NCST; the **President** notifies and **Parliament** alone alters.
xa: ⚠ For SCs, **Christian converts cannot claim SC status** (**Chinthada Anand**).
**366(25)** defines Scheduled Tribes.

n016de7ec4e3.s: The Usha Mehra Commission, constituted in 2007–08, recommended which of the following?
o: Amending Article 341 to enable States to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes
Including all Other Backward Classes in the Scheduled Caste list
n016de7ec4e3.x: The Usha Mehra Commission recommended amendment of Article 341 so that States could undertake sub-categorisation of Scheduled Castes.
n016de7ec4e3.tq: Match a commission with its specific recommendation.
xs: The **Usha Mehra Commission (2007-08)** recommended **amending Art. 341** to let **States sub-categorise SCs** — option **(1)** is correct.
It came after **Chinnaiah (2004)** blocked State sub-classification.
xa: **Davinder Singh (2024)** later held sub-classification **permissible** under **Arts. 14, 15, 16**.
Only **Parliament by law** can alter the SC list under **Art. 341**.
**Telangana** implemented **3** groups in **April 2025**.

n324ec05713e.s: The original form of Article 338 provided for—
o: a non-statutory multi-member commission appointed by the State Governments
a Special Officer designated as the Commissioner for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
a Parliamentary committee for monitoring reservations
a separate National Commission for Scheduled Castes and a separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
n324ec05713e.x: Originally, Article 338 provided for a Special Officer, known as the Commissioner for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, to investigate safeguards and report to the President.
n324ec05713e.tq: Track institutional evolution by identifying the original arrangement before later commissions were created.
xs: Original **Art. 338** provided a **Special Officer** (Commissioner for SCs and STs) — option **(2)** is correct.
He **investigated safeguards** and **reported to the President**.
Separate NCSC and NCST came only with the **89th Amendment (2003)**.
xa: **1978 Resolution**: non-statutory multi-member Commission for SCs and STs; modified in **1987**.
**1990**: the joint commission became **constitutional** (**Art. 338**).
**NCST** from **19 Feb 2004**.

nc571a3839da.s: What does Article 338(9) of the Constitution provide?
o: It empowers the President to create State Commissions for Scheduled Castes
It requires the Union and every State to consult the National Commission for Scheduled Castes on all major policy matters affecting SCs
It gives the NCSC power to amend the Scheduled Caste list
It provides grants-in-aid to State SC Commissions
nc571a3839da.x: Article 338(9) obliges the Union and State Governments to consult the NCSC on major policy matters affecting SCs. It does not empower the President to create State commissions (a trap in CDCA); State SC Commissions are created by State law. The SC list is altered only by Parliament under Article 341, and grants-in-aid are under Article 275(1) for ST welfare.
nc571a3839da.tq: 338(9) = duty to consult NCSC; State SC Commissions come from State law.
xs: **Art. 338(9)** requires the **Union and every State to consult the NCSC** on major policy matters — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ CDCA says 338(9) lets the President create State commissions — **wrong**; State SC Commissions are made by **State law**.
The SC list is altered only by **Parliament** (**Art. 341**); grants-in-aid are **Art. 275(1)**.
xa: NCSC and NCST have **civil-court powers** while inquiring.
AP has a statutory **State SC Commission** (chairman **K.S. Jawahar**).

n815e5ea4117.s: Which of the following is NOT an offence covered by the Protection of Civil Rights law in relation to untouchability?
o: Providing reservation in public employment to an eligible Scheduled Caste candidate
Denying access to shops, hotels and places of entertainment
Barring entry to a place of public worship
Justifying untouchability on religious or traditional grounds
n815e5ea4117.x: The Protection of Civil Rights law covers practices such as denial of temple entry, justification of untouchability and denial of access to public facilities. Providing reservation in public employment is not one of the listed offences.
n815e5ea4117.tq: Find the item outside the statutory list rather than choosing a familiar Scheduled Caste-related provision.
xs: **Providing reservation** to an eligible SC candidate is not a PCR offence — option **(1)** is the answer.
PCR offences: barring entry to **public worship**, **justifying untouchability**, denying access to **shops, hotels, entertainment**.
xa: Insulting an SC member "on the ground of untouchability" = **Sec. 7(1)(d)**.
The PCR Act was the **Untouchability (Offences) Act 1955**, renamed in **1976**.
Conviction disqualifies from elections under **Sec. 8, RPA 1951**.

nc5fccf79a96.s: According to reports associated with the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, which one of the following is NOT listed as a cause of caste atrocities?
nc5fccf79a96.x: Land alienation, bonded labour, indebtedness and non-payment of wages are listed causes. Religious causes are not included in the stated list.
nc5fccf79a96.tq: Find the excluded item in a familiar list rather than selecting a general social factor.
xs: **Religious causes** are NOT listed — option **(1)** (MPPSC **2015** trap).
The **National Commission for SCs & STs (1990)** listed **land alienation**, **bonded labour**, **indebtedness**, **non-payment of wages**.
xa: CDX factors: **caste hierarchy**, **upper-caste dominance**, **rising Dalit activism**, **political interference**.
NCRB (**2017**) added the head "forced to leave residence / facing **social boycott**".

na5c3abe8eb7.s: “I was born a Hindu, but I will not die a Hindu” was declared by B. R. Ambedkar at:
na5c3abe8eb7.x: B. R. Ambedkar made this declaration at Yeola in 1935.
na5c3abe8eb7.tq: Discriminate between a leader’s quotation, place and year.
xs: Ambedkar declared "I was born a Hindu... but I will not die a Hindu" at **Yeola** in **1935** — option **(4)** is correct.
It sits with his other stands: caste is "**a division of labourers**" and **Dalit** over 'Harijan'.
xa: He wrote **Annihilation of Caste** in **1936**.
**Kalaram Temple Entry**: **1930**, Nashik.
**Mahad Satyagraha**: **20 Mar 1927**.

nindian-society-40-6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Manual Scavengers Act, 2013?
o: It prohibits hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks.
It provides for rehabilitation of manual scavengers with alternative livelihoods.
It permits hazardous manual cleaning when done by private contractors.
nindian-society-40-6.x: The 2013 Act bans hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks by anyone, including private contractors, and requires mechanisation and rehabilitation.
n: The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act was passed in 2013. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act completely prohibits hazardous manual cleaning of sewer tanks. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act completely prohibits hazardous manual cleaning of septic tanks. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act mandates mechanization. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act mandates alternative livelihood rehabilitation. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
xa: It also **totally bans** manual cleaning of **unsanitary latrines** and **open drains** without protective gear.
An earlier **1993** Act prohibited manual scavengers and dry latrines.
**SRMS** (**2007**) was subsumed in **NAMASTE**, goal **zero sanitation deaths**.

nindian-society-42-10.s: The Bhikhu Ramji Idate Commission led directly to which scheme?
nindian-society-42-10.x: The Idate Commission surveyed denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic tribes and led to the SEED scheme for their economic empowerment.
n: The Bhikhu Ramji Idate Commission led directly to the formulation of the SEED Scheme. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Bhikhu Ramji Idate Commission concerned Scheduled Castes and De-Notified Tribes (DNTs). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xa: **Justice K.G. Balakrishnan Commission** (**2022**): SC status for Dalit converts to **Christianity and Islam**.
**Rajiv Gauba Committee** (**2024**): the **most backward SC sub-castes** (e.g. **Madigas**).

n594119825a4.s: Which sequence correctly represents the successive extensions of SC/ST reservation in legislatures under Article 334?
n594119825a4.x: The listed extensions were made through the 8th, 23rd, 45th, 62nd, 79th, 95th and 104th Amendments; the 104th extended the reservation up to 2030.
n594119825a4.tq: Track the reservation-extension series separately from promotion and service-related amendments.
xs: Correct sequence: **8th, 23rd, 45th, 62nd, 79th, 95th, 104th Amendments** — option **(1)**.
xa: **95th (2009)** took it from **60 → 70 years**.
⚠ **104th** = **2030** + end of **Anglo-Indian nomination**; **106th** = women's reservation (**334A**).

nindian-society-50-3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Protection of Civil Rights Act?
o: It prescribes penalties for practising untouchability.
It was renamed in 1976 from the Untouchability (Offences) Act.
It came into force on 1 June 1955.
It came into force on 30 January 1990.
nindian-society-50-3.x: The Act came into force on 1 June 1955; 30 January 1990 is the commencement date of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
n: The Protection of Civil Rights Act came into force on June 1, 1955. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Protection of Civil Rights Act was renamed in 1976 from the Untouchability Offences Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Protection of Civil Rights Act prescribes penalties for practicing untouchability. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act came into force on January 30, 1990. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
xa: **January 30, 1990** is when the **SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act** came into force.
The PCR Act enforces **Article 17**.
Only **24 cases** were registered nationwide under the PCR Act in **2023**.

n05437b0b6c9.s: The proviso to Article 335 relating to relaxation of qualifying marks in promotion was enabled by which Constitutional Amendment?
n05437b0b6c9.x: The Eighty-Second Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000 inserted the proviso to Article 335 permitting relaxation of qualifying marks and standards in promotion for SCs and STs.
n05437b0b6c9.tq: Separate the closely placed reservation amendments by their precise subject.
xs: The **82nd Amendment (2000)** added the proviso to **Art. 335** allowing **relaxed qualifying marks** in promotion — option **(3) Eighty-Second** is correct.
**77th (1995)** = 16(4A) promotion quota; **81st** = 16(4B) carry-forward; **85th** = consequential seniority.
⚠ G2 **2024** circulated key said **89th** — that is the **NCSC-NCST bifurcation** amendment.
xa: **M. Nagaraj (2006)** upheld the 77th, 81st, 82nd, 85th but required **quantifiable data**.
⚠ **77th – 82nd – 85th** = promotion quota – relaxed marks – consequential seniority.

nd9187c1e44a.s: The 85th Constitutional Amendment is associated with
o: relaxation in qualifying marks under Article 335
backlog vacancies being treated as a separate class
consequential seniority in promotion under Article 16(4A), with effect from 17 June 1995
reservation of seats for STs in the Lok Sabha
nd9187c1e44a.x: The 85th Amendment provided consequential seniority in promotion under Article 16(4A), with effect from 17 June 1995.
nd9187c1e44a.tq: Use the effective date and the phrase “consequential seniority” as the decisive identifiers.
xs: The **85th Amendment** gave **consequential seniority** in promotion under **16(4A)**, w.e.f. **17 June 1995** — option **(3)** is correct.
Relaxed marks = **82nd**; backlog as a separate class = **81st** (16(4B)); ST Lok Sabha seats = **51st**.
xa: The 85th is dated **2001** (IYB lists **2002**).
**16(4A)** itself was inserted by the **77th (1995)**.
**M. Nagaraj (2006)** upheld the 85th with the **quantifiable data** condition.

n749931348ca.s: Article 16(4B), on carrying forward unfilled reserved vacancies as a separate class, was introduced by the:
n749931348ca.x: The 81st Amendment inserted Article 16(4B); such vacancies are not counted against that year's 50% ceiling.
xa: **M. Nagaraj (2006)** upheld the **77th, 81st, 82nd, 85th** Amendments but required **quantifiable data**.
⚠ **77th – 82nd – 85th** = promotion quota – relaxed marks – consequential seniority.

nb20748fec10.s: In a constituency reserved for SCs or STs in a legislature, the representative is elected by:
o: Only SC/ST voters of the constituency
An electoral college of local bodies
nb20748fec10.x: Reserved seats are proportionate to population, but there are no separate electorates; all voters in the constituency elect the representative.
xa: **Art. 330** = Lok Sabha; **Art. 332** = Assemblies.
AP Assembly: **29 SC + 7 ST** of **175**.
AP SC Lok Sabha seats: **Amalapuram, Bapatla, Chittoor, Tirupati**.

ne658153f88c.s: Which is the ST-reserved Lok Sabha constituency of Andhra Pradesh?
ne658153f88c.x: Araku is AP's only ST Lok Sabha seat; of 25 seats, 4 are SC and 1 is ST.
xa: AP SC Lok Sabha seats: **Amalapuram, Bapatla, Chittoor, Tirupati**.
AP SC population: **84.69 lakh** = **17.08%**.
National: **84 SC, 47 ST** Lok Sabha seats after the **2008** delimitation.

nf3bf4a88fe0.s: What was the principal demand of the Madiga Dandora movement?
o: Categorisation of Scheduled Caste reservations into A–B–C–D groups
nf3bf4a88fe0.x: Madiga Dandora demanded categorisation of Scheduled Caste reservations into A–B–C–D groups, or reservation within reservation.
nf3bf4a88fe0.tq: Distinguish reservation sub-categorisation from general reservation demands.
xs: **Madiga Dandora** demanded **A-B-C-D categorisation** of AP's SC reservation — option **(3)** is correct.
It was the **MRPS** movement (**1994**) led by **Manda Krishna Madiga**.
xa: **Ramachandra Raju Commission (1996)**: **A** (Relli), **B** (Madiga), **C** (Mala), **D** (Adi-Andhra).
**AP Act 2000** fell in **E.V. Chinnaiah (2004)**; **Davinder Singh (2024)** allowed sub-classification.
**Telangana** first implemented SC sub-categorisation (**3** groups, **April 2025**).

n4ca1f59c53b.s: The Madiga Dandora movement alleged that which community dominated the 15 per cent Scheduled Caste quota?
n4ca1f59c53b.x: The movement alleged that the Mala community disproportionately dominated the 15 per cent Scheduled Caste quota, leading to the demand for a separate share.
n4ca1f59c53b.tq: Discriminate between closely related communities in a reservation controversy.
xs: The movement alleged **Mala** dominance of the **15%** SC quota — option **(1)** is correct.
**Madiga** were the complainants; **Relli** and **Adi-Andhra** were groups **A** and **D**.
xa: ⚠ **A – B – C – D** = **Relli – Madiga – Mala – Adi-Andhra**.
**AP** was first to sub-categorise SCs **by law** (**2000**); **Punjab 1975** by circular.
**Usha Mehra Commission (2007-08)** recommended amending **Art. 341** to let States sub-categorise.

nf3825e5a06b.s: The Justice P. Ramachandra Raju Commission placed the Malas in which category of Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Castes?
nf3825e5a06b.x: The Commission grouped SCs into four: A (Relli and others), B (Madiga), C (Mala) and D (Adi-Andhra).
xa: It was implemented by the **AP SC (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act, 2000**.
The Act fell in **E.V. Chinnaiah (2004)**.
The demand came from **Madiga Dandora** (**MRPS, 1994**).

ndf8f1e14de0.s: Which State was the first to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes by legislation, after the Justice Ramachandra Raju Commission process?
ndf8f1e14de0.x: Andhra Pradesh became the first State to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes by statute, through the AP SC (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act, 2000 (Punjab had done so earlier, in 1975, only by an executive circular).
ndf8f1e14de0.tq: Test a superlative linked to a specific legislative milestone.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** was first to sub-categorise SCs **by law** (**AP Act 2000**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Punjab** did so earlier (**1975**) only **by circular**.
**Telangana** was first to **implement** sub-categorisation after **Davinder Singh** (**April 2025**).
xa: The Act followed the **Justice Ramachandra Raju Commission** (**1996**).
It was struck down in **E.V. Chinnaiah (2004)**.
⚠ **A – B – C – D** = **Relli – Madiga – Mala – Adi-Andhra**.

n5b2b3f94212.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh?
o: It treated Scheduled Castes as a single homogeneous class.
It struck down the AP Scheduled Caste (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act, 2000.
It held that sub-classification did not interfere with the Article 341 list.
It examined the State law with reference to the Presidential list under Article 341.
n5b2b3f94212.x: Chinnaiah regarded sub-classification as interfering with the Article 341 Presidential list.
xa: Some notes date the Act **2005**.
**Davinder Singh (2024)**, **7-judge bench, 6:1**, overruled Chinnaiah.
**Usha Mehra Commission (2007-08)** recommended amending **Art. 341**.

n0fc849730c9.s: In State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024), the seven-judge Bench held that sub-classification within Scheduled Castes is permissible when the class is not homogeneous. What was the majority ratio?
n0fc849730c9.x: The seven-judge Bench permitted sub-classification by a majority of 6:1, overruling the position taken in E.V. Chinnaiah.
n0fc849730c9.tq: Test the exact judicial majority using closely spaced numerical distractors.
xs: **Davinder Singh (2024)** was decided **6:1** by a **7-judge bench** — option **(1)** is correct.
It held sub-classification within SCs **permissible** under **Arts. 14, 15, 16** where the class is not homogeneous.
It **overruled Chinnaiah (2004)**.
xa: AP angle: **Madiga Dandora** and the **2000** AP Act started the debate that ended in Davinder Singh.
**Telangana became the first State** to implement it (**April 2025**).
The Centre opposed an **income-based creamy layer** in SC/ST quotas (**7 Aug 2026**).

nb4b60a51419.s: Which case upheld the 77th, 81st, 82nd and 85th Constitutional Amendments, subject to the State showing quantifiable data on specified conditions?
o: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh
Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India
E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh
nb4b60a51419.x: M. Nagaraj upheld the four constitutional amendments but required quantifiable data concerning backwardness, inadequate representation and administrative efficiency.
nb4b60a51419.tq: Associate a cluster of constitutional amendments with the case that examined them.
xs: **M. Nagaraj (2006)** upheld the **77th, 81st, 82nd, 85th** Amendments — option **(3)** is correct.
But the State must show **quantifiable data** on **backwardness**, **inadequate representation** and **administrative efficiency**.
**Davinder Singh** and **Chinnaiah** concern **SC sub-classification**.
xa: ⚠ **77th – 82nd – 85th** = promotion quota – relaxed marks – consequential seniority.
**81st** = **16(4B)** carry-forward vacancies.
**Indra Sawhney (1992)** set the **50% ceiling**.

ne39820d6a99.s: Which State became the first to implement Scheduled Caste sub-categorisation after the Davinder Singh judgment?
ne39820d6a99.x: Telangana became the first State to implement Scheduled Caste sub-categorisation after Davinder Singh, with three groups in April 2025.
