ne39820d6a99.tq: Distinguish the State that enacted the earlier framework from the State that implemented the post-2024 classification.
xs: **Telangana** was first to implement SC sub-categorisation after **Davinder Singh** — option **(1)** is correct.
It made **3** groups in **April 2025**.
**AP** was first by law (**2000**), and **Punjab** first by circular (**1975**) — both before the judgment.
xa: **Davinder Singh (2024)** was decided **6:1**.
AP's **Ramachandra Raju Commission (1996)** made **four** groups.

naf1ef604cff.s: Among economic empowerment measures for disadvantaged communities, NSKFDC is associated with support for:
naf1ef604cff.x: NSKFDC supports sanitation workers; NSFDC covers SCs below the poverty line, PM-DAKSH skill development and VCF-SC economic support for SCs.
xa: **SRMS** (since **2007**) gave a one-time **₹40,000**.

n2c358a6487b.s: Which of the following is NOT a provision of the Manual Scavengers Act, 2013?
o: Identification and rehabilitation of affected persons
Prohibition of cleaning sewers and septic tanks without protective gear
Legalisation of dry latrines under regulated conditions
n2c358a6487b.x: The 2013 Act does not legalise dry latrines.
xa: **58,000** manual scavengers identified, but only **2,652** projects approved.
**498** sewer/septic deaths from **2019** to **June 2026**.

n18ac5835911.s: Caste hierarchy, upper-caste dominance, rising Dalit activism and political interference are identified as factors contributing to:
n18ac5835911.x: All four are identified as factors contributing to caste atrocities.
xa: The **1990** Commission listed land alienation, bonded labour, indebtedness, non-payment of wages.
Dalit labourers **hide complaints** for fear of boycott.
**UP** had **57** social-boycott cases in **2017**.

nbf2d026b09c.s: The Adi-Andhra movement, which claimed Dalits were the original inhabitants of Andhra, was active mainly during the:
nbf2d026b09c.x: The movement was active in the 1910s–30s and demanded access to education, temples and tanks.
xa: **Siddhantam Temple Entry** (**1933**, Krishna district) was one of the earliest in Andhra.
Andhra Dalit papers: **Adi Andhra** (Didla Pullaiah), **Nava Jeevan** (Undru Subbarao).

ncecc9ba7bc9.s: The Karamchedu incident took place in:
ncecc9ba7bc9.x: Karamchedu was in 1985, after the Siddhantam temple entry (1933) and before Tsundur (1991).
xa: Siddhantam was in **Krishna** district.
Tsundur was in **Guntur** district.

n5fe99523072.s: A conviction for an offence relating to untouchability results in disqualification from contesting elections under
o: Section 7 of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1976
Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
n5fe99523072.x: Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides disqualification from contesting elections upon conviction for untouchability offences.
n5fe99523072.tq: Match the consequence with the correct statutory source, not with the constitutional article governing reservation.
xs: Disqualification comes under **Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Sec. 7(1)(d)** of the PCR Act defines an offence (insulting an SC member), not disqualification.
**Art. 244** = Scheduled Areas; **Art. 330** = Lok Sabha seats.
xa: Only **Parliament** can prescribe punishment for Art. 17 offences (**Art. 35(a)(ii)**).
Only **24 cases** were registered under the PCR Act in **2023**; **97%** pendency.

nef19e51b46f.s: Which one of the following is correct under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and Rules?
o: Police investigation must ordinarily be completed within 60 days.
The Act was enacted in 1995 and the Rules framed in 1989.
Vigilance and monitoring committees exist only at the national level.
Police investigation must ordinarily be completed within 90 days.
nef19e51b46f.x: The investigation is to be completed within 60 days; the Act dates from 1989 and the Rules from 1995, with State and district vigilance and monitoring committees.
xa: The **PCR** and **PoA** Acts are overseen by the **Dept of Social Justice**.
AP gives **enhanced monetary relief** and **free legal aid** to PoA victims.
Vigilance committees **meet irregularly** (enforcement gap).

n75d1fbaeca0.s: Which combination is identified as the principal means of abolishing untouchability?
n75d1fbaeca0.x: Untouchability can be addressed through legislation, education and public awareness.
xa: Laws: **PCR Act** and **PoA Act 1989**.
Economic measures: **NSFDC**, **NSKFDC**, **PM-DAKSH**, **VCF-SC**.
Undefined untouchability lets **new indirect forms escape penalty**.

nd7227354216.s: Manual scavenging has been described as the:
o: Oldest surviving form of bonded labour
Worst surviving form of child labour
Last surviving form of forced labour
nd7227354216.x: Manual scavenging is described as the “worst surviving symbol of untouchability.”
xa: **Bezwada Wilson**'s **Safai Karmachari Andolan** campaigns against it (Magsaysay **2016**).
The **2013 Act** bans manual scavengers and unsafe sewer cleaning.
**NAMASTE** aims at **zero sanitation deaths**.

nac024a7e366.s: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 is significant because it was:
o: The first law providing reservation in the Lok Sabha
The first law using the expression Scheduled Tribes
The first law creating the National Commission for Scheduled Castes
nac024a7e366.x: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 was the first law enacted to enforce Article 17. The Government of India Act, 1935 had earlier used the term Scheduled Castes.
nac024a7e366.tq: Distinguish the first enforcement law from the earlier statutory use of the term Scheduled Castes.
xs: The **Untouchability (Offences) Act 1955** was the **first law enforcing Article 17** — option **(3)** is correct.
It was renamed the **Protection of Civil Rights Act** in **1976**.
The NCSC came under **Art. 338**, not this Act.
xa: The **GoI Act 1935** first used "**Scheduled Castes**".
Only **Parliament** can legislate on Art. 17 offences (**Art. 35**).

nindian-society-40-1.s: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 primarily prescribes penalties for which of the following?
o: Denying forest rights to traditional forest dwellers
Enforcing religious and social disabilities arising from untouchability
nindian-society-40-1.x: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, punishes enforcing religious and social disabilities that come from untouchability. Child labour and sex determination fall under other Acts.
nindian-society-40-1.tq: Match each Act to the wrong it punishes.
n: The Protection of Civil Rights Act was passed in 1955. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Civil Rights Act prescribes penalties for enforcing religious and social disabilities arising from untouchability. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act completely bans employing children below 14 in all occupations. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The PCPNDT Act strictly prohibits sex determination. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
xs: The **PCR Act, 1955** prescribes penalties for **enforcing religious and social disabilities arising from untouchability** — option **(2)**.
It **enforces Article 17** and **punishes the practice of untouchability**.
xa: It came into force on **June 1, 1955**.
Offences include barring entry to **public worship** and **justifying untouchability**.
A conviction **disqualifies** from elections under **Sec. 8, RP Act 1951**.

nb3f8b6c1933.s: Which one of the following combinations relating to Vaikom Satyagraha is correct?
o: Travancore — T.K. Madhavan and Keshava Menon — 1924–25
nb3f8b6c1933.x: Vaikom Satyagraha took place in Travancore in 1924–25 and was organised by T.K. Madhavan and Keshava Menon, with K. Kelappan also associated with it.
nb3f8b6c1933.tq: Start with the sure location and verify the corresponding leaders and date.
xs: **Travancore — T.K. Madhavan and Keshava Menon — 1924-25** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Mahad** was Ambedkar's (**1927**); **Nashik** = Kalaram (**1930**); **Krishna district** = Siddhantam (**1933**).
xa: **K. Kelappan** also took part; **Sree Narayana Guru** supported it.
**Periyar** was jailed in it.
⚠ **Mahad** = water (**20 Mar 1927**); **Kalaram** = temple (**1930**).

n341828a8bb4.s: The Mahad Chavdar Tank Satyagraha was led by B.R. Ambedkar to assert the right of Dalits to
o: Draw water from a public tank
Use roads around the Vaikom temple
n341828a8bb4.x: The Mahad Satyagraha, held at Mahad in Maharashtra on 20 March 1927, asserted Dalits’ right to draw water from the public Chavdar Tank.
n341828a8bb4.tq: Identify a movement from its precise immediate objective.
xs: **Mahad (Chavdar Tank) Satyagraha** asserted Dalits' right to **draw water from a public tank** — option **(2)** is correct.
Led by **Ambedkar** on **20 Mar 1927** at Mahad (Maharashtra).
xa: **Centenary (2026-27)** began **20 Mar 2026**.
**Manusmriti Dahan**: **25 Dec 1927**.
⚠ **Kalaram** = temple entry (**1930**, Nashik).

n865884ebc75.s: The Mahad (Chavdar Tank) Satyagraha led by B.R. Ambedkar was held on:
n865884ebc75.x: The Mahad Satyagraha was on 20 March 1927 (centenary from 20 March 2026); the Manusmriti Dahan was on 25 December 1927.
xa: ⚠ **Mahad** = water; **Kalaram** = temple.
Ambedkar led **15,000** volunteers at Kalaram.

n82956d2d4b1.s: Gurram Jashuva’s Gabbilam is based on the idea that
o: A bat can enter a temple while an untouchable cannot
A king grants land to temple servants
A crow carries a message from Buddha to an emperor
A temple priest abolishes caste through ritual
n82956d2d4b1.x: In Gabbilam, an untouchable labourer sends his plea to Lord Shiva through a bat because the bat may enter the temple while he may not.
n82956d2d4b1.tq: Test the central image and social contrast in a literary work.
xs: In **Gabbilam**, a bat may **enter the temple** while the untouchable cannot — option **(1)** is correct.
So the **untouchable labourer** sends his plea to **Lord Shiva** through the bat.
xa: Written by **Gurram Jashuva** in **1941**.
Modelled on **Kalidasa's Meghaduta**.
⚠ **Gabbilam** = bat (**1941**); **Gulamgiri** = slavery (**1873**).

n933958792d4.s: Karamchedu, Tsundur and Khairlanji are respectively associated with which States?
o: Andhra Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra
Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
n933958792d4.x: Karamchedu and Tsundur occurred in Andhra Pradesh, while Khairlanji occurred in Maharashtra.
n933958792d4.tq: Use location pairing to distinguish closely related atrocity incidents.
xs: **Karamchedu** — AP; **Tsundur** — AP; **Khairlanji** — **Maharashtra**: option **(1)** is correct.
**Karamchedu** (**17 Jul 1985**): then Prakasam, now Bapatla; **Tsundur** (**6 Aug 1991**): Guntur.
**Khairlanji** (**29 Sep 2006**): Bhandara district.
xa: Karamchedu **sparked the independent Dalit movement**.
**Hathras** (**2020**, UP): SC entrusted monitoring to the **Allahabad HC**.

n70af21c5bb3.s: Karamchedu incident is associated with which one of the following descriptions?
o: It resulted in monitoring by the Allahabad High Court.
It involved four members of a Dalit family in Bhandara district.
It led to the creation of the NCRB crime head for social boycott.
It sparked the independent Dalit movement.
n70af21c5bb3.x: The Karamchedu incident of 1985, in which Madiga Dalits were killed by dominant-caste landlords, sparked the independent Dalit movement.
n70af21c5bb3.tq: Identify the distinctive consequence attached to the incident.
xs: **Karamchedu** **sparked the independent Dalit movement** — option **(4)** is correct.
Madiga Dalits were killed by dominant-caste landlords (**17 Jul 1985**).
Allahabad HC monitoring = **Hathras**; Bhandara = **Khairlanji**.
xa: APP gives **1985**; CDX prints **1982**.
Then Prakasam district, now **Bapatla**.

nindian-society-42-12.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Rajiv Gauba Committee?
o: It concerned SC sub-castes such as the Madigas.
It was a Cabinet Secretary panel constituted in 2024.
It examined equitable mechanisms for the most backward SC sub-castes.
It was set up by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to examine ST status for the Madigas.
nindian-society-42-12.x: The Gauba panel was a 2024 Cabinet Secretary panel on the most backward SC sub-castes such as the Madigas; it was not a Tribal Affairs body and did not examine ST status.
n: The Rajiv Gauba Committee explored equitable administrative mechanisms for the most backward sub-castes among Scheduled Castes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Rajiv Gauba Committee was a Cabinet Secretary panel formed in 2024. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Rajiv Gauba Committee explored alternative interventions for the most backward sub-castes among Scheduled Castes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
Madigas were cited as an example of the most backward Scheduled Caste sub-castes considered by the Rajiv Gauba Committee. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Rajiv Gauba Committee was formed by the Central Government through the Department of Personnel and Training. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Rajiv Gauba Committee concerned Scheduled Castes (SCs). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xa: **Idate Commission** (**2017**) → **SEED Scheme**.
**K.G. Balakrishnan Commission** extended till **10 June 2026**.
**Davinder Singh** (**2024**) allowed sub-classification within SCs.

n590877d0f51.s: The first Dalit organisation in Hyderabad State was established by Bhagya Reddy Varma under the name
n590877d0f51.x: Bhagya Reddy Varma established Jagan Mitra Mandali in 1906, described as the first Dalit organisation in Hyderabad State.
n590877d0f51.tq: Match the organisation with its founder and year.
xs: **Bhagya Reddy Varma** founded **Jagan Mitra Mandali (1906)**, the first Dalit organisation in Hyderabad State — option **(2)** is correct.
His **Adi Hindu Social Service League** came later (originally **Manya Sangham**, **1911**).
**Harijan Sevak Sangh** was Gandhi's (**1932**), which Varma **criticised as paternalistic**.
xa: **Adi Andhra** (paper) = **Didla Pullaiah**; **Nava Jeevan** = **Undru Subbarao**.
The **Adi-Andhra movement** (**1910s-30s**) claimed Dalits were Andhra's original inhabitants.

n8aceebf725f.s: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 derives its constitutional basis primarily from:
n8aceebf725f.x: The Act was enacted to give effect to Article 17 of the Constitution, which abolishes untouchability.
n8aceebf725f.tq: Match the legislation with its specific constitutional provision.
xs: The **PCR Act** was enacted under **Article 17**, which abolishes untouchability — option **(4)** is correct.
It began as the **Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955** and was **renamed in 1976**.
xa: It extends to the **whole of India** (APPSC **2019** key).
**PCR Rules** were notified in **1977**.
⚠ **PCR 1955** vs **PoA 1989** (in force **30 January 1990**, Rules **1995**).

nc7f2f18ee37.s: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 was originally enacted as the:
nc7f2f18ee37.x: It was enacted under Article 17 as the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 and renamed in 1976; it extends to the whole of India.
xa: ⚠ The old UPSC note that the **PoA Act** excludes **J&K** is outdated — it applies there since **2019**.
PCR Rules: **1977**.

n025c213bad7.s: Offences under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 are:
o: Non-cognizable and triable only by a Sessions Court
Cognizable only with prior sanction of the State Government
n025c213bad7.x: Under Section 15, offences under the PCR Act are cognizable and may be tried summarily; they are also non-compoundable (MPPSC 2019 accepted both descriptions). They are not non-cognizable or compoundable, are not reserved for Sessions Courts, and need no prior sanction.
n025c213bad7.tq: PCR offences: cognizable, summary trial, non-compoundable.
xs: PCR offences are **cognizable and triable summarily** — option **(2)** is correct (**Sec. 15**).
They are also **non-compoundable**; MPPSC **2019** accepted both descriptions.
They are not non-cognizable, not Sessions-only, and need no prior sanction.
xa: First offence: **1-6 months** and **₹100-500** fine.
**PoA** offences are also **cognizable** — arrest without warrant.

n883d076c5e3.s: Which of the following is NOT a provision associated with the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
o: Grant of arms licences to members of SCs and STs
Enhanced punishment for public servants in specified circumstances
Cancellation of arms licences in atrocity-prone areas
Automatic dissolution of every local authority located in an atrocity-prone area
n883d076c5e3.x: The Act provides for cancellation of arms licences of potential offenders in atrocity-prone areas, licences for SC/ST persons and enhanced punishment for public servants. It does not provide for automatic dissolution of local authorities.
n883d076c5e3.tq: Find the option that introduces an institutional consequence not connected with the Act’s stated safeguards.
xs: **Automatic dissolution of local authorities** is not a PoA provision — option **(4)** is the answer.
The Act **cancels arms licences** of potential offenders in **atrocity-prone areas** and gives **licences to SC/ST persons**.
It gives **enhanced minimum punishment** for public servants.
xa: States identify **atrocity-prone areas**.
**Sec. 4** punishes **wilful neglect of duty**.

nindian-society-36-6.s: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act was enacted in which year?
nindian-society-36-6.x: The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act was passed in 2018, restoring safeguards after a Supreme Court ruling. The Protection of Civil Rights Act dates from 1955.
nindian-society-36-6.tq: Discriminate the 1955 Act from the 2018 amendment.
n: The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act was enacted in 2018. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 79-81]
xs: The **SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act** was enacted in **2018** — option **(3)**.
**1955** is the year of the **Protection of Civil Rights Act**.
xa: The 2018 Act inserted **Sec. 18A**: no **preliminary enquiry** and no **approval** before arrest.
It answered **Subhash Kashinath Mahajan** (**20 March 2018**).
**Prithvi Raj Chauhan** (Feb **2020**) upheld the 2018 amendment.

n091cb9d5b8e.s: Under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, Section 10A provides for:
n091cb9d5b8e.x: Section 10A provides for a collective fine; Section 5 covers refusal of admission and Section 12 the presumption.
xa: ⚠ **PCR Sec. 14** = companies; **PoA Sec. 14** = Special Courts.
**Sec. 6** = refusing to sell goods or render services.

n7c995db7519.s: Which one of the following is correct about Special Courts under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act?
o: They are set up in each district with the concurrence of the High Court Chief Justice.
They are set up by the Supreme Court without consulting the State judiciary.
Exclusive Special Courts were part of the original 1989 Act.
Trials under the Act are held only by ordinary Magistrates.
n7c995db7519.x: Special Courts are set up in each district with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court; Exclusive Special Courts were added by the 2015 amendment.
xa: **Sec. 14** = Special Courts; **14A** = appeal to the HC within **90 days**.
AP: **14 Special Sessions Courts + 1 Exclusive Court** (**Laxmipet, Srikakulam**).

nd5f48bbf510.s: An appeal from an order of a Special Court under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, including an order relating to bail, lies to the High Court within:
nd5f48bbf510.x: An appeal, including an appeal against a bail order, lies to the High Court within 90 days.
nd5f48bbf510.tq: Test the appellate time limit separately from the investigation and trial timelines.
xs: Appeal from a Special Court order (incl. bail) lies to the **High Court within 90 days** — option **(3)** is correct.
This is **Sec. 14A**, added in **2015**.
**60 days** is the charge-sheet limit under the **Rules, 1995**.
xa: **Sec. 19** = no probation for convicts.
**Sec. 18** = anticipatory bail barred.

n7facf7e8a78.s: The SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 came into force on:
n7facf7e8a78.x: Passed in 1989, it came into force on 30 January 1990; Section 18 bars anticipatory bail and Section 19 probation.
xa: **18A** (**2018**): no preliminary enquiry or approval before arrest.
**Kiran v Rajkumar Jivaraj Jain (2025)**: Sec. 18 bar applies where a **prima facie case** exists.

nfe8bfc348c4.s: Which of the following cases is associated with the Supreme Court directions that were perceived as diluting the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
o: Prithvi Raj Chauhan v. Union of India
Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v. State of Maharashtra
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
nfe8bfc348c4.x: In Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v. State of Maharashtra, decided on 20 March 2018, the Supreme Court issued directions concerning preliminary enquiry, anticipatory bail and prior approval for arrest.
nfe8bfc348c4.tq: Use the case-name and outcome association to distinguish closely related judgments.
xs: **Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v State of Maharashtra** (**20 March 2018**) was seen as **diluting** the Act — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC G2 **2024** key).
**Prithvi Raj Chauhan** (**2020**) **upheld** the 2018 restoring amendment; **Kiran (2025)** cancelled an anticipatory bail.
**Indra Sawhney** is a reservation case.
xa: Mahajan: **preliminary enquiry** before FIR, **anticipatory bail**, **prior approval** before arrest.
The **2018** Amendment inserted **Sec. 18A** to undo it.

nb068b19a60b.s: The Supreme Court decided Prithvi Raj Chauhan v. Union of India in:
nb068b19a60b.x: Prithvi Raj Chauhan came in February 2020, after the Mahajan judgment (2018) and its recall (2019).
xa: **Sec. 18A** came by the **2018** Amendment Act.
Model answer angle: the **2018** episode (**Mahajan → 18A**).

n2e3e9160ab5.s: In Kiran v. Rajkumar Jivaraj Jain (2025), the Supreme Court:
o: Declared Section 18 of the Atrocities Act unconstitutional.
Directed that a preliminary enquiry must precede every arrest.
Cancelled an anticipatory bail granted by a High Court and held that no mini-trial should be conducted at the bail stage.
Upheld anticipatory bail despite the existence of a prima facie case.
n2e3e9160ab5.x: The Supreme Court cancelled the High Court's anticipatory bail, held that Section 18 applies where a prima facie case exists and stated that a mini-trial is impermissible at the bail stage.
n2e3e9160ab5.tq: Match the latest case with its precise procedural holding, not with the earlier Mahajan directions.
xs: **Kiran v Rajkumar Jivaraj Jain (2025)** **cancelled an HC anticipatory bail** and barred a **mini-trial** at the bail stage — option **(3)** is correct.
It held the **Sec. 18** bar applies where a **prima facie case** exists — so Sec. 18 was not struck down.
xa: **Madras HC**: **no preliminary inquiry** before an FIR.
**Chauhan (2020)** allowed bail only where **no prima facie case** exists.

n515e0af9390.s: The first-offence punishment under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 is generally stated as:
o: Imprisonment from one to six months and fine from ₹100 to ₹500
Imprisonment up to three years without fine
Imprisonment from six months to one year and fine from ₹500 to ₹1,000
n515e0af9390.x: For a first offence, the stated punishment is imprisonment of one to six months and a fine of ₹100 to ₹500. The older wording is also expressed as imprisonment up to six months or fine up to ₹500 or both.
n515e0af9390.tq: Read the range carefully and avoid replacing a statutory range with a single figure.
xs: First offence: **imprisonment 1-6 months** and **fine ₹100-500** — option **(1)** is correct.
Older wording: "up to **6 months** or fine up to **₹500** or both".
xa: Offences are **cognizable**, triable **summarily** and **non-compoundable** (**Sec. 15**).
A convict is **disqualified** from contesting Parliament/State legislature.
**Sec. 10A** allows a **collective fine** on an area's inhabitants.

n5fbc5998490.s: Which Ministry is the nodal Ministry at the Union level for the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
n5fbc5998490.x: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is the nodal ministry, with the Ministry of Home Affairs also associated with implementation.
xa: On the ground, the Act is implemented by **State Govts/UT administrations**.
MoSJE also administers the **2013 manual scavenging Act**.

n6db445dae73.s: Under the 2015 amendment, the trial in an Exclusive Special Court is intended to be completed within:
o: 60 days of filing of the charge-sheet
90 days of arrest of the accused
30 days of registration of the FIR
n6db445dae73.x: The amendment envisages completion of trial within two months, that is, 60 days, from the filing of the charge-sheet.
n6db445dae73.tq: Convert the stated period of two months into the precise numerical option and note the starting point.
xs: Trial is to finish, as far as possible, **within two months** (**60 days**) of the **charge sheet** — option **(2)** is correct.
This came with the **2015** amendment's **Exclusive Special Courts**.
xa: Special Courts can take **direct cognizance**.
Charge-sheet itself is due within **60 days** (Rules, 1995).

n187454b4d2a.s: The 2015 amendment to the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act introduced a new chapter on:
n187454b4d2a.x: The 2015 amendment introduced a new chapter on the rights of victims and witnesses.
xa: It also added **Exclusive Special Courts** and direct cognizance.
PoA Rules give **travel/maintenance** for victims and witnesses.
Centre's task force (**2026**) suggested **counselling** and **State relief cells**.

n6cd02e3847d.s: Under the 2015 amendment to the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, economic boycott and social boycott were:
o: Left to the Protection of Civil Rights Act
n6cd02e3847d.x: The 2015 amendment defined economic and social boycott and made them offences amounting to atrocities.
xa: ⚠ They were added, not removed, and are in the **PoA Act**, not just the PCR Act.
PCR **Sec. 10A** = collective fine; atrocity-prone areas allow cancelling arms licences.

n092f40c60ee.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the significance of the Supreme Court's decision in Sukanya Shantha (2024)?
o: Article 17 applies only to physical exclusion from public wells and temples.
Article 17 permits purity-based distinctions when followed by customary communities.
Article 17 concerns only untouchability imposed by private employers.
n092f40c60ee.x: The Sukanya Shantha decision held that Article 17 bars caste-based purity stigma, expanding the understanding of untouchability beyond narrow physical exclusion.
n092f40c60ee.tq: Apply the constitutional provision to the precise form of discrimination identified by the judgment.
xs: **Sukanya Shantha (2024)** held that **Article 17 bars caste-based purity stigma** — option **(2)**.
The case came up again when a post-rally "**Shuddhikaran**" ritual revived the **untouchability** debate (2 Sep 2026).
So Art. 17 is not limited to physical exclusion and does not permit purity-based distinctions.
xa: "Untouchability" is **not defined** in the Constitution or the Act; the **Mysore HC** read it as the historically developed caste practice.
The **PCR Act** was enacted under **Art. 17** as the **Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955**, renamed in **1976**.
**PCR Sec. 7** punishes **preaching or justifying untouchability** and insulting an SC member on this ground.

n76aa66545be.s: A person convicted under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 is also subject to which electoral consequence mentioned in the law?
o: Permanent disqualification from voting in all elections
Disqualification from holding any private office
Disqualification from contesting elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
n76aa66545be.x: A person convicted under the Act is disqualified from contesting elections to Parliament or a State Legislature.
n76aa66545be.tq: Distinguish the specified electoral consequence from broader penalties not attached to the provision.
xs: A PCR convict is **disqualified from contesting** elections to **Parliament and State Legislatures** — option **(4)** is correct.
The law does not bar voting or remove a person from employment.
xa: ⚠ PCR offences also cover **justifying untouchability** and insulting SC persons.
First-offence punishment: **1-6 months** and **₹100-500** fine.
Offences are **cognizable**.

nfbb36ce74e0.s: Which one of the following is the correct combination regarding investigation under the SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Rules, 1995?
o: Investigation by an officer not below DSP rank; charge-sheet within 60 days
Investigation by an officer not below Inspector rank; charge-sheet within 30 days
Investigation by an officer not below Superintendent of Police rank; charge-sheet within 90 days
Investigation by an Executive Magistrate; charge-sheet within 60 days
nfbb36ce74e0.x: Investigation is to be conducted by a police officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police, and the investigation and filing of the charge-sheet are to be completed within 60 days.
nfbb36ce74e0.tq: Start from the sure pair of investigating rank and then verify the prescribed time limit.
xs: Investigation by an officer **not below DSP**; charge-sheet within **60 days** — option **(1)** is correct.
These are the **PoA Rules, 1995**.
xa: A High Court questioned a probe that changed hands **six** times, **26 months** past the **60-day** limit.
**97%** pendency rate.
Annual report goes to **Parliament**.

n636e75c6831.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the machinery for prevention of atrocities?
o: The State Vigilance and Monitoring Committee is chaired by the Chief Minister.
SC/ST Protection Cells function under an IG or ADGP of Police.
A Secretary-level nodal officer is designated in each State.
The District Vigilance and Monitoring Committee is chaired by the Superintendent of Police.
n636e75c6831.x: The District Vigilance and Monitoring Committee is chaired by the Collector.
xa: AP drew up an **SOP** with Police, Revenue, Judiciary and Welfare.
AP's Director of Prosecutions held a review in **Vijayawada** (**19 Jul 2026**) on **digital evidence**.

nc0bf59ba32d.s: Which legislation prohibited the employment of manual scavengers and the construction of dry latrines?
o: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
The Employment of Manual Scavengers and Construction of Dry Latrines (Prohibition) Act, 1993
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013
nc0bf59ba32d.x: The 1993 Act prohibited employing manual scavengers and constructing dry latrines. The 2013 Act subsequently widened the prohibition and rehabilitation framework.
nc0bf59ba32d.tq: Discriminate between the similarly named 1993 and 2013 enactments by their distinct scope.
xs: The **1993 Act** banned employing **manual scavengers** and **construction of dry latrines** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **2013 Act** later added the sewer/septic-tank ban and rehabilitation.
xa: **Safai Karamchari Andolan v UoI (2014)**: **₹10 lakh** per sewer death since **1993**.
Raised to **₹30 lakh** in **2023** (**Balram Singh**).

n17dcc9d8669.s: The National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation was established in which year and serves as the nodal agency for which scheme?
o: 1997 — Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers
n17dcc9d8669.x: NSKFDC was established in 1997 and is the nodal agency for the Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers.
n17dcc9d8669.tq: Combine the founding year with the exact scheme name to avoid confusing it with later programmes.
xs: **NSKFDC** was set up in **1997** and is the nodal agency for the **Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers** — option **(2)** is correct.
**1993** is the dry latrines Act; **2013** the Manual Scavengers Act; **2014** the SC compensation order.
xa: **NAMASTE (2023)** subsumed SRMS.
**Swachhata Udyami Yojana (2026)**: capital subsidy **₹5 lakh → ₹7.5 lakh**.

n1f235f18ce1.s: Which body monitors the implementation of measures relating to manual scavenging and rehabilitation?
n1f235f18ce1.x: The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis monitors implementation in this field.
n1f235f18ce1.tq: Match the specialised statutory subject with the institution specifically associated with it.
xs: The **National Commission for Safai Karamcharis (NCSK)** monitors — option **(1)** is correct.
**Vigilance Committees** also oversee the **2013 Act**.
xa: The Act is administered by **Social Justice & Empowerment**.
⚠ Sewer-death compensation: **₹10 lakh** (**2014**) → **₹30 lakh** (**2023**).

n2e6b588caa0.s: Which of the following correctly reflects the compensation developments relating to sewer deaths?
o: ₹10 lakh was ordered in 2014 and raised to ₹30 lakh in 2023
₹30 lakh was ordered in 2014 and reduced to ₹10 lakh in 2023
₹10 lakh was ordered in 1993 and raised to ₹50 lakh in 2014
₹5 lakh was ordered in 2014 and raised to ₹10 lakh in 2023
n2e6b588caa0.x: Safai Karamchari Andolan v. Union of India involved ₹10 lakh compensation, which was raised to ₹30 lakh in 2023 in Balram Singh.
n2e6b588caa0.tq: Track the sequence of the original ruling and the later enhancement rather than reversing the amounts.
xs: Sewer-death compensation: **₹10 lakh** was ordered in **2014** and **raised to ₹30 lakh in 2023** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Safai Karamchari Andolan v Union of India (2014)**: the SC ordered **₹10 lakh** for each sewer death since **1993**.
The **₹30 lakh** figure came in **2023** in the **Balram Singh** case — compensation was raised, never reduced, so option (2) reverses the order.
xa: The **Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013** bans hazardous cleaning of **sewers and septic tanks** without protective gear.
Under the 2013 Act, hazardous sewer cleaning is punishable with up to **2 years / ₹2 lakh**.
The earlier **Employment of Manual Scavengers and Construction of Dry Latrines (Prohibition) Act, 1993** banned employing manual scavengers and building dry latrines.
**NAMASTE (2023)** aims at **zero sanitation fatalities**.

n3fb9bf0c5ee.s: NAMASTE, launched in 2023, is associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Replacing all State Vigilance and Monitoring Committees
Formalising sewer and septic-tank workers and achieving zero sanitation fatalities
Constructing only dry latrines in rural areas
Providing compensation exclusively for denial of public-space access
n3fb9bf0c5ee.x: NAMASTE formalises sewer and septic-tank workers, subsumed the Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers, and aims at zero sanitation fatalities.
n3fb9bf0c5ee.tq: Identify the programme through its worker-formalisation and safety objective, not through a general sanitation function.
xs: **NAMASTE (2023)** aims at **formalising sewer and septic-tank workers** and achieving **zero sanitation fatalities** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It **subsumed SRMS** — the **Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers**.
**Vigilance and Monitoring Committees** are bodies under the **PoA Rules 1995**, not replaced by NAMASTE; the **2013 Act** in fact requires building **sanitary latrines**, not dry latrines.
xa: **NSKFDC (1997)** was the nodal agency for the Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers.
**Swachhata Udyami Yojana (2026)**: individual capital subsidy raised from **₹5 lakh → ₹7.5 lakh** (Aug 2026).
The **2013 Act** makes local authorities **survey** manual scavengers and build sanitary latrines within **3 years**; the **NCSK** monitors it.
⚠ Sewer-death compensation: **₹10 lakh** (2014, Safai Karamchari Andolan) → **₹30 lakh** (2023, Balram Singh).

n7e003a5c035.s: Offences under the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 are:
o: Civil wrongs punishable only with fine
Compoundable and triable only by the NCSK
n7e003a5c035.x: Offences under the 2013 Act are cognizable and non-bailable; a first contravention attracts up to 1 year or Rs 50,000, and hazardous sewer cleaning up to 2 years or Rs 2 lakh. They are not non-cognizable or bailable, not mere civil wrongs, and the NCSK monitors the Act; it does not try offences.
xs: Offences under the **2013 Manual Scavengers Act** are **cognizable and non-bailable** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Punishment: first contravention up to **1 year / ₹50,000**; hazardous sewer cleaning up to **2 years / ₹2 lakh** — so they are crimes, not mere civil wrongs.
The **NCSK** only **monitors** the Act; it does not try offences.
xa: Oversight under the Act is through **Vigilance Committees**; it is administered by the **Dept of Social Justice & Empowerment**.
Local authorities must **survey** manual scavengers and build **sanitary latrines** within **3 years**.
The Act also bans hazardous cleaning of **sewers and septic tanks** without protective gear.
⚠ Compare: **PCR Act** offences are **cognizable** and **non-compoundable** / triable **summarily**.

nc156c3a4ae5.s: Which of the following is correct about the expression 'untouchability'?
o: It is expressly defined in the Constitution.
It is expressly defined in the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.
The Mysore High Court interpreted it as a historically developed caste practice.
It is defined in both the Constitution and the 1955 Act.
nc156c3a4ae5.x: The term is defined in neither the Constitution nor the Act; the Mysore High Court read it as the historically developed practice.
xa: The Act is based on **Art. 17**.
**Sukanya Shantha (2024)** held Art. 17 bars **caste-based purity stigma**.

nd8958dda78c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
o: It creates offences not covered by the PCR Act or the IPC.
Section 3 deals with atrocities by persons who are not SC/ST members.
It applies only when the accused and victim belong to the same SC or ST.
Section 18 bars anticipatory bail for the accused.
nd8958dda78c.x: The Act principally covers offences by non-SC/ST persons against SC/ST persons.
xa: PoA Act: passed **1989**, in force **30 January 1990**, **23 sections**.
**Sec. 4** punishes **wilful neglect of duty** by public servants.

n0e6b8e12648.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and its 2015 amendment?
o: Denying access to irrigation facilities may be an atrocity.
Forcing a person to do manual scavenging may be an atrocity.
Calling a woman a witch is among the specified atrocities.
The Act applies only when the accused and victim belong to the same SC or ST.
n0e6b8e12648.x: The Act principally covers offences by non-SC/ST persons against SC/ST persons.
xa: Also: **obstructing voting**; digging graves; **social or economic boycott**.
The amendment came **in force from 2016**.

nd818ccd1638.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Subhash Kashinath Mahajan v. State of Maharashtra?
o: It contemplated a preliminary enquiry before registering an FIR.
It allowed anticipatory bail where no prima facie case existed.
It required prior approval of the appointing authority before arresting a public servant.
nd818ccd1638.x: The Mahajan directions (March 2018) were recalled on review in October 2019.
xa: The directions were **recalled** on review (Oct **2019**).
⚠ **2018** sequence: Mahajan → **18A** → review → **Chauhan** (Feb **2020**).

n37a1ecddf55.s: As per NCRB data for 2024, crimes against Scheduled Tribes declined by:
n37a1ecddf55.x: Crimes against STs fell by 23.1% and against SCs by 3.6%.
xa: The **NCRB** released Crime in India 2024 in **May 2026**.
In **2023**, crimes against SCs had risen **+0.4%** and against STs **+28.8%**.
Denial of access to public spaces (PoA): **180** cases in **2023**, **173 in UP**; **305** in **2022** (**300** in UP).
**AP**: crime rate **27.4 per lakh SC population** (**SDG India Index 2023-24**).

n0b50b9ef24d.s: Andhra Pradesh's Exclusive Court for SC/ST atrocity cases is located at:
n0b50b9ef24d.x: AP has 14 Special Sessions Courts and one Exclusive Court at Laxmipet, Srikakulam, with an SOP involving Police, Revenue, Judiciary and Welfare.
xa: Crimes against SCs/STs in AP **fell 24.32% in 2025** (Home Minister, 1 Jan 2026); the DGP reported a **30%** fall.
The Director of Prosecutions held a State-level review in **Vijayawada** (19 Jul 2026) → guidelines on **digital evidence** and timely charge-sheets.
AP crime rate: **27.4 per lakh SC population** (**SDG India Index 2023-24**).
Relief is paid under a **centrally sponsored scheme**, **50:50** Centre-State.

n091e4e7dcd5.s: The Mandal Commission was appointed under Article:
n091e4e7dcd5.x: Article 340 lets the President appoint a commission on the conditions of SEBCs; the Constitution does not define 'backward classes'.
xa: **Kaka Kalelkar** (**1953**) was the first Backward Classes Commission; **B.P. Mandal** (**1979**) the second.
Correct term = **Socially and Educationally** Backward Classes — ⚠ IYB's "Socially and Economically" is wrong.
**Art. 366(26C)** defines SEBCs by reference to **Art. 342A** (102nd).
**First AP BC Commission**: **Anantharaman Commission**, report **1970**.

n11fe97ba28c.s: The First Backward Classes Commission (1953) was chaired by:
n11fe97ba28c.x: Kaka Kalelkar chaired the First Commission (1953); B.P. Mandal chaired the Second (1979).
xa: Kalelkar reported in **1955**; Mandal in **1980**, estimating OBCs at **52%** of population.
Mandal used **11 indicators** — social, educational, economic.
Mandal recommended **27%** for OBCs; implemented by **V.P. Singh** in **1990**.

neaff0428529.s: The First Backward Classes Commission was appointed in which year, and its report was submitted in which year?
neaff0428529.x: The First Backward Classes Commission was appointed in 1953 and submitted its report in 1955. It was headed by Kaka Kalelkar.
neaff0428529.tq: Separate the appointment year from the report year instead of treating them as the same date.
xs: The First Backward Classes Commission was appointed in **1953** and reported in **1955** — option **(1)**.
It was headed by **Kaka Kalelkar**, set up under **Art. 340** by the **Nehru** Government.
**1979 and 1980** are the **Mandal** Commission's set-up and report years; **1990 and 1993** are Mandal's implementation years.
xa: Kalelkar listed about **2,399** castes; its report was **not implemented**.
Its criteria: low caste status, lack of education, poor representation in govt service, trade and industry.
First **AP** BC Commission: **Anantharaman**, report **1970**.

n17d6fbeaf18.s: The Second Backward Classes Commission, popularly known as the Mandal Commission, was set up in 1979 by the
n17d6fbeaf18.x: The B.P. Mandal Commission was established in 1979 by the Janata Government headed by Morarji Desai.
n17d6fbeaf18.tq: Avoid the common trap of confusing the government that appointed a commission with the government that implemented its recommendations.
xs: The Mandal Commission was set up in **1979** by the **Janata Government** of **Morarji Desai** — option **(1)**.
The **Nehru** Government set up the first commission (**Kalelkar**, **1953**).
The **V.P. Singh** Government **implemented** Mandal in **1990** — it did not set it up.
xa: Mandal reported in **1980**; OBCs = **52%** of population.
It used **11 indicators** and recommended **27%** for OBCs.
**27%** of central civil posts were reserved in **1993** (UPSC, IYB).

n82dab0359a1.s: Which one of the following is correct about the implementation of the Mandal Commission recommendations?
o: Implemented by the V.P. Singh Government in 1993; posts reserved in 1995
Implemented by the Morarji Desai Government in 1979; posts reserved in 1980
Implemented by the V.P. Singh Government in 1990; 27 per cent posts reserved in 1993
Implemented by the Rajiv Gandhi Government in 1989; posts reserved in 1990
n82dab0359a1.x: The V.P. Singh Government implemented the Mandal recommendations in 1990, and 27 per cent of Central civil posts were reserved for OBCs in 1993.
xa: Creamy layer criteria: **DoPT Office Memorandum of Sept 1993**, based on **Justice R.N. Prasad** committee.
Creamy-layer income limit: **₹1 lakh (1993)** → **₹8 lakh (2017)**.
Mandal Commission = reservation in **government employment** (APPSC **2019** key).

ne13faae748f.s: Which commission is associated with recommending reservation for backward classes in government employment, leading to the 27 per cent OBC quota?
ne13faae748f.x: The B.P. Mandal Commission (1979) is the commission on reservation in government employment (APPSC 2019, GS 2019); it recommended 27 per cent for OBCs. Kalelkar's report (1955) was not implemented; Rohini deals with OBC sub-categorisation; R.N. Prasad framed creamy-layer criteria.
xs: The **B.P. Mandal Commission** recommended reservation in **government employment**, leading to the **27%** OBC quota — option **(2)**.
**Kalelkar** (report **1955**) was **not implemented**.
**Rohini** deals with OBC **sub-categorisation**; **R.N. Prasad** framed **creamy-layer** criteria.
xa: GS **2019** / APPSC **2019** key: "commission on reservation in government employment" = **Mandal**.
Implemented by **V.P. Singh** in **1990**; central posts reserved in **1993**.
**Oversight Committee (M. Veerappa Moily, 2006)** raised total seats so general-category seats did not shrink.

n6d66ed36125.s: The permanent statutory body for backward-class lists directed by the Supreme Court in Indra Sawhney subsequently became the:
n6d66ed36125.x: The permanent statutory body directed for backward-class lists subsequently became the National Commission for Backward Classes.
n6d66ed36125.tq: Match the judicially directed institutional role with the body that performs it.
xs: The permanent statutory body directed in **Indra Sawhney** became the **National Commission for Backward Classes** — option **(4)**.
The statutory **NCBC Act 1993** was **repealed** in **2018**; the NCBC is now constitutional under **Art. 338B** (**102nd**).
xa: **NCBC role**: examines **inclusion/exclusion** requests for OBC lists.
Present NCBC is the **8th**; **Niranjan Jyoti** appointed Chairperson (2026).
Before 2018, **Art. 338(10)** sent BC complaints to the **SC commission**.

nb0a18f059be.s: Which one of the following was the principal objective of the Oversight Committee headed by M. Veerappa Moily in 2006?
o: To prepare the Central List of Scheduled Tribes
To implement OBC reservation by expanding seats so that general-category seats did not shrink
To identify the creamy layer among SCs and STs
To abolish reservation in Central educational institutions
nb0a18f059be.x: The Oversight Committee headed by M. Veerappa Moily planned implementation through expansion of seats, thereby protecting the existing number of general-category seats.
nb0a18f059be.tq: Use the committee’s stated implementation purpose rather than its year alone.
xs: The **Moily Oversight Committee (2006)** aimed to implement OBC reservation by **expanding seats** so **general-category seats did not shrink** — option **(2)**.
It proposed raising total seats by about **54%**, **phased**.
Creamy layer among SCs/STs is a later debate (CJI **Gavai**, **Nov 2025**), not Moily's task.
xa: The **CEI Act, 2006** gave **27% OBC** seats, in force **Jan 2007**.
**Rohini Commission** handles **sub-categorisation** of OBCs.

n69f4b15046a.s: Justice G. Rohini Commission was constituted in 2017 primarily for
o: identifying the first list of OBCs under Article 340
determining the constitutional validity of EWS reservation
preparing the list of Scheduled Tribes
n69f4b15046a.x: The Justice G. Rohini Commission was constituted in 2017 to examine the sub-categorisation of OBCs.
n69f4b15046a.tq: Match the commission's name and year with its specific mandate.
xs: The **Justice G. Rohini Commission** (Oct **2017**) was for **sub-categorisation of OBCs** — option **(1)**.
It was to sub-categorise about **3,000** Central-list OBC castes.
**Art. 340** commissions were **Kalelkar** and **Mandal**; **EWS** validity was decided in **Janhit Abhiyan**.
xa: It got **14 extensions**; report to the President **31 July 2023**.
Finding: **~97%** of benefits taken by **25%** of sub-castes.
Proposal: **3-4** sub-groups.

na2b68759511.s: Which of the following findings was associated with the Justice G. Rohini Commission?
o: About 97% of OBC benefits were taken by 25% of the sub-castes, while about 1,000 communities had zero representation.
The Commission found that only 100 Central-list OBC communities required sub-categorisation.
About 25% of benefits went to 97% of the sub-castes, while no community lacked representation.
All Central-list OBC castes received an equal share of benefits.
na2b68759511.x: The Commission found that approximately 97% of benefits had been taken by 25% of the sub-castes, while around 1,000 communities had zero representation.
na2b68759511.tq: Watch for reversed percentages and population groups in a comparison-based finding.
xs: Rohini finding: **~97%** of benefits taken by **25% of sub-castes**; **~1,000** communities with **zero representation** — option **(1)**.
Option (3) reverses the figures.
xa: Task: sub-categorise about **3,000** Central-list OBC castes into **3-4** sub-groups.
Report submitted **31 July 2023**; not yet public.
Set up **Oct 2017**; **14 extensions**.

n6fd51abd27b.s: The Justice G. Rohini Commission is associated with a proposal to divide the Central-list OBCs into
n6fd51abd27b.x: The proposal associated with the Commission envisaged three to four sub-groups among the Central-list OBCs.
n6fd51abd27b.tq: Distinguish the proposed range from nearby numerical alternatives.
xs: Rohini proposed **three or four sub-groups** (**3-4**) — option **(4)**.
Basis: **~97%** of benefits taken by **25%** of sub-castes.
xa: About **3,000** Central-list OBC castes covered.
Around **1,000** communities had **zero representation**.
Report to the President on **31 July 2023**.

n9a6f17d4afe.s: The National Commission for Backward Classes examines requests relating principally to:
o: Appointment of judges to the Supreme Court
Inclusion in or exclusion from backward-class lists
n9a6f17d4afe.x: The NCBC examines requests for inclusion in or exclusion from the lists of backward classes and advises on such matters.
n9a6f17d4afe.tq: Ask which constitutional body would handle the specific administrative request.
xs: The **NCBC** examines **inclusion in or exclusion from** backward-class lists — option **(3)**.
It is constitutional under **Art. 338B** (**102nd, 2018**); the statutory **NCBC Act 1993** was **repealed** in 2018.
xa: **Indra Sawhney** directed a **permanent statutory body** for OBC lists → the NCBC.
The present NCBC is the **8th**; **Niranjan Jyoti** appointed Chairperson (2026).
Before 2018, **Art. 338(10)** sent BC complaints to the **SC commission**.

nffe5f99e691.s: The combined quota shares of BC-A, BC-B, BC-C, BC-D and BC-E in Andhra Pradesh amount to:
nffe5f99e691.x: The shares are 7 per cent, 10 per cent, 1 per cent, 7 per cent and 4 per cent respectively, totalling 29 per cent.
nffe5f99e691.tq: Add the category-wise figures rather than confusing them with the local-body quota.
xs: AP BC shares total **29 per cent** — option **(3)**.
**34%** is the **local-body** BC quota (rural); **27%** is the central OBC quota.
xa: **BC-E** (**4%**) is for backward **Muslims**, added in **2007**.
Anantharaman's original quota was **25%**.
BC residential schools (**2024-25**) still admit by **BC-A to BC-E** groups.

nc60be6e2578.s: What was the effect of the Supreme Court’s interim order concerning the 4 per cent reservation for backward Muslim groups in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It permanently approved the quota without further judicial examination.
It allowed the quota to continue pending consideration by a Constitution Bench.
It converted the quota into an EWS reservation.
It abolished the quota immediately after the High Court judgment.
nc60be6e2578.x: Although the Andhra Pradesh High Court struck down the 2007 Act in 2010, the Supreme Court permitted the 4 per cent quota to continue by an interim order pending a Constitution Bench.
nc60be6e2578.tq: Distinguish an interim continuation from final constitutional approval.
xs: The SC's interim order **allowed the quota to continue pending a Constitution Bench** — option **(2)**.
The **AP HC** had struck down the **2007 Act (4%, BC-E)** in **2010**.
It was neither a final approval nor a conversion into EWS.
xa: Earlier **5%** quotas of **2004 and 2005** were struck down by the AP HC.
G2 **2011** answer (Muslim quota State): **Andhra Pradesh**.
BC-E Muslim quota remains a **live issue** in AP.

nindian-society-42-21.s: Which commission was the first to use social and educational criteria for identifying backward classes?
nindian-society-42-21.x: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission was the first to use social and educational tests to identify backward classes.
n: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission was the first commission to use social and educational criteria to identify backward classes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Kaka Kalelkar Commission concerned Other Backward Classes (OBCs). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xs: The **Kaka Kalelkar Commission** was the **first** to **use social and educational criteria** to identify backward classes — option **(3)**.
It was set up in **1953** by the **President** under **Article 340**.
xa: It **recommended** a **caste-based census** and **reservations**.
Its criteria: low caste status, lack of education, poor representation in govt service.
**Mandal** (**1979**) later used **11** indicators.

nindian-society-42-22.s: How many backward castes were identified by the B.P. Mandal Commission?
nindian-society-42-22.x: The Mandal Commission identified 3,743 backward castes. The other options shuffle the same digits.
n: The B.P. Mandal Commission identified 3,743 backward castes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xs: The **Mandal Commission** identified **3,743** backward castes — option **(2)**.
It was the **Second Backward Classes Commission** (**1979**), chaired by **B. P. Mandal**.
xa: It **recommended 27% reservation** for OBCs, estimated at **52%** of population.
⚠ Mandal's **11** indicators = social, educational and economic.
Its report came in **1980**.

o: Sub-categorisation within the Central OBC List
27% reservation for OBCs based on 11 indicators
nindian-society-42-30.x: Kalelkar recommended a caste-based census and reservations; sub-categorisation was Rohini's task, 27% and 11 indicators Mandal's, and 15% for minorities Ranganath Misra's.
n: The Justice G. Rohini Commission examined sub-categorization within OBCs in the Central List. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice G. Rohini Commission aimed to ensure equitable distribution of reservation benefits among underrepresented groups. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The B.P. Mandal Commission formulated 11 social, educational, and economic indicators. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The B.P. Mandal Commission recommended 27% reservation for OBCs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice Ranganath Misra Commission recommended 15% reservation for minorities in education and government jobs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice Ranganath Misra Commission recommended 10% reservation for Muslims in education and government jobs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Kaka Kalelkar Commission recommended a caste-based census. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Kaka Kalelkar Commission recommended reservations for backward classes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The B.P. Mandal Commission concerned Other Backward Classes (OBCs). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xa: Kalelkar was the **first commission** to use **social and educational criteria**.
Its outcome: **not implemented**; the Centre did not accept caste as the criterion.
First AP BC Commission: **Anantharaman Commission**, report **1970**.

ne2d841a7d2f.s: Before the 102nd Constitutional Amendment, Article 338(10) provided that references to Scheduled Castes would include such backward classes as were specified by the
ne2d841a7d2f.x: Before the 102nd Amendment, Article 338(10) treated references to Scheduled Castes as including such backward classes as the President specified. Consequently, complaints relating to backward classes could go to the SC Commission.
ne2d841a7d2f.tq: Identify the constitutional authority named in the transitional provision.
xs: Before **2018**, **Art. 338(10)** treated references to SCs as including backward classes specified by the **President** — option **(4)**.
Hence **BC complaints** went to the **SC commission** until the **102nd Amendment**.
The **NCBC** got constitutional status only through the **102nd (2018)** under **Art. 338B**, so it could not be the specifying authority earlier.
xa: **102nd (2018)** also inserted **Art. 342A** (SEBC lists) and **Art. 366(26C)**.
The statutory **NCBC Act 1993** was **repealed** in 2018; the present (**8th**) NCBC is constitutional.
102nd = **123rd Bill**; 105th = **127th Bill**; 103rd = **124th Bill**.
**Niranjan Jyoti** was appointed **NCBC Chairperson** (2026).

n357e0ae825b.s: Article 15(5) was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
n357e0ae825b.x: The 93rd Amendment (2005) inserted Article 15(5), enabling reservation in educational institutions including private unaided ones, but excluding minority institutions.
xa: It overcame **P.A. Inamdar (2005)**.
It is the base for the **CEI Act, 2006** — **27% OBC** seats, in force **Jan 2007**.
GS **2007** key: the CEI Act rests on the **93rd Amendment**.

na08c4722617.s: The 76th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1994 is associated with which one of the following?
o: Inserting Article 16(4A) for reservation in promotion
Placing Tamil Nadu's 69 per cent reservation law in the Ninth Schedule
Giving constitutional status to the NCBC
na08c4722617.x: The 76th Amendment (1994) placed Tamil Nadu's 69 per cent reservation law in the Ninth Schedule. Article 16(4A) came through the 77th (1995), consequential seniority through the 85th (2001), and constitutional status of the NCBC through the 102nd (2018).
xs: The **76th (1994)** put **Tamil Nadu's 69%** reservation law in the **Ninth Schedule** — option **(2)**.
**Art. 16(4A)** = **77th (1995)**; consequential seniority = **85th (2001)**; NCBC status = **102nd (2018)**.
xa: Indra Sawhney: total reservation **not above 50%** except in extraordinary cases.
SC reserved verdict on TN's BC (Muslim) quota for converts (8 Aug 2026).
**103rd (2019)**: **10% EWS** — over and above existing reservation.

n280cf3f490f.s: The 93rd Constitutional Amendment (2005), which inserted Article 15(5) enabling reservation in admissions including private institutions, was enacted to overcome which judgment?
n280cf3f490f.x: Article 15(5) was inserted by the 93rd Amendment to overcome P.A. Inamdar (2005), which had barred quotas in private unaided institutions; it excludes minority institutions and is the basis of the CEI Act, 2006. Indra Sawhney concerns Mandal, M. Nagaraj promotion reservation, Janhit Abhiyan EWS.
xs: The **93rd (2005)** inserting **Art. 15(5)** overcame **P.A. Inamdar (2005)** — option **(2)**.
**Art. 15(5)** covers admissions incl. **private aided or unaided** institutions, **excluding minority institutions**.
**Indra Sawhney** concerns the Mandal quota; **Janhit Abhiyan (2022)** upheld **EWS**.
xa: Art. 15(5) is the base for the **CEI Act, 2006**.
**Jaishri Patil** → answered by the **105th (2021)**.
**Champakam Dorairajan** → answered by **Art. 15(4)**.

n040a7f104ca.s: The Union Government opposed applying the creamy-layer principle to SCs and STs on the ground that their status flows from
n040a7f104ca.x: In August 2026, the Union Government opposed the proposal, stating that SC/ST status flows from Articles 341 and 342.
n040a7f104ca.tq: Discriminate between closely related constitutional provisions concerning reservations and community identification.
xs: The Union opposed SC/ST creamy layer because their status flows from **Articles 341 and 342** — option **(1)**.
**Arts. 338B and 342A** relate to the **NCBC** and **SEBC** lists (**102nd**), not SCs/STs.
**Arts. 15 and 16** are the reservation-enabling clauses.
xa: CJI **B.R. Gavai** had backed SC creamy layer (**Nov 2025**).
OBC creamy-layer income limit: **₹8 lakh** (**2017**).
**Art. 16(4A)** (**77th**) gives promotion reservation to SCs/STs.

nc20cd56454f.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 102nd Constitutional Amendment from the 105th Constitutional Amendment?
o: The 102nd introduced EWS reservation, while the 105th abolished Article 342A.
The 102nd created constitutional status for the NCBC and inserted Article 342A, while the 105th restored States’ power to identify and list SEBCs.
The 102nd restored State power over SEBC lists, while the 105th created the NCBC.
The 102nd created the first Backward Classes Commission, while the 105th repealed the NCBC Act, 1993.
nc20cd56454f.x: The 102nd Amendment Act, 2018 inserted Articles 338B and 342A and gave constitutional status to the NCBC. The 105th Amendment Act, 2021 restored the power of States to identify and list SEBCs.
nc20cd56454f.tq: Separate the institutional change made by the 102nd Amendment from the federal-list change made by the 105th.
xs: **102nd** gave the **NCBC** constitutional status and inserted **Art. 342A**; the **105th** **restored States' power** to identify and list SEBCs — option **(2)**.
EWS came through the **103rd (2019)**, not the 102nd; the first BC commission was **Kalelkar (1953)** under **Art. 340**.
The 105th answered **Jaishri Patil**; it did not create the NCBC.
xa: The statutory **NCBC Act 1993** was **repealed** in **2018**.

n73087ce63c8.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the 50 per cent ceiling referred to in the context of reservation from EWS reservation?
o: The ceiling applies to backward-class reservations, whereas EWS reservation was provided additionally under Articles 15(6) and 16(6).
The ceiling applies only to reservations in promotions.
The ceiling applies exclusively to EWS reservation.
The ceiling was abolished by the 103rd Amendment.
n73087ce63c8.x: The 50 per cent ceiling discussed in this context relates to backward-class reservations. EWS reservation was introduced additionally through Articles 15(6) and 16(6).
n73087ce63c8.tq: Separate the general reservation ceiling from the constitutional source of EWS reservation.
xs: The **50%** ceiling applies to **backward-class** reservations; EWS was added **additionally** under **Articles 15(6) and 16(6)** — option **(1)**.
**Janhit Abhiyan (2022)**: the **50% cap** applies to backward-class quotas.
The ceiling comes from **Indra Sawhney** and was not abolished; it is not limited to promotions.
xa: EWS is **over and above** / in addition to existing reservation.
Indra Sawhney: **carry-forward** allowed within **50%**, year by year.
**81st (2000)**: backlog vacancies sit outside the **50%** ceiling.

nfef0fbaef6b.s: According to the Indra Sawhney judgment, the backward classes referred to in Article 16(4) are to be identified mainly on the basis of:
nfef0fbaef6b.x: Indra Sawhney held that backward classes under Article 16(4) are identified mainly by caste and social backwardness, not by economic criteria alone.
nfef0fbaef6b.tq: Indra Sawhney: caste can be the starting point for backwardness under 16(4).
xs: **Indra Sawhney**: **Art. 16(4)** backward classes are identified mainly by **caste and social backwardness** — option **(1)**.
It held **caste can be the main criterion** of backwardness, overruling **Balaji** on this.
Income alone is not the test; it is used to exclude the **creamy layer**, which Indra Sawhney introduced.
xa: Indra Sawhney fixed the **50%** ceiling except in extraordinary cases, applied year by year.
It confined reservation to **initial appointment**, not promotion → answered by the **77th** (**Art. 16(4A)**).
It directed a **permanent statutory body** for OBC lists → the **NCBC**.

nda41ca63fd2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Indra Sawhney judgment?
o: Caste may be the main criterion for backwardness.
OBC reservation was extended to promotions as a general rule.
The creamy layer among OBCs should be excluded.
Total reservation should ordinarily not exceed 50 per cent.
nda41ca63fd2.x: Indra Sawhney confined reservation to initial appointments, not promotions.
xa: The **77th (1995)** answered it with **Art. 16(4A)** — promotion reservation for SCs/STs.
Indra Sawhney directed a **permanent statutory body** → the **NCBC**.
**Carry-forward** allowed within the **50%** ceiling, applied year by year.

n0440480c561.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the categories associated with the OBC creamy layer under the Indra Sawhney framework?
o: All children of persons belonging to OBC communities, irrespective of social or economic status
Children whose parents are both Class-II officers
n0440480c561.x: The framework identifies specified socially advanced categories, including children of Class-I officers and parents who are both Class-II officers. It does not exclude all OBC children irrespective of their circumstances.
n0440480c561.tq: Reject the sweeping option that converts specified exclusions into a universal exclusion.
xs: NOT a creamy-layer category: **all children of OBC persons irrespective of social or economic status** — option **(2)**.
The creamy layer excludes only **socially advanced** OBCs — specified status groups and high earners.
Included: children of **constitutional post-holders**, **Class-I officers**, and parents **both Class-II**.
xa: Also excluded: senior govt and **armed-forces** officers, **property owners/large landowners**.
Income limit: **₹8 lakh a year** (**2017**).
Origin: **Indra Sawhney**; criteria via **DoPT OM Sept 1993**.

ndf51f504584.s: The Sukhdev case concerning backward-class reservation in Andhra Pradesh resulted in which of the following conclusions?
o: Caste alone could not be the basis, and 112 classes were identified using poverty, residence and occupation.
All reservation for backward classes was unconstitutional.
Caste alone could be the basis for identifying backward classes.
Reservation could be based only on residence.
ndf51f504584.x: The High Court held in the Sukhdev case that caste alone could not be the basis; consequently, 112 classes were listed using poverty, residence and occupation as considerations.
ndf51f504584.tq: Link the judicial principle with the resulting classification exercise.
xs: **Sukhdev case (HC)**: **caste alone** cannot be the basis → **112** classes listed on **poverty, residence and occupation** — option **(1)**.
It did not strike down all BC reservation, nor rest on residence alone.
xa: After **1956**: separate BC lists for **Andhra (86 castes)** and **Telangana**.
**1963 GO**: **25%** medical seats for **139** castes.
⚠ Contrast: **Indra Sawhney** held caste **can** be the main criterion.

n80562f51aee.s: The OBC creamy-layer criteria in the DoPT Office Memorandum of September 1993 were based on the report of the:
n80562f51aee.x: The creamy-layer criteria were framed through the DoPT Office Memorandum of September 1993, based on the Justice R.N. Prasad Expert Committee.
xa: Status exclusions: children of **constitutional post-holders**, **Class-I officers**, parents both **Class-II**.
The creamy layer itself originated in **Indra Sawhney**.

n8924069b640.s: The income ceiling for determining the OBC creamy layer, after the 2017 revision and described as still current, is
n8924069b640.x: The income ceiling was revised to ₹8 lakh per annum in 2017 and is stated to remain current.
n8924069b640.tq: Distinguish the latest threshold from earlier figures in the revision sequence.
xs: The OBC creamy-layer ceiling since **2017** is **₹8 lakh per annum** — option **(1)**.
Earlier limits: **4.5 lakh (2008)**, **6 lakh (2013)** — now outdated.
xa: ⚠ **₹8 lakh** = OBC creamy-layer limit = **EWS** income ceiling.
**AP** aligned its State/public-sector definitions with the central threshold.

nfedf3a1834a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Kapu reservation proposal?
o: The Justice Manjunatha Commission was constituted in 2016.
In 2019, Kapus got 5% within the EWS quota, later withdrawn.
A 2017 Bill proposed 5% reservation for Kapus as BC-F.
The Centre approved the 2017 BC-F proposal.
nfedf3a1834a.x: The Centre never approved the 2017 BC-F proposal.
xa: Kapu demand and **BC-E** Muslim quota are AP's **live issues**.
AP BC shares: **A 7%, B 10%, C 1%, D 7%, E 4%**.
EWS: enabling, **not mandatory** for States.

nindian-society-42-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the B.P. Mandal Commission?
o: It was the second Backward Classes Commission.
It was constituted by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
nindian-society-42-2.x: The Mandal Commission was set up through the Ministry of Home Affairs, not Social Justice and Empowerment; it identified 3,743 backward castes and recommended 27% for OBCs.
n: The B.P. Mandal Commission was the second Backward Classes Commission. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The B.P. Mandal Commission was constituted by the Ministry of Home Affairs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The B.P. Mandal Commission identified 3,743 backward castes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The B.P. Mandal Commission recommended 27% reservation for OBCs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The B.P. Mandal Commission concerned Other Backward Classes (OBCs). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xa: It **formulated 11** social, educational and economic indicators; OBCs = **52%** of population.
The **27%** quota was implemented by **V.P. Singh** in **1990**.
The **Rohini Commission** (**2017**) was set up by Social Justice and Empowerment.

nfba26cc79ca.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Union of India v. Rohith Nathan?
o: The Court held that parental salary alone determines creamy-layer status.
The Court ordered the creation of supernumerary posts.
The verdict was delivered on 11 March 2026.
In August 2026, the Centre sought clarification on 958 CSE-2025 candidates.
nfba26cc79ca.x: The Court held that parental salary alone cannot place a candidate in the creamy layer.
xa: The SC is likely to set up a **special Bench** on it.
Creamy-layer limit: **₹8 lakh** (**2017**), via **DoPT OM** framework of **Sept 1993**.
Status exclusions include **Class-I officers** and parents both **Class-II**.

n5598e20ca98.s: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act was introduced in Parliament as the:
n5598e20ca98.x: It originated as the 124th Amendment Bill and inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6) for 10% EWS reservation.
xa: In force **January 2019**; upheld in **Janhit Abhiyan (7 Nov 2022)** by **3:2**.
EWS is **over and above** existing reservation.
States: enabling, **not mandatory**.

nf5868926854.s: For the States, EWS reservation under the 103rd Constitutional Amendment is:
o: Mandatory only for State educational institutions
Mandatory only for State government posts
nf5868926854.x: The amendment enables up to 10% EWS reservation outside SC/ST/OBC quotas but does not make it mandatory for States.
xa: EWS criteria: income **below ₹8 lakh**, **5 acres** farm land, **1,000 sq ft** flat.
Applies to jobs and education, incl. **private** central institutions.
⚠ **₹8 lakh** = OBC creamy-layer limit (**2017**) = EWS ceiling.

n91e48801574.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about EWS reservation under the 103rd Amendment?
o: It applies to central educational institutions.
It applies to posts under the Central Government.
It extends to private educational institutions.
It is compulsory for State Governments.
n91e48801574.x: Implementation of EWS reservation is not mandatory for State Governments.
xa: EWS is for those **not covered** by SC/ST/OBC quotas.
Upheld in **Janhit Abhiyan** by a **five-judge** bench (**3:2**).

n8870eab6013.s: For determining EWS eligibility, which one of the following combinations correctly represents the income and asset criteria stated for the purpose?
o: Annual family income below ₹5 lakh, land below 2 acres and flat below 800 sq ft
Annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 10 acres and flat below 1,000 sq ft
Annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and flat below 1,000 sq ft
Annual family income below ₹10 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and flat below 1,500 sq ft
n8870eab6013.x: The stated EWS criteria include annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and a flat below 1,000 square feet.
n8870eab6013.tq: Match the numerical threshold with the associated land and dwelling limits.
xs: EWS criteria: family income **below ₹8 lakh**, farm land below **5 acres**, flat below **1,000 sq ft** — option **(3)**.
Option (2) has the wrong land limit; options (1) and (4) have wrong income figures.
xa: ⚠ **₹8 lakh** is also the **OBC creamy-layer** limit since **2017**.
EWS: **10%**, over and above existing reservation.
Creamy-layer ladder: **₹1 lakh (1993)** → **₹8 lakh (2017)**.

n252b0eeb60c.s: In Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India, the 103rd Constitutional Amendment was upheld by a majority of:
n252b0eeb60c.x: The EWS amendment was upheld 3:2, with Chief Justice U.U. Lalit and Justice S. Ravindra Bhat dissenting.
xa: It held the **50% cap** applies to backward-class quotas.
103rd = **124th Amendment Bill**.

n12a97b78bf0.s: The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006, providing 27 per cent OBC reservation, came into force in:
n12a97b78bf0.x: Although enacted in 2006, the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act came into force in 2007.
n12a97b78bf0.tq: Separate the enactment year from the commencement year.
xs: The **CEI (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006** came into force in **Jan 2007** — option **(3)**.
It gives **27% OBC** seats in central institutions; based on **Art. 15(5)** (**93rd, 2005**).
**2006** is the enactment year, **2005** the 93rd Amendment year — not the commencement.
xa: GS **2007** key: **93rd Amendment** underlies the CEI Act.
**Oversight Committee (M. Veerappa Moily, 2006)** expanded seats (about **54%**, phased).

nb192bf986b8.s: The BC-E category in Andhra Pradesh was added through which measure and in which year?
nb192bf986b8.x: BC-E was added by the Andhra Pradesh Act of 2007. Earlier lists commonly included only BC-A to BC-D.
nb192bf986b8.tq: Match the category’s introduction with the specific legal instrument and year.
xs: **BC-E** was added by the **2007 Andhra Pradesh Act** — option **(1)**.
⚠ CDX lists only **BC-A to BC-D**.
**1984** = NTR's **20%** local-body BC quota; **2010** = AP HC struck the 2007 Act down; **2019** = EWS.
xa: BC-E share: **4%**, for socially and educationally backward **Muslims**.
Earlier **5%** quotas (**2004 and 2005**) were struck down by the **AP High Court**.
The **Supreme Court** let the 2007 quota continue by **interim order** pending a **Constitution Bench**.

n5b1d6ccfb1b.s: Which commission was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission and framed the A-D grouping along with a 25 per cent quota?
n5b1d6ccfb1b.x: The Anantharaman Commission was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission; its report was submitted in 1970 and it framed the A-D grouping and a 25 per cent quota.
n5b1d6ccfb1b.tq: Identify the commission from its distinctive first-commission and grouping role.
xs: The **Anantharaman Commission** was the first AP BC Commission (report **1970**), framing **A-D** grouping and a **25%** quota — option **(1)**.
**Mandal** was national (**1979**); **Muralidhara Rao** took charge **27 Jan 1982**; **Manjunatha (2016)** was on **Kapus**.
xa: **Muralidhara Rao** reviewed BC reservation and examined inclusion of minorities.
**BC-E** added later by the **2007** Act.
National first commission: **Kalelkar (1953)**.

n478653724b6.s: Which clause was added to the Constitution to overcome the judgment in State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan?
n478653724b6.x: Article 15(4) was inserted by the First Amendment, 1951 to overcome Champakam Dorairajan. Article 16(4) was in the original Constitution; Article 15(5) came by the 93rd Amendment (2005) and Article 16(4B) by the 81st (2000).
xs: **Article 15(4)** was added to overcome **Champakam Dorairajan** — option **(1)**.
**Art. 15(5)** = **93rd** (to overcome **P.A. Inamdar**); **Art. 16(4B)** = **81st** (backlog).
xa: Exam angle: "which article was added to overcome Champakam Dorairajan" → **15(4)**.
**Art. 16(4A)**: promotion reservation (**77th**).

n62ea688001e.s: In tribal usage, the term ‘Diku’ refers to:
o: An outsider-exploiter such as a moneylender, trader, landlord or contractor
n62ea688001e.x: Diku denotes an outsider-exploiter, including a moneylender, trader, landlord or contractor.
n62ea688001e.tq: Distinguish the exact social meaning of a culturally specific term.
xs: **Diku** = an **outsider-exploiter** — **moneylender, trader, landlord or contractor** — option **(4)**.
**Birsa's Ulgulan** targeted British land-grabbing and the **dikus**.
xa: **Abua Raj** = aim of Birsa's **Ulgulan**; **Dharti Aaba** = title of **Birsa Munda**.
**Nistar** = a **community right** under the FRA (with grazing, fishing).
**Marang Buru** = **Parasnath Hills** as revered by **Santhals**.

n23dd96cac80.s: The Forest Conservation Rules, 2022 became a subject of dispute between the NCST and the Environment Ministry because they:
o: Added a compulsory tribal veto over every forest diversion
Dropped the forest-dwellers’ consent clause before forest diversion
Prohibited all development projects in forest areas
Transferred all forests to Gram Sabhas
n23dd96cac80.x: The 2022 Rules dropped the consent clause of forest-dwellers before forest diversion, leading to a dispute between the NCST and the Environment Ministry.
n23dd96cac80.tq: Identify the precise legal change behind an institutional dispute.
xs: The **Forest Conservation Rules 2022** **dropped the forest-dwellers' consent clause** before forest diversion — option **(2)**.
This set the **NCST** against the **Environment Ministry**.
xa: MoEFCC guidelines had barred diversion until FRA processes (esp. **Gram Sabha consent**) were complete.
MoTA letter (**31 Aug 2026**): FRA has **"no provision"** for Gram Sabha consent for **Stage-II** clearance.
**Niyamgiri (2013)**: **Dongria Kondh** gram sabhas rejected bauxite mining → project cancelled.

nb3de704e8a3.s: Who identified political autonomy, recognition of identity and control over resources as objectives of modern tribal movements?
nb3de704e8a3.x: T. K. Oommen identified political autonomy, identity recognition and control over resources as objectives of modern tribal movements.
xa: Approaches: **isolation** (early **Elwin**), **assimilation** (**Ghurye**, **N.K. Bose**), **integration** (**Nehru**).
Birsa's Ulgulan aimed at **Abua Raj**.
⚠ Elwin = early **isolation**, later **integration** with Nehru.

ne0f4389b0b9.s: The first principle of Nehru's Panchsheel for tribal development is to:
o: Develop tribal people along the lines of their own genius
Impose a uniform administration on all tribal areas
Measure progress by the money spent
