Assimilate tribal people rapidly into mainstream culture
ne0f4389b0b9.x: The first principle is to develop tribal people along their own genius, respecting their distinct capacities and culture.
xa: Principle 2: respect tribal **rights in land and forests**.
Principle 3: train **tribal people for their own administration**.
⚠ CDI lists "encourage **tribal languages**" separately; standard wording keeps it inside principle 1.

n6d7199627b6.s: Which of the following is NOT a Panchsheel principle for tribal development?
o: Tribal rights in land and forests should be respected
Tribal people should be relied upon and trained for their own administration
Administration should be minimised and conducted through tribal institutions
Results should be judged by money spent rather than by the quality of human character evolved
n6d7199627b6.x: Panchsheel requires results to be judged by the quality of human character evolved, not by money spent; the other three are Panchsheel principles.
xa: Principle 1: develop **along their own genius**.
Source: Nehru's foreword to Elwin's **A Philosophy for NEFA**.
Nehru's approach = **integration**.

n513d260648d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC)?
o: It was set up in 2001 by splitting the joint SC/ST corporation
It lends to STs with income up to three times the poverty line
It runs the Adivasi Mahila Sashaktikaran Yojana
n513d260648d.x: NSTFDC lends to STs with income up to double, not three times, the poverty line.
xa: NSTFDC forest-dweller scheme: **90%** of cost at **6%** for FRA title-holders.
**25th Foundation Day** on **10 April 2026**.
⚠ **NSFDC** (**1989**) is for **SCs**; **NSKFDC** (**1997**) implements **NAMASTE**.

ncddb4e5b0c6.s: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was set up as a separate Union Ministry in:
ncddb4e5b0c6.x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was set up in 1999. 2001 is the year NSTFDC was set up, 2004 is when NCST began functioning, and 1989 is the year NSFDC was set up.
xs: The **Ministry of Tribal Affairs** was set up in **1999** — option **(2)**.
xa: MoTA is the **nodal ministry** for the **FRA** (UPSC **2021**).
TSP monitoring moved to MoTA in **January 2017**.
**TRIFED** handles tribal marketing via "**Tribes India**".

ne92b0768ba0.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338A was created by the:
ne92b0768ba0.x: Article 338A was inserted by the 89th Constitutional Amendment, 2003; NCST functions from 19 February 2004 with civil-court powers.
xa: ⚠ The **89th** split the SC/ST commission into NCSC and NCST.
**2022** dispute: NCST vs Environment Ministry over **Forest Conservation Rules**.
NCST is part of the ST-inclusion chain: State → **RGI** → **NCST** → Cabinet → Parliament.

nfa26ea7946d.s: Raising farm output with improved seeds and fertilisers, planting fruit-bearing trees and other income-raising activities in tribal areas are objectives of:
nfa26ea7946d.x: Agricultural improvement, fruit-bearing plantations and other income-generating activities in tribal areas are objectives of TADP/ITDA.
xa: **ITDA Project Officers** + DSTW monitor health schemes in ITDA areas.
TSP adopted in the **5th Plan (1974)**.

nded32577314.s: Monitoring of the Tribal Sub-Plan moved from the Planning Commission to the Ministry of Tribal Affairs in:
nded32577314.x: TSP monitoring shifted to MoTA in January 2017; online monitoring now covers the ST component of 41 ministries.
xa: TSP adopted in the **5th Plan (1974)**.
Funds over and above **normal plan flows**.

n87105d043c4.s: PM-AJAY, launched in 2021-22, is administered as a centrally sponsored intervention by which Union Ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
n87105d043c4.x: PM-AJAY was launched in 2021-22 as a 100 per cent centrally funded scheme under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
n87105d043c4.tq: Identify the correct ministry and distinguish the SC-focused scheme from tribal-area programmes.
xs: **PM-AJAY** (**2021-22**) is under the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment**, **100% central** — option **(2)**.
⚠ It targets **SC** poverty — not STs, so MoTA is wrong (APPSC G1 **2024**).
xa: It merged **SCA to SCSP + PMAGY + BJRCY**.
**Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana** (SC hostels) is now part of PM-AJAY.
**NAMASTE** is under **MoSJE + MoHUA**.

n5e51c6f405c.s: The nodal Ministry for implementation of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 is the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
n5e51c6f405c.x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is the nodal ministry for the Forest Rights Act, 2006.
n5e51c6f405c.tq: Use the who-is-responsible test to distinguish the nodal ministry from ministries involved in implementation.
xs: The **Ministry of Tribal Affairs** is the **nodal ministry** for the **FRA 2006** — option **(1)** (UPSC **2021**).
**MoEFCC** handles forest diversion; it was asked by MoTA for **CFR funds** (**12 Jan 2026**).
xa: FRA aims to undo the "**historical injustice**" and **overrides** inconsistent laws.
MoTA letter (**31 Aug 2026**): FRA has "no provision" for Gram Sabha consent for **Stage-II** clearance.
MoTA was set up in **1999**.

n6fc7ae5f4ee.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about processing of claims under the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
o: The Gram Sabha passes resolutions on claims
Claims are examined by Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees
Each of these committees consists of nine members
The committees include revenue, tribal and forest officials and elected panchayat members
n6fc7ae5f4ee.x: The Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees are six-member bodies, not nine-member; the other statements are correct.
xa: FDST cut-off: occupation **before 13 December 2005**.
OTFD: **3 generations (75 years)** of residence/dependence.
Ceiling: up to **4 hectares per family**.

ne7e053e2e96.s: Which of the following is NOT recognised as a forest right under the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
o: Automatic ownership of all mineral resources beneath forest land
Habitat rights for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups
ne7e053e2e96.x: The Act recognises rights such as minor forest produce, community forest resource management and PVTG habitat rights. It does not confer automatic ownership of all mineral resources beneath forest land.
ne7e053e2e96.tq: Find the option outside the statutory list of individual and community forest rights.
xs: NOT an FRA right: **automatic ownership of all mineral resources** beneath forest land — option **(1)**.
FRA rights list: **ownership of MFP**, **habitat rights for PVTGs**, **community forest resources** management, biodiversity/traditional knowledge.
xa: Individual rights: land, **habitation**, **self-cultivation**.
Community rights: **nistar**, **grazing**, fishing, **CFR** management.
⚠ **Samatha (1997)**: mining leases in Scheduled Areas to private non-tribals are **void**.

n7296cb37f2e.s: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 sought to undo the historical injustice done to:
n7296cb37f2e.x: The Act recognises forest rights of Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers, with the stated objective of undoing historical injustice to forest dwellers.
xa: Nodal ministry: **Tribal Affairs** (UPSC **2021**).
The Act **overrides** inconsistent laws.
Beneficiaries: **FDST** and **OTFD**.

nea7d498ee9c.s: A forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribe family claims recognition of rights under the Forest Rights Act. Which date is relevant for determining occupation of forest land?
nea7d498ee9c.x: Forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes must have been occupying the forest land before 13 December 2005 for eligibility under the stated cut-off criterion.
nea7d498ee9c.tq: Treat the cut-off date as a direct numerical-recall point and reject nearby constitutional or enactment dates.
xs: The cut-off for FDSTs is occupation **before 13 December 2005** — option **(3)**.
FDSTs must be **living in, dependent on and occupying** forest land before that date.
xa: **OTFDs** need **3 generations (75 years)** of residence before **2005**.
Ceiling: up to **4 ha** per family.
Claims start with the **Gram Sabha** (**Sec. 6**).

nce6ea8c9c61.s: For recognition under the Forest Rights Act, Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must establish residence in or dependence on forests for:
nce6ea8c9c61.x: Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must show residence in or dependence on forests for three generations, specified as 75 years, before 2005.
nce6ea8c9c61.tq: Separate the generation requirement from the ST cut-off date and convert it into the stated year equivalent.
xs: OTFDs need **three generations or 75 years** — option **(3)**.
FDSTs instead need occupation **before 13 December 2005**.
xa: OTFD = **Other Traditional Forest Dwellers**; FDST = **Forest-dwelling STs**.
Ceiling: up to **4 hectares per family**.
Committees: **six-member** Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees.

nca4c03ff3bb.s: What is the maximum extent of forest rights that may be recognised per family under the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
nca4c03ff3bb.x: The ceiling for forest rights is up to four hectares per family.
nca4c03ff3bb.tq: Test the statutory ceiling directly using close numerical distractors.
xs: The FRA ceiling is up to **4 hectares** per family — option **(1)**.
For public utilities (schools, dispensaries), diversion is up to **1 ha per project** on **Gram Sabha** recommendation.
xa: Individual rights: land, habitation, self-cultivation.
Titles (**2025-26**): **23.92 lakh individual + 1.22 lakh community**.
AP: **2,26,651** individual titles approved (APSES **2024-25**).

nf8d9156816d.s: Which of the following correctly states the relationship between the Forest Rights Act, 2006 and inconsistent laws?
o: The Act is subordinate to every earlier forest law
The Act applies only where no State law exists
The Act overrides laws that are inconsistent with it
The Act can be overridden by an executive circular alone
nf8d9156816d.x: The Forest Rights Act overrides laws that are inconsistent with its provisions.
nf8d9156816d.tq: Watch for the reversed legal relationship between the Act and inconsistent laws.
xs: The FRA **overrides laws inconsistent with it** — option **(3)** (UPSC).
It is not subordinate to earlier forest laws.
xa: Purpose: undo the **"historical injustice"** to forest dwellers.
**FCA linkage**: diversion barred until FRA processes complete — upheld by the **Supreme Court**.
⚠ MoTA letter (**31 Aug 2026**): FRA has "no provision" for Gram Sabha consent for **Stage-II** clearance.

nca1dd24c24d.s: The first Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group stated to have received habitat rights under the Forest Rights Act framework was:
nca1dd24c24d.x: Bharia of Madhya Pradesh was the first PVTG mentioned as receiving habitat rights; Kamar and Baiga of Chhattisgarh followed.
nca1dd24c24d.tq: Use the first-in-sequence trap to distinguish Bharia from the later Kamar and Baiga claims.
xs: The first PVTG to get habitat rights was the **Bharia of Madhya Pradesh** — option **(1)**.
**Kamar and Baiga** (Chhattisgarh) came **after** Bharia.
⚠ The **UPSC 2018** claim that **Baigas** were first is **false**.
xa: Habitat rights follow **2014 MoTA guidelines**.
**Four** State departments (Forest, Revenue, Tribal, Panchayati Raj) coordinate, with **UNDP** help.
**PM-JANMAN** covers **75 PVTGs**.

n4a72edac4fc.s: Under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, 'nistar' is classified as a/an:
n4a72edac4fc.x: Nistar, grazing, fishing and ownership and disposal of minor forest produce are listed community rights under the FRA.
xa: **Bamboo** is an MFP under the FRA (UPSC **2019**).
**Nistar** = a community right.
**TRIFED** gives **MSP for MFP**.

na11d0fa8fb1.s: Critical Wildlife Habitat under the Forest Rights Act refers to areas of national parks and sanctuaries that are to be:
o: Transferred exclusively to private conservation agencies
Kept inviolate after an open process involving affected communities
Opened for mining after approval by the Forest Department
na11d0fa8fb1.x: Critical Wildlife Habitats are areas within national parks and sanctuaries to be kept inviolate, and they are notified after an open process with affected communities.
na11d0fa8fb1.tq: Distinguish the legal definition from an assumed blanket exclusion of communities.
xs: **Critical Wildlife Habitats** are areas of national parks/sanctuaries **kept inviolate** after an **open process with affected communities** — option **(3)**.
They are defined and notified under the **FRA** (UPSC **2018**).
xa: ⚠ **Critical tiger habitats** (WPA) need **mandatory Gram Sabha consultation**.
**Agasthyamalai**: eviction orders ignored the FRA (**11 Aug 2026**).
The FRA overrides inconsistent laws.

n2dd9edd2e8c.s: The Indian Forest (Amendment) Act, 2017 did which of the following?
o: Removed bamboo grown outside forest areas from the definition of “tree”.
Granted an unrestricted right to fell bamboo in forest areas.
Removed all bamboo from the definition of minor forest produce.
Transferred ownership of all bamboo to private companies.
n2dd9edd2e8c.x: The 2017 amendment removed bamboo grown outside forest areas from the definition of “tree”. It did not confer a right to fell bamboo in forest areas.
n2dd9edd2e8c.tq: Watch for the false extension from bamboo outside forests to bamboo inside forests.
xs: **IFA (Amendment) 2017** **removed bamboo grown outside forest areas** from the definition of "**tree**" — option **(1)**.
⚠ It did **not** give a right to fell bamboo in forest areas — that comes from the **FRA**.
xa: Under the FRA, **bamboo is MFP**, owned by forest dwellers.
UPSC **2019**: statement on IFA right to fell = false.
**PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission** buys MFP at **MSP**.

n7b4f194b9f0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding forest diversion after the Forest Rights Act?
o: Completion of FRA processes is a prerequisite before forest diversion under the FCA
Forest diversion is permissible before completion of FRA claims if the project is of public importance
Gram Sabha consent is relevant to the FRA process
Niyamgiri saw Gram Sabha rejection of bauxite mining
n7b4f194b9f0.x: MoEFCC guidelines barred forest diversion under the FCA until FRA processes, especially Gram Sabha consent, were complete, a position upheld by the Supreme Court.
xa: **Forest Conservation Rules 2022** dropped the forest-dwellers' consent clause.
**Stage-II** row: MoTA said FRA has "no provision" for consent (**31 Aug 2026**).
Implementation gap: **JFMC/CAMPA** projects bypassing Gram Sabhas.

na2fb91a9128.s: Which of the following is NOT a reported gap in Forest Rights Act implementation?
o: Excessive focus on individual titles over CFR
Strong MoTA capacity ensuring complete CFR implementation
na2fb91a9128.x: The identified gap is weak, not strong, MoTA capacity; the other three are reported implementation gaps.
xa: Over **47,900** CFR/CFRR claims rejected.
⚠ **Forest Conservation Rules 2022** dropped prior consent.
**Agasthyamalai** evictions ignored the FRA.

nd60827fd466.s: Under the RFCTLARR Act, 2013, Social Impact Assessment is:
o: Required only for private projects and never for public projects
Replaced by a census of affected families
nd60827fd466.x: The RFCTLARR Act, 2013 makes Social Impact Assessment mandatory.
nd60827fd466.tq: Identify the statutory requirement without being distracted by exceptions not stated in the law summary.
xs: Under **RFCTLARR 2013**, **Social Impact Assessment** is **mandatory** — option **(2)**.
It is not optional in Scheduled Areas — there it applies along with **Gram Sabha** consent.
xa: Consent: **80% (private)**, **70% (PPP)** affected families.
Scheduled Areas: acquisition = **last resort**, with **Gram Sabha/Panchayat/Autonomous Council** consent.
**District Mineral Foundation** uses RFCTLARR's "affected" and "displaced" definitions.

n621537ca57f.s: In Scheduled Areas, acquisition under the RFCTLARR Act is treated as a last resort and requires consent of which body or bodies?
o: Only the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
Gram Sabha, Panchayat or Autonomous Council, as applicable
n621537ca57f.x: Acquisition in Scheduled Areas is a last resort and requires consent from the Gram Sabha, Panchayat or Autonomous Council, as applicable.
n621537ca57f.tq: Identify the local self-governing body rather than a supervisory or advisory institution.
xs: In Scheduled Areas, acquisition is a **last resort** and needs **Gram Sabha/Panchayat/Autonomous Council consent** — option **(4)**.
The **District Mineral Foundation** only uses RFCTLARR definitions of affected/displaced families.
xa: Consent: **80%** private, **70%** PPP.
**PESA** areas: at least **50%** seats to STs and **all chairpersons are STs**.
AP: **2,038** notified PESA Gram Sabhas (**AP PESA Rules 2011**).

n370c6957bf9.s: The PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission, associated with 2021-22, is run by TRIFED and includes which set of activities?
o: Civil Services coaching, NETS testing and residential schooling
PPE distribution, sewer profiling and sanitation stipends
Land purchase, pension payments and free electricity
Buying MFP at MSP, value addition and GI tags
n370c6957bf9.x: The PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission is run by TRIFED and focuses on buying Minor Forest Produce at MSP, value addition and GI tags.
n370c6957bf9.tq: Match the programme with its sector-specific activity cluster.
xs: **PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission** (**2021-22**, TRIFED): **buys MFP at MSP, value addition, GI tags** — option **(4)**.
Civil Services coaching = **DACE**; NETS = **SHRESHTA**; PPE/sewer profiling = **NAMASTE**.
xa: **VDVKs (2018)**: about **15** SHGs of up to **20** gatherers.
TRIFED brand: "**Tribes India**".
AP: **GCC Araku Valley Coffee** trademarked (**2024-25**).

o: Free coaching for SC students in Central Universities
MSP procurement from all farmers in border districts
Mechanised cleaning of septic tanks in urban areas
Skills and jobs for tribal youth in Left-Wing Extremism districts
n6f55973301f.x: Roshni, associated with the Ministry of Rural Development and 2013, provides skills and employment opportunities for tribal youth in LWE districts.
n6f55973301f.tq: Use the target group, geography and purpose together to identify the programme.
xs: **Roshni** = skills and jobs for **tribal youth in LWE districts** (**MoRD, 2013**) — option **(4)**.
Free coaching for SC students in Central Universities = **DACE**; septic-tank mechanisation = **NAMASTE**.
xa: **DACE** launched **22 April 2022** at **Banaras Hindu University**.
**PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission**: MFP at MSP.
**VDVKs**: at least **60% ST**.

n462ee58b18c.s: Eklavya Model Residential Schools are a Central Sector scheme under the:
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
n462ee58b18c.x: EMRS is a Central Sector scheme under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
n462ee58b18c.tq: Apply the ministry-ownership trap to a residential education scheme.
xs: **EMRS** is a **Central sector** scheme of the **Ministry of Tribal Affairs** — option **(2)**.
It is modelled on **Navodaya Vidyalayas** and run through **NESTS**.
xa: Started **1997-98**; target **740** schools.
**511** schools with **1.68 lakh** students (Aug 2026).

ndad47ce7baf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about scholarships for SC and ST students?
o: The Post-Matric Scholarship for SCs is the largest central scheme for SC students
ST pre-matric and post-matric scholarships are centrally sponsored schemes
National Fellowship, Top Class and National Overseas are central sector schemes
The cost of the SC Post-Matric Scholarship is shared in the ratio 75:25
ndad47ce7baf.x: The SC Post-Matric Scholarship cost is shared in the ratio 60:40, not 75:25; the other statements are correct.
xa: National Overseas: **20** awards (**17 ST + 3 PVTG**).
National Overseas income limit: **Rs 6 lakh**.
**SHRESHTA** places SC students in top residential schools via **NETS**.

n065050cd551.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Stand-Up India?
o: It is meant exclusively for existing enterprises
Every bank branch is to lend to at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower
It is administered by the Ministry of Finance
n065050cd551.x: Stand-Up India supports greenfield enterprises; it is not meant exclusively for existing enterprises.
xa: Loans: **Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore**; up to **85%** of project cost; repay over **7** years.
**SIDBI** refinance.
**2.75 lakh** loans worth **Rs 62,790 crore** by March 2025.

nfddc17ddbde.s: The Dr Ambedkar Centres of Excellence provide free Civil Services coaching to:
nfddc17ddbde.x: The Dr Ambedkar Centres of Excellence give free Civil Services coaching to SC students in Central Universities.
xa: Launched **22 April 2022** at **Banaras Hindu University**.

**Diku** = outsider-exploiter (moneylender, trader, landlord, contractor).

nd789f30e399.s: The source of Nehru’s Panchsheel for tribal development is identified as:
o: Nehru’s foreword to Verrier Elwin’s A Philosophy for NEFA
nd789f30e399.x: The principles are sourced to Nehru’s foreword to Verrier Elwin’s work A Philosophy for NEFA.
nd789f30e399.tq: Match the doctrine with its literary and constitutional context.
xs: Panchsheel's source: **Nehru's foreword to Verrier Elwin's A Philosophy for NEFA** — option **(2)**.
⚠ CDX credits **Elwin** with formulating it under Nehru's influence.
xa: Five principles: own **genius**; **land and forest rights**; tribal **self-administration**; **avoid over-administration**; judge by **human character**.
The **AP PESA Rules 2011** are unrelated — they notified **2,038** PESA Gram Sabhas.
Elwin = early **isolation**, later **integration**.

nindian-society-35-9.s: Which initiative focuses on mechanized sanitation ecosystems, zero manual scavenging deaths and rehabilitation of sanitation workers?
nindian-society-35-9.x: NAMASTE, now with SMILE, aims at mechanised sanitation, zero deaths from manual scavenging, and rehabilitation of sanitation workers.
nindian-society-35-9.tq: Match each scheme to its purpose.
n: The SMILE/NAMASTE Scheme promotes mechanized sanitation ecosystems. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
The SMILE/NAMASTE Scheme targets zero manual scavenging deaths. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
The SMILE/NAMASTE Scheme rehabilitates sanitation workers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
xs: The **SMILE/NAMASTE Scheme** promotes **mechanized sanitation ecosystems**, targets **zero manual scavenging deaths** and **rehabilitates sanitation workers** — option **(1)**.
It is run by **MoSJE + MoHUA**, implemented by **NSKFDC**.
xa: NAMASTE outlay: **Rs 349.70 crore**; capital subsidy up to **Rs 7.5 lakh**.
It profiles workers in **4,800+ ULBs**; skilling with a **Rs 3,000** stipend.
Legal backing: **Manual Scavengers Act 2013**.

nindian-society-37-13.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the NAMASTE portal?
o: It is associated with the Urban Affairs sector and Social Justice & Empowerment.
It digitally profiles sewer and septic-tank workers.
It conducts online CBT registration and seat allotment for SC students.
It supports health-insurance linkage and PPE verification.
nindian-society-37-13.x: Online CBT registration and seat allotment for SC students is done by the SHRESHTA portal; NAMASTE profiles sewer and septic-tank workers and links them to insurance and PPE.
n: The NAMASTE Mobile App and Portal are associated with Social Justice and Housing and Urban Affairs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The NAMASTE Mobile App and Portal digitally profile sewer and septic-tank workers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The NAMASTE Mobile App and Portal link workers with health insurance. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The NAMASTE Mobile App and Portal verify personal protective equipment (PPE). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The SHRESHTA Portal is a digital platform for Scheduled Castes (SC). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The SHRESHTA Portal provides online computer-based test registration. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The SHRESHTA Portal conducts merit evaluation. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The SHRESHTA Portal provides seat allotment. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The SHRESHTA Portal covers private residential schools for SC students. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
xa: NAMASTE goal: **zero sanitation deaths**.
SHRESHTA is run by the **National Testing Agency**.

n5ef0a9a5970.s: The duty of parents to provide education to children aged 6–14 years is contained in:
n5ef0a9a5970.x: The parental duty is a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(k); Article 39(e) protects the tender age of children from abuse.
xa: **Art. 39(f)**: opportunities to develop **in freedom and dignity**; protection from exploitation and abandonment.
39(f) was reworded by the **42nd Amendment 1976**.
**Art. 24**: no child below **14** in factories, mines or hazardous employment.

nfef4fd698c3.s: Article 39(f), which concerns the healthy development of children in freedom and dignity and their protection from exploitation and abandonment, was reworded by the:
nfef4fd698c3.x: Article 39(f) was reworded by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. The 86th Amendment is associated with Articles 21A, 45 and 51A(k).
nfef4fd698c3.tq: Separate the amendment connected with Article 39(f) from the later education amendment.
xs: **Art. 39(f)** was reworded by the **42nd Amendment, 1976** — option **(4)**.
The **86th (2002)** inserted **21A**, rewrote **45** and added **51A(k)** — not 39(f).
xa: 39(f): children develop healthily **in freedom and dignity**; protected from **exploitation and abandonment**.
**Art. 39(e)**: tender age of children not abused.

nae2bbba8342.s: Which Article of the Constitution prohibits employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines or other hazardous employment?
nae2bbba8342.x: Article 24 bars children below 14 from factories, mines and hazardous employment. Article 23 bans traffic in human beings and forced labour, Article 39(e) is a Directive Principle against abuse of tender age, and Article 21A is the right to education.
nae2bbba8342.tq: Art. 23 = trafficking/forced labour; Art. 24 = child labour below 14.
xs: **Article 24** bars children below **14** in **factories, mines or hazardous employment** — option **(2)**.
**Art. 23** bans **traffic in human beings and forced labour**; **Art. 21A** is right to education.
xa: Child labour (**5-14**): **4.35 million** main workers (Census **2011**); about **10.1 million** with marginal workers.
⚠ Child = below **18** (POCSO) vs below **14** (child labour) vs **6-14** (RTE).
**Art. 39(e)**: children not forced by economic necessity into unsuited avocations.

nfee9f21b1ae.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four core principles of the UNCRC?
o: Right to life, survival and development
nfee9f21b1ae.x: The four core principles are non-discrimination, best interests of the child, life-survival-development and respect for the child's views; free secondary education is not one of them.
xa: Four rights categories: **survival, development, protection, participation**.
UNCRC adopted **20 November 1989**.
**54 articles** (APPSC **2019**).

n6f42445b5a7.s: The Supreme Court has described quality elementary teacher education as vital to the effective realisation of
n6f42445b5a7.x: The Supreme Court stressed that quality elementary teacher education is vital to Article 21A, the constitutional right to education.
n6f42445b5a7.tq: Match the constitutional article with the right whose implementation depends on teacher quality.
xs: The SC called quality elementary teacher education vital to **Article 21A** (4 Sep 2026) — option **(1)**.
**Art. 21A** is the right to free and compulsory education for **6-14**, inserted by the **86th (2002)**.
xa: Teacher qualifications are set by **NCTE**; **TET** per NCTE guidelines.
RTE amended in **2012 and 2017** on teacher qualifications.
PTR: **30:1** primary, **35:1** upper primary.

n47fe1c44dcc.s: The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on:
n47fe1c44dcc.x: The UN General Assembly adopted the UNCRC on 20 November 1989.
n47fe1c44dcc.tq: Separate the adoption date from India’s accession date and the dates of the Optional Protocols.
xs: The **UNCRC** was adopted by the **UN General Assembly** on **20 November 1989** — option **(3)**.
**11 December 1992** is **India's accession**; **14 November** is **India's Children's Day**; **2000** is the year of two Optional Protocols.
xa: UNCRC has **54 articles** (APPSC **2019**).
**20 November** = **Universal Children's Day**.
Four rights: **survival, development, protection, participation**.

n8e7abd63c3b.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four broad categories of rights under the UNCRC?
n8e7abd63c3b.x: The four categories are survival, development, protection and participation; education is not listed as a separate category.
xa: Four principles: **non-discrimination**; **best interests of the child**; right to life, survival and development; respect for **views of the child**.
UNCRC: **20 November 1989**, **54 articles**.
**NPC 2013** has matching priority areas — survival, education, protection, participation.

naa953c93c00.s: India ratified the two 2000 Optional Protocols to the UNCRC in:
naa953c93c00.x: India ratified the two 2000 Optional Protocols in 2005 but is not a party to the 2011 Communications Procedure Protocol.
xa: UNCRC: **20 November 1989**; India acceded **11 December 1992**.
India reports to the **UN Committee on the Rights of the Child**.
**54 articles**.

ne4c3be7f6a1.s: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) was set up in which year, under which law?
o: 2007, under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
ne4c3be7f6a1.x: NCPCR was set up in 2007 under the CPCR Act, 2005. The JJ Act, RTE Act and POCSO Act are laws it monitors, not its parent law.
xs: NCPCR was set up in **2007** under the **Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (CPCR) Act 2005** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Act **2005**, Commission **2007**.
xa: Chairperson + **6** members; **civil court** powers.
Monitors **JJ 2015, POCSO 2012, RTE 2009**.
SCPCRs function at State level (e.g. **AP SCPCR**).

nf3d9b48e4f0.s: Which case upheld the 25 per cent quota in unaided private schools, while excluding unaided minority schools from its application?
o: Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
Unni Krishnan v. State of AP
Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust v. Union of India
Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. Union of India
nf3d9b48e4f0.x: Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. Union of India (2012) upheld the 25 per cent quota in unaided private schools, but not in unaided minority schools.
nf3d9b48e4f0.tq: Discriminate between the two cases concerning RTE applicability to private and minority schools.
xs: **Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. UoI (2012)** upheld the **25% quota** — option **(4)**.
It excluded **unaided minority schools**.
**Pramati (2014)** took **all minority schools** out of RTE; **Bachpan Bachao Andolan** was on **child trafficking**.
xa: ⚠ Rajasthan (**2012**) = quota **upheld**; Pramati (**2014**) = minority schools out.
**Sec. 12(1)(c)**: **25%** entry-level seats for EWS/disadvantaged; **State reimburses**.
**SC (Jan 2026)**: quota effective in only **16 States/UTs**.

n0c24248f669.s: Section 12(1)(c) of the Right to Education Act relates to which of the following?
o: Reservation of 50% seats in private schools for all children
Reservation of 25% seats in all government colleges for girls
Reservation of 25% entry-level seats in unaided private schools for specified children
Reservation of 35% seats in aided schools for minorities
n0c24248f669.x: Section 12(1)(c) requires unaided private schools, excluding minority institutions, to reserve 25% of entry-level seats for children from weaker sections and disadvantaged groups.
n0c24248f669.tq: Identify the exact statutory provision by matching its percentage and institutional coverage.
xs: **Sec. 12(1)(c)**: **25%** of **entry-level seats** in **unaided private schools** for weaker sections/disadvantaged groups — option **(3)**.
**Minority institutions** are excluded; the **State reimburses** per-child expenditure.
xa: **SC (Jan 2026)**, Bench of **Justice P.S. Narasimha**, reaffirmed it.
Quota effectively implemented in only **16 States/UTs**.
Upheld in the **Rajasthan schools case (2012)**.

n8ae3e4f15de.s: The amendment to the RTE Act that permitted detention at Classes V and VIII subject to safeguards was made in:
n8ae3e4f15de.x: The original Act barred detention up to Class VIII; the 2019 amendment allowed detention at Classes V and VIII after examinations and a re-examination opportunity.
xa: It ended **automatic promotion** with regular exams.
Further amended in **2022**.
Section 3 covers education till **elementary** level.

n5a4ecded694.s: Under the RTE Act, 2009, what proportion of the members of a School Management Committee must be parents or guardians?
n5a4ecded694.x: Three-fourths of SMC members must be parents or guardians; SMCs are provided under Section 21 in every government and aided school.
xa: **Sec. 38**: rule-making.
**NCPCR and SCPCRs** monitor RTE.

nefc564272cb.s: Which one of the following is NOT included within the principal coverage of the RTE Act as described?
o: Establishment of neighbourhood schools by the appropriate Government and local authority
Education at the pre-school and secondary levels as a statutory entitlement under the Act
A duty of parents or guardians to send the child to school
Free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years
nefc564272cb.x: The RTE Act does not include pre-school education below six years or secondary and higher education within its principal statutory entitlement.
nefc564272cb.tq: Find the option that extends the Act beyond its stated age and educational-stage coverage.
xs: NOT covered: **pre-school (below 6)** and **secondary** education — option **(2)**.
RTE covers free and compulsory education for **6-14**, **neighbourhood schools**, and the **parent's duty** to send the child to school.
xa: Pre-school care is under **Art. 45** (DPSP, **till 6**).
Parent's duty links to **Art. 51A(k)**.
**Samagra Shiksha** extends support (e.g. **KGBVs** up to Class **12**).

nfb75491271a.s: Under the RTE Act, an out-of-school child is to be admitted to:
o: The lowest class of the nearest school
A class decided by a screening test
nfb75491271a.x: The RTE Act provides age-appropriate admission for out-of-school children and prohibits screening and capitation fee.
xa: **Sec. 21**: **SMCs** with **three-fourths** parents.
Teacher norms: **NCTE**.

n57f0a88ec4c.s: The cost-sharing pattern mentioned for Samagra Shiksha is correctly stated as:
o: 100:0 generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and hill States
40:60 generally and 10:90 for North-Eastern and hill States
60:40 generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and hill States
50:50 generally and 75:25 for North-Eastern and hill States
n57f0a88ec4c.x: The Centre-State sharing pattern is 60:40 generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and hill States.
n57f0a88ec4c.tq: Test both parts of a funding ratio and watch for reversed shares.
xs: **Samagra Shiksha**: **60:40**, and **90:10** for NE and hill States — option **(3)**.
Education is **concurrent**, so Centre and States share costs — neither 100:0 nor 50:50.
xa: Outlay **Rs 42,100 crore** in **2026-27**; extended to **September 2026**.
It merged **SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education** (**2018**).
**KGBVs** up to Class **12**; CwSN support **Rs 3,500**.

n669edb4669e.s: The Supreme Court decision in Unni Krishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1993) recognised that children below 14 years have:
o: A right to employment in non-hazardous industries
A statutory right to adoption under Article 24
A fundamental duty to provide education under Article 51A(k)
A fundamental right to free education under Article 21
n669edb4669e.x: Unni Krishnan recognised a fundamental right to free education for children below 14 years under Article 21. The decision formed the basis for the later insertion of Article 21A.
n669edb4669e.tq: Link the landmark case to the right and constitutional provision it developed.
xs: **Unni Krishnan (1993)**: children below **14** have a **fundamental right to free education** flowing from **Art. 21** — option **(4)**.
It became the basis for **Art. 21A** (**86th**, **2002**).
**51A(k)** is a later Fundamental Duty, not what the case recognised.
xa: Unni Krishnan arose from **Andhra Pradesh**.
Follow-up: Constitution Amendment Bill (**July 1997**) → 86th Amendment (**Dec 2002**).
**RTE Act 2009** in force **1 April 2010**.

nindian-society-1-46.s: Which Constitutional Amendment first made education a Fundamental Right?
nindian-society-1-46.x: The 86th Amendment (2002) made education a Fundamental Right.
n: The first Juvenile Justice Act was enacted in 1986. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The 86th Amendment of 2002 was the first Constitutional Amendment making education a Fundamental Right. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
India ratified the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1992 as its first international convention on child rights. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The UNCRC was the first Child Rights Convention ratified by India in 1992. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Childline emergency helpline was first established at 1098. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xa: India ratified the UNCRC in **1992** (⚠ other notes say **acceded** on **11 December 1992**).
UNCRC adopted **20 November 1989**; **54 articles**.
Childline is now **integrated with ERSS-112**.

n6c0d8c030c6.s: Which case held that the RTE Act does not apply to minority schools?
o: Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust v. Union of India
Unni Krishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh
Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
n6c0d8c030c6.x: Pramati excluded aided and unaided minority schools from the RTE Act; Bachpan Bachao Andolan dealt with trafficking, circus children and FIRs on missing children.
xa: **Rajasthan schools case (2012)** upheld the **25%** quota.
**TrackChild** tracks missing and found children.
**Khoya-Paya** lets citizens report missing/sighted children.

n513d9f9f814.s:
Samagra Shiksha (2018) merged which of the following?
1. Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
2. Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan
3. Teacher Education
n513d9f9f814.x: Samagra Shiksha merged SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education into an integrated school education scheme.
xa: **SSA** began in **2001**.
Funding **60:40**; **90:10** for NE and hill States.
CwSN support **Rs 3,500**; **KGBVs** up to Class **12**.

n55fe6f5cce1.s: The composition of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights consists of:
o: Only a Chairperson and members nominated by the Supreme Court
A Chairperson and eight members, including three women
A Chairperson and six members, including at least two women
A Chairperson and four members, including one woman
n55fe6f5cce1.x: The NCPCR consists of a Chairperson and six members, of whom at least two must be women. It is not composed solely of judicial nominees.
n55fe6f5cce1.tq: Test the exact composition and the minimum representation requirement.
xs: NCPCR: **Chairperson + 6 members**, at least **2 women** — option **(3)**.
Its members are not nominated by the Supreme Court; it is set up under the **CPCR Act 2005**.
xa: It has **civil court** powers while inquiring into complaints.
Set up in **2007**.
Monitors **JJ Act 2015, POCSO Act 2012, RTE Act 2009**.

na25664fd242.s: Which of the following Acts is NOT specifically included among those monitored by the NCPCR?
o: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
na25664fd242.x: The specified monitoring mandate includes the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, the POCSO Act, 2012 and the RTE Act, 2009. The Child Labour Amendment Act, 2016 is not included in that stated list.
na25664fd242.tq: Find the one law outside the commission’s specifically stated monitoring list.
xs: NOT specifically listed: the **Child Labour Amendment Act, 2016** — option **(1)**.
NCPCR monitors the **JJ Act 2015**, **POCSO Act 2012** and **RTE Act 2009**.
xa: **CARA** is a statutory body under the **JJ Act 2015**.
NCPCR: Act **2005**, Commission **2007**.
Child = below **18** under POCSO.

n97fd3eb159d.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four priority areas of the National Policy for Children, 2013?
n97fd3eb159d.x: The four priority areas are survival, health and nutrition; education and development; protection; and participation. Vocational employment is not one of them.
xa: NPC 2013 adopted **April 2013**; child = below **18**.
**National Plan of Action 2016** operationalises it.
**Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat**: **100**-day campaign from **Dec 2025**.

n143a05e762f.s: The National Plan of Action for Children, 2016 primarily:
o: Introduced the constitutional right to education
Replaced the National Policy for Children, 2013
Limited child protection to the education sector
Operationalised the National Policy for Children, 2013
n143a05e762f.x: The National Plan of Action for Children, 2016 put the National Policy for Children, 2013 into operation. It follows the same four priority areas.
n143a05e762f.tq: Distinguish an implementation plan from the policy it operationalises.
xs: The **National Plan of Action for Children 2016** **operationalises NPC 2013** in the same four areas — option **(4)**.
It did not replace NPC 2013; the right to education came from the **86th Amendment**.
xa: ⚠ NPC **2013** = policy; Plan of Action **2016** = operationalises it.
NPC child = below **18**.
Priority areas include **participation** and **protection**.

n65952a507a5.s: The National Policy for Children, 2013 defines a child as a person below the age of:
n65952a507a5.x: The National Policy for Children, adopted in April 2013, treats every person below 18 as a child. 14 is the threshold of child labour law and Article 24, 16 is an age-of-consent figure that has been debated, and 21 is the marriage age for men.
xs: **NPC 2013** defines a child as below **18 years** — option **(3)**.
**14** is the child-labour (**Art. 24**) age.
xa: **DPDP Act 2023** also treats a child as below **18**, needing **verifiable parental consent**.
⚠ Child = below **18** (POCSO) vs below **14** (child labour) vs **6-14** (RTE).
NPC adopted **April 2013**.

n5126661cb58.s: The Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA) became a statutory body under the
o: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
n5126661cb58.x: CARA became a statutory body under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015.
n5126661cb58.tq: Match the statutory body with its parent legislation, not with the subject matter alone.
xs: **CARA** is a statutory body under the **Juvenile Justice Act, 2015** — option **(3)**.
**HAMA 1956** is the personal-law adoption route; **POCSO 2012** and **RTE 2009** are monitored by NCPCR, not adoption laws.
xa: CARA runs **CARINGS** — Child Adoption Resource Information and Guidance System.
**Adoption Regulations 2022**: surrendered children get a **2-month** reconsideration period.
The **JJ route** is open to **all religions**.

n63d06901815.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the age thresholds under the three child-related legal frameworks?
o: POCSO: below 21; child labour law: below 16; RTE: 6–14 years
POCSO: below 14; child labour law: below 18; RTE: 6–18 years
POCSO: 6–14 years; child labour law: below 18; RTE: below 14 years
POCSO: below 18; child labour law: below 14; RTE: 6–14 years
n63d06901815.x: POCSO defines a child as below 18 years, child labour law uses the below-14 threshold stated here, and RTE covers children aged 6–14 years.
n63d06901815.tq: Place each age range with its correct statute before comparing the three frameworks.
xs: **POCSO**: below **18**; **child labour law**: below **14**; **RTE**: **6-14** — option **(4)**.
The other options shuffle these three thresholds.
xa: **Art. 24**: no child below **14** in factories/mines.
**Art. 21A** and **Sec. 3** of RTE: **6-14 years**.
**DPDP Act 2023** and **NPC 2013**: child = below **18**.

nindian-society-1-61.s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (2007)?
nindian-society-1-61.x: The NCPCR was set up in 2007 with Shanta Sinha as its first chairperson.
n: The first National Policy for Children was adopted in 1974. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The first National Commission for Protection of Child Rights was established in 2007. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
Shanta Sinha was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The first Juvenile Justice Act was enacted in 1986. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xa: NCPCR's parent Act: **CPCR Act 2005**.
NCPCR = Chairperson + **6 members** (at least **2 women**).
**NPC 2013** defines a child as below **18**.

n0279d9c33ec.s: Which portal enables citizens to report missing or sighted children?
n0279d9c33ec.x: Khoya-Paya supports citizen reporting of missing or sighted children; TrackChild tracks missing and found children and CARINGS relates to adoption.
xa: **CHILDLINE 1098** integrated with **ERSS-112** across **36** States/UTs.
**e-Baal Nidan** = NCPCR complaints portal.
⚠ e-Baal Nidan = NCPCR complaints; CARINGS = CARA adoption.

o: Online complaints regarding violation of child rights
Tracking children rescued from hazardous employment only
nbcaba3aac7d.x: e-Baal Nidan is the NCPCR’s online complaint portal for violations of child rights. CARINGS is the adoption-related system, while CHILDLINE 1098 is the emergency helpline.
nbcaba3aac7d.tq: Identify the portal by its institutional purpose rather than its name alone.
xs: **e-Baal Nidan** = NCPCR's **online complaints** portal for **violation of child rights** — option **(1)**.
Adoption is **CARINGS** (CARA); emergency help is **CHILDLINE 1098**.
xa: NCPCR has **civil court** powers while inquiring.
**CARA** is statutory under the **JJ Act 2015**.
**Adoption Regulations 2022**: **2-month** reconsideration period.

o: An online portal exclusively for cybercrime complaints
A statutory commission for monitoring the RTE Act
A 24×7 child helpline integrated with ERSS-112
A judicial body for transferring juveniles aged 16–18 years
n4ec34df3afb.x: CHILDLINE 1098 is a 24×7 child helpline and is now integrated with ERSS-112.
n4ec34df3afb.tq: Distinguish a helpline from a portal, commission and judicial mechanism.
xs: **CHILDLINE 1098** is a **24x7 emergency helpline** for children, now **integrated with ERSS-112** — option **(3)**.
RTE monitoring is by **NCPCR/SCPCRs**; online complaints go to **e-Baal Nidan**.
xa: Integration covers **36 States/UTs** (CDI **2026**).
**TrackChild** tracks missing and found children (**Mission Vatsalya**).
**Khoya-Paya** is integrated with TrackChild.

nindian-society-37-6.s: Which platform provides real-time digital tracking of Anganwadi service delivery, stunting, wasting and nutrition metrics for children aged 0–6 years?
nindian-society-37-6.x: The Poshan Tracker app (WCD) tracks Anganwadi services, stunting, wasting and nutrition for children aged 0–6 in real time.
nindian-society-37-6.tq: Match each portal to its function.
n: The Poshan Tracker App is a digital platform for children and infants. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The Poshan Tracker App digitally tracks Anganwadi service delivery in real time. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The Poshan Tracker App tracks stunting and wasting. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The Poshan Tracker App tracks nutrition metrics for children aged 0–6 years. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The TrackChild Portal and Khoya-Paya are digital platforms for children and infants. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The TrackChild Portal and Khoya-Paya track missing children. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The TrackChild Portal and Khoya-Paya track vulnerable children. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The TrackChild Portal and Khoya-Paya track institutionalized children. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]

n8938b7958a3.s: Which authority lays down the minimum qualifications for appointment of teachers under the RTE framework?
o: State Council for Teacher Education alone
National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
n8938b7958a3.x: The minimum teacher qualifications are laid down by the academic authority notified by the Central Government, namely the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE).
n8938b7958a3.tq: Apply the 'who performs this function?' method to distinguish the national academic authority from monitoring bodies.
xs: Teacher qualifications are set by the **National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE)** — option **(1)**.
⚠ The academic authority is notified by the **Centre** — not a State council.
**NCPCR** monitors RTE; **SMCs** run schools — neither sets qualifications.
xa: **TET** follows NCTE guidelines.
RTE amended on teacher qualifications in **2012 and 2017**.
PTR: **30:1** primary, **35:1** upper primary.

n7725e359759.s: Which one of the following is NOT a correct feature of the RTE Act?
o: The Centre bears the sole financial responsibility for implementing the Act.
Parents or guardians have a duty to send the child to school.
The appropriate Government and local authority must establish neighbourhood schools.
Unaided private schools provide specified entry-level seats for weaker and disadvantaged groups.
n7725e359759.x: The Centre does not bear sole financial responsibility; funds are shared by the Centre and the States. The other statements describe features of the Act.
n7725e359759.tq: Identify the false financial-responsibility claim hidden among genuine statutory duties.
xs: NOT a feature: **the Centre bears sole financial responsibility** — option **(1)**.
Funds are **shared** by Centre and States (APPSC **2017** odd one out).
Neighbourhood schools, parent's duty and the **25%** private-school quota are features.
xa: **Samagra Shiksha** funding: **60:40** (**90:10** NE and hill States).
Education is **concurrent**.
The **State reimburses** private schools for the **25%** seats.

n59794efeaf4.s: As per the provisional figures of Census 2011, the child sex ratio (0-6 years) of India was:
n59794efeaf4.x: The child sex ratio (0-6) was 914 in Census 2011. 943 is the overall sex ratio in Census 2011, and 1,020 is the overall sex ratio in NFHS-5. 927 was the child sex ratio in Census 2001.
xs: Child sex ratio (**0-6**), Census **2011** = **914** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **943** is the **overall** sex ratio (Census 2011); **1,020** is NFHS-5's overall ratio.
xa: Child labour (5-14): **4.35 million** main workers.
**Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat**: **100-day** campaign against child marriage from **Dec 2025**.

nb7663ae9edb.s: Which one of the following is an example of physical child abuse by omission?
o: Using the child for sexual stimulation
nb7663ae9edb.x: Medical or nutritional neglect is physical abuse by omission. Beating and burning are examples of physical abuse by commission.
nb7663ae9edb.tq: Distinguish acts of commission from acts of omission within physical abuse.
xs: **Medical or nutritional neglect** is physical abuse by **omission** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Beating** (and burning) is physical abuse by **commission**, not omission.
**Using a child for sexual stimulation** is **sexual abuse (CSA)**; **verbal battering** is **emotional/non-physical** abuse.
xa: The four forms of child abuse in the notes: **physical**, **sexual**, **emotional/non-physical** and **social**.
Social abuse covers **infanticide**, **child marriage**, **child prostitution** and **beggary**.
Emotional abuse also includes **educational neglect** and **fostering delinquency**.

n58e27efd0f8.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of emotional or non-physical child abuse?
n58e27efd0f8.x: Child prostitution is a form of social abuse. Verbal battering, educational neglect and fostering delinquency are emotional or non-physical forms of abuse.
n58e27efd0f8.tq: Find the item belonging to the neighbouring social-abuse category.
xs: **Child prostitution** is a form of **social** abuse, not emotional abuse — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Verbal battering**, **educational neglect** and **fostering delinquency** are all listed as **emotional/non-physical** abuse.
xa: Other forms of social abuse: **infanticide**, **child marriage** and **beggary**.
Physical abuse = acts of **commission** (beating, burning) or **omission** (medical or nutritional neglect).
Online abuse / **CSAM**: over **4.5 lakh** cases reported in India in **2023**, dealt with under the **IT Act 2000**.

n51f8911940c.s: The Draft National Policy on Child Protection requires which of the following in all organisations?
o: A child-rights audit by the NCPCR
n51f8911940c.x: The Draft National Policy on Child Protection requires a zero-tolerance code of conduct in all organisations.
xa: **National Policy for Children 2013**: everyone below **18** a child; best interests first.
**Art. 39(e)**: tender age of children not abused; **Art. 39(f)**: protection against exploitation and moral/material abandonment.
**Mission Vatsalya** is the MWCD umbrella for child protection.

n8742e650cbf.s: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was drafted by which Ministry of the Government of India?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
n8742e650cbf.x: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was drafted by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
n8742e650cbf.tq: Identify the ministry associated with the legislation rather than its implementing agencies.
xs: **POCSO** was drafted by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development** — option **(1)** is correct.
The Act came into force on **14 November 2012**.
xa: A child = below **18 years**, **gender-neutral** for child and offender.
POCSO remains a separate special law after the **BNS 2023** replaced the IPC from **1 July 2024**.
The **NCPCR and SCPCRs** monitor POCSO.

n83b470bf61f.s: Under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, which one of the following is correct regarding the definition of a child?
o: A person below 16 years, only if female
A person below 14 years, irrespective of gender
A person below 21 years, irrespective of gender
A person below 18 years, irrespective of gender
n83b470bf61f.x: POCSO treats every person below 18 years as a child and applies in a gender-neutral manner.
n83b470bf61f.tq: Distinguish the age and gender-neutral definition under POCSO from other child-related laws.
xs: POCSO defines a child as a person **below 18 years**, **irrespective of gender** — option **(4)** is correct.
The Act is **gender-neutral** for both child and offender.
xa: Consent below **18** is **legally irrelevant** ("statutory rape").
**BNS (Sec. 63)** keeps the age of consent at **18**.
⚠ Marriage age is distinct: **18** for women, **21** for men.

n5396ea216e6.s: Which one of the following is inconsistent with the child-friendly procedure prescribed under the POCSO Act?
o: The statement should preferably be recorded by a woman police officer of at least Sub-Inspector rank who is not in uniform.
The child’s statement may be recorded at the child’s residence.
The statement may be recorded at a place chosen by the child.
The child must be questioned at the police station during the night to prevent interference.
n5396ea216e6.x: A child must not be kept at a police station at night. The statement is preferably recorded by a woman police officer of at least Sub-Inspector rank, not in uniform, at the child’s residence or chosen place.
xs: Questioning the child **at the police station during the night** breaks the POCSO procedure — option **(4)** is the inconsistent one.
**No child is kept at a police station at night**, and the child has **no contact with the accused**.
The statement is taken at the **child's residence or place of choice**, preferably by a **woman police officer (at least SI)** **not in uniform** — so (1), (2) and (3) are correct.
xa: **Special Courts** hold **in-camera** trials; investigation in **2 months**, trial within **1 year**.
Special Courts also order **compensation and rehabilitation**.
**NCPCR and SCPCRs** monitor the Act.

na93e24d5483.s: The offence of trafficking of persons, widened by the Criminal Law Amendment Act 2013, is now dealt with under which provision?
o: Section 370, Indian Penal Code, which continues in force
na93e24d5483.x: Trafficking is now Section 143 of the BNS 2023. Section 63 BNS is the rape provision that keeps the age of consent at 18; Section 19 POCSO concerns mandatory reporting; the IPC was replaced by the BNS from 1 July 2024.
xs: Trafficking is now under **Section 143, BNS 2023** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Section 63, BNS** keeps the **age of consent** at **18**; **Section 19, POCSO** is **mandatory reporting**.
The IPC no longer continues — the **BNS** replaced it from **1 July 2024**.
xa: The **Criminal Law Amendment Act 2013** widened trafficking, **irrespective of consent**.
It covers sexual exploitation, slavery, servitude, forced labour, organ removal.
**AHTUs** operate in districts under MHA funding.

n5346c869885.s: Which policy followed the recommendations associated with the Gurupadswamy Committee?
n5346c869885.x: The National Policy on Child Labour followed in 1987.
n5346c869885.tq: Separate the child-labour policy of 1987 from later general child-policy instruments.
xs: The **National Policy on Child Labour, 1987** followed — option **(1)** is correct.
The **National Policy for Children 2013** treats everyone below **18** as a child — a different policy.
xa: **Gurupadswamy Committee** = **1979**; Child Labour Act = **1986**; **NCLP** = **1988**.
The committee's line: ban hazardous work, **regulate** the rest.
**NCLP** was run by **MoLE**, not MoSJE.

n39fe7e07958.s: The PENCIL portal is primarily intended for enforcement of:
o: The Right to Education Act, 2009 only
The amended Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 only

xs: PENCIL enforces the **amended Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is not a portal for the RTE, JJ or POCSO Acts.
xa: Asked in APPSC-G2 **2025**.
Ministry: **Labour and Employment**; launched **2017**.
⚠ **POCSO e-Box** (**2016**, NCPCR) is the complaint channel for child sexual abuse.

n409e33e35e9.s: Which Ministry launched the PENCIL portal?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Women and Child Development

xs: PENCIL was launched by the **Ministry of Labour and Employment** — option **(3)** is correct.

**Amendment Rules 2017** were also notified by **MoLE**.

n4c8e4dbae38.s: The National Child Labour Project is run by the:

n4c8e4dbae38.x: The NCLP is run by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, not the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
n4c8e4dbae38.tq: Apply the ‘wrong ministry’ trap by separating labour administration from social-justice administration.
xs: The **NCLP** is run by the **Ministry of Labour and Employment** (MoLE) — option **(2)** is correct.

xa: NCLP started in **1988**.

NCLP was **merged into Samagra Shiksha** from **2021-22**.

nindian-society-38-19.s: What is the expanded form of PENCIL in the context of child labour enforcement?

xs: **PENCIL** = **Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour** — option **(1)**.

nc384b5f6a31.s: According to the Study on Child Abuse: India 2007, what proportion of children faced physical abuse?

nc384b5f6a31.tq: Distinguish the proportion for physical abuse from the separate percentage for sexual abuse.

**Boys** were as much at risk as **girls**.
Highest abuse rates: **AP, Assam, Bihar and Delhi**.

ne892827183f.s: The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 made compulsory the registration of:

ne892827183f.tq: Identify the exact institutional category covered by the compulsory-registration provision.

xa: **District Child Protection Units** handle child protection at district level.

n029562f24ae.s: Mission Vatsalya, the umbrella for child protection from 1 April 2022, is run by which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Women and Child Development

xa: Period **2021-22 to 2025-26**, outlay **Rs 10,916 crore**, funding ratio **60:40**.

Registration of **Child Care Institutions** is compulsory.

n5b9a43ce10f.s: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 replaced the term ‘juvenile’ with which term?
n5b9a43ce10f.x: The Act replaced the term ‘juvenile’ with ‘child’, reflecting a child-centred approach.
n5b9a43ce10f.tq: Directly distinguish the exact statutory terminology from nearby legal terms.
xs: The **JJ Act 2015** replaced "juvenile" with **"child"** — option **(3)** is correct.
It created two categories: **Children in Conflict with Law** and **Children in Need of Care and Protection**.
xa: **Heinous offence** = minimum punishment of **7 years or more**.
**CARA** was made a **statutory body** by the 2015 Act.
The Act was amended in **2021**.

nfca7e8726ce.s: Under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, a ‘heinous offence’ is one for which the minimum punishment is:
nfca7e8726ce.x: A heinous offence is defined by a minimum punishment of seven years or more.
nfca7e8726ce.tq: Focus on the statutory minimum threshold rather than the maximum sentence.
xs: A **heinous offence** carries a minimum punishment of **seven years or more** — option **(3)** is correct.
A child aged **16-18** accused of a heinous offence faces a **preliminary assessment** by the JJB.
xa: After assessment the case may go to the **Children's Court** — the "**transfer system**".
Critics say the **transfer system** erodes rehabilitation.
The punitive turn followed the **Delhi gang rape case (2012)**.

nb3930cdffe8.s: After a preliminary assessment of a 16–18-year-old accused of a heinous offence, the Juvenile Justice Board may transfer the case to the:
nb3930cdffe8.x: The JJB may transfer the matter to the Children's Court after the preliminary assessment, which does not itself establish guilt.
xa: **Heinous offence** = minimum punishment of **7 years or more**.
The transfer system came after the **Delhi gang rape case (2012)**.
Criticism: the **transfer system** erodes rehabilitation.

nf9770d5160e.s: The Juvenile Justice (Amendment) Act, 2021 made whom the focal point for implementation of the Act and empowered to decide adoption cases?
o: Chairperson of the Child Welfare Committee
Principal Magistrate of the Juvenile Justice Board
nf9770d5160e.x: The 2021 amendment made the District Magistrate the focal point for implementation and gave the DM power to decide adoption cases.
xa: The amendment came with the **JJ Amendment Rules** and **Adoption Regulations 2022**.
**CWC** = Chairperson + **4 members**.
**CARA** was made statutory by the **2015** Act.

ne1f207c1a94.s: Under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000, the age of a juvenile was made uniform at:
ne1f207c1a94.x: The JJ Act, 2000 prescribed a uniform age of 18 years and was amended in 2006.
ne1f207c1a94.tq: Distinguish the uniform age under the 2000 Act from the gender-based ages under the 1986 Act.
xs: The **JJ Act 2000** made the age uniform at **18 years** — option **(3)** is correct.
Earlier, the **1986** Act used **16** for boys and **18** for girls.
xa: The 2000 Act was amended in **2006**.
The **2015** Act brought the transfer system for **16-18**-year-olds in heinous offences.
**Children Act 1960** applied to **Union Territories**.

n9c8134954cd.s: The punitive turn associated with the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 followed which event?
o: The Delhi gang rape case of 2012
The enactment of the CPCR Act in 2005
n9c8134954cd.x: The 2015 Act followed the punitive policy response triggered by the Delhi gang rape case of 2012.
n9c8134954cd.tq: Link the legislative change to the event that acted as its immediate trigger.
xs: The punitive turn of the **JJ Act 2015** followed the **Delhi gang rape case (2012)** — option **(2)** is correct.
It brought the **transfer system** for **16-18**-year-olds accused of heinous offences.
The **CPCR Act 2005** created the NCPCR; the **Sivakasi** case (**1996**) concerned child labour.
xa: **Heinous offence** = minimum **7 years or more**.
The JJB's **preliminary assessment** decides on a transfer to the **Children's Court**.
The 2015 Act came into force on **15 Jan 2016**.

nd80df901f5c.s: The Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA) was given statutory status by the:
o: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
nd80df901f5c.x: The JJ Act 2015 made CARA a statutory body. HAMA 1956 is a separate adoption route for Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs; the 2021 amendment gave District Magistrates the power to decide adoptions; the CPCR Act 2005 created the NCPCR.

xs: The **Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015** made **CARA** (Central Adoption Resource Authority) a **statutory body** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **2021** amendment gave the **District Magistrate** power to decide adoptions; the **CPCR Act 2005** set up the **NCPCR**.
xa: **Adoption Regulations 2022** came with the 2021 amendment.
AP CWCs declared **55** children legally free for adoption in FY **2025-26**.
The 2015 Act replaced "juvenile" with "**child**".

n55235fc4895.s: Children in Conflict with Law are dealt with by:
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
n55235fc4895.x: Children in Conflict with Law come before Juvenile Justice Boards; every district has both a JJB and a CWC, each with at least one woman member.

**Mission Vatsalya** funds JJBs and CWCs in every district.

n18213e7e083.s: A Juvenile Justice Board consists of:
o: A Sessions Judge and four police officers
A Principal Magistrate and two social workers, at least one of whom is a woman
A Chairperson and four members, all of whom must be social workers
A District Magistrate and five elected representatives
n18213e7e083.x: The Board comprises a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate First Class serving as Principal Magistrate and two social workers, with at least one woman among the social workers.
n18213e7e083.tq: Test composition by separating the judicial member from the social-worker members.
xs: A JJB has a **Principal Magistrate** and **two social workers**, at least one a **woman** — option **(2)** is correct.
The Principal Magistrate is a **Metropolitan/Judicial Magistrate First Class**.
"Chairperson and four members" describes the **CWC**, not the JJB.
xa: ⚠ JJB = Magistrate + **2**; CWC = Chairperson + **4**.
The **Children's Court** (Sessions Court) tries transferred cases.
AP CWCs handled **4,189** cases and disposed **3,691** in FY **2025-26**.

n0fae1000ee2.s: The guiding principle in inquiries and proceedings involving children under the Juvenile Justice system is:
o: Best interests of the child through child-friendly and rehabilitation-oriented justice
Detention in every case until adulthood
Retributive punishment as the primary objective
n0fae1000ee2.x: The system is guided by the best interests of the child and follows child-friendly, rehabilitation-oriented justice rather than a punishment-centred approach.
n0fae1000ee2.tq: Identify the governing principle from the stated purpose of the legal process.
xs: Proceedings follow the **best interests of the child** through **child-friendly, rehabilitation-oriented justice** — option **(1)** is correct.
The system is about rehabilitation, **not punishment**, so detention or retribution is wrong.
xa: Juvenile delinquents are dealt with by **juvenile courts** (APPSC **2019**).
The principle was asked in APPSC **2019** and **2024**.
The **National Policy for Children 2013** also puts best interests first.

n2bd1c4546ae.s: Operation Smile and Operation Muskaan are primarily associated with:

n2bd1c4546ae.tq: Match the operation names with their distinctive field objective.
xs: **Operation Smile / Operation Muskaan** are **MHA**-led drives for **tracing and rescuing missing children** — option **(1)** is correct.
Child-care institutions, adoption and exams are not their purpose.
xa: The drives began in **2015**.
AP's **Operation Muskaan** rescued over **1,200 children** from railway stations, bus stands, markets and dhabas.
⚠ AP's **Operation Chinnari-Thalli** targets **sexual offences** against children.

nfba8652cc66.s: Which law widened the concept of trafficking to include sexual exploitation, slavery, servitude, forced labour and organ removal?
nfba8652cc66.x: The Criminal Law Amendment Act, 2013 widened trafficking to cover sexual exploitation, slavery, servitude, forced labour and organ removal.
xa: The definition applies **irrespective of consent**.

**Anti-Human Trafficking Units** work in districts under **MHA** funding.

n324c0fdb7d8.s: The primary responsibility for enforcement of the amended child labour law is vested in the:
o: Chairperson of the Child Welfare Committee
Principal Magistrate of the Juvenile Justice Board
n324c0fdb7d8.x: Enforcement powers under the amended framework rest with the District Magistrate.
n324c0fdb7d8.tq: Use the authority-power trap by identifying the designated enforcement authority.
xs: Enforcement rests with the **District Magistrate** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **CWC** chairperson and the **JJB**'s Principal Magistrate belong to the JJ system, not child-labour enforcement.
xa: **State Governments** implement; the Centre frames policy.
Tools: **labour inspectors**, surprise inspections, rescue and rehabilitation.
Offences are **cognizable**.

n03a752f4101.s: Under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, working children are treated as:
o: Adult workers requiring wage protection only
Children in conflict with law in every case
Children in need of care and protection
n03a752f4101.x: The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 treats working children as children in need of care and protection.
n03a752f4101.tq: Identify the correct statutory child-protection category.
xs: The **JJ Act 2015** treats working children as **children in need of care and protection** — option **(4)** is correct.
Such children go to the **Child Welfare Committee**, not the JJB.
xa: ⚠ CCL → **JJB**; CNCP → **CWC**.
**CWC** = Chairperson + **4 members**.
The NCPCR campaign rescued **3,800+** children from child labour (**2026**).

n4911a890e04.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the PENCIL portal?
n4911a890e04.x: The listed PENCIL components include the Child Tracking System, Complaint Corner, State Government, NCLP and Convergence. National Adoption Registry is not one of them.
n4911a890e04.tq: Find the component that belongs to adoption administration rather than labour-enforcement architecture.
xs: **National Adoption Registry** is not a PENCIL component — option **(3)** is correct.
Components: **Child Tracking System**, **Complaint Corner**, **State Government**, **NCLP** and **Convergence**.
xa: PENCIL = **Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour**.
Adoption is handled by **CARA** (statutory under the **JJ Act 2015**) and the **District Magistrate**.
PENCIL launched on **26 Sep 2017**.

n38a6d965eac.s: The principal objective of the National Child Labour Project is to:
o: Transfer all rescued children directly to juvenile courts
Regulate adult employment in hazardous industries
Withdraw children from labour and provide education and vocational training
Provide only financial compensation to employers
n38a6d965eac.x: The NCLP withdraws children from labour and provides education and vocational training.
n38a6d965eac.tq: Identify the scheme by its combined withdrawal, education and vocational-training objective.
xs: The NCLP aims to **withdraw children from labour** and give them **education and vocational training** — option **(3)** is correct.
It does not send children to juvenile courts, regulate adult work or compensate employers.
xa: **Special Training Centres** serve rescued children aged **9-14** before regular school.
They give **bridge education**, vocational training, **mid-day meal** and a **stipend**.
NCLP began in **1988** under **MoLE**.

ndba2fc0c6b7.s: Which one of the following cases held that child labour in construction violates fundamental rights?
o: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996)
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India (2011)
ndba2fc0c6b7.x: PUDR v. Union of India (1982) held that child labour in construction violates fundamental rights.
ndba2fc0c6b7.tq: Use the case-year pairing to distinguish judicial precedents.
xs: **PUDR v. Union of India (1982)** held child labour in **construction** violates **Fundamental Rights** — option **(1)** is correct.
**M.C. Mehta (1996)** concerned **hazardous industries** at Sivakasi; **Bachpan Bachao Andolan (2011)** stressed stricter enforcement and rescue.
xa: Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. UoI (**2011**): **rescue and rehabilitation** of child labourers.
M.C. Mehta: employer pays **₹20,000 per child**.
**NCPCR** was set up in **2007** under the **CPCR Act 2005** — a body, not a case.

n7ecec27992f.s: A Private Member’s Bill reported in December 2025 sought to lower the heinous-offence threshold under the juvenile justice framework from:
n7ecec27992f.x: The Bill sought to lower the heinous-offence threshold from 16 years to 14 years.
n7ecec27992f.tq: Track the direction and magnitude of the proposed age change.
xs: The **Private Member's Bill (Dec 2025)** seeks to lower it from **16 to 14** years — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **18 to 16** is the earlier standing-committee recommendation (APPSC **2022**).
xa: Under the JJ Act 2015, **16-18**-year-olds accused of heinous offences can be transferred.
**Heinous offence** = minimum punishment **7 years or more**.
Criticism: the **transfer system** erodes rehabilitation.

nindian-society-43-4.s: The Phulrenu Guha Committee dealt with:
nindian-society-43-4.x: The Phulrenu Guha Committee dealt with the status of women; Verma with crimes against women, Gurupadaswamy with child labour and Jaya Jaitly with marriage age.
n: The Jaya Jaitly Task Force dealt with marriage age and maternal health. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Justice J.S. Verma Committee dealt with crimes against women. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Phulrenu Guha Committee dealt with the status of women. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Gurupadaswamy Committee dealt with child labour and exploitation. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
xa: Phulrenu Guha produced the **Towards Equality Report** (**1974**).
Verma Committee (**2013**) shaped the **Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013**.
Gurupadaswamy's **dual approach** led to the **1986 Child Labour Act**.

nindian-society-43-8.s: Stalking and voyeurism were introduced as offences on the recommendation of the:
nindian-society-43-8.x: The J.S. Verma Committee (Home Affairs) widened the definition of rape and added stalking and voyeurism.
n: The nodal ministry for the Justice J.S. Verma Committee was the Ministry of Home Affairs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Justice J.S. Verma Committee expanded the definitions of rape. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Justice J.S. Verma Committee introduced stalking as an offence. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Justice J.S. Verma Committee introduced voyeurism as an offence. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Gurupadaswamy Committee dealt with child labour and exploitation. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
xa: It was constituted in **2013** after the **2012 Nirbhaya** incident.
⚠ The **Justice Deepak Verma Committee** dealt with **adoption** and childcare institutions.

nindian-society-43-9.s: The Phulrenu Guha Committee is associated with which report?
nindian-society-43-9.x: The Phulrenu Guha Committee produced the 'Towards Equality' report (1974). The Verma Committee shaped the 2013 Criminal Law Amendment, and the Gurupadaswamy Committee led to the 1986 Child Labour Act.
nindian-society-43-9.tq: Match each committee to its report or Act.
n: The Phulrenu Guha Committee produced the Towards Equality Report in 1974. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
xs: The **Phulrenu Guha Committee** produced the **Towards Equality Report** (**1974**) — option **(4)**.
The **Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013** was shaped by the **J.S. Verma Committee**.
The **1986 Child Labour Act** came from the **Gurupadaswamy Committee**.
xa: Phulrenu Guha came under the **Ministry of Education and Social Welfare**.
The report **uncovered** declining **sex ratios** and poor **health metrics**.
A **National Policy for Women** was recommended by **Pam Rajput**.

nindian-society-43-20.s: Which committee, associated with the Supreme Court and the Ministry of Women and Child Development, streamlined adoption processes?
nindian-society-43-20.x: The Justice Deepak Verma Committee simplified adoption and oversaw childcare institutions under the JJ framework.
n: The dual approach recommended by the Gurupadaswamy Committee led to the 1986 Child Labour Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The nodal agencies for the Justice Deepak Verma Committee were the Supreme Court of India and the Ministry of Women and Child Development. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Justice Deepak Verma Committee framed guidelines for streamlining adoption processes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Justice Deepak Verma Committee framed guidelines for oversight of childcare institutions. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The guidelines of the Justice Deepak Verma Committee concerned childcare institutions under the Juvenile Justice framework. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Justice Deepak Verma Committee dealt with child protection and adoption. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
xa: **CARA** is a statutory body under the **JJ Act 2015**.
**Adoption Regulations 2022** give surrendered children a **2-month** reconsideration period.

nindian-society-49-5.s: The 2021 amendment to the Juvenile Justice Act empowered which authority to issue adoption orders?
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights
nindian-society-49-5.x: The 2021 amendment (in force from 2022) gave District Magistrates the power to issue adoption orders in place of courts.
n: The 2021/2022 amendment to the Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection of Children) Act empowered District Magistrates (DMs) to issue adoption orders. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 101-102]
xa: The DM is the **focal point** for implementation of the JJ Act.
The amendment also set **eligibility conditions** for **CWC members**.
**Adoption Regulations 2022** followed.

n712c38f3233.s: Protection of children against exploitation and moral and material abandonment is provided under:
n712c38f3233.x: Article 39(f) guards against exploitation and moral and material abandonment; Article 39(e) protects tender age from abuse.
xa: **National Policy for Children 2013**: everyone below **18** is a child; best interests first.
The **NCPCR** (**2007**, **CPCR Act 2005**) monitors **POCSO**, the **JJ Act** and the **RTE Act**.
