The Criminal Law Amendment Act **2013** widened the trafficking definition; it is now **Section 143, BNS 2023**.

nc30f3e00bd3.s: Under the POCSO Act, an offence committed by a person in a position of trust is treated as
o: an offence applicable only to institutions
nc30f3e00bd3.x: The Act treats offences committed by a person in a position of trust as aggravated offences.
nc30f3e00bd3.tq: Test the legal consequence attached to a special relationship of trust.
xs: An offence by a person in **trust or authority** is an **aggravated** offence — option **(4)** is correct.
Examples: **police**, **security forces**, **public servant**.
xa: POCSO offences: **penetrative** and **non-penetrative** assault, aggravated forms, **sexual harassment**, **child pornography**.
**2019**: aggravated penetrative assault minimum **20 years**, up to **life or death penalty**.
Penetrative sexual assault minimum: **10 years**.

n391d18fc2db.s: The 21 April 2018 Ordinance relating to the POCSO Act primarily provided for
o: replacement of mandatory reporting with voluntary reporting
harsher punishment for rape of young girls
lowering the age of a child to 14 years
n391d18fc2db.x: The Ordinance of 21 April 2018 introduced harsher punishment for rape of young girls.
n391d18fc2db.tq: Match the dated legislative measure with its principal substantive change.
xs: The **21 April 2018** Ordinance provided **harsher punishment for rape of young girls** — option **(2)** is correct.
POCSO still keeps **mandatory reporting**, **Special Courts** and the age of **18**.
xa: **2019 Amendment**: penetrative assault minimum **10 years**; aggravated minimum **20 years**; up to **death penalty**.
**POCSO Rules 2020** replaced the 2012 Rules.
The 2018 date was asked by APPSC.

ncf9e0227760.s: Which of the following correctly describes the 2019 amendment to the POCSO Act?
o: It introduced the death penalty for aggravated penetrative assault and prescribed a minimum punishment of 20 years
It removed the punishment of imprisonment for aggravated penetrative assault
It made all POCSO offences compoundable
It reduced the minimum punishment to 7 years
ncf9e0227760.x: The 2019 amendment provided for the death penalty in aggravated penetrative assault cases and prescribed a minimum punishment of 20 years. The POCSO Rules were framed in 2020.
ncf9e0227760.tq: Use the precise punishment figures to distinguish the amendment from neighbouring provisions.
xs: The **2019** amendment brought the **death penalty** for **aggravated penetrative assault** and a minimum of **20 years** — option **(1)** is correct.
It raised punishments, so options (2) and (4) are wrong; the penetrative minimum is **10 years**, not 7.
xa: ⚠ **10** = penetrative minimum; **20** = aggravated minimum.
Storing child pornography without deleting/reporting: fine at least **Rs 5,000**; repeat **Rs 10,000**.
It also punishes giving **chemicals to hasten sexual maturity**.
**POCSO Rules 2020** replaced the 2012 Rules.

n8c88c0f4237.s: Under the POCSO Act, consent of a person below ____ years is legally irrelevant.
n8c88c0f4237.x: POCSO fixes the relevant age at 18 years, so apparent consent below 18 is irrelevant.
xa: The **MP High Court** asked the Centre to lower it to **16** (APPSC **2022**).
SC in **State of UP v. Anurudh** urged a **"Romeo-Juliet" clause**.

n24c793668d8.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the trial framework under the POCSO Act?
o: Trial before the High Court within one month without compensation provisions
In-camera trial, with investigation targeted within two months and trial within one year
Open trial within two years after investigation by any police station
Trial only before a Juvenile Justice Board within six months
n24c793668d8.x: POCSO provides for in-camera proceedings, investigation within two months and trial within one year; special courts also address compensation and rehabilitation.
n24c793668d8.tq: Combine the court type and statutory time limits without reversing them.
xs: POCSO provides an **in-camera trial**, investigation within **two months** and trial within **one year** — option **(2)** is correct.
Trials are before **Special Courts**, not the High Court or a JJB, and are not open.
Special Courts also provide **compensation and rehabilitation**.
xa: Statement recorded preferably by a **woman police officer (at least SI)**, **not in uniform**.
No child kept at a police station at night; no contact with the accused.
**Disposals** of cases are up (**109%**) but convictions are falling.

n01e267fa07b.s: The POCSO Act came into force on:
n01e267fa07b.x: POCSO came into force on 14 November 2012; the 2019 amendment set a 10-year minimum for penetrative sexual assault.
xa: Aggravated penetrative assault: minimum **20 years**, up to **death penalty**.
The **21 April 2018** Ordinance brought harsher punishment for rape of young girls.
Full name: **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012**.

ne7e7b923452.s: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 retains 18 years as the age of consent under Section:
ne7e7b923452.x: BNS Section 63 retains 18 years as the age of consent.
xa: **Standing Committee on Home Affairs, 167th Report (2012)** backed **18**.
**Law Commission 283rd Report (2023)**: lowering would make POCSO a **"paper law"**.
⚠ APPSC **2022** keyed as "true" that the committee recommended lowering the age from **18**.

n205af3cfd1b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Supreme Court's decision on the Calcutta High Court ruling on adolescent relationships?
o: The Supreme Court set aside the Calcutta High Court ruling
The Calcutta High Court ruling had excluded consensual adolescent relationships from POCSO
The Supreme Court used Article 142 for sentencing flexibility
The Supreme Court itself excluded consensual adolescent relationships from POCSO
n205af3cfd1b.x: The Supreme Court set aside the High Court ruling that had excluded consensual adolescent relationships from POCSO; it did not create such an exclusion itself.
xa: In **State of UP v. Anurudh** the SC flagged **misuse of POCSO** and urged a **"Romeo-Juliet" clause**.
Debate: **close-in-age exemption** vs keeping the age at **18** with judicial discretion.
SC: child assessments must involve **"minimum intrusion"** where the child is an alleged abuse victim.

nebd9b54d42f.s: The age of consent under POCSO should not be confused with the legal age of marriage, which is:
o: 18 years for women and 21 years for men
21 years for women and 18 years for men
18 years for women and 18 years for men
16 years for women and 18 years for men
nebd9b54d42f.x: The age of consent under POCSO is 18 years. The legal marriage age referred to here is 18 years for women and 21 years for men.
nebd9b54d42f.tq: Separate two closely related but legally distinct age thresholds.
xs: The marriage age is **18 for women and 21 for men** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is distinct from the age of consent under POCSO, which is **18** for all.
xa: NFHS-5: over **27%** of women aged **20-24** married before **18**; newer figure **23.3%**.
Child marriage is listed as **social** abuse.
**APSES 2024-25**: **877** child marriages prevented in AP.

n483ee8d530e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the age of consent under POCSO?
o: The Law Commission (283rd Report, 2023) recommended lowering the age of consent
The Standing Committee on Home Affairs (167th Report, 2012) supported retaining 18 years
The Law Commission warned that lowering the age could make POCSO a 'paper law'
The Supreme Court in January 2026 urged consideration of a Romeo-Juliet clause
n483ee8d530e.x: The 283rd Law Commission Report warned against lowering the age, saying it could make POCSO a 'paper law'.
xa: The **Justice Verma Committee** wanted **16**.
The **240th Report** (**2011**, Standing Committee on HRD) rejected minor consent.
The **MP High Court** asked for **16**, citing social-media exposure.

nf89bdbaa84e.s: Special Training Centres under the National Child Labour Project cater to rescued children of which age group?
nf89bdbaa84e.x: NCLP Special Training Centres serve rescued children aged 9-14 with bridge education, vocational training, mid-day meal and a stipend.
xa: NCLP started in **1988**, under **MoLE**.
Process: **identification → rescue → rehabilitation**.
**India rescues**: **40,000+** children in **2024-25**.

nindian-society-40-12.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the POCSO Act, 2012?
o: It excludes stringent punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault.
It includes capital punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault.
It provides for child-friendly special courts.
nindian-society-40-12.x: POCSO (amended 2019) has stringent punishment, including death, for aggravated penetrative sexual assault; it also has special courts and mandatory reporting.
n: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act was passed in 2012. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act was amended in 2019. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act prescribes stringent punishments. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act provides capital punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act provides child-friendly special courts. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act mandates reporting. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
xa: 2019: penetrative assault minimum **10** years; aggravated minimum **20** years.
POCSO is **gender-neutral**; it came into force **November 14, 2012**.
Non-reporting: up to **6 months** and/or fine.

nindian-society-49-6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the RTE Act?
o: It enforces Article 21A for children aged 6–14.
It came into force on 1 April 2010.
It mandates a 25% quota in private unaided schools for disadvantaged groups.
It mandates a 20% quota in private unaided schools for disadvantaged groups.
nindian-society-49-6.x: The RTE Act reserves 25%, not 20%, of seats in private unaided schools for disadvantaged children; it came into force on 1 April 2010.
n: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act came into force on April 1, 2010. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 101-102]
The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act enforces Article 21A for children aged 6–14 years. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 101-102]
The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act mandates a 25% quota in private unaided schools for disadvantaged groups. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 101-102]
xa: It aims at **universal elementary education**.
It **protects minority educational rights** under **Article 30**.
⚠ Child = below **18** (POCSO) vs below **14** (child labour) vs **6-14** (RTE).

nindian-society-40-38.s: Which of the following is a legal provision of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012?
o: Internal Complaints Committees in workplaces with 10 or more employees
Mandatory crèche facility in establishments with 50 or more employees
nindian-society-40-38.x: POCSO makes reporting of child sexual offences mandatory. Maintenance Tribunals belong to the Senior Citizens Act, ICCs to POSH, and crèches to the Maternity Benefit amendment.
nindian-society-40-38.tq: Match each provision to its Act.
n: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act was passed in 2012. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act mandates reporting. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The POSH Act mandates Internal Complaints Committees in workplaces with at least 10 employees. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act was passed in 2017. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act mandates a crèche facility for establishments with at least 50 employees. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act was passed in 2007. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act establishes Maintenance Tribunals. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
xs: **Mandatory reporting** of offences is a POCSO provision — option **(1)**.
Under **Section 19**, anyone who knows of an offence must report it; failure invites up to **6 months** and/or fine.
xa: **Burden of proof** lies on the accused (**Sec. 29-30**).
**False complaints** are punishable (**Sec. 22**), except good-faith ones.
The child's statement is recorded preferably by a **woman police officer**, **not in uniform**.

n6aeb293365d.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position of a child below 14 years after the 2016 amendment?
o: Employment is banned in all occupations and processes, subject to specified exceptions
Employment is banned only in mines and factories
Employment is permitted in all non-hazardous occupations without restriction
Employment is regulated only through the Right to Education Act
n6aeb293365d.x: After the 2016 amendment, employment of children below 14 years is prohibited in all occupations and processes, subject to specified exceptions.
n6aeb293365d.tq: Separate the post-amendment blanket prohibition from the earlier listed-work model.
xs: After **2016**, a child below **14** is **banned in all occupations and processes**, subject to exceptions — option **(1)** is correct.
The ban is linked to the **RTE** age.
xa: Exceptions: helping **family/family enterprise after school hours**; child **artist** in audio-visual entertainment (not circus).
**Adolescents** (**14-18**) are banned only from **hazardous** work.
⚠ 1986 = only **18** occupations, **65** processes banned.

n9cffc1dd8aa.s: The original 1986 law prohibited children below 14 years from employment in how many occupations and processes, respectively?
n9cffc1dd8aa.x: The original law listed 18 prohibited occupations and 65 prohibited processes for children below 14 years.
n9cffc1dd8aa.tq: Match the two numerical components without reversing their order.
xs: The **1986** Act banned children from **18 occupations and 65 processes** — option **(1)** is correct.
Other work was merely **regulated**, which clashed with the **RTE Act 2009**.
xa: ⚠ **83** was the number of entries in the earlier hazardous list, trimmed in **2016**.
Under the 1986 Act a child = one who has not completed **14 years**.
The **1986** year was asked in APPSC **2019**.

n767e2d911fc.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016?
o: A child may help the family or family enterprise after school hours
Offences under the Act are cognizable
The child-artist exception applies only if schooling is not affected
A child may work as an artist in audio-visual entertainment, including circus
n767e2d911fc.x: The audio-visual entertainment exception for child artists excludes circus.
xa: Child below **14**: banned in **all** occupations; adolescent **14-18**: banned in **hazardous** work only.
Penalty: **6 months-2 years** and/or **₹20,000-50,000**.
Fund: **Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund**.

n7095db75872.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about enforcement under the amended child labour law?
o: Imprisonment may range from six months to two years
Offences under the Act are non-cognizable
The fine may range from ₹20,000 to ₹50,000
A Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund is established under the Act
n7095db75872.x: The amendment made offences under the Act cognizable, not non-cognizable.
xa: Enforcement: **District Magistrate**.
Rules: **Amendment Rules 2017** notified by **MoLE**.
⚠ M.C. Mehta (**1996**): employer pays **₹20,000 per child** into a rehabilitation-cum-welfare fund.

n45610f1a067.s: The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016 introduced the category of 'adolescent'. Which of the following correctly describes it?
o: Persons aged 14-18, barred only from hazardous occupations and processes
Persons aged 14-18, barred from all occupations and processes
Persons aged 12-16, barred only from hazardous occupations
Persons aged 16-21, allowed in all occupations with parental consent
n45610f1a067.x: The 2016 amendment created the adolescent category (14-18), banned only from hazardous occupations and processes; children below 14 are banned from all occupations. Option B applies the child rule to adolescents, and C and D give wrong age bands.
n45610f1a067.tq: Below 14: total ban; 14-18 adolescents: hazardous ban only (2016).
xs: **Adolescents** are aged **14-18** and barred only from **hazardous occupations and processes** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) applies the **child** rule (below **14**, all work banned) to adolescents.
Options (3) and (4) give wrong age bands.
xa: The adolescent category came only in **2016**.
Hazardous list: **mines**, **inflammable substances/explosives**, **hazardous processes**.
**Mines Act 1952** bars anyone below **18**.

nindian-society-43-18.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Gurupadaswamy Committee?
o: It was associated with the Ministry of Labour.
Its recommendations led to the 1986 Child Labour Act.
It recognised that child labour is tied to poverty.
It recommended regulating hazardous child labour and banning all other forms.
nindian-society-43-18.x: The Committee recommended banning hazardous child labour and regulating other forms, the reverse of the statement; that approach led to the 1986 Act.
n: The nodal ministry for the Gurupadaswamy Committee was the Ministry of Labour. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Gurupadaswamy Committee recognized that child labour is directly tied to poverty. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Gurupadaswamy Committee recommended banning hazardous child labour. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Gurupadaswamy Committee recommended regulating other forms of child labour. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The dual approach recommended by the Gurupadaswamy Committee led to the 1986 Child Labour Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
xa: The 1986 Act banned only listed hazardous work (**18 occupations, 65 processes**).
The **2016** amendment banned all work below **14**.

n3fb619da0e0.s: After the IPC was replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita from 1 July 2024, the POCSO Act:
o: Was subsumed entirely into the BNS
Was merged with the Juvenile Justice Act
Continues as a separate special law
n3fb619da0e0.x: The IPC was replaced by the BNS from 1 July 2024, but POCSO continues as a separate special law.
xa: **BNS (Sec. 63)** keeps the age of consent at **18**.
Trafficking is now **Section 143, BNS 2023**.
POCSO was drafted by the **MWCD** and came into force on **14 November 2012**.

n82d7f214977.s: The Age of Consent Act, 1891 fixed the age of consent at:
n82d7f214977.x: The IPC 1860 fixed 10 years, the Age of Consent Act 1891 raised it to 12, the 1925 IPC amendment to 14, and POCSO 2012 to 18.
xa: The age was raised to **16** in **1949**.
**CLA 2013** also kept **18**; **BNS (Sec. 63)** keeps **18**.
⚠ Marriage age is distinct: **18** for women, **21** for men.

nf331d776072.s: According to Census 2011, the number of child labourers in the 5–14 age group in India was approximately:
nf331d776072.x: Census 2011 recorded approximately 10.1 million child labourers aged 5–14. The 4.35 million figure refers only to main workers.
nf331d776072.tq: Separate the overall count from the narrower main-worker figure.
xs: **Census 2011**: about **10.1 million** child labourers aged **5-14** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **4.35 million** counts **main workers only**; **8 M** is the rural share.
xa: Split: **5.6 M boys**, **4.5 M girls**; about **8 M** rural, **2 M** urban — urban child labour is rising.
Decline **2001-2011**: only **2.2% a year** (CRY).
Global: **137.6 million** in **2024** (**54 M** in hazardous work).

n708c162db01.s: The POCSO e-Box was launched in 2016 by the:
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
State Commission for Protection of Child Rights alone
Ministry of Home Affairs’ Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre
n708c162db01.x: The POCSO e-Box was launched in 2016 by the NCPCR for online complaints of child sexual abuse.
n708c162db01.tq: Apply the ‘who launched it?’ test to distinguish the NCPCR from cybercrime authorities.
xs: The **POCSO e-Box** was launched in **2016** by the **National Commission for Protection of Child Rights** (NCPCR) — option **(2)** is correct.
It takes **online complaints** of child sexual abuse.
xa: **NCPCR** is statutory, set up in **2007** under the **CPCR Act 2005**.
NCPCR monitors **POCSO**, the **JJ Act** and the **RTE Act**.
⚠ **cybercrime.gov.in** is run under **I4C, MHA** — not the e-Box.

n6aaf2e045b3.s: The National Child Labour Project was started in:
n6aaf2e045b3.x: The National Child Labour Project was started in 1988.
n6aaf2e045b3.tq: Distinguish the NCLP’s start year from the years of the Gurupadswamy Committee and National Policy on Child Labour.
xs: The **National Child Labour Project** started in **1988** — option **(3)** is correct.
**1979** = Gurupadswamy Committee; **1987** = National Policy on Child Labour; **1992** = India acceded to the UNCRC.
xa: NCLP is under **MoLE**, not MoSJE (UPSC **2007** key).
**Special Training Centres** serve rescued children aged **9-14** with bridge education, vocational training, mid-day meal and stipend.
NCLP was **merged into Samagra Shiksha** from **2021-22**.

nindian-society-38-2.s: Which system provides a confidential, direct digital reporting window for children and guardians to report online and physical sexual abuse?
nindian-society-38-2.x: The POCSO e-Box (NCPCR) lets children and guardians report sexual abuse, online or offline, directly and in confidence.
nindian-society-38-2.tq: Match each portal to its issue.
n: POCSO E-Box addresses child abuse, including sexual and cyber abuse. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
POCSO E-Box provides a confidential digital reporting window. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
POCSO E-Box provides a direct digital reporting window. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
POCSO E-Box enables children to report abuse. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
POCSO E-Box enables guardians to report abuse. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
POCSO E-Box enables reporting of online sexual abuse. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
POCSO E-Box enables reporting of physical sexual abuse. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
xs: The **POCSO E-Box** is a **confidential**, **direct digital reporting window** for children and guardians to report **online and physical sexual abuse** — option **(4)**.
It is associated with **MoWCD** and the **NCPCR**, launched in **2016**.
xa: Cyber abuse can also be reported on **cybercrime.gov.in** (**I4C**, MHA).
⚠ **POCSO e-Box** = NCPCR (**2016**); **PENCiL** = MoLE (**2017**).
**Operation Smile / Muskaan** (**2015**) trace and rescue missing children.

nab0a14de72b.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of forms of social child abuse?
o: Infanticide, child marriage, child prostitution and beggary
Verbal battering, educational neglect and fostering delinquency
Drug abuse, stealing, school dropout and trauma
Beating, burning, medical neglect and nutritional neglect
nab0a14de72b.x: Infanticide, child marriage, child prostitution and beggary are identified as forms of social abuse.
nab0a14de72b.tq: Classify all items in a group and eliminate groups containing consequences or other abuse categories.
xs: **Infanticide, child marriage, child prostitution and beggary** are all forms of **social** abuse — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) lists **emotional/non-physical** abuse; option (4) lists **physical** abuse (commission and omission).
Option (3) lists **consequences** of abuse — deviant behaviour, school dropout and trauma — not forms of abuse.
xa: **Sexual abuse (CSA)** = using a child for sexual stimulation.
**IT Rules 2021** require large platforms to detect **CSAM** automatically.
Sectors of child labour: **brick kilns**, pesticide-heavy farm work, toxic chemicals, **tea stalls**, begging.

ncd7d13d15b8.s: Which of the following is a cause of child abuse rather than a consequence?
ncd7d13d15b8.x: Parental alcoholism is listed as a cause. Loss of self-esteem, trauma and school dropout are consequences.
ncd7d13d15b8.tq: Separate the causes column from the consequences column before selecting the answer.
xs: **Parental alcoholism** is a **cause** of child abuse — option **(2)** is correct.
**School dropout**, **trauma** and **loss of self-esteem** are listed as **consequences** of abuse.
xa: Other causes: **poverty**, **family breakdown**, conflict between parents, lack of affectionate relationships, gaps in institutional care.
Other consequences: **deviant behaviour** (drug abuse, stealing), **delinquency**, interpersonal problems and **revictimisation**.

nef7db52f5e7.s: Which of the following is NOT an offence specifically identified under the POCSO Act?
o: Child marriage as an independent POCSO offence
nef7db52f5e7.x: POCSO identifies penetrative and non-penetrative sexual assault, aggravated forms, sexual harassment and child pornography. Child marriage is not listed as an independent POCSO offence in this classification.
nef7db52f5e7.tq: Find the item outside the statutory list of offences.
xs: **Child marriage** is not an independent POCSO offence — option **(4)** is correct.
POCSO offences: **penetrative** and **non-penetrative** assault, aggravated forms, **sexual harassment** and **child pornography**.
xa: Child marriage is a form of **social** abuse in the notes.
NFHS-5: over **27%** of women aged **20-24** married before **18**.
**2019**: child pornography defined; fine at least **Rs 5,000** for storing it.

nb1303ffaea7.s: With reference to the directions issued in M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu, which one of the following is correct?
o: The offending employer pays ₹20,000 per child into a Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund
The offending employer pays ₹5,000 per child directly to the child as compensation
The State pays ₹20,000 per child to the employer for rehabilitation
The family pays ₹20,000 per child into a welfare fund
nb1303ffaea7.x: The employer was directed to deposit ₹20,000 for each child into the Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund.
nb1303ffaea7.tq: Match the amount with the authority responsible for making the payment.
xs: The **employer** pays **₹20,000 per child** into a **Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund** — option **(1)** is correct.
**₹5,000** per child is paid by the **State** (if it cannot give an adult a job), not by the employer to the child.
xa: The **State** gives a job to an adult of the family, or pays **₹5,000** per child.
The child gets **education**.
UPPSC **2003** key "All of the above": the **Constitution**, the SC judgment of **10 Dec 1996** and the **UN Charter**.

n542cfd68289.x: ILO Convention No. 182 deals with the Worst Forms of Child Labour; Convention No. 138 deals with the Minimum Age for Employment.
xa: India ratified both in **2017**, to back "No Child Labour".
⚠ **138** = minimum age; **182** = worst forms.
**World Day Against Child Labour**: **12 June**.

nindian-society-43-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Jaya Jaitly Task Force?
o: It linked its recommendation with lowering MMR and IMR.
It recommended raising women's minimum marriage age from 18 to 20 years.
It recommended raising women's minimum marriage age from 18 to 21 years.
nindian-society-43-2.x: The Task Force recommended raising women's minimum marriage age from 18 to 21, not 20, to bring down MMR and IMR.
n: The Jaya Jaitly Task Force was constituted in 2020. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Jaya Jaitly Task Force recommended raising the legal minimum age of marriage for women from 18 to 21 years. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Jaya Jaitly Task Force aimed to lower MMR and IMR by raising the legal minimum age of marriage for women. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
xa: **Pam Rajput Committee** (**2015**): **50% reservation** for women in local bodies.
**Gurupadaswamy Committee** (**1979**): child labour.

nindian-society-46-5.s: Which judgement banned child labour in hazardous industries and mandated a Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund?
o: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
Independent Thought v. Union of India
nindian-society-46-5.x: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996) banned child labour in hazardous industries and ordered a Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund. Bachpan Bachao Andolan (2011) was about trafficking and child begging.
n: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu was decided in 1996. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu banned child labour in hazardous industries. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu mandated the establishment of a Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
xs: **M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu** (**1996**) **banned child labour in hazardous industries** and **mandated** a **Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund** — option **(1)**.
**Bachpan Bachao Andolan** (**2011**) dealt with **trafficking**, **child begging** and circus labour.
**Independent Thought** (**2017**) struck down the **marital rape exception** for minor wives.
xa: Employers pay **₹20,000 per child** into the fund.
The State gives a job to an adult of the family or pays **₹5,000** per child.
Judgment of **10 Dec 1996** concerned **Sivakasi** units.

nindian-society-46-11.s: Which judgement struck down the marital-rape exception in IPC Section 375 for wives below 18?
o: Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
Independent Thought v. Union of India
Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu
nindian-society-46-11.x: Independent Thought (2017) struck down the exception, holding sex with a girl under 18 is statutory rape even within marriage.
n: Independent Thought v. Union of India was decided in 2017. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Independent Thought v. Union of India struck down the marital rape exception for minor wives under Section 375 of the IPC. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Independent Thought v. Union of India held that intercourse with a girl below 18 is statutory rape regardless of marriage. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
xa: **POCSO** sets the age of consent at **18**; **BNS (Sec. 63)** keeps 18.

na334700d06b.s: Online child sexual abuse material (CSAM) in India is chiefly dealt with under which law, and which rules require large platforms to detect it automatically?
na334700d06b.x: CSAM (over 4.5 lakh cases reported in 2023) is dealt with under the IT Act 2000, and the IT Rules 2021 require large platforms to detect CSAM automatically. The other pairs name child-related laws that are not the stated basis for online CSAM detection.
na334700d06b.tq: CSAM: IT Act 2000 + IT Rules 2021 (automatic detection).
xs: Online **CSAM** is dealt with under the **IT Act 2000**, and the **IT Rules 2021** make large platforms detect it automatically — option **(1)** is correct.
POCSO, DPDP and JJ laws are child-related, but the notes do not name them as the basis for online CSAM detection.
xa: Over **4.5 lakh** CSAM cases were reported in India in **2023**.
CSAM and other online abuse can be reported on **cybercrime.gov.in** (**I4C, MHA**).
⚠ The **DPDP Act 2023** (**Sec. 9**) requires verifiable parental consent for anyone below **18** — a data-protection rule, not CSAM detection.

nca37fe44bb3.s: What percentage of child sexual-abuse offenders were reported to be known to the child according to NCRB 2021 data?
nca37fe44bb3.x: NCRB 2021 data reported that 97.1% of child sexual-abuse offenders were known to the child.
nca37fe44bb3.tq: Use the precise percentage and distinguish it from the broader finding on abusers in positions of trust.
xs: **97.1%** of child sexual-abuse offenders were known to the child (**NCRB 2021**) — option **(3)** is correct.
The other figures do not appear in the NCRB data in the notes.
xa: ⚠ Do not confuse with the MWCD **2007** study: **over 50%** of abusers known to the child or in a position of trust.
NCRB 2024: crimes against children rose about **6%**; **kidnapping and abduction** the largest category.
MWCD 2007: **53.22%** of children reported one or more forms of sexual abuse.

n4e24bbf93fa.s: Which additional conduct was specifically addressed by the 2019 amendment to the POCSO Act?
o: Failure to attend school up to 14 years
Employing a child in all forms of domestic work
Giving chemicals to hasten sexual maturity
Permitting marriage below the statutory age
n4e24bbf93fa.x: The 2019 amendment introduced punishment for giving chemicals to a child to hasten sexual maturity.
n4e24bbf93fa.tq: Identify the specific conduct added by the amendment instead of a related child-protection offence.
xs: The **2019** amendment punishes **giving chemicals to hasten sexual maturity** — option **(3)** is correct.
School attendance, domestic work and marriage age are not part of the 2019 POCSO changes in the notes.
xa: 2019: penetrative assault minimum **10 years**; aggravated minimum **20 years**; up to **life or death penalty**.
2019: **child pornography** defined; storing it without deleting/reporting = fine at least **Rs 5,000**, repeat **Rs 10,000**.
**POCSO Rules 2020** replaced the 2012 Rules.

n1cae43b54fd.s: The abolition of bonded labour is specifically associated with which law?
n1cae43b54fd.x: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976 outlawed bonded labour.
n1cae43b54fd.tq: Match the social evil with the legislation that abolished it.
xs: Bonded labour was outlawed by the **Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **Mines Act 1952** bars anyone below **18** from mines; the **Factories Act 1948** bars children below **14**.
The **JJ Act 2015** deals with children in conflict with law and children needing care.
xa: Debt bondage drives child labour in **farms**, **brick kilns** and **domestic work**.
It runs **across generations**.
Under the **JJ Act 2015**, working children are **children needing care and protection**.

n9669fb4c7cf.s: Which of the following correctly states the age limits under the Factories Act, 1948 and the Mines Act, 1952?
o: Factories Act: below 14 prohibited; Mines Act: below 16 prohibited
Factories Act: below 18 prohibited; Mines Act: below 14 prohibited
Factories Act: below 14 prohibited; Mines Act: below 18 prohibited
Factories Act: below 16 prohibited; Mines Act: below 18 prohibited
n9669fb4c7cf.x: The Factories Act, 1948 prohibits employment of children below 14, while the Mines Act, 1952 prohibits anyone below 18 from working in mines.
n9669fb4c7cf.tq: Compare the two age thresholds without interchanging the Acts.
xs: **Factories Act**: below **14** prohibited; **Mines Act**: below **18** prohibited — option **(3)** is correct.
The Factories Act is of **1948**, the Mines Act of **1952**.
xa: ⚠ Factories Act = below **14**; Mines Act = below **18**.
**2016**: **mines** stay on the hazardous list for adolescents.
The **1986** Act defined a child as one who has not completed **14 years**.

n3fc46134e16.s: The World Day Against Child Labour is observed on:
n3fc46134e16.x: The World Day Against Child Labour is observed on 12 June.
n3fc46134e16.tq: Recall the specific international observance date.
xs: The **World Day Against Child Labour** is on **12 June** — option **(4)** is correct.
The notes give no other date for this day; the other options are not linked to child labour in the notes.
xa: **ILO 138** = minimum age; **ILO 182** = worst forms of child labour; India ratified both in **2017**.
Global child labour: **137.6 million** in **2024** (**54 M** in hazardous work).
⚠ **10 Dec 1996** is the date of the M.C. Mehta (Sivakasi) judgment.

n8af051d6eda.s: Operation Chinnari-Thalli, launched by the Andhra Pradesh Police in February 2026, primarily targets which of the following?
n8af051d6eda.x: Operation Chinnari-Thalli was launched by the Andhra Pradesh Police in February 2026 to target sexual offences against children.
n8af051d6eda.tq: Identify the programme from its stated objective and implementing agency.
xs: **Operation Chinnari-Thalli** (AP Police, Feb **2026**) targets **sexual offences against children** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **Operation Muskaan** is the rescue of children from urban hubs, not sexual offences.
xa: It keeps **Sexual Offender Sheets**.
Aim: **zero pendency** in POCSO cases; chargesheets within **60 days**.
"Good touch-bad touch" awareness by the **Women & Child Safety Wing**.

nindian-society-38-7.s: PENCIL is an inter-agency tracking mechanism for:
nindian-society-38-7.x: PENCIL tracks child labour cases by linking Child Labour Committees, police and NGOs for rescue and rehabilitation.
n: PENCIL Portal is an inter-agency tracking mechanism. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
PENCIL Portal links Child Labour Committees. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
PENCIL Portal links the police. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
PENCIL Portal links NGOs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
PENCIL Portal supports rescue of children affected by child labour. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
PENCIL Portal supports rehabilitation of children affected by child labour. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
xa: PENCIL is run by **Labour and Employment**, launched **26 Sep 2017**.
Components: **Child Tracking System**, **Complaint Corner**, **State Government**, **NCLP**, **Convergence**.
**NCLP** (**1988**) merged into **Samagra Shiksha** from **2021-22**.

nd54458f5c4f.s: The principal beneficiaries of ICDS are:
o: Children aged 6–14 years and pregnant women
Children aged six months to six years, pregnant women and lactating mothers
Pregnant women and lactating mothers only
nd54458f5c4f.x: ICDS primarily covers children from six months to six years, pregnant women and lactating mothers.
xa: **Adolescent girls** were added via the **Scheme for Adolescent Girls**, now inside **Poshan 2.0**.
⚠ School meals are under **PM POSHAN**, not ICDS.
**Palna** creches also cover children **6 months-6 years**.

n8f5123a4c73.s: Under ICDS, Supplementary Nutrition is delivered through the:
n8f5123a4c73.x: Supplementary Nutrition is delivered through the Anganwadi Centre, while immunisation, health check-up and referral go through the health system.
xa: Pre-school non-formal education and **nutrition and health education** are also at the Anganwadi Centre.
ICDS has **six services** in all.
Not ICDS services: **PMMVY** cash maternity benefit and **PM POSHAN** school meals.

n21a95604152.s: An Anganwadi Worker (AWW), an honorary worker who runs the Anganwadi Centre, is a functionary of which scheme?
n21a95604152.x: The Anganwadi Worker is the ICDS functionary who runs the Anganwadi Centre (APPSC-G2 2025 key). The ANM and ASHA belong to the health system (NHM), PM POSHAN is the school-meal scheme and Samagra Shiksha is the school-education scheme.
xs: The **Anganwadi Worker** is a functionary of **Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)** — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Trap: not **ANM/NHM** (APPSC-G2 **2025** key).
**PM POSHAN** is the school-meal scheme of the **Ministry of Education**.
xa: The AWW runs the Anganwadi Centre and is an **honorary worker**.
The **Anganwadi Helper** cooks and serves meals.
ICDS at 50: **1.4 million AWCs**; **101 million** on **Poshan Tracker**.

n323980c9d9c.s: ICDS is now run as Anganwadi Services under:
n323980c9d9c.x: ICDS, a centrally sponsored MWCD scheme implemented by States/UTs, now runs as Anganwadi Services under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0.
xa: Funding: general **60:40**; NE/Himalayan + J&K **90:10**; UTs without legislature **100%**.
Launched **2 October 1975**; universalised **2006**.
ICDS has **six** services.

n92f016c6303.s: Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi primarily seeks to:
o: Provide one hot cooked meal to children in Classes I–VIII
Provide cash maternity benefit to pregnant women
Bring early childhood care and education into Anganwadis through play-based pedagogy
Provide take-home ration to adolescent girls
n92f016c6303.x: Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi integrates ECCE into Anganwadis and promotes play-based pedagogy, effectively developing them as pre-schools.
xa: AP: **55,607** AWWs trained under it.
**ECCE (3-6 yrs)** is one of Poshan 2.0's three verticals.
**Article 45**: ECCE for children up to **6**.

na8bcc571344.s: The foundational stage under the National Education Policy, 2020 comprises which of the following?
o: Ages 3–6, excluding the first two years of school
Ages 3–8, including three years of Anganwadi/pre-school and Classes 1–2
na8bcc571344.x: The NEP 2020 foundational stage covers ages 3–8: three years of Anganwadi or preschool followed by Classes 1 and 2.
na8bcc571344.tq: Break a composite age band into its preschool and school components.
xs: The **NEP 2020** foundational stage = **ages 3-8**: **three years** of Anganwadi/pre-school + **Classes 1-2** — option **(4)** is correct.
Options (1), (2) and (3) give the wrong age band or leave out Classes 1-2.
xa: **Bal Vatika** has been brought under **PM POSHAN**.
National ECCE Policy: **2013**.
AP: **1,030** Hub Anganwadi Centres with **ITC** and **Pratham**.

n918d4bb4532.s: Janani Suraksha Yojana was launched in 2005 under which framework and ministry?
o: National Food Security Act and Ministry of Women and Child Development
Samarthya and Ministry of Women and Child Development
Mission Vatsalya and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
National Rural Health Mission and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
n918d4bb4532.x: JSY was launched in 2005 under the National Rural Health Mission and is administered by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. It is a 100% Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
n918d4bb4532.tq: Separate JSY’s ministry and framework from PMMVY’s institutional arrangement.
xs: **JSY** was launched in **2005** under the **National Rural Health Mission** and **MoHFW** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Samarthya** and **NFSA** are linked to **PMMVY** (MWCD); **Mission Vatsalya** is child protection.
JSY is **100% centrally sponsored**.
xa: JSY gives cash for **institutional delivery**: **₹1,400** rural, **₹1,000** urban.
**JSSK** (**2011**): no out-of-pocket cost for pregnant women and sick newborns.
**PMSMA** (**2016**): free antenatal check-up on the **9th of every month**.

ncbd19a43526.s: The legal basis cited for the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana is which provision?
o: Section 4 of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015
Section 4 of the National Food Security Act, 2013
ncbd19a43526.x: PMMVY has its legal basis in Section 4 of the National Food Security Act, 2013.
ncbd19a43526.tq: Distinguish a statutory basis from constitutional provisions and unrelated legislation.
xs: **PMMVY**'s legal basis is **Section 4** of the **National Food Security Act, 2013** (**Sec 4, NFSA 2013**) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Article 45** is about ECCE up to age **6**, not maternity benefit.
xa: PMMVY is the only cash maternity benefit written into the **NFSA**.
Launched **1 January 2017**; ministry **MWCD** (**Samarthya**).
Purpose: **wage-loss compensation**.

n0c2faaa9c4d.s: Palna, the National Creche Scheme, is intended for children in which age group?
n0c2faaa9c4d.x: Palna covers children from 6 months to 6 years. Its creches may function whether or not the mother is employed, and 17,000 Anganwadi-cum-Creches were targeted.
n0c2faaa9c4d.tq: Use the exact age range to distinguish Palna from preschool and school-age programmes.
xs: **Palna** covers children **6 months-6 years** — option **(3)** is correct.
**3-8** is the **NEP 2020** foundational stage.
xa: Target: **17,000 Anganwadi-cum-Creches**.
Open **whether or not the mother is employed**.
⚠ ICDS also covers children **6 months-6 years**.

n0124bddbdb9.s: The Scheme for Adolescent Girls under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 covers which group?
o: Girls aged 14-18 years in Aspirational Districts and the North-Eastern Region
All boys and girls aged 6-14 years
Girls aged 10-14 years in all districts
Girls aged 15-19 years only in urban areas
n0124bddbdb9.x: The Scheme for Adolescent Girls covers girls aged 14-18 years in Aspirational Districts and the North-Eastern Region.
n0124bddbdb9.tq: Check both the age band and the geographical qualification; changing either creates a false option.
xs: The **Scheme for Adolescent Girls** covers girls aged **14-18** in **Aspirational Districts and the NER** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is now merged into **Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0**.
xa: Poshan 2.0 also merges **Anganwadi Services (SNP)** and **Poshan Abhiyaan**.
Nutrition support is one of the **three verticals**, incl. adolescent girls.

ne73bdfe1d31.s: Which of the following was NOT merged into Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 (2021)?
ne73bdfe1d31.x: PM POSHAN is a separate school-meal scheme; Poshan 2.0 merged Anganwadi Services/SNP, POSHAN Abhiyaan and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls.
xa: ⚠ PM POSHAN = **Ministry of Education**; ICDS/Poshan 2.0 = **MWCD**.
Adolescent girls covered: **14-18**, Aspirational Districts and NER.
Introduced in **2021**.

nc0a157f01ea.s: POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched on which occasion and at which place?
nc0a157f01ea.x: POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched on 8 March 2018 at Jhunjhunu in Rajasthan.
nc0a157f01ea.tq: Use the date-place combination to distinguish the launch from later campaign events.
xs: **POSHAN Abhiyaan** was launched on **8 March 2018** at **Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **BBBP** was launched at **Panipat** in **2015**; **Varanasi** hosted the **9th Poshan Maah** (**2026**).
xa: It was earlier called the **National Nutrition Mission**.
Goal: **Suposhit Bharat**, a **Jan Andolan**.
Mission goal: cut stunting to **25%** by **2022**.

na116c8774b1.s: The Mid-Day Meal Scheme was introduced on 15 August 1995 under which name?
o: National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education
na116c8774b1.x: The scheme was introduced on 15 August 1995 as the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education (NP-NSPE).
na116c8774b1.tq: Distinguish the original name from the later name PM POSHAN.
xs: The scheme began on **15 Aug 1995** as **NP-NSPE** — the **National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman** is the **2021** name (**PM POSHAN**).
xa: The mid-day meal was **first started in Tamil Nadu**.
Asked in APPSC **2025** (G2-GS 2025 key).
It is implemented under **NFSA 2013**.

na727be7e1ec.s: Tithi Bhojan, associated with community participation in PM POSHAN, was first introduced by which State?
na727be7e1ec.x: Tithi Bhojan, under which communities contribute meals on special occasions, was first introduced by Gujarat.
na727be7e1ec.tq: Test the origin State of a named community-participation practice.
xs: **Tithi Bhojan** was first introduced by **Gujarat** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ **Tamil Nadu** was where the **mid-day meal** first started.
xa: In Tithi Bhojan the **community contributes meals on special days**.
Other features: school nutrition gardens; **mandatory social audit** in every district.
AP runs the **Dokka Seethamma** Mid-Day Meal.

n3e07a357ede.s: The nodal ministry for PM POSHAN (the renamed Mid-Day Meal Scheme) is the:
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development
n3e07a357ede.x: PM POSHAN is run by the Ministry of Education (Department of School Education and Literacy); MWCD runs ICDS.
xa: National scheme began **15 Aug 1995** as **NP-NSPE**.
Sharing **60:40**.

nd0f1dbb0477.s: Which scheme is described as one of the world’s largest SHG-based rural livelihood programmes?
nd0f1dbb0477.x: DAY-NRLM, launched in 2011, is an SHG-based rural livelihoods programme described as one of the world’s largest.
nd0f1dbb0477.tq: Identify the scheme from its distinctive scale and SHG-based livelihood feature.
xs: **DAY-NRLM** (**2011**) is an SHG-based rural livelihood programme, **one of the world's largest** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Swadhar** gives shelter to women in difficult circumstances.
xa: Swadhar is now inside **Shakti Sadan**.
**Swavalambini** (**2022**): MSDE-NITI Aayog entrepreneurship programme for women students in the North-East.
PM Ujjwala: **10.57 crore+** connections.

n63341b6d2f4.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the six ICDS services?
n63341b6d2f4.x: Cash maternity benefit is provided under PMMVY, now associated with Mission Shakti, and is not one of the six ICDS services.
n63341b6d2f4.tq: Use the scheme-boundary test to distinguish ICDS services from a related maternity-benefit programme.
xs: **Cash maternity benefit** is not an ICDS service — option **(3)** is correct.
It is given under **PMMVY**, now under **Mission Shakti**.
**Pre-school non-formal education**, **referral services** and **nutrition and health education** are ICDS services.
xa: The six services: **SNP**, pre-school education, nutrition and health education, **immunisation**, health check-up, referral.
PMMVY: **₹5,000** for the first child; **₹6,000** if the second child is a girl.
PMMVY is the only cash maternity benefit written into the **NFSA**.

nd53b7e48c22.s: PM POSHAN is implemented as a rights-based Centrally Sponsored Scheme under which legislation?
nd53b7e48c22.x: PM POSHAN is a rights-based Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented under the National Food Security Act, 2013.
nd53b7e48c22.tq: Use the legal-basis trap by separating the governing legislation from related education and food institutions.
xs: PM POSHAN is implemented under the **National Food Security Act, 2013** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is a rights-based **centrally sponsored scheme**.
xa: Centre-State sharing **60:40**.
⚠ **PMMVY** also rests on **Sec 4, NFSA 2013**.

n16d5cd8645b.s: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) entitles pregnant women and sick newborns to:
o: A cash incentive for institutional delivery
Free delivery, drugs, diagnostics, blood, diet and transport
Rs 5,000 maternity benefit for the first child
A free antenatal check-up on the 9th of every month
n16d5cd8645b.x: JSSK, launched in 2011 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provides pregnant women and sick newborns free delivery, medicines, diagnostics, blood, diet and transport.
xa: **JSY** (**2005**) gives cash for institutional delivery: **₹1,400** rural, **₹1,000** urban.
**PMSMA** (**2016**): free antenatal check-up on the **9th of every month**.
**MAA** (**2016**): breastfeeding within one hour of birth.

n4feec05cda7.s: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan is associated with which of the following?
o: Promotion of breastfeeding within one hour of birth
Free treatment exclusively for sick newborns
Free antenatal check-up on the ninth of every month and identification of high-risk pregnancies
Cash assistance for institutional delivery at rural and urban rates
n4feec05cda7.x: PMSMA, launched in 2016 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provides free antenatal check-ups on the 9th of every month and helps identify high-risk pregnancies.
n4feec05cda7.tq: Use the fixed monthly date and service purpose as identifying clues.
xs: **PMSMA** gives a **free antenatal check-up on the 9th of every month** and spots **high-risk pregnancies** — option **(3)** is correct.
Breastfeeding is **MAA**; sick newborns are covered by **JSSK**; delivery cash is **JSY**.
xa: PMSMA was launched in **2016** under **MoHFW** (G2-GS **2022**).
**7.47 crore+** pregnant women examined at **22,349** facilities.
⚠ AP **ECCE day** is the **5th** of every month.

n3a04cf44138.s: Under PMMVY 2.0 (from April 2022), which of the following correctly describes the maternity benefit?
o: Rs 5,000 for the first child, and Rs 6,000 if the second child is a girl
Rs 5,000 in three instalments for the first two children irrespective of sex
Rs 6,000 for every live birth irrespective of birth order
Rs 1,400 for institutional delivery in rural areas
n3a04cf44138.x: PMMVY 2.0 gives Rs 5,000 for the first child and Rs 6,000 if the second child is a girl. Rs 5,000 in three instalments was the old PMMVY 1.0 design (a trap). It does not cover every birth. Rs 1,400 for rural institutional delivery is the JSY benefit.
xs: **PMMVY 2.0** gives **Rs 5,000 for the first child** and **Rs 6,000 if the second child is a girl** — option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **₹5,000 in 3 instalments** was the old **PMMVY 1.0** design.
**₹1,400** for rural institutional delivery is the **JSY** benefit.
xa: PMMVY 2.0 began in **April 2022**.
Helpline **1515**; tagline **"Matru Shakti Rashtra Shakti"**.
Legal basis: **Sec 4, NFSA 2013**.

n2972f8fcc88.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
o: It is primarily a behaviour-change campaign
It provides direct benefit transfers to every girl child
Funds for each district vary with its Sex Ratio at Birth
n2972f8fcc88.x: BBBP has no DBT component; it is a behaviour-change campaign with no asset creation.
xa: Aim: reverse falling **Child Sex Ratio**; secure the girl child's survival and education.
Girls' secondary GER **75.51% → 80.2%**.
BBBP runs under **Sambal** (Mission Shakti).

n0e70e855e9b.s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched at which place on 22 January 2015?
n0e70e855e9b.x: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched on 22 January 2015 at Panipat in Haryana.
n0e70e855e9b.tq: Use the place-date pair to distinguish the scheme from other women-centric initiatives.
xs: BBBP was launched on **22 January 2015** at **Panipat, Haryana** — option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **Bengaluru** is the base of the **Akshaya Patra Foundation**.
xa: ⚠ POSHAN Abhiyaan = **Jhunjhunu 2018**; BBBP = **Panipat 2015**.
BBBP runs under **Sambal** (**Mission Shakti**).

nb80478e7544.s: A Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana account matures after:
nb80478e7544.x: SSY, under the Ministry of Finance, allows up to two girls per family, deposits of ₹250 to ₹1.5 lakh a year, and matures at 21 years.
xa: **4.53 crore+** accounts.
⚠ BBBP is a **behaviour-change** campaign under **MWCD**, not a savings scheme.

n0c7a69896c1.s: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, the minimum legal age for marriage is:
o: 21 years for both girls and boys
18 years for girls and 21 years for boys
18 years for girls and 18 years for boys
21 years for girls and 18 years for boys
n0c7a69896c1.x: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 prescribes 18 years for girls and 21 years for boys.
n0c7a69896c1.tq: Directly discriminate between the two age thresholds in a commonly confused pair.
xs: Under **PCMA 2006** the minimum age is **18 years for girls and 21 years for boys** — option **(2)** is correct.
The other options swap or equalise the ages; raising women's age to **21** was only proposed in a Bill.
xa: The **Amendment Bill 2021** sought to raise women's age to **21**; it lapsed with the **17th Lok Sabha**.
A child marriage is **voidable** at the option of the minor party.
The **Allahabad HC (1 Jul 2026)** held the age limits apply to all citizens irrespective of religion.

n3a633e4de0c.s: An adult male who contracts, conducts or promotes a child marriage under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 may be punished with:
o: Rigorous imprisonment up to two years and fine up to Rs. 1 lakh
Fine up to Rs. 10 lakh only
Simple imprisonment up to five years without fine
Imprisonment up to one year and fine up to Rs. 50,000
n3a633e4de0c.x: The punishment may extend to two years of rigorous imprisonment and a fine up to Rs. 1 lakh.
n3a633e4de0c.tq: Retain both components of the penalty instead of selecting a partially correct punishment.
xs: The punishment is up to **2 years RI + fine up to Rs 1 lakh** — option **(1)** is correct.
It applies to an **adult male** who contracts, conducts or promotes a child marriage.
xa: **Child Marriage Prohibition Officers** are appointed by **State Governments**.
Minimum age: **18** (girls) / **21** (boys).
**'100-Day Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat'** campaign launched by **MWCD** in **December 2025**.

n94107935f69.s: The Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 2021 proposed to raise the minimum marriageable age of women to 21 years. What happened to the Bill?
o: It was withdrawn after being passed by both Houses.
It was rejected by the Supreme Court.
It was enacted as an Act in 2022.
It was referred to a Standing Committee and lapsed with the 17th Lok Sabha.
n94107935f69.x: The Bill was sent to a Standing Committee and subsequently lapsed with the 17th Lok Sabha.
n94107935f69.tq: Track the legislative stage and final status rather than only the proposed reform.
xs: The **Amendment Bill 2021** was sent to a **standing committee** and **lapsed with the 17th Lok Sabha** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was never passed or enacted.
xa: It sought to raise women's marriage age to **21**.
Present law: **18** for girls, **21** for boys.
NFHS-5: **23.3%** of women aged **20-24** married before **18**.

n612e462fdc2.s: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, the legal status of a child marriage is that it is:
o: Void ab initio in all cases
Voidable at the option of the party who was a minor at the time of marriage
Voidable only at the option of the State Government
n612e462fdc2.x: Under PCMA 2006 a child marriage is voidable at the option of the minor party, not automatically void. It is not fully valid and unchallengeable, and the option lies with the minor party, not the State Government.
n612e462fdc2.tq: Child marriage = voidable at minor party's option.
xs: A child marriage is **voidable at the option of the minor party** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is not void in all cases, not fully valid, and the option is not the State Government's.
xa: Minimum age: **18** (girls) / **21** (boys).
Punishment: up to **2 years RI** + fine up to **Rs 1 lakh**.
**Child Marriage Prohibition Officers** are appointed by **State Governments**.

n0f5bcd76b95.s: The ALIVA model to end child marriage originated in which district of Odisha?
n0f5bcd76b95.x: ALIVA originated in Nayagarh district, Odisha, not Ganjam.
xa: Highest: **West Bengal**, **Bihar**, **Tripura**.
The **Amendment Bill 2021** lapsed with the **17th Lok Sabha**.

n2ed066b4994.s: On 1 July 2026, the Allahabad High Court held that the age limits under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act apply:
o: Only to persons not governed by personal laws
To all citizens irrespective of religion
Only to residents of Uttar Pradesh
n2ed066b4994.x: The Allahabad High Court held that the PCMA age limits apply to all citizens irrespective of religion.
xa: A child marriage is **voidable** at the minor party's option.
Punishment: up to **2 years RI** + fine up to **Rs 1 lakh**.

nb16e15d0450.s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) is presently implemented under which component of Mission Shakti?
nb16e15d0450.x: BBBP is implemented under Sambal, the safety component of Mission Shakti.
nb16e15d0450.tq: Identify the correct umbrella mission by matching the scheme with its present administrative component.
xs: **BBBP** now runs under **Sambal** of **Mission Shakti** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Samarthya** houses **PMMVY**; **Mission Vatsalya** is child protection; **Poshan 2.0** is nutrition.
xa: BBBP was launched on **22 January 2015** at **Panipat**.
It has **100% central funding** and covers **all districts**.
Nodal ministry: **MWCD**, with Health and Education.

n49c094f5f01.s: CHILDLINE 1098 has been integrated with ERSS-112 in 36 States and Union Territories under
n49c094f5f01.x: Under Mission Vatsalya, CHILDLINE 1098 has been integrated with ERSS-112 in 36 States and Union Territories.
n49c094f5f01.tq: Match the helpline integration with the correct child-protection mission.
xs: **CHILDLINE 1098** is integrated with **ERSS-112** in **36 States/UTs** under **Mission Vatsalya** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Operation Muskaan** rescues children; **Samagra Shiksha** is school education.
xa: Mission Vatsalya outlay **Rs 10,916 crore** (Centre **Rs 6,928 crore**).
It keeps a **JJB and CWC in every district**.
Sponsorship/foster care: **Rs 4,000** per child per month.

n2e26dbf2811.s: Mission Vatsalya, introduced in 2021–22, subsumed the
n2e26dbf2811.x: Mission Vatsalya subsumed the Integrated Child Protection Scheme, or ICPS.
n2e26dbf2811.tq: Distinguish the child-protection scheme absorbed by Mission Vatsalya from education schemes.
xs: **Mission Vatsalya** (**2021-22**) subsumed **Child Protection Services/ICPS** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **NCLP** merged into **Samagra Shiksha**, not Mission Vatsalya.
xa: Ministry: **MWCD**; a **CSS**.
Objective: child protection + happy childhood aligned to **SDGs** (APPSC-G2 **2024**).
**CHILDLINE 1098** integrated with **ERSS-112**.

n0f564f25389.s: PM CARES for Children provides eligible COVID-19 orphaned children a corpus of ____ at the age of 23.
n0f564f25389.x: PM CARES for Children (2021), for children who lost parents or guardians to COVID-19, provides a corpus of Rs 10 lakh at 23 along with education and health support.
xa: Launched in **2021**.
Portal: **pmcaresforchildren.in**.
⚠ Mission Vatsalya aftercare runs to **21**, extendable to **23**.

n62f20f6fb7c.s: Under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Amendment Act, 2021, who has been made the focal point for adoption matters in a district?
n62f20f6fb7c.x: The JJ Amendment Act 2021 made the District Magistrate the focal point for adoption. The CWC is a statutory body for children in need of care, but not the designated focal point; the District Judge and SP are not given this role.
xs: The **JJ Amendment Act 2021** made the **District Magistrate** the focal point for adoption — option **(1)** is correct.
The **CWC** is the body for children needing care, not the adoption focal point.
xa: Mission Vatsalya keeps a **JJB and CWC in every district**.
CCI maintenance: **Rs 3,000** per month.
**Palna** targets **17,000** Anganwadi-cum-Creches.

n316c70a00bd.s: Swadhar, which provides shelter to women in difficult circumstances, is now part of:
n316c70a00bd.x: Swadhar now sits inside Shakti Sadan; Ujjawala deals with trafficking and PMUY (MoPNG) gives LPG connections.
xa: AP has **28 Shakti Sadans**.
PMUY subsidy: **₹300** per cylinder for up to **12** refills.
PMUY connections: **10.57 crore+**.

n7f378bab23d.s: Section 2(s) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, defines a person with disability as one having a long-term:
o: Physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairment which, in interaction with barriers, hinders full and effective participation
Sensory impairment certified exclusively by a Central institution
Physical impairment only, irrespective of social or environmental barriers
Temporary illness that prevents employment for more than six months
n7f378bab23d.x: Section 2(s) covers long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairment which, in interaction with barriers, hinders full participation in society.
n7f378bab23d.tq: Use the precise statutory wording and reject narrower or substituted definitions.
xs: **Section 2(s)**: a long-term **physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairment** which, **with barriers**, hinders full participation — option **(1)** is correct.
The definition is not limited to physical or sensory impairment and covers long-term, not temporary, conditions.
xa: **Benchmark disability** = at least **40%** of a specified disability.
**21** specified disabilities, e.g. **autism**, **acid attack victims**, **sickle cell disease**.
Monitoring: **Chief Commissioner for PwDs**, **Sec. 75(1)**.

nccc2d7d926d.s: The RPwD Act, 2016 increased the number of specified disabilities from 7 to:
nccc2d7d926d.x: The Act raised specified disabilities from 7 to 21, including autism, acid attack victims and sickle cell disease, and lets the Centre add more.
xa: ⚠ **Census 2027** categories are narrower than the Act's **21**.
Survivors of **forcible acid ingestion** are now recognised as acid attack victims (**5 May 2026**).
Benchmark disability: at least **40%**.

ndd5a7c830a0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016?
o: It increased specified disabilities from 7 to 21
Benchmark disability means at least 40% of a specified disability
Children with benchmark disabilities get free education from 6 to 18 years
It provides 5% reservation in government jobs and 4% in higher education seats
ndd5a7c830a0.x: The figures are reversed: the Act gives 4% reservation in government jobs and 5% in higher education.
xa: Allotment in land, housing, poverty-alleviation schemes: **5%**.
⚠ **4%** jobs vs **5%** higher education.
SC (Mar **2026**): **40%** is a **floor**, not a ceiling.

na40decbe20b.s: Survivors of forcible acid ingestion were recognised as acid attack victims under the RPwD Act after:
o: The adoption of the UNCRPD in 2006
The enactment of the National Trust Act in 1999
The ratification of the UNCRPD by India in 2007
na40decbe20b.x: After a Supreme Court interpretation in 2026, survivors of forcible acid ingestion were recognised as acid attack victims under the Act.
na40decbe20b.tq: Link the later judicial interpretation to the legal recognition it produced.
xs: Survivors of **forcible acid ingestion** were recognised as **acid attack victims** after a **Supreme Court interpretation** in **2026** (**5 May 2026**) — option **(1)** is correct.
The UNCRPD (**2006**/**2007**) and National Trust Act (**1999**) predate this ruling.
xa: **Acid attack victims** are among the RPwD Act's **21** specified disabilities.
**Census 2027** adds **acid attack**, neurological and blood disorders.
Groups say **autism and dwarfism** are left out of Census 2027.

n0d020df19e7.s: Which of the following bodies is a statutory authority under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, empowered to monitor implementation and take up complaints?
o: Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
n0d020df19e7.x: The Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities is the statutory authority under the RPwD Act, 2016, responsible for monitoring implementation and taking up complaints.
n0d020df19e7.tq: Identify the authority from its statutory monitoring and complaint-handling role.
xs: The **Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities** is the statutory authority under the **RPwD Act 2016** to monitor and take up complaints — option **(2)** is correct.
**NDFDC** gives loans; **RCI** regulates professionals' training; the **National Trust** serves specific disabilities.
xa: Monitoring section: **Sec. 75(1)**.
**State Commissioners for PwDs** do the same in each State.
SC directed **prison accessibility** per the RPwD Act (Dec **2025**).

n72c4c36fb20.s: SVNIRTAR, a national institute for persons with disabilities, is located at:
n72c4c36fb20.x: SVNIRTAR is at Cuttack; Dehradun hosts the visual-disability institute and NIEPID is at Secunderabad.
xa: **ABVT-CDS**, **Gwalior**: para-sports.
**ALIMCO** (CPSE, **1972**) makes aids and artificial limbs.
**Inclusive India** focuses on intellectual and developmental disabilities.

n22f98dbf74a.s: The Supreme Court recognised safe footpaths as a fundamental right under which Article, along with a minimum footpath width of 1.8 metres?
n22f98dbf74a.x: The Supreme Court recognised safe footpaths as part of the right to life under Article 21 and specified a minimum width of 1.8 metres.
n22f98dbf74a.tq: Link the judicially recognised right with the correct constitutional Article and measurement.
xs: The SC held safe **footpaths** are a fundamental right under **Article 21**, minimum width **1.8 m** — option **(1)** is correct.
Art. 21 is the right to life; the notes link no other Article to this ruling.
xa: SC also recognised **digital access** as part of **Art. 21**, citing the **UNCRPD**.
**Rajive Raturi v. UoI (2024)**: mandatory accessibility standards.
**Jeeja Ghosh v. UoI (2016)**: right to dignity; compensation.

nfb1de788fe8.s: Which of the following is NOT a service under Samagra Shiksha's inclusive education component for RPwD-listed disabilities?
nfb1de788fe8.x: Samagra Shiksha covers assessment, aids, assistive technology and therapy for children with disabilities, not exclusive education of gifted children.
xa: Samagra Shiksha covers **all RPwD-listed disabilities**.
It took over the old **IEDSS**.
AP: **Rs 3,500** per CwSN; **679 Bhavitha Centres**.

n45bd8af96b1.s: The Supreme Court directed that prison manuals be revised to ensure accessibility for prisoners with disabilities in line with:
o: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
The Rehabilitation Council of India Act, 1992
n45bd8af96b1.x: The Supreme Court directed prison accessibility and revision of prison manuals in accordance with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016.
xa: The direction came in Dec **2025**.
**Rajive Raturi (2024)**: mandatory accessibility standards.
SC recognised **digital access** under **Art. 21**.

n70f25489a74.s: The International Year of Disabled Persons was observed in:
n70f25489a74.x: The International Year of Disabled Persons was observed in 1981.
n70f25489a74.tq: Distinguish an international year from an annual observance or statutory enactment year.
xs: The UN's **International Year of Disabled Persons** was **1981** — option **(2)** is correct.
The other years are not linked to it in the notes.
xa: **International Day of Persons with Disabilities**: **3 December**.
⚠ **3 December** is also the launch day of the **Accessible India Campaign** (**2015**).
UNCRPD adopted **13 December 2006**.

ne5b39607a56.s: The Central Rehabilitation Register is maintained by the:
o: Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
ne5b39607a56.x: The Rehabilitation Council of India maintains the Central Rehabilitation Register; the National Trust covers autism, cerebral palsy and related conditions.
xa: The National Trust provides for **legal guardians**.
**Niramaya**: health insurance up to **Rs 1 lakh**/year.
**RCI Act, 1992** (statutory **1993**, amended **2000**).

nb1daec87cdf.s: Niramaya, a scheme of the National Trust, provides:
o: Five per cent reservation in higher education
Health insurance up to Rs. 1 lakh per year
nb1daec87cdf.x: Niramaya provides health insurance coverage of up to Rs. 1 lakh per year. Travel concessions and loans are associated with other initiatives or institutions.
nb1daec87cdf.tq: Link the scheme to its specific monetary entitlement rather than a general disability benefit.
xs: **Niramaya** gives **health insurance up to Rs 1 lakh per year** — option **(4)** is correct.
Concessional loans are **NDFDC**; free APSRTC travel is AP's **Divyang Shakti**; **5%** is the higher-education reservation.
xa: Niramaya is one of the **National Trust** schemes, with **Disha**, **Vikas**, **Samarth**, **Gharaunda**.
National Trust covers **autism, cerebral palsy, mental retardation and multiple disabilities**.
⚠ **ADIP** gives free aids and appliances.

n810de8f0522.s: The principal function of the Rehabilitation Council of India is to:
o: Provide legal guardianship under the National Trust Act
Monitor implementation of the RPwD Act through State Commissioners
Regulate the training of rehabilitation and special-education professionals and maintain the Central Rehabilitation Register
n810de8f0522.x: The Rehabilitation Council of India regulates training of rehabilitation and special-education professionals and maintains the Central Rehabilitation Register.
n810de8f0522.tq: Associate the professional regulator with training standards and the register it maintains.
xs: The **RCI** **regulates training of rehabilitation and special-education professionals** and keeps the **Central Rehabilitation Register** — option **(4)** is correct.
Loans = **NDFDC**; legal guardianship = **National Trust**; monitoring the RPwD Act = **Chief Commissioner** and **State Commissioners**.
xa: **RCI Act, 1992**; statutory **1993**; amended **2000** (APPSC **2018**).
⚠ The National Trust Act is of **1999**.
National Institutes: locomotor — **Kolkata**; visual — **Dehradun**.

n03c7f90595a.s: Divya Kala Shakti is best described as:
o: A health-insurance scheme of the National Trust
A cultural showcase of the artistic talent of persons with disabilities
A loan programme for self-employment of persons with disabilities
A programme for appointing legal guardians
n03c7f90595a.x: Divya Kala Shakti showcases the artistic talent of persons with disabilities and is associated with the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities.
n03c7f90595a.tq: Distinguish a cultural showcase from welfare, finance and guardianship programmes.
xs: **Divya Kala Shakti** is a **cultural showcase of the artistic talent of PwDs** — option **(2)** is correct.
Health insurance = **Niramaya**; loans = **NDFDC**; legal guardians = **National Trust**.
xa: It is run by the **Department of Empowerment of PwDs**.
⚠ **EKAM Fest** = entrepreneurship among Divyangjan.

n817dc774452.s: The Supreme Court’s recognition of digital access as part of Article 21 was made with reference to which international convention?
o: Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women
United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights
United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child
n817dc774452.x: The Supreme Court recognised digital access as part of Article 21 while citing the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.
n817dc774452.tq: Link the judicially recognised right with the specific international disability convention cited.
xs: The SC cited the **United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities** (UNCRPD) — option **(2)** is correct.
It recognised **digital access** as part of **Art. 21** (**2026**).
xa: UNCRPD adopted **13 December 2006**; India ratified **October 2007**.
India has **not ratified the Optional Protocol**.
**Sugamya Bharat** covers the **ICT** vertical.

nindian-society-42-19.s: Which committee drafted the initial replacement bill for the PwD Act, 1995, aligning India’s domestic legal architecture with the UNCRPD?
nindian-society-42-19.x: The Sudha Kaul Committee (2010) drafted the bill to replace the PwD Act, 1995, in line with the UN disability convention (UNCRPD). This led to the RPwD Act, 2016.
n: The Sudha Kaul Committee drafted the initial replacement bill for the PwD Act, 1995. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Sudha Kaul Committee aligned India’s domestic legal architecture with the UNCRPD. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Sudha Kaul Committee concerned Persons with Disabilities (PwD). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xs: The **Sudha Kaul Committee** drafted the **initial replacement bill** for the **PwD Act, 1995**, aligning Indian law with the **UNCRPD** — option **(3)**.
It was constituted in **2010** by the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment**.
Its work **culminated** in the **RPwD Act, 2016**.
xa: **UNCRPD** adopted **13 December 2006**; India ratified in **October 2007**.
India has **not ratified** the UNCRPD **Optional Protocol**.

nindian-society-7-6.s: Which ministry deals with persons with disabilities?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
nindian-society-7-6.x: Social Justice and Empowerment handles persons with disabilities, through its Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities.
nindian-society-7-6.tq: Match each group to its ministry.
n: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment deals with persons with disabilities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 28-30]
xs: **Persons with disabilities** are handled by **Social Justice and Empowerment** — option **(4)**.
It works through the **Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD)**.
xa: DEPwD runs the **UDID Portal**, **Sugamya Bharat App** and **PM-DAKSH Portal**.
The **Accessible India Campaign** (**2015**) is the DEPwD flagship.
**NDFDC** (MSJE) gives concessional loans to PwDs.

n41d34912ac2.s: 'Relief of the disabled and unemployable' is an entry in the:
n41d34912ac2.x: State List Entry 9 concerns relief of the disabled and unemployable; Article 41 covers public assistance in disablement.
xa: Proposal: **Minimum Universal Disability Pension Floor** under **Art. 41**.
Proposed national minimum disability pension: **Rs 8,000** a month.
AP disability pension raised to **Rs 6,000** a month.

n53f6ff8c7d1.s: The International Day of Persons with Disabilities is observed every year on:
n53f6ff8c7d1.x: 3 December is the International Day of Persons with Disabilities (the Accessible India Campaign was also launched on 3 December 2015). 1 October is the International Day of Older Persons, 10 December is Human Rights Day and 15 June is World Elder Abuse Awareness Day.
n53f6ff8c7d1.tq: 3 Dec = PwD Day; 1 Oct = Older Persons.
xs: The **International Day of Persons with Disabilities** is on **3 December** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **Accessible India Campaign** was also launched on **3 December 2015**.
xa: The **International Year of Disabled Persons** was **1981**.
UNCRPD adopted on **13 December 2006**.
⚠ **19 April 2017** is when the RPwD Act came into force.

n4b9fcda60cd.s: The Accessible India Campaign was launched on which date?
n4b9fcda60cd.x: The Accessible India Campaign was launched on 3 December 2015 as a flagship initiative for universal accessibility.
n4b9fcda60cd.tq: Use the exact launch date rather than confusing it with an observance date.
xs: The **Accessible India Campaign** was launched on **3 December 2015** — option **(3)** is correct.
3 December is also the **International Day of Persons with Disabilities**.
xa: It is the **DEPwD** flagship for **universal accessibility**.
Three verticals: **built environment, transport, ICT**.
**Sugamya Bharat App** crowdsources accessibility gaps.

n12845db9482.s: The Sugamya Bharat App is primarily a platform for which of the following?
o: Providing monthly pensions to persons with disabilities
n12845db9482.x: The Sugamya Bharat App functions as a crowdsourcing platform through which accessibility gaps can be reported.
n12845db9482.tq: Match the digital application with its operational function, not with another disability service.
xs: The **Sugamya Bharat App** is a **crowdsourcing** platform for **reporting accessibility gaps** — option **(4)** is correct.
Pensions = **IGNDPS**; professionals' register = **RCI**; disability certificates = **UDID**.
xa: Part of the **Accessible India Campaign** (**2015**).
Verticals: **built environment, transport, ICT**.
SC (**2026**) recognised **digital access** as part of **Art. 21**.

ne4ba7139b6a.s: The three verticals of the Accessible India Campaign are built environment, transport and:
ne4ba7139b6a.x: The verticals are built environment, transport and ICT; accessible booths and Braille-enabled EVMs are accessible-election measures, not a vertical.
xa: Accessible India Campaign launched **3 December 2015**.
