**Sugamya Bharat App** crowdsources gaps.
SC directed **prison accessibility** and revision of prison manuals (Dec **2025**).

n6bb33582ea6.s: Which scheme provides free aids and appliances to eligible persons below a monthly income of Rs 22,500 and subsidised assistance up to Rs 30,000?
n6bb33582ea6.x: The ADIP scheme provides free aids and appliances to persons below the stated income limit and subsidised assistance up to Rs 30,000.
n6bb33582ea6.tq: Match the income ceiling and assistance limit with the correct scheme.
xs: **ADIP** gives free aids and appliances below income **Rs 22,500/month** and subsidy up to **Rs 30,000** — option **(1)** is correct.
**SIPDA** = grants to implement the Act; **IGNDPS** = pension; **DDRS** = grants to NGOs.
xa: ADIP also covers **corrective surgery**.
Delivered through NIs, CRCs, **ALIMCO**, DDRCs.
⚠ **ADIP** = aids to individuals; **DDRS** = grants to NGOs; **EKAM** = entrepreneurship.

n93c312e274a.s: EKAM Fest is associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Providing free education to children with benchmark disabilities
Providing cultural training exclusively to government employees with disabilities
Promoting entrepreneurship among Divyangjan and creating awareness of the potential of persons with disabilities
n93c312e274a.x: EKAM stands for Entrepreneurship, Knowledge, Awareness and Marketing. It promotes entrepreneurship among Divyangjan and awareness of the potential of persons with disabilities; it is organised by NDFDC.
n93c312e274a.tq: Expand the acronym through the activity naturally associated with the event.
xs: **EKAM Fest** promotes **entrepreneurship among Divyangjan** and **awareness** of PwD potential — option **(4)** is correct.
The register is the **RCI**'s; free education for ages **6-18** is under the RPwD Act.
xa: EKAM = **Entrepreneurship, Knowledge, Awareness, Marketing** (APPSC **2018**).
It is organised by **NDFDC**.
⚠ **Divya Kala Shakti** is the cultural showcase.

nde98017442e.s: NHFDC, now known as the National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation, is primarily concerned with:
o: Legal guardianship for persons with multiple disabilities
Concessional loans for self-employment of persons with disabilities
nde98017442e.x: NHFDC, now NDFDC, provides concessional loans to persons with disabilities for self-employment. It functions under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities.
nde98017442e.tq: Identify the institution from its finance-related mandate and reject nearby welfare functions.
xs: **NHFDC**, now **NDFDC**, is the apex body for **concessional loans for self-employment** of PwDs — option **(3)** is correct.
Legal guardianship = **National Trust**; cultural showcase = **Divya Kala Shakti**.
xa: Loans up to **Rs 50 lakh** at **5-9%**; education loans at **4%**.
Eligibility: **40%+** disability, age **18+**.
Channels: **State Channelising Agencies**, PSBs, RRBs.

n6306e2e8ae6.s: UDID-based skilling and the Divyangjan Rozgar Setu for jobs are features of which portal introduced in 2023?
n6306e2e8ae6.x: The PM-DAKSH-DEPwD portal provides UDID-based skilling and the Divyangjan Rozgar Setu for employment opportunities.
xa: **UDID** is a single national disability card and certificate.
PM-DAKSH = skill training and job linkage for PwDs.
**NDFDC** gives concessional loans up to **Rs 50 lakh** for self-employment.

n0afb4ef7567.s: Which of the following correctly describes ALIMCO?
o: A statutory authority that monitors implementation of the RPwD Act
A National Trust scheme providing health insurance
A corporation that gives concessional loans for self-employment of Divyangjan
A Central Public Sector Enterprise set up in 1972 that makes aids and artificial limbs
n0afb4ef7567.x: ALIMCO is a Central Public Sector Enterprise established in 1972 that manufactures aids and artificial limbs; the other descriptions fit the Chief Commissioner, Niramaya and NDFDC.
xa: **ADIP** aids are delivered through NIs, CRCs, **ALIMCO** and DDRCs.
AP gave **52,263** assistive devices.
ADIP subsidy: up to **Rs 30,000**.

nindian-society-37-1.s: The UDID Portal (Swavlamban) is primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Centralized issuing of Unique Disability IDs and digital disability certificates
Online digital library for accessible books
Digital profiling of sewer and septic tank workers
Online registration for private residential schools
nindian-society-37-1.x: The UDID portal (Swavlamban), under DEPwD, issues Unique Disability IDs and digital disability certificates from one place, so benefits are easy to get.
nindian-society-37-1.tq: Match each portal to its function.
n: The UDID Portal is a digital platform for persons with disabilities (PwDs). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The UDID Portal is also known as Swavlamban. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The UDID Portal centralizes the issuance of Unique Disability IDs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The UDID Portal provides digital disability certificates. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The Sugamya Pustakalaya is an online digital library. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The NAMASTE Mobile App and Portal digitally profile sewer and septic-tank workers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The SHRESHTA Portal provides online computer-based test registration. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The SHRESHTA Portal covers private residential schools for SC students. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The UDID Portal enables seamless access to welfare services. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
xs: The **UDID Portal (Swavlamban)** centralizes issue of **Unique Disability IDs** and **digital disability certificates** — option **(1)**.
It is run by **DEPwD** under **Social Justice and Empowerment**.
An **online digital library** for accessible books is **Sugamya Pustakalaya**.
xa: UDID gives **seamless access** to welfare services.
**PRASHAST** screens schoolchildren for **21** disabilities.

n2efa2a0dd36.s: In March 2026, the Supreme Court held that the 40% threshold for benchmark disability is a:
o: Ceiling applicable only to Group A posts
Limit applicable only to locomotor disability
n2efa2a0dd36.x: The Court treated 40% as a floor, not a ceiling, with suitability judged by functional ability and reasonable accommodation.
xa: **Vikash Kumar v. UPSC (2021)**: scribe as reasonable accommodation even without benchmark disability.
Reservation in government jobs: **4%**.
SC (**2026**): safe **footpaths** are a fundamental right under **Art. 21**.

nindian-society-45-15.s: Which case held that the scribe facility cannot be restricted only to persons with benchmark disabilities?
o: Jeeja Ghosh v. Union of India
Disabled Rights Group v. Union of India
Rajive Raturi v. Union of India
nindian-society-45-15.x: Vikash Kumar v. UPSC (2021) treated reasonable accommodation as part of equality, so scribes cannot be limited to benchmark disabilities.
n: Vikash Kumar v. UPSC concerns Persons with Disabilities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 94-96]
Vikash Kumar v. UPSC was decided in 2021. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 94-96]
Vikash Kumar v. UPSC held that scribe facilities cannot be restricted only to persons with benchmark disabilities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 94-96]
Vikash Kumar v. UPSC recognized reasonable accommodation as an intrinsic component of equality. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 94-96]
xa: Benchmark disability = at least **40%** of a specified disability.
**SC, Mar 2026**: **40%** is a **floor**, not a ceiling.
**Rajive Raturi** (**2018**): accessibility in transport and buildings.

n5935361ae46.s: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding inclusive education for children with disabilities in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Inclusive education assistance is Rs 3,500 per child with special needs
AP Samagra Shiksha won the national award for Best State in implementing the RPwD Act for 2024-25
Samagra Shiksha's inclusive component targets exclusive education of gifted children
n5935361ae46.x: Samagra Shiksha's inclusive component covers assessment, aids, assistive technology and therapy; exclusive education of gifted children is not its target.
xa: AP follows a **Zero Rejection Policy**; **16,238** CwSN enrolled.
**Divyang Shakti**: **100% free travel** for PwDs in APSRTC buses from **18 March 2026**.
AP has **11.04 lakh** PwDs (Census **2011**).

n3cd0f077c8b.s: Which of the following correctly compares the Census 2011 figure for India with the approximate global estimate mentioned for persons with disabilities?
o: India: 2.21 percent; global estimate: about 16 percent
India: about 16 percent; global estimate: 2.21 percent
n3cd0f077c8b.x: India’s Census 2011 figure was 2.21 percent, whereas the approximate global estimate was about 16 percent; the difference suggests under-reporting in India.
n3cd0f077c8b.tq: Keep national census data separate from the international estimate and disability-type percentages.
xs: **Census 2011**: India **2.21%**; **WHO** global estimate about **16%** — option **(2)** is correct.
The gap points to **under-reporting** in India.
**20.3%**, **18.9%** and **18.8%** are shares of movement, hearing and seeing disability within PwDs.
xa: Census 2011 counted **2.68 crore** PwDs.
Today: about **6 crore** PwDs (Jun **2026**).
AP: **11.04 lakh** PwDs (Census **2011**).

n4a2711417f8.s: Among the following categories, which was the largest disability group in India according to the cited Census 2011 distribution?
n4a2711417f8.x: Movement disability was the largest among the cited categories at 20.3 percent, followed by hearing at 18.9 percent and seeing at 18.8 percent.
n4a2711417f8.tq: Compare the three close percentages rather than relying on a broad category impression.
xs: **Movement** disability was the largest (**20.3%**) — option **(1)** is correct.
It is followed by **hearing** (**18.9%**) and **seeing** (**18.8%**).
xa: ⚠ National largest = **movement**; AP largest = **orthopaedic** (**3.13 lakh**).
Census 2011: **2.68 crore** PwDs = **2.21%** of population.
**Census 2027** adds acid attack, neurological and blood disorders.

n0c61374f10d.s: Andhra Pradesh's Divyang Shakti (2026) provides persons with disabilities:
n0c61374f10d.x: Divyang Shakti gives 100% free APSRTC bus travel to persons with disabilities; concessional self-employment loans are associated with NDFDC.
xa: Free travel from **18 March 2026**, part of **'Indra Dhanassu'**.
For **40%+** disability in **5** APSRTC bus categories; escort gets **50%** concession.
NDFDC loans: up to **Rs 50 lakh** at **5-9%**.

n0d7a804dc53.s: The Inclusive India initiative is primarily aimed at:
o: Providing legal guardianship to persons with multiple disabilities
Providing concessional loans to persons with disabilities for self-employment
Bringing persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities into the mainstream
Regulating the training of rehabilitation professionals
n0d7a804dc53.x: The Inclusive India initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, associated with the National Trust, seeks to bring persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities into the mainstream.
n0d7a804dc53.tq: Match the initiative with its distinctive target group and purpose.
xs: The **Inclusive India initiative** brings **persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities into the mainstream** — option **(3)** is correct.
Legal guardianship is the **National Trust**'s role; loans are **NDFDC**; training regulation is **RCI**.
xa: It is run by **MoSJE / National Trust** (APPSC-G2 **2017**).
**NIEPID**, **Secunderabad**, is the National Institute for intellectual disabilities.
National Trust schemes: **Niramaya**, **Disha**, **Vikas**, **Samarth**, **Gharaunda**.

nffc35821cd2.s: The target group of special education is:
nffc35821cd2.x: The target group for special education is children with disabilities, or CwSN; it is not a programme exclusively for gifted groups.
xa: **Samagra Shiksha** covers all RPwD-listed disabilities.
It took over the old **IEDSS**.
AP: **Zero Rejection Policy**.

n52dba76b159.s: Under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, the obligation to maintain parents extends to:
o: Only biological sons above 18 years of age
Biological, adopted and step-children, and legal heirs in the relevant circumstances
n52dba76b159.x: The Act places obligations on biological, adopted and step-children, and also on legal heirs in relation to senior citizens who cannot maintain themselves.
n52dba76b159.tq: Watch for the restrictive word ‘only’ in the options on legal obligation.
xs: **Children (biological, adopted, step) and legal heirs** must maintain parents and senior citizens who cannot maintain themselves — option **(3)** is correct.
The duty is not limited to sons, daughters or government employees.
xa: The **2019 Amendment Bill** (lapsed) sought to add **sons/daughters-in-law and grandchildren**.
The Act **punishes neglect by children** (APPSC **2018**).
Maximum maintenance: **Rs 10,000 per month**.

n358757f93e7.s: Section 20 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 deals with:
n358757f93e7.x: Section 20 concerns the provision of medical care for senior citizens and forms the basis of the National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly.
n358757f93e7.tq: Use section-number matching and reject provisions belonging to Sections 23 or other parts of the Act.
xs: **Section 20** deals with **medical care of senior citizens** — option **(2)** is correct.
Property transfers are **Section 23**; abandonment is punished with up to **3 months** and/or **Rs 5,000**.
xa: Section 20 is the basis of **NPHCE** (MoHFW, **2010-11**).
⚠ **Sec 23** = property; **Sec 20** = medical care.
Case disposal within **90 days**.

ncf78358c4fe.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007?
o: Its 2019 Amendment Bill, removing the maintenance ceiling, was enacted by Parliament
Abandoning a senior citizen may attract imprisonment up to three months and/or a fine up to ₹5,000
At least one old-age home is contemplated in every district
It is administered by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
ncf78358c4fe.x: The 2019 Amendment Bill proposed removing the maintenance cap but was not passed.
xa: Maximum maintenance: **Rs 10,000 per month**.
Earlier State law: **Himachal Pradesh** Act, **2001**.
The **2019 Amendment Bill** lapsed.

n1b6f5ae8239.s: Which provision lets the Tribunal declare void a senior citizen's property transfer when the transferee fails to provide the promised care?
o: Section 12 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
Section 20 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
Section 23 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
Section 32 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
n1b6f5ae8239.x: Section 23 of the 2007 Act permits the Tribunal to declare such a transfer void when the promised basic needs and care are not provided.
xa: ⚠ **Section 20** = medical care.
Maintenance Tribunal in AP: **RDO / Sub-Collector**.
Maximum maintenance: **Rs 10,000 per month**.

n0ac52023bd4.s: The Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana for BPL senior citizens is funded from the:
n0ac52023bd4.x: The scheme is funded from the Senior Citizens' Welfare Fund and requires at least 30 per cent women beneficiaries in each district.
xa: Eligibility: **60+**, BPL or income up to **Rs 15,000** a month.
Aids: walking sticks, wheelchairs, **hearing aids**, **dentures**.
Implementing agency: **ALIMCO**.

n8c13ec53974.s: Under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPOP), a component of AVYAY, eligible NGOs may get up to what share of project cost?
n8c13ec53974.x: IPOP can fund up to 90 per cent of project cost for old-age homes, day-care centres and mobile medicare units.
xa: AVYAY's other components: **State Action Plan**, **RVY**, **Elder Line**.
AP: **7** physiotherapy centres treated **87,240** patients.
**Vayoshreshtha Samman** also honours seniors.

ndb5d8112b67.s: Which was the first State to enact a law for the maintenance of parents, before the central Act of 2007?
ndb5d8112b67.x: Himachal Pradesh enacted the Maintenance of Parents and Dependents Act, 2001, the first such State law. Kerala is first with a Senior Citizens' Welfare Department; Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka are not cited as first.
xs: **Himachal Pradesh** was the **first State** with a parents-maintenance law — option **(2)** is correct.
It was the **Himachal Pradesh Maintenance of Parents and Dependents Act, 2001**.
The notes name no such earlier law for AP, Kerala or Karnataka.
xa: The central Act came in **2007**, administered by **MoSJE**.
⚠ **RVY** was first launched at **Nellore**, AP.
The **2019 Amendment Bill** lapsed.

n8ab45c51f00.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the Maintenance Tribunal under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 is headed at the sub-divisional level by the:
n8ab45c51f00.x: In Andhra Pradesh, the Maintenance Tribunal functions at the sub-division level and is headed by the Revenue Divisional Officer or Sub-Collector.
n8ab45c51f00.tq: Use the level of the tribunal to identify the appropriate administrative authority.
xs: In AP the **Maintenance Tribunal** (sub-division level) is headed by the **RDO / Sub-Collector** (**Revenue Divisional Officer**) — option **(2)** is correct.
The **District Collector** heads the **Appellate Tribunal**.
xa: Case to be disposed within **90 days**.
AP cases: **2,549** filed, **2,236** resolved.
Victims of elder abuse or cyber fraud can approach the **RDO**.

naf532558697.s: Which one of the following is a correct provision of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007?
o: The Maintenance Tribunal can decide only cases relating to property transfer.
The Maintenance Tribunal has no power to permit an appeal.
The Maintenance Tribunal may award up to Rs 20,000 per month and should decide the case within 30 days.
The Maintenance Tribunal may award up to Rs 10,000 per month and should decide the case within 90 days.
naf532558697.x: The Act prescribed a maximum maintenance of Rs 10,000 per month, required disposal within 90 days and allowed an appeal.
naf532558697.tq: Combine the amount, time limit and appeal feature to distinguish the statutory tribunal provision.
xs: The Tribunal may award up to **Rs 10,000 per month** and must **decide within 90 days** — option **(4)** is correct.
Option (3) gives the wrong cap and time limit; the Tribunal is not limited to property cases, and an **Appellate Tribunal** exists.
xa: Appellate Tribunal: district level, **District Collector** (AP).
The **2019 Bill** sought to remove the **Rs 10,000** cap.
**Section 23** covers conditional property transfers.

n3e1467ffaab.s: Under the National Policy on Older Persons, 1999, an ‘older person’ is one who is:
n3e1467ffaab.x: The National Policy on Older Persons, 1999 defines an older person as an individual aged 60 years or above.
n3e1467ffaab.tq: Identify the policy definition rather than using a general retirement-age assumption.
xs: Under **NPOP 1999**, an older person is one aged **60 years or above** (**60+**) — option **(4)** is correct.
The other age cut-offs are not used by NPOP.
xa: NPOP was framed by **MoSJE**.
It lists **14 principal areas of intervention**, incl. health care and nutrition.
⚠ **Ayushman Vay Vandana** card is for **70+**; **IGNOAPS** pays **Rs 500** at **80+**.

nc1d355ee476.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about policies for the elderly?
o: The National Policy on Older Persons, 1999 was framed by MoSJE
The National Policy for Senior Citizens, 2011 gives special focus to elderly women
The National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly was launched by MoSJE
The National Policy for Senior Citizens, 2011 emphasises ageing in place
nc1d355ee476.x: NPHCE was launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in 2010-11, not MoSJE.
xa: NPHCE is based on **Section 20** (medical care).
The **2007 Act** is administered by **MoSJE**.
NPOP has **14** areas of intervention.

n31f212290d4.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the components of Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana?
n31f212290d4.x: The four components of AVYAY are the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens, State Action Plan, Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana and Elder Line. The National Family Benefit Scheme is an NSAP component.
n31f212290d4.tq: Use the programme-family distinction to reject an NSAP component.
xs: The **National Family Benefit Scheme** is not an AVYAY component — option **(1)** is correct.
AVYAY's four components: **Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens**, **State Action Plan**, **RVY** and **Elder Line**.
xa: AVYAY began in **April 2021**, renamed from the **National Action Plan for Senior Citizens**.
**Rs 287.81 crore** utilised (ES **2025-26**).
Innovation: **SAGE**, **AGRASR** elderly SHGs, **silver economy**.

n12f62579d88.s: Which organisation is associated with elderly-care services and the release of elder-abuse surveys in India?
n12f62579d88.x: HelpAge India runs elderly-care services and releases surveys relating to elder abuse.
n12f62579d88.tq: Match the organisation with its distinctive activity rather than with a general human-rights function.
xs: **HelpAge India** runs elderly-care services and releases **elder-abuse surveys** — option **(1)** is correct.
The notes do not link the other bodies to these surveys.
xa: **World Elder Abuse Awareness Day**: **15 June**.
AP's Senior Citizens Welfare Association flagged rising abuse and **cyber fraud** against elders living alone.
**NPSC 2011** wants **harsh punishment** for elder abuse.

nfcbbc52f442.s: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana was launched on 1 April 2017 at which place?
nfcbbc52f442.x: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana was launched at Nellore in Andhra Pradesh on 1 April 2017.
nfcbbc52f442.tq: Discriminate between closely related locations within the same State.
xs: **Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana** was launched on **1 April 2017** at **Nellore**, AP — option **(1)** is correct.
It was asked in APPSC-G2 **2017**.
xa: It is run by **MoSJE** through **ALIMCO**.
It gives free physical aids to **BPL senior citizens** (**60+**).
Funded from the **Senior Citizens' Welfare Fund** (unclaimed deposits).

n36affc5734d.s: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana is implemented through which combination?
n36affc5734d.x: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana is associated with the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and ALIMCO.
n36affc5734d.tq: Identify the implementing agency by separating the ministry from the delivery corporation.
xs: RVY is run by **MoSJE** through **ALIMCO** — option **(1)** is correct.
**MoHFW/LIC** do not fit: **LIC** runs **PMVVY** (Ministry of Finance); **MoRD** runs **IGNOAPS**.
xa: RVY is a component of **AVYAY**.
Launched **1 April 2017** at **Nellore**.
Funded from the **Senior Citizens' Welfare Fund**.

n591c700cfd9.s: Under the Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana as originally launched in 2017, which of the following combinations is correct?
o: 10% assured pension for 10 years; maximum purchase price ₹7.5 lakh; maximum pension ₹10,000 per month
8% assured pension for 5 years; maximum purchase price ₹10 lakh; maximum pension ₹7,500 per month
8% assured pension for 10 years; maximum purchase price ₹7.5 lakh; maximum pension ₹5,000 per month
7% assured pension for 15 years; maximum purchase price ₹5 lakh; maximum pension ₹3,000 per month
n591c700cfd9.x: PMVVY offered an assured pension at 8 per cent for 10 years, with a maximum purchase price of ₹7.5 lakh and maximum pension of ₹5,000 per month.
n591c700cfd9.tq: Match the three numerical limits without confusing duration, purchase price and pension ceiling.
xs: **PMVVY**: **8%** assured pension for **10 years**; max purchase **Rs 7.5 lakh**; max pension **Rs 5,000/month** — option **(3)** is correct.
The other options change the rate, term, purchase price or pension.
xa: Run by the **Ministry of Finance** through **LIC**; **GST-exempt**.
Closed for new subscription after **31 March 2023**.
⚠ **PMVVY** (pension) vs **Ayushman Vay Vandana** (health, **70+**).
n591c700cfd9.fixed: limits raised in 2018 to Rs 15 lakh / Rs 10,000 per month; stem must be dated

nd8fe7b4b1d1.s: IGNOAPS, a component of the National Social Assistance Programme, is administered by the:
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
nd8fe7b4b1d1.x: IGNOAPS is under NSAP and the Ministry of Rural Development; its assistance has been frozen at Rs 200 since 2007.
xa: NSAP pension erosion → calls for an **inflation-indexed minimum pension floor**.
Beneficiaries must be **BPL**.

n63e4341fc8b.s: The Ayushman Vay Vandana card under AB-PMJAY is meant for:
o: Children below 10 years from SECC households
Only women aged 70 years and above
All persons aged 60 years and above subject to an income ceiling
All persons aged 70 years and above irrespective of income
n63e4341fc8b.x: All senior citizens aged 70 years and above are eligible for the Ayushman Vay Vandana card irrespective of income.
n63e4341fc8b.tq: Test the age threshold together with the important income-related exception.
xs: The **Ayushman Vay Vandana card** is for **all aged 70+** (**70 years and above**) **irrespective of income** — option **(4)** is correct.
It gives health cover of **Rs 5 lakh** under **AB-PMJAY** (MoHFW, **2024**).
xa: ⚠ NPOP defines older persons as **60+**.
⚠ **PMVVY** = pension (LIC); **Vayoshri** = aids (ALIMCO).
NPHCE was launched by **MoHFW** in **2010-11**.

n01fa8cb7014.s: The UN Decade of Healthy Ageing covers which period?
n01fa8cb7014.x: The UN Decade of Healthy Ageing covers the period 2021–2030.
n01fa8cb7014.tq: Distinguish the decade framework from the earlier Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing.
xs: The **UN Decade of Healthy Ageing** is **2021-2030** — option **(2)** is correct.
**2002** was the **Madrid** Plan; **1999** NPOP.
xa: **International Day of Older Persons**: **1 October**.
**World Elder Abuse Awareness Day**: **15 June**.
India's **AVYAY** also began in **2021**.

n44494393903.s: The International Day of Older Persons is observed on
n44494393903.x: The International Day of Older Persons is observed on 1 October.
n44494393903.tq: Use direct date recall while distinguishing it from World Elder Abuse Awareness Day.
xs: The **International Day of Older Persons** is on **1 October** — option **(3)** is correct.
**15 June** is **World Elder Abuse Awareness Day**.
xa: **Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing**: **2002**.
**UN Decade of Healthy Ageing**: **2021-2030**.
NPOP: older person = **60+**.

n97a751e370c.s: World Elder Abuse Awareness Day is observed on
n97a751e370c.x: World Elder Abuse Awareness Day is observed on 15 June.
n97a751e370c.tq: Apply confusable-date discrimination between the two observances relating to older persons.
xs: **World Elder Abuse Awareness Day** is on **15 June** — option **(4)** is correct.
**1 October** is the **International Day of Older Persons**.
xa: **HelpAge India** releases elder-abuse surveys.
The 2007 Act punishes **abandonment**: up to **3 months** and/or **Rs 5,000**.
**Elder Line 14567** is the national senior-citizens helpline.

ne572187a671.s: Which sequence correctly represents the stages of demographic transition?
o: Both rates low → birth rate falls → death rate falls → high rates
High birth and death rates → death rate falls → birth rate falls → both rates low
High birth and death rates → birth rate falls → death rate rises → both rates high
Death rate falls → both rates low → birth rate rises → high death rate
ne572187a671.x: The demographic transition proceeds from high birth and death rates, to falling death rates, then falling birth rates, and finally low birth and death rates.
ne572187a671.tq: Track the sequence of mortality decline before fertility decline.
xs: **Demographic transition** runs: **high birth and death rates → death rate falls → birth rate falls → both low** — option **(2)**.
The **death rate falls first**; the birth rate follows later, which is why population grows fast in the middle stage.
Options that start with low rates or have the death rate rising reverse this sequence.
xa: India is presently in the **youth bulge** stage.
SRS 2024: India's **TFR 1.9**, below the replacement level of **2.1**.

n7be334adaaf.s: India is presently described, in demographic-transition terms, as being in the:
n7be334adaaf.x: India is described as being in the youth-bulge stage of demographic transition.
n7be334adaaf.tq: Identify the current demographic-stage label rather than a general population condition.
xs: In demographic-transition terms, India is in the **youth bulge** stage — option **(1)**.
A youth bulge means a large young and working-age share: SRS 2024 puts working age at **66.4%** and children at **24%**.
xa: **Demographic transition:** high birth and death rates → death rate falls → birth rate falls → both low.
A large workforce pays off only if **employed**; jobs are needed for about **9.7 million** new working-age people each year.

nee913050b66.s: In the history of India's population growth, the year 1921 is known as the:
o: Start of high but slowing growth
nee913050b66.x: After decline in 1911–1921 came the Great Divide in 1921, the explosion of 1961–1971 and high but slowing growth in 1981–2011.
xa: ⚠ **1921** is the "Great Divide" — after it India's population never declined again.
**Demographic transition:** high birth and death rates → death rate falls → birth rate falls → both low.
India today is in the **youth bulge** stage of the demographic transition.

n048c14121a1.s: Under which programme can NGOs receive support of up to 90% of the cost of old age homes?
o: National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly
n048c14121a1.x: The Integrated Programme for Older Persons provides NGOs with support of up to 90% of the costs of old age homes.
n048c14121a1.tq: Match the welfare intervention with the exact programme responsible for it.
xs: NGOs get up to **90%** of the costs of old age homes under the **Integrated Programme for Older Persons** — option **(1)**.
**AVYAY** (with **SAGE**) is the umbrella scheme giving equity to senior-care start-ups; **NPHCE** is the health-care programme.
xa: **SAGE:** equity of up to **₹1 crore** for senior-care start-ups.

naddb28f581f.s: As per Census 2011, India's decadal population growth rate for 2001-11 was:
naddb28f581f.x: Decadal growth in 2001-11 was 17.7%; India's population was about 121.09 crore, 68.9% of it rural.
xa: The **next Census** is due in **2027**.
Growth phases: **1911-21** decline, **1921** the **"Great Divide"**, **1961-71** explosion, **1981-2011** high but slowing.
AP's population is **495.77 lakh** — **4.09%** of India, ranked **10th** (2025-26).

nf5537c62d32.s: According to NFHS-5, which of the following correctly represents the total fertility rate of India and Andhra Pradesh?
nf5537c62d32.x: NFHS-5 recorded India’s total fertility rate at 2.0 and Andhra Pradesh’s at 1.7.
nf5537c62d32.tq: Compare the national and State figures without reversing their order.
xs: **NFHS-5** put India's **TFR at 2.0** and **Andhra Pradesh at 1.7** — option **(4)**.
AP is thus well below the replacement level of **2.1**.
xa: ⚠ **APPCA** quotes AP's TFR at **1.5**.
**Bihar** had the highest TFR in NFHS-5 (**3.0**).

n01c013bf1fc.s: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding the debate on population control?
o: Population control is considered necessary for environmental protection
Southern States that controlled population may lose relative representation and financial advantages
Delimitation could cost the southern States 8–10 seats
Population carries 40–50% weight in Finance Commission formulas
n01c013bf1fc.x: Population carries 15–25% weight in Finance Commission formulas, not 40–50%.
xa: ⚠ In the UPPSC 2023 key, the assertion was true but the **reason** given was false.
AP's draft **Population Management Policy** (Mar 2026) shifts from control to management.

n83b38c38d82.s: About how many new working-age people does India need jobs for every year?
n83b38c38d82.x: About 9.7 million new working-age people enter each year; the demographic dividend pays off only if they are employed.
xa: SRS 2024: working age = **66.4%**; children = **24%**.
India is in the **youth bulge** stage of the demographic transition.

na7c70af6f33.s: In Javed v. State of Haryana (2003), the Supreme Court:
o: Abolished two-child norms for local elections across India
Ruled only on the dependency ratio
na7c70af6f33.x: In Javed v. State of Haryana (2003), the Supreme Court upheld Haryana's two-child norm.
xa: ⚠ AP's draft policy (Mar 2026) **removes the two-child norm for local elections**.
AP's policy also offers **₹25,000** for a second or third child.

na09fb706583.s: Which of the following is a feature of Andhra Pradesh's draft Population Management Policy (March 2026)?
o: A two-child norm for contesting local body elections
An incentive of Rs 25,000 for a second or third child and removal of the two-child norm for local elections
A cash penalty on families with more than two children
Compulsory sterilisation after the second child
na09fb706583.x: The draft policy moves from population control to management, offers Rs 25,000 for a second or third child and removes the two-child norm for local elections. Imposing a two-child norm, penalties or sterilisation would be control measures, the opposite of the policy.
na09fb706583.tq: AP U-turn: pro-natalist, Rs 25,000, two-child norm removed.
xs: AP's draft policy offers **₹25,000** for a **second or third child** and **removes the two-child norm** for **local elections** — option **(2)**.
It moves from **control to management**, so a two-child norm, penalties or sterilisation would contradict it.
xa: ⚠ The SC had upheld Haryana's two-child norm in **Javed v State of Haryana (2003)**.
Counter-debate: southern states that controlled population could lose **8-10 seats** in delimitation.

na3b7ae0516c.s: About what percentage of elderly persons in India have no pension?
na3b7ae0516c.x: About 78% of the elderly have no pension and about 70% depend on others.
xa: **70% of elderly women** have no pension.
Elderly = **30-35%** of hospitalisation spending.
**Over 55%** of the elderly now live in **nuclear** households.

na049772104c.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position associated with NPSC 2011?
o: It supported ageing in place and drew attention to destitution among rural elderly persons.
It restricted elderly welfare exclusively to persons living in joint families.
It recommended abolishing NGO support for old age homes.
It favoured institutionalisation of all elderly persons in urban old age homes.
na049772104c.x: NPSC 2011 backed the concept of ‘ageing in place’ and highlighted destitution among the rural elderly.
na049772104c.tq: Distinguish community-based ageing support from compulsory institutional care.
xs: **NPSC 2011** backs **"ageing in place"** and flags **destitution among the rural elderly** — option **(1)**.
Ageing in place means the elderly staying in their own homes and communities, not being institutionalised.
xa: **NPOP 1999** came first; **NPHCE** in **2010-11**.
**Kerala** is the first state with a Senior Citizens' Welfare Department, Commission and Elderly Budget.

nbf6333c0df4.s: The dependency ratio is calculated by which of the following formulas?
nbf6333c0df4.x: The dependency ratio is calculated as the population aged 0–14 plus the population aged 65 and above, divided by the population aged 15–64.
nbf6333c0df4.tq: Separate the dependent-age groups in the numerator from the working-age denominator.
xs: **Dependency ratio** = **(0-14 plus 65+) ÷ (15-64)** — option **(4)**.
The numerator is the dependants (children and the old); the denominator is the **working-age** population.
xa: SRS 2024: working age = **66.4%**; children = **24%**.
Among the elderly, **70%** depend on others and **78%** have no pension.

n21e4f70c44d.s: Which State is the first in India to have a Senior Citizens’ Welfare Department, a Commission and an Elderly Budget?
n21e4f70c44d.x: Kerala is the first State to establish all three: a Senior Citizens’ Welfare Department, a Commission and an Elderly Budget.
n21e4f70c44d.tq: Identify the State associated with the complete institutional framework for senior citizens.
xs: **Kerala** is the **first state** with a **Senior Citizens' Welfare Department**, a **Commission** and an **Elderly Budget** — option **(2)**.
**Andhra Pradesh** is instead known for its pro-natalist draft **Population Management Policy** (Mar 2026).
xa: **India:** first national family planning programme (**1952**).

nd4a9016a540.s: The National Policy on Older Persons (NPOP) was announced in:
nd4a9016a540.x: The National Policy on Older Persons was announced in 1999. NPSC came in 2011, while 2007 is the year of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act.
nd4a9016a540.tq: 1999 was the International Year of Older Persons: NPOP 1999.
xs: The **National Policy on Older Persons (NPOP)** came in **1999** — option **(3)**.
**2011** is the year of **NPSC**, not NPOP.
xa: **NPHCE** came in **2010-11**.
**NPSC 2011** backs **"ageing in place"** and flags destitution among the rural elderly.
**AVYAY** with **SAGE**: equity of up to **₹1 crore** for senior-care start-ups.

n60260cc08a4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about NALSA v. Union of India?
o: It recognised transgender persons as the third gender
It held that gender identity must be decided by biological examination and State verification
It extended Articles 14, 15, 16, 19(1)(a) and 21 to transgender persons
n60260cc08a4.x: NALSA held that gender identity is self-determined, not dependent on biology or State verification.
xa: Delivered on **15 April 2014** by **Justices K.S. Radhakrishnan and A.K. Sikri**.
The **2019 Act's** Objects cited NALSA and the **right to self-perceived gender identity**.
⚠ The **2026** amendment **excludes self-perceived identity**.

n9eba223c38f.s: The 2026 amendment concerning transgender persons has been criticised primarily because it is viewed as:
o: Removing the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court over identity matters
Extending the NALSA principle to old-age pensions
Reversing the self-identification principle recognised in NALSA
Strengthening the self-identification principle of NALSA
n9eba223c38f.x: The principal criticism is that medical certification reverses the self-identification principle associated with the NALSA judgment.
n9eba223c38f.tq: Contrast the two competing legal principles: self-identification and medical certification.
xs: The 2026 Act is seen as **reversing NALSA's self-identification principle** — option **(3)**.
It replaces **self-identification** with **medical-board certification** and excludes self-perceived identity.
xa: **Section 4(2)** was omitted, ending legal recognition of self-determination.
It is under **SC challenge** by Laxmi Narayan Tripathi and Zainab Javid Patel.
**NHRC Advisory 2.0** asked the government to **review the amendment**.

n4e344da6092.s: Who moved the Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014 as a private member's Bill?
n4e344da6092.x: The Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014 was moved as a private member's Bill by Tiruchi Siva of the DMK.
n4e344da6092.tq: Match the legislative initiative with its mover and party.
xs: The **Rights of Transgender Persons Bill 2014** was a private member's bill moved by **Tiruchi Siva** (**DMK**) — option **(2)**.
It was passed by the **Rajya Sabha in April 2015**.
xa: It was the first private member's bill passed by the RS in **over four decades**.
It was **not passed by the Lok Sabha**.
The **2026 Amendment Bill** was introduced by **Virendra Kumar** in the Lok Sabha on **13 Mar 2026**.

nce7ebe1cd75.s: The Rights of Transgender Persons Bill, 2014, a private member's Bill, was passed by the Rajya Sabha in:
nce7ebe1cd75.x: It passed the Rajya Sabha in April 2015, the first private member's Bill passed there in over four decades, but was not passed by the Lok Sabha.
xa: Mover: **Tiruchi Siva** (**DMK**).
⚠ **2014** = NALSA judgment + the Bill; **2015** = RS passes it.

nca07eb8b313.s: Which of the following was a criticism of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019?
o: It prescribed heavier penalties than those for comparable crimes against women.
It completely abolished the role of the District Magistrate in identity certification.
It provided no reservation for transgender persons.
It excluded all socio-cultural transgender identities from its definition.
nca07eb8b313.x: Criticisms included lighter penalties than for similar crimes against women, District Magistrate gatekeeping of identity and the absence of reservation. The Act did include several socio-cultural identities.
nca07eb8b313.tq: Select the genuine criticism while rejecting options that reverse the Act’s provisions.
xs: A criticism of the 2019 Act was that it provided **no reservation** for transgender persons — option **(3)**.
Other criticisms: **lighter penalties** (not heavier) than for similar crimes against women, and **DM gatekeeping** of identity — so the DM's role was not abolished.
xa: NALSA had directed a **vertical** OBC-type quota; the community wants **horizontal** reservation.
**Karnataka** (2021) was the first state with a **1%** job quota.

n0b3c1f88bdf.s: The National Council for Transgender Persons is constituted as a statutory body under which legislation?
o: The National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993
The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019
n0b3c1f88bdf.x: The National Council for Transgender Persons is a statutory body constituted under the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.
n0b3c1f88bdf.tq: Identify the parent legislation of the statutory body.
xs: The **NCTP** is a **statutory body** under the **Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2019** — option **(4)**.
Its **Chairperson** is the **Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment**.
xa: Members: Health, Home, Minority Affairs etc. + **experts** + **community representatives**.
Role: **advises and monitors** policy.
2026: state/UT members by **rotation** — one each from North, South, East, West and North-East.

nac766a458da.s: Under the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, the certificate of identity is issued by the:
nac766a458da.x: The District Magistrate issues the certificate (a revised one after surgery); the National Council only advises and monitors policy.
xa: **Rules 2020** set the application procedure through the **national portal**.
⚠ Certificate: **2019** = DM alone; **2026** = DM on a **medical board's** recommendation.

n7765a03a70a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2026 amendment to the transgender persons law?
o: The District Magistrate issues the certificate on the recommendation of a designated medical board
The definition is limited to specified socio-cultural identities, intersex variations and persons forced to present as transgender
Self-perceived identity continues to be expressly included without restriction
Kidnapping and forcing a person to present as transgender were added as offences
n7765a03a70a.x: The amendment excludes self-perceived identity and omits Section 4(2).
xa: The Bill was introduced by **Virendra Kumar** on **13 Mar 2026**; assent by **Apr 2026**.

n6236893126a.s: The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 is administered by the:
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
n6236893126a.x: The Act (in force from 10 January 2020) is administered by MoSJE, and its National Council is chaired by the Union Social Justice Minister.
xa: The NCTP **advises and monitors** policy.
**SMILE** (**2022**) is also a **MoSJE** scheme.

n3657f0b4a2d.s: The goal of the SMILE scheme, launched by MoSJE in 2022, is:
n3657f0b4a2d.x: SMILE, an umbrella Central Sector scheme, aims at a begging-free India, 'Bhiksha Vritti Mukt Bharat'.
xa: Outlay: **Rs 365 crore**.
⚠ **Garima Greh** = shelter homes (**23** in **17** States/UTs).
Begging component covers **181 cities**; about **12,710** persons rehabilitated.

nd329cf0e572.s: What is the expanded form of SMILE in the context of welfare schemes?
o: Social Mission for Inclusive Livelihood and Employment
Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise
Scheme for Marginalised Inclusion, Livelihood and Education
Support Mission for Independent Living and Empowerment
nd329cf0e572.x: SMILE stands for Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise.
nd329cf0e572.tq: Test the exact official expansion of the scheme acronym.
xs: **SMILE** = **Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise** — option **(2)**.
It is a **2022** **MoSJE** umbrella **Central Sector** scheme.
xa: Goal: **"Bhiksha Vritti Mukt Bharat"**; outlay **Rs 365 crore**.
Components: welfare of **transgender persons** and rehabilitation of persons engaged in **begging**.

n5ac74dc1a86.s: Garima Greh under SMILE is primarily associated with which service?
n5ac74dc1a86.x: Garima Greh provides shelter homes for transgender persons.
n5ac74dc1a86.tq: Match the named sub-scheme with its core service.
xs: **Garima Greh** = **shelter homes** for transgender persons — option **(2)**.
There are **23** in **17 States/UTs** (ES 2025-26), with at least one per State.
xa: ⚠ **SMILE** is the umbrella scheme (**Rs 365 crore**); Garima Greh is one component.
**NHRC Advisory 2.0** asked for **more Garima Grehs**.

n194eec2e1e7.s: Which State was the first to formulate a transgender policy?
n194eec2e1e7.x: Kerala was the first State to formulate a transgender policy, in 2015.
n194eec2e1e7.tq: Test a first-in-the-country fact against neighbouring States associated with other transgender measures.
xs: **Kerala** was the first state with a transgender policy (**2015**) — option **(4)**.
⚠ Some notes give the year as **2021**.
xa: Kerala's **Sthree Suraksha** scheme covers EWS women and transgender persons.
**Tamil Nadu**: **Transgender Welfare Board (2008)**; **Karnataka**: first **1%** job quota (**2021**).

nff2ca253735.s: Invalidity and old-age pensions are listed in:
nff2ca253735.x: Invalidity and old-age pensions are in Concurrent List Entry 24, not State List Entry 9; NSAP rests on Articles 41 and 42.
xa: Central **IGNOAPS** is frozen at **Rs 200**.
AP's **NTR Bharosa** pays **Rs 4,000** to the elderly, widows and transgender persons.

nedab276c32d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the definition of a transgender person under the 2019 Act?
o: It excludes persons with intersex variations
It includes trans men and trans women
It includes socio-cultural identities such as kinner, hijra, aravani and jogta
nedab276c32d.x: The 2019 definition includes persons with intersex variations, along with trans men and women, genderqueer persons and the listed socio-cultural identities.
xa: ⚠ The **2026** definition is limited to socio-cultural identities, specified intersex/congenital variations and those **forced** to present as transgender.

na95e4d159e4.s: The NHRC Advisory 2.0 of May 2026 recommended that Census categories should include which of the following?
o: Only sexual minorities and senior citizens
Intersex persons, trans men and trans women
Only transgender persons and persons with disabilities
na95e4d159e4.x: The NHRC Advisory 2.0 recommended Census categories for intersex persons, trans men and trans women.
na95e4d159e4.tq: Identify the exact categories proposed in the advisory.
xs: **NHRC Advisory 2.0** (May 2026) asked for separate **intersex, transmen and transwomen** categories in **Census 2027** — option **(2)**.
It also asked the government to **review the amendment**.
xa: Other NHRC asks: admission by **self-identified gender**, ban on **non-consensual intersex surgery** on children, more **Garima Grehs**.
**Census 2011** counted about **4.88 lakh** transgender persons.

n8b52711ca31.s: According to Census 2011, approximately how many transgender persons were counted in India?
n8b52711ca31.x: Census 2011 counted approximately 4.88 lakh transgender persons in India.
n8b52711ca31.tq: Test the precise census estimate using close numerical distractors.
xs: **Census 2011** counted about **4.88 lakh** transgender persons — option **(3)**.
**Uttar Pradesh** had the highest count.
xa: Order: **UP** → **undivided Andhra Pradesh** → **Maharashtra** → **Bihar**.
**NHRC Advisory 2.0** wants separate intersex, transmen and transwomen categories in **Census 2027**.

n099a1b7dc7a.s: Under the NTR Bharosa Pension scheme in Andhra Pradesh, the monthly pension for elderly persons aged 60 years and above, widows and transgender persons is:
n099a1b7dc7a.x: NTR Bharosa provides Rs 4,000 per month to elderly persons aged 60 years and above, widows and transgender persons.
n099a1b7dc7a.tq: Discriminate between the common-category rate and the higher rates for specified disabilities or diseases.
xs: **NTR Bharosa** pays elderly (**60+**), widows and **transgender persons** **Rs 4,000** a month — option **(2)**.
**Rs 6,000** is the rate for **PwDs**.
xa: Chronic diseases = **Rs 10,000**; fully disabled = **Rs 15,000**.
Release in FY 2025-26: **Rs 32,754.90 crore**.

n4000a1f9e34.s: The 2026 amendment to the transgender persons law was challenged in the Supreme Court by:
o: Madhu Bai Kinnar and Shabnam Mausi
Laxmi Narayan Tripathi and Zainab Javid Patel
n4000a1f9e34.x: Laxmi Narayan Tripathi and Zainab Javid Patel challenged the amendment as contrary to the principles laid down in NALSA.
n4000a1f9e34.tq: Separate the petitioners challenging the amendment from the legislator and the NALSA Bench.
xs: The 2026 amendment was challenged in the **Supreme Court** by **Laxmi Narayan Tripathi and Zainab Javid Patel** as contrary to **NALSA** — option **(3)**.
**Virendra Kumar** introduced the Bill; **Shabnam Mausi** and **Madhu Bai Kinnar** were the first transgender MLA and mayor; **Joyita Mondal** was the first transgender judge.
xa: **SC, Aug 2026:** the Centre assured that ID cards issued before the 2026 Act remain valid.
Laxmi Narayan Tripathi was the first transgender person from Asia-Pacific to address the **UN General Assembly**.

ne0960423d41.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the nature of reservation sought by transgender persons in the context of the NALSA judgment?
o: A separate vertical reservation restricted to the General category
Reservation exclusively under the women’s quota
Horizontal reservation cutting across SC, ST, OBC and General categories
ne0960423d41.x: The transgender community has sought horizontal reservation, which would cut across the SC, ST, OBC and General categories. NALSA had directed treatment as socially and educationally backward, resembling a vertical OBC-type approach.
ne0960423d41.tq: Distinguish the two commonly confused forms of reservation by asking whether the quota cuts across existing categories.
xs: The community seeks **horizontal reservation** cutting across **SC/ST/OBC/General** — option **(4)**.
⚠ NALSA itself had directed a **vertical** OBC-type quota by treating them as **SEBC**.
xa: The demand **resurfaced** on **27 June 2023** with a Mumbai protest against Maharashtra's reply to the **Bombay High Court**.
**Karnataka** (2021) was first to give a **1%** quota in all government services.

nb3ed0e2629a.s: The issue of reservation for transgender persons resurfaced in June 2023 in connection with which State?
nb3ed0e2629a.x: The issue resurfaced through a Mumbai protest against Maharashtra’s reply to the Bombay High Court in June 2023.
nb3ed0e2629a.tq: Use the place of the protest and the State involved to separate a current issue from nearby State measures.
xs: The reservation issue resurfaced in **June 2023** (**27 June 2023**) through a **Mumbai** protest against **Maharashtra**'s reply to the **Bombay High Court** — option **(3)**.
The demand was for **horizontal** reservation across SC/ST/OBC/General.
xa: ⚠ **Karnataka** — first state with **1%** reservation in all government services (**July 2021**).
NALSA's quota was **vertical**, OBC-type.

n1922440f59d.s: For the purposes of the National Commission for Minorities Act, a community is a minority when it is:
o: Defined as such in the Act
n1922440f59d.x: The NCM Act does not define 'minority'; a community notified by the Centre is a minority for the Act, though States may notify their own for State purposes.
xa: **Jains** were State minorities in **11 States** before 2014.
The **State** is the unit for minority status (**T.M.A. Pai, 2002**).

n5a94c4c931a.s: After T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002), minority status is decided with reference to the population position in the:
n5a94c4c931a.x: The State, not the whole of India, is the unit for deciding minority status; minority rights are not absolute and may be regulated.
xa: ⚠ **APPSC G2 2017** treated "minority rights are **absolute**" as the untrue statement.
**St. Xavier's (1974):** regulations only for **standards/excellence**.
**In re Kerala Education Bill:** the State may impose **reasonable conditions** for aid.

n2e55f5e1c83.s: Which one of the following communities is NOT among the notified minority communities?
n2e55f5e1c83.x: The notified minority communities are Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains. Jews are not included in this listed group.
n2e55f5e1c83.tq: Find the outsider in a recognised statutory list rather than choosing a community from memory alone.
xs: **Jews** are NOT a notified minority — option **(2)**.
Notified: **Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis** (**1993**) and **Jains** (**2014**).
xa: Jains were added on **27 January 2014** as the **sixth**.
Six notified minorities ≈ **19%** of India's population.
n2e55f5e1c83.fixed: stem said 'pairs of communities' but options are single communities

ne4b6733feb9.s: Jains were notified as a minority community in:
ne4b6733feb9.x: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis were notified in 1993; Jains were added in 2014.
xa: Linguistic minorities come under the **Special Officer** (**Art. 350B**).
⚠ **1993** = five communities + first statutory NCM; **2014** = Jains.

n9deef8833ae.s: Under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, a 'minority' means a community notified as such by the Central Government under which provision?
n9deef8833ae.x: The Act does not define minority; under Section 2(c) a minority is any community notified by the Central Government. Section 3(2) requires five members including the Chairperson to be from minority communities; Article 29(1) protects the language, script or culture of any section of citizens; Section 9(1) of the Waqf Act, 1995 concerns the Central Waqf Council.
n9deef8833ae.tq: Sec 2(c) = Centre notifies minorities (criticised as 'unbridled power').
xs: Under **Section 2(c)** of the NCM Act, a minority = any community **notified by the Central Government** — option **(1)**.
**Section 3(2)** concerns minority members of the Commission; **Art. 29(1)** protects culture; **Section 9(1)** of the Waqf Act 1995 is the **Central Waqf Council**.
xa: Critics say Sec. 2(c) gives the Centre **"unbridled power"**, uneasy with **T.M.A. Pai**.
The Constitution uses "minority" in **Arts 29, 30, 350A, 350B** without defining it.

n149d86f69ff.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function or power of the National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions?
o: Determining the minority status of an educational institution
Adjudicating disputes relating to affiliation with universities
Amending the Constitution to define the term minority
n149d86f69ff.x: The Commission can determine minority status, decide affiliation disputes and issue minority certificates, and it has civil court powers. It has no power to amend the Constitution.
n149d86f69ff.tq: Find the option outside the statutory and quasi-judicial jurisdiction of the body.
xs: **Amending the Constitution to define minority** is NOT an NCMEI power — option **(3)**.
The **NCMEI** (Act of **2004**) decides **minority status** of institutions, **affiliation disputes** with universities and **minority certificate** issues, with **civil court powers**.
xa: It has a **quasi-judicial** role.

ndf53bf3eb7d.s: The Criminal Tribes Act, 1871, in relation to Denotified Tribes, was:
ndf53bf3eb7d.x: Denotified Tribes had been branded under the Criminal Tribes Act, 1871, which was repealed in 1952.
ndf53bf3eb7d.tq: Pair the historical enactment with its repeal year and beware of confusing repeal with replacement.
xs: The **Criminal Tribes Act 1871**, which branded **DNTs**, was **repealed in 1952** — option **(2)**.
So it was neither expanded nor constitutionalised.
xa: **Census 2027** will count DNTs.
**Renke Commission** (report **2008**) was the first DNT commission.

n0ca6516d8a6.s: T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka (2002) was decided by a Bench of how many judges?
n0ca6516d8a6.x: An 11-judge Bench made the State the unit for minority status and allowed regulation, but not control, of minority institutions.
xa: APP writes the case as "v. State of Kerala"; it is **v State of Karnataka**.

n2d1fd687f08.s: The Constitution refers to the term ‘minority’ in which of the following Articles, without defining it?
n2d1fd687f08.x: The Constitution uses the term ‘minority’ in Articles 29, 30, 350A and 350B, but does not provide a general definition of the term.
n2d1fd687f08.tq: Recall the exact Article group rather than selecting a familiar Fundamental Rights cluster.
xs: The Constitution uses "minority" in **Articles 29, 30, 350A and 350B** but never defines it — option **(2)**.
Only **religious and linguistic** minorities are recognised.
xa: The **NCM Act** also does not define it; under **Section 2(c)**, a minority = any community **notified by the Central Government**.
Arts **350A** and **350B** were inserted by the **7th Constitutional Amendment, 1956**.

na1b293f8d55.s: Which one of the following grounds is NOT expressly included in Article 29(2) as a basis for denying admission to a State-maintained or State-aided educational institution?
na1b293f8d55.x: Article 29(2) prohibits denial of admission on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language. Sex and place of birth are not included in this list.
na1b293f8d55.tq: Find the omitted ground rather than selecting one of the four expressly listed grounds.
xs: **Place of birth** is NOT a ground in **Art. 29(2)** — option **(2)**.
Art. 29(2) bars denial of admission on grounds **only of religion, race, caste or language**.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** **sex** and **place of birth** are not listed.
Art. 29(2) applies to **State-maintained or State-aided** institutions.
**Art. 29** protects any section of **citizens**; **Art. 30** only minorities.

nae84214ff59.s: Which provision bars denial of admission to State-maintained or State-aided educational institutions on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language?
nae84214ff59.x: Article 29(2) bars such denial; Article 29(1) protects the language, script or culture of any distinct section of citizens.
xa: **Art. 30** applies **only to minorities**; Madrasas are run under it.

nbe2f7c96109.s: A State seeks to deny aid to an educational institution solely because it is managed by a linguistic minority. Which constitutional provision is most directly attracted?
nbe2f7c96109.x: Article 30(2) provides that the State shall not discriminate in granting aid to an educational institution on the ground that it is under the management of a minority, whether religious or linguistic.
nbe2f7c96109.tq: Apply the factual situation to the specific clause dealing with State aid to minority-managed institutions.
xs: **Article 30(2)** — the State shall not discriminate against **minority-managed** institutions in **granting aid** — option **(1)**.
**Art. 29(1)** is about conserving language/culture, **29(2)** about admission, and **350A** about mother-tongue primary instruction.
xa: **Art. 30(1)** covers **all minorities, religious or linguistic** — the "Charter of Education Rights".
**Art. 30(1A)** was added by the **44th Amendment**.

nb74965aff79.s: Which Article bars the State from discriminating against minority educational institutions in granting aid?
nb74965aff79.x: Under Article 30 the State cannot discriminate against minority institutions in aid; it may regulate standards without destroying minority character.
xa: **St. Xavier's (1974):** right to administer protected; regulation only for **standards/excellence**.
**T.M.A. Pai (2002):** the State may **regulate** but not **control** administration.

n987999ad5e2.s: Clause (1A) of Article 30, which protects the right of minorities to establish educational institutions when their property is compulsorily acquired, was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
n987999ad5e2.x: The 44th Amendment, which removed the right to property, added Article 30(1A) so that removal of that right does not affect minorities' right to establish institutions and compensation is ensured on acquisition. The 7th Amendment (1956) inserted Articles 350A and 350B; the 93rd Amendment inserted Article 15(5) after P.A. Inamdar; the 42nd Amendment did not add Article 30(1A).
xs: **Art. 30(1A)** was added by the **44th Amendment** — option **(2)**.
It ensures that removing the **right to property** does not affect minorities' right to establish institutions, with **compensation** on acquisition.
xa: The **7th Amendment (1956)** inserted Arts **350A** and **350B**.
The **93rd Amendment** inserted Art. **15(5)** after **P.A. Inamdar**.

n76da84480c6.s: Articles 350A and 350B were inserted by the:
n76da84480c6.x: The 7th Amendment, 1956, linked to States reorganisation, inserted Articles 350A and 350B.
xa: The office was set up in **1957**; HQ **Prayagraj (Allahabad)**.
**350A:** instruction in the **mother tongue at the primary stage**.

n92af9232db9.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes religious and linguistic minorities in India?
o: Religious minorities are associated with the National Commission for Minorities, while linguistic minorities are considered State-wise and linked with the Article 350B officer
Religious minorities are identified only by States, while linguistic minorities are identified by the Union
Both categories are determined exclusively on an all-India basis
Neither category is recognised under the Constitution
n92af9232db9.x: Religious minorities are dealt with through the National Commission for Minorities and the Ministry of Minority Affairs. Linguistic minorities are identified State-wise, with the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B.
n92af9232db9.tq: Split the comparison by authority and territorial basis.
xs: **Religious minorities** go with the **NCM**; **linguistic minorities** are identified **State-wise** and linked with the **Art. 350B** officer — option **(1)**.
Linguistic minorities are **not** notified under the NCM Act.
xa: Both religious and linguistic minorities are recognised in the Constitution.
Six notified religious minorities ≈ **19%** of India's population.

n47590b068af.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the National Commission for Minorities?
o: Conducting elections to minority educational institutions
Looking into specific complaints relating to deprivation of minority safeguards
Monitoring constitutional and legal safeguards for minorities
n47590b068af.x: The Commission evaluates development, monitors safeguards, examines complaints and recommends measures; conducting elections to minority educational institutions is not one of its stated functions.
n47590b068af.tq: Find the option that assigns an unrelated administrative function to the Commission.
xs: **Conducting elections to minority educational institutions** is NOT an NCM function — option **(1)**.
NCM functions: evaluate minorities' **development**, **monitor constitutional and legal safeguards**, look into **specific complaints**, recommend measures, commission studies.
xa: It has **powers of a civil court** while inquiring.
⚠ Minority status of institutions is decided by the **NCMEI**, not the NCM.

n1a6dbaef0d4.s: While inquiring into complaints, the National Commission for Minorities has powers similar to those of a:
n1a6dbaef0d4.x: The NCM has civil-court-like powers such as summoning witnesses and calling for records; it cannot impose criminal sentences.
xa: ⚠ APPCA 2026 / older notes say "no automatic civil-court powers"; follow the Act.
The **NCMEI** also has **civil court powers**.

nad38df64b41.s: The National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions was established under an Act of:
nad38df64b41.x: The NCMEI is associated with the 2004 Act; statutory State Minority Commissions exist in 19 States/UTs, including Andhra Pradesh.
xa: ⚠ The APPSC 2016 key said **18**; older notes **15**.
Others include **Telangana, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra**.

nece167263bd.s: The Sachar Committee, set up in 2005 and chaired by Justice Rajinder Sachar, submitted its report in:
nece167263bd.x: The Sachar Committee was set up by the Prime Minister in 2005 and submitted its report in November 2006.
xa: Mandate: the **social, economic and educational status of Muslims**.
Proposals: **Equal Opportunity Commission**, **National Data Bank**, **Assessment and Monitoring Authority**.
⚠ **2006** = Sachar report; **2007** = Ranganath Misra; **2013-14** = Kundu.

nee61d2ecbac.s: The PM's New 15 Point Programme for the Welfare of Minorities was introduced in:
nee61d2ecbac.x: The programme, introduced in 2006, covers education, jobs, living conditions, prevention of communal violence and earmarked outlays.
xa: **Review committees** monitor it.
The **Ministry of Minority Affairs** also dates from **2006**.

n2591cff8610.s: Under the PM's New 15 Point Programme, about what share of targets and outlays in selected schemes is earmarked for minorities?
n2591cff8610.x: The programme earmarks about 15 percent of targets and outlays in selected schemes, aims to prevent communal riots and is monitored by review committees.
xa: The programme dates from **2006**.
⚠ The **Ranganath Misra** **15%** figure is a reservation proposal, not this earmarking.

n1a8a33cac6e.s: What percentage of PM-YASASVI slots is earmarked for girls?
n1a8a33cac6e.x: PM-YASASVI reserves 30 percent of slots for girls and follows a 60:40 cost-sharing ratio.
xa: Pre-matric (Class IX-X) = **Rs 4,000**.
**SHREYAS** funds **8,571** SC students at IITs and IIMs.

nf4037eaec59.s: The National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) functions under the:
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
nf4037eaec59.x: NBCFDC (1992) is under MoSJE; NMDFC is under the Ministry of Minority Affairs, and both lend through State Channelising Agencies.
xa: NBCFDC schemes: **New Swarnima** (women), **Saksham** (young professionals).
Comparable bodies: **NSFDC** (1989, SCs), **NSTFDC** (2001, STs).

n01a7f0f63ff.s: The NBCFDC's New Swarnima scheme is meant for:
n01a7f0f63ff.x: New Swarnima is for women and Saksham for young professionals; Virasat loans for artisans are associated with NMDFC.
xa: NBCFDC (**1992**, MoSJE) lends through **State Channelising Agencies**.
NMDFC also gives **education loans** and **micro-finance**.

n2376a7423f1.s: Under PM Vishwakarma, the credit support is structured as:
o: Rs 1 lakh followed by Rs 5 lakh without any interest
Rs 1 lakh followed by Rs 2 lakh at 5 percent interest
Rs 15,000 followed by Rs 2 lakh at 12 percent interest
Rs 2 lakh followed by Rs 1 lakh at 10 percent interest
n2376a7423f1.x: The scheme provides collateral-free credit of Rs 1 lakh initially and an additional Rs 2 lakh, with the credit carrying a 5 percent interest rate.
n2376a7423f1.tq: Read the staged amount and interest rate together to avoid reversing the figures.
xs: Credit is collateral-free **Rs 1 lakh** followed by **Rs 2 lakh** at **5%** interest — option **(2)**.
⚠ **Rs 15,000** is the **toolkit** incentive, not a loan.
xa: Launched **17 Sept 2023** for **18 trades**.
Training includes a **stipend**.

nce1507edb61.s: The nodal ministry for PM Vishwakarma is the:
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
nce1507edb61.x: MSME is the nodal ministry; MSDE and the Department of Financial Services are also involved in implementation.
xa: Over **1 crore** artisans registered.
Registration through **CSCs**.

na102af2ad77.s: The Idate Commission found about how many Denotified Tribes (DNTs) that had never been classified?
na102af2ad77.x: About 267-268 DNTs had never been classified, while about 1,200 were already in SC, ST or OBC lists.
xa: The first DNT commission was **Renke** (**2008**).
**SEED** (**2022**) is the DNT welfare scheme.

nbb06400c0ef.s: Andhra Pradesh's G.O. 1065 (August 2026) provides what BC reservation in urban local body polls?
nbb06400c0ef.x: G.O. 1065 gives 33.33% BC reservation in ULB polls; AP's 138 BC communities are in Groups A-E.
xa: BCs = **43.17%** of AP's population.
A **Swarnakara** Welfare and Development Corporation has been set up.

nba7a8a0309b.s: Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act has been criticised because it gives the Centre:
o: exclusive power to appoint State minority commissions
power to amend the Constitution without Parliament
nba7a8a0309b.x: Section 2(c) has been criticised as giving the Centre ‘unbridled power’ to notify minorities, raising concerns in the context of T.M.A. Pai.
nba7a8a0309b.tq: Match the statutory provision with the specific constitutional criticism rather than a broader unrelated power.
xs: Critics say **Section 2(c)** gives the Centre **"unbridled power"** to **notify minorities** — option **(1)**.
It sits uneasily with **T.M.A. Pai (2002)**, which made the **State** the unit for minority status.
xa: The NCM Act does not define minority; a minority = any community **notified by the Central Government**.
States may notify their own minorities — **Jains** in **11 States** before 2014.

n376dc9eaae7.s: The National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC) was established in:
n376dc9eaae7.x: NSFDC came in 1989 for SCs, NBCFDC in 1992 for Backward Classes and NSTFDC in 2001 for STs; NMDFC serves minorities.
xa: NBCFDC is under **MoSJE**; NMDFC is a **Section 8 company** under **MoMA**.
Both NBCFDC and NMDFC lend through **State Channelising Agencies**.

n1d654945506.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the decision in P.A. Inamdar (2005)?
o: A seven-judge Bench held that the State could impose its quota in unaided institutions without limitation.
A seven-judge Bench held that there could be no State quota or reservation in unaided institutions, contributing to the subsequent 93rd Amendment framework.
An 11-judge Bench abolished the distinction between aided and unaided institutions.
The Court held that minority status must be determined at the national level.
n1d654945506.x: P.A. Inamdar was decided by a seven-judge Bench and held that the State could not impose its quota or reservation in unaided institutions. The decision was followed by the constitutional development associated with Article 15(5) through the 93rd Amendment.
n1d654945506.tq: Combine bench strength, holding and constitutional consequence without confusing it with T.M.A. Pai.
xs: **P.A. Inamdar (2005)**, a **7-judge** bench, held the State cannot impose **reservation quotas** on **unaided** institutions, minority or non-minority — option **(2)**.
This led to Art. **15(5)** through the **93rd Amendment**.
xa: ⚠ **T.M.A. Pai (2002)** was the **11-judge** bench making the **State** the unit for minority status.
**St. Stephen's (1992)** concerned **aided** minority colleges.

n9323dca0af3.s: The decision in Bal Patil v. Union of India (2005) is associated with which of the following?
o: Directing the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority
Imposing reservation quotas on unaided minority institutions
Declaring that minority status must be determined nationally
Declining to direct the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority and leaving the matter to the States
n9323dca0af3.x: The Court declined to direct the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority, leaving the matter to the States and cautioning against the multiplication of minority claims.
n9323dca0af3.tq: Discriminate between a judicial direction and a refusal to issue that direction.
xs: **Bal Patil v Union of India (2005)** **declined to direct the Centre** to notify **Jains** as a national minority, leaving it to the **States** — option **(4)**.
It also warned against **multiplying minority claims**.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** UPSC notes describe it as a linguistic-institutions case — inaccurate.
The Centre later notified **Jains** on **27 January 2014**.

nindian-society-42-14.s: The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee highlighted severe under-representation of Muslims in which areas?
nindian-society-42-14.x: The Sachar Committee found Muslims badly under-represented in public jobs and higher education, against their share of the population.
n: The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee highlighted severe under-representation of Muslims in public employment. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee highlighted severe under-representation of Muslims in higher education. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee concerned minorities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee assessed the educational status of the Muslim community in India. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xs: The **Sachar Committee** found **severe under-representation** of Muslims in **public employment** and **higher education** — option **(1)**.
It assessed the **socio-economic** and **educational status** of the **Muslim community**.
xa: It proposed an **Equal Opportunity Commission**, **National Data Bank** and **Diversity Index**.
**Ajlafs** need attention like Hindu OBCs; **Arzals** (Dalit Muslims) are the most deprived.
⚠ **Ajlaf** ≈ OBC; **Arzal** ≈ SC; **Ashraf** = upper.

nee0f554912b.s: The Chairperson and members of the National Commission for Minorities are appointed by the:
nee0f554912b.x: NCM members are appointed by the Central Government, not the President; the statutory NCM dates from the 1992 Act, first constituted in 1993.
xa: The NCM is **statutory, not constitutional**, under the **Ministry of Minority Affairs**.
⚠ GS 2018 key: appointed by the **Union Government**.

nb4e49b60844.s: The Minorities Commission became a statutory body under the NCM Act in:
nb4e49b60844.x: The non-statutory Commission came in 1978, the NCM Act in 1992, the first statutory Commission in 1993 and the Vice-Chairperson in 1995.
xa: After 1995 the strength became **7**.
⚠ **1993** is also the year the first **five** communities were notified.

nc3071f1c831.s: Which commission was the first to examine the condition of Denotified Tribes among the commissions mentioned below?
nc3071f1c831.x: The Renke Commission, whose report was submitted in 2008, was the first such commission mentioned for Denotified Tribes.
nc3071f1c831.tq: Use the ‘first’ marker to distinguish the earlier Renke Commission from the later Idate Commission.
xs: The **Renke Commission** (report **2008**) was the **first** DNT commission — option **(3)**.
The **Idate Commission** came later (**2014-17**); **J.B. Koshy** concerned **Christian minorities** in Kerala; **Sachar** concerned **Muslims**.
xa: Idate: about **1,200** DNTs already in SC/ST/OBC lists; **267-268** never classified.
DNTs were branded under the **Criminal Tribes Act 1871**.

nindian-society-1-78.s: In which year was the first National Foundation for Communal Harmony established?
nindian-society-1-78.x: The National Foundation for Communal Harmony was set up in 1992. 1983 is the 15-Point Programme and 2005 the Sachar Committee.
nindian-society-1-78.tq: Recall the minority firsts by year.
xs: The **National Foundation for Communal Harmony** was first established in **1992** — option **(3)**.
**1983** is the first **15-Point Programme**; **2005** is the **Sachar Committee**.
xa: **National Integration Council**: **1961**; **Communal Award**: **1932**.

n7ded9b339b5.s: The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was established in:
n7ded9b339b5.x: The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was set up in 1957.
n7ded9b339b5.tq: Distinguish the office’s establishment year from the constitutional amendment year.
xs: The office of the **Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities** was set up in **1957** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **1956** is the **7th Amendment** that inserted Art. **350B**; the office followed in 1957.
xa: HQ: **Prayagraj (Allahabad)**.
**1964** is the year of the statutory **Central Waqf Council**.

nf407145d8da.s: Which of the following was NOT a proposal associated with the Sachar Committee?
nf407145d8da.x: The Sachar Committee proposed an Equal Opportunity Commission, National Data Bank and Assessment and Monitoring Authority. A National Linguistic Minorities Commission was not listed among its proposals.
nf407145d8da.tq: Eliminate the option belonging to a different institutional theme.
xs: A **National Linguistic Minorities Commission** was NOT a Sachar proposal — option **(4)**.
Sachar proposed an **Equal Opportunity Commission**, a **National Data Bank** and an **Assessment and Monitoring Authority**.
xa: It also recommended a **Diversity Index**.
The **Kundu Committee** (**2013-14**) repeated the call for an Equal Opportunity Commission and anti-discrimination law.

nbe1049b5a97.s: The Ranganath Misra Commission was associated with which of the following recommendations?
o: Replacement of all State languages by Hindi
A 15% reservation and delinking Scheduled Caste status from religion
Creation of the National Data Bank for census purposes only
nbe1049b5a97.x: The National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities, chaired by Justice Ranganath Misra, suggested a 15% quota for minorities and delinking SC status from religion.
nbe1049b5a97.tq: Match the commission with its distinctive recommendation rather than its general subject.
xs: The **Ranganath Misra Commission** suggested a **15%** reservation for minorities and **delinking SC status from religion** — option **(3)**.
It sought concrete steps for socially and economically backward sections among religious and linguistic minorities.
xa: It reported in **2007**.
The **National Data Bank** was a **Sachar** proposal.

nindian-society-11-19.s: The Ranganath Misra Commission was established in which year?
nindian-society-11-19.x: The Ranganath Misra Commission on religious and linguistic minorities was set up in 2004. The Sachar Committee followed in 2005.
nindian-society-11-19.tq: Arrange the minority bodies in time order.
xs: The **Ranganath Misra Commission** was established in **2004** — option **(3)**.
It is the **National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities**; ⚠ some notes say **constituted 2007** (its report year).
xa: It recommended **15%** reservation for minorities, **10%** for Muslims.
It urged **delinking SC status from religion**.
The **Sachar Committee** followed in **2005**.

n89a3b2ec410.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the five schemes merged into PM VIKAS?
n89a3b2ec410.x: PM VIKAS merges Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni and Nai Manzil. PMJVK is not one of the five merged schemes.
