n89a3b2ec410.tq: Find the area-based infrastructure scheme that does not belong to the merged skill and heritage package.
xs: **PM Jan Vikas Karyakram** is NOT among the five merged into PM VIKAS — option **(1)**.
PM VIKAS merges **Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni, Nai Manzil**.
xa: ⚠ **PM VIKAS** = Central Sector; **PMJVK** = Centrally Sponsored.
Critics say minority schemes lost visibility after the merger.

n22969031336.s: Which one of the following correctly describes PMJVK?
o: It is a Central Sector Scheme limited to minority students pursuing higher education.
It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for area development in minority concentration areas.
It is a constitutional programme implemented by the Election Commission.
It is a State scheme restricted to urban minority households.
n22969031336.x: PMJVK is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme aimed at area development in minority concentration areas.
n22969031336.tq: Identify the scheme from its funding pattern and broad area-development objective.
xs: **PMJVK** is a **Centrally Sponsored** infrastructure scheme for **minority-concentration areas** — option **(2)**.
It benefits **all residents**, not just minority students or urban households.
xa: Restructured in **May 2018** from **MSDP (2008-09)**.
**80%** to education, health and skills; **33-40%** for women.

nc3d3b17d6b6.x: PM Vishwakarma is intended for artisans and craftspeople engaged in 18 traditional trades. It is not a fishermen's scheme.
nc3d3b17d6b6.tq: Discriminate between the target group and the tempting but incorrect fishermen association.
xs: **PM Vishwakarma** targets **artisans and craftspeople** in **18 trades** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **Trap:** it is **not a fishermen's scheme** (APPSC G2 2023).
xa: Toolkit incentive: **Rs 15,000**.
Credit: collateral-free **Rs 1 lakh + Rs 2 lakh** at **5%**.

nd5b5700e8c8.s: PM VIKAS, a Central Sector scheme of 2022 merging five minority schemes, stands for:
o: Pradhan Mantri Vikas Aur Kaushal Samvardhan
Pradhan Mantri Virasat Aur Kala Sanrakshan
nd5b5700e8c8.x: PM VIKAS means Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan; it merges five schemes and runs until 2025-26.
xa: Merged: **Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni, Nai Manzil**.
About **9 lakh** beneficiaries; **33%** of skilling seats for women; linked to **NMDFC** loans.

nf5a8ac84f8d.s: The SEED scheme, launched in 2022, has a stated outlay of:
nf5a8ac84f8d.x: SEED (2022) has an outlay of Rs 200 crore and covers coaching, health insurance, livelihoods and housing for incomes below Rs 2.5 lakh.
xa: Only **Rs 69.3 crore** spent in five years.
Reason: States do not issue **DNT certificates**.

n9179e707223.s: The Wakf (Amendment) Act, 2013 enabled which body to direct State Waqf Boards?
n9179e707223.x: The 2013 amendment let the Central Waqf Council direct State Boards and barred sale, gift, mortgage, exchange and transfer of waqf property.
xa: The 2025 law put all waqf properties on a **central portal within 6 months**.

n51aae9249f2.s: Under the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, all waqf properties were to be placed on a central portal within:
n51aae9249f2.x: The 2025 amendment required waqf properties on a central portal within six months; the UMEED portal was launched in June 2025.
xa: The **UMEED** portal was launched in **June 2025**.
⚠ The **SC (Sep 2025)** capped non-Muslims at **3** in State Boards and **4** in the Central Council.

neab78c0ad31.s: The Central Waqf Council is best described as:
o: A temporary executive committee established in 1995 to conduct elections
A statutory body established in 1964 to advise the Centre on State Waqf Boards
A judicial body established in 2025 to decide all land disputes
A constitutional body established in 1950 to supervise courts
neab78c0ad31.x: The Central Waqf Council is a statutory body established in 1964. Its principal role is to advise the Central Government on State Waqf Boards.
neab78c0ad31.tq: Distinguish a statutory advisory body from constitutional and judicial bodies.
xs: The **Central Waqf Council** is a **statutory** body of **1964** that **advises the Centre on State Waqf Boards** — option **(2)**.
It was set up under Section 8A of the **1954** Act, now **Section 9(1)** of the **Waqf Act 1995**.
xa: Since **2013**, it can **direct** State Boards.
The 2025 law allows **non-Muslim** members; SC cap = **4** in the Central Council.

na0610e99016.s: Urdu was made the second official language of Andhra Pradesh under which law?
na0610e99016.x: Urdu is AP's second official language under the AP Official Language (Amendment) Act, 2022. The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 bifurcated the State; the Official Languages Act, 1963 deals with the Union's official languages; the 7th Amendment, 1956 inserted Articles 350A and 350B.
na0610e99016.tq: Urdu = AP second official language, 2022 amendment.
xs: **Urdu** is AP's **second official language** under the **AP Official Language (Amendment) Act, 2022** — option **(1)**.
The **7th Amendment (1956)** instead inserted Arts **350A** and **350B**.
xa: AP runs **Urdu-Ghar-cum-Shadikhanas** and **36** computer training centres across **26** districts.
AP has **6 pre-matric and 10 post-matric** minority hostels.

nf0fd42b840c.s: Which Muslim group was identified as requiring attention similar to that given to Hindu Other Backward Classes?
o: All Muslim groups equally under the same classification
nf0fd42b840c.x: The Ajlaf, described as backward Muslims or commoners and lower-caste converts, were identified as requiring attention similar to Hindu OBCs.
nf0fd42b840c.tq: Separate Ajlaf from Arzal by matching the group with the specific policy concern.
xs: The **Ajlaf** (backward Muslims — commoners/lower-caste converts) need attention similar to **Hindu OBCs** — option **(1)**.
The **Ashraf** are upper/claimed foreign origin; the **Arzal** are Dalit converts, the **most deprived**.
xa: ⚠ **Ajlaf** ≈ OBC; **Arzal** ≈ SC.
This classification was asked in **APPSC G2 2024**.

nb6ccc455ba6.s: PM Jan Vikas Karyakram was restructured from which earlier programme?
nb6ccc455ba6.x: PMJVK was restructured from the Multi-sectoral Development Programme (MSDP), which dates from 2008-09.
nb6ccc455ba6.tq: Use the predecessor-successor relationship to identify the correct programme.
xs: **PMJVK** was restructured in **May 2018** from the **Multi-sectoral Development Programme (MSDP)** of **2008-09** — option **(1)**.
The others are MoMA skilling, leadership and coaching schemes.
xa: It covers **870** minority concentration blocks + **321** towns, now all districts incl. **112 Aspirational Districts**.
**80%** of funds go to education, health and skills.

nindian-society-37-19.s: The PM-YASASVI Portal is meant for scholarship application and disbursement for which groups?
o: OBC, EBC and nomadic tribe students
nindian-society-37-19.x: The PM-YASASVI portal handles scholarship applications and payments for OBC, EBC and denotified/nomadic tribe students.
n: The SHRESHTA Portal covers private residential schools for SC students. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-YASASVI Portal is a digital platform for OBC, EBC, and nomadic-tribe students. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The National Testing Agency is the nodal agency for the PM-YASASVI Portal. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-YASASVI Portal provides a centralized scholarship application system. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-YASASVI Portal provides a scholarship disbursement system. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-YASASVI Portal serves OBC students. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-YASASVI Portal serves EBC students. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-YASASVI Portal serves nomadic-tribe students. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PMMVY Soft Portal serves pregnant mothers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PMMVY Soft Portal serves lactating mothers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The UDID Portal is a digital platform for persons with disabilities (PwDs). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
xs: The **PM-YASASVI Portal** handles scholarships for **OBC**, **EBC** and **nomadic-tribe students** — option **(1)**.
It is a **centralized scholarship application** and **disbursement system** run by the **National Testing Agency**.
xa: PM-YASASVI (**2021**, MoSJE): family income below **Rs 2.5 lakh**; cost shared **60:40**.
Pre-matric award: **Rs 4,000**; **30%** of slots for girls.
**SHREYAS** funds **8,571** SC students at IITs and IIMs.

n2abac1f3372.s: The e-Shram portal provides every registered unorganised worker with a 12-digit:
n2abac1f3372.x: e-Shram, India's first Aadhaar-seeded national database of unorganised workers, gives each worker a 12-digit UAN.
xa: Registrations: **over 31.78 crore** (July 2026).
**One-Stop Solution (2024)** links **15** central schemes.

n2f2ee30a73d.s: The Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008 has subsequently been merged into the:
n2f2ee30a73d.x: The Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008 was merged into the Code on Social Security, 2020.
n2f2ee30a73d.tq: Match the earlier statute with the Labour Code that subsumed it.
xs: The 2008 Act was **merged into the Code on Social Security, 2020** — option **(3)**.
The **Industrial Relations Code** deals with layoffs, strikes and fixed-term employment instead.
xa: The Code on Social Security is the first law to recognise **aggregators**, **gig** and **platform workers**.
It provides **National and State Social Security Boards**.

n7a9515fe888.s: Under the Social Security framework, gig workers can register from the age of:
n7a9515fe888.x: Gig workers can register from 16, with National and State Social Security Boards; registration does not confer employee status or a minimum wage.
xa: **Rajasthan** has a Gig Workers Act (**2023**); **Karnataka** (Bill **2024**) and **Telangana** proposed.
NITI estimate: **1.43 crore** gig workers (2025-26).

n9d1548615bb.s: Under the Industrial Relations Code, fixed-term workers become eligible for gratuity after:
n9d1548615bb.x: Fixed-term workers get the same wages and benefits as permanent workers and gratuity after one year.
xa: Layoff permission threshold: **300** workers.
Contract labour threshold: **50** workers.

nd0a9826f7b6.s: A trade union proposes to commence a strike five days after giving notice. Under the Industrial Relations Code, this proposal is:
o: Not permissible only when the establishment has more than 500 workers
Permissible if the establishment has fewer than 300 workers
Not permissible because a strike cannot occur within 14 days of giving notice
Permissible because notice has been given in writing
nd0a9826f7b6.x: A strike cannot be held within 14 days of giving notice. The Code also prohibits a strike without notice within the preceding 60 days before striking.
nd0a9826f7b6.tq: Apply the statutory time restriction to the facts of the situation.
xs: A strike **cannot occur within 14 days** of giving notice — so five days is **not permissible**, option **(3)**.
Nor can there be a strike without notice **within 60 days** before striking.
xa: Unions say this weakens **Article 19(1)(c)**.
The rule applies regardless of the **300**-worker threshold, which is for layoffs.

nf50c356e3a0.s: Which one of the following is NOT listed among the Schedule I schemes of the Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008?
nf50c356e3a0.x: Schedule I includes the National Family Benefit Scheme, Janani Suraksha Yojana and RSBY, among others. Atal Pension Yojana is not included in the listed Schedule I schemes.
nf50c356e3a0.tq: Find the scheme outside the statutory list rather than selecting a familiar welfare scheme.
xs: **Atal Pension Yojana** is NOT in Schedule I of the 2008 Act — option **(4)**.
Schedule I lists **IGNOAPS, National Family Benefit Scheme, Janani Suraksha Yojana, Janashree Bima Yojana, Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana, RSBY**, plus schemes for weavers, artisans, fishermen.
xa: APY came in **2015**, replacing **Swavalamban**.
The 2008 Act set up a **National Social Security Board**.

n63b0b98dafb.s: The Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY), launched in 2008 for BPL families, provided hospitalisation cover of:
n63b0b98dafb.x: RSBY (2008) gave BPL families ₹30,000 hospitalisation cover and was later subsumed in AB-PMJAY.
xa: It is listed in **Schedule I** of the **2008 Act**.
⚠ **Ashraya Bima** (**2001**) = job-loss; **Swavalamban** (**2010**) = NPS-Lite.

n705aa959c2d.s: The Swavalamban scheme for unorganised workers joining NPS-Lite was replaced in 2015 by:
n705aa959c2d.x: Swavalamban (2010) was replaced by the Atal Pension Yojana in 2015; Ashraya Bima Yojana (2001, LIC) was for workers who lost jobs.
xa: APY gives a guaranteed **₹1,000-5,000/month** from **60**, run by **PFRDA**.
Swavalamban is distinct from **PM-SYM** (**March 2019**), which pays **₹3,000/month** from **60**.

n6e4156892ec.s: The entry age for PM-SYM, which assures ₹3,000 a month from age 60, is:
n6e4156892ec.x: PM-SYM entry age is 18-40 (18-50 is PMJJBY); it covers unorganised workers earning up to ₹15,000 a month.
xa: Contribution: **₹55-200/month** by entry age; launched **March 2019**.
Enrolment: **over 54 lakh** (Aug 2026), **53.1%** women.

n05138a007e1.s: The Atal Pension Yojana (2015) is administered by:
n05138a007e1.x: APY gives a guaranteed pension of ₹1,000–₹5,000 from age 60 and is run by PFRDA.
xa: Entry age: **18-40**.
It replaced **Swavalamban** (**2010**).

nfc5a0ea6eaf.s: Which of the following is NOT a condition that excludes a person from PM-SYM and NPS-Traders eligibility?
o: Being a worker in the unorganised sector
nfc5a0ea6eaf.x: Membership of EPFO, ESIC or government-funded NPS, and being an income-tax payer, excludes eligibility. Being an unorganised-sector worker is not an exclusion; PM-SYM is specifically intended for such workers.
nfc5a0ea6eaf.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the list of exclusion conditions.
xs: **Being an unorganised-sector worker** is NOT an exclusion — option **(3)** — PM-SYM is meant for them.
Excluded: members of **EPFO, ESIC** or government-funded **NPS**, and **income-tax payers**.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** "NPS members are also eligible" is **wrong**.
PM-SYM is for workers earning **≤ ₹15,000/month**.

nd7232ce1881.s: Which one of the following persons is eligible for registration on the e-Shram portal?
o: A 15-year-old unorganised worker who is not an income-tax payer
A 25-year-old unorganised worker who is an income-tax payer
A 40-year-old unorganised worker who is not an income-tax payer and is not covered by EPFO or ESIC
A 62-year-old unorganised worker who is not covered by any social-security scheme
nd7232ce1881.x: Eligibility covers unorganised workers aged 16 to 59 who are not income-tax payers and are not members of EPFO or ESIC.
nd7232ce1881.tq: Apply all eligibility conditions together rather than relying on age alone.
xs: The **40-year-old** unorganised worker who is **not an income-tax payer** and **not in EPFO/ESIC** is eligible — option **(3)**.
Eligibility: ages **16-59**, so **15** and **62** are out; **income-tax payers** are excluded.
xa: ⚠ e-Shram age = **16-59**; gig registration under the Code = from **age 16**.
Registration gives a **12-digit UAN**.

n94f0ed06c0d.s: NCEUS was set up in 2004 under the chairmanship of:
n94f0ed06c0d.x: The National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector was set up in 2004 and chaired by Arjun Sengupta.
xs: **NCEUS** was set up in **2004** under **Arjun Sengupta** — option **(3)**.
It studied enterprises in the **unorganised sector**.
xa: Its **2007** report found about **77%** of Indians living on under **₹20 a day**.
Today **over 90%** of India's ~600 million workers are informal.

nbe1543de996.s: Which of the following correctly represents the informal workforce situation described for India?
o: Exactly 77% of the total workforce is informal.
Over 90% of the workforce is employed only in the organised sector.
Less than 50% of roughly 600 million workers are informal.
Over 90% of roughly 600 million workers are informal.
nbe1543de996.x: Over 90% of India's roughly 600 million workers are informal. This is distinct from the 77% figure in the NCEUS poverty estimate.
nbe1543de996.tq: Separate the informal-workforce percentage from the NCEUS poverty percentage.
xs: **Over 90%** of India's ~**600 million** workers are **informal** — option **(4)**.
⚠ **77%** is the NCEUS figure for people living on under **₹20 a day**, not the informal share.
xa: Total workforce: **61.6 crore** (PLFS 2025).
**e-Shram** registrations: **over 31.78 crore** (July 2026).

n403d8f5348f.s: At the district level, which body is responsible for identifying and releasing bonded labourers under the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976?
n403d8f5348f.x: District-level Vigilance Committees are responsible for identifying and releasing bonded labourers under the 1976 Act.
n403d8f5348f.tq: Identify the authority assigned the specific enforcement function.
xs: District-level **Vigilance Committees** identify and release bonded labourers — option **(4)**.
They work under the **Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976**.
xa: The Act gives effect to **Article 23**, which bans **begar** and forced labour.
A **Central Sector Scheme** for rehabilitation of bonded labourers came in **2016**.

nf35e099c44c.s: A complaint is not decided within 21 days of filing. Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, what is the consequence mentioned in the legislation?
o: It is deemed to have been dismissed
It is automatically transferred to the National Commission
It is deemed to have been admitted
nf35e099c44c.x: A complaint not decided within 21 days is deemed to have been admitted.
nf35e099c44c.tq: Use the precise statutory time limit and distinguish admission from dismissal.
xs: A complaint not decided within **21 days** is **deemed admitted** — option **(3)**.
It is not dismissed or transferred.
xa: Complaints may be filed where the complainant **lives or works**.
⚠ The e-commerce grievance officer must acknowledge in **48 hours** and redress in **one month**.

n1e9f3c7e201.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six consumer rights recognised under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
n1e9f3c7e201.x: The six rights include safety, information, choice, hearing, redressal and consumer awareness. A right to private ownership is not included in this list.
n1e9f3c7e201.tq: Find the odd legal entitlement among the recognised consumer rights.
xs: The **right to private ownership** is NOT one of the six consumer rights — option **(3)**.
The six: **safety**, be **informed**, **choose**, be **heard**, **seek redressal**, **consumer awareness**.
xa: Consumers may get **food samples tested** (UPSC 2012 key).
A **legal heir** of a deceased consumer may file a complaint.

n5cece6ae0bc.s: Which one of the following persons would generally be treated as a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
o: A person purchasing services for commercial exploitation
A person purchasing goods solely for a large-scale business activity
A person purchasing goods for resale
A person making an online purchase for personal use
n5cece6ae0bc.x: The definition includes online and electronic purchases for personal use. A person buying for resale or commercial use is generally excluded.
n5cece6ae0bc.tq: Apply the personal-use and commercial-purpose distinction to a factual situation.
xs: A person making an **online purchase** for **personal use** is a consumer — option **(4)**.
The definition **includes online and electronic purchases**; a buyer for **resale/commercial use** is not a consumer.
xa: **"Advertisement"** includes electronic media, internet and websites.
A **legal heir** of a deceased consumer may file a complaint.

n4e44aad7b8d.s: Which of the following bodies was introduced by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
n4e44aad7b8d.x: The 2019 Act introduced the CCPA, along with product liability, e-commerce rules and penalties for adulterated goods; the NCDRC dates from 1988.
xa: It also brought **e-filing** and **videoconference** hearings.
**Mediation** cells are attached to the Commissions.

n9f39214c1aa.s: The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission was set up in:
n9f39214c1aa.x: The NCDRC was set up in 1988; its original orders are appealable to the Supreme Court within 30 days.
xa: There are over **35** State and **600+** District Commissions.
**Aug 2026:** the SC sought an NCDRC report on pendency — **5.7 lakh** cases.

n036e648bbee.s: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, the District, State and National Commissions were called:
n036e648bbee.x: They were Consumer Forums under the 1986 Act; they are quasi-judicial bodies, not ordinary civil courts under the CPC.
xa: District → State appeal: **45 days**; State → National: **30 days**.
**NCDRC** was set up in **1988**.

n04b4b9cd2f2.s: An appeal against an order of a State Consumer Commission lies to the National Commission within:
n04b4b9cd2f2.x: State to National is within 30 days; District to State is within 45 days and National to Supreme Court within 30 days.
xa: ⚠ Appeal days: **45** only for District → State; both others **30**.
No appeal lies against a **mediated settlement**.

n2cdfec7232f.s: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, consumer mediation cells are attached to:
n2cdfec7232f.x: Mediation cells are attached to the District, State and National Consumer Commissions, not High Courts.
xa: **No appeal** lies against a mediated settlement.
Mediation was introduced by **CPA 2019**.

nb620a400c78.s: The Central Consumer Protection Authority came into existence on:
nb620a400c78.x: The CCPA came into existence on 24 July 2020; 24 December is National Consumer Day.
xa: **24 December** is National Consumer Day.
CCPA fined **Meta ₹10 lakh** over walkie-talkie listings.

n4369bfae700.s: Which body can inquire into violations of consumer rights, file class-action complaints and impose penalties?
n4369bfae700.x: The CCPA can inquire into violations, order recalls and refunds, file class-action complaints and impose penalties.
xa: Misleading ad penalty (**Section 21**): up to **₹10 lakh**; repeat **₹50 lakh**.
Criticism: platforms dispute **CCPA** jurisdiction.

nc07ff16ecb4.s: Under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, the grievance officer of an e-commerce entity must acknowledge a consumer complaint and redress it within:
nc07ff16ecb4.x: The Rules require acknowledgement within 48 hours and redressal within one month. 24 hours/15 days, 48 hours/21 days and 72 hours/one month each get at least one period wrong (21 days is the deemed-admission period of Consumer Commissions).
nc07ff16ecb4.tq: 48 hours to acknowledge, one month to redress.
xs: The grievance officer must **acknowledge** within **48 hours** and **redress** within **one month** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **21 days** is the deemed-admission period for Consumer Commissions, not this.
xa: The 2026 rules require platforms to join **NCH convergence**.
The Rules were notified under **CPA 2019**.

nc2637ffd4d8.s: The Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 specified how many dark patterns?
nc2637ffd4d8.x: The 2023 Guidelines specified 13 dark patterns, including false urgency and basket sneaking.
nc2637ffd4d8.tq: Test the exact numerical figure associated with the Guidelines.
xs: The **Dark Patterns Guidelines, 2023** specify **13** dark patterns — option **(3)**.
Examples: **false urgency**, **basket sneaking**.
xa: The 2026 rules require an **annual self-audit** and a displayed **compliance certificate**.
The Guidelines were issued under the **E-Commerce** framework of **CPA 2019**.

n30b5a8d6c88.s: The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026 were gazetted on 9 September 2026 and became effective on:
n30b5a8d6c88.x: The 2026 Amendment Rules were gazetted on 9 September 2026 and are effective from 1 January 2027.
n30b5a8d6c88.tq: Distinguish the gazette date from the date of commencement.
xs: The **2026 Amendment Rules** were gazetted **9 Sep 2026** and are effective **1 January 2027** — option **(3)**.
**24 December** is National Consumer Day; **15 March** is World Consumer Rights Day.
xa: They require disclosure of **importer and country of origin**.
Prior price for discounts = **lowest in the preceding 30 days**.

n554395258f7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026?
o: The prior price shown with a discount must be the lowest price in the preceding 30 days
E-commerce entities must join the National Consumer Helpline convergence process
Search results must not be manipulated
Sponsored listings need not be disclosed if the product is offered at a reduced price
n554395258f7.x: Sponsored listings must be clearly disclosed; there is no reduced-price exception.
xa: Dark patterns: **annual self-audit** + compliance certificate.
Platforms must also disclose **importer and country of origin**.

n4ec1dd05a5e.s: The e-Daakhil facility for online filing has been merged into which portal?
n4ec1dd05a5e.x: The e-Daakhil online filing facility has been merged into the e-Jagriti portal.
n4ec1dd05a5e.tq: Discriminate between similarly named digital public-service portals.
xs: **e-Daakhil** online filing is now merged into the **e-Jagriti** portal — option **(1)**.
CPA 2019 allows **e-filing** and **videoconference** hearings.
xa: ⚠ **e-Jagriti** = portal; **"Jagriti"** = mascot of **Jago Grahak Jago**.
**National Consumer Helpline**: toll-free **1915**.

n42f04a605e9.s: The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has been replaced by which of the following laws?
n42f04a605e9.x: The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was replaced by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The Legal Metrology Act, 2009 deals with weights and measures; the BIS Act, 2016 governs the ISI mark and hallmarking; the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 replaced the 1986 consumer law.
n42f04a605e9.tq: PFA Act 1954 -> Food Safety and Standards Act 2006.
xs: The **Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954** was replaced by the **Food Safety and Standards Act 2006** — option **(1)**.
The **BIS Act 2016** governs the ISI mark; **CPA 2019** replaced the 1986 Act.
xa: **Legal Metrology Act 2009:** **7** sections decriminalised (**2023**); **12** more proposed in Jan Vishwas 2.0.
Consumers may get **food samples tested**.

n6d2c7f98146.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the development of the UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection?
o: Adopted in 1985, expanded in 1999 and revised in 2015
Adopted in 1999, expanded in 2005 and revised in 2015
Adopted in 1985, expanded in 2005 and revised in 2020
Adopted in 1991, expanded in 1999 and revised in 2015
n6d2c7f98146.x: The Guidelines were first adopted in 1985, expanded in 1999 to include sustainable consumption and revised in 2015.
n6d2c7f98146.tq: Use the chronological sequence to distinguish closely related revision years.
xs: The **UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection** were first **adopted** by the UN General Assembly in **1985**, **expanded** in **1999** and **revised** in **2015** — option **(1)**.
The **1999** expansion added **sustainable consumption**.
xa: The 1985 adoption was asked in the **APPSC 2025** key.
**World Consumer Rights Day** is **15 March**; **National Consumer Day** is **24 December**.
**Consumers International** was founded in **1960** (as IOCU), based in **London**.

nad7ec3bea1e.s: World Consumer Rights Day commemorates the consumer-rights speech delivered by:
nad7ec3bea1e.x: The day marks John F. Kennedy's 1962 speech on consumer rights.
nad7ec3bea1e.tq: Discriminate between closely related political figures and years.
xs: **World Consumer Rights Day** (**15 March**) marks **John F. Kennedy's 1962** speech on consumer rights — option **(4)**.
The other presidents and years are not linked to the day.
xa: ⚠ **15 March** = World Consumer Rights Day; **24 December** = National Consumer Day (India).
**UN Guidelines** were first adopted in **1985**.

n1b9cb5b16da.s: For determining the pecuniary jurisdiction of a Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, the relevant criterion is:
o: The annual income of the complainant
The compensation claimed by the complainant
The market value of the goods at the time of filing
The value of consideration paid for the goods or services
n1b9cb5b16da.x: Jurisdiction is determined by the value of consideration paid for the goods or services, not by the compensation claimed.
n1b9cb5b16da.tq: Apply the governing criterion to distinguish consideration from compensation.
xs: Jurisdiction depends on the **value of the consideration paid** for goods/services — option **(4)**.
It is **not** the compensation claimed.
xa: Slabs (2021): District up to **₹50 lakh**; State **₹50 lakh-₹2 crore**; National above **₹2 crore**.
⚠ Original CPA 2019 slabs were **₹1 crore / ₹10 crore**.

n779ad2c2ad0.s: National Consumer Day in India is observed on:
n779ad2c2ad0.x: National Consumer Day is 24 December; World Consumer Rights Day is 15 March.
xa: ⚠ **e-Jagriti** is the filing portal, not the mascot.
**15 March** marks **J.F. Kennedy's 1962** consumer-rights speech; **24 December** marks the **1986** Act.

n7ef68bff721.s: In Indian Medical Association v. V.P. Shantha (1995), the Supreme Court held that:
o: All medical services, including wholly free services, are outside consumer law.
Medical services paid for, including services in hospitals charging some patients, constitute “service” under the Consumer Protection Act.
Medical negligence can never be considered by consumer fora.
Only services provided in government hospitals are covered by consumer law.
n7ef68bff721.x: The 1995 decision held that paid medical services, including services in hospitals that charge some patients, fall within the definition of service under consumer law. Wholly free services are excluded.
n7ef68bff721.tq: Use the paid-versus-wholly-free distinction to identify the holding.
xs: **IMA v. V.P. Shantha (1995):** **paid medical services**, including those in hospitals charging some patients, are a **"service"** under the Consumer Protection Act — option **(2)**.
So **medical negligence** can go to consumer fora; only **wholly free** services are excluded.
xa: A **legal heir** of a deceased consumer may file a complaint.
CPA 2019 brought **product liability** of service providers.

n487858c7287.s: Setting up Bhilai with the USSR and Rourkela with West Germany illustrates which determinant of India's foreign policy?
n487858c7287.x: Taking aid and technology from both blocs reflects the economy as a determinant; Himalayan frontiers reflect geography.
xa: ⚠ **Bhilai** = USSR; **Rourkela** = West Germany.
After **1991**, the economic determinant meant a push for investment.
**History:** the freedom struggle produced anti-colonialism and Asian solidarity.

ncf48c9e23db.s: Article 51 of the Constitution directs the State to encourage settlement of international disputes by:
ncf48c9e23db.x: Article 51 directs the State to encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration.
ncf48c9e23db.tq: Match the constitutional directive with its precise operative term.
xs: **Article 51** (DPSP) directs the State to encourage settlement of disputes by **arbitration** — option **(4)**.
Asked in **UPPSC 2016**.
xa: Art. 51 also asks the State to promote **international peace and security** and **just and honourable relations** between nations.
**Article 73:** treaties are made by the **executive**.

nc20dab3bd76.s: Foreign affairs is listed in which entry of the Union List?
nc20dab3bd76.x: Entry 10 is foreign affairs; Entry 14 treaties, Entry 15 war and peace, and Entries 11–13 diplomatic representation and the UN.
xa: These are in **List I** of the **Seventh Schedule**.
**Article 73** lets the executive make treaties.

nce08ad40f97.s: India's demand for UNSC reform is summed up in its call for:
nce08ad40f97.x: India seeks UNSC reform and advocates 'reformed multilateralism', strengthening rather than weakening multilateral bodies.
xa: **Article 51** encourages settlement of disputes by **arbitration**.
India pressed for **nuclear disarmament** at **Belgrade (1961)**.

n9562c674650.s: Nehru's Tribal Panchsheel (1952) was drafted with:
n9562c674650.x: Nehru's Tribal Panchsheel was drafted with Verrier Elwin in 1952 and dealt with tribal policy, unlike the international Panchsheel.
xa: International Panchsheel became a core NAM principle at **Belgrade (1961)**.
**UNGA** recognised it as a principle of international law in **1957**.

n15b13cccbb1.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the principles of Panchsheel (1954)?
n15b13cccbb1.x: Panchsheel includes mutual non-aggression, mutual non-interference in internal affairs, equality and mutual benefit and peaceful co-existence. Non-alignment is a separate policy of India and is not one of the Panchsheel principles (UPSC 1997 trap).
xs: **Non-alignment** is NOT a Panchsheel principle — option **(2)**.
Panchsheel includes mutual **non-aggression**, **non-interference**, **equality and mutual benefit**, **peaceful co-existence**.
xa: ⚠ This was the **UPSC 1997** trap.
Non-alignment was initiated by **Nehru**; NAM was founded at **Belgrade, 1961**.

ncc54daecc5f.s: Non-alignment, as distinguished from neutrality, implies:
o: Avoiding all international issues and conflicts
Supporting whichever bloc is militarily stronger
Active engagement and judging each issue on its merits
ncc54daecc5f.x: Non-alignment does not mean passive neutrality; it involves active engagement and an independent assessment of each issue on its merits.
ncc54daecc5f.tq: Separate the closely related concepts of non-alignment and neutrality.
xs: Non-alignment is **not neutrality**: it means **active engagement** and **judging each issue on its merits** — option **(4)**.
So it is neither avoiding issues nor siding with the stronger bloc.
xa: Today this is expressed as **strategic autonomy** and **multi-alignment**.
Non-alignment was initiated by **Nehru** (UPPSC 2014).

n055e92e7227.s: In the context of the Modi-Xi meeting mentioned in current discussions, China stressed which principle as the frame for bilateral ties?
n055e92e7227.x: China stressed Panchsheel as the framework for India-China ties during the Modi-Xi meeting referred to in the current context.
n055e92e7227.tq: Identify the diplomatic principle linked to the bilateral relationship.
xs: At the **Modi-Xi** meeting (**Sep 2025**), China stressed **Panchsheel** as the frame for ties — option **(1)**.
Panchsheel was signed on **29 April 1954** in the Nehru-**Zhou Enlai** era.
xa: It includes mutual **non-aggression** and **peaceful co-existence**.
⚠ **Non-alignment** is not one of its principles.

nc51946caeb8.s: Kwame Nkrumah, a founding leader of the Non-Aligned Movement, belonged to:
nc51946caeb8.x: Nkrumah was associated with Ghana, Nasser with Egypt, Tito with Yugoslavia and Nehru with India.
xa: The fifth founder was **Sukarno** of **Indonesia**.
They are called the **"Initiative of Five"**.

neb9ec758c54.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the core objectives of India's foreign policy?
o: Permanent alignment with a single military bloc
neb9ec758c54.x: Permanent alignment with a single military bloc is not a core objective. The listed objectives include independence, security, peace, disarmament and cooperation across ideological lines.
neb9ec758c54.tq: Reject an extreme formulation inconsistent with strategic autonomy.
xs: **Permanent alignment with a single military bloc** is NOT an objective — option **(2)**.
Core objectives: **political independence and security**, **world peace and disarmament**, **cooperation across ideological lines**, equal rights for all nations.
xa: Others: **partnerships for domestic development**; **leadership in global governance**.
Non-alignment meant **independence from power blocs**.

n4a24f6ed30c.s: Strategic autonomy in India's foreign policy is associated with:
n4a24f6ed30c.x: Nehruvian idealism, the Indira and Gujral Doctrines belong to individual leaders, while strategic autonomy is associated with all PMs since 1947.
xa: Gujral Doctrine dates from **1996**.
Strategic autonomy today = **multi-alignment**.

n64d74cf0d74.s: The Gujral Doctrine, formulated in 1996, emphasised:
o: Non-reciprocal goodwill towards smaller neighbours, non-interference and peaceful settlement
Reciprocal military alliances with larger powers
South Asia as an exclusive military zone
n64d74cf0d74.x: The Gujral Doctrine of 1996 emphasised non-reciprocal goodwill towards smaller neighbours, non-interference and peaceful settlement.
n64d74cf0d74.tq: Distinguish the doctrine's goodwill principle from reciprocal alliance-making.
xs: The **Gujral Doctrine (1996)** stressed **non-reciprocal goodwill towards smaller neighbours**, **non-interference** and **peaceful settlement** — option **(1)**.
⚠ South Asia as India's zone is the **Indira Doctrine**.
xa: **Strategic autonomy** runs through every phase of policy.
Domestic politics also shapes neighbourhood policy, e.g. **Tamil Nadu** on **Sri Lanka**.

nd270823e619.s: India opposed the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty of 1968 primarily because it regarded the treaty as
o: a treaty exclusively on chemical weapons
an instrument for ending the United Nations
inconsistent with the principle of peaceful settlement
nd270823e619.x: India opposed the NPT because it considered the division between nuclear-weapon states and non-nuclear-weapon states discriminatory.
nd270823e619.tq: Match the stated criticism with the correct international instrument.
xs: India opposed the **NPT (1968)** as **discriminatory** — option **(3)**.
It still pressed for **nuclear disarmament**, as at the **1961 Belgrade** summit.
xa: **World peace and disarmament** is a core objective.
India seeks **UNSC reform** and "reformed multilateralism".

n70a31cfa7b3.s: India's G20 Presidency theme of 2023, 'One Earth, One Family, One Future', reflects which principle of India's foreign policy?
n70a31cfa7b3.x: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam means 'the world is one family', which India's 2023 G20 theme expressed. Panchsheel is the 1954 set of five principles with China; the Gujral Doctrine (1996) concerns non-reciprocal goodwill to smaller neighbours; the Indira Doctrine treats South Asia as India's zone.
n70a31cfa7b3.tq: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam = One Earth, One Family, One Future (G20 2023).
xs: **Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam** ("The world is one family") is reflected in the **G20** theme **"One Earth, One Family, One Future"** (**2023**) — option **(1)**.
**Panchsheel** is the **1954** set of principles; **Gujral Doctrine** (**1996**) is goodwill to neighbours; **Indira Doctrine** treats South Asia as India's zone.
xa: Panchsheel and NAM underpin India's **Global South** outreach.
**Peaceful settlement** goes with strengthening the **UN** and seeking **UNSC reform**.

nea5de1533d5.s: Jawaharlal Nehru described India's membership of the Commonwealth as:
o: an agreement by free will, to be terminated by free will
a permanent constitutional obligation to the British Crown
a military alliance against the Soviet bloc
a condition imposed by the Indian Independence Act
nea5de1533d5.x: Nehru called Commonwealth membership 'an agreement by free will to be terminated by free will' (UPPSC 2017), consistent with independence from power blocs. It was not a permanent obligation to the Crown, not a military alliance (India followed non-alignment), and not an imposed condition.
nea5de1533d5.tq: Commonwealth = 'free will in, free will out' (Nehru).
xs: Nehru called Commonwealth membership **"an agreement by free will to be terminated by free will"** — option **(1)**.
Asked in **UPPSC 2017**; it reflects independence from power blocs, not a military alliance or permanent obligation.
xa: Non-alignment was initiated by **Nehru** (UPPSC 2014).
**Nehruvian idealism:** non-alignment, Panchsheel, faith in the UN, Asian solidarity.

ne94c3752f29.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the first phase of India’s foreign policy, 1946–1962?
ne94c3752f29.x: The 1946–1962 phase is described as optimistic non-alignment, marked by idealism, Panchsheel, NAM, Commonwealth membership and anti-imperialism.
ne94c3752f29.tq: Use the exact phase label rather than a related policy instrument.
xs: The first phase (**1946-62**) is labelled "**Optimistic non-alignment**" — so option **(2)** is correct.
Its features: **idealism**, **Panchsheel**, **NAM**, **Commonwealth membership** and **anti-imperialism**.
"**Realism and recovery**" was Phase 2 (**1962-71**); "**Regional assertion**" was Phase 3 (**1971-1991**); "**Safeguarding strategic autonomy**" was Phase 4 (**1991-98**).
xa: ⚠ Order of labels: optimistic non-alignment → realism and recovery → regional assertion → safeguarding strategic autonomy → **balancing power** → **energetic engagement**.
The **1962 war with China** showed the **limits of idealism** and closed Phase 1.
A criticism of the period: taking **Kashmir to the UN** in **Jan 1948**.

n9f855407908.s: Which of the following did NOT belong to the 1962–1971 phase of realism and recovery in India's foreign policy?
o: Refusal to sign the NPT in 1968
n9f855407908.x: The NSG waiver came in 2008; the other three belong to the 1962–1971 phase.
xa: Phase 2 is labelled "**Realism and recovery**"; it also included the **1965 war**.
The **Tashkent Declaration (1966)** is Lal Bahadur **Shastri**'s signature initiative.
Nuclear deal steps: joint statement **2005** → **Hyde Act 2006** → **NSG waiver 2008** → **123 Agreement** October 2008.

o: Supporting only developing countries in all disputes
Engaging rival powers at the same time to maximise national interest
Joining a fixed military alliance led by one power
n7d30f0f37fd.x: Multi-alignment means engaging rival powers simultaneously, such as through the Quad and BRICS/SCO, to maximise national interest.
n7d30f0f37fd.tq: Choose the operational definition rather than an extreme or one-sided interpretation.
xs: **Multi-alignment** = **engaging rival powers at once** to **maximise national interest** — option **(3)**.
Example: **Quad** together with **BRICS/SCO**.
It is not a fixed alliance and not isolation.
xa: The **BRICS New Delhi Declaration 2026** was described as "**multi-vector engagement**".
Multi-alignment is the hallmark of Phase 6 (**2014 onwards**), "**Energetic engagement**".
Arc: **non-alignment → multi-alignment**; constant = **strategic autonomy**.

n53311257ee1.s: The Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation (9 August 1971) was concluded for:
n53311257ee1.x: The treaty was for 20 years and countered the US-China-Pakistan axis during the Bangladesh crisis.
xa: It gave India a **security umbrella** and more **Soviet arms and aid**.
⚠ **9 Aug 1971** = Indo-Soviet Treaty; **16 Dec 1971** = Dhaka surrender; **18 May 1974** = Pokhran-I.
The treaty is one of **Indira Gandhi**'s signature initiatives, with **Bangladesh 1971**, **Simla** and **Pokhran-I**.

na78c86a7962.s: The Simla Agreement of 1972 is associated with which principle?
o: Bilateralism and exclusion of a third-party role
Joint control of the Ganga waters by India and Nepal
Internationalisation of the Kashmir issue through the United Nations
na78c86a7962.x: The Simla Agreement emphasised bilateralism and ruled out a third-party role in resolving India-Pakistan issues.
na78c86a7962.tq: Match the agreement with its distinctive diplomatic principle.
xs: The **Simla Agreement (1972)** stands for **bilateralism** and **no third-party role** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is the opposite of internationalising Kashmir, as India did by taking **Kashmir to the UN** (**Jan 1948**).
**Ganga water sharing** was the **Farakka Accord (1977)** — with **Bangladesh**, not Nepal.
xa: **Simla** is listed among **Indira Gandhi**'s initiatives.
It followed the **Bangladesh Liberation War** (**December 1971**).
Same era: **Pokhran-I** (**18 May 1974**), **Katchatheevu** ceded to Sri Lanka (**1974**).

n971e6d19ff3.s: Pokhran-I, conducted on 18 May 1974, was officially described as a:
n971e6d19ff3.x: India described the 18 May 1974 Pokhran-I test as a peaceful nuclear explosion.
n971e6d19ff3.tq: Use the exact official description attached to the event.
xs: **Pokhran-I** (**18 May 1974**) was called a "**peaceful nuclear explosion**" — so option **(4)** is correct.
It drew **international concern** and **tighter global nuclear controls**.
xa: ⚠ **Pokhran-I** = **Indira Gandhi**; **Pokhran-II** = **Vajpayee**.
After **Pokhran-II**, India **declared itself a nuclear-weapon state**; **No First Use** formal doctrine **2003**.
Earlier, India refused to sign the **NPT (1968)** in the "Realism and recovery" phase.

nd95c3029070.s: Operation Shakti resulted in India declaring itself a:
o: Signatory to the NPT as a nuclear-weapon state
Permanent member of the UN Security Council
Member of the Nuclear Suppliers Group
nd95c3029070.x: Following Pokhran-II, India declared itself a nuclear-weapon state. India did not become an NPT-recognised nuclear-weapon state or an NSG member through the tests.
nd95c3029070.tq: Reject status claims that confuse a national declaration with international treaty recognition.
xs: After **Pokhran-II** (Operation Shakti), India **declared itself a nuclear-weapon state** — so option **(3)** is correct.
India refused to sign the **NPT (1968)**; its claims to the **UNSC** and the **NSG** remain claims.
xa: **No First Use** announced by the **Vajpayee** government; formal doctrine **2003**.
Sanctions followed: **US (Glenn Amendment)**, **Japan** and others; then the **Jaswant Singh-Strobe Talbott** talks.
⚠ **Pokhran-I** (**18 May 1974**) = Indira Gandhi; **Pokhran-II** = Vajpayee.

nd1c3199a5a1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the aftermath of Pokhran-II (1998)?
o: The US imposed sanctions under the Glenn Amendment
No First Use was announced by the Vajpayee government and formalised in 2003
The Jaswant Singh–Strobe Talbott talks preceded the nuclear tests
nd1c3199a5a1.x: The Singh–Talbott talks followed the tests and sanctions; they did not precede them.
xa: After Pokhran-II India **declared itself a nuclear-weapon state**.
Then came the **Lahore Declaration** (**February 1999**) and the **Kargil War (1999)**.
Jaishankar's phase 5 (**1998-2013**): "**balancing power**" — Pokhran-II, NFU, Indo-US nuclear deal.

nb3d82d9378c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the milestones of the Indo-US civil nuclear deal?
o: The Hyde Act was enacted in 2008
A joint statement was issued in 2005
The NSG waiver was granted on 6 September 2008
The 123 Agreement was signed in October 2008
nb3d82d9378c.x: The Hyde Act was enacted in 2006, not 2008.
xa: The deal is **Manmohan Singh**'s signature initiative.
It falls in Jaishankar's phase 5 (**1998-2013**): India as a "**balancing power**".
Critics saw the **tilt to the US after 2005** as compromising autonomy.

n5e83b080b30.s: Since 2008, India's response to the movement towards a multipolar world has generally been described as:
o: Permanent military alignment with a single superpower
n5e83b080b30.x: India's response to the emerging multipolarity since 2008 is issue-based alignment, under which partnerships vary according to the issue involved.
n5e83b080b30.tq: Identify the precise policy description rather than choosing an extreme diplomatic position.
xs: Since **2008** the world has moved to **multipolarity**; India's response = **issue-based alignment** — option **(4)**.
**US**: security and technology (Quad); **Russia**: defence and energy.
xa: Also: outreach to **Africa and Latin America**; claim to the **UNSC** and the **NSG**.
**Issue-based coalitions** = partnerships chosen issue by issue, **not fixed alliances**.
Before **2008** came the "unipolar moment" (**1991-2008**).

ne6a8ba65555.s: With reference to BRICS, which one of the following is correct?
o: India is an observer but not a founding member.
India is a founding member and chaired BRICS in 2026.
ne6a8ba65555.x: India is a founding member of BRICS and chaired the grouping in 2026.
ne6a8ba65555.tq: Test membership status and chairmanship together to catch a wrong institutional description.
xs: India is a **founding member** of **BRICS** and **chaired BRICS 2026** — option **(2)**.
The 2026 chairship produced the **New Delhi Declaration**.
xa: The declaration **criticised unilateral sanctions** and **backed UN reform**; likened to India's **non-aligned past**.
It was described as "**multi-vector engagement**".
BRICS/SCO with the Quad illustrate **multi-alignment**.

naf3e61f9ec1.x: India held the Presidency from December 2022 to November 2023; the African Union became a permanent member and the theme was 'One Earth, One Family, One Future'.
xa: First **Voice of Global South Summit**: **January 2023**.
G20 Presidency is listed among **Narendra Modi**'s initiatives.

n6089c4e437b.s: The India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) was signed during the Prime Minister's visit to the United Kingdom in:
n6089c4e437b.x: The India-UK CETA was signed during the Prime Minister's UK visit in July 2025.
n6089c4e437b.tq: Match the agreement with its specific month and year.
xs: The **India-UK CETA** was signed during the PM's UK visit in **July 2025** — option **(4)**.
It forms part of India's contemporary engagement alongside the **UN, G20, G7, Quad, SCO and BRICS**.
xa: India chaired **BRICS 2026** (**New Delhi Declaration**).
**G20 Presidency**: **Dec 2022-Nov 2023**.
**LPG reforms** made attracting **FDI and markets** a foreign-policy goal.

n8ff7f9c69da.s: On reform of the United Nations, the BRICS New Delhi Declaration, 2026:
n8ff7f9c69da.x: The Declaration backed UN reform, criticised unilateral sanctions and was likened to India's non-aligned past.
xa: India, a **founding member**, chaired **BRICS 2026**.
The declaration was described as "**multi-vector engagement**".
India's claim to the **UNSC** is part of its post-**2008** issue-based alignment.

n8fd40f291e8.s: The Lahore Declaration of February 1999 was accompanied by:
n8fd40f291e8.x: The Lahore Declaration came with the Delhi–Lahore bus diplomacy in February 1999.
n8fd40f291e8.tq: Associate the declaration with its accompanying diplomatic initiative.
xs: The **Lahore Declaration** (**February 1999**) came with **Delhi-Lahore bus diplomacy** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Simla** was **1972**; **Tashkent** was **1966**.
xa: **Lahore bus diplomacy** is a **Vajpayee** initiative, with **Pokhran-II** and **NFU**.
Soon after came the **Kargil War (1999)** — the first conflict after both sides tested nuclear weapons.

n25a15458232.s: The 'Voice of Global South' initiative is associated with:
n25a15458232.x: Voice of Global South is associated with Narendra Modi; Gujral Doctrine with Gujral, Pokhran-II with Vajpayee and the nuclear deal with Manmohan Singh.
xa: **Gujral Doctrine (1996)**: goodwill to neighbours without asking anything in return.
Manmohan Singh also secured the **NSG waiver** (**6 September 2008**).
Modi: **Neighbourhood First**, **Act East**, **G20 Presidency**.

n204359820fc.s: In relation to the Korean War, India chaired the:
o: Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission for prisoners of war
United Nations Security Council committee on sanctions
South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation council
n204359820fc.x: India chaired the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission for prisoners of war during the Korean War, with General K.S. Thimayya associated with it.
n204359820fc.tq: Match the country’s diplomatic role with the exact international body.
xs: During the **Korean War**, India chaired the **Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission for prisoners of war** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The commission was headed by Gen. **K.S. Thimayya**.
**SAARC** came much later (India's support in **1985**), and the **NSG** figures only in the **2008** waiver.
xa: After Korea, ties with the **USSR** warmed: **food aid**, the **Soviet veto on Kashmir** and support over **Goa**.
This was part of the **Nehruvian years** — Phase 1, "**Optimistic non-alignment**" (**1946-62**).
Nehru's signature initiatives: **Non-alignment**, **Panchsheel (1954)**, **Commonwealth membership**.

nef16471f6fd.s: The 1962 war with China demonstrated the limits of:
nef16471f6fd.x: The 1962 war with China exposed the limitations of the idealist approach associated with the early Nehruvian phase.
nef16471f6fd.tq: Link the historical shock to the policy approach it challenged.
xs: The **1962 war with China** showed the **limits of idealism** in India's foreign policy — so option **(1)** is correct.
Idealism marked Phase 1, "**Optimistic non-alignment**" (**1946-62**).
**Look East** (**1991-92**), the **Gujral Doctrine** (**1996**) and West Asia economic diplomacy came decades later.
xa: After 1962 came Phase 2, "**Realism and recovery**" (**1962-71**): defence build-up, **1965 war**, **Tashkent (1966)**.
Debate point: "Phase 1 idealism **tested by 1962**".
Overall arc: **idealism → realism**; **non-alignment → multi-alignment**; the constant is **strategic autonomy**.

n17eb5c62c9d.s: In January 1948, India referred the Kashmir issue to the UN Security Council under which Article of the UN Charter?
n17eb5c62c9d.x: Nehru referred it under Article 35 of the UN Charter on 1 January 1948; UNSC Resolution 47 followed in 1948.
xa: The UN called for a **plebiscite conditional on Pakistan's withdrawal** — which never happened.
The **Instrument of Accession** (**26 October 1947**) ceded only **defence, external affairs and communications**.
Taking **Kashmir to the UN** is a standard criticism of early foreign policy.

n09cd920d2fa.s: The Instrument of Accession of Jammu and Kashmir was signed by Maharaja Hari Singh on:
n09cd920d2fa.x: Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947, after the tribal invasion. Indian troops were airlifted on 27 October.
n09cd920d2fa.tq: Separate the date of accession from the following day on which troops were airlifted.
xs: **Maharaja Hari Singh** signed the **Instrument of Accession** on **26 October 1947** — option **(4)**.
He signed **after the tribal invasion**.
**27 October 1947** is the date Indian **troops were airlifted**; **1 January 1948** relates to the UN reference.
xa: ⚠ Accession **26 Oct** vs airlift **27 Oct** — a classic trap.
It ceded only **defence, external affairs and communications**.
It led to the **first Indo-Pak war**, ended by the UN ceasefire of **1 January 1949**.

n0456880e35c.s: Which subject was NOT ceded to India under the Instrument of Accession signed by Maharaja Hari Singh?
n0456880e35c.x: The Instrument (26 October 1947) ceded only defence, external affairs and communications; land revenue stayed with the State.
xa: Signed by **Maharaja Hari Singh** on **26 October 1947**, after the tribal invasion.
**Article 370** became operative on **17 November 1952**; abrogated **5 August 2019**.
The **J&K Reorganisation Act 2019** created the UTs of **J&K** and **Ladakh**.

nf0583adf5de.s: The Supreme Court upheld the abrogation of Article 370 in:
nf0583adf5de.x: Article 370 was abrogated on 5 August 2019 and the Supreme Court upheld it in December 2023.
xa: The **J&K Reorganisation Act 2019** created the UTs of **J&K** and **Ladakh**.
Pakistan's response: **downgraded diplomatic ties**, suspended **bilateral trade** and the **Samjhauta Express**, raised it at the **UN**.

n366ad17f497.s: The Kartarpur Corridor was opened in November 2019 to mark:
o: The 550th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak
The centenary of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre
The signing of the Lahore Declaration
The 400th anniversary of the birth of Guru Arjan Dev
n366ad17f497.x: The corridor was opened in November 2019 to commemorate Guru Nanak’s 550th birth anniversary.
n366ad17f497.tq: Link the opening year and commemorative occasion of the connectivity initiative.
xs: The Kartarpur Corridor opened in **November 2019** for **Guru Nanak's 550th birth anniversary** — option **(1)**.
The India-Pakistan agreement was signed in **October 2019**.
xa: **Visa-free** access from **Dera Baba Nanak** to **Gurdwara Darbar Sahib**, Kartarpur (**Narowal**).
The **Lahore Declaration** was **February 1999** — unrelated.

n96977f833c5.s: Which one of the following correctly states the sequence in the Jammu and Kashmir crisis?
o: UN ceasefire, tribal invasion, accession, airlift of troops
Tribal invasion, accession, airlift of troops, First Indo-Pak war
Accession, UN reference, tribal invasion, airlift of troops
Airlift of troops, accession, tribal invasion, UN ceasefire
n96977f833c5.x: The sequence was tribal invasion, Instrument of Accession, airlifting of Indian troops to Srinagar and the First Indo-Pak war. The UN ceasefire followed in January 1949.
n96977f833c5.tq: Anchor the sequence with the invasion first and the ceasefire last.
xs: Correct order: **tribal invasion → accession → airlift of troops → first Indo-Pak war** — option **(2)**.
The **Instrument of Accession** was signed on **26 October 1947**, after the **tribal invasion** (Oct 1947); troops were **airlifted 27 October**.
The accession **led to the first Indo-Pak war**; the UN-brokered **ceasefire** came only on **1 January 1949**.
xa: ⚠ Accession **26 Oct** vs troops airlifted **27 Oct**.
Nehru took the issue to the **UNSC** in **January 1948** under **Article 35** of the UN Charter.
The **Karachi Agreement (July 1949)** fixed the **ceasefire line** after the 1947-48 war.

n69ad304a9ab.s: Which of the following was the immediate political outcome of the 1971 India–Pakistan war?
o: The ceasefire line was fixed under the Karachi Agreement.
Bangladesh was created and Pakistan surrendered on 16 December 1971.
The Indus Waters Treaty was signed.
Pakistan withdrew from Kargil under United States pressure.
n69ad304a9ab.x: The 1971 war resulted in the creation of Bangladesh, and Pakistan surrendered on 16 December 1971.
n69ad304a9ab.tq: Associate the decisive outcome with the correct war rather than with the later agreement.
xs: The **1971** war created **Bangladesh**, and **Pakistan surrendered on 16 December 1971** — option **(2)**.
The **Karachi Agreement** was **1949**; the **IWT** was **1960**; Kargil withdrawal under US pressure was **1999**.
xa: The war led to the **Simla Agreement (1972)**: **Indira Gandhi-Z.A. Bhutto**.
Under Simla, disputes are settled **bilaterally** and the ceasefire line became the **LoC**.
The **Indo-Soviet Treaty** was signed in **1971**.

na3f4eb444c8.s: India's military response in the 1999 Kargil conflict was called:
na3f4eb444c8.x: India's response was Operation Vijay; Kargil was the first war between nuclear-armed states, and Pakistan withdrew under US pressure.
xa: Kargil (**1999**) followed the **Lahore Declaration** (**February 1999**).
Soviet mediation belongs to **Tashkent (January 1966)**.

ne74acdb5bd7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Tashkent Declaration (January 1966)?
o: It was mediated by the Soviet Union, with Kosygin playing a key role
It provided for troop withdrawal and return of prisoners of war
It converted the ceasefire line into the Line of Control
ne74acdb5bd7.x: The ceasefire line became the LoC under the Simla Agreement, 1972, not under Tashkent.
xa: Signed by **Shastri-Ayub Khan** in **January 1966**, after the **1965** war.
It returned the strategic **Haji Pir pass**; **Shastri died suddenly** at Tashkent.

n025afe06884.s: Operation Meghdoot, associated with the Siachen dispute, was conducted in:
n025afe06884.x: India secured the Siachen glacier through Operation Meghdoot in April 1984.
n025afe06884.tq: Match the military operation with its year and geographical theatre.
xs: **Operation Meghdoot** secured **Siachen** in **April 1984** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **Gibraltar** (Pakistan, **1965**) – **Meghdoot** (Siachen, **1984**) – **Vijay** (Kargil, **1999**).
xa: The dispute is over the **unmarked line beyond NJ9842**.
**Siachen** is one of the **8 baskets** of the Composite Dialogue.

n83aa05824f2.s: The UNSC 1267 sanctions committee deals with:
n83aa05824f2.x: The 1267 committee lists ISIL/Al-Qaida-linked terrorists and entities for asset freezes and travel bans.
xa: **Masood Azhar** (JeM): listed **May 2019** after China lifted its "**technical hold**".
**Hafiz Saeed** (LeT/JuD): listed **2008**.

nf7849de7180.s: The Samjhauta Express between Attari and Lahore was started in:
nf7849de7180.x: It began in 1976 after the Simla Agreement and was bombed in 2007.
xa: It runs **Attari-Lahore**.
Pakistan also **downgraded ties**, **suspended trade** and raised Article 370 at the **UN**.

n9ea21e26b27.s: The Agra Summit of July 2001, which ended without a joint declaration, was held between Atal Bihari Vajpayee and:
n9ea21e26b27.x: The Agra Summit was between Vajpayee and Musharraf and ended without a joint declaration.
xa: ⚠ **Lahore (1999)** = Vajpayee-**Nawaz Sharif**.
The **Parliament attack** followed on **13 Dec 2001** → **Operation Parakram**.
The **Composite Dialogue**: agreed **1997** → resumed **2004**.

n6f74cf854dc.s: The Karachi Agreement between India and Pakistan was signed in:
n6f74cf854dc.x: The Karachi Agreement was in 1949, followed by Tashkent (1966), Lahore (1999) and Agra (2001).
xa: Simla came between: **2 July 1972**.
UPPSC 2002 order: **Tashkent → Indo-Soviet → Simla → Farakka**.
**Ganga Waters Treaty (1996)** with Bangladesh (**30 years**) followed Farakka.

n5f534cedabd.s: The Simla Agreement (2 July 1972) was signed by Indira Gandhi and:
n5f534cedabd.x: Indira Gandhi and Z.A. Bhutto signed it; it committed both sides to bilateral settlement and turned the ceasefire line into the LoC.
xa: Simla-based **bilateralism** is India's **fixed position**.
Simla being India-Pakistan was asked in **APPSC 2018**; the signatory pair in **APPSC 2022**.
The **Samjhauta Express** started in **1976** after Simla.

n17a6af78ead.s: The Indus Waters Treaty (Karachi, 1960), brokered by the World Bank, was signed by Ayub Khan and:
n17a6af78ead.x: Nehru and Ayub Khan signed the Treaty; Shastri and Ayub Khan were the Tashkent pair.
xa: The World Bank as broker was asked in **APPSC G2 2017**.
**Eastern** rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) = **India**; **Western** (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) = **Pakistan**.
The **2025** abeyance was the **first suspension** since **1960**.

n02026b7fcdb.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Permanent Indus Commission?
o: It has three Commissioners from India and one from Pakistan.
It is a court composed of judges from the Hague.
It consists only of representatives appointed by the World Bank.
It consists of one Commissioner from each country.
n02026b7fcdb.x: The Permanent Indus Commission has one Commissioner from India and one from Pakistan.
n02026b7fcdb.tq: Test the composition of the bilateral institutional mechanism.
xs: The **Permanent Indus Commission** has **one Commissioner from each country** — option **(4)**.
It is not a court and not a World Bank body; it handles "**Questions**" under **Article IX**.
xa: Indian side: the **Indus Wing** of the **Department of Water Resources**.
"**Differences**" → **Neutral Expert**; "**Disputes**" → **Court of Arbitration**.

nf2a28af0b04.s: The Cabinet Committee on Security placed the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance from:
nf2a28af0b04.x: Following the Pahalgam attack on 22 April 2025, the treaty was placed in abeyance from 23 April 2025.
nf2a28af0b04.tq: Separate the date of the triggering event from the date on which the governmental action took effect.
xs: The **CCS** put the IWT "**in abeyance**" from **23 April 2025** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **22 April 2025** is the date of the **Pahalgam attack** that triggered it.
**4 Jul 2026** is when the MEA said the Treaty **remains in force**.
xa: Abeyance lasts until Pakistan "**credibly and irrevocably**" gives up support for cross-border terrorism.
It was the **first ever suspension** of the IWT.

n1394c599095.s: The stated condition for ending the abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty was that Pakistan should:
o: Withdraw from the Permanent Indus Commission
Credibly and irrevocably give up support for cross-border terrorism
Return all western rivers to India
Accept the jurisdiction of the International Court of Justice
n1394c599095.x: The abeyance was to continue until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably gives up support for cross-border terrorism.
n1394c599095.tq: Identify the exact political condition attached to the abeyance decision.
xs: Abeyance lasts until Pakistan "**credibly and irrevocably**" **gives up support for cross-border terrorism** — option **(2)**.
It was imposed by the **CCS** from **23 April 2025** after **Pahalgam**.
xa: Effects: India **stops sharing flow data**; can **build storage on the western rivers**.
The Treaty itself **does not provide for** abeyance.

naf4105c2929.s: The Indus Waters Treaty gives India about what share of the waters?
naf4105c2929.x: India gets about 20% of the waters, and the Treaty is criticised for lacking aquifer and drought clauses.
xa: Pakistan gets about **80% of the total flow of 168 MAF**.
Pakistan relies on the system for **93%** of its water use.

nd2196a31777.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Indus Waters Treaty and India's current position?
o: The Treaty is presently in abeyance
Ravi, Beas and Sutlej are allocated to India for unrestricted use
India is seeking to renegotiate the Treaty
India has accepted the Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling
nd2196a31777.x: India has rejected, not accepted, the PCA ruling.
xa: The PCA ruled the IWT "**remains in force**", with interim measures on **Ratle**.
India said the court has "**no jurisdiction**" (**1 Sep 2026**).

na09dbfba611.s: The India–Pakistan Composite Dialogue, agreed in 1997, was resumed in:
na09dbfba611.x: It resumed in 2004 (Agra 2001 ended without a declaration) and was broken off after 26/11.
xa: It had **8 baskets**, including **J&K**, **Siachen**, **Sir Creek**, **Wullar Barrage/Tulbul**.
It **kept breaking down because of terrorism**.

n0f601fbb75d.s: Which one of the following was NOT one of the eight baskets of the India-Pakistan Composite Dialogue?
o: Peace and security and confidence-building measures
n0f601fbb75d.x: The eight baskets included peace and security/CBMs, J&K, Siachen, Wullar Barrage/Tulbul, Sir Creek, terrorism and drugs, economic cooperation, and friendly exchanges. Nuclear disarmament was not listed as a basket.
n0f601fbb75d.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the officially enumerated set.
xs: **Nuclear disarmament** was **not** a basket — option **(4)**.
The **8 baskets**: **peace and security/CBMs**; **J&K**; **Siachen**; **Wullar Barrage/Tulbul**; **Sir Creek**; **terrorism and drugs**; **economic cooperation**; **friendly exchanges**.
xa: Timeline: agreed **1997** → resumed **2004** → broken off after **26/11**.
Nuclear CBMs appear in the **Lahore Declaration** (**February 1999**).

n1cab2935c0d.s: Sir Creek is best described as a:
o: 96-kilometre freshwater river between Punjab and Sindh
96-kilometre tidal estuary between Gujarat and Sindh
154-kilometre mountain pass between Ladakh and Gilgit-Baltistan
60-kilometre coastal canal between Rajasthan and Sindh
n1cab2935c0d.x: Sir Creek is a 96-kilometre tidal estuary in the Rann of Kutch between Gujarat and Sindh.
n1cab2935c0d.tq: Link the geographical description with the distinctive numerical figure.
xs: **Sir Creek** is a **96-km tidal estuary** in the **Rann of Kutch**, between **Gujarat and Sindh** — option **(2)**.
It is not a freshwater river, a pass or a canal.
xa: Dispute: **Pakistan = 1914 map line** vs **India = mid-channel thalweg** rule.
Sir Creek is one of the **8 baskets** of the Composite Dialogue.

na484354ca79.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the differing positions of India and Pakistan regarding the Sir Creek boundary?
o: India supports the 1914 map line, while Pakistan supports the thalweg rule.
Pakistan supports the mid-channel thalweg rule, while India rejects any boundary line.
Pakistan cites the 1914 map line, while India supports the mid-channel thalweg rule.
Both countries support the 1914 map line but differ over its historical date.
na484354ca79.x: Pakistan cites the 1914 map line, while India relies on the mid-channel thalweg principle for determining the boundary.
na484354ca79.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap to separate the positions of the two countries.
xs: **Pakistan** cites the **1914 map line**; **India** supports the **mid-channel thalweg** rule — option **(3)**.
Option (1) reverses the positions.
xa: **Sir Creek**: a **96-km tidal estuary**, Rann of Kutch, between **Gujarat and Sindh**.
Other disputed place: **Siachen** — unmarked line beyond **NJ9842**.

n01ea66bbcaf.s: Masood Azhar was listed by the UNSC 1267 sanctions committee in May 2019 after:
n01ea66bbcaf.x: Masood Azhar, the chief of Jaish-e-Mohammed, was listed in May 2019 after China lifted its technical hold.
n01ea66bbcaf.tq: Test the diplomatic trigger associated with an international terror listing.
xs: **Masood Azhar** was listed in **May 2019** after **China lifted its "technical hold"** — option **(1)**.
He is the **JeM** chief.
xa: **Hafiz Saeed** (LeT/JuD) was listed in **2008**.
**JeM** carried out **Pulwama** (**14 Feb 2019**).
**FATF** grey list: Pakistan **June 2018** → removed **October 2022**.

nb2559945beb.s: Pakistan remained on the FATF grey list from:
nb2559945beb.x: Pakistan was under increased monitoring on the FATF grey list from June 2018 until its removal in October 2022.
nb2559945beb.tq: Recall both endpoints of a period rather than only the year of removal.
xs: Pakistan was on the **FATF grey list** from **June 2018** to **October 2022** — option **(2)**.
The grey list means **increased monitoring**.
xa: **FATF pressure on terror financing** is a lever India uses.
**Masood Azhar** was UNSC-listed in **May 2019**.

nd18e47b8c03.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about MFN status between India and Pakistan?
o: India granted MFN status to Pakistan in 1996
India imposed a 100% customs duty on Pakistani goods after withdrawal
Pakistan never reciprocated MFN status to India
India withdrew it in February 2019 after Pulwama
nd18e47b8c03.x: The customs duty imposed was 200%, not 100%.
xa: **Pulwama** (**14 Feb 2019**) also led to the **Balakot airstrike**.
Main land trade route: **Wagah-Attari**.

n65a2a30944a.s: The principal land trade route between India and Pakistan is:
n65a2a30944a.x: Wagah–Attari is the main land trade route between India and Pakistan.
n65a2a30944a.tq: Distinguish the principal trade route from pilgrimage and other cross-border routes.
xs: **Wagah–Attari** (Wagah-Attari) is the **main land trade route** — option **(2)**.
**Dera Baba Nanak-Kartarpur** is the **visa-free** pilgrim corridor, not the trade route.
xa: After **Pahalgam**, India **closed the Attari ICP** and revoked **SAARC visa-exemption** travel.
High Commission strength was cut from **55 to 35** (**2026**).
**MFN** withdrawn **February 2019** with a **200% customs duty**.

nfb65a221397.s: The India–Pakistan agreement on the Kartarpur Corridor was signed in:
nfb65a221397.x: The agreement was signed in October 2019, giving visa-free access from Dera Baba Nanak to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib, Kartarpur.
xa: Opened **November 2019** for **Guru Nanak's 550th birth anniversary**.
The Samjhauta Express started **1976**, was bombed **2007**, suspended **2019**.

n2d8cc2d5e26.s: Which of the following correctly describes the territorial positions mentioned in relation to Aksai Chin and Arunachal Pradesh?
o: India occupies about 38,000 sq km in Aksai Chin and China claims about 90,000 sq km in the north-east.
China occupies about 90,000 sq km in Aksai Chin and India claims about 38,000 sq km in the north-east.
China occupies about 38,000 sq km in Aksai Chin and claims about 90,000 sq km in the north-east.
India and China each occupy approximately 38,000 sq km in Aksai Chin.
n2d8cc2d5e26.x: China occupies about 38,000 sq km in Aksai Chin and claims about 90,000 sq km in the north-east, including most of Arunachal Pradesh.
n2d8cc2d5e26.tq: Split the options by checking the claimant, location and figures together.
xs: **China occupies about 38,000 sq km in Aksai Chin** and **claims about 90,000 sq km in the north-east** — option **(3)**.
The north-east claim covers most of **Arunachal Pradesh**, which China calls "**South Tibet**".
India occupies neither figure; the other options swap the numbers or the parties.
xa: **Shaksgam Valley** was ceded by Pakistan to China in **1963**.
The **USA** reaffirmed Arunachal as an integral part of India (**BPSC 2023**).

nde65473562e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the sectors of the Line of Actual Control?
o: The Western sector comprises Ladakh and includes Aksai Chin
The Middle sector is the most contested sector
The Middle sector comprises Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand
The Eastern sector comprises Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh and is associated with the McMahon Line
nde65473562e.x: The Middle sector is the least contested sector of the LAC.
xa: Border length: **3,488 km**.
The **1962** war was fought in the **Western (Aksai Chin/Ladakh)** and **Eastern (NEFA)** sectors.

n5194e63cfbe.s: The length of the India-China border is approximately:
n5194e63cfbe.x: The India-China border is approximately 3,488 km long.
n5194e63cfbe.tq: Direct figure recall with systematically shifted numerical distractors.
xs: The India-China border is **3,488 km** — option **(2)**.
It runs along the **LAC** through three sectors — **Western**, **Middle** and **Eastern**.
xa: LAC sectors: **Western** (Ladakh), **Middle** (Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand), **Eastern** (Sikkim, Arunachal).
The **Middle** sector is the **least contested**; the **Western** sees most standoffs.

nabd33cbe80d.s: The Shaksgam Valley, also known as the Trans-Karakoram Tract, was ceded to China by Pakistan under which agreement?
o: 1993 India-China Agreement on Peace and Tranquillity
nabd33cbe80d.x: Pakistan illegally ceded the Shaksgam Valley to China under the 1963 Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement. India regards it as an integral part of India.
nabd33cbe80d.tq: Direct agreement-identification question with neighbouring bilateral agreements as distractors.
xs: The **Shaksgam Valley** (**Trans-Karakoram Tract**) was illegally ceded by Pakistan under the **1963 Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement** — option **(3)**.
India reaffirmed it as **integral** (**2026**).
**Panchsheel (1954)** concerned **Tibet**; the **1993** agreement was on peace along the LAC.
xa: China occupies about **38,000 sq km** in **Aksai Chin**.
⚠ The **1963** agreement came **after** the 1962 war — not a cause of it.

nf05f241493d.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as a cause of the India-China war of 1962?
o: The Tibet question and the Dalai Lama's asylum in 1959
The unsettled boundary left without a clear line by the British
nf05f241493d.x: The 1963 Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement followed the 1962 war and was not a cause of it. The unsettled boundary, the Tibet question and India's Forward Policy were identified causes.
nf05f241493d.tq: Find the chronological impossibility among otherwise relevant border facts.
xs: The **1963 Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement** was not a cause — it came **after** the war — option **(3)**.
Causes: **unsettled boundary** (British left no clear line), **Tibet + Dalai Lama's asylum (1959)**, **India's Forward Policy**.
xa: The war ran **20 Oct-21 Nov 1962** and ended in **China's unilateral ceasefire**.
Under the 1963 agreement Pakistan ceded the **Shaksgam Valley**.

nf142112838e.s: Which agreement was signed in 1993 during Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao's visit to China?
o: Agreement on Peace and Tranquillity along the LAC
Agreement on Confidence-Building Measures in the Military Field
Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for Settlement of the Boundary Question
nf142112838e.x: The 1993 Agreement on Peace and Tranquillity along the LAC was associated with Prime Minister Narasimha Rao's visit.
nf142112838e.tq: Match the year, agreement and visiting dignitary without reversing the sequence.
xs: **1993**: the **Agreement on Peace and Tranquillity along the LAC**, during PM **Narasimha Rao**'s visit — option **(1)**.
**CBMs in the Military Field** = **1996**; **Border Defence Cooperation** = **2013**; **Political Parameters** = **2005**.
xa: **1996** came with President **Jiang Zemin**'s visit.
**2003**: Declaration on Principles + **Special Representatives** (PM **Vajpayee**).

n74a626b9f77.s: The 2005 agreement between India and China dealt with:
o: Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for settlement of the boundary question
Peace and Tranquillity along the LAC
n74a626b9f77.x: The 2005 agreement laid down Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for settlement of the boundary question.
n74a626b9f77.tq: Direct identification of the subject of a specific border agreement.
xs: **2005**: **Political Parameters and Guiding Principles** for settlement of the **boundary question** — option **(2)**.
**Peace and Tranquillity** = **1993**; **WMCC** = **2012**; **Border Defence Cooperation** = **2013**.
xa: It built on the **2003** Declaration on Principles, which appointed the **Special Representatives**.
Debate: an "**early harvest**" limited to **Sikkim** would weaken India's case for a full settlement.

n4ebda86a787.s: Under the 1954 Panchsheel Agreement, India accepted China's sovereignty over:
n4ebda86a787.x: India accepted China's sovereignty over Tibet under the 1954 Panchsheel Agreement.
n4ebda86a787.tq: Link the agreement with the specific territorial issue rather than with another Chinese region.
xs: Under the **1954 Panchsheel** agreement India accepted China's sovereignty over **Tibet** — option **(1)**.
The **Tibet question** remained a sore point and became a cause of the **1962** war.
xa: The **Dalai Lama's asylum (1959)** was a cause of the **1962** war.
**Kailash Mansarovar Yatra** resumed via **Lipulekh** and **Nathu La**.

n94fe2160129.s: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding recent India–China relations?
o: The Special Representatives mechanism dates from 2003
The 25th round of Special Representatives' talks was held in Beijing in August 2026
Ten PLA brigades were reported to remain on the LAC
India holds that relations can become normal even if the border remains unsettled and tense
n94fe2160129.x: India's stated position is that relations cannot be normal until the border is peaceful.
xa: The 25th round (**Doval + Wang Yi**) issued an **eight-point outcome document** to "improve understanding of the LAC".
**MoD Annual Report 2025-26**: PLA deployment **fell in 2025**, but **10 combined arms brigades** remain.
The **24th round** was in **New Delhi**, **Aug 2025**.

nb7c69b587fc.s: The India–China standoff at Doklam took place in:
nb7c69b587fc.x: Sumdorong Chu was in 1986-87, Depsang 2013, Doklam 2017 and Galwan 2020.
xa: Then **Yangtse** (**Dec 2022**), Tawang.
⚠ **Tawang** = Sumdorong Chu and Yangtse; **Doklam** = tri-junction with Bhutan.

n6da63a5c410.s: The Doklam standoff of 2017 occurred at the:
n6da63a5c410.x: The Doklam standoff occurred at the India-Bhutan-China tri-junction.
xs: **Doklam** (**2017**) is at the **India-Bhutan-China tri-junction** — option **(4)**.
Other standoffs: **Depsang** (Ladakh), **Sumdorong Chu** and **Yangtse** (Tawang).
xa: ⚠ **Doklam** = tri-junction with **Bhutan**; **Tawang** = Sumdorong Chu and Yangtse.
Next came **Galwan** (**15 June 2020**), **Eastern Ladakh**.

n0414cf0076c.s: The October 2024 understanding concerning Depsang and Demchok was endorsed at the meeting between Narendra Modi and Xi Jinping held at:
