n0414cf0076c.x: The understanding was endorsed at the Modi-Xi meeting in Kazan in October 2024.
n0414cf0076c.tq: Venue-based recall of a diplomatic meeting linked to disengagement.
xs: The **Oct 2024** understanding on **Depsang and Demchok** was endorsed at the Modi-Xi meeting in **Kazan** — option **(4)**.
The Kazan meeting was itself in **Oct 2024**.
xa: Earlier disengagements: **Galwan**, **Pangong Tso (2021)**, **Gogra-Hot Springs (2022)**.
Modi-Xi at the **SCO Summit, Tianjin (Aug 2025)**: "**development partners, not rivals**".

n7e156a6f8b0.s: India recognised the People's Republic of China on:
n7e156a6f8b0.x: India recognised the PRC on 30 December 1949 and established diplomatic ties on 1 April 1950, as the first non-socialist-bloc country to do so.
xa: Under the **1954 Panchsheel** agreement India accepted China's sovereignty over **Tibet**.
India-China border length: **3,488 km**.

nc52010c4e11.s: The India–China Strategic Economic Dialogue was set up in:
nc52010c4e11.x: The SED was set up in 2010 and held six rounds (2011-2019); 2013 is the BRI launch year.
xa: SED: **six rounds (2011-2019)** → revival discussed **2026**.
**Press Note 3 (2020)**: FDI from land-border countries needs **government approval**.

na88545e0728.s: Press Note 3 of 2020 requires government approval for FDI from:
o: Countries sharing a land border with India
Countries without a tax treaty with India
na88545e0728.x: Press Note 3 requires government approval for FDI from countries sharing a land border with India; it does not ban such investment.
xa: **App bans (2020)** were under **Sec. 69A** of the IT Act.
India depends on Chinese **machinery, electronics, APIs and solar equipment**.

naf274c49313.x: Kyaukphyu is in Myanmar; Hambantota is in Sri Lanka, Gwadar in Pakistan and Chittagong in Bangladesh.
xa: These ports reflect China's **BRI** (launched **2013**).
India's counter: **SAGAR/MAHASAGAR** + **Neighbourhood First**.

nbfe0f2e3dfe.s: The Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) was launched in:
nbfe0f2e3dfe.tq: Distinguish the launch year from nearby years associated with other India-China initiatives.
xs: The **BRI** was launched in **2013** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **2010** is when the **Strategic Economic Dialogue** was set up.
xa: **CPEC** is part of China-Pakistan ties; India opposes it as it passes through **PoJK**.
BRI ports: **Hambantota**, **Gwadar**, **Chittagong**, **Kyaukphyu**.

n97fd21989e8.s: India opposes the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor primarily because it:
o: excludes Pakistan from the Belt and Road Initiative
was established under the Panchsheel Agreement
passes through PoJK, raising a sovereignty issue
connects only Indian ports with Chinese ports
n97fd21989e8.x: India's objection is that CPEC passes through Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, creating a sovereignty concern.
n97fd21989e8.tq: Identify the territorial and sovereignty basis of a foreign-policy position rather than a trade-related distractor.
xs: India opposes **CPEC** because it **passes through PoJK** — a **sovereignty issue** — option **(3)**.
CPEC is part of China's **BRI**, which includes Pakistan; nothing links it to **Panchsheel (1954)**.
xa: CPEC reflects **China-Pakistan collusion**; **Gwadar** is in Pakistan.
India's counter: **SAGAR/MAHASAGAR** + **Neighbourhood First**.
**Shaksgam Valley** was ceded by Pakistan to China in **1963**.

n75cc91bfd60.s: The mega dam being constructed by China on the upper course of the Brahmaputra is associated with which name of the river?
n75cc91bfd60.x: The Brahmaputra is known as the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet, where China is building the mega dam.
n75cc91bfd60.tq: Discriminate between the names of transboundary Asian rivers.
xs: China's **mega dam** is on the **Yarlung Tsangpo (Brahmaputra)** — option **(2)**.
India raised concern in **Aug 2025**.
xa: **Expert Level Mechanism (2006)** on trans-border rivers.
**Flood-season data** MoUs cover the **Brahmaputra** and **Sutlej**.

n50d6053cac4.s: India and China have flood-season hydrological data MoUs for the Brahmaputra and the:
n50d6053cac4.x: The flood-season data MoUs cover the Brahmaputra and Sutlej; the Expert Level Mechanism deals with trans-border rivers.
xa: China's **mega dam** on the **Yarlung Tsangpo**; India raised concern **Aug 2025**.
**Nathu La** (Sikkim) reopened for trade in **2006**, the same year as the ELM.

n9eb5e1b2821.s: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, of which India is a founding member, is headquartered in:
n9eb5e1b2821.x: The AIIB is headquartered in Beijing, not New Delhi, and India is a founding member.
xa: Other forum: **RIC** (Russia-India-China).
**18th BRICS Summit**: **New Delhi**, **Sep 2026**.

nb4f65c4d2fa.s: The 2007 revision of the India-Bhutan Friendship Treaty removed the provision that Bhutan would be guided by India in its:
nb4f65c4d2fa.x: The 2007 revision removed the clause that Bhutan would be guided by India in foreign affairs.
nb4f65c4d2fa.tq: Identify the exact subject of the deleted treaty clause.
xs: The **2007** revision dropped the clause that Bhutan be "**guided**" by India in **foreign affairs** — option **(3)**.
The **India-Bhutan Friendship Treaty** dates from **1949**.
xa: ⚠ Bhutan treaty **1949**; Nepal treaty **1950**.
India **imports power from Bhutan** (**APPSC-G2 2017**); **Mangdechhu** inaugurated by PM Modi in **2019**.
India-Bhutan border: **699** km.

nba5ed9aaa61.s: Which treaty is associated with an open border and security cooperation, while Nepal seeks its revision?
o: India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship, 1950
nba5ed9aaa61.x: The 1950 India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship provides for an open border and security cooperation; Nepal has sought its revision.
nba5ed9aaa61.tq: Match the treaty's distinctive features with its correct bilateral relationship.
xs: The **India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship, 1950** provides an **open border** and **security cooperation**; **Nepal wants it revised** — option **(3)**.
The **Bhutan treaty** is **1949**; the **Land Boundary Agreement** (**1974**) exchanged enclaves; the **Ganga Water Treaty** (**1996**) is on water.
xa: In **2026**, Nepal's **youth-led leadership** is pushing to revise the **1950 Treaty**.
Other Nepal agreements: **Kosi (1954)**, **Gandak (1959)**, **Mahakali (1996)**.

n9ce5c4f13ee.s: Which of the following was NOT part of the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987?
o: Merger of the Northern and Eastern provinces
n9ce5c4f13ee.x: India banned the LTTE only in 1992, after Rajiv Gandhi's assassination in 1991; it was not part of the Accord.
xa: Signed by **Rajiv Gandhi-J.R. Jayewardene**.
The last IPKF troops left in **March 1990**.

nd7f38594344.s: Which of the following was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Kabul in 2015?
nd7f38594344.x: The Afghan Parliament building in Kabul was inaugurated by Prime Minister Modi in 2015.
nd7f38594344.tq: Distinguish an inauguration in Kabul from infrastructure projects in other Afghan locations.
xs: PM Modi inaugurated the **Afghan Parliament building** in **Kabul**, **2015** — option **(2)**.
The **Salma Dam** is in **Herat** (**2016**); **Zaranj-Delaram** is a **218 km** highway.
xa: **Zaranj-Delaram** was built by the **BRO** and links to **Iran's border** (Chabahar route).
India-Afghanistan border: about **106** km — the shortest.

n09b6750fed6.s: The Ganga Water Treaty of 1996 is associated with which of the following features?
n09b6750fed6.x: The 1996 Ganga Water Treaty with Bangladesh concerns Farakka and has a 30-year duration. It emerged in the context of the Gujral Doctrine's principle of non-reciprocity.
n09b6750fed6.tq: Match the treaty with its location and duration rather than with another water agreement.
xs: The **Ganga Water Treaty (1996)** = **Farakka**, **30 years** — option **(3)**.
It came out of the **Gujral Doctrine** (**non-reciprocity**).
**Tanakpur** belongs to the **Mahakali Treaty**; **Katchatheevu** is Sri Lanka; **Doklam** is the Bhutan tri-junction.
xa: ⚠ **1996** also saw the **Mahakali Treaty** with Nepal.
Other Bangladesh water issue: **Teesta** sharing.

nfd043a93d77.s: Who headed the elected government sworn in Bangladesh in February 2026?
nfd043a93d77.x: After the 2024 upheaval, an elected government under Tarique Rahman was sworn in Bangladesh in February 2026.
nfd043a93d77.tq: Match the political office-holder with the correct country and year.
xs: **Tarique Rahman** (**BNP**) heads the elected government sworn in in **Feb 2026** — option **(3)**.
It followed the **2024 upheaval**; **Om Birla** (Speaker) represented India at the swearing-in.
**J.R. Jayewardene** was the Sri Lankan signatory of the **1987** Accord.
xa: India-Bangladesh projects: **Akhaura-Agartala rail** (**2023**), **Friendship Pipeline** (diesel).
Bangladesh plants: **Rooppur** (nuclear, Russia-built) and **Maitree** (thermal, Rampal).

na96ad6a48d7.s: Nepal's hydropower potential is estimated at about:
na96ad6a48d7.x: Nepal's hydropower potential is put at 83,000 MW; the first trilateral power deal had Nepal supplying Bangladesh through the Indian grid.
xa: Bhutan projects: **Mangdechhu** (**2019**), **Punatsangchhu I and II**.
Nepal projects: **Pancheshwar**, **Arun III**.

n4d871b758d7.s: The Kalapani-Limpiyadhura-Lipulekh dispute is linked with which historical treaty and later development?
o: Indo-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987 and Sri Lanka's map of 2015
Gujral Doctrine of 1996 and Bhutan's map of 2007
Sugauli Treaty of 1816 and Nepal's new map of 2020
Treaty of Peace and Friendship of 1950 and Bangladesh's map of 1974
n4d871b758d7.x: The dispute is linked to the Sugauli Treaty of 1816 and Nepal's new map issued in 2020.
n4d871b758d7.tq: Connect the dispute with both its historical reference and modern trigger.
xs: **Kalapani-Limpiyadhura-Lipulekh** is tied to the **Sugauli Treaty 1816** and **Nepal's new map 2020** — option **(3)**.
The other options pair wrong treaties and maps.
xa: In **Jun 2026** the **MEA rejected** any "third-party" role in border talks.
Nepal wants the **1950 Treaty** revised.

nc0dea5b28b2.s: The 'India Out' campaign is associated with:
nc0dea5b28b2.x: India Out is a Maldives issue; Teesta concerns Bangladesh, Rohingya Myanmar/Bangladesh and Doklam Bhutan.
xa: **Katchatheevu** (ceded **1974**) — Sri Lanka.
**Kalapani-Limpiyadhura-Lipulekh** — Nepal.

n41e432f6171.s: Among the following, which country shares the longest border with India?
n41e432f6171.x: Bangladesh shares 4,096.7 km with India, China 3,488 km, Nepal 1,751 km and Bhutan 699 km.
xa: Bangladesh is the **longest**; Afghanistan the shortest listed.

nf702754184d.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Buddhist International Tourism Circuit promoted in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It targets pilgrims from Sri Lanka, Myanmar and Thailand.
It targets pilgrims from Maldives, Nepal and Sri Lanka only.
It targets pilgrims from Nepal, Bhutan and Afghanistan only.
It targets pilgrims from Bangladesh, China and Pakistan only.
nf702754184d.x: The Buddhist International Tourism Circuit in Andhra Pradesh targets pilgrims from Sri Lanka, Myanmar and Thailand.
nf702754184d.tq: Apply the tourism-circuit concept by identifying its stated target pilgrim groups.
xs: AP's **Buddhist International Tourism Circuit** targets **Sri Lankan, Myanmar and Thai pilgrims** — option **(1)**.
The other options name countries the notes do not link to the circuit.
xa: **Myanmar** links: **Kaladan Multimodal** and the **India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway**.
Current relevance: **Tarique Rahman**'s elected government in Bangladesh (**Feb 2026**).

n57a1a72f831.s: Among the following neighbours, India shares its shortest land border (about 106 km) with:
n57a1a72f831.x: India's border with Afghanistan is only about 106 km, far shorter than with Bhutan (699 km), Myanmar (1,643 km) or Nepal (1,751 km).
n57a1a72f831.tq: Longest Bangladesh 4,096.7 km; shortest Afghanistan 106 km.
xs: The shortest border listed is with **Afghanistan**: about **106** km — option **(3)**.
xa: Longest: **Bangladesh** **4,096.7 km**.
Afghan projects: **Zaranj-Delaram** (**218 km**), **Salma Dam**, **Parliament building**.

nffff72041ae.s: The Kaladan Multimodal project connects which of the following routes?
o: Kolkata–Sittwe port–Kaladan river and road route to Mizoram
nffff72041ae.x: The Kaladan Multimodal project links Kolkata with Sittwe port and then uses the Kaladan river-road route to Mizoram.
nffff72041ae.tq: Recall the distinctive multi-modal components of the project.
xs: **Kaladan Multimodal**: **Kolkata-Sittwe port-Kaladan river-road to Mizoram** — option **(4)**.
It is with **Myanmar**.
**Moreh-Mae Sot** is the **Trilateral Highway** (via Myanmar, not Bangladesh).
xa: Exam angle: "Kaladan is between India and ___" → **Myanmar** (**APPSC 2018**).
India engages Myanmar's junta for **Act East** + **north-east security**.

nd9209d7e10f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's connectivity projects with neighbours?
o: Greater Male Connectivity is an undersea tunnel linking Male with Sri Lanka
The Akhaura-Agartala rail link connects Tripura through Bangladesh
The India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway connects Moreh (Manipur) with Mae Sot
Broad-gauge cross-border rail lines with Nepal are under construction
nd9209d7e10f.x: Greater Male Connectivity is a bridge-causeway linking Male to nearby Maldivian islands, not a tunnel to Sri Lanka.
xa: Akhaura-Agartala rail dates from **2023**.
**Jaffna / KKS (Kankesanthurai)** port in Sri Lanka: an **India-funded upgrade**.

ncc9806d21b6.s: The India-Bangladesh Friendship Pipeline is primarily a:
ncc9806d21b6.x: The India-Bangladesh Friendship Pipeline is a diesel pipeline connecting the two countries.
ncc9806d21b6.tq: Separate the energy-transport project from rail, port and power projects.
xs: The **India-Bangladesh Friendship Pipeline** is a **diesel pipeline** — option **(2)** (**UPSC**).
Railway link with Bangladesh = **Akhaura-Agartala rail**.
xa: Bangladesh power plants: **Rooppur** (nuclear) and **Maitree** (thermal, Rampal).
**Nepal to Bangladesh through the Indian grid** was the **first trilateral power transaction**.

n9bc4234bb8c.s: Operation Pawan was the operation under which the:
o: IPKF was deployed in Sri Lanka
n9bc4234bb8c.x: Operation Pawan was the Indian Peace Keeping Force operation in Sri Lanka, during which the IPKF eventually fought the LTTE.
n9bc4234bb8c.tq: Match the operation code-name with its military context.
xs: **Operation Pawan** was the **IPKF** in **Sri Lanka** — option **(2)**.
The IPKF **ended up fighting the LTTE**; last troops left **March 1990**.
**Salma Dam** is Afghanistan; wheat to Afghanistan came after **2021**.
xa: ⚠ **Cactus** = Maldives coup (**1988**); **Pawan** = Sri Lanka IPKF; **Maitri** = Nepal earthquake.
The IPKF came under the **Indo-Sri Lanka Accord (1987)**.

n49d0c20431b.s: India launched which operation to provide assistance after the Nepal earthquake of 2015?
n49d0c20431b.x: Operation Maitri was launched by India in response to the Nepal earthquake of 2015.
n49d0c20431b.tq: Directly identify the operation associated with the specific crisis.
xs: **Operation Maitri** was India's response to the **Nepal earthquake** (**2015**) — option **(2)**.
**Operation Cactus** foiled the **1988** coup in the **Maldives**.
xa: ⚠ **Cactus** = Maldives; **Pawan** = Sri Lanka IPKF; **Maitri** = Nepal earthquake.
Nepal's new **Constitution** also came in **2015** (**20 Sep**).

ncc86f2034c3.s: Operation Cactus, launched by India in 1988, was associated with the foiling of a coup in which country?
ncc86f2034c3.x: Operation Cactus was the Indian operation that foiled a coup attempt in the Maldives in 1988.
ncc86f2034c3.tq: Match the named military operation with the country in which it was conducted.
xs: **Operation Cactus** (**1988**) foiled a **coup** in the **Maldives** — option **(4)**.
Sri Lanka's operation was **Pawan** (IPKF); Nepal's was **Maitri** (**2015**).
xa: Recent Maldives: "**India Out**" campaign → ties repaired; **Favara** linked with **UPI** (**Aug 2026**).
**Greater Male Connectivity**: bridge-causeway.

n54828b1999e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Look East and Act East policies?
o: Look East was launched in the early 1990s under P.V. Narasimha Rao
Look East was originally economic, focused on trade, investment and AIFTA with ASEAN
Act East was later extended to political, strategic and cultural fields
Act East was launched in 2014 at a SAARC Summit
n54828b1999e.x: Act East was launched in 2014 at the East Asia Summit in Myanmar under PM Modi, not at a SAARC Summit.
xa: Act East added **strategic, security, cultural** aims and the wider **Indo-Pacific**.
SAARC leaders were invited to the PM's swearing-in (**May 2014**) — that is **Neighbourhood First**.
Drivers of Look East: **countering China**, **new markets**, instability in **West and Central Asia** (UPSC).

n3d2cce754cc.s: The Act East Policy was initially conceived as a/an ____ policy.
n3d2cce754cc.x: Act East began as an economic policy and was later extended to political, strategic and cultural fields with an Indo-Pacific orientation.
xa: Act East: **2014**, **Narendra Modi**; Look East: **1991-92**, Rao.
The **North-East** is the **gateway to ASEAN**.
Exam angle: "**economic origin, strategic extension**" statement pairs.

n60665b6cf2a.s:
Which of the following were drivers of India's Look East Policy?
1. Countering China's influence
2. Access to new markets
3. Instability in West and Central Asia
Which of the above is/are correct?
n60665b6cf2a.x: All three - countering China, seeking new markets and instability in West and Central Asia - were drivers of the Look East Policy.
xa: Look East: early **1990s** (**1991-92**), **P.V. Narasimha Rao**.
Upgraded to **Act East** in **2014** (East Asia Summit, Myanmar).

na19ebf2a97f.s: India's Link West (Think West) policy mainly focuses on:
o: Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific Islands
na19ebf2a97f.x: Link West, also called Think West, focuses on the Gulf, Iran and Israel.
xa: The **GCC** is India's **largest socio-economic partner**: over **$160 billion** trade, **10 million** diaspora.
PM Modi: **15 visits** to GCC states + **two to Israel** (**Mar 2026**).
**I2U2** = **India, Israel, UAE, USA**.

n3059b3351d6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's maritime visions?
o: SAGAR stands for Security and Growth for All in the Region
SAGAR was announced in Sri Lanka in 2015
MAHASAGAR (2025) stands for Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions
SHANTI was announced on 13 July 2026 by EAM Jaishankar
n3059b3351d6.x: SAGAR (2015) and MAHASAGAR (2025) were both announced in Mauritius, not Sri Lanka.
xa: ⚠ SAGAR and MAHASAGAR were both launched in **Mauritius**; **SHANTI** by **EAM Jaishankar**, not the PM.
SHANTI will be operationalised first in the **Bay of Bengal**.

n27d801e5d7e.s: SHANTI, India's normative framework for shared maritime spaces, is to be operationalised first in the:
n27d801e5d7e.x: SHANTI is a normative framework for shared maritime spaces to be operationalised first in the Bay of Bengal.
xa: Launched **13 July 2026** by **EAM Jaishankar**.
Tied to India's **UNSC 2028-29** campaign.

n95c998d4439.s: PM Modi set out India's free, open and inclusive Indo-Pacific vision at the Shangri-La Dialogue in:
n95c998d4439.x: Prime Minister Modi set out this vision, with ASEAN centrality, in his Shangri-La Dialogue keynote in June 2018.
xa: The **Shangri-La Dialogue** is organised by **IISS** (London), in **Singapore** since **2002**.
**2026 edition**: the US called India a "**critical anchor**".

nf0d2d22c7e8.s: PM Modi proposed the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) at the 14th East Asia Summit in November 2019, held at:
nf0d2d22c7e8.x: IPOI was proposed at the 14th EAS in Bangkok; it is an open, non-treaty initiative with seven pillars that builds on SAGAR.
xa: Pillars include **Maritime Security**, **Maritime Ecology**, **Maritime Resources**, **Disaster Risk Reduction and Management**.
**Spain** joined the IPOI in **Jan 2026**.

nc61a5bc4ee7.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the pillars of the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative?
nc61a5bc4ee7.x: The seven IPOI pillars include Maritime Security, Maritime Ecology, Maritime Resources, Capacity Building and Resource Sharing, Disaster Risk Reduction and Management, Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation, and Trade, Connectivity and Maritime Transport. Nuclear Disarmament Verification is not one of them.
nc61a5bc4ee7.tq: Find the unrelated sector among the formally listed seven pillars.
xs: **Nuclear Disarmament Verification** is not an IPOI pillar — option **(4)**.
The **7 pillars**: **Maritime Security**; **Maritime Ecology**; **Maritime Resources**; **Capacity Building and Resource Sharing**.
Also: **Disaster Risk Reduction and Management**; **Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation**; **Trade Connectivity and Maritime Transport**.
xa: IPOI was proposed at the **14th East Asia Summit, Bangkok** (**Nov 2019**).
IPOI is open, **non-treaty**, and builds on **SAGAR**.

n44fd6edb678.s: The Gujral Doctrine, one of the roots of Neighbourhood First, emphasised:
n44fd6edb678.x: The Gujral Doctrine emphasised non-reciprocity, non-interference and not allowing a country's territory to be used against a neighbour.
xa: **Neighbourhood First** began in **2014** with SAARC leaders at the swearing-in.
BIMSTEC leaders were invited in **2019**.

n10efe5a8da8.s: Under the SAGAR doctrine, India projects itself in the Indian Ocean Region as a:
o: Junior partner of an external power
n10efe5a8da8.x: SAGAR presents India as a net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region, partly in response to China's String of Pearls.
xa: SAGAR: **2015**, **Mauritius**; upgraded to **MAHASAGAR** in **2025**.
**IPOI** builds on SAGAR.
Debate: the US sinking of Iran's **IRIS Dena** (**Mar 2026**) challenges the "net security provider" claim.

nf0131ab79ff.s:
Which of the following are ASEAN-linked connectivity projects?
1. Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project
2. India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway
3. Akhaura-Agartala railway link
nf0131ab79ff.x: Kaladan and the Trilateral Highway are ASEAN-linked projects; the Akhaura-Agartala rail link is associated with Bangladesh.
xa: The **North-East** is the gateway to **ASEAN**.
**Kaladan** and the Trilateral Highway are also Neighbourhood First examples (UPSC).

n48f25aeaaab.s: Indian coastal surveillance radars have been installed in which of the following group of countries?
o: Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius and Seychelles
Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Mauritius and Seychelles
Sri Lanka, Maldives, Bangladesh and Mauritius
n48f25aeaaab.x: The coastal radar chain covers Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius and Seychelles.
n48f25aeaaab.tq: Identify the complete set by eliminating the country substituted from a neighbouring maritime grouping.
xs: India's **coastal surveillance radars** are in **Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius and Seychelles** — option **(1)**.
**Bangladesh** is not in the listed radar chain.
xa: Recommendation (**Mar 2026**): strengthen it along with **IORA**.
Island projects: **Agalega** (Mauritius), **Assumption Island** (Seychelles), **Hanimaadhoo** (Maldives).

nc6a6036c197.s: The Agalega airstrip and jetty project is located in:
nc6a6036c197.x: Agalega is in Mauritius; Assumption Island is in Seychelles; Uthuru Thila Falhu and Hanimaadhoo are in the Maldives.
xa: **SAGAR** (**2015**) and **MAHASAGAR** (**2025**) were both launched in **Mauritius**.
Coastal radar chain: **Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius, Seychelles**.

n442019f78ea.s: The launch of Neighbourhood First in May 2014 was symbolised by inviting the leaders of ____ to the PM's swearing-in.
n442019f78ea.x: SAARC leaders were invited to the May 2014 swearing-in; BIMSTEC leaders were invited in 2019.
xa: Aim: **physical, digital and people-to-people connectivity** across South Asia.
Roots in the **Gujral Doctrine**: non-reciprocity, non-interference.

n683c61364f0.s: The first India-Central Asia Dialogue of foreign ministers was hosted by which country and held at which city?
n683c61364f0.x: Uzbekistan hosted the first India-Central Asia Dialogue at Samarkand in 2019. Afghanistan was also invited.
n683c61364f0.tq: Pair the host country with the city rather than confusing it with the policy-launch venue.
xs: **Uzbekistan** hosted the first India-Central Asia **Dialogue** at **Samarkand** (**2019**) — option **(3)**.
**Afghanistan** was invited (**APPSC 2019**: "Uzbekistan organised the first Dialogue" = correct).
**Bishkek** is where **Connect Central Asia** was announced (**2012**).
xa: ⚠ First Dialogue = **2019**, Samarkand (ministers); first Summit = **2022**, virtual (leaders).
Uzbekistan: **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership** (**Aug 2026**).

n8a8624ee7ff.s: The first India-Central Asia Summit was held in:
n8a8624ee7ff.x: The first India-Central Asia Summit was held virtually in January 2022.
n8a8624ee7ff.tq: Combine the year with the mode of meeting to distinguish the Summit from the earlier Dialogue.
xs: The first **India-Central Asia Summit** was in January **2022**, **virtual** — option **(2)**.
**2019** was the first **Dialogue** of foreign ministers, at **Samarkand**.
xa: ⚠ Dialogue = ministers (**2019**); Summit = leaders (**2022**).
**I2U2**'s first leaders' summit was also virtual, **2022**.

n8db5e4b7cbb.s: The Shangri-La Dialogue, held in Singapore since 2002, is organised by:
n8db5e4b7cbb.x: The Shangri-La Dialogue is run by the London-based IISS and has been held in Singapore since 2002.
xa: PM Modi's keynote was in **June 2018**.
**2026**: US called India a "**critical anchor**"; US reverted **INDOPACOM to PACOM** (**Jun 2026**).

n83b366af7d7.s: Kovvada, the proposed site for Westinghouse AP1000 reactors, is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
n83b366af7d7.x: Kovvada is in Srikakulam district and is the proposed site for the Westinghouse AP1000 reactors under India-US nuclear cooperation.
xa: **AP angle**: Kovvada = proposed site for the **US-designed reactors**.
The talks run under **iCET** (**2023**), relaunched as **TRUST** in **2025**.
Nuclear path: **Hyde Act 2006** → **123 Agreement 2008** → **NSG waiver Sept 2008**.

n6a3f52e0cb7.s: Which development is regarded as the turning point in India-US relations?
n6a3f52e0cb7.x: The 2008 India-US civil nuclear deal is regarded as the turning point in the relationship.
xa: The NSG waiver **allowed civil nuclear trade**.
**AP angle**: **Kovvada** (Srikakulam) is the proposed site for US-designed **AP1000** reactors.

n822bfadfac1.s: The 'Pivot to Asia' or 'Rebalance' policy of the United States, associated with the Obama era, was announced in which year?
n822bfadfac1.x: The Pivot to Asia, also called the Rebalance, was announced in 2011 during the Obama era to shift greater US strategic attention towards the Asia-Pacific region.
n822bfadfac1.tq: Use the date as the discriminator in a doctrine-year question.
xs: The **Pivot to Asia / Rebalance** came in the **Obama era**, **2011** — option **(2)**.
It shifted **USA** focus to the **Asia-Pacific** (**UPPSC 2015**).
xa: **CAATSA** (**2017**): US sanctions on buyers of **Russian arms**.
**Pressler Amendment** (**1985**): barred US aid to **Pakistan** without nuclear certification.
Quad leaders' summits began in **2021**.

n3b3dceaf8b1.s: In the India-US context, CAATSA (2017) is mainly about US sanctions on countries that:
n3b3dceaf8b1.x: CAATSA provides for US sanctions against buyers of Russian arms; India sought a waiver over its S-400 purchase.
xa: **Hyde Act (2006)** made the nuclear deal possible under US law.
India's US-origin platforms: **P-8I, C-17, Apache, MH-60R, M777**.

n259a355354d.s: LEMOA, an India–US foundational defence agreement, was signed in:
n259a355354d.x: GSOMIA was signed in 2002, LEMOA in 2016, COMCASA in 2018 and BECA in 2020.
xa: Later steps: **INDUS-X (2023)**, **Security of Supply Arrangement (2024)**, **10-year framework (Oct 2025)**.
⚠ **2018** also gave **STA-1** status.

nf2df1bf3b6e.s: STA-1 status, granted by the US to India in 2018, gives India:
o: Licence-free access to a wide range of US military and dual-use technology
Access only to civilian nuclear technology
A veto over US defence exports to third countries
nf2df1bf3b6e.x: STA-1 allows faster, licence-free access to a wide range of US military and dual-use technology, comparable to NATO allies, without NATO membership.
xa: ⚠ **2018** = COMCASA + STA-1.
**Major Defense Partner** came in **2016**.

n65878269cb6.s: GE F414 jet engines are to be co-produced in India with:
n65878269cb6.x: GE F414 engines are to be co-produced with HAL, not BEL; iCET (2023) was relaunched as TRUST in 2025.
xa: Under iCET: **Westinghouse AP1000** + **SMRs/AMRs** talks.
**India Semiconductor Mission**: **₹76,000 crore**, **Dec 2021**.

n856ac6cd6ac.s: The United States withdrew India's Generalized System of Preferences (GSP) benefits in:
n856ac6cd6ac.x: The United States withdrew India's GSP benefits in June 2019.
n856ac6cd6ac.tq: Use the exact month-year combination to distinguish the trade-policy event from later tariff developments.
xs: The US withdrew India's **GSP** benefits in **June 2019** — option **(1)**.
GSP was not restored; exports later fell (**Apr-Nov 2025**).
xa: **Mission 500** (**Feb 2025**): double trade to **$500 billion by 2030**.
The **10-year defence framework** keeps ties steady **despite trade friction**.

n48820fed29e.s: The India–US Strategic and Commercial Dialogue dates from:
n48820fed29e.x: The Strategic and Commercial Dialogue dates from 2015; the 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue from 2018.
xa: Relationship status: **Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership** (UPSC).
**Quad** leaders' summits began in **2021**.

n935d1c2cd91.s: India-US relations are officially described as a:
n935d1c2cd91.x: India-US ties are described as a Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership.
xa: US designated India a **Major Defense Partner** in **2016**.
Mechanisms: **Strategic and Commercial Dialogue (2015)**, **2+2 (2018)**, **Quad** summits (**2021**).

n46e0a8961e1.s: India was designated by the United States as a 'Major Defense Partner' in:
n46e0a8961e1.x: The United States designated India as a Major Defense Partner in 2016.
n46e0a8961e1.tq: Use the middle-year distinction among the successive defence milestones.
xs: The US named India a **Major Defense Partner** in **2016** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **2016** = **LEMOA** + Major Defense Partner.

n3e61e63004d.s: The India Semiconductor Mission, launched in December 2021, has an outlay of:
n3e61e63004d.x: The India Semiconductor Mission was launched in December 2021 with an outlay of ₹76,000 crore.
xa: **FORGE**: **Forum on Resource, Geostrategic Engagement** (critical minerals).

n5f1d1198434.s: The Declaration on Strategic Partnership between India and Russia was signed in:
n5f1d1198434.x: India and Russia signed the Declaration on Strategic Partnership in 2000, later developing it into a Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership.
n5f1d1198434.tq: Separate the historical treaty year from the later strategic-partnership declaration.
xs: India and Russia signed the **Declaration on Strategic Partnership** in **2000** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was later upgraded to the **Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership**.
**1971** is the year of the **Indo-Soviet Treaty**, the historical anchor of ties, not the Declaration.
xa: The **23rd Annual Summit (New Delhi)** marked the **25th anniversary** of the partnership.
⚠ Labels: Russia = "Special and **Privileged**"; Japan = "Special Strategic and **Global**"; Israel = "**Special Strategic**".
Other Gulf labels: **UAE** = Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (**2017**); **Saudi Arabia** = **Strategic Partnership Council** (**2019**).
Soviet-era landmarks: **Bhilai** and **Bokaro** steel plants.

neaaa73a5018.x: India and Japan have a Special Strategic and Global Partnership.
xa: India-Japan **CEPA** has been in force since **2011**.
Japan = India's **5th-largest FDI source**; trade **$27.47 billion (FY 2025-26)**.
Defence ties: **2+2 dialogue**, **ACSA (2020)** and the **UNICORN** naval antenna.

n3702caea8e2.s: Full diplomatic relations between India and Israel were established in which year under which Indian Prime Minister?
n3702caea8e2.x: India and Israel established full diplomatic relations in 1992 during the P. V. Narasimha Rao government.
n3702caea8e2.tq: Test the exact year and the government associated with a diplomatic milestone.
xs: India and Israel established full diplomatic relations in **1992** under **P.V. Narasimha Rao** — option **(2)**.
Relations have since grown into a **Special Strategic Partnership**, with defence as a key pillar.
xa: **Narendra Modi** became the **first Indian PM to visit Israel** in **2017**; by **March 2026** he had visited **twice**.
**I2U2** = India, Israel, UAE, USA.
India-Israel trade: **$3.75 billion (FY 2024-25)**; India = Israel's **2nd-largest trading partner in Asia**.
A **Bilateral Investment Agreement** was signed in **Sept 2025**; FTA **Terms of Reference** in **Nov 2025**.

nebd5f670b9b.s: With the FTA concluded at the 16th India-EU Summit (2026), the EU became India's ____ FTA partner.
nebd5f670b9b.x: The FTA concluded at the 16th Summit made the EU India's 22nd FTA partner; a Security and Defence Partnership was also signed.
xa: **BTIA** (Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement) talks had run since **2007**.
The **Trade and Technology Council** was agreed in **2022**; first **India-EU Strategic Dialogue** in **2025**.
⚠ **16th** is also the number of the **Japan Annual Summit** (2026).
⚠ **CETA** = UK (signed **July 2025**); **BTIA** = EU.

nad568357e49.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India–UAE relations?
o: They have had a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership since 2017
The India-UAE CEPA became operational in 2022
The UAE is India's second-largest trading partner
Bilateral trade exceeded $100 billion in FY 2024-25
nad568357e49.x: With over $100 billion in trade, the UAE is India's third-largest trading partner, not second.
xa: The UAE is the **first foreign investor** in India's **SPR (Mangaluru)**.
A **Strategic Defence Partnership** LoI came during the **2026 UAE President's visit**.
The **Oman CEPA** is India's **2nd CEPA in the GCC**, after the UAE.

n1e1656ff4db.s: The India-Oman CEPA, signed in December 2025, entered into force on:
n1e1656ff4db.x: The CEPA entered into force on 1 June 2026, with Oman giving 99% duty-free access to Indian exports.
xa: India-UAE **CEPA** became operational in **2022**.
An **India-GCC FTA** is still under negotiation (**2026**).
⚠ **CETA** = UK; **CEPA** = Japan, UAE, Oman.

n3c089ea35f8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 23rd India–Russia Annual Summit (New Delhi)?
o: It marked the 25th anniversary of the strategic partnership
It set a $100 billion trade target by 2030
About 96% of bilateral trade is settled in national currencies
n3c089ea35f8.x: Russia joined the International Big Cat Alliance; I2U2 is India, Israel, UAE and USA.
xa: The partnership dates to the **Declaration on Strategic Partnership (2000)**.
Defence deals with Russia: **S-400** (**2018** deal) and the **BrahMos** JV (Brahmaputra + Moskva).
Crude imports from Russia **declined** year-on-year in Apr-Nov **2025** as India diversified sources.
⚠ **23rd** = Russia summit; **16th** = India-EU and Japan summits; **18th** = BRICS.

n83b6b2bae2f.s: BTIA, in the context of India-European Union relations, stands for:
n83b6b2bae2f.x: BTIA stands for India-EU Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement; negotiations have been underway since 2007.
n83b6b2bae2f.tq: Test the exact expansion of an international agreement acronym.
xs: **BTIA** stands for **Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement** — option **(4)**.
It is the India-**EU** trade negotiation, with talks under way since **2007** (asked in UPSC **2017**).
xa: The **India-EU FTA** was concluded at the **16th India-EU Summit** (**2026**); EU = India's **22nd FTA partner**.
⚠ **CETA** = UK; **CEPA** = Japan, UAE, Oman; **BTIA** = EU.
The **Trade and Technology Council** with the EU was agreed in **2022**.

n61b55fa0037.s: The Mumbai–Ahmedabad High Speed Rail project, supported by Japanese ODA, uses which technology?
n61b55fa0037.x: The project uses Japan's Shinkansen technology with Japanese ODA support.
xa: At the **15th Summit (2025)**, Japanese firms committed **10 trillion yen (~$67 billion)** over ten years.
The **16th India-Japan Annual Summit** was held in **2026**.
India-Japan defence: **2+2 dialogue**, **ACSA (2020)**, **UNICORN** naval antenna.

n6ae96cec7e9.s: The UAE was India's first foreign investor in which of the following?
o: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail project
The Strategic Petroleum Reserve at Mangaluru
n6ae96cec7e9.x: The UAE became the first foreign investor in India's Strategic Petroleum Reserve at Mangaluru.
n6ae96cec7e9.tq: Identify the precise project associated with a foreign investment distinction.
xs: The UAE was the **first foreign investor** in India's **Strategic Petroleum Reserve** at **Mangaluru** — option **(4)**.
The other options belong elsewhere: **INSTC** and **Kudankulam** are Russia-linked; the **Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail** is Japan-backed.
xa: India-UAE: **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (2017)**, **CEPA** operational **2022**, **BIT 2024**.
A **Strategic Defence Partnership** LoI was signed during the **2026 UAE President's visit**.
**I2U2** = India, Israel, UAE, USA.

n209207070d7.s: The II India–Africa Forum Summit (2011) was held at:
n209207070d7.x: The I (2008) and III (2015) Summits were in New Delhi; the II Summit (2011) was in Addis Ababa.
xa: The **African Union** became a permanent **G20** member under India's presidency in **2023**.
The first **Mahatma Gandhi Convention Centre** is at **Niamey, Niger (Jan 2020)**.
**e-VBAB** = **e-VidyaBharati** (tele-education) + **e-ArogyaBharati** (tele-medicine) for Africa.

n1ea2b652abf.s: The International North-South Transport Corridor connects India, Iran and Russia and runs through:
n1ea2b652abf.x: The India-Iran-Russia INSTC runs through the Iranian port of Chabahar.
n1ea2b652abf.tq: Identify the specific transit location in a regional connectivity corridor.
xs: The **INSTC** (India-Iran-Russia corridor) runs via the Iranian port of **Chabahar** — option **(2)**.
It is one of the key India-Russia connectivity projects, listed with **S-400**, **BrahMos** and **Kudankulam**.
xa: **Kudankulam** = Russia-backed nuclear plant in **Tamil Nadu**.
**BrahMos** = JV named after the **Brahmaputra** + **Moskva**.
Trade target with Russia: **$100 billion by 2030** ("**Programme 2030**").
n1ea2b652abf.fixed: INSTC's core sea leg is Mumbai-Bandar Abbas; Chabahar is only a proposed link

n14e36491d10.s: The Charter of the United Nations was signed by 50 nations at which place and on which date?
n14e36491d10.x: The UN Charter was signed by 50 nations at San Francisco on 26 June 1945.
n14e36491d10.tq: Use the place-date combination rather than recalling either detail in isolation.
xs: The UN Charter was signed by **50 nations** at **San Francisco** on **26 June 1945** — option **(2)**.
**24 October 1945** is when the Charter **came into force** (UN Day), not the signing date.
xa: The UN has **193** member states and **six official languages**: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, Spanish.
**2026** marks the **81st anniversary** of the Charter's entry into force.
India signed the Charter as **British India (June 1945)** — a founding member.

n7f09307b200.s: The Charter of the United Nations came into force on:
n7f09307b200.x: The Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, observed as UN Day. 26 June 1945 is when 50 nations signed it at San Francisco. 1 January 1942 and 10 January 1946 are not the dates given for the Charter's entry into force.
n7f09307b200.tq: Signed 26 June 1945 (San Francisco); in force 24 Oct 1945 = UN Day.
xs: The UN Charter came into force on **24 October 1945**, observed as **UN Day** — option **(2)**.
**26 June 1945** is the date **50 nations** signed it at **San Francisco**.
xa: **2026** marks the **81st anniversary**.
First SG: **Trygve Lie** (Norway, **1946**-52).
The **Trusteeship Council** has been inactive since **1994** (Palau).

n46562871ed4.s: In the April 2024 UNSC vote on full UN membership for Palestine, which country used its veto?
n46562871ed4.x: The United States vetoed the proposal, while the United Kingdom and Switzerland abstained.
xa: **Palestine** and the **Holy See** are **non-member observer states** in the UNGA.
The P5 veto is under **Article 27**; **Uniting for Peace (Res. 377, 1950)** lets the UNGA act when a veto blocks the UNSC.
In the **22 May 2026** UNGA climate resolution, India **abstained** (**141-8-28**).

n2a66795b525.s: An amendment to the UN Charter, such as one for UNSC reform, requires:
o: A simple majority of members, including all five permanent members
A two-thirds majority of members, including ratification by all five permanent members
A two-thirds majority of members, without needing the permanent members
Unanimous approval of all UN members
n2a66795b525.x: A Charter amendment needs a two-thirds majority of members and ratification by all five permanent members of the Security Council.
xa: The **P5**: China, France, Russia, UK, USA; veto under **Article 27**.
**China** opposes India's permanent seat.
The **IGN** on reform was set up in **2008** as an informal UNGA working group.

n59babea084e.s: The first Secretary-General of the United Nations was:
n59babea084e.x: Trygve Lie took office in 1946, followed by Hammarskjold (1953), U Thant (1961) and Waldheim (1972).
xa: After Waldheim: **Perez de Cuellar** (Peru, first Latin American), **Boutros Boutros-Ghali** (Egypt, first African/Arab), **Kofi Annan** (Ghana).
Then **Ban Ki-moon** (South Korea, **2007**-16) and **Antonio Guterres** (Portugal, **2017**-).
**U Thant** was the **first Asian** SG.

nbec73304fa5.s: Which of the following is NOT a purpose listed in Article 1 of the UN Charter?
nbec73304fa5.x: Sovereign equality is stated in Article 2, not Article 1.
xa: ⚠ Art. **18** = two-thirds majority on UNGA "important questions"; Art. **23** = no immediate re-election to UNSC; Art. **27** = P5 veto.
**Charter amendment** needs **two-thirds** of members, including **all P5**.
Charter signed **26 June 1945**; in force **24 October 1945**.

nd3239be22d0.s: The first African Secretary-General of the United Nations was:
nd3239be22d0.x: Boutros Boutros-Ghali of Egypt was the first African SG; Kofi Annan came after him. U Thant was the first Asian SG.
xa: Present SG: **Antonio Guterres** (Portugal), since **2017**.
The next SG's selection is under way — four candidates addressed the UNGA on **21-22 April 2026**.
The SG is the **"Chief Administrative Officer"**.

n47a8365e7c9.s: The ICJ gave its unanimous advisory opinion on climate obligations in:
n47a8365e7c9.x: The ICJ issued the unanimous climate advisory opinion in July 2025.
xa: India **abstained** (**141-8-28**) on the **May 2026** UNGA climate resolution, citing the ICJ's **July 2025** opinion.
ICJ judges: **15**, with **9-year** terms.
Seat of the ICJ: **The Hague**.

nfcb602c89de.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the principal organs of the United Nations?
o: The General Assembly has all 193 members, with one vote each
The Security Council has 15 members and its decisions bind members
The Trusteeship Council has remained active continuously since 1994
The Secretariat is headed by the Secretary-General
nfcb602c89de.x: The Trusteeship Council has been inactive since 1994, after Palau attained self-government.
xa: **ECOSOC** = **54** members, 3-year terms.
**ICJ** = principal judicial organ at **The Hague**; **15 judges**, **9-year** terms.
⚠ **15** = UNSC members and ICJ judges; **54** = ECOSOC.

n9113ee6d341.s: The 'Uniting for Peace' resolution (Resolution 377) of the UN General Assembly was adopted in:
n9113ee6d341.x: Resolution 377 was adopted in 1950 and first used in the 1956 Suez Crisis.
xa: ⚠ Trap: one source dates the resolution itself to **1956** — it was adopted in **1950**.
The P5 veto rests on **Article 27**.
Other committees: **1267** (**1999**, Al-Qaida/ISIL), **1373** (**2001**, Counter-Terrorism), **1540** (**2004**, WMD).

nf81f62c3e76.s: The UNSC Counter-Terrorism Committee set up after 9/11 was created by Resolution:
nf81f62c3e76.x: 1373 (2001) set up the Counter-Terrorism Committee; 1267 covers Al-Qaida/ISIL sanctions and 1540 WMD and non-state actors.
xa: **Masood Azhar** (Jaish-e-Mohammed) was listed under the **1267 Committee** (APPSC-G1 **2019**).
India held its first **UNSCR 1540** capacity-building programme for Asia-Pacific at **NACIN, Palasamudram (AP)**, **Feb 2025**.
**Uniting for Peace (Res. 377)** dates from **1950**.

n51d933453ce.s: The Ezulwini Consensus (2005) demands for Africa:
o: Two permanent seats with veto, plus five non-permanent seats
n51d933453ce.x: Ezulwini demands two permanent seats with veto plus five non-permanent seats for Africa.
xa: **L.69** = developing countries from Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific; India is a member.
**IGN** (set up **2008**) publishes an annual "**Elements Paper**".
**China** opposes India's permanent seat and is not in the G4 (APPSC-G1 **2012**).

ndeb59f80e64.s: How many times had India served as an elected non-permanent member of the United Nations Security Council through the 2021–22 term?
ndeb59f80e64.tq: Count the complete sequence of terms rather than the number of years served.
xs: India has served **eight** UNSC terms through **2021-22** — option **(1)** "**Eight**".
xa: India's bid for **2028-29** was launched by EAM **Jaishankar** in New York on **13 July 2026**.
The rival for **2028-29** is **Tajikistan**, backed by the **OIC**.
Non-permanent members serve **2 years** and cannot be immediately re-elected (**Art. 23**).

n142154e5e75.s: Which Indian judge served as President of the International Court of Justice during 1985–1988?
n142154e5e75.x: Nagendra Singh, one of the Indian judges of the ICJ, served as its President from 1985 to 1988.
n142154e5e75.tq: Match the office and period with the correct person rather than merely identifying an Indian judge.
xs: **Nagendra Singh** was **ICJ President** from **1985-88** — option **(4)**.
**B.N. Rau**, **R.S. Pathak** and **Dalveer Bhandari** were also Indian ICJ judges, but not President in that period.
xa: ICJ = **15 judges**, **9-year** terms, elected by **UNGA and UNSC** separately.
In the **Kulbhushan Jadhav** case (**2019**), the ICJ found Pakistan breached the **Vienna Convention on Consular Relations**.
The ICJ gave a **unanimous advisory opinion on climate obligations** in **July 2025**.

n89be88978f7.s: In the Kulbhushan Jadhav case (2019), the ICJ held that Pakistan had breached the:
n89be88978f7.x: The ICJ held that Pakistan breached the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations and ordered a review of Jadhav's conviction.
xa: ICJ's **July 2025** advisory opinion on climate obligations was **unanimous**.
India **abstained** on the **22 May 2026** UNGA climate resolution, citing that ICJ opinion.
**Nagendra Singh** was ICJ President **1985-88**.

n20fac4eb68e.s: Which commission reviewed Agenda 21 and the Rio Declaration before being replaced by the High-Level Political Forum in 2013?
o: Commission on the Status of Women
n20fac4eb68e.x: The Commission on Sustainable Development reviewed Agenda 21 and the Rio Declaration and was replaced by the High-Level Political Forum in 2013.
n20fac4eb68e.tq: Link a body with both its mandate and institutional successor.
xs: The **Commission on Sustainable Development** reviewed **Agenda 21** and the **Rio Declaration** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2018**).
It was replaced by the **High-Level Political Forum** in **2013**.
The **Commission on the Status of Women** dates from **1946**; the **Statistical** and **Narcotic Drugs** commissions are other ECOSOC bodies.
xa: **ECOSOC** = **54** members; handles economic, social and **SDG** coordination.
**CSW-70** was held in **2026**.
The **Trusteeship Council** has been inactive since **1994**.

n0d15d00f967.s: India conducted its first capacity-building programme on UNSCR 1540 for Asia-Pacific countries in February 2025 at
n0d15d00f967.x: The programme was held at the National Academy of Customs, Indirect Taxes and Narcotics (NACIN), Palasamudram, Andhra Pradesh, in February 2025.
n0d15d00f967.tq: Test the location and date together; location swaps are common traps.
xs: India's first **UNSCR 1540** capacity-building programme for Asia-Pacific was held at **NACIN, Palasamudram, Andhra Pradesh** — option **(2)**, in **Feb 2025**.
Palasamudram is in **AP**, not Telangana or abroad.
xa: **Resolution 1540 (2004)** aims at stopping **WMD** reaching **non-state actors**.
**1267 (1999)** = Al-Qaida/ISIL sanctions; **1373 (2001)** = Counter-Terrorism Committee.
This is the topic's **AP angle**.

n05b44557c68.s: Who was the first woman to serve as India's Permanent Representative to the United Nations in New York?
n05b44557c68.x: Ruchira Kamboj was the first woman Permanent Representative of India to the UN (BPSC 2024). Sushma Swaraj was External Affairs Minister, not PR. Nirupama Rao was Foreign Secretary. Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit was President of the UN General Assembly, not India's PR in New York.
n05b44557c68.tq: First woman PR of India to the UN = Ruchira Kamboj.
xs: **Ruchira Kamboj** was the first woman **Permanent Representative of India to the UN** — option **(2)**.
This was asked as a FIRST in BPSC **2024**; the PR is India's envoy at the UN in **New York**.
xa: Other India-at-UN firsts: **Atal Bihari Vajpayee** gave the first UNGA speech in **Hindi** (**1977**).
India signed the Charter as **British India (June 1945)**.
India's UNSC **2028-29** bid was launched by EAM **Jaishankar** on **13 July 2026**.

nbb459eac5b9.s: The Information for All Programme is associated with which organisation?
nbb459eac5b9.x: The Information for All Programme, or IFAP, is a UNESCO programme.
nbb459eac5b9.tq: Match the programme title to the responsible agency.
xs: The **Information for All Programme (IFAP)** is a **UNESCO** programme — option **(3)**.
It was asked in **2019**; **UNDP**, **ILO** and **UNEP** have development, labour and environment mandates.
xa: Other UNESCO programmes: **Man and the Biosphere (MAB)**; UNESCO leads **SDG-4** (Education 2030).
UNESCO reports: **GEM**, **UNESCO Science Report**, **World Water Development Report**.
UNESCO HQ: **Paris**; **194 members + 12 associate members**.

n8264f3c92c6.s: Which report is published by UNFPA?
n8264f3c92c6.x: The State of World Population is a flagship report of UNFPA.
n8264f3c92c6.tq: Match the report title with the agency’s mandate.
xs: The **State of World Population** is a **UNFPA** report — option **(4)**.
**World Employment and Social Outlook** = **ILO**; **Human Development Report** = **UNDP**; **Emissions Gap Report** = **UNEP**.
xa: **UNFPA** is a **fund/programme** created by the GA.
UNESCO reports: **GEM**, **Science Report**, **World Water Development Report**.
**SOFI** is joint: **FAO, IFAD, UNICEF, WFP, WHO**.

n2cb30c2302e.s: The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), set up after the 1972 Stockholm Conference, is headquartered at:
n2cb30c2302e.x: UNEP was created in 1972 following the Stockholm Conference and has its HQ at Nairobi, Kenya. Geneva hosts WHO/ILO/ITU, Vienna hosts UNIDO/IAEA, and New York hosts UNICEF.
xs: **UNEP**, set up in **1972** after the **Stockholm Conference**, is headquartered at **Nairobi, Kenya** — option **(2)**.
**Geneva** hosts WHO/ILO/ITU, **Vienna** hosts UNIDO/IAEA, and **New York** hosts UNICEF.
xa: UNEP HQ was asked twice (**2018**, **2025**).
**Emissions Gap 2025**: current policies → ~**2.8°C**; full NDCs → **2.3-2.5°C**.
**UN-Habitat** also has its HQ in **Nairobi**.

n45af14189b0.s: The World Heritage Convention was adopted in which year?
n45af14189b0.x: The World Heritage Convention was adopted in 1972.
n45af14189b0.tq: Use the direct year-recall approach for a foundational convention.
xs: The **World Heritage Convention** was adopted in **1972** — option **(2)**.
**1981** is a UNHCR Nobel year and **1988** the UN Peacekeeping Forces' Nobel — not the Convention.
xa: Inscription needs a **Tentative List** entry + **Outstanding Universal Value** + **1 of 10 criteria**.
**WHL (July 2026)**: **1,273 properties in 173 countries**; **Italy 62**, China **61**.
The **ASI** is India's nodal agency for World Heritage.

n1b47e778d8d.s: Which of the following is a specialised agency of the United Nations?
n1b47e778d8d.x: IFAD is a UN specialised agency as well as an international financial institution serving rural poor populations.
n1b47e778d8d.tq: Distinguish specialised agencies from funds and programmes.
xs: The **International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD)** is a UN **specialised agency** — option **(4)**; it is also an **international financial institution** for the rural poor.
**WFP**, **UNICEF** and **UNDP** are **funds and programmes** created by the GA with **voluntary funding**, not specialised agencies.
xa: IFAD is headquartered in **Rome** (**1977**).
⚠ **Rome** = FAO, IFAD, WFP; **Nairobi** = UNEP, UN-Habitat.
⚠ **IAEA, WTO, OPCW** are **related organisations**, not specialised agencies.

n07d85b79c12.s: The protection of refugees is the mandate of:
n07d85b79c12.x: Refugees are UNHCR's mandate; UNICEF deals with children's rights and UNEP with climate, biodiversity and pollution.
xa: **WFP** won the Nobel Peace Prize in **2020**.
India signed a **5-year rice supply agreement with WFP** (**2026**).
**UNEP** HQ: **Nairobi, Kenya** (**1972**, after the Stockholm Conference).

n389a8303c62.s: The Global Environment Facility, established in 1992, is run in partnership by which of the following?
n389a8303c62.x: The GEF is a financial mechanism operated in partnership by UNDP, UNEP and the World Bank.
n389a8303c62.tq: Use the three-body partnership as the identifying feature.
xs: The **GEF (1992)** is a financial mechanism run in partnership by **UNDP, UNEP and World Bank** — option **(1)**.
The other trios (ILO/FAO/IFAD, UNICEF/UNHCR/UNESCO, WHO/WFP/UNFPA) have no role in the GEF per the notes.
xa: **UNDP** = development + poverty; co-builds the **Global MPI** with **OPHI**.
**UNEP** = climate, biodiversity, pollution; publishes the **Emissions Gap Report**.
The **World Bank** and **IMF** are counted among the **specialised agencies**.

n01210833e81.s: India has NOT ratified which pair of ILO Fundamental Conventions?
n01210833e81.x: India has not ratified C87 (Freedom of Association) and C98 (Right to Organise and Collective Bargaining); the other pairs are ratified.
xa: ⚠ India has **not ratified C87, C98, C189**.
**C189** = **Domestic Workers Convention (2011)**, adopted by the ILC.
ILO-UNICEF estimate: **160 million** child labourers globally.

n2b38aecc039.s: According to the ILO–UNICEF joint estimate for 2020 (released 2021), the number of child labourers globally was approximately:
n2b38aecc039.x: The ILO–UNICEF joint estimate places the number of child labourers globally at 160 million.
n2b38aecc039.tq: Place the figure correctly by checking the order of magnitude.
xs: The **ILO-UNICEF** joint estimate puts global child labourers at **160 million** — option **(3)**.
It is a **joint** estimate of the labour agency (**ILO**) and the children's-rights fund (**UNICEF**).
xa: India ratified the child-labour conventions **C138** and **C182** in **2017**.
**ILO Employment and Social Trends 2026**: unemployment **4.9% (186 million)**; **284 million** workers below **$3/day**.
UNICEF's mandate: **children's rights**.
n2b38aecc039.fixed: 2020 estimate = 160 mn; the 2025 release (for 2024) gives ~138 mn, so pin the year

n478528dc174.s: Sarnath was inscribed as India's 45th World Heritage Site in July 2026 at the World Heritage Committee session held in:
n478528dc174.x: Sarnath was inscribed at the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee in Busan, South Korea, in July 2026.
xa: **Hoysala temples** (Karnataka) were inscribed in **Sep 2023**.
The **ASI** looks after **28** WH properties among **3,688** centrally protected monuments.
First Indian WH site: **Ajanta** (with Ellora), **1983**.

n25a6be63564.s: The first Indian World Heritage site, inscribed along with Ellora, was:
n25a6be63564.x: Ajanta, along with Ellora, was India's first World Heritage site inscription in 1983.
n25a6be63564.tq: Use the historical first rather than the latest inscription in the same subject area.
