n66ab2eeb066.s: To meet its TRIPS obligations, India enacted the Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act in:
n66ab2eeb066.x: The GI Act, 1999 was enacted to meet TRIPS obligations; the Patents Act was amended in 2005 for the same purpose.
xa: **TRIPS (1995)** sets **minimum global IPR standards**.
India's flexibilities: **Section 3(d)** (anti-evergreening) + **compulsory licensing**.
First compulsory licence: **Natco-Bayer** (**2012**).

n177f977b14a.s: The Doha Declaration on TRIPS and public health affirmed that TRIPS:
o: Prevents members from regulating medicines in public interest
Must not stop members from protecting public health
Eliminates compulsory licensing by developing countries
n177f977b14a.x: The Doha Declaration of 2001 affirmed that TRIPS must not prevent members from taking measures to protect public health.
n177f977b14a.tq: Test the public-health flexibility principle against restrictive distractors.
xs: The **Doha Declaration (2001)** said TRIPS **must not stop members from protecting public health** — option **(3)**.
So it supports, not eliminates, flexibilities like **compulsory licensing**.
xa: First compulsory licence in India: **Natco-Bayer** (**2012**).
**India-South Africa** proposed a **COVID TRIPS waiver** (**2020**); **MC12** adopted a limited waiver (**2022**).
**Section 3(d)** is India's anti-evergreening clause.

n4a671235a9a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about WTO disputes involving India?
o: The USA challenged the JNNSM solar domestic-content rules and India lost in 2016
The EU, Japan and Chinese Taipei won a panel against India's ICT tariffs in 2023
The dispute over India's export subsidy schemes (MEIS, SEZ) was brought by the EU
The panel in the export subsidy (MEIS, SEZ) dispute ruled in 2019
n4a671235a9a.x: The MEIS/SEZ export subsidy case was brought by the USA, not the EU (panel 2019).
xa: India's appeals sit "**into the void**" as the **Appellate Body** lacks members.
The US **blocked Appellate Body appointments**.
**SCM** classes subsidies as prohibited, actionable or non-actionable.

n1b4752aa66c.s: The WTO moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions lapsed on:
n1b4752aa66c.x: The moratorium lapsed on 31 March 2026 after MC14 failed to extend it; 66 members then signed a plurilateral agreement banning such duties.
xa: The moratorium had run since **1998**.
The **TRIPS non-violation** moratorium (since **1995**) also lapsed at MC14.
**Investment Facilitation for Development** has **120+** backers.

n0615f17a3b9.s: India's core demand in the WTO food-security negotiations is a permanent solution for:
n0615f17a3b9.x: India's core food-security demand is a permanent solution for public stockholding (PSH).
xa: **AoA** governs market access, **domestic support** and **export subsidies**.
India also defends **SDT** for developing countries.
**Fisheries Phase 2** was deferred to the **General Council**.

n3ea7e56b76d.s: India opposes bringing which of the following plurilateral initiatives into the WTO rulebook?
n3ea7e56b76d.x: Investment Facilitation for Development, backed by more than 120 members, is a plurilateral initiative that India opposes bringing into the WTO rulebook.
xa: **66 members** signed the plurilateral E-commerce Agreement banning duties on electronic transmissions.
The multilateral e-commerce moratorium lapsed on **31 March 2026**.
The only new multilateral agreements: **Trade Facilitation** + **Fisheries Subsidies**.

n5accf91798f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference (Yaoundé, March 2026)?
o: A permanent solution on public stockholding was agreed
No fisheries subsidies Phase 2 deal was reached
n5accf91798f.x: MC14 ended without a permanent solution on public stockholding; both moratoria lapsed and no fisheries Phase 2 deal was reached.
xa: The e-commerce moratorium dated from **1998**; the TRIPS one from **1995**.
Fisheries Phase 2 (overcapacity, overfishing) was **deferred to the General Council**.
**MC13** was at **Abu Dhabi (Feb 2024)**.

nde56662990e.s: Which two agreements are identified as the only new WTO agreements concluded in the first 30 years of the organisation?
o: Trade Facilitation Agreement and Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
nde56662990e.x: The Trade Facilitation Agreement and the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies are identified as the only new WTO agreements in that period.
nde56662990e.tq: Use the word “only” carefully to identify the complete pair rather than older Uruguay Round agreements.
xs: The only new WTO agreements in **30** years are the **Trade Facilitation Agreement** and the **Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies** — option **(1)**.
**AoA, TRIPS, GATS, TRIMS, SPS, TBT** all came with the **Uruguay Round** package.
xa: **Fisheries Phase 2** (overcapacity, overfishing) remained unresolved at **MC14** → deferred to the **General Council**.
The WTO began on **1 January 1995**.
Plurilaterals like **Investment Facilitation for Development** are disputed; **India opposes** bringing them in.

n8d176c522e1.s: Section 3(d) of India's Patents Act, used as a TRIPS flexibility, is aimed against:
n8d176c522e1.x: India used Section 3(d) against evergreening, along with compulsory licensing, as TRIPS flexibilities for public health.
xa: First compulsory licence: **Natco-Bayer** (**2012**).
The **Doha Declaration (2001)** backs public-health measures under TRIPS.
India amended the **Patents Act** in **2005** to comply with TRIPS.

n02f7fd2b47e.s: Which one of the following organisations was established through the Bangkok Declaration of 1967?
n02f7fd2b47e.x: ASEAN was established in 1967 through the Bangkok Declaration.
n02f7fd2b47e.tq: Identify the organisation from its founding declaration and year.
xs: **ASEAN** was set up by the **1967 Bangkok Declaration** — option **(3)**, by Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore and Thailand.
**SAARC** came from the **Dhaka** Charter (**1985**); **BIMSTEC** from a **1997** Bangkok Declaration; **SCO** from **Shanghai** (**2001**).
xa: ASEAN Secretariat: **Jakarta**; members now **11** with **Timor-Leste** (**2025**).
⚠ Two "Bangkok Declarations": **1967** = ASEAN; **1997** = BIMSTEC (as BIST-EC).
**Myanmar** is the only ASEAN state bordering India.

n9832718fde1.s: BIMSTEC, set up through the 1997 Bangkok Declaration, has its Secretariat at:
n9832718fde1.x: BIMSTEC originated through the 1997 Bangkok Declaration and its Secretariat is in Dhaka.
xa: It began as **BIST-EC**: Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Thailand.
BIMSTEC has **7** members; **Nepal + Bhutan** joined in **2004**.
⚠ BIMSTEC Secretariat = **Dhaka**; ASEAN = **Jakarta**.

nf8d1fc8a893.s: The Council of Europe, founded in 1949, is headquartered at:
nf8d1fc8a893.x: The Council of Europe sits at Strasbourg; Brussels is the seat of the EU.
xa: Council of Europe: **47** members (asked **2019**); **Russia expelled March 2022**.
EU: **27** members; last to join **Croatia (2013)**.
**Article 50** TEU (Lisbon Treaty) = exit clause, used for **Brexit**.

n1526ada661b.s: How many members does SAARC have?
n1526ada661b.x: SAARC comprises eight members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
n1526ada661b.tq: Recall the exact membership count and verify it against the member list.
xs: SAARC has **8** members — option **(3)**.
It includes **every land neighbour of India except China** (and Myanmar).
xa: SAARC Charter: **Dhaka, 8 Dec 1985**; Secretariat: **Kathmandu**.
SAARC observers: **China, Japan, USA, EU, Iran**.
⚠ "Number of members" is a favourite: SAARC **8**, BIMSTEC **7**, ASEAN **11**, Council of Europe **47**.

n5774aa914d8.s: With the admission of Timor-Leste in 2025, the membership of ASEAN became:
n5774aa914d8.x: Timor-Leste joined ASEAN in 2025, taking its membership to 11.
xa: GCC (**1981**, Riyadh): Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman.
⚠ Newest: ASEAN = **Timor-Leste**; EU = **Croatia**; NATO = **Finland + Sweden**.
The **East Asia Summit** has **19** members, incl. all **11** ASEAN states.

n8c702191390.s: The headquarters of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation is located at
n8c702191390.x: The SAARC Secretariat is located in Kathmandu, while its Charter was signed in Dhaka.
n8c702191390.tq: Use the location trap involving the Charter venue and Secretariat headquarters.
xs: The SAARC Secretariat is at **Kathmandu** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Trap: the Charter was signed at **Dhaka** (**1985**), which also hosts the **BIMSTEC** Secretariat.
**Thimphu** hosts the **SAARC Development Fund**; **Colombo** hosted the **5th BIMSTEC Summit**.
xa: The **18th SAARC summit** (Kathmandu, **2014**) is the last one held.
The **19th** (Islamabad, **2016**) was cancelled after **Uri**.
**SAFTA** replaced **SAPTA**; in force **1 Jan 2006**.

n0aca886879a.s: Which one of the following is NOT an observer of SAARC?
n0aca886879a.x: SAARC's observers include China, Japan, the USA, the EU and Iran. Russia is not a SAARC observer.
n0aca886879a.tq: SAARC observers incl. China, Japan, USA, EU, Iran - not Russia.
xs: **Russia** is NOT a SAARC observer — option **(4)**.
SAARC observers: **China, Japan, USA, EU, Iran**.
xa: ⚠ China is a SAARC **observer** but **not** a member of **BIMSTEC**.
Russia was **expelled** from the **Council of Europe** (**March 2022**).
Russia is in the **East Asia Summit**'s **19** members.

ncee47dd4392.s: The Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) is associated with which of the following organisations?
ncee47dd4392.x: RATS is the counter-terrorism structure of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.
ncee47dd4392.tq: Identify the organisation from the specialised institutional function.
xs: **RATS** is the counter-terror structure of the **Shanghai Cooperation Organisation** — option **(4)**.
RATS is located at **Tashkent**, while the SCO HQ is **Beijing**.
xa: SCO was founded in **2001** at **Shanghai**.
India and Pakistan became full SCO members in **2017 (Astana)**.
⚠ IORA's Secretariat is at **Ebene, Mauritius**; NATO dates from **1949**.

n7cfe48dc464.s: Which country was expelled from the Council of Europe in March 2022?
n7cfe48dc464.x: Russia was expelled from the Council of Europe, which had 47 members in 2019, in March 2022.
xa: Council of Europe: founded **1949**, HQ **Strasbourg**.
⚠ **Strasbourg** = Council of Europe; **Brussels** = EU.
**NATO** also dates from **1949**.

na9a9ab7a0d0.s: Which country was the latest to join the European Union?
na9a9ab7a0d0.x: Croatia was the last country to join the European Union, in 2013.
na9a9ab7a0d0.tq: Recall the latest enlargement rather than an earlier enlargement round.
xs: **Croatia** (**2013**) was the last country to join the EU — option **(4)**.
The UK left the EU on **31 Jan 2020** (**Brexit**).
xa: EU: **27** members; HQ **Brussels**.
⚠ Newest: ASEAN = **Timor-Leste**; NATO = **Finland + Sweden**.
**Article 50** TEU = exit clause.

naf0c245ac96.s: Which is the only ASEAN country that shares a land border with India?
naf0c245ac96.x: Myanmar is the only ASEAN country sharing a land border with India.
xa: Myanmar joined **ASEAN + BIMSTEC** in **1997**.
China is a SAARC **observer**, with Japan, USA, EU and Iran.
BIMSTEC's **7**: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand.

n236aee3db8f.s: 'Bangkok Vision 2030' belongs to which regional grouping?
n236aee3db8f.x: Bangkok Vision 2030 belongs to BIMSTEC; the South Asia Satellite and COVID emergency fund were India's SAARC initiatives.
xa: In BIMSTEC, **India leads security** (counter-terrorism, disaster management, energy).
India gave a **21-point Action Plan** at the 6th BIMSTEC Summit.
The last SAARC summit was the **18th** (Kathmandu, **2014**).

nbeb163c4aa0.s: Which one of the following countries has not ratified the BBIN Motor Vehicles Agreement?
nbeb163c4aa0.x: The BBIN Motor Vehicles Agreement was signed by Bangladesh, Bhutan, India and Nepal at Thimphu in 2015, but Bhutan has not ratified it.
nbeb163c4aa0.tq: Distinguish signing from ratification and identify the exceptional member.
xs: **Bhutan** has not ratified the **BBIN Motor Vehicles Agreement** — option **(2)**.
The MVA was signed at **Thimphu** in **2015** by **Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal**.
xa: ⚠ **Thimphu** = BBIN MVA + **SAARC Development Fund**.
Bhutan and Nepal joined **BIMSTEC** in **2004**.
**SAFTA** in force **1 Jan 2006**.

ndf0c9f526ca.s: Which two countries joined BIMSTEC in 2004?
ndf0c9f526ca.x: Nepal and Bhutan joined in 2004; BIMSTEC began in 1997 as BIST-EC with Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
xa: Full name: **Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation**.
BIMSTEC sectors were cut from **14** to **7**, each with a lead country.
Secretariat: **Dhaka**.

nbcb6bba0472.s: The BIMSTEC Charter was adopted at the
nbcb6bba0472.x: The BIMSTEC Charter was adopted at the Fifth Summit held at Colombo in 2022.
nbcb6bba0472.tq: Match the summit number, venue and year with the institutional development.
xs: The **BIMSTEC Charter** was adopted at the **5th Summit, Colombo (2022)** — option **(4)**.
The **6th Summit, Bangkok (2025)** gave **Bangkok Vision 2030** and the **Maritime Transport Cooperation Agreement**.
xa: ⚠ BIMSTEC Charter = **Colombo**; Bangkok Vision 2030 = **Bangkok**; BBIN MVA = **Thimphu**.
**Bangladesh** chairs BIMSTEC for **2024-26**.
India's **21-point Action Plan** came at the 6th Summit.

nf5b6691218f.s: India opted out of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership in
nf5b6691218f.x: India opted out of RCEP in 2019.
nf5b6691218f.tq: Identify the withdrawal year from closely spaced policy dates.
xs: India **opted out of RCEP** in **2019** — option **(3)**.
**RCEP** dates from **2019**; India stayed with its **ASEAN** trade track via **AIFTA**.
xa: **AIFTA (goods)** has been in force since **2010**.
India seeks early completion of the **AITIGA review** (**32nd ARF**, July **2025**).
India-ASEAN: **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership** (**2022**).

n45bf7e09abb.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about BIMSTEC?
o: Each of its sectors has a lead country
Its sectors were expanded from 7 to 14
Myanmar earlier led the energy sector
n45bf7e09abb.x: BIMSTEC reduced its sectors from 14 to 7, not the other way round.
xa: India's security lead covers **counter-terrorism**, **disaster management** and **energy**.
First BIMSTEC army exercise: **MILEX 2018, Pune**.
BIMSTEC weaknesses: **few summits**, **broad focus**, **Rohingya + border issues**, **BCIM rivalry**.

ndaa8ea0066f.s: MILEX, the first BIMSTEC army exercise (2018), was held at:
ndaa8ea0066f.x: MILEX, the first BIMSTEC army exercise, was held at Pune in 2018.
xa: ⚠ BIMSTEC has a **military component** (MILEX); SAARC and ASEAN lack it.
**India leads security** in BIMSTEC.
India's **21-point Action Plan** came at the **6th Summit** (Bangkok, **2025**).

n9d9e30c7f2f.s: The BIMSTEC Charter was adopted at the 5th BIMSTEC Summit (2022) held at:
n9d9e30c7f2f.x: The Charter was adopted at the 5th Summit in Colombo (2022); the 6th Summit was at Bangkok in April 2025.
xa: 6th Summit theme: "**Prosperous, Resilient, and Open**"; outcome **Bangkok Vision 2030**.
The **Maritime Transport Cooperation Agreement** was signed there.
1st **BIMSTEC Youth Summit**: **Gandhinagar** (**Feb 2025**).

n9240bb0797c.s: India became a summit-level partner of ASEAN in:
n9240bb0797c.x: India became a sectoral partner in 1992, full dialogue partner in 1996, summit-level partner in 2002 and Comprehensive Strategic Partner in 2022.
xa: **AIFTA (goods)** came into force in **2010**.
India opted out of **RCEP** in **2019**.
ASEAN Regional Forum founded **1994**; East Asia Summit **2005**.

n77f7244edaa.s: The 19th SAARC Summit, scheduled at Islamabad in 2016, was cancelled after the
n77f7244edaa.x: The 19th SAARC Summit at Islamabad was cancelled after the Uri attack. The 18th Summit at Kathmandu in 2014 remains the last summit.
n77f7244edaa.tq: Link the cancelled event to its immediate stated cause.
xs: The **19th SAARC Summit** (**Islamabad, 2016**) was cancelled after the **Uri** attack — option **(2)**.
So the **18th summit** (**Kathmandu, 2014**) remains the **last** SAARC summit.
xa: SAARC and BIMSTEC are both constrained by India's tensions with **Islamabad** and **Dhaka**.
No neighbourhood leader attended the **Sep 2026** BRICS Summit.
India's SAARC proposals: **South Asia Satellite** (**2017**), **COVID emergency fund** (**2020**).

n97de81bf6b8.s: The East Asia Summit, founded at Kuala Lumpur in 2005, has how many members?
n97de81bf6b8.x: The EAS has 19 members: 11 ASEAN states plus India, China, Japan, the US, Russia, Australia, New Zealand and South Korea.
xa: The **20th EAS** (Kuala Lumpur **2025**) adopted the **Kuala Lumpur Declaration**.
**1994** = ASEAN Regional Forum.
ASEAN Secretariat: **Jakarta**.

n88193132b58.s: The 20th East Asia Summit held at Kuala Lumpur in 2025 adopted the
n88193132b58.x: The 20th East Asia Summit adopted the Kuala Lumpur Declaration in 2025.
n88193132b58.tq: Distinguish the declaration of the East Asia Summit from BIMSTEC’s Bangkok Vision 2030.
xs: The **20th East Asia Summit** (Kuala Lumpur, **2025**) adopted the **Kuala Lumpur Declaration** — option **(4)**.
**Bangkok Vision 2030** is BIMSTEC's; **Colombo** gave the BIMSTEC Charter; **Dhaka** the SAARC Charter.
xa: EAS founded **2005**, Kuala Lumpur; **19** members.
The **32nd ARF** was also held in **Kuala Lumpur** (**July 2025**).
**Timor-Leste** became ASEAN's **11th** member (**2025**).

n9af08d8c8e1.s: How many member states does the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), formed in 1997, have?
n9af08d8c8e1.x: IORA, formed in 1997, has 23 member states.
xa: **Nelson Mandela** was among IORA's leaders.
IORA Secretariat: **Ebene, Mauritius**.
**India is chair** of IORA.

n42b94c8b262.s: Which of the following countries is a member of the G7?
n42b94c8b262.x: Japan is one of the seven G7 members, along with the United States, United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy and Canada. China, India and Russia are not G7 members.
n42b94c8b262.tq: Separate formal membership from regular outreach participation.
xs: **Japan** is a member of the **G7** — option **(3)**.
**Russia**, **China** and **India** are common distractors: none is a G7 member; India is only an **outreach invitee**.
xa: Russia joined in **1997-98** to form the **G8**; suspended in **2014** after Crimea.
Other non-member distractors: **Netherlands**, **New Zealand**.
The **EU** attends G7 meetings.

nfdf72ca57e7.s: Which of the following is NOT a Quad initiative?
o: Indo-Pacific Partnership for Maritime Domain Awareness
nfdf72ca57e7.x: The Quad initiatives include the Quad Vaccine Partnership, the Critical and Emerging Technologies group and IPMDA. The Contingent Reserve Arrangement is associated with BRICS.
nfdf72ca57e7.tq: Identify the institution belonging to a different grouping.
xs: The **Contingent Reserve Arrangement** is NOT a Quad initiative — option **(2)**; it is a **BRICS** pool (**2014**, **$100 billion**).
Quad initiatives: **Quad Vaccine Partnership**, **IPMDA**, **Critical and Emerging Technologies** group.
xa: **IPMDA** = Indo-Pacific Partnership for Maritime Domain Awareness (**2022**).
Quad origin: **Tsunami Core Group** after the **2004** tsunami.
BRICS also runs the **NDB** (HQ **Shanghai**).

n2332365b78c.s: Which one of the following groupings consists of India, Israel, the United Arab Emirates and the United States?
n2332365b78c.x: I2U2 comprises India, Israel, the UAE and the United States.
n2332365b78c.tq: Identify a grouping from its complete membership rather than its acronym alone.
xs: **I2U2** = **India, Israel, UAE, USA** — option **(4)**.
**BASIC** = Brazil, South Africa, India, China; **IBSA** = India, Brazil, South Africa; **MIKTA** = Mexico, Indonesia, South Korea, Türkiye, Australia.
xa: India is **not** in MIKTA.
India **is** a member of I2U2, IBSA and BASIC.
**G4** = India, Brazil, Germany, Japan (UNSC bid).

n0d2ce55b311.s: Which of the following countries is a member of BASIC but not of IBSA?
n0d2ce55b311.x: BASIC comprises Brazil, South Africa, India and China, whereas IBSA comprises India, Brazil and South Africa. China is therefore the additional BASIC member.
n0d2ce55b311.tq: Compare overlapping memberships and identify the additional country.
xs: **China** is in **BASIC** but not **IBSA** — option **(2)**.
**BASIC** = Brazil, South Africa, India, China; **IBSA** = India, Brazil, South Africa — so India, Brazil and South Africa are in both.
xa: BASIC formed in **2009** before **COP15**.
IBSA formed in **2003** (**Brasilia Declaration**).
China chairs BRICS in **2027**.

nf8f75cbcc76.s: Indonesia, which joined BRICS in 2025, is also a member of:
nf8f75cbcc76.x: Indonesia is a member of BRICS (2025) and MIKTA, but not of the Quad or IBSA.
xa: Quad = **India, USA, Japan, Australia**; IBSA = **India, Brazil, South Africa**.
MIKTA = **Mexico, Indonesia, South Korea, Türkiye, Australia**.
Indonesia was in the G20 **Troika** of **2022** (with Italy and India).

n0cf76f63911.s: What is India's position on de-dollarisation in the context of BRICS?
o: India backs an immediate common BRICS currency
India has made de-dollarisation a core foreign-policy aim
India has left BRICS over de-dollarisation
n0cf76f63911.x: India avoids de-dollarisation even while participating in BRICS.
xa: India is a BRICS **founder** and hosted the **18th Summit** (**2026**).
**Russia, China, Iran** are seen as the "**anti-West**" wing.
India's multi-alignment = **bridge** between the Global South and the North.

nd386f250d1c.s: The first G20 Leaders' Summit was held in 2008 at:
nd386f250d1c.x: The first G20 Leaders' Summit was held in Washington, D.C., in 2008, in the context of the global financial crisis.
nd386f250d1c.tq: Match the first leaders' summit with its venue and crisis context.
xs: The first G20 **leaders' summit** was in **Washington, D.C.** in **2008** — option **(4)**, during the global financial crisis.
**Berlin** hosted the first (ministerial) meeting in **1999**; **Cologne** foreshadowed it; **New Delhi** hosted in **2023**.
xa: G20 = **19 countries + EU + African Union** (AU since **2023**).
G20 share: **~85% GDP**, **>75% trade**, **two-thirds** of population.
2025 G20 meetings: **Johannesburg, South Africa**.

n6e055d1e63a.s: The term “BRIC” was coined in 2001 by:
o: Amartya Sen of the United Nations
Joseph Stiglitz of the World Bank
n6e055d1e63a.x: The term BRIC was coined in 2001 by Jim O'Neill of Goldman Sachs.
n6e055d1e63a.tq: Match the coined term with its author and institution.
xs: The term "**BRIC**" was coined in **2001** by **Jim O'Neill of Goldman Sachs** — option **(4)**.
BRIC was **formalised in 2006**.
xa: First BRIC summit: **Yekaterinburg, Russia, 2009**.
**South Africa** joined in **2011**, making it BRICS.
BRICS now has **10** members (+ **Saudi Arabia** ambiguous).

nd313e2d1540.s: The first BRIC summit was held in 2009 at:
nd313e2d1540.x: The first BRIC summit was at Yekaterinburg, Russia, in 2009; BRIC was formalised in 2006 and South Africa joined in 2011.
xa: Term "BRIC": **2001**, **Jim O'Neill**.
UKPSC **2024**: "first summit **2009** in Russia" was correct; "BRICS = **46%** of global trade" was wrong.
**Indonesia** joined BRICS in **2025**.

nd8be01724e7.s: BASIC was formed in 2009 before which international climate conference?
nd8be01724e7.x: The BASIC grouping was formed in 2009 before the Copenhagen COP15.
nd8be01724e7.tq: Anchor the grouping to the conference immediately associated with its formation.
xs: **BASIC** was formed in **2009** before **COP15 at Copenhagen** — option **(2)**.
Its members are **Brazil, South Africa, India, China** — the initials spell BASIC.
xa: BASIC stands for **CBDR-RC** and **climate finance from developed countries**.
⚠ **China** is in BASIC but **not in IBSA**.

na3d7c730c37.s: The first Quad leaders' summit, in March 2021, was held:
na3d7c730c37.x: The first Quad leaders' summit was virtual (March 2021); the first in-person summit was in Washington in September 2021.
xa: The Quad was **revived in 2017**.
Quad initiatives: **Quad Vaccine Partnership**, **Critical and Emerging Technologies** group, **IPMDA (2022)**.
⚠ **New Delhi, Sep 2023** = G20 Summit, not Quad.

nb11c8922f89.s: Which of the following is one of the five pillars of the Colombo Security Conclave?
nb11c8922f89.x: The five pillars are maritime safety and security, counter-terrorism and radicalisation, trafficking and organised crime, cyber security and critical infrastructure, and HADR.
xa: CSC began as a **maritime trilateral** (**2011**).
It was renamed in **2020**; secretariat **Colombo**.
Observer: **Seychelles**.

o: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam – One Earth, One Family, One Future
Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability
n6302719d4f2.x: India's 2026 BRICS theme is “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”
n6302719d4f2.tq: Distinguish the BRICS theme from India's separate G20 theme.
xs: India's **2026 BRICS** theme is "**Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability**" — option **(4)**.
"**Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam - One Earth, One Family, One Future**" was India's **G20 (2023)** theme.
xa: The theme's initials spell out **BRICS**.
Summit: **New Delhi, 12 Sep 2026**, Bharat Mandapam.
India also hosted BRICS in **2012**, **2016** and **2021** (virtual).

n76f42864a5a.s: The Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII) was launched by the G7 in:
n76f42864a5a.x: The G7 launched PGII in Germany in 2022 as an infrastructure plan and a counter to the Belt and Road Initiative.
n76f42864a5a.tq: Link the programme with its launch year, venue and strategic purpose.
xs: The G7 launched **PGII** in **2022 in Germany** — option **(3)**.
It is a G7 infrastructure plan meant as a **counter to BRI**.
xa: The **2026** G7 summit was held in **France**.
The G7 became the **G8** with Russia in **1997-98**, until **2014**.
The G20 was foreshadowed at the G7 **Cologne summit (June 1999)**.

n9babb7f2add.s: The New Development Bank (NDB) was established at Fortaleza in 2014 and has its headquarters at:
n9babb7f2add.x: The NDB was established at Fortaleza in 2014 and its headquarters is located in Shanghai.
n9babb7f2add.tq: Match an institution with its founding venue and headquarters rather than confusing the two.
xs: The **NDB**, set up at **Fortaleza** in **2014**, is headquartered at **Shanghai** — option **(3)**.
**Fortaleza** is where it was agreed, not its HQ.
xa: The BRICS **Contingent Reserve Arrangement** (**2014**) is a **$100 billion** liquidity pool.
**Johannesburg** hosted the **2025** G20 meetings.
BRICS in **2011** had **20%** of GDP but only **11%** of IMF votes.

n98c86d1e78b.s: The Colombo Security Conclave began in 2011 as a maritime trilateral of India, Sri Lanka and:
n98c86d1e78b.x: The Colombo Security Conclave originated in 2011 as an India-Sri Lanka-Maldives maritime trilateral.
xa: Members now: **India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh**; observer **Seychelles**.
Secretariat: **Colombo**.
Five pillars include **maritime safety and security** and **HADR**.

ne62ef234512.s: Which of the following is an observer, not a member, of the Colombo Security Conclave?
ne62ef234512.x: Seychelles is an observer; India, Mauritius and Bangladesh are members.
xa: CSC members: **India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh**.
Origin: India-Sri Lanka-Maldives trilateral (**2011**); renamed **2020**.
Secretariat: **Colombo**.

na506496c62b.s: In climate negotiations, the BASIC grouping upholds the principle of:
o: Uniform emission cuts for all countries
Exclusive reliance on private climate finance
Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC)
Carbon border taxes on developing countries
na506496c62b.x: BASIC stands for CBDR-RC and climate finance from developed countries.
xa: BASIC formed in **2009**, before **Copenhagen COP15**.
Members: **Brazil, South Africa, India, China**.
India is also in **IBSA** (**2003**) with Brazil and South Africa.

o: More than 40% of global GDP, 46% of trade and 55% of population
40% of global GDP, 50% of trade and one-third of population
85% of global GDP, more than 75% of trade and two-thirds of population
20% of global GDP, 11% of trade and half of population
nd81c6310409.x: The G20 represents approximately 85% of global GDP, more than 75% of global trade and two-thirds of the world's population.
nd81c6310409.tq: Keep the three indicators together and reject figures belonging to other groupings or periods.
xs: The **G20** accounts for **~85%** of GDP, **>75%** of trade and **two-thirds** of population — option **(3)**.
Option 1 mixes **BRICS** figures (**>40%** GDP, **55%** population) with the false "**46%** of trade" claim.
xa: G20 = **19 countries + EU + AU**.
BRICS in **2011**: **20%** of GDP but only **11%** of IMF votes.
G20 first leaders' summit: **Washington D.C., 2008**.

n60114c6e791.s: Which of the following correctly describes the share of the expanded BRICS grouping?
o: More than 40% of global GDP on a PPP basis and about 50% of the world's population
Exactly 46% of global trade and one-third of the world's population
About 85% of global GDP and more than 75% of global trade
About 20% of global GDP and 11% of the world's population
n60114c6e791.x: The expanded BRICS grouping accounts for more than 40% of global GDP on a PPP basis and approximately 50% of the world's population. The exact estimates vary by source.
n60114c6e791.tq: Distinguish BRICS indicators from the G20 figures and avoid an unsupported exact percentage.
xs: The expanded **BRICS** has **>40%** of global GDP (**PPP**) and ~**50%** of population — option **(1)**.
Another source gives **nearly 40%** of GDP and **55%** of population; **85%** GDP / **>75%** trade is the **G20**.
xa: ⚠ "BRICS = **46%** of global trade" was the **wrong** statement in UKPSC **2024**.
BRICS in **2011**: **20%** of GDP but **11%** of IMF votes.
BRICS has **10** members (+ **Saudi** ambiguous).

o: The three largest economies of the G20
The current, previous and next presidencies
The G7, BRICS and European Union
The three permanent members of the G20 Secretariat
n6bdefa0e39a.x: The G20 troika comprises the previous, current and next presidencies (B). In 2022 it was Italy (previous, 2021), Indonesia (current, 2022) and India (next, 2023). The G20 has no permanent secretariat, and the troika is not based on economic size or on G7/BRICS/EU.
n6bdefa0e39a.tq: Resolve a terminology trap by identifying the institutional meaning of troika.
xs: The **G20 Troika** = **past, current and next presidencies** — option **(2)**.
In **2022** it was **Indonesia**, **Italy** and **India**.
The G20 has **no permanent secretariat or HQ**, so option 4 is wrong.
xa: India's presidency summit: **New Delhi, 9-10 Sep 2023**.
The presidency **rotates annually**.
**2025** G20: **Johannesburg, South Africa**.

n690798f859b.s: The Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG) was formed in 1975 in response to:
n690798f859b.x: The NSG was formed in 1975, popularly known as the London Club, in response to India's 1974 Pokhran-I test.
n690798f859b.tq: Match the organisation's origin with the triggering event.
xs: The **NSG** was formed in **1975** in response to India's **1974 Pokhran-I** test — option **(3)**.
It was popularly called the **"London Club"**.
The **CTBT** came later (**1996**) and North Korea's NPT exit was in **2003**, so neither could have triggered a 1975 body.
xa: The NSG is **voluntary, consensus-based**, with **no permanent secretariat** and **48 members**.
It controls **nuclear materials and technology**.
India got the **India-specific NSG waiver in 2008** (India-US Civil Nuclear Deal).
IAEA DG **Rafael Grossi** chaired the NSG in **2016**.

n4e15091c9ab.s: The Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) is headquartered at:
n4e15091c9ab.x: The OPCW is headquartered at The Hague and implements the CWC.
n4e15091c9ab.tq: Use location-based elimination among the headquarters of treaty organisations.
xs: The **OPCW** is headquartered at **The Hague** — option **(3)**.
**Vienna** hosts the **IAEA**; **Paris (OECD)** hosts the **FATF** secretariat.
xa: The OPCW **implements the CWC**, **monitors the chemical industry** and inspects destruction.
Organs: **Conference of States Parties**, **Executive Council**, **Technical Secretariat**.
⚠ It is **not an EU body** (UPSC 2016); it won the **Nobel Peace Prize 2013**.

n7e9b30c9298.s: The NPT, which entered into force in 1970, was extended indefinitely in:
n7e9b30c9298.x: The NPT (signed 1968, in force 1970) was extended indefinitely in 1995.
xa: ⚠ UPSC 2015 trap: only **China** and **France** among the options were NPT nuclear-weapon states.
India calls the NPT **discriminatory ("nuclear apartheid")** and won't sign until nuclear powers accept a **time-bound disarmament plan**.
**North Korea** left the NPT in **2003**; Review Conferences are held **every 5 years**.
Criticism: the NPT lets recognised powers **modernise without disarmament deadlines**.

nd570d17ec0a.s: India's principal objection to the NPT is that it:
o: does not contain any provision on nuclear energy
is discriminatory and perpetuates nuclear apartheid
recognises India as a nuclear-weapon state without conditions
nd570d17ec0a.x: India rejects the NPT as discriminatory, describing its structure as nuclear apartheid. India also seeks a time-bound disarmament plan from the nuclear powers before signing.
nd570d17ec0a.tq: Identify the stated policy objection rather than a consequence of the treaty.
xs: India rejects the NPT as **discriminatory**, calling it **"nuclear apartheid"** — so option **(3)** is correct.
India won't sign until the nuclear powers accept a **time-bound disarmament plan**.
The NPT recognises only the **P5** as nuclear-weapon states, so it does not recognise India as one.
xa: India is also **not a signatory to the CTBT** and **did not sign the TPNW**.
⚠ India is a party to **PTBT, CWC, BWC, CCW**; not to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.
India is called a **"de facto responsible nuclear state"** — **NFU doctrine**, export controls, entry into **3 of 4 regimes**.
The **2008 NSG India-specific waiver** opened civil nuclear trade despite India staying outside the NPT.

n9724ad6af83.s: India has not signed the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) primarily because it:
o: lacks a time-bound disarmament commitment and permits subcritical tests
does not ban any form of nuclear explosion
n9724ad6af83.x: India objects to the CTBT because it lacks a time-bound disarmament plan and still permits subcritical tests. The CTBT bans all nuclear explosions and was adopted in 1996.
n9724ad6af83.tq: Separate India's objection to the treaty from the treaty's stated prohibition.
xs: India has not signed the **CTBT** because it has **no time-bound disarmament** and still **allows subcritical tests** — option **(1)**.
The CTBT (**1996**) **bans all nuclear explosions**, so option (3) is wrong; it is a nuclear, not chemical, treaty.
It says nothing about recognising nuclear-weapon states — that is the **NPT**, which recognises the **P5**.
xa: The CTBT is **not in force**.
The **PTBT (1963)** bans tests **except underground**; **India is a party** to it.
India **did not sign the TPNW** (in force **2021**) — it "adds nothing to customary law".
⚠ India is not a party to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.

n082e244d1df.s: India, which has not signed the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW), holds that the treaty:
o: Is backed by all nuclear-armed states
Adds nothing to customary international law
n082e244d1df.x: India did not sign the TPNW and has stated that it adds nothing to customary international law.
xa: The TPNW entered into force in **2021**.
⚠ India: party to **PTBT, CWC, BWC, CCW**; not to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.
India supports **FMCT** negotiation at the **Conference on Disarmament**.

nbe3c331bb46.s: The Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW) entered into force in:
nbe3c331bb46.x: The TPNW, a binding treaty banning nuclear weapons, entered into force in 2021.
xa: **India did not sign** the TPNW — it **adds nothing to customary law**.
The **CTBT** (**1996**) bans all nuclear explosions but is **not in force**.
**US + Russia** hold about **90%** of global arsenals.

n2664d611632.s: India supports negotiation of the Fissile Material Cut-off Treaty (FMCT) at the:
n2664d611632.x: India supports FMCT negotiations at the Conference on Disarmament, for a treaty that does not cap existing stocks.
xa: India's other FMCT conditions: **universal, verifiable, non-discriminatory**.
India **did not sign the TPNW** — it **adds nothing to customary law**.
India is **not a signatory to the CTBT** — no time-bound disarmament; subcritical tests still allowed.

nf2f2b417aae.s: India is party to how many of the protocols of the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW)?
nf2f2b417aae.x: The CCW deals with inhumane conventional weapons, and India is party to all five of its protocols.
xa: ⚠ India is a party to **PTBT, CWC, BWC, CCW**; not to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.
The **Wassenaar Arrangement** (**1996**) controls **conventional arms and dual-use goods**.
The **BWC** has **no verification organisation**; India is a party.

n49fcd8f2681.s: North Korea withdrew from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) in:
n49fcd8f2681.x: North Korea left the NPT in 2003.
n49fcd8f2681.tq: Recall the specific withdrawal year rather than a nearby nuclear-crisis date.
xs: **North Korea** left the **NPT** in **2003** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The NPT was signed in **1968**, came into force in **1970** and was extended indefinitely in **1995**.
xa: The NPT recognises only the **P5 — US, Russia, UK, France, China** as nuclear-weapon states.
**NPT Review Conferences** are held **every 5 years**; the consensus rule lets a single state block outcomes.
**North Korea** is also outside the **MTCR**.
**Iran's Parliament** weighed an **NPT exit** in **Mar 2026** after US-Israel strikes on its nuclear sites (**June 2025**).

n6cf36e22986.s: The headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is located at:
n6cf36e22986.x: The IAEA is headquartered in Vienna and was established in 1957.
n6cf36e22986.tq: Separate the locations of the IAEA, FATF and OPCW.
xs: The **IAEA** is headquartered at **Vienna** — option **(2)**.
**The Hague** hosts the **OPCW**; **Paris (OECD)** hosts the **FATF** secretariat.
The IAEA was established in **1957** and verifies that civil nuclear material is **not diverted to weapons**.
xa: **India joined the IAEA in 1957** as a **founding member**.
⚠ **Vienna** is also the seat of the **Wassenaar Arrangement** (**1996**, **42** members).
IAEA DG **Rafael Grossi** voiced worry over hits on Iran's nuclear sites (**Apr 2026**); he chaired the **NSG in 2016**.

n73d76163c00.s: India joined the IAEA as a founding member in:
n73d76163c00.x: India joined the IAEA in 1957 as a founding member.
xa: ⚠ NSG waiver = **2008**; safeguards agreement = **2009**; **Additional Protocol** = **2014**.
The IAEA is headquartered at **Vienna**, established **1957**.
India-Canada uranium (**10,000 tonnes, 2027-2035**) is for PHWRs **under IAEA safeguards**.

n5d10041a5fa.s: India completed the destruction of its declared chemical-weapon stockpile under the CWC in:
n5d10041a5fa.x: India, a party to the CWC (in force 1997), completed destruction of its declared stockpile in 2009.
xa: The CWC is implemented by the **OPCW** at **The Hague** (Nobel Peace Prize **2013**).
The **BWC** (**1972**, in force **1975**) has **no verification organisation**; India is a party.
⚠ India: party to **PTBT, CWC, BWC, CCW**; not to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.

n40dd4c7c234.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the OPCW?
o: It implements the Chemical Weapons Convention
It inspects the destruction of chemical weapons
It is an institution of the European Union
It received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2013
n40dd4c7c234.x: The OPCW is not an EU body; it implements the CWC, monitors the chemical industry and won the 2013 Nobel Peace Prize.
xa: HQ: **The Hague**.
Organs: **Conference of States Parties**, **Executive Council**, **Technical Secretariat**.
The **CWC** was signed **1993**, in force **1997**; India finished destroying its stockpile in **2009**.

neb06cfe8716.s: The Biological Weapons Convention, adopted in 1972 and to which India is a party, entered into force in:
neb06cfe8716.x: The BWC was adopted in 1972, entered into force in 1975 and has no verification organisation.
xa: The **CWC** (signed **1993**, in force **1997**) is implemented by the **OPCW**.
⚠ India: party to **PTBT, CWC, BWC, CCW**; not to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.
The **Australia Group** (**1985**) controls **chemical and biological weapon precursors**.

nbf6f1efcec4.s: The secretariat of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) is located at:
nbf6f1efcec4.x: The FATF secretariat is at Paris (OECD); Vienna hosts the IAEA.
xa: FATF keeps a **grey list** (increased monitoring) and a **black list** (call for action).
India's **mutual evaluation** (adopted **June 2024**) → **"regular follow-up"**; India is also in the **APG**.
**Pakistan** was on the grey list **June 2018 to Oct 2022** for failing a **27-point action plan**.

nd950c6f833f.s: India's Additional Protocol to its IAEA safeguards agreement came into force in:
nd950c6f833f.x: India's Additional Protocol came into force in 2014.
xa: ⚠ Sequence: **NSG waiver 2008** → **safeguards agreement 2009** → **Additional Protocol 2014**.
The safeguards agreement covers **civilian facilities, excludes military**.
The **2008 waiver** stemmed from the **India-US Civil Nuclear Deal** → uranium/reactor imports.

n7917488eeac.s: The India-specific NSG waiver of 2008, associated with the India-US Civil Nuclear Deal, permits India to:
o: trade in civilian nuclear material and import uranium and reactors
join the NPT as a nuclear-weapon state
n7917488eeac.x: The 2008 waiver permits civil nuclear trade and the import of uranium and reactors by India. It does not make India an NPT member.
n7917488eeac.tq: Distinguish the practical effect of a waiver from formal membership in another treaty.
xs: The **2008 NSG waiver** lets India carry out **civil nuclear trade** and **import uranium and reactors** — option **(1)**.
It came through the **India-US Civil Nuclear Deal**; it does not make India an NPT member or give it a veto.
The NSG is **consensus-based**, so no member holds a special veto through the waiver.
xa: ⚠ NSG waiver = **2008**; safeguards agreement = **2009**; Additional Protocol = **2014**.
Uranium deals followed: **Canada (10,000 tonnes, 2027-2035)** and **Australia (July 2026)**.
The **India-Specific Safeguards Agreement** covers civilian facilities and **excludes military** ones.

n99878f81c20.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three basic principles of UN peacekeeping?
o: No use of force except in self-defence and defence of the mandate
Use of force to secure political compliance
n99878f81c20.x: The three principles are consent of the parties, impartiality, and no use of force except in self-defence and defence of the mandate.
n99878f81c20.tq: Identify the option that reverses the restrictive rule on use of force.
xs: **"Use of force to secure political compliance"** is not a peacekeeping principle — option **(4)**.
The three principles are **consent of the parties**, **impartiality**, and **no use of force except in self-defence and defence of the mandate**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **"Force only for self-defence"** is incomplete — force is also allowed in **defence of the mandate**.
The **UN Security Council** creates and ends missions by resolution; the **DPO** manages them.
**UNSC Resolution 2823 (2026)** strengthens accountability for crimes against **"Blue Helmets"**.

nbc8519d9a9a.s: Which United Nations body creates peacekeeping missions and ends them by resolution?
nbc8519d9a9a.x: The UN Security Council creates and terminates peacekeeping missions through resolutions, while the Department of Peace Operations manages them.
nbc8519d9a9a.tq: Distinguish the body that authorises missions from the department that manages them.
xs: The **UN Security Council** creates and ends peacekeeping missions **by resolution** — option **(3)**.
The **Department of Peace Operations (DPO)** only **manages** missions; it does not create them.
xa: Missions are funded by a **separate peacekeeping assessment scale**, outside the regular UN budget.
**UNSC Resolution 2823 (2026)** targets crimes against peacekeepers ("**Blue Helmets**").
Exam angle: statement questions on **who withdraws a mission** — the UNSC.

n5e6ea7fc7cb.s: The UN peacekeeping mission MINUSTAH was in:
n5e6ea7fc7cb.x: MINUSTAH was in Haiti; UNMIL was in Liberia, UNMISET in Timor-Leste and UNIFIL in Lebanon.
xa: **MINURCAT**: Central African Republic and **Chad**, **2007-2010**.
**UNDOF**: **Golan Heights** (Syria-Israel), **1974-**.
These hosts and periods appeared in a **UPSC 2026** match question.

n88301196b4c.s: India's first contribution to a United Nations peacekeeping operation was made to which mission in 1950?
n88301196b4c.x: India's first UN peacekeeping contribution was to the UN force in Korea in 1950.
n88301196b4c.tq: Use the date and earliest contribution to identify the correct mission.
xs: India's **first** UN peacekeeping contribution was to the **UN force in Korea (1950)** — option **(4)**.
**ONUC** (Congo) came later in **1960-64**; **UNMIL** (Liberia) ran **2003-2018**; **UNIFIL** (Lebanon) dates from **1978**.
xa: Cumulatively India served in **53 of 72** missions with **over 2,97,000 personnel**.
In **ONUC** India sent the **largest contingent** and fought to end the **Katanga** secession.
The **IPKF** in Sri Lanka (**Operation Pawan**) was an **India-only** force, not a UN mission.

n4af59ae553c.s: India is the largest troop contributor to which of the following UN missions?
n4af59ae553c.x: India is the largest troop contributor to UNMISS, with 1,775 personnel.
n4af59ae553c.tq: Match the specific leadership claim with the mission named in the data.
xs: India is the **largest troop contributor** to **UNMISS** (South Sudan), with **1,775** personnel — option **(3)**.
**UNMIL** (Liberia) ended in **2018**; **UNDOF** is in the **Golan Heights**; **UNIFIL** in **Lebanon**.
xa: **210** Indian peacekeepers got the **UN Medal** in **Juba** (**20 Aug 2026**).
UNMISS has run since **2011**.
Overall India is the **fourth-largest** contributor (**2026**).

n9b1ffeb7f67.s: India was among the first countries to deploy an all-women Formed Police Unit to which country in 2007?
n9b1ffeb7f67.x: India deployed an all-women Formed Police Unit to Liberia in 2007 and was among the first countries to do so.
n9b1ffeb7f67.tq: Link the special unit with its host country and year.
xs: India was among the first to deploy an **all-women Formed Police Unit** — to **Liberia** in **2007** — option **(1)**.
Liberia hosted **UNMIL** (**2003-2018**).
xa: Quick fact: **Liberia** = first all-women FPU; first **PBD** held in **2003**.
**UNMISS = South Sudan**; **MINUSTAH = Haiti**; **UNIFIL = Lebanon**.
**CUNPK, New Delhi** trains **10,000+ troops a year**.

nf596b3d31e8.s: As of 2026, India's rank among troop contributors to UN peacekeeping is:
nf596b3d31e8.x: In 2026 India is the fourth-largest troop contributor, with 5,200+ troops in 12 missions. Older questions (UPPSC 2011) keyed India as the biggest contributor, which is outdated; second- and tenth-largest are also incorrect.
xs: In **2026** India is the **fourth-largest** troop contributor — option **(3)**.
It has **5,200+ troops in 12 missions**.
⚠ **UPPSC 2011** keyed India as the **biggest** contributor — an outdated answer.
xa: India is the **largest** contributor to **UNMISS** alone (**1,775** personnel).
Cumulative: **53 of 72** missions, **over 2,97,000 personnel**.
Present deployments: **DR Congo, South Sudan, Abyei, Lebanon, Golan Heights**.

n26ff87ea4d7.s: The Salma Dam, an Indian development partnership project, is located in:
n26ff87ea4d7.x: The Salma Dam and the Parliament building are in Afghanistan; Metro Express is in Mauritius.
xa: The Salma Dam is also called the **Afghan-India Friendship Dam**.
Mauritius also got a **new Supreme Court building** from India.
Such grants are run by the **DPA** in the **MEA** (**2012**).

n6568787de06.s: The Development Partnership Administration (DPA) was set up in which Ministry and in which year?
o: Ministry of Commerce and Industry in 2014
n6568787de06.x: The Development Partnership Administration was established in the Ministry of External Affairs in 2012.
n6568787de06.tq: Identify the institution and the ministry responsible for it.
xs: The **DPA** was set up in the **Ministry of External Affairs** in **2012** — option **(1)**.
It manages India's development partnership, including grant projects and **Lines of Credit**.
xa: **ITEC** (**15 Sept 1964**) is a **training-based capacity-building** programme; **e-ITEC** is its online form.
**EXIM Bank** (HQ **Mumbai**) extends concessional **Lines of Credit** to foreign governments.

nb0fc5456365.s: Vaccine Maitri, launched in January 2021, primarily refers to India’s:
o: Programme for training foreign diplomats in India
Supply of COVID-19 vaccines to other countries
Evacuation of citizens from conflict zones
Financial support for overseas infrastructure projects
nb0fc5456365.x: Vaccine Maitri refers to India’s supply of COVID-19 vaccines to other countries and was launched in January 2021.
nb0fc5456365.tq: Separate health diplomacy from evacuation and development-finance initiatives.
xs: **Vaccine Maitri** (launched **January 2021**) was India's **supply of COVID-19 vaccines to other countries** — option **(2)**.
Evacuations had their own operations, e.g. **Ganga** (Ukraine) and **Kaveri** (Sudan); training is **ITEC**.
xa: ⚠ **Operation Maitri** (**2015**) was the **Nepal** earthquake relief — not Vaccine Maitri.
**DPI diplomacy** offers **India Stack** (Aadhaar, **UPI**, DigiLocker) to partners.
**Vande Bharat Mission** (**2020**) was the worldwide COVID-19 repatriation.

n570b9941b3d.s: The International Day of Yoga was established by a UN General Assembly resolution in December 2014 and was first observed in:
n570b9941b3d.x: The UNGA adopted the resolution in December 2014 and the first International Day of Yoga was observed in 2015. 2014 is the resolution year, not the first observance; 2016 and 2017 are later.
xs: **International Yoga Day** was first observed in **2015** — option **(2)**.
**2014** is the year of the **UNGA resolution (Dec 2014)**, not the first observance.
xa: Yoga is listed among India's soft-power tools with **ITEC training, scholarships, Bollywood**.
**ICCR** (**1950**) runs cultural centres and festivals.
**Study in India** launched in **2018**.

n9f3f308c53e.s: Operation Kaveri was India's evacuation operation from:
n9f3f308c53e.x: Kaveri was the Sudan evacuation; Ajay was Israel, Ganga was Ukraine and Dost was the Türkiye-Syria earthquake relief.
xa: Dates: Dost **Feb 2023**; Kaveri **Apr 2023**; Ajay **Oct 2023**; Ganga **2022**.
**Sankat Mochan** = **South Sudan** evacuation, **2016**.
**Vande Bharat Mission** = worldwide **COVID-19** repatriation, **2020**.

ndcd20cc5bca.s: The L.M. Singhvi High Level Committee on the Indian Diaspora, set up in 2000, submitted its report in:
ndcd20cc5bca.x: The committee was set up in 2000 and reported in 2002; it recommended Pravasi Bharatiya Divas, first held in 2003.
xa: The first **PBD** was held in **2003 at New Delhi**; **biennial since 2015**.
**OCI** came in **2005**; **PIO merged into OCI in 2015**.
PBD marks Gandhi's return from South Africa on **9 January 1915**.

n80ebd318b46.s: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas is observed on 9 January because Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa on that date in which year?
n80ebd318b46.x: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas commemorates Gandhi's return from South Africa on 9 January 1915.
n80ebd318b46.tq: Link the commemorative date with the historical event and year.
xs: **Gandhi** returned from **South Africa** on **9 January 1915** — option **(3)**.
That date is marked as **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas**.
xa: First PBD: **2003, New Delhi**; **biennial since 2015**.
**18th PBD**: **Bhubaneswar**, **8-10 Jan 2025**, theme **"Diaspora's Contribution to a Viksit Bharat"**.
The **President** confers the **Pravasi Bharatiya Samman** at PBD.

n5152cbf1925.s: The Pravasi Bharatiya Samman, the highest honour for overseas Indians, is conferred at Pravasi Bharatiya Divas by the:
n5152cbf1925.x: The Pravasi Bharatiya Samman is conferred by the President at Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.
xa: PBD marks Gandhi's return on **9 January 1915**.
The **L.M. Singhvi Committee** (**2000**) recommended PBD.
First PBD in **2003**; **biennial since 2015**.

ne06ebf21143.s: Which country hosts about 3.5 million Indians, the largest number of Indian nationals (NRIs) in any foreign country?
ne06ebf21143.x: The United Arab Emirates had approximately 3.5 million Indians in the cited December 2025 data.
ne06ebf21143.tq: Distinguish the country-specific diaspora count from general largest-diaspora claims.
xs: The **United Arab Emirates (UAE)** had about **3.5 million** Indians (**Dec 2025**) — option **(2)**.
It was the key for **"largest Indian population"** (**BPSC 2020**, Dec 2018 data).
xa: In **Australia**, Indian-origin people became the **largest immigrant-born community**, overtaking the UK-born (**Jul 2026**).
**1.46 crore passports** were issued in **2024**.
**"4 Ds"** of the Modi Doctrine: **Democracy, Demography, Demand, Diaspora**.
ne06ebf21143.fixed: 'according to the cited diaspora data' is odd wording referring to the notes

n7751ede9d79.s: The Leiden Plates, 21 copper plates from the time of Rajaraja Chola I, were returned to India by:
n7751ede9d79.x: The Netherlands returned the Leiden Plates, 21 Chola copper plates of Rajaraja Chola I's time.
xa: The PM visited the diaspora in the **Netherlands** and **Australia** in **2026**.
**Nalanda University**'s new **Rajgir** campus opened in **June 2024**.
The **Buddhist circuit** is another heritage-based soft-power tool.

nb986ad1334d.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four Ds of the Modi Doctrine?
nb986ad1334d.x: The four Ds are Democracy, Demography, Demand and Diaspora. Development is not included in the stated formulation.
nb986ad1334d.tq: Recall the complete four-item list and identify the substituted term.
xs: **Development** is not one of the **"4 Ds"** — option **(4)**.
The four Ds are **Democracy, Demography, Demand** and **Diaspora**.
xa: **UAE** has **3.5 million** Indians (**Dec 2025**).
**1.46 crore passports** were issued in **2024**.
Indian-origin people are now **Australia's largest immigrant-born community**.

n03e20ff4875.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region)?
o: It widened India's maritime vision to the Indo-Pacific and the Global South
It aims to make India the net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region
It is seen as countering China's 'String of Pearls'
n03e20ff4875.x: Widening the vision to the Indo-Pacific and the Global South is MAHASAGAR (2025), not SAGAR.
xa: SAGAR = **Security and Growth for All in the Region**.
⚠ Order: **SAGAR → MAHASAGAR → SHANTI** (SHANTI = **Bay of Bengal** maritime-security framework).
String of Pearls sites: **Gwadar**, **Hambantota**, **Djibouti**.

n19b83cbaa9a.s: MAHASAGAR, which widens SAGAR to the Indo-Pacific and the Global South, was introduced in:
n19b83cbaa9a.x: MAHASAGAR was introduced in 2025, extending SAGAR (2015) to the Indo-Pacific and the Global South.
xa: MAHASAGAR = **"Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security Across the Regions"**.
**SAGAR** (**2015**) made India the **net security provider** in the IOR.
⚠ Order: **SAGAR → MAHASAGAR → SHANTI**.

n98f74195787.s: The Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS) was launched by the Indian Navy, with its first meeting in New Delhi, in:
n98f74195787.x: IONS was launched in 2008; the claim of an inaugural IONS in 2015 is a known trap.
xa: India holds the **IONS Chairmanship** and hosted the **9th Conclave of Chiefs at Visakhapatnam** (**2026**).
⚠ **2015** = SAGAR; **2008** = IONS; **2011** = Colombo Security Conclave.
**IOS SAGAR** carried **16 IONS countries** on **INS Sunayna**.

n76a6d7946e4.s: The 9th Conclave of Chiefs of the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium was hosted at:
n76a6d7946e4.x: India hosted the 9th IONS Conclave of Chiefs at Visakhapatnam.
n76a6d7946e4.tq: Current institutional event and venue recall.
xs: India hosted the **9th IONS Conclave of Chiefs** at **Visakhapatnam** (**2026**) — option **(1)**.
India currently holds the **IONS Chairmanship**.
xa: **IONS** began in **2008**, first held in **New Delhi**.
Vizag also hosted the **Colombo Security Conclave table-top exercise** (**Sep 2026**) and **IFR 2026**.
**MILAN** began in **1995 at Port Blair**; **2022** and **2024** editions at Visakhapatnam.

n97ba5996e28.s: The Malabar naval exercise began in 1992 as a bilateral exercise between India and:
n97ba5996e28.x: Malabar began as an India-US exercise in 1992; Japan became permanent in 2015 and Australia joined in 2020.
xa: **MILAN** is a **multilateral** exercise hosted by the Indian Navy; **2022/2024** at **Visakhapatnam**.
**AIKEYME** = Africa-India Key Maritime Engagement, first edition **2025**, **Tanzania**.
**CTF-154** (HQ **Bahrain**): India took **command for the first time**.

na690d3e05fa.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's naval exercises and maritime platforms?
o: MILAN is a bilateral exercise of the Indian Navy
AIKEYME stands for Africa-India Key Maritime Engagement
The 2022 and 2024 editions of MILAN were held at Visakhapatnam
The first AIKEYME was held at Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, in 2025
na690d3e05fa.x: MILAN is a multilateral exercise hosted by the Indian Navy, not a bilateral one.
xa: MILAN began in **1995** at **Port Blair**.
AIKEYME's first venue was **Dar es Salaam**.
**Malabar** brings together all **Quad** members.

n701f22c26f7.s: India took command for the first time of which maritime task force in 2026?
o: Indian Ocean Naval Symposium Task Force
n701f22c26f7.x: India took command for the first time of CTF-154, a task force of the Combined Maritime Forces headquartered in Bahrain.
n701f22c26f7.tq: Distinguish the exact task-force number from neighbouring maritime force designations.
xs: India took **command for the first time** of **Combined Task Force 154** — option **(2)**.
CTF-154 belongs to the **Combined Maritime Forces**, HQ **Bahrain**.
xa: India's **IONS** chairship + **CTF-154** command are listed as **2026** current relevance.
⚠ **CTF-154** = **Bahrain**; **AIKEYME** = **Tanzania**.
India joined the **Djibouti Code of Conduct** (anti-piracy) as an **observer (2020)**.

n502c170a434.s: Visakhapatnam holds one of India’s three:
n502c170a434.x: Visakhapatnam holds one of India’s three Strategic Petroleum Reserves.
n502c170a434.tq: Use the exact institutional term rather than a look-alike expansion.
xs: **Visakhapatnam** holds one of India's **three Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPRs)** — option **(3)**.
It is part of Vizag's role as the **hub of naval diplomacy** (ENC, IFR, IONS, CSC exercise, **SPR**).
xa: The **UAE** is the **only** country storing oil in India's **SPR** and India's **4th**-largest crude supplier.
⚠ Thin SPR buffer: **9.5 days** vs the IEA's **90**.
About **50% of crude imports** pass through the **Strait of Hormuz**.

n696e69b9cc8.s: Chabahar port is located in which part of Iran?
o: Fars on the Gulf of Oman
Sistan-Baluchestan on the Gulf of Oman
n696e69b9cc8.x: Chabahar is located in Iran’s Sistan-Baluchestan province on the Gulf of Oman.
n696e69b9cc8.tq: Discriminate between Iranian provinces and adjoining maritime regions.
xs: **Chabahar** is in **Iran's Sistan-Baluchestan**, on the **Gulf of Oman** — option **(3)**.
India develops its **Shahid Beheshti terminal** via **IPGL**.
xa: It gives India **access to Afghanistan and Central Asia bypassing Pakistan** (UPSC **2017** key).
It links into the **INSTC**.
A **10-year** operating contract was signed in **May 2024**.

ne48e0b30417.s: The IMEC was announced at the G20 New Delhi Summit in:
ne48e0b30417.x: The India-Middle East-Europe Corridor was announced at the G20 New Delhi Summit in September 2023.
ne48e0b30417.tq: Use the event-year association for a recently announced corridor.
xs: **IMEC** was announced at the **G20 New Delhi** summit in **September 2023** — option **(3)**.
IMEC = **India-Middle East-Europe Corridor**.
xa: Partners: **India, UAE, Saudi Arabia, EU, France, Germany, Italy, USA**.
⚠ **INSTC = 2000** agreement; **Ashgabat = 2011**, India joined **2018**.
The **Global Biofuels Alliance** was also launched at the **G20** in India (**2023**).

n3f1ded74d69.s: The India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) was announced in:
n3f1ded74d69.x: IMEC was announced in 2023; the INSTC agreement dates to 2000, the Ashgabat Agreement to 2011 and India joined Ashgabat in 2018.
xa: Ashgabat is a **transit corridor** linking **Central Asia** with the **Persian Gulf**.
The **Armenia-Iran-India** trilateral (**Jan 2026**) is the newest route.
INSTC's western branch runs through **Azerbaijan** (UPSC **2025** key).

nbc2219c45ca.s: A newer trilateral initiative promotes a Persian Gulf–Black Sea corridor involving:
nbc2219c45ca.x: The newer initiative involves Armenia, Iran and India and promotes a Persian Gulf–Black Sea corridor.
nbc2219c45ca.tq: Identify the countries from a small trilateral arrangement rather than a larger corridor membership list.
xs: The newer **Persian Gulf-Black Sea** corridor involves **Armenia, Iran and India** — option **(2)**.
This trilateral was noted in **Jan 2026**.
xa: ⚠ The **INSTC**'s western branch runs through **Azerbaijan** (UPSC **2025**), not Armenia.
INSTC agreement: **2000**, **India, Iran, Russia**.
**Chabahar** links into the INSTC.

n33b5ecca4a7.s: TAPI and IPI pipelines are respectively associated with which countries?
n33b5ecca4a7.x: TAPI stands for Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India, while IPI stands for Iran-Pakistan-India and is also called the Peace Pipeline.
n33b5ecca4a7.tq: Expand both similar pipeline acronyms before selecting the country sequence.
xs: **TAPI** = **Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India**; **IPI** = **Iran-Pakistan-India** — option **(2)**.
IPI is called the **"Peace Pipeline"**.
xa: **UAE** is India's **4th**-largest crude supplier and only country storing oil in India's **SPR**.
**Uranium** comes from **Kazakhstan** and **Uzbekistan**.
About **50% of crude imports** pass the **Strait of Hormuz**.

nc6387fc0030.s: Which one of the following sets is associated with the concept of China’s ‘String of Pearls’?
nc6387fc0030.x: Gwadar, Hambantota and Djibouti are associated with the String of Pearls concept.
nc6387fc0030.tq: Group-recognition question using a known strategic cluster.
xs: **Gwadar, Hambantota and Djibouti** form China's **String of Pearls** — option **(4)**.
**Chabahar, Sittwe, Sabang** are **India's counters** to BRI; **Duqm, Agalega, Colombo West** are India's strategic-access sites.
xa: ⚠ **Hambantota / Gwadar** = String of Pearls (China); **Sittwe / Sabang** = India's counters.
**Djibouti** = China's **first overseas base (2017)**.
China's **"Malacca dilemma"** drives its port-building.

n0b81ad58a69.s: Which of the following ports are India’s counters to China’s Belt and Road Initiative?
n0b81ad58a69.x: Chabahar, Sittwe and Sabang are identified as India’s counters to China’s BRI.
n0b81ad58a69.tq: Identify the strategic trio rather than individual port locations.
xs: **Chabahar, Sittwe and Sabang** are India's **counters to BRI** — option **(1)**.
**Gwadar, Hambantota, Djibouti** are China's **String of Pearls**; **Diego Garcia** is a **US-UK** base.
xa: **Chabahar** (Iran) gives access to **Afghanistan and Central Asia bypassing Pakistan**.
**Sittwe** (Myanmar) is the sea port of the **Kaladan** project.
**Sabang** is in **Indonesia**.

n9c16cc7b1ef.s: China’s port-building strategy in the Indian Ocean is linked in strategic analysis to its:
n9c16cc7b1ef.x: China’s port-building is linked to its perceived Malacca dilemma.
n9c16cc7b1ef.tq: Match a strategic behaviour with the specific security dilemma driving it.
xs: China's port-building is driven by its **"Malacca dilemma"** (**Jul 2026**) — option **(1)**.
That port network is the **"String of Pearls"**: **Gwadar**, **Hambantota**, **Djibouti**.
xa: **Djibouti** = China's **first overseas base (2017)**.
**SAGAR** (**2015**) counters the String of Pearls.
India's counters to BRI: **Chabahar**, **Sittwe**, **Sabang**.
**Chagos** hosts the US-UK base at **Diego Garcia** — not a "dilemma" of China.

ncf31ab41aef.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four ‘A’s guiding India’s energy policy?
ncf31ab41aef.x: The four ‘A’s are availability, accessibility, affordability and acceptability. Autonomy is not included in the stated formulation.
ncf31ab41aef.tq: Find the look-alike substitute for an exact policy formulation.
xs: **Autonomy** is not one of the four 'A's — option **(2)**.
The four 'A's: **availability, accessibility, affordability, acceptability**.
xa: India imports about **88% of crude** and **50% of gas**.
India is the **third-largest energy consumer**.
Pipelines: **TAPI** and **IPI** ("**Peace Pipeline**").

nb3cf603bf4a.s: The International Solar Alliance (ISA) was launched on 30 November 2015 at:
o: The G20 Summit in New Delhi
nb3cf603bf4a.x: The ISA was launched on 30 November 2015 at COP21 in Paris.
nb3cf603bf4a.tq: Combine a precise date with the correct international forum and venue.
xs: The **ISA** was launched on **30 Nov 2015** at **COP21, Paris** — option **(2)**.
Its HQ is **Gurugram**, not Paris.
xa: ISA is **treaty-based** with **116+ members** (**2024**).
Flagship: **One Sun One World One Grid**.
The **Global Biofuels Alliance** was launched at the **G20** in India (**2023**).

n47edd3b575c.s: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched in 2023 at:
o: The World Energy Congress in Abu Dhabi
The BRICS Summit in South Africa
n47edd3b575c.x: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched in 2023 at the G20 Summit in India.
n47edd3b575c.tq: Identify the launch forum and year of a global initiative.
xs: The **Global Biofuels Alliance** was launched in **2023** at the **G20** in **India** — option **(4)**.
It now has **32 countries + 14 international organisations** (**2026**).
xa: **IMEC** was also announced at **G20 New Delhi** (**Sept 2023**).
The **ISA** was launched at **COP21, Paris** (**2015**).
**IEF** secretariat: **Riyadh**.

ncf481852fed.s: India’s status in the International Energy Agency is that of a/an:
ncf481852fed.x: India has been an Association country of the IEA since 2017 and is not a full member.
ncf481852fed.tq: Distinguish association status from full membership.
xs: India is an **IEA Association country since 2017** — option **(4)**.
⚠ India is **not a full member** of the IEA.
xa: The thin SPR buffer (**9.5 days**) falls short of the IEA's **90 days**.
India engages the **IEF** (secretariat **Riyadh**) and holds an **Energy Dialogue with OPEC**.
**ISA** HQ: **Gurugram**.

n95f31620de5.s: The headquarters of the treaty-based International Solar Alliance (ISA) is located at:
n95f31620de5.x: The ISA is treaty-based with its headquarters at Gurugram. Paris (COP21) is where it was launched, not its HQ; New Delhi is a distractor; Riyadh hosts the IEF secretariat.
n95f31620de5.tq: ISA: launched Paris (COP21, 2015), HQ Gurugram. IEF: Riyadh.
xs: The **ISA**'s HQ is at **Gurugram** — option **(3)**.
**Paris** is where it was launched (**COP21, 30 Nov 2015**); **Riyadh** hosts the **IEF** secretariat.
xa: ⚠ **Gurugram** hosts both **ISA** HQ and **IFC-IOR**.
ISA is **treaty-based**, **116+ members**; flagship **One Sun One World One Grid**.
The **Global Biofuels Alliance** began at the **G20** (**2023**).

nea1668a0110.s: The Coast Guard is responsible for coastal security in territorial waters and functions under which Ministry?
nea1668a0110.x: The Coast Guard provides coastal security in territorial waters and functions under the Ministry of Defence.
nea1668a0110.tq: Ask which ministry would normally exercise authority over the maritime defence function.
xs: The **Coast Guard** handles coastal security in **territorial waters** under the **Ministry of Defence** — option **(1)**.
It was raised in **1977**.
xa: Post-**26/11** three tiers: **Navy** = overall; **Coast Guard** = territorial waters; **coastal police** = shallow waters.
**Sagar Kavach** is the **biannual** Coast Guard coastal-security exercise.
Coastline: **11,098.81 km**.

nec2976ecf8a.s: India shares its longest international land border with:
nec2976ecf8a.x: The Bangladesh border (4,096.7 km) is longer than the China (3,488 km), Pakistan (3,323 km) and Nepal (1,751 km) borders.
xa: Others: **Myanmar 1,643**, **Bhutan 699**, **Afghanistan 106** (shortest).
**CIBMS** smart fencing covers the **Pakistan + Bangladesh** borders.
The **BSF** guards both the longest (**Bangladesh**) and the **Pakistan** border.

n0f832a9ac0a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Vibrant Villages Programme-II (VVP-II)?
o: It covers Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Ladakh
It covers villages on the Pakistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal and Bhutan borders
Its roads are built under PMGSY-IV
n0f832a9ac0a.x: The China-border states (HP, Uttarakhand, Arunachal, Sikkim, Ladakh) are covered by the first phase of the Vibrant Villages Programme, not VVP-II.
xa: **CIBMS** = smart fencing on Pakistan + Bangladesh borders.
The **Department of Border Management** (**2004**) is in the **MHA**.
⚠ **ITBP** guards the **China** border these Phase I states face.

nb2bab4e397c.s: The Comprehensive Integrated Border Management System (CIBMS), a technology-based smart-fencing system, is meant mainly for India's borders with:
nb2bab4e397c.x: CIBMS is a technology-based smart-fencing system for the Pakistan and Bangladesh borders.
xa: The **BSF** guards both these borders.
Bangladesh border: **4,096.7 km**; Pakistan: **3,323 km**.
**VVP-II** (**2024-25 to 2028-29**) develops border villages.

nfa2d2763826.s: Withdrawal of general consent for the CBI and the wider reach of the NIA and BSF are criticised as intruding into which State subjects?
nfa2d2763826.x: The criticism is that these moves enter the State subjects of police and public order.
xa: BSF jurisdiction in **Punjab** and **West Bengal** went from **15 km to 50 km**.
The NIA can probe scheduled offences **without state consent**.
The **MHA** controls all **CAPFs**.

n07abb58fb3a.s: The Department of Border Management, created in 2004, functions under which Ministry?
n07abb58fb3a.x: The Department of Border Management is in the Ministry of Home Affairs (APPSC 2018 key), which also controls all CAPFs. The Ministry of Defence controls the Army and Coast Guard, not this department; MEA handles foreign relations; the Cabinet Secretariat houses RAW.
n07abb58fb3a.tq: Border Management Dept = MHA (2004); MHA controls all CAPFs.
xs: The **Department of Border Management** is in the **Ministry of Home Affairs** — option **(2)** (APPSC **2018** key).
The **MHA** also controls all **CAPFs**; the **Cabinet Secretariat** houses **RAW**.
xa: The department was created in **2004**.
The **Coast Guard** is under the **MoD**.
The **Army** guards the **LoC** and **LAC**.

n5444c6aaed3.s: The Intelligence Bureau was set up in which year?
n5444c6aaed3.x: The Intelligence Bureau was set up in 1887.
n5444c6aaed3.tq: Use the agency-specific year rather than the dates associated with RAW or SPG.
xs: The **Intelligence Bureau** was set up in **1887** — option **(1)**.
xa: The **IB** is under the **MHA** (internal intelligence).
Head: **Mahesh Dixit** (AP cadre, **1993** IPS), appointed **Jun 2026**.
⚠ **IB** = MHA (internal); **RAW** = Cabinet Secretariat (external); **CERT-In** = MeitY.

nfb26866a132.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The NIA is a voluntary auxiliary force raised by the States
The NIA functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs
The NIA can investigate scheduled offences anywhere in India without State consent
Home Guards are voluntary auxiliary forces under the States
nfb26866a132.x: Home Guards, not the NIA, are voluntary auxiliary forces of the States; the NIA is a central agency under the MHA.
xa: The **NIA Act** came in **2008**, after **26/11**.
NIA's chargesheet against **Hafiz Saeed** (Pahalgam) cites **BNS, 2023** + **UAPA, 1967**.
Extended **NIA/BSF** reach is criticised as entering state subjects of police and public order.

nc32350b9d07.s: Which force protects the Prime Minister and former Prime Ministers?
nc32350b9d07.x: The SPG (SPG Act 1988) protects the PM and former PMs; the NSG ('Black Cats') is the MHA counter-terror force.
xa: The **SPG** was set up in **1985**; **SPG Act 1988**.
The **NIA Act (2008)** also followed **26/11**.
**NATGRID** (MHA) is to be widened under the counter-terror policy.

n6fdd3b0e37c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)?
o: The CDS heads the Department of Military Affairs
The CDS is military adviser to the Nuclear Command Authority
The CDS is Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee
The CDS is the principal military adviser to the Prime Minister
n6fdd3b0e37c.x: The CDS is principal military adviser to the Defence Minister, not the Prime Minister.
xa: Post created **Dec 2019**; first CDS **Gen Bipin Rawat** (**1 Jan 2020**).
Age limit: **65**.
The Department of Military Affairs sits in the **MoD**.

n56f7d14a465.s: Who became India's first Chief of Defence Staff on 1 January 2020?
n56f7d14a465.x: Gen Bipin Rawat became the first CDS on 1 January 2020, after the post was created in December 2019. Naravane, Dalbir Singh and V.K. Singh were Army Chiefs but not the first CDS.
n56f7d14a465.tq: CDS: post created Dec 2019; first CDS Bipin Rawat from 1 Jan 2020; age limit 65.
xs: **Gen Bipin Rawat** became the first **CDS** on **1 Jan 2020** — option **(2)**.
The post was created in **Dec 2019**.
xa: The CDS heads the **Department of Military Affairs** (MoD).
The CDS advises the **Nuclear Command Authority**.
Age limit: **65**.

nfb2dee5dfb1.s: Which is India's oldest paramilitary force?
nfb2dee5dfb1.x: Assam Rifles (1835) is the oldest; the CRPF began in 1939 as the Crown Representative's Police.
xa: CRPF marked its **88th** Raising Day in **2026**.
The **Internal Security Academy** of the CRPF is at **Mount Abu**.
The **MHA** controls all **CAPFs**.

n4ac7d9f6b30.s: The National Investigation Agency Act was enacted in 2008 following which major event?
n4ac7d9f6b30.x: The NIA Act was enacted in 2008 after the 26/11 Mumbai attacks.
n4ac7d9f6b30.tq: Link the legislation to the triggering security event and year.
xs: The **NIA Act (2008)** followed the **26/11 Mumbai attacks** — option **(4)**.
**Parliament attack** was in **2001**; **Pulwama** in **2019**; **Pahalgam** in **2025** — all different years.
xa: The NIA can probe **scheduled offences anywhere without state consent**.
The **NSG** played a key role in the **26/11** response.
After 26/11 came the **three-tier coastal security** system.

nb9b8234678b.s: The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act was enacted in:
nb9b8234678b.x: UAPA was enacted in 1967 and amended in 2004, 2008, 2012 and 2019.
xa: NIA's chargesheet against **Hafiz Saeed** cites **BNS, 2023** + **UAPA, 1967**, incl. waging war.
**BNS Section 113** defines "terrorist act".

nc48fd36b08d.s: Which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which replaced the IPC from 1 July 2024, defines a terrorist act?
nc48fd36b08d.x: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the IPC from 1 July 2024, and its Section 113 defines a terrorist act.
xa: The NIA's **Hafiz Saeed** chargesheet cites **BNS, 2023** + **UAPA, 1967**.
**UAPA**'s **2019** amendment lets the Centre designate individuals as terrorists.
**AFSPA** dates from **1958**.

n1db470944e0.s: The Coimbatore blasts took place in:
n1db470944e0.x: The Coimbatore blasts were in 1998, after the Rajiv Gandhi assassination (1991) and Mumbai blasts (1993) and before the Parliament attack (2001).
xa: Mumbai **1993**: **13 blasts**, **250+ killed**.
Parliament attack: **13 Dec 2001** (APPSC key).

nfc8209931b8.s: The responses associated with the Uri and Pulwama attacks were respectively:
o: Operation Cactus and Operation Blue Star
nfc8209931b8.x: The Uri attack in 2016 was followed by surgical strikes, while the Pulwama attack in 2019 was followed by Balakot action.
nfc8209931b8.tq: Preserve the chronological pairing rather than swapping the two responses.
xs: **Uri (2016)** → **surgical strikes**; **Pulwama (2019)** → **Balakot** — option **(4)**.
Option (2) reverses the pair.
xa: **Pahalgam (22 Apr 2025)** → **Operation Sindoor** from **7 May 2025**.
**Cactus** (**1988**) = Maldives; **Blue Star** (**1984**) = Amritsar.
**Mahadev** killed the **Pahalgam** mastermind; **Sadbhavana** is civic action.

n2c9fe5882e1.s: Operation Mahadev (2025), in which the Army and J&K Police killed the Pahalgam attack mastermind and two LeT terrorists, took place near:
n2c9fe5882e1.x: Operation Mahadev (APPSC 2025) was in J&K near Dachigam National Park. Gadchiroli is the C-60 anti-Naxal theatre, Amritsar was Operation Blue Star (1984) and Sriperumbudur was the site of Rajiv Gandhi's assassination (1991).
n2c9fe5882e1.tq: Mahadev = Dachigam, Pahalgam mastermind killed; Sindoor = strikes in Pakistan from 7 May 2025.
