AP's localised framework: **475 indicators**.

n9fa5028dcf7.s: In the SDG India Index 2023-24, which SDG was assessed only qualitatively?
n9fa5028dcf7.x: Scores were given for 16 SDGs; SDG 17 was assessed only qualitatively.
xa: **SDG 17** = **Partnerships for the Goals**.
The index used **113 indicators**, released **12 July 2024**.

nebd3465e688.s: In the SDG India Index 2023-24, which States topped the ranking with a composite score of 79?
nebd3465e688.x: Kerala and Uttarakhand jointly topped with 79. Himachal Pradesh (with Kerala) was ahead of Andhra Pradesh in the 2018 baseline index, not the 2023-24 topper pair. Bihar (57) and Jharkhand (62) were at the bottom. Andhra Pradesh scored 74 and ranked 9th.
xs: **Kerala and Uttarakhand** topped the 2023-24 Index with **79** — option **(1)**.
**Bihar (57)** and **Jharkhand (62)** were at the bottom.
xa: ⚠ In the first index (**2018**), **Himachal Pradesh** and **Kerala** were ahead of AP.
India's composite score: **71** (Front Runner).

n89ce5f1dd5a.s: In the SDG India Index, a State scoring between 65 and 99 is classified as:
n89ce5f1dd5a.x: Achiever is 100, Front Runner 65-99, Performer 50-64 and Aspirant below 50.
xa: Even the bottom state **Bihar (57)** is a **Performer**.
Top states **Kerala and Uttarakhand** scored **79**.
Goal-wise scores cover **16 SDGs**; **SDG 17** is assessed only qualitatively.

n6f7d101ebc3.s: Which Sustainable Development Goal saw Andhra Pradesh slip from 19th to 20th position and was identified as a concern?
n6f7d101ebc3.x: SDG 4 was the area of concern, with Andhra Pradesh slipping from 19th to 20th position.
n6f7d101ebc3.tq: Distinguish the concern indicator from the goals in which the State performed near the top.
xs: **SDG 4** (Quality Education) slipped from **19th to 20th** — option **(3)**.
**SDG 7** (**1st**) and **SDG 14** (**2nd**) are AP's best goals; **SDG 11** improved from **11th** to **9th**.
xa: **SDG 9** fell from **13th** to **21st**; **SDG 5** from **5th** to **14th**.

nc78cbe1efa3.s: According to the Sustainable Development Report 2025, India was placed:
o: 38th out of 139 economies with a score of 71
99th out of 167 countries with a score of about 67
99th out of 166 countries with a score of 79
81st out of 139 economies with a score of 67
nc78cbe1efa3.x: The Sustainable Development Report 2025 placed India 99th out of 167 countries, with a score of approximately 67, marking India’s first entry into the top 100.
nc78cbe1efa3.tq: Keep the international report’s rank, denominator and score separate from domestic index figures.
xs: In the **SDSN** Sustainable Development Report **2025**, India was **99th out of 167** with a score of **about 67** — option **(2)**.
India entered the **top 100 for the first time**.
⚠ **38th of 139** is India's **Global Innovation Index 2025** rank; **71** is India's SDG India Index score.
xa: Some notes say **166** countries.
Top three: **Finland, Sweden, Denmark**.

ne63e69763bd.s: India’s rank in the Global Innovation Index 2025 was:
ne63e69763bd.x: India ranked 38th in the Global Innovation Index 2025.
ne63e69763bd.tq: Recall the exact rank while rejecting nearby numerical distractors.
xs: India ranked **38th** in the **Global Innovation Index 2025** — option **(4)**.
It rose from **81st (2015)** to **38th (2025)** of **139** economies.
xa: **NITI Aayog** is India's **nodal body** for the GII.
NITI's **India Innovation Index** 3rd edition (**2021**) was released **21 July 2022**.

n02f1362c273.s: Which State ranked first among the major States in the Fiscal Health Index 2026?
n02f1362c273.x: Odisha ranked first among major States for the second consecutive year; Punjab was last.
xa: Achievers: **Odisha, Goa, Jharkhand**.
**AP ranked 17th** (Mar **2026**).
FHI 2026 is the **2nd edition**.

n54d8f88cecb.s: The Fiscal Health Index of NITI Aayog ranked Andhra Pradesh at which position for 2023–24?
n54d8f88cecb.x: Andhra Pradesh was ranked 17th in the NITI Aayog Fiscal Health Index for 2023–24.
n54d8f88cecb.tq: Recall the rank and distinguish it from nearby ordinal positions.
xs: **AP ranked 17th** in the **Fiscal Health Index 2026** (covering **2023-24**) — option **(1)**.
**Odisha** was **1st** among major states; **Punjab** last.
xa: FHI 2026 is NITI's **2nd edition**.
Achievers: **Odisha, Goa, Jharkhand**.
AP's SDG India Index rank fell **4th to 9th**.

n83154629c3a.s: The second India Electric Mobility Index was launched by which two organisations?
o: WRI India and the Asian Development Bank
NITI Aayog and the World Bank
Ministry of Heavy Industries and NITI Aayog
n83154629c3a.x: NITI Aayog and WRI India launched the second India Electric Mobility Index in September 2026.
n83154629c3a.tq: Apply the ‘who launched or developed it?’ authority trap.
xs: The **2nd India Electric Mobility Index** (Sep **2026**) was launched by **NITI Aayog and WRI India** — option **(4)**.
Its weights: **transport electrification 50%**, **charging infrastructure 30%**, **EV research and innovation 20%**.
xa: It uses **16 indicators**.
Other new 2026 indices: **FHI 2026** (2nd edition), **Investment Friendliness Index** (Jul 2026).

n3de9f63e707.s: The localised SDG framework of Andhra Pradesh consists of how many indicators?
n3de9f63e707.x: Andhra Pradesh has developed a localised SDG framework consisting of 475 indicators.
n3de9f63e707.tq: Distinguish the State-level indicator count from national index and NIF counts.
xs: AP's localised SDG framework has **475 indicators** — option **(4)**.
⚠ **113** = SDG India Index indicators; **169** = SDG targets; **277** = NIF indicators.
xa: The **Swarna Andhra KPIs Monitoring Framework** was launched on **13 Dec 2024**.
AP has **District, Mandal and Constituency Vision Plans**.
A **real-time dashboard** with district/mandal/village maps (**2024-25**).

nd257915fe46.s: In the SDG India Index 2023-24, Andhra Pradesh ranked first in:
nd257915fe46.x: AP ranked first in SDG 7 and second in SDG 14, and 9th overall.
xa: SDG-7 and SDG-14 ranks were **unchanged** from **2020-21**.
AP was **3rd** in **SDG 1** and **4th** in **SDG 12**.
AP also ranked **17th** in the **Fiscal Health Index**.

naa1c9393ffd.s: The document titled ‘Swarna Andhra @2047’ represents Andhra Pradesh’s version of which broader vision?
naa1c9393ffd.x: Swarna Andhra @2047 is Andhra Pradesh’s State Vision@2047 document aligned with Viksit Bharat @2047.
naa1c9393ffd.tq: Discriminate between similarly framed long-term national visions.
xs: **Swarna Andhra @2047** is AP's version of **State Vision@2047**, aligned with **Viksit Bharat @2047** — option **(2)**.
States write these under NITI's **State Support Mission**.
xa: **Swarna Andhra KPIs Monitoring Framework** launched **13 Dec 2024**.
**Strategy for New India @75** was released in **2018**.

nbb00e41f912.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about economic growth and economic development?
o: Economic development has a narrower scope than economic growth.
Economic development has qualitative and quantitative dimensions.
nbb00e41f912.x: Development has a broader, not narrower, scope than growth.
xa: Growth is measured by **real GDP/GNP**, per capita income; development by **HDI**, poverty ratio, literacy, life expectancy, inequality.
One-liner: growth = **increase in output**; development = **increase in wellbeing**.
Growth is **necessary but not sufficient** for development.

nc22dce5f0b8.s: Which is the oldest measure of development?
nc22dce5f0b8.x: Per capita real income is the oldest measure of development, though it may conceal how income is distributed among people.
xa: **MPI** came from **OPHI and UNDP** in **2010**.
Related measures: **IHDI**, **GDI**, **GII**, **Green GDP**, **Gini coefficient (1912)**.

n56bc1692828.s: Under the Swarna Andhra @2047 targets, which of the following combinations is correct?
o: GSDP ₹208 lakh crore, per capita income ₹35 lakh and growth above 10%, tracked through 451 KPIs
GSDP ₹308 lakh crore, per capita income ₹55 lakh and growth above 15%, tracked through 651 KPIs
GSDP ₹308 lakh crore, per capita income ₹55 lakh and growth above 12%, tracked through 651 KPIs
GSDP ₹350 lakh crore, per capita income ₹60 lakh and growth above 15%, tracked through 751 KPIs
n56bc1692828.x: Swarna Andhra @2047 targets GSDP of ₹308 lakh crore, per capita income of ₹55 lakh and growth above 15%, with progress tracked through 651 KPIs.
n56bc1692828.tq: Match all four target figures without substituting nearby values.
xs: Targets: **GSDP ₹308 lakh crore**, **per capita income ₹55 lakh**, **growth above 15%**, tracked through **651 KPIs** — option **(2)**.
Option (3) has the wrong growth rate; options (1) and (4) change the GSDP and KPI figures.
xa: AP's **GSDP 2025-26** (first advance estimates): **Rs 17.62 lakh crore**, growing **10.75%**.
AP per capita income **Rs 2,94,507** vs all-India **Rs 2,19,575**.
AP is the **first State** to publish **monthly economic reports**.

nb35606f692b.s: The comparison between Kerala’s HDI and per capita NSDP illustrates that:
o: Income ranking alone fully determines development ranking.
A State with a lower per capita income ranking can perform better in broader human development.
Kerala ranks first in both HDI and per capita NSDP among States.
HDI excludes health and education outcomes.
nb35606f692b.x: Kerala ranks second in HDI among States despite ranking seventh in per capita NSDP. This demonstrates that development extends beyond income.
nb35606f692b.tq: Infer the broader development lesson from a reversed income–HDI ranking.
xs: A State with a **lower per capita income ranking** can **perform better in human development** — option **(2)**.
**Kerala** is **2nd in HDI** among States despite being **7th** in per capita NSDP — development beyond income.
xa: HDI includes **health** and **education**: income is only **one of three** dimensions.
Growth = **increase in output**; development = **increase in wellbeing**.

n0e29407a42e.s: The Directive Principles of State Policy envisage which of the following as development objectives?
o: Adequate livelihood and reduction of inequality
n0e29407a42e.x: The Directive Principles envisage adequate livelihood and reduced inequality, rather than merely a higher national income.
n0e29407a42e.tq: Distinguish the constitutional welfare objective from a narrow income-growth objective.
xs: The **Directive Principles** envisage **adequate livelihood** and **reduction of inequality** — option **(4)**.
They aim beyond **just higher national income** — so options (1)-(3) are wrong.
xa: Welfare-centred alternatives: **Gandhian** model and the **capability approach**.
The **"new view"** of development stresses reduction of **poverty, unemployment and inequality**.

ncd640a8c10f.s: Who is associated with the new view of development expressed in The Meaning of Development?
ncd640a8c10f.x: Dudley Seers is associated with the new view of development and wrote The Meaning of Development in 1969.
ncd640a8c10f.tq: Link the named work and year to its associated development economist.
xs: The "new view" of development was framed by **Dudley Seers** in **The Meaning of Development** (**1969**) — option **(1)**.
**Rostow** gave the **stages of growth**; **Nurkse** the **vicious circle of poverty**; **Rosenstein-Rodan** the **Big push**.
xa: The new view (**1970s**): development = reduction of **poverty, unemployment and inequality**.
It does **not** rest on the **simple growth rate** alone (APPSC-G2 **2017**).

n2f6fc36b2af.s: Which one of the following is NOT emphasised by the new view of development?
o: The simple growth rate of the economy alone
n2f6fc36b2af.x: The new view does not rest on the simple growth rate alone. It emphasises reductions in poverty, unemployment and inequality.
n2f6fc36b2af.tq: Use the NOT formulation to isolate the narrow growth-only criterion.
xs: The new view does NOT emphasise **the simple growth rate of the economy alone** — option **(4)** (APPSC-G2 **2017**).
It defines development as reduction of **poverty**, **unemployment** and **inequality** within a growing economy.
xa: The new view was framed by **Dudley Seers** (**The Meaning of Development, 1969**).
PCI caveat: rising per-capita GNP is **not** development if poverty and unemployment also rise.

n34239922ec0.s: Which factor was given primary importance in the Western model of development?
o: High human development at modest income
Economic growth through rising GDP and industrialisation
n34239922ec0.x: The Western model places economic growth, rising GDP and industrialisation at the centre of development.
n34239922ec0.tq: Use the model’s defining emphasis to distinguish it from welfare-centred alternatives.
xs: The Western model gave priority to **economic growth** through **rising GDP and industrialisation** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2018**).
**Village industries** belong to the **Gandhian** model; **capability expansion** to **Amartya Sen**.
xa: The **"new view" (1970s)** shifted focus to **poverty, unemployment and inequality**.
Kerala shows **high HDI** (**2nd**) at modest income (**7th** in per capita NSDP).

n9fe425b757f.s: Which of the following is NOT a valid indicator of economic development?
o: A larger share of GDP originating from the primary sector
Structural transformation from agriculture to industry and services
n9fe425b757f.x: A larger share of GDP from the primary sector is not treated as an indicator of economic development. Institutional change, structural transformation and inclusive growth are valid indicators.
n9fe425b757f.tq: Find the exception by identifying the structural feature that does not signify transformation.
xs: A **larger share of GDP from the primary sector** is NOT an indicator of development — option **(1)** (APPSC-G2 **2008** framing).
Valid indicators: **institutional change**, **inclusive growth** and **structural transformation** (agrarian → industrial and service economies).
xa: Development means a **falling share of agriculture** and rising industry/services.
Other signs: rising **capital formation**, **social overhead capital**, **human resource development**.

n991ad460c66.s: Structural transformation in the context of economic development primarily refers to:
o: The replacement of human resources by natural resources
A shift from agrarian activity towards industrial and service activities
A shift from services to subsistence agriculture
A permanent increase in the share of agriculture in GDP
n991ad460c66.x: Structural transformation involves movement from an agrarian economy towards industrial and service sectors.
n991ad460c66.tq: Test the direction of structural change using the sectoral sequence.
xs: **Structural transformation** is the shift **from agrarian activity towards industrial and service** activities — option **(2)**.
It means a **falling share of agriculture** and rising industry/services — so options (3) and (4) are wrong.
xa: It is a valid indicator along with **institutional change** and **inclusive growth**.
⚠ A **larger share of GDP from the primary sector** is **not** an indicator (APPSC-G2 **2008**).

n14ee4320991.s: Other things remaining the same, a higher incremental capital-output ratio (ICOR) in an economy implies:
o: Higher growth for a given investment rate, because capital is used more efficiently
Lower growth for a given investment rate, because capital is used less efficiently
No effect on growth, because ICOR measures only the saving rate
Higher employment irrespective of the level of output
n14ee4320991.x: A higher ICOR means more capital is needed per unit of extra output, i.e. capital is less efficient, so a given saving and investment rate yields lower growth (growth = saving rate / capital-output ratio). The first option reverses this; ICOR is a capital-output ratio, not a saving rate; and it says nothing about guaranteed employment.
n14ee4320991.tq: Growth up with saving, down with ICOR.
xs: A higher **ICOR** means **lower growth** for a given investment rate, as capital is **used less efficiently** — option **(2)**.
The notes: higher ICOR (**less efficient capital**) → **lower growth**.
xa: **Harrod-Domar**: growth = **savings rate / capital-output ratio**.
Higher **saving and investment rate** → higher growth.
Capital formation fails if capital is **idle or badly used**.

n9de1d18bd4f.s: The trickle-down approach to development assumes that
o: Benefits of economic growth will automatically reach poorer sections
Growth must be restricted to rural areas
Only direct transfers can reduce poverty
n9de1d18bd4f.x: Trickle-down is the belief that the benefits of growth will percolate automatically to poorer sections of society.
n9de1d18bd4f.tq: Translate a growth strategy label into its underlying assumption.
xs: **Trickle-down** assumes **benefits of economic growth** reach the **poorer sections automatically** — option **(2)**.
It was the growth strategy of the **early Indian plans**.
xa: Trickle-down failing: HCES **2023-24** — **50% rural** and **20% urban** people cannot afford two thali meals a day.
**Hindu rate of growth** (**Raj Krishna**): about **3.5%** in the 1950s-1980s.

nfdad6965428.s: Which of the following best describes a green economy in the UNEP sense?
o: An economy in which environmental regulation is avoided to promote investment
An economy confined exclusively to agriculture
A low-carbon, resource-efficient and socially inclusive economy
A high-carbon economy based on unrestricted resource use
nfdad6965428.x: A green economy is low-carbon, resource-efficient and socially inclusive. It is not limited to agriculture and does not imply unrestricted resource use.
nfdad6965428.tq: Identify the option containing all three defining attributes.
xs: A **green economy** (UNEP) is a **low-carbon, resource-efficient and socially inclusive** economy — option **(3)**.
Options (1) and (4) contradict its low-carbon, resource-efficient nature.
xa: **Brundtland Report (1987)**: meet present needs without compromising future generations.
**Sustainable growth**: policy intervention for economic and social well-being (APPSC **2018**).
The **17 SDGs** came into force from **2016**.

nindian-economy-27-3.s: Economic development may not be higher despite rising real GNP if ____ increase.
nindian-economy-27-3.x: Higher real GNP need not mean development, because poverty and unemployment can still rise.
n: An increase in absolute real GNP does not necessarily mean higher economic development. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 40-41]
An increase in per-capita real GNP does not necessarily mean higher economic development. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 40-41]
Rising poverty can prevent an increase in real GNP from indicating higher economic development. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 40-41]
Rising unemployment can prevent an increase in real GNP from indicating higher economic development. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 40-41]
xa: The **"new view" of development (1970s)**: development = reduction of **poverty, unemployment and inequality**.
The new view was framed by **Dudley Seers** (The Meaning of Development, 1969).
It does **not** stress the **simple growth rate** of the economy (APPSC-G2 2017).

n42655dc1d02.s: The capability approach to development is associated with:
n42655dc1d02.x: The capability approach is Amartya Sen's; Pigou is linked with the welfare approach and Paul Streeten (with the ILO) with basic needs.
xa: Sen's book: **Development as Freedom**.
Welfare measures: **NEW** (**Samuelson**), **MEW** (**Nordhaus-Tobin**).
The **"new view"** was framed by **Dudley Seers**.

n970a5a519ad.s: Who is associated with the theory of the vicious circle of poverty?
n970a5a519ad.x: Ragnar Nurkse is associated with the vicious circle of poverty, expressed through the idea that a country is poor because it remains poor.
n970a5a519ad.tq: Use direct economist–theory association and distinguish it from neighbouring development theories.
xs: The **vicious circle of poverty** ("a country is poor because it is poor") is **Ragnar Nurkse**'s — option **(3)** (APPSC **2025**).
**Leibenstein** = **critical minimum effort**; **Rostow** = **stages of growth**; **Hirschman** = **unbalanced growth**.
xa: ⚠ **Nurkse** = vicious circle + **balanced growth**; **Hirschman** = unbalanced growth.
**Big push** (**1943**): **Rosenstein-Rodan**.

n0614ad77ced.s: The ‘Big Push’ theory of development was propounded by which economist?
n0614ad77ced.x: The Big Push theory was propounded by Paul Rosenstein-Rodan in 1943.
n0614ad77ced.tq: Test the economist associated with a named theory rather than its objective.
xs: The **Big push** theory (**1943**) was given by **Paul Rosenstein-Rodan** — option **(1)**.
**Hirschman** = **unbalanced growth**; **Leibenstein** = **critical minimum effort**; **Sen** = **capability approach**.
xa: **Balanced growth**: **Ragnar Nurkse** (with Rosenstein-Rodan).
**Harrod-Domar**: growth = savings rate / capital-output ratio.

n3bc7a1e8a6f.s: The 'critical minimum effort' thesis is associated with:
n3bc7a1e8a6f.x: Critical minimum effort is Leibenstein's; Nurkse gave balanced growth, Hirschman unbalanced growth and Rostow the stages of growth.
xa: Hirschman's book: **The Strategy of Economic Development (1958)**.
India's early plans followed **unbalanced growth** — the **Mahalanobis** model put heavy industry first.
**Big push** (**1943**): **Rosenstein-Rodan**.

nindian-economy-67-9.s: Which economist is associated with welfare economics, social choice and the capability approach?
nindian-economy-67-9.x: Amartya Sen is known for welfare economics, social choice theory and the capability approach. Mahbub-ul-Haq built the HDI on Sen's ideas.
n: Amartya Sen is associated with Welfare economics. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
Amartya Sen is associated with the Capability Approach. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
Amartya Sen is associated with Social Choice Theory. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
xs: **Amartya Sen** is associated with **welfare economics**, **social choice theory** and the **capability approach** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Morris D. Morris** = **PQLI**; **Ragnar Nurkse** = **vicious circle of poverty**; **Mahbub-ul-Haq** = **HDI**.
xa: Sen's book: **Development as Freedom** — development as expansion of substantive freedoms.
⚠ **Nurkse** = vicious circle + balanced growth; **Hirschman** = unbalanced growth.
The **big push** theory (**1943**) = **P.N. Rosenstein-Rodan**.

nindian-economy-67-13.s: Which Indian economist received the Leontief Prize for advancing the frontiers of economic thought, notably for work on gender and land rights?
nindian-economy-67-13.x: Bina Agarwal won the Leontief Prize of Tufts University's Global Development and Environment Institute for her work on gender, land rights and environment. Kelkar and Rangarajan are known for policy committees.
n: Bina Agarwal is an Indian economist. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
Bina Agarwal is associated with the Leontief Award 2009. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
xs: **Bina Agarwal**, an **Indian economist**, received the **Leontief Award 2009** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The notes list no Leontief link for **Vijay Kelkar**, **Rangarajan** or **Amartya Sen**; Sen is linked to the **capability approach**.
xa: **Amartya Sen** = welfare economics, social choice theory, **human development**.
**Harvey Leibenstein** = **critical minimum effort** thesis.
**W.W. Rostow** = stages of economic growth (**take-off**).

n63952a1ca8c.s: Which one of the following represents the correct sequence of Rostow’s stages of economic growth?
o: Traditional society → take-off → pre-conditions for take-off → drive to maturity → age of high mass consumption
Traditional society → pre-conditions for take-off → take-off → drive to maturity → age of high mass consumption
Pre-conditions for take-off → traditional society → take-off → age of high mass consumption → drive to maturity
Traditional society → drive to maturity → pre-conditions for take-off → take-off → age of high mass consumption
n63952a1ca8c.x: Rostow’s sequence is traditional society, pre-conditions for take-off, take-off, drive to maturity and age of high mass consumption.
n63952a1ca8c.tq: Identify the fixed first and final stages, then arrange the intervening stages.
xs: Rostow's order: **traditional society → pre-conditions for take-off → take-off → drive to maturity → age of high mass consumption** — option **(2)**.
**Take-off** comes after its pre-conditions and before the **drive to maturity**.
xa: Rostow's theory = **stages of economic growth (take-off)**.
**Harrod-Domar**: growth = savings rate / capital-output ratio.
**Leibenstein**: **critical minimum effort** thesis.

ndd156ebd962.s: 'Development as Freedom', which presents development as the expansion of substantive freedoms, is associated with:
ndd156ebd962.x: Amartya Sen's capability approach, associated with Development as Freedom, treats literacy and health as constituents of development.
xa: **HDI** was developed by **Mahbub ul Haq** with Amartya Sen (UNDP HDR **1990**).
The **basic needs** approach: **ILO (1976)**, Paul Streeten.

n83716479f06.s: The Human Development Index was introduced in the first Human Development Report of
n83716479f06.x: The first Human Development Report was published in 1990, when the HDI framework was introduced.
n83716479f06.tq: Direct year recall using a numerical distractor from a related index.
xs: The **HDI** came in the first **UNDP HDR of 1990** — option **(3)**.
**1979** is the **PQLI** year; **2010** is the **MPI** year.
xa: The first HDR team was led by **Mahbub ul Haq and Inge Kaul**.
HDI: **Mahbub ul Haq** with **Amartya Sen**.
First Indian state HDR: **Madhya Pradesh**.

n8f86d40b231.s: In the Human Development Index, standard of living is measured through:
o: GDP per capita at current prices
Net national income at factor cost
n8f86d40b231.x: The HDI measures standard of living through GNI per capita at PPP, alongside life expectancy and schooling.
xa: ⚠ PQLI uses life expectancy at age **one**, HDI at **birth**.
HDI began with the UNDP HDR **1990**.

nindian-economy-52-4.s: Which index focuses on basic necessities such as water, sanitation and housing?
nindian-economy-52-4.x: The BNI covers basic necessities like water, sanitation and housing; PQLI uses literacy, IMR and life expectancy.
n: PQLI focuses on physical quality of life. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
PQLI includes literacy. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
PQLI includes infant mortality rate. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
PQLI includes life expectancy. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
MPI focuses on poverty and deprivation. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
MPI includes health. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
MPI includes education. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
MPI includes living standards. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
BNI focuses on basic necessities. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
BNI includes water. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
BNI includes sanitation. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
BNI includes housing. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
PQLI measures physical quality of life. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
MPI measures multidimensional poverty. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
BNI measures basic necessities. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
xa: PQLI uses life expectancy at age **one**; HDI uses life expectancy at **birth**.
**MPI** uses 10 indicators; OPHI and UNDP, **2010**.
**GII** (UNDP) covers **health**, **empowerment**, **labour**.

nindian-economy-52-6.s: BNI is associated with which of the following?
nindian-economy-52-6.x: The Basic Necessities Index (BNI) appeared in the Economic Survey and covers water, sanitation and housing.
nindian-economy-52-6.tq: Match each index to its publisher.
n: BNI is associated with the Economic Survey. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
xs: **BNI** is associated with the **Economic Survey** — so option **(4)** is correct.
BNI = **Basic Necessities Index**, covering **water**, **sanitation** and **housing**.
**NSO** = CPI and IIP; **Office of the Economic Adviser** = WPI; **NITI Aayog** = State Health Index.
xa: **HDI** = **UNDP**: health, education, income.
**PQLI** = **Morris D. Morris** (0-100 scale).
**MPI** = **OPHI** and **UNDP**.

nindian-economy-52-7.x: WPI tracks wholesale prices; CPI tracks retail prices and IIP industrial output.
n: State Health Index measures state health performance. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #52 · pp 77-78]
xa: IIP covers **mining**, **manufacturing**, **electricity**.
**BNI** = basic necessities — **Economic Survey**.
**Per capita income** is the oldest measure but **hides distribution**.

nindian-economy-67-11.s: The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) is associated with:
nindian-economy-67-11.x: Morris D. Morris is linked with the PQLI; Mahbub-ul-Haq with the HDI, Kuznets with per capita income and Gini with the Gini coefficient.
n: Mahbub-ul-Haq is associated with HDI. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
Simon Kuznets is associated with the per-capita income measure. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
Morris D. Morris is associated with PQLI. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
Corrado Gini is associated with the Gini Coefficient. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
Simon Kuznets is associated with National income and development. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
Morris D. Morris is associated with Quality of life measurement. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
Corrado Gini is associated with Income inequality. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
xa: ⚠ Lorenz curve **1906** (no number); Gini **1912** (range **0** to **1**).
**Kuznets curve** = **inverted-U**: inequality first rises, then falls.
First HDR **1990**: team led by **Mahbub ul Haq and Inge Kaul**.

n1de4d16e707.s: The Kuznets curve describes which relationship?
o: A direct and continuously rising relationship between income and inequality
An inverse relationship between inflation and unemployment
An inverted-U relationship in which inequality first rises and later falls as income grows
A relationship between tax rates and tax revenue only
n1de4d16e707.x: The Kuznets curve presents an inverted-U relationship: inequality initially rises and subsequently falls with increasing income.
n1de4d16e707.tq: Recognize the shape and direction of the named curve.
xs: The **Kuznets curve** is an **inverted-U**: **inequality first rises and later falls as income grows** — option **(3)**.
Inflation vs unemployment is the **Phillips curve**; tax rate vs revenue the **Laffer curve**.
xa: The **Environmental Kuznets curve** applies the idea to **pollution** vs per capita income.
The **Lorenz curve** (**Max Lorenz, 1906**) shows income distribution visually.
The **Gini coefficient** (**1912**) gives inequality as a number from **0** to **1**.

o: Inflation always falls when unemployment rises
Any increase in tax rates always increases tax revenue
Beyond a certain point, higher tax rates may reduce tax revenue
Income inequality always rises with per capita income
n62f6fff5b06.x: The Laffer curve shows that tax revenue may decline when tax rates are increased beyond a certain point.
n62f6fff5b06.tq: Apply the threshold effect rather than accepting an ‘always’ statement.
xs: The **Laffer curve** shows that **beyond a point, higher tax rates cut tax revenue** — option **(3)**.
It is **Arthur Laffer**'s curve of **tax rate vs tax revenue** — so option (2) is wrong.
xa: **Phillips curve** (**A.W. Phillips**): inverse relation between **inflation and unemployment**.
**Kuznets curve**: **inverted-U** between inequality and income.
**Lorenz curve**: **Max Lorenz, 1906**.

n05fe25d9894.s: Which of the following correctly states the range of the Gini coefficient?
n05fe25d9894.x: The Gini coefficient ranges from 0, representing perfect equality, to 1, representing perfect inequality.
xa: Gini = area between the **equality line** and **Lorenz curve** / total area below the equality line.
Devised by **Corrado Gini**, **1912**.
⚠ The **Lorenz curve** (**1906**) is only visual and gives **no numerical value**.

nbb805c535fd.s: The Phillips curve, associated with A.W. Phillips, depicts:
o: An inverse relationship between inflation and unemployment
The relationship between tax rates and tax revenue
An inverted-U relationship between income inequality and per capita income
The cumulative share of income received by cumulative shares of population
nbb805c535fd.x: The Phillips curve shows an inverse relation between inflation and unemployment. Tax rate versus revenue is the Laffer curve; the inverted-U of inequality against income is the Kuznets curve; and cumulative population against cumulative income is the Lorenz curve.
nbb805c535fd.tq: Phillips = inflation vs unemployment; Laffer = tax; Kuznets = inverted-U.
xs: The **Phillips curve** shows an **inverse relation between inflation and unemployment** — option **(1)**.
Tax rate vs revenue is the **Laffer curve**; the inverted-U of inequality is the **Kuznets curve**; cumulative income shares is the **Lorenz curve**.
xa: Lorenz curve: farther from the **45-degree line** = more inequality.
**Environmental Kuznets curve**: pollution rises, then falls with income.

n260eb76dcc5.s: Economic growth is ____ for economic development.
n260eb76dcc5.x: Development cannot occur without some growth, but growth alone may not produce development.
xa: Growth = **means**, development = **end**.
**Growth without development** can happen through **jobless growth** or unequal gains.

n5711082bb0f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about indicators of economic development?
o: Workers moving out of agriculture may raise labour productivity.
Rising capital formation is a sign of development.
Social overhead capital contributes to development.
Human resource development is unrelated to economic development.
n5711082bb0f.x: Human resource development is an important sign and component of economic development.
xa: Valid indicators: **institutional change**, **structural transformation**, **inclusive growth**.
Not an indicator: a **larger share of GDP from the primary sector**.

n5b3bd03a94a.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Physical Quality of Life Index?
n5b3bd03a94a.x: PQLI uses literacy, infant mortality and life expectancy at age one; GNI per capita at PPP is an HDI component.
xa: PQLI was developed by **Morris D. Morris** in **1979**, on a **0-100** scale.
⚠ PQLI uses life expectancy at age **one**; HDI uses life expectancy at **birth**.

n2d3211b6a78.s: The Measure of Economic Welfare (MEW) is associated with:
n2d3211b6a78.x: MEW is associated with Nordhaus and Tobin; Net Economic Welfare is associated with Paul Samuelson.
xa: The Gini coefficient ranges from **0 (perfect equality)** to **1 (perfect inequality)**.
⚠ **Lorenz curve** (**1906**) gives no number; **Gini** (**1912**) gives a number.

n2fa5f49edb1.s: Which State was the first in India to publish a Human Development Report?
n2fa5f49edb1.x: Madhya Pradesh was the first Indian State to publish a Human Development Report.
n2fa5f49edb1.tq: Direct location recall with geographically plausible State distractors.
xs: The first Indian state HDR was published by **Madhya Pradesh** — option **(3)**.
**Kerala** is noted for being **2nd in HDI** among States, not for the first state HDR.
xa: The first HDR (**1990**) was led by **Mahbub ul Haq and Inge Kaul**.
HDI dimensions: health, knowledge, **decent standard of living**.

n68a0b53ffc0.s: Capital formation may fail to increase output when:
o: capital remains idle or is badly used
complementary inputs such as skills and infrastructure are absent
n68a0b53ffc0.x: Idle or misused capital, missing complementary inputs and inadequate demand can each stop capital formation from raising output.
xa: Higher saving and investment rate → **higher growth**; higher **ICOR** → **lower growth**.
**Capital-intensive investment** may add little employment.

nf2ed5fb95b3.s: Which of the following is classified as an economic determinant of growth?
nf2ed5fb95b3.x: Natural resources and technical progress are economic factors; institutions, rule of law, population quality and social structure are non-economic.
xa: **Human capital** (education, health, skills) is an **economic** factor.
**Governance, accountability, competition** are non-economic.

n90af7b933b9.s: Who coined the term ‘Hindu rate of growth’ to describe India's low and stagnant growth of roughly 3.5 per cent during the 1950s–1980s?
n90af7b933b9.x: Raj Krishna coined the term ‘Hindu rate of growth’ for India's stagnant or low growth of about 3.5 per cent during the period.
n90af7b933b9.tq: Direct term-coiner identification combined with the described phenomenon.
xs: **Raj Krishna** coined **"Hindu rate of growth"** for India's stagnant growth of about **3.5%** in the **1950s-1980s** — option **(4)**.
**Myrdal** wrote **Economic Theory and Underdeveloped Regions**; **Hirschman** gave **unbalanced growth**; **Sen** the **capability approach**.
xa: **Jobless growth**: output rises, employment does not (UNDP HDR **1996**).
**Trickle-down** was the growth strategy of the early Indian plans.

n9f6f40ffcaa.s: Which of the following was NOT included among the five forms of ‘bad growth’ identified in the UNDP Human Development Report 1996?
n9f6f40ffcaa.x: The five forms were jobless, ruthless, voiceless, rootless and futureless growth. Balanced growth was not included in that list.
n9f6f40ffcaa.tq: Find the odd term in a memorised named list.
xs: **Balanced growth** is NOT a "bad growth" — option **(1)**; it is **Ragnar Nurkse**'s theory.
The HDR **1996** five bad growths: **jobless, ruthless, voiceless, rootless, futureless**.
xa: ⚠ **Nurkse** = balanced growth; **Hirschman** = unbalanced growth.
**Jobless growth**: output rises, employment does not.

n3b611eaa69c.s: The Brundtland definition of sustainable development balances present needs with:
o: the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
a ban on present use of natural resources
n3b611eaa69c.x: Sustainable development meets present needs while preserving future generations' ability to meet theirs; it does not prohibit resource use.
xa: Report: **Our Common Future, 1987**.
Operationalised through **17 SDGs, 169 targets** (**2015-2030**).
SDGs adopted by the **UNGA 70th session**, **2015**; in force from **2016**.

nc9a34088663.s: The three pillars of India's inclusive growth model are:
o: Antyodaya, Empowerment and Poverty and Unemployment
nc9a34088663.x: The three pillars are Market Economics, Empowerment and Pragmatism.
xa: Inclusive growth = **broad-based, shared, pro-poor growth** raising people's participation.
Government framing: **"Sabka Saath Sabka Vikas aur Sabka Vishwas"**.
⚠ Do not confuse with the **WEF IDI** pillars or the **11th Plan**'s components of inclusive growth.

nc80edae0a23.s: Inclusive growth is best described as:
o: Rapid growth of national income concentrated in a few productive sectors
Broad-based, shared and pro-poor growth that increases people's participation in the growth process
Growth confined to rural areas through agricultural expansion
Growth achieved exclusively through redistribution of existing wealth
nc80edae0a23.x: Inclusive growth is broad-based, shared and pro-poor growth that raises people's participation in the growth process.
nc80edae0a23.tq: Select the option containing the complete definition rather than a single component of the concept.
xs: Inclusive growth is **broad-based, shared, pro-poor growth** that raises **people's participation** in growth — option **(2)**.
It looks at both the **pace and pattern** of growth (who benefits), not growth concentrated in a few sectors.
xa: Three pillars: **Market Economics, Empowerment and Pragmatism**.
It also covers **gender and regional balance** (UPSC).
The **11th Plan (2007-12)** first made inclusive growth the objective.

n6e5d3aaecb4.s: Besides the pace of growth, inclusive growth also examines:
o: only the rate of industrial output
the pattern of growth and who receives its benefits
only the rate of GDP growth
n6e5d3aaecb4.x: Inclusive growth considers the pattern of growth and distribution of benefits, including gender and regional balance.
xa: Inclusive development measures: **HDI, poverty rates, literacy, access to basic services**, gender equality.
Growth measures: **GDP**, industrial output, employment.

nindian-economy-70-21.s: Growth whose economic benefits are shared by all sections of society is called:
nindian-economy-70-21.x: Shared economic benefits are a feature of inclusive growth: growth whose gains reach all sections.
n: Inclusive growth requires education. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 101-102]
Education improves capabilities. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 101-102]
Inclusive growth requires health. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 101-102]
Health improves human capital. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 101-102]
Inclusive growth requires access to credit. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 101-102]
Access to credit enables productive activity. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 101-102]
Inclusive growth provides shared economic benefits. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 101-102]
xa: Government framing: "**Sabka Saath Sabka Vikas aur Sabka Vishwas**".
⚠ **Trap:** inclusive growth is **not** expected from a high national-income growth rate by itself (UPPSC 2013).
**12th Plan**: "**Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth**" — the last Five Year Plan.

nefd91a130fd.s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to minimise inequalities in income, status, facilities and opportunities?
nefd91a130fd.x: Article 38 seeks a social order based on social, economic and political justice and directs the State to minimise inequalities in income, status, facilities and opportunities.
xa: **Art. 31C** (**25th Amendment, 1971**) protects laws giving effect to **39(b) and (c)**.

nd449e554ac6.s: Article 31C, protecting laws giving effect to Articles 39(b) and 39(c), was inserted by the:
nd449e554ac6.x: Article 31C was inserted by the 25th Amendment, 1971.
xa: Only these two DPSPs — **39(b) and (c)** — override Fundamental Rights.

nca3126f6867.s: The Bhagwati-Sen debate is about the relative priority of:
o: Public sector first or private sector first
Export promotion first or import substitution first
Economic growth first or social infrastructure investment first
nca3126f6867.x: The debate contrasts the growth-first approach (Bhagwati) with prioritising investment in social infrastructure such as health and education (Sen).
xa: Books (**2013**): **Why Growth Matters** (Bhagwati-Panagariya); **An Uncertain Glory** (Sen-Dreze).
Sen: for backward countries, **primary education and health** get highest priority (APPSC-GS **2007**).

na8865e8d120.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Bhagwati-Sen debate?
o: Bhagwati, with Arvind Panagariya, prioritised rapid, market-led growth.
Sen argued that growth alone removes deprivation.
Sen, with Jean Dreze, prioritised public investment in education, health and nutrition.
Bhagwati held that growth creates jobs and revenue to finance social spending.
na8865e8d120.x: Sen argued that growth alone does not remove deprivation.
xa: ⚠ **Why Growth Matters** = Bhagwati-Panagariya; **An Uncertain Glory** = Sen-Dreze.
Sen's **"Kerala Model"**: high health and education at modest income.

n47b61e9e08f.s: Which of the following books is associated with Jagdish Bhagwati and Arvind Panagariya in the Bhagwati-Sen debate?
n47b61e9e08f.x: Why Growth Matters, published in 2013, is associated with Jagdish Bhagwati and Arvind Panagariya.
n47b61e9e08f.tq: Apply author-book matching and distinguish the two books central to the debate.
xs: **Why Growth Matters** (**2013**) is by **Bhagwati and Panagariya** — option **(2)**.
**An Uncertain Glory** is by **Sen and Dreze**; **Development as Freedom** is Sen's capability-approach book.
xa: The debate's core: **growth first** vs **social infrastructure first** (APPSC-G1 **2017**).
Bhagwati: growth creates **jobs and revenue** that later fund social spending.

nindian-economy-70-12.s: In inclusive development, education mainly contributes by:
o: improving capabilities through knowledge and skills
nindian-economy-70-12.x: Education builds capabilities through knowledge and skills; agricultural revival helps rural people and infrastructure widens access.
n: Inclusive growth requires infrastructure development. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 101-102]
Infrastructure development expands access and economic opportunities. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 101-102]
Inclusive growth requires agricultural development or revival. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 101-102]
Agricultural development or revival benefits the rural population. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 101-102]
Inclusive growth requires education. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 101-102]
Education improves capabilities. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 101-102]
Inclusive growth requires health. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 101-102]
Health improves human capital. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 101-102]
xa: **Employment opportunities** **enable participation in growth**.
**SHGs** enable **financial and economic participation**.
**Right to Education** brings disadvantaged children into the **mainstream**.

n0c7762c3afd.s: A major criticism of the trickle-down approach is that it:
o: Widens inequality and may miss vulnerable sections
Neglects the growth of national income
Relies too heavily on community participation
n0c7762c3afd.x: Critics argue that trickle-down (growth-first) growth can widen inequality and fail to reach vulnerable groups.
xa: The alternative **direct attack** uses targeted **wage/self-employment, food and cash transfers**.
**Welfare** approach: safety nets, health, education (**Nordic states**).

ne8939cd35f5.s: Which Five Year Plan first made inclusive growth an objective?
ne8939cd35f5.x: The Eleventh Five Year Plan, covering 2007–12, first made inclusive growth an objective.
ne8939cd35f5.tq: Distinguish the first adoption of a theme from its continuation in the succeeding Plan.
xs: The **Eleventh Five Year Plan (2007-12)** first made inclusive growth the objective — option **(3)**.
Its theme: **"Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth"**.
xa: Target **9%** → **10%** by the end; achieved about **8%**.
The **12th Plan (2012-17)**: "**Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth**" — the **last** Five Year Plan.

nef325ed661e.s: Which of the following was NOT a component of the Eleventh Five Year Plan's inclusive-growth strategy?
o: Exclusive dependence on urban service-sector expansion
nef325ed661e.x: The components included agricultural growth, employment and poverty reduction, reduction of regional and other disparities, and equitable growth. Exclusive dependence on urban services was not a component.
nef325ed661e.tq: Find the option that falls outside the stated component list.
xs: **Exclusive dependence on urban service-sector expansion** was NOT a component — option **(2)**.
The 11th Plan's components: **agricultural growth**; **employment and poverty reduction**; **reducing regional and other disparities**; **equitable growth**.
xa: ⚠ An **urban-only focus** does not help inclusive growth (APPSC).
11th Plan theme: **"Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth"** (**2007-12**).

n19cd08bdace.s: The theme of the Twelfth Five Year Plan (2012-17), India's last Five Year Plan, was:
o: Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth
Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth
Sabka Saath Sabka Vikas aur Sabka Vishwas
n19cd08bdace.x: The 12th Plan's theme was 'Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth'. 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth' was the 11th Plan (2007-12), the first to make inclusive growth the objective; 'Garibi Hatao' is linked to the 5th Plan's direct attack on poverty; and 'Sabka Saath...' is the present government's framing, not a Plan theme.
n19cd08bdace.tq: 11th = Towards Faster & More Inclusive; 12th adds Sustainable.
xs: The 12th Plan's theme was **"Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth"** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **"Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth"** was the **11th Plan**'s theme.
**"Garibi Hatao"** belongs to the **5th Plan**; **"Sabka Saath..."** is the current government framing.
xa: The 12th Plan (**2012-17**) had a **9%** target and was the **last** Five Year Plan.
The **11th Plan** was the **first** to make inclusive growth the objective; it achieved about **8%**.

n0949dc05acc.s: DAY-NRLM covers 10.05 crore women in about how many SHGs?
n0949dc05acc.x: DAY-NRLM covers 10.05 crore women in 90.09 lakh SHGs.
xa: **Lakhpati Didi** target: **3 crore** women with income above **Rs 1 lakh**.
**Aspirational Districts**: **Jan 2018**, **49 KPIs**, **5 themes**.

n6f1b3141f6c.s: VB-G RAM G, which replaced MGNREGA, guarantees how many days of rural wage employment?
n6f1b3141f6c.x: VB-G RAM G raised the employment guarantee from 100 days to 125 days.
xa: Allocation: **Rs 95,692 crore** in **Budget 2026-27**.
Centre released **Rs 2,545.50 crore** to AP under VB-G RAM G (Jul **2026**).

ne819eba81c3.s: The Aspirational Districts Programme, with 49 KPIs across five themes, began in:
ne819eba81c3.x: Aspirational Districts began in January 2018; Aspirational Blocks began in January 2023 covering 500 blocks.
xa: These are **area-based** instruments of inclusive growth (IYB **2026**).
Other instruments: **SHGs**, **MSMEs**, **rural wage jobs**, **skilling**.

n3035285dee8.s: MSMEs account for about what share of India's exports?
n3035285dee8.x: MSMEs contribute 48.58% of exports, 31.1% of GDP and 35.4% of manufacturing output.
xa: India has **8.7 crore+** MSMEs (LENSD, **28 Jun 2026**).
They are the **2nd-largest employer** after agriculture — **38.9 crore** livelihoods.

n006e958a68d.s: Which of the following is an indicator of inclusive development rather than of mere economic growth?
n006e958a68d.x: GDP, industrial output and employment measure growth, whereas HDI, poverty rates and access to basic services indicate inclusive development.
xa: Inclusive development measures also include **literacy** and **gender equality**.
The **WEF IDI** measures development **beyond GDP**.

n08f3d03896a.s: As per the World Bank, India's extreme poverty at the $3-a-day line fell from 27.1% in 2011-12 to ____ in 2022-23.
n08f3d03896a.x: Extreme poverty at $3 a day fell from 27.1% to 5.3%; 23.9% is the 2022-23 figure at the $4.20 line.
xa: But the **World Inequality Database** shows **rising income inequality**.
AP MPI headcount **6.06%** vs India **14.96%**.
**29%** of tertiary-educated youth are unemployed (**2026**).

n48683f1ef98.s: Which of the following correctly lists the three pillars of the Inclusive Development Index?
o: Growth and development; inclusion; intergenerational equity and sustainability
GDP growth; inflation control; fiscal consolidation
n48683f1ef98.x: The three pillars are growth and development, inclusion, and intergenerational equity and sustainability.
n48683f1ef98.tq: Recall the complete three-part structure of an index.
xs: IDI pillars: **growth and development**; **inclusion**; **intergenerational equity and sustainability** — option **(1)**.
The other options list unrelated macro goals, not the WEF's pillars.
xa: ⚠ Do not confuse with India's inclusive growth pillars: **Market Economics, Empowerment and Pragmatism**.
IDI measures development **beyond GDP** (**IDI 2018**).

n20d4b02ab38.s: According to Amartya Sen, backward countries should give the highest priority to:
n20d4b02ab38.x: Sen emphasised primary education and health as the highest priorities for backward countries.
xa: Sen's **capability approach**: **Development as Freedom**.
The **"Kerala Model"**: high health and education at modest income.
Book with Jean Dreze: **An Uncertain Glory** (**2013**).

nc5a18ec7072.s: Which of the following groups is specifically identified as a target segment of inclusive growth policies?
o: Marginal farmers, landless labourers and SC/ST communities
Large corporate borrowers and high-income professionals
nc5a18ec7072.x: The identified target segments include marginal farmers, landless labourers and SC/ST communities; the focus is not limited to persons in semi-urban areas.
nc5a18ec7072.tq: Identify the specified beneficiary groups and reject the narrow-location trap.
xs: Target segments are **marginal farmers, landless labourers and SC/ST communities** — option **(1)** (UPPSC **2016**).
⚠ **Trap:** "persons in **semi-urban areas**" is not a target segment.
xa: Inclusive growth comes from **rural development, agriculture, farm credit** (UPPSC **2013**).
Inclusive growth is **pro-poor** and broad-based.

nbb5ed7adf29.s: Which of the following combinations contains only instruments that help inclusive growth?
o: Cuts in social spending and import tariffs
Urban-only focus and cuts in social spending
nbb5ed7adf29.x: Education reform and vocational training support inclusive growth. An urban-only focus, import tariffs in the stated context and cuts in social spending are not identified as helpful instruments.
nbb5ed7adf29.tq: Separate positive policy instruments from the three stated non-instruments.
xs: **Education reform and vocational training** help inclusive growth — option **(3)** (APPSC).
**Urban-only focus**, **import tariffs** and **social-spending cuts** do **not** help.
xa: Skilling schemes: **PMKVY**, **DDU-GKY**, **RSETIs**; **PM Vishwakarma** for **18** artisan trades.
Inclusive growth also needs **rural development, agriculture, farm credit**.

nf168d07aa00.s: The Human Development Report primarily compares countries with reference to
o: Environment, defence expenditure and literacy alone
nf168d07aa00.x: The report compares countries on education, health and per-capita income as the principal dimensions of human development.
nf168d07aa00.tq: Identify the three broad dimensions rather than a related development indicator.
xs: The Human Development Report compares countries on **education, health and per-capita income** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2025 key).
These match the three HDI dimensions: **long and healthy life**, **education** and **decent standard of living**.
Exports, fiscal deficit, defence spending or tax revenue are not HDI dimensions.
xa: The HDR is published by **UNDP**; the first appeared in **1990**.
Income is measured as **GNI per capita (PPP $)**, using its **logarithm**.
HDI does not capture **inequality, poverty, human security, empowerment or environment**.

n320a2b1cab3.s: Which one of the following illustrates the role of policy choices in determining human development outcomes?
o: HDI is determined exclusively by GNI per capita
Malaysia has higher GNI per capita than Chile, but Chile has a higher HDI
Chile has higher GNI per capita and lower HDI than Malaysia
Both countries have identical life expectancy and schooling outcomes
n320a2b1cab3.x: Malaysia has higher GNI per capita, but Chile has a much higher HDI because of better life expectancy and schooling outcomes.
n320a2b1cab3.tq: Compare the income ranking with the HDI ranking instead of assuming that income alone determines development.
xs: **Malaysia has higher GNI per capita than Chile, but Chile has a higher HDI** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Chile has about **7 years** more life expectancy and **3 more years** of expected schooling, lifting its HDI.
Same income, different HDI shows the role of **national policy choices** (APPSC-G1 2024); HDI is not determined by GNI alone.
xa: Core idea: **GNI cannot replace HDI** — income is a **means, not the end**.
HDI = **geometric mean** of health, education and income indices, so a weak dimension is not offset by a strong one.
Life expectancy goalposts are **20–85 years**; expected schooling **0–18 years**.

nbb431327ea9.s: Who extended the capability approach by presenting a list of central human capabilities?
nbb431327ea9.x: Martha Nussbaum extended Sen's capability approach with a list of central human capabilities.
xa: **Mahbub ul Haq** conceived the HDI with **Amartya Sen**; **Inge Kaul** was also on the team.
Nussbaum's work is titled **Women and Human Development**.
The ultimate criteria of development are **people and their capabilities**.

nc45754c395c.s: Which one of the following is NOT a component indicator of the Human Development Index?
o: GNI per capita in PPP dollars
nc45754c395c.x: Environmental quality is not included in the HDI. The index uses life expectancy, schooling indicators and GNI per capita.
nc45754c395c.tq: Find the excluded environmental indicator among the three HDI dimensions.
xs: **Environmental quality** is not an HDI indicator — so option **(3)** is correct.
HDI indicators are **life expectancy at birth**, **expected** and **mean years of schooling**, and **GNI per capita (PPP $)**.
HDI ignores **environment** — hence the **Planetary pressures-adjusted HDI (PHDI)** introduced in **2020**.
xa: PHDI adjusts HDI for **CO2 emissions and material footprint**.
HDI also leaves out **inequality, poverty, human security, empowerment and participation**.
Income uses the **logarithm** of GNI per capita, goalposts **$100–$75,000**.

ndffc87f9f3d.s: Which one of the following is NOT captured by the HDI, although it is related to human development?
ndffc87f9f3d.x: HDI does not capture human security. It also does not directly capture inequality, poverty, empowerment, participation or the environment.
ndffc87f9f3d.tq: Separate the core index indicators from wider human-development concerns.
xs: **Human security** is not captured by the HDI — so option **(4)** is correct.
**GNI per capita**, **life expectancy** and **expected years of schooling** are all HDI indicators.
HDI also omits **inequality, poverty, empowerment, participation and environment**.
xa: HDI is criticised for ignoring **inequality, sustainability and gender** — hence **IHDI, GDI, GII and MPI**.
**MPI** (**2010**) measures **overlapping deprivations**.
**PHDI** (**2020**) adjusts HDI for **CO2 emissions and material footprint**.

neace0e93f0c.s: India's HDI value of 0.685 in HDR 2025 places it in which category?
neace0e93f0c.x: An HDI value from 0.550 to 0.699 falls in the medium human development category. India's 0.685 is just below the high-category threshold of 0.700.
neace0e93f0c.tq: Apply the category threshold to the given numerical value.
xs: India's **0.685** falls in **Medium human development** (**0.550–0.699**) — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2025 key).
It is just below the **0.700** threshold for **High**.
xa: ⚠ Older notes loosely say "Medium/High" — the correct answer is **Medium**.
Sub-national dataset gives a national average of **0.732** — use **0.685** for UNDP questions.
**Bihar** is the lowest state at **0.650**.

nde610fc1148.s: Which of the following best describes human capital formation?
o: Transfer of all public resources from agriculture to services
Investment in education, health, skills, migration and information that raises people's productive capacity
Accumulation of foreign exchange reserves through international trade
Investment in physical infrastructure alone to increase industrial output
nde610fc1148.x: Human capital formation includes investment in education, health, skills acquired through on-the-job training, migration and information, all of which enhance people's productive capacity.
nde610fc1148.tq: Identify the option that combines the complete components of the concept rather than a narrow definition.
xs: Human capital formation is **investment in education, health, skills, migration and information** that raises people's **productive capacity** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Physical infrastructure or forex reserves are not human capital.
xa: Skills include **on-the-job training**.
Returns: **higher productivity and earnings**, faster growth, **lower poverty**.
Poverty **35.1%** (no formal education) vs **14.9%** (post-secondary).

nindian-economy-69-13.s: In which year was the first Human Development Report published?
nindian-economy-69-13.x: The first Human Development Report came out in 1990, based on Mahbub-ul-Haq's human development approach.
n: Mahbub-ul-Haq developed the human development approach. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
Amartya Sen provided the intellectual foundation through the capability approach. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
The first Human Development Report was published in 1990. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
xa: The **HDR compares** education, health and per-capita income (APPSC-GS 2025 key).
**First state HDR**: **Madhya Pradesh** (**1995**); **first NHDR**: **2001**.
HDI formula = **geometric mean** of three dimension indices, introduced **2010**.

nindian-economy-69-15.s: The first Human Development Report was published by the:
nindian-economy-69-15.x: The UNDP published the first Human Development Report; OPHI works with the UNDP on the MPI.
n: Mahbub-ul-Haq developed the human development approach. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
Amartya Sen provided the intellectual foundation through the capability approach. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) publishes the Human Development Report. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
The MPI is associated with OPHI and UNDP. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
xa: The first HDR came out in **1990**; MPI first included in the HDR in **2010**.
**Martha Nussbaum** listed **central human capabilities**.
India's HDI **0.685** = **Medium** (APPSC-GS 2025 key).

nindian-economy-69-16.s: Which of the following is primarily an economic measure?
nindian-economy-69-16.x: GDP is mainly an economic measure; the HDI measures human development and the MPI multidimensional poverty.
n: GDP or per-capita income is primarily an economic measure. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
Human development is a broader, people-centred approach. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
The Human Development Index (HDI) measures human development. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) measures multidimensional poverty. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
xa: GDP focuses on **income and output**; human development on **capabilities and well-being**.
HDI income indicator = **GNI per capita (PPP $)**, using its logarithm.
⚠ Education index = **arithmetic** mean; HDI = **geometric** mean.

nc0db9ab0033.s: In the HDI, the minimum and maximum goalposts for life expectancy are:
nc0db9ab0033.x: Life expectancy goalposts are 20-85 years; 0-18 is for expected schooling and 0-15 for mean schooling.
xa: ⚠ Expected schooling max is **18**; mean schooling max is **15** — a common trap.
GNI per capita is in **2011 PPP $** and enters as a **logarithm**.
Education index = **arithmetic mean** of the two schooling sub-indices.

n7de8bba2a26.s: The education index in the HDI is obtained by taking the:
o: Geometric mean of life expectancy and income indices
Simple ratio of expected years to mean years of schooling
Arithmetic mean of the expected-years and mean-years schooling sub-indices
Weighted mean of GNI and schooling indices
n7de8bba2a26.x: The education index is the arithmetic mean of the indices for expected years of schooling and mean years of schooling.
n7de8bba2a26.tq: Identify the specific aggregation method used within the education dimension.
xs: The education index is the **arithmetic mean** of the **expected-years** and **mean-years** schooling sub-indices — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **geometric mean** is used for the overall HDI, not the education index.
No ratio of expected to mean years, and no GNI weighting, is involved.
xa: ⚠ Education index = **arithmetic** mean; HDI = **geometric** mean.
Goalposts: expected schooling **0–18**, mean schooling **0–15**.
Both schooling indicators came in with the **2010** revision, along with **GNI**.

nce2152e15e7.s: If the actual value of an HDI indicator is 50, with a minimum goalpost of 20 and a maximum goalpost of 80, the dimension index will be:
nce2152e15e7.x: The dimension index is calculated as (actual value − minimum value)/(maximum value − minimum value), which is (50−20)/(80−20) = 0.50.
nce2152e15e7.tq: Apply the normalized-index formula rather than recalling the formula mechanically.
xs: Dimension index = **(actual − min)/(max − min)** = (50 − 20)/(80 − 20) = **0.50** — so option **(2)** is correct.
0.40, 0.60 and 0.75 come from using the wrong numerator or denominator.
xa: Real life-expectancy goalposts are **20** and **85** years.
Education index = **arithmetic mean** of the two schooling indices; HDI = **geometric mean** of the three dimensions.
Worked example: **Georgia 0.769 = High** category.

nindian-economy-69-20.x: The MPI measures multidimensional poverty, while the HDI measures human development.
n: GDP or per-capita income is primarily an economic measure. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
The Human Development Index (HDI) measures human development. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) measures multidimensional poverty. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
The HDI considers health, education, and standard of living. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
The MPI considers health, education, and living standards. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
xa: HDI goalposts: life expectancy **20**-**85** years; expected schooling max **18**; mean schooling max **15**.
HDI categories: High **0.700-0.799**; Medium **0.550-0.699**.
⚠ **0.685** = UNDP India value; **0.732** = sub-national national average.

n598372164b9.s: Why is the logarithm of GNI per capita used in calculating the income index of the HDI?
o: To convert GNI into life expectancy
To give income a zero weight
To reflect diminishing returns to income
n598372164b9.x: The logarithm captures diminishing returns: an additional unit of income contributes less to human development at higher income levels.
n598372164b9.tq: Link the mathematical transformation with its economic rationale rather than treating it as a unit conversion.
xs: The **logarithm** of GNI per capita is used to reflect **diminishing returns** to income — so option **(4)** is correct.
Each extra dollar matters less for human development at higher incomes — **diminishing importance of income**.
Purchasing-power differences are handled by **PPP dollars**, not by the logarithm.
xa: Income goalposts: **$100** minimum, **$75,000** maximum (**2011 PPP $**).
HDI uses **GNI**, not GDP, per capita since the **2010** revision.
Indicator for **decent standard of living** = GNI per capita (PPP $).

nb69a09e3357.s: Since 2010, the HDI is calculated as the ____ of its three dimension indices.
nb69a09e3357.x: The geometric mean, introduced in 2010, prevents a strong dimension from fully offsetting a weak one.
xa: ⚠ Education index uses the **arithmetic** mean of its two sub-indices.
Worked example: **Georgia 0.769 = High** human development.
The **2010** revision also brought in **GNI** and the two schooling indicators.

n8304f553413.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI)?
o: It discounts the HDI for inequality.
The HDI-IHDI gap represents the loss due to inequality.
IHDI exceeds HDI whenever inequality exists.
n8304f553413.x: IHDI is lower, not higher, than HDI whenever inequality exists.
xa: With no inequality, **HDI = IHDI**.
HDI = **"potential"** human development; IHDI = **"actual"** human development.
**GII** and **MPI** also came in **2010**.

nba3417e8397.s: The Planetary pressures-adjusted HDI adjusts HDI for:
nba3417e8397.x: PHDI, introduced in 2020, adjusts HDI for planetary pressures represented by carbon dioxide emissions and material footprint.
nba3417e8397.tq: Match the environmental adjustment with the index carrying the planetary-pressures label.
xs: The **Planetary pressures-adjusted HDI (PHDI)** adjusts HDI for **CO2 emissions and material footprint** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was introduced in **2020**.
Gender inequality belongs to the **GII**, which covers reproductive health, empowerment and labour market.
xa: HDI by itself does not cover **environment** or sustainability.
**IHDI** discounts HDI for inequality; **GDI** is the female-to-male HDI ratio.
**MPI** (**2010**) measures overlapping deprivations.

nindian-economy-69-12.s: The Multidimensional Poverty Index is produced by:
nindian-economy-69-12.x: The MPI is produced by OPHI and UNDP together, not UNDP alone.
n: The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) measures multidimensional poverty. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
The MPI is associated with OPHI and UNDP. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #69 · pp 100-101]
xa: MPI was **first included** in the **Human Development Report** in **2010**.
MPI considers **health**, **education** and **living standards**.
**IHDI**, **GII** and MPI came in **2010**; **GDI** in **1995**.

n31e822adc44.s: The lower threshold of the 'medium' HDI category is:
n31e822adc44.x: Very high is 0.800+, high 0.700-0.799, medium 0.550-0.699 and low below 0.550.
xa: Worked example: **Georgia 0.769 = High**.
**Goa** and **Kerala** are above **0.86** in the state series.
**Assam 0.699** (24th of 29), **West Bengal 0.719**.

ne39da2179b9.s: In HDR 2025, which of the five original BRICS countries ranked lowest?
ne39da2179b9.x: Brazil, Russia, China and South Africa all ranked above India in HDR 2025.
xa: India's HDI value **0.685** puts it in the **Medium** category.
Comparative: India **149th** by nominal GDP per capita and **119th** by PPP in **2026**.

nd6db7566e0b.s: According to the Human Development Report 2023–24, based on HDI values for 2022, India was ranked:
nd6db7566e0b.x: India was ranked 134th among 193 countries in the HDR 2023–24, based on HDI values for 2022.
nd6db7566e0b.tq: Distinguish the report edition, reference year and total number of countries before selecting the rank.
xs: In **HDR 2023-24** (HDI values for **2022**), India ranked **134th out of 193 countries** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2024 key).
**124th**, **130th** and **139th** are distractors; the key figure is **134th**.
xa: India's HDI value **0.685** = **Medium** category.
In **HDR 2025**, **Sri Lanka** and **Maldives** were above India.
India is lowest among the five original **BRICS**.

n7aec3065d9f.s: Under the updated Rangarajan estimates (HCES 2022-23), rural poverty was highest in Chhattisgarh at:
n7aec3065d9f.x: Rural poverty was highest in Chhattisgarh (25.1%) and lowest in Himachal Pradesh (0.4%); urban poverty was lowest in Tamil Nadu (1.9%).
xa: These come from the **RBI's update of the Rangarajan line** on **HCES 2022-23** (Oct 2025).
The government now leans on **MPI** over income poverty lines.
Planning Commission **2011-12**: AP income poverty **9.20%** vs India **21.92%**.

nfd7dea66524.s: Which State is noted as moving to extreme-poverty-free status?
nfd7dea66524.x: Kerala is moving to extreme-poverty-free status, a current development in poverty debates.
nfd7dea66524.tq: Kerala: first in elderly welfare, now extreme-poverty-free.
xs: **Kerala** is moving to **extreme-poverty-free** status — so option **(4)** is correct.
Kerala also **consistently tops** state HDI (the **"Kerala Model"**).
xa: **Goa and Kerala** are above **0.86** in the state HDI series.
**Himachal** has the lowest rural poverty (**0.4%**); **Tamil Nadu** the lowest urban (**1.9%**).
**Bihar** is lowest on HDI at **0.650**.

nea2a3853898.s: The 'Kerala Model' refers to Kerala's position as the State that:
o: Consistently tops Indian States in human development
First published a Human Development Report
Has the lowest HDI in India
nea2a3853898.x: Kerala consistently tops Indian States in human development and is associated with the Kerala Model; Madhya Pradesh was the first State to publish an HDR.
xa: **Goa and Kerala** are above **0.86**; Kerala is **2nd** in the state series.
Kerala is moving to **extreme-poverty-free** status.
**Bihar** is lowest at **0.650**.

n60eebc1349d.s: Which group of States is identified as occupying the lowest end of the State human-development ranking?
o: Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh
West Bengal, Gujarat and Tamil Nadu
n60eebc1349d.x: Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh are identified among the lowest-ranking States in human development.
n60eebc1349d.tq: Recall the low-performing group rather than the consistently high-performing States.
xs: **Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh** are at the lowest end of state HDI — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bihar** is lowest at **0.650** vs India's **0.685** (**2023**).
**Kerala** and **Goa** are at the top, above **0.86**.
xa: **Assam 0.699** (24th of 29); **West Bengal 0.719**.
Sub-national national average: **0.732** (2023).
⚠ **0.685** = UNDP India value; **0.732** = sub-national average.

nd9ff24d1f79.s: The first State Human Development Report in India was prepared by:
nd9ff24d1f79.x: Madhya Pradesh had the distinction of producing the first State Human Development Report in 1995.
nd9ff24d1f79.tq: Distinguish the first state-level report from the first national report.
xs: **Madhya Pradesh** prepared India's **first State HDR** in **1995** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**2001** is the first **NHDR**; **2011** the second NHDR; **1990** the first global HDR by UNDP.
xa: **Kerala** consistently tops state HDI ("Kerala Model").
**Bihar** is lowest at **0.650**.
⚠ **1995** is also the year the **GDI** was introduced in the HDR.

n0c54ef83bfc.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the income-poverty percentages for Andhra Pradesh and India in 2011–12?
n0c54ef83bfc.x: In 2011–12, income poverty was 9.20% in Andhra Pradesh and 21.92% for India.
n0c54ef83bfc.tq: Match each percentage with the correct State or national figure and avoid reversing the comparison.
xs: Income poverty in **2011-12** (Planning Commission): **AP 9.20%**, **India 21.92%** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**6.06%** and **14.96%** are the MPI headcount ratios of AP and India, not income poverty.
xa: AP income poverty: rural **10.96%**, urban **5.81%**.
The government now leans on **MPI** over income poverty lines.
RBI Rangarajan-line update: rural poverty lowest in **Himachal (0.4%)**, highest in **Chhattisgarh (25.1%)**.

n2cfd680a698.s: Andhra Pradesh's multidimensional poverty headcount ratio reported for 2024-25 was:
n2cfd680a698.x: AP's headcount ratio was 6.06% (MPI 0.025), under half the national ratio of 14.96%.
xa: Rural headcount: AP **7.71%** vs India **19.28%**; urban AP **2.20%** vs India **5.27%**.
Intensity: AP **41.12%** vs India **44.39%**.
Data source: **NITI MPI 2023**, **NFHS-5**.

nb9bffb7a514.s: Which Five Year Plan carried the theme 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth'?
nb9bffb7a514.x: The Eleventh Plan (2007-12), the first to make inclusive growth its objective, carried this theme.
xa: Instruments: **SHGs** (women's credit), **MSMEs** (labour-intensive jobs), financial inclusion, **DBT**.
RBI FI-Index rose to **67.0** in 2025 from **53.9** in 2021.
Gini fell from **36.8** to **32.1**.

na32dc3863f7.s: The Human Poverty Index (HDR 1997) measured deprivation in:
o: Longevity, knowledge and a decent standard of living
na32dc3863f7.x: The HPI measured deprivation in longevity, knowledge and a decent standard of living, to complement the HDI.
xa: HPI was **replaced by the MPI** in **HDR 2010**.
HPI **indicates the standard of living** (APPSC-GS 2018 key).
⚠ Sequence: **1995 GDI/GEM – 1996 CPM – 1997 HPI – 2010 MPI/GII/IHDI**.

naf3a9f6d3cb.s: When inequality exists, a country's IHDI is:
naf3a9f6d3cb.x: The IHDI discounts HDI achievement for unequal distribution, so it is lower than the HDI whenever inequality exists.
xa: **HDI − IHDI** = **loss from inequality**, in %.
The **GII** is built on the **IHDI framework**.
IHDI was introduced in **2010**.

n512934483e6.s: A Gender Development Index value of 1 indicates
n512934483e6.x: A GDI value of 1 represents gender parity in the measured dimensions of health, education and earned income.
n512934483e6.tq: Distinguish the parity value of GDI from the direction of GII.
xs: A **GDI value of 1** means **gender parity** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ Notes describing "0 = equal to 1 = worst" are describing the **GII**, not the GDI.
xa: Countries are placed in **5 groups** by distance from parity.
GDI was introduced in **HDR 1995**.
**Higher GII = greater inequality**.

ndf9f898d5ce.s: The Gender Inequality Index (GII) was introduced in the Human Development Report of:
ndf9f898d5ce.x: The GII came in HDR 2010 to address shortcomings of the GDI; a higher GII means more inequality.
xa: GII dimensions: **reproductive health, empowerment, labour market**.
GII is built on the **IHDI framework**.
GDI groups countries into **5 groups** by distance from parity.

ne9a77060fc6.s: Under the Alkire-Foster method used for the Multidimensional Poverty Index, the MPI value is obtained as:
o: Headcount ratio multiplied by the intensity of poverty
Headcount ratio plus the intensity of poverty
Geometric mean of three normalised dimension indices
Share of population living below one dollar a day
ne9a77060fc6.x: MPI = headcount ratio (H) x intensity (A), which is why values are small (e.g. India 0.066). Adding the two is wrong; the geometric mean of dimension indices is how the HDI is computed; and the MPI is not a $1-a-day income measure (the UPPSC 2025 trap).
xs: Under **Alkire-Foster**, MPI = **headcount ratio multiplied by the intensity of poverty** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **geometric mean** of three dimension indices is the HDI's formula; MPI is not a $1-a-day measure.
xa: This product explains small values like **0.069** (exam traps 0.690, 0.096).
National MPI 2023: headcount **14.96%** × intensity **44.39%** → MPI **0.066**.
MPI-poor = deprived in at least **one-third** of weighted indicators.

nf6e5527b571.s: Which one of the following is NOT an indicator of the Capability Poverty Measure?
o: Births unattended by trained health personnel
Children under five who are underweight
nf6e5527b571.x: Male labour-force participation is not a CPM indicator. The CPM uses child underweight, unattended births and female illiteracy.
nf6e5527b571.tq: Find the indicator outside the three-item CPM set.
xs: **Male labour-force participation** is not a CPM indicator — so option **(2)** is correct.
CPM's three indicators are **underweight children under 5**, **births unattended by trained health personnel** and **female illiteracy**.
Female and male labour force participation belongs to the **GII's labour-market** dimension.
xa: CPM was introduced in **HDR 1996**.
**BPSC 2025 key**: child malnutrition + female illiteracy both included.
HPI (**1997**) measured deprivation in longevity, knowledge and standard of living.

n63ea4e795f3.s: India's National MPI uses how many indicators?
n63ea4e795f3.x: The National MPI uses 12 indicators against the Global MPI's 10, with the same three dimensions and the Alkire-Foster method.
xa: National additions: **maternal health** and **bank accounts**.
National MPI has **3 equally weighted dimensions** and **SDG-aligned** indicators.
National MPI estimated by **NITI Aayog** (APPSC-G2 2025 key).
