n27a1db3411e.s: How many indicators does the standard of living dimension of India's National MPI have?
n27a1db3411e.x: Health has three indicators, education two and standard of living seven.
xa: Health: **nutrition**, **child and adolescent mortality**, **maternal health**.
Education: **years of schooling**, **school attendance**.
India's additions over the Global MPI: **maternal health** and **bank accounts**.

ndaffdc96ab7.s: The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index is associated with which institutions?
o: NITI Aayog and the Finance Commission
ndaffdc96ab7.x: The Global MPI is associated with the United Nations Development Programme and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative.
ndaffdc96ab7.tq: Apply the report–institution matching method to distinguish global and national producers.
xs: The Global MPI is published by **UNDP and OPHI** (Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**NITI Aayog** estimates the **National** MPI, with UNDP and OPHI.
xa: Global MPI dates from **2010**; it uses the **Alkire-Foster** method.
It was proposed by **Alkire and Santos (2010)**.
Global MPI has **10** indicators; National MPI **12**.

nb10f1346363.s: India's National Multidimensional Poverty Index is estimated by:
o: NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI
nb10f1346363.x: India's National MPI is estimated by NITI Aayog in association with UNDP and OPHI.
xa: It uses the same **Alkire-Foster** method as the Global MPI.
**12** indicators — adds **maternal health** and **bank account**.
Monitored under the **Global Indices for Reforms and Growth (GIRG)**.

ne32a1401133.s: Which of the following is a standard-of-living indicator in India’s National MPI?
ne32a1401133.x: Standard-of-living indicators include cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets and bank accounts.
ne32a1401133.tq: Classify the indicator under the correct MPI dimension.
xs: **Bank accounts** is a standard-of-living indicator in the National MPI — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is one of India's two **national additions**, with **maternal health**.
Birth rate and labour force participation are not National MPI indicators.
xa: Standard of living has **7** indicators; health **3**; education **2**.
Global living-standard indicators: **electricity, drinking water, sanitation, housing, cooking fuel, assets**.

n7ad01d13ed3.s: As reported in the Global MPI 2022, how many people moved out of multidimensional poverty in India between 2005–06 and 2019–21?
n7ad01d13ed3.x: The Global MPI 2022 reported that 414 million people moved out of multidimensional poverty in India between 2005–06 and 2019–21.
n7ad01d13ed3.tq: Number recall with close numerical distractors.
xs: **Global MPI 2022**: **414 million** (**41.4 crore**) moved out of poverty, 2005-06 to 2019-21 — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2022 key).
**271 million** is the **Global MPI 2018** figure (2005-06 to 2015-16).
xa: Headcount fell from **55.1%** to **16.4%**; about **234 million** still poor.

n4a77969fc34.s: As per the Global MPI 2022, India's MPI value (for 2019-21) was:
n4a77969fc34.x: India's value was 0.069. 0.690 and 0.096 are misplaced-digit traps - the value is small because MPI = headcount x intensity. 0.061 is India's value in the Global MPI 2025 data, down from 0.064 in 2024.
xs: India's MPI value in **Global MPI 2022** (2019-21) was **0.069** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**0.690** and **0.096** are misplaced-digit traps; MPI is small because it is **headcount × intensity**.
**0.061** is the **Global MPI 2025** value.
xa: Headcount **16.4%** (~**234 million** poor) in 2019-21.
**414 million** moved out of poverty from 2005-06.
National MPI value for 2019-21: **0.066**.

n21d4f2ea27f.s: The Global MPI 2018 reported that, between 2005-06 and 2015-16, about ______ people in India moved out of multidimensional poverty, with ______ as the poorest State.
n21d4f2ea27f.x: The 2018 Global MPI reported 271 million moving out between 2005-06 and 2015-16, with Bihar the poorest State. 414 million is the Global MPI 2022 figure for 2005-06 to 2019-21; Kerala is the least poor State; and about 234 million is the number still poor in 2019-21, not those who exited.
xs: **Global MPI 2018**: **271 million** moved out of poverty (2005-06 to 2015-16), with **Bihar** the poorest state — so option **(1)** is correct.
**414 million** is the **2022** edition figure; **234 million** were still poor in 2019-21; **Kerala** is the least poor.
xa: ⚠ **271 million** (2018 edition) vs **414 million** (2022 edition).
**Bihar 0.16** (28th) remains highest MPI in 2019-21.
**Kerala 0.002** has the lowest MPI.

n4c90f289dd2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about NITI Aayog's January 2024 discussion paper on multidimensional poverty?
o: The headcount ratio fell from 29.17% to 11.28%.
About 24.82 crore people escaped multidimensional poverty.
It covered the nine years from 2013-14 to 2022-23.
n4c90f289dd2.x: The paper covered 2013-14 to 2022-23; 2015-16 to 2019-21 is the period of the Progress Review 2023.
xa: **UP** had the largest fall (**5.94 crore**).
The fall was **17.89** points.

n442ba43d2e4.s: Which pair of researchers is associated with the proposal of the Multidimensional Poverty Index in 2010?
o: Sabina Alkire and Maria Emma Santos
Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen
n442ba43d2e4.x: The MPI was proposed by Sabina Alkire and Maria Emma Santos in 2010.
n442ba43d2e4.tq: Name-pair recall with nearby poverty-measure scholars as distractors.
xs: The MPI was proposed by **Sabina Alkire and Maria Emma Santos** in **2010** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Alkire-Foster** is the name of the **method**, not of the proposers.
**Mahbub ul Haq** and **Amartya Sen** are linked to the HDI.
xa: Global MPI is published by **UNDP and OPHI**.
It **replaced the HPI** in **HDR 2010**.
National MPI is estimated by **NITI Aayog**.

nf26d27bfe2b.s: Which State recorded the largest fall in multidimensional poverty, amounting to 5.94 crore persons, according to the NITI Aayog discussion paper of January 2024?
nf26d27bfe2b.x: Uttar Pradesh recorded the largest fall, with 5.94 crore persons moving out of multidimensional poverty.
nf26d27bfe2b.tq: Match the state with the specific absolute reduction rather than with its MPI value.
xs: **Uttar Pradesh** had the largest fall in number of poor — **5.94 crore** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Others: **Bihar 3.77 crore**, **MP 2.30 crore**, **Rajasthan 1.87 crore**.
xa: NITI Discussion Paper (**Jan 2024**): **24.82 crore** exited in 9 years.
**Kerala** has the lowest MPI (**0.002**).

n17a9155d479.s: In the MPI ranking cited, Andhra Pradesh was ranked:
n17a9155d479.x: AP ranked ninth by MPI; among cited States Kerala had the lowest value (0.002) and Bihar the highest (0.16).
xa: Other low MPI: **Goa 0.003**, **Tamil Nadu 0.009**.
Other high MPI: **Meghalaya 0.133**, **Jharkhand 0.131**, **UP 0.103**.
AP headcount **6.06%** vs India **14.96%**.

ndc1155c3b1b.s: The Global Innovation Index is published by WIPO in association with
ndc1155c3b1b.x: WIPO co-publishes the Global Innovation Index with Cornell University and INSEAD; this association dates from 2007.
ndc1155c3b1b.tq: Use the co-publisher pair to distinguish the innovation index from other global indices.
xs: **WIPO** co-publishes the Global Innovation Index with **Cornell and INSEAD**, since **2007** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Yale/Columbia**, **Gallup/UN SDSN** and **FAO/World Bank** are not its co-publishers.
xa: WIPO: est. **1967**, UN agency in **Geneva**, **193** members.
GII has **7 pillars** = **5 input** + **2 output**.
Output pillars: **knowledge and technology outputs**, **creative outputs**.

n801b7d4870a.s: The successor to the World Bank's Doing Business report is
n801b7d4870a.x: B-READY is the successor to the discontinued Doing Business report.
n801b7d4870a.tq: Discriminate between the former index and its officially named successor.
xs: The World Bank's **B-READY** is the successor to Doing Business — so option **(1)** is correct.
The other names are not the successor named in the notes.
xa: **DPIIT** is the nodal agency.
India is in the **3rd report**, expected around **Sep 2026**.
Allied index: **IMD World Competitiveness** rank **43 (2021) → 41 (2025)**.

nindian-economy-63-5.s: The Global Gender Gap Report is published by the:
nindian-economy-63-5.x: The WEF publishes the Global Gender Gap Report; the World Bank publishes the World Development Report.
n: The World Bank publishes the World Development Report. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 92-93]
The World Bank published the Ease of Doing Business Report or Index. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 92-93]
Global Competitiveness Report or Index is published by the World Economic Forum (WEF). [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 92-93]
Global Gender Gap Report or Index is published by the World Economic Forum (WEF). [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 92-93]
xa: ⚠ The Ease of Doing Business report **has been discontinued**; successor = World Bank **B-READY**.
WEF also publishes the **Travel & Tourism Competitiveness Report**.
**Global Hunger Index** = **Concern Worldwide** + **Welthungerhilfe**.

nindian-economy-63-17.s: Which report/index is specifically identified as discontinued?
nindian-economy-63-17.x: The World Bank stopped the Ease of Doing Business report in 2021 after problems with its data. The HDR, GFSR and WDR still come out.
n: The Ease of Doing Business Report or Index has been discontinued. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 92-93]
xs: The **Ease of Doing Business Report/Index** (World Bank) **has been discontinued** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **HDR** (UNDP), **GFSR** (IMF) and **WDR** (World Bank) are not marked as discontinued.
xa: Successor: World Bank **B-READY**; **DPIIT** is the nodal body.
India's DB rank moved **142 → 63** over five years; **77/190** in DB 2019.
India's weakest indicators: **paying taxes** and **enforcing contracts** (**163/190**).

nindian-economy-63-19.s: The State of World Population Report is published by:
nindian-economy-63-19.x: UNFPA publishes the State of World Population; the IMF publishes the WEO and the ILO the World Social Protection Report.
n: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) publishes the World Economic Outlook. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 92-93]
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) publishes the Capability Poverty Measure. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 92-93]
The International Labour Organization (ILO) publishes the World Social Protection Report. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 92-93]
The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) publishes the State of World Population Report. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 92-93]
xa: The **HDR** and **HDI** are also **UNDP** publications.
**Global Wage Report** is also an **ILO** report.
**AOI**: ⚠ **Trap:** "published by IFPRI" is wrong (APPSC-G1 2022).

nindian-economy-63-16.s: Which of the following is NOT published by the UNDP?
nindian-economy-63-16.x: The Global Gender Gap Report is the WEF's; the other three are UNDP measures.
n: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) publishes the Human Development Report. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 92-93]
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) publishes the Human Development Index. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 92-93]
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) publishes the Capability Poverty Measure. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 92-93]
Global Gender Gap Report or Index is published by the World Economic Forum (WEF). [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 92-93]
xa: WEF also publishes the **Global Competitiveness Report**.
**WHR** uses six variables incl. **GDP per capita**, **social support**, **healthy life expectancy**.
⚠ GHI **4** indicators – WHR **6** variables – GII **7** pillars.

ndb80712720e.s: The Global Hunger Index is measured on a scale of 0 to 100 in which a higher score indicates
o: greater hunger severity or worse outcomes
ndb80712720e.x: The Global Hunger Index uses a 0–100 scale, and a higher score indicates worse hunger conditions.
ndb80712720e.tq: Check the direction of the scale before interpreting the score.
xs: On the GHI's **0-100** scale, a **higher score = worse** hunger — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is not a measure of food exports or farm productivity.
xa: GHI's **4** indicators: **undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting, child mortality**.
Publishers: **Concern Worldwide** and **Welthungerhilfe**.
GoI view: **3 of the 4** indicators cover only children.

n6dbfbb6b50d.s: One of India's objections to the EPI methodology was its preference for ____ emissions over per-capita emissions.
n6dbfbb6b50d.x: India objected to the preference for absolute over per-capita emissions, the neglect of CBDR-RC and the use of contested indicators.
xa: MoEFCC rejected the EPI methodology in **2022**.
**50% non-fossil** installed capacity in **2025** — five years before the **2030** NDC target.
EPI 2026 sub-ranks: **Air Quality 175th**, **Climate Mitigation 130th**.

nb25018b75b4.s: Which one of the following is NOT an indicator used in the Global Hunger Index?
nb25018b75b4.x: The GHI uses undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality; maternal mortality is not one of its four indicators.
nb25018b75b4.tq: Find the outsider by recalling the complete four-indicator list.
xs: **Maternal mortality** is not a GHI indicator — so option **(4)** is correct.
GHI's four: **undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting, child mortality**.
Maternal mortality ratio is a **Gender Inequality Index** indicator (reproductive health).
xa: ⚠ An older UPSC note lists only **three** indicators.
⚠ GHI **4** indicators – WHR **6** variables – GII **7** pillars.
GHI scale **0-100**, higher = worse.

n3f08ea3d363.s: How many input pillars does the Global Innovation Index have?
n3f08ea3d363.x: The GII has five input pillars and two output pillars (knowledge and technology outputs, and creative outputs).
xa: Input pillars: **institutions, human capital and research, infrastructure, market sophistication, business sophistication**.
Published by **WIPO** with **Cornell and INSEAD**.

ne8410619fc9.s: Which of the following is one of the six variables used in the World Happiness Report?
ne8410619fc9.x: The six variables are GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity and perceptions of corruption.
xa: ⚠ GHI **4** indicators – WHR **6** variables – GII **7** pillars.
Criticism: **perception surveys** may disadvantage populous developing countries.

nee6ff96dc11.s: In the Environmental Performance Index 2026, India's overall rank out of 177 countries was:
nee6ff96dc11.x: India ranked 176th of 177 overall, 175th in Air Quality and 130th in Climate Mitigation.
xa: EPI 2026 has **47 indicators**.
MoEFCC **rejected the EPI methodology in 2022**.
Counter-evidence: **23rd in CCPI 2026**; **50% non-fossil** capacity in 2025.

nda83d4a3325.s: The Global Hunger Index is based on undernourishment, child stunting, child mortality and:
nda83d4a3325.x: The four GHI indicators are undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality.
xa: India also objects that the **undernourishment** figure comes from a **small opinion-poll-type sample**.
The same objections apply to **FAO SOFI** indicators.
**Absorption/utilisation** (the body's ability to use food) is the dimension child stunting/wasting reflect.

n5408a0267cd.s: India's rank in the Doing Business 2019 report, released in 2018, was
n5408a0267cd.x: India ranked 77th among 190 economies in the Doing Business 2019 report released in 2018.
n5408a0267cd.tq: Match the report year with the release year rather than confusing it with the data year.
xs: In **DB 2019** (released **2018**), India ranked **77 out of 190** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2019 key).
xa: Rank moved **142 → 63** over five years.
India lagged in **paying taxes**; **enforcing contracts** **163/190**.
Successor: World Bank **B-READY**.

n147eca8ccbe.s: In which of the following areas did India lag in the Ease of Doing Business assessment?
n147eca8ccbe.x: India was specifically noted as lagging in paying taxes.
n147eca8ccbe.tq: Test the identified weak sub-index directly against neighbouring parameters.
xs: India lagged in **paying taxes** — the weakest cited indicator — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2019 key).
The other options add "only", which the notes do not support.
xa: **Enforcing contracts**: **163/190**.
DB 2020: **enforcing contracts** and **registering property** remained the worst.

n423e299a4c2.s: The Ease of Doing Business report served primarily as a ready reckoner for
n423e299a4c2.x: The report functioned as a ready reckoner for foreign investors by comparing business regulations across economies.
n423e299a4c2.tq: Link the index's practical purpose with its principal user group.
xs: The Doing Business report served as a ready reckoner for **foreign investors** — so option **(4)** is correct (APPSC 2019 key).
It compared business regulation for investment decisions — not for employees, tourists or farmers.
xa: Published by the **World Bank**; succeeded by **B-READY**.
What counts: **Single Window System**; not per-capita income, inflation, literacy.
India's rank: **142 → 63**.

n68ab47988a6.s: Which one of the following was counted in the World Bank's Ease of Doing Business assessment?
n68ab47988a6.x: A Single Window System for business clearances counts towards Ease of Doing Business. Per capita income, inflation and literacy are macro or social indicators that the assessment does not count (APPSC 2019).
n68ab47988a6.tq: EoDB measures business regulation, not macro or social outcomes.
xs: A **Single Window System** counts in Ease of Doing Business — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2019).
**Per-capita income, inflation and literacy** do NOT count.
xa: Report purpose: a ready reckoner for **foreign investors**.
India lagged in **paying taxes**; **enforcing contracts 163/190**.

n69e109bcad1.s: The Government of India criticised the Global Hunger Index methodology primarily because
o: three of its four indicators cover only children and undernourishment relies on a small opinion-poll survey
all its indicators measure only agricultural exports
it uses only official census data from India
n69e109bcad1.x: The Government of India argued that three of the four indicators concern only children and that the undernourishment measure rests on an opinion poll of about 3,000 respondents.
n69e109bcad1.tq: Identify the specific methodological objections instead of accepting an absolute statement about all indicators.
xs: GoI called the GHI flawed because **3 of the 4 indicators cover only children** and undernourishment rests on a **small opinion-poll survey** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The poll had about **3,000** respondents.
GHI does include **child mortality**, so option (4) is false.
xa: GHI indicators: **undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting, child mortality**.
MoEFCC separately **rejected the EPI methodology in 2022**.
Criticism: **perception surveys** disadvantage populous developing countries.

nff87a1a5d04.s: The ability of the environment to absorb degradation and neutralise pollutants without harm is called its:
nff87a1a5d04.x: Absorptive capacity is the ability of the environment to absorb degradation, i.e. the maximum pollutant load an ecosystem can process and neutralise without harm.
xa: Crisis: **waste > absorptive capacity** and **extraction > regeneration**.
**Resource depletion** = use **faster than regeneration**.
The environment's waste function: **absorbs and neutralises wastes**.

o: The rate of resource use is equal to its regeneration in every season
A forest is managed sustainably while biodiversity is retained
Resources are used faster than they can regenerate
The rate of resource use is slower than its regeneration
neb89e73458a.x: Resource depletion occurs when resources are used faster than their rate of regeneration. Sustainable forest management with retained biodiversity does not represent depletion.
neb89e73458a.tq: Translate the scenario into the rate comparison between extraction and regeneration.
xs: **Resource depletion** = resources **used faster than they can regenerate** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2024 key).
A forest managed sustainably with biodiversity retained is **not** depletion; use equal to or below regeneration is sustainable.
xa: Groundwater depletion: **deep bore tubewells**; topsoil: **brick production**.
Crisis: **extraction > regeneration** + **waste > absorptive capacity**.

na021480a3af.s: The 'grow first, clean up later' argument about growth and environmental protection reflects the:
na021480a3af.x: The trade-off view holds that environmental rules can slow growth, so countries should grow first and clean up later (Environmental Kuznets Curve logic).
xa: Protection is an **investment for long-term prosperity**.
The **poor** bear most of the cost.
World Bank (**2013**): cost ≈ **5.7% of GDP**.

n92a692f8615.s: Which Indian State was the first to adopt green GDP in the form of Gross Environment Product (GEP)?
n92a692f8615.x: Uttarakhand was the first Indian State to adopt green GDP in the form of Gross Environment Product.
n92a692f8615.tq: Test the state-level first-mover fact against plausible state alternatives.
xs: **Uttarakhand** was the first state to adopt green GDP, as its **Gross Environment Product (GEP)** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**GEP** is Uttarakhand's **state-level green GDP**.
xa: **Green GDP** = conventional GDP net of **natural-resource depletion** and degradation costs.
Other FIRSTs: **EIA** first used **1978**; **Telangana** first in land restoration (**4.18** Mha).
**Sir Partha Dasgupta** chaired the Expert Group on Green National Accounts.

n201f4a28ff0.s: Green GDP is best described as:
o: Conventional GDP adjusted for resource depletion and environmental degradation
GDP excluding the contribution of the services sector
GDP adjusted only for changes in the price level
GDP calculated only from renewable-energy industries
n201f4a28ff0.x: Green GDP adjusts conventional GDP for environmental consequences, particularly resource depletion and environmental degradation.
n201f4a28ff0.tq: Distinguish environmental adjustment from sectoral or price adjustment.
xs: **Green GDP** = **conventional GDP adjusted for resource depletion and environmental degradation** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is not a price-level adjustment or a services/renewables-only measure.
xa: **Uttarakhand**'s state version is the **Gross Environment Product (GEP)**.
Criticism: **GDP ignores depletion**, so growth can hide loss of natural capital.
**Partha Dasgupta** Expert Group on Green National Accounts (**2011**).

n0c1676e9bad.s: The concept of a green economy primarily focuses on
o: fostering green industries and creating green jobs
maximising GDP growth irrespective of resource use
expanding fossil-fuel subsidies to reduce poverty
n0c1676e9bad.x: A green economy fosters green industries and green jobs that preserve or restore environmental quality while decoupling development from resource use and pollution (APPSC-GS 2025 key). Growth at any cost and fossil-fuel subsidies run against it, and it does not ban industry.
n0c1676e9bad.tq: Green economy = green industries + green jobs + decoupling.
xs: A green economy focuses on **fostering green industries and creating green jobs** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2025 key).
It **decouples** development from resource use, so growth at any cost or fossil-fuel subsidies run against it; it does not ban industry.
xa: **Green jobs** preserve or restore environmental quality.
It reduces **environmental risks and ecological scarcities**.

n7d9e02c8334.s: Why can conventional GDP growth conceal environmental degradation?
o: GDP directly deducts the depletion of natural capital from output
GDP excludes all healthcare and productivity-related expenditure
GDP ignores depletion of natural resources, allowing growth to hide the loss of natural capital
GDP measures only biodiversity and ecosystem services
n7d9e02c8334.x: Conventional GDP does not account for the depletion of natural resources; consequently, recorded growth can coexist with a loss of natural capital.
n7d9e02c8334.tq: Apply the distinction between aggregate output and natural-capital accounting.
xs: **GDP ignores depletion of natural resources**, so growth can **hide the loss of natural capital** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (1) is false — conventional GDP does not deduct depletion; that is what **Green GDP** does.
xa: **Green GDP** = GDP net of natural-resource depletion and degradation costs.
**Uttarakhand** adopted green GDP as **GEP**.
MoSPI's **SEEA** accounts track natural assets **since 2018**.

ndae06e6d7ac.s: Green Revolution HYV crops contributed to the depletion of the water table mainly because of their:
ndae06e6d7ac.x: The irrigation needs of HYV crops depleted the water table, while monoculture and chemicals hurt soil fertility and biodiversity.
xa: **Urea** is about **56%** of fertiliser use; overuse degrades soil and water.
Low-carbon alternative: **green urea** (green hydrogen + captured CO2).
**Chemical-intensive farming** is a human-driven cause of degradation.

n9ee2e4de6cc.s: Under the AP Common Zoning Regulations 2026, which of the following groups is identified as development-restricted?
o: Forests, hills, water bodies, eco-sensitive areas and CRZ
Agricultural fields, industrial zones, towns and highways
Only coastal settlements and irrigation canals
n9ee2e4de6cc.x: Forests, hills, water bodies, eco-sensitive areas and Coastal Regulation Zone areas are development-restricted under the regulations.
n9ee2e4de6cc.tq: Find the complete restricted-category list and reject options that omit or replace categories.
xs: **Forests, hills, water bodies, eco-sensitive areas and CRZ** are development-restricted — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (4) lists only part of the group.
xa: The regulations set **nine** land-use categories.
AP has **638** green building projects.

n1c8e468e20f.s: Which of the following is NOT a human-driven cause of environmental degradation?
o: Expansion of roads and urban areas
n1c8e468e20f.x: Wildlife conservation is a conservation practice, not a human-driven cause of environmental degradation. Groundwater over-extraction, industrial emissions and urban expansion are causes.
n1c8e468e20f.tq: Find the conservation measure hidden among the listed degradation causes.
xs: **Wildlife conservation** is a conservation practice, not a cause of degradation — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2024 options).
**Road and urban expansion**, **industrial emissions** and **groundwater over-extraction** are human-driven causes.
xa: ⚠ Odd ones out: **sustainable agriculture, renewable energy production, wildlife conservation**.
Other causes: **deforestation** (APPSC-GS 2024 key), chemical-intensive farming, **dams**, **overfishing**.

n66da52569b0.s: Which pair correctly represents the two environmental threats faced by India?
o: Poverty-induced degradation and pollution from affluence and rapid industrial growth
Rural literacy and excessive renewable energy production
Only natural disasters and seasonal rainfall variation
n66da52569b0.x: India faces poverty-induced degradation as well as pollution associated with affluence and rapid industrial growth.
n66da52569b0.tq: Distinguish the dual-source formulation from single-cause and unrelated alternatives.
xs: India faces **poverty-induced degradation** and **pollution from affluence and rapid industrial growth** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Both coexist: degradation from **poverty** and pollution from **affluence and rapid industrial growth**.
xa: The **poor** (slums, flood-prone areas) bear most of the cost.
World Bank (**2013**): degradation costs about **5.7% of GDP**.
Main reasons for India's low EPI: **urban particulate pollution + coal-based power**.

nad2b3a93b62.s: Which organisation compiles India’s environment accounts in accordance with the UN System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA)?
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
nad2b3a93b62.x: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation compiles environment accounts based on SEEA and has released ecosystem and natural-asset accounts since 2018.
nad2b3a93b62.tq: Ask ‘which body performs this function?’ to avoid swapping ministries and institutions.
xs: **MoSPI (Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation)** compiles environment accounts on **SEEA** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It has released ecosystem and natural-asset accounts **since 2018**.
xa: SEEA Central Framework adopted by the UN Statistical Commission in **2012**.
MoSPI also publishes **EnviStats India** (annual), based on **FDES 2013**.

n7e5487032af.s: Environmental Impact Assessment was first used in India in 1978 for:
n7e5487032af.x: EIA began in 1978 with river valley projects; the EIA Notification came in 1994 and was revised in 2006.
xa: **Green Credit Rules 2023** come under the **EP Act 1986**.
**Sovereign Green Bonds** are a green financing tool.

n2433cfb7261.s: The Green Credit Rules, 2023 were framed under which legislation?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
n2433cfb7261.x: The Green Credit Rules, 2023 were framed under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
n2433cfb7261.tq: Use the ‘under the Act’ relationship and avoid confusing neighbouring environmental statutes.
xs: The **Green Credit Rules 2023** were framed under the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The Forest Rights Act, Water Act and Biological Diversity Act are not its parent law.
xa: **EIA Notification**: **1994**, revised **2006**; **39** project categories need clearance.
**Sovereign Green Bonds** = green financing tool.
EIA was first used in **1978**.

n15e45c76ff1.s: More than ____ of the world's rivers have been dammed or diverted.
n15e45c76ff1.x: Over 60% of rivers are dammed or diverted; about 40% of land is degraded and about one-third transformed.
xa: India: **97.85 Mha = 29.77%** degraded (**2018-19**, ISRO-SAC Atlas).
India restored **21.76 Mha** in **2011-2020**.

n89121fde158.s: Which State restored the largest area of land in India during 2011-2020?
n89121fde158.x: Telangana was first (4.18 Mha) and Andhra Pradesh was among the top five of the 21.76 Mha restored.
xa: Restoration stored **461.14** Mt carbon and beat the original **Bonn** pledge.
Target linked to **UNCCD COP17**.

n2077161c519.s: According to the World Bank assessment published in 2013, India's annual cost of environmental degradation was approximately what proportion of its GDP?
n2077161c519.x: B. The World Bank's 2013 assessment put India's annual cost of environmental degradation at about 5.7% of GDP (Rs 3.75 lakh crore, for 2009), through higher healthcare spending and lower labour productivity.
n2077161c519.tq: Use the precise institution-year-figure combination rather than a nearby percentage.
xs: **World Bank (2013)**: degradation costs India ≈ **5.7% of GDP** a year (Rs **3.75** lakh crore, **2009**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Mechanism: **higher healthcare spending + lower labour productivity**.
xa: The World Bank also developed the **Green Index**.
The **poor** bear most of the cost.
ISRO-SAC: **29.77%** of India's area degraded.

n4f0a91375e4.s: Which one of the following best explains the mechanism through which environmental degradation imposes an economic cost on India?
o: Higher healthcare spending and lower labour productivity
Higher exports and lower public expenditure
Lower healthcare spending and higher labour productivity
Lower agricultural output and higher foreign exchange reserves
n4f0a91375e4.x: Environmental degradation raises healthcare expenditure and reduces labour productivity, creating a combined economic cost.
n4f0a91375e4.tq: Identify the cause-effect chain rather than selecting unrelated economic indicators.
xs: Degradation costs the economy through **higher healthcare spending and lower labour productivity** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (3) reverses both effects.
xa: World Bank (**2013**): ≈ **5.7% of GDP**.
Necessity view: degradation raises **health costs** and lowers **labour efficiency**.
Protection = **investment for long-term prosperity**.

n90f7165ffa7.s: The decision to develop the Sustainable Development Goals was taken at which event?
n90f7165ffa7.x: The 2012 Rio+20 Conference, formally the United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development, took the decision to develop the SDGs.
n90f7165ffa7.tq: Distinguish the closely related Rio, Rio+10 and Rio+20 milestones.
xs: The decision to develop the SDGs was taken at **Rio+20** (UN Conference on Sustainable Development), **2012** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Rio 1992** (UNCED) gave the **Rio Declaration**; **Johannesburg 2002** was the **WSSD**.
xa: **Agenda 2030** was adopted on **25 Sep 2015** in **New York**.
Roots of Agenda 2030: **MDGs** (8 goals, **2000-2015**) + the **Rio+20** outcome.
The SDGs end in **2030**.

nbbdad63355e.s: Agenda 2030 for Sustainable Development was adopted in New York on:
nbbdad63355e.x: Agenda 2030 was adopted on 25 September 2015 in New York.
xa: Decision to develop SDGs: **Rio+20**, **2012**.
The SDGs carry **169 targets** (APPSC-GS 2025 key).
Principles: **universal**, interconnected, **"leave no one behind"**.
nbbdad63355e.fixed: oddly worded 'pairs correctly matched' stem with single-fact options

nb80fb75b3b5.s: The report 'Limits to Growth' was associated with:
o: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
nb80fb75b3b5.x: Limits to Growth was associated with the Club of Rome and appeared in 1972.
nb80fb75b3b5.tq: Match the landmark report with its originating group.
xs: **"Limits to Growth"** (**1972**) was by the **Club of Rome** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Brundtland Commission** produced **"Our Common Future"** (**1987**).
xa: Its theme: Earth's **finite carrying capacity**.
**Carrying capacity** = maximum population an environment can support **indefinitely without degradation**.
**World Conservation Strategy** (**1980**) by IUCN, UNEP, WWF.

nbc0c3d9a813.s: The Brundtland Commission was chaired by:
nbc0c3d9a813.x: The World Commission on Environment and Development was chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland, who was the Prime Minister of Norway.
nbc0c3d9a813.tq: Use the person-title and country association to identify the chairperson.
xs: The Brundtland Commission was chaired by **Gro Harlem Brundtland**, **Norway's Prime Minister** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Its formal name is the **World Commission on Environment and Development**.
xa: Its report **"Our Common Future"** (**1987**) first **defined** sustainable development.
APPSC 2025 key: popularised by the **Brundtland Commission Report 1987**, not the Rio Declaration **1992**.
Core goal: meet present needs **without reducing the options of future generations**.

nff262b34134.s: Which body is credited with the first formal definition of sustainable development?
o: World Commission on Environment and Development
nff262b34134.x: The World Commission on Environment and Development (Brundtland Commission) first defined sustainable development in Our Common Future.
xa: Chair: **Gro Harlem Brundtland**, Norway's PM.
APPSC 2025 key: first defined by the **Brundtland Report**, not Paris, Montreal or Kyoto.

nf058abf8ceb.s: Sustainable development seeks a balance among which three pillars?
o: Environmental protection, population control and conservation
Economic growth, social inclusion and environmental protection
Social inclusion, poverty reduction and employment
nf058abf8ceb.x: Sustainable development balances economic growth, social inclusion and environmental protection rather than maximising any one pillar alone.
xa: Overlaps: **socio-economic; socio-environmental; eco-environmental**.
Odd ones out of the core goal: **growth at any cost**, **profit maximisation**.
Agenda 2030 is **universal** — not only for developing countries.

n746459af79b.s: The basic goal of sustainable development is to:
o: Maximise economic growth for the present generation
Halt economic development to conserve resources
Meet present needs while preserving choices for future generations
Restrict present consumption to subsistence for future needs
n746459af79b.x: The core goal is to meet present needs without reducing the options available to future generations, within the Earth's carrying capacity.
xa: First defined in the **Brundtland Report** (**1987**).
**Intergenerational equity** was also a **Rio 1992** principle.

n2720b57b656.s: The maximum population an environment can support indefinitely without degradation is called its:
n2720b57b656.x: Carrying capacity is the maximum population that an environment can support indefinitely without degradation.
xa: Earth's **finite carrying capacity** concerned **"Limits to Growth"**, **"Our Common Future"** and **UNCED 1992**.
**Earth Overshoot Day** marks when yearly demand exceeds what Earth can regenerate.
Sustainable development = intergenerational equity **within carrying capacity**.

n2359b24e6b6.s: The date on which humanity's annual demand on nature exceeds what the Earth can regenerate that year is called:
n2359b24e6b6.x: Earth Overshoot Day marks the point when humanity's demand on nature in a year exceeds what the Earth can regenerate during that year.
xa: It is computed by the **Global Footprint Network**, yearly.
**Plastic Overshoot Day** is an analogue.
Related idea: **carrying capacity**.

n107614256a9.s: Which of the following is one of the three pillars of sustainability?
n107614256a9.x: The three pillars are economic growth, social inclusion or equity, and environmental protection.
xa: ⚠ Trap: the odd-one-out is anything outside these three, e.g. **military strength**.
Approach: **balance all three**; do not maximise any one.
Overlaps: **socio-economic, socio-environmental, eco-environmental**.

n2e692eef2b9.s: Which of the following principles was NOT endorsed at the 1992 Rio process?
n2e692eef2b9.x: The precautionary principle, polluter pays principle and common but differentiated responsibilities were endorsed at Rio 1992. Unrestricted resource exploitation is contrary to sustainable development.
n2e692eef2b9.tq: Find the policy principle that contradicts the Rio sustainability framework.
xs: **Unrestricted resource exploitation** was not a Rio principle — so option **(4)** is correct.
Rio **1992** principles: **intergenerational equity**, **precautionary principle**, **polluter pays**, **CBDR**.
xa: "**Exploiting resources for present gains**" is an odd-one-out to sustainable development's core goal.
UNCED 1992 gave the **Rio Declaration**.

n9eb30ccde2b.s: The principle that Agenda 2030 applies to developed, developing and least developed countries alike is known as its:
n9eb30ccde2b.x: Universality means that Agenda 2030 applies to all countries, irrespective of their level of development.
n9eb30ccde2b.tq: Match the exact principle with its defining scope rather than a related development term.
xs: Agenda 2030's **universal** character: it applies to **developed, developing and least developed** countries alike — so option **(3)** is correct.
Agenda 2030 is also **interconnected**, **inclusive**, **participatory** and built on **partnerships**.
xa: Other principles: **interconnected** goals, **"leave no one behind"**, inclusive and participatory, built on **partnerships**.
Focus group: **women and girls** (APPSC-GS 2025 key).

n9f523649465.s: Agenda 2030 places particular emphasis on ending all discrimination and violence against:
n9f523649465.x: A specific focus of Agenda 2030 is ending all discrimination and violence against women and girls.
n9f523649465.tq: Read the scope of the focus group precisely and avoid narrowing or broadening it without basis.
xs: Agenda 2030 focuses on ending all discrimination and violence against **women and girls** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2025 key).
The others add "only", narrowing a goal that the notes tie to women and girls.
xa: Principle: **"Leave no one behind"**.
Agenda 2030 is **universal**.
SDGs carry **169 targets**.

n2e2edd1a470.s: The two principal roots of Agenda 2030 are:
o: The World Trade Organization and the International Monetary Fund
The Kyoto Protocol and the Montreal Protocol
The Millennium Development Goals and the Rio+20 outcome
The Stockholm Convention and the Paris Agreement
n2e2edd1a470.x: Agenda 2030 grew from the Millennium Development Goals and the outcome of the Rio+20 Conference.
n2e2edd1a470.tq: Link the agenda to its stated development and conference antecedents.
xs: Agenda 2030's roots are the **MDGs** and the **Rio+20 outcome** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The MDGs had **8 goals** (**2000-2015**); Rio+20 (**2012**) decided to develop the SDGs.
xa: Agenda 2030 adopted **25 Sep 2015**, New York.
SDGs end in **2030**.

n5437aa58a66.s: How many targets are there under the 17 Sustainable Development Goals of Agenda 2030?
n5437aa58a66.x: The 17 SDGs carry 169 targets (APPSC-GS 2025 key). 99, 129 and 150 are distractors and do not match any SDG count.
xs: The SDGs carry **169** targets — so option **(4)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2025 key).
**99**, **129** and **150** are distractors.
xa: India's **National Indicator Framework 2026**: **277** indicators.
India lags on **13 of 17** goals (SDR 2026).

nf27e9311aad.s: In the SDSN Sustainable Development Report 2025, India entered the top 100 for the first time with a rank of:
nf27e9311aad.x: India ranked 99th out of 167 with a score of about 67 in 2025.
xa: Some notes give **99th** of **166**.
SDR 2025 top: **Finland, Sweden, Denmark**.
SDR 2026: **94th**, highest ever.

nf5da53238ce.s: India presented its first Voluntary National Review on the SDGs to the UN in:
nf5da53238ce.x: India's first VNR was in 2017 and covered 7 SDGs; NITI Aayog prepared the VNR 2025.
xa: VNRs are **presented to the UN**.
India's NIF 2026 (**MoSPI**): **277** indicators.

nc9370ec1b50.s: India's rank in the Sustainable Development Report 2026 was:
nc9370ec1b50.x: India ranked 94th in 2026, 18 places better than in 2015; it first entered the top 100 in 2025.
xa: India trails **Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal, Sri Lanka**.
Lags on **13 of 17** goals; **SDG 2** the main concern.

nd31146e3747.s: The Ganga Action Plan began in:
nd31146e3747.x: The Ganga Action Plan began in 1986; 1982 is the incorrect year associated with it.
nd31146e3747.tq: Discriminate between the stated year and the close but incorrect alternative.
xs: The **Ganga Action Plan** began in **1986** — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **1982** is the trap — "Ganga Action Plan 1982" was the **APPSC 2018** "incorrect pair".
xa: The **EP Act** also dates from **1986**.
The **M.C. Mehta** series of cases covered the **Ganga**, CNG in Delhi and the Taj Mahal.
**Eco-Mark** came in **1991**.

n7e9c7cada74.s: Environmental Impact Assessment is mandatory under the
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
n7e9c7cada74.x: Environmental Impact Assessment is mandatory under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
n7e9c7cada74.tq: Apply the authority trap by matching EIA with the stated enabling legislation.
xs: **EIA** notifications are issued under the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The EP Act is the **umbrella law**, with **Sec. 3** powers; **CRZ** notifications also come under it.
The **Air Act 1981** deals with air pollution; the **Wildlife Act 1972** with wildlife and hunting.
xa: **Environmental Protection Fund Rules, 2026**: fund under **Sec. 16** of the EPA.
Great Nicobar EC was questioned for **thin baseline data**.

n15e0fbb55c7.s: The National Environment Policy was adopted in:
n15e0fbb55c7.x: The National Environment Policy was adopted in 2006 and serves as India’s overarching environment policy.
n15e0fbb55c7.tq: Distinguish the policy year from the years of the umbrella Act and Eco-Mark scheme.
xs: The **National Environment Policy** was adopted in **2006** — so option **(3)** is correct.
xa: Core idea: **conservation and livelihood security go together**.
Principles: **precautionary approach, polluter pays, public trust doctrine**.
**NAPCC** followed in **2008** with **8 missions**.

n6b998eade8d.s: Which of the following is NOT a mission under the NAPCC?
n6b998eade8d.x: The eight NAPCC missions include Solar, Sustainable Agriculture and Green India; Coastal Security is not one of them.
xa: NAPCC was released in **2008**.
Core listing (**2026**) adds **climate change and human health**.

n8f162f2bdf7.s: The National Action Plan on Climate Change, with eight national missions, was released in:
n8f162f2bdf7.x: NAPCC came in 2008 with eight missions; 2006 is the National Environment Policy year.
xa: Missions: **Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture, Strategic Knowledge**.
Implemented via **nodal ministries** + **State Action Plans**.

n7578af59316.s: Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) provisions fall under which legislation?
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
n7578af59316.x: Coastal Regulation Zone provisions fall under the Environment (Protection) Act.
n7578af59316.tq: Identify the governing environmental statute rather than the pollution-specific Acts.
xs: **CRZ** provisions fall under the **Environment (Protection) Act** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The EP Act (**1986**) is the umbrella law under which **EIA and CRZ** notifications are issued.
xa: AP **Common Zoning Regulations 2026**: **9 land-use categories**.
**EP Fund Rules 2026**: fund under **Sec. 16** of the EPA.

n5541f815ce4.s: The burden of proving that an activity is benign, in the context of the precautionary principle, rests upon:
o: The person or entity undertaking the activity
n5541f815ce4.x: Under the precautionary principle, the burden of proof shifts to the actor undertaking the potentially harmful activity to demonstrate that it is benign.
n5541f815ce4.tq: Apply the principle by identifying who must establish that the risky activity is harmless.
xs: Under the **precautionary principle**, the **burden of proof shifts to the actor** — the **person or entity undertaking the activity** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It must show the activity is **benign**; the board, community or approving authority do not carry that burden.
xa: It means acting to prevent damage **without full scientific certainty** (APPSC 2024 and 2025).
Applied in **Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum (1996)**.
**NEP 2006** adopts the **precautionary approach**.

nba1fd2d74de.s: Under the Polluter Pays Principle, the polluter bears:
o: the costs of remediation and compensation for damage
only private compensation claimed by victims
no cost, as liability shifts to the State
nba1fd2d74de.x: The principle covers both remediation of environmental damage and compensation for those affected.
xa: **Bichhri (1996)**: chemical units in **Rajasthan** paid for clean-up.
**Vellore (1996)** applied Polluter Pays with the precautionary principle.
NEP 2006 principles: **precautionary approach + polluter pays + public trust doctrine**.

ne8d89684cb4.s: The Ratlam Municipality judgment is associated with which of the following?
o: Municipal duty to address public nuisance
Mandatory use of CNG in Delhi
ne8d89684cb4.x: Ratlam Municipality (1980) recognised the municipal duty to deal with public nuisance and protect public health and sanitation.
ne8d89684cb4.tq: Identify the local-governance duty rather than an environmental liability doctrine.
xs: **Ratlam Municipality (1980)** concerns the **municipal duty on public nuisance** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Absolute liability** = **Oleum gas leak** (M.C. Mehta, **1986**); **CNG** = **Taj Trapezium (1997)** / M.C. Mehta series.
xa: **Subhash Kumar (1991)**: clean environment in **Art. 21**.
**Kamal Nath (1997)**: public trust doctrine.
**Godavarman (1995)**: "forest" whatever the ownership.

n6cf9e842a3e.s: The Taj Trapezium case is associated with:
o: chemical units in Rajasthan paying for clean-up
the State holding natural resources in trust
the right to pollution-free water and air under Article 21
n6cf9e842a3e.x: The Taj Trapezium case mandated CNG; the Rajasthan chemical units clean-up was the Bichhri case.
xa: **Bichhri** = **Polluter Pays**.
**Subhash Kumar (1991)**: pollution-free water and air under **Art. 21**.

n32ee2d9dc89.s: Which of the following doctrines is listed among the principles of the National Environment Policy, 2006, along with the precautionary approach and polluter pays?
n32ee2d9dc89.x: NEP 2006 rests on the precautionary approach, polluter pays and the public trust doctrine. Eminent domain, pith and substance and laches are land-acquisition, federal and equity doctrines, not NEP principles.
n32ee2d9dc89.tq: NEP 2006 principles: precaution + polluter pays + public trust.
xs: NEP 2006 principles: **precautionary approach + polluter pays + public trust doctrine** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Eminent domain, pith and substance and laches are not NEP principles.
xa: Public trust: the **State holds natural resources in trust** for the public.
Case: **M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath (1997)**.

n53c5d7c40ea.s: The central idea of the National Environment Policy, 2006 is that:
o: Economic growth must always be stopped to protect natural resources
Conservation and livelihood security are mutually exclusive
Environmental protection should be separated from development planning
Conservation and livelihood security can proceed together
n53c5d7c40ea.x: The NEP 2006 rests on the idea that conservation and livelihood security go together rather than being opposed to each other.
n53c5d7c40ea.tq: Apply the policy’s balancing approach instead of choosing an extreme conservation-versus-development position.
xs: NEP 2006's core idea: **conservation and livelihood security go together** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It does not see them as opposed, nor separate environment from planning — it seeks to **integrate environment into development plans**.
xa: Objectives include **inter-generational equity** and **livelihood security for poor tribal communities**.
Also: **efficient resource use** and **good environmental governance**.

n35b1dd17142.s: The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) was constituted in 1974 as a statutory body under the
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
n35b1dd17142.x: CPCB was set up in 1974 under the Water Act and later got functions under the Air Act, 1981. The EP Act came only in 1986, and the Wildlife Act (1972) does not deal with pollution boards.
n35b1dd17142.tq: CPCB 1974 = Water Act; Air Act 1981 added later.
xs: **CPCB** (**1974**) is a statutory body under the **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It later also worked under the **Air Act 1981**; the **EP Act** came only in **1986**.
xa: CPCB **sets standards** and **monitors air and water**.
SPCB compensation powers: **Sec. 33A (Water Act)** + **Sec. 31A (Air Act)**.
**APPCB** is AP's SPCB under the Water and Air Acts.

nff6ce047d6d.s: The logo of the Eco-Mark scheme (1991) is:
nff6ce047d6d.x: The Eco-Mark logo is an earthen pot; products are certified by the BIS, not the CPCB.
xa: Notified products: **soaps and detergents**, **paper**, **plastics**, **cosmetics**, **aerosols**, **food items**.
**NAPCC (2008)** has **8 missions** on climate change.
**CPCB** (**1974**) is a statutory body under the **Water Act**.

n2f3986e3fbb.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board classification, 'White' category industries are:
n2f3986e3fbb.x: White-category industries are practically non-polluting; Green-category industries have low pollution potential.
xa: **APPCB** issues **consents** under the Water and Air Acts.
SC (Aug **2025**) upheld SPCB **compensation** powers.

n2c7139e37db.s: As per the AP Socio-Economic Survey, the value of all goods and services produced within the State in a period, counted without duplication, is called:
n2c7139e37db.x: This is the APSES definition of State Domestic Product. GNP is a national, nationality-based measure, and per capita income divides income by population.
xa: The APSES definition was asked **word for word** in **APPSC-GS 2025**.
AP per capita income is computed on **NSDP**.
AP per capita income **Rs 2,68,653** vs India **Rs 2,00,162** (**2024-25** FAE).

nindian-economy-27-5.x: GNP = NNP + depreciation; national income is NNP at factor cost.
n: National Income equals GNP at market price minus depreciation minus indirect taxes plus subsidies. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 40-41]
Net National Product (NNP) equals GNP minus depreciation. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 40-41]
GNP equals NNP plus depreciation. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 40-41]
National Income equals NNP at factor cost. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 40-41]
xa: National income = total factor income (wages, rent, interest, profits) of normal residents in a year.
National income is a **flow**; national wealth is a **stock**.
⚠ **Trap:** subsidies are **added back** when moving from market price to factor cost.

n0cd236d0e0f.s: A rising GNP or GDP deflator, other things remaining equal, generally implies:
o: No change in the general price level
An increase in the purchasing power of money
A decrease in the purchasing power of money
A fall in nominal prices only
n0cd236d0e0f.x: A rising GNP or GDP deflator indicates a higher general price level. Consequently, the purchasing power of money decreases.
n0cd236d0e0f.tq: Read a deflator as a broad price-level indicator and infer its purchasing-power effect.
xs: A rising deflator means a **higher price level**, so the **purchasing power of money falls** — option **(3)** is correct.
It cannot mean "no change" in prices or higher purchasing power.
xa: **GNP deflator** is the same ratio for GNP.
GDP deflator = **nominal / real GDP x 100**.

nbd6ab3ca28f.s: The GDP deflator is calculated as
o: (GDP at factor cost / GDP at market prices) x 100
nbd6ab3ca28f.x: GDP deflator = GDP at current prices / GDP at constant prices x 100 (APPSC-G2 2025). Option A is the inverse; a difference is not an index; the FC/MP ratio reflects net indirect taxes, not prices.
xs: **GDP deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) x 100** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-G2 2025).
Option (1) is the **inverse**; a difference is not an index.
xa: Most **comprehensive** measure of inflation.
Rising deflator → **lower purchasing power** of money.

n1aad85f6ace.s: The ratio of national income to population is referred to as
n1aad85f6ace.x: Per capita income is calculated as national income divided by population.
n1aad85f6ace.tq: Identify the term from its defining ratio.
xs: **Per Capita Income = National Income / Population** — so option **(4)** is correct (APPSC 2025; GS 2025 key).
**Personal disposable income** is what individuals can spend or save — not a ratio to population.
xa: PCI rises only when NI grows **faster than population**.
AP per capita income **Rs 2,68,653** vs India **Rs 2,00,162**.

n0df2bd20925.s: Which one of the following conditions is necessary for per capita income to rise?
o: Income must grow more slowly than population
Depreciation must be greater than income growth
Income must grow faster than population
n0df2bd20925.x: Per capita income rises only when the growth of income exceeds the growth of population.
n0df2bd20925.tq: Apply the numerator–denominator relationship rather than relying on absolute income growth alone.
xs: **PCI rises only when NI grows faster than population** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Slower income growth lowers PCI; population need not be constant.
xa: **PCI = National Income / Population**.
AP per capita income is computed on **NSDP**.

na881f4407b3.s: In Andhra Pradesh, per capita income is computed on the basis of:
o: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at the national level
na881f4407b3.x: Andhra Pradesh per capita income is computed on the basis of Net State Domestic Product (NSDP).
na881f4407b3.tq: Distinguish the net regional measure used for per capita income from the corresponding gross measure.
xs: AP per capita income is computed on **NSDP (Net State Domestic Product)** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Per capita **GSDP** is a **gross** measure; per capita **income** is **net**.
xa: Compare **gross with gross**, **net with net**.

n6f43ca764b7.s: Which one of the following correctly represents Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)?
o: Exports minus imports of goods and services
Domestic factor income minus domestic consumption
Factor income paid abroad minus factor income received from abroad
Factor income received from abroad minus factor income paid abroad
n6f43ca764b7.x: NFIA is factor income received from abroad minus factor income paid abroad. It is added to GDP to obtain GNP.
n6f43ca764b7.tq: Discriminate between income flows and trade flows.
xs: **NFIA = factor income received from abroad − factor income paid abroad** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Option (3) reverses the order; exports minus imports of goods is not factor income.
xa: **GNP = GDP + NFIA**; also written **GDP + X − M** (X = income of nationals abroad, M = income of foreigners in India).
**GNP > GDP** when NFIA is positive.
India's NFIA is usually **negative**.

nadc2bd49e6c.s: An Indian resident earning factor income in Saudi Arabia contributes that income to India's:
nadc2bd49e6c.x: Factor income earned by an Indian resident abroad is excluded from India's domestic product but included in its national product.
nadc2bd49e6c.tq: Distinguish domestic production from income earned by residents abroad.
xs: Income earned by Indians abroad (e.g. in **Saudi Arabia**) is **excluded from GDP but included in GNP** — so option **(2) GNP only** is correct.
GDP is **territorial**; GNP follows **nationality/residence**.
xa: **GNP = GDP + NFIA**.
India's NFIA is usually **negative** → GNP **lower** than GDP.

n3d207955e2d.s: India's GNP is usually lower than its GDP because net factor income from abroad is:
n3d207955e2d.x: India's NFIA is usually negative, making GNP lower than GDP.
xa: **GNP = GDP + NFIA**.
NFIA = factor income received from abroad − paid abroad.
GDP is territorial; GNP is nationality-based.

n4c72f5df597.s: Which of the following is a production tax rather than a product tax?
o: Sales tax on each unit sold
Excise duty per unit of output
n4c72f5df597.x: Production taxes are levied irrespective of the quantity of output; stamp duty and property tax are examples. GST, excise and sales tax are product taxes levied per unit or value of product.
n4c72f5df597.tq: Use the test of whether the levy varies with the quantity of output.
xs: **Stamp duty** is a **production tax** — levied **irrespective of output** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**GST/sales tax** and **excise** are **product taxes**, levied **per unit** of product.
xa: Other production taxes: **land revenue**, **property tax**.
**GVA at factor cost + net production taxes = GVA at basic prices**.
**GVA at basic prices + net product taxes = GDP**.

n7679df498b1.s: Personal disposable income is obtained from personal income by deducting:
o: Undistributed corporate profits and social security contributions
Personal direct taxes and non-tax payments such as fines and fees
n7679df498b1.x: Personal disposable income equals personal income minus personal direct taxes and non-tax payments such as fines and fees.
n7679df498b1.tq: Identify the final deductions in the personal-income identity.
xs: **Personal Disposable Income = Personal Income − personal direct taxes − non-tax payments (fines, fees)** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Undistributed profits, social security contributions and corporate tax are deducted earlier, from **NI to personal income**.
xa: PDI is what individuals **can spend or save**.
**National savings** = national disposable income − consumption.

nbdf110f7ed8.s: India's nodal agency for purchasing power parity estimation under the International Comparison Program is the:
nbdf110f7ed8.x: The World Bank is the global implementing agency and the NSO is India's nodal agency.
xa: PPP prices a **common basket** at each country's own prices.
India is **3rd** in PPP GDP (ICP **2021**).

n75bc786385a.s: Which of the following combinations represents the components of national income at factor cost?
o: Indirect taxes, subsidies, depreciation and exports
Consumption, investment, government expenditure and imports
Wages, rent, interest and profits earned by the country's normal residents
Only wages and salaries earned within domestic territory
n75bc786385a.x: National income is the sum of wages, rent, interest and profits earned by factors belonging to the country, including the adjustment for NFIA.
n75bc786385a.tq: Match the factor-payment composition with the standard aggregate.
xs: National income is the total **wages, rent, interest and profits** earned by the country's **normal residents** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Consumption, investment, exports and taxes are not factor incomes; wages alone are incomplete.
xa: It equals **net domestic factor income + NFIA**.
**Transfer payments** (pensions, scholarships) are excluded.
National income is a **flow** (per year).

nf7f8328abe4.s: Which one of the following is NOT treated as a transfer payment for purposes of national income accounting?
nf7f8328abe4.x: Commission on resale is payment for a productive service and is included. Pensions, scholarships and unemployment allowances are transfer payments.
nf7f8328abe4.tq: Find the item involving a productive service among non-factor transfers.
xs: **Commission on resale** is payment for a service and is **included** — so it is NOT a transfer payment; option **(3)** is correct.
**Pensions, scholarships, unemployment allowance** are **transfer payments** — no productive service in return.
xa: **Second-hand sales** themselves are excluded (already counted when produced).
Transfer payments are **added back** when moving from NI to **personal income**.
**Interest on public debt** and **tax revenue** are also excluded.

n71f5df02633.s: National wealth, measured at a point of time, is a ____ concept.
n71f5df02633.x: National wealth is a stock measured at a point of time; national income is a flow measured over a period.
xa: **National income = NNP at factor cost**.
It is the total **factor income** (wages, rent, interest, profits) of normal residents in a year.
**Per capita income** = national income / population.

ncf225a575fb.s: National income is the standard term for:
ncf225a575fb.x: NNP at factor cost is national income; NDP = GDP - depreciation and NNP = GNP - depreciation.
xa: **GNP = GDP + NFIA**.
NNP (MP) shows how much a country **can consume** in a period.
**FC = MP − net indirect taxes**.

nb19198aed10.s: A country has GDP at market prices of ₹500 crore, depreciation of ₹50 crore, NFIA of –₹10 crore and net indirect taxes of ₹40 crore. Its national income is
nb19198aed10.x: GNPMP = 500 – 10 = ₹490 crore; NNPMP = 490 – 50 = ₹440 crore; NNPFC = 440 – 40 = ₹400 crore. NNP at factor cost is national income.
nb19198aed10.tq: Perform the conversions in sequence: domestic, national, gross, net and market price to factor cost.
xs: **410** is **NDPfc**; **440** is NNPmp; **490** is GNPmp — the distractors stop at a wrong stage.
xa: Steps: add **NFIA**, subtract **depreciation**, subtract **net indirect taxes**.
Second example: GDP **110**, NFIA +10 → GNP **120**, NNP (MP) **105**, NI **100**.

na8e41beb8db.s: GDP at factor cost equals GDP at market prices:
na8e41beb8db.x: Indirect taxes and subsidies, not direct taxes, bridge GDP at market prices and at factor cost.
xa: ⚠ Some notes print "− subsidies" — wrong sign; **subsidies are added back**.
**GVA at basic prices + net product taxes = GDP**.

nce2ac7a2e5f.s: A country's nominal GDP rises from ₹1,000 crore to ₹1,200 crore, while its price index rises from 100 to 120. What happens to its real GDP?
nce2ac7a2e5f.x: The increase in nominal GDP is exactly matched by the increase in the price index from 100 to 120, so output measured at constant prices remains unchanged.
nce2ac7a2e5f.tq: Separate the price effect from the output effect using constant-price values.
xs: Nominal GDP **1,000 → 1,200** while the price index rises **100 → 120** — the rise is all price, so **real GDP remains unchanged** — option **(3)** is correct.
A **20 per cent** rise would be the nominal change, not the real one.
xa: **Real GDP** values output at **base-year prices**, stripping out inflation.
Nominal growth exceeds real by roughly the **inflation rate**.

n8718eb52fc2.s: Which of the following is ADDED to national income in arriving at personal income?
n8718eb52fc2.x: Transfer payments are added; undistributed profits, social security contributions and corporate tax are deducted.
xa: **Net interest paid by government** is also added.
**Personal Disposable Income** = personal income − **personal direct taxes** − **non-tax payments**.

n1be3a9a33ea.s: Andhra Pradesh's per capita income in 2024-25 (FAE) was:
n1be3a9a33ea.x: AP's per capita income was Rs. 2,68,653 against India's Rs. 2,00,162 in 2024-25 FAE.
xa: AP per capita income uses **NSDP**.
The **APSES** SDP definition was asked word for word in APPSC-GS 2025.

n7a3aca4c29c.s: The value of all final goods and services produced within the geographical boundaries of a country during a year, irrespective of who produces them, is called
n7a3aca4c29c.x: GDP measures the market value of final goods and services produced within a country's geographical boundaries during a year, including production by residents and non-residents.
n7a3aca4c29c.tq: Match the territorial definition with the correct aggregate.
xs: Value of all **final** goods and services produced **within the geographical boundaries** in a year, whoever produces them = **GDP** — so option **(2)** is correct (GS 2025 key).
**GNP** is the output of **nationals/normal residents**, wherever located; **NDP** and **NNP** deduct depreciation.
xa: ⚠ GDP = **territorial**; GNP = **nationality/residence**.
**GNP = GDP + NFIA**.
GDP counts production by both **residents and non-residents** inside the territory.

nd6fd5839299.s: Why is depreciation deducted while calculating net national or domestic product?
o: Because depreciation measures the income earned by foreign factors
Because depreciation is a direct tax on capital goods
Because depreciation represents transfer payments to households
Because output used merely to replace worn-out capital does not constitute new output
nd6fd5839299.x: Depreciation, or consumption of fixed capital, is deducted because production used only to replace worn-out capital adds nothing new to the productive stock.
nd6fd5839299.tq: Identify the economic purpose of the gross-to-net adjustment.
xs: Depreciation is deducted because **output that only replaces worn-out capital adds nothing new** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is **consumption of fixed capital** — not a tax, a transfer or foreign factor income.
xa: **NDP = GDP − Depreciation**; **NNP = GNP − Depreciation**.
⚠ **GVA includes depreciation**; **NVA excludes** it.

n3c944c65493.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Gross Value Added (GVA)?
o: GVA at basic prices has been the headline sectoral measure since the 2011-12 series.
GVA at basic prices is not used in the 2022-23 series.
n3c944c65493.x: GVA at basic prices continues to be used in the 2022-23 series.
xa: CSO/NSO headline growth is on **GVA at basic prices**.
**GVA at basic prices + net product taxes = GDP**.

n95f7aa10888.s: In the 2022–23 national accounts series, which method replaced single deflation for manufacturing and agriculture?
n95f7aa10888.x: The 2022–23 series uses double deflation, which separately deflates output prices and input prices.
n95f7aa10888.tq: Test the exact technical term used for a methodological change.
xs: The **2022-23** series uses **double deflation** — deflating **both output and input prices** for manufacturing and agriculture — so option **(1)** is correct.
It replaced **single deflation**.
xa: The new series also brought in **Supply-Use Tables**.
Released by **NSO** on **27 Feb 2026**.
Base year moved from **2011-12** to **2022-23**.

n4a942c9a3da.s: Which of the following is regarded as the most comprehensive measure of inflation in India?
n4a942c9a3da.x: The GDP deflator covers all goods and services in GDP (consumption, investment, government, exports), whereas WPI, CPI and CPI-IW price fixed baskets (APPSC-G2 2025 key).
n4a942c9a3da.tq: Whole GDP basket -> deflator is most comprehensive.
xs: The **GDP deflator** is the **most comprehensive** measure of inflation — so option **(3)** is correct (G2 2025 key).
It covers **all** goods and services in GDP — **consumption, investment, government, exports** — not a **fixed basket** like **CPI/WPI**.
xa: GDP deflator = **current-price GDP / constant-price GDP x 100**.
The 2022-23 series uses **double deflation**.

nb4ca55f4338.s: India's PPP-based GDP is much larger than its GDP measured at the market exchange rate primarily because:
o: Market exchange rates include transfer payments while PPP excludes them
India has higher domestic price levels than the United States and China
Prices are lower in India, so the same domestic output has greater purchasing power when compared internationally
PPP excludes services from GDP measurement
nb4ca55f4338.x: Lower prices in India make its output larger when valued using purchasing power parity than when converted at market exchange rates.
nb4ca55f4338.tq: Explain the direction of the PPP–market-rate difference through relative price levels.
xs: **Lower prices in India** make PPP GDP much **larger** than market-rate GDP — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (2) has it backwards; PPP does not exclude services or concern transfers.
xa: PPP prices a **common basket** at each country's own prices.
India: **3rd** in PPP, **4th** in nominal GDP.

nindian-economy-5-5.x: Real GDP uses constant base-year prices, nominal GDP current prices; real growth shows true output growth.
n: Nominal GDP is measured at current-year prices. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 7-8]
Real GDP is measured at constant or base-year prices. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 7-8]
Real GDP growth is a better indicator of actual output growth. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 7-8]
Base-year prices are used to calculate Real GDP. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 7-8]
Economic growth is a quantitative increase in output. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 7-8]
GDP measures economic growth. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 7-8]
xa: Base year now **2022-23** (earlier **2011-12**).
**GDP deflator = Nominal GDP / Real GDP x 100** — the most comprehensive measure of inflation.
2025-26: nominal growth **8.0%** vs real **7.4%** — nominal exceeds real by roughly the inflation rate.

nindian-economy-26-5.s: In Real GVA, a base year is used to:
o: remove the effect of price changes
nindian-economy-26-5.x: Real GVA uses constant base-year prices to strip out price changes; nominal GVA uses current prices.
n: Gross Value Added (GVA) measures the value added by producers to the economy. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 38-40]
Gross Value Added (GVA) measures the value added by sectors to the economy. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 38-40]
Real GVA is calculated at constant prices. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 38-40]
A base year is used when GVA is calculated at constant prices. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 38-40]
The use of a base year removes the effect of price changes from GVA. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 38-40]
Nominal GVA is calculated at current prices. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 38-40]
xa: **GVA vs NVA:** GVA includes depreciation; NVA excludes it.
**GVA at factor cost + net production taxes = GVA at basic prices**.
**PPP** compares GDP by pricing a **common basket** at each country's own prices.

n6a4d5aa8974.s: The value added (product) method measures national income by summing:
o: the value added by every producing unit
n6a4d5aa8974.x: The product method sums the value added by each producing unit, avoiding double counting.
xa: The production method is also called the **product/output** or **net product / final product** method.
**Income method** = compensation of employees + operating surplus (rent, interest, profit) + **mixed income**.
**Expenditure method** = **C + I + G + (X - M)**.
⚠ **"Cost and Accounting method" is NOT** a method of measuring national income (APPSC-G2 **2025**).

n84bb27a288d.s: Under the income method, national income sums compensation of employees, operating surplus and:
n84bb27a288d.x: The income method sums compensation of employees, operating surplus (rent, interest, profit) and mixed income.
xa: Full formula: **GDP = Compensation of employees + Consumption of fixed capital + (Taxes on production - subsidies on production) + Gross operating surplus**.
Operating surplus covers **rent, interest and profit**.
The income method is also called the **factor payment / distributed share** method.

n75ef0b503a4.s: Value added at a particular stage of production is equal to:
o: Value of output minus depreciation only
Value of output minus intermediate consumption
Value of output plus intermediate consumption
Intermediate consumption minus value of output
n75ef0b503a4.x: Value added is calculated as the value of output minus the value of intermediate consumption.
n75ef0b503a4.tq: Recall the accounting identity and distinguish intermediate consumption from depreciation.
xs: Value added = **value of output minus intermediate consumption** — option **(2)** is correct.
Subtracting **depreciation** turns GVA into **NVA**, so option (1) is wrong.
xa: **GVA includes depreciation**; **NVA = GVA - depreciation**.
Summing value added at each stage solves **double counting** (cotton farmer → weaver → tailor).
**Double deflation** (**2022-23** series): **Real GVA = Real output - Real intermediate consumption**.

na15db3cd77e.s: Double counting in national income (cotton → cloth → garment) is avoided by:
o: Adding the gross sales of all producers
Counting only the final product or the value added at each stage
Counting only the value of intermediate goods
Excluding the value of the final product
na15db3cd77e.x: Including only the final product, or summing the value added by the farmer, weaver and tailor, prevents the cotton being counted repeatedly.
xa: **Value added = value of output - intermediate consumption**.
The **production (value added) method** avoids double counting — the shirt is the final product.
Double counting is also a measurement difficulty in India due to **no occupational specialisation**.

n2473f4ec66c.s: In India, the income method of estimating national income is applied mainly to:
n2473f4ec66c.x: India uses the production method for agriculture, mining and manufacturing, and the income method for services.
xa: Production method sectors: **agriculture and allied activities, mining, manufacturing**.
Income method sectors: **trade, transport, banking, public administration**.
**PFCE** (expenditure data) serves as a check.

nabd12f56cce.s: The Income Method is principally used in India for estimating income generated by which group of activities?
o: Trade, transport, banking, real estate and public administration
nabd12f56cce.x: The income method is used for service activities such as trade, transport, banking, real estate, public administration and other services.
nabd12f56cce.tq: Use sectoral grouping to distinguish the production and income methods.
xs: The Income Method is used for **trade, transport, banking, real estate and public administration** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Agriculture, mining and manufacturing** use the **production (value added)** method — option (4) is wrong.
**Construction** is partly done by the **expenditure (commodity flow)** method.
xa: **India uses a combination of the production and income methods**.
Expenditure method = **cross-check** of demand-side components.
Income method sums **compensation of employees + operating surplus + mixed income**.

n047d88f51ab.s: Which of the following correctly describes the real flow in a two-sector circular flow model?
o: Money moves from firms to households and factor services move from firms to households
Taxes move from government to firms and exports move from households to firms
Factor services move from firms to households and goods move from households to firms
Factor services move from households to firms and goods and services move from firms to households
n047d88f51ab.x: In the real flow, households provide factor services to firms, while firms provide goods and services to households.
n047d88f51ab.tq: Separate physical flows from monetary flows in the circular-flow model.
xs: In the real flow, **factor services move from households to firms** and **goods and services move from firms to households** — option **(4)** is correct.
Movement of **money** (factor payments, consumption spending) is the **money flow**, not the real flow — so option (1) is wrong.
Option (3) reverses both directions of the real flow.
xa: **Money flow:** **factor payments** go firm → household; **consumption spending** goes household → firm.
Leakages: **saving, taxes, imports**; injections: **investment, government spending, exports**.
Equilibrium: **S + T + M = I + G + X** — total leakages equal total injections.

n7e8dd7e2d7a.s: Who associated the national dividend with the net aggregate of commodities and services produced annually by labour and capital acting on natural resources?
n7e8dd7e2d7a.x: Marshall defined the national dividend in terms of the net aggregate of commodities and services produced by labour and capital acting on natural resources.
n7e8dd7e2d7a.tq: Link the economist to the distinctive keyword in the definition.
xs: **Alfred Marshall** linked the **"national dividend"** to the net aggregate of commodities and services produced each year — option **(3)** is correct.
In Marshall's view, **labour and capital acting on natural resources** produce this net aggregate of **material and immaterial** commodities and services.
**Pigou** stressed income **measured in money**; **Fisher** stressed **consumption**; **Kuznets** stressed net output to consumers or **net additions to capital stock**.
xa: ⚠ Memory hook: **Marshall** = national dividend; **Pigou** = money measure; **Fisher** = consumption.
**Kuznets**: net output flowing to **ultimate consumers** from the productive system, or into **net additions to capital stock**.
**Pigou** included **income from abroad** in his definition.

n5e78c9a0d38.s: Whose definition of national income is based on consumption, i.e. services received by ultimate consumers?
n5e78c9a0d38.x: Fisher's definition is consumption-based; Kuznets added net additions to capital stock and Pigou included income from abroad.
xa: **Marshall** = **"national dividend"**: labour and capital acting on natural resources produce a net aggregate each year.
Marshall's aggregate includes both **material and immaterial** commodities and services.
⚠ Quick map: **Marshall** = dividend; **Pigou** = money; **Fisher** = consumption; **Kuznets** = capital additions.

n74746f3871c.s: In the expenditure method, national income is measured by aggregating
n74746f3871c.x: The expenditure method adds consumption, investment, government expenditure and net exports, represented by C + I + G + (X − M).
