n56fbb192e6e.s: What was the principal recommendation of the Dantwala Committee regarding unemployment estimation?
o: To replace NSS surveys with CMIE surveys
To provide separate estimates by status and by category
To use one single national number for all forms of unemployment
n56fbb192e6e.x: The Dantwala Committee rejected a single-number estimate and recommended separate estimates by usual, weekly and daily status, as well as by category.
n56fbb192e6e.tq: Identify the committee recommendation that rejects an over-simplified single measure.
xs: The **Dantwala Committee** recommended **separate estimates by status and by category** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It **rejected a single-number estimate**, so option 3 is the opposite; it did not drop daily status or bring in CMIE.
xa: Status = **usual, weekly, daily** — the basis of UPS, CWS and CDS.
Dantwala Committee: **1970**.
**Bhagwati Committee (1973)** reviewed estimates + **employment-oriented policies**.

n993e583a423.s: Which committee reviewed unemployment estimates and employment-oriented policies in 1973?
o: Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics
n993e583a423.x: The Bhagwati Committee, constituted in 1973, reviewed unemployment estimates and employment-oriented policies.
n993e583a423.tq: Match the committee with its year and subject of review.
xs: The **Bhagwati Committee** (Committee on Unemployment, **1973**) reviewed unemployment estimates and **employment-oriented policies** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Dantwala** (**1970**) dealt with estimates by status; the **SCLFS** designed the **PLFS**.
xa: ⚠ **Dantwala 1970** = estimates by status; **Bhagwati 1973** = estimates + policies.
SCLFS was set up on the **National Statistical Commission's** advice.
PLFS launched **April 2017**.

n7ad64b4952d.s: In Census terminology, a main worker is one who worked for at least ____ in the year.
n7ad64b4952d.x: A person who worked for 183 days or more is a main worker; less than 183 days makes a marginal worker.
xa: ⚠ **183** days is also the **UPS** "major time" line, but Census is **not** an NSS approach.
Census gives main/marginal worker data every **10** years.
UPSS adds subsidiary work of **30 days**.

n7e76c2171e9.s: Which organisation conducts the Employment–Unemployment Survey and the Quarterly Employment Survey of establishments?
o: Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment
Directorate General of Employment and Training alone
n7e76c2171e9.x: The Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment conducts the Employment–Unemployment Survey and the Quarterly Employment Survey of establishments.
n7e76c2171e9.tq: Use the survey title to identify the responsible labour institution.
xs: The **Labour Bureau (MoLE)** runs the **Employment-Unemployment Survey** and the **Quarterly Employment Survey** of establishments — so option **(2)** is correct.
**NSO (MoSPI)** runs the **PLFS**; **CMIE** runs **CPHS**; **DGE&T** holds job-seeker **registration** data.
xa: QES covers **establishments**, not households.
CMIE gives a **higher UR** than PLFS.
Census: worker data every **10** years.

n2a0a6e5a191.s: The Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics was set up on the advice of which body and was associated with the design of PLFS?
n2a0a6e5a191.x: The Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics was set up on the advice of the National Statistical Commission and designed the PLFS framework.
n2a0a6e5a191.tq: Match the technical committee with the institution that recommended it.
xs: The **SCLFS** was set up on the advice of the **National Statistical Commission** and designed the **PLFS** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its aim: **more frequent data** than 5-yearly NSS rounds.
xa: PLFS is run by the **NSO**, **MoSPI**.
Launched **April 2017**.
Revamp from **January 2025**: **monthly** CWS estimates.

ncdb81cafe9d.s: The Periodic Labour Force Survey was launched in:
ncdb81cafe9d.x: PLFS was launched in April 2017. Its first annual report, relating to 2017–18, was released in May 2019.
ncdb81cafe9d.tq: Distinguish the launch date from the release date of the first report.
xs: The **PLFS** was launched in **April 2017** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**May 2019** is when the first annual report (**2017-18**) came out; **January 2025** is the revamp.
xa: ⚠ Launched April 2017, but the first report only in **May 2019**.
Designed by the **SCLFS**.

neaff3eed6f1.s: CMIE unemployment data differ from PLFS data in being:
o: annual, with the same methodology as PLFS
monthly, but with a methodology identical to PLFS
based on the PLFS methodology with a smaller sample
monthly, with a larger sample and a different methodology
neaff3eed6f1.x: CMIE data are monthly with a larger sample and a different methodology, which makes their estimates diverge.
xa: CMIE: **53 million** unemployed (**Dec 2021**); UR ~**7.95%** in **Sep 2023**.
CMIE's survey is the **CPHS**; it gives a **higher UR** than PLFS.
PLFS is run by the **NSO**, MoSPI.

na885104fdde.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the PLFS revamp from January 2025?
o: Monthly all-India CWS estimates began to be produced.
Quarterly estimates were extended to rural areas.
The annual report shifted to the calendar year.
The sample was reduced to about one-half of its earlier size.
na885104fdde.x: The sample was raised, not reduced, to about 2,72,304 households.
xa: Original design: quarterly estimates for **urban** areas only.
PLFS 2025 (calendar year) UR: **3.1%**.

n7a65f5130f7.s: The unemployment rates under UPS, CWS and CDS in the NSS 68th Round for 2011–12 were respectively:
n7a65f5130f7.x: For 2011–12, the NSS 68th Round reported unemployment rates of 2.7% under UPS, 3.7% under CWS and 5.6% under CDS.
n7a65f5130f7.tq: Recall the ordered numerical series and preserve the approach sequence.
xs: NSS **68th round (2011-12)**: **UPS 2.7%**, **CWS 3.7%**, **CDS 5.6%** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The order rises with shorter reference periods: ⚠ **UPS < CWS < CDS**.
xa: The 68th was the **last quinquennial** round.
The high CDS rate shows **high intermittent** unemployment.

n66e5c27facd.s: PLFS 2022-23 put graduate unemployment at about:
n66e5c27facd.x: PLFS 2022-23 gave 3.2% overall unemployment and 13% for graduates.
xa: PLFS 2019-20 was asked in **APPSC 2022**.

n867c50880ed.s: As reported by CMIE, approximately how many persons were unemployed in India in December 2021?
n867c50880ed.x: CMIE reported approximately 53 million unemployed persons as of December 2021.
n867c50880ed.tq: Recall the distinctive large-scale numerical estimate associated with a private agency.
xs: **CMIE** reported about **53 million** unemployed as of **Dec 2021** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2021 answer).
CMIE is **private** and runs the monthly household survey **CPHS**.
xa: CMIE UR ~**7.95%** in **Sep 2023**, above official PLFS figures.
**CMIE vs PLFS** divergence: CMIE is monthly, has a larger sample and a different methodology.

n43ce891203c.s: Critics argue that the CWS measure of unemployment may mask:
n43ce891203c.x: CWS is criticised for masking underemployment and missing circular migration.
xa: India moved to monthly CWS data from **2025**.
CWS rates exceed **UPSS** because the short period catches seasonal unemployment.
**CMIE vs PLFS** divergence is another debate.

n8376a12bbeb.s: Under PLFS 2023-24 (usual status), Andhra Pradesh's unemployment rate was:
n8376a12bbeb.x: AP's rate was 4.1% against India's 3.2%; AP's rural rate (3.4%) was below its urban rate (5.9%).
xa: AP male UR **4.3%**, female **3.7%**.
AP informality: about **55%** overall.

o: Percentage change in employment divided by percentage change in output
Percentage change in output divided by percentage change in employment
Total employment divided by total population
Change in labour force divided by change in unemployment
nc1eef734928.x: Employment elasticity equals the percentage change in employment divided by the percentage change in output or GDP.
nc1eef734928.tq: Recall the numerator and denominator of the formula without reversing them.
xs: **Employment elasticity** = **% change in employment ÷ % change in output (GDP)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option 2 inverts the ratio; employment ÷ population is a different ratio altogether.
xa: A **low or near-zero** value → **jobless growth**.
Jobless growth term: **Nick Perna**, early **1990s**.
Post-1991, GDP grew **6-7%** but **formal job creation lagged**.

n76d06cf0f84.s: The expression ‘missing middle’ in the context of India’s employment pattern refers to:
o: The gap between rural and urban literacy rates
The shortage of middle-level government officials
The absence of a manufacturing stage between agriculture and services
n76d06cf0f84.x: India followed a services-led path that largely skipped the manufacturing stage, described as the ‘missing middle’.
n76d06cf0f84.tq: Discriminate between an economic structural term and literal interpretations of the words.
xs: The "**missing middle**" = India's **services-led path skipping the manufacturing stage** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is not about literacy, consumers or officials.
xa: It is one of the **post-1991** reasons for **jobless growth**.
Services' employment share rose **22.82% (1993-94) → 34.90% (2009-10)**; industry stayed ~**12%**.
Urban employment: services **62.0%** (2025-26).

nd10d0b55a5e.s: Which of the following correctly describes the rural–urban pattern of employment?
o: Agriculture 62.0% of rural employment; services 57% of urban employment
Agriculture 57% of rural employment; services 52% of urban employment
Agriculture 47% of rural employment; services 62.0% of urban employment
Agriculture 57% of rural employment; services 62.0% of urban employment
nd10d0b55a5e.x: Agriculture accounted for 57% of rural employment, whereas services accounted for 62.0% of urban employment.
xa: Rural self-employment: **62.8%**.
Agriculture = **42.4%** of total employment (**Q2 FY26**).
Total employment (Q2 FY26): **56.2 crore** (15+).

n9d0e52340e0.s: According to the U-shaped hypothesis, Female LFPR generally:
o: Falls with early income growth and rises later with education and service-sector opportunities
Rises with early income growth and falls with later education
Remains constant regardless of income and education
Falls continuously as service-sector employment expands
n9d0e52340e0.x: The U-shaped hypothesis proposes that Female LFPR initially falls with income growth and rises later as education and service-sector opportunities expand.
n9d0e52340e0.tq: Apply the two-stage movement implied by the U-shaped hypothesis.
xs: **U-shaped hypothesis**: FLFPR **falls with early income growth** and **rises later with education + service jobs** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option 2 describes an inverted U; FLFPR is neither constant nor continuously falling.
xa: Barriers: **social norms**, **unpaid care work**, **unsafe transport**.
AP: urban young women stay out due to **higher education** and **no flexible timings**.

nd5d013baa2d.s: Which one of the following best describes the gig economy?
o: Employment of workers exclusively in government departments
Engagement of independent contractors and freelancers instead of permanent workers
Employment based only on hereditary occupations
Permanent employment with guaranteed pension benefits
nd5d013baa2d.x: The gig economy is based on independent contractors and freelancers rather than permanent workers. Delivery services, ride-sharing and freelancing are common examples.
nd5d013baa2d.tq: Distinguish the exact meaning of a paired economic term from its misleading permanent-employment alternative.
xs: The **gig economy** uses **independent contractors and freelancers instead of permanent workers** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2019).
Examples: **delivery**, **ride-sharing**, **freelancing**.
xa: NITI Aayog: **77 lakh** gig workers in **2020-21**; **2.35 crore** projected by **2029-30**.
**Code on Social Security 2020** defines gig and platform workers.
Gig workers grew **55%** to about **120 lakh** in **FY25**.

n62dd52670d8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the employment problem of India's post-1991 growth?
o: Employment growth did not keep pace with labour-force growth.
Growth was not sufficiently concentrated in labour-intensive manufacturing.
Unemployment increasingly appeared in the unorganised sector.
Employment generation was sufficiently concentrated in labour-intensive manufacturing.
n62dd52670d8.x: Growth was not sufficiently concentrated in labour-intensive manufacturing.
xa: GDP grew **6-7%** but formal job creation lagged.
About **12 million** persons enter the job market each year.
"**Missing middle**": services-led path skipping manufacturing.

ncd073ac6ca7.s: Agriculture's share of India's workforce declined from 72% in 1951 to ____ in 1993–94.
ncd073ac6ca7.x: Agriculture's workforce share declined from 72% in 1951 to 64.75% in 1993–94.
xa: Industry stayed around ~**12%**.
Agriculture now: **42.4%** (Q2 FY26).

nf994bc56402.s: According to the India Employment Report 2024, what percentage of total employment in India was accounted for by self-employment in 2022?
nf994bc56402.x: Self-employment accounted for 55.8% of total employment in India in 2022, as reported in the India Employment Report 2024 prepared by ILO-IHD.
nf994bc56402.tq: Use the exact employment-share figure and distinguish it from rural and urban employment indicators.
xs: Per the **India Employment Report 2024**, **self-employment** was **55.8%** of total employment in **2022** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**42.4%** = agriculture's share; **49.8%** = urban regular wage jobs; **62.8%** = rural self-employment.
xa: The report is by **ILO + Institute for Human Development**.
ES 2025-26 also gives **55.8%** for **Q2 FY26**.
Casual labour: **18.9%** (Q2 FY26).

ndd63689f1fe.s: The overall informal-sector share of employment in Andhra Pradesh was approximately
ndd63689f1fe.x: The overall informal-sector share of employment in Andhra Pradesh was approximately 55%.
ndd63689f1fe.tq: Distinguish the approximate overall figure from the separate rural and urban shares.
xs: AP's overall **informal** share of employment is about **55%** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**62.3%** is the **rural** informal share and **45.6%** the **urban** share (2024-25).
xa: Nationally, Gen Z: only **14.2%** have a **formal job contract**.
Direct factory employment fell **61% to 47%** (2011-2023).

n25430c9f79a.tq: Identify the year-specific figure from adjacent PLFS values.
xs: **Female LFPR (15+)** in **2023-24** was **41.7%** — so option **(3)** is correct.
xa: AP female LFPR (15+): **44.8%** vs India **41.7%**.

n2d7f30c2b7a.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Female LFPR figures cited for 2025?
n2d7f30c2b7a.x: For 2025, the overall Female LFPR was approximately 40%, with 45.9% in rural areas and 27.7% in urban areas.
n2d7f30c2b7a.tq: Match the aggregate figure with the correct rural–urban breakdown.
xs: **Female LFPR 2025**: overall ~**40%**, **rural 45.9%**, **urban 27.7%** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Options 1, 2 and 4 swap these figures.
xa: Quarterly CWS female LFPR: **34.7%** (Jan-Mar 2026).

n8cbd84005d8.s: The widening rural–urban gap in Female LFPR is primarily indicated by which of the following?
o: A much larger increase in rural LFPR than in urban LFPR
A decline in rural LFPR and a rise in urban LFPR
Identical rural and urban LFPR levels by 2025
A larger increase in urban LFPR than in rural LFPR
n8cbd84005d8.x: Rural LFPR rose substantially more than urban LFPR, widening the rural–urban gap.
n8cbd84005d8.tq: Infer the trend from the comparative changes rather than from a single level.
xs: The widening gap comes from a **much larger rise in rural LFPR** (**33.0% → 45.9%**) than **urban** (**23.3% → 27.7%**) — so option **(1)** is correct.
Both rose, so options 2 and 4 are wrong; levels are far from identical.
xa: Period: **2019-20 to 2025** (July 2026 PLFS).
Rural women = **80%** of the rise in female workers (**2017-18 to 2023-24**).
⚠ **23.3%** = all-India FLFPR 2017-18 and also urban FLFPR 2019-20.

n909f2f8d90d.s: The Labour Bureau Quarterly Employment Survey covers establishments with at least 10 workers in how many sectors?
n909f2f8d90d.x: The QES covers establishments with 10 or more workers across nine sectors.
n909f2f8d90d.tq: Recall the survey’s coverage threshold and number of sectors.
xs: The Labour Bureau **QES** covers establishments with **10+ workers** in **9 sectors** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Sectors: manufacturing, construction, trade, transport, accommodation and restaurants, **IT/BPO**, education, health, financial services.
xa: QES is run by the **Labour Bureau**.
Q2 FY26: **8.7 lakh** new jobs over Q1.
Total employment Q2 FY26: **56.2 crore**.

nd729ecb1f2e.s: The India Employment Report 2024 was released jointly by:
o: The IMF and the Labour Bureau
The World Bank and NITI Aayog
The ILO and the Institute for Human Development
The UNDP and the National Statistical Office
nd729ecb1f2e.x: The India Employment Report 2024 was released by the International Labour Organization and the Institute for Human Development.
nd729ecb1f2e.tq: Identify the correct institutional partnership rather than a neighbouring international body.
xs: The **India Employment Report 2024** was released by the **ILO** and the **Institute for Human Development** — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ It is **ILO + IHD**, not NITI Aayog or the World Bank.
xa: It notes **informal and vulnerable jobs** even among **educated youth**.
Self-employment: **55.8%** (for 2022).
Gen Z: only **14.2%** have a formal job contract.

na58c49cf6cf.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a barrier to women’s labour-force participation?
na58c49cf6cf.x: Social norms, unpaid care work and unsafe transport are barriers; expansion of service-sector opportunities is associated with increased participation at a later stage.
na58c49cf6cf.tq: Find the supportive factor among the listed barriers.
xs: **Expansion of service-sector opportunities** is not a barrier — under the **U-shaped hypothesis** it later **raises** FLFPR — so option **(2)** is correct.
The listed barriers are **social norms**, **unpaid care work** and **unsafe transport**.
xa: Urban FLFPR only **27.7%** (2025) vs rural **45.9%**.
AP: urban young women stay out (**higher education**, **no flexible timings**).

n79d56188d2d.s: According to NITI Aayog's report titled ‘India's Booming Gig and Platform Economy’, the estimated number of gig workers in India during 2020-21 was
n79d56188d2d.x: NITI Aayog estimated 77 lakh gig workers in 2020-21.
n79d56188d2d.tq: Separate the base-year estimate from later actual and projected figures.
xs: NITI Aayog's "**India's Booming Gig and Platform Economy**" (**June 2022**) estimated **77 lakh** gig workers in **2020-21** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**2.35 crore** is the **2029-30** projection; **1.27 crore** the **2024-25** projection; **120 lakh** the **FY25** size.
xa: 2029-30 projection = **6.7%** of the workforce.
**1.43 crore** projected for **2025-26**.
PLFS does not yet capture gig workers as a distinct category.

n6796b45ae41.s: NITI Aayog projected that the number of gig workers would reach which of the following levels by 2029-30?
n6796b45ae41.x: The NITI Aayog projection was 2.35 crore gig workers by 2029-30, equivalent to about 6.7% of the workforce.
n6796b45ae41.tq: Use the time reference to distinguish a long-term projection from current estimates.
xs: NITI Aayog projected **2.35 crore** gig workers by **2029-30** (**6.7%** of workforce) — so option **(3)** is correct.
xa: Report: "India's Booming Gig and Platform Economy", **June 2022**.
FY25 size: about **120 lakh** (up **55%**).
Aggregators contribute **1-2%** of annual turnover under the **Code on Social Security 2020**.

n04524ba9869.s: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, aggregators are required to contribute what proportion of their annual turnover to a fund for the benefit of gig workers?
n04524ba9869.x: Aggregators contribute 1% to 2% of annual turnover to a fund intended to support life and health insurance and pensions for gig workers.
n04524ba9869.tq: Match the statutory contribution range with its stated social-security purpose.
xs: Under the **Code on Social Security 2020**, aggregators contribute **1-2% of annual turnover** to a fund — so option **(2)** 1% to 2% is correct.
The fund pays for **life/health insurance** and **pensions** for gig workers.
xa: The Code **defines gig and platform workers**.
Gig workers: **77 lakh** (2020-21) → about **120 lakh** (FY25).
Data gap: PLFS does not capture them as a distinct category.

n3cf12b051b4.s: Which of the following is correct about the measurement of gig workers in India?
o: PLFS records gig workers as a separate category.
All gig workers are registered on e-Shram.
PLFS does not yet capture gig workers as a distinct category.
n3cf12b051b4.x: PLFS does not yet identify gig workers separately, and most remain outside e-Shram registration.
xa: Gig workforce about **120 lakh** in **FY25**; over **2%** of workforce.
**Code on Social Security 2020** defines gig and platform workers.
NITI projection: **2.35 crore** by **2029-30**.

n4f734913978.s: Against Andhra Pradesh's all-age female LFPR of 35.8%, the all-India figure is:
n4f734913978.x: India's all-age female LFPR is 31.7%, lower than AP's 35.8%.
xa: Female LFPR 15+: AP **44.8%** vs India **41.7%**.
AP overall LFPR: **47.5%** (rural **50.1%**, urban **41.3%**).
Yet urban young women in AP stay out (**higher education**, **no flexible timings**).

nb2d4f31496b.s: According to PLFS 2025, India's LFPR, WPR and unemployment rate were approximately:
nb2d4f31496b.x: PLFS 2025 reported LFPR of about 59%, WPR of about 57% and an unemployment rate of about 3%.
xa: Workforce: **61.6 crore** (PLFS 2025).
Female LFPR 2025: ~**40%**.
AP overall LFPR: **47.5%**.

nc27a05fafe7.s: Which of the following is a self-employment programme?
nc27a05fafe7.x: IRDP (like NRLM) is a self-employment programme; NREP and MGNREGS are wage-employment programmes.
xa: Other wage programmes: **JRY, EAS, SGRY, NFFWP**.
Other self-employment programmes: **TRYSEM, DWCRA, SGSY, PMEGP**.
⚠ **PMRY** is **not** a wage employment programme (APPSC 2017).

n6bbdf90c7f5.s: PMEGP was formed by integrating which two earlier programmes?
n6bbdf90c7f5.x: PMEGP, launched in 2008, was formed by combining the Prime Minister’s Rozgar Yojana (PMRY) and the Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP).
n6bbdf90c7f5.tq: Identify the predecessor programmes rather than the ministry or beneficiary group.
xs: **PMEGP** (**2008**) merged **PMRY and REGP** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**NRLM** and **MGNREGS** are separate rural programmes; **NCS** and **PMKVY** are job-portal and skilling schemes.
xa: **PMRY** (**1993**): for educated unemployed youth.
PMEGP: margin money **15-35%**.
⚠ PMEGP = **MSME** ministry, implemented by **KVIC**.

n10d90f8ff0f.s: Which programmes were subsumed into NREGA in its districts from 2006?
n10d90f8ff0f.x: NFFWP and SGRY were subsumed into NREGA in the districts it covered from 2006.
xa: NFFWP launched **14 November 2004**.
NREGA launched **2 February 2006** in **200** districts.
⚠ **2005** Act – **2006** launch – **2008** all districts – **2009** "Mahatma Gandhi" added.

nc91d860460d.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the initial implementation of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act?
o: It began in 200 districts on 2 February 2006.
It began in 150 most backward districts in 2004.
It began in all districts on 1 April 2008.
It began in 625 districts on 2 October 2009.
nc91d860460d.x: The Act was launched on 2 February 2006 in 200 districts. The all-district coverage was achieved later, from 1 April 2008.
nc91d860460d.tq: Distinguish the initial coverage from later nationwide expansion.
xs: NREGA began on **2 February 2006** in **200** districts — so option **(1)** is correct.
**150 backward districts (2004)** = **NFFWP**; **all districts from 1 April 2008** was a later phase; **2 October 2009** was the renaming.
xa: **130** more districts were added in **2007-08**.
⚠ Trap: **625** = all-district coverage of **2008**, not the launch.
⚠ **2005** Act – **2006** launch – **2008** all districts – **2009** "Mahatma Gandhi".

na784fec32d8.s: Which of the following best expresses the wider significance of MGNREGA?
o: It certifies prior learning under the NSQF.
It is primarily an urban credit programme for informal workers.
It serves as a safety net during agrarian distress and crises such as COVID-19.
na784fec32d8.x: MGNREGA is significant as a safety net during agrarian distress and emergencies such as the COVID-19 crisis, in addition to being associated with the right to work.
na784fec32d8.tq: Apply the scheme’s broader social-protection role to a crisis situation.
xs: MGNREGA is a **safety net** in **agrarian distress** and crises like **COVID-19** — so option **(4)** is correct.
NSQF certification is **RPL**; it is **rural**, not urban credit; it has nothing to do with export manufacturing.
xa: It is the **only law built on the right to work**.
World Development Report **2014**: "**stellar example of rural development**".
Scale: **200-250 crore** person-days a year.

n8d899a31795.s: Under MGNREGA, the unit to which the employment guarantee is attached is:
o: Each adult individual in a rural area
Each registered worker in a Gram Panchayat
n8d899a31795.x: The entitlement under MGNREGA is provided to a household, not separately to every individual adult.
n8d899a31795.tq: Discriminate between the household-based entitlement and an individual-based interpretation.
xs: The MGNREGA entitlement attaches to the **household**, not the individual — so option **(2)** the rural household is correct.
APPSC 2017: the mandate is "**100 days** to every **household** whose adult members volunteer", **not** "100 days to every adult".
xa: Eligibility: **rural** households whose **adult** members volunteer for **unskilled manual** work.
Guarantee: at least **100 days** per **financial year**.
VB-G RAM G raises it to **125 days**/household.

ne79b78b766f.s: Which provision of the Constitution is associated with the right to work that provides the Directive Principles basis for MGNREGA?
ne79b78b766f.x: MGNREGA is anchored in Article 41, which relates to the right to work, education and public assistance in certain cases.
ne79b78b766f.tq: Match the policy objective with the relevant constitutional article.
xs: MGNREGA is anchored in **Article 41** (**right to work**, DPSP) — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is **rights-based** and **demand-driven**.
xa: A **Supreme Court** bench (**21 Aug 2026**) weighed placing the right to work on par with **Article 21**.
**Olga Tellis (1985)** tied livelihood to Article 21.
MGNREGA is the **only law built on the right to work**.

n24d8b0dbd55.s: MGNREGA covers rural households whose adult members volunteer for:
n24d8b0dbd55.x: MGNREGA targets rural households volunteering for unskilled manual work, not urban skilled workers.
xa: Main objective: **enhancing livelihood security** of rural households (APPSC 2023).
NRM targets **drought, deforestation, soil erosion**.
Permissible works: **water conservation**, land development, rural connectivity.

nac789e570d8.s: Which Ministry is the nodal Ministry for MGNREGA?
o: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
nac789e570d8.x: MGNREGA is administered by the Ministry of Rural Development.
nac789e570d8.tq: Use the ministry–scheme association and avoid neighbouring ministry substitutions.
xs: MGNREGA's nodal ministry is the **Ministry of Rural Development** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Labour and Employment** runs the **National Career Service**; **Gram Sabhas** only plan, monitor and audit works.
xa: **DDU-GKY** is also under **Rural Development**.
Monitoring: **Bhuvan** (ISRO) for geo-tagging, **NREGASoft** for MIS.
Constitutional anchor: **Article 41**.

n981748f792f.s: MGNREGA wages must be paid within how many days of the work done?
n981748f792f.x: Wages are due within 15 days, delay attracts compensation, and payment is by DBT to Aadhaar-linked accounts.
xa: ⚠ **15 days** twice: wages within 15 days of work; **allowance** if no work within 15 days of application.
VB-G RAM G: wages **weekly** or within a fortnight; floor **₹300/day**.
Unions demand a **₹700** wage.

n822c13e36cb.s: The primary objective of MGNREGA is
o: Providing 100 days of employment to every adult in rural and urban areas
Enhancing livelihood security of rural households by providing at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year
Providing skill training and placement to rural youth
Providing collateral-free credit to rural self-help groups
n822c13e36cb.x: MGNREGA aims at enhancing livelihood security of rural households through at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment per financial year (APPSC 2023). The guarantee is per household, not per adult, and covers only rural areas. Skilling and placement is DDU-GKY, and SHG credit falls under NRLM.
xs: MGNREGA's objective: **enhancing livelihood security** of rural households via at least **100 days** of **guaranteed wage employment** per **financial year** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2023).
The guarantee is per **household**, not every adult, and **rural only**; skilling is **DDU-GKY**; SHG credit is **NRLM**.
xa: Other aims: **durable asset creation**, **natural resource management**, reducing **distress migration**.
Successor **VB-G RAM G** guarantees **125 days**.

nff31dead314.s: What is the minimum share of women prescribed among MGNREGA beneficiaries?
nff31dead314.x: At least one-third of MGNREGA beneficiaries must be women, although their actual share has consistently exceeded 50 per cent of person-days.
nff31dead314.tq: Distinguish the statutory minimum from the actual participation trend.
xs: At least **one-third** of MGNREGA beneficiaries must be **women** — so option **(3)** is correct.
In practice women's share is consistently **above 50%** of person-days.
xa: Unemployment allowance: at least **1/4** of wage for the first **30** days, **1/2** thereafter.
Social audit by the **Gram Sabha** is mandatory.
Scale: **200-250 crore** person-days a year.

n3bb24588edf.s: Social audit of MGNREGA works is mandatory and is conducted by:
n3bb24588edf.x: Social audit is mandatory under MGNREGA and is conducted by the Gram Sabha. Gram Sabhas also plan and monitor works.
n3bb24588edf.tq: Identify the local participatory body responsible for the function.
xs: MGNREGA **social audit** is mandatory and done by the **Gram Sabha** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Gram Sabhas also **plan and monitor** works.
xa: Geo-tagging: **Bhuvan** (**ISRO**) — GeoMGNREGA.
MIS: **NREGASoft**.
VB-G RAM G: **no contractors**; Central and State **Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Councils**.

n1c8aa49dd7d.s: If employment is not provided within 15 days of an application under MGNREGA, the unemployment allowance is at least:
o: One-fourth of the wage throughout the period
One-fourth of the wage for the first 30 days and one-half thereafter
One-half of the wage for the first 30 days and one-fourth thereafter
The full wage for the first 30 days and one-half thereafter
n1c8aa49dd7d.x: The unemployment allowance is at least one-fourth of the wage for the first 30 days and one-half thereafter.
n1c8aa49dd7d.tq: Track the change in rate after the first 30-day period.
xs: If work is not given within **15 days** of application, the allowance is at least **1/4 (one-fourth) of the wage for the first 30 days** and **1/2 (one-half) thereafter** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option 3 reverses the fractions.
xa: ⚠ **15 days** also = deadline for paying wages after the work is done.
The allowance is **retained** under **VB-G RAM G**.
Women: at least **one-third** of beneficiaries.

n8423c6f59a0.s: Which 1985 Supreme Court case linked livelihood with Article 21?
n8423c6f59a0.x: Olga Tellis (1985) linked livelihood with Article 21; MGNREGA is described as the only law built on the right to work.
xa: MGNREGA's DPSP anchor: **Article 41**.
Unions sought rollback of VB-G RAM G, **200 days** and **₹700** wage.

nbeeda1a86bf.s: With effect from 1 July 2026, which legislation replaced the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act?
o: National Food for Work Programme Act, 2004
Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025
nbeeda1a86bf.x: The Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, replaced MGNREGA and came into force on 1 July 2026.
nbeeda1a86bf.tq: Identify the exact official title in a scheme-renaming and replacement question.
xs: From **1 July 2026**, MGNREGA was replaced by the **Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025** (**VB-G RAM G**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was passed by Parliament on **18 Dec 2025**.
**Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan (2020)** was a campaign for returnee migrants; **NFFWP (2004)** was a programme, not an Act.
xa: Guarantee: **125 days**/household (operated over **305** days).
Funding **60:40** (**90:10** NE/Himalayan States, UTs).
Job cards → **Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards**.

ndbd5a9f5a8c.s: Under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, the guaranteed wage employment and the period over which the programme is operated are respectively:
ndbd5a9f5a8c.x: VB-G RAM G provides 125 days of employment per household and operates over 305 days.
ndbd5a9f5a8c.tq: Compare the paired numerical features instead of recalling either number in isolation.
xs: **VB-G RAM G** guarantees **125 days**/household, operated over **305 days** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**100 days** was the old **MGNREGA** guarantee.
xa: States may **pause** works up to **60 days** in sowing/harvest.
⚠ **125 – 60 – 9%** = guarantee days – seasonal pause – admin ceiling.
Wage floor **₹300/day**; wages paid **weekly** or within a fortnight.

nfbd36bb6c63.s: The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) is implemented by the:
nfbd36bb6c63.x: PMEGP is administered by the Ministry of MSME and implemented by the KVIC.
xa: ⚠ PM-SVANidhi = **Housing & Urban Affairs**, not MSME.
PMEGP (**2008**) = **PMRY + REGP**.
PMEGP met its target of **4.02 lakh** new micro-enterprises; **80%** rural, **40%** women.

nfcccb833a61.s: DDU-GKY, which provides placement-linked skilling to rural poor youth, has its roots in the special projects of:
nfcccb833a61.x: DDU-GKY (2014, Ministry of Rural Development) grew out of the special projects of SGSY, not PMEGP.
xa: PM Vishwakarma offers **training, toolkits, credit**.
**SGSY** is a self-employment programme.
**Recognition of Prior Learning** certifies skills against **NSQF**.

o: Long-term housing loans to rural households
Subsidised loans to traditional artisans only
Collateral-free working-capital loans to street vendors
n7ad2b91687b.x: PM-SVANidhi provides collateral-free working-capital loans to street vendors. The scheme has covered more than 75 lakh vendors.
n7ad2b91687b.tq: Use the target occupation—street vendors—to separate PM-SVANidhi from other credit schemes.
xs: **PM-SVANidhi** gives **collateral-free working-capital loans to street vendors** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It has covered **75 lakh+** vendors.
Placement-linked skilling is **DDU-GKY**; artisans are covered by **PM Vishwakarma**.
xa: ⚠ PM-SVANidhi = **Housing & Urban Affairs**, not MSME.
PMEGP supports new **non-farm micro-enterprises**.
National Career Service (**2015**): job-matching portal.

ndbf377243e6.s: Recognition of Prior Learning under PMKVY is intended to:
o: Provide working capital to street vendors
Certify existing skills against the National Skills Qualifications Framework
Provide EPF support for new formal jobs
ndbf377243e6.x: Recognition of Prior Learning certifies skills that individuals already possess against the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF).
ndbf377243e6.tq: Identify the scheme by the action it performs—assessment and certification of existing skills.
xs: **Recognition of Prior Learning** (under **PMKVY**, **2015**) **certifies existing skills** against the **NSQF** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Street-vendor capital = **PM-SVANidhi**; **125 days** = **VB-G RAM G**; **EPF** support = **ABRY**.
xa: RPL falls under **Skill Development**.
**DDU-GKY** gives placement-linked skilling to rural poor youth.
**PM Vishwakarma** covers **18** artisan trades.

nindian-society-1-54.s: India's first National Nutrition Policy was formulated in:
nindian-society-1-54.x: The Nutrition Policy came in 1993; the first Health Policy in 1983 and the Population Policy in 1976.
n: The National Health Policy was first adopted in 1983. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The National Population Policy was first adopted in 1976. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The National Nutrition Policy was first adopted in 1993. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xa: **First Five-Year Plan** (**1951–56**) = first welfare-oriented development plan.
**First Constitutional Amendment** was enacted in **1951**.
**National Social Assistance Programme** first launched in **1995**.

n2a3e0882ad4.x: The Antyodaya programme was first launched in Rajasthan in 1977.
n2a3e0882ad4.tq: Recall the launch-place and year combination.
xs: **Antyodaya** was first launched in **Rajasthan** in **1977**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**1982** belongs to **DWCRA** and **RUDSETI** (Ujire, Karnataka), and **1975** is the launch year of the **Twenty Point Programme**, not Antyodaya.
xa: **Community Development Programme** began on **2 Oct 1952**: called the "mother of social development programmes".
**TRYSEM** (Training of Rural Youth for Self Employment) began on **15 Aug 1979**.
Strategy shift: **direct-attack** (target-group) programmes replaced reliance on **trickle-down** from the **5th-6th Plans**.

n11254b3a466.s: RUDSETI, which trains rural youth for self-employment, was established in 1982 at:
n11254b3a466.x: RUDSETI was set up at Ujire in Karnataka in 1982 and became the model for the present RSETIs.
xa: RUDSETI became the **model for today's RSETIs**.
⚠ **DWCRA** (group approach for women, forerunner of women's SHGs) also began in **1982**.
**TRYSEM** (**15 Aug 1979**) was the earlier rural-youth self-employment training programme.

n1478ae9c71d.s: The change from IRDP to SGSY replaced the individual-beneficiary approach with:
n1478ae9c71d.x: IRDP followed an individual beneficiary approach, whereas SGSY adopted an SHG-based group approach.
xa: **SGSY** (**1 April 1999**) merged **IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA, SITRA, Ganga Kalyan Yojana** and the **Million Wells Scheme**.
SGSY aimed to bring assisted poor families above the poverty line by organising them into **SHGs** (APPSC 2023, 2019).
SGSY → **NRLM "Aajeevika"** (restructured 2010, launched **2011**) → **DAY-NRLM** (2016).

n687b0cef6b6.s: Which one of the following combinations consists entirely of direct-attack poverty programmes?
n687b0cef6b6.x: IRDP, NREP, RLEGP and JRY are listed as direct-attack or target-group poverty programmes.
n687b0cef6b6.tq: Identify the common programme family rather than matching only one item.
xs: **IRDP, NREP, RLEGP and JRY** are the **direct-attack** (target-group) poverty programmes, so option **(3)** is correct.
**PAISA** and **SUSV** are **DAY-NULM** components, **SVEP** is a DAY-NRLM initiative, and **RSETIs** are training institutes — not in the direct-attack list.
xa: Direct attack replaced reliance on **trickle-down** from the **5th-6th Plans**.
⚠ Odd-one-out questions slip a non-poverty programme (crop insurance, a statistics body) beside IRDP/NREP/RLEGP/JRY.

nindian-economy-34-5.s: The Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (1989) was formed by merging NREP with:
nindian-economy-34-5.x: NREP (rural employment) and RLEGP (rural landless employment) were merged into JRY in 1989.
n: NREP is associated with rural employment. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 51-52]
RLEGP is associated with rural landless employment. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 51-52]
JRY was formed through the merger of NREP and RLEGP. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 51-52]
xa: **Strategy shift:** direct-attack programmes replaced reliance on trickle-down from the **5th-6th Plans**.
**Twenty Point Programme** launched **1975**; restructured **1982**, **1986**, **2006**.
**Antyodaya** first launched in **Rajasthan** (**1977**).

n602f5f9bb6a.s: The six programmes—IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA, SITRA, Ganga Kalyan Yojana and Million Wells Scheme—were merged to form which programme on 1 April 1999?
n602f5f9bb6a.x: The six earlier programmes were merged into Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY), launched on 1 April 1999.
n602f5f9bb6a.tq: Identify the programme formed by a merger of several predecessor schemes.
xs: The six programmes were merged into **Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)** on **1 April 1999**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**NRLM** came from restructuring SGSY (2010, launched **2011**) and became **DAY-NRLM** in 2016; **RLEGP** (1983) was a separate direct-attack programme.
xa: SGSY shifted from IRDP's **individual family** approach to the **SHG/group** approach.
SGSY aimed to bring assisted poor families **above the poverty line** through SHG **group financing** (APPSC 2023, 2019).
⚠ **SGSY → NRLM** is the rural chain; **SJSRY → NULM** is the urban chain.

nc0bb05f41d6.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the restructuring and renaming sequence of SGSY?
nc0bb05f41d6.x: SGSY was restructured as NRLM, branded as Aajeevika, in 2010 and launched in 2011; it was subsequently renamed DAY-NRLM in 2016.
nc0bb05f41d6.tq: Follow the scheme-renaming chain from the original programme to its current form.
xs: **SGSY → NRLM "Aajeevika" → DAY-NRLM** is the correct chain, option **(1)**.
SGSY was restructured in **2010**, NRLM launched in **2011**, renamed **DAY-NRLM** in **2016**.
**SJSRY → NULM** is the separate **urban** chain; **IRDP** and **NREP** came before SGSY, not after it.
xa: SGSY itself (**1 April 1999**) merged IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA, SITRA, Ganga Kalyan Yojana and the Million Wells Scheme.
DAY-NRLM is run by the **Ministry of Rural Development**.
APPSC 2019 asked that SGSY is "now known as **NRLM**".

n606019c61d9.s: Under DAY-NRLM, the tier above the Village Organisation is the:
n606019c61d9.x: DAY-NRLM's three tiers are SHG, Village Organisation and Cluster-Level Federation.
xa: Scale (3 Feb 2026): **91 lakh** SHGs, **5.35 lakh** VOs, **33,558** CLFs.
**Panchasutras**: regular meetings, savings, internal lending, recoveries, books.
In AP, **Velugu** built SHG federations as **village organisations** and **mandal samakhyas**.

n843668d65d4.s: IRDP was implemented in all blocks from:
n843668d65d4.x: IRDP, combining subsidy with bank credit to lift rural families above the poverty line, covered all blocks from 2 October 1980.
xa: IRDP: **1978-79**, part of the **6th Plan** (1980).
APPSC 2025 quoted IRDP as envisaging "assistance to poor rural families to come above the poverty line".
IRDP was merged into **SGSY** on **1 April 1999**; IRDP used an **individual family** approach.

n06dc6431991.s: Which SHG-based programme of 2001 aims at the integrated empowerment of women?
n06dc6431991.x: Swayamsiddha (2001) is SHG-based; Rashtriya Mahila Kosh (1993) gives micro-credit and STEP gives skills and employment.
xa: **Swalamban** = training and employment of poor women (former **NORAD** scheme).
**NABARD** launched the **SHG-Bank Linkage Programme** as a pilot in **1992**.
SHG concept: **Prof. Muhammad Yunus**, **Grameen Bank**, Bangladesh.

n8f3651c71cb.s: The general Centre-State funding ratio under DAY-NRLM is:
n8f3651c71cb.x: The general ratio is 60:40; 90:10 applies to the North-Eastern States including Sikkim, and UTs get 100%.
xa: Structure: SHG → **Village Organisation** → **Cluster-Level Federation**.
Eligibility via **Participatory Identification of Poor (PIP)**, vetted by the **Gram Sabha**.
**Lakhpati Didi** (2023): SHG member earning **₹1 lakh+** a year; target **6 crore by March 2029**.

n094b3782abe.s: Under DAY-NRLM, up to what share of SHG members may be slightly above the poverty line?
n094b3782abe.x: Only up to 30% may be slightly above the poverty line; beneficiaries are identified by PIP and vetted by the Gram Sabha.
xa: Structure: **SHG → Village Organisation → Cluster-Level Federation**.
**Panchasutras**: regular meetings, savings, internal lending, recoveries, books.
Ministry: **Rural Development**; launched **2011**.

n809e6f7d11c.s: A ‘Lakhpati Didi’ under the relevant livelihood initiative is an SHG member who earns at least
n809e6f7d11c.x: A Lakhpati Didi is an SHG member earning ₹1 lakh or more annually.
n809e6f7d11c.tq: Distinguish the official income threshold from nearby numerical distractors.
xs: A **Lakhpati Didi** is an SHG member earning **₹1 lakh+ a year**, option **(2)**.
The initiative under DAY-NRLM began in **2023**.
xa: Lakhpati Didis crossed **2 crore** (3 Feb 2026).
Target raised to **6 crore by March 2029** (Aug 2026).
**SVEP** (2016) promotes **non-farm enterprises** for SHG households.

n4d16efe56d8.s: The Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP) under DAY-NRLM promotes:
n4d16efe56d8.x: SVEP, launched in 2016, promotes non-farm enterprises among SHG households.
xa: SVEP: **4.32 lakh** enterprises, women at least **60%** (27 Jul 2026).
**Lakhpati Didi** (2023): SHG member earning **₹1 lakh+** a year.
Other DAY-NRLM initiatives: **BC Sakhis**, **SARATHI** app, **Samaveshi Aajeevika Yojana**.

n93ab7ca53ee.s: Indira Kranthi Patham (2004-05) in Andhra Pradesh was formed by merging Velugu with:
n93ab7ca53ee.x: IKP came later by merging Velugu (2000, World Bank-aided) and DWCRA; it was not Velugu's earlier name.
xa: Velugu = AP **District Poverty Initiatives Project**, run by **SERP**.
⚠ **SAPAP** = **UNDP** (1995); **Velugu** = **World Bank** (2000).
AP's **SERP/Velugu** model was the template for **NRLM**.

n8cbfa57a509.s: Unnati is a SERP programme in Andhra Pradesh for:
n8cbfa57a509.x: Unnati targets the poorest SC/ST SHG households; Stree Nidhi gives credit to SHG members in rural and urban areas.
xa: **SERP** = Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty (**2000**).
AP urban SHG mission = **MEPMA** (established **1 Sep 2007**).

nb5d389d75e8.s: Which State's SERP/Velugu model became a template for NRLM?
nb5d389d75e8.x: AP's SERP/Velugu model became NRLM's template, and AP leads in SHG-bank linkage.
xa: AP: **36%** of national SHG-Bank Linkage share, **99.66%** recovery.
**Velugu** (**2000**) was World Bank-aided and run by **SERP**.
Grameen project began in **1976**; some notes date the SHG concept to **1975**.

n4600a49b58f.s: The National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM), launched in 2013 and later renamed DAY-NULM, replaced which earlier programme?
n4600a49b58f.x: NULM (2013) replaced the urban SJSRY of 1997 and was later renamed DAY-NULM. SGSY was the rural programme restructured into NRLM. IRDP was merged into SGSY in 1999, and PMRY was merged into PMEGP in 2008.
n4600a49b58f.tq: Rural: SGSY -> NRLM; urban: SJSRY -> NULM.
xs: **NULM** (2013) replaced the urban **Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY)** of **1997**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**SGSY** was the **rural** programme restructured into **NRLM**; **IRDP** was merged into SGSY in **1999**.
xa: ⚠ **SJSRY → NULM** = urban chain; **SGSY → NRLM** = rural chain.
NULM was renamed **DAY-NULM** under **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana**; ministry: **Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation** (now Housing & Urban Affairs).
In AP, DAY-NULM is implemented by **MEPMA** (**1 Sep 2007**).

n02957fb9b7a.s: The Ministry associated with DAY-NULM was originally known as the Ministry of
n02957fb9b7a.x: DAY-NULM was associated with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation, now the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
n02957fb9b7a.tq: Distinguish the former and current name of the urban-affairs ministry.
xs: DAY-NULM's ministry was the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation**, now Housing & Urban Affairs, option **(3)**.
**Rural Development** runs **DAY-NRLM**, not NULM.
xa: Asked in **APPSC 2023**.
NULM (2013) replaced **SJSRY** (1997).
AP implementing agency: **MEPMA** (**2007**).

o: Portal for Affordable Credit and Interest Subvention Access
Programme for Agricultural Investment and Savings Assistance
Poverty Alleviation and Income Support Authority
Public Assistance Initiative for Social Advancement
n73c4f657279.x: PAISA means Portal for Affordable Credit and Interest Subvention Access.
n73c4f657279.tq: Test the exact official expansion of a short scheme-related acronym.
xs: **PAISA** = **Portal for Affordable Credit and Interest Subvention Access**, option **(1)**.
It is a **DAY-NULM** component (APPSC 2019).
xa: Other DAY-NULM components: **SM&ID**, **SUSV** (street vendors), **SUH** (urban homeless).
Ministry: **Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation**.
AP implementing agency: **MEPMA**.

n5ac1f2b7ecd.s: The agency implementing DAY-NULM in Andhra Pradesh is
n5ac1f2b7ecd.x: MEPMA, the Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas, is the implementing agency for DAY-NULM in Andhra Pradesh.
n5ac1f2b7ecd.tq: Distinguish the urban implementing agency from the rural agency SERP.
xs: **MEPMA** implements **DAY-NULM** in Andhra Pradesh, option **(4)**.
**SERP** is AP's **rural** agency (Velugu, IKP); **NABARD** runs the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme.
xa: MEPMA = Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas, established **1 Sep 2007**.
⚠ NRLM = Rural Development ministry; NULM = Housing and Urban ministry.
**Stree Nidhi** gives timely credit to SHG members in both **rural and urban** areas.

n5a9973dee4b.s: Which one of the following is NOT a role associated with NABARD in the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme?
o: Replacing all commercial banks as direct lenders to SHGs
n5a9973dee4b.x: NABARD refinances banks and trains and promotes SHGs; it does not replace all commercial banks as direct lenders to SHGs.
n5a9973dee4b.tq: Find the institutional role that goes beyond the stated functions of the organisation.
xs: NABARD does **not replace commercial banks as direct lenders**; it **refinances banks**, so option **(2)** is the odd one.
NABARD **refinances banks**, **trains and promotes SHGs**; the SHGs then borrow from banks collateral-free.
xa: NABARD launched the linkage programme as a pilot in **1992** — the world's largest microfinance programme.
**MYRADA** pioneered bank linkage in the **mid-1980s**.
AP ranks **1st**: **36%** of national share, **99.66%** recovery.

n5d1d68292d8.s: The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme, described as the world's largest microfinance programme, was launched as a pilot in 1992 by
n5d1d68292d8.x: NABARD launched the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme as a pilot in 1992; it refinances banks and trains and promotes SHGs. MYRADA pioneered bank linkage of SHGs in the mid-1980s but did not launch the national programme. RBI is the regulator and SIDBI lends to small industries.
xs: **NABARD** launched the **SHG-Bank Linkage Programme** as a pilot in **1992**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**MYRADA** pioneered bank linkage in the **mid-1980s** but did not launch the national programme.
xa: NABARD **refinances banks** and **trains and promotes SHGs**.
NABARD popularised SHGs in the **1980s**; SHGs became a formal tool in the **7th Plan (1985-90)**.
AP is **1st** in SHG-Bank Linkage with **36%** of the national share.

nad4d5363b5c.s: Indira Kranthi Patham was formed through the merger of:
nad4d5363b5c.x: Indira Kranthi Patham was formed in 2004-05 by merging Velugu and DWCRA and was implemented by SERP.
nad4d5363b5c.tq: Identify the merger partners rather than the implementing agency.
xs: **Indira Kranthi Patham** (2004-05) was formed by merging **Velugu and DWCRA**, option **(3)**.
It was implemented by **SERP**; **MEPMA** is the separate urban mission.
xa: **Velugu** (2000): World Bank-aided District Poverty Initiatives Project.
**Pavala Vaddi** (2004): interest subsidy for SHGs.
**SAPAP** (1995, UNDP): **Mahabubnagar**, **Kurnool**, **Anantapur**.

nfd34d912b9e.s: Pavala Vaddi, an interest subsidy for SHGs in Andhra Pradesh, was introduced in:
nfd34d912b9e.x: Pavala Vaddi came in 2004; Vaddi Leni Runalu rewards prompt (not delayed) repayment.
xa: **Stree Nidhi** gives timely credit to SHG members in **rural and urban** areas.
AP ranks **1st** in **SHG-Bank Linkage**: **36%** of national share, **99.66%** recovery.
**Indira Kranthi Patham** (2004-05) = **Velugu and DWCRA merged**, implemented by **SERP**.

na488e80d83b.s: SERP, associated with the Self-Help Group movement in Andhra Pradesh, stands for:
o: Society for Economic Reform and Planning
Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty
na488e80d83b.x: SERP stands for Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty. It is a registered society of the Andhra Pradesh Government established in 2000.
na488e80d83b.tq: Test the exact expansion of a commonly confused acronym.
xs: **SERP** = **Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty**, option **(3)**.
It is a **registered society** of the AP government set up in **2000**.
xa: SERP runs **Velugu** and **Indira Kranthi Patham**.
**Unnati**: SERP programme for the poorest **SC/ST** SHG households.
⚠ Rural = **SERP**; urban = **MEPMA**.

n3c9b317a372.s: The South Asia Poverty Alleviation Programme (SAPAP) in Andhra Pradesh, begun in 1995, was supported by:
n3c9b317a372.x: SAPAP was UNDP-supported in Mahabubnagar, Kurnool and Anantapur; the World Bank aided Velugu (2000).
xa: **SERP** followed in **2000**.
**Indira Kranthi Patham** (2004-05) merged Velugu and DWCRA.
AP leads SHG-Bank Linkage: **36%** of national share, **99.66%** recovery.

n81c507f2d1c.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or challenge relating to the SHG movement?
o: Debt stress caused by poor financial literacy
n81c507f2d1c.x: Uneven SHG quality, weak market links, debt stress due to poor financial literacy and political interference are identified challenges. An absence of political interference is not a criticism.
n81c507f2d1c.tq: Select the option that reverses a stated challenge.
xs: **Absence of political interference** is not a criticism — the notes list **political interference** itself as a problem, so option **(4)** is the answer.
Listed criticisms: **uneven SHG quality**, **weak market links**, **debt stress from poor financial literacy**, **political interference**.
xa: Significance: multidimensional poverty fell **29.17%** to **11.28%**, about **25 crore** people.
DAY-NRLM NPA is ~**1.7%** on **₹11 lakh crore+** of bank credit.
AP SHGs use **Amazon** and **Flipkart** to address marketing.

n2c3e13a7367.s: Which combination best represents the reported position of Andhra Pradesh in SHG–bank linkage?
o: Third rank, 36% of the national share and 90% recovery
First rank, 10% of the national share and 80% recovery
First rank, 36% of the national share and about 99.66% recovery
Second rank, 18% of the national share and 75% recovery
n2c3e13a7367.x: Andhra Pradesh is reported as ranking first in SHG–bank linkage, with 36% of the national share and about 99.66% recovery.
n2c3e13a7367.tq: Combine rank, percentage share and recovery figures without reversing the comparison.
xs: AP ranks **first** in SHG-Bank Linkage with **36%** of the national share and **99.66% recovery**, option **(3)**.
Every other option misstates the rank, the share or the recovery rate.
xa: About **₹32,190 crore** average disbursement in rural areas (2024-25); **10 lakh+** SHGs.
The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme was launched by **NABARD** as a pilot in **1992**.
⚠ **SAPAP** = **UNDP** (1995); **Velugu** = **World Bank** (2000).

n93a1260eaa7.s: The overdraft facility under PMJDY has been raised to:
n93a1260eaa7.x: Overdraft rose from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000, and RuPay accident cover from ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh.
xa: After **14 Aug 2018** the focus moved from "every household" to "**every unbanked adult**".
PMJDY accounts: **59.09 crore** (19 Aug 2026); scheme completed **12 years** (Aug 2026).
Women hold **32.92 crore** accounts.

n8841b5130b4.s: After 14 August 2018, the focus of the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana shifted from:
o: Rural households to urban households only
Every unbanked adult to every household
Every household to every unbanked adult
n8841b5130b4.x: The focus changed from covering every household to covering every unbanked adult.
n8841b5130b4.tq: Test the direction of change in a policy target rather than merely recalling both terms.
xs: After **14 Aug 2018**, PMJDY moved from "**every household**" to "**every unbanked adult**", option **(3)**.
Option **(2)** reverses the direction of the shift.
xa: PMJDY was launched on **28 Aug 2014**.
The same 2018 revision raised accident cover to **₹2 lakh** and overdraft to **₹10,000**.
Rural/semi-urban accounts: **45.95 crore** of **59.09 crore**.

n49424d7499a.s: In Phase II of PMJDY (2015-2018), unorganised-sector pensions were provided under:
n49424d7499a.x: Phase II added overdraft, a Credit Guarantee Fund for overdraft defaults and Swavalamban pensions.
xa: Overdraft limit: **₹10,000** (from **₹5,000**).
Implementing body: **Department of Financial Services**.

n6cc47f73edd.s: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was launched on 28 August 2014 and is implemented by the
n6cc47f73edd.x: PMJDY was launched on 28 August 2014 and is implemented by the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance. The Department of Economic Affairs, the RBI and NABARD are not its implementing agency.
xs: PMJDY (launched **28 Aug 2014**) is implemented by the **Department of Financial Services**, option **(2)**.
DFS also administers **PMJJBY** and **PMSBY** (Ministry of Finance).
xa: PMJDY accounts are the "**J**" of the **JAM** trinity — destination for funds.
**PMJJBY**/**PMSBY** premiums are **auto-debited** from PMJDY accounts.
⚠ **NABARD** is linked to SHG-bank linkage, not PMJDY.

n7604a7e39be.s: Which of the following is a recognised challenge of Aadhaar-enabled service delivery?
o: Exclusion due to biometric authentication failure
Easier authentication for those with worn fingerprints
n7604a7e39be.x: Biometric failure can exclude the elderly and labourers with worn fingerprints, and centralised data raises privacy concerns.
xa: **Puttaswamy I** (**2017**) made privacy a fundamental right under **Art. 21**.
**Puttaswamy II** (**2018**) struck down private use (**Sec 57**).
Kerala's DBT-over-doorstep pension move raised elderly-delivery concerns (Aug 2026).

n9ffed27f0c7.s: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) provides cover for:
n9ffed27f0c7.x: PMSBY covers accidental death and disability; death from any cause is covered by PMJJBY.
xa: Enrolments reached **58.09 crore+** by Apr 2026.
Premium **₹20**/yr since **1 June 2022**.

n6402f46d9ab.s: The National Social Assistance Programme was launched in 1995 under the:
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
n6402f46d9ab.x: NSAP was launched in 1995 under the Ministry of Rural Development.
n6402f46d9ab.tq: Use the implementing ministry as the identifying feature of the programme.
xs: **NSAP** was launched on **15 Aug 1995** under the **Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD)**, option **(4)**.
It is a **Centrally Sponsored** scheme for **BPL** households.
xa: Aim: **old age pension to the very poor** (UPPSC 2008).
Fulfils **Article 41**; **Core of Core** scheme since **2016**.
⚠ The **National Maternity Benefit Scheme** left NSAP for **MoHFW** in **2001**.

nc328bc67adf.s: The JAM trinity was first proposed in—
nc328bc67adf.x: The JAM trinity was first proposed in the Economic Survey 2014–15.
nc328bc67adf.tq: Distinguish the proposal year from the later DBT scale-up year.
xs: The **JAM trinity** was first proposed in **Economic Survey 2014-15**, option **(1)**.
JAM = **Jan Dhan** (account), **Aadhaar** (identity), **Mobile** (communication).
xa: First application: **PAHAL** (DBT for LPG), national launch **1 Jan 2015**.
DBT was piloted on **1 January 2013** and scaled up with JAM in **2015**.
PMJDY itself started on **28 Aug 2014**.

n5169aa72483.s: PAHAL, the DBT scheme for LPG, was launched nationally on—
n5169aa72483.x: PAHAL was launched nationally on 1 January 2015 and became the first application of JAM for LPG subsidy transfer.
n5169aa72483.tq: Discriminate between the DBT pilot date, PAHAL date and Ujjwala date.
xs: **PAHAL** (DBT for LPG) was launched nationally on **1 January 2015**, option **(2)**.
**1 May 2016** is **Ujjwala**; **1 January 2013** is the **DBT pilot**.
xa: PAHAL was the **first application of JAM**: LPG subsidy paid into accounts.
⚠ **PAHAL** = subsidy DBT (**2015**); **Ujjwala** = free LPG connections (**2016**, **Ballia**).
JAM was proposed in **Economic Survey 2014-15**.

nfbbb3552751.s: Ujjwala provides free LPG connections, to reduce indoor air pollution, to:
nfbbb3552751.x: Ujjwala gives free LPG connections to women of BPL households to reduce indoor air pollution.
xa: Launched **1 May 2016** at **Ballia**.
⚠ **PAHAL** (**2015**) = DBT of LPG **subsidy**; Ujjwala (**2016**) = LPG **connections**.
PAHAL was the first application of **JAM**.

nf3ef33c97db.s: Jeevan Pramaan, launched in 2014, enables pensioners to:
o: Create a digital life certificate using Aadhaar biometrics
nf3ef33c97db.x: Jeevan Pramaan (2014) lets pensioners create a digital life certificate using Aadhaar biometrics.
xa: Asked in **APPSC 2024**.
NSAP also uses a **Digital Life Certificate** app and the **SAMBAL** app.
Aadhaar risk: **biometric failure** for elderly with worn fingerprints.

nd31f46e43a8.s: The controversy in Kerala regarding pension delivery primarily concerned the choice between:
o: Bank accounts and postal savings certificates
DBT and doorstep delivery for elderly beneficiaries
nd31f46e43a8.x: Kerala’s decision to end doorstep pension delivery for DBT led to protests, highlighting the tension between digital transfers and doorstep delivery for the elderly.
nd31f46e43a8.tq: Identify the two alternative delivery mechanisms at the centre of the policy debate.
xs: **Kerala**'s move to end **doorstep pension delivery** in favour of **DBT** drew protests (8 and 11 Aug 2026): the debate is **DBT vs doorstep delivery for elderly**, option **(4)**.
It is not about private insurance, foodgrains or postal certificates — only the **delivery channel** for pensions.
xa: DBT in **FY 2024-25**: **₹6.9 lakh crore** across **327 schemes**.
Aadhaar risk: **biometric failure** for elderly with worn fingerprints.
**Jeevan Pramaan** (**2014**) lets pensioners give a **digital life certificate**.

n301a4f66632.s: The DBT pilot launched on 1 January 2013 covered:
n301a4f66632.x: The pilot covered 7 schemes in 20 districts; DBT was scaled up in 2015 using JAM.
xa: **FY 2024-25**: **₹6.9 lakh crore** across **327 schemes**.
Estimated savings **₹2-3 lakh crore** from removing ghost/duplicate beneficiaries.
Routing via **APBS** + **AePS**.

nfb75a927e48.s: Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016 permits Aadhaar to be made a condition for receiving—
o: Subsidies from the Consolidated Fund of India
nfb75a927e48.x: Section 7 of the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016 permits Aadhaar to be required for subsidies charged to the Consolidated Fund.
nfb75a927e48.tq: Use the exact statutory section and its limited welfare-related scope.
xs: **Sec 7** of the **Aadhaar Act, 2016** makes Aadhaar a condition for subsidies from the **Consolidated Fund**, option **(3)**.
Private use was under **Sec 57**, which **Puttaswamy II** (2018) struck down.
xa: Full name: Aadhaar (**Targeted Delivery** of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act.
**Puttaswamy II** (**2018**, **5 judges**, **4:1**) upheld Sec 7.
**Puttaswamy I** (**2017**, **9 judges**): privacy a fundamental right under **Art. 21**.

nd303e6307d3.s: In the 2017 Puttaswamy judgement, privacy was held to be a fundamental right under Article 21 by a Bench of:
nd303e6307d3.x: A nine-judge Bench decided in 2017; a five-judge Bench upheld Aadhaar for welfare in 2018.
xa: The 2018 verdict was **4:1**.
⚠ Trap: **9** judges = privacy (2017); **5** judges = Aadhaar (2018).
Aadhaar Act: **2016**.

n43a927a593d.s: The eShram portal creates a national database of unorganised workers and provides each worker with a:
n43a927a593d.x: The eShram portal is the National Database of Unorganised Workers and provides a Universal Account Number (UAN).
n43a927a593d.tq: Match the portal with its distinctive identification number.
xs: The **eShram** portal gives each unorganised worker a **Universal Account Number (UAN)**, option **(3)**.
eShram (**26 Aug 2021**) is the **National Database of Unorganised Workers**.
xa: **Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act** (**2008**) is now in the **Code on Social Security, 2020**.
The **4** labour codes replaced **29** laws.
Social protection coverage: **64.3%** in **2025** (from **22%** in **2016**).

nfe756d0d119.s: The four labour codes together replaced how many labour laws?
nfe756d0d119.x: The four codes replaced 29 laws; the 2008 Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act is subsumed in the Code on Social Security, 2020.
xa: **eShram** (**26 Aug 2021**) issues a **UAN** to unorganised workers.
**EPF & MP Act** (**1952**) covers establishments with **20 or more** employees.

n240d4acc33b.s: The National Social Assistance Programme fulfils the directive contained in Article ____ of the Constitution.
n240d4acc33b.x: NSAP, a Centrally Sponsored Core of Core scheme for BPL households, fulfils Article 41.
xa: Launched **15 Aug 1995** under **MoRD**.
Scale: about **3.09 crore** beneficiaries; **₹9,652 crore** for **FY 2025-26**.
States add a top-up of **₹50-3,200/month**.

n9e822fe99af.s: Under PMSBY, the cover for accidental death or total disability is:
n9e822fe99af.x: PMSBY gives ₹2 lakh for accidental death or total disability and ₹1 lakh for partial disability.
xa: Enrolments: **58.09 crore+** (to Apr 2026).
Both PMSBY and PMJJBY launched on **9 May 2015**.

nc87b05fcdf4.s: Which of the following correctly represents the age band, annual premium and life cover under PMJJBY?
nc87b05fcdf4.x: PMJJBY is a life insurance scheme for persons aged 18–50 years, with an annual premium of ₹436 and cover of ₹2 lakh.
nc87b05fcdf4.tq: Separate PMJJBY from PMSBY by comparing type, age, premium and cover.
xs: **PMJJBY**: age **18-50**, premium **₹436**/yr, cover **₹2 lakh** — option **(2)**.
**₹20** and **18-70** belong to **PMSBY**; **18-59** is Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana.
xa: PMJJBY is a **1-year renewable** life cover; claim settlement **99.95%**.
Enrolments: **27.43 crore+** (to Apr 2026).

n26a3bdcc115.s: Atal Pension Yojana, launched on 9 May 2015, primarily targets which category of persons?
o: Small and marginal farmers between 40 and 60 years
Unorganised-sector workers in the age group of 18–40 years
n26a3bdcc115.x: Atal Pension Yojana targets workers in the unorganised sector who enter the scheme between 18 and 40 years of age.
n26a3bdcc115.tq: Directly identify the target group and entry age of the scheme.
xs: **Atal Pension Yojana** (**9 May 2015**) targets **unorganised-sector workers** aged **18-40**, option **(4)**.
Small and marginal farmers are **PM-KMY**; Central Govt employees are under **NPS/UPS**.
xa: Income-tax payers are excluded.
Administered by **PFRDA**; **8.96 crore** subscribers.

n73dbdb41cb0.s: PM Shram Yogi Maan-dhan covers unorganised workers aged 18-40 with monthly income up to:
n73dbdb41cb0.x: The income limit is ₹15,000; persons covered under NPS, ESIC or EPFO are excluded.
xa: Income-tax payers are also excluded.
Worker + **equal matching** Central share.
Pension **₹3,000**/month at **60**.

n180282b5852.s: PM Kisan Maan-dhan provides small and marginal farmers a monthly pension at age 60 of:
n180282b5852.x: PM-KMY gives ₹3,000 a month at 60; ₹1,000-5,000 is the APY range.
xa: Contribution range asked in **APPSC 2019**.
**PM-SYM** gives the same **₹3,000** pension to unorganised workers.

n1c247cdfe12.s: The Unified Pension Scheme assures a pension of what share of average basic pay of the last 12 months for 25 years of service?
n1c247cdfe12.x: UPS assures 50% of average basic pay of the last 12 months; unlike NPS it is Government-backed.
xa: UPS was launched in **2025**.
NPS is compulsory for Central Govt civilian employees joining on or after **1 Jan 2004**.

n024ae85b581.s: The regulator of the National Pension System and the authority administering Atal Pension Yojana under the NPS architecture is—
n024ae85b581.x: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) regulates NPS and administers APY under the NPS architecture.
n024ae85b581.tq: Apply the ‘who regulates this financial product?’ method.
xs: **PFRDA** regulates **NPS** and administers **APY** under the NPS architecture, option **(3)**.
NPS is compulsory for Central Govt civilian employees joining on or after **1 Jan 2004**.
xa: NPS subscribers grew at **9.5% CAGR**; AUM at **37.3% CAGR** (**FY15-FY25**).
NPS also covers **OCIs**; minors via **NPS Vatsalya**.
APY: **8.96 crore** subscribers; a **Central Sector Scheme**.

nfc68c646017.s: The National Pension System became compulsory for Central Government civilian employees joining on or after—
nfc68c646017.x: NPS is compulsory for Central Government civilian employees who joined service on or after 1 January 2004.
nfc68c646017.tq: Distinguish the exact commencement date from nearby policy dates.
xs: NPS is compulsory for **Central Govt civilian employees joining on or after 1 January 2004**, option **(4)**.
Regulator: **PFRDA**.
xa: NPS is **defined contribution**, market-linked: corpus + annuity.
**UPS** (**2025**) is an assured-pension option for NPS employees.
⚠ Trap: an NPS account **cannot be opened for a third person** (APPSC 2024).

n91c0696d10a.s: A major criticism of the NSAP old-age pension is that inflation has eroded about ____ of its real value.
n91c0696d10a.x: Inflation has eroded nearly half of the real value of the NSAP old-age pension.
xa: States top up by **₹50-3,200/month**.
Old-age share is to rise **10.1% to 14.9%** (**2021-2036**) — more pension demand.
**Kerala**'s DBT move for pensions drew protests (Aug 2026).

n566138edf8a.s: According to the World Food Summit, 1996, food security exists when all people, at all times, have physical and economic access to which of the following?
o: Food of their choice irrespective of dietary needs
Adequate food supplied exclusively by the government
Sufficient, safe and nutritious food for an active and healthy life
Food grains available only during periods of shortage
n566138edf8a.x: The World Food Summit definition emphasizes physical and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food for an active and healthy life.
n566138edf8a.tq: Use the precise official definition and reject the look-alike phrase ‘food of their choice’.
xs: Per the **World Food Summit 1996** (FAO), food security means access to **sufficient, safe and nutritious food** for an **active and healthy life**, option **(3)**.
⚠ It does **not** mean food "**of their choice**" — a trap set in **APPSC G2 2017**; nor does it require supply only by government.
xa: The definition says **all people, at all times**, with **physical and economic access**.
Four dimensions: **availability, access (affordability), utilisation/absorption, stability**.
India achieved **national** food security (buffer stocks) without fully assuring **household** food security — hence **PDS** and **NFSA**.

n9bd8ff01055.s: Which one of the following is NOT a recognized dimension of food security?
n9bd8ff01055.x: Availability, accessibility, affordability or access, utilisation/absorption and stability are associated with food security. Accountability is not a dimension.
n9bd8ff01055.tq: Find the odd term among the established dimensions.
xs: **Accountability** is **not** a dimension of food security, option **(2)** (UPPSC 2025 trap).
**Stability**, **accessibility** and **availability** are recognised dimensions, along with **affordability** and **absorption/utilisation**.
xa: **Availability** = production + imports + previous stocks.
**Absorption/utilisation** = the body's ability to use the food.
Price and quantity of exports are also **not** dimensions.

n03ad716f3ea.s: According to Amartya Sen's entitlement approach, famines primarily arise from:
o: A fall in aggregate food production in every case
An increase in the nutritional content of food
Excessive buffer stocks maintained by the government
A collapse of people's command over food through income, exchange and transfers
n03ad716f3ea.x: Sen argued that famine results from a collapse of people's entitlements or command over food, not merely from a decline in overall food availability.
n03ad716f3ea.tq: Reject the supply-only explanation and apply the income-and-entitlement concept.
xs: For **Sen**, famines arise from a **collapse of people's command over food through income, exchange and transfers** (entitlements), option **(4)**.
He rejected the view that a **fall in food availability/supply** alone causes famine.
xa: Book: **Poverty and Famines**, **1981**.
⚠ Sen = **entitlement**, not availability.
The **Bengal Famine of 1943** (about **30 lakh** deaths) is the classic backdrop.

n44fb1f23486.s: Which of the following best distinguishes national food security from household food security?
o: National food security concerns only imports, whereas household food security concerns only domestic production.
National food security concerns aggregate availability, whereas household food security concerns actual access and affordability for each household.
National food security applies to urban areas, whereas household food security applies only to rural areas.
National food security is based on nutrition, whereas household food security is based only on buffer stocks.
n44fb1f23486.x: National food security refers to adequate aggregate production and stocks. Household food security requires that each household can actually obtain and afford food.
n44fb1f23486.tq: Split the comparison into aggregate availability versus household-level access.
xs: **National** food security = **aggregate production/availability + buffer stock**; **household** = each household can **access and afford** food — option **(2)**.
Neither is defined by urban/rural or by imports alone.
xa: India achieved national food security without fully assuring household — hence **PDS** and **NFSA**.
**Affordability** = money enough for sufficient, safe, nutritious food.
**Accessibility** = food within reach of every person.

n6a0da54e743.s: India's strategic foodgrain reserve is about how much above operational stocks?
n6a0da54e743.x: The strategic reserve is 5 million tonnes above operational stocks.
xa: Grain is sold at the lower **issue price** in deficit areas and calamities.
⚠ Norms fixed by **CCEA**; MSP by **CACP**; procurement by **FCI**.

n610cc6ac083.s: Which body fixes the minimum buffer stock levels for each quarter?
o: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
n610cc6ac083.x: The minimum buffer stock levels are fixed by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs and specified for each quarter.
n610cc6ac083.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the authority.
xs: Minimum buffer levels are fixed by the **Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA)**, option **(2)**.
They are set for each quarter: **1 April, 1 July, 1 October, 1 January**.
xa: ⚠ **CACP** advises MSP; **FCI** procures; **CCEA** sets norms.
Stocks: about **602 LMT**, around **3 times** the norms.
**OMSS** lets FCI sell surplus grain in the open market.

n58fe93dc171.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the entitlement of an Antyodaya Anna Yojana household under the NFSA?
o: 7 kg per person without any household ceiling
n58fe93dc171.x: An AAY household is entitled to 35 kg of foodgrains per household per month under the NFSA framework.
n58fe93dc171.tq: Watch the distinction between person-based and household-based quantities.
xs: An **AAY** household gets **35 kg per household per month**, option **(4)**.
**5 kg per person** is the **PHH** entitlement; **7 kg per person** is the 2026 draft proposal — and that keeps a **35 kg** cap.
xa: ⚠ PHH = **per person**; AAY = **per household**.
AAY grain is now **free** under **PMGKAY**.
AP: AAY **35 kg/card**, free.

n5d75f84d02c.s: Under the NFSA, pregnant women and lactating mothers are entitled to a free meal and a maternity benefit of at least:
n5d75f84d02c.x: NFSA gives pregnant women and lactating mothers a free meal and a maternity benefit of at least ₹6,000.
xa: ⚠ **Sec 4** = maternity; **Sec 15** = DGRO; **Sec 16** = State Food Commission.
Children **6 months - 6 years**: take-home ration or hot meal through **ICDS/Anganwadi**.
Children **6-14**: mid-day meal in school.

ndc78fb01a38.s: Children in the age group of 6 months to 6 years are entitled under the NFSA to:
o: A take-home ration or hot meal through ICDS/anganwadi services
Only a school meal under PM POSHAN
ndc78fb01a38.x: Children aged 6 months to 6 years receive a take-home ration or hot meal through ICDS and anganwadi services.
ndc78fb01a38.tq: Separate the NFSA entitlement by age group and delivery channel.
xs: Children **6 months - 6 years** get a **take-home ration or hot meal** through **ICDS/Anganwadi**, option **(1)**.
School meals (**PM POSHAN**) are for ages **6-14**; grain as wages is **Food-for-Work**.
xa: ICDS began in **1975**.
Mothers get a free meal + at least **₹6,000** maternity benefit.
AP is exploring **convergence with Anganwadi and MDM**.

n90f7a3b3d3a.s: Under NFSA, a Priority Household is entitled to:
o: 35 kg per household per month free of cost in all cases
7 kg per household per month at the market price
10 kg per person per month at a uniform price of ₹5
5 kg per person per month at ₹3/₹2/₹1 for rice, wheat and coarse grain respectively
n90f7a3b3d3a.x: PHH entitlement is 5 kg per person per month. The issue prices are ₹3 for rice, ₹2 for wheat and ₹1 for coarse grain.
n90f7a3b3d3a.tq: Keep the unit, quantity and commodity-wise prices together to avoid mixing NFSA and AAY provisions.
xs: A **PHH** gets **5 kg per person per month** at **Rs 3 rice / Rs 2 wheat / Rs 1 coarse grains**, option **(4)**.
**35 kg per household** is **AAY**; **7 kg** is the 2026 draft AAY proposal.
xa: Issue prices **3/2/1** have **not been revised since July 2013**.
Now all NFSA grain is **free** (PMGKAY merger, **1 January 2023**).
AP: PHH **5 kg/unit** rice, free; wheat **1 kg/card** at **Rs 16/kg**.

n23b05df32a9.s: Under the NFSA, the District Grievance Redressal Officer is provided under Section:
n23b05df32a9.x: Section 15 provides the DGRO; State Food Commissions monitor implementation and hear appeals.
xa: One DGRO in each district.
Transparency: **Vigilance Committees**, **social audits**, disclosure of PDS records.

n3d131198470.s: Under the NFSA, which body is provided in each State, though an existing commission may be designated for it?
n3d131198470.x: Each State has a State Food Commission, and an existing body may be designated to avoid new costs.
xa: DGRO is under **Sec 15**; one in each district.
⚠ **Sec 4** = maternity benefit.

n097dbf9e1b3.s:
Which of the following strengthen transparency and accountability in the PDS under the NFSA framework?
1. Social audits
2. Mandatory disclosure of PDS records
3. Vigilance committees
n097dbf9e1b3.x: Social audits, mandatory disclosure of PDS records and vigilance committees are all accountability mechanisms under the NFSA.
xa: Vigilance Committees: **state, district, block and FPS** levels.
**DGRO** (Sec 15) and **State Food Commission** (Sec 16) handle grievances.
AP: **98%** Aadhaar-linked ration cards.
