n64ad1c6911d.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh PDS, an Antyodaya Anna Yojana household receives free rice of:
n64ad1c6911d.x: AAY households get 35 kg per card; Priority Households get 5 kg per unit.
xa: **Ragi** (all) / **Jowar** (Rayalaseema): up to **3 kg/card**, free, in lieu of rice.
Under NFSA the Act price was **Rs 3/2/1**, unrevised since **July 2013**; all NFSA grain is free since **1 January 2023**.

n6afa41605f9.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh PDS, ragi (all areas) and jowar (Rayalaseema) may be supplied free of cost in lieu of rice up to:
n6afa41605f9.x: Ragi in all areas and jowar in Rayalaseema may be supplied up to 3 kg per card free of cost in lieu of rice.
xa: PHH: **5 kg/unit** rice, free.
AP is exploring a wider basket: **pulses, oil, fortified foods**.
Doorstep delivery via **Mobile Dispensing Units** (launched **2021**).

nc741b0991a5.s: The National Food Security Act commenced in:
nc741b0991a5.x: NFSA commenced in July 2013; 'NFSA 2014' is a known distractor.
xa: Coverage: up to **75% rural** + **50% urban** ≈ **two-thirds**.
~**80-81 crore** beneficiaries.

nbdc721d84ae.s: The combined NFSA coverage of up to 75 per cent of the rural population and 50 per cent of the urban population is approximately equal to:
nbdc721d84ae.x: The prescribed rural and urban coverage together amount to approximately two-thirds, or about 67 per cent, of India’s population.
nbdc721d84ae.tq: Translate separate coverage percentages into the broad national proportion.
xs: **75% rural + 50% urban** comes to about **two-thirds (≈67%)** of India's population, option **(3)**.
It is neither the whole population nor one-half.
xa: ~**80-81 crore** beneficiaries.
⚠ Exam angle: rural answer **75%**, urban **50%**.
NFSA is administered by **DFPD**.

n6a34f089910.s: For the purpose of issuing a ration card under the NFSA, the head of the household should ordinarily be:
o: The eldest male member irrespective of age
The person holding the Aadhaar card with the highest income
The eldest woman who is at least 18 years old
n6a34f089910.x: The eldest woman of the household, provided she is 18 years or older, is treated as the head for issuing the ration card.
n6a34f089910.tq: Apply the women-empowerment provision precisely, including the minimum age condition.
xs: The **eldest woman (18+)** is head of household for ration cards under NFSA, option **(4)**.
This is NFSA's **women empowerment** provision.
xa: Maternity benefit (**Sec 4**): free meal + at least **₹6,000**.
PHH: **5 kg per person per month**; AAY: **35 kg per household**.
Ration card and FPS operations follow the **TPDS (Control) Order 2015**.

n8a7c1814ef5.s: The draft National Food Security (Amendment) Bill, 2026 proposes to replace the AAY household entitlement with:
o: 7 kg per person, subject to an overall ceiling of 35 kg per household
35 kg per person, subject to an overall ceiling of 70 kg per household
10 kg per household, subject to a ceiling of 50 kg
5 kg per person, without a household ceiling
n8a7c1814ef5.x: The draft Bill proposes 7 kg per person for AAY households, while retaining an overall cap of 35 kg per household.
n8a7c1814ef5.tq: Read both parts of the proposed formula: the per-person figure and the household cap.
xs: The **draft NFS (Amendment) Bill, 2026** proposes **7 kg per person**, capped at **35 kg per household**, for AAY — option **(1)**.
It amends the first proviso to **Section 3(1)**.
xa: Released by **DFPD**, published **24 June 2026**; comments till **13 July**.
Aim: end the inequity where **small households get more per head**.
Opposed by **Tamil Nadu**, **Kerala** and **CPI(M)**.

na295c3a1bc1.s: The proposed amendment to the AAY entitlement is intended principally to address which issue?
o: The inequity whereby smaller households receive more foodgrains per head
The shortage of Aadhaar-seeded ration cards
The lack of portability between States
The rising economic cost of foodgrain procurement
na295c3a1bc1.x: The stated aim is to remove the inequity under which smaller AAY households receive a greater quantity per person when the entitlement is fixed per household.
na295c3a1bc1.tq: Identify the policy rationale rather than confusing it with digitisation, portability or procurement issues.
xs: The amendment aims to remove the inequity whereby **smaller households get more per head**, option **(1)**.
A fixed **35 kg per household** gives a small family more grain per person.
xa: New rule: **7 kg per person**, capped at **35 kg**.
Opposed by **Tamil Nadu**, **Kerala** and **CPI(M)** (10 Jul 2026).
Draft published **24 June 2026** by **DFPD**.

nca9bddf0f3d.s: Under the National Food Security Act, 2013, up to what percentage of the rural population is covered for subsidised foodgrains?
nca9bddf0f3d.x: NFSA covers up to 75% of the rural population (asked in APPSC G2 2017). 50% is the urban ceiling, about 67% (two-thirds) is the combined national coverage, and 90% is not a ceiling under the Act.
xs: NFSA covers up to **75 per cent** of the **rural** population, option **(3)** (APPSC G2 2017).
**50%** is the urban ceiling; **67%** (two-thirds) is the combined coverage.
xa: ~**80-81 crore** beneficiaries.
Ministry: Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution (**DFPD**).
Legal right commenced **July 2013**.

n8f1871d3a65.s: Buffer stocks in India were formally introduced during the:
n8f1871d3a65.x: Buffer stocks were formally introduced during the Fourth Five-Year Plan, covering 1969–74.
n8f1871d3a65.tq: Link the policy innovation with its Five-Year Plan period.
xs: Buffer stocks were formally introduced in the **Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-74)**, option **(3)**.
The earlier and later Plans are not linked to buffer stocks in the notes.
xa: Minimum buffer norms are fixed by the **CCEA** for each quarter.
**Strategic reserve**: **5 million tonnes** above operational stocks.
**PDS** is older — a **World War II rationing** measure of the 1940s.

na8d3cebee14.s: The Public Distribution System in India originated primarily as:
o: A World War II rationing measure
A replacement for the Integrated Child Development Services
na8d3cebee14.x: The PDS began as a rationing measure during the Second World War, against the background of the Bengal famine.
na8d3cebee14.tq: Use the historical origin rather than the later institutional form of the programme.
xs: PDS began as a **World War II rationing** measure in the 1940s, option **(1)**.
The **Bengal famine** (**1943**) was its backdrop.
xa: The **Essential Commodities Act 1955** is the base for PDS control orders.
**ICDS** (**1975**) is a separate nutrition scheme, not a PDS replacement.

nef18d930419.s: From 1 January 2023, PMGKAY was subsumed with the NFSA entitlement. What was the principal effect of this decision?
o: The entitlement was converted into a cash transfer
NFSA allocations were discontinued for all beneficiaries
The entire NFSA allocation became free of cost
Only the APL category received free grain
nef18d930419.x: From 1 January 2023, the entire NFSA allocation became free under the merged arrangement described as ‘One Nation–One Price–One Ration’.
nef18d930419.tq: Test the policy change after merger rather than the original launch feature.
xs: From **1 January 2023** the **entire NFSA allocation became free**, option **(3)** ("One Nation-One Price-One Ration").
It was not converted to cash and allocations continued.
xa: Extension: **1 Jan 2024 – 31 Dec 2028**, about **Rs 11.80 lakh crore**.
Issue prices **Rs 3/2/1** were never revised since **July 2013**.
Food subsidy (Budget **2026-27**): **Rs 2,27,629 crore**.

n5bada225ceb.s: The Targeted Public Distribution System was introduced in:
n5bada225ceb.x: TPDS came in June 1997, after RPDS (June 1992) and before NFSA (2013).
xa: Next: **PMGKAY 2020** → free NFSA grain from **2023**.
PDS began as a **World War II rationing** measure.
NFSA commenced in **July 2013**.

n90bb8030e7e.s: Bharat-brand atta, rice and dal are sold through which combination of channels as a consumer price intervention?
o: Only State Food Commissions and Fair Price Shops
Only private supermarkets licensed by NITI Aayog
NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar outlets and mobile vans
FCI warehouses and commercial banks only
n90bb8030e7e.x: Bharat-brand atta, rice and dal are sold at subsidised retail prices through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar outlets, as well as mobile vans.
n90bb8030e7e.tq: Match the intervention with its complete distribution-channel combination.
xs: **Bharat brand** atta, rice and dal are sold through **NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar** outlets and **mobile vans**, option **(3)**.
It is a **consumer price intervention**, outside Fair Price Shops.
xa: **NCCF**: set up in **1965**, under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & PD.
**OMSS** is FCI's open-market route to cool grain prices.
AP's **Mee Mart** (with **NCCF**) sells items **Rs 3-5** below market.

n169830f9407.s: The National Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India (NCCF) was set up in ____ and functions under the ____.
o: 1965; Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
1965; Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
1955; Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
n169830f9407.x: NCCF was set up in 1965 under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and PD, so A is right. B has the wrong ministry; C has the wrong year (1955 is the Essential Commodities Act); D has both wrong.
n169830f9407.tq: Don't confuse NCCF (1965) with the Essential Commodities Act (1955) or the Food Corporations Act (1964).
xs: **NCCF** was set up in **1965** under the **Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution**, option **(1)**.
⚠ **1955** is the **Essential Commodities Act**, not NCCF.
xa: NCCF **procures essential goods** and runs **price-stabilisation** operations.
It is a Bharat-brand channel with **NAFED** and **Kendriya Bhandar**.
AP **Mee Mart** is a Civil Supplies + **NCCF** partnership; first outlet **Lalupuram near Guntur**.

n8d6e9d83ffa.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective or effect of the Open Market Sale Scheme?
o: Replacing the Food Corporation of India’s procurement function with private procurement
Offloading excess central-pool stocks and reducing carrying costs
Raising grain supply during lean seasons and in deficit regions
n8d6e9d83ffa.x: OMSS involves FCI selling surplus central-pool grain at predetermined prices. It raises supply, moderates prices, offloads excess stocks and reduces carrying costs, but it does not replace FCI procurement with private procurement.
n8d6e9d83ffa.tq: Find the option that introduces a function not belonging to the scheme.
xs: **OMSS** does **not replace FCI procurement** with private procurement, so option **(1)** is the odd one.
Under OMSS, **FCI** sells surplus central-pool grain at **predetermined prices**.
Its purposes: **raise supply** in lean seasons/deficit regions, **moderate prices**, **offload excess stock**, **cut carrying cost**.
xa: **OMSS (Domestic)** sales are used to cool prices.
FCI was created by the **Food Corporations Act 1964**.
Stocks about **602 LMT** (around **3 times** norms) make OMSS sales possible.

n753d3754923.s: The stated objective of the National Food Security Act, 2013 is to provide:
o: Food and nutritional security by ensuring access to adequate quality food at affordable prices so that people can live a life with dignity
A guaranteed 100 days of wage employment to every rural household
Procurement of all foodgrains produced in India at the Minimum Support Price
A Public Distribution System Act replacing the Food Corporations Act, 1964
n753d3754923.x: The NFSA, 2013 aims at food and nutritional security at affordable prices so people live with dignity (APPSC 2025). Wage employment is MGNREGA's aim; the Act does not guarantee MSP procurement of all grain; 'PDS Act' and 'FCI Act' were the distractors in the exam.
n753d3754923.tq: NFSA = food + nutrition + affordable prices + dignity.
xs: NFSA 2013 aims at **food and nutritional security** at **affordable prices** so people **live with dignity**, option **(1)** (APPSC 2025).
It does not promise wage employment or MSP procurement of all grain; "**PDS Act**" and "**FCI Act**" were exam distractors.
xa: FCI was created by the **Food Corporations Act 1964**.
NFSA gives a **legal, justiciable right**; commenced **July 2013**.
**Article 47** (DPSP): duty to raise nutrition and the standard of living.

n9601b844962.s: Which of the following is a stated criticism of the present food subsidy framework?
o: Issue prices have remained frozen since 2013 while subsidy costs have risen.
The NFSA excludes all rural households from food support.
The PDS supplies only imported foodgrains and no domestic cereals.
Issue prices have increased every year while subsidies have been abolished.
n9601b844962.x: A criticism is that issue prices have been frozen since 2013 even as the subsidy burden has increased.
n9601b844962.tq: Identify the precise trend and avoid reversed or extreme statements.
xs: A key criticism: **issue prices frozen since 2013** while **subsidy** keeps rising, option **(1)**.
NFSA issue prices **Rs 3/2/1** were **not revised since July 2013** though MSP and economic cost rise.
xa: Food subsidy (Budget **2026-27**): **Rs 2,27,629 crore**.
PMGKAY extension costs about **Rs 11.80 lakh crore** (**2024-2028**).
NFSA covers **75% rural** and **50% urban** — not excluding rural households.

n1ce5c432c28.s: The Balwantrai Mehta Committee, which reviewed the Community Development Programme and National Extension Service, submitted its report in:
n1ce5c432c28.x: The Balwantrai Mehta Committee reviewed the Community Development Programme and National Extension Service and submitted its report in November 1957.
n1ce5c432c28.tq: Pair the committee with both its subject of review and its exact reporting year.
xs: The **Balwantrai Mehta Committee** reviewed **CDP and NES** and reported in **November 1957**, option **(3)**.
**1952** is the year of CDP itself, and **1974** is the **Minimum Needs Programme**.
xa: CDP began in **1952**, NES in **1953**.
CDP is the **first** rural development programme.
The topic's basis is **Unit 10 Decentralisation**.

n25f3f45bafa.s: The Drought-Prone Area Programme (DPAP) was launched in:
n25f3f45bafa.x: DPAP dates to 1973-74; the Desert Development Programme (1977-78) covers both hot and cold deserts.
xa: Both are under **Rural Development / Land Resources**.
**Food for Work** also dates to **1977-78**.
The **Madanapalle Water Grid** serves drought-prone **Rayalaseema** in AP.

n83fa8718170.s: In rural development, NRLM primarily promotes:
n83fa8718170.x: NRLM promotes SHG-based self-employment, while MGNREGA provides up to 100 days of wage employment.
xa: AP Budget **2026-27**: **NRLM Rs 955 crore**; **VB-G RAM G** (rural employment guarantee) **Rs 8,365 crore**.
The **MGNREGA Act** dates to **2005**, the year of **Bharat Nirman**.
**Food for Work** (**1977-78**) was an earlier wage-employment programme.

nindian-economy-3-1.s: Who originated the Etawah Pilot Project, the first rural-development pilot project, in September 1948?
nindian-economy-3-1.x: Lt. Col. Albert Mayer, an American town planner, started the Etawah Pilot Project in September 1948, India's first rural-development pilot.
nindian-economy-3-1.tq: Recall who began the Etawah project.
n: Lieutenant Colonel Albert Mayer originated the Etawah Pilot Project. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
xs: The **Etawah Pilot Project** (**September 1948**) was originated by **Lieutenant Colonel Albert Mayer** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was the **first rural-development pilot project**.
The project began in **September 1948**, before the **Community Development Programme** (**1952**).
xa: **National Extension Service** (**1953**) was the first programme of community development.
The **Balwantrai Mehta Committee** (**1957**) reviewed the CDP and NES.
⚠ CDP **1952** → NES **1953** → Balwantrai Mehta review **1957**.

nindian-economy-3-8.s: 'Garibi Hatao' was first introduced in which Five Year Plan?
nindian-economy-3-8.x: Garibi Hatao entered planning with the Fifth Plan.
n: Garibi Hatao was first introduced in the Fifth Five-Year Plan. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
The Employment Guarantee Scheme first started in Maharashtra in 1972. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
xa: **Food for Work** programme first started in **1977–78**.
**IRDP** became nationwide on **2 October 1980**.
**Mission Antyodaya** (Union Budget **2017-18**) aims at poverty-free Gram Panchayats.

n9ace05db59f.s: Which department became a separate Ministry in 2011 and, since June 2019, has been a Department under the Ministry of Jal Shakti?
n9ace05db59f.x: Drinking Water and Sanitation became a separate Ministry in 2011 and has been a Department under the Ministry of Jal Shakti since June 2019.
n9ace05db59f.tq: Track an institutional change through its two successive administrative stages.
xs: **Drinking Water & Sanitation** became a separate Ministry in **2011** and since **June 2019** is a Department under **Jal Shakti**, option **(2)**.
Land Resources handles DPAP and DDP, not drinking water.
xa: **Jal Jeevan Mission** (**15 Aug 2019**) and **SBM-G** sit under **Jal Shakti**.
⚠ JJM and SBM-G = **Jal Shakti**; PMGSY and PMAY-G = **Rural Development**.
SBM-G Phase II (**2020**) is run by **DDWS**.

n2b9bf7e3567.s: The objective of ODF Plus under SBM-Gramin Phase II is to:
o: Provide only individual household toilets in urban areas
Provide pucca houses in difficult terrain
Sustain open-defecation-free status and undertake solid and liquid waste management
n2b9bf7e3567.x: SBM-Gramin Phase II focuses on sustaining ODF status and managing solid and liquid waste, together described as ODF Plus.
n2b9bf7e3567.tq: Distinguish the second-phase qualitative objective from the original sanitation drive.
xs: **ODF Plus** under **SBM-G Phase II** means **sustaining ODF** plus **solid and liquid waste management**, option **(3)**.
It is a rural sanitation goal, not urban toilets, housing or roads.
xa: SBM-G Phase II was approved in **2020**, up to **2024-25**, under **Jal Shakti (DDWS)**.
Achievements: **12.19 crore** toilets, **1,288 GOBARdhan** plants, **5.68 lakh** ODF Plus villages.
AP Budget **2026-27**: SBM **Rs 1,037 crore**.

n21cdef6e244.s: The Vibrant Villages Programme, announced in the Budget 2022–23, is administered by the:
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
n21cdef6e244.x: The Vibrant Villages Programme was announced in Budget 2022–23 under the Ministry of Home Affairs and targets villages on the northern border.
n21cdef6e244.tq: Apply the ministry-swap trap to a border-area development programme.
xs: The **Vibrant Villages Programme** (Budget **2022-23**) is under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**, option **(1)**.
It covers **villages on the northern border**.
xa: ⚠ VVP = **Home Affairs**; JJM/SBM-G = **Jal Shakti**; PMGSY/PMAY-G = **Rural Development**.
**Mission Antyodaya** came in Union Budget **2017-18**.
**SPMRM** develops **300+** Rurban clusters.

n9420770c1e4.s: PMGSY-II, launched in 2013, focused mainly on:
o: Through routes and major rural links
n9420770c1e4.x: PMGSY-I (2000) gave new connectivity, PMGSY-II (2013) focused on upgradation and PMGSY-III (2019) on through routes and major rural links.
xa: PMGSY launched on **25 Dec 2000**.
It connects **99.6%** of targeted eligible areas.
LWE blocks need only **100+** population.

n6efff29aa84.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about population norms for habitations under PMGSY?
o: Hill States, North-East, deserts and Schedule V areas: 250 or more
n6efff29aa84.x: In LWE-affected blocks the norm is 100+, not 250+.
xa: ⚠ **500 – 250 – 100** = plains – hill/NE/tribal – LWE.
**RCPLWEA** (**2016**) builds LWE roads.

n083ad8c070b.s: Under PMAY-G, the unit assistance for a house is correctly stated as:
o: Rs 1.00 lakh in plains and Rs 1.20 lakh in hilly areas
Rs 1.30 lakh in plains and Rs 1.50 lakh in hilly areas
Rs 1.50 lakh in plains and Rs 1.80 lakh in difficult terrain
Rs 1.20 lakh in plains and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly or difficult terrain
n083ad8c070b.x: PMAY-G provides assistance of Rs 1.20 lakh per house in plain areas and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly or difficult terrain.
n083ad8c070b.tq: Compare the standard unit assistance with the higher difficult-terrain amount.
xs: PMAY-G gives **Rs 1.20 lakh** in **plains** and **Rs 1.30 lakh** in **hilly/difficult terrain**, option **(4)**.
The other pairs misstate one or both amounts.
xa: Beneficiaries from **SECC 2011** housing-deprivation data, verified by the **Gram Sabha**.
**3.13 crore** rural homes completed by mid-2026.
AP Budget **2026-27**: urban + rural housing **Rs 5,451 crore**.

n077fc6b780d.s: Beneficiaries under PMAY-G are identified primarily on the basis of:
o: Annual income-tax returns verified by the District Collector
Voter-list data approved by the State Cabinet
SECC 2011 housing-deprivation data, verified by the Gram Sabha
Census 2001 occupational data, without local verification
n077fc6b780d.x: PMAY-G beneficiaries are identified using housing-deprivation data from SECC 2011, followed by verification by the Gram Sabha.
n077fc6b780d.tq: Identify both the data source and the required local verification authority.
xs: PMAY-G beneficiaries come from **SECC 2011** housing-deprivation data, **verified by the Gram Sabha**, option **(3)**.
Income-tax returns, voter lists and Census 2001 are not the basis.
xa: Unit assistance: **Rs 1.20 lakh** / **Rs 1.30 lakh**.
Scheme launched in **2016**, under **Rural Development**.
Har Ghar Jal certification also uses a **Gram Sabha** resolution.

n01298eed273.s: Which institution conducts an annual Gram Panchayat-level ranking survey as part of its rural development framework?
n01298eed273.x: Mission Antyodaya includes an annual Gram Panchayat-level ranking survey and functions as a convergence framework for rural development.
n01298eed273.tq: Match the distinctive administrative activity with the institution performing it.
xs: **Mission Antyodaya** runs an **annual GP-level ranking survey**, option **(2)**.
It is a **convergence framework** to make **Gram Panchayats poverty-free**, from **Union Budget 2017-18**.
**CAPART** funds voluntary organisations; **DRDA** implemented district anti-poverty programmes; **ITDA** serves tribal areas.
xa: **CAPART** dates to **1986** (MoRD).
**DRDA** grew out of **IRDP** implementation.

n1a68cc5b645.s: The Functional Household Tap Connection target under the Jal Jeevan Mission covers which of the following?
o: Rural households and specified public institutions
Only urban households and panchayat offices
n1a68cc5b645.x: The target covers every rural household as well as schools, anganwadis, Gram Panchayat buildings, health centres and ashramshalas.
n1a68cc5b645.tq: Distinguish the complete beneficiary coverage from a limited institutional target.
xs: **FHTC** goes to **every rural household + public institutions** (schools, anganwadis, GP buildings, health centres, ashramshalas), option **(2)**.
It is not limited to households only or institutions only.
xa: FHTC = **Functional Household Tap Connection**.
Service level: **55 LPCD**.
**Har Ghar Jal** village: every household and institution has a tap, certified by **Gram Sabha**.

na94e658c373.s: The prescribed service level under the Jal Jeevan Mission is:
na94e658c373.x: The prescribed JJM service level is 55 litres per capita per day of water of the required quality.
na94e658c373.tq: Recall the exact quantitative service norm.
xs: JJM's service level is **55 litres per capita per day (LPCD)** of prescribed quality, option **(3)**.
70, 45 and 40 LPCD are not the JJM norm.
xa: Delivered through **FHTCs** to households and institutions.
Target **19.36 crore**; connected **15.86 crore (81.94%)**.
**2.89 lakh** fully covered villages (Aug 2026).

n949b5ed52b8.s: The Union Cabinet extended the Jal Jeevan Mission, originally due in 2024, up to:
n949b5ed52b8.x: JJM was extended to December 2028, with JJM 2.0 shifting focus to service delivery.
xa: JJM 2.0 outlay: **Rs 8.69 lakh crore**.
Union Budget **2026-27**: **Rs 67,600 crore**.

n97236fd0f47.s: Under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0, Union Territories without legislature receive:
n97236fd0f47.x: UTs without legislature get 100% Union funding; Himalayan/NE States and UTs with legislature 90:10; other States 50:50.
xa: JJM 2.0 outlay: **Rs 8.69 lakh crore**.
⚠ SPMRM uses **60:40** generally and **90:10** for NE and Himalayan States.
JJM 2.0 runs to **December 2028**.

n37c7bca1ff5.s: A village may be certified as a Har Ghar Jal village when:
o: A water scheme receives administrative sanction from the Union Government
At least 81.94 per cent of households receive tanker water
Every household and institution has a tap connection and the Gram Sabha passes a resolution
Every rural household has an electricity connection certified by the Gram Panchayat
n37c7bca1ff5.x: Har Ghar Jal certification requires tap connections for every household and institution, certified through a Gram Sabha resolution.
n37c7bca1ff5.tq: Apply the certification conditions to a practical village situation.
xs: A **Har Ghar Jal** village has a tap for **every household and institution**, certified by a **Gram Sabha resolution**, option **(3)**.
**81.94%** is the national connection share, not a certification test.
xa: **2.12 lakh+** villages certified (Mar 2025).
**Jal Arpan**: handover to GPs and **Paani Samitis/VWSCs**.
**Sujal Gaon ID**: digital ID for every rural piped scheme.

n3ff1295b468.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission?
o: Replacing all Gram Panchayats with urban local bodies
n3ff1295b468.x: The mission aims to stimulate local economic development, enhance basic services and create well-planned clusters. It does not replace Gram Panchayats with urban local bodies.
n3ff1295b468.tq: Find the option that exceeds the institutional scope of the mission.
xs: SPMRM does **not replace Gram Panchayats with urban local bodies**, so option **(4)** is NOT an objective.
Its PYQ objectives: **stimulate local economic development**, **enhance basic services**, **create well-planned clusters**.
xa: It keeps the "**rural soul**" while adding urban amenities.
Convergence of **MGNREGA, PMGSY, SBM, PMAY**.
⚠ The **16th FC** proposed an "**Urbanisation Premium**" for merging peri-urban villages.

ne18e66c3967.s: JJM 2.0 shifts the emphasis from infrastructure creation to:
o: service delivery, including operation and maintenance
ne18e66c3967.x: JJM 2.0 focuses on service delivery, including sustainable operation and maintenance.
xa: Cabinet extended JJM to **December 2028** (Mar 2026); original deadline **2024**.
Criticism: **cost overruns** and **poor-quality works**.
AP gave O&M to **panchayats** (Sept **2025**).

o: Funding voluntary organisations and promoting rural technology
Providing modern inputs only to desert farmers
nd9d4f0d2f30.x: CAPART, or the Council for Advancement of People's Action and Rural Technology, funds voluntary organisations and supports rural technology.
nd9d4f0d2f30.tq: Expand the acronym and connect it with its core institutional function.
xs: **CAPART** (Council for Advancement of People's Action and Rural Technology) **funds voluntary organisations and rural technology**, option **(3)**.
District anti-poverty implementation was the role of **DRDA**; all-weather roads are **PMGSY**.
xa: CAPART was set up in **1986** under **MoRD**.
**Mission Antyodaya** (**2017-18**) aims at poverty-free Gram Panchayats.
**ITDA/TADP** support tribal agriculture and livelihoods.

na623ee13fd9.s: The principal objective of ITDA/TADP is to:
o: Raise agricultural output through modern inputs, horticulture and fruit plantations, while supporting tribal livelihoods
Provide only urban amenities to selected villages
Construct national highways in tribal districts
Promote industrial exports from metropolitan regions
na623ee13fd9.x: ITDA and TADP seek to improve agricultural output through modern inputs, horticulture and fruit plantations and to strengthen tribal livelihoods.
na623ee13fd9.tq: Select the option containing the complete objective rather than a narrow fragment.
xs: **ITDA/TADP** aim to **raise agricultural output with modern inputs**, **horticulture/fruit plantations** and **tribal livelihoods**, option **(1)**.
A PYQ held **all listed objectives** of TADP and ITDA to be correct.
xa: ITDA = **Integrated Tribal Development Agency**; TADP = **Tribal Area Development Programme**.
Both are tied to the **Tribal Sub-Plan** of the **5th Plan**.
**PURA** (urban amenities in rural areas) is a different, **Abdul Kalam** idea.

nc7538114f14.s: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission is best described as:
o: A successor and expansion of the PURA approach
A special programme for urban slum redevelopment
A scheme exclusively for tribal hostels
A replacement for the National Extension Service
nc7538114f14.x: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission, launched in 2016, is the successor and expansion of the PURA approach.
nc7538114f14.tq: Use the successor–predecessor relationship to distinguish closely related rural development initiatives.
xs: **SPMRM** is the **successor/expansion of PURA**, option **(1)**.
Launched **21 Feb 2016** at **Kurubhat, Rajnandgaon** (Chhattisgarh).
xa: PURA = **Provision of Urban Amenities in Rural Areas**, by **Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**.
SPMRM aims at **300+ Rurban clusters**.
**NES** (**1953**) was an early rural extension programme, unrelated.

n1fcdc2e666e.s: A Rurban cluster in a plain or coastal area normally comprises contiguous villages having a population of:
n1fcdc2e666e.x: For plain and coastal areas, a Rurban cluster comprises contiguous villages with a population of 25,000 to 50,000.
n1fcdc2e666e.tq: Separate population norms by geographical category before selecting the range.
xs: A plain/coastal Rurban cluster has **25,000-50,000** population, option **(4)**.
**5,000-25,000** is one version of the **desert/hilly/tribal** range.
xa: Desert/hilly/tribal: **5,000-15,000** (some notes **5,000-25,000**).
Clusters are **contiguous villages**.
SPMRM aims at **300+** clusters.

nf9946d3149e.s: Critical Gap Funding under the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission is up to what share of project cost?
nf9946d3149e.x: The mission relies mainly on convergence of schemes, with Critical Gap Funding up to 30% of project cost.
xa: Centre:State **60:40**; **90:10** for NE and Himalayan States.
Launched **2016**; aims at **300+** clusters.
AP: **359** panchayats classified under Rurban clusters.

nb9c2df2999c.s: The PURA (Provision of Urban Amenities in Rural Areas) model, later elaborated in the book Target 3 Billion, was originally propounded by:
nb9c2df2999c.x: PURA was the idea of Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, elaborated in Target 3 Billion (co-authored with Srijan Pal Singh) to bridge the rural-urban divide. Balwantrai Mehta headed the 1957 committee on CDP/NES; Swaminathan is linked to the Green Revolution; Sen to the entitlement approach to famine.
nb9c2df2999c.tq: PURA = Kalam; SPMRM 2016 is its successor.
xs: **PURA** was propounded by **Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**, option **(1)**.
It was elaborated in **Target 3 Billion** with **Srijan Pal Singh**.
**Balwantrai Mehta** reviewed CDP and NES in **1957**.
xa: PURA = Provision of Urban Amenities in Rural Areas.
Successor: **SPMRM** (**21 Feb 2016**).
FIRST/LAST: **PURA idea = Abdul Kalam**; **CDP 1952** = first rural development programme.

ndf4bd828126.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a remaining rural infrastructure gap?
o: Operation and maintenance of water schemes
Universal availability of high-speed rail connectivity
ndf4bd828126.x: The identified gaps include piped water, operation and maintenance, housing and last-mile roads. High-speed rail connectivity is not listed as a rural infrastructure gap in this context.
ndf4bd828126.tq: Find the option outside the stated group of infrastructure deficiencies.
xs: **High-speed rail** is not listed as a rural infrastructure gap, so option **(3)** is the answer.
Listed gaps: piped water (~**18%** unconnected), **O&M of water schemes**, **housing**, **last-mile roads**.
xa: Achievements: **Saubhagya** — **100%** willing-household electrification.
SBM-G: **12.19 crore** toilets; **5.68 lakh** ODF Plus villages.
Poor quality and irregularities in **JJM works** is another gap.

n0b0a618bab4.s: As on 31 March 2024, the share of Andhra Pradesh rural households having Functional Household Tap Connections was approximately:
n0b0a618bab4.x: In Andhra Pradesh, 70.04 lakh households, representing 73 per cent, had FHTCs as on 31 March 2024.
n0b0a618bab4.tq: Distinguish the State-level coverage percentage from the national figure.
xs: On **31 Mar 2024**, **70.04 lakh** AP households — **73 per cent** — had FHTCs, option **(2)**.
**81.94%** is the **national** connection share, not AP's.
xa: AP sanctioned **77,917** works worth **Rs 27,248.86 crore** in saturation mode.
AP has **112** water testing labs and **2,00,101** hand pumps.
Action plan: **+5.40 lakh** FHTCs (2024-25); **+10 lakh** each in 2025-26 and 2026-27.

naa5f9da71d5.s: The Madanapalle Water Grid is intended primarily to provide drinking water to:
o: The coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh
naa5f9da71d5.x: The Madanapalle Water Grid is intended to provide drinking water in drought-prone Rayalaseema.
naa5f9da71d5.tq: Apply the location-purpose association of a regional infrastructure project.
xs: The **Madanapalle Water Grid** gives drinking water to **drought-prone Rayalaseema**, option **(4)**.
It is not a coastal, Himalayan or Visakhapatnam-only project.
xa: AP aims at safe water to **every household by 2028**.
AP had **70.04 lakh** households (**73%**) with FHTCs on 31 Mar 2024.
**DPAP** (**1973-74**) was the national programme for drought-prone areas.

ncd480fa12bc.s: Andhra Pradesh's Jal Jeevan Mission coverage in March 2024 was reported at:
ncd480fa12bc.x: AP's 73% was below the national 82%; its JJM 2.0 target is safe water to every household by 2028.
xa: National: **15.86 crore** of **19.36 crore** households connected.
**2.89 lakh** fully covered villages (Aug 2026).

nb7313633564.s: In 1951, moneylenders supplied approximately what share of rural credit?
nb7313633564.x: Moneylenders supplied approximately 70% of rural credit in 1951.
nb7313633564.tq: Recall the historical baseline and distinguish it from the later institutional-credit structure.
xs: In **1951**, **moneylenders** supplied the bulk — about **70%** — of rural credit, so option **(3)** is correct.
This dominance of moneylenders is the historical backdrop to the **AIRCS Committee** set up by the **RBI** in **1951**.
xa: AIRCS, chaired by **A.D. Gorwala**, reported in **1954**; its verdict: "**rural credit has failed, but cooperation must succeed**".
Its outcome was the **SBI** (**1955**), formed from the **Imperial Bank**.
⚠ Sequence trap: AIRCS **1951** → report **1954** → **SBI 1955**.
Non-institutional lenders today: **moneylenders, traders, landlords, relatives**.

n25636c9422a.s: The All India Rural Credit Survey Committee, set up by the RBI in 1951, was headed by:
n25636c9422a.x: The RBI constituted the committee in 1951 under A.D. Gorwala; its recommendations led to the State Bank of India (1955).
xa: Verdict of the Committee: "**rural credit has failed, but cooperation must succeed**".
In **1951** moneylenders supplied about **70%** of rural credit.
⚠ Order to remember: AIRCS **1951** → report **1954** → **SBI 1955**.

n7995a4ede74.s: The All India Rural Credit Survey Committee famously concluded that:
o: Rural credit has failed, but cooperation must succeed
Cooperation has failed, but rural credit must succeed
Rural credit has succeeded, but cooperation has failed
Cooperation has failed, but banking must succeed
n7995a4ede74.x: The Committee concluded that rural credit had failed, but cooperation must succeed, stressing cooperative institutions in rural credit.
xa: Committee: **RBI**, chair **A.D. Gorwala**, **1951**, report **1954**.
Outcome: **State Bank of India (1955)** from the **Imperial Bank**.
Today **cooperatives/PACS** remain institutional sources giving credit, **marketing and storage** to small and marginal farmers.

n3e3afeaf65d.s: Which of the following is a non-institutional source of rural credit?
n3e3afeaf65d.x: Traders (like relatives) are non-institutional lenders; commercial banks, PACS and RRBs are institutional sources.
xa: Other institutional sources: **RRBs**, **SFBs**, **SHG-bank linkage**.
Non-institutional list: **moneylenders, traders, landlords, relatives**.
About **50%** of AP farmers depend on **non-institutional credit** (NABARD study).

n211cadfabf9.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Kisan Credit Card scheme as described?
o: It has a validity period of five years.
It is restricted exclusively to landowning farmers and excludes tenants and sharecroppers.
It may be issued by public sector banks, private scheduled commercial banks, SFBs, RRBs and cooperative banks.
It covers crop, post-harvest, consumption and allied needs.
n211cadfabf9.x: Tenants, sharecroppers, SHGs and JLGs are eligible under the described Kisan Credit Card framework. The other three statements are correct features.
n211cadfabf9.tq: Use the eligibility exception to defeat the word ‘exclusively’.
xs: The false feature is that KCC is **restricted to landowning farmers** — option **(2)**; **tenants, sharecroppers, SHGs/JLGs** are eligible.
KCC is valid **5 years** — true.
It is issued by **PSBs, private SCBs, SFBs, RRBs and cooperative banks** — true.
It covers **crop, post-harvest, consumption and allied** needs — true.
xa: The KCC **limit** is fixed by the **cropping pattern**.
**MISS-KCC** benefits about **5.9 crore** farmers (Feb **2025**); applications via the **Kisan Rin Portal**.
AP has **CCRC** for tenant farmers, who carry more debt than owners (Guntur sample).

nindian-economy-58-15.s: Which of the following is NOT a beneficiary of credit from Small Finance Banks?
nindian-economy-58-15.x: Small finance banks lend to small businesses, small and marginal farmers and rural entrepreneurs; regulators are FSDC members, not borrowers.
n: Small Financing Banks provide credit to small business units. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 86-88]
Small Financing Banks provide credit to small and marginal farmers. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 86-88]
Small Financing Banks provide credit to entrepreneurs, particularly in rural areas. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 86-88]
xa: **Institutional** rural credit: commercial banks, RRBs, cooperatives/PACS, SFBs, SHG-bank linkage.
**Kisan Credit Card**: valid **5 years**; issued by PSBs, private SCBs, SFBs, RRBs, cooperative banks.
**AIRCS Committee** (**1951**, A.D. Gorwala) → **SBI** (**1955**) from the Imperial Bank.

n21bff2e6e1f.s: Based on their repayment pattern, informal loans are classified as:
n21bff2e6e1f.x: Informal loans are described as temporary (e.g. repaid after harvest), chronic, or debt-trap loans (a new loan taken to repay an old one).
xa: **Usurious interest** leads to **distress sale**, sale of **land/gold** and **bonded-labour-like** arrangements.
Informal debt is often the **immediate trigger in farmer suicides**.
The **microfinance route** runs through **SHGs, JLGs, BC Sakhis** under **DAY-NRLM**.

n897bdc9001f.s: Distress migration, unlike seasonal migration, is generally:
o: Forced by debt, landlessness or crop loss
Movement only during the harvest season with assured return
n897bdc9001f.x: Distress migration is forced by economic hardship such as debt, landlessness or crop loss; seasonal migration is movement for a season, such as harvest, followed by return.
xa: **Return migration** is also a type.
AP distress-migration belts: **Rayalaseema** and north Andhra (**Srikakulam**).
**MSMEs** help **reduce distress migration**.

n0bd0f0da80a.s: Feminisation of agriculture refers to which of the following phenomena?
o: The replacement of women agricultural workers by machines
The exclusive ownership of agricultural land by women
A rising share of women in the agricultural workforce as men move to non-farm and urban employment
The migration of women from urban areas to industrial centres
n0bd0f0da80a.x: Feminisation of agriculture means an increasing proportion of women among cultivators, agricultural labourers and unpaid family workers, particularly as men shift to non-farm and urban work.
n0bd0f0da80a.tq: Use the precise definition and distinguish workforce participation from ownership of land.
xs: **Feminisation of agriculture** is a **rising share of women** in the farm workforce as **men move to non-farm and urban work** — option **(3)**.
It covers women as **cultivators, labourers and unpaid family workers** — not land ownership (option 2).
xa: Main cause: **male out-migration**; also distress and **COVID-era return migration**.
**U-shaped curve** (Claudia Goldin): high in the **1980s**, fell **2004-05 to 2012**, rising after **2020**.

nf639f3c290b.s: The U-shaped curve in women’s work participation, associated with Claudia Goldin, indicates which of the following sequences?
o: Low participation in agriculture in the 1980s, followed by a continuous rise until 2012
High participation in agriculture in the 1980s, a fall during 2004-05 to 2012, and a subsequent rise after 2020
A continuous decline from the 1980s because of mechanisation
High urban participation followed by a complete withdrawal from work after 2020
nf639f3c290b.x: Women’s work participation was high in agriculture in the 1980s, fell with mechanisation between 2004-05 and 2012, and rose again after 2020, partly due to distress.
nf639f3c290b.tq: Track the turning points in the sequence instead of treating the curve as a continuous trend.
xs: Goldin's **U-shaped curve**: **high** in agriculture in the **1980s**, **fell** with **mechanisation** **2004-05 to 2012**, **rising after 2020** — option **(2)**.
The renewed rise is **partly out of distress**, not only empowerment.
xa: **Feminisation of agriculture**: rising women's share as men move to non-farm and urban work.
**COVID-era return migration** intensified women's farm work.

n8a3e17eaa5c.s: Under DAY-NRLM, the microfinance route for rural borrowers works through:
o: Commercial banks through Kisan Credit Cards only
n8a3e17eaa5c.x: The described microfinance route uses self-help groups, joint liability groups and BC Sakhis under DAY-NRLM.
xa: **SVEP** (Start-Up Village Entrepreneurship Programme), also under **DAY-NRLM**, funds rural **non-farm enterprises**.
**SHG-bank linkage** is counted among **institutional** credit sources.
**SHGs/JLGs** are also eligible for the **Kisan Credit Card**.

ned74542c273.s: The Start-Up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP) under DAY-NRLM funds:
ned74542c273.x: SVEP, under DAY-NRLM, funds rural non-farm enterprises.
xa: **KVIC** (KVI Act **1956**) implements **PMEGP**.
**DDU-GKY**: placement-linked skilling — **18.38 lakh** trained, **11.94 lakh** placed (Mar **2026**).
**MSMEs** give **38.9 crore** jobs, **2nd after agriculture**, and reduce distress migration.

n7fc3ef70212.s: Which body is the implementing agency of the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)?
o: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
n7fc3ef70212.x: KVIC, a statutory body under the KVI Act 1956 working under the Ministry of MSME, implements PMEGP. NABARD is the apex rural development bank, SIDBI finances MSMEs, and DAY-NRLM runs SHG-based livelihoods (including SVEP), not PMEGP.
n7fc3ef70212.tq: PMEGP is run by KVIC (Ministry of MSME).
xs: **KVIC** is the implementing agency of **PMEGP** — option **(2)**.
KVIC is a **statutory body** under the **KVI Act 1956** (amended **1987**, **2006**) under the **Ministry of MSME**.
**DAY-NRLM** runs the **SHG** route and **SVEP**, not PMEGP.
xa: **KVI sales**: **Rs 1.27 lakh crore** in **2025-26**.
**MSMEs**: **8.7 crore** enterprises, about **31.1%** of GDP.
**DDU-GKY**: **18.38 lakh** trained, **11.94 lakh** placed (Mar **2026**).

n0822fabf3fe.s: A parliamentary panel flagged which concerns about DDU-GKY?
o: Low enrolment and delayed fund release
n0822fabf3fe.x: The parliamentary panel flagged low wages and drop-outs in DDU-GKY, concerns about the quality and retention of placement-linked skilling.
xa: **SVEP** under **DAY-NRLM** funds rural non-farm enterprises.
**MSMEs**: **38.9 crore** jobs, second after agriculture.
**KVIC** implements **PMEGP**.

n07b661206cd.s: Which of the following is a pull factor of rural-urban migration?
n07b661206cd.x: Better wages attract migrants to cities (pull), while crop failure, poor rural healthcare and rural unemployment push people out of villages.
xa: **Unbalanced rural-urban development** is a push factor.
**BPSC 2024** PYQ: high urban labour demand, unbalanced development, few rural jobs — **all** are causes.
**26.8%** of rural Indians were migrants in **2020-21** (ES **2025-26**).

nab478025c21.s: The Khadi and Village Industries Commission is a statutory body under the Khadi and Village Industries Act of:
nab478025c21.x: KVIC is a statutory body under the KVI Act, 1956 (amended in 1987 and 2006); it works under the Ministry of MSME.
xa: KVIC is the implementing agency of **PMEGP**.
**KVI sales** reached **Rs 1.27 lakh crore** in **2025-26**.
**SVEP** (under **DAY-NRLM**) also funds rural non-farm enterprises.

nd322a2efcf3.s: NREGA came into force in 2006 and was renamed MGNREGA in:
nd322a2efcf3.x: The Act (passed 2005) came into force as NREGA in 2006 and was renamed MGNREGA in 2009.
xa: Wages are due within **15 days**; **one-third** women (actual **>50%** of person-days).
MGNREGA is replaced by **VB-G RAM G**.
⚠ **125 days** is AP's raised guarantee in distressed pockets under VB-G RAM G (Jun **2026**).

n97a519fcb6b.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26 figures cited, what proportion of rural Indians were migrants in 2020-21?
n97a519fcb6b.x: The cited estimate places the proportion of rural Indians who were migrants in 2020-21 at 26.8%.
n97a519fcb6b.tq: Identify the exact percentage from closely spaced demographic figures.
xs: **26.8%** of rural Indians were migrants in **2020-21** (ES **2025-26**) — option **(2)**.
**45.9%** is the rural FLFPR for **2025**, and **35%** the share of rural households lacking healthcare within **5 km**.
xa: About **65%** of people are still **rural**; about **26%** aged **10-24**.
Rural secondary dropout is **>17%**.
Cities are near capacity; rural exodus leaves an **ageing population** behind.

nc7b94c5d2e3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about farm indebtedness in Andhra Pradesh?
o: As per NSSO 77th Round, 93.2% of AP agricultural households are indebted
AP's indebtedness level is the highest among major States
A Guntur sample found tenant farmers more indebted than owner-cultivators
A NABARD study found only about 25% of AP farmers depend on non-institutional credit
nc7b94c5d2e3.x: The NABARD study puts dependence on non-institutional credit at about 50%, not 25%. The other three statements are correct.
xa: AP **distress-migration belts**: **Rayalaseema** (drought-prone) and north Andhra (**Srikakulam**).
**Gulf migration** sources: **YSR Kadapa** and **Godavari/Konaseema** districts.
AP angle: highest indebted farm households plus **high tenancy**.

ncbc8f3d6c81.s: The principal distress-migration belts of Andhra Pradesh are:
ncbc8f3d6c81.x: Drought-prone Rayalaseema and north Andhra, particularly Srikakulam, are identified as the main distress-migration belts.
xa: Gulf migration sources: **YSR Kadapa** and **Godavari/Konaseema**.
AP response: **125 days** under VB-G RAM G; **359 panchayats** in Rurban clusters.
About **50%** of AP farmers depend on non-institutional credit (NABARD).

n52e2d540305.s: Gulf migration from Andhra Pradesh comes mainly from:
n52e2d540305.x: Gulf migration comes mainly from YSR Kadapa and the Godavari/Konaseema districts.
xa: AP raised guaranteed days to **125 per year** in distressed pockets (Jun **2026**).
**359 panchayats** in **Rurban clusters** to curb migration (Mar **2026**).
Tenant farmers carry more debt than owners (**Guntur** sample).

n5e6a27d4cd0.s: Which one of the following is a statutory town?
o: Any settlement with more than 50% of workers in non-agricultural activities
Any settlement with a density of 400 persons per square kilometre
A village with a population of 5,000 and 75% male non-agricultural workers
A place notified as a municipality or governed by a municipal corporation
n5e6a27d4cd0.x: A statutory town is a place with a municipal corporation, municipality, cantonment board or notified town area, notified by the State and administered by an urban local body.
n5e6a27d4cd0.tq: Separate the legal or administrative definition of a statutory town from the demographic criteria of a census town.
xs: A **statutory town** is any place with a **municipal corporation, municipality**, nagar panchayat, **cantonment board** or **notified town area** — option **(4)**.
It is **notified by the State** under State law and run by a **ULB**.
Option (3) describes a **census town** — administratively a village meeting **5,000 / 75% / 400**.
xa: ⚠ The **60%** male non-farm criterion is wrong; correct figure **75%** (**UPPSC 2010**).
**2011**: about **4,041** statutory and **3,892** census towns.
**Census 2027** keeps the **1981** census-town criteria.

ne412520155c.s: Which combination correctly states the criteria for a census town?
o: Population above 5,000; at least 50% of male workers in non-agricultural activities; density at least 1,000 persons per sq km
Population above 10,000; at least 50% of workers in non-agricultural activities; density at least 200 persons per sq km
Population above 20,000; at least 75% of total workers in non-agricultural activities; density at least 400 persons per sq km
Population above 5,000; at least 75% of male workers in non-agricultural activities; density at least 400 persons per sq km
ne412520155c.x: A census town has a population exceeding 5,000, at least 75% of male workers engaged in non-agricultural work and a density of at least 400 persons per square kilometre.
ne412520155c.tq: Check all three numerical thresholds before selecting the combination.
xs: A census town needs population **≥5,000**, **≥75%** of **male workers** in non-agricultural work and density **≥400/sq km** — option **(4)**.
It is **administratively a village** that meets **all 3** criteria.
xa: ⚠ **Trap**: "**60%** of males" is wrong — correct is **75%** (**UPPSC 2010**).
**RGI** retains census towns for **Census 2027** despite **MoHUA's** objection.
**2011**: about **3,892** census towns vs **4,041** statutory towns.

n1f43dfa818a.s: How many population-size classes are used in the Census classification of Indian towns?
n1f43dfa818a.x: Indian towns are classified into six population-size classes, from Class I to Class VI.
n1f43dfa818a.tq: Recall the number of categories rather than the thresholds of one category.
xs: Census towns are grouped into **six** size classes, **Class I to VI** — option **(2) Six**.
This was the **CGPSC** answer "**06**".
xa: **Class I**: **1 lakh+**; **Class VI**: **below 5,000**.
**Class I cities hold 70%** of urban population (ES **2025-26**).
India has **53 million-plus** cities/UAs.

nfc7097bcb62.s: In absolute urban population, India ranks ____ in the world, after China and the United States.
nfc7097bcb62.x: India has the world's third-largest absolute urban population, after China and the United States.
xa: Urban population projected at about **60 crore by 2031**.
Cities to host nearly **a billion people by 2050**.
⚠ Satellite (**DEGURBA**) estimate puts India about **63%** urban.
nfc7097bcb62.fixed: India's urban population exceeds the total US population (y40fe7a854f4, y34b2b16bbb9), so India is 2nd, not 3rd

nb9136399bfe.s: How many million-plus cities were recorded in India in 2011?
nb9136399bfe.tq: Recall the census count while distinguishing it from the total number of towns.
xs: India had **53 million-plus** cities/UAs in **2011** — option **(3)**.
Largest UAs: **Greater Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata**.
xa: Highest slum share among million-plus: **Greater Visakhapatnam (~44%)**.
**Class I** = **1 lakh+**; Class I cities hold **70%** of urban population.
India is **3rd** in urban population after **China and USA**.

n4d8c309809b.s: India’s level of urbanisation increased from 27.81% in 2001 to approximately what level in 2011?
n4d8c309809b.x: The urbanisation rate rose from 27.81% in 2001 to 31.16% in 2011.
n4d8c309809b.tq: Compare the two census percentages and identify the later figure.
xs: Urbanisation rose from **27.81% (2001)** to **31.16% (2011)** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **31.80%** printed in some notes is wrong (**UPPSC 2023**).
xa: Urban population **37.71 crore** in **2011**; rural **68.84%**.
Phases: **slow 1901-31**, **medium 1931-61**, **rapid 1961 onward**.

n753eb8a4f1f.s: As per Census 2011, which was the least urbanised southern State?
n753eb8a4f1f.x: Andhra Pradesh, in the undivided-State comparison, had the lowest urbanisation level at about 33%, compared with Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
n753eb8a4f1f.tq: Use the comparison figures to separate the similar southern-State options.
xs: The least urbanised southern State (**2011**) was **Andhra Pradesh** (undivided, about **33%**) — option **(4)**.
Comparison: **TN ~48%**, **Kerala ~48%**, **Karnataka ~39%**.
xa: Yet **Greater Visakhapatnam** had the **highest slum share (~44%)** among million-plus cities.
Most urbanised State: **Goa (~62%)**; least: **Himachal Pradesh (~10%)**.
Highest decadal urban growth 2001-11: **Sikkim**.
n753eb8a4f1f.fixed: odd wording ('referred to in the comparative data')

n0c270de68a7.s: Which State recorded the highest decadal growth of urban population during 2001–2011?
n0c270de68a7.x: Sikkim recorded the highest decadal growth of urban population during 2001–2011.
n0c270de68a7.tq: Discriminate between a growth-rate fact and an urbanisation-level fact.
xs: **Sikkim** had the highest decadal urban growth in **2001-11** — option **(2)** (**UPPSC 2023**).
**Goa** was the **most urbanised** State (about **62%**), not the fastest-growing.
xa: Least urbanised: **Himachal Pradesh (~10%)**.
Least urbanised southern State: **Andhra Pradesh (~33%)**.
National level rose **27.81% → 31.16%**.

n2b01aec4b8d.s: When natural increase in rural and urban areas is broadly similar, the major component of urbanisation in India is:
n2b01aec4b8d.x: Migration is the major component of urbanisation when natural increase in rural and urban areas is broadly similar.
xa: Other causes: **industrialisation**, **commercialisation**, transport/communication, social change.
Also **natural growth** and **reclassification** (new towns).
**Population explosion + poverty-induced migration**.

nf1e3aac8309.s: Which one of the following is a governance-related urban challenge identified in India?
o: Complete fiscal autonomy of all cities
Absence of any panchayats in rapidly urbanising areas
Uniform administrative control over all urban local bodies
Fragmented authority and limited fiscal autonomy of cities
nf1e3aac8309.x: Fragmented authority and inadequate fiscal autonomy constrain city governance. Rapidly urbanising areas may also remain under panchayat administration.
nf1e3aac8309.tq: Use the governance lens to identify the institutional constraint.
xs: **Fragmented authority** and cities' **lack of fiscal autonomy** (ES **2025-26**) — option **(4)**.
Rapidly urbanising areas are often **left under panchayats** — so option (2) is wrong.
xa: **Property tax** is the most important own revenue of ULBs.
**Twelfth Schedule** lists **18 functions** for municipalities.
Official **31%** vs satellite **63%** — under-counting starves peri-urban areas of funds.

n0a5077cd01c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Finance Commission grants to urban local bodies?
o: All basic grants under the 16th FC are tied to sanitation, waste and water
Under the 15th FC, ULBs received 36% of local body grants
The 16th FC raises the urban share to 45%
Under the 16th FC, 80% is basic grant and 20% is performance grant
n0a5077cd01c.x: Only half of the basic grants are tied to sanitation, waste and water, not all of them. The other statements are correct.
xa: 16th FC: **Rs 3.6 lakh crore** ULBs vs **Rs 4.4 lakh crore** RLBs.
**Urbanisation Premium** for merging **peri-urban villages**.
**Local Finance Enquiry (1963)**: **K. Santhanam**.

ncf6679f9ab4.s: According to the UN World Urbanization Prospects, approximately what share of the world's population is projected to live in urban areas by 2050?
ncf6679f9ab4.x: The UN projects about 68% of the world to be urban by 2050 (a PYQ, linked to SDG 11). More than half (over 50%) of the world is already urban today, so 50% describes the present, not 2050; 58% and 80% are not the UN figures.
xs: The UN projects about **68 per cent** of the world urban by **2050** — option **(3)**.
**More than half** is already urban today (UNFPA SWOP), so **50%** is the present, not **2050**.
xa: It is a **PYQ** linked to **SDG 11**.
India's cities: nearly **a billion people by 2050**.

nd2007356a2c.s: The World Bank estimate cited for the number of slum dwellers in India is approximately
nd2007356a2c.x: The cited World Bank estimate places India’s slum-dwelling population at approximately 177 million, the largest such population in the world.
nd2007356a2c.tq: Separate the exact estimate from nearby rounded alternatives.
xs: The **World Bank** estimates **177 million** slum dwellers in India — the **largest in the world** — option **(3)**.
Highest slum share among million-plus (**2011**): **Greater Visakhapatnam ~44%**.
xa: **Greater Mumbai ~41%** and **Vijayawada ~41%**.
Urban **housing shortage**: about **18.78 million** units (**2012** Technical Group).
**Slum improvement** is a **Twelfth Schedule** function.

n9257d147ba6.s: According to Census 2011 data cited for million-plus cities, which city had the highest proportion of its population living in slums?
n9257d147ba6.x: Greater Visakhapatnam had the highest cited slum share among million-plus cities, at approximately 44%, compared with about 41% in Greater Mumbai and Vijayawada.
n9257d147ba6.tq: Compare close percentages instead of selecting the more famous city.
xs: **Greater Visakhapatnam** (about **44%**) had the highest slum share among million-plus cities — option **(3)**.
**Greater Mumbai** and **Vijayawada** were about **41%** each.
xa: ⚠ Trap: highest is **Visakhapatnam**, **not Mumbai**.
**177 million** slum dwellers in India (**World Bank**).
AP paradox: least urbanised southern State, yet highest slum share city.

nb7dca1badbd.s: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (2017) was formed by merging the Ministry of Urban Development with the Ministry of:
nb7dca1badbd.x: MoHUA was formed in 2017 by merging the Ministry of Urban Development and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation.
xa: That committee's chair: **Magunta Sreenivasulu Reddy**.
**RGI** still retains census towns for **Census 2027**.
First municipal bond: **Bangalore 1997**.

nc25b9bc4a20.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the most important source of own revenue of urban local bodies?
nc25b9bc4a20.x: Property tax is the most important source of own revenue for urban local bodies. Other sources include advertisement tax, professional tax, fees, fines and municipal enterprises.
nc25b9bc4a20.tq: Identify the principal item in a list of municipal revenue sources.
xs: **Property tax** is the most important own revenue of ULBs — option **(2)**.
Others: **advertisement tax**, **professional tax**, **octroi**, fees, fines, municipal enterprises.
xa: **State grants** come on top of own revenue.
**16th FC (2026-31)**: **Rs 3.6 lakh crore** for ULBs (**45%**).
First **municipal bond**: **Bangalore Mahanagara Palike (1997)**.

nceca033e486.s: The Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution contains how many functions assigned to municipalities?
nceca033e486.x: The Twelfth Schedule contains 18 functions relating to urban local governance.
nceca033e486.tq: Test the constitutional schedule number through a direct numerical recall question.
xs: The **Twelfth Schedule** has **18 functions** for municipalities — option **(2)**.
They include **urban planning**, **land-use regulation**, **water supply**, **public health and sanitation**, **slum improvement**.
xa: Also **urban poverty alleviation**, **fire services**, **urban forestry**, **vital statistics**.
**Property tax** is the main own revenue source.
**MoHUA** formed in **2017** by merging **MoUD and MoHUPA**.

n57698fa5645.s: Which urban local body issued the first municipal bond in India?
n57698fa5645.x: The first municipal bond in India was issued by Bangalore Mahanagara Palike in 1997.
n57698fa5645.tq: Match the pioneering institution with the year-specific financial innovation.
xs: India's first municipal bond: **Bangalore Mahanagara Palike** in **1997** — option **(3)**.
**Ahmedabad (1998)** was the first **without a State guarantee**.
xa: **Budget 2026-27**: **Rs 100 crore** incentive for a single issue above **Rs 1,000 crore**.
**City Economic Regions**: **Rs 5,000 crore per CER** over **5 years**.
**MoHUA** formed **2017**.

n6e426411ded.s: Which municipal corporation was the first in India to issue a municipal bond without a State Government guarantee?
n6e426411ded.x: Ahmedabad was the first municipal corporation to issue a municipal bond without a State Government guarantee, in 1998.
n6e426411ded.tq: Discriminate between the first municipal bond and the first bond issued without a State guarantee.
xs: **Ahmedabad** (**1998**) issued the first municipal bond **without a State guarantee** — option **(1)**.
⚠ The very first municipal bond was **Bangalore Mahanagara Palike (1997)**.
xa: **Budget 2026-27**: **Rs 100 crore** incentive for an issue above **Rs 1,000 crore**.
**Property tax** is the most important own revenue.
**CERs** get **Rs 5,000 crore** each over **5 years**.

n99d2de06e92.s: The Local Finance Enquiry Committee of 1963, which examined the finances of local bodies, was chaired by:
n99d2de06e92.x: K. Santhanam chaired the Local Finance Enquiry Committee (1963). Balwantrai Mehta (1957) and Ashok Mehta (1977-78) headed committees on panchayati raj; A. D. Gorwala chaired the All India Rural Credit Survey Committee (1951).
xs: The **Local Finance Enquiry Committee (1963)** was chaired by **K. Santhanam** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **A.D. Gorwala** chaired the **All India Rural Credit Survey Committee** (RBI, **1951**), not this one.
xa: **Property tax** is the most important own revenue of ULBs.
**15th FC**: ULBs got **36%** of local body grants.
**16th FC**: **45%**, with an **Urbanisation Premium**.

n044e0155d99.s: Under-counting of urbanisation in India is criticised mainly because it may:
o: Starve peri-urban areas of municipal funds
n044e0155d99.x: Under-counting can leave peri-urban areas outside municipal planning and finance, starving them of municipal funds.
xa: **16th FC** offers an **Urbanisation Premium** for merging **peri-urban villages**.
**RGI** retains census towns for **Census 2027** despite MoHUA's objection.

n6b94f03deed.s: Which Sustainable Development Goal is most directly associated with UN-Habitat’s urban-settlement mandate?
n6b94f03deed.x: SDG 11 seeks to make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable, directly corresponding to the UN-Habitat mandate.
n6b94f03deed.tq: Match the specialised agency’s mandate with the relevant SDG.
xs: **SDG 11** — **Sustainable Cities and Communities** — matches UN-Habitat's mandate — option **(2)**.
**UN-Habitat** (UN Human Settlements Programme) was set up in **1978** after **Habitat I (Vancouver, 1976)**.
xa: UN-Habitat HQ: **Nairobi**; publishes the **World Cities Report**.
About **68%** of the world urban by **2050** (PYQ linked to SDG 11).
A **UN-Habitat CoE** is to be set up in **Amaravati**.

n556e0e9b826.s: The concept of ‘Right to the City’ is associated with which thinker?
n556e0e9b826.x: The concept of the Right to the City was articulated by Henri Lefebvre in 1968.
n556e0e9b826.tq: Match the concept with its originator and associated year.
xs: **Right to the City** is **Henri Lefebvre's** idea (**1968**) — option **(3)**.
It means residents, **including migrant workers**, can **shape and live in the city**.
xa: Adopted in the **New Urban Agenda** at **Habitat III (Quito, 2016)**.
**Habitat I**: **Vancouver 1976**; **UN-Habitat HQ**: **Nairobi**.
**APMCHUD**: first meet **New Delhi, 2006**.

nede5aff3e75.s: The Right to the City was adopted in the New Urban Agenda at
nede5aff3e75.x: The Right to the City was adopted in the New Urban Agenda at Habitat III, held in Quito in 2016.
nede5aff3e75.tq: Match the forum, location and year without confusing the Habitat conferences.
xs: Right to the City entered the **New Urban Agenda** at **Habitat III, Quito, 2016** — option **(2)**.
**Habitat I** was at **Vancouver** in **1976** (option 3) — it led to UN-Habitat in **1978**.
xa: Concept by **Henri Lefebvre** (**1968**).
⚠ Habitat I = **Vancouver 1976**; Habitat III = **Quito 2016**; HQ = **Nairobi**.
**SDG 11**: Sustainable Cities and Communities.

nd2715ab1771.s: DEGURBA-based estimates of India's 'hidden urbanisation' put India at about what per cent urban?
nd2715ab1771.x: DEGURBA-based estimates cited by the EAC-PM put India at about 63% urban, far above the Census figure.
xa: Debate: India **under-counts** urbanisation, starving **peri-urban** areas of municipal funds.
**16th FC** gives an **Urbanisation Premium** for merging peri-urban villages.

nfc1ddb51439.s: In the context of Satavahana administration, the term 'Nigama Sabha' referred to
o: A military council of the Satavahana kings
nfc1ddb51439.x: Nigama Sabha denoted city administration under the Satavahanas and is mentioned in the Nanaghat inscription.
nfc1ddb51439.tq: Discriminate between an urban administrative institution and other possible historical bodies.
xs: **Nigama Sabha** was the **city administration** under the **Satavahanas** — option **(1)**.
It is known from the **Nanaghat inscription**.
xa: Modern AP capital: **Amaravati** (AP Capital Region).
Today's urban functions are listed in the **Twelfth Schedule** (**18 functions**).
**Right to the City** (**Henri Lefebvre**, **1968**) is the modern idea of citizen participation.

n656bb554bfc.s: Andhra Pradesh signed an MoU with UN-Habitat for a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs at:
n656bb554bfc.x: The MoU with UN-Habitat concerns a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs in Amaravati.
xa: **UN-Habitat**: set up **1978**, HQ **Nairobi**, publishes the **World Cities Report**.
**APMCHUD** first met in **New Delhi** (**2006**).
⚠ Habitat I = **Vancouver 1976**; Habitat III = **Quito 2016**.

nf2468a7bb22.s: Which of the following is NOT a thrust area of AMRUT?
nf2468a7bb22.x: AMRUT’s thrust areas include water supply, sewerage and septage, storm-water drains, green spaces and parks, non-motorised transport and capacity building. Crop procurement is unrelated.
nf2468a7bb22.tq: Separate urban-service components from an agricultural-sector activity.
xs: **Crop procurement** is not an AMRUT thrust area — option **(2)**.
Thrust areas: **water supply; sewerage and septage; storm-water drains; green spaces and parks; non-motorised urban transport; capacity building**.
xa: **AMRUT 2.0**: **100% sewerage/septage** in the **500** AMRUT cities.
Urban **tap connectivity** up **64% since 2011**.
Projects worth **Rs 2.79 lakh crore** sanctioned under AMRUT + 2.0.

n1d5a9f19507.s: AMRUT 2.0 (2021 to 2025-26) seeks universal water supply in:
n1d5a9f19507.x: AMRUT 2.0 aims at universal water supply in all statutory towns.

AP has **38,862 tanks** with a registered ayacut of **25.60 lakh acres**.
⚠ AP tanks show a **57%** utilisation gap.

n56ed6a9a5f4.s: The Right Canal of Nagarjuna Sagar is known as the:

⚠ **Polavaram** is on the **Godavari**, unlike Galeru-Nagari and Veligonda (Krishna).
**Upper Ganga Canal** = UP, Ganga at **Haridwar**; **Sirhind** = Punjab, Sutlej at **Ropar**.

nbab16611e4d.s: Minor irrigation provides about what share of India's irrigated area?
nbab16611e4d.x: Minor irrigation (CCA up to 2,000 ha) provides about 65% of India's irrigated area.
xa: **Minor** projects: CCA **up to 2,000 ha**; in AP, ayacut up to **5,000 acres**.

**AIBP** speeds up ongoing **major/medium** projects.

n1ab02d5905e.s: Under PM-KUSUM, solarisation of grid-connected pumps, including feeder-level solarisation, falls under:
n1ab02d5905e.x: Component C covers grid-connected pump solarisation; Component A is 10,000 MW of decentralised plants and Component B the 14 lakh standalone pumps.
xa: Component B pumps are up to **7.5 HP**, replace diesel pumps; none in **dark groundwater zones**.
AP Component-C: **228 plants of 1,162.80 MW**; completion by **Dec 2026**.
PM-KUSUM: **MNRE**, **2019**; JPSC PYQ called it an "agricultural solar pump system".

ned80fba2003.s: The Indira Gandhi Canal draws its water from the:
o: Krishna through the Nagarjuna Sagar reservoir
Harike barrage on the Sutlej–Beas system
ned80fba2003.x: The Indira Gandhi Canal originates at Harike barrage on the Sutlej–Beas system and runs in Rajasthan.
ned80fba2003.tq: Match the canal with its specific source location rather than only the river system.
xs: The **Indira Gandhi Canal** draws water from the **Harike barrage on the Sutlej-Beas** system (Punjab) — option **(2)** is correct.
It irrigates **Rajasthan** and is about **650 km** long.
**Ganga at Haridwar** feeds the **Upper Ganga Canal** (UP); **Sutlej at Ropar** feeds the **Sirhind Canal** (Punjab).
The **Krishna** via Nagarjuna Sagar feeds the **Nagarjuna Sagar canals** (AP / Telangana).
xa: Nagarjuna Sagar **Right** canal = **Jawahar canal**; **Left** = **Lal Bahadur Shastri canal**.
⚠ Harike (Sutlej-Beas) = Indira Gandhi Canal; Ropar (Sutlej) = Sirhind Canal.

nb80c77e0f81.s: The Polavaram project was recently reported to be about what per cent complete?
nb80c77e0f81.x: Polavaram was reported 89% complete and targeted for dedication by March 2027.

**194.6 TMC** storage; **960 MW**; **7.20 lakh acres**.

o: Andhra Pradesh Watershed and Land Taxation Act, 2005
Andhra Pradesh Water and Irrigation Regulation Act, 2015
Andhra Pradesh Water Allocation and Land Tenure Act, 2002

ne08a126a83d.x: APWALTA is the Andhra Pradesh Water, Land and Trees Act, 2002, which addresses issues including indiscriminate borewell digging.
ne08a126a83d.tq: Test the exact expansion and year of a similar-looking statutory acronym.
xs: **APWALTA** = **Andhra Pradesh Water, Land and Trees Act, 2002** — option **(4)** is correct.

n72fe06b17f6.s: Atal Bhujal Yojana was launched in December 2019 as a World Bank-aided:
o: State Sector scheme under the Ministry of Rural Development
Central Sector scheme under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Central Sector scheme under the Ministry of Jal Shakti
Centrally Sponsored Scheme under the Ministry of Agriculture
n72fe06b17f6.x: Atal Bhujal Yojana was launched in December 2019 as a World Bank-aided Central Sector scheme under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
n72fe06b17f6.tq: Identify the correct ministry and scheme classification together.
xs: **Atal Bhujal Yojana** is a World Bank-aided **Central Sector scheme under the Ministry of Jal Shakti** — option **(3)** is correct.
It was launched in **Dec 2019** with an outlay of **₹6,000 crore** (World Bank loan **₹3,000 crore**).
It is not a Centrally Sponsored or State Sector scheme, and not under MoEFCC, Rural Development or Agriculture.
xa: Focus: **demand-side** community management via **GP-level Water Security Plans**.
Coverage: **7 states** — Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, MP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, UP.
Ended **March 2026**; **AP is among 5 states in Phase II** (about **₹500 crore**).
⚠ Atal Bhujal = **Jal Shakti**; PM-KUSUM = **MNRE**.

n75c3bb2d227.s: Which of the following States was NOT among the seven States covered by Atal Bhujal Yojana?
n75c3bb2d227.x: The seven States covered were Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. Andhra Pradesh was not included in that list.
n75c3bb2d227.tq: Test membership in a specified list by identifying the excluded State.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** was not among Atal Bhujal's **7 states** — option **(3)** is the answer.
The 7 states: **Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, MP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, UP** — so Gujarat, Haryana and Rajasthan were covered.
xa: ⚠ AP joins only in **Phase II** — among **5 states**, about **₹500 crore**.
The scheme ended **March 2026**.
Launched **Dec 2019**; World Bank-aided, Ministry of **Jal Shakti**.

n1960f55ed21.s: The principal focus of Atal Bhujal Yojana is:
o: Demand-side community management through Gram Panchayat Water Security Plans
n1960f55ed21.x: Atal Bhujal focuses on demand-side groundwater management through community participation and Gram Panchayat-level Water Security Plans.
xa: Outlay **₹6,000 crore** (World Bank loan **₹3,000 crore**).
Covered **7 states**; ended **March 2026**.
⚠ Atal Bhujal = **Jal Shakti** (demand-side groundwater); PM-KUSUM = **MNRE** (solar pumps).

ndf61dcf2132.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Water, Land and Trees Act (APWALTA), 2002, rainwater harvesting structures are mandatory on plots of:
ndf61dcf2132.x: APWALTA requires rainwater harvesting on plots of 200 sq m and above (PYQ key). The other thresholds are not the ones in the Act.
xs: APWALTA requires **rainwater harvesting** on plots of **200 sq m and above** — option **(1)** is correct (PYQ key).
APWALTA = **AP Water, Land and Trees Act, 2002**, against indiscriminate **borewell** digging.
xa: **Over-exploited villages** are notified for strict regulation.
GEC 2024-25 proposed **258 villages**; GEC 2023-24 had **300**.
AP groundwater: **41%** of gross irrigated area, about **19 lakh borewells**.

n1ae33c59fd2.s: The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM) was launched in 2019 under the:
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
n1ae33c59fd2.x: PM-KUSUM was launched in 2019 under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE).
n1ae33c59fd2.tq: Use the ministry-allocation trap by distinguishing MNRE from agriculture and water ministries.
xs: **PM-KUSUM** was launched in **2019** under the **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **Jal Shakti** runs **Atal Bhujal**, not PM-KUSUM.
xa: Central support **₹34,422 crore**; target **34,800 MW**.
Objective: **de-dieselise agriculture** + add farmer income.
AP Component-C: **228 plants** of **1,162.80 MW**, completion by **Dec 2026**.

na0384ebf458.s: The principal aim of PM-KUSUM in agriculture is to:
o: De-dieselise agriculture and add to farmers' income
na0384ebf458.x: PM-KUSUM seeks to de-dieselise agriculture while adding to farmers' income through solar energy.
xa: JPSC PYQ described it as an "**agricultural solar pump system**".
Launched **2019** under **MNRE**; central support **₹34,422 crore**, **34,800 MW** target.
⚠ Criticism: solar pumps may drive **groundwater over-draw**; outcomes depend on local hydrogeology.

nb6c84013538.s: The Andhra Pradesh Micro Irrigation Project (APMIP) has been in operation since:
nb6c84013538.tq: Identify the programme’s starting year rather than confusing it with project foundation or PMKSY dates.
xs: **APMIP** has been running since **2003** — option **(3)** is correct.
It covers **42.25 lakh acres** and **15.09 lakh farmers**.
xa: **Rayalaseema** = **64%** of APMIP area.
Earlier coverage figure: **37.90 lakh acres**.
AP ranks **1st** in **micro-irrigation**.

n629a6e0dea3.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stage-of-extraction category used in the Central Ground Water Board assessment?
n629a6e0dea3.x: The CGWB categories are Safe, Semi-critical, Critical, Over-exploited and Saline. 'Adequately exploited' is not one of the listed categories.
n629a6e0dea3.tq: Find the plausible-sounding term that is absent from the official classification.
xs: **"Adequately exploited"** is not a CGWB stage-of-extraction category — option **(3)** is the answer.
The CGWB categories are **Safe, Semi-critical, Critical, Over-exploited**, plus **Saline**.
So **Semi-critical**, **Critical** and **Safe** are all valid categories.
xa: India's stage of extraction: **60.63%** (2025), up from **60.47%** (2024).
AP mandals (CGWB 2025 report): **12** over-exploited, **3** critical, **24** semi-critical, **39** saline, **601** safe, of **679**.
AP as a whole: **31.5% (Safe)**.

nca8ef684ab2.s: Groundwater meets about what share of India's irrigation needs?
nca8ef684ab2.x: Groundwater meets about 64% of India's irrigation needs; India accounts for about 25% of global groundwater extraction.
xa: CGWB categories: **Safe, Semi-critical, Critical, Over-exploited**, + Saline.
Tubewells are **47.3%** of India's net irrigated area (2021-22).

n5f4151d21ea.s: As per the Ground Water Estimation for Andhra Pradesh (GEC 2024-25), the State's stage of groundwater development is:
n5f4151d21ea.x: AP's stage of development is 31.5%, which is Safe; only 12 of its 679 mandals are over-exploited. 60.63% is India's all-India stage of extraction (2025), and 64% is groundwater's share of India's irrigation needs; AP as a whole is not over-exploited.
xs: AP's stage of groundwater development (GEC 2024-25) is **31.5%**, in the **Safe** category — option **(1)** is correct.
**60.63%** is India's all-India stage of extraction (2025), not AP's.
**64%** is groundwater's share of India's irrigation needs; AP as a whole is not over-exploited.
xa: Of AP's **679 mandals**: **12** over-exploited, **3** critical, **24** semi-critical, **39** saline, **601** safe.
APWALTA over-exploited villages: **258** proposed (GEC 2024-25).
CGWB categories: **Safe, Semi-critical, Critical, Over-exploited**, + Saline.

ncb3b6fb3af4.s: Per capita annual water availability below 1,700 cubic metres is classified as:
ncb3b6fb3af4.x: Per capita annual water availability below 1,700 m³ is treated as water-stressed.
ncb3b6fb3af4.tq: Separate the water-stressed threshold from the lower water-scarce threshold.
xs: Availability below **1,700 m³** per person per year is **water-stressed** — option **(4)** is correct.
Below **1,000 m³** is the stricter **water-scarce** level.
xa: ⚠ **1,700** = stressed; **1,000** = scarce; India is already below **1,700**.
Expected **1,341 m³ in 2025** → **1,140 m³ by 2050**, heading towards scarcity.

n893594b2a47.s: Per capita annual water availability below which level is classified as water-scarce?
n893594b2a47.x: Availability below 1,000 m³ per person per year is classified as water-scarce.
n893594b2a47.tq: Use threshold discrimination between two closely related classifications.
xs: Availability below **1,000 m³** per person per year is **water-scarce** — option **(1)** is correct.
**1,700 m³** is the **water-stressed** line, not the scarcity line.
xa: India's projected availability: **1,341 m³ in 2025** and **1,140 m³ by 2050**.
⚠ India is already below **1,700** (stressed) and heading towards **1,000** (scarce).

n86ba530552f.s: Which State was the first to make rooftop rainwater harvesting compulsory for all buildings?
n86ba530552f.x: Tamil Nadu was the first State to make rooftop rainwater harvesting compulsory for all buildings.
