**Meghalaya**'s first was a different one: first to approve a **draft State Water Policy**.
**AP**'s equivalent is **APWALTA 2002**.
xa: APWALTA requires rainwater harvesting on plots of **200 sq m** and above.
⚠ Meghalaya = first **State Water Policy** (APPSC 2019); Tamil Nadu = first **compulsory rooftop RWH**.

n8319ca39ea4.s: Which was the first State in India to approve a draft State Water Policy?
n8319ca39ea4.x: Meghalaya was the first State to approve a draft State Water Policy (APPSC 2019 key). Tamil Nadu was first to make rooftop rainwater harvesting compulsory; Andhra Pradesh's measure is APWALTA 2002; Gujarat tops the Composite Water Management Index.
n8319ca39ea4.tq: Water policy first = Meghalaya; rooftop RWH first = Tamil Nadu.
xs: **Meghalaya** was the first state to approve a draft **State Water Policy** — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC 2019 PYQ key).
**Tamil Nadu** was first to make **rooftop rainwater harvesting** compulsory.
**AP**'s measure is **APWALTA 2002**; **Gujarat** tops the **CWMI**.
xa: National Water Policy: **1987**, **2002**, **2012** (in force).
NWP-2012 wants a **Water Regulatory Authority in each state**.

nd0711b1e13e.s: The Ministry of Jal Shakti was formed in May 2019 by merging the Ministry of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation with the:
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation
nd0711b1e13e.x: In May 2019, the Ministry of Jal Shakti was formed by merging the Ministry of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation with the Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation.

xs: **Ministry of Jal Shakti** (**May 2019**) merged MoWR, RD&GR with the **Ministry of Drinking Water & Sanitation** — option **(4)** is correct.

6th edition launched **22 Mar 2025**: "**Jal Sanchay, Jan Bhagidari: Jan Jagrukta Ki Or**".
**Atal Bhujal** and other groundwater work fall under Jal Shakti.

n1617aa9386c.s: The Command Area Development Programme was launched in:

n0ae1beb5304.s: Which of the following is NOT a component associated with Command Area Development?
n0ae1beb5304.x: Field channels, drains, land levelling and Water Users' Associations are components of Command Area Development. Coal-mine reclamation is unrelated.

xs: **Coal-mine reclamation** is not a CAD component — option **(1)** is the answer.

**27** CAD&WM projects under LTIF are complete; **22.21 lakh ha** of CCA developed.

n2b9a195bd58.s: Command Area Development and Water Management (CADWM) operates under:
n2b9a195bd58.x: CADWM runs under PMKSY–Har Khet Ko Pani; new approvals stopped after 2021-22 and only ongoing works continue.
xa: **27** CAD&WM projects under LTIF complete; **22.21 lakh ha** developed.
AP: **7 CADWM projects**, CCA **1,78,620 ha**, **no physical progress in Apr-Dec 2025**.
Successor: **M-CADWM** from **2025-26**.

nc1d5de50c6d.s: The Task Force on Inter-Linking of Rivers was set up in 2002 under the chairmanship of:
o: The Chief Minister of the concerned State

nc1d5de50c6d.tq: Identify the person associated with the institutional event.
xs: The **2002 Task Force on Inter-Linking of Rivers** was headed by **Suresh Prabhu** — option **(3)** is correct.

**Ken-Betwa** is the **first NPP link** to be implemented.

n0983326f4d9.s: The National Water Resources Council is chaired by the:
n0983326f4d9.x: The National Water Resources Council is chaired by the Prime Minister; Chief Ministers are its members.
n0983326f4d9.tq: Identify the correct constitutional executive associated with the council.
xs: The **NWRC** is chaired by the **Prime Minister** — option **(4)** is correct (UPSC 2009 PYQ).
**Chief Ministers** are its members; it **adopts the National Water Policy**.
xa: National Water Policy editions: **1987** → **2002** → **2012**; **NWP-2012** is in force.
**Ministry of Jal Shakti** was formed in **May 2019**.
AP CM Naidu asked for **Godavari-Cauvery** to be a **national project**.

n61c7664d484.x: K.L. Rao proposed the Ganga–Cauvery link; Arthur Cotton first conceived river-linking in the 19th century and Suresh Prabhu headed the 2002 Task Force.
xa: ⚠ Some notes (**16 Jul 2026**) call K.L. Rao's idea a "**Godavari-Cauvery**" link.
AP CM Naidu asked for **Godavari-Cauvery** as a **national project**.

n54b770c9ee3.s: Which of the following is a criticism of the National River Linking Project?

It prevents displacement by avoiding reservoir construction
Surplus river basins may become unreliable because of climate change
It depends only on groundwater and not on river basins

xs: **Climate change** may make "**surplus**" basins unreliable — option **(3)** is correct.
River-linking is criticised for **displacement** and **ecological loss**, the reverse of options (1) and (2).
xa: **Ken-Betwa**: **10 villages** to be submerged; **Adivasi groups** resisting.
Daudhan dam lies inside **Panna Tiger Reserve**.

nd9952177a02.s: Which of the following is the first National Perspective Plan link to be implemented?
nd9952177a02.x: The Ken–Betwa Link Project is the first National Perspective Plan link to be implemented.
nd9952177a02.tq: Identify the first implemented project, not merely a proposed link.
xs: **Ken–Betwa (KBLP)** is the **first NPP link to be implemented** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Godavari-Cauvery** and **Modified Parbati-Kalisindh-Chambal** are other priority links; **Vamsadhara-Nagavali** is an AP intra-state link.
xa: Ken-Betwa: **MP-UP**; tripartite MoA **March 2021**.
Cost **₹44,605 crore** (Central **₹39,317 crore**).
Daudhan dam is inside **Panna Tiger Reserve**.

n929feb5e4de.s: Daudhan Dam, associated with the Ken–Betwa Link Project, is located inside the:
n929feb5e4de.x: The Daudhan Dam is located inside the Panna Tiger Reserve.
n929feb5e4de.tq: Match the project structure with its protected-area location.
xs: **Daudhan dam** of Ken-Betwa lies inside the **Panna Tiger Reserve** — option **(2)** is correct.

xa: Ken-Betwa is the **first NPP link** implemented; **MP-UP**.
**10 villages** to be submerged; **Adivasi groups** resisting.
Tripartite MoA **March 2021**; **₹44,605 crore**.

n66a8b1603c1.s: In the Godavari–Cauvery link proposal, the Krishna (Nagarjunasagar)–Pennar link ends at:
n66a8b1603c1.x: The three links are Godavari (Inchampalli)–Krishna (Nagarjunasagar), Krishna (Nagarjunasagar)–Pennar (Somasila) and Pennar (Somasila)–Cauvery (Grand Anicut).

n32fae12962b.s: The Pattiseema lift project links Polavaram with the:

ne021f0fdc33.s: The Krishna basin water diverted through Polavaram feeds which projects for the benefit of Rayalaseema?

xs: The diverted water feeds **HNSS and GNSS** for **Rayalaseema** — option **(1)** is correct.
Polavaram diverts **80 TMC** of Godavari water to the Krishna basin.

**Veligonda Phase-I** (**31 Aug 2026**) brought Krishna water to **Nallamala Sagar**.

n3c6b5137b83.s: Direct Seeded Rice can save up to how much water?
n3c6b5137b83.x: Direct Seeded Rice (like SRI) can save up to 50% water.

**ZBNF** promotes **mulching** and **contour farming**.

n13a6a437935.s: Which of the following is NOT a focus area of the National Water Policy, 2012?
o: Complete replacement of State water institutions by a single Union authority
n13a6a437935.x: The policy focuses on recycling and reuse, micro-irrigation incentives and community participation, among other measures. It does not prescribe complete replacement of State water institutions by one Union authority.
n13a6a437935.tq: Find the institutional extreme that is absent from the policy focus areas.
xs: **Replacing state water institutions with one Union authority** is not an NWP-2012 focus — option **(4)** is the answer.
NWP-2012 instead wants a **Water Regulatory Authority in each state**.
**Recycling and reuse**, **micro-irrigation incentives** and **community participation** are listed focus areas.
xa: Other focus areas: **national water framework law**, **benchmarks for water use**, arresting **groundwater decline** in over-exploited areas.
Water = **Entry 17, State List**; inter-state rivers = **Entry 56, Union List**.

n3d71a5adc73.s: The headline target of the National Water Mission is to raise water-use efficiency by:
n3d71a5adc73.x: The National Water Mission has a headline target of increasing water-use efficiency by 20%.
n3d71a5adc73.tq: Recall the exact percentage rather than the nearby round-number distractors.
xs: The **National Water Mission** aims to raise **water-use efficiency by 20%** — option **(3)** is correct.

n318f5bc03aa.x: IR-8 rice originated from the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) in the Philippines.
n318f5bc03aa.tq: Use institution–country association to distinguish rice research from wheat research.
xs: **IR-8** rice came from **IRRI, Philippines** — option **(4)** is correct.
The **M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation** was set up only in **1988**, long after IR-8.
xa: Wheat HYVs: **Kalyan Sona**, **Sonalika** (Borlaug's Mexican dwarf wheats).
Indian rice institutes: **CRRI** (now National Rice Research Institute), **Cuttack**; **IIRR**, **Hyderabad**.
AP rice station: **RARS Maruteru**.

ne83cba1e081.s: The HYV programme became full-fledged from 1966 following which combination of circumstances?
o: Introduction of the WTO and the launch of PMKSY
Two successive drought years, decline in foodgrain output and dependence on PL-480
A sharp rise in foodgrain output and complete food self-sufficiency
Abolition of irrigation projects and withdrawal of fertiliser subsidies
ne83cba1e081.x: The programme became full-fledged from 1966 after the 1965-66 and 1966-67 droughts, foodgrain production fell to 72.3 and 74.2 MT, and India depended on PL-480 supplies.
ne83cba1e081.tq: Connect the policy response with the crisis conditions that necessitated it.
xs: The HYV programme went full-fledged in **1966** after **two drought years**, a **fall in foodgrain output** and **PL-480** dependence — option **(2)** is correct.
The **1965-66** and **1966-67** droughts cut foodgrains to **72.3** and **74.2 MT**.
xa: The programme ran in the **Annual Plans (1966-69)**, with agricultural growth of **4.16%**.
In **1966**, **18,000 t** of Mexican wheat was imported into Punjab.
Wheat output then rose from **5** to **17 MT**.

naa09bdd0a6f.s: Punjab is called the 'Granary of India' because it was the pioneer State of the:
naa09bdd0a6f.x: Punjab was the pioneer State of the Green Revolution and is hence called the 'Granary of India'.
xa: Wheat production rose from **5** to **17 MT**.
Wheat HYVs: **Kalyan Sona**, **Sonalika**.
⚠ Indian Institute of **Maize** Research is at **Ludhiana** — same acronym **IIMR** as Millets Research (Hyderabad).

n6235e627a03.s: Which of the following was NOT part of the focus of the proposed Second Green Revolution?
o: Exclusive expansion of chemical pesticide use
n6235e627a03.x: The Second Green Revolution focused on pulses, oilseeds, millets, precision farming and micro-irrigation, not on expanding chemical pesticide use.
xa: Also: **climate-resilient varieties** (UPSC Env p.256).
**IPM** combines biological, cultural and need-based chemical control to **cut pesticide use**.

n8abe51eb84f.s: From 2022-23, the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) was merged into:
n8abe51eb84f.x: NMSA, one of the eight NAPCC missions, was merged into PM-RKVY from 2022-23.
xa: Another component: **Rainfed Area Development** (Integrated Farming Systems).
**Soil Health Cards** are issued **free every two years** under NMSA.

nf32b0254d59.s: PMKSY is best described as a/an:
o: Umbrella Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2015–16
nf32b0254d59.x: The Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana is an umbrella Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2015–16.
nf32b0254d59.tq: Check both the scheme structure and the launch period.
xs: **PMKSY** is an **umbrella Centrally Sponsored scheme**, launched **2015-16** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is neither State-funded nor a Central Sector scheme.
xa: Components: **AIBP**, **Har Khet Ko Pani**, **Watershed (WDC-PMKSY 2.0)**, **Per Drop More Crop**.
Over **10 years**: **27 million** farmers benefited; **24.61 Mha** covered.
**M-CADWM** sub-scheme: **2025-26**, **₹1,600 crore**.

n239f2839b8f.s: The World Bank-aided National Agricultural Technology Project (NATP) was launched in:
n239f2839b8f.x: NATP began in 1998 with World Bank aid; its successor NAIP ran from 2006 to 2014.
xa: NAIP components: **ICAR as a catalyst for change**, **production-to-consumption research**, **sustainable rural livelihood security**, **basic and strategic research**.
**ATMA** (**2005**) is a district extension society.

n3d969b1350c.s: The Indian Institute of Millets Research is located at:
n3d969b1350c.x: IIMR, like IIRR and IIOR, is located at Hyderabad.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** Indian Institute of **Maize** Research (also **IIMR**) is at **Ludhiana**.
**ICRISAT** is at **Patancheru**, Hyderabad.
**CTRI** is at **Rajahmundry**.

n54423e622e4.s: The first Krishi Vigyan Kendra was set up in 1974 at:
n54423e622e4.x: The first KVK was set up at Puducherry in 1974 on the Mohan Singh Mehta Committee's recommendation.
xa: Upgrade plan: **300 KVKs by March 2027**.
Entrepreneurship centres in all KVKs by **Dec 2028**.

n6ba40da0c11.s: The HYV wheat varieties associated with Norman Borlaug’s Mexican dwarf wheats include:
n6ba40da0c11.x: Kalyan Sona and Sonalika were associated with HYV wheat derived from Norman Borlaug’s Mexican dwarf wheats.
n6ba40da0c11.tq: Link the person, crop and specific varieties in a name-based agricultural question.
xs: **Norman Borlaug**'s Mexican dwarf wheats gave **Kalyan Sona** and **Sonalika** — option **(2)** is correct.
**IR-8** is a **rice** variety from **IRRI, Philippines**, not a wheat.
xa: In **1966**, **18,000 t** of Mexican wheat was imported and crossed with local varieties in **Punjab**.
Wheat production rose from **5** to **17 MT**.
**C. Subramaniam** was the Agriculture Minister who drove the policy shift.

n8e48df40af2.s: Which Union Agriculture Minister drove the policy shift towards the Green Revolution in India?
n8e48df40af2.x: C. Subramaniam, as Union Agriculture Minister, drove the shift; Borlaug and Swaminathan had scientific roles and Kurien led the White Revolution.
xa: PM **Manmohan Singh** called for a **Second Green Revolution** (APPSC 2025).
**Subhash Palekar** developed **ZBNF**.
**Amit Shah** launched **Nano DAP** in **April 2023**.

n4dac1814082.s: The call for a Second Green Revolution in India was made by:
n4dac1814082.x: The call for a Second Green Revolution was made by PM Manmohan Singh (APPSC 2025). M.S. Swaminathan coined the related term 'Evergreen Revolution', and Norman Borlaug is linked with the original Mexican dwarf wheats.
n4dac1814082.tq: Match the policy call with the person associated with it, avoiding confusion with agricultural scientists.
xs: PM **Manmohan Singh** called for a **Second Green Revolution** — option **(4)** is correct (APPSC 2025).
**M.S. Swaminathan** coined "**Evergreen Revolution**"; **Norman Borlaug** gave Mexican dwarf wheats.
xa: ⚠ **Swaminathan** = Evergreen Revolution term; **Manmohan Singh** = Second Green Revolution call.
Second GR focus: **pulses, oilseeds, millets (Shree Anna)**, **precision farming**, **micro-irrigation**.

n576928b5a11.s: The concept of the Evergreen Revolution, associated with M.S. Swaminathan, refers to:
o: Replacement of all traditional crops by HYV crops
Permanent increase in productivity without ecological harm
Expansion of agriculture only through irrigation-intensive farming
Continuous use of chemical inputs irrespective of environmental effects
n576928b5a11.x: The Evergreen Revolution means productivity improvement in perpetuity without ecological harm.
n576928b5a11.tq: Identify the definition by combining productivity growth with ecological sustainability.
xs: "**Evergreen Revolution**" = **productivity improvement in perpetuity without ecological harm** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is the opposite of continuous chemical use regardless of environment.
xa: Coined by **M.S. Swaminathan** (PYQ key).
⚠ Second Green Revolution call = PM **Manmohan Singh**.
**MSSRF** was set up in **1988**.

n9512c5b076f.s: Zero Budget Natural Farming was developed by:
o: The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority
n9512c5b076f.x: Zero Budget Natural Farming was developed by Subhash Palekar. Rythu Sadhikara Samstha only runs AP's natural-farming programme (APCNF), and APEDA handles NPOP organic certification.
n9512c5b076f.tq: Match the farming approach with its named proponent, not its implementing organisation.
xs: **Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF)** was developed by **Subhash Palekar** — option **(4)** is correct (UPSC Env p.259).
**Rythu Sadhikara Samstha (RySS)** runs AP's **APCNF**; **APEDA** handles **NPOP**; the **PPV&FR Authority** protects breeders.
xa: **APCNF** uses **jeevamrutham** and **ghanajeevamrutham**.
APCNF covers **10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha** (2025-26).
⚠ Swaminathan = "Evergreen Revolution"; Palekar = ZBNF.

n7024a0a8895.s: Which fertiliser receives the heaviest subsidy in India?
n7024a0a8895.x: Urea receives the heaviest fertiliser subsidy. Its price is controlled and kept artificially cheap, encouraging excessive nitrogen use.
n7024a0a8895.tq: Use the direct one-word identification of the highest-subsidy fertiliser.
xs: **Urea** is the most subsidised fertiliser — option **(4)** is correct.
Its price is controlled and kept **artificially cheap** → **nitrogen overuse**.
**DAP, MOP, SSP** are decontrolled **P&K** fertilisers under **NBS**.
xa: N:P:K ratio **10.9:4.1:1** (2023-24) vs ideal **4:2:1** — driven by cheap urea.
**Neem-coated urea**: **100%** of domestic urea from **1 Sep 2015**.
**National Investment Policy for Urea-2026** adds **10 MT** capacity.

nf863f5458e2.s: Under the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme (2010), the MRPs of P&K fertilisers are set by:
nf863f5458e2.x: Under NBS, covering 22 grades of decontrolled P&K fertilisers, manufacturers set the MRPs themselves.
xa: NBS gives a **fixed per-kg subsidy** on **N, P, K and S**, announced every year.
**Urea** stays under **statutory price control**.

neb2d533da1e.s: Under the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme, the subsidy is announced every year as a fixed amount per kilogram of
neb2d533da1e.x: NBS provides a fixed per-kilogram subsidy on nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and sulphur, announced annually.
neb2d533da1e.tq: Test the exact nutrient composition rather than the broader fertiliser category.
xs: NBS fixes a per-kg subsidy on **N, P, K and S**, announced every year — option **(3)** is correct.
Makers then set **MRPs** for P&K themselves.
xa: Introduced **2010**; **22 grades** of P&K fertilisers.

o: Slows nitrogen release and stops diversion of farm urea to industry
Raises the potassium content of urea
Increases diversion of urea to industry
ndc0ac34a489.x: Neem coating slows nitrogen release and stops diversion of subsidised farm urea to industry.
xa: Mandatory for **100%** of domestic urea from **1 Sep 2015**.
Urea is kept **artificially cheap** → nitrogen overuse.

n66752e2fe2f.s: Under PM-PRANAM, approved on 28 June 2023, States receive what share of the fertiliser subsidy saved by reducing chemical fertiliser use?
n66752e2fe2f.x: PM-PRANAM allows States to retain 50% of the subsidy saved through reduced chemical fertiliser consumption.
n66752e2fe2f.tq: Link the scheme’s incentive percentage with its approval date and objective.
xs: Under **PM-PRANAM** (**28 June 2023**), states keep **50 percent** of the subsidy saved — option **(3)** is correct.
The saving comes from **cutting chemical fertiliser use**.
xa: **NBS** (**2010**) covers P&K fertilisers.
**National Mission on Natural Farming** was approved in **Nov 2024**.
**APCNF** won the **Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity 2024**.

na068628f23e.s: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) in fertiliser subsidy began on a pilot basis in:
na068628f23e.x: Fertiliser DBT began as a pilot in October 2016 (PYQ key), with subsidy paid to companies after sale at PoS devices. September 2015 is when neem coating became mandatory for domestic urea; 2010 is when NBS was introduced; June 2023 is when PM-PRANAM was approved.
na068628f23e.tq: Fertiliser DBT pilot = Oct 2016; NBS = 2010; neem urea = 2015.
xs: Fertiliser **DBT** began on a **pilot basis in October 2016** — option **(1)** is correct (PYQ key).
**September 2015** = neem coating for domestic urea; **April 2010** fits **NBS** (**2010**); **June 2023** = **PM-PRANAM**.
xa: Under DBT, subsidy goes to companies **after sale at PoS**.
**Soil Health Card** scheme: **2014-15**.

n7218f50f5ec.s: Soil Health Cards are issued to farmers free of cost every:
n7218f50f5ec.x: Soil Health Cards (launched 2015) are issued free every two years.
xa: **25.79 crore** cards generated (**25.55 crore** as of Nov 2025).
Part of **NMSA** (Soil Health Management).
AP: soil sampling through **10,778 RSKs**.

na66a2af5016.s: Which of the following is classified as an input subsidy rather than public investment in agriculture?
o: Construction of a major irrigation project
Establishment of an agricultural research institute
na66a2af5016.x: Fertiliser subsidy is an input subsidy and represents a current transfer. Irrigation projects, agricultural research and rural infrastructure are forms of public investment and capital formation.
na66a2af5016.tq: Classify the item by asking whether it is a current transfer to inputs or capital formation.
xs: **Subsidised fertiliser supplied to farmers** is an **input subsidy** (a current transfer) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Irrigation projects**, **research** and **rural infrastructure** are **public investment** (capital formation).
xa: Input subsidies: **fertiliser, power, irrigation water, seed, credit (interest subvention)**.
⚠ **MSP** = price support, **not** an input subsidy.
Fertiliser subsidy is the **second-largest subsidy after food**.

neb1ebd179fd.s: The urea-centred fertiliser subsidy regime is criticised mainly because it:
neb1ebd179fd.x: A urea-centred subsidy distorts the balance among nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (the NPK ratio).
xa: The **ES** suggests **acre-based support** instead.
**PM-PRANAM**: states keep **50%** of the subsidy saved by cutting chemical fertiliser use.

nf1ff618d4e2.s: Among India's subsidies, the fertiliser subsidy ranks:
nf1ff618d4e2.x: The fertiliser subsidy is the second-largest subsidy after the food subsidy.
xa: The **West Asia crisis** doubled urea prices between **Dec 2025** and **Apr 2026**.
India: **2nd largest consumer** and **3rd largest producer** of fertilisers.
The **ES** suggests **acre-based support** instead of urea-centred subsidy.

n0698b6c6893.s: India is the ____ largest consumer of fertilisers in the world.
n0698b6c6893.x: India is the second-largest consumer and third-largest producer of fertilisers.
xa: Fertiliser subsidy is the **second-largest** after food.
AP fertiliser consumption: **39.39 LMT** in **2024-25**; requirement **41.70 LMT** for **2026-27**.

n986d81c90eb.s: Which one of the following correctly represents India’s N:P:K fertiliser consumption ratio in 2023–24 and the ideal ratio respectively?
n986d81c90eb.x: The 2023–24 N:P:K ratio was 10.9:4.1:1, against the ideal ratio of 4:2:1. The imbalance is associated with cheap urea and excessive nitrogen use.
n986d81c90eb.tq: Keep the observed ratio and the ideal benchmark in their correct order.
xs: N:P:K was **10.9:4.1:1** in **2023-24** vs the ideal **4:2:1** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes (**8 Jun 2026**) print **10.9:4.9:1** (option 1); follow the **ES** figure.
The skew is driven by **cheap urea**.
xa: The **ES** suggests **acre-based support** instead of urea-centred subsidy.
**Soil Health Cards** cut fertiliser use **8-10%**.

n54b2749fe8b.s: One 500 ml bottle of IFFCO Nano Urea is claimed to replace
o: one 25 kg bag of conventional urea
one 10 kg bag of conventional urea
one 50 kg bag of conventional urea
one 45 kg bag of conventional urea
n54b2749fe8b.x: A 500 ml bottle of IFFCO Nano Urea is stated to replace one 45 kg bag of conventional urea.
n54b2749fe8b.tq: Test the exact conversion figure using closely spaced bag-size distractors.
xs: A **500 ml** bottle of **IFFCO Nano Urea** replaces **one 45 kg bag** of conventional urea — option **(4)** is correct.
Nano Urea is an **IFFCO** product.
xa: Nano fertilisers are applied as a **foliar spray**; claimed absorption ~**80%**.
**Nano DAP**: **8% N**, **16% P**; launched by **Amit Shah** in **April 2023**.

n1fbdc497b88.s: Nano Urea and Nano DAP, applied mainly as foliar sprays, were developed by:
n1fbdc497b88.x: IFFCO makes Nano Urea and Nano DAP; their claimed absorption efficiency is about 80%.
xa: One **500 ml** Nano Urea bottle replaces a **45 kg** bag.

n38cac6548a3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about organic certification in India?
o: NPOP runs under the Commerce Ministry through APEDA
Under PKVY, clusters can be certified only through NPOP
PGS-India is an alternative certification route to NPOP
n38cac6548a3.x: PKVY clusters may be certified by PGS-India or NPOP, not only NPOP.
xa: PKVY (**2015**): cluster organic farming, **50 farmers / 50 acres** per cluster.
AP: **200 new PKVY clusters** in Visakhapatnam's tribal areas.
**National Mission on Natural Farming**: approved **Nov 2024**, stand-alone.

n41a6a25e68a.s: PM-KUSUM, which supports solar pumps and solarisation of farm pumps, was launched in:
xa: **Micro-irrigation** subsidy: up to **55%** (cap **5 ha**).
**PDMC** has covered **109 lakh ha** under micro-irrigation.

n72aaae567ee.s: India’s farm mechanisation level is estimated at approximately:
n72aaae567ee.x: India’s farm mechanisation level is reported as 40-45 percent.
n72aaae567ee.tq: Select the precise range rather than a rounded but unsupported estimate.
xs: India's farm mechanisation level is **40-45 percent** — option **(4)** is correct.
**SMAM** has subsidised **20.93 lakh** machines to raise it.
xa: **27,563** custom hiring centres under SMAM.
AP seeks Central help for **drones and mechanisation**.

n2778b590fa2.s: The percentage of crop area sown with certified or quality seed is called the:
n2778b590fa2.x: SRR is the share of area sown with certified/quality seed; VRR is the share under varieties released in the last three to five years.
xa: SRR = **% of a crop's area** sown with certified/quality seed.
**Seed Village**: farmers get **foundation seed** → produce **certified seed** locally.
**Seeds Act 1966** regulates quality of notified seeds.

n807638cb4cc.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001?
o: Farmers may sell farm-saved seed as branded seed
Farmers may save, use, exchange and sell farm-saved seed
n807638cb4cc.x: Farmers may sell farm-saved seed only as unbranded seed, so the branded-seed statement is false.
xa: The Act also **protects breeders**.
**Seeds Act 1966** regulates quality of notified seeds; **GEAC** approves GM crops.

nbf17ed9a5fd.s: Which of the following bodies is set up under the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules, 1971?
nbf17ed9a5fd.x: The Act and Rules set up the Central Insecticides Board and the Registration Committee.
xa: The **Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025** would replace them (comments due **4 Feb 2026**).
It proposes **higher penalties** and promotes **biological pesticides**.

n5b3606ce73c.s: Which pesticide was associated with the killing of mugger crocodiles in Kota?
n5b3606ce73c.x: Aldrin was linked to the killing of mugger crocodiles in Kota; Endosulfan was banned by the Supreme Court in 2011.
xa: AP pesticide use fell from **2,650 MT (2014-15)** to **1,716 MT (2024-25)**.
**IPM** cuts pesticide use by combining biological, cultural and need-based chemical control.

n959968e9a45.s: Kisan Call Centres answer farmers' queries in how many languages?
n959968e9a45.x: KCCs (launched 21 January 2004) work in 22 languages from 17 locations.
xa: **Meghdoot** app (IMD-ICAR, **2019**) gives agromet advisories.
**ANGRAU** runs weather-linked SMS alerts.

nd3c33cd9513.s: Andhra Pradesh Community Managed Natural Farming (APCNF) is run by:
nd3c33cd9513.x: APCNF is run by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha and uses jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham.
xa: Coverage: **10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha** (2025-26); some notes say **7 lakh+** farmers.
Won the **Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity 2024**.
APCNF is called a **global natural-farming model**.

nf7d5a5903ed.s: APCNF received which award for the year 2024?
nf7d5a5903ed.x: APCNF won the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity in 2024.
xa: It covers **10.20 lakh farmers** on **4.89 lakh ha** (2025-26).
It uses **jeevamrutham** and **ghanajeevamrutham**.
⚠ ZBNF itself was developed by **Subhash Palekar**.

n5e451e58332.s: The Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 would replace the Insecticides Act of:
n5e451e58332.x: The draft Bill would replace the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Insecticides Rules, 1971.
xa: Comments were due by **4 Feb 2026**.
India still uses at least **66 pesticides banned elsewhere**.

nfeffaf64088.s: Rythu Seva Kendras (formerly Rythu Bharosa Kendras) function mainly as:
o: Village-level one-stop centres for agricultural services
nfeffaf64088.x: Rythu Seva Kendras are village one-stop centres providing agricultural inputs and services.
xa: Soil sampling through **10,778 RSKs**, rationalised to **8,489** functional centres.
Permanent buildings coming up under **MGNREGS**.
AP Seeds supplies **7.46 lakh quintals** of subsidised seed through RSKs.

n520954b242d.s: Permanent buildings for the rationalised Rythu Seva Kendras are being taken up under:
n520954b242d.x: Permanent buildings for RSKs are coming up under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS).
n520954b242d.tq: Match the infrastructure activity with the implementing programme.
xs: Permanent buildings for the rationalised **Rythu Seva Kendras** are coming up under **MGNREGS** — option **(4)** is correct.
The **PPV&FR Act** protects breeders and farmers' seed rights; **NPOP** is organic certification — neither builds RSKs.
xa: Soil sampling ran through **10,778 RSKs**, rationalised to **8,489 functional centres**.
RSKs were formerly **Rythu Bharosa Kendras** — village one-stop centres.
Services: inputs, soil testing, **e-Panta**, **CCRCs**, insurance, procurement.
AP Seeds supplies **7.46 lakh quintals** of subsidised seed (**₹294 crore**) through RSKs (2026-27).

n970da8a0e1c.s: Which of the following is the scientific core of the Green Revolution package?
n970da8a0e1c.x: Although the package included HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, assured irrigation, pesticides and mechanisation, the scientific core was the use of HYV seeds.
n970da8a0e1c.tq: Distinguish the central technological element from the other complementary inputs.
xs: The scientific core of the Green Revolution was the **use of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2024).
Irrigation, machinery and pesticides supported the package, but none alone was its core.
xa: Wheat HYVs came from Mexican dwarf wheats (**Kalyan Sona**, **Sonalika**); rice from **IR-8** (**IRRI, Philippines**).
HYV programme became full-fledged from **1966**, during the **Annual Plans (1966-69)**.
**Punjab**, the pioneer state, is the "**Granary of India**".
⚠ **ICAR 2019-21** released **562** new high-yielding field-crop varieties (PYQ key).

na7e21cbfd5a.s: Which one of the following is NOT a green manure crop mentioned in relation to agricultural inputs?
na7e21cbfd5a.x: Sunn hemp, dhaincha and green gram are mentioned in connection with green manure seed. Bt cotton is a genetically modified crop and is not a green manure crop.
na7e21cbfd5a.tq: Find the odd item by classifying each crop according to its agricultural use.
xs: **Bt cotton** is not a green manure crop — option **(3)** is the answer.
AP's **Kharif 2026** green manure seed: **sunn hemp (Jilledu)**, **dhaincha (Janumu)** and **green gram**.
Bt cotton appears instead among the **Jan 2026** variety releases (**22 Bt cotton**).
xa: AP spent **₹62.20 crore** for **91,918 quintals** of green manure seed.
**Glyricidia** is a **green leaf manure** (PYQ key).
**PKVY**: **200 new clusters** in Visakhapatnam's tribal areas.

nca634e0586b.s: Glyricidia is used in agriculture mainly as a:
nca634e0586b.x: Glyricidia is a green leaf manure (PYQ key). Neem-based products are the bio-pesticides, Kamala is a genome-edited rice, and Nano Urea or Nano DAP are the nano fertilisers.
xs: **Glyricidia** is a **green leaf manure** — option **(1)** is correct (PYQ key).
**Neem-based pesticides** are the bio-pesticides; **Kamala** is a genome-edited rice; **Nano Urea/DAP** are nano fertilisers.
xa: **Vermicompost**: earthworms turn organic waste into rich manure (PYQ key).
AP green manure seeds: **sunn hemp (Jilledu)**, **dhaincha (Janumu)**, green gram.

n304276420d6.s: Under the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY, 2015), each organic farming cluster consists of:
n304276420d6.x: PKVY promotes cluster-based organic farming with 50 farmers and 50 acres per cluster, certified through PGS-India or NPOP. The other combinations are not the PKVY norm.
xs: **PKVY (2015)** clusters have **50 farmers covering 50 acres** — option **(1)** is correct.
Certification is through **PGS-India** or **NPOP**.
xa: **NPOP** (**2001**) runs under the Commerce Ministry/**APEDA**.
AP added **200 new clusters** in Visakhapatnam's tribal areas.

n4c2fcd48fe0.s: The Agriculture Integrated Command and Control Centre was inaugurated in March 2024 at
n4c2fcd48fe0.x: The Agriculture Integrated Command and Control Centre was inaugurated in March 2024 at Krishi Bhawan in Delhi.
n4c2fcd48fe0.tq: Use the location trap to distinguish the national command centre from agricultural extension institutions.
xs: The **Agriculture Integrated Command and Control Centre** was inaugurated in **March 2024** at **Krishi Bhawan, Delhi** — option **(4)** is correct (APPSC 2024).
It is in Delhi, not at **ANGRAU** or Puducherry.
xa: **Meghdoot** app: IMD-ICAR, **2019**.
**Kisan Call Centres**: launched **21 Jan 2004**.
First **KVK**: **1974, Puducherry**.

n67722b57b6f.s: Minimum Support Price (MSP) is classified as a/an:
n67722b57b6f.x: MSP is a price support measure; fertiliser, power, water, seed and credit support are input subsidies.
xa: Input subsidies: **fertiliser, power, irrigation water, seed, credit**.
Budget **2026-27** fertiliser subsidy: **₹1.71 lakh crore**.
The **ES** suggests **acre-based support** instead of urea-centred subsidy.

o: Biological, cultural and need-based chemical control
n4ff4fd1ad59.x: IPM combines biological control, cultural control and need-based chemical control in order to reduce pesticide use.
n4ff4fd1ad59.tq: Identify the management approach from the combination of control methods rather than from one component alone.
xs: **IPM** combines **biological, cultural and need-based chemical control** — option **(4)** is correct.
Its aim is to **cut pesticide use**.
xa: **Neem-based pesticides** are bio-pesticides.
Second Green Revolution stresses **integrated nutrient and pest management**.
AP pesticide use fell from **2,650 MT** to **1,716 MT** of active ingredient.

n34dbd6d91f7.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Green Revolution package approach?
o: Assured irrigation through canals and tubewells
Withdrawal of price support and formal credit
n34dbd6d91f7.x: The package included HYV seeds, assured irrigation, fertilisers, pesticides, mechanisation, institutional credit and MSP or assured procurement. Withdrawal of price support and formal credit was not a component.
n34dbd6d91f7.tq: Find the option that reverses a core element of the package approach.
xs: **Withdrawal of price support and formal credit** was not part of the GR package — option **(4)** is the answer.
The package in fact included **institutional credit** and **MSP / assured procurement** (UPSC Economy p.186).
Its other parts: **HYV seeds**, **assured irrigation** (canals, tubewells), **chemical fertilisers + pesticides**, **mechanisation**.
xa: HYV traits: **short-statured** (do not lodge), respond to fertiliser and water, mature quicker → **double cropping**.
First crop transformed: **wheat**; pioneer state: **Punjab**.
First semi-dwarf rice in India: **Taichung Native-1 (TN-1)**, **1965**.

na7dc1dd2129.s: Which feature of HYV crops helps them resist lodging?
na7dc1dd2129.x: The short stature of HYVs helps them resist lodging; quicker maturity is what permits double cropping.
xa: **Kalyan Sona** and **Sonalika** are Indian dwarf wheat selections that **resist lodging**.
The GR package also included **assured irrigation**, **chemical fertilisers** and **MSP**.

n05ea7054295.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the first crop transformed by the Green Revolution and its pioneer state?
n05ea7054295.x: Wheat was the first crop transformed by the Green Revolution and Punjab was the pioneer state. Rice gained in a wider, later phase, including in the AP and TN deltas; Haryana gained but was not the pioneer.
n05ea7054295.tq: First = wheat, Punjab; rice and the deltas came later.
xs: **Wheat** was the first crop transformed and **Punjab** the pioneer state — option **(3)** is correct.
Rice gained in a **wider, later phase** (AP and TN deltas); **Haryana** gained but was not the pioneer.
xa: Wheat **gained the most** of all crops.
Main GR region: **Punjab, Haryana and western UP**.

nindian-economy-2-5.s: India's first agricultural university was established in 1960 at:
nindian-economy-2-5.x: The first farm university was set up at Pantnagar in 1960.
n: Pantnagar was the first Agricultural University. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 3-4]
The first Agricultural University was established in 1960. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 3-4]
The first Krishi Vigyan Kendra was established in Puducherry. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 3-4]
The first Krishi Vigyan Kendra was established in 1974. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 3-4]
The first implementation of WBCIS took place in Karnataka during Kharif 2007. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 3-4]
The first introduction of HYV under the Green Revolution took place in 1966–67. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 3-4]
xa: First crop transformed by the GR = **wheat**; pioneer state = **Punjab**.
**IADP** began in **1960** in **7 districts**; AP's IADP district = **West Godavari**.
⚠ **Swaminathan** = Green Revolution (India); **Borlaug** = Green Revolution (world).

nd923b531af0.s: Which was the Intensive Agricultural District Programme (IADP) district in Andhra Pradesh?
nd923b531af0.x: IADP began in 1960 as a pilot in seven districts of seven States; West Godavari was AP's district.
xa: **IAAP** (**1964-65**) extended the approach to **114 districts**; **117** blocks in AP, starting in West Godavari.
⚠ **IADP** = **1960**, 7 districts; **IAAP** = **1964-65**, 114 districts.
**MTU** rice varieties come from **RARS Maruteru**, West Godavari.

n3a94cd7da2a.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the Intensive Agricultural Area Programme (IAAP) began in which district?
n3a94cd7da2a.x: IAAP in Andhra Pradesh began in West Godavari.
xa: IAAP began in **1964-65**; IADP in **1960**.
Coastal AP became a **rice-surplus belt** thanks to the **delta canals**.

n771aa68539f.s: Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI), a sub-scheme of RKVY, has been implemented since:
n771aa68539f.x: BGREI has been implemented since 2010-11, not 2014-15.
xa: Aim: raise **rice-based productivity in the eastern region**.
Tools: **HYVs**, irrigation, balanced nutrients, **IPM**.
UPSC notes list six BGREI states and omit **Chhattisgarh**.

neaaa8c2e376.s: BGREI aims to raise rice-based productivity in which region?
neaaa8c2e376.x: BGREI aims to raise rice-based productivity in eastern India through HYVs, irrigation, balanced nutrients and IPM.
xa: BGREI: **sub-scheme of RKVY**, since **2010-11**.
"**Purvodaya**" later took the same logic — shifting the rice bowl eastward.

n8b83d91f55d.s: Operation Flood was launched in 1970 by which organisation?
o: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
n8b83d91f55d.x: Operation Flood was launched in 1970 by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB).
n8b83d91f55d.tq: Apply the ‘who launched the programme?’ institutional trap.
xs: **Operation Flood** was launched by the **National Dairy Development Board (NDDB)** in **1970** — option **(2)** is correct.
It built a **national milk grid**.
xa: Model: **Amul (Anand, Gujarat)** three-tier cooperative.
Phase I (**1970-80**) was financed by the **World Food Programme**.
**Dr. Verghese Kurien** = Father of the **White Revolution**.

n641f432c5a1.s: White Revolution 2.0 (September 2024) was launched by the Ministry of:
n641f432c5a1.x: The Ministry of Cooperation launched White Revolution 2.0, which plans 75,000 new dairy cooperative societies.
xa: Procurement target: **1,007 lakh kg/day** by **2028-29**.
Milk output: **239.3 MMT** in **2023-24**, now about **248 MT**.

nb53419bd17c.s: Operation Flood was implemented by the National Dairy Development Board from 1970 mainly to:
o: Build a national milk grid based on the Anand cooperative model
Promote cotton exports through a technology mission
Expand marine fishing along the eastern coast
Increase oil-palm cultivation in rainfed areas
nb53419bd17c.x: Operation Flood was run by the NDDB from 1970 and built a national milk grid on the Anand or Amul cooperative model.
nb53419bd17c.tq: Identify the institution, time period and principal objective of a major programme together.
xs: Operation Flood (**NDDB**, **1970**) built a **national milk grid** on the **Anand** cooperative model — option **(1)** is correct.
Cotton = **Silver Fibre** Revolution; fisheries = **Blue**; oil palm = **Yellow** (NMEO-Oil Palm).
xa: Three tiers: **village society → district union → state federation**.
Phase II: milk sheds **18 → 136**.

n29efd2e4fa2.s: The current effort associated with the Yellow Revolution is the:
n29efd2e4fa2.x: The current Yellow Revolution effort is represented by the National Mission on Edible Oils.
n29efd2e4fa2.tq: Identify the current mission linked to a traditional revolution label.
xs: The current Yellow Revolution effort is the **National Mission on Edible Oils** → **NMEO-Oil Palm** — option **(3)** is correct.
Yellow Revolution = **oilseeds / edible oils** (**1986-87**).
xa: Linked with **Sam Pitroda**.
Blue Revolution's current vehicle is **PMMSY**.

ncf553ec9050.s: The Red Revolution (meat and tomato) is associated with:
ncf553ec9050.x: Red Revolution – Vishal Tewari; Pink – Durgesh Patel; Golden – Nirpakh Tutej; Blue – Hiralal Chaudhuri and Arun Krishnan.
xa: Blue = fisheries (current vehicle **PMMSY**); Pink = meat processing, prawn, onion, pharmaceuticals.
Red = meat and tomato; Golden = horticulture and honey (**1991-2003**).

nf8c7dbfe615.s: The Golden Revolution is associated with:
nf8c7dbfe615.x: Golden Revolution is horticulture and honey; jute is the Golden Fibre Revolution, cotton the Silver Fibre and eggs/poultry the Silver Revolution.
xa: Egg maximisation = **Silver Revolution** (APPSC 2018 key).
**Sweet** Revolution = honey / beekeeping.

o: A programme limited to horticulture and honey production
Only the simultaneous growth of foodgrain and dairy production
The sequence of phases of the Green Revolution
The umbrella of colour revolutions covering crops, livestock and fisheries
nb86f94dd12c.x: Rainbow Revolution is the umbrella term for the different colour revolutions and represents holistic agricultural growth across crops, livestock and fisheries.
nb86f94dd12c.tq: Distinguish an umbrella concept from one of its component revolutions.
xs: **Rainbow Revolution** is the **umbrella of all colour revolutions**, covering **crops, livestock and fisheries** — option **(4)** is correct.
It means **holistic agricultural growth**, not just horticulture or dairy.
xa: **Golden** Revolution alone covers horticulture and honey.
**Evergreen Revolution**: sustainable, climate-smart farming.

n36835257df8.s: Who among the following is associated with the Green Revolution in India and who with the Green Revolution at the global level, respectively?
n36835257df8.x: M.S. Swaminathan is associated with the Green Revolution in India, while Norman Borlaug is associated with it at the global level.
n36835257df8.tq: Discriminate between two persons associated with the same revolution at different levels.
xs: **M.S. Swaminathan** (India) and **Norman Borlaug** (world) — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (3) reverses them; **Pitroda**, **Kurien** and **Durgesh Patel** belong to other revolutions.
xa: Borlaug: **Mexican dwarf wheat** (**Lerma Rojo 64-A**, **Sonora 64**).
Green Revolution dated **1968**: foodgrains (HYV wheat, rice).

nfa7665968b3.s: The Yellow Revolution, initiated during 1986–87, was associated with which of the following persons?
nfa7665968b3.x: The Yellow Revolution of 1986–87, related to oilseeds and edible oils, is associated with Sam Pitroda.
nfa7665968b3.tq: Match the named person with the correct revolution and period.
xs: The **Yellow Revolution** (**1986-87**) is linked with **Sam Pitroda** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Kurien** = White; **Swaminathan** = Green (India); **Durgesh Patel** = Pink.
xa: Yellow = **oilseeds / edible oils**; current effort **NMEO-Oil Palm**.
⚠ **Kurien** = White; **Pitroda** = Yellow.

n5812e3ec933.s: 'Egg maximisation' and 'fisheries development' are associated respectively with which revolutions?
n5812e3ec933.x: Egg maximisation is the Silver Revolution (eggs and poultry) and fisheries development is the Blue Revolution (APPSC 2018 keys). Golden is horticulture and honey, Pink is meat processing, prawn and onion, Yellow is oilseeds and Grey is fertilisers.
xs: Egg maximisation = **Silver Revolution**; fisheries development = **Blue Revolution** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2018).
**Golden** = horticulture and honey; **Pink** = meat processing, prawn, onion; **Yellow** = oilseeds; **Grey** = fertilisers.
xa: ⚠ **Silver** = eggs; **Silver Fibre** = cotton.
Blue Revolution's current vehicle: **PMMSY**.
n5812e3ec933.fixed: stem oddly framed around an answer key; fact unchanged

n725535d9c11.s: The Green Revolution benefited most those farmers who held more than:
n725535d9c11.x: Farmers with more than 10 hectares benefited the most; the disparities were both regional and interpersonal.
xa: **Punjab** and **Haryana** extract **35-57%** more groundwater than recharge.
Soil costs: **salinity**, biodiversity loss, skewed **N:P:K of 10.9:4.1:1**.

nd5ca353498f.s: MTU rice varieties are associated with which research station?
o: Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi
Regional Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru, West Godavari
nd5ca353498f.x: MTU varieties come from the Regional Agricultural Research Station at Maruteru in West Godavari. BPT varieties are associated with Bapatla.
nd5ca353498f.tq: Origin-place discrimination between the MTU and BPT varietal groups.
xs: **MTU** varieties come from **Regional Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru (West Godavari)** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ **BPT** varieties come from **Bapatla**.
xa: **MTU 1010**: rabi rice of southern states; parent of **Pusa DST Rice 1**.
**MTU 7029 (Swarna)**: popular mega-variety.
**BPT 5204 (Samba Mahsuri)**: parent of **DRR Dhan 100 Kamala**.

n547fbdd6ef4.s: The Johl Committee proposed shifting what proportion of paddy area as part of crop-diversification efforts?
n547fbdd6ef4.x: The Johl Committee proposed shifting 20 per cent of the paddy area to address the problems associated with water-intensive rice-wheat monoculture.
n547fbdd6ef4.tq: Direct percentage recall linked to the policy response to monoculture.
xs: The **Johl Committee** proposed shifting **20 per cent** of paddy area — option **(3)** is correct.
The aim is **crop diversification** away from water-intensive rice-wheat.
xa: **Punjab** and **Haryana** extract **35-57%** more groundwater than recharge.
GR neglected **pulses, oilseeds and millets**.

n4584aa8387d.s: The National Mission on Oilseeds and Oil Palm (NMOOP, 2014) covers:
n4584aa8387d.x: NMOOP covers oilseeds and oil palm; INSIMP covers millets and BGREI rice-based systems of eastern States.
xa: BGREI (**2010-11**) is a sub-scheme of **RKVY**.
Pulses and maize were added to the **Technology Mission on Oilseeds** (**1986**).

n58985db16d5.s: Agricultural growth at 2011-12 prices in 2015-16 was approximately:
n58985db16d5.x: Agricultural growth in 2015-16 was about 0.7% at 2011-12 prices.
n58985db16d5.tq: Preserve the decimal place in a low-growth numerical fact.
xs: Agricultural growth in **2015-16** was about **0.7%** at **2011-12** prices — option **(2)** is correct (PYQ key).
It came right after **2014-15**, a **negative-growth** year.
xa: The other negative year: **2002-03** (drought).
FY16-FY25 average: **4.4%** a year — the highest decadal growth ever.
Agriculture's share in national income: **56.5%** in **1950-51** vs ~**18%** now.

nd165e94b414.s: The share of agriculture in national income declined from 56.5% in 1950-51 to approximately:
nd165e94b414.x: Agriculture's share in national income declined from 56.5% in 1950-51 to about 18% in the current reference period.
nd165e94b414.tq: Compare the historical and present shares without confusing share with growth rate.
xs: Agriculture's share in national income fell from **56.5% (1950-51)** to about **18% at present** — option **(1)** is correct.
The share shrank as the rest of the economy grew faster.
xa: Growth is now led by **livestock** (**7.1%**) and **fishing** (**8.8%**), while crops grew only **3.5%** (FY16-FY25).
Agricultural exports = **$54.70 billion**.
Holdings: **86%** small or marginal; average **1.08 ha**.

nde39dae565f.s: Agriculture and allied sector growth in Q1 FY27 was:
nde39dae565f.x: Q1 FY27 growth was 3.6%; FY26 (provisional) was 3.0% and FY24 was 2.7%.
xa: FY25 was later revised to **4.2%**.
FY16-FY25 average: **4.4%**, above the world's **2.9%**.

n31a975030fb.s: Agricultural yields fall by about how much for every 1°C rise in temperature?
n31a975030fb.x: Yields fall by about 8% per 1°C rise; a 1°C rise can wipe out about four years of rice and wheat productivity gains.
xa: A **20%** rainfall deficit also cuts yields ~**8%**.
El Niño years: pulse yield falls **5-25%**.

nfbdd4f8729c.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the effect of El Niño on pulses?
o: Acreage rises by 2–9% and output rises by 6–30%.
Acreage falls by 2–9% and output falls by 6–30%.
Acreage falls by 6–30% and output falls by 2–9%.
Acreage remains unchanged while output rises by 5–25%.
nfbdd4f8729c.x: In El Niño years, pulse acreage declines by about 2–9%, while output declines by about 6–30%.
nfbdd4f8729c.tq: Separating two similar percentage ranges by the variable they describe.
xs: In El Niño years, pulse **acreage falls 2-9%** and **output falls 6-30%** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (3) swaps the ranges; nothing rises.
xa: Pulse **yield** falls **5-25%** in El Niño years.
Kharif 2026 sowing was only ~**61%** of normal by **19 Aug** (El Nino).

n3deac2f3349.s: The National Food Security Mission (NFSM) was launched in:
n3deac2f3349.x: NFSM began in 2007-08 with rice, wheat and pulses and was renamed NFSNM in FY25.
xa: **PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana**: **100 low-productivity districts** (**2025-26 to 2030-31**).
**INSIMP** (**2011-12**) covers millets.

n990fcd59e97.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income was set up in 2016 and reported in 2018
The National Commission on Agriculture was set up in 1970
The NCA submitted its final report in 1976
The Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income was chaired by M.S. Swaminathan
n990fcd59e97.x: The Doubling Farmers' Income Committee was chaired by Ashok Dalwai, not M.S. Swaminathan.
xa: **National Agricultural Policy 2000**: target of **over 4% per annum** agricultural growth.
**PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana**: **100 low-productivity districts** (**2025-26 to 2030-31**).
"**Tilhan Mission**" (Feb **2020**) relates to **oilseed production**.

nd9ca3deb527.s: The total foodgrain production of India reached which figure in 2025-26 according to the cited estimate?
nd9ca3deb527.x: Total foodgrain production reached 376.56 million tonnes in 2025-26.
nd9ca3deb527.tq: Distinguish the total annual figure from kharif and rabi component estimates.
xs: **2025-26** foodgrains (2nd Advance Estimates) reached **376.56 million tonnes** — option **(4)** is correct.
**357.73 MT** is the **2024-25** final record.
xa: Kharif **1,741.44 LMT** and rabi **1,745.13 LMT** — both records.
Horticulture in **2025-26**: **377.78 MT**.

n2b33b5301cc.s: In 2024-25, India's horticulture production, which exceeded foodgrains, was:
n2b33b5301cc.x: Horticulture output was 367.72 MT, above foodgrain output of 357.73 MT.
xa: Horticulture range cited: **362-368 MT**.
In **2025-26**: foodgrains **376.56 MT** vs horticulture **377.78 MT**.

ne26dd5b7c37.s: Which one of the following sets contains only commodities in which India ranks first globally?
ne26dd5b7c37.x: India ranks first globally in milk, pulses and spices. Wheat, fruits, vegetables, eggs, cotton and silk are listed among commodities in which India ranks second.
ne26dd5b7c37.tq: Group identification by separating first-rank commodities from second-rank commodities.
xs: India ranks **1st** in **milk, pulses and spices** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Wheat, sugarcane, fruits, vegetables, eggs, cotton, silk** are **2nd**-rank items.
**Rice** is 1st per the newer figure, but wheat and sugarcane in option (2) are 2nd.
xa: Also 1st: **millets**, **jute**, dry onions.
**Fish**: **2nd** (official version), **1st in shrimp**.

n1b88d929ecc.s: India's rice yield of about 2,929 kg per hectare is best compared with China's rice yield of approximately:
n1b88d929ecc.x: India's rice yield was about 2,929 kg/ha, compared with approximately 7,100 kg/ha in China.
n1b88d929ecc.tq: Distinguish the China comparison from the separate global foodgrain average.
xs: China's rice yield is about **7,100 kg per hectare** vs India's **2,929 kg/ha** — option **(3)** is correct.
India's yield is **less than half** of China's.
**4,000 kg/ha** is the global average some notes give; **5,612** and **6,063** are AP paddy yields.
xa: ⚠ Some notes (**8** Jun 2026) call **2,929 kg/ha** the foodgrain yield.
**Punjab** has India's highest rice yield.

nf9d61366b05.s: The Kapas Kanti mission has a target of raising cotton yield to:
nf9d61366b05.x: The Kapas Kanti mission targets a cotton yield of 755 kg per hectare.
nf9d61366b05.tq: Separate a future mission target from the present Indian and global averages.
xs: The **Kapas Kanti** mission targets **755 kg per hectare** — option **(2)** is correct.
**770** is the global average; **480** is the **2023** Bt cotton level.
xa: Present cotton yield: about **440 kg/ha**.
India became a **net importer of raw cotton**.

n9c378fd83f5.s: Cereal yield is defined as the quantity of cereals produced per hectare of
n9c378fd83f5.x: Cereal yield is measured in kilograms per hectare of harvested land under cereals.
n9c378fd83f5.tq: Precise-definition discrimination among similar agricultural-area terms.
xs: **Cereal yield** = kg per hectare of **harvested land under cereals** (World Bank usage) — option **(4)** is correct.
It is not measured on irrigated, total cultivated or net sown area.
xa: India's yields of **cereals, maize, soybean and pulses** trail global averages.
Exception: **groundnut**.

n58ba0ceb22b.s: Custom Hiring Centres are a means of raising farm productivity through:
n58ba0ceb22b.x: Custom Hiring Centres serve mechanisation; better seed comes via SRR/VRR and genome editing, balanced nutrition via the Soil Health Card.
xa: Water pathways: **micro-irrigation**, **DSR**, **SRI**.
Causes they target: low **SRR** / HYV seed replacement and a skewed **NPK ratio**.

n7165f24d4ad.s: Which one of the following crops is identified as an exception to India's generally lower yields compared with global averages?
n7165f24d4ad.x: India's yields of cereals, maize, soybean and pulses trail global averages, whereas groundnut is identified as an exception because of semi-arid concentration and improved varieties.
n7165f24d4ad.tq: Exception-based recall from a comparative yield statement.
xs: **Groundnut** is the exception to India's lower-than-global yields — option **(3)** is correct.
Reasons: **semi-arid concentration** and **improved varieties**.
**Soybean**, **maize** and **pulses** trail global averages.
xa: **Gujarat** leads groundnut.

n5a651f2d55b.s: Which State is called the 'Rice Bowl of central India'?
n5a651f2d55b.x: Chhattisgarh is described as the 'Rice Bowl of central India'.
xa: **Punjab** has the **highest rice yield**.
Chhattisgarh is in the **BGREI** list of eastern rice states.

n001c5250750.s: After declines in cotton area and output, India became:
o: A net exporter of raw cotton
A net importer of raw cotton
n001c5250750.x: India became a net importer of raw cotton following declining cotton area and output.
xa: **Punjab's cotton area** fell **37.5%** to **80,000 ha** (2026).
**Bt cotton** had raised yields from **190 (2002)** to **480 kg/ha (2023)**.

nbebb14762e1.s: Which states are specifically associated with the highest pulse yields in the cited comparison?
nbebb14762e1.x: Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat have the highest pulse yields, helped by black or semi-arid soils and high seed replacement rates.
nbebb14762e1.tq: Link the yield ranking with the stated soil and seed-replacement factors.
xs: Highest pulse yields are in **Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat** — option **(4)** is correct.
Reasons: **black/semi-arid soils** and high seed replacement (**SRR**).
xa: **MP** is also the leading pulse producer.
Pulses are only ~**26%** irrigated.
El Niño years cut pulse yields **5-25%**.

nb06cae1965e.s: Which crop's output fell to 290.91 lakh bales in 2025-26 from about 350 lakh bales?
nb06cae1965e.x: Cotton area fell by 18 lakh ha and output declined to 290.91 lakh bales in 2025-26 from about 350 lakh bales.
xa: **India became a net importer of raw cotton**.
Cotton yield: about **440 kg/ha** vs global ~**770**.
**Kapas Kanti** mission targets **755 kg/ha**.

n06da1bbfa3f.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a major cause of India's cereal-yield gap?
o: Rainfed farming covering about 50–51% of net sown area
Universal access to efficient cold-chain infrastructure
Small and marginal holdings forming about 86% of holdings
A skewed NPK ratio and low seed replacement rate
n06da1bbfa3f.x: Universal access to efficient cold-chain infrastructure is not a stated cause; rather, cold-chain losses account for about 30%. The other three factors contribute to the yield gap.
n06da1bbfa3f.tq: Find the exception by reversing a stated constraint into an advantage.
xs: **Universal access to efficient cold-chain infrastructure** is not a cause — there are **30%** cold-chain losses — option **(2)** is the answer.
Real causes: **rainfed** farming (**50-51%** of net sown area), **86%** small/marginal holdings, skewed **NPK ratio** and low **SRR**.
xa: Average holding: **1.08 ha**.
Soybean below **2 t/ha** in many rainfed districts.

n57187ed779e.s: A major criticism of India's agricultural growth is that it has come more from:
o: Improvement in yield than expansion of area
Expansion of area than improvement in yield
n57187ed779e.x: The criticism is that growth has depended more on area expansion than on yield improvement.
xa: India's rice yield is **less than half** of China's.
Exception to the yield gap: **groundnut**.
Holdings: **86%** small or marginal; average **1.08 ha**.

nbd788ee47ce.s: The collapse of agricultural performance during the Third Plan, largely due to droughts, contributed to the beginning of the:
nbd788ee47ce.x: The drought-related collapse during the Third Plan helped set off the Green Revolution.
nbd788ee47ce.tq: Identify the policy or technological response linked to the stated crisis.
xs: The **3rd Plan** collapse (droughts) set off the **Green Revolution** — option **(1)** is correct.
Agricultural growth in the 3rd Plan (**1961-66**) was just **0.73%**, the lowest.
xa: The **Annual Plans 1966-69** that followed grew **4.16%**.
⚠ Lowest = **3rd Plan**; best = **8th Plan (4.68%)**.

n9e780cada6a.s: The Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses provides 100% MSP procurement of:
n9e780cada6a.x: The mission (2025-26 to 2030-31) provides 100% MSP procurement of tur, urad and masoor.
xa: Aim: **end pulse imports** (APPCA 2026).
India pulse output: **25.68 MMT**.

neb027ce3012.s: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (2025-26 to 2030-31) is to cover how many low-productivity districts?
neb027ce3012.x: The scheme covers 100 low-productivity districts during 2025-26 to 2030-31.
xa: **Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses** runs the same period, **₹11,440 crore**.
**NFSM** was renamed **NFSNM** in **FY25**.
**BGREI** (**2010-11**) targets rice systems of eastern states.

nbd85506a561.s: The Technology Mission on Oilseeds (1986) is associated with the:
nbd85506a561.x: The Technology Mission on Oilseeds (1986), later adding pulses and maize, is associated with the Yellow Revolution led by Sam Pitroda.
xa: Later oilseed missions: **NMOOP (2014)**, **NMEO-Oil Palm (2021)**, **NMEO-Oilseeds (2024)**.
NMEO targets nearly **70 million t** of oilseeds by **2030-31**.
"**Tilhan Mission**" (Feb **2020**, PYQ) also relates to **oilseed production**.

nefb9608baab.s: In 2024-25, the rabi paddy yield of Andhra Pradesh was:
nefb9608baab.x: AP's rabi paddy yield was 6,979 kg/ha, higher than the kharif yield of 5,612 kg/ha.
xa: AP paddy (about **6 t/ha**) is among the best.
AP paddy output **2024-25**: **127.15 lakh t**.

n4737feee8d7.s: The foodgrain production of Andhra Pradesh was 157.59 lakh tonnes in which year?
n4737feee8d7.x: Andhra Pradesh produced 157.59 lakh tonnes of foodgrains in 2017-18.
n4737feee8d7.tq: Match the exact state production figure with its agricultural year.
xs: AP produced **157.59 lakh tonnes** of foodgrains in **2017-18** — option **(4)** is correct (PYQ key; APPSC 2019).
xa: AP output: **143 → 162 → 190 lakh t** across **2023-26**.

nec75b3b5e45.s: In 2023-24, the only year of contraction in AP's Survey series, agriculture and allied growth was:
nec75b3b5e45.x: Agriculture and allied growth was −1.58%; the −9.82% figure is the separate fall in the crops sub-sector.
xa: AP foodgrains fell to **143.31 lakh t** in 2023-24.

nd55771b61f8.s: Andhra Pradesh's paddy yield, among the best in India, is about:
nd55771b61f8.x: AP's paddy yield is about 6 t/ha, among the best, though its foodgrain output fluctuates with the monsoon.
xa: Rabi paddy **6,979 kg/ha** vs kharif **5,612**.
AP maize: **6,453 kg/ha**.
AP output swung **143 → 162 → 190 lakh t** over **2023-26**.

naf68390bcea.s: The National Agricultural Policy, 2000, targeted agricultural growth of:
naf68390bcea.x: The National Agricultural Policy, 2000, set a target of more than 4% annual agricultural growth.
naf68390bcea.tq: Recall the policy target rather than the later realised growth rate.
xs: The **National Agricultural Policy 2000** targeted **over 4% per annum** growth — option **(1)** is correct.
The 5%, 3% and 2% figures are not the policy's target.
xa: The **8th Plan** had a **4.1%** target and achieved **4.68%**.
FY16-FY25 averaged **4.4%** a year.
**National Commission on Agriculture**: set up **1970**, final report **1976**.
**Ashok Dalwai Committee** (Doubling Farmers' Income): set up **2016**, report **2018**.

n3b73926c2d1.s: Which of the following correctly describes the trend in India's foodgrain production from 2019-20 to 2024-25?
o: It fluctuated without any definite direction.
n3b73926c2d1.x: Foodgrain production recorded a steady increase over the period from 2019-20 to 2024-25.
n3b73926c2d1.tq: Test the direction of a reported time-series trend.
xs: From **2019-20 to 2024-25**, production showed a **steady increase** — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC 2024; PYQ keys).
The run ended in a record **357.73 MT** in **2024-25**.
xa: **Oilseeds**: area, production and productivity all rose.
**NMEO** targets nearly **70 million t** of oilseeds by **2030-31**.
Paddy and pulses **recovered** in **2024-25**.

n0ca11410af9.s: India's pulse production and consumption position is correctly described as
n0ca11410af9.x: India is both the largest producer and the largest consumer of pulses, with production of 25.68 million metric tonnes as the cited latest figure.
n0ca11410af9.tq: Direct recall of a paired production-consumption position.
xs: India is the **largest producer and largest consumer** of pulses — option **(4)** is correct (APPCA 2026).
Pulse output: **25.68 MMT**.
xa: **Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses** (**2025-31**): tur, urad, masur — to end pulse imports.
Leading pulse state: **Madhya Pradesh**, then Rajasthan, Maharashtra.
El Niño years cut pulse output by **6-30%**.

n1166ecc87b4.s: In the Early Green Revolution phase (1968-81), HYV seeds were first introduced in:
n1166ecc87b4.x: HYV seeds came first in wheat; the Later phase (1987-92) spread the Green Revolution to rice and other regions.
xa: The Early phase package = **HYV seeds + fertiliser + irrigation**, called the **New Agricultural Strategy**.
Foodgrains rose from **72.3 MT (1965-66)** to a record **357.73 MT (2024-25)**.
⚠ Horticulture (**362.08 MT**) now exceeds foodgrain output.

n35b162f9b95.s: The National Commission on Agriculture, which submitted its report in 1976, was chaired by whom?
n35b162f9b95.x: The National Commission on Agriculture functioned during 1970–76 and submitted its report in 1976 under the chairmanship of Nathu Ram Mirdha.
n35b162f9b95.tq: Use the chairperson–commission association to eliminate names belonging to other agricultural bodies.
xs: The **National Commission on Agriculture** (**1970-76**, report **1976**) was chaired by **Nathu Ram Mirdha** — option **(1)**.
**M.S. Swaminathan** chaired the **National Commission on Farmers** (**18 November 2004**).
**Ashok Dalwai** headed the **Doubling Farmers' Income** Committee (**2016-18**); **K. Atchannaidu** is AP Agriculture Minister.
xa: The NCA recommended **HYVs, irrigation, credit reform** and coined **"social forestry"**.
Swaminathan Commission: MSP at **C2 + 50%**, universal crop insurance, **National Agricultural Risk Fund**.
Atchannaidu presented the separate AP Agriculture Budget **2026-27**.

n4df50ce0528.s: The National Commission on Agriculture (1976) is associated with coining the term:
n4df50ce0528.x: The National Commission on Agriculture recommended HYVs, irrigation and credit reforms and is associated with coining 'social forestry'.
xa: NCA's other recommendations: **HYVs**, **irrigation**, **credit reform**; chair **Nathu Ram Mirdha**.
⚠ Government MSP policy is **1.5 x A2+FL**, not the Commission's **C2 + 50%**.

n356639e52e4.s: The National Commission on Farmers (M.S. Swaminathan) recommended that MSP be fixed at:
n356639e52e4.x: The NCF recommended MSP at C2 + 50%; 1.5 times A2+FL is the Government's present MSP policy.
xa: MSPs are announced for **22 mandated crops**.
**National Commission on Agriculture** (**1970-76**) coined "**social forestry**".
**National Agriculture Policy 2000** targeted **over 4% annual growth** and a "**Rainbow Revolution**".

nd9efb571a2c.s: The National Agriculture Policy, 2000 envisaged annual agricultural growth of:
nd9efb571a2c.x: The policy targeted agricultural growth in excess of 4% per annum.
nd9efb571a2c.tq: Recall the exact threshold and distinguish 'in excess of' from an exact growth rate.
xs: **NAP 2000** targeted **more than 4%** (over 4%) annual agricultural growth — option **(4)**.
It was announced in **July 2000**.
xa: It sought private participation via **contract farming** and land leasing.
It promised price protection and **national agricultural insurance**.
It called for a **"Rainbow Revolution"** across all farm sub-sectors.

nd6cad766355.s: The National Agriculture Policy, 2000 envisaged a broad-based ____ covering all farm sub-sectors.
nd6cad766355.x: NAP 2000 emphasised a Rainbow Revolution across farm sub-sectors, along with private participation, price protection and insurance.
xa: Announced **July 2000**; growth target **over 4%**.
Rainbow colours: **Yellow**-oilseeds, **Blue**-fisheries, **Golden**-horticulture/honey, **Silver**-eggs, **Grey**-fertilisers.

n0818c81d01b.s: The Ashok Dalwai Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income used which base year?
n0818c81d01b.x: The base year was 2015-16, with 2022 as the target year.
xa: It shifted the focus from "**production**" to "**income**".
It listed **seven sources of income growth**, e.g. crop productivity, livestock productivity, better price realisation.
**National Rainfed Area Authority** set up in **2006** for dryland upgradation via a **watershed approach**.

n9f169f408c1.s: Rainfed farming accounts for approximately what share of India’s net sown area and food production, respectively?
n9f169f408c1.x: Rainfed farming covers about 50–60% of net sown area and contributes approximately 40% of food production.
n9f169f408c1.tq: Keep the area share and production share separate; they are not the same percentage.
xs: Rainfed farming covers about **50-60% of net sown area** and ~**40% of food production** — option **(1)**.
The other pairs overstate or understate both shares; the notes give only these two figures.
xa: ⚠ Some notes put rainfed area at **50%**.
The **National Rainfed Area Authority (NRAA)** was set up in **2006**.
**NMSA**'s **Rainfed Area Development** gives **₹30,000 per family** for **IFS** models.

n257310ea564.s: The National Rainfed Area Authority (NRAA), set up in 2006, mainly:
o: Provides knowledge inputs and coordinates rainfed-area upgradation through a watershed approach
n257310ea564.x: NRAA is an expert body that provides knowledge inputs and coordinates upgrading of dryland and rainfed areas through a watershed approach.
xa: Rainfed farming = **50-60%** of net sown area, ~**40%** of food production.
**NMSA** (climate-resilient, rainfed farming) is one of **8 NAPCC missions**.

n856f0ee66e4.s: The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture became a sub-mission of Krishonnati from:
n856f0ee66e4.x: NMSA became a Krishonnati sub-mission from 2018-19 and was brought under PM-RKVY from 2022-23.
xa: Operational launch **2014-15**; APPSC **2018** key treats it as started in **2011-12**.
Components: **RAD**, **Soil Health Management**, **Per Drop More Crop**, **Agroforestry**.

nd361d5a1457.s: Which one of the following is NOT a component of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture?
nd361d5a1457.x: RAD, Soil Health Management and Per Drop More Crop are NMSA components. National Agricultural Market is not listed as an NMSA component.
nd361d5a1457.tq: Find the one item belonging to agricultural marketing rather than the mission’s sustainability components.
xs: **National Agricultural Market** is not an NMSA component — option **(2)**; e-NAM is a price-realisation scheme (**April 2016**, SFAC).
NMSA components: **Rainfed Area Development**, **Soil Health Management**, **Per Drop More Crop**, **Agroforestry**.
xa: RAD gives **₹30,000 per family** for **ICAR** IFS models.
Soil Health Cards are free **every two years**; micro-irrigation subsidy up to **55%**.
e-NAM covers **1,656 mandis**, 23 States + 4 UTs.

n46e063e834a.s: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana announced for 2025-26 is proposed as a Central Sector scheme covering:
o: All agricultural districts for five years
100 low-performing agricultural districts for six years
n46e063e834a.x: The scheme is proposed as a Central Sector scheme for 100 low-performing agricultural districts for six years.
n46e063e834a.tq: Match the scheme with its coverage, duration and performance-based district selection.
xs: **PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana** (**2025-26**) is **Central Sector**, for **100 low-performing agri-districts for 6 years** — option **(4)**.
It targets **low-performing**, not high-performing or horticultural, districts.
xa: Another **2025-26** mission: **pulses**, with **100% MSP procurement** of **tur, urad, masoor** for **four years** via **NAFED/NCCF**.
Older mission: Technology Mission on Oilseeds, Pulses and Maize (**1986**) → **NMOOP (2014)**.

nbaa72524a1a.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the identified sources of growth in farmers’ income?
o: Exclusive dependence on traditional low-value crops
nbaa72524a1a.x: The seven sources include crop productivity, livestock productivity, resource-use efficiency, cropping intensity, diversification to high-value crops, better price realisation and movement to non-farm jobs. Exclusive dependence on traditional low-value crops is not one of them.
nbaa72524a1a.tq: Find the option that contradicts the diversification and productivity-based approach.
xs: **Exclusive dependence on traditional low-value crops** is not a source — option **(2)**; the Committee wanted **diversification to high-value crops**.
**Crop productivity**, **livestock productivity** and **diversification to high-value crops** are among the **seven sources**.
xa: Remaining sources: **resource-use efficiency**, **cropping intensity**, **better price realisation**, **shift to non-farm jobs**.
**Ashok Dalwai Committee** (**2016-18**): **14 volumes**, target **2022**, base **2015-16**.

n842547a4b4c.s: The Doubling Farmers' Income approach shifts the focus from production towards:
o: Income enhancement through value addition, market reform and post-harvest infrastructure
n842547a4b4c.x: The approach shifts from 'production' to 'income' via value addition, e-NAM and APMC reform, post-harvest infrastructure and allied integration.
xa: Other levers: **clusters**, **e-NAM/APMC** reform, **land-leasing laws**.
**Ashok Dalwai Committee** (**2016-18**), **14 volumes**, target **2022**.
**e-NAM** (**April 2016**, SFAC) now covers **1,656 mandis**.

n1178389591d.s: India’s entry into the WTO in 1995 was associated with which combination in the agricultural sector?
o: Reduced import competition and increased subsidies as a share of farm income
Increased import competition and declining subsidies as a share of farm income
Abolition of all domestic agricultural support
Reduced international trade and unchanged farm incomes
n1178389591d.x: WTO entry increased import competition, while subsidies declined as a share of farm income.
n1178389591d.tq: Pair the two stated effects and reject options that exaggerate them into total abolition or withdrawal.
xs: **WTO entry in 1995** brought **increased import competition** and **declining subsidies** as a share of farm income — option **(2)**.
Option (1) reverses both effects; domestic support was not abolished, only disciplined through **WTO boxes**.
xa: **Green Box** (research, infrastructure, food security) is allowed; **Amber Box** (MSP, input subsidies) has reduction commitments.
Amber Box de minimis: **5% developed**, **10% developing**.
Liberalisation after **1991** also cut government investment in agriculture.

n4816b04516c.s: Which one of the following correctly states the WTO treatment of the Amber Box?
o: It consists only of decoupled income support.
It is not trade-distorting and is freely allowed without limits.
It carries reduction commitments, subject to de minimis limits of 5% for developed and 10% for developing countries.
It consists of payments tied to limiting production and has no reduction commitment.
n4816b04516c.x: Amber Box support is subject to reduction commitments, with de minimis limits of 5% for developed and 10% for developing countries.
n4816b04516c.tq: Distinguish Amber Box reduction commitments from Green Box permission and Blue Box production-limitation payments.
xs: The **Amber Box** carries **reduction commitments**, with de minimis **5% for developed** and **10% for developing** countries — option **(3)**.
**Decoupled income support** and "not trade-distorting, allowed" describe the **Green Box**.
Payments **tied to limiting production** are the **Blue Box**.
xa: Amber Box covers **MSP** and input subsidies on power, fertiliser, seed and irrigation.
⚠ For India, the relevant de minimis is **10%**.
**WTO entry 1995** raised import competition and cut subsidies as a share of farm income.

nindian-economy-13-5.s: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, which of the following falls in the Amber Box?
nindian-economy-13-5.x: Price support is Amber Box; decoupled income support, environmental programmes and farmer training are Green Box.
n: Decoupled income support is an example of Green Box support. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 16-17]
Environmental programmes are examples of Green Box support. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 16-17]
Farmer training is an example of Green Box support. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 16-17]
Price support is an example of Amber Box support. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 16-17]
xa: Other Green Box items: **regional development**, **agricultural research**, **pest and disease control**.
Amber Box also covers **production-linked subsidies** and input subsidies (power, fertiliser, seed, irrigation).
**Blue Box**: direct payments tied to limiting production.

n56414f7667a.s: The National Food Security Mission was renamed as which of the following in Financial Year 2024-25?
o: National Food Security and Nutrition Mission
n56414f7667a.x: NFSM was renamed the National Food Security and Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) in FY 2024-25.
n56414f7667a.tq: Distinguish the original mission name from its later official renaming.
xs: NFSM was renamed the **National Food Security and Nutrition Mission (NFSNM)** in **FY25** — option **(4)**.
The renaming added **nutrition** to its mandate, matching its coverage of **coarse/nutri-cereals**.
xa: NFSM launched **October 2007**; **Centrally Sponsored**.
Crops: rice, wheat, pulses, **coarse/nutri-cereals**, commercial crops (cotton, jute, sugarcane).
⚠ Exam angle: which mission was renamed **NFSNM** — answer NFSM.

na16aed07289.s: Which of the following funding ratios is associated with the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture, including its special-region pattern?
o: 60:40 generally and 90:10 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States
50:50 generally and 75:25 for the North-Eastern States
90:10 generally and 60:40 for the Himalayan States
na16aed07289.x: MIDH follows a 60:40 sharing ratio generally and 90:10 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan regions.
na16aed07289.tq: Compare the normal cost-sharing ratio with the special-region ratio.
xs: **MIDH** is funded **60:40** generally and **90:10** for **NE/Himalayan** States — option **(2)**.
No **75:25** or **50:50** pattern is given for MIDH, so options (1), (3) and (4) are wrong.
xa: MIDH was launched in **2014-15**.
Coverage: fruits, vegetables, spices, flowers, mushrooms, coconut, cashew, cocoa, bamboo.
**NMSA** also dates from **2014-15** (operational launch).

nbd8e55d9dd7.s: The National Mission on Edible Oils–Oilseeds, announced on 3 October 2024, has an outlay of:
nbd8e55d9dd7.x: NMEO-Oilseeds has an outlay of ₹10,103 crore and aims to raise oilseed output from 39 MT to 69.7 MT by 2030-31.
xa: Oilseed output is to rise from **39 MT** to **69.7 MT**; crops include groundnut, mustard, soybean.
NMEO-Oil Palm focuses on **NE** and **A&N**.
AP leads India in **oil palm**: **2.49 lakh ha**, **48%** of India.

nd26003b0be4.s: Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) mainly aims to:
o: Give grants to raise State spending on agriculture through State-led plans
Give interest subvention on crop loans
nd26003b0be4.x: RKVY gives grants to raise State spending on agriculture through State-led agricultural plans; it now runs under PM-RKVY.
xa: Launched **2007-08**; now under the umbrella **PM-RKVY**.
