**NMSA** has been under **PM-RKVY since 2022-23**.
**NFSM** was launched in **October 2007**.

nf5e015f8912.s: Andhra Pradesh leads India in the area under which crop, with about 2.49 lakh hectares or 48% of the national area in 2024-25?
nf5e015f8912.x: AP leads India in oil palm: 2.49 lakh ha (48% of India's area; earlier 2.27 lakh ha) and 22.81 lakh MT of fresh fruit bunches in 2024-25 (SES 2025-26). AP is not recorded as holding that position for cashew, coconut or cocoa.
nf5e015f8912.tq: FFB (fresh fruit bunches) points to oil palm.
xs: AP leads India in **oil palm** — **2.49 lakh ha**, **48%** of India's area in **2024-25** — option **(2)**.
The notes record no such lead for cashew, coconut or cocoa (these are **MIDH** crops).
xa: Area rose from **2.27 lakh ha** earlier; output **22.81 lakh MT FFB** (SES **2025-26**).
**NMEO-Oil Palm** (**August 2021**, **₹11,040 crore**) focuses on **NE** and **A&N**.
AP aims at **30%** agri growth in five years with **17 growth engines**.

n62f262e528c.s: Under the Per Drop More Crop component of NMSA, the micro-irrigation subsidy can be up to:
n62f262e528c.x: Per Drop More Crop gives a micro-irrigation subsidy of up to 55%.
xa: The fourth component is **Agroforestry**.
NMSA is one of **8 NAPCC missions**; under **PM-RKVY since 2022-23**.

n103674493f6.s: Under PM-AASHA, which component involves procurement by NAFED and NCCF?
n103674493f6.x: The Price Support Scheme (PSS) under PM-AASHA involves procurement through agencies such as NAFED and NCCF.
n103674493f6.tq: Discriminate among similarly abbreviated PM-AASHA components by matching each one with its specific function.
xs: The **Price Support Scheme (PSS)** involves procurement by **NAFED/NCCF** — option **(1)**.
**PDPS** pays the MSP-price gap; **MIS** and the **Price Stabilisation Fund** are separate components.
xa: PDPS coverage raised to **40%** of State oilseed output; MIS **25%**.
**PM-AASHA** (**2018**) aims at remunerative prices.

nd2db89d22c0.s: The e-NAM platform was launched in April 2016 by which organisation?
nd2db89d22c0.x: e-NAM was launched in April 2016 by the Small Farmers’ Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC).
nd2db89d22c0.tq: Use the launching agency as the decisive clue in a scheme–institution question.
xs: **e-NAM** was launched in **April 2016** by **SFAC** — option **(4)**.
**NAFED/NCCF** procure under PM-AASHA's **PSS**.
xa: e-NAM is an online unified market over **APMC mandis**: **1,656 mandis**, **23 States + 4 UTs** (Mar **2026**).
**e-NAM/APMC** reform is a lever of **Doubling Farmers' Income**.

n765b50aa032.s: Operation Greens (Budget 2018-19) was widened from 2021-22 to cover:
n765b50aa032.x: Operation Greens was widened from the original TOP commodities to 22 perishables from 2021-22.
xa: It began to stabilise **Tomato-Onion-Potato (TOP)** prices "on the lines of **Operation Flood**".
Other price-realisation schemes: **PM-AASHA**, **e-NAM**, **Krishi UDAN**.

nab917b4b181.s: Which one of the following was an effect of liberalisation after 1991 on Indian agriculture?
o: Replacement of agricultural subsidies by foreign aid
Increase in government investment in agriculture in every period
A ban on all private participation in agriculture
Decline in government investment in agriculture
nab917b4b181.x: The stated policy impact of post-1991 liberalisation was a decline in government investment in agriculture.
nab917b4b181.tq: Identify the precise policy consequence instead of accepting the positive-sounding reversal.
xs: Post-**1991** liberalisation brought a **decline in government investment in agriculture** — option **(4)** (APPSC **2023** key).
Option (2) says the opposite; liberalisation encouraged, not banned, private participation (e.g. **contract farming** in NAP **2000**).
xa: GDP share of agriculture fell from **29.02% (1991)** to **17.9% (2014)**, with rising rural indebtedness.
**WTO entry 1995**: import competition rose; subsidies as a share of farm income declined.
Input costs rose over **300%** since the early 2000s.

n172b02e0e86.s: Which genetically modified crop was approved for commercial cultivation in India in 2002?
n172b02e0e86.x: Bt cotton, approved in 2002, is the only genetically modified crop identified as approved for commercial cultivation in India.
n172b02e0e86.tq: Use the crop-year pair to distinguish the approved GM crop from unapproved alternatives.
xs: **Bt cotton**, approved in **2002**, is India's only GM crop approved for commercial cultivation — option **(2)**.
No Bt rice, soybean or wheat is approved for commercial cultivation.
xa: It is listed among the post-**1991** liberalisation-era changes in farming.
Input costs rose over **300%** since the early 2000s.
**WTO entry 1995** brought rising import competition.

n9fbd070e23e.s: Sustainable agriculture seeks to combine environmental health, economic profitability and:
n9fbd070e23e.x: The three pillars of sustainable agriculture are environmental health, economic profitability and social and economic equity.
xa: Meaning: using land so its **quality remains intact** without compromising future generations (APPSC **2019** key).
**NMSA** components: Rainfed Area Development, **Soil Health Management**, **Per Drop More Crop**, Agroforestry.

n388f27005f7.s: PM-KISAN provides eligible landholding farmer families with:
o: ₹6,000 a year in two instalments of ₹3,000
₹6,000 a year in three instalments of ₹2,000
n388f27005f7.x: PM-KISAN, a Central Sector scheme from 1 December 2018, gives ₹6,000 a year in three instalments of ₹2,000.
xa: It runs from **1 Dec 2018**; land cut-off date **1 Feb 2019**.
The **23rd** instalment reached **9.49 crore** farmers; total **>₹4.47 lakh crore** (Aug **2026**).
⚠ **Tenant farmers** are outside PM-KISAN; AP's Annadata Sukhibhava covers them.

nb78d72eb15e.s: Under Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan in Andhra Pradesh, the total annual assistance per family is:
nb78d72eb15e.x: The combined annual assistance is ₹20,000 per family, consisting of ₹14,000 from Andhra Pradesh and ₹6,000 from the Centre.
nb78d72eb15e.tq: Add the State and Central components before choosing the combined annual assistance.
xs: **Annadata Sukhibhava - PM Kisan** gives **₹20,000/family/year** — option **(4)**.
It is **AP ₹14,000 + Centre ₹6,000**; ₹6,000 and ₹14,000 are only the two parts.
**₹13,500** was the old **YSR Rythu Bharosa** amount.
xa: It covers landholders **and tenant farmers**.
**2025-26**: **46.86 lakh** families, **₹6,309 crore** in **2** instalments.
**2026-27**: AP Budget **₹6,600 crore**; SES proposal **₹7,260 crore** for **51 lakh** families.

ne63273533b4.s: Andhra Pradesh's Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan scheme covers:
ne63273533b4.x: It covers landholders and tenant farmers; tenants are outside the central PM-KISAN.
xa: Total aid **₹20,000/family/year** (AP **₹14,000** + Centre **₹6,000**).
Predecessor **YSR Rythu Bharosa** (**₹13,500**) also covered tenant and **RoFR** farmers.

n55f61dd152b.s: According to the Union Budget 2026–27 figure cited for agriculture, the allocation was approximately:
n55f61dd152b.x: The Union Budget 2026–27 allocated ₹1.3 lakh crore to agriculture, representing a 2.6 per cent increase.
n55f61dd152b.tq: Distinguish the Union agriculture allocation from the separate Andhra Pradesh budget and scheme-specific figures.
xs: **Union Budget 2026-27** gave agriculture **₹1.3 lakh crore** (**+2.6%**) — option **(2)**.
**₹6,600 crore** is AP's Annadata Sukhibhava allocation; **₹53,753 crore** is AP's separate Agriculture Budget; **₹7,260 crore** is the SES proposal.
xa: Farm unions criticised the absence of statutory **MSP** and **debt relief**.
AP's Agriculture Dept got **₹12,153 crore**; agriculture is **33.20% of GSDP**.

n4001d8ddb09.s: Post-harvest losses of fruits and vegetables in India may be as high as:
n4001d8ddb09.x: Fruits and vegetables may lose up to 40% post-harvest; the cold-chain deficit is about 30%.
xa: ⚠ **30%** = cold-chain deficit; **40%** = F&V loss; **35%** = farmer's share of retail price.
The cause heading is **price volatility and middlemen**.
Yields fall about **8% per 1°C** of warming.

n722c117c07f.s: Which of the following is the recommended ideal N:P:K ratio for balanced soil nutrient application?
n722c117c07f.x: The recommended ideal N:P:K ratio is 4:2:1. The ratios beginning with 10.9 describe the reported imbalance in soil nutrient use.
n722c117c07f.tq: Discriminate between the existing input pattern and the recommended benchmark.
xs: The recommended ideal NPK ratio is **4:2:1** — option **(2)**.
**10.9:4.1:1** is the actual ratio (Economic Survey **2023-24**); **10.9:4.9:1** is kharif **2023** alone — both show overuse of N.
**2:4:1** reverses N and P.
xa: This imbalance is listed under **soil degradation** as a cause of agrarian crisis.
Average foodgrain yield is **2,929 kg/ha** against a **4,000 kg** world average.

nee2de52d524.s: About what share of India's groundwater blocks are over-exploited?
nee2de52d524.x: About 17% of groundwater blocks are over-exploited; groundwater supplies about 64% of irrigation.
xa: Distress drivers include **failed borewells** in rainfed areas.
Yields fall about **8% per 1°C** of warming.
Kharif **2026** rain deficit: opposition claimed **54.73%** deficit in **653 of 685** mandals.

nf771a7cb94e.s: Which of the following set of measures is associated with improving the viability of small and marginal holdings?
o: Reduction of irrigation and removal of collective institutions
Exclusive dependence on individual machinery ownership and informal credit
Custom Hiring Centres, cluster farming and cooperative or joint farming
Abolition of producer organisations and cluster-based activities
nf771a7cb94e.x: Custom Hiring Centres, cluster farming and cooperative or joint farming are identified as remedies for the viability constraints of small holdings.
nf771a7cb94e.tq: Select the option containing the complete set of stated institutional and operational remedies.
xs: **Custom Hiring Centres**, **cluster farming** and **cooperative/joint farming** are the remedies — option **(3)**.
The other options remove collective institutions, which the notes treat as remedies.
xa: AP: **210** primary Cooperative Joint Farming Societies.
Custom hiring answers the problem that **mechanisation is uneconomical** on small plots.

ncc58223d132.s: Why can actual cultivators be deprived of insurance and relief during a rainfall-deficit season?
o: Because they are missing from e-crop data
Because MSP procurement excludes all tenant farmers by definition
Because PM-KISAN is limited to urban households
Because CCRCs automatically cancel crop insurance
ncc58223d132.x: Actual cultivators missing from e-crop data can lose access to insurance and relief.
ncc58223d132.tq: Apply the record-visibility problem to the stated consequence for cultivators.
xs: Actual cultivators **missing from e-crop records** lose insurance, relief and credit — option **(1)**.
This surfaced in the **Kharif 2026** El Nino / rain deficit.
xa: Root problem: **tenant invisibility** in land records.
Opposition claimed a **54.73%** deficit in **653 of 685** mandals; sowing **69%** of normal.

nbdd2fb4dc2e.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the debt cycle faced by distressed farmers?
o: Borrowing → high input cost → asset sale → crop failure → fresh borrowing
High input cost → borrowing → crop failure or low price → inability to repay → fresh borrowing → asset sale → debt trap
Crop failure → institutional credit → higher income → asset purchase → debt repayment
Low input cost → borrowing → assured procurement → inability to repay → debt trap
nbdd2fb4dc2e.x: The stated cycle begins with high input costs, leads to borrowing, crop failure or low prices, non-repayment, fresh borrowing and asset sales, ultimately producing a debt trap.
nbdd2fb4dc2e.tq: Arrange the stages by cause and consequence, beginning with the initial financial pressure.
xs: The debt cycle: **high input cost → borrowing → crop failure or low price → inability to repay → fresh borrowing → asset sale → debt trap** — option **(2)**.
Option (1) puts borrowing before input cost; options (3) and (4) start with relief factors, not distress.
xa: Input costs rose **300%+** since the early 2000s.
ADSI **2015**: the biggest cause of farmer suicides = **bankruptcy or indebtedness**.
Root causes: debt = **immediate trigger**; roots = rain-fed risk, low prices, no social security.

nca35af099d2.s: As per the Agriculture Census 2015-16, semi-medium and medium holdings accounted for what share of operated area?
nca35af099d2.x: They operated 43.6% of the area while forming only 13.2% of holdings.
xa: ⚠ Small + marginal: **86.2%** of holdings but only **47.3%** of area.
All-India: **146 million** holdings, average **1.08 ha** (**2015-16**), down from **2.28 ha (1971)**.

n321796aa692.s: The NSSO 77th Round Situation Assessment Survey of agricultural households relates to the year:
n321796aa692.x: The 77th Round SAS relates to 2019; it found about half of agricultural households indebted, with average debt of about ₹74,121.
xa: Income composition: **wages** → **crop cultivation** → livestock.
**Telangana** = **91.7%** indebted; about half of AP farmers rely on **non-institutional credit** vs national **~31%**.
NSSO **70th Round** (**2013**): **Rajasthan** had the highest share of agricultural households.

ne10e6e29708.s: What proportion of agricultural households in Telangana were indebted, against 93.2% in Andhra Pradesh?
ne10e6e29708.x: Telangana's figure was 91.7%, lower than Andhra Pradesh's 93.2%.
xa: National indebtedness is only about **50%**.
AP farmers' reliance on **non-institutional credit** ~**50%** vs national ~**31%**.

n95e4461e520.s: As per the NSSO 77th Round, the largest source of agricultural household income was:
n95e4461e520.x: Wages formed the largest share, followed by crop cultivation and then livestock.
xa: Average monthly income **₹10,218** (**77th Round**).
**59%** nominal rise in farm household income **FY13 to FY19**.
**Kerala** (70th Round): over **60%** earned most income from **non-agricultural** sources.

n2c6d73d27b7.s: In the Guntur study, the average debt of tenant farmers was:
n2c6d73d27b7.x: Tenants had average debt of ₹2,07,444 against owners' ₹76,306.
xa: Guntur study (**NABARD**-supported, **2023**): **88%** of farmers in debt.
Informal share of loans **51.5%**; tenants' loans ~**60%** informal.
Tenants have no passbook, **KCC** or insurance in AP.

nb4b48005e42.s: In the Guntur study, informal sources accounted for what share of agricultural loans?
nb4b48005e42.x: Informal sources made up 51.5% of loans; about 60% of tenants' loans were informal.
xa: **88%** of Guntur farmers were in debt.
Tenants' average debt **Rs 2,07,444** vs owners' **Rs 76,306**.

n22b210d81d5.s: In the NCF's MSP formula, C2 includes A2 costs, imputed family labour and:
o: Imputed rent and interest on owned land and capital
n22b210d81d5.x: C2 = A2 + imputed family labour + imputed rent and interest on owned land and capital.
xa: The Commission recommended **MSP = C2 + 50%**.
⚠ Government applies **50%** over **A2+FL** instead.

nb0dac8bccc4.s: PM-KISAN pays ₹6,000 a year to farmers in:
nb0dac8bccc4.x: PM-KISAN, a Central Sector Scheme since February 2019, pays three instalments of ₹2,000 into Aadhaar-seeded accounts.
xa: **PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana** = pension for small farmers; **24.92 lakh** enrolled.
AP's **Annadata Sukhibhava** tops up PM-KISAN and includes tenants.
⚠ **KALIA** = Odisha; **Rythu Bandhu → Rythu Bharosa** = Telangana.

neab23d8dd6b.s: The Andhra Pradesh Microfinance Institutions (Regulation of Money Lending) Act was enacted in:
neab23d8dd6b.x: Andhra Pradesh enacted the Microfinance Institutions (Regulation of Money Lending) Act in 2011, following the 2010 microfinance crisis.
neab23d8dd6b.tq: Distinguish the year of the crisis from the year of the regulatory legislation.
xs: The **AP Microfinance Institutions (Regulation of Money Lending) Act** came in **2011** — option **(2)**.
**2010** was the year of the MFI **crisis** that led to it.
xa: Current microfinance guard-rails: max **3 lenders**, household cap **Rs 2 lakh**.
AP farmers rely ~**50%** on **non-institutional credit**.
The **AP Land Licensed Cultivators Act** (Loan Eligibility Cards) is also of **2011**.

nb31c1517b20.s: The principal source for official data on farmer and agricultural labourer suicides in India is which of the following?
o: Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households
Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India
nb31c1517b20.x: The National Crime Records Bureau publishes the report titled “Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India” (ADSI), which is the cited source for these suicide data.
nb31c1517b20.tq: Identify the exact official report title rather than a related agricultural publication.
xs: The source is the NCRB report **"Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India" (ADSI)** — option **(4)**.
The **SAS** covers household income and debt, not suicides.
xa: ADSI **2015**: biggest cause = **bankruptcy or indebtedness** (APPSC G1 **2017** key).
Farm sector total **10,546** = **6.2%** of suicides.
A **28-year** NCRB analysis (**1995-2023**) found a sharp resurgence in **2023**.

nc9c8eb57e60.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the regional pattern of farmer suicides?
o: Suicides have been concentrated mainly in irrigated belts
The analysis found a sharp resurgence in 2023 after a decade of decline
Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh have historically been among the worst affected
nc9c8eb57e60.x: Farmer suicides have been concentrated mainly in rain-fed belts, not irrigated ones.
xa: AP: Tenant Farmers Association says **300+** suicides, only **112** officially recognised.
CM ordered an audit of every farmer suicide (Feb **2026**).

n6a4802523a1.s: According to the NCRB report 'Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India' 2015, the biggest cause of suicides among farmers was:
n6a4802523a1.x: ADSI 2015 named bankruptcy or indebtedness as the biggest cause of farmer suicides (APPSC Group 1 2017 key). Crop failure, family problems and illness are also listed causes, but each ranked below indebtedness.
xs: ADSI **2015**: the biggest cause was **bankruptcy or indebtedness** — option **(2)** (APPSC G1 **2017** key).
The notes rank no other cause above it.
xa: Debt cycle: high input cost → borrowing → crop failure → fresh borrowing → asset sale → **debt trap**.
Debt is the **immediate trigger**; roots = rain-fed risk, low prices, no social security.
Hotspots: **Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh**.

ncbd34418bc8.s: Which of the following has been identified as a major obstacle in extending formal benefits to tenant cultivators in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Prohibition on crop insurance for tenants
Absence of crop cultivation in the State
ncbd34418bc8.x: The requirement of the landowner's signature is a major obstacle for tenant cultivators seeking formal credit and other benefits.
ncbd34418bc8.tq: Apply the institutional requirement to a practical tenant-finance situation.
xs: The **landowner's signature** requirement is a key obstacle — option **(1)**.
CCRCs need an **owner-tenant agreement**; tenants actually can get insurance through them.
xa: Tenants = **70-80%** of AP cultivators.
They seek (**2026**) **Rs 2 lakh unsecured crop loans** via **KCC** for **RMG/JLG** members.

n797b970e0d8.s: Which combination correctly represents the mechanisms through which Andhra Pradesh has been described as a pioneer in tenant finance?
n797b970e0d8.x: Andhra Pradesh has been described as a pioneer in tenant finance through Rythu Mitra Groups, Joint Liability Groups and Crop Cultivator Rights Cards.
n797b970e0d8.tq: Start from the sure pair of the three tenant-finance mechanisms.
xs: AP pioneered tenant finance via **RMGs (Rythu Mitra Groups)**, **JLGs** and **CCRCs** — option **(1)**.
**LECs** were the older **2011** card, not part of this trio.
xa: Tenants seek **Rs 2 lakh** unsecured KCC loans for RMG/JLG members.

n4234d5e42e0.s: Who chaired the Expert Group on Agricultural Indebtedness constituted in 2007?
n4234d5e42e0.x: R. Radhakrishna chaired the Expert Group on Agricultural Indebtedness constituted in 2007.
n4234d5e42e0.tq: Use the chairperson-name association rather than substituting a familiar agriculture or economic expert.
xs: The **Expert Group on Agricultural Indebtedness** (**2007**) was chaired by **R. Radhakrishna** — option **(2)**.
**M.S. Swaminathan** chaired the **National Commission on Farmers** (**2004**).
xa: ⚠ **Radhakrishna** = indebtedness (**2007**); **Swaminathan** = farmers (**2004**); **Mohan Kanda** = crop holiday (**2011**).
The **AP Commission on Farmers' Welfare** found main drivers: unstable prices, weak procurement, rising input costs, lack of institutional credit.

n5dacbe8bbac.s: Which of the following was NOT among the recommendations associated with the National Commission on Farmers?
o: Secure rights for women and tenants
n5dacbe8bbac.x: The Commission recommended affordable credit, not its abolition. It also recommended land reforms, rights for women and tenants, universal crop insurance and a National Agricultural Risk Fund.
n5dacbe8bbac.tq: Identify the option that reverses a recommendation by using an institutional opposite.
xs: **Abolition of affordable institutional credit** was not recommended — option **(2)**; it urged **affordable/cheaper institutional credit**.
It did recommend **universal crop insurance**, **secure rights for women and tenants** and a **National Agricultural Risk Fund**.
xa: Others: **land reforms**, **irrigation**, **market reforms**.
MSP at **C2 + 50%**; **five reports (2004-06)**.

nf520646c9b7.s: Which of the following was NOT a demand of the farmers’ protests at Delhi borders during 2020-21?
o: Replacement of the three farm laws with a new national crop insurance law
Withdrawal of the Electricity (Amendment) Bill and the Air Quality Management Ordinance
Repeal of the three farm laws
nf520646c9b7.x: The listed demands were repeal of the three farm laws, legal MSP, and withdrawal of the Electricity (Amendment) Bill and the Air Quality Management Ordinance. Replacement with a new crop insurance law was not among the stated demands.
nf520646c9b7.tq: Find the one demand outside the established three-part demand set.
xs: A **new national crop insurance law** was not a demand — option **(1)**.
Real demands: **repeal of the three farm laws**, a **legal MSP guarantee**, withdrawal of the **Electricity (Amendment) Bill** and the Air Quality Management Ordinance.
xa: Outcome: the three laws were **repealed in 2021**.
**2026**: **SKM** burnt copies of the kharif MSP order (**27-31 May**).

nbc1b28202a6.s: The special committee set up after the 2011 crop holiday by paddy farmers of Konaseema (East Godavari) was chaired by:
nbc1b28202a6.x: The special committee on the 2011 Konaseema crop holiday was chaired by Mohan Kanda (asked in APPSC Group 1 2012). Koneru Ranga Rao headed the AP Land Committee, R. Radhakrishna the Expert Group on Agricultural Indebtedness, and M.S. Swaminathan the National Commission on Farmers.
xs: The **2011 crop holiday** committee was chaired by **Mohan Kanda** — option **(2)** (APPSC G1 **2012** question).
**R. Radhakrishna** chaired the **Expert Group on Agricultural Indebtedness** (**2007**); **M.S. Swaminathan** the **National Commission on Farmers** (**2004**).
xa: The crop holiday was by paddy farmers of **Konaseema** (**East Godavari**).
⚠ No official key exists for that APPSC question.

ncb1eeac0988.s: The microfinance guard-rails referred to in the economic survey provide for which combination?
o: A maximum of two lenders per borrower and a household cap of ₹1 lakh
A maximum of five lenders per borrower and a household cap of ₹2 lakh
A maximum of three lenders per borrower and a household cap of ₹2 lakh
A maximum of three lenders per borrower and a household cap of ₹5 lakh
ncb1eeac0988.x: The guard-rails prescribe a maximum of three lenders per borrower and a household borrowing cap of ₹2 lakh.
ncb1eeac0988.tq: Pair the lender-count ceiling with the household monetary ceiling.
xs: Guard-rails: max **3 lenders** per borrower and a household cap of **Rs 2 lakh** (May **2025**) — option **(3)**.
Two or five lenders, or caps of ₹1 lakh / ₹5 lakh, are not the stated limits.
xa: Warning (**2025-26**): MFI over-indebtedness; outstanding loans down **14%**.
AP regulated MFI lending after the **2010** crisis via the **2011** Act.
AP tenants seek **Rs 2 lakh unsecured crop loans** via **KCC** (**2026**).

nd50bc56395c.s: Under ADWDRS 2008, farmers other than small and marginal farmers got one-time-settlement relief of:
nd50bc56395c.x: Other farmers got 25% OTS relief on paying the remaining 75%; small and marginal farmers got a full waiver.
xa: About **₹52,000 crore**; announced in **Union Budget 2008-09**.
Waivers create **moral hazard** and do not fix structural causes.

n28fec6e0a9d.s: Under the AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme, 2014, the ceiling of relief was:
n28fec6e0a9d.x: The AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme, 2014, prescribed a ceiling of ₹1.5 lakh per family.
n28fec6e0a9d.tq: Distinguish the general family ceiling from the separate horticulture ceiling.
xs: The **AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme, 2014** had a ceiling of **₹1.5 lakh per family** — option **(4)**.
**₹50,000** was the max per family only for **horticulture** (Rs **10,000/acre**).
xa: Covered crop loans and crop-purpose **gold loans** up to **31 Dec 2013**.
Implemented by **Rythu Sadhikara Samstha**; also called **Rythu Runa Mafi**.

n622114f79fc.s: Which body implemented the AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme, 2014?
n622114f79fc.x: The AP Agricultural Debt Redemption Scheme was implemented through Rythu Sadhikara Samstha.
n622114f79fc.tq: Apply the ‘which body implemented it?’ trap by distinguishing the implementing agency from financial institutions.
xs: **Rythu Sadhikara Samstha** implemented the **2014** AP debt redemption — option **(3)**.
It was a State scheme (**Rythu Runa Mafi**), so the RBI, FCI and NABARD were not the implementing body.
xa: Ceiling **₹1.5 lakh per family**; horticulture Rs **10,000/acre**, max Rs **50,000/family**.
Covered crop loans and gold loans up to **31 Dec 2013**.
Central precedent: **Debt Waiver and Debt Relief Scheme, 2008** (~**₹52,000 crore**).

ne1d1867871a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about farm loan relief schemes?
o: ADWDRS 2008 – full waiver of eligible overdue loans of small and marginal farmers
AP horticulture relief – ₹10,000 per acre with no family ceiling
AP Debt Redemption Scheme, 2014 – crop and crop-purpose gold loans up to 31 December 2013
Telangana crop-loan waiver – more than 25 lakh families
ne1d1867871a.x: AP horticulture relief of ₹10,000 per acre was subject to a family maximum, not free of a ceiling.
xa: AP 2014 ceiling: **₹1.5 lakh per family**, via **Rythu Sadhikara Samstha**.
2008 waiver: others got **25%** OTS relief on paying **75%**; about **₹52,000 crore**.

nd947d5fb872.s: PMFBY, introduced in 2016, replaced NAIS and:
nd947d5fb872.x: PMFBY replaced NAIS (1999) and MNAIS (2010); WBCIS was not replaced.
xa: Motto: **"One Nation, One Crop, One Premium"**.
It is a **Central Sector Scheme**; the Centre's premium subsidy goes straight to insurers.
Farmer's max premium: **2%** kharif, **1.5%** rabi, **5%** commercial/horticultural.

n024175f11c0.s: Which one of the following correctly expresses the principle associated with PMFBY?
o: One Nation, One Farmer, One Subsidy
One District, One Crop, One Insurance
One State, One Crop, One Premium
One Nation, One Crop, One Premium
n024175f11c0.x: The principle associated with PMFBY is ‘One Nation, One Crop, One Premium’.
n024175f11c0.tq: Test the exact official slogan rather than a similar-looking administrative phrase.
xs: PMFBY's principle is **"One Nation, One Crop, One Premium"** — option **(4)**.
The other slogans are distortions of this motto.
xa: **PMFBY (2016)** replaced **NAIS (1999)** and **MNAIS (2010)**.
Uniform farmer premium caps: **2%** kharif, **1.5%** rabi, **5%** commercial.
Helpline: **Krishi Rakshak** — **14447**.

n24f44a9e687.s: PMFBY became voluntary for all farmers from:
n24f44a9e687.x: PMFBY became voluntary in 2020; it covers pre-sowing to post-harvest losses.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say it is compulsory for loanee farmers.
From **Kharif 2026** it also covers **wild-animal attack and paddy inundation**.
**4.19 crore** farmers insured in **2024-25**.

n7c39d569ebf.s: Under PMFBY, YES-TECH is used for:
n7c39d569ebf.x: YES-TECH is remote-sensing yield estimation; WINDS is weather stations, DigiClaim digital claims and RWBCIS weather-index insurance.
xa: Helpline **Krishi Rakshak** — **14447**.
In **9** years: **78.62 crore** applications; claims **₹1.82 lakh crore**.

ndb3dd253f32.s: Under PMFBY, the farmer's premium share is correctly stated as:
o: 2% for Kharif, 1.5% for Rabi, and 5% for commercial and horticultural crops
1.5% for Kharif, 2% for Rabi, and 5% for commercial crops
5% for Kharif, 2% for Rabi, and 1.5% for horticultural crops
2% for all crops in every season
ndb3dd253f32.x: The farmer premium under PMFBY is 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops and 5% for commercial and horticultural crops.
ndb3dd253f32.tq: Avoid reversing the Kharif and Rabi rates and retain the separate commercial-crop rate.
xs: Farmer's max premium: **2% kharif**, **1.5% rabi**, **5% commercial/horticultural** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) swaps kharif and rabi; option (3) mixes up all three.
xa: The rest of the premium is **shared by Centre and states**.
Food and **oilseeds** fall under the 2% / 1.5% slabs.
Motto: **"One Nation, One Crop, One Premium"**.

n8410a062798.s: From Rabi 2024-25, crop insurance in Andhra Pradesh under PMFBY/RWBCIS became:
o: Compulsory, with the State paying the full premium
Voluntary, with the Centre paying the full premium
Voluntary, with farmers paying a small fixed share and the State and Centre sharing the rest equally
Compulsory, with FPOs paying the premium
n8410a062798.x: From Rabi 2024-25 enrolment became voluntary; farmers pay a small fixed share and the State and Centre share the balance equally.
xa: Before this, **2019-24** insurance was free (State paid all).
AP runs **RWBCIS** alongside PMFBY.
Coverage then fell to **10.63 lakh** farmers, **11.81 lakh ha**.

ndf7733dc08d.s: For Kharif 2026, the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister issued which directive regarding crop insurance?
o: Only loanee farmers' paddy crop to be insured, with banks accountable
Only horticulture crops to be insured, with FPOs accountable
Every cultivated crop to be insured, with District Collectors accountable
Insurance to be made optional for all crops, with Mandal officers accountable
ndf7733dc08d.x: In July 2026 the CM ordered that every cultivated crop be insured for Kharif 2026, making District Collectors accountable for coverage.
ndf7733dc08d.tq: Every crop insured; Collector answers for it.
xs: For **Kharif 2026** the CM ordered **every cultivated crop** insured, with **District Collectors** accountable (July **2026**) — option **(3)**.
It was not limited to loanee, paddy or horticulture farmers.
xa: Enrolment closed **31 July**; paddy **15 August**.
**AP Rythu Sangham** wants free insurance restored.

naf5c1f618bd.x: PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana is a pension scheme for small farmers.
xa: Contrast **PM-KISAN**: income support of **₹6,000/year**.
Telangana's **Rythu Bima** is a **life cover**.

n5c8541f9656.s: Telangana's Rythu Bandhu (later Rythu Bharosa) assistance was reportedly raised to:
n5c8541f9656.x: Rythu Bandhu/Rythu Bharosa was reported at ₹12,000 per acre, with a crop loan waiver for over 25 lakh families and Rythu Bima life cover.
xa: Rythu Bima claims: **₹8,003.40 cr** (IYB **2026**).
⚠ **KALIA** = Odisha; **Rythu Bandhu** = Telangana; **Annadata Sukhibhava** = AP.

n502dae37669.s: Under Dr YSR Free Crop Insurance in Andhra Pradesh (2019-24), the crop insurance premium was paid by:
o: The State and the Centre equally
n502dae37669.x: The State paid the entire premium, and CCRC holders were covered.
xa: The **AP Rythu Sangham** wants free insurance restored.
**2024**: **34.93 lakh** farmers on **28.67 lakh ha** covered.

na0fb4dd4ca6.s: The Central Sector scheme launched in 2020 with an outlay of ₹6,865 crore aims to form and promote how many FPOs?
na0fb4dd4ca6.x: The 10,000 FPO scheme was launched in 2020 with an outlay of ₹6,865 crore.
xa: FPOs answer small-holding problems such as **weak bargaining power** and poor credit.
Other remedies: **Custom Hiring Centres**, cluster farming, cooperative/joint farming.
AP has **210 primary Cooperative Joint Farming Societies**; federations under liquidation (**2024-25**).

nec9dfedc1c1.s: As per the NSSO 70th Round (2013), which State had the highest share of agricultural households among its rural households?
nec9dfedc1c1.x: Rajasthan had the highest share (UPSC 2018 key); the 70th Round was held in 2013.
xa: Next SAS **2026-27** along with **AIDIS**.
77th Round: ~**50%** indebted; income **₹10,218** a month.

n77353077141.s: Under the Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS), a payout is made when:
o: Crop yield falls below the threshold yield
Observed weather deviates from specified trigger levels
The market price falls below MSP
The farmer's landholding is below one hectare
n77353077141.x: RWBCIS is weather-index insurance: it pays when weather deviates from predetermined trigger levels.
xa: AP runs RWBCIS **alongside PMFBY**.
From **Rabi 2024-25** AP reintroduced **voluntary enrolment** under both.
PMFBY uses **WINDS** weather stations.

n02794d2219f.s: During the 1990s protests over the WTO, GATT and the Dunkel Draft, which farm leader supported globalisation?
n02794d2219f.x: Sharad Joshi of Shetkari Sangathan supported globalisation; Nanjundaswamy (KRRS) and Tikait (BKU) opposed it.
xa: Organisations: Joshi — **Shetkari Sangathan**; Nanjundaswamy — **KRRS**; Tikait — **BKU**.
**2020-21** Delhi protests ended with the three farm laws **repealed in 2021**.

n9d1114abf7f.s: The Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha (KRRS) was led by:
n9d1114abf7f.x: Nanjundaswamy led KRRS; Sharad Joshi led Shetkari Sangathan and Mahendra Singh Tikait led BKU.
xa: In the **Dunkel Draft** debate, Joshi **supported** globalisation; the other two **opposed**.
**SKM** (about **500** farm unions) protested **27-31 May 2026**.

n81ce0e1322f.s: What was the principal legislative outcome of the 2020-21 farmers’ protests at the Delhi borders?
o: The Dunkel Draft was withdrawn by the WTO in 2021
The three farm laws were repealed in 2021
The Electricity (Amendment) Bill was enacted in 2021
The three farm laws were constitutionally entrenched in 2021
n81ce0e1322f.x: The three farm laws were repealed in 2021.
n81ce0e1322f.tq: Link the protest episode to its stated outcome while rejecting nearby policy events.
xs: The **three farm laws were repealed in 2021** — option **(2)**.
The **Dunkel Draft** belongs to the **1990s** WTO/GATT protests.
xa: Demands also included a **legal MSP guarantee** and withdrawal of the **Electricity (Amendment) Bill**.
AP farm bodies protested from **30 March 2026** for MSP procurement.

nd5d85806a98.s: The crop holiday observed by paddy farmers in 2011 was associated with which region of Andhra Pradesh?
nd5d85806a98.x: The 2011 crop holiday was observed by paddy farmers of Konaseema in East Godavari district.
nd5d85806a98.tq: Use the location clue to identify the specific agrarian movement.
xs: The **2011 crop holiday** was by paddy farmers of **Konaseema** (**East Godavari**) — option **(1)**.
They stopped paddy cultivation in protest, a sign of AP's agrarian distress.
xa: A special committee under **Mohan Kanda** studied it (APPSC G1 **2012** question).
⚠ **Mohan Kanda** = crop holiday (**2011**); **Radhakrishna** = indebtedness (**2007**).
The **AP Land Licensed Cultivators Act** also dates from **2011**.

n02c8f25e2ca.s: The Andhra Pradesh Land Licensed Cultivators Act, 2011 primarily provided tenants with which instrument?
n02c8f25e2ca.x: The AP Land Licensed Cultivators Act, 2011 provided Loan Eligibility Cards (LECs) to tenant cultivators.
n02c8f25e2ca.tq: Discriminate between closely related agricultural card-based instruments.
xs: The **AP Land Licensed Cultivators Act, 2011** gave tenants **Loan Eligibility Cards (LEC)** — option **(1)**.
**Crop Cultivator Rights Cards** came later under the **2019** Act.
xa: LECs gave credit/insurance **without affecting owner's rights**.

nfeed0eb438f.s: Which is a remedy for tenant distress arising from tenants' invisibility in land records?
nfeed0eb438f.x: CCRCs are identified as a remedy for tenant distress, helping tenants access institutional credit.
xa: CCRCs come from the **AP Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019**, valid **11 months**.
**8.24 lakh** active CCRCs → **₹3,768 crore** tenant loans (**2025-26**).
Obstacle: the **landowner's signature** is needed.

n306e5df3dcd.s: The rent ceiling contemplated under tenancy reform was generally in the range of:
o: One-half to two-thirds of the produce
One-tenth to one-twentieth of the produce
One-third to one-half of the produce
One-fourth to one-sixth of the produce
n306e5df3dcd.x: Tenancy reform sought to regulate rent by limiting it to approximately one-fourth to one-sixth of the produce.
n306e5df3dcd.tq: Test the specific fraction range rather than the general idea of rent regulation.
xs: Rent was capped at **one-fourth to one-sixth** (**1/4 to 1/6**) of produce — option **(4)**.
This is the **regulation of rent** goal of tenancy reform.
xa: ⚠ Rent cap **1/4 to 1/6**; Bhoodan appeal **1/6th** of land; bargadar share **75%**.
AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act **1956**: max rent **30% wet / 25% dry**.
Other goals: **security of tenure**, **ownership rights** to tenants.

n2bf088aa2db.s: Land ceiling laws in India redistributed about what share of the cultivable area?
n2bf088aa2db.x: Despite two rounds of ceiling laws (1950s and early 1970s), less than 2% of cultivable area was redistributed.
xa: Exemptions (plantations, orchards, **"mechanised" farms**) limited the surplus.
AP phase II: **20 lakh acres** surplus estimated vs only **5 lakh acres** taken over.

nf16ee012aeb.s: Consolidation of holdings achieved comparatively greater success in which group of regions?
o: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
nf16ee012aeb.x: Consolidation succeeded in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, while it made little progress in southern and eastern States.
nf16ee012aeb.tq: Match the regional outcome with the correct geographical cluster.
xs: **Consolidation** succeeded in **Punjab, Haryana and western UP** — option **(4)**.
It made **little progress in southern and eastern States**, ruling out options (1), (2) and (3).
xa: Consolidation is one of the land-reform types along with abolition, tenancy and ceilings.
**Operation Barga** (**West Bengal**) was the eastern success — in tenancy, not consolidation.

n191c19dae8b.s: The 1972 national guidelines on land ceiling adopted which unit for fixing the ceiling?
n191c19dae8b.x: Pre-1972 laws used the individual as the unit, encouraging benami transfers; the 1972 guidelines shifted to the family.
xa: 1972 ceiling: **10-18 acres** two-crop irrigated, **27 acres** single-crop, **54 acres** dry.
⚠ AP **1961** Act = individual unit; **1973** Act = **family of 5**.
Less than **2%** of cultivable area was redistributed.

nb8667576a2d.x: The Kumarappa Committee recommended cooperative farming in 1949.
nb8667576a2d.tq: Match the committee with its specific farming recommendation.
xs: The **Kumarappa Committee (1949)** recommended **cooperative farming** — option **(4)**.
Joint cooperative farming is **voluntary**, so compulsory collective farming is wrong.
xa: The **Nagpur Resolution (1959)** made it a party goal.
It failed — **captured by rich peasants** to evade ceilings.
Features: land pooled **voluntarily**, members **retain ownership**, management **elected by all members**.

na8bf5d40065.s: Vinoba Bhave launched the Bhoodan movement in 1951 at:
na8bf5d40065.x: Bhoodan was initiated by Vinoba Bhave at Pochampally in Nalgonda (Telangana) in 1951.
xa: Appeal: donate **1/6th** of land; over **40 lakh acres** pledged, much barren.
It led to **Gramdan**.
AP's **1973** ceiling Act exempted **Bhoodan** lands.

nc96e48328cc.s: The Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016 was prepared by:
nc96e48328cc.x: The Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016 was prepared by NITI Aayog, with inputs associated with the T. Haque Committee.
nc96e48328cc.tq: Identify the institution associated with preparation of the model legislation.
xs: **NITI Aayog** prepared the **Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016** (**T. Haque** committee) — option **(1)**.
It is a model law for States, not an RBI, NDC or FCI measure.
xa: It **legalises leasing**, gives tenants credit/insurance and **protects owner's title**.
First State to implement it: **Uttarakhand** (APPSC **2018** key).
Leasing is **preferred to acquisition**.

nbb7fb6c5dc3.s: Which committee recommended the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act in the Andhra area?
nbb7fb6c5dc3.x: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act was recommended by the Prakasam Committee in 1938.
nbb7fb6c5dc3.tq: Identify the committee associated with the specific legislation.
xs: The **Prakasam Committee (1938)** recommended abolishing **zamindari and inamdari** in Andhra — option **(4)**.
**Subba Rao** advised the **1956** Tenancy Act; **Koneru Ranga Rao** led the **2006** Land Committee; **Kumarappa** (**1949**) recommended cooperative farming.
xa: ⚠ **Prakasam** = abolition (**1938**); **Subba Rao** = Andhra tenancy (**1956**); **Koneru Ranga Rao** = Land Committee (**2006**).
The Madras Estates Act came into force in **1950** (dated **1948**).

n959784455a5.s: The Koneru Ranga Rao Committee dealt mainly with:
n959784455a5.x: It was a Land Committee on land-related problems in Andhra Pradesh.
xa: Headed by **Koneru Ranga Rao**, constituted **2006**.
Focus areas: **assigned lands**, **land rights**, **tenancy regulation**, **land records**.
⚠ Eliminate **corporate farming** as a focus area.

n68c363ee23c.s: Clause (h), relating to rent and tenancy rights in Article 323B, was added by which Constitutional Amendment?
n68c363ee23c.x: Clause (h) concerning rent and tenancy rights was added to Article 323B by the 75th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1993.
n68c363ee23c.tq: Match the constitutional provision with the amendment number and year.
xs: Clause **(h)** "rent and tenancy rights" of **Art. 323B** came by the **75th Amendment (1993)** — option **(4)**.
Art. 323B deals with **tribunals**.
xa: **34th (1974) / 66th (1990)** placed more land laws in the Ninth Schedule.

n94fa125799b.s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Articles 31A and 31B and added the Ninth Schedule?
n94fa125799b.x: The First Amendment Act of 1951 inserted Articles 31A and 31B and created the Ninth Schedule in the context of land-reform protection.
n94fa125799b.tq: Link the constitutional provisions to the amendment that introduced them.
xs: The **1st Amendment (1951)** inserted **Arts. 31A, 31B** and the **Ninth Schedule** — option **(4)**.
The **25th (1971)** inserted **31C**; the **4th (1955)** widened 31A; the **17th (1964)** widened "estate".
xa: It followed **Kameshwar Singh v. Bihar**.
**I.R. Coelho (2007)**: laws added after **24 April 1973** are open to **Basic Structure** review.

nf97540775e2.s: The Seventeenth Amendment Act, 1964 widened the meaning of:
nf97540775e2.x: The 17th Amendment widened 'estate'; Article 31C came later through the 25th Amendment.
xa: The 17th was challenged in **Golaknath (1967)**.

ncacb0e8a47d.s: In I.R. Coelho, the Supreme Court held that Ninth Schedule laws added after which date are open to Basic Structure review?
ncacb0e8a47d.x: Laws added after 24 April 1973, the date of the Kesavananda Bharati judgment, can be reviewed against the Basic Structure.
xa: The Ninth Schedule was added by the **1st Amendment (1951)**.
**34th (1974) / 66th (1990)** added **55 State Acts incl. AP**.

n8bf4bdbf5dc.s: The first State to implement the Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016 was:
n8bf4bdbf5dc.x: Uttarakhand, not Andhra Pradesh, was the first State to implement the Model Act (APPSC 2018 key).
xa: The Model Act **2016** was prepared by **NITI Aayog** (T. Haque committee).
AP's **1956** Andhra Area Tenancy Act required a minimum **6-year** lease.

ndc8414f5d03.s: After the Hyderabad Jagir Abolition Regulation, 1949, jagirs and Sarf-e-khas lands became:
ndc8414f5d03.x: Following the Hyderabad Jagir Abolition Regulation, 1949, jagirs and Sarf-e-khas lands became Diwani, or ryotwari, lands after Police Action.
ndc8414f5d03.tq: Match the abolition measure with the resulting land-tenure status.
xs: Jagirs and **Sarf-e-khas** lands became **Diwani (ryotwari)** — option **(4)**.
This followed the **Hyderabad Jagir Abolition Regulation, 1949**, after **Police Action**.
xa: Next came the **Hyderabad (Telangana Area) Tenancy Act, 1950**.
In Andhra, zamindari/inamdari went under the **Madras Estates** Act.

nbfdc619067a.s: Under the Hyderabad (Telangana Area) Tenancy Act, 1950, a protected tenant could become owner by paying 60% of the market price in:
nbfdc619067a.x: Ownership was on paying 60% of the market price in 20 instalments, not 10.
xa: Earlier: **Hyderabad Jagir Abolition Regulation, 1949**.
Andhra counterpart: **AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956**.

n3b5cdf2d08e.s: Under the AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956, the maximum rent fixed for wet land was:
n3b5cdf2d08e.x: The Act (on the Subba Rao Committee's advice) capped rent at 30% for wet land and 25% for dry land.
xa: Telangana counterpart: **Hyderabad (Telangana Area) Tenancy Act, 1950**.
National rent cap: **1/4 to 1/6** of produce.

n30839f09742.s: The AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973 came into force on:
n30839f09742.x: Introduced under CM P.V. Narasimha Rao and placed in the Ninth Schedule, the Act came into force on 1 January 1975.
xa: Unit: **family of 5**; standard ceiling **10-27 acres wet**, **35-54 acres dry**.
**Benami** transfers after **30 Jan 1970** banned.
AP proposes to decriminalise **two** offences under it (Feb **2026**).

n03356047aa2.s: Under the AP Assigned Lands (Prohibition of Transfers) Act, 1977, land assigned to landless poor:
o: Can be mortgaged only to private moneylenders
Can be freely sold after five years
n03356047aa2.x: The Act prohibits the sale or transfer of land assigned to landless poor persons.
n03356047aa2.tq: Apply the statutory prohibition to a proposed transfer of assigned land.
xs: Under the **AP Assigned Lands (Prohibition of Transfers) Act, 1977**, assigned land **cannot be sold or transferred** — option **(1)**.
It protects land given to the **landless poor**; the notes give no time after which sale becomes free.
xa: The **AP Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 1982** punishes grabbers of government and weaker-section lands.
**Assigned lands** were a focus of the **Koneru Ranga Rao Committee** (**2006**).

na5a52095473.s: The AP Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 1982 is intended to punish persons who grab:
o: Only forest land outside municipal limits
na5a52095473.x: The Act punishes grabbers of government lands and lands belonging to weaker sections.
na5a52095473.tq: Identify the protected categories covered by the special prohibition law.
xs: The **AP Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 1982** punishes grabbers of **government and weaker-section lands** — option **(2)**.
It is not limited to cooperatives, urban apartments or forest land.
xa: **1977**: AP Assigned Lands (Prohibition of Transfers) Act — assigned land cannot be sold.
**1973**: AP Ceiling Act (in force **1 January 1975**).

nc1b2f27411b.s: The principal purpose of Operation Barga was to record the names of:
nc1b2f27411b.x: Operation Barga recorded the names of sharecroppers, known as bargadars, and thereby strengthened their rights.
nc1b2f27411b.tq: Use the programme’s distinctive administrative action to identify it.
xs: **Operation Barga** recorded names of **sharecroppers (bargadars)** — option **(1)** (APPSC **2019** key).
Recording gave them **heritable rights** and a **75%** share of produce.
xa: **West Bengal**, **Left Front**; launched **1978**.
⚠ Bargadar share **75%** vs tenancy rent cap **1/4 to 1/6**.

nd17890a3416.s: Acharya Vinoba Bhave began the Bhoodan movement in 1951 at:
nd17890a3416.x: Bhoodan began at Pochampally on 18 April 1951 amid the Telangana armed struggle; it later led to Gramdan.
xa: ⚠ Rent cap under tenancy reform = **1/4 to 1/6** of produce; Bhoodan appeal = **1/6th**.
**Operation Barga** (West Bengal, **1978**): recorded **bargadars**, giving a **75%** share of produce.
**Kumarappa Committee (1949)** recommended **cooperative farming**.

n2b057f01bc5.s: The National Council for Land Reforms was constituted in 2008 under the chairmanship of the:
n2b057f01bc5.x: The National Council for Land Reforms was constituted in 2008 under the Prime Minister.
n2b057f01bc5.tq: Identify the authority heading the national institutional mechanism.
xs: The **National Council for Land Reforms** (**2008**) is headed by the **Prime Minister** — option **(3)**.
Not the President, Agriculture Minister or Chief Justice.
xa: Its committee: **"State Agrarian Relations and Unfinished Task in Land Reforms"**.
⚠ AP's **Land Committee** (**2006**) was headed by **Koneru Ranga Rao**.
**NITI Aayog** prepared the **Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016**.

n2b3e6fc291c.s: The standard ceiling limits under the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973 were generally stated as:
n2b3e6fc291c.x: The standard ceiling range was 10–27 acres for wet land and 35–54 acres for dry land; some references cite 30–54 acres for dry land.
n2b3e6fc291c.tq: Read the land-class ranges in the correct order and avoid reversing wet and dry limits.
xs: Standard ceiling: **10-27 acres wet**, **35-54 acres dry** — option **(3)**.
Option (1) reverses wet and dry.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say **30-54** acres dry.
**1961** Act ceiling was **27-324** acres with an **individual** unit.
AP phase II: **20 lakh acres** surplus estimated, only **5 lakh acres** taken over.

n028568dfe1d.s: A Land Tribunal under the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973 was headed by the:
n028568dfe1d.x: The Land Tribunal was headed by the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO).
n028568dfe1d.tq: Identify the administrative authority associated with the statutory tribunal.
xs: The **Land Tribunal** was headed by the **RDO (Revenue Divisional Officer)** — option **(1)**.
It worked under the **AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act, 1973**.
xa: The Act also banned **benami** transfers after **30 Jan 1970**.
Exemptions: plantations, orchards, religious/charitable trusts, cooperatives, **Bhoodan** lands.
In force from **1 January 1975**.

nb1c21d1bae5.s: The Srikakulam Naxalite unrest and the 1966-69 droughts pushed which development in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The second phase of land reforms
nb1c21d1bae5.x: The Srikakulam unrest and the 1966-69 droughts pushed Phase II of land reforms in Andhra Pradesh.
xa: Phase II produced the **AP Ceiling Act, 1973** (family of 5; in force **1 January 1975**).
AP phase II: **20 lakh acres** surplus estimated, only **5 lakh acres** taken over.
National second round of ceiling laws came in the **early 1970s**.

n6435c9cfaf0.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of joint cooperative farming?
n6435c9cfaf0.x: Compulsory membership is not a feature of joint cooperative farming; participation is voluntary.
n6435c9cfaf0.tq: Find the compulsory element that contradicts the voluntary character of the institution.
xs: **Compulsory membership** is not a feature — option **(2)** (APPSC G2 **2017** key).
Real features: land pooled **voluntarily**, members **retain ownership**, management **elected by all members**.
xa: Produce shared per **land/labour contributed**.
Recommended by the **Kumarappa Committee (1949)**.

nfe46e1b1a43.s: ULPIN, also called Bhu-Aadhaar, is a:
o: 12-digit numeric ID based on the owner's Aadhaar number
14-digit alphanumeric ID generated from the geo-coordinates of a parcel's vertices
14-digit numeric ID based on the village survey number
16-digit alphanumeric ID issued for agricultural loans
nfe46e1b1a43.x: ULPIN (Unique Land Parcel Identification Number) is a 14-digit alphanumeric ID derived from the geo-coordinates of a parcel's vertices.
xa: Standards: **ECCMA + OGC**.
Rollout: **29 States/UTs**, **36.67 crore** parcels (**2025-26**).
⚠ **ULPIN** = parcel ID; **NGDRS** = registration software; **N-LRSI** = NCAER index.

n8891abbd20b.s: The NCAER Land Records and Services Index (N-LRSI) evaluates States primarily on:
o: Digitisation and quality of land records
n8891abbd20b.x: NCAER’s Land Records and Services Index grades States on the digitisation and quality of their land records.
n8891abbd20b.tq: Match the index with the specific dimensions it measures, not with broader economic indicators.
xs: **N-LRSI** (NCAER) grades States on **digitisation and quality of land records** — option **(4)**.
It is a land-records index, not a measure of farm output, population or investment.
xa: DoLR's own grading: **168 districts** in **16 States** got **"Bhoomi Samman" Platinum**.
RoR digitised **99.8%**; cadastral maps **97.24%**.

n92cb436ca19.s: Clear land titles are economically significant mainly because they:
o: abolish the need for land registration
turn land into collateral and help reduce litigation
guarantee that no land dispute ever arises
n92cb436ca19.x: Clear titles let land be used as collateral and can reduce litigation; they do not abolish registration or end every dispute.
xa: ~**80%** of AP public petitions are land disputes (**7 Feb 2026**).
Conclusive titling aims: fewer disputes, **easier credit**, **lower transaction costs**.

n6b5e45a232b.s: Under the National Digital Land Initiative (Land Stack), every land parcel is assigned a:
n6b5e45a232b.x: Land Stack is a cloud-based GIS framework that assigns a Bhu-Aadhaar to every parcel.
xa: Announced Jun **2026**.
DILRMP **Phase 3 (2026-31)**: GIS-based Land Stack for rural, semi-urban and urban parcels.
Bhu-Aadhaar = **ULPIN**, a **14-digit alphanumeric** ID.

n72aa1b1da4d.s: Under the conclusive system of land titling:
o: Title may be challenged through earlier deeds
The State guarantees the title once issued
n72aa1b1da4d.x: In the conclusive system the State guarantees title; in the presumptive system registration only records a transaction and title can be challenged.
xa: Presumptive keeps registration, survey and revenue records **separately**; conclusive has a **single authoritative title register**.
India's present system is **presumptive**.

n97bf6513d87.s: The National Land Records Modernisation Programme (NLRMP), launched in 2008, was formed by merging which two earlier schemes?
o: Computerisation of Land Records (CLR) and Strengthening of Revenue Administration and Updating of Land Records (SRA&ULR)
National Generic Document Registration System and ULPIN
n97bf6513d87.x: NLRMP (2008) merged CLR and SRA&ULR. SVAMITVA (2020) and NAKSHA are later schemes; NGDRS and ULPIN are DILRMP tools; Bhoomi (Karnataka) and Bhu Bharathi (AP) are State projects.
xs: **NLRMP (2008)** merged **CLR** (Computerisation of Land Records) and **SRA&ULR** — option **(1)** (UPPSC **2016** key).
**SVAMITVA** (**2020**) and **NAKSHA** are later schemes; **NGDRS** and **ULPIN** are DILRMP tools.
**Bhoomi** (Karnataka) and **Bhu Bharathi** (AP) are State projects.
xa: NLRMP was revamped as **DILRMP**, Central Sector from **1 April 2016**.
Tenure extended **2021-22 to 2025-26**.

n2ee4611747f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP)?
o: It has been a Central Sector Scheme with 100% central funding since 1 April 2016
It continues to be a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with cost-sharing by States
Digitisation of cadastral maps is one of its components
n2ee4611747f.x: DILRMP was centrally sponsored only before 2016; since 1 April 2016 it is a Central Sector Scheme.
xa: UPSC **2024** key: 100% central funding + cadastral map digitisation both correct.
Cadastral maps **97.24%** digitised.

n7b3da2ee45d.s: Andhra Pradesh's land resurvey under Jagananna Saswatha Bhu Hakku and Bhu Raksha commenced in:
n7b3da2ee45d.x: The resurvey began in December 2020, using drones, CORS and GIS, and covers 6,901 villages and 81 lakh parcels.
xa: **86,000** boundary disputes resolved; cost ~**₹6,000 crore**.
Centre gave a **₹400 crore** incentive (Jan **2026**).

n4744ab507f6.s: The tenure of DILRMP was extended up to which period, along with which two new components?
o: 2025-26; consent-based Aadhaar seeding of land records and computerisation of revenue courts
n4744ab507f6.x: The programme was extended from 2021-22 to 2025-26. Consent-based Aadhaar seeding of land records and computerisation of revenue courts were added as new components.
n4744ab507f6.tq: Pair the extension period with the two newly added components.
xs: **DILRMP** was extended **2021-22 to 2025-26**, adding **consent-based Aadhaar seeding** of land records and **computerisation of revenue courts** — option **(1)**.
**ULPIN** is a Phase 2 (**2016-26**) tool; **2026-31** is Phase 3 (**Land Stack**), not the extension.
xa: DILRMP is a **Central Sector Scheme** with **100% central funding** from **1 April 2016**.
A **gender column** in the Record of Rights is mandatory.
Predecessor: **NLRMP (2008)**.

n77ef11e7504.s: Under DILRMP, about what share of Records of Rights have been digitised?
n77ef11e7504.x: RoR digitisation is 99.8%; cadastral maps are 97.24% digitised and 95.73% of SROs computerised.
xa: ULPIN: **36.67 crore** parcels.
NAKSHA: **150+ cities**, **₹194 crore**.

o: Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas
Systematic Valuation and Mapping of Inhabited Technology Villages and Areas
Survey of Village Assets and Mapping through Integrated Technology in Village Areas
State Verification and Mapping of Titles in Village Agricultural Areas
nf55bdc279b8.x: SVAMITVA expands to Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas.
nf55bdc279b8.tq: Test the exact expansion of the acronym, where similar words are the main distractors.
xs: **SVAMITVA** = **Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas** — option **(1)**.
⚠ The word is **"Improvised"** Technology, and it covers **village (abadi)** areas, not agricultural land.
xa: Launched **24 April 2020** (National Panchayati Raj Day).
**Ministry of Panchayati Raj**; **Central Sector**.
Output: **Property Cards** (Record of Rights) with **DigiLocker** access.

n01d841c872e.s: SVAMITVA was launched on which occasion and date?
n01d841c872e.x: SVAMITVA was launched on 24 April 2020, the occasion of National Panchayati Raj Day. Its pilot was conducted in 2020 and it was taken nationwide in 2021.
n01d841c872e.tq: Combine the launch occasion with the exact date and distinguish it from the later nationwide rollout.
xs: SVAMITVA was launched on **24 April 2020**, **National Panchayati Raj Day** — option **(1)**.
Pilot in **2020**, nationwide in **2021**.
xa: Implementing agency **Survey of India**; technology **NICSI**.
Covers rural **inhabited (abadi)** areas only.
Pilot States included **Andhra Pradesh**.

n152b9e6bdd4.s: Which organisation is the implementing agency for SVAMITVA and which organisation provides its technology support?
o: NCAER and Department of Land Resources, respectively
Department of Land Resources and State Election Commissions, respectively
Survey of India and NICSI, respectively
NICSI and Survey of India, respectively
n152b9e6bdd4.x: The Survey of India is the implementing agency for SVAMITVA, while NICSI provides technology support.
n152b9e6bdd4.tq: Discriminate between the implementing agency and the technology-support agency.
xs: **Survey of India** implements SVAMITVA; **NICSI** provides technology — option **(3)**.
Option (4) reverses the two roles.
xa: Geo-referencing uses **CORS**; **State governments** prepare and distribute the cards.
Ministry: **Panchayati Raj** (not Mines).

n16b71df5d90.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about SVAMITVA?
o: Its Property Cards can be accessed through DigiLocker
Its Property Cards function as Records of Rights
Agricultural land is covered under its property-card survey
n16b71df5d90.x: SVAMITVA covers rural abadi areas, not agricultural land.
xa: **2.76 crore+** property cards (earlier **2.42 crore**, May **2025**).
⚠ SVAMITVA = **Panchayati Raj**, abadi only.

nb32d20bec0e.s: SVAMITVA scheme is implemented under which Ministry, and of what type of scheme is it?
o: Ministry of Mines; Centrally Sponsored Scheme
Ministry of Panchayati Raj; Central Sector Scheme
Ministry of Rural Development; Centrally Sponsored Scheme
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; Central Sector Scheme
nb32d20bec0e.x: SVAMITVA belongs to the Ministry of Panchayati Raj and is a Central Sector scheme. The Ministry of Mines is a common trap; Rural Development handles DILRMP's Department of Land Resources, and Agriculture has no role in it.
nb32d20bec0e.tq: SVAMITVA = Panchayati Raj (not Mines), Central Sector.
xs: SVAMITVA is under the **Ministry of Panchayati Raj**, a **Central Sector** scheme — option **(2)**.
⚠ **Ministry of Mines** is the common trap.
xa: Launched on **National Panchayati Raj Day** (**24 April 2020**).
Target **6.62 lakh villages**; cost **₹566.23 crore**.

n855013bc2a0.x: The target is 6.62 lakh villages at Rs 566.23 crore; over 2.76 crore property cards have been prepared.
xa: Earlier count **2.42 crore** (May **2025**).
Drone survey: **3.28 lakh villages** vs ~**3.44 lakh** notified.

n06a9c013d36.s: Adoption of the NITI Aayog Model Conclusive Land Titling Act, 2020 by States is:
o: A matter of each State's choice
Compulsory for States receiving DILRMP funds
n06a9c013d36.x: It is a model framework; adoption is left to the States. It aims to reduce disputes, ease credit and lower transaction costs.

n96b3a39ea10.tq: Connect legislative competence with the subject classification.
xs: Agriculture market is a **State subject**, so APMC Acts are **enacted by States** — **State List**, option **(3)**.
⚠ The **2020 farm laws** used Concurrent List **Entry 33**, though agriculture is **State List Entry 14**.
xa: AP's law is the **AP (Agricultural Produce and Livestock) Markets Act, 1966**.
The farm laws were **repealed in November 2021**, leaving reform to States.
The **Model APMC Act, 2003** and **Model APLM Act, 2017** are models for States to adopt.

n81891092e61.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature ensured by regulated agricultural markets?
o: Compulsory sale exclusively to unlicensed buyers
n81891092e61.x: Regulated markets provide open auctions, standard weights, recorded prices and licensed buyers; they do not require sale to unlicensed buyers.
n81891092e61.tq: Find the option that reverses the licensing principle of a regulated market.
xs: **Compulsory sale exclusively to unlicensed buyers** is not a feature — option **(1)** — regulated markets use **licensed buyers**.
Their features are **open auction**, **standard weights**, **recorded price** and **licensed buyers**.
xa: About **2,477** primary regulated markets + **4,843** sub-market yards.
Swaminathan's **National Commission on Farmers** suggested a regulated market within about **5 km** of farmers.
⚠ Problem side: **cartels of licensed traders** and **too few mandis**.

nc2169dd549d.s: The proposal known as “One Nation, One Regulator” in agricultural quality certification primarily seeks to address which issue?
o: Replacement of all State mandis by private markets
Transfer of procurement from FCI to SFAC
Ending dual certification under BIS and AGMARK
nc2169dd549d.x: The proposal seeks to end the dual certification arrangement involving BIS and AGMARK through a single regulatory framework.
nc2169dd549d.tq: Identify the policy problem addressed by the reform proposal.
xs: **"One Nation, One Regulator"** seeks to **end dual certification** under **BIS and AGMARK** — option **(4)**.
It is a quality-certification debate; it does not touch mandis, grading laboratories or FCI procurement.
xa: AGMARK is certified by the **DMI**, Ministry of Agriculture.
AGMARK law: **Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937**.
⚠ e-NAM's motto is **"One Nation, One Market"** — do not confuse.

n87419bc39cc.s: AGMARK, the quality certification mark for agricultural produce, is issued under which Act?
o: Agricultural Produce (Development and Warehousing) Corporations Act, 1956
n87419bc39cc.x: AGMARK is issued under the Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937. 'Grading and Marketing' is a common misprint used as a trap. The BIS Act governs BIS certification, and the 1956 Act set up the CWC.
xs: AGMARK is issued under the **Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937** — option **(2)**.
⚠ "Grading and **Marketing**" (option 1) is a misprint trap.
The **1956** Act set up the **CWC** (now under the **Warehousing Corporations Act 1962**).
xa: Certifying body: **DMI**, not the FCI.
**Central Agmark Laboratory**: **Nagpur**.
Dual certification (**BIS + AGMARK**) is the target of "One Nation, One Regulator" proposals.

n36cb14770a9.s: The Central Agmark Laboratory and the Central Quality Control Laboratory for agricultural produce are located at:
n36cb14770a9.x: Both the Central Agmark Laboratory (APPSC 2018 key) and the Central Quality Control Laboratory (APPSC 2025 key) are at Nagpur. New Delhi, Faridabad and Hyderabad are distractors.
xs: Both the **Central Agmark Laboratory** (APPSC **2018** key) and the **Central Quality Control Laboratory** (APPSC **2025** key) are at **Nagpur** — option **(3)**.
**State grading laboratories** grade produce for packers under Agmark.
xa: AGMARK is certified by the **DMI**, Ministry of Agriculture.
AGMARK Act: **Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937**.

ndba4b6c5b81.s: Which of the following is NOT a reform required from States for participation in e-NAM?
o: A single licence valid across the State
Regulating all agricultural prices through the State Government
A single-point levy of market fee
ndba4b6c5b81.x: The required reforms include a single State-wide licence, single-point market-fee levy and electronic trading. State-wide administrative price regulation is not the specified reform.
ndba4b6c5b81.tq: Find the option that substitutes price regulation for the actual market reform.
xs: **Regulating all agricultural prices** is not a required reform — option **(2)**; it was the distractor in APPSC **2016**.
States must **allow e-trading/e-auction**, give a **single licence** valid across the State and a **single-point levy** of market fee.
xa: ⚠ The APPSC **2016** answer was **allow electronic trading**.
The **Model APLM Act, 2017** proposed the same: **unified licence**, **single-point fee**, **e-trading**.
e-NAM grant: up to **₹75 lakh per mandi**.

n8c0402e88b7.s: Which one of the following was a feature of the Model APMC Act, 2003?
o: Whole State treated as one market area
Livestock and services brought within contract farming regulation
Contract farming kept outside the APMC framework
n8c0402e88b7.x: The Model APMC Act, 2003 permitted direct sale of agricultural produce to contract-farming sponsors. The other features are associated with the 2017 or 2018 model acts.
n8c0402e88b7.tq: Identify the feature belonging to the correct model act rather than a neighbouring reform.
xs: The **Model APMC Act, 2003** allowed **direct sale to contract sponsors** — option **(4)**.
**Whole State as one market area** is from the **Model APLM Act, 2017**.
Contract farming **outside APMC** and coverage of **livestock and services** are from the **2018** Model Contract Farming Act.
xa: The 2003 Act also gave **private markets**, **special markets for perishables**, **farmer-consumer markets** and **common registration of intermediaries**.
⚠ **2003** = Model APMC; **2017** = Model APLM; **2018** = Model Contract Farming.

o: keeping contract farming outside the APMC purview
treating the entire State as one market area
transfer of land title to the contract sponsor
nccf1e5808c0.x: The Model APLM Act, 2017 proposed treating the whole State as one market area; keeping contract farming outside APMC belongs to the 2018 Contract Farming Act.
xa: 2017 Act also: **warehouses as market yards**, **single-point (capped) market fee**, **unified licence**, **e-trading**, livestock included.
⚠ **2003** = Model APMC; **2017** = Model APLM; **2018** = Model Contract Farming.

ne9a8db7f3c2.s: Under the Model Contract Farming Act, 2018, the sponsor must purchase:
o: Only a part of the pre-agreed quantity
At least half of the pre-agreed quantity
Only produce that meets export grades
ne9a8db7f3c2.x: The sponsor must buy the entire pre-agreed quantity and gets no right in the farmer's land.
xa: The farmer is treated as the **weaker party**; the Act covers **livestock and services**.
**FPOs** may contract for farmers; produce is **insurable**.
Registration: **RARC**; disputes via **CFFGs** at the lowest level.

n18f41f3e670.s: The Model Contract Farming Act, 2018 treats which party as the weaker party?
n18f41f3e670.x: The model Act recognises the farmer as the weaker party and keeps contract farming outside the APMC Act.
xa: Sponsor must buy the **entire pre-agreed quantity**.
**No permanent structure** on the farmer's land.
Online registration by the **Registering and Agreement Recording Committee (RARC)**.

n6a2c050f355.s: Under the Model Contract Farming Act, 2018, online registration of agreements is done by the:
n6a2c050f355.x: Registration is by the RARC; CFFGs work at village/panchayat level.
xa: Sponsor must buy the **entire pre-agreed quantity**; gets **no title** to land.
Farmer is the **weaker party**; livestock and services covered.
AP has **district-level monitoring committees (D-MC)** in **13** districts — for FPOs, not contract registration.

n12cc8ef366f.s: Under the Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce Act, 2020, trade in a 'trade area' outside APMC yards was:
o: Subject to the State market fee
n12cc8ef366f.x: Trade-area transactions were outside APMC yards and free of State market fee; the Act did not mention MSP.
xa: ⚠ Concurrent **Entry 33** used; agriculture = State **Entry 14**.
The laws were **repealed in November 2021**.
Regulated APMC markets charge a **1%** market fee.

na220fefd785.s: The 2020 farm laws were repealed in:
na220fefd785.x: The laws were repealed in November 2021; the AP Markets Act, 1966 remains the operative framework.
xa: Criticism: **APMC monopoly vs farmer choice** — the **2020** repeal left reform to States.
The three Acts dated from **Sept 2020**.
⚠ Concurrent **Entry 33** used; agriculture = State **Entry 14**.

nb34b60064b2.s: e-NAM was launched in which month and year?
nb34b60064b2.x: The National Agriculture Market, or e-NAM, was launched in April 2016.
nb34b60064b2.tq: Test the exact launch date using closely spaced year options.
xs: e-NAM was launched in **April 2016** — option **(2)**.
It completed **10 years** in **April 2026**.
xa: Lead implementing agency: **SFAC**.
Motto: **"One Nation, One Market"**.
Coverage: **1,656 mandis** across **23 states and 4 UTs** (Mar 2026).

n6870f787a38.s: Which of the following e-NAM modules enables the sale of produce stored in WDRA-regulated warehouses?
n6870f787a38.x: Warehouse trading with electronic negotiable warehouse receipts (e-NWRs) enables produce stored in WDRA warehouses to be sold through e-NAM.
n6870f787a38.tq: Match the module with its distinctive operational function.
xs: **Warehouse trading with e-NWRs** lets produce in **WDRA** warehouses be sold on e-NAM — option **(2)**.
An **e-NWR** is an electronic ownership certificate for goods in a **WDRA-accredited warehouse**, tradable on e-NAM.
xa: NWRs exist for **143 agricultural**, **24** horticultural and **9** non-agricultural commodities.
**CGS-NPF** guarantees pledge loans against e-NWRs.
WDRA was constituted on **26 October 2010**.

n981f00a271b.s: In 2024-25, how many mandis in Andhra Pradesh participated in inter-mandi trade on e-NAM?
n981f00a271b.x: Only 11 mandis participated in inter-mandi trade, and online payments were just ₹26.88 lakh.
xa: AP has **33** e-NAM markets.
AP SES 2025-26 value traded: **₹5,054.86 cr**.

nfcc15eff37d.s: The e-Choupal initiative is associated with which organisation?
nfcc15eff37d.x: e-Choupal consists of ITC’s Internet kiosks linking farmers with markets.
nfcc15eff37d.tq: Use the organisation–initiative association rather than the general purpose of rural marketing.
xs: **e-Choupal** is **ITC**'s internet kiosks linking farmers to markets (**2000**) — option **(1)**.
**NAFED** and **NCCF** are central nodal agencies under **PM-AASHA**, not e-Choupal.
xa: Contract farming pioneer: **Punjab** (**PepsiCo**, late **1980s**).
**Rythu Bazar**: **Andhra Pradesh**, **1999**.
Karnataka's reformed market model is often cited as a success.

nf680c50eff7.s: How many markets in Andhra Pradesh are integrated with e-NAM?
nf680c50eff7.x: AP has 33 e-NAM markets trading dry chillies, cotton, turmeric, groundnut and more.
xa: AP SES 2025-26: **9.88 lakh MT** worth **₹5,054.86 cr** traded.
Registered farmers / traders / commission agents: **183 / 104 / 25**.

n08416ee63d5.s: Rythu Bazars in Andhra Pradesh are run by:
o: An Estate Officer under the Revenue Department
n08416ee63d5.x: An Estate Officer under the Revenue Department runs Rythu Bazars, outside the Agricultural Market Committees.
xa: Rythu Bazar = **Andhra Pradesh**, **1999**.
AMCs collect a **1%** market fee in regulated markets.
District supervision of the APMC system is by the **DATMO**.

n48df8afca4f.s: AGMARK certification is administered by which organisation?
n48df8afca4f.x: AGMARK certification is administered by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection (DMI) under the Ministry of Agriculture.
n48df8afca4f.tq: Identify the authority responsible for issuing the certification.
xs: AGMARK is certified by the **Directorate of Marketing and Inspection (DMI)**, Ministry of Agriculture — option **(2)**.
It is **not the FCI** (UPPSC **2023**); **BIS** is the other certifier in the dual-certification debate; **SFAC** leads e-NAM.
xa: AGMARK is issued under the **Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937**.
**Central Agmark Laboratory**: **Nagpur** (APPSC **2018** key).
**"One Nation, One Regulator"** proposals seek to end dual certification (**BIS + AGMARK**).

n3aaa3206d20.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the scheme for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 FPOs?
o: It was launched in 2020 with an outlay of ₹6,865 crore
Management support of ₹18 lakh per FPO is spread over three years
Handholding through CBBOs is given to each FPO for three years
n3aaa3206d20.x: Handholding through CBBOs lasts five years; it is the ₹18 lakh management support that is spread over three years.
xa: Implementing agencies: **SFAC, NABARD, NCDC, NAFED**.
Equity grant up to **₹2,000 per farmer member** (max **₹15 lakh** per FPO); credit guarantee up to **₹2 crore**.
**15%** of FPOs to be in Aspirational Districts.

n8c2e6881b82.s: Which implementing agency of the 10,000 FPO scheme also promotes cooperative-sector FPOs through the PACS route?
n8c2e6881b82.x: NCDC, one of the implementing agencies with SFAC, NABARD and NAFED, promotes cooperative FPOs through PACS.
xa: **NCDC** promotes cooperative-sector FPOs (target **1,100** via PACS).
**SFAC** is also the lead agency of **e-NAM**.
**NAFED** (set up **1958**) is the apex agricultural cooperative marketing body.

ned0c125ee56.s: The 10,000 FPO scheme envisages one FPO per:
ned0c125ee56.x: The norm is one FPO per block, not per district; 15% of FPOs are to be in Aspirational Districts.
xa: **6,070 FPOs** are on ONDC nationally; AP has **207**.
**5,048 FPOs** are on e-NAM.
AP has district-level monitoring committees (**D-MC**) in **13** districts.

n1fb4ad2f0e0.s: Under the 10,000 FPO scheme, the equity grant is up to how much per farmer member?
n1fb4ad2f0e0.x: The equity grant is Rs 2,000 per member, capped at Rs 15 lakh per FPO; credit guarantee is up to Rs 2 crore.
xa: ⚠ **5 years** is the handholding period via **Cluster-Based Business Organisations**.
Outlay **₹6,865 crore**; support till **2027-28**.
AP FPOs (2024-25): **99** seed, **97** fertiliser, **98** pesticide licences.

n2feb0398b78.s: Which of the following is NOT a rationale of the 10,000 FPO scheme?
n2feb0398b78.x: The scheme aims at bargaining power, scale economies and lower costs; it does not transfer land to FPOs.
xa: The **"Small Farmer Large Field"** idea also seeks **scale in inputs and marketing**.
**FPOs** may contract on behalf of farmers under the **2018** Model Contract Farming Act.
NAF (Walmart Foundation grant) works with **10 FPOs** to reach **12,500 farmers** in AP.

n2ad07a9b7d0.s: NAFED is best described as the:
o: Central agency for food-grain storage alone
n2ad07a9b7d0.x: NAFED is the apex agricultural cooperative marketing body and was set up in 1958.
n2ad07a9b7d0.tq: Test the exact institutional role rather than a related marketing function.
xs: **NAFED** is the **apex agricultural cooperative marketing body**, set up in **1958** — option **(2)**.
**TRIFED** handles **tribal produce**; **WDRA** regulates warehouse receipts.
xa: NAFED now works under the **Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act**.
Under **PM-AASHA** (Sept **2018**), **NAFED + NCCF** are the central nodal agencies.
NAFED/NCCF ran **discounted onion sales** during the **28 Aug 2026** price spike.

n5f1e801f404.s: Under the Price Support Scheme of PM-AASHA, procurement at MSP covers:
n5f1e801f404.x: The Price Support Scheme procures pulses, oilseeds and copra at MSP.
n5f1e801f404.tq: Discriminate between the commodity basket of PM-AASHA and that of Operation Greens.
xs: The **Price Support Scheme** buys **pulses, oilseeds, copra** at MSP — option **(3)**.
**Tomato, onion, potato** belong to **Operation Greens**; **all fruits and vegetables** to its **2020** extension.
xa: **PM-AASHA** (Sept **2018**): **NAFED + NCCF** are central nodal agencies.
From **2024-25**, procurement up to **25%** of production.
AP **DCMS** also procure at MSP.

o: Price support for oilseeds and copra
nd6ddd3464fb.x: TRIFED is concerned with marketing tribal produce. It was established in 1987 under the framework associated with the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 1984.
nd6ddd3464fb.tq: Apply the body-function test to distinguish TRIFED from agricultural marketing agencies.
xs: **TRIFED** is for **tribal produce marketing** — option **(4)**.
It was set up in **1987** under the **MSCS Act 1984**.
xa: ⚠ **NAFED** (**1958**) = apex agricultural cooperative marketing body; TRIFED = tribal produce.
Price support for oilseeds and copra is the **PSS** under **PM-AASHA**.
PACS-level grain storage is the **Ministry of Cooperation** plan.

ncc5bd968eda.s: Price spread in agricultural marketing is calculated as:
ncc5bd968eda.x: Price spread is the consumer price minus the price received by the farmer; it indicates marketing margins and the share of intermediaries.
ncc5bd968eda.tq: Use the formula direction carefully to avoid reversing the two prices.
xs: **Price spread** = **consumer price minus farmer's price** — option **(2)**.
It measures **marketing margins** and the **middlemen's share**; option (1) reverses the subtraction.
xa: Middlemen and brokers **raise consumer prices** and add **red tape**.
Onion hit **Rs 62/kg** in Delhi; the Centre blamed **hoarding and middlemen**.
**Rythu Bazars** cut the spread by letting farmers sell **directly to consumers**.
