n4b536ec94b8.s: Under e-NAM, payment for produce is made directly to:
n4b536ec94b8.x: e-NAM enables direct payment to farmers' accounts, besides transparent price discovery and wider buyer access.
xa: Pan-India portal and nationwide market access (UPSC **2017**: both correct).
**Quality assaying** is another advantage.
⚠ AP weakness: online payments only **Rs 26.88 lakh** (2024-25).

n1ab4600f0d7.s: The Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) was set up on 2 March 1957 under the:
o: Agricultural Produce (Development and Warehousing) Corporations Act, 1956
n1ab4600f0d7.x: CWC was established on 2 March 1957 under the Agricultural Produce (Development and Warehousing) Corporations Act, 1956. It is now associated with the Warehousing Corporations Act, 1962.
n1ab4600f0d7.tq: Use the parent-Act trap by distinguishing the original legal basis from the later Act.
xs: The **CWC** was set up on **2 March 1957** under the **Agricultural Produce (Development and Warehousing) Corporations Act, 1956** — option **(3)**.
It now works under the **Warehousing Corporations Act 1962**; the **2007** Act regulates warehouse receipts.
xa: CWC joins **NCDC**, NABARD and FCI in the **cooperative grain storage plan**.
WDRA was constituted on **26 October 2010**.
AP AMC godowns: **1,052**, capacity **9.65 lakh MT**.

n72c14dabdf0.s: The 'World's Largest Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector', piloted in 2023, is under which Ministry, and at what level are its godowns built?
o: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution; FCI depot level
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; district level
Ministry of Food Processing Industries; mega food park level
n72c14dabdf0.x: The plan belongs to the Ministry of Cooperation (piloted 2023) and builds godowns and processing units at the PACS level, with NCDC implementing it alongside NABARD, CWC and FCI. The other ministries and levels are distractors.
n72c14dabdf0.tq: Grain storage plan = Ministry of Cooperation + PACS.
xs: The plan is under the **Ministry of Cooperation**, building godowns at the **PACS level** — option **(2)**.
It was piloted in **2023**; **NCDC** implements it with **NABARD, CWC, FCI**.
xa: It converges **8** schemes, including **AIF** and **AMI**.
Effective interest for PACS: **1%**.
By July **2026**, cooperative grain-storage godowns existed in **313 PACS**.

nd2b5fa92f8a.s: e-NAM, a Central Sector Scheme, has been funded through the:
nd2b5fa92f8a.x: e-NAM is funded via the Agri-Tech Infrastructure Fund and now falls under ISAM-eNAM.
xa: One-time grant up to **₹75 lakh per mandi**.
Lead agency: **SFAC**.
Launched **April 2016**.

n034547f56f5.s: Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs) were proposed in the Union Budget:
n034547f56f5.x: GrAMs were announced in Budget 2018-19, to be exempt from APMC regulation and linked to e-NAM.
xa: **22,000 rural haats** to be upgraded.
Funding: **₹2,000 crore Agri-Market Infrastructure Fund**.
e-NAM covers **1,656 mandis** (Mar 2026).

n1cfab927cad.s: Operation Greens is implemented by the Ministry of:
n1cfab927cad.x: Operation Greens, modelled on Operation Flood and begun with TOP crops, is run by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries.
xa: Announced in **Union Budget 2018-19** (APPSC 2018 key).
Extended to **22 perishable crops** in Budget 2021-22.
Short-term interventions get **50%** subsidy on transport and storage; FPOs get **70%** for value-chain projects.

n7d0b5a009a8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Operation Greens?
o: Its extension to 22 perishable crops was announced in the Union Budget 2018-19
The 2020 Atmanirbhar Bharat package extended it to all fruits and vegetables
The Union Budget 2021-22 extended it to 22 perishable crops
It was announced for TOP crops in the Union Budget 2018-19
n7d0b5a009a8.x: Budget 2018-19 announced Operation Greens for TOP; the 22-crop extension came in Budget 2021-22.
xa: Implementing ministry: **Food Processing Industries**.
Modelled on **Operation Flood**.
Long-term projects: **50%** grant; **70%** for FPOs.

nf070cd201c4.s: Under Operation Greens, long-term value-chain projects of FPOs get grant-in-aid of:
nf070cd201c4.x: FPOs get 70% grant-in-aid (50% for others); short-term interventions get 50% subsidy on transport and storage.
xa: Operation Greens covers **Tomato, Onion, Potato**.
Extended to **22 perishable crops** in Budget **2021-22**.
Ministry: **Food Processing Industries**.

n6ac22824894.s: Which of the following was announced in the Union Budget 2018-19 to address the price volatility of tomato, onion and potato?
n6ac22824894.x: Operation Greens was announced in the Union Budget 2018-19 for TOP crops (APPSC 2018 key). Operation Flood is the dairy programme it is modelled on, Mission Indradhanush is an immunisation mission, and SAMPADA is a food-processing scheme.
xs: **Operation Greens** was announced in **Union Budget 2018-19** for TOP crops (APPSC **2018** key) — option **(4)**.
⚠ **Operation Flood**, **Mission Indradhanush** and **SAMPADA** were the distractors; Operation Greens is modelled on Operation Flood.
xa: Budget **2018-19** also announced upgrading **22,000 rural haats** into **GrAMs**.
Aim: curb erratic prices via **FPOs**, **agri-logistics**, **processing**.
Extended to all fruits and vegetables in **2020**.

n545bb3daed2.s: The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), launched in 2020, provides a medium- and long-term debt-financing facility of what amount for post-harvest infrastructure and community farming assets?
n545bb3daed2.x: The AIF is a ₹1 lakh crore medium- and long-term debt-financing facility launched in 2020 for post-harvest infrastructure and community farming assets.
n545bb3daed2.tq: Use the exact scheme-size figure and distinguish it from nearby financing amounts.
xs: The **AIF** is a **₹1 lakh crore** medium- and long-term debt-financing facility — option **(1)**.
It funds **post-harvest infrastructure** and **community farming assets**; launched **2020**.
xa: **3%** interest subvention on loans up to **₹2 crore**; credit guarantee via **CGTMSE**.
Mar **2026**: **₹84,681 crore** sanctioned for **1,71,267 projects**, mobilising **₹1.34 lakh crore**.

necba32a7573.s: The ‘Small Farmer Large Field’ model is based on:
o: Dividing large farms into individual plots for subsistence cultivation
Leasing all farmland to a single corporate sponsor
Pooling neighbouring small farmers’ holdings for joint operation as one large field
Compulsory consolidation of all landholdings by the State
necba32a7573.x: Under this model, neighbouring small farmers pool their holdings and operate them as one large field to obtain scale in inputs and marketing.
necba32a7573.tq: Translate the model’s name into its operational arrangement.
xs: **"Small Farmer Large Field"** means **neighbouring small farmers** organise into groups and **operate as one large field** — option **(3)**.
They **synchronise and harmonise** operations to gain **scale in inputs and marketing** (UPSC **2023**).
xa: **FPOs** pursue the same aims: **bargaining power** and **economies of scale**.
**Contract farming** = selling to an agri-business firm at a **price, quantity and/or time fixed in advance**.
**Price spread** = consumer price minus farmer's price.

n40a99fe7728.s: Which State is identified as the pioneer of contract farming, associated with PepsiCo in the late 1980s?
n40a99fe7728.x: Punjab is identified as the pioneer of contract farming in this context, with PepsiCo in the late 1980s.
n40a99fe7728.tq: Combine the State, corporate participant and period to identify the pioneer.
xs: **Punjab** is the **contract farming pioneer**, with **PepsiCo** in the late **1980s** — option **(1)**.
**Andhra Pradesh** pioneered **Rythu Bazar** (**1999**); **Tamil Nadu** has **Uzhavar Sandhai**; **Maharashtra** has **Hadapsar Mandi**.
xa: The **Model Contract Farming Act, 2018** keeps contract farming **outside APMC**.
The **2020** Price Assurance Act also dealt with **contract farming** with sponsors.
⚠ **Apni Mandi** is also **Punjab**.

n3d28201df62.s: The 2020 farm laws were enacted by Parliament by invoking which constitutional legislative entry, although agriculture is primarily in the State List?
n3d28201df62.x: The laws were enacted by invoking Concurrent List Entry 33, while agriculture is associated with State List Entry 14.
n3d28201df62.tq: Separate the constitutional entries by both List and entry number.
xs: The farm laws used **Concurrent List Entry 33**, though agriculture is **State List Entry 14** — option **(2)**.
Options (1) and (4) mix up the entries; **Entry 14** is in the **State List**.
xa: Agriculture market is a **State subject**, so **APMC Acts** are State laws.
The laws were **repealed in November 2021**.
Criticism: **no legal MSP guarantee**.

nb639d749a04.s: Which organisation is the lead implementing agency for e-NAM?
o: Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority
National Agriculture Cooperative Marketing Federation of India
nb639d749a04.x: The Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC) is the lead implementing agency for e-NAM.
nb639d749a04.tq: Identify the implementing body rather than the funding source or regulator.
xs: The lead implementing agency for e-NAM is the **Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC)** — option **(3)**.
**WDRA** accredits warehouses and NWRs; **NAFED** is the apex cooperative marketing body.
xa: e-NAM is a **Central Sector Scheme** funded via the **Agri-Tech Infrastructure Fund (ATIF)**.
It now runs under **ISAM-eNAM**.
SFAC is also an implementing agency of the **10,000 FPO** scheme.

n2c663e2e398.s: Krishi UDAN Yojana primarily seeks to achieve which of the following?
o: Transport farm produce, particularly perishables, by air to improve farmers’ prices and incomes
Establish permanent wholesale mandis in every district
Replace agricultural markets with electronic warehouses
Provide free crop insurance to farmers in drought-prone areas
n2c663e2e398.x: Krishi UDAN facilitates air transport of agricultural produce, especially perishables, helping farmers obtain better prices and higher incomes.
n2c663e2e398.tq: Link the scheme’s transport instrument with its intended marketing outcome.
xs: **Krishi UDAN Yojana** moves farm produce, **especially perishables, by air** → **better prices and higher incomes** (APPSC **2021**) — option **(1)**.
It is a transport scheme, not about mandis, warehouses or insurance.
xa: **Operation Greens** also targets perishables (**TOP**) through agri-logistics.
**GrAMs** are linked to **e-NAM** and exempt from APMC regulation.
Budget **2021-22** extended Operation Greens to **22 perishable crops**.

n2e9bcf35221.s: The National Commission on Farmers suggested that a regulated market should be available within approximately what distance of farmers?
n2e9bcf35221.x: The National Commission on Farmers suggested a regulated market within about 5 km of farmers.
n2e9bcf35221.tq: Recall the recommended market-density distance as a direct quantitative fact.
xs: The **National Commission on Farmers (Swaminathan)** suggested a regulated market within about **5 km** of farmers — option **(2)**.
This addresses low **market density** — one of the listed APMC problems is **too few mandis**.
xa: India has about **2,477** primary regulated markets and **4,843** sub-market yards.
Budget **2018-19** planned **22,000 rural haats** as **GrAMs** to bring markets closer.
AP has **129 functional** Rythu Bazars (2025-26).

n4934283a1fe.s: If the market price of an MSP-covered crop falls below the announced MSP, which of the following normally occurs under the MSP mechanism?
o: The Reserve Bank of India purchases the stock through open-market operations
Government agencies purchase the stock offered by farmers
The MSP is automatically cancelled for that season
Farmers are prohibited from selling the crop in the market
n4934283a1fe.x: When the market price falls below MSP, government agencies procure the stock offered, providing a safeguard against distress sales.
n4934283a1fe.tq: Apply the policy mechanism to a price-fall situation.
xs: When market price falls below MSP, **government agencies purchase the stock** offered — option **(2)**.
This floor protects farmers from **distress sales** in bumper years.
xa: **FCI** + State agencies buy all **wheat and paddy** meeting specifications → effectively open-ended.
Pulses, oilseeds, copra: limited **PSS** procurement capped at **25%** of production.
**PDPS** pays the **MSP minus market price** gap in cash without buying.

n3b66f50ca1f.s: Coarse grains are procured for the Central Pool primarily by:
o: State agencies with prior approval of the Government of India
The Reserve Bank of India after approval of the CACP
Only the Cotton Corporation of India
District cooperative banks without central approval
n3b66f50ca1f.x: State agencies procure coarse grains for the Central Pool, but prior approval of the Government of India is required.
n3b66f50ca1f.tq: Ask which agency performs the function and which approval condition accompanies it.
xs: Coarse grains: **States procure with GoI's prior approval** for the **Central Pool** — option **(1)**.
The **CCI** procures **cotton**; RBI and cooperative banks play no procurement role.
xa: **Wheat and paddy**: FCI + State agencies, effectively open-ended.
**States decide** where purchase centres go.
**DCP (1997)**: States procure, store, distribute.

nindian-economy-6-1.s: What does Minimum Support Price (MSP) mean?
o: Minimum export price fixed by farmers
Government-announced minimum price for selected agricultural commodities
Market-determined maximum price for all agricultural commodities
nindian-economy-6-1.x: MSP is the minimum price the government announces for selected farm crops, at which it will buy if market prices fall below it.
n: MSP stands for Minimum Support Price. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 8-9]
MSP is a government-announced minimum price for selected agricultural commodities. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 8-9]
xs: **MSP** is a **government-announced minimum price for selected agricultural commodities** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is a floor price announced before each **Rabi/Kharif** sowing season — not set by farmers, not a maximum price, not for industrial products.
xa: If the market price falls below MSP, government agencies buy the stock offered.
**CACP recommends MSP**; **CCEA** approves it.
MSP is an **administrative decision, not a legal right**.

nindian-economy-6-4.s: The Minimum Support Price is finally fixed by:
nindian-economy-6-4.x: The CACP recommends MSP, and the Government of India fixes it.
n: MSP is a government-announced minimum price for selected agricultural commodities. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 8-9]
Food stocks support the Public Distribution System (PDS). [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 8-9]
The CACP recommends MSP. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 8-9]
The Government of India fixes MSP. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 8-9]
xa: CACP also recommends the **FRP** for **sugarcane**.
CACP composition: Chairman + Member Secretary + one official + two non-official members.
MSPs cover **22 mandated crops**.

nindian-economy-7-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Sugarcane is covered under the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP).
The CCEA approves the FRP for sugarcane.
The CACP approves the FRP for sugarcane.
nindian-economy-7-2.x: The CCEA, not the CACP, approves the FRP; the CACP only recommends prices.
n: MSP applies to MSP commodities. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 9-10]
FRP applies to sugarcane. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 9-10]
CACP recommends MSP. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 9-10]
CACP recommends FRP. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 9-10]
The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) recommends FRP for sugarcane. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 9-10]
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approves FRP. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 9-10]
xa: **FRP** = legally mandated minimum price **sugar mills** must pay; linked to **sugar recovery %**.
FRP replaced the **Statutory Minimum Price** from **2009-10**.
**State Advised Price** is set by some States, usually above FRP.

n5c456841f26.s: The Minimum Support Price in India is:
o: A statutory entitlement under an MSP law
An administrative decision not backed by a statute
n5c456841f26.x: MSP is an administrative decision announced before sowing; it is not backed by a statute.
xa: Farmer groups demand a **legal guarantee**; economists fear it could breach **WTO** norms.
**Supreme Court** issued notice on a plea for MSP ≥ weighted average cost of production (**14 Apr 2026**).
Market price < MSP → government agencies buy the stock offered.

nef8efbfba58.s: Market Intervention Scheme action may be triggered by a price fall of at least:
nef8efbfba58.x: MIS can be triggered by a price fall of 10% or more, or a production rise of 10% or more.
xa: MIS losses: **50:50** Centre-State; **75:25** for NE States.
MIS covers perishables not under MSP.
MIS is one of the **2026** PM-AASHA components with **PSS** and **PDPS**.

nindian-economy-6-6.s: The Agricultural Prices Commission was renamed the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) in:
nindian-economy-6-6.x: The APC was set up in 1965 and renamed CACP in 1985.
n: The CACP was established in January 1965. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 8-9]
The main objective of the CACP is to incentivise farmers. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 8-9]
xa: Factors considered: **cost of production**, **demand and supply**, **inter-crop price parity**, **minimum 50% margin** over cost.
**FCI** was also set up in **1965**.

na2de24fd291.s: The cost concept that includes paid-out costs and the imputed value of family labour, but excludes rent on owned land and interest on fixed capital, is
na2de24fd291.x: A2+FL consists of A2 paid-out costs plus the imputed value of family labour. Rent on owned land and interest on fixed capital are added only under C2.
na2de24fd291.tq: Separate the intermediate cost concept from the comprehensive cost concept.
xs: **A2+FL** = paid-out costs (**A2**) + imputed **family labour** — option **(3)**.
**C2** adds **rent on owned land** and **interest on fixed capital** — the comprehensive cost.
xa: **A2** = seeds, fertilisers, chemicals, hired labour, fuel, irrigation.
MSP = **1.5 × A2+FL**, not C2.
The **Swaminathan Commission** wanted **C2 + 50%**.

nc90e163b025.s: The present MSP formula fixes MSP at least at:
nc90e163b025.x: The current formula is 1.5 times A2+FL; C2 + 50% was the Swaminathan Commission's recommendation.
xa: SKM: paddy at C2+50% should be **₹3,243/q** for 2026-27 vs **₹2,441** fixed.
**C2** = A2+FL + rent on owned land + interest on fixed capital.
Debate: **A2+FL vs C2** as cost base.

nindian-economy-7-13.s: Which of the following correctly represents C2 in the agricultural cost concept?
o: A2 + FL + land rent + fixed capital costs and other costs
nindian-economy-7-13.x: C2 is the fullest cost: A2 + FL plus rent on land and interest on fixed capital and other costs. A2 + FL leaves out land and capital.
nindian-economy-7-13.tq: Build up from A2 to C2.
n: C2 means A2 + FL + land rent + fixed capital costs and other costs. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 9-10]
xs: **C2** = **A2 + FL + land rent + fixed capital costs and other costs** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**A2** = actual **paid-out costs**; **A2 + FL** = paid-out cost plus **family labour** — both leave out land and capital.
**FL + land rent** omits paid-out costs, so it is not C2.
xa: Current MSP policy = **1.5 times A2+FL**, not C2.
SKM: paddy at C2+50% should be **₹3,243/quintal** for 2026-27 vs **₹2,441** fixed.
⚠ "**MSP = 1.5 × C2**" is the trap.

n9579c6d4a44.s: Bt cotton was approved for commercial cultivation in India in:
n9579c6d4a44.x: Bt cotton was approved in 2002, long after the 1950-65 phase of land reforms, community development and irrigation expansion.
xa: **Green Revolution** (mid-1960s): **HYV wheat and rice**; **APC and FCI** set up in **1965**.
"**Wheat Revolution**" stamp released in **July 1968**.
**Post-1991**: liberalisation, **WTO membership 1995**, e-NAM, FPOs, **PM-KISAN**.

n062378a537e.s: Which of the following is a cash crop?
n062378a537e.x: Tobacco, like cotton, sugarcane and oilseeds, is a cash crop grown mainly for sale; rice, millets and pulses are subsistence crops.
xa: Of the cash crops, **cotton** and **sugarcane** (FRP) are among the **commercial** MSP crops.
Oilseeds get MSP: **7** oilseeds, including **nigerseed**.
Phases: Pre-Green Revolution (**1950-65**), Green Revolution (mid-1960s), price-support, post-1991.

n847b78b3040.s: The CACP classification of the 22 mandated MSP crops comprises:
n847b78b3040.x: The stated split is 14 kharif crops, 6 rabi crops and 2 commercial crops, totalling 22 mandated crops.
n847b78b3040.tq: Check whether the category counts add up to the mandated total.
xs: The CACP split is **14 kharif, 6 rabi and 2 commercial** (jute, copra) — option **(1)**.
xa: Groups: **cereals (7)**, **pulses (5)**, **oilseeds (7)**, **commercial (4)** incl. sugarcane FRP.
CCEA approved MSP for **14 kharif crops** for 2026-27 on **13 May 2026**.
Toria and de-husked coconut MSPs are derived from rapeseed-mustard and copra.

nc848020c3b2.s: Which of the following crops is procured at MSP on an effectively open-ended basis?
nc848020c3b2.x: FCI and State agencies buy all wheat and paddy meeting specifications; pulses and oilseeds get limited PSS procurement.
xa: Procurement is concentrated in **Punjab, Haryana, Telangana, AP, Chhattisgarh**.
**Shanta Kumar HLC (2015)**: only about **6% of farmers** sell at MSP.
Wheat RMS **2026-27**: **>35 MT** procured.

nb375662d711.s: Under the pulses mission associated with PM-AASHA, 100% procurement at MSP for four years is promised for:
nb375662d711.x: The pulses mission promises 100% procurement at MSP for four years for tur, urad and masoor through NAFED and NCCF under PSS.
nb375662d711.tq: Use the exact three-pulse combination to avoid substituting other MSP crops.
xs: The pulses mission promises **100% procurement of tur, urad and masoor** at MSP for **4 years** — option **(4)**.
It runs through **NAFED/NCCF** under the **PSS** of **PM-AASHA**.
xa: Normally PSS procurement is capped at **25%** of production (from **2024-25**).
**5** MSP pulses: gram, tur/arhar, moong, urad, masur.
The **Price Stabilisation Fund** holds **pulses** buffers along with onion and potato.

nindian-economy-7-4.s: How many crops are covered under MSP in all?
nindian-economy-7-4.x: MSP covers 22 crops: 7 cereals, 5 pulses, 7 oilseeds and 3 commercial crops.
n: Cereals comprise 7 MSP crops. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 9-10]
Pulses comprise 5 MSP crops. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 9-10]
Oilseeds comprise 7 MSP crops. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 9-10]
Commercial crops comprise 3 MSP crops. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 9-10]
xa: **Oilseeds** = **7** crops incl. **nigerseed** and **safflower**.
CACP split: **14 kharif + 6 rabi + 2 commercial**.
⚠ Plus **sugarcane FRP** = **23** in all.

nindian-economy-7-10.s: Which of the following commercial crops is covered under MSP?
nindian-economy-7-10.x: Raw jute, along with cotton and copra, is a commercial crop under MSP.
n: Cotton is a commercial crop covered under MSP. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 9-10]
Raw Jute is a commercial crop covered under MSP. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 9-10]
xa: Cotton MSP nodal agency = **Cotton Corporation of India** (Ministry of Textiles).
Kharif 2026-27 cotton MSP: **8,267** (medium) / **8,667** (long staple).
**Niger** gets MSP, is a **kharif** crop and is used by some tribal people (UPSC 2023).

n31c706892f6.s: Which agency is the nodal agency for MSP operations relating to cotton?
o: Food Corporation of India under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs
National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation under the Ministry of Finance
Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices under the Ministry of Commerce
Cotton Corporation of India under the Ministry of Textiles
n31c706892f6.x: The Cotton Corporation of India, under the Ministry of Textiles, is the nodal agency for cotton MSP operations.
n31c706892f6.tq: Use the agency-ministry pairing and reject the neighbouring procurement bodies.
xs: Cotton MSP's nodal agency is the **Cotton Corporation of India** under the **Ministry of Textiles** — option **(4)**.
MSP is announced for **medium and long staple** cotton.
xa: Cotton is one of **4** commercial crops: copra, cotton, raw jute, sugarcane (FRP).
**FCI** handles **wheat and paddy**; **NAFED** and NCCF handle **PSS**.

nf1474055396.s: Among the following Kharif 2026-27 MSP increases, the largest hike was recorded for:
nf1474055396.x: Sunflower recorded the largest hike, increasing by ₹622 per quintal. The increases for cotton, niger seed and common paddy were ₹557, ₹515 and ₹72 respectively.
nf1474055396.tq: Compare the increments rather than the absolute MSP values.
xs: **Sunflower** got the biggest hike: **+622** — option **(1)**.
Others: **cotton +557**, **niger seed +515**, **common paddy +72**.
xa: Sunflower seed **2026-27** MSP: **8,343**.
⚠ Highest MSP = **sesamum (10,346)**.
Soyabean **+380**; groundnut **+254**.

n9758db0c9c5.s: The Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) for sugarcane is notified under which legal framework?
o: Sugarcane Regulation Act, 1955 under the Agricultural Produce Markets Act
Essential Commodities (Sugarcane Pricing) Rules, 1966 under the Food Corporation of India Act
Sugarcane Development Act, 2009 under the National Food Security Act
Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966 under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955
n9758db0c9c5.x: FRP is fixed under the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966, issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.
n9758db0c9c5.tq: Identify the exact parent law and subordinate order rather than a nearby agricultural statute.
xs: FRP's legal basis is the **Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966** under the **Essential Commodities Act, 1955** — option **(4)**.
The other options name Acts not cited in the notes.
xa: FRP: legally mandated minimum that **sugar mills** must pay, linked to **sugar recovery %**.
Fixed by **CCEA** on **CACP** recommendation.
PYQ (CGPSC **2021**): FRP relates to **sugarcane**.

n9fd2844af2b.s: The Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of sugarcane is fixed by:
o: The CCEA on the CACP's recommendation
n9fd2844af2b.x: FRP is fixed by the CCEA on CACP's recommendation and linked to the mill's recovery rate; the State-announced price is SAP.
xa: FRP basis: **Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966**.
Replaced SMP from **2009-10**.

nc869023d8ca.s: The Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) is primarily associated with:
o: Industrial raw materials procured by the CCI
Perishable commodities not covered under MSP
Only wheat and paddy under open-ended procurement
nc869023d8ca.x: MIS provides price support for perishable commodities that are not covered under MSP.
nc869023d8ca.tq: Separate MIS for uncovered perishables from MSP and commodity-specific procurement schemes.
xs: **MIS** covers **perishable commodities not covered under MSP** — option **(2)**.
Examples: **onion, tomato, apple, chillies, grapes, garlic**.
xa: Trigger: **≥10% price fall** or **≥10% production rise**.
Losses shared **50:50** (Centre-State); **75:25** for NE States.
**Price Stabilisation Fund** (**2014-15**) also buffers **onion, potato, pulses**.

n655fc971ef7.s: Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA) was launched in which month and year?
n655fc971ef7.x: PM-AASHA was launched in September 2018 by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
n655fc971ef7.tq: Use the exact launch date to distinguish the scheme from later agricultural initiatives.
xs: **PM-AASHA** was launched in **September 2018** by the **Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare** — option **(2)**.
It aims to make **MSP reach farmers**, incl. small and marginal farmers.
xa: Outlay **₹35,000 crore** for extension to **2025-26** (APPSC-GS **2023** key).
**2026** components: **PSS, PDPS, MIS**; **PPSS** was the **2018** pilot.
Beneficiaries: **farmers** (APPSC **2018**; CGPSC **2024**).

n964b9715fbd.s: A farmer sells an oilseed in the market below its MSP, but no physical procurement takes place. Under which PM-AASHA component may the farmer receive the difference between MSP and the market price in cash?
n964b9715fbd.x: The Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS) makes a cash payment equal to the gap between MSP and the market price, mainly for oilseeds, without physical purchase.
n964b9715fbd.tq: Apply the no-procurement and cash-payment distinction to the agricultural scenario.
xs: **PDPS** pays the **MSP minus market price** gap in cash, with **no physical procurement** — option **(2)**.
**PSS** involves physical buying; **MIS** is for perishables; **PPSS** used private stockists.
xa: PDPS is mainly for **oilseeds**.
⚠ **PSS** = physical buying; **PDPS** = cash gap; **MIS** = perishables.
Economists prefer **PDPS-type deficiency payments** over a legal MSP.

nd1067084095.s: Under the Market Intervention Scheme of PM-AASHA, losses for North-Eastern States are shared between the Centre and the State in the ratio:
nd1067084095.x: NE States share MIS losses 75:25; other States ordinarily share them 50:50.
xa: Trigger: **≥10%** price fall or production rise.
MIS covers **onion, tomato, apple, chillies, grapes, garlic**.
PM-AASHA outlay: **₹35,000 crore** to **2025-26**.

nca15fb394f9.s: The outlay for the extension of PM-AASHA up to 2025-26 during the Fifteenth Finance Commission cycle is:
nca15fb394f9.x: The outlay for the Fifteenth Finance Commission cycle up to 2025-26 is ₹35,000 crore.
nca15fb394f9.tq: Recall the scheme outlay using the exact Finance Commission cycle and terminal year.
xs: PM-AASHA's outlay for extension to **2025-26** (**15th FC cycle**) is **₹35,000 crore** (APPSC-GS **2023** key) — option **(3)**.
PM-AASHA was launched in **September 2018** by the **Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare**.
xa: **2026** components: **PSS, PDPS, MIS**; **PPSS** was the **2018** pilot.
PSS **2024-25**: **61.87 LMT** procured; MSP value **>₹39,000 crore**; **26.56 lakh farmers**.
Purpose: make **MSP reach farmers**, incl. small and marginal farmers.

n9efaaaa7052.s: Under the Price Support Scheme (PSS) of PM-AASHA, physical procurement of pulses, oilseeds and copra at MSP is undertaken by:
n9efaaaa7052.x: NAFED and NCCF are the central nodal agencies that procure pulses, oilseeds and copra under PSS at a State's request. FCI handles wheat and paddy and CCI handles cotton; the warehousing corporations store produce; SFAC and NABARD promote FPOs.
xs: Under **PSS**, **NAFED and NCCF** buy **pulses, oilseeds, copra** at MSP at a state's request — option **(2)**.
**FCI** handles **wheat and paddy**; **CCI** handles **cotton**.
xa: Only **registered farmers with valid land records** qualify.
Cap: **25%** of production from **2024-25**.
⚠ **PSS** = physical buying; **PDPS** = cash gap, no buying; **MIS** = perishables.

n3734d210097.s: The Price Stabilisation Fund was established in 2014–15 mainly to:
o: Provide unlimited procurement of all MSP crops
Finance sugar mills’ purchase of cane at SAP
Create buffers of onion, potato and pulses and release them during price spikes
Guarantee exports of wheat and paddy
n3734d210097.x: The Price Stabilisation Fund was set up in 2014–15 to hold buffers of onion, potato and pulses and release them to curb sharp price increases.
n3734d210097.tq: Combine the establishment year with the specific commodities and stabilisation purpose.
xs: The **Price Stabilisation Fund** (**2014-15**) holds **buffers of onion, potato and pulses**, released to curb **price spikes** — option **(3)**.
It is a buffer fund for **perishables and pulses**, not for procurement, sugar mills or exports.
xa: **MIS** covers perishables not under MSP.
**Kerala** was first to fix **floor prices for 16 vegetables** (Nov **2020**).
In AP, the opposition alleged the State's promised fund was **abandoned** (May **2026**).

n42e076a94d2.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 suggested using savings from procurement efficiency to fund:
o: higher MSPs for rice and wheat
open-ended wheat procurement in all States
voluntary crop diversification away from water-guzzling rice and wheat
n42e076a94d2.x: The Survey proposed using procurement-efficiency savings for voluntary diversification away from water-guzzling rice and wheat.
xa: Procurement **crop bias** toward **paddy and wheat** is a key criticism.
Economists warn a legal MSP could **entrench monoculture**.
Pulses mission: **100%** procurement of **tur, urad, masoor** for **4 years**.

nf1f3d3961aa.s: Decentralised Procurement (DCP) of foodgrains was introduced in:
nf1f3d3961aa.x: DCP began in 1997; States procure, store and distribute, and the Centre reimburses economic cost minus CIP.
xa: AP procures paddy for **FCI's Central Pool** with **DBT** inside **48 hours**.
Decentralised procurement is listed among **alternatives** to a legal MSP.
States decide where **purchase centres** go.

nb6aed429436.s: The principal purpose of PM-AASHA is to ensure that:
o: the benefits of MSP reach farmers, including small and marginal farmers
all agricultural produce is procured by private agencies
agricultural exports are completely exempt from taxation
fertiliser subsidies reach only large farmers
nb6aed429436.x: PM-AASHA seeks to make MSP reach farmers, including small and marginal farmers.
nb6aed429436.tq: Identify the scheme objective rather than its implementing component.
xs: PM-AASHA's purpose is to **make MSP reach farmers**, **including small and marginal farmers** — option **(1)**.
It is a **farmer-welfare** scheme, not about private procurement, export tax or fertiliser subsidy.
xa: Full form: **Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan**.
Launched **September 2018**; outlay **₹35,000 crore** to **2025-26**.

n9bba5c97ee1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the pattern of MSP procurement?
o: Procurement is concentrated mainly in paddy and wheat
Procurement is concentrated in a few States
Punjab, Haryana, Telangana, AP and Chhattisgarh are among the main procuring States
Eastern and North-Eastern farmers are the main beneficiaries of procurement
n9bba5c97ee1.x: Eastern and North-Eastern farmers gain comparatively little from the existing procurement pattern.
xa: **Shanta Kumar HLC (2015)**: only about **6% of farmers** sell at MSP.
**ES 2025-26**: fund **voluntary crop diversification** away from water-guzzling rice and wheat.
Wheat RMS 2026-27 leaders: **Punjab 12.1 MT**, MP **10.4 MT**.

n8916ea62f05.s: The Shanta Kumar High-Level Committee (2015) estimated that approximately what proportion of farmers sell to procurement agencies at MSP?
n8916ea62f05.x: The Shanta Kumar Committee estimated that only about 6 per cent of farmers sell their produce to procurement agencies at MSP.
n8916ea62f05.tq: Retain the committee’s low participation estimate against larger distractor percentages.
xs: The **Shanta Kumar HLC (2015)** found only about **6 per cent** of farmers sell at MSP — option **(2)**.
This reflects the **crop bias** (paddy and wheat) and **regional bias** of procurement.
xa: MSP covers **22** crops, but procurement is mostly **paddy and wheat**.
**Eastern + NE** farmers gain little.
MSP is an **administrative decision**, not a legal right.

nc332da99c5b.s: Farmer unions demanding a legal guarantee for MSP primarily seek a law that would:
o: Replace all MSP procurement with direct cash transfers
Bind procurement agencies to purchase eligible produce at MSP
Transfer the power to fix MSP from CACP to State governments
nc332da99c5b.x: The legal-guarantee demand seeks to bind procurement at MSP. It does not automatically mean abolition of private trade or transfer of MSP powers to States.
nc332da99c5b.tq: Identify the precise legal obligation sought rather than broader consequences or policy alternatives.
xs: Farmer unions want a law **binding procurement at MSP** — option **(3)**.
MSP today is an **administrative decision, not a legal right**; no statute backs it.
xa: Economists fear a legal MSP could **distort trade**, entrench **monoculture** and breach **WTO** norms.
**Supreme Court** issued notice on a plea for MSP ≥ weighted average cost of production (**14 Apr 2026**).
Debate: **legal MSP guarantee vs WTO limits + fiscal cost**.

n56cede77ceb.s: Which of the following is NOT a concern economists have raised about a statutory MSP guarantee?
o: It would make deficiency-payment models such as PDPS unnecessary in every case
It could create difficulties with WTO norms
n56cede77ceb.x: Economists warn of trade distortion, monoculture and WTO problems, and often prefer PDPS-type deficiency payments as an alternative.
xa: Alternatives: **wider procurement**, **price-deficiency payments**, **PM-KISAN**, **decentralised procurement**, **e-NAM** digital procurement.
India joined the **WTO** in **1995**.
**PDPS** pays **MSP minus market price** without buying.

n85d5dad660e.s: Niger seed, which has an MSP and whose oil is used for cooking by some tribal communities, is a:
n85d5dad660e.x: Niger seed is a Kharif crop covered under MSP.
xa: ⚠ Highest MSP is **sesamum** (**10,346**), not niger.
Nigerseed is one of the **7** oilseeds in the MSP list.

n2b269f88845.s: The common paddy MSP for Kharif 2016–17 was
n2b269f88845.x: The common paddy MSP for Kharif 2016–17 was ₹1,470 per quintal.
n2b269f88845.tq: Separate the historical MSP figure from the later Kharif 2026–27 values.
xs: Common paddy MSP for **Kharif 2016-17** was **₹1,470 per quintal** (APPSC-G2 **2017** key) — option **(4)**.
**₹2,441** is the **2026-27** common paddy MSP and **₹2,461** the 2026-27 **Grade A** MSP.
xa: Kharif **2025-26** common paddy: **2,369**.
The **2026-27** hike for paddy was **+72**.
SKM says C2+50% paddy should be **₹3,243/q**.

ndbd93e4d82e.s: Which State was the first to fix floor prices for 16 vegetables in November 2020?
ndbd93e4d82e.x: Kerala became the first State to fix floor prices for 16 vegetables in November 2020.
ndbd93e4d82e.tq: Use the State-and-number association to distinguish floor-price policy from central MSP.
xs: **Kerala** was the **first State** to fix **floor prices for 16 vegetables** (Nov **2020**) — option **(1)**.
Vegetables are otherwise **not covered by MSP** and fall under **MIS**.
xa: MIS trigger: **≥10%** price fall or production rise.
**Price Stabilisation Fund** (**2014-15**): buffers of onion, potato, pulses.
MIS losses shared **50:50** (**75:25** for NE States).

n30750c2e8cb.s: The Food Corporation of India was established under which Act on the recommendation of which committee?
o: Food Corporations Act, 1964; Food Grains Prices Committee chaired by L. K. Jha
Essential Commodities Act, 1955; Agricultural Prices Commission
Agricultural Produce Markets Act; Kelkar Committee
n30750c2e8cb.x: FCI was set up under the Food Corporations Act, 1964, on the recommendation of the Food Grains Prices Committee associated with L. K. Jha in 1964.
n30750c2e8cb.tq: Match the statutory basis with the recommending committee instead of confusing the Food Corporations Act with other agriculture and food laws.
xs: FCI was set up under the **Food Corporations Act, 1964** on the recommendation of the **Food Grains Prices Committee (L.K. Jha)** — option **(1)**.
The **Agricultural Prices Commission** was a separate body set up the same year (**1965**), not FCI's recommender.
xa: FCI date: **14 January 1965**; HQ **New Delhi**.
FCI is the **nodal agency** for procuring **wheat and paddy** under price support.
FCI challenges: **rising operating costs**, **excess stocks + wastage**, **falling issue-price earnings**.

nac5436939c0.s: Which of the following is NOT a mission of the Food Corporation of India?
o: Efficient procurement of foodgrains at MSP
Making foodgrains accessible to weaker sections through TPDS
nac5436939c0.x: Regulating agricultural markets falls under State APMC laws, not FCI; the other three are FCI missions.
xa: ⚠ **Not** an FCI mission = **regulating markets in agricultural products** (APPSC-GS **2018**).
FCI's **Anna Darpan** modernises its supply chain.
**OSM** rolled out from **1 April 2022**.

n9c77ce6660b.s: The Indian Grain Storage Management and Research Institute, associated with foodgrain storage research and training, has its headquarters at
n9c77ce6660b.x: The Indian Grain Storage Management and Research Institute has its headquarters at Hapur (UP); Hyderabad and Ludhiana host its field stations.
n9c77ce6660b.tq: Distinguish the institute's headquarters from FCI's headquarters and from its field stations.
xs: **IGMRI** has its headquarters at **Hapur (UP)** — option **(4)**.
It handles **grain storage management and research**.
xa: **FCI** HQ is **New Delhi**.
**NCDC** implements the cooperative **Grain Storage Plan**.
**CAP** storage and PPP **steel silos** are the two storage modes in the notes.

n40604fa974b.s: Food-grain stocks remaining far above the prescribed buffer norms most directly lead to:
o: a fall in food subsidy expenditure
n40604fa974b.x: Stocks well above norms raise carrying costs because larger quantities must be stored and maintained.
xa: **Economic cost** = **MSP + bonus** + **procurement incidentals** + **distribution cost**; pooled grain cost is about **two-thirds** of it.
A **hidden subsidy** example: FCI's carrying cost financed by borrowing instead of budget releases.
FCI challenges: rising operating costs, **excess stocks + wastage**, falling issue-price earnings.

nc2fccdd7cf4.s: The Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) is primarily intended to enable the Food Corporation of India to:
o: Sell wheat and rice from the Central Pool in the open market at predetermined prices
Transfer the entire food subsidy directly to State Governments
Purchase pulses exclusively from small farmers
Distribute all procured grain only through fair price shops
nc2fccdd7cf4.x: Under OMSS(D), FCI sells wheat and rice from the Central Pool at predetermined prices to moderate market prices.
nc2fccdd7cf4.tq: Match the scheme mechanism with its stated market-stabilisation purpose.
xs: Under **OMSS(D)**, FCI **sells wheat and rice from the Central Pool** in the open market at **pre-determined prices** — option **(1)**.
The aim is to **moderate market prices**.
xa: Procurement objective: **market intervention to check prices**.
**Food subsidy** = **economic cost minus CIP**.
⚠ **CIP** = Centre's issue price, not FPS retail.

n600578d704b.s: The recommendation to hand over procurement in surplus States to the respective State Governments was intended primarily to enable the FCI to focus on which region?
n600578d704b.x: The committee proposed that procurement in surplus States such as Punjab, Haryana and Andhra Pradesh be handled by those States, allowing FCI to focus on the eastern States.
n600578d704b.tq: Link the administrative redistribution of work with its intended regional focus.
xs: Handing procurement in surplus States to those States was meant to let the FCI focus on the **Eastern States** — option **(3)** is correct.
The surplus States named were **Punjab**, **Haryana** and **Andhra Pradesh**.
xa: The **Shanta Kumar HLC** (constituted **2014**, report **2015**) also urged wider **DCP** by States.
Under **DCP (1997)**, designated States procure, store and distribute grain for TPDS; the Centre pays the gap between the State's economic cost and **CIP**.
**FCI** was set up on **14 January 1965** under the **Food Corporations Act, 1964**, as the **nodal agency** for procuring wheat and paddy.

ndce17ceee07.s: The 'Central Issue Price' (CIP) in India's food management refers to the price at which:
o: Farmers are assured a floor price announced before sowing
The Centre issues foodgrains to States for distribution under the PDS
Fair Price Shops sell grain to beneficiaries, as fixed by the FCI
FCI sells wheat in the open market under OMSS(D)
ndce17ceee07.x: CIP is the price at which the Centre issues grain to States and beneficiaries for PDS. A floor price announced before sowing is MSP. The FPS retail price is fixed by the States, not the FCI. OMSS(D) sales are at separate predetermined prices.
ndce17ceee07.tq: CIP = Centre's issue price; retail FPS price = States; food subsidy = economic cost - CIP.
xs: **CIP** is the price at which **the Centre issues foodgrains to States** for PDS — option **(2)**.
The pre-sowing floor is **MSP**; the FPS retail price is fixed by **States**, not FCI; OMSS(D) uses separate **pre-determined prices**.
xa: Food subsidy = **economic cost minus CIP**.
Under **DCP**, the Centre pays the State's **economic cost minus CIP**.
⚠ **CIP** ≠ FPS retail price.

ne83c9eeef90.s: Food subsidy has two principal components, namely:
o: FCI subsidy and subsidy to decentralised procurement States
ne83c9eeef90.x: The two components are the FCI subsidy, covering NFSA, other welfare schemes and strategic reserve, and subsidy to DCP States.
ne83c9eeef90.tq: Identify the two-part structure of food subsidy instead of confusing it with other agricultural subsidies.
xs: Food subsidy has two components: **FCI subsidy** and **subsidy to DCP States** — option **(2)**.
FCI subsidy covers **NFSA**, **other welfare schemes** and the **strategic reserve**.
xa: Food subsidy = **economic cost − CIP**.

n3ce8f4e06ca.s: Which of the following is an example of a 'hidden' food subsidy?
o: The food subsidy amount shown in the Union Budget
The difference between economic cost and CIP reimbursed to DCP States through budget releases
FCI's carrying cost financed by borrowing instead of budget releases
The MSP paid to farmers for wheat
n3ce8f4e06ca.x: A hidden subsidy is a cost not shown as subsidy, such as FCI's carrying cost financed by borrowing (e.g. NSSF loans) instead of budget releases. An amount shown in the budget, including budgeted reimbursement to DCP States, is an explicit subsidy. MSP is a procurement price, not a subsidy category.
n3ce8f4e06ca.tq: Explicit = shown in budget; hidden = off-budget borrowing such as NSSF loans.
xs: **FCI's carrying cost financed by borrowing instead of budget releases** is a **hidden subsidy** — option **(3)**.
Amounts **shown in the budget** (incl. budgeted DCP reimbursements) are **explicit subsidy**.
xa: **NSSF** loans made the subsidy **off-budget** until **Budget 2021-22**.
Food subsidy = **economic cost minus CIP**.
Criticism: **stocks above norms** raise carrying costs.

n5a234f3a1e0.s: Under the Decentralised Procurement scheme, designated States are responsible for:
o: Procuring, storing and distributing grain for TPDS themselves
Fixing the national MSP for all agricultural commodities
Replacing the FCI in every State without financial support
Only importing foodgrains for the Central Pool
n5a234f3a1e0.x: Under DCP, designated States procure, store and distribute grain for TPDS themselves. The Centre pays the difference between the State's economic cost and the Central Issue Price.
n5a234f3a1e0.tq: Ask which authority performs the complete procurement-to-distribution chain.
xs: Under **DCP**, designated States **procure, store and distribute grain for TPDS** themselves — option **(1)**.
They get financial support: the Centre pays **economic cost minus CIP**, so option (3) is wrong.
xa: Benefits: **local procurement**, **less transport**, **more MSP reach**.
Food subsidy to **DCP States**: **₹70,410.60 cr** in **2024-25**.
MSP is recommended by **CACP** and approved by **CCEA**, not by States.

o: Covered and Plinth storage, in which grain is kept on raised plinths under polythene covers
Centralised agricultural procurement storage in steel silos
Containerised agricultural produce storage at ports
nb4f0c3fcaa2.x: CAP means Cover and Plinth storage. Surplus grain is kept on raised plinths under polythene covers.
nb4f0c3fcaa2.tq: Expand the acronym and connect it with the physical arrangement used for open grain storage.
xs: **CAP** = **Cover and Plinth** — grain kept **on raised plinths under polythene covers** — option **(1)**.
It is **open storage** used for **surplus grain**.
xa: **Steel silos** under **PPP** modernise bulk storage.
Cooperative plan: PACS silos of **50/100/200 MT**.
**IGMRI** at **Hapur (UP)** does grain storage research.

n696165a32ee.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of major developments in India's Public Distribution System?
n696165a32ee.x: The sequence was PDS, followed by RPDS in June 1992, TPDS in June 1997 and AAY on 25 December 2000.
n696165a32ee.tq: Use the first-and-last items to eliminate reversed sequences.
xs: The sequence is **PDS — RPDS — TPDS — AAY** — option **(1)**.
Rationing (PDS) began in the **1940s**; **RPDS** June **1992**; **TPDS** June **1997**; **AAY** **25 Dec 2000**.
xa: **NFSA** came in **2013**; **ONORC** from **2019** onward.
NFSA grain made **free** under **PMGKAY** from **1 Jan 2023**.
⚠ **TPDS** (**1997**) is the same year as **DCP**.

nb66ef863e5b.s: The Public Distribution System in India first began in the 1940s primarily in the context of which event?
o: The introduction of the National Food Security Act
nb66ef863e5b.x: Rationing began in the 1940s against the backdrop of the Bengal famine. The system was later revived during the food shortages of the 1960s.
nb66ef863e5b.tq: Identify the historical context associated with the origin of the policy.
xs: Rationing began in the **1940s** against the backdrop of the **Bengal famine** — option **(2)**.
It was **revived during the 1960s shortages**, so option (1) "1960s food surplus" is wrong.
xa: **RPDS** (June **1992**) for backward, hilly and drought areas.
**TPDS** (June **1997**): separate **BPL and APL** entitlements.
**AAY** (**25 Dec 2000**): **35 kg/family/month**.

nea7c4c24bfa.s: The Revamped Public Distribution System (RPDS) for backward, hilly and drought-prone areas was launched in:
nea7c4c24bfa.x: RPDS was launched in June 1992; separate BPL and APL entitlements came later under TPDS.
xa: **NFSA** (**2013**) covers about **800 million** people.

nfd1a470e544.s: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) was launched on 25 December 2000 to provide how much foodgrain per family per month to the poorest households?
nfd1a470e544.x: AAY was launched on 25 December 2000 for the poorest households, with an entitlement of 35 kg of foodgrain per family per month.
nfd1a470e544.tq: Use the exact date and quantity rather than confusing AAY with other food entitlements.
xs: **AAY** (**25 Dec 2000**) gives **35 kg** per family per month to the poorest — option **(3)**.
It came after **RPDS** (**1992**) and **TPDS** (**1997**).
xa: **NFSA** (**2013**): legal entitlement for about **800 million** people.
Covid-era **PMGKY**: **5 kg/month** free on top of NFSA entitlements.

nbdbe27bdf9a.s: Which system tracks foodgrain end-to-end from procurement to the Fair Price Shop with real-time stock monitoring?
nbdbe27bdf9a.x: SARTHAK-PDS digitally tracks grain from procurement to the Fair Price Shop and monitors stocks in real time to check leakage.
xa: SARTHAK-PDS = "Scheme for Assistance in Ration Transport and Handling-Income with Automation in PDS", approved by the **CCEA** for **2026-2031**.
It is an **umbrella scheme**: intra-state movement, **FPS dealer margins** and **SMART-PDS**.
It uses **AI/ML, blockchain and NLP** for monitoring and grievances.

n02c70fd9ce5.s: SARTHAK-PDS, the umbrella PDS reform scheme approved by the CCEA, covers the period:
n02c70fd9ce5.x: SARTHAK-PDS, which subsumes SMART-PDS (April 2023 - March 2026), was approved for 2026-2031; End-to-End Computerisation of TPDS ran October 2012 - March 2020.
xa: **IM-PDS** began in **Apr 2018** for national portability (ONORC).
**OSM** was rolled out from **1 April 2022** for storage, movement and distribution under TPDS.
⚠ **SMART-PDS** is folded into **SARTHAK-PDS**.

n71837e7e6aa.s: A migrant NFSA beneficiary using ONORC may draw foodgrains at an ePoS-enabled fair price shop after:
o: Obtaining a new ration card in the destination State only
Receiving prior approval from the District Collector of both States
Surrendering the ration card to the destination fair price shop
Biometric or Aadhaar authentication, with the family able to draw the balance at home
n71837e7e6aa.x: ONORC permits a migrant to lift the full or partial entitlement at an ePoS-enabled fair price shop after biometric or Aadhaar authentication; the family can draw the balance at the original location.
n71837e7e6aa.tq: Trace the portability process from authentication to division of the household entitlement.
xs: Under ONORC a migrant lifts grain after **biometric or Aadhaar authentication**, with the **family** able to draw the **balance** at home — option **(4)** is correct.
No new ration card or approval is needed: NFSA ration cards are **portable** nationwide via **ePoS** at any FPS.
xa: The migrant may lift the **full or part** entitlement.
Rollout target was **1 June 2020**; mobile app **"Mera Ration"**.
**187 crore+ transactions** and ~**443 LMT** grain moved under portability (Aug 2019 - Sep 2025).

n6d69be745fc.s: The SARTHAK-PDS programme for the period 2026–31 was approved by which of the following?
o: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution alone
n6d69be745fc.x: SARTHAK-PDS for 2026–31 was approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA).
n6d69be745fc.tq: Identify the correct approving authority rather than the implementing or associated body.
xs: SARTHAK-PDS (**2026-31**) was approved by the **Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs** (**CCEA**) — option **(3)** is correct.
The approval came on **28 May 2026**.
xa: It is an umbrella scheme: **intra-state movement**, **FPS dealer margins** and **SMART-PDS**.
It gives end-to-end tracking of grain from procurement to the **FPS** with real-time stock monitoring.
The **CCEA** also approves the **MSP** recommended by the **CACP**.

na26132c101b.s: The PDS seeks to provide a guaranteed minimum quantity of grain at affordable prices to:
na26132c101b.x: PDS aims at affordable grain for low-income groups, equitable distribution and control of price swings.
xa: ⚠ Export of foodgrains is **not** a food-management objective.
PDS evolution: rationing in the **1940s** → **RPDS** (June **1992**) → **TPDS** (June **1997**) → **AAY** (**25 Dec 2000**).
**NFSA** (**2013**) gives a legal entitlement to about **800 million** people.

nb57d0baeab8.s: Procurement operations make grain available to weaker sections under:
nb57d0baeab8.x: Procurement aims to assure MSP, supply grain to weaker sections under PMGKAY and check prices.
xa: **Open-ended** procurement: wheat and paddy; **target-based**: PSS for pulses and oilseeds, capped at **25%**.
**DCP (1997)**: designated States procure, store and distribute for TPDS.
PMGKAY gives free grain to **80 crore+** NFSA beneficiaries from **1 Jan 2023**.

n81d214d7890.s: Which of the following is NOT a challenge faced by the Food Corporation of India?
o: Regulation of agricultural markets by FCI
n81d214d7890.x: Market regulation is not an FCI function; it falls under State APMC laws.
xa: Criticism: **stocks far above norms → carrying costs**; rising **economic cost**.
**Shanta Kumar HLC** recommended **restructuring FCI's debt**.
**NSSF** loans met FCI's funding gap → subsidy **off-budget**.

nf71af021ebc.s: The retail price of foodgrains at Fair Price Shops is fixed by:
nf71af021ebc.x: States fix the FPS retail price and handle the operational role in the PDS.
xa: Food subsidy = **economic cost minus CIP**.
By end-2025, **5.50 lakh of 5.51 lakh FPS** use ePoS.

nc3c3be7ddbf.s: The food subsidy, earlier partly met off-budget through NSSF loans to FCI, was brought back on budget in:
nc3c3be7ddbf.x: Budget 2021-22 brought the food subsidy back on budget.
xa: A **hidden subsidy** is a cost not shown as subsidy, e.g. FCI's carrying cost financed by borrowing.
An **explicit subsidy** is shown in the budget.
Shanta Kumar HLC: **restructure FCI's debt**.

nf3f04382b4e.s: Which of the following is NOT a measure for addressing leakages in the PDS?
o: Biometric authentication at Fair Price Shops
nf3f04382b4e.x: e-PoS, ONORC and biometric authentication tackle leakages; ending procurement is not such a measure.
xa: By end-2025, **5.50 lakh of 5.51 lakh FPS** used ePoS.
About **99.8%** of FPS are automated for Aadhaar-based distribution; ~**99.9%** of ration cards are Aadhaar-seeded.
**SARTHAK-PDS (2026-31)** adds real-time stock monitoring to stop leakage.

n86274c32b04.s: SMART-PDS is part of which umbrella scheme?
n86274c32b04.x: SARTHAK-PDS covers SMART-PDS, intra-state movement and FPS dealer margins.
xa: It was approved by the **CCEA** for **2026-2031** (**28 May 2026**).
It gives end-to-end digital tracking of grain from procurement to the **FPS**, with real-time stock monitoring.
⚠ **SMART-PDS** (2023-26) is folded into **SARTHAK-PDS** (2026-31).

n4bc43ab88d3.s: Which institutions are associated respectively with selection and implementation under the Grain Storage Plan in the cooperative sector?
o: District Cooperative Development Committees and NCDC
n4bc43ab88d3.x: PACS are selected by District Cooperative Development Committees, while the National Cooperative Development Corporation implements the plan.
n4bc43ab88d3.tq: Start with the institutional pair and distinguish the body that selects from the body that implements.
xs: PACS are selected by **District Cooperative Development Committees**, and **NCDC** implements — option **(1)**.
**CACP and CCEA** handle MSP; **NSSF** loans financed FCI; FCI and CWC are not named for selection here.
xa: Facilities: silos of **50/100/200 MT**, procurement centres, FPS, processing units, custom hiring centres.
**NCCF** works with AP Civil Supplies on **Mee Mart** outlets.
**IGMRI** (Hapur) handles grain storage research.

n476e05e78a8.s: The Shanta Kumar High Level Committee proposed cutting NFSA coverage from 67% to about:
n476e05e78a8.x: The HLC (2014-15) proposed about 40% coverage and estimated PDS leakage at about 46%.
xa: Recommended expanding **DCP**, **DBT/cash transfers** and adding **pulses and millets** to PDS.
Proposed handing procurement in surplus States to the States, with FCI focusing on **eastern States**.
**FCI** set up in **1965** under the **Food Corporations Act, 1964**.

nb4c3e3f7f80.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Shanta Kumar Committee's recommendations?
o: Cutting NFSA coverage to about 50% of the population
Use of DBT or cash transfers where feasible
Greater private participation in storage and logistics
nb4c3e3f7f80.x: The committee proposed cutting NFSA coverage from 67% to about 40%, not 50%.
xa: It also recommended **restructuring FCI's debt** and cutting NFSA coverage from **67%** to about **40%**.
The committee was constituted in **2014** and reported in **2015**; older notes say "set up in 2015".
It put PDS leakage at about **46%** (NSS **2011-12** data).

n94131c969ed.s: The Online Storage Management system of the Food Corporation of India was rolled out from
n94131c969ed.x: FCI's Online Storage Management (OSM) system was rolled out from 1 April 2022 for efficient storage, movement and distribution of foodgrains under TPDS.
n94131c969ed.tq: Separate the rollout date of OSM from the establishment year of FCI and the date of the governing Act.
xs: **Online Storage Management (OSM)** was rolled out from **1 April 2022** — option **(1)**.
It aims at efficient **storage, movement and distribution** under **TPDS** (APPSC-GS **2021**).
xa: ⚠ **OSM** = storage; **Anna Darpan** = FCI supply chain, not Agriculture Ministry.
**SMART-PDS** (**Apr 2023 - Mar 2026**) is folded into **SARTHAK-PDS** (**2026-2031**).
**End-to-End Computerisation of TPDS**: **Oct 2012 - Mar 2020**.

ne67e93b5de0.s: Anna Darpan is intended to modernise the supply chain of:
ne67e93b5de0.x: Anna Darpan belongs to the food and PDS side and modernises FCI's supply chain; it is not an Agriculture Ministry system.
xa: **OSM** (from **1 April 2022**) is the storage system.
**IM-PDS** (from **Apr 2018**) gives national portability (**ONORC**).
**SARTHAK-PDS** adds **AI/ML, blockchain, NLP** for monitoring.

n010e8debf4b.s: Cash transfer (DBT) of NFSA food subsidy is implemented in which of the following?
n010e8debf4b.x: DBT in food under NFSA is implemented in Chandigarh, Puducherry and urban Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
xa: The **Shanta Kumar Committee** recommended cash transfers in well-connected areas.
Food subsidy = **economic cost minus CIP**, reimbursed to FCI and to **DCP States**.

n24e26fcc6d9.s: Integrated Management of PDS (IM-PDS), introduced from April 2018, is principally associated with:
o: Conversion of Fair Price Shops into mini-marts
n24e26fcc6d9.x: IM-PDS began in April 2018 and is associated with national portability under ONORC.
n24e26fcc6d9.tq: Associate a reform name with its principal operational function.
xs: **IM-PDS** (from **Apr 2018**) is associated with **national portability** under **ONORC** — option **(3)** is correct.
FPS-to-mini-mart conversion is AP's **Mee Mart**; free grain is **PMGKAY**; fortified rice carries **iron, B12, folic acid**.
xa: ONORC uses **ePoS**, **Aadhaar-seeded** cards and fingerprint/iris authentication.
ONORC is rolled out in **all 36 States/UTs**, covering about **80 crore** NFSA beneficiaries.
Its mobile app is **"Mera Ration"**.

n1319fb10c73.s: The mobile application associated with One Nation One Ration Card is:
n1319fb10c73.x: The mobile application associated with ONORC is named “Mera Ration”.
n1319fb10c73.tq: Recall the exact official name of the scheme-linked application.
xs: ONORC's mobile app is **"Mera Ration"** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2021).
ONORC gives nationwide **portability** of NFSA ration cards through ePoS and Aadhaar authentication.
xa: The rollout target was **1 June 2020** (APPSC 2018).
**IM-PDS** (from **Apr 2018**) is the scheme behind national portability.
ONORC now covers **all 36 States/UTs**.

nb0b401cd273.s: One Nation One Ration Card enables beneficiaries to:
o: Receive cash in place of grain
Draw ration away from where their card was issued
Buy grain directly from FCI depots
nb0b401cd273.x: ONORC gives ration portability through ePoS devices, Aadhaar-seeded cards and biometric authentication.
xa: A migrant lifts full or part entitlement anywhere; the **family back home** draws the balance.
Mobile app: **"Mera Ration"** (APPSC **2021**).
**2.07 billion+** portability transactions; **99.8%** of FPS automated.

n01614b21b19.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about AP e-PDS?
o: Only about half of its rice cards are Aadhaar-seeded
It enables biometric transactions with intra-State portability
Distribution was extended to Mid-Day Meal and Anganwadi centres
n01614b21b19.x: AP e-PDS has 100% Aadhaar seeding of rice cards, not about half.
xa: About **29,783** automated FPS serve **4.3 crore** people.
⚠ **29,796** FPS (APSES) vs **29,783** automated FPS (NIC AP); **1.48 crore** beneficiaries vs **1.44 crore** rice cards.
APSES 2024-25: **98%** Aadhaar-linked ration cards; **9,260** MDUs.

n906af6fa914.s: The occurrence of undernutrition and overnutrition in the same population is known as:
n906af6fa914.x: The coexistence of undernutrition and overnutrition in the same population is called the double burden of malnutrition.
n906af6fa914.tq: Test the exact official term for a paired concept.
xs: Undernutrition and overnutrition together in the same population is the **double burden of malnutrition** — option **(4)** is correct.
**NFHS-6** confirms India faces this double burden (**5 Jun 2026**).
xa: Undernutrition covers protein-energy malnutrition, micronutrient deficiency, stunting and wasting.
Overnutrition = **overweight and obesity**.
NFHS-6: stunting down to **29.3%**, yet the double burden persists.

nad42965b15e.s: Which of the following is a form of overnutrition?
nad42965b15e.x: Overnutrition covers overweight and obesity; stunting, wasting and micronutrient deficiency are undernutrition.
xa: Both together in one population = **double burden of malnutrition**; **NFHS-6** confirms India faces it.
**Underweight** = low weight-for-age.

nc578b622a61.s: The restriction concerning HFSS foods mentioned in the context of school nutrition relates to their sale within what distance of schools?
nc578b622a61.x: The cited policy debate concerns the ban on HFSS foods within 50 metres of schools.
nc578b622a61.tq: Identify the precise distance attached to the regulatory restriction.
xs: The ban covers **HFSS foods** within **50 metres** of schools — option **(2)** is correct.
It appears with **FSSAI labelling** in the debates (**29 Jun 2026**).
xa: Other debates: **cereal-centric PDS** vs dietary diversity and the **GHI** methodology.
AP angle: last-mile gaps in **tribal hamlets** and **Rayalaseema**.

ndf696e6a9fb.s: Which of the following is regarded as the biggest factor contributing to the malnutrition burden?
o: Poor dietary habits and food insecurity
ndf696e6a9fb.x: Poor dietary habits and food insecurity are identified as the biggest factors contributing to the malnutrition burden.
ndf696e6a9fb.tq: Identify the principal cause rather than a secondary associated factor.
xs: The biggest factor is **poor dietary habits and food insecurity** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-G2 2025 key).
High literacy and improved sanitation reduce malnutrition; **open defecation and unsafe water** are the causes.
xa: Other causes: **cereal-heavy diets**, **early (adolescent) pregnancy**, poverty and gender gaps, weak counselling.
Malnutrition is **multi-causal**, so nutrition is combined with **WASH**.

nb0f8b38dc05.s: The adolescent-girl programme in Andhra Pradesh is implemented in which of the following districts or areas?
o: All districts uniformly through urban Anganwadi Centres
ASR, Parvathipuram Manyam and YSR Kadapa
nb0f8b38dc05.x: The adolescent-girl programme is implemented in ASR, Parvathipuram Manyam and YSR Kadapa, covering 14,942 girls.
nb0f8b38dc05.tq: Test the exact geographical coverage instead of assuming statewide uniformity.
xs: AP's adolescent-girl coverage is in **ASR, Parvathipuram Manyam and YSR Kadapa** — option **(2)** is correct.
It covers **14,942** adolescent girls.
xa: Poshan 2.0 in AP covers **19.13 lakh** children below 6.
**₹99.58 crore** was released for **9,958 AWCs**; **192** new AWCs under **PM JANMAN**.

n718d8414b99.s: The Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) was launched on:
n718d8414b99.x: ICDS was launched on 2 October 1975 during the Fifth Five-Year Plan.
xs: **ICDS** was launched on **2 October 1975**, in the **5th Plan** — option **(4)** is correct.
**15 Aug 1995** is the Mid-Day Meal (NP-NSPE); **1992** is NIDDCP; **2016** is MAA.
xa: ICDS is under the Ministry of **Women & Child Development**.
AP ICDS (2024-25): **55,607 AWCs** and **257 projects** in 26 districts.

n78851c095e2.s: The idea underlying the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education, later associated with the Mid-Day Meal initiative, started in:
n78851c095e2.x: The idea of the Mid-Day Meal initiative started in Tamil Nadu; the national programme was launched on 15 August 1995.
n78851c095e2.tq: Separate the place where the idea began from the date of national launch.
xs: The Mid-Day Meal idea started in **Tamil Nadu** — option **(4)** is correct.
The national **NP-NSPE / Mid-Day Meal** began on **15 Aug 1995**.
xa: It was renamed **PM POSHAN** in **2021**, under the Ministry of **Education**.
Fortified rice Phase I (**2021-22**) covered **ICDS and PM POSHAN**.

n2b1be20079f.s: The National Goitre Control Programme was renamed as the National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme (NIDDCP) in:
n2b1be20079f.x: The National Goitre Control Programme was launched in 1962 and renamed NIDDCP in 1992.
n2b1be20079f.tq: Distinguish the original launch year from the renaming year.
xs: The Goitre programme became **NIDDCP** in **1992** — option **(3)** is correct.
**1962** is when the **National Goitre Control Programme** began; **1970** is the Vitamin A and anaemia prophylaxis programmes.
**1999** is a trap: "NIDDCP - 1999" was a **wrong** pair in APPSC-GS 2024.
xa: NIDDCP is under **Health & FW**; AP runs it under **NP-NCD**.
**Double-fortified salt** carries **iodine + iron**.

n6a76d291c9a.s: MAA, or Mothers’ Absolute Affection, is a programme related to:
n6a76d291c9a.x: MAA is a breastfeeding promotion programme launched in 2016.
n6a76d291c9a.tq: Decode the programme title and connect it with its health objective.
xs: **MAA (Mothers' Absolute Affection)** promotes **breastfeeding** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was launched in **2016** under **Health & FW** (correctly dated in APPSC-GS 2024).
xa: NFHS-6: breastfeeding within 1 hour of birth rose from **41.8%** to **50.1%**.
Complementary feeding (6-8 months): **45.9% to 59.5%**.

n5a43147ff40.s: PM POSHAN, which renamed the Mid-Day Meal scheme in 2021, is administered by which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
n5a43147ff40.x: PM POSHAN (renamed from MDM in 2021) is under the Ministry of Education. ICDS is under Women and Child Development; NIDDCP, MAA and Anaemia Mukt Bharat are under Health and Family Welfare; the PDS is under Food and Public Distribution.
n5a43147ff40.tq: School meals = Education; ICDS = WCD; NIDDCP/MAA/AMB = Health.
xs: **PM POSHAN** (renamed from Mid-Day Meal in **2021**) is under the **Ministry of Education** — option **(3)** is correct.
**ICDS** is under **Women & Child Development**; **NIDDCP**, **MAA** and **Anaemia Mukt Bharat** are under **Health & FW**.
xa: The Mid-Day Meal (NP-NSPE) began on **15 Aug 1995**; the idea came from **Tamil Nadu**.
Fortified rice Phase I (**2021-22**) covered ICDS and PM POSHAN.

ncc1a11be136.s: Which of the following is a component of the Anaemia Mukt Bharat strategy?
o: Replacement of all supplementary nutrition with cereals
IFA tablets, deworming and outreach for six target groups
ncc1a11be136.x: Anaemia Mukt Bharat uses IFA tablets, deworming and outreach directed at six target groups. It is not limited to calcium supplementation.
ncc1a11be136.tq: Identify the intervention bundle rather than a single nutrient measure.
xs: Anaemia Mukt Bharat uses **IFA tablets, deworming and outreach for six target groups** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is about iron and folic acid, not calcium-only or cereal-only measures.
xa: **WIFS**: weekly IFA for adolescents aged **10-19**.
It began in **2018** under **Health & FW**.
POSHAN Abhiyaan also targets **anaemia** among children **6-59 months** and women/girls **15-49**.

nb19745ab616.s: The principal goal associated with POSHAN Abhiyaan is expressed as:
nb19745ab616.x: POSHAN Abhiyaan aims to achieve a Suposhit Bharat through convergence, technology and a Jan Andolan.
nb19745ab616.tq: Distinguish the programme’s stated goal from other national slogans.
xs: POSHAN Abhiyaan's goal is **Suposhit Bharat** — option **(1)** is correct.
It works through **convergence**, **technology** and **Jan Andolan**.
xa: It targets **stunting**, **undernutrition/underweight**, **anaemia** and **low birth weight**.
**Mission Poshan 2.0** runs over the **15th FC period 2021-22 to 2025-26**.
The **POSHAN Tracker** app monitors Anganwadi services in real time.

n358fdd03690.s: Which of the following is NOT among the major outcomes targeted by POSHAN Abhiyaan?
o: Reduction in anaemia among children, women and adolescent girls
n358fdd03690.x: POSHAN Abhiyaan targets reductions in stunting, undernutrition or underweight, anaemia and low birth weight. Universal increase in adult obesity is not an objective.
n358fdd03690.tq: Find the option outside the programme’s stated target set.
xs: **Universal increase in adult obesity** is not a POSHAN Abhiyaan target — option **(1)** is the answer.
It targets reduction of **stunting**, **undernutrition/underweight**, **anaemia** and **low birth weight**.
xa: Anaemia targets cover children **6-59 months** and women and adolescent girls **15-49**.
Obesity is **overnutrition**, the other half of the double burden.
Goal: **Suposhit Bharat**.

n8cd9eb59205.s: The POSHAN Tracker application is used for:
o: tracking PDS grain from procurement to Fair Price Shops
n8cd9eb59205.x: The POSHAN Tracker enables real-time monitoring of Anganwadi services.
xa: Poshan Tracker data (**July 2025**) show **UP** worst for stunting (**48.8%**).
**Bihar** is worst for wasting (**9.3%**); **MP** for underweight (**24.8%**).

n19f7fa1d121.s: Anna Amrutha Hastham provides which benefit?
o: A corpus payable to orphaned children at age 23
Free antenatal check-up on the ninth day of every month
One full meal a day at the Anganwadi Centre for pregnant and lactating women
A monthly supply of 30 eggs to children aged 6–36 months
n19f7fa1d121.x: Anna Amrutha Hastham provides one full meal a day at the Anganwadi Centre to pregnant and lactating women.
n19f7fa1d121.tq: Match the scheme name with its direct service benefit.
xs: **Anna Amrutha Hastham** gives **one full meal a day** at Anganwadi centres to **pregnant and lactating women** — option **(3)** is correct.
**30 eggs** a month for children 6-36 months is the **tribal-area package**, not this scheme.
xa: **Bala Sanjeevani** gives these women Take Home Ration plus a **₹250** monthly nutrition kit.
Bala Sanjeevani runs through **47,296 AWCs** in plain areas.

naf1ddbb96d4.s: Children aged 36–72 months under the plain-area package receive:
o: A meal, one egg and 200 ml milk
A hot cooked meal, one egg and 100 ml milk
A hot cooked meal, two eggs and 200 ml milk
naf1ddbb96d4.x: Children aged 36–72 months receive a hot cooked meal, one egg and 100 ml milk under the plain-area package.
naf1ddbb96d4.tq: Match the age group with its specific meal and milk entitlement.
xs: Plain-area children **36-72 months** get a **hot cooked meal**, **egg** and **100 ml milk** — option **(2)** is correct.
**200 ml** milk is the **tribal-area** provision.
xa: ⚠ The tribal package doubles milk for 36-72 months (**100 ml → 200 ml**).
Children **6-36 months** (plain) get **Balamrutham 2.5 kg + 25 eggs + 2.5 l milk** a month.

n3f73ce4d710.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the tribal-area nutrition package?
o: Children aged 36–72 months get a meal, one egg and 200 ml milk
Children aged 6–36 months get 2.5 kg Balamrutham per month
Children aged 6–36 months get 30 eggs and 6 litres milk per month
Children aged 6–36 months get fewer eggs than in the plain-area package
n3f73ce4d710.x: The tribal package gives 30 eggs, more than the 25 in the plain-area package.
xa: Plain-area 6-36 months milk is only **2.5 l**.
Older notes call the tribal package **YSR Sampoorna Poshana Plus**.

nfaa986ad742.s: As per 2024-25 data, the ICDS network in Andhra Pradesh comprises about:
nfaa986ad742.x: AP ICDS (2024-25) has 55,607 AWCs and 257 projects (200 rural, 33 urban, 24 tribal) in 26 districts. 47,296 is the number of AWCs delivering Bala Sanjeevani in plain areas; 9,958 AWCs received ₹99.58 crore; 192 are new AWCs under PM JANMAN.
nfaa986ad742.tq: AP ICDS: 55,607 AWCs, 257 projects (200 rural, 33 urban, 24 tribal).
xs: AP ICDS (2024-25) has **55,607 AWCs** and **257 projects** — option **(2)** is correct.
**47,296** is Bala Sanjeevani's plain-area AWCs; **9,958** AWCs got funds; **192** are new PM JANMAN AWCs.
xa: The 257 projects split into **200 rural**, **33 urban**, **24 tribal**, across **26** districts.
ICDS was launched on **2 Oct 1975**.

n9afdf7ae277.s: Adolescents aged 10–19 years receive weekly iron and folic acid supplementation under which intervention?
n9afdf7ae277.x: Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation, abbreviated WIFS, covers adolescents aged 10–19 years under Anaemia Mukt Bharat interventions.
n9afdf7ae277.tq: Separate the similarly placed nutrition acronyms by their specific intervention.
xs: **WIFS** gives weekly IFA to adolescents aged **10-19** — option **(2)** is correct.
**NIDDCP** is the iodine programme and **MAA** promotes breastfeeding.
xa: WIFS falls under **Anaemia Mukt Bharat**: **IFA** tablets, deworming, outreach for **6 target groups**.
Anaemia Mukt Bharat dates to **2018**, under Health & FW.

n04e9bd8e774.s: Which symbol represents the FSSAI fortification logo?
n04e9bd8e774.x: The FSSAI fortification logo is represented by the symbol '+F'.
n04e9bd8e774.tq: Test the exact official label rather than a descriptive expansion of the logo.
xs: The FSSAI fortification logo is **"+F"** — option **(2)** is correct.
It marks fortified foods such as the **fortified rice** supplied through **ICDS**, **PM POSHAN** and **TPDS**.
xa: **Double-fortified salt** carries **iodine + iron**.
Fortified rice reached **all TPDS districts** in Phase III (**2023-24**).

n0926ca1d306.s: Double-fortified salt contains which combination of nutrients?
n0926ca1d306.x: Double-fortified salt is fortified with iodine and iron.
n0926ca1d306.tq: Separate the nutrient pair in double-fortified salt from other fortification combinations.
xs: **Double-fortified salt** carries **iodine and iron** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Iron and folic acid** is the **IFA** tablet combination of Anaemia Mukt Bharat, not the salt.
xa: The FSSAI fortification logo is **"+F"**.
**NIDDCP** (**1992**), formerly the Goitre programme (**1962**), tackles iodine deficiency.
Anaemia Mukt Bharat tackles iron deficiency with **IFA** tablets and deworming.

n35323266363.s: The Golden Revolution in India is associated with the period:
n35323266363.x: The horticulture boom during 1991–2003 is known as the Golden Revolution.
n35323266363.tq: Associate the named revolution with its stated time span.
xs: The **Golden Revolution** (horticulture boom) covers **1991-2003** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **Golden Revolution** = horticulture, but **Golden Fibre** = **jute**.
xa: **Silver Fibre** = cotton; **Sweet Revolution** = honey; **Blue** = fisheries; **White** = milk.
**MIDH** (since **2014-15**) is today's horticulture scheme.

ned4b87a8c56.s: Which one of the following is the leading fruit in India by production?
ned4b87a8c56.x: Banana is India's top fruit by production, ahead of mango, apple and grapes.
ned4b87a8c56.tq: Distinguish production ranking from export prominence.
xs: India's top fruit by production is **banana** — option **(3)** is correct.
Mango, apple and grapes rank below it.
xa: AP sent **32,000 MT** of bananas to the Gulf on **8** refrigerated trains from **Tadipatri**.
Banana is part of the **Rayalaseema** horticulture hub.
Export mango varieties: **Alphonso**, **Kesar**, **Banganapalli** and **Totapuri**.

nf84d21b3f20.s: The leading egg-producing State in India is:
nf84d21b3f20.x: Andhra Pradesh leads (18.37%), followed by Tamil Nadu; India is 2nd in the world in egg output.
xa: Other top egg States: **Telangana**, **West Bengal**, **Karnataka**.
AP produced **2,548.74 crore eggs** (2023-24) — **1st in eggs**.
⚠ AP = **1st** in eggs but only **7th** in milk.

n0f61b175eff.s: India's present position in global milk production and its approximate share of world output are:
n0f61b175eff.x: India is the world's number-one milk producer and accounts for approximately 25 per cent of global milk output.
n0f61b175eff.tq: Link the rank with the corresponding global share.
xs: India is **No. 1** in milk with about **25 per cent** of world output — option **(3) First** is correct.
Some notes give the share as **24.76%**.
xa: Per capita availability: **471 g/day**.
Top States: **Uttar Pradesh (15.66%)**, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra.
⚠ Older notes give **190 MT** and **394 g** — stale.

nfb28c83c4c8.s: The Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) functions under the Ministry of:
