nfb28c83c4c8.x: MPEDA, headquartered at Kochi, is the apex body for marine exports under the Ministry of Commerce.
xa: ⚠ **MPEDA** is under **Commerce**, not the Department of Fisheries (APPSC-GS 2019).
Agri exports (2024-25) hit a record **$51.9 billion** = **11.86%** of merchandise exports.

n565cec32eaf.s: India occupies which position in the production of silk, and what distinction is associated with its silk production?
o: First; it produces only one variety of silk
Second; it is the only country producing all five varieties of silk
Second; it produces only the mulberry variety
Third; it is the only country producing three varieties of silk
n565cec32eaf.x: India is the second-largest silk producer and is identified as the only country producing all five varieties of silk.
n565cec32eaf.tq: Combine the rank and the associated distinction instead of treating them as separate clues.
xs: India is the **second** largest silk producer and the **only country** producing **all five varieties of silk** — option **(2)** is correct.
The five: **mulberry**, **tropical tasar**, **oak tasar**, **eri**, **muga**.
xa: Mulberry = **Karnataka**; tasar = **Jharkhand**; muga & eri = **Assam**.
AP is the **2nd largest raw silk producer** (**61,394 MT** cocoons, 2024-25).

n099d24f9bee.s: Which State is the largest producer of fruits in India?
n099d24f9bee.x: Andhra Pradesh leads India in fruit production; it also leads in shrimp, oil palm and eggs. Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka are not first in fruit.
n099d24f9bee.tq: Identify the State rank and retain the associated national share.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** leads in fruit — option **(1)** is correct.
AP leads in **shrimp**, **fruit**, **oil palm** and **eggs**.
xa: AP is **1st** in eggs and oil palm, **2nd** in sheep and poultry numbers.
AP horticulture: **46.43 lakh acres**, **406.38 lakh MT**.
**Banana** is India's top fruit by production.

n32be88d5036.s: Andhra Pradesh ranks ____ among States in milk production.
n32be88d5036.x: AP is seventh in milk production (India is first); its principal national lead is in aquaculture.
xa: AP's milk fell **9.41%**; it was **5th** on 2022-23 figures.
India's milk share is about **25%** of world output; top State **UP (15.66%)**.

n0a8241e5a9c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's horticulture sector?
o: It contributes about half of agricultural GVA
It exceeded foodgrain output of 357.73 million tonnes
It uses less than 14% of the cropped area
Its output in 2024-25 was 367.72 million tonnes
n0a8241e5a9c.x: Horticulture contributes about 33% (one-third) of agricultural GVA, not half.
xa: Older 2026 notes put the GVA share at **30.4%**.
Top fruit by production: **banana**.
AP horticulture: **46.43 lakh acres**, **406.38 lakh MT** (AP Survey 2025-26).

n5349f96153d.s: Which allied agricultural sub-sector has recorded an annual growth rate of about 9.08% since 2014-15?
n5349f96153d.x: Fisheries has been the fastest-growing allied sub-sector, recording growth of about 9.08% annually since 2014-15.
n5349f96153d.tq: Associate the distinctive growth rate with the correct allied sector.
xs: **Fisheries** is the fastest-growing allied sub-sector at **9.08%** a year since **2014-15** — option **(2)** is correct.
ES 2025-26 puts the decadal rate (FY16-FY25) at **8.8%**.
xa: Output rose **103%**: **95.79 lakh t** (2013-14) → about **195 lakh t**.
**Inland fisheries** give over **75%** of output.
In AP, fishing & aquaculture is the largest allied sub-sector, growing **17.69%**.

n18cce1160d6.s: What proportion of India’s total fish output is contributed by inland fisheries?
n18cce1160d6.x: Inland fisheries contribute more than 75% of India’s total fish output.
n18cce1160d6.tq: Use the broad percentage category rather than an artificially precise figure.
xs: **Inland fisheries** give **more than 75%** of total fish output — option **(2)** is correct.
Some notes rank inland differently, but the over-**75%** share is the stated figure.
xa: Fish output rose **103%** to about **195 lakh t**.
River ranching in the **Ganga** by **ICAR-CIFRI** under **Namami Gange**.

n8e340bff4ea.s: Which is the largest and fastest-growing allied sub-sector in Andhra Pradesh?
n8e340bff4ea.x: Fisheries is AP's largest and fastest-growing allied sub-sector, with 17.69% growth.
xa: AP gives about **29-30%** of India's fish output, mostly **Vannamei** shrimp.
NABARD 2026-27: **₹21,098 crore** to fisheries in AP.

n7766be2b9d0.s: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) has been implemented since:
n7766be2b9d0.x: MIDH is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme running since 2014-15. 2005-06 is the launch year of the National Horticulture Mission, which MIDH later subsumed.
n7766be2b9d0.tq: Distinguish the implementation year of MIDH from the launch year of NHM.
xs: **MIDH** has been a Centrally Sponsored Scheme since **2014-15** — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2023).
**2005-06** is the year of the **NHM**, which MIDH later subsumed.
xa: MIDH also subsumed the **NE/Himalayan horticulture mission**.
The horticulture boom of **1991-2003** is called the **Golden Revolution**.
Horticulture output (**367.72 MT**, 2024-25) now exceeds foodgrains (**357.73 MT**).

n279481a5a0e.s: The Credit Guarantee Scheme for the Livestock Sector was launched by:
o: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying
n279481a5a0e.x: The Credit Guarantee Scheme for the Livestock Sector was launched by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (APPSC-G2 2025). NABARD, RBI and the Ministry of Finance are the usual distractors and are wrong.
n279481a5a0e.tq: Livestock credit guarantee = DAHD, not NABARD/RBI/MoF.
xs: The **Credit Guarantee Scheme for the Livestock Sector** was launched by the **Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-G2 2025).
⚠ Distractors **NABARD**, **RBI** and **MoF** are wrong.
xa: The same department runs **AHIDF** (**2020**) and the **National Livestock Mission**.
**LHDCP** controls disease through **prophylactic vaccination**.

n6fa87864f33.s: Which of the following is covered under the Central Sector component of PMMSY?
o: Production subsidy exclusively for general States
n6fa87864f33.x: The Central Sector component includes training, quarantine, harbour modernisation and data systems.
n6fa87864f33.tq: Match the activity with the correct scheme component.
xs: PMMSY's **Central Sector** component covers **training and capacity building** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is **100%** Centre-funded: training, quarantine, harbour modernisation, data systems.
Production and regulation fall under the **Centrally Sponsored** component instead.
xa: CSS funding: **60:40** general, **90:10** NE/Himalayan, **100%** UTs.
**NFDB** handles training under PMMSY.

o: A Central Sector sub-scheme under PMMSY for formalising fisheries and supporting fisheries micro-enterprises
A fund exclusively for constructing fishing harbours
A Centrally Sponsored scheme for horticultural exports
A programme for inland river ranching under Namami Gange
nba2f7768c0b.x: PM-MKSSY, or Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana, is a Central Sector sub-scheme under PMMSY aimed at formalising the fisheries sector and supporting fisheries micro-enterprises.
nba2f7768c0b.tq: Distinguish a sub-scheme’s purpose from related fisheries programmes.
xs: **PM-MKSSY** is a **Central Sector sub-scheme under PMMSY** for **formalising** fisheries and supporting **micro-enterprises** — option **(1)** is correct.
Fishing harbours fall under **FIDF**; river ranching under **Namami Gange**.
xa: Full name: **Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana**.
All three PYQ statements on it were correct (APPSC-G1 2024).

ne47ef61168b.s: The Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) is primarily associated with the development of:
ne47ef61168b.x: FIDF supports fisheries and aquaculture infrastructure, particularly fishing harbours and landing centres.
ne47ef61168b.tq: Identify the infrastructure-specific fund from its functional area.
xs: **FIDF** funds **fishing harbours and landing centres** — option **(4)** is correct.
Its full name is the **Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund**.
xa: **AHIDF** (**2020**) is the animal husbandry equivalent.
PMMSY's Central Sector part includes **harbour modernisation**.

n09a11f7df35.s: India is the largest producer of turmeric, and the National Turmeric Board is headquartered at:
n09a11f7df35.x: India is the largest producer of turmeric, and the National Turmeric Board is located at Nizamabad.
n09a11f7df35.tq: Match the commodity leadership fact with the Board’s location.
xs: The **National Turmeric Board** is at **Nizamabad** — option **(2)** is correct.
India is the **largest producer** of turmeric.
xa: **NDDB** is at **Anand, Gujarat** (set up **1965**).
**MPEDA** is at **Kochi**, under the Ministry of **Commerce**.

n9523a03b273.s: Operation Flood (1970–1996) was implemented in how many phases?
n9523a03b273.x: It ran in three phases; it was launched by NDDB (1965, Anand) on the Amul model.
xa: It built a **national milk grid** and made India the world's **largest milk producer**.
**White** Revolution = milk.

n3202d910efb.s: The National Beekeeping and Honey Mission, launched in 2020 under Atmanirbhar Bharat, implements the Sweet Revolution through the:
n3202d910efb.x: The National Beekeeping and Honey Mission implements the Sweet Revolution through the National Bee Board.
xs: The **National Beekeeping and Honey Mission** runs the Sweet Revolution through the **National Bee Board** — option **(4)** is correct.
**NFDB** trains under PMMSY and **NDDB** launched Operation Flood — neither runs the honey mission.
xa: The mission was launched in **2020** under **Atmanirbhar Bharat**.
**Sweet Revolution** = honey (apiculture); **Golden Revolution (1991-2003)** = horticulture.
**NDDB** was set up in **1965** at **Anand, Gujarat**.

nf056021e0b1.s: PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana is an umbrella scheme of which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
nf056021e0b1.x: PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana is the umbrella scheme of the Ministry of Food Processing Industries.
nf056021e0b1.tq: Apply the ‘which Ministry’ trap by distinguishing neighbouring ministries.
xs: **PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana** is the umbrella scheme of the **Ministry of Food Processing Industries** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is a food-processing scheme, not one of Commerce, Rural Development or Agriculture.
xa: **Mega Food Parks** follow a **cluster approach** linking farms → processing → markets.
**PMFME** works under **One District One Product (ODOP)**.
Processed food export share (2024-25): "around **23%**" (APPSC-GS 2025 key).

nd068b1822d3.s: The cluster approach adopted under Mega Food Parks primarily seeks to establish a link between:
nd068b1822d3.x: Mega Food Parks use a cluster approach that links farms to processing facilities and then to markets.
nd068b1822d3.tq: Identify the complete value-chain sequence in the scheme.
xs: **Mega Food Parks** use a **cluster approach** linking **farms**, **processing** and **markets** — option **(1)** is correct.
The cluster runs from **farms → processing → markets**, not across banks, schools or transport hubs.
xa: **PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana** is the umbrella scheme of the **Ministry of Food Processing Industries**.
**Operation Greens (TOP)**, **2018**, now covers all fruits and vegetables.
**PMFME** formalises **micro** food-processing units under **ODOP**.

n6925f5443aa.s: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) is associated with which approach?
n6925f5443aa.x: PMFME formalises micro food-processing units under the One District One Product (ODOP) approach.
n6925f5443aa.tq: Discriminate between similar one-unit policy slogans.
xs: **PMFME** formalises **micro food-processing units** under **One District One Product (ODOP)** — option **(1)** is correct.
The other "One ..." labels are not linked to PMFME.
xa: **Mega Food Parks** use a **cluster approach**.
**PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana** is the **MoFPI** umbrella scheme.

n5b69fe5c11c.s: Andhra Pradesh holds which position in coconut production among the rankings cited?
n5b69fe5c11c.x: Andhra Pradesh is 4th in coconut production. It is 1st in oil palm (2.27 lakh ha), so do not confuse the two rankings.
n5b69fe5c11c.tq: Distinguish the coconut rank from the State’s first rank in oil palm and fruit production.
xs: AP is **4th in coconut** — option **(4) Fourth** is correct.
⚠ Do not confuse it with **oil palm**, where AP is **No. 1** (**2.27 lakh ha**).
xa: AP is **1st in eggs** but only **7th in milk**.
AP is **5th in meat** and **2nd** largest raw silk producer.

n7a6d1a3c757.s: Andhra Pradesh's rank among Indian States in raw silk production (2024-25) is:
n7a6d1a3c757.x: AP is the 2nd largest raw silk producer (61,394 MT of cocoons in 2024-25), with its belt around Hindupur (Sri Sathya Sai/Anantapur) and Chittoor. India as a whole is also 2nd in the world. First, third and fifth are wrong.
n7a6d1a3c757.tq: AP = 2nd in raw silk; India = 2nd in world silk.
xs: AP is the **2nd largest raw silk producer** — option **(2) Second** is correct.
It produced **61,394 MT** of cocoons in **2024-25**.
xa: AP's sericulture belt: **Sri Sathya Sai / Anantapur** around **Hindupur**, and **Chittoor**.
India too is the **2nd largest silk producer** in the world.
India is the only country producing **all five silks**.

nc5131a03ee6.s: Which of the following crops or products is NOT included among the horticultural activities identified for the development of Rayalaseema as a horticulture hub?
nc5131a03ee6.x: The identified activities include banana, oil palm, cashew, coconut and Araku coffee. Tea is not included in that list.
nc5131a03ee6.tq: Find the crop outside the stated regional horticulture cluster.
xs: **Tea** is not in the Rayalaseema hub list — option **(3)** is the answer.
The hub covers **banana**, **oil palm**, **cashew**, **coconut** and **Araku coffee**.
xa: **NABARD 2026-27** AP plan: **₹5,313 crore** for horticulture in Rayalaseema and Prakasam.
AP is **No. 1** in oil palm (**2.27 lakh ha**) and **4th** in coconut.
nc5131a03ee6.fixed: Araku coffee is from Araku Valley (ASR district, north coastal AP), not Rayalaseema

nc9e3903d925.s: The main sericulture belt of Andhra Pradesh is associated primarily with:
o: Sri Sathya Sai/Anantapur around Hindupur and Chittoor
nc9e3903d925.x: The principal sericulture belt lies in Sri Sathya Sai/Anantapur, particularly around Hindupur, and in Chittoor.
nc9e3903d925.tq: Identify the precise geographical concentration from a set of nearby districts.
xs: AP's sericulture belt is **Sri Sathya Sai / Anantapur** around **Hindupur**, and **Chittoor** — option **(2)** is correct.
These Rayalaseema districts are named as AP's sericulture belt.
xa: AP is the **2nd largest raw silk producer** (**61,394 MT** cocoons, 2024-25).
**Chittoor** is also AP's top dairy district.
⚠ Mulberry = **Karnataka**; tasar = **Jharkhand**; muga & eri = **Assam**.

n29a578131d0.x: TISCO came in 1907, after the first Bombay cotton mill (1854) and the Rishra jute mill (1855), and before sugar tariff protection (1932).
xa: Some notes date the Bombay cotton mill to **1853**; it was set up by **Cowasjee Nanabhoy**.
**Indian Cement** came in **1914**.
**1900-1947** saw steel, cement, sugar and paper come up.

n7ee4a9edf60.s: The number of industries reserved for the public sector under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, and the number retained under the 1991 policy were, respectively
n7ee4a9edf60.x: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 reserved 17 industries for the public sector, while the 1991 policy reduced the number to 8.
n7ee4a9edf60.tq: Compare the two policy benchmarks and watch for reversal of the figures.
xs: **IPR 1956** reserved **17** industries for the public sector; the **1991 policy** cut this to **8** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (3) reverses the two numbers.
xa: The **Second Plan (1956-61)** pushed heavy and basic industries on the **Nehru-Mahalanobis model**.
After 1991, cheap imports shut many **small units**.

nf7a310972ea.s: Which of the following was NOT a principal factor behind India's industrial deceleration during 1965–80?
nf7a310972ea.x: Wars, droughts, infrastructure bottlenecks and licensing caused the slowdown; import liberalisation was not a feature of that period.
xa: Partial liberalisation came only in the **1980s**, with a recovery of about **7-8%**.
Full liberalisation came from **1991**.

n3254c4b195e.s: The Second Five Year Plan, based on the Mahalanobis model, emphasised:
n3254c4b195e.x: The Second Plan and the Mahalanobis model stressed basic and heavy industries.
xa: **Bhilai**, **Rourkela** and **Durgapur** were set up in the Second Plan.
**IPR 1956** reserved **17** industries for the public sector.

ne8a16bbd2dd.s: In the cotton textile industry, the bulk of cloth is produced by the:
ne8a16bbd2dd.x: Of the mill, powerloom and handloom segments, powerlooms produce the bulk of cloth.
xa: Textiles employ **4.5 crore** directly.
The first successful cotton mill was in **Bombay** (**1854**).

nc7801adadb8.s: Industrial concentration in India is particularly pronounced in which group of States?
o: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh
nc7801adadb8.x: Industrial activity is regionally concentrated in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, while eastern and central States lag behind.
nc7801adadb8.tq: Identify the established industrial cluster and contrast it with lagging regions.
xs: Industry is concentrated in **Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Eastern and central** States lag.
xa: Highest capital intensity in manufacturing (2017-18): **Madhya Pradesh** (MPPSC 2025).
PSU townships such as **Bhilai, Rourkela, Bokaro** were meant for regional balance.

nde061c5a921.s: Which of the following best shows 'jobless growth' in Indian factories during 2011-2023?
o: Direct factory employment rose from 47% to 61% of the workforce
The share of directly employed workers fell from 61% to 47%, and contract workers now make up about 42%
Contract workers fell to about 4% of the factory workforce
Factory employment grew faster than factory output
nde061c5a921.x: Directly employed workers fell from 61% to 47% of the factory workforce (2011-2023), and contract workers now make up about 42%. Option A reverses the trend, C understates contract labour, and D is the opposite of jobless growth.
xs: **Jobless growth**: direct factory employment fell from **61%** to **47%** (**2011-2023**); contract workers are now about **42%** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the trend; (3) understates contract labour.
xa: Regular CPSE employment fell by **30,000** in **2024**, replaced by contract workers.
About **57 lakh** jobs were added in organised manufacturing (2015-16 to 2024-25).

n7110d0c5491.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of early public-sector industrial enterprises mentioned in the context of India's industrial base?
o: Bombay Dyeing, Raymond, Grasim and Lakshmi Mills
ONGC, TISCO, Bombay Dyeing and Hindustan Cables
Sindri Fertilizers, Chittaranjan Locomotives, Integral Coach Factory and HMT
TISCO, Bengal Iron Works, Indian Cement and Raymond
n7110d0c5491.x: Sindri Fertilizers, Chittaranjan Locomotives, Integral Coach Factory, HMT, ITI and Hindustan Cables formed part of the early public-sector industrial base.
n7110d0c5491.tq: Eliminate groups containing privately established or unrelated enterprises.
xs: **Sindri Fertilizers, Chittaranjan Locomotives, Integral Coach Factory and HMT** were all early public-sector units — option **(3)** is correct.
**Bombay Dyeing**, **Raymond**, **TISCO** and **Grasim** were private firms.
xa: The early base also had **Hindustan Aircraft**, **ITI**, **Hindustan Cables** and a **penicillin unit**.
**PDIL** carries the **Sindri** lineage in fertiliser design.

ne96cce52366.s: The expression ‘commanding heights’ in the context of India’s public sector primarily refers to control over
ne96cce52366.x: The public sector occupied the commanding heights by entering capital-heavy and long-gestation sectors that private capital was reluctant to undertake.
ne96cce52366.tq: Identify the precise economic meaning of a policy expression.
xs: 'Commanding heights' meant **capital-intensive**, **long-gestation** sectors private capital avoided — option **(1)** is correct.
It did not mean small-scale consumer, export-service or farm markets.
xa: Examples: **Coal India** (coal), **ONGC** (oil), **BHEL** (heavy engineering), **RCF, FCI** (fertilisers).
**IPR 1956** reserved **17** industries for the public sector.

ndfed10a7c8d.s: Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited contributed significantly to the transformation of which place into a heavy-industry and port hub?
ndfed10a7c8d.x: RINL helped transform Visakhapatnam into a major heavy-industry and port hub.
ndfed10a7c8d.tq: Match the enterprise with the location of its regional-industrial impact.
xs: **RINL** turned **Visakhapatnam** (Vizag) into a heavy-industry and port hub — option **(3)** is correct.
**Neyveli** = **NLC**; **Bokaro** and **Bhilai** = steel townships.
xa: RINL was a **USSR** collaboration; foundation stone **20 Jan 1971**, agreement **12 Jun 1979**.
AP angle: manufacturing is about **11%** of GSDP.

n4de84aac592.s: Which of the following was the first textile unit of its kind in the Madras Presidency?
o: Munagala Raja's textile unit at Vijayawada
n4de84aac592.x: Munagala Raja's textile unit at Vijayawada, established in June 1906, was the first of its kind in the Madras Presidency.
n4de84aac592.tq: Link the regional industrial milestone with its founder and location.
xs: **Munagala Raja's textile unit** at **Vijayawada** (**June 1906**) was the first of its kind in **Madras Presidency** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Bombay Dyeing** and **Raymond** were not in Madras Presidency; **Lakshmi Mills** came later, in **1910**.
xa: The first successful cotton mill was in **Bombay** (**1854**).
**Bombay Dyeing** dates to **1879**, **Raymond** to **1925**.

n23d6e251b76.s: The first public-sector steel unit in India was
n23d6e251b76.x: Visvesvaraya Iron & Steel Works at Bhadravati was the first public-sector steel unit in India.
n23d6e251b76.tq: Use the historical-priority clue and distinguish the early unit from the Second Plan plants.
xs: The first public-sector steel unit was **Visvesvaraya Iron & Steel Works, Bhadravati** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Rourkela** was the first **integrated** PSU steel plant; **Bhilai** and **Bokaro** came with the USSR.
xa: Rourkela had **1 MT** capacity, with **West Germany**.
**TISCO** (private) was incorporated in **1907** at Jamshedpur.

nbba76e1ff97.s: BHEL's first plant at Bhopal was established with the collaboration of
nbba76e1ff97.x: BHEL's first plant at Bhopal was built with British collaboration, specifically involving AEI.
nbba76e1ff97.tq: Apply the foreign-collaboration trap by separating BHEL units from steel plants.
xs: BHEL **Bhopal** was built with **Britain** through **AEI** — option **(3)** is correct (MPPSC 2024).
**Haridwar** = USSR; **Tiruchirappalli** and **Hyderabad** = Czechoslovakia.
xa: BHEL makes **boilers, turbines, transformers**.
BHEL is a **Maharatna** CPSE.

n4b3f7f9c9ae.s: The three public-sector steel plants established during the Second Plan were
n4b3f7f9c9ae.x: The Second Plan period, 1956–61, saw the establishment of Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur with foreign assistance.
n4b3f7f9c9ae.tq: Recall the standard three-plant Second Plan group.
xs: The Second Plan (**1956-61**) plants were **Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Bhadravati** was the first PSU steel unit; **Bokaro** and **Visakhapatnam** came later.
xa: Bhilai = **USSR**; Rourkela = **West Germany**; Durgapur = **UK**.
**Bhilai, Rourkela, Bokaro** grew as public-sector townships.

n4e8269c4ed0.s: The concept of premature deindustrialisation, associated with Dani Rodrik, means that
o: manufacturing's share peaks at a lower income level than in early industrialising countries
industrial employment rises continuously after reaching high income
services remain smaller than agriculture at every income level
n4e8269c4ed0.x: Premature deindustrialisation occurs when manufacturing's share of output or employment peaks at a lower income level than it did in early industrialisers.
n4e8269c4ed0.tq: Distinguish a lower-income peak from the complete disappearance of manufacturing.
xs: **Premature deindustrialisation** (**Dani Rodrik**): **manufacturing**'s share **peaks** at a **lower income** than in early industrialisers — option **(1)** is correct.
It does not mean manufacturing vanishes or that employment keeps rising.
xa: After 1991, **cheap imports** shut many small units.
**Services**, not industry, gained most GDP share after 1991.

n7902c5555df.s: Which sector gained the most share of India's GDP after 1991?
n7902c5555df.x: Services gained the most GDP share after 1991, while post-LPG industrial growth favoured capital- and skill-intensive sectors.
xa: ES 2025-26: medium- and high-tech manufacturing share is **46.3%**.
About **57 lakh** jobs were added in organised manufacturing (2015-16 to 2024-25).

n035000ac7ab.s: Industry accounts for approximately what share of Gross Value Added in India?
n035000ac7ab.x: Industry accounts for approximately 25.3 per cent of GVA. The 13–14 per cent figure relates to the public sector's contribution to GDP, while 17–18 per cent refers to manufacturing's real-term share.
n035000ac7ab.tq: Separate similar percentages by linking each figure to its correct economic aggregate.
xs: Industry is about **25.3 per cent** of GVA — option **(4)** is correct.
**13-14%** is the public sector's share of GDP; **17-18%** is manufacturing's real share.
xa: Real industry GVA grows at about **7%**.
Industry GVA grew **7.0%** in H1 FY26.

n3747e7f72e7.s: Why did manufacturing's share of nominal GVA decline despite its real-term share remaining broadly stable?
o: Because the private sector withdrew from manufacturing
Because construction was excluded from GVA
Because manufacturing output ceased to grow after 1991
n3747e7f72e7.x: The decline in manufacturing's nominal GVA share was attributed to relative price changes. In real terms, manufacturing's share remained broadly steady at 17–18 per cent.
n3747e7f72e7.tq: Distinguish nominal changes caused by prices from real changes in output.
xs: Manufacturing's **nominal** GVA share fell only because of **relative price** changes — option **(1)** is correct.
Its **real** share stayed steady at **17-18%**, so output did not stop growing.
xa: Manufacturing GVA grew **9.13%** in Q2 FY26.
Industry as a whole is about **25.3%** of GVA.

n8c16764077f.s: India was the world's second-largest crude steel producer in 2024, with production of
n8c16764077f.x: India produced 149.4 million tonnes of crude steel in 2024 and ranked second after China, which produced 1,005.1 million tonnes.
n8c16764077f.tq: Distinguish production from capacity and from the leading country's output.
xs: India produced **149.4 million tonnes** of crude steel in **2024**, 2nd largest — option **(4)** is correct.
**1,005.1 MT** is China's output; **200.33 MT** is India's capacity; **93** is the % of coal-based ironmaking.
xa: India depends on **imported coking coal**, its main imported input.
SAIL plants **Bhilai**, **Rourkela**, **Durgapur** date to the **Second Plan**.

ne3f9fea316c.s: The principal cause of capacity under-utilisation in Indian industry is
ne3f9fea316c.x: Deficient basic infrastructure is identified as the main cause of capacity under-utilisation, although weak demand also contributes.
ne3f9fea316c.tq: Select the primary cause while distinguishing it from a secondary contributing factor.
xs: The main cause of capacity under-utilisation is **deficient basic infrastructure** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2007).
**Weak demand** also adds: the Manufacturing PMI in **Jul 2026** was the lowest since **Aug 2021**.
xa: Other problems: **regional concentration**, **jobless growth**, **import dependence**, **low R&D**.
Infrastructure bottlenecks also drove the **1965-80** slowdown.
ne3f9fea316c.fixed: stem referred to 'the material'; APPSC 2007 wording

n19b31df2683.s: As per 2017-18 data, which State had the highest capital intensity in manufacturing?
n19b31df2683.x: Madhya Pradesh had the highest capital intensity in manufacturing in 2017-18 (MPPSC 2025). Maharashtra, Gujarat and Tamil Nadu are where industry is concentrated, which is a different point from capital intensity.
n19b31df2683.tq: Capital intensity top (2017-18) = MP; concentration = Maha, Guj, TN, Kar.
xs: **Madhya Pradesh** had the highest capital intensity in manufacturing (**2017-18**) — option **(3)** is correct (MPPSC 2025).
**Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu** are where industry is **concentrated** — a different point.
xa: Eastern and central States lag in industry.
Contract workers are now **42%** of the factory workforce.

n53b7e3c2019.s: In FY 2023, which use-based groups of the IIP recorded the highest growth?
n53b7e3c2019.x: In FY 2023, the capital goods and infrastructure/construction goods indices grew the most (BPSC 2024). Primary goods had the highest weight in the 2011-12 series, but they were not the fastest-growing group. The other pairs did not lead.
n53b7e3c2019.tq: FY23 IIP leaders: capital goods + infra/construction goods.
xs: In **FY 2023**, the **capital goods** and **infrastructure/construction goods** indices grew most — option **(2)** is correct (BPSC 2024).
**Primary goods** had the highest **weight** (**34%**) in the 2011-12 series, but did not grow fastest.
xa: **Capital goods** had the lowest weight (**8.22%**) in that series.
In **Feb 2026**, non-core manufacturing and capital goods outpaced core sectors.

n46b05f790d7.s: The Index of Industrial Production covers mining, manufacturing and:
n46b05f790d7.x: IIP covers mining, manufacturing and electricity; agriculture, services and construction lie outside it.
xa: It is compiled monthly by the **NSO (MoSPI)**.
The base moved from **2011-12** to **2022-23** from **1 June 2026**.

ncde69c31f4c.s: The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is compiled monthly by the:
o: National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
ncde69c31f4c.x: The IIP is compiled monthly by the National Statistical Office under MoSPI. The NSO replaced the earlier Central Statistical Office in this role.
ncde69c31f4c.tq: Identify the present compiling agency while distinguishing it from the former agency.
xs: The IIP is compiled monthly by the **National Statistical Office** under **MoSPI** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was formerly done by the **CSO**.
⚠ The **Index of Eight Core Industries** is compiled by **DPIIT** (Office of the Economic Adviser), not the IIP.
xa: The new **Index of Services Production** (base **2024-25**) was first released on **14 July 2026**.

n79c7d83135f.s: With effect from 1 June 2026, the base year of the IIP was shifted from:
n79c7d83135f.x: The new IIP series shifted the base year from 2011-12 to 2022-23, effective 1 June 2026. Readings before June 2026 use the old base.
n79c7d83135f.tq: Test the direction and effective date of a base-year revision.
xs: The IIP base moved from **2011-12 to 2022-23**, effective **1 June 2026** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Any IIP reading from before June 2026 is on the old base.
xa: The new basket has **1,042 products** in **463** item groups (old: **407** items).
The **WPI** base was revised to **2022-23** at the same time.
This was the **10th** revision.

nd867e6d4570.s: The Index of Services Production, with base year 2024-25, is best described as:
o: A supplementary index of agricultural production
A measure of wholesale price inflation in services
A replacement for the IIP covering only manufacturing
The services counterpart of the IIP
nd867e6d4570.x: The Index of Services Production is the services counterpart of the IIP. Its first release was scheduled for 14 July 2026 with a 60-day lag.
nd867e6d4570.tq: Discriminate between two similarly named production indices by their sectoral coverage.
xs: The **Index of Services Production** (base **2024-25**) is the **services counterpart of the IIP** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is not about agriculture, prices or manufacturing; services lie **outside** the IIP.
xa: Its first release came on **14 July 2026**, with a **60-day** lag.
The IIP itself was rebased to **2022-23** from **1 June 2026**.
IIP is compiled by the **NSO (MoSPI)**.

ncb500eb4322.s: The MSMED Amendment Bill, 2026, as described in the current policy context, requires every CPSE to settle MSME invoices through
ncb500eb4322.x: The 2026 amendment requires every CPSE to settle MSME invoices on the Trade Receivables Discounting System, or TReDS.
ncb500eb4322.tq: Match the current legal requirement with the exact institutional platform.
xs: The **MSMED (Amendment) Bill 2026** makes every CPSE settle MSME invoices on **TReDS** — option **(3)** is correct.
It was passed by the **Rajya Sabha** (**Aug 2026**).
**DPE schedules** set CEO pay and **BRPSE** advised on sick CPSEs — neither handles invoices.
xa: Budget **2026-27** proposes **REITs** to recycle CPSE real estate.
There are **250+ operating CPSEs**.

n34e815d74b8.s: In the 2011-12 series of the IIP, which use-based category had the highest and which had the lowest weight respectively?
n34e815d74b8.x: Primary goods had the highest weight at about 34 per cent, while capital goods had the lowest weight at 8.22 per cent in the 2011-12 series.
n34e815d74b8.tq: Pair the maximum and minimum values instead of considering either value in isolation.
xs: In the 2011-12 series, **primary goods** weighed most (**34%**) and **capital goods** least (**8.22%**) — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (4) reverses them.
xa: In **FY 2023**, **capital goods** and **infrastructure/construction goods** indices grew most (BPSC 2024).
New-series weights: **manufacturing 76.1%**, mining **11.1%**, electricity and gas **10.9%**.

n557ce5d0396.s: Which of the following has been added to the new IIP series?
o: Gas supply, water supply, sewerage and waste management
n557ce5d0396.x: The new series adds gas, water, sewerage and waste management, minor and rare-earth minerals, and shows renewable electricity separately.
xa: New weights: manufacturing **76.1%**, mining **11.1%**, electricity and gas **10.9%**, water supply **2.02%**.
Weights rest on each sector's share of **GVA in 2022-23**.

n7eda5747391.s: In the new IIP series, sectoral weights are based on each sector's share of:
o: Gross Domestic Product at current prices in 2022-23
n7eda5747391.x: The weights in the new IIP series are derived from the sectoral shares of Gross Value Added in 2022-23.
n7eda5747391.tq: Distinguish the statistical basis of weights from other macroeconomic aggregates.
xs: New IIP weights are based on each sector's share of **Gross Value Added in 2022-23** — option **(3)** is correct.
GDP, employment and exports are not the weighting basis.
xa: Manufacturing **76.1%**, mining **11.1%**, electricity and gas **10.9%**, water supply **2.02%**.
The base year itself is **2022-23**, effective **1 June 2026**.

nf0997021454.s: The revised series of the Index of Core Industries has base year:
nf0997021454.x: The revised ICI (Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT) uses 2022-23 as base and adds iron ore at 4.905% weight.
xa: The revision came in **July 2026**, with effect from **April 2023**.
⚠ IIP = **NSO (MoSPI)**; ICI = **DPIIT**.

n06f0f9082e7.s: Under the revised 2022-23 series of the Index of Core Industries, which one of the following has the highest weight?
n06f0f9082e7.x: Electricity carries the highest weight in the revised series, at 30.93 per cent. Refinery products have the second-highest weight at 22.57 per cent.
n06f0f9082e7.tq: Compare the revised weights rather than relying on the older series.
xs: In the 2022-23 series **electricity** weighs most (**30.93%**) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Refinery products** come second (**22.57**), then **steel** (**17.58**) and **crude oil** (**7.43**).
xa: In the old series, **refinery products** led (**28.04%**), electricity was second (**19.85%**).
**Fertilisers** remain the lowest (**2.73** new; **2.63** old).

n17f48d79f75.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the number of industries and the combined IIP weight under the revised 2022-23 series of the Index of Core Industries?
n17f48d79f75.x: The revised series contains nine core industries and their combined weight in the IIP is 32.88 per cent. Iron ore was added to the earlier list of eight industries.
n17f48d79f75.tq: Split the option into two parts and verify both the count and the percentage.
xs: The revised ICI has **9 industries** with a combined IIP weight of **32.88 per cent** — option **(4)** is correct.
The old series had **8** industries weighing **40.27%**.
xa: **Iron ore** is the ninth, newest core industry (weight **4.905%**).
In **Jun 2026**, the new-series ICI grew **5%**, driven by iron ore (+**43.9%**).

Disputes go to the **MSE Facilitation Council**.
**MSME Samadhaan** (**2017**) takes cases under the **45-day** rule.

n4716df97d75.s: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 identified the handicaps of small industries as relating to:
o: Raw materials, finance, marketing and technology
n4716df97d75.x: IPR 1948 identified difficulties relating to raw materials, finance, marketing and technology.
xa: Today's problems still include a **credit gap**, **obsolete technology** and **weak marketing**.
Others: **delayed payments**, compliance burden, **skill deficit**.

n8e8c9d16552.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a major problem faced by MSMEs?
o: Excessive access to low-cost collateral-free credit
n8e8c9d16552.x: The identified problems include obsolete technology, weak marketing and exports, compliance burden, skill deficit and costly or inadequate credit; excessive access to cheap credit is not a problem listed here.
n8e8c9d16552.tq: Use the ‘not a problem’ format to separate a real constraint from its opposite.
xs: **Excessive access to low-cost collateral-free credit** is not a problem — option **(1)** is the answer.
The real issue is a **credit gap**: little collateral and **costly credit**.
**Weak marketing and exports**, **skill deficit** and **obsolete technology** are listed problems.
xa: Other problems: **delayed payments** and **compliance burden**.
**CGTMSE** gives **collateral-free credit guarantee** cover.

n209954fdc5d.s: SIDBI co-founded the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) in:
n209954fdc5d.x: CGTMSE was co-founded by the Ministry of MSME and SIDBI in 2000 to provide credit guarantee support for collateral-free lending.
n209954fdc5d.tq: Distinguish the year of SIDBI’s establishment from the later year of CGTMSE’s formation.
xs: **CGTMSE** was set up in **2000** by the **Ministry of MSME** and **SIDBI** — option **(3)** is correct.
**1990** is SIDBI's own founding year.
xa: It gives **collateral-free credit guarantee** cover to lenders.
Its corpus is shared **Government : SIDBI = 4:1**.

n8e8db636bd6.s: The corpus contribution ratio between the Government and SIDBI in CGTMSE is:
n8e8db636bd6.x: The corpus of CGTMSE is shared between the Government and SIDBI in the ratio of 4:1.
n8e8db636bd6.tq: Recall the exact institutional contribution ratio rather than the scheme’s broad objective.
xs: The CGTMSE corpus is shared **Government : SIDBI = 4:1** — option **(1)** is correct.
CGTMSE was set up in **2000**.
xa: Budget **2026-27** adds **CGTMSE** guarantees for **TReDS** discounting.
**MUDRA** ceiling: **₹20 lakh** (**Tarun Plus**).

nc2abf48e7c0.s: TReDS platforms such as RXIL, M1xchange and Invoicemart, which discount MSME receivables, are regulated by:
nc2abf48e7c0.x: TReDS platforms are RBI-regulated and discount MSME receivables owed by corporates, government and PSUs.
xa: TReDS has run since **2017**.
Budget **2026-27**: **all CPSE purchases from MSMEs** to settle on TReDS, plus a **GeM-TReDS** link.

n20478ddf73d.s: With reference to TReDS, Budget 2026-27 announced which of the following?
o: TReDS platforms will be regulated by SEBI instead of the RBI
All CPSE purchases from MSMEs are to be settled on TReDS, with CGTMSE guarantees for TReDS discounting
TReDS will be merged with the MSME Samadhaan portal
Only private corporates will be allowed to use TReDS
n20478ddf73d.x: Budget 2026-27 mandated settlement of all CPSE purchases from MSMEs on TReDS, CGTMSE guarantees for TReDS discounting, a GeM-TReDS link and receivables as asset-backed securities. TReDS platforms remain RBI-regulated, are not merged with Samadhaan (a delayed-payment portal), and serve government and PSU buyers as well as corporates.
n20478ddf73d.tq: Budget 2026-27: CPSE-MSME bills via TReDS + CGTMSE cover + GeM link.
xs: Budget 2026-27 said **all CPSE purchases from MSMEs** are to be settled on **TReDS**, with **CGTMSE guarantees for TReDS discounting** — so option **(2)** is correct.
TReDS platforms are **RBI-regulated** (since **2017**), not SEBI-regulated.
**MSME Samadhaan** (2017) is a separate delayed-payment portal; TReDS also serves **government and PSU** buyers, not only private corporates.
xa: The Budget also proposed a **GeM-TReDS link** and treating receivables as **asset-backed securities**.
TReDS platforms include **RXIL**, **M1xchange** and **Invoicemart**.
**GeM:** **Rs 18.4 lakh crore** GMV with **11 lakh+** MSEs (Aug 2026).

na0efaf5d5d1.s: Which one of the following is a feature of Udyam Registration?
o: It is operated only for enterprises receiving PMEGP subsidy.
It is restricted to large manufacturing companies.
It is a paid, paper-based registration requiring physical verification in every case.
It is a free, paperless, self-declaration portal linked with GeM, income tax, GST and TReDS.
na0efaf5d5d1.x: Udyam Registration, introduced in 2020, is free, paperless and based on self-declaration; it is linked with GeM, income tax, GST and TReDS.
na0efaf5d5d1.tq: Identify the exact administrative features of a digital registration system.
xs: **Udyam Registration** is a **free, paperless, self-declaration portal linked with GeM, income tax, GST and TReDS** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is not paid or paper-based, is not restricted to large companies, and is not limited to **PMEGP** beneficiaries.
xa: Udyam Registration began in **2020**; **6.63 crore** MSMEs registered between **1 July 2020** and **31 July 2025**.
**Micro units** form **95.88%** of Udyam registrations.
Of the registrations, **2.72 crore** are informal micro enterprises; **46.7 lakh+** are women-owned (Aug 2025).

n21f2cc0ac76.s: The RAMP programme for strengthening MSME institutions, market access and credit is supported by:
n21f2cc0ac76.x: RAMP is a World Bank-supported programme to strengthen Centre-State MSME institutions, market access and credit.
xa: **ECLGS 5.0** (**May 2026**) gives a **100% guarantee** to units hit by the **West Asia crisis**.
**MSE-CDP** funds cluster common facilities and industrial parks; **SFURTI** regenerates traditional-industry clusters.
**CGTMSE** has given collateral-free credit guarantee cover since **2000**.

n1b02301eeec.s: In the case of a non-individual enterprise under Stand-Up India, eligibility requires that at least what shareholding and control be with SC/ST persons or women?
n1b02301eeec.x: A non-individual enterprise qualifies when at least 51 per cent of its shareholding and control is held by SC/ST persons or women.
n1b02301eeec.tq: Use a percentage threshold to distinguish eligibility conditions.
xs: A non-individual enterprise qualifies under **Stand-Up India** if at least **51 per cent** shareholding and control is with **SC/ST** persons or **women** — so option **(3)** is correct.
51% is the majority-control threshold the scheme fixes; 26, 33 and 75 are not the notes' figure.
xa: Stand-Up India was launched in **April 2016**.
It supports **greenfield** enterprises only.
⚠ **PMEGP** gives women up to **35%** capital subsidy — a different scheme.

n2b11392804a.s: Stand-Up India, launched in April 2016, supports which kind of enterprise?
n2b11392804a.x: Stand-Up India supports only greenfield (new) enterprises promoted by SC/ST persons or women. It is not a rehabilitation scheme for sick units, does not fund expansion of existing units, and has nothing to do with disinvestment of PSEs.
n2b11392804a.tq: Stand-Up India = greenfield only; 51% SC/ST or women.
xs: **Stand-Up India** (**April 2016**) supports **greenfield enterprises only** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is not for sick-unit rehabilitation, expansion of existing units or disinvestment of public enterprises.
xa: Non-individual enterprises qualify if **51%** shareholding and control are with **SC/ST** persons or **women**.
**YSR Navodayam** (**2019**) in AP restructured stressed MSME loans — the rehabilitation-type scheme.
**PMEGP** gives a margin-money subsidy for **new micro-enterprises**, run by **KVIC**.

o: 12 trades, with credit up to ₹3 lakh at 7% interest
24 trades, with credit up to ₹5 lakh at 4% interest
18 trades, with credit up to ₹10 lakh at 5% interest
18 trades, with credit up to ₹3 lakh at 5% interest
n518c2910198.x: PM Vishwakarma covers 18 trades and provides credit up to ₹3 lakh at 5 per cent interest.
xa: Other components: **ID card**, skilling with **Rs 500/day** stipend, toolkit incentive up to **Rs 15,000**, marketing support.
It is a scheme of the **Ministry of MSME**.
**PMMY (MUDRA)** tiers: **Shishu**, **Kishor**, **Tarun**, **Tarun Plus**.

n29b17084a3b.s: Under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs Order, 2012, central ministries and CPSEs are required to procure what minimum share of their annual procurement from MSEs?
n29b17084a3b.x: The mandatory procurement share from MSEs is 25 per cent; it was raised from 20 per cent in 2018.
n29b17084a3b.tq: Test the current mandatory share against its earlier level.
xs: Central ministries and CPSEs must buy at least **25 per cent** of annual procurement from MSEs — so option **(3)** is correct.
**20 per cent** was the earlier mandate, raised to 25% in **2018**.
xa: Sub-targets: **4%** from **SC/ST-owned** MSEs and **3%** from **women-owned** MSEs.
**Achieved** in FY26 (to **1 Dec 2025**): **44.76%**, above the mandate.
**GeM:** **Rs 18.4 lakh crore** GMV; **11 lakh+** MSEs.

nb0d67271ae3.s: Under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs, the sub-target for procurement from women-owned MSEs is:
nb0d67271ae3.x: The sub-targets are 3 per cent from women-owned MSEs and 4 per cent from SC/ST-owned MSEs.
xa: Overall mandate: **25%** of annual procurement (raised from **20%** in **2018**).
Order issued as the **Public Procurement Policy for MSEs Order, 2012**.
Actual MSE procurement reached **44.76%** in FY26.

n1c5b835c390.s: A revamped MSME Policy introduced in Andhra Pradesh in 2026 particularly adds incentives for:
n1c5b835c390.x: The revamped Andhra Pradesh MSME Policy 2026 adds incentives for women-led MSMEs.
n1c5b835c390.tq: Test the beneficiary group of a recently introduced policy measure.
xs: AP's revamped **MSME Policy 2026** adds incentives for **women-led MSMEs** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The policy is for MSMEs, not multinationals, state corporations or export-only PSEs.
xa: The earlier **AP MSME & Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0** covers **2024-29** (**G.O.Ms.No.69**, **26 Oct 2024**).
AP has about **20.77 lakh** MSMEs, mostly in **services**.
The **single window** for MSMEs in AP is run by **DICs**.

n73577835f26.s: Udyam Abhilasha is best described as:
o: A KVIC subsidy programme for traditional artisans launched in 2008
A World Bank credit programme for CPSEs launched in 2020
A SIDBI entrepreneurship-awareness campaign launched in 2021 in aspirational districts
A GeM procurement platform launched in 2016
n73577835f26.x: Udyam Abhilasha is a SIDBI entrepreneurship-awareness campaign of 2021 aimed at aspirational districts.
n73577835f26.tq: Match the programme with its implementing institution, year and target area.
xs: **Udyam Abhilasha** is a **SIDBI entrepreneurship-awareness campaign** launched in **2021** in **aspirational districts** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **KVIC** scheme formed in **2008** is **PMEGP**, not Udyam Abhilasha.
**RAMP** is the **World Bank**-supported programme; Stand-Up India (not GeM) dates from **2016**.
xa: **SIDBI** was set up on **2 April 1990** under the **SIDBI Act, 1989**, HQ **Lucknow**.
SIDBI is the implementing agency of **PM SVANidhi**.
⚠ **Udyam Abhilasha** = SIDBI (2021); **PMEGP** = KVIC (2008).

n8b3e236dc6b.s: The Andhra Pradesh MSME & Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 covers which period?
n8b3e236dc6b.x: AP MSME & Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 covers 2024-29 and was issued through G.O.Ms.No.69 dated 26 October 2024. 2019 is the year of YSR Navodayam, and 2026 brought a revamped MSME Policy for women-led units, not a 2026-31 policy.
xs: AP **MSME & Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0** covers **2024-29** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was issued as **G.O.Ms.No.69** dated **26 Oct 2024**.
**2019** is the year of **YSR Navodayam**; **2026** brought a revamped policy for **women-led** MSMEs, not a 2026-31 plan.
xa: AP follows the same national MSME definition (**APSES 2024-25**).
AP MSME base: about **20.77 lakh** units, **48%** services.
In AP, **MSE-CDP** is implemented through **APIIC**.

n7d3bcaf34d9.s: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 was announced by:
n7d3bcaf34d9.x: The 1948 Resolution was announced by Industry Minister Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee.
n7d3bcaf34d9.tq: Use the person-policy association as the deciding clue.
xs: **IPR 1948** was announced by Industry Minister **Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**P.V. Narasimha Rao** (PM) and **Manmohan Singh** (FM) are linked to the **New Industrial Policy, 24 July 1991**, not 1948.
xa: IPR 1948 was announced on **6 April 1948** and was the **first industrial policy of independent India**.
It laid the foundation of a **mixed economy**.
Sequence: Statement of Industrial Policy, **1945** → **IPR 1948** → **IDR Act, 1951**.

n777dc75e165.s: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948 laid the foundation for which economic system in India?
n777dc75e165.x: The 1948 Resolution defined roles for both the public and private sectors and thereby laid the foundation of a mixed economy.
n777dc75e165.tq: Identify the economic system from the stated public-private division of roles.
xs: **IPR 1948** laid the foundation of a **mixed economy** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It defined roles for **both public and private sectors**, so it was neither purely capitalist nor purely socialist/command.
xa: Key sectors (**arms**, **atomic energy**, **railways**) were reserved for the State.
**18** centrally regulated industries stayed private under Central regulation; the residual sector was open to **private and co-operative** enterprise.
⚠ "**Socialist pattern of society**" is the goal behind **IPR 1956** (Avadi, **1955**).

nb89d5118f1a.s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948, shipbuilding was placed in the:
nb89d5118f1a.x: Coal, mineral oils, iron and steel, aircraft, shipbuilding and telephone/telegraph apparatus formed the six mixed-sector industries.
xa: Exclusive Central monopoly: **arms & ammunition**, **atomic energy**, **railways**.
Mixed-sector private units were allowed **10 years**, then review.
The **joint sector** came later, with the **Industrial Policy of 1970**.

nc1c12a94fb5.s: The socialist pattern of society was adopted as the goal of economic policy at the Congress session held at:
nc1c12a94fb5.x: The socialist pattern of society was adopted as the goal at the Avadi session in 1955.
nc1c12a94fb5.tq: Link a policy objective with the correct session and year.
xs: The **socialist pattern of society** goal was adopted at the **Avadi** session in **1955** — so option **(4)** is correct.
This goal underlies **IPR 1956**.
xa: IPR 1956 was announced on **30 April 1956**.
It was based on the **Mahalanobis model** and the **Second Five Year Plan**.
IPR 1956 is called the "**Economic Constitution of India**".

n457a6b040ce.s: Schedule A of the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, reserved for the State, contained how many industries?
n457a6b040ce.x: Schedule A had 17 basic or strategic industries under the exclusive responsibility of the State.
xa: **Arms**, **atomic energy**, **railways** and **air transport** were government monopolies in Schedule A.
**Schedule B** = **12** industries, progressively State-owned.
⚠ Reserved public-sector list: **17 → 8 → 3 → 2**.

ndf2ca5db5bc.s: Schedule B of the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 contained how many industries?
ndf2ca5db5bc.x: Schedule B had 12 industries to be progressively State-owned, with the private sector supplementing State effort.
xa: Schedule B examples: other minerals, road & sea transport, **machine tools**, ferro-alloys, basic chemicals, **aluminium**.
Licensing basis: **IDR Act, 1951**.

nefbb57ec500.s: Which of the following was a feature of the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956?
nefbb57ec500.x: IPR 1956 provided for licensing, public-sector expansion, small and cottage industries, balanced regional development and labour welfare. DICs came under the 1977 policy.
xa: Goal: "**Socialist pattern of society**" (Avadi, **1955**).
Plan basis: **Second Five Year Plan**, **Mahalanobis model**.
Epithets: "**Economic Constitution of India**", "**Bible of State Capitalism**".

n4d84c82ac3d.s: The licensing system associated with the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 derived its statutory basis from the:
n4d84c82ac3d.x: Industrial licensing under the 1956 regime rested on the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951.
n4d84c82ac3d.tq: Match a regulatory mechanism with its enabling legislation.
xs: Licensing under IPR 1956 rested on the **Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **MRTP Act** came in **1969**; the **Competition Act 2002** replaced MRTP later.
xa: Sequence: Statement of Industrial Policy **1945** → **IPR 1948** → **IDR Act 1951**.
The licensing regime grew into the "**Licence-Permit Raj**".
**FERA** dates from **1973**, **SICA** from **1985**.

n58f163adb81.s: The R. K. Hazari report of 1967 primarily examined which subject?
n58f163adb81.x: The R. K. Hazari report examined industrial licensing and reported that big business houses had cornered licences.
n58f163adb81.tq: Match the committee or report with its precise policy subject.
xs: The **R.K. Hazari report (1967)** examined **industrial licensing** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It showed that **big houses cornered licences**.
xa: The **Subimal Dutt** Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee (**1967**, report **1969**) led to the **MRTP Act**.
⚠ **Hazari** = report (1967); **Dutt** = Inquiry Committee → MRTP.
Item reservation for SSI also began in **1967**.

ne666e8462b8.s: Which industrial policy emphasised 'tiny' units, khadi and handlooms, and employment generation?
ne666e8462b8.x: The 1977 Statement emphasised small-scale and tiny units, khadi and handlooms, and employment generation.
xa: **DICs** gave one-roof support in every district.
Drafted largely by **George Fernandes** (Janata Government).
⚠ **1977** = tiny units, DICs, IBM/Coca-Cola exit; **1980** = export orientation, economic federalism.

na9ba2225f33.s: District Industries Centres (1977) were set up mainly to:
o: Grant licences to large industrial houses
Provide one-roof support to small and cottage industries in each district
na9ba2225f33.x: DICs were established in every district to give integrated, one-roof support to small and cottage industries.
xa: The 1977 Statement was drafted largely by **George Fernandes**.
The 1977 policy also identified **'tiny' units**.

n5dcf44bf1b9.s: The New Industrial Policy, 1991 was announced during the Prime Ministership of P. V. Narasimha Rao, with Manmohan Singh serving as:
n5dcf44bf1b9.x: The 1991 policy was announced by Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao, with Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister.
n5dcf44bf1b9.tq: Match the reform policy with the correct political and ministerial combination.
xs: **Manmohan Singh** was **Finance Minister** when the NIP was announced — so option **(3)** is correct.
The PM was **P.V. Narasimha Rao**; the policy came on **24 July 1991**.
xa: It followed the **balance-of-payments crisis**.
It had two parts: large/medium industry + **SSI**.
⚠ IPR 1948 was announced by Industry Minister **Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee**.

n24ca3a1c696.s: The New Industrial Policy, 1991 was introduced in the context of which major economic difficulty?
n24ca3a1c696.x: The 1991 policy was introduced after India faced a severe balance-of-payments crisis.
n24ca3a1c696.tq: Link a major policy response with the economic crisis that triggered it.
xs: **NIP 1991** followed a **balance-of-payments crisis** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Forex reserves were not in excess then; today they are at an all-time high of **USD 702.28 bn** (Nov 2025).
xa: Announced on **24 July 1991** by PM **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and FM **Manmohan Singh**.
GDP growth moved from the "**Hindu rate**" (~**3.5%**) to **7-8%**.
The **National Renewal Fund (1992)** cushioned workers hit by restructuring.

n2cdb98ed898.s: After later reductions, compulsory industrial licensing under the New Industrial Policy, 1991 continues for how many industries?
n2cdb98ed898.x: Licensing was first retained for 18 industries and later cut to five: alcohol, cigarettes and tobacco, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, industrial explosives, and hazardous chemicals.
xa: The 5: **alcohol**, **cigarettes/tobacco**, **electronic aerospace & defence equipment**, **industrial explosives**, **hazardous chemicals**.
⚠ Older notes say **6** — the post-1998-99 list included **drugs & pharmaceuticals**, since delicensed.

n350b2a0c97e.s: Which of the following was NOT among the five industries retained under compulsory industrial licensing after the later reduction of the list?
n350b2a0c97e.x: The five retained industries were alcohol, cigarettes/tobacco, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, industrial explosives and hazardous chemicals. Drugs and pharmaceuticals appeared in the older six-item list but were later delicensed.
n350b2a0c97e.tq: Use the later-versus-older licensing list to detect the excluded item.
xs: **Drugs and pharmaceuticals** are not in today's list of five — so option **(3)** is the answer.
They were in the older **6**-item list but were later delicensed.
**Alcohol**, **hazardous chemicals** and **industrial explosives** are still licensed.
xa: The other two of the five: **cigarettes/tobacco** and **electronic aerospace & defence equipment**.
**Coal** and **petroleum** were delicensed in the **Budget 1998-99**, leaving **6**.
Delicensed units file only an **Industrial Entrepreneur Memorandum (IEM)**.

n35564685dd7.s: An industrial unit delicensed under the New Industrial Policy, 1991 was required to file:
o: A Foreign Investment Promotion Board application
n35564685dd7.x: Delicensed units were required to file only an Industrial Entrepreneur Memorandum (IEM).
n35564685dd7.tq: Match the simplified compliance requirement with delicensing.
xs: Delicensed units had to file only an **Industrial Entrepreneur Memorandum (IEM)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**FIPB** handled foreign-investment approvals; **BIFR** handled sick companies; MRTP asset thresholds were scrapped.
xa: Licensing was abolished except **18 industries**, later reduced to **5**.
**1993**: **automobiles**, **white goods**, **leather** delicensed.
**FIPB** was abolished in **June 2017**.

n37fbc4a4e41.s: Which of the following was a major effect of the 1991 industrial reforms?
o: Replacement of private industry by exclusive state ownership
Continuation of all expansion limits and price controls
Removal of licensing, expansion limits, price controls and import-export restrictions
n37fbc4a4e41.x: The 1991 reforms ended the licence-permit-quota raj by removing industrial licensing, expansion limits, price controls and import-export restrictions.
n37fbc4a4e41.tq: Identify the option that correctly combines the reform measures without reversing their direction.
xs: The 1991 reforms brought **removal of licensing, expansion limits, price controls and import-export restrictions** — option **(4)** is correct.
They **ended** the **licence-permit-quota raj**, which **IPR 1956** had begun.
xa: Public-sector reservation was cut from **17** to **8**.
Automatic approval for up to **51%** foreign equity in **high-priority** industries.
**MRTP** asset threshold scrapped; Act later replaced by the **Competition Act 2002**.

n76735162489.s: Which industry was NOT on the public-sector-only list of the New Industrial Policy, 1991 as originally framed?
n76735162489.x: Defence equipment, atomic energy and railway transport were on the public-sector-only list; pharmaceuticals were never reserved for the public sector.
xa: Today only **atomic energy** and **railway operations** are reserved.
Licensed industries now (**5**): alcohol, cigarettes/tobacco, electronic aerospace & defence equipment, industrial explosives, hazardous chemicals.
**Arms & ammunition** were opened to private players in **May 2001**.
n76735162489.fixed: defence is no longer public-sector-only (opened May 2001); anchor the stem to 1991

ncb2fb4156e9.s: Under the New Industrial Policy, 1991, equity participation in small-scale industry units by other industrial undertakings (foreign or domestic) was permitted up to:
ncb2fb4156e9.x: Equity participation in small-scale industry units by other industrial undertakings, foreign or domestic, was permitted up to 24%.
ncb2fb4156e9.tq: Separate the small-scale industry ceiling from the 51% high-priority-industry ceiling.
xs: Other undertakings could hold up to **24%** equity in SSI units — so option **(2)** is correct.
**51%** was the automatic foreign-equity limit for **high-priority** industries.
xa: ⚠ 1991 = **51%** automatic foreign equity (priority list); SSI = **24%**; now **100%** automatic in most sectors.
SSI reservation continued after **1991**; last items dereserved in **2015**.
The 1991 policy had two parts: large/medium industry + **SSI**.

nf95ede7505a.s: A criticism of the post-1991 industrial policy is that investment became concentrated in:
o: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Odisha and Assam
Kerala, West Bengal, Jharkhand and Bihar
nf95ede7505a.x: Investment concentrated in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, making regional imbalance a criticism.
xa: Other criticisms: **jobless growth**, **premature deindustrialisation** of small units, **import dependence**, **environmental** damage.
Correctives now: **PLI** and the **National Manufacturing Mission**.
The **1980** policy had used "**economic federalism**" for backward districts.

n997ddf0c5f7.s: Which one of the following was NOT a criticism of the 1991 industrial policy?
n997ddf0c5f7.x: Increase in consumer choice was an achievement associated with the post-1991 reforms, not a criticism. The other three were criticisms.
n997ddf0c5f7.tq: Separate achievements from criticisms by locating the positive outcome.
xs: **Increase in consumer choice** was an achievement, not a criticism — so option **(3)** is the answer.
Criticisms: **regional concentration**, capital-intensive **jobless growth**, **premature deindustrialisation**.
xa: ⚠ Achievements (not criticisms): **higher growth**, **FDI + forex surge**, **consumer choice**, **global Indian MNCs**.
Growth rose from the "**Hindu rate**" (~**3.5%**) to **7-8%**.
Other criticism: **environmental degradation**.

n71bddae1815.s: Formulation of India's FDI policy falls within the mandate of:
n71bddae1815.x: DPIIT's mandate includes FDI policy, Startups, industrial corridors and IPR matters.
xa: It also covers **Make in India**, **PLI**, **PM GatiShakti NMP** and **EoDB**.
Logistics was added in **Nov 2021**.
DIPP became **DPIIT** in **2019**.

naab3bc6309f.s: The MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 (2024-29) provides for how many MSME parks?
naab3bc6309f.x: Policy 4.0 provides for 175 MSME parks, 'One Family One Entrepreneur' by 2030 and capital subsidy of 25% (45% for special categories).
xa: The policy covers **2024-29**.
The rest of the 4.0 suite: **Food Processing**, **Private Parks**, **EV 4.0**; **Aerospace & Defence**, **Space 4.0** (**2025-30**).
AP Industrial Policy 4.0 targets **175+ industrial parks**.

n0627822c0cd.s: The beginning of the ‘licence-permit-quota raj’ in India is generally associated with which policy resolution?
n0627822c0cd.x: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 is associated with the beginning of the licence-permit-quota raj.
n0627822c0cd.tq: Identify the policy linked with the historical label rather than the later reform policy.
xs: The **licence-permit-quota raj** began with the **Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2019**).
**NIP 1991** ended it; **IPR 1948** laid the mixed economy.
xa: Licensing rested on the **IDR Act, 1951**.
IPR 1956 is also the "**Economic Constitution of India**" and "**Bible of State Capitalism**".
**R.K. Hazari (1967)** showed big houses cornered licences.

nb4d776cb70f.s: Which industrial policy formed the basis of the Second Five-Year Plan?
nb4d776cb70f.x: The IPR 1956, built on the Mahalanobis model of heavy and basic industries, formed the basis of the Second Plan. IPR 1948 came before the First Plan; the 1977 Statement stressed small and cottage industries and DICs; the 1980 Statement stressed economic federalism and exports.
xs: The **Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956** formed the basis of the **Second Five-Year Plan** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2024**).
It followed the **Mahalanobis model** of heavy and basic industries.
**1977** stressed DICs and small units; **1980** stressed economic federalism and exports.
xa: IPR 1956 was announced on **30 April 1956**.
Goal: "**Socialist pattern of society**" (Avadi, **1955**).
IPR 1948 was the **first** industrial policy (**6 April 1948**).

n696ad1bd603.s: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 is significant because it:
o: Established the public-sector-led, licence-based industrial model that continued until 1991
Introduced complete deregulation of all industries
Ended the role of the public sector in basic industries
Restricted industrial development entirely to foreign companies
n696ad1bd603.x: The 1956 Resolution shaped a public-sector-led and licence-based industrial model that continued until the 1991 reforms.
n696ad1bd603.tq: Identify the defining institutional feature associated with the 1956 Resolution.
xs: **IPR 1956** set up the **public-sector-led, licence-based** model that lasted **until 1991** — option **(1)** is correct.
It expanded, not ended, the public sector; it did not deregulate industry.
xa: Schedule A reserved **17** industries for the State; Schedule B (**12**) progressively State-owned.
It began the **Licence-Permit Raj**.
It was the basis of the **Second Five Year Plan**.

nindian-economy-39-12.s: The New Industrial Policy announced in 1991 served as the primary starting anchor of:
nindian-economy-39-12.x: The New Industrial Policy of 24 July 1991 was the starting point of liberalisation. It ended licensing for most industries.
n: The New Industrial Policy was the primary starting anchor of Liberalisation. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
xs: The **New Industrial Policy** (**24 July 1991**) was the primary starting anchor of **Liberalisation** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It came under PM **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and FM **Manmohan Singh** after the balance-of-payments crisis.
It ended the **licence-permit-quota raj**: licensing, expansion limits, price controls and import-export restrictions went.
xa: Licensing abolished except **18 industries**, later reduced to **5**.
Public sector reservation cut from **17** to **8**.
Automatic approval for up to **51%** foreign equity in high-priority industries.

nee9248f3c0a.s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948, which group was placed under exclusive Central monopoly?
o: Coal, iron and steel, and cement
Arms and ammunition, atomic energy, and railways
nee9248f3c0a.x: Arms and ammunition, atomic energy and railways were placed under exclusive Central monopoly in the 1948 policy.
nee9248f3c0a.tq: Match the correct industry group with the ownership category.
xs: Under IPR 1948, **arms and ammunition, atomic energy and railways** were an **exclusive Central monopoly** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Coal**, **iron & steel** fell in the **mixed sector (6)**; **cement**, **automobiles**, **sugar**, **textiles**, **paper**, **fertilizers**, **heavy chemicals** were **centrally regulated (18)**.
xa: Mixed sector (6): coal, mineral oils, iron & steel, aircraft, shipbuilding, telephone/telegraph apparatus.
In the mixed sector, new units were for the State; existing private units got **10 years**, then review.
Residual industries were open to private and co-operative enterprise.

n7480f0f8870.s: Under Schedule C of the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, the industries not included in Schedules A and B were:
o: Placed under joint ownership of the Centre and States
Left to private initiative subject to licensing
n7480f0f8870.x: Schedule C covered all remaining industries and left them to private initiative under an industrial licensing system.
n7480f0f8870.tq: Test the residual category and its regulatory condition.
xs: **Schedule C** industries were **left to private initiative, subject to licensing** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They were neither State-reserved (that was **Schedule A**) nor free of regulation.
xa: Licensing rested on the **Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951**.
The 1956 regime grew into the "**Licence-Permit Raj**".

n7eed0321e28.s: A major significance of the post-1991 reforms was the shift in the role of government from:
n7eed0321e28.x: The reforms shifted the government’s role from direct regulation towards facilitation, forming the basis for today’s FDI framework and competition law.
n7eed0321e28.tq: Watch for the reversed comparison in the two roles of government.
xs: Post-1991, the government's role shifted from **regulator to facilitator** — option **(1)** is correct.
This shift is the base of today's **FDI** and **competition law**.
xa: **IPR 1956** had shaped the public-sector-led, licence-based model until **1991**.
The **Competition Act 2002** replaced the MRTP Act.
Now up to **100%** automatic-route FDI in most sectors.

n2f0d183ce9d.s: Who chaired the Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee which submitted its report in 1969?
n2f0d183ce9d.x: The Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee was chaired by Subimal Dutt. Its report was submitted in 1969 and contributed to the enactment of the MRTP Act.
n2f0d183ce9d.tq: Separate the report author from the later legislation and its commonly used committee name.
xs: The Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee was chaired by **Subimal Dutt** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) names the committee, not its chairman; **R.K. Hazari** wrote the **1967** report on licensing.
xa: The committee was set up in **1967** and reported in **1969**.
Its report led to the **MRTP Act** (**1969**, in force **1970**).
The **joint sector** came with the **1970** licensing policy after the Dutt Committee.
n2f0d183ce9d.fixed: options 'Dutt Committee' and 'Subimal Dutt' were both correct

n0ea637f6f38.s:
The licence raj was criticised for:
1. Encouraging rent-seeking
2. Creating entry barriers
3. Producing excess scale in firms
Which of the above is/are correct?
n0ea637f6f38.x: The licence raj was criticised for rent-seeking, entry barriers and preventing firms from reaching adequate scale, not for excess scale.
xa: It began with **IPR 1956** and ended with **NIP 1991**.
**R.K. Hazari report (1967)**: big houses cornered licences.
After 1991, the government's role shifted from **regulator → facilitator**.

necd70179b95.s: Under the New Industrial Policy, 1991, autonomy was granted to public-sector undertakings through:
necd70179b95.x: The 1991 policy granted PSU autonomy through MoUs, referred sick PSUs to BIFR and began disinvestment in 1991-92.
xa: **BIFR** was set up under **SICA 1985**; in **2016** SICA was repealed and BIFR dissolved, cases going to the **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code**.
Public-sector reservation was cut from **17** to **8**.
Today only **atomic energy** and **railway operations** remain reserved.

nf4f83a86aac.s: How many industries were reserved for the public sector under the New Industrial Policy, 1991?
nf4f83a86aac.x: Eight industries were reserved in 1991; this was cut to three and, after May 2001, to two (atomic energy and railway operations).
xa: ⚠ Trap: "**atomic energy and defence**" as today's two is WRONG.
IPR 1956 Schedule A had **17** industries reserved for the State.

ned2050546a2.s: SICA was repealed and BIFR dissolved, with cases moving under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, in:
ned2050546a2.x: SICA was repealed and BIFR dissolved in 2016; pending cases moved under the IBC.
xa: BIFR handled chronically sick PSUs referred for **revival or closure** after **1991**.
Enactment timeline: **IDR Act 1951**, **MRTP 1969**, **FERA 1973**, **SICA 1985**.
The **MRTP Act** was replaced by the **Competition Act 2002**.

nc945a9c91a9.s: The MRTP Act was replaced by:
nc945a9c91a9.x: The MRTP Act was replaced by the Competition Act, 2002, after the 1991 policy scrapped the MRTP asset threshold.
xa: **MRTP Act**: **1969** (in force **1970**), after the **Subimal Dutt** committee.
The **1980** Statement had let MRTP firms expand up to **25%** without fresh approval.
M&A was freed from MRTP pre-approval after 1991.

n78c63bc3f52.s: The mandatory convertibility clause in the 1991 industrial policy framework concerned:
o: Rupee convertibility on the current account
Conversion of foreign equity into domestic equity
Conversion of PSUs into joint-stock companies
Financial institutions converting term loans into equity
n78c63bc3f52.x: The clause concerned financial institutions converting term loans into equity and was relaxed for term loans of less than 10 years.
xa: **FIPB** was created to speed foreign-investment approvals.
**National Renewal Fund (1992)** was the workers' safety net.
⚠ Learn the key's wording: "term loans of **less than 10 years**".
n78c63bc3f52.fixed: odd wording 'according to the stated provision'

n90927787efa.s: Automatic approval up to 51 per cent foreign equity under the New Industrial Policy, 1991 initially applied to which category?
o: High-priority, high-investment and high-technology industries on the specified list
n90927787efa.x: Automatic approval up to 51 per cent foreign equity applied to a specified list of high-priority, high-investment and high-technology industries. It was not available to all industries without restriction.
n90927787efa.tq: Reject the extreme word ‘all’ and identify the specified sectoral category.
xs: Automatic approval up to **51%** foreign equity applied to **high-priority, high-investment and high-technology industries** on a list — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Trap: it did **not** apply to all industries (APPSC-G1 **2012**).
Examples: **capital goods**, **entertainment electronics**, **food processing**.
xa: It also applied to **export trading companies**.
**Foreign technology agreements** also got automatic approval in high-priority industries.
Now: up to **100%** automatic-route FDI in most sectors, **negative-list** approach.

ne2197b46f81.s: Which body was established under the New Industrial Policy, 1991 to speed up foreign investment approvals?
o: Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
Department of Investment and Public Asset Management
ne2197b46f81.x: The FIPB was set up as part of the liberalised foreign investment framework of the 1991 policy.
xa: Automatic approval for up to **51%** foreign equity in high-priority industries.
FIPB was abolished in **June 2017**.
Gross inward equity FDI (2022-23 to 2025-26) = **$317.80 bn**; repatriation **$178.9 bn** → net FDI falling.

n6cb4c6ed4b4.s: The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) was abolished in:
n6cb4c6ed4b4.x: FIPB was abolished in June 2017 and approvals moved to the FIF portal.
xa: FIF portal integrated with the **National Single Window System** since **Aug 2022**.
FIPB was created under **NIP 1991**.
**DPIIT** handles **FDI policy**.

nfdb9f78ea6e.s: After 1991, many small-scale units were adversely affected by:
o: A ban on imports of capital goods
Import competition following removal of protection
nfdb9f78ea6e.x: Removal of protection exposed small units to import competition, which hurt many of them; SSI reservation continued after 1991.
xa: Premature deindustrialisation: cheap imports from **China** closed many units.
Under 1991, others could hold up to **24%** equity in SSI units.
SSI item reservation began in **1967**.

n09c9c798783.s: DIPP was renamed the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) in:
n09c9c798783.x: DIPP became DPIIT in 2019, adding internal trade, traders' welfare and Startups; logistics was allotted only in November 2021.
xa: DPIIT mandate: **Make in India**, **PLI**, **PM GatiShakti NMP**, industrial corridors, **FDI policy**, EoDB.
It also handles **IPR** — patents, trademarks, designs, GIs.
**DIPP** itself was created in **1995**.

nfb3905e4570.s: The Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion (DIPP) was created as a separate department in:
nfb3905e4570.x: DIPP was created as a separate department in 1995. 1961 is when the Department of Industry was set up, 1967 is when it was renamed the Department of Industrial Development, and 2019 is when DIPP was renamed DPIIT.
xs: **DIPP** was created as a separate department in **1995** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2019**).
**1961**: Department of Industry; **1967**: renamed Department of Industrial Development; **2019**: DIPP renamed **DPIIT**.
xa: **2000**: Department of Industrial Development merged with DIPP.
**Nov 2021**: logistics mandate given to DPIIT.
DPIIT stands for **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade**.

nb4ab7c0917c.s: Which of the following is NOT a target of Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0?
nb4ab7c0917c.x: The targets include ₹30 lakh crore investment, USD 10 billion FDI and five lakh manufacturing jobs; USD 100 billion FDI is not specified.
nb4ab7c0917c.tq: Spot the altered magnitude in a set of policy targets.
xs: **USD 100 billion FDI** is not a target — so option **(3)** is the answer; the FDI target is **USD 10 bn**.
Targets: **₹30 lakh crore** investment, **USD 10 bn FDI**, **5 lakh** manufacturing jobs.
xa: Exports to rise from **USD 20 → 40 bn**.
**175+ industrial parks**.
CII Partnership Summit, Visakhapatnam (**14-15 Nov 2025**): **₹2,80,384 crore** committed.

n239a3061874.s: Which authority chairs the State Investment Promotion Board (SIPB) in Andhra Pradesh?
n239a3061874.x: The SIPB is chaired by the Chief Minister, while the SIPC is associated with the Chief Secretary.
n239a3061874.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish the two approval bodies.
xs: The **SIPB** is chaired by the **Chief Minister** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **SIPC** is chaired by the **Chief Secretary**.
xa: ⚠ **SIPB** = CM; **SIPC** = Chief Secretary.
