Investment bands: **Large** ₹500-1,000 cr, **Mega** ₹1,000-5,000 cr, **Ultra Mega** >₹5,000 cr.
AP Industrial Development Policy 4.0: **G.O. Ms. No. 68**, **26 Oct 2024**.

n2950209ae88.s: The target for industrial parks and exports under Industrial Development Policy (4.0) 2024-29 is:
o: 200 industrial parks and increase exports from US$10 billion to US$30 billion
40+ industrial parks and increase exports from US$20 billion to US$175 billion
175+ industrial parks and increase exports from US$20 billion to US$40 billion
175+ industrial parks and increase exports from US$40 billion to US$20 billion
n2950209ae88.x: The policy targets more than 175 industrial parks and an increase in exports from US$20 billion to US$40 billion.
n2950209ae88.tq: Pair the infrastructure target with the correct export base and destination figures.
xs: Targets: **175+ industrial parks** and exports from **USD 20 bn to USD 40 bn** — option **(3)** is correct.
Option (4) reverses the export figures.
xa: Other targets: **₹30 lakh crore** investment, **USD 10 bn FDI**, **5 lakh** manufacturing jobs.
Policy issued as **G.O. Ms. No. 68**, **26 Oct 2024**.
⚠ The MSME Policy 4.0 separately plans **175 MSME parks**.

nac7516ab3c6.s: Under Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0 (2024-29), which of the following is classified as a 'propelling' sector rather than a 'sustenance' sector?
nac7516ab3c6.x: Propelling sectors are semiconductors and electronics, EVs, aerospace-defence, blue economy and green energy. Automobiles, pharmaceuticals and textiles (with chemicals) are sustenance sectors.
nac7516ab3c6.tq: Sustenance = old base (auto, pharma, chemicals, textiles); propelling = new tech.
xs: **Semiconductors and electronics** is a **propelling** sector — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Auto**, **pharma**, **chemicals** and **textiles** are **sustenance** sectors.
xa: Other propelling sectors: **EVs**, **aerospace-defence**, **blue economy**, **green energy**.
Policy period **2024-29**; valid **5 years**.
Approvals: **SIPB** (CM), **SIPC** (Chief Secretary).

n50de0e7416c.s: Which one of the following was opened to the private sector in May 2001, thereby reducing the industries reserved for the public sector?
n50de0e7416c.x: Defence production, including arms and ammunition, was opened to the private sector in May 2001. Atomic energy and railway operations continued in the reserved category.
n50de0e7416c.tq: Distinguish the industry removed from the reserved list from those retained.
xs: **Defence production** (arms & ammunition) was opened to the private sector in **May 2001** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Atomic energy** and **railway operations** are the two still reserved.
**Atomic minerals** were in the **8** of 1991 and dropped from the later list of three in some notes.
xa: Reservation fell **17 → 8 → 3 → 2**.
⚠ Trap: "atomic energy, atomic minerals and rail transport de-reserved in **1993**" is WRONG — those were the ones kept.
Under **IPR 1948**, arms & ammunition, atomic energy and railways were an exclusive Central monopoly.

n0debb182996.s: Under the original SICA, 1985, a sick industrial company had to be registered for at least:
n0debb182996.x: The original definition required at least seven years of registration, accumulated losses equal to or exceeding net worth, and cash losses.
xa: The **1993 amendment** cut the age to **5 years** and dropped the cash-loss test.
⚠ SICA: **7 years** (original) → **5 years** (1993).
**RBI** test for micro/small units: NPA **> 3 months** or net worth eroded **50%**.

neef0fe8cec2.s: Which change was introduced by the 1993 amendment to the SICA definition of a sick company?
o: The registration requirement was increased to ten years and cash losses were retained.
The registration requirement was reduced to three years and net worth was excluded.
The registration requirement was abolished and accumulated losses were ignored.
The registration requirement was reduced to five years and the cash-loss test was dropped.
neef0fe8cec2.x: The 1993 amendment reduced the minimum registration period from seven to five years and dropped the cash-loss test.
neef0fe8cec2.tq: Compare the original and amended definitions by isolating both changed elements.
xs: The **1993 amendment** cut the registration requirement to **five years** and **dropped the cash-loss test** — option **(4)** is correct.
The original **SICA 1985** test needed **7 years** of registration.
xa: The net-worth test (accumulated losses ≥ net worth) stayed.
Older notes give only the **7-year** version.
**BIFR** under SICA was set up in **January 1987**.

n03dd5afeafe.s: Under RBI norms, a micro or small unit is sick if any of its borrowal accounts stays NPA for more than:
n03dd5afeafe.x: An NPA lasting more than 3 months marks a micro or small unit as sick (with 50% net-worth erosion as the other test).
xa: The 2016 Framework also set up **Committees for Stressed MSMEs**.
**One-time restructuring** of stressed MSME loans without downgrade: **2019**, extended **2020-21**.
⚠ RBI: NPA **> 3 months** or net worth eroded **50%**.

n9489c20125c.s: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of industrial sickness?
o: Bank loans turning into non-performing assets
Plant, land and funds lying idle
Increase in revenue receipts of the exchequer
n9489c20125c.x: Idle assets in sick units cause revenue loss to the exchequer, not an increase; NPAs, locked capital and unemployment are real consequences.
xa: To protect jobs, the State took over sick private units, esp. **textiles and engineering**.
This **lowered PSU returns**.
NPAs **weaken lenders**.

nd5ac3fa1ec3.s: Obsolete technology as a cause of industrial sickness is classified as an:
nd5ac3fa1ec3.x: Obsolete technology is an internal production cause; poor working-capital management is internal finance, competition external demand, EXIM changes external policy.
xa: Internal management causes: poor planning, **diversion of funds**, faulty project appraisal.
External infrastructure causes: chronic **power shortages**, transport bottlenecks.
External credit cause: **delayed and costly credit**.

ne42f5a575d2.s: The State takeover of certain sick private textile and engineering units was mainly intended to:
o: Earn dividend income for the State
ne42f5a575d2.x: The State took over certain sick private units, especially in textiles and engineering, mainly to protect jobs.
xa: The public sector absorbing these units **lowered PSU returns**.
Sickness is concentrated in **textiles (cotton mills)**, **jute**, **sugar** and **engineering**.
**IRBI** (**1971**) was set up to rehabilitate sick units.

nf94b8ee466e.s: Industrial sickness has been particularly concentrated in which group of sectors?
nf94b8ee466e.x: The sectors especially associated with industrial sickness are textiles, including cotton mills, jute, sugar and engineering.
nf94b8ee466e.tq: Recall the sectoral cluster rather than selecting a group of generally important industries.
xs: Industrial sickness is concentrated in **textiles, jute, sugar and engineering** — option **(2)** is correct.
Within textiles, **cotton mills** stand out.
xa: Sick private textile and engineering units were taken over by the State to protect jobs.
Internal causes include **obsolete technology** and poor quality control.
The **Kohli Working Group (1999-2000)** looked at rehabilitation of sick **SSI** units.

n135804dac1c.s: A one-time restructuring of stressed MSME loans without asset-classification downgrade was permitted in which year (later extended during 2020-21)?
n135804dac1c.x: The one-time restructuring of stressed MSME loans without downgrade was permitted in 2019 and extended during 2020-21.
xa: The **2016 framework** stresses early identification via **SMA-0/1/2**.
The 2016 framework also set up **Committees for Stressed MSMEs**.
Delayed payments now go to **MSME Samadhaan**.

n38317221094.s: The Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act (SICA) was enacted in:
n38317221094.x: SICA was enacted in 1985 following the Tiwari Committee (1984-85); BIFR was set up in January 1987.
xa: ⚠ **SICA** = 1985 Act; **BIFR** under it set up **January 1987**.
⚠ **Tiwari** → SICA; **Eradi** → NCLT; **Viswanathan** → IBC.
Appeals from BIFR went to the **AAIFR**.

necace1d2f4b.s: Which institution, set up in 1971, was associated with the rehabilitation of sick industrial units?
o: Appellate Authority for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
necace1d2f4b.x: The Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India, established in 1971, was set up to rehabilitate sick industrial units.
necace1d2f4b.tq: Match the institution with its rehabilitation role and distinguish it from later forums.
xs: The **Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India (IRBI)**, set up in **1971**, rehabilitated sick units — option **(3)** is correct.
**NCLT** and **NCLAT** date from the **IBC 2016** era; **AAIFR** heard BIFR appeals; the **National Renewal Fund** began in **1992**.
xa: IRBI was the **first dedicated rehabilitation bank**.
BIFR was the **last SICA-era forum** (dissolved **1 Dec 2016**).
**Liberalized Margin Money Scheme** (**June 1987**) reduced sickness in the small-scale sector.
necace1d2f4b.fixed: 1971 body was IRCI; it became IRBI only in 1985

n92e86b23531.s: The principal purpose of the National Renewal Fund was to:
o: Finance voluntary retirement, retraining and redeployment of displaced workers
Provide foreign exchange to importing firms
n92e86b23531.x: The Fund financed voluntary retirement schemes, retraining and redeployment for workers displaced by restructuring or closure of industrial units.
n92e86b23531.tq: Recognise the social-safety-net function from the worker-displacement scenario.
xs: The **National Renewal Fund** financed **VRS compensation, retraining and redeployment** of displaced workers — option **(1)** is correct.
It was not an export, forex or irrigation fund.
xa: Set up in **1992** as a **social safety net for industrial restructuring**.
It also supported restructuring and **modernisation** of industries.
It was **wound up in 2000**.

n1b0963e08ee.s: Under the new insolvency regime, the BIFR was succeeded by the:
n1b0963e08ee.x: BIFR was succeeded by the NCLT and AAIFR by the NCLAT; SICA's regime was replaced by the IBC, 2016.
xa: The IBC regulator is **IBBI**, with licensed **Insolvency Professionals**.
IBC aims at **time-bound resolution** and "**maximisation of asset value**".
IBC came from the **T.K. Viswanathan (BLRC, 2015)** committee.

n4be54db95a5.s: The Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) was concerned with:
o: Refinancing banks that lend to small industries
Early detection of sickness, revival of viable units and closure of unviable units
n4be54db95a5.x: BIFR dealt with early detection of industrial sickness, revival of viable units and winding-up of unviable units.
xa: BIFR covered both **public and private** companies with industrial undertakings.
Appeals: **AAIFR**.
BIFR ceased on **30 November 2016**; cases went to **NCLT/NCLAT** under **IBC 2016**.

n61fc03676c0.s: Which committee examined insolvency and winding-up, leading to the NCLT and NCLAT?
n61fc03676c0.x: The Eradi Committee led to NCLT/NCLAT; Tiwari led to SICA and BIFR, Goswami studied corporate restructuring, Kohli sick SSI units.
xa: **T.K. Viswanathan (BLRC, 2015)** → bankruptcy law → **IBC 2016**.
⚠ **Tiwari** → SICA; **Eradi** → NCLT; **Viswanathan** → IBC.

n9c5b92b5551.s: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 was based on the recommendations of the:
n9c5b92b5551.x: The IBC was based on the T.K. Viswanathan Committee, also known as the Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee, 2015.
n9c5b92b5551.tq: Identify the committee associated with a reform.
xs: **IBC 2016** came from the **T.K. Viswanathan Committee** (**BLRC, 2015**) — option **(4)** is correct.
The **Eradi Committee (1999)** led to NCLT/NCLAT; **Tiwari** to SICA.
xa: IBC is administered through **NCLT** (adjudicating) and **NCLAT** (appellate), with regulator **IBBI**.
IBC shifted from **debtor-in-possession** to **creditor-in-control**.
SICA → IBC shifted power to creditors and improved **ease of doing business**.

nead13809679.s: The Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 provided for:
o: Licensing of new or expanded industrial units and Development Councils
Control of monopolies and restrictive trade practices
nead13809679.x: The IDRA, 1951 provided for licensing of industrial units when started or expanded, and for Development Councils.
xa: The Act was **amended in 1953**.
It is the base of the licensing regime: **IDRA 1951** → **MRTP 1969** → **FERA 1973** → **SICA 1985**.
Today only **5** industries need a compulsory licence.

n95923a5ec97.s: The Hazari Report (1967) and the Dutt Committee (1969) found that industrial licensing had favoured:
n95923a5ec97.x: Both found that the licensing system favoured large business houses, which led to the MRTP framework.
xa: Some notes date the Dutt Committee to **1964**.
The Dutt Committee is the **Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee**.
The MRTP Act was enacted in **1969** and came into force in **1970**.

n9231b124a9a.s: Leather was removed from compulsory industrial licensing in:
n9231b124a9a.x: Leather was delicensed in 1993; the five remaining licensed categories are alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, and industrial explosives.
xa: NIP **1991** started with **18** licensed industries.
The **1988** negative list had **26** industries.
In the **1980s**, **32** groups were delicensed.

nebdecf919e3.s: The MRTP Act, 1969 was replaced by which legislation?
nebdecf919e3.x: The Competition Act, 2002 replaced the MRTP Act. The MRTP Commission was replaced by the Competition Commission of India.
nebdecf919e3.tq: Use the enactment-year trap to distinguish the Competition Act from FEMA.
xs: The MRTP Act was replaced by the **Competition Act, 2002** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2018** key).
**FEMA 1999** replaced **FERA**, not MRTP.
xa: Some notes say "**Competition Act, 2001**" — the key is **2002**.
The Act commenced on **31 Mar 2003**; **CCI** was established on **14 Oct 2003**.
⚠ Replacements: **FERA → FEMA**; **MRTP → Competition Act**; **SICA → IBC**.

n957687aafd5.s: The MRTP Act, 1969 was recommended by the
n957687aafd5.x: The Dutt Committee, formally the Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee, recommended the MRTP legislation.
n957687aafd5.tq: Trap the closely associated Hazari and Dutt committees by asking which one made the recommendation.
xs: The **MRTP Act, 1969** was recommended by the **Dutt Committee** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **Hazari Report (1967)** exposed licensing bias but was a report, not the recommending committee; **Rangarajan** (**1993**) was on disinvestment.
xa: Dutt Committee = **Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee** (**1969**).
MRTP came into force in **1970**.
Purpose: **control private monopoly** and concentration of economic power.

n21a0a7b8db5.s: Which Act was replaced by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 in relation to the earlier sick-industrial-company regime?
n21a0a7b8db5.x: The IBC, 2016 replaced the SICA regime, which had been associated with the functioning of BIFR.
n21a0a7b8db5.tq: Identify the predecessor regime rather than the more widely known foreign-exchange replacement.
xs: The **IBC 2016** replaced the **SICA, 1985** regime — option **(3)** is correct.
**MRTP** was replaced by the **Competition Act**; **FERA** by **FEMA**.
xa: SICA created **BIFR** (functioning **1987**).
BIFR → **NCLT**; its appeals forum → **NCLAT**.
**IDRA 1951** was the licensing law.

n5c9b6058875.s: After 1991, the role of the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (APIIC) shifted to that of a:
n5c9b6058875.x: After 1991, APIIC's role shifted towards being a facilitator of industrial development.
xa: AP's PPP ports: **Krishnapatnam** and **Gangavaram**.
**Liberalisation** = removal of licences, quotas and controls.
After 1991, licensing was cut to **18** industries, now **5**.

nc1735edba24.s: The MRTP Act was enacted in:
nc1735edba24.x: The MRTP Act was enacted in 1969 and came into force in 1970.
xa: The original asset threshold was **₹20 crore+**.
**NIP 1991** scrapped the asset threshold.
⚠ Market share **33% → 25%** (1984); assets **₹20 crore → ₹100 crore** (1985).

n02366bad0c6.s: What was the effect of the New Industrial Policy, 1991 on the MRTP asset threshold of Rs. 100 crore?
o: It made the threshold applicable only to public sector firms
It reduced the threshold to Rs. 50 crore
It doubled the threshold to Rs. 200 crore
It scrapped the threshold for large firms
n02366bad0c6.x: The New Industrial Policy, 1991 scrapped the MRTP asset threshold. Large firms no longer required prior approval for expansion, mergers or takeovers merely because of their asset size.
n02366bad0c6.tq: Apply the reform measure to the specific regulatory restriction being removed.
xs: **NIP 1991** **scrapped the MRTP asset threshold** (₹100 crore since **1985**) — option **(4)** is correct.
Large firms no longer needed **prior approval** to expand, merge or take over.
xa: Original threshold: assets **₹20 crore+** or **33%** market share.
In **1984**, the share criterion was cut to **25%**.
MRTP was later replaced by the **Competition Act, 2002**.

n74de472415e.s: The Competition Act, 2002 was recommended by which committee?
n74de472415e.x: The Competition Act, 2002 was recommended by the S.V.S. Raghavan Committee in 2000.
n74de472415e.tq: Distinguish the committee associated with competition law from committees on insolvency and company law.
xs: The **Competition Act, 2002** was recommended by the **S.V.S. Raghavan Committee** (**2000**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**T.K. Viswanathan** (BLRC **2015**) led to the IBC; **Eradi** to NCLT; the **Disinvestment Commission** (**1996**) advised on PSU sales.
xa: The Act was introduced by **Arun Jaitley**.
It replaced the **MRTP Act**.

nd5aa1771deb.s: The sale of government equity in public sector enterprises is known as:
nd5aa1771deb.x: Selling government equity is disinvestment; liberalisation is removal of licences, quotas and controls.
xa: **Privatisation** = transfer of **ownership and management control** to the private sector.
**Monetisation** leases assets; **ownership stays with government**.
**Strategic sale** = block of shares (usually **50%+**) plus transfer of management control.

n7a56f54da80.s: The Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) was dissolved on:
n7a56f54da80.x: BIFR, created under SICA 1985, was dissolved on 1 December 2016 and its cases went to NCLT/NCLAT.
xa: **IBC 2016** came from the **T.K. Viswanathan BLRC 2015**; it is **creditor-in-control**.
NCLT was set up on the **Eradi Committee**'s advice.

n1f5b0efb5fb.s: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 followed the Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee headed by:
n1f5b0efb5fb.x: The IBC was enacted on 28 May 2016 after the T.K. Viswanathan-led BLRC (2015).
xa: **IBBI** is the regulator under the IBC.
**BIFR** was dissolved on **1 Dec 2016**; cases moved to **NCLT/NCLAT**.
⚠ NCLT = **s.408**; NCLAT = **s.410** of the Companies Act 2013.

nae9b65943f1.s: The National Company Law Tribunal was set up on 1 June 2016 under which section of the Companies Act, 2013?
nae9b65943f1.x: NCLT was constituted under Section 408; the NCLAT is under Section 410.
xa: NCLT is the **adjudicating authority** under IBC.
IBC was enacted on **28 May 2016**.
BIFR cases went to **NCLT/NCLAT** after **1 Dec 2016**.

nd1d7b27163f.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes disinvestment from privatisation?
o: Disinvestment always transfers management control; privatisation may retain government control
Both always transfer management control to the private sector
Disinvestment reduces government equity; privatisation transfers ownership and management control to the private sector
Privatisation reduces equity without transfer of control; disinvestment transfers ownership
nd1d7b27163f.x: Disinvestment is a reduction of government equity, possibly with government retaining control; privatisation transfers ownership and management control to the private sector.
xa: **Strategic sale**: a block of shares (usually **50%+**) plus transfer of management control.
**Complete privatisation**: **100%** sold — the most comprehensive mode.
⚠ **Monetisation** leases assets; disinvestment sells equity permanently.

n3bddf1f0874.s: A government retains more than 51 per cent equity and control in a public sector enterprise while selling a part of its holding. This is called
n3bddf1f0874.x: Under minority disinvestment, the government retains more than 51 per cent ownership and control. Majority disinvestment transfers control while retaining a minority stake.
n3bddf1f0874.tq: Apply the percentage and control test to distinguish minority and majority disinvestment.
xs: Keeping **more than 51%** and control while selling part is **minority disinvestment** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Majority disinvestment** transfers control but keeps a minority stake; **complete privatisation** sells **100%**.
xa: **Strategic sale** = block of shares (usually **50%+**) + transfer of management control.
The first round (**1991-92**) sold minority stakes in **31 PSUs**.
**Economic Survey 2025-26** proposes letting the stake in listed CPSEs fall to **26%** while keeping "Government company" status.

n7ccc1456062.s: A strategic sale of a public sector enterprise generally involves:
o: Sale of a block of shares, usually 50% or more, with transfer of management control
Sale of a minority stake with the government retaining control
Leasing assets for a fixed period with ownership retained by the government
Listing shares through an IPO without any change in management
n7ccc1456062.x: A strategic sale normally involves a block of shares, usually 50% or more, along with transfer of management control to a strategic partner.
xa: The **Disinvestment Commission (1996)** recommended strategic sales.
First strategic sales came in **1999-2004**.
Since **2016**, in-principle approval for strategic sale of **36 CPSEs**; **13 completed**.

nd2c5356f431.s: Which of the following is a disinvestment instrument used by DIPAM?
nd2c5356f431.x: CPSE ETF, Offer for Sale, IPO/FPO and strategic sale are disinvestment instruments; SLR, CRR and repo are monetary and banking tools.
xa: DIPAM manages **Central Government equity + disinvestment** under the **Ministry of Finance**.
**Bharat Bond ETF (2019)** raised **₹32,400 crore**.
**LIC IPO** (**17 May 2022**) was the biggest IPO then, with about **73 lakh** applications.

n6fdbf2d205e.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or concern relating to disinvestment?
o: Automatic improvement in public ownership of strategic assets
National-security concerns in oil, defence and transport
n6fdbf2d205e.x: The identified concerns include undervaluation, loss of dividend income and national-security risks in sectors such as oil, defence and transport. Automatic improvement in public ownership is not a criticism of disinvestment.
n6fdbf2d205e.tq: Find the option that is inconsistent with the stated criticism of the policy.
xs: **Automatic improvement in public ownership** is not a concern — option **(2)** is the answer; disinvestment reduces public ownership.
Listed concerns: **undervaluation**, **loss of dividend income**, **national-security** concerns in **oil, defence, transport**.
xa: Main criticism: "**selling the family silver**" to fill the **fiscal deficit**.
**Risk of private monopolies** and **union resistance** are also debated.
**New PSE Policy 2021** keeps a "**bare minimum**" **1-4** CPSEs in **4** strategic sectors.

n4cc65403bbf.s: How does asset monetisation differ from disinvestment?
o: Asset monetisation permanently sells equity; disinvestment leases assets temporarily
Both permanently transfer ownership to private operators
Asset monetisation leases public assets for a fixed period with ownership retained by the government; disinvestment permanently sells equity
Both lease public assets for a fixed period without any sale of equity
n4cc65403bbf.x: Asset monetisation leases existing public assets for a fixed period after which they return to the government, whereas disinvestment is a permanent sale of equity.
xa: Monetised assets include **roads**, **railways**, **power lines**, **pipelines** — all **de-risked** brownfield assets.
**Strategic sale** transfers management control.
**NMP 2.0** was launched on **1 Mar 2026**.

n7b7a426d225.s: The Rangarajan Committee (1993) recommended disinvestment in PSUs reserved for the public sector up to:
n7b7a426d225.x: It recommended disinvestment up to 49% in PSUs reserved for the public sector and up to 74% in other enterprises.
xa: ⚠ **Rangarajan** = **49%** / 74%; **Arjun Sengupta** = MoU, not disinvestment.
The **Disinvestment Commission** (**1996**, first chair **G.V. Ramakrishna**) recommended strategic sales.
The **V. Krishnamurthy Committee** (**1991**) set out an early approach.

n8268c5140df.s: Who was the first chairman of the Disinvestment Commission set up in 1996?
n8268c5140df.x: The Disinvestment Commission (1996) was first chaired by G.V. Ramakrishna; the 49% recommendation came from the Rangarajan Committee (1993).
xa: First strategic sales followed in **1999-2004**.
**Department of Disinvestment**: **1999**; **DIPAM**: **2016**.
**Arjun Sengupta** (**1984**) dealt with PSU autonomy and MoUs.

n1bd85c49d9e.s: DIPAM, which manages Central Government equity and disinvestment, functions under the Ministry of:
n1bd85c49d9e.x: DIPAM (renamed from the Department of Disinvestment in 2016) works under the Ministry of Finance.
xa: DIPAM modes: **strategic sale**, **OFS**, IPO/FPO, **CPSE ETF**.
**C. Rangarajan Committee** (**1993**): disinvestment up to **49%** in PSUs reserved for the public sector.
Disinvestment Commission (**1996**): first chair **G.V. Ramakrishna**.

nde8aa4520fa.s: Since which financial year has there been no separate disinvestment head in the Budget, with disinvestment receipts merged into Miscellaneous Capital Receipts?
nde8aa4520fa.x: Since FY24, there has been no separate disinvestment head; it has been merged into Miscellaneous Capital Receipts.
nde8aa4520fa.tq: Use the time marker to identify the change in budget classification.
xs: Since **FY24** (FY 2024), there is **no separate disinvestment head**; receipts are in **Miscellaneous Capital Receipts** — option **(3)** is correct.
This reflects falling disinvestment receipts, with **no separate disinvestment heading** in the Budget.
xa: Policy has shifted from **selling PSUs → earning dividends**.
Disinvestment receipts have fallen since **2022-23**.
**NMP 2.0** was launched on **1 Mar 2026**.

nfbb409d8684.s: The National Land Monetisation Corporation (NLMC) is associated with the monetisation of:
o: foreign exchange reserves held by the Government of India
surplus land and buildings of Central Public Sector Enterprises, including loss-making enterprises
only privately owned industrial land acquired by the government
only the shares of listed Central Public Sector Enterprises
nfbb409d8684.x: NLMC monetises surplus land and buildings belonging to Central Public Sector Enterprises, including those that are loss-making.
nfbb409d8684.tq: Match the specialised institution with its precise asset and beneficiary group.
xs: **NLMC** monetises **surplus land and buildings of CPSEs, including loss-making ones** — option **(2)** is correct.
It does not sell CPSE shares — that is **DIPAM**'s work.
xa: NLMC is **100% GoI**, incorporated **3 June 2022** under **DPE**.
DIPAM modes: **strategic sale**, **OFS**, **IPO/FPO**, **CPSE ETF**.
Monetisation objective: **new financial structures** to unlock value.

n339612a34cf.s: The strategic sale of Air India, completed in 2021-22, was made to:
n339612a34cf.x: Air India was sold to the Tata Group. Sterlite (Vedanta) bought BALCO, Hindustan Lever bought Modern Food Industries, and PFC acquired REC.
n339612a34cf.tq: Air India, VSNL and NINL all went to Tata companies.
xs: **Air India** was sold to the **Tata Group** (**2021-22**) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Sterlite (Vedanta)** bought **BALCO**; **Hindustan Lever** bought **Modern Food Industries**; **PFC** acquired **REC**.
xa: **VSNL** also went to the **Tata group** (**2002**).
The **2019-20** target of **Rs 1,05,000 crore** had included Air India.
**IDBI Bank** strategic sale is in the pipeline.

n17d078803bc.s: If the CCI does not decide on a combination within the prescribed deadline, the combination is:
n17d078803bc.x: A combination is deemed approved if the CCI misses the prescribed decision deadline.
xa: Combinations (**s.5-6**) = mergers/acquisitions above thresholds.
Abuse of dominant position falls under **s.4**; anti-competitive agreements under **s.3**.
CCI sits under the **Ministry of Corporate Affairs**.

ne6d5e5d865a.s: The term ‘disinvestment’ was introduced in the Indian policy framework through which of the following?
ne6d5e5d865a.x: The term ‘disinvestment’ was introduced in the Interim Budget presented in July 1991.
ne6d5e5d865a.tq: Use the exact year and policy document rather than associating the term with a later committee.
xs: The term **disinvestment** was introduced in the **Interim Budget, July 1991** — option **(2)** is correct.
It means **reducing government share** in the public sector, the government possibly keeping majority and control.
xa: First round: **1991-92**, minority stakes in **31 PSUs** (**20%** announced).
First-year target: **Rs 2,500 crore**.
**C. Rangarajan Committee** (**1993**) recommended the disinvestment policy.

n614aa0a5e7b.s: The disinvestment target set for 2019-20, which included the proposed sale of Air India, was:
n614aa0a5e7b.x: The 2019-20 target was Rs 1,05,000 crore. Rs 47,000 crore was the 2025-26 target, Rs 80,000 crore is the 2026-27 target, and Rs 1.75 lakh crore was the 2021-22 target (of which only about Rs 13,534 crore was realised).
xs: The **2019-20** target, including **Air India**, was **Rs 1,05,000 crore** — option **(3)** is correct.
xa: 2021-22 realised only about **Rs 13,534 crore**.
**Air India** went to the **Tata Group** in **2021-22**.
2020-21 PSB/FI target: **Rs 90,000 crore** (UPPSC **2021**).

n36110e12863.s: The New PSE Policy, 2021 classifies how many sectors as strategic?
n36110e12863.x: There are four strategic sectors (including banking, insurance and financial services), each retaining a bare minimum of 1-4 CPSEs.
xa: Strategic sectors: atomic energy/space/defence; transport & telecom; power/petroleum/coal/minerals; banking/insurance/financial services.
**16th FC**: close **308** inactive State PSUs; privatise **DISCOMs**.
**ES 2025-26**: let stake in listed CPSEs fall to **26%**.

n59e759c3b86.s: Which one of the following was the principal purpose of the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969?
o: To control private monopolies and concentration of economic power
To promote foreign direct investment in high-priority industries
To provide automatic approval for technology agreements
n59e759c3b86.x: The MRTP Act, 1969 aimed to control private monopolies and prevent concentration of economic power. Its enactment followed the recommendations associated with the Dutt Committee.
n59e759c3b86.tq: Distinguish the objective of the MRTP Act from objectives of later liberalisation measures.
xs: The **MRTP Act, 1969** aimed to **control private monopolies and concentration of economic power** — option **(1)** is correct.
It also curbed **monopolistic, restrictive and unfair trade practices** (APPSC-GS **2019**).
Foreign exchange control was **FERA**'s job (**1973**), later replaced by **FEMA 1999**.
xa: It was recommended by the **Dutt Committee**.
Original MRTP threshold: assets **₹20 crore+** or **33%** market share.
Replaced by the **Competition Act, 2002**; MRTP Commission → **CCI**.

n2f988447cde.s: Which one of the following was associated with PSU autonomy and Memoranda of Understanding rather than with the disinvestment policy recommendations?
n2f988447cde.x: Arjun Sengupta’s 1984 work was associated with PSU autonomy and Memoranda of Understanding, not with the later disinvestment recommendations.
n2f988447cde.tq: Separate a nearby but distinct reform theme from the committees directly concerned with disinvestment.
xs: **Arjun Sengupta** (**1984**) is linked to **PSU autonomy and MoUs**, not disinvestment — option **(2)** is correct.
**Rangarajan** (**1993**) and **G.V. Ramakrishna** (Disinvestment Commission, **1996**) were about disinvestment.
xa: Rangarajan recommended up to **49%** in reserved PSUs, **74%** in others.
Post-1991, PSUs also got greater autonomy through **MoUs**.
The Disinvestment Commission recommended **strategic sales**.

nca1ba262f9d.s: The expression “selling the family silver” is used in criticism of disinvestment because:
o: all public assets are sold below their book value in every transaction
the proceeds are used to bridge the fiscal deficit instead of building assets
disinvestment necessarily increases dividend income for the government
the proceeds are exclusively invested in new public enterprises
nca1ba262f9d.x: The expression criticises the use of disinvestment proceeds to bridge the fiscal deficit rather than to create or build assets.
nca1ba262f9d.tq: Interpret an idiomatic expression through the policy criticism it represents.
xs: "**Selling the family silver**" criticises using **proceeds to bridge the fiscal deficit instead of building assets** — option **(2)** is correct.
Disinvestment actually means **loss of dividend income**, not more.
xa: Other concerns: **undervaluation** of PSU assets; **national-security** concerns in oil, defence, transport.
Debates also note **union resistance** and the **risk of private monopolies**.
NIF rule: proceeds credited, **only income** used.

n5b8d0296722.s: The National Manufacturing Policy, 2011 aimed to raise manufacturing's share of GDP within a decade to:
n5b8d0296722.x: NMP 2011 targeted a 25% manufacturing share of GDP within a decade and 100 million jobs.
xa: Its infrastructure was to be built on a **PPP** basis.
**National Manufacturing Mission** (Budget 2025-26): **25%** share + **143 million** jobs by **2035**.
**Make in India** (**25 September 2014**): logo is a **lion made of cogwheels**.

n044322737ee.s: Which of the following was specifically included as a measure in the National Manufacturing Policy?
o: Replacing industrial training with fiscal incentives
Restricting skill development to metropolitan areas
n044322737ee.x: Skilling of rural youth was specifically included among the policy measures.
xa: Infrastructure was on a **PPP** basis.
Design: **sector-, location- and technology-neutral**.
Notified **November 2011**.

ndf8e3446e75.s: The National Manufacturing Mission announced in Budget 2025-26 aims by 2035 to achieve which combination?
o: Manufacturing share of 20 percent and 100 million jobs
Manufacturing share of 25 percent and 75 million jobs
Manufacturing share of 25 percent and 143 million jobs
Manufacturing share of 30 percent and 100 million jobs
ndf8e3446e75.x: The National Manufacturing Mission targets a 25 percent manufacturing share and 143 million jobs by 2035.
ndf8e3446e75.tq: Distinguish the latest mission's target from the earlier policy targets.
xs: The **National Manufacturing Mission** targets a **25 percent** share and **143 million jobs** by **2035** — option **(3)** is correct.
**100 million** jobs was the NMP 2011 / Make in India target.
xa: The Mission was announced in **Budget 2025-26**.
ES **2025-26** credits **PLI** and the Mission with driving investment.
Industry GVA grew **7.0%** in **H1 FY26**.

na18b3d3d799.s: Which one of the following was NOT an original quantitative target of Make in India?
o: Raising the manufacturing share of GDP to 50 per cent by 2030
Manufacturing growth of 12–14 per cent annually
Increasing the manufacturing share of GDP from 16 per cent to 25 per cent
na18b3d3d799.x: The stated targets were 12–14 per cent annual manufacturing growth, a rise in the manufacturing share from 16 to 25 per cent, and 100 million additional jobs. A 50 per cent share by 2030 was not an original target.
na18b3d3d799.tq: Find the quantitative statement that does not belong to the stated target set.
xs: **50 per cent of GDP by 2030** was not a Make in India target — option **(1)** is the answer.
Original targets: manufacturing growth **12-14%** a year; share **16% → 25%**; **100 million** additional jobs.
xa: The share target date was **2022**, later **2025**.
Manufacturing remains only **~16.3-17.5%** of GVA/GDP.
Strategy has shifted to **global value chains** and design capability.

n2e1fad459df.s: Manufacturing's present share of India's GVA is about:
n2e1fad459df.x: Manufacturing remains about 16.3–17.5 per cent of GVA, below the 25 per cent target, so the strategy has shifted to scale, design and global value chains.
xa: The shift was noted in **Jun 2026**.
Criticism: "**Assemble in India**" vs value addition; PLI gains concentrated in **electronics** and **semiconductors**.
Medium- and high-tech manufacturing = **46.3%** of total (ES **2025-26**).

n407a3a08c11.x: PM GatiShakti came in October 2021; the National Logistics Policy followed in September 2022.
xa: Make in India's **New Infrastructure** pillar covers **corridors** and **smart cities**.
**ISM** also dates from **Dec 2021**.
**NSWS** gives access to **686** central and **7,498** state approvals.

n1073a4c0a8e.s: The e-Biz platform was introduced as which of the following?
o: A State-level portal exclusively for environmental clearances
A Mission Mode Project under the National e-Governance Plan for online registration, filing and payments
A World Bank index for measuring business regulations
An investment promotion joint venture between FICCI and CII
n1073a4c0a8e.x: e-Biz is a Mission Mode Project under NeGP that enables online registration, filing and payment for businesses.
n1073a4c0a8e.tq: Distinguish the function of a digital business service from an investment agency or ranking index.
xs: **e-Biz** is a **Mission Mode Project under the National e-Governance Plan (NeGP)** for **online registration, filing and payments** — option **(2)** is correct.
The FICCI-CII joint venture describes **Invest India**, not e-Biz.
xa: e-Biz is part of the **New Processes** pillar of Make in India.
**NSWS** gives access to **686** central and **7,498** state approvals.
**DPIIT Single Window Systems Guidebook (2025)**: **80** services = **44** essential + **36** desirable.

n958b352c7ae.s: A large integrated industrial township with zoned land use, clean technology and social infrastructure is called a:
n958b352c7ae.x: NIMZs are conceived as large integrated industrial townships with zoned land use, clean technology and social infrastructure.
xa: NIMZs differ from **SEZs** in size, infrastructure planning, governance, exit policy and fiscal incentives.
AP NIMZs: **Chittoor** and **Prakasam** (in-principle approval).
An **SEZ** is an export-oriented enclave treated as **foreign territory** for trade and duties.

n6020285d7e2.s: Under the National Manufacturing Policy, 2011, infrastructure development was envisaged primarily on which basis?
n6020285d7e2.x: The National Manufacturing Policy, 2011 provided for infrastructure on a PPP basis. It did not restrict funding to the public sector, foreign grants or cooperatives.
xs: NMP 2011 envisaged infrastructure on a **public-private partnership (PPP)** basis — option **(1)** is correct.
It did not restrict funding to the State, foreign aid or cooperatives.
xa: It also focused on skilling **rural youth**.
Targets: **25%** of GDP, **100 million** jobs.
It was **technology-neutral**, except for incentives to **green technology**.

n0a878e89ff9.s: The logo of Make in India is a ____ made of cogwheels.
n0a878e89ff9.x: Make in India (25 September 2014) has a lion made of cogwheels as its logo.
xa: Nodal ministry: **Ministry of Commerce & Industry**.
Linked slogans: '**Vocal for Local**', "Make in India for the World".
Original coverage: **25** sectors.

nfd9b8292820.s: Make in India 2.0 covers how many priority sectors?
nfd9b8292820.x: Make in India 2.0 covers 27 sectors: 15 manufacturing under DPIIT and 12 services under the Department of Commerce.
xa: The **Action Plan for Champion Services Sectors** covers **12** sectors.
⚠ Trap: the APPSC **2018** key gave "**10**" for this count.
Original Make in India covered **25** sectors.

n62a9be3a941.s: The original Make in India initiative launched in September 2014 covered how many sectors?
n62a9be3a941.x: The original Make in India covered 25 sectors across manufacturing, infrastructure and services. 27 is the count of priority/champion sectors under Make in India 2.0 (2021); 14 is the number of PLI sectors; 12 is the number of champion services sectors.
xs: Original Make in India covered **25** sectors — option **(1)** is correct.
**27** = Make in India 2.0 (**2021**); **14** = PLI sectors; **12** = champion services sectors.
xa: The 25 spanned **manufacturing**, **infrastructure** and **services**.
Make in India 2.0 = **15** manufacturing (DPIIT) + **12** services (Commerce).
Launched **25 September 2014**.

n0a70f07179c.s: Which one of the following is NOT a sector included in the PLI scheme as listed?
n0a70f07179c.x: White goods, solar PV modules and specialty steel are included sectors. Coal mining equipment is not included in the listed PLI sectors.
n0a70f07179c.tq: Use the complete sector list to eliminate the outside item.
xs: **Coal mining equipment** is not a PLI sector — option **(1)** is the answer.
**Specialty steel**, **solar PV modules** and **white goods** are PLI sectors.
xa: Other PLI sectors: mobiles/electronics, IT hardware, telecom, bulk drugs, pharma, medical devices, food products.
Also: auto & components, **ACC battery**, textiles (**MMF** & technical), **drones**.
PLI covers **14 sectors** with **Rs 1.97 lakh crore**.

n9bdb0c657af.s: The expression “China+1” in the context of Make in India and PLI refers most closely to:
o: A bilateral tax treaty between India and China
Diversifying global supply chains by adding India as an alternative manufacturing location
Adding one percentage point to India's GDP growth
Replacing China with one Indian state in all trade
n9bdb0c657af.x: “China+1” refers to diversification of global value chains by creating an additional manufacturing base, such as India, alongside China.
n9bdb0c657af.tq: Interpret the policy phrase in its global value-chain context rather than literally.
xs: **"China+1"** means **diversifying global supply chains by adding India as an alternative manufacturing location** — option **(2)** is correct.
EoDB and PLI aim to lift manufacturing's share and help India **join global value chains**.
xa: Make in India's strategy shifted to **integration with global value chains** (**Jun 2026**).
Smartphones became India's **largest export category in 2025**.
Medium- and high-tech manufacturing = **46.3%** of total (ES **2025-26**).

n32fecc97851.s: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme was designed primarily to provide incentives on which basis?
o: Incremental sales of goods manufactured in India
n32fecc97851.x: PLI provides incentives linked to incremental sales of goods made in India; in electronics, the incentive is stated as 4–6 per cent.
n32fecc97851.tq: Apply the scheme’s name to identify the production-and-sales trigger.
xs: PLI gives incentives on **incremental sales of goods manufactured in India** — option **(3)** is correct.
In electronics the incentive is **4-6%**.
xa: PLI supports **sunrise industries**.
⚠ PLI **4-6%** on incremental sales vs MPMS **2.25-5%** on eligible sales.
**PLI-Auto** (**Rs 25,938 crore**) needs at least **50%** domestic value addition.

nc490a5816e5.s: The PLI scheme for the automobile sector (PLI-Auto) has an outlay of:
nc490a5816e5.x: PLI-Auto has an outlay of ₹25,938 crore and requires at least 50 per cent domestic value addition.
xa: PLI covers **14 sectors**, **Rs 1.97 lakh crore** (announced **2020**).
Results to **Sep 2025**: **12.60 lakh** jobs.
PLI-LSEM ended on **31 March 2026**, replaced by **MPMS**.

n531d6f9ba91.s: The outlay of PM E-DRIVE, launched by the Ministry of Heavy Industries in 2024, is:
n531d6f9ba91.x: PM E-DRIVE has an outlay of ₹10,900 crore; ₹11,500 crore was FAME-II, which it succeeded.
xa: It **succeeded FAME-II** and **subsumed EMPS-2024**.
First-ever support for **e-trucks** and **e-ambulances**.
e-2W/3W support till **31 Mar 2026**; others till **31 Mar 2028**.

n0c7b0175ca9.s: Under the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (FY2026-27 to FY2030-31), the extra incentive for domestic sourcing is up to:
n0c7b0175ca9.x: The scheme gives 2.25-5% on eligible sales, up to 1.5% extra for domestic sourcing and 3% extra for design and R&D by Indian brands.
xa: MPMS outlay: **Rs 62,500 crore** for **FY2026-27** to **FY2030-31**.
PLI-LSEM ended on **31 March 2026**.
⚠ PLI **4-6%** on incremental sales vs MPMS **2.25-5%** on eligible sales.

n737dfd93b84.s: How many projects have been approved under the India Semiconductor Mission?
n737dfd93b84.x: ISM has approved 12 projects with about ₹1.64 lakh crore of commitments; capital assistance may go up to 50%.
xa: ISM 1.0 outlay: **Rs 76,000 crore**.
Project locations: Gujarat **6**, Odisha **2**, Assam, UP, Punjab, **AP 1 each**.
**ISM 2.0** aims at **70-75%** self-sufficiency by **2029**.

ndfc6185cec6.s: In the proposed framework replacing SEZ rules, 'DESH' stands for:
o: Development of Export and Special Hubs
Development of Export and Services Hubs
ndfc6185cec6.x: DESH is Development of Enterprise & Service Hubs; it would drop compulsory positive NFE, allow DTA sales and be WTO-compliant.
xa: DESH = **Development of Enterprise & Service Hubs**, a proposed reform of the **SEZ Act, 2005**.
SEZ **Sec 10AA** benefits end for units not operational by **30 June 2020**.
SEZs are treated as **foreign territory** for trade and duties.

ncfa4b9c3255.s: The Foreign Investment Facilitation portal was merged with the National Single Window System in:
ncfa4b9c3255.x: The FIF portal was merged with the NSWS in August 2022.
xa: **e-Biz** is a Mission Mode Project under **NeGP**.
DPIIT's guidebook lists **80** single-window services.
**Invest India** was set up in **2009**.

n0b524a015ca.s: In NITI Aayog's Investment Friendliness Index (July 2026), Andhra Pradesh was placed in which category?
n0b524a015ca.x: Andhra Pradesh was among the Frontrunners (score 45-50); Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Goa and Odisha were Top Performers.
xa: ⚠ Doing Business = **10** parameters; B-READY = **3** pillars; this index = **8** pillars.
AP's **Single Desk Portal** cleared **99.20%** approvals within SLA.
IMD Competitiveness rank: **43** (2021) → **41** (2025).

n47fb9430bbb.s: Which areas are identified as weak indicators affecting India's ease of doing business?
n47fb9430bbb.x: Contract enforcement and property registration remain major bottlenecks; digital literacy and export promotion are not cited.
xa: Other bottlenecks: **labour** (four **labour codes**) and **compliance** burden.
**DILRMP**, **ULPIN** and **NGDRS** target registering property.
**Commercial courts** and **e-Sanchit** customs filing are among the credited EoDB reforms.

n5b8a4464f75.s: The India Semiconductor Mission functions under the:
n5b8a4464f75.x: ISM operates under the Digital India Corporation of MeitY and supports fabs, OSAT/ATMP units and chip design.
xa: Capital assistance up to **50%**.
ISM 1.0: **12 projects**, ~**Rs 1.64 lakh crore**.
ATMP unit at **Sanand**: **₹22,516 crore**.

nd2c09114368.s: The Semicon India programme (India Semiconductor Mission) of MeitY, approved in 2021, has an outlay of:
nd2c09114368.x: Semicon India/ISM under MeitY was approved in 2021 with an outlay of Rs 76,000 crore.
xa: ISM was set up in **Dec 2021**.
ISM 2.0 (**₹1,27,500 crore**) approved by Cabinet (**16 Jul 2026** report).
ISM supports **fabs**, **OSAT/ATMP** and **chip design**.

n9dfb411e419.s: In Andhra Pradesh, NIMZs have been proposed in which districts?
n9dfb411e419.x: NIMZs have received in-principle approval in Chittoor and Prakasam districts of Andhra Pradesh.
n9dfb411e419.tq: Apply the location trap by matching the initiative with the correct districts.
xs: AP's NIMZs are proposed in **Chittoor and Prakasam** — option **(3)** is correct.
They have **in-principle approval**, and a **TEFS** report was submitted (**2025-26**).
xa: **NIMZs** are large integrated industrial townships with **zoned land use**, **clean technology** and **social infrastructure**.
NIMZs differ from SEZs in **size**, **infrastructure planning**, **governance**, **exit policy** and **fiscal incentives**.
AP's **Rayalaseema manufacturing hub** includes JSW steel **Kadapa**, **Kia** and Royal Enfield **Tirupati**.

n23f261b39bf.s: The SEZ Act, 2005, along with the SEZ Rules, came into force on:
n23f261b39bf.x: The SEZ Act and Rules came into force on 10 February 2006.
xa: **Sec 10AA**: **100%** export income tax exemption for **5 years**, then **50%** for 5 years.
Sunset: only units operational by **30 June 2020** get 10AA benefits.
Proposed **DESH** framework (**Jun 2026**) would drop compulsory **positive NFE**.

nd2efb398949.s: Under Section 10AA, the income-tax exemption on export income of an eligible SEZ unit is structured as:
o: 100 per cent for five years, 50 per cent for the next five years and 50 per cent of ploughed-back profit for a further five years
50 per cent for five years, 100 per cent for the next five years and nil thereafter
50 per cent for the entire fifteen-year period
100 per cent for ten years followed by 25 per cent for five years
nd2efb398949.x: Section 10AA provides 100 per cent exemption for the first five years, 50 per cent for the next five years and 50 per cent of ploughed-back profit for another five years.
nd2efb398949.tq: Track the exemption sequence and distinguish the successive time periods.
xs: **Sec 10AA**: **100%** for **five years**, **50%** for the next five, and **50% of ploughed-back profit** for a further five — option **(1)** is correct.
The exemption is on **export income** of an eligible SEZ unit.
xa: Only units operational by **30 June 2020** get this (extended from **31 March 2020**).
The **SEZ Act, 2005** came into force on **10 February 2006**.
SEZs are **single-window**, export-oriented enclaves.

n99cca0a3ead.s: The three pillars of the World Bank's B-READY framework are:
o: Regulatory framework, public services and operational efficiency
n99cca0a3ead.x: B-READY rests on regulatory framework, public services and operational efficiency.
xa: ⚠ Doing Business = **10** parameters; B-READY = **3** pillars; NITI Investment Friendliness Index = **8** pillars.
B-READY replaced **Doing Business**, discontinued in **2021**.
India joins the **third** B-READY report.

n0ebeed1eb6e.s: The four labour codes and the proposed central rules primarily seek to promote which broad outcome?
o: Replacement of all state labour laws by municipal laws
Formalisation of labour and consolidation of labour regulations
Restriction of employment to the public sector
n0ebeed1eb6e.x: The four labour codes and the draft central rules are associated with labour-law consolidation and increasing formalisation. They do not eliminate informal employment completely.
n0ebeed1eb6e.tq: Link the reform instrument with its stated broad policy objective.
xs: The four **labour codes** aim at **formalisation of labour** and consolidation of labour regulations — option **(3)** is correct.
Formalisation is projected to rise from **60.4% to 75.5%**, with **77 lakh** jobs — but **over 80%** of workers remain informal, so informality is not eliminated.
xa: Draft central rules were issued in **Dec 2025**.
The debate: EoDB must be matched by "**ease of living**" and **workers' rights**.
DPIIT's **Reducing Compliance Burden** exercise tackles regulatory cost.

n5121ae9c5da.s: India's rank in the World Bank's Doing Business 2020 report was:
n5121ae9c5da.x: India rose from 142nd in 2014 to 63rd in DB 2020; the report was discontinued in 2021 over data irregularities.
xa: Doing Business was conceptualised by the **IFC** and published by the **World Bank Group**.
Its replacement is **B-READY**.

ne620fe738ed.s: Of the 355 provisions amended by the Jan Vishwas 2.0 Bill, how many were decriminalised?
ne620fe738ed.x: The Bill (introduced 18 August 2025, passed 2026) amended 355 provisions across 16 Acts and decriminalised 288 of them.
xa: It covers **16** Acts across **10** ministries.
**Jan Vishwas Act 2026**: an **Improvement Notice** for first-time Legal Metrology lapses.
DPIIT runs a **Reducing Compliance Burden** exercise.

n4a039b643b6.s: India’s position in mobile phone manufacturing is best described as follows:
o: The second-largest mobile phone manufacturer in the world
The fifth-largest mobile phone manufacturer in the world
The largest mobile phone manufacturer in the world
The third-largest mobile phone manufacturer in the world
n4a039b643b6.x: India is identified as the second-largest mobile phone manufacturer.
n4a039b643b6.tq: Use the precise rank rather than assuming that the largest domestic market is the largest manufacturer.
xs: India is the world's **second-largest mobile phone manufacturer** — option **(1)** is correct.
Some **2026** notes say "**among the top 3** in volume".
xa: Mobile output rose from **₹18,900 crore (2014-15)** to **₹5.45 lakh crore (2024-25)**, CAGR ~**40%**.
**99.2%** of phones used in India are made domestically.
Smartphones were the **largest export category in 2025**.

nae1a13a54e4.s: The SPICe+ reform was introduced to improve which ease-of-doing-business area?
nae1a13a54e4.x: SPICe+ supports starting a business; online building-plan approvals target construction permits, IBC insolvency and GST taxes.
xa: **SPICe+** (**2020**) bundles **11 services** of **3 ministries**; also **MCA21 V3**.
**DILRMP**, **ULPIN**, **NGDRS** improved **registering property**.
**GST** as an EoDB reform was the APPSC-G2 **2025** key.

n355f2bb5682.s: Invest India, established in 2009, is best described as:
o: A statutory regulator under the Reserve Bank of India for foreign exchange transactions
A World Bank Group index for ranking investment destinations
A not-for-profit joint venture involving DIPP, FICCI, CII, NASSCOM and the States, serving as the national investment promotion agency
A private company established exclusively by NASSCOM for software exports
n355f2bb5682.x: Invest India was established in 2009 as a not-for-profit joint venture involving DIPP, FICCI, CII, NASSCOM and the States, and serves as the national investment promotion agency.
n355f2bb5682.tq: Separate the investment-promotion agency from a regulator, index or private industry body.
xs: **Invest India** (**2009**) is a **not-for-profit JV of DIPP, FICCI, CII, NASSCOM and the States**, the **national investment promotion agency** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is not a regulator, an index or a NASSCOM-only company.
xa: It also acts as an **investment-facilitation SPV**.
**NSWS**: **686** central + **7,498** state approvals.
The **FIF** portal joined NSWS in **Aug 2022**.

n5ab115ed65f.s: Business Reform Action Plan, commonly abbreviated as BRAP, was first released in 2015 by:
o: DIPP, now DPIIT, in association with the World Bank Group
The Ministry of Finance and the IMF
n5ab115ed65f.x: BRAP was first released in 2015 by DIPP, now DPIIT, with the World Bank Group.
n5ab115ed65f.tq: Who-launched-what trap using neighbouring institutions as distractors.
xs: **BRAP** was first released in **2015** by **DIPP (now DPIIT)** with the **World Bank Group** — option **(1)** is correct.
NITI Aayog runs a separate **Investment Friendliness Index**.
xa: BRAP = **Business Reform Action Plan** (APPSC-GS **2019**).
AP was **2nd** in BRAP **2015** (Gujarat **1st**).
DPIIT is preparing **BRAP 2026**.

n38193fa09a4.s: In BRAP 2016, Andhra Pradesh shared the No. 1 rank with:
n38193fa09a4.x: Andhra Pradesh was jointly first with Telangana in BRAP 2016 and has been described as No. 1 consistently since.
xa: APPSC-GS **2023** key: AP **1st**.
BRAP **2024** was the **7th edition** with **435** reform points.
NITI Aayog's index (**Jul 2026**) put AP among **"Frontrunners"**.

n91930c7b17f.s: The four principles associated with the 435 reform points in BRAP 2024 were:
n91930c7b17f.x: The BRAP 2024 reform points were organised around Simplification, Elimination, Digitisation and Decriminalisation.
n91930c7b17f.tq: Direct recall of a four-part policy framework.
xs: BRAP **2024**'s **435** points follow **Simplification, Elimination, Digitisation and Decriminalisation** — option **(4)** is correct.
These are **state-specific** reform points, aimed at cutting and digitising procedures, not adding inspections or penalties.
xa: BRAP **2024** was the **7th edition**.
**DBRAP** extends reforms to **Tier-II** and **Tier-III** cities.
**Jan Vishwas** laws also pursue **decriminalisation**.

n2342f55d1e0.s: District BRAP, or DBRAP, is intended primarily to:
o: Extend business reforms to district-level administration and Tier-II and Tier-III cities
Measure the competitiveness of Indian states against foreign countries
Rank only metropolitan cities on exports
n2342f55d1e0.x: DBRAP extends the reform process to districts and Tier-II and Tier-III cities.
n2342f55d1e0.tq: Apply the meaning of the district-level extension to the appropriate administrative scope.
xs: **DBRAP** takes business reforms to **district level** and **Tier-II and Tier-III cities** — option **(1)** is correct.
It does not replace state-level BRAP or compare states with foreign countries.
xa: State-level **BRAP** began in **2015** under **DIPP** with the **World Bank Group**.
DPIIT is preparing **BRAP 2026**.
AP has been **No. 1** consistently from **2016**.

n09dea6f1d04.s: Which strategy most directly reflects the central approach of Make in India?
o: Replacing digital services with traditional services
Restricting manufacturing to wholly state-owned enterprises
Attracting foreign direct investment and global firms to manufacture in India
Promoting only domestic consumption without export orientation
n09dea6f1d04.x: Attracting FDI and global firms to establish manufacturing in India is the strategy most typical of Make in India.
n09dea6f1d04.tq: Match the initiative with its characteristic strategy rather than its general developmental effects.
xs: The most typical Make in India strategy is **attracting FDI and global firms to manufacture in India** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is not about state-only manufacturing or domestic-only consumption.
xa: Slogan: "**Make in India for the World**".
**New Sectors** pillar opened **FDI** in defence, insurance, medical devices.
EoDB and PLI aim to join global value chains (**"China+1"**).

n67035b50fa0.s: The World Bank's Doing Business rankings were meant mainly to guide which of the following?
n67035b50fa0.x: Per the APPSC-GS 2019 key, the Doing Business rankings mainly guide foreign investors on the ease of doing business in a country. They are not meant for consumers, election bodies or monetary policy.
xs: Doing Business rankings mainly guided **foreign investors** — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2019**).
They were not tools for consumers, election bodies or central banks.
xa: The report was conceptualised by the **IFC**, the World Bank Group's private-sector arm.
It had **10** parameters, from **starting a business** to **resolving insolvency**.
India's rank improved from **142** to **63**.

n708c6b29953.s: Which of the following is NOT a reform credited with improving India's Ease of Doing Business?
o: Removal of all foreign ownership restrictions
Land records reforms through DILRMP and ULPIN
n708c6b29953.x: Faceless assessment, faster electricity connections and land-record reforms were credited; removal of all foreign ownership restrictions was not.
xa: ⚠ Trap — not reforms: removal of all foreign ownership restrictions, **nationalisation**, **PSU expansion**.
Other credited reforms: **GST**, **IBC 2016**, **SPICe+**, **e-Sanchit**, **commercial courts**.
The new EoDB wave stresses **digital governance** and **trust-based regulation** (**9 Jun 2026**).

ne2ac60c601c.s: A deep-tech start-up retains start-up status for up to how many years from incorporation?
ne2ac60c601c.x: A deep-tech start-up qualifies up to 20 years and ₹300 crore turnover, against 10 years and ₹200 crore for an ordinary start-up.
xa: The **₹200 crore** turnover cap is a revision; older notes give **₹100 crore**.
⚠ Trap: an entity formed by **splitting or reconstructing** a business is not a start-up.
Benefit: income-tax deduction for **3 consecutive years out of 10** under **s.80-IAC**.

nba35d846c9d.s: Which institution is the nodal agency for recognition of start-ups under the Startup India framework?
nba35d846c9d.x: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) is the nodal agency for Startup India recognition.
nba35d846c9d.tq: Identify the correct institutional authority rather than a financing agency.
xs: The nodal agency for Startup India recognition is **DPIIT** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Startup India was launched on **16 January 2016** with DPIIT as nodal body and a **19-point** Action Plan.
**NCGTC** gives the guarantee under **CGSS**; **SIDBI** manages the **Fund of Funds** — neither recognises start-ups.
xa: **16 January** is now observed as **National Startup Day**.
DPIIT also runs the **States' Startup Ranking Framework**, which assesses state start-up policies.
⚠ **DPIIT** = Startup India; **Ministry of Finance** = Stand-Up India.

n06857a8d5f8.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated benefit available under the Startup India framework?
o: Self-certification under specified labour and environmental laws
Permanent exemption from all taxes for the entire life of the enterprise
Income-tax deduction for three consecutive years out of ten under Section 80-IAC
n06857a8d5f8.x: The framework provides a tax deduction for three consecutive years out of ten, self-certification and fast-track patent facilities. It does not provide a permanent exemption from all taxes.
n06857a8d5f8.tq: Find the exaggerated benefit using the extreme-word trap.
xs: **Permanent exemption from all taxes** is NOT a Startup India benefit — option **(3)**.
The tax benefit is limited: a deduction for **3 consecutive years out of 10** under **Section 80-IAC**.
**Fast-track patents** and **self-certification** under labour and environment laws are genuine benefits.
xa: The s.80-IAC deduction applies to start-ups incorporated before **1 Apr 2030**.
Start-ups can also be **wound up under IBC** (a faster exit).
**Angel tax** was abolished for all investors in **Budget 2024-25**.

n06064db02d1.s: Angel tax was abolished for all classes of investors in the Union Budget:
n06064db02d1.x: Angel tax was abolished for all investors in Budget 2024–25.
xa: **FFS** corpus **₹10,000 crore** (SIDBI); **FFS 2.0** adds another ₹10,000 crore for deep tech, space, AI.
**SISFS**: up to ₹20 lakh grant + ₹50 lakh investment, via incubators.
Startup tax benefit: deduction for **3 consecutive years out of 10** under **s.80-IAC**.

n97a05df12f4.s: Which one of the following correctly describes venture capital?
o: Early-stage equity investment accompanied by active guidance for high-growth firms
Collateral-free bank lending guaranteed through NCGTC
Individuals investing their own money at the idea or seed stage
Small sums collected from many people through online platforms
n97a05df12f4.x: Venture capital consists of early-stage equity investment with active guidance for high-growth firms. The other descriptions refer to crowdfunding, angel investment and CGSS respectively.
n97a05df12f4.tq: Discriminate among similar start-up financing sources by their defining features.
xs: **Venture capital** = **early-stage equity** with **active guidance** for high-growth firms — option **(1)**.
Option (2) describes **CGSS** (collateral-free loans guaranteed through **NCGTC**).
Option (3) describes **angel investors**; option (4) describes **crowdfunding**.
xa: **CGSS** was introduced in **Oct 2022**; maximum **₹20 crore** per borrower; fee **1%** for champion sectors.
CGSS replaced the earlier **Credit Guarantee Fund for Startups**.
**Fund of Funds** (₹10,000 crore, **SIDBI**) invests via SEBI-registered **AIFs**.

ndb2f7f794d4.s: The Stand-Up India Scheme was launched on:
ndb2f7f794d4.x: Stand-Up India was launched on 5 April 2016.
ndb2f7f794d4.tq: Use the direct date-recall approach for a flagship scheme.
xs: Stand-Up India was launched on **5 April 2016** — option **(1)**.
**19 April 2021** = **Seed Fund (SISFS)** launch; **16 January 2016** = **Startup India** launch.
**22 January 2020** = notification of the **National Startup Advisory Council**.
xa: Stand-Up India is run by the **Ministry of Finance** through scheduled commercial bank branches.
Loans of **₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore** to **SC/ST and women** entrepreneurs (18+).
Operational till **31 March 2025**: **2.75 lakh** loans, **₹62,790 crore**.

n91c7971a615.s: Under the Stand-Up India Scheme, the loan amount generally ranges between:
n91c7971a615.x: Stand-Up India loans range from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore.
n91c7971a615.tq: Identify the correct range among closely spaced monetary figures.
xs: Stand-Up India loans range from **₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore** — option **(1)**.
They go to **SC/ST and women** entrepreneurs for **greenfield** enterprises.
xa: Loan covers up to **85%** of project cost; borrower contribution min **10%**.
Repayment up to **7 years** with an **18-month moratorium**.
⚠ **MUDRA** covers micro units only up to **₹20 lakh** (**Tarun Plus**).

n296d1181cdb.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the nodal ministry and the online portal of the Stand-Up India Scheme?
n296d1181cdb.x: Stand-Up India (5 April 2016) is run by the Ministry of Finance through scheduled commercial bank branches, and its portal is Standupmitra. DPIIT is nodal for Startup India, the Udyam portal is for MSME registration, and NITI Aayog is not the nodal body.
n296d1181cdb.tq: Stand-Up = Finance Ministry + Standupmitra; Startup = DPIIT.
xs: Stand-Up India: **Ministry of Finance**, portal **Standupmitra** — option **(1)**.
**DPIIT** is the nodal body for **Startup India**, not Stand-Up India.
Stand-Up India works through **scheduled commercial bank branches**.
xa: Launched **5 April 2016**.
**SIDBI** provides **₹10,000 crore** refinance.
Status: extended for the **15th FC** period; operational till **31 March 2025** (IYB 2026).

ne52682968ac.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS)?
o: It has an outlay of ₹945 crore.
Start-ups receive the support directly from commercial banks.
It gives up to ₹20 lakh grant for proof of concept.
ne52682968ac.x: SISFS is routed through incubators (up to ₹5 crore each), not commercial banks; the other statements are correct.
xa: **Fund of Funds (FFS)**: **₹10,000 crore**, managed by **SIDBI**, invests through SEBI-registered AIFs.
**FFS 2.0** adds another ₹10,000 crore for **deep tech, space, AI**.
**CGSS** (Oct 2022) supports collateral-free loans through **NCGTC** guarantees.

n4c7d53196c9.s: The ₹10,000 crore Fund of Funds for Startups is managed by:
n4c7d53196c9.x: FFS is managed by SIDBI and invests through SEBI-registered AIFs, not directly in start-ups.
xa: ⚠ **SIDBI** both manages the Fund of Funds and gives **Stand-Up India refinance** — each **₹10,000 crore**.
**Seed Fund (SISFS)**: **₹945 crore**, launched **19 April 2021**, routed via incubators.
**Angel tax** was abolished for all investors in **Budget 2024-25**.

n99c04a97827.s: Under DST's NIDHI programme, the Entrepreneur-in-Residence (EIR) component offers a fellowship of up to:
n99c04a97827.x: NIDHI's EIR programme offers a fellowship of up to Rs 30,000 per month; PRAYAS supports prototype development.
xa: NIDHI also supports **TBIs** (technology business incubators).
⚠ **NIDHI** = DST; **ASPIRE** = Ministry of MSME; **Udyam Abhilasha** = SIDBI.
**AIM 2.0**: till March 2028, **₹2,750 crore**, **2,500** new ATLs.

n3ed8dd1c354.s: Which institution functions as the State nodal agency for start-ups and innovation in Andhra Pradesh?
n3ed8dd1c354.x: The AP Innovation Society (APIS) is the State nodal agency for start-ups and innovation in Andhra Pradesh.
n3ed8dd1c354.tq: Identify the institution associated with the exact administrative role.
xs: The State nodal agency for start-ups and innovation is the **AP Innovation Society (APIS)** — option **(4)**.
**DPIIT** is the national nodal body; **RTIH** is a hub-and-spoke innovation hub, not the nodal agency.
xa: FY 2024-25: **6,935** start-ups; **2,493 (36%)** DPIIT-recognised; **1,203** women-led.
**50** incubators (**7th largest** start-up infrastructure); **175** mentors on APIS portal.
**564** EISCs and **590 ATLs**; **25,000** jobs; **₹480 crore** raised.

ndf0fe2023b4.s: The hub of the hub-and-spoke model of Ratan Tata Innovation Hub is located at:

xs: The RTIH hub is at **Amaravati (Mangalagiri)** — option **(3)**.
**Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam and Tirupati** are **spokes**, not the hub.
xa: Other spokes: **Rajahmundry** and **Anantapuramu** (2025-26).

nc5b886059d2.s: The Ratan Tata Innovation Hub aims to create, over five years,

nc5b886059d2.tq: Match the target numbers and time period as a single policy objective.
xs: RTIH aims at **20,000 start-ups and one lakh jobs** in five years — option **(4)**.

**1,203** is AP's count of **women-led** start-ups; **25,000** is jobs created per APIS data.

nd334053a3c2.s: The States’ Startup Ranking Framework of DPIIT primarily promotes:
o: Allocation of all start-up funds exclusively to one state
Direct ranking of individual start-up founders by personal income
Competitive federalism by assessing state start-up policies and their implementation
Assessment of only the number of unicorns in each district
nd334053a3c2.x: The framework promotes competitive federalism by assessing the policies adopted by states and their implementation for start-up development.
nd334053a3c2.tq: Identify the framework’s purpose rather than a narrow output indicator.
xs: The framework promotes **competitive federalism** by assessing **state start-up policies and implementation** — option **(3)**.

xa: Categories: **Best Performers, Top Performers, Leaders, Aspiring Leaders, Emerging Start-up Ecosystems**.
AP was **No. 1 in the National States Startup Ranking 2022**.
AP was **9th in the India Innovation Index 2022**.

n20a0d4b94b1.s: The National Startup Advisory Council was notified in:
n20a0d4b94b1.x: The National Startup Advisory Council was notified on 22 January 2020.
xa: About **53%** of start-ups come from **Tier-2/3** cities.
**Udyam Abhilasha** was a national-level entrepreneurship awareness campaign (**APPSC-GS 2018**), linked to **SIDBI**.
**NIDHI** (**DST**) is the umbrella programme turning knowledge-based innovations into start-ups.

n2af853207be.x: Stand-Up India supports greenfield enterprises in manufacturing, services, trading and agri-allied activities through scheduled commercial bank branches.
xa: Launched **5 April 2016** by the **Ministry of Finance**.
**SIDBI** gives **₹10,000 crore** refinance; portal **Standupmitra**.
Extended for the **15th FC** period; operational till **31 March 2025**.

n231f6d04715.s: Stand-Up India covers loans in the range of:
n231f6d04715.x: Stand-Up India covers loans of ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore, while MUDRA covers micro units up to ₹20 lakh under Tarun Plus.
xa: Stand-Up loans cover up to **85%** of project cost; repayment up to **7 years**.
Stand-Up India was launched on **5 April 2016** by the **Ministry of Finance**.
Norm: at least **one SC/ST and one woman borrower per bank branch**.

n2d9c6ba3236.s: The Special Economic Zone (SEZ) Policy was announced in April 2000 through which policy framework?
n2d9c6ba3236.x: The SEZ Policy was announced in April 2000 through the EXIM Policy 2000-01.
n2d9c6ba3236.tq: Identify the policy framework associated with the announcement year.
xs: The SEZ Policy of **April 2000** was announced through the **EXIM Policy 2000-01** — option **(3)**.
This was the APPSC-GS **2025** key.
Sequence: Policy **2000** → **SEZ Act 2005** → Act and Rules in force **10 Feb 2006**.
xa: Before SEZs came **EPZs** from **1965**, Kandla being the first.
APPSC-G1 2018 treated the policy as "announced" in **both 2000 and 2006**.
**SEZ (Amendment) Rules 2025** cut minimum land for semiconductor SEZs from **50 ha to 10 ha**.

nc4249d3e6de.s: An SEZ may be set up by:
o: The Central or a State Government only
The Central Government, a State Government or any person
nc4249d3e6de.x: SEZs may be set up jointly or severally by the Centre, a State or any person, including public, private and joint-sector entities.
xa: SEZs under the Act are **mainly private**.
Purpose: manufacturing, services, or a **Free Trade Warehousing Zone**.
Proposals go via the **State** to the **Board of Approval**.

ndb847e55ace.s: Which change is associated with the proposed DESH Bill?
o: Removal of the positive Net Foreign Exchange condition
Mandatory positive NFE for all units
Immediate repeal of the SEZ Act by an enacted law
A ban on Domestic Tariff Area sales

xa: DESH was announced in **Budget 2022-23**.

**Baba Kalyani Committee** (2018) earlier proposed the **"3Es"** rename.

nindian-economy-18-4.s: India's first private-sector Export Processing Zone was at:
nindian-economy-18-4.x: Surat was the first private-sector EPZ (converted into an SEZ on 1 November 2000); Kandla was India's first EPZ.
n: The SEZ Act and Rules came into effect on February 10, 2006. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 26-27]
