Surat had India's first private-sector Export Processing Zone (EPZ). [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 26-27]
The Surat EPZ was converted into an SEZ on November 1, 2000. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 26-27]
Kandla, Gujarat, had Asia's first Export Processing Zone (EPZ). [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 26-27]
xa: Kandla was also **Asia's first** EPZ and India's first Free Trade Zone.
**Falta** EPZ = West Bengal; **SEEPZ** = Mumbai; **MEPZ** = Chennai.

nindian-economy-18-5.s: The Special Economic Zones Act received Presidential assent on:
nindian-economy-18-5.x: The SEZ Act was passed in May 2005, got assent on 23 June 2005 and came into force on 10 February 2006.
n: India's first SEZ policy was announced on April 1, 2000. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 26-27]
The SEZ Act was passed by Parliament in 2005. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 26-27]
The President gave assent to the SEZ Act on June 23, 2005. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 26-27]
The SEZ Act and Rules came into effect on February 10, 2006. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 26-27]
xa: The SEZ policy was announced in the **EXIM Policy 2000-01** (APPSC-GS 2025 key).
**Baba Kalyani Committee (2018)** proposed renaming SEZs as "**3Es**".
**DESH Bill** (Budget **2022-23**) is to replace the SEZ Act; still pending.

nindian-economy-53-1.s: Kandla, Asia's first Export Processing Zone, was set up in:
nindian-economy-53-1.x: Kandla EPZ was set up in 1965 as India's (and Asia's) first; the SEZ policy came in 2000.
n: Kandla was the first Asian EPZ in 1965. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 79-80]
Kandla was India's first EPZ. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 79-80]
Surat was the first private-sector EPZ. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 79-80]
The SEZ policy was introduced in 2000. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 79-80]
xa: Surat EPZ was established in **1997** and converted to an SEZ on **November 1, 2000**.
Existing **EPZs** and **EOUs** could convert into SEZs.
SEZs: **100% FDI** under the automatic route for most manufacturing.

nindian-economy-53-6.s: The Special Economic Zones (SEZ) Act was enacted in which year?
nindian-economy-53-6.x: The SEZ Act was passed in 2005. The policy came in 2000, and the Act took effect in February 2006.
nindian-economy-53-6.tq: Discriminate the policy, Act and start-date years.
n: The SEZ Act was enacted in 2005. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 79-80]
xs: The **SEZ Act** was enacted in **2005** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was passed by Parliament in May 2005 and got **President's assent** on **June 23, 2005**.
**2000** = SEZ policy; **2006** = Act and Rules came into effect; **1965** = Kandla EPZ.
xa: ⚠ "SEZ is set up **primarily** to generate employment" is not true — the primary aim is **exports** (APPSC-G2 2017 key).
**s.18** allows an **IFSC** in an SEZ; **s.10AA** gives the tax holiday (**100-50-50**).
SEZ (Amendment) Rules 2025 cut minimum land for semiconductor SEZs from **50 ha to 10 ha**.

nfd5abc15680.s: A principal institutional feature introduced under the SEZ framework is:
o: Mandatory clearance only through the Reserve Bank of India
Single-window clearance for Central and State matters
Separate customs clearance for every unit
nfd5abc15680.x: The SEZ framework provides single-window clearance for matters involving both the Central and State Governments.
nfd5abc15680.tq: Match the institutional mechanism with its practical administrative purpose.
xs: The SEZ framework gives **single-window clearance for Central and State matters** — option **(3)**.
This came with the SEZ Act and **SEZ Rules** in force from **10 Feb 2006**.
xa: SEZ proposals go via the **State** to the **Board of Approval**.
SEZs can be set up **jointly or severally** by the Centre, a State or **any person**.
**100% FDI** is allowed under the automatic route for most manufacturing in SEZs.

n03019700de6.s: Proposals for setting up SEZs are routed through the State Government to which body for approval?
n03019700de6.x: Proposals for SEZs are routed through the State Government to the Board of Approval.
n03019700de6.tq: Identify the specific approving body rather than a neighbouring economic institution.
xs: SEZ proposals go through the State to the **Board of Approval** — option **(2)**.
The SEZ framework provides **single-window clearance** for Central and State matters.
xa: Developers: Centre, State or **any person**, **jointly or severally**.
⚠ Trap: SEZs are set up primarily for **exports**, not employment (APPSC-G2 **2017** key).
**s.18** of the SEZ Act allows an **IFSC** in an SEZ.

n1b3fbe370bc.s: With the SEZ framework in force from 2006, which existing units were allowed to convert into Special Economic Zones?
o: Export Processing Zones and Export Oriented Units
National Investment and Manufacturing Zones and Coastal Economic Zones
Industrial corridors and industrial smart cities
n1b3fbe370bc.x: Existing EPZs and EOUs could convert into SEZs (Kandla, for example, became an SEZ). NIMZs and CEZs are later, separate concepts; corridors and smart cities are not SEZ conversions; FTWZs are a type of SEZ purpose, not a unit that converts.
xs: Existing **Export Processing Zones** and **Export Oriented Units** could convert into SEZs — option **(1)**.
**Kandla**, for instance, began as an EPZ and later became an SEZ.
**Coastal Economic Zones** are a separate **Sagarmala** concept, and industrial corridors are not SEZ conversions.
xa: A **Free Trade Warehousing Zone** is one of the purposes an SEZ may serve.
SEZ Act and Rules in force from **10 Feb 2006**.
EPZs had existed from **1965**.

n697aab565a3.s: Which one of the following was identified as a criticism of the performance of SEZs?
o: SEZs received more than half of total foreign direct investment.
Domestic tariff area sales were completely unrestricted.
SEZs received less than 3% of foreign direct investment.
No SEZ units were shut during the five-year period.
n697aab565a3.x: SEZs received less than 3% of FDI. Other criticisms included capped DTA sales and the closure of many units.
n697aab565a3.tq: Select the qualified performance criticism and reject reversed or absolute statements.
xs: A criticism is that SEZs received **less than 3% of FDI** — option **(3)**.
**DTA sales** were **capped**, not unrestricted.
**466 units shut** in five years across seven SEZs (**100** in FY25), so option (4) is false.
xa: Export growth was **<4%** in FY25.
Other criticisms: land acquisition (**Nandigram**), revenue loss, under-used land, **WTO**-inconsistent subsidies.
Scale: **6,695** units, investment **₹7,82,192 crore**.

n7995d16653c.s: Coastal Economic Zones were proposed under which programme's port-led industrialisation pillar?
n7995d16653c.x: The 14 CEZs, port-proximate clusters and SEZs, were proposed under Sagarmala's port-led industrialisation pillar.
xa: Corridors are integrated with **Sagarmala** to **cut logistics costs** (Jan 2026).
**BHAVYA** (2026) separately plans **100** plug-and-play industrial parks.
⚠ Kandla was **Asia's first EPZ** (1965) — an EPZ, not a CEZ.

na89c1dd89d5.s: The Baba Kalyani Committee, constituted in 2018, recommended renaming SEZs as:
na89c1dd89d5.x: The committee recommended renaming SEZs as 3Es—Employment and Economic Enclaves.
na89c1dd89d5.tq: Discriminate among closely similar expansions of an official abbreviation.
xs: The **Baba Kalyani Committee** (2018) proposed renaming SEZs **"3Es" — Employment and Economic Enclaves** — option **(3)**.
It also called for separate rules for **manufacturing and services**.
xa: Other recommendations: **extend the sunset clause** and a **unified IFSC regulator**.
The **DESH Bill** (Budget 2022-23) proposes to replace the SEZ Act.
DESH = **Development of Enterprise and Services Hubs**.

ncde5b0a131e.s: Which department and ministry are associated with NICDC?

Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
Department of Heavy Industry, Ministry of Steel

Operational smart cities: **Dholera** (Gujarat) and **Shendra-Bidkin** (Maharashtra).
AP nodes: **Orvakal** (HBIC) and **Kopparthy** (VCIC).

ne7de4247a73.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about BHAVYA?
o: It has an allocation of ₹33,660 crore.
It is implemented by NICDC through an SPV of NICDIT and a State agency.
It aims to establish 50 plug-and-play industrial parks.
ne7de4247a73.x: BHAVYA aims at 100 plug-and-play industrial parks, not 50; the other statements are correct.

NICDIT gets **₹3,000 crore** in BE **2026-27**.
Corridors come under **DPIIT**, Ministry of Commerce & Industry.

nd355ac9b5a8.s: The Orvakal industrial node in Andhra Pradesh is part of which corridor?
nd355ac9b5a8.x: Orvakal is on HBIC; Kopparthy is on VCIC and Krishnapatnam on CBIC.
xa: Orvakal: **2,621 acres**, **₹1,781 crore**.
Kopparthy: **2,596 acres**, **₹1,264 crore**.
⚠ **Orvakal** = HBIC (Kurnool); **Kopparthy** = VCIC (Kadapa).
**VCIC 2035** targets: manufacturing output **₹4.20 trillion**, **33%** women, **24x7** power.

n506644f193f.s: Special Economic Zones in India are set up primarily to:
o: Raise tax revenue for State Governments
n506644f193f.x: An SEZ is an export-oriented enclave; its primary aim is exports. Employment is a benefit but 'primarily to generate employment' was the wrong option in the APPSC-G2 2017 key. Raising State revenue or giving land to farmers is not its purpose.
n506644f193f.tq: SEZ primary aim = exports, not jobs.
xs: SEZs are set up primarily to **promote exports** — option **(2)**.
⚠ "Primarily to **generate employment**" is NOT true — the **APPSC-G2 2017** key.
Raising State revenue or giving land to landless farmers is not their purpose; land acquisition is in fact a criticism.
xa: SEZ exports FY 2024-25: **₹14,63,669 crore (~US$173 bn)**, **~21%** of India's exports.
SEZs employ **31,77,893** people in **6,695** units.
The **Baba Kalyani Committee** proposed renaming SEZs **"Employment and Economic Enclaves"**.

n486842cc0bf.s: The Nandigram protests of 2007 were associated with opposition to land acquisition for a:
o: Free Trade Warehousing Zone at Kandla
n486842cc0bf.x: Nandigram in West Bengal witnessed violent protests in 2007 against land acquisition for a chemical-hub SEZ.
n486842cc0bf.tq: Link the place and year to the specific project that triggered the conflict.
xs: Nandigram (**West Bengal, 2007**) saw protests against land acquisition for a **chemical-hub SEZ** — option **(2)**.
The protests were **violent**, making Nandigram the symbol of SEZ land disputes.
xa: Other criticisms: **revenue loss**, **under-used land**, **WTO**-inconsistent export subsidies.
**466 units shut** in five years across seven SEZs.
⚠ **Falta** EPZ is also in **West Bengal**.

n72a515f314d.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or debate concerning SEZs and industrial policy?
o: Land acquisition, including the Nandigram controversy
Guaranteed expansion of employment in every notified SEZ
n72a515f314d.x: Land acquisition, revenue loss, under-used land and WTO-inconsistent export subsidies are identified criticisms. Guaranteed employment expansion in every SEZ is not listed as a criticism.
n72a515f314d.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated criticism set.
xs: **Guaranteed expansion of employment in every SEZ** is NOT a listed criticism — option **(4)**.
Listed criticisms: **land acquisition** (**Nandigram**), **revenue loss**, **under-used land**, **WTO**-inconsistent export subsidies.
xa: Slowdown: **466 units shut** in five years; export growth **<4%** in FY25.
SEZs get **<3%** of FDI.
⚠ SEZs are primarily for **exports**, not employment (APPSC-G2 2017 key).

n259280c74e9.s: The criticism that SEZ incentives may be WTO-inconsistent relates primarily to:
n259280c74e9.x: One criticism is that export subsidies associated with SEZs may be inconsistent with WTO obligations.
n259280c74e9.tq: Match the international trade concern with its precise subject.
xs: The WTO-inconsistency criticism concerns **export subsidies** — option **(3)**.
It is listed with **land acquisition**, **revenue loss** and **under-used land**.
xa: SEZ tax holidays (**s.10AA**) were phased out **2017-2020** under a sunset clause.
The **DESH Bill** removes the positive **NFE** condition.
**Nandigram** (2007) is the land-acquisition example.

nbebe4977410.s: Which of the following is the correct description of a free trade zone?
o: An area reserved exclusively for agricultural exports
An area where goods may be landed, stored, processed and re-exported without customs duty
An area where imported goods must be consumed before re-export
An area where only domestically produced goods may be sold without State taxes
nbebe4977410.x: A free trade zone permits goods to be landed, stored, processed and re-exported without payment of customs duty.
nbebe4977410.tq: Apply the operational definition by checking all four permitted activities.
xs: A **free trade zone** is an area where goods may be **landed, stored, processed and re-exported without customs duty** — option **(2)**.
No restriction to agricultural exports or to domestic consumption is part of the definition.
xa: **Kandla (Gujarat)** was India's **first Free Trade Zone** and **Asia's first EPZ** (**1965**).
Existing **EPZs** and **EOUs** could convert into SEZs.
An SEZ may also serve as a **Free Trade Warehousing Zone**.

n948116b891b.s: The National Infrastructure Pipeline (FY2019-20 to FY2024-25) envisaged an investment of about:
n948116b891b.x: The NIP envisaged about ₹111 lakh crore across both economic and social infrastructure.
xa: Largest share: **Energy ~24%**, then roads **~18%**, urban **~17%**, railways **~12%**.
Funding split: Centre **39%**, States **40%**, private **21%**.
The pipeline now stands at **₹185-213 lakh crore** across **30+** sectors.

o: Greenfield assets, with ownership transferred to buyers
Brownfield assets, with ownership permanently transferred
Brownfield core infrastructure assets, with ownership retained by the Government
Greenfield assets, with ownership retained by the Government

n24995243bc0.s: The value of National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0 (FY26-FY30) is:
n24995243bc0.x: NMP 2.0 is valued at ₹16.72 lakh crore (including ₹5.8 lakh crore of private participation); NMP 1.0 was ₹6 lakh crore.

nd5af6f7b18c.s: In NMP 1.0, which sector was the largest sector?

NMP 2.0 largest share: **highways/MMLPs/ropeways 26%**.
⚠ NIP's largest share is **Energy**, not roads.

n9437bed0837.s: Which of the following is NOT an instrument of asset monetisation under the NMP?
n9437bed0837.x: NMP instruments include PPP concessions, InvITs, TOT and securitisation; cancelling public ownership is not one, since ownership stays with the Government.
xa: NMP covers **brownfield** core infrastructure.

nb866fc2b5f3.s: The National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0, launched on 23 February 2026, was prepared by which body, and which sector group has the largest share in it?

nb866fc2b5f3.x: NMP 2.0 (FY26-FY30, ₹16.72 lakh crore) was prepared by NITI Aayog, and highways/MMLPs/ropeways have the largest share (26%), followed by power 17%, railways 16%, ports 16% and coal 13%. The other pairings are wrong.
xs: NMP 2.0 was prepared by **NITI Aayog**; largest share **highways/MMLPs/ropeways** — option **(1)**.

xa: NMP 2.0: **FY26-FY30**, **₹16.72 lakh crore** (incl. ₹5.8 lakh crore private).
NMP 1.0's largest sector was **Roads**; **coal** gave the most actual monetisation.
Monitoring: **CGAM** under the **Cabinet Secretary**.

n536704d4ca7.s: Andhra Pradesh’s Blue Economy target is to reach approximately:

Largest private port: **Krishnapatnam** (BOST 2004).

n01ce6b187d4.s: The estimated multiplier associated with infrastructure capital expenditure is:

n411e78241d8.s: NaBFID, set up under the NaBFID Act, 2021, has a paid-up capital of:
n411e78241d8.x: NaBFID was established under the NaBFID Act, 2021 with Rs 20,000 crore paid-up capital and a Rs 5,000 crore grant.

n61de7634746.s: The National Monetisation Pipeline was announced in the:
n61de7634746.x: The National Monetisation Pipeline was announced in the Union Budget 2021-22.
n61de7634746.tq: Distinguish the announcement year from later implementation and revision years.
xs: The NMP was announced in **Union Budget 2021-22** — option **(3)**.

xa: **NMP 1.0**: **FY22-FY25**, **₹6 lakh crore**; largest sector **Roads**.
**NMP 2.0**: **FY26-FY30**, **₹16.72 lakh crore**; launched **23 Feb 2026**.
⚠ Budget **2025-26** figure of **₹10 lakh crore** for NMP 2.0 is superseded.

n8cd4c3f91cb.s: PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan is best described as a:

n67e59691c32.s: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of Sagarmala?

nae6d43fc91f.s: The National Rail Plan 2030 seeks to raise the railways' share in freight from 28% to:
nae6d43fc91f.x: The National Rail Plan 2030 aims to raise rail's freight share from 28% to 45% and to expand Kavach.

n434536c07b7.s: Bhogapuram airport near Visakhapatnam is being developed by GMR under which model?

Bhogapuram runway: **3,800 m**.

ne1f03d5e5ae.s: By 2030, Andhra Pradesh aims to have which combination of infrastructure?

n33bebbd1691.x: Andhra Pradesh has a coastline of about 1,053.07 km, the 3rd longest in India. The other length/rank combinations are wrong.

Greenfield ports: **Ramayapatnam** (Nellore), **Mulapeta** (Srikakulam), **Machilipatnam** (Krishna).

nad4cf284003.s: Which body is responsible for technical planning and generation adequacy plans in India's power sector?

**CERC** = central and inter-State **tariffs**; **PNGRB** = downstream oil-gas regulator; **BEE** = **star labelling**.

**Electricity Act 2003**: tariffs by **ERCs**; **Section 63** = competitive bidding.
Demand-supply gap fell from **4.2%** to **zero** (**Nov 2025**).

n58ee2385061.s: The Electricity Act, 2003 replaced the Indian Electricity Act, 1910, the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948 and the:
n58ee2385061.x: The 2003 Act replaced the 1910 Act, the 1948 Supply Act and the Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act, 1998.

**Section 63** = tariff by **competitive bidding**.
⚠ **UDAY** (2015) = DISCOM debt takeover; **RDSS** (2021) = AT&C losses + smart meters.

n6e314525f54.s: Under which Section of the Electricity Act, 2003 are tariffs determined through competitive bidding?

n6e314525f54.tq: Use the article-or-section number directly, with nearby statutory provisions as distractors.
xs: **Section 63** of the Electricity Act 2003 covers **competitive bidding** — option **(2)**.
Tariffs otherwise are set by **ERCs**.
xa: **APERC** approved **1,600 MW** coal power via **Section 63 DBFOO** bidding.
That is the first phase of **5,588 MW** by **2035-36** (Aug 2026).
The Act also introduced **open access**.

nc5330e02c9f.s: India's AT&C losses fell from 22.62% in FY14 to ____ in FY25.
nc5330e02c9f.x: AT&C losses fell to 15.04% in FY25, and the demand-supply gap fell from 4.2% to zero by November 2025.

Record peak demand: **270.82 GW** (**21 May 2026**).
AP under RDSS: **₹15,083.14 crore**.

nf0b76487dd7.s: APERC approved how much coal power through Section 63 DBFOO bidding as the first phase of Andhra Pradesh's plan?
nf0b76487dd7.x: APERC approved 1,600 MW, the first phase of a planned 5,588 MW by 2035-36.
xa: **Section 63** of the **Electricity Act 2003** = competitive bidding.
**APERC** sets State tariffs; **CERC** central/inter-State.
Largest thermal: **Vindhyachal** (MP) **4,760 MW**.

ned089d8650d.s: The original 2010 solar capacity target of the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission was:

nb299c94e498.s: The MNRE's Solar Park Scheme mainly makes which of the following available to developers?

xs: **Vindhyachal** (NTPC) is in **Madhya Pradesh**, **4,760 MW** — option **(1)**.
**1,000 MW** is the **Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park** in AP.
xa: **Bhadla** (Rajasthan) is a desert/wasteland solar model.
**Solar Park Scheme** (MNRE) gives parks land + transmission.
Record peak demand **270.82 GW** (21 May 2026).

n6f42d28ce5e.s: The National Biofuel Coordination Committee is chaired by the:
o: Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Minister of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare
Minister of New and Renewable Energy
n6f42d28ce5e.x: The Petroleum Minister chairs the National Biofuel Coordination Committee, which approves the use of surplus food grains for ethanol.
n6f42d28ce5e.tq: Use the ‘who heads the body?’ approach and distinguish the petroleum portfolio from neighbouring ministries.
xs: The **NBCC** is chaired by the **Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas** — option **(2)**.

**National Policy on Biofuels 2018**; **EBP** target **20%** by **2025**.

n6cb40f4c799.s: A proposal is made to use surplus food grains for ethanol production. Which body is responsible for approving such use?
n6cb40f4c799.x: Approval for using surplus food grains for ethanol is given by the National Biofuel Coordination Committee.

The NBCC is chaired by the **Petroleum Minister**.
**CEA** is a power-sector planning body, not a biofuel approver.
xa: ⚠ PYQ 2025: A and R true, but **R not the explanation** (farmers' price risk).
EBP: **20%** blending by **2025** — cuts oil imports, helps sugarcane farmers.
India imports about **80%** of petroleum.

nc7b52d7caa0.s: India meets roughly what share of its petroleum requirement through imports?
nc7b52d7caa0.x: India imports more than 80% of its petroleum requirement.
xa: **SPRs**: **Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru, Padur** — about **9.5 days** of cover.
**IEA** norm: **90 days** of cover.
Domestic supply boost: **HELP**, **OALP**, coal gasification.
nc7b52d7caa0.fixed: India imports ~85% of crude and ~half of its natural gas, not 25%

ncf6aa6a18d4.s: Which of the following is the correct set of locations of India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPRs)?
ncf6aa6a18d4.x: The Strategic Petroleum Reserves mentioned are located at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur.
ncf6aa6a18d4.tq: Test a named-location list as a complete set and reject location substitutions.
xs: India's SPRs are at **Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur** — option **(3)**.

xa: ⚠ **IEA** norm is **90 days** — India is far short.
Import dependence: **80%** petroleum, **25%** gas.
Decontrol: petrol **2010**, diesel **2014**.

nd43010410f8.s: India's strategic petroleum reserves provide about how many days of import cover (IEA norm: 90 days)?
nd43010410f8.x: India's SPR capacity gives about 9.5 days of import cover, far below the IEA norm of 90 days.
xa: SPR sites: **Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru, Padur**.
India imports about **80%** of petroleum.
**HELP** and **OALP** aim to boost domestic supply.

n5f21fd001b4.s: The nodal agency of the Andhra Pradesh Solar Power Policy, 2018 is:
n5f21fd001b4.x: NREDCAP is the nodal agency; the policy notes the State has about 300 sunny days a year.
xa: Govt was to develop **4,000 MW** initially.
**PM-KUSUM** in AP covers **2.93 lakh** pumps.
**Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park**: **1,000 MW**.

n4db0ef59148.s: PM-KUSUM in Andhra Pradesh covers about how many pumps?
n4db0ef59148.x: PM-KUSUM in Andhra Pradesh covers 2.93 lakh pumps.
xa: AP under **RDSS**: **₹15,083.14 crore**.
**NREDCAP** is the nodal agency of the **AP Solar Power Policy 2018**.
**AP ICEP 2024** covers RE, pumped storage, green hydrogen, biofuels, EV charging.

nc7a2c7b0583.s: Andhra Pradesh's Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy, which aims to make the State a global green hydrogen hub, was issued in:
nc7a2c7b0583.x: The Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy, 2023 aims to make Andhra Pradesh a global green hydrogen hub.
xa: ICEP 2024 offers **capital subsidies + tax exemptions** (APSES 2024-25 **p.336**).
**AP Solar Power Policy 2018**: nodal **NREDCAP**.
National Green Hydrogen Mission (**2023**): **5 MMT** a year by **2030**.

n38beca6a657.s: The expression 'Licence-Permit-Quota Raj', used to describe the pre-1991 regime of controls in India, was coined by:
n38beca6a657.x: C. Rajagopalachari coined 'Licence-Permit-Quota Raj' to criticise the control regime that was a long-term cause of the 1991 crisis. Nehru led the planned economy, Mahalanobis designed the Second Plan model, and Raja Chelliah headed the 1991 tax reform committee.
xs: **C. Rajagopalachari** coined **Licence-Permit-Quota Raj** — option **(2)**.
**Raja Chelliah** headed the **tax** reform committee, not the term's author.
xa: The control regime (incl. **MRTP 1970**) was a long-term cause of the crisis.
1991 **Industrial Policy** abolished licensing for all but **5-6** industries.
MRTP **asset limits** were abolished in 1991.

nb050ee6cfbd.s: Who is widely called the 'father of Indian economic reforms'?
nb050ee6cfbd.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao is called the father of Indian economic reforms; Dr. Manmohan Singh is regarded as the architect of liberalisation.
xa: The era is called the "**Manmohan-Rao era**".
Rao took office on **21 June 1991**.
Some liberalisation had begun under **Rajiv Gandhi** in the **1980s**.

n0e06670831f.s: The Narasimham Committee of 1991 was primarily concerned with:
o: Industrial licensing and foreign trade quotas
Financial-sector reform, including interest deregulation and private banks
n0e06670831f.x: The Narasimham Committee focused on financial-sector reform, including interest deregulation and the development of private banks such as HDFC and ICICI.
n0e06670831f.tq: Distinguish the committee's sector from neighbouring reform committees.
xs: The **Narasimham Committee** (**1991**) dealt with **financial-sector reform** — interest deregulation and private banks — option **(3)**.
Private banks such as **HDFC** and **ICICI** were allowed.
**Insurance** reform was the **Malhotra Committee** (1993).
xa: ⚠ **Narasimham** = banking; **Chelliah** = tax; **Rangarajan** = disinvestment; **Malhotra** = insurance.
RBI shifted from **regulator to facilitator**.
**SEBI** became statutory in **1992**.

n157d24265ab.s: After the financial-sector reforms, the RBI was expected to shift from being a regulator to being a:
n157d24265ab.x: The reforms envisaged the RBI moving from direct regulation towards facilitation of the financial system.
xa: **SEBI** became statutory in **1992**.
**Narasimham Committee**: interest deregulation, private banks (HDFC, ICICI).
Stabilisation used **tight monetary policy by RBI** to control inflation.

n525991b2382.s: The sharp reduction in the list of industries reserved for the public sector in 1991 is known as
n525991b2382.x: Dereservation means reducing the industries reserved for the public sector and opening them to private participation.
n525991b2382.tq: Discriminate between similarly prefixed reform terms.
xs: Cutting industries reserved for the public sector is **dereservation** — option **(3)**.
It happened in **1991**, opening those industries to private players.
**Disinvestment** = sale of PSU equity — a different privatisation measure.
xa: Sick units: **BIFR** set up to revive them.
**New PSE Policy (2021)** made strategic disinvestment a major reform.

nindian-economy-39-8.s: Reduction of tariffs and quantitative restrictions under the 1991 reforms is termed:
nindian-economy-39-8.x: Import liberalisation cut tariffs and QRs; de-licensing ended licensing, disinvestment sold PSE equity, globalisation integrated India with the world.
n: De-licensing is associated with international trade. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
Deregulation is associated with foreign investment. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
Import liberalisation is associated with multinational corporation participation. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
Liberalisation promotes greater market orientation. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
xa: Average import tariff fell from **~125%** (late 1980s) to **~30%** (early 2000s).
Remaining **QRs removed April 2001**.
⚠ LERMS **1992** → unified rate **1993** → convertibility **1994** → WTO **1995**.

nindian-economy-37-11.s: LPG reforms were associated with which of the following?
nindian-economy-37-11.x: The LPG reforms opened the door to multinational corporations. Licensing, the joint sector and public-sector dominance belong to the pre-1991 policies.
n: LPG reforms were associated with multinational corporations. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
xs: **LPG reforms** were associated with **multinational corporations** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Globalisation facilitated **expanded entry and participation of MNCs**.
**Industrial licensing**, the **joint sector** and **public-sector** dominance belong to pre-1991 policy.
xa: Indian MNCs that went global: **Tata, Reliance, Infosys, Sun Pharma**.
Licensing abolished for all but **5-6** industries.
**Navratnas (1996)**: **9** PSUs; **Miniratnas**: **97** profit-making PSUs.

nd43ab0c42b2.s: Which one of the following represents a long-term cause rather than an immediate trigger of the 1991 crisis?
o: Persistent fiscal profligacy and rising fiscal deficit
nd43ab0c42b2.x: Persistent fiscal profligacy was a long-term domestic structural cause. The other three were immediate external-financing or geopolitical pressures.
nd43ab0c42b2.tq: Find the structural domestic factor among short-term external shocks.
xs: **Persistent fiscal profligacy** is a **long-term cause** — option **(3)**.
**NRI deposit flight**, the **Gulf War** and **foreign banks stopping lending** were **immediate triggers**.
xa: Other long-term causes: **Licence-Permit-Quota Raj** (MRTP 1970), **PSU losses**, **weak exports**.
⚠ **9.4%** = Centre + States; **8.4%** = Centre's GFD.

nindian-economy-39-1.s: The 1991 New Economic Policy was introduced primarily to address which of the following?
o: Dominance of the public and joint sectors
Decline in agriculture's share of GDP
nindian-economy-39-1.x: The 1991 New Economic Policy was a response to a severe balance-of-payments crisis, when foreign reserves covered only about two weeks of imports.
nindian-economy-39-1.tq: Recall the trigger for the 1991 reforms.
n: The 1991 New Economic Policy was introduced to address the severe 1991 Balance of Payments crisis. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
xs: The **1991 New Economic Policy** was introduced to address the **severe 1991 Balance of Payments crisis** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Forex reserves had fallen to **$975 million (June 1991)** — about **two weeks** of imports.
SEZs, joint-sector dominance and agriculture's share were not its trigger.
xa: Crisis indicators: **high inflation**, **low forex reserves**, **large fiscal deficit** (APPSC 2025).
Triggers: **Gulf War (Aug 1990)**, political instability, **NRI deposit flight**.
**67 tonnes of gold** were pledged to the **Bank of England and UBS**.

n2bdbe1a67af.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the causes of India's 1991 balance of payments crisis?
o: The Gulf War led to a doubling of oil prices.
Current account deficits had been financed by foreign borrowing since the 1980s.
Remittances from the Gulf region rose sharply.
n2bdbe1a67af.x: Gulf remittances dried up rather than rising; the other three were causes of the crisis.
xa: Other trigger: **collapse of the Soviet Union** (**Dec 1991**) — a lost trading partner.
Political instability: **two changes of government** Dec 1989 - June 1991.
Long-term cause: **fiscal profligacy** — GFD **5.4%** (1981-82) to **8.0%** (1989-90).

nb50ea3d9032.s: The foreign exchange reserves of India in June 1991 were approximately
o: $975 million, sufficient for about two weeks of imports
$69.3 billion, sufficient for about one year of imports
$22.8 billion, sufficient for about three months of imports
$9.75 billion, sufficient for about six months of imports
nb50ea3d9032.x: India's foreign exchange reserves stood at approximately $975 million in June 1991, covering only about two weeks of imports.
nb50ea3d9032.tq: Match the crisis-year figure with its associated coverage period.
xs: Reserves were **$975 million** in **June 1991** — enough for about **two weeks** of imports — option **(1)**.
**$69.3 bn** was external debt; **$22.8 bn** was external debt in **1983-84**.
xa: Reserves later rose to **$701.4 bn** (~**11 months** of import cover).
⚠ Forex cover: **2 weeks (1991)** vs **over 11 months** now.
In **May 2026** the PM urged citizens to cut fuel, gold and foreign-travel spending — a step not taken even in **1991**.

nc9295a0156a.s: The gross fiscal deficit of the Centre in 1990-91 was approximately
nc9295a0156a.x: The Centre's gross fiscal deficit was 8.4 per cent of GDP in 1990-91, compared with 6.1 per cent in 1980-81. The 9.4 per cent figure refers to the combined Centre and States figure.
nc9295a0156a.tq: Distinguish the Centre-only figure from the combined Centre and States figure.
xs: The Centre's GFD in 1990-91 was **8.4 per cent** of GDP — option **(4)**.
⚠ **9.4%** is the **combined Centre + States** figure; **3.2%** is the trade deficit/CAD share.
xa: Inflation about **12%**; GDP growth **1.1%**.
Govt internal debt reached **53%** of GDP (1990-91).

n75e9a77e40d.s: The Indian rupee became convertible on the current account in:
n75e9a77e40d.x: The rupee became market-determined in 1993 and current-account convertible in 1994; capital-account convertibility stayed partial.
xa: ⚠ Devaluation **1991** → market rate **1993** → convertibility **1994**.
**LERMS (March 1992)**: dual rate — **60%** at market rate, **40%** at official rate.
**WTO** founding member **1995**; **FERA → FEMA** in **1999**.

n50a2017c909.s: Which of the following was NOT a fiscal policy measure of 1991?
n50a2017c909.x: The tax net was widened, not contracted; expenditure control, subsidy cuts and better tax collection were part of the package.
xa: Also included: discipline in managing **Centre and State funds**.
Lower peak income/corporate tax rates (**Chelliah**).
Fiscal deficit (Centre + States) had reached **9.4%** of GDP.

n5a134a72806.s: Under the post-1991 liberalisation measures, tax rates were ____ and the tax base was ____.
n5a134a72806.x: Tax rates were cut and the base widened, alongside scrapping MRTP asset limits, deregulating interest rates and allowing private banks.
xa: **SEBI** became statutory in **1992**.
Industrial licensing abolished except for a few (**5-6**) industries.
Liberalisation = **reduction of state control**.

n7f9b41dca6f.s: After the 1991 delicensing, delicensed firms got:
o: Freedom in pricing but curbs on expansion
Price controls and curbs on expansion
Price controls but no curbs on expansion
Freedom in pricing and no curbs on expansion
n7f9b41dca6f.x: Delicensed firms gained pricing freedom and faced no expansion curbs; licensing stayed only for a few (5-6) industries.
xa: MRTP asset limits, pre-entry restrictions and merger controls were abolished.
Telecom, banking and civil aviation were **reshaped** by reforms.
**Dereservation**: public-sector-reserved industries cut sharply in **1991**.

n6f1831def02.s: Which of the following was NOT removed from the MRTP framework by the Industrial Policy of 1991?
n6f1831def02.x: The 1991 policy abolished MRTP asset limits, pre-entry restrictions and merger/expansion controls; SEBI's statutory status was a separate financial-market reform.
xa: In the 1980s the MRTP limit had been raised to **₹100 crore**.
**MRTP 1970** was part of the Licence-Permit-Quota Raj.
Licensing abolished for all but **5-6** industries.

nc2ad8b7b53e.s: When the Navratna scheme was introduced, how many public sector undertakings were given Navratna status?
nc2ad8b7b53e.x: The Navratna scheme initially covered nine PSUs, distinct from the 97 profit-making Miniratnas.
xa: ⚠ **9** Navratnas vs **97** Miniratnas.
PSU autonomy also via **MoUs**.
Disinvestment aims: **financial discipline, modernisation, FDI**.
nc2ad8b7b53e.fixed: Navratna scheme (9 PSUs) was introduced in 1997, not 1996

n77322e4e289.s: India removed its remaining quantitative restrictions on imports in:
n77322e4e289.x: The remaining QRs went in April 2001; average tariffs fell from about 125% to about 30% and general customs duty was later cut to 10%.
xa: Import licensing was dismantled; **EXIM scrips** and quotas removed.
**DGFT** changed from controller of trade to "**facilitator**".
Strategy shifted from **import substitution to export promotion**.

nc3c0489337c.s: Disinvestment of PSU equity under the 1991 reforms was first undertaken mainly to:
nc3c0489337c.x: Disinvestment was first used to bridge the fiscal deficit and only later for efficiency; nationalisation was not part of the NEP.
xa: **Dereservation** (1991) opened public-sector-reserved industries to private players.
**New PSE Policy (2021)** for **Atmanirbhar Bharat**.

n0afbb9e1a99.x: Globalisation expanded trade and technology access, but imports grew faster than exports.
xa: India's world trade share had fallen from **1.78%** (1950) to **0.6%** (1995).
IT/outsourcing boom **cushioned the CAD**.
CAD peaked at **4.8%** of GDP (**FY13**).

n17422fda018.s: Which of the following was NOT an element of the Washington Consensus?
n17422fda018.x: Privatisation, deregulation and property rights were among the ten Washington Consensus rules; expanding import quotas was not.
xa: It is blamed for the **1997** and **2008** crises.
It is now seen as **obsolete** (14 Mar 2026).
SAP conditions also included **currency devaluation** and **austerity**.

nae8d810e0c9.s: During the 1991 BoP crisis, about how many tonnes of gold were pledged to the Bank of England and UBS?
nae8d810e0c9.x: About 67 tonnes of gold were pledged, an IMF loan was taken, and the rupee was devalued in two steps (1 and 3 July 1991).
xa: Earlier IMF borrowings came in **July 1990** and **Jan 1991**.
Market-determined exchange rate came in **1993**.
⚠ **Demonetisation** was **not** part of 1991 (India's were in **1978** and **2016**).

nbe62fb726a6.s: The principal immediate purpose of the 1991 rupee devaluation was to:
o: Increase the price of Indian exports in foreign markets
Make Indian exports cheaper and help correct the balance of payments
Finance the fiscal deficit through currency expansion
nbe62fb726a6.x: Devaluation makes domestic goods relatively cheaper for foreign buyers and was undertaken to help address the balance of payments crisis.
nbe62fb726a6.tq: Apply the economic effect of devaluation rather than recall only its date.
xs: Devaluation aimed to **make Indian exports cheaper** and **correct the balance of payments** — option **(3)**.
This was the **APPSC 2024** key.
Option (1) is the opposite effect; capital account convertibility is still **not** full.
xa: Devaluation: about **20%**, in two steps on **1 and 3 July 1991**.
**Currency devaluation** is a standard **SAP** conditionality.
Strategy shift: **import substitution → export promotion**.

n0dea1e2c345.s: Stabilisation measures under the New Economic Policy are essentially:
n0dea1e2c345.x: Stabilisation corrects short-term imbalances (fiscal deficit, inflation, BoP) through demand management; structural adjustment is the supply side.
xa: Lead institutions: **IMF** (stabilisation) and **World Bank (IBRD)** (structural adjustment).
Stabilisation tools: subsidy cuts, **tight monetary policy** by RBI, **rupee devaluation**.
Some UPSC notes also list trade liberalisation under stabilisation.

nfe71a2f5c3f.s: Structural Adjustment Programmes are best described as
o: short-term central-bank operations for controlling currency circulation
domestic programmes confined to agricultural subsidies
WTO agreements dealing exclusively with customs valuation
IMF and World Bank loan packages intended to reduce fiscal imbalances and adjust economies for long-term growth
nfe71a2f5c3f.x: SAPs are IMF and World Bank loan packages designed to reduce fiscal imbalances and promote long-term economic adjustment and growth.
nfe71a2f5c3f.tq: Identify the defining combination of institutions, loans and long-term objectives.
xs: SAPs are **IMF/World Bank loan packages** to **reduce fiscal imbalances** and **adjust economies for long-term growth** — option **(4)**.
This is the **APPSC 2018** definition.
xa: Conditions: **austerity, privatisation, deregulation**, **currency devaluation**, better tax collection.
SAP outcomes raised poverty in the Global South — growth fell from **3.2% to 0.7%** a year.
The **Washington Consensus** (**10** rules) is now seen as obsolete.

n8c209a86821.s: Which plan began immediately after the phase of structural adjustment and macroeconomic stabilisation?
n8c209a86821.x: The Eighth Plan, covering 1992–97, began after structural adjustment and macroeconomic stabilisation.
n8c209a86821.tq: Link the plan period with the reform transition rather than with the preceding Annual Plans.
xs: The **Eighth Plan (1992-97)** began right after structural adjustment and macro-stabilisation — option **(2)**.
The **Sixth** and **Seventh** Plans saw rising deficits — average GFD **6.3%** and **8.2%**.
xa: Average growth **6.8%** from **1993-94**.

nindian-economy-37-8.s: Structural adjustment under the 1991 reforms is:
nindian-economy-37-8.x: Structural adjustment is long-term and supply-side, while stabilisation is short-term and demand-side.
n: Stabilisation is short-term in nature. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
Stabilisation is demand-side in nature. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
Structural adjustment is long-term in nature. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
Structural adjustment is supply-side in nature. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
xa: Lead institution: stabilisation = **IMF**; structural adjustment = **World Bank (IBRD)**.
Stabilisation comes **first**; structural adjustment follows or runs alongside.
The **Eighth Plan (1992-97)** began right after structural adjustment and stabilisation.

nindian-economy-37-9.s: Which of the following best describes free trade?
o: Reduction or removal of trade barriers
Provision of an internationally competitive environment
Creation of a level playing field for exports
nindian-economy-37-9.x: Free trade means reducing or removing trade barriers such as tariffs and quotas. The other options are SEZ objectives.
nindian-economy-37-9.tq: Discriminate free trade from SEZ aims.
n: Free trade involves the reduction or removal of trade barriers. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 54-56]
xs: **Free trade** = the **reduction or removal of trade barriers** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The other options describe aims such as attracting investment and competitiveness, not the meaning of free trade.
xa: **Globalisation** involves the **reduction of import duties** on capital goods.
**Import substitution** gave way to **export promotion** after **1991**.
**WTO** founding member, **1995** — successor to **GATT** (**1948**, **23** countries).

nf213b2d5de5.s: The Liberalised Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS) was introduced in:
nf213b2d5de5.x: LERMS came in March 1992 (60% at market rate, 40% at official rate); a unified market rate followed in March 1993.
xa: ⚠ LERMS **1992** → unified rate **1993** → convertibility **1994** → WTO **1995** → FEMA **1999** → QRs removed **2001**.
The rupee was devalued about **20%** on **1 and 3 July 1991**.
Capital account is only **partly** convertible.

nc71e11307dc.s: SEBI was given statutory status in:
nc71e11307dc.x: SEBI received statutory status in 1992; FEMA replaced FERA in 1999.
xa: **LERMS** came in **March 1992**.
Current account convertibility: **1994**.
WTO founding member: **1995**.

n6234f391e76.s: The growth of India's IT and outsourcing exports after 1991 helped to:
n6234f391e76.x: IT and outsourcing generated services exports that helped cushion India's current account deficit.
xa: **1,800+ Global Capability Centres** earned **$38.25 bn** of services exports in **July 2026**.
CAD was **0.8%** of GDP in **H1 FY26**; peak **4.8%** (FY13).
**ES 2025-26**: persistent CAD = structural cause of India's **high cost of capital**.

n2ce49779152.s: Which of the following was a feature of the economic groundwork laid during the 1980s?
o: Complete abolition of all industrial licensing
Broad-banding of licences and easier imports of capital goods
n2ce49779152.x: The 1980s saw broad-banding of licences, easier capital-goods imports, a higher MRTP limit and relaxation of FERA. Complete delicensing and FEMA came later.
n2ce49779152.tq: Distinguish preparatory 1980s measures from post-1991 reforms.
xs: The 1980s saw **broad-banding of licences** and **easier imports of capital goods** — option **(2)**.
Other 1980s steps: MRTP limit raised to **₹100 crore**; **FERA** eased.
Licensing was abolished (for all but **5-6** industries) only in **1991**; **FERA → FEMA** came in **1999**.
xa: This groundwork was under **Indira and Rajiv Gandhi** (**1984-89**).
Growth touched **5.5%**, breaking the Hindu rate, but was **debt-fuelled**.
⚠ **Full capital account convertibility** has still not been adopted.

nc72ea1ad67e.s: Which of the following sets contains only structural adjustment measures?
o: Delicensing, tariff reduction and public-sector disinvestment
Subsidy cuts, tight money and devaluation
Inflation control, deficit reduction and tight money
Demand management, exchange control and subsidy expansion
nc72ea1ad67e.x: Delicensing, tariff reduction and public-sector disinvestment are structural measures aimed at improving supply-side efficiency and long-term growth.
nc72ea1ad67e.tq: Group measures by their policy objective instead of by the reform year.
xs: **Delicensing, tariff reduction and PSU disinvestment** are structural adjustment measures — option **(1)**.
Structural adjustment is **supply-side**, aimed at **long-term** efficiency and growth.
Subsidy cuts, **tight money**, **devaluation** and deficit reduction are **stabilisation** tools.
xa: Structural tools also include **MRTP relaxation**, **FDI opening**, **QR removal**, export promotion.
Lead institution for structural adjustment: **World Bank (IBRD)**.
The **Eighth Plan (1992-97)** began right after structural adjustment and stabilisation.

nf9c76f4110f.s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the 1991 New Economic Policy?
nf9c76f4110f.x: Nationalisation was not a feature of the 1991 New Economic Policy. The policy instead promoted delicensing, disinvestment and greater foreign investment.
nf9c76f4110f.tq: Find the measure that reverses the reform direction.
xs: **Nationalisation** was NOT a 1991 NEP feature — option **(2)**.
It was the **odd one out** in **APPSC 2018**.
**Disinvestment**, **FDI liberalisation** and **delicensing** were NEP features.
xa: Also NOT NEP: strengthening the **License Raj/MRTP**, import substitution, more SSI reservation.
The economy was opened to foreign and private investment in **1991** (APPSC 2018).
FDI up to **100%** via automatic route in high-priority industries.

n5d4d2677561.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 1991 New Economic Policy?
o: Full capital-account convertibility was not adopted.
Devaluation, tariff cuts and removal of import quotas were external-sector measures.
FDI was liberalised through an automatic route in high-priority industries.
Demonetisation formed part of the 1991 reform package.
n5d4d2677561.x: Demonetisation was not part of the 1991 package; India's demonetisations were in 1978 and 2016.
xa: ⚠ **FDI in retail and defence** opened only much later.
**100% FDI in insurance** is now in place (May 2026).
**Nationalisation** was the odd one out (APPSC 2018).

n87d6d321942.s: Which of the following reflects the post-1991 reform direction?
o: Raising tariffs to protect domestic producers
Expanding the list of industries reserved for the public sector
Inviting FDI and FPI, with IT and services exports acting as a cushion
Restricting foreign investment to joint ventures with PSUs
n87d6d321942.x: The post-reform approach lowered tariffs, invited FDI and FPI, and benefited from IT and services exports as a cushion.
xa: Direction: **import substitution → export promotion**.
Economy moved to **enhanced global integration** (**PYQ 2025**).
**1,800+ GCCs** earned **$38.25 bn** of services exports in July 2026.

n2a71cca38f1.s: A persistent current account deficit has been identified as a structural cause of India's:
n2a71cca38f1.x: Persistent CAD has been identified as a structural cause of India's high cost of capital.
xa: CAD was **0.8%** of GDP in **H1 FY26**; peaked at **4.8%** (FY13).
In 1991 the CAD was **3.1-3.2%** of GDP.
IT/services exports help **cushion the CAD**.

nindian-economy-39-5.s: Integration of the domestic economy with the world economy, with greater participation of MNCs, is called:
nindian-economy-39-5.x: Globalisation linked India to the world economy through trade, FDI and technology flows and drew in more MNCs.
n: Globalisation integrates the domestic economy with the world economy. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
Globalisation integrates the domestic economy with the world economy. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
Globalisation facilitates expanded participation of Multinational Corporations. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
Globalisation occurs through trade. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
Globalisation occurs through foreign direct investment capital. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
Globalisation occurs through cross-border technology. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
Globalisation facilitates technology flows. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
Globalisation promotes greater global integration. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
Globalisation facilitates expanded entry of Multinational Corporations. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #39 · pp 58-60]
xa: Globalisation also involves the **reduction of import duties on capital goods**.
**Liberalisation** and **privatisation** are strategies; **globalisation** is their outcome, with **outsourcing** a major feature.
**FERA → FEMA** (**1999**) was a globalisation measure.

n4d57b96c3b4.s: Which adverse outcome was associated with the pattern of growth after economic reforms?
o: Growth became entirely dependent on public-sector employment.
Agriculture received all investment and labour-intensive sectors disappeared.
Capital-intensive sectors generated more jobs than the available labour force.
Agriculture was neglected and capital-intensive growth generated too few jobs.
n4d57b96c3b4.x: The pattern of growth was criticised for neglecting agriculture and concentrating growth in capital-intensive sectors, which created too few employment opportunities.
n4d57b96c3b4.tq: Identify the stated distributional and employment consequence rather than the aggregate growth benefit.
xs: **Agriculture was neglected** and **capital-intensive** growth created **too few jobs** — option **(4)**.
This is the **Beyond GDP essay** criticism.
xa: **Jobless growth**: output rose faster than jobs; many graduates end in **gig work**.
**Agrarian neglect**: public investment in agriculture lagged.
**Crony capitalism**: gains concentrated among large, politically connected firms.

n60d8d0a8d35.s: India's GDP growth in 1994–95 was about:
n60d8d0a8d35.x: Growth was below 1% in 1991–92, about 5% in 1992–94 and 6.3% in 1994–95.
xa: Average growth: **5.18%** in the 1980s vs **6.8%** from **1993-94**.
GDP growth had been **1.1%** in **1990-91**.

na58f83b5a40.s: Foreign-exchange reserves increased from approximately $975 million in 1991 to about
na58f83b5a40.x: Foreign-exchange reserves rose from about $975 million in 1991 to approximately $701.4 billion, providing around 11 months of import cover as stated.
na58f83b5a40.tq: Handle changes in units carefully when comparing a million figure with a billion figure.
xs: Reserves rose from **$975 million** (1991) to about **$701.4 billion** — option **(3)**.
That gives about **11 months** of import cover.
xa: ⚠ Forex cover: **2 weeks (1991)** vs **over 11 months** now.
In **1991** **67 tonnes of gold** had to be pledged abroad.
PM's **May 2026** appeal to save forex was not made even in 1991.

na9177f55f10.s: Which one of the following sectors remained largely a state monopoly after the reforms?
na9177f55f10.x: Railways remained a state monopoly, although modernisation continued to be pursued. The other sectors experienced greater private-sector participation or competition.
na9177f55f10.tq: Find the sector that was comparatively untouched among reform-exposed industries.
xs: **Railways** remained a **state monopoly** — option **(2)**.
Modernisation is still in progress (**LENS, May 2026**).
**Civil aviation**, **consumer electronics** and **telecom** saw private entry.
xa: Other slow sectors: **power distribution** (DISCOM privatisation debated), **agriculture**, **ports**.
**Civil aviation** saw **private airlines** enter.
Telecom: falling prices after private and foreign entry.

neb42d4db81a.s: Which of the following best illustrates the criticism of crony capitalism?
o: Agricultural investment increases uniformly across regions
Small firms exclusively control public-sector disinvestment
All firms receive equal access to public resources
Gains are concentrated among large, politically connected firms
neb42d4db81a.x: Crony capitalism is criticised because economic gains become concentrated among large firms with political connections.
neb42d4db81a.tq: Recognise the concept through its distributional consequence.
xs: Crony capitalism = **gains concentrated among large, politically connected firms** — option **(4)**.
It is one of three main criticisms of the reforms.
xa: **Jobless growth**: output rose faster than jobs.
**Agrarian neglect**: public investment in agriculture lagged.
**Washington Consensus** is now seen as obsolete (14 Mar 2026).

n8afaf8cd15a.s: The criticism of 'jobless growth' made against India's post-1991 growth refers to a situation in which:
o: Unemployment was eliminated but output stagnated
n8afaf8cd15a.x: Jobless growth means output grew much faster than jobs, so many people, including graduates, ended up in gig work. Employment rising faster than output is the reverse. A fall in both is a recession, and stagnant output with no unemployment does not describe the criticism.
n8afaf8cd15a.tq: Jobless growth = GDP up, jobs lag.
xs: Jobless growth = **output rose faster than employment** — option **(1)**.
Many **graduates** end up in **gig work**.
Option (2) is the reverse of the criticism.
xa: Growth was concentrated in **capital-intensive** sectors.
Other criticisms: **agrarian neglect** and **crony capitalism**.
Some formalisation, but the **informal sector** stays dominant.

n99c8ebb8542.s: India's 1991 balance of payments crisis was marked by:
o: Stable prices, rising gold reserves and a balanced budget
High inflation, low foreign exchange reserves and a large fiscal deficit
Low inflation, high reserves and a fiscal surplus
High exports, falling public debt and a current account surplus
n99c8ebb8542.x: The 1991 crisis featured high inflation, critically low forex reserves and a large fiscal deficit.
xa: CAD: **3.1-3.2%** of GDP; trade deficit **₹10,644 crore**.
External debt: **$69.3 bn**.

n29331ae8ac5.s: The strategy of export-led growth was introduced in India as part of:
o: The Second Five Year Plan's Mahalanobis model
The Green Revolution strategy of the 1960s
n29331ae8ac5.x: Export-led growth came with the 1991 LPG reforms, which moved India from import substitution to export promotion. The Mahalanobis model of the Second Plan was based on heavy industry and import substitution. The Green Revolution was about farm output, and bank nationalisation in 1969 was about state control of credit.
n29331ae8ac5.tq: Export-led growth = 1991 LPG (import substitution to export promotion).
xs: **Export-led growth** came with the **LPG reforms of 1991** — option **(3)**.
This was the **PYQ 2025 / APPSC 2025** key.
It marked the shift from **import substitution to export promotion**.
xa: Tariffs cut; **QRs** and **EXIM scrips** abolished.
⚠ Trap: after globalisation, **imports grew faster than exports**.
Post-reform the economy moved to **enhanced global integration** (APPSC 2025).

n33580fa3486.s: The post-reform Indian economy is characterised by:
o: Complete isolation and a smaller private sector
Greater global integration and a larger private sector
Replacement of private investment by foreign aid
n33580fa3486.x: The post-reform economy shows greater global integration and an expanded private sector.
xa: Reforms 1.0 = **LPG (1991)**; Reforms 2.0 = **DPI (2014 onwards)**.
FDI inflows **rose sharply**; reserves rose to **$701.4 bn**.
Services became the **largest sector**.

n14f61032f09.s: The pillars of the next-generation reforms begin with which two factor markets?
n14f61032f09.x: The stated pillars begin with land, including easier acquisition, and labour, including simpler laws.
n14f61032f09.tq: Recall the opening pillars rather than the broader reform list.
xs: Next-generation reform pillars begin with **land** (easier acquisition) and **labour** (simpler laws) — option **(4)**.
Capital, energy and services are not named as the starting pillars.
xa: Land: **DILRMP, ULPIN, NGDRS**.
Labour: **29** laws → **4 Codes**.
Capital: **IBC**, capital-market reform.

n85436abd95f.s: Under the National Monetisation Pipeline, which assets are monetised and how?
o: Greenfield assets sold permanently to private parties
Brownfield assets sold permanently through strategic sale
Brownfield, de-risked assets leased via OMT and InvITs, with ownership retained by government
Greenfield assets leased with ownership transferred to operators
n85436abd95f.x: NMP leases brownfield, de-risked assets through OMT and InvITs; ownership stays with the government and assets return after the lease.
xa: NMP: **₹6 lakh crore** over **FY2022-25** (announced **Aug 2021**).
Shares: **Roads ~27%**, **railways ~25%**, **power ~15%**.
IYB 2026 lists an **SPV for Land Monetisation** (surplus CPSE land).

nindian-economy-15-10.s: Which Article provides restrictions relating to taxation of supplies outside a State and import-export?
nindian-economy-15-10.x: Article 286 limits States from taxing supplies outside the State or in the course of import and export. Article 269A covers IGST on inter-State supply.
nindian-economy-15-10.tq: Match each Article to its GST role.
n: Article 286 provides restrictions relating to taxation of supplies outside a State and import-export. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 19-22]
xs: **Article 286** provides **restrictions** on **taxation of supplies outside a State** and **import-export** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Article 246A** = power of Parliament and State Legislatures to **levy GST**; **269A** = **IGST** on inter-State supplies; **279A** = **GST Council**.
xa: **Article 366(12A)** gives the constitutional definition of GST.
The **101st Constitution Amendment Act, 2016** inserted Art. 246A (assent **8 Sep 2016**).
GST came into force on **1 July 2017**; first State to ratify = **Assam**.

ned25be0afe9.s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of initiatives for digitising land records?
ned25be0afe9.x: DILRMP, ULPIN and NGDRS are associated with digitising land records.
ned25be0afe9.tq: Identify the complete set belonging to one factor market.
xs: **DILRMP, ULPIN and NGDRS** digitise land records — option **(2)**.
**IBBI** relates to insolvency (capital market), not land.
xa: Land-record digitisation was noted on **9 Jun 2026**.
Capital-market reform: **IBC**.
Next-generation reform pillars begin with **land** and **labour**.

nb2017c4bd2e.s: Which of the following is the correct number of Central laws merged into the four Labour Codes?
nb2017c4bd2e.x: The four Labour Codes merged 29 Central labour laws.
nb2017c4bd2e.tq: Distinguish the total number of laws from the individual code-wise counts.
xs: The four Codes merged **29** central labour laws — option **(3)**.
⚠ Trap: some notes say the **Code on Wages** merges 29 — it merges only **4**; 29 is all four Codes together.
xa: Split: **4 – 3 – 9 – 13** = Wages – IR – Social Security – OSH.
Sections cut from **1,232 to 480**; rules from **1,436 to 401**.
Codes operational from **21 November 2025**.

ne64d843f192.s: Which one of the following laws is NOT merged into the Code on Wages, 2019?
ne64d843f192.x: The Code on Wages subsumes the Minimum Wages Act, Payment of Wages Act, Payment of Bonus Act and Equal Remuneration Act. The Contract Labour Act is merged into the OSH and Working Conditions Code, not the Code on Wages.
ne64d843f192.tq: Find the wrongly placed law by distinguishing neighbouring Codes.
xs: The **Contract Labour Act 1970** is NOT in the Code on Wages — option **(3)**.
It is part of the **OSH Code** (**UPPSC 2021** PYQ).
Code on Wages merges **Payment of Wages 1936**, **Minimum Wages 1948**, **Payment of Bonus 1965**, **Equal Remuneration 1976**.
xa: OSH Code (**13** laws) also has the **Factories Act 1948**, **Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act 1979**, **BOCW Act 1996**.
The Code on Wages is the only **2019** Code.
⚠ The Code on Wages merges **4** laws, not 29.

nd6de1d8e755.s: The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 is subsumed in which Labour Code?
nd6de1d8e755.x: The Code on Wages includes the Equal Remuneration Act; the IR Code has the Trade Unions Act, the SS Code the Employees' Compensation Act, the OSH Code the Factories Act.
xa: IR Code also has the **Industrial Disputes Act 1947**.
Social Security Code covers **gig and platform workers**.
OSH Code also has the **Contract Labour Act 1970**.

ne83ea64f32a.s: Under the new Labour Codes, 26 weeks of maternity leave is provided in the:
ne83ea64f32a.x: The Code on Social Security provides for 26 weeks of maternity leave.
xa: ⚠ **300** = IR Code threshold; **50+** = crèche; **500+** = OSH safety committee.
Code on Wages: **8-hour day, 48-hour week** (2026 Rules).
IR Code: gratuity for fixed-term workers after **1 year**.

n95dd407408a.s: Under the Code on Wages, 2019, the national floor wage is fixed by:
n95dd407408a.x: The Centre fixes the national floor wage; the Code also provides a universal minimum wage and bars gender discrimination.
xa: **50% rule** on allowances for PF/gratuity/bonus.
It merges **4** laws and is the only **2019** Code.
⚠ The **Contract Labour Act** is not in it.

n38e23a3447c.s: Under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, the threshold for prior permission for lay-off, retrenchment and closure was raised from 100 to:
n38e23a3447c.x: The IR Code raised the prior-permission threshold from 100 to 300 workers.
xa: Unions call this **hire-and-fire** (12 Jun 2026).
⚠ **300** = IR Code; **500+** = OSH safety committee.
IR Code subsumes **3** laws.

n4a08b7b2186.s: Labour is placed in which List of the Constitution of India?
n4a08b7b2186.x: Labour is included in the Concurrent List, allowing both the Union and the States to legislate on the subject.
n4a08b7b2186.tq: Use the subject classification to discriminate between Union, State and Concurrent powers.
xs: Labour is on the **Concurrent List** — option **(1)**.
So both the Centre and States frame rules under the Codes.
xa: **29** central laws → **4** Codes.
Central Rules for all four were notified in **May 2026**, nearly six years after enactment.
Sections were cut from **1,232 to 480**; rules from **1,436 to 401**.

n33bdfdd1114.s: Fixed-term employment was extended to all sectors by the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Central (Amendment) Rules of:
n33bdfdd1114.x: The 2018 Amendment Rules extended fixed-term employment to all sectors and removed the termination notice for temporary workmen.
xa: ⚠ Trap: both statements correct in the **UPSC 2019** PYQ.
IR Code 2020: fixed-term workers get **parity + gratuity after 1 year**.
Unions call the IR Code **hire-and-fire** (12 Jun 2026).

nae6e81e9057.s: In the factor-market reform framework, the IBC and capital-market reform are classed as:
nae6e81e9057.x: The framework covers land (land-record digitisation), labour (four Labour Codes) and capital (IBC and capital-market reform).
xa: Corporates are **moving to non-bank funding** (ES 2025-26).
"Next Generation Reforms" pillars start with **land** (easier acquisition) + **labour** (simpler laws).
**29** central labour laws were merged into **4** Codes.

n7aa301b301a.s: The Goods and Services Tax came into force in India on:
n7aa301b301a.x: GST came into force on 1 July 2017.
n7aa301b301a.tq: Distinguish the constitutional amendment date from the implementation date.
xs: GST came into force on **1 July 2017** — option **(2)**.
**8 Sep 2016** was the assent to the **101st Amendment**.
xa: **Art. 246A** = power to levy GST; **Art. 279A** = GST Council; **Art. 269A** = IGST.
First State to ratify: **Assam**.
ES 2025-26 calls **GST 2.0** the most radical overhaul since **2017**.

nb8154cbf8d2.s: Which of the following taxes subsumed under GST was a State tax rather than a Central tax?
nb8154cbf8d2.x: Central excise, service tax and CST were Central taxes subsumed under GST; State VAT was a State tax.
xa: GST ended **cascading** through input tax credit.
**IGST** (Art. **269A**) applies to inter-state supply and imports.
GST in force from **1 July 2017**.

n46f8ec21c67.s: Which was the first State to ratify the Constitution Amendment relating to GST?
n46f8ec21c67.x: Assam was the first State to ratify the GST amendment; GST follows the Canadian dual model and traces to the Vijay Kelkar Committee.
xa: GST came into force on **1 July 2017**.
GST is a **destination-based consumption tax** with input tax credit — ends **cascading**.
**GST 2.0** (Aug 2025) added a **40% slab** for sin/luxury goods.

n81c68296dfd.s: Next-Generation GST (GST 2.0), announced in August 2025, introduced a special slab for sin and luxury goods of:
n81c68296dfd.x: GST 2.0 brought rate rationalisation and a 40% slab for sin and luxury goods; input tax credit was retained.
xa: GST 2.0 also gave **90%** provisional export refunds in **7 days** (Sep 2025).
ES 2025-26: most radical overhaul since **2017**.
Rate rationalisation was the main plank.

n8393856de91.s: Which of the following was NOT credited with improving India's Market Distortions Performance Index position?
n8393856de91.x: GST, IBC and trade facilitation were credited; restoration of import quotas was not cited.
xa: The index rank moved from **82nd (2010)** to **57th (2023)** (Competere Foundation).
**IBC** is a **capital**-market factor reform.
GST came into force on **1 July 2017**; **GST 2.0** announced **Aug 2025**.

n8d3f796d8ad.s: NITI Aayog was established in 2015 primarily to replace the Planning Commission and promote:
n8d3f796d8ad.x: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission and promotes cooperative and competitive federalism.
n8d3f796d8ad.tq: Match an institutional reform with its stated objective.
xs: **NITI Aayog** (**2015**) replaced the Planning Commission to promote **cooperative and competitive federalism** — option **(2)**.
Centralised licensing and exclusive public ownership run against the post-1991 reform direction.
xa: **DBT** began on **1 Jan 2013** (**JAM** trinity).
Corporate tax cut: **Sept 2019**.
**Jan Vishwas** Act 2023 decriminalised minor offences.

n5a2f0ad2dd6.s: Under the September 2019 corporate tax cut, new manufacturing units were given a tax rate of:
n5a2f0ad2dd6.x: The 2019 cut set 22 per cent for existing companies and 15 per cent for new manufacturing units.
xa: **PLI** came in **2020** (Atmanirbhar **₹20 lakh crore** package).
Three **farm Acts** came in **Sept 2020** and were repealed in **2021**.
S&P upgraded India from **BBB- to BBB** (ES 2025-26).

n7a8177196cc.s: The principal purpose of the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023 is:
o: Ranking of States on business reforms
n7a8177196cc.x: The Jan Vishwas Act, 2023 decriminalised minor offences to ease compliance.
xa: Compliance burden: **48,000+** compliances reduced; **3,400+** provisions decriminalised.
**Over 350** reforms incl. fewer **Quality Control Orders** (Budget 2026-27).
Critics want "**ease of living**" above "ease of doing business".

n36551296c68.s: The National Monetisation Pipeline (₹6 lakh crore over FY2022-25) was announced in:
n36551296c68.x: The NMP was announced in August 2021 and covers core assets of central ministries and CPSEs.
xa: Model: **brownfield**, de-risked assets leased (**OMT**, **InvITs**).
**Ownership stays with government**; assets handed back; **no land sale**.
⚠ Largest share = **Roads**, then railways, then power.

n4444846d77c.s: Which of the following correctly represents the approximate NMP sectoral shares?
n4444846d77c.x: The approximate shares are roads 27 per cent, railways 25 per cent and power 15 per cent.
n4444846d77c.tq: Preserve the order of sectors and their percentages in a comparison table.
xs: **Roads 27%, railways 25%, power 15%** — option **(4)**.
⚠ Largest share = **Roads**, then **railways**, then **power**.
xa: NMP covers core assets of **central ministries and CPSEs**.
Model: brownfield assets leased via **OMT** and **InvITs**.
Value: **₹6 lakh crore** over **FY2022-25**.

n211c130f7e8.s: According to the Budget 2026–27 reference, the number of reforms counted was:
n211c130f7e8.x: The Budget 2026–27 counts more than 350 reforms.
n211c130f7e8.tq: Read the threshold carefully; “350+” means more than 350, not an exact figure.
xs: Budget 2026-27 counts **more than 350** reforms — option **(2)**.
They include **GST simplification**, **Labour Codes** and rationalised **Quality Control Orders**.
xa: ES 2025-26 "slew of reforms": GST overhaul, insurance **100% FDI**, nuclear power opened to private sector.
S&P upgraded India from **BBB- to BBB**.
Labour Codes operational since **Nov 2025**.

n652da9cfcb6.s: According to the World Bank's Doing Business ranking, India's rank improved from 142 in 2014 to:
n652da9cfcb6.x: India's World Bank Doing Business rank improved from 142 in 2014 to 63 in 2019.
n652da9cfcb6.tq: Pair the institution, years and ranks without mixing them with IMD figures.
xs: India's Doing Business rank rose from **142 (2014)** to **63 in 2019** — option **(1)**.
The ranking was conceived by the **IFC** (World Bank).
xa: **AP** has been **ranked No. 1 since BRAP 2016**.
Compliance: **48,000+** compliances reduced; **3,400+** provisions decriminalised.
AP angle: **District Industries Centres** run the **single window** and implement the **MSMED Act**.

n5501f373bd7.s: Andhra Pradesh has ranked first since which edition of the Business Reforms Action Plan?
n5501f373bd7.x: Andhra Pradesh has ranked number one since BRAP 2016.
n5501f373bd7.tq: Distinguish the first release year from the edition associated with Andhra Pradesh's ranking.
xs: AP has been **ranked No. 1 since BRAP 2016** — option **(1)**.
BRAP = **Business Reforms Action Plan**, the States' ease-of-doing-business ranking.
xa: AP's **Single Desk Portal** is linked to the **Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor** EoDB loan.
**District Industries Centres** run the **single window** and implement the **MSMED Act**.
India's World Bank Doing Business rank: **142 (2014) → 63 (2019)**.

nc7bb9972f77.s: The Single Desk Portal in Andhra Pradesh is linked to the:
o: Andhra Pradesh Power Distribution Recapitalisation Fund
nc7bb9972f77.x: The Single Desk Portal is linked to the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor ease-of-doing-business loan.
nc7bb9972f77.tq: Use the distinctive institutional and corridor pairing to avoid confusing related State initiatives.
xs: AP's **Single Desk Portal** is linked to the **Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor EoDB loan** — option **(3)**.
Source: **APSES Ch. 6**.
xa: **District Industries Centres** run the **single window** + implement the **MSMED Act**.
AP **ranked No. 1 since BRAP 2016**.
World Bank Doing Business was conceived by the **IFC**.

n8788f7ff2df.s: The theory of absolute advantage in international trade is associated with:
n8788f7ff2df.x: Absolute advantage is Adam Smith's idea; Ricardo gave comparative advantage based on lower opportunity cost.
xa: ⚠ **Adam Smith** = absolute advantage; **Ricardo** = comparative advantage.
**Intra-industry trade**: a country imports and exports the **same product**.
**Import substitution** = inward-looking; **export promotion** = outward-looking.

nc33fe6f3a4c.s: Export promotion and import substitution are respectively described as:
nc33fe6f3a4c.x: Import substitution is an inward-looking strategy, whereas export promotion is an outward-looking strategy.
nc33fe6f3a4c.tq: Test the paired terms by reversing them mentally and checking their policy orientation.
xs: **Export promotion** is **outward-looking**; **import substitution** is **inward-looking** — option **(2)**.
Option (3) reverses the pair.
The **1991 New Trade Policy** moved India away from **import substitution** and **QRs** to a price-based regime.
xa: The 1991 shift came with a two-step **rupee devaluation (July 1991)**.
**FTP 2023** targets **$2 trillion** exports by **2030** — an export-promotion goal.
An **import quota** is a **quantitative restriction (QR)** on imports.

nb3ddc03615d.s: A countervailing duty is imposed to:
o: Counter imports sold below the home-market price
Determine the national source of goods
Offset the effect of foreign subsidies
nb3ddc03615d.x: Countervailing duty offsets foreign subsidies; anti-dumping duty addresses imports below home-market price, and rules of origin decide the national source.
xa: Example: US preliminary **CVD of 125.87%** on an Indian product (**Mar 2026**).
India has **14 FTAs and 6 PTAs** (**Apr 2026**), but exports to FTA partners fell **7%**.
**Entrepot trade** = re-export of imports.

n8dcee3d5929.s: When a country both imports and exports the same product, for example cars, the trade is called:
n8dcee3d5929.x: Intra-industry trade is the import and export of the same product by a country. Entrepot trade is re-exporting imported goods. Inter-industry trade is exchanging different products, as comparative advantage predicts. Dumping is exporting below the home-market price or cost.
n8dcee3d5929.tq: Same product both ways = intra-industry trade.
xs: A country importing and exporting the **same product** carries on **intra-industry trade** — option **(2)** (PYQ 2025).
**Entrepot trade** is the **re-export of imports**.
**Dumping** is exporting below home-market price or cost.
xa: **Comparative advantage** (**Ricardo**): specialise in the good with lower opportunity cost.
**Composition** = items traded; **direction** = country-wise/region-wise pattern.
**Volume** = money value of exports and imports.

nea6bb9ab841.s: Which department frames and monitors India's Foreign Trade Policy?
nea6bb9ab841.x: The Department of Commerce frames and monitors India's Foreign Trade Policy.
nea6bb9ab841.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish neighbouring government departments.
xs: The **Foreign Trade Policy** is framed and monitored by the **Department of Commerce** — option **(1)**.
**FTP 2023** came into force from **1 April 2023**, with no end date, reviewed as needed.
xa: FTP 2023 targets **$2 trillion** exports by **2030**.
**APEDA**, the nodal agency for Agri Export Zones, also works under the **Department of Commerce**.
Pillars: duty-free input schemes, **Districts as Export Hubs**, logistics, better FTA use.

n0c0334de878.s: For trade and tariff purposes, a duty-free enclave in an SEZ is treated as:
o: A bonded warehouse under State control
n0c0334de878.x: A duty-free enclave is treated as foreign territory for trade and tariff purposes, though it lies within India.
xa: SEZ policy announced **April 2000**; **SEZ Act 2005**; **SEZ Rules 2006**.
The SEZ concept was proposed in the **EXIM Policy 1997-2002**.
First **EPZ**: **Kandla, 1965**.

ne0a70b53c43.s: A tax levied on imports is called a:
ne0a70b53c43.x: A tax on imports is a tariff; an import quota is a quantity restriction and import licensing an administrative restriction.
xa: **Anti-dumping measures** protect against goods exported **below normal value**.
**Entrepot trade** = import, store and **re-export** goods.
**Countervailing duty** offsets foreign subsidies.

nindian-economy-54-5.s: Importing goods, storing or trading them, and then re-exporting them is called:
nindian-economy-54-5.x: Entrepot trade means importing, storing or trading and then re-exporting goods.
n: Rules of origin determine the country of origin for trade-policy purposes. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 80-81]
Entrepot trade involves importing goods. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 80-81]
Entrepot trade involves storing or trading imported goods. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 80-81]
Entrepot trade involves re-exporting goods. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #54 · pp 80-81]
xa: Rules of origin decide which goods qualify for **FTA concessions**.
**Intra-industry trade**: importing and exporting the **same product**.
**CEPA** = Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement.

n94f8202a13f.s: Net terms of trade (NTT) is calculated as:
o: Import price index / Export price index × 100
Export price index / Import price index × 100
n94f8202a13f.x: NTT = export price index / import price index × 100; gross terms of trade is import quantity over export quantity.
xa: **ITT** = NTT x export quantity index.
**Marshall-Lerner condition**: devaluation helps only if export + import demand elasticities sum to **greater than 1**.
**J-curve**: after depreciation the trade balance first worsens, then improves.

n7f7c4e52afe.s: After a currency depreciation, the J-curve effect implies that the trade balance generally:
o: Worsens only when exports become cheaper abroad
Remains unchanged because prices do not change
Improves immediately and then worsens permanently
First worsens and improves only after export and import volumes adjust
n7f7c4e52afe.x: Under the J-curve effect, import bills rise immediately after depreciation, so the trade balance initially worsens; it improves later as quantities adjust.
n7f7c4e52afe.tq: Apply the time sequence—initial price effect followed by volume adjustment—to the trade balance.
xs: **J-curve**: after depreciation the trade balance **first worsens** (import bills rise at once) and **improves only as volumes adjust** — option **(4)**.
It does not improve immediately, so option (3) is the reverse of the J-curve.
xa: **Marshall-Lerner condition**: devaluation improves the balance only if export + import demand elasticities sum to **greater than 1**.
Depreciation makes **exports cheaper abroad and imports dearer at home**.
The weak rupee was credited in part for the **Aug 2026** export surge.

n3fa1bb49183.s: The immediate effect of devaluation or depreciation of a currency is that:
o: Exports become dearer abroad and imports cheaper at home
Exports become cheaper abroad and imports dearer at home
Both exports and imports become cheaper
Export and import prices are unaffected
n3fa1bb49183.x: Devaluation or depreciation makes exports cheaper for foreign buyers and imports dearer at home.
xa: The Commerce Secretary credited the **weak rupee** in part for the **Aug 2026** export surge.
**J-curve**: trade balance first worsens, improves later.
**1991**: two-step rupee devaluation in **July 1991**.

na2c2528ad38.s: According to the Marshall–Lerner condition, devaluation improves the trade balance when:
o: Only export demand is perfectly inelastic
The sum of export and import demand price elasticities is greater than one
The sum of export and import demand price elasticities is equal to zero
The sum of export and import demand price elasticities is less than one
na2c2528ad38.x: The Marshall–Lerner condition is satisfied when the sum of the absolute values of export and import demand price elasticities exceeds one.
na2c2528ad38.tq: Recall the threshold condition and distinguish greater than one from less than one.
xs: **Marshall-Lerner condition**: devaluation improves the trade balance only if export + import demand price elasticities sum to **greater than 1** — option **(2)**.
A sum less than one or zero fails the condition.
