ndbf1edf379f.s: FEMA, which replaced FERA, came into force on:
ndbf1edf379f.x: FEMA was proposed in the 1997-98 Budget and came into force on 1 June 2000.
xa: Tarapore II was set up in **March 2006**.
⚠ Some notes say Tarapore II was **constituted** on 31 July 2006.
FEMA in force **1 June 2000**.

ncedb98c7e22.s: Which committee provided a roadmap for fuller capital account convertibility in India?
ncedb98c7e22.x: The Tarapore Committee (report of 31 July 2006) gave the roadmap; India has full current but only partial capital account convertibility.
xa: Current account convertibility came in **August 1994** (IMF **Article VIII**).
**Tarapore I (1997)**; **Tarapore II (2006)**.
**FEMA 1999** replaced the restrictive **FERA 1973**.

n8c6a584aa5b.s: Which of the following is identified as a set of long-run determinants of the exchange rate?
o: Daily spot intervention by the central bank
Purchasing power parity, savings-investment balance and the current account
n8c6a584aa5b.x: Long-run exchange-rate determinants include PPP, the savings-investment balance and the current account.
xa: **ES 2025-26** long-term anchor = savings-investment balance + current account (**East Asian** lesson: manufacturing exports).
Other determinants: **fiscal deficit**, **CAD**, short-term debt, interest rates, capital flows.
Higher imports ≠ depreciation if backed by **net investment inflows**.

nf59dd8a0b2b.s: Higher imports may be accompanied by currency stability or appreciation when supported by:
nf59dd8a0b2b.x: Net investment inflows can finance imports, so higher imports do not always cause depreciation.
xa: **East Asian** lesson: manufacturing exports.
**PPP** is a long-run determinant.
Large inflows can cause **appreciation** (**Dutch disease**).

n82d58842c7d.s: RBI intervention in the foreign exchange market primarily aims to:
o: Defend a permanently fixed rupee-dollar level
n82d58842c7d.x: The RBI intervenes mainly to curb volatility, using reserves if needed, not to defend a fixed rate.
xa: Reserves fell **$23.6 bn in FY26** defending the rupee.
**Forex swaps** inject rupee liquidity without permanently cutting reserves.
**Repo 5.25%**, unchanged for the **4th** meeting (**Aug 2026**).

n441524537b3.s: The Reserve Tranche Position of a country in the International Monetary Fund refers to:
o: The share of SDRs allocated to private commercial banks
The total amount of gold held by the country
The portion of the IMF quota that can be drawn without conditions
The country’s annual export earnings deposited with the IMF
n441524537b3.x: The reserve tranche is the part of a member country’s IMF quota that it can draw without conditionality.
n441524537b3.tq: Use the precise meaning of ‘tranche’ instead of confusing it with SDR allocation or gold holdings.
xs: The **reserve (gold) tranche** is the part of a member's **IMF quota** paid in reserve assets, **drawable any time without conditions** — option **(3)**.
Historically it was paid in **gold**.
xa: **RTP** is the smallest of the four reserve components.
**SDR** = interest-bearing reserve asset created by the IMF.
Order: **FCA > Gold > SDR > RTP**.

nd59fa844fba.s: The rupee symbol (₹) was introduced in:
nd59fa844fba.x: The rupee symbol came in 2010, after current account convertibility (1994), the First Tarapore Committee (1997) and FEMA (2000).
xa: **Tarapore II** came in **2006**.
FEMA was proposed in the **1997-98** Budget.
⚠ FIRST/LAST: rupee symbol **2010**; current account convertibility **1994**.

ne260dd8e9dc.s: India's dual exchange rates under LERMS were replaced by a unified rate on:
ne260dd8e9dc.x: LERMS came in 1992-93, the unified rate on 1 March 1993, and current account convertibility in August 1994.
xa: LERMS split: **40%** official / **60%** market.
Rupee delinked from **sterling** in **September 1975**.
**FEMA** enacted **1999**, in force **1 June 2000**.

n66de3fc237d.s: Which one of the following correctly describes import cover?
o: The number of months for which a country's reserves can pay for its imports
The share of imports financed by foreign direct investment
The period during which a forward exchange contract remains valid
The percentage change in the exchange rate during a year
n66de3fc237d.x: Import cover measures the number of months for which available foreign-exchange reserves can finance imports.
n66de3fc237d.tq: Match the term with the unit in which it is conventionally expressed.
xs: **Import cover** = the **months of imports** that **reserves** can pay for — option **(1)**.
It is not an FDI share, forward contract period or exchange-rate change.
xa: **Jan 2026**: reserves **$701.4 bn** gave **~11 months** import cover (2025-26).
Adequate reserves (import cover) are a key BoP safeguard.
Reserves also covered **~94%** of external debt.

n2555d805a91.s: Devaluation is described as an expenditure-switching policy because it generally:
o: Raises export prices in foreign currency and lowers import prices
Makes imports cheaper and encourages spending on foreign goods
Makes domestic goods cheaper for foreigners and imports costlier for domestic consumers
Eliminates the need for fiscal and monetary measures
n2555d805a91.x: Devaluation makes home-produced goods relatively cheaper for foreigners and imported goods costlier at home, thereby switching expenditure towards domestic production.
n2555d805a91.tq: Apply the price effects of a weaker currency to domestic and foreign spending.
xs: **Devaluation** is **expenditure-switching**: it makes **home goods cheaper for foreigners** and **imports costlier at home** — option **(3)**.
Spending switches to **home-produced goods**; it does **not** raise export prices (option 1).
xa: Other BoP correction methods: **exchange control**, **monetary/fiscal measures**, **import curbs**.
Limits: **imported inflation**, **inelasticity trap** (oil), costlier **ECB** repayment.
The trade balance **tends to improve**.

nindian-economy-47-3.s: Devaluation may improve export competitiveness because:
nindian-economy-47-3.x: A cheaper domestic currency makes domestic goods relatively cheaper abroad.
n: Devaluation makes the domestic currency cheaper. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #47 · pp 69-71]
Devaluation makes domestic exports relatively cheaper abroad. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #47 · pp 69-71]
Devaluation may improve export competitiveness. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #47 · pp 69-71]
xa: ⚠ It does **not necessarily improve** the trade balance.
Devaluation is an **expenditure-switching** policy.
Limits: **imported inflation**, the **inelasticity trap** (oil), costlier **ECB** repayment.

nindian-economy-47-8.s: High inflation and a large fiscal deficit tend to ____ a currency's exchange value.
nindian-economy-47-8.x: Both inflation and a fiscal deficit can weaken a currency's exchange value.
n: Inflation can affect the exchange value. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #47 · pp 69-71]
A fiscal deficit can affect the exchange value. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #47 · pp 69-71]
xa: Other determinants: **CAD**, interest rates, capital flows, short-term debt.
Long-run determinants: **PPP**, savings-investment balance, current account.
⚠ The **World Bank** does not determine the currency price.

nf6112771bcc.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes spot and forward exchange rates?
o: A spot rate is for immediate delivery, whereas a forward rate is agreed now for delivery on a future date
A forward rate is determined only after the future delivery date
A spot rate is agreed today for future delivery, whereas a forward rate is for immediate delivery
Both rates necessarily relate only to cash transactions settled on the same day
nf6112771bcc.x: A spot rate applies to immediate delivery, while a forward rate is fixed by agreement today for settlement at a specified future date.
nf6112771bcc.tq: Use the timing of delivery to separate two closely related terms.
xs: A **spot rate** is for **immediate delivery**; a **forward rate** is **agreed now for delivery at a future date** — option **(1)**.
Option (3) reverses the two; a forward rate is fixed in advance, not after delivery.
xa: Spot settlement happens **within two days**.
**Hedging** = covering exchange-rate risk, e.g. via **forwards**.
**Arbitrage** = buying cheap in one market and selling dearer in another at the same time.

ndeeac00ad9a.s: In FY 2025-26 up to January 2026, the rupee had:
ndeeac00ad9a.x: The rupee depreciated by 5.4% in FY 2025-26 up to January and was among the most depreciated currencies, along with the yen.
xa: Rupee crossed **96.2/$** on **18-19 May 2026**.
Reserves fell **$23.6 bn in FY26** defending the rupee.
The rupee stayed at **95-96/$** through 2026 on the **West Asia** crude shock.

nb4addeaddd2.s: Which one of the following is NOT a tool of the Reserve Bank of India for managing rupee volatility?
nb4addeaddd2.x: Fiscal policy adjustments are Government measures, not RBI exchange-rate management tools. Spot intervention, forex swaps and monetary policy signalling are RBI tools.
nb4addeaddd2.tq: Find the institutionally misplaced policy instrument.
xs: **Fiscal policy adjustments** are **not** an RBI tool — option **(1)** (APPSC-G2 2025 key).
RBI's core tools: **market intervention** (spot and forward), **forex reserves**, **forex swaps**, **monetary policy signalling**.
xa: **Import curbs + export promotion** = Government (structural) measures.
RBI aims to curb **volatility**, not defend a fixed level.
Hawkish stance / repo hike attracts **carry-trade** capital.

n19fa4ef2ae7.s: In the context of offshore Non-Deliverable Forward markets, which measure is used by the RBI to reduce speculative pressure on the rupee?
o: Abolishing all forward contracts in India
Restricting domestic banks’ participation in offshore NDF markets and enforcing Net Open Position limits
Permitting unlimited offshore positions by domestic banks
n19fa4ef2ae7.x: The RBI restricts domestic banks’ offshore NDF participation and enforces Net Open Position limits to curb speculative pressure and volatility.
n19fa4ef2ae7.tq: Match the regulatory action with the market through which pressure is transmitted.
xs: RBI **restricts domestic banks' offshore NDF participation** and enforces **Net Open Position** limits — option **(2)**.
The offshore **Non-Deliverable Forward** market is used to **short the rupee**.
xa: NDF centres: **Singapore/London**.
**Apr 2026**: RBI moved on **Non-Deliverable Derivative (NDD)** contracts to curb volatility.
RBI's aim: curb **volatility**, not defend a fixed level.

n5e532793d3e.s: Which of the following is a Government structural measure rather than an RBI exchange-rate tool?
o: Selling dollars in the spot market
n5e532793d3e.x: Import curbs and export promotion are Government structural measures. Spot intervention, NOP limits and dollar-rupee swaps are associated with RBI action.
n5e532793d3e.tq: Distinguish structural Government measures from central-bank market operations.
xs: **Import curbs and export promotion** are **Government (structural) measures** — option **(4)**.
**Net Open Position** limits, **dollar-rupee swaps** and **spot sales of dollars** are RBI tools.
xa: **Fiscal policy** adjustments are also not an RBI tool (APPSC-G2 2025 key).
RBI's aim: curb **volatility**.
**Capital-inflow** steps: **ECB** easing, FCNR(B) hedging support.

n04a29054f4f.s: India’s foreign exchange reserves of approximately $701.4 billion were reported to provide import cover of about:
n04a29054f4f.x: Reserves of approximately $701.4 billion were associated with import cover of about 11 months.
n04a29054f4f.tq: Match the reserve figure with its stated duration of import cover.
xs: Reserves of **$701.4 bn** (**Jan 2026**) gave **~11 months** of import cover (2025-26) — option **(3)**.
They also covered **~94%** of external debt (ES 2025-26).
xa: All-time high then: **$728.494 bn** (week to **27 Feb 2026**).
**Import cover** = months of imports reserves can pay for.

n4bc425a7c6f.s: Which one of the following combinations was associated with the rupee crossing ₹96.2 per US dollar on 19 May 2026?
o: Brent crude near $110 and FPI outflows exceeding ₹2 lakh crore
A sharp increase in official interest rates and a trade surplus
A fall in imports and a rise in gold exports
Brent crude near $50 and strong FPI inflows
n4bc425a7c6f.x: On 19 May 2026, the rupee crossed ₹96.2 per dollar amid Brent crude near $110 and FPI outflows of more than ₹2 lakh crore.
n4bc425a7c6f.tq: Link the exchange-rate movement with the simultaneous external and capital-flow pressures.
xs: The rupee crossed **96.2/$** on **18-19 May 2026** amid **Brent near $110** and **FII equity sales of over ₹2 lakh crore** — option **(1)**.
It was down **6.3%** since **1 Jan 2026**.
xa: Brent touched **$110.8**.
RBI aims to curb **volatility**, not defend a fixed level.

nd72a906ad0a.s: In a dollar-rupee buy/sell swap, banks:
o: Buy dollars from the RBI and sell them back later at a discount
Sell dollars to the RBI permanently
Buy rupee bonds from the RBI
Sell dollars to the RBI and buy them back later at a premium
nd72a906ad0a.x: Banks sell dollars to the RBI and repurchase later at a premium, injecting rupee liquidity without permanently altering reserves.
xa: **$5 billion, 3-year** swaps (**Dec 2025**; another **Apr-May 2026**).
Forex swaps are one of RBI's **core tools**.
Spot intervention, by contrast, means **selling dollars from reserves**.

nad5036a9154.s: The largest component of India's foreign exchange reserves is:
nad5036a9154.x: Foreign Currency Assets are the largest, followed by gold; SDRs and the reserve tranche are small.
xa: Four components: **FCA**, **Gold**, **SDRs**, **Reserve Tranche Position** (APPSC-G2 2025 key).
**RBI** is the custodian.
Week to **31 Jul 2026**: reserves **$692.866 bn**, of which FCA **$564.68 bn**.

n270e1d2f179.s: In September 2026, India became the world's fourth-largest holder of foreign exchange reserves after overtaking:
n270e1d2f179.x: With reserves of $785.71 billion in September 2026, India became the fourth-largest holder after overtaking Russia.
n270e1d2f179.tq: Identify the country displaced in the ranking rather than the countries above India.
xs: With **$785.71 bn** (**15 Sep 2026**) India became the **4th largest** holder, overtaking **Russia** — option **(3)**.
**China**, **Japan** and **Switzerland** remain ahead.
xa: China **$3.85 tn**, Japan **$1.21 tn**, Switzerland **$1.09 tn**.
Reserves fell **$23.6 bn in FY26** defending the rupee.

n055949040ac.s: The rise in the share of gold in India's foreign exchange reserves is principally associated with:
o: Replacement of SDRs by domestic tax revenue
A prohibition on holding foreign currencies
n055949040ac.x: The increased share of gold has been associated with diversification of India's foreign exchange reserves.
n055949040ac.tq: Link the reserve-composition change with its stated policy rationale.
xs: **Gold**'s share in reserves has risen significantly for **diversification** — option **(3)**.
**FCA** is still the largest component, so it has not been eliminated.
xa: Order: **FCA > Gold > SDR > RTP**.
**SDRs** are called **"paper gold"**.
**RBI** is the custodian of reserves.

n15249eedbe3.s: Who acts as the custodian of India's foreign exchange reserves?
n15249eedbe3.x: The Reserve Bank of India is the custodian of India's foreign exchange reserves.
n15249eedbe3.tq: Identify the domestic authority responsible for custody rather than an international institution.
xs: The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is the **custodian** of India's forex reserves — option **(3)**.
The **IMF** holds the **reserve tranche** and allots **SDRs**, but is not the custodian.
xa: Components: **FCA**, **Gold**, **SDRs**, **RTP**.
RBI uses reserves for **spot intervention** — selling dollars.
India's reserves: **$785.71 bn** (**15 Sep 2026**).

n75ed946e4ae.s: Special Drawing Rights, popularly called 'paper gold', were created by the IMF in:
n75ed946e4ae.x: SDRs were created in 1969 under the IMF's First Amendment (agreed in 1967).
xa: ⚠ Some notes date the SDR to **1967**, when it was agreed.
SDRs exist as **book-keeping/accounting entries**.
Largest general allocation: about **$650 bn (SDR 456 bn)** in **August 2021**.

nf4b45a8b38a.s: The form in which Special Drawing Rights are maintained is best described as:
nf4b45a8b38a.x: SDRs exist as book-keeping or accounting entries in the IMF’s records; they are not physical currency or metal.
nf4b45a8b38a.tq: Distinguish the reserve-asset concept from a physical medium of payment.
xs: **SDRs** exist as **book-keeping or accounting entries** — option **(3)** (APPSC-G2 2025 key; PYQ 2025).
They are not physical gold, silver or circulating notes.
xa: ⚠ Trap: where options are only paper currency/gold/silver, the key chose **paper currency** (PYQ 2025).
Called **"paper gold"**.
Created in **1969** under the IMF's **First Amendment**.

n03be05cd78a.s: Which one of the following is NOT included in the SDR basket?
n03be05cd78a.x: The SDR basket contains the US dollar, euro, Chinese renminbi, Japanese yen and pound sterling. The Indian rupee is not included.
n03be05cd78a.tq: Find the outsider in a named five-currency basket.
xs: The **Indian rupee** is **not** in the SDR basket — option **(2)**.
Basket (since **1 Oct 2016**): **US dollar, euro, Chinese renminbi, Japanese yen, pound sterling**.
xa: ⚠ Older notes list only four currencies, without the **renminbi**.
SDR = **interest-bearing** reserve asset created by the IMF.
Largest allocation: **SDR 456 bn** in **August 2021**.

n000492ba05c.s: The RBI instituted the SAARC Currency Swap Framework in:
n000492ba05c.x: The framework (2012) offers short-term BoP liquidity through bilateral swaps with the RBI, with a 3-month tenor rollable twice.
xa: **2024-2027** window: **₹250 billion** INR window + **$2 billion** USD-euro facility.
**Maldives** drew **$400 million** (**Oct 2024**).
First **₹30 billion** INR drawdown: Maldives, **Apr 2026**.

n9b515b212ab.s: Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVAs) are rupee accounts of:
o: Indian banks maintained with foreign banks
Foreign banks maintained with banks in India
The RBI with foreign central banks
n9b515b212ab.x: SRVAs are rupee accounts of foreign banks with Indian banks, enabling INR trade settlement; since 2025 surplus balances may go into corporate bonds and CPs.
xa: ⚠ **Vostro** = "yours"; **nostro** = "ours".
SRVA countries: **Russia**, **UAE**, **Tanzania**.
INR framework: RBI, **July 2022**.

nindian-economy-43-6.s: The Special Drawing Right (SDR), created by the IMF in 1969, was meant to:
o: Replace the US dollar in trade
Fix the world price of gold
nindian-economy-43-6.x: The SDR is an IMF reserve asset created in 1969 to supplement member countries' official reserves.
n: The SDR was created to supplement member countries' official reserves. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 63-64]
xa: Originally defined in gold: **35 SDR = 1 ounce**; redefined on a **basket of currencies** after **1973**.
Basket since **1 Oct 2016**: **US dollar, euro, Chinese renminbi, Japanese yen, pound sterling**.
SDRs exist as **book-keeping/accounting entries** (APPSC-G2 2025 key).

nindian-economy-43-8.s: The Reserve Tranche Position (RTP) was historically known by which name?
nindian-economy-43-8.x: The reserve tranche was once called the 'gold tranche', because it was paid in gold. 'Paper gold' means the SDR.
n: The Reserve Tranche Position was historically called the gold tranche. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 63-64]
xs: The **Reserve Tranche Position** was historically called the **Gold Tranche** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is a member's **unconditional drawing position** with the IMF.
"**Paper gold**" refers to the **SDR**, not the reserve tranche; **FCA** is a separate reserve component.
xa: India's reserves: **FCA > Gold > SDR > RTP**; **RBI** is the custodian.
Reserve (gold) tranche = part of the **IMF quota** paid in reserve assets.
Reserves at **$785.71 bn** (15 Sep 2026) — India **4th largest** holder.

nca598715203.s: The INR trade settlement mechanism was incorporated into which of the following?
nca598715203.x: The INR trade settlement framework introduced by the RBI in July 2022 was built into the Foreign Trade Policy 2023.
nca598715203.tq: Link the framework with its specific policy instrument and year.
xs: The **INR trade settlement framework** (RBI, **July 2022**) was built into **Foreign Trade Policy 2023** — option **(1)**.
**FEMA 1999** is the forex law, not the vehicle for this framework.
xa: It uses **Special Rupee Vostro Accounts** (e.g. **Russia**, **UAE**, **Tanzania**).
Since **2025**, surplus SRVA balances can go into corporate bonds and **CPs**.
Rupee-dirham settlement is operational with the **UAE**.

n01e4cc1dc8a.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a Vostro account from a Nostro account?
o: Vostro is denominated only in US dollars, whereas Nostro is denominated only in euros.
Vostro means a foreign bank's rupee account with a domestic bank, whereas Nostro means our account with a foreign bank.
Vostro is an account maintained only by the RBI, whereas Nostro is maintained only by the IMF.
Vostro is used for domestic taxation, whereas Nostro is used for government borrowing.
n01e4cc1dc8a.x: “Vostro” means “yours” and refers to the foreign bank's account with a domestic bank. “Nostro” means “ours” and refers to a domestic bank's account with a foreign bank.
n01e4cc1dc8a.tq: Separate the two look-alike banking terms by asking whose account is being described.
xs: **Vostro** = "yours" — a **foreign bank's account with a domestic bank**; **nostro** = "ours" — our account with a foreign bank — option **(2)**.
Neither is tied to a single currency, the IMF or taxation.
xa: **Special Rupee Vostro Accounts** enable INR trade settlement.
SRVA examples: **Russia**, **UAE**, **Tanzania**.
Surplus SRVA balances can be invested in corporate bonds and **CPs** since **2025**.

n2530ad5e9aa.s: The Indian rupee symbol ₹ was adopted on 15 July 2010. Who designed it?
n2530ad5e9aa.x: The symbol ₹ was adopted on 15 July 2010 and was designed by D. Udaya Kumar.
n2530ad5e9aa.tq: Combine the date and designer in a direct identification question.
xs: The rupee symbol **₹** was adopted on **15 July 2010** and designed by **D. Udaya Kumar** — option **(1)**.
The others named are not credited with the design in the notes.
xa: ⚠ FIRST/LAST: rupee symbol **2010**; current account convertibility **1994**.
**Masala bonds** — rupee bonds issued abroad — first issued **2014**.
INR trade settlement framework: **July 2022**.

n20d969e1106.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about masala bonds?
o: They are rupee-denominated bonds issued abroad, with currency risk on the investor.
Maharashtra was the first Indian State to issue them.
The name was given by the IFC.
The first masala bonds were listed on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange.
n20d969e1106.x: Kerala (2019), not Maharashtra, was the first State to issue masala bonds.
xa: **Samurai** = yen / Japan; **Panda** = yuan / China.
Rupee symbol adopted **15 July 2010**.
**SRVA** surplus balances can be invested in corporate bonds since **2025**.

n7f093fa5655.s: The first INR drawdown under the SAARC framework was made by:
n7f093fa5655.x: The first INR drawdown under the SAARC framework was made by the Maldives in April 2026.
n7f093fa5655.tq: Use the first-event and country-date combination as a three-part recall test.
xs: The first INR drawdown under the **SAARC** framework was by the **Maldives** in **April 2026** — option **(1)**.
It was **₹30 billion**, from the dedicated INR window.
xa: Maldives had drawn **$400 million** in **Oct 2024**.
**2024-2027** window: **₹250 billion** INR + **$2 billion** USD-euro.
Framework set up by RBI in **2012**.

n7a5e18348a3.s: FEMA, 1999, which replaced the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973, came into force on:
n7a5e18348a3.x: FERA, 1973 was replaced by FEMA, 1999, which came into force on 1 June 2000.
xa: Replacement proposed in the **1997-98** Budget.
FERA was **restrictive**.
**Tarapore Committee I** came in **1997**.

n9d61cc9b207.s: The Director-General of the World Trade Organization is:
n9d61cc9b207.x: The WTO, headquartered in Geneva, is headed by Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala; India is a founding member of both GATT and the WTO.
xa: The WTO was established on **1 Jan 1995** and had **166 members** in **Apr 2026**.
India ranked **18th** in merchandise exports with a **1.8%** share (**WTO Global Trade Outlook, April 2025**).
Only two new WTO agreements in **30 years**: **TFA** and **AFS**.
The **AFS** is the WTO's first agreement with an **environmental-sustainability objective**.

nc28eaf12de7.s: Under the WTO's Most-Favoured-Nation principle, a customs advantage given to one trading partner must generally be:
o: Extended to all other WTO trading partners
nc28eaf12de7.x: MFN means non-discrimination among trading partners, so an advantage given to one partner must generally go to all other WTO partners, subject to permitted exceptions.
xa: ⚠ **US unilateral tariffs** (**2025-26**) violate **MFN** and bound-rate obligations.
**National treatment**: imports are treated like domestic goods **once inside** the market.
The **Singapore issues** (**MC1, 1996**): investment, competition, procurement transparency, trade facilitation.
Plurilaterals such as the **E-Commerce Agreement** (**66 members**) and **IFD** are debated against WTO **consensus**.

nce3952442cf.s: As of April 2026, the World Trade Organization had how many members?
nce3952442cf.x: The WTO had 166 members as of April 2026. 123 was the number of contracting parties in the Uruguay Round (and India was the 123rd member to accept the Fisheries Subsidies Agreement); 164 and 150 are older or wrong membership figures.
xs: The WTO had **166 members** in **April 2026** — option **(4)**.
**123** is the number of **Uruguay Round contracting parties** (and India's number as an **AFS** acceptor), not WTO membership.
xa: ⚠ "**110** countries" is a later GATT-era membership, and **23** was GATT's founding number.
**MC14** at **Yaounde** (**Mar 2026**) was attended by all **166** members.
The **IFD** plurilateral was backed by **129 of 166** members, but **India blocked** it at MC14.
WTO: established **1 Jan 1995**; HQ **Geneva**; DG **Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala**.

nab2d9e6b2a6.s: The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies was adopted at:
nab2d9e6b2a6.x: MC12 at Geneva (June 2022) adopted the Fisheries Subsidies Agreement and a COVID-related TRIPS waiver.
xa: The **AFS** entered into force in **September 2025**.
**India** became the **123rd** member to deposit its Instrument of Acceptance (**July 2026**).
The moratorium **lapsed on 31 Mar 2026** for the first time (**MC14**).
AFS is the WTO's **first agreement with an environmental-sustainability objective**.

n18cabf95880.s: The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies is the first WTO agreement with which objective?
n18cabf95880.x: The Fisheries Subsidies Agreement is the WTO's first agreement with an environmental-sustainability objective.
xa: Only two new WTO agreements in **30 years**: the **TFA** and the **AFS**.
Adopted at **MC12 Geneva (2022)**; **in force September 2025**.
**India** became the **123rd** member to deposit its Instrument of Acceptance (**July 2026**).
**Aquaculture and inland fishing** are exempt; a **Fish Fund** helps poorer members.

n609b4bd2ce9.s: Phase 2 of the WTO fisheries subsidies negotiations, on overcapacity and overfishing, was at MC14:
o: Deferred to the General Council in Geneva
Referred to the Dispute Settlement Body
n609b4bd2ce9.x: Phase 2 was not concluded at MC14; it was sent to the General Council in Geneva.
xa: **Phase 1** (the **AFS**) was adopted at **MC12 (2022)** and entered into force in **September 2025**.
AFS bans subsidies to **IUU fishing**, unregulated high seas and overfished stocks.
MC14 also left **PSH** deadlocked and saw the **moratorium** lapse.

n912ff00ddce.s: The WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement was concluded as part of the Bali package at:
n912ff00ddce.x: The TFA came from the Bali package at MC9 (2013); India ratified it in 2016.
xa: Bali also gave the interim **Peace Clause** on food stockholding.
TFA and **AFS** are the only two new agreements in **30 years**.
**Trade facilitation** was one of the "**Singapore issues**" from **MC1 (1996)**.

nd1c2c12cfb6.s: WTO dispute DS456, which India lost to the US in 2016, related to:
nd1c2c12cfb6.x: DS456 concerned solar cells; DS541 (MEIS, SEZ, EOU) went against India in 2019 and the ICT panel ruled against India in 2023.
xa: **Sugar** case (**Brazil, Australia, Guatemala**): panel against India **2021**; appealed.
Appeals go "into the void" because the **Appellate Body** is non-functional since **Dec 2019**.
India has **not joined** the stop-gap **MPIA**.

n2a3a408a3ca.s: India's main concern about plurilateral initiatives such as the IFD and the E-Commerce Agreement is that they:
o: May fragment the WTO by moving away from consensus
n2a3a408a3ca.x: India fears plurilaterals may fragment the WTO by weakening consensus-based multilateralism.
xa: The **E-Commerce Agreement** was signed separately by **66 members**, barring duties on digital trade.
The WTO's **Ministerial Conference** is the highest decision-making body.
MC14 (**Yaounde**, **Mar 2026**) failed to issue a declaration.

nindian-economy-12-2.s: Which of the following about the WTO is NOT correct?
o: It was established under the Marrakesh Agreement of 1994
It came into being on 1 January 1994
nindian-economy-12-2.x: The WTO came into being on 1 January 1995, not 1994, under the Marrakesh Agreement signed in 1994; it replaced the GATT and is headquartered in Geneva.
n: WTO was established on 1 January 1995. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 15-16]
The agreement associated with WTO is the Marrakesh Agreement of 1994. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 15-16]
The headquarters of WTO is in Geneva, Switzerland. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 15-16]
WTO was established in 1995. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 15-16]
xa: WTO has **166 members** (Apr 2026); DG **Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala**.
WTO = **third pillar** of the world economy with the **IMF** and **World Bank**.
India is a founding member of both **GATT** and **WTO**.

n5cef36a18ed.s: The Uruguay Round, launched at Punta del Este in 1986, was which round of GATT negotiations?
n5cef36a18ed.x: The Uruguay Round was the eighth GATT round, launched at Punta del Este in September 1986 and concluded in 1993 with 123 contracting parties.
xa: Uruguay Round aims: cut **farm subsidies**, open **services**, cover **investment** and **IPR**.
The **Dunkel Draft** (**December 1991**) carried **Arthur Dunkel**'s proposals for the Uruguay Round agreements.
⚠ **123** is also the number India got when it deposited its **AFS** Instrument of Acceptance (**July 2026**).
GATT itself was signed in **1947** with **23 countries** and held **8 rounds** in all.

n621fe788bfb.s: The Dunkel Draft contained proposals for the agreements of which round of trade negotiations?
n621fe788bfb.x: The Dunkel Draft was made up of proposals by Arthur Dunkel, GATT Director-General and Chair of the Trade Negotiations Committee, for the Uruguay Round agreements.
xa: The draft was tabled in **December 1991** (some notes say **20 October 1991**).
The Uruguay Round ran **1986-1993** with **123** contracting parties.
It led to the **Marrakesh Agreement** (**April 1994**) and the **WTO** (**1 January 1995**).
The WTO is called the **third pillar** of the world economy, with the **IMF** and the **World Bank**.

nf2df7412b87.s: Trade-related investment measures are covered by which WTO agreement?
nf2df7412b87.x: TRIMS covers investment measures; TRIPS covers IPR, GATS services and SPS/TBT health and technical standards.
xa: TRIPS compliance: **Patents Act** amended **2005** (product patents); **GI of Goods Act, 1999**.
TRIMS example: **local-content rules** — India phased out local-content conditions.
SPS/TBT compliance: **Food Safety and Standards Act 2006**.
**TFA (Bali 2013)** simplifies customs; **ITA (1996)** gives zero duty on IT products.

naf2e2174c85.s: For geographical-indication protection, India relies on:
o: The Lisbon Agreement, of which it is a founding member
The Lisbon Agreement, applied only to farm exports
TRIPS, as it is not a member of the Lisbon Agreement
The Lisbon Agreement in preference to TRIPS
naf2e2174c85.x: India is not a member of the Lisbon Agreement on appellations and prefers TRIPS for GI protection.
xa: India's GI law: the **GI of Goods Act, 1999**.
**TRIPS (1995)** sets **minimum IPR standards**.
Other TRIPS-linked laws: **Patents Act** amended **2005**; **PPV&FR Act 2001**.

nindian-economy-12-5.s: The World Trade Organization, which grew out of GATT's Uruguay Round, came into effect in:
nindian-economy-12-5.x: GATT dates from 1948 and the WTO from 1995.
n: WTO originated from the Uruguay Round of GATT. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 15-16]
GATT came into effect in 1948. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 15-16]
The main focus of GATT was the reduction of tariffs and quantitative restrictions. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 15-16]
GATT was established in 1947. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 15-16]
WTO was established in 1995. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 15-16]
xa: Uruguay Round: **1986 to 1993**, launched at **Punta del Este**; **123** contracting parties.
**Dunkel Draft**: tabled **December 1991** by **Arthur Dunkel**.
Marrakesh Agreement signed **April 1994**.

nindian-economy-13-6.s: GATS, TRIPS and TRIMS extended trade rules beyond goods as a result of which GATT round?
nindian-economy-13-6.x: The Uruguay Round expanded the framework beyond goods through GATS, TRIPS and TRIMS.
n: The Uruguay Round expanded the trade framework beyond goods. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 16-17]
The Uruguay Round expanded the trade framework to include GATS. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 16-17]
The Uruguay Round expanded the trade framework to include TRIPS. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 16-17]
The Uruguay Round expanded the trade framework to include TRIMS. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 16-17]
xa: Uruguay Round: **8th round**, **1986 to 1993**.
India amended the Patents Act in **2005** (product patents) for TRIPS.
**TFA** (Bali **2013**) — India ratified in **2016**.

n012be0ccfa6.s: The first WTO Ministerial Conference was held at:
n012be0ccfa6.x: MC1 was at Singapore (1996), MC2 Geneva (1998), MC3 Seattle (1999) and MC4 Doha (2001).
xa: **MC5 Cancun (2003)** collapsed over agriculture/Singapore issues; the **G-33** was formed.
**MC6 Hong Kong (2005)**: farm export subsidies to end; **duty-free quota-free** for LDCs.

n04acaf0aba1.s: The Doha Development Agenda was launched at:
n04acaf0aba1.x: MC4 at Doha (2001) launched the Doha Development Agenda and adopted the TRIPS-public health declaration.
xa: The **Doha Round** is the "**development round**" (agriculture, **NAMA**, services) — still **unfinished**.
The **G-33** was formed in **2003** during the Doha process.
**NAMA-11**: developing countries (incl. India) on non-agricultural market access.
**G-90** = **African Group** + **ACP** + **LDCs**.

n6fe2a84f140.s: The elimination of agricultural export subsidies was associated with the WTO Ministerial Conference held at:
n6fe2a84f140.x: The Nairobi Ministerial Conference of 2015 adopted the outcome concerning elimination of agricultural export subsidies.
n6fe2a84f140.tq: Use the distinctive agricultural outcome to identify the correct conference.
xs: The **elimination of agricultural export subsidies** came at **MC10, Nairobi, 2015** — option **(4)**.
**Bali 2013** = TFA + Peace Clause; **Buenos Aires 2017** = no declaration; **Geneva 2022** = AFS.
xa: **MC6 Hong Kong (2005)** first agreed that farm export subsidies would end.
**Export competition** is one of the three **AoA** pillars, with domestic support and market access.
**SCM Agreement** classes subsidies as **prohibited**, **actionable** and **non-actionable**.
⚠ India lost the **export subsidies** case (**US, DS541**) over **MEIS, SEZ, EOU** schemes in **2019**.

n0046fdfe8ef.s: At the WTO MC14 at Yaoundé (2026), India blocked the addition of which plurilateral agreement to Annex 4?
n0046fdfe8ef.x: At MC14 India blocked adding the Investment Facilitation for Development (IFD) plurilateral agreement to Annex 4, although 129 of 166 members backed it.
xa: Debate: **plurilaterals** (**IFD**, **E-Commerce Agreement**) vs **consensus**; India fears **fragmentation**.
The **TRIPS non-violation moratorium** lapsed at MC14.
No **permanent solution on PSH** at MC14.
MC14 was held on **26-29 Mar 2026** at **Yaounde, Cameroon**.

n5c61c22eae0.s: The Doha Round of WTO negotiations, which remains unfinished, began in:
n5c61c22eae0.x: The Doha Round began in 2001; it deals with agriculture, non-agricultural market access and services and remains unfinished.
xa: It is called the "**Development round**"; launched at **MC4 Doha** with a **TRIPS-public health declaration**.
**NAMA-11**: developing countries (incl. India) negotiating **non-agricultural market access**.
**G-33** formed in **2003** during the Doha talks at **Cancun**.
⚠ "Doha Round concluded" is a trap — it **never concluded**.

ne2e13eb215c.s: The Fourteenth WTO Ministerial Conference (MC14), held in March 2026, took place at which of the following places?
ne2e13eb215c.x: WTO MC14 was held at Yaoundé, Cameroon, from 26 to 29 March 2026.
ne2e13eb215c.tq: Use the venue-based direct-recall method for international conferences.
xs: **MC14** was held at **Yaoundé, Cameroon**, on **26-29 Mar 2026** — option **(3)**.
xa: MC14 ended with **no ministerial declaration** — only a draft "**Yaounde package**".
The **e-commerce moratorium** and **TRIPS non-violation moratorium** lapsed.
**India blocked** adding the **IFD** to **Annex 4**.
⚠ MC9 Bali = TFA + Peace Clause; MC12 Geneva = AFS; MC14 Yaounde = no declaration.

nba95d0a7aef.s: Under the WTO Agreement on Subsidies and Countervailing Measures (SCM), subsidies for research and development, regional development and environmental purposes have been classed as:
nba95d0a7aef.x: The SCM Agreement groups subsidies as prohibited (the 'red light' category), actionable (open to countervailing duty) and non-actionable (R&D, regional and environmental). Amber Box is an Agreement on Agriculture category for trade-distorting farm support, not an SCM class.
nba95d0a7aef.tq: SCM traffic lights: prohibited (red), actionable, non-actionable (R&D, regional, green).
xs: Subsidies for **R&D, regional and environmental** purposes are **non-actionable** under the **SCM Agreement** — option **(3)**.
**Prohibited** subsidies form the "**red light**" category; **actionable** ones attract **countervailing duty**.
**Amber Box** is an **AoA** category, not an SCM class.
xa: ⚠ "Red box" is not an AoA box — "red light" belongs only to the **SCM** prohibited category.
**Amber Box** = trade-distorting farm support measured as **AMS**.
India lost the **export subsidies** case (**US, DS541**) over **MEIS, SEZ, EOU** schemes.

nfc19f0f3353.s: The Peace Clause adopted at Bali in 2013 provides protection to developing countries from disputes concerning:
o: Trade in banking and insurance services
nfc19f0f3353.x: The Bali Peace Clause shields developing-country public stockholding programmes from disputes until a permanent solution is found.
nfc19f0f3353.tq: Link the clause to its conference, year and specific agricultural issue.
xs: The **Peace Clause (Bali MC9, 2013)** shields developing countries' **public stockholding for food security** from disputes — option **(2)**.
It is **interim** protection until a **permanent solution** — no legal challenge even if procurement breaches **AoA** limits.
xa: India first invoked the Peace Clause for **rice** in **2020**.
**MC14 (2026)** still produced no **permanent solution on PSH**.
The **Bali package** also included the **Trade Facilitation Agreement**.
India's **GI** protection works through **TRIPS** (not the **Lisbon Agreement**) — a separate issue.

nb53574094eb.s: Which one of the following is NOT prohibited under the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies?
o: Subsidies for fishing on unregulated high seas
Subsidies for illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing
Subsidies for fishing in overfished stocks, unless rebuilding conditions apply
nb53574094eb.x: The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies covers marine wild capture fishing and at-sea support. Aquaculture and inland fishing are exempt.
nb53574094eb.tq: Find the excluded activity rather than selecting one of the prohibited forms of fishing support.
xs: Subsidies for **inland fishing** are **not banned** — **aquaculture and inland fishing are exempt** from the AFS — option **(2)**.
The AFS covers **marine wild capture** and **at-sea support**.
It bans subsidies to **IUU fishing**, **unregulated high seas** and **overfished stocks** (unless rebuilding) — options (1), (3), (4).
xa: Developing countries/LDCs get a **2-year** EEZ exemption; a **Fish Fund** helps poorer members.
Adopted at **MC12 (2022)**; **in force September 2025**.
**Phase 2** (overcapacity, overfishing) was deferred at **MC14** to the **General Council**.
AP angle: AFS rules matter for **AP's marine fisher folk**; fisher bodies sought a "**fisher-centric**" approach.

n816c0ad7b79.s: Which pair of WTO agreements is identified as the only two new agreements concluded in the last 30 years?
o: TFA and Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
n816c0ad7b79.x: The Trade Facilitation Agreement and the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies are identified as the only two new WTO agreements concluded in the last 30 years.
n816c0ad7b79.tq: Start from the distinctive pair and eliminate agreements belonging to the original WTO package.
xs: The only two new WTO agreements in **30 years** are the **TFA** and the **Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies** — option **(2)**.
**TRIPS**, **GATS**, **TRIMS**, **SPS/TBT** date from the WTO's start (**TRIPS 1995**); the **ITA** dates from **1996**.
xa: **TFA**: **Bali MC9 (2013)**; simplifies **customs procedures**; India ratified in **2016**.
**AFS**: adopted **MC12 (2022)**; in force **September 2025**.
AFS = WTO's **first agreement with an environmental-sustainability objective**.
**India blocked** adding the **IFD** plurilateral to **Annex 4** at **MC14**.

nb6be5333423.s: The WTO dispute brought by Brazil, Australia and Guatemala against India concerned:
nb6be5333423.x: The sugar dispute concerned India's cane prices and export subsidies; the panel ruled against India in 2021 and the matter was appealed.
xa: ⚠ Appeals are stuck: the **Appellate Body** has been non-functional since **Dec 2019**.
**DS541** (**US**): MEIS, SEZ, EOU — panel against India **2019**.
The **MPIA** (**EU**-led, **2020**) is a stop-gap; India has not joined.

n1e4efa65ea3.s: Indian fisher bodies, including Andhra Pradesh's marine fisher folk, have sought which approach to WTO fisheries-subsidy rules?
n1e4efa65ea3.x: The rules matter to Andhra Pradesh's marine fisher folk, and Indian fisher bodies have sought a fisher-centric approach to implementing them.
xa: The AFS covers **marine wild capture** + at-sea support.
Developing countries get a **2-year** EEZ exemption and a **Fish Fund**.
India joined the AFS in **July 2026** as the **123rd** member.

nf63ac3c0fa0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about subsidy boxes under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture?
o: Amber Box covers price- or quantity-linked support such as MSP, measured as AMS.
Blue Box covers direct payments under production-limiting programmes.
Green Box support is not trade-distorting and has no limits.
Blue Box support is subject to reduction commitments.
nf63ac3c0fa0.x: Blue Box payments are exempt from reduction commitments.
xa: **De minimis**: developed **5%**, developing **10%** of value of agricultural output.
⚠ "Red box", "Orange box", "Yellow box" are not AoA boxes.
AoA pillars: **domestic support, market access, export competition**.

n48e064cc4c7.s: The Agreement on Agriculture (AoA) rests on which of the following three pillars?
o: Domestic support, market access and export competition
Market access, investment protection and government procurement
Export competition, services and industrial subsidies
Domestic support, intellectual property and trade facilitation
n48e064cc4c7.x: The AoA has three pillars: domestic support, market access and export competition.
n48e064cc4c7.tq: Identify the standard three-part structure of the agreement.
xs: The **AoA (1995)** rests on **domestic support, market access and export competition** — option **(1)**.
Investment, IPR and trade facilitation belong to **TRIMS**, **TRIPS** and the **TFA**, not the AoA pillars.
xa: Domestic support is sorted into **Green**, **Blue** and **Amber** boxes.
Market access: **tariffication** of non-tariff barriers.
Export competition: **MC10 Nairobi (2015)** eliminated agricultural export subsidies.
The **Uruguay Round** aimed to cut **farm subsidies**.

n6208cd95cea.s: Which situation best illustrates the national-treatment principle under WTO rules?
o: A country gives an export subsidy to domestic firms.
A country grants the same tariff concession to every foreign trading partner.
An imported product, after entering the domestic market, is treated like a similar domestic product for internal taxation and regulation.
A country imposes a quantitative restriction on all imports.
n6208cd95cea.x: National treatment requires imported goods to be treated like domestic goods once they have entered the market, particularly in internal taxation and regulation. Equal treatment among foreign trading partners is the MFN principle.
n6208cd95cea.tq: Separate national treatment from MFN by focusing on the point after importation.
xs: **National treatment** means an **imported product**, once **inside** the domestic market, is **treated like a similar domestic product** — option **(3)**.
Giving the same tariff concession to every foreign partner is **MFN** (no discrimination among trading partners), not national treatment.
xa: **MFN** = no discrimination **among** trading partners; national treatment = no discrimination between **imports and domestic goods**.
⚠ **US unilateral tariffs** (**2025-26**) violate **MFN** and bound-rate obligations.
**TRIMS** deals with investment measures affecting trade, e.g. **local-content rules**.
India lost the **solar cells** case (**US, DS456**) over **domestic content** in the **National Solar Mission**.

nd89cfb3b692.s: The de minimis limit for agricultural domestic support is what percentage of production value for developed and developing countries, respectively?
nd89cfb3b692.x: The de minimis limit is 5% of production value for developed countries and 10% for developing countries.
nd89cfb3b692.tq: Read the paired percentages in the correct developed-country/developing-country order.
xs: **De minimis** Amber support allowed without penalty is **5%** of agricultural output value for **developed** and **10%** for **developing** countries — option **(2)**.
Option (1) reverses the two figures.
xa: **Tariffication**: developed cut **36%** over **6 years**; developing **24%** over **10 years**.
**Amber Box** support (**MSP**, power, fertiliser, seed, irrigation) is measured as **AMS**.
India's **NFSA** procurement counts in the Amber box on an **outdated reference price**.
The **Peace Clause** shields food-security procurement even if it breaches **AoA** limits.

n9a9bd641ce8.s: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, conversion of non-tariff barriers into tariffs is called:
n9a9bd641ce8.x: This is tariffication; developed countries were then to cut tariffs by 36% over 6 years.
xa: **Market access** is one of the three AoA pillars with **domestic support** and **export competition**.
**De minimis**: **5%** (developed) vs **10%** (developing) of agricultural output value.
The **AoA** dates from **1995**.

n076fc55cf3d.s: Which country first invoked the WTO Peace Clause for rice in 2020?
n076fc55cf3d.x: India was the first country to invoke the Peace Clause for rice in 2020.
n076fc55cf3d.tq: Distinguish the invoking country from countries associated with India’s sugar dispute.
xs: **India** first invoked the **Peace Clause** for **rice** in **2020** — option **(3)**.
**Brazil**, **Australia** and **Guatemala** were complainants against India in the **sugar** dispute, not Peace Clause users.
xa: The Peace Clause comes from **Bali MC9 (2013)**, shielding **public stockholding**.
India's demand: a **permanent solution** — **MSP** procurement for **NFSA** counts in the **Amber box**.
**India** + **African Group** want a permanent shield for programmes like the **NFSA**.
The **sugar** panel went against India in **2021**; India appealed.

n99f6780c423.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 14th WTO Ministerial Conference at Yaounde (March 2026)?
o: It produced only a draft 'Yaounde package' and no ministerial declaration.
A permanent solution on public stockholding was achieved.
The e-commerce moratorium lapsed on 31 March 2026.
Sixty-six members signed a separate E-Commerce Agreement barring duties on digital trade.
n99f6780c423.x: The permanent public-stockholding solution remained deadlocked at MC14.
xa: The **TRIPS non-violation moratorium** also lapsed at MC14.
**India blocked** adding the **IFD** plurilateral to **Annex 4** (backed by **129 of 166**).
Fisheries **Phase 2** was deferred to the **General Council, Geneva**.
MC14 is widely seen as a **failure**.

n07fb5d4687c.s: At MC14 (2026), India sought a permanent shield for public stockholding programmes like the NFSA along with the:
n07fb5d4687c.x: India and the African Group sought a permanent solution, which MC14 did not deliver.
xa: **MC13 Abu Dhabi (2024)** also produced **no PSH solution**.
The interim **Peace Clause** dates from **Bali MC9 (2013)**.
India first invoked the Peace Clause for **rice** in **2020**.
MSP procurement counts in the **Amber box** on an **outdated reference price**.

n4c24fce9fbf.s: The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies, adopted in 2022, entered into force in:
n4c24fce9fbf.x: Adopted at MC12 in 2022, it entered into force in September 2025.
xa: AFS is the WTO's **first agreement with an environmental-sustainability objective**.
Only two new WTO agreements in **30 years**: **TFA** and **AFS**.
**India** joined as the **123rd** member to deposit acceptance in **July 2026**.
⚠ **123** is also the number of **Uruguay Round** contracting parties.

nc0f5aa22b82.s: India became the 123rd WTO member to deposit its Instrument of Acceptance for the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies in:
nc0f5aa22b82.x: India deposited its Instrument of Acceptance in July 2026, becoming the 123rd WTO member to do so.
nc0f5aa22b82.tq: Combine a membership number with the exact month and year of a treaty action.
xs: India deposited its **AFS Instrument of Acceptance** as the **123rd member** in **July 2026** — option **(4)**.
**September 2025** is when the AFS **entered into force**; **March 2026** was **MC14** at Yaounde.
xa: ⚠ **123** is also the number of **Uruguay Round** contracting parties.
The AFS was adopted at **MC12 (2022)** — the WTO's first agreement with an **environmental** objective.
Developing countries/LDCs get a **2-year** EEZ exemption.
AP angle: the rules matter for **AP's marine fisher folk**; fisher bodies sought a "**fisher-centric**" approach.

n2b8d0c3d1b5.s: The WTO moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions, in place since 1998, lapsed on:
n2b8d0c3d1b5.x: The moratorium lapsed for the first time on 31 March 2026.
xa: **MC12 (2022)** extended it; **MC13 (2024)** extended it to **31 Mar 2026**.
It lapsed **for the first time** at **MC14** (**Yaounde**).
Developing countries **lose tariff revenue** on digital imports.
**66 members** separately signed an **E-Commerce Agreement**.

n76ab42c3c3b.s: The WTO Appellate Body has been non-functional since:
n76ab42c3c3b.x: The Appellate Body stopped functioning in December 2019 as the US blocked appointments; India has not joined the EU-led MPIA (2020).
xa: MPIA = **Multi-Party Interim Appeal Arbitration Arrangement**.
India's **DS541** loss (**2019**) was "**appealed into the void**".
**BRICS New Delhi Declaration (Sep 2026)** sought restoration of the **two-tier WTO dispute settlement**.

n765173bfee1.s: Along with IMF and World Bank quota and voting reform, the BRICS New Delhi Declaration (September 2026) sought:
o: Restoration of the WTO Appellate Body
Replacement of the WTO by a BRICS trade body
Merger of the IMF and the World Bank
n765173bfee1.x: The declaration sought IMF and World Bank quota and voting reform and restoration of the two-tier WTO dispute-settlement system, i.e. the Appellate Body.
xa: The **Appellate Body** is paralysed since **Dec 2019** — the **US** blocked appointments.
The **MPIA** (**EU**-led, **2020**) is a stop-gap; India has not joined.
The WTO is the **third pillar** of the world economy with the **IMF** and **World Bank**.

n9192e4e8e59.s: The WTO Ministerial Conference, its highest decision-making body, must meet at least once every:
n9192e4e8e59.x: Under the Marrakesh Agreement the Ministerial Conference meets at least once every two years.
xa: **MC1** was at **Singapore (1996)**; **MC14** at **Yaounde, Cameroon (26-29 Mar 2026)**.
**MC14** ended with **no ministerial declaration** — only a draft "**Yaounde package**".
⚠ **MC11 Buenos Aires (2017)** also produced **no ministerial declaration**.
Earlier breakdowns: **Seattle 1999** and **Cancún 2003**.

n276e3416002.s: The G-33, formed in 2003 during the Doha process, mainly focuses on:
o: Interests of the African Group, ACP and LDCs
Food security, Special Safeguard Mechanism and special products
n276e3416002.x: The G-33 is a group of 40-plus developing countries, including India, focused on food security, the Special Safeguard Mechanism and special products.
xa: It was formed at **MC5 Cancun (2003)**, which collapsed over agriculture and Singapore issues.
**NAMA-11**: developing countries on **non-agricultural market access**.
**G-90** = **African Group** + **ACP** + **LDCs**.
The fisheries issue is handled by the **AFS**, not the G-33.

n76313474fa5.s: Which one of the following is NOT an official subsidy box under the Agreement on Agriculture?
n76313474fa5.x: Green, Blue and Amber are the subsidy boxes under the AoA. Red, Orange and Yellow are not AoA boxes; a prohibited-subsidy category described as a red-light category belongs to the SCM context.
n76313474fa5.tq: Find the odd term in a closely related list of official categories.
xs: **Red Box** is not an AoA box — option **(3)**.
The AoA boxes are **Green**, **Blue** and **Amber**.
xa: ⚠ "**Red box**", "**Orange box**" and "**Yellow box**" are all distractors.
A "**red light**" category exists only for **prohibited subsidies** under the **SCM Agreement**.
**Green** = not trade-distorting; **Blue** = production-limiting; **Amber** = trade-distorting.
SCM classes: **prohibited**, **actionable** (countervailing duty), **non-actionable**.

n695415e97f3.s: India argues that its MSP procurement for the National Food Security Act is counted as an Amber Box subsidy using:
n695415e97f3.x: India's public stockholding grievance is that MSP procurement is treated as Amber Box support calculated against an outdated historical reference price.
xa: **De minimis** limit for developing countries: **10%** of the value of agricultural output.
The **Peace Clause (Bali, 2013)** gives interim protection from disputes.
India first invoked it for **rice** in **2020**.
**MC14 (2026)**: no permanent PSH solution.

n379100a2348.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes FDI from FPI?
o: FDI is always debt; FPI is always equity
FDI is generally long-term and may carry management control; FPI is liquid and short-term
FDI is regulated only by SEBI; FPI only by the RBI
FDI is limited to unlisted firms; FPI to government securities
n379100a2348.x: FDI is generally long-term and may bring management control and technology, while FPI is liquid, potentially short-term 'hot money'.
xa: Threshold: **>=10%** in a listed company = FDI; **<10%** = FPI.
FPI opened in India in **1992**; **FII and FPI** are essentially the same.
FPI flows are driven by the **US Fed**/interest rates and global risk appetite — "**flight to safety**" outflows.

nindian-economy-20-7.s: Foreign Institutional Investment (FII) is a form of:
nindian-economy-20-7.x: FII is portfolio investment, whereas FDI is direct investment in enterprises or sectors.
n: FDI is direct investment. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 29-30]
FDI involves investment in enterprises or sectors. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 29-30]
xa: FII is **more short-term** and **more volatile** than FDI.
FDI brings **capital along with technology and management**.
FPI opened in India in **1992**.

nindian-economy-20-2.s: Which of the following about the SEBI FPI Regulations, 2019 is NOT correct?
o: They kept QFIs outside the FPI framework
They brought FIIs under the FPI framework
They brought sub-accounts under the FPI framework
They unified several foreign investor categories as FPIs
nindian-economy-20-2.x: The 2019 Regulations brought FIIs, sub-accounts and QFIs together under the FPI framework, so QFIs were not kept outside.
n: The SEBI FPI Regulations, 2019 unified FIIs under the FPI framework. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 29-30]
The SEBI FPI Regulations, 2019 unified sub-accounts under the FPI framework. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 29-30]
The SEBI FPI Regulations, 2019 unified QFIs under the FPI framework. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 29-30]
The SEBI FPI Regulations were issued in 2019. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 29-30]
xa: FII and FPI are essentially the same.
FPI regulators: **SEBI (FPI Regulations, 2019) + RBI**.
Foreign capital includes **FDI, trade credit, NRI deposits and ECBs** (APPSC-GS 2019 key).

nb485fa8cc32.s: For a listed company, foreign investment is generally classified as FDI when the investor’s equity holding is:
nb485fa8cc32.x: Under the threshold associated with the Arvind Mayaram Committee classification, an equity holding of 10% or more in a listed company is treated as FDI. Holdings below 10% are classified as portfolio investment.
nb485fa8cc32.tq: Separate the threshold from the maximum sectoral cap.
xs: A holding of **10% or more** (**>=10%**) of equity in a **listed** company is **FDI** — option **(3)**.
Below **10%** (**<10%**) in a listed company is **FPI**, so "less than 10%" and "less than 5%" describe portfolio holdings.
xa: In an **unlisted** company, **any stake** counts as FDI.
The 10% line comes from the **Arvind Mayaram Committee** (under **FEMA**).
FDI = long-term, **management control**, technology; FPI = short-term, liquid "**hot money**".
⚠ The **March 2026** PN3 amendment also uses a **10%** line — for Chinese/HK beneficial ownership.

n5871cc36cdd.s: External commercial borrowings, trade credit and NRI deposits are all forms of:
n5871cc36cdd.x: Foreign capital in India includes FDI, trade credit, NRI deposits and ECBs.
xa: **FDI** and **FPI** are **non-debt**; **ECB, trade credit, FCCB** are **debt**.
**NRI deposits** (**FCNR(B), NRE**) are **banking capital** (debt).
**ADR/GDR** equity raised abroad is counted as **portfolio investment** in BoP data.

n2601098c4b2.s: Which one of the following is correctly classified as debt capital?
n2601098c4b2.x: External commercial borrowing is debt capital. FDI and FPI are non-debt forms, while ADRs represent equity raised abroad through depository receipts.
n2601098c4b2.tq: Separate debt instruments from non-debt equity instruments.
xs: An **External Commercial Borrowing (ECB)** is **debt** — option **(3)**.
**FDI** and **FPI** are **non-debt**; **ADR** equity is counted as **portfolio investment**.
xa: Other debt forms: **trade credit** and **FCCB**.
**ECBs are regulated by RBI** under **FEMA, 1999**.
**NRI deposits** (**FCNR(B), NRE**) count as banking capital (debt).

nbdcc4684322.s: In balance of payments data, ADRs and GDRs are counted as:
nbdcc4684322.x: ADRs and GDRs represent equity raised abroad through depository receipts and are counted as portfolio investment in balance of payments data.
nbdcc4684322.tq: Distinguish the form of fund-raising from its classification in BoP data.
xs: **ADRs/GDRs** — equity raised abroad through depository receipts — are counted as **portfolio investment** in **BoP** data — option **(4)**.
**NRI deposits** are banking capital; **ECBs** and **trade credit** are debt.
xa: **Participatory notes** are also a **portfolio channel**.
**FPI** is **non-debt**, portfolio (**<10%**) and liquid.
**FCCBs** are **debt**.

n35c39c7b4e4.s: Foreign Portfolio Investment was opened to India in:
n35c39c7b4e4.x: FPI was opened in 1992 and is regulated by SEBI under the FPI Regulations, 2019, along with the RBI.
xa: **FII and FPI** are essentially the same.
FPI debt limits (General Route): **6%** of Central G-secs, **2%** of State securities.
**VRR** and **FAR** steadied debt flows.
India's inclusion in the **JP Morgan EM bond index** draws passive bond inflows.

n4f97ecc0f72.s: Hyundai's facility at Sriperumbudur is an example of:
n4f97ecc0f72.x: Greenfield investment creates a new facility; brownfield means acquiring an existing business (e.g., Vodafone-Hutchison Essar).
xa: ⚠ Pharma: **greenfield 100% automatic**; **brownfield 74% automatic**, beyond needs approval.
FDI brings **technology and jobs** and finances the **CAD** with stable capital.

nindian-economy-19-1.s: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) is best described as:
o: A short-term domestic loan to Indian enterprises
A relatively volatile investment mainly in securities
A largely non-debt, longer-term foreign investment in Indian enterprises
A government investment made through public expenditure
nindian-economy-19-1.x: FDI is a mostly non-debt capital flow bringing longer-term foreign investment into Indian enterprises; volatile investment in securities is FPI.
n: FDI is a largely non-debt-creating capital flow. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FDI generally represents longer-term foreign investment in Indian enterprises. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FPI is more volatile than FDI. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FPI primarily represents financial capital. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FPI primarily involves investment in securities. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FDI is associated with capital. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
xa: FDI brings **technology transfer**, **management skills**, **innovation** and **employment**.
⚠ **Portfolio investment** does not automatically constitute FDI.
FDI types: **greenfield** (new facility) and **brownfield** (acquisition).

nindian-economy-19-2.s: Which of the following about FDI and FPI is NOT correct?
o: FDI can bring technology and management skills
FDI targets specific sectors or enterprises
FDI is generally more volatile than FPI
FPI is mainly investment in securities
nindian-economy-19-2.x: FDI is more stable and long-term; it is FPI that is the more volatile flow.
n: FDI is relatively stable and long-term. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FPI is more volatile than FDI. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FDI can bring technology and management skills. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FDI targets specific sectors and enterprises. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FPI primarily involves investment in securities. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FDI is associated with technology transfer. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FDI is associated with management skills. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
xa: FDI gives **greater involvement and control**; FPI has no comparable managerial involvement.
FPI is regulated by **SEBI + RBI**; FDI by **DPIIT + RBI**.

ne4221d238b1.s: Under the automatic route, foreign direct investment requires:
o: No prior approval, but post-facto reporting to the RBI
Prior approval of the concerned Ministry
ne4221d238b1.x: The automatic route needs no prior RBI or Government approval, only post-facto reporting to the RBI.
xa: Government-route applications go via the **FIF Portal** (**FIFP**), part of **NSWS** since **Aug 2022**.
**Negative list**: more than **90% of sectors** are automatic.
Government route examples: defence beyond **74%**, multi-brand retail, broadcasting, print media.

n6cb913990d0.s: In India, 100% FDI under the automatic route is allowed in which e-commerce model?
n6cb913990d0.x: The marketplace model allows 100% FDI through the automatic route; FDI in the inventory model is generally barred, apart from a later export-related relaxation.
xa: **Jul 2026**: inventory FDI allowed where inventory is used to **export domestically made goods**.
It is the first big relaxation in nearly a decade.
India's e-commerce exports are only **~$5 bn** vs **China**'s **$300 bn**.
**Multi-brand retail**: **51%**, Government route.

nb1811c1b3f0.s: In July 2026, FDI in inventory-based e-commerce was allowed in a specific situation when:
o: The inventory is used for exporting domestically manufactured goods.
The platform operates only as a marketplace.
The inventory is owned entirely by foreign companies for domestic resale.
The inventory is used to sell imported goods in the domestic market.
nb1811c1b3f0.x: The July 2026 relaxation allowed inventory-based e-commerce FDI where the inventory is used to export domestically manufactured goods.
nb1811c1b3f0.tq: Identify the precise condition attached to a policy relaxation rather than its broader sector label.
xs: **DPIIT** (**July 2026**) allowed inventory-based e-commerce FDI when **the inventory is used for exports of domestically manufactured goods** — option **(1)**.
Selling imported or foreign-owned inventory in the domestic market stays **barred**; marketplace was already **100% automatic**.
xa: First big relaxation in nearly a **decade**.
India's e-commerce exports: **~$5 bn** vs **China**'s **$300 bn**.
Inventory model was barred to **protect small traders**.

nf11f05f6855.s: Which of the following about India's FDI policy is NOT correct?
o: Caps were raised after 2014 in defence, insurance and pension.
The e-commerce marketplace model permits 100% FDI via the automatic route.
All sectors are exclusively on the automatic route.
More than 90% of sectors are on the automatic route.
nf11f05f6855.x: Some sectors still need the Government route, though over 90% are on the automatic route.
xa: India follows a **negative list** approach.
Some sectors are fully **prohibited** — e.g. **lottery**, **chit funds**, **atomic energy**.
Government-route applications use the **FIF Portal** (**NSWS**).

n9c5be931bbc.s: FDI in brownfield pharmaceutical projects is permitted under the automatic route up to:
n9c5be931bbc.x: Brownfield pharma allows 74% automatically (approval beyond), greenfield pharma and medical devices 100% automatically.
xa: **Greenfield** = new facility; **brownfield** = acquisition.
Also **100% automatic**: **NBFCs**, construction and real-estate broking.
⚠ **20%** Government route is the **public sector bank** limit, not pharma.

nb08401b0c2d.s: The FDI limit in the insurance sector was raised to 74% in:
nb08401b0c2d.x: The insurance FDI cap went from 26% to 49% in 2015, 74% in 2021 and 100% in 2025.
xa: **100%** is **automatic**, subject to **IRDAI**, on condition that the **entire premium** is invested in India.
It was announced in Union Budget **2025-26** and enabled via the **FEMA (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019**.
Insurance = **Entry 47, Union List**; IRDAI HQ **Hyderabad**.

n6bde8791ee6.s: FDI in the defence sector is permitted under the automatic route up to:
n6bde8791ee6.x: Defence allows 74% FDI under the automatic route and up to 100% through the Government route.
xa: Post-**2014** caps were raised in **defence**, **insurance**, **pension**.
Government route covers "defence **beyond 74%**".
**Space**: up to **100%** with sectoral conditions.

n0095650da90.s: The foreign investment cap in private-sector banks in India is:
n0095650da90.x: Private banks allow 74% (49% automatic); public-sector banks allow 20% via the Government route.
xa: The private-bank cap was raised to **74%** in **2004**.
Private banks illustrate "**automatic up to a cap, approval beyond**".
**NBFCs** are **100% automatic**.

n835d4a04665.s: The FDI limit and route for multi-brand retail trading in India is:
n835d4a04665.x: Multi-brand retail allows up to 51% FDI only through the Government route (in practice treated as barred). 100% automatic applies to single-brand retail, telecom and e-commerce marketplaces; 74% automatic is the defence limit; 49% automatic is the automatic slab within the private-bank and scheduled-airline caps.
xs: **Multi-brand retail**: **51%**, **Government route** — option **(3)**.
**100% automatic** is single-brand retail/telecom; **74% automatic** is defence; **49% automatic** is the private-bank/airline automatic slab.
xa: In practice multi-brand retail is treated as **barred** (**TH, Jul 2026**).
Exam angle: "**multi-brand retail cap**" — **51%**.
The **inventory e-commerce** ban also keeps the multi-brand retail curbs.

nindian-economy-19-5.s: In e-commerce, FDI is permitted under:
nindian-economy-19-5.x: FDI is allowed in the marketplace model but not in the inventory-based model.
n: FDI can be made through equity shares. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FDI can be made through debentures. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FDI can be made through preference shares. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FDI can be made through share warrants. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
The Automatic Route does not require prior government approval. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FDI is permitted under the marketplace model. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FDI is not permitted under the inventory-based model. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FDI can enter through the Automatic Route. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
FDI under the Automatic Route is subject to applicable conditions. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 27-29]
xa: **July 2026**: DPIIT allowed FDI in inventory e-commerce when inventory is used for **exports** of domestically made goods.
**Government Route** needs prior approval via the **FIFP**, integrated with **NSWS** since Aug 2022.
More than **90% of sectors** are on the automatic route.

nc505121e782.s: Which of the following is NOT a sector prohibited for FDI in India?
nc505121e782.x: Railway operations are prohibited except for permitted activities, but railway infrastructure is included among sectors permitting 100% automatic FDI. Lottery business, chit funds and atomic energy are prohibited sectors.
nc505121e782.tq: Separate a prohibited activity from a permitted infrastructure activity.
xs: **Railway infrastructure** is a **100% automatic** sector, not prohibited — option **(4)**.
**Lottery**, **chit funds** and **atomic energy** are prohibited.
xa: ⚠ **Railway operations** (other than permitted activities) are prohibited — not railway infrastructure.
Other prohibited: **gambling and betting (incl. casinos)**, **Nidhi companies**, **trading in TDRs**.
Also prohibited: **real estate business and farmhouses**; **cigars/cigarettes of tobacco**.
Civil aviation **MRO** and **ports** are also **100% automatic**.

n2aabe3ae1fc.s: Foreign Portfolio Investors in India must be registered with:
n2aabe3ae1fc.x: FPIs must register with SEBI and are overseen by SEBI and the RBI.
xa: Law for FPIs: **SEBI (FPI) Regulations 2019**.
FPI opened in India in **1992**.
**DPIIT** is under the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**.

nb54f57f93bc.x: India follows a negative-list approach; FIPB was abolished in June 2017 and DPIIT is the nodal department.
xa: Under the negative list, FDI is up to **100% automatic in most sectors**.
DPIIT issued the **Consolidated FDI Policy 2020**.
Applications now go to **concerned ministries/departments** via the **FIF Portal**.

nc5f232f7083.s: DPIIT, the nodal department for FDI policy and data, is under the Ministry of:
nc5f232f7083.x: DPIIT is under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry; its FIF Portal has been part of the NSWS since August 2022.
xa: DPIIT issued the **Consolidated FDI Policy 2020**.
It replaced the role of the **FIPB** (abolished **June 2017**).
**July 2026**: DPIIT allowed FDI in **inventory e-commerce** for **exports** of domestically made goods.

n6eac3fe240b.s: External Commercial Borrowings are regulated by:
n6eac3fe240b.x: FEMA, 1999 replaced FERA, 1973, and ECBs are regulated by the RBI under FEMA.
xa: FEMA governs **foreign exchange transactions**.
The **10%** FDI/FPI line (**Arvind Mayaram Committee**) operates under FEMA.
Insurance **100%** FDI was enabled by amending the **FEMA (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, 2019**.

ne5fddb90591.s: Which of the following countries is NOT covered by Press Note 3 (April 2020)?
ne5fddb90591.x: Press Note 3 covers land-border countries (China, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan, Afghanistan); Sri Lanka shares no land border.
xa: Amended **March 2026**, effective **1 May 2026**.
Firms with up to **10%** land-border beneficial ownership may use the **automatic route**.
**29 projects worth ₹4,895.65 crore** received by Aug 2026.

n15d20ba35d9.s: Under the March 2026 amendment to Press Note 3, a foreign firm may use the automatic route from 1 May 2026 if its Chinese or Hong Kong beneficial ownership is up to:
n15d20ba35d9.x: Firms with Chinese or Hong Kong beneficial ownership up to 10% may use the automatic route, provided they are not registered in China, Hong Kong or another land-border country.
xa: The amendment was approved by the **Cabinet** in **March 2026**.
**Beneficial owner** is defined as per the **PML Rules, 2005**.
Response: **29 projects worth ₹4,895.65 crore** by **Aug 2026**.

n64c54e5bbbe.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about FDI?
o: Gross FDI consists entirely of fresh capital.
It is associated with stable capital.
It can help finance the current account deficit.
n64c54e5bbbe.x: Gross FDI may include accounting changes and is not entirely fresh capital.
xa: About **$40 bn** of **$560 bn** equity inflows (**2014-15** to **2025-26**) were accounting changes.
FY26: record gross **$94.6 bn** but net only **$7.6 bn**.
FDI is **long-term** with **management control**, unlike "hot money" FPI.

na69cb57fc05.s: India's net FDI in FY 2024-25 was only about:
na69cb57fc05.x: In FY 2024-25 gross FDI was $81 billion but net FDI only $353 million.
xa: Top sources FY 2024-25: **Singapore (30%)**, **Mauritius (17%)**, **US (11%)**.
Services sector was the top recipient.

nb3a7b67bfdd.s: The three leading sources of FDI in India during FY 2024-25, in descending order, were:
o: Singapore, Mauritius and the United States
The United States, Japan and the Netherlands
Singapore, Japan and the United Arab Emirates
nb3a7b67bfdd.x: Singapore contributed 30%, Mauritius 17% and the United States 11% of FDI in FY 2024-25.
nb3a7b67bfdd.tq: Arrange the source countries by their stated shares, not by general economic size.
xs: FY 2024-25 top sources: **Singapore (30%)**, **Mauritius (17%)**, **US (11%)** — option **(1)**.
**Japan**, **Netherlands** and the **UAE** were not in FY 2024-25's top three.
xa: **FY26** (RBI) order: **Singapore, US, Mauritius, Japan, Netherlands**.
⚠ Earlier **FY23**: **Mauritius 26%**, **Singapore 23%**.
**April 2026**: **>75%** of inflows came from **Japan, Singapore, Mauritius**.

ned0f392dfa4.s: Net FDI may remain weak despite high gross inflows mainly because of:
o: Exclusion of services from net FDI
Profit repatriation, outward FDI and PE/VC exits
Exclusion of all foreign equity from net FDI
Deduction of imports from gross FDI
ned0f392dfa4.x: Net FDI is reduced by profit repatriation, outward FDI by Indian firms and PE/VC exits.
xa: **ODI** was **$23.6 bn in FY25** (top: **Singapore**, **US**, **UAE**).
About **$40 bn** of **2014-26** equity "inflows" were **accounting changes**, not fresh capital.
FY26: record gross **$94.6 bn** but net only **$7.6 bn**.
Gross vs net FDI is debated between the **CEA** and critics.

n83aab0e8192.s: India's record gross FDI in FY 2025-26 was:
n83aab0e8192.x: FY 2025-26 saw record gross FDI of $94.6 billion, with net FDI of $7.6 billion.
xa: **$23.6 bn** is **ODI in FY25**; **$9.4 bn** is **Karnataka**'s H1 FY26 FDI.
Net FDI was **negative for five straight months** (**Sep 2025-Jan 2026**) due to repatriation + **ODI**.
**Feb 2026**: net FDI **+$4.6 bn**, first positive after **6 months**.
**April 2026**: gross **$15.3 bn**, net **$6.6 bn** — highest in nearly **5 years**.

n7d24366efd1.s: India's inclusion in the JP Morgan Emerging Market bond index, expected to draw passive bond inflows, carries a target weight of:
n7d24366efd1.x: India entered the JP Morgan EM bond index with a target weight of 10%, which is expected to attract passive bond inflows.
xa: FPI G-sec limits: **6%** Central, **2%** State (General Route).
**VRR** and **FAR** routes steadied debt flows.
Rupee weakness in **May 2026** (past **96/$**) came from FPI **equity** outflows.

nde3dc2c4e20.s: Which of the following correctly gives the order of the top three states by FDI during the first half of FY 2025-26?
nde3dc2c4e20.x: Maharashtra ranked first, Karnataka second and Tamil Nadu third during the first half of FY 2025-26.
nde3dc2c4e20.tq: Arrange the states by rank and avoid confusing current rankings with older percentage data.
xs: **H1 FY26**: **Maharashtra** first, **Karnataka** (**$9.4 bn**) second, **Tamil Nadu** (**$3.6 bn**) third — option **(1)**.
Maharashtra's share fell to **30%** but it stayed on top.
xa: **FY23** (older): **Maharashtra 29%**, **Karnataka 24%**, **Gujarat 17%**, **Delhi 13%**, **Tamil Nadu 5%**.
**IT** FDI doubled to **$9 bn** = **25%** of the total in H1 FY26.
⚠ Mumbai's RBI region received the most cumulative FDI (**Apr 2000-Mar 2015**).

n41b0d4e10a1.s: Google announced a $15 billion, 1 GW AI data centre in Andhra Pradesh at:
n41b0d4e10a1.x: Google's $15 billion AI data centre is in Visakhapatnam; AP's Industrial Development Policy 4.0 targets at least $10 billion FDI.
xa: It is Google's **largest AI hub outside the US**, announced in **Oct 2025**.
The AP State Budget (**2026**) called it "**A.P.'s mother of all deals**".
⚠ **$94.6 bn** is India's FY26 gross FDI and **$23.6 bn** India's FY25 ODI — not AP figures.

nb5a379a3c2f.s: The debate concerning gross and net FDI in India has involved the Chief Economic Adviser and critics primarily because:
o: net FDI excludes all foreign equity inflows
gross FDI may include accounting changes and therefore may not reflect fresh capital fully
manufacturing FDI is always higher than services FDI
gross FDI and net FDI always represent identical flows
nb5a379a3c2f.x: The debate arises because gross FDI can include accounting changes, whereas the amount of fresh capital may be considerably lower, as reflected in the difference between gross and net figures.
nb5a379a3c2f.tq: Apply the gross-versus-net distinction to the stated policy debate.
xs: **Gross FDI** may include **accounting changes**, so it does not fully reflect **fresh capital** — option **(2)**.
About **$40 bn** of **$560 bn** equity inflows (**2014-15** to **2025-26**) were accounting changes, fuelling the **CEA vs critics** debate.
xa: Net FDI also falls due to **profit repatriation**, **ODI** and **PE/VC exits**.
**Manufacturing**'s share of effective inflows fell to **10.6%** (**2026**).
