**Nachiket Mor (2013)** = SFBs and payments banks.
**Bimal Jalan (2019)** = RBI's Economic Capital Framework.

n0a585916ad6.s: The S.H. Khan Working Group of 1998 was concerned with:
o: Determining the contingent risk buffer of the RBI
Restructuring weak public sector banks through seven parameters
Setting up the Banks Board Bureau
Harmonising the roles of banks and Development Finance Institutions
n0a585916ad6.x: The S.H. Khan Working Group examined how the roles of banks and Development Finance Institutions could be harmonised, leading towards universal banking.
n0a585916ad6.tq: Separate the universal-banking recommendation from committee work on weak banks and RBI reserves.
xs: The **S.H. Khan Working Group (1998)** dealt with **harmonising the roles of banks and DFIs** — so option **(4)** is correct.
This led to **universal banking**.
The **contingent risk buffer** is **Bimal Jalan**; **7 parameters** is **M.S. Verma**; **BBB** is **P.J. Nayak**.
xa: **Narasimham-II (1998)** also backed universal banking and merging strong banks and DFIs.
**Rangarajan (2006)** dealt with financial inclusion.

n512ccf55c95.s: The Nachiket Mor Committee was constituted in 2013 and is associated with recommendations concerning:
o: Small finance banks and payments banks
n512ccf55c95.x: The Nachiket Mor Committee, constituted in 2013, examined differentiated banks, including small finance banks and payments banks.
n512ccf55c95.tq: Use the year and distinctive institutional reform as confirmation clues.
xs: The **Nachiket Mor Committee (2013)** led to **small finance banks and payments banks** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Surplus transfer to Govt was the **Bimal Jalan** committee.
xa: It dealt with **differentiated banking / financial inclusion** and universal bank accounts.
It laid the groundwork for **PMJDY**.
⚠ **Rangarajan (2006)** was the earlier financial-inclusion committee.

nbfc2cf71036.s: The Banks Board Bureau was established to perform which of the following functions in relation to public sector banks?
o: Determine the statutory liquidity ratio for all banks
Select chairpersons of public sector banks
Approve the Union Budget on behalf of Parliament
nbfc2cf71036.x: The Banks Board Bureau selects chairpersons of public sector banks. Its creation followed the recommendations of the P.J. Nayak Committee.
nbfc2cf71036.tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish institutional functions.
xs: The **Banks Board Bureau** selects **PSB chairmen/whole-time directors** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It also advises on governance; it does not fix SLR, regulate securities or approve budgets.
xa: BBB came from **2016** after the **P.J. Nayak Committee (2014)**.
Composition: a chairman + **3** ex-officio members + **5** experts.
Replaced in **2022** by the **Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB)**.

n1f4ba30a578.s: The merger of 10 public sector banks into 4 came into effect from:
n1f4ba30a578.x: Ten public sector banks were merged into four with effect from 1 April 2020.
n1f4ba30a578.tq: Anchor the reform to its exact effective date and distinguish it from the 2017 recapitalisation announcement.
xs: The "**ten into four**" merger took effect from **1 April 2020** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1 April 2019** was the **Dena + Vijaya → Bank of Baroda** merger.
xa: 2020 mergers: OBC + United → **PNB**; Syndicate → **Canara**; Andhra + Corporation → **Union Bank**; Allahabad → **Indian Bank**.
It followed the **SBI-associates merger of 2017**.
PSB count fell from **27 (2017) to 12 (2020)**.

nc4c907732a1.s: Which of the following was NOT an expected gain from the consolidation of public sector banks?
o: Creation of lenders capable of competing globally
Economies of scale and lower costs
Permanent elimination of all non-performing assets
Better capital utilisation and risk management
nc4c907732a1.x: The expected gains included scale, lower costs, global-size lenders, better capital use and improved risk management. Permanent elimination of all NPAs was not stated as an expected gain.
nc4c907732a1.tq: Reject the extreme outcome that goes beyond the stated objectives of bank consolidation.
xs: **Permanent elimination of all NPAs** was NOT a stated merger gain — so option **(3)** is correct.
Stated gains: **scale**, **global-size lenders**, **lower costs**, **stronger capital**, **better capital use and risk management**.
xa: The idea of fewer, stronger banks came from **Narasimham-II**.
Mergers bring **integration costs** (criticism).
PSB count fell from **27** to **12**.

nab365168b5f.s: The idea of creating fewer and stronger banks through mergers was associated particularly with:
nab365168b5f.x: Narasimham-II recommended consolidation through mergers of strong banks and the creation of fewer, stronger banking institutions.
nab365168b5f.tq: Distinguish the consolidation agenda of Narasimham-II from the foundational reforms of Narasimham-I.
xs: Fewer, stronger banks through mergers was a **Narasimham-II** idea — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Narasimham-I** focused on prudential norms and SLR/CRR cuts; **Goiporia** = customer service; **Malhotra** = insurance.
xa: Narasimham-II: set up **Dec 1997**, report **April 1998**; **3-tier structure**.
It recommended **CRAR 10%** and **universal banking**.

n09da6ee2199.s: Which of the following is cited as a criticism of public sector bank privatisation by trade unions?
o: It would make recapitalisation unnecessary in every case
It would weaken priority sector lending, rural credit and financial inclusion
It would increase the number of rural branches automatically
It would eliminate all integration costs arising from mergers
n09da6ee2199.x: Trade unions have argued that privatisation could weaken priority sector lending, rural credit and financial inclusion.
n09da6ee2199.tq: Connect the policy proposal with its stated social-sector concern.
xs: Unions argue privatisation would **weaken priority sector lending, rural credit and financial inclusion** — so option **(2)** is correct (**2 Feb 2026**).
The pro-privatisation case is **efficiency and governance**; the counter is the PSB **social mandate**.
xa: **AITUC** called the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act 2025 a "clear call to privatisation".
Budget **2021-22** announced privatisation of **two PSBs and one general insurance company**.
Mergers bring **integration costs** — another criticism.

nindian-economy-66-1.x: Tarapore II (2006) was on fuller capital account convertibility; Tarapore I (1997) on capital account convertibility; Narasimham I and II on the financial system and banking reforms.
n: Tarapore Committee – I focused on Capital Account Convertibility (CAC). [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
Tarapore Committee – II focused on Fuller Capital Account Convertibility (FCAC). [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
Narasimham Committee – I focused on Financial Sector / Banking Reforms. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
Narasimham Committee – II focused on Banking Sector Reforms. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
xa: ⚠ **Narasimham-I** = Committee on the Financial System; **Narasimham-II** = Committee on Banking Sector Reforms.
Narasimham-II was set up in **Dec 1997** and reported in **April 1998**; it proposed a **3-tier structure** and **CRAR 10%**.
**Raghuram Rajan Committee** (**2008**) = Committee on Financial Sector Reforms — "**A Hundred Small Steps**".

nindian-economy-66-5.s: The Tax Reforms Committee of 1991 was headed by:
nindian-economy-66-5.x: Raja Chelliah headed the 1991 Tax Reforms Committee; Kelkar led the 2002 tax task forces and the PPP review.
n: Chelliah Committee focused on Tax Reforms. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
Kelkar Task Force focused on Direct & Indirect Tax Reforms. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
Kelkar Committee focused on the PPP Infrastructure Model. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
Malhotra Committee focused on Insurance Sector Reforms. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
xa: **Malhotra Committee** (**R.N. Malhotra**, **1993**) led to the **IRDA Act 1999**.
**Vijay Kelkar** is associated with **tax reforms** and **PPP reforms**.
**Rangarajan** committees: **1993** = **disinvestment**; **2006** = **financial inclusion**.

nindian-economy-66-8.x: Malhotra covered insurance reform; the Rangarajan committees covered financial inclusion, sugar decontrol and disinvestment.
n: Rangarajan Committee – Financial Inclusion focused on Financial Inclusion. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
Rangarajan Committee – Sugar focused on sugar-sector deregulation. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
Rangarajan Committee – Disinvestment focused on the disinvestment of PSUs. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
Malhotra Committee focused on Insurance Sector Reforms. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
xa: ⚠ Two **Rangarajan** committees: **1993** = disinvestment; **2006** = financial inclusion.
**Malhotra Committee** led to the **IRDA Act 1999**.
**C. Rangarajan** is also linked to **poverty-related** committees.

nindian-economy-66-16.s: The Vaghul Committee was constituted in:
nindian-economy-66-16.x: Vaghul dates from 1987; Narasimham I from 1991, Narasimham II from 1997 and the Raghuram Rajan committee from 2008.
n: Narasimham I was constituted in 1991. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
Narasimham II was constituted in 1997. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
Narasimham II submitted its report in 1998. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
Raghuram Rajan Committee was constituted in 2008. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
xa: **Vaghul Committee** dealt with the **call money market**.
⚠ **Narasimham-I (1991)** = Committee on the Financial System; **Narasimham-II (1998)** = Committee on Banking Sector Reforms.
Rajan's report is titled "**A Hundred Small Steps**" (some notes date it **2009**).

nindian-economy-67-18.s: The Committee on Financial Sector Reforms (2008) was chaired by:
nindian-economy-67-18.x: Raghuram Rajan chaired the 2008 committee; Narasimham chaired the 1991 and 1998 banking reform committees.
n: Rangarajan is associated with Financial inclusion. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
Rangarajan is associated with poverty-related committees. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
Rangarajan is associated with disinvestment-related committees. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
Vijay Kelkar is associated with Tax reforms. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
Vijay Kelkar is associated with PPP reforms. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
M. Narasimham is associated with banking reforms. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
M. Narasimham is associated with financial-sector reforms. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
Raghuram Rajan is associated with the Financial Sector Reforms Committee. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #67 · pp 96-98]
xa: **S.S. Tarapore** → **Capital Account Convertibility** (I) and **Fuller CAC** (II).
**R.N. Malhotra** → **insurance sector reforms**.
**Raja J. Chelliah** → **tax reforms**.

nbba1be5610d.s: In 2004, FDI in private sector banks in India was allowed up to:
nbba1be5610d.x: FDI up to 74% in private banks was permitted in 2004; prudential norms and CRAR came in 1992.
xa: **Interest-rate deregulation** was a key post-1991 reform (APPSC-GS 2023 key).
Private banks **HDFC** and **ICICI** entered by **1995**; the **Banking Ombudsman** came in **1995**.
**FERA** was replaced by **FEMA** in **1999**; insurance opened by the **IRDA Act 1999**.
⚠ **Bank nationalisation (1969/1980)** and the **FRBM Act 2003** are not financial-sector reforms.

nefb68b3b097.s: The Banking Ombudsman was introduced in India in:
nefb68b3b097.x: The Banking Ombudsman came in 1995; SEBI became statutory in 1992.
xa: Market-determined exchange rate: **1993**.
**FERA** replaced by **FEMA** in **1999**; insurance opened by the **IRDA Act 1999**.
⚠ **Bank nationalisation (1969/1980)** and **FRBM Act 2003** do not belong to the 1991 financial-sector reforms.

n195a51967a1.s: Which of the following does NOT belong to the financial-sector reforms initiated after 1991?
n195a51967a1.x: The FRBM Act, 2003 was a fiscal reform, not a financial-sector reform. The other three were components of post-1991 financial-sector reforms.
n195a51967a1.tq: Separate financial-sector reforms from a fiscal-policy measure.
xs: The **FRBM Act, 2003** does NOT belong — it is a **fiscal** reform — so option **(4)** is correct.
**SLR/CRR cuts**, **private bank entry** and **prudential norms** were all core post-1991 financial-sector reforms.
xa: ⚠ **Bank nationalisation (1969/1980)** is also pre-reform and does not belong.
SLR was **38.5%** in **1991-92** before the cuts.
**HDFC** and **ICICI** entered by **1995**; **FDI up to 74%** in private banks (**2004**).

n8db880652c5.s: The Basel Accords are framed by which of the following bodies?
o: International Organization of Securities Commissions under the BIS
Financial Stability Board under the International Monetary Fund
Basel Committee on Banking Supervision under the Bank for International Settlements
International Monetary Fund under the World Bank
n8db880652c5.x: The Basel Accords are formulated by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS), which functions under the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).
n8db880652c5.tq: Identify the correct international body and distinguish it from neighbouring financial institutions.
xs: The Basel Accords are framed by the **Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS)** under the **Bank for International Settlements (BIS)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
They cover **capital risk, market risk and operational risk**.
xa: BIS was set up in **1930**, the world's oldest international financial organisation.
Basel I **1988**, Basel II **2004**, Basel III post-2008 crisis (India from **1 Jan 2013**).
⚠ The **Basel Convention (1989)** is a UNEP treaty on **hazardous wastes**, not banking.

n9346d3c5132.s: Basel I (1988), which focused on credit risk, prescribed minimum capital of what share of risk-weighted assets?
n9346d3c5132.x: Basel I addressed credit risk and set minimum capital at 8 per cent of risk-weighted assets (India prescribed 9 per cent).
xa: Basel I used five risk buckets: **0, 10, 20, 50, 100%**.
India set CRAR at **9%** under Basel I (**1999**).

n1d594d1f81d.s: Which of the following sets correctly represents the three pillars of Basel II?
o: Capital adequacy, monetary stability and deposit insurance
Credit risk, exchange-rate risk and sovereign risk
Liquidity coverage, stable funding and countercyclical lending
Minimum capital requirements, supervisory review and market discipline
n1d594d1f81d.x: Basel II rests on three pillars: minimum capital requirements, supervisory review and market discipline.
n1d594d1f81d.tq: Recall the standard three-part framework and reject terms belonging to Basel III liquidity norms.
xs: Basel II's three pillars: **minimum capital requirements, supervisory review and market discipline** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Liquidity coverage and stable funding (**LCR**, **NSFR**) came with **Basel III**.
xa: Basel II was issued in **2004**.
Basel III pillars (as notes phrase them): **absorb shocks**; improve risk management and governance; improve transparency and disclosure.
The **leverage ratio** came with Basel III, not Basel II.

na46d8031c4c.s: India introduced the Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) in 1992. Under the Basel I framework, India prescribed CRAR at:
na46d8031c4c.x: India introduced CRAR in 1992 and prescribed it at 9 per cent under Basel I, one percentage point above the Basel minimum of 8 per cent.
na46d8031c4c.tq: Separate the Indian norm from the lower international minimum.
xs: India set CRAR at **9 per cent** under Basel I (**1999**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
That is stricter than the BCBS minimum of **8%**.
**10.5%** is the BCBS CRAR + CCB; **6%** is the BCBS Tier 1 minimum.
xa: RBI introduced CRAR in **1992**, following BIS standards.
**Narasimham-II** recommended **CRAR 10%**.

nb1998fe3bcd.s: Which of the following correctly defines Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) or CRAR?
o: Total capital divided by risk-weighted assets
Total deposits divided by total advances
Tier 1 capital divided by total non-risk-weighted exposure
Liquid assets divided by short-term liabilities
nb1998fe3bcd.x: CAR or CRAR is calculated as capital divided by risk-weighted assets. The leverage ratio, in contrast, uses total non-risk-weighted exposure.
nb1998fe3bcd.tq: Distinguish risk-weighted capital adequacy from the non-risk-weighted leverage measure.
xs: **CAR/CRAR = capital / risk-weighted assets** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Tier-1 capital / total **non-risk-weighted** exposure is the **leverage ratio**.
xa: RBI CRAR norm **9%** vs BCBS **8%**.
SCB **CRAR** rose to **17.36%**; **PSB CRAR** to **16.10%**.
**HDFC Bank** CAR **19.6%** vs regulatory norm **11.9%** (19 Jul 2026).

n689e88c28f4.s: Which of the following may be included in a bank's Tier 2 capital?
n689e88c28f4.x: Tier 2 has a mixed equity-debt character and may include subordinated debt; paid-up capital, reserves and undistributed profits are Tier 1 core equity.
xa: **AT-1 bonds** are **perpetual** debt with a call option.
**SBI** raised **₹4,691 crore** in the first Basel III AT-1 bonds of FY27.
RBI Tier 1 norm: **7%**; BCBS **6%**.

nd2c33e6f095.s: In October 2025, the RBI proposed lower risk weights under Basel III for which of the following sectors?
nd2c33e6f095.x: In October 2025, the RBI proposed lower Basel III risk weights for MSMEs and real estate.
nd2c33e6f095.tq: Use the sector-pair association while rejecting plausible but unlisted alternatives.
xs: In **Oct 2025**, RBI proposed (draft) lower **differentiated risk weights** for **MSMEs and real estate** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This would lower minimum capital needs under Basel III.
xa: Risk weights were **raised** on unsecured consumer credit in **Nov 2023** to cool risky lending.
An **ECL** shift may cut Tier-1 ratios by **100-150 bps**.
**LTV caps** limit loans to a share of collateral value (housing, gold).

n65d712c7611.s: In India, the countercyclical capital buffer framework was introduced by the RBI in 2015. Its main trigger is the:
n65d712c7611.x: The RBI introduced the countercyclical capital buffer framework in 2015, with the credit-to-GDP gap as its main trigger.
n65d712c7611.tq: Match the macroeconomic indicator with the regulatory buffer it activates.
xs: The CCyB's main trigger is the **credit-to-GDP gap** — so option **(4)** is correct.
RBI introduced the framework in **2015** but has **not activated** it.
xa: CCyB range: **0-2.5%** of extra capital.
CCB is a separate fixed **2.5%** buffer.
Other macroprudential tools: **LTV caps**, risk weights, liquidity ratios (**LCR**, **NSFR**).

nf2d10dcdcc3.s: The four focus areas of EASE 8.0, also called “EASE ₹ise”, for FY2026 are:
o: Risk and Resilience, Innovation, Socio-economic impact, Excellence
nf2d10dcdcc3.x: EASE 8.0 or EASE ₹ise focuses on Risk and Resilience, Innovation, Socio-economic impact and Excellence.
nf2d10dcdcc3.tq: Match the programme version with its exact four-part theme set.
xs: **EASE 8.0 / "EASE ₹ise"** focuses on **Risk & Resilience, Innovation, Socio-economic impact, Excellence** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The initials spell **R-I-S-E**, matching the name "₹ise".
xa: **EASE 5.0-7.0** = **EASENext**, after **PSB Manthan 2.0** (**Apr 2022**).
EASE was launched in **2017**; PSB Reforms Agenda from **Jan 2018**.

nindian-economy-66-10.x: Vaghul covered the call money market; Goswami industrial sickness, Janakiraman the stock-market scam and Abid Hussain SSI de-reservation.
n: Goswami Committee focused on Industrial Sickness. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
Janakiraman Committee focused on the Stock Market Scam. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
Vaghul Committee focused on the Call Money Market. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
Abid Hussain Committee focused on the de-reservation of small-scale industry items. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 95-96]
xa: **Goiporia Committee** → **customer service** in banks.
**M.S. Verma** (**1999**) → **7 parameters** to identify weak PSBs.
**S.H. Khan Working Group** (**1998**) → harmonising banks and DFIs → **universal banking**.

ndb622c955a2.s: The Economic Capital Framework of the RBI, associated with Bimal Jalan, dealt particularly with:
o: Merging strong banks and closing weak banks
Transfer of reserves and surplus to the Government
ndb622c955a2.x: Bimal Jalan chaired the committee on the RBI’s Economic Capital Framework, including the issue of reserves and surplus transfer to the Government.
ndb622c955a2.tq: Distinguish RBI balance-sheet and surplus issues from banking-structure reforms.
xs: The **Bimal Jalan** Economic Capital Framework dealt with **RBI reserves and surplus transfer to the Government** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Merging strong / closing weak banks = **Narasimham-II**; customer service = **Goiporia**; payments banks = **Nachiket Mor**.
xa: It set a **Contingent Risk Buffer** of **5.5-6.5%**.
Jalan's committee sat **2018-19** (report **2019**).

n7b42ac9a376.s: Which of the following correctly presents the RBI norms for CET1, Tier 1 capital and total CRAR?
n7b42ac9a376.x: The RBI norms listed are CET1 5.5 per cent, Tier 1 capital 7 per cent and total CRAR 9 per cent.
n7b42ac9a376.tq: Read the three-column ratio comparison without substituting the BCBS minimums.
xs: RBI norms: **CET1 5.5%**, **Tier 1 7%**, **total CRAR 9%** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (4) gives the **BCBS** minimums (4.5%, 6%, 8%); options (1) and (2) mix the two sets.
xa: RBI CRAR + CCB: **11.5%** vs BCBS **10.5%**.
CCB is **2.5%** under both.
RBI's **9%** is stricter than BCBS's **8%**.

n0870d67c5c0.s: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) was established in which year?
n0870d67c5c0.x: The BIS was established in 1930 and is described as the world's oldest international financial organisation.
n0870d67c5c0.tq: Use the year-based elimination method with closely spaced numerical options.
xs: The **BIS** was established in **1930** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is the **world's oldest international financial organisation**.
xa: The **BCBS** under the BIS frames the **Basel Accords**.
Basel I (**1988**) covered credit risk only, with a minimum of **8%** of risk-weighted assets.
Basel II (**2004**) rests on three pillars.

n28e75d6727a.s: India began implementing Basel III norms from:
n28e75d6727a.x: India applied Basel III from 1 January 2013; Basel III was the response to the 2007-09 global financial crisis.
xa: Basel III features: **CET1**, capital buffers, **leverage ratio**, **LCR**, **NSFR**, counterparty credit risk.
RBI leverage ratio: **4%** for D-SIBs, **3.5%** for others (BCBS **3%**).

n5ba8e45455e.s: The BCBS minimum for the Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio is:
n5ba8e45455e.x: The BCBS minimums are CET1 4.5%, Tier 1 6%, capital conservation buffer 2.5% and countercyclical buffer 0–2.5%.
xa: RBI norms are stricter: **CET1 5.5%**, **Tier 1 7%**, CRAR **9%**.
⚠ Notes listing "Tier I 4.5%" confuse it with the BCBS **CET1** floor.

n42745014d94.s: The countercyclical capital buffer, introduced in India in 2015 but not yet activated, allows extra capital during credit booms in the range of:
n42745014d94.x: The CCyB ranges from 0 to 2.5 per cent during credit booms; India has had the framework since 2015 but has not activated it.
xa: Its main trigger is the **credit-to-GDP gap**.
RBI kept the CCyB inactive in **May 2026**.
CCB is a fixed **2.5%**; ⚠ do not mix CCB with CCyB.

n71310ae3151.s: The Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) under Basel III requires enough high-quality liquid assets to survive a stress period of:
n71310ae3151.x: LCR covers a 30-day stress; the NSFR concerns stable funding over a one-year horizon.
xa: **LCR** and **NSFR** must each be at least **100%**.
Leverage ratio norm: **4%** for **D-SIBs**, **3.5%** for others (BCBS **3%**); it came with **Basel III**, not Basel II.
**Level 1 HQLA** = cash, G-secs, central-bank reserves; **Level 2** = highly rated corporate bonds.
**CCyB** (**0-2.5%**) checks excess credit growth; trigger = **credit-to-GDP gap**.

n249fa9e4fd2.s: The Basel Convention, administered by UNEP, deals with:
n249fa9e4fd2.x: The Basel Convention concerns hazardous wastes; the Basel Accords (BCBS/BIS) concern bank capital, liquidity and risk.
xa: The Basel Convention was adopted in **1989** and came into force in **1992**.
BIS was set up in **1930**, the world's oldest international financial organisation.
Basel I **1988**, Basel II **2004**, Basel III in India from **1 Jan 2013**.

ne9444f5029b.s: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) is a wholly owned subsidiary of:
ne9444f5029b.x: DICGC is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India.
xa: Set up in **1978** by merging the **Deposit Insurance Corporation (1962)** and the **Credit Guarantee Corporation**.
Cover: **₹5 lakh per depositor per bank**.
The premium is **paid by banks**, not depositors.

nindian-economy-30-7.s: In which year were five associate banks and Bharatiya Mahila Bank merged into SBI?
nindian-economy-30-7.x: The SBI merger took place in 2017; New Bank of India joined PNB in 1993 and ten PSBs were merged into four in 2020.
n: New Bank of India merged into Punjab National Bank in 1993. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
Five SBI associate banks merged into the State Bank of India in 2017. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
Bharatiya Mahila Bank merged into the State Bank of India in 2017. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
Ten Public Sector Banks merged into four anchor banks in 2020. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
The Central Government approved a Strategic Disinvestment and Modernisation Policy framework in 2021 and later. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
The 8 princely state-associated banks later became known as SBI Associate Banks. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
The merger of New Bank of India into Punjab National Bank was the first major PSB merger. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
The 1993 merger reduced the number of nationalised banks from 20 to 19. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
SBBJ merged into the State Bank of India in 2017. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
SBH merged into the State Bank of India in 2017. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
SBM merged into the State Bank of India in 2017. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
SBP merged into the State Bank of India in 2017. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
SBT merged into the State Bank of India in 2017. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
The mega PSB consolidation took effect on April 1, 2020. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
The policy framework provides for the potential privatisation of selected public sector lenders. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
The policy framework provides for the potential stake reduction of selected public sector lenders. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
The policy framework retains a minimum government presence in strategic sectors. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
The policy framework prioritises digital banking units. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
The policy framework prioritises PSB governance reforms. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
xa: **Dena Bank + Vijaya Bank** → **Bank of Baroda** on **April 1, 2019**.
The five SBI associates: **SBBJ, SBH, SBM, SBP, SBT**.
PSB count fell from **27 (2017) to 12 (2020)**.

nindian-economy-30-15.s: New Bank of India merged into which bank because of financial distress?
nindian-economy-30-15.x: The loss-making New Bank of India merged into Punjab National Bank in 1993, the first merger of two nationalised banks.
n: New Bank of India merged into Punjab National Bank because of financial distress. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
xs: **New Bank of India** merged into **Punjab National Bank** — option **(1)**.
It happened in **1993** because of **financial distress** — the **first major PSB merger**.
It **reduced nationalised banks** from **20 to 19**.
xa: New Bank of India was one of the **six banks** nationalised in **1980**.
**Bank of Baroda** took in **Dena Bank** and **Vijaya Bank** in **2019**.
**Union Bank of India** absorbed **Andhra Bank** and **Corporation Bank** in **2020**.

nindian-economy-30-18.s: Following the 2020 Mega PSB Consolidation, the number of Public Sector Banks in India was reduced to:
nindian-economy-30-18.x: The 2020 mergers cut the number of public sector banks to 12, from 27 in 2017.
n: The 2020 PSB consolidation reduced the number of Public Sector Banks in India to 12. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
xs: The **2020 mega PSB consolidation** reduced the number of PSBs to **12** — option **(2)**.
**Ten PSBs** merged into **four anchor banks** from **April 1, 2020**.
PSB count fell from **27 (2017) to 12 (2020)**.
xa: The **2017** merger of **SBI associates** and **Bharatiya Mahila Bank** came first.
**Dena** and **Vijaya** joined **Bank of Baroda** on **April 1, 2019**.
**Narasimham-II** idea: fewer, stronger banks.

nindian-economy-30-20.s: The merger of Dena Bank and Vijaya Bank into Bank of Baroda took effect on:
nindian-economy-30-20.x: The Bank of Baroda merger took effect on 1 April 2019; the 2020 mergers took effect on 1 April 2020 and the SBI merger on 1 April 2017.
n: The Bank of Baroda consolidation took effect on April 1, 2019. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
xa: The **SBI associates** merger took effect on **1 Apr 2017**.
**1993:** **New Bank of India** → **PNB**, the first major PSB merger.
Vijaya Bank was among the **six banks** nationalised in **1980**.

nindian-economy-30-17.s: Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank were merged into:
nindian-economy-30-17.x: Andhra and Corporation Banks went into Union Bank; Syndicate into Canara, Allahabad into Indian Bank, and OBC and United Bank into PNB.
n: Allahabad Bank merged into Indian Bank in 2020. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #30 · pp 44-46]
xa: These took effect on **1 Apr 2020** and cut PSBs to **12**.
**Andhra Bank** (**Machilipatnam**, **1923**, **Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya**) merged into **Union Bank** (APPSC GS 2025 PYQ).
Expected gains: **scale**, lower costs, stronger capital — a **Narasimham-II** idea.

n6221c95ee47.s: How many parameters were used for identifying weak banks by the M.S. Verma Committee?
n6221c95ee47.x: The M.S. Verma Committee identified weak banks using seven parameters.
n6221c95ee47.tq: Recall the exact count attached to a committee’s diagnostic framework.
xs: The **M.S. Verma Committee (1999)** used **7 parameters** to identify weak banks — so option **(2)** is correct.
It dealt with **Restructuring Weak PSBs**.
xa: **P.J. Nayak (2014)** studied governance of PSB boards → **Banks Board Bureau**.
**Narasimham-II** wanted weak/unviable banks closed.
⚠ Do not confuse with **Indradhanush's 7-point plan (A-G)** of **2015**.

n7185a00f270.s: For the purpose of the LCR, highly rated corporate bonds are classified as:
n7185a00f270.x: Cash, government securities and central-bank reserves are Level 1 HQLA; highly rated corporate bonds are Level 2.
xa: **LCR** = stock of **HQLA** to survive a **30-day** stress; minimum **100%**.
**NSFR** = stable funding over a **1-year** horizon.
RBI deferred revised LCR norms to **31 Mar 2026**.

ncebe44cc479.s: The public sector bank recapitalisation package announced in October 2017 was worth:
ncebe44cc479.x: The October 2017 package was ₹2.11 lakh crore, of which ₹1.35 lakh crore came through recapitalisation bonds.
xa: About **₹58,000 crore** was to be raised by banks.
The bonds pushed up **central debt**.
**4R strategy**: Recognition, Resolution, Recapitalisation, Reforms.

nba4b39bb038.s: Indradhanush, introduced in August 2015, was primarily associated with which of the following reforms?
o: A seven-point plan for capitalisation and governance reform of public sector banks
A fiscal-deficit reduction programme for the Union Government
A scheme for consolidation of Regional Rural Banks
A framework for regulating private insurance companies
nba4b39bb038.x: Indradhanush was a seven-point plan introduced in August 2015 for capital infusion and governance reform in public sector banks.
nba4b39bb038.tq: Identify the programme by its distinctive reform objective and date.
xs: **Indradhanush (Aug 2015)** was a **seven-point plan for capitalisation and governance reform of PSBs** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is a PSB scheme, not a fiscal, RRB or insurance framework.
xa: **7-point plan (A-G)**: Appointments, **Banks Board Bureau**, Capitalisation, De-stressing, Empowerment, Framework of accountability, Governance.
It provided **₹70,000 crore** of budget capital over **4 years**.
The **BBB** began in **2016** as an Indradhanush idea.

n0f0129d981c.s: How do recapitalisation bonds support public sector banks without requiring an equivalent immediate cash outgo from the Union budget?
o: The Government transfers its tax receipts directly to bank depositors
The Government writes off all outstanding bank loans through monetary creation
Banks issue equity directly to the Reserve Bank of India without Government involvement
The Government issues bonds to banks and invests the proceeds back into them as equity
n0f0129d981c.x: Under the mechanism, the Government issues bonds to public sector banks and puts the money back into them as equity; therefore, no equivalent fresh cash leaves the budget immediately.
n0f0129d981c.tq: Trace the transaction sequence rather than judging the policy only by its name.
xs: The **Government issues bonds to banks and invests the proceeds back into them as equity** — so option **(4)** is correct.
So **no fresh cash leaves the budget** immediately, though it **pushes up central debt**.
xa: The **Oct 2017** package: **₹2.11 lakh crore**, with **₹1.35 lakh crore** via recap bonds.
**4R strategy**: Recognition, Resolution, Recapitalisation, Reforms.
Banks now also raise capital via **AT-1** and **Tier 2** bonds (e.g. **Canara Bank** up to **₹4,500 crore** AT-1).

n1ba7a1e3fb8.s: The '4R' strategy adopted for cleaning up public sector banks stands for:
n1ba7a1e3fb8.x: The 4R strategy is Recognition (of NPAs), Resolution, Recapitalisation and Reforms. The other options swap in terms such as Recovery, Restructuring, Regulation, Refinance and Reorganisation, which are not part of the official 4Rs.
xs: The **4R strategy** = **Recognition, Resolution, Recapitalisation, Reforms** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Recovery, Restructuring, Regulation, Refinance and Reorganisation are not among the 4Rs.
xa: Consolidation + recapitalisation + 4Rs lifted SCB **CRAR to 17.36%** and **PSB CRAR to 16.10%**.
SCB credit grew from **₹67 lakh crore (Mar 2015)** to **₹181 lakh crore (Mar 2025)**.
GNPA fell to a multi-decadal low.

n76720fbbe83.s: The P.J. Nayak Committee proposed creating a ____ to hold the Government's stake in public sector banks.
n76720fbbe83.x: The committee proposed a Bank Investment Company, cutting the Government's stake below 50% and professional PSB boards.
xa: The **P.J. Nayak Committee (2014, RBI)** found weak PSB board governance.
It led to the **Banks Board Bureau (2016)**.
Some notes misprint the name as "J. Nayak".

n57ad0df7c4f.s: The Banks Board Bureau was established in 2016 as an idea associated with which initiative?
n57ad0df7c4f.x: The Banks Board Bureau originated from the Indradhanush initiative and began functioning in 2016.
n57ad0df7c4f.tq: Link the institutional reform body with the programme from which it emerged.
xs: The BBB (**2016**) was an **Indradhanush** idea — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Banks Board Bureau** is item "B" of Indradhanush's **7-point plan (A-G)**.
xa: It followed the **P.J. Nayak Committee (2014)**.
It selects **PSB chairmen/whole-time directors**.
Replaced in **2022** by the **FSIB**.

n0a5957a283e.s: In 2022, the Banks Board Bureau was replaced by the:
n0a5957a283e.x: The Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB) replaced the Banks Board Bureau in 2022.
n0a5957a283e.tq: Use the successor institution to resolve a governance-body question.
xs: In **2022**, the BBB was replaced by the **Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB)** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Like the BBB, it selects **PSB chairmen/whole-time directors**.
xa: The BBB started in **2016** (an **Indradhanush** idea).
BBB had a chairman + **3** ex-officio members + **5** experts.
The **P.J. Nayak Committee** proposed a **Bank Investment Company** — ⚠ not the same as option (3).

n6305c1b5c55.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about EASE (Enhanced Access and Service Excellence)?
o: It was conceptualised in 2015 and launched in 2017
It is governed by a board of heads of premier financial institutions
It became the PSB Reforms Agenda from January 2018
PSBs report quarterly against its benchmarks, overseen by IBA's EASE Steering Committee
n6305c1b5c55.x: EASE is run by the Indian Banks' Association's EASE Steering Committee, not a board of heads of premier financial institutions.
xa: **EASE 5.0-7.0** = **EASENext**, after **PSB Manthan 2.0** (**Apr 2022**).
The **EASE Index** ranks mid-size and large PSBs every quarter.

n97cae7d4b6c.s: Which of the following deposits IS covered by DICGC deposit insurance?
o: Deposits in Indian branches of foreign banks
n97cae7d4b6c.x: DICGC covers all commercial banks including foreign bank branches in India; inter-bank, NBFC and government deposits are excluded.
xa: **RRBs** and **co-operative banks** are also covered.
Cover: **₹5 lakh per depositor per bank**.
Premium is paid by banks.

n85ad825e629.s: The Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 raised the 'substantial interest' threshold from ₹5 lakh to:
n85ad825e629.x: The threshold rose from ₹5 lakh to ₹2 crore; the Act also raised co-operative bank directors' tenure from 8 to 10 years.
xa: The Act came into force on **1 Aug 2025** with **19 amendments**.
**AITUC** called it a "clear call to privatisation" (**2 Feb 2026**).

n3f88d61f836.s: Under UDAY (November 2015), States took over what share of DISCOM debt?
n3f88d61f836.x: UDAY shifted 75% of DISCOM debt to the States; RDSS came later, in 2021.
xa: **Indradhanush** for PSBs was also launched in **2015** (Aug).
⚠ UDAY = DISCOM debt takeover; RDSS = results-linked funding and smart meters.

nbcb64541bef.s: The Union Budget 2026–27 announced the restructuring of which institutions?
nbcb64541bef.x: Budget 2026–27 announced restructuring of PFC and REC, along with a High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat.
xa: The CCyB framework (**0-2.5%**) has existed since **2015**; trigger = **credit-to-GDP gap**.
RBI's **Oct 2025** draft proposed lower risk weights for MSMEs and real estate.
An **ECL** shift may cut Tier-1 ratios by **100-150 bps**.

ne2c29415a19.s: Viability Plan 2.0 tracks Regional Rural Banks on how many parameters, such as CRAR, CD ratio and NPAs?
ne2c29415a19.x: Viability Plan 2.0 tracks RRBs on 30 parameters including CRAR, credit-deposit ratio and NPAs.
xa: **4 pillars**: operational excellence, asset quality, profitability, growth.
**15 RRBs** amalgamated, effective **1 May 2025**.

ncd9845bef2c.s: After the 2020–21 consolidation, the number of Regional Rural Banks came down to:
ncd9845bef2c.x: There were originally 196 RRBs; the 2020–21 consolidation brought the number down to 43.
xa: **15 RRBs** were amalgamated, effective **1 May 2025**.
The Centre keeps its **50%** share.
**Viability Plan 2.0** tracks all **28** RRBs on **30 parameters**.

n569d333ba78.s: The DICGC deposit insurance limit was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh in the Budget for:
n569d333ba78.x: The deposit insurance limit was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh in the 2020–21 Budget, following the PMC Bank crisis.
n569d333ba78.tq: Connect the revised figure with the budget year in which it was introduced.
xs: The limit rose from **₹1 lakh** to **₹5 lakh** in the **2020-21 Budget** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It followed the **PMC Bank** crisis.
xa: DICGC is a wholly owned **RBI subsidiary**, set up in **1978**.
Cover is **per depositor per bank**.
⚠ NBFC deposits are **not** DICGC-insured.

n5f0f1ce947e.s: With regard to DICGC insurance, who bears the premium burden?
o: The insured bank, and not the depositor
RBI and the depositor in equal shares
n5f0f1ce947e.x: Banks pay the DICGC insurance premium; the depositor does not pay it.
n5f0f1ce947e.tq: Identify the party responsible for payment rather than the beneficiary of insurance.
xs: The DICGC premium is **paid by the insured bank, not the depositor** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Neither the Govt nor the depositor pays it; the bank bears the cost of the insurance.
xa: DICGC: wholly owned **RBI subsidiary**, set up **1978**.
Cover: **₹5 lakh** per depositor per bank (from **₹1 lakh**, in the **2020-21 Budget**).
Excluded: government, inter-bank and **NBFC** deposits.

nc134761bb82.s: LIC acquired a majority stake in IDBI Bank in 2019. What was the consequence of this transaction for the regulatory classification of IDBI Bank?
o: It was reclassified by RBI as a private sector lender
It was classified as a foreign bank subsidiary
It was converted into a cooperative bank
It was classified by RBI as a regional rural bank
nc134761bb82.x: Following LIC’s acquisition of a majority stake in 2019, RBI reclassified IDBI Bank as a private sector lender.
nc134761bb82.tq: Link the transaction to its direct regulatory consequence.
xs: After **LIC** bought a majority stake in **2019**, RBI **reclassified IDBI Bank as a private lender** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was not made a foreign subsidiary, co-operative bank or RRB.
xa: Govt + LIC are selling a combined **60.72%** strategic stake.
Budget **2021-22** announced privatisation of **two PSBs and one general insurance company**.
Minority stake sales were weighed in **UCO**, **BoM**, **Central Bank**, **Punjab & Sind** and **IOB**.

na405f10472d.s: The Union Budget 2021–22 announced the privatisation of:
o: Three public sector banks and one general insurance company
Two private banks and one public sector insurer
One public sector bank and two life insurance companies
Two public sector banks and one general insurance company
na405f10472d.x: The Budget 2021–22 announced the privatisation of two public sector banks and one general insurance company.
na405f10472d.tq: Keep the numerical composition of the privatisation announcement intact.
xs: Budget **2021-22** announced privatisation of **two PSBs and one general insurance company** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The other options change the number or type of entities named in the Budget.
xa: The debate: **efficiency and governance** vs **social mandate** (rural branches, priority lending).
**IDBI Bank** was reclassified as a private lender after **LIC** bought a majority stake (**2019**).
Govt + LIC are selling a combined **60.72%** IDBI stake.

n78afd5c161c.s: In the debate over privatising public sector banks, the main argument for public ownership is that it supports:
o: Social mandates such as rural branches and priority lending
n78afd5c161c.x: The debate weighs possible efficiency and governance gains from privatisation against the social mandate of PSBs, including rural branches and priority lending.
xa: Unions say privatisation would weaken **PSL**, rural credit and inclusion (**2 Feb 2026**).
Budget **2021-22**: privatise **two PSBs** and **one general insurer**.
**DICGC** cover is unrelated to privatisation.

nef64e8cee27.x: Goiporia covered customer service in banks; Malhotra insurance, Rangarajan financial inclusion and P.J. Nayak bank-board governance.
xa: ⚠ Two **Rangarajan** committees: **1993** = disinvestment, **2006** = financial inclusion.
Nayak led to the **Banks Board Bureau** (**2016**), replaced by **FSIB** in **2022**.

n344543996e9.s: A Special Mention Account classified as SMA-1 has overdue payments of:
n344543996e9.x: SMA-0, SMA-1 and SMA-2 cover 1–30, 31–60 and 61–90 overdue days; SMAs are early-warning accounts, not yet NPAs.
xa: Beyond **90 days** overdue the account becomes an NPA.
Sequence: Standard → SMA-0/1/2 → sub-standard → doubtful → loss.

nb7b6d7bce8a.s: A loan or advance is generally classified as a Non-Performing Asset when the interest or principal instalment remains overdue for more than:
nb7b6d7bce8a.x: An asset becomes an NPA when interest or principal remains overdue for more than 90 days.
nb7b6d7bce8a.tq: Use the precise numerical threshold rather than a nearby overdue period.
xs: A loan becomes an **NPA** when interest or principal is overdue for **more than 90 days** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-G1 2022 key).
**30** and **60** days fall within the **SMA** bands (still standard assets).
xa: Farm loans: **2 crop seasons** (short-duration crops), **1 crop season** (long-duration crops).
The **90-day** test stays under the new Master Directions (from **1 April 2027**).

n053d18a30a0.s: A loan for a short-duration crop becomes an NPA when it remains overdue for:
n053d18a30a0.x: Agricultural loans become NPAs after two crop seasons for short-duration crops and one crop season for long-duration crops.
xa: Non-farm loans become NPAs when overdue **more than 90 days**.
Agriculture GNPA is still high at **6.0%** (some notes **5.7%**).

n0806f07e243.s: Under income-recognition norms, interest on an NPA is booked as income:
o: Only when it is actually received
After the asset is written off
When it is accrued, whether or not received
n0806f07e243.x: Interest on an NPA is not recognised as income until it is actually received. This forms part of the IRACP framework.
n0806f07e243.tq: Apply the recognition rule to distinguish accrual from actual receipt.
xs: Under **income recognition**, interest on an NPA is booked **only when actually received** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Booking on accrual regardless of receipt is what the rule prevents.
xa: It is part of **IRACP**: Income Recognition, Asset Classification, Provisioning.
An asset is an NPA when overdue **more than 90 days**.

na640b7107ca.s: The Provision Coverage Ratio (PCR) of a bank is:
na640b7107ca.x: PCR is provisions held divided by gross NPAs; Gross NPA minus provisions gives Net NPA.
xa: An **NPA** is a loan whose interest or principal is **overdue for more than 90 days**.
**SMA-0/1/2** = overdue **0-30 / 31-60 / 61-90** days — still standard.
**Evergreening** hides defaults by fresh loans; the **AQR** (**2015**) ended it.

n0bebec0de13.s: The Interest Coverage Ratio (ICR) of a borrower is calculated as:
n0bebec0de13.x: ICR = operating earnings (EBIT) divided by interest due; it indicates a borrower's present and emerging risk.
xa: **PCR** = provisions held / gross NPAs.
**IRACP** = Income Recognition, Asset Classification, Provisioning.

o: Writing off all old loans immediately
Converting all NPAs into equity automatically
Giving fresh loans to repay old loans and conceal default
nc736c58c516.x: Evergreening involves extending fresh loans to repay old loans, thereby keeping the underlying default hidden.
nc736c58c516.tq: Recognise the concealment mechanism rather than confuse it with write-off or restructuring.
xs: **Evergreening** = **fresh loans to repay old ones**, so default stays hidden — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **AQR** (RBI, **2015**) ended it.
xa: After the AQR, disclosed NPAs jumped, peaking in **2018**.
**Stressed assets** = NPAs + restructured loans + written-off assets.
**Wilful defaulter**: can pay but does not, or diverts funds.

n7108f25c660.s: The twin balance sheet problem refers to the simultaneous existence of:
o: High exports and low public debt
Fiscal surplus and excess bank liquidity
High household savings and low inflation
Over-leveraged corporates and capital-starved, NPA-laden banks
n7108f25c660.x: The twin balance sheet problem describes over-leveraged firms alongside capital-starved banks burdened with NPAs.
n7108f25c660.tq: Identify the two linked balance-sheet weaknesses rather than one symptom alone.
xs: The **twin balance sheet problem** = **over-leveraged corporates** plus **capital-starved, NPA-laden banks** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Firms cannot invest → banks cannot lend → private capex stalls.
xa: Framed in the **Economic Survey 2016-17** (CEA **Arvind Subramanian**).
The chapter called it the **"festering"** twin balance sheet problem.
The **AQR (2015)** exposed it.

nd70a2c9f5c3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the twin balance sheet problem?
o: Private investment can decline as a result
Banks may freeze new lending rather than recall old loans
Over-leveraged firms can undertake fresh investment without difficulty
nd70a2c9f5c3.x: Over-leveraged firms find it hard to invest, which is why private investment falls.
xa: Framed in the **Economic Survey 2016-17**.
Government response: **4R strategy** with **IBC**, recapitalisation and **NARCL**.

n32d57662c6e.s: Aggressive bank lending during 2010-15 that later turned into NPAs went largely to:
n32d57662c6e.x: Lending in 2010-15 went largely to infrastructure, steel and power without strict appraisal, leading to stalled projects.
xa: **Wilful defaults and fraud**: promoters diverted funds to shell companies.
**Evergreening** kept defaults hidden.
Vicious cycle: lending + shocks → NPAs → provisioning → capital erosion → weak credit.

n08a3a3fc6c5.s: In the NPA vicious cycle, the accumulation of NPAs leads directly to:
n08a3a3fc6c5.x: Aggressive lending and shocks create NPAs, which require provisioning and erode capital, resulting in weak credit growth.
xa: Aggressive lending in **2010-15** went to infrastructure, steel and power.
The **2008** crisis and weak exports hurt borrowers' cash flows.
This cycle fed the **twin balance sheet problem**.

ndc0bb497995.s: The twin balance sheet problem was prominently framed in the Economic Survey:
ndc0bb497995.x: The Economic Survey 2016–17, under Chief Economic Adviser Arvind Subramanian, discussed the festering twin balance sheet problem.
ndc0bb497995.tq: Use the year and institutional context together to avoid nearby Economic Survey years.
xs: The twin balance sheet problem was framed in the **Economic Survey 2016-17** — so option **(1)** is correct.
CEA **Arvind Subramanian** called it the **"festering"** twin balance sheet problem.
xa: It means **over-leveraged corporates** + **NPA-laden banks** at the same time.
The **AQR (2015)** had exposed the problem; NPAs peaked in **2018**.

n7c9dac1266b.s: Following the RBI's Asset Quality Review, NPA levels of banks peaked in:
n7c9dac1266b.x: The AQR sharply raised disclosed NPAs, which peaked in 2018, and exposed the twin balance sheet problem.
xa: It led on to the **IBC** and recapitalisation.

n1023bfb5493.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the new borrower-level NPA tagging system?
o: Banks must identify NPAs through automated systems
It is to be effective from 1 April 2027
If one loan of a borrower becomes an NPA, all its loans at that bank become NPAs
An account can be upgraded even if arrears on one facility remain unpaid
n1023bfb5493.x: An account is upgraded only after all arrears on every facility are paid.
xa: The **90-day** overdue test stays.
RBI is moving to a 3-stage **ECL** model.

nf0b5229db8c.s: Under its new provisioning framework, the RBI is moving from which approach to which approach?
o: From a 3-stage ECL model to a 2-stage incurred-loss model
From incurred-loss model to a 3-stage Expected Credit Loss model
From a 90-day overdue test to a 180-day overdue test
nf0b5229db8c.x: The RBI is shifting from the incurred-loss model to a forward-looking 3-stage Expected Credit Loss (ECL) model; the 90-day overdue test stays.
nf0b5229db8c.tq: Provide before the loss happens: incurred → expected.
xs: RBI is moving **from the incurred-loss model to a 3-stage ECL model** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses it; the **90-day** test is unchanged.
xa: Stage 1 = **12-month** loss; Stage 2 = lifetime; Stage 3 = full lifetime provision.
Loss allowances use the **effective interest rate (EIR)** method.
ECL may cut Tier-1 ratios — a capital concern.

nc72f7946216.s: The GNPA ratio of Scheduled Commercial Banks reached an approximate peak of 11.2 per cent in:
nc72f7946216.x: SCB GNPA peaked at approximately 11.2 per cent in March 2018, after the Asset Quality Review.
nc72f7946216.tq: Use the peak-year clue to distinguish pre-AQR, post-AQR and recovery-period figures.
xs: SCB GNPA peaked at **~11.2%** in **March 2018** — so option **(1)** is correct.
That peak came after the **AQR (2015)** forced recognition.
xa: **Sep 2025**: **2.15%**, a historic low below the 2010-11 level.
GNPA has fallen for **eight straight years**.

n5c556b0b813.s: The GNPA of Scheduled Commercial Banks in March 2026, together with the corresponding NNPA, was:
n5c556b0b813.x: In March 2026, GNPA was 1.93 per cent and NNPA was 0.39 per cent, described as a decadal low.
n5c556b0b813.tq: Pair the two related ratios with the same reporting date.
xs: In **March 2026**, SCB GNPA was **1.93 per cent** and NNPA **0.39 per cent** — so option **(3)** is correct (a decadal low).
xa: March 2025 GNPA: **2.2-2.3%**, lowest since 2011-12.
Large private banks (June 2026): HDFC **1.17%**, ICICI **1.38%**, Axis **1.28%**.

n94b62429187.s: Credit of Scheduled Commercial Banks rose from about ₹67 lakh crore in 2015 to about ____ in 2025.
n94b62429187.x: SCB credit nearly tripled from about ₹67 lakh crore (2015) to about ₹181 lakh crore (2025), with CRAR at about 17.3%.
xa: GNPA fell to **1.93%** (March 2026).
GNPA has fallen for **eight straight years**.

nf2587a1ac7c.s: Debt Recovery Tribunals were set up under:
o: Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993
nf2587a1ac7c.x: DRTs were established under the Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993; they are also used under SARFAESI.
xa: **39 DRTs** and **5 DRATs**; debts **above ₹20 lakh**.
**e-DRT** launched **1 Oct 2018**; e-filing mandatory from **1 Feb 2023**.
⚠ **1987** = Lok Adalats; **1993** = DRTs; **2002** = SARFAESI.

n31a4eef9262.s: Debt Recovery Tribunals deal with debts due to banks and financial institutions above:
n31a4eef9262.x: The DRTs and DRATs handle debts above ₹20 lakh under the stated framework.
n31a4eef9262.tq: Use ascending monetary thresholds to distinguish DRT jurisdiction from the CIRP default threshold.
xs: DRTs handle debts **above ₹20 lakh** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**₹1 crore** is the minimum default for triggering **CIRP** under the IBC.
xa: DRTs were set up under the **RDDBFI Act, 1993**.
**Lok Adalats** handle **small NPAs** only.
**e-DRT**: launched **1 Oct 2018**.

nfc10f329f2b.s: Which mechanism accounted for the largest share of bank recoveries in FY 2024?
nfc10f329f2b.x: In FY 2024, IBC accounted for 48% of recoveries, SARFAESI 32%, DRTs 17% and Lok Adalats 3%.
xa: **Lok Adalats** handle small NPAs only.
Comparison: **SARFAESI** (secured lenders, no court) vs **IBC** (collective, NCLT-led) vs **DRT** (tribunal recovery).
FM: IBC realises **94.95%** of fair value.

n577c48ff42f.s: The Lok Adalats that facilitate settlement of small non-performing assets derive their statutory status from which enactment?
o: The Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993
n577c48ff42f.x: Lok Adalats are statutory forums under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
n577c48ff42f.tq: Identify the statute specifically associated with the forum.
xs: Lok Adalats are statutory forums under the **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**1993** is the **RDDBFI Act** (DRTs); **2002** is **SARFAESI**; **2016** is the **IBC**.
xa: They offer **quick, fee-free settlement** of small loans by compromise.
**National Lok Adalat (13 Sep 2026)**: **DRT Visakhapatnam bench** settled **13** cases worth **₹46.11 crore**.
Lok Adalats delivered **3%** of FY24 bank recoveries.

n4c246d40b93.s: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) replaced the Company Law Board, the BIFR and the:
n4c246d40b93.x: NCLT replaced the Company Law Board, BIFR and AAIFR; it did not replace the Securities Appellate Tribunal.
xa: **BIFR** was dissolved on **1 Dec 2016**; cases went to NCLT/NCLAT.
The IBC replaced **SICA 1985/BIFR** and scattered Companies Act provisions.
NCLT/NCLAT constituted **1 June 2016**.

n0ad36fe229c.s: Which authority is the adjudicating authority for corporate insolvency under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016?
n0ad36fe229c.x: The NCLT is the adjudicating authority for corporate insolvency under the IBC, 2016. The DRT is the authority for individuals and partnership firms.
n0ad36fe229c.tq: Ask which body would handle the dispute by distinguishing corporate from individual insolvency.
xs: The **National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)** is the adjudicating authority for corporate insolvency (**companies and LLPs**) — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC GS 2019 key).
The **DRT** handles **individuals and partnership firms**; the **NCLAT** hears appeals.
xa: NCLT also handles **personal guarantors of corporate debtors**.
CIRP is triggered by a default of at least **₹1 crore**.
⚠ NCLT = **companies and LLPs**; DRT = **individuals and partnership firms**.

nbf47913a80f.s: Recovery by secured lenders without court intervention is the principal feature of:
nbf47913a80f.x: SARFAESI allows secured lenders to recover without courts; IBC is collective, NCLT-led resolution and DRTs are tribunal-based recovery.
xa: FY24 recovery shares: **IBC 48%**, **SARFAESI 32%**, **DRTs 17%**.

n88f1f83314a.s: An Interest Coverage Ratio (ICR) below 1 means the firm:
o: Cannot service its interest from earnings
n88f1f83314a.x: ICR = EBIT ÷ interest payable; below 1, earnings do not cover interest.
xa: Lenders use ICR to judge a borrower's **present and emerging risk**.
**PCR** = provisions / gross NPA; higher PCR → more resilient bank.
**Twin Balance Sheet problem**: over-leveraged corporates + capital-starved banks.

n4330706b895.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the SARFAESI Act, 2002?
o: Lenders holding 60% of the dues can issue a 60-day notice under Section 13(2)
The threshold was 75% of dues before the 2016 amendment
Under Section 13(4), lenders can take possession of the secured asset, take over management or sell it
Under Section 13(8), the borrower can redeem the asset after the auction notice by paying 25% of the dues
n4330706b895.x: Under Section 13(8) the borrower can redeem only by paying the full dues, not 25%.
xa: **Sec 17**: appeal to the **DRT** within **45 days**; **Sec 18** bars civil courts.

n0431a442939.s: The SARFAESI Act, 2002 was based on the recommendations of the:
n0431a442939.x: The SARFAESI Act, 2002 was based on the recommendations of the Narasimham Committee.
xa: Core feature: banks enforce security on NPAs **without court intervention**.
⚠ The **IBC** was based on the **T.K. Viswanathan Committee (2015)**, not Narasimham.
**ARCs** under SARFAESI are registered with and regulated by **RBI**.

ncf765cb25e9.s: Under Section 17 of the SARFAESI Act, an appeal lies to the DRT within:
ncf765cb25e9.x: Section 17 allows an appeal to the DRT within 45 days; the Section 13(2) demand notice is of 60 days.
xa: ⚠ **60%** of lenders + **60-day** notice; appeal within **45 days**.

n71a597eb02f.s: The NCLAT hears appeals against orders of the NCLT, IBBI, CCI and:
n71a597eb02f.x: NCLAT hears appeals from NCLT, IBBI, CCI (from 26 May 2017) and NFRA (from 7 May 2018).
xa: Further appeal from NCLAT lies to the **Supreme Court**.
NCLAT sits at **New Delhi** (Principal Bench) and **Chennai**.

n55114d91433.s: Under the IBC waterfall mechanism, which of the following ranks above government dues?
n55114d91433.x: Resolution costs, workmen's dues and secured creditors' claims are placed above government dues in the IBC waterfall.
xa: The **2026** amendment cut liquidation to **180 + 90 days**.
FM: IBC realises **94.95%** of fair value; "not a debt-recovery tool".
Criticism: **deep haircuts** and guarantor liability.

ncc4b2ba377b.s: Under the Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) framework, capital infusion, a change of management or a merger may be ordered by the:
ncc4b2ba377b.x: Under PCA, the RBI may restrict lending, branch expansion, dividends and pay, and may order capital infusion, a management change or a merger.
xa: Curbs last until capital and asset quality improve.
PCA was introduced in **2002**; full form **Prompt Corrective Action**.

ne34f2f52ec6.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the NCLT bench is located at:
ne34f2f52ec6.x: The NCLT bench sits at Amaravati, while the DRT bench is at Visakhapatnam.
xa: **13 Sep 2026** National Lok Adalat: DRT Visakhapatnam settled **13** cases worth **₹46.11 crore**.

na7f04d84360.s: The Scheme for Sustainable Structuring of Stressed Assets (S4A) was introduced by the RBI in:
na7f04d84360.x: S4A came in 2016 and split a stressed firm's debt into sustainable and unsustainable parts; 2018 is Project Sashakt.
xa: S4A was an **RBI** scheme to rework the financial structure of stressed firms.
**SDR (2015)** preceded it.

ndfbd205b1e5.s: Project Sashakt (2018) for resolving stressed assets was based on the recommendations of the:
ndfbd205b1e5.x: Project Sashakt came from the Sunil Mehta Committee; its plan binds all lenders once 66% approve, with the lead bank driving it.
xa: Its **Inter-Creditor Agreement** aimed at **faster resolution of stressed assets** (UPSC 2019 key).
The **Prudential Framework (2019)** made the ICA mandatory.

n927057f21f7.s: A higher Provision Coverage Ratio (PCR) indicates a bank that is:
n927057f21f7.x: PCR = provisions ÷ gross NPA; a higher PCR means more bad loans are provided for, so the bank is more resilient.
xa: SCB PCR: **76.3%** (Mar 2025, FSR basis).
Govt data gives **93.14%** for SCBs — a different basis.

n4eadb45ca41.s: The March 2026 SCB Gross NPA ratio of 1.93 per cent was characterised as a:
n4eadb45ca41.x: The March 2026 Gross NPA ratio of 1.93 per cent was described as a decadal low.
n4eadb45ca41.tq: Match the latest numerical value with its stated trend description.
xs: SCB GNPA of **1.93%** in **Mar 2026** was a **decadal low** — so option **(3)** is correct.
NNPA was **0.39%**.
xa: Up next: **ECL** provisioning and higher risk weights on unsecured consumer credit + NBFC exposures.

n979d03d0ea9.s: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 was based on the recommendations of the:
n979d03d0ea9.x: The IBC came from the T.K. Viswanathan (Bankruptcy Law Reforms) Committee, 2015; Narasimham is linked to SARFAESI.
xa: ⚠ PYQ: "September assent" and "13-member IBBI" were both wrong (IBBI has **10** members).
IBC completed **10 years** in May 2026.

nc365723b535.s: Which change in the control structure of insolvency proceedings was introduced by the IBC?
nc365723b535.x: The IBC shifted the framework from debtor-in-possession to creditor-in-control.
nc365723b535.tq: Test a paired conceptual comparison by identifying the direction of institutional change.
xs: The IBC shifted control **from debtor-in-possession to creditor-in-control** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (4) reverses the change.
xa: It created a single, **time-bound** process — a structural reform.
The **2026** amendment's **CIIRP** is a hybrid of debtor-in-possession + creditor-in-control.
The **Committee of Creditors** (financial creditors) votes on resolution plans.

n8a48f197309.s: A promoter classified as a wilful defaulter, or a promoter associated with an NPA, is generally barred from bidding under which provision of the IBC?
n8a48f197309.x: Section 29A prevents wilful defaulters and promoters of NPAs from submitting resolution bids, subject to the statutory framework.
n8a48f197309.tq: Direct recall of the relevant statutory provision.
xs: **Section 29A** bars **wilful defaulters**/NPA promoters from bidding for their own firms — so option **(2)** is correct.
They are **barred from bidding under IBC** (May 2026), so they cannot regain the firm cheaply.
xa: The **Committee of Creditors** votes on resolution plans.
**Lalit Kumar Jain v. UoI (2021)**: **personal guarantors** stay liable after plan approval.
The **Fugitive Economic Offenders Act 2018** covers cases of **₹100 crore** and above.

nc9aaedbb78a.s: The minimum default required to trigger the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) is:
nc9aaedbb78a.x: CIRP needs a default of at least Rs 1 crore; it can be triggered by financial or operational creditors.
xa: CIRP timeline: **180 days** + **90 days**; outer limit **330 days** incl. litigation.
**Sec 29A**: wilful defaulters/NPA promoters cannot bid for their own firms.
NCLT is the adjudicating authority for **companies and LLPs**.

n5da0f5c5c50.s: The outer time limit for completing CIRP, including litigation, is:
n5da0f5c5c50.x: CIRP ordinarily runs 180 days with extension, with an outer limit of 330 days including litigation; actual cases have often taken longer.
xa: **67%** of cases exceed the timeline (ES 2025-26).
Causes: protracted litigation, NCLT capacity/staff shortages.

n31bed9faee2.s: The Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process for MSMEs was introduced in:
n31bed9faee2.x: The PPIRP for MSMEs was introduced in 2021 and has a 120-day limit.
n31bed9faee2.tq: Combine the launch year and time limit to distinguish the pre-pack process from ordinary CIRP.
xs: **PPIRP** for **MSMEs** came in **2021** with a **120-day** limit — so option **(4)** is correct.
**180 days** is the CIRP period; **330 days** is the CIRP outer limit.
xa: Only **14 admissions in 4 years** under PPIRP (ES 2025-26).
⚠ Timelines: CIRP **180 + 90** (outer **330**); PPIRP **120**; CIIRP **150**.

n0b8951857ba.s: Under the IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026, the liquidation timeline has been cut to:
n0b8951857ba.x: Liquidation is cut to 180 + 90 days; the Act also adds the hybrid Creditor-Initiated Insolvency Resolution Process (Secs 54C–54P).
xa: CIIRP: **150 days**, needs **51%** by value of notified financial creditors.
Criticism: **limits on who can start CIIRP**.

n2beba729f8a.s: The deterrent effect of the IBC is shown mainly by:
o: Completion of all cases by NCLT within 330 days
Settlement of a large number of cases before admission
Transfer of all recovery cases to Lok Adalats
n2beba729f8a.x: The settlement of 30,310 cases worth ₹13.78 lakh crore before admission was cited as evidence of the IBC's deterrent effect.
xa: FM: IBC realises **94.95%** of fair value; "not a debt-recovery tool".
IBC delivered **48%** of bank recoveries in FY24.

n7304eba2ae5.s: Under which provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 are the NCLT and NCLAT respectively set up?
n7304eba2ae5.x: NCLT is established under Section 408 and NCLAT under Section 410 of the Companies Act, 2013.
n7304eba2ae5.tq: Check the order of the statutory provisions instead of treating the two tribunals as interchangeable.
xs: NCLT is set up under **Sections 408** and NCLAT under **410** of the **Companies Act 2013** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (3) reverses them; **Sec 61** (IBC) is the NCLAT appeal provision; **Secs 202 and 211** relate to IBBI.
xa: Both were constituted on **1 June 2016**.
NCLT has **16 benches**, incl. **Amaravati** and **Hyderabad**.
NCLAT: Principal Bench **New Delhi** + a bench at **Chennai**.

n199cccf6c77.s: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) sits at:
n199cccf6c77.x: NCLAT sits in New Delhi and Chennai and hears appeals from NCLT under Section 61 of the IBC.
xa: NCLT has **16 benches**, incl. **Amaravati** and **Hyderabad**.
Further appeal lies to the **Supreme Court**.

n58b2316b07b.s: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) regulates:
n58b2316b07b.x: IBBI regulates insolvency professionals, insolvency professional agencies, information utilities and registered valuers.
xa: IBBI (**2016**) is the apex statutory regulator; it has **10** members.
IBBI proposed stronger safeguards for **guarantor insolvency** (**16 Sep 2026**).

nc3ea38d7e2b.s: The IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026 changed 'may' to 'shall' in Section 7(5)(a) of the Code. This change overturned the ruling in:
o: Lalit Kumar Jain v. Union of India
Swiss Ribbons v. Union of India
nc3ea38d7e2b.x: The change from 'may' to 'shall' in Sec 7(5)(a) makes admission of a financial creditor's CIRP plea mandatory once default is proved, overturning the Vidarbha Industries ruling, which had read 'may' as giving the NCLT discretion. Lalit Kumar Jain (2021) concerns personal guarantors' liability; Swiss Ribbons and Essar Steel are other IBC judgments not affected by this change.
xs: Changing "may" to "**shall**" in **Sec 7(5)(a)** overturned the **Vidarbha Industries** ruling — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Lalit Kumar Jain v. UoI (2021)** is about **personal guarantors** staying liable after plan approval.
xa: Other 2026 changes: NCLT admission within **14 days**, plan ruling within **30 days**.
New **CIIRP**: **150 days**, **51%** of notified financial creditors.
Clean-slate protection + cross-border insolvency framework.

nc5f14b5d796.s: NARCL, described as India’s ‘bad bank’, was announced in which Budget?
nc5f14b5d796.x: The National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited (NARCL) was announced in Budget 2021–22.
nc5f14b5d796.tq: Use the announcement-year distinction among closely placed Budgets.
xs: **NARCL**, India's "bad bank", was announced in **Budget 2021-22** — so option **(2)** is correct.
NARCL was one of the cited reasons for the fall in NPAs, alongside the **4R strategy** and **IBC**.
xa: It aggregates large stressed loans **above ₹500 crore**, targeting about **₹2 lakh crore**.
**IDRCL** resolves the assets, incl. by sale to **AIFs**.
Funding: **15% cash** + **85% in Security Receipts**.

n89d4b320ea1.s: NARCL pays for stressed assets ____ in cash and the rest in Security Receipts.
n89d4b320ea1.x: NARCL pays 15% in cash and 85% in Security Receipts; the Government guarantee of Rs 30,600 crore runs for 5 years.
xa: NARCL targets about **₹2 lakh crore** of fully or partly provided assets, in phases.
**₹2,410 crore** recovered by **30 Jun 2025**.

nc7bd80dc02e.s: What is meant by ‘evergreening’ of loans?
o: Writing off an old loan after full recovery
Giving a fresh loan to repay an old loan so that the NPA remains hidden
Increasing the maturity of a standard loan without any new borrowing
Converting every NPA into a government-guaranteed bond
nc7bd80dc02e.x: Evergreening occurs when fresh loans are used to repay old loans, thereby concealing the underlying NPA.
nc7bd80dc02e.tq: Discriminate between concealment through fresh lending and genuine recovery.
xs: **Evergreening** = a **fresh loan to repay an old loan**, so the **NPA stays hidden** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **AQR** exposed this practice.
xa: Other causes of NPAs: **loan frauds and diversion of funds**, weak credit appraisal, slow recovery machinery, corporate over-leverage.
The **twin balance sheet problem** stalls private capex and squeezes **MSME** credit.
**ICR** below **1** → the firm cannot service its interest.

na05e4adca59.s: In the context of banking supervision, PCA stands for:
na05e4adca59.x: PCA stands for Prompt Corrective Action, a framework used by the Reserve Bank of India to intervene in banks with weakening financial health.
na05e4adca59.tq: Test the exact expansion of a frequently confused institutional acronym.
xs: **PCA = Prompt Corrective Action** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2019 key).
RBI uses it to intervene in banks whose financial health is failing.
xa: Introduced by RBI in **2002**.
Current triggers: **capital, asset quality, leverage**.
Curbs: **lending, branch expansion**, risky exposures, **dividends**, management pay.

n2356df2faeb.s: The Prompt Corrective Action framework was introduced by the Reserve Bank of India in:
n2356df2faeb.x: The RBI introduced the Prompt Corrective Action framework in 2002 to monitor and restrict banks whose financial metrics deteriorate.
n2356df2faeb.tq: Use the year-based direct-recall method for a regulatory framework.
xs: RBI introduced the **PCA** framework in **2002** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Weak banks are placed under watch and restricted until capital and asset quality recover.
xa: Revised **Nov 2021**, effective **1 Jan 2022**.
The older **profitability (RoA)** trigger was dropped.
⚠ **2002** is also the year of **SARFAESI**.

n23d222c153c.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes insolvency from bankruptcy?
o: Bankruptcy is the inability to pay debts as they fall due, whereas insolvency is a court-approved resolution plan
Insolvency is a legal declaration, whereas bankruptcy is a financial state
Insolvency is the inability to pay debts as they fall due, whereas bankruptcy is the legal declaration or process that follows
Both insolvency and bankruptcy refer exclusively to liquidation of companies
n23d222c153c.x: Insolvency is the financial state of being unable to pay debts when due. Bankruptcy is the legal declaration or process that follows insolvency.
n23d222c153c.tq: Discriminate between two closely related legal terms by identifying the state and the subsequent legal process.
xs: **Insolvency** = inability to pay debts as they fall due; **bankruptcy** = the legal declaration/process that follows — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (2) swaps the two — the **BPSC 2023** trap.
xa: Insolvency is a **financial state**; bankruptcy is a **legal** process.
The IBC moved from **debtor-in-possession to creditor-in-control**.

nb0a182d6a0c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about personal guarantors in insolvency?
o: Personal guarantors remain liable after approval of a resolution plan
The Supreme Court affirmed it in 2021
The principle was affirmed in Lalit Kumar Jain v. Union of India
Approval of a resolution plan automatically releases every personal guarantor
nb0a182d6a0c.x: Approval of a resolution plan does not automatically release guarantors; they remain liable, as affirmed in Lalit Kumar Jain (2021).
xa: **IBBI** proposed stronger safeguards for guarantor insolvency (**16 Sep 2026**).
Draft rules for personal-guarantor repayment plans: valuation + bar on related-party voting.
NCLT also handles **personal guarantors of corporate debtors**.

n5fda900a496.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or debate concerning the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code?
n5fda900a496.x: Protracted litigation, limited NCLT capacity, deep haircuts and guarantor liability are identified concerns. The Code has not eliminated guarantor liability.

xs: **Complete elimination of guarantor liability** is NOT a criticism — so option **(3)** is correct.

Real criticisms: **deep haircuts**, **protracted litigation**, **NCLT capacity** shortages.

Limits on who can start **CIIRP** are another debate.

n8b1a36df51b.s: The National Mission for Financial Inclusion was announced on which date and formally launched on which date?

nde117d2c735.s: The minimum balance required in a PMJDY basic savings bank deposit account is:

n908a9a249a1.s: PMJDY account holders can get an overdraft of up to:

**₹50,000** is the **Shishu** limit under **MUDRA**.
**Life cover** of **₹30,000** for early enrollees.

nff531e04c45.s: PMJDY accounts may be linked with PMJJBY, PMSBY and:

nd74e5883afa.s: The annual premium under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) is:

ne6b40dcabcf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Atal Pension Yojana?
o: It provides a pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 per month after age 60

ne6b40dcabcf.x: APY is administered under PFRDA, not IRDAI; the other statements are correct.

n47f09a20b39.s: The annual premium of the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), as revised in 2022, is:

PMSBY pays **₹1 lakh** for partial disability.

n560631b2bc5.s: The RuPay-BHIM UPI incentive scheme gives an incentive on eligible BHIM-UPI person-to-merchant payments up to ₹2,000 of:

nf5c387dd747.s: The wholesale pilot of India's e-rupee (e-rupee-W) began on:

n338829983c3.s: Under MUDRA, the 'Kishore' category covers loans of:

n3d078833430.s: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) was launched on which date?

ndaa1abd7871.s: Who chaired the Committee on Comprehensive Financial Services for Small Businesses and Low-Income Households, which provided the basis for PMJDY and payments and small finance banks?

n2a179b67051.s: Who chaired the Chief Ministers' Committee on Digital Payments during 2016–17?

nc59c55ab889.s: Which Union Ministry administers the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana?

Ministry of Finance through the Department of Financial Services

n4d543bc2250.s: Promotion of digital payments was shifted from MeitY to which department of the Ministry of Finance?

o: Compulsory transfer of all bank deposits to the RBI

xa: Social security trio: **PMJJBY** (life, **₹436**), **PMSBY** (accident, **₹20**), **APY** (pension).

naf05600a379.s: UPI accounted for approximately what share of the world's real-time payments in 2025?

n060a88db382.s: The Bahamas' Sand Dollar is notable because it was
o: the world's first live retail CBDC, launched in 2020
the first wholesale CBDC pilot in the world
the first CBDC used exclusively for cross-border payments
the first cryptocurrency issued by a central bank

Sweden **e-Krona**; Eurozone **Digital Euro**.
India's retail pilot **e₹-R** from **1 Dec 2022**.

n2975d21356f.s: In 2020, the Supreme Court of India, in a case relating to cryptocurrency:

Struck down the RBI's 2018 circular barring banks from dealing with cryptocurrency businesses
Declared cryptocurrency to be legal tender
Directed the RBI to launch the Digital Rupee

n2975d21356f.tq: RBI ban 2018 → SC struck down 2020 → ban bill 2021 pending → 30% tax 2022.
xs: In **2020** the SC **struck down** the RBI's **2018** banking ban on crypto — option **(2)**.

n290b3db47a6.s: The UPI feature 'UPI LITE X' is meant for:

n06fcc2caf3e.s: Which payment system is described as the largest interoperable ATM network in India?

n06fcc2caf3e.tq: Use the superlative carefully and distinguish network infrastructure from payment applications.

xa: NFS was asked in **APPSC GS 2024**.

n6e86788359a.s: Zero MDR on RuPay debit card and BHIM-UPI transactions has applied since:

xa: **Taxation and other Laws (Amendment) Bill 2026** lets the Centre modify zero-MDR.

nabaefedb747.s: The principal objective of the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) is to
o: issue a sovereign digital currency for online purchases
create an open network that reduces the dominance of e-commerce platforms
regulate cryptocurrency exchanges through the RBI
replace Aadhaar with a private digital identity system
nabaefedb747.x: ONDC seeks to create an open digital commerce network and break e-commerce platform monopolies. It is not a currency or cryptocurrency-regulation platform.
nabaefedb747.tq: Match the initiative with its institutional objective and reject unrelated digital-finance functions.
xs: **ONDC** aims to **democratise e-commerce and break platform monopolies** — option **(2)**.
