n8cbc8b34406.s: In India, gains from cryptocurrency are taxed at:
n8cbc8b34406.x: Crypto gains attract 30% tax and 1% TDS; the 2021 bill to ban private crypto remains pending.
xa: The **30% / 1% TDS** regime applies since **2022**.
SC (**2020**) struck down RBI's **2018** banking ban.
Crypto: private, decentralised, no central issuer (**Bitcoin 2009**).

n9f59a2c799b.s: Under the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, UPI is to stay free for consumers, while MDR may be imposed on:
n9f59a2c799b.x: The Bill, passed by the Lok Sabha, lets the Centre modify zero-MDR so that MDR may apply to high-value payments while UPI stays free for consumers.
xa: Zero MDR has applied since **1 Jan 2020** under **Sec 10A**, PSS Act **2007**.
Debate: the **cost of zero-MDR** for **PSPs**.

ncf26fa76ae5.s: The money market (instruments of up to one year maturity) in India is regulated by the:
ncf26fa76ae5.x: The money market is regulated by the RBI and the capital market (maturity above one year) by SEBI.
xa: Money-market instruments: **T-bills, CP, CD**; **equities** are a capital-market instrument.

CCPs: **RBI** regulates **CCIL**; **SEBI** regulates **NSCCL** and **ICCL**.

n398583a1849.s: Which of the following is correctly classified as a hybrid capital-market instrument?
n398583a1849.x: Convertible preference shares and partly or optionally convertible debentures are hybrid instruments. Equity shares are pure instruments, while T-Bills and CPs belong to the money market.
n398583a1849.tq: Separate pure, hybrid and money-market instruments.
xs: A **convertible preference share** is a **hybrid** instrument — option **(3)**.
Hybrids also include **partly/optionally convertible debentures**.
**Equity** shares are **pure** instruments (with preference shares, debentures, bonds).
**Commercial Paper** and **Treasury Bills** are **money-market** instruments.

Capital market is regulated by **SEBI**, maturity above 1 year.

n0bc5623c9ca.s: An unsecured short-term promissory instrument issued by eligible corporates is called a:
n0bc5623c9ca.x: Commercial Paper is an unsecured short-term promissory instrument issued by eligible corporates.

Individuals do not directly participate in the money market, and it has **no physical location**.

ncf2419c661d.s: Commercial Paper was introduced in India in 1990 on the recommendation of the:
ncf2419c661d.x: CP (1990) and CDs (1989) both came on the Vaghul Committee's recommendation; CP can now be issued for 7 days to 1 year.

CP is **unsecured**, issued by corporates with net worth **≥ ₹5 crore**, rated by **CRISIL/ICRA**.

nb5e9bf885f7.s: The industrial securities market, a segment of the Indian capital market, is divided into:
nb5e9bf885f7.x: The industrial securities market has primary and secondary segments; DFIs and intermediaries such as venture capital companies are other parts of the capital market.
xa: Structure: **gilt-edged market**, **industrial securities market**, **DFIs**, **financial intermediaries**.
**Venture capital** = long-term start-up capital to new entrepreneurs.
**Private equity** = investment in **unlisted** firms.

n163e714d619.s: The Budget 2026–27 framework for financial markets proposed derivatives on:
n163e714d619.x: The framework included market-making for corporate bonds, derivatives on corporate bond indices and support for bigger municipal bond markets.
xa: Corporate bonds: **~98%** via private placement; market = **16% of GDP** (Korea **79%**).
**85-90%** of corporate bonds are **AAA**.
AP plans SDL borrowings of **₹73,383 crore** in 2026-27.

nf9f534d2746.s: Under the Government Securities Act, 2006, a G-Sec is best described as:
o: A tradeable instrument acknowledging debt of the Central or a State Government
A share issued by a government-owned company
An unsecured promissory note issued by a private company
A negotiable instrument issued only by commercial banks
nf9f534d2746.x: A G-Sec is a tradeable instrument issued by the Central or State Government acknowledging government debt. It is issued by the RBI on behalf of the government under the Government Securities Act, 2006.
nf9f534d2746.tq: Identify the exact statutory nature of the instrument.
xs: A **G-Sec** is a **tradeable instrument acknowledging debt of the Central or a State Government** — option **(1)**.
It is issued by the **RBI on behalf of the Government** under the **Government Securities Act, 2006**.
A share of a government company is equity, an unsecured promissory note of a company is **Commercial Paper**, and bank-issued instruments are **CDs** — none is a G-Sec.
xa: Types: **Treasury Bills** (91/182/364 days), **Cash Management Bills**, **dated securities** (1 year or more), **SDLs** (States).
The **gilt-edged market** deals in G-Secs — "gilt-edged" because **default risk ≈ zero**.
Individuals can buy G-Secs directly via a **Retail Direct Gilt (RDG) account**.

n5e0d629fd16.s: Cash Management Bills are issued to meet:
o: Temporary cash mismatches of the Central Government
Long-term borrowing needs of State Governments
Working-capital needs of public sector undertakings
n5e0d629fd16.x: CMBs cover the Centre's temporary cash mismatches; T-Bills are zero-coupon and SDLs are long-term State Government borrowings.
xa: T-bill maturities: **91, 182, 364 days** (original maturity < 1 year).
**Dated securities**: **1 year or more**, issued by the Centre.
**OMOs**: RBI **sells** G-Secs to absorb liquidity, **buys** to inject.

o: Government securities such as Treasury Bills and Government bonds
Commercial Paper and Certificates of Deposit only
nce2b9be069a.x: The gilt-edged market is the market for Treasury Bills and Government bonds (government and government-guaranteed securities). It is called 'gilt-edged' because default risk is almost zero. Blue-chip shares are corporate equity, CP and CDs are money-market instruments of corporates and banks, and gold is a commodity.
nce2b9be069a.tq: Gilt-edged = government paper, near-zero default risk.
xs: The **gilt-edged market** deals with **Government securities such as Treasury Bills and Government bonds** — option **(2)**.
It covers govt securities and those **guaranteed by govt**; called "gilt-edged" because **default risk ≈ zero**.
It does not deal with corporate paper: **CP** and **CD** are money-market instruments of corporates and banks/FIs.
xa: T-bills: **91, 182, 364 days**; dated securities: **1 year or more**; SDLs: State Governments.
The gilt-edged market is the first segment of the **capital market** structure.
Issued under the **Government Securities Act, 2006** by the RBI on behalf of the Government.

nindian-economy-61-4.s: Treasury Bills are sold through auction by which institution?
nindian-economy-61-4.x: The RBI sells Treasury Bills by auction on behalf of the Central Government.
nindian-economy-61-4.tq: Discriminate the issuer from the auctioneer.
n: The Reserve Bank of India sells Treasury Bills through auction. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 90-91]
xs: **Treasury Bills** are sold through **auction** by the **RBI** — option **(4)**.

**SEBI** regulates the **capital market**; **State Governments** issue **State Development Loans**.

Tenors: **91, 182 and 364 days**.
T-bills were **first issued** in India in **1917**.

n8d394842507.s: The largest primary dealer in Government securities in India is:
n8d394842507.x: SBI DFHI is the largest primary dealer; primary dealers are RBI-regulated underwriters and market makers in G-Secs.
xa: G-Sec traders: **banks, PDs, insurers, MFs, provident funds, FPIs** and individuals (via Retail Direct).
G-Secs are issued by the **RBI on behalf of the Government** under the **Government Securities Act, 2006**.
**OMOs**: RBI **sells** G-Secs → absorbs liquidity; **buys** → injects.

n7b345bbf98b.s: If the Reserve Bank of India wants to absorb liquidity from the banking system through open market operations, it should generally:
n7b345bbf98b.x: An RBI sale of Government securities withdraws liquidity from the banking system. RBI purchases through OMOs inject liquidity.
n7b345bbf98b.tq: Apply the buy–sell direction to determine the liquidity effect.
xs: To absorb liquidity, RBI should **sell Government securities** — option **(2)**.
In **OMOs**, an RBI **sale** of G-Secs absorbs liquidity; a **purchase** injects liquidity.
**SDLs** are issued by **State Governments**, not used by RBI to absorb liquidity.
xa: RBI buying through OMOs, plus foreign inflows, makes **yields fall**.
**Primary dealers** are RBI-regulated market makers in G-Secs; **SBI DFHI** is the largest.
G-Secs are issued under the **Government Securities Act, 2006**.

nindian-economy-61-5.s: Treasury Bills were first issued in India in which year?
nindian-economy-61-5.x: India first issued Treasury Bills in 1917, during the First World War.
n: Treasury Bills were first issued in India in 1917. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 90-91]
xs: **Treasury Bills** were first issued in India in **1917** — option **(4)**.
They are **short-term debt instruments** — **money-market instruments**.
They are sold by the **RBI** through **auction**.
xa: T-bills pay **no periodic interest** — **zero-coupon**, sold at a **discount**.
Tenors: **91, 182 and 364 days** — less than one year.
The **gilt-edged market** is the market for **T-bills and Government bonds**.

n2145565f098.s: Hedge funds that use leveraged trading fall under which SEBI category of Alternative Investment Funds?

n0b637c3081f.s: In September 2025, SEBI added an Alternative Investment Fund category specifically for which group?
n0b637c3081f.x: In September 2025, SEBI added an AIF category intended only for accredited investors.
n0b637c3081f.tq: Use the date-category association and avoid confusing accredited investors with retail or institutional investors.
xs: SEBI added an AIF category only for **accredited investors** — option **(4)**.
AIFs are **privately pooled** vehicles regulated by **SEBI**, not retail or state-owned schemes.
xa: **Category III** (hedge funds, leveraged trading) is allowed in **commodity derivatives**.
**Category I**: venture capital, **angel**, SME, social venture, **infrastructure** funds.
**REITs** and **InvITs** pool income-yielding assets for **asset monetisation**.

nindian-economy-60-18.s: The date on which a bond's principal becomes repayable is called its:
nindian-economy-60-18.x: The repayment date is maturity; the coupon is the interest, and face value is the nominal value.
n: A bondholder receives interest or returns according to the bond’s terms. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 89-90]
An issuer is a government, company, or other eligible entity raising funds. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 89-90]
Maturity is the date when the principal or face value becomes repayable. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 89-90]
The face value or par value is the nominal value of a bond. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 89-90]
The coupon or interest is the stated interest payment on a bond. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #60 · pp 89-90]
xa: A bondholder is a **creditor** or **lender** to the issuer.

**Masala bond** = **rupee-denominated bond issued overseas**.

nfc957a57832.s: In a Masala bond, the currency risk is borne by the:

xa: **Sovereign green bonds** are now **FAR-eligible**.
**Social bond** = social projects; **inflation-indexed bond** = principal/coupon adjusted to inflation.
**Zero-coupon bond** = issued at discount, no periodic interest (e.g. T-bills).

n3ef98217beb.s: The Sovereign Gold Bond scheme, launched in 2015, paid interest of ____ in addition to gold-price-linked returns.
n3ef98217beb.x: SGBs were launched in 2015 with 2.5% interest plus gold-price-linked returns; fresh issuance has been discontinued.
xa: **Inflation-indexed bond**: principal/coupon adjusted to inflation.
**Green bond**: proceeds only for climate/environment projects.

nindian-economy-3-3.s: The first green bond was issued in 2007 by the:
nindian-economy-3-3.x: The European Investment Bank issued the first green bond in 2007; the World Bank issued a labelled green bond in 2008.
n: The Green Bond was first introduced by the European Investment Bank in 2007. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
The World Bank labelled a bond as a Green Bond in 2008. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
xa: Green bond proceeds go only to **climate/environment projects**; **sovereign green bonds** are now **FAR-eligible**.
**Sovereign Gold Bond** launched **2015** at **2.5%** interest; **fresh issuance discontinued**.
**Masala bond** = **rupee-denominated bond issued overseas**.

nindian-economy-61-10.s: Treasury Bills differ from Government Bonds because Treasury Bills are:
nindian-economy-61-10.x: Government Bonds pay interest, whereas Treasury Bills are zero-coupon securities.
n: Treasury Bills are zero-coupon securities. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 90-91]
Government Bonds are interest-bearing securities. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 90-91]
xa: T-bills are issued at a **discount** and redeemed at **face value** on **maturity**.
Bonds have maturity of **at least one year**; T-bills **less than one year** (**91, 182, 364 days**).

n4dfda51c18f.s: Which of the following generally tends to LOWER government bond yields?
o: RBI purchases of G-secs through OMOs
n4dfda51c18f.x: OMO purchases support bond prices and inject liquidity, lowering yields; higher policy rates, inflation and borrowing raise yields.
xa: Core rule: **price and yield move inversely**.
OMOs: RBI **sells** G-Secs to absorb liquidity, **buys** to inject.
**June 2026**: FAR widened to new **15-, 30- and 40-year G-Secs** and sovereign green bonds.

nd9a545be1e6.s: A circuit breaker in a securities market is intended to:
o: Halt trading when an index or stock moves beyond prescribed limits
nd9a545be1e6.x: A circuit breaker temporarily halts trading when the movement in an index or stock exceeds specified limits.
nd9a545be1e6.tq: Identify the market-stabilisation function rather than an investor-return function.

On the same calendar day only

nindian-economy-10-4.x: The secondary market trades securities already issued; SEBI regulates stock exchange operations.
n: SEBI regulates stock exchange operations. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-14]

nf8d67ce9bda.s: In an IPO, the proceeds of an offer for sale go to the:

Price band, and the final price is set from the bids
Price set by the stock exchange after listing
Price equal to the face value

Anchor investors are retail investors who bid after the issue closes

xa: **F&O curbs**: **6** regulations; expiry day **Tuesday/Thursday**.
SEBI took **58** ease-of-business initiatives.
**Ketan Parekh (2001)** scam led to rolling settlement.

n42a202956a1.s: The Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) for the top 1,000 listed companies is prescribed by:
n42a202956a1.x: BRSR is prescribed by SEBI (not the RBI) and replaced the earlier BRR; BRSR Core needs reasonable assurance on key ESG metrics.
xa: **BRSR** = Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report.
**T+0** optional settlement alongside **T+1**.
**SME IPOs** surged **87% (FY23-25)**.

n8cd0ab7c125.s: The East Asian financial crisis of 1997 involved the collapse of the:
n8cd0ab7c125.x: The crisis involved the Thai baht collapse and short-term foreign debt; India's impact was limited by capital controls and low short-term debt.
xa: **Taper tantrum (2013)**: FPI outflow, rupee fall; CAD peaked **4.8% of GDP (FY13)**.
**GFC (2007-09)**: US sub-prime mortgages → FPI outflow, market crash in India.
**FSDC** was set up in **December 2010** under the **G-20** push.

na6374a3d154.s: Teaser loans are best described as loans having:
o: No repayment obligation during the entire loan period
A high fixed interest rate initially and a lower rate later
A low fixed interest rate in the early years and a higher rate subsequently
Only a floating interest rate linked to gold prices
na6374a3d154.x: Teaser loans offer a low fixed rate in the early years and a higher rate later, creating future default risk for banks.
na6374a3d154.tq: Discriminate between the initial and later interest-rate features.
xs: **Teaser loans** carry a **low fixed rate in the early years and a higher rate later** — option **(3)**.
They are a form of **sub-prime lending**; banks face **future default risk**.
xa: ⚠ Key: **statement 1 only** (**UPSC 2011**).
**Credit Default Swap**: insurance-like derivative; seller pays on default.
Sub-prime loans were **securitised** into mortgage-backed securities sold worldwide.

n626f34a48a6.s: A Credit Default Swap is best described as:
o: A deposit insurance product with no counterparty exposure
A government grant to banks for purchasing government securities
An insurance-like derivative on bonds in which the seller pays upon default, with counterparty risk
A loan arrangement in which the borrower pays only after maturity
n626f34a48a6.x: A Credit Default Swap is an insurance-like derivative on bonds; the seller pays when default occurs, and the contract carries counterparty risk.
n626f34a48a6.tq: Identify the instrument from its payoff condition and associated risk.
xs: A **Credit Default Swap** is an **insurance-like derivative on bonds**; the **seller pays upon default**, with **counterparty risk** — option **(3)**.
It is not deposit insurance — that is **DICGC** (₹5 lakh per depositor per bank).
xa: **Teaser loans** were a form of **sub-prime lending**.
**Shadow banking**: financial activity of **non-bank** entities outside regular bank regulation.
**"Too big to fail"** institutions get **closer supervision**.

o: Unauthorised branches of scheduled commercial banks
Financial activity of non-bank entities carried on outside regular bank regulation
Off-balance-sheet lending by the RBI to the government
Banking services provided only during non-working hours
ne68ff564d86.x: Shadow banking means financial (credit) activity by non-bank entities such as NBFCs that lies outside regular bank regulation (UPPSC 2014 key). It is not about unauthorised bank branches, RBI lending to government, or banking hours.
xs: **Shadow banking** = **financial activity of non-bank entities outside regular bank regulation** — option **(2)** (**UPPSC 2014** key).
It is not about unauthorised bank branches, RBI lending or banking hours.
xa: NBFCs **cannot take demand deposits, issue cheques or join the payment system**.
**Asset-liability mismatch** exposed when **IL&FS** defaulted (**2018**).
NBFCs are registered under the **Companies Act**.

nba128d09f52.s: Global Systemically Important Banks (G-SIBs) are identified by the:
nba128d09f52.x: G-SIBs are identified by the FSB, and no Indian bank is among them; LIC, GIC Re and New India Assurance are IRDAI's D-SIIs.
xa: **D-SIBs** (RBI): **SBI, ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank** — extra **CET1** surcharge.
**"Too big to fail"** = failure would disrupt the whole system.
RBI regulates banks/NBFCs, **IRDAI** insurers; **FSDC** coordinates.

n617225b8e67.s: Which of the following is a characteristic of NBFCs?
o: They can accept demand deposits and issue cheques as banks do.
They are registered under the Companies Act but cannot take demand deposits, issue cheques or join the payment system.
They are covered by DICGC irrespective of the type of deposit.
They are outside all forms of RBI regulation.
n617225b8e67.x: NBFCs are registered under the Companies Act and cannot take demand deposits, issue cheques or join the payment system; their deposits are not covered by DICGC.
n617225b8e67.tq: Use the contrast between bank functions and NBFC restrictions.
xs: NBFCs are **registered under the Companies Act** but **cannot take demand deposits, issue cheques or join the payment system** — option **(2)**.
NBFCs are **not covered by DICGC**, and they are regulated by **RBI**.
xa: **Scale-Based Regulation (Oct 2022)**: **Base, Middle, Upper, Top** layers.
RBI named **17 NBFC-UL for 2026-27**.
**Shadow banking** = non-bank financial activity outside regular bank regulation.

n07a0fff4048.s: The RBI's Scale-Based Regulation (October 2022) for NBFCs has Base, Middle, Upper and ____ layers.
n07a0fff4048.x: Scale-Based Regulation has Base, Middle, Upper and Top layers.
xa: RBI named **17 NBFC-UL for 2026-27**.
Proposed test: assets **≥ ₹1 lakh crore**.
NBFCs are **not covered by DICGC**.

n48e1a4f30dd.s: The Banking Regulation (Amendment) Act, 2020 brought which institutions under RBI supervision?
o: Only payment banks and small finance banks
All insurance companies and mutual funds
Only foreign banks operating in India
n48e1a4f30dd.x: The 2020 amendment brought urban and multi-state cooperative banks under RBI supervision.
n48e1a4f30dd.tq: Identify the precise institutional coverage of the amendment.
xs: The Act brought **urban and multi-state co-operative banks** under **RBI supervision** — option **(4)**.
It followed the **PMC Bank (2019)** failure under dual control.
xa: Deposit insurance: **₹5 lakh** per depositor per bank (**DICGC**).
**PCA** watches weak banks on **capital, asset quality, leverage**.
RBI regulates banks/NBFCs; **IRDAI** regulates insurers.

n920b25b2ec8.s: In India's financial system, the role of the FSDC is to:
n920b25b2ec8.x: The RBI regulates banks and NBFCs and IRDAI regulates insurers; the FSDC coordinates among financial regulators.
xa: FSDC is chaired by the **Union Finance Minister** (**Dec 2010**).
⚠ **D-SIBs** by **RBI**; **D-SIIs** by **IRDAI**; **G-SIBs** by the **FSB**.
Co-op banks came under **RBI supervision** via the **Banking Regulation (Amendment) Act, 2020**.

ndff4d9ee183.s: The Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC), set up in December 2010, is chaired by the:
ndff4d9ee183.x: FSDC was set up in December 2010 and is chaired by the Union Finance Minister; it is not an organ of NITI Aayog.
xa: It monitors **macroprudential supervision** and **inter-regulatory coordination**.
**CFSA** is co-chaired by an **RBI Deputy Governor and the Finance Secretary**.

n5913bd10ac7.s: The Financial Stability Report is published by the RBI with what periodicity?
o: Quarterly, in March, June, September and December
n5913bd10ac7.x: The RBI publishes the Financial Stability Report half-yearly, generally in June and December.
n5913bd10ac7.tq: Test the exact issuing authority and publication frequency.
xs: The **FSR** is published by **RBI** **half-yearly (June, December)** — option **(1)**.
Each FSR includes **macro stress tests**.
xa: **Dec 2025 FSR** (foreword by Governor **Sanjay Malhotra**): external/geopolitical risks; banks + NBFCs resilient.
**FSR June 2026**: fintech small-ticket personal loan defaults **6.4%** (Mar 2026) vs ~**4%** (Mar 2024).
RBI kept **CCyB inactive** (May 2026).

ne5197588dea.s: The RBI's Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) framework applies to:
o: Weak banks, monitored on capital, asset quality and leverage
Strong banks with high capital, to give them more freedom
ne5197588dea.x: PCA watches weak banks on capital, NPAs and leverage and can restrict their lending, branch expansion and dividends.
xa: Other tools: macro **stress tests** in each FSR; **CRILC** for large credits.
Bank NPAs at a **multi-decadal low**: GNPA **2.2%**, NNPA **0.5%**.

nc01df0a163a.s: The Committee on Financial Sector Assessment (CFSA) in India was co-chaired by:
o: The Union Finance Minister and the RBI Governor
An RBI Deputy Governor and the Finance Secretary
The SEBI Chairperson and the Chief Economic Adviser
The RBI Governor and the NITI Aayog Vice-Chairperson
nc01df0a163a.x: CFSA was co-chaired by an RBI Deputy Governor and the Finance Secretary (MPPSC 2020 key). The Finance Minister chairs FSDC and the RBI Governor chairs its sub-committee; SEBI, CEA and NITI Aayog did not co-chair CFSA.
xs: **CFSA** was co-chaired by an **RBI Deputy Governor and the Finance Secretary** — option **(2)** (**MPPSC 2020** key).
The **Finance Minister** chairs **FSDC**, and the **RBI Governor** chairs its sub-committee.
xa: FSDC: set up **December 2010**; **not** a NITI Aayog organ.
**FSR** is published by RBI half-yearly.
**Comparative**: RBI regulates banks/NBFCs, IRDAI insurers; FSDC coordinates.

n7fd9f64c3ad.s: The Global Financial Crisis of 2007-09 originated in:
n7fd9f64c3ad.x: The GFC began with US sub-prime mortgages; India then saw FPI outflows and set up the FSDC in December 2010.
xa: Sub-prime chain: weak-borrower loans → **securitised** MBS → rates rise → **home-loan defaults** → US bank failures.
⚠ Trap: the GFC was **not** caused by oil prices (**UPPSC 2010** key).
**Teaser loans** were a form of sub-prime lending.

na127ea23212.s: Which one of the following was NOT a link in the sub-prime crisis chain described for its impact on India?
o: Securitisation into mortgage-backed securities sold worldwide
A rise in interest rates followed by home-loan defaults
A sustained fall in oil prices causing the banking collapse
na127ea23212.x: The crisis chain involved weak borrowers, securitisation, rising rates, defaults and US bank failures. It was not caused by falling oil prices.
na127ea23212.tq: Identify the unrelated causal explanation inserted into a recognised sequence.
xs: **A sustained fall in oil prices** was NOT a link — option **(4)**.
⚠ The sub-prime crisis was **not caused by oil prices** (**UPPSC 2010** key).
Real chain: **weak borrowers** → **securitisation** → **rates rise** → **home-loan defaults** → US bank failures.
xa: In India: **FPI outflow** and **market crash**.
**Teaser loans**: low rate early, higher later — a form of sub-prime lending.
**Credit Default Swap**: seller pays on default; carries **counterparty risk**.

n2b27476e04a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC)?
o: It is an organ of NITI Aayog
Its sub-committee is chaired by the RBI Governor
n2b27476e04a.x: FSDC is not an organ of NITI Aayog; it handles macroprudential supervision and inter-regulatory coordination.
xa: FSDC: chaired by the **Union Finance Minister**; set up **December 2010**.
It came under the **G-20** push after the **GFC (2007-09)**.

nbd058aabac7.s: The credit-deposit ratio of Andhra Pradesh was reported as 157.40 per cent. What does this most directly indicate?
o: The State had no dependence on bank deposits for lending.
Banks accepted 157.40 per cent more deposits than they lent.
Bank lending was very high relative to deposits.
Deposits were 157.40 per cent of bank credit.
nbd058aabac7.x: A credit-deposit ratio of 157.40 per cent indicates that lending was very high relative to deposits in Andhra Pradesh. It does not mean that deposits exceeded credit.
nbd058aabac7.tq: Interpret the direction and meaning of a ratio rather than reversing its numerator and denominator.
xs: AP's credit-deposit ratio of **157.40%** means **bank lending was very high relative to deposits** — option **(3)**.
Credit exceeds deposits, so options (2) and (4) reverse the relationship.
xa: Deposit insurance: **₹5 lakh** per depositor per bank (**DICGC**).

nindian-economy-58-13.s: Besides financial stability and development, the FSDC also focuses on:
nindian-economy-58-13.x: The FSDC covers financial stability and development and also financial literacy and inclusion.
n: The Financial Stability and Development Council is an apex-level forum for financial stability and development. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 86-88]
The Financial Stability and Development Council also focuses on financial literacy and financial inclusion. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #58 · pp 86-88]
xa: The FSDC is **chaired** by the **Union Finance Minister**; members include **financial-sector regulators**.
It was set up in **December 2010**; its sub-committee is chaired by the **RBI Governor**.
⚠ FSDC is **not** a NITI Aayog organ.

nb23861e0a4b.s: Inflation in only a few commodities, such as food, while overall inflation remains low is known as:
nb23861e0a4b.x: Skewflation describes a situation in which prices rise sharply in a few items while prices of other items remain stable and overall inflation is low.
nb23861e0a4b.tq: Discriminate between similar inflation labels by examining their scope.
xs: **Skewflation** = prices rise in **a few items (e.g. food)** while overall inflation is low — option **(2)**.
**Reflation** = inflation returning after deflation; **stagflation** = high inflation + stagnant growth.
xa: ⚠ **Disinflation** = rate falls but stays positive; **Deflation** = prices fall.
**Hyperinflation** is the fastest speed class, after **galloping**.
**Food inflation** is measured by the **CFPI**.

ne23c78cea5e.s: Inflation returning after a period of deflation, seen as a sign of recovery, is called:
ne23c78cea5e.x: Reflation is inflation returning after deflation; a falling but positive inflation rate is disinflation.
xa: **Skewflation**: prices rise in a few items while overall inflation is low.
**Stagflation**: high inflation + stagnant growth/unemployment.
Speed classes: creeping (**below 3%**), walking/trotting (**3-10%**), galloping, hyperinflation.

nindian-economy-51-5.s: Inflation accompanied by slow growth and unemployment is called:
nindian-economy-51-5.x: Stagflation combines inflation with slow growth and unemployment.
n: Demand-pull inflation occurs when demand increases. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 75-77]
Cost-push inflation occurs when production costs increase. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 75-77]
Bottleneck inflation results from a supply constraint. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 75-77]
Stagflation combines inflation, slow growth, and unemployment. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 75-77]
xa: **Skewflation** = prices rise in a few items while others stay stable.
⚠ **Disinflation** = rate falls but stays positive; **deflation** = prices fall.
By speed: creeping (below **3%**), walking (**3-10%**), galloping, hyperinflation.

n2a42aa98e2e.s: In May 2026, the relative ordering of food, headline and core inflation was
n2a42aa98e2e.x: In May 2026, food inflation was 4.85%, headline inflation was 3.93% and core inflation was 3.73%, giving the order Food > Headline > Core.
n2a42aa98e2e.tq: Arrange the three measures by comparing their actual percentages.
xs: May 2026: **Food > headline > core** — option **(3)**.
xa: Same order as the **APPSC G1 2024** key (2023-24).
2025 was the reverse: **Core > Headline > Food** (food **-0.2%**).
AP retail inflation **4.9% (May 2026)** vs India **3.9%**.

n900a0e89e9c.s: Food inflation in India is measured by the:
o: Wholesale Price Index - Primary Articles only
n900a0e89e9c.x: Food inflation is measured by the Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI), which has 10 sub-groups such as cereals, pulses, vegetables and milk. WPI primary articles is a wholesale measure, CPI-IW is for industrial workers' DA, and IIP measures industrial output, not prices.
xs: Food inflation is measured by the **Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI)** — option **(1)**.
CFPI has **10 sub-groups**: cereals, meat and fish, egg, milk, oils, fruits, vegetables, pulses, sugar, spices.
**CPI-IW** is for industrial workers' DA; **IIP** measures industrial output, not prices.
xa: Food & beverages = **36.75%** of the new CPI basket (old 2012 series **~46%**).
Aug 2026: food inflation **5.7%**, headline **4.8%**.
Food inflation causes: **monsoon**, **supply shocks**.

nb8150bd8557.s: The CPI (Rural/Urban/Combined) in India is published by which organisation?
o: National Statistical Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT
nb8150bd8557.x: The CPI for Rural, Urban and Combined sectors is published by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
nb8150bd8557.tq: Identify the institution associated with the index rather than confusing it with the WPI publisher.
xs: **CPI (Rural/Urban/Combined)** is published by **NSO, MoSPI** — option **(1)**.
**CPI-IW/AL/RL** come from the **Labour Bureau**; **WPI** from the **Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT**.
xa: ⚠ CPI = **NSO**; CPI-IW/AL/RL = **Labour Bureau**; WPI = **OEA, DPIIT**.
New CPI base **2024** (from 2012).
Some older notes say **CSO** (now NSO).

n2b1306e0678.s: The current base year of the new CPI (Rural/Urban/Combined) series is
n2b1306e0678.x: The new CPI series uses 2024 as its base year and was introduced from the earlier 2012-based series.
n2b1306e0678.tq: Use the latest base year and distinguish it from the earlier CPI series.
xs: The new CPI base year is **2024** — option **(2)**.
It moved from **2012**; the new series came out on **12 Feb 2026** with the Jan 2026 index.
**2011-12** is WPI's base; **2022-23** is the GDP deflator's base.
xa: Old **2012** series: food and beverages **~46%**.
New series: **358 items**, **12 divisions** (COICOP 2018).
Oct 2025 **0.3%** → lowest in the 2012 series.

na5eed8d64bf.s: CPI-IW is primarily used for determining the dearness allowance of
na5eed8d64bf.x: CPI-IW is used for determining dearness allowance for industrial workers.
na5eed8d64bf.tq: Link the specialised index to the category of workers it represents.
xs: **CPI-IW** is used for the **DA of industrial workers** — option **(3)**.
**CPI-AL** serves farm labourers' wage revision.
xa: CPI-IW: **Labour Bureau**, base **2016**.
AP CPI-IW centres: **Guntur, Visakhapatnam, Nellore**.
Uses: CPI → **DA**; WPI → **contract escalation**, industrial analysis.

ne3c0b7093be.s: The GDP deflator is calculated as
o: Real GDP multiplied by nominal GDP divided by 100
Nominal GDP divided by real GDP multiplied by 100
Nominal GDP minus real GDP divided by 100
Real GDP divided by nominal GDP multiplied by 100
ne3c0b7093be.x: GDP deflator equals nominal GDP divided by real GDP, multiplied by 100. A rise in the deflator reduces the purchasing power of money.
ne3c0b7093be.tq: Recall the numerator-denominator order in the formula rather than reversing it.
xs: GDP deflator = **nominal GDP divided by real GDP multiplied by 100** — option **(2)**.
It is published by **NSO**, series base **2022-23**.
xa: It is the **broadest** index — all goods and services produced.
A rising deflator **decreases purchasing power** (**APPSC G2 2025**).
**WPI** covers no services; the deflator covers the whole economy.

n93acdcfbaa6.s: The current Wholesale Price Index (WPI) in India is compiled by which body and with which base year?
o: Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry; base 2011-12
n93acdcfbaa6.x: WPI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT (Ministry of Commerce and Industry), with base 2011-12 (revised from 2004-05 in 2017); it has 697 items and no services. NSO publishes CPI (base 2024), the Labour Bureau publishes CPI-IW (base 2016), and the RBI does not compile WPI.
xs: **WPI**: **Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry**; base **2011-12** — option **(3)**.
Base revised from **2004-05** in **2017**; **697** items, **no services**.
**NSO** publishes CPI (**2024**); the **Labour Bureau** publishes CPI-IW (**2016**).
xa: Items: primary **117**, manufactured **564**, fuel and power **16**.
New WPI (**2022-23**): **957** items; runs with a **PPI** for **5** years.
WPI rose to a **38-month high of 3.88%** (Mar 2026).

na904d7ea7f1.s: Which institution publishes national income and GDP estimates in India?
o: State Directorate of Economics and Statistics
Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT
na904d7ea7f1.x: National income and GDP estimates are published by the NSO, under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation; the table also identifies the earlier CSO association.
na904d7ea7f1.tq: Identify the publishing body from the statistic concerned.
xs: National income/GDP is published by the **NSO (CSO), MoSPI** — option **(3)**.
**GSDP** is by the State **DES**; **WPI** by the **OEA, DPIIT**.
xa: **IIP**: NSO, monthly on the **28th**, **14** source agencies.
**Employment**: **PLFS** — NSO.
GDP deflator series base **2022-23**.

n2cbc27d5cbf.s: Before the adoption of CPI (Combined) by the RBI in April 2014, India used which index as the headline inflation measure?
n2cbc27d5cbf.x: WPI was earlier used as India's headline inflation measure. The RBI adopted CPI (Combined) as its key measure in April 2014 following the Urjit Patel Committee framework.
n2cbc27d5cbf.tq: Test the before-and-after distinction in a policy transition.
xs: Earlier, **WPI** was the headline measure — option **(3)**.
RBI adopted **CPI (Combined)** in **April 2014** on the **Urjit Patel Committee**'s advice.
xa: **Urjit Patel (2014)**: CPI as **nominal anchor**, **flexible inflation targeting**.
**Monetary Policy Framework Agreement (Feb 2015)** → RBI Act amended **2016**.
Target: **4% ± 2%** of CPI-C.

nc0fab8b8f2e.s: Inflation-indexed bonds are securities in which:
o: Only the coupon rate is fixed permanently, irrespective of inflation
Repayment is linked exclusively to the exchange rate
The principal is linked to the stock-market index alone
The principal and/or interest is linked to an inflation index
nc0fab8b8f2e.x: In inflation-indexed bonds, the principal and/or interest payments are linked to an inflation index, protecting the investor’s real return.
nc0fab8b8f2e.tq: Use the defining contractual feature to distinguish the instrument.
xs: In **inflation-indexed bonds**, **principal and/or interest is linked to an inflation index** — option **(4)**.
They give investors a **real-return** hedge against inflation.
xa: RBI issued **IIBs in 2013**.
Govt benefits: **cheaper borrowing** when credible, **signal** of low-inflation commitment.
Also: **wider investor base**, savings moved **away from gold**.

nindian-economy-51-2.s: Which of the following is INCORRECT?
o: The NSO compiles CPI-Rural and CPI-Urban.
CPI-Combined is the RBI's inflation-target measure.
CPI-IW is compiled by the NSO.
nindian-economy-51-2.x: CPI-IW is compiled by the Labour Bureau; the NSO compiles CPI-Rural, CPI-Urban and CPI-Combined.
n: CPI-IW is compiled by the Labour Bureau. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 75-77]
WPI excludes services. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 75-77]
CPI-Combined is used as the monetary policy inflation measure. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 75-77]
CPI-Rural is compiled by the NSO. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 75-77]
CPI-Urban is compiled by the NSO. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 75-77]
CPI-Combined is compiled by the NSO. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #51 · pp 75-77]
xa: ⚠ CPI-Rural/Urban/Combined = **NSO**; CPI-IW/AL/RL = **Labour Bureau**.
CPI-IW base year: **2016**; CPI-Combined moved to base **2024**.
WPI = **Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT**.

n45fade5dd9d.s: How many items does the new WPI series contain?
n45fade5dd9d.x: The new WPI series has 957 items, against 697 in the earlier series; its weights are based on Gross Value of Output.
xa: It runs with a new **PPI** for **5 years** → then WPI is phased out.
Current WPI still uses **2011-12**.

n85204f6a4ce.s: Which index is regarded as the broadest measure because it covers all goods and services produced in the economy?
n85204f6a4ce.x: The GDP deflator is the broadest measure because it covers all goods and services produced in the economy, including services.
n85204f6a4ce.tq: Use the coverage clue to distinguish the economy-wide deflator from price-basket indices.
xs: The **GDP deflator** is the broadest — **covers all goods and services produced** — option **(3)**.
**WPI** covers goods only; **CPI-IW** and **CPI-Combined** cover consumer baskets.
xa: GDP deflator = **nominal GDP / real GDP x 100**.
Series base **2022-23**, published by **NSO**.
⚠ WPI has **no services**.

ncb7a711fd72.s: Which group carries the largest weight (about 64%) in WPI?
ncb7a711fd72.x: Manufactured products carry about 64% weight in WPI, which covers goods only.
xa: WPI items: manufactured **564** of **697**.
New CPI: food & beverages **36.75%**.
CPI covers **retail** prices; WPI **first-point bulk sale**.

ne903d47ff41.s: Who established an inverse relationship between unemployment and wage inflation in 1958?
ne903d47ff41.x: A.W. Phillips established the inverse relationship between unemployment and wage inflation (the Phillips curve) in 1958.
xa: Lower unemployment comes with **higher inflation**.
India's curve is **flat** (IIP-CPI data **2012-2026**).
**92% informal workforce** → weak wage bargaining.

nae0ed7fe1df.s: According to Friedman, the long-run Phillips curve is:
nae0ed7fe1df.x: Friedman held the long-run Phillips curve to be vertical, implying no lasting trade-off between inflation and unemployment.
xa: India's Phillips curve is **flat**: **92% informal workforce**.
**Stagflation risk**: rate hikes cut output and jobs without lowering supply-driven inflation much.
IIP-CPI data **2012-2026** show little trade-off.

n4daa07c1fc5.s: Under the flexible inflation targeting framework, the inflation target retained for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031 is:
o: 2% core CPI with a band of +/- 2%
n4daa07c1fc5.x: The Centre, with the RBI, retained the target of 4% CPI-Combined inflation with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (i.e. 2-6%) for 2026-2031 by Gazette notification. WPI and core CPI are not the target index, and 6% is the upper limit of the band, not the target.
xs: **4% CPI-Combined** with a band of **± 2%** — option **(1)**.
Retained for **1 Apr 2026-31 Mar 2031** by **Gazette notification**.
**6%** is the upper band, not the target; WPI and core CPI are not the target index.
xa: **Sec 45ZA**: target set by the **Centre with RBI** every **5 years**.
June 2026: CPI **4.38%** — first breach of the **4%** target.
After FIT, average CPI fell from **6.8%** to **4.9%**.

nec853ce2240.s: The first breach of the 4% CPI inflation target in the new series occurred in
nec853ce2240.x: Headline CPI inflation reached 4.38% in June 2026, marking the first breach of the 4% target.
nec853ce2240.tq: Distinguish the first threshold breach from later higher readings.
xs: The first breach came in **June 2026**, at **4.38%** — option **(2)**.
Food inflation that month was **5.05%**.
xa: Headline CPI back **above 4%** in June-July 2026, **food-led**, core stable.
2025: headline **2.2%** — a **12-year low**.
Repo held at **5.25%** (Aug 2026).

n6969c2fed78.s: Deflation can initiate a deflationary spiral because it may lead to which sequence?
o: Postponed purchases, lower profits, higher unemployment and a heavier real debt burden
Immediate purchases, higher profits, lower unemployment and lighter real debt
Higher wages, greater demand, rising output and lower real debt
Higher inflation expectations, increased exports and full employment
n6969c2fed78.x: During deflation, consumers may postpone purchases, causing profits and production to fall; unemployment can rise and the real burden of debt increases.
n6969c2fed78.tq: Follow the causal chain from falling prices to demand, profits, employment and debt.
xs: **Postponed purchases, lower profits, higher unemployment and a heavier real debt burden** — option **(1)**.
This is the **deflationary spiral**.
xa: Deflation makes **purchasing power rise**.
⚠ **Deflation** = prices fall; **disinflation** = rate falls but stays positive.
**Reflation** = inflation returning after deflation → sign of recovery.

nf38d62f3fcb.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the distributional effects of inflation?
o: Debtors may gain as the real value of repayment falls
Creditors may lose as money received buys less
Fixed-income groups such as pensioners are automatically protected
Holders of real assets may gain from rising prices
nf38d62f3fcb.x: Fixed-income groups are generally vulnerable to inflation unless their incomes are adjusted; debtors and real-asset holders may gain while creditors may lose.
xa: Rule: **Debtors gain and creditors lose**.
CPI is used for **DA**.
**Savers** are also among the losers.

ne3b4032190f.s: Which explanation was given for WPI inflation being far above CPI inflation in June and July 2026?
o: The inclusion of services in the WPI basket
Higher fuel costs associated with the West Asia conflict
A change in the CPI base year alone
A sharp fall in manufactured-goods prices due to domestic oversupply
ne3b4032190f.x: WPI inflation was 9.87% in June and 9.78% in July 2026, far above CPI inflation mainly because of fuel costs associated with the West Asia conflict.
ne3b4032190f.tq: Link the observed divergence between indices to the stated sector-specific cause.
xs: WPI ran far above CPI because of **higher fuel costs from the West Asia conflict** — option **(2)**.
WPI covers **no services**, so option (1) is wrong.
xa: WPI rose to a **38-month high of 3.88%** (Mar 2026).
**Cost-push** example: **West Asia oil shock 2026**.

n9de3b0a4505.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about supply-side measures against food inflation?
o: NCCF and NAFED released onion from the Price Stabilisation Fund buffer
Bharat Atta, Rice and Dal are sold through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar
Pulses and onions are held in the Price Stabilisation Fund buffer
Under OMSS (Domestic), FCI sells pulses and onions at fixed prices
n9de3b0a4505.x: Under OMSS, FCI sells wheat and rice; pulses and onions belong to the PSF buffer.
xa: **Price Stabilisation Fund** buffer holds **pulses and onions**.
**Bharat Chana Dal** from **July 2023** at **₹60/kg**.
Onion export duty **halved to 20%** on **13 Sep 2024**.

n73f43073681.s: The main limitation of the repo rate in controlling inflation is that it:
o: Cannot directly resolve supply shocks such as onion or crude-oil price spikes
Can be changed only by the Union Government
Acts only on the supply side
n73f43073681.x: The repo rate works on aggregate demand and liquidity, so it cannot directly remove supply shocks like onion or crude-oil price rises.
xa: **Stagflation risk**: rate hikes cut output and jobs without lowering supply-driven inflation much.
Supply-side tools: **OMSS**, **PSF** buffer, **Bharat Atta**.
Criticism: targeting **headline CPI** when most shocks are **supply-side**.

n7570f03443e.s: The Reserve Bank of India issued Inflation-Indexed Bonds in:
n7570f03443e.x: The RBI issued Inflation-Indexed Bonds in 2013.
n7570f03443e.tq: Recall the introduction year using adjacent-year distractors.
xs: RBI issued **IIBs in 2013** — option **(3)**.
IIBs link **principal and/or interest** to an inflation index.
xa: Investor benefit: **real-return** hedge.
Govt benefit: savings moved **away from gold**.
⚠ Don't confuse with **April 2014** — RBI's adoption of **CPI (Combined)**.

nda9942020ee.s: Core inflation generally excludes the prices of:
nda9942020ee.x: Core inflation excludes volatile food and fuel prices to show the underlying, demand-side trend.
xa: Debate: target **headline or core**? Core is **stickier** and responds more to policy.
July 2026: core **< 3%** (excl. precious metals), unchanged.
May 2026: core **3.73%** vs food **4.85%** and headline **3.93%**.

n9893f16b287.s: Which of the following generally mitigates, rather than causes, supply-side inflation in India?
n9893f16b287.x: Monsoon failure, El Nino, costlier crude and rupee depreciation create supply shocks; better storage and distribution efficiency eases them.
xa: **West Asia conflict** pushed up fuel and input costs in **2026**.
Other factors: **MSP hikes**, **hoarding**, **expectations**.
Repo rate is a **demand-side** tool → cannot fix supply shocks.

n053a39b682b.s: Stagflation refers to inflation accompanied by:
o: A sustained rise in productive capacity
Slow growth and falling industrial output
n053a39b682b.x: Stagflation is inflation combined with falling industrial output and slow growth; higher government spending can add the inflationary pressure.
xa: ⚠ Key: **a and b only** (**APPSC-G2 2025**).
**Stagflation** = high inflation + stagnant growth/unemployment.
Rate hikes risk stagflation: they cut output and jobs without lowering **supply-driven** inflation much.

n04acf0e693c.s: Which of the following would generally reduce cost-push inflationary pressure in India?
o: A permanent fall in input costs
n04acf0e693c.x: A fall in input costs reduces cost-push pressure, whereas hoarding, MSP increases and inflation expectations add to inflation.
xa: **Supply shocks** dominate: monsoon, **El Niño**, crude, rupee depreciation.
**Demand side**: public expenditure, loose monetary policy, higher incomes.
Control: **Price Stabilisation Fund** buffer of pulses and onions.

nf8413a6c833.s: A rise in the GDP deflator, other things remaining the same, indicates a reduction in the
nf8413a6c833.x: An increase in the GDP deflator reflects a rise in the general price level and therefore reduces the purchasing power of money.
nf8413a6c833.tq: Translate the movement of a price index into its effect on money value.
xs: A rising **GDP deflator** means lower **purchasing power of money** — option **(1)** (**APPSC G2 2025**).
Inflation **lowers the purchasing power of money** (**APPSC 2025**).
xa: GDP deflator = **nominal GDP / real GDP x 100**; series base **2022-23**.
It is the **broadest** index — covers all goods and services produced.
Deflation, by contrast, makes purchasing power **rise**.

n37e45252ab8.s: The Phillips curve observed in India during 2012–2026 has been described as relatively flat primarily because:
o: The Reserve Bank of India fixes all wages
The formal workforce has complete wage flexibility
Around 92% of workers are informal and have weak wage-bargaining power
Food prices are excluded from the CPI
n37e45252ab8.x: India’s relatively flat Phillips curve is linked to the large informal workforce, estimated at about 92%, whose weak wage-bargaining power prevents wages from responding strongly to output changes.
n37e45252ab8.tq: Link the observed macroeconomic outcome with its structural cause.
xs: India's curve is flat because **~92% of workers are informal** with **weak wage-bargaining** — option **(3)**.
Wages **do not rise with output**; IIP-CPI data (**2012-2026**) show little trade-off.
xa: **A.W. Phillips (1958)**: inverse unemployment–inflation relation.
**Friedman**: long run vertical, no lasting trade-off.
**Stagflation risk** from rate hikes on supply-driven inflation.

na79eb6c731a.s: Under the RBI Act, 1934 (amended 2016), which Section requires a report when the inflation band is breached for three consecutive quarters?
na79eb6c731a.x: Section 45ZN requires the report; Section 45ZA deals with target-setting and Section 45ZB with the MPC.
xa: 45ZN was **first invoked in 2022**.
**RBI Act amended 2016** → MPC, statutory **flexible inflation targeting**.
Target **4% ± 2%** retained for **1 Apr 2026-31 Mar 2031**.

n65a4ac589a9.s: India's CPI inflation in 2025 was 2.2%, a ____ low.
n65a4ac589a9.x: CPI inflation of 2.2% in 2025 was a 12-year low.
xa: The **2025** order was **Core > Headline > Food**.
**Oct 2025**: **0.3%** → lowest in the 2012 series.
CPI fell from **6.7% (FY23)** to **1.7%** (Apr-Dec FY26).

n6de20273884.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the State-level Price Monitoring Committee is headed by the:
n6de20273884.x: The Chief Secretary heads AP's State-level Price Monitoring Committee; the DES monitors 8 essential commodities daily.
xa: AP retail inflation **4.9% (May 2026)** vs India **3.9%**.
AP has put inflation on its **"Needs Attention"** list.

ndee9fbcd95a.s: A payment made for a specific service, involving quid pro quo, is called a:
ndee9fbcd95a.x: A fee is paid for a specific service and involves quid pro quo; a tax has no direct quid pro quo.
xa: **Surcharge**: extra charge on tax payable; **not shared with States** (**Art. 271**).
Federal grievance: cesses and surcharges are **outside the divisible pool**.
Example cess: **Clean Energy Cess** on coal (**Finance Act 2010**).

n1c3e0f28628.s: Under Article 271 of the Constitution, surcharge proceeds are treated as follows:
o: They are compulsorily shared with States through the divisible pool
They are collected only by States
They are transferred exclusively to local bodies
They are retained by the Centre and are not shared with States
n1c3e0f28628.x: Surcharges under Article 271 are retained by the Centre and are not shared with States. Cesses are also outside the divisible pool.
n1c3e0f28628.tq: Recall the constitutional treatment of a specific revenue instrument.
xs: Under **Art. 271**, surcharges are **retained by the Centre and not shared with States** — option **(4)**.
Like cesses, they lie **outside the divisible pool** — a **federal grievance**.
xa: A surcharge is a **% of tax**, usually **permanent**.
**80th Amendment, 2000**: Union taxes shared with States on **FC** advice (effective **1 April 1996**).
**Article 265**: no tax except by **authority of law**.

nindian-economy-44-7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Wealth tax was a direct tax on net wealth, abolished in 2015
Capital gains tax is a direct tax on profit from selling a capital asset
Gift tax was a direct tax on property received without consideration
Customs duty is a direct tax on imports and exports
nindian-economy-44-7.x: Customs duty is an indirect tax on imports and exports.
n: Wealth Tax is an example of a direct tax. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 64-66]
Capital Gains Tax is an example of a direct tax. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 64-66]
Gift Tax is an example of a direct tax. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 64-66]
Customs Duty is an example of an indirect tax. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 64-66]
xa: Wealth, gift and estate duty were "**paper taxes**" — never yielded much revenue.
**STT** (from **1 Oct 2004**) is a **direct** tax though collected by the exchange.
Wealth tax dates from **1957**.

nindian-economy-44-5.s: A tax whose rate rises with income at first and then becomes flat is called:
nindian-economy-44-5.x: A degressive tax rate rises initially and then levels off; a proportional tax has one rate for all.
n: A regressive tax has a relative burden that tends to be higher on lower-income groups. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 64-66]
A proportional tax has the same tax rate regardless of income level. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 64-66]
A degressive tax rate initially rises with income and then becomes flat. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 64-66]
xa: **Progressive:** **average tax burden increases with income** — e.g. **income tax**.
Regressive examples: **excise**, **customs**, **GST on essentials**.
India: **progressive direct taxes** + **regressive indirect taxes**.

nindian-economy-44-6.s: Under a progressive tax, as income rises the average tax burden:
o: First rises and then becomes flat
nindian-economy-44-6.x: Higher income slabs are taxed at higher marginal rates, so the average tax burden increases with income.
n: A progressive tax has an average tax burden that increases with income. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 64-66]
xa: Progressive tax follows the "**ability to pay**" principle — e.g. **income tax**.
**Proportional:** **same rate** at all incomes; **degressive:** rises then **becomes flat**.
Income up to **₹12 lakh** is tax-free under the new regime.

n98351fe0b9d.s: The 80th Constitutional Amendment, 2000, on sharing Union taxes with States, took effect from:
n98351fe0b9d.x: The 80th Amendment was made in 2000 but took effect from 1 April 1996.
xa: Other Union taxes: **non-agricultural income tax**, **Union excise**, **CGST/IGST**.
**Cesses** and **surcharges** are not shared with States.
Residuary taxing power: **Parliament** (gift, wealth, expenditure taxes).

n668cea04241.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law?
n668cea04241.x: Article 265 establishes the constitutional requirement that every levy and collection of tax must have the authority of law.
n668cea04241.tq: Recall the exact constitutional Article associated with a taxation principle.
xs: **Article 265**: **no tax levied or collected except by authority of law** — option **(2)**.
**Art. 271** covers surcharges; **Art. 276** covers profession tax.
xa: A tax is a **pecuniary burden imposed by legislative authority** (**APPSC 2023**).
Taxing entries: **Union List 15, State List 20, Concurrent List 3**.
**80th Amendment, 2000**: sharing of Union taxes on FC advice.

nbda006464c4.s: Agricultural income tax can constitutionally be levied only by the States under which entry?
nbda006464c4.x: Agricultural income tax is assigned to the States under Entry 46 of the State List.
nbda006464c4.tq: Identify the correct legislative entry rather than the general tax category.
xs: Agricultural income tax is levied **only by States** under **State List Entry 46** — option **(1)**.
Agricultural income is **exempt** under the **Income-tax Act (Sec 10(1))**.
xa: **Nursery saplings** = agricultural income; **poultry/dairy** are not.
Union income tax covers only **non-agricultural** income.
Profession tax is also a **State levy** (**Art. 276**).

ndf557ba1012.s: GST was introduced in India with effect from:
ndf557ba1012.x: GST, an indirect tax on the supply of goods and services, came into effect on 1 July 2017.
ndf557ba1012.tq: Discriminate among the nearby dates associated with tax reforms and financial measures.
xs: **GST** came into effect on **1 July 2017** — option **(4)**.
It is an **indirect** tax on the **supply** of goods or services.
**1 Oct 2004** is **STT**; **1 April 1996** is the effective date of the **80th Amendment**.
xa: GST subsumed **service tax** and largely **sales tax/VAT**.
⚠ **1986** MODVAT → **2000** CENVAT → **2003** Haryana VAT → **2005** State VAT → **2017** GST.
Indirect tax buoyancy only **0.3** in 2026-27 BE — GST not keeping pace with GDP.

n9162e99b81f.s: An additional charge levied on the tax payable is called a:
n9162e99b81f.x: A surcharge is an additional charge on tax payable, so none is due when no tax is due; a cess is imposed for a specific purpose.
xa: A surcharge is **usually permanent**; a cess ends when its purpose is met.
Both are **not shared with States**.
A **fee** involves **quid pro quo**; a **tax** does not.

na706f6f3395.s: Corporation tax in India is levied on:
na706f6f3395.x: The base of corporation tax is the net profit of companies.
xa: STT applies from **1 Oct 2004** on securities traded on exchanges.
Corporation tax: **22%** base rate, effective **~25.17%**.
**GST** from **1 July 2017**.

nb6f3f26a268.s: In which year was wealth tax introduced in India?
nb6f3f26a268.x: Wealth tax on net wealth was introduced in 1957 and abolished in 2015.
xa: **Estate duty** and **gift tax** are direct taxes now abolished.
PYQ: income, corporate and wealth-type taxes → **"all of the above"** are direct (**APPSC 2021**).
Residuary power covers **gift, wealth, expenditure taxes**.

n77c19fb9bd5.s: Moving the burden of a tax forward to consumers or backward to suppliers is called:
n77c19fb9bd5.x: This is tax shifting; impact is on whom the tax is first imposed and incidence is on whom it finally falls.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes **reverse** impact and incidence.
Direct tax: impact and incidence on the **same person**.
Indirect tax: burden **shifted to consumer** through price.

n5bcb41dcf26.s: Which kind of taxes is generally progressive in nature?
n5bcb41dcf26.x: Direct taxes are generally progressive, while indirect taxes may be regressive; a higher direct-tax share improves progressivity.
xa: Direct tax share: **61.2%** in **2026-27 BE**.
Income tax is the **largest tax** in 2026-27 BE.
Regressive examples: **excise, customs, GST on essentials**.

n4f85112978c.s: Which tax was the single largest source of tax revenue in the Budget Estimate for 2026–27?
n4f85112978c.x: Income tax was identified as the single largest tax source in the 2026–27 Budget Estimate.
n4f85112978c.tq: Distinguish the leading current source from other major tax heads.
xs: **Income tax** is the single largest tax source in **2026-27 BE** — option **(1)**.
It is **21%** of the Centre's rupee, ahead of **corporation tax (18%)**.
**Wealth tax** was abolished in **2015**; **customs** is only **4%**, **Union excise** **6%**.
xa: ⚠ "Largest source of Centre's receipts" = **borrowings (24%)**; "largest tax" = **income tax**.
GST and other taxes: **15%**.
Non-tax revenue: **10%**.

nd3ddb89d5a4.s: According to the Budget 2026–27 presentation of the Centre’s rupee, which is the largest single source of the Centre’s receipts?
nd3ddb89d5a4.x: Borrowings and other liabilities constitute 24% of the Centre’s rupee and are the largest overall source. Income tax is the largest individual tax source at 21%.
nd3ddb89d5a4.tq: Distinguish the largest overall receipt source from the largest tax source.
xs: **Borrowings and other liabilities** are the largest source — **24%** — option **(2)**.
**Income tax (21%)** is the largest **tax**; **corporation tax** is **18%**; **non-tax revenue** **10%**.
xa: GST and other taxes **15%**; Union excise **6%**; customs **4%**.
Non-debt capital receipts: **2%**.
Non-tax revenue (BE 2026-27): **₹2,80,434 crore**.

n501a411024f.s: Which of the following correctly represents the leading components of Andhra Pradesh’s own-tax revenue in 2024–25?
n501a411024f.x: In Andhra Pradesh, SGST contributed 38% and State Excise contributed 22% of own-tax revenue in 2024–25.
n501a411024f.tq: Compare the two leading State revenue components without reversing their shares.
xs: AP (**2024-25 RE**): **SGST 38%** and **State Excise 22%** — option **(2)**.
SGST **₹36,296 crore** of own tax revenue **₹94,967 crore**; State Excise **₹21,300 crore**.
xa: States overall: own tax revenue ≈ **50%** of revenue receipts (FY25).
Share in central taxes **~32%**.
States' own tax revenue ≈ **7% of GSDP**.

n924f654c636.s: The tax-GDP ratio is total tax revenue divided by:
n924f654c636.x: The tax-GDP ratio uses nominal GDP; a low ratio may reflect a large informal sector or high evasion.
xa: Tax-GDP is a yardstick of **fiscal capacity**.
**World Bank** benchmark: **15%** = tipping point for sustainable growth.
Evasion: ~**4.3%** of tax revenue lost yearly.

n8a78c4d36ca.s: The World Bank regards a tax-GDP ratio of ____ as a tipping point for sustainable growth.
n8a78c4d36ca.x: The World Bank benchmark is 15 per cent; India's 2001-2022 average was 16.36 per cent.
xa: Combined (Centre + States): **~19.6%** (**Bank of Baroda** report).
Centre: **~11.5%** of GDP post-pandemic (FY22-FY25).
Evasion: ~**4.3%** of tax revenue lost yearly.

n8004fa49c82.s: The gross tax revenue of the Centre was approximately what percentage of GDP in 2019–20?
n8004fa49c82.x: The Centre's gross tax revenue was about 9.9 per cent of GDP in 2019–20.
n8004fa49c82.tq: Distinguish the earlier reference-year figure from later tax-GDP estimates.
xs: Centre's gross tax revenue was **9.9 per cent** of GDP in **2019-20** — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2021**, ES 2021-22).
**11.2%** is FY24 and **~11.5%** the post-pandemic average (FY22-FY25).
xa: Some notes quote **~11.7%** (2024).
Combined (Centre + States): **~19.6%**.
Centre's GTR grew only **3.7%** in **Q1 2026-27**.

nbcc7555363d.s: A falling tax-GDP ratio, other things remaining unchanged, implies that:
o: Tax revenue is growing slower than GDP, weakening fiscal space and increasing borrowing requirements
Tax revenue is growing faster than GDP and fiscal space is expanding
Tax buoyancy is necessarily above one
nbcc7555363d.x: A falling ratio indicates that tax revenue is growing more slowly than GDP. This weakens fiscal space and may lead to greater borrowing.
nbcc7555363d.tq: Translate the direction of a ratio into its fiscal consequence.
xs: A falling ratio means **tax revenue grows slower than GDP** → **weaker fiscal space, more borrowing** — option **(2)**.
This corresponds to **buoyancy < 1**, not above one.
xa: Centre's gross tax buoyancy **0.8** in **2026-27 BE**.
**ES 2025-26** credits buoyant revenues → deficit **4.4%** of GDP in FY26.
Low ratio = large informal sector or high evasion.

n67f267bfcc2.s: The response of tax revenue to GDP, excluding discretionary changes in rates and base, is called:
n67f267bfcc2.x: Tax elasticity excludes discretionary changes, while tax buoyancy includes them.
xa: Centre's gross tax buoyancy: **0.8 in 2026-27 (BE)** — direct **1.1** vs indirect **0.3**.
**Laffer curve:** inverted-U, popularised by **Arthur Laffer (1974)**.
**Base widening** (more taxpayers, fewer exemptions) = the **Chelliah** approach.

nindian-economy-44-8.s: Which of the following is an indirect tax?
nindian-economy-44-8.x: VAT is an indirect tax passed on to buyers, like excise, service tax and sales tax.
n: Excise Duty is an example of an indirect tax. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 64-66]
Service Tax is an example of an indirect tax. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 64-66]
Sales Tax is an example of an indirect tax. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 64-66]
VAT is an example of an indirect tax. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 64-66]
xa: **Service tax** and **sales tax / VAT** are now largely in **GST**.
Taxable events: excise → **manufacture**; VAT → **sale**; service tax → **provision of service**.

n2fbd9ef8b22.s: The Chelliah approach to tax reform primarily favours:
o: Abolition of all tax exemptions without widening the base
Higher tax rates with a narrow base
Lower tax rates with a broader tax base
n2fbd9ef8b22.x: The Chelliah approach favours base widening through more taxpayers and fewer exemptions, together with lower rates rather than rate hikes.
n2fbd9ef8b22.tq: Identify the reform principle expressed through the rates-versus-base comparison.
xs: The **Chelliah approach** favours **lower rates with a broader base** — option **(4)**.
**Base widening**: more taxpayers, **fewer exemptions**, preferred to **rate hikes**.
xa: **Raja J. Chelliah** headed the **Tax Reforms Committee (1991-93)**.
**Service tax** came in **1994-95** on the Chelliah Committee's advice.
A **simpler tax system** removes **deadweight costs** (**APPSC-G1 2024** A-R).

n22ff1cf44a4.s: Who chaired the Indirect Taxation Enquiry Committee that suggested the introduction of VAT in India?
n22ff1cf44a4.x: The Indirect Taxation Enquiry Committee headed by L.K. Jha in 1976 suggested VAT for India.
n22ff1cf44a4.tq: Match the chairperson with the specific tax-reform recommendation.
xs: **L.K. Jha** chaired the **Indirect Taxation Enquiry Committee (1976)**, which suggested **VAT** — option **(2)**.
**Raja J. Chelliah** led the Tax Reforms Committee (**1991-93**); **Parthasarathi Shome** (**2012**) dealt with **GAAR**.
xa: L.K. Jha's VAT-at-manufacturing idea → **MODVAT** (**1 March 1986**).
**VAT** was first implemented in **France, 1954**.
**CENVAT** replaced MODVAT on **1 April 2000**; **Haryana** first State VAT (**1 April 2003**).

n8f2f6c37195.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Parthasarathi Shome?
o: The Shome Committee (2012) dealt with GAAR
He recommended VAT at the manufacturing stage, leading to MODVAT
The Shome Committee advised scrapping retrospective tax
The Tax Administration Reform Commission (2013) was headed by him
n8f2f6c37195.x: VAT at the manufacturing stage (MODVAT) came from the L.K. Jha Committee (1976), not Shome.
xa: **Raja J. Chelliah** (Tax Reforms Committee, **1991-93**): **lower rates, broader base, fewer exemptions**.
**MODVAT** began on **1 March 1986**; replaced by **CENVAT** on **1 April 2000**.
The **Chelliah approach** (lower rates, broader base) = **base widening**.

nfd7129535d1.s: A reduction in direct taxes is most likely to produce which immediate effect, other things remaining equal?
o: Lower disposable income and lower consumption demand
Lower disposable income but higher tax buoyancy by definition
Higher disposable income and higher consumption demand
nfd7129535d1.x: A cut in direct taxes raises disposable income, which can increase consumption demand. It may also support savings and investment.
nfd7129535d1.tq: Follow the causal chain from a tax change to disposable income and demand.
xs: A direct tax cut gives **higher disposable income and higher consumption demand** — option **(4)** (**APPSC 2018**).
It also lifts **savings** and **investment**.
xa: Example: income up to **₹12 lakh** tax-free under the new regime.
Caution: personal income tax revenue growth in 2025-26 only **0.037%** after rate rationalisation.
Direct tax buoyancy **1.1** (2026-27 BE).

ne6aff88fee7.s: Under the new tax regime from Budget 2025-26, income in the slab of ₹20–24 lakh and income above ₹24 lakh are taxed respectively at:
ne6aff88fee7.x: The ₹20–24 lakh slab carries a 25% rate, while income above ₹24 lakh is taxed at 30%.
ne6aff88fee7.tq: Test the upper-end slabs separately, where rate shifts are commonly confused.
xs: Under the new regime, **₹20-24 lakh is taxed at 25%** and **above ₹24 lakh at 30%** — option **(2)**.
**30%** is the top rate; no slab carries **35%**, ruling out options (1) and (3).
**20%** belongs to the **₹16-20 lakh** slab, so option (4) is one slab too low.
xa: In the **2020-21** first new regime, the **30%** rate started **above 15 lakh**.
**Budget 2026-27** made **no change** in slabs.

n4d5c3c384c1.s: Under the first new optional income-tax regime of Budget 2020-21, income in the slab of Rs 5 lakh to Rs 7.5 lakh was taxed at:
n4d5c3c384c1.x: In the 2020-21 new regime, 0-2.5 lakh was nil, 2.5-5 lakh 5%, 5-7.5 lakh 10% (APPSC 2019 key), 7.5-10 lakh 15% and 10-12.5 lakh 20%. So 5%, 15% and 20% belong to other slabs.
n4d5c3c384c1.tq: 2020-21 regime: steps of 2.5 lakh, rate +5% each.
xs: In the **Budget 2020-21** first new optional regime, **₹5-7.5 lakh** was taxed at **10%** — option **(2)** (APPSC 2019).
xa: The rest of that ladder: **0-2.5 lakh nil**; **12.5-15 lakh 25%**; **above 15 lakh 30%**.
**Budget 2023-24** raised the nil slab to **3 lakh** and cut the top surcharge **37% → 25%**.
From **Budget 2025-26**, **₹8-12 lakh** is the **10%** slab.

nd2de29b546f.s: In a PAN, which character shows the holder type ('P' for individual, 'C' for company)?
nd2de29b546f.x: PAN is a 10-character alphanumeric identifier whose 4th character shows the holder type.
xa: **AIS** (Annual Information Statement) shows all reported transactions; widens **Form 26AS** data for pre-filled returns (**2021**).
**Budget 2026-27**: resident buyers of NRI property can deduct TDS using **PAN instead of TAN**.

n2c451c235da.s: Under FAST-DS 2026, a 30% tax plus an equal additional amount gives an effective burden of:
n2c451c235da.x: 30% tax plus an equal additional amount makes 60%; the threshold is ₹1 crore, or ₹5 crore for previously taxed but unreported assets.
xa: Full form: **Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers - Disclosure Scheme**; announced in **Budget 2026-27**.
In force **16 Aug 2026**; declarations till **31 Dec 2026**.
The ₹5 crore category carries a **₹1 lakh** fee; valuation at **FMV as on 31 Mar 2026**.
Benefit: immunity from penalty/prosecution under the **Black Money Act, 2015**.

n9f8d8760e2e.s: India's default, exemption-free new income-tax regime is provided under Section:
n9f8d8760e2e.x: Section 115BAC provides the default exemption-free new regime; the old regime with deductions remains optional.
xa: New-regime slabs date from **Budget 2025-26** and were **unchanged in Budget 2026-27**.
The first new optional regime came in **Budget 2020-21** (0-2.5 lakh nil).
Income up to **₹12 lakh** is tax-free under the new regime via the **Section 87A rebate**.

n94f6a63caba.s: Budget 2023-24 cut the highest surcharge under the new regime, for income above ₹2 crore, from 37% to:
n94f6a63caba.x: Budget 2023-24 reduced the highest surcharge from 37% to 25% for income above ₹2 crore under the new regime.
xa: **Budget 2020-21** had introduced the **first new optional regime** with a ₹2.5 lakh nil slab.
**Budget 2025-26** made income up to **₹12 lakh** tax-free.

n2f763a74a22.s: Income tax was first introduced in India in 1860 by:
n2f763a74a22.x: James Wilson, the first Finance Member, introduced income tax in India in 1860. Dalhousie and Ripon were Governors-General/Viceroys known for other reforms, and Kaldor advised on tax reform in 1956.
xs: Income tax was first introduced in India in **1860** by **James Wilson** — option **(2)**.
**Nicholas Kaldor** came much later: his **1956** advice led to **wealth tax (1957)**, **expenditure tax (1958)** and **gift tax (1958)**.
xa: The **Income Tax Department** was created under the **1922 Act**.
**Expenditure tax (1958)** was the first introduced in independent India, by FM **T.T. Krishnamachari** (APPSC 2019).
The **Income-tax Act, 1961** (effective **1 April 1962**) was replaced by the **Income-tax Act, 2025** from **1 April 2026**.

n3ebcd69faf3.s: Minimum Alternate Tax is primarily imposed on companies which:
o: Have no book profits but earn only agricultural income
Are registered as unlisted start-ups receiving share premium
Show book profits but otherwise pay little or no regular income tax
n3ebcd69faf3.x: MAT taxes so-called zero-tax companies on their book profits, ensuring a minimum tax liability despite low or nil regular income-tax liability.
n3ebcd69faf3.tq: Apply the purpose of the tax to a company’s accounting and regular-tax situation.
xs: MAT targets companies that **show book profits but pay little or no regular income tax** — option **(4)**.
It taxes so-called **"zero-tax companies"** on **book profits** at **15%**.
Share premium of unlisted start-ups was **angel tax**; dividends were hit by **DDT**; rural agricultural income is **exempt**.
xa: MAT was introduced in the **1986-87 Budget** at **15.75%**.
Companies opting into the **2019 concessional rates** (115BAA/115BAB) are **outside MAT**.
**Budget 2026-27**: MAT **14%**, a **final tax**; old credit set off up to **1/4** of liability.

n9063576ecd2.s: The Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019 cut the tax rate for domestic companies from 30% to:
n9063576ecd2.x: The 2019 Act cut the rate to 22% and set 15% for new manufacturing companies; MAT does not apply to those opting in.
xa: The cuts were announced in **Sept 2019** by Ordinance, then enacted as the **Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019**.
ES 2025-26 calls this the **first pillar** of tax reform.

n9e85eb4b28f.s: Under Section 115BAB, new manufacturing companies incorporated after 1 October 2019 pay a base tax rate of:
n9e85eb4b28f.x: Section 115BAB gives a 15% rate (effective about 17.01%); Section 115BAA gives 22% (effective about 25.17%).
xa: ⚠ **115BAA = 22%** (existing) vs **115BAB = 15%** (new manufacturing).
Companies opting into these rates are **outside MAT**.
Route: **Taxation Laws (Amendment) Ordinance** (Sept 2019) → **Act, 2019**.

n35a8b958614.s: Expenditure tax was introduced in 1958, on Nicholas Kaldor's advice, by Finance Minister:
n35a8b958614.x: Finance Minister T.T. Krishnamachari introduced the expenditure tax in 1958 on Kaldor's advice.
xa: Expenditure tax 1958 was the **first introduced in independent India** (APPSC 2019); it has since been **abolished**.
⚠ **Wealth tax 1957** - **expenditure tax 1958** - **gift tax April 1958** = all **Kaldor** (committee **1956**).
**Gift tax** was abolished in **Oct 1998**; **wealth tax** in **2015**.

n4ad8e5805c4.s: Which body's 2004 work related to implementation of the FRBM framework and proposed a GST roadmap?
n4ad8e5805c4.x: The Kelkar Task Force covered direct and indirect taxes in 2002 and FRBM implementation with a GST roadmap in 2004.
xa: It is credited with the **GST roadmap**.
**Parthasarathi Shome (2012)** – GAAR review; **R.V. Easwar (2015-16)** – simplifying the I-T Act.
**Akhilesh Ranjan** headed the new-**DTC** task force (report **2019**).

n038d988c6c5.s: The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Yojana (2016), introduced after demonetisation, carried a total levy of:
n038d988c6c5.x: PMGKY 2016 carried a 50% levy; the 1997 scheme was VDIS, not PMGKY.
xa: **IDS 2016** (1 June - 30 Sept 2016) carried a **45%** levy.
**FAST-DS 2026**: **30% tax + equal additional amount = effective 60%**.
**Vivad se Vishwas**: Act **2020**, second scheme **2024**.

nf07ce357db5.s: Vivad se Vishwas primarily seeks to achieve which of the following?
o: Introduction of a global minimum corporate tax
nf07ce357db5.x: Vivad se Vishwas is a direct-tax dispute resolution scheme under the Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas Act, 2020; a second scheme was introduced in 2024.
nf07ce357db5.tq: Match the scheme with its precise statutory purpose.
xs: **Vivad se Vishwas** aims at **settling pending direct-tax disputes** — option **(1)**.
It rests on the **Direct Tax Vivad se Vishwas Act, 2020**; a second scheme came in **2024**.
Foreign-asset disclosure is **FAST-DS 2026**; the **15%** global minimum tax is **OECD Pillar Two**.
xa: **Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021** withdrew retrospective demands (**Vodafone, Cairn**).
**Expenditure tax** (1958) has been **abolished**.

nc8f00ac7608.s: Income tax is generally classified as which of the following?
nc8f00ac7608.x: Income tax is a direct tax and is classically progressive because the rate generally rises with taxable income.
nc8f00ac7608.tq: Discriminate between the two independent classifications—directness and progressivity.
xs: Income tax is a **progressive direct tax** — option **(4)**.
The notes call income tax the **classic progressive tax**: its rate rises with income, as the **Nil → 30%** slab ladder shows.
It is a **tax** receipt, not non-tax revenue, and **direct**, not indirect — ruling out options (1)-(3).
xa: Income tax was **first levied in 1860** by **James Wilson**.
The **Income Tax Department** was created under the **1922 Act**.
The apex body for direct taxes is the **CBDT**, a statutory body under the **Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963**.

nadfc361909d.s: The 1992 revision of wealth tax was based on the recommendations of the:
nadfc361909d.x: The Raja Chelliah Committee advocated lower rates, a broader base and fewer exemptions and formed the basis of the 1992 wealth-tax revision.
xa: The **Raja J. Chelliah Tax Reforms Committee** dates to **1991** (the 1990s).
**Kelkar Task Force (2002)** later took up rationalisation of exemptions and simplification.
**Wealth tax** itself was introduced in **1957** and abolished in **2015**.

n5cdaf6c4758.s: Project Insight, launched in 2017 and made operational in 2019, is associated with:
o: Artificial intelligence and data analytics for tax compliance
Issuance of corporate bonds by SEBI
Digitisation of land records for State Governments
n5cdaf6c4758.x: Project Insight uses artificial intelligence and data analytics to improve tax compliance.
n5cdaf6c4758.tq: Match the named project with its specific technology and administrative objective.
xs: **Project Insight** uses **AI/data analytics for tax compliance** — option **(2)**.
It was **launched 2017** and **operational 2019**.
xa: **Faceless assessment** + **Taxpayers' Charter**: **13 August 2020**; faceless appeals **Sept 2020**.
**AIS** (**2021**) widens Form 26AS data for pre-filled returns.
**CBDT**, in the **Department of Revenue**, is the cadre controller of the **IRS**.

nbcaaad1f1c1.s: As a general rule, a capital asset held for up to ____ months is a short-term capital asset.
nbcaaad1f1c1.x: Generally, an asset held up to 24 months is short-term; rural agricultural land is not a capital asset at all.
xa: **Indexation** uses the **Cost Inflation Index**, notified by **CBDT**, base year **2001-02**.
From **Budget 2026-27**, **share buybacks** are taxed as capital gains.

n3d3bf910f9e.s: Indexation for computing capital gains uses which of the following?
o: Wholesale Price Index notified by the RBI, with base year 1991-92
Cost Inflation Index notified by CBDT, with base year 2001-02
Consumer Price Index notified by SEBI, with base year 2011-12
GDP deflator notified by the Finance Commission, with base year 2004-05
n3d3bf910f9e.x: Indexation uses the Cost Inflation Index notified by the CBDT, and the stated base year is 2001-02.
n3d3bf910f9e.tq: Match the index, notifying authority and base year as one precise combination.
