xs: Indexation uses the **Cost Inflation Index**, notified by **CBDT**, base year **2001-02** — option **(2)** (APPSC 2019).
The notifying body is **CBDT** — not RBI, SEBI or the Finance Commission.
xa: **CBDT** is a statutory body under the **Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963**.
**LTCG** rate is **12.5%**; **short-term** = held up to **24 months**.
**Rural agricultural land** is **not a capital asset**.

n291400a471e.s: 'Angel tax', often called a tax on venture capital, refers to tax on:
o: Share premium received by unlisted start-ups in excess of fair value
Capital gains on sale of rural agricultural land
Interest earned by foreign investors on government securities
n291400a471e.x: Angel tax was the tax on excess share premium received by unlisted start-ups above fair value (APPSC 2019); introduced in 2012 and abolished in Budget 2024-25. Dividends were covered by DDT, rural agricultural land is not a capital asset, and G-Sec interest of FIIs was exempted in 2026.
n291400a471e.tq: Angel tax = excess share premium, unlisted start-ups.
xs: Angel tax is tax on **share premium received by unlisted start-ups in excess of fair value** — option **(2)** (APPSC 2019).
It was dubbed a **"tax on venture capital"** / angel capital.
Dividends were covered by **DDT**; **rural agricultural land** is not a capital asset; G-Sec interest of **FIIs** was exempted by the **2026** Bill.
xa: Angel tax was **introduced 2012** and **abolished in Budget 2024-25**.
**Equalisation levy**: **6%** on online advertising (2016); **2%** on e-commerce (2020, dropped 2024).
**OECD Pillar Two** sets a **15%** global minimum corporate tax for large MNEs.

n9e04f3f0d42.s: Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, which one of the following replaces the concepts of the Assessment Year and the Previous Year?
n9e04f3f0d42.x: The Act introduces a single 12-month ‘Tax Year’ beginning on 1 April, replacing the separate Assessment Year and Previous Year terminology.
n9e04f3f0d42.tq: Test the exact statutory term and distinguish it from plausible but non-official alternatives.
xs: The **Income-tax Act, 2025** replaces Assessment Year and Previous Year with a single **"Tax Year"** — option **(3)**.
The Tax Year is a **12-month FY from 1 April**.
xa: Other changes: **simpler language**; **obsolete provisions removed**.
The Act is **effective 1 April 2026**, replacing the **1961 Act** (effective **1 April 1962**).
**ICDS** merged into **Ind AS**; separate ICDS accounting dropped from **tax year 2027-28**.

n629629a8b67.s: Faceless assessment and the Taxpayers' Charter were launched on:
n629629a8b67.x: They were launched on 13 August 2020 under 'Transparent Taxation - Honouring the Honest'; faceless appeals followed in September 2020.
xa: **Project Insight**: launched **2017**, operational **2019**; AI/data analytics for compliance.
**CBDT** is the apex direct-tax body; the I-T Department has **18 regions**.

nff69e19080e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)?
o: It is the apex body for direct taxes
It is a statutory body under the Central Boards of Revenue Act, 1963
It is the cadre controller of the Indian Revenue Service
It is placed in the Department of Expenditure
nff69e19080e.x: CBDT is placed in the Department of Revenue, not the Department of Expenditure.
xa: The **Income Tax Department** has **18 regions**.
**CBDT** notifies the **Cost Inflation Index** (base **2001-02**).
**T.R. Rustagi** committee dealt with **restructuring of CBDT**.

n30827d25188.s: The Vodafone tax dispute led to which of the following developments?
o: A 50% levy under PMGKY after demonetisation
A retrospective amendment in 2012 relating to indirect transfers, followed by withdrawal of retrospective demands in 2021
A 2016 levy on online advertising followed by its abolition in 2025
A 15% global minimum corporate tax under OECD Pillar Two
n30827d25188.x: Following the Supreme Court's 2012 Vodafone ruling, indirect transfers were taxed retrospectively through the Finance Act, 2012. The Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 withdrew the retrospective demands involving Vodafone and Cairn.
n30827d25188.tq: Track the legal sequence rather than confusing it with a digital levy.
xs: Vodafone led to a **retrospective amendment in 2012** on **indirect transfers**, and the **withdrawal of retrospective demands in 2021** — option **(2)**.
After the **Vodafone** ruling (SC, **2012**), the **Finance Act 2012** taxed indirect transfers retrospectively.
The **Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021** withdrew the demands (**Vodafone, Cairn**).
The **50%** levy is **PMGKY**; the **2016** advertising levy is the **equalisation levy**; **15%** global minimum tax is **OECD Pillar Two**.
xa: The **Shome Committee** (**2012**) advised scrapping retrospective tax.
Critics say **retrospective taxation hurt investor confidence**.
**GAAR can override tax treaties** (Jan 2026).

n30f320eb569.s: The Revenue Neutral Rate for GST was worked out by the committee headed by:
n30f320eb569.x: The Arvind Subramanian committee (2015) worked out the RNR, the rate that keeps revenue equal to the pre-GST level.
xa: The committee put the RNR at **~15-15.5%** and the standard rate at **17-18%**.
⚠ Some notes date the committee **2018** instead of 2015.
GST 2.0 now has just **5%** (merit) and **18%** (standard) + **40%** (sin).

n6b8df9e55c3.s: Which State was the first to ratify the 101st Constitutional Amendment?
n6b8df9e55c3.x: Assam was the first State to ratify the 101st Constitutional Amendment, which required ratification by the States.
n6b8df9e55c3.tq: Use the distinctive first-ratifier fact rather than confusing it with a major GST-consuming State.
xs: **Assam** was the **first State to ratify** the GST amendment (**12 Aug 2016**) — option **(1)**.
Ratification by **at least half the State legislatures** was needed, as it changed federal provisions.
xa: ⚠ Trap: some notes say Assam was "first to implement GST" — it was first to **ratify**.
Presidential assent followed on **8 Sep 2016**.
GST rolled out on **1 July 2017**.

n92f305e161c.s: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act received Presidential assent on:
n92f305e161c.x: Presidential assent came on 8 September 2016; GST rolled out on 1 July 2017.
xa: The 122nd Bill became the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016**.
The **GST Council** was formed in **September 2016**.
The Empowered Committee roadmap dates to **2008**.

nbc7094f7be2.s: The Constitution (122nd Amendment) Bill, 2014 became the:
nbc7094f7be2.x: The 122nd Amendment Bill became the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016. The Bill number and the enacted Amendment Act number are different.
nbc7094f7be2.tq: Separate the Bill number from the number of the enacted Constitutional Amendment Act.
xs: The **122nd Amendment Bill** became the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016** — option **(2)**.
Bills and Acts are numbered separately; the **115th** was an earlier Bill (Mar **2011**) that **lapsed**.
xa: The Bill was tabled in **Dec 2014**; assent on **8 Sep 2016**.
The Act inserted **246A, 269A, 279A** and omitted **268A**.
⚠ Exam trap: **122nd (Bill)** vs **101st (Act)**.

nindian-economy-15-1.s: GST was implemented in India on which date?
nindian-economy-15-1.x: GST came into force on 1 July 2017, after the 101st Constitutional Amendment of 2016.
n: GST was implemented on 1 July 2017. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 19-22]
xs: **GST** was implemented on **1 July 2017** — option **(1)**.
It was introduced through the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016**.
It was rolled out at a **midnight session** of Parliament (**30 June/1 July 2017**).
xa: GST is a **multi-stage**, **destination-based** indirect tax; taxable event: **supply**.
Presidential assent to the Amendment: **8 Sep 2016**.
**Assam** was the **first State to ratify** (**12 Aug 2016**).

n14cfd7d42bf.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with inter-State GST?
n14cfd7d42bf.x: Article 269A concerns inter-State GST; 246A gives GST law-making power and 279A provides for the GST Council.
xa: ⚠ Council = **Article 279A**, not 269A (**APPSC G2 2025**).
Under 246A, **Parliament alone** legislates on **inter-State supply**.
Also amended: Arts. **248, 249, 250, 268, 269, 270, 271, 286, 366, 368** + Sixth and Seventh Schedules.

na8dfc9f0316.s: Under Article 246A, Parliament alone has the power to make laws concerning GST when the supply is:
o: Made by a local authority only
na8dfc9f0316.x: Article 246A gives Parliament and State Legislatures concurrent GST legislative power, but Parliament alone legislates in relation to inter-State supplies.
na8dfc9f0316.tq: Apply the constitutional division of legislative power to an inter-State supply.
xs: Under **Art. 246A**, **Parliament alone** makes GST laws on **inter-State** supply — option **(4)**.
For other supplies, **Parliament and State legislatures** both legislate (concurrent GST power).
xa: Only **Parliament** legislates on **IGST**.
**Art. 269A**: IGST levied by the Union, apportioned on Council advice.
**Mohit Minerals (2022)**: Parliament and States have **simultaneous power** to legislate on GST.

n089243b2cd4.x: The GST Council is formed by the President under Article 279A of the Constitution.
n089243b2cd4.tq: Ask which constitutional authority performs the formal constituting function.
xs: The **GST Council** is formed by the **President** (September **2016**) — option **(2)**.
It is a **constitutional body** under **Art. 279A**, not created by ordinary legislation.
xa: It was **never a statutory body** (APPSC G1 2024).
Chair: **Union Finance Minister**; first chair **Arun Jaitley**.
**55th** meeting: **21 Dec 2024**, Jaisalmer; GST 2.0 approved at the **56th** (3-4 Sep **2025**).

n233fb34da9b.s: A supplier pays tax on inputs and seeks to set it off against the tax payable on outward supplies. This facility is known as:
n233fb34da9b.x: Input Tax Credit allows tax paid on inputs to be set off against output tax. It helps prevent cascading of taxes.
n233fb34da9b.tq: Identify the mechanism from its practical business operation.
xs: Setting off input tax against output tax is **Input Tax Credit (ITC)** — option **(2)**.
**RCM** shifts liability to the recipient; **anti-profiteering** passes benefits to consumers; **destination principle** assigns revenue to the consuming State.
xa: ITC ends **cascading** (tax on tax); blocked-ITC rules apply.
**Zero-rated** supplies get a **full ITC refund**; nil-rated/exempt get none.
**E-invoicing** helps verify ITC and curb fake invoices.

n0b7acad945f.s: The principal purpose of e-invoicing is to:
o: Replace all GST returns with paper invoices
Digitally report invoices, curb fake invoices and verify input-tax credit
Set the GST Council’s voting weights
Determine the annual borrowing limit of States
n0b7acad945f.x: E-invoicing digitally reports invoices, helps curb fake invoices and supports verification of input-tax credit.
n0b7acad945f.tq: Connect the digital mechanism with its compliance objectives.
xs: **E-invoicing** means **digital reporting of invoices** to **curb fake invoices** and **verify ITC** — option **(2)**.
It works with **HSN/SAC codes**; it does not bring back paper invoices or touch Council voting or State borrowing.
xa: **E-way bill**: electronic document for moving goods worth **> ₹50,000**; valid **1 day per 200 km**.
**GSTN** does **ITC matching** and uses **AI tools**.
**Anti-profiteering (Sec 171)**: ITC benefits must reach consumers.

ne12dbf0a67b.s: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act inserted which Article relating to the GST Council?
ne12dbf0a67b.x: Article 279A provides for the GST Council; the same Amendment omitted Article 268A.
xa: It also inserted **246A** (GST law-making) and **269A** (IGST).
Presidential assent: **8 September 2016**.
⚠ Bill number **122nd** vs Act number **101st** is the classic trap.

n3647d559d1c.s: The GST constitutional amendment required ratification by at least:
n3647d559d1c.x: Since the amendment affected the federal distribution of powers, ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures was required.
n3647d559d1c.tq: Distinguish the constitutional ratification threshold from higher thresholds such as two-thirds or unanimity.
xs: Ratification by **at least half the State legislatures** was needed — option **(4)**.
Reason: it amended **federal provisions** of the Constitution.
xa: **Assam** ratified first (**12 Aug 2016**).
Presidential assent: **8 September 2016**.
The Act is the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016**.

na4302256ea7.s: The quorum of the GST Council is:
na4302256ea7.x: The GST Council's quorum is one-half of its total members.
xa: Centre's vote = **1/3** of votes cast; all States together = **2/3**.
Decisions need a **3/4 majority** of weighted votes of members present and voting.

na66be97febf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Union of India v. Mohit Minerals (2022)?
o: It held GST Council recommendations to be persuasive, not binding
It held that the GST Council is a statutory body
It recognised simultaneous power of Parliament and States to legislate on GST
It described India as a 'flexible federation'
na66be97febf.x: The GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A and was never statutory.
xa: APPSC G1 2024 tested "statutory then constitutional" — that statement is **false**.
The Council is an institution of **cooperative federalism**.

n42e08c955ed.s: Which of the following is outside the current GST levy?
n42e08c955ed.x: Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is outside GST, as are electricity, stamp-duty real estate transactions and ATF.
xa: Other four petroleum products: **crude, petrol, high-speed diesel, natural gas**.
⚠ Alcohol is excluded by the **Constitution**; petroleum awaits a **Council** date.

n975a29dd14b.s: From 1 October 2024, GST anti-profiteering cases are heard by the:
n975a29dd14b.x: Anti-profiteering functions moved from NAA to CCI in December 2022 and to the GSTAT Principal Bench from 1 October 2024.
xa: **GSTN** is the IT backbone; it uses **AI tools** for scrutiny.
**GSTIN** is a **15-digit** registration number.

n89fa301952c.s: IGST revenue is finally settled to the:
n89fa301952c.x: GST is destination-based, so IGST revenue goes to the consuming State.
xa: **Destination principle**: revenue accrues to the **State of consumption**.
IGST covers inter-State supplies and **imports**; apportioned under **Art. 269A**.

n9945fbc076d.s: Which is the largest source of Andhra Pradesh's own tax revenue (2024-25 RE)?
n9945fbc076d.x: SGST is AP's largest own tax source at about Rs 36,296 crore (38%); State excise (22%) is second.
xa: AP HC: Centre and State tax authorities must decide **inter se** who investigates (May **2026**).
Stamp duty and **motor vehicle tax** stay **outside GST** with the States.
**SGST** is levied by the **State** on intra-State supply, in **equal halves** with CGST.

nindian-economy-15-13.s: Under GST, the Centre administers and collects:
nindian-economy-15-13.x: The Centre collects CGST and IGST, States collect SGST, and the GST Council recommends.
n: The GST Council makes recommendations. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 19-22]
The Centre administers and collects CGST and IGST. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 19-22]
States administer SGST. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 19-22]
xa: **IGST** applies to **inter-State** supply and **imports**; only **Parliament** legislates on it.
**UTGST** applies in UTs without legislature.
Act ceilings: **CGST 20%**; **IGST 40%**.

n8401247ff93.s: Which State levy was NOT subsumed in GST?
n8401247ff93.x: Stamp duty is retained outside GST; purchase, luxury and entry taxes were subsumed.
xa: Other State taxes subsumed: **State VAT/Sales Tax**, **Central Sales Tax**, **Octroi**, taxes on **advertisements, lotteries, betting, gambling**.
Also outside GST: **electricity duty**, **motor vehicle tax**, **property tax**, **State excise on liquor**.

n6f6d256705a.s: The number of Central and State taxes subsumed into GST, as conventionally stated, is respectively:
n6f6d256705a.x: The conventional classification identifies eight Central taxes and nine State taxes as subsumed into GST.
n6f6d256705a.tq: Recall the paired numerical classification rather than counting only one category.
xs: **8 Central** and **9 State** taxes were subsumed — option **(1)**.
Central: **Central Excise**, **Service Tax**, **CVD**, **SAD**, central cesses and surcharges, among others.
xa: State: **VAT/Sales Tax**, **CST**, **Purchase, Luxury, Entry Tax**, **Octroi**, **Entertainment Tax**, etc.
**Basic Customs Duty** was **not** subsumed.
The "**declared goods of special importance**" concept was dropped.

n7d83045857a.s: Which one of the following is constitutionally excluded from GST rather than merely awaiting a notified date for levy?
n7d83045857a.x: Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is constitutionally excluded from GST. The listed petroleum products are constitutionally within GST but have not been brought under it for levy.
n7d83045857a.tq: Compare the constitutional treatment of liquor with petroleum products.
xs: **Alcoholic liquor for human consumption** is **excluded by the Constitution** itself — option **(3)**.
**ATF, natural gas, crude** are petroleum products **constitutionally within GST**, awaiting a date the **GST Council recommends**.
xa: ⚠ Petroleum = in the Constitution, waiting for Council date; alcohol = excluded and stays with **States**.
Five petroleum products: **crude, petrol, diesel, ATF, natural gas**.
APPSC-G2 2025: no GST on petrol/diesel, liquor, electricity, charitable services → "**All of the above**".

n939558d2a3c.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five petroleum products kept outside the current levy of GST?
n939558d2a3c.x: The five petroleum products are crude oil, petrol or motor spirit, high-speed diesel, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel. Lubricating oil is not included in that specified list.
n939558d2a3c.tq: Recall the complete five-item list and identify the outsider.
xs: **Lubricating oil** is not among the five petroleum products — option **(1)**.
The five: **crude, petrol (motor spirit), high-speed diesel, natural gas, ATF**.
xa: These are constitutionally within GST; levy starts only from a date the **GST Council recommends**.
**Alcoholic liquor for human consumption** is excluded by the Constitution itself.
**Electricity** supply and real estate (**stamp duty**) are also outside GST.

n1f92b32361e.s: Goods and Services Tax is regarded as the biggest indirect tax reform in India since Independence primarily because it:
o: replaced the need for all direct taxes
abolished the divisible pool of taxes
created a unified framework for a large number of indirect taxes
transferred all taxation powers to the States
n1f92b32361e.x: GST is considered the biggest indirect tax reform since Independence because it established a unified framework for indirect taxation by subsuming several indirect taxes.
n1f92b32361e.tq: Identify the precise significance rather than choosing extreme claims about direct taxes or complete transfer of powers.
xs: GST is the **biggest indirect tax reform since Independence** as it **created a unified framework** for many indirect taxes — option **(3)**.
It subsumed **8 Central + 9 State taxes** into a **single destination-based tax** ("one nation, one tax").
It did not replace direct taxes or move all powers to States; States in fact **gave up** indirect-tax powers.
xa: Objective: end **cascading** (tax on tax); **one nation-one market**.
GST applies at **both central and state levels** (APPSC 2023).
Record gross GST: **₹2.43 lakh crore in April 2026**.

nindian-economy-15-8.s: GST aims to end 'tax on tax', known as the:
nindian-economy-15-8.x: Reducing cascading (tax on tax) and creating a unified national market are major GST objectives.
n: A major objective of GST is to create a common or unified national market. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 19-22]
A major objective of GST is to reduce cascading of taxes. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 19-22]
xa: GST aims at "**one nation, one tax**" — a **single destination-based tax on value addition** (APPSC 2024).
GST applies at both **central and state levels** (APPSC 2023).
**GST 2.0** slabs: **5%** (merit), **18%** (standard), **40%** (demerit), from **22 Sep 2025**.

naffe2d196ec.s: The Revenue Neutral Rate Committee recommended an RNR of approximately:
naffe2d196ec.x: The Revenue Neutral Rate Committee, chaired by Arvind Subramanian, recommended an RNR of about 15–15.5% and a standard rate of 17–18%.
naffe2d196ec.tq: Keep the RNR range distinct from the proposed standard-rate range.
xs: The RNR Committee recommended an RNR of **~15-15.5%** and a standard rate of **17-18%** — option **(4)**.
It was chaired by **Arvind Subramanian** (**2015**; some notes say **2018**).
xa: **RNR** = the rate keeping revenue equal to the **pre-GST level**.
Statutory ceilings: **CGST 20%**, **IGST 40%**.

n4f5e725c118.s: Under the GST Acts, the ceiling for CGST is:
n4f5e725c118.x: The CGST Act provides a ceiling of 20%. The corresponding IGST ceiling is 40%.
n4f5e725c118.tq: Keep the CGST ceiling separate from the IGST ceiling.
xs: The CGST ceiling in the Acts is **20%** — option **(3)**.
**40%** is the **IGST** ceiling; **5%** and **18%** are GST 2.0 slabs.
xa: Rates change by **government notification on GST Council recommendation**, not by amending the Acts.
GST 2.0's top rate of **40%** (sin goods) equals the IGST ceiling.

n8447aab1d68.s: GST rates are normally changed by:
o: An order of the Reserve Bank of India
Amending the GST Acts through Parliament in every case
Government notification issued on the recommendation of the GST Council, subject to statutory ceilings
A resolution of the Finance Commission
n8447aab1d68.x: Rates are normally changed through government notification on the recommendation of the GST Council, rather than by amending the Acts each time.
n8447aab1d68.tq: Ask which authority performs the operational rate change and who recommends it.
xs: GST rates are changed by **government notification on GST Council recommendation**, within statutory ceilings — option **(3)**.
The Acts need **not be amended** for each change; RBI and the Finance Commission have no role.
xa: Ceilings in the Acts: **CGST 20%**, **IGST 40%**.
GST 2.0 approved at the **56th Council (3-4 Sep 2025)**, effective **22 Sep 2025**.

n87d5f26af95.s: At the 56th meeting of the GST Council, the tax slabs were identified as which of the following?
o: 5% merit, 18% standard and 40% de-merit or sin
n87d5f26af95.x: The 56th meeting provided for slabs of 5% for merit goods, 18% as the standard rate and 40% for de-merit or sin goods.
n87d5f26af95.tq: Match each rate with its classification instead of remembering the numbers alone.
xs: The **56th Council** set slabs of **5% (merit)**, **18% (standard)** and **40%** for sin/de-merit goods — option **(3)**.
It merged the old **5, 12, 18, 28%** slabs, so options with **12%** or **28%** are the old structure.
xa: Meeting dates: **3-4 Sep 2025**; effective **22 Sep 2025**.
Rates cut on ~**375 items**.
The **55th** meeting was held on **21 Dec 2024** at **Jaisalmer**.

n9b60216ba80.s: Under the Reverse Charge Mechanism in GST, the liability to pay tax is shifted from the:
n9b60216ba80.x: Under reverse charge, the recipient, rather than the supplier, pays GST on specified supplies.
n9b60216ba80.tq: Distinguish the direction of liability by asking who actually remits the tax.
xs: Under **Reverse Charge (RCM)**, liability shifts from the **supplier to the recipient** — option **(3)**.
The **recipient**, not the supplier, pays GST on **specified supplies**.
xa: **ITC** sets off input tax against output tax.
**Composition scheme**: turnover up to **₹1.5 crore** (₹50 lakh services); flat **1%** goods, **6%** services; **no ITC**.
**E-way bill** needed for moving goods worth **> ₹50,000**.

n6a715d86072.s: Under the GST composition scheme, the turnover limit for goods is:
n6a715d86072.x: The limit is ₹1.5 crore for goods and ₹50 lakh for services, at 1% and 6%, with no ITC.
xa: ITC is not available on **exempt or non-taxable** supplies; **nil-rated/exempt** also give no ITC.
Under **RCM**, the **recipient**, not the supplier, pays GST on specified supplies.
**Budget 2026-27**: **automated registration** within **3 working days** for low-risk applicants.

n611c21ad53a.s: An e-way bill is required for movement of goods valued above:
n611c21ad53a.x: An e-way bill is needed for goods above ₹50,000, valid one day per 200 km.
xa: **E-invoicing**: digital reporting of invoices to curb **fake invoices** and verify **ITC**; uses **HSN/SAC** codes.
**GSTN** is the IT backbone for registration, returns and ITC matching.
**GSTIN** is a **15-digit** registration number.

n555b3c0fcf2.s: Under the GST 2.0 changes referred to in the current tax structure, which of the following is exempted?
o: All motor vehicle insurance premiums without exception
Individual life and health insurance premiums
n555b3c0fcf2.x: GST 2.0 provides exemption for individual life and health insurance premiums. The exemption is not stated as a blanket exemption for every insurance service.
n555b3c0fcf2.tq: Avoid extending a specific exemption into an unsupported blanket exemption.
xs: GST 2.0 exempts **individual life and health insurance premiums** — option **(4)**.
The notes speak only of **individual** policies — no blanket exemption for all commercial or motor insurance or banking.
xa: **Rare-disease medicines** are fully exempt (Jun **2026**).
GST 2.0 slabs: **5%** merit, **18%** standard, **40%** sin/ultra-luxury.
Rates were cut on ~**375 items**.

n026eafd7e01.s: After the general withdrawal of GST compensation cess from 22 September 2025, it continued only on:
n026eafd7e01.x: The cess was scrapped for all goods except tobacco; its levy was extended to March 2026 to repay compensation loans.
xa: Compensation cess **ended 31 March 2026**.
From **1 Feb 2026**: higher **excise on tobacco** and **Health Security se National Security Cess** on pan masala.
Compensation itself ended in **June 2022**.

nf1a175b9ad3.s: The Health Security se National Security Cess is levied on pan masala units on the basis of:
nf1a175b9ad3.x: It is levied on machine production capacity, and its proceeds go to the Consolidated Fund of India without being shared with States.
xa: Tobacco faces higher excise under the **Central Excise (Amendment) Act, 2025**.
Criticism: **cesses** stay **outside the divisible pool**.

n186c2d26cda.s: GST compensation to States assumed an annual revenue growth of ____ over the 2015-16 base.
n186c2d26cda.x: Compensation was for five years at 14% annual growth over 2015-16; it ended in June 2022.
xa: Cess scrapped **22 Sep 2025** except tobacco; ended **31 March 2026**.
⚠ Compensation (ended **2022**) vs cess (ended **2026**).

n31131978e00.s: In which month did monthly gross GST collections first exceed ₹2 lakh crore?
n31131978e00.x: Monthly gross GST collections crossed ₹2 lakh crore for the first time in April 2024.
n31131978e00.tq: Test a milestone date using close year alternatives.
xs: Monthly gross GST first exceeded **₹2 lakh crore** in **April 2024** — option **(4)**.
**April 2026** is the later **record** month (**₹2.43 lakh crore**), not the first crossing.
xa: FY 2017-18 average: **₹82,000 cr/month**.
**FY 2024-25**: **₹22.08 lakh crore**, avg **₹1.84 lakh crore**/month.

n2cecde77f09.s: Which one of the following correctly represents India’s gross GST collection during FY 2024-25?
o: ₹22.08 lakh crore, with an average of ₹1.84 lakh crore per month
₹24.08 lakh crore, with an average of ₹2.04 lakh crore per month
₹22.08 lakh crore, with an average of ₹2.43 lakh crore per month
₹17.4 lakh crore, with an average of ₹1.82 lakh crore per month
n2cecde77f09.x: Gross GST collection in FY 2024-25 was ₹22.08 lakh crore, averaging ₹1.84 lakh crore per month.
n2cecde77f09.tq: Separate an annual total from its monthly average using precise numerical matching.
xs: **FY 2024-25** gross GST: **₹22.08 lakh crore**, average **₹1.84 lakh crore** per month — option **(1)**.
**₹2.43 lakh crore** is the **April 2026** record month; **₹17.4 lakh crore** is the **Apr-Dec 2025** total.
xa: Collections **doubled in 4 years**, a **CAGR of 18%**.
FY 2017-18 average was only **₹82,000 cr/month**.

nffb0d603c0f.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the GST rate structure from 22 September 2025?
o: 0%, 5% as merit rate, 18% as standard rate and 40% as demerit rate
nffb0d603c0f.x: GST 2.0 rationalised the principal slabs into 0%, 5%, 18% and 40%, with 5% as the merit rate, 18% as the standard rate and 40% as the demerit rate.
nffb0d603c0f.tq: Compare the post-rationalisation labels and rates as a complete structure.
xs: From **22 Sep 2025** slabs are **0, 5% (merit), 18% (standard), 40% (demerit)** — option **(3)**.
**5, 12, 18, 28%** was the pre-2.0 structure; the **12%** slab no longer exists.
xa: Old **12%** slab: ~**99%** of items moved to **5%**.
Approved at the **56th Council** (3-4 Sep 2025).

n07c1fccf1f5.s: The GST rate applicable to rough diamonds and gold, silver and jewellery under the special-rate structure is, respectively:
n07c1fccf1f5.x: Rough diamonds attract a special rate of 0.25%, while gold, silver and jewellery attract 3%.
n07c1fccf1f5.tq: Read paired numerical rates in the order in which the commodities are given.
xs: Special rates: **0.25%** on **rough diamonds**, **3%** on **gold/silver/jewellery** — option **(4)**.
Option (2) reverses the two rates.
xa: Main slabs: **0, 5% (merit), 18% (standard), 40% (demerit)**.
**Tractors 12% → 5%**.
**Small cars, bikes ≤350cc, ACs 28% → 18%**.

n347ad5e17ca.s: The four-slab structure of GST was originally intended to be:
o: A permanent arrangement for all goods and services
A mechanism for distributing IGST among States
A structure applicable only to petroleum products
n347ad5e17ca.x: The four-slab GST structure was conceived as a transitional arrangement rather than a permanent structure.
n347ad5e17ca.tq: Test the intended character of a policy arrangement rather than its numerical details.
xs: The four-slab structure was meant to be **transitional**, ahead of simplification — option **(4)**.
It had slabs **5%, 12%, 18%, 28%** (2017) + exempt goods.
xa: GST 2.0 replaced it with **0, 5, 18, 40%** from **22 Sep 2025**.
Multiple rates caused **misclassification** and **classification disputes**.
Further ask: **GST 3.0** simplification (CII AP, **1 Feb 2026**).

nccc09cb9892.s: Which of the following correctly represents the original GST rate structure introduced in 2017, apart from exempt goods and compensation cess?
nccc09cb9892.x: The original GST structure contained slabs of 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%, along with exempt goods and compensation cess over 28% for specified goods.
nccc09cb9892.tq: Recall the complete original slab sequence.
xs: The **2017** structure had slabs of **5%, 12%, 18%, 28%** + exempt goods — option **(4)**.
A **compensation cess** sat over **28%** on luxury/sin goods.
xa: GST 2.0: **0, 5% (merit), 18% (standard), 40% (demerit)**.
Special rates: **0.25%** rough diamonds; **3%** gold/silver/jewellery.

n07b0beeae44.s: Which of the following is the most direct contribution of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) to inter-State commerce?
o: Replacement of input tax credit by a turnover tax
Creation of a common national market through tax harmonisation
Exemption of all inter-State supplies from taxation
Retention of State border check-posts for all goods
n07b0beeae44.x: GST created a common national market by harmonising indirect taxation across States. It also helped reduce the cascading effect through input tax credit.
n07b0beeae44.tq: Identify the core objective rather than choosing an extreme or reversed consequence.
xs: GST's key contribution: a **common national market** through **tax harmonisation** — option **(2)**.
**ITC at every stage** was kept, not replaced (ending **cascading**); inter-State supplies are taxed under **IGST**.
Border **check-posts were dismantled**, not retained.
xa: **Digital tools**: e-invoicing, e-way bills, auto-generated returns; reduced human interface.
Taxpayer base: **66.5 lakh (2017) → 1.51 crore (2025)**.

na08415295e8.s: An e-way bill under GST is valid for one day for every:
na08415295e8.x: Validity is one day per 200 km; the e-way bill is mandatory above ₹50,000.
xa: E-way bills replaced physical checks, so State border **check-posts were dismantled**.
E-way bills with **e-invoicing** and AI scrutiny counter **fake invoicing**.

n9252a6082dd.s: The removal of inter-State check-posts after the rollout of e-way bills primarily resulted in:
o: A shift from digital to manual tax reporting
Reduced transit time and logistics costs
The abolition of input tax credit
n9252a6082dd.x: The replacement of physical checks and the dismantling of border check-posts reduced truck waiting time, transit time and logistics costs.
n9252a6082dd.tq: Link the administrative reform to its practical logistics outcome.
xs: Removing check-posts **cut transit time and logistics costs** — option **(2)**.
It also cut **truck waiting time**, once **entry tax** was subsumed and **e-way bills** replaced physical checks.
It moved reporting **toward digital**, with fewer physical checks — the opposite of options (1) and (3).
xa: E-way bill: needed for goods over **Rs 50,000**; valid **1 day per 200 km**.
E-way bill volumes rose **21%** in Apr-Dec 2025.
**ITC** at every stage ended the **cascading effect**.

n908af9d08a3.s: Which of the following best indicates the expansion of formalisation under GST between 2017 and 2025?
o: The taxpayer base remained unchanged at 66.5 lakh
The taxpayer base increased from 1.51 crore to 66.5 lakh
The taxpayer base increased from 66.5 lakh to 1.51 crore
The taxpayer base declined from 1.51 crore to 66.5 lakh
n908af9d08a3.x: The taxpayer base expanded from 66.5 lakh in 2017 to 1.51 crore in 2025, indicating greater formalisation.
n908af9d08a3.tq: Compare the direction and magnitude of a two-point trend without reversing the figures.
xs: The GST taxpayer base grew **from 66.5 lakh (2017) to 1.51 crore (2025)** — option **(3)**.
This expansion signals **greater formalisation**.
xa: MSME gains: **credit access/eligibility** and **procurement parity** for small firms.
**Composition scheme**: turnover up to **Rs 1.5 crore** (Rs **50 lakh** for services).
Still a burden: **multiple returns + ITC matching**.

n04b36a3f856.s: A taxpayer under the GST composition scheme pays a flat rate of ____ on goods.
n04b36a3f856.x: The composition scheme levies 1% on goods and 6% on services, and the taxpayer cannot claim ITC.
xa: Taxpayer base grew from **66.5 lakh (2017)** to **1.51 crore (2025)** — greater formalisation.
**E-way bill** is mandatory for goods worth over **Rs 50,000**.
⚠ **Inverted Duty Structure:** input rate > output rate → refund of unutilised ITC allowed.

ne9a00b1aa9c.s: Which practice is characteristic of the ITC fraud involving bogus entities?
o: Paying output tax twice on genuine transactions
Issuing invoices without actual supply of goods or services
Using only government invoices for exports
Claiming refunds on petroleum products outside GST
ne9a00b1aa9c.x: Bogus entities issue invoices without any corresponding supply in order to fraudulently claim input tax credit.
ne9a00b1aa9c.tq: Identify the fraudulent mechanism from a practical transaction scenario.
xs: In **ITC fraud**, bogus entities **issue invoices without actual supply** — option **(2)**.
An **AP-Telangana-Karnataka** network used **fake registrations + scrap bills** to claim ITC (**3 Jan 2026**).
xa: Countered by **e-invoicing**, **UPI/Aadhaar tracking** and **AI scrutiny**.
AP's **Legal-AI assistant** was trained on ~**22,000 judgments**.
**E-way bills** add to AI-based scrutiny against fake invoicing.

n5555d8e6a50.s: The destination principle of GST generally favours:
o: States with the highest rates of State excise duty
Producing States because tax is collected at the point of manufacture
Consuming States because taxation follows the place of consumption
n5555d8e6a50.x: GST follows the destination principle, under which consuming States benefit because revenue is associated with the place of consumption.
n5555d8e6a50.tq: Distinguish destination-based taxation from origin-based taxation.
xs: The destination principle favours **consuming States**, since taxation follows the **place of consumption** — option **(3)**.
GST revenue goes to the State where goods/services are **consumed, not produced** — so producing States do not gain (option 2).
xa: **IGST** on inter-State supply (**Art. 269A**): levied by the Centre, apportioned; the **destination State** gets the State share.
Manufacturing States (**Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka**) feared loss.
AP, a **consuming State**, benefits via **IGST settlement**.

n778a49bd111.s: Andhra Pradesh, being a consuming State, benefits from GST primarily through:
o: State excise on petroleum under GST
Abolition of its own tax revenue
n778a49bd111.x: As a consuming State, Andhra Pradesh benefits from the destination principle through IGST settlement.
n778a49bd111.tq: Apply the destination principle to the fiscal position of a particular State.
xs: AP, a **consuming State**, benefits mainly through **IGST settlement** — option **(2)**.
Under the destination principle, the **destination State** receives the State share of IGST.
**Petroleum** is still outside GST, so option (3) is impossible.
xa: AP's **Net GST** = **SGST + IGST settlement share**.
GST is AP's largest own-tax source: **38%** = **Rs 36,296 crore** (2024-25 RE).
Up to **Aug 2026**, AP net GST was **₹16,452.62 cr**.

nd2173cb9b12.s: Which group of States mainly represents manufacturing or producing States that feared revenue loss under the destination-based GST system?
o: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
nd2173cb9b12.x: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka were identified as manufacturing States that feared losses because GST revenue follows consumption rather than production. This concern contributed to the five-year compensation guarantee.
nd2173cb9b12.tq: Match the policy effect with the group of affected producing States.
xs: **Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka** — manufacturing States — feared loss — option **(1)**.
Under the destination principle, revenue goes to the **consuming** State, not the producing one.
xa: This fear was a key reason for the **5-year compensation guarantee**.
Today **manufacturing States gain** from concentrated buoyancy; **unorganised-sector States** depend on FC devolution.
AP, a **consuming State**, benefits via IGST settlement.

nfce796e8580.s: For Andhra Pradesh, “Net GST” is defined as:
o: Gross GST collections minus customs revenue
SGST plus the State’s share of IGST settlement
SGST minus the State’s share of IGST settlement
nfce796e8580.x: Andhra Pradesh’s Net GST consists of SGST plus its share received through IGST settlement.
nfce796e8580.tq: Discriminate between a State’s own GST component and its settled IGST share.
xs: AP's **Net GST** = **SGST + the State's share of IGST settlement** — option **(3)**.
IGST settlement is **added**, not subtracted, and **State Excise** is outside GST.
xa: Up to **Aug 2026**: net GST **₹16,452.62 cr**; commercial taxes **₹25,449.80 cr** (+18.05%).
AP benefits as a **consuming State** via IGST settlement.

n36f94e21761.s: In May 2026, the Andhra Pradesh High Court held that where Central and State GST investigations overlap, the authorities must:
o: Abandon the investigation if the entity operates in more than one State
Decide inter se which authority will proceed
Transfer every case automatically to the Union Government
Both proceed simultaneously against the same entity
n36f94e21761.x: The Court held that Central and State GST authorities must decide inter se who will proceed against a common entity, thereby preventing dual action.
n36f94e21761.tq: Identify the precise institutional solution to overlapping jurisdiction.
xs: The **AP High Court** (May **2026**) held that Central and State GST authorities must **decide inter se** who proceeds — option **(2)**.
The aim is to **prevent dual action** against one entity — so option (4) is the very thing ruled out.
xa: **Mohit Minerals (2022)**: Council recommendations **persuasive, not binding**.
Fake invoicing is countered by **e-invoicing** + AI-based scrutiny with e-way bills.

n14c39e4189d.s: The GST compensation cess was continued after the compensation period primarily to:
o: Repay loans taken to pay compensation during the COVID-19 period
n14c39e4189d.x: After the compensation period, the cess was continued to repay loans taken for paying GST compensation during the COVID-19 period.
n14c39e4189d.tq: Identify the stated purpose behind continuation of a fiscal instrument.
xs: The cess was continued to **repay COVID back-to-back loans** taken to pay compensation — option **(2)**.
It ran to **March 2026** for that purpose, long after compensation ended in **June 2022**.
xa: Scrapped **22 September 2025** except **tobacco products**.
The **tobacco cess** continues until cess-account **loan obligations are discharged**.
Compensation period: **5 years** at **14%** growth.

nc7877927b5f.s: With effect from 22 September 2025, the GST compensation cess was scrapped for all goods except:
nc7877927b5f.x: The compensation cess was scrapped on 22 September 2025 except for tobacco products, on which it continues until cess-account loan obligations are discharged.
nc7877927b5f.tq: Test the exception to a general abolition of the cess.
xs: From **22 September 2025**, the cess was scrapped for all goods except **tobacco products** — option **(3)**.
The tobacco cess continues until **cess-account loan obligations** are discharged.
**Online gaming** and luxury cars now fall in the **40%** demerit slab; aerated drinks lost the cess.
xa: Original cess goods: **luxury cars, aerated drinks, pan masala, tobacco**.
GST 2.0 took effect on the same date, **22 September 2025**.
Unused balance: **50% to Centre**, **50% to States**.

n34e33dfc475.s: How is the unused balance of the GST compensation cess to be shared?
o: Entirely to the States in proportion to their population
50% to the Centre and 50% to the States in proportion to their SGST revenue
As per the Finance Commission's horizontal devolution formula
n34e33dfc475.x: The unused balance goes 50% to the Centre and 50% to the States, with the States' half shared in proportion to their SGST revenue. It does not all go to the Centre (A), it is not shared by population (B), and the Finance Commission formula (D) does not apply because cess is outside the divisible pool.
n34e33dfc475.tq: Unused compensation cess: 50:50, States' half by SGST share.
xs: The unused cess balance goes **50% to the Centre** and **50% to the States**, in proportion to **SGST revenue** — option **(3)**.
It is not all to the Centre, not by population, and not by the FC formula — cesses sit **outside the divisible pool**.
xa: Cess **scrapped 22 September 2025** except tobacco.
Compensation: **July 2017 - June 2022** at **14%** growth.
Law: **GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017**.

nd38e00b9022.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about GST compliance for small businesses?
o: The composition scheme has eased the compliance burden
Automated registration has eased the compliance burden
Multiple returns and ITC matching remain a burden
The reform agenda proposes replacing pre-filled returns with manual filing
nd38e00b9022.x: The reform agenda calls for pre-filled returns, time-bound digital registration and automated exporter refunds, not manual filing.
xa: The agenda also seeks **time-bound digital registration** and **automated refunds for exporters** (Aug 2025).
Composition: flat **1%** goods / **6%** services.

n6e5c56992cc.s: What is identified as the biggest drawback of the multiple-rate structure under GST?
o: Delay in settlement of IGST between the Union and the States
Dependence of States on Finance Commission devolution
Misclassification of goods and services and classification disputes
Complete exclusion of petroleum products from taxation
n6e5c56992cc.x: The multiple-rate structure creates difficulties in classifying goods and services, resulting in frequent classification disputes.
n6e5c56992cc.tq: Directly identify the specific weakness associated with a tax structure.
xs: The biggest drawback of multiple rates is **misclassification of goods and services** and **classification disputes** — option **(3)** (APPSC-G1 2017).
Near-identical products land in **different slabs** → disputes and **litigation**.
xa: The **four-slab** structure was meant to be **transitional**.
Pending reform (Aug 2025): "**standardise product classification**".
GST 2.0 cut the main slabs to **5%** and **18%** + **40%**.

n561b7368e2e.s: Under a multi-rate GST, placing near-identical products in different slabs mainly leads to:
n561b7368e2e.x: Differing classification of similar products invites litigation; standardising classification is a pending reform.
xa: Misclassification is the **biggest drawback** of multiple rates (APPSC-G1 2017).
Sector pleas: notebook makers hit by the **Sep 2025** rate revision (9 Sep 2026).

nd0e95de3d4a.s: Which of the following continue to remain outside the GST framework?
nd0e95de3d4a.x: Petroleum and electricity remain outside the GST framework.
nd0e95de3d4a.tq: Use confusable sector exclusions to distinguish items inside and outside a tax regime.
xs: **Petroleum and electricity** are still **outside GST** — option **(1)**.
Petroleum (**crude, petrol, diesel, natural gas, ATF**) is within GST law but taxed only from a date the **GST Council recommends** (**Art. 279A(5)**).
xa: Other asks: **GST 3.0** simplification (CII AP, **1 Feb 2026**).
Criticism: **vertical fiscal imbalance** and loss of **state tax autonomy**.
Cesses remain **outside the divisible pool**.

n36d95beb0d7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the GST Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT)?
o: Its Principal Bench is located in Mumbai
It was created through the Finance Act, 2024
It was formally launched in September 2025
n36d95beb0d7.x: GSTAT's Principal Bench is at New Delhi, not Mumbai.
xa: GSTAT **Procedure Rules 2025**.
First President = **former Chief Justice of Jharkhand HC**.

nea920a96c02.s: As of mid-2025, which problem was associated with the GST Appellate Tribunal?
o: State benches had exclusive jurisdiction over direct taxes
The tribunal had replaced the Supreme Court as the final court of appeal
Only the New Delhi Principal Bench had been abolished
Functional benches were absent in many States despite notification
nea920a96c02.x: Although GSTAT had been notified, functional benches were absent in many States as of mid-2025, causing appeals to accumulate in High Courts.
nea920a96c02.tq: Distinguish notification or legal creation from actual operationalisation.
xs: Mid-2025: GSTAT was **notified**, but **functional benches were absent in many States** — option **(4)**.
As a result, appeals **piled up in High Courts** (Jul **2025**).
xa: It was **formally launched Sep 2025**, with **hearings from Dec 2025**.
Created via **Finance Act 2024**; **Procedure Rules 2025**.
Appeals are to be filed **online within 3 months**.

n6d9ea995f10.s: Why does the Centre have an effective veto in the GST Council?
o: Because the Centre’s one-third vote can prevent a three-fourths majority
Because the Centre has two-thirds of the weighted vote
Because State representatives cannot vote on tax matters
Because the Centre alone nominates all State members
n6d9ea995f10.x: Since three-fourths weighted support is required and the Centre holds one-third of the vote, the Centre can block a proposal without its support.
n6d9ea995f10.tq: Infer institutional power from the voting weights and decision threshold.
xs: The **Centre's one-third vote** can **prevent a three-fourths majority** — option **(1)**.
With **2/3** weight, the States alone fall short of **3/4**, so no decision passes without the Centre.
The Centre has **1/3**, not 2/3, so option (2) is wrong.
xa: The weights are of **votes present**.
Debate: **loss of state tax autonomy** and **vertical fiscal imbalance**.

n29679fb8af2.s: Which of the following groups of petroleum products is covered by the GST law but remains outside GST taxation until a date recommended by the GST Council?
o: Crude oil, petrol, diesel, natural gas and ATF
Natural gas, electricity, alcohol, tobacco and ATF
Coal, electricity, iron ore, cement and steel
Gold, silver, diamonds, petrol and coal
n29679fb8af2.x: Crude oil, petrol, high-speed diesel, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel are within the GST law but are taxed outside GST until the Council recommends a date under Article 279A(5).
n29679fb8af2.tq: Test the complete list and distinguish legal inclusion from present tax treatment.
xs: **Crude, petrol, diesel (HSD), natural gas, ATF** are within GST law but taxed only from a date the **GST Council recommends** — option **(1)**.
The power is in **Art. 279A(5)**; until then they remain **outside GST**.
**Electricity**, **alcohol**, **coal** and **gold** are not part of this petroleum group.
xa: Coverage gap: **petroleum and electricity** still outside GST.
**Gold/silver/jewellery** are taxed at a special **3%**.

n03d351b2bfa.s: Which of the following is a criticism of cesses in the GST framework?
o: They can be imposed only by State legislatures
They are always included in the divisible pool for distribution to States
They remain outside the divisible pool, contributing to concerns over State fiscal autonomy
n03d351b2bfa.x: Cesses outside the divisible pool reduce the share available for devolution and are therefore linked with concerns about States’ fiscal autonomy and vertical fiscal imbalance.
n03d351b2bfa.tq: Connect the fiscal instrument with its federal consequence.
xs: **Cesses remain outside the divisible pool**, feeding concerns over **State fiscal autonomy** — option **(3)**.
They are not in the divisible pool (option 2) and do not remove **vertical fiscal imbalance** (option 4).
xa: Other criticism: **loss of state tax autonomy**; vertical fiscal imbalance.
The unused compensation cess balance is split **50:50** between Centre and States.
States' **weak own revenues** mean **dependence on transfers**.

n14b6807abef.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025–26, a cut in GST rates may have what effect on revenue?
o: Volume effects may offset the initial revenue loss
It necessarily eliminates all future GST revenue
It reduces transaction volumes in every sector
It affects only customs revenue and not GST revenue
n14b6807abef.x: The Economic Survey 2025–26 observed that increased volume of transactions following a rate cut may offset the associated revenue loss.
n14b6807abef.tq: Recognise the stated dynamic revenue effect instead of assuming a static tax-base response.
xs: **ES 2025-26**: after a rate cut, **volume effects may offset the revenue loss** — option **(1)**.
The Survey does not say a cut wipes out revenue or shrinks volumes.
xa: ES 2025-26 calls **GST 2.0** the **third pillar of tax reform**, with "**no net tax hike**".
**ES 2019-20**: rationalisation shocks raise collections only for **1-3 months**.
GST revenue growth in **H2 2025-26** was only **4.67%**.

na3b03b7ff2d.s: The Economic Survey 2025–26 described GST 2.0 as the:
na3b03b7ff2d.x: GST 2.0 was described as the third pillar of tax reform, after the 2019 corporate tax cut and the 2025 personal income-tax reform.
na3b03b7ff2d.tq: Use the sequence of reforms rather than identifying GST only by its tax rates.
xs: **ES 2025-26** called **GST 2.0** the **third pillar of tax reform** — option **(3)**.
It follows the **2019 corporate tax cut** (first) and the **April 2025 personal income tax reform** (second).
xa: The Survey stressed "**no net tax hike**".
It also said rate-cut **volume effects may offset revenue loss**.
GST 2.0 took effect on **22 Sep 2025**.

n387eb308366.s: One major fiscal consequence for States of surrendering independent indirect-tax powers under GST has been:
o: Greater dependence on transfers because of weak own revenues
Automatic equalisation of revenues among all States
Complete elimination of State taxation powers
n387eb308366.x: The surrender of independent indirect-tax powers, combined with weak own revenues, has increased States’ dependence on transfers.
n387eb308366.tq: Link the loss of fiscal autonomy with the resulting dependence on transfers.
xs: Surrendering indirect-tax powers left States with **weak own revenues** and **greater dependence on transfers** — option **(1)**.
Taxes given up: **VAT, entry tax, luxury tax, entertainment tax, octroi**.
FC devolution was not abolished — **unorganised-sector States depend on FC devolution**.
xa: Only **16 States/UTs** had post-settlement GST growth above the national average.
Compensation: **5 years** at **14%** growth, under the **GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017**.
Criticism: **vertical fiscal imbalance**.

nc1698d4aa19.s: The GST 2.0 reforms were approved at which GST Council meeting and became effective from which date?
nc1698d4aa19.x: The GST 2.0 reforms were approved at the 56th GST Council meeting held on 3–4 September 2025 and became effective on 22 September 2025.
nc1698d4aa19.tq: Pair the reform package with both its approving meeting and effective date.
xs: GST 2.0 was approved at the **56th GST Council meeting** (3-4 Sep 2025), effective **22 September 2025** — option **(4)**.
The **57th** meeting is fixed for **12 Sep 2026**, a year later.
xa: Also called the **NextGen GST reforms**.
Inverted-duty refunds were flagged for the **57th** meeting.
**ES 2025-26**: GST 2.0 = **third pillar of tax reform**.

n1a035e8b68e.s: Which Article is associated with grants in lieu of export duty on jute and jute products to Assam, Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha?
n1a035e8b68e.x: Article 273 provided grants in lieu of export duty on jute and jute products to Assam, Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.
n1a035e8b68e.tq: Discriminate between the two nearby grant provisions by the specific beneficiary States and purpose.
xs: **Article 273** gives grants **in lieu of jute export duty** to **Assam, Bihar, WB, Odisha** — option **(4)**.
**Art. 275** = statutory FC grants; **Art. 282** = discretionary grants; **Art. 293** = State borrowing.
xa: **Art. 275** grants go to States in need, **ST welfare** and **Scheduled Areas**.
**Art. 276**: tax on professions, trades, callings, ceiling **₹2,500**.
**Art. 280/281**: Finance Commission / its recommendations laid before Parliament.

nef6659ac357.s: The constitutional ceiling on taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments under Article 276 is:
nef6659ac357.x: Article 276 concerns taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments, subject to a ceiling of ₹2,500.
nef6659ac357.tq: Use the exact statutory ceiling and distinguish it from nearby round-value distractors.
xs: The ceiling on taxes on **professions, trades, callings** under **Art. 276** is **₹2,500** — option **(3)**.
The Constitution itself fixes this cap in **Art. 276**; **₹1,000**, **₹2,000** and **₹5,000** are not the ceiling the notes give.
xa: **Art. 265**: no tax except by authority of law.
**Art. 271**: surcharge on Art. 269/270 taxes, wholly for the Union.
**Art. 273**: grants in lieu of **jute export duty**.

nd74e48526e5.s: Statutory grants-in-aid recommended by the Finance Commission are made under Article:
nd74e48526e5.x: Article 275 grants are statutory and recommended by the Finance Commission; Article 282 allows discretionary grants for any public purpose.
xa: Art. 275 serves **States in need**, **ST welfare**, **Scheduled Areas**.
Art. 282 grants are used for **CSS** and were once the **larger part** of Central grants.
Criticism: Art. 282 grants are seen as **politically motivated**, **bypassing the FC**.

nace1acbe3a3.s: Grants for any public purpose chosen by the executive are associated with Article:
nace1acbe3a3.x: Article 282 covers grants for any public purpose; Article 275 grants are for States in need, ST welfare and Scheduled Areas.
xa: Art. 275 grants are **FC-recommended** and **charged on the CFI**.
AP's **Revenue Deficit Grants** come under **Art. 275**.
⚠ **275** = statutory, FC; **282** = discretionary.

nfdc44859203.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about grants to States?
o: Article 275 grants are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
Plan grants continued after the Planning Commission was abolished in 2015
Article 282 grants are criticised as bypassing the Finance Commission
nfdc44859203.x: Plan grants ended when the Planning Commission was abolished in 2015.
xa: Art. 282 grants were formerly recommended by the **Planning Commission**.
Discretionary grants once formed the **larger part** of Central grants.

nac164030a6c.s: What was the principal feature of the 'grand bargain' proposed by the 16th Finance Commission in relation to cesses?
o: All cesses would be transferred directly to local bodies
States would accept a smaller share of a larger pool if most cesses were merged into regular taxes
States would receive a larger share of a smaller pool without any change in cesses
States would impose all Union cesses within their territories
nac164030a6c.x: The proposal envisaged States taking a smaller share of a larger pool if the Centre merged most cesses into regular taxes.
nac164030a6c.tq: Test both linked conditions of a policy proposal rather than only its title.
xs: The **16th FC "grand bargain"** (para **7.67**): **States take a smaller share of a larger pool** if the Centre **merges most cesses into regular taxes** — option **(2)**.
The 16th FC made **no recommendation to curb/cap cesses** directly (**2 Mar 2026**).
xa: Cesses + surcharges per ₹100 of Central tax: **₹13.5** (2021-22, decade high) → **₹11** (2025-26 est.).
Effective devolution is only ~**30-32%** of gross tax revenue.
Centre's defence: it spent **105%** of cess collections on States over six years.

n504d475bd3c.s: The amount of cesses and surcharges per ₹100 of Central tax was at a decade high in which year and at what level?
n504d475bd3c.x: Cesses and surcharges amounted to ₹13.5 per ₹100 of Central tax in 2021–22, described as a decade high. The estimate for 2025–26 was ₹11.
n504d475bd3c.tq: Keep the year-value pair intact and avoid swapping the historical figure with the estimate.
xs: Cesses + surcharges hit a **decade high** of **₹13.5** per ₹100 of Central tax in **2021-22** — option **(3)**.
**₹11** is the **2025-26 estimate**, not the peak.
xa: Effect: effective devolution only ~**30-32%** of gross tax revenue.
States' share in total tax receipts ~**34%** vs **41%** headline.
They are not shared because they sit outside the **Art. 270** divisible pool.

n03ea7b11e43.s: What was the approximate effective devolution to the States as a percentage of gross tax revenue, despite the headline 41% share of the divisible pool?
n03ea7b11e43.x: Because cesses and surcharges are outside the divisible pool, the effective devolution was approximately 30–32% of gross tax revenue, lower than the headline 41% of the divisible pool.
n03ea7b11e43.tq: Distinguish a percentage of the divisible pool from a percentage of gross tax revenue.
xs: Effective devolution is about **30-32%** of gross tax revenue — option **(1)**.
Reason: **cesses and surcharges** sit **outside the divisible pool**, so the **41%** headline overstates it.
xa: States' share in **total tax receipts** is only ~**34%** (2 Feb 2026).
Critics call this the "**41% illusion**".
Cesses + surcharges per ₹100 of Central tax: **₹13.5** (2021-22), **₹11** (2025-26 est.).

nc72e5a4261a.s: Which of the following aggravates vertical fiscal imbalance between the Centre and States?
o: Cesses and surcharges kept outside the divisible pool
Removal of conditionalities on Centrally Sponsored Schemes
Retention of independent indirect taxes by States
nc72e5a4261a.x: Cesses and surcharges, loss of independent indirect taxes to GST, CSS conditionalities and weak State revenue all aggravate the imbalance.
xa: Root cause: the **Union holds larger, more buoyant tax bases** (corporate tax, income tax, most of GST).
Of the budgeted rise in transfers, ~**42%** was **CSS** revenue transfers, reinforcing Centre-set conditionality.
Transfers 2026-27: **₹25.44 lakh crore**.

n597d3b8f2c2.s: The Rajamannar Committee (1969), which advocated greater State autonomy, was set up by the:
n597d3b8f2c2.x: The Tamil Nadu Government constituted the Rajamannar Committee in 1969; it argued for greater State autonomy and more resources.
xa: Rajamannar: **1969**.
⚠ **Rajamannar** = set up by **Tamil Nadu**, not the Union.
**Sarkaria (1983-88)** and **Punchhi (2007-10)** were set up by the **Union**.

nd2a6e28fee9.s: The Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations functioned during:
nd2a6e28fee9.x: The Sarkaria Commission sat during 1983–1988; the Rajamannar Committee dates to 1969 and the Punchhi Commission to 2007–2010.
xa: Sarkaria led to the **Inter-State Council (Art. 263)** in **1990**.
Punchhi: **5% cap on cesses**, **time-bound disposal of bills**.
Rajamannar was set up by **Tamil Nadu**.

n4053d01080a.s: The Inter-State Council under Article 263 was set up in 1990 on the recommendation of the:
n4053d01080a.x: The Union-appointed Sarkaria Commission's recommendations led to the Inter-State Council in 1990.
xa: Punchhi is credited with a **5% cap on cesses**.

nf2b0aed58b7.s: The award period of the 16th Finance Commission is:
nf2b0aed58b7.tq: Check both the starting and ending years of the stated award period.
xs: The **16th FC** award covers **2026-27 to 2030-31** — option **(3)**.
It is in force from **1 Apr 2026**, so it is the "**present Finance Commission**".
xa: Chair: **Dr. Arvind Panagariya**.
Total grants: **₹9.47 lakh cr**.
AP's share rose to **4.217%** from **4.047%**.

nf5f4c8b11ad.s: Who chaired the Fourteenth Finance Commission?
nf5f4c8b11ad.x: Y.V. Reddy chaired the 14th FC; Rangarajan the 12th, Kelkar the 13th and N.K. Singh the 15th.
xa: **12th = Rangarajan** was asked in **MPPSC 2023**; **11th-14th** chairs in **UPPSC 2025**.
**16th** = **Arvind Panagariya**.
**11th** = **A.M. Khusro**.

nindian-economy-50-1.s: Who chaired the Fifth Finance Commission (1968)?
nindian-economy-50-1.x: Mahaveer Tyagi chaired the 5th FC (1968); K.C. Neogy chaired the 1st (1951) and K.C. Pant the 10th (1992).
n: The 1st Finance Commission was constituted in 1951. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 74-75]
K.C. Neogy was the chairman of the 1st Finance Commission. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 74-75]
The 5th Finance Commission was constituted in 1968. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 74-75]
Mahaveer Tyagi was the chairman of the 5th Finance Commission. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 74-75]
The 10th Finance Commission was constituted in 1992. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 74-75]
K.C. Pant was the chairman of the 10th Finance Commission. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 74-75]
The 15th Finance Commission was constituted in 2017. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 74-75]
N.K. Singh was the chairman of the 15th Finance Commission. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 74-75]
xa: ⚠ **10th - 11th - 12th - 13th** = **Pant - Khusro - Rangarajan - Kelkar**.
**14th FC** = **Y.V. Reddy** (**2015-20**); **16th FC** = **Arvind Panagariya**.
Some notes spell the 5th FC chairman **Mahavir Tyagi**.

nindian-economy-50-2.s: Who was the chairman of the 16th Finance Commission constituted in 2023?
nindian-economy-50-2.x: Arvind Panagariya chairs the 16th Finance Commission, set up in 2023 for 2026–31. N.K. Singh chaired the 15th and Y.V. Reddy the 14th.
nindian-economy-50-2.tq: Recall the recent Finance Commission chairs.
n: The 16th Finance Commission was constituted in 2023. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 74-75]
Arvind Panagariya was the chairman of the 16th Finance Commission. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 74-75]
xs: The **16th Finance Commission** is chaired by **Arvind Panagariya** — option **(4)**.
He is a former **Vice-Chairman, NITI Aayog**; the award period is **2026-27 to 2030-31**.
**N.K. Singh** chaired the **15th**, **Y.V. Reddy** the **14th** and **Vijay L. Kelkar** the **13th**.
xa: The 16th FC was constituted on **31 Dec 2023**; report submitted **17 Nov 2025**.
16th FC weights: **income distance 42.5**, **population 17.5**, new **GDP contribution 10**.
AP's share rose to **4.217%** (from **4.047%**).

neddc1526032.s: Under the Fourteenth Finance Commission, income distance carried a weight of:
neddc1526032.x: The 14th FC gave 50% to income distance, 17.5% to 1971 population, 10% to 2011 population and 15% to area.
xa: ⚠ Income distance **50 → 45 → 42.5** (14th → 15th → 16th).
2011 population weight: **10 → 15 → 17.5**.
1971 population was dropped after the 14th.

nf3012ddc5cc.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the devolution criteria of the 16th Finance Commission?
o: The tax and fiscal effort criterion was dropped
The weight of income distance was reduced to 42.5%
Contribution to GDP was added with a 10% weight
nf3012ddc5cc.x: The 16th FC cut the weight of area to 10%.
xa: **2011 population** raised to **17.5%**; **demographic performance** **10%**.
**Forest cover / ecology** kept at **10%**.

n7c075d97fc1.s: The award of the Thirteenth Finance Commission to undivided Andhra Pradesh was apportioned between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana under:
o: Section 46(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014
n7c075d97fc1.x: Section 46(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 provided for apportionment using population ratio and other parameters.
n7c075d97fc1.tq: Identify the exact statutory provision rather than a related constitutional Article.
xs: The **13th FC** award to undivided AP was split under **Sec 46(1)**, **AP Reorganisation Act 2014** — option **(4)**.
It was apportioned on **population ratio and other parameters**.
xa: The **13th FC** (**Vijay Kelkar**, **2010-15**) gave a **32%** share.
Post-bifurcation AP leaned on **14th and 15th FC revenue deficit grants**.

n742bd665aae.s: Which distinction was ended by the Fourteenth Finance Commission?
n742bd665aae.x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission ended the distinction between Plan and non-Plan expenditure.
xs: The **14th FC** ended the **Plan and non-Plan** distinction — option **(3)**.
It also made **tax devolution** the main route of transfers.
xa: 14th FC award: **2015-20**; chair **Y.V. Reddy**.
Local body grants: **₹2,87,436 cr** (panchayats **₹2,00,292 cr**).

n0ae1fb66779.s: The 13th Finance Commission (chaired by Vijay Kelkar) recommended what share of the divisible pool for the States?
n0ae1fb66779.x: The 13th FC (2010-15) recommended 32%. 29.5% was the 11th FC, 30.5% the 12th FC, and 42% the 14th FC, which raised the share by 10 points from the 13th FC's 32%.
xs: The **13th FC** (**Vijay Kelkar**) recommended a **32%** share — option **(3)**.
Its award period was **2010-15**.
xa: Its award to undivided AP was split under **Sec 46(1)**, AP Reorganisation Act **2014**.
The **14th FC** then made **tax devolution** the main route of transfers.
⚠ **12th** = **Rangarajan**; **13th** = **Kelkar**.

n5b2859e5bd5.s: The 16th Finance Commission raised the weight of population to:
n5b2859e5bd5.x: Population weight was raised to 17.5% and a GDP criterion was added; all five southern States saw their shares rise.

n8b1fad89506.s: The Fifteenth Finance Commission provided grants for Rural Local Bodies amounting to approximately:
n8b1fad89506.x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission provided ₹2.36 lakh crore for Rural Local Bodies during 2021–26. The Fourteenth Finance Commission gave gram panchayats about ₹2.00 lakh crore.
n8b1fad89506.tq: Separate successive commission amounts that are close in wording and subject.
xs: The **15th FC** gave **₹2.36 lakh cr** to **Rural Local Bodies** (**2021-26**) — option **(2)**.
The **14th FC** gave about **₹2.00 lakh cr**; **₹4.35 lakh cr** is the **16th FC** rural grant.
xa: 15th FC **urban** local bodies: **₹1.5 lakh cr**.
15th FC **total grants**: **₹10.1 lakh cr**.
14th FC total local body grants: **₹2,87,436 cr**.

n24d94a2710e.s: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended ₹4,800 crore for the period 2022–23 to 2025–26 to incentivise States for:
n24d94a2710e.x: An amount of ₹4,800 crore was recommended to incentivise States on educational outcomes during 2022–23 to 2025–26.
n24d94a2710e.tq: Match the specific amount and time period with its policy objective.
xs: The **15th FC**'s **₹4,800 cr** (**2022-23 to 2025-26**) rewards States' **educational outcomes** — option **(3)**.
Wastewater is a **16th FC** component (**₹56,100 cr**).
xa: This was a **UPSC 2025** PYQ.
15th FC total grants: **₹10.1 lakh cr**, including revenue deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants.

n2ee7c4a83e6.s: The 15th Finance Commission was mandated to use the population data of which Census?
n2ee7c4a83e6.x: Its terms of reference required 2011 population data, and also covered disaster-management financing and a non-lapsable defence fund.
xa: **Southern States** objected to the **2011 population** mandate (UPSC).
Chair: **N.K. Singh**, constituted **Nov 2017**.

n7bdac9b3758.s: Under the 16th Finance Commission, local bodies receive grants of about:
n7bdac9b3758.x: Of total grants of ₹9.47 lakh crore, local bodies get ₹7.91 lakh crore (rural 4.35, urban 3.56).
xa: Rural **₹4.35 lakh cr**, urban **₹3.56 lakh cr**.
No **revenue deficit grants** were recommended.

n5f7d24ca448.s: Under the 16th Finance Commission's disaster-funding framework, the Centre-State cost-sharing ratio for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and for other States is, respectively:
n5f7d24ca448.x: North-Eastern and Himalayan States share disaster funding 90:10 with the Centre; all other States share it 75:25. A reverses the two, and B and D give ratios the Commission did not recommend.
xs: Disaster cost-share: **90:10** for **NE/Himalayan** States and **75:25** for others — option **(3)**.
Option (1) reverses the two ratios.
xa: Disaster grants **₹1.55 lakh cr**; State corpus **₹2.04 lakh cr**.
**Heatwave and lightning** added as notified disasters.

n6f85745fcb9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Finance Commission grants and Andhra Pradesh?
o: 15th FC grants for 2024-25 and 2025-26 were drawn in advance by the previous government
AP's revenue deficit during 2014-19 was ₹48,000 crore
AP said it could lose up to ₹38,000 crore after the 16th FC dropped special grants
AP's projected revenue deficit for 2025-26 was ₹48,000 crore
n6f85745fcb9.x: AP's revenue deficit during 2014-19 was ₹16,000 crore; ₹48,000 crore was the projected revenue deficit for 2025-26.
xa: The **16th FC** recommended **no revenue deficit**, sector- or State-specific grants.
Post-bifurcation AP had leaned on **14th and 15th FC** revenue deficit grants + disaster funds.

n31c3f292a03.s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission was constituted on
n31c3f292a03.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission was constituted on 31 December 2023. Its report was tabled on 1 February 2026.
n31c3f292a03.tq: Separate the constitution date from the report-tabling date.
xs: The **16th FC** was constituted on **31 December 2023** — option **(4)**.
**1 Feb 2026** = report **tabled**; **1 Apr 2026** = award comes **into force**.
xa: ⚠ **UPPSC 2023** trap: constituted **2023**, not 2024.
Report submitted **17 Nov 2025**.
Chair: **Dr. Arvind Panagariya**.

n567701261f5.s: Post-bifurcation Andhra Pradesh depended substantially on which of the following sources for meeting its fiscal and disaster-related requirements?
o: 15th and 16th Finance Commission special category grants only
14th and 15th Finance Commission revenue deficit grants and disaster funds
Central plan assistance under the 12th Finance Commission
n567701261f5.x: Post-bifurcation Andhra Pradesh depended heavily on the revenue deficit grants and disaster funds provided through the 14th and 15th Finance Commissions.
n567701261f5.tq: Identify the correct Finance Commission pair linked with the State’s post-bifurcation support.
xs: Post-bifurcation AP depended on **14th and 15th FC revenue deficit grants** + **disaster funds** — option **(3)**.
The **16th FC** recommended **no revenue deficit grants**, so option (2) is wrong.
xa: AP could lose up to **₹38,000 cr** after FC-16 dropped special grants.

nb20c6d00c69.s: Which Article requires the President to lay the report of the Finance Commission before each House of Parliament along with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken?
nb20c6d00c69.x: Article 281 requires the President to lay the Finance Commission’s report before each House of Parliament together with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken.
nb20c6d00c69.tq: Distinguish the Article dealing with presentation of the report from the Article establishing the Commission and its functions.
xs: **Article 281** requires the President to lay the Finance Commission's report before **Parliament** with an action-taken memorandum — option **(3)** is correct.
**Article 280** is the provision under which the President **constitutes** the Commission, not the one on laying its report.
**Article 270** governs the **divisible pool** of shareable Union taxes; **Art. 243I** links the FC to State funds for **Panchayats**.
xa: The Finance Commission is a **quasi-judicial** body constituted **every 5 years** (5th year) or earlier.
Composition: **Chairman + 4 members**; qualifications under the **Finance Commission (Misc. Provisions) Act, 1951**.
Its recommendations are **advisory**, not binding on the government.

n6f935215b9f.s: The Finance Commission’s function of recommending measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State for supplementing the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities was added through the:
n6f935215b9f.x: The relevant function was added by the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, 1992, relating respectively to Panchayats and Municipalities.
n6f935215b9f.tq: Associate the local-government finance function with the constitutional amendments that strengthened local self-government.
xs: The local-body function was added by the **73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, 1992** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is **Art. 280(3)(bb) and (c)**: measures to augment a State's **Consolidated Fund** to support **Panchayats and Municipalities**.
It is linked to **Art. 243I** (Panchayats) and **Art. 243Y** (Municipalities).
xa: **Art. 280(3)(a)**: distribution of **net proceeds of shareable taxes**, vertical and horizontal.
**Art. 280(3)(b)**: principles for **grants-in-aid** (Art. 275) from the **Consolidated Fund of India**.
The **16th FC** gives only **local body** (**₹7.91 lakh crore**) and **disaster** grants.

n41ee428f5fd.s: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President every:
n41ee428f5fd.x: The quasi-judicial FC is constituted every fifth year or earlier; its recommendations are advisory.
xa: Report + action-taken memorandum laid before **Parliament** under **Art. 281**.
Composition: **Chairman + 4 members**; qualifications under the **Finance Commission (Misc. Provisions) Act, 1951**.
"The present Finance Commission" now means the **Sixteenth** (Chairman **Arvind Panagariya**).

nd1a33aa3bdb.s: Which of the following is NOT a duty of the Finance Commission under Article 280(3)?
o: Maintaining the income-expenditure accounts of the Union and State Governments
Recommending the distribution of the net proceeds of shareable taxes between the Centre and the States
Recommending principles governing grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of India
Recommending measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities
nd1a33aa3bdb.x: Maintaining government income-expenditure accounts is not a Finance Commission function. Its duties include tax devolution, grants-in-aid principles and augmentation of State funds for local bodies.
nd1a33aa3bdb.tq: Find the administrative accounting function that does not belong to the Finance Commission.
xs: **Maintaining the income-expenditure accounts** of the Union and States is NOT an FC duty — option **(1)** (the **APPSC-G2 2017** key).
Distribution of **net proceeds of shareable taxes** is **Art. 280(3)(a)**.
**Principles for grants-in-aid** from the **Consolidated Fund of India** is **Art. 280(3)(b)**.
Augmenting a State's **Consolidated Fund** for **Panchayats and Municipalities** is **Art. 280(3)(bb), (c)**.
xa: Also outside the FC: **cesses/surcharges**, **GST** revenue sharing (**GST Council**) and plan/discretionary grants.
**Art. 280(3)(d)**: any matter **referred by the President**.
Exam angle: "which is NOT a function" questions are a favourite on this topic.

n360f411dc8e.s: Which institution primarily deals with the sharing of GST revenue?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
n360f411dc8e.x: GST revenue-sharing recommendations are dealt with through the GST Council, not as a function of the Finance Commission.
n360f411dc8e.tq: Use institutional discrimination to separate closely related fiscal bodies.
xs: **GST** revenue sharing is dealt with by the **GST Council** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **Finance Commission** does **not** cover GST revenue sharing; it recommends sharing of the **divisible pool** and **grants-in-aid**.
The **CAG** figures only as certifier: the 16th FC recommends annual **CAG-certified** disclosure of net tax proceeds.
xa: The divisible pool includes **CGST** and the **Centre's IGST share** under **Art. 270**.
The FC also does not cover **cesses/surcharges** or plan/discretionary grants.
FC recommendations are **advisory**, not binding.

n5683e034d92.s: In the context of fiscal federalism in India, vertical devolution refers to
o: allocation of grants among local bodies
sharing of net tax proceeds between the Union and the States
distribution of the States' share among individual States
distribution of centrally sponsored schemes among districts
n5683e034d92.x: Vertical devolution means sharing net tax proceeds between the Union and the States. Distribution of the States' share among individual States is horizontal devolution.
n5683e034d92.tq: Distinguish the two closely related terms before considering the options.
xs: **Vertical devolution** = sharing of **net tax proceeds between the Union and the States** — option **(2)** is correct.
Distribution of the States' share **among individual States** is **horizontal devolution** (option 3).
Both are recommended under **Art. 280(3)(a)**.
xa: **Divisible pool**: taxes under **Art. 270** (corporation tax, income tax, **CGST**, Centre's **IGST** share).
**Tax devolution** under Art. 270 is **untied**.
Vertical share now **41%** (15th and 16th FCs).

nc45024ea5ce.s: Article 275 grants are NOT generally meant for:
o: Welfare of Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Areas
nc45024ea5ce.x: Article 275 grants support revenue deficits, local bodies, disasters and tribal welfare, not every CSS.
xa: Art. 275 grants are recommended by the **Finance Commission** and **charged on the CFI**.
The **16th FC** gives only **local body** + **disaster** grants (total **₹9.47 lakh crore**).
The **15th FC** gave RD, sector-specific and State-specific grants totalling **₹10.1 lakh crore**.

n883d434da8c.s: Which approach was associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission’s treatment of Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
o: Linking them to measurable outcomes and reviewing inefficient schemes
Charging all CSS directly to the Consolidated Fund of India as Article 275 grants
Transferring their administration exclusively to local bodies
