n3ef1370b3c0.x: Fiscal deficit is financed through market borrowings, small savings or NSSF, provident funds and external loans. Routine PSU dividends are revenue non-tax receipts, not a financing source of fiscal deficit in this classification.
n3ef1370b3c0.tq: Find the revenue receipt that is not a borrowing or financing channel.
xs: **Routine dividends from public-sector undertakings** are NOT listed as a source of financing the fiscal deficit — option **(1)**.
Listed sources: **market borrowings** (dated G-Secs, T-bills, bonds), **small savings / NSSF**, provident funds and **external loans**.
xa: Net home borrowing also includes indirect borrowing from banks via **SLR**.
Budget 2026-27: **borrowings and other liabilities = 24 paise** of every rupee of receipts — the largest single item.
Non-debt receipts include **disinvestment** and **asset monetisation**.

nb927f797b55.s: Which of the following is an expenditure-side measure for reducing fiscal deficit?
nb927f797b55.x: Rationalising subsidies through direct benefit transfer is an expenditure-side deficit-reduction measure. Tax-base expansion and disinvestment operate on the revenue or receipts side.
nb927f797b55.tq: Identify the side of the budget on which the measure operates.
xs: **Rationalising subsidies through DBT** is an **expenditure-side** measure — option **(4)**.
Direct-tax collection, **widening the tax base** and **disinvestment** are **revenue-side** measures.
xa: Another expenditure measure: cut **unproductive revenue spending**.
Check capital-asset grants are not diverted (**CAG**, **NITI Aayog**).
**Asset monetisation** gives **non-debt receipts**.

n4bc15b9a054.s: The target for the central debt-GDP ratio by March 2031 is
n4bc15b9a054.x: The target is 50 ± 1% by March 2031. Central debt is projected at 55.6% in BE 2026-27.
n4bc15b9a054.tq: Use the exact target range rather than confusing it with the general government debt ceiling.
xs: The central debt-GDP target is **50 ± 1% by March 2031** — option **(2)**.
It comes under the **debt-anchor rule** that operates from **2026-27**.
**60%** was the FRBM (2018) general-government ceiling and **40%** the Centre's FRBM ceiling — not the 2031 target.
xa: ⚠ The debt anchor allows a higher debt ratio than FRBM's **40%** (2 Feb 2026 critique).
FD target for 2026-27: **4.3%** of GDP.

n473b0a62613.s: Who was the first to develop a theory linking fiscal policy with economic performance in the modern sense?
n473b0a62613.x: J. M. Keynes developed the theory linking fiscal policy with economic performance. His General Theory was published in 1936 and formed the basis of active demand management.
n473b0a62613.tq: Use the economist-contribution association rather than the similarly named fiscal-policy committee figures.
xs: **J.M. Keynes** first developed a theory linking fiscal policy with economic performance — option **(3)**.
His **General Theory** (**1936**) became the basis of **active demand management**.
**V.P. Singh** presented the Long-Term Fiscal Policy (**1985**); **N.K. Singh** headed the **2016** FRBM review committee.
xa: **Richard Musgrave** gave the three budget functions and popularised **fiscal federalism** (**1959**).
N.K. Singh Committee debt anchor: **60%** = Centre **40%** + States **20%**.
Fiscal policy influences **aggregate demand**, allocation and distribution.

nef24c76e6d8.s: The Long-Term Fiscal Policy of India, announced in 1985, was presented by
nef24c76e6d8.x: India's Long-Term Fiscal Policy was presented in 1985 by Finance Minister V. P. Singh.
xs: The Long-Term Fiscal Policy (**1985**) was presented by Finance Minister **V.P. Singh** — option **(1)**.
It is listed among the FIRSTs of Indian fiscal policy.
xa: **J.M. Keynes** (General Theory, **1936**) first linked fiscal policy to economic performance.
**FRBM Act 2003**: FD **3%**, RD zero; amended **2018**.
**N.K. Singh** Committee **2016**, report **2017**.

nf91853628af.s: The N. K. Singh Committee's debt-anchor framework referred to general government debt of
o: 60% of GDP, comprising Centre 40% and States 20%
70% of GDP, comprising Centre 40% and States 30%
60% of GDP, comprising Centre 50% and States 10%
50% of GDP, comprising Centre 30% and States 20%
nf91853628af.x: The N. K. Singh Committee recommended a general government debt anchor of 60% of GDP, divided into 40% for the Centre and 20% for the States.
nf91853628af.tq: Separate the aggregate debt anchor from its Centre-State components.
xs: N.K. Singh Committee debt anchor: **60% of GDP = Centre 40% + States 20%** — option **(1)**.
Committee set up in **2016**, report in **2017**.
The **FRBM (2018)** ceilings adopted this: general govt debt **60%**, **Centre 40%** by **Mar 2025**.
xa: FRBM (2018) also set **FD 3% by Mar 2021**.
New target: central debt **50 ± 1% by March 2031**.
⚠ S&P says general government debt is **above 80% of GDP**.

nea843b00574.s: The original FRBM Act, 2003 targeted which of the following for the Union Government?
o: Fiscal deficit 3% of GDP and revenue deficit eliminated
Fiscal deficit 4.5% of GDP and revenue deficit 2% of GDP
Fiscal deficit eliminated and revenue deficit 3% of GDP
Debt-GDP ratio of 50% and fiscal deficit 4.3% of GDP
nea843b00574.x: The FRBM Act, 2003 set the fiscal deficit target at 3% of GDP and revenue deficit at zero; it was amended in 2018. 4.5% was the FY22 glide-path commitment for 2025-26; 50 ± 1% debt by 2031 and FD 4.3% belong to the 2026-27 debt-anchor framework; FD was never targeted at zero.
xs: The **FRBM Act 2003** targeted **fiscal deficit 3%** of GDP and **revenue deficit zero** — option **(1)**.
It was **amended in 2018**.
**4.5%** was the FY 2021-22 commitment for **2025-26**; **50 ± 1%** debt and FD **4.3%** belong to the later debt-anchor phase.
xa: FRBM (2018): **FD 3% by Mar 2021**; general govt debt **60%**; **Centre 40%** by **Mar 2025**.
FRBM bars the RBI from subscribing to **primary issues** of G-Secs from **2006-07**, except under the **escape clause**.
**ERD** was written into FRBM by the **2012 amendment**.

n336ce18f50e.s: Which one of the following is NOT an objective of fiscal policy?
o: Management of money supply and liquidity
n336ce18f50e.x: Managing liquidity and money supply is an objective of monetary policy, not fiscal policy. Fiscal policy objectives include employment, price stability, growth, redistribution, mobilisation and regional balance.
n336ce18f50e.tq: Find the monetary-policy function among the fiscal-policy objectives.
xs: **Management of money supply and liquidity** is NOT a fiscal-policy objective — option **(2)**.
Managing liquidity, money supply and directing interest rates belong to **monetary policy**.
**Full employment**, **price stability** and **balanced regional development** are fiscal-policy objectives.
xa: ⚠ "Directing interest rates" was an APPSC GS **2023** distractor.
Other objectives: **economic growth**, **equitable distribution** of income and wealth, **resource mobilisation**.
Monetary tools: **Repo, CRR, SLR, OMOs, LAF** (RBI / MPC).

n64017341227.s: According to the Economic Survey 2016-17, public expenditure in India (Centre and States combined) is about what share of GDP?
n64017341227.x: Public expenditure of the Centre and States together is about 28% of GDP (ES 2016-17; asked in APPSC G2 2017). 13% is close to Union expenditure alone (13.6% in BE 2026-27); 18% and 40% are not the cited figure.
xs: Public expenditure in India is about **28% of GDP** (ES **2016-17**) — option **(3)**.
This was asked in APPSC G2 **2017**.
xa: Public expenditure is a fiscal tool; capex is used as **"pump priming"**.
Capex in BE 2026-27: **₹12.2 lakh crore** (up from ₹11.2 lakh crore).
**Capex multiplier** estimated at **2.5-3** in India.

n776b1953fba.s: From 2006-07, the FRBM framework bars the RBI, in normal times, from:
o: Subscribing to primary issues of Government securities
Acting as banker to the States
n776b1953fba.x: The RBI cannot subscribe to primary issues of G-Secs except under the escape clause.
xa: **Monetised deficit** = part of the deficit financed by the **RBI** → inflationary.
**Ad hoc T-bills** abolished from **1 April 1997** (**1994** agreement).
**FRBM Act 2003**: FD **3%**, RD zero; amended **2018**.

nba0c257f7e3.s: Under the FY 2021-22 glide path, the Union fiscal deficit was to be brought below what share of GDP by 2025-26?
nba0c257f7e3.x: The commitment was below 4.5% of GDP by 2025-26 (met at 4.4%); from 2026-27 the fiscal deficit is calibrated each year to keep the debt-GDP ratio falling.
xa: Debt target: **50 ± 1% by March 2031**.
FY27 BE fiscal deficit: **4.3%** of GDP (~**₹16.96 lakh crore**).
COVID peak FD in **2020-21**: **9.2%** of GDP.

nffeb27e426e.s: Resource mobilisation, equitable distribution and balanced regional development are objectives of:
nffeb27e426e.x: Economic growth, equitable distribution, resource mobilisation and balanced regional development are all objectives of fiscal policy.
xa: Also: **full employment** and **price stability**.
NOT fiscal objectives: **directing interest rates**, managing **liquidity and money supply** (monetary policy).
Direct taxes = **58.8%** of total taxes in **FY25** — evidence of progressive taxation.

n44282143bce.s: Which of the following is NOT an instrument of fiscal policy?
n44282143bce.x: The repo rate is a monetary policy tool of the RBI/MPC; the others are fiscal tools of the Government.
xa: Other fiscal tools: **public expenditure** (capex as **"pump priming"**), the **budget**, **PLI**.
Monetary tools: **Repo, CRR, SLR, OMOs, LAF**.
Trade policy (Ministry of Commerce): **tariffs, quotas, export incentives**.

n8cdc5e5e55a.s: Monetary policy can act relatively quickly because the MPC takes decisions:
n8cdc5e5e55a.x: The MPC decides bi-monthly, whereas fiscal policy works through the slower budget cycle.
xa: Fiscal authority: **Govt (MoF)**; monetary authority: **RBI / MPC**.
Fiscal tools: **taxation, public expenditure, public debt, subsidies**, DBT, PLI.
Monetary tools: **Repo, CRR, SLR, OMOs, LAF**.

n57db492c3a7.s: If the Fiscal Deficit is ₹4 crore and GDP is ₹400 crore, the Fiscal Deficit as a percentage of GDP will be:
n57db492c3a7.x: Fiscal Deficit as a percentage of GDP = (₹4 crore ÷ ₹400 crore) × 100 = 1 percent.
n57db492c3a7.tq: Convert the deficit-to-GDP ratio into a percentage by multiplying by 100.
xs: FD as % of GDP = **4 / 400 × 100 = 1 percent** — option **(2)**.
The notes give exactly this example: FD **4** on GDP **400** = **1% of GDP**.
xa: FD target for 2026-27 is ~**₹16.96 lakh crore**.

n822ce9894bf.s: From 1 April 1997, ad hoc Treasury Bills were replaced by:
n822ce9894bf.x: Ad hoc T-bills, which meant automatic monetisation, were replaced by WMA; an overdraft is only use of WMA beyond the limit.
xa: The phase-out began with the **1994** RBI-Government agreement.
**Budget deficit** stopped being the headline measure after ad hoc T-bills ended.
**FRBM:** RBI barred from **primary issues** from **2006-07**, except under the **escape clause**.

n6be3c9268c6.s: Use of Ways and Means Advances beyond the permitted limit is called:
n6be3c9268c6.x: WMA are temporary RBI advances for cash mismatches; using them beyond the limit is an overdraft.
xa: WMA replaced **ad hoc Treasury Bills** from **1 April 1997**.
RBI money creation → **money supply ↑** → **inflation** — the **most inflationary route**.
**Borrowings and other liabilities** = **24 paise** of every rupee of receipts (**2026-27**).

n6c4ada0bd2f.s: A fiscal stance that runs deficits in recessions and consolidates in booms is called:
n6c4ada0bd2f.x: Counter-cyclical policy runs deficits in slumps (e.g. Atma Nirbhar Bharat, 2020); pro-cyclical policy deepens volatility.
xa: Recession response: **more spending on public projects** (UPSC PYQ).
**Neutral** stance: balanced effect on demand → stable equilibrium.
Related terms: **fiscal drag**, **pump priming**, **fiscal neutrality**.

n219700b05fc.s: With reference to Union Government deficits, which one of the following correctly represents the fiscal deficit in 2020-21 and 2026-27 (BE), respectively?
n219700b05fc.x: The fiscal deficit was 9.2% of GDP in 2020-21, the peak shown in the series, and is estimated at 4.3% in 2026-27 (BE).
n219700b05fc.tq: Split the options by the two years and match the fiscal-deficit column precisely.
xs: **4.8%** was FY25 actual; **7.3%** and **1.5%** are RD figures; **8.4%** was **1990-91** gross FD.
xa: Consolidation **9.2% → 4.4%** brought **three sovereign rating upgrades in 2025**.
FD target 2026-27: ~**₹16.96 lakh crore**.

n97fe157ea24.s: The gross fiscal deficit of the Union Government reached the earlier peak of 8.4% of GDP in:
n97fe157ea24.x: The earlier gross fiscal-deficit peak was 8.4% of GDP in 1990-91.
n97fe157ea24.tq: Discriminate between adjacent crisis-period years using the exact benchmark year.
xs: Gross fiscal deficit was **8.4% of GDP** in **1990-91** — option **(1)**.
This was the historical peak before the COVID year.

na87dad76f99.s: Tax concessions and cheap credit are examples of:
na87dad76f99.x: Tax concessions and cheap credit can constitute hidden subsidies.
xa: Explicit subsidies: **food, fertiliser, export** and **interest** subsidies.
Implicit subsidies: under-pricing of **education, health** and other public services.

n92e776aeaa8.s: India's fiscal deficit declined from 9.2 per cent to ____ per cent during its fiscal consolidation.
n92e776aeaa8.x: The decline from 9.2 to 4.4 per cent was linked to three sovereign rating upgrades in 2025 by Morningstar DBRS, S&P and R&I.
xa: ⚠ The marginal **4.4% → 4.3%** step is criticised for slowing rating upgrades.
**9.2%** was the COVID peak FD in **2020-21**.

n842ece2513a.s: Public borrowing used to finance the Fiscal Deficit may be classified as:
o: Only external borrowing through multilateral institutions
n842ece2513a.x: Public borrowing may be internal, such as bonds, Treasury Bills and small savings, or external, such as multilateral borrowing and sovereign bonds. It finances the Fiscal Deficit.
n842ece2513a.tq: Identify the complete classification and reject the ‘only’ alternatives.
xs: Public borrowing is **internal** and **external** — option **(2)**.
**Internal** = bonds, T-bills, small savings; **External** = multilateral loans, sovereign bonds.
Public borrowing **finances the fiscal deficit**; taxation is not borrowing.
xa: Other sources: **market borrowings** (dated G-Secs), **small savings / NSSF**, provident funds.
Net home borrowing includes indirect borrowing from banks via **SLR**.
Budget 2026-27: **borrowings and other liabilities = 24 paise** of every rupee of receipts.

ncf96498bdbc.s: A zero primary deficit means the government borrows only to:
ncf96498bdbc.x: Zero PD means FD equals interest payments, so borrowing only services past debt, a debt-trap signal.
xa: **Debt trap** = borrowing to make interest payments.
**FD** always equals **borrowings and other liabilities**.

n90512fb6d5a.s: Which way of financing a deficit may expose the economy to currency risk?
n90512fb6d5a.x: External borrowing creates currency risk; RBI financing creates money and public borrowing absorbs liquidity.
xa: Money-printing = the **most inflationary route**.
**Crowding out**: heavy govt borrowing pushes up interest rates → **private investment falls**.
Ad hoc T-bills (automatic monetisation) abolished from **1 April 1997**.

n0a07d34a33b.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the most desirable source for financing a current account deficit?
n0a07d34a33b.x: Foreign direct investment is identified as the most desirable source of CAD financing. FPI is volatile, while other sources include ECBs, NRI deposits, reserve drawdown and multilateral loans.
n0a07d34a33b.tq: Compare external financing sources by stability and desirability rather than merely identifying a foreign source.
xs: **Foreign direct investment** is the **most desirable** CAD financing source — option **(1)**.
**FPI** is **volatile**; forex reserve drawdown and **ECBs** are other, less preferred, sources.
xa: Other sources: **NRI deposits**, **IMF/World Bank** loans.
**Twin deficit** = fiscal deficit + current account deficit.

n9d420530818.s: The fiscal multiplier is defined as:
o: Fiscal Deficit divided by Primary Deficit
Change in government spending divided by change in GDP
Change in GDP divided by change in government spending or taxes
Total tax revenue divided by total expenditure
n9d420530818.x: The fiscal multiplier measures the change in GDP resulting from a change in government spending or taxes. It is expressed as change in GDP divided by the change in government spending or taxes.
n9d420530818.tq: Recall the direction of the multiplier formula carefully.
xs: **Fiscal multiplier = change in GDP / change in government spending or taxes** — option **(3)**.
Option (2) inverts the ratio.
xa: **Capex multiplier** in India estimated at **2.5-3**.
It is larger for **capital expenditure** than for revenue spending or transfers.
**Crowding in**: public capex draws private investment.

nd2ddd155535.s: 'Crowding out' in fiscal policy refers to a situation in which:
o: Heavy government borrowing pushes up interest rates and private investment falls
Public capital expenditure creates infrastructure that draws in private investment
Government cuts spending in a slump and raises it in a boom
Rising incomes push taxpayers into higher tax brackets and slow demand
nd2ddd155535.x: Crowding out: heavy government borrowing absorbs loanable funds, pushes up interest rates and reduces private investment (UPSC 2026). Public capex attracting private investment is crowding in; cutting in slumps and spending in booms is pro-cyclical policy; bracket creep slowing demand is fiscal drag.
nd2ddd155535.tq: Crowding out = govt borrowing up, rates up, private investment down.
xs: **Crowding out**: **heavy government borrowing pushes up interest rates and private investment falls** — option **(1)** (UPSC **2026** key).
Public capex drawing private investment is **crowding in**.
Cutting in a slump and spending in a boom is **pro-cyclical** policy.
xa: Borrowing from the public **absorbs liquidity** and can slow private activity.
**Capex multiplier** estimated at **2.5-3** in India.

n361619284f1.s: Under the national Direct Benefit Transfer system for fertiliser rolled out in 2018, subsidy is released to companies after:
o: Retail sale is recorded through PoS machines with Aadhaar authentication of the buyer
The State Legislature approves each individual transaction
The fertiliser is manufactured, without any retail verification
The buyer submits a post-purchase paper claim to the Finance Ministry
n361619284f1.x: Under fertiliser DBT, retail sale is recorded on PoS machines and the buyer is authenticated through Aadhaar; the subsidy is then released to the companies.
n361619284f1.tq: Follow the transaction sequence and identify the point at which the subsidy is released.
xs: Subsidy is paid **after retail sale is recorded through PoS machines with Aadhaar authentication of the buyer** — option **(1)**.
This is the **DBT in fertiliser** system, national rollout **2018**.
xa: **Urea** is the largest fertiliser subsidy item.
Rationalising subsidies via **DBT** is an **expenditure-side** deficit-reduction measure.

n7a5da11c28c.s: Budget deficit plus borrowings and other liabilities of the Government is equal to:
n7a5da11c28c.x: Fiscal deficit = budget deficit + borrowings and other liabilities (APPSC 2019). Revenue deficit is revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts; primary deficit is FD minus interest payments; monetised deficit is the part financed by the RBI.
xs: **Budget deficit + borrowings and other liabilities = Fiscal deficit** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2019**).
**Revenue deficit** = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts; **primary deficit** = FD − interest payments.
**Monetised deficit** = the part financed by the **RBI**.
xa: FD always equals **borrowings and other liabilities**.
FD = **total expenditure − total receipts excluding borrowings**.

nfd4b9262c65.s: Under the original FRBM Act, 2003, the fiscal deficit was to be brought down to 3% of GDP by:
nfd4b9262c65.x: FD was to reach 3% by 31 March 2008; the revenue deficit was to be eliminated by 31 March 2009.
xa: The **tax-GDP ratio** was never a legal target; it is one of the four indicators in the **Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement**.
The FRBM Act was introduced by **Yashwant Sinha** and enacted in **2003**; Rules notified **2004**.
⚠ The **2018 amendment** later reset the FD target to **3% by 31 March 2021** and dropped RD/ERD targets.

nb7680ee2661.s: The FRBM Act, 2003 was introduced by Finance Minister:
nb7680ee2661.x: Yashwant Sinha introduced the FRBM Act; its Rules came into force on 5 July 2004.
xa: First Budget in India: **1860**, by **James Wilson**.
First Budget of free India: **1947**, by **R.K. Shanmugham Chetty**.
Original legal targets: **FD 3% of GDP by 31 March 2008**; **revenue deficit eliminated by 31 March 2009**.

n9f351d49433.s: Which one of the following is NOT an objective of the FRBM Act, 2003?
n9f351d49433.x: The FRBM Act aims at inter-generational equity, long-run macroeconomic stability, elimination of the revenue deficit and reduction of the fiscal deficit, fiscal discipline, transparency and a balanced budget over time. Fixing the repo rate is a monetary-policy function of the RBI's MPC, not an FRBM objective.
n9f351d49433.tq: FRBM objectives: equity across generations, RD elimination, transparency.
xs: **Fixing the policy repo rate** is NOT an FRBM objective — option **(4)**.
FRBM objectives: **inter-generational equity**, long-run macroeconomic stability, **elimination of the revenue deficit**, reduction of FD.
It also seeks to institutionalise fiscal discipline, **transparency** and a **balanced budget** over time — so options (1), (2) and (3) are objectives.
xa: The Act was introduced by **Yashwant Sinha** and enacted in **2003** for **fiscal discipline** (APPSC 2019).
FRBM Rules notified **2004**, in force from **5 July 2004**.
Original annual reduction under the Rules: **FD by 0.3%** and **RD by 0.5%** of GDP each year.

n57fa7e7ad4a.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the FRBM framework?
o: Penal provisions automatically applicable when targets are missed
Disclosure of borrowings and contingent liabilities
n57fa7e7ad4a.x: The FRBM framework does not provide penal provisions for missing the prescribed targets. It does provide deficit limits, transparency disclosures and fiscal statements.
n57fa7e7ad4a.tq: Test the favourite FRBM trap by distinguishing compliance requirements from penal consequences.
xs: **Penal provisions** for missing targets are NOT a feature of FRBM — option **(1)**.
The Act does **not provide penal provisions** for missing targets (APPSC-G2 2017) — the favourite exam trap.
It does prescribe **deficit limits**, **statements laid with the Budget** and **disclosure of borrowings and contingent liabilities** — options (2), (3), (4).
xa: Additional guarantees against the **Consolidated Fund** are capped at **0.5% of GDP** a year.
FRBM does not make the Centre answerable for **States' failures**; States have their own Acts.
Design gap critics cite: **no penalty clause** and **no independent fiscal council** yet.

n6e44aa5521e.s: The additional guarantees issued against the Consolidated Fund in a year are capped at:
n6e44aa5521e.x: Additional guarantees against the Consolidated Fund are capped at 0.5% of GDP in a year.
n6e44aa5521e.tq: Recall the annual ceiling and avoid confusing it with the fiscal-deficit target.
xs: Additional guarantees against the **Consolidated Fund** are capped at **0.50% of GDP** a year — option **(2)**.
This cap is part of what FRBM **prescribes**, along with deficit limits and transparency disclosures.
⚠ **3%** is the FD target; **0.25%** is the buoyancy-clause FD cut — not the guarantee cap.
xa: Escape-clause deviation is also capped at **0.5% of GDP** in a year.
The Act has **no penal provisions** for missing targets.
Buoyancy clause: FD must fall by **at least 0.25% of GDP** when growth rises sharply.

n279e7e8dca4.s: From which year were the FRBM three-year rolling fiscal targets suspended to give post-pandemic flexibility?
n279e7e8dca4.x: The three-year rolling targets were suspended from 2021-22 to provide flexibility in the post-pandemic period.
xa: COVID year **2020-21**: FD peaked at **9.2% of GDP**; the escape clause was used without a fresh amendment.
The **2025-26** FD target "below **4.5%**" (set in FY 2021-22) was met at **4.4%**.
Budget 2026-27 shifted to a **debt-GDP rule** (**50 ± 1% by 2031**).

n4089495541e.s: The fiscal responsibility limits under the Andhra Pradesh FRBM framework mainly restrain the State's:
n4089495541e.x: AP's FRBM limits impose fiscal and borrowing discipline, restraining its open-market borrowing.
xa: Slippage: borrowings **₹81,071 crore**; FD **5.05%** vs **4%** ceiling (7 Mar 2026).

nbeccb2f84ec.s: The 2004 Task Force on Implementation of the FRBM Act was chaired by:
nbeccb2f84ec.x: Vijay Kelkar chaired it and recommended tax reform and a comprehensive GST; he later headed the Thirteenth FC.
xa: ⚠ **Kelkar 2004** = implementing FRBM; **N.K. Singh 2016-17** = reviewing FRBM, **debt anchor**.
The **FRBM Act** was introduced by **Yashwant Sinha**; enacted **August 2003**.
FRBM came into effect on **5 July 2004**.

n5ca1cea60d6.s: The recommendations of the N.K. Singh FRBM Review Committee were reflected in which Union Budget?
n5ca1cea60d6.x: The committee was announced in Budget 2016-17, and its recommendations were reflected in Budget 2017-18.
n5ca1cea60d6.tq: Separate the announcement of a committee from the later Budget reflecting its recommendations.
xs: The N.K. Singh Committee's recommendations were reflected in **Budget 2017-18** — option **(3)**.
The committee was announced in **Budget 2016-17**, constituted in **2016**, and reported in **2017**.
The **2018 amendment** later wrote its **debt anchor** and **escape clause** into the Act.
xa: It recommended **FD 3% of GDP** for the next three years, then a lower glide path.
Escape clause: deviation up to **0.5% of GDP** on defined grounds.
APPSC-G2 2017 asked the head of the FRBM review panel = **N.K. Singh**.

n7413ef7157e.s: The Fiscal Council recommended by the N.K. Singh Committee was envisaged as:
o: A department of the Reserve Bank of India
A committee of Parliament with executive powers
A body with binding powers over the Budget
n7413ef7157e.x: The proposed Fiscal Council was an independent, advisory institution without binding executive or judicial powers.
xa: The committee made **debt** the principal anchor: general govt **60% of GDP by 2023** (Centre **40%** + States **20%**).
It also recommended an escape clause with deviation up to **0.5% of GDP**.
Another design gap critics cite: **no penalty clause**.

n440a83f0e00.s: With regard to fiscal discipline, States generally operate under:
o: The Union FRBM Act, applied identically
Rules framed by the Finance Commission
n440a83f0e00.x: States have their own fiscal responsibility Acts; the Union FRBM framework does not automatically apply to them.
xa: States enacted their laws mostly after the **12th FC** tied debt relief (**Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility**) to it.
AP's law: **Andhra Pradesh FRBM Act, 2005** — eliminate RD, FD at **3% of GSDP**.
The FRBM Act also provides **no penal provisions** for missing targets.

n59940fda81a.s: The N.K. Singh FRBM Review Committee recommended which indicator as the principal fiscal anchor?
n59940fda81a.x: Debt-to-GDP was the principal anchor and fiscal deficit the operational target, with general government debt at 60% by 2023.
xa: Other recommendations: **FD 3% of GDP** for three years; **RD 0.8% of GDP by 2023**; an independent advisory **Fiscal Council**.
⚠ The new 2026-27 debt rule targets Central debt of **50 ± 1%** by **2031** — above FRBM's **40%**.
The **2018 amendment** set general govt **60%**, Centre **40%** by **31 March 2025**.

nd40f0caa93e.s: The debt anchor and escape-clause recommendations of the N.K. Singh Committee were incorporated into the FRBM Act through which amendment?
nd40f0caa93e.x: The committee's debt anchor and escape clause were written into the FRBM Act through the 2018 amendment.
nd40f0caa93e.tq: Match the substantive institutional change with the later amendment, not the amendment that added expenditure projections.
xs: The debt anchor and escape clause were written into the Act by the **2018 amendment** — option **(1)**.
2018 also set **FD 3% by 31 March 2021**, dropped RD/ERD targets and added a **buoyancy clause**.
**2012** added ERD and the MTEFS; **2015** deferred target dates — neither brought the debt anchor.
xa: 2018 debt anchor: general govt **60%**, Centre **40%** by **31 March 2025**.
The escape-clause deviation is capped at **0.5% of GDP**.
The Act is now cited as "**FRBM Act, 2003 (amended 2018)**".

n32158396316.s: The 2018 amendment to the FRBM framework envisaged which combination of targets?
o: Fiscal deficit of 3% by 31 March 2021, general government debt of 60% and Central debt of 40% by 31 March 2025
Fiscal deficit of 3% by 31 March 2018 and Central debt of 50% by 2025
Fiscal deficit of 4.5% by 31 March 2025, general government debt of 50% and Central debt of 30% by 2031
Revenue deficit of zero and Central debt of 60% by 31 March 2021
n32158396316.x: The 2018 amendment set a 3% fiscal-deficit target by 31 March 2021 and debt anchors of 60% for general government and 40% for the Centre by 31 March 2025.
n32158396316.tq: Combine the year, date and multiple numerical targets without swapping their deadlines.
xs: The 2018 amendment set **FD 3% by 31 March 2021**, general govt debt **60%** and Central debt **40% by 31 March 2025** — option **(1)**.
It also dropped RD/ERD targets and added an **escape clause** (**0.5%** cap) and a **buoyancy clause**.
The **50%** Central debt by **2031** figure belongs to the new **2026-27** debt rule, not the 2018 amendment.
xa: The Government has acknowledged **deviation** from the Act's **3% FD** and **40% Central debt** targets.
COVID **2020-21**: FD **9.2%**; escape clause used, no amendment.

nb64424eed15.s: During COVID-19 in 2020–21, India's fiscal deficit was recorded at:
nb64424eed15.x: The fiscal deficit reached 9.2 per cent of GDP in 2020–21, after which targets were recalibrated with a gradual return path.
xa: The commitment to halve the 2020-21 FD in five years was met: **4.4% in 2025-26**.
In **2020-21** the escape clause was used with no amendment, to keep flexibility.

n0b2dfd78d1b.s: Which of the following is NOT a ground for invoking the FRBM escape clause?
o: Sharp fall in real output growth
Routine tax shortfall due to administrative delay
n0b2dfd78d1b.x: Grounds include national security, war, calamity, agricultural collapse, structural reforms and a sharp output fall, not routine administrative delays.
xa: Deviation limit: **not more than 0.5% of GDP** in a year.
The government must justify the deviation and give a return path, placed before **Parliament**.
⚠ Escape clause = deviation up to **0.5%**; buoyancy clause = FD cut of at least **0.25%**.

n5802e51028d.s: When the FRBM escape clause is invoked, the Government must place before Parliament:
o: An RBI approval for the deviation
A justification and a path back to the target
n5802e51028d.x: The Government must justify the deviation (capped at 0.5% of GDP) and lay a path back to the target before Parliament.
xa: Grounds: **national security, war, national calamity**, collapse of agriculture, **structural reforms**, severe slowdown.
Slowdown test: real output growth **3 percentage points** below the average of the previous four quarters.
⚠ **Buoyancy clause:** FD must fall by **at least 0.25%** if growth rises sharply.

nc8dfcd4d9b4.s: The commitment to halve the 2020-21 fiscal deficit within five years was fulfilled when the fiscal deficit reached:
nc8dfcd4d9b4.x: The 2020-21 fiscal deficit of 9.2% was more than halved to 4.4% in 2025-26. This was a commitment, not a legislative target.
nc8dfcd4d9b4.tq: Calculate the direction of change while retaining the distinction between a commitment and a statutory target.
xs: The halving commitment was met when FD reached **4.4% of GDP in 2025-26** — option **(3)**.
**2020-21** FD was **9.2%**; halving it in five years was a commitment, **not a legislative target**.
xa: The **2025-26** target "below **4.5%**" (set in FY 2021-22) was met.
The **16th FC** path: Centre FD **3.5% of GDP by 2030-31**.

n4224e6a9d24.s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission described State fiscal rules as:
n4224e6a9d24.x: It called State fiscal rules 'effectively unenforced' and sought a wider deficit definition covering off-budget borrowing.
xa: **AP FRBM Act, 2005**: eliminate the revenue deficit; FD at **3% of GSDP**.

ncf0e536984b.s: The newer debt anchor targets debt of ____ of GDP by 2031.
ncf0e536984b.x: The new anchor is 50 ± 1 per cent by 2031, criticised as tolerating more debt than the 40 per cent associated with FRBM.
xa: Central debt in **BE 2026-27**: **55.6%** of GDP; FD **4.3%**.
Under the new rule, **debt**, not FD, is the primary target.
Experts want a published debt and FD glide path with a **nominal GDP** assumption (5 Feb 2026).

nc2df4070c15.s: Who presented the first Budget in India in 1860?
nc2df4070c15.x: James Wilson presented India's first Budget in 1860; R.K. Shanmukham Chetty presented free India's first Budget in 1947.
xa: **Vijay Kelkar** chaired the **Task Force on Implementation of the FRBM Act, 2004** and the **13th Finance Commission** (**2010-15**).
The FRBM Act was introduced by **Yashwant Sinha** and enacted in **2003**.
FRBM Rules came into force on **5 July 2004**.

n4d849b378f6.s: The FRBM escape clause can be triggered when real output growth falls ____ percentage points below the average of the previous four quarters.
n4d849b378f6.x: One escape-clause trigger is a fall in real output growth by 3 percentage points below the average of the previous four quarters.
xa: Deviation under the escape clause: **not more than 0.5% of GDP** in a year.
Buoyancy clause: if growth rises sharply, FD must fall by **at least 0.25% of GDP**.

n32fa00bc111.s: Under the buoyancy clause of the 2018 FRBM amendment, a sharp rise in real output growth requires the fiscal deficit to fall by at least:
n32fa00bc111.x: The buoyancy clause requires at least a 0.25% of GDP cut in the fiscal deficit; it never permits an automatic increase.
xa: ⚠ Escape clause = deviation up to **0.5%**; buoyancy clause = FD cut of at least **0.25%**.
2018 also set the **debt anchor**: general govt **60%**, Centre **40%** by **31 March 2025**.

n4523b10dbe2.s: Which one of the following correctly states the fiscal-deficit recommendations associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: Centre 3.5% of GDP and States 3% of GSDP by 2030-31
Centre 4.3% of GDP and States 3% of GSDP by 2026-27
Centre 3.5% of GDP and States 4% of GSDP by 2030-31
Centre 3% of GDP and States 3.5% of GSDP by 2030-31
n4523b10dbe2.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended that the Centre reach a fiscal deficit of 3.5% of GDP and States reach 3% of GSDP by 2030-31.
n4523b10dbe2.tq: Keep the Centre and State limits separate before comparing the two figures.
xs: The **16th FC**: Centre FD **3.5% of GDP** and States **3% of GSDP** by **2030-31** — option **(1)**.
**4.3%** is the Centre's FD in **2026-27 BE**, not an FC recommendation.
**4%** of GSDP was the **15th FC** State borrowing limit for **2021-22**.
xa: The 16th FC also asked for State fiscal-rule reform and a wider deficit definition covering **off-budget borrowing**.
It found State fiscal rules "**effectively unenforced**".
⚠ FRBM 2018 target for the Centre was **3%**; the 16th FC path is **3.5%** by 2030-31.

n9b42ac3f86b.s: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act enacted?
n9b42ac3f86b.x: The AP FRBM Act was enacted in 2005; it aims to eliminate the revenue deficit and limit the fiscal deficit to 3% of GSDP.
xa: It has been amended from time to time to match **Finance Commission** borrowing limits.
**AP BE 2026-27**: FD **3.84%**, RD **1.11%** of GSDP — above the **3%** norm.
Slippage: FD **5.05%** vs mandated **4%** ceiling; borrowings **₹81,071 crore**.

ncb70fd0ebe3.s: State fiscal responsibility legislation was promoted after the Twelfth Finance Commission because debt relief was linked to:
o: The Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility
The Goods and Services Tax Compensation Fund
ncb70fd0ebe3.x: The Twelfth Finance Commission linked debt relief for States to the enactment of fiscal responsibility legislation through the Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility.
ncb70fd0ebe3.tq: Identify the specific facility associated with the debt-relief incentive.
xs: The **12th FC** tied debt relief to the **Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility** — option **(1)**.
States enacted Fiscal Responsibility Legislation mostly after this link.
Several States passed FRBM Acts on the **central model**; AP's came in **2005**.
xa: AP FRBM Act targets: eliminate RD, **FD 3% of GSDP**.
The central FRBM Act does **not apply to States**.
**16th FC** found State fiscal rules "**effectively unenforced**".

ne1b566ac340.s: Under the Fifteenth Finance Commission, the net borrowing limit for States in 2022-23 was:
ne1b566ac340.x: The limits were 4% in 2021-22, 3.5% in 2022-23, and 3% from 2023-24 to 2025-26 plus 0.5% for power-sector reforms.
xa: FRBM limits restrain AP's **open-market borrowing**.
AP slippage: FD **5.05%** vs mandated **4%** ceiling (7 Mar 2026).
**16th FC**: States **3% of GSDP** by **2030-31**.

n9c9920cfa13.s: Along with the end of the Plan/non-Plan classification, the Union Budget began to be presented on:
n9c9920cfa13.x: The Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget and the Budget was presented on 1 February.
xa: ⚠ **2017** = three changes together: **Railway merger** + **1 February** date + **plan/non-plan** ended.
The separate Railway Budget had run from **1924** (**Acworth Committee**, 1921) — a **92-year** practice ended.
The plan/non-plan split was removed on the advice of the **Expenditure Management Commission**.

n88431aced69.s: The separate Railway Budget was introduced in 1924 on the recommendation of the:
n88431aced69.x: The separate Railway Budget began in 1924 following the recommendations of the Acworth Committee constituted in 1921.
n88431aced69.tq: Match the reform with the committee that recommended it.
xs: The separate Railway Budget began in **1924** on the **Acworth Committee** (**1921**) recommendation — option **(2)**.
It was merged with the Union Budget in **2017** (Budget 2017-18), ending a **92-year** practice.
The **Expenditure Management Commission** is linked to ending the plan/non-plan split, not the Railway Budget.
xa: The Budget date also moved to **1 February** in **2017**.
**Outcome Budget / Gender Budget** came in **2005-06**; the Budget went **paperless** in **2021**.

nbf1ed27f8b7.s: India's Budget has been presented in paperless or digital form since:
nbf1ed27f8b7.x: The Budget has been presented in paperless or digital form since 2021.
nbf1ed27f8b7.tq: Recall the starting year of the digital reform.
xs: The Budget has been **paperless (digital)** since **2021** — option **(4)**.
**2017** is the year the Budget moved to **1 February** and the Railway Budget merged.
**2019** is when **Nirmala Sitharaman** began presenting every Budget.
xa: Printing begins with the **Halwa ceremony** at **North Block**.
The word "Budget" comes from French **bougette** ("little bag") and is **not in the Constitution**.

nc3b399d33d0.s: The word 'Budget' comes from the French word 'bougette', meaning:
nc3b399d33d0.x: 'Bougette' means 'little bag'; Budget printing begins with the Halwa ceremony at North Block.
xa: The **Budget circular** is issued in **September**.
The Budget is prepared by the **Budget Division, Department of Economic Affairs**, Ministry of Finance.

n046c31a766b.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the Appropriation Bill?
n046c31a766b.x: Article 114 covers the Appropriation Bill; 112 is the Annual Financial Statement, 113 the estimates, 115 supplementary grants.
xa: **Art. 116** = **vote on account**, vote of credit, exceptional grants; **Art. 117** = special provisions on financial bills.

nbe170911dcd.s: Who prepares the Union Budget through the Budget Division?
o: NITI Aayog independently of the Ministry of Finance
Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
nbe170911dcd.x: The Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs in the Ministry of Finance prepares the Union Budget, in coordination with NITI Aayog and spending ministries.
nbe170911dcd.tq: Apply the ‘who performs this job?’ test to distinguish adjoining financial institutions.
xs: The Budget is prepared by the **Budget Division, Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance** — option **(2)**.
It works with **NITI Aayog** and the spending ministries — NITI does not prepare it independently.
The **Department of Revenue** (**CBDT/CBIC**) only furnishes revenue estimates.
xa: The DEA also prepares budgets of **States under President's Rule** and **UTs**.
The **Budget circular** is issued in **September**; printing begins with the **Halwa ceremony** at **North Block**.

n22f3262bf5b.s: A Finance Bill is treated as a Money Bill under which constitutional provision?
n22f3262bf5b.x: A Finance Bill comes within the scope of a Money Bill under Article 110(1)(a), insofar as it contains provisions dealing with taxation.
n22f3262bf5b.tq: Distinguish the constitutional provision governing taxation-related Money Bills.
xs: The Finance Bill is a **Money Bill** under **Article 110(1)(a)** — option **(2)**.
It gives effect to the **tax proposals** and comes with an explanatory **Memorandum**.
**Art. 112** is the **Annual Financial Statement**, not the Finance Bill.
xa: The Finance Bill must be enacted within **75 days** (**Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931**).
It is the **sixth** and last stage of the budget process, after the **Appropriation Bill**.

n776eba82eb2.s: The Public Account of India is provided for under Article:
n776eba82eb2.x: The Public Account is under Article 266(2); withdrawals need no appropriation since the government acts only as banker.
xa: **Art. 266** = Consolidated Fund; **Art. 267** = Contingency Fund.
The **Contingency Fund** corpus was raised to **₹30,000 crore** from **2021-22**.

n1385f7066b1.s: The list of expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India is laid down in:
n1385f7066b1.x: Article 112(3) lists charged expenditure (President's emoluments, debt charges, judges' salaries, CAG etc.). Art 114(3) bars withdrawal from the CFI without an Appropriation Act, Art 266(2) is the Public Account, and Art 110(1)(a) brings tax provisions within a Money Bill.
n1385f7066b1.tq: Charged list = 112(3); discussable but not votable = 113(1).
xs: Charged expenditure is listed in **Article 112(3)** — option **(1)**.
**Art. 114(3)** bars withdrawal from the CFI without an **Appropriation Act**.
**Art. 266(2)** is the **Public Account**; **Art. 110(1)(a)** is the **Finance Bill**.
xa: Charged items include the **President**'s emoluments, **debt charges**, **SC judges**' salaries, the **CAG**.
Charged expenditure is **not voted**, only **discussed** (**Art. 113(1)**).

nf521d354954.s: Which of the following gives effect to the tax proposals of the Union Budget?
nf521d354954.x: The Finance Bill gives effect to tax proposals; the Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund.
xa: The Finance Bill must be enacted within **75 days** (**Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931**).
The **Public Account** needs no appropriation — the government acts as banker.

na16675e79fb.s: Under the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931, the Finance Bill must be enacted within:
na16675e79fb.x: The Finance Bill must be enacted within 75 days under the stated provision of the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931.
na16675e79fb.tq: Recall the statutory time limit using closely spaced numerical options.
xs: The Finance Bill must be enacted within **75 days** — option **(3)**.
This comes from the **Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931**.
The Finance Bill is a **Money Bill** under **Art. 110(1)(a)** and gives effect to tax proposals.
xa: Budget = estimate statement; **Finance Bill** = the legal instrument for taxes.
The Finance Bill comes with an explanatory **Memorandum**.

n0d2f3a1aee2.s: No money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India without:
n0d2f3a1aee2.x: Withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund (Article 266) needs an Appropriation Act; a vote on account authorises advance spending.

n5e3a6f38ac0.s: A government has a fiscal deficit of Rs 80,000 crore and interest payments of Rs 25,000 crore. Its primary deficit is:
n5e3a6f38ac0.x: Primary deficit equals fiscal deficit minus interest payments. Therefore, it is Rs 80,000 crore minus Rs 25,000 crore, or Rs 55,000 crore.
n5e3a6f38ac0.tq: Apply the primary-deficit formula and subtract interest payments from fiscal deficit.
xs: Primary deficit = **Rs 55,000 crore** — option **(3)**.
Formula: **PD = FD - interest payments** = Rs 80,000 crore - Rs 25,000 crore.
**Rs 80,000 crore** is the FD itself; **Rs 1,05,000 crore** wrongly adds interest.
xa: **FD** = total expenditure - receipts excluding borrowings.
**RD** = revenue expenditure - revenue receipts.
Interest takes **20** paise of every rupee spent in 2026-27.

n97914b3449b.s: Which of the following is an example of charged expenditure?
n97914b3449b.x: Interest on public debt is charged expenditure: non-votable but discussable, and shown separately in appropriation.
xa: Charged expenditure comes **straight from the Consolidated Fund**.

n5953f3f07b6.s: The salaries of the CAG and UPSC members are charged expenditure, which means they are:
n5953f3f07b6.x: Charged expenditure, such as for presiding officers, UPSC and CAG, is discussable but not voted.
xa: Also charged: **President**'s emoluments, **debt charges**, **SC judges**' salaries and pensions.

neeb71617fef.s: Cut motions on the Budget are moved at the stage of:
neeb71617fef.x: Cut motions come at the voting on demands; the general discussion has no cut motions or voting.
xa: Six stages: presentation → general discussion → **DRSC** scrutiny → voting on demands → **Appropriation Bill** → **Finance Bill**.
**Voting on demands** (**Art. 113**) is **only in Lok Sabha**.

ne1c01bde94a.s: Voting on Demands for Grants takes place in:
o: A joint sitting of both Houses
ne1c01bde94a.x: General discussion is in both Houses, but Demands for Grants are voted only in the Lok Sabha.
xa: Demands need the **President's recommendation**.
**Guillotine**: remaining demands put to vote **without discussion** on the last allotted day.

nda25f416435.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
o: President’s emoluments; interest on public debt; salary and office expenses of the CAG
Salaries of all Members of Parliament; grants to States; election expenditure
All Demands for Grants; salaries of ministers; public debt receipts
Finance Commission grants; subsidies; salaries of all government employees
nda25f416435.x: The President’s emoluments, interest on public debt, and the salary and administrative office expenses of the CAG are charged expenditure. The other sets contain items not identified as charged expenditure here.
nda25f416435.tq: Use elimination by checking whether every item belongs to the charged category.
xs: **President's emoluments; interest on public debt; salary and office expenses of the CAG** — all charged — option **(1)**.
Charged items also include salaries of RS **Chairman/Deputy Chairman** and LS **Speaker/Deputy Speaker**, and **UPSC** chairman/members.
**Court decrees/awards** and anything **Parliament declares charged by law** are also charged.
xa: Basis: **Art. 112(3)**; charged items are **not voted**, only discussed.
⚠ **SC judges** = salaries + pensions charged; **HC judges** = only **pensions** charged.

ne544b969420.s: Which of the following is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
ne544b969420.x: Salaries, allowances and pensions of Supreme Court judges, and pensions of High Court judges, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
xa: Other charged items: **President**'s emoluments, **CAG**'s salary, **UPSC**, **debt charges**.

n95de3f93d7b.s: In parliamentary financial procedure, the guillotine refers to
o: putting all outstanding demands to vote without discussion on the last day
the automatic rejection of all demands for grants
the President's power to withhold assent to a Money Bill
the referral of a financial Bill to a Joint Parliamentary Committee
n95de3f93d7b.x: On the last day fixed for the discussion of demands, all outstanding demands are put to vote without further discussion. This procedure is called the guillotine.
n95de3f93d7b.tq: Recognise the procedural meaning of a specialised parliamentary term.
xs: The **guillotine** puts **all outstanding demands to vote without discussion on the last day** — option **(1)**.
This was a **PYQ in APPSC-GS 2025**.
It applies to **voting on demands** in **Lok Sabha** (**Art. 113**).
xa: ⚠ **Policy cut** = reduce to **₹1**; **token cut** = by **₹100**; **economy cut** = by a stated amount.
General discussion runs **3-4 days** in both Houses.

nfc674947bf0.s: A Vote on Account is provided for under Article:
nfc674947bf0.x: Article 116 provides for a Vote on Account, usually for two months; it is still used in election years.
xa: In election years it covers **3-5 months**.
It covers **only expenditure**, until the budget is passed.

n040999cfa53.s: A cut motion that seeks to reduce a demand to Re 1 is called a:
n040999cfa53.x: A policy cut reduces the demand to Re 1; an economy cut reduces it by a stated amount and a token cut by Rs 100.
xa: Cut motions are moved during **voting on demands**, not in general discussion.
**Guillotine**: outstanding demands put to vote **without discussion**.

n6888538a4ac.s: Budget 2026-27, which continued fiscal consolidation without big tax cuts, estimated the Union fiscal deficit at:
n6888538a4ac.x: Budget 2026-27 kept to fiscal consolidation with a 4.3% fiscal-deficit estimate and a debt-GDP path, without large tax cuts.
xa: Tax proposals: **no slab change**; **MAT 15% → 14%**; **STT** raised on futures and options.
**New Income-tax Act, 2025** effective **1 April 2026**.

n880d53b3df9.x: ZBB is linked to Peter Pyhrr and was first used in government by Jimmy Carter; the Hoover Commission is linked to performance budgeting.
xa: India adopted performance budgeting from the **late 1960s** on ARC advice.
**Outcome Budget** was introduced in **2005**, from **2005-06**.
APPSC-G2 2025: justifying the entire budget from the beginning = **zero-base budgeting**.

na711b7d51a2.s: A budget in which each item of expenditure is justified afresh from zero in every period is called:
na711b7d51a2.x: Zero-based budgeting requires every expenditure item to be justified afresh from zero for each period.
na711b7d51a2.tq: Identify the exact official term from its defining procedure.
xs: Justifying every activity afresh from zero each period is a **zero-based budget** — option **(1)**.
It was developed by **Peter Pyhrr** and first used in government by **Jimmy Carter**.
A **performance** budget links spending to activities and results; an **outcome** budget tracks outputs and outcomes.
xa: APPSC-G2 2025: justifying the entire budget from the beginning = **zero-base budgeting**.
The **line-item** budget is the traditional type — control over items of expenditure.

n19b37c207fc.s: Budgeting that links outlays to measurable outcomes is called:
n19b37c207fc.x: Outcome budgeting links outlays to outcomes; performance budgeting links spending to activities.
xa: Performance budgeting: **First Hoover Commission** (USA); India from the **late 1960s** on **ARC** advice.
**Green** budgeting tracks environment-related spending.

n27c2f3731db.s: Revenue estimates in the Union Budget are furnished by which of the following?
o: CBDT and CBIC under the Department of Revenue
Department of Expenditure and Comptroller and Auditor General
NITI Aayog and the Reserve Bank of India
n27c2f3731db.x: Revenue estimates are furnished by the Department of Revenue through the CBDT and CBIC.
n27c2f3731db.tq: Identify the responsible department rather than the department that compiles the Budget.
xs: Revenue estimates come from the **Department of Revenue** — **CBDT and CBIC** — option **(1)**.
The **Budget Division** of the **DEA** prepares the Budget itself.
The Budget Division works with **NITI Aayog** and spending ministries.
xa: The **Receipt Budget** gives detailed estimates and trends of **tax, non-tax and capital receipts**.
Net tax to the Centre 2026-27 BE: **₹28,72,135 crore** (**+7.2%**).

n9f0474b356c.s: Which sequence correctly represents the classification order of receipts in the budget?
o: Tax revenue → Revenue receipts → Capital receipts → Non-tax revenue
Revenue receipts → Tax revenue → Non-tax revenue → Capital receipts
Capital receipts → Revenue receipts → Tax revenue → Non-tax revenue
Non-tax revenue → Tax revenue → Revenue receipts → Capital receipts
n9f0474b356c.x: The prescribed sequence is Revenue receipts, Tax revenue, Non-tax revenue and Capital receipts.
n9f0474b356c.tq: Use the first-and-last elements to eliminate incorrect sequences.
xs: **Revenue receipts → Tax revenue → Non-tax revenue → Capital receipts** — option **(2)**.
This is the **APPSC-GS 2025** key sequence.
Revenue receipts (tax and non-tax) create no liability and reduce no assets; capital receipts do one or the other.
xa: **Debt** capital receipts create liabilities (market loans, T-Bills, external loans).
**Non-debt** capital receipts reduce assets (**recovery of loans**, **disinvestment**).

nce9c2755377.s: Recovery of loans is classified as a:
nce9c2755377.x: Recovery of loans is a non-debt capital receipt; market borrowings are debt capital receipts.
xa: Other debt receipts: **T-Bills**, external loans, small savings/PF, borrowing from RBI.
Rupee comes from: **borrowings and other liabilities 24 paise** — the largest source in 2026-27.

n93b6c05bc48.s: Which of the following is an example of capital expenditure?
n93b6c05bc48.x: Capital expenditure creates assets or reduces liabilities; examples include capital works, loans given and debt repayment.
xa: Capex 2026-27 BE: **₹12.22 lakh crore**.
ES 2025-26: capex up **28%** (Apr-Nov 2025, ~**59%** of BE), revenue expenditure up only **1.8%**.

ncd5494bf184.s: Fiscal deficit of the Union Government is best defined as:
o: Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings
Total expenditure minus tax revenue only
ncd5494bf184.x: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure minus receipts excluding borrowings. Revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts is the revenue deficit; fiscal deficit minus interest payments is the primary deficit; subtracting only tax revenue ignores non-tax and non-debt capital receipts.
ncd5494bf184.tq: FD = borrowing need; PD = FD - interest; RD = RE - RR.
xs: **Fiscal deficit** = **total expenditure minus receipts excluding borrowings** — option **(2)**.
**Revenue expenditure - revenue receipts** is the **revenue deficit** (option 1).
**FD - interest payments** is the **primary deficit** (option 3).

nindian-economy-32-5.s: Dividends and profits from government enterprises are:
nindian-economy-32-5.x: Dividends and profits are revenue receipts; land, machinery and loans to States are capital payments.
n: The Capital Budget consists of capital receipts and capital payments. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 47-49]
Capital payments include the acquisition of land, buildings, and machinery. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 47-49]
Capital payments include loans and advances to States, Union Territories, and others. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 47-49]
Dividends and profits from government enterprises are revenue receipts. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 47-49]
Dividends and profits belong to the Revenue Account. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 47-49]
Asset creation expenditure belongs to the Capital Account. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 47-49]
xa: Capital receipts: **market borrowings**, **Treasury Bills**, **foreign loans**.
**Investments in shares** are also capital payments.
Guiding rule: **borrow only to invest**, not to fund current spending.

nindian-economy-45-4.x: Disinvestment is a capital receipt that reduces assets; salaries and allowances are revenue expenditure.
n: Capital receipts create a liability or reduce assets. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 66-68]
Disinvestment reduces assets. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 66-68]
Revenue expenditure includes salaries and allowances. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #45 · pp 66-68]
xa: **Non-tax revenue:** interest receipts, **dividends and profits**, spectrum, fees, fines.
**Pensions**, **subsidies** and **interest payments** are also revenue expenditure.
Disinvestment target **2026-27**: **₹80,000 crore**.

nindian-economy-48-5.s: Which of the following is a revenue receipt?
nindian-economy-48-5.x: Interest receipts are revenue receipts, like tax revenue, dividends/profits and fees; the others are capital receipts.
n: Tax revenue is a revenue receipt. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 71-72]
Interest receipts are revenue receipts. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 71-72]
Dividends and profits are revenue receipts. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 71-72]
Fees are revenue receipts. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 71-72]
xa: Non-tax revenue also includes **RBI surplus**, **spectrum**, **fines** and **licence fees**.
**Recovery of loans** and **disinvestment** are **non-debt capital receipts**.
Net tax to Centre **2026-27 BE**: **₹28,72,135 crore**.

nindian-economy-48-6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: A revenue receipt neither creates a liability nor reduces assets
Treasury Bills are a long-term domestic borrowing instrument
Disinvestment is a capital receipt that reduces assets
Foreign loans are capital receipts from external borrowing
nindian-economy-48-6.x: Treasury Bills are short-term domestic borrowing instruments.
n: A revenue receipt neither creates a liability nor reduces assets. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 71-72]
Disinvestment is a capital receipt. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 71-72]
Foreign loans are capital receipts. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 71-72]
Treasury Bills are capital receipts. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 71-72]
xa: Foreign loans include **loans from the World Bank**.
**Debt** capital receipts: **market borrowings**, **T-Bills**, external loans, small savings/PF.
**Borrowings create a liability**.

nbb4a0378d0e.s: The 1997-98 Union Budget is known as the:
nbb4a0378d0e.x: 1997-98 was the Dream Budget, while 1973-74 was the Black Budget.
xa: Budget 2026-27 was presented on **1 February 2026**, a **Sunday**.
⚠ Older notes calling **Indira Gandhi** the "only woman" to present a budget are outdated.
**Peter Pyhrr** developed zero-based budgeting; **Jimmy Carter** first used it in government.

nb35766b952c.s: A budget in which receipts equal expenditure is called a:
nb35766b952c.x: A balanced budget has receipts equal to expenditure; a surplus budget curbs inflation but may slow growth.
xa: **Zero-based budgeting** — developed by **Peter Pyhrr**; first used in government by **Jimmy Carter**.
**Outcome** and **Gender** budgets date from **2005-06**.
**Performance budgeting** came from the **First Hoover Commission** (USA).

n02f85189d3c.s: Under the erstwhile Plan/non-Plan classification, interest payments were classified as:
n02f85189d3c.x: Plan expenditure covered Central Plans and central assistance for State/UT Plans; interest was non-Plan.
xa: The distinction was removed in **2017-18** (**Expenditure Management Commission**).
APPSC-G2 2025: non-plan expenditure = **interest payments**.

o: Debt charges and court decrees only
n7cf47a9c3a1.x: Developmental expenditure covers economic and social services, whereas interest, defence, administration and pensions are classified as non-developmental.
n7cf47a9c3a1.tq: Discriminate between the developmental service group and the non-developmental group.
xs: Developmental expenditure covers **economic and social services** — option **(2)**.
**Interest, defence, administration and pensions** are **non-developmental** — so options (3) and (4) are wrong.
**Debt charges** and **court decrees** are charged items, not the definition of developmental spending.
xa: Development expenditure examples: **education, health, employment, industry**.
**Defence** is "**committed**" spending, with little scope for cuts.
The old **plan/non-plan** split was replaced by **revenue/capital** from **2017-18**.

n4c9d137347f.s: In the Union Budget 2026-27, the fiscal deficit was estimated at:
n4c9d137347f.x: The FD was 4.3% of GDP, with expenditure of ₹53,47,315 crore and debt at 55.6 per cent.
xa: Capex 2026-27 BE: **₹12.22 lakh crore**.
Budget 2026-27 kept to consolidation with **no big tax cuts**.

n86cdc5da4b3.s: The Union Budget 2026-27 was billed as a:
n86cdc5da4b3.x: It was billed as a 'Yuva Shakti-driven Budget', presented by Nirmala Sitharaman on 1 February 2026 with three Kartavyas.
xa: The three Kartavyas: accelerate growth; fulfil aspirations and build capacity; ensure access for all (**Sabka Sath, Sabka Vikas**).
Capex **₹12.22 lakh crore**; FD **4.3%**.

n0e7766c59a2.s: What was the estimated capital expenditure in the Union Budget 2026-27?
n0e7766c59a2.x: Capital expenditure in the Union Budget 2026-27 was estimated at ₹12.22 lakh crore.
n0e7766c59a2.tq: Use direct numerical recall with nearby budget figures as distractors.
xs: Capex in Budget 2026-27: **₹12.22 lakh crore** — option **(1)**.
**₹16.96 lakh crore** is the **fiscal deficit** (**4.3%** of GDP), not capex.
Defence capital outlay alone is **₹2,19,306 crore** (**+17.6%**).
xa: Total expenditure **₹53,47,315 crore**.

n5e3dd9062d2.s: Which ministry received the highest allocation in the Union Budget 2026-27?
o: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
n5e3dd9062d2.x: The Ministry of Defence received the highest allocation, amounting to ₹7,84,678 crore.
n5e3dd9062d2.tq: Identify the highest allocation from the comparison table.
xs: **Defence** got the highest allocation: **₹7,84,678 crore** (15%) — option **(3)**.
Next: **Road Transport and Highways** ₹3,09,875 crore, **Railways** ₹2,81,377 crore, **Home Affairs** ₹2,55,234 crore.
Defence capital outlay: **₹2,19,306 crore** (**+17.6%**).
xa: Rupee goes to: **Defence 11** paise.
⚠ Largest outflow = **States' share** (**22** paise), then **interest** (**20**).

n61e9b415903.s: Which scheme replaced MGNREGA in the Union Budget 2026-27?
n61e9b415903.x: VB-G RAM G replaced MGNREGA and received an allocation of ₹95,692 crore. MGNREGS had a residual allocation of ₹30,000 crore.
n61e9b415903.tq: Use the scheme-replacement relationship as the decisive clue.
xs: **VB-G RAM G** replaced **MGNREGA** — option **(4)**.
It got **₹95,692 crore** — the largest scheme allocation; **MGNREGS residual** ₹30,000 crore.
**Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana** is a separate new scheme (**₹20,083 crore**); **PM-KISAN** got ₹63,500 crore.
xa: **Jal Jeevan Mission** ₹67,670 crore; **PMAY-G** ₹54,917 crore.
**BharatNet** and **RDI**: ₹20,000 crore each; **Biopharma SHAKTI** ₹10,000 crore.
Other initiatives: **ISM 2.0**; seven high-speed rail corridors.

n5fea2ef5291.s: The new Income-tax Act, 2025 becomes effective from:
n5fea2ef5291.x: It takes effect from 1 April 2026; Budget 2026-27 made no slab change and cut MAT from 15% to 14%.
xa: Earlier reforms: **2019** corporate tax cut; personal income-tax restructuring (**April 2025**); **GST 2.0** (**Sep 2025**).
Budget 2026-27 made **no big tax cuts**.

nfa7a4fe7cea.s: In Budget 2026-27, the largest item of 'rupee goes to' was:
o: States' share of taxes and duties
nfa7a4fe7cea.x: The States' share (22 paise) was the largest outflow, ahead of interest (20 paise); borrowings (24 paise) were the largest source.
xa: Next sources: **income tax 21**, **corporation tax 18**, **GST 15** paise.
Next outflows: **central sector schemes 17**, **defence 11** paise.
**Major subsidies** = **6** paise; **civil pensions** = **2** paise.

nff1e535ec6b.s: As the principal instrument of fiscal policy, the Union Budget performs the functions of:
o: Resource allocation, income redistribution and stabilisation
Regulation of banks and financial markets
nff1e535ec6b.x: The Budget allocates resources, redistributes income and stabilises the economy.
xa: FD at **26.8%** of target by July (**CGA**, 1 Sep 2026).
Tax devolution Apr-Jul 2026: **₹3,72,354 crore**.

n70a884788c2.s: The combined fiscal deficit of the States in FY25 rose to:
n70a884788c2.x: It rose to 3.2 per cent in FY25; 18 States exceeded the 15th FC's 3 per cent limit in FY24.
xa: Union FD for comparison: **4.3%** of GDP in **2026-27 BE**.
AP: CAG flagged its **revenue deficit** for three years.

nc4d056e476e.s: The distinction between plan and non-plan expenditure was removed in 2017-18 on the recommendation of the:
nc4d056e476e.x: The plan/non-plan distinction was removed in 2017-18 following the recommendation of the Expenditure Management Commission.
nc4d056e476e.tq: Use the committee-function association and avoid swapping reform bodies.
xs: The plan/non-plan distinction was removed in **2017-18** on the **Expenditure Management Commission**'s recommendation — option **(4)**.
It was replaced by the **revenue/capital** classification.
The **Acworth Committee** (**1921**) is linked to the separate Railway Budget of **1924**.
xa: Non-plan expenditure was the larger part: **interest payments, defence, subsidies, salaries, pensions**.
APPSC-G2 2025: non-plan expenditure = **interest payments**.
⚠ **2017-18** also saw the **Railway merger** and the **1 February** date.

nf299871c655.s: Which one of the following was a non-Plan expenditure item under the former classification?
o: Expenditure on a new Central Plan
Central assistance for Union Territory Plans
nf299871c655.x: Interest payments formed part of the larger non-Plan expenditure category. Central Plans and central assistance for State and Union Territory Plans were Plan expenditure.
nf299871c655.tq: Use the direct association between interest payments and the former non-Plan category.
xs: **Interest payments** were **non-plan** expenditure — option **(2)**.
Non-plan was the **larger part**: interest, **defence, subsidies, salaries, pensions**, and maintenance of earlier Plan assets.
Central Plans and central assistance for **State/UT Plans** were **plan** expenditure — options (1), (3), (4).
xa: APPSC-G2 2025 key: non-plan expenditure = **interest payments**.
Rupee goes to: **interest payments** take **20** paise in 2026-27.
Interest takes **40%** of revenue receipts.

n3fcaef4b5e3.s: The Halwa ceremony in the Union Budget process marks the:
n3fcaef4b5e3.x: The Halwa ceremony marks the printing of the Budget documents; the Budget circular is issued earlier, in September.
xa: The DEA also prepares budgets of **States under President's Rule** and **UTs**.
Revenue estimates come from **CBDT/CBIC** (Department of Revenue).

nb9a4e47ff82.s: The revised estimate of the fiscal deficit for 2024-25 was:
nb9a4e47ff82.x: RE 2024-25 was 4.8 per cent, higher than the 4.4 per cent BE for 2025-26.

nbb92bf947a8.s: Since 1998-99, what proportion of Gross Budgetary Support is generally earmarked for the North-Eastern region by every ministry, subject to a few exemptions?
nbb92bf947a8.x: Every ministry, barring a few exempted ministries, earmarks 10% of Gross Budgetary Support for the North-Eastern region since 1998-99.
nbb92bf947a8.tq: Combine the percentage with the qualifying exception instead of treating the rule as absolute.
xs: Every ministry (barring a few exempted) earmarks **10% of Gross Budgetary Support** for the Northeast since **1998-99** — option **(2)**.
This is a standing earmark, not a one-year scheme.
⚠ **15%** is Defence's share of the 2026-27 Budget, not the Northeast earmark.
xa: Defence: **₹7,84,678 crore** — highest ministry allocation in 2026-27.
Mission VATSALYA: **Rs 900 crore** (Budget 2021-22).

nindian-economy-46-6.s: Salaries, pensions and statutory transfers were classified as:
nindian-economy-46-6.x: Maintenance of infrastructure, salaries, pensions and statutory transfers were all non-plan expenditure.
n: Non-plan expenditure includes maintenance of infrastructure. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 68-69]
Non-plan expenditure includes salaries. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 68-69]
Non-plan expenditure includes pensions. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 68-69]
Non-plan expenditure includes statutory transfers. [Indian Economy · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 68-69]
xa: **Interest payments** = classic non-plan example (APPSC-G2 2025 key).
The **plan/non-plan** distinction was removed from **2017-18** (**Expenditure Management Commission**).
**Plan expenditure** covered Central Plans and assistance for State/UT Plans.

n9434e497bea.s: The Economic Survey of India is prepared by which of the following bodies?
o: Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, under the Revenue Secretary
Economic Division, Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, under the Chief Economic Adviser
Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, under the Finance Secretary
n9434e497bea.x: The Economic Survey is prepared by the Economic Division of the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, under the Chief Economic Adviser.
n9434e497bea.tq: Identify the correct department and supervising authority rather than a neighbouring ministry body.
xs: The Survey is prepared by the **Economic Division, Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance**, under the **Chief Economic Adviser** — option **(3)**.
It is not a **NITI Aayog**, **Department of Revenue** or **Department of Expenditure** document.
It is presented in **both Houses** during the Budget Session, **before the Union Budget**.
xa: First Survey: **1950-51**; presented separately from the Budget since **1964**.
Current CEA: **V. Anantha Nageswaran** (**2022-23** to **2025-26** editions).
⚠ The Union Budget is prepared by the **Budget Division** of the same **DEA**.

n1f00a3739fc.s: The Economic Survey has been presented separately from the Union Budget since:
n1f00a3739fc.x: The first Survey was for 1950-51, but it has been presented separately from the Budget only since 1964.
xa: It is presented in **both Houses**, **before the Union Budget** — by convention.
Single volume + statistical appendix since **2021-22**.

nb4fce6fbfff.s: Presentation of the Economic Survey before the Union Budget is:
o: A requirement under the FRBM Act
nb4fce6fbfff.x: It is only a convention; Article 112 concerns the Annual Financial Statement.
xa: ⚠ Survey = convention; Budget (AFS) = **Art. 112** obligation.
Prepared by the **Economic Division, DEA**, under the CEA.

n48426fddf4d.s: Which two subjects were added as chapters in the Economic Survey 2025-26?
n48426fddf4d.x: Artificial intelligence and urbanisation were added as chapters in the reconfigured Economic Survey 2025-26.
n48426fddf4d.tq: Use a subject-pair question to test the distinctive additions to a particular edition.
xs: ES 2025-26 added chapters on **artificial intelligence and urbanisation** — option **(3)**.
It was reconfigured to **17 chapters**.
It also has a chapter on **Environment and Climate Change**, favouring **adaptation over mitigation**.
xa: Theme: "**Building Strategic Indispensability**" + **entrepreneurial policy making**.
Conclusion: **Sreya vs Preya** (**Katha Upanishad**).

n30b63af9072.s: Which of the following reforms was NOT listed among the reforms of 2025 in the Economic Survey 2025-26?
o: Opening nuclear power to the private sector
n30b63af9072.x: The listed reforms included a GST overhaul, 100 per cent FDI in insurance, opening nuclear power to the private sector, notification of four Labour Codes and placing QCOs on hold. Complete abolition of GST was not listed.
n30b63af9072.tq: Distinguish an overhaul from an abolition and identify the exaggerated policy claim.
xs: **Complete abolition of GST** was NOT listed — option **(2)**.
The 2025 reforms included a **GST overhaul**, **100% FDI in insurance** and **nuclear power** opened to the private sector.
**Four Labour Codes** were notified; **QCOs** were put on hold.
xa: ES 2025-26: shift from "regulation and control" to "**enabling**".
"**Process reforms** more important than policy reforms".

na1cd7457b00.s: The Economic Surveys 2018-19 to 2020-21 are associated with:
na1cd7457b00.x: K.V. Subramanian: 2018-19 to 2020-21; Arvind Subramanian: 2014-15 to 2017-18; Sanyal: 2021-22; Nageswaran: 2022-23 to 2025-26.
xa: Arvind Subramanian's Surveys: **JAM trinity**, **Chakravyuha**, **UBI**, **Twin Balance Sheet**.
K.V. Subramanian's: **nudge**, **Thalinomics**, **Bare Necessities Index**.

nd464baa188d.s: The term ‘Chakravyuha challenge’ in the Economic Survey referred to which of the following situations?
o: Low agricultural productivity and high food imports
High public debt and low tax collection
High inflation combined with low economic growth
Easy entry but blocked exit of firms
nd464baa188d.x: The Chakravyuha challenge described an economy in which firms could enter relatively easily but faced difficulty in exiting. The exit problem was subsequently addressed through the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
nd464baa188d.tq: Test the exact meaning of a distinctive metaphor rather than its associated year.
xs: The **Chakravyuha challenge** = **easy entry but blocked exit of firms** — option **(4)**.
It was in **ES 2015-16**, under **Arvind Subramanian**.
The exit problem was later addressed by the **IBC**.
xa: ⚠ **Chakravyuha** (2015-16) and **Twin Balance Sheet** (2016-17) were both answered by **IBC**.
**2016-17** also had the **Universal Basic Income** chapter.

nf250497cdca.s: Which Economic Survey introduced the idea of behavioural economics through the concept of ‘nudge’ and the expression ‘Homo Sapiens, not Homo Economicus’?
nf250497cdca.x: The 2018-19 Economic Survey discussed behavioural economics and the idea of using nudges, describing people as Homo Sapiens rather than purely rational Homo Economicus.
nf250497cdca.tq: Discriminate between closely sequenced annual editions using the signature concept.
xs: **ES 2018-19** introduced the **nudge** — "**Homo Sapiens, not Homo Economicus**" — option **(2)**.
It was **K.V. Subramanian**'s first Survey.
xa: **2020-21**: **Bare Necessities Index** (housing, water, sanitation, electricity, clean cooking fuel).
K.V. Subramanian's editions: **2018-19 to 2020-21**.

na6b9c621a34.s: The theme of the Economic Survey 2025-26 is
na6b9c621a34.x: The overall theme of the Economic Survey 2025-26 is “Building Strategic Indispensability”. “State of the Economy: Pushing the Growth Frontier” is the title of Chapter 1.
na6b9c621a34.tq: Distinguish the Survey's overall theme from the title of its first chapter.
xs: The theme of ES 2025-26 is "**Building Strategic Indispensability**" — option **(2)**.
"**Pushing the Growth Frontier**" is the title of **Chapter 1** ("State of the Economy"), not the theme.
The theme pairs with **entrepreneurial policy making** in a world of geopolitical friction.
xa: ES 2025-26 had **17 chapters**, adding **AI** and **urbanisation**.
Conclusion: **Sreya vs Preya** (**Katha Upanishad**).

n360538be8c3.s: The Bare Necessities Index in the Economic Survey 2020-21 measured Ease of Living at which level?
n360538be8c3.x: The Bare Necessities Index in the Economic Survey 2020-21 measured Ease of Living at the State level.
n360538be8c3.tq: Identify the geographical level of an index and reject narrower or broader substitutes.
xs: The **Bare Necessities Index** measured Ease of Living at **State level** — option **(1)**.
It appeared in **ES 2020-21**.
It used NSO **69th (2012)** and **76th (2018)** rounds.
xa: Components: **housing, water, sanitation, electricity, clean cooking fuel**.
Budget 2026-27 pillar: "**Ease of Doing Business and Ease of Living**".

nb5c7812d07d.s: The climate chapter of the Economic Survey 2025-26, given scarce fiscal resources, favoured:
o: Near-term emission cuts over development spending
Diverting health funds to emission cuts
nb5c7812d07d.x: It favoured adaptation and argued against diverting resources from health, agriculture and poverty reduction; it called civilisational collapse unlikely.
xa: Global scenarios for **2026**: **Systemic Shock Cascade (10-20%)**, worse than **2008**.
ES 2017-18 had a chapter on **climate change and agriculture**.

ne186f7f37a8.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 placed real GDP growth for FY26 (First Advance Estimates) at:
ne186f7f37a8.x: FY26 growth was 7.4% (FAE); FY27 was projected at 6.8%-7.2% and potential growth raised to 7.0% from 6.5%.
xa: Sector growth FY26: **agriculture 3.1%**, **manufacturing 7.0%**, **services 9.1%**.
PFCE **61.5%** of GDP; GFCF steady at **30%**.

nc250510d072.s: Which sector was described as the ‘stabilising anchor’ in the Economic Survey 2025-26?
nc250510d072.x: The services sector, with projected FY26 growth of 9.1 per cent, was described as the stabilising anchor.
nc250510d072.tq: Match the descriptive phrase with the sector to which it specifically refers.
xs: **Services** was the "**stabilising anchor**" — option **(1)**.
It grew **9.1%** in FY26 — the fastest sector.
**Manufacturing** grew **7.0%** and **agriculture** **3.1%**.
xa: ES 2024-25 also found **services** robust in high-frequency indicators in **FY25**.
FY27 growth projection: **6.8% - 7.2%**.

n396e43bd8d3.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 treated India's high foreign exchange cover as:
n396e43bd8d3.x: High forex cover was reported as an external strength; the Survey's concerns were State revenue deficits and unconditional cash transfers.
xa: FY25 FD **4.8%** of GDP vs **4.9%** budgeted.
**S&P** upgrade **BBB- to BBB**.

n12ec85bf320.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, the repo rate was cut since February 2025 by:
n12ec85bf320.x: Repo was cut by 125 bps; banks' gross NPAs fell to a multi-decade low of 2.2%.
xa: Headline CPI **1.7%** (Apr-Dec FY26), on falling food prices.
**S&P** upgraded India **BBB- to BBB**.

nca19a794311.s: Deregulation was the central theme of the Economic Survey:
nca19a794311.x: Deregulation was the central theme of ES 2024-25; ES 2023-24 spoke of 'letting go' and lighter MSME inspections.
xa: ES 2025-26: **trust-based compliance** replacing inspection.

n520343728b6.s: Public capital expenditure proposed for FY 2026-27 under the Viksit Bharat @2047 framework is:

nf0574545040.s: In response to supply disruptions, the Economic Survey 2022-23 identified which combination of measures?
o: Reducing both fuel excise and food subsidies
Raising fuel taxes and cutting food and fertiliser subsidies
Raising fuel excise and increasing food subsidies only
Cutting fuel excise and increasing food and fertiliser subsidy support

nf0574545040.tq: Catch the reversed policy-action trap by separating tax measures from subsidy support.
xs: **Cutting fuel excise** and **raising food and fertiliser subsidy support** — option **(4)**.

n8379c8ab55f.s: The conclusion involving ‘Sreya’ and ‘Preya’ in the Economic Survey 2025-26 drew upon which text?

nfe1b5f439a9.s: National Accounts and the Index of Industrial Production were rebased to which base year, as reported in the Economic Survey 2025-26?
