ne0ae4309a6e.s: The sovereign rating upgrade mentioned in the Economic Survey 2025-26 was from:

nd026434cb95.s: The Universal Basic Income chapter of the Economic Survey 2016-17 presented UBI primarily as a radical idea to address which problem?

ES 2016-17: most women without toilets had to **travel long distances** for a toilet facility.

n38b3ed8a7c7.s: According to the Economic Survey 2016-17, most women in households without toilets:

used toilets built under MGNREGA on their premises
were covered by the Bare Necessities Index

xs: Most women in households without toilets had to **travel long distances for a toilet facility** — option **(2)**.

n1a58a26c202.s: Andhra Pradesh was bifurcated under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 on which date?
n1a58a26c202.x: The erstwhile State of Andhra Pradesh was bifurcated on 2 June 2014 under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
n1a58a26c202.tq: Direct date-recall question using closely related reorganisation dates as distractors.
xs: AP was bifurcated on **2 June 2014** under the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014** — option **(2)**.
**1 November 1956** was the formation of undivided AP (**20** districts); **4 April 2022** was the district reorganisation to **26**.
xa: The Centre accepted the residuary State would be adversely affected; the PM gave assurances in the **Rajya Sabha**.

AP became a **chronic revenue-deficit State** after bifurcation.

n3d7d6615d86.s: Hyderabad alone contributed approximately what percentage of the total revenue of undivided Andhra Pradesh in 2012-13?
n3d7d6615d86.x: Hyderabad contributed about 48% of the undivided State's total revenue of ₹70,548 crore in 2012-13.
n3d7d6615d86.tq: Numerical recall using the population-ratio figures as nearby distractors.
xs: **Hyderabad alone** gave about **48%** of undivided AP's total revenue — option **(3)**.
The undivided State's total revenue was **₹70,548 crore** (**2012-13** estimate).
xa: Telangana kept the **IT, commercial and industrial assets** + the capital.
AP got the bulk of the **agrarian population**, irrigation-project liabilities and **power-sector deficits**.
Result: AP = **chronic revenue-deficit State**.

n6dc784485f0.s: Which of the following contributed to residuary Andhra Pradesh becoming a chronic revenue-deficit State?
o: Inheritance of the IT and industrial assets
Transfer of power-sector deficits to Telangana
n6dc784485f0.x: The loss of Hyderabad's revenue base, a large agrarian population, and liabilities for irrigation and power deficits made residuary AP revenue-deficit.
xa: Result: AP became a **chronic revenue-deficit State**.
**Hyderabad** alone ≈ **48%** of undivided AP's revenue (**2012-13**).
Ongoing strains: asset-liability allocation, institutional division, **river waters**.

n3a5b813b3e2.s: Which one of the following best explains why Andhra Pradesh had to construct a new capital after bifurcation?
o: All irrigation projects were transferred to Telangana.
The State had no districts after bifurcation.
The capital and several major institutions remained with Telangana.
The Reorganisation Act abolished the existing capital permanently.
n3a5b813b3e2.x: The capital remained with Telangana, compelling Andhra Pradesh to develop Amaravati and establish many institutions from scratch.
n3a5b813b3e2.tq: Application question asking which consequence follows from the location of the former capital.
xs: **The capital and several major institutions remained with Telangana** — option **(3)**.
So AP had to build a new capital (**Amaravati**) and many institutions **from scratch**.
Irrigation-project **liabilities** came to AP, not Telangana.
xa: Telangana also kept the **IT, commercial and industrial** assets.
The bifurcation left AP without Hyderabad's **IT export base** → new IT parks in **Visakhapatnam, Tirupati, Vijayawada**.
Amaravati Economic Region covers **9** districts.

n4db21e03ebe.s: Andhra Pradesh accounts for about what share of India's area?

nd0d5f48d51d.s: Andhra Pradesh ranks ____ among Indian States in GSDP.

xa: Area: **7th** among States (**8th** counting J&K).

n9688c9cb7f5.s: In 2025-26, Andhra Pradesh ranked first in India in:

ndc83e04bba8.s: Casual labour forms what share of rural workers in Andhra Pradesh?

na225b1fd2b0.s: Which set of cities emerged as locations for new IT parks in Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation?
na225b1fd2b0.x: After bifurcation left Andhra Pradesh without Hyderabad's IT export base, new IT parks came up in Visakhapatnam, Tirupati and Vijayawada.

n64cb57e0a7a.s: The share of agriculture : industry : services in Andhra Pradesh's GSVA in 2025-26 FAE (current prices) was about:

n78b233ba6a8.s: According to the State Economic Survey 2024-25, the workforce distribution in Andhra Pradesh is approximately:

n21eefcd5b53.s: In 2024-25 (FAE), Andhra Pradesh's agriculture sector grew by:

2023-24 FRE: agriculture **-1.58%**, industry **7.52%**, services **7.71%**.

nfeaf4a93e5f.s: The average growth of agriculture and allied activities in Andhra Pradesh since bifurcation, as reported in 2018, was approximately:

nc6302f25817.s: India's new GDP series released by MoSPI uses the base year:

nd88c95a3456.s: In 2025-26 (FAE), Andhra Pradesh grew faster than the All-India economy on

n51736a28347.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the seven backward districts covered by the special development package under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
n51736a28347.x: Nalgonda is not an Andhra Pradesh backward district; it is located in Telangana. The seven districts include Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor.
n51736a28347.tq: NOT-correctly-matched question using a neighbouring State's district as the trap.
xs: **Nalgonda** is NOT among them — option **(3)** is correct; it is in **Telangana**.
**Srikakulam** (North Coastal) and **Kurnool**, **Chittoor** (Rayalaseema) are among the **7** districts.
xa: Others: **Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Kadapa, Anantapur**.
Coastal Andhra (**Krishna-Guntur**) is the more developed region.
**Vizianagaram** is also an **Aspirational District** (NITI Aayog).

n6bc9f68fb0b.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh has the highest MPI headcount?
n6bc9f68fb0b.x: Kurnool has the highest headcount (12.84%) and West Godavari the lowest (2.42%); AP's 6.06% is below India's 14.96%.
xa: **Vizianagaram** is among AP's **Aspirational Districts** (NITI Aayog, **112** districts).
The **BRGF** (Backward Regions Grant Fund) is now defunct.
**Zero Poverty-P4** targets poverty eradication — Phase 1 **21.8 lakh+ families**.

n917bf45bf69.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the districts of Andhra Pradesh?
o: The latest number of districts is 28
Undivided AP had 20 districts on 1 November 1956
The reorganisation of 4 April 2022 raised the number to 26
xa: District series (GDDP, PCI) before and after **2022** are not directly comparable.
Bifurcation took effect on **2 June 2014**.
AP has **3** economic regions: **Visakhapatnam**, **Amaravati**, **Tirupati**.

nda7fc760efc.s: Which is the largest port in Andhra Pradesh by cargo volume?
nda7fc760efc.x: Visakhapatnam is the largest port on India’s east coast by volume.
nda7fc760efc.tq: Use the location-and-superlative combination to identify the port.
xs: **Visakhapatnam Port** is the largest port on the east coast by volume — option **(3)**.
The notes name no other port with this distinction.
xa: AP's coastline: **1,053.07 km**, the **3rd** longest (SES 2025-26).
Visakhapatnam ER covers **10 districts** and is a **NITI Aayog** growth-hub pilot.
⚠ Visakhapatnam has the **most bank branches** but the **fewest** post offices.
nda7fc760efc.fixed: Paradip, not Visakhapatnam, is the largest east-coast port by volume (~145 MT vs ~81 MT, FY24); options are all AP ports so restrict stem to AP

na5253e82eaa.s: Compared with India, Andhra Pradesh's growth from 2024-25 onwards was:
na5253e82eaa.x: AP grew more slowly than India in 2023-24 but faster from 2024-25 onwards.
xa: CM claim: growth rose to **11.3%** (16 Aug 2026).
Q2 2025-26 review: real GSDP growth **9.9%**.

n171921f1f0c.s: Which of the following was covered by the White Paper on agriculture-related sectors in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Horticulture, textiles, ports, railways, animal husbandry and marketing
Agriculture, horticulture, sericulture, animal husbandry, dairy, fisheries and marketing
Agriculture, mining, defence, banking, dairy, fisheries and tourism
Sericulture, information technology, defence, fisheries, tourism and banking
n171921f1f0c.x: The White Paper covered agriculture, horticulture, sericulture, animal husbandry, dairy, fisheries and marketing.
n171921f1f0c.tq: Recall the complete sectoral list and reject options containing unrelated administrative sectors.
xs: The White Paper covered **Agriculture, Horticulture, Sericulture, Animal Husbandry, Dairy, Fisheries and Marketing** — option **(2)** is correct.
Textiles, ports, railways, mining, defence, banking, IT and tourism were not in it.
xa: APPSC 2022 A-R question on it: **both true, R explains A**.
Swarnandhra horticulture KPIs: micro-irrigation, horticulture area, **oil palm** area, post-harvest infrastructure, productivity.
Target: **30% growth** in agri & allied over five years through **17 growth engines**.

n955adb65d22.s: Which institutions constitute the education and health anchors identified for Andhra Pradesh's emerging services sector?
o: AIIMS Mangalagiri, IIM Visakhapatnam and IIT Tirupati
AIIMS Tirupati, IIM Mangalagiri and IIT Visakhapatnam
AIIMS Visakhapatnam, IIM Tirupati and IIT Mangalagiri
AIIMS Vijayawada, IIM Guntur and IIT Amaravati
n955adb65d22.x: The identified anchors are AIIMS Mangalagiri, IIM Visakhapatnam and IIT Tirupati.
n955adb65d22.tq: Match each institution with its correct Andhra Pradesh location.
xs: **AIIMS Mangalagiri, IIM Visakhapatnam and IIT Tirupati** — option **(1)** is correct.
They are the education and health anchors named in the **Industrial Policy 2024-29**; the other options swap the cities.
xa: IT parks: **Visakhapatnam, Tirupati, Vijayawada**.
**GCC Park at Kapuluppada** (Visakhapatnam) — **US$10 bn** partnership.
Industrial Development Policy **4.0 (2024-29)** puts manufacturing at the centre.

nc0f2091373a.s: According to data as on March 2016, the districts having the maximum number of post offices, telephone connections and bank branches respectively were:
nc0f2091373a.x: As per the March 2016 data, Chittoor had the most post offices, while Visakhapatnam led in both telephone connections and bank branches.
nc0f2091373a.tq: Sequence-based recall of three linked district leaders.
xs: **Chittoor, Visakhapatnam and Visakhapatnam** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC G2 2017, data as on March 2016).
Chittoor led post offices; Visakhapatnam led both telephone connections and bank branches.
xa: ⚠ Latest (31 Dec 2024): post offices led by **Prakasam (668)**; bank branches still **Visakhapatnam (624)**.
Landlines (13 old districts): **Krishna (8,764)**; mobiles (2025): **Visakhapatnam (3.77 lakh)**.
Answers change with district reorganisation — note the **data year**.

nd05689ce746.s: In Q2 2025–26, which sector was reported to be the best-performing sector in Andhra Pradesh, with a growth rate of 13.5%?
nd05689ce746.x: Agriculture was the best-performing sector in Q2 2025–26, recording growth of 13.5%.
nd05689ce746.tq: Link the performance ranking with the stated sector-specific growth rate.
xs: **Agriculture** was the best-performing sector in Q2 2025-26 at **13.5%** — option **(1)** is correct.
Industry grew **10.6%** and services **9.9%**.
xa: Annual FAE 2025-26: agri-allied **10.14%**, led by **fisheries**.
Overall quarterly update (Aug 2026): **10.7%**.
⚠ FAE fastest sector = **services (10.67%)**.

nb94b383912a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding per capita GSDP and per capita income?
o: Gross measures should be compared with gross measures
PCI is NSDP divided by population
Per capita GSDP is a gross measure
Per capita GSDP and PCI are interchangeable terms
nb94b383912a.x: They are not interchangeable: per capita GSDP is gross, while PCI is based on net NSDP.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** "GSDP ÷ population" is loose; the Survey's PCI is **NSDP-based**.
⚠ Never compare AP's per capita GSDP with India's per capita income.
2023-24: AP per capita GSDP **₹2,70,295** vs India per capita GDP **₹2,15,935**.

n07ac5a771dd.s: Per capita income in the Survey is based on:
n07ac5a771dd.x: PCI uses NSDP, which is net of depreciation, at current or constant prices.
xa: **DDP** (district GDP) is compiled by the State **DES**, also nodal agency for GSDP.

n8b646134ff8.s: In 2024-25, Telangana's per capita income was how many times Andhra Pradesh's?
n8b646134ff8.x: It was 1.35 times in 2024-25, up from 1.3 times in 2013-14 and 6% higher in 2004-05.
xa: Telangana's economy = **96.5%** of AP's size (2024-25).
Metro **Hyderabad** = **47.5%** of Telangana's output.
⚠ GDP share 2023-24: **Telangana 4.9%** > **AP 4.7%**.

n169e75cefb1.s: In the latest Andhra Pradesh series, per capita income growth was fastest (15.26%) in:
n169e75cefb1.x: PCI growth was fastest at 15.26% in 2021-22 and slowest at 4.10% in 2019-20.
xa: ⚠ The **SES 2024-25** series put the 2021-22 peak at **17.35%**.
India's 2021-22 PCI growth: **18.6%**.

n663a725333a.s: Andhra Pradesh's per capita income growth in 2025-26 was:
n663a725333a.x: AP's PCI grew 10.43% against India's 6.9%; AP's PCI stayed above the national average throughout.
xa: AP ≈ **1.34 times** the national figure.

n2c011a24170.s: Rayalaseema accounts for about what share of Andhra Pradesh's horticulture output?
n2c011a24170.x: Drought-prone Rayalaseema has 43% of AP's horticulture area and 52% of its output.
xa: Rayalaseema districts: **Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur, Chittoor**.
**4** of the **7** backward districts are in Rayalaseema.

na63a0fbc56b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about district development monitoring in Andhra Pradesh?
o: District Vision Action Plans are tracked at district, constituency and mandal levels
Collectors are rated on the rise in district per capita income
Collectors are rated on investment and jobs
District Domestic Product is compiled by the National Statistical Office
na63a0fbc56b.x: District Domestic Product is compiled by the State Directorate of Economics and Statistics.
xa: NTR district PCI target: **₹4,17,412**.
DES is also the nodal agency for **GSDP**.

nab65bed1149.s: Per capita income rises only when national income grows:
o: At the same rate as population
nab65bed1149.x: PCI = income / population, so it rises only if income grows faster than population.
xa: AP's **PCI** = **NSDP ÷ population** — a net measure, after depreciation.
⚠ Never compare AP's per capita **GSDP** with India's per capita **income** — match gross with gross, net with net.
Limits: an average **hides inequality** and ignores cost-of-living differences.

nad0fc5251ac.s: Per capita income alone cannot fully show economic well-being mainly because it:
o: Is an average that conceals inequality and cost-of-living differences
Is compiled only once a decade
Is measured only at constant prices
nad0fc5251ac.x: Being an average, PCI hides inequality and ignores cost-of-living variation.
xa: High PCI can coexist with **poverty + inequality**; the **P4** scheme targets that gap.
Karnataka: **Bengaluru Urban** PCI **₹8,55,960** vs State **₹3,86,156**.
Telangana: **Rangareddy ₹9.5 lakh** vs **Vikarabad ₹1.8 lakh** (2023-24).

n9dd9672501c.s: In which year did India's per capita income record its fastest growth among the years specified?
n9dd9672501c.x: The fastest growth was recorded in 2021-22, at 18.6 percent, reflecting the post-COVID rebound.
n9dd9672501c.tq: Link the peak growth rate with the post-COVID rebound.
xs: India's PCI grew fastest in **2021-22** (**+18.6%**) — option **(3)** is correct — a **post-COVID rebound**.
xa: ⚠ AP's PCI grew **15.26%** in 2021-22 — **below** India's that year.
AP's lowest PCI growth: **4.10% (2019-20)**.

n5cd6acbd7a9.s: Under the Swarna Andhra objective, the target per capita income by 2047 is approximately:
n5cd6acbd7a9.x: Swarna Andhra envisages per capita income above $42,000 by 2047, about ₹55 lakh; ₹5.43 lakh is the 2028-29 per capita GSDP target.
xa: ⚠ Dollar and rupee targets are separate statements.
Vision aim: **double PCI every five years**.

ne48b607c7c1.s: The P4 scheme is intended primarily to address which issue associated with a high per capita income?
o: The difference between central and state tax rates
The gap between NSDP and population estimates
The gap between average income and the persistence of poverty and inequality
The difference between current prices and constant prices
ne48b607c7c1.x: The P4 scheme targets the gap in which a high average per capita income coexists with poverty and inequality.
ne48b607c7c1.tq: Connect the policy intervention with the specific criticism of the average-income indicator.
xs: P4 targets **the gap between average income and the persistence of poverty and inequality** — option **(3)** is correct.
High PCI can coexist with **poverty + inequality** because PCI is an average.
xa: P4 = **Public-Private-People Partnership**.
PCI also ignores **cost-of-living** differences.

nd13550b6926.s: The National Income Committee (1951) estimated India's per capita income for 1948-49 at:
nd13550b6926.x: It put PCI for 1948-49 at ₹225; AP's PCI rose from ₹7,781 in 1960 to about ₹2.07 lakh in 2021-22.
xa: 2021-22 PCI later revised (older notes **₹1,97,214** SRE; latest **₹1,93,703**).
2020-21 PCI: about **₹1.70 lakh** (SES).

n2e11d3df5d7.s: According to the EAC-PM report on Relative Economic Performance of Indian States, the respective shares of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana in national GDP in 2023-24 were:
n2e11d3df5d7.x: The EAC-PM report placed Andhra Pradesh's share at 4.7 per cent and Telangana's at 4.9 per cent in FY 2023-24 national GDP.
n2e11d3df5d7.tq: Check the order of the two States before comparing their shares.
xs: EAC-PM: **AP 4.7 per cent** and **Telangana 4.9 per cent** of national GDP (FY 2023-24) — option **(2)** is correct.
Option **(4)** reverses the two shares (APPSC-G2 2023 key).
xa: Report: **Relative Economic Performance of Indian States (1960-61 to 2023-24)**.
⚠ Telangana's GDP share is larger though its economy = **96.5%** of AP's size (2024-25).
Telangana PCI = **1.35 times** AP's (2024-25).

n0f05fc999f7.s: Among Telangana, Karnataka, Haryana and Tamil Nadu, which had the highest per capita income in 2022-23?
n0f05fc999f7.x: The order was Telangana (₹3.54 lakh), Karnataka (₹3.44 lakh), Haryana and Tamil Nadu (₹3.09 lakh).
xa: Telangana = **richest major State**.
⚠ In **2025-26** Tamil Nadu (**₹4.08 lakh**) is **2nd after Karnataka**.
Telangana PCI = **1.35 times** AP's.

n2976e995b6a.s: The rise in the Gini coefficient of per capita income across Indian States from 0.230 in 1994-95 to 0.261 in 2025-26 indicates:
n2976e995b6a.x: The increase in the Gini coefficient indicates greater divergence in per capita income among Indian States.
n2976e995b6a.tq: Read the direction of change in the inequality measure before interpreting it.
xs: A rising Gini (**0.230** in **1994-95** → **0.261** in **2025-26**) shows **divergence among States** — option **(3)** is correct.
A higher Gini means **more** inter-State inequality, not convergence or uniformity.
xa: AP is **not in that list**.
District gaps exist in every southern State (e.g. Bengaluru Urban **₹8,55,960**).

na4452e0c279.s: Which of the following coastal regions of Andhra Pradesh has historically been more developed than North Andhra and Rayalaseema?
na4452e0c279.x: The Krishna-Guntur coastal belt has historically been more developed than North Andhra and Rayalaseema.
na4452e0c279.tq: Identify the precise regional comparison rather than selecting a neighbouring region.
xs: The **Krishna-Guntur coastal belt** has historically been more developed — option **(2)** is correct.
Kadapa-Chittoor and Kurnool-Anantapur are in **Rayalaseema**; Srikakulam-Vizianagaram is **North Andhra** — the lagging regions.
xa: North Andhra: **Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam**.
Rayalaseema: **Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur, Chittoor**.
Economic regions: **Visakhapatnam (10)**, **Amaravati (9)**, **Tirupati (10)**.

n2367ed69304.s: The seven backward districts identified under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 consisted of:
o: Four Rayalaseema districts and three North Coastal districts
Three Rayalaseema districts and four North Coastal districts
Two Rayalaseema districts and five North Coastal districts
Four Coastal Andhra districts and three Rayalaseema districts
n2367ed69304.x: The backward-area package covered seven districts—four in Rayalaseema and three in the North Coastal region.
n2367ed69304.tq: Split the total into its two component regional counts.
xs: The **7** backward districts = **4 Rayalaseema + 3 North Coastal** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (4) is wrong: Coastal Andhra (Krishna-Guntur) is the **developed** belt.
xa: Package: **₹50 cr per district a year**; releases stalled.
⚠ **Nalgonda** (Telangana) is NOT an AP backward area (APPSC-GS 2022 key).

n997fb7a7b33.s: Which district recorded the lowest multidimensional poverty percentage among the old 13 districts of Andhra Pradesh on the NFHS-5 basis?
n997fb7a7b33.x: West Godavari recorded the lowest multidimensional poverty percentage at 2.42%.
n997fb7a7b33.tq: Discriminate between the lowest and higher district-level poverty figures.
xs: **West Godavari** had the lowest MPI share — **2.42%** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Kurnool** was the highest (**12.84%**, MPI **0.054**); **Vizianagaram 8.66%**, **Visakhapatnam 7.60%**.
xa: Basis: **NFHS-5**, old **13** districts.
⚠ **Nalgonda** (Telangana) is NOT an AP backward area.

ncc632648028.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as a major driver of Visakhapatnam's leading district per capita income?
ncc632648028.x: The identified drivers were Vizag Port; RINL, Hindustan Shipyard and HPCL refinery; Rushikonda IT Park; and the Eastern Naval Command. Amaravati Capital Region Secretariat was not included in that list.
ncc632648028.tq: Find the option outside the stated set of sectoral and institutional drivers.
xs: **Amaravati Capital Region Secretariat** is NOT a driver — option **(3)** is correct.
Drivers: **Vizag Port**; **RINL**, **Hindustan Shipyard**, **HPCL refinery**; **Rushikonda IT Park**; IT; **Eastern Naval Command**.
xa: Visakhapatnam ranked **1st in PCI** for FY 2025-26 (DES, May 2026).
**NTR district**: PCI **₹3,21,651 (2023-24)**; top KPI score (**83** of **315** KPIs).

ndca27c3b837.s: In 2024-25, Telangana's per capita income was about how many times that of Andhra Pradesh?
ndca27c3b837.x: Telangana's PCI was 1.35 times AP's, while its economy was 96.5% of AP's size.
xa: GDP share 2023-24: Telangana **4.9%** vs AP **4.7%**.

n0e6d23bf4e2.s: Which of the following correctly represents the area of residual Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation, as given in the relevant data?
o: 1,62,970 sq km from the date of bifurcation
1,60,205 sq km, later revised to 1,62,970 sq km
n0e6d23bf4e2.x: Residual Andhra Pradesh had an area of 1,60,205 sq km, subsequently shown as 1,62,970 sq km. Telangana covers 1,12,077 sq km.
n0e6d23bf4e2.tq: Use the exact area figures and distinguish the original and revised values.
xs: Residual AP had **1,60,205 sq km**, later revised to **1,62,970 sq km** — option **(4)** is correct.
The rise came from **7 Khammam mandals** moved to AP for **Polavaram**.
**1,12,077 sq km** is **Telangana**; **2,75,000 sq km** is undivided AP; 1,62,970 was not the figure from the date of bifurcation.
xa: Population (Census 2011): AP **4.96 crore**, Telangana **3.52 crore**.
APRA population ratio: **58.32 : 41.68**.
Telangana is **landlocked** — AP kept the **entire coastline**.

nf46746b977a.s: According to the 2011 Census, the population of residual Andhra Pradesh was about:
nf46746b977a.x: Residual Andhra Pradesh had 4.96 crore people and Telangana 3.52 crore; the APRA population ratio was 58.32:41.68.
xa: Central Generating Station power: AP (**58%** population) got only ≈ **46%**.
Undivided AP ≈ **2,75,000 sq km**.

n9c3989eb25c.s: After the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, which State retained the entire coastline and all the ports of the undivided State?
o: Both Andhra Pradesh and Telangana equally
n9c3989eb25c.x: Telangana is landlocked; therefore, residual Andhra Pradesh retained the entire coastline and all the ports of the undivided State.
n9c3989eb25c.tq: Use the geographical condition to identify the State retaining the coastal assets.
xs: **Residual Andhra Pradesh** kept the **entire coastline** and **all ports** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Telangana is landlocked**, so it got no coast.
xa: Ports: **Visakhapatnam, Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, Kakinada, Machilipatnam**.
Coastline: **1,053.07 km**, **3rd longest** (after Gujarat, Tamil Nadu).
AP kept the coast, deltas and Krishna-Godavari tail-end; lost **coal** + Hyderabad industrial base.

n98d36064bac.s: After the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, coal resources went mainly to:
n98d36064bac.x: Coal went mainly to Telangana, while residual Andhra Pradesh retained important coastal and basin minerals.
xa: AP called "**Ratna Garbha**" for its minerals.
AP's minor coal: **Godavari valley belt** (East/West Godavari, ASR).
SCCL's existing coal linkages for AP plants continue (**Twelfth Schedule**).

nc5dbf30158f.s: Mangampet in YSR Kadapa district has India's largest deposit of:
nc5dbf30158f.x: Mangampet has India's largest barytes deposit; Tummalapalle (YSR Kadapa) is AP's uranium site and AP's bauxite is in Araku, Chintapalli and Paderu.
xa: Coal went mainly to **Telangana**.
Limestone: AP **3rd** in India.

n4c485bd2e31.s: Under the Twelfth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, existing SCCL coal linkages for AP thermal plants were:
n4c485bd2e31.x: Existing SCCL linkages were kept unchanged, and new linkages were to be provided under the Government of India's coal policy.
xa: SCCL equity: **51%** Telangana + **49%** GoI.
APGENCO units split by **location**.
AP installed capacity **16,615 MW**; renewables **8,998 MW**.

n11e87528dbf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Green India Mission?
o: It was launched in 2011 as one of the eight missions under the NAPCC
It targets 10 million hectares of new forest cover
It is linked to an additional carbon sink of 2.5-3.0 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2030
Its sub-missions cover forest quality, forest cover and livelihoods
n11e87528dbf.x: GIM targets 5 mha of new forest cover plus 5 mha of quality improvement, not 10 mha of new cover. The other three statements are correct.
xa: **NAP and GIM** merged from **2021-22**; run through the **SFDA** (federation of **22 FDAs**).
**Nagar Van Yojana:** **61 Nagar Vans** sanctioned to AP; State's **Nagaravanam:** **37** city forests.
National Forest Policy **1988** aims at **33%** cover (**66%** in hills).

n8df63537c3a.s: Which one of the following is the principal function of CAMPA as described in the relevant framework?
o: It manages only urban parks in municipal areas.
It allocates coal linkages to thermal power plants.
It spends compensatory levies collected for forest land diverted to non-forest use on afforestation.
It fixes the minimum support price for all agricultural crops.
n8df63537c3a.x: CAMPA, set up by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, uses compensatory levies for afforestation after forest land is diverted to non-forest use.
n8df63537c3a.tq: Ask which institution would perform the compensatory-afforestation function.
xs: **CAMPA** spends **compensatory levies** for forest land diverted to **non-forest use** on **afforestation** — option **(3)**.
It was set up by the **MoEFCC**.
Coal linkages and MSP have nothing to do with CAMPA.
xa: Forest land diverted (Apr-Dec 2025): **149.5687 ha** under **FCA 1980**.
FCA 1980 renamed **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam** from **29 Dec 2023**.

n5b6af99e174.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
o: It recognises the habitat rights of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups
It gives ownership rights over minor forest produce
Under it, the Gram Sabha recommends diversion of forest land only for commercial mining
n5b6af99e174.x: Under FRA the Gram Sabha recommends diversion of forest land for public utilities, not commercial mining. PVTG habitat rights, MFP ownership and nistar rights are all recognised.
xa: **PESA 1996:** Gram Sabhas control **MFP**.
**Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980** renamed **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam** from **29 Dec 2023**.
**AP Forest Act 1967, Section 28:** power to declare that a protected forest ceases to be one.

n4588a705727.s: As per the 2023-24 remeasurement, the coastline of Andhra Pradesh is:
n4588a705727.x: The 2023-24 remeasurement gives 1,053.07 km, the third-longest after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu; 974 km is the older figure.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** some notes say "longest" — wrong.
Telangana is landlocked; AP kept the **entire coastline**.
Fisheries: AP ≈ **29%** of India's fish.

nd750301b82f.s: Which notified non-major port of Andhra Pradesh handles the most cargo?
nd750301b82f.x: Krishnapatnam handles the most cargo among the notified non-major ports; Visakhapatnam is the State's one major port.
xa: **17** notified non-major ports under **GoAP**.
⚠ Only **1** major port (Visakhapatnam); most cargo among non-major = **Krishnapatnam**.

n4928d7f5782.s: Andhra Pradesh is the third-largest producer of which mineral, after Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh?
n4928d7f5782.x: Andhra Pradesh is the third-largest limestone producer after Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh. Limestone occurs in Kurnool, Kadapa, Guntur, Palnadu and NTR districts.
n4928d7f5782.tq: Use the producer ranking to identify the mineral.
xs: AP is **3rd** in **Limestone** after **Rajasthan** and **MP** — option **(4)** is correct (LENS, Oct 2025).
Limestone districts: **Kurnool, Kadapa, Guntur, Palnadu, NTR**.
xa: Barytes: **Mangampet** — largest in India.
Bauxite: **615 MT** resources (Visakhapatnam Agency).
Uranium: **Tummalapalle**.

n92d19905f0f.s: The beach-sand minerals ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet and monazite are associated in Andhra Pradesh mainly with the coastal areas of:
n92d19905f0f.x: These beach-sand minerals occur mainly along the Srikakulam, Visakhapatnam and Kakinada coast.
n92d19905f0f.tq: Group several minerals with their common geographical belt.
xs: Beach sand minerals lie on the **Srikakulam, Visakhapatnam and Kakinada** coast — option **(1)** is correct.
**Kurnool-Kadapa-Palnadu** = limestone; **Araku-Chintapalli-Paderu** = bauxite; **Tummalapalle** = uranium.
xa: Minerals: **ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet, monazite**.
AP kept coastal + basin minerals after bifurcation.

n79a74137e58.s: Among the old districts of Andhra Pradesh, which had the highest forest cover?
n79a74137e58.x: Visakhapatnam had the highest forest cover; YSR Kadapa had the largest forest area and Krishna the least.
xa: Largest forest: **Nallamala** (NSTR).
Forest type: mostly **tropical dry deciduous**.
Dry deciduous belt: **Kadapa and Kurnool** (**75-100 cm**).

ndb7c8940218.s: Under Schedule XI of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, which use of water gets the highest priority?
ndb7c8940218.x: Schedule XI gives drinking water priority over irrigation and irrigation priority over power; tribunal allocations already made remain unchanged.
xa: Undivided AP's **KWDT-I** Krishna allocation: **811 TMC**; ad hoc split **66:34** (AP **512** : TG **299** TMC).
Ongoing projects to be completed: **Handri-Neeva, Telugu Ganga, Galeru-Nagari, Veligonda**, Kalwakurthy, Nettempadu.
**Polavaram** is a **national project** under **Sec. 90**.

n6fef1ae2b93.s: Polavaram is declared a national project under which section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
n6fef1ae2b93.x: Polavaram is a national project under Section 90, and Telangana's consent is deemed to have been given.
xa: Only project declared national by the **Reorganisation Act itself**.
**7 Khammam mandals** moved to AP (Polavaram Ordinance).

n7ee6500461f.s: The planned power-generation capacity of the Polavaram Project is:
n7ee6500461f.x: Polavaram is associated with 960 MW of generation, irrigation of 7.20 lakh acres and transfer of 80 TMC to the Krishna basin.
xa: Polavaram = national project (**Sec. 90**); Telangana's consent **deemed given**.
**Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar** uses only floodwater flowing to sea (Jan 2026).
AP area rose to **1,62,970 sq km** with the Khammam mandals.

nbcbffec4ec2.s: Which region of Andhra Pradesh is largely rain-shadow and drought-prone?
nbcbffec4ec2.x: The Godavari, Krishna and Penna deltas are fertile coastal alluvium, while Rayalaseema is rain-shadow and drought-prone.
xa: AP has **6 agro-climatic zones**.
Rainfall (Jun-Dec 2025): **896.8 mm** = **4.2%** above normal.

n278b7328e56.s: The number of agro-climatic zones identified for Andhra Pradesh is:
n278b7328e56.x: Andhra Pradesh is divided into six agro-climatic zones in the cited data.
n278b7328e56.tq: Recall the exact classification count and reject nearby numerical distractors.
xs: AP has **6** agro-climatic zones — option **(3)** is correct.
The notes give **6 agro-climatic zones**, not 4, 5 or 8.
xa: Fertile deltas: **Godavari, Krishna, Penna**.
**Rayalaseema**: rain-shadow, drought-prone.
Groundwater development (2025-26): **31.5%**.

n3e82085058b.s: Which of the following did residual Andhra Pradesh lose after bifurcation?
n3e82085058b.x: AP retained the coast, the deltas and the Krishna-Godavari tail-end, but lost coal and the Hyderabad industrial base.
xa: Telangana is **landlocked** → AP kept the **entire coastline** + all ports.
AP ("**Ratna Garbha**") kept coastal + basin minerals.
Krishna: ad hoc split **66:34** (AP **512** : TG **299** TMC).

n4ec6786b4b8.s: Forest and tree cover together account for what percentage of the geographical area of Andhra Pradesh?
n4ec6786b4b8.x: Forest plus tree cover accounts for 21.74% of Andhra Pradesh's geographical area according to the cited APPSC assessment.
n4ec6786b4b8.tq: Use the exact combined-cover figure rather than the forest-only percentage.
xs: Forest + tree cover = **21.74%** of AP's area — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC 2025 key).
**23.59%** is forest area incl. scrub; **22.96%** is notified forest area.
xa: National Forest Policy 1988 aims **33%** (**66%** in hills).
TTD: **89.40%** green cover in Tirumala, Seshachalam Hills.

n3d611c23aa0.s: As per ISFR 2021, Andhra Pradesh's Recorded Forest Area of 37,258 sq km ranked it ____ in India.
n3d611c23aa0.x: AP's Recorded Forest Area was 37,258 sq km and it ranked eighth in India, not fifth.

nf4b2f6729ed.s: For ISFR classification, forest cover means land with a tree canopy density of at least:
nf4b2f6729ed.x: Forest cover is land with canopy density of at least 10%, irrespective of legal ownership or notification status.
xa: ISFR published every **two years** by **FSI (Dehradun)**.
Scrub (**8,351.62 sq km**) is not counted as forest cover.

nf7fa38e6881.s: Why is the figure of 38,436.58 sq km, or 23.59%, not identical to the ISFR 2023 forest-cover figure for Andhra Pradesh?
o: It represents the geographical area of Nallamala alone.
It includes only mangrove and littoral vegetation.
It excludes moderately dense forest and open forest.
It includes 8,351.62 sq km of scrub, which ISFR does not count as forest cover.
nf7fa38e6881.x: The larger figure includes 8,351.62 sq km of scrub. ISFR’s forest-cover calculation does not count this scrub area as forest cover.
nf7fa38e6881.tq: Resolve a data discrepancy by identifying the excluded or additionally included category.
xs: It **includes 8,351.62 sq km of scrub**, which ISFR does not count as forest cover — option **(4)** is correct.
Forest cover proper (VDF+MDF+OF) is **30,084.96 sq km**.
xa: ⚠ **23.59%** (incl. scrub) vs **21.74%** (forest + tree cover).
Forest cover = canopy density **≥10%**.

n70b2f65d127.s: Andhra Pradesh is predominantly covered by which type of forest?
n70b2f65d127.x: AP is mostly tropical dry deciduous forest and has 3 national parks, 13 wildlife sanctuaries and 1 tiger reserve.
xa: Protected area **8,139.88 sq km**.
Mangroves ("**Coringa**") at Godavari and Krishna mouths.
Dry deciduous: **Kadapa and Kurnool**.

n1ac294c2a12.s: Which of the following provisions is associated with the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 rather than the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
o: Recognition of community or nistar rights
Ownership of minor forest produce by forest-rights holders
Control of minor forest produce by Gram Sabhas
n1ac294c2a12.x: PESA, 1996 gives Gram Sabhas control over minor forest produce. Ownership of minor forest produce, PVTG habitat rights and community or nistar rights are associated here with the FRA, 2006.
n1ac294c2a12.tq: Separate the similar-looking roles of PESA and FRA by assigning each provision to the correct law.
xs: **Control of minor forest produce by Gram Sabhas** is a **PESA 1996** provision — option **(3)**.
**FRA 2006** gives **ownership of MFP**, **nistar** rights and **PVTG habitat rights**.
xa: FRA: the Gram Sabha recommends diversion for **public utilities**.
**VSS** = village **JFM** bodies.

n0bca6abd8f6.s: Andhra Pradesh accounts for approximately what share of India's cultured-shrimp exports?
n0bca6abd8f6.x: AP accounts for about 75 per cent of India's cultured-shrimp exports and about 29 per cent of India's fish production.
xa: Mangroves at the river mouths are called "**Coringa** forests".
**Great Green Wall of AP**: mangroves → palmyra → wider green cover.

nde13cbc8b75.s: Which is the largest forest of Andhra Pradesh, home to NSTR, India's largest tiger reserve?
nde13cbc8b75.x: Nallamala is AP's largest forest; NSTR, India's largest tiger reserve, lies in it and is shared with Telangana.
xa: Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve: **4,756 sq km**.
Red sanders ranges include **Nallamala**, Seshachalam, Veligonda, Lankamala, Talakona.

nc84e7afbcb1.s: In Andhra Pradesh, tidal or mangrove forests occur mainly at:
o: The mouths of the Godavari and Krishna
nc84e7afbcb1.x: Mangrove (Coringa) forests occur near the Godavari and Krishna mouths; moist deciduous forests are in the north-coastal hills, dry deciduous in Kadapa-Kurnool and thorn-scrub in interior Rayalaseema.
xa: AP's forests are mostly **tropical dry deciduous**.
Rainfall: moist deciduous **125-200 cm**; dry deciduous **75-100 cm**; thorn/scrub **below 75 cm**.
AP has the **second-largest mangrove** ecosystem (Godavari-Krishna estuaries).

na24c5247029.s: The Red Sanders Protection Scheme covers Seshachalam, Veligonda, Lankamala, Talakona and ____ ranges.
na24c5247029.x: The scheme covers the five ranges Seshachalam, Veligonda, Lankamala, Nallamala and Talakona.
xa: Districts: **Annamayya, Kadapa, Nandyal, Chittoor, Nellore, Tirupati, Prakasam**.
2023-24: **₹2,500 lakh** allocated; **₹1,529 lakh** spent.
Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve: **4,756 sq km**.

n1c868b2aa92.s: How many Nagar Vans were sanctioned to Andhra Pradesh under the Central Nagar Van Yojana?
n1c868b2aa92.x: The Central Nagar Van Yojana sanctioned 61 Nagar Vans; the State's Nagaravanam programme completed 37 city forests and seven Temple Eco-parks.
xa: ⚠ Do not mix up **Nagaravanam (37)** and **NVY (61)**.
NVY: sanctioned between **2021-22 and 2024-25**; **₹9,913.926 lakh** released, **₹5,248.641 lakh** spent by **31 Dec 2024**.
⚠ The 2023 PYQ on the NVY count has no answer key.

ndaede288f05.s: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 was renamed as the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 with effect from:
ndaede288f05.x: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 was renamed with effect from 29 December 2023. The change was an amendment and not a repeal of the law.
ndaede288f05.tq: Use the exact effective date and distinguish renaming by amendment from repeal.
xs: The FCA 1980 became the **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980** from **29 December 2023** — option **(2)**.
It was **amended, not repealed**.
xa: Forest land diverted (Apr-Dec 2025): **149.5687 ha** under FCA 1980.
**CAMPA** spends compensatory levies on afforestation.
**FRA 2006**: Gram Sabha recommends diversion for **public utilities**.

n01478878eed.s: Under Section 28 of the Andhra Pradesh Forest Act, 1967, which power is conferred?
o: Power to declare that a protected forest ceases to be a protected forest
Power to determine the minimum support price of minor forest produce
Power to authorise diversion of any forest land for mining
Power to declare that a reserved forest has become a village forest
n01478878eed.x: Section 28 confers the power to declare that a protected forest ceases to be a protected forest.
n01478878eed.tq: Match the exact statutory section with the specific power rather than a neighbouring forest-law function.
xs: Section 28 gives the **power to declare that a protected forest ceases to be a protected forest** — option **(1)** (APPSC **2024**).
This is under the **AP Forest Act 1967**.
xa: **FCA 1980** renamed **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam** from **29 Dec 2023**.
**PESA 1996**: Gram Sabhas control **MFP**.
AP ranks **8th** in **Recorded Forest Area**.

n2810ad3b553.s: The Hyderabad region, including Rangareddy and Medak, contributed nearly what share of the undivided State's tax and non-tax revenue?
n2810ad3b553.x: The Hyderabad region, together with Rangareddy and Medak, contributed nearly 50 percent of the undivided State's tax and non-tax revenue.
n2810ad3b553.tq: Use the region-based share rather than the city-specific figure.
xs: The **Hyderabad region** (+ **Rangareddy, Medak**) gave **nearly 50 percent** of undivided AP's tax + non-tax revenue — option **(3)**.
Key sources: **corporate taxes**, **stamp duties**, **commercial taxes**.
xa: Losing Hyderabad left AP with a **structural revenue deficit**.
Lost assets: **HITEC City**, Financial District, **Genome Valley**, corporate and bank head offices.
Tax impact: lower **GST (then VAT)**, stamp duty and **motor-vehicle tax** collections.

n2c59035a618.s: Which one of the following was NOT identified as part of the economic base lost with Hyderabad?
o: The entire agricultural base of residual Andhra Pradesh
HITEC City and the Financial District
n2c59035a618.x: The lost economic base included HITEC City, the Financial District, Genome Valley, corporate and bank head offices, commercial real estate and related MSME supply chains. It did not comprise the entire agricultural base of residual Andhra Pradesh.
n2c59035a618.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the Hyderabad economic cluster.
xs: **The entire agricultural base of residual AP** was NOT lost with Hyderabad — option **(1)**.
Lost: **HITEC City + Financial District**, **Genome Valley** pharma cluster, **corporate and bank head offices**, commercial real estate, MSME supply chains.
xa: Effect: **structural revenue deficit** and a **narrower tax base**.
Tax collections cut: **GST (then VAT)**, stamp duty, motor-vehicle tax.

n7382f453bf2.s: The resource-gap estimates for Andhra Pradesh were ₹4,118 crore, ₹13,776 crore and ₹16,078 crore according to, respectively:
o: The Union Finance Ministry, the CAG and the State
The Union Finance Ministry, the State and the CAG
The State, the Union Finance Ministry and the CAG
The CAG, the State and the Union Finance Ministry
n7382f453bf2.x: The Union estimate was ₹4,118 crore, the CAG-linked estimate was ₹13,776 crore and the State estimate was ₹16,078 crore.
n7382f453bf2.tq: Match each figure with the authority that produced or reported it.
xs: **₹4,118 crore** = **Union Finance Ministry**; **₹13,776 crore** = **CAG**; **₹16,078 crore** = **State** — option **(1)**.
The CAG figure covers **2 Jun 2014 - 31 Mar 2015** (APPSC-GS 2016 key).
xa: Centre's lower figure excluded scheme costs like the **farm-loan waiver**.
⚠ The printed APPSC 2016 key is garbled ("...3,776 Cr"); it is not ₹20,745 / 16,211 / 21,481 crore.
APPSC-GS 2022 key: gap **more than ₹15,000 crore**.

n1152a534c77.s: The resource gap of Andhra Pradesh in the bifurcation year (2014-15) was:
o: Between Rs 5,000 crore and Rs 10,000 crore
Between Rs 10,000 crore and Rs 12,000 crore
n1152a534c77.x: The APPSC-GS 2022 key puts the bifurcation-year gap at more than Rs 15,000 crore (the State itself claimed Rs 16,078 crore). The lower ranges match only the Union Finance Ministry's narrower assessment of about Rs 4,118 crore or are unsupported.
xs: APPSC-GS 2022 key: the bifurcation-year gap was **more than Rs 15,000 crore** — option **(4)**.
AP's own claim was **₹16,078 crore**.
The lower ranges fit only the Centre's narrower ≈ **₹4,118 crore**.
xa: CAG figure: **₹13,776 crore** (2 Jun 2014 - 31 Mar 2015).
Resource gap = **revenue deficit** for the first ten months.
n1152a534c77.fixed: drop 'according to APPSC answer key' wording; no exam phrases it so

n265d9ed1360.s: As per the APPSC 2021 reference, the revenue deficit of Andhra Pradesh for 2022-23 was projected at about:
n265d9ed1360.x: The 2022-23 revenue deficit was projected at about Rs 17,000 crore; the actual turned out to be Rs 43,487 crore (3.3% of GSDP). Rs 4,118 crore was the Union's 2014-15 gap estimate and Rs 60,285 crore is the 2024-25 revenue deficit.
xs: The 2022-23 RD was projected at about **Rs 17,000 crore** (APPSC **2021**) — option **(2)**.
The actual was **₹43,487 crore** (**3.3%**).
**₹4,118 crore** was the Centre's 2014-15 gap estimate; **₹60,285 crore** is the 2024-25 RD.
xa: CAG flagged high revenue deficit **three years running**.

n9e5c3913335.s: In January 2026, the amount of special assistance fast-tracked for Amaravati was
n9e5c3913335.x: Special assistance of ₹15,000 crore was fast-tracked for Amaravati in January 2026.
n9e5c3913335.tq: Use the distinctive figure and date to distinguish the Amaravati assistance from the broader assistance package.
xs: **₹15,000 crore** central assistance was **fast-tracked for Amaravati** — option **(2)**.
**₹3,979 crore** was the 2014-15 RD grant.
xa: Sec. 94(3): **₹2,500 crore** for **capital buildings**.
AP blames the **loss of capital city** among its fiscal pressures.

n079f48336b6.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the appointed day for the bifurcation of the State was:
n079f48336b6.x: The State was divided on 2 June 2014, which was the appointed day. The Act received presidential assent on 1 March 2014.
n079f48336b6.tq: Distinguish the date of assent from the appointed day.
xs: The **appointed day** was **2 June 2014** — option **(2)**.
⚠ The Act got assent on **1 March 2014**; "came into effect on **2 March 2014**" is a wrong claim in some notes.
**31 March 2015** ends the **first year** (2 June 2014 - 31 March 2015).
xa: **Resource gap** = revenue deficit for the **first ten months**.
CAG put the 2014-15 revenue deficit at **₹13,776 crore**.

na4173aa7155.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the difference between the Centre’s and Andhra Pradesh’s estimates of the post-bifurcation resource gap?
o: The Centre calculated only capital expenditure, whereas the State calculated only tax expenditure
The Centre used CAG figures, whereas the State used Finance Commission projections
The Centre included all new State schemes, whereas the State excluded them
The Centre used standardised accounting and excluded new State schemes, whereas the State counted its actual expenditure
na4173aa7155.x: The Union calculation used standardised accounting and left out new State schemes, while Andhra Pradesh counted its actual spending.
na4173aa7155.tq: Split the options by comparing the accounting method and treatment of new schemes.
xs: The **Centre used standardised accounting and excluded new State schemes**; the **State counted its actual expenditure** — option **(4)**.
Option (3) reverses the positions.
xa: Centre's figure ≈ **₹4,118 crore**; State's **₹16,078 crore**; CAG **₹13,776 crore**.
First year: **2 June 2014** to **31 March 2015**.

ne717b45b6eb.s: In the context of Andhra Pradesh's bifurcation, the 'resource gap' for the first post-bifurcation year refers to:
o: The fiscal deficit of the State for the full financial year 2014-15
The revenue deficit (revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts) for the first ten months
The shortfall in capital outlay compared with the 13th Finance Commission projection
The difference between borrowings and repayments for 2014-15
ne717b45b6eb.x: The resource gap was defined as the revenue deficit, i.e. revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts, for the first ten months (2 June 2014 to 31 March 2015). It is not the full-year fiscal deficit, a capital-outlay shortfall or a net borrowing figure.
ne717b45b6eb.tq: Resource gap = revenue deficit, first 10 months.
xs: Resource gap = **the revenue deficit (revenue expenditure − revenue receipts) for the first ten months** — option **(2)**.
Period: **2 June 2014** (appointed day) to **31 March 2015**.
It is not the full-year **fiscal deficit**, a capital-outlay shortfall or net borrowing.
xa: Estimates: CAG **₹13,776 crore**; State **₹16,078 crore**; Centre ≈ **₹4,118 crore**.
RD grant for 2014-15: **₹3,979 crore**.

na208cc39fb7.s: The Fourteenth Finance Commission fixed a normative post-devolution revenue gap for Andhra Pradesh from:
na208cc39fb7.x: The 14th FC fixed a normative, static post-devolution gap from 2015-16; AP argued its actual deficits exceeded it.
xa: 14th FC gave AP **₹22,113 crore** post-devolution RD grants over **2015-20**.
14th FC raised devolution from **32% to 42%**.

n5146b91def3.s: Andhra Pradesh sought tax holidays for post-bifurcation industrialisation under which section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
n5146b91def3.x: AP's demands included tax holidays under Section 94(1) and backward-area packages under Section 46, besides revenue-deficit grants, Polavaram funding and capital-city grants.
xa: Main demand: **Special Category Status**.

nfb8edf48a1a.s: The Special Assistance Measure for Andhra Pradesh involved the Centre funding what share of externally aided projects?
nfb8edf48a1a.x: Under the Special Assistance Measure, the Centre funded the 90 percent share of externally aided projects, serving as an alternative to Special Category Status.
nfb8edf48a1a.tq: Distinguish the project-support share from general tax devolution percentages.
xs: Under **SAM**, the Centre funds **90 percent** of **externally aided projects** — option **(4)**.
It was given **instead of SCS**.
**32%** and **42%** are devolution shares; **60%** is the normal CSS share.
xa: ⚠ SCS meant **90%** of **CSS costs**; SAM = **90%** of **externally aided projects**.
The **₹3,979 crore** RD grant was part of SAM.

n7542b051fd8.s: How much central assistance was provided for capital buildings of Andhra Pradesh under Section 94(3) of the Reorganisation Act?
n7542b051fd8.x: ₹2,500 crore was given for capital buildings under Section 94(3); ₹3,979 crore was the 2014-15 revenue deficit grant and ₹22,113 crore the 2015-20 post-devolution grants.
xa: **₹15,000 crore** central assistance fast-tracked for **Amaravati**.

na02b9f403a7.s: Under the 16th Finance Commission, which ended revenue deficit grants for all States, Andhra Pradesh's share of the divisible pool rose to:
na02b9f403a7.x: The 16th FC ended revenue deficit grants for all States, and AP's divisible-pool share rose to 4.22%.
xa: **14th FC** gave AP **₹22,113 crore** in RD grants (**2015-20**).
14th FC devolution: **32% → 42%**.

n4a16fb859e0.s: Corporate taxes, stamp duties and ____ were important components of the Hyderabad region's revenue in the undivided State.
n4a16fb859e0.x: Corporate taxes, stamp duties and commercial taxes were key parts of Hyderabad's revenue contribution; agricultural land revenue was not its basis.
xa: Hyderabad region gave nearly **50%** of undivided AP's tax + non-tax revenue.
Loss of HITEC City + Financial District → loss of **IT/ITeS exports**.
Result: a **narrower tax base** for residual AP.

nfc3117e48f4.s: In the 2026-27 Budget Estimates of Andhra Pradesh, the revenue deficit and fiscal deficit are respectively about:
nfc3117e48f4.x: 2026-27 BE: RD Rs 22,002 crore (1.11%) and FD Rs 75,868 crore (3.84%). 3.79%/5.11% are 2024-25 Finance Accounts, 2.33%/4.57% are 2025-26 RE, and 3.3%/4.3% mix the 2022-23 RD and 2023-24 FD ratios.
xs: In rupees: RD **₹22,002 crore**, FD **₹75,868 crore**.
xa: Rounded Budget 2026-27 targets: RD **1.1%**, FD **3.8%**.

n8cbe6b3bfef.s: In FY25, the combined fiscal deficit of Indian States stood at about:
n8cbe6b3bfef.x: States' combined fiscal deficit was about 3.2% of GDP in FY25, and revenue balances worsened in 18 States between FY19 and FY25.
xa: ⚠ The notes' national context says only that **18 states'** revenue balances worsened FY19-FY25.

n31877006545.s: The debt of Andhra Pradesh in the 2024-25 revised estimates was reported as ₹5,64,488 crore, equivalent to
n31877006545.x: Andhra Pradesh's debt was reported at ₹5,64,488 crore, or 35.15 percent of GSDP, in the 2024-25 revised estimates.
n31877006545.tq: Match the absolute debt figure with its corresponding ratio rather than confusing it with deficit ratios.
xs: Debt of **₹5,64,488 crore** = **35.15 percent of GSDP** (2024-25 RE) — option **(1)**.
Market loans make up **75%** of it.

nb76509efdf1.s: As per Accounts at a Glance 2024-25, Andhra Pradesh's fiscal deficit, against an FRBM ceiling of 4%, was:
nb76509efdf1.x: AP recorded a fiscal deficit of 5.05% against the 4% ceiling and a revenue deficit of 3.75% against the 2.70% target.
xa: Finance Accounts give **3.79% / 5.11%**.
Borrowings **₹81,071 crore**; misstatements ~**₹6,120 crore**.

nd0c53d4842b.s: The additional borrowing window linked to power-sector reforms permitted States to borrow up to:
o: 3.5% of GSDP, with an additional 0.5% conditional on power-sector reforms
4% of GSDP, with an additional 1% conditional on tax reforms
nd0c53d4842b.x: The Department of Expenditure allowed a fiscal deficit of 3.5% of GSDP plus an additional 0.5% if power-sector reforms were undertaken.
nd0c53d4842b.tq: Separate the basic borrowing limit from the conditional additional window.
xs: Borrowing window: FD **3.5% of GSDP + 0.5%** conditional on **power-sector reforms** — option **(1)**.
It was set by the **Department of Expenditure**.
xa: AP undertook the DoE reforms in **February 2021** — the **second** State.
CAG: power subsidy spending at **121% (2023)** and **120% (2024)** of BE.

nc7701996369.s: In February 2021, Andhra Pradesh became the ______ State to undertake the power-sector reforms stipulated by the Department of Expenditure.
nc7701996369.x: The stated APPSC 2023 answer key treated Andhra Pradesh as the second State to undertake the reforms.
nc7701996369.tq: Test the ordinal detail directly, since close ordinal distractors are commonly used.
xs: AP was the **second** State to undertake the DoE power reforms (**February 2021**) — option **(3)** (APPSC **2023** key).
The reforms unlocked the extra **0.5%** borrowing over **3.5%** of GSDP.
xa: CAG: power subsidy at **121%** (2023) and **120%** (2024) of BE.
**APSPDCL**: first AP DISCOM to connect **50,000** rooftop-solar services.

nf38d977eb82.s: Justice R.S. Bachawat was the Chairperson of which pair of tribunals?
nf38d977eb82.x: Justice R.S. Bachawat chaired KWDT-I and the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal, whereas KWDT-II was chaired by Justice Brijesh Kumar.
nf38d977eb82.tq: Discriminate between tribunal chairpersons by matching the repeated name with the correct two tribunals.
xs: Justice **R.S. Bachawat** chaired **KWDT-I and GWDT** — option **(4)**.
**KWDT-II** was chaired by Justice **Brijesh Kumar**, so options (1) and (3) are wrong.
The **Tungabhadra Board** is a board under the **Andhra State Act, 1953**, not a tribunal.
xa: KWDT-I award **1973**, final **1976**; GWDT award **1980**.
KWDT-II award **2010** (further report **2013**).
GWDT was based on **inter-State agreements**.

ne5324b8f7e5.s: At 75 per cent dependability, which set of shares was awarded by KWDT-I to Maharashtra, Karnataka and the united Andhra Pradesh respectively?
ne5324b8f7e5.x: KWDT-I awarded 560 TMC to Maharashtra, 700 TMC to Karnataka and 800 TMC to the united Andhra Pradesh at 75 per cent dependability.
ne5324b8f7e5.tq: Use the fixed three-State numerical sequence and avoid swapping neighbouring entries.
xs: **560, 700 and 800 TMC** — Maharashtra, Karnataka, united AP — option **(2)**.
These are KWDT-I shares at **75%** dependability.
xa: AP's **800** + **11** return flows = **811 TMC** (APPSC-GS 2021 key gives AP **800**).

n55f5855fda0.s: The united Andhra Pradesh share of 800 TMC under KWDT-I became 811 TMC when what was added?
n55f5855fda0.x: The 800 TMC allocation, together with 11 TMC of return flows, produced the 811 TMC figure used in the ad hoc division.
n55f5855fda0.tq: Test the small numerical component that explains the difference between two closely related totals.
xs: **11 TMC of return flows** were added to AP's **800 TMC** to make **811** — option **(1)**.
The notes mention no evaporation, recharge or inter-basin item in this sum.
xa: Telangana demands **50:50**, citing larger basin area.

n82973e0609e.s: The Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal-II was chaired by:
n82973e0609e.x: KWDT-II was chaired by Justice Brijesh Kumar; its award came in 2010 with a further report in 2013.
xa: CDI notes put AP's added share at **196 TMC**.

n06c4b22a41f.s: Telangana's demand for a 50:50 split of Krishna water rests on its:
n06c4b22a41f.x: Telangana's 50:50 demand rests on its larger basin area, not population; the 2014 ad hoc split gave AP 512 TMC and Telangana 299 TMC (66:34).
xa: **KWDT-I** gave **united AP 800 TMC** (+ **11** return flows).
**Sec. 89:** KWDT-II's term was extended for **project-wise allocation** and an **operational protocol** for **deficit flows**.
**KRMB** HQ is in **Andhra Pradesh**; **GRMB** HQ is in **Telangana**.

n864243a1340.s: In the Cauvery water dispute, the Supreme Court’s 2018 verdict fixed the share of Tamil Nadu at:
n864243a1340.x: The 2018 Cauvery verdict fixed Tamil Nadu’s share at 404.25 TMC. Karnataka, Kerala and Puducherry were allocated 284.75, 30 and 7 TMC respectively.
n864243a1340.tq: Separate the largest State share from the other three figures in the comparative allocation.
xs: The SC **2018** Cauvery verdict gave **Tamil Nadu 404.25 TMC** — option **(3)**.
**Karnataka 284.75**, **Kerala 30**, **Puducherry 7** tmcft.
xa: Compare Krishna: KWDT-I gave united AP **800 TMC** (**811** with return flows).
AP's ad hoc Krishna share: **512 TMC** (**66 : 34**).

n3b854920a87.s: Who is the Chairperson of the Apex Council constituted under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
n3b854920a87.x: The three-member Apex Council is chaired by the Union Minister of Water Resources, with the CMs of AP and Telangana as members.
xa: ⚠ NOT the **PM**, Home Minister or Governors.
It supervises **GRMB and KRMB**.

nb629930e47a.s: Under Schedule XI of the AP Reorganisation Act, a function of the KRMB and GRMB is:
o: Approving new projects on the Krishna and Godavari
Regulating supply from notified headworks according to tribunal awards
Redetermining the shares of AP and Telangana every water year
Referring water disputes to a tribunal
nb629930e47a.x: The Boards regulate supply from notified headworks as per tribunal awards and release water by State shares; approving projects and referring disputes belong to the Apex Council, and redetermining shares is not their function.
xa: **Sec. 88**: a Board may make regulations.
**Aug 2026**: KRMB committee allowed only **drinking water** from Srisailam + Nagarjuna Sagar.

n789e269ccb5.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the purposes for which KWDT’s term was extended under Section 89?
o: Addressing project-wise and operational issues within the scope of the reference
Automatically dividing the undivided Andhra Pradesh share between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
Fixing an operational protocol for releases during deficit flows
Making project-wise allocations where no tribunal had done so
n789e269ccb5.x: Section 89 covered project-wise allocation where necessary and an operational protocol for deficit flows. It did not itself automatically divide the Andhra Pradesh share between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
n789e269ccb5.tq: Distinguish the express terms of a statutory reference from a later political or legal demand.
xs: **Automatically dividing the undivided AP share** is NOT a **Sec. 89** purpose — option **(2)**.
Sec. 89 extended KWDT-II's term for **(a) project-wise allocation** where no tribunal had done so and **(b) an operational protocol** for releases in **deficit flows**.
The division of AP's share came later through **Sec. 5(1)** of the **ISRWD Act** (**Oct 2023**).
xa: AP wanted allocations redone among **four States**.
KWDT-II award: **2010**; not notified, challenged in SC.

n2f6145ffb30.s: In October 2023, the Centre gave KWDT-II further terms of reference under:
o: Section 89 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014
Section 5(1) of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956
Section 87 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014
Section 3 of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956
n2f6145ffb30.x: The October 2023 terms of reference were given under Section 5(1) of the ISRWD Act, 1956, not Section 89 of APRA alone.
xa: **Sec. 89** extended KWDT-II's term for **project-wise allocation** and a **deficit-flow protocol**.
The **Apex Council** refers disputes not covered by KWDT to a tribunal under the **ISRWD Act, 1956**.
Apex Council: **Union Minister of Water Resources** (chair) + **CMs of AP and Telangana** — **3 members**.

n068b5b26e50.s: Under Section 84(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Apex Council for the Krishna and Godavari rivers was constituted by the Centre from which date?
o: The date of constitution of the two River Management Boards
The date of publication of the tribunal awards
The date of enactment of the Act
n068b5b26e50.x: Section 84(1) provides for constitution of the Apex Council by the Centre from the appointed day.
n068b5b26e50.tq: Recall the statutory trigger date rather than the date of a later institutional action.
xs: Under **Sec. 84(1)**, the Apex Council is constituted by the Centre **from the appointed day** — option **(1)**.
The Boards came later — within **60 days** of the appointed day (**Sec. 85(1)**).
xa: **Sec. 84(3)** lists Apex Council functions.
Members: Union Minister of Water Resources (Chair) + CMs of AP and Telangana.

n8fb1c10ffcf.s: The power to approve a new project on the Krishna or Godavari, after appraisal by the concerned Board and the Central Water Commission, belongs to which body?
o: The Krishna River Management Board alone
The Godavari River Management Board alone
n8fb1c10ffcf.x: Under Section 84(3), approval of new Krishna or Godavari projects after the prescribed appraisal is a function of the Apex Council.
n8fb1c10ffcf.tq: Use the authority-based trap by distinguishing the Apex Council from the subordinate Boards.
xs: The **Apex Council** approves new Krishna/Godavari projects after **Board + CWC** appraisal — option **(2)**.
The **Boards** regulate supply per tribunal awards but do not sanction projects.
xa: ⚠ "Power to sanction new projects" = **Apex Council**, not the Boards or the Ministry.
Chair: **Union Minister of Water Resources**.

n5ac8ab09075.s: The Ministry of Jal Shakti notified the jurisdiction of the KRMB and GRMB on:
n5ac8ab09075.x: Both Boards' jurisdiction was notified on 15 July 2021; under Section 87 the Boards have jurisdiction over projects notified by the Centre.
xa: ⚠ **Allocating or redetermining shares** is **NOT** a Board function.

nab748903547.s: A State fails to comply with the directions applicable to a River Management Board. Under Section 92 read with Schedule XI, which consequence may follow?
o: Financial and other penalties imposed by the Centre
Automatic dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly
Cancellation of the relevant tribunal award by the Board
Transfer of all State water projects to the Supreme Court
nab748903547.x: A defaulting State may face financial and other penalties from the Centre under Section 92 and Schedule XI.
nab748903547.tq: Identify the consequence linked to non-compliance without confusing it with judicial or constitutional sanctions.
xs: A defaulting State faces **financial and other penalties** from the **Centre** — option **(1)** (**Sec. 92 / Schedule XI**).
Boards cannot cancel tribunal awards.
xa: Boards: **autonomous bodies** under the Centre's administrative control (**Sec. 85(3)**).
**CISF** guards reservoirs (**85(7)**).

nfb21198e20d.s: The Tungabhadra Board was set up under Section 66 of which Act?
nfb21198e20d.x: The Board was set up under Section 66 of the Andhra State Act, 1953; under Section 91(1) of APRA, AP and Telangana replaced undivided AP on it.
xa: **Sec. 92 / Schedule XI:** a defaulting State faces financial and other penalties.
**Sec. 88:** a Board may make regulations.

n9a91729cd98.s: Polavaram was declared a national project under which section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
n9a91729cd98.x: Section 90 of APRA declared Polavaram a national project; it is planned for 960 MW.
xa: Polavaram floodwater diversion: **200 tmcft** via the Nallamala Sagar link.
**Telangana and Odisha** object to Polavaram **submergence**.

n5ca8ed43b13.s: The Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar Link envisages diversion of water:
o: From the Krishna through the Godavari to the Penna
From the Godavari through the Krishna to the Penna
From the Penna through the Krishna to the Godavari
From the Godavari through the Penna to the Krishna
n5ca8ed43b13.x: The link envisages diversion from the Godavari through the Krishna basin to the Penna basin.
xa: The link was earlier **Polavaram-Banakacherla**.
**Palamuru-Rangareddy**, Dindi — Telangana projects on the **Krishna**.

n0c3c55b0c1d.s: Telangana objects to AP's Pothireddypadu Head Regulator/Rayalaseema Lift project on the ground that Srisailam is mainly a:
n0c3c55b0c1d.x: Telangana's objection is that Srisailam is mainly a power project; AP built the scheme on the Krishna.
xa: **Aug 2026**: KRMB allowed only drinking water from Srisailam + Nagarjuna Sagar.
Disputes over **hydel drawal** continue.

n9a172380906.s: Kaleshwaram, a subject of inter-State objections, is a Telangana project on which river?
n9a172380906.x: Kaleshwaram is Telangana's Godavari project; AP sought clearances for it while Telangana wants national-project status.
xa: Kaleshwaram is a Telangana project on the **Godavari**.
Telangana raised Kaleshwaram's national status at the **31st Southern Zonal Council** (Aug 2026).

nac53c172d82.s: Andhra Pradesh plans to divert how much Polavaram flood water through the Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar Link?
nac53c172d82.x: Andhra Pradesh plans to divert 200 TMC of Polavaram flood water through the proposed link.
nac53c172d82.tq: Distinguish the proposed diversion quantity from project-capacity and tribunal-share figures.
xs: AP plans to divert **200 TMC** of Polavaram floodwater — option **(3)**.
It would serve ~**80 lakh** people and ~**7.5 lakh** acres via reservoirs at **Bollapalli** and **Banakacherla**.
**960** is Polavaram's MW; **404.25** is TN's Cauvery share; **120 MW** is a wrong Polavaram figure.
xa: **Telangana withdrew** its SC petition against the link (Jan 2026).
AP says the link uses only floodwater flowing to the sea.

n3cf766f6eb0.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the Apex Council under Section 84(3) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Referring disputes not covered by KWDT to a tribunal under the ISRWD Act, 1956
Allocating or redetermining the shares of the States in river waters
Approving new projects on the Krishna and Godavari after appraisal by the Board and the CWC
Supervising the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards
n3cf766f6eb0.x: The Apex Council can supervise the Boards, approve new projects after appraisal, settle disputes by negotiation and refer certain disputes to a tribunal. Allocation or redetermination of shares is not stated as its function here.
n3cf766f6eb0.tq: Separate the power to approve projects and settle disputes from the power to allocate water shares.
xs: **Allocating or redetermining the shares** is NOT an Apex Council function — option **(2)**.

Its **Sec. 84(3)** functions: **supervise both Boards**, **approve new projects** after Board + CWC appraisal, settle disputes by negotiation, refer disputes to a tribunal under the **ISRWD Act, 1956**.
xa: ⚠ Allocating shares is **not a Board function** either.
Shares come from tribunals: **KWDT-I**, **KWDT-II**, **GWDT**.

n0ec87c3bd2c.s: What is the installed hydel capacity of the Polavaram Project?
n0ec87c3bd2c.x: The Polavaram hydel component has an installed capacity of 960 MW, made up of 12 units of 80 MW each.
xa: Irrigation: **7.20 lakh acres** (= **2.91 lakh ha**).
Gross storage **194.6 TMC**; utilisation **322.73 TMC**.
**23.44 TMC** is earmarked for **Visakhapatnam** drinking water and industry.

n8515ab1e556.s: How much Godavari water does the Polavaram Right Main Canal transfer to the Krishna?
n8515ab1e556.x: Polavaram transfers 80 TMC of Godavari water to the Krishna through the Right Main Canal; 23.44 TMC is provided for Visakhapatnam.
xa: Split of the 80 TMC: **45 TMC** to AP + **35 TMC** to Karnataka (**21**) and Maharashtra (**14**).
**Pattiseema** is a temporary lift into the Polavaram **RMC**.
GWDT was set up in **1969**; award in **1980**.

nfc38d492dbb.s: The Polavaram Project site, earlier identified with West Godavari district, now lies in which district?
nfc38d492dbb.x: The project is near Polavaram village in Eluru district; the site was earlier identified with West Godavari district.
xa: ⚠ **West Godavari** is the old PYQ key for the district.
Dam: **2,467.50 m** earth-cum-rock fill; spillway **1,121.20 m**.
Started under **Jalayagnam** in **2005**; first contemplated in **1941**.

nfc74cacaa3c.s: The Polavaram proposal was named "Ramapada Sagaram" by:
nfc74cacaa3c.x: Sir Sonti Venkataramamurthy named the proposal Ramapada Sagaram; the project was first contemplated in 1941.
xa: **2014** is the year of the **AP Reorganisation Act**, whose **Section 90** made Polavaram a national project.
The **Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal** (set up **1969**) gave its award in **1980**.
Site: on the **Godavari**, near Polavaram village, **Eluru district**.

ndb99475332f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal?
o: Of the 80 TMC diverted into the Krishna above Vijayawada, AP gets 45 TMC
It was set up in 1969 and gave its award in 1980
Its award cleared Polavaram with an FRL of +150 ft
Of the remaining 35 TMC, Karnataka gets 14 TMC and Maharashtra 21 TMC
ndb99475332f.x: The remaining 35 TMC is split 21 TMC to Karnataka and 14 TMC to Maharashtra, not the reverse.
xa: The transfer runs via the **Right Main Canal**.
Telangana says the proposed **Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar** link violates the **1980 GWDT award** and **APRA 2014**.

n0dad6854863.s: The proposed Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar link was earlier known as the:
n0dad6854863.x: The Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar link was earlier called the Banakacherla link; Telangana contends it violates APRA 2014 and the 1980 GWDT award.
xa: GWDT award: **80 TMC** Godavari water diverted into Krishna — **45** to AP, **35** to Karnataka and Maharashtra.
Polavaram: **960 MW**; **7.20 lakh acres**; FRL **45.72 m**.
The **Right Main Canal** feeds the **Krishna delta**; the **Left Main Canal** runs to **Visakhapatnam**.

n13c01050950.s: The target for completion of the Polavaram Project was shifted from December 2027 to:
n13c01050950.x: The completion target was moved forward from December 2027 to March 2027, before the 2027 Godavari Pushkaralu.
n13c01050950.tq: Distinguish the revised target from the original target and the R&R deadline.
xs: The completion target moved from Dec 2027 to **March 2027** — option **(1)**.
The aim is to finish before the **2027 Godavari Pushkaralu**.
**December 2026** is the target for **R&R colonies**, not the whole project.
xa: Aug 2026: **90% civil works**, **77% overall**.
LMC up to **Visakhapatnam** also targeted for **Mar 2027**.

n89df7e8fe6a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Polavaram Project under Section 90 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Section 90 declares Polavaram a national project
Under Section 90(4), the Government of Andhra Pradesh shall execute the project and obtain all clearances
Under Section 90(3), the consent of Telangana is deemed to have been given
In practice, AP executes the irrigation component on behalf of GoI and claims reimbursement
n89df7e8fe6a.x: Section 90(4) says the Central Government shall execute the project and obtain environmental, forest and R&R clearances, not the AP Government.
xa: ⚠ "Which section" — answer **90**; an old key says Section **30**, some CA notes say **89** — both wrong.
Centre funds **100%** of the remaining irrigation cost from **1 April 2014**.

ncf4e8a0e8bf.s: The Polavaram Irrigation Project was declared a national project under which section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
ncf4e8a0e8bf.x: Section 90 declares Polavaram a national project, with the Union taking control of it, Telangana's consent deemed and the Centre executing it. Section 30 appears in an old wrong key, Section 89 concerns the KWDT reference, and Section 94 covers fiscal/industrial incentives and capital support.
xs: Polavaram was declared a national project under **Section 90** of the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014** — option **(3)**.
⚠ An old key says **Section 30** and some CA notes say **Section 89** — both wrong.
xa: **90(2)**: Union takes control of the project for **irrigation**.
**90(3)**: Telangana's consent **deemed to have been given**.
**90(4)**: **Central Government shall execute** it and obtain environmental, forest and R&R clearances.

n052a5c67811.s: The Left Main Canal of the Polavaram Project carries water to:
n052a5c67811.x: The Left Main Canal carries water to Visakhapatnam, while the Right Main Canal feeds the Krishna delta.
xa: **Revised Administrative Sanction** for the LMC came in **Jun 2026**.
LMC up to **Visakhapatnam** is targeted for **Mar 2027** (as of **15 Aug 2026**).

nc0f84212ae5.s: The Polavaram Ordinance, 2014 kept the submergence-area villages and mandals of which district with Andhra Pradesh?
nc0f84212ae5.x: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014 amended the territorial provision so that Khammam villages and mandals in the Polavaram submergence area remained with Andhra Pradesh.
xa: Formal name: **AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014**.
The Bill was passed by the **Lok Sabha on 11 July 2014**.
AP's area rose from **1,60,205** to **1,62,970 sq km**.

n3ce16b0c163.s: From 1 April 2014, the Centre funds 100 per cent of the remaining cost of which Polavaram component?
n3ce16b0c163.x: The Centre funds 100 per cent of the remaining irrigation-component cost; drinking-water and hydel components are not covered.
xa: Older RCE: **₹55,548 crore**; release delayed.
Expenditure by Dec 2025: **₹25,700.47 crore**; GoI advance **₹5,052.71 crore**.
CM (26 Jan 2026): ~**₹12,000 crore** pending from the Centre.

n5455c5f6d49.s: In February 2026, how much did Andhra Pradesh seek from the Centre for Polavaram Phase-II?
n5455c5f6d49.x: On 11 Feb 2026 AP sought Rs 32,000 crore for Polavaram Phase-II along with permanent lifting of the MoEF stop-work order; Rs 55,548 crore is the older RCE and Rs 3,320 crore the 2026-27 Budget allocation.
xa: Centre covers **100%** of the remaining **irrigation** cost from **1 April 2014** — not drinking water or hydel.
Budget 2026-27 storage limit: **41.15 m**.
Dec 2025: expenditure **₹25,700.47 crore**; GoI advance **₹5,052.71 crore**.

nc288b9a7570.s: Which of the following Polavaram issues remains unresolved?
o: Clearance of the revised cost estimate
Constitution of the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal
nc288b9a7570.x: The revised cost estimate of the Polavaram Project had not yet been cleared; the other items are not pending.
xa: Other criticisms: **tribal displacement** and Phase-I storage at **41.15 m** instead of **45.72 m**.
Older RCE: **₹55,548 crore**; AP seeks **₹32,000 crore** for **Phase-II**.

n5c387ef4fe5.s: The office of the CEO of the Polavaram Project Authority is located in:
n5c387ef4fe5.x: The Authority, constituted after APRA 2014 with inter-State coordination functions, has its CEO in New Delhi.
xa: **Shiv Nandan Kumar** was CEO as of **25 May 2024** (APPSC 2024 key).
**M. Raghuram** — Member-Secretary; **M. Ramesh Kumar** — Chief Engineer, **Rajamahendravaram**.
CAG (audit to **Mar 2023**) asked AP to settle submergence issues with neighbours **in consultation with PPA**.

nd53b012ddb4.s: As of 25 May 2024, who was the Chief Executive Officer of the Polavaram Project Authority?
nd53b012ddb4.x: Shiv Nandan Kumar was the PPA CEO as of 25 May 2024 (APPSC 2024 key); the CEO sits in New Delhi. M. Raghuram is Member-Secretary, M. Ramesh Kumar is Chief Engineer at Rajamahendravaram, and Sonti Venkataramamurthy named the original 'Ramapada Sagaram' proposal.
xs: **Shiv Nandan Kumar** was CEO of the PPA as of **25 May 2024** — option **(2)** (APPSC 2024 key).
**M. Raghuram** is the PPA's **Member-Secretary**; **M. Ramesh Kumar** is Chief Engineer at **Rajamahendravaram**.
**Sir Sonti Venkataramamurthy** named the original **"Ramapada Sagaram"** proposal.
xa: The PPA CEO sits in **New Delhi**.
The PPA is a **central body** routing national-project funding and mediating inter-State coordination.

n01068b09602.s: Telangana's submergence concern about Polavaram relates to backwater at:
n01068b09602.x: Telangana's concern is backwater at Bhadrachalam, while Odisha and Chhattisgarh objected over protective embankments.
xa: Odisha and Chhattisgarh submergence cases are pending in the **Supreme Court**.
CAG (audit to **Mar 2023**): settle submergence issues **in consultation with PPA** and build embankments.
Jul 2026: ~**189 villages** on alert in **Polavaram district** during **Godavari-Sabari** floods.

nbd5a03c316b.s: The tribal communities displaced by the Polavaram Project are reported to be predominantly which of the following?
nbd5a03c316b.x: The displaced population is predominantly composed of Koya and Kondh tribals.
nbd5a03c316b.tq: Identify the precise community names instead of relying on broad tribal associations.
xs: Those displaced are mostly **Koya and Kondh** tribals — option **(4)**.
Their complaints: **land-rights violation**, **low compensation**, **poor rehabilitation**.
xa: **Koya river traditions** face loss (Aug 2026).
R&R progress Aug 2026: **94% land acquisition**, **52% relocation**.
Compensation follows the **RFCTLARR Act, 2013**.

n226d8b516f3.s: For the Polavaram Project, the value of a house site in R&R colonies was increased from Rs 1 lakh to:
n226d8b516f3.x: The house-site value was doubled to Rs 2 lakh; Rs 1,943 crore was paid in three phases under the RFCTLARR Act, 2013.
xa: Aug 2026: **94% land acquisition**, **52% relocation**; R&R colonies targeted **Dec 2026**.
Complaints of **Koya and Kondh** tribals: low compensation, poor rehabilitation, land-rights violation.

n7bd583638b5.s: In December 2025, land acquisition and R&R for the Polavaram Project were only about ____ complete.
n7bd583638b5.x: LA and R&R stood at only 27.40% in December 2025, the main bottleneck; by August 2026 LA reached 94% and relocation 52%.
xa: **₹1,943 crore** compensation paid in three phases (Mar 2026).
House-site value doubled from **₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh** (**1 May 2026**).
Displaced are mostly **Koya and Kondh** tribals.
