n2cc9d94414c.s: By August 2026, the civil works of the Polavaram Project were reported to be:
n2cc9d94414c.x: By August 2026, civil works were at 90% and overall progress at 77%.
xa: Dec 2024 overall progress: **53.47%**.
Completion target: **March 2027**.

n1ed0d9c3c64.s: The Telugu Ganga project mainly supplies drinking water to which city?
n1ed0d9c3c64.x: Telugu Ganga carries Krishna surplus through the Srisailam-Somasila-Kandaleru-Poondi system to supply drinking water to Chennai and irrigate parts of Rayalaseema and Nellore.
xa: An **NTR-era** project, begun **1983** (**Sixth Plan**).
Listed in the **Eleventh Schedule** of APRA **2014** for completion with existing water sharing.
Rayalaseema's Krishna-lift projects (HNSS, GNSS, Telugu Ganga) "often run dry".

n80c0660581a.s: The intended command area of the Galeru-Nagari Sujala Sravanthi project is:
n80c0660581a.x: Galeru-Nagari (38 TMC) has an intended command area of 2.60 lakh acres covering Kadapa, Annamayya, Tirupati, Chittoor and Nellore.
xa: GNSS uses **Krishna flood waters**; **38 TMC**.
Listed in APRA 2014's **Eleventh Schedule**.
Still unfinished under **Jalayagnam** in **2025-26**.

n5a2c13b8c24.s: Which project is listed in the Eleventh Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 for completion with existing water sharing?
n5a2c13b8c24.x: The Eleventh Schedule lists Handri-Neeva, Telugu Ganga, Galeru-Nagari, Veligonda, Kalwakurthy and Nettempadu for completion with the existing water-sharing arrangements.
xa: **KRMB and GRMB** were set up under **Schedule 11** principles.
**KWDT** allocations are the basis of the **KRMB** operation protocol.

n7088d32ea42.s: Vamsadhara Project is popularly known as the ‘Lifeline of North Coastal Andhra Pradesh’. It is associated with which district?
n7088d32ea42.x: The Vamsadhara Project is associated with Srikakulam district and is described as the Lifeline of North Coastal Andhra Pradesh.
n7088d32ea42.tq: Use the title–location association to distinguish nearby irrigation projects.
xs: **Vamsadhara** is in **Srikakulam** — option **(2)**; "**Lifeline of North Coastal AP**" (APPSC 2025).
**Phase-II Stage-II** is **93.5%** done, with **20,000 acres** new ayacut.
xa: **Vamsadhara-Nagavali link** due by December (Apr 2026).
**Gandipalem** (Pillaperu, **SPSR Nellore**) was also an APPSC 2025 question.

na7da4c27cc9.s: Gandipalem Project is a medium irrigation project on which river and in which district?
na7da4c27cc9.x: Gandipalem is a medium project on the Pillaperu River in SPSR Nellore district.
na7da4c27cc9.tq: Directly test the river–district association of a less familiar project.
xs: **Gandipalem** is a medium project on the **Pillaperu River** in **SPSR Nellore** — option **(2)** (APPSC 2025).
**Pennar** hosts **Somasila**; **Vamsadhara** is in **Srikakulam**.
xa: Vamsadhara = "**Lifeline of North Coastal AP**" (APPSC 2025).
National medium class: CCA **2,000-10,000 ha**.

ncb14d215c4e.s: The Veligonda project draws Krishna water by gravity through Nallamala tunnels from which reservoir?
ncb14d215c4e.x: Veligonda takes Krishna water from Srisailam by gravity through tunnels in the Nallamala range into Nallamala Sagar.
xa: Capacity **43.50 TMC**; **4.47 lakh acres**; **30 mandals**.
Also called **Poola Subbaiah** Veligonda; foundation **5 Mar 1996**.
Phase-I: **10.70 TMC** into Nallamala Sagar, **1.19 lakh acres**, drinking water to **4 lakh** people.

n8fdc681cf6f.s: Under APFAMGS, farmers prepare crop-water budgets and voluntarily regulate:
n8fdc681cf6f.x: APFAMGS promotes farmer-led collection of rainfall and well-level data, crop-water budgeting and voluntary regulation of pumping.
xa: APFAMGS = **AP Farmer Managed Groundwater Systems**, an **FAO-supported NGO project** in drought-prone districts.
AP has ~**19 lakh** bore wells; **40,000-50,000** added yearly.

ncf078cf4f1a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about irrigation debates in Andhra Pradesh?
o: HNSS, GNSS and Telugu Ganga are Krishna-lift projects that Rayalaseema depends on
Telangana supports Andhra Pradesh's proposed Godavari links
A key criticism is the gap between irrigation potential created and utilised
These Rayalaseema lift projects often run dry
ncf078cf4f1a.x: Telangana objects to AP's Godavari links, saying they violate APRA 2014 and the 1980 GWDT award.
xa: Irrigation White Paper (**Jul 2026**): **36 projects by Dec 2028** at **Rs 35,555 crore**.
**Rs 24,611 crore** was spent in the previous two years.

n0c6e409dbef.s: The Pattiseema lift scheme lifts Godavari water into which canal to carry it to the Krishna at Prakasam Barrage?
n0c6e409dbef.x: Pattiseema lifts Godavari water into the Polavaram Right Main Canal, which carries it to the Krishna at Prakasam Barrage - the first Godavari-Krishna link.
xa: **Lift irrigation scheme** (PYQ) with **24 pumps**; commissioned **2015**.
~**450 TMC** transferred so far.
Beneficiaries: **Krishna delta** farmers (PYQ 2018, 2017).

n08a596ccf80.s: The Pattiseema lift irrigation scheme on the Godavari mainly benefits farmers of the:
n08a596ccf80.x: Pattiseema lifts Godavari water for Krishna delta farmers, as a temporary arrangement until Polavaram's gravity flow begins.
xa: Exam angle: "Pattiseema is a **lift irrigation project**" (PYQ 2018, 2017).
It is the **first Godavari-Krishna link**.
n08a596ccf80.fixed: drop meta reference 'as per the PYQ'

n33d649b8c56.s: The GWDT award of 1980 permitted diversion of how much Godavari water to the Krishna?
n33d649b8c56.x: The 1980 GWDT award permitted the Polavaram diversion of 80 TMC of Godavari water to the Krishna.
n33d649b8c56.tq: Recall the tribunal-specific diversion quantity and year.
xs: The **1980 GWDT award** permitted diversion of **80 TMC** Godavari water to the Krishna — option **(2)**.
**40 TMC** is HNSS's capacity — a distractor.
xa: **Pattiseema** was the first Godavari-Krishna link via the **Polavaram RMC**.
After Polavaram, ~**200 TMC** Godavari water is planned for **Nagarjunasagar** ayacut.

n7940340c451.s: In 2023-24, canals accounted for approximately what share of Andhra Pradesh's Gross Irrigated Area?
n7940340c451.x: Canals accounted for about 40% of GIA, wells and tube wells about 48%, tanks about 8% and other sources about 3%.
xa: ⚠ **12%** is India's "others" share of net irrigated area in **2021-22**.
Groundwater = **41%** of GIA; ~**19 lakh** bore wells.
Tanks matter on the peninsular plateau; **canals dominate the Godavari-Krishna deltas**.

n3cdb3a50ebe.s: Andhra Pradesh has approximately how many bore wells?
n3cdb3a50ebe.x: AP has about 19 lakh bore wells, and groundwater is the largest source of its Gross Irrigated Area.
xa: Groundwater irrigation: **29.12 lakh acres net**, **41.44 lakh acres gross** (2023-24).
Groundwater is **roughly 45%** of net irrigated area (derived).

neb59cd708f6.s: Which source had the largest share (47.3%) of India's net irrigated area in 2021-22?
neb59cd708f6.x: Tube wells accounted for 47.3% of India's net irrigated area in 2021-22, followed by canals at 24.7%.
xa: ⚠ India's largest = **tube wells 47.3%**; AP's GIA largest = **wells/tube wells ~48%**.
India's GIA/GCA: **55.8%**.
AP's canals: ~**40%** of GIA (2023-24).

nac4ebcd675a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about sources of irrigation in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Wells and tube wells accounted for about 48% of GIA in 2023-24
Tank irrigation is important because of undulating plateau relief and impervious rocks
Canals dominate irrigation in the Godavari-Krishna deltas
Tanks were the largest source of Gross Irrigated Area in 2023-24
nac4ebcd675a.x: Wells and tube wells were the largest source (about 48% of GIA) in 2023-24; tanks accounted for only about 8%.
xa: Tanks: **2.69 lakh ha** of GIA 2023-24.
**Neeru-Chettu** works include **desilting tank beds** and developing **tank cascades**.

n571b6d6a180.s: Which of the following is a component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)?
n571b6d6a180.x: PMKSY's components are AIBP, Har Khet Ko Pani, Watershed and Per Drop More Crop; the others are Andhra Pradesh State programmes.
xa: **M-CADWM** was approved in **2025-26** as a sub-scheme of **PMKSY-AIBP**.
**PDMC** gives **55%** to small/marginal farmers, **45%** to others.

nf654f83cbd8.s: Jawaharlal Nehru laid the foundation stone of the Nagarjuna Sagar project on:
nf654f83cbd8.x: Nehru laid the foundation stone on 10 December 1955, in the last months of the First Plan; the dam is on the Krishna.
xa: It is one of the **largest masonry dams** in the world and serves **AP and Telangana**.
It was launched in the **First Plan**; completion was prioritised in the **Fifth Plan (1974-79)**.
⚠ Nagarjuna Sagar foundation = Nehru **1955**; **Veligonda** foundation = Naidu **1996**.

nc83f792d8d1.s: Construction of the Prakasam Barrage on the Krishna at Vijayawada began in:
nc83f792d8d1.x: Construction began in February 1954 under the Prakasam ministry; the barrage replaced Cotton's Krishna anicut of the 1850s.
xa: Completed **1957**; a **First to Second Plan** project.
Pattiseema water reaches the **Krishna at Prakasam Barrage** via the Polavaram RMC.

n371ecb22a7d.s: The foundation stone of the Veligonda project was laid on:
n371ecb22a7d.x: N. Chandrababu Naidu laid the foundation stone of the Veligonda project on 5 March 1996.
xa: Veligonda = **Poola Subbaiah** project, gravity from **Srisailam** via twin **Nallamala tunnels**.
Phase-I inaugurated at **Gantavanipalli** (Markapuram district), three decades after the foundation stone.
Naidu also launched **Neeru-Meeru** (**2000**).

n346dec0e16a.s: Jalayagnam, launched during the Tenth Five Year Plan, was launched by:
n346dec0e16a.x: Jalayagnam was launched by Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy; N. Chandrababu Naidu is linked to Neeru-Meeru (2000).
xa: Aim: irrigate **1 crore acres**, stabilise **21 lakh acres**.
**52 major and medium** projects; **41 major + 25 minor** proposed.

ndf2e15d00f0.s: The Krishna River Management Board and Godavari River Management Board operate under the:
o: Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, with Schedule 11 principles
ndf2e15d00f0.x: KRMB and GRMB operate under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, following the principles in Schedule 11.
ndf2e15d00f0.tq: Apply the wrong-law trap to identify the governing statute.
xs: **KRMB and GRMB** are under the **AP Reorganisation Act 2014**, on **Schedule 11** principles — option **(2)**.
**KWDT** allocations form the basis of the KRMB operation protocol.
xa: Existing tribunal allocations unchanged; **future excess-flow allocations** bind both states.
Boards advise on **floods and droughts**, with **full authority to enforce orders**.
The **Tungabhadra Board** releases water to **HLC, LLC** and the **RDS**.

n284626d21a0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about groundwater in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The stage of groundwater development is about 30%, in the safe category
About 40,000-50,000 new bore wells are added every year
The area irrigated per well is rising
n284626d21a0.x: With 40,000-50,000 new bore wells added each year, the area irrigated per well is falling, not rising.
xa: AP has **3,005 telemetry wells**; real-time monitoring set up by the **National Hydrology Project**.
**258 over-exploited villages** proposed under APWALTA.

nbb1b3a34c31.s: The nodal department for Neeru-Chettu in Andhra Pradesh is the:
nbb1b3a34c31.x: The Water Resources Department is nodal for Neeru-Chettu, launched on 2 October 2014 as a water-conservation sub-mission.
xa: Works: **desilting** of tank beds, strengthening **tank bunds**, **check dams**, tank cascades.
**Neeru-Meeru** (**2000**) was the earlier watershed and rainwater-harvesting drive.

n17b690d9e2a.s: APWALTA, 2002 requires rainwater-harvesting structures on premises measuring at least:
n17b690d9e2a.x: APWALTA, 2002 requires rainwater-harvesting structures on residential, commercial and other premises of 200 sq m or more.
xa: Bore-well siting follows **APWALTA-2002 norms**.
**258 over-exploited villages** proposed for notification (GEC 2024-25; SES 2025-26).
**Water Protection Board** set up in **2002**.

na264ed064eb.s: Which Andhra Pradesh law seeks to check indiscriminate digging of borewells?
o: AP Water, Land and Trees Act, 2002
AP Farmer Managed Groundwater Systems Act, 2005
na264ed064eb.x: APWALTA - the AP Water, Land and Trees Act, 2002 - is AP's law against indiscriminate borewell digging (PYQ 2018) and also mandates rainwater harvesting on premises of 200 sq m or more. APFAMGS is a farmer-managed project, not an Act; the other two titles are distractors.
xs: **APWALTA** — **AP Water, Land and Trees Act, 2002** — option **(2)** (PYQ 2018).
**APFAMGS** is an **FAO-supported NGO project**, not an Act.
xa: It mandates rainwater harvesting on premises of **200 sq m** or more.
**Neeru-Meeru** (**2000**): watershed + rainwater harvesting drive.
**Neeru-Chettu** (**2 Oct 2014**): **Water Resources Department** is nodal.

n937ba83dda3.s: The Neeru-Meeru programme mainly focused on:
o: Rainwater harvesting and raising groundwater levels
n937ba83dda3.x: Neeru-Meeru was a watershed and rainwater-harvesting drive intended to raise groundwater levels.
xa: **Neeru-Chettu** followed on **2 Oct 2014**, with the **Water Resources Department** as nodal department.
**Water Protection Board** was set up in **2002**.
**APWALTA, 2002** mandates rainwater harvesting on premises of **200 sq m** or more.

n6be1eae3c01.s: Under Per Drop More Crop, assistance to small and marginal farmers for drip and sprinkler systems is:
n6be1eae3c01.x: PDMC (from 2015-16, under RKVY since 2022-23) gives 55% to small and marginal farmers and 45% to others.
xa: **102 lakh ha** covered nationally since **2015-16**.
⚠ PDMC **55%** small/marginal vs **45%** others; **APMIP 100%** for SC/ST.
PDMC is a component of **PMKSY**.

n4bdd84fbc5f.s: The Andhra Pradesh Micro Irrigation Project (APMIP) was launched in which year, and under which scheme is it now run?
n4bdd84fbc5f.x: APMIP began in 2003 and now runs as RKVY-PDMC. 2015 relates to PDMC's start nationally (and Har Khet Ko Pani is a different PMKSY component), Neeru-Meeru (2000) and Neeru-Chettu (2014) are water-conservation programmes, not micro-irrigation.
xs: **APMIP** was launched in **2003** and now runs as **RKVY-PDMC** (**RKVY-Per Drop More Crop**) — option **(1)**.
**Neeru-Meeru** (**2000**) and **Neeru-Chettu** (**2014**) are water-conservation programmes; **Har Khet Ko Pani** is a separate **PMKSY** component.
xa: Coverage: **37.90 lakh acres**, **13.49 lakh farmers**; **75% drip, 25% sprinkler**.
**PDMC** began **2015-16**; under **RKVY since 2022-23**.

n7f756db32ff.s: In Andhra Pradesh, minor irrigation covers schemes with an ayacut up to:
n7f756db32ff.x: In AP, minor irrigation means an ayacut up to 5,000 acres; nationally, minor means a CCA up to 2,000 ha.
xa: ⚠ AP minor = up to **5,000 acres**; national minor = CCA up to **2,000 ha**.
Largest source of irrigation in AP: **wells / tube wells** (~**48%** of GIA).
AP ranked **1st** nationally in **micro-irrigation** in **2024-25**.

n6df0080bcb0.s: As per 'AP Economy in Brief 2020', the ratio of Gross Irrigated Area to Gross Cropped Area (GIA/GCA) in Andhra Pradesh was about:
n6df0080bcb0.x: The PYQ (2021) figure for AP's GIA/GCA is 52%, per AP Economy in Brief 2020. A derived 2023-24 figure is about 55% and India's is 55.8%; 36% is close to AP's net-sown-area share of geographical area, and 64%/75% are not supported.
xs: AP's **GIA/GCA** was **52%** (AP Economy in Brief 2020) — option **(2)**, a **PYQ 2021** figure.
A derived 2023-24 figure is **about 55%** (cropping intensity **1.21** on **49.55 lakh ha** NSA).
xa: 2024-25 cropping intensity: **1.88**.

n14adf2d08f3.s: The ₹10,000 crore Micro Irrigation Fund, which funds Andhra Pradesh among eight States, is maintained through:
n14adf2d08f3.x: The Micro Irrigation Fund has a ₹10,000 crore corpus maintained through NABARD, and AP is among the eight States funded.
xa: **APMIP** (**2003**) now runs as **RKVY-PDMC**.
AP ranked **1st** nationally in micro-irrigation **2024-25**.

nfe53d697da6.s: The National Hydrology Project helped Andhra Pradesh establish:
nfe53d697da6.x: The National Hydrology Project set up Andhra Pradesh's real-time groundwater monitoring system.
xa: Groundwater development stage: **~30% (safe)**.
**40,000-50,000** new bore wells added yearly; area irrigated per well **falling**.

nap-geography-22-2.s: Which of the following about tanks in Andhra Pradesh is NOT correct?
o: Coastal Andhra has over 6,800 active tanks mainly for recharge
Rayalaseema's tanks support irrigation and groundwater recharge
Coastal Andhra has more than 14,000 minor tanks
Rayalaseema has more than 6,800 active tanks
nap-geography-22-2.x: The over 6,800 active tanks for irrigation and recharge belong to Rayalaseema, not Coastal Andhra, which has over 14,000 minor tanks.
n: Coastal Andhra has more than 14,000 minor tanks. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 46-48]
Coastal Andhra has the highest concentration of tanks. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 46-48]
Rayalaseema has more than 6,800 active tanks. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 46-48]
Rayalaseema tanks support irrigation. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 46-48]
Rayalaseema tanks support groundwater recharge. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 46-48]
xa: Tanks give about **8%** of AP's gross irrigated area (**2.69 lakh ha**, 2023-24).
Tank irrigation suits the peninsular plateau's **undulating relief** and **impervious rocks**.
Canals dominate the **Godavari-Krishna deltas** (~**40%** of GIA).

nd4cb1f99d4d.s: Which centres of IT exports did residual Andhra Pradesh lose after bifurcation?
o: Rushikonda IT Park and Kakinada SEZ
HITEC City and the Financial District
Tirupati electronics cluster and Sri City
nd4cb1f99d4d.x: The residual State lost Hyderabad's HITEC City and Financial District, important centres of IT and ITES exports.
xa: Pharma: **Genome Valley** and the Hyderabad belt went; AP kept only a **bulk-drug base at Vizag**.
**MSMEs**: thousands of ancillary units ended up across the border, **breaking supply chains**.
Offsetting advantage: coastline and ports → **port-led, EXIM** strategy.

nb4ffced7be1.s: After bifurcation, residual Andhra Pradesh kept only a bulk-drug base at:
nb4ffced7be1.x: Genome Valley and the Hyderabad pharma belt went with Telangana; AP kept only a bulk-drug base at Visakhapatnam.
xa: IT/ITeS: AP lost **HITEC City** and the **Financial District**.
Corporate and bank regional HQs stayed in Hyderabad — **no commercial nerve centre**.

n4bb98692dd5.s: Just after bifurcation, manufacturing accounted for around what share of residual Andhra Pradesh's GSDP?
n4bb98692dd5.x: Manufacturing was about 10.5 percent of GSDP (not the whole industry sector), and the State was about 60 percent agriculture-dependent.
xa: 2025-26 GVA: services **43%**, agriculture **33%**, industry **24%**; manufacturing **10.84%**.
AP got **58%** of population but only **46%** of revenue.

ne83f4916c53.s: After remeasurement, the coastline of Andhra Pradesh is reported as about:
ne83f4916c53.x: The older figure was 974 km; remeasurement gave 1,053 km, supporting the State's port-led EXIM strategy.
xa: AP lost **HITEC City** and **Genome Valley** to Telangana.
2025-26 GVA: industry **24%**, manufacturing **10.84%**.

na2b52973599.s: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 made Amaravati the sole capital by inserting:
na2b52973599.x: The 2026 Amendment inserted Section 5(3) making Amaravati the sole capital; Section 5 had made Hyderabad the common capital till 2024.
xa: State Cabinet resolution: **27 Mar 2026**.
Government moved to **Velagapudi (Amaravati)**.

nefa53873040.s: The backward-area programmes under Section 94 of the AP Reorganisation Act cover how many districts of residual AP?
nefa53873040.x: They cover seven districts (4 Rayalaseema + 3 North Coastal); new units there get 15% additional depreciation and 15% investment allowance.
xa: SCS was refused citing the **14th Finance Commission**; the Centre offered the **Special Assistance Measure** instead.
⚠ Schedule **IX = 91** companies; Schedule **X = 142** institutions.

nd90e07dcca5.s: Why did the retention of corporate and bank regional headquarters in Hyderabad create a difficulty for residual Andhra Pradesh?
o: It deprived the State of all banking services
It prevented the formation of any district administration
It left the State without a commercial nerve centre
It transferred all ports to Telangana
nd90e07dcca5.x: Corporate and bank regional headquarters stayed in Hyderabad, leaving residual Andhra Pradesh without a commercial nerve centre.
nd90e07dcca5.tq: Infer the institutional consequence from the location of headquarters.
xs: With corporate and bank regional HQs in Hyderabad, AP had **no commercial nerve centre** — option **(3)**.
AP kept its **ports** — its coastline drives a **port-led, EXIM** strategy.
xa: **Investment chill** after 2014: capital uncertainty, no ready administrative set-up, agitations.
Government moved from Hyderabad to **Velagapudi (Amaravati)**; APSWAN HQ moved in **2017**.

n39232f8809e.s: The investment chill in Andhra Pradesh after 2014 arose mainly from:
o: Capital uncertainty and no ready administrative set-up
n39232f8809e.x: The chill came from capital uncertainty, no ready administrative set-up and agitations, not from any lack of coastline.
xa: Coastline: **974 km** (old), **1,053 km** (remeasured) → **port-led, EXIM** strategy.
The **2026** Amendment Act (Amaravati sole capital) ends the **2019-24** three-capitals uncertainty.

n87f1cd505da.s: After bifurcation, residual Andhra Pradesh got about 58% of the population and debt but only about ____ of the revenue.
n87f1cd505da.x: AP received about 58% of the population and debt but only around 46% of the revenue, reflecting the loss of Hyderabad's revenue base.
xa: Hyderabad's revenue base stayed with Telangana: **HITEC City**, **Genome Valley**.
SCS refused citing the **14th Finance Commission**; **Special Assistance Measure** of **₹24,350 crore** offered.

n846804840f7.s: Which one of the following sources does NOT form part of the installed power capacity mix of Andhra Pradesh?
n846804840f7.x: Andhra Pradesh has no nuclear component in its installed capacity. Its capacity mix includes thermal, hydel, gas and renewable sources.
n846804840f7.tq: Find the excluded source by identifying the one that does not belong to the stated mix.
xs: AP has **no nuclear power** in its installed capacity — option **(4)** (APPSC 2023).
Its mix is **thermal, hydel, gas and renewables**.
xa: **Kovvada, Srikakulam** is only **proposed**; no operating plant.
Dec 2025: APGENCO thermal **4,210 MW**, APPDCL thermal **2,400 MW**, APGENCO hydel **1,773.60 MW**.

nb45db9acbd2.s: How many hours of free daytime power do Andhra Pradesh's 22.36 lakh farm pump sets receive?
nb45db9acbd2.x: 22.36 lakh farm pump sets receive nine hours of free daytime power; aqua power is priced at Rs 1.50 per unit.
xa: Peak demand: **15,016 MW** (**21 May 2026**); transmission losses **2.6%**.
State demand: **59,166.70 MU** (Apr-Dec 2025).

n2c5d0902acc.s: Which renewable-energy source has the largest installed capacity in Andhra Pradesh according to the APSES 2025–26 figures?
n2c5d0902acc.x: Solar is the largest renewable-energy source in Andhra Pradesh, with an installed capacity of 5,614.52 MW.
n2c5d0902acc.tq: Compare the source-wise table and identify the maximum value.
xs: **Solar** is AP's largest RE source — option **(3)**, with **5,614.52 MW** (Dec 2025).
**Wind** is next at **4,397.67 MW**; small hydro (**106.80**) and bagasse co-gen (**206.95 MW**) are far smaller.
xa: State RE total: **10,639.75 MW**.
Bagasse, biomass, small hydro and waste together: **627.56 MW**.
**Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park** is AP's solar landmark.

n9b48f9cff43.s: The installed power capacity of Andhra Pradesh as of March 2022 was about:
n9b48f9cff43.x: The PYQ key gives 25,726.89 MW (about 25.7 GW) as of March 2022. 27,392 MW is the 30 Nov 2024 figure, 21,297.03 MW is the Dec 2025 installed/contracted figure on a different basis, and 33,240 MW is AP's pumped-storage potential.
n9b48f9cff43.tq: Match figure to year: Mar 2022 = 25,726.89 MW.
xs: **27,392 MW** = **30 Nov 2024**; **21,297.03 MW** = Dec 2025 installed/contracted; **33,240 MW** = **PSP potential**.
xa: ⚠ Match the figure to the question's year and basis.
Peak demand **15,016 MW** (21 May 2026); **15,680 MW** expansion programme.
n9b48f9cff43.fixed: stem oddly refers to 'PYQ answer key'; fact unchanged

n83e7585ee78.s: What is the correct expansion of APEPDCL?
o: Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited
Andhra Pradesh Energy Power Development Company Limited
Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Corporation Limited
Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Development Corporation Limited
n83e7585ee78.x: APEPDCL stands for Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited.
n83e7585ee78.tq: Test the exact official expansion and distinguish Company from Corporation.
xs: APEPDCL = **AP Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited** — option **(1)**.
"**Corporation**" is used in the PYQ key for **APCPDCL**, not APEPDCL.
xa: APSPDCL = AP **Southern** Power Distribution **Company** Ltd (Tirupati).
⚠ PYQ key says "Corporation" for APCPDCL; some notes say "Company".

n72923266c96.s: The present Vijayawada-based APCPDCL was carved out of APSPDCL in:
n72923266c96.x: The new APCPDCL was carved out of APSPDCL in 2020; the pre-2014 APCPDCL was headquartered at Hyderabad.
xa: APCPDCL now covers **Krishna, Guntur, Prakasam**.
The four DISCOMs date from the **2000** unbundling.

ndccfcf8c89b.s: Which one of the following is associated with solar power generation in Andhra Pradesh?
ndccfcf8c89b.x: The Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park is identified with solar power generation in Andhra Pradesh.
ndccfcf8c89b.tq: Separate the solar project from the pumped-storage projects listed separately.
xs: **Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park** is AP's solar landmark — option **(3)**.
**Gadikota** (**1,200 MW**) and **Upper Sileru** (**1,350 MW**) are **pumped storage projects**; Kamalapadu is also a PSP (**950 MW**).
xa: **Tata Power hybrid**: **800 MW** — Pathikonda solar + Kanekallu wind.
Solar is AP's largest RE source: **5,614.52 MW**.

n63deeef6c2e.s: Andhra Pradesh's identified pumped storage potential is approximately:
n63deeef6c2e.x: AP's pumped-storage potential is 29 sites totalling 33,240 MW, of which APGENCO has six approved PSPs (1,320 + 1,200 + 1,000 + 950 + 800 + 750 = about 6,020 MW). 15,680 MW is the generation expansion programme and 160 GW is the clean-energy policy target.
xs: AP's PSP potential: **29 sites, 33,240 MW** — option **(3)**.
APGENCO has **six** approved PSPs; **15,680 MW** is the generation expansion programme; **160 GW** is the clean-energy target.
xa: Approved PSPs: **Aravetipalli 1,320**, **Gadikota 1,200**, **Yaganti 1,000**, **Kamalapadu 950**, **Rajupalem 800**, **Deenepalli 750**.
**APGENCO-NHPC JV** (Sep 2024): five PSPs incl. **Upper Sileru 1,350 MW**.

ndd50f848e9b.s: The Upper Sileru Pumped Storage Project of 1,350 MW is being taken up by:
ndd50f848e9b.x: The APGENCO-NHPC JV (Sep 2024) covers five PSPs including Upper Sileru PSP of 1,350 MW. Tata Power is behind the Pathikonda-Kanekallu hybrid project, APGIC is an oil and gas company, and NTPC Green is not mentioned.
xs: **Upper Sileru PSP (1,350 MW)** is under the **APGENCO-NHPC joint venture** — option **(2)** (Sep 2024).
The JV covers **five PSPs**.
**Tata Power** runs the Pathikonda-Kanekallu hybrid; **APGIC** (APIIC + APGENCO) is in **KG** exploration.
xa: ⚠ Upper Sileru **1,350** vs largest APGENCO approved PSP **Aravetipalli 1,320**.
PSP potential: **29** sites, **33,240 MW**.

n0005ddd0636.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated feature of the Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024?
o: Target of more than 160 GW of clean energy
n0005ddd0636.x: The policy targets Net Zero by 2047, not by 2030. Its other stated features include over 160 GW of clean energy, ₹10 lakh crore investment and 7.5 lakh jobs.
n0005ddd0636.tq: Reject the altered year in a policy target.

nadaae376b18.s: The Andhra Pradesh Maritime Policy 2024–29 aims to make the State India's leading:

nf44d31ac434.s: South Coast Railway, India's 18th railway zone, is headquartered at:

n8f014fa5d72.s: The creation of South Coast Railway was promised in which Schedule of the A.P. Reorganisation Act, 2014?

**VCIC** is part of **ECEC**, ADB-funded.

n524649ffee8.s: The Raipur–Visakhapatnam greenfield expressway is associated with which programme?

nd50b3641e78.x: Bhogapuram airport became operational on 1 August 2026; 1 June 2026 is when the SCoR zone became operational.

Port limits cut under the **Indian Ports Act, 2025**.

n281fbc1af33.x: The Act provided for examining a major port at Duggirajupatnam, a new railway zone and upgrades to the Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati airports.
xa: The railway zone became **SCoR** — India's **18th zone**, HQ **Visakhapatnam**, promised in the **13th Schedule**.
**Bhogapuram airport** became operational on **1 Aug 2026**.

ne8fd076c840.s: Which scheme, introduced in 2021, replaced UDAY in power distribution reform?

n7a199f45a0d.s: The equity of APGIC is held by APIIC and APGENCO in the ratio:

**Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration**, Amaravati, **19 July 2025** — nodal agency **SRM University**.

APIIC has **25 JVs** (SES 2025-26).

n25024313e17.s: The wholly State-owned APIIC mainly focuses on:

n9852c66aeb8.s: APIIC can allot up to how many acres of land without Cabinet approval?

APIIC footprint: **635 clusters**; land bank **41,998 acres**; **25 JVs**.
APIIC is **wholly state-owned** — parks, estates, SEZs, EMCs.

n72afe8cad81.s: The Kakinada-Konaseema region is known as Andhra Pradesh's:
n72afe8cad81.x: The Kakinada-Konaseema region is AP's oil and gas hub, associated with the KG basin.

The **Rayalaseema** industrial hub has **Kia, JSW, Royal Enfield**.

n7abfe782c2e.s: The AP Tourism Policy 2024-29 is aligned with which vision?
n7abfe782c2e.x: The policy is aligned with Swarna Andhra @2047, not Viksit Bharat @2047.
xa: Tourism + hospitality get **industry status across all segments**.
Targets: tourism > **20%** of state GVA and **20%** of the workforce.
**Swarna Andhra Tourism Vision 2047** was unveiled at the **FAITH** conclave.

n0af79ec2910.s: Under the AP Tourism Policy 2024-29, tourism and hospitality have been accorded:
o: Industry status only for Mega projects
Industry status only for heritage hotels
n0af79ec2910.x: Tourism and hospitality got industry status across all segments, with fiscal, recurring, special and non-fiscal incentives and tailor-made packages for Mega and Ultra Mega projects.

**Investment Facilitation Cell at Vijayawada**.

ndd82659ea27.s: The AP Tourism Policy 2024-29 aims to place Andhra Pradesh among India's top ____ tourist destinations.
ndd82659ea27.x: The policy targets a top-three rank, with tourism above 20% of State GVA and 20% of the workforce.
xa: "**Best Tourism Promotion State**" at **GTM 2026**.

n08ff454b3c0.s: Budget hotels were promoted in Andhra Pradesh mainly with which objective?

To provide accommodation exclusively to government employees
n08ff454b3c0.x: Budget hotels were promoted mainly to attract tourists by expanding affordable accommodation facilities.

Private hotels: **Oberoi** at Peruru (Tirupati), Gandikota, Annavaram; **Hyatt** at Tirupati.
**IITTM Nellore** trains hospitality staff.

nde6540a6803.s: Andhra Pradesh is described as the birthplace of which form of Buddhism?
nde6540a6803.x: AP is described as the birthplace of Mahayana Buddhism and has about 40 Buddhist monuments.

**Simhachalam, Annavaram** are PRASHAD; **Gandikota** is SASCI; **Borra Caves** is SD 2.0.
xa: CBDD = **Challenge Based Destination Development**.
**Salihundam** and **Ghantasala** are **Buddhist** sites.

Beach-shack policy modelled on **Goa's**.

n83a59b68021.s: Swarna Andhra Tourism Vision 2047 was unveiled at the:

n349b07e237b.s: The Union Budget 2026–27 proposed how many regional medical hubs for medical tourism?

n338d00da633.s: AP State FiberNet Ltd (APSFL), incorporated in October 2015, was launched on:

n628d7844428.s: In Andhra Pradesh, BharatNet Phase-II, implemented by APSFL, covers how many Gram Panchayats?

ndf308beb1bf.s: Which Andhra Pradesh initiative seeks to interconnect all e-governance systems through a whole-of-government approach?

n478b6b8e7da.s: The Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) of Andhra Pradesh has functioned since:

n98cf911e574.s: Mana Mitra (WhatsApp Governance) of Andhra Pradesh was launched on:

xa: WhatsApp number: **9552300009**.
**865 services** per SES 2025-26; **921 services** shown to **Bill Gates**; target **1,000**.

nf7d6e7f9fcb.s: Amaravati Quantum Valley, described as India's first Quantum Valley, functions under the:

nb8ffd5d5be3.s: The custodian ministry of the Information Technology Act, 2000 is the:

⚠ IT Act **2000** amended **2008**; AP e-Service Rules **2011**.
**AP Cyber Security Policy** came in **2017**.

n35878bf5f13.s: Which RTGS tool of Andhra Pradesh provides disaster early warning?

nd8f17f27661.s: AP Technology Services Ltd (APTS), the nodal agency for IT procurement and cyber security, was set up in:

n8aa17636219.s: Andhra Pradesh's IT & GCC Policy 4.0 covers which period?

nf09bce18c90.s: APCNF targets coverage of how many farmers by 2028–29?

nb46d5e37e55.s: Which one of the following correctly states the action-plan coverage under the National Mission on Natural Farming?

**14.43 lakh** farmers certified (Aug 2026).

n9d178d81bab.s: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) promotes organic farming in clusters certified under:

neccf06d02cd.s: The ex-gratia assistance provided to the family of a deceased fisherman in Andhra Pradesh is:

**KCC** for fishers since **2018-19**.

nf7e5981d286.s: Among the following Kharif crops, the highest MSP for 2026–27 was fixed for:

xa: Swarna Andhra strategy expands area under **sunflower, sesamum and millets**.
**Groundnut** is the main crop of **Anantapuramu**.

na960f50fbe9.s: In 2024-25, paddy accounted for approximately what share of the food-grain area of Andhra Pradesh?
na960f50fbe9.x: Paddy covered 20.97 lakh hectares out of the 37.51 lakh hectares under food grains, which is approximately 56%.

xs: Paddy covered **20.97 lakh ha** of **37.51 lakh ha** food-grain area = about **56%** — option **(3)**.

xa: Derived yield ≈ **6.1 t/ha**.
Paddy has the **largest area of any crop** in AP (**PYQ 2018**).

nafbd8012f76.s: By how much did the food-grain area of Andhra Pradesh increase in 2024-25?
nafbd8012f76.x: The food-grain area rose by 12.85% in 2024-25, following an 11.7% rainfall surplus; 16.5% was the previous year's rainfall deficit.
xa: Food-grain area went **33.24 → 37.51 lakh ha**.

n46f3663d779.s: Which crop occupies the largest area among all crops in Andhra Pradesh?
n46f3663d779.x: Paddy has the largest area of any crop in AP (PYQ 2018): 20.97 lakh ha in 2024-25, about 56% of the food-grain area. Groundnut, cotton and maize are important but cover far less.
n46f3663d779.tq: Paddy = largest area; cotton = fastest-expanding commercial crop.
xs: **Paddy** has the **largest area of any crop** in AP — option **(4)** (**PYQ 2018**).
In **2024-25** it covered **20.97 lakh ha**, about **56%** of the food-grain area.
xa: **Cotton** ("white gold") is the commercial crop that expanded most (**PYQ 2022**).
Criticism: paddy's dominance displaces indigenous crops and is a major **methane** source.

nffbe620bb54.s: Which commercial crop, called 'white gold', has expanded most in area in Andhra Pradesh in recent years?
nffbe620bb54.x: Cotton ('white gold') is the commercial crop whose area expanded most (PYQ 2022). Tobacco, sugarcane and chillies are commercial crops but are not identified as the fastest-expanding.
nffbe620bb54.tq: White gold = cotton (Palasa cashew is also nicknamed so; don't mix).
xs: **Cotton** ("**white gold**") expanded most among commercial crops — option **(1)** (**PYQ 2022**).
**Tobacco** (FCV) is concentrated in **Prakasam** and **Nellore**; **chillies** in **Guntur**.
xa: Cotton is grown in the **Krishna zone** (Krishna, Guntur, Prakasam) with paddy and chillies.
⚠ **Palasa** is the cashew "**White Gold City**" — do not confuse with cotton.

nfc975a51340.s: In December 2019, Kakinada farmers were advised to stop growing Bondalu paddy because its earlier buyer State began growing it. Which State?
nfc975a51340.x: Kerala, the earlier buyer of Bondalu rice from AP, had started producing it itself.

Paddy land in the delta is shifting to **aquaculture**.

n45decdd2f67.s: Which region is Andhra Pradesh's main rice-growing area and aquaculture hub?
n45decdd2f67.x: The Godavari delta, covering East and West Godavari, is the main rice-growing area and an aquaculture hub.
xa: Delta paddy land is being converted to aquaculture.
**India's first Mega Aqua Food Park**: **Godavari Mega Aqua Food Park, Tundurru** (West Godavari).

naa1a35601cc.s: The cropping pattern of Andhra Pradesh is currently shifting mainly towards:
naa1a35601cc.x: The shift is towards fruits, vegetables, flowers and spices because of their profitability and export potential.
xa: Horticulture is the fastest-growing farm segment (about **10%** a year).
AP is **India's largest fruit producer** (**15.6%** of national fruit output).

nc68f754189e.s: The first separate agriculture budget in undivided Andhra Pradesh was presented in:
nc68f754189e.x: Undivided Andhra Pradesh first presented a separate agriculture budget in 2013.

xs: The **first separate agri budget** was in undivided AP in **2013** — option **(3)**.

xa: **2026-27** budget: **~₹53,753 crore**, by **K. Atchannaidu** (third time).
**₹500 crore** Price Stabilisation Fund in it.

n74bdbecc72d.s: e-Crop booking at Rythu Seva Kendras is a:

**10,778** RBKs were set up; rationalised to **8,489** functional RSKs.

n5f6add82473.s: What is Andhra Pradesh's rank in coffee production in India?
n5f6add82473.x: Andhra Pradesh ranks fourth in coffee production, and 100% of its coffee comes from Araku Valley.

AP is **1st in productivity** of **oil palm, papaya, lime, cocoa, tomato, coconut** (2025-26).
AP is **India's largest fruit producer** (**15.6%** of national output).

n8ecfb7f5e8a.s: The ICAR Indian Institute of Oil Palm Research is located at

n8ecfb7f5e8a.x: The ICAR Indian Institute of Oil Palm Research is located at Pedavegi in the West Godavari region.

xs: ICAR **IIOPR** is at **Pedavegi** (West Godavari region) — option **(1)**.

Oil palm main producers: **East Godavari** + **Kakinada**.

nc89011923d9.s: In 2023-24, milk production in Andhra Pradesh declined by:

n4c0e45b9a7e.s: Milk production in Andhra Pradesh was sustained comparatively because of:

ndf8a8a8e97c.s: India produced 239.30 MT of milk in 2023-24, with per capita availability of:

n899b8567f5c.s: The 20th Livestock Census was conducted in:

AP Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019; 3 years
n01d874b7afd.x: CCRCs are issued under the AP Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019 and are valid for 11 months. The new AP Tenancy Act, 2024 is only planned; 5-year and 3-year validities are wrong.

**Annadata Sukhibhava** covers **tenant farmers** holding CCRCs.

n1ebbd5667f1.s: Farm ponds under Panta Sanjeevani were dug through convergence with:

na5870771d83.s: The Indo-Israel Centre of Excellence for vegetables in Andhra Pradesh is located at:

n209a7326bbc.s: Which allied-sector output of Andhra Pradesh retained the first national rank in each of the years 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25?

n26b1dd577ad.s: Which of the following correctly represents the premium-sharing ratio under Pasu Bhima Padhakam for BPL, SC and ST beneficiaries?

nc6af3d579f2.s: The implementation period and outlay of PM-MKSSY are:

n02e524c1313.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the 11 crops targeted for productivity improvement under the 17 growth engines of Swarna Andhra @2047?

nbcd8644fc92.s: The agricultural and allied-sector strategy under APSES 2024-25 targets what growth over five years?

n9e12cf8a263.s: Andhra Pradesh, with horticulture GVA of Rs 1,52,950 crore, ranked third in India after:

**Mega:** FCI **₹1,001-5,000 crore** or **2,000+** direct jobs.

nff63f31a26c.s: The PLI top-up under Industrial Development Policy (4.0) is:
o: 10% of the Government of India PLI incentive, capped at 5% of FCI
5% of the Government of India PLI incentive, capped at 10% of FCI
15% of export turnover, capped at 5% of FCI
nff63f31a26c.x: The PLI top-up is 10% of the Government of India incentive and is capped at 5% of FCI.
nff63f31a26c.tq: Keep the subsidy base separate from its maximum cap.
xs: The **PLI top-up** = **10% of the GoI PLI incentive**, **capped at 5% of FCI** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (3) swaps the two percentages; option (1) wrongly drops the ceiling.
xa: **Early Bird**: **40%** subsidy for PLI-sector projects with CFE within **24 months**.
**De-carbonisation subsidy** up to **6%** of FCI.
**Local procurement subsidy**: **1% of export turnover** for **3** years.

n67e0dedc5e8.s: What mechanism was added in IDP 4.0 to ensure timely payment of promised subsidies?
n67e0dedc5e8.x: IDP 4.0 introduced an Escrow Guarantee mechanism for timely payment of promised subsidies.
n67e0dedc5e8.tq: Identify the exact institutional mechanism rather than a similarly named financial facility.
xs: IDP 4.0 added an **"Escrow Guarantee" mechanism** so promised subsidies are paid on time — option **(3)** is correct.
It addresses **MSME incentive arrears**.
The **Investment Tracker** tracks large projects; **CGTMSE** is the credit guarantee under the MSME corpus.
xa: Delayed incentive payments are a long-standing MSME grievance.
**ReSTART (May 2020)** mainly cleared pending incentive arrears (about **₹1,110 crore**).
IDP 4.0 also set up a **Dedicated Investment Facilitation Cell** with liaison officers.

n5e5f1c46ed3.s: AP's Electronics Manufacturing Policy (4.0) 2024-29 focuses on electronics clusters at Kopparthy, Tirupati and:
n5e5f1c46ed3.x: The electronics policies focus on ESDM and electronics manufacturing clusters at Kopparthy, Tirupati and Sri City.
xa: Electronics Manufacturing Policy (4.0) = **G.O.70** (notified **26 Oct 2024**).
**Semiconductors and electronics** are a **Propelling** sector.
**Nellore** and **Anantapur** are listed for electronics.

ne652b282653.s: MSMEs account for about what share of India's exports?
ne652b282653.x: The cited national figures for MSMEs are about 30% of GDP, 46% of exports and 28 crore jobs.
xa: **6.63 crore** Udyam + Udyam Assist registrations (Jul 2020 - Jul 2025).
Of these, **2.72 crore** are informal micro units.
⚠ AP MSMEs = **23.5%** of GSDP (not 33.5%).

n7bda648ba3a.s: How many clusters does the approved AP Cluster Development Programme for 2026-30 cover?
n7bda648ba3a.x: The AP CDP has a ₹200 crore outlay, covers 45 clusters with Common Facility Centres and funds up to 80% of project cost.
xa: Ordered by **G.O. Ms. No. 17** (**10 Jan 2026**).
At least **2** CFCs per district.

n37f6ef98642.s: APEDB opened APEX Korea, the State's first overseas investment facilitation centre, at:
n37f6ef98642.x: APEDB opened APEX Korea at Busan as the State's first overseas investment facilitation centre.
xa: APEDB statute: **AP Economic Development Board Act, 2018** (APPSC 2023).
It does investor outreach with the **Industries Department**, incl. a delegation to the **USA**.
IDP 4.0 also has **country-specific desks** for foreign investors.

n575b33495ef.s: Under Industrial Development Policy 4.0, the dedicated Investment Facilitation Cell is intended primarily to provide:
o: Handholding, approval tracking and resolution of delays
Land acquisition through compulsory purchase alone
n575b33495ef.x: The Investment Facilitation Cell provides investor handholding, tracks approvals and helps resolve delays.
n575b33495ef.tq: Match the facilitation cell with its investor-support functions.
xs: The **Dedicated Investment Facilitation Cell** gives **handholding, approval tracking and resolution of delays** — option **(1)** is correct.
It works through **liaison officers**.
xa: It has **country-specific desks** for foreign investors.
Large projects are tracked on the **"Investment Tracker"**.
**Tourism Policy 2024-29** has its own cell at **Vijayawada**.

ndf0d36fa26e.s: Which of the following strategic sectors are being targeted by Andhra Pradesh for directing FDI?
o: AI infrastructure, critical minerals, semiconductors, energy transition and advanced technologies
Only conventional textiles, leather and tourism
Agriculture subsidies, public distribution and municipal services
Only coal mining and petroleum refining
ndf0d36fa26e.x: The strategic FDI push covers AI infrastructure, critical minerals, semiconductors, energy transition and advanced technologies.
ndf0d36fa26e.tq: Prefer the comprehensive sectoral grouping over options narrowed by ‘only’.
xs: AP is steering FDI into **AI infrastructure, critical minerals, semiconductors, energy transition and advanced technologies** — option **(1)** is correct (7 Sep 2026).
These sectors = about **45%** of greenfield projects worldwide.
xa: The push came ahead of the **Visakhapatnam CII Partnership Summit**.
Google's **1 GW AI data centre** (**US$15 bn**) at Visakhapatnam-Anakapalli.
Critical minerals: **lithium and gallium** traces at **Tummalapalle**.

nf03a4c54a2c.s: Rayalaseema is being developed as a hub for which combination of sectors?
o: Maritime administration, education, health and mining
nf03a4c54a2c.x: Rayalaseema is being developed into an automobile, steel, defence and space hub.
nf03a4c54a2c.tq: Recall the complete sectoral combination and avoid replacing one sector with a neighbouring economic activity.
xs: Rayalaseema is being built into an **auto, steel, defence and space** hub (Jul 2026) — option **(2)** is correct.
The other combinations are not stated for Rayalaseema.
xa: Steel: **JSW Steel** **2 MTPA** at **Kadapa**.
Auto: **Kia India** in **Sri Sathya Sai** district.
Defence: DRDO **AMCA** centre, **Bharat Forge**, **HFCL**.

n7f39555a7dc.s: The Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, dedicated to the nation on 1 August 1992, was built with technical collaboration from:
n7f39555a7dc.x: The Visakhapatnam Steel Plant is a shore-based integrated steel plant built with Soviet (USSR) technical collaboration.
xa: Operator: **Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL)**.
Visakhapatnam's other central PSUs: **HPCL Visakh Refinery**, **Hindustan Shipyard Ltd**, **NTPC Simhadri**.
**JSW Steel** plans a **2 MTPA** plant at **Kadapa**.

n0f6e6a07058.s: Under IDP (4.0), an Ultra Mega unit is one with investment above:
n0f6e6a07058.x: Ultra Mega units involve investment above Rs 5,000 crore and get a tailor-made package; the standard period is four years.
xa: **Large**: standard period **3 years from CFE**; paid over **7** instalments.
Mega can also qualify by **2,000+** direct jobs.
Mega/ultra-mega packages are decided **case by case**.

n730290a8c2e.s: A project involving investment of ₹2,000 crore or generating 2,000 or more direct jobs is classified as:
n730290a8c2e.x: A mega project involves ₹1,001–5,000 crore investment or 2,000 or more direct jobs.
n730290a8c2e.tq: Apply the alternative investment-or-employment test for project classification.
xs: A project of **₹1,001-5,000 crore** or **2,000+ direct jobs** is **Mega** — option **(3)** is correct.
₹2,000 crore is above Large's **₹501-1,000 crore** and below Ultra-Mega's **₹5,001 crore**.
xa: Mega gets up to **15%**, a **tailor-made** package.
Packages decided **case by case**.
Final decisions on mega projects: **SIPB**, chaired by the **CM**.

n839c11d45bb.s: Which of the following combination correctly identifies the schemes mentioned as supporting women entrepreneurs nationally?
o: VCIC loan and RAMP export meet
n839c11d45bb.x: Stand Up India and MUDRA (Tarun) are the schemes mentioned as supporting women entrepreneurs.
n839c11d45bb.tq: Start with the sure pair linking the beneficiary group to the relevant schemes.
xs: National support: **Stand Up India** + **MUDRA (Tarun)** — option **(1)** is correct.
**ReSTART** is AP's COVID relief; **PARIVESH 3.0** is environmental clearance; **E-Samudra** is maritime administration; **RAMP** is a World Bank MSME scheme.
xa: Women own only **20.37%** of MSMEs.
Women face **credit and collateral gaps**.
AP: **+5%** capital subsidy for women and other groups.

ndb41ec7e9bc.s: A local procurement subsidy under Industrial Development Policy (4.0) is linked to:
o: 1% of export turnover for three years
10% of export turnover for two years
5% of domestic turnover for three years
ndb41ec7e9bc.x: The local procurement subsidy is 1% of export turnover for three years.
ndb41ec7e9bc.tq: Match the subsidy percentage with its correct base and period.
xs: Local procurement subsidy = **1% of export turnover for 3 years** — option **(2)** is correct.
Not linked to FCI or domestic turnover.
xa: **PLI top-up** = **10%** of GoI PLI incentive (cap **5% of FCI**).
**De-carbonisation subsidy** up to **6%** of FCI.
**Revival support** for sick units is also standard.

nc5bb6dc8da7.s: The Employment Creation Subsidy for units with more than five employees is up to what share of FCI?
nc5bb6dc8da7.x: The subsidy is up to 10% of FCI for units with more than five employees (8–9% for five or fewer), paid over five years.
xa: **Local hiring**: **75%** reserved for locals under the **2019 Act**.
**Fixed power cost** reimbursed at **₹1 per unit for 2 years** from DCP.
**SGST**: **100% of net SGST for 5 years**.

n2d66db2f64e.s: Under IDP (4.0), eligible units get reimbursement of what share of net SGST for five years from commercial production?
n2d66db2f64e.x: IDP (4.0) reimburses 100% of net SGST for five years on final products made, sold and registered in AP.
xa: Some notes give a sliding scale **100% / 50% / 25%** for micro / small / medium-large; flat 100% is followed.
Under **IDP 2020-23**, SGST reimbursement was tied to **employment creation**, for **5 years** (APPSC 2023).
Stamp duty: **100% stamp and transfer duty** reimbursement.

n5bfdd84210b.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 2020-23, SGST reimbursement for medium, large and mega units was linked to which condition?
n5bfdd84210b.x: For medium, large and mega units, SGST reimbursement was tied to employment creation for five years.
n5bfdd84210b.tq: Link the incentive to its qualifying performance condition rather than its duration.
xs: Under **IDP 2020-23**, SGST reimbursement for medium, large, mega units was tied to **employment creation**, for **5 years** — option **(4)** is correct (APPSC 2023).
Land area, patents and export turnover are not the stated condition.
xa: IDP 2020-23 reserved **16.2%** of APIIC plots for **SC** entrepreneurs.
Its **micro-unit definition** was also tested in APPSC 2023.
IDP 4.0 now gives **100% of net SGST for 5 years** from commercial production.

n1996ca32f1c.s: What percentage of plots in APIIC parks was reserved for SC entrepreneurs under IDP 2020-23?
n1996ca32f1c.x: IDP 2020-23 reserved 16.2% of plots in APIIC parks for SC entrepreneurs.
n1996ca32f1c.tq: Use the exact percentage and reject rounded figures.
xs: **16.2%** of plots in APIIC parks were reserved for **SC** entrepreneurs under **IDP 2020-23** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2023).
12.5%, 15.0% and 20.0% are distractors.
xa: APIIC was set up on **26 Sept 1973**; land bank **41,998 acres**.
APIIC parks: **25%** rebate on land cost, up to **₹20 lakh** per enterprise.
APIIC can allot up to **50 acres** directly, without Cabinet approval (Jun 2026).

nc3f9ccd7de7.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's 2019 Act on local employment in industries, what share of jobs is reserved for locals?
nc3f9ccd7de7.x: The 2019 Act reserves 75% of jobs in industrial units for local candidates. 25%, 50% and 100% are not the figure in the Act.
xs: The **2019 Act** reserves **75%** of jobs for locals — option **(3)** is correct.
25%, 50% and 100% are distractors.
xa: The Act was challenged in the **High Court**.
**Employment Creation Subsidy**: up to **10% of FCI** (more than 5 employees), **8-9%** (5 or fewer).
IDP 4.0 targets **5 lakh** first-time manufacturing jobs.

n553cf28eaf4.s: Pavala vaddi enables a unit to pay interest effectively at which rate per ₹100 per month?
n553cf28eaf4.x: Under pavala vaddi, the State reimburses interest above 3% a year, so the unit effectively pays a quarter rupee, or 25 paise, per ₹100 per month.
n553cf28eaf4.tq: Convert the named fraction into its numerical amount.
xs: **Pavala vaddi**: the State reimburses interest above **3%** a year, so the unit pays **"a quarter rupee"** — i.e. **twenty-five paise** per ₹100 a month — option **(3)** is correct.
3% a year ÷ 12 months = a quarter rupee per ₹100 a month.
xa: **APSEZ units** get a **3%** interest subsidy on term loans.
**MSME Policy 4.0**: collateral-free loans + **interest subventions**.
**Escrow Guarantee** (IDP 4.0) ensures promised subsidies are paid on time.

nce756864b73.s: Under the MSE-CDP of the Government of India, which organisation serves as the State Implementing Agency in Andhra Pradesh?
nce756864b73.x: APIIC is the State Implementing Agency for the MSE Cluster Development Programme in Andhra Pradesh.
nce756864b73.tq: Use the implementation-agency trap among closely related industrial institutions.
xs: **APIIC** is the **State Implementing Agency** for MSE-CDP — option **(1)** is correct.
**APMSMEDC** runs **RAMP**; **APEDB** handles investor outreach; **DPIIT** runs BRAP.
xa: MSE-CDP: **29** projects approved (**11** completed, **18** at advanced stages).
Pipeline: **28** new proposals + **3** new industrial parks.
APIIC was set up on **26 Sept 1973**.

n21582d2fa6c.s: Andhra Pradesh's Industrial Development Policy (4.0), notified on 26 October 2024, was issued as:
n21582d2fa6c.x: IDP (4.0) is G.O.Ms.68; the MSME policy is G.O.69, Electronics Manufacturing G.O.70 and Food Processing G.O.71.
xa: ⚠ MSME is **69**, not **G.O.71** (Food Processing).

Also in the suite: Private Industrial Parks ("Plug and Play") and Sustainable Electric Mobility.
Companion: Textile & Garments **2024-29**; **IT & GCC Policy (4.0)** effective **12 Dec 2024**.

n2cbbf15233e.s: Under IDP (4.0), a Large project that has installed only 50% of its capacity gets an investment subsidy restricted to:
n2cbbf15233e.x: For a Large project with only 50% capacity installed, the subsidy is limited to 6%; otherwise the ceiling may be up to 12%.
xa: Large: **₹501-1,000 crore**; standard period **3 years from CFE**.
Subsidy cut by **0.5% per month** of delay.
Paid over **7** instalments.

nade61a71f23.s: ReSTART, launched by the Government of Andhra Pradesh in May 2020, was primarily intended as:
o: A COVID-19 relief package for MSMEs
A policy for foreign direct investment in defence
A programme for constructing industrial corridors
nade61a71f23.x: ReSTART was Andhra Pradesh’s COVID-19 relief package for MSMEs, launched in May 2020.
nade61a71f23.tq: Use the launch date and sector-purpose combination to distinguish the scheme from other industrial initiatives.
xs: **ReSTART (May 2020)** was AP's **COVID relief for MSMEs** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was about **₹1,110 crore**.
xa: It mainly **cleared pending incentive arrears**.
IDP 4.0's **Escrow Guarantee** now addresses incentive arrears.
Delayed payments nationally: MSME **Samadhaan**; **45-day** payment rule (May 2026).

n36ad7421453.s: Which one of the following best describes the principal use of the ReSTART package?
o: Clearing pending incentive arrears of MSMEs
Providing only export subsidies to large enterprises
Financing only new steel plants in Rayalaseema
n36ad7421453.x: The ReSTART package mainly cleared pending incentive arrears and provided COVID-19 relief to MSMEs.
n36ad7421453.tq: Distinguish the principal objective of a scheme from unrelated sectoral initiatives.
xs: ReSTART was mainly used for **clearing pending incentive arrears of MSMEs** — option **(1)** is correct.
**PARIVESH 3.0** is the central environmental clearance window, unrelated to ReSTART.
xa: ReSTART: **May 2020**, about **₹1,110 crore**.
IDP 4.0 added the **Escrow Guarantee** so subsidies are paid on time.
Delayed incentive payments = long-standing MSME grievance.

nd9b75ae2cf9.s: Under the revised definition effective from 1 April 2025, a small enterprise has an investment limit of:

xa: 2020 small limit was **₹10 cr / ₹50 cr**.

The 2020 limits came by **MSMED Act** notification.

n663abb06189.s: The Andhra Pradesh MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy (4.0) aims to establish more than 175 MSME parks with at least:
n663abb06189.x: The policy envisages more than 175 MSME parks, with at least one park in each assembly constituency.
n663abb06189.tq: Match the numerical target with its territorial unit.
xs: **175+ MSME parks**, at least **one per assembly constituency** — option **(2)** is correct.

IDP 4.0 also targets **175+** industrial parks.
**22 plug-and-play industrial clusters** link MSMEs with anchor units.

n68f9b9d6da2.s: The AP MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy (4.0) 2024-29 targets "One Family, One Entrepreneur" by:
n68f9b9d6da2.x: The policy targets One Family, One Entrepreneur by 2030 and investment of Rs 50,000 crore.
xa: **175+ MSME parks**, one per **assembly constituency**.
**500+ MSME Champions** in global trade.
Policy period: **2024-29**, **G.O.Ms.No. 69**.

n89df49c7dd3.s: Which of the following MSME limits is NOT correct?
o: 2020: Micro – investment Rs 1 crore, turnover Rs 5 crore
2025 revision: Small – investment Rs 25 crore, turnover Rs 100 crore
2020: Medium – investment Rs 50 crore, turnover Rs 250 crore
2020: Small – investment Rs 10 crore, turnover Rs 100 crore
n89df49c7dd3.x: The 2020 small-enterprise turnover limit was Rs 50 crore; Rs 100 crore (with Rs 25 crore investment) is the revised 2025 limit.
xa: Revised (1 April 2025): micro **₹2.5 cr / ₹10 cr**; small **₹25 cr / ₹100 cr**; medium **₹125 cr / ₹500 cr**.
The micro definition was tested in **APPSC 2023**.

n5d2d0f88ba3.s: From 1 April 2025, the limits for a medium enterprise are:
o: Investment Rs 25 crore, turnover Rs 100 crore
Investment Rs 50 crore, turnover Rs 250 crore
Investment Rs 100 crore, turnover Rs 400 crore
Investment Rs 125 crore, turnover Rs 500 crore
n5d2d0f88ba3.x: The 2020 medium limits of Rs 50 crore and Rs 250 crore became Rs 125 crore and Rs 500 crore from 1 April 2025.
xa: Revised micro **₹2.5 cr / ₹10 cr** (2020: **₹1 cr / ₹5 cr**).
Revised limits effective **1 April 2025**.

n1d7af339f77.s: As of February 2024, the number of registered MSMEs in Andhra Pradesh was approximately:
n1d7af339f77.x: The policy baseline recorded about 9 lakh registered MSMEs in Andhra Pradesh in February 2024.
n1d7af339f77.tq: Distinguish the dated registered-MSME figure from later broader estimates.
xs: AP had about **9 lakh** registered MSMEs in **Feb 2024** — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ **20 lakh** is the later count by the AP MSMEDC CEO (**6 Apr 2026**).
xa: That was **3.23%** of India's formal MSMEs, mostly **services**.
**28** exclusive MSME parks; MSMEs = **23.5%** of GSDP.
Nationally, the **Udyam portal** has over **7 crore** enterprises.

n18cce3c986f.s: The motto of the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy (4.0) is to:
o: Increase imports and restrict domestic manufacturing
Replace all private investment with public investment
Cut the cost of production and raise the speed of doing business
Maximise taxation and reduce industrial employment
n18cce3c986f.x: The policy motto is to cut the cost of production and raise the speed of doing business.
n18cce3c986f.tq: Recall the exact wording of the policy motto and avoid opposite-policy distractors.
xs: The motto: **cut the cost of production** and **raise the speed of doing business** — option **(3)** is correct.
The other options contradict the policy's goals.
xa: "**Speed of Doing Business**" is AP's new pitch.
Vision: globally competitive hub built on **sustainability + digital innovation + resilience**.
The **AP Omnibus (Speed of Doing Business) Bill 2026** amended the **2002** Single Window Act.

n16eeab587a3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the AP Single Desk Portal?
o: It enables online application, payment, tracking and certificates
It is a single Government-to-Business point for industrial clearances
It requires physical visits to regulators for every clearance
n16eeab587a3.x: The portal is designed to provide clearances without physical visits to regulators.
xa: Processes **93+ clearances across 19 departments** within **21 days**.
Approvals within SLA: **99.20%** (APSES 2024-25).
Statutory basis: **AP Industrial Single Window Clearance Act, 2002**.

nce39e88dc75.s: The AP Single Desk Portal was originally designed to provide 93 clearances from how many departments within 21 days?
nce39e88dc75.x: The portal was designed for 93 clearances from 19 departments within 21 days.
xa: Still a **21-day** target under IDP 4.0.
**Pre-establishment and pre-operation** approvals within **21 days** (APPSC 2021, 2023).
Tourism investors: **13 pre-establishment** + **11 pre-operation** clearances.

n6cb3b42b7b6.s: The statutory basis for the single-window clearance mechanism in Andhra Pradesh is provided by which of the following Acts?
o: Andhra Pradesh Industrial Single Window Clearance Act, 2002
Andhra Pradesh Ease of Doing Business Act, 2020
n6cb3b42b7b6.x: The Andhra Pradesh Industrial Single Window Clearance Act was enacted in 2002 and gives statutory force to the single-window mechanism.
n6cb3b42b7b6.tq: Use the exact statute-year pair and avoid confusing it with the later portal launch year.
xs: **AP Industrial Single Window Clearance Act, 2002** gives the single window statutory force — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ **2015** is the launch of the **Single Desk Portal**, not the statute year.
xa: The Act provides **deemed approval** if a department misses its deadline.
Amended by the **AP Omnibus (Speed of Doing Business) Bill 2026** (passed **20 Aug 2026**).
APEDB was set up under the **AP Economic Development Board Act, 2018**.

n72867263aae.s: Under AP's statutory single-window framework, an application not decided within the service-level deadline is:
n72867263aae.x: The Act provides for deemed approval when a department misses the prescribed deadline.
xa: "Deemed approval if the **SLA** is breached" is one approval category.
**CGD policy (G.O. Ms. No. 8, Mar 2026)** also uses **deemed clearances**.
⚠ New FDI SOP (May 2026): **presumed consent after 8 weeks**.

n7ae90b75ed9.s: Which of the following is a stated function of the Single Desk system for investment proposals?
o: Providing one application point for every clearance required by an investment proposal
Providing only post-operation approvals to existing factories
Replacing all industrial licences with tax exemptions
n7ae90b75ed9.x: The Single Desk system provides one application point for every clearance required by an investment proposal.
n7ae90b75ed9.tq: Identify the core administrative purpose instead of confusing it with a substantive regulatory power.
xs: It provides **one application point for every clearance** an **investment proposal** needs — option **(1)** is correct.
APPSC 2018: the policy was for clearing **investment proposals**.
It covers **pre-establishment and pre-operation** approvals, not only post-operation.
xa: Benefit: removes **physical interaction** with regulators.
**93+ clearances across 19 departments** within **21 days**.

n5981cb54192.s: Which legislation was passed by the Andhra Pradesh Assembly in 2026 in relation to speeding up business processes?
o: AP Omnibus (Speed of Doing Business) Bill, 2026
n5981cb54192.x: The Andhra Pradesh Assembly passed the AP Omnibus (Speed of Doing Business) Bill, 2026.
n5981cb54192.tq: Use the exact official title and avoid substituting a generic industrial-law name.
xs: The **AP Omnibus (Speed of Doing Business) Bill, 2026** was passed in **Aug 2026** — option **(2)** is correct.
It **amended the 2002** Single Window Clearance Act.
xa: Passed on **20 Aug 2026**.
IDP 4.0 motto: raise **speed of doing business**.
⚠ Statute **2002**; portal **April 2015**; Omnibus Bill **2026**.

n5c7948de708.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's Single Desk Portal, within what time are pre-establishment and pre-operation approvals to be given?
n5c7948de708.x: The Single Desk Portal grants pre-establishment and pre-operation approvals within 21 days (APPSC 2021, 2023), and IDP 4.0 keeps the 21-day target. 93 is the number of clearances, not days; 15 and 30 days are not the stated limit.
xs: **Pre-establishment and pre-operation** approvals within **21 days** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2021, 2023).
**93** is the number of clearances, not days.
xa: Still a **21-day** target under IDP 4.0.
**19 departments** are covered.
⚠ New FDI SOP: **12 weeks** (earlier 10).

nfcd9379dafb.s: Which body was empowered to allot up to 50 acres directly without Cabinet approval?
nfcd9379dafb.x: APIIC was empowered to allot up to 50 acres directly without Cabinet approval.
xa: APIIC: set up **26 Sept 1973**; land bank **41,998 acres**.
APIIC coordinates **Single Desk** clearances.
APIIC-**Union Bank** MoU (**July 2022**) for loans in **39** parks.

n06d91060834.s: Which organisation coordinates Single Desk clearances in Andhra Pradesh?
n06d91060834.x: APIIC coordinates Single Desk clearances in Andhra Pradesh.
n06d91060834.tq: Use the institutional-ownership trap by distinguishing APIIC from APEDB and financial bodies.
xs: **APIIC** coordinates **Single Desk clearances** (SES 2025-26) — option **(1)** is correct.
**APEDB** = investor outreach; **APCOB** = cooperative bank; **FIEO** = partner in the RAMP buyer-seller meet.
xa: APIIC land bank: **41,998 acres**.
APIIC is the State Implementing Agency for **MSE-CDP**.
Single Desk: **93+ clearances**, **21 days**.

n64bee8efb52.s: The Andhra Pradesh Economic Development Board (APEDB) functions under which statute?
o: AP Industrial Single Window Clearance Act, 2002
n64bee8efb52.x: APEDB has statutory backing under the AP Economic Development Board Act, 2018 (APPSC 2023). The 2002 Act is the single-window law, there is no 2015 MSMEDC Act, and IDP 4.0 is a policy, not a statute.
xs: APEDB functions under the **AP Economic Development Board Act, 2018** — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2023).
The **2002** Act is the single-window statute.
xa: APEDB does investor outreach with the **Industries Department**.

nb8a1c3acda5.s: Which one of the following correctly shows the revenue deficit of Andhra Pradesh in 2026-27 BE?

xs: The 2026-27 BE revenue deficit is **₹22,003 crore, equal to 1.1% of GSDP** — option **(1)**.
**₹75,868 cr (3.8%)** is the 2026-27 **fiscal** deficit, not the revenue deficit.
xa: Some notes give the RD as **₹22,002 crore (1.11%)**; FD as **3.84%**.
The RD was cut to **1.1%** because the **16th FC ended revenue-deficit grants**.
The fiscal deficit of **3.8%** is still above the **3% norm** (16th FC cap for States).

nbe8a4961708.s: The Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27 has a total outlay of ₹3,32,205 crore. What is its net expenditure, excluding debt repayment?
nbe8a4961708.x: Net expenditure excluding debt repayment is ₹3,10,058 crore (12% over 2025-26 RE); adding debt repayment of ₹22,147 crore gives the total outlay of ₹3,32,205 crore. ₹2,56,143 crore is revenue expenditure; ₹2,69,928 crore was net expenditure in 2024-25 BE.
nbe8a4961708.tq: Net exp ₹3,10,058 cr + debt repayment ₹22,147 cr = outlay ₹3,32,205 cr.

**₹2,56,143 cr** is **revenue expenditure**; **₹2,69,928 cr** was net expenditure in **2024-25 BE**.
xa: Net expenditure grew **+12%** on 2025-26 RE.
Capital outlay **₹48,698 cr** (+47%) ≈ **15.7%** of net spending.
⚠ **₹3,32,205 cr** = total outlay; **₹3,10,058 cr** = net of debt repayment.

ncb87b00e630.s: What fiscal deficit does the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27 (BE) project?
ncb87b00e630.x: The 2026-27 BE fiscal deficit is ₹75,868 crore, about 3.8% of GSDP. ₹81,362 crore (5.11%) was the 2024-25 actual; ₹80,567 crore (4.57%) the 2025-26 RE; ₹22,003 crore (1.1%) is the 2026-27 revenue deficit.
xs: 2026-27 BE fiscal deficit: **₹75,868 crore, 3.8% of GSDP** — option **(3)**.
**₹22,003 cr (1.1%)** is the 2026-27 **revenue** deficit.
xa: Some notes give the FD as **3.84%**.
**16th FC** caps States' fiscal deficit at **3% of GSDP** (Union 3.5% of GDP) — AP is still above it.
**₹11,000 cr** of 50-year interest-free capex loans lie outside that ceiling.

n2356ff46a46.s: Andhra Pradesh's allocation for education in 2026-27 was:

CAG monthly data (2023-2025): recurring revenue deficits, rising committed spending, weak non-tax revenue.

n1744f299dd1.s: Raising user charges for public services is generally used as a measure of:
n1744f299dd1.x: Increasing user charges is a standard fiscal-consolidation tool because it can augment non-tax revenue and reduce the gap between receipts and expenditure.
n1744f299dd1.tq: Apply the fiscal meaning of higher service charges to the stated policy objective.
xs: Raising **user charges** is a standard tool of **fiscal consolidation** — option **(2)**.
User charges are **non-tax revenue**, so they raise receipts without new taxes.
xa: AP user charges (2024-25 RE): **Medical & Health Rs. 313 Cr**, **Police Rs. 389 Cr**, Education Rs. 55 Cr.
Non-tax revenue = receipts **not raised by taxing the public**.
AP's own non-tax fell from BE **10,576** to RE **7,018** (₹ cr) in 2024-25.

n94ae23b3d7d.s: In Andhra Pradesh, mica is associated mainly with the:

Mining & quarrying IIP (2023-24): **-7.21%** over 2022-23.
Mines & Minerals is AP's **largest** own non-tax source.

n36c40832791.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about developmental and non-developmental expenditure?
o: Construction of irrigation dams can be developmental capital expenditure
Developmental expenditure may be incurred as revenue expenditure
Salaries of teachers can be developmental revenue expenditure
The developmental classification is identical to the revenue-capital classification
n36c40832791.x: The developmental/non-developmental division cuts across the revenue/capital division; it is not identical to it.
xa: Developmental = social & economic services; non-developmental = general services.
Welfare schemes are revenue expenditure — no assets, recurring liability.
AP 2026-27 BE capital outlay **₹48,698 cr** vs revenue expenditure **₹2,56,143 cr**.

n6aebc662c3e.s: In 2026-27, interest payments and principal repayment together accounted for how many paise of every rupee in Andhra Pradesh?
n6aebc662c3e.x: Interest and principal took 18 paise, level with welfare at 17 paise, and the State continued to run a primary deficit.
xa: Interest 2026-27: **₹37,281 cr** (**16%** of revenue receipts).
Golden rule: borrow **only for capital assets**.
Key debt indicators (ES 2025-26): **debt-GSDP** and **IP/RR**.

neb9a484e6b6.s: High interest payments, administrative costs and welfare commitments in AP's finances lead to:
o: Fiscal rigidity and crowding out of capital outlay
neb9a484e6b6.x: These committed items create fiscal rigidity and crowd out capital outlay.
xa: Interest **₹37,281 cr (16%)** and pensions **Rs. 23,713 Cr (10%)** of revenue receipts.

ES 2025-26: unconditional cash transfers crowd out capex.

n36004a0a342.s: Andhra Pradesh's interest payments account for about what share of its revenue receipts?
n36004a0a342.x: Interest payments of Rs 37,281 crore are about 16% of revenue receipts; pensions are Rs 23,713 crore.

Interest has more than doubled since **2017-18** (**14,783**, RE).

n38598efa715.s: In budget classification, welfare spending such as pensions and recurring subsidies is:

xa: NTR Bharosa Pension alone is ~**11%** of revenue expenditure.
ES 2025-26 urges **conditional transfers or sunset clauses**.
Welfare (17 paise) vs interest + principal (**18 paise**) of every rupee.

nd13f54cffc5.s: The capital outlay of Andhra Pradesh in 2026-27 Budget Estimates is approximately what share of net spending?
nd13f54cffc5.x: The capital outlay of ₹48,698 crore in 2026-27 BE constituted approximately 15.7 percent of net spending.

xs: Capital outlay is about **15.7 percent** of net spending in 2026-27 BE — option **(4)**.

Revenue exp : capital outlay improves from ~**9.3 : 1** to ~**5.3 : 1**.

n61ad7ea2321.s: During 2014-15 to 2023-24, capital expenditure of all States formed about what share of their total spending?

All States: committed expenditure + subsidies = **51.76%** of revenue expenditure (2023-24).

nbb37899f77c.s: Andhra Pradesh's higher capital outlay is directed mainly towards:
o: Irrigation and flood control, water supply and sanitation, and urban development
Rice subsidy, fee reimbursement and DBT schemes

nbb37899f77c.x: Higher capital outlay is directed towards irrigation and flood control, water supply and sanitation, and urban development.

n3fb10b84fb1.s: Capital expenditure by a State government mainly reflects its commitment to:
n3fb10b84fb1.x: As per the PYQ key, capex signals commitment to building infrastructure; AP's capex stayed below 15% of total expenditure in 2016-21.
xa: All States: capex **13-20%** of total spending (2014-15 to 2023-24).

Golden rule: borrow **only for capital assets**.

na043823ab62.s: Since Andhra Pradesh continues to run a primary deficit, its borrowing is used to meet:
na043823ab62.x: With a primary deficit, borrowing also finances current spending, not just past interest.
xa: **Golden rule**: borrow only for capital assets.
About **three-quarters** of 2024-25 borrowing covered the revenue gap.
Key indicators: **debt-GSDP** and **IP/RR**.

n42b7e34cbe9.s: The ‘golden rule’ of public borrowing implies that borrowing should generally be used for:
n42b7e34cbe9.x: The golden rule states that borrowing should be undertaken only for creating capital assets, rather than for routine revenue expenditure.
n42b7e34cbe9.tq: Apply the fiscal principle to distinguish capital creation from current spending.
xs: The golden rule: borrow only for **capital assets** — option **(1)**: creating capital assets.

xa: AP still runs a **primary deficit** → borrowing also meets current spending.
Capex creates **productive assets**; committed spending squeezes it.
AP's ₹11,000 cr of 50-year interest-free capex loans lie outside the FD ceiling.

n1b13e57ce87.s: Interest payments in the Andhra Pradesh Budget are treated as:
o: A voted item of developmental expenditure
A discretionary grant to local bodies
n1b13e57ce87.x: Interest payments are a charged item and are not subject to voting. They are also committed, non-developmental expenditure.

xs: Interest is a **charged** item of expenditure, not voted — option **(1)**.

xa: SES 2025-26: interest crowds out developmental spending.
2026-27 BE interest: **₹37,281 cr** (16% of revenue receipts).
Interest + principal repayment = **18 paise** of every rupee.

n9da20f39ebf.s: Investments of the Consolidated Sinking Fund are made in:
n9da20f39ebf.x: States contribute to the CSF to amortise liabilities, and it is invested in Government of India securities.
xa: The CSF is **RBI-administered**.

n34bb31c074f.s: Guarantees given by the Andhra Pradesh government crystallise as liabilities only when they are:

xa: The **GRF** (RBI) helps States meet invoked guarantees.

Union fiscal deficit capped at 3.5% of GDP

n28f44493ec9.s: The allocation for welfare of SCs, STs, OBCs and minorities in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27 was

nbaf3d7ee331.s: According to the 2026–27 Budget Estimates of Andhra Pradesh, the revenue receipts of the State are estimated at:

nadb83da5c58.s: By November 2025, Andhra Pradesh's non-tax revenue collection stood at:

n0bdad048003.x: Budget 2026–27 showed outstanding guarantees of ₹1,77,328 crore, equivalent to 10% of GSDP. The earlier figure was ₹1,54,797 crore, or 11% of GSDP, in 2023–24.
