n23a9023ea4f.s: The World Meteorological Organization’s standard period for describing climate normals is:
n23a9023ea4f.x: The WMO standard describes climate using average weather conditions over a period of 30 years.
n23a9023ea4f.tq: Test the standard numerical period directly.
xs: The **WMO** standard for climate is average weather over **30 years** — option **(3)**.
Climate is long-term; weather is the state at **one place and time**.
xa: IMD's SW monsoon normal (**868.6 mm**) uses the **1971-2020** base period — a 30-year normal.
A **biome** is a large natural community shaped by **climate**.
**Climograph**: temperature as a **line**, rainfall as **bars**.

n8fe0468982f.s: Which one of the following climatic regions is characterised by dense evergreen hardwoods such as mahogany and ebony, with rain almost every day?
n8fe0468982f.x: The equatorial region, including the Amazon, Congo and Indonesia, has dense evergreen hardwood forests and almost daily rainfall.
n8fe0468982f.tq: Directly link the vegetation and rainfall pattern with the climatic region.
xs: The **equatorial** region has **dense evergreen hardwoods** (**mahogany, ebony**) and **rain almost daily** — option **(2)**.
**Mediterranean** has winter rain; **taiga** conifers; **savanna** tall grass.
xa: Equatorial belt (**0-10 deg**): **Amazon, Congo, Indonesia**, SE Asia.
Afternoon **convectional rain**; rain **50-260 inches**.
Very small annual range (**2-3 degC**) with rain every month = equatorial; **Pygmies** live in these forests.

n4c055362484.s: Which of the following regions is associated with the China-type climate?
o: Sudan belt and East Africa only
n4c055362484.x: The China-type climate is associated with central and southern China, as well as areas such as the south-eastern United States, southern Brazil and eastern Australia.
n4c055362484.tq: Identify the representative area from a climate classification list.
xs: The **China type** climate covers **central and southern China** — option **(2)**.
It is a **warm humid east-margin** climate with **summer rain**; also **SE USA**, S Brazil, E Australia.
Arctic coasts are **tundra**; Sahara and Kalahari **hot desert**; Sudan belt **savanna**.
xa: ⚠ **China type** = east margin; **Mediterranean** = **30-45 deg** western margins; **hot deserts** = **15-30 deg** western margins.
Notes confirm the sub-tropical biome = **eastern China and SE USA**.
**British type** deciduous biome = **NW Europe**.

na247256bb65.s: The British-type climate is characterised by which combination?
o: Westerlies, rainfall throughout the year and mild conditions
Summer drought, winter rain and evergreen shrubs
Wet summer, dry winter and tall grass
Permafrost, no trees and very low precipitation
na247256bb65.x: The British type is influenced by westerlies and has rainfall throughout the year with mild conditions.
na247256bb65.tq: Distinguish the British type from Mediterranean and savanna climates by rainfall seasonality.
xs: The **British type** has **westerlies**, **rain throughout the year** and **mild** conditions — option **(1)**.
Summer drought with winter rain is **Mediterranean**; wet summer/dry winter is **savanna**; permafrost is **tundra**.
xa: British type = temperate deciduous of **NW Europe**; also British Columbia, S Chile, New Zealand.
Trees **oak, beech, maple, birch** shed leaves in **autumn**.
Mid-latitude location (APPSC G2 **2025**).

n9900a1edc35.s: The Mediterranean climate occurs mainly between which latitudes on the western margins of continents?
n9900a1edc35.x: The Mediterranean climate lies at about 30-45° N and S on western margins; 15-30° on western margins is the hot desert belt.
xa: Hot desert causes: **subtropical high** + offshore **trade winds** + **cold currents**.
China type areas: Central/S China, **SE USA**, S Brazil, E Australia; **summer rain**.
Mediterranean: **hot dry summers, mild wet winters** — rain from **westerly depressions**.

necf59401c4b.s: Which combination best explains the occurrence of hot deserts on the western margins of continents?
o: Subtropical high pressure, offshore trade winds and cold currents
Polar easterlies, glaciers and high humidity
Equatorial low pressure, onshore trade winds and warm currents
Monsoon depressions, warm currents and rising air
necf59401c4b.x: Subtropical high pressure suppresses rainfall, offshore trade winds reduce moisture supply, and cold currents further stabilise and dry the air.
necf59401c4b.tq: Match the desert location with the combined pressure, wind and current conditions.
xs: Hot deserts on western margins result from **subtropical high pressure**, **offshore trade winds** and **cold currents** — option **(1)**.
Equatorial low pressure, onshore winds and warm currents bring rain, not deserts.
xa: **Cold currents** cool and dry coasts, making tropical west coasts arid.
Hot desert: rain **under 25 cm**, high diurnal range, **xerophytes**.
Desert peoples: **Bedouin** (Arabia, Sahara), **Tuareg** (Sahara), **Bushmen (San)** (Kalahari).

n61652e0d5b3.s: A biome is best described as which one of the following?
o: A transition zone between two adjacent ecosystems
An artificial ecosystem maintained only by human beings
A small community containing only one species
A large natural community of flora and fauna over a major habitat, shaped mainly by climate
n61652e0d5b3.x: A biome is a large natural community of flora and fauna occupying a major habitat and shaped by climate. It contains many habitats.
n61652e0d5b3.tq: Distinguish the definition of a biome from community, ecosystem and ecotone.
xs: A **biome** is a **large natural community of flora and fauna** over a **major habitat**, **shaped by climate** — option **(4)**.
It **contains many habitats**, so it is not a single-species community or a transition zone; human-made units are **anthromes**.
xa: **Anthromes**: ecological units shaped by **sustained human use** (croplands, villages, cities).
**Taiga** is the **largest land biome**.
**Tree line**: beyond it trees cannot grow (APPSC GS **2019**).

n300372f1e0e.s: Mediterranean climate receives most of its rainfall during winter because
o: the subtropical high-pressure belt dominates in winter
cold ocean currents produce continuous monsoon rainfall
westerly depressions and cyclonic systems affect the region in winter
the trade winds reverse and produce convection throughout winter
n300372f1e0e.x: In winter, the seasonal shift of pressure belts allows westerly depressions to bring cyclonic rainfall to Mediterranean regions.
n300372f1e0e.tq: Connect the seasonal pressure-belt shift with the timing of rainfall.
xs: Mediterranean winter rain comes from **westerly depressions** (**cyclonic rain**) — option **(3)**.
Reason: the **seasonal shift of pressure belts**; in **summer** the **subtropical high** brings hot, dry drought — so option (1) is reversed.
xa: Pattern: **hot dry summers, mild wet winters**.
Location: **30-45 deg N/S** on **western margins**.
India's parallel: Koeppen **As** on the **Coromandel coast**.

n1571a128396.s: The Mediterranean climatic region is popularly known for the cultivation of
n1571a128396.x: Mediterranean regions are known as orchard lands and are associated with citrus fruits, grapes and wine production.
n1571a128396.tq: Use the characteristic crop association to identify the climate.
xs: Mediterranean regions are known for **citrus fruits, grapes and wine** — option **(2)** ("**orchard lands**").
Natural vegetation: **evergreen shrubs, olives, citrus**.
xa: Climate: **hot dry summers, mild wet winters**.
Location: **30-45 deg N/S**, western margins.
⚠ **Warm dry summer, mild wet winter** description = Mediterranean.

n06d2dbfb966.s: The Atacama Desert is regarded as one of the driest regions of the world and is located in
o: central Australia, west of the Great Dividing Range
southern Argentina, east of the Andes
the interior of the Arabian Peninsula
northern Chile, west of the Andes
n06d2dbfb966.x: The Atacama Desert lies in northern Chile, west of the Andes, and is recognised for extreme aridity.
n06d2dbfb966.tq: Combine the climatic superlative with the correct location.
xs: The **Atacama** Desert lies in **northern Chile, west of the Andes** — option **(4)**.
It is the world's **driest** place.
xa: Hot deserts lie at **15-30 deg** on **western margins** — subtropical high, offshore trade winds, **cold currents**.
India's driest: **Ruyli, Jaisalmer** (**8.33 cm**) in the Thar.
Wettest: **Mawsynram**, mean **1,187 cm**.

nfc2b6fbd369.s: A climate with a very small annual range of temperature (2-3°C) and rain in every month is:
nfc2b6fbd369.x: A tiny annual range with rain every month is typical of the equatorial climate.
xa: **Warm dry summer, mild wet winter** = **Mediterranean**.
Equatorial: rain **almost daily** (afternoon convectional rain).
Savanna: **wet summer, dry winter**; tall grass with scattered trees.

nworld-geography-1-11.s: The world's largest hot desert is:
nworld-geography-1-11.x: The Sahara is the largest hot desert; Antarctica is the largest desert overall (a cold desert).
n: Antarctica is the world’s largest desert by cold-desert classification. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-3]
The Sahara is the world’s largest hot desert. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-3]
xa: **Driest place:** the **Atacama Desert**, northern Chile.
**Driest polar region:** the **McMurdo Dry Valleys**.
**Lowest recorded:** **Vostok (Antarctica), -89.2 degC**.

nworld-geography-18-5.s: Which biome is often described as the world's largest terrestrial biome?
nworld-geography-18-5.x: The taiga or boreal forest is often called the largest land biome.
n: The highest percentage of the world’s forest area by type is represented by temperate coniferous forests. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Tropical rainforests are also called Selva forests. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Tropical rainforests have broadleaf evergreen trees. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Mangrove forests are also called tidal forests. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Mangrove forests occur in coastal, saline, tidal environments. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Mangrove forests contain salt-tolerant trees. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Mangrove forests occur in coastal tropical regions. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
xa: Mangroves have **salt-tolerant trees** with **pneumatophores**.
Taiga = **needle-leaved evergreen softwood** trees of **conical shape**.
Rainforests: **more than 200 cm** rainfall, **multilayered canopy**.

nworld-geography-18-17.s: Cork trees are characteristic of which forest type?
nworld-geography-18-17.x: Mediterranean forests, with hot dry summers and mild wet winters, contain evergreen shrubs, oaks and cork trees.
n: Mediterranean forests have hot, dry summers. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Mediterranean forests have mild, wet winters. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Mediterranean forests contain evergreen shrubs. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Mediterranean forests contain oaks. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Mediterranean forests contain cork trees. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
xa: Location: **30-45 deg** N/S on **western margins**.
Economy: **citrus**, **grapes and wine** ("orchard lands").
Towns: **Rome, Athens**, **Los Angeles**, **Santiago**, **Cape Town**, **Perth**.
Indian parallel: Koeppen **As** on the **Coromandel coast**.

nd7b7d41d8e8.s: The tropical monsoon region of India and South-East Asia is chiefly associated with which vegetation?
nd7b7d41d8e8.x: Tropical monsoon forests in India and South-East Asia include teak and sal; the trees shed their leaves during the dry season.
nd7b7d41d8e8.tq: Match the climatic region with its representative vegetation.
xs: Tropical monsoon forests have **teak and sal** — option **(1)**.
Trees **shed leaves in the dry season**; rainfall **700-2,000 mm**.
**Spruce and fir** belong to the **taiga**; **mosses and lichens** to the **tundra**; **oak and maple** to temperate deciduous forests.
xa: Region: **India, SE Asia, N Australia**; seasonal wind reversal, summer rain.
AP is Koeppen **Aw** (tropical wet and dry).
Temperate deciduous trees (oak, beech, maple, birch) shed leaves in **autumn**.

na922e665148.s: The Steppe belt is significant because it separates:
na922e665148.x: The Eurasian Steppe belt separates Cold Asia from Dry Asia.
na922e665148.tq: Test the geographical relationship associated with a named region.
xs: The Steppe belt separates **Cold Asia from Dry Asia** — option **(3)** (APPSC G1 **2022**).
It runs from **Ukraine to Central Asia** — Russia east of the **Urals**.
xa: Steppes are **temperate** grasslands.
Fauna of temperate grasslands: **bison, prairie dogs, antelope**.
**Central Asian steppes** are cited as rangelands (UN Year **2026**).

nac3149ac8cd.s: The Downs are the temperate grasslands of:
nac3149ac8cd.x: The Downs are the Australian temperate grassland; the Veld is in South Africa, the Pampas in Argentina and Canterbury in New Zealand.
xa: Exam angle: Prairies are in USA **and** Canada (not USA alone, not Mexico).
Tropical grasslands: **savanna** (Africa), **Llanos** (Venezuela), **Campos** (Brazil).
⚠ **Llanos** = Venezuela; **Pampas** = Argentina; **Campos** = Brazil.

na1a60a58138.s: Which one of the following is a tropical grassland rather than a temperate grassland?
na1a60a58138.x: Llanos is a tropical grassland of the Orinoco basin, whereas Pampas, Steppes and Veld are temperate grasslands.
na1a60a58138.tq: Separate the tropical category from the group of temperate grasslands.
xs: The **Llanos** (**Venezuela**-Colombia, **Orinoco basin**) is a **tropical** grassland — option **(3)**.
**Steppes, Veld** and **Pampas** are all **temperate** grasslands.
xa: Other tropical grasslands: **savanna** (Africa), **Campos** (Brazilian Highlands).
Temperate: **Prairies, Pampas, Steppes, Veld, Downs, Canterbury**.
Savanna climate: **wet summer, dry winter** (tropical wet-dry).

nworld-geography-19-8.x: Tropical grasslands are called savannas; Africa's savannas have the richest large-mammal diversity.
n: Tropical grasslands are also called savannas. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 31-33]
Africa's tropical grasslands have the richest large mammal diversity. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 31-33]
xa: Savanna wildlife: **African elephants, lions, cheetahs, zebras, giraffes**.
Savanna vegetation: **elephant grass**, **baobab**, **acacia**; naturally **fire-prone**.
Savanna peoples: **Masai** of **Kenya, Tanzania**.

nworld-geography-19-10.s: Bison are the signature grazers of:
nworld-geography-19-10.x: The American bison belongs to the temperate prairies of North America, not the tropical grasslands.
n: Bison are wildlife of tropical grasslands. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 31-33]
Bison in the tropical grasslands note are associated with North America. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 31-33]
xa: **Prairies** = **USA and Canada**.
Temperate grassland fauna: **bison, prairie dogs, antelope**.
Temperate grassland rain: only **25-50 cm**.

nworld-geography-10-27.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Afridi?
o: A Polynesian indigenous people associated with New Zealand
A Pashtun tribal group associated with Pakistan and South Asia
An Orang Asli community associated with Malaysia
An Indigenous Negrito group associated with the Philippines
nworld-geography-10-27.x: The Afridi are a Pashtun tribe of Pakistan near the Khyber Pass.
nworld-geography-10-27.tq: Recall the identity of each people.
n: Afridi are a Pashtun tribal group. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Afridi are associated with Pakistan and South Asia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
xs: The Afridi are **a Pashtun tribal group associated with Pakistan and South Asia** — option **(2)**.
They live around the **Khyber Pass** and **Safed Koh** — the **strategic Khyber region**.
**Orang Asli** = **Sakai**, Malaysia; **Indigenous Negrito** of the Philippines = **Aeta**.
xa: **Kirghiz** = **Pamir** and **Tianshan**, nomadic herders.
**Ainu** = **Hokkaido**, **Sakhalin**.
**Semang** = **Negrito** of the **Malay Peninsula**.

n0800b9d0d1c.s: The Kirghiz and Kazakh peoples are traditionally associated with the
n0800b9d0d1c.x: The Kirghiz and Kazakh peoples are associated with the grasslands and steppes of Central Asia.
n0800b9d0d1c.tq: Use the natural-region association to distinguish steppe peoples from desert and tundra groups.
xs: The **Kirghiz and Kazakh** are peoples of the **Central Asian steppes** — option **(4)**.
Greenland tundra = **Inuit**; Kalahari = **Bushmen (San)**; Congo forest = **Pygmies**.
xa: Steppes separate **Cold Asia from Dry Asia** (APPSC G1 **2022**).
Steppe climate: hot summers, chilly winters, rain **25-50 cm**.
**Yakuts** live in Siberia (taiga/Arctic).

n6c8bdfa5cd1.s: The Masai herders belong to which natural region?
o: Equatorial forest of the Congo basin
n6c8bdfa5cd1.x: The Masai are herders of the Kenya-Tanzania savanna; Pygmies live in the Congo forest, Bushmen in the Kalahari and Inuit in the tundra.
xa: ⚠ **Masai** = savanna; **Pygmies** = equatorial forest; **Bushmen** = Kalahari.
**Bedouin** and **Tuareg** — hot deserts; **Sami** — tundra.
**Yakuts** — Siberia (taiga/Arctic).

nworld-geography-18-4.s: Siberia, Canada and Scandinavia are covered mainly by which forest type?
nworld-geography-18-4.x: Siberia, Canada and Scandinavia carry the taiga (boreal forest).
n: The Congo Basin is the second-largest tropical rainforest. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Temperate coniferous forests are also called Taiga forests. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Temperate coniferous forests are also called boreal forests. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Temperate coniferous forests occur in Canada. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Temperate coniferous forests occur in Scandinavia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Temperate coniferous forests occur in Siberia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Temperate deciduous forests occur in the eastern United States. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Temperate deciduous forests occur in Western Europe. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Mediterranean forests occur in Mediterranean lands. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Mediterranean forests occur in the Mediterranean Basin. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
xa: Mediterranean forests also in **California**, **Central Chile**, **SW Australia**, **Cape Province**.
**Mangroves** (tidal forests): **Sundarbans** and coastal tropics.
**Tropical deciduous** (monsoon) forests: **India, Africa, Myanmar, SE Asia**.

nworld-geography-10-5.x: The Ainu were traditionally hunters and fishermen; the Kirghiz were nomadic herders.
n: Ainu were traditionally hunters and fishermen. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Aeta were traditionally forest foragers and hunters. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Kirghiz or Kyrgyz groups are nomadic herders. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
xa: Kirghiz habitat: **Pamir Plateau**, **Tianshan Mountains** (Central Asia).
Aeta = **Indigenous Negrito group** of the **Philippines**.
Kirghiz/Kazakh are linked with the **steppes**.

nworld-geography-10-7.s: Which of the following groups is associated with reindeer herding?
nworld-geography-10-7.x: The Sami (Lapps) of Lapland, like the Nenets of Siberia, herd reindeer; the Tuareg and Berbers live in the Sahara and North Africa.
n: Lapps or Sami are traditionally associated with reindeer herding. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Samoyed or Nenets groups are nomadic reindeer herders. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Yakuts adapted horse and cattle breeding to extremely cold permafrost conditions. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Berber communities practice agriculture and pastoralism. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Lapps are also called Sami. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
xa: Nenets traditionally use **conical tents** called **chums**.
Sami countries: **Norway, Sweden, Finland**, NW Russia.
**Yakuts** breed **horses and cattle** in permafrost.

nworld-geography-10-12.s: The Eskimo of the Arctic are also called:
nworld-geography-10-12.x: Eskimo is also called Inuit; they live in the Arctic of Canada, Alaska and Greenland.
n: Eskimo is also called Inuit. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Eskimo or Inuit groups inhabit the Arctic tundra and northern regions. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Eskimo or Inuit groups are found in Canada, Alaska, and Greenland. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Eskimo or Inuit groups belong to North America and the Arctic. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Eskimo or Inuit groups are described as Mongoloid in the notes. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
xa: Inuit are **adapted to cold conditions**.
**Sami (Lapps)** = **tundra** of Scandinavia.
**Yakuts (Sakha)** = **Lena** basin, eastern **Siberia**.

nworld-geography-10-13.s: Which of the following groups are described as nomadic pastoralists?
nworld-geography-10-13.x: The Bedouin are nomadic pastoralists of the Arabian and Saharan deserts. The San and Pintupi are hunter-gatherers.
nworld-geography-10-13.tq: Recall the livelihood of each people.
n: Bedouin groups are nomadic pastoralists. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
xs: The **Bedouin** are **nomadic pastoralists** — option **(1)** is correct.
Bedouin live in the **Arabian Desert** and **Sahara** margins, **Middle East and North Africa**.
**Ainu** were **hunters and fishermen**; **Bushman (San)** are **hunter-gatherers**.
xa: **Tuareg** = **desert nomads** of the Sahara.
**Kirghiz** = **nomadic herders** of Central Asia.
Bedouin are linked with the **hot desert** climate type.

nworld-geography-10-20.s: The Samoyed or Nenets groups traditionally inhabit which of the following regions?
o: The Atlas Mountains of North Africa
The mountainous rainforest interiors of Luzon
The eastern coastal plateau plain of South Africa
The tundra of northern and western Siberia
nworld-geography-10-20.x: The Nenets live on the tundra of northern and western Siberia.
nworld-geography-10-20.tq: Recall the habitat of each people.
n: Samoyed or Nenets groups inhabit the tundra of northern and western Siberia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
xs: The Nenets inhabit **the tundra of northern and western Siberia** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Samoyed (Nenets)** are **nomadic reindeer herders** of **Russia/Eurasia**.
**Atlas** = **Berbers**; **Luzon** = **Aeta**; **eastern coastal plateau of South Africa** = **Zulu**.
xa: They use **conical tents** called **chums**.
**Chukchi** = **Chukchi Peninsula**, **maritime hunting**.
**Sami** also herd **reindeer** in Lapland.

nworld-geography-10-21.s: The Chukchi and Koryak inhabit the tundra of:
nworld-geography-10-21.x: The Chukchi and Koryak live on the tundra of the Chukchi Peninsula and Bering Sea coast in far north-east Siberia.
n: Chukchi is grouped with Koryak in the notes. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Chukchi or Koryak groups inhabit the Chukchi Peninsula and the Bering Sea coast. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Chukchi or Koryak groups are found in far northeastern Siberia and Russia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Chukchi or Koryak communities inhabit tundra regions. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
xa: **Nenets** = reindeer herders of **western Siberia**.
**Yakuts** = **Lena/Verkhoyansk** region, **cold adaptation**.
**Oymyakon** is the **coldest inhabited place**.

nworld-geography-10-36.s: The Lapps or Sami are indigenous people of:
o: Lapland in Norway, Sweden, Finland and north-west Russia
nworld-geography-10-36.x: The Sami are indigenous Europeans of Lapland (Fennoscandia) in Norway, Sweden, Finland and north-west Russia.
n: Lapps or Sami inhabit the Arctic and sub-Arctic regions of Fennoscandia and Lapland. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Lapps or Sami are found in Norway, Sweden, Finland, and northwestern Russia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
Lapps or Sami are Indigenous northern European people. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 13-16]
xa: **Samoyed (Nenets)** also herd reindeer, in **Siberia**.
Natural region of the Sami: **tundra**.
**Inuit (Eskimo)** = Canada, Alaska, Greenland.

n1532195b977.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about a climograph?
o: Rainfall is generally shown by a line.
Temperature is generally shown by a line.
It shows the monthly temperature and rainfall of a station on one chart.
It helps identify the climate type of a place.
n1532195b977.x: In a climograph rainfall is shown by bars, while temperature is shown by a line.
xa: Climate = average weather over **30 years** (WMO).
**Biome**: large natural community of flora and fauna over a major habitat, shaped by climate (UPSC).
**Anthromes**: ecological units shaped by sustained human use (croplands, villages, cities).

nb8febb3b60c.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the climatic contrast produced by distance from the sea?
o: Distance from the sea affects rainfall but not temperature
Coastal areas have continental extremes, while interiors are equable
Coastal areas are generally equable, while interiors experience greater extremes
Both coasts and interiors have identical seasonal ranges
nb8febb3b60c.x: The sea moderates temperatures near the coast, whereas inland areas tend to experience greater temperature extremes and a continental climate.
nb8febb3b60c.tq: Identify the correctly reversed coastal–continental comparison.
xs: **Coasts are equable/maritime**, while **interiors are extreme/continental** — option **(3)**.
Option (2) reverses this; the sea moderates both seasonal and daily ranges.
xa: **A&N Islands**: equable, humid; the **monsoon arrives there first**.
⚠ Distance from a **river** is not a climate control.
Other controls: latitude, altitude, relief, ocean currents, winds and pressure belts.

nbdeb22e3f44.s: Thornthwaite proposed his climatic classification in 1931 and revised it in:
nbdeb22e3f44.x: Thornthwaite's scheme, based on precipitation effectiveness and thermal efficiency, dates from 1931 and was revised in 1948.
xa: Koeppen groups: **A** tropical humid, **B** dry, **C** warm temperate, **D** cold snow-forest, **E** polar, **H** highland.
Group **A**: coldest month above **18 degC**; group **E**: warmest month below **10 degC**.
Second letters: **f** no dry season, **m** monsoon, **w** dry winter, **s** dry summer.

n2750fb595fb.s: The taiga (boreal) biome is associated with which soil?
n2750fb595fb.x: The taiga's evergreen conifers grow on acidic podzol soils.
xa: **Taiga is the largest land biome**; it has the **lowest productivity** of all forests.
⚠ Taiga has a **wide** winter-summer temperature range — "narrow range" was the wrong statement (**APPSC G1 2023, 2024**).
Taiga wildlife: **moose, beavers, lynxes, wolves, wolverines**.

n910ba977f05.s: The vegetation of the tundra consists mainly of:
n910ba977f05.x: Tundra has permafrost, mosses and lichens, and generally no trees.
xa: Tundra lies on **Arctic coasts** of N America and Eurasia; **alpine tundra** above the tree line.
Fauna: **reindeer, arctic fox, musk-ox**.
Peoples: **Inuit** (Canada, Alaska, Greenland), **Sami** (Scandinavia).

n74025ddccce.s: The Pampas temperate grasslands are found in:
n74025ddccce.x: The Pampas are in Argentina and Uruguay; Venezuela-Colombia has the Llanos, a tropical grassland.
xa: **Prairies** = **USA and Canada**; **Veld** = **South Africa**; **Downs** = **Australia**.
**Steppes** separate **Cold Asia from Dry Asia** (**APPSC G1 2022**).
⚠ **Campos** = **Brazil** (tropical); **Llanos** = Venezuela (tropical).

n64cac10501e.s: The lowest temperature ever recorded on Earth is associated with
n64cac10501e.x: Vostok in Antarctica recorded the lowest known temperature, about −89.2°C. Oymyakon and Verkhoyansk are associated with the cold pole among inhabited places.
n64cac10501e.tq: Separate the absolute recorded extreme from the coldest inhabited locations.
xs: The lowest recorded temperature is at **Vostok, Antarctica** — **-89.2 degC** — option **(4)**.
**Oymyakon / Verkhoyansk** are the **cold pole** for **inhabited** places; **Death Valley** is the hottest; **Mawsynram** the wettest.
xa: Hottest: **Death Valley**, **56.7 deg C** (**1913**).
India lowest: **-45 deg C at Dras** (**1908**).
⚠ Hottest = Death Valley (not **Al Aziziya**); coldest = **Vostok**.

n2fe4534d2a5.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the exceptional rainfall of Mawsynram and Cherrapunji?
o: Funnelling of moist air and orographic lifting
Cold currents and subtropical high pressure
n2fe4534d2a5.x: Mawsynram and Cherrapunji receive more than 1,100 cm of annual rainfall because moist air is funnelled and forced to rise over the terrain.
n2fe4534d2a5.tq: Link the climatic extreme to the physical mechanism producing it.
xs: **Funnelling** of moist air and **orographic lifting** explain their rainfall — option **(3)**.
**Mawsynram and Cherrapunji** get **over 1,100 cm** a year; descending air and rain-shadow would make them dry.
xa: **Mawsynram** (Khasi Hills, Meghalaya) — mean **1,187 cm**, the wettest place.
**Relief**: windward slopes wet, leeward rain-shadow dry.
Driest in the world: **Atacama**; in India: **Ruyli, Jaisalmer** (**8.33 cm**).

n89720541f6b.s: India's lowest noted temperature, about −45°C in 1908, was recorded at:
n89720541f6b.x: Dras recorded about −45°C in 1908, India's lowest noted temperature; Ganganagar holds the highest (about 50°C in 1935).
xa: ⚠ India lowest = **Dras**, highest = **Ganganagar**.
World: hottest **Death Valley** (**56.7 deg C**); lowest **Vostok** (**-89.2 degC**).
Wettest: **Mawsynram** (mean **1,187 cm**).

n1c4eff8a76f.s: The highest air temperature ever recorded on Earth, 56.7 °C (1913), is associated with:
n1c4eff8a76f.x: Death Valley in California holds the record of 56.7 °C (1913); the WMO rejected Al Aziziya, Libya. Ganganagar's ~50 °C (1935) is India's highest, and the Atacama is the driest place, not the hottest.
xs: The **56.7 °C** (**1913**) record belongs to **Death Valley, California** — option **(2)**.
The **WMO rejected Al Aziziya, Libya**; **Ganganagar** (~**50**, **1935**) is India's highest; the **Atacama** is the driest place.
xa: ⚠ Hottest = Death Valley; coldest = **Vostok** (**-89.2**).
Cold pole for inhabited places: **Verkhoyansk / Oymyakon**, Siberia.

n587242ba629.s: In 2025, what share of the excess heat in the climate system was held by the oceans?
n587242ba629.x: Oceans held more than 90% of the excess heat in 2025.
xa: About **40** coastal districts may warm by over **1** degC by **2040**.
**Bakhira Lake** (UP) holds a **25,000-year** monsoon record.
Cold currents make tropical west coasts arid; warm currents make east coasts warm and rainy.

nworld-geography-2-3.s: The driest non-polar desert in the world is the:
nworld-geography-2-3.x: The Atacama is the driest non-polar desert; Antarctica's McMurdo Dry Valleys are among the driest places overall.
n: The Atacama Desert is the driest place on Earth. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 3-4]
The McMurdo Dry Valleys are the driest polar region. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 3-4]
xa: Atacama lies in **northern Chile**, west of the **Andes**.
**Hottest recorded:** **Furnace Creek**, **Death Valley** (**56.7 deg C**, **1913**).
**Wettest:** **Mawsynram**, Meghalaya — mean **1,187 cm**.

nworld-geography-18-8.s: Tropical rainforests receive annual rainfall of more than:
nworld-geography-18-8.x: Tropical rainforests receive over 200 cm of rain a year and stay hot and humid throughout.
n: Tropical rainforests receive more than 200 cm of rainfall. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Tropical rainforests have hot and humid conditions. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
xa: They have **nutrient-poor soil** and **rapid decomposition**.
Found in the **Amazon Basin**, **Congo Basin**, **Indonesia**, **SE Asia**.
⚠ Other notes give rainforest rain as **50-260 inches**.

n79af0edd017.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about temperate forests?
o: Temperate deciduous forests have broadleaf trees that shed their leaves in autumn.
Temperate coniferous (taiga) forests consist of broadleaf hardwood trees.
Temperate coniferous forests occur in Canada, Scandinavia, Russia and Alaska.
Temperate deciduous forests occur in the eastern USA, Western Europe and East Asia.
n79af0edd017.x: The taiga is made of needle-leaved evergreen softwood conifers, not broadleaf hardwoods; the other three statements are correct.
xa: Taiga also called **boreal** forest; **cold-temperate**, **long winters**.
Temperate deciduous trees: **oak, beech, maple, birch**.
Taiga soils are acidic **podzol**.

ndba5afa4694.s: The Fulani of the West African savannas are traditionally:
ndba5afa4694.x: The Fulani are traditionally pastoral, while the Hausa were settled farmers and traders.
xa: **Kenya and Tanzania** are home of the **Masai**.
**Tuareg** = desert nomads of the **Sahara**.
**Zulu** = **Bantu-speaking**, **KwaZulu-Natal**, South Africa.

n0d1affce4c9.s: The Bantu-speaking Zulu live mainly in:
n0d1affce4c9.x: The Zulu, a Bantu-speaking people, live in KwaZulu-Natal and the eastern coastal plateau plain of South Africa.
xa: **Bantu** = widespread linguistic group of **East, Central and Southern Africa**.
**Bushman (San)** of the **Kalahari** also live in **South Africa**, Botswana, Namibia.
**Masai** = cattle pastoralists of **Kenya, Tanzania**.

n254908719d5.s: The Sakai (Senoi), an Orang Asli community, live in:
o: Central highland rainforests of the Malay Peninsula
n254908719d5.x: The Sakai (Senoi) are Orang Asli of the Malay Peninsula's central highland rainforests; Hokkaido and Sakhalin are home to the Ainu.
xa: **Semang** = **Negrito** group of Malaysia's tropical forests.
**Ainu** were **hunters and fishermen**.
**Aeta** = Negrito foragers of **Luzon**.

n7dced60bbf2.s: The tree line refers to the altitude or latitude beyond which:
n7dced60bbf2.x: The tree line is the altitude or latitude beyond which trees cannot grow; alpine tundra lies above it.
n7dced60bbf2.tq: Test the exact definition of a geographical term.
xs: The **tree line / timber line** is the altitude or latitude **beyond which trees cannot grow** — option **(3)** (APPSC GS **2019**).
It is the **upper limit of tree growth** on mountains or in high latitudes.
xa: Above it lies **alpine tundra** — in the **Himalayas, Andes, Alps**.
Tundra: **permafrost**, mosses, lichens, no trees.
Koeppen **H** = highland, cold due to altitude.

nabe2432cfaa.s: Alpine tundra is generally found in which situation?
o: In the humid equatorial belt below 10° latitude
Above the tree line in mountains such as the Himalayas, Andes and Alps
Below the tree line in tropical lowlands
nabe2432cfaa.x: Alpine tundra occurs above the tree line in high mountain systems such as the Himalayas, Andes and Alps.
nabe2432cfaa.tq: Apply the definition of alpine tundra to altitude and location.
xs: **Alpine tundra** is found **above the tree line** in the **Himalayas, Andes and Alps** — option **(2)**.
The **tree line** is where trees cannot grow, so alpine tundra cannot be below it or in equatorial lowlands.
xa: Arctic tundra: **Arctic coasts** of N America and Eurasia; **permafrost**.
Tree line asked in APPSC GS **2019**.
Koeppen **E** (polar): warmest month below **10 degC** — **ET** tundra, **EF** ice cap.

nworld-geography-18-22.s: Tropical deciduous forests, which receive 100–200 cm of seasonal rain, are also called:
nworld-geography-18-22.x: Tropical deciduous forests are called monsoon forests and get 100–200 cm of seasonal rain.
n: Tropical deciduous forests are also called monsoon forests. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
Tropical deciduous forests receive seasonal rainfall of 100–200 cm. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 29-31]
xa: Trees **shed leaves** in the **dry season**.
Found in **India, Africa, Myanmar, SE Asia**.
Tropical monsoon trees: **teak, sal**.

o: The state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time
The long-term distribution of vegetation over a region
The average atmospheric condition over a period of 30 years
The seasonal variation in ocean currents only
n811ba11e764.x: Weather refers to the state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time. Climate refers to average weather over a long period.
n811ba11e764.tq: Distinguish the short-term weather definition from the long-term climate definition.
xs: **Weather** is the **state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time** — option **(1)**.
The **30-year average** describes **climate**, not weather.
xa: ⚠ **Weather** = one place and time; **Climate** = **30-year** average (WMO).
A **climograph** plots a station's monthly temperature (line) + rainfall (bars).
Elements: temperature, pressure, winds, humidity, precipitation, cloudiness.

n3d521b62c54.s: Anthropogenic biomes, also called anthromes, are ecological units shaped by which of the following?
o: Sustained human use such as croplands, villages and cities
n3d521b62c54.x: Anthropogenic biomes are ecological units shaped by sustained human use and include croplands, villages and cities.
n3d521b62c54.tq: Apply the definition to examples of human-shaped ecological units.
xs: **Anthromes** (anthropogenic biomes) are shaped by **sustained human use** — **croplands, villages, cities** — option **(1)**.
Natural biomes, by contrast, are shaped by **climate**.
xa: A **biome** contains many habitats.
**Climograph**: monthly temperature (line) + rainfall (bars).
Climate = average weather over **30 years** (WMO).

nworld-geography-19-3.s: Marsupials and monotremes are a noted feature of which zoogeographic realm?
nworld-geography-19-3.x: The long isolation of the Australasian realm let marsupials and monotremes evolve with no rivals.
n: Marsupials and monotremes characterize the Australasian realm. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 31-33]
The uniqueness of Australasian marsupials and monotremes is due to isolation. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 31-33]
Marsupials are signature wildlife of the Australasian realm. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 31-33]
xa: Australasian wildlife: **kangaroos, koalas, platypuses, emus, dingoes**.
**Madagascar:** **lemurs, tenrecs**, **high endemism**.
**Koalas** are also listed under Australia's temperate forests.

nworld-geography-19-21.s: Lemurs and tenrecs are wildlife of:
nworld-geography-19-21.x: Lemurs and tenrecs are wildlife of Madagascar, an island of very high endemism.
n: Lemurs are wildlife of Madagascar. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 31-33]
Tenrecs are wildlife of Madagascar. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 31-33]
Madagascar has high endemism. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 31-33]
xa: **Australasian realm:** **marsupials and monotremes**, unique due to **isolation**.
Rainforests have the **highest biodiversity**.
Tropical grasslands of **Africa** have the richest **large mammal** diversity.

n20afbb2a210.s: The United Nations has declared 2026 as the International Year for:
n20afbb2a210.x: The UN declared 2026 the International Year for Rangelands and Pastoralists. Rangelands (grasslands, savannas, shrublands) cover about half of Earth's land. The other options are not the 2026 theme.
xs: The UN declared **2026** the **International Year for Rangelands and Pastoralists** — option **(2)**.
Rangelands (**grasslands, savannas, shrublands**) cover about **half** of Earth's land.
xa: Examples: **Central Asian steppes**, African savanna, **US Great Plains**.
Pastoralist peoples: **Masai** (savanna), **Kirghiz / Kazakh** (steppes).
Steppe rainfall: only **25-50 cm**.

nc7be9aea55b.s: The hottest year on record, about 1.55°C above pre-industrial levels, was:
nc7be9aea55b.x: 2024 was the hottest year on record at about 1.55°C above pre-industrial; 2025 was the warmest La Niña year.
xa: **India** warmed about **0.7 degC since 1900** vs **1.59 degC** for global land.
**Gangotri** retreated about **1,700 m since 1935** (**APPSC G2 2025**).
**Sea level** is up about **11 cm since 1993**.
Earth's **energy imbalance** is at a **65-year peak**.

n5ca49692583.s: The Gangotri Glacier has retreated by approximately how much since 1935?
n5ca49692583.x: Gangotri Glacier has retreated approximately 1,700 metres since 1935, with global warming identified as the cause of its melting.
n5ca49692583.tq: Use the exact distance and reference year together to avoid range-based guessing.
xs: **Gangotri Glacier** has retreated about **1,700 m since 1935** — option **(3)**.
The notes attribute its melting to **global warming** (asked in **APPSC G2 2025**).
xa: **Sea level** has risen about **11 cm since 1993**.
**WMO 2025:** **Arctic** sea ice near record lows; **Antarctic** sea ice **3rd lowest**.
Earth's **energy imbalance** is at a **65-year peak**.

n321fb4c831b.s: Global sea level has risen by about how much since 1993?
n321fb4c831b.x: Global sea level is up about 11 cm since 1993.
xa: **Gangotri** has retreated about **1,700 m since 1935**.
Earth's **energy imbalance** is at a **65-year peak**.
Sea-level rise comes from **thermal expansion** plus **ice melt**; **Kiribati** and **Tuvalu** are at risk.

na1a73e26976.s: Satellite observations since 1978 show that solar output has:
na1a73e26976.x: Satellites show no net increase in solar output since 1978, so recent warming cannot be explained by a brighter Sun.
xa: **Milankovitch cycles** (orbital factors) drive **ice-age cycles**.
**Volcanoes:** **SO2 + ash** act as **cooling aerosols**.
IPCC **AR6**: warming had already reached **1.1 degC** in **2011-2020**.

n97de2e703ba.s: Which of the following is NOT a direct cause of sea-level rise?
n97de2e703ba.x: Sea-level rise comes from thermal expansion and melting ice; higher snow albedo only reflects more radiation.
xa: **Sea level** is up about **11 cm since 1993**.
Islets **Tebua Tarawa** and **Abanuea** were **submerged in 1999**.
**Kiribati** and **Tuvalu** are at risk.

n79301be6ed3.s: The Little Ice Age is generally placed approximately between:
n79301be6ed3.x: The Little Ice Age is placed approximately in the period 1500–1850.
n79301be6ed3.tq: Use the historical range as the discriminator among overlapping climate periods.
xs: The **Little Ice Age** is placed about **1500-1850** — option **(3)**.
It is listed among the **natural** variations of climate.
xa: **Milankovitch cycles** (eccentricity, obliquity, precession) drive **ice-age cycles**.
**Volcanoes** cool climate through **SO2 + ash** aerosols.
**Continental drift** and **ocean currents** are other natural causes.

n803fef95cd1.s: Volcanic eruptions cause short-term cooling mainly because ____ and ash form aerosols that reflect sunlight.
n803fef95cd1.x: Sulphur dioxide and ash generate cooling aerosols that reflect incoming sunlight.
xa: Its risk is **"termination shock"** — **rapid warming** if injection stops.
Other natural causes: **Milankovitch cycles**, **solar output**, **continental drift**, **ocean currents**.
**Little Ice Age:** about **1500-1850**.

n45bfd9ceb18.s: How many members does the IPCC have?
n45bfd9ceb18.x: The IPCC has 195 members and assesses existing scientific literature rather than conducting its own research.
xa: It shared the **Nobel Peace Prize 2007** with **Al Gore**.
**WG I** physical science basis; **WG II** impacts, adaptation, vulnerability; **WG III** mitigation.
The **AR7** cycle began in **July 2023**.

nf3531be7287.s: The Nobel Peace Prize awarded to the IPCC in 2007 was shared with which of the following persons?
nf3531be7287.x: The IPCC shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore.
nf3531be7287.tq: Test the person-organisation association directly, using nearby climate personalities as distractors.
xs: The IPCC shared the **Nobel Peace Prize 2007** with **Al Gore** — option **(2)**.
The IPCC itself **assesses** literature and does **no research of its own**.
xa: IPCC membership: **195**.
⚠ Do not confuse with the **Nobel Prize in Physics 2021** — **Syukuro Manabe** and **Klaus Hasselmann** for climate modelling.
**AR6 Synthesis Report** came out on **20 March 2023**.

ne95a522e231.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the IPCC Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C (SR1.5)?
o: Global CO2 emissions must fall about 45% from 2010 levels by 2050.
At the current rate, warming is likely to reach 1.5°C between 2030 and 2052.
ne95a522e231.x: SR1.5 says the 45% cut from 2010 levels is needed by 2030; 2050 is the date for net zero.
xa: ⚠ **SR1.5** = 1.5 degC between **2030 and 2052**; **AR6** = breach in the **early 2030s**.
**AR6** says emissions must **peak before 2025**.
**Net zero:** human emissions balanced by **removals** (sinks, capture).

nd1059b4a406.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the IPCC AR6 Synthesis Report?
o: It stated that emissions may peak after 2035 without affecting the mid-century net-zero objective.
It noted that warming during 2011–2020 had reached about 1.1°C.
It indicated that 1.5°C is likely to be breached in the early 2030s.
nd1059b4a406.x: AR6 said emissions must peak before 2025, not after 2035; the other three statements are correct.
xa: ⚠ **SR1.5** (2018) gave **2030-2052** for reaching 1.5 degC; **AR6** gives the **early 2030s**.
**AR7** cycle began **July 2023**.
**AR6** also warns up to **25%** of mountain species face extinction.

n3cd163483d7.s: According to the UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025, current policies would lead to about ____ of warming.
n3cd163483d7.x: Current policies point to about 2.8°C; even full NDC implementation gives about 2.3-2.5°C.
xa: **SR1.5** (**2018**): **1.5 degC** likely between **2030 and 2052**; **net zero around 2050**.
**AR6** (**20 March 2023**): warming already **1.1 degC**; 1.5 degC breach in the **early 2030s**; emissions must **peak before 2025**.
**COP31** meets in **Turkiye** in **November 2026**.

n6bd98e685b8.s: The CMIP7 scenarios drop which worst-case pathway?
n6bd98e685b8.x: CMIP7 drops the worst-case SSP5-8.5 pathway and places the world near 2.8°C by 2100.
xa: **UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025** also projects **~2.8 degC** under current policies.
Full **NDCs** would give **2.3-2.5 degC**.
**COP31:** **Turkiye**, **November 2026**.

ncba7fba5ae7.s: Ocean acidity has increased by about ____ since the Industrial Revolution.
ncba7fba5ae7.x: Ocean acidity has risen about 30% since the Industrial Revolution; AR6 says up to 25% of mountain species may face extinction.
xa: The **1.2 degC** threshold for warm-water reef collapse is **already crossed**.
Warmer, wetter conditions spread **vector-borne diseases** (**malaria, dengue**).
Haryana's trans-Gangetic plains: **buffalo milk yields** hit by warming.

n3a13bc41720.s: Warmer and wetter conditions can widen the geographical range of which category of diseases?
o: Vector-borne diseases such as malaria and dengue
n3a13bc41720.x: Warmer and wetter conditions can expand the range of vectors and thereby increase the spread of malaria and dengue.
xa: India 2025: **4,419 deaths** and **17.4 million ha** of crops damaged by extreme weather.
**Ocean acidity** up **30%** since the Industrial Revolution.
AP angle: **heatwaves** in **Palnadu, Kurnool, Anantapur**.

nccb0546b87d.s: Cirrus cloud thinning is intended to cool the Earth by:
o: Seeding high cirrus clouds so that more outgoing heat escapes
Spraying sea salt into low marine clouds
Making high cirrus clouds thicker so that they reflect more sunlight
Increasing the amount of sulphur dioxide in volcanic plumes
nccb0546b87d.x: Cirrus cloud thinning seeks to reduce the insulating effect of high cirrus clouds and allow more outgoing heat to escape.
nccb0546b87d.tq: Match the geoengineering proposal with the direction of its radiative effect.
xs: **Cirrus cloud thinning** seeds **high cirrus clouds** so they thin out and **more outgoing heat escapes** — option **(1)**.
**Sea-salt spray** into marine clouds is **marine cloud brightening**; adding **SO2** is **stratospheric aerosol injection**.
xa: ⚠ Cirrus thinning works on **outgoing heat**; the other two **reflect sunlight**.
Aerosol injection risks **"termination shock"**.
Marine cloud brightening could weaken a **Super El Nino**, per a study.

nf4970252a97.s: In marine cloud brightening, sea-salt spray mainly acts as:
nf4970252a97.x: Sea-salt spray can act as cloud condensation nuclei, potentially making marine clouds brighter.
xa: **Stratospheric aerosol injection:** **sulphuric-acid aerosols** reflect sunlight; risk of **termination shock**.
**Cirrus cloud thinning:** seeding **high cirrus** so more outgoing heat escapes.

ne1d944a63c6.s: In the context of climate policy, 'net zero' means that:
o: All greenhouse-gas emissions are stopped permanently.
Natural emissions are completely eliminated from the atmosphere.
Human-caused emissions are balanced by removals through sinks or capture.
Only carbon dioxide emissions are reduced to zero without removals.
ne1d944a63c6.x: Net zero is achieved when human-caused emissions are balanced by removals through natural sinks or technological capture, resulting in zero net addition.
ne1d944a63c6.tq: Apply the definition to distinguish net emissions from gross emissions.
xs: **Net zero** means **human-caused emissions** are **balanced by removals** through sinks or capture — option **(3)**.
The net addition to the atmosphere becomes **zero**; emissions need not stop entirely, so (1) is wrong.
xa: **SR1.5:** to limit warming to 1.5 degC, net zero is needed **around 2050**.
**SR1.5:** global CO2 must fall about **45%** from **2010** levels by **2030**.
**AR6:** emissions must **peak before 2025**, with **net zero by mid-century**.

nad3a9ce873a.s: The Nobel Prize in Physics 2021 was awarded in part to which scientists for the physical modelling of Earth's climate?
nad3a9ce873a.x: Syukuro Manabe and Klaus Hasselmann shared the 2021 Physics Nobel (with Giorgio Parisi) for physical modelling of Earth's climate. Al Gore shared the 2007 Peace Prize with the IPCC, and Pachauri chaired the IPCC; Hansen, Mann, Arrhenius and Keeling are climate scientists who did not receive this prize.
xs: **Syukuro Manabe and Klaus Hasselmann** won the **Nobel Prize in Physics 2021** for **physical modelling of Earth's climate** — option **(2)**.
They shared it with **Giorgio Parisi**.
**Al Gore** shared the **Nobel Peace Prize 2007** with the IPCC — a different prize.
xa: The **IPCC** has **195 members** and **assesses** literature.
IPCC **WG I** covers the **physical science basis**.

n97d69b0fd72.s: COP31 is scheduled to meet in which country and month?
n97d69b0fd72.x: COP31 is scheduled to meet in Türkiye in November 2026.
n97d69b0fd72.tq: Combine the host location and month to avoid confusing the event with another climate meeting.
xs: **COP31** meets in **Turkiye** in **November 2026** — option **(2)**.
It is listed as a **current relevance** point for climate change.
xa: **CMIP7** scenarios drop the worst case **SSP5-8.5** and put the world near **2.8 degC by 2100**.
**UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025:** current policies lead to **~2.8 degC**.
**AR7** cycle began **July 2023**.

nb2aee08806f.s: In Andhra Pradesh, Uppada in the Kakinada region is associated with:
nb2aee08806f.x: Uppada is associated with coastal erosion; Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur are linked with heatwaves.
xa: **APSES 2024-25** tracks climate action under **SDG 13**.
India 2025: **4,419 deaths** from extreme weather (WMO 2025).
**India** has warmed about **0.7 degC since 1900**.

nda5f3a1b8c4.s: Which is the correct order of the oceans from largest to smallest by area?
nda5f3a1b8c4.x: The order by area is Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic; the Arctic Ocean is the smallest.
nda5f3a1b8c4.tq: Recall the complete size ranking and use the smallest ocean as a final check.
xs: By area the order is **Pacific > Atlantic > Indian > Southern > Arctic** — option **(1)**.
The **Arctic is the smallest** ocean (APPSC GS 2018); the **Pacific** is the largest.
xa: Oceans cover about **70-71%** of earth's surface (APPSC GS 2019).
Oceans hold about **97%** of earth's water (APPSC GS 2025).
⚠ Deepest points: Pacific = **Mariana**, Indian = **Sunda (Java)**, Atlantic = **Puerto Rico**.

n1e26e8a5185.s: Oceans contain about what share of Earth's water?
n1e26e8a5185.x: Oceans hold about 97% of Earth's water and cover about 70–71% of its surface.
xa: The rest: **ice ~2%**, **usable fresh water ~1%**.
Of fresh water, **groundwater** far exceeds **lakes and rivers**.
Size ranking: **Pacific > Atlantic > Indian > Southern > Arctic**.

nfb397ed1b94.s: Which of the following stores the most fresh water?
nfb397ed1b94.x: Groundwater far exceeds the fresh water stored in lakes and rivers.
xa: Earth's water: **oceans ~97%**, **ice ~2%**, **usable fresh water ~1%**.
Oceans are the **largest part of the hydrosphere**.

n8af736b002f.x: A fathom is a unit of depth equal to 6 feet, or approximately 1.83 metres.
n8af736b002f.tq: Distinguish the exact unit conversion from nearby length values.
xs: One **fathom** = **6 feet** (about **1.83 m**) — option **(3)**.
A fathom is a unit of **depth** (APPSC GS 2019).
xa: ⚠ **Fathom** = depth unit; **Seamount** = does not reach surface; **Guyot** = flat-topped seamount.
**Bathymetry** = measuring ocean depth and mapping the sea floor (APPSC GS 2018).
**Isobaths** join points of **equal depth**.

nc2486877193.s: The ocean's 'twilight zone', at about 200–1,000 m depth, is the:
nc2486877193.x: The mesopelagic zone (about 200-1,000 m) is popularly called the twilight zone.
xa: It drives the **biological carbon pump** (CMLRE report, Aug 2026).
**Pelagic** = open-ocean water column beyond the shelf; **benthic / hadal** = sea floor / trenches.
Deep sea (below **200 m**) is the **oldest and largest biome**.

n9298f220ab0.s: The measurement of ocean depth and the mapping of the sea floor is called:
n9298f220ab0.x: Bathymetry is the measuring of ocean depth and the study and mapping of the sea floor (APPSC GS 2018); hypsometry relates to the share of surface at each height and depth.
xa: **Fathom** = unit of **depth** (APPSC GS 2019).
**Echo sounding / sonar** times a sound pulse to the floor and back.
**CTD sensors** measure conductivity, temperature and depth.

n239726598d7.s: The continental shelf generally extends to a depth of about:
n239726598d7.x: The continental shelf, a gently sloping submerged edge of the continent, reaches about 200 m.
xa: **Continental slope:** ~**200-3,000 m**, with **canyons and trenches**.
**Deep sea plain:** about **3,000-6,000 m**, the flattest surface on earth.
Shelf holds the **richest fishing grounds**, **oil and gas**.

nd0c240d15e1.s: The deepest trench of the Indian Ocean is the:
nd0c240d15e1.x: The Sunda (Java) Trench is the Indian Ocean's deepest trench.
xa: **Diamantina Deep:** south-east Indian Ocean, south-west of Australia.
**Carlsberg Ridge:** Arabian Sea; India sought rights in **2024**.
Polymetallic sulphide licence on the **Indian Ocean Ridge** valid to **Sept 2031**.

nd78df6dd306.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the horizontal distribution of ocean temperature?
o: In the tropics, the western side of an ocean is warmer than the eastern side.
In the tropics, upwelling makes the eastern side of an ocean warmer.
In temperate latitudes, the westerlies make eastern sections warmer, as with the North Atlantic Drift.
In the tropics, trade winds pile warm water westward.
nd78df6dd306.x: In the tropics the western side is the warmer one, as trade winds pile warm water westward; the eastern side is not made warmer.
xa: Both temperate and tropical points were correct in **UPSC 2021**.
NH oceans are **warmer** than SH oceans (more land).
**Annual range** is smaller in the **Pacific** than in the **Atlantic**.

ne8f4376e74c.s: Oceans absorb about what share of the excess heat from current global warming?
ne8f4376e74c.x: Oceans take up more than 90% of the excess heat; ocean heat content reached a record in 2025.
xa: **Marine heatwave:** SST **3-4 deg C** above average for at least **5 days**.
Vertical layers: warm surface layer to **~500 m** → **thermocline** (~**500-1,000 m**) → cold deep layer near **0-4 deg C**.
**CTD sensors** were fitted even to **sharks** in **2026** for hurricane forecasting.

n4d469fcd807.s: Which factor contributes to Northern Hemisphere oceans being warmer than Southern Hemisphere oceans?
o: Lower salinity in the Northern Hemisphere
Greater ocean area in the Northern Hemisphere
Greater land area in the Northern Hemisphere
Absence of ocean currents in the Southern Hemisphere
n4d469fcd807.x: The greater land area of the Northern Hemisphere contributes to its relatively warmer oceans.
xa: **Enclosed tropical seas** are the **warmest**.
⚠ Tropics: **west warmer**; temperate: **east warmer**.
The **annual range** is smaller in the **Pacific** than in the **Atlantic**.

nd32b3b30621.s: Marine water has a salinity of about:
nd32b3b30621.x: Marine water is about 35 ppt; brackish water (5-35 ppt) is less saline.
xa: **Raised by** evaporation + freezing; **lowered by** precipitation, river inflow + ice melt.
Salinity is **highest in the subtropics** (~**20-30 deg**).

naf09e416321.s: The only major port of Andhra Pradesh is:
naf09e416321.x: Visakhapatnam is the only major port on Andhra Pradesh's 1,053 km coast, the third-longest among states.
xa: AP's shelf covers about **33,000 sq km**.
**Mahadevan Canyon** lies **off Visakhapatnam**.
**NIOT** has a **Nellore seafront facility**.

nphysics-19-11.s: SONAR is based primarily on which of the following principles?
o: Reflection of ultrasonic waves and measurement of the time interval
Absorption of infrasonic waves by water
nphysics-19-11.x: SONAR sends ultrasonic pulses, receives their echoes and uses the time interval to find distance. It is reflection, not refraction or interference.
nphysics-19-11.tq: Recall SONAR as echo ranging with ultrasound.
n: SONAR works by reflection of ultrasonic waves. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 76-81]
SONAR measures the time interval between sending and receiving the reflected pulse. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 76-81]
SONAR stands for Sound Navigation And Ranging. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 76-81]
SONAR works on the echo method. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 76-81]
SONAR sends ultrasonic pulses toward an object. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 76-81]
The ultrasonic pulses are reflected by the object. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 76-81]
SONAR uses ultrasound as its wave. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 76-81]
xs: SONAR is based on **reflection of ultrasonic waves and measurement of the time interval** — option **(1)**.
It **sends ultrasonic pulses**, which an object **reflects**; it measures the **time** between **sending and receiving**.
Ultrasound is used for its **high frequency**, **less diffraction** and **greater directionality**.
xa: SONAR = **Sound Navigation And Ranging**.
**Echo sounding:** depth = **speed of sound in water x half** the echo time.
**Bathymetry** = measuring ocean depth and mapping the sea floor (**APPSC GS 2018**).
**Fathom** = unit of **depth** = **6 feet** (**APPSC GS 2019**).

nb321ef9741b.s: Which of the following ocean-floor divisions is usually the deepest?
nb321ef9741b.x: Oceanic deeps are deepest, followed by deep-sea plains, continental slopes and continental shelves.
xa: **Continental rise:** apron of sediment at the foot of the slope.
**Deep sea plain** is the **most extensive part** of the ocean floor.
⚠ **Canyons and trenches** = slope; **volcanoes and earthquakes** = deeps.

n620ca5bfa3e.s: Polymetallic nodules are particularly associated with which part of the ocean floor?
n620ca5bfa3e.x: Polymetallic nodules occur on the deep-sea plains.
n620ca5bfa3e.tq: Link a resource to its characteristic ocean-floor environment.
xs: **Polymetallic nodules** lie on the **deep sea (abyssal) plain** — option **(3)**.
The plain lies at about **3,000-6,000 m** and is the **most extensive part** of the ocean floor.
xa: **Seamounts** carry **cobalt-rich crusts** (LENS Apr 2025).
India holds a **polymetallic sulphide** licence on the **Indian Ocean Ridge** valid to **Sept 2031**.
**Varaha** mining machine trialled at **5,270 m** in the Central Indian Ocean.

n1331d4d416d.s: Most oceanic deeps and trenches are located in the:
n1331d4d416d.x: Oceanic trenches, long and narrow features linked with volcanoes and earthquakes, occur mostly in the Pacific.
xa: Trenches mark **subduction zones**, where one plate dives under another.
**Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep)** is the **deepest point on earth**, about **11 km**.
⚠ **Canyons and trenches** = slope feature in the APPSC G2 2023 match.

nbc0f32fcb54.s: The deep sea below about 200 metres is described as Earth's:
nbc0f32fcb54.x: The deep sea below 200 m is the oldest and largest biome, occupying about 90–95 per cent of Earth's habitable space.
xa: **Mesopelagic ("twilight zone")** lies at **200-1,000 m**.
The **deep sea plain** is the most extensive part of the ocean floor.
**Deep Ocean Mission** surveys found about **39** potentially new species.

n42ce82f3d08.x: Oceanic trenches commonly occur at subduction zones, where one plate descends beneath another.
xa: **Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep)** is the **deepest point on earth**.
Most trenches lie in the **Pacific**.
**Sunda (Java)** is the Indian Ocean's deepest trench.

ne72f3410249.s: Land-derived gravel, sand, silt and mud laid down on the continental shelves and slopes are called:
ne72f3410249.x: Terrigenous deposits come from the land and settle mainly on the shelves and slopes, getting finer away from the shore.
xa: **Pelagic deposits:** deep-sea **oozes** (calcareous, siliceous) + **red clay** on deep-sea plains and deeps.
**Red clay** is the **most widespread deep-sea deposit**, largest in the deep **Pacific**.
**Siliceous ooze** (diatom, radiolarian) forms in colder or deeper water.

na8d1d6d7911.s: The annual range of ocean temperature is generally smaller in the Pacific Ocean than in the Atlantic Ocean because the Pacific is:
o: Deeper only in its eastern part
Located entirely in the Southern Hemisphere
na8d1d6d7911.x: The annual range of ocean temperature is smaller in the vast Pacific than in the Atlantic: a larger, more extensive body of water heats and cools more slowly, so its temperature varies less over the year.
na8d1d6d7911.tq: Test the direct comparison and avoid confusing ocean size with hemispheric location.
xs: The annual temperature range is **smaller in the vast Pacific** than in the **Atlantic** — option **(3) Vast and more extensive**.
Its sheer size makes its temperature vary less over the year.
xa: The **Pacific** is the **largest** ocean: **Pacific > Atlantic > Indian > Southern > Arctic**.
**Northern hemisphere** oceans are warmer than southern (more land).
**Enclosed tropical seas** are warmest.

n87feb00d394.s: A flat-topped seamount whose top was planed by waves before it sank is called a(n):
n87feb00d394.x: A guyot is a flat-topped seamount planed by waves and then sunk; an atoll is a ring-shaped reef around a lagoon.
xa: Atoll examples: **Lakshadweep**, **Maldives**.
**Submarine canyon:** deep valley across shelf and slope — e.g. **Mahadevan Canyon off Visakhapatnam**.
**Deep Ocean Mission** surveys found about **25 seamounts** and **2 active + 2 inactive hydrothermal vents**.
**CMS COP15** declared seamounts **critical habitat**.

nd74263642da.s: An atoll is best described as a:
o: Ring- or horseshoe-shaped coral reef enclosing a central lagoon
Deep gorge cut across the continental slope
Flat-topped submarine mountain formed only by tectonic uplift
Submarine volcanic peak with a pointed summit
nd74263642da.x: An atoll is a ring- or horseshoe-shaped coral reef surrounding a central lagoon. Lakshadweep and Maldives provide examples.
nd74263642da.tq: Apply the characteristic-shape clue to identify the landform.
xs: An **atoll** is a **ring- or horseshoe-shaped coral reef** around a **central lagoon** — option **(1)**.
Examples: **Lakshadweep** and **Maldives**.
A gorge across the slope is a **submarine canyon**; a flat-topped seamount is a **guyot**; a volcanic peak is a **seamount**.
xa: **Guyot:** planed by waves, then sunk.
**Mahadevan Canyon** lies off **Visakhapatnam**.

nb8cf13e26f4.s: The Mahadevan Canyon, mentioned in relation to submarine canyons, is located off the coast of:
nb8cf13e26f4.x: Mahadevan Canyon is a submarine canyon located off Visakhapatnam.
nb8cf13e26f4.tq: Test the location attached to a named geographical feature.
xs: **Mahadevan Canyon** is a submarine canyon **off Visakhapatnam** — option **(2)**.
Submarine canyons are deep, steep-sided valleys across the **shelf and slope**, often off **river mouths**.
xa: Another example: **Hudson Canyon**.
**Visakhapatnam** is AP's only **major port**.
AP's coast is **1,053 km** long, the **3rd longest**.

n56861fc5475.s: The deepest point on Earth, the Challenger Deep, is located in the:
n56861fc5475.x: The Challenger Deep lies in the Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean and is about 11 km deep.
n56861fc5475.tq: Match the superlative with its exact geographical feature.
xs: **Challenger Deep** lies in the **Mariana Trench** — option **(3)**.
It is in the **Pacific**, the **deepest point on earth**, about **11 km**, next to the **Northern Mariana Islands**.
**Tonga** and **Kermadec** are in the south-west Pacific; **Aleutian** in the North Pacific.
xa: Indian Ocean's deepest: **Sunda (Java)**; Atlantic's: **Puerto Rico**.
Trenches mark **subduction zones**.

nbc66e5b6422.s: Which islands rise above parts of the S-shaped Mid-Atlantic Ridge?
nbc66e5b6422.x: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is S-shaped, and Iceland and the Azores rise above parts of it.
xa: **East Pacific Rise:** Pacific.
**Ninety East Ridge:** Indian Ocean, along **90 deg E**.
**Carlsberg Ridge:** north-west Indian Ocean (**Arabian Sea**).

ndd9331287de.s: The Telegraph Plateau is located in the North Atlantic, south of Iceland, and is associated with:
o: The deepest point of the Atlantic Ocean
ndd9331287de.x: The Telegraph Plateau lies south of Iceland in the North Atlantic and was used as a route for transatlantic cables.
ndd9331287de.tq: Link a geographical feature with its distinctive human-use association.
xs: The **Telegraph Plateau** carried the **route of the transatlantic cable** — option **(4)**.
It lies in the **North Atlantic, south of Iceland**.
The Atlantic's deepest point is the **Puerto Rico Trench**, not this plateau.
xa: **Mid-Atlantic Ridge:** S-shaped; **Iceland** and **Azores** rise above it.
**Walvis Ridge:** South Atlantic, off **Namibia**.

n6467ff795e8.s: India's continental shelf is broadest off the coast of:
n6467ff795e8.x: India's shelf is broadest off Gujarat and parts of Maharashtra and relatively narrow along the east coast.
xa: **Mumbai High (Bombay High)** oilfield lies on the wide **western shelf**.
AP's shelf covers about **33,000 sq km**.
AP's **1,053 km** coast (**3rd longest**) fronts the narrow east-coast shelf.

n1e2e75b71ad.s: The Mumbai High oil field is situated on:
o: The continental slope off the Bay of Bengal
n1e2e75b71ad.x: Mumbai High lies on the wide western continental shelf, particularly in the Gujarat-Mumbai sector.
n1e2e75b71ad.tq: Associate the resource location with the correct coastal shelf sector.
xs: **Mumbai High** lies on the **wide western continental shelf** — option **(3)**.
The western shelf is **broadest off Gujarat and part of Maharashtra** (Gujarat-Mumbai).
xa: Shelf resources: **oil and gas** (Bombay High, **KG basin**), placer minerals, fisheries.
The **east coast** shelf is **narrow**.
**40th Amendment, 1976** vests shelf minerals in the **Union**.

nebc7026526c.s: Under the Constitution (Fortieth Amendment) Act, 1976, minerals of the continental shelf and the EEZ are vested in the:
nebc7026526c.x: The Constitution (Fortieth Amendment) Act, 1976 vests minerals of the continental shelf and the EEZ in the Union.
nebc7026526c.tq: Apply the authority-identification method to a constitutional resource provision.
xs: The **Constitution (40th Amendment) Act, 1976** vests minerals of the **continental shelf and EEZ** in the **Union** — option **(3)**.
So neither **State Governments** nor port authorities own them.
xa: **Territorial sea:** **12 nm / 22 km**, largely overlapping the productive shelf.
**2025:** India widened its shelf claim by **~10,000 sq km** in the central Arabian Sea before the **CLCS**.
Data for the claim came from **NCPOR Goa**.

n38b20853329.s: Calcareous ooze is primarily composed of:
o: Fine inorganic clay and volcanic dust alone
Gravel and sand transported from continental rivers
Silica skeletons of diatoms and radiolarians
Lime shells of tiny organisms such as globigerina and pteropods
n38b20853329.x: Calcareous ooze consists mainly of the lime shells of tiny organisms, including globigerina and pteropods.
n38b20853329.tq: Match each ooze type with its distinctive biological composition.
xs: **Calcareous ooze** is made of **lime shells** of tiny organisms such as **globigerina and pteropods** — option **(4)**.
**Silica skeletons** of diatoms and radiolarians form **siliceous ooze**; clay and volcanic dust form **red clay**.
**Gravel and sand** from land are **terrigenous** deposits.
xa: Siliceous ooze forms in **colder or deeper water**.
**Red clay** is largest in the **deep Pacific**.

n1d6fa361418.s: In tropical oceans, the thermocline lies at a depth of about:
n1d6fa361418.x: Tropical oceans have a warm surface layer to about 500 m, a thermocline at about 500-1,000 m and a cold deep layer.
xa: Oceans take up **>90%** of excess heat.
**Marine heatwave:** SST **3-4 deg C** above average for at least **5 days**.
Surface temperature is mainly controlled by **latitude** and **insolation**.

n755aa194ac2.s: Which combination contains only processes that generally increase salinity?
n755aa194ac2.x: Evaporation and freezing increase salinity because they remove freshwater. Precipitation, river inflow and ice melt generally lower salinity.
n755aa194ac2.tq: Classify processes according to whether freshwater is removed or added.
xs: **Evaporation and freezing** raise salinity — option **(4)**.
**Precipitation, river inflow** and **ice melt** lower it, so options (1), (2) and (3) are wrong.
xa: **Currents and winds** redistribute salinity.
Highest in the **subtropics** (~**20-30 deg**); lower at the **rainy equator**.
Marine water **~35 ppt**; brackish **5-35 ppt**.

n7fa4039002a.s: The highest oceanic salinity is generally found in the subtropical belt approximately between:
n7fa4039002a.x: Oceanic salinity is generally highest in the subtropics, around 20°–30° latitude, because of high evaporation and relatively lower rainfall.
n7fa4039002a.tq: Use the latitude range as the decisive geographical clue.
xs: Salinity is **highest in the subtropics**, about **20-30 deg** latitude — option **(4)**.
It is **lower at the rainy equator** (option 2's belt).

xa: An ocean current = a **steady volume of water** moving along a **set path**.
**Trade winds** drive equatorial currents **westward**; **westerlies** drive drifts **eastward**.
**Gyres** form from winds, **Coriolis force** and **land barriers**.

nf6a94217d63.s: Near the equator, solar heating makes ocean water:
o: Expand, creating a slight slope down which water flows
Flow towards the equator from the poles
nf6a94217d63.x: Solar heating expands equatorial water, creating a slight surface slope down which gravity moves water.
xa: **Density differences**: saltier, colder water is **denser → sinks**; lighter water rises → **thermohaline** circulation.
Warm currents move from the **equator towards the poles** along the surface.
**Coriolis force** deflects currents **right in the N hemisphere**, **left in the S**.

nd9122d4168c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about density-driven ocean circulation?
o: Density differences help drive deep thermohaline circulation.
Saltier water is denser than less salty water.
Cold water sinking at the poles moves rapidly towards the equator.
nd9122d4168c.x: Cold water that sinks at the poles moves slowly, not rapidly, towards the equator.
xa: Other drivers: **solar heating, wind, gravity, Coriolis force**.
**Cold currents** move from poles towards the equator, usually along **west coasts**.
**Upwelling** brings **cold, nutrient-rich** water up — e.g. **Peru/Humboldt**, **Somalia/Findlater**.

n5bf5d84baee.s: In low and middle latitudes, warm currents usually flow along the ____ coasts of continents.
n5bf5d84baee.x: In low and middle latitudes warm currents usually run along the eastern coasts of continents.
xa: Cold west-coast currents **chill/dry** coastal lands → **deserts** (Atacama-Humboldt, Namib-Benguela, Sonoran-California).
**North Atlantic Drift** keeps **NW Europe** mild and ports like **Murmansk** ice-free.
Warm + cold meeting points = **fishing grounds** (Grand Banks, Japan).

n9cedb9a0e2d.x: El Nino means 'the Christ child'; it recurs about every 3-7 years.
xa: **La Nina:** **trade winds strengthen**, eastern Pacific cooler, strong upwelling.
**Bjerknes feedback:** weaker easterlies → warm water slides east → trades weaken further.
El Nino: Indian monsoon **delayed, weakened**; **6 of 10** El Nino years brought deficient rain.
**Negative SOI** = El Nino; **positive SOI** = La Nina.

n5c57eabeb94.s: Under the IMD definition, El Nino is declared when the central equatorial Pacific is at least ____ warmer than average for five consecutive overlapping three-month periods.
n5c57eabeb94.x: The IMD criterion is at least 0.5°C; a Super El Nino exceeds +2.0°C.
xa: El Nino recurs about every **3-7 years**.
**Kelvin wave** along the equatorial Pacific = early El Nino signal.

n0d19ece9e4d.s: The SAMUDRA application is operated by:
n0d19ece9e4d.x: INCOIS operates the SAMUDRA app and provides PFZ advisories and marine hazard alerts.
xa: INCOIS runs the **Indian Tsunami Early Warning System (ITEWS)**.
INCOIS set up a second **Coastal Flood Monitoring System** at **Kollam** for **Kallakkadal** forecasts.
⚠ **INCOIS** = Hyderabad (tsunami); **NIOT** = Chennai (OMNI buoys).

n2a7596884ac.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Indian Tsunami Early Warning System (ITEWS)?
o: It uses Bottom Pressure Recorders, tide gauges and a Decision Support System.
It can issue a warning within about 10 minutes.
It is a UNESCO regional tsunami service provider for 25 Indian Ocean countries.
It is operated by NIOT, Chennai.
n2a7596884ac.x: ITEWS is run by INCOIS, Hyderabad; NIOT, Chennai runs the OMNI buoys.
xa: ITEWS monitored **32** major earthquakes in **2025**.
INCOIS also gives **Ocean State Forecast**, **PFZ advisories**, the **SAMUDRA** app.
IMD's 24-h cyclone track error fell **93 → 74 km** (**2013-2022**).

nc41399438fd.s: A 'Super El Nino' is identified when the sea-surface temperature anomaly in the central Pacific is:
nc41399438fd.x: A Super El Nino is associated with a sea-surface temperature anomaly above +2.0°C in the central Pacific.
nc41399438fd.tq: Use the sign and threshold of the anomaly to distinguish an extreme warm event.
xs: A **Super El Nino** has an SST anomaly **above +2.0°C** in the central Pacific — option **(4)**.
The ordinary IMD threshold is only **0.5°C** warmer than average.
xa: **1997**: a strong **positive IOD** saved India from drought despite a **Super El Nino**.
El Nino recurs every **3-7 years**.
**6 of 10** El Nino years brought depressed Indian rainfall.

ndada70b35bb.s: The Equatorial Counter Current is best described as a current that flows:
o: From south to north only in the Indian Ocean
From north to south along the western coasts of continents
From east to west between the polar currents
From west to east between the North and South Equatorial Currents
ndada70b35bb.x: The Equatorial Counter Current flows west to east between the North and South Equatorial Currents. It returns water piled up in the west through the calm doldrums belt.
ndada70b35bb.tq: Identify the current by its position and direction rather than by its name alone.
xs: The **Equatorial Counter Current** flows **west to east** between the **North and South Equatorial Currents** — option **(4)**.
**Trade winds** pile water on the **western side**; it flows back east through the calm **doldrums** belt.
The equatorial currents themselves flow **westward**; west-coast equatorward flows are **cold currents**.
xa: **Trade winds** → equatorial currents westward; **westerlies** → drifts eastward.
North Atlantic gyre: **N. Equatorial - Gulf Stream - N. Atlantic Drift - Canary**.
Gyres run **clockwise** in the Northern Hemisphere, **anticlockwise** in the Southern.

n85deaecbcc9.s: In the Northern Hemisphere, oceanic gyres circulate:
o: Clockwise in summer and anticlockwise in winter
n85deaecbcc9.x: Gyres turn clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and anticlockwise in the Southern Hemisphere.
xa: **North Atlantic gyre:** N. Equatorial – **Gulf Stream** – N. Atlantic Drift – **Canary**.
**South Indian Ocean gyre:** South Equatorial → **Agulhas** → West Wind Drift → **West Australian**.
**Sargasso Sea** = calm centre of the North Atlantic gyre — "**sea without shores**".

n2fec2f1d2e2.s: Which one of the following forms the northern boundary of the Sargasso Sea?
n2fec2f1d2e2.x: The Sargasso Sea is bounded by the North Atlantic Drift in the north, the Gulf Stream in the west, the Canary Current in the east and the North Equatorial Current in the south.
n2fec2f1d2e2.tq: Test one boundary of a current-defined region.
xs: The **North Atlantic Drift** forms the **northern** boundary of the **Sargasso Sea** — option **(4)**.
Other boundaries: **Gulf Stream (W)**, **Canary Current (E)**, **North Equatorial Current (S)**.
xa: The Sargasso Sea is the only sea bounded by **currents, not land** — "sea without shores".
It is the calm centre of the **North Atlantic gyre**; calm, warm, salty, with floating **Sargassum** seaweed.
The **North Atlantic Drift** (Gulf Stream extension) keeps **NW Europe** mild and **Murmansk** ice-free.

n508025e4c27.s: The Sargasso Sea is unusual because it is
o: the only sea bounded by ocean currents rather than land
a sea enclosed entirely by coral reefs
the only sea located in the Southern Hemisphere
n508025e4c27.x: The Sargasso Sea lies in the North Atlantic and is bounded by currents rather than land. It is also calm, warm, salty and rich in floating Sargassum weed.
n508025e4c27.tq: Use the distinctive geographical exception in the definition.
xs: The **Sargasso Sea** is the **only sea bounded by currents rather than land** — option **(2)**.
It lies in the **North Atlantic** (Northern Hemisphere) and is full of floating **Sargassum** seaweed — so options (1) and (4) are wrong.
xa: Boundaries: **Gulf Stream (W)**, **North Atlantic Drift (N)**, **Canary (E)**, **North Equatorial Current (S)**.
It is the calm centre of the **North Atlantic gyre**; calm, **warm, salty**.
Called the **"sea without shores"**.

n424c84d18f8.s: Which of the following is a warm current of the North Pacific?
n424c84d18f8.x: The Kuroshio is a warm North Pacific current; the Humboldt and Falkland are cold southern-hemisphere currents.
xa: **Kuroshio + Oyashio** meet off **Japan** → rich fishing ground.
**Humboldt** → **Atacama** desert and **Peru** upwelling fisheries.
North Pacific gyre: **N. Equatorial - Kuroshio - N. Pacific Drift - California**.
