Intense monsoon rainfall is a trigger for landslides in the Western Ghats and Konkan region. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
Deforestation is a trigger for landslides in the Western Ghats and Konkan region. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
Localised heavy rainfall is a trigger for landslides in the Eastern Ghats. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
Earthquakes are associated with landslides. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
Heavy rainfall is the main trigger for landslides in India. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
xa: Eastern Ghats landslide area: the **Araku region**.
NW Himalaya states: **J&K**, **Himachal Pradesh**, **Uttarakhand**.
Western Ghats: **Kerala**, **Karnataka**, **Maharashtra**, **Goa**, **Nilgiris**.
**Char Dham:** **43 ha** diverted; about **7,000** deodars approved for felling (**23 Jan 2026**).

ndisaster-management-31-5.s: Which of the following is a human cause of avalanches?
ndisaster-management-31-5.x: Skiing and mountaineering (like explosive triggering) are human causes; heavy snowfall and wind loading are natural.
n: Heavy snowfall is a natural cause of avalanches. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
Wind loading is a natural cause of avalanches. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
Skiing is a human or other cause of avalanches. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
Mountaineering is a human or other cause of avalanches. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
Artificial triggering using explosives is a human or other cause of avalanches. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
xa: Other natural causes: **weak snow layers**, **steep slopes** of **30°–45°**, **earthquakes**, **rain falling on snow**.
Other human causes: **road construction**, **deforestation**, **climate change effects**.
**J&K** is the **most affected** avalanche region.

ndisaster-management-31-9.s: Avalanches are commonly triggered on steep slopes of about:
ndisaster-management-31-9.x: Steep slopes of 30°–45° are a natural cause of avalanches, along with weak snow layers, earthquakes, rapid warming and rain on snow.
n: Weak snow layers caused by a temperature gradient are a natural cause of avalanches. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
Steep slopes of 30°–45° are a natural cause of avalanches. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
Earthquakes and seismic activity are natural causes of avalanches. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
A rapid temperature rise is a natural cause of avalanches. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
Rain falling on snow is a natural cause of avalanches. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
xa: Other natural causes: **heavy snowfall**, **wind loading**.
**Human/other causes:** **skiing**, **mountaineering**, **road construction**, **explosives**, **deforestation**.
**Structural** measures: **snow bridges**, **snow nets**, **retaining walls**, **galleries**.

nf927abc8e3e.s: Urban flooding in Vijayawada is associated with the:
nf927abc8e3e.x: Vijayawada's urban flooding is linked to the Budameru rivulet.
xa: Urban flood causes: **unplanned concretisation**, blocked drains, encroached lakes and extreme rainfall.
**AP City Flood Alert** uses satellite **DEM** plus ~**30 years** of Budameru data.
It gives **48-hour rainfall** forecasts and **6-hour flash-flood** warnings.

n6aeaeed5e00.s: Andhra Pradesh's AI-based City Flood Alert platform (July 2026) is to be implemented first in:
n6aeaeed5e00.x: It starts in Vijayawada (using Budameru data) and later covers all ULBs; it was built by RTGS and APSDMA with IIT Gandhinagar.
xa: It uses **satellite DEM** plus about **30 years** of **Budameru** data.
**Vijayawada** floods come from the **Budameru rivulet**; Visakhapatnam and Guntur are other AP flood cities.
Urban floods come under the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs**.

n03d90452781.s: A drought defined by rainfall falling below the long-period average is called:
n03d90452781.x: A rainfall decline below the long-period average defines meteorological drought; ecological drought involves collapsing ecosystem productivity.
xa: **Hydrological** drought: fall in surface and groundwater after prolonged deficiency.
**Agricultural** drought: soil-moisture deficit causing crop failure.
Drought effects include **land degradation**, desertification and **ecosystem damage**.

n6f10a1e45e9.s: Which of the following ocean-atmosphere conditions can trigger drought in India?
n6f10a1e45e9.x: El Nino, along with irregular or delayed monsoon, monsoon breaks and high temperature and evaporation, can trigger drought.
xa: Normal SW-monsoon rainfall: **868.6 mm** (**1971-2020** base).
About **68%** of the cultivable area is drought-vulnerable.
Drought-prone: Western Rajasthan, Kutch-Saurashtra, Marathwada-Vidarbha, interior Karnataka, **Rayalaseema**.

n6cf1a5b47c7.s: The chief cause of tsunamis is:
n6cf1a5b47c7.x: Subduction-related undersea earthquakes are the chief cause; landslides, eruptions and impacts can also generate tsunamis.
xa: Definition: series of waves from **sudden vertical displacement of the ocean floor**.
Most tsunamis affecting India originate in the **Indian Ocean** (**Sumatra-Andaman / Sunda** subduction zone).
The **Makran zone** threatens the **west coast**.

nfc4286bd1ae.s: Which of the following can magnify the coastal-flooding impact of storm surges?
nfc4286bd1ae.x: Sea-level rise magnifies storm-surge impacts and can cause permanent inundation of low-lying land.
xa: Cyclones affect **13 coastal states/UTs** and **84 coastal districts**.
The **east coast** gets far more cyclones than the west.
AP coast: **62+ cyclonic events** in four decades.

n7862b3720c0.s: Besides the Himalaya, the major landslide zone of India is the:
n7862b3720c0.x: The major landslide zones are the Himalaya and the Western Ghats (Kerala, Konkan, Nilgiris), not the Eastern Ghats.
xa: Himalayan landslide states: **J&K, HP, Uttarakhand, NE**.
**GSI** is the nodal agency for landslide studies.
Causes: unregulated construction, **deforestation + road widening**, **cloudbursts and deglaciation**.

nb8e51b1328a.s: Which of the following contributes to the increasing frequency of landslides?
o: Increase in forest cover on slopes
nb8e51b1328a.x: Unregulated construction on unstable slopes increases landslide frequency, along with deforestation, road widening, cloudbursts and deglaciation.
xa: **Char Dham** road widening: **43 ha** diverted, ~**7,000 deodars** approved for felling (**23 Jan 2026**).
**Cloudbursts and deglaciation** also add to landslides.
Nodal agency: **GSI**.

n79277bb5684.s: Apart from accidents at nuclear power plants such as Chernobyl and Fukushima, which of the following is identified as a source of nuclear hazards?
n79277bb5684.x: Nuclear hazards arise from plant accidents and from improper disposal of radioactive waste. Solar panels, check dams and shelter belts carry no radioactive risk.
n79277bb5684.tq: Nuclear hazards = plant accidents + radioactive waste disposal.
xs: Besides plant accidents, **improper disposal of radioactive waste** is a nuclear hazard — option **(1)**.
Solar panels, check dams and shelter belts carry no radioactive risk.
xa: **Chernobyl**: **26 Apr 1986**, Reactor No. 4 explosion.
**Fukushima Daiichi**: **11 Mar 2011**, earthquake-tsunami → meltdowns.
**HSDPR** scheme builds **CBRN** medical management centres.

nf81c7e4cc48.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's notified-disaster list for the 2026-31 award period?
o: Adding heatwaves and lightning raised the list from 12 to 14.
The addition was made on the Fifteenth Finance Commission's recommendation.
Droughts, hailstorms, frost/cold waves and pest attacks are handled by the Agriculture Ministry.
The remaining notified disasters are handled by the Ministry of Home Affairs.
nf81c7e4cc48.x: The addition was made on the Sixteenth Finance Commission's recommendation, not the Fifteenth.
xa: Disaster = **Hazard x Vulnerability**.
India's economic loss from disasters: about **0.4% of GDP** a year (**1990-2024**).
**2025**: **over 4,000 deaths** from climate-induced disasters; heaviest toll in **HP and Uttarakhand**.

ngeneral-geography-11-3.s: A cloudburst has strong potential to cause:
ngeneral-geography-11-3.x: A cloudburst dumps very intense rain on a small area, so runoff surges and causes a flash flood.
n: A cloudburst consists of extremely intense localized rainfall. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
A cloudburst produces very intense rainfall over a small area. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Cloudbursts are highly localized. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Cloudbursts are extremely intense. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Cloudbursts produce rapid runoff. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Cloudbursts have strong flash-flood potential. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
A cloudburst causes flash floods. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
xa: **IMD:** at least **100 mm (10 cm)** in **one hour** over about **20–30 square kilometres**.
Cloudbursts mostly occur at **1,000 to 2,500 metres** in mountains.
Ordinary heavy rainfall may **cover a larger area** and be **prolonged**; its runoff **depends on duration and intensity**.
**Flash flood → Landslide** is the next link in the secondary-hazard chain.

ngeneral-geography-11-21.s: A main danger associated with flash floods is:
ngeneral-geography-11-21.x: Flash floods carry debris and cause landslides, erosion and infrastructure damage.
n: Debris is a main danger associated with flash floods. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Flash floods are associated with landslides. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Flash floods are associated with erosion. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Flash floods are associated with infrastructure damage. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
xa: Flash floods have a **very rapid onset** and a **very short warning time**.
**Triggers:** intense rainfall or a **cloudburst**, **sudden water release**, **steep terrain**.
**Vulnerable:** **mountains**, **steep catchments** and **urban areas**.

ndisaster-management-19-1.s: According to the IMD definition, a cloudburst is:
o: Rainfall of at least 100 mm in one hour over approximately 20–30 sq km
Rainfall of at least 100 mm in three hours over approximately 50–60 sq km
Rainfall of at least 50 mm in one hour over approximately 20–30 sq km
Rainfall of at least 200 mm in one hour over approximately 10–15 sq km
ndisaster-management-19-1.x: The IMD defines a cloudburst as at least 100 mm of rain in one hour over about 20–30 sq km.
ndisaster-management-19-1.tq: Recall the 100 mm per hour rule.
n: The IMD defines a cloudburst as extremely intense rainfall over an area of approximately 20–30 square kilometres. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 45-47]
The IMD definition of a cloudburst requires rainfall of at least 100 mm (10 cm) in one hour. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 45-47]
xs: The IMD defines a cloudburst as at least **100 mm in one hour** over about **20–30 sq km** — option **(1)**.
**100 mm** equals **10 cm**.
xa: Cloudbursts are **highly localised**, **short-duration** events, often with **thunderstorms**.
They mostly occur at **1,000 to 2,500 metres** in **mountainous regions**.
They trigger **flash floods** and **landslides** — the **major secondary hazards**.

ncb499a6a817.s: Cloudbursts mostly occur in mountainous regions at altitudes of:
ncb499a6a817.x: Cloudbursts mostly occur at 1,000 to 2,500 metres; they are rapid-onset events triggering flash floods and landslides.
xa: **IMD:** at least **100 mm** in **one hour** over about **20–30 sq km**.
Cloudbursts are **extremely difficult** to forecast; tools: **Doppler Weather Radar**, **nowcasting**.
**Famous events:** **Leh (2010)**, **Kedarnath (2013)**.

ndisaster-management-19-5.s: Parts of Kerala, Karnataka and Maharashtra are cloudburst-prone because of intense monsoon rain on the ____ side of the Western Ghats.
ndisaster-management-19-5.x: Intense monsoon rain on the windward side of the Western Ghats makes these areas cloudburst-prone.
n: Flood management includes flood forecasting, warnings, and disaster preparedness. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 45-47]
Steep slopes contribute to the vulnerability of the Himalayan region to cloudbursts. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 45-47]
The orographic effect contributes to the vulnerability of the Himalayan region to cloudbursts. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 45-47]
The monsoon contributes to the vulnerability of the Himalayan region to cloudbursts. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 45-47]
The Western Ghats include parts of Kerala, Karnataka, and Maharashtra as areas vulnerable to cloudbursts. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 45-47]
Intense monsoon rainfall on the windward side contributes to the vulnerability of the Western Ghats. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 45-47]
The Himalayan region includes Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, and Sikkim as vulnerable cloudburst-prone areas. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 45-47]
The main cloudburst trigger mechanism is the orographic lifting of moist air. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 45-47]
xa: Plains get cloudbursts **occasionally — rare**, from **localised convection**.
Himalayan cloudburst areas: **Uttarakhand**, **Himachal Pradesh**, **J&K**, **Ladakh**, **Sikkim**.
**Non-structural** flood measures: **flood-proofing**, **flood fighting**, **flood insurance**.

n179d0ede5df.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about avalanche work by DGRE and BRO?
o: DGRE functions under DRDO and does avalanche forecasting, research and hazard mapping.
The BRO builds and maintains roads and protection structures.
The daily winter avalanche warning bulletins are issued by the BRO, not DGRE.
n179d0ede5df.x: DGRE (earlier SASE) itself issues the daily avalanche warning bulletins in winter; the BRO handles roads and protection structures.
xa: DGRE was **earlier known** as the **Snow and Avalanche Study Establishment (SASE)**.
**BRO** constructs and maintains **roads** and installs **protection structures** in avalanche-prone areas.
Nodal ministry for avalanches: **Ministry of Defence**.

ndisaster-management-31-6.s: Which organisation constructs and maintains roads in avalanche-prone areas and installs protection structures?
ndisaster-management-31-6.x: The BRO builds and maintains roads in avalanche zones and installs protection structures such as snow nets and galleries.
n: The Border Roads Organisation (BRO) constructs roads in avalanche-prone areas. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
The Border Roads Organisation maintains roads in avalanche-prone areas. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
The Border Roads Organisation installs protection structures in avalanche-prone areas. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
Snow bridges are structural measures for avalanche management. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
Snow nets are structural measures for avalanche management. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
Retaining walls are structural measures for avalanche management. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
Galleries are structural measures for avalanche management. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
xa: **Non-structural:** **hazard zonation mapping**, **restricted movement**, **training**, **awareness**.
**DGRE** (under **DRDO**) issues **daily avalanche warning bulletins** in **winter**.
**NDMA guidelines:** **risk zonation**, **early warning**, structural and non-structural mitigation.

ndisaster-management-31-17.s: Which of the following is a non-structural measure for avalanche management?
ndisaster-management-31-17.x: Hazard zonation mapping, restricted movement, training and awareness are non-structural; snow nets, bridges and galleries are structural.
n: Hazard zonation mapping is a non-structural measure for avalanche management. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
Restricted movement is a non-structural measure for avalanche management. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
Training is a non-structural measure for avalanche management. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
Awareness is a non-structural measure for avalanche management. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
xa: **Structural:** **snow bridges**, **snow nets**, **retaining walls**, **galleries**.
**BRO** installs **protection structures** in avalanche-prone areas.
**DGRE** undertakes **hazard mapping** and issues **daily warning bulletins**.

na8be4eb3a84.s: An ISRO study attributed the Dharali flash flood (5 August 2025) to the collapse of an ice patch on the:
na8be4eb3a84.x: ISRO linked the Dharali flood to an ice-patch collapse on the Srikanta glacier; the floods diverted the Bhagirathi.
xa: **Mandi (HP)** got nearly **20 times** normal rain in **2025**.
**Kedarnath (June 2013):** a **cloudburst** and a **GLOF** contributed.
**Nepal:** catastrophic GLOF flash floods on **26 Aug 2026**; **26 GLOFs since the 1970s** (UNDP).
Central Himalaya **glacier area** down **>20%** in three decades.

ndisaster-management-11-7.s: The Kedarnath (Uttarakhand) flood caused by a cloudburst and GLOF occurred in:
ndisaster-management-11-7.x: Kedarnath was in 2013; Mumbai's flood was in 2005, Chennai's in 2015 and Kerala's in 2018.
n: Mumbai experienced a major flood in 2005. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
Mumbai received 944 millimetres of rain in 24 hours in 2005. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
Drainage failure was a key cause or impact of the 2005 Mumbai flood. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
Uttarakhand experienced a major flood in 2013. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
The 2013 Uttarakhand flood affected Kedarnath. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
A cloudburst contributed to the 2013 Uttarakhand flood. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
A Glacial Lake Outburst Flood contributed to the 2013 Uttarakhand flood. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
Chennai experienced a major flood in 2015. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
Extreme rain contributed to the 2015 Chennai flood. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
Wetland destruction contributed to the 2015 Chennai flood. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
Kerala experienced a major flood in 2018. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
Heavy rain contributed to the 2018 Kerala flood. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
Dam releases contributed to the 2018 Kerala flood. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
xa: **Bihar 2008:** an **embankment breach** in the **Kosi** region.
**Mumbai** Prep date: **26 July 2005**; **Chennai:** **Dec 2015**.
**Kerala 2018:** **heavy rain** and **dam releases**.
**Kedarnath:** a **cloudburst** and a **GLOF** contributed.

ndisaster-management-11-17.s: The major 2008 Bihar flood in the Kosi region was caused by:
ndisaster-management-11-17.x: Bihar's 2008 flood happened because the Kosi embankment breached.
n: Bihar experienced a major flood in 2008. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
An embankment breach caused the 2008 Bihar flood in the Kosi region. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 27-30]
xa: **Assam** and **Bihar** are the **worst-affected** flood states.
The **Kosi** basin is a **riverine flood** basin with the **Ganga**, **Brahmaputra**, **Godavari**.
Other major floods: **Mumbai 2005**, **Kedarnath 2013**, **Chennai 2015**, **Kerala 2018**.

ndisaster-management-31-1.s: An avalanche is best defined as:
o: Breaking and sliding of rocks only along a fault
Rapid flow of water and silt through a river valley
Rapid flow of snow, ice, and debris down a mountain slope
Sudden movement of molten rock from a volcanic slope
ndisaster-management-31-1.x: An avalanche is a rapid flow of snow, ice and debris down a mountain slope. Option B is a flash flood and option D a lava flow.
ndisaster-management-31-1.tq: Recall the definition of an avalanche.
n: An avalanche is a rapid flow of snow, ice, and debris down a mountain slope. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
xs: An avalanche is a **rapid flow of snow, ice and debris down a mountain slope** — option **(3)**.
It is a **geological** and **snow-related** natural hazard.
xa: In India avalanches occur mainly in the **Himalayan region**, in **high-altitude areas**.
⚠ A **landslide** is the mass movement of **rocks, debris or earth** down slopes or riverbanks.
**Slab avalanche** is the **most dangerous type**.

ndisaster-management-31-4.s: An avalanche in which a large cohesive slab of snow breaks off and slides is a:
ndisaster-management-31-4.x: A slab avalanche is a large cohesive snow slab breaking off; a loose-snow avalanche is a small dry slide.
n: A slab avalanche occurs when a large cohesive slab of snow breaks off and slides. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
A loose snow avalanche, also called a sluff, consists of small slides of dry, powdery snow. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
An ice avalanche involves ice masses from glaciers. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
A rock or debris avalanche consists of a mixture of rock, soil, and snow. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 66-68]
xa: ⚠ The **slab avalanche** is the **most dangerous type**.
**Steep slopes** of **30°–45°** are a natural cause.
**Weak snow layers** form through a **temperature gradient**.

nda13ae83593.s: Which one of the following is NOT a long-term consequence of recurrent droughts?
o: A sustained increase in farm output
nda13ae83593.x: Droughts generally reduce farm output; they contribute to groundwater depletion, land degradation, desertification and distress migration.
nda13ae83593.tq: Identify the reversed trend in a list of long-term consequences.
xs: **A sustained increase in farm output** is not a drought effect — so option **(3)** is correct.
Droughts cause **lower farm output**, not higher.
The real long-term effects are **groundwater depletion**, **land degradation and desertification** and **rural (distress) migration**.
xa: Drought also brings **rural indebtedness** and **ecosystem damage**.
In **Rayalaseema**, **deep borewells** cause severe groundwater depletion.
About **68%** of the cultivable area is drought-vulnerable.

ndisaster-management-8-1.s: Which of the following best defines drought?
o: A prolonged deficiency of rainfall or moisture leading to water scarcity
A permanent change in the course of a river
A sudden excess of rainfall causing widespread flooding
A short-term rise in groundwater levels after rainfall
ndisaster-management-8-1.x: Drought is a long shortage of rain or moisture that leads to water scarcity. A sudden excess of rain is a flood.
n: Drought is a prolonged deficiency of rainfall or moisture leading to water scarcity. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Drought is a serious shortfall in the availability of water. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
xs: Drought is **a prolonged deficiency of rainfall or moisture leading to water scarcity** — option **(1)**.
It is a **serious shortfall** in the **availability of water**.
A **sudden excess of rainfall** causing flooding describes a **flood**, not drought.
xa: Drought is **slow-onset** — a **creeping emergency** or **creeping hazard**.
It mainly affects **agriculture**, **drinking-water supply** and **industry**.
**Normal SW-monsoon rainfall:** **868.6 mm** (**1971-2020** base).
**Drought** nodal ministry: **Agriculture and Farmers Welfare**.

ndisaster-management-8-4.s: Meteorological drought is associated with a rainfall deficiency of at least ____ of the long-period average.
ndisaster-management-8-4.x: Meteorological drought means rain at least 25% below the long-period average.
n: Meteorological drought is indicated by a rainfall deficiency of at least 25% from the long-period average. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Socio-economic drought occurs when demand for water exceeds supply. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Socio-economic drought causes social and economic stress. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
xa: **Agricultural** drought: **soil moisture insufficient** for crop growth.
**Hydrological** drought: depletion of **reservoirs**, **rivers**, **aquifers**.
**Ecological** drought: ecosystem productivity collapses.

nd58902fef7f.s: Which organisation publishes the annual Global Report on Internal Displacement?
nd58902fef7f.x: The Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre, headquartered in Geneva, publishes the annual Global Report on Internal Displacement.
nd58902fef7f.tq: Match the report with its specialised international institution.
xs: The **Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC)**, based in **Geneva**, publishes the annual **Global Report on Internal Displacement** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The IDMC tracks people displaced within their own countries; disasters displace **millions** every year.
xa: **Water-related disasters worldwide (2025):** about **5,000 deaths** and **8 million** displaced.
**Emerging Asia (OECD):** about **100 disasters a year** affecting about **80 million** people.
India's main risk drivers are **floods and storms**.

n0e0e5820f81.s: Unlike tides, tsunamis result mainly from:
o: Gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun
Sudden displacement of the ocean floor
n0e0e5820f81.x: Tsunamis come from sudden displacement of the ocean floor, usually tectonic; tides come mainly from the Moon's and Sun's gravity.
xa: Causes: mainly **undersea earthquakes**, also volcanic eruptions, **submarine landslides** and asteroid impacts.
Deep ocean: speed up to **800 km/h**, height **under 1 m**.
Warning sign: sudden **receding of sea water**.

n06b7d283256.s: In the deep ocean, a tsunami can travel at about:
n06b7d283256.x: Deep-ocean tsunamis travel at about 700-800 km/h with very long wavelength and height usually under 1 m.
xa: Near the coast it causes **massive inundation**.
Warning signs: sudden **receding of sea water**, rapid sea-level rise, earthquake shaking.
**ITWS** warns **25** Indian Ocean countries within **10 minutes**.

n16b17253a6b.s: Tsunamis affecting India mostly originate from which combination of regions?
o: Bering Sea and Gulf of Mexico
n16b17253a6b.x: Most tsunamis affecting India originate in the Indian Ocean, particularly from the Sunda-Andaman subduction zone; the Makran zone poses a threat to India’s west coast.
n16b17253a6b.tq: Start from the sure geographical source and distinguish the eastern and western Indian Ocean threat zones.
xs: Tsunamis affecting India mostly come from the **Sunda-Andaman** and **Makran** subduction zones — so option **(2)** is correct.
Most originate in the **Indian Ocean** (APPSC 2025 key), at the **Sumatra-Andaman (Sunda) subduction zone**.
The **Makran zone** threatens India's **west coast**.
xa: **Andaman & Nicobar** is the **very high** risk zone, being near the Sunda subduction zone.
The **2004** tsunami was triggered by the **Sumatra-Andaman earthquake**, **Mw ~9.1**.
**NIOT Nellore**'s **OMNI buoys** feed the tsunami warning system.

nac8a345d145.s: The term ‘tsunami’ is derived from which combination of Japanese words and meanings?
nac8a345d145.x: In Japanese, ‘tsu’ means harbour and ‘nami’ means wave; hence tsunami literally means ‘harbour wave’.
nac8a345d145.tq: Test the exact meaning of a look-alike term rather than accepting the familiar but incorrect ‘tidal wave’.
xs: **Tsu = harbour, nami = wave** ("harbour wave") — so option **(1)** is correct.
The word is **Japanese**.
xa: A tsunami is a **series of waves** from **sudden vertical displacement of the ocean floor**.
⚠ **Trap:** a tsunami is not a "**tidal wave**" — tides come from **gravitational pull**.
Main cause: **undersea earthquakes** at **subduction zones**.

n6c59c01eb14.s: Which of the following is the correct order of tsunami risk zones from highest to moderate risk in India?
o: Tamil Nadu—Andaman and Nicobar—Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra and Gujarat
Andhra Pradesh and Odisha—Gujarat and Maharashtra—Andaman and Nicobar
Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra and Gujarat—Tamil Nadu—Andaman and Nicobar
Andaman and Nicobar—Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry and Odisha—Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra and Gujarat
n6c59c01eb14.x: Andaman and Nicobar Islands are in the very-high-risk zone; Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry and Odisha are in the high-risk zone; Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra and Gujarat are in the moderate-risk zone.
n6c59c01eb14.tq: Read the risk classification from highest to moderate without reversing the geographical grouping.
xs: The order is **Andaman & Nicobar → TN, AP, Puducherry, Odisha → Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra, Gujarat** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Very high:** **Andaman & Nicobar**, near the **Sunda subduction zone**.
**High:** Tamil Nadu, **Andhra Pradesh**, Puducherry, Odisha; **Moderate:** Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra, Gujarat.
xa: ⚠ Very high risk = **A&N**; worst hit in **2004** = **Tamil Nadu** (**Nagapattinam**).
The **Makran zone** threatens the west coast.
**ITWS** warns **25** Indian Ocean countries within **10 minutes**.

n586bd1d9e38.s: Which was the worst-affected district of Tamil Nadu in the tsunami of 26 December 2004?
n586bd1d9e38.x: Nagapattinam was the worst-affected district in Tamil Nadu in the tsunami triggered by the magnitude 9.1 Sumatra-Andaman earthquake.
xa: **Tamil Nadu** was the **worst-hit state** (APPSC 2025 key).
Also hit: **A&N Islands, Kerala, AP, Puducherry**.
⚠ Very high risk zone = **A&N**, but worst hit in 2004 = **Tamil Nadu**.

n6176b5c7c63.s: Which Indian State was the worst hit by the Indian Ocean tsunami of 26 December 2004?
n6176b5c7c63.x: Tamil Nadu was the worst-hit State, with Nagapattinam the worst-affected district. Andhra Pradesh and Kerala were also hit but less severely; Odisha was not among the main affected areas listed.
xs: **Tamil Nadu** was the worst-hit state in the **26 Dec 2004** tsunami — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Nagapattinam** was the worst district/coast (APPSC 2025 key).
**Andhra Pradesh** and **Kerala** were also hit, along with A&N Islands and Puducherry, but less than Tamil Nadu.
xa: The trigger was the **Sumatra-Andaman earthquake**, **Mw ~9.1**.
⚠ Very high risk zone = **A&N**; worst hit in 2004 = **Tamil Nadu**.
High-risk zone: Tamil Nadu, **Andhra Pradesh**, Puducherry, Odisha.

n6bee5cbac1d.s: Cyclones in India affect 13 coastal States/UTs and how many coastal districts?
n6bee5cbac1d.x: Cyclones affect 13 coastal States/UTs and 84 coastal districts; Andhra Pradesh is identified as the most cyclone-prone state.
xa: AP coast: **62+ cyclonic events** in four decades.
Cyclone/tsunami exposure: ~**5,700 km** of the old **7,516.6 km** coastline.
**Mangroves** buffer storm surges.

na60d9f68a0a.s: The Bhopal gas leak occurred in:
na60d9f68a0a.x: The Bhopal gas leak was in 1984; Chernobyl was on 26 April 1986.
xa: **Nuclear hazards:** plant accidents plus **improper disposal of radioactive waste**.
**HSDPR scheme (2021-26):** **2 tertiary and 10 secondary** CBRN medical management centres.
**NIDM Southern Campus** is at **Kondapalli, AP**.
Nuclear and radiological emergencies come under the **Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)**.

n914d36e370e.x: Disaster = Hazard × Vulnerability, so a hazard with very low vulnerability need not become a major disaster.
xa: India is **2nd most vulnerable** in the **World Risk Index 2025**.
Floods, droughts, cloudbursts = **hydro-meteorological**; tsunamis = **geological** hazards.
India's risk drivers: **floods and storms**.

ngeneral-geography-11-16.s: Besides inundation, coastal flooding commonly causes:
ngeneral-geography-11-16.x: Storm surge, tides or waves on a low coast cause coastal floods, which bring both inundation and salinity.
n: Coastal flooding results from storm surge, tidal action, or wave action affecting a low-lying coast. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Coastal flooding causes inundation. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Coastal flooding causes salinity. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
xa: **Coastal flood → salinity intrusion** (secondary hazard).
A **cyclone** produces a **storm surge**; a **high tide** gives a **higher baseline water level**.
**Sea-level rise** increases coastal exposure; a **low-lying delta** suffers **greater inundation**.

ngeneral-geography-11-9.s: Forests help in flood management by:
ngeneral-geography-11-9.x: Forests increase infiltration and interception; wetlands store water, mangroves buffer coasts and riparian plants hold banks.
n: Wetlands store excess water. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Mangroves buffer coastal hazards. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Forests increase infiltration. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Forests increase interception. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Riparian vegetation stabilises banks. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
xa: **Floodplains** provide **temporary water storage**.
**Urban green infrastructure** increases **infiltration** and reduces **runoff**.
**Mangroves** with shelter belts **buffer storm surges**.

n32b47434223.s: According to the World Risk Index 2025, India is the world's second most vulnerable country after which country?
n32b47434223.x: The World Risk Index 2025 places India as the second most vulnerable country, after the Philippines.
xs: In the **World Risk Index 2025**, India is the **2nd most vulnerable** country, after **the Philippines** — so option **(4)** is correct.
India's risk is dominated by **floods and storms**, while **China and Indonesia** face higher **seismic** risk.
xa: India loses about **0.4% of GDP every year** to disasters (1990-2024).
About **58.6%** of the landmass faces moderate-to-very-high earthquakes; ~**68%** of cultivable area is drought-vulnerable.
Core formula: **Hazard x Vulnerability = Disaster**.

n33daf630c9b.s: India loses about ____ of its GDP every year to disasters (1990-2024).
n33daf630c9b.x: India's disaster losses are about 0.4% of GDP a year, driven mainly by floods and storms.
xa: **2025 toll:** about **331** days of climate impacts and **over 4,000 deaths**; heaviest toll in **HP** and **Uttarakhand**.
**IDMC** (Geneva) publishes the annual **Global Report on Internal Displacement**.
**Emerging Asia (OECD):** about **100** disasters a year affecting about **80 million** people.
**World Risk Index 2025:** India is the **2nd most vulnerable** country, after the **Philippines**.

na20d1346730.s: The remeasurement that produced the revised coastline length was undertaken by the:
o: India Meteorological Department with the Geological Survey of India
National Disaster Management Authority with the Indian Coast Guard
Central Water Commission with the Forest Survey of India
National Hydrographic Office with the Survey of India
na20d1346730.x: The revised coastline was measured by the National Hydrographic Office in association with the Survey of India.
na20d1346730.tq: Identify the correct institutional pair and avoid swapping neighbouring technical agencies.
xs: The coastline was remeasured by the **National Hydrographic Office** with the **Survey of India** — option **(4)**.
It was reported by the **MHA** in **Dec 2024** (remeasurement **2023-24**).
xa: New length **11,098.81 km**, up from **7,516.6 km** (+~**47.7%**) — **only the method changed**, not the land.
**Gujarat** is first (**2,340.62 km**); **Tamil Nadu** second; **AP** third (**1,053.07 km**).
**GSI** is the nodal agency for **landslide** studies — a different body.

n078ab5b2da6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's remeasured coastline (2023-24)?
o: Andhra Pradesh now has the second-longest coastline.
It rose from 7,516.6 km to 11,098.81 km because the measurement method changed.
Gujarat has the longest revised coastline.
Tamil Nadu now has the second-longest coastline.
n078ab5b2da6.x: Under the revised figures Tamil Nadu is second and Andhra Pradesh (1,053.07 km) third.
xa: ⚠ Older notes and **APSDMA's "second"** carry the old ranking.
AP's rank **3** is from **APSES 2024-25**.
Remeasured by the **National Hydrographic Office** with the **Survey of India**; reported by **MHA**, **Dec 2024**.

n59320c577c3.s: India's tsunami warning system can warn 25 Indian Ocean countries within about:
n59320c577c3.x: The system warns 25 Indian Ocean countries within 10 minutes.
xa: **NIOT Nellore's OMNI buoys** feed the tsunami warning system.
Tsunamis mostly originate in the **Indian Ocean** — **Sumatra-Andaman (Sunda)** subduction zone (**APPSC 2025** key).
The **Makran** zone threatens the **west coast**.

ngeneral-geography-11-17.s: Which of the following is characteristic of flash floods?
o: Very rapid onset with short warning time
Slow onset with long warning time
ngeneral-geography-11-17.x: Flash floods start very fast with little warning, triggered by intense rain, cloudbursts, sudden releases or steep terrain.
n: Flash floods have a very rapid onset. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Intense rainfall or a cloudburst can trigger a flash flood. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Sudden water release can trigger a flash flood. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Steep terrain can trigger a flash flood. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
Flash floods have a very short warning time. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
A cloudburst causes flash floods. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 67-72]
xa: Vulnerable: **mountains**, **steep catchments**, **urban areas**.
Main dangers: **high flow velocity** and **debris**.
**IMD** gives **flash-flood guidance** for India and neighbours (**Bangladesh**, **Bhutan**, **Nepal**).

ndisaster-management-29-6.s: The nodal ministry for avalanches in India is the:
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
ndisaster-management-29-6.x: Defence is nodal for avalanches; Earth Sciences for earthquakes, Jal Shakti for floods and Agriculture for drought.
n: The nodal ministry for earthquakes is the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES). [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 63-65]
The nodal ministry for cyclones and tornadoes is the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES). [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 63-65]
The nodal ministry for tsunamis is the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES). [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 63-65]
The nodal ministry for floods is the Ministry of Jal Shakti. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 63-65]
xa: **MoES** with **IMD** handles **cyclone** and **earthquake forecasting**; also **tsunamis**.
**Urban floods** — **Housing and Urban Affairs** (not Jal Shakti).
Avalanche technical agency: **DGRE** (earlier **SASE**) under **DRDO**.

ndisaster-management-29-10.s: Which of the following is the nodal ministry for industrial and chemical disasters?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
ndisaster-management-29-10.x: The Environment, Forest and Climate Change Ministry is nodal for industrial and chemical disasters.
ndisaster-management-29-10.tq: Match each hazard to its ministry.
n: The nodal ministry for industrial and chemical disasters is the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 63-65]
xs: **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** is nodal for **industrial and chemical disasters** — option **(3)**.
**Ministry of Mines** handles **landslides**; **Health and Family Welfare** handles **biological disasters and epidemics**.
**Ministry of Defence** handles **avalanches** and **oil spills**.
xa: **MoEFCC** is also nodal for **forest fires**.
**Bhopal gas leak** — **1984**, **Madhya Pradesh**.
**NIDM Southern Campus (Kondapalli)** prepares safety audits for **chemical corridors** and port clusters.

ndisaster-management-8-9.s: Drought is described as a 'creeping hazard' because it is:
ndisaster-management-8-9.x: Drought is a slow-onset disaster that builds up gradually, hence a creeping hazard.
n: Drought is a slow-onset disaster. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Drought is also called a creeping emergency. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Drought is a slow-onset natural disaster or creeping hazard. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
xa: **Rapid-onset** disasters: **cyclone**, **flood**, **tsunami**.
Long-term effects: **groundwater depletion**, **land degradation**, **distress migration**, rural indebtedness.
**El Nino:** **6 of 10** El Nino years depressed Indian rain.

nd2424d99960.s: The NIDM Southern Campus at Kondapalli is associated with which activity?
o: Conducting crop-weather surveys in drought-prone districts
Forecasting earthquakes in the Eastern Ghats
Preparing safety audits for chemical corridors and port clusters
Monitoring ocean currents in the Bay of Bengal
nd2424d99960.x: The NIDM Southern Campus at Kondapalli, Andhra Pradesh, prepares safety audits for chemical corridors and port clusters.
nd2424d99960.tq: Identify the institution from its specialised function.
xs: **NIDM Southern Campus, Kondapalli (AP)** prepares **safety audits for chemical corridors and port clusters** — option **(3)**.
Ocean monitoring belongs to bodies like **NIOT Nellore** (OMNI buoys), not NIDM.
xa: **HSDPR** (2021-26): **2 tertiary and 10 secondary** CBRN centres.
**Bhopal gas leak** (**1984**) is India's classic industrial disaster.
AP's three hazards: **coastal cyclones, delta floods, Rayalaseema drought**.

n2d16c91849c.s: An earthquake occurring in an uninhabited desert, without causing damage to people or property, is best classified as a:
n2d16c91849c.x: A hazard is a potentially damaging event. It becomes a disaster when it interacts with a vulnerable population or exposed assets.
n2d16c91849c.tq: Apply the hazard–disaster distinction to a concrete situation.
xs: An earthquake in an **empty desert** is a **hazard**, not a disaster — option **(4)**.
A **hazard** is a **potentially damaging event**; it becomes a **disaster** only when it meets a **vulnerable population**.
**Vulnerability** = exposure + inability to cope; **risk** = likelihood of loss — neither describes the event itself.
xa: **Hazard x Vulnerability = Disaster**.
**Sec. 2(d)** of the DM Act: disaster = catastrophe causing substantial loss **beyond the community's coping capacity**.
Earthquakes are a **geological** hazard (with landslides, volcanoes, tsunamis).

necfa4f842ee.s: Under Section 2(d) of the DM Act, 2005, a disaster causes substantial loss beyond the coping capacity of the:
necfa4f842ee.x: Section 2(d) refers to the coping capacity of the affected community, not the State Government.
xa: **Hazard x Vulnerability = Disaster**.
**Vulnerability** = **exposure + inability to cope**.
An **earthquake in an empty desert** is a **hazard**, not a disaster.
**Hazard types:** geological, hydro-meteorological, biological (**epidemics**, **pest attacks**).

nbb4e748cdbc.s: Which of the following was NOT an emphasis of the 2009 National Policy on Disaster Management?
nbb4e748cdbc.x: The 2009 policy emphasised prevention, mitigation, community participation and mainstreaming DRR; exclusive reliance on relief runs against it.
xa: The **DM Act 2005** made the same shift: **from relief-centric to proactive prevention, mitigation and preparedness**.
Criticism: spending is **still relief-centric** rather than mitigation-focused.
**APSDMA** too moved from **relief-centric to mitigation-centric**.

n0cbf3f9d10f.s: The National and State Disaster Mitigation Funds are primarily meant for:
n0cbf3f9d10f.x: The Mitigation Funds are intended for long-term risk reduction and mitigation rather than immediate relief alone.
xa: NDMF is under **s.47**; the funds are **underused**.
**NDMF** projects: **Rs 4,645 crore** for **9** states, including AP.
AP allocated **Rs 521.17 crore** under **SDMF/NDMF**.

n5992c329f1a.s: Hazard-specific plans of the Union ministries are prepared under which Section of the DM Act, 2005?
n5992c329f1a.x: Hazard-specific plans fall under Section 35 and Ministry DM Plans under Section 37; Section 25 concerns the DDMA.
xa: NDMA's **"Resilient India 2047"** (**Jun 2026**) asks Union ministries for these plans.
NDMA (**s.3**) approves the **National Plan**.

n59a1cf95136.s: Under the DM (Amendment) Act, 2025, an Urban Disaster Management Authority is headed by the:
n59a1cf95136.x: A UDMA is headed by the Municipal Commissioner; UDMAs cover Municipal Corporation cities except Delhi and Chandigarh.
xa: The **2025 amendment** gives **statutory status** to the **NCMC** and the **High-Level Committee**.
It creates **national and state disaster databases** for data-driven planning.
It **updates definitions** of **risk** and **resilience**, aligning with **Sendai**.
Prep adds a **mandatory SDRF** in every state.

ne4d3098932f.x: CAP-SACHET is used for early warning dissemination, a preparedness measure like mock drills and stockpiling.
xa: **CAP (Common Alerting Protocol)** integrates **public warnings**.
**Aapda Mitra** community volunteers and the **National School Safety Programme** are preparedness tools.
IMD's **MHEW-DSS** (2024) reaches ~**80%** of the population.

n25ef1f7e2e3.s: Compensation and psychosocial care are measures of which phase of the disaster management cycle?
n25ef1f7e2e3.x: Compensation and psychosocial care are recovery measures; response includes restoring critical services.
xa: Recovery also covers **damage assessment, livelihoods, "Build Back Better"**.
Response is by **NDRF** and the **armed forces**.
Some notes put response under **post-disaster**.

nc7f036a5e1c.s: Landslide Hazard Zonation divides hill areas into homogeneous zones on the basis of:
o: Degree of susceptibility, hazard or risk
nc7f036a5e1c.x: Zoning is based on the degree of susceptibility, hazard or risk; such maps are probabilistic, not certain predictions.
xa: **GSI** is the nodal agency for landslide zonation, susceptibility maps and the **Landslide Atlas**.
GSI's **Bhukosh** portal covers **4.3 lakh sq km** of landslide-susceptibility maps.
**Seismic microzonation** is built into **Smart Cities** and **AMRUT**.

n06f268ce714.s: The State Emergency Operations Centre of Andhra Pradesh is run by:
n06f268ce714.x: APSDMA runs the State Emergency Operations Centre, coordinates districts, operates early warnings and plans restoration.
xa: APSDMA is chaired by the **Chief Minister** under the **AP DM Rules 2007**.
It is the **apex statutory state body** for DM policy and plans.
AP moved from **relief-centric** to **mitigation-centric** DM and is seen as a national leader in DRR.

n16585d9c789.s: Cyclone Michaung (December 2023) made landfall in Andhra Pradesh near:
n16585d9c789.x: Michaung made landfall near Bapatla; Hudhud hit Visakhapatnam in October 2014.
xa: **APSDMA** is chaired by the **Chief Minister** under the **AP DM Rules 2007**.
APSDMA runs the **State Emergency Operations Centre**.
AP cyclone measures: **IMD warnings**, **cyclone shelters**, evacuation, shelter belts and **mangroves**.
**7 cyclone warning centres** include **Visakhapatnam**.

ndisaster-management-2-17.s: Regulating deforestation is a measure of which phase of disaster management?
ndisaster-management-2-17.x: Prevention, which is proactive and long-term, includes controlling deforestation.
n: Prevention includes regulating deforestation. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Prevention is proactive and long-term. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
xa: Prevention, mitigation and preparedness are **pre-disaster** phases.
The post-2005 **three Ps:** **prevention**, **preparedness**, **proofing/mitigation**.
**Mitigation** is the **most cost-effective** phase.

ndisaster-management-2-21.s: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the response phase of disaster management?
ndisaster-management-2-21.x: Response is time-critical; being a long-term activity describes recovery.
n: Response aims to save lives. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Response aims to meet basic needs. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]

ndisaster-management-32-11.s: Loss of mangroves that increases cyclone impact is an example of:

xa: **Economic** examples: **daily wage workers**, **small farmers**, **informal sector workers**.

ndisaster-management-12-1.s: According to the Disaster Management Act, 2005, mitigation refers to measures aimed at:
o: Providing relief only after a disaster has occurred
Reducing the risk, impact or effects of a disaster or threatening disaster situation
Restricting disaster management to structural constructions
ndisaster-management-12-1.x: Under the DM Act, mitigation means measures to reduce the risk, impact or effects of a disaster or threatening disaster. The other options narrow or distort it.
ndisaster-management-12-1.tq: Recall the DM Act's definition of mitigation.
n: Mitigation consists of measures aimed at reducing the risk, impact or effects of a disaster or threatening disaster situation. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 30-32]
The definition of mitigation is provided in the Disaster Management Act, 2005. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 30-32]
xs: Mitigation means measures **reducing the risk, impact or effects of a disaster or threatening disaster situation** — option **(2)**.
It is a **pre-disaster** phase, not relief after a disaster; it includes **non-structural** measures too.
xa: Goal: **reduce vulnerability** and **lessen the impact of hazards**.
The **most cost-effective** phase of the cycle.
**Non-structural mitigation:** **community awareness and education** programmes.

n2779b8d2db9.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a community vulnerability factor?
n2779b8d2db9.x: Kutcha housing, weak health infrastructure and weak early warning increase vulnerability. High crop-insurance coverage tends to reduce vulnerability.
n2779b8d2db9.tq: Reverse the vulnerability indicators and identify the protective condition.
xs: **High crop-insurance coverage** is **not** a vulnerability factor — option **(2)**.
The listed factor is **low** crop-insurance cover; high cover reduces vulnerability.
**Kutcha housing**, **thin health infrastructure** and **weak early warning** are listed factors.
xa: Also listed: **dependence on farm labour**.
Risk **falls** with **coping capacity**.
Biological hazards: **epidemics, pest attacks**.

n8445bc61dfc.s: Scientific flood forecasting in India began in 1958 on the:

xa: **CWC** remains the warning agency for **river floods**.

**1987**: Disaster Management Institute, **Bhopal**, after the gas tragedy.

n21d2c4029af.s: The High Powered Committee on Disaster Management (1999) was chaired by:

ndb57a928f09.s: The Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction covers the period:

**Build Back Better** is part of the **recovery and reconstruction** phase.

n617f2a3c73d.s: The Disaster Management Cell established in the 1990s in response to the UN International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction was placed under the:

nf253643abf2.s: India's first National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) was issued in:

**Sendai goal:** universal access to **multi-hazard early warning by 2030**.

nd2d4212aa86.s: The nodal agency for landslide hazard zonation, susceptibility maps and the Landslide Atlas is:
nd2d4212aa86.x: The Geological Survey of India is the nodal agency for landslide hazard zonation, susceptibility mapping and the Landslide Atlas.
nd2d4212aa86.tq: Match the specialised agency with its technical function.
xs: The **Geological Survey of India (GSI)** is the nodal agency for landslide hazard zonation, susceptibility maps and the **Landslide Atlas**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**NCS** covers earthquakes, **IMD** covers cyclones and rain, and **CWC** covers river floods.
xa: GSI's **Bhukosh** portal hosts landslide-susceptibility maps of **4.3 lakh sq km**, mirrored to NDMA's GIS portal via WMS.
**Landslide Hazard Zonation** divides hill areas into homogeneous zones by susceptibility, hazard or risk; the maps are **probabilistic**.
For glacial lakes, NDMA tested an indigenous **GLOF alert at Sissu, HP**; ISRO made a **Glacial Lake Atlas**.

n7b40a5e9d75.s: Google Earth Engine is particularly useful in disaster management because it:
o: Processes large satellite-image archives for rapid flood mapping
Operates India’s network of cyclone shelters
Issues statutory evacuation orders to district authorities
n7b40a5e9d75.x: Google Earth Engine is a cloud platform that processes extensive satellite-image archives and can support rapid flood mapping.
n7b40a5e9d75.tq: Match the technology with its specific operational use.
xs: **Google Earth Engine** is a cloud platform that **processes large satellite-image archives for rapid flood mapping**, so option **(1)** is correct.
It does not run cyclone shelters, measure earthquake magnitude or issue evacuation orders.
xa: **Remote sensing** gives a fast, synoptic view: inundation mapping, damage assessment, flood-hazard zoning, drought early warning.
**GIS** overlays spatial data; its key use is **hazard mapping**.
**NDEM**, the GIS repository for the whole DM cycle, is maintained by **ISRO**.

nac55ed5d39f.s: In flood management, a Geographic Information System (GIS) mainly helps authorities by:
o: Analysing flood patterns together with topography so that proactive action can be taken
Replacing the need for rainfall data
Issuing compensation cheques to flood victims
nac55ed5d39f.x: GIS stores and overlays spatial data, analysing flood patterns and topography for hazard mapping and proactive action. It is an analysis tool: it does not build embankments, it needs rainfall data rather than replacing it, and it does not pay compensation.
nac55ed5d39f.tq: GIS = overlay flood pattern + topography -> hazard mapping.
xs: GIS **analyses flood patterns together with topography** so authorities can act proactively, so option **(1)** is correct.
GIS is an analysis tool: it does not raise embankments, replace rainfall data or pay compensation.
xa: GIS stores, analyses and **overlays** remote-sensed and spatial data; key use = **hazard mapping** (earthquake, landslide, flood, fire).
**Google Earth Engine** processes satellite archives for **rapid flood mapping**.
River-flood warnings come from the **Central Water Commission**, which began scientific flood forecasting in **1958** on the Yamuna at Delhi.

ndisaster-management-1-4.s: The theme of the High Powered Committee Report was:
ndisaster-management-1-4.x: The HPC theme 'Building a Culture of Prevention' marked a shift from relief to prevention, mitigation and preparedness.

ndisaster-management-1-5.s: The first state in India to establish a dedicated Ministry of Disaster Management was:

**Bhuj earthquake (2001)** influenced institutional reforms.

ne42a80a7263.s: A major institutional gap that can strain the NDRF during simultaneous disasters is that:

n902e617d7dc.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about disaster management funds?

ndisaster-management-24-14.s: The National Disaster Response Fund has its legal basis in which Section of the DM Act, 2005?

ndisaster-management-13-13.s: The National Advisory Committee, which gives expert advice on policies and plans, operates under the:
