ndisaster-management-12-9.s: Mitigation belongs to which phase of the Disaster Management Cycle?
ndisaster-management-12-9.x: The pre-disaster phase is made up of prevention, mitigation and preparedness.
n: Mitigation belongs to the pre-disaster phase of the Disaster Management Cycle. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 30-32]
Prevention, mitigation and preparedness belong to the pre-disaster phase. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 30-32]
xa: Mitigation is the **most cost-effective** phase.
**Paradigm shift:** from **relief-centric** (**3Rs**) to **mitigation-centric**.
**During-disaster** = **response**; **post-disaster** = **recovery**.

ndisaster-management-26-5.s: In GIS applications across the disaster management cycle, evacuation route planning belongs to:
ndisaster-management-26-5.x: Evacuation route planning is preparedness; hazard zonation is prevention and real-time damage assessment is response.
n: GIS is used for hazard zonation mapping during prevention or mitigation. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 57-59]
GIS is used for evacuation route planning during preparedness. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 57-59]
GIS is used for real-time damage assessment during response. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 57-59]
GIS is used for “Build Back Better” planning during recovery or reconstruction. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 57-59]
xa: Preparedness also uses **resource mapping** and **early warning systems**.
Response also uses **search and rescue coordination**, **resource allocation**.
Prevention also uses **vulnerability assessment**, **risk mapping**, **land-use planning**.

nb274c8a2988.s: A sudden recession of the sea, requiring immediate movement inland or uphill, may precede a:
nb274c8a2988.x: A sudden sea recession may precede a tsunami, which is why immediate inland or uphill movement is advised.
xa: Tsunamis are a **geological** hazard, with earthquakes, landslides and volcanoes.
Tsunami warning in India: **INCOIS, Hyderabad** (Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre, **2007**).
**Tsunami escape-route signage** is one of the listed preparedness tools.
Tsunami-ready villages are verified by the **National Tsunami Ready Recognition Board**, chaired by the **Director, INCOIS**.

n2af6837ee0b.s: IMD's Multi-Hazard Early Warning Decision Support System (MHEW-DSS) was launched in 2024 under:
n2af6837ee0b.x: MHEW-DSS is a webGIS platform launched by IMD in 2024 under Mission Mausam, reaching about 80% of the population.
xa: **Cyclone track error** (24 h) fell from **93 to 74 km**; (72 h) from **201 to 153 km**.
**Severe-weather forecasts** improved **40-50%**.
**Hudhud:** Oct **2014**, **Visakhapatnam**.

n4aa36715add.s: The Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre at INCOIS, Hyderabad was established in:
n4aa36715add.x: The ITEWC at INCOIS was set up in 2007 and issues alerts within about 10 minutes.
xa: It serves **25** countries and monitored **32 major earthquakes in 2025**.
The **National Tsunami Ready Recognition Board** is chaired by the **Director, INCOIS**.
⚠ Tsunami = **INCOIS**; landslides = **GSI**; river floods = **CWC**.

n19a61d00121.s: The National Database for Emergency Management (NDEM), a GIS repository for the disaster management cycle, is maintained by:
n19a61d00121.x: NDEM is maintained by ISRO, not IMD.
xa: **Damini App** gives **lightning** alerts.
**Google Earth Engine** processes satellite archives for **rapid flood mapping**.
**ISRO Disaster Management Support Programme** covers floods, cyclones, droughts, forest fires, landslides, earthquakes.
**NADAMS** — **agricultural drought assessment**.

ndisaster-management-2-5.s: Restoring normal life after a disaster is the objective of which phase?
ndisaster-management-2-5.x: Restoring normal life is the goal of recovery; preparation covers warnings, evacuation and emergency resources.
n: Preparation includes warning systems. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Preparation includes evacuation arrangements. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Preparation includes emergency resources. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Preparation includes coordination. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Recovery aims to restore normal life. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
Recovery aims to restore normalcy. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-7]
xa: Preparedness also covers **mock drills**, **stockpiling**, **Aapda Mitra** training, **Emergency Operation Centres**, **contingency plans**.
Preparedness is the **first and critical step**.
Prep early-warning tool: **CAP-SACHET**.

ndisaster-management-3-1.s: The Indian Tsunami Warning Centre (ITEWC) is located in which city?
ndisaster-management-3-1.x: The Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre is at INCOIS, Hyderabad. GSI is in Kolkata, and the NDRF Academy is in Nagpur.
ndisaster-management-3-1.tq: Match each centre to its city.
n: The Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre (ITEWC) is located in Hyderabad. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 7-10]
Hyderabad is the location of the tsunami warning centre operated through INCOIS. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 7-10]
xs: The **Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre (ITEWC)** is in **Hyderabad**, housed in **INCOIS** — option **(4)**.
**Nagpur** has the **NDRF Academy**; **Kolkata** is the **GSI** HQ; **New Delhi** has **NDMA** and **IMD**.
xa: ITEWC was set up in **2007**; it alerts within **10 min** and serves **25** countries.
**INCOIS** also issues **storm-surge** and **high-wave** warnings.
**NRSC** is also in **Hyderabad** — remote-sensing support for disasters.

ndisaster-management-29-4.s: The technical agency for earthquakes in India is the:
ndisaster-management-29-4.x: The National Centre for Seismology (MoES) handles earthquakes; IMD handles cyclones, INCOIS tsunamis and CWC floods.
n: The technical agency for cyclones is the India Meteorological Department (IMD). [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 63-65]
The technical agency for tsunamis is INCOIS (Hyderabad). [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 63-65]
The technical agency for floods is the Central Water Commission (CWC). [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 63-65]
The technical agency for earthquakes is the National Centre for Seismology, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES). [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 63-65]
xa: **GSI** is the agency for **landslides**.
**IndiaQuake** app for earthquakes; **Damini** app for lightning.
NDMA tested an indigenous **GLOF alert at Sissu, HP**.

o: Natural and man-made disasters, including CBRN emergencies
ndisaster-management-15-5.x: The NDRF handles natural disasters, man-made disasters and CBRN emergencies, and also does mountain rescue.
n: NDRF responds to floods. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 37-39]
NDRF responds to earthquakes. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 37-39]
NDRF responds to cyclones. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 37-39]
NDRF responds to building collapses. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 37-39]
NDRF responds to industrial accidents. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 37-39]
NDRF responds to chemical emergencies. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 37-39]
NDRF responds to biological emergencies. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 37-39]
NDRF responds to radiological emergencies. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 37-39]
NDRF responds to nuclear emergencies. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 37-39]
NDRF has flood rescue skills. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 37-39]
NDRF has mountain rescue skills. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 37-39]
xa: Other skills: **Collapsed Structure Search and Rescue (CSSR)**, **Medical First Response**.
It **pre-positions** teams **before disasters**.
It also responds to **landslides** and **avalanches**.

ndisaster-management-14-7.s: Storm surge and high-wave warnings in India are issued by:
ndisaster-management-14-7.x: INCOIS warns of storm surge and high waves; IMD forecasts, tracks and names cyclones.
n: The India Meteorological Department handles cyclone forecasting, tracking, naming, and early warning. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 34-37]
INCOIS provides storm-surge and high-wave warnings. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 34-37]
NDMA provides policy guidelines and overall coordination. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 34-37]
NDRF and SDRF support pre-positioning, evacuation, search, and rescue. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 34-37]
xa: **APSDMA** handles **mitigation and response** in **Andhra Pradesh**.
**7 cyclone warning centres** include **Visakhapatnam**.
**IMD colour code:** **Red** = take action.

nebf59fb7bbe.s: In the colour-coded warning system of the India Meteorological Department, the colour ORANGE indicates:
nebf59fb7bbe.x: Green means all well, yellow means be aware, orange means be prepared and red means take action.
nebf59fb7bbe.tq: Discriminate between closely related warning colours and their meanings.
xs: IMD **Orange** = **"Be prepared"** — option **(3)**.
**Green** = all well; **Yellow** = be aware; **Red** = take action.
xa: IMD runs **7 cyclone warning centres**, including **Visakhapatnam**.
**Damini** app gives **lightning** alerts.
IMD's 24-h cyclone track error fell **93 to 74 km** (**2013-2022**).

na74d31d39b4.s: Which of the following safety actions is NOT correctly recommended?
o: During a flood, avoid walking or driving through flowing water.
During a flood, move to higher ground.
During a cyclone warning, stand under a large tree until the storm passes.
Indoors during an earthquake, drop, cover and hold under a strong table away from windows.
na74d31d39b4.x: During a cyclone one must move to a cyclone shelter or safer building and never stand under trees.
xa: **Tsunami:** move **inland/uphill** immediately if the **sea recedes suddenly**.
Preparedness tools: **mock drills**, **Aapda Mitra** volunteers, **National School Safety Programme**.
**IMD colour code:** **Green** all well, **Yellow** be aware, **Orange** be prepared, **Red** take action.

n564b5980396.s: The Community-Based Disaster Risk Reduction programme through Panchayati Raj Institutions (Rs 507.37 crore) is jointly run by:
o: Ministry of Panchayati Raj and NDMA
Ministry of Rural Development and NIDM
Ministry of Earth Sciences and INCOIS
n564b5980396.x: The CBDRR-through-PRIs programme is run jointly by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj and NDMA, covering 20 States and 81 districts. The other pairs name bodies with different roles: response force, training, and tsunami warning.
n564b5980396.tq: CBDRR via PRIs = MoPR + NDMA; 20 states, 81 districts.
xs: CBDRR through PRIs is jointly run by the **Ministry of Panchayati Raj and NDMA**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**NDRF** is the response force, **NIDM** does training and research, and **INCOIS** gives tsunami warnings: none runs this programme.
xa: Outlay: **Rs 507.37 crore**.
Coverage: **20 states**, **81 districts** (**20 GPs** per district), with **20 model GPs**.
Other community tools: **Aapda Mitra** volunteers, **mock drills**, the **National School Safety Programme**.

n8c0f3663845.s: The Andhra Pradesh Disaster Management Rules under which APSDMA is chaired by the Chief Minister were made in:
n8c0f3663845.x: The Andhra Pradesh Disaster Management Rules were made in 2007.
n8c0f3663845.tq: Separate the State rules year from the Act, policy and plan years.
xs: The **AP DM Rules** were made in **2007**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**2005** is the DM Act, **2009** the National Policy on DM, **2016** the first NDMP.
xa: Under these rules **APSDMA** is chaired by the **Chief Minister**.
APSDMA is the **apex statutory state body** for DM policy and plans.
Under the DM Act, the **SDMA** is set up under **s.14**; its State Executive Committee is under the **Chief Secretary**.

neb6b41bd9a8.s: The Exclusive Economic Zone extends up to how many nautical miles from the baseline?
neb6b41bd9a8.x: The EEZ extends to 200 nautical miles, where the coastal state has sovereign rights over living and non-living resources.
xa: India's EEZ: **~2.37 million sq km** (~**24 lakh sq km**), the world's **18th largest**.
⚠ EEZ gives **sovereign rights** only; full **sovereignty** applies in the **12 nm** territorial sea.
India's **EEZ Rules 2025**: an **Access Pass** is mandatory for mechanised and motorised vessels **>=24 m**.

n7ca1ba0cc18.s: India's domestic law on maritime zones (territorial waters, continental shelf and EEZ) was enacted in:
n7ca1ba0cc18.x: The Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, EEZ and Other Maritime Zones Act was passed in 1976. 1982 and 1994 are when UNCLOS was adopted and came into force; 1956 is unrelated.
xs: India's **Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, EEZ and Other Maritime Zones Act** was passed in **1976**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**1982** and **1994** are when UNCLOS was adopted and came into force.
xa: ⚠ The Indian Act (**1976**) came before UNCLOS (**1982**).
Territorial sea **12 nm**; EEZ **200 nm**.
The **OAMDR Act 2002** (amended **2023**) governs offshore mineral leases.

n5c2b559bfec.s: India's Exclusive Economic Zone, about 2.37 million sq km, is the world's:
n5c2b559bfec.x: India's EEZ of about 2.37 million sq km is the world's 18th largest, much of it added by the Andaman-Nicobar and Lakshadweep islands.
xa: That is about **24 lakh sq km**; older notes also say **2.02 million sq km**.
The **Andaman-Nicobar** and **Lakshadweep** islands add much of it.
GSI has surveyed **3,10,761 sq km** of a **5,89,160 sq km** EEZ target.

nc0f36c5eef9.s: Gas hydrates are best described as:
o: Methane ice occurring in seabed sediments
nc0f36c5eef9.x: Gas hydrates are methane ice deposits occurring in seabed sediments.
nc0f36c5eef9.tq: Distinguish a precise scientific definition from nearby marine substances.
xs: Gas hydrates are **methane ice in seabed sediments**, so option **(3)** is correct.
They are not solid petroleum, frozen seawater or beach salts.
xa: Explored under the **National Gas Hydrate Programme** in the **KG basin, Mahanadi and Andaman**.
Other seabed resources: **nodules** (nickel, copper, cobalt, manganese) and **polymetallic sulphides**.
Oil and gas basins: **Mumbai High**, **Krishna-Godavari**, **Cauvery**, **Gulf of Khambhat**.

n404929dd2aa.s: Chavara, Manavalakurichi and Chatrapur are known for beach placers of:
n404929dd2aa.x: Chavara (Kerala), Manavalakurichi (Tamil Nadu), Chatrapur (Odisha) and the Andhra coast have monazite (thorium) and ilmenite (titanium) beach placers.
xa: **Chavara** = Kerala; **Manavalakurichi** = Tamil Nadu; **Chatrapur** = Odisha.
AP's beach sand minerals lie on the north coast (**Srikakulam-Bhimunipatnam**).
**Heavy minerals**: **16** offshore blocks, handed to **DAE**.

n8a25d0998b7.s: Seabed deposits carrying copper, zinc, lead and iron along with silver, gold and platinum are called:
n8a25d0998b7.x: Polymetallic sulphides carry copper, zinc, lead, iron, silver, gold and platinum; polymetallic nodules contain nickel, copper, cobalt and manganese.
xa: Polymetallic sulphides form at **hydrothermal vents on mid-ocean ridges** and are key for EVs, grids and solar.
**Gas hydrates** = methane ice in seabed sediments.
India's first ISA contract: **polymetallic nodules, Central Indian Ocean Basin** (**2002**).

n6864749eda4.s: India became the first Pioneer Investor in the Central Indian Ocean Basin in:
n6864749eda4.x: India became the first Pioneer Investor in the Central Indian Ocean Basin in 1987.
n6864749eda4.tq: Discriminate between the Pioneer Investor date and later ISA contract dates.
xs: India became the first **Pioneer Investor** in the **Central Indian Ocean Basin** in **1987**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**2002** is the year of India's ISA nodule contract; **1976** is the Maritime Zones Act; **1982** is UNCLOS adoption.
xa: Licences come from the **ISA**, set up under UNCLOS.
Later contracts: sulphides, Central and South West Indian Ridge (**2016**); sulphides, **Carlsberg Ridge** (**15 Sep 2025**).
**Matsya 6000** is designed to dive to **6,000 m** in the Central Indian Ocean.

n7ed94f7fdac.s: The north-west Pacific fishing ground is associated with the meeting of which currents?
n7ed94f7fdac.x: The north-west Pacific fishing ground lies where the Kuroshio and Oyashio meet; the Gulf Stream-Labrador meeting is the Grand Banks.
xa: ⚠ **Grand Banks** = Newfoundland; **Dogger Bank** = North Sea.
The **NE Pacific** ground lies along the **Alaska-British Columbia** coast.
Current mixing gives **plankton-rich** waters.

n532803f34d6.s: Which is the nodal ministry for India's Deep Ocean Mission?
o: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
n532803f34d6.x: The Deep Ocean Mission (approved June 2021, ₹4,077 crore) is run by the Ministry of Earth Sciences, not the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.
xa: It is one of the nine **PM-STIAC** missions.
It has **six** focus areas, including **deep-sea mining** and a **manned submersible**.
**NIOT's Nellore** facility tests **nodule-mining crawlers** and **LTTD desalination**.

n2554a8dae09.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Deep Ocean Mission?
o: It is one of the nine PM-STIAC missions.
Its focus areas include deep-sea mining and a manned submersible.
It excludes ocean energy and freshwater-related activities.
Ocean biodiversity and ocean survey are among its focus areas.
n2554a8dae09.x: Ocean energy and freshwater are also among the mission's focus areas, so saying it excludes them is false; the other three are correct.
xa: The sixth focus area is a **marine biology station**.
Approved **June 2021**, **₹4,077 crore** over **5 years**, under **MoES**.
**NIOT's Nellore** seafront tests **LTTD desalination** and **wave-energy** units.

n32d65d9d897.s: The first tranche of offshore mineral blocks auctioned under a composite licence (November 2024) had how many blocks?
n32d65d9d897.x: The first tranche, auctioned on 28 November 2024 under the OAMDR Act, had 13 offshore blocks offered under a composite licence.
xa: Offshore blocks: lime mud **3**, **heavy minerals 16** (handed to **DAE**), construction sand **9**, polymetallic crust/nodules **7**.
GSI survey: **3,10,761 sq km** covered of a **5,89,160 sq km** EEZ target.

n9acfc0e754c.s: Which of the following is NOT a favourable condition for the development of major fishing grounds?
o: Highly arid interiors with no coastal access
Upwelling and mixing of warm and cold currents
n9acfc0e754c.x: Wide shelves, current mixing, upwelling and indented coasts favour fishing. An arid interior with no coastal access is not a stated favourable condition.
n9acfc0e754c.tq: Find the geographical condition that does not support marine fishing.
xs: **Highly arid interiors with no coastal access** is not a favourable condition, so option **(2)** is the answer.
Favourable conditions: wide shallow **continental shelves**, **mixing of warm and cold currents**, upwelling, and **indented coasts with harbours**.
xa: Also listed: **cool temperate water** and **limited farmland** pushing people to sea.
Fishing-dependent countries: **Norway, Japan, Iceland**.
Major grounds: **Grand Banks**, **Dogger Bank**, **NW Pacific**, **NE Pacific**.

n38eec767c40.s: India is currently described as the world's:
o: third-largest fish producer, after Japan and China
largest fish producer, ahead of China
fourth-largest fish producer, after Norway, China and Japan
n38eec767c40.x: India is the second-largest fish producer after China and contributes approximately 8–9% of global output.
n38eec767c40.tq: Use the ranking comparison directly rather than confusing production with exports.
xs: India is the **2nd-largest fish producer, after China**, so option **(4)** is correct.
India gives ~**8-9%** of global output (about **9%** of aquatic animal production, **2024**).
xa: **Inland fisheries** make up **>75%** of production.
Workforce: **50 lakh+** fishers in **13** maritime States/UTs; women ~**32%**.
Seafood exports: **₹62,408 crore** (FY **2024-25**), led by frozen shrimp to the US and China.

nbdee2d5a91b.s: The annual mechanised fishing ban in India's territorial waters lasts how many days?
nbdee2d5a91b.x: Territorial-water fisheries (0-12 nm) are a State subject, with an annual two-month (61-day) ban on mechanised fishing.
xa: **EEZ Rules 2025:** **Access Pass** mandatory for vessels **>=24 m**, via the **ReALCraft** portal.
**Traditional crafts** are exempt; tuna boats specially allowed.
India has **50 lakh+** fishers across **13** maritime States/UTs.

n4469c4b5113.s: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (2020) comes under which ministry?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
n4469c4b5113.x: PMMSY, the Blue Revolution flagship, is under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying; the Ministry of Earth Sciences runs the Deep Ocean Mission.
xa: PMMSY funds **cold chains, processing, harbours, deep-sea modernisation**.
AP's **10 fishing harbours** (**₹3,699.09 crore**) are under **PMMSY, not Sagarmala**.
Other fisheries instruments: **FIDF** and the **National Marine Fisheries Policy 2017**.

n4a4ba531b06.s: The blue economy is best described as the:
o: Exclusive commercial use of deep-sea minerals
Replacement of all terrestrial economic activities by maritime trade
Use of coastal waters only for naval security
Sustainable use of ocean, coastal and inland waters for growth, jobs and conservation
n4a4ba531b06.x: The blue economy involves sustainable use of ocean, coastal and inland waters to promote economic growth, employment and conservation.
n4a4ba531b06.tq: Choose the definition that includes both development and conservation.
xs: The blue economy is the **sustainable use of ocean, coastal and inland waters for growth, jobs and conservation**, so option **(4)** is correct.
It is not limited to deep-sea minerals or naval security.
xa: Sectors: **fisheries, aquaculture, ports and shipping, marine biotech, coastal tourism, offshore renewable energy, deep-ocean resources, maritime security**.
India's EEZ potential (**2026**): ~**US$24 billion**.
**Draft Blue Economy Policy Framework**: **MoES**, **2021**.

n1463f26e555.s: The Draft Blue Economy Policy Framework was prepared by which ministry in 2021?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
n1463f26e555.x: The Draft Blue Economy Policy Framework, 2021, is associated with the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
n1463f26e555.tq: Apply the wrong-ministry trap carefully and identify the responsible authority.
xs: The **Draft Blue Economy Policy Framework** (**2021**) was prepared by the **Ministry of Earth Sciences**, so option **(4)** is correct.
The Fisheries ministry runs **PMMSY**, not this framework.
xa: MoES is also the nodal ministry for the **Deep Ocean Mission** (June **2021**).
India's EEZ potential (**2026**): ~**US$24 billion**.
A **Centre of Excellence on Blue Economy** is at **Vignan's University, Vadlamudi (Guntur)**.

n20002412dce.s: SAGAR, the Indian Ocean vision articulated by the Prime Minister in 2015, stands for:
o: Sustainable Alliance for Global Aquatic Resources
Security and Governance of All Regional Waters
Strategic Agreement for Governance of Asian Routes
Security and Growth for All in the Region
n20002412dce.x: SAGAR means “Security and Growth for All in the Region.” It was articulated as India's Indian Ocean vision in 2015 at Mauritius.
n20002412dce.tq: Test the exact expansion of an acronym, not a similar-looking phrase.
xs: **SAGAR** = **"Security and Growth for All in the Region"**, so option **(4)** is correct.
It is the PM's **Indian Ocean** vision, set out in **2015** at **Mauritius**.
xa: **Maritime security** is one of the blue-economy sectors.
**Draft Blue Economy Policy Framework**: **MoES**, **2021**.
India's EEZ: **~2.37 million sq km**, the world's **18th largest**.

n44ee8e1acf7.s: Which one of the following is an aquaculture district of Andhra Pradesh?
n44ee8e1acf7.x: West Godavari is among the listed aquaculture districts, along with Eluru, Krishna, Bapatla, Nellore, Konaseema and Kakinada.
n44ee8e1acf7.tq: Use district-resource association to identify the correct location.
xs: **West Godavari** is an AP aquaculture district, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Anantapur, Kurnool and Kadapa** are not in the aqua-district list.
xa: Aqua districts: **West Godavari, Eluru, Krishna, Bapatla, Nellore, Konaseema, Kakinada**.
AP leads India in **aquaculture** and **shrimp exports** (**31%**).
Main species: **Vannamei** shrimp.

n53dfeda6a21.s: The programme under which 10 fishing harbours are under construction in Andhra Pradesh is:
n53dfeda6a21.x: The 10 fishing harbours are being constructed under PMMSY, not Sagarmala.
n53dfeda6a21.tq: Use the programme-name distinction to avoid the famous-scheme trap.
xs: AP's **10 fishing harbours** are being built under **PMMSY (Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana)**, so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ They are **not under Sagarmala**.
xa: Upgrades: **Visakhapatnam** modernisation (**₹178.51 crore**); **Kakinada** upgrade (**₹58.95 crore**).
PMMSY (**2020**) is the **Blue Revolution** flagship.

n7f04fc6e77a.s: The Centre of Excellence on Blue Economy mentioned in connection with Andhra Pradesh is located at:
n7f04fc6e77a.x: The Centre of Excellence on Blue Economy is located at Vignan's University, Vadlamudi, in Guntur.
n7f04fc6e77a.tq: Use the institution-location association and avoid substituting other marine research centres.
xs: The **Centre of Excellence on Blue Economy** is at **Vignan's University, Vadlamudi (Guntur)**, so option **(1)** is correct.
It was set up on **23 Aug 2026**.
xa: **NIOT Nellore** and **CMFRI** centres support marine research in AP.
AP leads India in **aquaculture** and **shrimp exports**.
AP's harbour programme runs under **PMMSY** (**2024-25**).

n25f28816c3c.x: Minerals are abiotic, not biotic; fossil fuels are non-renewable, while forests and fish are renewable.
xa: Biotic = **plants, animals, micro-organisms**; abiotic = land, water, minerals, rocks, metals.
By status of development: **potential, developed, stock, reserve**.
**Overuse** of natural resources leads to **resource depletion**.

n09143fb21d4.s: A resource that exists but cannot be used at present because suitable technology is unavailable is called a:
n09143fb21d4.x: A stock exists but lacks the technology for its use; hydrogen from water is an example.
xa: ⚠ **Stock** = technology lacking; **Reserve** = usable now, kept for the future.
Other development-based types: **potential** and **developed**.
"Exhausted with use" describes **non-renewable** resources, not stock.

nb4f79e3678e.s: Which one of the following is NOT included in the nine-fold land-use classification?
nb4f79e3678e.x: The nine-fold classification includes forests, non-agricultural uses, barren and unculturable land, permanent pastures, miscellaneous tree crops, culturable wasteland, current fallow, other fallow and net sown area. Seasonal plantation reserve is not one of the categories.
nb4f79e3678e.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the standard classification list.
xs: **Seasonal plantation reserve** is not a category, so option **(2)** is the answer.
The nine: **forests; non-agricultural uses; barren and unculturable land; permanent pastures; miscellaneous tree crops; culturable wasteland; current fallow; other fallow; net sown area**.
xa: Current fallow: **up to 1 year**; other fallow: **1-5 years**.
Culturable wasteland: uncultivated **more than 5 years**.
**Punjab and Haryana** have the highest net sown share (over **80%**).

n428f60243fd.s: Which of the following is NOT a commonly identified cause of land degradation?
n428f60243fd.x: Soil erosion, waterlogging, salinisation, nutrient depletion, falling water tables and soil pollution are causes of land degradation. Natural enrichment of soil nutrients is not a degradation cause.
n428f60243fd.tq: Find the option that reverses the process described by the other alternatives.
xs: A **natural increase in soil nutrients** is not a cause of degradation, so option **(3)** is the answer.
Listed causes: **soil erosion, waterlogging, salinisation**, **nutrient depletion**, falling water tables and soil pollution.
xa: These are **mostly human-induced**.
The global response was the **UNCCD** (**1994**).
**Jhum** with shortened fallow cycles causes forest degradation and **soil erosion**.

n708741d12f2.s: India became the first country to sign an International Seabed Authority contract to explore polymetallic sulphides on which feature?
o: Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean
Sunda Trench in the Indian Ocean
Carlsberg Ridge in the Arabian Sea
n708741d12f2.x: India signed the first ISA contract for exploration of polymetallic sulphides on the Carlsberg Ridge in the Arabian Sea.
n708741d12f2.tq: Use the distinctive location–institution association rather than a generic oceanic feature.
xs: India was the **first country** to sign an **ISA** contract for **polymetallic sulphides** on the **Carlsberg Ridge** in the **Arabian Sea** (Sep **2025**), so option **(4)** is correct.
The other features are not named.
xa: Carlsberg deposits are rich in **copper, zinc, lead, iron, silver, gold**.
The **ISA** is **Jamaica-based**, created under **UNCLOS**.
**DR Congo** is the world's leading **cobalt** source.

n215cfb9dd93.s: The Brundtland Commission report 'Our Common Future', which defined sustainable development, was published in:
n215cfb9dd93.x: 'Our Common Future' was published in 1987; 1972 is the year of the Club of Rome's 'Limits to Growth'.
xa: Club of Rome: **1968**; "Limits to Growth": **1972**.
The global response to land degradation was the **UNCCD** (**1994**).
**Overuse** of resources leads to **resource depletion**.

nae1e415eeb4.s: In the nine-fold land-use classification, land left uncultivated for more than 5 years is called:
nae1e415eeb4.x: Culturable wasteland has been uncultivated for over 5 years; other fallow is 1-5 years and current fallow up to 1 year.
xa: ⚠ Fallow ladder: current fallow **up to 1 year** → other fallow **1-5 years** → culturable wasteland **more than 5 years**.
**Net sown area** share is highest in **Punjab and Haryana** (over **80%**).
**Wasteland** = degraded land that can be brought under vegetative cover with reasonable effort.

nd26df3efd85.s: Shifting cultivation in the north-eastern hills is known as:
nd26df3efd85.x: Shifting cultivation in the NE hills is jhum; shorter fallow cycles degrade forests and increase soil erosion.
xa: Jhum is practised on NE hill slopes, e.g. **Arunachal**.
The **Himalaya and NE hills** region has **forests, hydropower, jhum lands**.
**Silviculture** = raising and tending forest trees (regeneration, thinning, rotation).

n6244af07486.s: After ten years, PMKSY interventions had created or restored about how much irrigation potential?
n6244af07486.x: PMKSY created or restored 24.61 million hectares of irrigation potential and benefited about 27 million farmers.
xa: Source: PIB, **3 Jul 2026**.
PMKSY is an umbrella scheme of **2015-16**.
Water demand: about **1,100 BCM/yr**, projected **1,447 BCM by 2050**.

n8c60f37e12d.s: Brick production is chiefly linked to the depletion of:
n8c60f37e12d.x: Brick production removes topsoil; deep bore tubewells deplete groundwater and agricultural expansion destroys biodiversity habitats.
xa: India is the **world's largest groundwater user** (~a **quarter** of global extraction).
Over-exploitation is worst in **Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Delhi**.
Land degradation causes: **soil erosion, waterlogging, salinisation**, nutrient depletion, falling water tables, soil pollution.

ne9357b2592c.s: Which region of India is known as its mineral heartland?
ne9357b2592c.x: The Peninsular plateau is the mineral heartland; the Indo-Gangetic plains are known for alluvium and groundwater, the Himalaya/NE for forests and hydropower, and the Thar for scarce water.
xa: The plateau (Chota Nagpur, Dharwar, Eastern Ghats) gives **iron ore, coal, bauxite, mica**.
**Western Ghats** = evergreen forests, west-flowing rivers.
Thar harvesting: **tanka, kuan, johad**.

n56054beff1a.s: Under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, who has the authority to manage, protect and regenerate community forest resources?
n56054beff1a.x: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 gives Gram Sabhas authority over the management, protection and regeneration of community forest resources.
xa: FRA gives **individual and community titles** to **STs and other traditional forest dwellers**.
**JFM** guidelines (**1990**): village committees share protection and usufruct.
JFM forerunner: **Arabari** (West Bengal, **1972**).

n1b42ec72d15.s: Arabari, the forerunner of Joint Forest Management (1972), is in which State?
n1b42ec72d15.x: Arabari (1972) is in West Bengal; Appiko began in Karnataka's Salkani forest and Chipko in the Himalayas.
xa: **JFM** Central guidelines came in **1990**.
**NFP 1988** formally introduced **JFM**.
**FRA 2006** empowers **Gram Sabhas** over community forests.

n995b8bc7dfe.s: The International Seabed Authority, which grants contracts for deep-sea mineral exploration, is headquartered in:
n995b8bc7dfe.x: The ISA, created under UNCLOS, is based in Jamaica. Geneva hosts bodies such as IDMC, Nairobi hosts UNEP, and Hamburg hosts the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea, a different UNCLOS body.
xs: The **ISA** is based in **Jamaica**, so option **(2)** is correct.
It was created under **UNCLOS** and gives contracts for **deep-sea exploration**.
xa: India signed the first ISA contract for **polymetallic sulphides** on the **Carlsberg Ridge** (Sep **2025**).
Other water bodies: **CWPRS Pune** (**1916**) = hydraulic research; **NABARD** set up the **Watershed Development Fund**.
⚠ **CWC** = surface water; **CGWB** = groundwater.

nfdda2439f6b.s: The Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act was originally enacted in:
nfdda2439f6b.x: The MMDR Act was enacted in 1957.
nfdda2439f6b.tq: Recall the foundational year before testing the later amendments.
xs: The **MMDR Act** was enacted in **1957**, so option **(2)** is correct.
It is the **parent law** for mining.
xa: **2015** amendment: **auction** mandatory; created the **DMF** and the National Mineral Exploration Trust.
**2023** amendment: Centre auctions **critical and strategic minerals**; exploration licence.
**MMDR Amendment Act 2026** passed **14 Aug 2026**.

n422c5dccee5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2015 amendment to the MMDR Act?
o: It funded the District Mineral Foundation entirely from the Consolidated Fund of India.
It created the National Mineral Exploration Trust.
It made auction mandatory for the grant of mineral concessions.
Under it, the District Mineral Foundation gets miners' contributions linked to royalty.
n422c5dccee5.x: The DMF is funded by miners' contributions linked to royalty, not by the Consolidated Fund of India; auction and the NMET were indeed introduced in 2015.
xa: The **DMF** works in **mining-affected districts**.
Parent law: **MMDR Act 1957**.
The **2026** amendment bars States taxing mineral rights except within Central limits.

nd135f4054ed.s: The 2023 amendment to the MMDR Act provided that critical and strategic minerals such as lithium would be:
o: Removed from the scope of mineral legislation
Auctioned by the Centre, with an exploration licence introduced
nd135f4054ed.x: The 2023 amendment provided for central auctions of critical and strategic minerals, including lithium, and introduced an exploration licence.
nd135f4054ed.tq: Identify both linked provisions rather than selecting an option containing only one detail.
xs: The **2023** amendment has **critical and strategic minerals** (lithium etc.) **auctioned by the Centre**, with an **exploration licence introduced**, so option **(2)** is correct.
Districts and private imports have no such role.
xa: The **2015** amendment made **auction** mandatory and created the **DMF**.
Lithium triangle: **Chile, Argentina, Bolivia**.
AP's **Javakula** gold blocks are under **G2-level** exploration before auction.

na720da4bec1.s: Under the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026, States may tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands:
o: Only within limits prescribed by the Centre
na720da4bec1.x: The 2026 amendment bars States from taxing mineral rights or mineral-bearing lands except within limits prescribed by the Centre.
xa: Passed **14 Aug 2026**.
Criticism: **Section 9D** undercuts the **2024 nine-judge SC verdict** (MADA vs SAIL).
⚠ **Entry 50** = mineral rights; **Entry 49** = mineral land (State List).

n2f487b74d74.s: In Mineral Area Development Authority v. SAIL (2024), the Supreme Court held that States can tax mineral rights under which entry of the State List?
n2f487b74d74.x: The nine-judge bench held that States can tax mineral rights under Entry 50 and mineral land under Entry 49, and that royalty is not a tax.
xa: The 2026 Act bars States from taxing mineral rights or mineral-bearing lands except within **Central limits**.
Its **retrospective** clause voids unrecovered State cesses.
**MMDR Act 1957** is the parent law; **2015 amendment** made **auction** mandatory.

n914a114f232.s: Commercial gold mining in Andhra Pradesh began at ____ in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district.
n914a114f232.x: Commercial gold mining in AP began at Jonnagiri, in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district.
xa: Javakula blocks are under **G2-level** exploration before auction (**29 Jun 2026**).
**Ramagiri** revival includes **reprocessing mine waste**.
World gold region: **Witwatersrand**, South Africa.

nb455bf7cb4a.s: The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification was adopted as a global response to land degradation in:
nb455bf7cb4a.x: The UNCCD was adopted in 1994 as an international response to desertification and land degradation.
nb455bf7cb4a.tq: Distinguish the UNCCD year from the nearby 1987 and 1992 environmental milestones.
xs: The **UNCCD** was adopted in **1994** as the global response to land degradation, so option **(3)** is correct.
**1987** is the Brundtland report "Our Common Future".
xa: Club of Rome's **"Limits to Growth"**: **1972**.
Degradation causes: **soil erosion, waterlogging, salinisation**, nutrient depletion.
Wastelands are mapped with **IRS** data (IRS commissioned **1988**).

n35582365a29.s: Kiruna and Gallivare in Swedish Lapland are known for:
n35582365a29.x: Kiruna and Gallivare are known for magnetite iron ore, not gold; they are in Swedish Lapland, not South Africa.
xa: South Africa's gold region is **Witwatersrand ("Rand")**.
**Katanga** (DR Congo) = copper and cobalt.

na5160cc5cd6.s: Project Vault, associated with the United States in the critical-minerals sector, refers to a:
na5160cc5cd6.x: US Project Vault is described as a $12 billion mineral stockpile.
na5160cc5cd6.tq: Match the programme with its sector and monetary scale, avoiding neighbouring technology categories.
xs: **Project Vault** is a US **$12 billion critical-mineral stockpile** (Jun **2026**), so option **(2)** is correct.
It is not about semiconductors, reactors or military networks.
xa: **China** leads refining of **19 of 20** strategic minerals.
**Indonesia** dominates new **nickel** supply.
Top-3 refiners' average share rose to **86%** in **2024**.

n26ba8b976fe.s: At the 18th BRICS Summit held in New Delhi, the Prime Minister cautioned against the weaponisation of which resource?
n26ba8b976fe.x: The warning at the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi concerned the weaponisation of critical minerals.
n26ba8b976fe.tq: Use the summit-resource association to distinguish the correct current-affairs link.
xs: At the **18th BRICS Summit, New Delhi**, the PM warned against weaponising **critical minerals**, so option **(3)** is correct.
xa: Critical minerals: **lithium, cobalt, nickel, graphite, copper, REE**.
**China** leads refining of **19 of 20** strategic minerals.
**Project Vault**: US **USD 12 bn** stockpile.

nworld-geography-4-4.x: Bolivia, Argentina and Chile together form the Lithium Triangle.
n: Indonesia is the world's number-one producer of nickel. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 5-6]
The Democratic Republic of the Congo accounts for more than 70% of global cobalt mine supply. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 5-6]
Bolivia, Argentina, and Chile together form the Lithium Triangle. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 5-6]
Bolivia, Argentina, and Chile have major lithium brine resources. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 5-6]
The Democratic Republic of the Congo is dominant in cobalt reserves and production. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 5-6]
xa: Indonesia supplies **more than half** of global mined nickel.
**China dominates** downstream **cobalt refining**.
**Australia** is the leading **hard-rock lithium** producer.

n3ed201e3828.s: Which country is the world's largest producer of nickel?
n3ed201e3828.x: Indonesia produces over half of the world's mined nickel; the DRC dominates cobalt and South Africa leads in manganese.
xa: **Kalahari Manganese Field** is a major global manganese resource.
Other manganese producers: **Gabon**, **China**, **India**, **Australia**.
Nickel producers: **Philippines**, **Russia**, **New Caledonia**, **Canada**.

nworld-geography-11-23.s: Which country has the world's largest identified lithium resources?
nworld-geography-11-23.x: Bolivia has the largest identified lithium resources. Australia is the largest producer.
n: Bolivia has the world's largest identified lithium resources. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 16-18]
xs: **Bolivia** has the **world's largest identified lithium resources** — option **(2)**.
**Australia** is the **leading hard-rock lithium producer**; **Chile** has **major lithium reserves**.
xa: **Lithium Triangle:** **Bolivia**, **Argentina**, **Chile** — major **brine** resources.
Other lithium producers: **Chile**, **Argentina**, **China**.
**MMDR 2023 amendment:** critical minerals like **lithium** auctioned by the Centre.

n49c0e6173fb.s: Which traditional water-harvesting system consists of tanks collecting glacier melt in Ladakh?
n49c0e6173fb.x: Zing is the Ladakh system of tanks used to collect glacier meltwater.
n49c0e6173fb.tq: Directly distinguish systems by their distinctive physical setting.
xs: **Zing** is the Ladakh system of tanks collecting **glacier melt**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Zabo** = Nagaland; **Kuhl** = HP diversion channels; **Katta** = Karnataka check dams.
xa: ⚠ **Zing** (Ladakh) vs **Zabo** (Nagaland): similar names, different systems.
**Kuhl** also draws water from **glacier streams**.
APPSC asked **Eri, Ahar-pyne and Zabo** directly (**2024**).

n5dd845d7543.s: Zabo, Johad, Phad and Eri are respectively associated with which regions?
o: Nagaland, Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu
Meghalaya, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh
South Bihar, Delhi, Nagaland and Rajasthan
n5dd845d7543.x: Zabo is associated with Nagaland, Johad with Rajasthan, Phad with Maharashtra and Eri with Tamil Nadu.
n5dd845d7543.tq: Begin with the distinctive Zabo–Nagaland pair and match the remaining regional associations.
xs: **Zabo** = Nagaland, **Johad** = Rajasthan, **Phad** = Maharashtra, **Eri** = Tamil Nadu, so option **(1)** is correct.
Zabo: ponds on terraced hill farms; Johad: crescent earthen check dams (Alwar).
Phad: community canal irrigation (**Tapi** basin); Eri: tank cascades.
xa: Johad is also found in **Haryana**.
**Ahar-pyne** = South Bihar; **Zing** = Ladakh; **Kuhl** = HP.
APPSC asked **Eri, Ahar-pyne and Zabo** in **2024**.

naf6bf43c058.s: Ahar-pyne, a traditional flood-water harvesting system, is associated with which region?
naf6bf43c058.x: Ahar-pyne is practised in South Bihar; the ahar is a catchment basin and the pyne is a channel.
naf6bf43c058.tq: Test both the system and its regional setting through a direct association.
xs: **Ahar-pyne** belongs to **South Bihar**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ahar** = catchment basin; **pyne** = channel; it harvests flood water.
**Eri** = Tamil Nadu; **Katta** = Dakshina Kannada; **kuan/kui** = Western Rajasthan.
xa: APPSC asked Ahar-pyne directly in **2024**.
**Tanka** = rooftop cisterns in the Thar.
**Bawari/Baoli** = stepwells in Rajasthan and Delhi.

n6c3b3160024.s: Kuhl, Katta, Bawari or Baoli are respectively associated with which of the following?
o: Diversion channels from glacier streams; temporary check dams; stepwells
Tank cascades; flood basins; rooftop cisterns
Community canals; seepage wells; terraced farm ponds
Glacier tanks; forest-agriculture ponds; tank irrigation
n6c3b3160024.x: Kuhl consists of diversion channels in Himachal Pradesh and Jammu, Katta consists of temporary check dams in Karnataka, and Bawari or Baoli means stepwells in Rajasthan and Delhi.
n6c3b3160024.tq: Identify each system by its engineering form before checking the option sequence.
xs: **Kuhl** = diversion channels from glacier streams; **Katta** = temporary check dams; **Bawari/Baoli** = stepwells, so option **(1)** is correct.
Kuhl is in **Himachal Pradesh** (and Jammu); Katta in **Dakshina Kannada**; Bawari in **Rajasthan, Delhi**.
xa: Tank cascades = **Eri** (TN); rooftop cisterns = **Tanka** (Thar).
Seepage wells = **Kuan/kui** (Western Rajasthan); terraced farm ponds = **Zabo** (Nagaland).
Glacier tanks = **Zing** (Ladakh).

nefadc65c57f.s: Which sequence correctly gives the states in descending order of the number of large dams?
nefadc65c57f.x: Maharashtra has the largest number of large dams, followed by Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat.
nefadc65c57f.tq: Apply a descending-order comparison and check the first-ranked state before the remaining pair.
xs: By number of large dams: **Maharashtra > Madhya Pradesh > Gujarat**, so option **(1)** is correct.
Source: the **National Register of Large Dams**.
xa: **Ukai** (Tapi) is in **Gujarat**; **Indira Sagar** (Narmada) in **MP**.
**Phad** irrigation is in **Maharashtra** (Tapi basin).
ILR flagship link: **Ken-Betwa**, implemented by **NWDA**.

nindian-geography-11-3.s: The Buckingham Canal, a coastal backwater canal of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, runs along which coast?
nindian-geography-11-3.x: The Buckingham Canal lies along the Coromandel Coast in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, which makes it a coastal backwater canal.
n: The Buckingham Canal is associated with the coastal and backwater system. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 34-35]
The Buckingham Canal is located along the Coromandel Coast in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 34-35]
xa: **Farakka Canal** — **Ganga system**, **Murshidabad**.
**Chambal Canal** — **MP** and **Rajasthan**.
**Indira Gandhi Canal** — from **Harike Barrage**.

n3d323728087.s: The Bhakra-Nangal project, benefiting Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh, is on which river?
n3d323728087.x: Bhakra-Nangal is on the Sutlej; Gandhi Sagar is on the Chambal and Indira Sagar on the Narmada.
xa: **Hirakud** = Mahanadi, Odisha.
**Ukai** = Tapi, Gujarat.
**Indira Gandhi Canal** starts at the **Harike barrage** (Sutlej-Beas).

n2e99e88d3b2.s: Rihand Project, also known as Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar, is located in which state and supplies power to which states?
o: Uttar Pradesh; Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh
Madhya Pradesh; Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan
n2e99e88d3b2.x: Rihand Project is in Sonbhadra, Uttar Pradesh, and its power benefits Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.
n2e99e88d3b2.tq: Distinguish the project state from the states receiving its power benefits.
xs: **Rihand** (**Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar**) is in **Uttar Pradesh** (Sonbhadra) and powers **UP and MP**, so option **(1)** is correct.
It is on the **Rihand**, a **Son tributary**.
xa: **Ramganga** (Kalagarh dam, Uttarakhand) irrigates **UP**.
**Indira Sagar** (Narmada) is in MP (**Khandwa**).
**Gandhi Sagar** (Chambal) is in MP, shared with Rajasthan.

n0e9fe556f6a.s: The Godavari-Krishna river transfer in Andhra Pradesh is associated with:
n0e9fe556f6a.x: The Godavari-Krishna transfer is associated with Pattiseema; Kurnool-Cuddapah is a canal project.
xa: **Pattiseema** lift water fed the **Krishna delta** in the **2026** El Nino deficit (**7,158 cusecs**).
**Gandikota** reservoir on the **Pennar** (Telugu Ganga) serves Rayalaseema.
ILR plan: **30 links**, implemented by **NWDA**.

n8c98f68fee8.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a criticism of river interlinking?
o: Climate change may make surplus basins unreliable.
Interlinking guarantees a stable surplus in all monsoon basins.
The concept of surplus and deficit basins may be difficult to sustain.
Monsoons may be unreliable for identifying permanently surplus basins.
n8c98f68fee8.x: River interlinking has been criticised because monsoons and climate change can make supposedly surplus basins unreliable. It does not guarantee a stable surplus in all basins.
n8c98f68fee8.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated criticism by making an absolute guarantee.
xs: "Interlinking **guarantees a stable surplus** in all monsoon basins" is not a criticism, so option **(2)** is the answer.
The criticism is the opposite: **monsoons + climate change** make **"surplus" basins unreliable**, so ILR is called a **flawed paradigm**.
xa: ILR plan: **30 links** (**14 Himalayan, 16 Peninsular**), NWDA.
Flagship link: **Ken-Betwa**.
India's water crisis is "as much **institutional** as hydrological".

ncf1595268cb.s: During the El Niño-related deficit, Pattiseema lift water supported which area?
ncf1595268cb.x: Pattiseema lift water supported the Krishna delta during the El Niño-related deficit.
ncf1595268cb.tq: Match the water-transfer source with the beneficiary delta.
xs: **Pattiseema** lift water fed the **Krishna delta** in the **2026** El Nino deficit, so option **(2)** is correct.
**7,158 cusecs** were released into canals (**10 Aug 2026**).
xa: Pattiseema is the **Godavari-Krishna** transfer.
**Rayalaseema** is served by **Gandikota** reservoir on the **Pennar**.
ILR is implemented nationally by **NWDA**.

nindian-geography-10-1.s: The Tapovan Vishnugad Project is associated with which river and location?
nindian-geography-10-1.x: The Tapovan Vishnugad Project is on the Dhauliganga in Chamoli, Uttarakhand.
nindian-geography-10-1.tq: Recall the river and district of each project.
n: Tapovan Vishnugad is on the Dhauliganga River. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 32-34]
Tapovan Vishnugad is located in Chamoli, Uttarakhand. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 32-34]
xs: The **Tapovan Vishnugad Project** is on the **Dhauliganga** in **Chamoli, Uttarakhand** — option **(2)**.
**Rihand** is at **Sonbhadra (UP)**; **Pamba** at **Pathanamthitta (Kerala)**; **Kishau** on the **Tons** (HP–Uttarakhand).
xa: **Tehri** is on the **Bhagirathi**, **Uttarakhand**.
**Chamoli glacier burst** — **2021**.
**Baglihar** and **Dulhasti** are on the **Chenab** (J&K).

nindian-geography-10-6.s: The Krishna Sagar dam in Karnataka is on which river?
nindian-geography-10-6.x: Krishna Sagar is on the Cauvery in Karnataka, as is Mettur in Tamil Nadu; Sardar Sarovar and Omkareshwar are on the Narmada.
n: Sardar Sarovar is on the Narmada River. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 32-34]
Sardar Sarovar is located in Gujarat. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 32-34]
Omkareshwar is on the Narmada River. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 32-34]
Omkareshwar is located in Khandwa, MP. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 32-34]
Krishna Sagar is on the Cauvery River. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 32-34]
Krishna Sagar is located in Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 32-34]
Mettur is on the Cauvery River. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 32-34]
Mettur is located in Tamil Nadu. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 32-34]
xa: **Indira Sagar** is also on the **Narmada** at **Khandwa**.
**Bargi** — **Narmada**, **MP**.
**Nagarjuna Sagar** — **Krishna**, AP–Telangana region.

nindian-geography-11-1.s: The Indira Gandhi Canal takes Sutlej-Beas water to western Rajasthan from which barrage?
nindian-geography-11-1.x: The Indira Gandhi Canal starts at the Harike Barrage in Punjab; Bhimgoda, Narora and Banbasa are the heads of the Upper Ganga, Lower Ganga and Sharda canals.
n: The Indira Gandhi Canal has Harike Barrage as its source. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 34-35]
The Indira Gandhi Canal is linked to the Sutlej. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 34-35]
The Indira Gandhi Canal is linked to the Beas. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 34-35]
The Indira Gandhi Canal runs from Punjab to Western Rajasthan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 34-35]
The Upper Ganga Canal is associated with the Ganga. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 34-35]
The Upper Ganga Canal has Bhimgoda as its source. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 34-35]
The Upper Ganga Canal is located at Haridwar, Uttarakhand. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 34-35]
The Lower Ganga Canal is associated with the Ganga. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 34-35]

nb16c8933c94.s: The Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP) was formed by merging all of the following EXCEPT:

nf6e50194580.s: Raising and tending forest trees, including regeneration, thinning and rotation, is called:

nd1f236fd9d3.s: India's per-capita water availability, over 5,000 m³ at Independence, is now about:

nda6648c63f4.s: India accounts for about what share of global groundwater extraction?

n067da73544c.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the principal groundwater assessment categories used by the Central Ground Water Board?

na1c06d5a7c8.s: Which agency implements India's Interlinking of Rivers programme?

n4f7c43ab943.s: Under PMKSY, the Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme (AIBP) is meant for:

Faster completion of major and medium irrigation projects
n4f7c43ab943.x: AIBP is for faster completion of major and medium irrigation projects; command area development and RRR of water bodies fall under Har Khet Ko Pani.

**WDC-PMKSY 2.0** is the watershed component for degraded and rain-fed areas.

n36440353ec7.s: The Atal Bhujal Yojana is the first Centrally Sponsored Scheme focused on:

n36440353ec7.x: Atal Bhujal is the first community-led CSS on demand-side groundwater management; Ganga sewage treatment belongs to Namami Gange.

India is the **world's largest groundwater user** (~a quarter of global extraction).

nindian-geography-26-2.s: The tank system for watershed development is particularly associated with which type of region?
nindian-geography-26-2.x: Tank systems for watershed development are typical of semi-arid India, where they store scarce rain.

nworld-geography-18-1.s: Which region contains the world’s largest continuous rainforest?
nworld-geography-18-1.x: The Amazon Basin holds the largest continuous rainforest. The Congo Basin is second.

xs: The **Amazon Basin** has the **world's largest continuous rainforest** — option **(2)**.

xa: Dense forests are mostly **near the equator**.

n4153771cb9a.s: Under the National Forest Policy, 1988, the target of two-thirds area under forest applies to:

**Chipko** = Himalayas; **Appiko** = Karnataka (**1983**).

n3dc68652c02.s: The polymetallic sulphide deposits explored by India on the Carlsberg Ridge are rich in which of the following?

Copper, zinc, lead, iron, silver and gold

n3f4c97905a8.s: The blue colour of sapphire is produced by:
n3f4c97905a8.x: Iron and titanium give sapphire (a corundum) its blue colour; chromium gives ruby its red, and chromium or vanadium gives emerald its green.

nworld-geography-18-16.s: Which forest biome is described as the world’s largest terrestrial biome?

**Amazon Basin** — largest continuous rainforest.

nc70e589676d.s: The share of net sown area in total reporting area is highest in which pair of States?

**NABARD** set up the **Watershed Development Fund**.

n131e697fd1f.s: Which is the correct descending order of continents by area?
