The **Strait of Malacca** is the **world's busiest commercial strait**.

nindian-geography-25-17.s: The Strait of Hormuz links the Persian Gulf with the:
nindian-geography-25-17.x: Hormuz links the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.
n: The Bering Strait is located between Asia and North America. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 84-85]
The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 84-85]
The Strait of Dover connects the English Channel and the North Sea. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 84-85]
The 10° Channel is located in the Bay of Bengal and Andaman Sea region. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 84-85]
xa: About **20%** of **global oil trade** passes through **Hormuz**, between **Iran** and **Oman**.
The **10° Channel** separates the **Andaman group** from the **Nicobar group**.
The **Nine Degree Channel** separates **Minicoy** from main **Lakshadweep**.

n1b1f805bf10.s: The latitudinal extent of the present State of Andhra Pradesh is approximately:
n1b1f805bf10.x: The latitudinal extent of present-day Andhra Pradesh is approximately 12°41′ N to 19°07′ N. An extent reaching 22° N is not applicable to the present State of Andhra Pradesh.
n1b1f805bf10.tq: Check the precise latitude limits and reject the broader, outdated-looking range.
xs: Present AP lies between **12 deg 41' N and 19 deg 07' N**, so option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Some older notes say up to **22 deg N**; that is wrong for present AP.
xa: AP lies wholly **south of the Tropic of Cancer**.
The **Tropic of Cancer** roughly halves India.
AP area: about **1,62,970 sq km** (~**4.96%** of India), **7th** by area.

n2956a963ec4.s: Which water bodies separate India from Sri Lanka?
o: Gulf of Mannar and Ten Degree Channel
Eight Degree Channel and Gulf of Mannar
Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar
Gulf of Khambhat and Palk Strait
n2956a963ec4.x: The Palk Strait and the Gulf of Mannar separate India from Sri Lanka.
n2956a963ec4.tq: Distinguish the Sri Lanka water bodies from the channels around Lakshadweep and Andaman.
xs: India and Sri Lanka are separated by the **Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar**, so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Ten Degree** and **Eight Degree** channels are in the A&N and Lakshadweep areas.
xa: Asked in APPSC-GS **2025**.
Sea neighbours: **Sri Lanka** and **Maldives**.
The **Eight Degree Channel** separates **Minicoy** from the **Maldives**.

n3ba64b9ef49.s: Among the southern States, which one borders the maximum number of other States?
n3ba64b9ef49.x: Karnataka borders Goa, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala, the maximum among the southern States.
n3ba64b9ef49.tq: Count the adjoining States rather than relying on the State's geographical size.
xs: **Karnataka** borders the most states in the south, so option **(3)** is correct.
It borders **Goa, Maharashtra, Telangana, AP, TN, Kerala**.
xa: Asked in APPSC-G1 **2023**.
AP borders **Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu**.
**Mahe** (Puducherry) lies within **Kerala**.

nindian-geography-15-1.s: The Gulf of Mannar is located between which of the following?
o: South-west India and the Arabian Peninsula
India and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
nindian-geography-15-1.x: The Gulf of Mannar lies between south-east India and Sri Lanka, south of the Palk Strait.
nindian-geography-15-1.tq: Recall the location of each water body.
n: The Gulf of Mannar lies between south-east India and Sri Lanka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 46-49]
xs: The **Gulf of Mannar** lies **between south-east India and Sri Lanka** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Kerala** lies near **Lakshadweep** (**Malabar Coast**), and the **Andaman Sea** lies east of the **A&N Islands** — not the Gulf of Mannar.
xa: India and Sri Lanka are separated by the **Palk Strait** and the **Gulf of Mannar**.
The **Palk Strait** is shallow and has **Adam's Bridge** (**Ram Setu**).
**Sri Lanka** and **Maldives** are India's **sea neighbours**.

n054e878626d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the dimensions of the Himalayas?
o: They narrow to about 200 km in Arunachal Pradesh.
They extend about 2,414 km from Nanga Parbat to Namcha Barwa.
They are about 500 km wide in Kashmir.
They cover an area of about 15 lakh sq km.
n054e878626d.x: The Himalayas cover about 5 lakh sq km, not 15 lakh sq km.
xa: IYB 2026 gives the length as "about **2,400 km**", depth **240-320 km**.
The Himalayas are **wider in Kashmir**, **narrower in the North-East**; folds of Himadri are **asymmetrical**.
Uplift ran through the **Tertiary** (**Eocene to Pliocene**, ~**60-7 million years ago**).
**Western end** = **Nanga Parbat**; **eastern end** = **Namcha Barwa**.

n72fdf15eb59.s: The steep slope of the Himalayas faces:
n72fdf15eb59.x: The Himadri has asymmetrical folds: the steep slope faces the plains and the gentler slope faces Tibet.
xa: The **Himadri core** is **granite**.
APPSC-G1 2024 key: the Himalayas are **wider in Kashmir**, **narrower in the North-East**.
**Himadri** is the **loftiest and oldest** Himalayan range, averaging **over 6,000 m**.

ne550a1dd670.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the three longitudinal parallel ranges of the Himalayas?
ne550a1dd670.x: The three principal longitudinal parallel ranges are Himadri or Greater Himalaya, Himachal or Lesser Himalaya and Shiwalik or Outer Himalaya.
ne550a1dd670.tq: Separate the longitudinal-range classification from the regional west-to-east classification.
xs: The three longitudinal parallel ranges are **Himadri, Himachal and Shiwalik** — option **(3)**.
**Himadri** = Greater, **Himachal** = Lesser, **Shiwalik** = Outer Himalaya.
**Punjab, Kumaon, Nepal** (and Assam) are **regional** divisions; **Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar** are **Trans-Himalayan** ranges.
xa: **Northernmost** of the three = **Himadri**, not the Shiwalik (APPSC-GS 2025).
**Himadri**: loftiest and oldest, average **over 6,000 m**.
**Shiwalik**: youngest and narrowest, width **15-50 km**, average **1,300 m**.
**Purvanchal** is one of the **3** northern mountain groups, not a parallel range.

nafd5b8d1db3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the parallel ranges of the Himalayas?
o: The Karakoram is part of the Trans-Himalaya.
The Kashmir Valley separates the Zaskar from the Pir Panjal.
The Zaskar Range lies south of the Karakoram.
The Ladakh Range continues eastwards into Tibet as the Zaskar Range.
nafd5b8d1db3.x: The Ladakh Range continues into Tibet as the Kailash Range, not the Zaskar; the other three statements are correct.
xa: Karakoram glaciers: **Siachen, Rimo, Baltoro**.
The **Trans-Himalayas** were formed **before** the Himalayas.
**Ladakh Plateau** is the **highest plateau** in India.

n8266272b146.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Himalayan ranges?
o: The Himadri is the loftiest and oldest range, with a granite core.
The Shiwalik is the youngest and narrowest range.
The Shiwalik averages about 1,300 m in height.
The Shiwalik is the northernmost of the three parallel ranges.
n8266272b146.x: The Himadri is the northernmost of the three; the Shiwalik is the outermost (southernmost) range.
xa: **Shiwalik** width: **15-50 km**; simple **'Jura'-type folds** of river deposits.
**Himadri** averages **over 6,000 m**; its folds are **asymmetrical**.
⚠ **Nanda Devi** and **Trisul** belong to the **Greater Himalaya**, not the Middle Himalaya.

n4eaf0c8238a.s: Which of the following ranges belongs to the Himachal (Lesser) Himalaya?
n4eaf0c8238a.x: The Pir Panjal is a major Lesser Himalayan range, about 300 km long in the Jhelum-Beas sector.
xa: Other Himachal ranges: **Dhauladhar**, **Mussoorie**, **Mahabharat**.
Pir Panjal passes: **Banihal** (**2,833 m**, Jammu-Srinagar) and **Rohtang** (**3,978 m**, Kullu-Lahaul-Spiti).
The **Kashmir Valley** separates **Pir Panjal** from the **Zaskar**.

n8c0f7597570.s: Which is regarded as the highest plateau in India?
n8c0f7597570.x: The Ladakh Plateau of the Trans-Himalaya, which formed before the Himalayas, is the highest plateau in India.
xa: The Trans-Himalaya is also called the **Tibetan Himalaya**.
**K2** (Godwin Austen) in the Karakoram is the **2nd highest** peak in the world.
The **Ladakh** range continues into Tibet as the **Kailash** range.

n6ecf0e62d62.s: Nanda Devi belongs to which Himalayan range?
n6ecf0e62d62.x: Nanda Devi belongs to the Greater Himalaya (Himadri), not the Middle Himalaya as some notes wrongly place it.
xa: **Trisul** is also a **Greater Himalaya** peak, often wrongly put in the Middle Himalaya.
**Nanda Devi** = highest peak **wholly in India**; **Kanchenjunga** = highest in India.
**Kailash** lies in the **Trans-Himalaya**, Tibet.

nf4698b1df6d.s: After the knee-bend near Namcha Barwa and the Dihang gorge, the Himalayas turn south as the:
nf4698b1df6d.x: Beyond the Dihang gorge the Himalayas turn south as the Purvanchal hills, generally 500-3,000 m high.
xa: **Garo-Khasi-Jaintia** and **Naga** hills run **east-west**; **Mizo** and **Rakhine** run **north-south**.
**Barail** (Assam) links the Naga and Mizo hills.
Purvanchal is one of the **3** northern mountain groups.

nf16c239118f.s: Debris from which Himalayan system helped build the Indo-Gangetic Plain?
nf16c239118f.x: Debris through the Shiwalik system helped form the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
xa: **Plains** form about **43%** of India's area.
Western end **Nanga Parbat**; eastern end **Namcha Barwa**.
**Himadri** is oldest and loftiest vs **Shiwalik** youngest and narrowest.

nd0b650a2624.s: In the standard (Burrard) division, the Kumaon Himalaya lies between which rivers?
nd0b650a2624.x: The Kumaon Himalaya lies between the Sutlej and Kali; Punjab is Indus-Sutlej, Nepal is Kali-Teesta and Assam is Teesta-Dihang.
xa: Punjab Himalaya peaks: **Nanga Parbat, Rakaposhi, Haramosh**; mainly **sedimentary** rocks.
Kumaon: **Nanda Devi, Trisul, Panchchuli**; lakes **Nainital, Bhimtal**.
Nepal Himalaya: **Everest, Kanchenjunga, Dhaulagiri**.
Assam Himalaya ends at the **Namcha Barwa** knee-bend.

na28a03cc8e1.s: The Punjab Himalaya is chiefly associated with which of the following groups of peaks?
na28a03cc8e1.x: Nanga Parbat, Rakaposhi and Haramosh are prominent peaks of the Punjab or Kashmir-Himachal Himalaya.
na28a03cc8e1.tq: Use the regional-division cluster to associate each division with its characteristic peaks.
xs: The Punjab Himalaya holds **Nanga Parbat, Rakaposhi and Haramosh** — option **(3)**.
**Nanda Devi, Trisul, Panchchuli** are **Kumaon** peaks; **Everest, Kanchenjunga, Dhaulagiri** are **Nepal** Himalaya peaks.
**Namcha Barwa** is Assam Himalaya; **Kailash** is Trans-Himalaya.
xa: Punjab Himalaya lies between the **Indus and Sutlej**; mainly **sedimentary** rocks.
**Nanga Parbat** (PoK) marks the **western end** of the Himalayas.
⚠ Some notes end the Punjab Himalaya at the **Beas**; standard = **Sutlej**.

n3e70aaccb07.s: Near Namcha Barwa, the Himalaya takes a sharp knee-bend at the:
n3e70aaccb07.x: The Himalaya bends at the Dihang gorge near Namcha Barwa and turns south as the Purvanchal hills.
xa: Purvanchal heights range **500-3,000 m**.
The **Assam Himalaya** spans **Teesta-Dihang (Brahmaputra)**.
**Namcha Barwa** (Tibet, China) is the **eastern end** of the Himalayas.

nindian-geography-12-5.s: Which of the following Himalayan peaks lies farthest east?
nindian-geography-12-5.x: From east to west the order is Namcha Barwa, Kanchenjunga, Everest and Nanda Devi.
n: The east-to-west Himalayan peak order is Namcha Barwa, Kanchenjunga, Mount Everest, and Nanda Devi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
Kanchenjunga is located in Sikkim and Nepal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
Nanda Devi is located in Uttarakhand. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
Mount Everest is located in Nepal and Tibet. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
Namcha Barwa is located in Tibet. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
Mount Everest is located in Nepal and China’s Tibet region. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
Kanchenjunga is located in Sikkim and Nepal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
xa: ⚠ **Kanchenjunga** = highest in India; **Nanda Devi** = highest **wholly** in India.
**Nanga Parbat** marks the **western end**.
⚠ **Nanda Devi** and **Trisul** belong to the **Greater Himalaya**, not the Middle Himalaya.

n7ac24c44b50.s: The highest peak lying wholly within India is:
n7ac24c44b50.x: Kanchenjunga is India's highest peak but lies on the India-Nepal boundary; the highest wholly in India is Nanda Devi.
xa: ⚠ Highest **wholly in India** = **Nanda Devi** (Uttarakhand).
**K2** (Godwin Austen) is the **2nd highest** in the world.
Highest range of Assam: **Barail**.

n5667ddb0dbb.s: Godwin Austen (K2), the world's second-highest peak (8,611 m), belongs to which range?
n5667ddb0dbb.x: K2 (8,611 m) belongs to the Karakoram and lies in territory under Pakistan-China control.
xa: The **Karakoram** is a **Trans-Himalayan** range with the **Siachen, Rimo, Baltoro** glaciers.
**Kanchenjunga** = highest in India; **Nanda Devi** = highest wholly in India.
**Ladakh Plateau** is the highest plateau in India.

nindian-geography-13-19.x: The Brahmaputra enters India near Yang Yap in Arunachal Pradesh.
n: The Brahmaputra enters India near Yang Yap. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
xa: Other Arunachal passes: **Bomdila**, **Bum La**, **Diphu**, **Pangsau**.
The Himalaya bends at the **Dihang gorge** near **Namcha Barwa** and turns south as **Purvanchal**.
The **Assam Himalaya** lies between the **Teesta** and the **Dihang (Brahmaputra)**.

nworld-geography-12-5.s: K2 (8,611 m) lies in which mountain range?
nworld-geography-12-5.x: K2 is in the Karakoram on the Pakistan-China border.
n: Mount Everest is the highest peak of the Himalayas. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
Mount Everest is 8,849 m high. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
K2 is 8,611 m high. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
K2 is located in the Karakoram range. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
K2 is located on the Pakistan–China border. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
Kangchenjunga is 8,586 m high. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
Kangchenjunga is located in the Himalayas. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
Kangchenjunga is located on the India–Nepal border. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
Lhotse is 8,516 m high. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
Lhotse is located in the Himalayas. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
Lhotse is located on the Nepal–China border. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 18-20]
xa: K2 is also called **Godwin Austen** — **2nd highest in the world**.
**Lhotse** and **Makalu** both lie on the **Nepal–China** border.
**Siachen**, **Rimo** and **Baltoro** glaciers lie in the **Karakoram**.

na43e5511ea3.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of avalanche-prone Himalayan passes?
o: Zoji La, Khardung La, Rohtang and Mana
Banihal, Shipki La, Nathu La and Bomdi La
Lipulekh, Banihal, Zoji La and Shipki La
Rohtang, Nathu La, Bomdi La and Lipulekh
na43e5511ea3.x: Zoji La, Khardung La, Rohtang and Mana are identified as avalanche-prone passes.
na43e5511ea3.tq: Identify the complete group rather than selecting a familiar individual pass.
xs: The avalanche-prone passes are **Zoji La, Khardung La, Rohtang and Mana** — option **(1)**.
Each other group mixes in passes like **Banihal**, **Nathu La**, **Bomdi La** or **Lipulekh** that are not on this list.
xa: **Rohtang** (HP, **3,978 m**) is crossed by the **Atal Tunnel**.
**Nathu La** (Sikkim) links **Gangtok** with Tibet via the **Chumbi valley**.
**Lipulekh** (Uttarakhand) is on the **Kailash-Mansarovar** route.

nindian-geography-13-11.s: Mana Pass connects which of the following?
nindian-geography-13-11.x: Mana Pass, north of Badrinath in Chamoli district, links Uttarakhand with Tibet. Nathu La and Jelep La link Sikkim with Lhasa, and Pangsau leads to Myanmar.
nindian-geography-13-11.tq: Place the pass on the map, then name what lies across it.
n: Mana Pass is associated with India and Tibet. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
xs: **Mana Pass** connects **India (Uttarakhand) and Tibet** — so option **(4)** **Uttarakhand–Tibet** is correct.
**Jelep La** connects **Eastern Sikkim and Lhasa**; **Diphu La** and **Pangsau** lie on the **India-Myanmar border**.
xa: **Niti Pass** is also on the **Uttarakhand-Tibet route**.
**Lipulekh** (**Pithoragarh**) is on the **Kailash-Mansarovar route**.
**Mana** is one of the **avalanche-prone passes**.

nindian-geography-13-14.s: Diphu La and Pangsau passes lie on India's border with:
nindian-geography-13-14.x: Both Diphu La and Pangsau are on the India-Myanmar border.
n: Diphu La is on the India-Myanmar border. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
Pangsau is on the India-Myanmar border. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
xa: Both lie in **Arunachal Pradesh**.
**Tuju** (Manipur) is on the **Imphal-Tamu/Myanmar route**.
**Bum La** (**Tawang**) is on the **India-China border**.

n6f20b4621a2.s: The Kumaon Himalaya is particularly associated with which of the following glaciers?
n6f20b4621a2.x: Pindari, Milam and Kafni glaciers are associated with the Kumaon Himalaya of Uttarakhand.
n6f20b4621a2.tq: Test a distinctive list through direct recall rather than confusing it with Trans-Himalayan glaciers.
xs: The Kumaon Himalaya has the **Pindari, Milam and Kafni** glaciers — option **(2)**.
**Siachen, Rimo, Baltoro** are **Karakoram** glaciers.
**Gangotri** is in the **Greater Himalaya**, source of the **Bhagirathi**.
xa: Kumaon lies between the **Sutlej and Kali** in **Uttarakhand**.
Kumaon peaks: **Nanda Devi, Trisul, Panchchuli**.
Kumaon lakes: **Nainital, Bhimtal**.

n0ba424c6e2d.s: The Siachen Glacier, in the Nubra region, lies in which range?
n0ba424c6e2d.x: Siachen lies in the Karakoram and marks Ladakh's northern limit.
xa: **Rimo** is another Karakoram glacier.
**Gangotri** (Greater Himalaya) is the source of the **Bhagirathi** at **Gaumukh**.
Kumaon glaciers: **Pindari, Milam, Kafni**.

nd76038641bb.s: Gangotri Glacier is associated with which one of the following combinations?
o: Pir Panjal Range and source of the Chenab
Kumaon Range and source of the Mandakini
Greater Himalaya and source of the Bhagirathi
nd76038641bb.x: Gangotri Glacier is located in the Greater Himalaya of Uttarakhand and is the source of the Bhagirathi at Gaumukh.
nd76038641bb.tq: Match the glacier with both its range and its associated river source.
xs: **Gangotri** lies in the **Greater Himalaya** and is the **source of the Bhagirathi** — option **(4)**.
Its snout is at **Gaumukh**, in **Uttarakhand**.
**Nubra** is the Karakoram region of **Siachen**, not Gangotri.
xa: Kumaon glaciers: **Pindari, Milam, Kafni**.
Karakoram glaciers: **Siachen, Rimo, Baltoro, Biafo, Hispar**.
⚠ **Nanda Devi** and **Kamet** (Uttarakhand) are also in the **Himadri**.

n2afa903e867.s: The Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills lie in which State?
n2afa903e867.x: The Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills form the Shillong Plateau in Meghalaya; Mizoram has the Mizo (Lushai) hills.
xa: **Naga Hills** — Nagaland; **Manipur Hills** — Manipur (**Loktak Lake**).
**Molasse basin** lies in **Mizoram** (soft unconsolidated deposits).
Purvanchal heights: **500-3,000 m**.

nbaaaccc8d74.s: Which of the following Purvanchal hill groups runs north-south?
nbaaaccc8d74.x: The Garo-Khasi-Jaintia and Naga hills run east-west, joining the north-south Mizo and Rakhine hills.
xa: **Garo, Khasi, Jaintia** are in **Meghalaya** (Shillong Plateau).
**Mizo (Lushai) Hills** — **Mizoram**; **Patkai Bum** — Arunachal Pradesh.
The knee-bend is at the **Dihang gorge** near **Namcha Barwa**.

n5f288d972f2.s: The Molasse Basin in the Indian Himalayan context is associated with
n5f288d972f2.x: The Molasse Basin is associated with Mizoram and consists of soft, unconsolidated deposits.
n5f288d972f2.tq: Pair the basin with its state and characteristic material.
xs: The **Molasse basin** is in **Mizoram**, of **soft unconsolidated deposits** — option **(2)** (APPSC-GS 2025).
The **granite** core belongs to the **Himadri**, not the Molasse basin.
xa: **Mizoram** has the **Mizo (Lushai) Hills**.
**Barail** links the **Naga and Mizo** hills — highest range of **Assam**.
**Manipur Hills** hold **Loktak Lake**.

nindian-geography-14-11.s: The Arakan Yoma is located in:
nindian-geography-14-11.x: The Arakan Yoma is in western Myanmar; the Chin Range reaches Manipur.
n: The Chin Range is located in Manipur. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
The Arakan Yoma is located in western Myanmar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
xa: The **Garo–Khasi–Jaintia Range** lies in **Meghalaya** (Shillong Plateau).
The **Miri Hills** are in **Arunachal Pradesh**; the **Mizo (Lushai) Hills** in **Mizoram**.
The **Barail** (Assam) links the **Naga** and **Mizo** hills.

nindian-geography-13-13.s: Bum La is located on which border?
nindian-geography-13-13.x: Bum La, near Tawang in Arunachal Pradesh, lies on the India–China (Tibet) border and is a border personnel meeting point. Pangsau and Diphu are on the Myanmar border.
nindian-geography-13-13.tq: Recall the border of each pass.
n: Bum La is on the India-China border. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 39-41]
xs: **Bum La** lies on the **India-China border** near **Tawang**, Arunachal Pradesh — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **India-Myanmar** border passes are **Diphu La** and **Pangsau**, not Bum La.
xa: **Bomdila** (**West Kameng**) is on the **Arunachal-Tibet route**.
**Arunachal** passes: **Bomdila**, **Bum La**, **Diphu**, **Pangsau**, **Yang Yap**.
The **Brahmaputra** enters India near **Yang Yap**.

nf781c9ff857.s: Approximately what proportion of India's total area is occupied by plains?
nf781c9ff857.x: Plains form the largest relief division of India and account for about 43 percent of the country’s area.
nf781c9ff857.tq: Choose the precise approximate share and avoid shifting the stated percentage by ten points.
xs: **Plains** occupy about **43 percent** of India's area — option **(3)**.
They form the **largest** relief portion of India (APPSC-GS 2024 key).
xa: **Shiwalik** debris helped build the **Indo-Gangetic plain**.
The Himalayas cover about **5 lakh sq km**.
The Himalayas form India's **northern boundary** and a **climatic barrier**.
nf781c9ff857.fixed: remove odd 'stated relief-share classification' wording; fact per APPSC-GS 2024

nb38daf9758a.s: India covers about what share of the world's land area?
nb38daf9758a.x: India's 32,87,263 sq km is about 2.4% of the world's land, making it the seventh largest country.
xa: India has **28 states and 8 UTs**.
Largest / smallest state: **Rajasthan / Goa**; largest / smallest UT: **Ladakh / Lakshadweep**.
Extent: **3,214 km** N-S and **2,933 km** E-W.

ne4795226f82.s: The mainland of India extends approximately between:
ne4795226f82.x: India's mainland extends from 8°4′ N to 37°6′ N latitude and 68°7′ E to 97°25′ E longitude.
xa: N-S extent **3,214 km**; E-W extent **2,933 km**.
**Standard meridian 82°30′ E** passes through **Mirzapur** and near **Kakinada** in AP.
The **Tropic of Cancer** crosses **8 states**.

nef00e60e910.s: The north-south extent of India's mainland is about:
nef00e60e910.x: India's mainland extends about 3,214 km north-south and 2,933 km east-west.
xa: Longitudes: **68°7′ E - 97°25′ E**.
Southernmost point of India: **Indira Point** (**6°45′ N**), Great Nicobar.
Area **32,87,263 sq km** ≈ **2.4%** of world land; **7th largest**.

n36f1b60d38b.x: India has 28 States and 8 Union Territories.
xa: Largest / smallest state: **Rajasthan / Goa**.
Largest / smallest UT: **Ladakh / Lakshadweep**.
**Uttar Pradesh** borders the most states: **8 states + Delhi**.

n59c150fe8c2.s: Besides the NCT of Delhi, Uttar Pradesh shares borders with how many States?
n59c150fe8c2.x: Uttar Pradesh borders eight States and the National Capital Territory of Delhi.
xa: Longest land border of India: **Bangladesh**.
Largest state **Rajasthan**; smallest **Goa**.
The **standard meridian** passes through **Mirzapur** (UP).

nf0598f42a9d.s: The Tropic of Cancer crosses how many States of India?
nf0598f42a9d.x: The Tropic of Cancer crosses eight States; the Standard Meridian 82°30' E passes through Mirzapur.
xa: ⚠ **Peninsular Plateau** = largest and oldest division; **Northern Plains** = youngest.
The Peninsular Plateau is a "**storehouse of economic minerals**".
Longitudes: **68°7′ E - 97°25′ E**.

n8403c832572.s: Which is the longest glacier in India?
n8403c832572.x: Siachen Glacier, in the Karakoram of Ladakh, is the longest glacier in India.
xa: The **Karakoram** is part of the **Trans-Himalaya**, north of the Himadri.
Himadri: average **>6,000 m**, **granite** core, permanently snow-bound.
Regional divisions: Punjab **Indus-Sutlej**, Kumaon **Sutlej-Kali**, Nepal **Kali-Tista**, Assam **Tista-Dihang**.

n4f4b810c6c6.s: The Rann of Kutch in Gujarat is a seasonal:
n4f4b810c6c6.x: The Rann is a seasonal salt marsh (Great Rann to the north, Little Rann to the south); it was a lowland, not a high mountainous tract.
xa: The Rann has the **Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary** and is rich in **solar energy**.
**Agariya** salt farmers work the Rann of Kutch.
The **Luni** ends in the Rann of Kutch.

n4f9ac148940.s: The Pal Ghat gap lies between the Nilgiris and the:
n4f9ac148940.x: Pal Ghat lies between the Nilgiris and the Anaimalai hills, between Kerala and Tamil Nadu, about 24-30 km wide.
xa: **Palani** (Kodaikanal) and **Cardamom** (Agastyamalai) lie **south of the Palghat gap**.
The Ghats **meet at the Nilgiri Hills**.
**Anamudi** (**2,695 m**) lies in the **Anaimalai**.

ncffd3bd974d.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three official India-Tibet trade routes?
ncffd3bd974d.x: Shipki La, Nathu La and Lipulekh are the official trade routes; Bomdila is the gateway to Tawang.
xa: **Shipki La**: Kinnaur, HP, **3,930 m**; Sutlej enters India.
**Nathu La**: Sikkim, among the **highest motorable passes**.
**Lipulekh**: Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand; **Kailash-Mansarovar** route.

n03e19f62ab5.s: Emergent coasts, with wide plains, bars, lagoons and deltas, result from:
n03e19f62ab5.x: Emergent coasts form when land rises or the sea falls, giving wide plains, bars, lagoons and deltas.
xa: The **east coast** is **emergent**: broad, dry, big **deltas**.
The **west coast** is **submergent**: narrow, wet, with estuaries that suit ports.
**Malabar** is a **compound** coast.

ncd14a1368e1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Chilika is a lagoon lake in Odisha.
Pulicat is the second-largest brackish lagoon.
Kolleru continues to be a coastal lagoon separated from the sea.
Kolleru is a freshwater lake between the Krishna and Godavari.
ncd14a1368e1.x: Kolleru was formerly a lagoon but became an inland freshwater lake due to coastal emergence.
xa: **Pulicat** lies on the **AP-TN** border.
The east coast is **emergent** — wide plains, bars, lagoons, deltas.
**Vembanad** is the largest Kerala **kayal**.

n4aede93db48.s: The southernmost island of Lakshadweep is:
n4aede93db48.x: Minicoy is the largest and southernmost island; the Amindivi group lies north of 11° N.
xa: **Nine Degree Channel**: Minicoy from the rest of Lakshadweep (**Kavaratti** group).
**Eight Degree Channel**: Minicoy from the **Maldives**.
⚠ **Ten Degree** = Andaman/Nicobar.
n4aede93db48.fixed: Andrott, not Minicoy, is the largest Lakshadweep island

n0fcbff36fb2.x: Kavaratti is the capital of Lakshadweep, a group of coral atolls and India's smallest UT (about 32 sq km).
xa: **36** islands, **10 inhabited**; lies in the **Arabian Sea** off Kerala.
**Minicoy** is its largest and southernmost island.
Groups: **Amindivi** (north of **11°** N) and **Cannanore** (south).

ngeneral-geography-5-13.s: The Peninsular Plateau of India is best described as:
ngeneral-geography-5-13.x: The Peninsular Plateau is an ancient stable crystalline landmass; the Northern Plains are alluvial and the Indian Desert is the arid west.
n: The Northern Plains are vast alluvial depositional plains. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
The Peninsular Plateau is an ancient stable crystalline landmass. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
The Indian Desert is an arid western region. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
India’s coastal plains are narrow in the west and broader in the east. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
xa: **Six divisions**: **Himalayas, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains, Islands**.
⚠ **Peninsular Plateau** = largest and oldest; **Northern Plains** = youngest.
The Northern Plains contain **Bhabar**, **Terai**, **Bhangar** and **Khadar**.

nindian-geography-44-9.s: Which of the following valleys is NOT in Himachal Pradesh?
nindian-geography-44-9.x: Lahaul, Parvati and Kullu are in Himachal Pradesh; Tura is in Meghalaya.
n: Lahaul Valley is located in Himachal Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 115-116]
Parvati Valley is located in Kullu, Himachal Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 115-116]
Kullu Valley is located in Himachal Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 115-116]
Tura Valley is located in Meghalaya. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 115-116]
xa: The **Parvati Valley** lies in **Kullu** district.
**Kashmir, Kangra and Kullu** valleys belong to the **Himachal** range.
**Shipki La** (**Kinnaur**) and **Rohtang** are **Himachal Pradesh** passes.

nindian-geography-32-12.x: Salsette is India's most populous island; Elephanta is about 10 km from the Gateway of India.
n: Salsette is the most populous Indian island. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-100]
Elephanta is approximately 10 km from the Gateway of India. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-100]
xa: **Divi** (**Diviseema**) in Krishna district is linked to **Krishna distributaries**.
**Rameswaram** (**Ramanathapuram**) lies between **India** and **Sri Lanka**.
**Barren Island** is India's **only active volcano**.

nindian-geography-28-20.s: Which of the following hills is NOT located in Karnataka?
nindian-geography-28-20.x: Biligiriranga, Nandi and Chamundi are in Karnataka; the Garo Hills are in Meghalaya.
n: Biligiriranga Hills are located in Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 88-91]
Nandi Hills are located in Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 88-91]
Chamundi Hills are located in Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 88-91]
Garo Hills are located in Meghalaya. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 88-91]
xa: **Biligiriranga** lies in **southeastern Karnataka**, with the **Ranganatha Temple**.
**Mullayanagiri** (**1,892 m**) is Karnataka's peak.
**Malnad** (**Malenadu**) is the forested west of **Karnataka**.

nindian-geography-40-18.s: Malnad (Malenadu), a mountainous and densely forested region, lies in:
nindian-geography-40-18.x: Malnad is the forested hilly west of Karnataka.
n: The Karnataka Plateau is situated in the interior of Peninsular India. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 110-112]
The Karnataka Plateau includes Malnad, also called Malenadu, in western Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 110-112]
Malnad is mountainous in western Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 110-112]
Malnad is densely forested in western Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 110-112]
The Coimbatore Plateau is located in Tamil Nadu. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 110-112]
The Coimbatore Plateau lies around Coimbatore. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 110-112]
xa: The **Coimbatore Plateau** is part of the **southern Peninsular plateau system**.
The **Biligiriranga**, **Nandi** and **Chamundi** hills are in **Karnataka**.
**Mullayanagiri** (**1,892 m**) is in **Karnataka**.

n2a2828ad750.s: Karewas of the Kashmir Valley are best described as:
o: Lacustrine gravel-and-mud terraces belonging to the Tertiary system
Floodplain deposits renewed annually by the Ganga
Coral reefs formed along the western coast
Young volcanic cones of the Trans-Himalaya
n2a2828ad750.x: Karewas, also called Vudr, are lacustrine gravel-and-mud terraces in the Kashmir Valley and form part of the Tertiary system. They are famous for saffron cultivation.
n2a2828ad750.tq: Identify the landform from its depositional environment and material.
xs: **Karewas (Vudr)** are **lacustrine gravel-and-mud terraces** of the Kashmir Valley, part of the **Tertiary system** — option **(1)**.
They are famous for **saffron (zafran)**.
Annually renewed floodplain alluvium is **Khadar**, not karewa.
xa: **Bhabar**: coarse gravel at the Shiwalik foot where streams sink.
**Terai**: marshy, waterlogged belt where Bhabar water re-emerges.
**Bhangar** = older alluvium with **kankar**; **Khadar** = newer alluvium.

n732b4c3f1e9.s: In the Northern Plains, the marshy belt where Bhabar streams re-emerge is the:
n732b4c3f1e9.x: Terai is the marshy, forested belt where Bhabar streams re-emerge; kankar-bearing older alluvium is the Bhangar.
xa: ⚠ Belt order: **Bhabar → Terai → Bhangar/Khadar**.
**Khadar** = newer floodplain alluvium, renewed yearly.
**Kosi plain** (north Bihar) = a huge **megafan**.

n29f37580b1e.s: The Molassis Basin is associated with which of the following regions?
n29f37580b1e.x: The Molassis Basin is located in Mizoram in the Purvachal hills and consists of soft, unconsolidated deposits.
n29f37580b1e.tq: Test the location of a specialised geological basin against nearby regional distractors.
xs: The **Molassis basin** is in **Mizoram** in the **Purvachal hills** — option **(1)**.
It consists of **soft unconsolidated deposits** (NCERT).
xa: **Karewas** are lake deposits of the **Kashmir Valley**, famous for **saffron**.
The **Kosi plain** is an alluvial **megafan** of north Bihar.
**Kutch** was once an **island** amid seas and lagoons.

nindian-geography-12-9.s: Which of the following is NOT located in Maharashtra?
nindian-geography-12-9.x: The Balaghat, Harishchandra and Satmala ranges are in Maharashtra; the Mandav Hills are in Gujarat.
n: The Balaghat Range is located in Maharashtra. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
The Harishchandra Range is located in Maharashtra. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
The Satmala Range is located in Maharashtra. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
The Mandav Hills are located in Gujarat. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 35-39]
xa: **Satmala-Ajanta** lies between the **Tapi** and **Godavari**.
**Harishchandragarh-Balaghat** lies between the **Godavari** and **Bhima**.
**Kalsubai** (**1,646 m**) is the Sahyadri peak of **Maharashtra**.

nindian-geography-14-4.s: The Mandav Hills are located in:
nindian-geography-14-4.x: The Mandav Hills are in Gujarat; the Biligirirangans are in south-eastern Karnataka.
n: The Biligirirangan Hills are located in southeastern Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
The Shevaroy Hills are located in Salem, Tamil Nadu. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
The Mandav Hills are located in Gujarat. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
The Garo–Khasi–Jaintia Range is located in Meghalaya. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
xa: **Biligiriranga Hills** are linked with the **Ranganatha Temple**.
**Nandi Hills** and **Chamundi Hills** are also in **Karnataka**.
**Nokrek** lies in the **Garo Hills**.

n0e498939350.s: The Kashmir, Kangra and Kullu valleys lie in which Himalayan range?
n0e498939350.x: Kashmir, Kangra and Kullu valleys lie in the Himachal or Lesser Himalaya, not the Shiwalik.
xa: Himachal ranges: **Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, Mahabharat** (Nepal).
Himachal hill stations: **Shimla, Mussoorie, Nainital, Darjeeling**.
**Shiwaliks**: youngest, narrowest (**15-50 km**), average ~**1,300 m**.

n926af544806.s: The true desert in the western part of the Thar is called:
n926af544806.x: Marusthali (west) is the true desert; Bagar (east) is the semi-arid strip bordering the Aravallis.
xa: IYB: **Great Desert** (Rann edge beyond the Luni, northward) and **Little Desert** (Luni to Jaisalmer-Jodhpur).
A **rocky limestone** belt lies between them.
Dunes: **barchan** and **seif**.

ngeneral-geography-5-103.s: A salt marsh that floods in the monsoon and dries into a desert describes the:
ngeneral-geography-5-103.x: The Rann of Kutch is a salt marsh and a seasonal marshy desert.
n: The Rann of Kutch is a salt marsh. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
The Rann of Kutch is a seasonal marshy desert. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
xa: Kutch was once an **island**; aridity turned the lowland into a **salt plain**.
**Great Rann** (north) vs **Little Rann** (south); the **Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary** lies here.
The **Luni** ends in the **Rann of Kutch**; **Agariya** are its salt farmers.

nindian-geography-44-19.s: The Narmada Valley lies between which ranges?
nindian-geography-44-19.x: The Narmada flows between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.
n: Brahmaputra Valley is located in Assam. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 115-116]
Narmada Valley lies between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 115-116]
xa: The **Godavari** and **Tapi** valleys lie in **Peninsular India**.
The **Ganga Valley** lies in **Northern India**.
The **Satpura** lies between the **Narmada and Tapi** valleys.

nindian-geography-40-15.s: The Bhander Plateau forms the ____ part of the Vindhyan scarpland.
nindian-geography-40-15.x: The Bhander Plateau is in the Vindhyan region and forms the southern part of the scarpland, not the northern.
n: The Bhander Plateau belongs to the Vindhyan region. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 110-112]
The Bhander Plateau forms the southern part of the Vindhyan Scarpland. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 110-112]
xa: It is **associated with the Vindhya Mountains**.
The **Malwa** lies **between the Aravalli and Vindhya**.
The **Mukandara Hills** extend the **Vindhyan Range** into Rajasthan.

n6016ec73ce1.s: Which plain was formed mainly by the tributaries of the Indus and is marked by doabs?
n6016ec73ce1.x: The Punjab Plain was formed by Indus tributaries and contains doabs. The Brahmaputra Plain is the Assam valley; the Kosi Plain is an alluvial fan in north Bihar.
xa: **Ganga plain**: about **3,75,000 sq km**; alluvium **2,000-3,000 m** thick.
Ganga plain divisions: **Ganga-Yamuna Doab, Rohilkhand, Avadh, Bihar, Bengal**.
The Brahmaputra enters **Bangladesh**.

n4ebfc51f6f9.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five divisions of the Ganga Plain listed in the regional classification?
n4ebfc51f6f9.x: The five listed divisions are the Ganga–Yamuna Doab, Rohilkhand, Avadh, Bihar and Bengal plains. Malwa is a plateau region and is not a division of the Ganga Plain.
n4ebfc51f6f9.tq: Find the outsider in a regional classification list.
xs: **Malwa** is not a Ganga Plain division — option **(3)**.
The five divisions are **Ganga-Yamuna Doab, Rohilkhand, Avadh, Bihar, Bengal** plains.
**Malwa** is a plateau of the **Central Highlands** (Deccan Trap basalt).
xa: Ganga plain area: about **3,75,000 sq km**.
Doab: upper **>200 m**, middle **100-200 m**, lower **<100 m**.
The **Vindhyas** lie on the **south** of the Malwa plateau.

n04455153ab4.s: The Central Highlands of the Peninsular Plateau lie north of which river?
n04455153ab4.x: The Central Highlands lie north of the Narmada and include the Aravalli, Malwa and Vindhya regions.
xa: **Aravalli** is the **oldest**; **Vindhyas** form an **escarpment**.
**Aravalli** = an **Archaean horst**; highest **Guru Shikhar** (**1,722 m**, Mt Abu).
The **Malwa plateau** (MP) is **Deccan Trap basalt**.

n005bcf537ac.s: The Vindhyas lie to the ____ of the Malwa Plateau.
n005bcf537ac.x: The Vindhyas lie south of the Malwa Plateau; the Malwa is not south of the Vindhyas.
xa: Chhotanagpur = **Ranchi plateau**, **Jharkhand**.
**Parasnath** (about **1,350 m**) is the Chhotanagpur peak.
Central Highlands average **800-1,200 m**.

n5f5662e6430.s: The Deccan Plateau, lying south of the Narmada, is largely made up of:
n5f5662e6430.x: The Deccan Plateau lies south of the Narmada and is largely composed of basaltic rocks.
xa: Deccan plateau: about **7 lakh sq km**, **inverted triangle**, **stable**.
Deccan Trap weathering gives **regur** (black cotton soil).
The plateau **tilts east**, so most rivers flow east.

n74b9a1b3fa6.s: The word 'trap' in Deccan Traps comes from a Swedish word meaning:
n74b9a1b3fa6.x: 'Trap' is Swedish for step; the Traps formed by fissure eruptions of basaltic lava.
xa: Area: once about **10 lakh sq km**, now about **5 lakh sq km**.
Thickness: **3,000 m** in the west → **150 m** in the east.
Weathering gives **regur** (black cotton soil) for **cotton**.

n2c373881d13.s: The Deccan Traps originally covered about 10 lakh sq km; today they cover about:
n2c373881d13.x: They now cover about 5 lakh sq km, thinning from about 3,000 m in the west to about 150 m in the east.
xa: Spread today: **Kuchchh, Saurashtra, Maharashtra, Malwa, N Karnataka**.
Formed by **fissure eruptions** of basaltic lava, **end-Cretaceous to early Eocene**.
'**Trap**' = Swedish for **step**.

n244debf513d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Peninsular Plateau?
o: It is the largest and oldest physiographic division.
It is a Precambrian Gondwana shield.
It tilts towards the west, so most rivers flow westward.
It is a triangular block of igneous and metamorphic rocks.
n244debf513d.x: The Peninsular Plateau tilts eastward, so most of its rivers flow east.
xa: ⚠ **Northern Plains** = youngest division (aggradational alluvium).
It is the "**storehouse of economic minerals**".
Sub-divisions: **Central Highlands**, Malwa, **Deccan**, **Chhotanagpur**.

ndb495d71dc2.s: Weathering of the Deccan Trap produces which soil, well suited to cotton?
ndb495d71dc2.x: Deccan Trap weathering yields regur or black soil, particularly suitable for cotton.
xa: Trap thickness: **3,000 m** in the west → **150 m** in the east.
Area: once **10 lakh sq km**, now about **5 lakh sq km**.
**Kayals** and **deltas** support ports and fisheries.

ngeneral-geography-5-4.s: The Deccan Plateau is predominantly ____ in origin.
ngeneral-geography-5-4.x: The Deccan Plateau is built mainly of basaltic lava.
n: The Deccan Plateau has a predominantly basaltic volcanic origin. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
The Chotanagpur Plateau is mineral-rich. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
The Chotanagpur Plateau is drained by the Damodar. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
The Deccan Trap is a basaltic lava plateau. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
The Chotanagpur Plateau has Damodar drainage. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
The Chotanagpur Plateau is mineral-rich. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
xa: The **Deccan Traps** are **fissure eruptions** of basaltic lava, **end-Cretaceous to early Eocene**.
Deccan Trap weathering produced **regur** (**black cotton soil**).
Chhotanagpur has **iron, coal, manganese** and **Hundru Falls**.

ngeneral-geography-5-18.s: Which plateau is mineral-rich and drained by the Damodar?
ngeneral-geography-5-18.x: Chotanagpur is mineral-rich and drained by the Damodar; Malwa lies between the Aravalli and Vindhya.
n: The Malwa Plateau lies between the Aravalli and Vindhya ranges. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
The Chotanagpur Plateau is mineral-rich. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
The Chotanagpur Plateau is drained by the Damodar. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
Dandakaranya is a central-eastern highland region. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
The Bhander Plateau forms the southern part of the Vindhyan scarpland. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
The Malwa Plateau lies between the Aravalli and Vindhya ranges. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
The Chotanagpur Plateau has Damodar drainage. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
The Chotanagpur Plateau is mineral-rich. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
Dandakaranya is a central or eastern Peninsular highland. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
xa: **Bundelkhand** and **Baghelkhand** are **eastern extensions** of the Central Highlands.
The **Meghalaya Plateau** is a **detached extension** of the Peninsular Plateau.
**Dandakaranya** covers about **89,078 square kilometres**.

nindian-geography-14-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the ranges of central and north-western India?
o: The Vindhya and Satpura ranges converge at Yercaud.
The Narmada and Tapti flank the Satpura Range.
The Aravalli extends from Rajasthan into Haryana, reaching Delhi.
The Vindhya Range lies in Central India.
nindian-geography-14-2.x: The Vindhya and Satpura ranges meet near Amarkantak, not Yercaud, which is in the Shevaroy Hills.
n: The Aravalli Range is located in Rajasthan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
The Aravalli Range is located in Haryana. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
The Vindhya Range is located in Central India. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
The northern extension of the Aravalli Range reaches Delhi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
The Narmada River flanks the Satpura Range. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
The Tapti River flanks the Satpura Range. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
The Vindhya Range and the Satpura Range converge at Amarkantak. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
The Aravalli Range is located in Delhi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
xa: The **Vindhyan Range** lies **north of the Narmada Valley**.
**Mukandara Hills** (SE Rajasthan) extend the **Vindhyan Range**.
**Dhupgarh** is the **Satpura**'s highest peak.

nindian-geography-40-4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Malwa Plateau?
o: It lies between the Aravalli and Vindhya ranges.
It lies to the east of Bundelkhand.
The Aravalli range lies to its north.
The Vindhya range lies to its south.
nindian-geography-40-4.x: Malwa lies west of Bundelkhand; Bundelkhand is on its east.
n: The Malwa Plateau lies between the Aravalli Range and the Vindhya Range. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 110-112]
The Malwa Plateau extends eastward to Bundelkhand. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 110-112]
The Aravalli Range lies north of the Malwa Plateau. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 110-112]
The Vindhya Range lies south of the Malwa Plateau. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 110-112]
Bundelkhand lies east of the Malwa Plateau. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 110-112]
