A&N tribes: **Jarawa, Sentinelese**.
Capital: **Sri Vijaya Puram** (renamed **2024**).

nindian-geography-32-17.s: Salsette Island, covering Mumbai and Thane, is in:
nindian-geography-32-17.x: Salsette is in Maharashtra (Mumbai-Thane); Minicoy is in Lakshadweep.
n: Barren Island is located in the Andaman Sea, Andaman and Nicobar Islands. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-100]
Nicobar is located in the southeastern Bay of Bengal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-100]
Minicoy is located in Lakshadweep. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-100]
Salsette is located in Mumbai and Thane, Maharashtra. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-100]
xa: **Minicoy** is the **largest and southernmost** island of Lakshadweep.
⚠ **Ten Degree** = Andaman/Nicobar; **Nine Degree** = Minicoy/Lakshadweep; **Eight Degree** = Minicoy/Maldives.
**Indira Point**, Great Nicobar, is the **southernmost point**.

nindian-geography-32-18.s: Divi Island lies among the distributaries of which river?
nindian-geography-32-18.x: Divi lies among the Krishna distributaries; Sriharikota separates Pulicat from the Bay of Bengal.
n: Barren Island has an active volcano. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-100]
Sriharikota separates Pulicat from the Bay of Bengal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-100]
Divi is associated with Krishna distributaries. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-100]
Rameswaram lies between India and Sri Lanka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 98-100]
xa: Barren Island last erupted in **2017**; **Narcondam** is **dormant**.
**Pulicat** (AP-TN) is the **2nd largest brackish lagoon**.
**Kolleru** is a **freshwater** lake between the **Krishna** and **Godavari**.

ngeneral-geography-5-105.s: Which of the following is India's only active volcano?
ngeneral-geography-5-105.x: Barren Island is India's only active volcano; Narcondam is dormant.
n: Barren Island is an active volcano. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
Narcondam is volcanic and inactive-dormant. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
xa: Barren Island lies in the **Andaman Sea** — India's **only active volcano**, last erupted **2017**.
The **A&N** islands are a **submerged extension** of the **Arakan Yoma**.
**Lakshadweep** islands are of **coral origin**.

nfcd44ebdcb9.s: The Himalayan mountain system extends approximately from:
nfcd44ebdcb9.x: The Himalayas extend for about 2,414 kilometres from Nanga Parbat in the west to Namche Barwa in the east.
nfcd44ebdcb9.tq: Recall the western and eastern terminal points of the mountain system.
xs: The Himalayas run from **Nanga Parbat to Namche Barwa** — option **(4)**.
They are **young fold mountains**, **2,414 km** long.
xa: Area about **5 lakh sq km**; width **200-500 km**.
They rose from **Tethys** sediments as the Indian plate moved north (**Eocene-Pliocene**); uplift continues.
Northern edge of the plains: **Himalayan Frontal Fault**.

n9ef8a4ff304.s: Which feature of the Indian Desert appears only with rainfall?
n9ef8a4ff304.x: Seasonal streams appear during rainfall; the desert otherwise has arid weather, sand dunes and thorny bushes.
xa: Rivers: **Luni**, Machhu, Rupen, Saraswati, Banas, Ghaggar — **inland drainage** into salt lakes or sand.
**Luni** is the only significant river; it ends in the **Rann of Kutch**.
**Sambhar** is a **saline lake**.

n9fa1d9ba8d3.s: Under the revised measurement, Andhra Pradesh's coastline is about:
n9fa1d9ba8d3.x: The revised figure is 1,053.07 km, ranking AP third after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu; the earlier 974 km placed it second.
xa: India's revised coastline: **11,098.81 km** (2023-24).
District coastline: longest **Srikakulam (193 km)**; shortest **West Godavari (23 km)**.
Quote the **survey year** with AP's figure — sources differ.

n05b60f8c2f3.s: The 2023-24 remeasurement that placed India's coastline at 11,098.81 km was carried out by:
o: the Geological Survey of India and ISRO
the National Hydrographic Office and the Survey of India
the Indian Coast Guard and the Ministry of Earth Sciences
the Central Water Commission and NITI Aayog
n05b60f8c2f3.x: The National Hydrographic Office and the Survey of India carried out the remeasurement, and the Ministry of Home Affairs reported it in December 2024. The figure rose from 7,516.6 km because of finer 1:250,000 GIS tracing, not land growth. The other agencies are not credited with it.
n05b60f8c2f3.tq: 11,098.81 km = NHO + Survey of India, reported by MHA (Dec 2024).
xs: The remeasurement was by the **National Hydrographic Office** and the **Survey of India** — option **(2)**.
It was reported by the **MHA** in **Dec 2024**.
xa: The coastline rose from **7,516.6 km** (+**47.7%**).
Land did not grow: finer **1:250,000 GIS** tracing caught **creeks and inlets**.
It also counted **1,389 islands** (**1,298** offshore + **91** inshore).

nindian-geography-14-14.s: Yercaud is located in which hills?
nindian-geography-14-14.x: Yercaud is in the Shevaroy Hills; Ooty is in the Nilgiris and Anaimudi tops the Anaimalai Range.
n: Ooty is located in the Nilgiri Range. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
Udhagamandalam is located in the Nilgiri Range. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
The Anaimalai Range is part of the Western Ghats. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
The Cardamom Range is part of the Western Ghats. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
Yercaud is an important place in the Shevaroy Hills. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 41-46]
xa: **Anaimudi** (**2,695 metres**) is the **highest peak of South India**.
The **Nilgiri** is the **meeting point** of the **Eastern and Western Ghats** — the **Blue Mountains**.
**Doddabetta** (**2,637 metres**) is the **Nilgiri**'s highest peak.

ngeneral-geography-5-100.s: The Chambal region is particularly associated with which of the following features?
o: Salt marsh and seasonal marshy desert
ngeneral-geography-5-100.x: The Chambal valley is known for ravines and badlands made by gully erosion. Coral islands fit Lakshadweep and salt marsh the Rann.
ngeneral-geography-5-100.tq: Recall the landform of each region.
n: The Chambal has ravines and badland topography. [General Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 33-42]
xs: The **Chambal** is associated with **ravines and badland topography** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Coral islands and atolls** fit **Lakshadweep**; **salt marsh / seasonal marshy desert** fits the **Rann of Kutch**.
**Volcanic** features fit **Barren Island** and **Narcondam**.
xa: **Western Ghats rivers** are **short and swift**, with **estuarine mouths**.
The **Ganga-Brahmaputra** is the **world's major delta system**.
The **Kosi** is the "**Sorrow of Bihar**".

nbef44523865.s: Which is the northernmost of the major Himalayan structural zones?
nbef44523865.x: From north to south the zones are the Indus-Tsangpo Suture, Main Central Thrust, Main Boundary Thrust and Himalayan Frontal Fault.
xa: The Himalayas are **young fold mountains** from **Tethys** sediments; uplift still going on.
Width **200-500 km**; area about **5 lakh sq km**.
Order of ranges: **Trans-Himalaya → Himadri → Himachal → Shiwaliks**.

n0002cc4a668.s: The Kosi Plain of north Bihar is best described as a:
o: Huge alluvial fan formed by shifting channels
n0002cc4a668.x: The Kosi forms a huge alluvial fan in north Bihar. Its shifting channels have earned it the description ‘Sorrow of Bihar’.
n0002cc4a668.tq: Identify the landform from the river’s depositional and shifting-channel behaviour.
xs: The **Kosi plain** is a **huge alluvial fan** with **shifting channels** — option **(1)**.
It is called a **megafan**; the Kosi is the "**Sorrow of Bihar**".
xa: Northern Plains: **6,52,000 sq km**, **2,400 km** long.
Gradient: only **~200 m** drop over **1,600 km** from Delhi to the Bay.
**Khadar** floodplains are renewed yearly.

ne7bd455e21e.s: The Araku Valley is popularly known by which of the following names in Andhra Pradesh?
ne7bd455e21e.x: Araku Valley is popularly called the “Ooty of Andhra Pradesh”.
ne7bd455e21e.tq: Recall the exact popular epithet and avoid substituting a familiar geographical nickname.
xs: **Araku Valley** is called the "**Ooty of AP**" — option **(2)**.
It lies in AP's **Eastern Ghats**, whose highest point **Arma Konda** is in **ASR district**.
xa: AP's Eastern Ghats: **Papikondalu, Nallamala, Erramala, Seshachalam, Velikonda**.
Highest: **Arma Konda (Sitamma Konda), 1,680 m**.
A survey found **three new plant species** in AP's Eastern Ghats (May 2026).

n0f27761c14f.s: Which one of the following rivers does NOT originate in the Mansarovar–Kailash area?
n0f27761c14f.x: The Beas originates near the Rohtang region, not in the Mansarovar–Kailash area. Karnali, Indus and Brahmaputra are included among the rivers originating in or near that region.
n0f27761c14f.tq: Find the outsider in a grouped source-location list.
xs: The **Beas** rises at **Rohtang**, not in the Mansarovar-Kailash area — option **(4)**.
**Indus**, **Brahmaputra** and **Karnali** all rise in the **Mansarovar-Kailash** area.
xa: Also not from Mansarovar: **Ganga** (Gangotri), **Yamuna** (Yamunotri), **Chenab** (Baralacha pass), **Jhelum** (Verinag), **Ravi**.
The **Sutlej** rises at **Rakas Tal** in the Mansarovar area.
The Beas is the **Hyphasis** of the Greeks.

nae9e19eb53d.s: The Chenab is formed by the confluence of which two rivers at Tandi in Himachal Pradesh?
nae9e19eb53d.x: The Chenab is formed by the union of the Chandra and Bhaga rivers at Tandi in Himachal Pradesh.
nae9e19eb53d.tq: Identify the constituent streams of a major river.
xs: The **Chenab** is formed by **Chandra + Bhaga** at **Tandi** (HP) — option **(2)**.
The **Chenab** rises at the **Baralacha pass**, not in the Mansarovar area.
xa: Greek name **Acesines**; Vedic name **Asikni**.
**Chenab** is the **largest tributary of the Indus**.
Chenab projects: **Baglihar, Salal, Dul Hasti** (J&K).

nindian-geography-1-34.s: In Pakistan, the Kishanganga river is known as the:
nindian-geography-1-34.x: The Kishanganga is called the Neelum in Pakistan; the Jhelum rises at Verinag.
n: Jhelum originates at Verinag at the foot of the Pir Panjal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Jhelum flows through Srinagar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Jhelum flows through Wular Lake. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Jhelum enters Pakistan through a deep and narrow gorge. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Kishanganga is called Neelum in Pakistan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xa: The Greek name of the Jhelum is **Hydaspes**; its Vedic name **Vitasta**.
**Wular** is the **largest freshwater lake** of India, fed by the Jhelum.
Under the **Indus Waters Treaty 1960**, the **Jhelum** is a **western river** (primarily Pakistan).

nindian-geography-1-51.s: In Pakistan, the Ravi joins the:
nindian-geography-1-51.x: The Ravi joins the Chenab, which also takes the Jhelum, and the combined flow joins the Sutlej before the Indus.
n: Ravi joins Chenab in Pakistan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Chenab receives Jhelum. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Chenab receives Ravi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Sutlej receives Chenab. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Sutlej joins Indus. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xa: The **Chenab** is the **largest tributary** of the Indus — formed by **Chandra + Bhaga at Tandi**.
⚠ **Hydaspes** = Jhelum; **Hyphasis** = Beas; **Acesines** = Chenab.
The **Indus** reaches the **Arabian Sea** near **Karachi**.

n33ef54543c2.s: The Indus enters the Arabian Sea near:
n33ef54543c2.x: The Indus flows between Ladakh and Zaskar, turns south at Nanga Parbat and meets the Arabian Sea near Karachi.
xa: Indus source: **Singge Khabab**, Kailash range (**5,182 m**).
Its largest tributary is the **Chenab**.
Tributaries W to E: **Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej**.

n300d31f4138.s: Tso Moriri, a brackish lake with Ramsar-site status, is located in:
n300d31f4138.x: Tso Moriri is a brackish lake in Ladakh and a Ramsar site.
xa: **Pangong Tso** (Ladakh, shared with Tibet) is also brackish/saline.
**Loktak** has floating **phumdis**.
**Bhimtal** (Kumaon) is freshwater.

nindian-geography-2-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the tributaries of the Indus?
o: The Kishanganga is a tributary of the Sutlej.
The Kishanganga is called the Neelum in Pakistan.
The Sutlej is a tributary of the Indus.
The Chenab is the largest tributary of the Indus.
nindian-geography-2-2.x: The Kishanganga (Neelum) is a tributary of the Jhelum, not the Sutlej.
n: Chenab is the largest tributary of the Indus. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Kishanganga is known as Neelum in Pakistan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Sutlej is a major tributary of the Indus. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Kishanganga is a tributary of the Jhelum. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Chenab is a major tributary of the Indus. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
xa: The **Sutlej**'s tributaries are the **Beas**, **Spiti** and **Baspa**.
The **Spiti** rises at **Kunzam La** and joins the Sutlej near **Khab** (Kinnaur).
The **Zanskar** joins the Indus at **Nimu**; **Leh** lies on the Indus's **right bank**.

nindian-geography-31-2.x: The Telugu Ganga Project carries Krishna water to Chennai.
nindian-geography-31-2.tq: Recall the purpose of each project.
n: Telugu Ganga Project supplies Chennai. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
xs: The **Telugu Ganga Project** (**Andhra Pradesh**) **supplies Chennai** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Srisailam** is on the **Krishna** (AP–Telangana border); **Pochampad** on the **Godavari** (Telangana); **Babli** is in **Maharashtra**.
xa: **Nagarjuna Sagar** is also on the **Krishna** at the **AP–Telangana border**.
The **Tungabhadra** project serves **AP** and **Karnataka**.
**Jayakwadi** is on the **Godavari**.

ne8c4618bc41.s: At which place do the headstreams Bhagirathi and Alaknanda unite before the river acquires the name Ganga?
ne8c4618bc41.x: Bhagirathi and Alaknanda unite at Devprayag. Downstream of this confluence, the river is called the Ganga.
ne8c4618bc41.tq: Directly identify the place associated with a river confluence.
xs: **Bhagirathi** and **Alaknanda** join at **Devprayag**, where the river becomes the **Ganga** — option **(3)**.
These two are the Ganga's **headstreams**; the river is called the Ganga only **from Devprayag**.
xa: The **Bhagirathi** rises at **Gomukh**, **Gangotri** glacier.
**Tehri** dam is on the **Bhagirathi** (Uttarakhand).
The Ganga is navigable up to **Prayagraj**.

n652354e75b0.s: At Farakka, the left arm of the Ganga is the:
n652354e75b0.x: The left arm is the Bhagirathi-Hooghly; the right arm, the Padma, joins the Brahmaputra and Meghna.
xa: The Brahmaputra (**Jamuna**) joins the Padma at **Goalundo**.
The **Barak** is the **Meghna**'s headstream.
**Mahananda** is the **easternmost** Ganga tributary.

nc70894321d0.s: The Barak River, rising in the Manipur hills, is described as the headstream of the:
nc70894321d0.x: The Barak rises in the Manipur hills and is described as the headstream of the Meghna.
nc70894321d0.tq: Distinguish the Barak–Meghna relationship from the Brahmaputra–Jamuna relationship.
xs: The **Barak**, rising in the **Manipur hills**, is the **Meghna**'s headstream — option **(4)**.
The Ganga-Brahmaputra waters enter the Bay of Bengal as the **Meghna**.
xa: The **Padma** is the Ganga's right arm into Bangladesh.
The **Bhagirathi-Hooghly** is the Ganga's left arm at **Farakka**.
The Brahmaputra (**Jamuna**) joins the Padma at **Goalundo**.

nindian-geography-1-1.s: The Bhagirathi originates from which of the following places?
nindian-geography-1-1.x: The Bhagirathi rises at Gomukh in Uttarkashi district. The Alaknanda rises at Satopanth and the Yamuna at Yamunotri.
nindian-geography-1-1.tq: Recall the source of each river.
n: Bhagirathi originates at Gomukh in Uttarkashi district, Uttarakhand. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Alaknanda originates at Satopanth Glacier above Badrinath. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Yamuna originates at Yamunotri Glacier on the western slopes of Banderpunch Peak. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Son originates at Amarkantak Hill. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xs: The **Bhagirathi** originates at **Gomukh** in **Uttarkashi district**, Uttarakhand — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Yamunotri Glacier** is the **Yamuna**'s source; **Amarkantak Hill** is the **Son**'s source.
**Satopanth Glacier** above **Badrinath** is the source of the **Alaknanda**.
xa: The **Alaknanda** and **Bhagirathi** meet at **Devprayag** to form the **Ganga**.
**Uttarkashi** is situated on the Bhagirathi; the **Tehri** dam is across it.
The Ganga **enters the plains at Haridwar**.

ncf862e9981e.s: India's drainage systems are conventionally classified into which of the following four groups?
o: Northern, Southern, Eastern and Western drainage
Himalayan, Deccan, Coastal and Inland drainage
Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra and Peninsular drainage
Glacial, Perennial, Seasonal and Tidal drainage
ncf862e9981e.x: The four broad groups are Himalayan drainage, Deccan drainage, Coastal drainage and Inland drainage of western Rajasthan.
ncf862e9981e.tq: Directly recall the official four-fold classification and distinguish it from river-basin groupings.
xs: The four groups are **Himalayan, Deccan, Coastal and Inland** drainage — option **(2)**.
**Inland** drainage belongs to **western Rajasthan**.
**Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra** are the three **Himalayan** basins, not the four groups.
xa: Himalayan rivers are **antecedent** and **perennial**.
The **Ganga** basin drains nearly **40%** of India's area.
The **Indus** enters the **Arabian Sea** near **Karachi**.

ne55808d6a8d.s: The Son is regarded as the second-largest right-bank tributary of the Ganga after the Yamuna. It joins the Ganga near
ne55808d6a8d.x: The Son is the second-largest right-bank tributary after the Yamuna and joins the Ganga near Maner, close to Patna.
ne55808d6a8d.tq: Combine rank and confluence location to identify a tributary.
xs: The **Son** joins the Ganga near **Maner, Patna** — option **(3)**.
**Farrukhabad** is the **Ramganga** confluence; **Etawah** is where the **Chambal** joins the Yamuna; **Hamirpur** is the **Betwa**'s.
xa: The Son rises at **Amarkantak**.
Bihar-Jharkhand MoU on Son water: **5.75 MAF** Bihar + **2 MAF** Jharkhand of **7.75 MAF** (**1973** **Bansagar Accord**).
**Rihand** (G.B. Pant Sagar), on the Son system, is the **largest artificial lake by volume**.

nbe6ecf15f4c.s: Gandak is known as which of the following names in Nepal?
nbe6ecf15f4c.x: The Gandak is known as Narayani in Nepal. Sadanira is its name in the Shatapatha Brahmana.
nbe6ecf15f4c.tq: Discriminate between regional and historical names of the same river.
xs: In Nepal the Gandak is the **Narayani** — option **(2)**.
**Sadanira** is its name in the **Shatapatha Brahmana**, not in Nepal.
The **Karnali** is the **Ghaghara**, a Mansarovar-area river.
xa: The Gandak enters India at **Valmikinagar**.
It is a **left-bank** (Himalayan) tributary of the Ganga.
Confluence order: **Ghaghara → Son → Gandak → Kosi**.

nd82a0dbc22d.s: The Betwa joins the Yamuna at:
nd82a0dbc22d.x: The Betwa joins the Yamuna at Hamirpur; the Chambal joins in Etawah.
xa: Other right-bank Yamuna tributaries: **Sindh, Ken**.
The Yamuna rises at **Yamunotri** and joins the Ganga at **Prayagraj**.
The Yamuna is the **westernmost and longest** Ganga tributary.

nf1edfa21845.s: Which one of the following is both the westernmost and the longest tributary of the Ganga?
nf1edfa21845.x: The Yamuna, rising at Yamunotri and joining at Prayagraj, is the westernmost and longest tributary of the Ganga. The Son is the second-largest right-bank tributary; the Ghaghara and Ramganga are left-bank Himalayan tributaries.
xs: The **Yamuna** is the **westernmost and longest** Ganga tributary — option **(3)** (PYQ 2025).
The **Son** is the **2nd largest right-bank** tributary after the Yamuna.
**Ghaghara** and **Ramganga** are **left-bank** Himalayan tributaries.
xa: **Mahananda** is the **easternmost** Ganga tributary.
Yamuna right-bank tributaries: **Chambal, Betwa, Sindh, Ken**; left bank: **Hindon**.
⚠ PYQ 2024: **Burhi Dihing** and **Dhansiri** are **Brahmaputra** tributaries, not the Ganga's.

n3163b1b8e49.s: The 2026 Bihar-Jharkhand MoU on sharing the waters of the Son, which ended a 25-year dispute, divides the 7.75 MAF available under which agreement?
n3163b1b8e49.x: The MoU allots 5.75 MAF to Bihar and 2 MAF to Jharkhand out of the 7.75 MAF set under the 1973 Bansagar Accord. The Indus Waters Treaty is with Pakistan, and the Ganga and Mahakali treaties are with Bangladesh and Nepal.
n3163b1b8e49.tq: Son water: Bansagar Accord 1973; Bihar 5.75 + Jharkhand 2 = 7.75 MAF.
xs: The **7.75 MAF** comes from the **1973** **Bansagar Accord** — option **(2)**.
The MoU gives **5.75 MAF** to **Bihar** and **2 MAF** to **Jharkhand**, ending a **25-year** dispute (1 Sep 2026).
The **Indus Waters Treaty, 1960** splits the **Indus** rivers, not the Son.
xa: The **Son** rises at **Amarkantak** and joins the Ganga near **Maner, Patna**.
**Rihand** (G.B. Pant Sagar), on the **Son** system, is the **largest artificial lake by volume**.
IWT: eastern rivers **Ravi, Beas, Sutlej** → India.

nindian-geography-1-17.x: The Ghaghra rises at Mapchachungo Glacier and meets the Ganga at Revilganj in Saran, Bihar.
n: Ghaghra originates at Mapchachungo Glacier. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Sharda joins Ghaghra in the plains. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Ghaghra meets Ganga at Revilganj in Saran district, Bihar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Ramganga joins Ganga near Kannauj, Uttar Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xa: ⚠ Other notes say the **Ramganga** joins at **Farrukhabad**.
The **Gandak** joins at **Sonpur** near **Patna**; it is the **Narayani** in Nepal.
The **Kosi** has the **Sun Kosi**, **Arun Kosi** and **Tamur Kosi** as tributaries.

nindian-geography-1-19.s: The last left-bank tributary of the Ganga is the:
nindian-geography-1-19.x: The Mahananda is the last left-bank tributary and joins the Ganga in West Bengal.
n: Mahananda is the last left-bank tributary of Ganga. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Mahananda joins Ganga in West Bengal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xa: The Mahananda is the **easternmost** Ganga tributary; the **Yamuna** is the **westernmost**.
Left-bank tributaries: **Ramganga**, **Gomati**, **Ghaghara**, **Gandak**, **Kosi**, **Mahananda**.
Confluence order below Prayagraj ends **Gandak → Kosi → Mahananda**.

nindian-geography-2-9.x: The Damodar flows into the Hugli.
n: Yamuna is a right-bank tributary of the Ganga. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Son is a right-bank tributary of the Ganga. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Damodar flows into the Hugli. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Chambal is a right-bank tributary of the Yamuna. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
xa: The **Yamuna** is the **longest tributary** of the Ganga; the **Son** is the 2nd largest right-bank tributary.
The **Barakar** is the Damodar's **main tributary** — the **Barakar–Damodar–Hugli chain**.
The **Damodar** rises at **Khamarpat Hill** and flows through a **rift valley**.

nindian-geography-2-11.s: Which of the following joins the Yamuna on its left bank?
nindian-geography-2-11.x: The Hindan joins the Yamuna from the left; the Chambal, Sind, Betwa and Ken join from the right.
n: Tons is a left-bank tributary of the Yamuna. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Hanuman Ganga is a left-bank tributary of the Yamuna. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Sasur Khaderi is a left-bank tributary of the Yamuna. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
xa: Other left-bank tributaries: **Tons**, **Hanuman Ganga**, **Sasur Khaderi**.
The **Betwa** joins at **Hamirpur**; the **Matatila** project lies on it.
The **Chambal** joins in **Etawah**.

nindian-geography-31-13.s: The Kosi Project is located in which combination of places?
nindian-geography-31-13.x: The Kosi Project is shared by Bihar and Nepal.
nindian-geography-31-13.tq: Recall the states of each project.
n: Kosi Project is located in Bihar and Nepal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
xs: The **Kosi Project** lies in **Bihar and Nepal** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**MP and Rajasthan** — **Chambal**; **AP and Karnataka** — **Tungabhadra**; **Jharkhand and West Bengal** — **Damodar Valley**.
xa: The **Kosi** is the "**Sorrow of Bihar**".
Its tributaries are the **Sun Kosi**, **Arun Kosi** and **Tamur Kosi**.
The **Kosi** plain of north Bihar is a huge **megafan**.

nindian-geography-31-14.s: The Chambal Valley Project is located in:
nindian-geography-31-14.x: The Chambal Valley Project serves MP and Rajasthan; the Tungabhadra Project serves AP and Karnataka.
n: Tungabhadra Project is located in Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
Chambal Valley Project is located in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
xa: **Telugu Ganga** (AP) **supplies Chennai**.
**Hirakud** and the **Mahanadi Project** are in **Odisha**.
The **Kosi** project is shared by **Bihar and Nepal**.

n305337d0adf.s: At which place does the Brahmaputra turn southward after flowing through Tibet?
n305337d0adf.x: The river, known as the Tsangpo or Yarlung Zangbo in Tibet, turns south at Namche Barwa.
n305337d0adf.tq: Associate a major change in river direction with its landmark location.
xs: The **Tsangpo** turns south at **Namche Barwa** — option **(2)**.
It enters Arunachal Pradesh as the **Dihang/Siang** via the **Dihang gorge**.
**Pasighat** is where **Dibang** and **Lohit** join; **Dhubri** marks the entry to Bangladesh.
xa: **Nanga Parbat** is where the **Indus** turns south.
Names: **Tsangpo** (Tibet) → **Dihang/Siang** → **Brahmaputra** (Assam) → **Jamuna** (Bangladesh).
It joins the Ganga (**Padma**) at **Goalundo**.

n9a82978614b.s: The Dihang becomes the Brahmaputra in Assam after the confluence of which rivers near Pasighat/Sadiya?
n9a82978614b.x: Dibang and Lohit join the Dihang near Pasighat/Sadiya, after which the combined river is called the Brahmaputra.
n9a82978614b.tq: Identify the tributaries responsible for a change in the river’s regional name.
xs: **Dibang** and **Lohit** join the **Dihang** near **Pasighat/Sadiya** — option **(1)**.
The combined river is the **Brahmaputra**, running down the **Assam valley**.
The **Rangeet** joins the **Teesta**; **Subansiri, Manas, Kameng, Sankosh** are right-bank tributaries in Assam.
xa: The Dihang enters via the **Dihang gorge** after turning at **Namche Barwa**.
Navigable **1,280 km** up to **Dibrugarh**.
**Majuli** lies in upper Assam.

nindian-geography-1-5.s: The Brahmaputra is known as the Jamuna in:
nindian-geography-1-5.x: The Brahmaputra is the Tsangpo in Tibet, the Dihang in Arunachal and the Jamuna in Bangladesh.
n: Brahmaputra is called Tsangpo or Sanpu in Tibet. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Brahmaputra is called Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Brahmaputra is called Jamuna in Bangladesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xa: It turns south at **Namche Barwa**; the **Dibang** and **Lohit** join near **Pasighat/Sadiya**.
It is navigable **1,280 km** up to **Dibrugarh**; called the "**sorrow of Assam**".
**Majuli** is a river island in the Brahmaputra in **Assam**.

n9a9c23eaf9a.s: The Brahmaputra rises at which glacier in the Kailash range?
n9a9c23eaf9a.x: The Brahmaputra rises at the Chemayungdung Glacier in the Kailash range, east of Lake Mansarovar.
n9a9c23eaf9a.tq: Distinguish the source glacier of one Himalayan river from those of other major rivers.
xs: The Brahmaputra rises at the **Chemayungdung Glacier** in the **Kailash range**, east of Mansarovar — option **(2)**.
**Gangotri** is the **Bhagirathi**'s source.
xa: In Tibet it is the **Tsangpo / Yarlung Zangbo**.
It turns south at **Namche Barwa**.
Length **2,900 km**; only **885 km** in India.

nc09d64fee91.s: Which one of the following is a right-bank tributary of the Brahmaputra?
nc09d64fee91.x: Subansiri is a northern, Himalayan or right-bank tributary of the Brahmaputra. Burhi Dihing, Dhansiri and Dikhu are southern or left-bank tributaries.
nc09d64fee91.tq: Apply the river-bank convention to distinguish northern and southern tributaries.
xs: **Subansiri** is a **right-bank** (north, Himalayan) tributary — option **(4)**.
**Burhi Dihing, Dhansiri, Dikhu** are **left-bank** (south) tributaries.
⚠ UPSC notes label Subansiri/Manas "left"; the standard convention treats the **north bank as right**.
xa: Other right-bank tributaries: **Kameng (Jia Bhareli), Manas, Puthimari, Pagladiya, Sankosh**.
The **Teesta** joins in **Bangladesh**.
**Dhansiri** rises in the **Nagaland hills**.

n291a0074593.s: The Brahmaputra is called the 'sorrow of Assam' mainly because of its:
n291a0074593.x: The Brahmaputra is called the 'sorrow of Assam' because of the floods it causes.
xa: It has many tributaries: right bank **Subansiri, Manas**; left bank **Burhi Dihing, Dhansiri**.
The **Kosi** is the "**Sorrow of Bihar**".
**Majuli** is the largest riverine island.

n0b7ecf3546c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the antecedent Himalayan rivers?
o: They existed before the Himalayan uplift.
They kept their courses by cutting deep gorges.
Valley-in-valley topography and paired terraces mark them.
Entrenched meanders are not found along them.
n0b7ecf3546c.x: Entrenched meanders are also a feature of antecedent rivers, so saying they are not found is wrong.
xa: The **Indus** turns south at **Nanga Parbat** through an **antecedent gorge**.
Himalayan rivers are **perennial** — fed by **rain + snowmelt**.
In the plains they **meander** and form **ox-bow lakes**.

n6d752a2d76f.s: The Ganga is navigable up to:
n6d752a2d76f.x: The Ganga is navigable up to Prayagraj, not only up to Farakka.
xa: ⚠ Length: **2,525 km** (APP: **2,465 km** total, **2,071 km** in India).
The **Yamuna** is the **westernmost and longest** tributary (PYQ 2025).
**Namami Gange** (**2014**) is implemented by the **NMCG**.
n6d752a2d76f.fixed: Ganga basin drains ~26% of India's area, not 40% (40% is population share)

n85fafb933db.s: About how much of the Brahmaputra's 2,900 km course lies in India?
n85fafb933db.x: Only about 885 km of the Brahmaputra's roughly 2,900 km course lies in India.
xa: Navigable **1,280 km** up to **Dibrugarh**.
**Majuli** (upper Assam) is the **largest riverine island** in the world (**60 km x 20 km**).
Floods make it the "**sorrow of Assam**".

nc7b7d48014b.s: The Teesta river rises at which lake in North Sikkim?
nc7b7d48014b.x: The Teesta (about 414 km) rises at Tso Lhamo Lake; the Rangeet is its largest tributary.
xa: The Teesta joins the Brahmaputra in **Bangladesh**.
The draft **2011** Teesta sharing treaty is still **stalled** (Jul 2026).
The Teesta is a **right-bank** tributary of the Brahmaputra.

nfa915209637.s: Which State has the highest number of polluted river stretches?
nfa915209637.x: Maharashtra has the most polluted river stretches (BOD above 3 mg/L).
xa: The Alliance extends the **River Cities Alliance** of Indian cities.
**Namami Gange** launched in **2014**.
Indus flows **+8%** vs Ganga **-17%** (IIT-Gandhinagar).

nindian-geography-1-12.s: The Rangeet is a tributary of the:
nindian-geography-1-12.x: The Rangeet joins the Teesta, not the Brahmaputra directly; the Manas and Kopili are direct Brahmaputra tributaries.
n: Manas is a tributary of Brahmaputra. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Kopili, or Kapili, is a tributary of Brahmaputra. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Rangeet is a tributary of Teesta. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Kishanganga is a tributary of Jhelum. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xa: Major Brahmaputra tributaries: **Dibang**, **Lohit**, **Subansiri**, **Kameng**, **Sankosh**, **Manas**, **Burhi Dihing**, **Dhansiri**, **Kopili**, **Teesta**.
The **Teesta** rises at **Tso Lhamo lake** and joins the Brahmaputra in **Bangladesh**.
The **Kameng** is also called the **Jia Bharali**.

n48da8f87616.s: On entering the plains, Himalayan rivers typically develop:
o: Meanders, shifting channels, ox-bow lakes and floodplains
n48da8f87616.x: The gentle gradient of the plains makes Himalayan rivers meander, shift channels and form ox-bow lakes and floodplains.
xa: The **Kosi** is the "**Sorrow of Bihar**"; the **Brahmaputra** the "**sorrow of Assam**".
**Majuli** (upper Assam) is the **largest riverine island** in the world.
Antecedent features: **valley-in-valley, paired terraces, entrenched meanders**.

na556428ab84.s: Baglihar, Salal and Dul Hasti projects are associated with which river?
na556428ab84.x: Baglihar, Salal and Dul Hasti are projects on the Chenab River in Jammu and Kashmir.
na556428ab84.tq: Group the three projects sharing one river instead of treating them as separate river associations.
xs: **Baglihar, Salal and Dul Hasti** are on the **Chenab** (J&K) — option **(3)**.
**Bhakra** is on the **Sutlej**; **Pandoh** on the **Beas**; **Tehri** on the **Bhagirathi**.
xa: **Salal** (**690 MW**, NHPC) is India's first project in the region under the **IWT**.
The Chenab forms from **Chandra + Bhaga** at **Tandi**.
The Chenab is a **western river** under the IWT.

nindian-geography-31-5.s: The Rihand Project is located in:
nindian-geography-31-5.x: Rihand is in Uttar Pradesh; Hirakud is in Odisha and Damodar Valley serves Jharkhand and West Bengal.
n: Bhakra–Nangal Project is located in Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
Damodar Valley Project is located in Jharkhand and West Bengal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
Hirakud Project is located in Odisha. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
Rihand Project is located in Uttar Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
xa: **Rihand** (**G.B. Pant Sagar**) is the **largest artificial lake by volume**.
The **Tilaiya** dam lies on the **Barakar** (Damodar system).
The **Sirhind Canal** draws from the **Sutlej** at **Ropar**.

nindian-geography-31-8.s: The Srisailam Project is on which river?
nindian-geography-31-8.x: Srisailam is on the Krishna, not the Tungabhadra; Nagarjuna Sagar is also on the Krishna and Pochampad on the Godavari.
n: Nagarjuna Sagar Project is constructed across the Krishna River. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
Pochampad Project is constructed across the Godavari River. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
Srisailam Project is constructed across the Krishna River. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 95-98]
xa: Both **Nagarjuna Sagar** and **Srisailam** lie on the **AP–Telangana border**.
The **Tungabhadra** project lies on the **Tungabhadra** (AP and Karnataka).
**Shivasamudram** is on the **Cauvery**.

n5260081662c.s: The perennial nature of the Himalayan rivers is primarily due to their being fed by
n5260081662c.x: Himalayan rivers receive water both from rainfall and from the melting of snow, which helps them maintain flow throughout the year.
n5260081662c.tq: Test the paired causes of a geographical characteristic rather than a single-source explanation.
xs: Himalayan rivers are **perennial** because they are fed by **rain + snowmelt** — option **(3)**.
PYQ 2023 Assertion-Reason: both true, and the reason explains the assertion.
xa: They are **antecedent**: they existed before the uplift and cut deep gorges.
The four river groups: **Himalayan, Deccan, Coastal, Inland** drainage.
The **Bhagirathi** rises at **Gomukh**, Gangotri glacier.

na6ad6d62e74.s: Salal, identified as India’s first project in the region under the Indus Waters Treaty, is a hydropower project on the
na6ad6d62e74.x: The Salal project is a 690 MW NHPC project on the Chenab and is identified as India’s first project in the region under the treaty.
na6ad6d62e74.tq: Match a project with the river on which it is situated.
xs: **Salal** is a **690 MW** NHPC project on the **Chenab** — option **(3)**.
It is India's **first project** in the region under the **IWT** (Jan 2026).
xa: Other Chenab projects: **Baglihar** and **Dul Hasti** (J&K).
Under the **IWT 1960**, the **Chenab** is a **western** river (primarily Pakistan).
**Bhakra** is on the **Sutlej**; **Pandoh** on the **Beas**.

nb4f1eff32cc.s: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, 1960, which group of rivers is allocated to India as the 'eastern rivers'?
nb4f1eff32cc.x: The eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej go to India, while the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab go primarily to Pakistan. The other options mix eastern and western rivers.
xs: The **eastern rivers** **Ravi, Beas and Sutlej** go to India — option **(2)**.
The **western rivers** **Indus, Jhelum and Chenab** go primarily to Pakistan; the other options mix the groups.
xa: The treaty dates from **1960**.
**Salal** (Chenab) is India's first project in the region under the **IWT**.
IIT-Gandhinagar study (**1980-2021**): Indus flows **+8%** vs Ganga **-17%**.

na1b2667682b.s: The Namami Gange programme is implemented by the
na1b2667682b.x: The National Mission for Clean Ganga implements the Namami Gange programme. The programme was launched as a flagship initiative in 2014.
na1b2667682b.tq: Apply the 'who implements the programme?' method to distinguish the executing body from related institutions.
xs: **Namami Gange** is implemented by the **National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG)** — option **(1)**.
The **Global River Cities Alliance** was launched **by** the NMCG; it does not implement Namami Gange.
xa: Namami Gange was launched as a flagship in **2014**.
The Alliance was launched at **COP28, Dubai (Dec 2023)**.
Polluted stretch = **BOD > 3 mg/L**; **Maharashtra** has the most.

nindian-geography-1-4.s: The Yamuna rises at the Yamunotri Glacier on the slopes of:
nindian-geography-1-4.x: The Yamuna rises at Yamunotri on the western slopes of Banderpunch Peak.
n: Yamuna originates at Yamunotri Glacier on the western slopes of Banderpunch Peak. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Chambal flows through Sawai Madhopur in Rajasthan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Chambal flows through Dholpur in Rajasthan before joining Yamuna. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Chambal joins Yamuna. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xa: The **Chambal** rises at **Mhow**, MP.
The **Yamuna** and **Ganga** meet at **Prayagraj**.
The **Chambal Valley** projects serve **Madhya Pradesh** and **Rajasthan**; the Chambal is known for **ravines**.

n76b568b3aa8.s: The east-flowing rivers of Peninsular India generally form ____ at their mouths.
n76b568b3aa8.x: East-flowing rivers form large deltas on the Bay of Bengal; west-flowing rivers more commonly form estuaries.
xa: East-flowing examples: **Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Mahanadi, Pennar, Palar, Vamsadhara, Nagavali**.
⚠ East-flowing = **deltas + irrigation**; west-flowing = **estuaries + hydropower**.
The **Godavari delta** is **Konaseema**, with **7 distributaries**.

n48336062889.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of west-flowing rivers?
n48336062889.x: Narmada, Tapi, Sabarmati and Mahi flow westwards towards the Arabian Sea. The other groups contain east-flowing rivers.
n48336062889.tq: Classify the entire group by its drainage direction before examining individual rivers.
xs: **Narmada, Tapi, Sabarmati, Mahi** all flow **west** to the Arabian Sea — option **(2)**.
**Pennar, Palar, Vamsadhara, Nagavali** and **Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Mahanadi** flow **east**.
Option **(4)** mixes east-flowing Godavari and Krishna with west-flowing **Periyar** and **Sharavati**.
xa: Other west-flowing rivers: **Periyar, Mandovi, Sharavati**.
West-flowing rivers form **estuaries, not deltas** → natural harbours.
**Narmada** (**1,312 km**) is the longest west-flowing river.

nbbaba2070e0.s: Which of the following river-linking proposals is identified as a priority for Andhra Pradesh?
o: Tapti Basin Mega Recharge and Aghanashini-Vedavathi
nbbaba2070e0.x: Vamsadhara-Penna intra-linking and the Godavari-Krishna link are identified as priorities for Andhra Pradesh.
nbbaba2070e0.tq: Match the state priority with the exact pair of proposed links.
xs: AP's priorities are **Vamsadhara-Penna intra-linking** and the **Godavari-Krishna link** — option **(1)** (TH, 27 Feb 2026).
Vamsadhara-Penna is **immediate**; Godavari-Krishna follows.
**Ken-Betwa**, **Par-Tapi-Narmada**, **Tapti Mega Recharge** and **Aghanashini-Vedavathi** are other states' projects.
xa: The CM defended the **Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar** link against **Telangana**'s objection (Feb 2026).
~**75%** of AP lies in the **Godavari, Krishna, Pennar** basins.
**Vamsadhara** tribunal (AP-Odisha): **2010**, award **2017**.

nd13fdb687d1.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the lifeline of Rayalaseema?
nd13fdb687d1.x: The Pennar is described as the lifeline of Rayalaseema.
nd13fdb687d1.tq: Use the regional association to identify the river.
xs: The **Pennar** is the **lifeline of Rayalaseema** — option **(3)**.
It rises in the **Nandi hills** (Karnataka).
xa: City: **Pennar-Nellore**.
AP interstate rivers: **Godavari, Krishna, Pennar, Vamsadhara, Nagavali**.
**Vamsadhara-Penna** intra-linking is AP's immediate priority.

n5d7b508c4d0.s: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, which of the following rivers is allocated to India?
n5d7b508c4d0.x: The eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej go to India; the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab mainly to Pakistan.
xa: The treaty has been **in abeyance** since **2025**.
India rejected the **Court of Arbitration**'s award as "**null and void**" (May 2026).
**Baglihar** and **Salal** (Chenab) sluices were closed after **Pahalgam** (2025).

nindian-geography-2-6.s: Which of the following is a right-bank tributary of the Mahanadi?
nindian-geography-2-6.x: The Ong, Tel and Jonk join from the right; the Seonath, Hasdeo, Mand and Ib join from the left.
n: Seonath/Shivnath is a left-bank tributary of the Mahanadi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Hasdeo is a left-bank tributary of the Mahanadi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Mand is a left-bank tributary of the Mahanadi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Ib is a left-bank tributary of the Mahanadi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Ong is a right-bank tributary of the Mahanadi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Tel is a right-bank tributary of the Mahanadi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
Jonk is a right-bank tributary of the Mahanadi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 9-15]
xa: Seonath is also called **Shivnath**; Hasdeo is also written **Hasdo**.
**Amritdhara** falls are on the **Hasdeo**, in Chhattisgarh.
The Mahanadi rises at **Sihawa** and flows through **Cuttack**.

ne2f97a28dde.s: Which of the following is an example of an antecedent river?
ne2f97a28dde.x: Antecedent rivers such as the Indus, Sutlej and Brahmaputra rise in the Trans-Himalaya and cut gorges as ranges rise.
xa: Himalayan rivers are **perennial** (rain + snowmelt).
Peninsular rivers are **older**, with graded valleys.
Himalayan rivers have **meandering, shifting** courses in the plains.

nba6bf167fa0.s: The Tapi flows through a rift valley between which ranges?
nba6bf167fa0.x: The Tapi's rift lies between the Satpura and Ajanta ranges; the Vindhya-Satpura rift belongs to the Narmada.
xa: The Tapi rises at **Multai** tank, **Satpura** plateau (Betul, MP).
**Tapti Basin Mega Recharge**: **MP and Maharashtra** MoU (PYQ 2025).
City pair: **Tapi-Surat**.

n56f1f5a4ff2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about rivers rising in the Aravallis?
o: The Sahibi is a south-flowing river.
The Banas is an east-flowing river.
The Luni ends in the Rann of Kutch.
The Sabarmati is a west-flowing river.
n56f1f5a4ff2.x: The Sahibi is a north-flowing river from the Aravallis, not south-flowing.
xa: **Sabarmati** flows past **Ahmedabad**.
The Luni is an Aravalli-born **desert** river.
The **Mahi** crosses the **Tropic of Cancer twice**.

nbee95db6105.s: The Narmada and Son rivers originate from which of the following places?
nbee95db6105.x: Both the Narmada and Son originate at Amarkantak in the Maikal range of Madhya Pradesh.
nbee95db6105.tq: Link the common source with the two rivers rather than selecting a source associated with only one river.
xs: **Narmada** and **Son** rise at **Amarkantak** in the **Maikal** range (MP) — option **(4)**.
**Multai** is the **Tapi**'s source; **Sihawa** the **Mahanadi**'s; **Mahabaleshwar** the **Krishna**'s.
xa: The Narmada flows west through a **rift valley** between the Vindhyas and Satpuras.
The Son flows north to the Ganga as a **right-bank** tributary.
**Narmada and Kaveri** basins are about the same size.

n6feb0fc580f.s: The Vamsadhara, Nagavali, Machkund, Sileru and Sabari rivers originate in the:
n6feb0fc580f.x: All five rivers originate in the Eastern Ghats.
xa: **Sileru** is a tributary of the **Sabari**; its upper course is the **Machkund**.
The **Sabari** joins the Godavari near **Kunavaram/K.R. Puram**.
**Vamsadhara** (AP-Odisha): tribunal **2010**, award **2017**.

n923af70f467.s: The Western Ghats are called the ‘Water Tower of Peninsular India’ mainly because they provide the sources of which group of rivers?
n923af70f467.x: The Western Ghats are described as the Water Tower of Peninsular India because they provide the sources of the Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri river systems.
n923af70f467.tq: Connect the descriptive geographical title with the river systems originating in the region.
xs: The Western Ghats are the "**Water Tower of Peninsular India**" for the **Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri** — option **(1)**.
**Narmada** rises at **Amarkantak**; **Luni, Sabarmati, Banas** rise in the **Aravallis**.
xa: **Godavari**: Brahmagiri-**Trimbakeshwar** hills (Nashik).
**Krishna**: **Mahabaleshwar**; **Kaveri**: **Brahmagiri / Talakaveri** (Kodagu).
**Mahanadi** rises at **Sihawa** (Chhattisgarh).

n5dcc3dec0f9.s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the longest Peninsular rivers in descending order?
n5dcc3dec0f9.x: The order is Godavari (1,465 km), Krishna (about 1,400 km), Narmada (1,312 km), Mahanadi (858 km) and Tapi (724 km).
n5dcc3dec0f9.tq: Compare adjacent river lengths instead of relying only on whether they flow east or west.
xs: Order: **Godavari > Krishna > Narmada > Mahanadi > Tapi** — option **(3)**.
xa: The Godavari is the **2nd longest** river in India.
The **Kaveri** is **805 km**.
**Ganga** (**2,525 km**) is India's longest river.

nba34541249c.s: Which river is regarded as India's longest river?
nba34541249c.x: The Ganga (2,525 km) is India's longest river; the Brahmaputra is longer overall but only 885 km lies in India.
xa: ⚠ Trap: overall length vs length **in India**.
**Godavari** (**1,465 km**) is the 2nd longest in India.

n9bfcab5c9e1.s: The Kabini is a tributary of the:
n9bfcab5c9e1.x: The Kabini is a right-bank tributary of the Kaveri, not the Krishna.
xa: Kaveri tributaries: left **Hemavathi, Shimsha, Arkavathi**; right **Kabini, Bhavani, Amaravati**.
⚠ Largest tributary: Godavari = **Pranhita**; Krishna = **Tungabhadra**.
Mahanadi left bank: **Seonath, Hasdeo**.

n93b828b4e6b.x: The Bhagirathi rises at Gomukh, at the Gangotri glacier.
n93b828b4e6b.tq: Identify the precise source rather than the source of another major Himalayan river.
xs: The **Bhagirathi** rises at **Gomukh** at the **Gangotri glacier** — option **(3)**.
**Amarkantak** is the source of the **Narmada and Son**.
xa: It joins the **Alaknanda** at **Devprayag** to form the Ganga.
Antecedent rivers like the **Indus, Sutlej, Brahmaputra** rise in the **trans-Himalaya**.
**Prayagraj**: Ganga + Yamuna confluence.

nde7bd385278.s: The westernmost and longest tributary of the Ganga is the:
nde7bd385278.x: The Yamuna is the westernmost and longest tributary of the Ganga; the Chambal and Betwa join it first.
xa: Left bank west to east: **Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi, Mahananda** (easternmost).
The **Betwa** is the **south-side** tributary in the APPSC 2025 key.
The **Chambal** rises at **Mhow** in the Vindhyas.

nbd1e622c69f.s: Hogenakkal Falls is on which river?
nbd1e622c69f.x: Hogenakkal, Sivasamudram and Chunchanakatte are all Kaveri waterfalls.
xa: Kaveri islands: **Srirangam** (with the Kollidam) and **Shivanasamudram**.
The Kaveri rises at **Brahmagiri / Talakaveri** (Kodagu).
Narmada falls: **Dhuandhar, Kapildhara, Dhardi**.

n8c5652a0ac9.s: Which is described as the longest lake of India?
n8c5652a0ac9.x: Vembanad, a brackish backwater in Kerala, is the longest lake; Chilika is Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon.
xa: **Loktak** is freshwater and a **Ramsar site**.
**Kolleru** (AP) is **freshwater**; **Pulicat** (AP-TN) is a **brackish lagoon**.
**Sambhar** lies in the **northern Aravallis**.

n189e000fc7c.s: Wular Lake is situated on which river and between which ranges?
o: Kaveri; Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats
n189e000fc7c.x: Wular is a freshwater lake on the Jhelum, situated between the Pir Panjal and Zaskar ranges.
n189e000fc7c.tq: Combine the waterbody, river and physiographic-location clues.
xs: **Wular** lies on the **Jhelum**, between the **Pir Panjal and Zaskar** — option **(4)**.
It is a **freshwater** lake in **J&K**.
xa: City: **Jhelum-Srinagar**.
**Loktak** (Manipur) is the freshwater lake with **phumdis**.
The Jhelum is a **western river** under the IWT.

nfff37640a5f.s: Aliabet is the largest island in which river?
nfff37640a5f.x: Aliabet is the largest island in the Narmada; Srirangam lies between the Kaveri and Kollidam.
xa: Srirangam is at **Tiruchirappalli**.
**Majuli** (Assam) is the **world's largest river island**, ~**60 x 20 km**.
Kaveri falls: **Sivasamudram, Chunchanakatte, Hogenakkal**.

nf5f2d4dca91.s: Kolleru, Andhra Pradesh's major lake, is a:
nf5f2d4dca91.x: Kolleru is a freshwater lake; Vembanad is a brackish backwater and Sambhar an inland saline lake.
xa: **Pulicat** (AP with TN) is a **brackish lagoon**.
**Lonar** (Maharashtra) is a **meteorite-impact crater** lake.
**Chilika** (Odisha) is **Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon**.

n58f4a3067e5.s: The Baglihar dam is on which river?
n58f4a3067e5.x: Baglihar is on the Chenab; Pandoh is on the Beas.
xa: In **2025** India closed **Baglihar**'s (and **Salal**'s) sluices after **Pahalgam**.
**Pandoh** feeds the **Beas-Sutlej link**.
Srisailam feeds **Telugu Ganga** and **Veligonda**.

na2d076d8f35.s: The idea of interlinking India's rivers was first proposed in the 19th century by:
na2d076d8f35.x: Sir Arthur Cotton first proposed river linking in the 19th century; the 1980 National Perspective Plan is implemented through the NWDA.
xa: NPP 1980 identified **30 links** = **14** Himalayan + **16** peninsular.
Critique: climate change erodes the "**surplus basin**" assumption.
**Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage** is at **Dowleswaram** on the Godavari.

nc5016042b76.s: Which State opposed the proposed Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar river link?
nc5016042b76.x: Telangana opposed the Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar link; climate change is also cited against the surplus-basin assumption.
xa: AP's CM defended the Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar link (Feb 2026).
AP's immediate priority: **Vamsadhara-Penna** intra-linking.
ILR idea: **Sir Arthur Cotton**, 19th century.

n2b2e2e4f63a.s: In May 2026, how did India respond to the Court of Arbitration's award under the Indus Waters Treaty?
o: It referred the award to the World Bank
It challenged the award at the ICJ
It rejected the award as 'null and void'
n2b2e2e4f63a.x: India rejected the award as 'null and void'; it has held the treaty in abeyance since 2025.
xa: Eastern rivers **Ravi, Beas, Sutlej** → India.
Western rivers **Indus, Jhelum, Chenab** → mainly Pakistan.
**Indus** flows are rising vs **Ganga** flows falling.

nindian-geography-1-6.x: The Krishna rises at Mahabaleshwar; the Godavari near Nashik, the Narmada at Amarkantak and the Tapi at Multai.
n: Godavari originates at Nasik, or Nashik, in Maharashtra. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Krishna originates at Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Narmada originates at Amarkantak in the Maikal Range. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Tapi originates at Multai in Betul district, Madhya Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xa: **Amarkantak** is also the source of the **Son**.
**Mahanadi** rises at **Sihawa** (Chhattisgarh); **Kaveri** at **Brahmagiri / Talakaveri** (Kodagu).
⚠ **Brahmagiri** = two sources: **Kaveri** (Kodagu) and **Godavari** (Nashik).

nindian-geography-1-7.s: Sihawa is associated with the origin of which river?
nindian-geography-1-7.x: The Mahanadi rises near Sihawa in Chhattisgarh.
nindian-geography-1-7.tq: Recall the source of each river.
n: Godavari originates at Nasik, or Nashik, in Maharashtra. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Sihawa is the origin of Mahanadi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Narmada originates at Amarkantak in the Maikal Range. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xs: **Sihawa** is the origin of the **Mahanadi** — option **(1)**.
**Cauvery** rises at **Brahmagiri / Talakaveri**, the **Narmada** at **Amarkantak** and the **Godavari** at **Nashik**.
xa: The Mahanadi flows through **Cuttack**; the **Kuakhai** is part of its delta near **Bhubaneswar**.
Mahanadi length: **858 km**.
Left-bank tributaries: **Seonath**, **Hasdeo**, **Mand**, **Ib**; right-bank: **Ong**, **Tel**, **Jonk**.

nindian-geography-1-25.s: Majuli is which of the following?
o: A delta of the Godavari on the eastern coast
A river island in the Brahmaputra in Assam
A waterfall on the Cauvery in Karnataka
A tributary of the Krishna in Telangana
nindian-geography-1-25.x: Majuli is a large river island in the Brahmaputra in Assam.
nindian-geography-1-25.tq: Recall the feature of each river.
n: Majuli is a river island in Brahmaputra in Assam. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Godavari forms a delta on the eastern coast. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Musi is a tributary of Krishna. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Shivasamudram Falls is associated with Cauvery. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xs: **Majuli** is **a river island in the Brahmaputra in Assam** — option **(2)**.
It is the **world's largest river island**, about **60 x 20 km**.
xa: **Charaichung (Majuli)** was set up in **1633** by Ahom king **Pratap Singha**; called Asia's first protected bird site.
**Srirangam** (Tamil Nadu) is an island between the **Kaveri** and **Kollidam**.
**Aliabet** (Gujarat) is the largest island in the **Narmada**.

nindian-geography-1-31.x: The Tapi rises at Multai in Betul district (MP) and flows west; Surat is near its mouth.
n: Tapi originates at Multai in Betul district, Madhya Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Tapi flows through Surat, Gujarat. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Tapi flows westward to the Arabian Sea. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xa: The Tapi flows between the **Satpura** and **Ajanta** ranges.
Tapi = **second longest west-flowing river** (**724 km**).
**Tapti Basin Mega Recharge:** **MP and Maharashtra** MoU (PYQ **2025**).

n60135a297e1.s: Which of the following is NOT a tributary of the Godavari?
n60135a297e1.x: Pranhita, Indravati, Manjira and Kinnerasani are Godavari tributaries; the Ghataprabha is a tributary of the Krishna.
xa: PYQ **2025**: **Indravati and Sabari** = the Godavari pair.
Pranhita is formed by **Wardha + Wainganga** and joins near **Kaleshwaram**.
⚠ Largest tributary: Godavari = **Pranhita**; Krishna = **Tungabhadra**.

nindian-geography-3-11.s: Bhalkund (Rahatgarh) Falls in Madhya Pradesh is on which river?
nindian-geography-3-11.x: Bhalkund, also called Rahatgarh, is on the Bina in Madhya Pradesh, not on the Narmada.
n: Bhalkund is also known as Rahatgarh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 15-16]
Bhalkund is on the Bina River. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 15-16]
Bhalkund is located in Madhya Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 15-16]
xa: Narmada falls: **Dhuandhar**, **Kapildhara**, **Dugdhdhara**, **Bheraghat**.
**Chulia** is on the **Chambal** (Rajasthan-MP region).

nap-geography-3-7.s: The Sabari River is also known by which name?
nap-geography-3-7.x: The Sabari is called the Kolab in Odisha. Langulya is the Nagavali, Araniyar the Arani and Matsya Kundala the Machkund.
nap-geography-3-7.tq: Recall the other names of rivers.
n: The Nagavali is also called Langulya. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 5-10]
The Machkhand is also called Matsya Kundala. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 5-10]
The Sabari is also called the Kolab River. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 5-10]
The Arani is also called Araniyar. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 5-10]
xs: The **Sabari** is also known as the **Kolab River** — option **(2)**.
**Matsya Kundala** is another name of the **Machkhand**, not the Sabari.
xa: The Sabari is the **main tributary** of the **Godavari**, rising in the **Sinkaram Hill ranges** of **Odisha**.
The **Sileru** is a major tributary of the Sabari.
PYQ **2025**: **Indravati and Sabari** = the Godavari pair.

na8b9c7c0b61.s: Which of the following is a right-bank tributary of the Godavari?
na8b9c7c0b61.x: Pravara, Manjira and Manair join the Godavari from the right; Purna, Pranahita, Indravati and Sabari join from the left.
xa: Largest Godavari tributary: **Pranhita** (**Wardha + Wainganga**), joining near **Kaleshwaram**.
**Indravati** (left bank) rises in **Kalahandi**, Odisha, and flows through **Bastar**.
**Kinnerasani** is also listed among Godavari tributaries.

n3d6f4c4cbde.s: The Godavari is popularly known as:
n3d6f4c4cbde.x: The Godavari is known as Dakshin Ganga or Dakshina Ganga.
xa: The Godavari is the **longest peninsular river** (**1,465 km**).
Delta: **Konaseema**; mouth near **Antharvedi**.
City: **Godavari-Rajamahendravaram**.

n6a28e467b0c.s: The Godavari delta is known as the:
n6a28e467b0c.x: The Godavari delta is Konaseema, with seven distributaries including the Gautami, Vasishta and Vainateya.
xa: The delta's mouth is near **Antharvedi**.
Godavari floods (Jul 2026): **5.2 lakh cusecs** released at **Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage, Dowleswaram**.
**150 relief camps** were set up in Polavaram district.

n5bccdb63e7b.s: The Pranhita, the largest tributary of the Godavari, is formed by the Wardha and the:
n5bccdb63e7b.x: The Pranhita is formed by the Wardha and Wainganga and joins the Godavari near Kaleshwaram; the Manjira is a right-bank tributary.
xa: ⚠ Largest tributary: Godavari = **Pranhita**; Krishna = **Tungabhadra**.
The **Wainganga** joins the Godavari via the Pranhita.
⚠ Some notes say the **Sileru** joins the Pranhita.

n1577d6a8ad0.s: The Sabari joins the Godavari near:
n1577d6a8ad0.x: The Sabari joins the Godavari near Kunavaram in Andhra Pradesh. The Pranhita joins near Kaleshwaram, and Sangameswaram is a Krishna–Tungabhadra confluence.
xa: The Sabari rises in the **Eastern Ghats**, Odisha.
**Sileru** (upper course **Machkund**) joins the Sabari at the **AP-Chhattisgarh-Odisha tri-junction**.
The Sabari is a **left-bank** Godavari tributary.

n72326281ab2.s: The Gandak is regarded as India's second-largest habitat for gharials after which river?
n72326281ab2.x: The Gandak is India's second-largest gharial habitat, after the Chambal.
n72326281ab2.tq: Use the ranking clue and identify the river placed first.
xs: The **Gandak** is India's **2nd largest gharial habitat** after the **Chambal** — option **(3)**.
The **Chambal** rises at **Mhow** and joins the **Yamuna**.
xa: City: **Chambal-Kota**.
The **Gandak** is a **left-bank** Ganga tributary.
The **Kosi** is also left-bank; the **Son** is right-bank.

nindian-geography-34-5.s: The largest salt-water lake of India is:
nindian-geography-34-5.x: Sambhar is the largest salt lake; Wular is the largest freshwater lake and Chilika the largest brackish lagoon.
n: The Ganga basin is the largest river basin in India. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 102-103]
Wular Lake is the largest freshwater lake in India. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 102-103]
Chilika Lake is the largest brackish-water lagoon. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 102-103]
Sambhar Lake is the largest salt-water lake. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 102-103]
xa: **Chilika** (Odisha) is **Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon** and India's first **Ramsar site** (**1981**).
**Wular** (J&K) is a freshwater lake on the **Jhelum**.
**Sambhar** (Rajasthan) is an inland **saline** lake in the northern **Aravallis**.

nindian-geography-34-10.s: The largest river island of India is:
nindian-geography-34-10.x: Majuli in Assam is the largest river island.
n: The Sundarbans, or Ganga–Brahmaputra Delta, is the largest delta. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 102-103]
The Thar Desert is the largest desert. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 102-103]
The Deccan Plateau is the largest plateau. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 102-103]
Majuli is the largest river island in India. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 102-103]
Majuli is in Assam. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 102-103]
xa: **Majuli** is the **world's largest river island**, on the **Brahmaputra**.
Largest **district** by area: **Kutch, Gujarat** (**45,674 km²**); largest **state**: **Rajasthan**.
**Aliabet** (Gujarat) is the largest island in the **Narmada**.

nindian-geography-1-26.s: Nanded is situated on which river?
nindian-geography-1-26.x: Nanded is on the Godavari, which flows from Nashik through Maharashtra, Telangana and AP.
n: Godavari flows from Nashik through Maharashtra, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Nanded is situated on Godavari. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Nashik is situated on Godavari. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Godavari forms a delta on the eastern coast. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xa: Godavari = longest peninsular river (**1,465 km**), **2nd longest** in India; ~**250 km** in AP.
The delta is **Konaseema**; mouth near **Antarvedi** through **7 distributaries**.
⚠ Largest tributary: **Pranhita** (Wardha + Wainganga); the AP sheet calls the **Sabari** the main tributary.

nindian-geography-1-42.s: Prayagraj is at the confluence of the Ganga and the:
nindian-geography-1-42.x: Prayagraj lies at the Ganga-Yamuna confluence; Varanasi, Patna and Bhagalpur are on the Ganga.
n: Varanasi is situated on Ganga. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Bhagalpur is situated on Ganga. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Patna is situated on Ganga. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Prayagraj is situated at the confluence of Ganga and Yamuna. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
xa: Other Ganga cities: **Haridwar**, **Fatehpur**, **Kanpur**.
**Yamuna** cities: **Delhi**, **Agra**, **Mathura**, **Etawah**.
The Ganga begins at **Devprayag** (Alaknanda + Bhagirathi).

nap-geography-3-12.s: Sir Arthur Cotton's anicut on the Godavari is at:
nap-geography-3-12.x: Cotton's anicut on the Godavari is at Dowleswaram; the river is 2.7 km wide at Rajahmundry.
n: The Godavari divides into seven branches in the erstwhile East Godavari and West Godavari districts. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 5-10]
The Godavari is 2.7 km wide at Rajahmundry. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 5-10]
Sir Arthur Cotton's dam on the Godavari is at Dhawaleswaram. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 5-10]
xa: Branches: **Gowthami**, **Vashista**, **Vinateya**, **Tulya**, **Bharadwaja**, **Koushika**, **Athreya**.
**Godavari floods (Jul 2026):** **5.2 lakh cusecs** released at the **Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage, Dowleswaram**.
Sir Arthur Cotton also proposed **ILR** (19th c.).

nap-geography-4-9.s: The Vasishta branch of the Godavari meets the sea at:
nap-geography-4-9.x: The Vasishta meets the sea at Antarvedi; the Gautami at Yanam and the Vainateya at Komaragiripatnam.
n: Gowthami is a branch of Godavari located at Yanam. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 10-15]
Vashista is a branch of Godavari located at Antarvedi. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 10-15]
Vinateya is a branch of Godavari located at Komarigiripatnam. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 10-15]
Tulya is a branch of Godavari located at Bendamoorlanka. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 10-15]
xa: **Bharadwaja** also reaches **Bendamoorlanka**; **Athreya** is at **Coringa village**.
**Koushika** is in the **Kakinada** / **Coringa delta** region.
The delta is called **Konaseema**.

n6fe7959822a.s: Which of the following is a right-bank tributary of the Krishna?
n6fe7959822a.x: Ghataprabha is a right-bank tributary of the Krishna. Bhavani joins the Kaveri, Sheonath the Mahanadi, and Musi is a left-bank Krishna tributary.
xa: Krishna right bank: **Tungabhadra, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Koyna**.
Krishna left bank: **Bhima, Dindi, Musi**.
⚠ PYQ 2025: **Ghataprabha** is a Krishna tributary, not the Godavari's.

nc57ab85f711.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Tungabhadra?
o: It is a left-bank tributary of the Krishna.
It is formed by the union of the Tunga and the Bhadra.
It joins the Krishna at Sangameswaram (Nandyal).
Vedavathi (Hagari) and Handri are its tributaries.
nc57ab85f711.x: The Tungabhadra is the largest right-bank tributary of the Krishna, not a left-bank one.
xa: Tungabhadra: **531 km**, ~**149 km** in AP.
**Raichur doab** lies between the **Krishna and Tungabhadra**.
**Vedavathi** joins the Tungabhadra at **Siruguppa**.

n0ed9a9f54e2.s: Which one of the following is a left-bank tributary of the Krishna?
n0ed9a9f54e2.x: Musi is a left-bank tributary of the Krishna. Tungabhadra, Ghataprabha and Malaprabha are classified as right-bank tributaries.
n0ed9a9f54e2.tq: Use bank-side classification to separate similar Krishna tributaries.
xs: The **Musi** is a **left-bank** Krishna tributary — option **(2)**.
**Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Tungabhadra** are **right-bank** tributaries.
xa: Other left-bank tributaries: **Bhima** (joins in Telangana), **Dindi**.
**Munneru** and **Paleru** join on the left bank in **AP**.
Urban river: **Musi - Hyderabad**.

na123d0d2ffb.x: The Musi rises in the Anantagiri hills of Telangana.
na123d0d2ffb.tq: Match the river with its exact source hills.
xs: The **Musi** rises in the **Anantagiri hills**, Telangana — option **(1)**.
It is a **left-bank** tributary of the **Krishna**.
xa: **Musi - Hyderabad**; **Mithi - Mumbai**; **Mula-Mutha - Pune**.
The **Bhima** also joins the Krishna in Telangana.
Krishna in AP: ~**485 km**, sea at **Hamsaladeevi**.

n351847da5a2.s: The Raichur Doab lies between the:
n351847da5a2.x: The Raichur Doab is the land tract lying between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers.
n351847da5a2.tq: Identify the two bounding rivers of a named doab.
xs: The **Raichur doab** lies between the **Krishna and Tungabhadra** — option **(4)**.
The Tungabhadra joins the Krishna at **Sangameswaram (Nandyal)**.
xa: Punjab doabs: **Bist** (Beas-Sutlej), **Bari** (Beas-Ravi), **Rechna** (Ravi-Chenab).
**Chaj** (Chenab-Jhelum), **Sind Sagar/Thal** (Jhelum-Indus).
The Tungabhadra is the **largest** Krishna tributary.

n97e4b24e5e5.s: The Krishna meets the Tungabhadra at:
n97e4b24e5e5.x: The Krishna meets the Tungabhadra at Sangameswaram (Nandyal). Hamsaladeevi is the Krishna's sea outlet and Antarvedi the Godavari's.
xa: Sangameswaram is in **Nandyal**.
The **Tungabhadra** is the **largest** Krishna tributary.
**Raichur doab** lies between the **Krishna and Tungabhadra**.

nindian-geography-1-11.s: Ujjain is situated on which river?
nindian-geography-1-11.x: Ujjain is on the Kshipra; Hyderabad is on the Musi and Jagdalpur on the Indravati.
n: Hyderabad is associated with Musi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Jagdalpur is situated on Indravati. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
Ujjain is situated on Kshipra. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-9]
