It does not raise salinity; alkaline soils are reclaimed with **gypsum**.
xa: **Strip cropping** and **contour ploughing** also check erosion.
**Soil conservation** prevents **soil erosion** (APPSC 2025).

n23d1aba3196.s: The FAO 2026 assessment found sustainable soil-management practices worsening in about what share of assessments?
n23d1aba3196.x: Practices were worsening in 58% of assessments and improving in only about 10%.
xa: The report covered **75 countries**.
Soil-biodiversity loss ranks **4th of 7** threats.

na2dbacd80af.s: The Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP) began in:
na2dbacd80af.x: IWMP started in 2009-10 and was merged into the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY in 2015-16.
xa: National programmes: **IWMP, NMSA, RKVY, Desert Development Programme, Soil Health Card**.
ICAR made national **C** and **P-factor** maps for erosion estimation.

n9eb19fc6c18.s: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched on 19 February 2015 at:
n9eb19fc6c18.x: It was launched at Suratgarh, Rajasthan; cards are issued every two years and the slogan is 'Swasth Dharaa, Khet Haraa'.
xa: **12 parameters** tested: N, P, K, S, micronutrients (Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B), physical properties.
**25.79 crore cards** generated up to Feb **2026**; **Uttar Pradesh** issued the most.
Village-Level Soil Testing Labs target: **7,500** (**2023-26**).

n6786bd0a3f9.s: How many parameters are tested under the Soil Health Card scheme?
n6786bd0a3f9.x: The scheme tests 12 parameters: N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, pH, EC and organic carbon.
n6786bd0a3f9.tq: Use the exact quantitative value after identifying the complete parameter list.
xs: The scheme tests **12 parameters** — option **(3)**.
They cover **N, P, K, S**, the micronutrients **Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B**, and physical properties.
xa: Cards come **every two years**.
**FY 2025-26**: **97.53 lakh** samples collected, **92.87 lakh** tested.

n3a95e5280d7.s: Which group consists only of soils generally described as acidic?
n3a95e5280d7.x: Laterite, peaty and forest soils are generally acidic. Black soil and saline-alkaline soils are neutral to alkaline, and arid, alluvial and red soils are not listed as acidic, so every other group includes a non-acidic soil.
n3a95e5280d7.tq: Identify the common chemical reaction shared by the three soils.
xs: **Laterite, peaty and forest** soils are acidic — option **(2)**.
**Black** and **saline-alkaline** soils are **neutral to alkaline**, so groups with them are wrong.
xa: Peaty soils are **black, heavy and highly acidic**.
**Lime** reclaims **acidic** soils; **gypsum** reclaims **alkaline** soils.

n1c7a741d4a9.s: Very intense bursts of rainfall can make soil drier because they:
o: Always infiltrate completely and recharge the soil
Exceed infiltration capacity, causing runoff or evaporation instead of recharge
Convert all soil organic carbon directly into clay
Prevent surface water from moving downslope
n1c7a741d4a9.x: When rainfall intensity exceeds infiltration capacity, water runs off or evaporates rather than recharging the soil. This drying effect can offset the benefit of greater annual rainfall.
n1c7a741d4a9.tq: Apply the infiltration-excess mechanism to an observed rainfall scenario.
xs: Intense bursts **exceed infiltration capacity**, so water **runs off or evaporates** instead of recharging soil — option **(2)**.
Two **2026** studies (**Nature**, **Nature Geoscience**) link concentrated rainfall to drier soils.
xa: This drying effect roughly **cancels the gain** from more annual rain.
⚠ **Intensity matters more than total rainfall** for erosion.

n7b0451f5e8c.s: Red soils cover about what share of Andhra Pradesh's cultivated area?
n7b0451f5e8c.x: Red soils cover about 60%; black soils about 25%, deltaic alluvium 5–6% and laterite about 1%.
xa: AP has **six** agro-climatic zones (APSES **2024-25**).
Laterite occurs in AP but is **poor in nitrogen**.

n8c91e841121.s: Which region of India is poor in minerals because it is made of recent alluvium?
n8c91e841121.x: The Gangetic plains are recent alluvium and poor in minerals, while the peninsular plateau is mineral-rich.
xa: **Archaean/Dharwar** rocks hold metallic minerals.
**Tertiary rocks** in the NE and offshore hold **petroleum**.
**Gondwana** rocks hold coal (**Damodar, Mahanadi**).

nindian-geography-43-13.s: Gondwana rocks are the main source of India's:
nindian-geography-43-13.x: Gondwana rocks hold coal; Dharwar rocks copper, Tertiary rocks petroleum and gas, and metamorphic rocks garnet.
n: Dharwar Rocks are associated with copper. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
Gondwana Rocks are associated with coal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
Tertiary sedimentary rocks are associated with petroleum. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
Tertiary sedimentary rocks are associated with natural gas. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
Metamorphic rocks are associated with garnet. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
xa: Tertiary rocks occur in **Assam**, **Gujarat**, **Rajasthan** and offshore basins.
The **Gangetic plains** are recent alluvium, poor in minerals.

nindian-geography-43-16.s: Which rock basin of Andhra Pradesh is associated with barytes, asbestos, diamond and uranium?
nindian-geography-43-16.x: The Cuddapah basin has barytes, asbestos, copper, iron, lead, diamond and uranium.
n: The Cuddapah Basin is associated with barytes. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
The Cuddapah Basin is associated with asbestos. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
The Cuddapah Basin is associated with copper. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
The Cuddapah Basin is associated with iron. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
The Cuddapah Basin is associated with lead. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
The Cuddapah Basin is associated with diamond. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
The Cuddapah Basin is associated with uranium. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
Tertiary sedimentary rocks are associated with petroleum. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
Tertiary sedimentary rocks are associated with natural gas. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
Deccan Trap is also called basalt. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
Deccan Trap/basalt is associated with black soil. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
Black soil is also called Regur. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-115]
xa: **Mangampet** (Kadapa) barytes is among the world's largest deposits.
**Malwa** Deccan Trap basalt is poor in metallic ores.

nchemistry-3-46.s: The chemical formula of dolomite is:
nchemistry-3-46.x: Dolomite is CaMg(CO₃)₂; magnesite is MgCO₃, rock salt NaCl and carnallite KCl·MgCl₂·6H₂O.
n: The formula of Rock Salt is NaCl. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
The formula of Carnallite is KCl·MgCl₂·6H₂O. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
The formula of magnesite is MgCO₃. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
The formula of dolomite is CaMg(CO₃)₂. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
xa: Other sodium ores: **trona**, **Chile saltpetre**.
**Sylvine** = **KCl**.

nchemistry-1-18.s: Rock salt is an ore of:
nchemistry-1-18.x: Sodium comes from rock salt; potassium from sylvine and carnallite, magnesium from magnesite and calcium from limestone.
n: Rock salt is a main mineral of sodium. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Sylvine and carnallite are main minerals of potassium. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Magnesite and dolomite are main minerals of magnesium. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Limestone and gypsum are main minerals of calcium. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xa: **Fluorspar** (**CaF₂**) is another calcium ore.
Carnallite is an ore of both **potassium** and **magnesium**.

nd0968054ca5.s: The North-Eastern Plateau mineral belt of India is rich in:
o: Coal, iron ore, manganese, mica, bauxite and copper
nd0968054ca5.x: The North-Eastern Plateau belt is rich in coal, iron ore, manganese, mica, bauxite and copper.
xa: The belt also yields **uranium**; it spans **Chota Nagpur**, the **Odisha plateau**, WB and parts of Chhattisgarh.
Mines here: **Koderma** (mica), **Jaduguda** and **Turamdih** (uranium), **Lohardaga** (bauxite) — all in **Jharkhand**.
Its coal comes from **Gondwana** rocks of the **Damodar** and **Mahanadi** valleys.

n8325e9414e2.s: The beach sands of Srikakulam and Visakhapatnam are known for:
o: Ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet and monazite
n8325e9414e2.x: These beach sands contain ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet and monazite.
xa: **Ilmenite** and **rutile** are ores of **titanium**.
**Monazite** gives **thorium and rare earths** (Kerala, AP, Odisha sands).
**Kerala** sands are noted for **atomic minerals**.
**Budget 2026-27** proposes **rare-earth corridors** in Odisha, Kerala, **AP** and TN.

n9527c5fdd99.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the predominant type of iron ore is which one of the following?
n9527c5fdd99.x: Most of Andhra Pradesh's iron ore is haematite, and Anantapur ranks first in the State for iron ore. Magnetite has the most iron, but it is not AP's main ore; limonite and siderite are lower grades.
n9527c5fdd99.tq: Apply the State-specific mineral fact rather than the general national grade comparison.
xs: Most of AP's iron ore is **haematite** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Magnetite** has the most iron but is not AP's main ore; **limonite** and **siderite** are lower grades.
xa: **Anantapur** ranks **1st** in AP for iron ore.
Haematite holds **60-70%** Fe; it is the most used commercially.
AP's **Dharwar** rocks hold iron ore and gold.

n4294218f6db.s: With respect to iron ore, India is:
o: Dependent on imports for almost all its needs
n4294218f6db.x: India is self-sufficient in iron ore and a net exporter (about 46 million tonnes exported in 2023–24).
xa: India is **near self-sufficient** in **bauxite**.
About **75%** of **lead** needs are imported.

nchemistry-3-12.s: Bailadila in Chhattisgarh is famous for high-grade:
nchemistry-3-12.x: Bailadila is famous for high-grade haematite; ilmenite occurs in beach sands from Kerala to Odisha.
n: Bailadila iron ore is high grade. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Titanium occurs as ilmenite in beach sands from the Kerala to Odisha coast. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Iron occurs as haematite at Bailadila in Chhattisgarh. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
xa: **Monazite** beach sands (thorium): **Kerala**, **Tamil Nadu**, **Odisha**, **Andhra Pradesh**.
Ilmenite = **FeTiO₃**, an ore of **titanium**.

nchemistry-3-22.x: Carnallite (KCl·MgCl₂·6H₂O) is an ore of both potassium and magnesium.
n: Carnallite is an ore of potassium (K). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Magnesite is an ore of magnesium (Mg). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Dolomite is an ore of magnesium (Mg). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Carnallite is an ore of magnesium (Mg). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Limestone is an ore or source of calcium (Ca). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
xa: **Sylvine** (**KCl**) is the other potassium ore.
**Talc** is a **magnesium silicate**, the **softest mineral**.

nchemistry-3-24.s: Which of the following is NOT an ore of manganese?
nchemistry-3-24.x: Ilmenite is a titanium ore; pyrolusite, manganite and hausmannite are manganese ores.
n: Pyrolusite is an ore of manganese (Mn). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Manganite is an ore of manganese (Mn). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Hausmannite is an ore of manganese (Mn). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Ilmenite is an ore of titanium (Ti). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
xa: Pyrolusite = **MnO₂**.
Manganese areas: **Dharwar**, **Keonjhar**, **Chitradurga**, **Balaghat**.

nchemistry-3-38.x: Cinnabar is mercury sulphide; galena is lead, chalcopyrite copper and zinc blende zinc.
n: Galena is an ore of lead (Pb). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
The formula of galena is PbS. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Cinnabar is an ore of mercury (Hg). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
The formula of cinnabar is HgS. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Chalcopyrite is an ore of copper (Cu). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
The formula of chalcopyrite is CuFeS₂. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Zinc Blende is an ore of zinc (Zn). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
The formula of Zinc Blende is ZnS. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
xa: Zinc blende is called **Black Jack**.
**Cerussite** is another lead ore; **smithsonite** (**ZnCO₃**) another zinc ore.

nchemistry-3-43.s: The chemical formula of iron pyrites is:
nchemistry-3-43.x: Iron pyrites is FeS₂; magnetite is Fe₃O₄, siderite FeCO₃ and limonite FeO(OH)·nH₂O.
n: The formula of magnetite is Fe₃O₄. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
The formula of limonite is FeO(OH)·nH₂O. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
The formula of siderite is FeCO₃. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
The formula of Iron Pyrites is FeS₂. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
xa: ⚠ **Magnetite** = highest Fe (best ore); **Haematite** = most used commercially; **Siderite** = lowest grade.
Haematite: **60-70%** Fe; limonite **40-60%** Fe.

nchemistry-3-77.s: Thorium occurs in Indian beach sands in the form of:
nchemistry-3-77.x: Thorium occurs as monazite and titanium as ilmenite in beach sands.
n: Titanium occurs as ilmenite in beach sands from the Kerala to Odisha coast. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Thorium occurs as monazite in beach sands. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Monazite beach sands occur in Tamil Nadu. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Monazite beach sands occur in Andhra Pradesh. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Copper, zinc, and lead occur in combined form as sulphides. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
xa: Monazite is a **rare-earth phosphate**.
Thorium sands: **Kerala**, **Tamil Nadu**, **Odisha**, **Andhra Pradesh**.

nchemistry-1-5.s: Haematite and magnetite are ores of:
nchemistry-1-5.x: Iron comes from haematite and magnetite; aluminium from bauxite, copper from chalcopyrite and zinc from zinc blende.
n: Bauxite is a main ore of aluminium. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Cryolite and corundum are minerals of aluminium. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Haematite and magnetite are main ores of iron. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Chalcopyrite and cuprite are main ores of copper. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Zinc blende and smithsonite are main ores of zinc. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xa: Other zinc ores: **zincite**, **franklinite**.
Other copper ores: **chalcocite**, **malachite**, **azurite**.

nchemistry-1-10.s: Which of the following is a sulphide mineral?
nchemistry-1-10.x: Galena (PbS) is a sulphide; smithsonite and calcite are carbonates and cassiterite an oxide.
n: The formula of galena is PbS. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
The formula of cinnabar is HgS. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
The formula of smithsonite is ZnCO₃. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
The formula of cassiterite is SnO₂. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Cinnabar is mercury sulphide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xa: Other sulphides: **zinc blende (ZnS)**, **argentite (Ag₂S)**, **chalcocite (Cu₂S)**.
Copper, zinc and lead occur in nature as **sulphides**.

n140d7f31c8f.s: The Central mineral belt of India, with iron ore, manganese, coal and limestone, mainly covers:
n140d7f31c8f.x: The Central belt covers Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh, with iron ore (Bailadila), manganese (Balaghat), coal and limestone.
xa: **Vizag Steel Plant** gets its iron ore mainly from **Bailadila** (Chhattisgarh).
**Balaghat** (MP) also has copper at **Malanjkhand**.
MP's manganese areas: **Balaghat** and **Chhindwara**.

n407ada63f32.s: Neyveli in the Southern mineral belt is a major area of:
n407ada63f32.x: Neyveli is a major lignite area of the Southern belt, which also has iron ore, gold, manganese and chromite.
xa: The Southern belt (**Karnataka-AP-TN**) has **iron ore, gold, manganese, chromite** and **lignite**.
AP's new private gold mine is **Jonnagiri / Swarnagiri** (Kurnool), commercial from **24 Jun 2026**.
**Boksampalli** gold blocks lie in the **Ramagiri-Penakacherla greenstone belt**, Anantapur.

n7a486aaf99b.s: The Khetri copper area is located in:
n7a486aaf99b.x: Khetri (Jhunjhunu) is in Rajasthan; Malanjkhand is the copper area of Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand's copper is in Singhbhum.
xa: Jharkhand's copper is in **Singhbhum**.
⚠ **Zawar** = lead-zinc, not copper.
AP's copper-zinc-silver is at **Agnigundala and Bondalamottu** (Guntur).

nb5c83fd52c1.s: The chromite deposits of the Kondapalli Hills are associated with which district of Andhra Pradesh?
nb5c83fd52c1.x: Chromite occurs in the Kondapalli Hills of Krishna district in Andhra Pradesh.
nb5c83fd52c1.tq: Link the named hill range with its district, not with a nearby mineral district.
xs: **Kondapalli hills** chromite lies in **Krishna** district — option **(4)** is correct.
**Anantapur** leads iron ore; **Kurnool** has cement limestone and Jonnagiri gold; **Srikakulam** has beach sands.
xa: National chromite: Odisha (**Sukinda**), Karnataka (**Hassan, Chikmagalur**), **Manipur**.
AP's nickname is **"Ratna Garbha"**.
AP uranium is at **Thummalapalli** (Kadapa).

nd1db7c1aa71.s: Visakhapatnam Steel Plant obtains its iron ore mainly from which area?
nd1db7c1aa71.x: Visakhapatnam Steel Plant gets its iron ore mainly from Bailadila in Chhattisgarh.
nd1db7c1aa71.tq: Identify the source area of a major industrial plant by matching plant and ore field.
xs: **Vizag Steel Plant** gets its iron ore mainly from **Bailadila** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Bailadila** is in Bastar, **Chhattisgarh** (Central belt).
**Bellary** (Karnataka), **Keonjhar** (Odisha) and **Singhbhum** (Jharkhand) are other iron-ore areas, not its main source.
xa: The Central belt also has **Balaghat** manganese.
India exported ~**21 Mt** iron ore in **2022-23** and ~**46 Mt** in **2023-24**.
⚠ **Malanjkhand** = copper; **Sukinda** = chromite.

n6aa4a4638d0.s: The Zawar mines are associated with:
n6aa4a4638d0.x: Zawar is associated with lead-zinc; Koderma with mica, Bailadila with iron ore and Khetri with copper.
xa: **Koderma** is in **Jharkhand**; **Bailadila** in **Chhattisgarh**; **Khetri** and **Zawar** in **Rajasthan**.
Mica belts: **Koderma-Gaya-Hazaribagh**, **Nellore**, **Bhilwara-Ajmer**.
⚠ **Malanjkhand** (MP) is also copper.

n1d9197cdd72.s: Thummalapalli in YSR Kadapa district is known for deposits of:
n1d9197cdd72.x: Thummalapalli in YSR Kadapa is associated with uranium; Agnigundala and Bondalamottu in Guntur have copper, zinc and silver.
xa: AP chromite: **Kondapalli** (Krishna); AP barytes: **Mangampet** (Kadapa).
AP mineral revenue: **Rs 2,707 crore** up to **8 Jan 2026** (SES 2025-26).

n0c79208793e.s: India is described as being near self-sufficient in which one of the following minerals?
n0c79208793e.x: India is near self-sufficient in bauxite. About 75 per cent of India's lead requirements are imported.
n0c79208793e.tq: Use the self-sufficiency versus import-dependence contrast.
xs: India is **near self-sufficient** in **bauxite** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Lead** is the opposite case: about **75%** of needs are **imported**.
The notes give no self-sufficiency claim for **copper** or **gold**; **Chile** is India's largest supplier, mainly **copper**.
xa: India is **self-sufficient in iron ore** and a **net exporter**: ~**21 Mt** (**2022-23**), ~**46 Mt** (**2023-24**).
**Odisha** leads bauxite (Kalahandi, Sambalpur, Koraput).
Bauxite forms by **residual weathering** (laterite-linked).

nindian-geography-8-1.s: Panna in Madhya Pradesh is known for:
nindian-geography-8-1.x: Panna is known for diamonds; Koderma for mica, Keonjhar for manganese and Sukinda for chromite.
n: Keonjhar is in Odisha. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Manganese is found at Keonjhar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Kodarma/Koderma is in Jharkhand. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Mica is found at Kodarma/Koderma. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Panna is in Madhya Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Diamond is found at Panna. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Sukinda is in Odisha. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Chromite is found at Sukinda. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
xa: Manganese also at **Dharwar** and **Chitradurga** (Karnataka) and **Balaghat** (MP).
AP diamonds: **Vajrakarur**, **Anantapur**.
AP chromite: **Kondapalli hills** (Krishna).

nindian-geography-8-4.s: Digboi in Assam is associated with:
nindian-geography-8-4.x: Digboi is an oilfield; Zawar has zinc and Tummalapalle in AP has uranium.
n: Bilaspur is in Chhattisgarh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Zawar is in Rajasthan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Zinc is found at Zawar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Uranium is found in AP. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Thorium is found in Kerala coastal sands. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Dolomite is found at Bilaspur. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
xa: AP uranium: **Thummalapalli** (YSR Kadapa).
Jharkhand uranium mines: **Turamdih**, **Jaduguda**.
Thorium comes from **monazite** beach sands.

nindian-geography-8-6.s: Bastar, Bilaspur, Dantewada and Jashpur are bauxite areas of:
nindian-geography-8-6.x: All four are bauxite areas of Chhattisgarh.
n: Bastar is in Chhattisgarh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Bauxite is found at Bastar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Bilaspur is in Chhattisgarh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Bauxite is found at Bilaspur. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Dantewada is in Chhattisgarh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Bauxite is found at Dantewada. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Jashpur is in Chhattisgarh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Bauxite is found at Jashpur. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
xa: Other Chhattisgarh bauxite: **Kanker**, **Kawardha/Kabirdham**, **Korba**, **Raigarh**, **Surguja**; Amarkantak.
**Odisha** leads in bauxite (**Koraput**, **Lanjigarh**, **Kalahandi**).
Bauxite forms by **residual weathering** (laterite-linked).

nindian-geography-8-7.s: The Noamundi iron-ore area is located in:
nindian-geography-8-7.x: Noamundi and Singhbhum are in Jharkhand; Badampahar is in Odisha, Bailadila in Chhattisgarh and Kudremukh in Karnataka.
n: Badampahar is in Odisha. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Iron ore is found at Badampahar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Sundargarh is in Odisha. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Iron ore is found at Sundargarh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Dalli-Rajhara is in Chhattisgarh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Iron ore is found at Dalli-Rajhara. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Bailadila is in Chhattisgarh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Iron ore is found at Bailadila. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Noamundi is in Jharkhand. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Iron ore is found at Noamundi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Singhbhum is in Jharkhand. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Iron ore is found at Singhbhum. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Kudremukh is in Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Iron ore is found at Kudremukh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Bellary/Ballari is in Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Iron ore is found at Bellary/Ballari. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
xa: **Bailadila** gives high-grade **haematite**; it feeds the **Vizag Steel Plant**.
AP iron ore is mostly **haematite**; **Anantapur ranks 1st**.
India is **self-sufficient in iron ore** and a net exporter.

nindian-geography-8-13.s: Koraput, Lanjigarh and Kalahandi are bauxite areas of:
nindian-geography-8-13.x: Koraput, Lanjigarh and Kalahandi are Odisha bauxite areas.
n: Koraput is in Odisha. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Bauxite is found at Koraput. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Lanjigarh is in Odisha. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Bauxite is found at Lanjigarh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Kalahandi is in Odisha. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Bauxite is found at Kalahandi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
xa: **Odisha** leads bauxite; **Sambalpur** is another site.
AP bauxite: **Araku, Ananthagiri, Chintapalli, Paderu**.
**Jharkhand** bauxite: **Palamu**; **Lohardaga** mine.

nindian-geography-8-16.s: Which of the following is still worked as India's main gold mine?
nindian-geography-8-16.x: Hutti in Karnataka is India's main working gold mine; the Kolar Gold Fields closed in 2001.
n: Mosabani is in Jharkhand. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Copper is found at Mosabani. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Alwar is in Rajasthan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Copper is found at Alwar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Gold is found in Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Kolar Gold Fields is in Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Gold is found at Kolar Gold Fields. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Hutti is in Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Gold is found at Hutti. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
xa: **Khetri** (Rajasthan) and **Malanjkhand** (MP) are also copper.
AP gold: **Ramagiri** (Anantapur); **Swarnagiri (Jonnagiri)**, Kurnool.
Copper = the **non-ferrous mineral of the north-west** (Aravalli).

nindian-geography-8-22.s: Mainpat in Surguja district of Chhattisgarh is known for:
nindian-geography-8-22.x: Surguja has bauxite at Mainpat; Dantewada in Chhattisgarh has tin.
n: Surguja is in Chhattisgarh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Limestone is found in Vindhya. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Salt is found in Rajasthan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Tin is found at Dantewada. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Tin is found in Chhattisgarh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
xa: **Kaimur–Rohtas** (Bihar) is another limestone area.
**Rajasthan** also leads in **gypsum**.

nindian-geography-8-5.s: Kaimur–Rohtas in Bihar is associated with:
nindian-geography-8-5.x: Kaimur–Rohtas in Bihar has limestone; Rajasthan has gypsum.
n: Kaimur–Rohtas is in Bihar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Limestone is found at Kaimur–Rohtas. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
Gypsum is found in Rajasthan. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 24-29]
xa: Gypsum uses: **cement**, **fertiliser**, **plaster**.
Limestone uses: cement, steel flux, glass, fertiliser; **Kurnool** cement-grade in AP.
Most **limestone blocks** operationalised in FY2025-26 were in **Gujarat**.

nb5b41d08fc7.s: In the South-Western Plateau mineral belt, Kerala is noted for:
nb5b41d08fc7.x: The belt spans Karnataka, Goa, the TN uplands and Kerala; Kerala is noted for monazite.
xa: The belt has **high-grade iron ore, manganese, limestone** and **bauxite**.
Karnataka gold mines: **Hutti** (state-run) and **Kolar** (closed).
**Monazite** is the source of **thorium and rare earths** (Kerala, AP, Odisha sands).

nae773585877.s: The North-Western (Aravalli) mineral belt is known mainly for:
o: Non-ferrous minerals such as copper and lead-zinc
nae773585877.x: The North-Western belt is known for non-ferrous minerals, plus gypsum, salt, limestone and Gujarat's petroleum.
xa: **Copper** is the non-ferrous mineral of the north-western (Aravalli) region (**APPSC-GS 2025**).
Mines: **Khetri** (Jhunjhunu) = copper; **Zawar** (Udaipur) = lead-zinc.
**Rajasthan** is the leading **gypsum** state and leads **lead** output.

n9e6b83711d7.s: Araku, Ananthagiri, Chintapalli and Paderu in Andhra Pradesh are known for deposits of:
n9e6b83711d7.x: These Eastern Ghats agency areas hold bauxite; mining clashes with PVTG rights and Eastern Ghats ecology.
xa: AP bauxite also conflicts with **FCA/FRA**.
The **Eastern Ghats Mobile Belt** (khondalite, charnockite) holds bauxite, manganese, graphite.
Bauxite forms by **residual weathering** (laterite-linked).

nd2b87247a18.s: Which one of the following non-metallic minerals is chiefly used in the manufacture of cement and as a flux?
nd2b87247a18.x: Limestone is used in cement manufacture and as a flux. It is associated with Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat.
nd2b87247a18.tq: Use the mineral–application association rather than relying only on the state distribution.
xs: **Limestone** is used in **cement** and as a **steel flux** (also glass, fertiliser) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Kyanite** and **sillimanite** are **refractories**; **asbestos** is for fire-proofing and cement sheets.
xa: Limestone states: **MP, Rajasthan, AP** (Kurnool cement-grade), **Gujarat**.
In FY2025-26 **Gujarat** operationalised the most limestone blocks (**4**).
AP's **Kurnool group** holds cement limestone.

n77ae85b4f9d.s: Sona Pahar in Meghalaya is an important occurrence of:
n77ae85b4f9d.x: Sona Pahar is associated with sillimanite; Lapsa Buru with kyanite and the Cuddapah basin with asbestos.
xa: Gypsum is used in **cement, fertiliser, plaster**.
Kyanite and sillimanite are **refractories**; sillimanite also in **Kerala** sands.
**Barytes** at **Mangampet** (Kadapa) is among the world's largest deposits.

nce6e3cee67c.s: Mangampet in Kadapa district of Andhra Pradesh is internationally notable for deposits of which mineral?
nce6e3cee67c.x: Mangampet in Kadapa is among the world's largest deposits of barytes. Barytes is used in oil-well drilling mud.
nce6e3cee67c.tq: Link the distinctive place name with the specialised mineral use.
xs: **Mangampet** (Kadapa) has among the world's largest **barytes** deposits — option **(2)** is correct.
Barytes is used in **oil-well drilling mud**.
**Gypsum** leads in **Rajasthan**; **kyanite** at **Lapsa Buru** (Jharkhand).
xa: Barytes is linked to the **Cuddapah and Vindhyan** supergroups.
AP's **Cuddapah basin** — one of India's largest **Proterozoic** basins — gives barytes and asbestos.
AP asbestos: **Pulivendula, Kadapa**.

nf93af26d410.s: Over 90% of India's coking-coal reserves are in:
nf93af26d410.x: Over 90% of coking-coal reserves are in Jharia; it is a Critical and Strategic Mineral under the MMDR Act, 1957.
xa: India's first list of **30 critical minerals** came in **June 2023**.
**Gondwana** rocks hold coal (**Damodar, Mahanadi**).
Critical and strategic block auctions: **46** blocks sold in **6** tranches; **7th tranche (19 blocks)** opened **23 Mar 2026**.

n5776c1dab98.s: The rare-earth corridors proposed in the Union Budget 2026–27 cover Odisha, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and:
n5776c1dab98.x: The proposed rare-earth corridors cover Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
xa: **Monazite** gives **thorium and rare earths** (Kerala, AP, Odisha sands).
AP's CM ordered **comprehensive mineral mapping**, with value addition through **APMDC** (**1 Jul 2026**).
**India-US critical minerals and rare earths framework**: **May 2026**.

nadfcb1f44a1.s: The Critical Mineral Recycling Incentive Scheme, covering e-waste, lithium-ion batteries and other scrap, is a:
nadfcb1f44a1.x: It is a Central Sector scheme covering e-waste, lithium-ion batteries and other scrap.
xa: It runs from **FY2025-26 to FY2030-31**.
It sits alongside the **National Critical Mineral Mission**, which also uses recovery from **overburden and tailings**.
India's first list of **30 critical minerals**: **June 2023**.

n903dda7e74f.s: The royalty formula upheld by the Supreme Court in July 2026 uses an Average Sale Price that includes:
n903dda7e74f.x: The upheld formula's Average Sale Price includes royalty, DMF and NMET; royalty itself is not a tax (MADA v. SAIL, 2024).
xa: The **2026 Bill** restricts states' power to tax mineral rights.
**DMF** and **NMET** were created by the **2015** amendment.
Swarnagiri pays AP a **4% royalty**.

n98f490fa8df.s: The Dharwar system of Andhra Pradesh is associated mainly with:
n98f490fa8df.x: The Dharwar system (over 2,500 million years old) holds iron ore and gold; barytes and asbestos belong to the Cuddapah basin.
xa: ⚠ Older notes place Dharwar in **Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, East Godavari** instead.
**Kurnool group**: cement limestone.
**Eastern Ghats Mobile Belt**: bauxite, manganese, graphite.

n275af77783c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Swarnagiri Gold Mine?
o: It was renamed from the Jonnagiri Gold Mine
It is an underground mine operated under a ten-year lease
It belongs to the Jonnagiri greenstone belt
It is located in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district
n275af77783c.x: Swarnagiri is an open-pit mine with a 30-year lease, not an underground mine on a ten-year lease.
xa: Developer: **Geomysore**, **Rs 405 crore**; **4% royalty** to AP.
Area **597.820 ha**; renamed by **G.O. Ms. No.181**.
India's **first private-sector gold mine after Independence**.

nap-geography-6-11.s: At which place do apatite reserves and production rank first?
nap-geography-6-11.x: Kasipatnam in Visakhapatnam district leads in apatite (and vermiculite) reserves and production. Bethamcherla is a limestone centre.
nap-geography-6-11.tq: Recall the leading place for each mineral.
n: Apatite reserves and production rank first at Kasipatnam in Visakhapatnam. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 18-20]
xs: Apatite reserves and production rank first at **Kasipatnam in Visakhapatnam** — option **(2)**.
**Jammalamadugu** (Kadapa) is known for high-quality **limestone**; **Bethamcherla** (Kurnool) is a major limestone centre.
xa: **Vermiculite** also ranks first at **Kasipatnam**.
AP beach sands (**Srikakulam**, **Visakhapatnam**) hold ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet, monazite.

nchemistry-3-47.s: The chemical formula of gypsum is:
nchemistry-3-47.x: Gypsum is CaSO₄·2H₂O; limestone and calcite are CaCO₃ and fluorspar CaF₂.
n: The formula of limestone or calcite is CaCO₃. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
The formula of gypsum is CaSO₄·2H₂O. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
The formula of fluorspar is CaF₂. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
xa: Gypsum is mined mainly in **Rajasthan**.
Dolomite (**CaMg(CO₃)₂**) contains both calcium and magnesium.

ne7ca2b9466a.s: Which one of the following groups of minerals is characteristically associated with placer deposits?
ne7ca2b9466a.x: Gold, tin and platinum are associated with placer deposits formed in alluvial sands. Coal, gypsum and salt are typical of sedimentary beds, while copper and lead commonly occur in veins or lodes.
ne7ca2b9466a.tq: Use the mineral group as the clue to distinguish placer deposits from lodes and sedimentary beds.
xs: **Gold, tin and platinum** are placer minerals — option **(3)** is correct.
**Tin, copper, lead** (and zinc) form **veins / lodes**; **coal, gypsum, salt** form **sedimentary beds**.
**Bauxite** comes from **residual weathering**.
xa: Placers are concentrations of **heavy minerals** in alluvial sands.
**Gold** as a placer mineral is the **APPSC 2024** key.
Beach sands hold **ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet, monazite**.

n085d3ac401c.s: Bauxite deposits are generally formed by:
n085d3ac401c.x: Residual weathering may produce laterite-linked bauxite; veins/lodes give tin, copper, zinc and lead.
xa: **Placer** deposits (alluvial sands) give **gold**, tin, platinum.
AP bauxite: **Araku, Ananthagiri, Chintapalli, Paderu**.
The **Eastern Ghats Mobile Belt** in AP holds bauxite, manganese and graphite.

nce08831d181.s: Mica is used in the electrical and electronic industries because it is:
nce08831d181.x: Mica is valued as an insulator, not a conductor; it occurs in pegmatite veins in granite, gneiss and schist.
xa: Main belts: **Koderma-Gaya-Hazaribagh** (Jharkhand-Bihar), **Nellore** (AP), **Bhilwara-Ajmer** (Rajasthan).
⚠ Phlogopite and pegmatite → mica (PYQ, APPSC-G1 **2023** key).
Erstwhile **Nellore** ranks **first** in AP for mica production and reserves.

n190b66671f9.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh is one of India's major mica belts?
n190b66671f9.x: The major mica belts are Nellore, Koderma–Gaya–Hazaribagh and Ajmer–Bhilwara.
xa: **Nellore** is historically famous for mica.
**SPSR Nellore** also has quartz, feldspar, silica sand, vermiculite.
**Koderma** (Jharkhand) is a mica mine.

nchemistry-3-7.s: Which of the following metals is NOT found in the free (native) state?
nchemistry-3-7.x: Aluminium is very reactive and found combined, mainly as bauxite; gold, silver and platinum occur native.
n: Gold occurs in the free or native state. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Silver occurs in the free or native state. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Platinum occurs in the free or native state. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Aluminium occurs in combined form as bauxite. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
xa: **Copper** also occurs native (bottom of the reactivity series).
Gold is a **placer** mineral (APPSC **2024** key).

nchemistry-3-70.s: Which of the following metals is too reactive ever to be found free in nature?
nchemistry-3-70.x: K, Na, Ca, Mg and Al are at the top of the reactivity series and never occur free; Au, Ag and Pt occur native.
n: Potassium, sodium, calcium, magnesium, and aluminium are at the top of the reactivity series. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Potassium, sodium, calcium, magnesium, and aluminium are never found free in nature. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Gold, silver, platinum, and copper are at the bottom of the reactivity series. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
Gold, silver, platinum, and copper are found in the native state. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 10-16]
xa: Copper, zinc and lead occur combined as **sulphides**.
Sodium, potassium, calcium and magnesium occur as **salts or carbonates**.

n79487e0acc7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Critical Mineral Mission?
o: It targets 1,200 domestic exploration projects by 2030-31
It bars PSUs and private firms from acquiring mineral assets abroad
It aims to acquire 50 overseas mineral assets
A national stockpile is one of its tools
n79487e0acc7.x: The mission supports PSU and private acquisition of mineral assets abroad.
xa: Aim: secure critical-mineral supply from **domestic and foreign** sources.
It targets output of at least **15** critical minerals.
Other tools: exploration incentives, recovery from **overburden and tailings**, fast-track approvals.

ndc49af23432.s: KABIL, the company associated with overseas acquisition of critical mineral assets, is a joint venture of which organisations?
ndc49af23432.x: KABIL is a joint venture of National Aluminium Company Limited, Hindustan Copper Limited and Mineral Exploration Corporation Limited.
ndc49af23432.tq: Test composition by identifying the exact public-sector partners.
xs: **KABIL** is a JV of **NALCO + HCL + MECL** — option **(4)** is correct.
**NMDC, SAIL, GAIL, NTPC, ONGC** and **Coal India** are not KABIL partners in the notes.
xa: KABIL holds **15,703 ha in Catamarca, Argentina** for **lithium** (**Aug 2026**).
India-**Argentina** mineral-exploration agreement: **Feb 2025** (**APPSC 2025** key).
The **National Critical Mineral Mission** targets **50 overseas assets**.

nf859c81f9ef.s: India’s partnership with Australia announced in 2022 concerning critical minerals primarily relates to which minerals?
nf859c81f9ef.x: India’s 2022 partnership with Australia concerns lithium and cobalt.
nf859c81f9ef.tq: Use the partner–mineral association rather than selecting common Indian mineral pairs.
xs: India's **2022** partnership with **Australia** concerns **lithium and cobalt** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Chile** is the copper supplier; **barytes/asbestos** and **iron ore/manganese** are domestic minerals, not this deal.
xa: GSI's **'Uncover India'** is with **Geoscience Australia**.
**KABIL** holds lithium land in **Catamarca, Argentina**.
**India-US** framework signed **May 2026**.

nc093fbb1de7.s: Under the recent MMDR amendment, States must approve adding a critical mineral to a lease within:
nc093fbb1de7.x: States must approve within 30 days; the amendment also removed captive-sale limits.
xa: The **2025** amendment also let **new minerals** be added to a lease and removed the **captive-sale limit**.
The **2021** amendment let captive mines **sell part of output**.
The **2015** amendment brought **auction-only** allotment, **DMF** and **NMET**.

n807c33ab4fb.s: India's first list of critical minerals, released by the Ministry of Mines in June 2023, contained how many minerals?
n807c33ab4fb.x: The June 2023 list named 30 critical minerals; 50 is the overseas-asset target of the Critical Mineral Mission.
xa: It was released by the **Ministry of Mines**, identified by an **expert committee** (**APPSC-GS 2023**).
The Mission aims at output of at least **15** critical minerals.
⚠ Also **30**: mineral blocks operationalised in **FY2025-26**.

n3c8c0eef682.s: In February 2025, India signed a mineral-exploration agreement with which country, where KABIL holds lithium blocks in Catamarca province?
n3c8c0eef682.x: The Feb 2025 agreement was with Argentina, where KABIL holds 15,703 ha in Catamarca for lithium. Chile is India's largest supplier (mainly copper), Australia was the 2022 lithium-cobalt partner, and Bolivia is not mentioned.
xs: The **Feb 2025** mineral-exploration agreement was with **Argentina** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Chile** is India's largest supplier (mainly copper); **Australia** was the **2022** lithium-cobalt partner; **Bolivia** is not mentioned.
xa: **KABIL** (NALCO + HCL + MECL) holds **15,703 ha** in **Catamarca** for lithium.
This was the **APPSC 2025** key.
**India-US** framework: **May 2026**.

n88f93c74205.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the MMDR Act, 1957?
o: It is administered by the Ministry of Mines
It excludes petroleum, natural gas and atomic minerals
Major minerals in the First Schedule are regulated by the Centre
Minor minerals such as building stone, gravel and sand are regulated by the Centre
n88f93c74205.x: Minor minerals such as building stone, gravel and sand are regulated by the States.
xa: The Act was amended in **2015** and **2025** (also **2021**).
⚠ The **2026 Bill** restricts states' power to **tax mineral rights**.
**MADA v. SAIL** (**2024**): royalty is **not a tax**.

nbde51bfd75c.s: Which of the following was a key feature of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2015?
o: Replacement of the MMDR Act by the National Mineral Policy, 2019
Removal of all State powers over minor minerals
Auction-only allotment of mineral concessions and creation of DMF and NMET
Prohibition of captive mining in every circumstance
nbde51bfd75c.x: The 2015 amendment introduced auction-only allotment and created the District Mineral Foundation and the National Mineral Exploration Trust.
nbde51bfd75c.tq: Associate the amendment year with its distinctive institutional and allocation reforms.
xs: The **2015** amendment brought **auction-only allotment** and created **DMF** and **NMET** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **National Mineral Policy 2019** replaced the **2008 policy**, not the MMDR Act; minor minerals stay with the **states**.
xa: **2021**: **NMET** made a **non-profit autonomous body**; captive mines allowed to sell part of output.
**PMKKKY (2015)** uses **DMF** funds for mining-affected people and areas.
**2025**: **captive-sale limit removed**.

n8e792869b79.s: Which one of the following was NOT a stated feature of the 2025 amendment to the MMDR Act?
o: New minerals may be added to an existing lease.
All minor minerals were placed under exclusive Central regulation.
The limit on sale of captive-mined output was removed.
Prior central approval was removed for composite-licence auctions of specified minerals.
n8e792869b79.x: The 2025 amendment did not place all minor minerals under exclusive Central regulation. It allowed addition of new minerals to leases, removed the captive-sale limit and changed prior-approval requirements for specified composite-licence auctions.
n8e792869b79.tq: Reject the option that reverses the Centre–State regulatory distinction.
xs: **Exclusive Central regulation of all minor minerals** was **not** a 2025 feature — option **(2)** is the answer.
Minor minerals (building stone, gravel, sand) stay with the **states**.
The 2025 amendment did let **new minerals** be added to a lease, **removed the captive-sale limit**, and dropped prior central approval for **composite-licence** auctions.
xa: Those auctions cover **bauxite, iron ore, limestone, manganese**.
**Apr 2026** amendment: states must approve a critical mineral addition **within 30 days**.
Source: **IYB 2026**.

nde9e2e8c3cd.s: The 2026 Bill concerning mineral rights and mineral-bearing land primarily sought to:
o: Prohibit royalty collection by the Union Government
Transfer all offshore minerals to private ownership without auction
Restrict States' power to tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing land through uniform rates
nde9e2e8c3cd.x: The Bill, passed in August 2026, sought uniform rates by restricting States' power to tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing land. It was criticised on grounds of fiscal federalism.
nde9e2e8c3cd.tq: Identify the bill from its authority-and-taxation consequence.
xs: The **2026 Bill** sought to **restrict states' power to tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing land** for **uniform rates** — option **(4)** is correct.
It did not abolish the **MMDR Act 1957**; offshore leases are only by **auction** (OAMDR 2023).
xa: It passed in **Aug 2026** and was criticised on **fiscal federalism** grounds.
⚠ **MADA v. SAIL** (**2024**) had held states **may tax** mineral-bearing land.
**SC (Jul 2026)** upheld the Centre's **royalty formula**.

n18c8c1effea.s: The Pradhan Mantri Khanij Kshetra Kalyan Yojana is associated with:
o: Using DMF funds for mining-affected people and areas, with yearly audit
Financing only offshore mineral exploration by private companies
Providing export subsidies for iron ore
Regulating petroleum and natural gas production
n18c8c1effea.x: PMKKKY uses District Mineral Foundation funds for the welfare of mining-affected people and areas and provides for a yearly audit.
n18c8c1effea.tq: Identify the scheme by matching its fund source with its beneficiary group.
xs: **PMKKKY (2015)** uses **DMF funds** for **mining-affected people and areas**, with a **yearly audit** — option **(1)** is correct.
Offshore leases fall under the **OAMDR Act**; petroleum and natural gas are outside the Ministry of Mines' MMDR scope.
xa: **DMF** was created by the **2015** MMDR amendment.
**NMET** became a **non-profit autonomous body** in **2021**.
**National Mineral Policy 2019** replaced the **2008** policy.

nfbe564527d1.s: The National Mineral Policy, 2019 replaced which earlier policy?
nfbe564527d1.x: The National Mineral Policy, 2019 replaced the National Mineral Policy, 2008.
nfbe564527d1.tq: Use the policy-year sequence to distinguish the replaced policy from later amendments.
xs: The **National Mineral Policy 2019** replaced the **2008** policy — option **(1)** is correct.
**2015** is the auction-only MMDR amendment year, not a policy year.
xa: **PMKKKY (2015)**: DMF funds for mining-affected areas.
**Art. 297** vests offshore minerals in the **Union**.
**OAMDR Amendment Act 2023**: offshore production leases only by **auction**.

n7f9b499387f.s: In Mineral Area Development Authority v. Steel Authority of India (2024), the Supreme Court held that:
o: Royalty is a tax, so States cannot tax mineral-bearing land
Royalty is not a tax, and States may tax mineral-bearing land
Only Parliament may levy any tax on minerals
Offshore minerals vest in the States
n7f9b499387f.x: MADA v. SAIL (2024) held that royalty is not a tax and that States may tax mineral-bearing land. Option A states the reverse, option C denies the States' power, and offshore minerals vest in the Union under Art. 297.
n7f9b499387f.tq: MADA v SAIL 2024: royalty is not a tax.
xs: **MADA v. SAIL** (**2024**) held **royalty is not a tax** and **states may tax mineral-bearing land** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) states the reverse; offshore minerals vest in the **Union** under **Art. 297**.
xa: **SC (Jul 2026)** upheld the Centre's ad valorem **royalty formula**.
The **2026 Bill** (**Aug 2026**) restricts states' power to tax mineral rights.
It is criticised on **fiscal federalism**.

n15f66f19c89.s: Which State accounted for the largest share in the value of mineral production in India in 2021–22?
n15f66f19c89.x: Odisha had the highest share, at 44.11%, in the value of mineral production in 2021–22.
n15f66f19c89.tq: Identify the top-ranked state from the comparative share table.
xs: **Odisha** had the top share — **44.11%** — of the value of mineral production in **2021-22** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Karnataka** was next at **17.34%**; **Jharkhand** **4.36%**; **MP** **2.96%**.
xa: This was the **APPSC 2023** key.
⚠ By **IMYB 2022** the top producers are **Rajasthan**, then **MP and AP** — a different measure.
**Odisha** also leads **bauxite** and has iron ore at **Keonjhar, Bonai, Mayurbhanj**.

n2d9f628ccf6.s: The ‘Uncover India’ project is being undertaken by GSI in collaboration with which organisation to probe deep-seated deposits?
n2d9f628ccf6.x: GSI’s ‘Uncover India’ project is being carried out with Geoscience Australia to probe deep-seated deposits.
n2d9f628ccf6.tq: Identify the exact international technical partner in a bilateral scientific project.
xs: GSI's **'Uncover India'** is with **Geoscience Australia**, probing **deep-seated deposits** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **USGS**, **British** and **Canadian** surveys are not named in the notes.
xa: India-**Australia** (**2022**) partnership covers **lithium and cobalt**.
The Ministry of Mines administers **GSI** and **IBM**.
**National Critical Mineral Mission** targets **1,200** domestic exploration projects.

nb6e27a5373a.s: Which Article of the Constitution vests offshore minerals in the Union?
nb6e27a5373a.x: Article 297 vests offshore minerals in the Union; the 2023 amendment allows production leases only through auction.
xa: The parent law is the **Offshore Areas Mineral (D&R) Act 2002**.
Onshore, the **2015** MMDR amendment also made allotment **auction-only**.
Minor minerals are regulated by **states**.

n42bd209c72a.s: According to the Geological Survey of India, approximately what share of India’s area is landslide-prone?
n42bd209c72a.x: The GSI estimates that approximately 12.6–15 per cent of India’s area, or about 0.42 million square kilometres, is landslide-prone.
n42bd209c72a.tq: Tests a hazard-exposure range and its associated agency.
xs: GSI puts **12.6-15 per cent** of India as landslide-prone — option **(1)** is correct.
That is about **0.42 million sq km**, mostly in **hilly** areas.
xa: Landslide regions: **Himalaya, NE, Western Ghats** (incl. **Nilgiris**), **Eastern Ghats, Vindhyas**.
Landslide zonation maps are **probabilistic**.
GSI's warning system is under the **LANDSLIP** project.

n80f573ab5b5.s: How many seismic zones does India's official IS 1893 (BIS) zoning map presently have?
n80f573ab5b5.x: The official map has four zones: II, III, IV and V.
xa: The **2002 revision** merged old **Zone I into Zone II** after the **1993 Killari** quake.
**Zone V** quakes: **Kutch and NE**; **AP has no Zone V** area.
⚠ **IS 1893** = seismic design criteria and zoning map; **IS 13920** = ductile detailing.

n8ad7b10abf2.s: After the 1993 Killari earthquake, the 2002 seismic-zone revision merged old Zone I into:
n8ad7b10abf2.x: Killari struck a low-risk area, leading to the 2002 revision in which old Zone I was merged into Zone II.
xa: Killari (**Latur**, Maharashtra) was an **intraplate** quake.
The current map has **4 zones: II-V**.
Exam angle: **"zones merged"** (I into II).

n8779dbd19f2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the proposed revision of India's seismic zoning map?
o: It was based on Probabilistic Seismic Hazard Assessment
The four-zone IS 1893 map (Zones II–V) still applies
It used PGA values of 0.15–0.75 g
It was implemented nationwide in March 2026
n8779dbd19f2.x: The Centre rolled the revision back in March 2026 after criticism of its methodology and cost, so it was not implemented.
xa: The **2002** revision merged **Zone I into Zone II** after the **1993 Killari** quake.
The revision gave PGA values **0.15-0.75 g** for Zones II-VI, from **69,519** events.
⚠ **IS 1893** = seismic design criteria; **IS 13920** = ductile detailing.

n9caed985277.s: In India's building-safety standards, IS 13920 covers:
n9caed985277.x: IS 13920 covers ductile detailing; IS 1893 covers seismic design criteria, and the National Building Code also applies.
xa: ⚠ IS 1893 also carries the **zoning map**.
**Vulnerability Atlas** published by **BMTPC** (**1 Apr 2026**).
**Himalayan** safer codes delayed over **cost** (**22 Mar 2026**).

n3f949eae79f.s: The Killari earthquake of 1993 is classified as a:
n3f949eae79f.x: The 1993 Killari earthquake in Latur, Maharashtra, was an intraplate earthquake.
n3f949eae79f.tq: Distinguishes two similarly named earthquake events by their type.
xs: The **1993 Killari** quake (**Latur**, Maharashtra) was an **intraplate** quake — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ The **reservoir-induced** case is **Koyna (1967)**.
xa: Killari struck a **low-risk** area and led to the **2002** revision (Zone I merged into II).
**Bhuj** (Kutch) quake: **26 Jan 2001**.
**Zone V**: Kutch and NE.

n06d85a9bfa9.s: The snow avalanche at Badrinath (Mana) in February 2025 killed workers of which organisation?
n06d85a9bfa9.x: The Badrinath-Mana avalanche resulted in the death of Border Roads Organisation workers.
xa: On **Badrinath-Mana (NH-7)**, **hanging-glacier** and avalanche risk is rising as settlement grows (**Apr 2026**).
**Chamoli** (**2021**): glacier/rock-ice flood.
**Kedarnath** (**June 2013**): cloudburst and flash flood.

ndisaster-management-23-6.s: Which body is the focal point for the Sendai Framework and global disaster risk reduction?
ndisaster-management-23-6.x: The UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) is the focal point for Sendai and global DRR.
n: The United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction is the focal point for the Sendai Framework. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 51-53]
The United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction focuses on global disaster-risk reduction. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 51-53]
The Pacific Tsunami Warning Center issues tsunami warnings for the Pacific Ocean. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 51-53]
xa: The **ITIC** is also in **Honolulu**, supported by **UNESCO-IOC** and **NOAA**.
The **IOC** (Paris) coordinates **global tsunami-warning systems**.

ndisaster-management-23-11.s: The IOC-coordinated Indian Ocean Tsunami Warning System was established after the Indian Ocean tsunami of:
ndisaster-management-23-11.x: The system was set up after the 2004 tsunami, with regional centres in India, Indonesia, Australia and others.
n: The Indian Ocean Tsunami Warning System is coordinated through the IOC. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 51-53]
The Indian Ocean Tsunami Warning System has regional centres in India, Indonesia, Australia, and other countries. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 51-53]
The Indian Ocean Tsunami Warning System was established after the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 51-53]
xa: India's centre: **ITEWC** at **INCOIS, Hyderabad**, operating since **2007**.
Most exposed: **east coast and A&N Islands**.

n63000f8d06b.s: Which organisation is developing a regional Landslide Early Warning System under the LANDSLIP project?
n63000f8d06b.x: The Geological Survey of India is developing a regional Landslide Early Warning System under the LANDSLIP project.
n63000f8d06b.tq: Tests the correct institutional responsibility for a disaster-warning project.
xs: The **Geological Survey of India** is building a regional **Landslide Early Warning System** under **LANDSLIP** — option **(2)** is correct.
**BIS** issues building codes; IMD handles weather and cyclone warnings, not this project.
xa: GSI estimates **12.6-15%** of India as landslide-prone.
GSI monitors crustal strain via **34 GNSS stations**.
Zonation maps are **probabilistic**.

ndisaster-management-18-5.s: Landslide Hazard Zonation mapping is classed as which type of mitigation measure?
ndisaster-management-18-5.x: Hazard zonation mapping is non-structural; retaining walls are structural and hill building codes regulatory.
n: Retaining walls are structural landslide mitigation measures. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
Landslide Hazard Zonation mapping is a non-structural landslide mitigation measure. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
Mountain-specific building codes should be enforced. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
Retaining walls against steep slopes are a landslide mitigation measure. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
xa: Other non-structural measures: **Early Warning Systems**, **land-use regulation**, **awareness**.
GSI is building a **Landslide Early Warning System** under **LANDSLIP**.

ndisaster-management-18-16.s: Rock bolting, wire mesh, drainage improvement and slope grading are which type of landslide-mitigation measure?
ndisaster-management-18-16.x: All four are structural landslide-mitigation measures.
n: Rock bolting is a structural landslide mitigation measure. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
Wire mesh is a structural landslide mitigation measure. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
Drainage improvement is a structural landslide mitigation measure. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
Slope grading is a structural landslide mitigation measure. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
xa: Landslide-prone area: **12.6-15%** of India (GSI).
Zonation maps are **probabilistic**.

nb34784e5035.s: Which parts of India are described as the most exposed to tsunami risk?
o: The Himalayan foothills and the Rann of Kutch
The east coast and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
The western coast and Lakshadweep Islands
The Indo-Gangetic Plain and the Western Ghats
nb34784e5035.x: India’s east coast and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are the most exposed areas to tsunami risk.
nb34784e5035.tq: Use the location clue and distinguish tsunami-exposed coasts from earthquake- or landslide-prone regions.
xs: The **east coast and A&N Islands** are most exposed to tsunami — option **(2)** is correct.
This was shown in the **2004** tsunami.
xa: About **5,700 km** of coastline faces cyclone/tsunami exposure.
Warning comes from **INCOIS, Hyderabad**.
The **Indo-Gangetic plain** faces **liquefaction**; the Himalaya faces **landslides**.

nfa1a550df59.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) is chaired by the:

ndc2ef8d9f10.s: The Rs 507.37 crore NDMA-MoPR community disaster risk reduction project is to be implemented through which institutions?
o: Urban local bodies in metro cities only
Coast Guard stations on the east coast
ndc2ef8d9f10.x: The NDMA-Ministry of Panchayati Raj project works through panchayats in 81 districts across 20 States. It is not limited to metros, to SDRFs or to the Coast Guard.
xs: The **₹507.37 crore** NDMA-MoPR community DRR project works through **panchayats** in **81 districts** of **20 states** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is not limited to **metro ULBs**, **SDRFs** or the **Coast Guard**.
xa: **DM Act 2005** stresses **prevention, mitigation, preparedness**.
**APSDMA** runs AP's **State EOC**.
The revised seismic map (**Zone VI**) was withdrawn in **March 2026**.

n01c2e3a9b9c.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the locations of an IMD cyclone warning centre?
n01c2e3a9b9c.x: The seven IMD cyclone warning centres are Chennai, Mumbai, Kolkata, Ahmedabad, Thiruvananthapuram, Visakhapatnam and Bhubaneswar. Hyderabad is not among them.
n01c2e3a9b9c.tq: Finds the one location that does not belong to a named institutional list.
xs: **Hyderabad** is not an IMD cyclone warning centre — option **(1)** is the answer.
The **7** centres: **Chennai, Mumbai, Kolkata, Ahmedabad, Thiruvananthapuram, Visakhapatnam, Bhubaneswar**.
xa: ⚠ Hyderabad hosts the **Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre** at **INCOIS** (MoES).
IMD severe-weather forecasts improved **40-50%** at a **5-day** lead time.
**ISRO DMS** runs the **NDEM** database.

n9a11f45132d.s: The Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre, operating since 2007, is located at:
n9a11f45132d.x: The centre is at INCOIS, Hyderabad, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
xa: It uses **seismic monitoring, ocean buoys, sirens**.
⚠ Tsunami warning = **INCOIS**, not IMD.
Most exposed: **east coast and A&N Islands** (**2004**).

ndisaster-management-23-7.s: The Asian Disaster Preparedness Centre (ADPC) is located in:

n: The International Tsunami Information Centre is located in Honolulu, Hawaii, USA. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 51-53]
The UNESCO Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission is located in Paris, France. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 51-53]
The Asian Disaster Preparedness Centre is located in Bangkok. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 51-53]
The Asian Disaster Reduction Center is located in Kobe, Japan. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 51-53]
xa: ADPC does **regional capacity building** in **Asia**.
ADRC focuses on **information sharing** and **research**.

n87c0ceb3c3c.s: The Disaster Management Act, 2005 is significant mainly because it:
o: Shifted policy focus from post-disaster relief to prevention, mitigation and preparedness
Created the Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre
Made disaster management exclusively a State subject
n87c0ceb3c3c.x: The DM Act 2005 moved India's approach from relief to prevention, mitigation and preparedness. The tsunami centre is INCOIS's (2007), seismic zoning is a BIS code, and the Act does not make disasters a State-only subject.
xs: The **DM Act 2005** shifted policy from **relief** to **prevention, mitigation and preparedness** — option **(1)** is correct.
The tsunami centre is at **INCOIS, Hyderabad** (operating since **2007**), and seismic zoning comes from the **BIS** code **IS 1893** — not the Act.
xa: Disaster = **hazard x vulnerability**.
**APSDMA** works under the **AP Disaster Management Rules, 2007**.
NDMA-MoPR community DRR project: **₹507.37 crore**, **20 states, 81 districts**.

o: Dividing hilly areas into homogeneous units by actual or potential landslide susceptibility, hazard or risk
Deterministic prediction of the exact date of each landslide
Mapping of coastal areas exposed to tsunami
Classifying plains by their flood frequency
nd06369fa8bc.x: Landslide Hazard Zonation divides hill areas into homogeneous units by susceptibility, hazard or risk; such maps are probabilistic, not exact forecasts. Tsunami and flood mapping are different exercises, and landslide zonation is done mostly for hilly areas.
nd06369fa8bc.tq: LHZ = hill areas zoned by susceptibility; probabilistic.
xs: **Landslide Hazard Zonation** divides **hill areas** into **homogeneous units** by actual or potential **susceptibility, hazard or risk** — option **(1)** is correct.
Its maps are **probabilistic**, not exact-date forecasts; tsunami and flood mapping are separate exercises.
xa: Zonation is done mostly for **hilly** areas (PYQ).
About **12.6-15%** of India is landslide-prone.
Prone regions: **Himalaya, NE, Western Ghats**.

ndisaster-management-18-19.s: Which of the following is the appropriate regulatory measure for high-risk landslide zones?
o: Construction should be shifted to riverbanks
Construction should be permitted without regulation
ndisaster-management-18-19.x: In high-risk landslide zones, building should be restricted. The other options would increase exposure.
ndisaster-management-18-19.tq: Find the option that reduces risk.
n: Construction in high-risk zones should be restricted. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 43-45]
xs: In high-risk zones, **construction should be restricted** — option **(4)**.
Settlements in hazard-prone areas must be **regulated**, and **mountain-specific building codes** enforced.
xa: Landslide-prone regions: **Himalaya**, **North-East**, **Western Ghats** incl. **Nilgiris**.
The Himalaya is prone due to **young, fragile geology** and active tectonics.

nab7049c6825.s: Telangana became the 29th State of India on:

nac94f016892.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Polavaram-related territorial changes of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Seven Polavaram-affected mandals were transferred from Khammam to Andhra Pradesh
The transfer was effected through the 2014 Polavaram ordinance and amendment
Chinturu division is now part of Polavaram district
Polavaram district was created mainly to manage the drought-prone Rayalaseema uplands

nfadbadaeedb.s: The Pataskar award of 1960 is associated with which of the following territorial adjustments?
o: Transfer of seven Khammam mandals to Andhra Pradesh
Formation of Telangana as the 29th State
Transfer of most of Tiruttani taluk to Tamil Nadu and some Tiruvallur villages to Andhra Pradesh
Formation of Andhra State with Kurnool as its capital
nfadbadaeedb.x: In 1960, the Pataskar award transferred most of Tiruttani taluk to Tamil Nadu and some villages of Tiruvallur to Andhra Pradesh.
nfadbadaeedb.tq: Use the wrong-person-or-event trap by distinguishing an earlier award from the 2014 Polavaram transfer.
xs: The **1960 Pataskar award** sent most of **Tiruttani** taluk to **TN** and some **Tiruvallur** villages to AP — option **(3)** is correct.

xa: AP was formed on **1 Nov 1956** — the **first linguistic state**.
**Pulicat** is a saltwater lagoon shared with **TN**.
Rayalaseema borders **TN, Karnataka, Telangana**.

nd28488bb4ea.s: Andhra State, formed on 1 October 1953, had its capital at:
nd28488bb4ea.x: Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953 with Kurnool as capital; Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956.
xa: AP was the **first linguistic state** (1953/1956).

**1960**: **Pataskar** award adjusted the TN border.

n04a875fff54.s: As on 31 December 2025, how many districts did Andhra Pradesh have?
n04a875fff54.x: AP had 28 districts, including Markapuram (from western Prakasam) and Polavaram.
xa: Markapuram population: ~**11.42 lakh**.
Polavaram: **11 mandals**, **2** revenue divisions, ~**3.49 lakh**, mostly tribal.

ne25b213c6ff.s: Andhra State, regarded as the first linguistic State, was formed in which year?
ne25b213c6ff.x: Andhra State was formed in 1953 (1 October), and Andhra Pradesh followed in 1956.
xa: Andhra State: **1 Oct 1953**, capital **Kurnool**.
AP: **1 Nov 1956**, with **20** districts.

n55aa339eba3.s: According to the Government of AP, the present area of Andhra Pradesh (about 4.96% of India) is:

xa: AP is the **7th largest state** (after Rajasthan, MP, Maharashtra, UP, Gujarat, Karnataka).

nf13c228f636.s: The title ‘Rice Bowl’ of Andhra Pradesh is primarily associated with its:
nf13c228f636.x: The coastal plains, particularly the Godavari and Krishna deltaic region, are known as the Rice Bowl of Andhra Pradesh.
nf13c228f636.tq: Connect an economic-geographical title with the relevant physical region.
xs: The **coastal plains and deltas** (**Godavari and Krishna**) are AP's **"Rice Bowl"** — option **(4)** is correct.

nc3c9a043018.s: The Western, or Rayalaseema, plateau of Andhra Pradesh is:

The Rayalaseema plateau is drought-prone.

n28c65c7655d.s: Which region of Andhra Pradesh holds the river deltas, most of the farm output and the highest population density?

nap-geography-27-7.s: YSR (Kadapa), Annamayya, Tirupati and Chittoor districts belong to which region of Andhra Pradesh?

n8148ae23a9d.s: The Uttarandhra region of Andhra Pradesh is also called:

**Coastal Andhra** has **18** districts including Uttarandhra.

nap-geography-1-2.s: Asia's first rubber dam was built on which river, a tributary of the Nagavali?

The Janjavathi River is a tributary of the Nagavali River. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-3]
xa: **Vani Vilasa Sagar (Marikanive)** was the **first dam** built by **M. Visvesvaraya**.
AP's first ex-situ biodiversity park: **Dolphin Conservation Society**, **Visakhapatnam**.

n56a844cbc92.s: The figure of 1,60,205 sq km for Andhra Pradesh refers to its area:

At the formation of Andhra State in 1953
Left after the 2014 bifurcation, before the Polavaram mandals were added

AP extends **12°41' N to 19°07' N** and **77° E to 84°40' E**.
**Yanam** (Puducherry, **30 sq km**) is an enclave in the Godavari delta.

n44addd007d9.s: The 82.5° E meridian, used for Indian Standard Time, passes through which place in Andhra Pradesh?

**Vijayawada, Tirupati** and **Visakhapatnam** are not on it per the notes.
xa: AP's longitude spans **77° E to 84°40' E**.
**Coringa** mangroves lie near **Kakinada**, Godavari estuary.
**Uppada** (Kakinada) is the worst coastal **erosion** spot.

ne0229b7b53e.s: Which State borders Andhra Pradesh on the south?
ne0229b7b53e.x: Tamil Nadu is on the south; Odisha and Chhattisgarh on the north, and Karnataka and Telangana on the west.
xa: On the **east** is the **Bay of Bengal**.
Longitude: **77° E to 84°40' E**.
The **82.5° E** meridian passes through **Kakinada**.

n70fa0329e19.s: According to the recalculated measurement, the coastline of Andhra Pradesh is about:
n70fa0329e19.x: The recalculated AP coastline is 1,053.07 km, third after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu; 974 km is the older figure.

Order: **Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, AP**; AP is still the longest on the **east coast**.

n2eb0d22b1d5.s: The increase in India's measured coastline from 7,516.6 km to 11,098.81 km primarily reflects:
o: Actual creation of new coastal land
A change in the political boundary of India
GIS retracing at a scale of 1:250,000
n2eb0d22b1d5.x: The increase resulted from GIS retracing at 1:250,000 scale and does not represent an actual physical change in India's coastline.

xs: The rise from **7,516.6 km to 11,098.81 km** is due to **GIS retracing at 1:250,000** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is **not real coastal change** or a boundary change.
xa: AP's figure became **1,053.07 km** in the same exercise.
Exam angle: **"recalculated"** questions want **1,053.07 km**.
NCCR: **38%** of the east coast is eroding vs **30%** of the west.

nabb9811bb3a.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh has the longest coastline (about 193 km)?
nabb9811bb3a.x: Srikakulam has the longest district coast (193 km) and West Godavari the shortest (23 km).
xa: **North end**: Srikakulam; **south end**: **Tirupati/Nellore at Pulicat**.
AP coastline: **1,053.07 km**.
**Uppada** (Kakinada) is the worst erosion spot.

n79027581f43.s: The Eastern Ghats join the Western Ghats near the:
n79027581f43.x: The Eastern Ghats, starting with Mahendragiri in the north and running through the Javadi and Shevaroy hills, join the Western Ghats near the Nilgiris.

Rivers rising here: **Vamsadhara, Nagavali, Sabari**.

ne144d74c1a5.s: The Eastern Ghats are made mainly of:
ne144d74c1a5.x: The Eastern Ghats are made mainly of Archaean khondalite and charnockite, over 2.5 billion years old.
xa: AP's **Eastern Ghats Mobile Belt** carries these rocks.
They are **discontinuous, rugged, highly eroded**.
The **Godavari and Krishna** split them in AP.

n53f8b8f2857.s: Horsley Hills is situated in which district?
n53f8b8f2857.x: Horsley Hills is located in Annamayya district near Madanapalle and the Karnataka border.
n53f8b8f2857.tq: Use the district–town association to identify the hill station.
xs: **Horsley Hills** is in **Annamayya** district (**Madanapalle**), near the **Karnataka** border — option **(2)** is correct.
**Araku** and **Lambasingi** are in **ASR**; **Ethipothala** falls is in **Palnadu**.
xa: Horsley Hills is about **1,265 m** high.
It gets **forest-fire alerts** each **April-May** (**2 Mar and 9 Apr 2026**).
**Annamayya** is part of the **Mysore plateau extension** with Chittoor and Kadapa.

n75713c61bd4.s: According to NCCR (Aug 2026), which is Andhra Pradesh's worst coastal-erosion spot?
n75713c61bd4.x: Uppada in Kakinada district is AP's worst erosion spot; nationally 38% of the east coast is eroding against 30% of the west coast.
xa: AP's coastline is **1,053.07 km**, 3rd longest after **Gujarat** and **Tamil Nadu**.
**Srikakulam** has the longest district coast (**193 km**); **West Godavari** the shortest (**23 km**).

nindian-geography-28-3.s: The Shevaroy Hills are located in:
nindian-geography-28-3.x: The Shevaroy are in Salem; the Javadi in Vellore–Tiruvannamalai and the Nandi Hills in Karnataka.
