Javadi Hills are located in Tamil Nadu. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 88-91]
Shevaroy Hills are located in Salem, Tamil Nadu. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 88-91]
Nandi Hills are located in Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 88-91]
xa: **Yercaud** is the important place in the Shevaroy Hills.
⚠ Seshachalam is **Eastern Ghats**, not "Nilgiri Hills" (PYQ key).

nap-geography-14-13.s: The Uppalapadu Protection Centre in Andhra Pradesh is noted as a nesting site for:
o: Great Indian Bustards and lesser floricans
Spot-billed storks, pelicans and black-headed ibises
nap-geography-14-13.x: Spot-billed storks, cattle egrets, pelicans and black-headed ibises nest at Uppalapadu.
n: Uppalapadu Protection Centre has spot-billed storks. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Uppalapadu Protection Centre has cattle egrets. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Uppalapadu Protection Centre has pelicans. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Uppalapadu Protection Centre has black-headed painted ibises. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
xa: **Nelapattu** (Tirupati) hosts **spot-billed pelicans**, **flamingos**, **open-billed storks**.
**Coringa** (Kakinada) has **fishing cats** and **otters** in estuarine mangroves.

n7ec5783837a.s: Which one of the following best explains the formation of the Andhra coastal plain?
o: A narrow rocky coast produced exclusively by volcanic activity
An emergent, broad coast built by river deposition and containing large deltas
A desert coast formed by wind-blown sand alone
A submerged coast formed mainly by glacial deposition
n7ec5783837a.x: The Andhra coastal plain is an emergent, broad coast built by river deposition and characterised by large deltas.
n7ec5783837a.tq: Infer the coastal landform from its formation process and associated delta pattern.
xs: The **Eastern Coastal Plain** is an **emergent, broad coast built by river deposition**, with **large deltas** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is not volcanic, glacial or wind-formed per the notes.
xa: ⚠ North of the Krishna = **Northern Circars**; south = **Coromandel**.
Dimensions: **~950 km** long, **~60 km** wide.
**Dolphin's Nose** (Yarada hills, **335 m**) shelters Visakhapatnam port.

na6799c12d7f.s: The Andhra coast north of the Krishna river is called the:
na6799c12d7f.x: North of the Krishna is the Northern Circars coast; south of it is the Coromandel coast.
xa: The **Coromandel Coast** also names the whole east coastal plain.
The Northern Circars are also called the **"Circar coast"**.
The east coast is an **emergent** coast with large deltas.

n864a949fe5a.s: 'Konaseema' refers to the delta of which river?
n864a949fe5a.x: Konaseema is the Godavari delta; the Krishna delta covers Krishna, Guntur and Bapatla districts.
xa: **Kolleru** lies between the **Godavari and Krishna** deltas.
**Krishna WLS** protects the Krishna estuary mangroves.
The **Penna** delta is small (**Nellore**).

n4acec06e175.s: Pulicat Lake is separated from the sea by which barrier island?
n4acec06e175.x: Sriharikota Island separates Pulicat Lake from the Bay of Bengal.
n4acec06e175.tq: Test the lake–barrier island association directly.
xs: **Pulicat** is cut off from the Bay by **Sriharikota island** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Majuli, Divar, Diu** are not mentioned.
xa: Pulicat is India's **2nd largest brackish-water lagoon**, shared with **TN** (**APPSC-GS 2025**).
The **Buckingham Canal** passes through it; it hosts **flamingos**.
Threats: **ISRO launches, thermal plants, sand mining**.

n9bdd77535f0.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a threat to the coastal lakes mentioned in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Glacial erosion caused by Himalayan ice fields
Thermal plants and sand mining degrading Pulicat
n9bdd77535f0.x: Glacial erosion by Himalayan ice fields is not a stated threat. Kolleru faces aquaculture encroachment, while Pulicat is affected by launches, thermal plants and sand mining.
n9bdd77535f0.tq: Find the geographically unrelated threat among the location-specific environmental pressures.
xs: **Glacial erosion by Himalayan ice fields** is not a stated threat — option **(1)** is the answer.
Stated threats: **Kolleru** — **aquaculture encroachment**; **Pulicat** — **ISRO launches, thermal plants, sand mining**.
xa: Kolleru is AP's **Ramsar** site (**2002**).
Pulicat is cut off by **Sriharikota island**.
The **Tammileru** drains into Kolleru.

ndbbedb03d35.s: Pulicat Lake is correctly described as which of the following?
o: India's second-largest brackish lagoon, shared by Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
A saline lake in northern Rajasthan
A freshwater lake wholly within Andhra Pradesh
ndbbedb03d35.x: Pulicat is a brackish lagoon shared by Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu and is regarded as India's second-largest brackish lagoon.
ndbbedb03d35.tq: Discriminate Pulicat from Kolleru by type and state relationship.
xs: **Pulicat** is India's **2nd largest brackish-water lagoon**, shared by **AP and TN** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is not freshwater (that is **Kolleru**) and not in Rajasthan or Maharashtra.
xa: It lies in **Tirupati** (earlier Nellore).
**Sriharikota island** separates it from the Bay.
⚠ Some notes wrongly place it at the **Penna** mouth; the Penna reaches the sea at **Utukuru**.

nfdfd7510152.s: Kolleru, lying between the Godavari and Krishna deltas, is a:
nfdfd7510152.x: Kolleru is a freshwater lake between the two deltas; Pulicat is a saltwater lagoon shared with Tamil Nadu.
xa: Kolleru area: ~**305 sq km** (CDI 2026).
Pulicat has the **Buckingham Canal** and **flamingos**.
Kolleru shrinks from **aquaculture encroachment**.

nc6890e13726.s: Which river drains into Kolleru Lake?
nc6890e13726.tq: Distinguish a feeder stream from the major delta distributaries.
xs: The **Tammileru** drains into **Kolleru** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Nagavali** rises in the **Eastern Ghats** (with Vamsadhara, Sabari); **Vasishta** and **Gautami** are not named in the notes.
xa: Kolleru: AP's **largest freshwater lake**; **Ramsar** site **2002**.
It holds the **Atapaka** bird sanctuary.
It lies between the **Godavari and Krishna** deltas.

nap-geography-14-10.s: Greater flamingos in Andhra Pradesh are associated with which sanctuary?
nap-geography-14-10.x: Greater flamingos belong to Pulicat, not Kolleru; Kolleru has painted storks, grey pelicans and glossy ibises.
n: Kolleru and Atapaka Bird Sanctuary is a freshwater wetland. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Kolleru Lake is a key feature of Kolleru and Atapaka Bird Sanctuary. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Kolleru and Atapaka Bird Sanctuary has painted storks. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Kolleru and Atapaka Bird Sanctuary has grey pelicans. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Kolleru and Atapaka Bird Sanctuary has glossy ibises. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Kolleru and Atapaka Bird Sanctuary has herons. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Kolleru and Atapaka Bird Sanctuary has egrets. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Kolleru and Atapaka Bird Sanctuary has migratory ducks. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
xa: Kolleru also has **Barringtonia forests** and freshwater tanks.
Kolleru area: **~305 sq km** (some notes **~250 sq km**); aquaculture shrinks it.

ncedc8e544f4.s: The Penna River forms a small delta mainly in which district?
ncedc8e544f4.x: The Penna forms a small delta in Nellore district.
ncedc8e544f4.tq: Match the smaller river delta with its stated district rather than a major delta district group.
xs: The **Penna** forms a **small delta** in **Nellore** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kakinada** is Godavari delta; **Bapatla** is Krishna delta; **Srikakulam** is not a delta district in the notes.
xa: ⚠ The Penna meets the sea at **Utukuru, Nellore** — not at Pulicat.
**Nallamala** lies between the **Krishna and Penna** basins.
**Erramala** divides the Krishna (north) and Penna (south) basins.

n2af72194d7e.s: The Simhachalam and Yarada hills are located in which district?
n2af72194d7e.x: Simhachalam and Yarada are in Visakhapatnam; Velikonda is in SPSR Nellore–Tirupati and Palakonda in YSR Kadapa–Tirupati.
xa: **Palakonda** holds the **Tirupati** pilgrim centre.
Seshachalam has **Tirumala** hills and **red sanders**.
**Velikonda** is the easternmost of the southern ranges.

nba262e8b177.s: Which river basin pair is associated with the Nallamala hill range?
nba262e8b177.x: The Nallamala range lies between the Krishna and Penna basins. It is also the largest continuous forest and hill range among these ranges.
nba262e8b177.tq: Use the basin relationship rather than the district location alone.
xs: **Nallamala** lies between the **Krishna and Penna** basins — option **(2)** is correct.
It is the **largest continuous** range and forest tract.
xa: Districts: **Kurnool, Nandyal, Prakasam, Guntur, Kadapa**.
It holds **NSTR** (est. **1983**, ~**3,728 sq km**), India's largest TR.
Home to the **Chenchu** PVTG (ITDA at **Srisailam**).

n78b3e0d36e5.s: The Chenchu Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group associated with the Nallamala hills has its Integrated Tribal Development Agency at:

xa: Nallamala holds **NSTR** — Telangana part is **Amrabad TR**.
**Gaur** to be translocated to NSTR and Nallamala from **Sep 2026** (WII support).
Other tribes: **Savara, Jatapu** (Srikakulam); **Gadaba, Bagata** (Araku).

n98cd86c0ed5.s: Red sanders forests in Andhra Pradesh are especially associated with which hill range?
n98cd86c0ed5.x: The Seshachalam hills, including the Tirumala hills, are noted for their red sanders forests.
n98cd86c0ed5.tq: Use the distinctive vegetation association to identify the range.
xs: **Red sanders** forests are linked to **Seshachalam** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Papikondalu** is the Godavari gorge; **Mahendragiri** is in Srikakulam; **Erramala** is the Krishna-Penna water divide.
xa: Seshachalam includes the **Tirumala** hills and forms the **Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve**.
It lies in **Kadapa and Chittoor** (**APPSC-GS 2024**).
**Talakona** hills are also a Red Sanders zone.

ncf7289391d1.s: The Seshachalam hills are a part of the:
ncf7289391d1.x: Seshachalam belongs to the Eastern Ghats; calling it part of the Nilgiris is incorrect.
xa: Seshachalam lies in **Kadapa and Chittoor** (**APPSC-GS 2024**).
It holds **Tirumala** and **red sanders**; forms a **Biosphere Reserve**.
The Eastern Ghats meet the Western Ghats near the **Nilgiris**.

nb30a7287a60.s: The Erramala hills form the water divide between:
o: The Krishna basin to the north and the Penna basin to the south
The Penna basin to the north and the Krishna basin to the south
The Bay of Bengal and the Eastern Ghats
nb30a7287a60.x: Erramala (Kurnool–Nandyal) divides the Krishna basin in the north from the Penna basin in the south.
xa: Erramala lies in **Kurnool / Nandyal**.
**Nallamala** lies between the Krishna and Penna basins.
The Penna meets the sea at **Utukuru, Nellore**.

n7f8c949fbd0.s: The Eastern Ghats in Srikakulam district are locally known as:
n7f8c949fbd0.x: In Srikakulam the Ghats are called Mahendragiri (Mahendra Girulu), running into Odisha. Papikondalu is the Godavari gorge section, Velikonda is on the Nellore-Tirupati side and Palakonda is in YSR Kadapa.
xs: In **Srikakulam** the Ghats are called **Mahendragiri (Mahendra Girulu)**, running into **Odisha** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Papikondalu** is the **Godavari gorge**; **Velikonda** is on the **Nellore-Tirupati** side; **Palakonda** is in **YSR Kadapa**.
xa: Asked in **APPSC-G2 2025**.
⚠ **Mahendragiri** peak (**1,501 m**) is in **Gajapati**, Odisha.
Srikakulam tribes: **Savara and Jatapu**.

n0750ed264fe.s: Under the proposed programme from September 2026, gaur are to be translocated from Central India to:
n0750ed264fe.x: Gaur are to be moved from Central India to NSTR and Nallamala from September 2026 with WII support.
xa: There is a push for a unified **Eastern Ghats Wildlife Sanctuary**.
Nallamala is home to the **Chenchu** PVTG.

ndfe81c53f46.s: The Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve was established in:
ndfe81c53f46.x: NSTR was established in 1983 and covers about 3,728 sq km in the Nallamala hills of AP.
xa: It lies in the **Nallamala** and is India's **largest TR** (**Jul 2026**).
**Gaur** translocation to NSTR from **Sep 2026**.
Nallamala lies between the **Krishna and Penna** basins.

nindian-geography-28-2.s: Srisailam is situated on the flat top of which hills?
nindian-geography-28-2.x: Srisailam stands on the flat top of the Nallamala Hills.
nindian-geography-28-2.tq: Recall the hill of each place.
n: Nallamala Hills are associated with Srisailam. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 88-91]
Srisailam is situated on the flat top of Nallamala Hills. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 88-91]
xs: **Srisailam** is on the flat top of the **Nallamala Hills** — option **(4)**.
The **Seshachalam Hills** are linked with **Tirupati**, not Srisailam.
xa: The Nallamala runs **north to south**, **parallel** to the **Coromandel Coast**.
It is the **largest continuous** range in AP, holding **NSTR**; home to the **Chenchu** PVTG.

nap-geography-8-5.s: The southern section of the Eastern Ghats in Andhra Pradesh is called the:
nap-geography-8-5.x: The northern section is the Eastern Ranges and the southern section the Kadapa Ranges.
n: The northern section of the Eastern Ghats is called the Eastern Ranges. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 21-23]
The southern section of the Eastern Ghats is called the Kadapa Ranges. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 21-23]
The Khondalite hills or mountains are bauxite-bearing mountain areas. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 21-23]
The Eastern Ranges are located in North Andhra Pradesh. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 21-23]
The Kadapa Ranges are located in South Andhra Pradesh. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 21-23]
xa: The **Godavari and Krishna** split the AP Ghats into these two parts.
Khondalites lie mainly in erstwhile **Visakhapatnam** and **East Godavari**.

nap-geography-9-3.s: The Ganjikunta pass in the Eastern Ghats links which two hill ranges?
nap-geography-9-3.x: Ganjikunta is a notable pass because it connects the Seshachalam and Nallamala sections.
n: Ganjikunta is a notable mountain pass in the Eastern Ghats. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 23-24]
Ganjikunta connects sections between the Seshachalam and Nallamala hill ranges. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 23-24]
xa: It forms a **geographical break** between uplands and lowlands.
The area has **dry deciduous forests** and **rocky elevations**.

nb081924215a.s: From the coast towards the interior, the physiographic regions of Andhra Pradesh are:
o: Coastal plains – Eastern Ghats – Western plateau
Eastern Ghats – Coastal plains – Western plateau
Western plateau – Eastern Ghats – Coastal plains
Coastal plains – Western plateau – Eastern Ghats
nb081924215a.x: From east to west the sequence is Coastal plains, Eastern Ghats and Western plateau.
xa: Coastal plains: **Srikakulam to Nellore/Tirupati**, alluvial deltas, **"Rice Bowl"**.
Eastern Ghats: **750-1,680 m**, forests, tribal belts.
Western plateau: **150-600 m**, crystalline rocks, red soils, drought-prone.

n57010e2f292.s: Which of the following districts belongs to the Western plateau physiographic region of Andhra Pradesh?
n57010e2f292.x: Sri Sathya Sai is included in the Western plateau or Rayalaseema region. The region is generally 150–600 metres high, has crystalline rocks and red soils, and is drought-prone.
n57010e2f292.tq: Distinguish plateau districts from coastal and Eastern Ghats districts.
xs: **Sri Sathya Sai** is in the **Western plateau (Rayalaseema)** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Parvathipuram Manyam** and **Nandyal** are in the **Eastern Ghats** hill region; **Srikakulam** is on the **coastal plains**.
xa: Plateau districts: **Kurnool, Anantapur, Sri Sathya Sai**.
The plateau is **150-600 m**, with **crystalline rocks, red soils**, drought-prone.
**Chittoor, Kadapa, Annamayya** form the **Mysore plateau extension**.

n75caa445bdf.s: The Coringa mangroves near Kakinada lie at the estuary of the:
n75caa445bdf.x: Coringa is at the Godavari estuary near Kakinada; the Krishna Wildlife Sanctuary covers the Krishna estuary mangroves.
xa: **"Koringa" tidal forests** lie at the Godavari-Krishna mouths.
⚠ AP **SES 2025-26** calls AP's mangroves India's **2nd largest**; **ISFR 2023** gives that place to **Gujarat**.
**Uppada** (Kakinada) is the worst erosion spot.

n472e5af747d.s: The Eastern Ghats are best described as a:
o: Discontinuous, eroded hill system cut by major rivers
Volcanic chain with no river gaps
Recent block mountain parallel to the west coast
n472e5af747d.x: The Eastern Ghats are discontinuous, eroded hills dissected by the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri.
xa: Rocks: **charnockites and khondalites**, **Archaean**, over **2.5 billion** years.
Average height **400-600 m** (some say **600-900 m**).
They meet the Western Ghats near the **Nilgiris**.

n48254418e06.s: Which of the following rivers rise in the Eastern Ghats?
n48254418e06.x: The Vamsadhara, Nagavali and Sabari rise in the Eastern Ghats.
xa: The Eastern Ghats begin in AP with **Mahendragiri** (Srikakulam).
**Savara and Jatapu** tribes live in **Srikakulam**.
**Katiki** falls lie on the **Gosthani** course.

ne37ed44df9b.s: What is the height of Galikonda peak in the Eastern Ghats?
ne37ed44df9b.x: Galikonda is 1,643 m; Arma Konda is 1,680 m, Sintram Gutta 1,620 m and Mahendragiri 1,501 m.

nc23d0da33fc.s: According to the normal rainfall pattern of Andhra Pradesh, which monsoon contributes approximately two-thirds of the State's annual rainfall?

Timber goes to artisans on a **no-profit** basis.
**Teak** grows in **dry deciduous** forests (Eastern Ghats, Nallamala).

n8c12f7f7f72.s: Which technology has been used against red sanders smuggling in Seshachalam?
n8c12f7f7f72.x: Thermal-imaging drones have been used against red sanders smuggling in the Seshachalam region.
n8c12f7f7f72.tq: Apply a current conservation measure to its specific enforcement context.
xs: **Thermal-imaging drones** are used against red sanders smuggling in **Seshachalam** — so option **(4)** is correct (**Feb 2026**).
The other options (fishing locators, elephant collars, sonar) are not linked to red sanders.
xa: Red sanders: IUCN **Endangered**, **Schedule IV** WPA **1972**, **CITES Appendix II**.
**APFDC** exports red sanders wood.
A red sanders wood bank is at **Tirupati**.

nindian-geography-50-15.s: Sundari is the characteristic tree of:
nindian-geography-50-15.x: Sundari is the typical tree of tidal (littoral) forests.
n: Sundari is characteristic of Littoral or Tidal forests. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 124-126]
Khair is associated with Acacia catechu. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 124-126]
xa: Tidal forests contain **mangroves**; in AP they are the **Koringa forests** at the **Krishna and Godavari** mouths.
**Teak-dominant** forests: **Madhya Pradesh**, **Chhattisgarh**, **Odisha**.
**Alpine** forests grow at **3,000–4,900 m** in the Himalayas.

nap-geography-13-11.s: Short thorn forests occur in areas receiving annual rainfall of:
nap-geography-13-11.x: Short thorn forests occur below 70 cm; dry deciduous forests need 75–100 cm and moist deciduous 125–200 cm.
n: Moist deciduous forests occur in areas receiving 125–200 cm of rainfall. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 28-30]
Dry deciduous forests occur in areas receiving 75–100 cm of rainfall. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 28-30]
Short thorn forests occur in areas receiving less than 70 cm of rainfall. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 28-30]
xa: Moist deciduous gets the **maximum rainfall** — the **wetter** areas.
Short thorn forests occupy the **driest** areas (Kadapa, Kurnool, Chittoor, Anantapur).
⚠ **Seshachalam** = dry deciduous; **Papikonda** = moist deciduous.
Tropical thorn species: **Acacia**, **Ziziphus**, **Prosopis** (invasive).

nap-geography-19-6.s: Forests in Andhra Pradesh are predominantly which type?
nap-geography-19-6.x: AP's forests are mostly tropical deciduous, both dry and moist. Thorn and mangrove forests cover smaller areas.
nap-geography-19-6.tq: Recall the main forest type of AP.
n: Forests in Andhra Pradesh are predominantly deciduous forests. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 41-43]
xs: Forests in AP are **predominantly deciduous** — option **(4)**.
**Tropical dry deciduous** forests cover the **largest area** (Eastern Ghats, Nallamala, Seshachalam).
**Short thorn** and **tidal / mangrove** forests are limited to the driest tracts and the delta mouths.
xa: Southern Dry Mixed Deciduous = **15,128 sq km**; Dry Deciduous Scrub = **12,551 sq km**.
Mangroves and Littoral = only **418 sq km**.
Dry deciduous species: **teak**, **Terminalia**, **red sanders**, **Anogeissus**.
Moist deciduous hill forests: **Araku, Paderu**, Papikondalu.

n54c5cce9c6a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about APFDC plantations?
o: Coffee plantations are in Visakhapatnam and East Godavari
Cashew plantations are confined to Visakhapatnam and the East Godavari agency
Clonal eucalyptus occupies the largest plantation area
Cashew is grown on the Guntur-Prakasam-Nellore coast
n54c5cce9c6a.x: APFDC cashew is on the Guntur-Prakasam-Nellore coast and in East Godavari, West Godavari and Chittoor, so it is not confined to the agency.
xa: APFDC is the **largest Eucalyptus grower among PSUs** in India.
APFDC total plantation: **49,742 ha**; cashew **5,664**, coffee **4,010**, bamboo **2,359**, teak **956** ha.
APFDC generates ~**9 lakh man-days** a year.
APFDC is the agent for **exporting red sanders wood and beedi leaf**.

ne1fed361ef5.s: According to the ISFR 2023-related assessment, the increase in green cover was 1,445 sq km, of which true forest accounted for:
ne1fed361ef5.x: The reported green-cover gain was 1,445 sq km, but only 156 sq km represented true forest. The distinction highlights that green cover is broader than forest cover.
ne1fed361ef5.tq: Split the headline total from the smaller true-forest component.
xs: Only **156 sq km** of the **1,445 sq km** green-cover gain was **true forest** — so option **(4)** is correct (**18 Aug 2026**).
Green cover is broader than **forest cover**.
xa: Similar criticism: **"Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam"** (**140 crore** saplings) adds **tree cover, not forest**.
**Vanam-Manam** adds green cover outside reserved forests (**5.29 crore** seedlings).
National forest-cover goal: **33%**.

n9d066397332.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the mangroves of Andhra Pradesh?
o: The Godavari-Krishna estuaries are called India's second-largest mangrove ecosystem
By ISFR mangrove-cover area, Gujarat ranks above AP
By mangrove-cover area, AP is second on the east coast
By ISFR mangrove-cover area, AP ranks second in India after West Bengal
n9d066397332.x: By ISFR mangrove-cover area, AP ranks behind West Bengal, Gujarat and Andaman & Nicobar, not second in India.
xa: Mangroves and Littoral area: **418 sq km** (2025-26 analysis).
Mangrove species: **Rhizophora, Avicennia, Excoecaria**.
Key sites: **Coringa**, Krishna delta, **Pulicat**.

nc660d0ec8f4.s: Approximately what share of Andhra Pradesh's notified forest area is Reserved Forest?
nc660d0ec8f4.x: The notified forest area is about 85.8% Reserved, 13.6% Protected and 0.6% Unclassed.
xa: Protected-area network (NPs + WLS): **8,139.88 sq km** = **4.99%** of the state.
⚠ Some notes label this same figure "protected forests".
Largest ISFR **2023** density class: **Open Forest** (**14,363.50 sq km**).

n550717be0bd.s: The protected-area network comprising National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries covers approximately what area and share of Andhra Pradesh?
n550717be0bd.x: The protected-area network covers 8,139.88 sq km, equivalent to 4.99% of the State's area.
n550717be0bd.tq: Pair the exact area with its percentage instead of confusing it with forest-density areas.
xs: The protected-area network (**NPs + WLS**) covers **8,139.88 sq km** = **4.99%** of AP — so option **(2)** is correct.
**14,363.50 sq km** is **Open Forest**; **8,351.62 sq km** is **Scrub** (ISFR **2023**).
xa: ⚠ Some notes label the same figure "protected forests".
Legal classes: Reserved ~**85.8%**; Protected ~**13.6%**; Unclassed ~**0.6%**.
Very Dense Forest: **1,995.71 sq km** (~**1.2%**).

n70001b6612d.s: As per the India State of Forest Report 2019, which pre-2022 district of Andhra Pradesh had the highest forest cover?
n70001b6612d.x: Visakhapatnam had the highest forest cover and Krishna had the lowest among the pre-2022 districts.
n70001b6612d.tq: Use the district-wise percentage-cover comparison rather than total forest area.
xs: **Visakhapatnam** had the highest forest cover; **Krishna** the lowest — so option **(3)** is correct.
**YSR Kadapa** leads in forest **area**, not cover.
xa: ⚠ Largest forest area = **Kadapa**; highest cover = **Visakhapatnam**.
**Krishna** is lowest on both measures.
The Visakhapatnam region's northern Eastern Ghats (**Araku, Paderu**) carry moist deciduous hill forests.
n70001b6612d.fixed: PYQs y1c7ea24a695, y6b36f0676e1: East Godavari highest forest cover (4,994.10 sq km)

nap-geography-19-5.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh has the highest forest area?
nap-geography-19-5.x: YSR Kadapa has the most forest area and Krishna the least; Nallamala is the biggest forest.
n: Nallamala Forests are the biggest forests in Andhra Pradesh. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 41-43]
YSR Kadapa has the highest forest area. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 41-43]
Krishna has the least forest area. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 41-43]
xa: ⚠ Largest forest area = **Kadapa**; highest forest percentage = **Visakhapatnam**.
Highest rainfall: **Visakhapatnam**; lowest: **Anantapur**.
AP had India's **highest** fire-affected forest area in 2023-24 = **5,286.76 sq km**.
TTD reports **89.40%** green cover at **Tirumala (Seshachalam)**.

n1d3d5185304.s: Red sanders is listed in which Appendix of CITES?
o: It is not listed in CITES
n1d3d5185304.x: Red sanders is in CITES Appendix II; it is also IUCN Endangered and in Schedule IV of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
xa: It is endemic to the **Seshachalam**, Palakonda and Veligonda ranges.
**Thermal-imaging drones** fight smuggling in Seshachalam (**Feb 2026**).
**APFDC** is the government's agent for **exporting red sanders wood** and beedi leaf.

nf9542eb8ba4.s: Which one of the following best captures the criticism of plantation drives such as “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam”?
o: They reduce all forms of tree cover in urban areas.
They focus exclusively on mangrove restoration.
They replace forest conservation with mining expansion.
They may add tree cover without necessarily creating natural forests.
nf9542eb8ba4.x: The criticism is that planting drives, including the target of 140 crore saplings under “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam”, can increase tree cover without creating natural forests.
nf9542eb8ba4.tq: Distinguish the broader category of tree cover from ecologically richer natural forest.
xs: Drives like **"Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam"** add **tree cover, not forest** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The drive aims at **140 crore** saplings.
xa: ISFR 2023: green-cover gain **1,445 sq km**, but only **156 sq km** true forest.
**Van Adhiniyam** changes (**2026**) allow commercial plantations on degraded forest land.
**CAMPA** funds compensatory afforestation.

nfb53417694d.s: Which institution is the Government’s agent for exporting red sanders wood and beedi leaf in Andhra Pradesh?
nfb53417694d.x: The Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation is the Government’s agent for exporting red sanders wood and beedi leaf.
nfb53417694d.tq: Distinguish the State corporation handling exports from the tribal-produce procurement agencies.
xs: **APFDC** is the government's agent for exporting **red sanders wood and beedi leaf** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**GCC** buys MFP from tribals; **TRIFED** runs the **MSP for MFP**.
xa: APFDC is the **largest Eucalyptus grower among PSUs** in India (**33,584 ha**).

**2.20 lakh** pepper standards on its coffee estates.

n418267119e4.s: Which agency is the nodal agency for the minimum support price (MSP) for minor forest produce?
n418267119e4.x: TRIFED is the nodal agency for MSP for MFP; the Girijan Co-operative Corporation buys minor forest produce from tribals.
xa: GCC = **Girijan Co-operative Corporation**, **Visakhapatnam**.

**NTFP** is worth more than **₹500 crore** a year.

naa0f541f6eb.s: The principal purpose of CAMPA funds mentioned in relation to forests is to finance:
o: Urban road construction outside forest areas
Compensatory afforestation through an Annual Plan of Operation
naa0f541f6eb.x: CAMPA funds compensatory afforestation through an Annual Plan of Operation.
naa0f541f6eb.tq: Ask which institutional mechanism performs the stated compensatory function.
xs: **CAMPA** funds **compensatory afforestation** through an **Annual Plan of Operation** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is an afforestation fund, not a mining or road fund.
xa: **Vanam-Manam**: green cover outside reserved forests; **5.29 crore** seedlings in 2024-25 (to December).
**Mixed Plantation Scheme**: **87 km** of avenue plantations.
Forest diversion under the **Van Adhiniyam, 1980**: **27,641.252 ha** up to **31 Dec 2024**.

n57b07d54c8a.s: Which of the following is a stated change associated with the Van Adhiniyam in 2026?
o: Open forests were removed from all forest-related criteria.
The national forest-cover goal was reduced to 21.74%.
Commercial plantations were prohibited on all degraded forest land.
Commercial plantations were allowed on degraded forest land toward the national goal of 33% forest cover.
n57b07d54c8a.x: The 2026 change allows commercial plantations on degraded forest land and is linked to the national goal of 33% forest cover.
n57b07d54c8a.tq: Identify the policy change by focusing on the action permitted and its stated national objective.
xs: The **Van Adhiniyam** changes (**2026**) allow **commercial plantations on degraded forest land** toward the national goal of **33%** forest cover — so option **(4)** is correct.
The goal stays **33%**; open forests were actually **added** to the **16th Finance Commission** criterion.
xa: Full name: **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980**.
**CAMPA** funds compensatory afforestation.

n7a3e02b9be4.s: The craft wood banks at Kondapalli, Etikoppaka, Settigunta, Madhavamala, Udayagiri and Bobbili primarily serve which purpose?

Supplying timber to artisans on a no-profit basis
Distributing free seedlings to coffee estates
Storing only bamboo for paper industries
n7a3e02b9be4.x: The craft wood banks supply timber to artisans on a no-profit basis. The named banks are distinct from the red sanders, bamboo and central banks.

xs: The craft wood banks supply **timber to artisans on a no-profit basis** — so option **(2)** is correct (**11 Aug 2026**).

xa: Other banks: red sanders → **Tirupati**; bamboo → **Rajamahendravaram**; central → **Dowleswaram**; teak → **Kapavaram**.
2024-25 (Apr-Dec): **bamboo nil**; timber only **1,562.886 cmt**.
Forest revenue: **₹32.81 crore** (2023-24).

n152676b51d1.s: The forest revenue of Andhra Pradesh during 2023–24 was approximately:
n152676b51d1.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded forest revenue of ₹32.81 crore in 2023–24. The figure of ₹19.63 crore relates to 2024–25 up to December only, while NTFP harvesting yields more than ₹500 crore annually.
n152676b51d1.tq: Separate the full-year figure from the partial-year and annual NTFP figures.
xs: AP's forest revenue in 2023-24 was **₹32.81 crore** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**₹19.63 crore** is 2024-25 **up to December only**; **more than ₹500 crore** is the annual **NTFP** value.
xa: Timber 2023-24 **exceeded target** (**27,049.16 cmt**).
APFDC total plantations: **49,742 ha**.
APFDC employment: ~**9 lakh man-days** a year.

n799883c222c.s: APFDC acts as the government's agent for exporting:
o: Red sanders wood and beedi leaf
n799883c222c.x: APFDC exports red sanders wood and beedi leaf; GCC buys minor forest produce and TRIFED runs the MSP for MFP.
xa: Forest revenue was only **₹32.81 crore** (2023-24).
TRIFED: **1987**, Ministry of **Tribal Affairs**.
GCC is based at **Visakhapatnam**.

nc2ebb5c82cb.s: For the first time, the 16th Finance Commission included open forests in the devolution forest criterion through:
nc2ebb5c82cb.x: The 16th Finance Commission included open forests in the devolution forest criterion using density-based weights.

xs: The **16th Finance Commission** counts **open forests** in the forest criterion for the first time, with **density-based weights** — so option **(3)** is correct (Feb 2026).
Earlier only denser classes counted; now **open forest** earns weight too, scaled by **density**.
xa: **Open Forest** is AP's largest density class: **14,363.50 sq km** (ISFR **2023**).
Very Dense Forest: **1,995.71 sq km**; Moderately Dense: **13,725.75 sq km**.
National forest-cover goal: **33%**.

n71eea1f6877.s: The 1879 Rekapalli revolt in Andhra Pradesh was associated with opposition to:
n71eea1f6877.x: The Rekapalli revolt of 1879 was directed against British forest laws.
n71eea1f6877.tq: Link the historical event to the specific forest-related cause rather than a general colonial grievance.
xs: The **1879 Rekapalli revolt** was against **British forest laws** — so option **(3)** is correct (APHQ).
It is AP's historical angle on forest governance.
xa: **GCC (Visakhapatnam)** today buys MFP from tribals.
**TRIFED** (**1987**) runs the **MSP for MFP** under the Ministry of **Tribal Affairs**.
Today's forest law: **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980**.

n5fc39e20790.s: Which class of forest occupied the largest area in Andhra Pradesh under the ISFR 2023 classification?
n5fc39e20790.x: Open Forest was the largest class, covering 14,363.50 sq km.

xs: **Open Forest** was the largest class, **14,363.50 sq km** (ISFR 2023) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Moderately Dense Forest** = **13,725.75 sq km**; **Scrub** = **8,351.62**; **Very Dense Forest** = **1,995.71**.
xa: ⚠ Largest density class = **Open Forest**, not Moderately Dense.
The **16th Finance Commission** counts **open forests** in the forest criterion for the first time.

n8d22c6fc533.s: As per the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25, how many wildlife sanctuaries does Andhra Pradesh have?
n8d22c6fc533.x: AP has 13 wildlife sanctuaries, 3 national parks, 4 deer parks and 2 zoological parks.

nbe65b25293c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Papikonda National Park?
o: A Reserved Forest was established there in 1882
It is associated with the Godavari gorge through the Papikonda hills
It was declared a Wildlife Sanctuary in 1978
It was declared a National Park in 1978

nd91b6d8c9ed.s: India's largest tiger reserve by area is:

xa: Survey count: **1 tiger reserve and 1 biosphere reserve**.

n07618466685.s: The Nallamala Hills extend through which region of Andhra Pradesh?
n07618466685.x: Nallamala extends through Nandyal, Prakasam and Palnadu; Seshachalam is in Tirupati–Annamayya and Palakonda in Kadapa–Annamayya.

The **K-G mouths** (Kakinada, Krishna, Bapatla) carry **"Koringa forests"**.

n00d08261c7a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the mangroves of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Coringa WLS and Krishna WLS protect them
Large-scale afforestation in deltaic mangroves dates from the Sixth Five-Year Plan
ISFR 2023 places Gujarat second, though State surveys call AP's the second-largest

n00d08261c7a.x: AP's mangroves are in the Godavari and Krishna estuaries (Coringa and Krishna WLS), not the Vamsadhara-Nagavali.

n0678fcba0dc.s: Uppalapadu is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?

**Naupada** (Srikakulam) is a coastal and marine biodiversity area.

n199c4d7c8c9.s: Jerdon's courser is protected in which wildlife sanctuary of Andhra Pradesh?
n199c4d7c8c9.x: Jerdon's courser, a critically endangered nocturnal bird, is protected in Sri Lankamalleswara WLS.

Papikonda also has **tiger, gaur, mouse deer**.

nc71f9e38651.s: The boundary of a National Park can be altered only on the recommendation of the:

xa: AP has **3 national parks**: **Papikonda**, **Sri Venkateswara**, **Rajiv Gandhi**.

n0d942b6857e.s: The only elephant sanctuary of Andhra Pradesh is:

xa: AP has **one** tiger reserve: **NSTR**, India's largest (~**3,728 sq km**).
Seshachalam BR area: **4,755.997 sq km**.

na16cfe781bf.s: The smallest wildlife sanctuary of Andhra Pradesh is:
na16cfe781bf.x: Nelapattu (4.58 sq km) is the smallest sanctuary; Rollapadu is 6.14 sq km.
xa: Largest PA: **NSTR/Rajiv Gandhi WLS**.
Rajiv Gandhi NP was notified in **2005**.
Nelapattu (**Tirupati**) is a **pelican breeding** site.

nap-geography-14-4.s: The Indira Gandhi Zoological Park is located in:
nap-geography-14-4.x: Indira Gandhi Zoological Park is in Visakhapatnam, not Tirupati.
n: Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam is a tiger reserve. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]

n74adf66cf9d.s: Krishna Wildlife Sanctuary is located in which districts?

Mangroves grow mainly in the **Godavari and Krishna estuaries**.

nfc328f98475.s: Sri Venkateswara National Park lies inside:

n072e1bdb800.s: Which of the following represents the oldest-to-newest sequence given for the selected Andhra Pradesh wildlife sanctuaries?

xs: **Nelapattu** (**Tirupati**) is the **spot-billed pelican breeding** colony — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Pulicat** is known for **flamingos**; **Telineelapuram** and **Uppalapadu** are **not** notified sanctuaries.
xa: Nelapattu (**4.58 sq km**) is AP's **smallest WLS**.
Notified **1976** — oldest in the APPSC 2025 key order.
**Kolleru** is one of the world's largest spot-billed pelican breeding grounds.

n3251c2db7dc.s: The mass mortality reported at Telineelapuram involved which species?
n3251c2db7dc.x: The mass mortality at Telineelapuram involved the spot-billed pelican, Pelecanus philippensis.
n3251c2db7dc.tq: Discriminate the reported species from other birds associated with wetlands.
xs: The mass mortality at **Telineelapuram** involved the **spot-billed pelican (Pelecanus philippensis)** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was **not** flamingo, openbill or sarus (APPSC-G1 **2022**).
xa: Telineelapuram is in **Srikakulam**; it hosts **painted storks** and pelicans.
It is **not** a notified sanctuary.
**Kolleru** and **Nelapattu** are the major pelican breeding sites.

n8100d6f2d89.s: Which protected area is described as the only elephant habitat in Andhra Pradesh?
n8100d6f2d89.x: Kaundinya Wildlife Sanctuary is associated with the Asian elephant and is described as the only elephant habitat in Andhra Pradesh.
n8100d6f2d89.tq: Identify the protected area from the exclusive habitat description.
xs: **Kaundinya WLS** is AP's **only elephant habitat** (**Asian elephant**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Gundla Brahmeswaram** is a **tiger corridor**; **SV** has the **Indian leopard**; **Papikonda** has **tiger, gaur, mouse deer**.
xa: Kaundinya: **Chittoor**, **357.60 sq km**, borders **Tamil Nadu**; notified **1990**.
Elephant reserve = **Koundinya + Rayala Elephant Reserve**.
Man-animal conflict compensation: **Rs 130 lakh** paid up to **Dec 2025**.

nap-geography-14-18.s: Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary is located in:
nap-geography-14-18.x: Sri Lankamalleswara sanctuary is in Kadapa (Cuddapah); Nelapattu is in Tirupati district.
n: Sri Lanka Malleshwara Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Cuddapah. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
Nelapattu Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Tirupathi district. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 30-33]
xa: Sri Lankamalleswara (**464.42 sq km**) is the home of **Jerdon's Courser**; notified **1988**.
Nelapattu (**4.58 sq km**) is the **smallest** sanctuary — a **pelican breeding** site.
**Pulicat WLS** is also in **Tirupathi** — known for **flamingos**.
**Sri Venkateswara WLS** is in **Annamayya, Tirupati**.

nbde209b2a02.s: Gundla Brahmeswaram Wildlife Sanctuary is characterised by which of the following?
o: Pelican breeding colony and migratory waterfowl
Dry deciduous forest and the new CR herb Euphorbia chalamensis
nbde209b2a02.x: Gundla Brahmeswaram (Nandyal-Prakasam, the extended core of NSTR in the Nallamala) is a dry deciduous forest sanctuary where the new Critically Endangered (CR) herb Euphorbia chalamensis was recorded in 2026. Pelican colonies (Nelapattu), brackish lagoon flamingos (Pulicat) and mangrove crocodiles (Coringa) belong to other sanctuaries.
nbde209b2a02.tq: Identify the habitat-feature pair rather than the better-known wetland associations.
xs: **Gundla Brahmeswaram WLS** has **dry deciduous forest** and the new CR herb **Euphorbia chalamensis** (**2026**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Pelican colony** = **Nelapattu**; **brackish lagoon + flamingos** = **Pulicat**; **mangroves + saltwater crocodile** = **Coringa**.
xa: It is the **NSTR extended core** in the **Nallamala** (**Nandyal, Prakasam**).
It acts as a **tiger corridor** next to NSTR.

nd50a205991f.s: Andhra Pradesh's only biosphere reserve, notified in 2010, is the:
nd50a205991f.x: The Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve (4,755.997 sq km, 2010) is AP's only biosphere reserve. Some sources wrongly call it the Sri Venkateswara BR; SV is a national park and sanctuary. Nallamala holds the NSTR tiger reserve and Papikonda is a national park.
xs: AP's only BR, notified **2010**, is the **Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Some notes wrongly call it the **Sri Venkateswara** BR; SV is a **NP and WLS**. Nallamala holds **NSTR**; Papikonda is an **NP**.
xa: Area: **4,755.997 sq km**; spread over the **Tirupati and Kurnool circles**.
**Red Sanders** is endemic to the **Seshachalam**, Palakonda and Veligonda ranges.
Survey count: **1 tiger reserve and 1 biosphere reserve**.

n84cc8d682b2.s: The Rajiv Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary, which is a tiger reserve and part of the Nallamala landscape, extends over which districts according to APSES 2024–25?
o: Eluru, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Kakinada
n84cc8d682b2.x: The Rajiv Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary (Tiger Reserve) extends over Nandyal, Prakasam and Palnadu districts and forms part of the Nallamala landscape.
n84cc8d682b2.tq: Match the tiger reserve with its complete post-reorganisation district spread.
xs: **Rajiv Gandhi WLS (Tiger Reserve)** spans **Nandyal, Prakasam and Palnadu** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is in the **Nallamala** and forms the **core of NSTR**.
xa: Largest PA: **NSTR/Rajiv Gandhi WLS**.
**Rajiv Gandhi NP** (**2.30 sq km**) is AP's smallest NP, notified **2005**.

n9c496ff829d.s: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam was declared a tiger reserve in:
n9c496ff829d.x: NSTR, in the Nallamala hills along the Krishna, was declared a tiger reserve in 1983.
xa: Area ~**3,728 sq km** — **India's largest tiger reserve**.
Tigers: **63-67** (All India Tiger Estimation **2022**).
**600 Chenchus** serve as protection watchers and guides (2025-26).

nc180d68541d.s: Tiger reserves in India are managed on a core-buffer model under the:
nc180d68541d.x: Tiger reserves follow a core-buffer model under the NTCA, in accordance with the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
xa: NSTR core: **Nandyal, Prakasam, Palnadu**, about **3,325 sq km** in total.
**Gundla Brahmeswaram** is the **extended core**.
AP has **one** tiger reserve (2024-25 and 2025-26 surveys).

n12833ea90a0.s: According to the All India Tiger Estimation 2022 figure given for Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve, the tiger population was in which range?
n12833ea90a0.x: The tiger population figure given for the reserve is 63–67 according to the All India Tiger Estimation 2022.
n12833ea90a0.tq: Compare the numerical ranges carefully; the correct range is neither the lowest nor the highest distractor.
xs: NSTR had **63-67** tigers (All India Tiger Estimation **2022**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
These tigers live in the **Nallamala** hills along the **Krishna**, in a reserve spanning **AP + Telangana**.
xa: NSTR is **India's largest tiger reserve** by area (~**3,728 sq km**) and by core habitat.
It was declared in **1983**.
**600 Chenchus** work as protection watchers and guides.
Hence "largest tiger habitat is in AP" (UPPSC **2011**).

n47d911d2d49.s: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve is managed by which forest circle?
n47d911d2d49.x: NSTR is managed by the Srisailam circle; its AP core areas lie in Nandyal, Prakasam and Palnadu.
xa: ⚠ Some notes call NSTR a BR; the survey supports neither that nor SV/Papikondalu tiger reserves.
Core about **3,325 sq km**; Rajiv Gandhi WLS (**2,131.67 sq km**) is its core.
Management: **core-buffer** model under **NTCA** (WPA **1972**).

n965bb217aa5.s: The elephants migrated into the Palamaner region during the 1980s mainly because of drought in which areas?
n965bb217aa5.x: The migration was attributed to drought in the Hosur-Dharmapuri reserve forests and Bannerghatta.
n965bb217aa5.tq: Link the stated environmental cause with the resulting species movement.
xs: Elephants moved into **Palamaner** in the **1980s** due to **drought in the Hosur-Dharmapuri forests and Bannerghatta** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2024 key).
The elephants settled in **Palamaner/Kaundinya**, which became AP's elephant habitat.
xa: **Kaundinya** is AP's only **Asian elephant** habitat (**Chittoor**, borders TN).
Kaundinya area: **357.60 sq km**; notified **1990**.
**1 Elephant Reserve**: Koundinya + **Rayala Elephant Reserve** (Anantapuramu circle).

n1a4b6d4de65.s: Andhra Pradesh's elephant reserve comprises the Koundinya Sanctuary and the:
n1a4b6d4de65.x: AP has one elephant reserve, formed by the Koundinya Sanctuary and the Rayala Elephant Reserve (Anantapuramu circle); Koundinya is AP's only Asian elephant habitat. Nallamala, Seshachalam and Papikonda are tiger, biosphere and national-park areas respectively, not the elephant reserve.
xs: AP's elephant reserve = **Koundinya Sanctuary + Rayala Elephant Reserve** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Rayala lies in the **Anantapuramu circle**; **Nallamala** = tiger reserve, **Seshachalam** = BR, **Papikonda** = NP.
xa: **Kaundinya** is AP's only **Asian elephant** habitat.
Elephants entered **Palamaner** in the **1980s** after drought in **Hosur-Dharmapuri** and **Bannerghatta**.
Koundinya (**Chittoor**) borders **Tamil Nadu**.

nd14c6737663.s: Red Sanders, scientifically known as Pterocarpus santalinus, is especially associated with which region of Andhra Pradesh?
nd14c6737663.x: Red Sanders is endemic to the southern Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh and is characteristic of the Seshachalam and Palakonda belts.
nd14c6737663.tq: Identify the endemic species by linking it to its regional distribution.
xs: **Red Sanders** is endemic to the **southern Eastern Ghats** of AP — so option **(4)** is correct.
Its ranges: **Seshachalam, Palakonda and Veligonda** (SV NP/WLS landscape).
The **K-G mouths** are **mangrove** country; **thorn forests** occupy the lowest-rainfall tracts.
xa: It is listed as AP's flagship **flora** (2024-25).
**Seshachalam** (**Tirupati-Annamayya**) and **Palakonda** (**Kadapa-Annamayya**) are dry deciduous hills.
A **special protection area** covers this endemic-tree belt.

nap-geography-19-9.s: In Andhra Pradesh, dry deciduous forests are associated mainly with the:
nap-geography-19-9.x: Dry deciduous forests cover the Seshachalam–Nallamala belt, and the forest region reaches south to the Palakonda and Nallamala hills.
n: Dry deciduous forests are associated with the Seshachalam–Nallamala belt. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 41-43]
The southern extent of the forest region reaches the Palakonda and Nallamala Hills. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 41-43]
xa: **Northern** extent: **Simhachalam Hills**; **western**: **Balaghat Hills**.
**Palakonda hills** (Kadapa-Annamayya): dry deciduous; **Red Sanders** belt.
**Nallamala** = largest forest in AP; home of **NSTR**.

n551e6b6b6ac.s: Kolleru Lake, a freshwater lake between the Krishna and Godavari deltas, was designated a Ramsar site in:
n551e6b6b6ac.x: Kolleru was declared a Ramsar site in 2002. 1999 is the year Kolleru was notified as a wildlife sanctuary, 2008 is when Papikonda became a national park, and 2010 is when the Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve was notified.
xs: **Kolleru** became a **Ramsar site in 2002** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**1999** = Kolleru notified as WLS; **2008** = Papikonda NP; **2010** = Seshachalam BR.
xa: Kolleru WLS: **308.55 sq km**, **Eluru / West Godavari**.
It is a **freshwater lake** between the **Krishna and Godavari** deltas.
Flagship: **spot-billed pelican** and migratory water birds.

n95568d9502a.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the biodiversity highlights of Andhra Pradesh listed in APSES 2024–25?
n95568d9502a.x: The listed biodiversity highlights are red sanders, tiger, Indian bison, Great Indian Bustard and golden gecko. One-horned rhinoceros is not included in that list.
n95568d9502a.tq: Find the option outside the stated state-specific biodiversity list.
xs: The **one-horned rhinoceros** is not in AP's list — so option **(3)** is correct.
APSES **2024-25** flagship and endemic species: **Red Sanders** (flora), **tiger**, **Indian Bison**, **Great Indian Bustard**, **Golden Gecko**.
xa: **Golden gecko**: **Tirumala hills** (Sri Venkateswara NP).
**Great Indian Bustard**: **Rollapadu WLS** (Nandyal grassland).
**Red Sanders** is endemic to the **Seshachalam, Palakonda and Veligonda** ranges.
Man-animal conflict compensation: **Rs 130 lakh** paid up to **Dec 2025**.

nfe89596c54f.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of protected areas located in Telangana?
o: Papikonda, Kolleru and Seshachalam National Parks
Coringa, Krishna and Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuaries
Mrugavani, Kasu Brahmananda Reddy National Park and Eturunagaram Wildlife Sanctuary
Nagarhole, Mrugavani and Coringa Wildlife Sanctuaries
nfe89596c54f.x: Mrugavani National Park, Kasu Brahmananda Reddy National Park and Eturunagaram Wildlife Sanctuary are located in Telangana.
nfe89596c54f.tq: Use the common-location clue to separate neighbouring-state distractors.
xs: **Mrugavani, Kasu Brahmananda Reddy NP and Eturunagaram WLS** are all in **Telangana** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Papikonda**, **Coringa, Krishna, Rollapadu** are AP areas; **Nagarhole** is in **Karnataka**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes list these Telangana PAs under AP.
AP's **13** WLS include **Coringa** (Kakinada), **Krishna** (Bapatla) and **Rollapadu** (Nandyal).
**NSTR** spans **AP + Telangana**.

n3ec3fea96c0.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the moist or tidal forest belt occurs in areas receiving rainfall of:
n3ec3fea96c0.x: The moist or tidal belt receives 125–200 cm; dry deciduous forests get 75–100 cm and thorn forests the lowest rainfall.
xa: Forest-bearing hills: North **Simhachalam**; West **Balaghat**; South **Palakonda and Nallamala**.
Mangroves grow in the **Godavari and Krishna estuaries**.

n8d92585fd28.s: Black (regur) soil, the second-largest soil group of Andhra Pradesh, covers about ____ of the State.
n8d92585fd28.x: Black soil covers about one-fourth (25 per cent) of AP, not 45 per cent.
xa: ⚠ Order by area: **Red > Black > Deltaic alluvium > Laterite**.
**Red** soil is the most extensive — **~66%** of AP (APPSC 2025 key).
⚠ Some notes put deltaic alluvium at **~5%**.
India's most widespread soil is **alluvium (45.6%)** — the source of the 45 trap.

nf465ab4f36f.s: In Andhra Pradesh, red soils are widely distributed in:
nf465ab4f36f.x: Red soils are widespread in Rayalaseema (Anantapur, Sri Sathya Sai, Kadapa, Nandyal, Kurnool) and also occur in coastal uplands.
xa: Red soil also covers coastal uplands: **Tirupati, Prakasam, Guntur, Eluru, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam, Srikakulam**.
The **Scarce Rainfall** agro-climatic zone is the **red soil** zone.
Rayalaseema's red soils are **shallow** with low organic matter.

n30df7f844d3.s: Deep black soils in Andhra Pradesh occur at:
n30df7f844d3.x: Deep black soils occur at Adoni and Alur; black soils cover about 25 per cent of AP.
xa: It is **self-ploughing**: deep cracks form when dry.
It is rich in **calcium, potash, magnesium**.
Very deep black soils lie in the **north-western Deccan Plateau**.

n3232fdc357f.s: Which soil is most suitable for the fertile agricultural tracts of the Krishna-Godavari deltas?
n3232fdc357f.x: The Krishna-Godavari deltaic tracts are characterised by highly fertile deltaic alluvial soil.
n3232fdc357f.tq: Use the regional soil-crop setting to identify the most suitable soil.
xs: The fertile **Krishna-Godavari deltas** have **deltaic alluvial soil** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Shallow red soil** marks **Rayalaseema**; **laterite** is acidic and of poor fertility; **skeletal** soils have no nutritive value.
xa: Alluvium is renewed with **silt each flood**.
It is rich in **potash and lime**.
Alluvium → **rice** (paddy) and **sugarcane**.

n92bc74ab542.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of areas associated with laterite soils in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Anantapur, Sri Sathya Sai, Kadapa and Nandyal only
Kurnool, Nandyal, Palnadu, Bapatla and Guntur
Ellavaram, Peddapuram, Kavali, Kovvur, Gudur and Sullurpeta
Konaseema, Krishna delta, Godavari delta and Nellore delta
n92bc74ab542.x: Ellavaram, Peddapuram, Kavali, Kovvur, Gudur and Sullurpeta are listed as laterite-soil areas. Laterite also occurs in elevated areas such as Satyavedu and Puttur and in coastal pockets.
n92bc74ab542.tq: Check whether every location in the option belongs to the same soil-distribution group.
xs: **Ellavaram, Peddapuram, Kavali, Kovvur, Gudur and Sullurpeta** are coastal **laterite** areas — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Anantapur, Sri Sathya Sai, Kadapa, Nandyal** are **red** soil; **Kurnool, Palnadu, Bapatla, Guntur** **black**; **Konaseema** and the deltas **alluvium**.
xa: Elevated laterite: **Satyavedu, Puttur**.
Inland laterite belt: **Tirupati, Gudur, Sullurpet, Satyavedu, Puttur**.
Pockets: Nellore, Srikakulam, East Godavari, Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam.

n8c20f46859b.s: The saline soils of the Rayalaseema plateau, with high lime and salt, are generally:
o: The most fertile soils of the State
n8c20f46859b.x: Saline soils of the Rayalaseema plateau contain much lime and salt and are generally unfit for cropping.
xa: Salinity lowers yields + breaks down soil structure.
**39 watersheds (896 villages)** classed "saline" (2025-26).
Reclamation: drain and leach salts; **gypsum** for alkaline soils.

nb51c8c1a54d.s: Heavily eroded tracts of Rayalaseema may develop skeletal soils that are characterised by:
o: High nutrient value and deep profiles
High water retention and abundant humus
nb51c8c1a54d.x: Severe erosion in Rayalaseema can leave skeletal soils with no nutritive value.
nb51c8c1a54d.tq: Infer the soil-quality outcome from the stated erosion process.
xs: Skeletal soils in heavily eroded tracts have **no nutritive value** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Fresh silt** deposition renews **deltaic alluvium**, the opposite case.
xa: Rayalaseema red soils are **shallow** with low organic matter.
**Podu** (shifting) cultivation strips topsoil in **ASR, Parvathipuram Manyam**.
Responses: **watershed** development + **MGNREGA** soil-and-water works.

n090ad9d159a.s: Which of the following is NOT a cause of soil degradation in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Heavy chemical use in the Guntur chilli belt
Periodic deposition of fresh river silt in the deltas
n090ad9d159a.x: Fresh flood silt renews deltaic alluvium; it does not degrade the soil.
xa: Delta problems come from **poor drainage + faulty irrigation**.
**APCNF** natural farming restores soil organic carbon.
**Podu** cultivation strips topsoil in **ASR**.

n41c7669da20.s: Under Rainfed Area Development in Andhra Pradesh, assistance per farm family is:
n41c7669da20.x: Rainfed Area Development gives Rs 30,000 per farm family.
xa: Other responses: **watershed** development + **MGNREGA** soil-and-water works.
**₹62.20 crore green-manure drive** for Kharif 2026.
**Soil Health Card** samples: **6.0 lakh** collected, **5.523 lakh** tested (2025-26).

n7c6c9896c73.s: Village-wise nutrient mapping and soil-sample analysis are functions of:
n7c6c9896c73.x: Soil Health Cards give soil-sample analysis and village-wise nutrient mapping so farmers know their soil's nutrient status.
xa: Launched **19 Feb 2015** at **Suratgarh**.
Now runs as **"Soil Health & Fertility" under RKVY** (since 2022-23).
AP 2025-26: **6.0 lakh** samples collected; **5.523 lakh** tested and uploaded.
Sampling via **10,778 Rythu Seva Kendras** in all **26** districts.

nd2d7bdbe858.s: Among pulses, black gram does best on which soil?
nd2d7bdbe858.x: Black gram does best on black soil, while red gram, green gram and horse gram suit red soil.
xa: Red soil also carries **groundnut**, castor, millets.
Black gram on black soils is a **UPSC** fact.
Black soil main crops: **cotton, chillies, tobacco, turmeric**.

n099c0282b45.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the distribution of soils?
o: Alluvium is India's most widespread soil, covering 45.6% of the country
Karnataka has mostly black soil, followed by red soil
Red soil is the dominant soil type in Andhra Pradesh
Alluvium covers about 6% of Andhra Pradesh
n099c0282b45.x: Karnataka has mostly red soil, followed by black soil.
xa: AP order: **Red > Black > Deltaic alluvium > Laterite**.
**Granitoid-gneiss** bedrock underlies much of AP.

nindian-geography-19-16.s: Sugarcane, jute, maize, oilseeds and fruits and vegetables are all suited to ____ soil.
nindian-geography-19-16.x: All five crops suit alluvial soil.
n: Alluvial soil is suitable for sugarcane. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Alluvial soil is suitable for jute. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Alluvial soil is suitable for maize. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Alluvial soil is suitable for oilseeds. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Alluvial soil is suitable for fruits and vegetables. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
xa: Alluvium is **deposited by rivers** — the **largest and most widespread** soil group.
It is rich in **potash, phosphoric acid, lime**; poor in **nitrogen and humus**.
Old alluvium = **"Bangar"**; new alluvium = **"Khaddar"**.
In AP, delta alluvium grows **rice** and **sugarcane**.

nindian-geography-19-28.s: Coffee, rubber and cashew are typically grown on ____ soil.
nindian-geography-19-28.x: Laterite soil grows coffee, rubber and cashew; red soil grows millets, pulses and groundnut.
n: Red soil is suitable for millets. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Red soil is suitable for pulses. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Red soil is suitable for groundnut. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Laterite soil is suitable for coffee. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Laterite soil is suitable for rubber. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Laterite soil is suitable for cashew. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
xa: **Alluvial**: wheat, rice, sugarcane, jute; **black**: cotton.
In AP, laterite grows **mango, cashew**, tamarind.
AP red soil pulses: **red gram, green gram, horse gram**; also castor.
Laterite forms under **high temperature and heavy rainfall**.

nindian-geography-19-14.s: Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Assam are widely covered by ____ soil.
nindian-geography-19-14.x: Alluvial soil is widely found in all six of these States.
n: Alluvial soil occurs in Punjab. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Alluvial soil occurs in Haryana. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Alluvial soil occurs in Uttar Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Alluvial soil occurs in Bihar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Alluvial soil occurs in West Bengal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Alluvial soil occurs in Assam. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
xa: **Deltaic alluvium**: **Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna** and **Cauvery** deltas.
**Valleys**: the **Narmada** and **Tapi**.
In AP: **Godavari and Krishna deltas**, Konaseema; also along the **Vamsadhara** and **Penna**.

nindian-geography-19-20.s: Which characteristic of black soil is specifically associated with drying?
o: It becomes permanently waterlogged on drying
It loses all mineral constituents on drying
nindian-geography-19-20.x: Black soil swells when wet and develops deep cracks on drying, which lets it self-plough.
nindian-geography-19-20.tq: Recall the features of black soil.
n: Black soil develops cracks on drying. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
xs: Black soil **develops cracks on drying** — option **(3)**.
The deep cracks let it **turn itself over** — **"self-ploughing"**.
This goes with its **clayey** texture and **very high water retention**.
xa: Black soil is particularly suitable for **cotton**.
AP black soils are **neutral to strongly alkaline**.
⚠ Desert soil, by contrast, is **sandy** with **low moisture retention**.

nindian-geography-19-31.s: Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Karnataka are major areas of ____ soil.
nindian-geography-19-31.x: All four are major black-soil areas.
n: Black soil occurs in Maharashtra. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Black soil occurs in Madhya Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Black soil occurs in Gujarat. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
Black soil occurs in Karnataka. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 56-64]
xa: It develops from **basaltic / lava** rocks.
AP's **very deep black soils** lie towards the **north-western Deccan Plateau**.
AP black soil districts: **Kurnool, Nandyal, YSR Kadapa, Guntur, Prakasam, Palnadu**.

nap-geography-20-5.s: In Andhra Pradesh, rice is mainly grown on:
nap-geography-20-5.x: Rice, like sugarcane, is mainly grown on delta alluvium, not the red soils of Rayalaseema.
n: Sugarcane grows in alluvial soils of delta areas. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 43-45]

The Kurnool Rock System is associated with erstwhile Cuddapah and Kurnool. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 54-55]
The Deccan Trap is found in Prakasam and Guntur. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 54-55]

nbf5841d565b.s: Which State is the top producer of limestone in India?

n816e1ebc367.s: Coal in the Godavari valley is associated with which formation?

n60b1012f3eb.s: The Cuddapah formation of Andhra Pradesh is best described as which of the following?

A Gondwana formation containing only coal deposits
A Proterozoic formation of about 1.6 billion years associated with barytes, limestone and uranium
A recent coastal formation containing only beach sands
n60b1012f3eb.x: The Cuddapah formation is Proterozoic, approximately 1.6 billion years old, and occurs mainly in the Kadapa, Nandyal, Kurnool, Annamayya and Prakasam areas. It contains barytes, limestone, uranium and other minerals.
xs: The **Cuddapah** formation is **Proterozoic, about 1.6 billion years** old, with **barytes, limestone and uranium** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It also holds asbestos, dolomite, steatite and diamonds, in Kadapa, Nandyal, Kurnool, Annamayya and Prakasam.

**Tummalapalle** uranium (YSR Kadapa) lies in the Cuddapah basin; its ore is **low-grade**.
**Mangampeta** barytes and Kadapa **steatite** (soapstone) both come from the Cuddapah system.
⚠ **Gondwana** = coal; **Cuddapah** = barytes; **khondalites** = bauxite.

nebfb1416cd1.s: Chromite in Andhra Pradesh is associated with:

**Eastern Ghats khondalites** carry bauxite, graphite and manganese.
