n37a12a19e25.tq: Distinguish the launch dates of successive adult-literacy programmes.
xs: **National Literacy Mission**: **5 May 1988** — option **(1)**.
**2 Oct 1978** = **NAEP**; **8 Sep 2009** = **Saakshar Bharat**; **5 Nov 2024** = AP ULLAS classes began.
xa: NLM aimed at **functional literacy**; its mass strategy was the **TLC**.
⚠ NAEP = age **15-35**; Saakshar Bharat and ULLAS = **15+**.

nfcaeb21ef52.s: Saakshar Bharat, launched on International Literacy Day 2009, primarily targeted:
o: Adults aged 15+ years, with focus on women
Youth aged 15–29 years in urban areas
nfcaeb21ef52.x: Saakshar Bharat was launched on 8 September 2009 for adults aged 15 years and above, with special focus on women.
xa: International Literacy Day: **UNESCO** day since **1966**, first observed **1967**.
**ULLAS** (**2022**) also targets non-literates aged **15+**.
ILD **8 Sep 2026** theme: "**Literacy for people, the planet and prosperity**".

nf6aa91f1680.s: The National Literacy Mission was launched in:
nf6aa91f1680.x: The order was Farmers' Functional Literacy Programme (1967-68), NAEP (1978), National Literacy Mission (1988) and Saakshar Bharat (2009).
xa: **Operation Blackboard**: **1987**, under **NPE 1986**.

nbf1129f5921.s: ULLAS (New India Literacy Programme) targets non-literates aged:
nbf1129f5921.x: ULLAS, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (2022-23 to 2026-27), targets non-literates aged 15 and above.
xa: It is **volunteer-based**; full literacy = **95%+**.
Five components: **FLN**, **critical life skills**, **basic education**, **vocational skills**, **continuing education**.

n726e4ef81d5.s: The national benchmark for declaring a population ‘fully literate’ under ULLAS is literacy among at least:
o: 75% of persons aged 7 years and above
95% of persons aged 15 years and above
85% of persons aged 10 years and above
90% of persons aged 15 years and above
n726e4ef81d5.x: Under ULLAS, the national benchmark for being fully literate is 95% literacy among persons aged 15 years and above.
n726e4ef81d5.tq: Discriminate using both the percentage and the specified age group.
xs: Under **ULLAS**, "fully literate" = **95%+** among persons aged **15 and above** — option **(2)**.
The **7+** age is the Census/PLFS literacy definition, not the ULLAS benchmark.
xa: First fully literate UT: **Ladakh (2024)**; first state: **Mizoram (2025)**.
**Uttarakhand**: **6th** state, **Jul 2026**, **98%+**.
ULLAS motto: "**Jan Jan Saakshar**".

n493f1ae8c23.s: NIPUN Bharat is primarily associated with foundational literacy and numeracy by which grade, and its extended deadline is:
n493f1ae8c23.x: NIPUN Bharat focuses on foundational literacy at the Grade-3 level, and its deadline was extended from 2025 to 2026-27.
n493f1ae8c23.tq: Separate NIPUN Bharat’s Grade-3 goal from NEP 2020’s broader adult-literacy target.
xs: **NIPUN Bharat**: foundational literacy by **Grade 3**, deadline now **2026-27** — option **(3)**.
NEP's original **2025** FLN target was moved.
xa: **NEP 2020** foundational stage covers ages **3-8**.
**FLN Index** (Institute for Competitiveness for **EAC-PM**): **Punjab** highest in the second edition.
ULLAS also has an **FLN** component for adults.

nf07d3bd617c.s: Which of the following is NOT a target of NEP 2020 mentioned in relation to enrolment and literacy?
o: Bringing 2 crore out-of-school children back into education
nf07d3bd617c.x: The target for 100% youth and adult literacy is 2030, not 2025. The other three are stated NEP 2020 targets.
nf07d3bd617c.tq: Find the changed year in an otherwise familiar target statement.
xs: **100% youth and adult literacy by 2025** is wrong — option **(1)**; the target year is **2030**.
The real targets: **2 crore** out-of-school children back, **100% GER in school by 2030**, **50% GER in higher education by 2035**.
xa: ⚠ The **2025** date belongs to NEP's FLN-by-Grade-3 goal, now moved to **2026-27** under **NIPUN Bharat**.
Assessment centre: **PARAKH**.

n0abc585a5b0.s: The first State to attain full literacy (2025) was:
n0abc585a5b0.x: Mizoram was first in 2025, followed by Goa and Sikkim; Uttarakhand became the sixth in July 2026.
xa: **Ladakh** (UT, **2024**) came before all.
**Tripura** and **Himachal Pradesh** also preceded Sikkim.

n846108c1f73.s: AP's ULLAS implementation focuses on SHG members, school cooks and helpers, night watchmen and:
n846108c1f73.x: The AP focus groups are SHG members, school cooks and helpers, night watchmen and anganwadi ayahs.
xa: All **26** districts; **41,500** SHG volunteer teachers (**SERP**) for **4,15,000** learners.
Classes from **5 Nov 2024**; video lessons via **TCS**.
Target-oriented drive for districts **below the state average**.

nf31c0426f06.s: The National Education Policy, 2020 introduced which curricular structure?
nf31c0426f06.x: NEP 2020, which replaced NPE 1986 after 34 years, adopted the 5+3+3+4 structure.
xa: Targets: **100% GER in school by 2030**; **50% GER** in higher education by **2035**.
**Operation Blackboard (1987)** came under **NPE 1986**.

n7439b94408e.s: Operation Blackboard was introduced in which year and under which policy?
n7439b94408e.x: Operation Blackboard was introduced in 1987 under the National Policy on Education, 1986.
n7439b94408e.tq: Separate the launch year from the year of the policy under which the programme operated.
xs: **Operation Blackboard**: **1987**, under **NPE 1986** — option **(1)**.
**Samagra Shiksha** came in **2018**; **NEP 2020** replaced NPE 1986.
xa: Aim: basic facilities for **primary schools in educationally backward areas** (APPSC-GS 2025 key).
Minimum: **two rooms**, **two teachers**, **teaching aids**.

nee2d3fa7d32.s: Which of the following was NOT among the basic provisions associated with Operation Blackboard?
o: English laboratories in every government school
At least two rooms for a primary school
nee2d3fa7d32.x: Operation Blackboard provided basic facilities such as two rooms, two teachers and teaching aids. English laboratories were part of the Nadu-Nedu facilities, not Operation Blackboard.
nee2d3fa7d32.tq: Distinguish facilities of neighbouring education schemes by identifying the misplaced provision.
xs: **English laboratories** were not under Operation Blackboard — option **(1)**.
Operation Blackboard gave at least **two rooms**, **two teachers** and **teaching aids**.
**English labs** are among the **nine** facilities of AP's **Nadu-Nedu**.
xa: Operation Blackboard: **1987**, under **NPE 1986**.
Nadu-Nedu launched **14 Nov 2019**.

n9e7a2e83324.s: Mana Badi Nadu-Nedu was launched in Andhra Pradesh on:
n9e7a2e83324.x: Mana Badi Nadu-Nedu was launched on 14 November 2019.
n9e7a2e83324.tq: Use the date-specific scheme identification method and distinguish it from the 2018 launch of Samagra Shiksha.
xs: **Mana Badi Nadu-Nedu** was launched on **14 November 2019** — option **(3)**.
It transforms **government schools** in phases with **nine basic facilities**.
xa: Facilities: **toilets**, **drinking water**, **furniture**, **paint**, **repairs**, **lights and fans**, **green chalkboards**, **English labs**, **compound walls**.
⚠ **14 November** is the date; the year is **2019**, not 2018.

na2108da0829.s: According to the Census definition, a literate person is one who:
o: is aged seven years or above and can both read and write with understanding in any language
is aged five years or above and can read and write without understanding
is aged ten years or above and has completed primary education
is aged seven years or above and can only read in any language
na2108da0829.x: A literate person is aged seven years or above and must be able to both read and write with understanding in any language. A person who can only read is not treated as literate.
na2108da0829.tq: Use the exact official definition and distinguish ‘read and write with understanding’ from merely reading.
xs: Census literate = aged **7 and above** who can **both read and write with understanding** in any language — option **(1)**.
One who can **only read** is **not literate** — so option **(4)** fails.
Age **5+** was used only in **1951-1971**; completing primary school is not part of the test.
xa: Age **7+** has been used since **1981**.
**ULLAS** full literacy = **95%+** among those aged **15+**.
**PLFS** uses the same **7+** definition, but on a sample survey.

n626fcd0fd04.s: Which State recorded the highest FLN score in the second edition of the Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Index released for the EAC-PM?
n626fcd0fd04.x: Punjab recorded the highest FLN score in the second edition of the FLN Index.
n626fcd0fd04.tq: Use the ranking fact directly and avoid substituting a generally high-literacy State for the indexed State.
xs: **Punjab** had the highest FLN score in the second edition — option **(2)** (APPSC-GS 2022 key).
The **FLN Index** is by the **Institute for Competitiveness** for the **EAC-PM**.
xa: **NIPUN Bharat** targets Grade-3 FLN by **2026-27**.
NEP 2020 foundational stage: ages **3-8**.
n626fcd0fd04.fixed: stem cited an answer key; reworded (y84eb9277d15)

n35df3829871.s: Census 2027 is expected to add a question relating to:
n35df3829871.x: Census 2027 adds a digital literacy question.
n35df3829871.tq: Identify the exact census indicator rather than a broader technology-related distractor.
xs: **Census 2027** adds a **digital literacy** question — option **(2)** (**15 Aug 2026**).
It extends literacy measurement beyond the basic **read and write with understanding** test.
xa: Census literate = **7+**, can **read and write with understanding**.
ULLAS full literacy = **95%+** among **15+**.
**Uttarakhand**: 6th fully literate state (**Jul 2026**).

n48c5f726e61.s: In the Census, a main worker is one who worked for at least ____ in the reference year.
n48c5f726e61.x: A main worker worked 183 days (six months) or more in the reference year.
xa: Census 2011: main workers **75.2%**, marginal **24.8%** of all workers.
Four categories: **cultivators**, **agricultural labourers**, **household industry**, **other workers**.
⚠ PLFS **UPSS** counts as employed anyone who worked **30+ days** in the year.

nbb7aabefbf2.s: For a Census Town, at least what share of male main workers must be in non-agricultural activities?
nbb7aabefbf2.x: A Census Town needs 5,000+ population, 75%+ of male main workers in non-agricultural work and density of at least 400 per sq km.
xa: Criteria **unchanged since 1981**; retained for **Census 2027** (**17 Sep 2026**).
Census non-workers include **students**, **household duties**, **dependants**, **pensioners**, **rentiers**.

n888a1d00728.s: Which factor has contributed to the increasing feminisation of farm work in India?
o: A rise in women’s share of operational holdings to 55%
n888a1d00728.x: Men’s out-migration has increased women’s participation in farm work, even though women hold only 12.8% of operational holdings.
n888a1d00728.tq: Link the stated demographic movement with its occupational consequence.
xs: **Men's out-migration** drives the **feminisation of farm work** — option **(3)**.
Women hold only **12.8%** of operational holdings, not 55%.
**Mechanisation** cut manual demand, and **unpaid family work** has risen — options **(2)** and **(4)** fail.
xa: Women workers (2011): **55%** agricultural labourers.
Mechanisation cut manual demand (**2004-05 to 2012**).

n558509f752d.s: Which of the following is NOT a Census category of non-workers?
n558509f752d.x: The Census categories include students, household-duty persons, dependants, pensioners, rentiers, beggars or vagrants and others. Permanent industrial employers are not listed as a category.
n558509f752d.tq: Identify the outsider in a classification list.
xs: **Permanent industrial employers** are not a non-worker category — option **(1)**.
Census non-workers: **students**, **household duties**, **dependants**, **pensioners**, **rentiers**, **beggars/vagrants**, others.
xa: Worker categories: **cultivators**, **agricultural labourers**, **household industry**, **other workers**.

n69f0e3c2720.s: Under UPSS, a person is counted as employed if he or she worked for at least ____ in the year.
n69f0e3c2720.x: UPSS counts 30 or more days of work in the 365-day reference year as employment.
xa: **CWS**: 7-day week; employed if worked at least **1 hour** on any one day.
CWS captures **short-term / seasonal** unemployment.
⚠ UR denominator = **labour force**; PU and WPR denominator = **population**.
PLFS is run by the **NSO (MoSPI)**.

n0a59af57144.s: Which one of the following is the correct expression for the Worker Population Ratio (WPR)?
o: Labour force divided by total population multiplied by 100
Employed persons divided by total population multiplied by 100
Unemployed persons divided by labour force multiplied by 100
Unemployed persons divided by total population multiplied by 100
n0a59af57144.x: WPR equals employed persons divided by total population, multiplied by 100.
n0a59af57144.tq: Focus on the denominator to distinguish WPR from LFPR and unemployment rate.
xs: **WPR = employed persons / total population x 100** — option **(2)** (RPSC 2024 key).
(Employed + unemployed)/population = **LFPR**; unemployed/labour force = **UR**; unemployed/population = **PU**.
xa: ⚠ UR denominator = **labour force**; PU and WPR = **population**.

nb63103b7bad.s: The Periodic Labour Force Survey is conducted by the:
o: NITI Aayog under the Ministry of Finance
Registrar General of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs
Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Rural Development
nb63103b7bad.x: The PLFS is conducted by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
nb63103b7bad.tq: Use the institution-authority association to reject swapped departmental options.
xs: PLFS is run by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** under **MoSPI** — option **(1)**.
It gives **LFPR**, **WPR**, **UR** and **PU** indicators.
xa: Headline rates for age **15+**.
"Working age" varies: **15-59**, **15-64** or **16-64** — check the stem.
Status measures: **usual status**, **UPSS**, **CWS**, **CDS**.

n19033cf2692.s: Under Current Weekly Status, a person is counted as employed if he or she worked for at least ____ on any day of the reference week.
n19033cf2692.x: CWS counts one hour of work on any day of the reference week as employment.
xa: ⚠ The **1-hour CWS rule** may hide distress and underemployment.
**WPR** = employed / **total population** x 100.

ncefd7f5229e.s: The U-curve of female labour force participation is associated with:
ncefd7f5229e.x: Claudia Goldin's U-curve says women's work participation first falls and then rises with development; India followed the declining half till 2018-19.
xa: Reasons for the rise: **unpaid family work**, **distress**, **COVID return migration**, broader **survey coverage**.

nfe06239c544.s: As per Census 2011, which category formed the largest share of India's workers?
nfe06239c544.x: Other workers formed 41.6% of workers, ahead of agricultural labourers (30.0%), cultivators (24.6%) and household industry workers (3.8%).
xa: ⚠ In 2011, **labourers outnumbered cultivators** for the **first time**.
Agriculture's share of workers: **58.2% (2001)** → **54.6% (2011)**.

n06c6567c885.s: According to the 2011 Census, which category first exceeded the other in India?
n06c6567c885.x: In 2011, agricultural labourers constituted 30.0% of workers, exceeding cultivators at 24.6% for the first time.
n06c6567c885.tq: Direct comparison of two closely related occupational categories.
xs: In **2011**, **agricultural labourers exceeded cultivators** for the **first time** — option **(4)**.
Labourers **30.0%** vs cultivators **24.6%**.
xa: ⚠ **2001**: cultivators **31.7%** > labourers **26.5%**.
Women workers: **55%** agricultural labourers vs **24%** cultivators.

na886ff19bf8.s: According to Census 2011, the largest share of all workers in Andhra Pradesh was engaged as:
na886ff19bf8.x: Agricultural labourers formed 47.9% of all workers in Andhra Pradesh, followed by other workers at 34.8%.
na886ff19bf8.tq: Identify the maximum value in the state-wise occupational share comparison.
xs: **Agricultural labourers** were AP's largest group: **47.9%** of all workers — option **(4)**.
**Other workers 34.8%**, **cultivators 14.5%**, **household industry 2.9%**.
xa: All agricultural labourers: **110.52 lakh** (**86.12** main + **24.40** marginal).
⚠ India's largest group is **other workers (41.6%)**.

n5e92de48bf2.s: In Census 2011, marginal workers formed about ____ of India's total workers.
n5e92de48bf2.x: Of 4,818.89 lakh workers, main workers were 75.2% and marginal workers 24.8%.
xa: Marginal workers: **1,193.23 lakh**.
Non-workers: **7,288.27 lakh** (about **60%** of population).

n6380aaa8f8e.s: The share of agriculture in India’s workforce declined from 2001 to 2011 from:
n6380aaa8f8e.x: Agriculture’s share of workers declined from 58.2% in 2001 to 54.6% in 2011, while the secondary and tertiary shares increased.
n6380aaa8f8e.tq: Read the direction of change carefully and reject the reversed sequence.
xs: Agriculture's share of workers fell **58.2% (2001)** → **54.6% (2011)** — option **(2)**.
**Secondary and tertiary** shares rose.
xa: **NSS 2011-12**: agriculture about **48.9%** of workers.
**PLFS Q2 FY26**: agriculture **42.4%** of employment.

na3c280481ab.s: In 2011–12, agriculture employed about ____ of India's workers.
na3c280481ab.x: Agriculture employed about 48.9% and services about 27% of workers in 2011–12.
xa: Census: agriculture **54.6%** (2011).
PLFS Q2 FY26: agriculture **42.4%**.

n56996ed0067.s: In rural India, Scheduled Castes are concentrated mostly among:
n56996ed0067.x: Scheduled Castes are largely marginal farmers and landless agricultural labourers.
xa: High agricultural-labourer states: **Bihar, AP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha**.
Agricultural labourer = works on **another person's land for wages**.

nbfaf00f570e.s: The overall Work Participation Rate of India in Census 2011 was:
nbfaf00f570e.x: The overall WPR was 39.8% (male 53.3%, female 25.5%); about 60% were non-workers.
xa: Workers: **4,818.89 lakh** — main **75.2%**, marginal **24.8%**.
Main worker = worked at least **183 days**; marginal = less than **183 days**.
2011: **agricultural labourers (30.0%)** outnumbered **cultivators (24.6%)** for the first time.
AP's Census 2011 WPR: about **46.6%** — above India.

nc579d7fb1a6.s: Which of the following groups is correctly associated with a high cultivator share among workers?
nc579d7fb1a6.x: Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland are identified with a high cultivator share. Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry have high shares of other workers.
nc579d7fb1a6.tq: Use the occupational-category distinction to avoid confusing cultivator-heavy and other-worker-heavy regions.
xs: High **cultivator** share: **Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland** — option **(2)**.
**Delhi, Chandigarh, Puducherry** have high "**other workers**"; **Bihar, AP** have high **agricultural-labourer** shares.
xa: High agricultural labourers: **Bihar, AP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha**, Jharkhand, West Bengal, MP.
**HP** also has a high **WPR**.

n45082475e2b.s: In Census 2011, women formed about ____ of India's agricultural labourers.
n45082475e2b.x: Women were 55% of agricultural labourers but only 24% of cultivators, and held 12.8% of operational holdings.
xa: **Men's out-migration** → **feminisation** of farm work (UPSC).
Rural women gave **80%** of the rise in female workers (2017-18 to 2023-24).
n45082475e2b.fixed: 55%/24% are shares of women workers by category, not women's share of all labourers/cultivators (women are ~43% of agri labourers)

nde06c82d639.s: In Q2 of FY 2025–26 (July–September 2025), agriculture's share of total employment in India was:
nde06c82d639.x: Agriculture had 42.4% of employment, self-employment 55.8% and casual labour 18.9%.
xa: Rural jobs **57%** agricultural; urban jobs **62%** in services.
**56.2 crore** employed (15+); **8.7 lakh** jobs added over Q1 (ES 2025-26).

n4632f049071.s: Which of the following correctly gives the annual PLFS 2025 values for LFPR, WPR and UR, respectively?
n4632f049071.x: The annual PLFS 2025 figures were 59% for LFPR, 57% for WPR and approximately 3% for unemployment rate.
n4632f049071.tq: Preserve the order of the three indicators while matching the annual release figures.
xa: Youth UR: **9.9%**.

n8328f9d7b56.s: For January–March 2026 under CWS for persons aged 15 years and above, which combination is correct?
n8328f9d7b56.x: For January–March 2026, the CWS estimates were LFPR 55.5%, WPR 52.8% and UR 5.0%.
n8328f9d7b56.tq: Match the release period and survey status before comparing the figures.
xs: **59 / 57 / 3** are annual PLFS 2025.
xa: Urban UR **6.6%**, rural **4.3%**.
Female LFPR **34.7%**.

ne07a4fc02ee.s: India's female LFPR (aged 15 and above) in 2017–18 was:
xa: Rural women gave **80%** of the rise.
Rural gains led by **West Bengal, UP, Bihar**.

n69ef7432619.s: A fall in the unemployment rate may not signal better jobs because it may reflect:
n69ef7432619.x: A lower unemployment rate may reflect distress entry into low-productivity work rather than creation of decent, secure employment.
xa: The **1-hour CWS rule** may hide underemployment.
Jan-Mar 2026 UR: **5.0%**; annual PLFS 2025: **3%**.

n0873a836cc9.s: The Census 2011 Work Participation Rate of Andhra Pradesh, calculated from 230.81 lakh workers out of a population of 495.77 lakh, was approximately:
n0873a836cc9.x: Dividing 230.81 lakh workers by 495.77 lakh population gives an approximate WPR of 46.6%, higher than the all-India rate.
n0873a836cc9.tq: Apply the WPR formula and distinguish the Census estimate from the later PLFS estimate.
xs: **39.8%** is India's Census WPR; **43.7%** and **45.6%** are PLFS 2023-24 WPRs for India and AP.
xa: AP = **4.79%** of India's workers.
AP agricultural labourers: **47.9%** of all workers.

nacf6dc5e473.s: As per PLFS 2023–24 (usual status, all ages), the LFPR of Andhra Pradesh was:
nacf6dc5e473.x: AP's LFPR was 47.5% and WPR 45.6%, above India's 45.1% and 43.7%.
xa: AP female LFPR **35.8%** vs India **31.7%**.
AP LFPR rural **50.1%**, urban **41.3%**.

n4b158ed2cce.s: Which of the following has contributed to low female work participation in India?
o: Mechanisation reducing demand for manual labour
Wide availability of flexible working hours
n4b158ed2cce.x: Mechanisation, greater education of girls, lack of flexible hours, distance, safety concerns and family duties have lowered female work participation.
xa: ⚠ **Subsistence farming** explains the **rise**, not low levels.
Women hold only **12.8%** of operational holdings.

necad73005d0.s: As per PLFS 2023-24, the female LFPR of Andhra Pradesh is:
necad73005d0.x: AP's female LFPR is 35.8%, above India's 31.7%, yet urban young women (15-29) have a WPR of only 15.9%.
xa: AP female WPR: **39.6% rural** vs **22.8% urban** (PLFS 2023-24).
**MGNREGS** is one reason for higher rural female WPR.

n3456e8fbc9f.s: In 2011, main agricultural labourers formed about ____ of Andhra Pradesh's main workers.
n3456e8fbc9f.x: AP had 86.12 lakh main agricultural labourers out of 193.17 lakh main workers, about 45%.
xa: AP = **4.79%** of India's total workers.
AP main cultivators: **30.93 lakh** (~**16.0%**).

na77e09ccbc9.s: MGNREGA was launched on 2 February 2006 at which place?
na77e09ccbc9.x: MGNREGA was launched on 2 February 2006 at Bandlapalli in Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh.
na77e09ccbc9.tq: Apply the who-where-when recall pattern to a flagship employment programme.
xs: MGNREGA was launched at **Bandlapalli, Anantapur** (AP) — option **(1)**.
So the national programme began in **Andhra Pradesh**, not Tirupati, Amaravati or Vijayawada.
xa: Guarantees up to **100 days** of wage work.
**MGNREGS** helps explain AP's higher **rural female WPR** (**39.6%**).

nb5ee42f58b1.s: According to Census 2011, the Scheduled Caste population of India was approximately:
nb5ee42f58b1.x: India’s Scheduled Caste population was approximately 20.14 crore, or 16.6% of the total population, in Census 2011.
nb5ee42f58b1.tq: Keep the absolute count and percentage together; the nearby 12.6% and 18.5% figures refer to urban and rural population shares.
xs: SCs: **20.14 crore**, **16.6%** of India's population (2011) — option **(3)**.
**18.5%** and **12.6%** are SC shares of **rural** and **urban** India.
xa: About **20%** more than in **2001**.
About **76%** of SCs live in rural areas.

n1b8267620c8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the rural–urban distribution of Scheduled Castes in 2011?
o: About 76% of SCs lived in rural areas
About 24% of SCs lived in urban areas
SCs formed about 18.5% of India's rural population
SCs formed about 18.5% of India's urban population
n1b8267620c8.x: SCs formed about 12.6% of the urban population; 18.5% is their share of the rural population.
xa: **STs** are even more rural: **89.97%**.
SCs are more likely to live in rural, **low-income** areas (UPSC).

n8d67f831f89.s: In Census 2011, the Scheduled Caste share of Punjab's population was about:
n8d67f831f89.x: Punjab had about 31.9% SCs, Himachal Pradesh 25.2% and West Bengal 23.5%; Mizoram only about 0.1%.
xa: Highest number: **Uttar Pradesh** (about **4.1 crore**).

nd27618dd3c2.s: According to Census 2011, which State had the largest Scheduled Caste population in absolute numbers?
nd27618dd3c2.x: Uttar Pradesh had the largest SC population (about 4.1 crore, roughly 20% of India's SCs), followed by West Bengal and Bihar. Punjab has the highest SC share (31.9%), not the largest number.
xs: **Uttar Pradesh** has the largest SC **number** — about **4.1 crore**, ~**20%** of India's SCs — option **(3)**.
Then **West Bengal**, **Bihar**, **Tamil Nadu**; **Punjab** leads only in **share**.
xa: PYQs: UPPSC **2014**, BPSC **2011**.

nd674bdb28ab.s: The Scheduled Caste infant mortality rate (2018) was ____, against 32 nationally.
nd674bdb28ab.x: SC infant mortality was 44 against 32 nationally; SC unemployment was 5.5% against 5%.
xa: SCs are only **14%** of district judges.
SCs: mostly **marginal farmers and landless agricultural labourers**.

n8dd63e605b7.s: Some north-eastern and island territories have no notified Scheduled Caste population because their populations are:
n8dd63e605b7.x: Their people are overwhelmingly tribal, while SC status is tied to untouchability in the Hindu caste order.
xa: No SC notified: **Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, A&N Islands, Lakshadweep**.
**83rd Amendment (2000)**: no SC panchayat reservation needed in **Arunachal Pradesh**.

n71f612ac92b.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of States/UTs with no notified Scheduled Caste population?
o: Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Nagaland and Lakshadweep
Nagaland, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Arunachal Pradesh
Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep
n71f612ac92b.x: SCs are not notified in Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep. Mizoram (about 0.1%) and Meghalaya (about 0.6%) have small but non-zero SC populations, so A and C are wrong; Manipur also has notified SCs, so D is wrong.
n71f612ac92b.tq: Zero-SC four: Arunachal, Nagaland, A&N, Lakshadweep; Mizoram is a near-zero trap.
xs: No notified SCs: **Nagaland, Lakshadweep, A&N Islands, Arunachal Pradesh** — option **(2)**.
**Mizoram** has a **negligible (≈ 0.1%)** share, not zero; **Meghalaya** has ~**0.6%**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: the APPSC 2022 key grouped Mizoram with the zero-SC list.
Single "zero SC" state: **Nagaland** (UPPSC 2016).

nf753d9bcdee.s: Scheduled Castes are particularly concentrated in:
o: Fertile alluvial plains and coastal deltas
nf753d9bcdee.x: SCs are dense in fertile alluvial plains such as Punjab, the Ganga plain, West Bengal and coastal deltas, where settled farming used landless labour.
xa: Examples: **Punjab**, **Ganga plain**, **West Bengal**.
Highest district: **Koch Bihar** (about **50%**).

nbac00cc4800.s: The Scheduled Caste population of Andhra Pradesh in Census 2011 was approximately what percentage of India’s total Scheduled Caste population?
nbac00cc4800.x: Andhra Pradesh had about 84.69 lakh Scheduled Castes, constituting approximately 4.21% of India’s Scheduled Caste population.
nbac00cc4800.tq: Distinguish the State’s share of India’s Scheduled Caste population from its share within the State population.
xs: AP's **84.69 lakh** SCs = **4.21%** of India's SCs — option **(2)**.
They are ≈ **17%** of AP's **495.77 lakh** people — **17%** is the state share, not the national.

n7b15d011f1b.s: Which Constitutional Amendment removed SC seat reservation in the panchayats of Arunachal Pradesh?
n7b15d011f1b.x: The 83rd Amendment (2000) did this because Arunachal Pradesh is wholly tribal.
xa: Other no-SC areas: **Nagaland**, **A&N Islands**, **Lakshadweep**.
SC status open only to **Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists**.

ndab1e4b3b3c.s: Buddhists were made eligible for Scheduled Caste status in:
ndab1e4b3b3c.x: SC status covers Hindus, Sikhs (added 1956) and Buddhists (added 1990); Jains are not included.
xa: SCs notified in **31** States/UTs, **1,241** groups.
SC status rests on **untouchability** in the Hindu caste order.

n044a00c1c03.s: Census 2027 is expected to be significant because it will:
o: replace the population Census with a socio-economic survey
enumerate only Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes for the first time after independence
exclude caste information from the population enumeration
enumerate all castes for the first time in independent India, rather than only SCs and STs
n044a00c1c03.x: Census 2027 is described as the first enumeration of all castes in independent India, rather than an enumeration limited to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
n044a00c1c03.tq: Watch the scope trap between ‘all castes’ and ‘only SCs/STs’.
xs: **Census 2027** will **enumerate all castes** for the first time in independent India, not only SCs/STs — option **(4)**.
Its **Q.10** reads "**SC/ST/Caste**".
xa: ⚠ Post-2026 **delimitation** will re-fix SC/ST seats on new Census shares.
SCs today: notified in **31** States/UTs, **1,241** groups.

n928839737a3.s: The sex ratio of India's Scheduled Tribes in Census 2011 was:
n928839737a3.x: The ST sex ratio was 990; STs numbered 10.43 crore (8.6%), about 89.97% of them rural.
xa: ST literacy: **59%** vs **73%** nationally.
**705** notified STs in **30** States/UTs.
⚠ **Most STs** = **Madhya Pradesh**; **highest ST share** = **Lakshadweep (94.8%)**; **most notified tribes** = **Odisha (62)**.
No notified ST: **Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, Puducherry**.

n76f0797fd0d.s: As per the latest official figure, how many notified Scheduled Tribe groups are there in India?
n76f0797fd0d.x: The latest figure is 705 notified ST groups in 30 States/UTs; older references cite 698.
xa: STs are notified in **30** of the **35** States/UTs of 2011.
**Odisha** has the most notified tribes (**62**).
n76f0797fd0d.fixed: stem referred to unseen 'latest figure cited'

nd16b6519aaa.s: Which State has the highest share of Scheduled Tribes in its population?
nd16b6519aaa.x: Mizoram has the highest ST share among States (94.4%); Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population, and Lakshadweep the highest overall share (94.8%).
xa: ⚠ **Most STs** = **Madhya Pradesh**; **highest ST share** overall = **Lakshadweep**; **most notified tribes** = **Odisha (62)**.
After Mizoram come **Nagaland 86.5%**, **Meghalaya 86.1%** and **Ladakh 79.5%**.
**Tripura** (about **31.8%**) has the lowest ST share among the four NE states — APPSC-GS **2019** key.

n5e3a78784a7.s: Which Union Territory had the highest proportion of Scheduled Tribes in its total population according to the 2011 figures?
n5e3a78784a7.x: Lakshadweep had the highest ST share, at approximately 94.8%, followed by Mizoram at about 94.4%.
n5e3a78784a7.tq: Separate percentage share from absolute population and compare close numerical values.
xs: **Lakshadweep** had the highest ST share in 2011 — **94.8%** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is just ahead of **Mizoram** (**94.4%**), the top State.
**Ladakh** is lower at **79.5%**.
xa: ⚠ Highest ST **number** = **Madhya Pradesh** (**153.17 lakh**); highest **share** = **Lakshadweep**.
**Nagaland 86.5%** and **Meghalaya 86.1%** follow Mizoram.
No notified STs: **Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Chandigarh, Puducherry**.

n85e3cb19d86.s: Bihar was dropped from the proviso to Article 164(1) by the:
n85e3cb19d86.x: The 94th Amendment dropped Bihar and added Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, alongside MP and Odisha.
xa: The 94th Amendment added **Chhattisgarh** and **Jharkhand**.
**Art. 342**: President notifies STs after consulting the **Governor**; only **Parliament** can change the list.
Base order: **Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950**.
**Art. 338A**: **National Commission for STs**.

n50ab0a9d03f.s: Under the Fifth Schedule, the Tribes Advisory Council (TAC) of a State consists of:
o: Not more than 20 members, of whom about three-fourths are ST members of the State Legislative Assembly
Not more than 30 members, all nominated by the President
Not more than 20 members, of whom half are ST Members of Parliament
Exactly 10 members, all elected by the Autonomous District Councils
n50ab0a9d03f.x: The Fifth Schedule provides for a Tribes Advisory Council of up to 20 members, about three-fourths of whom are ST members of the State Legislative Assembly. It is not a body of 30 Presidential nominees, its members are MLAs rather than MPs, and Autonomous District Councils belong to the Sixth Schedule, not the Fifth.
n50ab0a9d03f.tq: TAC: max 20, about 3/4 ST MLAs (Fifth Schedule).
xs: The TAC has up to **20 members**, about **3/4** of them ST MLAs — option **(1)** is correct.
Its members are **ST MLAs**, not MPs or Presidential nominees.
**Autonomous District Councils** belong to the **Sixth Schedule**, not the Fifth.
xa: The TAC is part of the **Fifth Schedule** machinery with the **Governor's special powers**.
Fifth Schedule = **Art. 244(1)**; Scheduled Areas in **10** States.
Sixth Schedule: **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**.

n617d1732f8d.s: The Gadda Brahmin community was added to the ST list of Jammu and Kashmir in:
n617d1732f8d.x: Gadda Brahmin was added in 2024 with the Pahari and Paddari groups; the Sippis were added in 1991.
xa: The **2024** Act also added **Koli**.
Base list: ST Order **1950**; each change needs an amending Act.
Assam GoM (**Nov 2025**) proposed an **ST (Valley)** tier.

n7df9b2ca642.s: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission, constituted in 1953, is associated with which of the following observations regarding Scheduled Tribes?
o: Tribal communities are identified exclusively on the basis of geographical isolation
Tribal communities are defined only by their economic backwardness
Tribes must profess a particular religion
Tribes generally lead a separate and exclusive existence and may belong to any religion
n7df9b2ca642.x: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission stated that Scheduled Tribes lived a separate and exclusive existence, while also recognising that tribes could belong to any religion.
n7df9b2ca642.tq: Use the mandate rather than confusing the commission with later committees on land alienation or ST criteria.
xs: **Kaka Kalelkar** said STs lead a **separate, exclusive existence** and may follow **any religion** — option **(4)** is correct.
It was set up in **1953** under **Art. 340**.
xa: **Lokur** (**1965**) later framed the criteria: primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact, backwardness.
**Elwin Committee** (**1959**): Multi-Purpose Tribal Development Blocks.
**Dhebar** (**1960-61**) = first Art. 339 commission.

n07ecea5bc46.s: The Korku tribe is associated with the:
n07ecea5bc46.x: The Korku live in the Satpura–Melghat region of MP and Maharashtra; the Tharu are in the Terai and the Kadar in the Anamalai Hills.
xa: Nilgiri tribes: **Toda, Kota, Kurumba, Irula**.
**Kadar** are the southern odd one out among middle-Indian tribes (CGPSC **2024**).
**Baiga** = Mandla-Balaghat hills.

n4f8ec41f2eb.s: The Bhils are associated with the:
n4f8ec41f2eb.x: Bhils live in the Aravalli-Vindhya-Satpura belt; Santhals in the Santhal Parganas, Gonds in Gondwana and Bastar, Todas in the Nilgiris.
xa: **Onge** = Little Andaman; **Shompen** = Great Nicobar.
**Bonda** = **Malkangiri** hills, Odisha (most isolated PVTG).
**Dongaria Kondh** = **Niyamgiri Hills**, Odisha.

n6d0036c2000.s: Santali, Ho and Mundari belong to which language group?
n6d0036c2000.x: Santali, Ho and Mundari are Austro-Asiatic; Toda, Kota and Gondi are Dravidian.
xa: **Khasi** is also Austro-Asiatic; **Kurukh** and **Kui** are Dravidian.
**Tibeto-Chinese**: Bhotia, Lepcha, Garo, Naga.
**Bhili** = **Indo-European**.

n74c61596baa.s: According to Census 2011 figures used for Andhra Pradesh, which of the following correctly represents the Scheduled Caste population and share?
n74c61596baa.x: The Scheduled Caste population was 84.69 lakh, constituting 17.08% of the population of the 13-district Andhra Pradesh of 2011.
n74c61596baa.tq: Split the options by both population figure and percentage rather than relying on one value.
xs: AP's SCs number **84.69 lakh** (**17.08%**) — option **(4)** is correct.
**27.39 lakh** and **5.53%** are AP's **ST** figures.
xa: SC share **17.08%** = APPSC-G2 **2017** key.
AP has **34** ST communities.
Data are for the **13**-district AP of **2011**.

n35570ea6cc3.s: What was the Supreme Court's position concerning the Hindu Succession Act and notified Scheduled Tribes?
o: It abolished customary tribal succession in all cases.
It held that the Act automatically applies to all notified Scheduled Tribes.
It held that the Act does not apply to notified Scheduled Tribes.
It transferred succession matters entirely to Panchayats.
n35570ea6cc3.x: The Supreme Court held that the Hindu Succession Act does not apply to notified Scheduled Tribes.
n35570ea6cc3.tq: Test the judicial holding without confusing statutory non-application with abolition of custom.
xs: The SC held the **Hindu Succession Act does not apply** to **notified STs** — option **(3)** is correct.
It did not abolish tribal customs or hand succession to panchayats.
xa: STs are notified under **Art. 342**; only **Parliament** can change the list.
Khasi: **youngest daughter** inherits.
Shompen allege pressure over the **Great Nicobar project**.

nindian-geography-21-2.s: Which of the following about Census 2011 is INCORRECT?
o: Uttar Pradesh had the highest population.
Kerala had the highest literacy rate.
Bihar had the highest population density.
Arunachal Pradesh had the highest population density.
nindian-geography-21-2.x: Arunachal Pradesh had the lowest density (17 per sq km); Bihar had the highest (1,106).
n: Uttar Pradesh had the highest population. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 66-68]
Kerala had the highest literacy rate. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 66-68]
Bihar had the lowest literacy rate. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 66-68]
Bihar had the highest population density. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 66-68]
xa: **Kerala** also has the highest **sex ratio**; **Haryana** the lowest.
**Arunachal Pradesh** has the highest **child sex ratio**.
Urbanisation: highest **Goa**, lowest **Himachal Pradesh**.
Literacy lowest: **Bihar**.

nindian-geography-21-4.s: Which State had the highest child sex ratio (972) in Census 2011?
nindian-geography-21-4.x: Arunachal Pradesh had 972; Kerala had the highest overall sex ratio and Haryana the lowest.
n: Kerala had the highest sex ratio. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 66-68]
Haryana had the lowest sex ratio. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 66-68]
Arunachal Pradesh had the highest child sex ratio. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 66-68]
Haryana had the lowest child sex ratio. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 66-68]
xa: Haryana also has the lowest **child sex ratio**.
MP has **153.17 lakh** STs.
Highest ST share: **Lakshadweep 94.8%**, **Mizoram 94.4%**.
Most notified tribes: **Odisha (62)**.

nindian-geography-21-5.s: The second-largest Scheduled Tribe group of India is the:
nindian-geography-21-5.x: The Bhil are largest, the Gond second and the Santhal third; MP has the largest ST population.
n: Madhya Pradesh had the highest Scheduled Tribe population. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 66-68]
Bhil was the largest Scheduled Tribe group. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 66-68]
Gond was the second-largest Scheduled Tribe group. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 66-68]
Punjab had no notified Scheduled Tribe. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 66-68]
Santhal was the third-largest Scheduled Tribe group. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 66-68]
xa: Order: **Bhil > Gond > Santhal** (then Mina).
Bhil count ≈ **1.7 crore** of ~**10.4 crore** STs → about **16%**.
Others with no notified ST: **Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, Puducherry**.
Largest PVTG: **Sahariya**.

n05fa05542ac.s: Gondi, the language of the Gonds, belongs to which language family?
n05fa05542ac.x: The Gonds are the second-largest tribe, and Gondi is a Dravidian language.
xa: Gond = second largest (JPSC **2021**); **Gondwana**, **Bastar**.
Gond: '**ghotul**' youth dormitory, **Sulur** flute; sub-groups **Raj, Madia, Dhurve**.
**Adi Vaani** covers **Gondi**.

na0b8248c0c4.s: The Santhals revere ____ as Marang Buru.
na0b8248c0c4.x: The Santhals revere Parasnath Hills as Marang Buru; the Nilgiris are associated with the Todas.
xa: Parasnath / Marang Buru is **contested with Jains**.
Nilgiri Hills = **Toda, Kota, Kurumba, Irula**.
President **Droupadi Murmu** is a Santhal.

nce9479d0360.s: Longpi pottery is associated with the:
nce9479d0360.x: Longpi pottery is Tangkhul Naga; pukhor embroidery is Toda and the ghotul and Sulur flute are Gond.
xa: Niyam Raja; Niyamgiri festival (April) — **Dongria Kondh**.
Last to practise head-hunting — **Konyak** Naga.
**Snake-venom** expertise — **Irula**.

n0b424ea8ff5.s: Bastar Dussehra is associated with which State?
n0b424ea8ff5.x: Bastar Dussehra is associated with Chhattisgarh, whereas the Hornbill Festival belongs to Nagaland.
xa: **Niyamgiri festival** (April) = **Dongria Kondh**.
**Magha/Ba** festival = **Munda**.
Nagaland ST share **86.5%**.

n7511119a528.s: Under PESA, 1996, Scheduled Tribes get at least ____ of the seats in panchayats.
n7511119a528.x: STs get at least 50% of seats, and every chairperson must be an ST.
xa: **9** of **10** states have framed PESA rules; **Odisha** has only draft rules.
PESA came from the **Bhuria Committee** (**1994-95**).
Scheduled Areas are in **10** States.

n5362cc3223e.s: The competing claims over Parasnath and Marang Buru involve which two communities or religious traditions?
n5362cc3223e.x: The debate concerns competing Jain and Santhal claims over the religious significance of Parasnath and Marang Buru.
n5362cc3223e.tq: Discriminate between a place-based religious dispute and unrelated tribal cultural markers.
xs: **Jains** and **Santhals** clash over **Parasnath** / **Marang Buru** — option **(2)** is correct.
Santhals revere the **Parasnath Hills** as **Marang Buru**.
xa: Santhals live mainly in **Jharkhand**; **Manjhi-Paragana** system.
President **Droupadi Murmu** is a Santhal.
Santali script: **Ol Chiki**.

nac889714cef.s: The Sahariya tribe is found mainly in:
nac889714cef.x: The Sahariya live in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, not Kerala.
xa: **Bhil**: Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP, Maharashtra and others.
**Munda**: Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Chhattisgarh, Bihar.
**Kadar** and **Moplah** are the **Kerala** groups.
The Gond traditionally practise **hunting and fishing**, and **shifting cultivation**.

na7d90b1d73e.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of minor tribes of India?
na7d90b1d73e.x: Jarawa, Onge, Andamanese and Arandan are minor tribes. Bhil, Gond, Santhal, Mina, Naikda and Oraon are the major tribes.
xs: **Jarawa, Onge and Arandan** are minor tribes — option **(2)** is correct.
**Bhil, Gond, Santhal, Mina, Naikda, Oraon** are on the major-tribe list.
xa: Minor tribes: **Jarawa, Onge, Andamanese, Arandan**.
**Jarawa** and **Onge** are Negrito PVTGs of A&N; **Onge** = **Little Andaman**.
Smallest PVTGs: **Sentinelese** + **Great Andamanese**.

nac487add99b.s: The Chenchu, Koya and Konda Reddi belong to which regional tribal group?
nac487add99b.x: They form the southern group; Bhil, Mina and Warli are western and Khasi, Garo and Naga north-eastern.
xa: Central zone: **Gond, Baiga, Santhal, Munda, Oraon, Ho, Korku**.
Lakshadweep groups: **Amindivi, Koya, Malmi, Melacheri**.
Himalayan tribes include **Gaddi, Gujjar, Bakarwal, Changpa, Tharu, Bhotia**.

n585e8ed8368.s: The Mangarh massacre of 1913 is associated with which tribal community and leader?
n585e8ed8368.x: The 1913 Mangarh massacre is associated with the Bhils and Govind Guru.
n585e8ed8368.tq: Match the historical event with its correct tribe and associated leader.
xs: The **Mangarh massacre 1913** is linked with the **Bhil** and **Govind Guru** — option **(1)** is correct.
Bhils live in the **Aravalli-Vindhya-Satpura** hills.
xa: Bhil = **largest** tribe of India; name from '**billu**' (bow).
Language **Bhili** is **Indo-European**.
Bhil count ≈ **1.7 crore** (~**16%** of STs).

n287832736b9.s: President Droupadi Murmu belongs to which tribal community?
n287832736b9.x: President Droupadi Murmu is a member of the Santhal tribal community.
n287832736b9.tq: Link the constitutional office-holder with the community explicitly associated with her.
xs: President **Droupadi Murmu** is a **Santhal** — option **(2)** is correct.
Santhals live mainly in **Jharkhand** (also West Bengal, Odisha).
xa: Santali is **Austro-Asiatic**; script **Ol Chiki**; Eighth Schedule by the **92nd Amendment, 2003**.
Santhals revere **Parasnath Hills** as **Marang Buru** (contested with Jains).
**Manjhi-Paragana** system; **Santhal Parganas**.

n8f69318ed02.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sentinelese?
o: Like the Shompen, they are classified as Mongoloid
Their island has been a tribal reserve since 1956
They live on North Sentinel Island
A 3-nautical-mile prohibited zone surrounds their island
n8f69318ed02.x: The Sentinelese are Negrito like the Jarawa and Onge; only the Shompen of Great Nicobar are Mongoloid.
xa: Smallest PVTGs: **Sentinelese** + **Great Andamanese**.
Other Negrito PVTGs: **Jarawa, Onge, Great Andamanese**.
**Onge** = Little Andaman; **Shompen** = Great Nicobar.

ndcd9c67a90a.s: The last tribe in India to practise head-hunting was the:
ndcd9c67a90a.x: The Konyak Naga were the last head-hunters; the Tangkhul Naga are known for Longpi pottery.
xa: **Bison Horn Maria** = Gond sub-tribe, Chhattisgarh.
Irula = **artisans** (Vidyarthi and Rai).
**Hornbill Festival** = **Nagaland**.

nbd37eda0c0d.s: Adi Vaani, India's first AI translation platform for tribal languages, was launched under the:
nbd37eda0c0d.x: Adi Vaani was launched under the Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan and covers Bhili, Gondi, Mundari and Santali.
xa: **TribeX** teaches tribal languages and crafts.
Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan: **20 lakh** grassroots leaders; **1 lakh** villages.
**Odisha** teaches in **21 tribal languages** in **1,483** schools.

nbdb04f3ff64.s: Eklavya Model Residential Schools are modelled on the:
nbdb04f3ff64.x: EMRS follow the Navodaya model; the target is 740 schools.

**PM-JANMAN** (**Nov 2023**): **Rs 24,104 cr** for **75 PVTGs**.
**DAJGUA** (**Sep 2024**): **Rs 79,156 cr**, **17 ministries**.

nddad3f1be27.s: The Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan aims to develop how many grassroots leaders?
nddad3f1be27.x: It aims for 20 lakh leaders across 1 lakh villages, linked to Tribal Village Vision 2030.
xa: **Adi Vaani**, the AI tribal-language platform, was launched under this Abhiyan.
**DAJGUA**: about **63,000** villages, **5** years.
**PM-JANMAN**: **75** PVTGs, **11** interventions.

nf2dfb816b33.s: In Andhra Pradesh, tribal settlements are mainly concentrated in:
o: The Eastern Ghats, Godavari basin hill tracts and Nallamala belt
nf2dfb816b33.x: AP's tribal settlements are concentrated in the Eastern Ghats, north coastal hill tracts, Godavari basin and Nallamala belt, following forested uplands rather than deltas.
xa: The **Chenchu** PVTG lives in the **Nallamala**.

**3,512** tribal villages.

nindian-geography-7-21.s: The Kadar tribe are forest dwellers of the:

n: The Irula tribe is located in Tamil Nadu. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Irula tribe is located in South India. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Kadar tribe is located in Kerala. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Kadar tribe is located in South India. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
xa: The **Kadar** are forest foragers of the **Anamalai** hills — the "odd one out" among middle-Indian tribes.
The **Irula** are known for **snake-venom expertise**.
**Nilgiris** tribes: **Toda, Kota, Kurumba, Irula**.
**Chenchu** live in the **Nallamala** region of AP.

nindian-geography-9-2.s: Which of the following about the Tharu is INCORRECT?
o: They are a pastoral tribe of the Dhauladhar Range.
They are found in the Terai of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
They are found in Nainital, Uttarakhand.
They are found in Khatima and Sitarganj of Udham Singh Nagar.
nindian-geography-9-2.x: The Dhauladhar pastoralists are the Gaddi; the Tharu are a Terai people of UP, Bihar and Uttarakhand.
n: Tharu are found in the Terai of Uttar Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
Tharu are found in the Terai of Bihar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
Tharu observe Diwali as a sorrow. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
Tharu are located in Nainital, Uttarakhand. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
Tharu are located in Khatima, Udham Singh Nagar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
Tharu are located in Sitarganj, Udham Singh Nagar. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
