n1fde5b1fdae.s: The largest PVTG of India is the:
n1fde5b1fdae.x: The Sahariya are the largest PVTG; the Sentinelese and Great Andamanese are the smallest.
xa: PVTGs total **75**.
AP's **3** Feb **2024** variants: **Bondo Porja, Khond Porja, Konda Savara**.
First PVTG with habitat rights: **Bharia (MP)**.

nb0c60492780.x: The Baiga are from MP, the Chenchu from AP, the Toda from Tamil Nadu and the Great Andamanese from A&N.
xa: Other A&N PVTGs: **Jarawa, Onge, Sentinelese, Shompen**.
TN PVTGs also include **Kota** and **Irula**; MP also has **Sahariya**.
**Birhor** = Jharkhand PVTG.

n681a88af67d.s: Under Section 3(1)(e) of the Forest Rights Act, which PVTG was the first to receive habitat rights?
n681a88af67d.x: Bharia of Madhya Pradesh were the first PVTG to receive habitat rights, followed by Kamar and Baiga of Chhattisgarh.
n681a88af67d.tq: Distinguish the first beneficiary from the groups that followed.
xs: **Bharia (MP)** was the first PVTG to get habitat rights under FRA **Sec. 3(1)(e)** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Kamar** and **Baiga** (Chhattisgarh) got them **after** Bharia.
xa: **FRA 2006** covers STs and **OTFDs** (**3** generations or **75** years of residence).
Occupation must predate **13 Dec 2005**; ceiling **4 ha**.
Largest PVTG = **Sahariya**.

nf8b2c6f8789.s: Among the Khasi, who traditionally inherits the family property?
o: The eldest daughter only after marriage
nf8b2c6f8789.x: Khasi society is matrilineal, and the youngest daughter inherits the family property.
nf8b2c6f8789.tq: Test the specific inheritance rule rather than the general label of matriliny.
xs: Among the **Khasi**, the **youngest daughter** inherits — option **(1)** is correct.
Khasi are **matrilineal** and the largest community of **Meghalaya**.
xa: The **Garo** are also matriarchal.
Khasi language is **Austro-Asiatic**.
Meghalaya ST share **86.1%**.

ncb419b569a6.s: The Onge, a Negrito PVTG, live on:
ncb419b569a6.x: The Onge are of Little Andaman; the Shompen are in Great Nicobar and the Sentinelese on North Sentinel Island.
xa: ⚠ **Onge** = Little Andaman; **Shompen** = Great Nicobar; **Sentinelese** = North Sentinel.
The **Shompen** first voted in **April 2024** (Lok Sabha, A&N seat).
Sentinelese: tribal reserve since **1956**; **3-nautical-mile** prohibited zone.
**Great Andamanese** live on **Strait Island**.

nfd63f1a94ce.s: The ghotul youth dormitory is associated with the:
nfd63f1a94ce.x: The ghotul belongs to the Gonds; the Bhil name comes from 'billu' (bow).
xa: Todas: **pukhor** embroidery (GI); PVTG.
Birhor and Chenchu = **forest hunters** (Vidyarthi and Rai).
Birhor is a **PVTG**.

nf4750540a38.s: The Changpa nomads of Ladakh have been recognised as a Scheduled Tribe since:
nf4750540a38.x: The Changpa of the Changthang plateau, who rear pashmina goats and yaks, have had ST status since 1989.
xa: Ladakh ST share **79.5%**.
Changpa are in the **Himalayan** zone with Gaddi, Gujjar, Bakarwal.
**Gaddi** = **Bharmour** (Chamba), HP.

n2dee5391a04.s: PMJVM is implemented by TRIFED and primarily promotes which of the following through Van Dhan Vikas Kendras?
n2dee5391a04.x: PMJVM is implemented by TRIFED and uses Van Dhan Vikas Kendras for Minor Forest Produce-related activities.
n2dee5391a04.tq: Identify the implementing agency and the scheme's functional objective together.
xs: **PMJVM** promotes **Minor Forest Produce** (MFP) through **Van Dhan Vikas Kendras** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is implemented by **TRIFED** and began in **2021-22**.
xa: **4,172 VDVKs** sanctioned.
Residential schooling is the job of **EMRS**, not PMJVM.
**DAJGUA** (**Sep 2024**) covers **17** ministries.

nindian-geography-7-1.s: The Pahadi Korba tribe is found in:
nindian-geography-7-1.x: The Pahadi Korba live in Jashpur; the Bharia are in Chhindwara and the Chenchu in the Nallamala.
n: The Bharia tribe is located in Chhindwara. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Bharia tribe is located in Madhya Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Pahadi Korba tribe is located in Jashpur. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Pahadi Korba tribe is located in Chhattisgarh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Chenchu tribe is located in Andhra Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Chenchu tribe is located in the Nallamala region. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Sentinelese tribe is located on North Sentinel Island. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Sentinelese tribe is located in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
xa: **Maria** are listed in **Chhindwara**, **Patalkot** (MP); other notes put them in **Bastar**.
Bharia were the first PVTG with **habitat rights** under FRA.
Chenchu are **forest hunters** in Vidyarthi and Rai's economic types.
**Muria** are in **Chhattisgarh** (ghotul youth dormitory).

nindian-geography-7-4.s: The Mikir (Karbi) tribe lives mainly in:
nindian-geography-7-4.x: The Mikir (Karbi) live in Assam, mainly in Karbi Anglong; the Dafla are in Arunachal Pradesh.
n: The Toda tribe is located in Tamil Nadu. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Toda tribe is located in the Nilgiri Hills. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Moplah tribe is located in Kerala. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Mikir tribe is located in Assam. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
The Dafla tribe is located in Arunachal Pradesh. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 21-24]
xa: Toda: **buffalo** herders; **pukhor** embroidery (GI).
**Lepcha** → **Sikkim**; **Lushai / Mizo** → **Mizoram**.
**Kuki** → predominantly **Manipur**.

n37eaa288f16.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission (1953) was set up under Article 340
The U.N. Dhebar Commission (1960-61) was the first Article 339 commission
The Dilip Singh Bhuria Commission (2002-04) was the second Article 339 commission
The Virginius Xaxa Committee (2013) was set up by the Planning Commission
n37eaa288f16.x: The Xaxa high-level committee was set up by the PMO, not the Planning Commission.
xa: Xaxa reported in **2014** on socio-economic, health and educational status.
**Bhuria Committee** (**1994-95**) → **PESA 1996**.
Dhebar → **PTG** category (**1973**).

n8476f01710d.s: The category of Primitive Tribal Groups (PTGs), later renamed Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), is associated with the recommendations of which commission?
n8476f01710d.x: The Dhebar Commission drew attention to the least-developed tribal groups, leading to the PTG category. The term PTG was later renamed PVTG in 2006.
n8476f01710d.tq: Identify the commission associated with the creation or renaming of a special category.
xs: The PTG category came from the **Dhebar Commission** — option **(2)** is correct.
Dhebar (**1960-61**) flagged the least-developed groups → **PTG** (**1973**) → renamed **PVTG** in **2006**.
**Lokur** (**1965**) framed the general ST criteria, not the PTG category.
xa: PVTG criteria: **pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, economic backwardness, declining/stagnant population**.
**Feb 2024**: **7** sub-tribes added as variants (Odisha **4**, AP **3**).

n6592e9d625d.s: Primitive Tribal Groups (PTGs) were renamed PVTGs in:
n6592e9d625d.x: 52 PTGs were declared in 1975, 23 added in 1993, the name changed to PVTGs in 2006, and seven variants added in February 2024.
xa: The PTG category itself was created in **1973**, based on the **Dhebar Commission** (**1960-61**).
Feb **2024** additions: Odisha **4**, AP **3** (**Bondo Porja, Khond Porja, Konda Savara**).
**Odisha (13)** has the most PVTGs, then **AP + Telangana (12)**.

na872eff9324.s: PM-JANMAN was launched in which month and year?
na872eff9324.tq: Distinguish the launch date from the dates of other tribal development initiatives.
xs: **PM-JANMAN** was launched in **November 2023** (**15 Nov 2023**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**September 2024** is **DAJGUA**'s launch.
xa: Outlay **Rs 24,104 cr** (Centre **15,336**); **75** PVTGs; **11** interventions.
Targets **4.90 lakh** houses and **8,000 km** roads; **2.26 lakh** houses sanctioned.

nf880ead3859.s: PM-JANMAN covers how many Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups?
nf880ead3859.x: PM-JANMAN covers 75 PVTGs with 11 interventions during 2023-24 to 2025-26.
xa: Outlay **Rs 24,104 cr** (Centre **15,336**).
Interventions include **4.90 lakh** houses and **8,000 km** roads.
Launched **15 Nov 2023**.

nf3e43fd0286.s: Which one of the following States has the largest number of notified Scheduled Tribes?
nf3e43fd0286.x: Odisha has the largest number of notified Scheduled Tribes among the States listed, with 62 groups in the cited data.
nf3e43fd0286.tq: Do not confuse the number of tribal communities with the total tribal population.
xs: **Odisha** has the largest number of notified STs — **62** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Madhya Pradesh** has the largest ST **population** (**153.17 lakh**), not the most notified tribes.
xa: ⚠ **Most STs** = **MP**; **highest share** = **Lakshadweep**; **most notified tribes** = **Odisha (62)**.
Odisha also has the most **PVTGs** (**13**).
India has **705** notified STs in **30** States/UTs.

n45cb12a91be.s: Which of the following States is NOT covered by the Sixth Schedule?
n45cb12a91be.x: The Sixth Schedule applies to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Odisha is among the Fifth Schedule States.
n45cb12a91be.tq: Separate the four Sixth Schedule States from the Fifth Schedule group.
xs: **Odisha** is not a Sixth Schedule State — option **(1)** is correct.
The Sixth Schedule (**Art. 244(2)**) covers **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**.
Odisha has **Fifth Schedule** Scheduled Areas.
xa: Sixth Schedule machinery: **Autonomous District and Regional Councils**.
Fifth Schedule: Governor's special powers; **Tribes Advisory Council**.
Fifth Schedule areas are called **Scheduled Areas**; Sixth Schedule areas **Tribal Areas**.

n56559a2d2ef.s: How many States are listed as having Fifth Schedule Scheduled Areas?
n56559a2d2ef.x: The ten States are Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan and Telangana.
n56559a2d2ef.tq: Count the members of the constitutional list.
xs: Scheduled Areas exist in **10** States — option **(3)** is correct.
They are **AP, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, HP, Jharkhand, MP, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, Telangana**.
xa: The Fifth Schedule applies to all States except **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**.
AP's Scheduled Areas = **16,267.63 sq km** (**10.15%** of AP) in **5** districts.
**Bihar** has **no Scheduled Areas** now.

n0df1cceba27.s: Under Article 342(2), a community can be included in or excluded from the notified ST list only by:
o: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
n0df1cceba27.x: Article 342(2) provides that only Parliament may alter the notified ST list by law; the lists are specific to each State or UT.
xa: Base list: Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, **1950**.
**Art. 366(25)** defines STs by reference to Art. 342.
J&K additions in **2024**: **Pahari ethnic group, Paddari tribe, Koli, Gadda Brahmin**.

ne23e43532c5.s: Under Article 366(25) of the Constitution, Scheduled Tribes are defined by reference to
ne23e43532c5.x: Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes by reference to the communities notified under Article 342.
ne23e43532c5.tq: Use an exact constitutional cross-reference with nearby article distractors.
xs: **Art. 366(25)** defines STs by reference to **Article 342** — option **(4)** is correct.
Under Art. 342 the **President** notifies STs for each State/UT **after consulting the Governor**.
xa: Only **Parliament** can change the list (**ST Order, 1950**).
**Art. 338A** = National Commission for STs.
Lists are **state-specific**.

n29de7accdb2.s: The proposed ST (Valley) tier in Assam was recommended by:
n29de7accdb2.x: A Group of Ministers proposed it (report, Nov 2025) for six communities including Tai Ahom and Tea Tribes; tribal bodies opposed it.
xa: Assam is a **Sixth Schedule** State with **Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**.
J&K additions in **2024**: Pahari, Paddari, Koli, Gadda Brahmin.

nc3fede53d6b.s: Which one of the following is NOT among the criteria used to identify Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)?
o: Residence in a Sixth Schedule area
nc3fede53d6b.x: The four PVTG criteria are pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, economic backwardness and a declining or stagnant population, so the first three options are criteria. Residence in a Sixth Schedule area is not a criterion; PVTGs are found across many States and in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
nc3fede53d6b.tq: PVTG = pre-agri tech + low literacy + economic backwardness + stagnant/declining population.
xs: **Residence in a Sixth Schedule area** is not a PVTG criterion — option **(4)** is correct.
The four criteria: **pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, economic backwardness, declining/stagnant population**.
xa: Origin: **Dhebar Commission** → PTG (**1973**) → PVTG (**2006**).
Total PVTGs: **75**.
Tribal Ministry wants a **separate PVTG count** in **Census 2027**.

nafa0e59b290.s: Santali was added to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution by which amendment, and in which script is it written?
nafa0e59b290.x: Santali entered the Eighth Schedule through the 92nd Amendment, 2003, and is written in Ol Chiki. The 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali; Warang Citi is the script of Ho, not Santali; the 96th Amendment (2011) changed Oriya to Odia.
xs: **Santali** was added by the **92nd Amendment, 2003** and is written in **Ol Chiki** — option **(2)** is correct.
Santali is an **Austro-Asiatic** language.
xa: Santhals live mainly in **Jharkhand**.
Other Austro-Asiatic: **Ho, Mundari, Khasi**.
**Adi Vaani** covers **Santali**.

n2179b3df8a4.s: The ceiling on land recognised under the Forest Rights Act, 2006 is:
n2179b3df8a4.x: The ceiling is 4 hectares; occupation must predate 13 December 2005.
xa: **Community forest rights** still reach only a fraction of the eligible.
**PESA 1996**: STs get **at least 50%** of seats; every chairperson must be an ST.

n54a0a5128d4.s: Among the 10 PESA States, which has only draft PESA rules?
n54a0a5128d4.x: Rules are framed in 9 of the 10 States; Odisha has only draft rules.
xa: PESA: STs get **at least 50%** seats; **every chairperson** an ST.
The **Bhuria Committee** recommended extending panchayats to Scheduled Areas → **PESA 1996**.
The **10** states: AP, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, HP, Jharkhand, MP, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, Telangana.

ne19db30fcf9.s: Which of the following correctly states the Scheduled Tribe population and share of Andhra Pradesh according to Census 2011 figures used by APSES?
ne19db30fcf9.x: The Scheduled Tribe population was 27.39 lakh, constituting 5.53% of Andhra Pradesh’s population. The figures 26.31 lakh and 5.3% occur in older material but are not the APSES figures used here.
ne19db30fcf9.tq: Use the paired population-and-share figure and reject the older alternative.
xs: AP's STs number **27.39 lakh** (**5.53%**) — option **(2)** is correct.
**26.31 lakh** / **5.3%** is the older figure before the **7 Polavaram mandals** moved to AP (**2014**).
**8.6%** is India's ST share; **84.69 lakh** / **17.08%** are AP's SCs.
xa: AP has **34** ST communities.
**12 PVTGs** (shared with Telangana) — second only to Odisha.
Scheduled Areas = **16,267.63 sq km** (**10.15%** of AP).

n747d510dc95.s: The Scheduled Areas of Andhra Pradesh form about ____ of the State's area.
n747d510dc95.x: They cover 16,267.63 sq km, 10.15% of AP's area, across five districts.
xa: Districts: **Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalli, Eluru**.
**3,512** tribal villages.
AP is a **Fifth Schedule** state with **34** ST communities.

n1adc67eda56.s: How many Scheduled Tribe communities does Andhra Pradesh have?
n1adc67eda56.x: AP has 34 ST communities and 12 PVTGs (shared with Telangana); it is a Fifth Schedule State.
xa: AP STs: **27.39 lakh** = **5.53%** (2011); older figure **26.31 lakh** before the Polavaram mandals moved.
AP Scheduled Areas: **16,267.63 sq km** (**10.15%**), **3,512** tribal villages.
**Chenchu** is AP's PVTG of the **Nallamala**.
AP tribal habitat: **Eastern Ghats** + **Nallamala** belt.

nfae55de9f56.s: The Lokur Committee was set up in:
nfae55de9f56.x: Lokur was 1965, the Bhuria Committee 1995, the Dilip Singh Bhuria Commission 2002 and the Xaxa Committee 2013–14.
xa: ⚠ Some notes date the Bhuria Committee **1991**.
**Xaxa Committee** was set up by the **PMO** and reported in **2014**.
**Dhebar Commission** = **1960-61**; **Kaka Kalelkar** = **1953**.

n413d6d211e1.s: Which one of the following was a recommendation associated with the Virginius Xaxa Committee?
o: Agro-based training institutions, labour-intensive processing, organic farming and eco-forestry
Extension of Panchayats to non-Scheduled urban areas
Creation of the category of Primitive Tribal Groups
Constitution of the first Tribes Advisory Council
n413d6d211e1.x: The Virginius Xaxa Committee, whose report concerned 2013–14, suggested measures including agro-based training institutions, labour-intensive processing, organic farming and eco-forestry.
n413d6d211e1.tq: Distinguish the livelihood-oriented recommendations from constitutional and identification mandates.
xs: The **Xaxa Committee** suggested **agro-based training institutions, labour-intensive processing, organic farming and eco-forestry** — option **(1)** is correct.
**PTGs** came from the **Dhebar Commission**; panchayat extension to Scheduled Areas came from the **Bhuria Committee**.
xa: Xaxa was a **High-Level Committee** set up by the **PMO** in **2013**, reporting in **2014**.
It examined the **socio-economic, health and educational status** of tribes.
APPSC-G2 **2025** asked its chair — **Virginius Xaxa**.

ncee3b9b7d77.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the criteria associated with the Lokur Committee for specifying Scheduled Tribes?
ncee3b9b7d77.x: The Lokur criteria include primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact with the community at large and backwardness. Advanced urbanisation is not one of them.
ncee3b9b7d77.tq: Find the outsider in a characteristic list.
xs: **Advanced urbanisation** is not a Lokur criterion — option **(3)** is correct.
The five criteria: **primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact** with the community at large, **backwardness**.
xa: Committee year **1965**; chair **B.N. Lokur**.
PVTG criteria differ: **pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, economic backwardness, declining/stagnant population**.
STs are **89.97%** rural.

n5bb80855a8b.s: Who chaired the High-Level Committee set up in 2013 to examine the socio-economic, health and educational status of tribal communities in India?
n5bb80855a8b.x: The 2013 High-Level Committee set up by the PMO was chaired by Virginius Xaxa and reported in 2014 (APPSC-G2 2025 key). Dilip Singh Bhuria headed the 1994-95 committee behind PESA and the 2002-04 commission; B.N. Lokur headed the 1965 committee on criteria for specifying STs; U.N. Dhebar headed the 1960-61 Article 339 commission.
xs: The **2013** High-Level Committee was chaired by **Virginius Xaxa** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-G2 **2025** key).
**Dilip Singh Bhuria** headed the **1994-95** committee (PESA) and the **2002-04** commission.
**B.N. Lokur** headed the **1965** ST-criteria committee; **U.N. Dhebar** the **1960-61** Art. 339 commission.
xa: Xaxa was set up by the **PMO** and reported in **2014**.
It suggested **organic farming** and **eco-forestry** for livelihoods.
**Kaka Kalelkar** (**1953**) was under **Art. 340**.

n3ad87126ddc.s: The Shompen, who voted for the first time in the April 2024 Lok Sabha election, inhabit:
n3ad87126ddc.x: The Shompen of Great Nicobar voted for the first time in April 2024 in the Andaman and Nicobar constituency; they are classified as Mongoloid.
xa: Shompen speak **Shompenese** (Austroasiatic); nomadic hunter-gatherers living on **pandanus**.
They allege pressure over the **Great Nicobar project**.
North Sentinel Island = **Sentinelese** (uncontacted).

n1bfe52a4c79.s: Which one of the following is the odd one out on the basis of its regional association?
n1bfe52a4c79.x: Gond, Baiga and Muria are associated with central or middle India, whereas Kadar is a southern tribe of the Anamalai Hills.
n1bfe52a4c79.tq: Identify the member belonging to a different geographical region.
xs: **Kadar** is the odd one out — option **(4)** is correct (CGPSC **2024**).
Kadar are **southern** forest foragers of the **Anamalai** hills.
**Baiga, Muria, Gond** are **central-Indian** tribes.
xa: **Kharia** is also central-Indian.
Central zone: **MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha**.
Southern zone: **Toda, Kota, Irula, Paniya, Kadar, Chenchu, Koya, Siddi**.

n564ff48c3a8.s: Niyam Raja and the Niyamgiri festival held in April are associated with the:
n564ff48c3a8.x: Niyam Raja and the Niyamgiri festival are associated with the Dongria Kondh.
n564ff48c3a8.tq: Match the religious-cultural term with the tribe.
xs: **Niyam Raja** and the **Niyamgiri festival** (April) belong to the **Dongria Kondh** — option **(2)** is correct.
They live in the **Niyamgiri Hills**, Odisha.
xa: Dongaria Kondh **stopped bauxite mining** (SC, **2013**); they are a **PVTG**.
**Marang Buru** = Santhal; **head-hunting** = Konyak Naga.
Odisha has the most PVTGs (**13**).

nindian-geography-9-5.s: The cattle-rearing Maasai pastoralists are found in:
o: Kenya, northern Tanzania and eastern Uganda
nindian-geography-9-5.x: The Maasai are cattle-rearing pastoralists of Kenya, northern Tanzania and eastern Uganda.
n: Maasai traditionally practice cattle rearing. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
Maasai are found in Kenya. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
Maasai are found in northern Tanzania. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
Maasai are found in eastern Uganda. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
xa: **Bakarwal** (J&K): **seasonal pastoralism**.
**Gaddi** (HP): **seasonal livestock herding** and migration.
**Bhotia**: **migratory pastoralism** in Uttarakhand.
**Changpa** (Ladakh): Tibetan nomads rearing **Pashmina** goats and yaks.

nindian-geography-9-11.s: The Bakarwal community of Jammu and Kashmir is traditionally associated with:
nindian-geography-9-11.x: The Bakarwal herd goats and sheep, moving between high summer pastures and winter plains - seasonal pastoralism.
n: Bakarwal traditionally practice seasonal pastoralism. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 29-32]
xa: **Gaddi** (Kangra, Chamba) also herd seasonally, near the **Dhauladhar Range**.
**Bhotia (Bhotiya)**: migratory pastoralism in Uttarakhand.
The **Toda** are the pastoralists in Vidyarthi and Rai's economic types.
J&K inclusion (**1991**): **Gujjars, Bakarwals, Gaddis, Sippis** added to the ST list.

n71f865d5a73.s: Of India's 6,40,867 villages in 2011, how many were inhabited?
n71f865d5a73.x: India had 6,40,867 villages, of which 5,97,608 (about 93.2%) were inhabited.
xa: Rural population (**2011**) ≈ **83.3 crore**.
PYQ: "About how many villages" → "None of these" (MPPSC **2010**); true figure ≈ **6.4 lakh**.

n969f3391b20.s: For the first time since Independence, during which decade did urban India add more people than rural India?
n969f3391b20.x: During 2001–2011, urban India added more people than rural India for the first time since Independence.
n969f3391b20.tq: Use the distinctive historical turning point and its associated decade.
xs: In **2001-11**, urban India for the **first time** since Independence added more people than rural India — option **(2)** is correct.
The rise of **census towns** made **reclassification** a major driver.
xa: Census towns rose **1,362 to 3,894**.
Rural population **2011** ≈ **83.3 crore**.

n051bca83762.s: How many census towns did India have in Census 2011?
n051bca83762.x: Census towns rose from 1,362 (2001) to 3,894 (2011); the 7,935 towns of 2011 comprised 4,041 statutory and 3,894 census towns.
xa: ⚠ A **2026** item gives census towns as **3,784**.

n48d3f777a9a.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh recorded the highest level of urbanisation in Census 2011?
n48d3f777a9a.x: Visakhapatnam was the most urbanised district at 47.45%, followed by Krishna (40.81%); Srikakulam was the lowest at 16.16%.
xa: Visakhapatnam's lead is about **31** points over Srikakulam.
More urbanised regions of India: **south and west**.
Low-urbanisation tracts include **Telangana** and the **flood-prone peninsular tracts**.

n61bdfcb70b4.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of urban population growth?
n61bdfcb70b4.x: Urban growth occurs through natural increase, rural-to-urban migration, reclassification of settlements and expansion of town boundaries to include villages. Decline in town boundaries is not a stated component.
n61bdfcb70b4.tq: Find the reversed or negative version of a recognised urban-growth component.
xs: **Decline in town boundaries** is not a component — option **(2)** is correct.
Components: **natural increase**, **rural-to-urban migration**, **reclassification**, and town boundaries **expanding** to take in villages.
xa: Natural increase differs little between rural and urban → **migration** explains most of the gap.
**Reclassification** was a major component in **2001-11**.

n3f1c7e8ec60.s: Which of the following combinations contains only pull factors of urbanisation?
o: Industrialisation, trade and commerce, better health and education
n3f1c7e8ec60.x: Industrialisation, trade and commerce, better health and education, and transport links attract people towards cities. The other combinations contain rural push factors.
n3f1c7e8ec60.tq: Classify each factor as an attraction to cities or a pressure from rural areas.
xs: **Industrialisation, trade and commerce, better health and education** are all **pull** factors — option **(1)** is correct.
**Failed monsoon, poverty, landlessness, rural unemployment** are **push** factors.
xa: **Transport links** are also a pull factor.
Migration explains most of the rural-urban growth gap.
**Rakesh Mohan**: metropolitanisation, commercialisation, rural (subsistence) urbanisation.

n5750c73de7c.s: Which of the following is one of the three processes of urbanisation identified by Rakesh Mohan?
n5750c73de7c.x: Rakesh Mohan identified metropolitanisation, commercialisation and rural or subsistence urbanisation.
xa: Pull factors: **industrialisation**, trade, health, education, transport.
Push factors: **failed monsoon**, poverty, landlessness.
Reclassification was major in **2001-11**.

n6a3d7c0553b.s: Which north-eastern State is an exception to the region's generally low level of urbanisation?
n6a3d7c0553b.x: Mizoram is the north-eastern exception, being relatively more urbanised than the regional pattern.
xa: More urbanised: **Goa, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Maharashtra, Gujarat**.
**HP** is also less urbanised.
**NE tribal hills** are a low-urbanisation tract.

ne01289c9983.s: Which of the following groups contains only States identified as relatively more urbanised in India?
o: Goa, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Maharashtra and Gujarat
Bihar, Assam, Odisha, Himachal Pradesh and Rajasthan
Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Assam, Odisha and Sikkim
Assam, Mizoram, Bihar, Odisha and Himachal Pradesh
ne01289c9983.x: The southern and western group of relatively more urbanised States includes Goa, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Maharashtra and Gujarat.
ne01289c9983.tq: Use regional grouping to eliminate sets containing States identified as less urbanised.
xs: **Goa, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Maharashtra, Gujarat** are the more urbanised states — option **(1)** is correct.
**Bihar, Assam, Odisha, HP** are less urbanised.
xa: More urbanised regions = **south and west**; NE exception **Mizoram**.
Low tracts: **middle/lower Ganga plains**, **Telangana**, **western Rajasthan**.
AP highest district: **Visakhapatnam 47.45%**.

n3d43159b433.s: Which of the following correctly represents the cephalic index?
o: Maximum length divided by maximum breadth, multiplied by 100
Maximum breadth divided by maximum length, multiplied by 100
Stature divided by head length, multiplied by 100
Nasal breadth divided by nasal length, multiplied by 100
n3d43159b433.x: Cephalic index is calculated as (maximum breadth / maximum length) × 100.
n3d43159b433.tq: Recall the exact formula rather than the reversed ratio.
xs: **Cephalic index = (maximum breadth / maximum length) x 100** — option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) inverts the ratio; stature and nasal measures are separate indices.
xa: **Brachycephalic** (round) = living head CI **82 and above**.
**Dolichocephalic** (long) = living head CI **76.99** and below.
**S.S. Sarkar** built his **six ethnic elements** on the cephalic index.

n6c50dfedb7d.s: A person has a nasal index of 86. Under the stated classification, this person would belong to which nasal category?
n6c50dfedb7d.x: Platyrrhine refers to a broad nose with a nasal index of 85 or above. Leptorrhine is below 70 and mesorrhine is 70–84.9.
n6c50dfedb7d.tq: Apply the numerical boundary to the category instead of recalling labels alone.
xs: A nasal index of **86** is **Platyrrhine** (broad nose; **85 and above**) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Mesorrhine** = **70-84.9**; **Leptorrhine** = under **70**.
**Dolichocephalic** is a head-shape term, not a nasal one.
xa: **Risley** ranked castes mainly by the **nasal index**.
Risley's dictum: caste status varies **inversely** with nasal index.
⚠ **Risley** = nasal index; **Sarkar** = cephalic index; **Haddon** = hair form.

n5390ef01deb.s: The cephalic index of a living person is 83. Under the standard classification, this head type is:
n5390ef01deb.x: For a living head, a cephalic index of 82 and above is brachycephalic (round-headed), 77-81.99 is mesocephalic and 76.99 and below is dolichocephalic (long-headed), so 83 is brachycephalic. Platyrrhine is a nasal-index class (85 and above), not a head type.
n5390ef01deb.tq: Living head CI: ≤76.99 dolicho, 77-81.99 meso, ≥82 brachy.
xs: A living CI of **83** is **Brachycephalic** (round; **82 and above**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Mesocephalic** = **77-81.99**; **Dolichocephalic** = **76.99** and below.
**Platyrrhine** is a nasal category.
xa: Dry skull: brachycephalic = **80 and above**.
Guha's **Western Brachycephals**: Alpinoid, Dinaric, Armenoid.
CI = (maximum breadth / maximum length) x **100**.

n32ed3e4defe.s: With reference to Risley’s classification, the term ‘Dravidian’ is associated with:
o: The Himalayan and north-eastern hills only
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands only
North-west India and the Punjab only
n32ed3e4defe.x: Risley used ‘Dravidian’ for South India and Chota Nagpur. In linguistic usage, however, Dravidian properly denotes a language family.
n32ed3e4defe.tq: Distinguish Risley’s geographical racial label from the later linguistic meaning of Dravidian.
xs: Risley's **Dravidian** type = **South India and Chota Nagpur** (and central India) — option **(1)** is correct.
BPSC **2016** key: Dravidian races confined to **South India**.
Himalaya and NE = Risley's **Mongoloid**; NW = **Turko-Iranian**/**Indo-Aryan**.
xa: Dravidian traits: **long head, broad nose, dark skin**; e.g. **Paniyan, Santals**.
'Dravidian' properly names a **language family**.
India's two main ethno-linguistic groups = **Indo-Aryan** + **Dravidian**.

ndbfd720133e.s: Which one of the following Risley racial types is associated with Baluchistan and the North-West Frontier Province?
ndbfd720133e.x: The Turko-Iranian type was associated with Baluchistan and the North-West Frontier region.
ndbfd720133e.tq: Match the regional distribution with the correct Risley type.
xs: **Turko-Iranian** = **Baluchistan** and **NWFP** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Indo-Aryan** = Punjab, Rajasthan, Kashmir; **Aryo-Dravidian** = UP, Bihar; **Mongolo-Dravidian** = Bengal, Odisha.
xa: **Scytho-Dravidian** = Maharashtra, Saurashtra, Coorg.
**Mongoloid** = Himalaya, Assam and NE.
**Dravidian** = South India, Chota Nagpur, central India.

nda902a4e05a.s: Under Risley's classification, Punjab, Rajasthan and Kashmir were associated with which type?
nda902a4e05a.x: Risley linked Punjab, Rajasthan and Kashmir to the Indo-Aryan type; Scytho-Dravidian was linked to western India (Maharashtra, Saurashtra, Coorg).
xa: **Turko-Iranian** = Baluchistan, NWFP.
**Aryo-Dravidian** = **UP, Bihar**.
Risley gave **7** types.

naab781ce5ba.s: Which racial group is associated with straight, coarse hair described as leiotrichi?
naab781ce5ba.x: Straight, coarse hair, termed leiotrichi, is associated with the Mongoloid group. Woolly or frizzy hair, termed ulotrichi, is associated with the Negroid group.
naab781ce5ba.tq: Distinguish the similar hair classifications by their exact technical terms.
xs: **Leiotrichi** (straight, coarse hair) is **Mongoloid** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Cymotrichi** (straight-wavy) = **Caucasoid**; **ulotrichi** (woolly) = **Negroid**.
xa: ⚠ **leio – cymo – ulo** = **straight – wavy – woolly**.
**Haddon (1924)** used **hair form** as the main basis for world populations.
Mongoloids have **sparse hair**.

ne4cc48221d6.s: The Parsis have been placed under which racial type and sub-type respectively?
ne4cc48221d6.x: The Parsis are associated with the Western Brachycephal group and are identified with the Armenoid sub-type.
ne4cc48221d6.tq: Use the community-subtype pairing to avoid confusing broad racial groups with their sub-types.
xs: **Parsis** = **Western Brachycephal**, **Armenoid** sub-type — option **(3)** is correct.
Western Brachycephal sub-types: **Alpinoid, Dinaric, Armenoid**.
xa: Western Brachycephals are broad-headed: **Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka (Coorg), Bengal-Odisha**.
**Tibeto-Mongoloid** = Tibetans of Sikkim.
**Andamanese** = Negrito.

n509b29bec87.s: Palaeo-Mediterranean, Mediterranean and Oriental are sub-types of which one of Guha's racial groups?
n509b29bec87.x: The Mediterranean group was divided into Palaeo-Mediterranean, Mediterranean and Oriental. The Oriental sub-type was associated with Punjab and Rajasthan.
n509b29bec87.tq: Match the sub-type cluster with its parent group.
xs: **Palaeo-Mediterranean, Mediterranean, Oriental** are sub-types of Guha's **Mediterranean** group — option **(2)** is correct.
Western Brachycephals = **Alpinoid, Dinaric, Armenoid**.
xa: Palaeo-Mediterranean = **south** (Dravidian-speaking); Mediterranean = **north**; Oriental = **Punjab, Rajasthan**.
AP's plains population is mainly **Mediterranean (Dravidian-speaking)**.
Mongoloid sub-types: **Palaeo-Mongoloid, Tibeto-Mongoloid**.

n293d332f7b5.s: The racial element generally associated with the tribal groups of north-eastern India is:
n293d332f7b5.x: The tribal groups of the north-eastern hills and forests are generally associated with the Mongoloid racial element.
n293d332f7b5.tq: Apply the region-to-racial-element association for the north-eastern hills.
xs: NE tribes are **Mongoloid** — option **(2)** is correct (UPPSC **2003** key).
Mongoloids live in the **hilly, forested NE**.
xa: Mongoloid traits: **yellowish** skin, **oblique eyes**, **high cheekbones**.
Risley's **Mongoloid** = Himalaya, Assam and NE.
**Central India** = Proto-Australoid (Santhal).

n4ec32dde349.s: The tribal population of the Andaman Islands is associated with which racial stock?
n4ec32dde349.x: The Andaman tribes are Negrito, regarded as a sub-race of the Negroid group; the Shompen of Nicobar are Mongoloid.
xa: Negrito: **Jarawa, Onge, Great Andamanese, Sentinelese**.
**Griffith Taylor**: primitive races pushed to the periphery like the **Andaman Islands**.
Negrito traces in the south: **Kadar, Irula**.

n50b098d0fc9.s: Which one of the following tribes is regarded as the standard example of the Proto-Australoid racial element in Central India?
n50b098d0fc9.x: The Santhal is the standard example of a Central Indian tribe associated with the Proto-Australoid racial element.
n50b098d0fc9.tq: Identify the representative tribe linked with the central Indian racial element.
xs: **Santhal** is the standard **Proto-Australoid** example — option **(3)** is correct (UPPSC **2002** key).
**Jarawa** = Negrito; **Shompen** = Mongoloid; **Paniyan** = Risley's "Dravidian".
xa: Other Proto-Australoids: **Munda, Oraon, Ho, Bhil, Chenchu**.
Proto-Australoid traits: **long head, depressed nasal root, wavy hair**.
Risley called Santals **Dravidian**.

n866e0cd469c.s: The Chenchus of the Nallamala region are generally classified under which racial group?
n866e0cd469c.x: The Chenchus of the Nallamala region are classified as Proto-Australoid.
n866e0cd469c.tq: Use the tribe’s regional location and standard classification together.
xs: The **Chenchus** of the **Nallamala** are **Proto-Australoid** — option **(2)** is correct.
Most central and south Indian tribes, incl. AP's, are **Proto-Australoid**.
xa: AP plains population = **Mediterranean (Dravidian-speaking)**.
Negrito examples (**Kadar, Irula**) are in southern hills **beyond AP**.

n5a5037f0e3d.s: The plains population of Andhra Pradesh is mainly associated with which racial element?
n5a5037f0e3d.x: AP's plains population is mainly Mediterranean and predominantly Dravidian-speaking.
xa: Palaeo-Mediterranean covers the **Dravidian-speaking south** and much of the peninsula.
Negrito examples (**Kadar, Irula**) lie beyond AP.
AP ST sex ratio **1009**.

n12cd6ee6401.s: How many racial types did Risley's classification of the Indian population have?
n12cd6ee6401.x: Risley gave seven types; Guha gave six main groups (with nine sub-types).
xa: Guha used **1931** Census data; Risley the **1901** Census.
Risley's types include **Turko-Iranian, Indo-Aryan, Scytho-Dravidian, Aryo-Dravidian, Mongolo-Dravidian, Mongoloid, Dravidian**.
Guha's is the **most widely cited** classification.

nworld-geography-27-1.s: The Caucasoid racial group is mainly distributed across which of the following regions?
o: East Asia, Southeast Asia, Central Asia, and Arctic regions
Most populations of West, Central and Southern Africa
Australia, Australian Melanesia and Sub-Saharan Africa
Europe, North Africa, Middle East, and parts of Central and South Asia
nworld-geography-27-1.x: Caucasoids are spread across Europe, North Africa, the Middle East and parts of Central and South Asia.
nworld-geography-27-1.tq: Recall the region of each racial group.
n: Caucasoids are distributed in Europe. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Caucasoids are distributed in North Africa. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Caucasoids are distributed in the Middle East. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Caucasoids are distributed in parts of Central Asia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Caucasoids are distributed in parts of South Asia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids are distributed in East Asia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids are distributed in Southeast Asia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids are distributed in Central Asia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids are found in the Arctic. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negroids are distributed among most populations of West Africa. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negroids are distributed among most populations of Central Africa. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negroids are distributed among most populations of Southern Africa. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negroids are associated with Sub-Saharan Africa. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Australoids are distributed in Australia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Australoids are distributed in Australian Melanesia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
xs: Caucasoids are spread across **Europe, North Africa, the Middle East, and parts of Central and South Asia** — option **(4)**.
**East Asia, Southeast Asia, Central Asia and the Arctic** is the **Mongoloid** range.
**West, Central and Southern Africa** is the **Negroid** range; **Australia** and **Australian Melanesia** are **Australoid**.
xa: Caucasoid traits: **light to olive skin**, **straight or wavy hair**, **narrow noses**, medium to tall stature.
Caucasoids include **Europeans, Arabs, Persians, many North Indians**.
Caucasoid hair is **cymotrichi** (straight-wavy); blood group **more A than B**.

nworld-geography-27-5.s: Chinese, Japanese, Koreans, Mongols and American Indians are associated with which racial group?
nworld-geography-27-5.x: These peoples are associated with the Mongoloid group; Europeans, Arabs, Persians and many North Indians are Caucasoid.
n: Europeans are included among Caucasoids. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Arabs are included among Caucasoids. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Persians are included among Caucasoids. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Many North Indians are included among Caucasoids. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Chinese are included among Mongoloids. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Japanese are included among Mongoloids. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Koreans are included among Mongoloids. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongols are included among Mongoloids. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
American Indians are included among Mongoloids. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Proto-Australoids are found among many tribal groups of Central India. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Proto-Australoids are found among many tribal groups of South India. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Munda are an example of Proto-Australoid tribal groups. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Santhal are an example of Proto-Australoid tribal groups. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Bhil are an example of Proto-Australoid tribal groups. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids include Native Americans. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Australoids are associated with some Indian tribes. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Proto-Australoids occur in India. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
xa: **Proto-Australoids** occur in **India**; **Santhal** is the standard example.
AP's **Chenchus** (Nallamala) are **Proto-Australoid**.
The **Mongoloids** of India live in the hilly, forested **north-east**.

nc46a4dcfcf1.s: H.H. Risley was the Census Commissioner for which census and wrote which book?
o: Census of 1931; The Races of India
Census of 1901; The People of India
Census of 1881; The Tribes of India
nc46a4dcfcf1.x: H.H. Risley was the Census Commissioner for 1901 and wrote The People of India, published in 1908.
nc46a4dcfcf1.tq: Link the official position, census year and book title in one recall unit.
xs: **H.H. Risley** was Census Commissioner for **1901** and wrote **The People of India** (**1908**) — option **(3)** is correct.
He organised the **1901 ethnographic survey** and gave **7** racial types.
xa: ⚠ **People of India** project (**1985**) = **K.S. Singh**.
⚠ **Hutton** and **Guha** = **1931** Census.
Risley = exponent of the **racial theory of caste**.

n8914a56ca39.s: H.H. Risley is particularly associated with which one of the following ideas?
n8914a56ca39.x: Risley was the exponent of the racial theory of caste, which treats caste as a by-product of racial difference.
n8914a56ca39.tq: Identify the scholar by his characteristic theory.
xs: **Risley** is linked with the **racial theory of caste** — option **(3)** is correct.
He saw caste as a **by-product of racial difference**.
xa: Dictum: caste status varies **inversely** with its **nasal index**.
Now rejected as **colonial race science**.
Risley gave **7** types; Guha **6** groups.

n9f99ac65cde.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about scholars of racial classification in India?
o: S.S. Sarkar used the cephalic index
Haddon classified populations mainly on the basis of the cephalic index
The nasal index was Risley's measure
J.H. Hutton (Census Commissioner, 1931) held that India was peopled by successive waves of migration
n9f99ac65cde.x: Haddon classified populations by hair form (leiotrichi, cymotrichi, ulotrichi), not the cephalic index.
xa: ⚠ **Risley** = nasal index; **Sarkar** = cephalic index; **Haddon** = hair form.
⚠ **Risley** = **1901 Census**; **Hutton** and **Guha** = **1931 Census**.
**Eickstedt** (1930s): four groups — Weddid, Melanid, Indid, Mongolid.
**Griffith Taylor**: migration-zone theory — primitive races pushed to the periphery.

n95b7e5b52a6.s: B.S. Guha's racial classification of the Indian population was based on the data of which Census?
n95b7e5b52a6.x: Guha's classification, the most widely cited, was based on 1931 Census data and gave 6 main racial groups with 9 sub-types.
xa: Guha was the **first Director** of **AnSI**.
⚠ Only Guha lists **Negrito** and **Proto-Australoid** separately.
Groups: Negrito, Proto-Australoid, Mongoloid, Mediterranean, Western Brachycephals, Nordic.

n13d59f6d4f4.s: In which year did India ratify the ICERD?
n13d59f6d4f4.x: India ratified ICERD in 1968; the UN CERD recently reviewed India for the first time since 2007.
xa: SC asked the Centre to consider treating **racial slurs** against North-Easterners as a hate crime.
Risley's **racial theory of caste** is rejected.
Violence against NE citizens shows racial prejudice persists.

n867ac84b4df.s: The racial type described by a long head, depressed nasal root and wavy hair is:
n867ac84b4df.x: The Proto-Australoid type is described by a long head, depressed nasal root and wavy hair.
n867ac84b4df.tq: Identify the classification from its distinguishing physical traits.
xs: A **long head**, **depressed nasal root** and **wavy hair** mark the **Proto-Australoid** — option **(4)** is correct.
Proto-Australoids also have **dark skin**, a **broad flat nose** and short-to-medium stature.
**Negrito** have **woolly/frizzy** hair; **Nordic** are tall and fair; **Western Brachycephals** are broad-headed.
xa: Guha's Proto-Australoids: **Santhal, Munda, Oraon, Ho, Bhil, Chenchu** (central and southern India).
**Santhal** = standard central-India example (UPPSC **2002** key).
AP's **Chenchus** (Nallamala) = Proto-Australoid.

n33d637fe268.s: The description ‘yellow complexion, oblique eyes, high cheek bones, sparse hair and medium height’ refers to which racial type?
n33d637fe268.x: Yellow complexion, oblique eyes, high cheek bones, sparse hair and medium height are characteristic descriptions associated with the Mongoloid type.
n33d637fe268.tq: Discriminate between racial types by their distinctive physical descriptions.
xs: **Yellowish complexion, oblique eyes, high cheekbones, sparse hair, medium height** describe the **Mongoloid** — option **(3)** is correct (UPSC **1997** key).
Mongoloids also have a **broad head** and **flat face**.
**Negrito** have dark skin and woolly hair; **Nordic** are tall and fair.
xa: Mongoloid eye: **medial epicanthic fold**; hair **leiotrichi** (straight, coarse); blood group **high B**.
**North-east** tribes = Mongoloid (UPPSC **2003** key).
**Shompen** of Great Nicobar are Mongoloid.

nd1052f3baea.s: A high nasal bridge and a narrow nose are characteristic of which racial group?
nd1052f3baea.x: Caucasoids have a high bridge and narrow nose; Mongoloids a low-to-medium bridge; Negroids a low bridge and broad nose.
xa: Skin: Caucasoid pale reddish-white to olive brown; Mongoloid **saffron to yellow-brown**; Negroid brown to brown-black.
⚠ **leio – cymo – ulo** = **straight – wavy – woolly**.

n47b04d3b507.s: The older racial schemes of India have been criticised primarily because they relied heavily on
o: visible physical traits and colonial ethnography
n47b04d3b507.x: Older schemes relied on visible traits and colonial ethnography. Risley's race-caste theory is now rejected.
n47b04d3b507.tq: Identify the stated basis of the criticised classification rather than its later scientific alternative.
xs: Old racial schemes rested on **visible physical traits** and **colonial ethnography** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Risley**'s race-caste theory, built on the **nasal index**, is rejected.
xa: Modern science **rejects ranking by race**.
Anthropometric race typologies (Risley) are **discredited**.
All humans share **over 99%** of genetic material.

nworld-geography-27-2.s: Which of the following descriptions of racial groups is INCORRECT?
o: Mongoloids – light skin, wavy hair, narrow noses, tall stature
Caucasoids – light to olive skin, straight or wavy hair, narrow noses
Mongoloids – straight black hair, epicanthic folds, broad faces
Negroids – dark skin, woolly hair, broad noses, thick lips
nworld-geography-27-2.x: Option 3 describes Caucasoid traits; Mongoloids have straight black hair and epicanthic folds.
n: Caucasoids have light to olive skin. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Caucasoids have straight or wavy hair. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Caucasoids have narrow noses. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids have yellowish to brown skin. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids have straight black hair. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids have an epicanthic fold. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Mongoloids have broad faces. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negroids have dark brown to black skin. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negroids have woolly or curly hair. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negroids have broad noses. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
Negroids have thick lips. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 44-45]
