AP signed an **MoU with UN-Habitat** for a **Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs** in Amaravati.
**DDA (1957)** was India's **first UDA**.

na27198c1bc0.s: The first Urban Development Authority (UDA) set up in India was in:
na27198c1bc0.x: The Delhi Development Authority (Delhi Development Act, 1957) was India's first UDA; APPSC 2008 dated it 1964, but the answer was still Delhi. Mumbai's MMRDA (1975), Kolkata's KMDA (1970) and Chennai's CMDA (1974) came later.
xs: The **first UDA** was in **Delhi** — the **Delhi Development Authority** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was set up under the **Delhi Development Act, 1957**.
⚠ **APPSC 2008** dated it **1964**, but the answer was still **Delhi**.
xa: DDA prepares **MPD-2021**.
⚠ **Madras** (**1688**) = first **municipal corporation** — don't confuse with first UDA.
AP's capital authority is **APCRDA** (Amaravati).

nbe3f9c29a98.s: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 added which Schedule to the Constitution?
nbe3f9c29a98.x: It inserted Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule (18 functions for urban local bodies) and came into force on 1 June 1993.
xa: Functions include **urban planning**, **slum improvement**, **urban forestry**, **poverty alleviation**.
**Art. 243P**: metropolitan area = **10 lakh** or more.
**Art. 243ZE**: **Metropolitan Planning Committee**.

n1258e0e1110.s: The 100 cities of the Smart Cities Mission were selected in how many rounds?
n1258e0e1110.x: The 100 cities were chosen in four rounds (Jan 2016-Jun 2018); the Mission was launched in 2015 as a CSS, and Visakhapatnam is one of them.
xa: Central support: **₹48,000 crore**.
**7,636 of 8,063 projects (95%)** were done as on 11.07.2025.
**AMRUT** and **HRIDAY** were also launched in **2015**.

n231ed9a2c8b.s: Which one of the following is NOT an urban-rejuvenation programme?
n231ed9a2c8b.x: The SPM Rurban Mission is concerned with rural clusters showing urban traits and is not an urban-rejuvenation programme.
n231ed9a2c8b.tq: Find the one programme whose target area is rural rather than urban.
xs: **SPM Rurban Mission** is **not** an urban-rejuvenation programme — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC G1 2017 PYQ).
It is for **rural clusters showing urban traits**, under the **Ministry of Rural Development**.
**Smart Cities**, **AMRUT** and **HRIDAY** are urban schemes.
xa: Rurban was launched in **2016**.
**Smart Cities**, **AMRUT** and **HRIDAY** date from **2015**.
**AMRUT** covers **HRIDAY** cities.

n2d4d98910c5.s: In India's urbanisation data, the figure 31.80% denotes:
n2d4d98910c5.x: 31.80% is the 2001-11 decadal growth of urban population (286 to 377.1 million); 31.16% is the 2011 urban share.
xa: Rural share in 2011: **68.84%** (833.1 million).
Urban increase **91.0 million** > rural **90.4 million** — a first since Independence.

nf459c214beb.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a cause of urbanisation in India?
o: Pressure of population on rural land
nf459c214beb.x: Growth of industry and trade, pressure on rural land, low farm productivity, services and transport are identified causes. The complete disappearance of transport services is not a cause stated in this context.
nf459c214beb.tq: Find the extreme reversal of a recognised development factor.
xs: **Complete disappearance of transport services** is not a cause — so option **(3)** is correct.
Causes (APPSC 2008, "all of the above"): **industry and trade**, **pressure on rural land**, **low farm productivity**, **services and transport**.
xa: Push factors: **monsoon failure**, **rural unemployment**.
Pull factors: **jobs**, **health and education**, **transport links**.
**Industrialisation** creates urban jobs.

n0572058bd65.s: According to Census 2011, approximately how many people were counted as living in slums in India?
n0572058bd65.x: Census 2011 counted approximately 6.54 crore people living in slums.
n0572058bd65.tq: Recall the exact census figure and eliminate options that alter the leading digit.
xs: Census 2011 counted **6.54 crore** people in slums — so option **(3)** is correct.
Slums are the first listed **problem of urbanisation**.
xa: Other problems: **housing shortage**, **solid waste**, **water and sewerage**, **traffic congestion**, **pollution**, **urban floods**.
**World Cities Report 2026**: **1.1 billion** people live in slums or informal settlements worldwide.
Migration brings **slums**, **"dual city"** and **ghettoisation**.

n95f821b745c.s: Under the 16th Finance Commission (2026-31), grants for urban local bodies amount to about ______, and the urban share of local-body grants rises from ______.
n95f821b745c.x: The 16th FC gives Rs 3.6 lakh crore to ULBs and raises the urban share from 36% to 45%. Rs 1 lakh crore is the Urban Challenge Fund; the third option reverses the share change; Rs 2.3 lakh crore is the PMAY-U 2.0 aid figure.
n95f821b745c.tq: 16th FC: Rs 3.6 lakh cr for ULBs, urban share 36 -> 45%.
xs: **₹3.6 lakh cr** for ULBs; urban share **36% → 45%** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option 3 reverses the share change.
**₹1 lakh crore** is the **Urban Challenge Fund**; **₹2.30 lakh cr** is **PMAY-U 2.0** aid.
xa: The **16th Finance Commission** covers **2026-31**.
ES: cities are **"administered, not governed"**.
**Municipal bonds** get a **₹100 cr** incentive for single issues above **₹1,000 cr**.

ne65ae2e3bfb.s: Which of the following criticisms has been made regarding the Census definition of urbanisation in India?
o: It counts all peri-urban areas as urban by default.
It uses only satellite data for measuring urbanisation.
It excludes all statutory towns from urban statistics.
It may make India's urbanisation appear slower than it is.
ne65ae2e3bfb.x: India's urbanisation appears slow under the Census definition because peri-urban areas may not be adequately captured.
ne65ae2e3bfb.tq: Identify the consequence of an official definition rather than confusing it with an alternative method.
xs: The **Census definition** makes urbanisation **look slow** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It does not count peri-urban areas by default; the **UN "Degree of Urbanisation"** method would.
xa: **EAC-PM** satellite data: as high as **63% in 2015**.
**Janaagraha's ASICS 2023**: Census **undercounts** urbanisation.
**World Bank (2010)**: **55.3%** in "urban-like" areas.

n3074e87ea7d.s: Cities occupy approximately what share of India's land and produce approximately what share of its GDP?
n3074e87ea7d.x: Cities occupy about 3% of India's land but produce about 60% of its GDP.
n3074e87ea7d.tq: Pair the small land share with the much larger economic contribution.
xs: Cities cover **3%** of land and produce about **60% of GDP** — so option **(3)** is correct.
ES 2025-26 calls cities **"critical economic infrastructure"**.
xa: Census 2011 urban share: **31.16%**.
Urban population projected at about **60 crore by 2031**.
Migration **drives the cities' share of GDP**.

n250af779719.s: What proportion of the members of a Metropolitan Planning Committee are elected by and from among the elected members of municipalities and chairpersons of panchayats in the metropolitan area?
n250af779719.x: Two-thirds of the members of a Metropolitan Planning Committee are elected by the elected municipal members and panchayat chairpersons of the area.
n250af779719.tq: Recall the constitutional proportion rather than confusing it with one-half or one-third.
xs: **Two-thirds** of MPC members are elected — so option **(3)** is correct.
They are elected by **elected municipal members** and **panchayat chairpersons** of the area (**Art. 243ZE**).
xa: An MPC is set up for every **metropolitan area** (**10 lakh+**).
**Art. 243P** defines a metropolitan area.
Part IXA runs from **Art. 243P to 243ZG**.

na69987dedab.s: A chain of merged metropolitan areas is known as a:
na69987dedab.x: A megalopolis is a chain of merged metropolitan areas; a conurbation is a continuous urban area formed by merging towns.
xa: ⚠ **Gottmann** = megalopolis; **Geddes** = conurbation; **Jefferson** = primate city.
**Umland** is a **German term** for a town's **hinterland** (UPPSC 2017).
**Megacity** = **10 million+** (1 crore+) people.

ncaaee3aa7a9.s: A city with a population of 10 million or more is generally classified as a:
ncaaee3aa7a9.x: A megacity has a population of 10 million or more, equivalent to one crore or more. A million-plus city has a lower threshold of 10 lakh or more.
ncaaee3aa7a9.tq: Discriminate between the 10-million megacity threshold and the 1-million-plus-city threshold.
xs: A city of **10 million or more** is a **Megacity** — so option **(2)** is correct.
That equals **1 crore+** people.
A **million-plus / metropolitan** city has only **10 lakh** or more.
xa: India's 2011 megacities: **Greater Mumbai**, **Delhi**, **Kolkata**.
India's urban population is projected at **951 million by 2050**.
A **primate city** is several times larger than the next city.

n8074c93f0e9.s: Jakarta replaced Tokyo as the world's most populous city in WUP 2025 mainly because of:
o: a change in Japan's census year
the merger of Jakarta with neighbouring provinces
n8074c93f0e9.x: The change is attributed to the new city-definition method adopted in World Urbanisation Prospects 2025, not to a demographic collapse of Tokyo.
xa: Earlier lists had **Tokyo** as the largest city (**APPSC 2018** key).
The **largest city of Asia** = largest of the world under the current list (**Jakarta**; formerly Tokyo).
Cities hold **45%** of the world's **8.2 billion** people.

n2b83abc597b.s: According to the World Urbanization Prospects 2025, which is the world's most populous city?
n2b83abc597b.x: The order is Jakarta, Dhaka, Tokyo and New Delhi.
xa: The change came from a **new city-definition method**.
⚠ Earlier lists: **Tokyo 1st**, **Delhi 2nd**, **Mumbai 7th**, **Kolkata 10th**.
**WUP 2025** is published by **UN DESA**.

n9ef28cf91b4.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, the growth of 16 major Indian cities during 2000-2020 has been:
o: vertical, with the core growing faster than the periphery
horizontal, with the periphery growing faster than the core
horizontal, with the core growing faster than the periphery
vertical, with the periphery growing faster than the core
n9ef28cf91b4.x: The periphery grew faster than the core and expansion was predominantly horizontal; the administrative city no longer matches the economic metropolitan region.
xa: So the ES argues for a **unified metropolitan authority**.
ES 2025-26 Ch. 15: cities = **"critical economic infrastructure"**.
ES favours **integrating informality** and **reforming land markets**.

ndd38413fa40.s: The Chennai Metropolitan Area is planned by:
ndd38413fa40.x: Chennai is planned by CMDA (1974); KMDA (1970) is Kolkata's, VMRDA plans Visakhapatnam and APCRDA plans Amaravati.
xa: **MMRDA (1975)** plans the Mumbai Metropolitan Region.
An AP delegation studied **MMRDA, CIDCO** and the **Slum Rehabilitation Authority** (Jan 2026).
**DDA (1957)** = first UDA.

n483d578e8ed.s: Which of the following States is NOT a participating unit of the National Capital Region?
n483d578e8ed.x: The NCR comprises NCT of Delhi and parts of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan; Punjab is not part of it.
xa: Haryana towns: **Rohtak, Karnal**, Panipat, Sonipat, Gurugram, Faridabad.
UP towns: **Khurja**, Meerut, Ghaziabad, Noida; Rajasthan: **Alwar**.
**NCR Planning Board** set up under the **NCRPB Act, 1985**.

n381e12143b2.s: The National Capital Region Planning Board was established under which Act?
n381e12143b2.x: The NCR Planning Board was set up under the NCRPB Act of 1985.
n381e12143b2.tq: Test the statutory-basis trap by separating the NCRPB Act from other urban-planning laws.
xs: The **NCR Planning Board** was set up under the **NCRPB Act, 1985** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Delhi Development Act, 1957** created the **DDA**, not the NCRPB.
xa: NCRPB approved four greenfield **"Namo Cities"** (Jun 2026).
**PARIVARTAN**: **₹9,585 crore** clean-mobility scheme to replace about **2.07 lakh** BS-IV or older trucks and buses.
NCR = **NCT Delhi** + parts of **Haryana, UP, Rajasthan**.

nc1c9508a66a.s: Which one of the following towns is NOT a part of the National Capital Region (NCR)?
nc1c9508a66a.x: Ambala is not in the NCR (UPPSC 2011 trap). Rohtak and Karnal are in the Haryana part of the NCR, and Khurja (Bulandshahr) is in the UP part.
nc1c9508a66a.tq: NCR trap: Ambala is out; Rohtak, Karnal, Khurja are in.
xs: **Ambala** is **not** in the NCR — so option **(4)** is correct (**UPPSC 2011** trap).
**Rohtak** and **Karnal** are in the **Haryana** part; **Khurja** (**Bulandshahr**) in the **UP** part.
xa: Rajasthan's NCR town: **Alwar**.
⚠ **Punjab and Madhya Pradesh** are not in the NCR.
Other Haryana NCR towns: **Panipat, Sonipat, Gurugram, Faridabad**.

n1e9b36081fd.s: Which organisation approved Namo Cities in June 2026?
n1e9b36081fd.x: The National Capital Region Planning Board approved Namo Cities in June 2026.
n1e9b36081fd.tq: Match the current urban initiative with the responsible planning body.
xs: The **National Capital Region Planning Board** approved **Namo Cities** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Four greenfield cities, on the **TOD** model around **Namo Bharat (RRTS)** corridors (Jun 2026).
xa: NCRPB was set up under the **NCRPB Act, 1985**.
NCRPB's **PARIVARTAN**: **₹9,585 crore** clean-mobility scheme.
**QCI** conducts **Swachh Survekshan**, not NCR planning.

n338bbadc684.s: The slum population constituted approximately what percentage of India's urban population according to Census 2011?
n338bbadc684.x: Slum dwellers accounted for about 17.4% of India's urban population in Census 2011.
n338bbadc684.tq: Identify the precise percentage rather than the nearest-looking estimate.
xs: Slum dwellers were about **17.4%** of urban population — so option **(3)** is correct.
Census 2011 counted **6.54 crore** in slums.
xa: **Maharashtra** had the largest slum population; **undivided AP** the highest share (**about 36%**).
**World Bank**: **177 million** slum dwellers, most of any country.
**Greater Visakhapatnam** had the highest share of slum households (**about 44%**).

n92f79c78b25.s: Among million-plus cities in Census 2011, the highest share of slum households was in:
n92f79c78b25.x: Greater Visakhapatnam (about 44%) was ahead of Mumbai (about 41%), though Greater Mumbai had the largest slum population.
xa: ⚠ Largest **number** = **Maharashtra / Greater Mumbai**; highest **share** = **Undivided AP / Greater Visakhapatnam**.
Undivided AP: about **36%** of urban population in slums.
Slums = about **17.4%** of urban population.

nf79a7d3eb34.s: In Census 2011, which State had the highest share of its urban population living in slums?
nf79a7d3eb34.x: Undivided Andhra Pradesh had the highest share, at about 36%.
xa: Census 2011: **6.54 crore** slum dwellers.
**World Bank**: **177 million** (broader definition).
**Greater Mumbai** had the largest slum population among million-plus cities.

nb981f8cd996.s: Which of the following is a major cause of urban flooding in expanding cities?
o: Construction over lakes, wetlands and floodplains
nb981f8cd996.x: Urban flooding is caused by construction over water bodies and floodplains, concretisation of permeable soil and blocked drains.
xa: **Bengaluru**: built-up land **8% (1973) → about 74% (2013)**.
**Visakhapatnam**: flash floods after only a few hours of rain.
Vegetation loss also feeds the **urban heat island**.

n5fc068d5253.s: India generates about how much municipal solid waste a year?
n5fc068d5253.x: India generates about 62 million tonnes of MSW a year; about 70% is collected but only 30% processed.
xa: **DRAP** targets **214** legacy dumpsites by **Dec 2026**.
Megacities need stronger **Metropolitan Waste Management Authorities**.
**Swachh Survekshan** (run by **MoHUA**, conducted by **QCI**) ranks cities on cleanliness.

n32de2532a64.s: How many of the world's ten most polluted cities are in India?
n32de2532a64.x: Eight of the world's ten most polluted cities are in India, and Delhi is identified as the most polluted capital.
xa: **PARIVARTAN** (**₹9,585 crore**) will replace about **2.07 lakh** old trucks and buses in the NCR.
The **urban heat island** comes from **dense construction, asphalt**, lost tree cover.
Commuters lose **1.5-2 hours** a day in traffic.

nb13e79e8145.s: India has about one urban planner per ______ people, against one per 5,000 in developed countries.
nb13e79e8145.x: India has approximately one planner per one lakh people, whereas developed countries have about one per 5,000.
xa: Commuters lose **1.5-2 hours** a day (**BCG**).
ES 2025-26 wants a statutory city plan and a **unified metropolitan authority**.
Cities are **"administered, not governed"** (ES).

n7d125f9a85c.s: Which combination best explains the urban heat island effect?
o: Low building density, irrigated fields and cool winds
Open wetlands, permeable soil and increased tree cover
Dense construction, asphalt surfaces and loss of tree cover
Reduced construction, bare rock and expanded forests
n7d125f9a85c.x: Dense construction, asphalt and the loss of tree cover trap heat and intensify the urban heat island effect.
n7d125f9a85c.tq: Select the complete causal combination rather than an isolated factor.
xs: **Dense construction, asphalt and lost tree cover** trap heat — so option **(3)** is correct.
Open **wetlands**, **permeable soil** and **more trees** would reduce, not cause, the effect.
xa: A **UEA** study of **104** cities found **Patiala** could warm at **double** the projected rate.
**Bengaluru** vegetation fell from **68%** to under **15%**.
**Delhi** is the **most polluted capital**.

n25414015af5.s: Swachh Survekshan began in 2016 with how many cities?
n25414015af5.x: It began in 2016 with 73 cities; run by MoHUA and conducted by QCI, the 2024-25 survey covered 4,589 cities.
xa: It is the **world's largest cleanliness survey**.
**Indore** topped the 10 lakh+ Super Swachh League for the **8th time**.
AP set up **PMUs in 46 ULBs** for Swachh Survekshan 2026.

n1dd4e9e5509.s: Which cities were listed in the Super Swachh League (10 lakh+ population) of Swachh Survekshan?
n1dd4e9e5509.x: Indore, Surat and Navi Mumbai were in the 10 lakh+ Super Swachh League; Noida, Chandigarh and Mysuru in its 3-10 lakh category.
xa: **Swachh Shahar** is a **new category** in 2024-25.
**Indore** was 1st for the **8th time**.
**4,589 cities** were surveyed in 2024-25.

na665f7e1e6c.s: Which of the following cities is included among the newer Tier-2 cities topping the Ease of Living Index?
na665f7e1e6c.x: Pune, Navi Mumbai and Tirupati are identified among the newer Tier-2 cities topping the Ease of Living Index.
na665f7e1e6c.tq: Match the index with the city-level example rather than with a Swachh Survekshan category.
xs: **Tirupati** is among the newer Tier-2 cities topping the **Ease of Living Index** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The others named are **Pune** and **Navi Mumbai** (ES 2025-26).
**Mira-Bhayandar** and **Jamshedpur** are **Swachh Shahar** winners; **Patiala** is the heat-island example.
xa: The **Ease of Living Index** is run by **MoHUA**.
**Navi Mumbai** was also 3rd in the Super Swachh League (10 lakh+).
**Indore** tops Swachh Survekshan for the **8th time**.

n37e67c7f18d.s: Amartya Sen's book 'Development as Freedom' was published in:
n37e67c7f18d.x: 'Development as Freedom' came out in 1999; 1990 is the year of the first HDR, conceived by Mahbub ul Haq with Sen.
xa: Sen won the Nobel in Economics in **1998**.
The HDR is published by **UNDP**.
Core idea: development = **enlargement of human choices**, not just income.
First **NHDR of India**: **2001**.

nd24e3ce1951.s: Amartya Sen received the Nobel Prize in Economics in:
nd24e3ce1951.x: Sen received the Nobel in 1998; the human development approach views development as the enlargement of human choices.
xa: Two countries with the **same GNI per capita** can reach different outcomes.
Sen's **"Development as Freedom"** appeared in **1999**.
**Growth** is quantitative; **development** is quantitative + qualitative.

n4341075e041.s: Unlike human development, which has both quantitative and qualitative dimensions, economic growth is primarily:
n4341075e041.x: Economic growth is primarily quantitative and associated with income.
xa: Development = **enlargement of human choices**.
The HDR aims to make **people and their capabilities** the test of development.
HDI dimensions: **long and healthy life**, **knowledge**, **income**.

nc38354a94f6.s: Since 2010, the three dimension indices of the HDI are combined using the:
nc38354a94f6.x: The HDI is the geometric mean of the three indices, which replaced the arithmetic mean in 2010.
xa: India's GNI per capita: **$9,046.76** (PPP) in HDR 2025.
Health indicator: **life expectancy at birth**.
Knowledge: **MYS** and **EYS**.

n418d181d2d2.s: The income dimension of the HDI is measured by:
n418d181d2d2.x: HDI uses GNI per capita; education uses mean years of schooling (25+) and expected years of schooling.
xa: India's **GNI per capita**: **$9,046.76** (PPP).
India's **EYS** is **13 years** — the weak point of its Education Index.
Income enters as a **logarithm** with a **$75,000** cap.

n7abc6187114.s: Which one of the following is NOT a component of the Human Development Index?
n7abc6187114.x: The HDI combines life expectancy at birth (health), mean and expected years of schooling (knowledge) and GNI per capita (income). Military expenditure, like inequality, poverty and gender gaps, is not part of the HDI; inequality is captured separately by the IHDI.
n7abc6187114.tq: HDI = health + knowledge + income only; inequality, poverty, gender, military spending are outside it.
xs: **Military expenditure** is not an HDI component — so option **(3)** is correct.
HDI uses **life expectancy at birth**, **MYS/EYS** and **GNI per capita**.
xa: Also excluded: **inequality, poverty, gender gaps, human security, empowerment, environment** (APPSC-GS key).
Inequality is captured by the **IHDI** — "loss due to inequality" (APPSC-G2 2017).
⚠ "Which is NOT an HDI component" often uses **inequality**, **military spending**, **MPI**.

nfc878e7a92c.s: The two persistent weaknesses flagged for India in the HDR 2025 discussion were
o: Low life expectancy and low school enrolment
nfc878e7a92c.x: The report identified gender inequality and income inequality as India's two persistent weaknesses.
nfc878e7a92c.tq: Recall the report’s diagnostic issues rather than general economic problems.
xs: The two weaknesses are **gender inequality** and **income inequality** — so option **(1)** is correct.
India's **Education Index** is also weak because **EYS is low**.
xa: **World Inequality Database**: top 10% earn **13x** the bottom 10% (2023-24).
Gender gaps are measured by the **GDI** and **GII**.
Inequality loss is captured by the **IHDI**.

n649cf71637a.s: The Human Development Report 2025 placed India at which position among countries and territories?
n649cf71637a.x: India was ranked 130th among 193 countries and territories in the Human Development Report 2025.
n649cf71637a.tq: Pair the rank with the correct report coverage instead of remembering the rank alone.
xs: HDR 2025 ranked India **130th among 193** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**189** countries were ranked in **HDR 2018/2019**; **191** in **HDR 2021-22**.
xa: **Bangladesh** shares rank **130**.
⚠ Always pair the rank with the **report year** and **total countries**.

n1e4dc6440ae.s: Which one of the following groups consists only of countries that had a better HDI performance than India in the cited comparison?
n1e4dc6440ae.x: China, Sri Lanka and Bhutan were listed above India, with ranks 78, 89 and 125 respectively. Bangladesh had the same rank of 130 in the cited comparison.
n1e4dc6440ae.tq: Use group elimination to identify the set containing only higher-ranked countries.
xs: **China, Sri Lanka and Bhutan** rank above India — so option **(2)** is correct.
Ranks: **China 78**, **Sri Lanka 89**, **Bhutan 125**; India **130**.
**Bangladesh** is level (**130**); **Nepal (145), Myanmar (150), Pakistan (168)** are below.
xa: **Sri Lanka** was the "neighbour ahead of India" answer (**APPSC-GS 2025**).
India's HDI: **0.685**, **Medium** category.
**Pakistan** is lowest among listed neighbours.

ne12939c3500.s: In the Human Development Report 2025, India's HDI value of 0.685 places it in which category?
ne12939c3500.x: 0.685 lies in the Medium band (0.550-0.699), just below the 0.700 threshold for High. Low is below 0.550, and Very high is 0.800 and above, so neither applies.
ne12939c3500.tq: India 0.685 = Medium, just short of High (0.700).
xs: India's **0.685** is **Medium** (**0.550-0.699**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is just below the **0.700** **High** threshold (APPSC-GS 2025).
**Low** is below **0.550**; **Very High** is **0.800+**.
xa: India's HDI was **0.676** in 2022.
⚠ The sub-national series gives India **0.732** — do not mix with UNDP's **0.685**.

n03a490406d9.s: Where inequality exists in a country, its Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI) is:
n03a490406d9.x: The IHDI discounts the HDI for inequality in each dimension, so it is lower when inequality exists and equals the HDI only when there is none.
xa: "Loss in potential development due to inequality" = **IHDI** (**APPSC-G2 2017**).
Inequality is **excluded** from the HDI itself.
**GDI** = ratio of **female to male HDI**.

n47df971de92.s: Which index is the ratio of female to male HDI?
n47df971de92.x: GDI is the female-to-male HDI ratio; GII covers reproductive health, empowerment and labour market; PQLI uses literacy, infant mortality and life expectancy.
xa: **MPI** is produced by **UNDP-OPHI**; its forerunner was the **HPI**.
**PQLI** was a **pre-HDI** index.
⚠ **GII**: **0 = equality, 1 = worst**; **GDI** close to **1 = parity**.

n083d30ed9e8.s: In the Gender Inequality Index (GII), a value of 0 denotes:
o: maximum inequality between women and men
female HDI higher than male HDI
male HDI higher than female HDI
n083d30ed9e8.x: On the GII scale, 0 = equality and 1 = worst outcome; the GDI (female-to-male HDI ratio) near 1 means parity.
xa: ⚠ "0 = equal, 1 = women worst" belongs to the **GII**, not the GDI.
**IHDI** = HDI discounted for inequality; **IHDI < HDI** unless there is no inequality.
**MPI** measures deprivations in health, education and living standards (**UNDP-OPHI**).
**HPI** was the forerunner of the MPI.

nb3f77d4e49f.s: The Human Poverty Index was the forerunner of which index?

xa: Full list: Bodo Gadaba, Gutob Gadaba, Bondo, Khond and Parengi Poroja, **Dongaria Khond**, **Kutia Khond**, **Chenchu**, **Konda Reddi**, **Konda Savara**, **Kolam**, **Thoti**.

n4b582694a92.s: The Savaras are particularly known for which combination of cultural practices?
o: Wall paintings and buffalo sacrifice called Gour
n4b582694a92.x: The Savaras are known for wall paintings and the buffalo sacrifice known as Gour.
n4b582694a92.tq: Match a tribe with its distinctive cultural practices.
xs: The Savaras are known for **wall paintings** (Idital) and **buffalo sacrifice (Gour)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Basket making and fortune-telling = **Yerukula**; Teej = **Lambada**; horned-headgear dance = **Koya**.
xa: **Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy** designed a **Savara script** and Savara-Telugu dictionaries.
Savaras live in the north coastal hills (**Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam**).

n19a5859edba.s: The Sammakka–Saralamma Jatara is held at Medaram and is generally conducted once in every:
n19a5859edba.x: The Sammakka–Saralamma Jatara at Medaram is held every two years, in February, and is associated with the Koyas.
n19a5859edba.tq: Test the exact periodicity of a festival rather than its associated tribe alone.
xs: The **Sammakka-Saralamma Jatara** at **Medaram** is held every **2 years** (in Feb) — so option **(1)** is correct.

xa: Other Koya festivals: **Bhumi Panduga**, **Mamidi Panduga**.

n56902b00168.s: Who designed a script for the Savara language and compiled Savara-Telugu dictionaries?
n56902b00168.x: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy designed a Savara script and compiled Savara-Telugu dictionaries. Kandukuri Veeresalingam was a social reformer, Gurajada Apparao a playwright and C. P. Brown a Telugu lexicographer; none of them made the Savara script.
xs: **Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy** designed a **Savara script** and compiled **Savara-Telugu dictionaries** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The notes credit no Savara work to the other three names.
xa: Savaras are known for **wall paintings** (Idital) and **buffalo sacrifice (Gour)**.
Savaras live in the north coastal hills: **Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam**.

n946d09966a4.s: The submergence associated with Polavaram threatens the Koyas’ traditional “Pander Valla”, which refers to their:

xs: "**Pander Valla**" is the Koyas' **river-fishing tradition**, threatened by **Polavaram** submergence — so option **(1)** is correct.

**Koya and Kondh** groups oppose displacement.

nap-geography-5-4.s: The Yanadi tribe is associated with which area of Andhra Pradesh?

Lambadi is also known as Banjara. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 15-18]

nap-geography-5-11.s: The Yerukula tribe is traditionally associated with:

n: Yerukula is associated with almost all plain districts. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 15-18]

xa: They also do **rope making** and **pig-rearing**.

nfb7e1e6535e.s: Which of the following tribes is associated with podu cultivation in the hill tracts of East and West Godavari and is also a PVTG?

n96addf9ad9e.s: The Konda Doras served as which of the following in the Rampa agency?
n96addf9ad9e.x: The Konda Doras served as Mutadars, or hill chiefs, of the Rampa agency.

xs: The **Konda Doras** served as **Mutadars**, the **hill chiefs** of the **Rampa** agency — so option **(1)** is correct.

xa: **Alluri Sitarama Raju** led the **Rampa rebellion (1922-24)** against forest laws and the **muttadari** system.

xs: **Bodo Gadaba, Gutob Gadaba** and the **Poraja** groups (Bondo, Khond, Parengi) live in the **Araku Valley / Visakhapatnam agency** — so option **(2)** is correct.

n44e8be311d8.s: The Dhimsa dance is associated with which of the following groups of tribes?

Creating the category of Primitive Tribal Groups
Allowing bauxite mining in the Araku agency

Conflict with the 1/70 Regulation, PESA and the Forest Rights Act

xa: The **APPSC-G2 2008** key left this question unanswered.

n6798e38465d.s: Farming that applies high labour and capital input per unit of land is called:
n6798e38465d.x: Intensive farming uses high input per unit of land; extensive farming uses large areas with low input.
xa: Intensive subsistence farming: **Monsoon Asia** (wet paddy).

nc4d12a9f2c7.s: Oriental intensive farming is primarily associated with which of the following regions and characteristics?
o: The Mediterranean basin; winter rainfall and olives
The Prairies; mechanised wheat and high output per worker
The Pampas; extensive cattle ranching and low labour input
Monsoon Asia; wet paddy, high output per hectare and low output per worker
nc4d12a9f2c7.x: Oriental intensive farming belongs to monsoon Asia. It is characterised by wet-paddy cultivation, high output per hectare and relatively low output per worker.
nc4d12a9f2c7.tq: Contrast output per hectare with output per worker to identify the oriental intensive system.
xs: **Oriental intensive** farming = **Monsoon Asia**, **wet paddy**, **high output per hectare, low output per worker** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Winter rain and olives = **Mediterranean**; mechanised wheat = **commercial grain** (Prairies).
xa: It matches the **intensive subsistence** type: small plots, heavy labour.
**IRRI** (Los Baños, Philippines, **1960**) released **IR8** "miracle rice".

nworld-geography-15-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about plantation agriculture?
o: Tea is associated with India and Sri Lanka.
Cocoa is associated with South Asia.
It is mainly practised in tropical regions.
nworld-geography-15-2.x: Cocoa is linked with West Africa (Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana), not South Asia.
n: Plantation agriculture is practised in tropical regions. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Tea plantation agriculture is practised in India. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Tea plantation agriculture is practised in Sri Lanka. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Coffee plantation agriculture is practised in Brazil. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Cocoa plantation agriculture is practised in West Africa. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xa: **Rubber** plantations are associated with **Malaysia**.
Plantation agriculture: **large estates**, **single cash crop**, **capital-intensive**, **export-oriented**.
World cocoa: **Côte d'Ivoire 1st, Ghana 2nd**.

nworld-geography-15-5.s: Livestock ranching is a form of:
nworld-geography-15-5.x: Ranching is large-scale and commercial; nomadic herding involves seasonal migration for fodder and water.
n: Nomadic herding involves seasonal migration with animals. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Nomadic herding is undertaken in search of fodder and water. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Intensive subsistence farming involves high labour input on small plots. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Livestock ranching involves large-scale commercial rearing of animals. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xa: Ranching regions: **western US**, **Pampas**, **Australia**, **New Zealand**, **South Africa**.
Nomadic herding regions: **Sahara**, **Central Asia**, **Arabian Desert**, parts of **Rajasthan** and **J&K**.
Intensive subsistence farming gives a **high yield per hectare** in **Monsoon Asia**.

nbe7e0dac253.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about shifting cultivation?
o: It is found in high-rainfall forests of the Amazon, Tropical Africa, South-East Asia and North-East India
It is primitive subsistence, slash-and-burn agriculture
Forests are cleared by burning and cultivated temporarily with low technology
It is a capital-intensive, export-oriented commercial agriculture
nbe7e0dac253.x: Shifting cultivation is primitive subsistence farming, not capital-intensive export-oriented commercial agriculture.
xa: AP's version is **podu**, in the agency tracts.

**Intensive subsistence** farming uses **family labour** on small plots.

nworld-geography-15-10.s: Nomadic herding is NOT practised in:
o: the Arabian Desert and parts of Rajasthan
nworld-geography-15-10.x: The Amazon and Congo rainforests support shifting cultivation, not nomadic herding, which is found in dry or cold lands.
n: Nomadic herding is practised in the Sahara. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Nomadic herding is practised in Central Asia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Nomadic herding is practised in the Arabian Desert. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Nomadic herding is practised in parts of Rajasthan. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Nomadic herding is practised in parts of Jammu and Kashmir. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xa: Herders migrate seasonally in search of **fodder and water**.
**Livestock ranching** is the commercial, large-scale form of animal rearing.
Shifting cultivation regions: **Amazon Basin**, **Tropical Africa**, **South-East Asia**, **North-East India**.

nworld-geography-15-11.s: Intensive subsistence farming, which gives a high yield per hectare, mainly relies on:
nworld-geography-15-11.x: Intensive subsistence farming uses family labour on small holdings and produces high yields per hectare.
n: Intensive subsistence farming uses family labour. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Intensive subsistence farming produces a high yield per hectare. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xa: **Rice dominates** in **wet areas**.
Region: **Monsoon Asia** — East, South and South-East Asia.
Whittlesey's **Oriental intensive** type: **high output per hectare, low output per worker**.

nworld-geography-15-13.s: Which crop dominates intensive subsistence farming in wet areas?
nworld-geography-15-13.x: Rice dominates intensive subsistence farming in wet areas; wheat takes over in drier parts.
nworld-geography-15-13.tq: Recall the main crop of each farming type.
n: Rice dominates intensive subsistence farming in wet areas. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xs: **Rice** dominates intensive subsistence farming in wet areas — option **(4)**.
Intensive subsistence farming in **Monsoon Asia** relies on **wet paddy**.
**Wheat** dominates **commercial grain farming**; **tea** and **coffee** are **plantation** crops.
xa: It uses **high labour input** on **small plots** with **family labour**.
It gives a **high yield per hectare**.
**China** is the largest rice producer; **India** the **second-largest** and **number-one exporter**.

n5a3f35f2e7e.s: Regions of Mediterranean agriculture receive most of their rainfall in:
n5a3f35f2e7e.x: Mediterranean regions get winter rain; viticulture, citrus and olives are typical.
xa: **Viticulture** = grape cultivation.
Whittlesey mapped **13** regions (**1936**).

n120b2b332d1.s: Mocha coffee is named after a port in:
n120b2b332d1.x: Mocha is an Arabica coffee named after the Yemeni port of Mocha; Arabica originated in Ethiopia.
xa: India is the **7th** coffee producer; **Karnataka** grows **71%**.
AP is **4th** in India (**Araku**).

n571643b09c5.s: The core region of India's Green Revolution was:
o: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
n571643b09c5.x: The core region was Punjab, Haryana and western UP; M.S. Swaminathan and C. Subramaniam were key Indian figures.
xa: **Borlaug** = father of the global Green Revolution (**Nobel Peace Prize 1970**).
**William Gaud** coined the term in **1968**.

nworld-geography-3-7.s: Which country leads the world in copper production?
nworld-geography-3-7.x: Chile leads in copper; China leads in crude steel, Australia in iron ore and Brazil in coffee.
n: China is the world’s largest producer of crude steel. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
China is the world’s largest producer of coal. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
Australia is the world’s largest producer of iron ore. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
Australia is the world’s largest producer of bauxite. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
xa: **Australia** also leads in **bauxite**.
Diamonds: **Russia** by volume; **Botswana** by value.
World's largest fishing ground: **Northwest Pacific**; busiest container port: **Shanghai**.

nworld-geography-15-3.s: Plantation agriculture, an export-oriented monoculture, is a product of:
nworld-geography-15-3.x: Colonial estates were set up to grow one crop for export to the home country.
n: Plantation agriculture is a product of colonialism. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Plantation agriculture is export-oriented monoculture. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Plantation agriculture generally involves a single cash crop. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Plantation agriculture is export-oriented. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xa: It is **capital-intensive**.
Regions: **Latin America**, **South-East Asia**, **South Asia**, **Sub-Saharan Africa**.
Examples: **tea** (India, Sri Lanka), **coffee** (Brazil), **rubber** (Malaysia), **cocoa** (West Africa).

nworld-geography-15-4.s: Which type of farming particularly requires refrigeration and transport?
nworld-geography-15-4.x: Dairy farming needs refrigeration and transport; Mediterranean agriculture specialises in olives, grapes and citrus.
n: Dairy farming requires refrigeration. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Dairy farming requires transport. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mediterranean agriculture specialises in olives. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mediterranean agriculture specialises in grapes. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mediterranean agriculture specialises in citrus fruits. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mediterranean agriculture specialises in fruits. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mediterranean agriculture includes viticulture. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xa: Dairy regions: **Denmark**, the **Netherlands**, **New Zealand**, the US **Midwest**, **south-eastern Australia**.
Mediterranean regions: **California**, **Central Chile**, the **Cape Province**, **south-western Australia**.
**Whittlesey (1936)** mapped **13** agricultural regions.

nworld-geography-15-7.s: Which of the following is NOT a region of commercial grain farming?
nworld-geography-15-7.x: The Prairies, Pampas and Steppes are grain regions; the Mediterranean Basin has Mediterranean farming.
n: Commercial grain farming is practised in the Prairies of the United States and Canada. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Commercial grain farming is practised in the Pampas of Argentina. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Commercial grain farming is practised in the Steppes of Russia and Ukraine. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mediterranean agriculture is practised in the Mediterranean Basin. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xa: The **Downs** of **Australia** are also a commercial grain region.
Commercial grain farming: **large, highly mechanised** farms; **wheat dominates**; **temperate grasslands**.
It is **extensive**, with a **high commodity rate**.

nworld-geography-15-17.s: Mixed farming, as practised in Western Europe, the eastern USA and Argentina, combines:

crops and livestock on the same farm

n: Mixed farming combines crops and livestock on the same farm. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mixed farming is highly mechanised. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mixed farming is practised in Western Europe. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mixed farming is practised in the eastern United States. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mixed farming is practised in Argentina. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mixed farming is practised in south-eastern Australia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mixed farming is practised in New Zealand. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Mixed farming is practised in South Africa. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xa: Mixed farming is also found in **NW Europe** and **eastern North America**.
**Dairy farming** specialises in **milk** and needs **refrigeration and transport**.
**Livestock ranching** is large-scale commercial rearing on **ranches**.

nworld-geography-15-19.s: Denmark, the Netherlands and New Zealand are noted for which type of farming?

Dairy farming is practised in Denmark. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]

Dairy farming is practised in New Zealand. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Dairy farming is practised in the Midwest of the United States. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Dairy farming is practised in south-eastern Australia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xa: Dairy farming **specialises in milk production**.
It **requires refrigeration and transport**.
**New Zealand** also has **mixed farming** and **livestock ranching**.

nworld-geography-15-23.s: Mediterranean agriculture is practised in which of the following regions?

n: Mediterranean agriculture is practised in south-western Australia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xs: Mediterranean agriculture is practised in **south-western Australia** — option **(2)**.

The **Pampas** are a **commercial grain** and **ranching** region; the **eastern United States** has **mixed farming**.
**New Zealand** is linked with **dairy**, mixed farming and ranching.
xa: Mediterranean agriculture specialises in **fruits, olives, grapes, citrus**; includes **viticulture**.
Whittlesey: Mediterranean areas have **winter rain**.
**Dairy** regions include **south-eastern Australia**, not the south-west.

His **Oriental intensive** region: Monsoon Asia, wet paddy.

n5f8baa35cc1.s: Who is associated with the crop-combination method of agricultural regionalisation introduced in 1954?
n5f8baa35cc1.x: J. C. Weaver introduced the crop-combination method in 1954. Doi and Rafiullah subsequently modified the method.

xs: **J.C. Weaver (1954)** devised the **crop combination** method — so option **(1)** is correct.

**Bhatia** = diversification and concentration; **Kendall** = efficiency; **Sengupta** = macro regions of India.

**Sengupta and Sdasyuk** = **4** macro agricultural regions (APPSC-G1 2023 key).

xa: **AP** is India's **largest fruit producer**.

Horticulture output (**362-367 MT**) now exceeds foodgrains.
**Vertical farming** gives year-round crops in non-tropical regions.

n90736bdf8ba.s: Which country is the world's largest producer of cocoa?

**Natural rubber**: India 6th producer, 2nd consumer; Kerala grows **70-75%**.

n1711ee99a8f.s: Who pioneered Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF)?
n1711ee99a8f.x: Subhash Palekar pioneered Zero Budget Natural Farming. It is distinct from the broader organic-farming framework and from the Green Revolution breeding programme.

xs: **Subhash Palekar** pioneered **Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF)** — so option **(3)** is correct.

**National Mission on Natural Farming**: **8.80 lakh ha** + **18.19 lakh** farmers by Mar 2026.

nworld-geography-3-4.s: Which country is the world's largest exporter of rice?
nworld-geography-3-4.x: India is the largest rice exporter because it produces a large surplus over domestic consumption.

India is the world’s number-one exporter of rice. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
xa: **China** is the largest producer of rice.
**Intensive subsistence** farming in **Monsoon Asia** is dominated by **rice** in wet areas.
**IRRI** released **IR8** "miracle rice".

nworld-geography-3-10.s: Which country is the world's largest producer of diamonds by value?

Botswana is the world’s largest producer of diamonds by value. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 4-5]
xa: **Chile** leads in **copper**; **Australia** in **iron ore** and **bauxite**.
**China** leads in **gold**, coal and crude steel.
**Thailand** leads in **natural rubber**.

n62c9d9e0ba2.s: The term 'Green Revolution' was coined in 1968 by:
n62c9d9e0ba2.x: William Gaud coined the term in 1968; Norman Borlaug bred semi-dwarf wheat in Mexico and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.
xa: ⚠ Term **1968** (Gaud) vs Nobel **1970** (Borlaug).
India's key figures: **M.S. Swaminathan** and **C. Subramaniam**.

n1f693f8f7a0.s: The International Rice Research Institute (IRRI), which released IR8, is located in:

xa: **Norman Borlaug** bred semi-dwarf wheat in **Mexico**; **Nobel Peace Prize 1970**.

**M.S. Swaminathan** + **C. Subramaniam** were key Indian figures.
**Subhash Palekar** pioneered **ZBNF**.

n5cbb1b89757.s: Which programme is described as the world's largest agro-ecological programme, covering about 10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh hectares?
n5cbb1b89757.x: APCNF (Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming) is the world's largest agro-ecological programme, with 10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha. xs: **APCNF** is the **world's largest agro-ecological programme**: **10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh ha** (Jul 2026) — so option **(2)** is correct.

xa: **ZBNF** was pioneered by **Subhash Palekar**.
⚠ **Hydroponics** and **aquaponics** are not agroecological.

n49b1a66b07a.s: The United Nations has designated 2026 as the:

International Year of Sustainable Rice Cultivation

New World: **maize, potato, tomato, tobacco, cocoa, rubber, cassava, groundnut, chilli**.

n255872cb722.s: In which of the following crops does Andhra Pradesh rank first in India?

xa: AP is also 1st in **papaya, cocoa, chillies**.

nf38ceed9a8e.s: The dominant cropping system of the Indo-Gangetic Plains is:
nf38ceed9a8e.x: Rice-wheat is the dominant cropping system of the Indo-Gangetic Plains, with paddy followed by wheat as double cropping.

**Lower Gangetic Plains** (West Bengal) = **rice, jute**; **Eastern Himalayan** = plantations, jhum.

n046d4a441fd.s: Which one of the following examples represents parallel cropping?

Maize and green gram grown together without competition
The next crop sown into a standing crop before its harvest
Paddy followed by wheat in the same year

**Ratoon**: crop regrows from **stubble**; yield falls each cycle.
**Crop rotation**: fixed, planned sequence to keep soil fertile and cut pests.
Maize is a **kharif** crop led by **Karnataka, MP**.

n469db7f0cfb.s: From Kharif 2026, the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana was reported to cover which additional or specifically recognised contingencies?
o: Only drought affecting wheat and maize
Cyclones affecting all crops without exception
n469db7f0cfb.x: From Kharif 2026, PMFBY coverage was reported to include wild-animal attacks and paddy inundation.

Dalhan Aatmanirbharta Mission: **100% MSP procurement** of tur, urad, masoor.

nindian-geography-24-4.s: Which of the following is a Zaid crop?

Lentil is a Rabi pulse crop. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 80-84]
Pea is a Rabi pulse. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 80-84]

Lathyrus is a Rabi crop. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 80-84]

Lathyrus is a Rabi pulse crop. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 80-84]

nbiology-22-10.s: The cause of ear cockle of wheat is:

xs: **Ear cockle** of wheat is caused by **a nematode** — so option **(2)**.

nd6f8d8a17e8.s: Which of the following combinations regarding wheat cultivation is correct?

Perennial crop; uniform rainfall throughout the year
Rabi crop; cool growing season, 50–75 cm rainfall and warm sunny ripening
Kharif crop; very high humidity and rainfall above 150 cm
nd6f8d8a17e8.x: Wheat is a rabi crop requiring a cool growing season, about 50–75 cm rainfall and warm, sunny conditions during ripening.
nd6f8d8a17e8.tq: Match the crop season with its growth and ripening requirements.
xs: Wheat is a **rabi** crop needing a **cool growing season**, **50-75 cm** rainfall and **bright warm sun at ripening** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Wheat is not kharif: very high humidity and heavy rainfall describe **rice** (above **100 cm**), which is the **kharif** cereal.

xa: Wheat also grows on the **black soil of the Deccan** — the APPSC-G1 2024 trap called it unsuitable, which is incorrect.
⚠ Rice **above 100 cm** vs wheat **50-75 cm**; rice = **kharif**, wheat = **rabi**.
Leading wheat states (2026 order): **Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana**.
India is **2nd** in the world in wheat with **117.94 MMT**.

n14074283f5f.s: Rice is especially suited to which of the following soil and geographical environments?
o: Clayey or loamy soils of deltaic and coastal alluvial areas
Laterite soils of upland plateaus only
n14074283f5f.x: Rice is well suited to clayey or loamy soils, particularly the deltaic and coastal alluvium.

xs: Rice suits **clayey or loamy soils** of **deltaic and coastal alluvium** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Sandy soils** of the driest tracts suit **bajra**, not rice; **red soils** are linked with **ragi**.
Rice needs **above 100 cm** rainfall, so desert and arid soils are unsuitable.
xa: **AP and TN rice deltas** gained in the Green Revolution through irrigation.
Wheat grows on the alluvium of the **Ganga-Satluj plains** and the **black soil of the Deccan**.
**Lower Gangetic Plains** (West Bengal) zone: **rice, jute**.
AP paddy output **127.15 lakh MT** (2024-25).

n1839e1750de.s: Pulses are used in crop rotation because they:

xa: A **pulse-cereal rotation** leaves fixed nitrogen for the next crop.
**Intercropping** example: **tur with jowar or maize**.

**Rajasthan** leads bajra; **Karnataka** leads ragi.

naa64ec2268a.s: Wheat in India is chiefly associated with which group of States?

xa: **West Bengal** = "**Rice Bowl of India**", largest producer (2026).
**Rajasthan** leads **bajra**; **Karnataka** leads **ragi**.
Rice-wheat is the dominant **double cropping** system of the **Indo-Gangetic plains**.

nac7aef0b42d.s: Which States are listed as the leading maize producers of India?

ncf05aad9069.s: Which State is known as the 'Rice Bowl of India' and is currently the largest producer of rice?
ncf05aad9069.x: West Bengal is called the Rice Bowl of India and is the largest rice producer. Uttar Pradesh, Punjab (irrigated rice) and Andhra Pradesh are also important rice states, but none leads West Bengal.

**Lower Gangetic Plains** zone (West Bengal): **rice, jute**.

n37c0e24d78e.s: The first phase of the Green Revolution (mid-1960s to 1980s) was centred largely on:

xa: The crops most benefited were **wheat and rice** (APPSC 2025 key).

Crop imbalance — **pulses, oilseeds, millets neglected** — is a key limitation.

ne44535c39ef.s: Which factors have been identified as favouring rice–wheat cultivation, including paddy in Punjab?

nindian-geography-24-10.s: Rice requires a temperature of about:

n1e29ce99474.s: Which millet is a drought-tolerant crop of hot, dry conditions, led by Rajasthan?

n24a21ce998a.s: The core Green Revolution belt among the following agro-climatic regions is:

n205fdef9efe.tq: Use the exact local-name and location association rather than confusing neighbouring tribal regions.
xs: **Dipa** is shifting cultivation in **Bastar, Chhattisgarh** (APPSC 2025) — option **(1)**.
**Kumari** belongs to the **Western Ghats**; **Masole** to **Central Africa**; **Podu** to the **AP and Odisha agency**.
xa: Dipa is also reported from the **Andaman**.
APPSC-GS 2025 key: **Dipa**.
**Bewar / Dahiya** = Madhya Pradesh; **Jhum** = north-east.
Method: **slash and burn**, then move on.

n49dd3d086ee.s: Which of the following communities are associated with the practice of shifting cultivation in Andhra Pradesh?
n49dd3d086ee.x: In Andhra Pradesh, shifting cultivation is practised by the Konda Reddi, Koya and Savara communities. The practice involves slash-and-burn cultivation followed by movement to another site.
n49dd3d086ee.tq: Identify the communities linked to the regional practice instead of relying on general tribal associations.
xs: In AP, shifting cultivation is practised by the **Konda Reddi, Koya, Savara** — option **(3)**.
The method is **slash and burn**, then move on.
xa: AP's form is **Podu / Penda** in the **Eastern Ghats** agency; **Pondu** is a variant spelling.
APPSC 2025: the South Indian state practising **jhumming** = **Andhra Pradesh**.
Podu is also found in **Odisha**.
**Dipa** = Bastar, Chhattisgarh.

n9267bfa31ee.s: Which South Indian State practises shifting cultivation (jhumming), locally called podu, in the tribal tracts of the Eastern Ghats?
n9267bfa31ee.x: As the APPSC 2025 key held, Andhra Pradesh practises shifting cultivation known as podu (or penda) in its Eastern Ghats agency areas. Kerala's form is called ponam, and the Western Ghats form (Kerala, Karnataka) is called kumari; Tamil Nadu is not listed.
n9267bfa31ee.tq: Podu/Penda = AP Eastern Ghats; Kumari = Western Ghats.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** practises **jhumming**, locally **podu**, in **Eastern Ghats** tribal tracts (APPSC 2025) — option **(4)**.
Kerala's form is **Ponam**; the Western Ghats (Kerala, Karnataka) form is **Kumari**.
xa: Podu is also called **Penda**; **Pondu** is a variant spelling.
AP practitioners: **Konda Reddi, Koya, Savara**.
Podu also occurs in **Odisha**.
⚠ APPSC-GS 2025 key for Bastar: **Dipa**.

n4fb3082e095.s: The shifting cultivation known as 'Masole' is practised in:
n4fb3082e095.x: Masole is the shifting cultivation of Central Africa (Congo). Roca is practised in Brazil, Ladang in Indonesia and Malaysia, and Milpa in Mexico and Central America.
xs: **Masole** is the shifting cultivation of **Central Africa (Congo)** — option **(2)**.
**Roca** = Brazil; **Ladang** = Indonesia, Malaysia; **Milpa** = Mexico, Central America.
xa: APPSC-G1 2024 match: **II-I-IV-III**.
**Taungya** = Myanmar; **Ray** = Vietnam; **Conuco** = Venezuela.
Indian names: **Jhum** (NE), **Podu** (AP), **Dipa** (Bastar).
Method: **slash and burn**.

nworld-geography-15-24.s: 'Chena' is the name for shifting cultivation in:
nworld-geography-15-24.x: Chena is used in Sri Lanka; milpa in Central America and Mexico, conuco in Venezuela and tavy in Madagascar.
n: Milpa is the name for shifting cultivation in Central America. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Milpa is the name for shifting cultivation in Mexico. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Chena is the name for shifting cultivation in Sri Lanka. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Conuco is the name for shifting cultivation in Venezuela. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
Tavy is the name for shifting cultivation in Madagascar. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 23-25]
xa: **Jhum** = North-East India; **Ladang** = Indonesia/Malaysia.
**Roca** = Brazil; **Taungya** = Myanmar; **Masole** = Central Africa.
Ray = Vietnam; Tamrai = Thailand.

nworld-geography-21-7.s: The USA Corn Belt is a classic region of which crop?
nworld-geography-21-7.x: Maize grows in temperate and subtropical regions, the US Corn Belt being classic; wheat grows on the temperate grasslands.
n: Wheat is grown in temperate grasslands such as the Prairies, Steppes, and Pampas. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
Wheat includes winter wheat and spring wheat. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
Maize is grown in temperate and subtropical regions. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
The USA Corn Belt is a classic maize-producing region. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
xa: Wheat needs a **cool growing season**, **bright sunshine** at ripening and **well-drained loamy soil**.
Maize producers: **USA > China > Brazil**, with Argentina and India listed.
Wheat producers: **China > India > Russia**.

n0ac99081056.s: Which one of the following cereals ranks first in India in terms of importance and is a staple food for more than half of the country's population?
n0ac99081056.x: Rice is the first-ranking cereal in India and is the staple food of more than half of the country's population.
n0ac99081056.tq: Use the rank and population-share clue to identify the cereal.
xs: **Rice** is India's **1st** cereal and the staple of **over half of India** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Wheat** is the **2nd** most important cereal; **maize** and **millets** are kharif crops of lesser rank.
Rice needs **20-35°C** (above **25°C** ideal), high humidity and **above 100 cm** rainfall.
xa: **West Bengal** is the "**Rice Bowl of India**" and the largest producer.
India (**150.18 MT**) has now **surpassed China** (**145.28 MT**) as the world's largest rice producer.
India is the **largest rice exporter**, with **~40%** of world trade.
Rice suits **clayey/loamy**, deltaic and coastal alluvium soils.

o: Growing a crop only on fallow land
Sowing the next crop after complete removal of the previous crop
Growing one crop continuously for several years
Growing two or more crops together in definite rows
n1861f266c92.x: Intercropping involves growing two or more crops together in definite rows, such as tur with jowar or maize.
n1861f266c92.tq: Separate intercropping from mixed cropping by focusing on the definite row arrangement.
xs: **Intercropping** = **two or more crops together in definite rows** — option **(4)**.
Example: **tur with jowar or maize**.
xa: ⚠ **Mixed cropping** = seeds mixed, **no row pattern**; insures against failure.
**Parallel cropping**: crops of different growth habit, **no competition** (maize + green gram).
**Relay cropping**: next crop sown into the **standing crop** before harvest.
**Multiple/double**: crops in **succession** in one year (paddy then wheat).

n2d3c05a9ffa.s: Sowing the next crop into the standing crop before it is harvested is called:
n2d3c05a9ffa.x: Relay cropping sows the next crop into the standing crop; ratoon cropping is regrowth from stubble and mixed cropping sows crops together without a row pattern.
xa: Mixed cropping **insures against failure**.
**Intercropping** keeps crops in **definite rows** (tur with jowar or maize).
**Parallel cropping**: maize + green gram, no competition.
**Double cropping**: paddy followed by wheat.

n2186d80c394.s: India's cropping intensity in 2021-22 was approximately:
n2186d80c394.x: India's cropping intensity was 155.4% in 2021-22, reflecting a gross cropped area well above the net sown area. 121% and 188% resemble Andhra Pradesh's figures (1.21 in 2023-24, 1.88 in 2024-25), and 100% would mean no multiple cropping.
xs: India's **cropping intensity** was **155.4%** in **2021-22** — option **(3)**.
It reflects gross cropped area (**219.16 MH**) well above net sown area (**141 MH**).
**121** and **188** echo AP's figures (**1.21** in 2023-24, **1.88** in 2024-25); **100%** would mean no multiple cropping.
xa: Multiple/double cropping = two or more crops **in succession in one year**.
Gross irrigated **120.3 MH** (**54.9%** of GCA).
Net sown area is **42.8%** of the geographical area (**328.7 MH**).

n0f713a409f8.s: How many agro-climatic zones did the Planning Commission identify in the Seventh Plan?
n0f713a409f8.x: There are 15 agro-climatic zones based on soil, climate and cropping pattern, sub-divided into 72 sub-zones.
xa: **Trans-Gangetic Plains** (Punjab, Haryana, Delhi): wheat, rice; **highest productivity**.
**Upper Gangetic Plains** (western UP): core **Green Revolution** belt.
**Lower Gangetic Plains** (West Bengal): **rice, jute**.
**Eastern Himalayan** zone (NE states, Sikkim): plantations, **jhum**.

n50e714cabc7.s: The Dalhan Aatmanirbharta Mission, announced in October 2025, provides for 100% Minimum Support Price procurement of which group of pulses for four years?
n50e714cabc7.x: The mission provides 100% MSP procurement of tur, urad and masoor for a period of four years.
n50e714cabc7.tq: Use the exact crop group linked with the scheme instead of choosing a nearby pulse combination.
xs: The **Dalhan Aatmanirbharta Mission** (**Oct 2025**) gives **100% MSP procurement** of **tur, urad and masoor** for **four years** — option **(4)**.
**Gram, moong, soybean, groundnut** are not in the mission's procurement list.
xa: Outlay ₹**11,440 crore**; target **350 lakh tonnes** a year.
India is the world's **largest producer and consumer of pulses**.
AP allocation: Mission Aatmanirbharta in Pulses ₹**3,928.50 lakh**.
Leading pulse states: **MP, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, UP, Karnataka**.

nce92f0bfde1.s: Wheat, mainly a rabi crop, is the ____ most important cereal in India.
nce92f0bfde1.x: Wheat is India's second most important cereal; it is grown in the Ganga-Satluj plains and also the black-soil region of the Deccan.
xa: Wheat's main belt is the **Ganga-Satluj plains** (Indo-Gangetic "**wheat bowl**").
Wheat rainfall: **50-75 cm**.
Wheat states: **UP, MP, Punjab, Haryana** (2026 order).
The first Green Revolution phase (mid-1960s-1980s) was largely **wheat**.

ndeff8ef9b24.s: In 1970, Norman Borlaug, who developed Mexican dwarf wheat, received the Nobel Prize for:
ndeff8ef9b24.x: Borlaug received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970; M.S. Swaminathan is the father of India's Green Revolution and C. Subramaniam was the Union Agriculture Minister who backed it.
xa: ⚠ Father in the **world** = **Borlaug**; father in **India** = **Swaminathan**.
The Green Revolution began in **1965** as the **New Agricultural Strategy** (dated **1968** in current notes).
Inputs: **HYV seeds**, chemical fertilisers, pesticides, assured irrigation, mechanisation and **MSP**.
Crops most benefited: **wheat and rice** (APPSC **2025** key).

n1f433839126.s: The Green Revolution in India mainly increased the production of:
n1f433839126.x: Wheat (first phase) and rice (later, wider phase) gained most, as in the APPSC 2025 key. Pulses, oilseeds and coarse cereals lagged; cotton and sugarcane were not the focus of the strategy.
n1f433839126.tq: Green Revolution = wheat first, then rice; pulses/oilseeds left behind.
xs: The Green Revolution mainly increased **wheat and rice** (APPSC 2025 key) — option **(2)**.
**Pulses, oilseeds, coarse cereals lagged**, so options 1 and 3 are wrong.
xa: First phase largely **wheat**; rice gained in the **later, wider phase**.
It locked the north-west into **rice-wheat monoculture** and groundwater over-use.
**Cotton, jute, sugarcane** were added to **NFSM** only in **2014-15**.
⚠ Father in world = **Borlaug**; in India = **Swaminathan**.

ne2ab53c1e99.s: Swaminathan's proposed remedy for the adverse effects and ecological limitations of the Green Revolution is known as:
ne2ab53c1e99.x: The Evergreen Revolution was proposed as a sustainable corrective approach associated with M.S. Swaminathan.
ne2ab53c1e99.tq: Distinguish the sustainability-oriented term from revolutions associated with fisheries, milk or broad diversification.
xs: Swaminathan's remedy is the **Evergreen Revolution** — option **(2)**.
It answers Green Revolution ills: **groundwater depletion, salinity**, **rice-wheat monoculture**, fertiliser imbalance.
xa: Swaminathan = **Father of the Green Revolution in India**.
Borlaug = Father in the **world**, **Nobel Peace Prize 1970**.
Fertiliser imbalance: **10.9:4.1:1** vs ideal **4:2:1**.
Gains went to farmers with **>10 ha**.

n15a1cc92b7a.s: Procurement in India is criticised for being confined mainly to which crops, which use over two-thirds of India's urea?
n15a1cc92b7a.x: Procurement is concentrated on rice, wheat and sugarcane, which together account for more than two-thirds of India's urea use.
xa: **MSP + free power** favour rice-wheat (**paddy in Punjab**).
Climate-proofing: procurement must diversify **beyond rice-wheat**, across crops and regions.
The **third phase** of the Green Revolution was marked by **MSP and procurement**.
Fertiliser imbalance N:P:K **10.9:4.1:1** vs ideal **4:2:1**.

nindian-geography-24-16.x: Jowar is grown mainly in peninsular and semi-arid India, led by Maharashtra and Karnataka. The Ganges delta grows rice and jute, the northern plains wheat, and humid coastal Kerala plantation crops.
nindian-geography-24-16.tq: Match the crop's dry-land needs to a region.
n: Jowar is grown in peninsular and semi-arid India. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 80-84]
xs: **Jowar** is grown mainly in **peninsular and semi-arid India** — so option **(2)**.
It needs a **warm climate** and is **comparatively drought tolerant** — one of the major **Kharif millets**.
The **Ganges Delta** is a major **rice** area; the **northern and north-western plains** grow **wheat**.
xa: **Bajra** suits **hot and dry** conditions — **Rajasthan** and other semi-arid regions.
**Ragi** is grown in peninsular India, especially **Karnataka**.
Jowar states: **Maharashtra, Karnataka**; **AP** was marked the major jowar state (APPSC **2025** key).

nworld-geography-21-6.s: Which country is the world's leading producer of maize?
nworld-geography-21-6.x: Maize runs USA > China > Brazil; wheat runs China > India > Russia.
n: Indonesia, Bangladesh, and Vietnam are listed among the world’s top rice producers. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
China ranks ahead of India among the world’s wheat producers. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
India ranks ahead of Russia among the world’s wheat producers. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
Russia, the USA, France, Ukraine, and Australia are listed among the world’s top wheat producers. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
The USA ranks ahead of China among the world’s maize producers. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
China ranks ahead of Brazil among the world’s maize producers. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
Brazil, Argentina, and India are listed among the world’s top maize producers. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
xa: Rice is a major crop of **Monsoon Asia**, needing a **hot and wet climate** and **clayey soil**.
Wheat grows on **temperate grasslands** — **Prairies, Steppes, Pampas**.
Potato: **China** ahead of **India**, India ahead of **Russia**.

n3f2ec9da1db.s: Which of the following is a major cotton-producing State of India?
n3f2ec9da1db.x: The major cotton States are Gujarat, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, mainly in black-soil regions.
xa: Cotton needs **21-37°C**, **50-70 cm** rainfall and **180-200 frost-free days**.
India is **2nd in cotton** in the world.
Cotton = **Silver Fibre Revolution** (Technology Mission on Cotton).
ICAR released **24 cotton** climate-resilient varieties (**22 Bt**) on 5 Jan 2026.

n871627bc45e.s: Which State leads India in both area and production of sugarcane?
n871627bc45e.x: Uttar Pradesh leads in both sugarcane area and production. Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu follow it; they belong to the tropical belt, which has higher yields but a smaller area under cane.
n871627bc45e.tq: Sugarcane: UP first (area and output), then Maharashtra.
xs: **Uttar Pradesh** leads sugarcane in **area and production** — option **(3)**.
**Maharashtra, Karnataka, TN** follow; they are in the **tropical** belt with **higher yield and sucrose**.
xa: North concentration: **fertile alluvium rich in lime + potash**, level land, dense market, **compact blocks**.
**Western UP** = main sugar-mill belt.
Sugarcane gets **FRP**, not MSP.
India is **2nd** in world sugarcane.

n8fe1d0bd0fa.s: Which one of the following crops is associated with a temperature range of approximately 21–37°C, 50–70 cm rainfall and 180–200 frost-free days?
n8fe1d0bd0fa.x: Cotton requires about 21–37°C, 50–70 cm rainfall and 180–200 frost-free days. Black or regur soil is particularly suitable for it.
n8fe1d0bd0fa.tq: Identify the crop from its climatic figures.
xs: **Cotton** needs **21-37°C**, **50-70 cm** rainfall and **180-200 frost-free days** — option **(4)**.
Tea needs **150-300 cm**, coffee **150-250 cm**, rubber **200-300 cm** — far wetter.
xa: Some notes give cotton **21-30°C**.
Soil: deep black **regur** / deep sandy loam, pH **5.8-8.0**.
Black soils have **clay over 62%** and are moisture-retentive.
Leading states: **Gujarat, Maharashtra, Telangana, AP, MP**.

nebc836124b2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about plantation crops in India?
o: Rubber grows on the alluvial flood plains of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta with 50-70 cm of rain
Tea needs about 20-30°C, 150-300 cm of rain and acidic, well-drained hill slopes
Coffee needs about 15-28°C, shade and 150-250 cm of rain
Coffee needs deep, humus-rich, well-drained soil
nebc836124b2.x: Rubber needs a hot humid climate (25-35°C) with heavy rainfall; it is not a crop of the delta flood plains with 50-70 cm rain.
xa: **Cotton** needs **50-70 cm** of rain and **180-200 frost-free days**, on deep black **regur**.
**Sugarcane** is a long-duration crop of **10-15 months**.
Rubber leaders: **Kerala**, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka; India is **5th** in natural rubber.

n792ce1d65a3.s: Jute cultivation is most closely associated with which combination?
o: Cool dry climate and black soils
Cold climate, acidic hill slopes and low rainfall
Semi-arid climate and deep sandy loam
Hot humid climate, heavy rainfall and alluvial flood plains
n792ce1d65a3.x: Jute requires a hot, humid climate, high rainfall and alluvial soils of flood plains, particularly in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta.
n792ce1d65a3.tq: Link a fibre crop with its characteristic physical setting.
xs: Jute needs a **hot, high-humidity** climate, **heavy** rainfall and **alluvial flood plains** of the **Ganga-Brahmaputra delta** — option **(4)**.
Black soils, acidic hill slopes and sandy loam suit **cotton** or **tea**, not jute.
xa: Jute leaders: **West Bengal**, Bihar, Assam.
India is **1st** — the **largest raw jute producer**.
Jute = **Golden Fibre**.
**Jute Packaging Materials Act, 1987**: **100% food grains and 20% sugar** in jute.

n2a3d4d6b0e5.s: Which of the following is a relatively water-efficient crop alternative in Indian agriculture?
n2a3d4d6b0e5.x: Millets, pulses and oilseeds are water-efficient; paddy in Punjab and sugarcane in Maharashtra reflect subsidy distortions.
xa: Sugarcane is a **long-duration** crop of **10-15 months**.
Oilseed area, production and productivity **rose** (ES 2025-26).
ICAR released **13** climate-resilient oilseed varieties.
**Yellow Revolution** = oilseeds.

n59017c9dfd8.s: The laterite soil of the Western Ghats is linked to which crop?
n59017c9dfd8.x: Laterite soil is linked to rubber; jute grows on alluvial flood plains, and black soils suit cotton, chillies and tobacco.
xa: Black soils have **clay over 62%** and retain moisture.
Black soils of **western AP** grow cotton, chillies, tobacco.
Cotton soil is **regur**, pH **5.8-8.0**.
Sugarcane grows on **alluvial/black** soil.

nd7a15f29a3d.s: Plantation crops such as tea, coffee, rubber and coconut are generally:
nd7a15f29a3d.x: Plantation crops need substantial labour and capital; colonial plantations were European-dominated and export-oriented.
xa: Tea began in the **Brahmaputra valley** in the first half of the **19th** century.
**CPCRI** (plantation crops) = **Kasaragod**.
Coffee: **Arabica** + **Robusta** in the Western Ghats.
**Nilgiri Hills** (TN) grow tea and coffee.

n370fbea7b3b.s: The Araku coffee cluster is located in which State?
n370fbea7b3b.x: Araku and the ASR district are AP's coffee clusters; Kodagu is in Karnataka and the Nilgiris in Tamil Nadu.
xa: AP coffee clusters were proposed in APSES **2024-25**.
Karnataka's **Baba Budan hills** saw Arabica introduced.
Coffee needs **15-28°C**, **shade**, **150-250 cm**.
**Coffee Board** = **Bengaluru**.

ndb24aa1ce2c.s: Sugarcane is a long-duration crop of about:
ndb24aa1ce2c.x: Sugarcane takes about 10-15 months, needs hot humid conditions and grows on alluvial or black soil.
xa: **UP** leads in area and production.
Tropical belt has **higher yield and sucrose**.
Sugarcane in **Maharashtra** is cited as a **subsidy distortion**.
ICAR released **6** sugarcane varieties (5 Jan 2026).

n571b7211abf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about cash crops in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Chilli and tobacco are grown in the black-soil belt
Guntur is a major chilli-trade hub
The Tobacco Board is headquartered at Guntur
AP ranks first in turmeric and second in chilli
n571b7211abf.x: The ranks are reversed: AP ranks first in chilli and second in turmeric.
xa: Black soils of **western AP** grow **cotton, chillies, tobacco**.
⚠ **Lakadong turmeric** is from **Meghalaya** (high curcumin).
AP also leads **oil palm** and grows **Araku** coffee.
Black soils have **clay over 62%**.

nb4cdf4c3943.s: Under MIDH, the Centre-State funding ratio for North-Eastern and Himalayan States is:
nb4cdf4c3943.x: MIDH funding is 60:40, and 90:10 for NE and Himalayan States; its sub-schemes include NHM, HMNEH and the National Bamboo Mission.
xa: MIDH lifted productivity to **12.56 MT/ha**.
Horticulture (**362-367 MT**) now exceeds food grains.
**AP** is India's largest fruit producer (**15.6%**).

nd0cf34deebb.s: Lakadong, a high-curcumin turmeric variety, belongs to:
nd0cf34deebb.x: Lakadong turmeric is from Meghalaya, which also leads in pineapple; Arunachal grows over half of India's kiwi.
xa: **Arunachal Kiwi Mission** runs under **Ashtalakshmi** (May 2026).
Lakadong is known for **high curcumin**.
**AP** is the largest fruit producer (**15.6%**).
**HMNEH** under MIDH covers **11 states**.

n6244a16f836.s: Indian jute goods face export competition mainly from:
n6244a16f836.x: Bangladesh competes with Indian jute goods in exports, while cotton competes with synthetic fibres.
xa: India is **2nd** in cotton and **1st** in jute.
Jute push (Sep 2026): jute-viscose apparel with **NIFT**.
Cotton = **Silver Fibre**; jute = **Golden Fibre**.
**Jute Corporation of India** buys raw jute at **MSP**.

nindian-geography-24-26.s: Which one of the following combinations is correct?
o: Red chilli — hot and dry conditions — Rajasthan
Red chilli — warm climate — Andhra Pradesh
Red chilli — cool season — northern India
Red chilli — warm and humid climate — Ganges Delta
nindian-geography-24-26.x: Red chilli needs a warm climate and is a major crop of Andhra Pradesh.
nindian-geography-24-26.tq: Recall the needs and regions of each crop.
n: Red chilli requires a warm climate. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 80-84]
Andhra Pradesh is an important chilli-growing region. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 80-84]
xs: **Red chilli — warm climate — Andhra Pradesh** is the correct combination — option **(2)**.
**Andhra Pradesh** is an **important chilli-growing region**; AP ranks **1st in chillies** (APSES 2024-25).
**Hot and dry** conditions suit **bajra**; the **Ganges Delta** suits **jute**.
xa: **Guntur** is the **chilli-trade hub** and seat of the **Tobacco Board**.
AP's **black-soil belt** grows chillies and tobacco.
AP is **2nd in turmeric** among states.

nworld-geography-21-3.s: Sugar mills are located near the cane fields because sugarcane is a:
nworld-geography-21-3.x: Cane loses weight and sugar after cutting, so mills are located near the fields.
n: Sugarcane mills are located near the fields. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
Sugarcane is a weight-losing crop. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
xa: Sugarcane needs a **hot and humid** climate, **heavy rainfall** or **irrigation** and **fertile soil**.
Producers: **Brazil > India > China**, with Thailand listed.
India is **2nd** in sugarcane.

nworld-geography-21-16.s: Which is a major jute-producing delta region of the world?
nworld-geography-21-16.x: Jute grows in hot, humid deltas, which is why the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta leads.
n: Jute grows in hot, humid delta regions. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
The Ganga–Brahmaputra region is a major jute-producing delta region. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]
xa: Jute producers: **India** ahead of **Bangladesh**.
Indian jute leaders: **West Bengal**, Bihar, Assam.
⚠ **Golden Fibre** = jute.

ne098b5c1f5e.s: Tea plantations in India began in the first half of the nineteenth century in the:
ne098b5c1f5e.x: The first tea plantations were begun in the first half of the nineteenth century in the Brahmaputra Valley of Assam.
ne098b5c1f5e.tq: Link the historical origin of plantation tea with its geographical valley rather than with a hill region.
xs: Tea plantations began in the **first half of the 19th century** in the **Brahmaputra Valley (Assam)** (APPSC-G2 2025) — option **(4)**.
The **Nilgiri Hills** grow tea and coffee but were not the first.
xa: **Assam** is the leading tea state.
**Darjeeling Tea** = India's **first GI-tagged product**.
West Bengal tea areas: **Darjeeling, Dooars**.
Colonial plantations were **European-dominated, export-oriented**.

nc13701b89ed.s: In India, inland fisheries contribute more than what proportion of total fish output?

n2628dbe4119.s: Kolleru Lake, the largest freshwater lake in Andhra Pradesh, lies between the deltas of:

Breeding ground of the **spot-billed pelican**, also painted storks.
Sanctuary limit: the **+5 ft contour**.

n691becc3914.s: Kolleru Wildlife Sanctuary is associated with which of the following bird species as a breeding ground?

xa: **Ramsar site** since **2002**.
Sanctuary limit **+5 ft contour**.
