The **Sonnagar-Dankuni PPP** failed.

nef52017d1bb.s: The 1,506-km Western Dedicated Freight Corridor is funded by:
nef52017d1bb.x: The Western DFC is JICA-funded; the 1,337-km Eastern DFC is World Bank-funded.
xa: Eastern: **Ludhiana-Sonnagar** (**1,337 km**); Western: **Dadri-JNPT** (**1,506 km**).
Full **2,843 km** network operational.

n0c71cf569a9.s: Which railway carries Bailadila iron ore to Visakhapatnam port through tunnels in the Eastern Ghats?
n0c71cf569a9.x: The Kottavalasa–Kirandul railway carries Bailadila iron ore to Visakhapatnam port through tunnels in the Eastern Ghats.
n0c71cf569a9.tq: Match the mineral source, railway and port.
xs: The **Kottavalasa–Kirandul** (KK) line carries **Bailadila iron ore** to **Visakhapatnam port** — option **(2)** is correct.
It runs through **Eastern Ghats** tunnels.
**Guntakal-Ballari** links Rayalaseema to Karnataka and Goa, not Bailadila.
xa: **South Coast Railway** (**18th zone**) has its HQ at **Visakhapatnam**.
Rail also carries cement, granite, minerals to **Gangavaram** and **Krishnapatnam**.

ncb7fe665851.s: Which public-private partnership project is described as having failed?
ncb7fe665851.x: The Sonnagar–Dankuni PPP is identified as a failed project.
ncb7fe665851.tq: Directly match the project with the reported outcome while avoiding confusion with other connectivity projects.
xs: The **Sonnagar-Dankuni** PPP is cited as a **failed** project — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Guntakal-Ballari** 3rd & 4th lines were **approved** by the **CCEA** (Jul 2026) — a current project, not a failed PPP.
**Sonnagar** is the end point of the **Eastern DFC** (**Ludhiana-Sonnagar**, **1,337 km**).
xa: **Eastern DFC** = **World Bank**-funded; **Western DFC** (**Dadri-JNPT**, **1,506 km**) = **JICA**-funded.
The full **2,843 km** DFC network became operational on **10 Sep 2026**.
Guntakal-Ballari lines: **₹1,264 crore**, **+16.22 MTPA**, target **2028-29**.
Other debate: the logistics-cost figure (**7.97% vs 13-14%**).

n5128f95a820.s: Approximately what share of India's transhipment cargo passes through Colombo or Singapore?
n5128f95a820.x: About 75% of India's transhipment cargo passes through Colombo or Singapore.
n5128f95a820.tq: Distinguish the transhipment concentration figure from the larger sea-route share of total trade.
xs: **75%** of India's transhipment cargo goes via **Colombo** or **Singapore** — option **(3)** is correct.
**95%** is the sea share of trade by volume, not transhipment.
xa: AP: **Ramayapatnam port** **74.34%** built (Oct 2025).
Four greenfield ports in AP to add **145 MTPA by 2030**.

nc7c647dc512.s: Which of the following was the correct order of major ports in terms of cargo handled in FY 2026, beginning with the highest?
nc7c647dc512.x: Deendayal Port led with 160.11 MT, followed by Paradip and JNPA in FY 2026.
nc7c647dc512.tq: Use ranking order and begin with the port explicitly associated with the highest volume.
xs: **Deendayal (Kandla)** led with **160.11 MT**, then **Paradip**, then **JNPA** — option **(1)** is correct.
Options (2)-(4) misplace Deendayal or swap Paradip and JNPA.
xa: Top non-major port: **Krishnapatnam** (**41.09 MMT**).
Sea routes carry **~95%** of trade by volume.

nc64629a7005.s: In LEADS 2023, Andhra Pradesh was placed in which category among coastal States?
nc64629a7005.x: Andhra Pradesh was classified as an 'Achiever' among coastal States in LEADS 2023.
nc64629a7005.tq: Directly identify the precise ranking category rather than confusing it with the categories of other States.
xs: AP was an "**Achiever**" in **LEADS 2023** — option **(2)** is correct.
LEADS is run by **DPIIT** (since **2018**).
xa: LEADS 2025 coastal top performer: **Tamil Nadu**.
It combines **perception + objective data**.

n64adc844421.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's logistics sector?
o: The official logistics cost is 7.97% of GDP (2023-24)
NLP 2022 targets a single-digit logistics cost
NLP 2022 aims for a top-25 LPI rank by 2030
India ranked 25th in the World Bank LPI 2023
n64adc844421.x: India ranked 38th in LPI 2023; a top-25 rank is only the NLP target for 2030.
xa: **LEADS** (DPIIT, since **2018**) ranks States; ⚠ **LPI** = World Bank.
LEADS 2025 leaders: **Tamil Nadu** (coastal), **UP** (landlocked), **Mizoram** (NE), **Delhi** (UT).
AP was an "**Achiever**" in **2023**.

n405a5ed531d.s: The National Rail Plan targets what share of freight for rail transport by 2030?
n405a5ed531d.x: Rail currently carries about 27% of freight, while the National Rail Plan targets a 45% share by 2030.
n405a5ed531d.tq: Distinguish the present freight share from the future policy target.
xs: The **National Rail Plan** targets a **45%** rail freight share **by 2030** — option **(3)** is correct.
Rail's present share is only **~27%**.
xa: Rail emits **~90% less CO2** than road.
**99.6%** of broad gauge is electrified (May **2026**).

n7c46d9f6c76.s: Which one of the following is identified as a criticism or debate concerning India's logistics sector?
o: Sea routes carry less than 10% of India's trade by volume.
The official logistics-cost estimate is disputed against the older 13–14% figure.
Rail freight already accounts for 90% of total freight.
The National Logistics Policy excludes technology and skills.
n7c46d9f6c76.x: The logistics-cost estimate of 7.97% is debated in comparison with the older 13–14% figure. The other statements contradict the stated transport and policy facts.
n7c46d9f6c76.tq: Identify the genuine criticism while rejecting statements that reverse established sectoral facts.
xs: The **logistics-cost figure is disputed**: the official **7.97% of GDP (2023-24)** against the older **13-14%** figure — so option **(2)** is correct.
Sea routes carry **~95%** of India's trade by volume, not less than **10%** — option (1) is wrong.
Rail's share of freight is only **~27%**, not **90%** — option (3) is wrong.
The **National Logistics Policy 2022** explicitly improves **processes, regulation, skills, technology** — option (4) is wrong.
xa: Another debate: the **Sonnagar-Dankuni PPP** failed.
**NLP 2022** targets (by **2030**): **single-digit logistics cost** and a **Top 25** rank in the **LPI**.
India ranked **38th** in the World Bank **LPI (2023)**.
⚠ **LPI** = World Bank (countries); **LEADS** = **DPIIT** (States), begun **2018**.

ne89b269343b.x: The Orient Express linked Paris and Istanbul.
xa: **Union Pacific** = first US transcontinental line (**1869**).
**Trans-Australian** = **Sydney - Perth**.
ne89b269343b.fixed: Canadian Pacific runs Montreal-Vancouver, not Halifax-Vancouver (y2c53e544585); so B, C, D only

nworld-geography-17-1.s: Which railway runs from Moscow to Vladivostok in Russia and is the longest continuous railway?
nworld-geography-17-1.x: The Trans-Siberian Railway runs from Moscow to Vladivostok. Qinghai–Tibet is the highest railway and the Orient Express a luxury train.
nworld-geography-17-1.tq: Recall the route of each railway.
n: The Trans-Siberian Railway runs from Moscow to Vladivostok in Russia. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 27-29]
The Trans-Siberian Railway is the longest continuous railway. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 27-29]
The Trans-Siberian Railway is the longest single railway line. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 27-29]
xs: The **Trans-Siberian Railway** runs **Moscow** to **Vladivostok** — the longest continuous railway, option **(3)**.
It is about **9,289 km** long and crosses **8 time zones**.
**Qinghai–Tibet** is the **highest railway**; the **Orient Express** is a **luxury train**; the **Canadian Pacific** is Canada's first transcontinental line.
xa: Built mainly **between 1891 and 1916**.
The **Baikal–Amur Mainline** runs **parallel** to it.
APPSC G1 **2024** asked its end points: **Moscow to Vladivostok**.

nworld-geography-17-5.s: The Trans-Siberian Railway was built mainly between:
nworld-geography-17-5.x: The Trans-Siberian Railway was built mainly in 1891–1916; the Baikal–Amur Mainline runs parallel to it.
n: The Baikal–Amur Mainline is parallel to the Trans-Siberian Railway. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 27-29]
The Channel Tunnel, also called the Eurotunnel, connects the United Kingdom and France under the English Channel. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 27-29]
The Trans-Siberian Railway was built mainly between 1891 and 1916. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 27-29]
xa: The Channel Tunnel carries **rail** and **road transport**.
The Trans-Siberian aided **Russian expansion** and the development of **Siberia**.
**US Transcontinental Railroad** was completed in **1869**.

nworld-geography-17-6.s: The Trans-Siberian Railway, which crosses 8 time zones, is how long?
nworld-geography-17-6.x: The Trans-Siberian Railway is 9,289 km long and crosses 8 time zones.
n: The Trans-Siberian Railway is approximately 9,289 km long. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 27-29]
The Trans-Siberian Railway crosses 8 time zones. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 27-29]
The Trans-Siberian Railway has strategic and economic significance. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 27-29]
xa: It runs **Moscow** to **Vladivostok**.
Built mainly **between 1891 and 1916**.
**Trans-Australian** (**Sydney - Perth**) has the world's longest straight track (**478 km**).

nworld-geography-17-14.s: Which railway was the first transcontinental railway in North America and was completed in 1869?
nworld-geography-17-14.x: The US Transcontinental Railroad, finished in 1869, was North America's first transcontinental line. The Canadian Pacific came in 1885.
n: The first transcontinental railway in North America was the US Transcontinental Railroad. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 27-29]
The US Transcontinental Railroad was completed in 1869. [World Geography · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 27-29]
xs: The **US Transcontinental Railroad**, completed in **1869**, was the first transcontinental railway in **North America** — option **(4)**.
The **Canadian Pacific** was **Canada's first** transcontinental railway (**Montreal** to **Vancouver**).
The **Trans-Siberian** is in **Russia**, not North America.
xa: **Union Pacific**: **New York - San Francisco**.
**Trans-Canadian Railway** runs **across Canada**.
**Canadian National Railway** runs **Atlantic** to **Pacific**.

n5a3120ee8de.s: Curiosity-driven inquiry is a characteristic of:
n5a3120ee8de.x: Basic research is curiosity-driven; applied research addresses a set problem and technology produces products and processes.
xa: **Translational research** takes lab results to use.
**Invention** = first creation of a product/process; **innovation** = turning it into value in market or society.
The future lies in **interdisciplinary and translational research** (**2026**).

n54a9294167f.s: Turning an invention into value in the market or society is called:
n54a9294167f.x: Innovation turns an invention (the first creation of a product or process) into market or social value.
xa: The **first objective** of the STI Policy 2013 was to **spread scientific temper**.
The **SPR 1958** resolved to **"foster, promote and sustain"** science.
STI phases: **1980s** self-reliance; **2010s** innovation; now **AI, quantum, semiconductors**.

nc97337b2e99.s: In the scientific method, which stage comes immediately after framing the question?
nc97337b2e99.x: The sequence is observation, question, hypothesis, experiment, analysis and conclusion.
xa: After the conclusion comes **replication/peer review**.
**Theory** = well-tested explanation of **why**; **law** = description (often mathematical) of **what** always happens, e.g. **Newton's laws**.
⚠ **Trap:** a theory does not "become" a law.

ncaac9e9d39f.s: A claim that asserts scientific status without being testable is:
ncaac9e9d39f.x: Pseudoscience claims scientific status while lacking testability; science is systematic, self-correcting and reproducible.
xa: Per astrophysicist **J.V. Narlikar**, **astrology** has **not** been considered a science (**UPPSC 2018**).
Scientific method ends with **replication/peer review** after the conclusion.
⚠ **Trap:** a **theory** does not "become" a **law**.

n0c5a291309b.s: Which one of the following groups contains only branches classified as natural sciences?
o: Agriculture, medicine, logic, statistics and geography
Physics, chemistry, biology, earth science and space science
Mathematics, logic, statistics, engineering and medicine
Engineering, mathematics, computing, medicine and agriculture
n0c5a291309b.x: Natural sciences include physics, chemistry, biology, earth science and space science. Mathematics, logic and statistics are formal sciences, while engineering, medicine and agriculture are applied fields.
n0c5a291309b.tq: Classify every option by the branch of science before selecting the complete group.
xs: **Natural sciences** are **physics, chemistry, biology, earth, space** — option **(2)**.
**Mathematics, logic, statistics** are **formal** sciences.
**Engineering, medicine, agriculture** are **applied** sciences — so options (1), (3) and (4) mix in non-natural branches.
xa: **Geoinformatics** = geography + IT (**GIS, RS, GPS**).
**Data science** = statistics + computing; **biotechnology** = biology + engineering.
**ESSO (2007, MoES)** covers ocean, atmospheric and climate science, geoscience, polar science and cryosphere.

nf2c663153b3.s: Digital embossing is particularly useful for producing which of the following for persons with visual impairment?
nf2c663153b3.x: Digital embossing produces raised tactile printing and is used for braille maps for visually impaired persons.
nf2c663153b3.tq: Identify the distinctive application associated with a specialised technology.
xs: **Digital embossing** is used for **braille maps** for the visually impaired — option **(3)** (**APPSC-G1 2022**).
It gives raised (tactile) printing **without chemicals or solvents, no pollutants**.
RFID ID cards use **radio waves**; 3D models come from **additive manufacturing** — not embossing.
xa: **3D printing** builds an object **layer by layer** from a digital model.
**Geospatial technology** = **GIS, GPS/GNSS, remote sensing**.
**Wearables** may even be **implanted or tattooed on skin**, part of **IoT**.

ne05b125fb6d.s: The process in which an object is built layer by layer from a digital model is known as:
ne05b125fb6d.x: Three-dimensional printing is an additive manufacturing process in which an object is constructed layer by layer from a digital model.
ne05b125fb6d.tq: Match the process description with the precise technical term.
xs: Building an object **layer by layer** from a digital model is **additive manufacturing** (**3D printing**) — option **(1)**.
**Remote sensing** is part of **geospatial** technology; **biometric authentication** uses physical traits; **digital embossing** makes raised tactile print.
xa: **Digital embossing** works **without chemicals or solvents** — used for **braille maps** (**APPSC-G1 2022**).
**Geospatial technology** = **GIS, GPS/GNSS, remote sensing**.
**Wearables** combine **sensors + software + wireless**, part of **IoT**.

n99830d7abee.x: FASTag is a passive RFID tag powered by the toll reader's field; a metro smart card is passive NFC.
xa: **NFC** works at **13.56 MHz** with a range of about **4 cm**.
⚠ **RFID** (FASTag) = no line of sight, longer reach; **NFC** = about **4 cm** only.
**Biometrics** identifies people by fingerprint, iris, face.

n4c2f5c2851f.s: The Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme finances projects beginning at which Technology Readiness Level?
n4c2f5c2851f.x: The RDI Scheme finances projects at TRL 4 and above, along with strategic technologies and a Deep-Tech Fund of Funds.
n4c2f5c2851f.tq: Use the threshold figure to distinguish the scheme from early-stage basic research support.
xs: Projects are financed at **TRL 4 and above** — option **(3)**.
Per the notes, the **ANRF Governing Board** finances projects at **TRL 4 and above**, plus **strategic technologies** and a **Deep-Tech Fund of Funds**.
**TRL 4** is where **validation in lab and relevant environment** begins (TRL 4-6), after **TRL 1-3** lab proof of concept.
xa: **TRL 7-9:** operational demonstration → **proven in actual use**.
**Deep-tech start-up eligibility** was notified in **Feb 2026**; convener **JS DPIIT**.
TRLs are of **NASA origin**.

n613bb2f102e.s: Which Article asks citizens to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform?
n613bb2f102e.x: Article 51A(h), added by the 42nd Amendment (1976), carries this duty; Nehru popularised the phrase 'scientific temper'.
xa: **Statement on Scientific Temper** — **1981**.
**Kerala Sastra Sahitya Parishad** — **1962**.
The **STI Policy 2013**'s first objective was to **spread scientific temper**.

nbcbfd1caa79.s: Vigyan Jyoti is primarily intended to encourage which group in STEM fields?
nbcbfd1caa79.x: Vigyan Jyoti is intended to encourage girls to pursue Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics.
nbcbfd1caa79.tq: Identify the target beneficiaries of the scheme rather than its implementing institution.
xs: **Vigyan Jyoti** encourages **meritorious girls** of **Classes 9-12** in STEM — option **(2) Girls**.
It runs with the **Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti**.
xa: ⚠ **INSPIRE** is for all young students, not girls-only; **Vigyan Jyoti** = girls only.
**INSPIRE (DST)**: **3.75 lakh** beneficiaries in five years; **no competitive exam**.
**National Science Day** (**28 Feb**) is for science popularisation.

n6ea9df1ce0a.s: India's rank in the Global Innovation Index 2025 was:
n6ea9df1ce0a.x: India ranked 38th in the GII 2025; it was 49th in the Network Readiness Index 2024.
xa: STI phases now focus on **AI, quantum, semiconductors**.
India rose from **5th to 3rd** in nanoscience publications.
STI phase of the **2010s** = innovation, after **1980s** self-reliance.

nchemistry-8-8.s: Which pair of monomers forms Nylon-2-Nylon-6?
nchemistry-8-8.x: Nylon-2-Nylon-6 is made from glycine and aminocaproic acid and is biodegradable. Nylon-6,6 uses hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid.
nchemistry-8-8.tq: Recall the monomers of each nylon.
n: Nylon-6 is formed from caprolactam. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
Melamine-formaldehyde is formed from melamine and formaldehyde. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
Glyptal is formed from ethylene glycol and phthalic acid. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
Nylon-2-Nylon-6 is formed from glycine and amino caproic acid. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
xs: **Nylon-2-Nylon-6** is formed from **glycine and amino caproic acid**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Caprolactam** forms **Nylon-6**; **ethylene glycol and phthalic acid** form **Glyptal**.
**Melamine and formaldehyde** form **melamine-formaldehyde** resin.
xa: **Nylon-6,6** is formed from **hexamethylenediamine** and **adipic acid**.
**PHBV** is formed from **3-hydroxybutanoic acid** and **3-hydroxypentanoic acid**.
**Terylene** is formed from **ethylene glycol** and **terephthalic acid**.

nchemistry-8-11.x: Neoprene is made from chloroprene; natural rubber is from isoprene.
n: Polypropene (PP) is formed from propene (CH₃–CH=CH₂). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
Natural rubber is formed from isoprene (2-methyl-1,3-butadiene). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
Neoprene is formed from chloroprene (2-chloro-1,3-butadiene). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
Nylon-6,6 is formed from hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
xa: Natural rubber is **cis-1,4-polyisoprene**; isoprene is **2-methyl-1,3-butadiene**.
Chloroprene is **2-chloro-1,3-butadiene**.
**Nylon-6** is formed from **caprolactam**.

nchemistry-8-18.s: PHBV is formed from which pair of monomers?
nchemistry-8-18.x: PHBV is made from 3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid and is biodegradable. Terylene, nylon-6,6 and nylon-2-nylon-6 use the other pairs.
n: PHBV is formed from 3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 30-33]
xs: **PHBV** is formed from **3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid** form **Terylene (PET)**.
**Hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid** form **Nylon-6,6**; **glycine and amino caproic acid** form **Nylon-2-Nylon-6**.
xa: **Bakelite** is formed from **phenol** and **formaldehyde**.
**Buna-S** is formed from **1,3-butadiene** and **styrene**.
**Glyptal** is formed from **ethylene glycol** and **phthalic acid**.

nbiology-24-1.s: Vitamin B7 is also known as:
nbiology-24-1.x: B7 is biotin (vitamin H); B1 is thiamine, B2 riboflavin and B12 cobalamin.
n: Vitamin B1 is chemically called thiamine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B2 is chemically called riboflavin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B7 is chemically called biotin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B7 is also called vitamin H. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B12 is chemically called cobalamin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B12 is chemically called cyanocobalamin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
xa: B1 deficiency: **beri-beri**; B12 deficiency: **pernicious anaemia**.
B7 deficiency: **skin disease**, **hair fall**.
B2 deficiency: **cheilosis**, **glossitis**, **ariboflavinosis**.

nbiology-24-4.s: Which of the following vitamins is water-soluble?
nbiology-24-4.x: B9 (like B1 and C) is water-soluble; vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble.
n: Vitamin B1 is water-soluble. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B9 is water-soluble. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin C is water-soluble. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin D is associated with fat. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin K is fat-soluble. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
xa: Fat-soluble vitamins: **A, D, E, K**.
**B9 (folic acid)** deficiency: **anaemia**, **growth retardation**.
**Vitamin C (ascorbic acid)** aids **iron absorption** and **wound healing**.

nbiology-24-6.x: B6 is pyridoxine; B3 is niacin, B5 pantothenic acid and A retinol.
n: Vitamin A is chemically called retinol. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B3 is chemically called niacin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B5 is chemically called pantothenic acid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin B6 is chemically called pyridoxine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
xa: Vitamin A deficiency: **night blindness**, **xerophthalmia**.
B3 deficiency: **pellagra**.
B6 functions in **amino-acid metabolism**.

nbiology-24-15.x: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid. Cobalamin is B12, calciferol D and folic acid B9.
nbiology-24-15.tq: Recall the chemical names of vitamins.
n: Vitamin C is chemically called ascorbic acid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
xs: Vitamin C is chemically **ascorbic acid**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Cobalamin** is **B12**; **calciferol** is **vitamin D**; **folic acid** is **B9**.
xa: Vitamin C functions: **collagen**, **wound healing**, **iron absorption**, **antioxidant**.
Deficiency: **scurvy**, **bleeding gums**.
**Amla** is the **richest source** of vitamin C.

nbiology-24-17.x: D3 is cholecalciferol; D2 is ergocalciferol.
n: Vitamin D is chemically called calciferol. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin D2 is chemically called ergocalciferol. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin D3 is chemically called cholecalciferol. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
xa: Vitamin D deficiency also causes **osteomalacia** and **osteoporosis** — **soft or weak bones**.
Vitamin D functions in **calcium** and **bone metabolism**.
McCollum **helped discover** **vitamins B and D**.

nbiology-24-22.x: Vitamin K is chemically a naphthoquinone. Calciferol is D, tocopherol E and ascorbic acid C.
nbiology-24-22.tq: Recall the chemical names of vitamins.
n: Vitamin K is chemically called naphthoquinone. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
xs: Vitamin K is chemically **naphthoquinone**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**Calciferol** is **vitamin D**; **tocopherol** is **vitamin E**; **ascorbic acid** is **vitamin C**.
xa: Vitamin K functions in **blood clotting**.
Its deficiency gives **prolonged clotting time** and **bleeding**.
Vitamin K is **fat**-soluble.

nbiology-24-23.s: Night blindness and xerophthalmia are caused by deficiency of:
nbiology-24-23.x: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness, xerophthalmia and skin keratinisation.
n: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin A deficiency causes xerophthalmia. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
Vitamin A deficiency causes skin keratinization. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 41-42]
xa: Vitamin A is **retinol**; functions: **vision**, **epithelial tissue**, **immunity**.
Vitamin A is **fat**-soluble.
Sources: **carrot**; **mango** — richest among the given fruits.

nbiology-21-1.x: Niacin deficiency causes pellagra; B1 causes beriberi, C scurvy and D rickets.
n: Vitamin B1 deficiency causes beriberi. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 35-37]

nchemistry-14-8.s: Which process is used for desalination of sea water and purification of water by removing ions and bacteria?

xs: **Reverse osmosis** desalinates seawater and purifies water, so option **(1)** is correct.

xa: **Plant roots** absorb water by **osmosis**.

The ovaries produce estrogen. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 47-49]
The ovaries produce progesterone. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #29 · pp 47-49]
xa: **Placenta** produces **chorionic gonadotropin**.
Pituitary **FSH** and **LH** are tropic hormones.
**Adrenal cortex** also secretes **androgens**.

nphysics-11-17.s: Which of the following is associated with Conservation of Momentum?
o: Recoil of a gun and rocket propulsion
nphysics-11-17.x: Gun recoil and rocket propulsion conserve momentum: the forward momentum of bullet or exhaust equals the backward momentum of the gun or rocket.
nphysics-11-17.tq: Recall the applications of momentum conservation.
n: The Conservation of Momentum explains recoil of a gun. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
The Conservation of Momentum explains rocket propulsion. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
The Conservation of Momentum explains recoil of a gun. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
The Conservation of Momentum explains rocket launch. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 25-31]
xs: Conservation of Momentum explains the **recoil of a gun and rocket propulsion**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Hydraulic lift and syringe** follow **Pascal's Principle**, not momentum conservation.
xa: **Conservation of Angular Momentum** explains **ice-skater spin** and **planetary orbits**.
**Conservation of Energy** applies to **roller coasters**, **pendulums** and **power generation**.
**Bernoulli's Principle** explains **lift on an aeroplane wing**.

nphysics-18-65.s: What is the optical action of a burning glass on sun rays?
nphysics-18-65.x: A burning glass is a convex lens that converges sun rays to a point and can ignite paper.
nphysics-18-65.tq: Recall that a convex lens converges light.
n: A burning glass converges sun rays. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 64-76]
xs: A burning glass **converges** sun rays, so option **(3)** is correct.
A **burning glass** is a **convex** lens — it **converges sun rays**.
xa: A convex lens is also a **magnifying glass** — a **virtual magnified image** with the object within F.
A **concave** lens **diverges** rays — used in spectacles for **myopia**.
A convex lens has **positive** power.

nphysics-16-1.s: What is the SI unit of resistivity?
nphysics-16-1.x: Resistivity is measured in ohm-metre (Ω m), since ρ = RA/l. Ohm is for resistance and S/m is for conductivity.
nphysics-16-1.tq: Discriminate resistance, resistivity and conductivity units.
n: The SI unit of resistivity is the ohm-metre (Ω m). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The SI unit of potential difference or voltage is the volt (V). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The SI unit of resistance is the ohm (Ω). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The SI unit of conductivity is the siemens per metre (S/m). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
xs: The SI unit of resistivity is the **ohm-metre (Ω m)**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ohm (Ω)** is the unit of **resistance**; **volt (V)** is the unit of **potential difference**.
**Siemens per metre (S/m)** is the unit of **conductivity**.
xa: Resistivity is also expressed in **ohm-centimetres (Ω cm)**.
**Conductivity** is the **reciprocal of resistivity** — **σ = 1/ρ**.
**Conductance** = **1/R**, unit **siemens (S)**, older unit **mho**.

nphysics-16-19.s: The SI unit of conductivity is:
nphysics-16-19.x: Conductivity (1/ρ) is measured in S/m; siemens is the unit of conductance.
n: Resistivity is also measured in ohm-centimetres (Ω cm). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The SI unit of conductivity is the siemens per metre (S/m). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
Conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity (σ = 1/ρ). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
The SI unit of conductance is the siemens (S). [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
xa: SI unit of **resistivity** is the **ohm-metre (Ω m)**.
**Conductance** = **1/R**; older unit **mho**.
⚠ **Conductivity** (S/m) is the reciprocal of **resistivity**; **conductance** (S) is the reciprocal of **resistance**.

n9f755ffee7f.s: Hydrogels find application in which of the following groups?
o: Contact lenses, wound dressings, diapers and drug delivery
Solar cells, transformers, magnets and satellites
Brake fluids, cement, glass and steel
Tyres, batteries, optical fibres and semiconductors only
n9f755ffee7f.x: Hydrogels are water-absorbing polymers used in contact lenses, wound dressings, diapers and drug delivery.
n9f755ffee7f.tq: Match the smart material with its cluster of daily-life applications.
xs: **Hydrogels** are used in **contact lenses, wound dressings, diapers, drug delivery** — option **(1)**.
They are **water-absorbing polymers**.
xa: **Accelerometer (MEMS)** senses sudden deceleration to **trigger airbags**.
**Graphene oxide sensor**: low-cost flexible sensor with **pencil-drawn electrodes** (**VIS 2026**).
**Flexible batteries** power **wearables and flexible displays**.

n7d11bc3c2ef.s: India's own satellite-based navigation system is known as
n7d11bc3c2ef.x: NavIC is India's own satellite-based navigation system and supports location-related services.
n7d11bc3c2ef.tq: Distinguish the national navigation system from transport communication standards and health platforms.
xs: India's own satellite navigation system is **NavIC** — option **(4)**.
**DSRC** and **C-V2X** are vehicle-communication technologies; **IHIP** is a disease-surveillance platform.
xa: **GPS tracking** powers **location-based services**.
⚠ **C-V2X** = 4G/5G; **DSRC** = Wi-Fi-based.
**FASTag** = passive RFID; metro cards = passive NFC.

nc7b14060634.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's S&T policies?
o: SPR 1958, under Nehru, was the first comprehensive S&T policy
TPS 1983, under Indira Gandhi, stressed technological self-reliance
The STI Policy, 2013 was issued under Manmohan Singh
The S&T Policy, 2003 was issued under Manmohan Singh
nc7b14060634.x: The S&T Policy, 2003 came under A.B. Vajpayee; Manmohan Singh's was the STI Policy, 2013.
xa: ⚠ **1958 – 1983 – 2003 – 2013 – 2020** = **Nehru – Indira Gandhi – Vajpayee – Manmohan Singh – Modi**.
**Draft STIP 2020** is India's **5th** S&T policy, with **bottom-up** consultation.
**STI 2013** made **innovation** central — "**Science, Technology and Innovation for the People**".
SPR 1958 came during the **Second Plan (1956-61)**; **DRDO** was formed the same year.

nc7b3108e1c5.s: STIP 2020 is India's ____ national science and technology policy.
nc7b3108e1c5.x: SPR 1958 was the first national S&T policy and STIP 2020 the fifth.
xa: STIP 2020 used a decentralised, **bottom-up** consultation.
STIP 2020 stressed **Atmanirbhar Bharat**, **open science**, **gender equity**.

n9242285238a.s: The Draft STIP 2020 proposed which approach to research governance?
n9242285238a.x: Draft STIP 2020 proposed decentralised, bottom-up governance with self-reliance, open science and equity.
xa: STIP 2020 is India's **5th** national S&T policy, under **Narendra Modi**.
Vision: India among the **top three scientific superpowers** in the coming decade.
**Open Science Framework**: **"One Nation, One Subscription"**, **FAIR** data, **INDSTA** portal.

n92f134d467f.s: Which one of the following was NOT an outcome of the Draft STIP 2020?
n92f134d467f.x: Atal Innovation Mission was not an outcome of STIP 2020; it was set up by NITI Aayog in 2016 as a separate initiative promoting innovation among students. ONOS and RIEF were associated with the draft policy proposals.
n92f134d467f.tq: Use the separate-initiative trap: identify the programme established outside the policy.
xs: **Atal Innovation Mission** was NOT an outcome of STIP 2020 — option **(1)** (**BPSC 2025**).
**AIM** was set up by **NITI Aayog in 2016** as a separate initiative promoting innovation among students.
**ONOS** and **RIEF** were outcomes; open science was part of its **Open Science Framework**.
xa: ONOS was approved by Cabinet in **Nov 2024** (about **₹6,000 crore**).
**NITI Aayog** also publishes the **India Innovation Index**.
Exam angle: "which is **NOT** an outcome/objective" of a given policy.

n9ca46ecc29d.s: Who is the President of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF)?
n9ca46ecc29d.x: The Prime Minister is ANRF's President; the Ministers of S&T and Education are Vice-Presidents.
xa: ANRF is statutory under the **ANRF Act, 2023**.
About **₹36,000 crore** of its funds is expected from **non-government sources**.
The **RDI Fund** runs through a **Special Purpose Fund** in ANRF.

nc1b7038f594.s: Which of the following is a role of State Councils of Science and Technology such as APCOST?
o: Issuing national patents and regulating all Union laboratories
Framing state science and technology policy, providing research grants and popularising science
Serving as the statutory governing council of ANRF
Determining India’s Global Innovation Index methodology
nc1b7038f594.x: State S&T councils frame state S&T policy, provide research grants and popularise science. They do not perform the national statutory functions of ANRF or NITI Aayog.
nc1b7038f594.tq: Apply the state-level institutional role to the functions listed.
xs: State S&T councils **frame state S&T policy, give research grants, popularise science** — option **(2)**.
**APCOST** = **Andhra Pradesh Council of Science and Technology**, under AP's **Environment, Forests, Science and Technology** department.
ANRF governance and **GII** work belong to national bodies (**PM-led ANRF**, **NITI Aayog**).
xa: APCOST gets support under DST's **State S&T Programme**.
AP angle: **DST-STI Hub** at **SPMVV, Tirupati** for **SC/ST women** (3-year project, **Jul 2026**).
Tamil Nadu's council works on translating academic research into use.

n76d3a26e63c.s: APCOST functions under which department of the Government of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Industries, Commerce and Information Technology Department
Higher Education and Skill Development Department
Environment, Forests, Science and Technology Department
n76d3a26e63c.x: APCOST works under the Andhra Pradesh Environment, Forests, Science and Technology Department.
n76d3a26e63c.tq: Use the department-name distinction to avoid a neighbouring-department trap.
xs: **APCOST** works under AP's **Environment, Forests, Science and Technology** department — option **(4)**.
APCOST = **Andhra Pradesh Council of Science and Technology**.
xa: It gets support under DST's **State S&T Programme**.
State S&T councils **frame state S&T policy, give research grants, popularise science**.
AP angle: **DST-STI Hub** at **SPMVV, Tirupati** for **SC/ST women** (**Jul 2026**).

nd1cfcb0e77b.s: The STI Policy, 2013 aimed to place India among the top ____ scientific powers by 2020.
nd1cfcb0e77b.x: The STI Policy, 2013 made innovation central and aimed for India to be among the top five scientific powers by 2020.
xa: ⚠ **top five** by 2020 = STI 2013; **top three** in the coming decade = **STIP 2020**.
Target: raise share of global publications from **3.5% to over 7%**.
**Quadruple** papers in **top 1%** journals.

n948436a74cd.s: The STI Policy, 2013 aimed to raise India's share of global publications from 3.5% to over:
n948436a74cd.x: It aimed to raise the share from 3.5% to over 7% and to quadruple papers in the top 1% journals.
xa: STI 2013 aim: India in the **top five** scientific powers **by 2020**.
GERD target: **2% of GDP**, with private sector **matching** public spending.
New tools: **"small idea-small money"**, **"Risky Idea Fund"**.

n6dd409c26ad.s: The STI Policy, 2013 proposed direct intervention in about how many high-impact sectors?

Publications target: **3.5% to over 7%** of the global share.

nf3358842633.s: The Defence Research and Development Organisation was formed by merging which of the following?

**DST, DBT, CSIR** and **DSIR, SERB, ANRF** are civilian S&T bodies, not DRDO's constituents.
xa: SPR 1958 came during the **Second Plan (1956-61)**.
**SERB** was later subsumed into **ANRF**.

na64b9493124.s: The vision of the Draft STIP 2020 included making India:

Dependent on the top three foreign research systems
The sole scientific superpower within five years
One of the top three scientific superpowers in the coming decade

Funding: **STI Development Bank** — corpus fund for long-term strategic areas.

nb353bb9af5a.s: The Scientific Policy Resolution, 1958 was introduced during which Five Year Plan?

n43725ea4078.s: Which of the following was NOT an objective of the Science and Technology Policy, 2003?

Placing India among the top five scientific powers by 2020
Optimal utilisation of existing physical and knowledge resources

n8831abe6d5a.s: The National Innovation Council, established in 2010, was associated with which of the following?

Sam Pitroda and the promotion of inclusive innovation

**NITI Aayog** publishes the **India Innovation Index**.

ndbf64be5e7c.s: The 2026 recommendations on research funding proposed a unified fellowship called:

ne3acbee0ece.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund?

nab300ea29da.s: The draft National Health Research Policy, 2026 proposes governance with how many tiers?

nd9c933df392.s: Which of the following correctly describes INSPIRE?

n211059003a2.s: According to the figures for FY 2023–24, India's Gross Expenditure on Research and Development (GERD) as a percentage of GDP was:

n5b3bf829560.s: In FY 2023–24, the share of private industry in India's R&D expenditure was approximately:

n13cb102831c.s: India had approximately how many full-time-equivalent researchers per million people?

xa: India is **3rd** globally in **publications**.
Indian agencies fund **<10%** of grant applications.

n309d3c00e69.s: India's global rank in scientific publications was reported as:
n309d3c00e69.x: India ranked third globally in scientific publications; its nanoscience publications also ranked third after China and the USA.
n309d3c00e69.tq: Distinguish the overall publication rank from the leading countries in nanoscience.
xs: India ranks **third** (**3rd**) globally in **publications** (**Aug 2026**) — option **(2)**.
In **nanoscience** publications India is also **3rd**, after **China and USA**.
xa: Patent filing activity: **6th** (**WIPO 2023**).

**262 FTE researchers per million** people.

n7bbc096b9af.s: According to WIPO 2023 data, India's position in global patent filing activity was:
n7bbc096b9af.x: India ranked sixth in the world in patent filing activity according to WIPO 2023.
n7bbc096b9af.tq: Match the rank with the correct indicator rather than with a similarly reported index.
xs: India was **6th** in patent filing activity (**WIPO 2023**) — option **(1)**.
**38th** is the **GII 2025** rank; **49th** and **79th** are **NRI** ranks (2024 and 2019).
xa: Resident applicants: **about 62%** of filings in **2024-25**.
**Patents Act, 1970** gives **20 years** of protection.

n60efc173af4.s: India's Global Innovation Index rank in 2015 was:
xa: 2025 rank is out of **139 economies**.

nc132ed2bb68.s: Which of the following is a category in the India Innovation Index?
nc132ed2bb68.x: The categories are Major States, North-East and Hill States, and Union Territories and City States.
xa: The index is by **NITI Aayog** (with Institute for Competitiveness).
**III 2021** was released **21 July 2022**.
⚠ **GII** = WIPO; **India Innovation Index** = NITI Aayog.

n8ff4f6157a1.s: The Patents Act, 1970 gives patent protection for:
n8ff4f6157a1.x: Patents under the 1970 Act last 20 years; the invention must be novel with commercial application.
xa: **National IPR Policy, 2016** slogan: **"Creative India; Innovative India"**.
**IPAB (2003)** was **abolished in 2021**; appeals go to **High Courts**.
Resident applicants filed **about 62%** of patents in **2024-25**.

nc8643d4f49a.s: The slogan of the National IPR Policy, 2016 is:
o: Make in India; Innovate in India
nc8643d4f49a.x: The National IPR Policy, 2016 slogan is 'Creative India; Innovative India'.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** some older notes still describe IPAB as working.
Under SIPP, **>95%** applications are filed online.
**Patents Act, 1970**: protection **20 years**.

n6a2d2307060.s: IIITDM Kurnool in Andhra Pradesh has which of the following statuses?
o: State Council of Science and Technology
n6a2d2307060.x: IIITDM Kurnool is an Institute of National Importance. It is not a CSIR laboratory, a DBT autonomous institute, or a state S&T council like APCOST.
xs: **IIITDM Kurnool** is an **Institute of National Importance** — option **(1)**.
It is listed in the notes only with that status — not as a CSIR lab, a DBT institute or a state S&T council.
xa: **IISER Tirupati** — **20th in Nature Index 2026**; h-index **70**.
**MANAGE, Hyderabad** — agri-start-up incubation.
Concern: no Indian science **Nobel** in nearly a century.

n3640991ef82.s: Which body is the custodian of the RDI Scheme fund approved on 1 July 2025?
n3640991ef82.x: ANRF is the custodian of the Rs 1 lakh crore RDI fund.
xa: The fund runs **over seven years**.
**ANRF (Act 2023)** funds **basic and applied research**.
Deep-tech start-up eligibility was notified in **Feb 2026**.

n4bb1098153d.s: The Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF), established under the Act of 2023, is intended to fund:
o: Basic as well as applied research
n4bb1098153d.x: The ANRF Act, 2023 provides for funding both basic research and applied research.
n4bb1098153d.tq: Watch for the restrictive word “only” in the alternatives.
xs: **ANRF (Act 2023)** funds **basic and applied research** — option **(2)**.
So "only basic", "only commercial" or "only defence" are all wrong.
xa: ANRF is the **custodian** of the **₹1 lakh crore RDI** fund.
⚠ **~80%** of ANRF funding goes to **IITs** — criticised (**Aug 2026**).
**VigyanDhara** upgrades academic research infrastructure.

n4f3cb759b98.x: Startup India was launched on 16 January 2016.
n4f3cb759b98.tq: Match the programme with its launch date rather than a later start-up policy date.
xs: **Startup India** was launched on **16 Jan 2016** — option **(4) 16 January 2016** (UPSC).
It has a **Fund of Funds ₹10,000 crore**.
xa: **Tax exemption** for **3 years**; **self-certification** under **9** labour and environment laws.
**Winding up in 90 days**; **fast-track patents**.
**Startup Fund of Funds 2.0** (**Nov 2025**).

n158011bcd33.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature associated with Startup India?
o: Self-certification under nine labour and environment laws
n158011bcd33.x: Startup India provides for winding up in 90 days, not 30 days. The Fund of Funds, three-year tax exemption and self-certification provisions are associated features.
n158011bcd33.tq: Locate the altered numerical period in an otherwise familiar policy description.
xs: Startup India allows **winding up in 90 days**, not "within **30 days**" — option **(2) Mandatory winding up within 30 days** is NOT a feature.
Real features: **Fund of Funds ₹10,000 crore**, **tax exemption for 3 years**, **self-certification under 9 laws**.
xa: Launched **16 Jan 2016** (UPSC).
It also gives **fast-track patents**.
India = **3rd-largest** start-up hub; **1.59 lakh** DPIIT-recognised start-ups (**Sep 2025**).

n77f04421d72.s: Which one of the following is NOT an autonomous body listed under the Department of Science and Technology?
n77f04421d72.x: NRDC is a public sector undertaking controlled by DSIR, not an autonomous body listed under DST. ARIES, Wadia Institute and BSIP are associated with DST.
n77f04421d72.tq: Find the institutional mismatch by separating DST autonomous bodies from DSIR public sector undertakings.
xs: **NRDC** is NOT a DST autonomous body — it is one of **DSIR**'s **2 PSUs** (**NRDC** and **CEL**) — option **(4)**.
DST autonomous bodies: **Bose Institute, JNCASR, Raman Research Institute, ARIES Nainital, Wadia Institute, BSIP, SCTIMST**.
xa: **Survey of India** (**NIGST, Hyderabad**) is under DST.
**DSIR** (**January 1985**) also controls **CSIR**.
**Bose Institute** (DST autonomous) is India's **nodal body for FAIR**.

nf7aabdf7be1.s: BIRAC, DBT's not-for-profit company for biotech start-ups, was set up in:
nf7aabdf7be1.x: BIRAC was set up in 2012, not 2008.
xa: BIRAC = **Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council**.
**BRIC (2023)** integrates **14** DBT institutions.
DBT came from the **National Biotechnology Board** in **1986**.

nad19ae5c147.s: Under the ANRF Act, 2023, SERB was:
nad19ae5c147.x: The ANRF Act, 2023 repealed the SERB Act, 2008 and subsumed SERB into ANRF; its schemes continue.
xa: SERB was a **statutory board** under the **SERB Act, 2008**.
SERB schemes: **Core Research Grant**, **SERB-POWER**, **SERB Overseas Fellowship**.
**RDI Scheme**: DST nodal, for **private R&D**.

n98027a1683f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the leadership of CSIR?
o: The Prime Minister is its ex officio President
The Union S&T Minister is its ex officio President
The Director-General of CSIR is also Secretary, DSIR
The Director-General heads the Governing Body
n98027a1683f.x: The Prime Minister is CSIR's ex officio President; the Union S&T Minister is Vice-President.
xa: ⚠ CSIR president = **PM**; **BRIC** chair = **Union S&T Minister**.
CSIR network: **37** labs, **39** outreach centres, **1** innovation complex, **3** units.
**DSIR** controls **CSIR** + **2** PSUs (**NRDC**, **CEL**).

n62e5010e95a.s: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) has a network of how many national laboratories?
n62e5010e95a.x: CSIR has 37 national laboratories, along with 39 outreach centres, 1 innovation complex and 3 units, and 3,300+ scientists. 39 is the number of outreach centres and 3,300 approximates its scientists; 27 is not a correct figure.
xs: CSIR has **37 national laboratories** — option **(2)**.
**39** is the number of **outreach centres**; **3,300** approximates its **scientists** (**3,300+**).
xa: CSIR also has **1 innovation complex** and **3 units**.
CSIR was set up in **September 1942**.
⚠ **CCMB, IICT, NGRI** = all **Hyderabad**.

n2ada309c7e0.s: CSIR's Central Salt and Marine Chemicals Research Institute (CSMCRI) is located at:
n2ada309c7e0.x: CSMCRI, established in 1954, is at Bhavnagar and works on salt, marine chemicals and desalination.
xa: Exam angle: **Nagpur, Hyderabad, Lucknow and Bhavnagar** recur as lab locations.
**CECRI** (**Karaikudi**, Tamil Nadu) — electrochemistry, batteries.
**NIO** (**Goa**, **1966**) — oceanography.

nff769414b93.s: Which CSIR laboratory maintains national measurement standards and keeps Indian Standard Time?
nff769414b93.x: The National Physical Laboratory (NPL), New Delhi, maintains national measurement standards and keeps Indian Standard Time.
nff769414b93.tq: Identify the institution from a unique statutory or national function.
xs: **NPL**, New Delhi, keeps **national measurement standards** and **Indian Standard Time** — option **(3)** (**APPCA 2026**).
**NCL** = chemistry; **NIO** = oceanography; **NGRI** = geophysics.
xa: NPL was set up in **1947**.
**CRRI, New Delhi** built the world's first **steel slag road**.
**IMTECH** — microbial technology, **Chandigarh**.

ne223316e8f6.s: The Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), a CSIR laboratory, is located at:
ne223316e8f6.x: CDRI, set up in 1951 for drug research, is at Lucknow (CIMAP is also in Lucknow). Nagpur hosts NEERI, Bhavnagar hosts CSMCRI and Pune hosts NCL.
xs: **CDRI** is at **Lucknow** — option **(2)**.
It works on **drug research** (est. **1951**); **CIMAP** is also in Lucknow.
**Nagpur** = NEERI; **Bhavnagar** = CSMCRI; **Pune** = NCL.
xa: CDRI developed **Saheli** (**centchroman**), a weekly oral contraceptive pill.
⚠ **CDRI** and **CIMAP** = both Lucknow.
Exam angle: "headquarters of X is located in" — **Nagpur, Hyderabad, Lucknow and Bhavnagar**.

na535ae8d417.s: The Indian Institute of Science (IISc) was founded in 1909 with the vision of:
na535ae8d417.x: IISc, Bengaluru, was founded in 1909 with the vision of Jamsetji Tata.
na535ae8d417.tq: Link a major institution with its founder or founding vision and year.
xs: **IISc**, **Bengaluru** (**1909**) was founded on the vision of **Jamsetji Tata** — option **(2)**.
**J.C. Bose** founded the **Bose Institute** (**1917**, Kolkata).
xa: Nano research hubs: **IISc**, **JNCASR**, **TIFR**.
**NCESS** (**1978**, Kerala) — under **MoES** since **2014**.
**INCOIS** (**1999**, Hyderabad) — **tsunami early warning**.

nd85511be7de.s: INCOIS, located in Hyderabad, is particularly associated with:
nd85511be7de.x: INCOIS was established in 1999 under MoES and is associated with tsunami early warning.
nd85511be7de.tq: Identify an institution from its public-service application.
xs: **INCOIS**, **Hyderabad** (**1999**, **MoES**) is known for **tsunami early warning** — option **(4)**.
Food technology = **CFTRI**; medicinal plants = **CIMAP**; steel slag roads = **CRRI**.
xa: INCOIS and **NIGST** are **non-CSIR** bodies in Hyderabad.
**NCESS** (**1978**) has been under **MoES** since **2014**.
**NIO** (**Goa**) works on **oceanography**.

n0850c944fc1.s: The Bose Institute, Kolkata (1917), is India's nodal body for:
n0850c944fc1.x: The Bose Institute, a DST autonomous institute founded by J.C. Bose, is India's nodal body for FAIR.
xa: **FAIR** is funded **50:50 by DST and DAE**.
**CMERI, Durgapur** built the **beam catcher** for FAIR, **Germany**.
Other DST autonomous bodies: **JNCASR, Raman Research Institute, ARIES Nainital**.

nfcab87ce70f.s: NEERI-ZAR, developed by the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute, is primarily associated with which of the following?
nfcab87ce70f.x: NEERI-ZAR is a gravity water purifier that operates without electricity. It was developed by NEERI, Nagpur.
nfcab87ce70f.tq: Link the technology with the specialised field of its developing laboratory.
xs: **NEERI-ZAR** is a **gravity water purifier** — option **(4) Gravity-based water purification**.
It needs **no electricity**; **100 units** went to the **Assam floods**; capacity **2,500 L/hr**.
Methanol to **DME** is **NCL**; batteries is **CECRI**; oceanography is **NIO**.
xa: NEERI is at **Nagpur** (**APPSC 2011, 2018**).
NEERI works on **environmental engineering** (est. **1958**).
Current relevance: NEERI-ZAR in Assam floods (**Aug 2026**).

n9baa39a0a7f.s: Saheli, the weekly oral contraceptive pill based on centchroman, was developed by:
n9baa39a0a7f.x: Saheli, a centchroman-based weekly oral contraceptive, was developed by the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow.
n9baa39a0a7f.tq: Discriminate between laboratories in the same city by their signature technology.
xs: **Saheli** (**centchroman**), the weekly oral contraceptive pill, is from **CDRI, Lucknow** — option **(3)**.
**CIMAP, Lucknow** works on medicinal and aromatic plants; **NCL** made **DME**; **CSIO** transferred **MSCOPE** etc.
xa: CDRI does **drug research** (est. **1951**).
⚠ **CDRI** and **CIMAP** = both **Lucknow**.
**FELUDA** COVID test came from **CSIR-IGIB**.

nb6bb1e35bb2.s: Methanol-to-DME technology, described as an LPG substitute, was scaled up by which laboratory?
nb6bb1e35bb2.x: NCL, Pune, developed and scaled up methanol-to-DME technology, with DME serving as an LPG substitute.
nb6bb1e35bb2.tq: Match the fuel technology with the correct CSIR laboratory.
xs: **NCL, Pune** scaled up **methanol to DME** (**LPG substitute**) in the **2026 fuel crisis** — option **(1)**.
**NEERI** made **NEERI-ZAR**; **CMERI** built the FAIR beam catcher; **CRRI** built the **steel slag road**.
xa: NCL works on **chemistry** (est. **1950**).
**CMERI, Durgapur** built the **beam catcher** for the **FAIR** accelerator, Germany.
**CRRI, New Delhi** — world's first **steel slag road**.

n00728a5a7e0.s: The world's first steel slag road was developed by:
n00728a5a7e0.x: CRRI built the steel slag road; NAL made HANSA-3 (NG) and CMERI the FAIR beam catcher.
xa: HANSA-3 (NG) drew **LoIs for 114** aircraft.
HANSA-3 (NG) = **first indigenously developed aircraft** to be **commercially manufactured** in India.
**CCMB** set up a **zoo bio-bank** at **Darjeeling**.

n6453f13fb15.s: PRISM, PACE, BIRD-crf and A2K+ are components of the Umbrella Industrial R&D scheme of:
n6453f13fb15.x: All four are components of DSIR's Umbrella Industrial R&D scheme.
xa: **Core Research Grant**, **SERB-POWER** and the **SERB Overseas Fellowship** are SERB schemes.
**INSPIRE, Vigyan Jyoti, STI Hubs** are DST schemes.
**PM Research Fellowship**: **₹70,000-80,000/month** (**Aug 2026**).

n81cc40e9329.x: SERB-POWER is for women researchers; the SERB Overseas Fellowship is for the diaspora.
xa: **SERB** was a statutory board under the **SERB Act, 2008**.
The **ANRF Act, 2023** repealed the SERB Act — SERB **subsumed into ANRF**.
Return fellowships: **Ramanujan** (repatriate scientists), **Ramalingaswami Re-entry** (life sciences).

ndd0353ccb16.s: Which public sector undertaking is controlled by DSIR?
ndd0353ccb16.x: DSIR controls two PSUs, NRDC and CEL; CSIR is a research organisation, not a PSU.
xa: **DG CSIR** = also **Secretary, DSIR**.
DSIR was set up in **January 1985**.
DSIR recognition brings **income tax and customs duty exemptions**.

nc251d294445.s: Recognition by DSIR makes eligible in-house R&D centres and other recognised institutions for which of the following benefits?
o: Income tax and customs duty exemptions
nc251d294445.x: DSIR recognition makes the recognised institutions eligible for income tax and customs duty exemptions.
nc251d294445.tq: Apply the institutional recognition to its stated fiscal consequence rather than to unrelated regulatory benefits.
xs: DSIR recognition makes them eligible for **income tax and customs duty exemptions** — option **(1)**.
Recognised: **2,000+ in-house R&D centres**, **900+ SIROs**, **500+ public-funded institutions**.
xa: DSIR is **one of 3** departments of **MoST**.
DSIR controls **CSIR**, **NRDC** and **CEL**.
DSIR runs **PRISM, PACE, BIRD-crf, A2K+** for industrial R&D.

n1d8754fb8af.s: Which one of the following is an institute of the Department of Biotechnology (DBT)?
o: Central Glass and Ceramic Research Institute
Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology
Centre of Innovative and Applied Bioprocessing
n1d8754fb8af.x: The Centre of Innovative and Applied Bioprocessing (CIAB), Mohali, is a DBT institute (APPSC-G2 2025). CFTRI, the Central Glass and Ceramic Research Institute and CCMB are CSIR laboratories.
xs: **CIAB** (**Centre of Innovative and Applied Bioprocessing**), **Mohali**, is a **DBT** institute — option **(4)** (**APPSC-G2 2025**).
**CFTRI**, **Central Glass and Ceramic RI** and **CCMB** were the PYQ distractors — all **CSIR** labs.
xa: Other DBT institutes: **NII**, **NIPGR** (New Delhi), **RCB** (Faridabad), **NCCS** (Pune).
**CDFD** and **NIAB** are DBT institutions in **Hyderabad**.
BRIC integrates **14 DBT institutions**.

n83d3d087f5b.s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of CSIR laboratories or centres located in Hyderabad?
o: NIGST, NIO Regional Centre and CCMB
n83d3d087f5b.x: CCMB, IICT and NGRI are CSIR laboratories or centres located in Hyderabad. CDFD and NIAB are DBT institutions, while INCOIS and NIGST are non-CSIR institutions.
n83d3d087f5b.tq: Classify each institution by both location and parent organisation before selecting the all-correct set.
xs: **CCMB, IICT, NGRI** are all **CSIR** labs in **Hyderabad** — option **(1)**.
**CDFD** and **NIAB** are **DBT**; **INCOIS** and **NIGST** are **non-CSIR**; the **NIO Regional Centre** is at **Visakhapatnam**.
xa: **Bullayya College** (Visakhapatnam) signed an **MoU** with **IICT** (**2026**).
**CCMB** (**1977**) — cellular and molecular biology.
**NGRI** (**1961**) — geophysics, earthquakes, groundwater.

n1bf6d3935b7.s: The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) was established in:
n1bf6d3935b7.x: ICAR was established in 1929; DARE, its administrative department, came in December 1973.
xa: DARE is under the **Ministry of Agriculture**.
ICAR network: **113 institutes** — **72** research institutes, **6** national bureaux, **12** NRCs.
**ICFRE** (**1986**) is under **MoEFCC**, not DARE.

nf66f2ee3085.s: The Department of Atomic Energy was set up in 1954 by:
nf66f2ee3085.x: DAE was set up in 1954 by a Presidential Order, not an Act, and is directly under the Prime Minister.
xa: **AEC** was set up in **1948**.
**ISRO** was formed on **15 August 1969**; the **Space Commission** in **1972** with DoS.
**INCOSPAR** dates from **1962**.

n41a97b6ac0c.s: Which of the following correctly describes DRDO?
o: Headquartered at Hyderabad; conducts agricultural research
Headquartered at Bengaluru; plans space missions
Headquartered at DRDO Bhawan, New Delhi; develops indigenous defence technology
Headquartered at Gandhinagar; regulates atomic energy
n41a97b6ac0c.x: DRDO is headquartered at DRDO Bhawan, New Delhi, and develops indigenous defence technology through its network of laboratories.
xa: DRDO is under the **Dept of Defence R&D**, **Ministry of Defence**.
DRDO Chairman: **Samir V. Kamat** (since **2022**).
Kamat is also **Secretary, DDR&D** (as of **Jun 2026**).
n41a97b6ac0c.fixed: DRDO lab count was cut from ~52 to ~41 after restructuring; '52' outdated

n401f563fbe9.s: The Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), established in 1945 at Bombay, is associated with which development?
o: The production of rare earth minerals
The establishment of district-level agricultural extension centres
The beginning of organised nuclear research in India
n401f563fbe9.x: TIFR was established in 1945 at Bombay and marked the beginning of organised nuclear research in India.
n401f563fbe9.tq: Connect the institution with its historical role rather than a later operational function.
xs: **TIFR** (**1945**, **Bombay**) marked the **start of organised nuclear research** — option **(4)**.
Rare earths = **IREL**; KVKs = **ICAR**; radiation safety = **AERB**.
xa: **NCRA-TIFR** runs the **GMRT** near **Pune** (**APPCA 2026**).
TIFR leads the **INO** (Neutrino Observatory) at **Bodi West Hills, Theni**.
**NCRA-TIFR, Pune** is India's lead for the **Square Kilometre Array**.

n4b4a18819cf.s: The Atomic Energy Commission was set up in
n4b4a18819cf.x: The Atomic Energy Commission was set up in 1948.
n4b4a18819cf.tq: Test the institutional year against nearby formation years.
xs: The **AEC** was set up in **1948** — option **(2)**.
**1948** is also the year of the **first Atomic Energy Act**.
xa: AEC handles **policy and strategic planning**; oversees **BARC, NPCIL, AERB**.
AEC is **chaired by Secretary, DAE**.
**DAE** came in **1954** by **Presidential Order**.

nbfb9d233ab7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Space Commission?
o: It is chaired by the Secretary, DoS, who is also the ISRO Chairman
It is associated with the Department of Space
The Department of Space reports to the Minister of Science and Technology
nbfb9d233ab7.x: The Department of Space reports directly to the Prime Minister.
xa: ⚠ **DAE** and **DoS** = both directly under the **PM**.
**ISRO** (**15 August 1969**) superseded **INCOSPAR**.
ISRO Chairman: **V. Narayanan** (**Jan 2026**).

n1dfb2e4f05b.x: ISRO came in 1969; INCOSPAR was formed in 1962 under Vikram Sarabhai and DAE.
xa: **TERLS** was also set up in **1962**.
**DoS** and the **Space Commission** came in **1972**.
⚠ Older notes say November 1969 — use **August**.

nenvironment-28-7.s: The National Research Centre for Agroforestry is located at:
nenvironment-28-7.x: The National Research Centre for Agroforestry, now CAFRI, is in Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh.
nenvironment-28-7.tq: Match each forest institute to its city.
n: The National Research Centre for Agroforestry is located in Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 50-52]
xs: The **National Research Centre for Agroforestry** is at **Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh**, so option **(2)** is correct.
It was **established** in **1988** at Jhansi and **renamed** the **Central Agroforestry Research Institute** in **December 2014**.
xa: **Indian Grassland & Fodder Research Institute** is also at **Jhansi**.
**Indian Institute of Soil Science** is at **Bhopal**.
**Indian Institute of Soil & Water Conservation** is at **Dehradun**.

nd8b670e2a71.s: Which body is India's regulator for nuclear and radiation safety?
nd8b670e2a71.x: AERB regulates nuclear and radiation safety; IREL handles beach-sand minerals and the Heavy Water Board makes heavy water.
xa: **IGCAR, Kalpakkam** — **fast breeder reactor** R&D.
**NPCIL** (**1987**) builds and runs nuclear power plants.
NPCIL holds equity in **BHAVINI** (fast breeders).

n301047b3e87.s: The Bhabha Atomic Research Centre began in 1954 as the Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay, and was renamed in 1967 after:
n301047b3e87.x: AEET was renamed Bhabha Atomic Research Centre in 1967 in honour of Homi Jehangir Bhabha.
n301047b3e87.tq: Use the renamed-in-honour-of relationship to distinguish prominent Indian scientists.
xs: **AEET** (**1954**) was renamed **BARC** in **1967** after **Homi Bhabha** — option **(3) Homi Jehangir Bhabha**.
**Sarabhai** is linked to **INCOSPAR** (**1962**), not BARC.
xa: BARC covers **reactor design, fuel cycle, radioisotopes** and runs the **BARC Training School**.
BARC reactors: **APSARA** (Asia's first), **Dhruva** (largest), **KAMINI** (U-233).
**TIFR** (**1945**) marked the start of organised nuclear research.

n363de00268d.s: Which BARC reactor is fuelled by uranium-233?
n363de00268d.x: KAMINI is the only U-233-fuelled reactor of the group; APSARA was Asia's first research reactor and Dhruva the largest.
xa: APSARA went **critical 1956**.
CIRUS was built with **Canadian help**.
**IGCAR, Kalpakkam** does **fast breeder** R&D.

nbdda5c55b89.s: The Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture (CIFA) is located at:
nbdda5c55b89.x: CIFA is at Bhubaneswar; CRRI/NRRI is at Cuttack and ICRISAT at Patancheru.
xa: **IARI** (Pusa Institute) began in **1905 at Pusa, Bihar**; in Delhi from **1936**.
**CRRI** (Central Rice RI) is now **NRRI** (est. **1946**).
**NRCWA** (now **CIWA**) is also in **Bhubaneswar**.

nb2ab1b4d339.s: The Central Potato Research Institute is located at:
nb2ab1b4d339.x: CPRI is at Shimla; CAZRI is at Jodhpur and NDRI at Karnal.
xa: CPRI dates to **1949**; CAZRI to **1959** (**APPSC 2018**).
⚠ **CIAH** and **NRC on Camel** = **Bikaner**; **CAZRI** = **Jodhpur**.
**HFRI** (ICFRE) is also in **Shimla**.

nindian-geography-22-3.s: The Indian Grassland & Fodder Research Institute is located at:
nindian-geography-22-3.x: IGFRI is at Jhansi; Bhopal has the soil science institute and Karnal the NDRI.
n: The National Rice Research Institute (NRRI) is located in Cuttack, Odisha. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 68-77]
The Indian Institute of Soil Science (IISS) is located in Bhopal. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 68-77]
The Indian Grassland & Fodder Research Institute (IGFRI) is located in Jhansi. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 68-77]
The National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI) is located in Karnal, Haryana. [Indian Geography · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 68-77]
xa: NDRI began in **1923** at **Bengaluru** and moved to Karnal in **1955**.
**Central Soil Salinity Research Institute** is also at **Karnal**.
