ne80ef5ea1ee.s: SEATS (Scheme for Early Attraction of Talents for Science) targets:
ne80ef5ea1ee.x: SEATS targets school students; AORC concerns doctoral and post-doctoral careers.
xa: INSPIRE is a **DST** flagship launched in **2008**.
AORC = INSPIRE **Fellowship** (PhD) and INSPIRE **Faculty**.

nb93f714179c.s: The INSPIRE component 'MANAK', aimed at school students of Classes VI-X, stands for:
o: Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge
Million Awards for National Academic Knowledge
Mission for Advancing National Aptitude and Knowledge
Model Awards for Nurturing Aspiring Kids
nb93f714179c.x: MANAK = Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge, for Classes VI-X (age 10-15). The other expansions are made up; 'Million Awards for National Academic Knowledge' is a common wrong guess.
nb93f714179c.tq: MANAK = Million MINDS (school ideas), not awards.
xs: MANAK stands for **Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is aimed at Classes **VI-X**, aged **10-15**.
xa: Other INSPIRE components: **SEATS**, **SHE**, **AORC**.

nf062bcb0b0d.s: Which one of the following is NOT a scheme or initiative of the Department of Science and Technology (DST)?
nf062bcb0b0d.x: The Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship is a DBT (Department of Biotechnology) scheme for Indian life-science and biotech scientists abroad who return, so it is the odd one out. INSPIRE, Vigyan Jyoti and the Nano Mission are DST schemes.
nf062bcb0b0d.tq: Separate departmental flagship schemes from fellowships administered in the research-grant system.
xs: The **Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship** is a **DBT** scheme, not DST — so option **(1)** is the odd one out.
It is for Indian **life-science/biotech** scientists abroad returning to India.
**INSPIRE** (**2008**) and **Vigyan Jyoti** are DST schemes.
xa: ⚠ DBT's women scheme is **BioCARe**; DST's is **WISE-KIRAN**.
⚠ **Ramanujan Fellowship** (SERB/ANRF) covers all returning scientists.
nf062bcb0b0d.fixed: odd wording 'in the material listed'; Ramalingaswami = DBT

n0819037f4ee.s: Which of the following is NOT a component associated with NIDHI?
n0819037f4ee.x: NIDHI includes PRAYAS, Entrepreneur-in-Residence, Seed Support System, Technology Business Incubators, Accelerators and Centres of Excellence. The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups is a separate startup-support programme associated with NCGTC.
n0819037f4ee.tq: Find the programme component belonging to another startup scheme.
xs: The **Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups** is not a NIDHI component — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is run by **NCGTC**.
NIDHI's components include **PRAYAS**, **Entrepreneur-in-Residence**, **Seed Support System**, **Technology Business Incubators**, Accelerators and Centres of Excellence.
xa: NIDHI is a **DST** initiative of **2016**.
**Fund of Funds for Startups** — **SIDBI**, **₹10,000 crore**.

n4a890dc6dc6.s: Which scheme, implemented with the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti, targets meritorious girl students of Classes 9 to 12?
n4a890dc6dc6.x: Vigyan Jyoti targets meritorious girl students in Classes 9 to 12 and is implemented with the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti.
xa: Exam angle: Vigyan Jyoti = **women/girls** in STEM (APPSC-GS 2023).
**WIDUSHI** = senior women scientists in **interdisciplinary** S&T (APPSC-G1 2024).

n1cc90190525.s: WISE-KIRAN, which includes WISE-PhD, WISE-PDF and WIDUSHI, is an initiative of:
n1cc90190525.x: WISE-KIRAN is a DST initiative for women scientists, especially those with career breaks.
xa: **340+** women have been selected.
WISE = **Women in Science and Engineering**.
⚠ Career-break women in **biotechnology** = **BioCARe** (DBT).

na3f847edccc.s: WIDUSHI, associated with WISE-KIRAN, is intended primarily for which of the following groups?
o: Women scientists seeking their first extramural biotechnology grant
Senior women scientists conducting interdisciplinary research in science and technology
na3f847edccc.x: WIDUSHI is meant for senior women scientists engaged in interdisciplinary research in science and technology.
na3f847edccc.tq: Confusable-pair discrimination between WIDUSHI, BioCARe, GATI and Vigyan Jyoti.
xs: **WIDUSHI** is for **senior women scientists** doing **interdisciplinary** research in S&T — so option **(3)** is correct.
First extramural biotech grant = **BioCARe**; gender-equity charter = **GATI**; school girls = **Vigyan Jyoti**.
xa: WIDUSHI falls under DST's **WISE-KIRAN** (APPSC-G1 2024).
WISE-KIRAN fellowships: **WISE-PhD, WISE-PDF, WIDUSHI** — **340+** women selected.

nc756759ae7a.s: The Swarnajayanti Fellowship was begun in connection with:
o: The centenary of the Indian Science Congress
nc756759ae7a.x: The Swarnajayanti Fellowship began in 1997 to mark 50 years of India’s Independence and supports young scientists with a proven record.
nc756759ae7a.tq: Date-event association using a commemorative milestone.
xs: The **Swarnajayanti Fellowship** began in **1997** to mark **50 years of India's Independence** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is a **DST** fellowship for **young scientists with a proven record**.
xa: **J.C. Bose Fellowship** is for active **senior** scientists.
**PMRF** (**2018**, Ministry of Education) is for PhD scholars in top institutions.

n08dded67025.s: Which one of the following programmes was launched through collaboration between CSIR and Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan in 2017?
n08dded67025.x: JIGYASA was started through CSIR–Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan collaboration in 2017.
n08dded67025.tq: Identify the programme from its partner bodies and launch year.
xs: **JIGYASA** was launched by **CSIR + Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan** in **2017** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is a student-scientist connect, bringing **KV students into CSIR labs**.
**Smart India Hackathon** = Ministry of Education + AICTE; **VIPNET** = Vigyan Prasar science clubs; **ARISE** = AIM for MSMEs.
xa: Smart India Hackathon also runs **from 2017**.
⚠ JIGYASA = **CSIR**, not DST.

n48af6087349.s: The Smart India Hackathon is associated with the Innovation Cell of:
n48af6087349.x: SIH is run with the Ministry of Education's Innovation Cell, with AICTE as partner since 2017.
xa: **JIGYASA** (**2017**) connects KV students with **CSIR** labs.
**VIPNET** is Vigyan Prasar's network of **science clubs**.

nd608216048a.s: TIDE 2.0 (Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs), which supports ICT start-ups through incubators, is implemented by:
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
nd608216048a.x: TIDE 2.0 is a MeitY programme launched in 2019 to support ICT and technology start-ups through incubators.
xa: DST's start-up initiative is **NIDHI** (**2016**).
**Technology Business Incubators** are hosted in academic/R&D institutes under NIDHI.

nb95be8d74b3.s: INSPIRE was launched in 2008 by which organisation as a flagship programme?
nb95be8d74b3.x: INSPIRE, or Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research, is a flagship programme of the Department of Science and Technology launched in 2008.
xs: **INSPIRE** is a flagship programme of the **Department of Science and Technology**, launched in **2008** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Its components: **SEATS** (school students), **MANAK** (Classes **VI-X**), **SHE** (UG/PG) and **AORC** (doctoral/post-doctoral).
xa: **INSPIRE Fellowship 2025**: **653** doctoral fellowships; **65% female**.
**INSPIRE Faculty**: **2,944** applications against the **2024** call.
INSPIRE, **VAJRA** and the **Ramanujan Fellowship** are brain drain → brain gain schemes (APPSC-G1 2022).

n837e2e21cae.s: The National Supercomputing Mission (2015) is implemented by C-DAC and:
n837e2e21cae.x: NSM, run by DST and MeitY, is implemented by C-DAC and IISc Bengaluru, not IIT Bombay.
xa: First NSM system = **PARAM Shivay** (**2019**, IIT (BHU) Varanasi).
**PARAM Pravega** is at **IISc Bengaluru**; **PARAM Siddhi-AI** at **C-DAC Pune**.

n0f3037b5626.s: NM-ICPS provides for how many Technology Innovation Hubs set up as Section-8 companies?
n0f3037b5626.x: NM-ICPS provides for 25 Technology Innovation Hubs as Section-8 companies in host institutes.
xa: NM-ICPS: Cabinet **2018**, **₹3,660 crore** for **nine years** (older notes say five years).
AP: **IISER Tirupati TIH (IITTNiF)** — Positioning & Precision Technologies.

n06d44b42be3.s: The NM-ICPS Technology Innovation Hub associated with IISER Tirupati focuses on
n06d44b42be3.x: The IISER Tirupati TIH, IITTNiF, is associated with Positioning and Precision Technologies.
n06d44b42be3.tq: Match the host institution with its specific technology vertical.
xs: The **IISER Tirupati TIH (IITTNiF)** focuses on **Positioning and Precision Technologies** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is one of NM-ICPS's **25 Technology Innovation Hubs**.
Product innovation for national challenges = **Atal New India Challenges**; 3D printing in schools = **Atal Tinkering Labs**.
xa: NM-ICPS = National Mission on **Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems**, Cabinet **2018**.
Other AP links: **590 ATLs** and the **Amaravati Quantum Valley**.

nf16d1b14767.s: The National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS) was approved by the Union Cabinet in which year and with what outlay?
nf16d1b14767.x: NM-ICPS was approved by the Cabinet in 2018 with Rs 3,660 crore (for nine years per current sources; older sources say five), and set up 25 Technology Innovation Hubs. Rs 6,003.65 crore (2023) is the National Quantum Mission, Rs 10,371.92 crore (2024) is the IndiaAI Mission, and 2015 is the year NSM began.
xs: NM-ICPS was approved by the Cabinet in **2018** with **Rs 3,660 crore** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The outlay is for **nine years** (older notes say five years).
**₹6,003.65 crore** is the **National Quantum Mission** outlay; **2015** is when NSM began.
xa: NQM runs for **8 years**.
NM-ICPS set up **25 Technology Innovation Hubs** as Section-8 companies.

n15f35190725.s: NIDHI, launched in 2016, is an initiative of which department?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
n15f35190725.x: NIDHI, or National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations, was launched in 2016 by the Department of Science and Technology.
xs: **NIDHI** (**National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations**) was launched in **2016** by the **Department of Science and Technology** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**MeitY** runs **TIDE 2.0**; **DPIIT** runs the **Startup India Seed Fund Scheme**.
xa: NIDHI components: **PRAYAS**, **EIR**, **Seed Support System**, **Technology Business Incubators**, Accelerators, Centres of Excellence.
⚠ PRAYAS = prototyping grants; EIR = Entrepreneur-in-Residence.

n5c44fcef8c5.s: Which of the following is a DST infrastructure-upgradation programme rather than a brain-gain scheme?
n5c44fcef8c5.x: FIST upgrades infrastructure; VAJRA, Ramanujan Fellowship and INSPIRE aim at brain gain.
xa: **Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship** (DBT) does the same for life-science/biotech scientists.
INSPIRE is a **DST** flagship of **2008**.

nf5875e55947.s: Under the Atal Innovation Mission, which component focuses on rural and underserved areas?
nf5875e55947.x: ACICs focus on rural and underserved areas; ATLs are in schools and AICs support start-ups.
xa: **ARISE** — Atal Research and Innovation for **Small Enterprises** (MSMEs).
**Atal New India Challenges** — product innovation for national challenges.
AIM is a **NITI Aayog** flagship, set up **2016**.

n258ed9af6db.s: Atal Tinkering Labs, which expose students to IoT, 3D printing and robotics, are set up for students of:
n258ed9af6db.x: ATLs are established in schools for students of grades 6–12.
xa: AIM 2.0 adds **2,500 new ATLs**.
ATL funding rose from **₹500 crore to ₹3,200 crore** in Union Budget **2026-27**.
Generative-AI assistants are being added to **10,000 ATLs**; AP has **590 ATLs**.

nf7a118c52b1.s: Atal Innovation Mission is a flagship initiative of
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
nf7a118c52b1.x: Atal Innovation Mission is a flagship initiative of NITI Aayog.
nf7a118c52b1.tq: Identify the parent institution rather than a collaborating ministry.
xs: **Atal Innovation Mission** is a **NITI Aayog** flagship — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was set up in **2016** (announced in Budget **2015**).
**DST** runs **NIDHI** and **INSPIRE**; **MeitY** runs **TIDE 2.0**; **AICTE** partners the Smart India Hackathon.
xa: Components: **ATLs**, **AICs**, **ACICs**, **ARISE**, **Atal New India Challenges**.

n5228000c8d9.s: Which State was identified as the first State Innovation Mission under AIM 2.0?
n5228000c8d9.x: Tripura was identified as the first State Innovation Mission under AIM 2.0.
n5228000c8d9.tq: Use the first-in-series fact to distinguish the state from other innovation leaders.
xs: **Tripura** is the first State Innovation Mission under AIM 2.0 (Jun **2026**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
AIM 2.0 (**2024**) has **₹2,750 crore** and runs till **March 2028**.
xa: AP has **590 ATLs**; AP's NM-ICPS hub is **IISER Tirupati (IITTNiF)**.
Other AP item: **Amaravati Quantum Valley**.

n1de2bc50f6f.s: Atal Innovation Mission 2.0, approved in 2024, has an outlay of:
n1de2bc50f6f.x: AIM 2.0 has Rs 2,750 crore and runs till March 2028. Rs 500 crore to Rs 3,200 crore is the 2026-27 Budget rise for Atal Tinkering Labs, and Rs 10,000 crore is the SIDBI Fund of Funds for Startups.
n1de2bc50f6f.tq: AIM 2.0 = 2,750 crore, till 2028; 3,200 crore = ATL budget.
xs: AIM 2.0 (**2024**) has **Rs 2,750 crore till March 2028** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Rs 500 crore to Rs 3,200 crore** is the ATL budget rise in **2026-27**; **Rs 10,000 crore** is SIDBI's Fund of Funds for Startups.
xa: AIM 2.0 includes **LIPI**, **2,500 new ATLs**, **10** Atal Sectoral Innovation Launchpads and a **Deeptech Reactor**.
First State Innovation Mission: **Tripura**.

n27d873bdad3.s: The allocation for Atal Tinkering Labs in the Union Budget 2026–27 rose from:
n27d873bdad3.x: The allocation for ATLs increased from ₹500 crore to ₹3,200 crore in the Union Budget 2026–27.
n27d873bdad3.tq: Read the paired before-and-after figures together rather than treating them as separate amounts.
xs: ATL funding rose from **₹500 crore to ₹3,200 crore** in **Union Budget 2026–27** — so option **(2)** is correct.
That is nearly a **six-fold** rise (Feb **2026**).
**₹2,750 crore** is the **AIM 2.0** outlay.
xa: **India-France ATL Bridge** launched at **Nice** at Bharat Innovates **2026**.
Generative-AI assistants are being added to **10,000 ATLs**.

nadb93218586.s: Which of the following institutions jointly steers the National Supercomputing Mission?
nadb93218586.x: The mission is jointly steered by the Department of Science and Technology and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
nadb93218586.tq: Identify the correct pair of nodal agencies rather than the implementing institutions.
xs: The National Supercomputing Mission is jointly steered by **DST and MeitY** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was launched in **2015**; implementing agencies are **C-DAC, Pune** and **IISc, Bengaluru**.
xa: Planned: **40 systems (>64 PF)**; **37** commissioned with **39 PF** at **37** locations.
⚠ Earlier figure: **33** systems, **32 PF** as of **Dec 2024**; older notes say a **45 PF** target.
Systems are linked on the **National Supercomputing Grid** over the **National Knowledge Network**.

n25c75e1159d.s: AIRAWAT, the artificial-intelligence supercomputer associated with the National Supercomputing Mission, is located at:
n25c75e1159d.x: AIRAWAT is located at C-DAC, Pune.
n25c75e1159d.tq: Test the host institution of a named machine rather than its ranking.
xs: **AIRAWAT**, the AI supercomputer, is at **C-DAC, Pune** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It ranked **75th** in **Top500** at **ISC 2023** (Germany).
**NCMRWF Noida** hosts **Mihir**; **IIT Madras** hosts **PARAM Shakti**; **IISc Bengaluru** hosts **PARAM Pravega**.
xa: C-DAC built **PARAM 8000** (**1991**), India's first supercomputer.
**C-DAC, Pune** is a co-implementing agency of NSM with **IISc**.

nedaacd49a56.s: Vijay Bhatkar is associated with which description?
o: Architect of the Deep Ocean Mission
Founder of India’s quantum communication mission
Chairperson of the ANRF Governing Board
nedaacd49a56.x: Vijay Bhatkar is recognised as the father of Indian supercomputing.
nedaacd49a56.tq: Match the personality with the precise title used in the field.
xs: **Vijay Bhatkar** is the **father of Indian supercomputing** — so option **(1)** is correct.
He led **C-DAC**'s **PARAM 8000** (**1991**), India's first supercomputer.
The **ANRF** Governing Board is headed by the **PM** as ex officio President.
xa: The programme began in the **late 1980s**.
⚠ First NSM machine = **PARAM Shivay**, not PARAM 8000.

n529fa5f6d79.s: The supercomputer Pratyush is located at:
n529fa5f6d79.x: Pratyush is at IITM Pune; Mihir is at NCMRWF Noida, Flosolver at NAL Bengaluru and Anupam at BARC.
xa: **PARAM 8000** (**1991**, C-DAC) was India's first supercomputer.
⚠ Both **Pratyush** and **Mihir** are **weather** machines.

n28cb78a07f8.s: India's first supercomputer, developed by C-DAC in 1991, was:
n28cb78a07f8.x: PARAM 8000 (1991) was built by C-DAC under Vijay Bhatkar and was India's first supercomputer. PARAM Shivay (2019) was the first NSM machine, Anupam is a BARC machine, and AIRAWAT is the later AI supercomputer at C-DAC Pune.
n28cb78a07f8.tq: First supercomputer = PARAM 8000; first NSM system = PARAM Shivay.
xs: India's first supercomputer was **PARAM 8000** (**1991**), developed by **C-DAC** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was built under **Vijay Bhatkar**, father of Indian supercomputing.
**PARAM Shivay** was the first **NSM** machine; **Anupam** is a **BARC** machine; **AIRAWAT** is the AI supercomputer at C-DAC Pune.
xa: The programme began in the **late 1980s**.
AIRAWAT ranked **75th** in Top500 (ISC **2023**).

n58f9591aec7.s: The supercomputer PARAM Pravega is hosted at:
n58f9591aec7.x: PARAM Pravega is at IISc Bengaluru; PARAM Shivay is at IIT (BHU), PARAM Porul at NIT Tiruchirappalli and PARAM Ananta at IIT Gandhinagar.
xa: **PARAM Kamrupa** → **IIT Guwahati** (**14th** machine, dedicated by the President).
**AIRAWAT** (AI supercomputer) → **C-DAC, Pune**, **75th** in Top500 (ISC **2023**).
⚠ PARAM Shivay is NOT at IIT Guwahati.

ne6c118a21ab.s: In the National Supercomputing Mission, 'Rudra' refers to:
o: The interconnect used in all PARAM systems
A C-DAC high-performance computing chip programme
A server board on which the Rudra machines are built
ne6c118a21ab.x: The Rudra machines are built on the Rudra server; AUM is the separate C-DAC HPC chip programme.
xa: **PARAM Rudra**: **3** systems at Pune (GMRT), Delhi (IUAC), Kolkata (S.N. Bose Centre).
India's actual first supercomputer = **PARAM 8000** (**1991**, C-DAC).

n8c1462f1e2e.s: The National Quantum Mission, with an outlay of ₹6,003.65 crore for 2023–24 to 2030–31, is implemented by:
n8c1462f1e2e.x: The National Quantum Mission is under DST, with an outlay of ₹6,003.65 crore over eight years (2023–24 to 2030–31).
xa: Target: intermediate-scale computers of **50-1000 physical qubits** in **8 years**.
**Central Fabrication Facilities** at IIT Delhi, IISc, IIT Bombay, IIT Kanpur (~**₹720 crore**).

n48871e2d4cc.s: The National Quantum Mission aims to develop intermediate-scale quantum computers containing approximately:
n48871e2d4cc.x: The target is intermediate-scale computers with 50 to 1000 physical qubits within eight years.
n48871e2d4cc.tq: Use the exact numerical range and distinguish physical qubits from logical qubits.
xs: NQM aims at intermediate-scale quantum computers of **50–1000 physical qubits** in **8 years** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Platforms: **superconducting** and **photonic**.
xa: Communication target: **satellite QKD** over **2000 km** within India and inter-city QKD over **2000 km**.
Start-up **QpiAI** built a **64-qubit QPU**.
Quantum Computing T-Hub = **IISc Bengaluru**.

n61daeb6a43f.s: In the Bio-E3 Policy (2024), Bio-E3 stands for Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and ____.
n61daeb6a43f.x: Bio-E3 means Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment; its core aim is a bio-manufacturing ecosystem.
xa: India's bioeconomy: over **US$165 billion (2024)**.
**Budget 2026-27**: **Biopharma SHAKTI**, **₹10,000 crore** over **5** years.

n144c3ac5d18.s: Who is the ex officio President of the Governing Board of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF)?
o: The Union Minister of Science and Technology
n144c3ac5d18.x: Under the ANRF Act, 2023 the Prime Minister is the ex officio President of the ANRF Governing Board (the ANRF subsumed SERB).
xa: ANRF is custodian of the **₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund**.
ANRF schemes include **MAHA-EV**, **SERB-SURE**, **JC Bose Grant** and **Ramanujan Fellowship**.
**Criticism:** funding shortfalls followed the **SERB-to-ANRF** transition.

n6a93e76bd51.s: The ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund is associated with the ANRF through a:
n6a93e76bd51.x: ANRF is the custodian of the ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund through a two-tier Special Purpose Fund.
n6a93e76bd51.tq: Combine the fund amount with its institutional mechanism.
xs: ANRF is custodian of the **₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund** through a **two-tier Special Purpose Fund** — so option **(4)** is correct.
ANRF was set up under the **ANRF Act, 2023**; the **PM** is ex officio President of its Governing Board.
xa: ANRF **subsumed SERB**; funding shortfalls followed the transition.
ANRF schemes: PMECRG, **MAHA-EV**, MAHA MedTech, AI-SE, PAIR, **SERB-SURE**, JC Bose Grant, Ramanujan Fellowship.

na9431112ae0.s: Where is the 1Q Quantum Test and Reference Facility in Andhra Pradesh located?
na9431112ae0.x: The 1Q facility is at Medha Towers, Gannavaram, while the 1S test bed is at SRM University-AP.
xa: Opened on **14 April 2026** (**World Quantum Day**).
Components from **TIFR, IISc, DRDO, IIT Bombay**; built with **Qubit Force/Qubitekk**.

nbce9a4b443c.s: The foundation stone of the Amaravati Quantum Valley was laid at which of the following places?
nbce9a4b443c.x: The foundation stone of the Amaravati Quantum Valley was laid at Uddandarayunipalem.
nbce9a4b443c.tq: Use the location-based direct-recall method and distinguish the foundation site from associated facilities.
xs: The foundation stone of the Amaravati Quantum Valley was laid at **Uddandarayunipalem** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Acharya Nagarjuna University** hosts NIELIT classes; **Medha Towers, Gannavaram** hosts the **1Q** test bed.
xa: The Valley has **50 acres** under NQM, with two **18-storey towers** (**₹1,205 crore**, L&T).
AP plans to train **4.5 million** people in AI and quantum.

nfe3be4a7878.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the incentives in the Amaravati Quantum Valley?
o: Andhra Pradesh plans to train 4.5 million people in AI and quantum technologies
Technology firms get 100% exemption from stamp duty
Technology firms get 100% exemption from registration fees
The exemption applies only to registration fees and not to stamp duty
nfe3be4a7878.x: The policy gives 100% exemption from both stamp duty and registration fees, so saying it excludes stamp duty is wrong.
xa: Quantum Computing Policy: **50+** proposals, **7** approvals.
IBM will **train 1 lakh youth** under the Feb **2026** MoUs.

na777af50ea8.s: Classes of the MeitY's NIELIT Quantum and AI campus, Amaravati, are scheduled to begin in September 2026 at:
na777af50ea8.x: The NIELIT campus (Ministry of Electronics and IT) is to start classes from September 2026 at Acharya Nagarjuna University, Guntur.
xa: A **NIELIT Quantum AI deemed university** was among the **seven MoUs** (Feb **2026**).
**PanIIT Summit** on deep tech: **Vijayawada**, **3 Oct 2026**.

nc0f65f62adf.s: Which was the first State in India to have a dedicated quantum computing policy?
nc0f65f62adf.x: Andhra Pradesh is the first State with a dedicated quantum computing policy and aims to make Amaravati Quantum Valley a top-five global quantum hub by 2030.
xa: India's first **Quantum Reference Facility** test beds opened in AP on **14 April 2026**.
Foundation stone at **Uddandarayunipalem**.

n68f80272dd6.s: India’s bioeconomy was valued at over which amount in 2024?
n68f80272dd6.x: India’s bioeconomy was valued at over US$165 billion in 2024.
n68f80272dd6.tq: Recall the exact scale figure and distinguish it from public-sector mission outlays.
xs: India's bioeconomy was over **US$165 billion** in **2024** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This is cited under the **Bio-E3 Policy** (**2024**).
xa: Bio-E3 = **Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment**.
Budget 2026-27: **Biopharma SHAKTI**, **₹10,000 crore** over **5** years (biologics, biosimilars).

n0b60b2e9ef6.s: J.C. Bose was a pioneer in microwave and millimetre-wave radio research and used which of the following components?
n0b60b2e9ef6.x: J.C. Bose pioneered microwave and millimetre-wave radio research and worked with a coherer and a galena semiconductor detector.
n0b60b2e9ef6.tq: Match the scientist’s research area with the characteristic apparatus associated with it.
xs: J.C. Bose used the **coherer and galena detector** (a semiconductor detector) in microwave/millimetre-wave radio — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **crescograph** was his plant-growth instrument, not a radio component.
xa: He worked at **IACS**, Kolkata.
Honours: knighted **1917**, **FRS 1920**.
Area: **plant physiology** and **radio/microwave physics**.

n7fb3c58760e.s: Which one of the following is a book written by J.C. Bose?
o: The Mathematical Theory of Black Holes
n7fb3c58760e.x: The Nervous Mechanism of Plants was written by J.C. Bose. His other listed works include Response in the Living and Non-Living and the Bengali science-fiction work Niruddesher Kahini.
n7fb3c58760e.tq: Distinguish the scientist’s own book from works associated with other disciplines or authors.
xs: **The Nervous Mechanism of Plants** was written by **J.C. Bose** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Chromosome Atlas of Cultivated Plants** was co-authored by **Janaki Ammal**.
xa: Bose also wrote **Response in the Living and Non-Living** (**1902**).
He wrote the Bengali science fiction **Niruddesher Kahini**.
⚠ Tagore's **Visva-Parichay** (**1937**) was dedicated to **S.N. Bose**, not J.C. Bose.

ncc377c12599.s: J.C. Bose founded the Bose Institute, Kolkata, in:
ncc377c12599.x: J.C. Bose, who showed that plants respond to stimuli, founded the Bose Institute in Kolkata in 1917.
xa: Bose invented the **Crescograph** to measure plant growth.
⚠ **Saha** = thermal ionisation + Damodar Valley plan.

nd3be8ba1b24.s: Srinivasa Ramanujan worked at Cambridge with which mathematician?
nd3be8ba1b24.x: Srinivasa Ramanujan worked with the British mathematician G.H. Hardy at Cambridge.
nd3be8ba1b24.tq: Identify the collaborator from a set of scientists connected with different fields.
xs: Ramanujan worked at **Cambridge** with **G.H. Hardy** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Amrit Lal Sircar** invited C.V. Raman to IACS; **P.M.S. Blackett** guided **Bibha Chowdhuri**'s PhD; **D.M. Bose** worked with Bibha on cosmic rays.
xa: **1729** is the **Hardy-Ramanujan number**.
Ramanujan: born **22 December 1887**, Erode (TN); died **1920**; **FRS 1918**, Fellow of Trinity College.

nf4411f71d0e.s: The number 1729 is popularly known as the:
nf4411f71d0e.x: The number 1729 is known as the Hardy-Ramanujan number.
nf4411f71d0e.tq: Recognise a famous numerical association rather than a date or institutional fact.
xs: **1729** is the **Hardy-Ramanujan number** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It recalls Ramanujan's collaboration with **G.H. Hardy** at **Cambridge**.
xa: **22 December** = **National Mathematics Day**; **2012** = **National Mathematical Year** (**125th** birth anniversary).
Ramanujan: **FRS 1918**.

n5981f8de491.s: The Raman Effect was discovered by C.V. Raman on 28 February 1928 at which institution?
o: Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science, Kolkata
n5981f8de491.x: C.V. Raman discovered the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928 at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science in Kolkata.
n5981f8de491.tq: Link the exact date of a discovery with its location and institution.
xs: Raman discovered the Raman Effect on **28 February 1928** at the **Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science (IACS), Kolkata** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Raman Research Institute** (**1948**) and **Indian Academy of Sciences** (**1934**) were founded by him later; he was IISc's first Indian director.
xa: Raman worked at IACS outside office hours while in the **Accountant General's Office**, Calcutta (from **1907**), invited by **Amrit Lal Sircar**.
IACS was founded in **1876** by **Mahendra Lal Sircar**; **150th anniversary in 2026**.
Raman Effect = change in **wavelength** of light when it scatters.

nea62c8f59e5.s: The Saha equation was formulated by Meghnad Saha from his theory of:
nea62c8f59e5.x: Meghnad Saha formulated the Saha, or ionisation, equation from his theory of thermal ionisation of elements.
nea62c8f59e5.tq: Link an equation to the theory from which it was derived.
xs: The Saha (ionisation) equation came from Saha's theory of **thermal ionisation of elements** — so option **(4)** is correct (UPPSC 2014).
**Plant response to stimuli** is **J.C. Bose**; **quantum statistics of bosons** is **S.N. Bose**.
xa: The Saha equation is a basic tool for reading **spectra of stars** (temperature, ionisation state).
Saha's instrument measures the **weight and pressure of solar rays**.
Saha: **FRS 1927**; elected to **Lok Sabha (1952)**.

nf4133e8026b.s: The Saha equation is a basic tool for reading stellar spectra because it helps determine the:
o: Distance and magnetic field of oceans
Temperature and ionisation state of stars
Age and chemical composition of plants
Mass and rotation of planets only
nf4133e8026b.x: The Saha equation helps interpret stellar spectra by indicating the temperature and ionisation state of stars.
nf4133e8026b.tq: Apply the scientific equation to the observational problem it is used to solve.
xs: The Saha equation helps read stellar spectra by giving the **temperature and ionisation state of stars** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It came from Saha's theory of **thermal ionisation**.
xa: Saha's area: **astrophysics**.
⚠ **Saha** = thermal ionisation; **Bhabha** = cosmic rays.
Saha came from **Dacca district** (now Bangladesh).

nbded0b158de.s: Meghnad Saha, regarded as the chief architect of river planning in India, prepared the original plan for the:
nbded0b158de.x: Meghnad Saha prepared the original plan for the Damodar Valley Project.
xa: Saha was elected to the **Lok Sabha** in **1952**.
He founded **NASI** (**1930**) and the **Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics** (Kolkata).
⚠ **Saha** = thermal ionisation + Damodar Valley plan.

nd47b100ecff.s: Which group of scientists all worked at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science, Kolkata?
o: Homi Bhabha, Vikram Sarabhai, Satish Dhawan and C.V. Raman
J.C. Bose, Meghnad Saha, S.N. Bose and C.V. Raman
Vikram Sarabhai, A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, Raja Ramanna and S.N. Bose
Srinivasa Ramanujan, Birbal Sahni, Homi Bhabha and Meghnad Saha
nd47b100ecff.x: J.C. Bose, Meghnad Saha, S.N. Bose and C.V. Raman all worked at IACS.
xa: Raman worked at IACS outside office hours while in the **Accountant General's Office** (from **1907**), invited by **Amrit Lal Sircar**.
IACS: founded **1876**; **150th anniversary in 2026**.

nphysics-4-5.s: Who is known as the Father of India’s Atomic Energy Programme?
nphysics-4-5.x: Homi J. Bhabha founded TIFR and BARC and is the father of India's atomic energy programme. C.V. Raman is known for the Raman effect.
nphysics-4-5.tq: Recall the founders of Indian science institutions.
n: Homi J. Bhabha is called the father of India's atomic energy programme. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
xs: **Homi J. Bhabha** is the **Father of India's atomic energy programme**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Niels Bohr** is the **Father of atomic physics**; **C.V. Raman** the **Father of Indian physics**.
**Ernest Rutherford** is the **Father of nuclear physics**.
xa: Bhabha was associated with **TIFR**.
**Enrico Fermi** is the **Architect of the Nuclear Age**.
**Oppenheimer** is often called the **father of the nuclear bomb**.

nphysics-9-8.s: The scientist Henri Becquerel was associated with which country?
nphysics-9-8.x: Becquerel was French; Marie Curie was associated with both Poland and France.
n: Marie Curie was associated with Poland. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
Marie Curie was associated with France. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
C.V. Raman was associated with India. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
Homi J. Bhabha was associated with India. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
Henri Becquerel was associated with France. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
xa: Curie worked at the **University of Paris** and the **Radium Institute**.
**Wilhelm Röntgen**, **Planck** and **Heisenberg** were from **Germany**.
Bhabha was associated with **TIFR**.

nbiology-13-4.x: J.C. Bose invented the crescograph to measure tiny plant growth and responses. Köhler and Milstein made hybridomas and Funk named vitamins.
n: The crescograph was invented by Jagadish Chandra Bose. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 20-21]
Hybridoma technology was invented by César Milstein. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 20-21]
Hybridoma technology was invented by Georges J. F. Köhler. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 20-21]
xs: The **Crescograph** was invented by **Jagadish Chandra Bose**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**César Milstein** and **Georges Köhler** developed **hybridoma technology**.
**Casimir Funk** gave the **concept of vitamins**.
xa: The Crescograph **measures plant growth**; Bose established that **plants have life**.
Bose founded the **Bose Institute, Kolkata** (**1917**).
⚠ **J.C. Bose** = plants + radio; **S.N. Bose** = bosons.

nf6050ff80ce.s: In which year did C.V. Raman found the Raman Research Institute in Bengaluru?
nf6050ff80ce.x: Raman founded the Raman Research Institute in 1948; he founded the Indian Academy of Sciences in 1934.
xa: Raman studied the harmonic nature of the **tabla and mridangam**.
Raman: **Nobel 1930**, **Bharat Ratna 1954**, knighted **1929**.

ndcd6c8c157d.s: Which of the following institutions was established in 1945?
ndcd6c8c157d.x: TIFR was founded in 1945; the Bose Institute dates from 1917, the Indian Academy of Sciences from 1934 and the Raman Research Institute from 1948.
xa: **NASI** was founded by Meghnad Saha in **1930**.
**Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay** (**1954**) was renamed **BARC** after Bhabha's death (**1967**).

n005c5c15ef8.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the honours received by C. V. Raman?
o: Nobel Prize in 1930, Bharat Ratna in 1954 and knighthood in 1929
Nobel Prize in 1954, Bharat Ratna in 1929 and knighthood in 1930
Nobel Prize in 1929, Bharat Ratna in 1930 and knighthood in 1954
FRS in 1930, Padma Bhushan in 1954 and knighthood in 1929
n005c5c15ef8.x: C. V. Raman received the Nobel Prize in 1930, was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1954 and was knighted in 1929.
n005c5c15ef8.tq: Use the exact year-and-honour combination to avoid swapped-date traps.
xs: Raman got the **Nobel Prize in 1930**, **Bharat Ratna in 1954** and **knighthood in 1929** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Options 2 and 3 shuffle these years; **Padma Bhushan 1954** was **Bhabha**'s.
xa: Raman's Nobel was India's first science Nobel — **first Asian and first non-White** science Nobel.
⚠ **1954** = Raman's Bharat Ratna + Bhabha's Padma Bhushan + S.N. Bose's Padma Vibhushan.

n414be0661e5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Homi Bhabha and S. N. Bose?
o: S. N. Bose became an FRS in 1941
Homi Bhabha received the Padma Bhushan in 1954
S. N. Bose received the Padma Vibhushan in 1954
Homi Bhabha became an FRS in 1941
n414be0661e5.x: S. N. Bose became an FRS in 1958; it was Homi Bhabha who became an FRS in 1941.
xa: Bhabha also won the **Adams Prize (1942)**.
S.N. Bose was made a **National Professor**.
⚠ **1954** also = Raman's **Bharat Ratna**.

nce0ba367c19.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about early Indian women scientists?
o: Kamala Sohonie was the first woman to obtain a D.Sc. from an Indian university
Anandibai Joshi earned an MD in Western medicine in 1886
Kamala Sohonie was the first woman admitted to IISc
Asima Chatterjee obtained a D.Sc. from Calcutta University in 1944
nce0ba367c19.x: The first woman D.Sc. from an Indian university was Asima Chatterjee (Calcutta, 1944), not Kamala Sohonie.
xa: ⚠ **Kamala Sohonie** = first science **PhD** (Cambridge, **1939**) — APPSC-G1 2024.
Sohonie's field: **biochemistry**.

n6321a02fe86.s: Who was the first woman General President of the Indian Science Congress (1975)?
n6321a02fe86.x: Asima Chatterjee, also the first woman D.Sc. of an Indian university (Calcutta, 1944), became the first woman General President of the Indian Science Congress in 1975.
xa: Her field: **organic chemistry**.
⚠ First science **PhD** = **Kamala Sohonie** (**1939**).

n9ea195fd013.s: Anna Mani is popularly known as the ‘Weather Woman of India’ primarily because of her work in which field?
o: Meteorological instruments, solar radiation and wind energy
Cosmic rays, mesons and particle detectors
n9ea195fd013.x: Anna Mani contributed to making India self-reliant in meteorological instruments and worked on solar radiation and wind energy. She also served as Deputy Director-General of the India Meteorological Department.
n9ea195fd013.tq: Infer the field from the descriptive title and the associated applications.
xs: **Anna Mani**, the "Weather Woman of India", made India self-reliant in **meteorological instruments, solar radiation and wind energy** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Organic chemistry/anti-malarials = **Asima Chatterjee**; sugarcane breeding = **Janaki Ammal**; cosmic rays and mesons = **Bibha Chowdhuri**.
xa: Anna Mani served as **Deputy DG, IMD**.
Her field: **physics, meteorology**.

n38295985de9.s: Who was the first Indian woman to obtain a PhD in a science discipline (Cambridge, 1939)?
n38295985de9.x: Kamala Sohonie, a biochemist, earned her PhD from Cambridge in 1939 and was also the first woman admitted to IISc. Asima Chatterjee was the first woman to get a D.Sc. from an Indian university (Calcutta, 1944). Janaki Ammal was a pioneer of plant breeding, and Anna Mani is known as the 'Weather Woman of India'.
n38295985de9.tq: Sohonie = first science PhD; Chatterjee = first D.Sc.
xs: **Kamala Sohonie** was the first Indian woman to get a **PhD in a science discipline** (Cambridge, **1939**) — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-G1 2024).
**Asima Chatterjee** was the first woman **D.Sc.** (Calcutta, **1944**); **Janaki Ammal** pioneered plant breeding; **Anna Mani** is the "Weather Woman of India".
xa: Sohonie was also the **first woman admitted to IISc**; her field was **biochemistry**.
⚠ **Anandibai Joshi** = first Western-medicine degree (**1886**).

nbiology-14-24.s: The plant geneticist known for breeding high-yield 'Super Rice' is:
nbiology-14-24.x: Gurdev Singh Khush, a plant geneticist, bred high-yield super rice.
n: Gurdev Khush Singh worked on Super Rice. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 21-24]
Gurdev Khush Singh worked in plant genetics and agriculture. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 21-24]
Gurdev Khush Singh developed high-yield rice. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 21-24]
xa: **J.C. Bose** studied **plant growth** with the **Crescograph**.
**Ian Wilmut and Keith Campbell** — **Dolly cloning** (somatic-cell cloning).
**Karl von Frisch** — **bee communication** by **dance**.

nphysics-4-6.s: The hydrogen spectrum was explained by:
nphysics-4-6.x: Bohr explained the hydrogen spectrum; Planck explained black-body radiation, Einstein the photoelectric effect and Maxwell unified electromagnetism.
n: Albert Einstein explained the photoelectric effect. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
Max Planck explained black-body radiation. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
Niels Bohr explained the hydrogen spectrum. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
James Clerk Maxwell developed the unified theory of electromagnetism. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
xa: **Brownian motion** was also explained by **Einstein**.
**Raman effect** — **inelastic scattering of light** — by **C.V. Raman**.
**Faraday:** **electromagnetic induction** and the **field concept**.

nphysics-4-13.s: Who is known as the man who 'weighed the Earth'?
nphysics-4-13.x: Henry Cavendish is called the man who weighed the Earth; Oppenheimer is the father of the atomic bomb and Bohr of atomic physics.
n: Niels Bohr is called the father of atomic physics. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
C. V. Raman is called the father of Indian physics. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
Henry Cavendish is known as the man who weighed the Earth. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
Oppenheimer is often called the father of the nuclear bomb. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
xa: **Max Planck** is the **Father of quantum mechanics**.
**Thomas Edison** is **America's greatest inventor**.
**Michael Faraday** is the **Father of Electricity**.

nphysics-9-15.s: Who is known as the Father of Quantum Theory?
nphysics-9-15.x: Max Planck is the Father of Quantum Theory; Bohr is the Father of Atomic Physics, Raman of Indian Physics and Bhabha of India's nuclear programme.
n: Niels Bohr is known as the Father of Atomic Physics. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
Max Planck is known as the Father of Quantum Theory. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
C.V. Raman is known as the Father of Indian Physics. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
Homi J. Bhabha is known as the Father of the Indian Nuclear Programme. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
xa: Bohr worked at the **University of Copenhagen**, **Denmark**.
Planck was at the **University of Berlin**.
Raman worked at **IACS** and **IISc**.

nphysics-9-16.s: Who is known as the 'Architect of the Nuclear Age'?
nphysics-9-16.x: Enrico Fermi is called the architect of the nuclear age; Michael Faraday is known as the father of electricity.
n: Michael Faraday is popularly known as the Father of Electricity. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
Enrico Fermi is known as the Architect of the Nuclear Age. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
xa: Fermi worked on the **controlled nuclear reaction** — **Chicago Pile-1**.
Faraday is linked to **electromagnetic induction** and **electrochemistry**.
**Oppenheimer** — **father of the nuclear bomb**.

nphysics-9-5.s: Albert Einstein was associated with which of the following institutions?
nphysics-9-5.x: Einstein worked at Princeton's Institute for Advanced Study; Rutherford was at the Cavendish Laboratory and Manchester, and Bohr at Copenhagen.
n: Ernest Rutherford was associated with the Cavendish Laboratory. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
Ernest Rutherford was associated with Manchester. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
Niels Bohr was associated with the University of Copenhagen. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
Niels Bohr was associated with the Institute for Theoretical Physics. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
Albert Einstein was associated with the Princeton Institute for Advanced Study. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 21-23]
xa: **J.J. Thomson** was also at the **Cavendish Laboratory, Cambridge**.
**Fermi** → **University of Chicago** and **Columbia**.
**Marie Curie** → **University of Paris** and the **Radium Institute**.

nebdc3332fff.s: The particle class 'bosons', named after S.N. Bose, was named by:
nebdc3332fff.x: Paul Dirac coined the name 'bosons'; Bose had sent his paper 'Planck's Law and the Hypothesis of Light Quanta' to Einstein (1924).
xa: ⚠ **Bosons** named by **Dirac**; paper translated by **Einstein**.
BEC was observed in space by NASA experiments on the **ISS**.
Tagore's **Visva-Parichay** (**1937**) was dedicated to S.N. Bose.

n113ffad182b.s: The Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science (IACS), Kolkata, was founded in 1876 by:
n113ffad182b.x: IACS was founded in Kolkata in 1876 by Mahendra Lal Sircar.
n113ffad182b.tq: Match the institution with its founder and founding year.
xs: IACS, Kolkata was founded in **1876** by **Mahendra Lal Sircar** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It celebrates its **150th anniversary in 2026**.
xa: It is the oldest institute for basic research; funded by **DST** + **West Bengal**.
**J.C. Bose, Saha, S.N. Bose and Raman** all worked there.
⚠ **Amrit Lal Sircar** invited Raman to IACS — do not confuse with founder Mahendra Lal Sircar.

nfa7dd19f79a.s: National Mathematics Day, marking the birthday of Srinivasa Ramanujan, is observed on:
nfa7dd19f79a.x: Ramanujan was born on 22 December 1887, and that date is observed as National Mathematics Day.
xa: Ramanujan was born in **Erode** (TN) and died in **1920**.
**1729** = Hardy-Ramanujan number.

nfc5ded9b3fd.s: Rabindranath Tagore dedicated his only science book, *Visva-Parichay*, to:
nfc5ded9b3fd.x: Rabindranath Tagore dedicated *Visva-Parichay*, published in 1937, to S. N. Bose.
nfc5ded9b3fd.tq: Link the literary work, its year and its dedicatee rather than its scientific subject.
xs: Tagore dedicated **Visva-Parichay**, his only science book (**1937**), to **S. N. Bose** — so option **(1)** is correct.
S.N. Bose is the physicist of **Bose-Einstein Statistics**.
xa: S.N. Bose's paper **"Planck's Law and the Hypothesis of Light Quanta"** (**1924**) was sent to **Einstein**.
⚠ **J.C. Bose** wrote **Response in the Living and Non-Living** (**1902**) and **The Nervous Mechanism of Plants**.

nbiology-13-3.s: The Jarvik-7 artificial heart was made by:
nbiology-13-3.x: Robert Jarvik made the Jarvik-7 artificial heart; Hans Berger developed the EEG.
n: The Jarvik-7 was invented by Robert Jarvik. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 20-21]
The electroencephalogram was invented by Hans Berger. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 20-21]
The Jarvik-7 is an artificial heart. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 20-21]
xa: **Hybridoma technology** — **César Milstein** and **Georges Köhler**.
**Biorock technology** — **Wolf Hilbertz**.
**Concept of vitamins** — **Casimir Funk**.

nbiology-13-5.s: Biorock reef technology was invented by:
nbiology-13-5.x: Wolf Hilbertz invented Biorock technology; Robert Jarvik made the Jarvik-7 artificial heart.
n: The Jarvik-7 was invented by Robert Jarvik. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 20-21]
Biorock technology was invented by Wolf Hilbertz. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 20-21]
The Jarvik-7 is an artificial heart. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #13 · pp 20-21]
xa: **EEG** was invented by **Hans Berger**.
**Crescograph** — **Jagadish Chandra Bose**.
**Hybridoma technology** — **Milstein** and **Köhler**.

n407e13f60cd.s: INCOSPAR, headed by Vikram Sarabhai from 1962, became ISRO in:
n407e13f60cd.x: INCOSPAR became ISRO in 1969, and Sarabhai served as ISRO's first Chairman until his death in 1971.
xa: Sarabhai is the **Father of the Indian space programme**.
He was also **Chairman, Atomic Energy Commission** (**1966**).
He led planning for **SITE** (**1975-76**), TV education to **2,400 villages**.

n6b96c8b8c3a.s: Which institution was founded by Vikram Sarabhai in Ahmedabad in 1947?
n6b96c8b8c3a.x: Vikram Sarabhai founded the Physical Research Laboratory in Ahmedabad in 1947. The Community Science Centre was established in 1965, while TERLS was set up near Thiruvananthapuram.
n6b96c8b8c3a.tq: Use the founding year and location to distinguish among institutions associated with Sarabhai.
xs: Sarabhai founded the **Physical Research Laboratory**, Ahmedabad, in **1947** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **Community Science Centre**, Ahmedabad, came in **1965**; **TERLS** is near **Thiruvananthapuram**; **Darpana Academy** was with **Mrinalini Sarabhai**.
xa: TERLS was renamed **Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre**.
The **Chandrayaan-2 lander "Vikram"** is named after him.

n59790e1cf19.s: Who was the first Chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)?
n59790e1cf19.x: Vikram Sarabhai was the first Chairman of ISRO. Satish Dhawan, Brahm Prakash and U.R. Rao are other prominent figures associated with India’s space programme.
n59790e1cf19.tq: Apply the first-in-office cue while distinguishing among closely associated space-science leaders.
xs: **Vikram Sarabhai** was ISRO's **first Chairman** — so option **(3)** is correct.
He headed **INCOSPAR (1962)**, which became ISRO in **1969**, and served until his death in **1971**.
xa: **Satish Dhawan** later oversaw **Aryabhata**; **U.R. Rao** was Chairman **1984-94**.
Sarabhai is the **Father of the Indian space programme**.

n49ce6471d65.s: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan is associated with which of the following scientific discoveries?
o: Development of the first artificial satellite
Atomic structure of the 30S ribosomal subunit
Structure of the DNA double helix
n49ce6471d65.x: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan is known for determining the atomic structure of the 30S ribosomal subunit, which provided insight into protein synthesis.
n49ce6471d65.tq: Use the scientist–discovery association and distinguish ribosomal research from unrelated landmark discoveries.
xs: Ramakrishnan determined the **atomic structure of the 30S ribosomal subunit** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It gave insight into **protein synthesis**.
xa: He worked at the **MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology, Cambridge**.
**Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2009** with **Thomas A. Steitz and Ada Yonath**.
⚠ **1968** Medicine = Khorana (genetic code); **2009** Chemistry = Ramakrishnan (ribosome).

n84aba96d766.s: Har Gobind Khorana received the Nobel Prize for:
o: Determining the structure of the 30S ribosomal subunit
Interpreting the genetic code and its role in protein synthesis
Discovering the structure of the neutron
n84aba96d766.x: Khorana was recognised for interpreting the genetic code and explaining its role in protein synthesis.
xa: Khorana was an **Indian-origin American molecular biologist**.
He made the **first synthetic gene** from **oligonucleotides**.

nf041585d7d9.s: M.S. Swaminathan was described by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) as the:
nf041585d7d9.x: UNEP called M.S. Swaminathan the 'Father of Economic Ecology' (UPPSC 2007). He is the architect of India's Green Revolution. The Blue Revolution is fisheries and the White Revolution is milk (linked to Verghese Kurien), and 'Father of Green Chemistry' is not his title.
nf041585d7d9.tq: Swaminathan: UNEP = Father of Economic Ecology; first World Food Prize 1987.
xs: **UNEP** called Swaminathan the **"Father of Economic Ecology"** — so option **(2)** is correct (UPPSC 2007).
He is the architect of India's **Green Revolution**.
xa: He chaired the **National Commission on Farmers** (**18 November 2004**).
He founded **MSSRF**, Chennai.

n244bee82dac.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about A.P.J. Abdul Kalam?
o: He is called the 'Missile Man of India'
He was project director of SLV-3, which put Rohini in orbit in 1980
He led the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme
He was the 11th President of India from 2007 to 2012
n244bee82dac.x: Kalam was the 11th President from 2002 to 2007, not 2007 to 2012.
xa: Kalam played a key role in **Pokhran-II (1998)**.
He flew the **Sukhoi-30 MKI** (**2006**) — first President to fly a fighter.
Kalam received the **Bharat Ratna** in **1997**; ⚠ "Missile Woman" = **Tessy Thomas**.

nd58c4a5139f.s: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2009 jointly with:

Thomas A. Steitz and Ada Yonath

Robert W. Holley and Marshall W. Nirenberg

nfb9542d96dc.s: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan, winner of the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, was born at:

n71e18a00f21.s: M.S. Swaminathan received the first World Food Prize in:

n30ce5796703.s: M.S. Swaminathan was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2024:

during his lifetime for work in space science

nc3510f7a6cc.s: Tessy Thomas is popularly known as the “Missile Woman” because she was associated with:

nd6b1657767b.s: Yellapragada SubbaRow, associated with important contributions to biochemistry and medicine, was born at which place?

nf07bee363da.s: The Fiske–SubbaRow method is associated with the study of the role of which substances in muscle?

n48891505ab8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Yelavarthy Nayudamma?

SubbaRow worked on **folic acid**, **methotrexate**, **aureomycin** and **Hetrazan**.

nec585a6d095.s: The COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal was constituted in 1990 for:

n7e71d309009.s: Who became the first Indian woman and the fourth Indian to win the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal in 2026?
n7e71d309009.x: Annapurni Subramaniam won the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal in 2026, becoming the first Indian woman and the fourth Indian recipient.

n89939a4fcd3.s: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for studies of the:

Structure and function of the ribosome
n89939a4fcd3.x: Ramakrishnan shared the 2009 Chemistry Nobel for studies of the structure and function of the ribosome.

n1aa9b694174.s: In which year did Har Gobind Khorana receive the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine?

nab17a82cdfe.s: Abhijit Banerjee shared the 2019 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for
o: the mathematical theory of black holes
an experimental approach to alleviating global poverty
the discovery of the Raman Effect
research on the structure of the ribosome

xa: Earlier Indian Economics laureate: **Amartya Sen** (**1998**).

n11f9b6986f8.s: Who among the following received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913?

nda90c50efe5.s: S. Chandrasekhar received the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on:

n3bd6ebcc724.s: C.V. Raman became the first Indian scientist Nobel laureate in:

nf442c92463d.s: How many Padma Awards were conferred in 2025?

n31083c34f7d.s: The UNESCO Kalinga Prize for the popularisation of science was instituted in 1952 with a donation from:

n5e79e0fca1b.s: Which of the following is NOT a category of the Infosys Prize?

n1f3e7925827.s: The J.C. Bose Fellowship or Grant is associated with

n89ebdd22aed.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about types of computers?

Digital computers, such as PCs, process discrete (binary) data

n309e53bafaf.s: Which one of the following was the first commercial microprocessor?

n675064c6cd3.s: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) is best understood as an umbrella term covering devices and applications used to
