xa: ICT aims at human-human, human-machine and **M2M** communication.
Criticisms: **privacy risks**, **digital divide**, job insecurity, over-reliance on technology.

n3fb9507e721.s: Which component of the CPU fetches and decodes program instructions?
n3fb9507e721.x: The control unit fetches, decodes and directs; the ALU does arithmetic and logic, and the PSU only supplies power.
xa: The **CPU** is the computer's **"brain"**.
The **motherboard** links components; **GPUs** handle **graphics/AI**.
Speed order: **registers > cache > RAM > SSD > HDD**.

n95149c84d08.s: Which one of the following devices can function as both an input and an output device?
n95149c84d08.x: A touch screen displays output and also receives input through touch.
n95149c84d08.tq: Apply the input-output classification to a dual-function device.
xs: A **touch screen** is both an input and an output device — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Keyboard** and **microphone** are input only; **plotter** is output only.
xa: Input devices also include **barcode reader**, **OCR**, **MICR** (cheques), **OMR** (answer sheets).
Output devices: monitor, printer, **plotter**, speaker, projector.

n7ef57142668.s: Which of the following is an impact printer?
n7ef57142668.x: Dot-matrix and daisy-wheel printers are impact printers; laser, inkjet and thermal printers are non-impact.
xa: A **plotter** is an output device.
A **touch screen** is both **input and output**.
**MICR** reads **cheques**; **OMR** reads **answer sheets**.

n9c96a221d91.s: A nibble in computer terminology consists of
n9c96a221d91.x: A nibble is a group of four bits.
n9c96a221d91.tq: Recall the fixed-size relationship between binary storage units.
xs: A **nibble = 4 bits** — so option **(4)** is correct.
A **byte = 8 bits**; the **bit** is the smallest unit (APPSC 2025).
xa: Order: bit < nibble < byte < **KB (1,024 bytes)** < MB < GB < TB < PB < EB < ZB < YB.
**ASCII** is **7-bit** with **128** characters.

n0d0632d94df.s: Which type of RAM is used as cache memory?
n0d0632d94df.x: SRAM is used as cache, while DRAM is used as main memory.
xa: **Cache** is small, very fast memory between **CPU and RAM**.
⚠ **EPROM** is erased by **UV**; **EEPROM** is erased **electrically**.
**Byte = 8 bits**; **nibble = 4 bits** (**APPSC 2025**).

nc9fb18a4fa9.s: Which of the following has the highest access speed?
nc9fb18a4fa9.x: The speed order is registers, cache, RAM and magnetic tape.
xa: **Registers** are inside the **CPU**.
**Magnetic tape** is **sequential access**, used for backup and archival.

nb2a1abcea35.s: Which secondary storage is sequential-access and mainly used for backup and archival?
nb2a1abcea35.x: Magnetic tape is sequential-access, the slowest in the speed order, and used for backup and archival; an SSD uses flash memory with no moving parts.
xa: **HDD** uses magnetic **spinning disks**.
**DVD** holds **4.7 GB** single layer; **Blu-ray** **25 GB** (blue-violet laser).
Speed order: **registers > cache > RAM > SSD > HDD > optical disc > magnetic tape**.

n7bf8ad5d5e9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about types of operating systems?
o: Real-time operating systems have no fixed response deadlines
In a time-sharing OS such as UNIX, many users share CPU time
Real-time operating systems are used in missile guidance and air-traffic control
A batch OS groups jobs and runs them without user interaction
n7bf8ad5d5e9.x: Real-time OS work to fixed response deadlines, which is why they are used for missile guidance and air-traffic control.
xa: Real-time OS are **hard** or **soft**.
**Distributed / network** OS link many machines.

n6f7bb61ddc2.s: The Android mobile operating system, associated with Google, is based on:
n6f7bb61ddc2.x: Android is Linux-based and associated with Google; iOS is Apple's, and BharOS was developed at IIT Madras.
xa: CLI examples: **MS-DOS**, **UNIX shell**; GUI examples: **Windows**, **macOS**.
**Linux** kernel was written by **Linus Torvalds** (**1991**).

ncaefd624676.s: A language translator that translates and runs a program line by line is called a/an:
ncaefd624676.x: An interpreter translates and executes line by line, while a compiler translates the whole program before execution.
xa: Assembly language is converted by an **assembler**.
All three are **language translators** (system software).

n093e5d8607e.s: Which of the following are known as universal gates?
n093e5d8607e.x: NAND and NOR are the universal gates; AND, OR and NOT are the basic gates.
xa: Boolean algebra was given by **George Boole**.
**De Morgan**: (A+B)' = A'.B'.

n000321e587e.s: The Boolean identity (A + B)′ = A′ · B′ is known as:
n000321e587e.x: (A + B)′ = A′ · B′ is De Morgan's law.
xa: Boolean algebra: **George Boole**.
**NAND** and **NOR** are universal gates.

n9127c2c8f1e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about computer performance terms?
o: Bandwidth is the data-transfer rate, measured in bits per second
Word length is the number of bits the CPU handles at once
Clock speed is measured in bits per second
MIPS stands for million instructions per second
n9127c2c8f1e.x: Clock speed is measured in hertz (GHz); bits per second is the unit of bandwidth.
xa: **FLOPS** = **floating-point operations per second** — supercomputer speed.
The **Linpack (HPL) benchmark** is the basis of world supercomputer rankings.
Word length examples: **32-bit**, **64-bit**.

n8bc68a1fb7c.s: Which benchmark measures floating-point performance while solving large dense linear systems and forms the basis of world supercomputer rankings?
n8bc68a1fb7c.x: The Linpack, or HPL, benchmark measures floating-point power in solving large dense linear systems and is used for world supercomputer rankings.
n8bc68a1fb7c.tq: Identify the benchmark from its distinctive workload and ranking application.
xs: The **Linpack (HPL) benchmark** measures floating-point power on **large dense linear systems** and underlies world supercomputer rankings — so option **(1)** is correct.
**ASCII** and **Unicode** are character codes, and **MIPS** counts instructions — none rank supercomputers.
xa: Results are in **FLOPS**.
**ISC 2026** list: China's **LineShine** replaced US **El Capitan** at the top.

ndb37ed12bf0.s: According to the ISC 2026 list, the world's fastest supercomputer is:
ndb37ed12bf0.x: China's LineShine topped the ISC 2026 supercomputer list, replacing the United States' El Capitan.
xa: Rankings use the **Linpack (HPL)** benchmark in **FLOPS**.
**Param Shakti**: **3.1 petaflops**, C-DAC **RUDRA** servers.

nc143219d7a8.s: The 3.1-petaflop supercomputer Param Shakti was launched by MeitY at:
nc143219d7a8.x: Param Shakti, funded under the National Supercomputing Mission, was launched by MeitY at IIT Madras.
xa: World's fastest (**ISC 2026**): China's **LineShine**, replacing US **El Capitan**.
**Q-Day:** when quantum computers can break **RSA-2048**.
Quantum computers use **qubits** — **superposition** and **entanglement**.

n254ba73cc7f.s: Q-Day refers to the point at which quantum computers may be capable of
o: breaking RSA-2048 public-key encryption using Shor’s algorithm
converting every file into PDF format
increasing the clock speed of classical processors
n254ba73cc7f.x: Q-Day denotes the anticipated point when quantum computers can break RSA-2048 public-key encryption through Shor’s algorithm, proposed in 1994.
n254ba73cc7f.tq: Link the specialised term to its specific security consequence and algorithm.
xs: **Q-Day** is when quantum computers can break **RSA-2048 public-key encryption** using **Shor's algorithm** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Shor's algorithm dates from **1994**.
xa: Quantum computers use **qubits** (superposition, entanglement).
Quantum applications include **cryptography** and **optimisation**.

n2699a037f91.s: ASCII is a ____-bit character-encoding scheme representing 128 characters.
n2699a037f91.x: ASCII is a 7-bit code (2^7 = 128 characters); Unicode extends its range.
xa: ASCII = **American Standard Code for Information Interchange**.
A **byte** = **8 bits**; a **nibble** = **4 bits**.

nacb926f71fb.s: ICT aims to facilitate communication among:
nacb926f71fb.x: ICT aims at efficient human-human, human-machine and machine-to-machine communication.
xa: ICT covers **mobiles, networks, software, internet, satellites**.
⚠ Concerns include the **digital divide** and **privacy risks**.

n1092974fdcf.s: A barcode is best described as
o: a printed image converted into editable text
a two-dimensional matrix of square modules
machine-readable vertical bars of varying widths
a magnetic character sequence used on cheques
n1092974fdcf.x: A conventional barcode consists of machine-readable vertical bars of varying widths.
n1092974fdcf.tq: Distinguish barcode, QR code, OCR and MICR by physical form and function.
xs: A barcode is **machine-readable vertical bars of varying widths** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2019).
A **2-D matrix** is a **QR code**; converting printed text is **OCR**; cheque characters are read by **MICR**.
xa: **OMR** reads answer sheets.
Mouse-to-computer communication is **simplex** (one-way) (APPSC 2019).

ne260a4432e6.s: The communication from a computer mouse to the computer is an example of which transmission mode?
ne260a4432e6.x: A mouse only sends signals to the computer, so the communication is one-way, or simplex (APPSC 2019). Half duplex is two-way but one direction at a time, as in a walkie-talkie. Full duplex is two-way at once, as in a telephone. Multiplexing combines several signals on one channel; it is not a direction mode.
xs: A mouse sends signals one way only — **simplex** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC 2019).
The data flows only from mouse to computer, never back — that one-way flow defines **simplex**.
xa: The mouse was invented by **Douglas Engelbart**.
Other input devices: **keyboard, scanner, joystick, light pen, microphone, webcam**.

nbde258dcdd8.s: The pictorial representation of an algorithm is called a:
nbde258dcdd8.x: A flowchart is the pictorial form of an algorithm, which is a finite step-by-step procedure (APPSC 2019). Pseudocode is an English-like text outline, a compiler is a language translator, and source code is the written program.
nbde258dcdd8.tq: Algorithm in pictures = flowchart; in English-like text = pseudocode.
xs: The pictorial form of an algorithm is a **Flowchart** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC 2019).
**Pseudocode** is an **English-like outline**; a **compiler** is a translator.
xa: An **algorithm** is a **finite step-by-step procedure**.
Flowchart symbols: **oval** = start/end, **diamond** = decision.

n94f6040fe3f.s: ARPANET, established in 1969, was developed under which organisation and is regarded as the forerunner of the Internet?
n94f6040fe3f.x: ARPANET was developed under the United States Department of Defense in 1969 and became the forerunner of the Internet.
n94f6040fe3f.tq: Link the historical network with its sponsoring organisation and legacy.
xs: **ARPANET** (**1969**) was developed under the **US Department of Defense** — so option **(1)** is correct.
ARPANET is regarded as the **forerunner of the internet**.
**W3C** was founded by **Tim Berners-Lee** in **1994** — it sets web standards, it did not build ARPANET.
xa: The **WWW** was invented by **Tim Berners-Lee** in **1989** at **CERN**.
India's firsts: **ERNET** (**1986**, academic network) → **VSNL** public internet (**15 August 1995**) → **Satyam Infoway (Sify)**, first private ISP (**1998**).
⚠ Do not confuse the **internet** (ARPANET lineage, 1969) with the **WWW** (Berners-Lee, 1989).

n3542c6c3f2c.s: VSNL launched public internet in India on:
n3542c6c3f2c.x: VSNL launched public internet on 15 August 1995, after ERNET (1986) and before Satyam Infoway became the first private ISP (1998).
xa: Global milestones: **ARPANET** (**1969**) → **WWW** (**1989**, CERN) → **W3C** (**1994**).
**ICANN** (**1998**) coordinates the global domain name system and IP address allocation.
**NIXI** (**2003**) runs India's internet exchange points and the **.in registry**.

n6df720371e8.s: A firm linking its LANs in Mumbai, Bengaluru and New Delhi is using a:
n6df720371e8.x: Linking LANs in different cities needs a WAN; a MAN covers only a city and a PAN links personal devices (APPSC 2019).
xa: A **LAN** covers an office, home or campus.
A **WAN** spans large areas and links LANs — **the internet is a global WAN**.
A **VPN** is an encrypted **"tunnel"** over a public network.

n7a72959b7bc.s: A Virtual Private Network primarily provides:
o: A replacement for all network protocols
A wireless connection restricted to one room
A physical cable exclusively owned by a user
An encrypted tunnel over a public network
n7a72959b7bc.x: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel through a public network, improving the privacy of communication.
n7a72959b7bc.tq: Identify the function rather than the physical form of the network.
xs: A **VPN** provides an **encrypted tunnel over a public network** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It does not replace protocols, is not a one-room wireless link and is not a privately owned cable.
xa: Network types by scope: **PAN** (personal, Bluetooth) → **LAN** (office/home/campus) → **MAN** (a city) → **WAN** (large areas).
**The internet is a global WAN**.
**HTTPS** also encrypts browser-server traffic, via **TLS**.

n6ac44766ab1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about network topologies?
o: In a bus topology, all nodes share one backbone cable
In a star topology, failure of one node stops the whole network
In a ring topology, each node is linked to two neighbours
A mesh topology links every node to every other node
n6ac44766ab1.x: In a star, a failed node is only isolated; it is a hub failure that stops the whole network.
xa: A **tree** is a hierarchy of star networks; a branch fails if its parent fails.
In a **bus**, a backbone break stops the whole network.
A firm linking LANs in Mumbai, Bengaluru and New Delhi uses a **WAN** (**APPSC 2019**).

ncedc9a74bee.s: Which network device forwards frames using MAC addresses?
ncedc9a74bee.x: A switch forwards frames by MAC address; a hub broadcasts to all ports, a router routes by IP and a modem converts signals.
xa: A **repeater** regenerates a weak signal (Physical layer); a **bridge** works like a switch (layer 2).
A **gateway** joins networks that use **different protocols** (all/upper layers).
Modem = **Modulator-demodulator**.

n9858c787405.s: Which of the following represents the correct top-to-bottom order of the OSI model?
o: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical
Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
Application, Session, Presentation, Network, Transport, Data Link, Physical
Presentation, Application, Session, Transport, Data Link, Network, Physical
n9858c787405.x: From the top layer downward, the OSI model is Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link and Physical.
n9858c787405.tq: Use the first and last layers, then verify the middle sequence.
xs: Top to bottom: **Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) is the bottom-to-top order; options (3) and (4) swap layers.
xa: Layer **7 Application**: **HTTP, FTP, SMTP, DNS**.
Layer **4 Transport**: **TCP, UDP**; layer **3 Network**: **IP**, router.
Layer **2 Data Link**: **MAC addresses**, switch, bridge, NIC; layer **1 Physical**: cables, hub, repeater.

nb1af8516cbe.s: Which protocol assigns IP addresses automatically?
nb1af8516cbe.x: DHCP assigns IP addresses automatically; DNS turns domain names into IP addresses and TCP ensures reliable delivery.
xa: ⚠ **SMTP** sends mail; **POP3** downloads and deletes; **IMAP** keeps mail on the server.
**MAC address** = **48 bits**; **IPv4** = **32 bits**; **IPv6** = **128 bits**.
Three elements of a protocol: **syntax**, **semantics**, **timing**.

ncf904f1ba5c.s: NIXI, the not-for-profit body under MeitY that runs the .in registry and IRINN, was established in:
ncf904f1ba5c.x: NIXI was established in 2003 and runs internet exchange points, the .in registry and IRINN.
xa: **BhashaNet** (**2022**) is a MeitY-NIXI initiative for **Universal Acceptance**.
**ICANN** (**1998**) coordinates the global domain name system.
**IDNs** are domain names in local scripts, e.g. **.Bharat** in Devanagari.

n2016445e002.s: A website opens for users of one ISP but not for users of another. This is consistent with:
o: Expiry of the website's domain name
ISP-level DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering
n2016445e002.x: ISPs may block sites through DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering, so access can differ between ISPs; the other causes would affect all users.
xa: **SNI filtering** is used to block **HTTPS** sites.
Government can order ISPs to block content under **Sections 69A and 79** of the **IT Act, 2000**.
**DNS** turns domain names into IP addresses — poisoning it misdirects users.

n103f0b0fb08.s: Chief Minister Naidu and Sunil Mittal discussed which of the following for Andhra Pradesh?
o: Last-mile connectivity, data centres and an undersea cable landing station
Coal mining, irrigation dams and inland waterways
Satellite launching and missile testing facilities
Steel plants, minor ports and airports
n103f0b0fb08.x: The discussion concerned last-mile connectivity, data centres and an undersea cable landing station for Andhra Pradesh.
xa: **BharatNet** fibre reaches **2.18 lakh gram panchayats** (ES 2025-26).
Connections rose from **25.15 crore (2014)** to **96.96 crore (2024)**.
**Satellite internet** needs no terrestrial wire (space, ground, VSAT segments).

n5be9343d7ed.s: In a URL, which part comes immediately after the protocol (such as https://)?
n5be9343d7ed.x: A URL has the protocol, then the domain name, then the path to the file.
xa: **URL** = **Uniform Resource Locator**.
**DNS** turns the domain name into a numerical **IP address**.
**NIXI** runs India's **.in registry**.

n4d79ebd22d4.s: ICANN, established in 1998 as a United States non-profit organisation, is primarily associated with:
o: Coordinating the global domain name system and IP address allocation
n4d79ebd22d4.x: ICANN coordinates the global Domain Name System and IP address allocation. It was established in 1998 as a US non-profit organisation.
n4d79ebd22d4.tq: Use the organisation-function and year combination.
xs: **ICANN** (**1998**) **coordinates the global domain name system and IP address allocation** — so option **(4)** is correct.
India's **.in registry** is run by **NIXI**, not ICANN.
xa: ICANN is a **US non-profit**.
**NIXI** (**2003**), under **MeitY**, runs internet exchange points, the .in registry and **IRINN**.
**BhashaNet** (**2022**, MeitY-NIXI) promotes **Universal Acceptance** for Indian languages.

n9aa51a7d473.s: An IPv6 address is how many bits long?
n9aa51a7d473.x: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits (eight hexadecimal groups); IPv4 is 32 bits and a MAC address 48 bits.
xa: IPv4 offers **~4.3 billion** addresses.
A MAC address = **6 bytes**, **12 hex digits**; used at the **data link** layer.
**DNS** only turns names into IP addresses.

n46fed6d94c9.s: The first-octet range of IPv4 Class D (multicast) addresses is:
n46fed6d94c9.x: Class D is 224–239 for multicast; 240–255 is Class E, 192–223 Class C and 128–191 Class B.
xa: **127.x.x.x** is the **loopback** range.
Classes are decided by the **first octet**.
IPv4 is **32 bits**; IPv6 is **128 bits**.

n4e250e0abcd.s: Communication through a walkie-talkie is an example of which transmission mode?
n4e250e0abcd.x: Half duplex allows two-way transmission one at a time, as in a walkie-talkie; radio/TV is simplex and a telephone call full duplex.
xa: A **keyboard** is another simplex example.
Connection media: **DSL** (telephone copper), **cable** (coaxial TV cable), **fibre** (light pulses).

n36440e7c307.x: DSL uses telephone copper lines; cable internet uses coaxial TV cable and fibre internet uses light pulses in optical fibre.
xa: **Simplex** = one way; **half duplex** = both ways one at a time; **full duplex** = both at once.
**Li-Fi** carries data on **LED light**.
**Wi-Fi Direct** links devices with no LAN.

nd7dbec71847.s: Bluetooth, a personal area network (PAN) technology, follows the IEEE standard:
nd7dbec71847.x: Bluetooth follows IEEE 802.15.1, while Wi-Fi follows IEEE 802.11.
xa: Bluetooth uses the **2.4 GHz ISM band**; microwave ovens and cordless phones share 2.4 GHz.
**Li-Fi** carries data on **LED light** — better bandwidth and security than Wi-Fi.
The **2019** APPSC key gave **Bluetooth 5.1** as the latest version.

n7dd1120d6fc.s: HTTP primarily specifies which of the following?
o: How messages pass between web browsers and web servers
How domain names are converted into IP addresses
How wireless devices communicate within a PAN
How e-mails are downloaded to a device
n7dd1120d6fc.x: HTTP specifies the communication of messages between web browsers and web servers. DNS, POP3 and Bluetooth serve different functions.
n7dd1120d6fc.tq: Match the protocol with its immediate communication function rather than with a neighbouring networking function.
xs: **HTTP** sets **how messages pass between web browsers and web servers** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Turning domain names into IP addresses is **DNS**.
Downloading e-mail to a device is **POP3**; PAN devices use **Bluetooth**.
xa: **HTTPS** encrypts browser-server traffic via **TLS**.
HTTP is an **Application** layer (**7**) protocol.
Three elements of a protocol: **syntax** (format), **semantics** (meaning), **timing** (when and how fast).

n20cca932072.s: Which of the following indexes webpages so that they can be found?
n20cca932072.x: A search engine indexes pages; a web server stores and serves them and a browser displays them.
xa: ⚠ Exam angle: "which one displays webpages" = **browser**; "which one stores them" = **server**.
**URL** parts: **protocol** + **domain name** + **path to the file**.
The **surface web** (~**4-5%**) is the part indexed by search engines.

n5dc502c6388.s: The principal role of the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) is to:
o: Assign MAC addresses to network cards
Operate the global DNS root servers
n5dc502c6388.x: W3C develops and maintains web standards so that webpages function consistently across different browsers.
n5dc502c6388.tq: Identify the responsible body by its standard-setting function.
xs: **W3C** **develops and maintains web standards** so pages work the same across browsers — so option **(1)** is correct.
MAC addresses are **burnt into the network card**; the global domain name system is coordinated by **ICANN**.
xa: W3C was founded by **Tim Berners-Lee** in **1994**.
Berners-Lee invented the **WWW** in **1989** at **CERN**.
Core front-end technologies: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript**.

n7511a9a3333.s: What does the abbreviation SIM stand for in mobile telephony?
n7511a9a3333.x: SIM stands for Subscriber Identity Module, the card that identifies the subscriber on a mobile network. The other expansions are invented.
n7511a9a3333.tq: Test the exact expansion of a commonly confused telecommunications abbreviation.
xs: **SIM** stands for **Subscriber Identity Module** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The other expansions are made up; SIM has nothing to do with "Internet" or "Memory".
xa: The **first handheld call** was made by **Martin Cooper** (Motorola) on **3 April 1973**.
**Mobile Number Portability** began within a circle on **20 Jan 2011**, after a **Haryana** pilot on **25 Nov 2010**.
Generations: **1G (1980s) → 5G** now; **6G** expected in the early **2030s**.

nc896eea0b91.s: The dominant 4G technology, which uses OFDM and MIMO, is:
nc896eea0b91.x: 4G runs on LTE using OFDM and MIMO; WiMAX lost out to LTE.
xa: Mobile generations run **1G (1980s) → 5G now → 6G**.
**Martin Cooper** (Motorola) made the first handheld call on **3 April 1973**.
Android is Google's mobile OS built on the **Linux kernel**.

n16e4ddd1588.s: The first handheld mobile phone call was made on 3 April 1973 by:
n16e4ddd1588.x: Martin Cooper of Motorola made the first handheld mobile call on 3 April 1973. Bell is linked with the telephone, Marconi with radio, and Jack Dorsey co-founded Twitter.
xs: **Martin Cooper** of **Motorola** made the first handheld call on **3 April 1973** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Jack Dorsey** co-founded **Twitter** (**2006**), not the mobile phone.
xa: **MNP** began within a circle on **20 Jan 2011**.
**SIM** = Subscriber Identity Module.
**6G** is expected in the early **2030s**.

n32def74cca8.s: QR (Quick Response) codes were designed in 1994 for the car industry by:
n32def74cca8.x: Denso Wave designed QR codes in Japan in 1994 for the car industry.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **"1996"** is wrong — the APPSC **2019** key was "only a".
**NFC** works at a few cm and **106-424 kbps**.
RBI allowed **offline UPI Lite payments over NFC**.

n536828c00fa.s: Which one of the following is an m-governance application that crowdsources reports of inaccessible places?
n536828c00fa.x: The Sugamya Bharat app crowdsources reports of inaccessible places and belongs to the m-governance sector.
n536828c00fa.tq: Identify the application from its distinctive real-world use.
xs: **Sugamya Bharat** app crowd-sources reports of **inaccessible places** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**SWAYAM** = free online courses (m-learning); **eHospital** and **NowClinic** are m-health.
xa: Another m-governance app: **UMANG** (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance).
**eSanjeevani** = telemedicine; **Tele-MANAS** = tele mental health.
**Agrimarket** = m-agriculture (prices **within 50 km**).

n798dfedbe04.s: Since 2016, LinkedIn has been owned by:
n798dfedbe04.x: LinkedIn has been owned by Microsoft since 2016; Facebook belongs to Meta.
xa: LinkedIn (**Reid Hoffman**, **2003**) = **professional networking**.
Twitter / X = **micro-blogging**.
The **hashtag** was popularised on **Twitter**.

nba1501228c4.s: Hashtag (#) was popularised on which social-media platform?
nba1501228c4.x: The hashtag (#) was popularised on Twitter (APPSC 2019), the micro-blogging platform founded by Jack Dorsey and others in 2006 and renamed X in 2023. Facebook and LinkedIn are networking sites and Amazon is an e-commerce company.
nba1501228c4.tq: Associate the content term with the platform that popularised it, not merely a platform where it is used.
xs: The **hashtag (#)** was popularised on **Twitter** (APPSC **2019**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Facebook** is social networking; **LinkedIn** is professional networking.
xa: Twitter was founded by **Jack Dorsey** and others (**2006**); renamed **X** (**2023**).
Twitter is a **micro-blogging** platform.
**Folksonomy** = user-created tagging (social tagging).

n52eb0fe87df.s: In which year was Twitter renamed X?
n52eb0fe87df.x: Twitter was renamed X in 2023; LinkedIn was founded in 2003, Facebook in 2004, and LinkedIn came under Microsoft in 2016.
xa: ⚠ The notes give **LinkedIn (2003)** before **Facebook (2004)** — by the notes the order is C, D, B, A.
Twitter was founded in **2006** by **Jack Dorsey** and others.
Facebook's parent is **Meta**.
n52eb0fe87df.fixed: LinkedIn 2003 precedes Facebook 2004, so order is C, D, B, A

o: A single e-commerce platform owned by one seller
A payment gateway regulated by RBI
n149027008d5.x: ONDC is a network-based protocol, not a single platform; it connects buyer and seller apps across B2C and B2B and aims to help MSMEs.
xa: ONDC was **beta-tested in Bengaluru**.
**Digital India** (**11 years**, 2015-2026) is built on JAM, eSanjeevani, GeM, **ONDC** and AgriStack.
**D2C** = brand sells directly to the consumer.

nfe6dc73ce7b.s: As per the textbook position, 100% FDI under the automatic route in e-commerce is permitted in:
nfe6dc73ce7b.x: 100% FDI under the automatic route is allowed in the marketplace model, while FDI is not permitted in the inventory model.
xa: The **Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020** cover both **marketplace and inventory** entities.
They require a **grievance officer** and display of **country of origin**.
**ONDC** is an open protocol helping **MSMEs**.

n2b99625b982.s: The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 are framed under the:
n2b99625b982.x: The Rules are under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and cover both marketplace and inventory entities.
xa: **IT Rules, 2021** regulate social media, **OTT** and digital news.
**Code on Social Security, 2020** defined **gig and platform workers** for the first time.

n8ca5eb8ae92.s: The IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 were framed under which section of the IT Act?
n8ca5eb8ae92.x: The Rules were framed under Section 87; Section 79 is the safe-harbour provision.
xa: **IT Amendment Rules, 2023:** platforms ignoring orders on false content lose **safe harbour**.
**Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020** require display of **country of origin**.
**50 OTT platforms** were blocked over two years for obscenity or IT Act violations.

n5eb1ddf831e.s: Under the IT Amendment Rules, 2023, an intermediary ignoring government orders on false content may lose safe-harbour protection under Section ____ of the IT Act.
n5eb1ddf831e.x: Safe-harbour protection is under Section 79, which an intermediary may lose for not complying with such orders.
xa: The rules were **amended again in Feb 2026**.
**Sections 69A and 79** let government order ISPs and intermediaries to block content.

nc13d46f2b05.s: Under the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, the Online Gaming Authority of India is a digital attached office of the:
o: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
nc13d46f2b05.x: OGAI is a digital attached office of MeitY, not the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting; the Act also banned real-money gaming.
xa: Rules notified **Apr 2026**; effective **1 May 2026**.
Also called the **"Online Gaming (Regulation) Act, 2025"** in some summaries.
WHO lists **Gaming Disorder** in **ICD-11**.

n77e258971e2.s: Gig and platform workers were defined for the first time in the:
o: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
n77e258971e2.x: The Code on Social Security, 2020 first defined gig and platform workers; aggregators contribute to their social-security fund.
xa: The **Online Gaming Act, 2025** banned **real-money gaming**.
It created the **Online Gaming Authority of India (OGAI)** under MeitY.
The gaming rules took effect on **1 May 2026**; **e-sports** registration is mandatory.

nc7678c1f7de.s: Which body includes Gaming Disorder in ICD-11?
nc7678c1f7de.x: The World Health Organization lists Gaming Disorder in ICD-11.
nc7678c1f7de.tq: Match the health classification with the responsible international body.
xs: The **World Health Organization (WHO)** lists **Gaming Disorder** in **ICD-11** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Other digital-age terms like **nomophobia**, **FOMO** and **doomscrolling** are not formal disorders in the notes.
xa: **NIMHANS, Bengaluru** runs the **SHUT Clinic** (Service for Healthy Use of Technology).
The **Online Gaming Act, 2025** banned **real-money gaming**.
Kerala Police run **D-DAD** centres.

nb593fcc4eb6.s: Which of the following is NOT a central measure concerning screen time and digital addiction?
o: PRAGYATA framework of the Ministry of Education
nb593fcc4eb6.x: Agmarknet is related to agricultural market information. Central measures include the Ministry of Education's PRAGYATA framework, CBSE safe-internet guidelines, NCPCR screen-time guidelines and a plan to widen Tele-MANAS for digital addiction.
nb593fcc4eb6.tq: Identify the unrelated programme among measures addressing screen use and digital addiction.
xs: **Agmarknet** is an agricultural market-price source, not a screen-time measure — so option **(4)** is correct.
Central measures: MoE's **PRAGYATA**, **CBSE** safe-internet guidelines, **NCPCR** screen-time guidelines.
xa: Plan to widen **Tele-MANAS** to cover **digital addiction**.
Agmarknet feeds the **Agrimarket** app (markets **within 50 km**).
**NIMHANS** runs the **SHUT Clinic**.

n2754db87517.s: The proposed separate law on age-based access to social media is reported to favour:
o: A ban limited only to digital news platforms
A blanket ban for every person below 18 years
Graded limits based on age rather than a blanket ban
n2754db87517.x: The proposed approach favours graded limits based on age instead of imposing a blanket ban on all persons below a specified age.
n2754db87517.tq: Focus on the contrast between graded regulation and an absolute prohibition.
xs: The proposed law favours **graded limits based on age rather than a blanket ban** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is a separate law on **age-based social-media access**.
xa: **DPDP Act**: anyone **below 18** is a child; **verifiable parental consent** needed (**Sec 9**).
**Australia** = world's first nationwide **under-16** ban, effective **10 Dec 2025**.
⚠ AP's ban = **under 13**; Karnataka's = **under 16**.

n3fcdf0b7587.s: Which e-mail field sends copies to several recipients without revealing their addresses to one another?
n3fcdf0b7587.x: BCC (blind carbon copy) hides the recipients' addresses from one another.
xa: **SMTP** sends mail; **POP3/IMAP** receive it.
An e-mail address = **username @ domain name**.

nb6b849a934a.s: Which one of the following is NOT among the essentials of video conferencing?
nb6b849a934a.x: Video conferencing needs a camera, microphone, speaker/display, a broadband link and conferencing software (codec). An RFID reader is used to read RFID tags and is not a video-conferencing component.
nb6b849a934a.tq: VC kit: camera, mic, speaker/display, broadband, codec.
xs: An **RFID reader** is not a video-conferencing essential — so option **(4)** is correct.
Essentials: **camera, microphone, speaker/display, broadband link and conferencing software (codec)**.
xa: Multimedia components: **text, images/graphics, audio, video, animation**.
Telemedicine apps like **eSanjeevani** rely on such video links.
TV broadcasting methods: terrestrial, cable, satellite/**DTH**, IPTV/OTT.

nb4b888d999f.s: Which was the first Indian news agency to offer syndicated video news?
nb4b888d999f.x: ANI, established in 1971, was the first Indian news agency to offer syndicated video news.
xa: **e-journals** are published on the **Internet** (APPSC **2019**).
TV broadcasting: terrestrial, cable, satellite/**DTH**, IPTV/OTT.

nd789b030f69.s: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, a 'child' is anyone below the age of:
nd789b030f69.x: The DPDP Act treats anyone below 18 as a child, and Section 9 requires verifiable parental consent for a child's data.
xa: India's upcoming law favours **graded limits** over a blanket ban.
⚠ AP's ban = **under 13**; Karnataka's = **under 16**.
**Digital India** completed **11 years** (2015-2026).

n403702a86bc.s: Near Field Communication (NFC) works over a range of:
n403702a86bc.x: NFC works over only a few centimetres at 106-424 kbps and uses less power than Bluetooth.
xa: **QR code** = **Quick Response**, designed in **1994** by **Denso Wave** (Japan).
First handheld call: **Martin Cooper** (Motorola), **3 April 1973**.
**Mobile Number Portability** began within a circle on **20 Jan 2011**.

n42d9a69fcf4.x: e-journals are electronic journals published on the Internet. Printed paper and microfilm are physical formats, and television broadcasting carries audio-visual programmes, not journals.
xs: **e-journals** are published on **the Internet** (APPSC **2019**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
They are electronic, not print, microfilm or TV broadcast.
xa: m-learning includes **SWAYAM** courses, **e-books** and e-journals.
Multimedia components: text, images/graphics, audio, video, animation.
**ANI** (**1971**) first offered syndicated video news in India.

n02c37ab5953.s: The defining technology of Industry 3.0 was:
n02c37ab5953.x: Industry 1.0 used steam, 2.0 electricity and mass production, 3.0 computers and electronics, and 4.0 cyber-physical systems.
xa: **Industry 5.0** puts **human-machine collaboration** and people at the centre.
The term **Fourth Industrial Revolution** was coined by **Klaus Schwab** (WEF founder) in **2016**.
⚠ **3.0** = automation and computers; **4.0** = cyber-physical systems.

naa5e53f8a63.s: Steam-powered weaving looms are characteristic of:
naa5e53f8a63.x: Steam-powered looms belong to Industry 1.0, while Industry 4.0 is marked by cyber-physical systems, IoT, AI and big data.
xa: Industry 4.0 brings **smart factories**, where digital, physical and biological technologies converge.
**SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0** (Ministry of Heavy Industries) spreads Industry 4.0 via demonstration centres.
AP has an **Industry Policy 4.0** (**24 Apr 2026**).

n5cfa34a44a5.s: A system in which computing is tightly integrated with physical processes, a core element of Industry 4.0, is called a:
n5cfa34a44a5.x: A cyber-physical system integrates computing closely with physical processes and is central to Industry 4.0 and NM-ICPS.
xa: Cyber-physical systems are the **core of Industry 4.0**.
India's **NM-ICPS** mission targets them; it runs **25 Technology Innovation Hubs**.
⚠ **3.0** = automation; **4.0** = cyber-physical systems.

n1a0ad02c3e5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding IoT and AI?
o: IoT devices collect and exchange data through sensors
A smart thermostat is an example of AI rather than IoT
AI analyses data, recognises patterns and makes decisions
Chatbots and image recognition are examples of AI
n1a0ad02c3e5.x: A smart thermostat is listed as an IoT example, not an AI example.
xa: IoT is **rule-based, limited learning**; AI uses **machine and deep learning**.
A **fitness wearable** is another IoT example.

n2863249b23b.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of wearable devices such as smartwatches and fitness bands?
o: Producing steam power for industrial machinery
Tracking heart rate, steps and sleep
n2863249b23b.x: Wearables track health indicators, support biometric authentication and act as IoT end-devices; they do not produce steam power.
xa: IoT applications: smart farming, smart homes, smart grids, **healthcare**, logistics, smart cities.
A **fitness wearable** is an IoT (not AI) example.

n3c92d5fafd3.s: The humanoid robot Manav was developed by:
n3c92d5fafd3.x: Manav was developed by A-SET Training & Research Institutes, Delhi, not Genrobotics.
xa: Manav is India's **first 3D-printed humanoid** (**2017**).
**DRDO CAIR** builds unmanned and multi-agent robotic systems.
⚠ **Bandicoot** = sewers; **HomoSEP** = septic tanks.

n1a076ed1baa.x: ISO 10218 covers industrial-robot safety, not surgical robots; ISO TC 299 is the robotics committee.
xa: MeitY's inter-ministerial committee (convener **Secretary MeitY**) is drafting a robotics ecosystem strategy.
Members: **DoT, DSIR, DST, DPIIT, NITI Aayog**.

n5977374dd84.s: A fully computer-generated world that shuts out the real world is created by:
n5977374dd84.x: A fully computer-generated world is VR; AR places digital layers over the real world and XR is an umbrella term for VR, AR and MR.
xa: In **VR** the user is still a **real person** (**APPSC 2024**).
**Metaverse** is a shared 3D virtual space using **XR** and **avatars**.
**VARCoE** is at **IIT Bhubaneswar**.

o: A network limited to industrial robots
Only computers connected through wired networks
A system in which data can be exchanged only after manual approval
Devices with sensors linked in a network and exchanging data without human intervention
nc8552929b5b.x: IoT consists of sensor-equipped devices connected through networks that exchange data without human intervention.
nc8552929b5b.tq: Select the precise definition and reject restrictive qualifiers such as ‘only’.
xs: **IoT** = **devices with sensors linked in a network, exchanging data without human intervention** — so option **(4)** is correct.
This definition was asked in APPSC **2023** and **2024**.
xa: IoT three-layer model: **perception** (sensors, RFID) → **network** → **application**.
The **mMTC** slice of **5G** serves dense IoT sensors.
IoT applications: smart farming, smart homes, **smart grids**, healthcare, logistics, smart cities.

n7dc7cd9bf2b.s: In 5G, the mMTC (massive machine-type communication) slice is meant for:
n7dc7cd9bf2b.x: mMTC supports dense IoT sensor deployments in 5G networks.
xa: **NDCP 2018** covers **5G, IoT and M2M**.
IoT devices exchange data **without human intervention**.
**DHRUV64** (C-DAC) is a **RISC-V** processor for **5G, IoT, automotive**.

n302bcfa4f76.s: Which policy covers 5G, the Internet of Things (IoT) and machine-to-machine (M2M) communication?
n302bcfa4f76.x: The National Digital Communications Policy (NDCP) 2018 covers 5G, IoT and M2M. The Drone Rules 2021 govern drones, the IT Rules 2021 regulate intermediaries and digital media, and the E-Commerce Rules 2020 protect online consumers.
xs: **NDCP 2018** (National Digital Communications Policy) covers **5G, IoT and M2M** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Drone Rules, 2021** set drone weight classes; they do not cover 5G or IoT.
xa: The **mMTC** slice of 5G serves dense IoT sensors.
IoT is also part of **Digital India**.
MeitY-NASSCOM **IoT CoEs** include **Visakhapatnam**.

neab85f98593.s: Which district was offered for aerospace, drone and semiconductor manufacturing under the stated Andhra Pradesh proposal?
neab85f98593.x: Sri Sathya Sai district, near Bengaluru, was offered for aerospace, drone and semiconductor manufacturing.
neab85f98593.tq: Use the precise district-location association; do not substitute a nearby technology centre.
xs: **Sri Sathya Sai district** (near **Bengaluru**) was offered — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was pitched for **aerospace, drone and semiconductor** manufacturing (**5 Jun 2026**).
xa: **WEF** Fourth Industrial Revolution Centre in AP = India's **3rd**, after **Mumbai** and **Telangana**.
AP has an **Industry Policy 4.0** (**24 Apr 2026**).
**JNTU Kakinada** + Efftronics launched an **M.Tech in IoT**.

nd843ccd85c5.s: Printing that adds materials which change shape over time is called:
nd843ccd85c5.x: 4D printing adds materials that change shape over time; additive manufacturing (3D printing) builds layer by layer from a CAD model.
xa: India's first **3D-printed post office**: **Bengaluru**, **2023**.
3D printing is used for **prosthetics** and **implants**.
**Additive manufacturing** is a course area under **FutureSkills PRIME**.

n96dceb37aed.s: A semi-passive RFID tag differs from an active RFID tag because the semi-passive tag:
o: Uses its battery to run the chip but uses the reader’s field to reply
Has no internal power and cannot contain identity data
Has an independent transmitter and broadcasts over a long range
Uses only a satellite signal for communication
n96dceb37aed.x: A semi-passive tag’s battery powers its chip, but it still uses the reader’s field to send its response. An active tag has its own battery and transmitter.
n96dceb37aed.tq: Focus on the exact distinction between battery use and transmission capability.
xs: A **semi-passive** tag's **battery runs the chip only**; it **uses the reader's field to reply** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Having an independent **transmitter** and broadcasting over long range describes an **active** tag.
xa: **Passive** tags have **no internal battery** and backscatter the reader's signal.
⚠ Trap: passive tags are **not** powered by an internal circuit (APPSC-G1 **2022**).
RFID sits in the **perception** layer of IoT.

na2829037b6f.s: An RFID tag that has its own battery and transmitter is called a(n):
na2829037b6f.x: An active tag has its own battery and transmitter; a passive tag has no battery and backscatters the reader's signal.
xa: ⚠ This is the **APPSC-G1 2022** trap (key: **II and IV only**).
**Semi-passive**: battery runs the chip only; still replies via the reader's field.
Passive tags are **cheap, short range**; active tags broadcast over **long range**.

n87795311d61.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three-layer model of the Internet of Things, from the device-facing layer to the user-facing layer?
n87795311d61.x: The three-layer IoT model consists of the perception layer, network layer and application layer. The perception layer senses, the network layer transmits and the application layer provides smart services.
n87795311d61.tq: Recall the ordered layers and their functional progression.
xs: The three layers are **perception, network, application** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Perception**: sensors, **RFID**; **network**: transmission; **application**: smart services.
xa: Variants: **IIoT** (industrial automation), **IoNT** (nano-devices), Internet of Mobile Things, mission-critical IoT (military).
IoT is **rule-based** with limited learning; **AI** uses machine and deep learning.

ne085b0cd45f.s: Drone swarms are best described as:
o: Large drones operated manually by a single pilot from different locations
Many drones coordinated by software for surveillance, light shows or strikes
Drones restricted exclusively to agricultural spraying
Fixed-wing aircraft that cannot exchange operational data
ne085b0cd45f.x: A drone swarm consists of many drones coordinated through software and may be used for surveillance, light shows or strikes.
ne085b0cd45f.tq: Choose the definition that captures both coordinated operation and the stated applications.
xs: **Swarms** are **many drones coordinated by software** for **surveillance, light shows or strikes** — so option **(2)** is correct.

xa: **Swarm robotics** is a listed robotics trend.
Drone types: **fixed-wing, multi-rotor, hybrid VTOL**.
**DRDO CAIR** builds unmanned and **multi-agent** robotic systems.

nb356e018b4c.s: Kisan drones are primarily associated with which of the following activities?
o: Operating light shows and conducting strikes
nb356e018b4c.x: Kisan drones are used to spray crops and map land; 100 were flagged off in February 2022.
nb356e018b4c.tq: Link the named agricultural technology to its direct field applications.
xs: **Kisan drones** **spray crops and map land** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**100** were flagged off in **Feb 2022**.
Light shows and strikes are uses of drone **swarms**.
xa: **Namo Drone Didi** gives drones to **women SHGs** for agri-services.
IoT application: **smart farming**.

n4f51302d94f.s: The Namo Drone Didi initiative is associated with providing drones to:
o: women’s Self-Help Groups for agricultural services
DGCA training institutes for flight certification
n4f51302d94f.x: Namo Drone Didi provides drones to women’s Self-Help Groups for agricultural services.
n4f51302d94f.tq: Identify the beneficiary group and purpose together rather than relying on the programme name alone.
xs: **Namo Drone Didi** gives drones to **women SHGs** for **agri-services** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is distinct from **DGCA-approved training institutes**, which train pilots.
xa: **Kisan drones** spray crops and map land (**100** flagged off, **Feb 2022**).
**Drone Shakti** backs **Drone-as-a-Service** startups.
**PLI** covers drones and components.

n43802d76cd2.s: Which robot was developed to clean manholes and sewers to end manual scavenging?
n43802d76cd2.x: Bandicoot (Genrobotics, Kerala) cleans manholes and sewers; HomoSEP cleans septic tanks, Daksh defuses IEDs and Vyommitra is ISRO's half-humanoid.
xa: Bandicoot was asked in **APPSC-G2 2025**.
**SSI Mantra** = India's first indigenous surgical robotic system.
**Manav** (A-SET, Delhi) = first 3D-printed humanoid (**2017**).

n60d4012d555.s: India's first indigenous surgical robotic system is:
n60d4012d555.x: SSI Mantra is India's first indigenous surgical robotic system; Manav is India's first 3D-printed humanoid (2017).
xa: Bandicoot cleans **sewers** to end **manual scavenging** (**APPSC-G2 2025**).
**Vyommitra** (ISRO) is the half-humanoid for **Gaganyaan**.
**Daksh** (DRDO) handles and defuses **IEDs**.

n7a12bbf0523.s: Which of the following is NOT a measure identified for making India a global drone hub by 2030?
o: A ban on DGCA-approved training institutes
Production Linked Incentive for drones and components
n7a12bbf0523.x: The measures include liberalised Drone Rules, 2021, DigitalSky, PLI, Drone Shakti, DGCA-approved training institutes and Bharat Drone Mahotsav. A ban on such institutes is contrary to the stated approach.
n7a12bbf0523.tq: Identify the option that reverses a supportive policy into a restrictive one.
xs: **A ban on DGCA-approved training institutes** is not a measure — the policy **promotes** them — so option **(3)** is correct.
Tools: liberalised **Drone Rules, 2021**, **DigitalSky**, **PLI** for drones, **Drone Shakti**, DGCA-approved institutes.
xa: Aim: India as a **global drone hub by 2030**.
**Bharat Drone Mahotsav** is also part of the push.
AP offered **Sri Sathya Sai district** for aerospace, drone and semiconductor manufacturing.

ne4d6895aca3.s: The India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) was launched in:
ne4d6895aca3.x: The ISM was launched in 2021 with a ₹76,000 crore PLI outlay.
xa: ISM results: **56 chips fabricated at 180 nm**; Chips to Startup reaches **397 universities**.
Semicon 2.0 offers up to **40%** capital subsidy for CMOS silicon fabs.
⚠ **DHRUV64** = C-DAC, 64-bit; **Vikram 3201** = ISRO SCL, 32-bit.

n299a6ddda8e.s: Under Semicon 2.0, the capital subsidy for CMOS silicon fabs is up to:
n299a6ddda8e.x: CMOS silicon fabs get up to 40%; compound and display fabs get 35%, R&D up to 75% and conventional packaging 25%.
xa: Advanced **OSAT/ATMP** gets **35%**.
Semicon 2.0 outlay: **₹1,27,500 crore** (**2 Sep 2026**).
Talent pillar: **1 lakh** more engineers.

n23979e538d8.s: SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0, which spreads Industry 4.0 through demonstration centres, is an initiative of the:
n23979e538d8.x: SAMARTH (Smart Advanced Manufacturing and Rapid Transformation Hub) Udyog Bharat 4.0 is a Ministry of Heavy Industries initiative.
xa: **NDCP 2018** covers **5G, IoT and M2M**.
**IoT CoEs** (MeitY-NASSCOM): **Bengaluru, Gurugram, Gandhinagar and Visakhapatnam**.
Robotics is a vertical of the **25 Technology Innovation Hubs** under **NM-ICPS**.

n29e70bcf436.s: The IoT Centres of Excellence established through the MeitY-NASSCOM initiative are located at:
n29e70bcf436.x: The MeitY-NASSCOM IoT Centres of Excellence are located at Bengaluru, Gurugram, Gandhinagar and Visakhapatnam.
n29e70bcf436.tq: Check the complete location list rather than identifying only one familiar city.
xs: The **MeitY-NASSCOM** IoT CoEs are at **Bengaluru, Gurugram, Gandhinagar and Visakhapatnam** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Hyderabad** hosts the **IMAGE CoE**, not an IoT CoE.
xa: ⚠ IoT CoEs include **Visakhapatnam**; **IMAGE** = Hyderabad; **VARCoE** = **IIT Bhubaneswar**.
Efftronics + **JNTU Kakinada** launched an industry-sponsored **M.Tech in IoT** (Jul 2026).
**Digital India** includes IoT; **NDCP 2018** covers 5G, IoT and M2M.

ne760d337cce.s: India’s first 3D-printed post office, identified as an example of rapid construction, was established in:
ne760d337cce.x: India’s first 3D-printed post office was established in Bengaluru in 2023.
ne760d337cce.tq: Combine the landmark, location and year in one recall unit.
xs: India's first **3D-printed post office** was set up in **Bengaluru** in **2023** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is listed under **construction** uses of 3D printing.
xa: Other uses: **food** (custom shapes), **health** (prosthetics, implants), automotive prototypes, aerospace parts.
India's first 3D-printed **humanoid**: **Manav** (**2017**).

nd1bd743d713.s: The VR/AR Centre of Excellence (VARCoE), set up by MeitY and STPI with Odisha, is located at:
nd1bd743d713.x: VARCoE is at IIT Bhubaneswar with Odisha as partner; the IMAGE CoE, partnered by Telangana, is at Hyderabad.
xa: ⚠ IoT CoEs (MeitY-NASSCOM) include **Visakhapatnam**.
**XR** = umbrella for VR + AR + MR.

n723dce929e4.s: The World Economic Forum’s proposed Fourth Industrial Revolution Centre in Andhra Pradesh would be India’s:
o: first such centre after Mumbai and Telangana
fourth such centre after Bengaluru, Mumbai and Telangana
third such centre after Mumbai and Telangana
n723dce929e4.x: The proposed centre in Andhra Pradesh would be India’s third, after the centres in Mumbai and Telangana.
n723dce929e4.tq: Count the ordinal position from the explicitly named earlier locations.
xs: The **WEF** centre in AP would be India's **third**, after **Mumbai** and **Telangana** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is a **Fourth Industrial Revolution Centre**.
xa: The term **Fourth Industrial Revolution** was coined by **Klaus Schwab**, founder of **WEF**, in **2016**.
AP has an **Industry Policy 4.0** (**24 Apr 2026**).

n6e73806157f.s: With reference to Virtual Reality (VR), which one of the following is correct?
o: It overlays digital layers on the real world, as in Pokemon Go.
It creates a fully computer-generated, immersive world in which the user is still a real person.
It replaces the user with a computer-generated avatar who is not a real person.
It is the umbrella term covering AR and MR.
n6e73806157f.x: VR is a fully computer-generated, immersive world; the person experiencing it is still a real person (APPSC 2024). Overlaying digital layers on the real world is AR, and the umbrella term for VR, AR and MR is XR.
n6e73806157f.tq: VR = fully virtual world, real user (APPSC 2024).
xs: **VR** creates a **fully computer-generated, immersive world** in which the user is **still a real person** — so option **(2)** is correct.
This was the APPSC **2024** angle.
Digital layers over the real world (e.g. **Pokemon Go**) is **AR**; the umbrella for VR, AR and MR is **XR**.
xa: **MR**: real and virtual objects interact in real time.
The **metaverse** is a persistent, shared **3D** virtual space using XR, avatars and digital assets.
**VARCoE** (VR/AR Centre of Excellence) is at **IIT Bhubaneswar**.

nd6b6562ebf6.s: Which one of the following best describes Narrow or Weak Artificial Intelligence (ANI)?
o: A system designed to perform one specific task and unable to transfer across domains
A system that learns only through physical interaction with humans
A system capable of human-level reasoning across all domains
A hypothetical system surpassing humans in every way
nd6b6562ebf6.x: Narrow or Weak AI is designed for a single task, such as voice assistance or content recommendation, and cannot transfer its capability across domains.
nd6b6562ebf6.tq: Use the precise meaning of the technical term and distinguish it from neighbouring AI categories.
