xs: "Digital freedom with digital responsibility" means **online dialogue should be constructive and privacy should be respected** — so option **(1)** is correct.

o: Irrational fear of being without one's mobile phone
Fear of receiving unsolicited friend requests
Fear of sharing personal information online

ndb5f7255443.x: Filter bubbles arise because algorithms prioritise content by user preference, isolating users from other viewpoints.
xa: Filter bubbles **isolate users from other viewpoints** (echo chambers).
Counter: **NEP 2020** critical thinking, media literacy, fact-checkers.

ndce87d181cf.s: Which of the following is a characteristic of a responsible digital citizen?
o: Disclosing personal data to establish trust
ndce87d181cf.x: A responsible digital citizen identifies misinformation, verifies sources, protects personal data, respects privacy and participates in civil discourse.
ndce87d181cf.tq: Choose the behaviour that combines verification with responsible digital participation.
xs: A responsible digital citizen is marked by **identifying misinformation and verifying sources** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The citizen also **protects personal data**, so disclosing it is wrong, and engages in **civil discourse** rather than withdrawing.
Forwarding everything is the risk: **one misleading forward** → panic, violence or reputational damage.
xa: Rights side: **online grievance redressal**, **e-consultations**, **open government data**.
AP example: **Grama and Ward Sachivalayam** system.

n2a9e65d482c.s: False content spread without any intent to deceive is called:
n2a9e65d482c.x: Misinformation is false content spread without intent to deceive; disinformation is deliberately created false content and malinformation is genuine information shared to cause harm.
xa: ⚠ **Mis**information = no intent; **Dis**information = deliberate; **Mal**information = genuine info shared to harm.
**Filter bubbles/echo chambers** isolate users from other viewpoints.
Fake news is driven by **profit motive** and causes **polarisation**.

n016cce0f274.s: Which one of the following is NOT recommended as an online safety practice?
o: Being cautious while sharing personal or sensitive information
Accepting friend requests from unknown persons without caution
n016cce0f274.x: Accepting friend requests from unknown persons without caution is not a safe online practice. Strong passwords, verification before sharing and caution with sensitive information are recommended.
n016cce0f274.tq: Find the one unsafe practice among otherwise safe digital habits.
xs: **Accepting friend requests from unknown persons without caution** is not recommended — so option **(4)** is correct (APPSC PYQ).
Recommended: **strong passwords**, **verifying information before sharing**, caution with **personal/sensitive information**.
xa: Exam angle: "which is NOT a **safe practice**" and **odd-one-out** questions.
Authentication methods: **passwords, biometrics, multi-factor authentication**.

na43df3d9c3b.s: A person receives a message from a friend urgently asking for money. Which is the safest immediate course of action?
o: Verify the request through another channel before making any payment
Transfer the money immediately because the request came from a known contact
Scan a QR code sent by the friend to receive the money
Click the accompanying link to confirm the friend's identity
na43df3d9c3b.x: A friend's account or identity may have been hacked, so the request should be independently verified before payment. Links or QR codes should not be clicked or scanned to receive money.
na43df3d9c3b.tq: Apply the cyber-hygiene rule to a realistic digital-fraud situation.
xs: **Verify the request through another channel before making any payment** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The "friend's" ID **may be hacked**, so don't rush to pay.
**Never click a link or scan a QR code to receive money** — options (3) and (4) are traps.
xa: Source: **Telangana Cyber Security Bureau**, **#OnlineButUnafraid**, **20 Mar 2026**.
Keep your **digital footprint low**; use **WPA3** Wi-Fi.
Report cyber fraud at **cybercrime.gov.in / 1930**.

n58c4594961a.s: The Digital Detox initiative of the Karnataka Government was undertaken with which organisation and focused on which area?
o: I4C; takedown notices and court orders
n58c4594961a.x: The Karnataka Government's Digital Detox initiative was undertaken with the All India Game Developers Forum and addressed gaming and social-media use.
n58c4594961a.tq: Match the initiative with its partner organisation and subject area.
xs: Karnataka's **Digital Detox** was done with **AIGDF** (All India Game Developers Forum) on **gaming and social-media use** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-G2 **2025** PYQ).
**PIB FCU** debunks government-related fake news; **I4C** runs **SAHYOG** takedowns.
xa: WHO lists **Gaming Disorder** in **ICD-11**.
**UK** announced a social-media ban for **under-16s**.

ne78184b6360.s: The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 treats which combination as important educational emphases and a counter-measure against fake news?
o: Anonymous posting and reduced classroom discussion
Only vocational licensing and biometric enrolment
ne78184b6360.x: NEP 2020 stresses critical thinking and civic engagement. Critical-thinking education in curricula can help counter fake news.
ne78184b6360.tq: Select the constructive educational pair rather than digital behaviours that amplify misinformation.
xs: **NEP 2020** stresses **critical thinking and civic engagement** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Critical-thinking education is a **fake-news counter-measure**.
xa: Other counter-measures: **media-literacy programmes**, **fact-checkers**, platform policies to remove/down-rank fake content.
**Minors** lack skills to tell truth from misinformation.

n7b0e55b54d3.s: Which of the following mandates watermarking as a response to deepfakes and AI-generated content?
n7b0e55b54d3.x: The EU AI Act mandates watermarking. The ECI advisory requires mandatory labels on AI content in election campaigns, the DPDP Act provides penalties, and the IT Rules 2021 set intermediary due-diligence duties; none of these is the watermarking mandate.
n7b0e55b54d3.tq: Watermark = EU AI Act; label = ECI.
xs: The **EU AI Act** mandates **watermarking** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**ECI advisory** = mandatory **labels** in campaigns; **DPDP Act** = penalties; **IT Rules 2021** = intermediary **due diligence**.
xa: I4C does **takedowns** of deepfakes.
PIB FCU flagged **50+ deepfakes/manipulated videos in one month**, many from "Pakistani propaganda" handles.

n33aec89f250.s: The PIB Fact Check Unit (FCU) was set up in:
n33aec89f250.x: The FCU was set up in November 2019; it was formally notified under PIB in March 2024. April 2023 was the IT Rules amendment.
xa: Channels: WhatsApp **+91 8799711259**, factcheck@pib.gov.in.
⚠ **SC** stayed the FCU notification (**March 2024**); **Bombay HC** struck down the 2023 amendment (**September 2024**).

n6a3ee4290d4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021?
o: They were notified under Section 87 of the IT Act, 2000.
Significant social media intermediaries must appoint a Resident Compliance Officer.
They provide for a grievance officer and a nodal contact.
Significant social media intermediaries must submit annual compliance reports.
n6a3ee4290d4.x: Significant social media intermediaries must submit monthly, not annual, compliance reports.
xa: **April 2023** amendment: loss of **safe harbour** for content flagged fake by PIB FCU.
Platform duties: due diligence, **prompt removal of harmful content**, grievance processes esp. for children.

n2c656847531.s: Under the April 2023 IT Rules amendment, an intermediary could lose safe harbour if content on Central Government business was flagged as fake by:
n2c656847531.x: The April 2023 amendment provided for loss of safe harbour where content concerning Central Government business was flagged as fake by the PIB Fact Check Unit.
xa: It was challenged in the **Bombay HC** as **executive overreach, no due process**.
Bombay HC struck down the **2023** amendment in **September 2024**.
Criticism: FCU = **government as judge of truth about itself**.

n5a92ba8046b.s: In September 2024, the 2023 amendment providing for the PIB Fact Check Unit was struck down by the:
n5a92ba8046b.x: The Bombay High Court struck down the 2023 FCU amendment in September 2024; the Supreme Court had stayed the FCU notification in March 2024.
xa: ⚠ **SC** = stay (**March 2024**); **Bombay HC** = struck down (**September 2024**).
Grounds: **executive overreach**, **no due process**.

nc2e24625bc3.s: A victim of an online financial or cyber offence may report it through which combination?
nc2e24625bc3.x: Cyber offences can be reported at cybercrime.gov.in or through the helpline 1930.
nc2e24625bc3.tq: Identify the dedicated reporting channel and number rather than a related government portal.
xs: Cyber offences are reported at **cybercrime.gov.in and helpline 1930** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**factcheck.pib.gov.in** is the PIB **Fact Check Unit** channel; **SAHYOG** is I4C's **takedown** portal.
xa: PIB FCU WhatsApp: **+91 8799711259**.
**SAHYOG Portal** runs alongside the **Cyber Crime Reporting Portal**.

n45ca38aad4d.s: Ahead of the 2019 Lok Sabha election, which platform launched a tip line to curb fake news?
n45ca38aad4d.x: WhatsApp launched a tip line to help curb fake news ahead of the 2019 Lok Sabha election.
n45ca38aad4d.tq: Recall the platform associated with the election-related fact-check initiative.
xs: **WhatsApp** launched a **tip line** to curb fake news before the **2019 Lok Sabha election** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC PYQ).
**SAHYOG** is I4C's takedown portal; **DigiLocker** is not a fact-check tool.
xa: PIB FCU (set up **November 2019**) also takes reports on WhatsApp **+91 8799711259**.
**ECI advisory** mandates labels on AI content in campaigns.

nad5f3887ba1.s: The SAHYOG Portal for takedown notices is run by:
nad5f3887ba1.x: The SAHYOG Portal is run by I4C under MHA; platforms must remove flagged unlawful content within three hours.
xa: MHA sends ~**290** takedown notices a day.
**PIB Fact Check Unit** was set up in **November 2019**.
**WhatsApp tip line** was launched ahead of the **2019 Lok Sabha election**.

o: Provide advanced coding training to urban professionals
Make one person in every rural family digitally literate
Provide financial literacy to adults under ULLAS
n7862392afe6.x: PMGDISHA promotes rural digital literacy with the aim of one digitally literate person in every family; it was launched by the Prime Minister at Gandhinagar.
xa: **ULLAS**: **2022-27**, Ministry of Education; "Critical Life Skills" include **digital + financial literacy**.
**Digital India Vision Area 3** begins with **Universal Digital Literacy**.

n0588f611482.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ULLAS?
o: It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for 2022-27.
It is implemented by the Ministry of Electronics and IT.
It covers adults aged 15 years and above.
Its Critical Life Skills component includes digital and financial literacy.
n0588f611482.x: ULLAS is implemented by the Ministry of Education, not MeitY. The other statements are correct.
xa: **PMGDISHA**: one digitally literate person in every family.
**Computer Literacy Day**: **2 December**.
Only **one-third** of India's internet users are women.

n717aeff7fec.s: Computer Literacy Day is observed every year on:
n717aeff7fec.x: Computer Literacy Day is observed on 2 December (asked in UPPSC). 21 March is Universal Acceptance Day, 1 July marks Digital India's launch anniversary and 10 December is Human Rights Day.
xs: **Computer Literacy Day** is on **2 December** — so option **(2)** is correct (UPPSC PYQ).
It links to the push for **Universal Digital Literacy** under **Digital India Vision Area 3**.
xa: **PMGDISHA** launched by PM at **Gandhinagar**.
**Himachal Pradesh** = **5th State/UT** with full functional literacy.

naf58417ceef.s: Which of the following is a measure mentioned for responding to deepfakes?
o: Removal of all online political content
A ban on every form of digital communication
ECI advisory requiring labels on AI-generated content in campaigns
naf58417ceef.x: Measures for responding to deepfakes include the ECI advisory on mandatory labels for AI content in campaigns, DPDP Act penalties and I4C takedowns.
naf58417ceef.tq: Identify the specific institutional response rather than an extreme blanket restriction.
xs: An **ECI advisory requiring labels on AI-generated content in campaigns** responds to deepfakes — so option **(3)** is correct.
Other responses: **DPDP Act** penalties and **I4C** takedowns.
xa: **EU AI Act** mandates **watermarking**.
PIB FCU flagged **50+ deepfakes** in one month.

nbbf574ba8bf.x: AES uses the same secret key to encrypt and decrypt (symmetric); RSA is asymmetric and underlies PKI.
xa: **Digital signature** proves **origin and integrity**.
**Hashing**: any change alters the hash.

n036d730f98a.s: Malware that attaches to files and generally needs the user to run the infected file is a:
n036d730f98a.x: A virus attaches to files or programmes and usually needs the user to execute the infected file; a worm spreads without user interaction.
xa: A virus **corrupts/deletes data**.
⚠ **Virus** = user must run it; **Worm** = spreads without user interaction.
APPSC **2024** key gave **Virus** for the malware definition.

na5c613e5bdd.s: A malicious programme is disguised as legitimate software, does not self-replicate and opens a backdoor into a system. It is best classified as a:
na5c613e5bdd.x: A Trojan is disguised as legitimate software, does not self-replicate and may open a backdoor for unauthorised access.
na5c613e5bdd.tq: Apply the three-part distinction of disguise, self-replication and backdoor access.
xs: Disguised as legitimate software, **no self-replication**, opens **backdoors** = **Trojan** — so option **(4)** is correct.
A **worm** self-replicates; a **virus** attaches to files; a **rootkit** hides other malware.
xa: Example: **Zeus Trojan**; CERT-In flagged the **Dyreza Trojan** (**2014**).
Exam angle: "no self-replication, disguised" = **trojan**.

nacd884836b4.s: Malware that shows unwanted ads and comes bundled with free or pirated software is called:
nacd884836b4.x: Adware shows unwanted ads bundled with free/pirated software; encrypting files for ransom is ransomware.
xa: Examples: spyware **Pegasus**, adware **Fireball**, keylogger **DarkHotel**.
Adware comes bundled with **free/pirated software**.

n6adea90bf02.s: Which of the following is the principal feature of a rootkit?
o: It spreads only through infected removable files
It sends repeated advertising messages to users
It demands ransom in cryptocurrency after encrypting files
It obtains administrator-level access and hides other malware
n6adea90bf02.x: A rootkit gains deep administrator-level access and conceals other malicious components, making it particularly difficult to detect.
n6adea90bf02.tq: Identify the defining privilege and concealment feature of the malware.
xs: A rootkit **obtains administrator-level access and hides other malware** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is the **hardest to detect** malware type.
Ads = **adware**; ransom for encrypted files = **ransomware**.
xa: Example: **Stuxnet** components.
⚠ **Rootkit** = hides other malware; **Keylogger** = records keystrokes.

o: Ransomware that spread as a worm
ncd35c72d216.x: WannaCry was a ransomware worm using EternalBlue, developed by the US NSA; NSO Group made Pegasus spyware.
xa: WannaCry is attributed to **North Korea's Lazarus group**.
EternalBlue exploits a **Windows SMB** flaw.

n9b35800d026.s: Stuxnet was notable primarily because it:
o: Hijacked IoT devices to conduct DDoS attacks
Encrypted files on the computers of AIIMS Delhi
Targeted Iran’s Natanz uranium centrifuges using a worm with rootkit components
Affected Apple II computers as the first virus in the wild
n9b35800d026.x: Stuxnet was a worm containing rootkit components that sabotaged Siemens PLC-controlled uranium centrifuges at Iran’s Natanz facility.
n9b35800d026.tq: Connect the named malware with its distinctive target and industrial-control context.
xs: **Stuxnet** (**2010**) **targeted Iran's Natanz uranium centrifuges using a worm with rootkit components** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It attacked **Siemens PLCs** to sabotage **Iran's nuclear programme**.
IoT DDoS = **Mirai**; AIIMS Delhi = **ransomware**; Apple II = **Elk Cloner**.
xa: Rootkit = deep admin-level access, **hides** other malware.
Cyber espionage is **often state-sponsored** and uses **zero-days**.

nc1d2ea98d7e.s: Pegasus, a zero-click spyware, is associated with:
o: The NSA of the United States
nc1d2ea98d7e.x: Pegasus is state-grade zero-click spyware associated with Israel's NSO Group that can exploit zero-days without user interaction.
xa: **Spyware** secretly monitors users and steals passwords/banking data.
**Zero-day** = flaw developers have had "zero days" to fix.

n55e1d69ecec.s: Mirai, known for massive DDoS attacks using hijacked IoT devices, is a:
n55e1d69ecec.x: Mirai is a botnet that hijacked IoT devices and used them to launch large-scale DDoS attacks.
xa: **DDoS** floods a server from many machines so genuine users are denied service.
Botnets are also used for **spam** and **crypto-mining**.

n5031b5c142f.s: Brain (1986), the first IBM-PC boot-sector virus, originated in:
n5031b5c142f.x: Brain came from Lahore, Pakistan. Creeper (1971) was the first self-replicating program, and Elk Cloner infected Apple II computers.
xa: ⚠ **Creeper** = first virus; **Elk Cloner** = first "in the wild"; **Brain** = first IBM-PC virus.
**Reaper** removed Creeper.
**Petya** and **WannaCry** are **ransomware** (**APPSC-G2 2025**).

ne7a4cb1499a.s: 'Petya' and 'WannaCry', which caused worldwide disruption in 2016-17, are related to:
ne7a4cb1499a.x: Petya and WannaCry are ransomware (APPSC-G2 2025): Petya encrypts the master boot record and WannaCry spread as a worm through EternalBlue, demanding ransom. Spyware (e.g. Pegasus) secretly monitors users, adware shows unwanted ads, and a rootkit hides other malware with admin-level access.
xs: **Petya** and **WannaCry** are **ransomware** — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-G2 **2025** PYQ).
Petya encrypts the **master boot record**; WannaCry spread as a worm via **EternalBlue**.
**Spyware** (e.g. Pegasus) monitors users; **adware** shows ads; a **rootkit** hides other malware.
xa: ⚠ Trap: the scanned key is **garbled** — the correct answer is **ransomware**.
Indian ransomware case: **AIIMS Delhi (2022)**.

n96a97c871b2.s: The SolarWinds incident (2020) is an example of a:
n96a97c871b2.x: SolarWinds (2020) is a supply-chain attack; Pegasus is cited as an example of a zero-day exploit.
xa: **Pegasus** is **zero-click spyware** by **NSO Group** (Israel).
**Phishing** = deceptive emails/messages; **vishing** = voice calls.
**DDoS** uses a **botnet** (e.g. **Mirai**).

n1c56846b9bc.s: Mirai is an example of a:
n1c56846b9bc.x: Mirai is a botnet associated with DDoS attacks, which use multiple machines to deny genuine users access to a service.
xa: Mirai hijacked **IoT devices**.
Worms **eat bandwidth** and are the fastest spreading.

ne3bb9e7cc3a.s: Flooding a server with traffic describes which type of cyber attack?
ne3bb9e7cc3a.x: Server flooding is a denial-of-service attack; cyber espionage is often state-sponsored and uses spear-phishing and zero-days.
xa: **Pegasus** (NSO Group) is a **zero-click** spyware exploiting zero-days.
Cyber terrorism disrupts **critical infrastructure**.

n932db0bd280.s: A cyber attack exposes confidential medical records, alters several records and prevents doctors from accessing the hospital system. Which information-security principles have been compromised?
n932db0bd280.x: Exposure compromises confidentiality, alteration compromises integrity, and denial of access compromises availability; together they cover all elements of the CIA triad.
n932db0bd280.tq: Map each consequence in a scenario to the relevant CIA principle.
xs: Exposing records hits **confidentiality**, altering them hits **integrity**, blocking access hits **availability** — so option **(2) Confidentiality, integrity and availability** is correct.
Together these are the whole **CIA triad**.
xa: **AIIMS Delhi (2022)**: **ransomware** that disrupted hospital services.
Stolen personal, **medical**, IP data is sold on the **dark web**.

n55537f34db3.s: Which security mechanism is primarily intended to prevent unauthorised network access?
n55537f34db3.x: A firewall controls network traffic and helps prevent illegal or unauthorised access to a network or system.
n55537f34db3.tq: Match the security tool with its principal protective function.
xs: A **firewall** **prevents illegal (unauthorised) network access** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS **2025** PYQ).
**Antivirus** prevents and heals infections; a **honeypot** is a decoy for attackers.
xa: ⚠ **Firewall** = blocks unauthorised access; **Antivirus** = prevents and heals infections.
**VPN** = encrypted tunnel over a public network.
Cyber security scope: **firewalls, encryption, passwords**.

n1edac6c0cf6.s: Logging in with a password followed by an OTP or biometric proof is known as:
n1edac6c0cf6.x: Two-factor or multi-factor authentication uses two independent proofs, such as a password plus an OTP or biometric.
xa: Authentication methods: **passwords, biometrics, multi-factor authentication**.
**SIM swap / OTP diversion** frauds target the **OTP** factor.

nbff9419a09e.s: A security team intentionally exposes a decoy computer so that intruders can be attracted and their methods observed. The decoy is called a:
nbff9419a09e.x: A honeypot is a decoy system designed to lure attackers and enable security teams to study their behaviour and techniques.
nbff9419a09e.tq: Infer the tool from its deliberate decoy-and-observation role.
xs: A decoy system that **lures attackers to study them** is a **honeypot** — so option **(4)** is correct.
A **zero-day** is an unpatched flaw; a **VPN** is an encrypted tunnel; a **firewall** blocks unauthorised access.
xa: **Virtual keyboards** defeat **keyloggers**.
**Antivirus** prevents and heals infections.

n7e466b70ec9.s: Manipulating people through trust, urgency or curiosity to make them take an intended action is called:
n7e466b70ec9.x: Social engineering targets human behaviour, manipulating trust, urgency or curiosity; it can also be AI-enabled.
xa: **Phishing** and **digital arrest** scams rely on social engineering.
Current: **AI-enabled phishing** on Instagram accounts.

nca128a4c333.s: Which of the following is a characteristic of the dark web?
o: It is a secure government-only network used exclusively for defence communication.
It is a hidden part of the internet, reachable through tools such as Tor, and may host illicit marketplaces and data dumps.
It is the publicly indexed portion of the internet accessible through ordinary search engines.
It is a type of antivirus database maintained by CERT-In.
nca128a4c333.x: The dark web is a hidden part of the internet commonly accessed through tools such as Tor. It may contain illicit marketplaces, hacking tools and data dumps.
nca128a4c333.tq: Separate a hidden network from the ordinary publicly indexed web.
xs: The dark web is **a hidden part of the internet, reachable through tools such as Tor**, hosting **illicit marketplaces and data dumps** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It also hosts **hacking tools**; it is not the indexed web.
xa: Stolen data — **personal, medical, IP** — is sold on the dark web.
CERT-In is a **CVE Numbering Authority**, not a dark-web database.

n3767a9f1928.s: Attribution of cyber terrorism is difficult because attackers use VPNs, proxies and:
n3767a9f1928.x: VPNs, proxies and botnets hide the true source of attacks; cyber terrorism mainly aims to disrupt critical infrastructure.
xa: **Cyber espionage** is often **state-sponsored** and uses zero-days.
State-linked operations cost projected **$10.5 trillion** in 2025.

n2e855e001cb.s: Which of the following most accurately describes ‘digital arrest’ in the context of cyber crime?
o: A cyber criminal’s use of fake police or agency officials on a video call to frighten a victim and extort money
A court-ordered arrest carried out entirely through an online warrant
Police surveillance of cyber criminals through digital devices
Temporary suspension of a person’s digital identity by an internet service provider
n2e855e001cb.x: Digital arrest is a criminal intimidation technique in which impostors claim that the victim is under arrest and demand money, often while keeping the victim on a video call.
n2e855e001cb.tq: Reject the official-sounding but incorrect meaning and identify the criminal modus operandi.
xs: "Digital arrest" is **a cyber criminal's use of fake police or agency officials on a video call to frighten a victim and extort money** — so option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-G2 **2025** key).
⚠ Some notes describe it as **police tracking of criminals** digitally — that contradicts the exam key.
xa: SC ordered **SOPs, zero FIRs** and restoring victims' money.

ne3aaa36853a.s: In digital-arrest cases, the Supreme Court directed SOPs to be framed by the Centre, States, RBI and:
ne3aaa36853a.x: The directions called for SOPs by the Centre, States, RBI and telecom authorities, use of zero FIRs and restoration of victims' money.
xa: NCRP digital-arrest complaints fell from **1,23,672 (2024)** to **58,249 (2025)**.
Current relevance mentions **time-bound refunds**.

n4697958fd56.s: Identity theft is punishable under which section of the IT Act, 2000?
n4697958fd56.x: Identity theft falls under Section 66C; Sections 66E/67A apply to sextortion.
xa: **Sec. 43A** is compensation for failure to protect **sensitive personal data**.
**Digital arrest:** fake police/CBI officials keep a victim on video call to **extort money**.
**SIM swap** lets fraudsters intercept **OTPs**.

n53835c2d664.s: In digital payments, a QR code is scanned only to:
n53835c2d664.x: A QR code is scanned to make a payment, never to receive money; fraudsters exploit this misconception.
xa: **SIM swap / OTP diversion** = duplicate SIM to intercept OTPs.
**Loan-app fraud**: illegal instant-loan apps extort borrowers.

o: Encrypting a wallet with a public key
Stealing a cryptocurrency exchange's physical building
Scanning a QR code to receive cryptocurrency
Using a victim's device secretly to mine cryptocurrency
n14ed5eddde9.x: Crypto-jacking is the unauthorised and concealed use of a victim's computing device to mine cryptocurrency; botnets may also be used for this purpose.
n14ed5eddde9.tq: Use the action-object relationship to distinguish a malware-related term.
xs: Crypto-jacking is **using a victim's device secretly to mine cryptocurrency** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Botnets** are also used to mine crypto.
Scanning a QR code is never needed to **receive** money — that is the **QR fraud** trick.
xa: Botnet = "**zombie**" devices controlled remotely; also used for **DDoS** and **spam**.
**Ransomware** demands ransom, often in **crypto**.

n078eb7436be.s: The Critical Government Infrastructure of Andhra Pradesh is monitored through APCSOC by which organisation?
n078eb7436be.x: APTS (Andhra Pradesh Technology Services) monitors the State's Critical Government Infrastructure through APCSOC and has audited 270 GoAP applications. CERT-In, I4C and MeitY are national bodies.
n078eb7436be.tq: Identify the responsible state-level agency from the institutional relationship.
xs: **APTS** monitors AP's Critical Government Infrastructure through **APCSOC** — so option **(3)** is correct.
APTS has audited **270 GoAP applications**.
**CERT-In** and **MeitY** are national bodies; **I4C** is under MHA.
xa: **AP Cyber Security Policy 2017**.
AP Police-**IIT Tirupati** MoU for a **Cyber Crime Investigation and Training Academy**.

n74e5abb8b92.s: The e-Nagarpalika portal, an online civic tax payment portal hit by a cyber attack in December 2023, belongs to which State?
n74e5abb8b92.x: The e-Nagarpalika portal attack (Dec 2023) hit Madhya Pradesh's online civic tax payment portal (APPSC-G1 2024). Maharashtra is linked to the Cosmos Bank fraud (2018), Tamil Nadu to the Kudankulam NPP malware (2019), and Delhi to the AIIMS ransomware attack (2022).
xs: The **e-Nagarpalika** portal belongs to **Madhya Pradesh** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-G1 **2024** PYQ).
**Maharashtra** = Cosmos Bank (**2018**); **Tamil Nadu** = Kudankulam (**2019**); **Delhi** = AIIMS (**2022**).
xa: e-Nagarpalika was hit in **Dec 2023**.
Stolen data (personal, medical, IP) is sold on the **dark web**.

n5fe1233bd53.s: DRDO-led Exercise Cyber Suraksha is associated with which of the following?
o: Developing a national antivirus for private companies
Training bank customers in digital payments over 12 months
Testing satellite navigation systems for civilian transport
Training the armed forces in cyber preparedness over 12 days

India is also in the US-led **Counter Ransomware Initiative** and the **Quad Senior Cyber Group**.

n8adf091904a.s: In the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index 2024, India received a score of:
n8adf091904a.x: India scored 98.49 and was strong in all five pillars; the 2024 Index uses tiers, not numerical ranks.
xa: ⚠ GCI 2020 = rank **10**; GCI 2024 = **Tier-1**, no ranks.
The GCI is published by the **ITU**.

nf91a9939d7f.s: India was ranked 10th in which edition of the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index?
nf91a9939d7f.x: India was ranked 10th in the GCI 2020. The GCI 2024 shifted from numerical ranks to tiers.
nf91a9939d7f.tq: Numerical-year discrimination between the earlier rank-based edition and the later tier-based edition.
xs: India was ranked **10th** in **GCI 2020** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**GCI 2024** has no ranks; it uses **tiers**, and India is **Tier-1 "Role Modelling"**.
xa: GCI 2024 score: **98.49**, strong in all **five pillars**.
The index is brought out by the **ITU** (International Telecommunication Union).

ne1c8366474c.s: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, recognising privacy as intrinsic to life and liberty, was decided unanimously by a bench of:
ne1c8366474c.x: A unanimous nine-judge bench held privacy protected under Article 21 and Part III.
xa: Date: **24 August 2017**.
Overruled **M.P. Sharma (1954)** and **Kharak Singh (1962)** to the extent they denied privacy.
Follow-up: the **DPDP Act 2023** with a **Data Protection Board**.

nf6d57d688e6.s: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India overruled M.P. Sharma and Kharak Singh to the extent that those decisions:
o: Recognised proportionality as the sole test for all restrictions
Denied the existence of privacy as a protected constitutional interest
Declared education to be a Directive Principle
nf6d57d688e6.x: Puttaswamy overruled M.P. Sharma (1954) and Kharak Singh (1962) insofar as they denied privacy as a constitutional protection.
nf6d57d688e6.tq: Focus on the limited extent of overruling instead of treating the earlier judgments as wholly erased.
xs: Puttaswamy overruled them to the extent they **denied privacy** as a protected constitutional interest — so option **(2)** is correct.
**M.P. Sharma** was **1954**; **Kharak Singh** was **1962**.
xa: Yet **Kharak Singh v State of UP (1962)** is also cited for early recognition of privacy concerns under **Art. 21**.
**Gobind v State of MP (1975)** recognised privacy as part of personal liberty.
Puttaswamy: **nine-judge**, unanimous, **24 August 2017**.

n3621a0c3986.s: A government measure restricts personal data without any supporting law, although it claims to pursue a public objective. Which requirement of the privacy test is most clearly absent?
n3621a0c3986.x: The legality requirement demands that an intrusion into privacy be supported by a law. A claimed public objective cannot substitute for the existence of legal authority.
n3621a0c3986.tq: Apply the first step of the privacy test by asking whether the restriction has a legal basis.
xs: With no supporting law, the first test — **Legality** (a law) — is missing; option **(2)** is correct.
A public objective would satisfy the **legitimate aim** test, so option 1 is not what is absent.
The three tests are **legality**, **legitimate aim / need** and **proportionality**.
xa: These tests were later applied to **Aadhaar (2018)**.
**NAFRS** (facial recognition) runs **without a statute**, so it is questioned under the Puttaswamy tests.
Any state surveillance must meet the **Puttaswamy tests**.

nf9e400a5b0f.s: Who dissented in the 4:1 Aadhaar judgment of 26 September 2018?
nf9e400a5b0f.x: The five-judge Bench decided 4:1, with Justice D.Y. Chandrachud dissenting.
xa: Upheld: Aadhaar Act and passage as **Money Bill**; mandatory for welfare (**Sec. 7**); **PAN/ITR linking**.
Struck down: **Sec. 57** (private entities); bank-account and **SIM** linking.

n932b9a23a85.s: Safeguards on interception of communications in India were laid down in:
o: Kharak Singh v State of UP (1962)
K.S. Puttaswamy v Union of India (2017)
Shreya Singhal v Union of India (2015)
n932b9a23a85.x: Interception safeguards come from PUCL v Union of India (1997), not Kharak Singh.
xa: **Kharak Singh (1962)** is an early privacy case under **Art. 21**.
**Pegasus** committee: **Justice R.V. Raveendran**; malware on **5 of 29** phones.

ndde4747d394.s: As understood in India, the Right to Be Forgotten:
o: Applies only to biometric data collected by UIDAI
Limits name-based searches without necessarily erasing judicial records
Automatically cancels the judgment of a court
Prohibits every search involving the person's name
ndde4747d394.x: The Indian understanding of RTBF does not erase judicial records; it can limit name-based searches in appropriate circumstances.
xa: Delhi HC in **Laksh Vir Singh Yadav v UoI**: framework to de-index name searches of **acquitted persons**.
In India RTBF flows from **Art. 21** (Puttaswamy) and is **not absolute**.
Origin: **Google Spain v. AEPD (2014)**.

na12e51cbb2f.s: The 2018 draft personal data protection Bill was prepared by the:
na12e51cbb2f.x: The Justice B.N. Srikrishna Committee drafted the 2018 Bill (2017-18), before the 2019 PDP Bill, its 2022 withdrawal and the 2023 DPDP Act.
xa: **2021**: JPC report with **93 amendments**, covering personal and non-personal data.
**2012**: **Justice A.P. Shah** Group of Experts on Privacy.
DPDP Act assent: **11 Aug 2023**.

n11a223969c3.s: The 2021 Joint Parliamentary Committee report on the Personal Data Protection Bill proposed how many amendments?
n11a223969c3.x: The 2021 JPC report proposed 93 amendments and covered both personal and non-personal data; the Bill was withdrawn in 2022.
xa: After withdrawal, a narrower **DPDP draft** was released; the **DPDP Act** passed in **2023**.
The PDP Bill traces to the **Justice B.N. Srikrishna Committee** (MeitY).

n0f2b8d59f62.s: The Kris Gopalakrishnan Committee is associated with:
n0f2b8d59f62.x: The Kris Gopalakrishnan Committee dealt with non-personal data; A.P. Shah with privacy, Srikrishna with the PDP Bill and A.K. Bhargava with net neutrality.
xa: ⚠ Trap: an "A.P. Shah Committee (2015)" on net neutrality is wrong — that was **A.K. Bhargava**.
The A.P. Shah group worked under the **Planning Commission**.

nde9ce66c7ee.s: The final Digital Personal Data Protection Rules were notified on:
nde9ce66c7ee.x: The final DPDP Rules were notified on 14 November 2025; 3 January 2025 was the date of release of the draft Rules.
nde9ce66c7ee.tq: Distinguish the draft-release date from the final-notification date.
xs: Final **DPDP Rules** were notified on **14 November 2025** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**3 Jan 2025** = draft Rules; **11 Aug 2023** = Act's assent; **May 2027** = full compliance.
xa: Phases: Board **immediately**; **Consent Manager** in **November 2026**; full compliance **May 2027**.
Rules require **plain-language notices** and **purpose limitation**.

n82fab83b9d5.s: Under the DPDP Act, 2023, for a child under 18, the Data Principal is the:
n82fab83b9d5.x: For a child under 18, the parent or guardian is treated as the Data Principal, not the Data Fiduciary.
xa: GDPR equivalents: **Data Subject / Data Controller**.
**Consent Manager**: registered entity through which a principal gives, manages and withdraws consent.

n5243aa1d359.s: Which one of the following is NOT an additional obligation of a Significant Data Fiduciary?
o: Appointment of a Data Protection Officer in India
Automatic exemption from all consent requirements
n5243aa1d359.x: A Significant Data Fiduciary must appoint a Data Protection Officer in India, appoint an independent auditor and undertake impact assessment. It does not receive an automatic exemption from consent requirements.
n5243aa1d359.tq: Find the option that reverses an additional compliance duty into an exemption.
xs: **Automatic exemption from all consent requirements** is not an SDF obligation — so option **(3)** is correct.
SDF extra duties: appoint a **DPO in India**, an **independent auditor**, and conduct an **impact assessment**.
xa: SDFs are notified by the Centre on **volume, sensitivity and risk**.
Penalty for breaching SDF duties: up to **Rs 150 crore**.

na11e0eaa9b1.s: Which of the following best describes a Consent Manager?
o: A government officer who investigates cybercrime
A registered entity through which a Data Principal gives, manages and withdraws consent
An auditor appointed only by a Significant Data Fiduciary
A tribunal hearing appeals from the Board
na11e0eaa9b1.x: A Consent Manager is a registered entity enabling a Data Principal to give, manage and withdraw consent.
na11e0eaa9b1.tq: Exact-term discrimination based on function and institutional role.
xs: A **Consent Manager** is a **registered entity** through which a Data Principal **gives, manages and withdraws consent** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Appeals from the Board go to **TDSAT**, not a Consent Manager.
xa: Consent Manager provisions come into force in **November 2026** (12 months after the Rules).
Full compliance: **May 2027** (18 months).

n3c8bf6b5b17.s: Which set of practices is most consistent with the DPDP Rules?
o: Clear and specific consent, plain-language notices and purpose limitation
Consent without information, unrestricted collection and unlimited reuse
Implied consent, technical notices and indefinite retention
Anonymous consent, no retention controls and compulsory foreign storage
n3c8bf6b5b17.x: The Rules require clear, specific and informed consent, plain-language notices, purpose limitation, data minimisation and retention controls.
n3c8bf6b5b17.tq: Select the option containing the complete set of positive compliance practices.
xs: **Clear and specific consent, plain-language notices and purpose limitation** fit the Rules — so option **(1)** is correct.
Unrestricted collection, indefinite retention and no retention controls all contradict **data minimisation** and **retention controls**.
xa: Consent must also be **informed**.
Full operational compliance: **May 2027**.

n32395f1588c.s: Under the DPDP framework, the maximum penalty for breach of obligations regarding children's data is:
n32395f1588c.x: Children's data obligations carry up to ₹200 crore; additional SDF duties ₹150 crore and residual breaches ₹50 crore.
xa: Highest: **₹250 crore** for failure of **security safeguards**.
DPDP penalties are **financial only**; GDPR adds criminal ones in some states.

n2ec215bf784.s: The Supreme Court-appointed technical committee in the Pegasus matter was supervised by:
n2ec215bf784.x: Justice R.V. Raveendran supervised the committee, which found malware on 5 of 29 phones but could not conclusively link it to Pegasus.
xa: Safeguards on interception: **PUCL v UoI (1997)**.

nf975a2050b8.s: Under the DPDP Act, 2023, 'legitimate uses' allowing the State to process personal data without consent are in:
nf975a2050b8.x: Section 7 covers legitimate uses; Section 17 lets the Centre exempt notified State agencies on grounds of sovereignty, security and public order.
xa: **Startups** can be exempted; **journalism** gets no exemption.
Max penalty for security safeguard failure: **Rs 250 crore**.
Appeals from the **Data Protection Board** lie to **TDSAT**.

nf23d97dd652.s: Under the DPDP framework, verifiable parental consent is required for persons below the age of:
nf23d97dd652.x: Verifiable parental consent is needed below 18 years; tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted ads aimed at children are banned.
xa: Penalty for breach of **children's data** obligations: up to **Rs 200 crore**.
**DPDP Rules** were notified on **14 November 2025**.
**Consent Manager** provisions come into force in **November 2026**.

nd1a3233a86f.s: Appeals against decisions of the Data Protection Board of India lie to:
nd1a3233a86f.x: Appeals lie to TDSAT; the Board is headquartered in New Delhi and its members are appointed by the Central Government.
xa: The Board is an **adjudicatory** body.
Board provisions came into force **immediately** on **14 November 2025** Rules.

n0eaa6f38d0e.s: Under the DPDP Rules notified on 14 November 2025, full operational compliance is due by:
n0eaa6f38d0e.x: Full compliance is due 18 months after notification, in May 2027; Consent Manager provisions come in November 2026.
xa: Draft Rules: **3 Jan 2025**.
Fiduciary duties: **purpose limitation**, **data minimisation**, **retention controls**.

nc2a65eaa909.s: Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act was amended by which provision of the DPDP Act, 2023?
nc2a65eaa909.x: Section 44(3) of the DPDP Act amended Section 8(1)(j), letting authorities refuse all personal information and removing the public-interest override.
xa: Petition by **Venkatesh Nayak**; challenges **referred to a Constitution Bench**.
In **Aug 2026** the SC asked whether the law is "**crippling RTI**".

n9a090d59d9e.s: Which of the following is NOT a concern of India's first national standards for cloud, data centres and ethical AI?
n9a090d59d9e.x: The standards focus on bias, data sovereignty and privacy and are linked to the DPDP Act; spectrum auction pricing is not among them.
xa: These are India's **first national standards for Cloud Computing, Data Centres and Ethical AI**.
They are **aligned with the DPDP Act**.

n7e340af0a98.s: The GDPR formalised the Right to be Forgotten as the 'Right to Erasure' under Article:
n7e340af0a98.x: The GDPR's Right to Erasure is Article 17; RTBF originated in Google Spain v. AEPD (2014), and the DPDP Act gives a Right to Erasure under Section 12.
xa: ⚠ Right to Erasure = GDPR **Art. 17**; DPDP **Sec. 12**; privacy itself = Indian **Art. 21**.
In India RTBF is part of privacy under **Art. 21** (Puttaswamy) but **not absolute**; no standalone law.

n7824c2691ce.s: Which of the following is NOT a recognised right of a Data Principal under the DPDP framework?
o: Right to impose criminal penalties on a Data Fiduciary
n7824c2691ce.x: The listed rights include information and access, correction, erasure, grievance redress, withdrawal of consent and nomination. A Data Principal does not impose criminal penalties on a Data Fiduciary.
n7824c2691ce.tq: Identify the outsider by separating an individual data right from an enforcement power.
xs: There is no right to **impose criminal penalties** on a Data Fiduciary — so option **(1)** is correct.
Rights: **information/access**, **correction, erasure**, grievance redress, **withdrawal of consent**, **nomination**.
xa: DPDP penalties are **financial only**, up to **Rs 250 crore**.
**Data portability** is not a statutory right under DPDP (explicit in GDPR).

na92bc7bb3b4.s: Under the DPDP Act, transfer of personal data outside India is:
o: Permitted only to countries approved by the RBI
Permitted except to countries restricted by the Central Government
na92bc7bb3b4.x: The DPDP Act follows a blacklist (negative-list) approach: transfers are allowed unless the Central Government restricts particular countries.
xa: Critics call the approach **light-touch**.
RBI's separate rule (**April 2018**): payment-system data stored **only in India**.

nd96e4821fb2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the DPDP Act, 2023 and the GDPR?
o: The DPDP Act covers only digital personal data, whereas the GDPR covers all personal data.
Both frameworks use the term 'Data Fiduciary' for the entity deciding the purposes of processing.
The DPDP Act provides for financial penalties only.
Data portability is an explicit GDPR right but not a statutory right under the DPDP Act.
nd96e4821fb2.x: The GDPR uses 'Data Controller'; 'Data Fiduciary' is DPDP Act terminology.
xa: DPDP maximum penalty: **Rs 250 crore**.
Regulator: **Data Protection Board of India** vs a **DPA in each member state**.

n5e3dd185c78.s: The RBI mandate requiring all payment-system data to be stored only in India was issued in:
n5e3dd185c78.x: The RBI's April 2018 mandate required all payment-system data to be stored only in India.
xa: DPDP cross-border: **blacklist (negative-list)** — allowed except to countries the Centre restricts.
Critics call the DPDP approach **light-touch**.
⚠ DPDP = **blacklist**; GDPR = **whitelist / adequacy**.

n7340df379e2.s: Aryabhata, India's first satellite, was launched on 19 April 1975 from:
n7340df379e2.x: Aryabhata was launched by the Soviet Kosmos-3M from Kapustin Yar in the USSR.
xa: Aryabhata was conceptualised by **Sarabhai**; satellite team led by **U.R. Rao**.
It went up during **Satish Dhawan**'s tenure (**1972-84**).
⚠ Exam angle: "Which cosmodrome launched Aryabhata?" — **Soviet** (Kapustin Yar).

n4d73f6a9781.s: APPLE, India's first experimental geostationary communication satellite, was launched by:
o: Ariane-1 from Kourou in French Guiana
n4d73f6a9781.x: APPLE was launched on 19 June 1981 by Ariane-1 from Kourou, French Guiana.
n4d73f6a9781.tq: Separate APPLE from Rohini by matching the satellite with its foreign launch vehicle and site.
xs: **APPLE** was launched by **Ariane-1** from **Kourou**, French Guiana — so option **(3)** is correct.
**SLV-3** carried **Rohini**; **Challenger** carried **INSAT-1B**; **Kosmos-3M** carried **Aryabhata**.
xa: APPLE: **19 Jun 1981**, India's **first GEO satellite**.
It is part of **Indo-French** cooperation, along with **Megha-Tropiques** (2011) and **SARAL** (2013).

n5e675db986f.s: The first Indian-made sounding rocket, launched on 20 November 1967, was:
n5e675db986f.x: RH-75 was the first Indian-made sounding rocket; Nike-Apache (TERLS, 1963) was the first, American-built.
xa: **Aryabhata** (**19 Apr 1975**) — first Indian satellite, on Soviet **Kosmos-3M**.
**SITE** (**1975**-76) reached **2,400 villages** with **NASA**.
**Satellite Telecommunication Earth Station**, Ahmedabad — **1 Jan 1967**.

n425f8e17795.s: Rohini, the first satellite launched on an Indian rocket (18 July 1980), was carried by:
n425f8e17795.x: Rohini was launched by SLV-3 from Sriharikota; with it India became the sixth nation to orbit a satellite on its own launch vehicle.
xa: ⚠ **Aryabhata** = Kosmos-3M (Kapustin Yar); **Bhaskara** = Intercosmos (Baikonur); **APPLE** = Ariane-1 (Kourou).
**APPLE** (**19 Jun 1981**) was the first experimental **geostationary** satellite.
India is **4th** in Mars orbit (**Mangalyaan**, **2014**) and docking (**SpaDeX**).

ndb17bfae0b2.x: APPLE was the first geostationary satellite; Aryabhata was the first satellite and Rohini the first indigenous launch.
xa: First Indian-made sounding rocket: **RH-75** (**20 Nov 1967**).
First operational remote sensing: **IRS-1A** (1988).
First private rocket to orbit: **Skyroot's Vikram-1** (**18 Jul 2026**).

n616f670d12f.s: The Satellite Instructional Television Experiment (1975–76), which reached about 2,400 villages, was conducted with:
n616f670d12f.x: SITE was conducted with NASA using the ATS-6 satellite, reaching about 2,400 villages and nearly 5 million people.
xa: SITE is the classic **Indo-US** cooperation example.
It was planned during **Sarabhai**'s tenure (1969-71).
Next experiment: **STEP** (1977-79) on the **Symphonie** satellite.

ne27af6c1886.s: Which Indian mission became the first to land near the lunar south pole in 2023?
ne27af6c1886.x: In 2023 Chandrayaan-3 achieved the first landing near the lunar south pole, while Aditya-L1 was sent to the L1 point.
xa: Both were in **2023**, under **S. Somanath** (**2022-25**).
Next missions: **Chandrayaan-4 and 5**, **Venus Orbiter Mission**.

na6cba28944e.s: In which year did India conduct Mission Shakti?
na6cba28944e.x: Mission Shakti was in 2019, after Chandrayaan-1 (2008) and Mangalyaan (2014), and before Chandrayaan-3 (2023).
xa: ⚠ Chandrayaan-1 = **Madhavan Nair**; Mangalyaan = **Radhakrishnan**; Chandrayaan-3 = **Somanath**.
**Chandrayaan-2** and Mission Shakti fell under **K. Sivan** (2018-22).

n9ec40cd0592.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about recent Indian launch milestones?
o: LVM3-M6 carried BlueBird Block-2 on 24 December 2025.
SpaDeX made India the third country to demonstrate space docking.
Vikram-1 became the first privately developed Indian rocket to reach orbit on 18 July 2026.
n9ec40cd0592.x: SpaDeX made India the fourth docking nation, after the US, Russia and China.
xa: SpaDeX was launched by **PSLV-C60** on **30 Dec 2024** — a **space docking technology** demonstrator.
⚠ India is also **4th** in the world to reach **Mars orbit**.

n8499ce084db.s: In 1966, during his lifetime, Vikram Sarabhai was awarded the:
n8499ce084db.x: Sarabhai got the Padma Bhushan in 1966; the Padma Vibhushan came posthumously in 1972.
xa: He is the "**Father of the Indian Space Programme**" (**1919-71**).
**Aryabhata** was conceptualised by Sarabhai but launched after his death; team led by **U.R. Rao**.
**COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal** (since **1990**): 2026 winner **Annapurni Subramaniam**.

n140bde948e7.s: Who is known as the 'Father of the Indian Space Programme'?
n140bde948e7.x: Dr Vikram Sarabhai (1919-71) is called the Father of the Indian Space Programme and was the first ISRO Chairman till his death in 1971. Homi Bhabha led the atomic energy programme (Sarabhai succeeded him at the AEC in 1966); Satish Dhawan was a later ISRO Chairman (1972-84); Kalam is linked with SLV-3 and missiles, not this title.
xs: **Dr Vikram Sarabhai (1919-71)** is the "**Father of the Indian Space Programme**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Bhabha** preceded him as Atomic Energy Commission chairman; **Satish Dhawan** was ISRO Chairman **1972-84**.
xa: Sarabhai's tenure (**1969-71**): ISRO founded, **TERLS**, **SITE** planned.
Awards: **Padma Bhushan 1966**; **Padma Vibhushan posthumously 1972**.
Successor: **M.G.K. Menon** (1972, brief).

n6d311e64e28.s: U.R. Rao served as ISRO Chairman during:
n6d311e64e28.x: U.R. Rao served 1984-94, after Sarabhai (1969-71) and Dhawan (1972-84), and before Kasturirangan (1994-2003).
xa: Dhawan era: **Aryabhata, SLV-3/Rohini, APPLE, Bhaskara**.
U.R. Rao era: **ASLV**, PSLV development, **IRS-1A**.
Kasturirangan era: **PSLV operational**, **GSLV first flight**.

n1bb49af144f.s: Shubhanshu Shukla flew to the International Space Station in June–July 2025 on which mission?
n1bb49af144f.x: Shubhanshu Shukla flew to the ISS on Axiom-4 during June–July 2025.
xa: Human spaceflight next: **Gaganyaan** — crew of **3**, **400 km** orbit, **3 days**.
**ISRO-ESA** Technical Implementing Plan: **ground-tracking support for Gaganyaan**.

ne3b8d4e0470.s: APPLE, a milestone of Indo-French space cooperation, was launched on:
ne3b8d4e0470.x: APPLE was launched on Ariane-1; Megha-Tropiques and SARAL are other Indo-French milestones.
xa: Megha-Tropiques: **2011**.
**Indo-US** example: **SITE** with **NASA** (1975-76).
APPLE launched from **Kourou**, French Guiana.

n3ecadb0d367.s: Gaganyaan plans to carry a crew of three for three days to an orbit of about:
n3ecadb0d367.x: Gaganyaan plans a 3-member crew to a 400 km orbit for 3 days, ending in splashdown in Indian waters.
xa: Docking was shown by **SpaDeX** (**16 Jan 2025**).
**ISRO-ESA** plan gives **ground-tracking support for Gaganyaan**.

n61a757c437f.s: Which of the following is NOT among the next missions listed in the Indian Space Vision 2047 roadmap?
n61a757c437f.x: NISAR is an Indo-US mission launched in 2025; Chandrayaan-4, Chandrayaan-5 and the Venus Orbiter Mission are the roadmap's next missions.
xa: Venus Orbiter Mission: **Rs 1,236 crore**, **approved**.
**Bharatiya Antariksh Station** by **2035**.
New launch pad: **Kulasekarapattinam**.

n67f26292216.s: Under India's Space Vision 2047 (as of 1 January 2026), the Bharatiya Antariksh Station is targeted to be set up by:
n67f26292216.x: The Bharatiya Antariksh Station is targeted by 2035. 2047 is the overall Vision horizon, not the station target; 2028 and 2030 are not the stated target years.
xs: **Bharatiya Antariksh Station** is targeted **by 2035** (as of 1 Jan 2026) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**2047** is the horizon of the **Space Vision**, not the station's date.
xa: **Gaganyaan**: crew of **3**, **400 km**, **3 days**.
Venus Orbiter Mission approved at **Rs 1,236 crore**.

na77cfca3ea5.s: In which year was Bhaskara I launched?
na77cfca3ea5.x: Bhaskara I was launched in 1979, after Aryabhata (1975) and before Rohini (1980) and APPLE (1981).
xa: Next: **INSAT-1B** (1983, Challenger); **IRS-1A** (1988, Vostok).
⚠ Launchers: Aryabhata **Kosmos-3M**; Bhaskara **Intercosmos**; Rohini **SLV-3**; APPLE **Ariane-1**.

na0dab3e5fab.s: ISRO replaced INCOSPAR in the year:
na0dab3e5fab.x: ISRO replaced INCOSPAR on 15 August 1969; INCOSPAR was set up in 1962 and the DoS in 1972.
xa: **1972**: **Space Commission and DoS** set up; ISRO brought under DoS on **1 June 1972**.
Work on **TERLS** (near Thiruvananthapuram) began under INCOSPAR.
⚠ Trap: some notes say ISRO formed **November 1969**; most give **August**.

n69073a484b2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the institutional development of India's space programme?
o: The Department of Space works directly under the Prime Minister.
ISRO was brought under the Department of Space on 1 June 1972.
NSIL was established in 1972 as the first space-sector commercial arm.
xa: The **ISRO Chairman** is also **Secretary, DoS** and **Chairman, Space Commission**.
**IN-SPACe** (**2020**, Ahmedabad) is the single-window **regulator**.

n0998e61680b.s: The Chairman of ISRO also holds which of the following posts?
o: Chairman of IN-SPACe and CMD of NSIL
Secretary, Department of Space and Chairman, Space Commission
Scientific Adviser to the Prime Minister
n0998e61680b.x: The ISRO Chairman is also Secretary of the Department of Space and Chairman of the Space Commission; DoS works directly under the Prime Minister. IN-SPACe has its own chairman (Pawan Kumar Goenka) and NSIL is a separate CPSE; the AEC chairmanship belongs to the atomic energy set-up (Sarabhai held it after Bhabha in 1966, but it is not tied to the ISRO post); Scientific Adviser is not part of the role.
n0998e61680b.tq: ISRO Chairman = Secretary DoS + Chairman Space Commission.
xs: The ISRO Chairman is also **Secretary, Department of Space** and **Chairman, Space Commission** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**IN-SPACe** has its own chairman (**Pawan Kumar Goenka**).
xa: The DoS works **directly under the Prime Minister**.
Current chairman: **Dr V. Narayanan**, from **January 2025**, succeeding **S. Somanath**.
⚠ **Sarabhai** was also **AEC Chairman** after Bhabha (**1966**) — a separate post.

n91895bfa764.s: Who was the Project Director of SLV-3?
n91895bfa764.x: Kalam directed the SLV-3 project; SHAR honours Satish Dhawan and URSC honours U.R. Rao.
xa: ⚠ Named after: **VSSC**/TERLS = Sarabhai; **SHAR** = Dhawan; **URSC** = U.R. Rao.
Kalam, the "**Missile Man**", was President **2002-07**.

n44ce3c5a666.s: The Indian Institute of Remote Sensing (IIRS), Dehradun, a constituent unit of ISRO, was originally established in 1966 as the:
o: Centre for Space Science and Technology Education in Asia and the Pacific
n44ce3c5a666.x: IIRS began in 1966 as the Indian Photo-interpretation Institute (IPI) and is located at Dehradun under ISRO/DoS. NRSA is the forerunner of NRSC, Hyderabad; CSSTEAP is a UN-affiliated centre set up in 1995 and hosted at IIRS; Survey Training Institute is not its origin.
xs: **IIRS** began in **1966** as the **Indian Photo-interpretation Institute (IPI)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**CSSTEAP** is a separate UN-affiliated centre (**1995**) hosted at IIRS.
xa: IIRS: **Dehradun**, a **constituent unit of ISRO**, Department of Space.
Disciplines: **remote sensing, photogrammetry, cartography**, geo-informatics/GIS.

n7714f8d06ca.s: As of 2026, India's comprehensive Space Activities Act:
o: Was enacted with the Indian Space Policy 2023
n7714f8d06ca.x: As of 2026 India has no comprehensive Space Activities Act, though it has introduced policy and institutional reforms.
xa: Space governance pillars: **DoS**, **IN-SPACe** (regulator, **2020**) and **NSIL** (commercial arm, **2019**).
The DoS functions **directly under the Prime Minister**.
Under Space Policy 2023, an **AICTE-approved Space Technology course** is among the 2026 student initiatives.

n4ebe39632a7.s: Who succeeded S. Somanath as Space Secretary and ISRO Chairman in January 2025?
n4ebe39632a7.x: V. Narayanan succeeded S. Somanath in January 2025.
xa: Narayanan is called the **11th** Space Secretary and ISRO Chairman.
**URSC** (U R Rao Satellite Centre, Bengaluru) is named after U.R. Rao.

nb814ab0cb0d.s: The Space Applications Centre (SAC) of ISRO is located at:
nb814ab0cb0d.x: SAC is at Ahmedabad; Bengaluru hosts URSC, ISTRAC and ISRO HQ, and NRSC is at Hyderabad.
xa: ISRO HQ, **URSC** and **ISTRAC** are in **Bengaluru**.
**LPSC**: Valiamala (Thiruvananthapuram), with a Bengaluru unit.

n687144f5c4f.s: The ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC) is located at Mahendragiri in:
n687144f5c4f.x: Mahendragiri is in Tamil Nadu; IPRC assembles and tests liquid and cryogenic engines and stages.
xa: **VSSC**, Thiruvananthapuram, is the lead centre for **launch-vehicle design**.
**ISRO headquarters** is at **Bengaluru**.
**MCF** at **Hassan** and **Bhopal** controls geostationary satellites.

n9ca33b76523.s: The Space Applications Centre (SAC) at Ahmedabad is primarily associated with:
n9ca33b76523.x: SAC at Ahmedabad develops payloads for communication and remote sensing and undertakes applications research.
n9ca33b76523.tq: Match the applications-oriented function with SAC.
xs: **SAC, Ahmedabad** handles **payloads** (communication, remote sensing) and **applications research** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Tracking is **ISTRAC**; cryogenic engine work is **IPRC**.
xa: Also in **Ahmedabad**: **PRL** and **IN-SPACe** HQ.
Satellites themselves are built at **URSC**, Bengaluru.

n12f11877c91.s: ISRO's Master Control Facility (MCF) for geostationary satellites has facilities at Hassan and:
n12f11877c91.x: MCF operates from Hassan and Bhopal; ISTRAC at Bengaluru tracks launch vehicles and satellites.
xa: ISTRAC stations abroad: **Mauritius**, **Brunei**, **Biak (Indonesia)**.
**Indian Deep Space Network**: **Byalalu** near Bengaluru.

n66fd80a8fb4.s: Which of the following is NOT an overseas ISTRAC station?
n66fd80a8fb4.x: Byalalu near Bengaluru hosts the Indian Deep Space Network; Mauritius, Brunei and Biak are overseas ISTRAC stations.
xa: ISTRAC HQ: **Bengaluru**; runs the **TTC network** tracking launch vehicles through ascent.
**MCF** at **Hassan** and **Bhopal** controls geostationary satellites.

n59643ef2ff8.s: ISRO's Space Technology Incubation Centres (STICs) mainly promote space-technology activities in:
o: Universities in tier-2 and tier-3 cities
n59643ef2ff8.x: The six STICs promote space-technology activities in universities, particularly in tier-2 and tier-3 cities.
xa: Numbers: **STC 9**, **STIC 6**, **RACS 6**.
**UNNATI** (**2018**): nanosatellite training; **SpIN** (**2022**): innovation network.

n8cc6d7da5b7.s: Sriharikota, home of SDSC-SHAR, is now in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
n8cc6d7da5b7.x: Sriharikota is now in Tirupati district; earlier it was in Nellore district.
xa: ⚠ **Nellore** was the answer in APPSC **2019** PYQs, before the **2022** reorganisation.
Location: between **Pulicat Lake** (west) and the **Bay of Bengal** (east).

nef1a2b81dc7.s: Sriharikota barrier island is situated between which of the following?
o: Kolleru Lake and the Arabian Sea
Pulicat Lake and the Bay of Bengal
Chilika Lake and the Indian Ocean
Vembanad Lake and the Bay of Bengal
nef1a2b81dc7.x: Sriharikota lies between Pulicat Lake to the west and the Bay of Bengal to the east.
nef1a2b81dc7.tq: Use the east-west geographical relationship to separate nearby coastal locations.
xs: Sriharikota lies between **Pulicat Lake** (west) and the **Bay of Bengal** (east) — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is a **barrier island**, ISRO's primary spaceport.
xa: **East coast** location lets rockets launch **eastward** over the sea and gain from Earth's rotation.
Now in **Tirupati district** (earlier Nellore).

ne405e5adfba.s: The Solid Propellant Space Booster Plant (SPROB) at SDSC-SHAR is associated with the casting of which boosters?
o: Solid motors of sounding rockets only
ne405e5adfba.x: SPROB is a major solid-propellant plant that casts the S200 boosters used in LVM3.
ne405e5adfba.tq: Match the plant function with the specific booster designation.
xs: **SPROB** casts the **S200 boosters of LVM3** — so option **(1)** is correct.
SPROB = **Solid Propellant Space Booster Plant**, one of the **largest** solid-propellant plants in the world.
xa: Liquid and cryogenic stages belong to **LPSC** and **IPRC**.
Sriharikota's **Launch View Gallery** opened in **2019**.

naff31ebdacf.s: What is the principal strategic advantage of the Kulasekarapattinam launch complex for SSLV missions?
o: It is exclusively intended for launches of heavy-lift launch vehicles.
It permits direct southward launch into polar and sun-synchronous orbits without manoeuvring around Sri Lanka.
It is situated closer to the equator than Sriharikota and therefore eliminates all launch-cost constraints.
It enables launches directly into geostationary orbit without a cryogenic stage.
naff31ebdacf.x: Kulasekarapattinam allows a direct southward trajectory into polar and sun-synchronous orbits, avoiding the fuel-costly manoeuvre around Sri Lanka required from Sriharikota.
naff31ebdacf.tq: Apply the location to the launch trajectory and fuel-saving reason rather than to the vehicle name alone.
xs: It allows **direct southward launch** into **polar/sun-synchronous orbit** without manoeuvring around **Sri Lanka** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is meant mainly for the small **SSLV**, not heavy-lift vehicles.
xa: Foundation stone laid **27 Aug 2025**.
Opposition questioned a reported **handover** of the spaceport.

n7985f630d6c.s: The Kulasekarapattinam SSLV Launch Complex is in which district of Tamil Nadu?
n7985f630d6c.x: It is in Thoothukudi (Tuticorin) district and is meant mainly for SSLV launches.
xa: Foundation stone: **27 Aug 2025**.
Reason: **southward** launch avoiding the fuel-costly manoeuvre around **Sri Lanka**.

nbaeda9f2a0c.s: The Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology was set up as a deemed university under the Department of Space in:
nbaeda9f2a0c.x: IIST was established in 2007 as a deemed university under the DoS.
xa: IIST is **Asia's first space university**, at **Thiruvananthapuram**.
CSSTEAP: **UN**-affiliated, **1995**, hosted at IIRS **Dehradun**.

nap-geography-18-1.s: NARL is located at which place?
nap-geography-18-1.x: NARL, the atmospheric research laboratory, is at Gadanki near Tirupati. Sriharikota hosts the SDSC SHAR launch centre.
nap-geography-18-1.tq: Discriminate institutions in the same district.
n: NARL is located at Gadanki, Tirupati. [AP Geography · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 39-41]
xs: **NARL** is at **Gadanki, Tirupati**, so option **(1)** is correct.
NARL (**National Atmospheric Research Laboratory**) does **atmospheric research** and **meteorological** activities.
**Sriharikota** hosts **SDSC SHAR**; **Vijayawada** hosts **APSAC**; **Visakhapatnam** hosts **NSTL**.
xa: NARL's work includes **atmospheric radar**, lidar and monsoon dynamics.
**SHAR** and **NARL Gadanki** are AP's two DoS assets.
**PRL** (space and planetary science) is at **Ahmedabad**.

n6c139722696.s: SPARK, launched by ISRO on 10 August 2022, is best described as:
n6c139722696.x: SPARK is ISRO’s virtual space museum, launched on 10 August 2022.
n6c139722696.tq: Test the exact function and launch date of a named initiative.
xs: **SPARK** is ISRO's **virtual space museum**, launched **10 Aug 2022** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Nanosatellite training is **UNNATI**; university research funding is **RESPOND**.
xa: **YUVIKA** for school students: launched **2019**.
SPARK featured in an APPSC **2021** PYQ.

nb8e16f62611.s: Which Indian launch vehicle made its first flight in 1987?
nb8e16f62611.x: First flights: SLV-3 (1979), ASLV (1987), PSLV (1994), GSLV (2001).
xa: PSLV is the **third-generation** vehicle; GSLV the **fourth**.

n0db9a7039d9.s: ASLV was an all-solid launch vehicle with how many stages?
n0db9a7039d9.x: ASLV had five solid stages; SLV-3 had four.
xa: **PSLV** was the **first Indian vehicle with liquid stages**.
SLV-3 weighed **17 t** and stood **22 m** tall.

nd55ebd539dc.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about GSLV Mk II?
o: Its first stage uses HTPB solid propellant.
Its third stage is cryogenic, using LH2 and LOX.
Its second stage uses a Vikas engine with UH25 and N2O4.
nd55ebd539dc.x: GSLV Mk II has four liquid strap-ons, not two solid ones.
xa: GSLV = one solid + one **earth-storable liquid** + one **cryogenic** stage (APPSC G2 **2025**).
GSLV Mk II carries **2-2.5 t** class satellites to **GTO**.

o: Four solid stages followed by a Vikas liquid stage
Two S200 solid strap-ons, an L110 liquid core and a C25 cryogenic stage
Three solid stages and a liquid velocity-trimming module
HTPB first stage, UH25 second stage and CE-7.5 third stage
na10b814d8db.x: LVM3 uses two S200 solid strap-ons, an L110 liquid core and a fully indigenous C25 cryogenic stage.
xa: The **C25** stage is **fully indigenous**.
**SPROB** at Sriharikota casts the **S200** boosters.
Capacity: **4 t** to GTO; **8 t** to LEO (some notes ~**10 t**).

o: Four stages in a solid-liquid-solid-liquid sequence
One solid, one liquid and one cryogenic stage
Three solid stages and a liquid Velocity Trimming Module
nb0159d73f7a.x: SSLV has three solid stages and a liquid Velocity Trimming Module that provides precise orbit insertion.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "**two solid stages**" is WRONG — it has three.
Capacity: **500 kg** to a **500 km** LEO.

nf66a7bb6742.s: In launch terminology, GTO stands for:
nf66a7bb6742.x: GTO is the Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit, served by GSLV and LVM3; SSO is PSLV's speciality.
xa: **GEO** = GSO over the equator, so the satellite stays **fixed in the sky**.
**Apogee** = farthest point; **perigee** = nearest.

n0bbab47285c.s: Which launch vehicle serves SSO, LEO and GTO missions, including Chandrayaan-1 and the Mars Orbiter Mission?
n0bbab47285c.x: PSLV serves SSO, LEO and GTO and launched Chandrayaan-1 and the Mars Orbiter Mission.
xa: PSLV: ~**1,750 kg** to SSO, ~**1,425 kg** to GTO.
⚠ Chandrayaan-1 = **PSLV**; Chandrayaan-2 = **GSLV Mk III-M1**; Chandrayaan-3 = **LVM3-M4**.

nabe91b2bfcd.s: Which launch vehicle is primarily associated with placing 2–2.5 tonne communication and navigation satellites into GTO?
nabe91b2bfcd.x: GSLV Mk II is designed to place 2–2.5 tonne communication and navigation satellites into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit.
nabe91b2bfcd.tq: Match the payload class and target orbit with the appropriate launcher.
xs: **GSLV Mk II** carries **2-2.5 t** class communication/navigation satellites to **GTO** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**ASLV** managed **150 kg**; **SSLV** **500 kg** to LEO; **PSLV** ~**1,425 kg** to GTO.
xa: Examples: **NVS-01** on **GSLV-F12**; **NVS-02** on **GSLV-F15**.
**LVM3** handles **4 t** to GTO.

n7be003c4df0.s: According to the stated capacity figures, LVM3 can carry approximately how much payload to GTO and LEO respectively?
o: 8 tonnes to GTO and 4 tonnes to LEO
4 tonnes to GTO and 8 tonnes to LEO
2 tonnes to GTO and 4 tonnes to LEO
500 kg to GTO and 1,750 kg to LEO
n7be003c4df0.x: The stated LVM3 capacity is about 4 tonnes to GTO and 8 tonnes to LEO, although some descriptions cite approximately 10 tonnes to LEO.
n7be003c4df0.tq: Read the orbit–capacity pair in the correct order.
xs: **LVM3**: **4 tonnes to GTO** and **8 tonnes to LEO** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option 1 swaps the two numbers.
xa: Some notes give ~**10 t** to LEO.
LVM3 ended dependence on foreign launchers for **4-tonne** satellites.
LVM3 has flown **6** missions.

ne88f3107b10.s: SSLV, with three solid stages, can place about 500 kg into a LEO of about:
ne88f3107b10.x: SSLV places about 500 kg into a 500 km LEO; SSLV-D1 failed, while D2 and D3 succeeded.
xa: ⚠ "Two solid stages" is **wrong** — SSLV has **three**.
**HAL** won a **₹511 crore** ToT deal to build SSLV.
SSLV's dedicated spaceport: **Kulasekarapattinam** (Thoothukudi, TN).

nb44807bb825.s: LVM3 ended India's dependence on foreign launchers for placing satellites of about what mass into GTO?
nb44807bb825.x: LVM3 can place about 4 tonnes into GTO and ended India's dependence on foreign launchers for 4-tonne satellites.
xa: **HLVM3**: crew to **400 km** LEO for **3 days**.

ncc99c6ff84a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about orbits?
o: A geostationary orbit is a geosynchronous orbit over the equator.
Apogee is the point of an orbit nearest to the Earth.
GTO is an elliptical transfer orbit with its apogee near 36,000 km.
A geosynchronous orbit has a period of one day.
ncc99c6ff84a.x: Apogee is the farthest point of an orbit; perigee is the nearest.
xa: **SSO** is near-polar and passes each place at the same local solar time.
**Eastward** launches gain Earth's rotational speed.
Polar/SSO launches go **southward** — hence the **Kulasekarapattinam** site.

n06b7b62b381.s: EOS-05, India's first imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit, was launched by:
n06b7b62b381.x: GSLV-F17 placed EOS-05 into a sub-GTO on 4 September 2026.
xa: GSLV-F17/EOS-05 was the **107th** launch from Sriharikota.
**NISAR** (**GSLV-F16**, **30 Jul 2025**) was the first GSLV launch to **sun-synchronous polar orbit**.
**PSLV-C61** and **PSLV-C62** both failed at the **third stage**.

n9dc61d7543e.s: The current foreign direct investment rules permit what level of automatic FDI in launch vehicles and spaceports?
n9dc61d7543e.x: The revised rules allow 49% automatic FDI in launch vehicles and spaceports.
n9dc61d7543e.tq: Recall the precise percentage and distinguish it from nearby investment thresholds.
xs: **49% automatic FDI** is allowed in **launch vehicles and spaceports** (**Jul 2026**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**HAL** won a **₹511 crore** ToT to build and operate **SSLV**.
xa: **ISSAR 2025**: **315** successful launches worldwide; **4,651** objects placed in orbit.
All orbital launches, incl. private **Agnibaan**, are from **Sriharikota**.

n7b7acf0c933.s: Which was the first sounding rocket launched from Thumba?
n7b7acf0c933.x: The first sounding rocket launched from Thumba was the American Nike-Apache on 21 November 1963.
n7b7acf0c933.tq: Distinguish the first foreign rocket from later indigenous sounding rockets and other early foreign rockets.
xs: The first rocket from Thumba was **Nike-Apache** on **21 Nov 1963** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**M-100** (Russia) and **Centaure** (France) were later imported rockets; **1975** is when the **RSR programme** was consolidated.
xa: Indigenous sounding rockets began in **1965**.
RH numbers = **diameter in mm** (RH-200, RH-300, RH-560).

n5a430982eb2.s: CARE, launched by LVM3 on 18 December 2014, was a:
n5a430982eb2.x: CARE was a suborbital experimental payload launched by LVM3 on 18 December 2014.
n5a430982eb2.tq: Distinguish an experimental suborbital payload from operational orbital satellites.
xs: **CARE** (**18 Dec 2014**) was a **suborbital** experimental payload — so option **(3)** is correct.
LVM3's first orbital flight (**2017**, D1) carried **GSAT-19**.
xa: LVM3 = ex-**GSLV Mk-III**, "**Bahubali**".
Human-rated **LVM3** will fly **Gaganyaan**.

ncf91d57e144.s: Chandrayaan-3 was launched by which of the following?
ncf91d57e144.x: Chandrayaan-3 was launched by LVM3-M4 in July 2023.
ncf91d57e144.tq: Distinguish the LVM3 flight used for Chandrayaan-3 from the earlier Chandrayaan-2 flight.
xs: **Chandrayaan-3** flew on **LVM3-M4** (Jul 2023) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**GSLV Mk III-M1** carried **Chandrayaan-2** (2019); **GSLV-F10** carried **GISAT-1**.
xa: ⚠ Chandrayaan-1 = **PSLV**; Chandrayaan-2 = **GSLV Mk III-M1**; Chandrayaan-3 = **LVM3-M4**.
LVM3 also flew two **OneWeb** missions (M2, M3) with **72** satellites.

n00275333c3b.s: The record for launching the largest number of satellites in a single Indian launch was set by:
n00275333c3b.x: PSLV-C37 launched 104 satellites in February 2017, establishing the multi-satellite record stated here.
n00275333c3b.tq: Pair the record with both its launch vehicle and date to avoid nearby record traps.
xs: **PSLV-C37** set the record with **104 satellites** on **15 Feb 2017** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It carried a **Cartosat-2 series** satellite + **101 foreign** satellites.
xa: ⚠ Most satellites = PSLV-C37; heaviest payload = **LVM3-M6** (**6,100 kg**).
**Cartosat-3** (+**13** US nanosatellites) flew on **PSLV-C47** (Nov 2019).

na2db7fffc47.s: A sun-synchronous satellite is particularly suitable for imaging because it:
o: always travels in an eastward equatorial orbit
passes over a given place at the same local solar time
na2db7fffc47.x: A sun-synchronous orbit is generally near-polar and passes over a given location at approximately the same local solar time, which is useful for consistent imaging conditions.
na2db7fffc47.tq: Link the orbital characteristic with its practical imaging advantage.
xs: A sun-synchronous satellite passes over a place at the **same local solar time** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is a **near-polar** orbit — **PSLV's speciality**.
Remaining fixed over the equator is **GEO**; apogee near **36,000 km** is **GTO**.
xa: **NISAR** (**GSLV-F16**, **30 Jul 2025**): first GSLV launch to a sun-synchronous polar orbit.
PSLV carries ~**1,750 kg** to SSO.

n9a4787eb7bb.s: Thumba was selected for the establishment of TERLS mainly because:
o: It lies close to the international date line
It is located near the Baikonur Cosmodrome
The geomagnetic equator passes through it
n9a4787eb7bb.x: Thumba was selected because the geomagnetic equator passes through the location, making it suitable for sounding-rocket experiments.
n9a4787eb7bb.tq: Identify the geographical and scientific reason for site selection, not a transport or altitude advantage.
xs: Thumba was chosen because the **geomagnetic equator** (magnetic equator) passes through it — so option **(3)** is correct.
TERLS is a **sounding-rocket** station near **Thiruvananthapuram**.
xa: First launch: **Nike-Apache**, **21 Nov 1963** — start of the Indian space programme.
⚠ Sriharikota was chosen instead for its **east-coast** location (eastward launches over the sea).

n1e83dfd20a2.s: Rohini sounding rockets are primarily used for:
o: Geostationary communication and television broadcasting only
Atmospheric research and qualification of launch-vehicle subsystems
n1e83dfd20a2.x: Rohini sounding rockets carry payloads for atmospheric research and are also used to test and qualify systems intended for larger launch vehicles.
n1e83dfd20a2.tq: Identify the operational uses rather than the launch vehicle’s name alone.
xs: Rohini rockets carry payloads for **atmospheric research** and **qualify launch-vehicle subsystems** — so option **(2)** is correct.
They are sounding rockets, not orbital or crewed vehicles.
xa: Number = **diameter in mm**: **RH-200, RH-300, RH-560**.
Payload **8-100 kg**; apogee **80-475 km**.

n631dde8a6dd.s: In the Rohini sounding-rocket designations RH-200, RH-300 and RH-560, the number indicates the:
n631dde8a6dd.x: The number in an RH designation denotes the rocket diameter in millimetres.
n631dde8a6dd.tq: Break the designation into its technical meaning rather than treating it as an altitude or payload figure.
xs: The number is the rocket's **diameter in millimetres** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Payload range is **8-100 kg** and apogee **80-475 km** — not encoded in the name.
xa: RSR programme consolidated in **1975**.
**RH-200**: **200th consecutive** successful launch in **Nov 2022**.

n07fc57a2e79.s: The 200th consecutive successful launch from Thumba was achieved by RH-200 in:
n07fc57a2e79.x: RH-200 completed its 200th consecutive successful launch from Thumba in November 2022.
n07fc57a2e79.tq: Link the milestone number with its specific month and year.
xs: **RH-200** made the **200th consecutive** successful launch from Thumba in **November 2022** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It featured in an **APPSC 2021** PYQ.
xa: RH numbers denote **diameter in mm**.
First Thumba launch: **Nike-Apache**, **21 Nov 1963**.

n6ed20c1e93a.s: The fuel saving from an eastward launch is greatest for launch sites located:
n6ed20c1e93a.x: Eastward launches gain Earth's rotational speed, and sites nearer the equator gain the most.
xa: Sriharikota's **east coast** lets rockets fly over the **sea**, away from populated land.
**Polar/SSO** launches go **southward** instead.

n859a7a722f0.s: Polar and Sun-synchronous orbit launches from Sriharikota generally require a dog-leg trajectory around Sri Lanka because they proceed:
n859a7a722f0.x: Polar and Sun-synchronous launches generally follow a southward trajectory from Sriharikota; a dog-leg is used to avoid Sri Lanka.
n859a7a722f0.tq: Connect the orbit type with the launch direction and geographical constraint.
xs: Polar/SSO launches go **southward**, so from Sriharikota they need a **dog-leg around Sri Lanka** — option **(2)** is correct.
That costly manoeuvre is why the **SSLV** site is at **Kulasekarapattinam** in the south.
xa: Kulasekarapattinam foundation: **27 Aug 2025**.
**SSO** is near-polar and passes each place at the same **local solar time**.

ne339d25aa57.s: A second spaceport for SSLV launches is being established at:
ne339d25aa57.x: Orbital launches, including private Agnibaan missions, take place from Sriharikota; a second SSLV spaceport is coming up at Kulasekarapattinam in Tamil Nadu.
xa: Kulasekarapattinam is in **Tamil Nadu**; foundation laid **27 Aug 2025**.
Sriharikota's **100th launch**: **GSLV-F15/NVS-02**, **29 Jan 2025**.

nb003a5a99e5.s: Which company won the ₹511 crore Transfer of Technology agreement to build and operate SSLV independently?
nb003a5a99e5.x: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) won the ₹511 crore SSLV Transfer of Technology agreement. It was described as the first full Transfer of Technology of an ISRO launch vehicle to industry.
nb003a5a99e5.tq: Match the industrial agency with the specific technology-transfer arrangement.
xs: **HAL** (**Hindustan Aeronautics Limited**) won the **₹511 crore** ToT deal — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is the **first full ToT** of an ISRO launch vehicle to industry.
xa: SSLV: **500 kg** to **500 km** LEO.
**49% automatic FDI** in launch vehicles and spaceports (**Jul 2026**).

nfccf5a3618a.s: SpaDeX was launched on 30 December 2024 by:
nfccf5a3618a.x: SpaDeX flew on PSLV-C60 and docked on 16 January 2025, making India the fourth docking nation.
xa: Next PSLV flights **C61** and **C62** both failed at the **third stage**.
