SpaDeX used **two small spacecraft** to demonstrate **space docking** technology.

n5334c8a5ae9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about RLV-LEX?
o: It refers to autonomous landing tests of the Reusable Launch Vehicle Technology Demonstrator.
Its first test took place on 2 April 2023.
It was a cryogenic engine test for GSLV Mk-II.
The later reusable-vehicle landings of 2024 are called the 'Pushpak' landings.
n5334c8a5ae9.x: RLV-LEX is a landing experiment, not an engine test.
xa: First indigenous cryogenic success: **GSLV-D5 (2014)**; engines tested at **IPRC, Mahendragiri**.
Foreign reusables: **Falcon 9** (SpaceX), **New Shepard** (Blue Origin, sub-orbital).

n98150d90321.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV)?
o: Its lift-off mass is about 1,000 tonnes.
It is meant to support a crewed lunar landing by 2030.
It is meant to support the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035.
n98150d90321.x: NGLV is linked to the 2040 crewed lunar-landing goal, not 2030.
xa: It needs the **Third Launch Pad** (~**4** years).
The **SCE-200** semi-cryogenic engine is meant for the **LVM3 upgrade and NGLV**.

nd868ae9c9f7.s: PSLV's four stages, in order, are:
nd868ae9c9f7.x: PSLV is solid-liquid-solid-liquid with no cryogenic stage; it was the first Indian launch vehicle with liquid stages.
xa: ⚠ **GSLV** = **3** stages (solid-liquid-cryo); **SSLV** = **3** solid + VTM.
PSLV's 2nd stage uses the **Vikas** engine.
PSLV first success: **IRS-P2** (**15 Oct 1994**).

neba7a9584c1.s: Engine tests for Indian cryogenic and semi-cryogenic systems are conducted at:
neba7a9584c1.x: The tests are conducted at the ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC), Mahendragiri, in Tamil Nadu. LPSC Valiamala is associated with design work and is not the testing facility identified here.
neba7a9584c1.tq: Discriminate between the design centre and the propulsion-test facility.
xs: Engine tests happen at **IPRC, Mahendragiri, Tamil Nadu** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**LPSC Valiamala** (Kerala) **designs** but does not test.
xa: ⚠ Trap: notes placing the test facility in **Kerala** are wrong.
**SCE-200** semi-cryogenic engine: for the **LVM3 upgrade** and **NGLV**.

nfdc747b0e1a.s: ISRO's SCE-200 semi-cryogenic engine, meant for the LVM3 upgrade and the NGLV, uses which propellant combination?
nfdc747b0e1a.x: A semi-cryogenic engine burns refined kerosene with liquid oxygen; SCE-200 is meant for the LVM3 upgrade and NGLV. LH2 + LOX is the fully cryogenic combination (CE-7.5, C25); UH25 + N2O4 is the earth-storable Vikas combination; HTPB is a solid propellant.
nfdc747b0e1a.tq: Semi-cryo = kerosene + LOX; cryo = LH2 + LOX.
xs: **SCE-200** uses **refined kerosene and liquid oxygen** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**LH2 + LOX** is the **cryogenic** CE-7.5; **UH25 + N2O4** is **Vikas**; **HTPB** is GSLV's solid 1st stage.
xa: It is meant for the **LVM3 upgrade** and **NGLV**.
The **Third Launch Pad** is planned for NGLV and semi-cryo LVM3.

na6f3c9d3a54.s: Which one of the following is an earth-storable liquid propellant combination?
na6f3c9d3a54.x: UH25 and N2O4 are listed as earth-storable liquid propellants. Refined kerosene and LOX are semi-cryogenic, while LH2 and LOX are cryogenic.
na6f3c9d3a54.tq: Separate earth-storable liquid propellants from cryogenic and semi-cryogenic combinations.
xs: **UH25 and N2O4** is an **earth-storable liquid** combination — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Refined kerosene + LOX** is **semi-cryogenic**; **LH2 + LOX** is **cryogenic**.
**Solid fuel + liquid oxidiser** is a **hybrid** propellant.
xa: Other earth-storable liquids: **hydrazine, MMH, UDMH**; they are **throttleable and restartable** (Isp ~**290-320 s**).
ISRO's **Vikas** engine runs on **UH25 + N2O4** (PSLV 2nd stage, GSLV 2nd stage and strap-ons, LVM3 **L110** core).
**Hypergolic** = hydrazine family + **N2O4** — ignites on contact but is **highly toxic**.

n8ddfab2c8f9.s: Hydrazine-family propellants combined with N2O4 are classified as hypergolic because they:
o: Are non-toxic and suitable for large reusable boosters
Require cryogenic storage and have the highest specific impulse
Ignite on contact and are useful for spacecraft manoeuvring
n8ddfab2c8f9.x: Hypergolic propellants ignite on contact and are useful for spacecraft manoeuvring, although they are highly toxic.
n8ddfab2c8f9.tq: Use the defining property of hypergolic propellants to identify the correct application.
xs: Hydrazine-family + **N2O4** propellants are hypergolic because they **ignite on contact** and are **useful for spacecraft manoeuvring** — option **(4)**.
They are **highly toxic**, so option (1) "non-toxic" is wrong; **semi-cryogenic** kerosene + LOX is the non-toxic one.
**Cryogenic storage and highest Isp** describe **LH2 + LOX** (~**450 s**), not hypergolics.
xa: Hydrazine, **MMH** and **UDMH** are also listed as **earth-storable** liquids — throttleable and **restartable**.
**Solid** (HTPB) motors are the ones that **cannot be throttled or stopped**.
⚠ **Hypergolic** = ignite on contact; **Cryogenic** = LH2 + LOX; **Semi-cryogenic** = kerosene + LOX.

n51ae2c03f51.s: In a cryogenic engine, liquid hydrogen is stored at about:
n51ae2c03f51.x: LH2 (the fuel) is stored at about -253°C and LOX (the oxidiser) at about -183°C; the exhaust is only water vapour.
xa: Cryogenic specific impulse ~**450 s** — the **highest** of all propellant categories.
LH2 density is only **0.071 g/ml** → huge tanks; unsuited to **military missiles**.
Used in **rocket upper stages**/space shuttle; **Discovery's** tanks held LH2 + LOX (UPPSC **2006**).
The propellant pair was asked in **UPPSC 2004**.

n6e0072c783d.s: Cryogenic propulsion, the most efficient propellant category, has an approximate specific impulse of:
n6e0072c783d.x: Cryogenic propulsion has an approximate specific impulse of 450 seconds, the highest among the propellant categories.
xa: Propellants: **LH2 (-253°C)** fuel + **LOX (-183°C)** oxidiser; exhaust only **water vapour**.
ISRO cryogenic engines: **CE-7.5** (GSLV Mk II) and **CE-20** (LVM3 **C25**).
Earth-storable liquids give Isp ~**290-320 s**.

ndef2ff2d664.s: What was the outcome of the 1991 Glavkosmos agreement concerning cryogenic technology?
o: Russia transferred all cryogenic technology without restriction.
The United States supplied seven cryogenic engines to India.
US MTCR-based sanctions stopped technology transfer, although Russia supplied seven engines.
The agreement was cancelled by India before any engines were supplied.
ndef2ff2d664.x: Glavkosmos agreed to sell engines and technology in 1991, but US MTCR-based sanctions in 1992 stopped technology transfer; Russia supplied seven engines only.
ndef2ff2d664.tq: Separate the original agreement, the later sanctions and the limited engine supply.
xs: **US MTCR-based sanctions (1992)** stopped technology transfer, and Russia supplied only **seven engines** — option **(3)**.
Under the **Glavkosmos deal (1991)** Russia agreed to sell engines + technology, but the transfer never happened, so option (1) is wrong.
The engines came from **Russia**, not the US, so option (2) is wrong.
xa: India then pursued the **Cryogenic Upper Stage Project** (begun **1994**, **₹300 crore**).
Full cryogenic stage tested in **2006**; **GSLV Mk II** with **CE-7.5** flew on **5 Jan 2014**.
⚠ India is not the fourth nation with cryogenic tech — **Europe/France** and **Japan** also had it.

n0750e9d5600.s: Cryogenic engines (liquid hydrogen + liquid oxygen) are mainly used in:
o: Military missiles kept ready for long periods
n0750e9d5600.x: Cryogenic propulsion is used in rocket upper stages (and was used on the space shuttle) because of its very high specific impulse (~450 s). Its low-density LH2 needs huge tanks and cannot be stored long, so it is unsuited to military missiles; attitude-control thrusters use hypergolic propellants that ignite on contact; sounding rockets use solid motors.
xs: Cryogenic (LH2 + LOX) engines are mainly used in **rocket upper stages** — option **(1)** (UPSC **1995**, UPPSC **1993**).
Low-density LH2 (**0.071 g/ml**) needs huge tanks and cannot be stored long, so they are **unsuited to military missiles**.
**Hypergolic** propellants (ignite on contact) are the ones ideal for **spacecraft manoeuvring**.
xa: They were also used on the **space shuttle** — **Discovery's** tanks held LH2 + LOX.
Isp ~**450 s** — highest; exhaust only **water vapour**.
Indian examples: **CE-7.5** (GSLV Mk II upper stage) and **CE-20** (LVM3 **C25** upper stage).

naa945e0076e.s: What is the significance of the CE-20 bootstrap-mode start test?
o: It eliminates the need for liquid oxygen in the engine.
It proves that CE-20 can operate only with solid propellant.
It demonstrates starting on the engine’s own propellant flow without external gas, supporting in-space restart.
It converts CE-20 into a hypergolic engine.
naa945e0076e.x: Bootstrap mode starts the engine using its own propellant flow without external gas and is important for in-space restart capability.
naa945e0076e.tq: Connect the test method with its operational consequence rather than with a propellant change.
xs: The bootstrap-mode test shows CE-20 **starting on its own propellant flow without external gas**, key for **in-space restart** — option **(3)**.
CE-20 still burns **LOX + LH2**, so options (1), (2) and (4) are wrong — it is neither solid nor **hypergolic**.
xa: The test was passed in **Nov 2025**.
CE-20: **200 kN** class, **gas-generator** cycle, **LVM3 C25** upper stage.
⚠ **CE-7.5** (GSLV Mk II) uses **staged combustion**.

n808d1577114.s: India's Cryogenic Upper Stage Project began in:
n808d1577114.x: The project began in 1994 at a cost of ₹300 crore, and a full cryogenic stage was tested in 2006.
xa: **GSLV Mk II** flew with the indigenous cryo stage (**CE-7.5**) on **5 Jan 2014**.
⚠ India is **not the fourth** to have cryogenic tech — Europe/France and Japan also had it.
**Glavkosmos deal (1991)** → **US MTCR sanctions (1992)** → Russia supplied only **7 engines**.

n9d8519312ab.s: SE2000 is planned for which applications?
o: Replacing the C25 in GSLV Mk II only
The PSLV first stage and S200 booster only
Replacing the L110 in LVM3-SC and for the NGLV
n9d8519312ab.x: SE2000 is planned for LVM3-SC, replacing the L110, and for the NGLV.
n9d8519312ab.tq: Match the engine with its planned vehicle-stage applications.
xs: **SE2000** is planned for **LVM3-SC (replacing the L110)** and the **NGLV** — option **(4)**.
**C25** belongs to **LVM3** (with CE-20), not GSLV Mk II; the **PSLV first stage/S200** are **solid HTPB** motors.
xa: SE2000 burns **refined kerosene + LOX** (semi-cryogenic).
It cleared **integrated test campaigns** (**2026**); **3rd hot test of the PHTA** at **60%** power validated ignition and start-up.
NGLV **"Soorya"** is planned with **semi-cryogenic** propulsion, **20,000 kg to LEO**.

n56cb369e8d4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the proposed NGLV 'Soorya'?
o: It is planned as a reusable heavy-lift rocket.
It is designed to carry about 10,000 kg to low Earth orbit.
Its projected LEO payload is about 2.5 times that of LVM3.
It is planned to use semi-cryogenic propulsion.
n56cb369e8d4.x: Soorya is designed to carry about 20,000 kg to LEO, not 10,000 kg.
xa: Size ~**90 m** tall; lift-off mass ~**1,000 t**.
Launch site: **Third Launch Pad**, Sriharikota.
Purpose: **Bharatiya Antariksh Station** (**2035**) and crewed lunar landing (**2040**).
Its semi-cryogenic engine is **SE2000** (refined kerosene + LOX).

n67d22df0d33.s: Agnilet, developed by Agnikul Cosmos, is described as the world’s first:
n67d22df0d33.x: Agnilet is described as the world’s first single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine.
n67d22df0d33.tq: Identify the exact superlative and engine category associated with the named product.
xs: **Agnilet** is the world's **first single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine** — option **(2)**.
The **800 kN full-flow staged combustion LOX-methane** engine is Astrobase's **EVEREST**.
**Agnite** is the 3D-printed **booster engine** for **Agnibaan**.
xa: Agnilet flew in **2024** from **"Dhanush"**, India's **first private launch pad** at Sriharikota.
**Agnikul Cosmos** is a **Chennai** start-up.
Agnite, made of **Inconel**, is the world's **largest single-piece 3D-printed booster engine**.

n6c786ff1c24.s: Agnilet was flown in 2024 from which launch pad?
o: Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre’s private pad
Dhanush, India’s first private launch pad at Sriharikota
Satish Dhawan Space Centre’s second launch pad
A private launch pad at Bengaluru
n6c786ff1c24.x: Agnilet was flown in 2024 from Dhanush at Sriharikota, described as India’s first private launch pad.
n6c786ff1c24.tq: Test the precise location and identity of the launch facility.
xs: Agnilet flew in **2024** from **"Dhanush"**, India's **first private launch pad** at **Sriharikota** — option **(2)**.
It is Agnikul Cosmos's own pad, not a pad of **VSSC**, SDSC's second pad, or a Bengaluru site.
xa: Agnilet: world's **first single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine**.
**Agnikul Cosmos** is a **Chennai** start-up; its **Agnite** engine is for the **Agnibaan** booster.
**Astrobase** (**Bengaluru**) unveiled **EVEREST** in **Aug 2026**.

n34502ccb4c5.s: EVEREST, unveiled by Astrobase in August 2026, is described as India’s first private:
o: 800 kN full-flow staged combustion LOX-methane engine
solid motor for the Agnibaan booster
n34502ccb4c5.x: Astrobase’s EVEREST is described as India’s first private 800 kN full-flow staged combustion LOX-methane engine.
n34502ccb4c5.tq: Combine the distinctive thrust rating with the engine cycle and propellant pair.
xs: **EVEREST** is India's first private **800 kN full-flow staged combustion LOX-methane** engine — option **(1)**.
The **300 mN Hall thruster** is ISRO's **Stationary Plasma Thruster**; the single-piece semi-cryogenic engine is **Agnilet**.
The **Agnibaan** booster engine is **Agnite** (Agnikul).
xa: **Astrobase** is based in **Bengaluru**; EVEREST was unveiled in **Aug 2026**.
**LOX-methane** is **cleaner and cheaper**, key for Mars-return and **In-Situ Resource Utilization**.
**Starship** also burns ~**1,200 t** of liquid methane + LOX.

nd030d4d9c1b.s: Skyroot's Vikram-1 reached orbit as India's first private orbital rocket on Mission:
nd030d4d9c1b.x: Vikram-1 (three solid stages + one liquid stage, 290 kg to 500 km SSO) reached orbit on Mission Aagaman.
xa: Vikram-1 reached orbit on **Mission Aagaman** (Jul **2026**) → **India's first private orbital rocket**.
Skyroot also static-tested the **KALAM 1200** solid motor at **SDSC-SHAR**.
Agnikul's **Agnilet** flew in **2024** from the private pad **"Dhanush"**.

n61dc44eab56.s: What is the principal function of the spent PS4 stage in POEM?
o: It is used as a planetary landing engine.
It is converted into a reusable crew capsule.
It is reused as an orbital platform for start-up and academic payloads.
It serves as a cryogenic upper stage for GSLV.
n61dc44eab56.x: POEM reuses the spent PS4 stage as an orbital platform for start-up and academic payloads.
n61dc44eab56.tq: Follow the transformation of the spent stage into its orbital-platform role.
xs: POEM reuses the **spent PS4 stage** as an **orbital platform for start-up and academic payloads** — option **(3)**.
It is not a landing engine, crew capsule or **GSLV** cryogenic stage (that is **CE-7.5**).
xa: POEM = **PSLV Orbital Experimental Module**.
ISRO's **300 mN** Hall-type **xenon** thruster completed a **1,000-hour life test**.
**LOX-methane** is cleaner + cheaper and suits **In-Situ Resource Utilization**.

n741dedb3cb9.s: Which one of the following best explains the principal advantage of a scramjet over a conventional rocket during atmospheric flight?
o: It operates with subsonic airflow at speeds below Mach 2.
It eliminates the need for fuel during hypersonic flight.
It uses oxygen from the atmosphere, thereby reducing the weight of onboard oxidiser.
It uses a compressor to compress atmospheric air before combustion.
n741dedb3cb9.x: A scramjet uses oxygen from the atmosphere, so it need not carry the entire oxidiser required by a rocket. It still requires fuel and works with supersonic airflow.
n741dedb3cb9.tq: Use the function-based option; distinguish an air-breathing engine from a rocket.
xs: A scramjet uses **atmospheric oxygen**, so it **cuts onboard oxidiser weight** — option **(3)**.
It still needs **fuel**, so option (2) is wrong.
It burns in **supersonic** airflow at **Mach 5-6+** — subsonic combustion above **Mach 2** is a **ramjet**.
Compression comes from **forward speed**, **no compressor**, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: Challenge: **"a candle in a hurricane"**.
India became the **4th** country (after **US, Russia, China**) to demonstrate scramjet flight (ATV, **Aug 2016**).
DRDO's actively cooled scramjet combustor ran **20 minutes** on indigenous **endothermic hydrocarbon** fuel (May **2026**).
n741dedb3cb9.fixed: a scramjet does not 'carry' atmospheric oxygen; it draws it in

n6c077bb86e4.s: With ISRO's ATV scramjet flight test (August 2016), India became the ____ country to demonstrate scramjet flight.
n6c077bb86e4.x: India became the fourth country, after the US, Russia and China.
xa: **HSTDV** is **DRDO's** scramjet vehicle — ⚠ ATV = ISRO, HSTDV = DRDO.
Scramjet: **supersonic** combustion, **Mach 5-6+**.
DRDO's scramjet combustor ran **20 minutes** (May **2026**).

n6a970e54ec0.s: HSTDV, a scramjet vehicle, was developed by:
n6a970e54ec0.x: HSTDV is DRDO's scramjet vehicle; DRDO has also tested an actively cooled full-scale scramjet combustor with an indigenous endothermic fuel.
xa: ⚠ **ATV** = ISRO (**2016**); **HSTDV** = DRDO.
ISRO's ATV made India the **4th** country to demonstrate scramjet flight.
Scramjets burn in **supersonic** airflow at **Mach 5-6+**.

nphysics-23-23.s: The International Space Station (ISS) is located at an altitude of approximately:
nphysics-23-23.x: The ISS orbits at about 400 km, inside Low Earth Orbit. 36,000 km is geostationary height.
nphysics-23-23.tq: Recall ISS altitude as a LEO value.
n: The International Space Station is approximately 400 km above Earth. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 96-98]
xs: The ISS is at about **400 km** — option **(2)**, inside **Low Earth orbit**.
**36000 km** is the **geostationary** height; **160 km** and **2000 km** are only the lower and upper limits of LEO.
xa: **LEO** = **160 km to 2000 km** above Earth.
GEO has a **period of 24 hours**, moving **west to east** in the equatorial plane.
The ISS orbits in **LEO**, while communication satellites like INSAT use **GEO**.

n907a35a5697.s: A geostationary satellite orbits at about ____ above the equator.
n907a35a5697.x: GEO is about 35,786 km above the equator with a 24-hour period; the height does not depend on the satellite's mass.
xa: The satellite moves **west to east** in the **equatorial plane** (zero inclination), so it looks stationary.
**Low Earth orbit** spans **160 km to 2000 km**; the **ISS** is about **400 km** up.
A **polar** orbit passes over the **poles**; an **elliptical** orbit has different **apogee** and **perigee**.

n9e04e08c967.s: APPLE, India's first experimental communication satellite launched in 1981, stands for:
o: Asian Public Platform for Long-distance Education
Aerial Payload and Propulsion Laboratory Experiment
n9e04e08c967.x: APPLE stands for Ariane Passenger PayLoad Experiment, India's first experimental communication satellite (1981).
xa: **INSAT-1A** (**1982**) was the **first INSAT**.
INSAT system **commissioned 1983** → operational since **INSAT-1B**.
**INSAT-2** (**1992-1999**) was the **first fully indigenous** INSAT series.

ncf0803650c7.s: INSAT satellites are controlled from the Master Control Facility at:
ncf0803650c7.x: The MCF is at Hassan, Karnataka; INSAT is a joint venture of DoS, DoT, IMD, AIR and Doordarshan coordinated by the ICC.
xa: System **commissioned 1983**; operational since **INSAT-1B**.
**10** in-orbit communication satellites were transferred to **NSIL** in **2022**.
India has **19** operational communication satellites (**2026**).

nc6b9ba87c71.s: INSAT-4C was lost in 2006 when which launch vehicle failed?
nc6b9ba87c71.x: INSAT-4C was lost on GSLV-F02 (2006); its replacement INSAT-4CR flew on GSLV-F04 in 2007.
xa: India has **19** operational communication satellites (2026).
The INSAT system was **commissioned in 1983** and became operational with **INSAT-1B**.
INSAT is coordinated by the **INSAT Coordination Committee (ICC)** and controlled from **MCF, Hassan (Karnataka)**.
**APPLE** (1981) was India's first experimental communication satellite; **INSAT-1A** (1982) the first INSAT.

nc5c0363c38a.s: The Indian National Satellite (INSAT) system is best described as a:
o: Combined communication and meteorological satellite system
nc5c0363c38a.x: INSAT serves both communication and meteorology from geostationary orbit (JPSC 2021 keyed it as a 'meteorological satellite'), and also carries broadcasting, disaster warning and search-and-rescue. It is not purely military, not a sun-synchronous remote-sensing system (that is IRS), and not a navigation system (that is NavIC).
xs: INSAT is a **combined communication and meteorological** system — option **(2)**; JPSC **2021** keyed it as "**Meteorological Satellite**".
It sits on a **geostationary** platform, so it is not a sun-synchronous remote-sensing system, and it also serves civil broadcasting, so it is not purely military.
xa: It also carries **TV broadcasting, disaster warning and search-and-rescue**.
Joint venture of **DoS, DoT, IMD, AIR and Doordarshan**, coordinated by the **ICC**.
First INSAT: **INSAT-1A** (**1982**); system commissioned **1983**.

n4c70554af92.s: The INSAT system was commissioned in:
n4c70554af92.x: The INSAT system was commissioned in 1983 with satellites procured abroad; the INSAT-2 series began in 1992.
xa: **INSAT-1A** (**1982**) was the first INSAT.
INSAT-2 was the **first fully indigenous** INSAT series.
**APPLE** (**1981**) was India's first experimental communication satellite.

ndf5357088b1.s: KALPANA-1 holds which distinction in the Indian satellite programme?
o: First fully indigenous communication satellite series
First satellite for encrypted naval links
First commercial communication satellite in low Earth orbit
ndf5357088b1.x: KALPANA-1 was India's first exclusive weather satellite.
ndf5357088b1.tq: Direct recall of a first-in-category distinction.
xs: **KALPANA-1** is India's **first exclusive weather satellite** — option **(4)**.
The **first fully indigenous** INSAT series is **INSAT-2** (**1992-1999**); encrypted naval links are **CMS-03**.
xa: KALPANA-1 (**METSAT**) was launched in **Sep 2002** by **PSLV**.
Later weather satellites: **INSAT-3D** (**2013**), **INSAT-3DR** (**2016**), **INSAT-3DS**.
INSAT is a dual **meteorological + communication** system (JPSC **2021**).

n502e74d2c37.s: The heaviest communication satellite launched from Indian soil is:
n502e74d2c37.x: CMS-03/GSAT-7R (4,410 kg, LVM3-M5, Nov 2025) is the heaviest launched from India; GSAT-11 (~5.8 t) is the heaviest ISRO-built, launched abroad.
xa: GSAT-N2 (GSAT-20) is for **broadband** and in-flight connectivity.
⚠ CMS-03 weight: **LENS** gives **4,400 kg** instead of 4,410 kg.
**GSAT-31** (6 Feb 2019) and **GSAT-30** (2020) were launched from **Kourou** on **Ariane**.
**GSAT-30** (17 Jan 2020, Kourou) is a **telecommunication** satellite (APPSC 2018 PYQ).

nd3b74033e3c.s: GSAT-30, launched on 17 January 2020 from Kourou, French Guiana, is primarily a:
nd3b74033e3c.x: GSAT-30 is a telecommunication satellite launched by Ariane from Kourou on 17 Jan 2020 (APPSC 2018 PYQ theme). Navigation is NavIC/NVS, earth observation is EOS/IRS, and the exclusive weather satellite was KALPANA-1.
xs: **GSAT-30** is a **telecommunication** satellite — option **(1)** (APPSC **2018** PYQ).
It was launched on **17 Jan 2020** from **Kourou** by Ariane.
The **exclusive meteorological** satellite was **KALPANA-1**.
xa: **GSAT-31** was also launched from Kourou on **6 Feb 2019**.
Other Kourou launches: **INSAT-3A** (**2003**), **INSAT-4A** (**2005**), **INSAT-4B** (**2007**), **GSAT-8**, **GSAT-11**.
**GSAT-N2** instead flew on SpaceX **Falcon 9** from **Cape Canaveral**.

nf46ddeef888.s: Which of the following sets contains only high-throughput or broadband satellites?
nf46ddeef888.x: GSAT-19, GSAT-29, GSAT-11 and GSAT-N2 are identified with high-throughput broadband services for underserved areas, in-flight links and defence, complementing BharatNet.
nf46ddeef888.tq: Group satellites by service category and reject meteorological, educational and strategic-only sets.
xs: **GSAT-19, GSAT-29, GSAT-11 and GSAT-N2** are the high-throughput/broadband satellites — option **(1)**.
**KALPANA-1, INSAT-3D/3DR** are meteorological; **GSAT-7** series and **GSAT-6** are strategic; **APPLE/INSAT-1** are early satellites.
xa: Uses: **underserved areas**, **in-flight links**, **defence**.
They **complement BharatNet**.
**Ka-band** is used for high-throughput broadband (GSAT-11, GSAT-N2).

n73faa683e72.s: CMS-03 (GSAT-7R), giving encrypted anti-jam naval links up to 2,000 km from the coast, was launched by:
xa: Launched **Nov 2025**; **4,410 kg** — heaviest communication satellite from **Indian soil** (LENS gives **4,400 kg**).
It replaced **GSAT-7 "Rukmini"** for the **Navy**.
Bands: **UHF, S, C, Ku**.

ne9e0cd17442.s: The early-warning capability of INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR has had which of the following effects?
o: It sharply reduced cyclone-related deaths on the east coast, including Andhra Pradesh.
It provided encrypted naval communication up to 2,000 km from the coast.
It made BlueBird Block-2 the largest satellite in low Earth orbit.
It enabled the South Asian countries to opt out of satellite services.
ne9e0cd17442.x: INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR early warnings sharply reduced cyclone deaths along the east coast, including Andhra Pradesh.
ne9e0cd17442.tq: Identify the concrete consequence of a satellite-based warning system.
xs: **INSAT-3D/3DR** early warnings **sharply cut cyclone deaths** on the **east coast, incl. Andhra Pradesh** — option **(1)**.
Encrypted naval links up to **2,000 km** are **CMS-03's** role, not INSAT-3D's.
xa: INSAT-3D (**2013**) and INSAT-3DR (**2016**) serve **advanced meteorology** (cyclone, monsoon, rainfall).
Cyclones cited: **Phailin, Fani, Amphan**.
**INSAT-3DS** data feed **Bhuvan** warnings (Apr **2026**).

n8cea058ea15.s: GSAT-7A 'Angry Bird' (2018) is the dedicated satellite of the:
n8cea058ea15.x: GSAT-7A serves the Air Force; GSAT-7 'Rukmini' serves the Navy and GSAT-7B is proposed for the Army.
xa: **CMS-03 (GSAT-7R)**, **4,410 kg**, gives **encrypted, anti-jam** links up to **2,000 km** from the coast.
**GSAT-6** (**2015**) has a large deployable antenna for mobile/strategic use.
**UHF** band is used for **military** communication.

n25f63de61fc.s: The South Asia Satellite (GSAT-9) was launched in May 2017 on:
n25f63de61fc.x: GSAT-9 flew on GSLV-F09 in May 2017; Pakistan opted out of it.
xa: **GSAT-7 "Rukmini"** (2013) = **Navy**; **GSAT-7A "Angry Bird"** (2018) = **Air Force**; **GSAT-7B** = Army (proposed).
**GSAT-6** (2015) has a large deployable antenna for mobile/strategic use.
⚠ CMS-03 replaced **GSAT-7 Rukmini** for the Navy.

n5dc0d154909.s: Which satellite frequency band is typically used for DTH and VSAT?
n5dc0d154909.x: Ku-band serves DTH and VSAT; C for telecom/TV distribution, Ka for high-throughput broadband and S for mobile satellite services.
xa: C-band covers **4-8 GHz**; Ku-band **12-18 GHz**.
**UHF** is used for **military** links (CMS-03 has **UHF, S, C, Ku**).
**MF is not used** in INSAT/GSAT communication (RPSC **2021**).
⚠ DWS: uplink **C-band**, downlink **S-band**.

n719b914d1a0.s: In satellite applications, MSS refers to:
n719b914d1a0.x: MSS means mobile satellite services; DTH is Direct-to-Home broadcasting, VSAT business networks and DSNG satellite news gathering.
xa: **Ku-band** carries **DTH and VSAT**; **S-band** carries mobile satellite services.
**Swayam Prabha** uses **GSAT-15** for **40 free DTH education channels**.
Other services: radio networking, **telemedicine**, **Village Resource Centres**.

nca956721812.s: Swayam Prabha's 40 free DTH education channels are beamed through:
nca956721812.x: Swayam Prabha uses GSAT-15 to provide 40 free Direct-to-Home education channels.
xa: GSAT-15 also carries a **GAGAN** payload (with **GSAT-8**, **GSAT-10**).
**EDUSAT (GSAT-3)** provided **two-way classroom links**.
Other social services: **GRAMSAT**, telemedicine, **Village Resource Centres**.

n852de5fcc84.s: In the Disaster Warning System, cyclone warnings from the Cyclone Warning Centre at Chennai are
o: sent upward through S-band and received through C-band by all receivers without selection
sent upward through UHF and received through MF by television households
sent upward through C-band and received through S-band by selectively addressable receivers
sent upward through Ku-band and received through Ka-band only by military stations
n852de5fcc84.x: The warning signal goes up on C-band and comes down on S-band to selectively addressable DWS receivers along the coast.
n852de5fcc84.tq: Trace the communication path in order: uplink band, downlink band and receiver type.
xs: DWS warnings go **up on C-band** and **down on S-band** to **selectively addressable receivers** — option **(3)**.
The warnings originate at the **Cyclone Warning Centre, Chennai**.
**MF** is not used in INSAT communication; **UHF** is a military band.
xa: DWS receivers are placed **along the coast**.
**INSAT-3D/3DR** warnings sharply cut cyclone deaths on the east coast, incl. **AP**.
INSAT also carries **search-and-rescue** transponders under **COSPAS-SARSAT**.

n8db4e468e9a.s: INSAT’s search-and-rescue transponders operate under the international programme known as
n8db4e468e9a.x: INSAT carries search-and-rescue transponders under the international COSPAS-SARSAT programme.
n8db4e468e9a.tq: Separate search-and-rescue terminology from navigation and education programmes.
xs: INSAT's search-and-rescue transponders work under the international **COSPAS-SARSAT** programme — option **(3)**.
**Swayam Prabha** is a DTH education service; **GAGAN** is a payload on **GSAT-8, -10, -15**; **BharatNet** is terrestrial broadband.
xa: INSAT's multipurpose platform also covers telecom, **TV broadcasting**, **meteorology** and **disaster warning**.
⚠ DWS: uplink **C-band**, downlink **S-band**.
INSAT is controlled from **MCF, Hassan**.

n5ede4ff1f6c.s: Which one of the following frequency bands is NOT used for INSAT/GSAT satellite communication?
n5ede4ff1f6c.x: MF is not used in INSAT/GSAT communication (RPSC 2021). C/extended C serves telecom and TV distribution, Ku serves DTH and VSAT, and S serves mobile satellite services and the DWS downlink.
n5ede4ff1f6c.tq: Satellites use C, Ku, Ka, S, UHF; not MF.
xs: **MF (Medium Frequency)** is **not used** in INSAT/GSAT communication — option **(4)** (RPSC **2021**).
**C-band** serves telecom and TV distribution; **Ku** serves **DTH and VSAT**; **S** serves mobile satellite services and the **DWS downlink**.
xa: **Ka-band** is for high-throughput broadband (**GSAT-11**, **GSAT-N2**).
**UHF** is for **military** use (CMS-03).
C-band: **4-8 GHz**; Ku-band: **12-18 GHz**.

nbd2dfff37b7.s: GPS satellites in the original design orbit at an altitude of about:
nbd2dfff37b7.x: GPS (US DoD, 1973) was designed with 24 satellites in 6 orbits at about 20,200 km; each circles the Earth twice a day.
xa: First GPS satellite: **1978**; now about **30** satellites (Mar **2026**).
⚠ **GPS** = 24 satellites, 6 orbits, global; **NavIC** = **7** satellites, regional.

nda1901e67f7.s: NavIC's four inclined geosynchronous satellites are at about ____ to the equator.
nda1901e67f7.x: NavIC has seven satellites: three in geostationary orbit and four in inclined geosynchronous orbit at about 29°.
xa: Coverage: India + **1,500 km** beyond its borders.
Bands: **L5 and S**; **NVS** satellites add civilian **L1**.
⚠ **GPS** = **24** satellites, **6** orbits, **20,200 km**, global.

n23405a4dc8a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about NavIC signals and services?
o: The newer NVS satellites add a civilian L1 signal.
The original NavIC signals are broadcast in the L1 and L2 bands.
The Standard Positioning Service is open to all civilians, with accuracy better than 20 m.
The Restricted Service is the encrypted service.
n23405a4dc8a.x: Original NavIC signals are in the L5 and S bands; L1 and L2 are GPS signals.
xa: The **Restricted Service (RS)** is **encrypted**, for authorised/military users.
SPS timing is better than **40 ns**.
NavIC = **7 satellites** (**3 GEO + 4 inclined GSO** at **29°**), covering India + **1,500 km**.
⚠ **GPS** = **24** satellites in **6** orbits at **20,200 km**; NavIC is regional.

nfd76bd92f93.s: Which organisation is the nodal authority for both NavIC and GAGAN?
o: Satellite Navigation Programme Office under ISRO
Directorate General of Civil Aviation alone
Ministry of Defence’s Integrated Defence Staff
nfd76bd92f93.x: The Satellite Navigation Programme Office under ISRO is the nodal authority for NavIC and GAGAN.
nfd76bd92f93.tq: Identify the coordinating authority rather than an implementing or certifying agency.
xs: The **Satellite Navigation Programme Office** under ISRO is nodal for **NavIC and GAGAN** — option **(1)**.
**AAI** co-developed GAGAN and **DGCA** certified it, but neither is the nodal authority.
xa: GAGAN = **GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation**.
⚠ **GAGAN** augments GPS (aviation); **NavIC** is an independent regional system.
GAGAN ground segment: **INRES, INMCC, INLUS**.

ne7aec29a898.s: NavIC, a regional system unlike the global GPS, covers India and about how far beyond its borders?
ne7aec29a898.x: NavIC is regional, covering India plus about 1,500 km beyond its borders, whereas GPS is global.
xa: Other limitations: a **thin receiver ecosystem** (L5/S not in phone chips).
Repeated **atomic-clock failures** and the **NVS-02** launch failure (Mar **2026**).
GPS has about **30** satellites; NavIC is designed for **7**.

n0d2b78fe557.s: An error of approximately one microsecond in an atomic clock used for positioning may produce a position error of about:
n0d2b78fe557.x: A one-microsecond clock error can produce an approximate position error of 300 metres, illustrating the importance of atomic clocks in navigation.
n0d2b78fe557.tq: Convert the stated clock-error relationship without changing the unit scale.
xs: A **1 microsecond** clock error gives a position error of ~**300 metres** (300 m) — option **(3)**.
This is why navigation satellites carry **atomic clocks**.
xa: NavIC's first-generation **SpectraTime** (Swiss) rubidium clocks kept failing → ISRO switched to **indigenous SAC clocks** in **2018**.
**NVS-01** was the first with an **indigenous rubidium atomic clock**.
NavIC SPS gives timing better than **40 ns**.

n0294b71a0d2.s: NavIC (formerly IRNSS) became fully operational in:
n0294b71a0d2.x: NavIC became fully operational in 2018; navigation satellites have been launched since 2013. Its genesis lies in the Kargil (1999) GPS denial.
xa: Full form "Navigation with Indian Constellation" was asked in **CGPSC 2021**.
**11** navigation satellites launched since **2013** (Mar **2026**).
Coverage: India + **1,500 km** beyond its borders.

n25612bd605c.s: The IRNSS-1 series satellites were launched from Sriharikota using:
n25612bd605c.x: All IRNSS satellites were launched from Sriharikota, and the IRNSS-1 series used PSLV launch vehicles.
xa: **IRNSS-1A to 1G** formed the 7 + replacements; **11** navigation satellites since **2013**.
NVS series uses **GSLV**: **NVS-01** (**GSLV-F12**) and **NVS-02** (**GSLV-F15**).
**IRNSS-1D** was decommissioned to **600 km above GEO** (**9 Apr 2026**).

na7680b95e67.s: NVS-01, the first navigation satellite with an indigenous rubidium atomic clock, was launched in May 2023 by:
na7680b95e67.x: NVS-01 was launched in May 2023 on GSLV-F12 and was the first to carry an indigenous rubidium atomic clock; GSLV-F15 flew in January 2025.
xa: NVS-01 is the **second-generation** NavIC satellite.
First-generation clocks came from Swiss firm **SpectraTime** and kept failing.
NVS-01 is one of only **3** PNT-capable satellites left (with **IRNSS-1B, 1I**).

n004c42c038b.s: The launch of NVS-02 in January 2025 was which milestone launch from Sriharikota?
n004c42c038b.x: NVS-02 (GSLV-F15) was the 100th Sriharikota launch; a valve glitch left it in the wrong orbit.
xa: **NVS-01** (May **2023**, **GSLV-F12**) was the first with an **indigenous rubidium atomic clock**.
**11** navigation satellites have been launched since **2013**, all from **Sriharikota**.
First-generation **SpectraTime** (Swiss) clocks failed; ISRO switched to **SAC** indigenous clocks in **2018**.

n3e145c95f02.s: The repeatedly failing rubidium clocks of first-generation IRNSS satellites were supplied by a firm from:
n3e145c95f02.x: They came from Swiss firm SpectraTime; ISRO switched to indigenous clocks in 2018.
xa: **NVS-01** was the **first with an indigenous rubidium atomic clock**.
**IRNSS-1F's** last clock failed on **13 Mar 2026**.
A **1 microsecond** clock error ≈ **300 m** position error.

nd2dd3bbceb5.s: After the last clock on IRNSS-1F failed on 13 March 2026, how many PNT-capable NavIC satellites remained?
nd2dd3bbceb5.x: Only IRNSS-1B, IRNSS-1I and NVS-01 remained PNT-capable, three satellites, below the four needed for the service.
xa: 1F still continues **one-way messaging** (**15 and 20 Mar 2026**).
**IRNSS-1D** was decommissioned to **600 km above GEO** (**9 Apr 2026**).
ISRO was urged to fix issues before the next **NVS** launches.

n557ff96a0d5.s: Which company developed India’s first NavIC-based device intended to provide precise directions for infrastructure projects?
n557ff96a0d5.x: Elena Geo Systems developed India’s first NavIC-based device for precise directions on infrastructure projects.
n557ff96a0d5.tq: Match the specialised company with its specific technological product.
xs: India's first NavIC-based device was made by **Elena Geo Systems** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2023**).
It gives **precise directions on infrastructure projects**.
**SpectraTime** was the Swiss clock supplier; **AAI** co-developed **GAGAN**; **Qualcomm** makes NavIC-supporting chipsets.
xa: **Qualcomm Snapdragon** chipsets support NavIC.
**MoRTH's AIS-140** rule made NavIC trackers compulsory in **public transport vehicles**.
Government urged NavIC for **Indian Standard Time** (Mar **2026**).

nfd13da926a9.s: MoRTH's AIS-140 rule makes NavIC-enabled location trackers compulsory in:
nfd13da926a9.x: AIS-140 covers public transport vehicles, not all private cars; Snapdragon chipsets support NavIC.
xa: The first NavIC-based device was by **Elena Geo Systems** (APPSC 2023).
Reconfigured **IRNSS-1A** broadcasts **cyclone, tsunami** and high-wave warnings to **fishermen**.
Uses include **precise timing** (power, telecom, banking), **surveying** and **vehicle tracking**.

ndcb20bf7138.s: Reconfigured IRNSS-1A helped fishermen at sea by broadcasting warnings relating to:
ndcb20bf7138.x: Reconfigured IRNSS-1A broadcasts cyclone, tsunami and high-wave warnings to fishermen at sea.
ndcb20bf7138.tq: Match the satellite function with the specific maritime-warning group.
xs: Reconfigured **IRNSS-1A** broadcasts warnings of **cyclones, tsunamis and high waves** to fishermen at sea — option **(2)**.
It does not carry earthquake, pollution or solar-flare alerts.
xa: AP angle: fishermen alerts over NavIC help the **long AP coastline** during cyclones.
NavIC also serves **disaster management** and **marine navigation**.
**IRNSS-1A to 1G** formed the original **7** + replacements.

n856cb704850.s: GAGAN is an augmentation system whose full form is:
n856cb704850.x: GAGAN stands for GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation.
n856cb704850.tq: Use exact expansion discrimination among similar navigation terms.
xs: GAGAN = **GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation** — option **(1)**.
It was developed by **ISRO and the Airports Authority of India (AAI)**.
xa: It is an **SBAS** — it broadcasts corrections for **orbit, clock and ionospheric delay**.
Payloads ride on **GSAT-8, GSAT-10, GSAT-15**.
⚠ **GAGAN** augments GPS; **NavIC** is an independent regional system.

nfe8ecce6eed.s: The principal function of a Satellite-Based Augmentation System is to:
o: replace every navigation satellite with a ground-based radar
broadcast real-time corrections for orbit, clock and ionospheric delay
increase satellite altitude without correcting navigation data
nfe8ecce6eed.x: An SBAS broadcasts real-time corrections for orbit, clock and ionospheric delay, improving accuracy, integrity and availability.
nfe8ecce6eed.tq: Identify the correction functions that define SBAS operation.
xs: An SBAS **broadcasts real-time corrections for orbit, clock and ionospheric delay** — option **(3)**.
This improves GPS **accuracy, integrity and availability** (UPSC **2025**, statement I correct).
xa: SBAS examples: **WAAS** (USA), **EGNOS** (Europe), **MSAS** (Japan), **GAGAN** (India).
GAGAN serves the Indian **Flight Information Region**.
**DGCA** certified GAGAN for approach guidance in **2015**.

nf1f0afe3a38.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about GAGAN?
o: It was jointly developed by ISRO and DRDO.
It serves the Indian Flight Information Region.
It supports precision approach and landing for civil aviation.
DGCA certified it for aviation approach guidance in 2015.
nf1f0afe3a38.x: GAGAN was developed by ISRO and the Airports Authority of India, not DRDO.
xa: **GAGAN** = **GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation**; payloads on **GSAT-8, GSAT-10, GSAT-15**.
Other SBAS: **WAAS** (USA), **EGNOS** (Europe), **MSAS** (Japan).
⚠ **GAGAN** augments GPS; **NavIC** is an independent regional system.
Ground segment: **INRES**, **INMCC**, **INLUS**.

n1bcb1a8da4f.s: GAGAN payloads are carried on GSAT-8, GSAT-10 and:
n1bcb1a8da4f.x: GAGAN payloads are on GSAT-8, GSAT-10 and GSAT-15.
xa: GAGAN serves the Indian **Flight Information Region**.
Use: **precision approach and landing** for civil aviation.
**DGCA** certified it in **2015**.

nbe5a10d88f1.s: The thin ecosystem of NavIC receivers was initially related mainly to the fact that:
o: L5 and S bands were not commonly included in mobile-phone chipsets
NavIC had no satellites in orbit
GPS prevented all receivers from using satellite signals
NavIC signals were transmitted only through optical fibre
nbe5a10d88f1.x: Receiver adoption was constrained because L5 and S bands were not commonly supported in phone chipsets; the newer civilian L1 signal helps address this limitation.
nbe5a10d88f1.tq: Connect the receiver limitation with the relevant frequency-band issue.
xs: The receiver ecosystem was thin because **L5 and S bands** were **not in common phone chips** — option **(1)**.
This eased only with the civilian **L1** signal on **NVS** satellites.
xa: **Qualcomm Snapdragon** chipsets support NavIC.
Other limitations: **regional coverage** only; repeated **atomic-clock failures**.
**AIS-140** pushed NavIC trackers into public transport vehicles.

nbb3f2e11be9.s: Which combination best explains why NavIC could not fully replace GPS over India as reported in March 2026?
o: Absence of any regional coverage and lack of satellites since 1999
Excessive global coverage and too many civilian receivers
Repeated atomic-clock failures and the NVS-02 launch failure
Only the use of geostationary satellites, with no clock problems
nbb3f2e11be9.x: Repeated atomic-clock failures and the NVS-02 launch failure reduced the effective constellation, preventing NavIC from fully replacing GPS over India.
nbb3f2e11be9.tq: Combine the operational failure causes rather than choosing a coverage or orbit distraction.
xs: **Repeated atomic-clock failures** and the **NVS-02 launch failure** left NavIC unable to replace GPS over India — option **(3)** (Mar **2026**).
NavIC does have regional coverage (India + **1,500 km**), so option (1) is wrong.
xa: After **IRNSS-1F's** last clock failed (**13 Mar 2026**), only **3** PNT-capable satellites remained, below the **4** needed.
The Swiss **SpectraTime** clocks were replaced by indigenous **SAC** clocks in **2018**.
NVS-02 (**GSLV-F15**) ended up in the wrong orbit after a **valve glitch**.

ne4c45deaa38.s: Which one of the following is an example of an active remote-sensing system?
ne4c45deaa38.x: LiDAR sends its own laser pulse and reads the echo, so it is active (APPSC 2023: laser is active). Multispectral cameras, infrared radiometers and visible cameras record sunlight reflected or heat emitted by the target, so they are passive.
ne4c45deaa38.tq: Own pulse + echo = active: RISAT SAR, LiDAR.
xs: **Laser-based LiDAR** is **active** — it sends its own pulse and reads the echo — option **(3)** (APPSC **2023**).
**Multispectral cameras**, **infrared radiometers** and **visible cameras** are **passive** — they record sunlight or emitted heat.
xa: Another active system: **RISAT radar (SAR)**.
LiDAR maps **elevation, 3D terrain and forest canopy height**.
Resourcesat and Oceansat are passive systems.

n4ff806e568c.s: Which one of the following most appropriately describes remote sensing?
o: Preparation of maps only through manual surveying
Measurement of only the chemical composition of rocks by direct sampling
Recording of atmospheric pressure exclusively through ground instruments
Collection of information about the Earth without physical contact, using reflected or emitted electromagnetic radiation
n4ff806e568c.x: Remote sensing obtains information about the Earth without physical contact by detecting reflected or emitted electromagnetic radiation.
n4ff806e568c.tq: Use the precise definition and eliminate options that restrict the concept to one application or instrument.
xs: Remote sensing is the **collection of information about the Earth without physical contact**, using **reflected or emitted electromagnetic radiation** — option **(4)**.
Manual surveying, direct rock sampling and ground pressure gauges all involve contact or on-site measurement, so they are not remote sensing.
xa: Chain: **energy source** → radiation through atmosphere → **interaction with target** → sensor recording → **transmission, reception and processing** → interpretation → application.
**Passive** sensors use sunlight or emitted heat; **active** sensors send their own pulse (e.g. **RISAT SAR**, **LiDAR**).
In India, data are processed at **NRSC, Hyderabad** (nodal).

n8099481514f.s: Hyperspectral remote sensing is particularly useful for:
o: Producing radar echoes from a single microwave band
Identifying materials or chemicals using hundreds of narrow spectral bands
Measuring only the revisit interval of a satellite
Determining satellite launch velocity without imaging
n8099481514f.x: Hyperspectral sensing uses hundreds of narrow spectral bands, enabling identification of materials and their chemical characteristics.
n8099481514f.tq: Link the prefix ‘hyper’ with numerous narrow bands and material discrimination.
xs: Hyperspectral sensing uses **hundreds of narrow bands** for **material/chemical identification** — option **(2)**.
Radar echoes come from **SAR** (active, microwave), not hyperspectral imagers.
xa: Example: DRDO's hyperspectral **EOS-N1 "Anvesha"** — lost on **PSLV-C62** (Jan **2026**).
**HySIS** is ISRO's hyperspectral imaging satellite.
**EOS-05** carries multispectral + hyperspectral imaging (visible to long-wave IR) from GEO.

nfa3d37506cc.s: Which technique is most directly suited to detecting heat from volcanic eruptions, forest fires and urban heat?
nfa3d37506cc.x: Thermal infrared sensing records emitted heat and is therefore useful for volcanic eruptions, forest fires and urban heat mapping.
nfa3d37506cc.tq: Link emitted heat with thermal infrared and eliminate techniques measuring vegetation, elevation or deformation.
xs: **Thermal infrared** records **emitted heat** — **volcanic eruptions**, forest fires, urban heat — option **(4)**.
APPSC **2023** asked about **infrared-sensitive sensors** for volcanic eruptions.
**NDVI**, **LiDAR** and **InSAR** map vegetation, elevation and deformation respectively.
xa: Forest-fire monitoring is a national use (**INFFRAS**).
**EOS-05** sensors span visible, near-IR, **short-wave IR** and **long-wave IR**.
Infrared radiometers are **passive** sensors.

n9b2be30b3dd.s: The typical altitude of a sun-synchronous polar orbit is about:
n9b2be30b3dd.x: SSOs are near-polar at about 500-900 km, passing a place at the same local solar time for uniform lighting.
xa: **PSLV** was built for this: ~**1,600 kg** to **620 km SSO**.
**MEO** (**2,000-30,000 km**) is used for navigation (**GPS**).
GEO and GSO both have a period of about **23 h 56 min**; geostationary has **zero inclination**.

n2cab6322a5c.s: Following the stoppage of the last rubidium atomic clock on IRNSS-1F on 13 March 2026, which one of the following describes NavIC's status?
o: Five PNT-capable satellites remained, enough for a position fix
All seven satellites lost navigation capability
Only three PNT-capable satellites remained, while a PNT fix needs at least four
IRNSS-1F was replaced the same week by NVS-02
n2cab6322a5c.x: After IRNSS-1F's last clock stopped (3 days after its 10-year design life), only IRNSS-1B, 1I and NVS-01 remained PNT-capable: three, below the minimum four needed. 'Five' and 'all seven lost' are wrong counts, and NVS-02 never reached its circular orbit (Jan 2025).
xs: Only **3** PNT-capable satellites remained, while a PNT fix needs **at least 4** — option **(3)**.
The **3** are **IRNSS-1B, 1I and NVS-01**.
**NVS-02** never reached its circular orbit (**29 Jan 2025**), so it could not replace 1F.
xa: **IRNSS-1F's** last rubidium clock stopped on **13 March 2026** — **3** days after its **10-year** design life.
NavIC's design constellation is **7** satellites (**3 GEO + 4 GSO**).
NavIC has been operational since **2018**.

nda2a20c2a12.s: The first IRS satellite launched on PSLV from Sriharikota was:
nda2a20c2a12.x: IRS-P2 (1994) was the first on PSLV; IRS-1A, 1B and 1C were launched from Baikonur on Soviet rockets.
xa: IRS-1A flew on a Soviet **Vostok** launcher; **IRS-1B** in **1991**.
Precursors: experimental **Bhaskara-1 and Bhaskara-2**.
The IRS programme is the **largest civilian remote-sensing constellation** in the world.

n574e1b4b689.s: India's IRS programme, regarded as the world's largest civilian remote-sensing constellation, began in 1988 with:
n574e1b4b689.x: The IRS programme began with IRS-1A in 1988 and is regarded as the largest civilian remote-sensing constellation in the world.
xa: Precursors: **Bhaskara-1 and Bhaskara-2**.
**EOS** is the new naming for all EO satellites.
IRS data are processed at **NRSC, Hyderabad** and shared via **Bhuvan**.

n89e97d4baf3.s: EOS-05, launched by GSLV-F17 on 4 September 2026, was formerly known as:
n89e97d4baf3.x: EOS-05 was formerly GISAT-1A and became the first EO imager working from geosynchronous orbit; GISAT-1 was EOS-03.
xa: Mass **2,367 kg**; multispectral + hyperspectral imaging from visible to **long-wave IR**.
It images priority targets every **5 min** and all of India every **30 min**.
⚠ APPSC **2021** called **EOS-03** the geo-imaging satellite — it was lost at launch.

n20bd9d3148e.s: In NISAR, the radar provided by ISRO operates in the:
n20bd9d3148e.x: ISRO gives the S-band and NASA the L-band radar; NISAR was launched by GSLV-F16 on 30 July 2025.
xa: NISAR is the world's first **dual-frequency radar** satellite.
**EOS-09** (C-band SAR) was lost on **PSLV-C61** (May 2025).
DRDO's hyperspectral **EOS-N1 "Anvesha"** was lost on **PSLV-C62** (Jan 2026).

n38e3a973c94.s: GSAT-7 'Rukmini', the Indian Navy's communication satellite, was launched in 2013 by:
n38e3a973c94.x: GSAT-7 was launched by Ariane-5 from Kourou in 2013.
xa: **GSAT-10** (Ariane-5, **2012**) carries a **GAGAN** payload.
**INSAT-4CR** (**2,130 kg**, **GSLV-F04**, **2007**) was the heaviest satellite launched from India in its day.
**19** operational communication satellites; **10** transferred to **NSIL** in **2022**.

n811b59e0c55.s: Which satellite was fully funded by the Ministry of Earth Sciences and launched by GSLV-F14 on 17 February 2024?
n811b59e0c55.x: INSAT-3DS is a weather satellite fully funded by the Ministry of Earth Sciences and was launched by GSLV-F14 on 17 February 2024.
n811b59e0c55.tq: Match the funding ministry with the satellite’s weather function and launch date.
xs: **INSAT-3DS**, fully funded by **MoES**, was launched on **GSLV-F14** on **17 Feb 2024** — option **(2)**.
**GSAT-10** is a communication satellite with GAGAN; **Cartosat-3** maps; **EOS-03** was lost on GSLV-F10.
xa: **Bhuvan** flood-inundation maps and cyclone tracks use **RISAT and INSAT-3DS** data (Apr **2026**).
Earlier exclusive weather satellite: **Kalpana-1** (**2002**).
India's earlier geostationary "eyes" were the **INSAT-3D series** weather satellites.

n2484c4906d2.s: India's first experimental geostationary communication satellite, APPLE (1981), was launched by:
n2484c4906d2.x: APPLE was launched in 1981 on Ariane-1 from Kourou. SLV-3 launched Rohini (1980); the Space Shuttle Challenger carried INSAT-1B (1983); the Vostok launcher carried IRS-1A (1988).
xs: **APPLE** (**1981**) was launched by **Ariane-1 from Kourou** — option **(3)**.
**Space Shuttle Challenger** carried **INSAT-1B**; the **Soviet Vostok** launcher carried **IRS-1A** (**1988**).
xa: APPLE was India's **first experimental geostationary communication satellite**.
INSAT was **commissioned in 1983** with INSAT-1B.
IRS-1A, 1B, 1C flew from **Baikonur** on Soviet rockets.

n501adac5357.s: NVS-02, which did not reach its circular orbit, was launched on 29 January 2025 by:
n501adac5357.x: NVS-02 was launched by GSLV-F15 on 29 January 2025, the 100th launch from Sriharikota; a loose pyro connector was blamed for the failure.
xa: It was the **100th launch from Sriharikota**.
A review panel blamed a **pyro connector that came loose** (**26 Feb 2026**).
**NVS-01** (**2023**) was the first of the **2nd-generation** NVS series.

nb8f779b2b84.s: Which of the following applications is NOT associated with EOS-05?
nb8f779b2b84.x: EOS-05 is intended for applications such as floods, cyclones, forest fires, crops and security. Deep-sea submarine communication is not listed among its applications.
nb8f779b2b84.tq: Find the option outside the satellite's Earth-imaging application set.
xs: **Deep-sea submarine communication** is NOT an EOS-05 application — option **(2)**.
EOS-05 serves **floods, cyclones, forest fires, crops and security**.
xa: Multispectral + hyperspectral imaging (visible to **long-wave IR**) from GEO.
It images priority targets every **5 min** and all of India every **30 min**.

n6d33bbf0f60.s: Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) advisories mainly use data from the:
n6d33bbf0f60.x: Oceansat supports PFZ advisories; Resourcesat serves crops and watersheds, Cartosat mapping and RISAT SAR imaging.
xa: **Cartosat-3** gives ~**25 cm** imagery.
**EOS-04 (RISAT-1A)** SAR fed NRSC's **CROP** wheat estimate; **EOS-06 (Oceansat-3)** gives PFZ advisories.
**SARAL** is an **ISRO-CNES** altimetry satellite; **HySIS** is **hyperspectral**.

n1895ced8028.s: The KASTURI and Bharat Darshan heritage apps are powered by imagery from:
n1895ced8028.x: Cartosat-3 imagery (~25 cm resolution) powers KASTURI and Bharat Darshan; Cartosat-1 gave stereo images for 3D maps.
xa: Cartosat-3 flew on **PSLV-C47** with **13** US nanosatellites.
A Cartosat-2 series satellite (**714 kg**) went up on **PSLV-C37** in the record **104-satellite** launch.
Cartosat-3 also serves **Smart Cities**, **PM Gati Shakti** and border surveillance.

n5400010ccce.s: Cartosat-3 (2019), with about 25 cm resolution, was launched on:
n5400010ccce.x: Cartosat-3 flew on PSLV-C47 with 13 US nanosatellites; GSLV-F16 launched NISAR.
xa: Uses: **Smart Cities**, **PM Gati Shakti**, border surveillance.
Its imagery powers the **KASTURI** and **Bharat Darshan** heritage apps (Apr **2026**).
**Cartosat-1** (**2005**) gave stereo images for 3D maps.

n5166fa871a5.s: Which mission formed part of the record launch of 104 satellites into a 506 km sun-synchronous orbit on 15 February 2017?
n5166fa871a5.x: The Cartosat-2 series was launched by PSLV-C37 on 15 February 2017 and formed part of the record 104-satellite launch into a 506 km SSO. Its mass was 714 kg.
n5166fa871a5.tq: Combine the date, launch vehicle, orbit and record number to identify the mission.
xs: A **Cartosat-2 series** satellite on **PSLV-C37** (**15 Feb 2017**) was part of the record **104-satellite** launch into SSO at **506 km** — option **(1)**.
**EOS-03** was lost on **GSLV-F10**; **Cartosat-3** flew on **PSLV-C47** (**2019**); **INSAT-3DS** on **GSLV-F14** (**2024**).
xa: The Cartosat-2 series satellite weighed **714 kg**.
Cartosat-2 series: **sub-metre** resolution, used for **Smart Cities** and border management.
**PSLV** can put ~**1,600 kg** into **620 km SSO**.

naa4f552e0dd.s: EOS-03, also known as GISAT-1, was intended primarily for:
o: Near-real-time geo-imaging of floods and cyclones
Measuring ocean winds for cyclone forecasting
naa4f552e0dd.x: EOS-03, formerly GISAT-1, was designed for geo-imaging and near-real-time observation of events such as floods and cyclones.
naa4f552e0dd.tq: Separate the intended mission application from the later launch outcome.
xs: **EOS-03 (GISAT-1)** was meant for **near-real-time geo-imaging of floods and cyclones** from geostationary orbit — option **(2)** (APPSC **2021** PYQ).
It was **lost** on **GSLV-F10** in **Aug 2021** (cryogenic stage failure).
xa: **SCATSAT-1** measures ocean winds; **SARAL** carries the **Ka-band** altimeter.
EOS-05 images all of India every **30 min**.

n9734b8c29d7.s: INSAT-1B (1983), with which the INSAT system was commissioned, was launched by:
n9734b8c29d7.x: INSAT-1B went up on the US Space Shuttle Challenger; Ariane-1 carried APPLE (1981).
xa: INSAT bands: **C, extended-C, Ku, Ka, S**.
**INSAT-4CR** (**2,130 kg**, GSLV-F04, 2007) was the heaviest satellite launched from India in its day.
Disaster warning: **C-band** uplink from Chennai → **S-band** downlink to coastal receivers.

n30e3ae0f80c.x: Besides telecom, TV, meteorology, telemedicine and tele-education, INSAT supports COSPAS-SARSAT search and rescue.
xa: Disaster warning: **C-band** uplink from Chennai → **S-band** downlink to coastal **DWS** receivers.
**Kalpana-1** (**2002**) was the exclusive weather satellite.
Bands carried: **C, extended-C, Ku, Ka, S**.

n21c49baead1.s: GEO and GSO satellites share an orbital period of one sidereal day, which is about:
n21c49baead1.x: One sidereal day is about 23 h 56 min; only the geostationary case appears fixed in the sky.
xa: NavIC's **4** inclined satellites are in GSO.
MEO (**2,000-30,000 km**) is used for **GPS** navigation.
GEO is used for **communication and weather**.

n2338840b632.s: EOS-06 is the new name of:
n2338840b632.x: EOS-06 is Oceansat-3 (used for PFZ advisories); EOS-04 is RISAT-1A.
xa: EOS-06 supplies **PFZ** fishing advisories (Apr **2026**).
**CROP** = Comprehensive Remote Sensing Observation on Crop Progress — tracks sowing, growth, harvest.
**EOS-08** is a microsatellite on **SSLV-D3** (**2024**).

n4891e417df1.s: EOS-03 (GISAT-1), launched by GSLV-F10 in August 2021, failed because of a problem in the:
n4891e417df1.x: The EOS-03 mission failed due to a cryogenic-stage problem.
xa: It was meant for near-real-time **floods/cyclones** monitoring (APPSC **2021** PYQ).
Its successor **EOS-05 (GISAT-1A)** succeeded on **GSLV-F17** (**4 Sep 2026**).

n9a730fe831b.s: IRNSS/NavIC covers India and a region extending up to ____ beyond it.
n9a730fe831b.x: NavIC covers India plus 1,500 km, with 3 GEO + 4 GSO satellites, broadcasting in L5 and S bands.
xa: **IRNSS-1F**'s last rubidium clock stopped on **13 March 2026**; only **3** PNT-capable satellites remain.
A PNT fix needs at least **4** satellites.
**NVS-02** (**GSLV-F15**, 29 Jan 2025) never reached circular orbit; a loose **pyro connector** was blamed.

nd95c8f1354a.s: NRSC's CROP framework tracks crop sowing, growth and harvest using SAR data from:
nd95c8f1354a.x: CROP uses EOS-04 SAR data near real time; Bhuvan's flood maps and cyclone tracks use RISAT and INSAT-3DS data.
xa: CROP = **Comprehensive Remote Sensing Observation on Crop Progress**.
**Yuktdhara** portal helps gram panchayats plan **MGNREGA** assets.
National uses include **FASAL** crop forecasting and drought assessment.

ne8671bd30c3.s: India's first geosynchronous land-imaging satellite is:
ne8671bd30c3.x: EOS-05 is India's first geosynchronous land-imaging satellite; EOS-03 was lost at launch and the INSAT-3D series are weather satellites.
xa: ⚠ APPSC **2021** called EOS-03 the geo-imaging satellite — it never reached orbit.
EOS-05 was formerly **GISAT-1A**; EOS-03 was **GISAT-1**.
EOS-05 flew on **GSLV-F17** on **4 Sep 2026**.

n73c68c46b63.s: IIRS and CSSTEAP, which build capacity in space applications, are located in:
n73c68c46b63.x: Both IIRS and CSSTEAP are in Dehradun.
xa: EOS-05 was formerly **GISAT-1A** — first EO imager from geosynchronous orbit.
Data processing is centred at **NRSC, Hyderabad**.
AP's remote-sensing agency is **APSAC**.

ne3f40fe894a.s: QZSS, a regional satellite navigation system, belongs to:
ne3f40fe894a.x: QZSS (Japan) and NavIC (India) are regional; BeiDou is China's and GLONASS Russia's global system.
xa: **GPS** (USA, ~**30** satellites, MEO) and **Galileo** (European Union) are global.
India is the only developing country with its own independent regional system.
NavIC = **3 GEO + 4 GSO**, operational since **2018**.

n35a029485e6.s: India’s NavIC is distinctive among developing countries because it is:
o: the only system using both civilian and military signals
the only developing country operating a global navigation system
the only developing country with an independent regional navigation system
the first system jointly owned by India and the United States
n35a029485e6.x: India is described as the only developing country with its own independent regional navigation system.
n35a029485e6.tq: Identify the precise comparative claim rather than confusing regional and global status.
xs: India is the **only developing country with its own independent regional navigation system** — option **(3)**.
NavIC is **regional**, not global, and is India's own — not jointly owned with the USA.
xa: NavIC = **Navigation with Indian Constellation**; operational since **2018**.
Constellation: **7** satellites — **3 GEO + 4 GSO**.
The other regional system is Japan's **QZSS**.

n1fc87cb9eaa.s: Which of the following is NOT a national Earth-observation application listed for NRSC and related platforms?
o: Operation of civil aviation precision-landing systems
n1fc87cb9eaa.x: Groundwater mapping, FASAL crop forecasting and INFFRAS forest-fire monitoring are listed Earth-observation applications. Civil aviation precision landing is associated with GAGAN, not this list of NRSC applications.
n1fc87cb9eaa.tq: Separate the application domain of NRSC platforms from the aviation function of GAGAN.
xs: **Civil aviation precision landing** is NOT a listed EO application — option **(1)**; it is the job of **GAGAN**.
Listed uses include **FASAL** crop forecasting, forest-fire monitoring (**INFFRAS**) and **groundwater prospects** mapping.
xa: Others: **wastelands**, **wetlands inventory**, **snow and glaciers**, coastal zones, **drought assessment**.
**NUIS** and **SIS-DP** are also listed.
Data are processed at **NRSC, Hyderabad**.

n0eb0c35980d.s: In the Indian remote sensing data chain, processing is carried out at the nodal centre located at:
n0eb0c35980d.x: After collection and reception at a ground station, remote sensing data are processed at the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), Hyderabad, which functions as the nodal centre.
n0eb0c35980d.tq: Test the institutional location by distinguishing the processing centre from the launch and headquarters locations.
xs: Data are processed at the nodal **NRSC, Hyderabad** — option **(3)**.
Chain: **data collection** → **ground station** → **processing at NRSC** → supply to ministries, states, disaster agencies.
xa: Data are stored in **Indian data centres** and opened through **NRSC** and the **Bhuvan geoportal**.
Other ISRO platforms: **Bhoonidhi**, **MOSDAC**, **VEDAS** (**2026**).
NRSC released the **Landslide Atlas of India** (**2023**).

n7ece0891f63.s: Which platform is the ISRO geoportal through which Earth-observation data are made openly accessible?
n7ece0891f63.x: Bhuvan is the ISRO geoportal through which Earth-observation data are made openly accessible along with NRSC data services.
n7ece0891f63.tq: Identify the platform by matching the service with its specific function.
xs: **Bhuvan** is ISRO's **geoportal** for open EO data — option **(4)**.
**Yuktdhara** helps gram panchayats plan **MGNREGA** assets; **INFFRAS** is the forest-fire system; **SIS-DP** is a national use.
xa: Bhuvan gives **flood-inundation maps** and **cyclone tracks** from **RISAT and INSAT-3DS** data (Apr **2026**).
Other ISRO platforms: **Bhoonidhi**, **MOSDAC**, **VEDAS**.
Processing happens at **NRSC, Hyderabad**.

na689896badf.s: NRSC mapped the Joshimath subsidence using images from:
na689896badf.x: Joshimath subsidence was mapped with Cartosat-2S images; NRSC also released the Landslide Atlas of India (2023).
xa: **EOS-06 (Oceansat-3)** gives **PFZ** fishing advisories.
**NRSC, Hyderabad** is the nodal data processor; data open through **Bhuvan** geoportal.
Other ISRO platforms: **Bhoonidhi**, **MOSDAC**, **VEDAS**.

n80d5492a458.s: The coastal location of SDSC-SHAR enables it to contribute data for tracking cyclones over which water body for APSDMA?
n80d5492a458.x: SDSC-SHAR contributes data for Bay of Bengal cyclone tracking for APSDMA.
n80d5492a458.tq: Link the geographic location of the centre with the nearby cyclone-monitoring region.
xs: SDSC-SHAR contributes data for **Bay of Bengal** cyclone tracking for **APSDMA** — option **(2)**.
This follows from its **coastal location** at Sriharikota.
xa: SDSC-SHAR lies in **Tirupati district**, AP.
AP's own remote-sensing agency is **APSAC**.
**Bhuvan** cyclone tracks use **RISAT and INSAT-3DS** data.

ndb8a5683f99.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stage of a standard remote sensing system?
o: Interaction of radiation with the target
ndb8a5683f99.x: Remote sensing gathers information without physical contact, so physical sampling is not a stage; recording, interaction with the target and transmission/reception/processing are.
xa: Full chain: **energy source/illumination** → radiation through the atmosphere → interaction with target → recording → transmission/processing → **interpretation** → **application**.
Remote sensing works **without physical contact**, via **reflected or emitted** electromagnetic radiation.
⚠ "**Chemical**" resolution is another APPSC trap (**2025**) — it does not exist.

n1970791ad86.s: Which one of the following is NOT a type of resolution in remote sensing?
n1970791ad86.x: The four resolution types are spatial, spectral, temporal and radiometric. 'Chemical resolution' does not exist (APPSC 2025 trap). Radiometric, temporal and spectral are all genuine resolution types.
n1970791ad86.tq: Resolutions: spatial, spectral, temporal, radiometric - no 'chemical'.
xs: **Chemical resolution** does not exist — option **(3)** (APPSC **2025** trap).
The four real types are **spatial, spectral, temporal and radiometric**.
xa: ⚠ Another APPSC trap: "interaction of energy with **minimisation**" is not a remote-sensing component (**2022**).
Chemical identification is done by **hyperspectral** sensing — via spectral detail, not a separate resolution.
**Cartosat-3** gives ~**25 cm** spatial resolution.

n29c71115eb7.s: Compared with geosynchronous imagers, LEO imaging satellites generally provide:
o: The same detail and revisit frequency
Coarser detail with very frequent observation
n29c71115eb7.x: LEO gives finer detail but revisits periodically; geosynchronous imagers give coarser detail but observe priority targets very frequently.
xa: LEO spans **200-2,000 km**; GEO is **35,786 km** over the Equator.
EOS-05 was launched on **GSLV-F17** on **4 Sep 2026**.
India's earlier geostationary "eyes" were weather satellites (**INSAT-3D** series).

n846d7370a30.s: RISAT-1 carries a Synthetic Aperture Radar operating in the:
n846d7370a30.x: RISAT-1 (PSLV-C19) carries a C-band (5.35 GHz) SAR for day-night, all-weather imaging.
xa: **EOS-09 (RISAT-1B)**, a C-band SAR, was lost on **PSLV-C61** (**18 May 2025**).
RISAT belongs to the **strategic surveillance** domain with **Cartosat**, **EMISAT** and **EOS-N1**.
**PSLV-C48** also carried Israel's **Duchifat-3**.

n2cca9f61153.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about SpaDeX?
o: It made India the fourth country to dock in space, after the US, Russia and Japan.
It was launched by PSLV-C60 on 30 December 2024.
Its docking capability is needed for the Bharatiya Antariksh Station.
It did not set India's record for most satellites in one mission, which is PSLV-C37's 104.
n2cca9f61153.x: The three earlier docking nations were the US, Russia and China, not Japan.
xa: SpaDeX docked on **16 Jan 2025**, in a **474 km** orbit.
Heaviest payload: **BlueBird Block-2**, **6,100 kg** (**LVM3-M6**, 24 Dec 2025).
BlueBird Block-2 has a **223 m²** phased array for direct-to-smartphone broadband.

ne2af38f4913.s: The heaviest payload launched by an Indian rocket, BlueBird Block-2 (6,100 kg), was launched on 24 December 2025 by:
ne2af38f4913.x: LVM3-M6 launched the 6,100 kg BlueBird Block-2 (223 sq m phased array, direct-to-smartphone broadband) on 24 Dec 2025. PSLV-C60 launched SpaDeX, GSLV-F17 launched EOS-05, and SSLV is a small-satellite launcher.
xs: **BlueBird Block-2** (**6,100 kg**) flew on **LVM3-M6** on **24 Dec 2025** — option **(3)**.
**PSLV-C60** launched **SpaDeX**; **GSLV-F17** launched **EOS-05**.
xa: BlueBird Block-2 has a **223 m²** phased array for **direct-to-smartphone broadband**.
Earlier reports said **6,500 kg** and **64 m²**; flown figures are **6,100 kg** and **223 m²**.
Most-satellites record: **PSLV-C37**, **104** satellites (**2017**).

n4a9706e961f.s: Kalpana-1, India's first exclusive meteorological satellite, was launched in 2002 by:
n4a9706e961f.x: Kalpana-1 was India's first exclusive meteorological satellite, launched by PSLV in 2002.
xa: The other weather satellite listed is **INSAT-3DS** (**GSLV-F14**, **2024**, **MoES**).
Science missions: **XPoSat**, **Aditya-L1**.
Aditya-L1 flew on **PSLV-C57** (**2023**).

n32efae660eb.s: The GSLV-F17/EOS-05 mission ended a launch pause of about ____ that followed two PSLV failures.
n32efae660eb.x: GSLV-F17/EOS-05 ended an eight-month pause that followed two PSLV failures.
xa: EOS-05 is a geo-platform "eye in the sky" for **agriculture, environment, disasters**.
An **external team** joined the PSLV failure probe (**3 Feb 2026**).

ne0ed842494a.s: POEM platforms are best described as:
o: Spent PS4 stages used as orbital laboratories
Reusable crew capsules for ISS missions
Foreign customer satellites launched by PSLV
ne0ed842494a.x: POEM platforms use the spent PS4 stage as an orbital laboratory.
ne0ed842494a.tq: Interpret the platform’s function from its structural origin and orbital use.
xs: POEM platforms are **spent PS4 stages used as orbital labs** — option **(2)**.
They are not ground stations, crew capsules or foreign customer satellites.
xa: Re-entry experiments: **SRE-1** (**PSLV-C7**, **2007**) and **CARE** (**LVM3**, **2014**).
PSLV-C62 planned a **PS4 de-boost**.

n8479146edc4.s: Proba-3 was launched by PSLV-C59 in December 2024 for which agency?
n8479146edc4.x: Proba-3 was an ESA satellite mission launched by PSLV-C59 in December 2024.
n8479146edc4.tq: Distinguish the European agency from the agencies involved in other joint missions.
xs: **Proba-3** was an **ESA** mission launched by **PSLV-C59** (Dec **2024**) — option **(3)**.
**Duchifat-3** was Israel's; **OneWeb** was the UK's.
xa: OneWeb's **72** satellites flew on **LVM3** in **2** missions.
The first dedicated commercial LVM3 flight carried **36** OneWeb satellites (**2022**).
ISRO has launched **433** foreign satellites of **34+** countries.

ne6b2571c02c.s: ISRO has launched how many foreign satellites from more than 34 countries?
ne6b2571c02c.x: ISRO has launched 433 foreign satellites from over 34 countries, more than half from the US.
xa: **NSIL**: **141** satellites incl. **138 international** (Jul **2026**).
**OneWeb** (UK): **72** satellites on **LVM3** in **2** missions.
**Proba-3** (ESA) flew on **PSLV-C59** (Dec **2024**).

nccdc5d2809f.s: GSAT-7B has been proposed for the:
nccdc5d2809f.x: GSAT-7B is proposed for the Army; GSAT-7 serves the Navy and GSAT-7A the IAF.
xa: Strategic surveillance: **RISAT**, **Cartosat**, **EMISAT** (electronic intelligence), **EOS-N1**.
India has **19** operational communication satellites; **10** moved to **NSIL** in **2022**.
Weather domain: **INSAT-3DS**, **Kalpana-1**.

n6bb5f14358c.s: The 1980 SLV-3/Rohini launch made India the ____ nation to launch a satellite indigenously.
n6bb5f14358c.x: SLV-3/Rohini made India the sixth such nation; Aryabhata (1975) had flown on a Soviet rocket.
xa: Space Shuttle's first flight: **Columbia, April 1981 (STS-1)**.
⚠ **Challenger** lost in **1986**; **Columbia** lost in **2003** (Kalpana Chawla).
First satellite repaired in orbit: **Solar Maximum Mission**, by **Challenger** crew, **April 1984**.

n0ba64feeecf.x: Mangalyaan flew on PSLV-C25; Chandrayaan-1 used PSLV-C11, AstroSat PSLV-C30 and Chandrayaan-2 GSLV Mk III-M1.
xa: **Chandrayaan-3** flew on **LVM3-M4** (**14 July 2023**).
⚠ Trap: **GSLV-F14/INSAT-3DS** was **2024**, not 2022.

n52a9f9fb8f0.x: Chandrayaan-3 launched on 14 July 2023, before Aditya-L1 (2 Sep 2023), XPoSat (1 Jan 2024) and SpaDeX (30 Dec 2024). (Sequence not targeted; one-liner as asked.)
xa: APPSC **2023** match order: Ch-2 **Jul 2019** → Ch-3 **Jul 2023** → Aditya-L1 **Sep 2023** → SpaDeX **Dec 2024**.
SpaDeX docked on **16 Jan 2025** → India **4th** to dock in space.
⚠ A PYQ wrongly dated XPoSat **May 2023**.

n9f86adf17bc.s: The pair GSLV-F14 and INSAT-3DS is associated with which year?
n9f86adf17bc.x: GSLV-F14 launched INSAT-3DS in February 2024. Therefore, the pairing with 2022 is incorrect.
n9f86adf17bc.tq: Watch for the famous-year trap in a mission and vehicle combination.
xs: **GSLV-F14/INSAT-3DS** belongs to **2024** (Feb **2024**) — option **(3)**.
⚠ "GSLV-F14/INSAT-3DS – **2022**" is the known **incorrect** PYQ pair.
xa: Another PYQ pair: **PSLV-C56/DS-SAR** — **July 2023**.
**XPoSat** also flew in **2024** (**1 Jan**, **PSLV-C58**).
**Aditya-L1** flew on **PSLV-C57** in **2023**.

n033f9bb2cfc.s: Which one of the following is NOT a payload of Chandrayaan-1?
n033f9bb2cfc.x: TMC, Mini-SAR and CIXS were among the Chandrayaan-1 payloads. Lyman Alpha Photometer was one of Mangalyaan’s five payloads.
n033f9bb2cfc.tq: Identify the instrument that belongs to the neighbouring Mars mission.
xs: **Lyman Alpha Photometer** is NOT a Chandrayaan-1 payload — option **(3)**; it is one of **Mangalyaan's 5** payloads.
**Mini-SAR**, **CIXS** and **TMC** are Chandrayaan-1 payloads.
xa: Other Ch-1 payloads: **HySI, LLRI, HEX, SIR-2, SARA, RADOM** and NASA's **M3**.
MOM's other payloads: **Methane Sensor for Mars**, **MENCA**, **Mars Colour Camera**, **TIS**.
Ch-1 confirmed **water molecules** on the Moon.

ncb3cdcd41fd.s: India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory (2015, PSLV-C30) is:
ncb3cdcd41fd.x: AstroSat observes in visible, ultraviolet and X-ray bands; XPoSat flew on PSLV-C58 on 1 Jan 2024.
xa: XPoSat = India's **first polarimetry mission**, world's **second** after NASA's **IXPE**.
XPoSat partner: **Raman Research Institute (RRI), Bengaluru**.
⚠ A PYQ wrongly dated XPoSat **May 2023**.

n46b154cfa07.s: The first soft landing on the far side of the Moon (2019) was made by:
n46b154cfa07.x: Chang'e-4 made the first far-side soft landing with rover Yutu-2; Chang'e-3 (2013) was the first soft landing since 1976 and Chang'e-6 a far-side sample return.
xa: The Chang'e series belongs to **China (CNSA)**.
China soft-landed on the Moon before India — India was **4th** (after US, Russia, China).
China also runs **SuperView** commercial EO satellites.

nfc03c929bc9.s: India signed the Artemis Accords in:
nfc03c929bc9.x: India signed the Artemis Accords in 2023; Artemis I (2022) was an uncrewed SLS-Orion test.
xa: **Artemis II (2026)** flew the first crewed trip around the Moon in 50+ years.
**Artemis III** → crewed test flight in Earth orbit in **2027**.
**Europa Clipper** (Oct 2024) targets Jupiter's moon **Europa**.

n0218622aab5.s: Chandrayaan-1, 2 and 3, Mangalyaan, AstroSat, Aditya-L1 and XPoSat were all launched from which facility?
o: Satish Dhawan Space Centre SHAR, Sriharikota
n0218622aab5.x: The missions were launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre SHAR at Sriharikota, located in Tirupati district of Andhra Pradesh.
n0218622aab5.tq: Identify the launch facility by distinguishing it from satellite centres and missile-test facilities.
xs: All the missions were launched from **Satish Dhawan Space Centre SHAR, Sriharikota** — option **(1)**.
SDSC SHAR is in **Tirupati district, AP**.
xa: **Aditya-L1** (**PSLV-C57**) and **Chandrayaan-3** (**LVM3**) both flew from Sriharikota.
India is the **4th** country to dock in space (**SpaDeX**, **16 Jan 2025**).
India targets **50 launches a year**.
n0218622aab5.fixed: stem referred to 'this section'; oddly worded

nb339805a5f7.s: The minimum speed required for an object to escape the gravitational field of Earth is approximately:
nb339805a5f7.x: Earth’s escape velocity is approximately 11.2 km/s.
nb339805a5f7.tq: Check the decimal place carefully in a standard numerical value.
xs: Earth's escape velocity is **11.2 km/s** — option **(2)**.
It is the **minimum speed** to escape a body's gravity.
xa: **Soft landing** limits for Ch-3: vertical **≤ 2 m/s**, horizontal ≤ **0.5 m/s**, slope ≤ **12 degrees**.
**Hohmann transfer**: fuel-efficient elliptical orbit with **two engine burns**; **MOM** used it.
**Lagrange points**: **five** (L1-L5).

n1f0c1757fe1.s: Chandrayaan-1 carried how many scientific instruments, including NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper?
n1f0c1757fe1.x: Chandrayaan-1 (orbiter + Moon Impact Probe) carried 11 instruments and confirmed water molecules on the lunar surface.
xa: Instruments came from **India, USA, UK, Germany, Sweden, Bulgaria**; mass **1,380 kg**.
It made **3,400+ orbits**; contact lost **29 Aug 2009** after **312 days**.
Launched **22 Oct 2008** on **PSLV-C11**.

na83558cb08e.s: India became the fourth nation to place its flag on the Moon through an impact probe. Which sequence lists the nations preceding India in this achievement?
na83558cb08e.x: India was the fourth nation to place its flag on the Moon through an impact probe, after the USSR, the USA and Japan.
na83558cb08e.tq: Use the stated rank and identify the preceding countries without substituting later lunar powers.
xs: India was **4th** to place its flag on the Moon via an impact probe, after the **USSR, USA and Japan** — option **(1)**.
Chandrayaan-1's **MIP** hit the lunar south polar region on **14 Nov 2008** at **Jawahar Point**.
xa: ⚠ Site names: **Jawahar Point** = Ch-1 MIP; **Tiranga point** = Ch-2 crash; **Shiv Shakti** = Ch-3 landing.
First probe to hit the Moon: **Luna 2** (USSR, **1959**).
NASA's **LCROSS** (**2009**) impacted a polar crater to find water.

n1ae96a53876.s: The SHAPE payload of Chandrayaan-3 was carried by the:
n1ae96a53876.x: The Propulsion Module carried the SHAPE payload, which studies Earth from lunar orbit.
