n1ae96a53876.tq: Ask who carried the payload rather than what the payload studies.
xs: **SHAPE** was carried by the **Propulsion Module** — option **(4)**; it studies **Earth from lunar orbit**.
The Propulsion Module carried the lander-rover to a **100 km** lunar orbit.
xa: Lander payloads: **ChaSTE, ILSA, RAMBHA-LP, LRA (NASA)**.
Rover payloads: **APXS** and **LIBS**.
The **MIP** belonged to **Chandrayaan-1**, not Ch-3.

nc5e49d7b070.x: Chandrayaan-3 flew on LVM3-M4 and soft-landed on 23 Aug 2023; PSLV-C57 launched Aditya-L1.
xa: Launch date: **14 July 2023** from **SDSC SHAR**.
Total mass **3,900 kg** (lander **1,752 kg** incl. the **26 kg** rover).
Mission life: **one lunar day (~14 Earth days)**.

n80335193f34.s: The impact site of Chandrayaan-1's Moon Impact Probe is called:
n80335193f34.x: Jawahar Point is the MIP impact site; Tiranga Point is where Chandrayaan-2's Vikram crashed and Shiv Shakti Point Chandrayaan-3's landing site.
xa: Shiv Shakti lies ~**600 km** from the South Pole, between craters **Manzinus C** and **Simpelius N**.
**23 August** is **National Space Day**.
MIP hit the Moon on **14 Nov 2008**.

n25246a990b4.s: India observes National Space Day on:
n25246a990b4.x: National Space Day (23 August) marks Chandrayaan-3's soft landing on 23 Aug 2023.
xa: India was the **1st** to land **near the lunar south pole**.
Landing site: **Shiv Shakti point**, about **600 km** from the South Pole.
**Pragyan** confirmed **sulphur** near the south pole (APPSC 2023).

n8a42724a160.s: Which element did Chandrayaan-3's Pragyan rover confirm near the lunar south pole?
n8a42724a160.x: Pragyan confirmed sulphur near the south pole; its LIBS also detected Al, Ca, Fe, Cr, Ti, Mn, Si and O. Helium-3, uranium and nitrogen are not among the elements Pragyan confirmed.
xs: **Pragyan** confirmed **sulphur** near the lunar south pole — option **(2)** (APPSC **2023**).
Its **LIBS** also detected **Al, Ca, Fe, Cr, Ti, Mn, Si and O**.
xa: **APXS** found Shiv Shakti soil **rich in iron + magnesium**, **poor in aluminium**.
The soil is chemically similar to lunar meteorite **ALHA 81005** (Jun **2026**).
Pragyan's rover mass: **26 kg**.
n8a42724a160.fixed: stem cited 'asked in APPSC 2023'; unexam-like wording (y70c33fea3d0)

n6245be4affa.s: A Hohmann transfer is best described as:
o: A controlled low-speed touchdown on a planetary surface
A point of gravitational balance in a two-body system
A direct vertical launch requiring continuous engine thrust
A fuel-efficient transfer between two orbits using an elliptical orbit and two engine burns
n6245be4affa.x: A Hohmann transfer uses an elliptical transfer orbit and two engine burns to move between two orbits efficiently. Mangalyaan used this method to reach Mars.
n6245be4affa.tq: Match the operational description with the correct orbital-mechanics term.
xs: A **Hohmann transfer** is a **fuel-efficient elliptical orbit between two orbits** using **two engine burns** — option **(4)**.
**Controlled low-speed touchdown** is a **soft landing**; a **balance point** is a **Lagrange point**.
xa: **Mangalyaan (MOM)** used a Hohmann transfer to reach Mars.
MOM entered Mars orbit on **24 September 2014** — on the **first attempt**.
Escape velocity: **11.2 km/s**.

n19ff21b468f.s: India’s first interplanetary mission, launched on PSLV-C25, was designated as which of the following?
n19ff21b468f.x: Mangalyaan was India’s first interplanetary mission and was also known as the Mars Orbiter Mission. It was launched on PSLV-C25.
n19ff21b468f.tq: Identify the alternate official name of the mission from its launch vehicle association.
xs: India's first interplanetary mission is the **Mars Orbiter Mission** (Mangalyaan) — option **(3)**.
Launched on **5 Nov 2013** by **PSLV-C25**.
**AstroSat** is a space observatory; **Chandrayaan-1** went to the Moon; **Aditya-L1** studies the Sun.
xa: MOM entered Mars orbit on **24 September 2014**, on its **maiden attempt**.
ISRO became the **4th space agency** to orbit Mars.
Designed for **6 months**, it worked about **8 years**.

n3343073b144.s: Contact with Mangalyaan, designed for six months, was lost in:
n3343073b144.x: Mangalyaan entered Mars orbit on 24 Sep 2014 and worked about eight years until contact was lost in 2022.
xa: Launch: **5 Nov 2013**, **PSLV-C25**.
It used a **Hohmann transfer** to reach Mars.
It was the **lowest-cost** Mars mission.

ne3728b8984e.s: Through the Mars Orbiter Mission, India became ____ to place a spacecraft in Mars orbit.
o: The first country in the world
ne3728b8984e.x: Through Mangalyaan (the Mars Orbiter Mission), India became the first Asian nation to place a spacecraft in Mars orbit.
xa: MOM: launched **2013** on **PSLV-C25**; orbit insertion **24 September 2014**.
ISRO was the **4th space agency** to orbit Mars (after **NASA, Roscosmos, ESA**).
Designed for **6 months**, it worked about **8 years**.

n56372d73003.s: The first satellite repaired in orbit was which of the following?
n56372d73003.x: NASA’s Solar Maximum Mission satellite was repaired by the crew of Space Shuttle Challenger in April 1984 during mission STS-41C.
n56372d73003.tq: Directly identify the unique satellite associated with the first in-orbit repair.
xs: NASA's **Solar Maximum Mission** was the **first satellite repaired in orbit** — option **(1)**.
It was repaired by the **Challenger** crew in **April 1984** (**STS-41C**).
**Aryabhata** (**1975**) was India's first satellite and **Rohini** (**1980**) went up on **SLV-3** — neither was repaired in orbit.
xa: First Shuttle flight: **Columbia, April 1981 (STS-1)**.
**Challenger** itself was lost in **1986**.
Programme ended in **2011** with **Atlantis**.

n515673b8d68.s: The Sun-Earth L1 point, where Aditya-L1 is in a halo orbit, is about how far from Earth?
n515673b8d68.x: L1 is about 1.5 million km from Earth; Aditya-L1 launched on 2 Sep 2023 (PSLV-C57).
xa: Halo-orbit insertion: **6 January 2024** (APPSC **2022** key).
L1 gives a **continuous view of the Sun**, with no occultation/eclipse.
It is India's **first space-based solar observatory**.

ne2f70082451.s: Which Aditya-L1 payload images the solar corona?
ne2f70082451.x: VELC images the corona; ASPEX and PAPA are in-situ payloads studying solar-wind particles. Aditya-L1 has 7 payloads (4 remote sensing, 3 in-situ).
xa: ASPEX: solar-wind **protons** and heavier ions; PAPA: solar-wind **electrons** and heavier ions.
Remote sensing: **VELC, SUIT, SoLEXS, HEL1OS**.
⚠ **VELC** = IIA (corona); **SUIT** = IUCAA (photosphere, chromosphere).

n61f1f7a810c.s: Which of the following Aditya-L1 payloads was built by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics?
n61f1f7a810c.x: The Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) was built by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.
n61f1f7a810c.tq: Test the institution–payload association rather than the scientific function alone.
xs: **VELC** (Visible Emission Line Coronagraph) was built by the **Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA)** — option **(3)**.
**SUIT** was built by **IUCAA**; **ASPEX** and **PAPA** are in-situ solar-wind payloads.
xa: VELC does **corona imaging and spectroscopy**.
It recorded the **first-ever spectroscopic observations of CMEs in visible wavelengths** (**2025**, IIA with NASA).
⚠ **VELC** = IIA; **SUIT** = IUCAA.

n2007ceb5fdd.s: XPoSat is the world's second X-ray polarimetry mission, after:
n2007ceb5fdd.x: XPoSat is India's first and the world's second X-ray polarimetry mission after NASA's IXPE.
xa: Launched **1 Jan 2024** on **PSLV-C58**.
Payloads: **POLIX** (by **RRI**) and **XSPECT** (by **URSC**).
⚠ A PYQ wrongly dated it **May 2023**.

n739bd645d3a.s: The POLIX payload of XPoSat was developed by
o: Inter-University Centre for Astronomy and Astrophysics
n739bd645d3a.x: POLIX was developed by the Raman Research Institute (RRI), Bengaluru.
n739bd645d3a.tq: Use the payload–institution association and distinguish it from AstroSat's partner institutions.
xs: **POLIX** was built by the **Raman Research Institute (RRI), Bengaluru** — option **(3)**.
The other XPoSat payload, **XSPECT**, was built by **URSC** (U. R. Rao Space Centre).
**IUCAA** built Aditya-L1's **SUIT**; **IIA** built **VELC**.
xa: XPoSat launched on **1 Jan 2024** (**PSLV-C58**).
It is the world's **second** X-ray polarimetry mission after **IXPE**.
RRI is also among **AstroSat's** partner institutions.

n8f7136287df.s: The Venus Orbiter Mission, also known as Shukrayaan, is intended to enter orbit around
n8f7136287df.x: Shukrayaan, or the Venus Orbiter Mission, targets Venus. It is not a mission to Saturn.
n8f7136287df.tq: Use the mission name and target association to avoid the Venus–Saturn substitution trap.
xs: The **Venus Orbiter Mission (Shukrayaan)** targets **Venus** orbit — option **(1)**.
It does **not** target Saturn — APPSC-G1 **2022** keyed "none of the above" for that option.
xa: Cost: **₹1,236 crore**, approved by the **Union Cabinet**.
**ESA** is exploring complementary cooperation (**10 Sep 2026**).
Venus and Mars missions are part of the **Space Vision 2047** roadmap.

n92e06408af9.s: Chandrayaan-4, with a landing site near Mons Mouton, is planned as a:
o: Joint lunar polar mission with JAXA
n92e06408af9.x: Chandrayaan-4 is a sample-return mission (regolith and ice); the JAXA partnership is Chandrayaan-5/LUPEX.
xa: Chandrayaan-4's planned timeline is **2027**.
⚠ **Chandrayaan-4** = sample return (ISRO); **Chandrayaan-5 / LUPEX** = with JAXA (water ice).
ISRO will focus on **Chandrayaan-4, BAS, Venus and Mars** missions.

n3ff657e30ba.s: Under India's Space Vision 2047, an Indian is to be placed on the Moon by:
n3ff657e30ba.x: The vision envisages the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and an Indian on the Moon by 2040.
xa: The roadmap also includes a **Venus mission** and **Mars again**.
**SpaDeX** docking (**16 Jan 2025**) is a step towards BAS.
India targets **50 launches a year** (**25 Aug 2026**).

nea73e51aec2.s: Gaganyaan, India's first human spaceflight programme, was approved in:
nea73e51aec2.x: Gaganyaan was approved in 2018; its Crew Module is to splash down in Indian sea waters.
xa: The aim is to demonstrate human spaceflight to **LEO**.
Gaganyaan would make India the **4th** nation with its own crewed launch, after **USSR/Russia** (**1961**), **USA** and **China**.
**Gagarin** flew the first crewed launch on **Vostok** in **1961**.

n08c07c7dc77.s: Russia's Soyuz and China's Shenzhou spacecraft both use a three-module configuration consisting of:
n08c07c7dc77.x: Both Soyuz and Shenzhou use a three-module configuration: orbital, descent and service modules.
xa: ⚠ Trap: Gaganyaan = **two** parts; Soyuz/Shenzhou = **three** modules.
The **USSR/Russia** made the first own crewed launch (**Gagarin**, **Vostok**, **1961**); **USA** and **China** followed.
China's own space station is **Tiangong** (**Tianhe** core + **Wentian** + **Mengtian**).

n99f9fb2fb30.s: Which one of the following is the human-rated launch vehicle for the Gaganyaan mission?
n99f9fb2fb30.x: Gaganyaan will use the human-rated LVM3, also referred to as HLVM3 or HRLV. The earlier GSLV Mk-III structures were redesigned for human rating.
n99f9fb2fb30.tq: Apply the wrong-launcher trap by separating vehicle generations and variants.
xs: Gaganyaan will fly on the **Human-rated LVM3 (HLVM3 / HRLV)** from **Sriharikota** — option **(1)**.
**GSLV Mk-III** structures were redesigned for **human rating** to create it.
xa: The **Vikas** engine for the human-rated **L110** stage was qualified in **3 tests** (**730 s** total).
**LVM3** has had **6 flights**; **LVM3-M6** carried the **6,100 kg** BlueBird Block-2 — its heaviest payload.
Flight sequence: uncrewed **G1 → G2 → G3**, then crewed **H1**.

ndaec8f59d17.s: The principal purpose of India’s analogue space mission is to:
o: Simulate life in an interplanetary habitat
Develop a replacement for the SSLV
Test satellite communication with the ISS
ndaec8f59d17.x: The mission simulates life in an interplanetary habitat and generates data for astronaut selection and training, ECLSS design, work-rest schedules and ground-crew protocols.
ndaec8f59d17.tq: Identify the underlying operational purpose rather than a single secondary outcome.
xs: The analogue mission's purpose is to **simulate life in an interplanetary habitat** — option **(2)**.
Its data refine astronaut selection/training, crew-module **ECLSS** design, **work-rest schedules** and ground-crew protocols.
xa: It reduces reliance on **foreign agencies**.
**HOPE** at **Tso Kar** is a Mars-like habitat station.
**MITRA** is a crew behavioural study with the IAF's **IAM**.

na1f50a4870b.s: Which of the following countries already had its own crewed space-launch capability before Gaganyaan?
na1f50a4870b.x: Only the USSR/Russia, the USA and China have their own crewed launch capability; Gaganyaan would make India the fourth.
xa: Gaganyaan aims at a **crew of 3** to **400 km LEO** for **3 days**.
⚠ Separately, **SpaDeX** (**16 Jan 2025**) made India the **4th** nation to **dock** in space.
Gaganyaan was approved in **2018**.

n91c391f7724.s: In the Gaganyaan flight sequence, the first crewed flight is designated:
n91c391f7724.x: Uncrewed G1, G2 and G3 come first, then crewed H1, now targeted for Q1 2027.
xa: Launch vehicle: **Human-rated LVM3 (HLVM3)** from Sriharikota.
Vikas engine for the human-rated **L110** stage was qualified in **3 tests (730 s)**.
⚠ Repeated slippage (**2021 → 2023 → 2027**): quote any date with the date of the statement.

nd9d6b23fc36.s: What did the TV-D1 mission demonstrate?
o: Only the docking of two spacecraft in orbit
Deployment of the Bharatiya Antariksh Station
In-flight crew escape at Mach 1.2, crew-module separation and sea recovery
nd9d6b23fc36.x: TV-D1 demonstrated an in-flight abort of the Crew Escape System at Mach 1.2, followed by crew-module separation and sea recovery.
nd9d6b23fc36.tq: Identify the mission by its demonstrated safety sequence and speed.
xs: **TV-D1** demonstrated **in-flight crew escape at Mach 1.2**, **crew-module separation and sea recovery** — option **(3)**.
Docking was shown by **SpaDeX** (**16 Jan 2025**), not TV-D1; **BAS** is not yet deployed (first module **2028**).
xa: TV-D1 flew on **18 Oct 2023**; TV-D1 and all Gaganyaan launches are at **Sriharikota (AP)**.
**TV-D2** is the next abort test, still to come.
**Indian on the Moon by 2040** is only a Space Vision **2047** goal.

nb067ff9cbf2.s: Which Gaganyaan-related test was for crew-module re-entry?
nb067ff9cbf2.x: CARE tested re-entry; IADT-01 and IADT-02 were air-drop tests and SOLVE a solid-motor test.
xa: SOLVE's solid motor is derived from **PSLV strap-ons**.
IADT-02 was recovered with the **Navy**.
July **2026** qualification tests: **Crew Module Uprighting System** (cold gas), apex cover separation.

n1bf963f03f9.s: Shubhanshu Shukla's stay aboard the ISS during Axiom-4 (2025) lasted about:
n1bf963f03f9.x: Shukla's ISS stay was 18 days; Axiom-4 launched on 25 June 2025 on a SpaceX Dragon/Falcon 9.
xa: Shukla = **first Indian aboard the ISS** and **second Indian in space**, after **Rakesh Sharma**.
Crew: **Peggy Whitson** (commander), Shukla (pilot), Uznanski (Poland), Kapu (Hungary).
**7 microgravity experiments** by Indian institutions, coordinated under **HSFC**.

n6380f0c335d.s: The Axiom-4 crew in which Shubhanshu Shukla flew as pilot was commanded by:
n6380f0c335d.x: Peggy Whitson commanded Axiom-4; Shukla became the first Indian aboard the ISS and the second Indian in space.
xa: Ax-4 launched **25 June 2025** on **SpaceX Dragon** (**Falcon 9**).
Other crew: **Slawosz Uznanski** (Poland), **Tibor Kapu** (Hungary).
Shukla's ISS stay was **18 days**.

nd41761e3b55.s: The Third Launch Pad at Sriharikota was approved by the Union Cabinet in:
nd41761e3b55.x: It was approved in January 2025 at about Rs 4,000 crore to serve the NGLV and future human spaceflight.
xa: NGLV: ~**90 m** tall, ~**1,000 t** lift-off mass.
**Dhanush** at Sriharikota is India's **first private launch pad**, by **Agnikul Cosmos**.
SSLV complex foundation stone: **27 August 2025**.

nb831ad437e7.s: Dhanush, India's first private launch pad at Sriharikota, was built by:
nb831ad437e7.x: Agnikul Cosmos built Dhanush with its own mission control centre.
xa: Dhanush has its own **mission control centre**; first launch from it in **2024**.
The **Third Launch Pad** at Sriharikota serves the **NGLV**.
India's **first analogue space mission** was at **Leh, Ladakh**, in **November 2024**.

n7281300ebcf.s: The Human Space Flight Centre (HSFC), a new ISRO vertical supporting Gaganyaan, is based in:
n7281300ebcf.x: HSFC is in Bengaluru, as is the IAF's Institute of Aerospace Medicine; DRDO contributes parachutes, life support and crew recovery.
xa: **ESA** adds ground stations under a **Technical Implementing Plan** (**10 Sep 2026**).
IAM does crew selection, aeromedical training and **MITRA**.
ISRO Human Spaceflight Expo: **Jawaharlal Nehru Planetarium, Bengaluru**, **22-24 July 2022**.

o: Space motion sickness in the first days
Optic disc swelling and vision changes
n2b700f405c8.x: SANS causes optic disc swelling and vision changes; space motion sickness is Space Adaptation Syndrome.
xa: SANS = **Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome**.
**Radiation exposure** raises **cancer and cataract** risk.
Bone loss: **1-1.5%** per month without load.

n2a84f6958c6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about microgravity and space medicine?
o: Space medicine is studied only through actual spaceflight, not ground analogues.
Radiation exposure increases the risk of cancer and cataracts.
Daily resistance and treadmill exercise are used as countermeasures.
Diet and medication are part of the countermeasure strategy.
n2a84f6958c6.x: Space medicine is also studied through ground analogues such as Leh and HOPE.
xa: **Muscle atrophy** weakens postural muscles; Ax-4 tested **muscle regeneration**.
Bone loss: **1-1.5%** per month without load.
**Fluid shift**: "puffy face, bird legs".

n17ea186d6e9.s: The Gaganyaan test flight TV-D1 was conducted at:
n17ea186d6e9.x: TV-D1, both air-drop tests, all Gaganyaan launches and the proposed Third Launch Pad are at Sriharikota.
xa: **IADT-01** was conducted at **SDSC-SHAR**.
TLP: Cabinet approval **January 2025**, about **₹4,000 crore**, for **NGLV** and human spaceflight.
India's **first private launch pad**, **Dhanush** (Agnikul Cosmos), is also at Sriharikota.

n95c8c8d0949.s: IADT-01, the first Integrated Air Drop Test, was conducted at:
n95c8c8d0949.x: IADT-01 was conducted at SDSC-SHAR; IADT-02 was associated with April 2026.
xa: **IADT-01** (**24 Aug 2025**): **4.8-tonne** dummy module dropped from **3 km** by IAF **Chinook**.
**IADT-02** (**10 Apr 2026**): **5.7-tonne** module, **10 parachutes of 4 types**, recovered with the Navy.
**ESA** agreed tracking support (**10 Sep 2026**).

ne9d85fa42f0.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of the four Gaganyatris named in February 2024?
o: Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair, Pankaj M. Sinha, Angad Pratap and Shubhanshu Shukla
Ajit Krishnan, Pankaj M. Sinha, Angad Pratap and Shubhanshu Shukla
Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair, Ajit Krishnan, Pankaj M. Sinha and Angad Pratap
Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair, Ajit Krishnan, Angad Pratap and Shubhanshu Shukla
ne9d85fa42f0.x: The four Gaganyatris named in February 2024 were Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair, Ajit Krishnan, Angad Pratap and Shubhanshu Shukla. Pankaj M. Sinha is not one of them.
ne9d85fa42f0.tq: Eliminate the option containing the non-member of the named group.
xs: The four **Gaganyatris** are **Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair, Ajit Krishnan, Angad Pratap and Shubhanshu Shukla** — option **(4)**.
**Pankaj M. Sinha** is not a Gaganyatri, which rules out options (1), (2) and (3).
xa: They were named in **February 2024**; all are **Indian Air Force test pilots**.
Nair, Krishnan and Pratap were **Group Captains**; Shukla was a **Wing Commander** (later Group Captain).
PYQ: **APPSC-G1 2024** key: I, II, IV, V.

nef5d4c53cc3.s: Rakesh Sharma became the first Indian in space aboard:
nef5d4c53cc3.x: Rakesh Sharma was the first Indian in space and flew aboard Soyuz T-11 in April 1984, under the USSR programme.
nef5d4c53cc3.tq: Combine the person, spacecraft and date while rejecting one-element swaps.
xs: **Rakesh Sharma** flew aboard Soviet **Soyuz T-11** in **April 1984** — option **(1)**.
He flew on **2 Apr 1984** to **Salyut-7**.
xa: ⚠ **Rakesh Sharma** = first Indian **in space**; **Shukla** = first Indian **on the ISS**.
**Kalpana Chawla** = first Indian-born woman in space (**1997**).
Axiom-4 was India's first government-sponsored flight in **40+ years**.

n8a6c185e4c4.s: Gaganyatri selection and aeromedical testing were done by the IAF's:
n8a6c185e4c4.x: IAM Bengaluru did selection and testing; basic training was at the Yuri Gagarin Centre, Russia, then ISRO's facility in Bengaluru.
xa: **HSFC**, Bengaluru leads Gaganyaan as a new ISRO vertical.
**Mission MITRA** at Leh is the crew behavioural study with IAM.
The four Gaganyatris, named in **February 2024**, are all **IAF test pilots**.

n610901cbb8b.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the areas of the seven Indian microgravity experiments conducted during Axiom-4?
n610901cbb8b.x: The experiments included muscle regeneration, crop viability and cognitive performance, among other biological and life-science themes. Lunar soil mining was not listed as an experiment area.
n610901cbb8b.tq: Find the option outside the common experiment theme instead of being distracted by space-related wording.
xs: **Lunar soil mining** was not among the Axiom-4 experiments — option **(4)**.
The **7 microgravity experiments** covered **muscle regeneration**, algal growth, **crop viability** (moong, methi), microbial survivability, tardigrades, **cognitive performance**, cyanobacteria.
xa: Experiments were coordinated under **HSFC**.
Other studies: **rice, horse gram, tomato** seeds from **IIST**.
Microgravity causes **muscle atrophy** — hence the muscle regeneration test.

n81df7e244e1.s: India’s first analogue space mission was launched by ISRO at which location and in which month and year?
n81df7e244e1.x: India’s first analogue space mission was launched by ISRO at Leh in Ladakh in November 2024.
n81df7e244e1.tq: Combine the place and date rather than confusing the analogue mission with launch-pad or expo events.
xs: **India's first analogue space mission** was at **Leh, Ladakh** in **November 2024** — option **(3)** (PYQ; APPSC 2023).
**Tso Kar** hosts the separate **HOPE** station; **Kulasekarapattinam** has the SSLV complex (**August 2025**).
xa: It was run by ISRO's **HSFC**.
Partners: **AAKA Space Studio**, **University of Ladakh**, **IIT Bombay**, Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council.
It simulates life in an **interplanetary habitat**.

n1027a7e781b.s: Why was Ladakh selected for the HOPE analogue station?
o: It has the same atmospheric composition as the International Space Station.
It provides zero gravity because of its high altitude.
It has conditions resembling early Mars, including high UV flux and low air pressure.
It contains India’s only active equatorial launch site.
n1027a7e781b.x: HOPE, or Himalayan Outpost for Planetary Exploration, was located in Ladakh because of early-Mars-like conditions such as high UV flux, low air pressure, cold extremes and saline permafrost.
n1027a7e781b.tq: Match the environmental features to the analogue-mission rationale without treating high altitude as zero gravity.
xs: Ladakh was chosen for **HOPE** for **early-Mars-like** conditions: **high UV flux** and **low air pressure** — option **(3)**.
It also has **cold extremes** and **saline permafrost**.
xa: **HOPE** = **Himalayan Outpost for Planetary Exploration**, at **Tso Kar**.
⚠ **HOPE** = Mars-like habitat station; **MITRA** = crew behavioural study (with **IAM**).
India's first analogue mission was at **Leh** in **November 2024**.

na3fe74384fe.s: Mission MITRA is primarily associated with which activity?
o: A seven-experiment microgravity package on Axiom-4
A launch-pad construction project at Sriharikota
A behavioural study at Leh involving the IAF’s IAM under hypoxia, cold and isolation
na3fe74384fe.x: Mission MITRA is a behavioural study at Leh conducted with the IAF’s Institute of Aerospace Medicine, testing crew under hypoxia, cold and isolation.
na3fe74384fe.tq: Distinguish the named analogue study from the separate Axiom-4 and launch-vehicle activities.
xs: **Mission MITRA** is an ISRO **behavioural study** at **Leh** with the IAF's **IAM**, under **hypoxia, cold and isolation** — option **(3)**.
The **seven-experiment** package was **Axiom-4**'s; LVM3-M6 carried **BlueBird Block-2**.
xa: MITRA = **Mapping of Interoperable Traits and Response Assessment**.
⚠ **MITRA** = crew study; **HOPE** = Mars-like habitat station at **Tso Kar**.
IAM, **Bengaluru**, also did crew selection and aeromedical testing.

n961a50aef03.s: The expression “puffy face, bird legs” in relation to astronauts refers to:
o: Fluid shifting towards the head in microgravity
Loss of bone mass in the legs
n961a50aef03.x: Microgravity causes body fluids to shift towards the head, producing a puffy face and comparatively thinner-looking legs.
n961a50aef03.tq: Distinguish fluid redistribution from bone loss and muscle atrophy.
xs: "**Puffy face, bird legs**" describes **fluid shift** — fluids move towards the **head** — option **(3)**.
Bone loss is **osteopenia**; radiation raises **cancer and cataract** risk — neither is this effect.
xa: **Space Adaptation Syndrome** = space motion sickness in the first days.
**SANS** = optic disc swelling, vision changes.
Space medicine is studied on the **ISS** and in ground analogues (**Leh**, **HOPE**).

nphysics-23-15.s: Which of the following weightlessness situations is INCORRECTLY explained?
o: Centre of Earth – Gravitational pull becomes negligible with distance
Freely falling lift – The floor no longer pushes up, so normal force is zero
Orbiting satellite – Satellite and astronaut accelerate towards Earth with the same g
Deep space far from all masses – Gravitational pull becomes negligible with distance
nphysics-23-15.x: At the Earth's centre true g is zero because the pulls of the surrounding mass cancel; negligible pull with distance is the deep-space case.
n: At the centre of Earth, g equals zero. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 96-98]
In free fall, the normal force becomes zero. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 96-98]
An orbiting satellite and its astronaut both accelerate towards Earth with the same g. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 96-98]
Apparent weight N is zero when effective gravity is zero. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 96-98]
xa: Apparent weight **N** is zero when **effective gravity** is zero.
Microgravity experiments study **fluid behaviour**, **crystal growth** and **human physiology**.
Astronauts in space stations are in **continuous free fall**.

naec76c197b9.s: Which of the following agencies jointly operate the International Space Station?
o: NASA, Roscosmos, JAXA, ESA and CSA
NASA, ISRO, CNSA, ESA and Roscosmos
Roscosmos, CNSA, JAXA, ISRO and NASA
NASA, ESA, ISRO, CNSA and CSA
naec76c197b9.x: The ISS is operated by NASA, Roscosmos, JAXA, the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Canadian Space Agency (CSA).
naec76c197b9.tq: Recall the exact five-agency partnership rather than confusing it with China’s independent station.
xs: The **ISS** is run by **NASA, Roscosmos, JAXA, ESA and CSA** — option **(1)**.
**ISRO** and **CNSA** are not ISS partners; China has its own station, **Tiangong**.
xa: The ISS is a modular microgravity lab in **LEO** (~**400 km**), **continuously inhabited since November 2000**.
It is planned to retire around **2030** with a controlled de-orbit; private stations to follow.
Tiangong was completed in **2022** (**Tianhe** core + **Wentian** + **Mengtian**).

n541af7ef612.s: The first module of the International Space Station (1998) was:
n541af7ef612.x: Zarya was the first module; the ISS, at about 400 km, has been inhabited since November 2000 and is to retire around 2030.
xa: ISS partners: **NASA, Roscosmos, JAXA, ESA and CSA**.
Other modules: **Destiny** (US), **Kibo** (Japan), **Columbus** (ESA).
**Tiangong** is China's own station: **Tianhe** core + **Wentian** + **Mengtian**.

n948c077b6fc.s: The full Bharatiya Antariksh Station is targeted for completion by:
n948c077b6fc.x: The full station is targeted by 2035 (BAS-1 by 2028); 2040 is the target for an Indian on the Moon.
xa: Precursors: **SpaDeX** (docked **16 Jan 2025**), **Axiom-4**, **Gaganyaan**.
SpaDeX made India the **4th** nation to dock in space.
Indian on the Moon by 2040 is part of **Space Vision 2047**.

n38a1b6d630d.s: Vyommitra, planned to fly on the uncrewed G1 and G2 missions, is:
o: A male humanoid robot for the crewed flight
The parachute recovery system of the Crew Escape System
n38a1b6d630d.x: Vyommitra is an AI-enabled, female-form semi-humanoid robot meant to fly on the uncrewed G1 and G2 missions before the crewed flight.
xa: ⚠ Trap: an **APPSC 2022** statement calling it a "male robot" was false.
Sequence: **G1 → G2 → G3 → H1** (crewed).
Parachute recovery of the **Crew Escape System** was tested by **DRDO**.

n34d3d513894.s: GSAT-7A, nicknamed 'Angry Bird', mainly serves which service?
n34d3d513894.x: GSAT-7A serves the Indian Air Force and supports network-centric warfare and drone operations.
xa: ⚠ **Rukmini** = Navy (GSAT-7); **Angry Bird** = Air Force (GSAT-7A).
**GSAT-7R (CMS-03)** replaces GSAT-7 for the Navy.
**Cartosat** also gives high-resolution border imagery.

nf0aa0ccd44b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the GSAT-7 series?
o: GSAT-7 provides secure naval communication and maritime surveillance.
GSAT-7R, also designated CMS-03, is intended for the Indian Navy.
GSAT-7 was launched by GSLV from Sriharikota.
GSAT-7B is associated with the Indian Army.
nf0aa0ccd44b.x: GSAT-7 was launched by Ariane-5, not GSLV.
xa: GSAT-7R was launched on **2 Nov 2025** on **LVM3-M5**.
**GSAT-7A** (**2018**, "Angry Bird") = **Indian Air Force**.
**EMISAT** (**2019**, DRDO) = ELINT; launched on **PSLV-C45**.

nd77f88f8778.s: EMISAT, a DRDO satellite launched by PSLV-C45 in 2019, is used for:
nd77f88f8778.x: EMISAT is a DRDO satellite that performs electronic intelligence (ELINT); it was launched by PSLV-C45 in 2019.
xa: EMISAT was launched on **PSLV-C45**.
**RISAT-2** series gives the armed forces **radar surveillance** of borders.
⚠ **DSA** = tri-service agency; **DSRO** = its R&D arm.

n8e62c068576.x: RISAT is the Radar Imaging Satellite, carrying a SAR that images day and night and through clouds.
xa: **RISAT-1** (**2012**) = India's **first fully indigenous** radar imaging satellite, **C-band (5.35 GHz)**.
⚠ **RISAT-2** (**2009**, X-band, Israeli-built) flew **before** RISAT-1.
ISRO has moved to **EOS naming** for earth-observation satellites.

n67966485c2c.s: India's first fully indigenous radar imaging satellite (2012, C-band SAR) was:
n67966485c2c.x: RISAT-1 (PSLV-C19, 2012) was the first fully indigenous one; RISAT-2 (2009), launched earlier, was Israeli-built with an X-band radar.
xa: **RISAT-2BR1** (Dec 2019, **PSLV-C48**) was the **50th flight of PSLV**.
**EOS-09 (RISAT-1B)**, **1,696 kg**, was lost on **PSLV-C61** after a **third-stage** pressure drop.
In 2019 **RISAT-2B** made a collision avoidance manoeuvre using **NETRA** data.

n46f21fc44c0.s: EOS-09, a C-band SAR satellite lost on PSLV-C61, was formerly designated:
n46f21fc44c0.x: EOS-09 (1,696 kg) was formerly RISAT-1B; PSLV-C61 failed after a pressure drop in the third-stage motor.
xa: **PSLV-C62/EOS-N1** (**12 Jan 2026**) also failed — a **roll-rate disturbance** at the end of the third stage.
Two consecutive PSLV failures (C61, C62) hit **surveillance satellites**.
ISRO now uses **EOS naming** for earth-observation satellites.

n803ad107420.s: In 2019, RISAT-2B performed a collision avoidance manoeuvre against a defunct US satellite using data from which system?
n803ad107420.x: RISAT-2B performed a collision avoidance manoeuvre against a defunct US satellite using NETRA data.
n803ad107420.tq: Match the space-safety operation with the system that supplied the tracking data.
xs: **RISAT-2B** used **NETRA** data for its **2019** collision avoidance manoeuvre against a defunct US satellite — option **(4)**.
The other systems are not linked to this manoeuvre in the notes.
xa: RISAT-2B (**May 2019**) flew on **PSLV-C46** for **X-band** surveillance.
**RISAT-2BR1** followed in **Dec 2019** on **PSLV-C48**.
RISAT carries **SAR**: all-weather, day-and-night imaging.

n78cdb5e7d26.s: The PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 mission failed because of:
o: A roll-rate disturbance at the end of the third stage
A pressure drop in the third-stage solid motor
Premature shutdown of the fourth-stage engine
n78cdb5e7d26.x: PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 failed after a roll-rate disturbance at the end of the third stage; the pressure-drop failure was associated with EOS-09 on PSLV-C61.
xa: C62 flew on **12 Jan 2026** — the **64th PSLV flight**, **105th launch** from Sriharikota.
It was the **9th** dedicated **NSIL** commercial mission.
It carried **15 co-passengers**, incl. a **KID re-entry capsule**.

nd064800d74f.s: EOS-05, India's first earth-imaging satellite meant for geosynchronous orbit, will operate at an altitude of about:
nd064800d74f.x: EOS-05 is intended for geosynchronous orbit at about 36,000 km, supporting observation of floods, cyclones, fires and security events.
xa: ISRO has moved to **EOS naming** for earth-observation satellites.
⚠ **EDUSAT** was also geostationary, at **74 degrees E** — but for education, not imaging.
Two consecutive PSLV failures (**C61**, **C62**) hit surveillance satellites.

n088341571a4.s: The SBS-3 programme, approved by the Cabinet Committee on Security in November 2024, envisages how many satellites?
n088341571a4.x: SBS-3 has 52 satellites: 21 by ISRO and 31 by private industry.
xa: Cost sharing: **Army, Navy, Air Force 20% each**; **NTRO and ARC 15% each**; **MHA 10%**.
**DSA** ran the first tri-services space exercise **Antariksha Abhyas-2024**.
**DSRO** = DSA's R&D arm.

nf4d31195584.s: India's first tri-services space exercise, 'Antariksha Abhyas-2024', was conducted by the:
nf4d31195584.x: The tri-service DSA (2019, Bengaluru) ran it; DSRO is the DSA's R&D arm and IN-SPACe authorises private space activity.
xa: **SBS-3**: **52 satellites** (**21 by ISRO, 31 by private industry**), **CCS approval November 2024**.
SBS-3 cost: **₹25,221.75 crore**; Army, Navy, Air Force **20% each**, **MHA 10%**.
**EMISAT** (2019, DRDO) = **electronic intelligence (ELINT)**.

n58cff0e53b6.s: GSAT-3, India's first satellite dedicated to education, is popularly known as:
n58cff0e53b6.x: GSAT-3, popularly known as EDUSAT, was India's first satellite dedicated to education and provided two-way satellite communication to classrooms.
xa: Launched **20 September 2004** on **GSLV-F01** from **SHAR, Sriharikota**.
Lift-off mass **1,950.5 kg**; geostationary at **74 degrees E**.
Users: schools, colleges, distance-education networks (**virtual classrooms**).

naf6e0bdd5cd.s: EDUSAT was launched on 20 September 2004 by:
naf6e0bdd5cd.x: EDUSAT was launched on 20 September 2004 by GSLV-F01 from Sriharikota.
xa: EDUSAT = **GSAT-3**; launched from **SHAR, Sriharikota**.
Mass **1,950.5 kg**; geostationary at **74 degrees E**.
⚠ **GSAT-1** was the first GSLV payload (**2001**) — not a student satellite.

n0030763c430.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about student-built satellites?
o: ANUSAT (2009), by Anna University, was the first satellite built by an Indian university.
StudSat, India's first pico-satellite, was built by IIT Kanpur.
Kalamsat-V2 was the first to use the PS4 stage as an orbital platform.
Jugnu was built by IIT Kanpur.
n0030763c430.x: StudSat (2010) was built by a consortium of 7 engineering colleges of Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh; IIT Kanpur built Jugnu.
xa: **WESAT** (LBS Institute, Kerala) = **first Indian satellite fully built by women students** (PSLV-C58 POEM-3).
**AzaadiSAT** (**750 girl students**) failed on **SSLV-D1**.
⚠ **GSAT-1** is **not** a student satellite — it was the first GSLV payload, **2001**.

nac63e5e1fce.s: The satellite Jugnu was built by:
nac63e5e1fce.x: Jugnu was built by IIT Kanpur; SRMSAT by SRM University, SATYABAMASAT by Sathyabama University and Kalamsat-V2 by Space Kidz India.
xa: ⚠ Jugnu and SRMSAT = same launcher (**PSLV-C18**, **2011**).
SATYABAMASAT (**2016**, **PSLV-C34**) gave **greenhouse-gas** data.
Kalamsat-V2 flew on **PSLV-C44** (**Jan 2019**).

ndc067ac9067.s: AzaadiSAT, built by 750 girl students of government schools with Space Kidz India, was launched in August 2022 on:
ndc067ac9067.x: AzaadiSAT was launched on SSLV-D1 in August 2022 but failed to reach orbit.
xa: AzaadiSAT launched in **Aug 2022**.
⚠ **AzaadiSAT** (girl students, failed) vs **WESAT** (women students, flew).
WESAT flew on **PSLV-C58 POEM-3** (**Jan 2024**).

nedbded2d2c3.s: The StudSat consortium included colleges from which State, when it was undivided?
nedbded2d2c3.x: The StudSat consortium included colleges from Andhra Pradesh, when the State was undivided.
xa: StudSat = **India's first pico-satellite** (**2010**, **PSLV-C15**).
AP angle: all these student satellites launched from **Sriharikota**.
First university satellite: **ANUSAT** (**Anna University**).

n70e5db30062.s: The ATL Space Challenge is associated with which institutional combination?
o: Atal Innovation Mission, ISRO and CBSE
UNESCO, ISRO and the Ministry of Defence
Department of Space, UGC and NCERT
n70e5db30062.x: The ATL Space Challenge is an initiative involving the Atal Innovation Mission, ISRO and CBSE for school students.
n70e5db30062.tq: Use the institutional-combination trap to distinguish the participating bodies from neighbouring agencies.
xs: The **ATL Space Challenge** involves **Atal Innovation Mission, ISRO and CBSE** for school students — option **(2)**.
The other combinations are not linked to it in the notes.
xa: **YUVIKA** = ISRO summer programme for **class 9** students.
**Space Labs** set up in **75 Eklavya Model Residential Schools** (Apr **2026**).
**UNNATI** = nanosatellite training for developing countries.

n6f26afa490f.s: Under India's revised space-sector FDI policy, the automatic-route limit for launch vehicles and spaceports is:
n6f26afa490f.x: Launch vehicles and spaceports: 49%; satellite manufacturing/operation and data: 74%; components and subsystems: 100%.
xa: Beyond these limits the **government route** applies.
⚠ Memory aid: **100 – 74 – 49** = components – satellites/data – launch vehicles/spaceports.
The **June 2020** reforms opened the sector to **NGEs**.

n83b980253d0.s: Under India's revised FDI policy for the space sector, what is the overall ceiling for foreign direct investment in non-sensitive space segments?
n83b980253d0.x: FDI up to 100% is allowed overall in non-sensitive space segments, with segment-wise automatic-route limits of 100%, 74% and 49% and the government route beyond those limits.
xs: FDI up to **100%** is allowed overall in **non-sensitive** space segments — option **(4)**.
Within it, segment limits on the automatic route are **100%** (components), **74%** (satellites/data) and **49%** (launch vehicles/spaceports).
xa: Beyond the segment limits, the **government route** applies.
⚠ **49%** is the lowest limit — for **launch vehicles and spaceports**.
The **Space Policy 2023** lets NGEs do **end-to-end** space activity.

nce94a783c67.s: The AP Space Tech Summit-2026 was held at:
nce94a783c67.x: The AP Space Tech Summit-2026 was held at Vignan’s University in Vadlamudi, Guntur.
nce94a783c67.tq: Use the complete venue-location combination to avoid a nearby-place trap.
xs: The **AP Space Tech Summit-2026** was at **Vignan's University, Vadlamudi (Guntur)** — option **(3)**.
It was held on **23 Jan 2026**; Vadlamudi is in Guntur, not Vijayawada.
xa: AP announced **Space Policy 4.0**.
**Tirupati Space City**: **3,000 acres** near **Sriharikota**.
AP angle: **VIT-AP**'s **VISWA-M** payload flew on **Vikram-1**.

nd056aea2462.s: IN-SPACe was established in 2020 primarily as:
o: a statutory appellate tribunal for space disputes
an autonomous single-window agency under the Department of Space
a financial institution for satellite insurance
nd056aea2462.x: IN-SPACe was established in 2020 as an autonomous single-window agency under the Department of Space to facilitate non-governmental space activities.
nd056aea2462.tq: Identify the institutional character and parent department before considering its functions.
xs: **IN-SPACe** (**2020**) is an **autonomous single-window agency under the Department of Space** — option **(3)**.
It **promotes, authorises and supervises** NGEs and gives them access to **DoS facilities**.
xa: Full name: **Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre**.
HQ **Ahmedabad**; chairman **Dr Pawan Kumar Goenka**.
It runs the **IN-SPACe Seed Fund Scheme** for space start-ups.

n2cca69c7411.s: IN-SPACe, chaired by Dr Pawan Kumar Goenka, is headquartered at:
n2cca69c7411.x: IN-SPACe is headquartered at Ahmedabad, and Dr Pawan Kumar Goenka is its chairman.
xa: ⚠ HQ: **IN-SPACe = Ahmedabad**; **NSIL = Bengaluru**.
IN-SPACe received **834 applications**, processed **499** (**294 satellites**, **103 launch vehicles**).
It authorised the first private launch **Vikram-S** (**2022**).

nf8891401326.s: NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) is headquartered at:
nf8891401326.x: NSIL (CPSE under DoS, 2019) is in Bengaluru; Ahmedabad is IN-SPACe's HQ.
xa: **Antrix** was set up in **September 1992**; **Miniratna** in **2008**; supply-driven model.
NSIL follows a **demand-driven** model: builds, owns and operates satellites for committed customers.
**GSAT-24** (2022) was NSIL's **first demand-driven mission**.
**10** in-orbit communication satellites were transferred to NSIL in **2022**.

nb2dfe177b15.s: The demand-driven model followed by NewSpace India Limited primarily means that it:
o: only markets satellites built by private companies
builds, owns and operates satellites against assured customer demand
builds satellites first and searches for customers later
transfers all satellite operations to Antrix Corporation
nb2dfe177b15.x: Under the demand-driven model, NSIL builds, owns and operates satellites against assured or committed customer demand, unlike the earlier supply-driven approach.
nb2dfe177b15.tq: Distinguish the operating model by asking whether production follows assured demand or precedes it.
xs: NSIL **builds, owns and operates satellites against assured customer demand** — option **(2)**.
It replaces the old approach of **ISRO building first and then looking for users**.
xa: **GSAT-24** (**2022**) = NSIL's **first demand-driven mission**; capacity leased to **Tata Play** for **DTH**.
**GSAT-N2 (GSAT-20)** (**2024**) = fully funded and owned by NSIL.
Antrix was **supply-driven**.

na4a67cca72c.s: LVM3's first dedicated commercial mission in 2022 carried how many OneWeb satellites?
na4a67cca72c.x: LVM3's first dedicated commercial mission, in 2022, carried 36 OneWeb satellites.
xa: NSIL has launched **141** satellites (**138** international/customer) as of July **2026**.
NSIL's earlier launch count was **127**; it now operates **11** communication satellites.
NSIL's model is **demand-driven**.

nc23ed25bfb3.s: Which satellite is recognised as India’s first demand-driven satellite?
nc23ed25bfb3.x: GSAT-24, associated with NSIL and launched in 2022, is identified as the first demand-driven satellite.
nc23ed25bfb3.tq: Identify the mission associated with the distinctive ‘first’ description.
xs: **GSAT-24** is India's first demand-driven satellite — **NSIL's first demand-driven mission** (**2022**) — option **(3)**.
**GSAT-1** was the first GSLV payload, not a demand-driven satellite.
xa: GSAT-24 was launched from **Kourou, French Guiana**.
Its capacity went to **Tata Play** for **DTH**.
**GSAT-N2 (GSAT-20)** (**2024**) = **fully funded and owned by NSIL**.

na787620b137.s: The capacity of GSAT-24, NSIL's first demand-driven mission, was leased for DTH to:
na787620b137.x: GSAT-24 (2022) capacity was leased to Tata Play; GSAT-N2 was fully NSIL-funded and flew on a SpaceX Falcon 9.
xa: GSAT-24 was launched from **Kourou, French Guiana**.
GSAT-N2 gives **Ka-band broadband** and **in-flight connectivity**.
PYQ: **APPSC-G1 2024** key — statements I and III correct.

n01339069ec7.s: TSAT-1A, a sub-metre optical surveillance satellite launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 in 2024, was built by Tata Advanced Systems with:
n01339069ec7.x: TSAT-1A was built by Tata Advanced Systems with Satellogic and launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 in 2024.
xa: TSAT-1A = India's **first privately built sub-metre surveillance satellite** (optical "spy" satellite).
**GSAT-N2** also flew on a Falcon 9 (**Nov 2024**).
**GalaxEye**'s "**Drishti**" is a multi-sensor (**SAR + optical**) satellite.

n132b805450d.s: Which of the following quantitative combinations is correct for India’s space-sector objectives?
o: 50 launches a year and 2 lakh jobs
100 launches a year and 2 lakh jobs
n132b805450d.x: India’s stated objectives include 50 launches a year and the creation of approximately 2 lakh jobs.
n132b805450d.tq: Keep the launch target and employment target as a combined pair.
xs: The goals are **50 launches a year** and **2 lakh jobs** — option **(1)**.
They sit with the target of **US$44 billion by 2033**.
xa: Current size: about **US$8.4 billion** (Oct **2025**).
Target share: about **8%** of the global space economy.
Data services: **70%** of future revenues.

nefb83ea6cf3.s: Skyroot's four-stage Vikram-1, India's first private orbital rocket, can carry up to ____ to LEO.
nefb83ea6cf3.x: Vikram-1 is a four-stage rocket with up to 350 kg to LEO.
xa: Vikram-1 flew on **18 July 2026**, mission **"Aagaman"** — India's **first private orbital launch**.
It is built by **Skyroot Aerospace (Hyderabad)**.
Its payloads went to a **450 km** LEO.

n016405da60e.s: With the launch of Vikram-1, India became the third country after which two countries to possess private orbital launch capability?
n016405da60e.x: India was described as the third country, after the United States and China, with private orbital launch capability following Vikram-1.
n016405da60e.tq: Use the order-of-countries comparison rather than the rocket’s technical specifications.
xs: With **Vikram-1**, India became the **3rd** country after the **US and China** with private orbital launch capability — option **(3)**.
This was noted on **20 Jul 2026**.
xa: Global firms that reached orbit: **SpaceX**, **Rocket Lab**, **Firefly**, some Chinese firms.
Vikram-1: **4 stages**, up to **350 kg** to LEO.
⚠ **Aagaman** = Vikram-1 orbital (**2026**); **Prarambh** = Vikram-S suborbital (**2022**).

n9711bf1c723.s: India's first private rocket launch, the suborbital Vikram-S (18 Nov 2022), was named Mission:
n9711bf1c723.x: Mission Prarambh launched Vikram-S; Mission Aagaman (18 Jul 2026) launched Vikram-1, the first private orbital rocket.
xa: Vikram-1: **4 stages**, up to **350 kg** to LEO; payloads went to **450 km LEO**.
With Vikram-1, India became the **3rd country** (after US and China) with private orbital launch capability.
**Skyroot Aerospace** is based in **Hyderabad**.
**VIT-AP**'s **VISWA-M** payload flew on the SOLARAS nanosatellite.

n4ff60a04abf.s: Vikram-1 carried the SOLARAS nanosatellite, built with Grahaa Space, bearing the VISWA-M payload of:
n4ff60a04abf.x: Vikram-1 carried the SOLARAS nanosatellite with VIT-AP University's VISWA-M solar-spectrum payload, built with Grahaa Space.
xa: Other payloads: Skyroot's **SCOPE** and Cosmoserve's **Embrace**, to **450 km** LEO.
AP angle: the **VIT-AP** payload flew on Vikram-1.
**Agnibaan** has the 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine.

nfc170bc34e4.s: Agnikul Cosmos, which uses a single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine, is based in:
nfc170bc34e4.x: Agnikul is based in Chennai (IIT Madras) and launched from its own pad, Dhanush, at Sriharikota in 2024.
xa: Agnikul's rocket is **Agnibaan** (**Agnibaan SOrTeD**).
IN-SPACe authorised **Agnikul's launch**.
⚠ Skyroot's solid motors are the **Kalam** series.

n94a56ea8f51.s: Which one of the following is correctly described as India's only operational spaceport?
n94a56ea8f51.x: Sriharikota is India's only operational spaceport. Tirupati Space City is a future-oriented development that builds on the existing Sriharikota base.
n94a56ea8f51.tq: Use the unique-location clue and distinguish an operational facility from a proposed or developing project.
xs: **Sriharikota, AP** is **India's only operational spaceport** — option **(2)**.
The **private launch pad** and all launches are there; **Tirupati Space City** is a future project that builds on it.
xa: Tirupati Space City + **Space Policy 4.0** build on Sriharikota.
**Agnikul**'s **Dhanush** pad is at Sriharikota.
AP angle: **Skyroot** is from **Hyderabad**, but its rockets launch from Sriharikota.

n4178ba32b1e.s: The public-private Earth-observation constellation approved by IN-SPACe is led by:
n4178ba32b1e.x: IN-SPACe approved a PPP Earth-observation constellation led by Pixxel, with Dhruva Space, SatSure Analytics India and Piersight Space as partners.
xa: Reported in LENSD, **20 Jul 2026**.
IN-SPACe also enabled **SSLV technology transfer** to private consortia (Feb **2026**).
**Dhruva Space** flew **two** nano-satellites as rideshare on **PSLV-C54**.

nf31d7a5e083.s: The draft Space Activities Bill, proposing licensing of private space activity, was first put out in:
nf31d7a5e083.x: The draft Bill was first put out in 2017; India still has no Space Activities Act.
xa: The **Liability Convention** (**1972**) makes the **launching State** liable for damage.
Gaps: no statutory framework on **liability, dispute resolution and risk-sharing** for private entities.
No **sovereign-backed insurance** exists for private ventures.

n14c51e292b7.s: Under the Liability Convention of 1972, liability for damage caused by a space object is placed on the:
o: State where the satellite is operated
n14c51e292b7.x: The Liability Convention of 1972 makes the launching State liable for damage caused by a space object.
n14c51e292b7.tq: Identify the legally responsible authority rather than the operator or manufacturer.
xs: The **Liability Convention** (**1972**) makes the **launching State** liable for damage — option **(1)**.
Not the UN, the operating State or the manufacturer alone.
xa: India's draft **Space Activities Bill** came in **2017**.
India has **no Space Activities Act yet**.
The expected law is to cover **treaty compliance**.

n972669709e6.s: India targets expanding its space economy to about ____ by 2033.
n972669709e6.x: The target is US$44 billion by 2033 (IN-SPACe Decadal Vision), from about US$8.4 billion now, raising the global share from ~2% to ~8%.
xa: Some notes give a **US$44-60 billion** range.
Other goals: **50 launches a year**; **2 lakh** jobs.
Downstream data services: **70%** of future revenues.

n1f9a4b55fa9.s: The Rs 1,000 crore Venture Capital Fund for space start-ups is managed through:
n1f9a4b55fa9.x: The VC Fund is managed through SIDBI; the Technology Adoption Fund is run by IN-SPACe.
xa: Space start-ups grew from single digits in **2014** to **440+**.
Space economy target: **US$44 billion by 2033**, about **8% global share**.
Current size: about **US$8.4 billion** (Oct 2025).

nb0bb5afb0d7.s: According to Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh (August 2026), the number of space start-ups in India, which was in single digits in 2014, has now grown to more than:
nb0bb5afb0d7.x: The Minister said India now has more than 440 space start-ups, up from single digits in 2014 (some older sources give 300+). 40 and 140 understate the growth, and 1,400 overstates it.
xs: Space start-ups have grown to **more than 440** — option **(3)**.
**Dr Jitendra Singh** said so on **25 Aug 2026**, up from single digits in **2014**.
xa: ⚠ Some older notes say "**300+**" (2025-26).
Funding: **₹1,000 crore** VC Fund through **SIDBI**.
IN-SPACe **Seed Fund Scheme** supports start-ups.

n0b94617fdab.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Bellatrix Aerospace?
o: It develops green propulsion and electric thrusters.
Its green propulsion system was demonstrated on PSLV-C58's POEM-3.
The system was developed under the Technology Development Fund.
n0b94617fdab.x: Bellatrix Aerospace is based in Bengaluru, not Hyderabad.
xa: PYQ: **APPSC-G1 2024** — all statements correct.
**Ananth Technologies** (**Hyderabad**) = **India's first private satellite integration facility**.
Other private firms: **Pixxel** (hyperspectral), **Digantara** (space situational awareness).

n4b3bb311e09.s: Andhra Pradesh's space-sector initiative includes dedicated space cities and Space Policy:
n4b3bb311e09.x: Andhra Pradesh has announced Space Policy 4.0 and is developing dedicated space cities to promote space manufacturing.
xa: Tirupati Space City covers **3,000 acres**.
It aims at about **US$4 bn** investment (**Nara Lokesh** at SPIEF, **5 Jun 2026**).
**AP Space Tech Summit-2026**: **Vignan's University, Vadlamudi (Guntur)** (**23 Jan 2026**).

n05b7decc978.s: The Tirupati Space City is planned over about ____ near Sriharikota.
n05b7decc978.x: It is planned over about 3,000 acres and aims at about US$4 billion of investment.
xa: AP announced **Space Policy 4.0** with dedicated space cities.
The city plans **launch-vehicle assembly**, satellite manufacturing and avionics.
**AP Space Tech Summit-2026** was held at Vignan's University, Vadlamudi (Guntur).

nb0f73b303ec.s: Which of the following satellites is an example of active (radar) remote sensing?
nb0f73b303ec.x: Active systems transmit their own signal, as RISAT's radar does; Resourcesat and Oceansat illustrate passive sensing of naturally available radiation.
xa: Remote sensing gathers information **without physical contact**, from reflected/emitted radiation.
**Microwave (radar/SAR)** bands see through **cloud and darkness**.
⚠ **Active** = own signal (**RISAT**); **passive** = sunlight.

n4ea0c630081.s: SAR (microwave) remote sensing is especially useful for flood mapping because it can:
o: Observe through cloud cover and in darkness
Measure thermal emission from water bodies
Record images only in visible light
Operate only in daylight under clear skies
n4ea0c630081.x: Microwave/SAR systems can observe through cloud cover and in darkness, making them useful for flood mapping in cloudy conditions.
xa: Assam's planned flood satellites may carry **SAR** — the State is cloudy half the year (**25 Mar 2026**).
**RISAT/SAR** = flood mapping through cloud.
Bhuvan combines satellites into **flood-inundation maps** and **cyclone warnings**.

n40c36409ef8.s: InSAR detects ground deformation by comparing which property of two or more radar images of the same area?
n40c36409ef8.x: Interferometric SAR compares the phase of two or more radar images of the same area to detect ground deformation.
xa: Uses: **earthquakes**, **land subsidence**, **landslides**, **volcanoes**, **glacier movement**.
PYQ: **APPSC 2024** — statement A correct.
**NISAR** detects ground movement to the **centimetre**.

n7f1b0769597.s: The Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) is computed as:
n7f1b0769597.x: NDVI = (NIR − Red) / (NIR + Red); it works because healthy vegetation reflects strongly in the near-infrared band.
xa: NDVI is the most widely used index for **operational drought assessment** (PYQ).
**Vegetation Condition Index (VCI)** is derived from NDVI and used for **drought declaration**.
**NH Green Cover Index 2025-26** (NHAI + NRSC) uses **chlorophyll detection** over **30,000 km** in **24** States.

n57f43d20669.s: Among the following, the index most widely used for the operational assessment of drought is
n57f43d20669.x: NDVI is the most widely used spectral vegetation index for operational drought assessment.
n57f43d20669.tq: Direct recall of the standard operational index.
xs: **NDVI** is the most widely used index for **operational drought assessment** — option **(2)** (PYQ).
**VCI** is **derived from NDVI** — used for drought declaration, but NDVI is the base index.
xa: NDVI = **(NIR - Red) / (NIR + Red)**, range **-1 to +1**.
APSAC makes **fortnightly mandal-level VCI** in AP.
AP declared **103** drought mandals in **7** districts (**80** severe) in **2024-25**.

n9a57e8d6bf1.s: The NH Green Cover Index 2025-26 is India's first satellite-based green-cover assessment of:
n9a57e8d6bf1.x: The NH Green Cover Index is India's first satellite-based green-cover assessment of highways and uses chlorophyll detection.
xa: It covers about **30,000 km** in **24 States**.
**NRSC** is in **Hyderabad**.
Remote sensing can measure **chlorophyll**, forest cover and vegetation.

n340e6cfc315.s: Which satellite system supports flood mapping even through cloud cover?
n340e6cfc315.x: RISAT's SAR can map floods through clouds; INSAT-3DS tracks cyclones, Oceansat gives ocean-state data and Cartosat maps damage.
xa: Bhuvan combines these into **flood-inundation maps and cyclone warnings**.
PYQ: "spread of a disease" (**APPSC 2022**) and "heart attack" (**APPSC 2025**) were the CANNOT answers.
Fire hotspots come from **MODIS** and **VIIRS**.

n404a7c63a45.s: Bhuvan combines RISAT/SAR imagery and INSAT-3DS cyclone-track data mainly to provide:
n404a7c63a45.x: Bhuvan combines RISAT/SAR flood imagery and INSAT-3DS cyclone-track information to support flood-inundation mapping and cyclone warnings.
xa: Bhuvan was launched in **2009** by **NRSC**.
**Cartosat** = damage mapping; **Oceansat** = ocean state.
States must request satellite data from **NRSC** (**25 Mar 2026**).

n02f29099f21.s: Which type of sensor is best suited for measuring soil moisture from space?
n02f29099f21.x: Microwave and SAR sensors are particularly suitable for soil-moisture measurement; NISAR uses L-band and S-band radar for this.
xa: Microwave/SAR also sees **through cloud and darkness**.
**SLUSI** maps soil resources from satellite data.
The **SAC drought geoportal** tracks **soil moisture** with rainfall and temperature.

n0877dc097a4.s: Resourcesat-series data are mainly used for:
o: Crop acreage assessment, watershed management and precision farming
n0877dc097a4.x: Resourcesat data support crop acreage assessment, watershed management and precision farming.
xa: Resourcesat is a **passive** (sunlight) sensor system.
**CROP** framework used **Resourcesat-2A** with **EOS-04** and **EOS-06** for the wheat estimate.
**SLUSI** maps soil resources from satellite data.

nbc49160818d.s: Which one of the following agencies functions as the nodal agency for receiving, processing and supplying satellite data, while also operating Bhuvan and providing disaster-support services to States?
nbc49160818d.x: The National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), Hyderabad, receives, processes and supplies satellite data, runs Bhuvan and supports States in disaster management.
nbc49160818d.tq: Identify the agency from its distinctive combination of functions.
xs: The **National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), Hyderabad** is the **nodal agency** that receives, processes and supplies satellite data — option **(3)**.
It runs **Bhuvan** and gives **disaster support to States**.
**IIRS** = training; **SAC** = sensors and applications; **NESAC** = North-East.
xa: NRSC also handles **DMS**, crop estimates, and the **Shadnagar** earth station.
⚠ **NRSC** = Hyderabad; **IIRS** = Dehradun; **SAC** = Ahmedabad.
**5 RRSCs** work under NRSC.

n7d440b2dacb.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the North Eastern Space Applications Centre (NESAC)?
o: It is located at Umiam (Shillong), Meghalaya
It is a joint body of the Department of Space and the North Eastern Council
It is the national agency for training and education in remote sensing and GIS
It provides space applications for the North-East
n7d440b2dacb.x: Training and education in remote sensing and GIS is the role of IIRS, Dehradun, not NESAC.
xa: ⚠ **NRSC** = data (Hyderabad); **IIRS** = training (Dehradun); **SAC** = sensors (Ahmedabad).
NESAC is also written **NE-SAC**.
The **5 RRSCs** do regional projects for States.

n44e146f0df4.s: Which portal provides meteorological and oceanographic satellite data?
n44e146f0df4.x: MOSDAC (SAC) provides meteorological and oceanographic satellite data; Bhoonidhi (NRSC) is an EO data archive and VEDAS visualises EO data.
xa: **Bhuvan**, ISRO's geoportal, is run by **NRSC, Hyderabad**; launched **2009**.
**Bhuvan Panchayat** supports **gram panchayat** development planning (SIS-DP).
**SVAMITVA** = **drone mapping** of rural inhabited properties with **Survey of India**.
AP integrated **271 GIS layers across 27 departments** on **PM Gati Shakti**.

nfd6d8fd2558.s: In GIS, overlay analysis refers to:
o: Converting raster data into vector data
Creating a buffer zone around a feature
Combining different data layers for analysis
nfd6d8fd2558.x: Overlay analysis combines multiple thematic layers to derive and analyse relationships between them.
xa: Each theme (roads, soils, land use, water) = a **layer**.
PM Gati Shakti (AP) integrates **271** layers across **27** departments.
GIS software example: **QGIS**.

n03e93f8c6f2.s: Potential Fishing Zone advisories are prepared mainly using satellite-derived information on
n03e93f8c6f2.x: PFZ advisories identify fish-rich areas using satellite observations of chlorophyll and sea-surface temperature.
n03e93f8c6f2.tq: Separate marine biological and thermal indicators from terrestrial remote-sensing variables.
xs: **PFZ advisories** use satellite data on **chlorophyll** and **sea-surface temperature** to locate fish-rich zones — option **(4)**.
Soil moisture is for drought; ground deformation is **InSAR**'s field.
xa: PFZ advisories are issued by **INCOIS, Hyderabad**.
They now use **EOS-06 (Oceansat-3)** data and **cut fuel costs**.
The **Oceansat** series generates PFZ advisories.

nb36b8503e43.s: Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) advisories, now using EOS-06 (Oceansat-3) data, are issued by:
nb36b8503e43.x: INCOIS, Hyderabad issues PFZ advisories using EOS-06 (Oceansat-3) data; it also issues the Ocean State Forecast.
xa: PFZ uses **chlorophyll** and **sea-surface temperature** to locate fish-rich zones.
**Nabhmitra** (SAC, Ahmedabad) is a satellite **fishermen safety** device, tested at **Neendakara (Kerala)**, Aug **2023**.
**GEMINI** (INCOIS with AAI) sends PFZ, OSF and disaster alerts to fishermen at sea.

ndisaster-management-26-15.s: The National Database for Emergency Management is abbreviated as:
ndisaster-management-26-15.x: NDEM is the National Database for Emergency Management. NADAMS is the drought system and DMSP ISRO's programme.
n: The National Database for Emergency Management is abbreviated as NDEM. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 57-59]
xs: The **National Database for Emergency Management** is **NDEM** — option **(3)**.
**DMSP** = ISRO's **Disaster Management Support Programme**; **NADAMS** = National Agricultural **Drought** Assessment and Monitoring System.
xa: NDEM is a **GIS repository** for the full disaster cycle, at **NRSC, Hyderabad**.
ISRO took the **lead role** in the **International Charter Space and Major Disasters** for **6 months from April 2025**.
INSAT **DWS**: Chennai → **C-band** uplink → **S-band** downlink to coastal receivers.

n15d0ec25e7f.s: The Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast Centre (MNCFC), which makes ISRO's crop-forecasting methods operational, was set up in:
xa: MNCFC = **Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast Centre**.
**FASAL** gives pre-harvest crop acreage and production forecasts.
**YES-TECH** = crop yield for **PMFBY**.

nbea5d5d729e.s: Which one of the following CANNOT be monitored using satellite remote sensing?
o: Spread of a disease among humans
nbea5d5d729e.x: Floods, cyclones, drought, forest fires, tsunami inundation, landslides and post-quake ground deformation can all be monitored from space. Individual human-health events cannot: the spread of a disease among humans (APPSC 2022) and a heart attack (APPSC 2025) were the 'cannot be monitored' answers. Forest fires, tsunami inundation and landslides are all monitorable, so they are wrong.
nbea5d5d729e.tq: 'Cannot be monitored from space' → always the human-health event.
xs: **Spread of a disease among humans** cannot be monitored from space — option **(3)** (**APPSC 2022**).
**Forest fires**, **tsunami inundation of coasts** and **landslides** can all be monitored.
xa: Exam angle: the "CANNOT be monitored" answer is always the **human-health event** — also **heart attack** (**APPSC 2025**).
Also monitorable: floods, cyclones, drought, post-quake **ground deformation**.
⚠ Earthquakes **cannot be predicted**.

n582bd565731.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about fire-hotspot monitoring?
o: Hotspot data are passed to the India Meteorological Department, which runs the forest-fire alert system
Thermal-infrared sensors such as MODIS and VIIRS detect fire hotspots
MODIS flies on NASA's Terra and Aqua satellites
Hotspot data are received at NRSC's Shadnagar earth station
n582bd565731.x: The hotspot data go to the Forest Survey of India alert system, not to IMD.
xa: These sensors fly on **polar** satellites.
Forest fires (**wildfires**) can be monitored from space.
NRSC is the **nodal agency** for satellite data.

n9dbffe8cbec.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about satellite support during disasters in India?
o: The Decision Support Centre is located at NRSC, Hyderabad
States can use satellite data during disasters without requesting it from NRSC
The National Database for Emergency Management (NDEM) is located at NRSC, Hyderabad
The Decision Support Centre acts as a single window for satellite inputs during disasters
n9dbffe8cbec.x: States must request satellite data from NRSC; the other statements are correct.
xa: **NDEM** = **National Database for Emergency Management** — a GIS repository for the full disaster cycle.
NRSC gives **disaster support to States**.
**APSDMA-NRSC MoU** (**15 Apr 2026**) to prevent **lightning deaths** in rural AP.

nb1ab4f0b0f3.s: ISRO took the lead role in the International Charter Space and Major Disasters for six months beginning in:
nb1ab4f0b0f3.x: ISRO assumed the lead role in the International Charter Space and Major Disasters for six months from April 2025.
nb1ab4f0b0f3.tq: Test the precise commencement date using closely spaced year options.
xs: ISRO took the **lead role** in the **International Charter Space and Major Disasters** for **6 months from April 2025** — option **(2)**.
The other years are not in the notes.
xa: ISRO's own **DMS programme** uses **INSAT/IRS** for warning + damage assessment.
**NDEM** and the **Decision Support Centre** sit at **NRSC**.
India proposed a **BRICS Space Economy** + stronger BRICS remote-sensing constellation (**25 Jun 2026**).

n59620ada674.s: Which sequence correctly represents the communication chain in the INSAT Disaster Warning System?
o: Coastal receiver → C-band uplink → Cyclone Warning Centre, Chennai → S-band downlink
Cyclone Warning Centre, Chennai → C-band uplink → S-band downlink → coastal receivers
S-band uplink → NRSC, Hyderabad → C-band downlink → inland receivers
Forest Survey of India → optical uplink → INSAT-3DS → ocean receivers
n59620ada674.x: The system follows the chain: Cyclone Warning Centre at Chennai, C-band uplink, S-band downlink and reception by coastal disaster-warning receivers.
n59620ada674.tq: Follow the first-to-last communication sequence and eliminate reversed links.
xs: The chain is **Cyclone Warning Centre, Chennai → C-band uplink → S-band downlink → coastal DWS receivers** — option **(2)**.
Uplink is **C-band** and downlink **S-band** — option (3) reverses the bands.
xa: This is the **INSAT Disaster Warning System**.
**INSAT-3DS** tracks cyclones.
**INCOIS**'s **Ocean State Forecast** also gives cyclone tracks.

ndisaster-management-26-12.s: The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) uses GIS for:
o: Planning, decision support and developing guidelines
ndisaster-management-26-12.x: NDMA uses GIS for planning, decision support and drafting guidelines.
n: NDMA uses GIS for planning. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 57-59]
NDMA uses GIS for decision support. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 57-59]
NDMA uses GIS for developing guidelines. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 57-59]
xa: **NRSC, Hyderabad** is a **Decision Support Centre** giving **satellite-based inputs** during disasters.
**NDEM** (National Database for Emergency Management) is a GIS repository at NRSC.
ISRO's **Disaster Management Support Programme (DMSP)** uses INSAT/IRS for warning and damage assessment.

nfd38c03c56d.s: Nabhmitra, tested at Neendakara in Kerala in August 2023, is
o: a satellite-based safety device for fishermen
nfd38c03c56d.x: Nabhmitra is a satellite-based fishermen safety device developed by ISRO’s Space Applications Centre, Ahmedabad, and tested at Neendakara in August 2023.
nfd38c03c56d.tq: Combine the device, developer, location and date to avoid confusing it with GEMINI.
xs: **Nabhmitra** is a **satellite-based fishermen safety device** — option **(2)**.
It was developed by **ISRO Space Applications Centre, Ahmedabad** and tested at **Neendakara (Kerala)**, **Aug 2023** (PYQ; APPSC **2023**).
xa: It offers **two-way messaging via GSAT**.
⚠ **GEMINI** is from **INCOIS with AAI**, using **GAGAN**.
AP: **RTGS hub, Vijayawada** sends satellite alerts to coastal fishermen.

nb2c84c03787.s: The satellite-based coastal-fishermen alert service run from the RTGS hub at Vijayawada warns about:
o: Cyclones, high waves and fish shoals
nb2c84c03787.x: The RTGS hub at Vijayawada provides satellite-based alerts to coastal fishermen about cyclones, high waves and fish shoals.
xa: RTGS also built **City Flood Alert** with **APSDMA** and **IIT Gandhinagar**.
**INCOIS** issues **PFZ** advisories and **Ocean State Forecasts**.
**Nabhmitra** gives two-way messaging via **GSAT**.

nf98570d2b7e.s: The lightning-alert app Damini was developed by:
nf98570d2b7e.x: Damini is from IITM Pune (MoES); Mausam is IMD's weather app.
xa: ⚠ **Damini** = lightning; **Meghdoot** = agro-met; **Mausam** = weather.
**APSDMA-NRSC MoU** (**15 Apr 2026**) targets **lightning deaths** in rural AP.
City Flood Alert was first used in **Vijayawada**.

n7014694491b.s: Andhra Pradesh's City Flood Alert system was first implemented in:
n7014694491b.x: It was first implemented in Vijayawada, using satellite DEMs and Budameru flood data.
xa: **APSDMA-NRSC MoU** (15 Apr 2026) aims to prevent **lightning deaths** in rural AP.
⚠ **Damini** = lightning; **Meghdoot** = agro-met; **Mausam** = weather.
**Damini** was developed by **IITM Pune** (MoES).

n2d7f79e4d6c.s: The MoU signed on 15 April 2026 between APSDMA and NRSC primarily seeks to address which problem in rural Andhra Pradesh?
n2d7f79e4d6c.x: The APSDMA-NRSC MoU aims to prevent lightning deaths in rural Andhra Pradesh.
n2d7f79e4d6c.tq: Link the institutional agreement with its stated problem-specific objective.
xs: The **APSDMA-NRSC MoU** (**15 Apr 2026**) aims to prevent **lightning deaths** in rural AP — option **(2)**.
Crop yield is **YES-TECH**'s; coastal erosion is APSAC shoreline mapping.
xa: The lightning alert app **Damini** is from **IITM Pune**.
**NRSC, Hyderabad** is the **nodal agency** for satellite data.
NRSC's director spoke at **AP Space Tech Summit 2026** in **Guntur** (**23 Jan 2026**).

nccc04659e7d.s: ISRO's single-window centres for tele-education, telemedicine, weather and land/water advisories are called:
nccc04659e7d.x: ISRO's Village Resource Centres are single-window centres for these services.
xa: **Swayam Prabha** = **40 free DTH channels** on **GSAT-15**.
INSAT/GSAT tele-education: **EDUSAT, GRAMSAT**.
**Space Labs** have been set up in **75 EMRS** (Apr 2026).

nc6baab2e3e2.s: Tele-education, telemedicine and Village Resource Centres in India have been enabled by which satellite systems?
nc6baab2e3e2.x: INSAT and GSAT satellite communication systems have enabled tele-education, telemedicine and Village Resource Centres.
xa: Tele-education used **EDUSAT** and **GRAMSAT**.
The **DMS** programme is also listed among INSAT applications.
Satellite telemedicine still matters where **terrestrial internet is absent** (**30 Jan 2026**).

nfc847729bfd.s: Swayam Prabha provides how many free DTH channels through GSAT-15?
nfc847729bfd.x: Swayam Prabha provides 40 free DTH channels through GSAT-15.
xa: Earlier tele-education: **EDUSAT** and **GRAMSAT**.
**Space Labs** in **75 EMRS** (Apr **2026**).
**GSAT-15** also carries **GAGAN** payloads.

ndd2372da6f5.s: The Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicle Tracking System (APMVTS) uses AIS-140 devices mainly to track:
ndd2372da6f5.x: APMVTS fitted 50,000 mineral vehicles with AIS-140 tracking devices.
xa: It is a **navigation** application of space technology.
Mineral-vehicle tracking also feeds GIS **situational awareness**.
Satellite timing lets **banks** time-stamp transactions.

n1fa0f7faaba.s: Swayam Prabha's educational DTH channels are carried on:
n1fa0f7faaba.x: Swayam Prabha's DTH channels are on GSAT-15.
xa: Swayam Prabha has **40** free DTH channels.
**GEMINI** uses **GAGAN** to alert fishermen.
Swayam Prabha, telemedicine and KASTURI extend space use into **governance**.

n06ddb5df993.s: NISAR detects centimetre-scale ground movement for studying land subsidence, earthquakes and glaciers using:
n06ddb5df993.x: NISAR uses radar observations, which let it detect centimetre-scale ground movement.
xa: **InSAR** compares the **phase** of two or more radar images to map **ground deformation**.
NISAR's radar is also used for **soil moisture**.
InSAR uses: earthquakes, **land subsidence**, **landslides**, **volcanoes**, **glacier movement**.

n9f2f9533b82.s: Remote sensing is used to assess which of the following natural-resource features?
o: Surface and groundwater prospects, snow and glaciers, wetlands, and mineral and hydrocarbon zones
n9f2f9533b82.x: All of these are listed as measurable by remote sensing, along with land cover, vegetation, soil and crop yield.
xa: Also: land cover, vegetation, **chlorophyll**, forest cover, soil.
Crop area and **yield** are measured too (**YES-TECH**).
**NRSC, Hyderabad** is the nodal agency for satellite data.

na708c3572cc.s: The Vegetation Condition Index (VCI), used in drought declaration, is derived from:
na708c3572cc.x: VCI is derived from vegetation-related NDVI data and is used in drought declaration.
xa: In AP, **APSAC** generates **fortnightly mandal-level VCI**.
AP declared **103 drought mandals** in **7 districts** (2024-25).
⚠ Sea-surface temperature is used for **PFZ** fishing advisories, not VCI.

n32b5406f5a1.s: In a GIS, QGIS is an example of:
n32b5406f5a1.x: QGIS is GIS software; GIS hardware means the computer, digitizer, scanner, GPS receiver and plotter.
xa: The fourth GIS component is **people and methods** — analysts and procedures.
Each theme (roads, soils, land use) is a **layer**; **overlay** analysis combines them.
Real-time layers give **situational awareness** for disaster response and flood alerts.

n7735548f86f.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Spatial Data Infrastructure (APSSDI) has standardised how many GIS layers to ISO standards?
n7735548f86f.x: APSSDI has standardised 74 GIS layers to ISO standards and is registered with the National Data Registry.
xa: ⚠ PM Gati Shakti (AP) has **271** layers across **27** departments.
APSAC water-supply mapping: **38,000** rural schemes; **1,200** mapped so far.
GIS software **QGIS** is used in APSAC workshops.

naa85be2ad62.s: Space debris is best defined as:
o: Operational satellites that have drifted from their assigned orbit
All non-functional man-made objects, including fragments, in orbit or re-entering
Natural meteoroids passing through Earth orbit
Fragments created only by anti-satellite tests
naa85be2ad62.x: Space debris consists of non-functional man-made objects, including fragments, that are in orbit or re-entering the atmosphere.
xa: Sources: **defunct satellites**, **spent rocket stages**, **fragmentation** (main source), **ASAT tests**, tools lost on spacewalks.
Scale: **over 1.2 million** objects larger than **1 cm** (**ESA Space Environment Report 2025**).
A **10-cm** object can shatter a satellite.

nc68134f1747.s: What is the main source of space debris?
nc68134f1747.x: Fragmentation from collisions and explosions is the main source; the others are also sources of debris.
xa: India's **Mission Shakti** (**27 March 2019**) raised debris concerns.
**Kessler Syndrome**: collisions create more debris in a self-sustaining **cascade**.
**MMOD** is the top risk in **LEO**.

ne0a2bd84171.s: Mission Shakti, conducted on 27 March 2019, involved:
o: The deployment of India's first space station
A soft landing of a rover on the Moon
A kinetic-kill ASAT test that destroyed Microsat-R at about 300 km
A test of a reusable launch vehicle at 300 km altitude
ne0a2bd84171.x: Mission Shakti was a DRDO kinetic-kill anti-satellite test that destroyed the Indian satellite Microsat-R at approximately 300 km altitude, raising debris concerns.
ne0a2bd84171.tq: Match the mission, agency-related capability, target and altitude in one precise statement.
xs: **Mission Shakti** was a DRDO **kinetic-kill ASAT test** destroying **Microsat-R** at about **300 km** — option **(3)**.
It was held on **27 March 2019** and raised **debris concerns** (UPSC).
xa: **ASAT tests** are a listed source of space debris.
The **US** declared a moratorium on destructive direct-ascent ASAT tests in **April 2022**.
Way forward: clear limits on **destructive ASAT tests** in the OST.

n4e78878c99e.s: Under its Debris Free Space Missions (DFSM) pledge, India aims to make all its space missions debris-free by:
n4e78878c99e.x: The DFSM target year is 2030; India made the pledge at the 2024 IADC meeting.
xa: **IADC** was set up in **1993**; ISRO is a member.
**POEM** tests **drag-augmentation devices** to speed re-entry.
BRICS HoSA meet in **Bengaluru** put **debris-free missions** on the agenda (**25 Jun 2026**).

n1b996c3a5e5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about space-sustainability challenges facing India?
o: Space debris threatens Gaganyaan and India's in-orbit satellites
Differences in national licensing conditions may push operators to permissive regimes
Mega-constellations are a newer challenge not adequately addressed by older treaties
Existing treaties adequately address the cumulative harm caused by orbital debris
n1b996c3a5e5.x: The treaties date from the 1960s–70s and do not adequately address cumulative debris harm or mega-constellations.
xa: There is **no international duty-of-care standard** for orbits.
India has **no Space Activities Act** for liability.
Debris also threatens **BAS**.

nae5b9d1aaa0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about space debris risks?
o: Kessler Syndrome is a self-sustaining cascade of debris-creating collisions that can make orbits unusable
MMOD (micrometeoroids and orbital debris) is the top risk mainly in geostationary orbit
Kessler Syndrome is named after NASA scientist Donald Kessler
The Kessler Syndrome idea dates from 1978
nae5b9d1aaa0.x: MMOD is the top risk in low Earth orbit (LEO), not GEO.
xa: MMOD = **micrometeoroids and orbital debris**.
Main debris source: **fragmentation** from collisions and explosions.
Over **1.2 million** objects larger than **1 cm**.

nf50ba2d7f25.s: The principal aim of Project NETRA is to:
o: Track only military aircraft in Indian airspace
Safeguard Indian space assets from debris and collisions
Provide satellite television services to rural areas
Develop reusable launch vehicles for lunar missions
