nf50ba2d7f25.x: Project NETRA aims to provide indigenous space situational awareness and safeguard Indian space assets from debris and collisions.
nf50ba2d7f25.tq: Match the system with its operational purpose rather than its name alone.
xs: **Project NETRA** aims to **safeguard Indian space assets from debris and collisions** — option **(2)** (PYQ).
It is **ISRO**'s indigenous **SSA** capability.
xa: NETRA = **Network for Space Object Tracking and Analysis**.
It gives **24-72 hours** advance warning, with **Green/Yellow/Red** alerts.
Policy push: expand NETRA with **radars and telescopes**.

n9b7921cfb7b.s: Bengaluru-based start-up Digantara works mainly in:
o: Space situational awareness and debris tracking
n9b7921cfb7b.x: Digantara is a space-situational-awareness start-up building space-surveillance satellites and generating debris-tracking data.
xa: Policy push: private firms to build **LiDAR satellites and SSA systems**.
ISRO's own SSA: **NETRA**, **IS4OM**, **SSACC**.
NETRA alerts: **Green/Yellow/Red**.

na890fb6684b.s: Which Article of the Outer Space Treaty deals with national responsibility, including for private actors?
na890fb6684b.x: Article VI deals with national responsibility; Article VII concerns liability and Article IX due regard and environmental considerations.
xa: The OST bars **national sovereignty/appropriation**.
India ratified the OST in **1982**.
**ATLAC**: UN working group on lunar landing-site coordination + debris rules.

n943fc6fdbad.s: Project NETRA, which gives 24–72 hours' warning of close approaches in space, is run by:
n943fc6fdbad.x: NETRA is an ISRO project to safeguard Indian space assets; IS4OM compiles the annual ISSAR.
xa: **SSACC** is ISRO's Space Situational Awareness Control Centre.
ISSAR 2025: ISRO made **18** collision avoidance manoeuvres; over **1.5 lakh** close-approach alerts.
**Digantara** (Bengaluru) is an SSA start-up tracking debris.

n51410387839.s: How many collision avoidance manoeuvres (CAMs) did India record in 2025?
n51410387839.x: 18 CAMs were recorded in 2025, continuing regular CAMs for Cartosat, Resourcesat and GSAT.
xa: The 18 CAMs were in **LEO and GEO**.
**RISAT-2B** avoided a defunct US satellite (**2019**).
Indian satellites logged **over 1.5 lakh** close-approach alerts in 2025.

n7eaa7e929ad.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's 2026 rules on re-entry of space objects?
o: Clearance is needed from a foreign State whose territory holds the re-entry site
Clearance is needed when the re-entry site lies in a foreign State's exclusive economic zone
Aircraft and ships in the re-entry area must be warned at least 30 days before re-entry
The rules turn IADC and UNCOPUOS soft-law guidance into domestic rules
n7eaa7e929ad.x: The warning must be given at least 45 days before re-entry, not 30.
xa: The re-entry rules came on **24 Aug 2026**.
Gap: **no international duty-of-care standard** for orbits.
⚠ India still has **no Space Activities Act** for liability.

n874ab54eb2d.s: ISRO's planned Active Debris Removal mission will capture a defunct rocket body using a servicer craft fitted with:
n874ab54eb2d.x: The planned ADR mission uses a servicer craft with a robotic arm or net to capture a defunct Indian rocket body; it is being tested at URSC.
xa: **POEM** uses **inflatable sails** for faster re-entry.
**PS4 de-boost** was planned on **PSLV-C62** (Jan **2026**).
India pledged **DFSM by 2030** at the **2024 IADC** meeting.

nbbfe71dd9b8.s: Which country declared a moratorium on destructive direct-ascent anti-satellite tests in April 2022?
nbbfe71dd9b8.x: The United States declared the moratorium on destructive direct-ascent ASAT tests in April 2022, and the issue was subsequently taken up in a UNGA resolution.
nbbfe71dd9b8.tq: Use the date-country association to distinguish the declared moratorium from other space powers.
xs: **The United States** declared the destructive direct-ascent ASAT test moratorium in **April 2022** — option **(4)**.
It was then taken up in a **UNGA resolution**.
xa: India's own ASAT test was **Mission Shakti** (**27 March 2019**).
**PAROS** is a **Conference on Disarmament** agenda item.
Way forward: **behaviour-based norms** and confidence-building.

nd3942f7e97f.s: India ratified the Outer Space Treaty of 1967 in:
nd3942f7e97f.x: India is a party to the Outer Space Treaty, which bars national appropriation of space, and ratified it in 1982.
xa: OST: **Art. VI** national responsibility incl. private actors; **Art. VII** liability; **Art. IX** due regard/environment.
"The OST does **not recognise sovereignty** in outer space" — a lunar landing gives no ownership (**5 Aug 2026**).
⚠ The **Moon Agreement 1979** is the only one India **signed but not ratified**.

n420d7d1b799.s: Which space treaty has India signed but not ratified?
n420d7d1b799.x: The Moon Agreement is the only one India has signed but not ratified.
xa: **Outer Space Treaty 1967**: **no national sovereignty**; India ratified it in **1982**.
⚠ **Liability Convention 1972**: **absolute** liability on Earth, **fault** liability in space.
The Moon Agreement treats the Moon as **common heritage of mankind**.

n0b9413747f5.s: Under the Liability Convention, 1972, a launching State's liability for damage caused by its space object is:
o: Absolute for damage on the Earth's surface and fault-based for damage in outer space
Fault-based for damage on the Earth's surface and absolute for damage in outer space
Absolute in all cases, whether the damage is on Earth or in outer space
Limited to damage caused by private operators only
n0b9413747f5.x: The Liability Convention (1972), to which India is a party, makes the launching State absolutely liable for damage on the Earth's surface and liable only for fault for damage caused in outer space. Option B reverses the two rules. Option C ignores the fault standard in space. Option D is wrong because liability rests on the launching State, including for private activity.
n0b9413747f5.tq: Liability Convention: Earth = absolute; space = fault.
xs: **Absolute** liability for damage **on Earth**, **fault** liability **in space** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) reverses the two rules; option (3) ignores the fault rule in space.
Liability lies on the **launching State** (OST **Art. VI** covers private actors too).
xa: India is a **party** to the Liability Convention.
OST **Art. VII** also covers liability.
India has **no Space Activities Act** for liability.

nd6b4333ce0c.s: Which of the following is identified as a significant legal gap in India's space sector?
o: Absence of a national space policy
Absence of a Space Activities Act addressing liability
Absence of a body to authorise private space activities
nd6b4333ce0c.x: India does not have a Space Activities Act specifically addressing liability, which is identified as a significant legal gap.
xa: India's **2026 re-entry rules** turn **IADC + UNCOPUOS** soft law into domestic rules.
The **Liability Convention 1972**: **absolute** liability on Earth, **fault** in space.
OST **Art. VI**: national responsibility including **private actors**.

n3f7dcfc406e.s: UNCOPUOS, of which India is a founding member, was established in:
n3f7dcfc406e.x: The UN Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space was established in 1959, and India is a founding member.
xa: UNCOPUOS = **UN Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space**.
Its **Long-term Sustainability (LTS) Guidelines** + debris-mitigation guidelines guide India's **DoS**.
India's **2026** re-entry rules turn IADC + UNCOPUOS soft law into domestic rules.

n701512689e1.s: The Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee (IADC), of which ISRO is a member, was established in:
n701512689e1.x: IADC was established in 1993 and ISRO is a member; India made its DFSM-2030 pledge at the 2024 IADC meeting.
xa: IADC = **Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee**.
India pledged **DFSM by 2030** at the **2024** IADC meeting.
India's re-entry rules draw on **IADC** soft law.

n41b056327c0.s: India signed the Artemis Accords in:
n41b056327c0.x: India signed in 2023; the US launched the Accords in 2020 as non-binding principles, and they now have over 60 signatories.
xa: **UNCOPUOS** (1959): India is a **founding member**.
**IADC** (**1993**): venue of India's **DFSM by 2030** pledge (2024 meeting).
The **Zero Debris Charter** has been signed by **12** nations.

n051f348750c.s: The Prevention of an Arms Race in Outer Space (PAROS) is best described as
o: a treaty governing aircraft warnings during re-entry
a long-running agenda item of the UN Conference on Disarmament
a private debris-removal programme led by commercial firms
a bilateral satellite-navigation agreement between India and the United States
n051f348750c.x: PAROS is a long-running agenda item in the UN Conference on Disarmament and is backed by UN General Assembly resolutions.
n051f348750c.tq: Match the acronym with its institutional location and subject matter.
xs: **PAROS** (Prevention of an Arms Race in Outer Space) is a long-running **UN Conference on Disarmament** agenda item — option **(2)**.
It is backed by **UNGA resolutions**.
xa: The **US** declared a destructive direct-ascent ASAT test moratorium in **April 2022**.
Way forward: clear limits on **destructive ASAT tests** and deliberate debris creation.
India's stance: "**cooperation over confrontation**" (Paris, **10 Sep 2026**).

n14d17905e94.s: At the International Space Summit in Paris on 10 September 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi advocated
o: national ownership of all orbital regions
competition over cooperation in outer space
n14d17905e94.x: The stated approach was 'cooperation over confrontation', with the aim of a safe, secure, peaceful and sustainable space domain anchored in international law.
n14d17905e94.tq: Recall the exact contrast used in the stated diplomatic position.
xs: PM Modi called for "**cooperation over confrontation**" at the **International Space Summit, Paris** (**10 Sep 2026**) — option **(3)**.
He sought a **safe, secure, peaceful, sustainable** space domain anchored in **international law**.
xa: The **OST** does **not recognise sovereignty** in outer space.
Way forward includes **more SSA data-sharing**.
India signed the **Artemis Accords** in **2023**.

ned5c1ca8e5e.s: Which of the following is identified as a major gap in the international governance of orbital activities?
o: Absence of international interest in space debris
Absence of any national licensing system for satellites
Absence of an international duty-of-care standard for orbits
Absence of all collision avoidance technology
ned5c1ca8e5e.x: There is no international duty-of-care standard for orbits. Differences in licensing conditions across countries can encourage operators to choose more permissive regimes.
ned5c1ca8e5e.tq: Find the precise institutional gap and reject extreme claims such as absence of any licensing or technology.
xs: The gap is the **absence of an international duty-of-care standard for orbits** — option **(3)**.
Licensing conditions differ, so **operators pick permissive regimes** (**1 Apr 2026**).
xa: Treaties date from the **1960s-70s** and miss **cumulative harm** and **mega-constellations**.
India's **2026 re-entry rules** turn soft law into domestic rules.
CAMs exist — **18** in **2025** — so collision technology is not absent.

nd95ed977c52.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about DRDO?
o: It was formed by merging the TDEs, the DTDP and the Defence Science Organisation
Its headquarters, DRDO Bhawan, is in Pune
It started with 10 laboratories and now runs about 52
nd95ed977c52.x: DRDO Bhawan is in New Delhi.
xa: Staff: about **5,000 scientists** + **25,000** support staff.
Motto: "**Balasya Mulam Vigyanam**" ("the source of strength is science").
Older notes say "**50+**" labs.

nbf979403d75.s: DRDO's current vision is to empower the nation with state-of-the-art indigenous ____ technologies.
nbf979403d75.x: DRDO's current vision is to empower the nation with state-of-the-art indigenous defence and security technologies.
xa: Older vision: make India prosperous with a **world-class S&T base** and give the Services a **decisive edge**.
Overall goal: **Aatmanirbharta** + less import dependence.
⚠ Motto: **Balasya Mulam Vigyanam** — not Tejasvinavadhitamastu.

ne376b1b5bd7.s: Which one of the following is the motto of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)?
ne376b1b5bd7.x: DRDO's motto is 'Balasya Mulam Vigyanam' ('the source of strength is science'), the answer asked in RPSC 2021. Tejasvinavadhitamastu is the classic trap; it is not DRDO's motto. Yogah Karmasu Kaushalam and Satyameva Jayate are mottoes of other bodies, not DRDO.
ne376b1b5bd7.tq: DRDO: strength comes from science = Balasya Mulam Vigyanam.
xs: DRDO's motto is "**Balasya Mulam Vigyanam**" ("the source of strength is science") — option **(1)** (RPSC **2021**).
⚠ **Tejasvinavadhitamastu** is the classic trap — it is **not** DRDO's motto.
xa: DRDO HQ: **DRDO Bhawan, New Delhi**.
DRDO's parent: **Department of Defence R&D**, **Ministry of Defence**.
Chairman: **Dr Samir V. Kamat** (since **2022**).

n6c4537eed58.s: Rustom/TAPAS BH-201, Nishant and Lakshya are associated with which DRDO laboratory?
o: Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics
n6c4537eed58.x: The Aeronautical Development Establishment (ADE), Bengaluru works on UAVs such as Rustom/TAPAS BH-201, Nishant and the Lakshya target drone.
n6c4537eed58.tq: Separate the DRDO laboratory ADE from the autonomous society ADA.
xs: **Rustom/TAPAS BH-201**, **Nishant** and **Lakshya** are from the **Aeronautical Development Establishment (ADE)** — option **(1)**.
⚠ **ADA** (Aeronautical Development **Agency**) is not a DRDO lab — it designs **LCA Tejas**.
xa: ADE is in **Bengaluru**; Rustom/TAPAS is a **MALE** UAV.
**Lakshya** is a **target drone**.
ADE is in the **Aeronautics** cluster with GTRE, CABS, ADRDE.

n43d798ebb74.s: The Secretary, Department of Defence R&D, also serves as:
n43d798ebb74.x: In the hierarchy, the Secretary DD R&D is also Chairman DRDO, above the Director Generals and lab directors.
xa: Level I: Secretary DD R&D and Chairman DRDO.
Level II: **DG (Technology Clusters)** and **DG (Corporate)**.
Level III: directors of labs/establishments and corporate directorates.

n159b76954b1.s: Who is the Chairman of DRDO, as stated for February 2026?
n159b76954b1.x: Dr Samir V. Kamat has been Chairman of DRDO since 2022 and was still in office in February 2026.
n159b76954b1.tq: Use the current office-holder detail rather than the names of former scientific administrators.
xs: **Dr Samir V. Kamat** is DRDO Chairman — option **(4)**.
He has held the post **since 2022** and was in office in **Feb 2026**.
xa: The Chairman is also **Secretary, Department of Defence R&D**.
He received an **honorary doctorate** from **SRM University-AP** (**15 Feb 2026**).
At SRM University-AP he cited **5 newly established labs** and **15 new DRDO centres**.

ndc77f85daee.s: In DRDO's three-level leadership structure, Level II consists of:
o: The Secretary, DDR&D, who is also Chairman of DRDO
The Defence Minister and the Secretary, DDR&D
ndc77f85daee.x: Level I is the Secretary DDR&D and Chairman, Level II the two DGs, and Level III the lab directors and corporate directorates.
xa: Each technology cluster is headed by a **Director General**.
Lab directors report to their cluster DG.
Chairman: **Dr Samir V. Kamat**.

nd5cba30bd56.s: The Technology Development Fund (TDF), a Ministry of Defence programme executed by DRDO, is implemented under:
nd5cba30bd56.x: TDF is a Ministry of Defence flagship programme executed by DRDO under the Make in India initiative.
xa: Industry (**MSMEs + start-ups**) gets a **grant of up to ₹50 crore**.
New TDF policies target **deep-tech and cutting-edge technologies**.
DRDO also gives **royalty-free** access to its patents (since **2020**).

ne6bfccbf1a2.s: The Pinaka system was designed by which DRDO laboratory?
ne6bfccbf1a2.x: ARDE, Pune (guns, ammunition, warheads) designed Pinaka, with HEMRL, Pune as partner.
xa: ARDE and HEMRL form the **Armaments & Combat Engineering** cluster.
NSTL makes **torpedoes, mines, AUVs**.
**VRDE** (**Ahmednagar**) handles vehicles.

ne0818342743.s: DIPAS, the DRDO laboratory that studies soldier physiology at high altitude and in cold, is located in:
ne0818342743.x: DIPAS is in Delhi; Dehradun hosts DEAL.
xa: **CAIR** (Bengaluru) = AI and robotics; **ADE** (Bengaluru) = UAVs.
**INMAS** also made the **bike ambulance**.
**DFRL**, Mysuru makes **Meals Ready to Eat**.

nfa508df9563.s: Which DRDO laboratory works on fuel-cell Air Independent Propulsion (AIP)?
nfa508df9563.x: Fuel-cell AIP is NMRL's work; NPOL, Kochi works on sonars.
xa: **DEAL** (**Dehradun**) = communication.
**VRDE** (**Ahmednagar**) = vehicles.
NPOL and NMRL are in the **Naval Systems & Materials** cluster.

nb182c9fd57a.s: The CBRN Field Training Centre under INMAS, Delhi trains personnel of:
nb182c9fd57a.x: The centre trains personnel of the Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Home Affairs and National Disaster Management Authority in CBRN preparedness.
xa: **INMAS** = **Institute of Nuclear Medicine & Allied Sciences**, **Delhi** — nuclear medicine and **CBRN protection**.
INMAS also made the **bike ambulance** and, with **Dr Reddy's Laboratories**, the anti-COVID drug **2-DG** (**2021**).
**DIPAS**, also in **Delhi**, studies soldier physiology (high altitude, cold).

n3c903f98daa.s: Which one of the following combinations contains only DRDO-designed systems identified as contributing to defence self-reliance?
o: INS Vikrant, INS Viraat, INS Khanderi and Admiral Gorshkov
Agni, Prithvi, Tejas, Pinaka and Akash
n3c903f98daa.x: DRDO designed or contributed to systems including Agni, Prithvi, Tejas, Pinaka and Akash, forming part of the foundation of Aatmanirbharta in defence.
n3c903f98daa.tq: Select the group whose members belong to the same indigenous DRDO-design category.
xs: **Agni, Prithvi, Tejas, Pinaka and Akash** are DRDO-designed systems that anchor **Aatmanirbharta** — option **(4)**.
The notes list DRDO flagships: Agni & Prithvi, Tejas, Pinaka, Akash, **BrahMos**, **ASAT**, **AEW&C**, **Arjun**, **Varunastra**.
The other options are not DRDO designs listed in the notes.
xa: **Pinaka** was designed by **ARDE, Pune**, with **HEMRL** as partner.
**Arjun** tank: **CVRDE, Chennai**; **Varunastra** torpedo: **NSTL, Visakhapatnam**.
**LCA Tejas** is designed by **ADA** with DRDO — ⚠ ADA is not a DRDO lab.
The **Agni** series is the field of **ASL, Hyderabad**.

n04db5dbb391.s: DRDO Industry Academia Centres of Excellence (DIA-CoEs), set up at premier institutions such as IITs and IISc, number:
n04db5dbb391.x: DIA-CoEs are a network of 15 centres at premier institutions working on critical and futuristic defence technologies.
xa: DIA-CoE = **DRDO Industry Academia Centres of Excellence**.
**JCBCAT** at **Jadavpur University** was set up with DRDO support.
Academia handles **early-stage R&D**; labs, start-ups & MSMEs take products to deployment.

n5831e85e515.s: The Agnishodh research cell is associated with:
o: The Indian Army at IIT Madras
The Indian Air Force at IISc Bengaluru
The Indian Navy at IIT Delhi
n5831e85e515.x: Agnishodh is the Indian Army's research cell at IIT Madras and links Army requirements with academic research and development.
n5831e85e515.tq: Discriminate among closely related military–academic research arrangements.
xs: **Agnishodh** is the **Indian Army's research cell** at **IIT Madras** — option **(1)** (PYQ **2025**).
It links **Army** needs to academic R&D.
xa: ⚠ **Agnishodh** = **Army** cell (not DRDO); **JCBCAT** = **DRDO**.
**DIA-CoEs** sit at IITs, IISc and central universities.
**DIAT, Pune** = DRDO's deemed university.

nad283435bd1.s: The Jagadis Chandra Bose Centre for Advanced Technology (JCBCAT) at Jadavpur University, Kolkata, was set up with the support of:
nad283435bd1.x: JCBCAT was set up at Jadavpur University with the support of DRDO (APPSC-G1 2018). ISRO, BARC and CSIR were the distractors in that question; none of them set it up.
xs: **JCBCAT** at **Jadavpur University, Kolkata** was set up with **DRDO** support — option **(4)** (APPSC-G1 **2018**).
It was **not** set up by **ISRO**, **BARC** or **CSIR**.
xa: It is also spelt **Jagadis Chandra Bose Centre for Advanced Technology**.
⚠ **Agnishodh** (IIT Madras) is the **Army**'s, not DRDO's.
**DIA-CoEs**: network of **15**.

n156da04a235.s: The oral anti-COVID drug 2-DG was developed by INMAS in association with:
n156da04a235.x: 2-DG was developed by INMAS with Dr Reddy's Laboratories.
xa: INMAS also made the **bike ambulance**.
**DEBEL** made **medical oxygen plants** during COVID.
INMAS runs the **CBRN Field Training Centre** in **Delhi**.

nd5c63312089.s: The bike ambulance was developed by which DRDO laboratory?
nd5c63312089.x: INMAS developed the bike ambulance; DEBEL made the medical oxygen plant and DRL, Tezpur the snake repellent.
xa: ⚠ NETRA mini-UAV ≠ **Netra AEW&C** (airborne early-warning aircraft).
DEBEL also makes **underwater breathing apparatus** and an **air sterilisation unit**.
⚠ **Nocdurna** is not a DRDO product.

nc7e20b86288.s: NETRA, referred to in the context of civilian applications, is best described as a:
o: Mini-UAV for police and disaster management
nc7e20b86288.x: NETRA or Netra V2 is a mini-UAV intended for police and disaster-management applications. It should not be confused with Netra AEW&C, the airborne early-warning aircraft.
nc7e20b86288.tq: Discriminate between two look-alike names by focusing on the platform and its use.
xs: Civilian **NETRA (Netra V2)** is a **mini-UAV for police and disaster management** — option **(4)**.
⚠ It is not **Netra AEW&C**, the **airborne early-warning aircraft**.
xa: It was made by **DRDO with IdeaForge** (LENS Jun **2025**).
**ADE** builds UAVs like **Rustom/TAPAS** and **Nishant**.
DRDO flagships include **AEW&C**.

n4d367872116.s: Since 2020, Indian industry gets ____ access to DRDO patents through Transfer of Technology.
n4d367872116.x: Since 2020 access to DRDO patents is royalty-free; DRDO has given more than 2,100 free ToTs and opened its test facilities to the private sector.
xa: MoD approved ToT of **all DRDO conventional missiles** (Astra, Rudram, Nag, VSHORADS) in Aug 2026.
Nuclear-capable **Agni** and **K-series** stay in state production.
**TDF** gives industry a **grant of up to ₹50 crore**.

nf56a57bb737.s: Which of the following groups consists only of conventional DRDO missiles approved for technology transfer to private industry in August 2026?
nf56a57bb737.x: The approved conventional-missile group comprises Astra, Rudram, Nag and VSHORADS. Nuclear-capable Agni and K-series missiles remain in state production.
nf56a57bb737.tq: Separate the approved conventional group from the excluded strategic missiles.
xs: The conventional missiles approved for ToT are **Astra, Rudram, Nag and VSHORADS** — option **(1)**.
Nuclear-capable **Agni** and **K-series** stay in **state production** (**30 Aug 2026**).
xa: **ASL, Hyderabad** develops the **Agni series**.
**2,100+** free ToTs covering **132+** systems so far.
DRDO patents are **royalty-free** for industry since **2020**.

nd28d8ae867e.s: Under DRDO's Technology Development Fund, the grant to industry, including MSMEs and start-ups, may extend up to:
nd28d8ae867e.x: TDF grants extend up to ₹50 crore to support co-development of emerging technologies.
xa: TDF is a **Ministry of Defence** flagship programme **executed by DRDO** under **Make in India**.
DRDO has given **2,100+ free ToTs** to Indian industry, covering **132+ systems**.
In **Aug 2026** the MoD approved **ToT of all DRDO conventional missiles** (Astra, Rudram, Nag, VSHORADS) to private industry.
⚠ Nuclear-capable **Agni** and **K-series** missiles stay in **state production**.

n46a6b59c65f.s: Nagayalanka in Krishna district is associated with which of the following?
o: A CBRN training centre for national agencies
A naval weapons laboratory for underwater batteries
An aircraft integration complex for flight testing
A DRDO missile test range for flight trials of tactical missiles
n46a6b59c65f.x: Nagayalanka in coastal Krishna district is the site of DRDO's planned missile test range for flight trials of tactical missiles. NSTL Visakhapatnam is the naval weapons lab, the ADA flight-testing complex is in Sri Sathya Sai district, and the CBRN Field Training Centre is in Delhi.
n46a6b59c65f.tq: Distinguish the planned coastal range from the other AP facilities.
xs: **Nagayalanka** (Krishna district, coastal AP) is the site of a **DRDO missile test range** for **flight trials of tactical missiles** — option **(4)**.
The **naval weapons lab** (underwater batteries) is **NSTL, Visakhapatnam**.
The **aircraft integration complex** is the **ADA** complex in **Sri Sathya Sai district**; the **CBRN Field Training Centre** is in **Delhi** under **INMAS**.
xa: The other AP test range is **near Kurnool**, where **ULPGM-V3** final trials were completed (**21 May 2026**).
The **ADA Aircraft Integration & Flight Testing Complex** involves an investment of **₹15,803 crore**.
The nearest missile complex is in **Hyderabad (Telangana)**: **DRDL, RCI, ASL**.

n6a19e734727.s: Which DRDO laboratory is located at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh?
n6a19e734727.x: NSTL is at Visakhapatnam; other AP defence locations include the Kurnool test range, the planned Nagayalanka range and the ADA complex in Sri Sathya Sai district.
xa: AP is pushing to become a **defence-manufacturing hub** with **BDL, Kalyani, HFCL** units (**May 2026**).
The DRDO chairman got an **honorary doctorate** from **SRM University-AP** (**15 Feb 2026**).
Chairman **Dr Samir V. Kamat** (since **2022**) announced **5 newly established labs** and **15 new DRDO centres**.

n3d2d89c132b.s: Which of the following correctly represents the Hyderabad missile-laboratory cluster?
o: ARDE, HEMRL, NSTL, CAIR and ADE
LRDE, CVRDE, VRDE, DEAL and NPOL
DFRL, INMAS, DIPAS, DIPR and NMRL
DRDL, RCI, ASL, DMRL and DLRL
n3d2d89c132b.x: DRDL, RCI, ASL, DMRL and DLRL are all located in Hyderabad. They cover missile development, guidance, ballistic missiles, materials and electronic warfare.
n3d2d89c132b.tq: Use a group-location question to identify the complete cluster rather than one laboratory.
xs: The Hyderabad missile hub is **DRDL, RCI, ASL, DMRL and DLRL** — option **(4)**.
**ARDE/HEMRL** are in **Pune**; **LRDE/CAIR/ADE** in **Bengaluru**; **NSTL** in **Visakhapatnam**.
xa: They cover missiles, guidance, Agni-series, metals and electronic warfare.
Hyderabad (Telangana) neighbours AP's DRDO facilities.
**DFRL** is at **Mysuru**.

n509725ec88d.s: The Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA), which designs the LCA Tejas with DRDO, is:
o: An autonomous society under the Ministry of Defence
A directorate of the Indian Air Force
n509725ec88d.x: ADA is an autonomous society under the Ministry of Defence, not itself a DRDO laboratory.
xa: ADA = **Aeronautical Development Agency**.
**ADA Aircraft Integration & Flight Testing Complex** in **Sri Sathya Sai district** — **₹15,803 crore** (**21 May 2026**).
⚠ **ADE** (Establishment) is the DRDO UAV lab.

n3fae4d2aade.s: Which one of the following is NOT a DRDO product among the products listed below?
n3fae4d2aade.x: Nocdurna is a commercial drug and is not a DRDO product. Lukoskin, Amtooth and Eczit are DRDO-associated civilian products.
n3fae4d2aade.tq: Identify the outsider from a group of products associated with DRDO civilian spin-offs.
xs: **Nocdurna** is **not** a DRDO product — it is a **commercial drug** — option **(3)**.
**Amtooth**, **Eczit** and **Lukoskin** are herbal products of **DIBER**.
xa: Lukoskin treats **leucoderma**; Amtooth = toothache; Eczit = eczema.
DIBER is at **Haldwani**.
**2-DG** is DRDO's anti-COVID drug (**2021**).

nefd18a80cb8.s: Under the IGMDP, which missile was developed during the 1992–2008 phase?
nefd18a80cb8.x: Prithvi and Trishul were developed in 1984–89, Nag and Akash in 1989–92, and Agni in 1992–2008.
xa: IGMDP was **launched in 1983** under **Dr APJ Abdul Kalam**.
After **2008**, later missiles were developed as **separate projects**.
⚠ **Trishul**, from the first phase, was the IGMDP missile **never inducted**.

n32ce6f9373c.s: The nodal laboratory of the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP) was:
n32ce6f9373c.x: DRDL, Hyderabad was the nodal lab, working with RCI and ASL; IGMDP was launched in 1983 under Kalam.
xa: Phases: **1984-89** Prithvi + Trishul; **1989-92** Nag + Akash; **1992-2008** Agni.
Spin-offs: **ring laser gyros**, composites, radomes.
⚠ **BrahMos** was **not part of IGMDP**.

n6f4c3956794.s: Under the Ministry of Defence approval, technology of conventional missiles such as Nag is transferred to:
n6f4c3956794.x: Conventional missiles, including Nag, go to private industry, while Agni remains in state production.
xa: **Nag**: **4-7 km**, **fire-and-forget**, **IIR** seeker.
**Agni** is operated by the **Strategic Forces Command**.
Agni is built by **DRDO** — ⚠ not ISRO.

n9c185d9ab12.s: Akash, a medium-range surface-to-air missile, travels at a speed of about:
n9c185d9ab12.x: Akash is a medium-range SAM with a range of about 25-30 km, a speed of about Mach 2.5 and an altitude capability of 18 km.
xa: Base Akash: launch weight **720 kg**.
**Akash Prime**: indigenous **active RF seeker**; **Akash-NG**: about **70 km**, canister-launched.
⚠ **Akashteer** (BEL + Army) is an air-defence **control** system, NOT a missile.

n89bf05c0d91.s: Which missile has a range of about 25–30 km?
n89bf05c0d91.x: Akash has about 25–30 km; Nag is 4–7 km, Trishul about 9 km, and Agni ranges from about 700 km to over 5,000 km.
xa: ⚠ Older notes give **Nag** as **0.5-4 km** and **Trishul** as **12 km**.
**Prithvi**: **150-350 km**, liquid fuel.
**Agni** is solid-fuelled and operated by the **Strategic Forces Command**.

n338448e6b8f.s: Agni-VI, in the context of India’s missile programme, is described as a:
n338448e6b8f.x: Agni-VI is described as a proposed longer-range intercontinental ballistic missile.
n338448e6b8f.tq: Distinguish a proposed future system from operational Agni variants.
xs: **Agni-VI** is a **proposed longer-range ICBM** — option **(1)**.
The **naval version of Prithvi** is **Dhanush**; the interceptor is **PAD / Pradyumna**.
xa: **Agni-V**: **5,000+ km**, below the **5,500 km** ICBM threshold, so formally **IRBM** class.
Agni is developed by **DRDO** — ⚠ not ISRO (APPSC **2019**).
**Agni-P (Prime)**: **1,000-2,000 km**, new-generation **canisterised**.

n48dae472f15.s: India's Agni missiles, built by DRDO, are operated by the:
n48dae472f15.x: Agni is DRDO-built, fully indigenous and operated by the Strategic Forces Command.
xa: In **Aug 2026**, conventional missiles (incl. **Nag**) went to private industry via ToT; **Agni** stays in **state production**.
Agni means **Fire**.
**Mission Divyastra (2024)**: Agni-V with **MIRV**.

n8ccab3d44f6.s: The Trishul surface-to-air missile programme was shut down in:
n8ccab3d44f6.x: Trishul was never inducted; the programme was shut on 27 February 2008.
xa: ⚠ Replacements: **Spyder** (IAF), **Barak-1** (Navy), **Akash** (Army).
Indigenous successor: **QRSAM**.
Trishul's range: ~**9 km** (some notes **12 km**).

n9c413a318dc.s: What is meant by the term 'fire-and-forget' in missile technology?
o: The missile is incapable of changing its course after launch.
The missile can guide itself after launch, allowing the operator to take cover.
The missile is fired only after the target has been destroyed by another weapon.
The missile must remain continuously controlled by the operator until impact.
n9c413a318dc.x: A fire-and-forget missile guides itself after launch, enabling the operator to seek cover or perform another task.
n9c413a318dc.tq: Translate the technical term into its operational consequence.
xs: **Fire-and-forget**: the missile **guides itself after launch**, so the operator can **take cover** — option **(2)**.
Examples: **Nag**, **HELINA**, **MPATGM**.
xa: **Top attack**: missile climbs, then dives onto the tank's thin **top armour**.
**Nag** has both **top-attack** and **direct-attack** modes.
Nag is a **third-generation** fire-and-forget ATGM (APPSC-G1 **2018** key).

ne0a9de3f972.s: Which one of the following is NOT an identified spin-off of the IGMDP?
ne0a9de3f972.x: Long-range tracking systems, composites, ring laser gyros and radomes were identified as IGMDP spin-offs. A satellite-based navigation constellation is not included in this list.
ne0a9de3f972.tq: Find the item outside the stated group of technological spin-offs.
xs: A **satellite-based navigation constellation** is not listed among IGMDP spin-offs — option **(1)**.
The listed spin-offs are the **long-range tracking system**, **composites**, **ring laser gyros** and **radomes**.
xa: **Agni-IV** uses a **ring-laser-gyro INS** with **RINS + MINGS** navigation.
IGMDP was **launched in 1983** and **completed in 2008**.
Nodal lab: **DRDL Hyderabad**.

n86bdb413548.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam?
o: He was project director of SLV-III
SLV-III, under his direction, launched Rohini
He was the first Indian Head of State to fly a fighter aircraft
He was Chief Scientific Adviser at the 1974 Pokhran-I test
n86bdb413548.x: Kalam was Chief Scientific Adviser at Pokhran-II in 1998, not Pokhran-I in 1974.
xa: Kalam led **IGMDP** from **1983** and is called the "**Missile Man of India**".
⚠ **Dr Tessy Thomas** = "**Missile Woman of India**" / **Agniputri**.
**Pokhran Field Firing Range** is in **Rajasthan**.

n1289a739e71.s: The first missile developed under the IGMDP was:
n1289a739e71.x: Prithvi was the first IGMDP missile; Prithvi-I serves the Army and Prithvi-II the Air Force.
xa: **Prithvi-III / Dhanush** serves the **Navy** (ship-launched).
Prithvi-II was **first tested in 1996** and **inducted in 2003**.
Prithvi-II and Agni-I were **test-fired together** (**Jul 2025**).

n9d4f984505b.x: Prithvi-I and Prithvi-II use liquid fuel, whereas Agni-I uses solid fuel.
xa: Prithvi-II and Agni-I were test-fired together in **Jul 2025**.
**Agni-I**: single-stage solid, about **700-800 km**, about **15 m** long.
An **Agni-1** test was held at **ITR Balasore** on **22 May 2026**.

n53458ef7c95.s: Agni-I is best described as a:
o: Two-stage liquid-fuel missile of about 2,000–3,000 km range
Single-stage solid-fuel missile of about 700–800 km range
Single-stage liquid-fuel missile of about 150 km range
Three-stage solid-fuel missile of about 5,000 km range
n53458ef7c95.x: Agni-I is a single-stage solid-fuel missile with a range of about 700–800 km and is approximately 15 metres long.
n53458ef7c95.tq: Identify the missile from its stage, fuel and range combination.
xs: **Agni-I** is a **single-stage solid-fuel** missile of about **700-800 km** range — option **(2)**.
It is about **15 m** long, with accurate navigation.
**2,000-3,000 km** is **Agni-II** (two-stage solid); **150 km** liquid is **Prithvi-I**; **5,000 km** three-stage is **Agni-V**.
xa: Agni-I is **nuclear-capable**, fired by the Army from **road-mobile TEL** trucks.
Agni-I test: **ITR Balasore**, **22 May 2026**.
⚠ Some notes give Agni-I as **~700-900 km** (SRBM/MRBM).

n66753ff1cef.s: Agni-V is a ____-stage, solid-fuel, canister-launched missile.
n66753ff1cef.x: Agni-V is a three-stage solid-fuel, canister-launched missile with a stated range of 5,000 km or more; MIRV has been tested with it.
xa: Agni-V is **fully indigenous** — ⚠ "not exclusively indigenous" is the wrong statement (UPPSC **2015**).
**Dr Tessy Thomas** played a key role in Agni-V.
⚠ Formally **IRBM** class: the ICBM threshold is **5,500 km**.

nf3a81ce506e.s: On 24 September 2025, Agni-Prime was test-fired from a:
nf3a81ce506e.x: Agni-Prime, a canisterised 1,000–2,000 km missile, was fired from a rail-based mobile launcher.
xa: Agni series operator: **Strategic Forces Command**.
**Agni-4** user trial: **ITR Chandipur, 6 Aug 2026**.
An advanced Agni with **MIRV** was tested on **8 May 2026**.

nbcfa86b6d5f.s: Mission Divyastra (2024) tested MIRV technology on which missile?
nbcfa86b6d5f.x: Mission Divyastra, conducted in 2024, flight-tested Agni-V with Multiple Independently targetable Re-entry Vehicles (MIRVs).
xa: Advanced Agni with a **MIRV** was tested on **8 May 2026**.
Agni-V: **three-stage solid**, **canister-launched**, **5,000+ km**.
All 2026 Agni tests were under the **Strategic Forces Command**.

n56a11f51df5.s: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island, used for missile trials, lies off the coast of:
n56a11f51df5.x: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island is off the Odisha coast; ranges on the AP and Odisha coasts support sea-skimming trials such as LRAShM.
xa: Kalam Island was formerly **Wheeler Island**.
**ITR Chandipur** is at **Balasore, Odisha**.
**Kurnool** range in AP: **ULPGM-V3** trials.

n64b5b9a13ab.x: Lakshya is a target drone; Pinaka is a rocket launcher, Tejas an aircraft and Nishant a UAV.
xa: **Arjun** = tank; **Rustom** = UAV; **NAMICA** = Nag carrier vehicle.
⚠ **BrahMos** was **not part of IGMDP**.

n2b7bd4e4fc9.s: The Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme is regarded as significant because it:
o: Ended all missile development in India after the completion of Prithvi.
Turned India from a missile importer into a missile-exporting power and formed a base for later Agni-V MIRV, BMD and BrahMos-era programmes.
Restricted India to importing surface-to-air missiles from foreign suppliers.
Was created exclusively for developing civilian launch vehicles.
n2b7bd4e4fc9.x: The IGMDP transformed India from a missile importer into a missile-exporting power and provided the foundation for Agni-V MIRV, ballistic missile defence and BrahMos-era programmes.
n2b7bd4e4fc9.tq: Select the option that captures both the strategic transformation and the later technological base.
xs: IGMDP turned India from a **missile importer** into a **missile-exporting power**, and laid the base for **Agni-V MIRV, BMD and BrahMos-era programmes** — option **(2)**.
Missile work did not end: after **2008**, later missiles came as **separate projects**.
xa: Launched in **1983** under **Dr APJ Abdul Kalam**, after the **1962, 1965, 1971** wars.
**Mission Divyastra (2024)**: Agni-V with **MIRV**.
Spin-offs: **long-range tracking system**, **composites**, **ring laser gyros**, **radomes**.

n1ead5f0015a.s: Prithvi-II, first tested in 1996, was inducted in:
n1ead5f0015a.x: Prithvi-II was inducted in 2003; the naval version is Dhanush.
xa: Prithvi-II: **350 km**, payload **500-1,000 kg**, **nuclear-capable SRBM**.
Dhanush means **Bow**.
**PAD / Pradyumna** is the Prithvi-based exo-atmospheric interceptor.

n8e3a67fbd28.s: Akash Prime, an upgraded Akash Mk-I with an indigenous active RF seeker, was first tested on:
n8e3a67fbd28.x: Akash Prime was first tested on 27 September 2021.
xa: Akash Prime destroyed high-speed targets at high altitude in **Ladakh**.
Base Akash: **Mach 2.5**, altitude **18 km**.
⚠ **Akashteer** is an air-defence **control** system, not a missile.

n6a12a10e0b4.s: The canister-launched Akash-NG has an approximate range of:
n6a12a10e0b4.x: Akash-NG has a range of about 70 km and was cleared for induction in 2023 for the Army and IAF.
xa: **Akash Mk-I** ~**25 km**; **Akash Prime** **25-30 km**; **Akash S1** **30-35 km**.
Base Akash: **Mach 2.5**, **18 km** altitude.
Akash means **Sky**.

na0871e4df8c.s: The later indigenous short-range successor to Trishul is known as:
na0871e4df8c.x: QRSAM, or Quick Reaction Surface-to-Air Missile, is the later indigenous short-range successor to Trishul.
na0871e4df8c.tq: Distinguish the indigenous successor from the Service-specific replacement systems.
xs: The indigenous successor to Trishul is **QRSAM** (Quick Reaction SAM) — option **(4)**.
**Barak-1** was the **Navy**'s replacement (imported); **Prithvi** is a ballistic missile.
⚠ **BrahMos** (India-Russia) was **not part of IGMDP**.
xa: Other replacements: **Spyder** (IAF), **Akash** (Army).
Trishul: quick-reaction SAM, **above Mach 2**, never inducted.

nfa05b856456.s: Nag Mk-2, the tracked fire-and-forget 'tank killer' approved for Army procurement, is called:
nfa05b856456.x: NAMIS is the tracked Nag Mk-2; Dhruvastra is the IAF's helicopter-launched Nag, HELINA the Army Aviation version and SANT an air-launched stand-off ATGM.
xa: **NAMICA** = tracked amphibious **Nag Missile Carrier**, carries up to **six** missiles.
**HELINA** (about **7 km**) is for **Army Aviation**.
**SANT** range: **15-20 km**.

nf78199a5290.s: HELINA, the helicopter-launched variant of the Nag missile, is meant for:
nf78199a5290.x: HELINA is the helicopter-launched Nag variant for Army Aviation, whereas Dhruvastra is intended for the Indian Air Force.
xa: ⚠ Remember: **HELINA** = Army Aviation; **Dhruvastra** = IAF.
HELINA is a **fire-and-forget** missile, like Nag and MPATGM.
**SANT** is the **air-launched stand-off** ATGM (**15-20 km**).

nacb770d9cb3.s: HELINA is the helicopter-launched version of which missile?
nacb770d9cb3.x: HELINA is the helicopter-launched Nag, a fire-and-forget anti-tank missile.
xa: Nag: **IIR** seeker and an **8 kg HEAT tandem warhead**.
**NAMIS** (Nag Mk-2) is also fire-and-forget — the tracked "**tank killer**".
⚠ "Which is a fire-and-forget anti-tank missile?" → **Nag** (not Prithvi, Akash or Trishul).

nee65fc4655d.s: Each Nag Missile Carrier (NAMICA) can carry up to how many missiles?
nee65fc4655d.x: Each NAMICA, a tracked amphibious vehicle, can carry up to six Nag missiles.
xa: Nag is a **third-generation fire-and-forget ATGM** (APPSC-G1 **2018** key), range **4-7 km**.
Its **Imaging Infra-Red (IIR)** seeker gives **night-strike** capability.
**Nag Mk-2 / NAMIS** — tracked "**tank killer**", approved for Army procurement (**2026**).
⚠ NAMICA is a **carrier vehicle**, not a missile.

n0909d88a39a.s: Dr Tessy Thomas, who played a key role in Agni-V, is popularly called:
n0909d88a39a.x: Dr Tessy Thomas, the 'Missile Woman of India', played a key role in Agni-V and is called 'Agniputri'.
xa: **Agni-V**: **three-stage solid**, **canister-launched**, range **5,000+ km**, **MIRV** tested.
**Mission Divyastra (2024)** tested Agni-V with **MIRVs**.
Agni is operated by the **Strategic Forces Command**.

n23c8ba2e60f.s: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island was formerly known as:
n23c8ba2e60f.x: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island was formerly known as Wheeler Island and lies off the Odisha coast.
n23c8ba2e60f.tq: Recognise the renamed test location from its former name.
xs: **Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island** was formerly **Wheeler Island** — option **(4)**.
It lies **off the Odisha coast**.
**Chandipur** is the **Integrated Test Range** at Balasore; **Pokhran** is a field firing range in Rajasthan.
xa: **Agni-4** user trial: **ITR Chandipur**, **6 Aug 2026**.
**Agni-1** test: **ITR Balasore**, **22 May 2026**.
Kalam is the "**Missile Man of India**", who led IGMDP from **1983**.

ndfde582b6f3.s: A missile that stays powered throughout its flight and uses aerodynamic lift at relatively low altitude is a:
ndfde582b6f3.x: A cruise missile is powered throughout; a ballistic missile is powered mainly in boost phase and then follows a high parabolic arc.
xa: Ballistic examples: **Agni**, **Prithvi**, **Pralay**.
Cruise examples: **BrahMos**, **Nirbhay**.
⚠ **Pralay** is **quasi-ballistic** with **manoeuvrable re-entry**.

naa392915f9d.s: Hypersonic speed means speed faster than:
naa392915f9d.x: Hypersonic means faster than Mach 5; a Hypersonic Glide Vehicle glides at Mach 5+ while manoeuvring.
xa: **HSTDV** = indigenous **scramjet** demonstrator, flew at **Mach 6+**.
**LR-AShM**: ~**1,500 km**, peak **Mach 10**, average **Mach 5**.
India's **first long-range hypersonic missile** flew on **16 Nov 2024**.

n01a27baf709.s: A scramjet engine is characterised by:
o: Subsonic combustion after the air is slowed down
Supersonic combustion and no rotating parts
Carrying all the oxygen needed for combustion
n01a27baf709.x: A scramjet uses supersonic combustion and has no rotating compressor or turbine parts; unlike a rocket, it does not carry its oxidiser.
xa: HSTDV flew at **Mach 6+**, with thermal protection above **2,000°C**.
**Jan 2026**: a scramjet combustor ran **over 12 minutes**.
Compare **SFDR** (solid fuel ducted ramjet): also uses **atmospheric air** for combustion.

n7a4c9c60761.s: Solid Fuel Ducted Ramjet (SFDR) technology is intended mainly for
n7a4c9c60761.x: SFDR uses atmospheric air for combustion and was demonstrated from ITR Chandipur for application in long-range air-to-air missiles.
n7a4c9c60761.tq: Match the propulsion system with its stated operational application.
xs: **SFDR** (solid fuel ducted ramjet) is meant for **long-range air-to-air missiles** — option **(2)**.
It uses **atmospheric air for combustion** and was demonstrated from **ITR Chandipur**.
xa: **Astra Mk-3 'Gandiva'** is being built with an **SFDR** engine, range **350+ km**.
⚠ **BrahMos** uses a **liquid ramjet**; SFDR is a **solid fuel** ramjet.
**Astra Mk-2** uses a **dual-pulse solid motor** (about **200 km**).

n5b146a66e6d.s: In BrahMos Aerospace, DRDO holds a share of:
n5b146a66e6d.x: DRDO holds 50.5% and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya 49.5%.
xa: BrahMos's first successful test: **12 June 2001**, **Chandipur**.
BrahMos is an **India-Russia** joint venture (APPSC-G2 2025 key).
**Philippines** = first BrahMos export customer, **$375 million** deal (**2022**).

nc9f27d80c38.s: BrahMos had its first successful test on 12 June 2001 at:
nc9f27d80c38.x: BrahMos, a supersonic cruise missile of about Mach 2.8–3.0, was first successfully tested at Chandipur, Odisha.
xa: Propulsion: **solid booster → liquid ramjet**.
Range: **290 km** originally, **290-400 km** in extended versions.
**BrahMos-NG** is lighter (**about 1.5 t**); **BrahMos-II** is planned **hypersonic**.
First reported combat use: **Operation Sindoor** (May 2025).

n37837482888.s: BrahMos uses a solid booster followed by a:
n37837482888.x: BrahMos has a solid booster and a liquid ramjet, combines inertial and satellite navigation, and is canister-launched in fire-and-forget mode.
xa: It cruises at ~**15 km** and dives to **10 m** in the terminal phase.
It has a **low radar cross-section**.
⚠ **Nirbhay** uses a **turbojet**, not a ramjet.

n93e28480ec6.s: Which BrahMos variant is a planned hypersonic missile capable of speeds above Mach 5?
n93e28480ec6.x: BrahMos-II is the planned hypersonic variant; BrahMos-NG is a lighter version for platforms such as Tejas.
xa: **P-17A frigates** carry BrahMos.
BrahMos-NG flies at about **Mach 3.5**.
**Land-attack** BrahMos uses **mobile launchers** (Army).

n3d48a889988.s: BrahMos was reportedly used in combat for the first time during:
n3d48a889988.x: The first reported combat use of BrahMos was during Operation Sindoor in May 2025.
n3d48a889988.tq: Link the operation name with its reported year and avoid substituting another Indian military operation.
xs: BrahMos was first reportedly used in combat in **Operation Sindoor** (**May 2025**) — option **(4)**.
The notes do not link the other operations to BrahMos.
xa: **BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility, Lucknow** was inaugurated on **11 May 2025**.
First BrahMos export: **Philippines** (**$375 million**, **2022**).
**UAE**: early-stage talks on **BrahMos** and **Akashteer** (**23 Jun 2026**).

nfee502d9128.s: The BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility inaugurated on 11 May 2025 is located at
nfee502d9128.x: The BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility at Lucknow (in the UP defence corridor) was inaugurated on 11 May 2025, with the first batch flagged off within five months. Hyderabad and Nagpur are other defence-industry centres, and Chandipur is the test range where BrahMos was first tested in 2001.
xs: The **BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility** is at **Lucknow**, inaugurated **11 May 2025** — option **(2)**.
Its **first batch** was flagged off **within five months**.
**Chandipur** is the test range where BrahMos was **first tested** (**2001**).
xa: First combat use: **Operation Sindoor** (**May 2025**).
First export customer: **Philippines**.
BrahMos-NG is meant for **Tejas**, smaller warships and submarines.

n371b98f8255.s: Nirbhay, India's subsonic long-range land-attack cruise missile, is powered by a:
n371b98f8255.x: Nirbhay is turbojet-powered; the liquid ramjet belongs to the supersonic BrahMos.
xa: Successor **ITCM** uses the indigenous **'Manik' small turbofan engine** (GTRE).
⚠ **Nirbhay** = **subsonic**; **BrahMos** = **supersonic**.
Nirbhay navigation: **inertial + GPS/NavIC**.

nd92ccdd97c6.s: Astra, developed by DRDO with an active radar seeker, is a family of:
nd92ccdd97c6.x: Astra is a DRDO-developed family of beyond-visual-range air-to-air missiles using an active radar seeker.
xa: **BVR** = engaging beyond **20 nautical miles (37 km)**.
**Astra Mk-1** is on the **Su-30MKI**, planned for **Tejas Mk-1A** and **Rafale**.
**Indonesia** is the first Astra buyer (**Jul 2026**).

n819397cbbd8.s: Astra Mk-3 'Gandiva' is powered by a:
n819397cbbd8.x: Gandiva uses an SFDR with range of 350+ km; the dual-pulse solid motor powers Astra Mk-2.
xa: Astra is a **BVRAAM** with an **active radar seeker**; BVR = beyond **20 nautical miles (37 km)**.
**Indonesia** deal (Jul 2026) = **first-ever export** of the Astra family.
Astra was test-fired from an **LCA AF Mk1** prototype on **12 Mar 2025**.

n4b6e5697a31.s: Which Indian air-defence system is man-portable, for use against low-altitude threats?
n4b6e5697a31.x: VSHORADS is the man-portable system; QRSAM is the Army's mid-range IADWS layer and VL-SRSAM a ship-borne SAM derived from Astra.
xa: **Rudram-I** = India's **first indigenous anti-radiation missile**.
**Pralay** = quasi-ballistic, **150-500 km**; salvo of two on **31 Dec 2025**.
**NASM-SR** = first indigenous **helicopter-launched anti-ship** missile.

na6045ced6f2.s: Which one of the following groups contains only missiles associated with Russia?
na6045ced6f2.x: BrahMos is a joint venture with Russia, while R-73 Archer and S-400 are Russian systems. The other groups contain missiles associated with Israel, Iran, North Korea, Pakistan or the United States.
na6045ced6f2.tq: Classify each item by partner or country before selecting the complete group.
xs: **BrahMos, R-73 Archer and S-400** are all linked to **Russia** — option **(3)**.
**Barak-1, Spyder, Barak-8** are **Israeli**; **Shahab, Fattah** are **Iranian** and **Hwasong** is **North Korean**.
**Abdali** is **Pakistani** and **Minuteman III** **American**.
xa: **Kinzhal** and **Zircon** are also Russian.
⚠ **Zircon** = ship-launched; **Kinzhal** = air-launched.
BrahMos is a **joint venture**: **DRDO 50.5%**, **NPOM 49.5%**.

ne840c2416a6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's missile exports?
o: The Philippines is India's first BrahMos export customer
BrahMos deliveries to the Philippines began in 2024
BrahMos and Akashteer have already been delivered to the UAE
The Astra Mk-1 deal with Indonesia (July 2026) is the first Astra-family export
ne840c2416a6.x: With the UAE, BrahMos and Akashteer talks are only at an early stage; nothing has been delivered.
xa: Philippines deal value: **$375 million**.
**Akashteer** is an air-defence **control** system.

ne8ad2142017.s: The Minuteman III is associated with which one of the following descriptions?
o: An American ICBM forming the land leg of the US nuclear triad
ne8ad2142017.x: Minuteman III is a United States intercontinental ballistic missile and forms the land leg of the US nuclear triad.
ne8ad2142017.tq: Identify the system from its strategic role rather than its name alone.
xs: **Minuteman III** is an **American ICBM**, the **land leg of the US triad** — option **(2)**.
The **450 km** Pakistani SSM is **Abdali**; the Russian air-launched hypersonic missile is **Kinzhal**; the Iranian claimed hypersonic is **Fattah**.
xa: **Hwasong** is North Korea's ICBM/IRBM series.
**Abdali** (Pakistan) is a **450 km** SSM named after **Ahmed Shah Abdali**.
**Jun 2026**: India's multi-layered BMD showed it can engage threats **up to ICBM class**.

n7565d12b82a.s: The Indigenous Technology Cruise Missile (ITCM), successor to Nirbhay, is powered by the:
n7565d12b82a.x: ITCM is the successor to Nirbhay and is powered by the indigenous Manik small turbofan engine developed by GTRE.
xa: The family is now called **Long-Range Land Attack Cruise Missile (LR-LACM)** (**Jun 2026**).
Nirbhay itself is **turbojet** powered.

nfc98fbcd16c.s: Which one of the following missiles is India's first indigenous anti-radiation missile designed to home passively on radar emissions?
nfc98fbcd16c.x: Rudram-I is India's first indigenous anti-radiation missile. It passively homes on radar emissions to destroy enemy radars and communication sites.
nfc98fbcd16c.tq: Identify the missile from its distinctive operational role.
xs: **Rudram-I** is India's **first indigenous anti-radiation missile** — option **(3)**.
It **homes passively on radar emissions** to **destroy enemy radars and communication sites** (APPSC-G1 **2018**).
**Pralay** is a quasi-ballistic SSM; **QRSAM** and **VSHORADS** are air-defence missiles.
xa: Rudram-I is **air-to-surface**, fired from the **Su-30MKI**, range **100-200 km**.
⚠ Rudram-I attacks **radars**; **Mission Shakti**'s interceptor attacked a **satellite**.

n0132505fab1.s: Which one of the following missiles is a canister-launched, hypersonic, nuclear-capable surface-to-surface tactical missile with a range of about 700–1,900 km?
n0132505fab1.x: Shaurya is a canister-launched hypersonic surface-to-surface tactical missile with a range of about 700–1,900 km and nuclear capability.
n0132505fab1.tq: Use the range and launch-mode clues to identify the missile.
xs: **Shaurya** is a **canister-launched hypersonic surface-to-surface** tactical missile, about **700-1,900 km**, **nuclear-capable** — option **(2)**.
**Prahaar** is ~**150 km**; **Pralay** is **150-500 km** with a conventional warhead.
xa: **Pralay**: quasi-ballistic, **manoeuvrable re-entry**; salvo on **31 Dec 2025**.
**Rudram-I**: first indigenous **anti-radiation** missile.
Hypersonic = faster than **Mach 5**.

n52f7d4ecc2e.x: Zircon is ship-launched; Kinzhal is air-launched. Hwasong is North Korean and Fattah Iranian.
xa: **Abdali** is a **Pakistan** **450 km** SSM.
**Minuteman III** is a **USA** ICBM, land leg of the US triad.
**Patriot** intercepted **six** Kinzhals in one night over **Kyiv** (May 2023).

n6c9a38c7629.s: The first flight-trial of India's long-range hypersonic missile was reported on
n6c9a38c7629.x: India's first reported flight-trial of the long-range hypersonic missile took place on 16 November 2024.
n6c9a38c7629.tq: Separate closely spaced test dates by linking each date to its specific programme.
xs: India's **first long-range hypersonic missile** had its first flight-trial on **16 November 2024** — option **(4)**.
⚠ **11 Mar 2024** is **Mission Divyastra** (first **MIRV** test on **Agni-V**).
xa: **LR-AShM**: range ~**1,500 km**, peak **Mach 10**, **two-stage solid motor**.
LR-AShM was shown at the **77th Republic Day Parade**.
AP coast ranges were used for **LRAShM** validation rounds (**Jan 2026**).

n739f987a476.s: India's long-range hypersonic anti-ship missile reportedly uses skipping manoeuvres with a peak speed of about:
n739f987a476.x: It reportedly peaks at about Mach 10, with an average speed of about Mach 5.
xa: Range: **1,500+ km**; **two-stage solid motor**.
First long-range hypersonic missile trial: **16 Nov 2024**.
⚠ **HSTDV** (**Mach 6+**) is a scramjet demonstrator, not LR-AShM.

n80edd873e68.s: Mission Shakti, the joint DRDO–ISRO anti-satellite test, was conducted on:
n80edd873e68.x: It was conducted on 27 March 2019; Microsat-R was hit in low LEO (~283 km) so the debris would decay quickly.
xa: Interceptor: DRDO **PDV Mk-II**.
India = **4th nation** with ASAT capability, after **USA, Russia and China**.
Microsat-R was launched by **PSLV-C44** in Jan **2019**.

n777fd1d84d3.s: In Mission Shakti, the live satellite Microsat-R was destroyed by which DRDO interceptor?
n777fd1d84d3.x: A DRDO PDV Mk-II interceptor destroyed the live satellite Microsat-R during Mission Shakti.
xa: Microsat-R orbited in **LEO** at about **283 km**.
Microsat-R was a **DRDO satellite** launched by **PSLV-C44** (**Jan 2019**).
⚠ Correct PYQ statement: "destroyed a **live satellite in LEO**".

n5d0495adb20.s: India became the fourth country to demonstrate an anti-satellite capability. Which of the following shows the three countries that preceded India?
n5d0495adb20.x: India became the fourth country with demonstrated ASAT capability after the USA, Russia and China.
n5d0495adb20.tq: Use the rank clue to reconstruct the preceding three countries without adding other space powers.
xs: India was the **fourth** ASAT nation, after the **USA, Russia and China** — option **(4)**.
France, Japan, UK and Israel are not named in the notes as ASAT states.
xa: ASAT = **missile-based system to attack satellites**.
India's test: **Mission Shakti**, **27 March 2019**.
Interceptor **PDV Mk-II**; target **Microsat-R**.

n0f0dbaeaa3e.s: Which of the following Indian missiles is subsonic?
n0f0dbaeaa3e.x: Nirbhay is subsonic; BrahMos is supersonic and BrahMos-II is hypersonic.
xa: ⚠ **Nirbhay** = subsonic, turbojet; **BrahMos** = supersonic, ramjet.
**LR-AShM** is also in the **hypersonic** class.
**BrahMos-NG**: lighter (**about 1.5 t**), about **Mach 3.5**.

n791b1d10a4b.s: In a fusion (thermonuclear) weapon, the fusion of light hydrogen isotopes is triggered by:
n791b1d10a4b.x: A fission 'primary' supplies the heat to trigger fusion; a fission weapon splits U-235 or Pu-239 in a chain reaction.
xa: Fission example: **Pokhran-I**; fusion was tested in **Pokhran-II**.
Pokhran-II used **five** devices, both **fission and fusion**.
Bomb detonators are fired by a **Krytron**.

n9924ef5260f.s: Pokhran-I, officially described as a peaceful nuclear explosion, was conducted on:
n9924ef5260f.x: Pokhran-I took place on 18 May 1974 under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and was described as a peaceful nuclear explosion.
xa: Pokhran-I code name: "**Smiling Buddha**"; team led by **Raja Ramanna**.
Site: **Pokhran Test Range**, **Jaisalmer district, Rajasthan**.
⚠ **Operation Shakti** (**1998**) ≠ **Mission Shakti** (**2019** ASAT).

nd557eac9d75.x: Pokhran-II (11 and 13 May 1998) was 'Operation Shakti'; Pokhran-I (1974) was 'Smiling Buddha'.
xa: Pokhran-I was a "**peaceful nuclear explosion**" under **Indira Gandhi**.
Pokhran-II: under **Vajpayee**, led by **Kalam** and **Chidambaram**.
**11 May** = **National Technology Day**.

n8c5524df915.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's nuclear doctrine?
o: No First Use was first declared by the Indira Gandhi government after Pokhran-I
The draft doctrine with No First Use came from the Vajpayee government in 1999
The draft followed the Pokhran-II tests of 1998
The Cabinet Committee on Security formally adopted it on 4 January 2003
n8c5524df915.x: NFU dates from the Vajpayee government after Pokhran-II (1998), not from Pokhran-I (1974).
xa: Tenets: **credible minimum deterrence**, **massive** retaliation, **non-use against non-nuclear-weapon states**.
The **Political Council**, chaired by the **Prime Minister**, alone can authorise use; the **Executive Council** is chaired by the **NSA**.
**Strategic Forces Command** (tri-service, **2003**) manages the nuclear arsenal.

nea02c679880.s: Which of the following is NOT a tenet of India's nuclear doctrine?
o: Use of nuclear weapons against every non-nuclear-weapon state
nea02c679880.x: The doctrine provides for no use against non-nuclear-weapon states (subject to the clause on major biological or chemical attacks).
xa: Exception: nuclear option kept against a major **biological or chemical** attack.
Continued **moratorium on testing**; strict export controls.
Support for **disarmament** and the **FMCT**.

n831403d0b79.s: India's nuclear doctrine retains the nuclear option against a major attack involving:
n831403d0b79.x: The doctrine retains the nuclear option against a major biological or chemical attack.
xa: **Non-use against non-nuclear-weapon states** is another tenet.
Retaliation will be **massive**, causing **unacceptable damage**.
Doctrine adopted by the **CCS**: **4 January 2003**.

n09ebf5acd1a.s: Under India’s No First Use policy, nuclear weapons may be used in retaliation against
o: any conventional attack on Indian territory
a nuclear attack on Indian territory or Indian forces
a cyberattack on India’s strategic infrastructure
any military alliance formed against India
n09ebf5acd1a.x: India’s No First Use policy permits nuclear weapons only in retaliation against a nuclear attack on Indian territory or Indian forces.
n09ebf5acd1a.tq: Distinguish the exact condition attached to a strategic policy from broader military contingencies.
xs: Under **No First Use**, nuclear weapons are used only in **retaliation against a nuclear attack on Indian territory or forces** — option **(2)**.
A conventional or cyberattack alone does not qualify.
xa: Exception kept: a major **biological or chemical** attack.
**Non-use against non-nuclear-weapon states**.
Retaliation is **massive**, to cause **unacceptable damage**.

n9707ee692b2.s: The next strategic step associated with India’s SSBN-based deterrence is
o: ending the No First Use policy
replacement of all missiles by free-fall bombs
n9707ee692b2.x: Continuous at-sea deterrence is identified as the next step in strengthening India’s SSBN-based nuclear deterrence.
n9707ee692b2.tq: Identify the policy objective that follows from the capability already described.
xs: The next step is **continuous at-sea deterrence** — option **(2)**.
SSBNs give **second-strike capability**, which supports **No First Use** — so ending NFU is not the step.
xa: **INS Aridhaman** (third boat) was commissioned on **3 Apr 2026** at **Visakhapatnam**.
A **fourth boat** is likely next year.
**K-5 / K-6** longer-range SLBMs are **under development**.

n3531c9b8e2b.s: The Strategic Forces Command is best described as
o: a joint research body of DRDO and ISRO
a civilian body regulating nuclear exports
a tri-service command managing and operating India’s nuclear arsenal
a parliamentary committee supervising defence expenditure
n3531c9b8e2b.x: The Strategic Forces Command is a tri-service command responsible for managing and operating India’s nuclear arsenal.
n3531c9b8e2b.tq: Match the organisation with its precise institutional role.
xs: The **Strategic Forces Command** is a **tri-service** command that **manages and operates** the nuclear arsenal — option **(3)**.
It was set up in **2003**.
xa: Agni user trials are held "**under the aegis of SFC**" (**Aug 2026**).
The **Political Council** (PM) alone authorises use.
**Executive Council** is chaired by the **National Security Advisor**.

n18e8f03ba87.s: Why are SSBNs regarded as the most survivable leg of the nuclear triad?
o: They eliminate the need for land-based deterrence.
They remain permanently visible to adversaries.
Their concealment supports a guaranteed second-strike capability.
n18e8f03ba87.x: SSBNs are difficult to detect and destroy, thereby supporting a reliable second-strike capability that underpins India’s No First Use posture.
n18e8f03ba87.tq: Connect survivability with the strategic purpose of assured retaliation.
xs: **SSBNs** are the **most survivable** leg; they guarantee **second-strike capability** — option **(4)**.
That second-strike capability **underpins No First Use**.
xa: Next step: **continuous at-sea deterrence**.
**SIPRI** links **12** deployed warheads to **SSBN deterrence patrols**.
India's SSBNs are based at **Visakhapatnam**; **Rambilli** naval base is nearby.

n2ef7b1a431a.s: The operational deployment of Indian warheads cited in the June 2026 assessment was linked particularly to
o: Dhanush missiles mounted exclusively on aircraft carriers
only free-fall bombs carried by Jaguar aircraft
SSBN deterrence patrols and canisterised Agni missiles
civilian nuclear reactors and space launch vehicles
n2ef7b1a431a.x: The cited deployment was linked to SSBN deterrence patrols and canisterised Agni missiles.
n2ef7b1a431a.tq: Match a current quantitative assessment with the two capabilities associated with it.
xs: **SIPRI** linked **12** "operationally deployed" Indian warheads to **SSBN deterrence patrols** and **canisterised Agni** — option **(3)**.
The assessment is dated **30 Jun 2026**.
xa: **SSBNs** are the **most survivable** leg, giving **second-strike capability**.
The air leg uses **Jaguar** and **Mirage 2000** with **free-fall** bombs.
**Agni-4** user trial, **6 Aug 2026**: **4,000 km**, **two-stage solid**, **road-mobile**.

n9115a31111c.s: The land-based leg of the United States nuclear triad consists of:
n9115a31111c.x: The US triad consists of Minuteman III ICBMs (land leg), strategic bombers and Ohio/Columbia-class SSBNs.
xa: India's land leg: **Prithvi** and **Agni**; air leg: **Jaguar** and **Mirage 2000**.
India's sea leg: **K-15 / K-4** from **Arihant-class SSBNs**.
India now has a **fully operational triad** (**Apr 2026**).

n77914b79376.s: The Advanced Technology Vessel (ATV) project was undertaken to build India's:
n77914b79376.x: The ATV project was initiated by DRDO and private firms, with Russian assistance, to build SSBNs.
xa: First product: **INS Arihant**, commissioned **2016**.
**IAI** (Israel) partnered DRDO on **MRSAM / Barak-8**, not on the ATV.
Arihant-class boats carry **K-15 / K-4** SLBMs.

n2af19c3b673.s: MRSAM or Barak-8 has been developed through cooperation between:
n2af19c3b673.x: MRSAM/Barak-8 is an India-Israel programme involving DRDO and Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI).
n2af19c3b673.tq: Use the development-agency trap to distinguish DRDO-IAI cooperation from other partnerships.
xs: **MRSAM / Barak-8** is an India-Israel system of **DRDO** and **Israel Aerospace Industries** — option **(1)**.
Its Army version was tested in **Apr 2025**.
xa: The **DAC** approved MRSAM procurement in **Jul 2026**.
MRSAM is a **building block** of **Mission Sudarshan Chakra**.
**Barak-1** (Israel) is the Navy's ship-based point-defence SAM.

nd562745c2fe.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India and nuclear regimes?
o: India has not signed the NPT, calling it discriminatory
India has been an NSG member since its 2008 waiver
India will not sign the CTBT until it is tied to time-bound global disarmament
India keeps a voluntary nuclear-test moratorium
nd562745c2fe.x: India is not an NSG member (blocked by China); it got the 2008 NSG waiver and follows NSG guidelines.
xa: ⚠ Member: **MTCR 2016 – Wassenaar 2017 – Australia Group 2018**.
India follows guidelines via the **WMD Act** + **SCOMET** list.
India supports a verifiable **FMCT** that does not cap existing stockpile.

n2632a6b1f78.s: India supports a universal and verifiable Fissile Material Cut-off Treaty provided that it
o: does not cap India’s existing stockpile
n2632a6b1f78.x: India supports a universal and verifiable FMCT, but its position is that the treaty should not cap its existing stockpile.
n2632a6b1f78.tq: Focus on the qualification attached to India’s support for an international treaty.
xs: India supports a **universal, verifiable FMCT** that **does not cap its existing stockpile** — option **(1)**.
FMCT = **Fissile Material Cut-off Treaty**.
xa: The doctrine includes support for **disarmament** and the **FMCT**.
India has **not signed** the **CTBT** or the **NPT**.
Export controls are followed via the **WMD Act** + **SCOMET**.

n8bb39a857e1.s: India is described as having a fully operational nuclear triad along with which of the following countries?
o: France, the United Kingdom and Pakistan
The United States, Russia and China
n8bb39a857e1.x: India is described as having a fully operational triad alongside the United States, Russia and China.
n8bb39a857e1.tq: Use the membership comparison rather than selecting other nuclear-capable states.
xs: India has a **fully operational triad** alongside the **USA, Russia and China** — option **(3)**.
This was reported in **Apr 2026**, after **INS Aridhaman** was commissioned.
xa: Sea leg: **K-15 / K-4** SLBMs from **Arihant-class SSBNs**.
SSBNs give **second-strike capability**, underpinning **No First Use**.
Next step: **continuous at-sea deterrence**.

ndc6701f6b28.s: Pokhran-II was conducted under which Prime Minister?
ndc6701f6b28.x: Pokhran-II was conducted under A.B. Vajpayee, with A.P.J. Abdul Kalam and R. Chidambaram in the scientific leadership.
xa: Dates: **11 and 13 May 1998**; code name "**Operation Shakti**".
**11 May** is observed as **National Technology Day**.
**Pakistan** tested soon after in **1998**.

n19c902b2b9c.s: INS Chakra II, leased by India from Russia, was a:
n19c902b2b9c.x: INS Chakra II was a leased Akula-class SSN (formerly Nerpa); the first INS Chakra was a Charlie-class boat.
xa: The first **INS Chakra** was a leased **Charlie-class** SSN (**1988**).
INS Arihant (S2), Arighaat (S3), Aridhaman (S4) form the **Arihant class**.
India now has a **fully operational triad**, alongside USA, Russia, China.

n6774a5a156b.s: In India's BMD programme, PAD (Prithvi Air Defence) is the:
n6774a5a156b.x: PAD is the higher-altitude exo-atmospheric interceptor; AAD is the lower-altitude endo-atmospheric interceptor and Swordfish is a tracking radar.
xa: India's BMD is a **two-tier** system — **outside (exo-)** and **inside (endo-)** the atmosphere.
**AD-1, AD-2** are **Phase II** interceptors.
Swordfish tracks targets at **1,500+ km**.

n44b8ffa0652.s: AD-1 and AD-2 interceptors belong to which phase of India's BMD programme?
n44b8ffa0652.x: AD-1 and AD-2 are Phase II BMD interceptors meant for longer-range threats of about the 5,000-km class.
xa: **Swordfish** **Long-Range Tracking Radar** tracks missiles and space objects at **1,500+ km**.
**Jun 2026**: DRDO showed **multi-layered BMD**; interceptors destroyed targets.
Same series: maiden test of **NASM-MR** (**14 Jun 2026**).

n085e816c508.s: The Swordfish radar is primarily used to:
o: Jam drone-control signals at short range
Track ballistic missiles and space objects at distances exceeding 1,500 km
n085e816c508.x: The Long-Range Tracking Radar, known as Swordfish, tracks ballistic missiles and space objects at distances of more than 1,500 km.
n085e816c508.tq: Identify the sensor by its tracking function and range rather than by the interceptor it supports.
xs: **Swordfish** (**Long-Range Tracking Radar**) tracks **ballistic missiles and space objects** at **1,500+ km** — option **(2)**.
Jamming drone signals is **Akash Tarang**'s job.

n26c245d7eab.s: Radar cross-section (RCS) of a target indicates:

nce26dcd48d7.s: HAL's 2025 contract for LCA Mk1A aircraft covers how many aircraft?

n2657a3dd4df.s: INS Astradharini is best described as a:

Capital acquisition follows **DAP 2020**, which sets the **Buy (Indian-IDDM)**-first priority order.
xa: The **SP model** (**2017**) is part of the **DPP**, for major platforms with foreign **OEMs**.
**2025** = MoD's **'Year of Reforms'**.
MoD signed **193 contracts** worth **₹2,09,050 crore** in **2024-25**; **92%** to domestic industry.

n0dadf48b5de.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's defence production and exports?
o: Defence production reached a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in FY 2025-26
DPEPP 2020 targeted Rs 50,000 crore defence exports by 2025
DPEPP 2020 targeted Rs 1.75 lakh crore defence production by 2025
Defence exports rose from Rs 686 crore (2013-14) to Rs 23,622 crore (2024-25)
n0dadf48b5de.x: The DPEPP 2020 export target for 2025 was Rs 35,000 crore, not Rs 50,000 crore.
xa: FY 2024-25 production: **₹1,51,339 crore**.
Defence R&D budget FY 2026-27: **₹29,100 crore**.
MoD signed **193 contracts** in 2024-25, **92%** to domestic industry.

nab036cf1ed1.s: Bharat Forge is establishing India's first private marine gas turbine MRO facility at:
nab036cf1ed1.x: Bharat Forge is setting up India's first private marine gas turbine MRO facility at Visakhapatnam.
nab036cf1ed1.tq: Use location-based recall for a specialised defence-industrial facility.
xs: **Bharat Forge** (Kalyani Group) is setting up **India's first private marine gas turbine MRO** facility at **Visakhapatnam** (**May 2026**) — option **(4)**.
**GTRE** is developing the MGT "**Samudra**" from the **Kaveri** engine.
xa: Visakhapatnam also hosts **NSTL**, the **Naval Dockyard** and the **Rambilli** submarine base.
⚠ **Boeing India**'s **₹413 crore** deal is for **P-8I** MRO, not marine gas turbines.
**Kalyani Strategic Systems** and **BDL** are investing in AP.

n010f6c0e770.s: NSTL, Visakhapatnam, DRDO's naval weapons laboratory, is associated with:
o: Torpedoes such as Varunastra, mines and AUVs
n010f6c0e770.x: NSTL is DRDO's naval weapons laboratory, associated with torpedoes such as Varunastra, mines and AUVs.
xa: The **Naval Dockyard** at Visakhapatnam is the **Eastern Naval Command** refit yard.
**Bharat Forge** MGT MRO is at Visakhapatnam.
**ADA** aircraft integration and flight testing is in **Sri Sathya Sai** district.

nd7a62c964fd.s: Indonesia is associated with India's export of which missile?
nd7a62c964fd.x: Indonesia is the Astra buyer, the Philippines bought BrahMos, and the UAE is in talks.
xa: Exports rose from **₹686 crore** to **₹23,622 crore** (~**34-fold**).
India still imports **jet engines** + **defence chips**.
The **BrahMos** unit at **Lucknow** is in the **UP corridor**.

nc55e1c8b33b.s: Swathi Weapon Locating Radar and Akash control centres are associated with:
nc55e1c8b33b.x: Swathi Weapon Locating Radar and Akash control centres are associated with Bharat Electronics Limited.
nc55e1c8b33b.tq: Match defence systems with the organisation responsible for them.
xs: **Swathi** WLR and **Akash** control centres are **BEL** (**Bharat Electronics Limited**) products — option **(3)**.
**Navantia** is the Spanish partner of **L&T**; **HVF Avadi** licence-builds the **T-90**; **HAL** builds **Tejas**, **Dhruv** and **Su-30 MKI**.
xa: **BEL** and **HAL** set up the **DIO**, which runs **iDEX**.
**BEL Palasamudram** (Sri Sathya Sai district) integrates **missile + radar** systems.
**BEL Machilipatnam** works on **opto-electronics / night vision**.

nd323164a0ff.s: Under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, the Bureau of Energy Efficiency and NMEEE promote energy efficiency through:
nd323164a0ff.x: BEE and the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency under NAPCC work through ESCOs.
xa: The **Draft National Electricity Policy 2026** sets GHG-intensity targets for **208 industrial units** under the same Act.
Emission intensity is **down 36%** below **2005**.
**ESCOs** = Energy Service Companies.

nb51e26b1dd2.s: Peak demand on an electricity grid is defined as:
o: The average power drawn over a full day
The highest power drawn in a 15-minute interval
The total electricity generated in a month
The maximum annual energy produced by renewable sources
nb51e26b1dd2.x: Peak demand is the highest power drawn from the grid during a 15-minute interval.
nb51e26b1dd2.tq: Distinguish instantaneous or interval-based peak power from aggregate energy generation.
xs: **Peak demand** is the **highest power drawn** on the grid in a **15-minute interval** — option **(2)**.
**Peak shortage** = unmet peak demand (**MW**); **energy shortage** = unmet energy requirement (**MU**).
xa: Record peak: **270.8 GW** (**May 2026**).
**Evening peak (6-11 p.m.)**: cooling demand after solar output drops.
NGAP: peak demand to reach **459 GW by 2035-36**.

nd6105bae500.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four A's on which energy security rests?
nd6105bae500.x: The four A's are availability, accessibility, affordability and acceptability. Accumulation is not included.
nd6105bae500.tq: Find the look-alike term that is absent from the standard four-part formulation.
xs: **Accumulation** is not one of the four A's — option **(3)**.
Energy security rests on the **Four A's**: **availability, accessibility, affordability, acceptability**.
xa: **Energy intensity** = energy used per unit of **GDP**; a falling value = growth **decoupling**.
**Peak demand** = highest power drawn in a **15-minute interval**.
⚠ **Energy shortage** in **MU**; **peak shortage** in **MW**.

nphysics-16-26.x: 1 kWh is a 1 kW device running for 1 hour = 1,000 W × 3,600 s = 3.6 × 10⁶ J; it is the 'unit' on electricity bills.
n: One kilowatt-hour is the energy consumed by a 1 kW device in 1 hour. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
One kilowatt-hour equals 3.6 × 10⁶ joules. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
Electricity cost is charged per unit in kWh. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 50-57]
xa: **Energy shortage** is counted in **MU** (million units); **peak shortage** in **MW**.
**Peak demand** = highest power drawn in a **15-minute interval**.
**Energy intensity** = energy used per unit of **GDP**.

nb7638f2be9c.s: The annual publication titled “Energy Statistics” is brought out by which organisation?
o: Central Electricity Authority under the Ministry of Power
Central Statistics Office, now functioning as the National Statistics Office under MoSPI
nb7638f2be9c.x: Energy Statistics was published by the Central Statistics Office (CSO), now the National Statistics Office (NSO) under MoSPI.
nb7638f2be9c.tq: Identify the correct publishing authority rather than a related sectoral body.
xs: The annual "**Energy Statistics**" is published by the **Central Statistics Office (CSO)**, now the **National Statistics Office, MoSPI** — option **(2)**.
APPSC **2019** keyed **CSO** as the answer.
**CEA** publishes the **NGAP** and **Electric Power Survey**; **NITI Aayog** publishes **IESS 2047**.
xa: Coverage: reserves + potential, installed capacity, production, **imports/exports**, consumption, **energy balance**.
Fuels covered: **coal, lignite, crude oil, natural gas, electricity**.
⚠ **IESS 2047** = NITI Aayog; **NGAP** + **EPS** = CEA; **WEO** = IEA; Energy Statistics = CSO/NSO.

n02b42f06936.s: The India Cooling Action Plan was launched in 2019 by:
n02b42f06936.x: MoEFCC launched it in 2019; it aims to cut cooling demand by 20–25% and refrigerant demand by 25–30% by 2037–38.
xa: Cooling energy to be cut **25-40%**.
AC ownership grows **15-20%** a year.
Peak demand rose **37%**: **183 GW** (Dec 2020) → over **250 GW**.

n2b551a79d38.s: Which sector uses about 50% of India's electricity?
n2b551a79d38.x: Industry, not households, uses about half of India's electricity; household electrification is about 99%.
xa: **Saubhagya** connected **26 million** households.
Industry was also the largest energy sector in the IESS **2012** base (**2,367 TWh**).
Urban population grows ~**2.5%** a year.

nb256986a5b3.s: The World Energy Outlook is published by:
nb256986a5b3.x: The IEA publishes it; WEO 2022 projected India's coal generation and oil imports to peak around 2030.
xa: The IEA also publishes the **India Energy Outlook**, an India-specific WEO special report.
⚠ **IESS 2047** = NITI Aayog; **NGAP** + **EPS** = CEA; **WEO** = IEA.

n96c021f0d7e.s: The CEA's National Generation Adequacy Plan (2026–27 to 2035–36) projects peak power demand by 2035–36 of:
n96c021f0d7e.x: NGAP projects 459 GW peak demand, 1,121 GW installed capacity and 70% non-fossil capacity.
xa: Peak demand grows **5.58%/yr**.
Coal still **51%** of generation; storage need **174 GW/888 GWh**.
Storage split: **94 GW** pumped storage + **80 GW** BESS (**17 May 2026**).

nf7ea6aba52c.s: As per NITI Aayog's India Energy Security Scenarios projection, India's energy demand between 2012 and 2040 was expected to rise by:
nf7ea6aba52c.x: Total energy demand was projected to rise 2.7–3.2 times from 2012 to 2040, while electricity demand would rise 4.5-fold.
xa: IESS 2047 is by **NITI Aayog**.
