Separately, energy demand is expected to **triple by 2047**.

n9b19d6a9f49.s: Andhra Pradesh's Resource Adequacy Plan (2025–26 to 2035–36) seeks about how much new thermal capacity?
n9b19d6a9f49.x: The plan seeks about 5,588 MW of new thermal capacity; APERC cleared the first 1,600 MW.
xa: AP electricity requirement grows **6.90% CAGR**; peak demand **7.10%**.
APERC approval was dated **6 Aug 2026**.

n09e00f35d6f.s: Nuclear energy is significant for India's energy system mainly because it:
o: Provides 24×7 baseload power and can reduce fossil-fuel imports
n09e00f35d6f.x: Nuclear power gives round-the-clock baseload electricity and can cut dependence on fossil-fuel imports.
xa: Nuclear installed capacity: **8.78 GW**.
NITI scenario: nuclear's share of generation **3%** → **5-8%** by **2070**.
Crude oil import dependence is **~88%**.

ndd325798fd9.s: Which source supplies approximately 55% of India’s energy mix and over 74% of its power generation?
ndd325798fd9.x: Coal supplies about 55% of the energy mix and more than 74% of power generation.
ndd325798fd9.tq: Match the quantitative share with the correct fuel source.
xs: **Coal** supplies **55% of the energy mix** and **over 74% of power generation** (2025-26) — option **(1)**.
India is the world's **second-largest coal consumer**; coal leads installed capacity (**230 GW**).
xa: **Solar** is second in installed capacity (**157 GW, ~29%**) and the second source after fossil fuels (UPPSC **2021**).
**Nuclear** has only **8.78 GW** of installed capacity.
NITI scenario: coal's share of generation **~74% → 6-10%** by **2070**.

n5fa0b5a5aa1.s: India is the world's ____-largest energy consumer.
n5fa0b5a5aa1.x: India is the third-largest energy consumer and the second-largest coal consumer; its energy demand is expected to triple by 2047.
xa: Coal = **55% of the energy mix**, over **74%** of power generation.
**Solar** is the second source after fossil fuels (UPPSC 2021).
Installed capacity: coal **230 GW**, solar **157 GW**, wind **56.8 GW**.

nbeb86903b46.s: India’s per-capita electricity consumption increased from 957 kWh in FY 2014 to approximately what level in FY 2025?
nbeb86903b46.x: Per-capita electricity consumption rose from 957 kWh in FY 2014 to 1,460 kWh in FY 2025.
nbeb86903b46.tq: Use the time labels carefully and select the correct terminal value.
xs: Per-capita electricity consumption rose from **957 kWh (FY 2014)** to **1,460 kWh (FY 2025)** — option **(1)**.
Older notes gave **1,181 kWh**, "about half the world average".
xa: Per-capita **generation** in **2024**: India **1,418 kWh**, China **7,097**, USA **12,701**.
India's per-capita electricity ≈ **a fifth** of China's and **a ninth** of the USA's.
IESS 2047 projects **2,911-2,924 kWh** per capita.

ne1064f68b9a.s: India’s per-capita energy consumption is approximately what fraction of the world average?
ne1064f68b9a.x: India’s per-capita energy consumption is reported as only one-third of the world average.
ne1064f68b9a.tq: Separate the current world-gap ratio from older references to one-half of the world average.
xs: India's per-capita energy is only **one-third of the world average** — option **(2)**.
⚠ "**About half** the world average" is an older figure for per-capita **electricity** (**1,181 kWh**).
xa: Consumption is **low** with a large **urban-rural disparity**.
Per-capita electricity ≈ **a fifth** of China's, **a ninth** of the USA's.

nb83fae2fbf3.s: The policy objective of raising per-capita electricity consumption is linked to the Human Development Index primarily because:
o: Electricity consumption is unrelated to social development indicators
Higher electricity consumption automatically eliminates urban-rural disparity
A minimum level of per-capita consumption is needed for a minimally acceptable level of well-being
HDI measures only the availability of commercial energy
nb83fae2fbf3.x: Per-capita electricity consumption acts as a proxy for energy use, and a certain minimum level is required to ensure a minimally acceptable level of well-being.
nb83fae2fbf3.tq: Apply the development-indicator relationship to the policy objective.
xs: A **certain minimum level of per-capita consumption** is needed to ensure a **minimally acceptable level of well-being** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2016** key).
Per-capita electricity, a proxy for all energy, **correlates with HDI**, so policy aims to raise it.
xa: India's per-capita electricity rose from **957 kWh** to **1,460 kWh** (FY 2014 → FY 2025).
Consumption is **low per capita** with a large **urban-rural disparity**.
Energy security rests on the **Four A's**: availability, accessibility, affordability, acceptability.

nf5ae301eb97.s: India's per-capita energy consumption is best described as:
o: Uniform across urban and rural areas
Low, with a large urban-rural disparity
High in rural areas and negligible in urban areas
nf5ae301eb97.x: India has low per-capita energy consumption with a large urban-rural gap.
xa: Per-capita electricity ≈ **a fifth** of China's and **a ninth** of the USA's.
Household electrification is **~99%**.
**Saubhagya** connected **26 million** households.

n09fd621a080.s: By 2040, which sector is projected to remain the largest consumer of energy in India?
n09fd621a080.x: Industry remains the largest sector, with 8,764 TWh under BAU in 2040, while cooking demand falls as clean fuels replace biomass.
xa: **2012** base: industry **2,367 TWh**, cooking **1,072**, transport **929**; total **4,926**.
IESS 2047 is by **NITI Aayog**: energy demand up **2.7-3.2 times** (2012-2040), electricity up **4.5-fold**.
Import dependence projected **31%** → **36-55%**.

n3da349ffd18.s: Which of the following combinations best represents the emerging drivers of India's peak electricity demand?
o: Electric vehicles, farm pumps, appliances, cooling and data centres
Declining appliance ownership and reduced telecom activity
Only household lighting in rural areas
Only coal mining and railway electrification
n3da349ffd18.x: Electric vehicles, farm pumps, appliances, cooling demand, data centres and telecom operations all contribute to rising electricity demand.
n3da349ffd18.tq: Group the closely related demand-side drivers rather than selecting an exclusive cause.
xs: **EVs, farm pumps, appliances, cooling** and **data centres** drive peak demand — option **(1)**.
EVs, pumps and appliances lifted peak demand **37%**, from **183 GW (Dec 2020)** to **over 250 GW (Apr 2026)**.
xa: **Data centres + telecom** need **continuous power**.
**AC ownership** grows **15-20%** a year.
Jan-Feb **2026** demand hit a **five-year high**.

n1ca32c1ffee.s: India's peak electricity demand rose by approximately 37%, from 183 GW in December 2020 to over what level in April 2026?
n1ca32c1ffee.x: Peak demand increased from 183 GW in December 2020 to more than 250 GW in April 2026, representing a rise of about 37%.
n1ca32c1ffee.tq: Match the percentage change with the correct end-point figure.
xs: Peak demand rose **37%** from **183 GW (Dec 2020)** to **over 250 GW (Apr 2026)** — option **(1)**.
Drivers: **EVs, farm pumps, appliances**.
xa: All-time high: **270.8 GW** in **May 2026**, ~**90 GW** above **2019**.
**25 Apr 2026**: **256.1 GW**, about a third met by RE.
CEA's **NGAP** projects peak demand of **459 GW by 2035-36** (**5.58%/yr**).

n349cfbc58ac.s: India's non-fossil share of installed power capacity rose from 32% in 2014 to ____ in 2025.
n349cfbc58ac.x: It reached 51% in 2025, crossing the 50% target five years early.
xa: The **2031-35 NDC** raises the non-fossil target to **60%**.
First NDC (**2015**) targeted **40%** non-fossil by **2030**.
CEA's NGAP sees **70%** non-fossil in **1,121 GW** of capacity by **2035-36**.

n2785268819f.s: NITI Aayog's 'Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero' projects renewables' share of power generation rising from about 20% (2024-25) to about ____ by 2070.
n2785268819f.x: The study projects renewables rising from about 20% to about 80% of generation by 2070, with coal falling from about 74% to 6-10%.
xa: Coal today = **over 74%** of power generation and **55%** of the energy mix.
NGAP: coal still **51%** of generation by **2035-36**.
**Nuclear** = **24x7** baseload; cuts fossil imports.

n6195d413553.s: India's per-capita electricity consumption is about ____ of China's.
n6195d413553.x: It is about one-fifth of China's and one-ninth of the USA's.
xa: Per-capita generation **2024**: India **1,418 kWh**, China **7,097**, USA **12,701**.
OECD average: a little above **8,000 kWh**.
Per-capita electricity consumption: **1,460 kWh** (FY **2025**).

n50a3cd9e6eb.s: India's all-time high peak electricity demand recorded in May 2026 was:
n50a3cd9e6eb.x: The May 2026 peak demand was an all-time high of 270.8 GW, about 90 GW above the 2019 level.
xa: The record pushed **long-duration storage** (**over 8 hours**) to the centre of policy.
Peak demand had risen **37%** from **183 GW (Dec 2020)**.
On **25 Apr 2026** non-solar hours saw a **2% (4,243 MW)** deficit.

n89f1b907e9f.s: Which of the following correctly describes the coverage of India's Energy Statistics publication?
o: Coal, lignite, crude oil and natural gas, including imports and exports, plus the energy balance
Production data only, excluding imports and exports
Crude oil and natural gas only
n89f1b907e9f.x: It covers coal, lignite, crude oil, natural gas, electricity consumption and the energy balance, including imports and exports.
xa: Publisher: **CSO**, now **NSO, MoSPI** (APPSC **2019** key: CSO).
The **Electric Power Survey** is **CEA**'s official long-term electricity demand forecast.

nb82a03935df.s: Delhi's response to the 6–11 p.m. evening electricity peak, caused by cooling demand after solar output drops, is:
nb82a03935df.x: Delhi uses time-of-day tariffs and smart meters to manage the evening peak.
xa: **El Niño 2026** dented **wind and hydro** output.
**Regional imbalance**: poor storage + slow transmission strand renewables.
Rules: **15-day coal stock**; **12-month** advance power plans.

n996947cf721.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's fuel position?
o: India's crude-oil import dependence is about 88%
India holds about 7% of the world's oil reserves
India has the fourth-largest coal reserves, about 344 billion tonnes
Coal makes up about 55% of India's primary energy
n996947cf721.x: India holds only about 0.4% of world oil reserves; 7% is its share of coal reserves.
xa: India holds **17%** of world population but only **0.6% of gas** reserves.
Natural gas: ~**50-51%** imported.
FY26 coal output: **1,040.08 MT**.

n116db7d7078.s: During the 2026 gas crisis, which strait was identified as a risk to India's LPG supplies?
n116db7d7078.x: The Strait of Hormuz was identified as the risk; India imports about 50–51% of its natural gas/LNG.
xa: India holds only **0.6%** of world gas reserves.
IEA **WEO 2022**: India's gas imports **double**.
Crude oil import dependence **~88%**.

nb3469479526.s: Which authority has been allowed to import coal under the Andhra Pradesh energy roadmap?
nb3469479526.x: APGENCO has been allowed to import coal under the Andhra Pradesh energy roadmap.
nb3469479526.tq: Ask which operational entity, rather than regulator or central agency, performs the specified action.
xs: **APGENCO** has been allowed to **import coal** — option **(2)**.
**APERC** is the regulator that approved **1,600 MW**; **NHPC** partners the **500 MW/1,000 MWh** VGF storage.
xa: Roadmap: **15-day coal stock** required.
**1,500 MW/6,000 MWh BESS** for the evening peak.
Thermal-plant coal **imports down 27.4%** nationally.

nfcd3bdba467.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's NDC targets (versus 2005)?
o: The first NDC (2015) targeted a 33–35% cut in emission intensity by 2030
The 2031–35 NDC targets 50% non-fossil capacity by 2035
The 2031–35 NDC targets a 47% cut in intensity by 2035
The updated NDC (Aug 2022) targeted a 45% cut in intensity and 50% non-fossil capacity by 2030
nfcd3bdba467.x: The 2031–35 NDC sets a 60% non-fossil capacity target, not 50%.
xa: Emission intensity is already **down 36%** below **2005**.
Non-fossil capacity: **32% (2014)** → **51% (2025)**; **50%** reached five years early.

n64277a63776.s: The COP31 goal described as “35 by 35” seeks to make electricity account for what share of final energy by 2035?
n64277a63776.x: The “35 by 35” goal seeks to raise electricity's share to 35% of final energy by 2035.
n64277a63776.tq: Read the target directly from the compact numerical slogan.
xs: **COP31 "35 by 35"**: electricity = **35%** of final energy by **2035** — option **(3)**.
Today only ~**one-fifth** of India's energy use is electricity.
xa: Per-capita energy **2024**: **7,893 kWh**.
The **2031-35 NDC** targets **47%** intensity cut by **2035** and **60%** non-fossil.
IESS: electricity demand up **4.5-fold** (2012-2040).

n8e1ebba2091.s: Which scheme is associated with electricity connections to about 26 million households?
n8e1ebba2091.x: The Saubhagya programme is associated with connecting approximately 26 million households.
xa: Other schemes: **RDSS**, **DDUGJY**, **IPDS**.
Household electrification is **~99%**.

n5e72c969971.s: India's aggregate technical and commercial (AT&C) losses declined from 22.62% in FY14 to approximately what level in FY25?
n5e72c969971.x: AT&C losses fell from 22.62% in FY14 to 15.04% in FY25, alongside measures such as RDSS, IPDS, smart meters and time-of-day tariffs. 10.04%, 18.62% and 12.50% are not the reported FY25 figure.
xs: **AT&C losses** fell from **22.62% (FY14)** to **15.04% (FY25)** — option **(1)**.
They are listed with **RDSS**, **DDUGJY**, **IPDS** and **Saubhagya** as measures against the deficit.
xa: Other measures: **ToD tariffs**, **smart meters**, **BESS**, **pumped storage**.
**National Electricity Plan 2023 (CEA)**: non-fossil **485 GW** (**62.4%**) of **777 GW** by **2029-30**.

nab84a904b23.s: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 was issued by:
nab84a904b23.x: It is from the Ministry of Power; it replaces the 2005 policy and proposes 100 GW of pumped storage by 2047.
xa: The draft policy replaces the **2005** policy and targets **100 GW of pumped storage by 2047**.
**Saubhagya** connected **26 million** households.

neecccf1b4df.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's September 2026 energy roadmap, the central VGF battery-storage project with NHPC has a size of:
neecccf1b4df.x: The NHPC VGF project is 500 MW/1,000 MWh; the 1,500 MW/6,000 MWh BESS is planned for the evening peak.
xa: **APGENCO** is allowed to import coal.
AP angle: **El Niño**-driven peaks → **1,600 MW** thermal + **2,000 MW** of BESS.
The roadmap is dated **9 Sep 2026**.

n0f94ebf7fac.s: An energy crisis, in the sense used in discussions of conventional energy resources, refers to:
o: A rise in electricity consumption during solar hours
A temporary fall in renewable-energy generation only
The danger that fossil fuels such as coal and petroleum may run out
A shortage limited to nuclear fuel imports
n0f94ebf7fac.x: Energy crisis refers to the danger of exhaustion of fossil fuels such as coal and petroleum.
n0f94ebf7fac.tq: Identify the underlying resource-depletion meaning rather than a short-term grid event.
xs: An **energy crisis** is the danger that **fossil fuels** like **coal and petroleum** will **run out** — option **(3)** (UKPSC **2006** key).
Fossil fuels still dominate: **coal** = **55%** of the energy mix.
xa: India has **17%** of world population but only **0.6% of gas**, **0.4% of oil** and **7% of coal** reserves.
Crude oil import dependence is **~88%**.
**Solar** is the second source after fossil fuels (UPPSC **2021**).

nab555ef7c10.s: India's emissions intensity has declined by what percentage below the 2005 level, according to the stated achievement?
nab555ef7c10.x: Emissions intensity has declined by 36% below the 2005 level.
nab555ef7c10.tq: Distinguish the achieved reduction from the future 2030 NDC target.
xs: **Emission intensity** is **down 36%** below **2005** — option **(2)**.
NDC target is **45% by 2030**; IESS modelled **45-53%**.
xa: Non-fossil capacity reached **51%** in **2025**.
Efficiency tools: **BEE** + **NMEEE** under the **Energy Conservation Act 2001**.

nc538f624dad.s: The evening peak has become central to India’s storage push primarily because:
o: Renewable energy cannot contribute during daylight hours
Coal supplies less than one-tenth of power generation
The remaining deficit occurs mainly during non-solar evening hours
Electricity demand is highest only during solar hours
nc538f624dad.x: Although solar-hour supply has improved, the non-solar evening peak still creates a deficit, making storage important for meeting that period’s demand.
nc538f624dad.tq: Infer the policy response from the timing of the remaining grid deficit.
xs: The remaining deficit now falls in **non-solar evening hours**, so **storage** is needed — option **(3)**.
On **25 Apr 2026** solar hours had no shortage but non-solar hours a **2% (4,243 MW)** deficit.
xa: NGAP storage need: **174 GW/888 GWh** = **94 GW** pumped storage + **80 GW** BESS.
**Draft National Electricity Policy 2026**: **100 GW** of pumped storage by **2047**.
Delhi uses **ToD tariffs** and smart meters for the **6-11 p.m.** peak.

n8e098f388cb.s: According to recent estimates, India holds the world's ______ largest coal reserves.
n8e098f388cb.x: The current estimate identifies India as the world’s fifth-largest holder of coal reserves; an older estimate had placed it fourth.
n8e098f388cb.tq: Distinguish the current ranking from the older alternative ranking.
xs: India is the world's **fifth** largest holder of coal reserves (2025-26) — option **(2)**.
⚠ Older notes say **4th** (~**344 bt**) — option (1) is the outdated figure.
xa: ⚠ Coal: **fifth-largest reserves** but **third-largest producer**.
Coal import share is still **~26%**.
India holds **7%** of world coal reserves vs **17%** of population.
n8e098f388cb.fixed: odd wording 'in the current estimate referred to'

nc75fd561fed.s: Which country is identified as a key supplier of LNG to India?
nc75fd561fed.x: Qatar is identified as a key LNG supplier to India.
nc75fd561fed.tq: Distinguish the major LNG supplier from countries listed mainly in the crude-import movement.
xs: **Qatar** is India's key **LNG** supplier — option **(1)**.
Natural gas / LNG import share is **~47-51%**.
xa: The **Strait of Hormuz** carries a fifth of global **LNG** trade.
**Coking coal** for steel comes mainly from **Australia** and **Indonesia**.
**CBO** in CGD aims to substitute **LNG** imports.

ne12179db60a.s: India's import dependence for lithium is about:
ne12179db60a.x: Lithium import dependence is about 90%; crude oil is about 88% and coal about 26%.
xa: India has **17%** of world population but only **0.6%** gas, **0.4%** oil, **7%** coal reserves.
⚠ Coal: **fifth-largest reserves** (older: 4th) but **third-largest producer**.
Of **26** sedimentary basins, only **7** produce.

nbe1c765377c.s: In 2026, India is described as the world's ______ largest oil consumer.
nbe1c765377c.x: India is the third-largest oil consumer and also the third-largest energy consumer in the world. Second, fourth and fifth are incorrect.
nbe1c765377c.tq: India: 3rd in energy, 3rd in oil consumption.
xs: India is the world's **third** largest oil consumer (**2026**) — option **(2)**.
It is also the **3rd largest energy consumer**.
xa: Crude import dependence: **88.5%** (**PPAC**, **July 2026**).
⚠ In coal, India is the **third-largest producer** but has the **fifth-largest reserves**.
India holds only **0.4%** of world oil reserves.

nd7108e9f90b.s: According to PPAC data, India's crude oil import bill in July 2026 rose year-on-year by approximately:
nd7108e9f90b.x: PPAC reported that the crude import bill of $13.7 billion in July 2026 was up 41% year-on-year. The 13.3% rise refers to import volume and 10% to petroleum product exports.
xs: **PPAC**: the July 2026 crude import **bill** (**$13.7 billion**) rose **41%** YoY — option **(2)**.
**13.3%** is the rise in import **volume**; **10%** the rise in product exports.
xa: Volume: **21.4 MMT**.
Crude basket **$82.04/bbl** vs **$70.95** a year earlier.
The **41-MT** strategic storage plan followed the 2026 Hormuz disruption.

n0e4db3fc62d.s: In cooking applications, methanol can partly replace:
n0e4db3fc62d.x: Methanol, a low-carbon hydrogen-carrier fuel, can partly replace LPG and kerosene in cooking, besides petrol/diesel in transport.
xa: **DME** = two methanol molecules minus one water molecule; can **substitute propane in LPG**.
**M15** (15% methanol) cuts gasoline imports by at least **15%**.
**20% DME in LPG** saves **₹6,000 crore/yr**.
NITI's Methanol Economy aims: cut oil import bill, cut **GHG**, use coal + **municipal solid waste** (APPSC-G1 2024: all three).

ne70d4068a67.s: The Compressed Biogas Obligation in the City Gas Distribution sector mainly aims to substitute imports of:
ne70d4068a67.x: The CBO is intended to promote compressed biogas and substitute LNG imports.
xa: Natural gas / LNG import share: **~47-51%**.
**Qatar** is the key LNG supplier.
No underground **natural-gas** storage exists in India.

na67d4abbd72.s: Of India's 26 sedimentary basins, how many are producing hydrocarbons?
na67d4abbd72.x: India has 26 sedimentary basins, of which only 7 are producing.
xa: **Hydrocarbon Vision 2025** calls for **appraisal of all sedimentary basins**.
**HELP** (single licence for all hydrocarbons) and **OALP** drive upstream exploration.
The **KG Basin** (offshore, East Coast) is one of India's most prolific hydrocarbon zones.

n40d6e61e437.s: Roughly what share of world crude-oil trade passes through the Strait of Hormuz?
n40d6e61e437.x: About 15 million bbl/day, roughly 34% of world crude trade, passes through it, along with about a fifth of global LNG trade.
xa: **Iran** effectively closed it in **early March 2026**.
The closure led to a **41%** jump in India's July crude bill and an **LPG** crunch.

nb96cc8c8c4d.s: The increase in international oil prices is most directly associated with which combination of macroeconomic effects in India?
o: A rise in exports and elimination of the current account deficit
Lower inflation and a narrower trade deficit
A wider trade deficit and higher inflation
A fall in import expenditure and currency appreciation
nb96cc8c8c4d.x: Higher oil prices increase import costs, thereby widening the trade deficit and contributing to inflation.
nb96cc8c8c4d.tq: Apply the import-cost transmission mechanism to macroeconomic outcomes.
xs: Higher oil prices cause a **wider trade deficit** and **higher inflation** — option **(3)**.
Oil is the **biggest driver** of the **trade deficit/CAD**, and global volatility feeds **domestic inflation**.
xa: India's crude basket: **$82.04/bbl** in **July 2026** vs **$70.95** a year earlier.
Fiscal angle: **subsidy and excise** pressure when prices spike.

n6887e9e022e.s: After the Strait of Hormuz closure in March 2026, India proposed a strategic fuel system of what capacity?
n6887e9e022e.x: The disruption was linked to a 41% jump in the July crude bill, an LPG crunch and a proposed 41 MT strategic fuel system.
xa: July 2026 crude import bill: **$13.7 billion**.
The **41 MT** plan = **28 MT crude + 9 MT LNG + 4 MT LPG**.
Hormuz carries ~**15 million bbl/day** (~**34%** of world crude trade) and a fifth of global **LNG** trade.

nf24d571e2d2.s: India has about 17% of the world's population. Approximately what share of the world's oil reserves does it hold?
nf24d571e2d2.x: India holds only about 0.4% of world oil reserves. 0.6% is its share of gas reserves and 7% its share of coal reserves; 4% is not a stated figure.
nf24d571e2d2.tq: Reserves vs 17% population: gas 0.6, oil 0.4, coal 7.
xs: India holds only **0.4%** of world **oil** reserves — option **(1)**.
**0.6%** is its share of **gas** reserves and **7%** of **coal** reserves.
xa: This gap explains crude import dependence of **88.5%** (**PPAC**, **July 2026**).
Only **7** of **26** sedimentary basins produce.
**ONGC Videsh (OVL)** buys **equity oil** and gas abroad to offset the gap.

n1a705ff5913.s: In recent years, India's largest crude-oil supplier has been:
n1a705ff5913.x: Russia was the largest supplier; Iraq and Saudi Arabia were also major suppliers.
xa: Other top suppliers: **UAE**, **USA** (~**8%**).
**IOC** signed new **2027** deals with **Algeria** + more US crude.
India's imports from **OPEC** have fallen **below 50%**.

n3117a6560cc.s: OPEC produces about what share of global oil?
n3117a6560cc.x: OPEC produces about 40% of global oil; its share of India's crude imports has fallen below 50%.
xa: **Russia** is now India's largest crude supplier (~**35%**).
**West Asia + Africa** supply ~**65%**.

nd2719adac9f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Phase I Strategic Petroleum Reserves?
o: They are underground rock caverns at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur
Their capacity is 5.33 MMT, about 9.5 days of cover when full
The IEA norm for strategic reserves is 60 days of cover
Actual stocks of about 3.37 MT give only about 5 days of cover
nd2719adac9f.x: The IEA norm is 90 days of cover, not 60.
xa: **Phase II**: **Chandikhol (Odisha)** and **Padur (Karnataka)**; proposed **Bikaner**, **Rajkot**.
Proposed strategic fuel programme: **41 MT** = **28 MT crude + 9 MT LNG + 4 MT LPG**.
LPG semi-strategic caverns hold only ~**0.14 MT**; no underground gas storage.

nac5438e478a.s: The strategic petroleum reserve at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, has a capacity of:
nac5438e478a.x: The Visakhapatnam reserve has a stated capacity of 1.33 MMT; Padur (Karnataka) has 2.5 MMT.
xa: ⚠ **Padur** is in both **Phase I** and **Phase II**.
Phase II: **Chandikhol (Odisha)** and **Padur** approved.
Visakhapatnam also hosts the **HPCL** refinery and **IIPE**.

n9db62ef4af8.s: Under the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP), companies get:
o: Separate licences for oil and for gas
A single licence for all hydrocarbons
n9db62ef4af8.x: HELP provides a single, unified licence for all hydrocarbons; OALP concerns upstream exploration and production.
xa: **One Nation One Gas Grid** is part of the upstream push.
Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 sought **equity oil abroad**.

n76c4d03374e.s: The Krishna-Godavari Basin, one of India's most prolific hydrocarbon zones, is located:
n76c4d03374e.x: The KG Basin is an offshore East Coast zone, where Andhra Pradesh produces gas and crude oil.
xa: **IIPE Visakhapatnam** (est. **2016**, **INI 2017**) has a **shale**-modelling pact with **OIL India** for the KG basin.
**Visakhapatnam** hosts the **SPR**, **HPCL** refinery and **IIPE**.
Only **7** of **26** sedimentary basins produce.

nc42272c3af1.s: Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 was adopted by the Government of India in
nc42272c3af1.x: Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 was adopted by the Government of India in 2000.
nc42272c3af1.tq: Distinguish the adoption year from the policy’s horizon year in its title.
xs: **Hydrocarbon Vision 2025** was adopted by GoI in **2000** — option **(2)**.
It is a **long-term hydrocarbon sector plan**, linked in exams with **storage of petroleum products** (UPPSC **2000**).
xa: Focus: energy security via domestic output + **equity oil abroad**; **strategic and buffer stocks**.
Also: appraisal of all sedimentary basins, globally competitive refining, **free market**, better fuel quality.
⚠ "**2025**" is the vision's horizon, not its year of adoption.

nefa350f4037.s: Which one of the following is NOT a focus area associated with Hydrocarbon Vision 2025?
o: Complete prohibition of private participation in hydrocarbons
nefa350f4037.x: Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 promotes a free market and competition; it does not seek complete prohibition of private participation. The other three are stated focus areas.
nefa350f4037.tq: Find the option that reverses the policy’s market-oriented approach.
xs: **Complete prohibition of private participation** is not a focus — option **(1)**; the vision backs a **free market + competition**.
Stated focus areas include **appraisal of all sedimentary basins**, **globally competitive refining** and **free market**.
xa: Other focus areas: **strategic and buffer stocks**, **equity oil abroad**, **better fuel quality**.
Adopted in **2000**.
Upstream follow-ups: **HELP**, **OALP**, **One Nation One Gas Grid**.

n967a7dbf307.s: From FY 2028-29, the Compressed Biogas Obligation is set at what share of CNG-PNG?
n967a7dbf307.x: The obligation is 1% in FY26, 3% in FY27, 4% in FY28 and 5% from FY 2028-29.
xa: CBO applies to **CNG/PNG** consumption in **CGD**.
Aim: substitute **LNG** imports.
Gas / LNG import share is **~47-51%**.

n8fbf6dabd7a.s: India’s LPG supply depends mainly on which of the following?
o: Underground storage maintained by state governments alone
n8fbf6dabd7a.x: India’s LPG supply depends mainly on stocks held by oil marketing companies. Semi-strategic underground LPG storage is only about 0.14 MT.
n8fbf6dabd7a.tq: Identify the principal operational source rather than the limited reserve arrangement.
xs: LPG supply depends mainly on **oil marketing company (OMC) stocks** — option **(4)**.
Semi-strategic underground LPG storage is only ~**0.14 MT**.
xa: **2026**: **LPG shortage** after the Hormuz shock; refineries ordered under the **LPG control order** raised output **35 to 54 TMT/day** in five days.
**PNGRB** authorised **~1,800 km** of LPG pipelines in **six States**.
The proposed **41 MT** strategic fuel programme includes **4 MT LPG** (six weeks' cover).

n6916a267212.s: Which of the following is identified as the core challenge affecting India’s oil consumption and energy security?
o: Only the shortage of coal in inland regions
Declining use of renewable energy and falling global prices
Excess domestic crude production and stable prices
Supply-chain disruptions and fluctuating global oil prices
n6916a267212.x: India’s core oil-related challenge is the combination of supply-chain disruptions and fluctuating global oil prices.
n6916a267212.tq: Select the option that combines the two linked causes rather than an isolated factor.
xs: The core challenge is **supply-chain disruptions and fluctuating global oil prices** — option **(4)** (APPSC-G2 **2025** key).
India is the **3rd largest energy consumer** and **3rd largest oil consumer**.
xa: **Price** volatility feeds domestic inflation; **fiscal** pressure through subsidies and excise.
Oil is the biggest driver of the **trade deficit/CAD**; managed by **SPR, ethanol, EVs, RE**.
Chokepoint risk: the **Strait of Hormuz**.

nfc66c43d102.s: The Indian Institute of Petroleum and Energy (IIPE), Visakhapatnam, established in 2016, was declared an Institution of National Importance in:
nfc66c43d102.x: IIPE was established in 2016, became an Institution of National Importance in 2017 and signed a shale-modelling pact with OIL India in April 2026.
xa: The shale-modelling pact is for the **KG basin**.
**KG Basin** (offshore, East Coast) is one of India's most prolific hydrocarbon zones; AP produces gas + crude in the **Godavari** basin.
**Visakhapatnam** also hosts the **HPCL** refinery and the Phase I **SPR**.

n2ebd82142c9.s: The PNGRB, set up under its 2006 Act, regulates:
n2ebd82142c9.x: PNGRB regulates petroleum and natural gas under MoPNG.
xa: **Department of Atomic Energy** is directly under the **Prime Minister**.
OIL India is a **Navratna** under MoPNG.
MNRE mission (APPSC-G2 2025): energy security, clean power, access, affordability, equity.

nf3df05bbb04.s: The Draft National Energy Policy (2017) was prepared by:
o: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
nf3df05bbb04.x: National Energy Policy is NITI Aayog's; the National Electricity Policy (2005) is the Ministry of Power's.
xa: ⚠ **National Energy Policy** = NITI; **National Electricity Policy** = Ministry of Power.
**Integrated Energy Policy** (**2006**, approved 2008) was by an expert committee under **Kirit Parikh**.
**Draft National Electricity Policy 2026** (Ministry of Power) replaces NEP 2005.

nddcefb91631.s: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 replaces the National Electricity Policy of:
nddcefb91631.x: Issued by the Ministry of Power, it replaces the National Electricity Policy 2005.
xa: The 2026 draft covers **hybrid RE, BESS, smart grids, Time-of-Day tariffs**.
It also targets **100 GW PSH by 2047**.
It is paired with **EC Act 2001** targets for **208 industrial units** → domestic carbon market.

nd81589c9cc8.s: The Integrated Energy Policy, prepared in 2006, was approved by the Union Cabinet in:
nd81589c9cc8.x: It was approved in December 2008 and aimed to meet energy needs up to 2031–32.
xa: Pricing: **market-determined / trade-parity pricing** of tradable fuels.
Subsidies: **targeted** to the poor, not a general price subsidy.
Governance: **independent regulators + competition**.

n3e9da0e5824.s: The Integrated Energy Policy (2006) was prepared by an Expert Committee of the Planning Commission chaired by:
n3e9da0e5824.x: The Integrated Energy Policy was drafted by the Planning Commission's Expert Committee chaired by Kirit Parikh, reported in 2006 and was approved by the Cabinet in December 2008. The other economists did not chair this committee.
xs: The expert committee was chaired by **Kirit Parikh** — option **(1)**.
The **Planning Commission** committee reported in **2006**; the Cabinet approved the policy in **December 2008**.
xa: Aim: meet energy needs at least cost, reliably and sustainably till **2031-32**.
Recommendations: **trade-parity pricing**, **targeted subsidies**, **efficiency**, **independent regulators**, **strategic oil reserves**.

n7dd60c8ce25.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's electricity policies?
o: The Electricity Act 2003 requires a National Electricity Policy and a Tariff Policy
The Tariff Policy of 2006 was revised in 2016
The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 was issued by NITI Aayog
The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 replaces the National Electricity Policy 2005
n7dd60c8ce25.x: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 comes from the Ministry of Power, not NITI Aayog.
xa: The Act lets **SERCs** fix the **RPO**.
The 2026 draft covers **hybrid RE, BESS, smart grids, Time-of-Day tariffs**.
⚠ NITI Aayog drafted the National **Energy** Policy (**2017**).

n2d5ba6b06a7.s: The energy-intensity targets for 208 industrial units under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 are intended to feed into which mechanism?
o: The National Green Hydrogen Mission alone
The State Energy and Climate Index
n2d5ba6b06a7.x: Greenhouse-gas emission-intensity targets for 208 industrial units under the Energy Conservation Act 2001 feed into the domestic carbon market.
n2d5ba6b06a7.tq: Link the statutory target, the number of industrial units and the specific market mechanism.
xs: The **GHG emission-intensity targets for 208 industrial units** under the **EC Act 2001** feed the **domestic carbon market** — option **(1)**.
They are paired with the **Draft National Electricity Policy 2026** (Jun 2026).
The **State Energy and Climate Index** is a BEE index, not a market mechanism.
xa: **BEE** works under the **Energy Conservation Act 2001** and runs **NMEEE** under NAPCC.
Fiscal incentives (**13 May 2026**): States' incentives now linked to RE adoption → more **PPAs**.

nb9ca3f74bfc.s: India’s stated goal of achieving energy independence is associated with which year?
nb9ca3f74bfc.x: India has set the goal of achieving energy independence by 2047. Net zero emissions is the separate 2070 target.
nb9ca3f74bfc.tq: Distinguish the energy-independence year from the net-zero year.
xs: Energy independence is targeted by **2047** — option **(3)**.
**2070** is the separate **net zero** target.
xa: **INSA**'s framework: energy self-reliance by **2047**, net zero by **2070**.
**AP ICEP-2024** targets **Net Zero by 2047**, **160 GW+** clean energy.
**500 GW** non-fossil capacity by **2030** is the live Panchamrit target.

nf7ac15cb63f.s: Under the Electricity Act, 2003, Renewable Purchase Obligations are fixed by:
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
nf7ac15cb63f.x: The Electricity Act 2003 enables State Electricity Regulatory Commissions to fix Renewable Purchase Obligations.
xa: The Act requires both the **National Electricity Policy 2005** and the **Tariff Policy 2006** (revised **2016**).
The **Central Electricity Authority** prepares the **National Generation Adequacy Plan 2026-27 to 2035-36**.
Electricity is a **concurrent subject** — **Entry 38, List III**.

n6b97e2384d7.s: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 proposes how much pumped storage hydropower capacity by 2047?
n6b97e2384d7.x: It proposes 100 GW of pumped storage by 2047, along with Time-of-Day tariffs.
xa: The draft also covers **hybrid RE, BESS** and **smart grids**, and replaces **NEP 2005**.
It comes from the **Ministry of Power**.

nc4a7863153a.s: The Entropy Effect, as discussed in energy-sector debates, refers to the risk that:
o: nuclear expansion automatically eliminates all import dependence
rapid decarbonisation without adequate buffers may increase grid volatility
slow electrification always reduces grid volatility
fuel subsidies cause a permanent fall in renewable generation
nc4a7863153a.x: The Entropy Effect describes the possibility that rapid decarbonisation without sufficient buffers can raise grid volatility, as observed in the Netherlands and Spain.
nc4a7863153a.tq: Apply the definition to the cause-effect relationship rather than selecting a general decarbonisation statement.
xs: The **"Entropy Effect"** is the risk that **rapid decarbonisation without buffers** raises **grid volatility** — option **(2)**.
The **Economic Survey 2025-26** cites the experience of the **Netherlands and Spain**.
xa: Other debates: import reliance **88% crude, 51% gas**; ~**25 GW** stranded gas capacity.
The **Draft National Electricity Policy 2026** answers with **BESS**, **100 GW PSH by 2047** and smart grids.

n4a6711876e7.s: For tradable fuels, the Integrated Energy Policy recommended:
o: Free pricing only for imported products
A universal price subsidy irrespective of income
n4a6711876e7.x: It recommended market-determined or trade-parity pricing for tradable fuels, with subsidies targeted to the poor.
xa: Pricing reforms followed: **petrol** deregulation **June 2010**, **diesel** **October 2014**.
**LPG subsidy** via DBT (**PAHAL**) — **2015**.
The government has cut **excise duty** on petrol and diesel during price spikes.

n8dcca1a3996.s: On fuel subsidies, the Integrated Energy Policy recommended:
o: A general price subsidy for all consumers
n8dcca1a3996.x: It recommended subsidies targeted to the poor, with trade-parity pricing, not a general price subsidy.
xa: Pricing logic: **trade-parity pricing + targeted subsidy**.
**PAHAL** (**2015**) delivered the LPG subsidy via **DBT**.
IEA's strategic oil stock standard: **90 days** of net imports.

n425eae8f235.s: Diesel prices in India were deregulated in:
n425eae8f235.x: Diesel was deregulated in October 2014; petrol in June 2010.
xa: The **Integrated Energy Policy** recommended **trade-parity pricing** + **targeted** subsidies.
It was approved by the Cabinet in **December 2008**.
It also recommended building **strategic oil reserves**.

nf4fa825114f.s: Fossil fuels account for nearly what share of India's commercial primary energy supply?
nf4fa825114f.x: Fossil fuels constitute nearly 90% of commercial primary energy supply and are increasingly imported.
xa: Import reliance (**2 Jul 2026**): **88% crude, 51% gas**.
MoPNG target: cut oil imports **10%** from the **2014-15** level by **2022**.
Primary energy import dependence: **31% (2012)** → **36-55% (2040)**.

nb6af350cf66.s: The Ministry of Power, earlier the Ministry of Energy Sources, became an independent ministry on:
nb6af350cf66.x: It became independent on 2 July 1992; oil and gas belong to MoPNG.
xa: Electricity is a **concurrent subject** — **Entry 38, List III**.
**MoPNG**'s regulator is **PNGRB** (Act **2006**); **OIL India** is a Navratna under it.
The **Draft National Electricity Policy 2026** comes from the **Ministry of Power** and replaces **NEP 2005**.

ncb3553ee9ad.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the stated missions of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy?
ncb3553ee9ad.x: MNRE's missions include energy security, a larger share of clean power, energy availability and access, affordability and equity. Exclusive dependence on imported energy is not a mission.
ncb3553ee9ad.tq: Find the option that reverses the objective of an energy ministry.
xs: **Exclusive dependence on imported energy** is not an MNRE mission — option **(1)**.
MNRE's five missions: **energy security**, **bigger share of clean power**, **energy availability + access**, **affordability** and **equity** — so options (2), (3) and (4) are all missions.
xa: This list of all five missions was the **APPSC-G2 2025** key.
MNRE evolved from **DNES 1982** → **MNES 1992** → **MNRE 2006**.
India's import reliance: **88% crude, 51% gas** — why energy security tops the agenda.

n99fe3ad38f8.s: India's new NDC (2031–35) targets a cut in the emissions intensity of GDP by 2035 of:
n99fe3ad38f8.x: The new NDC targets a 47% intensity cut and 60% non-fossil capacity by 2035; 45% and 50% are the 2030 targets.
xa: The earlier NDC targeted **33-35%**.
**Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy** went to **UNFCCC** at **COP27 (2022)**.

n2231b5abe5d.s: Before clean-cooking access expanded, about how many people in India relied on solid biomass for cooking?
n2231b5abe5d.x: The baseline was about 500 million relying on solid biomass, with about 304 million without electricity.
xa: Now: **near-universal household electrification** + expanded clean cooking access.
Supply hours (Jul 2026): **22.6 h rural / 23.4 h urban**; peak shortage **0.03%**.
Schemes behind it: **DDUGJY**, **Saubhagya**, **PMUY**.

ndbef5bddd4f.s: About how much gas-based power capacity in India is described as stranded?
ndbef5bddd4f.x: About 25 GW of gas capacity is stranded, and net-zero investment needs exceed $20 trillion.
xa: The ES 2025-26 "**Entropy Effect**": fast decarbonisation without buffers raises grid volatility.
Net zero target: **2070** (Panchamrit).

nenvironment-7-14.s: Under the Panchamrit targets, India aims for non-fossil capacity of ____ by 2030.
nenvironment-7-14.x: Panchamrit targets 500 GW non-fossil capacity, 50% energy from renewables, 1 billion tonnes less emissions and 45% lower carbon intensity by 2030, and net zero by 2070.
n: India targets 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
India targets meeting 50% of its energy requirements from renewable energy by 2030. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
India targets reducing projected cumulative carbon emissions by 1 billion tonnes by 2030. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
India targets reducing carbon intensity by 45% by 2030. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
India targets achieving Net Zero by 2070. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
xa: Updated NDC (**2022**): **50%** installed capacity non-fossil by **2030**.
New NDC: **60%** non-fossil + **47%** intensity cut by **2035**.
Non-fossil share: **51.55%** on **30 Nov 2025**.

n5f0b25ab083.s: In the Constitution, 'Electricity' is placed under:
n5f0b25ab083.x: Electricity is a concurrent subject, placed under Entry 38 of List III.
xa: The **Electricity Act 2003** requires a **National Electricity Policy 2005** and a **Tariff Policy 2006** (revised **2016**).
Under the Electricity Act 2003, **SERCs** fix the **RPO** (Renewable Purchase Obligation).
The **Ministry of Power** became an independent ministry on **2 July 1992**.

n7deac8a3434.s: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy received the name MNRE in:
n7deac8a3434.x: It began as DNES in 1982, became MNES in 1992 and was renamed MNRE in 2006.
xa: Ministry of Power became independent on **2 July 1992**.
Electricity is a **concurrent subject**: **Entry 38, List III**.
**PNGRB** (Act **2006**) is the regulator under **MoPNG**.

naa7218cc793.s: The first in-depth review of India's energy policies was published by which institution?
naa7218cc793.x: The first in-depth review of India's energy policies was published by the International Energy Agency in 2020, in association with NITI Aayog.
naa7218cc793.tq: Identify the publishing institution rather than the associated Indian body.
xs: The first in-depth review of India's energy policies was by the **International Energy Agency (IEA)** — option **(3)**.
It was the **India 2020 Energy Policy Review**, released with **NITI Aayog** in **January 2020** (APPSC 2018 key).
**WEF** publishes the **Energy Transition Index**; **BEE** the **State Energy and Climate Index**.
xa: IEA is an **OECD-affiliated** body headquartered in **Paris**.
IEA reports: **World Energy Outlook**, **India Energy Outlook**, **Global Methane Tracker**, **Electricity Market Report**.
Exam distractors: **World Energy Council**, **OPEC**, **IRENA**.

nd72f9e6f71e.s: The report 'Renewables Integration in India 2021' was brought out by:
o: NITI Aayog and the International Energy Agency
MNRE and the International Renewable Energy Agency
Central Electricity Authority and the World Bank
Bureau of Energy Efficiency and the World Economic Forum
nd72f9e6f71e.x: Renewables Integration in India 2021 was prepared by NITI Aayog with the IEA (APPSC-G1 2022 key). IRENA, the World Bank and WEF are common distractors; WEF publishes the Energy Transition Index and BEE the State Energy and Climate Index.
nd72f9e6f71e.tq: RE Integration in India 2021 = NITI + IEA.
xs: **Renewables Integration in India 2021** was by **NITI Aayog and the International Energy Agency** — option **(1)** (APPSC-G1 2022 key).
**IRENA**, the **World Bank** and **WEF** are distractors; **WEF** publishes the **Energy Transition Index**, and **BEE** the **State Energy and Climate Index**.
xa: IEA and NITI Aayog also released the **India 2020 Energy Policy Review** in **January 2020**.
The **Central Electricity Authority** prepares the **National Generation Adequacy Plan 2026-27 to 2035-36**.

naf628db2c0c.s: The three components of Phase I of the National Bioenergy Programme are:
o: Solar pumps, wind farms and fuel cells
Coal gasification, oil refining and hydrogen storage
naf628db2c0c.x: The three parts are waste-to-energy, biomass and biogas.
naf628db2c0c.tq: Test the exact composition of the programme rather than its broader renewable-energy context.
xs: Phase I of the **National Bioenergy Programme** has three parts: **waste-to-energy, biomass and biogas** — option **(4)**.
**Solar pumps** belong to **PM-KUSUM**; **fuel cells** and **rooftop solar** are examples of distributed energy resources, not bioenergy components.
xa: The programme runs **2021-26**, with a Phase I outlay of **₹858 crore**.
**PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana**: rooftop solar for **1 crore households**.
**PM-KUSUM**: solar pumps + decentralised plants.

n33c5fd7c837.s: Which of the following set consists entirely of distributed energy resources?
o: Battery storage, biomass generators, fuel cells and rooftop solar PV
Large hydropower dams, coal plants, fuel cells and refineries
Battery storage, oil terminals, nuclear reactors and rooftop solar PV
Coal mines, biomass generators, gas pipelines and fuel cells
n33c5fd7c837.x: Battery storage, biomass generators, fuel cells and rooftop solar PV all qualify as distributed energy resources.
n33c5fd7c837.tq: Check every item against the small, consumer-near generation or storage concept.
xs: **Battery storage, biomass generators, fuel cells and rooftop solar PV** are all distributed energy resources — option **(1)** (UPSC 2024 key: all four).
DERs are **small generation/storage units near the consumer**; large dams, coal plants, refineries, oil terminals, nuclear reactors and pipelines are centralised assets, not DERs.
xa: DERs turn users into "**prosumers**" and **ease grid load**.
DER policy vehicles: **PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana** (rooftop solar for **1 crore households**) and **PM-KUSUM** (solar pumps + decentralised plants).
AP: **virtual net metering** with a focus on **SC/ST** households.

nccaa6e71768.s: A household with rooftop solar and battery storage that uses part of its power and sells the surplus to the grid is called a:
nccaa6e71768.x: A consumer who also produces or stores electricity is a prosumer; DERs turn consumers into prosumers.
xa: Qualifying DERs: **battery storage, biomass generators, fuel cells, rooftop solar PV** (UPSC 2024 key).
**PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana**: rooftop solar for **1 crore households**.
AP uses **virtual net metering**, focused on **SC/ST** households.

n891a9a46c23.s: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana aims to provide rooftop solar for how many households?
n891a9a46c23.x: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana focuses on rooftop solar for one crore households.
xa: Both schemes are **DER policy vehicles** (Nov 2025; Mar 2026).
AP: **virtual net metering** for **SC/ST** households.

n0cba1083c37.s: Andhra Pradesh's virtual net metering under its distributed energy policy focuses on:
n0cba1083c37.x: Andhra Pradesh has introduced virtual net metering with a focus on SC/ST households.
xa: **NEDCAP** is AP's state nodal agency for renewable energy.
AP's **ICEP-2024**: **160 GW+** clean energy, **₹10 lakh crore** investment, **7.5 lakh jobs**, **Net Zero by 2047**.
First ICEP project: SAEL's **600 MW** solar in **Kadapa** (Rayalaseema).

n146e6e6b00b.s: Under the Renewable Purchase Obligation, which entities must buy a prescribed share of power from renewable sources?
o: DISCOMs and open-access or captive users
n146e6e6b00b.x: RPO requires DISCOMs and open-access or captive users to buy a prescribed share of renewable power; SERCs fix the obligation.
xa: The Electricity Act 2003 also requires the **National Electricity Policy 2005** and **Tariff Policy 2006** (revised **2016**).
Fiscal incentives (**13 May 2026**) linked to RE adoption → more **PPAs**.
RE (incl. large hydro) stood at **253.96 GW** on **30 Nov 2025**.

n61ac68a272b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about IREDA?
o: It was listed on the stock exchanges in November 2023
It promotes, develops and finances renewable-energy projects
It was set up in 1987 under the Ministry of Power
It received Navratna status in April 2024
n61ac68a272b.x: IREDA was set up in 1987 under MNRE, not the Ministry of Power.
xa: MNRE lineage: **DNES 1982** → **MNES 1992** → **MNRE 2006**.
Sovereign green bonds were first issued by the **RBI** for the Government in **Jan 2023**.
Net-zero financing need: **over $20 trillion** by **2070**.

n6bb28f9cc21.s: India's first sovereign green bonds were issued in:
n6bb28f9cc21.x: They were first issued in January 2023; proceeds are ring-fenced for climate or environmental projects.
xa: **IREDA** was set up in **1987** under **MNRE**; **Navratna** in **Apr 2024**.
**RPO**: DISCOMs must buy a set share of power from RE.
DERs (UPSC 2024): **battery storage, biomass generators, fuel cells, rooftop solar PV** — all four.

n34ec98961c2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra Pradesh's Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024 (ICEP-2024)?
o: Its first project is SAEL's 600 MW solar plant in Kadapa
It targets 160 GW+ of clean energy
It targets Rs 10 lakh crore of investment and 7.5 lakh jobs
It targets net zero for the State by 2070
n34ec98961c2.x: ICEP-2024 targets net zero by 2047; 2070 is India's national target.
xa: **NEDCAP** is AP's state nodal agency.
**ASSET** aims to cut power purchase cost to **₹4.20/unit by 2030**.
AP's DER push includes **virtual net metering** for **SC/ST** households.

n90c44b3bb1d.s: Which body is Andhra Pradesh's state nodal agency for new and renewable energy?
n90c44b3bb1d.x: NEDCAP (New and Renewable Energy Development Corporation of AP) is the state nodal agency. APGENCO is the state generation company, APERC the electricity regulator and APTRANSCO the transmission utility.
xs: **NEDCAP** is Andhra Pradesh's **state nodal agency** for renewable energy — option **(1)**.
It is AP's counterpart to **MNRE**, the Centre's nodal ministry for all new and renewable energy.
xa: AP's **ICEP-2024**: **160 GW+** clean energy, **Net Zero by 2047**.
AP: **virtual net metering** with focus on **SC/ST** households.
First ICEP project: SAEL's **600 MW** solar in **Kadapa** (Rayalaseema).

n669976e1d2b.s: The International Energy Agency (IEA), an OECD-affiliated energy policy body, is headquartered at:
n669976e1d2b.x: The IEA is headquartered in Paris; Abu Dhabi hosts IRENA, Vienna hosts OPEC and Gurugram hosts the International Solar Alliance.
xa: IEA reports: **Global Methane Tracker** (annual), **Electricity Market Report**, **Energy Efficiency Report**, **Net Zero Roadmap**.
With **NITI Aayog**: **India 2020 Energy Policy Review** and **Renewables Integration in India 2021**.
Exam distractors: **World Energy Council**, **OPEC**, **IRENA**.

nb69c490722e.s: The National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE) is located in:
nb69c490722e.x: NIWE is in Chennai; the Gurugram solar R&D body is NISE and NIBE is at Kapurthala.
xa: ⚠ **NISE** = solar, Gurugram; **NIWE** = wind, Chennai; **NIBE** = bio-energy, Kapurthala.
NIWE is the **nodal agency for the wind roadmap**.
**DHRE, IIT Roorkee** gives technical support for small hydro but is **not** under MNRE's control.

n416cd1d9444.s: IREDA, a PSU and NBFC under MNRE, was set up in:
n416cd1d9444.x: IREDA was set up in 1987; 1992 is when MNES was formed.
xa: IREDA signed an MoU with **IIT Bhubaneswar** (APPSC 2024).
⚠ **NISE** = solar, **Gurugram**; **NIWE** = wind, **Chennai**; **NIBE** = bio-energy, **Kapurthala**.
**SECI** implements the **National Solar Mission**.

na16a18ab5de.s: IREDA signed a Memorandum of Understanding for innovation and research in renewable energy with which institution?
na16a18ab5de.x: IREDA's MoU for innovation and research in renewable energy was with IIT Bhubaneswar (APPSC 2024). IIT Tirupati is linked to an AP solar Centre of Excellence with UNSW, and IIT Roorkee's DHRE supports small hydro; IIT Madras is not mentioned.
xs: IREDA's MoU for RE innovation and research was with **IIT Bhubaneswar** — option **(1)** (APPSC 2024).
**IIT Tirupati** is linked to AP's **Solar CoE with UNSW** (31 Jul 2026); **IIT Roorkee** hosts **DHRE** (small hydro support).
xa: IREDA: **PSU + NBFC** under MNRE, est. **1987**.
It funds itself partly through **green bonds**.
⚠ **DHRE, IIT Roorkee** is **not** under MNRE's control.

n20d433f5f29.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about renewable-energy initiatives in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The Tata project is a 5,000 MW floating solar project implemented by SECI
The Tata Renewable project involves an investment of ₹5,750 crore
A solar Centre of Excellence is associated with IIT Tirupati and UNSW
Tata Renewable has a planned 800 MW hybrid project
n20d433f5f29.x: The Tata project is an 800 MW hybrid project, not a 5,000 MW SECI floating solar project.
xa: **SECI** is the implementing arm for the **National Solar Mission** and wind projects.
⚠ IREDA's research MoU was with **IIT Bhubaneswar**, not IIT Tirupati.

nf1ba902850f.s: The National Clean Energy Fund was primarily established to fund:
o: Oil and gas exploration by private companies
Research and innovative projects in clean energy technologies
nf1ba902850f.x: The NCEF was intended to fund research and innovative projects in clean energy technologies, promote renewable energy technologies and reduce carbon emissions.
nf1ba902850f.tq: Match the fund with its stated purpose rather than its revenue source.
xs: The **NCEF** was set up to fund **research and innovative projects in clean energy technologies** — option **(4)**.
In exam wording: **promote renewable energy technologies and reduce carbon emissions** (APPSC-G2 2025 key).
xa: Created in **2010-11**, financed by a **clean energy cess on coal** (lignite and peat too).
Cess rose from **₹50/tonne** to **₹400/tonne**; later renamed **Clean Environment Cess**.
Coal cess subsumed into **GST Compensation Cess** (**July 2017**) → NCEF lost its dedicated inflow.

n46dba6ce6b0.s: In July 2017, the clean energy cess on coal that financed the National Clean Energy Fund was subsumed into the:
n46dba6ce6b0.x: It was subsumed into the GST Compensation Cess, ending NCEF's dedicated inflow; the cess had risen from Rs 50 to Rs 400 per tonne.
xa: NCEF purpose: fund **research and innovative projects** in clean energy (APPSC-G2 2025).
The cess was later renamed **Clean Environment Cess**.

n56e9d1484d6.s: One Sun One World One Grid (OSOWOG) refers to:
o: A national coal transmission grid under the Ministry of Coal
A transnational solar grid under the International Solar Alliance
A biofuel blending programme under the Global Biofuels Alliance
A global wind-purchasing platform operated by IREDA
n56e9d1484d6.x: OSOWOG is a transnational solar grid under the International Solar Alliance; its roadmap was operationalised at the 8th ISA Assembly in New Delhi. It is not a coal grid, a biofuel programme or an IREDA platform.
n56e9d1484d6.tq: Distinguish the grid concept from other renewable-energy programmes by its transnational scope.
xs: **OSOWOG** is a **transnational solar grid under the International Solar Alliance** — option **(2)**.
Its roadmap was operationalised at the **8th ISA Assembly** in **New Delhi**.
xa: **Green Grids Initiative-OSOWOG** was launched by **India and UK** at **COP26 Glasgow (2021)**.
The **Global Biofuels Alliance** (G20 New Delhi, **Sept 2023**) promotes sustainable biofuels — a separate initiative.

nac3ddb9463b.s: The International Solar Alliance was launched at COP21 (2015) by India and:
nac3ddb9463b.x: ISA was launched by India and France; GGI-OSOWOG by India and the UK, and LeadIT by India and Sweden.
xa: **LeadIT** focuses on **low-carbon heavy industry**.
ISA HQ: **Gurugram**.

n4e3a44a153c.s: The headquarters of the International Solar Alliance is located at:
n4e3a44a153c.x: The ISA, launched by India and France at COP21 in Paris in 2015, is headquartered in Gurugram (Haryana). Paris was only the launch venue, New Delhi hosted the 8th ISA Assembly, and Abu Dhabi hosts IRENA.
xs: The **ISA** is headquartered at **Gurugram** — option **(1)**.
**Paris** was the launch venue (**COP21, 2015**); **New Delhi** hosted the **8th ISA Assembly**.
xa: ⚠ Gurugram also hosts **NISE**, MNRE's solar R&D focal point.
ISA is an **India + France** initiative and a **solar deployment** platform.

n6c96e5f4af1.s: The 8th Mission Innovation ministerial meeting held with the 14th Clean Energy Ministerial in July 2023 was hosted at:
n6c96e5f4af1.x: The combined MI-8 and 14th Clean Energy Ministerial event was held in Goa in July 2023.
n6c96e5f4af1.tq: Match the energy event with its host city.
xs: **MI-8** with the **14th Clean Energy Ministerial** (**July 2023**) was hosted at **Goa** — option **(3)** (APPSC 2024).
**Gandhinagar** hosted **RE-INVEST** (4th edition, Sept 2024); **New Delhi** hosted the **8th ISA Assembly**.
xa: **India Energy Week**: **2023** Bengaluru, **2024** Goa, **2025** New Delhi.
8th ISA Assembly: **137 nations**, **36 organisations**.

n7820fb345a3.s: The two-year biodiesel project of the Belgian firm VITO, launched in April 2023, is located at:
n7820fb345a3.x: VITO's two-year biodiesel project (April 2023) is at Ayodhya, UP (APPSC 2023). Diu is the first 100% solar-powered UT in daytime, Vaikom is on the route of the solar ferry Aditya, and Gandhinagar hosted RE-INVEST 2024.
xs: **VITO**'s **2-year biodiesel project** (Apr 2023) is at **Ayodhya**, UP — option **(1)** (APPSC 2023).
**Diu** = first **100% solar UT** (daytime); **Vaikom** = solar ferry **Aditya**; **Gandhinagar** = **RE-INVEST** 4th edition.
xa: VITO is a **Belgian** firm.
First solar ferry **Aditya** dates to **2017**.

n1f6a0459ca5.s: India became the world's 3rd-largest solar power producer by overtaking:
n1f6a0459ca5.x: India overtook Japan; it also ranks 3rd in total renewable capacity and 4th in wind.
xa: ⚠ Older notes put India **4th** in total RE capacity (IYB 2026).
India was the **2nd-largest solar growth market** in 2025.

n00baef07ca1.s: By December 2025, the non-fossil share of India's installed power capacity was reported as:
n00baef07ca1.x: The share was 51.93%, so the COP26 Panchamrit goal of 50% by 2030 was met five years early.
xa: Installed capacity (15 Aug 2026): ~**552 GW**; non-fossil **>54%**.
⚠ Coal is still ~**55%** of primary energy and **>70%** of generation (Aug 2026).

n065eef71445.s: India's reported wind-energy target for 2030 is:
n065eef71445.x: The reported wind-energy targets are 100 GW by 2030 and 155 GW by 2035.
xa: India ranks **4th** in the world in wind.
**NIWE** (Chennai) is the nodal agency for the **wind roadmap**.
Solar capacity: **164.59 GW** (15 Aug 2026).

n9cff898c1bd.s: India became the first country in the world to establish a Ministry specifically for:
n9cff898c1bd.x: India was the first country in the world to set up a ministry for non-conventional energy sources.
n9cff898c1bd.tq: Direct recall of a distinctive international first.
xs: India was the **first country in the world** to set up a ministry for **non-conventional energy sources** — option **(2)** (APPSC 2023).
That ministry was the **MNES**, created in **1992** by upgrading **DNES** (**1982**).
xa: MNES was renamed **MNRE** in **2006**.
The earliest body was **CASE** (**1981**).
Institutions under MNRE: **NISE** (Gurugram, solar), **NIWE** (Chennai, wind), **NIBE** (Kapurthala, bio-energy).

naaeb2c87a21.s: PM Surya Sarovar projects are required to add battery energy storage systems (BESS) having a minimum duration of:
naaeb2c87a21.x: PM Surya Sarovar projects must add BESS with a minimum storage duration of two hours.
naaeb2c87a21.tq: Identify the minimum technical specification from close duration options.
xs: **PM Surya Sarovar** projects must add **BESS** of at least **2 hours** — option **(2)** (1 Aug 2026).
Globally, **25%** of new utility-scale solar is paired with batteries (**IRENA 2025**) — battery storage is a key distributed energy resource.
xa: Rooftop Solar Phase-II (target **40,000 MW**) was **subsumed in PM Surya Ghar**.
Bio-power stands at ~**11.75 GW** (Aug 2026).
Green-hydrogen **fuel cells** are more efficient than combustion engines.

n2289d2603fa.s: Phase-II of the Grid-Connected Rooftop Solar Programme was subsumed in:
n2289d2603fa.x: Phase-II of the rooftop programme (40,000 MW target) was subsumed in PM Surya Ghar.
xa: Bio-power capacity: ~**11.75 GW** (Aug 2026).
Off-grid tribal: New Solar Power Scheme under **PM JANMAN + DA JGUA** electrified **4,919 households** in 2025.

nca988d6db96.s: Compared with combustion engines, green-hydrogen fuel cells are generally:
nca988d6db96.x: Green-hydrogen fuel cells are more efficient than combustion engines.
xa: Battery storage: **25%** of new utility-scale solar paired with batteries (IRENA 2025).
**PM Surya Sarovar** projects need **≥2-hour BESS**.

n405d758fb42.s: Which type of coal has the highest carbon content?
n405d758fb42.x: In descending order: anthracite, bituminous, sub-bituminous, lignite, peat.
xa: **Peat** is the **first stage of wood to coal**.
**Sub-bituminous** lies between bituminous and lignite and is used in **power plants**.
**Bituminous** is the most widely used type and the **coking grade**.

nf84bf433f7c.s: Which type of coal is most widely used and is also the coking grade?
nf84bf433f7c.x: Bituminous coal is the most widely used type and includes the coking grade.
nf84bf433f7c.tq: Identify the coal type by its use and industrial grade.
xs: **Bituminous** coal is the most widely used type and the **coking grade** — option **(1)**.
It has **60-80%** carbon (some notes say 40-80%) and occurs in **Jharkhand, Odisha, WB, Chhattisgarh, MP**.
**Lignite** is "brown coal" with **40-55%** carbon; **sub-bituminous** is used in power plants.
xa: **Jharia** is the largest **coking-coal** field.
Coking coal is imported mainly from **Australia**.

n4cf0b0525f6.s: Which of the following set of places is associated with lignite occurrences mentioned in the classification?
n4cf0b0525f6.x: Neyveli, Palana and Lakhimpur are identified with lignite occurrences. The other groups are associated with major coalfields of higher-rank coal regions.
n4cf0b0525f6.tq: Recognise the lignite-location group instead of a group of Gondwana coalfields.
xs: **Neyveli, Palana and Lakhimpur** are lignite sites — option **(1)**.
**Korba, Raigarh** (Chhattisgarh), **Singrauli** (MP), **Talcher, Deogarh** (Odisha), **Raniganj** (WB), **Jharia, Bokaro, Giridih** (Jharkhand) are coalfields.
xa: Neyveli is in **Tamil Nadu**, Palana in **Rajasthan**, Lakhimpur in **Assam**.
Lignite: **40-55%** carbon, "**brown coal**"; reserves **47.295 BT**.

n82a4bb5dbc2.s: Jharia coalfield is particularly noted for which of the following?
o: Lignite deposits in the Satpura Basin
The first commercial coal mine in India
n82a4bb5dbc2.x: Jharia in Jharkhand is the largest coking-coal field and is situated in the Damodar Valley.
n82a4bb5dbc2.tq: Directly distinguish the coalfield by its special characteristic.
xs: **Jharia** (Jharkhand) is India's **largest coking-coal field** — option **(2)**.
The **first coal mine** was at **Raniganj** (**1774**); **Tertiary coal** is at **Mawlong** (Meghalaya) and Makum (Assam); **Satpura** is an MP basin.
xa: **Jharkhand** has India's **largest coal reserves**; other Jharkhand fields: **Bokaro, Giridih, Karanpura**.
The **Damodar valley** holds about **one-fourth** of India's coal.
Coking coal is a **Gondwana** coal; the MMDR amendment made it a **Critical and Strategic Mineral**.

n59f6ed98920.s: To improve coal quality for its RTPP and Dr NTTPS units, APGENCO buys washed coal from:
n59f6ed98920.x: APGENCO buys washed coal from MCL's IB Valley Washery, posts engineers at mines to stop grade slippage and seeks better coal from SCCL. The other sources are not the ones stated.
n59f6ed98920.tq: APGENCO washed coal = MCL IB Valley Washery.
xs: APGENCO buys **washed coal from MCL's IB Valley Washery** — option **(1)**.
It feeds **RTPP 600 MW** and **Dr NTTPS 500/800 MW** units.
xa: APGENCO also **posts engineers at mines** to stop grade slippage.
It seeks **better coal from SCCL**.
IB Valley (**Deogarh**) is in **Odisha**.

n9bba8c5dc0c.s: Mawlong coalfield, associated with Tertiary coal, is located in:
n9bba8c5dc0c.x: Mawlong is in Meghalaya and is associated with Tertiary coal.
xa: **Tertiary coal**: NE India and J&K, about **2%** of reserves.
⚠ **Gondwana** = **98%**, coking coal; **Tertiary** = NE India, about 2%.
**Makum** (Assam) is another NE coalfield.

n0e36502a860.s: Which State leads India in lignite resources (estimated at 47.295 billion tonnes)?
n0e36502a860.x: Lignite resources are 47.295 billion tonnes, with Tamil Nadu (Neyveli) leading, followed by Rajasthan and Gujarat.
xa: Lignite ("**brown coal**") has **40-55%** carbon.
Other lignite sites: **Palana** (Rajasthan), **Lakhimpur** (Assam); **Barmer** (Rajasthan).

naa4f866e635.s: The Neyveli lignite field is located in:
naa4f866e635.x: Neyveli is in Tamil Nadu; Bokaro and Giridih are in Jharkhand and Raigarh in Chhattisgarh.
xa: Other Jharkhand fields: **Jharia** (largest coking coal), **Karanpura**.
**Korba** (Chhattisgarh) lies on the **Hasdeo** (Mahanadi basin).
**Singareni** is in **Telangana**.

n405c14d7f0b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Gondwana coal?
o: It consists predominantly of Tertiary lignite deposits
It accounts for about 98% of India's coal reserves
It is about 250–300 million years old
It occurs in the Damodar, Mahanadi, Son and Godavari valleys
n405c14d7f0b.x: Gondwana coal is not Tertiary lignite; Tertiary deposits are younger and include lignite.
xa: Gondwana coal holds the **coking coal**.
⚠ **Gondwana** = 98%, coking; **Tertiary** = NE India, about 2% (e.g. **Mawlong**, Meghalaya).

nf651a1b1c57.s: Which State has the largest coal reserves in India?
nf651a1b1c57.x: Jharkhand leads; GSI put India's coal resources at 389.421 billion tonnes (1 April 2024).
xa: Reserves are mainly in **Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh**, WB, MP, Telangana, Maharashtra.
⚠ Older notes: about **344 BT** and "**4th largest in the world**".

n132c25ff9c5.s: India recorded coal production of how much in 2024–25, marking the first year in which production exceeded one billion tonnes?
n132c25ff9c5.x: India recorded 1,047.50 MT of coal production in 2024–25, the first time production crossed one billion tonnes.
n132c25ff9c5.tq: Use the exact production figure and distinguish it from the target and import figures.
xs: Coal output was **1,047.50 MT in 2024-25**, the first year above **1 billion tonnes** — option **(2)**.
xa: Imports fell **7.9%** to **243.62 MT**, saving about **$7.13 billion**.
By Aug 2025 output reached **381.749 MT**.
Coal meets about **55%** of commercial energy needs.

nde8b948288d.s: Coal accounts for approximately what share of India’s commercial energy needs?
nde8b948288d.x: Coal meets about 55% of India’s commercial energy needs.
nde8b948288d.tq: Distinguish the share in commercial energy needs from the higher share in power generation.
xs: Coal meets about **55%** of India's **commercial energy needs** — option **(3)**.
**About 70%** (some notes **71.4%**) is coal's share of **power generation**, not energy needs.

n40597f370ca.s: The planning arm of Coal India Limited is:
n40597f370ca.x: CMPDI is CIL's planning arm; SCCL is a Telangana-GoI company, not a CIL subsidiary.
xa: **SHAKTI policy** (**2017**) replaced the NCDP-2007 linkage regime.
Commercial coal auctions began in **2020**; **134 mines** sold after **12 rounds**.
**Coking coal** is now a **Critical and Strategic Mineral**.

n11c8766ca2c.s: Under the SHAKTI coal linkage policy (2017), coal linkages are given through:
n11c8766ca2c.x: SHAKTI, which replaced the NCDP-2007 regime, gives linkages through auction or tariff-based bidding.
xa: **199 mines** were allocated under the **CMSP Act 2015** and **MMDR Act 1957**.
Revenue-sharing **commercial auctions** began in **2020**.

nc2f7fa22347.s: Which of the following can be produced through coal gasification?
nc2f7fa22347.x: Ethanol and urea can be produced through coal gasification; nitroglycerine is not among the stated products.
xa: Urea comes via **ammonia for fertilisers**.
Other products: **SNG, methanol, hydrogen, DME, ammonium nitrate**.
**Talcher** will host the first gasification-based fertiliser plant (by Dec **2027**).

nee6de6e03b8.s: The Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification, approved on 13 May 2026, has an outlay of:
nee6de6e03b8.x: The outlay is ₹37,500 crore, with incentives up to 20% of plant and machinery cost, capped at ₹5,000 crore per project.
xa: It targets about **75 MT** toward the **100 MT** goal; coal linkage tenure extended to **30 years**.
Earlier scheme (**2024**): **₹8,500 crore** for public and private projects.
Status (5 Sep 2026): **no bidders** so far.

nd57fcb41bc4.s: Commercial coal blocks get a 50% rebate on revenue share if at least what share of their output goes to gasification?
nd57fcb41bc4.x: Commercial blocks get a 50% rebate on revenue share if at least 10% of their output is used for gasification.
xa: **₹37,500 crore** scheme: incentive up to **20%** of plant cost, cap **₹5,000 crore** per project.
Mission goal: **100 MT** by **2030**.
14th-round mines carried the first **UCG** clauses.

nd2bec7c43df.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about underground coal gasification (UCG)?
o: It is an in-situ process injecting air or oxygen and steam into coal seams to make syngas
The MoEFCC expert panel waived the 300 m minimum depth for UCG pilots
Groundwater contamination is a risk associated with it
It can use coal that is deep, thin or otherwise unmineable
nd2bec7c43df.x: The MoEFCC expert panel refused to waive the 300 m minimum depth.
xa: **CBM** ("sweet gas") is methane held in coal seams.
The **14th** commercial round had the first agreements with **UCG** clauses.
The **₹37,500 crore** gasification scheme drew **no bidders**.

n64e768b62b4.s: Revenue-sharing commercial coal auctions in India began in:
n64e768b62b4.x: Revenue-sharing commercial coal auctions began in 2020.
n64e768b62b4.tq: Place the auction mechanism in time against the nearby years of the CMSP Act, SHAKTI policy and later auction rounds.
xs: Revenue-sharing **commercial coal auctions** began in **2020** — option **(3)**.
**2015** is the **CMSP Act**; **2017** is **SHAKTI**; **2025** saw the **13th round** (**21 Aug 2025**).
xa: After **12 rounds**: **134 mines** sold, peak rated capacity **277.04 MTPA**.
**14th round**: mines to **Reliance Industries + Axis Energy**, first **UCG** clauses (2 May 2026).

n986ac7749fe.s: The agreements in the 14th round were significant because they were the first agreements to include clauses relating to:
n986ac7749fe.x: The 14th-round agreements were the first to include underground coal gasification clauses.
n986ac7749fe.tq: Link the special contractual clause with the correct technology rather than with the auction mechanism itself.
xs: 14th-round agreements were the first with **underground coal gasification (UCG)** clauses — option **(4)** (2 May 2026).
**Tariff-based bidding** belongs to the **SHAKTI** linkage policy (**2017**), not these clauses.
xa: **UCG** is an **in-situ** process: air/oxygen + steam injected into coal seams → syngas underground.
UCG uses deep, thin or unmineable coal; risk: **groundwater contamination**.
MoEFCC panel refused to waive the **300 m** minimum depth for UCG pilots.

nc986d13a8d2.s: Revenue-sharing commercial coal auctions began in India in:
nc986d13a8d2.x: They began in 2020; the 13th round opened on 21 August 2025.
xa: Raniganj (Sitarampur) is in **West Bengal**.
After **12 rounds**: **134 mines**, **277.04 MTPA**; the 13th round offered **14 mines**.
The **14th round** brought the first **UCG** clauses (**2 May 2026**).

n792d34d0e3c.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a problem affecting the Indian coal sector?
o: Excessive availability of high-quality domestic coking coal
n792d34d0e3c.x: The identified problems include poor quality, movement bottlenecks, low washery use, rising coking-coal imports and administrative issues. Excessive availability of high-quality domestic coking coal is not a stated problem.
n792d34d0e3c.tq: Find the option that reverses the sectoral problem described.
xs: **Excessive availability of high-quality domestic coking coal** is not a problem — option **(1)**; in fact **coking-coal imports are rising**.
Listed problems (BPSC key: all are problems): **poor quality**, **movement bottlenecks**, **low washery use**, **rising coking-coal imports**, **administrative issues**.
xa: Indian coal: **high ash (35-45%)**, low calorific value.
Coking coal comes mainly from **Australia**.

n0d25fc9dadf.s: The National Coal Gasification Mission aims to gasify how much coal by 2030?
n0d25fc9dadf.x: The National Coal Gasification Mission has a target of gasifying 100 million tonnes of coal by 2030.
n0d25fc9dadf.tq: Recall the mission target and distinguish it from the sub-target under the incentive scheme.
xs: The **National Coal Gasification Mission** aims to gasify **100 million tonnes** of coal by **2030** — option **(1)**.
**75 MT** is what the **₹37,500 crore** surface gasification scheme targets toward that goal.
xa: The Coal Ministry says the target will be met (**26 Apr 2026**).
⚠ EY (Apr 2026): few advanced projects → **100 MT** goal doubtful.
Commercial blocks get a **50%** revenue-share rebate if ≥**10%** of output is gasified.

n94ee8fd6b9c.s: Which of the following is the only commercial-scale coal gasification plant identified in the sector?
o: The Talcher fertiliser plant in Odisha
MCL's IB Valley Washery in Odisha
n94ee8fd6b9c.x: JSPL's plant at Angul, Odisha, is identified as the only commercial-scale coal gasification plant.
n94ee8fd6b9c.tq: Match the project with its distinctive status and location.
xs: **JSPL at Angul (Odisha)** is the **only commercial-scale gasification plant** — option **(1)**.
**BCGCL** (Lakhanpur) and the **Talcher** fertiliser plant are still being built; **IB Valley** is a **washery**.
xa: BCGCL: **BHEL-CIL** JV (**21 May 2024**); **2,500 TPD** coal → **2,000 TPD** ammonium nitrate.
Talcher plant due by **Dec 2027**.

n81861df2ced.s: The ownership pattern of Singareni Collieries Company Limited is:
n81861df2ced.x: SCCL is owned 51% by Telangana and 49% by the Government of India.
n81861df2ced.tq: Watch for the reversed ownership percentages and the swapped governments.
xs: **SCCL** is owned **51% by Telangana** and **49% by the Government of India** — option **(1)**.
This follows the **AP Reorganisation Act Schedule**; existing coal linkages continue.
xa: **Singareni** coalfield is in **Telangana**.
APGENCO seeks **better coal from SCCL**.

nf883a04fba3.s: Which mineral was declared a Critical and Strategic Mineral through an amendment to the MMDR framework, enabling the Centre to auction its leases?
nf883a04fba3.x: Coking coal was declared a Critical and Strategic Mineral, allowing the Centre to auction its leases.
nf883a04fba3.tq: Identify the specific coal variety and avoid substituting the broader category of coal.
xs: **Coking coal** was declared a **Critical and Strategic Mineral** — option **(3)**.
This lets the **Centre** auction its leases under the **MMDR** amendment.
xa: **Jharia** is the largest coking-coal field; coking coal is imported mainly from **Australia**.
Rising **coking-coal imports** are a listed coal-sector problem.
Coking coal is held in **Gondwana** coal.

n5a90b83e481.s: India imports coking coal mainly from:
n5a90b83e481.x: Coking coal is imported mainly from Australia, whereas non-coking coal comes mainly from Indonesia and South Africa.
xa: Coking coal was made a **Critical and Strategic Mineral** under the MMDR amendment.
Gasification-substitutable imports (incl. coking coal) ≈ **₹2.77 lakh crore** in **FY2025**.

nf124d2fb678.s: The Kalol oilfield lies in the:
nf124d2fb678.x: Kalol, like Ankleshwar, is a Cambay Basin field.
xa: **Bombay High** was developed after the **1973** oil shock.
Assam fields: **Digboi (1889)**, Naharkatiya, **Moran**.

nc068feece26.s: Trishna gas project is located in
nc068feece26.x: The Trishna gas project is located in Tripura and is associated with the Tripura Fold Belt.
xs: The **Trishna** gas project is in **Tripura** (**Tripura fold belt**) — option **(3)** (APPSC 2018 key).
The **Tripura fold belt** is not a **Category I** (commercial production) basin.
xa: **Rajasthan**: Mangala and **Dandewala**; **Assam**: Digboi, Naharkatiya, Moran; **AP**: Ravva, KG-D6.
The **Indradhanush** NE gas grid (~**1,656 km**) covers the eight NE States.

n0a524952bfc.s: India's oil industry began in 1889 at which oil field?
n0a524952bfc.x: Digboi (1889) in the Assam-Arakan/Assam Shelf basin marks the start of India's oil industry. Ankleshwar is a Cambay Basin field in Gujarat, Bombay High in the Mumbai Offshore Basin was developed after the 1973 oil shock, and Mangala is a Rajasthan Basin field.
n0a524952bfc.tq: Digboi, Assam = 1889 = India's first oil field.
xs: India's oil industry began at **Digboi** in **1889** — option **(1)**.
Digboi is in the **Assam-Arakan / Assam Shelf** basin.
**Ankleshwar** is a **Cambay** field; **Bombay High** came after the **1973** oil shock; **Mangala** is in **Rajasthan**.
xa: Other Assam fields: **Naharkatiya, Moran**.
Gas was first found in **Assam and Maharashtra (1960s)**.

nd505135729d.s: Shale gas and oil are primarily held in
o: permeable sandstone and extracted without stimulation
coal seams and released mainly by pumping water
fine-grained shale and generally require hydraulic fracturing and horizontal drilling
