nd505135729d.x: Shale hydrocarbons occur in fine-grained shale and require fracking and horizontal drilling. Coal seams hold coal bed methane, while gas hydrates occur as methane-water crystals.
nd505135729d.tq: Discriminate unconventional resources by their host formation and extraction method.
xs: **Shale gas/oil** is held in **fine-grained shale** and needs **fracking + horizontal drilling** — option **(3)**.
**Coal seams** with pumping of water describe **CBM**; **ice-like crystals in deep-sea sediments** are **gas hydrates**.
xa: **Cambay** basin has the **largest shale gas reserves** (APPSC-G1 2017).
Other shale basins: **KG, Cauvery, Damodar, Assam-Arakan, Indo-Gangetic**.
Unconventional gas needs **costly technology**.

n01fdc9c076f.s: Which sedimentary basin of India has the largest shale gas reserves?
n01fdc9c076f.x: The Cambay Basin (Gujarat) has the largest shale gas reserves (APPSC-G1 2017 key). Krishna-Godavari, Cauvery and Damodar are other shale basins, with KG still under study, but none holds the largest reserves.
n01fdc9c076f.tq: Shale gas largest = Cambay; first CBM = Raniganj.
xs: The **Cambay Basin** has India's **largest shale gas reserves** — option **(2)** (APPSC-G1 2017; APPSC 2017 key).
**KG** is under study; **Cauvery** and **Damodar** are other shale basins.
xa: Other shale basins: **Assam-Arakan, Indo-Gangetic**.
Shale needs **fracking + horizontal drilling**.
Cambay fields: **Ankleshwar, Kalol** (Gujarat).

ndeb91702ce2.s: The Andhra Pradesh Gas Infrastructure Corporation holds what share in a consortium with ONGC, OIL, NTPC and British Gas for four KG-basin blocks?
ndeb91702ce2.x: APGIC holds a 10 per cent share in the consortium involving ONGC, OIL, NTPC and British Gas for four KG-basin blocks.
ndeb91702ce2.tq: Direct recall of consortium participation and percentage.
xs: **APGIC** holds **10 per cent** in the consortium with **ONGC, OIL, NTPC and British Gas** — option **(2)**.
The consortium covers **four KG-basin blocks**.
xa: KG fields: **Ravva** (offshore, **Cairn-ONGC**), **KG-D6** (**Reliance-BP**).
AP has both **onshore and offshore** oil; gas + crude from the **Godavari (KG)** basin.

n342300661ab.x: LPG is mainly propane and butane, a by-product of oil refining and gas processing, and heavier than air.
xa: ⚠ **LNG** is lighter than air.
India has **33 crore** LPG connections; domestic gas could supply **30 crore** via PNG.
New SPR plan: about **six weeks** of LPG; levy **₹1.29/kg** on LPG.

n2a32c85f74a.s: In petroleum geology, the impervious bed that seals an oil trap is called the:
n2a32c85f74a.x: The cap rock seals the trap; reservoir rock is porous and permeable, and source rock is organic-rich shale.
xa: Layering by density (top down): **gas, oil, water**.
Commercial oil sits at **crests of anticlines**.

n7789710cf54.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP), 2016?
o: It provides a single licence for conventional and unconventional hydrocarbons
It replaced NELP's revenue-sharing contracts with production-sharing contracts
It gives marketing and pricing freedom
n7789710cf54.x: It is the reverse: HELP brought biddable revenue-sharing contracts in place of NELP's production-sharing contracts.
xa: ⚠ **NELP** = production-sharing; **HELP** = revenue-sharing (APPSC-G1 2017 key).
**OALP** lets companies choose and bid for blocks year-round.

n5e52fb2aa39.s: Under the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP), identification of blocks is supported by the:
n5e52fb2aa39.x: OALP lets companies choose blocks and bid year-round, using data from the National Data Repository.
xa: Its aim: boost **domestic E&P**.
**Samudra Manthan** is open to **OALP block holders**.
OALP works under **HELP (2016)**'s open acreage.

n3bf532e7db3.s: The Discovered Small Fields policy primarily relates to the auction of small fields held by which entities?
n3bf532e7db3.x: Under the Discovered Small Fields policy of 2015, small fields held by ONGC and OIL are auctioned to increase domestic output.
n3bf532e7db3.tq: Direct recall of the concerned public-sector entities.
xs: The **Discovered Small Fields policy** (**2015**) auctions small fields held by **ONGC and OIL** — option **(2)**.
Its aim is to **boost output**.
xa: **HELP** (**2016**): single licence, revenue-sharing.
**OALP**: year-round block bidding via the **National Data Repository**.

n7e7982b06f8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Samudra Manthan?
o: Its outlay of ₹84,084 crore runs up to 2030-31
It is restricted to blocks held by ONGC alone
It is the National Offshore Exploration Scheme
It is a 100 per cent Central Sector scheme
n7e7982b06f8.x: It is open to OALP block holders, not only ONGC.
xa: Covers **seismic mapping + risk drilling** (**50%** support, capped at **₹675 crore** per well).
About **60 deep-water wells**; Cabinet approval **3 Aug 2026**.

ne53bc25be5c.s: Compiling coal statistics, monitoring captive coal blocks and hearing objections on acquisition of coal-bearing land are functions of the:
ne53bc25be5c.x: The Coal Controller's Organisation performs all three functions.
xa: It also does **coal grading** and quality checks.
It is under the **Ministry of Coal**, based in **Kolkata**.
⚠ **Energy Statistics** is a separate publication by **NSO, MoSPI**.

n38d249d5916.s: The publication titled ‘Energy Statistics’ is brought out by the:
o: Coal Controller’s Organisation under the Ministry of Coal
Central Electricity Authority under the Ministry of Power
National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
NITI Aayog under the Ministry of Finance
n38d249d5916.x: Energy Statistics is published by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
n38d249d5916.tq: Identify the publishing authority and avoid swapping it with a sectoral regulator or ministry.
xs: **Energy Statistics** is published by the **NSO** under **MoSPI** — option **(3)**.
The **Coal Controller's Organisation** is the source of **coal statistics**, not Energy Statistics.
xa: Coal Controller's Organisation: **Ministry of Coal**, **Kolkata**.
Coal = **~55%** of primary energy, **>70%** of power generation (Aug 2026).

n49b746db9b4.s: The Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) gas pipeline passes through which states?
o: Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal
n49b746db9b4.x: The HVJ pipeline of GAIL connects Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh; Maharashtra is not on this route.
n49b746db9b4.tq: Use route sequencing and the excluded-state trap to identify the correct corridor.
xs: **HVJ** runs through **Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh** — option **(2)**.
It is a **GAIL** pipeline and does **not** pass through **Maharashtra** (APPSC-G2 2025 key).
xa: **PM Urja Ganga** (JHBDPL): **UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, WB, Odisha**.
**East-West** pipeline: **Kakinada** to **Bharuch**.

nbdd527f78b1.s: The idea of a national gas grid was first proposed in 1955 by:
nbdd527f78b1.x: S. H. Zaheer of RRL Hyderabad (now CSIR-IICT) proposed it; One Nation One Gas Grid began in 2014.
xa: Pipelines (**31 Mar 2025**): **34,223 km** authorised; **25,429 km** operating.
**HVJ** pipeline: **Gujarat - Madhya Pradesh - Uttar Pradesh** (not Maharashtra).
**Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga** = Jagdishpur-Haldia-Bokaro-Dhamra (**JHBDPL**), GAIL.

nb87c7b8e868.s: The East-West gas pipeline runs from Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh to:
nb87c7b8e868.x: The East-West pipeline runs from Kakinada to Bharuch in Gujarat.
xa: ⚠ HVJ does **not** pass through **Maharashtra** (APPSC-G2 2025 key).
Indradhanush NE grid: JV of **IOCL, ONGC, GAIL, OIL, NRL**.

nee4a260b8f1.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with gas hydrates?
nee4a260b8f1.x: Damodar Valley is a major coal bed methane region; gas hydrates are associated with KG, Mahanadi and Andaman offshore.
xa: CBM key areas: **Raniganj, Jharia, Bokaro, Sohagpur**.
**Shale**: largest reserves in **Cambay**.

n2b855ce235e.s: India's targeted share of gas in the energy mix by 2030 is approximately
n2b855ce235e.x: The target is to raise the share of gas in the energy mix from about 6.7 percent to 15 percent by 2030.
n2b855ce235e.tq: Distinguish the present approximate share from the future target.
xs: Gas share target: **15 percent** of the energy mix by **2030** — option **(3)**.
**6.7%** is the current share.
xa: Gas imports: **~47-51%**.
~**25 GW** of gas power is **stranded**.
One Nation One Gas Grid: **>32,000 km**, link all States by **2027**.

n3c3963bd44f.s: The Indradhanush North-East Gas Grid joint venture comprises:
o: IOCL, ONGC, GAIL and OIL only
ONGC, GAIL, OIL and NRL only
IOCL, ONGC, GAIL, OIL and NRL
n3c3963bd44f.x: All five - IOCL, ONGC, GAIL, OIL and NRL - form the joint venture.
xa: Length about **1,656 km** across the **eight NE States**.
**PM Urja Ganga** links the East and North-East to the national grid.

nb68c42510f7.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB)?
o: Authorising geographical areas for city gas distribution
Acting as a statutory regulator under the PNGRB Act, 2006
nb68c42510f7.x: PNGRB does not regulate crude oil production.
xa: It regulates **refining, storage, distribution, marketing and sale** of products and gas.
⚠ UPSC 2025 trap: PNGRB regulates **only two** of the four listed activities.

n6ac7a628d32.s: Which of the following activities is NOT regulated by the PNGRB?
o: Marketing and sale of petroleum products
n6ac7a628d32.x: PNGRB regulates refining, storage and distribution, and marketing and sale; crude oil and natural gas production are outside it.
xa: PNGRB is statutory under the **PNGRB Act 2006**, under **MoPNG**.
It authorises **CGD Geographical Areas** and sets pipeline tariffs.
In AP, PNGRB approved **10 GAs**.

n65ac7412fa7.s: Which of the following correctly represents the Phase I locations of India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves?
n65ac7412fa7.x: Phase I of India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves comprises Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur in Karnataka.
n65ac7412fa7.tq: Use location-based elimination among closely related energy projects.
xs: SPR Phase I sites: **Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru, Padur (Karnataka)** — option **(2)**.
**Digboi** is an oil field, **Raniganj** and **Talcher** are coalfields, **Neyveli** is lignite and **Barmer** is a Rajasthan field.
xa: Phase I cover: about **9.5 days** of imports vs the **IEA** norm of **90 days**.
Operator: **ISPRL**, under MoPNG through **OIDB**.
New plan (**6 Aug 2026**): **$42 billion** strategic fuel reserve.

nb43f9ed344c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves?
o: Phase I reserves cover about 9.5 days of imports
They are operated by ISPRL under MoPNG through OIDB
The IEA norm for strategic reserve cover is 60 days of imports
Phase I sites are Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur
nb43f9ed344c.x: The IEA norm is 90 days of imports, not 60.
xa: Phase I sites: **Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru, Padur**.
New **$42 billion** reserve will be the **first beyond crude**.

ne194f5fba93.s: India's proposed new strategic fuel reserve is planned to hold about how much LPG?
ne194f5fba93.x: It plans about six weeks of LPG and two months of crude and LNG, funded partly by levies on LPG and gas.
xa: It is the **first reserve beyond crude**.
Old Phase I covered only about **9.5 days** of imports.
The SPR levy plan was driven by **West Asia** supply shocks.

n90ca8350ffe.s: Among the world's coal producers, India ranks:
n90ca8350ffe.x: India is the second-largest producer (about 10%) after China (51%); its output was 1,040.08 MT in FY 2025-26.
xa: Thermal-plant coal imports fell **27.4%**; coal imports ~**26%** (May 2026).
⚠ Some notes (May 2026) say India is **third**.

nc191d6b33f9.s: The Supreme Court’s cancellation of 204 coal blocks in 2014 was followed by which legislative measure for auction-based allocation?
o: Mines and Minerals Act, 1957, without amendment
nc191d6b33f9.x: The cancellation of 204 coal blocks in 2014 led to the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015, which enabled auction-based allocation.
nc191d6b33f9.tq: Match the judicial event with the specific corrective legislation that followed it.
xs: After the SC cancelled **204 blocks** (**2014**), auctions came under the **Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act 2015** — option **(3)**.
The **Electricity Act 2003** concerns power, not coal block allocation.
xa: **Commercial mining** auctions began in **2020**.
**Window-II** auction was at a premium.

ncb6eb4520ee.s: The coal associated with the Godavari valley is:
ncb6eb4520ee.x: The Godavari valley coalfields are associated with Singareni, which is now in Telangana. The historical observation was that Andhra lacked coal and would draw on Singareni.
ncb6eb4520ee.tq: Location-resource association using a nearby regional distractor.
xs: **Godavari valley** coal = **Singareni** — option **(3)**, now in **Telangana**.
The **SRC** noted Andhra lacked coal and would draw on Singareni.
**Raniganj** (WB) and **Jharia** (Jharkhand) are Damodar coal; **Neyveli** is lignite (TN).
xa: **SCCL**: **51% Telangana, 49% GoI**.
SCCL is one of the Ministry of Coal PSUs with **CIL** and **NLC India**.

nf5245def303.s: Commercial mining auctions for coal commenced from
nf5245def303.x: Commercial mining auctions for coal began in 2020.
nf5245def303.tq: Separate the year of the special-provisions legislation from the year commercial auctions began.
xs: **Commercial mining** auctions began in **2020** — option **(4)**.
**2014** is the SC cancellation of **204 blocks**; **2015** is the **CMSP Act**.
xa: **Window-II** auction was at a premium.

nee6f13a6e01.s: India's oil industry began at Digboi in:
nee6f13a6e01.x: Digboi marks 1889; the first coal mine at Raniganj was in 1774, the gas grid proposal in 1955 and Coal India in 1975.
xa: **One Nation One Gas Grid** began in **2014**.
Gas was first found in **Assam and Maharashtra (1960s)**.

nb2c09ed41da.s: Oil formation is chiefly associated with which geological period?
nb2c09ed41da.x: The Tertiary period is the period of oil formation, and most reserves occur in anticlines and fault traps.
xa: Traps: **anticlines, fault traps, salt domes**.
**Reservoir rock** = porous, permeable sandstone or fissured limestone; **cap rock** seals the trap.
Petroleum = **90-95% hydrocarbons**.

nd938a1d94fc.s: The first commercial output of coal bed methane in India came from:
nd938a1d94fc.x: Raniganj produced the first commercial CBM; Jharia, Bokaro and Sohagpur are other key CBM areas.
xa: CBM areas lie in the **Damodar valley** coalfields.
**Gas hydrates**: **KG, Mahanadi, Andaman** offshore.

n8f8d652cd1d.s: Foreign Direct Investment in many segments of India's petroleum and natural gas sector is permitted up to:
n8f8d652cd1d.x: FDI is permitted up to 100 per cent in many petroleum and natural gas segments. In PSU refining, the limit is 49 per cent without disinvestment.
n8f8d652cd1d.tq: Contrast the general ceiling with the sector-specific exception.
xs: **FDI** is allowed up to **100 per cent** in many segments — option **(4)**.
**49%** applies to **PSU refining** without disinvestment.
xa: **HELP** gives **marketing and pricing freedom**.
India has been a **net exporter of petroleum products** since **2001-02**.

ne8d9ea01e1d.s: India has been a net exporter of petroleum products since
ne8d9ea01e1d.x: India became a net exporter of petroleum products in 2001-02. 1991-92 (the reform year), 2011-12 and 2016-17 are distractors with no link to this milestone. India still imports most of its crude oil; it exports refined products.
ne8d9ea01e1d.tq: Net exporter of PRODUCTS (not crude) since 2001-02.
xs: India has been a **net exporter of petroleum products** since **2001-02** — option **(2)**.
It exports refined products even though import reliance is about **88% for crude**.

ne6c5606e612.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the cleanest fossil fuel?

ncbea015fb77.s: The equity of Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) is held as follows:

n2d99e589160.s: How much solar capacity was added in India during 2025-26?

ne1d7bb5ad61.s: NITI projects that coal's share in India's electricity generation may fall from about 74% to ____ by 2070.

n2785a015376.s: According to the latest reported figures, India's total installed electricity generation capacity and the share of non-fossil sources are approximately

ne8db4c1cb52.s: Which of the following is the largest renewable-energy component in India's installed capacity?

n176ef49dc4f.s: The Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (APERC) was set up under:

nc249188f3b2.s: Non-fossil sources make up over half of India's installed capacity, but roughly what share of actual electricity output?

ndd3bcc80682.s: The Electricity Act, 2003 required State Electricity Boards to be:

nc2915516694.s: The annual publication 'Energy Statistics (India)' is brought out by

Average revenue realised minus AT&C loss

n937b9062d21.s: The National Electricity Plan is a report of:
n937b9062d21.x: The National Electricity Plan is a CEA report; NITI Aayog is associated with India Energy Security Scenarios 2047.

Adopted by all **36** States/UTs.

nee1fe62d6fc.s: Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana (UDAY), launched in November 2015, mainly aimed at:

n2a065cb2111.s: Which is the nodal agency for the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY)?

ndf17cf4ce2c.s: The nodal agencies of the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) are:
ndf17cf4ce2c.x: RDSS, a reform-based, results-linked scheme extended to FY 2027-28, has REC and PFC as nodal agencies.

n530153fd280.s: Which organisation signed an MoU with PNGRB for smart domestic PNG meters?
n530153fd280.x: EESL, which aggregates demand for large smart-metering programmes, signed an MoU with PNGRB for smart domestic PNG meters.
xa: RDSS smart meters: **~4.7 crore installed, 20.34 crore sanctioned**; **TOTEX (PPP)** model.
RDSS is **reform-based, results-linked**, extended to **FY 2027-28**.

n72cbb39deeb.s: Andhra Pradesh, which has no coal of its own, draws coal for its thermal plants from:
n72cbb39deeb.x: Andhra Pradesh has no coal of its own and depends on Singareni and MCL.
xa: AP coal plants: **Simhadri (NTPC, 2,000 MW)**, **Dr NTTPS**, **RTPP**, **Krishnapatnam**, **Hinduja**.
**APERC** approved buying **1,600 MW** coal power under **Section 63** (Aug 2026).
**CEA** plan: **5,588 MW** thermal additions in AP by **2035-36**.

n3275ea025de.s: The transmission and distribution (T&D) losses of Andhra Pradesh's power system are reported at about
n3275ea025de.x: AP's T&D losses are 9.25%, with 376 EHT substations and 33,379.72 ckm of transmission lines. 15.04% and 22.62% are the national AT&C losses for FY25 and FY14, and 4.2% was India's peak power shortage in 2014.
xs: AP's **T&D losses** are **9.25%** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**15.04%** and **22.62%** are national **AT&C losses** (FY25, FY14); **4.2%** was India's power **shortage in 2014**.
xa: AP has **376 EHT substations** and **33,379.72 ckm** of transmission lines.
National shortage fell to **0.03% (2025)**.
AP's RDSS sanction: **₹15,083.14 crore**.

n4edfa664238.s: Who introduced free electricity for farmers in Andhra Pradesh after becoming Chief Minister on 14 May 2004?
n4edfa664238.x: Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy introduced free electricity for farmers after becoming Chief Minister on 14 May 2004.
n4edfa664238.tq: Match the policy decision with the correct office-holder and date.
xs: **Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy** gave **free electricity to farmers** after becoming CM on **14 May 2004** — so option **(2)** is correct.

xa: **Aqua farmers** pay a concessional **₹1.50/unit**.
**20.79 lakh** BPL SC/ST households get free power up to **200 units a month**.
States spend ~**₹2.4 lakh crore/yr** subsidising farm and domestic power.

nd62b1ac0787.s: In Andhra Pradesh, BPL SC/ST households receive free electricity up to how many units a month?
nd62b1ac0787.x: About 20.79 lakh BPL SC/ST households get free power up to 200 units a month. 100, 150 and 300 units are not the stated limit. Aqua farmers, by contrast, get a concessional tariff of Rs 1.50 per unit.
nd62b1ac0787.tq: SC/ST BPL: 200 units free; aqua: Rs 1.50/unit.

About **20.79 lakh** such households benefit.
xa: **Aqua farmers:** concessional **₹1.50/unit**.

nc2310e04dab.s: Which one of the following was NOT identified as a cause of the financial sickness of State Electricity Boards?
o: Autonomy of State Governments over power generation and distribution
Sale of electricity to agricultural and domestic consumers below cost
nc2310e04dab.x: State autonomy over power generation and distribution was identified as not being a problem. Below-cost sales, high T&D losses and poor cost recovery were causes of financial sickness.

n31419786d17.s: Which one of the following is a demand-side intervention under UDAY?
n31419786d17.x: The use of energy-efficient LED bulbs is a demand-side intervention. Coal swapping, transformer upgrades and feeder metering are operational interventions.

**Feeder/DT metering**, **transformer upgrading** and **coal swapping** are **operational interventions**.
xa: Other demand-side items: energy-efficient **agricultural pumps, fans and ACs**; LED bulbs came via **UJALA**.
Other operational items: **consumer indexing**, **smart meters**, reducing **AT&C loss**.
UDAY was launched in **Nov 2015** for the **financial turnaround of DISCOMs**.

n45515d3ec32.s: Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) are especially relevant to India's power system for:
o: Reducing transmission losses on long lines
Meeting the evening peak in demand
n45515d3ec32.x: BESS is highlighted for managing the evening demand peak, especially alongside variable renewable generation.
xa: The **NGAP** plans storage of **174 GW/888 GWh**: **94 GW** pumped storage + **80 GW BESS**.
AP plans BESS for the evening peak while buying **1,600 MW** of thermal power.
Record peak demand: **270.82 GW** on **21 May 2026**.

n52f4e853cc9.s: In a hydroelectric power plant, energy is converted in the sequence:
n52f4e853cc9.x: Stored water's potential energy becomes kinetic energy as it falls, turns the turbine (mechanical) and the generator produces electricity.
xa: Net transformation: **Potential → Electrical** (APPSC 2023; APPSC-GS 2023 key).
**Pumped storage** reverses the cycle: surplus power pumps water uphill, released at peak.
**Run-of-the-river** plants use natural flow with little or no storage.

nc6bdad4e000.s: Which APGENCO thermal plant commissioned a Stage V 1x800 MW unit in December 2023?
nc6bdad4e000.x: Dr NTTPS near Vijayawada commissioned its Stage V 800 MW unit in December 2023 (total 2,560 MW). RTPP at Muddanur is 1,650 MW, Simhadri belongs to NTPC, and Hinduja National Power is a private plant.
xs: **Dr NTTPS, Vijayawada** commissioned **Stage V 1x800 MW** in **Dec 2023** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**RTPP Muddanur** is **1,650 MW**; **Simhadri** is NTPC's; **Hinduja** is private.
xa: Dr NTTPS total = **2,560 MW** (APGENCO).
**Krishnapatnam (SDSTPS)** Stage I = **2x800 MW**.
APGenco plans two **3,200 MW** plants.

nphysics-14-13.s: Mechanical energy is the sum of:
nphysics-14-13.x: Mechanical energy is KE + PE; thermal energy is internal energy due to molecular motion.
n: Kinetic energy can be translational. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 38-44]
Kinetic energy can be rotational. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 38-44]
Potential energy can be gravitational. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 38-44]
Potential energy can be elastic or spring energy. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 38-44]
Mechanical energy equals kinetic energy plus potential energy. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 38-44]
Thermal or heat energy is internal energy due to molecular motion. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 38-44]
xa: Other forms of potential energy: **electric**, **chemical**, **nuclear**.
In a hydro plant, **potential → electrical** (APPSC 2023).
**Friction in brakes** converts **kinetic → heat**.

nphysics-14-16.x: A solar cell turns light into electrical energy; a battery converts chemical, and a generator mechanical, energy into electrical energy.
n: A generator or dynamo converts mechanical energy into electrical energy. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 38-44]
An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 38-44]
A battery or cell converts chemical energy into electrical energy. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 38-44]
A solar cell converts light energy into electrical energy. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 38-44]
xa: **LED / bulb**: **electrical → light**.
**Nuclear power plant**: **nuclear → heat → electrical**.
In a hydro plant, the generator works by **electromagnetic induction**.

nphysics-14-34.s: A body in free fall converts:
nphysics-14-34.x: A falling body, like a swinging pendulum or a descending roller coaster, converts potential energy into kinetic energy.
n: Free fall demonstrates conversion of potential energy into kinetic energy. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 38-44]
A pendulum demonstrates conversion of potential energy into kinetic energy. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 38-44]
A roller coaster demonstrates conversion of potential energy into kinetic energy. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 38-44]
xa: Hydro plant: stored water (**potential**) → falling water (**kinetic**) → turbine (**mechanical**) → **electrical**.
**Friction in brakes**: **kinetic → heat**.
**Mechanical energy** = kinetic + potential.

n60d6caace76.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about types of hydroelectric plants?
o: A storage plant uses a dam to store water and regulate output
A run-of-the-river plant has little or no storage
A run-of-the-river plant needs a large reservoir that substantially alters the watercourse
A pumped-storage plant acts as a 'grid battery'
n60d6caace76.x: A run-of-the-river plant uses the natural flow with little or no storage and does not much alter the watercourse.
xa: ⚠ **Small hydro (≤25 MW) = MNRE**; **large hydro (>25 MW) = Ministry of Power**.
Large hydro was declared **renewable** in **March 2019**.
India's hydro potential is **>145 GW**, only ~**36%** developed.

n845c676b993.s: Large hydro projects (above 25 MW) are dealt with by:
n845c676b993.x: The Ministry of Power treats projects above 25 MW as large hydro, while MNRE handles small hydro up to 25 MW.
xa: The ceiling was raised to **25 MW** in **November 1999**.
⚠ Large hydro, though under the Ministry of Power, is counted as **renewable** since **March 2019**.
Installed: large hydro **51.96 GW**; small hydro **5.18 GW**.

n2775959e11e.s: In November 1999, the ceiling for small hydro projects under MNRE was raised to:
n2775959e11e.x: Small hydro up to 3 MW was transferred to MNRE in 1989 and the ceiling was raised to 25 MW in November 1999.
xa: Today small hydro (**≤25 MW**) = **MNRE**; large hydro (**>25 MW**) = **Ministry of Power**.
**Small hydro potential:** **21,133 MW from 7,133 sites** (IIT Roorkee HRED, July 2016).

n6f70d1689f1.s: East-flowing peninsular rivers are generally more suited to:
n6f70d1689f1.x: East-flowing peninsular rivers are generally more suitable for irrigation, while waterfalls on peninsular rivers aid hydropower.
xa: Peninsular example: **Koyna** (Maharashtra, **Western Ghats**) = **1,960 MW**.
**Srisailam** and **Nagarjuna Sagar** are on the **Krishna**.
Main hydro potential lies in the **Himalayan/Northeast** belt.

n47a9e5bf95d.s: Pumped-storage hydropower is especially useful for grid balancing because it is the:
o: Only storage that needs no reservoir
Only storage that works without transmission
n47a9e5bf95d.x: Pumped storage is the fastest-responding large-scale storage, useful for balancing renewables and peak demand.
xa: It is called a "**giant water battery**".
It lets solar and wind stand in for coal at **peak hours** — needed for **500 GW** non-fossil.
ISTS charges are waived for **BESS and PSP till 2028**.

n35b88e0333b.s: Which pumped-storage projects are exempted from concurrence of the Central Electricity Authority?
n35b88e0333b.x: Off-stream closed-loop pumped-storage projects are exempted from CEA concurrence.
xa: ISTS charges are **waived for BESS and PSP till 2028**.
AP feasibility reports: **29 locations = 33,240 MW** potential.
**Sharavathi PSP** (Karnataka): **2,000 MW**.

n3e514d2092f.s: Flue-gas desulphurisation (FGD) scrubbers in thermal power plants mainly trap:
n3e514d2092f.x: FGD scrubbers trap sulphur dioxide in the stacks of thermal power plants.
xa: Old units are to be **retired** to meet pollution norms (Mar 2026).
Coal plants = **largest CO2 source**, major **PM2.5** source, heavy **water** users.
**Biomass co-firing** of **5%** is mandated (**SAMARTH**).

ncc2b2fe9274.s: Biomass co-firing in coal power plants was mandated under which initiative?
ncc2b2fe9274.x: The 5% biomass co-firing policy was implemented under the SAMARTH mission.
ncc2b2fe9274.tq: Identify the programme directly associated with the stated reform measure.
xs: **5% biomass co-firing** in coal plants was mandated under the **SAMARTH mission** (MoP policy, **2021**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**SHAKTI Window-II** concerns coal bidding at a **premium**, not biomass.
xa: **Revised SHAKTI (May 2025):** **Window-I** = central/state plants at **notified price**.
**FGD scrubbers** trap **SO2** in stacks.
Coal plants are major **PM2.5** sources.

nd01afca95f3.s: Andhra Pradesh's hydro and reverse-pumped potential is about:
nd01afca95f3.x: Andhra Pradesh has about 4 GW of hydro and reverse-pumped potential.
xa: AP's **Pumped Storage Promotion Policy 2022**: **29 locations = 33,240 MW** potential.
**Pinnapuram** (Greenko, Kurnool) PSP = **1,680 MW**.
**Upper Sileru PSP** = **1,350 MW (9 x 150 MW)**, largest in AP.

n5b776f275e0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about dams in India?
o: Maharashtra has the most dams, followed by Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat
About 98.5% of specified dams are owned by the States
India ranks second in the world in terms of large dams
n5b776f275e0.x: India ranks third, not second, in the world in terms of large dams.
xa: Total storage is about **330 BCM**.
⚠ **6,628** = specified dams; **7,133** = small-hydro sites.
Dam safety bodies: **NCDS**, **NDSA**, **SCDS** (**Dam Safety Act, 2021**).

nphysics-14-58.s: Which of the following is NOT a form of potential energy?
nphysics-14-58.x: Thermal energy is internal energy from molecular motion; electric, chemical and nuclear energy are stored (potential) energy.
n: Potential energy can be electric. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 38-44]
Potential energy can be chemical. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 38-44]
Potential energy can be nuclear. [Physics · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 38-44]
xa: Potential energy also includes **gravitational** and **elastic / spring**.
**Kinetic energy** is **translational** or **rotational**.
Other types: **sound**, **light**, **electrical**, **magnetic**.

o: Displacement caused by the Tehri dam
Tree felling in the Garhwal Himalaya
Resettlement of people displaced by the Narmada project
nbf053892184.x: Rally for the Valley was an NBA campaign on the resettlement of people displaced by the Narmada project.
xa: NBA was led by **Medha Patkar** against **Sardar Sarovar**.
⚠ **Narmada = Medha Patkar**; **Tehri (Bhagirathi) = Sunderlal Bahuguna**.
**18.5 million** were affected by projects **1950-1990**.

n38404a18b74.s: Who described large dams such as Bhakra Nangal as the “temples of modern India”?
n38404a18b74.x: Jawaharlal Nehru used the expression “temples of modern India” for large dams such as Bhakra Nangal.
n38404a18b74.tq: Match the quotation with its speaker and the associated dam-development context.
xs: **Jawaharlal Nehru** called large dams like **Bhakra Nangal** the "**temples of modern India**" — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Medha Patkar** led the **Narmada Bachao Andolan**; **Sunderlal Bahuguna** led the anti-**Tehri** movement.
xa: **Bhakra Nangal** (Sutlej) is among India's largest hydro plants with **Koyna** and **Tehri**.
Bhakra Nangal, Sardar Sarovar and Tehri **displaced millions**.
**Silent Valley** movement — **Kerala**.

nenvironment-32-1.s: In which year did the Chipko Movement start?
nenvironment-32-1.x: The Chipko Movement began in 1973 in Chamoli (now Uttarakhand). Gaura Devi's women's action at Raini came in 1974.
nenvironment-32-1.tq: Discriminate the 1973 start from the 1974 Raini action.
n: The Chipko Movement started in 1973. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 56-57]
xs: The **Chipko Movement** started in **1973** — option **(2)**.
It began in the **Garhwal Himalayas** of **Uttarakhand**; people **hugged trees** to **prevent felling**.
**1974** is when **Gaura Devi** led the village women at **Raini**.
xa: **Chandi Prasad Bhatt** was a key figure; **Sunderlal Bahuguna** had a leading role.
Chipko slogan: "**Ecology is permanent economy**".
**Appiko** = **P. Hegde**, **Karnataka**.

nenvironment-32-2.s: The Silent Valley Movement took place in which State?
nenvironment-32-2.x: The Silent Valley Movement was in Kerala; Chipko was in Uttarakhand and Appiko in Karnataka.
n: The Chipko Movement was associated with Uttarakhand. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 56-57]
The Narmada Bachao Movement was associated with the Narmada Valley. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 56-57]
The Silent Valley Movement was associated with Kerala. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 56-57]
The Appiko Movement was associated with Karnataka. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 56-57]
The Chipko Movement took place in the Garhwal Himalayas of Uttarakhand. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 56-57]
xa: **Silent Valley** is linked with **Dr. Salim Ali**.
**Narmada Bachao Andolan** = **Medha Patkar** (against Sardar Sarovar).
⚠ **Tehri (Bhagirathi)** = **Sunderlal Bahuguna**.

nenvironment-32-4.s: The Appiko Movement is associated with:
nenvironment-32-4.x: Appiko is linked with Panduranga Hegde; Chipko with Gaura Devi, Narmada Bachao with Medha Patkar and Silent Valley with Salim Ali.
n: Gaura Devi was associated with the Chipko Movement. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 56-57]
P. Hegde was associated with the Appiko Movement. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 56-57]
Medha Patkar was associated with the Narmada Bachao Movement. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 56-57]
Dr. Salim Ali was associated with the Silent Valley Movement. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 56-57]
xa: **Rally for the Valley** (1999) highlighted **resettlement** of the displaced.
**Nehru** called large dams "**Temples of modern India**".
Chipko started in **1973**.

nenvironment-32-5.s: Who led the village women at Raini in 1974 during the Chipko Movement?
nenvironment-32-5.x: Gaura Devi led the women of Raini in 1974; Sunderlal Bahuguna was another leading Chipko figure.
n: Gaura Devi led village women at Raini in 1974. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 56-57]
Sunderlal Bahuguna played a leading role in the Chipko Movement. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 56-57]
Sunderlal Bahuguna was associated with the Chipko Movement. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 56-57]
xa: **Chandi Prasad Bhatt** was a protagonist of Chipko.
Chipko began in **1973** in the **Garhwal Himalayas**.
Bahuguna also led the anti-**Tehri** dam movement.

n03478ab330b.s: Which one of the following is NOT a major trade-off associated with large dams?
o: Seismic risk in the Himalayan region
Improved migration routes for riverine fish without intervention
n03478ab330b.x: Large dams can block fish migration rather than improve it. Displacement, sedimentation and Himalayan seismic risk are recognised concerns.
n03478ab330b.tq: Identify the option that reverses an ecological impact of dams.
xs: Large dams **block fish migration**; they do not improve it — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Displacement**, **sedimentation** (reduces reservoir capacity) and **seismic risk in the Himalayan region** are real trade-offs.
xa: **18.5 million** people affected by projects **1950-1990**; over **3,300** dams built.
**Gestation:** **10-20 years** for major projects.
Bhakra Nangal, Sardar Sarovar and Tehri displaced millions.

na22799804d9.s: Which of the following was NOT part of the March 2019 large-hydro reforms?
o: Abolition of all renewable purchase obligations for discoms
Budgetary support for flood moderation and storage hydroelectric projects
Declaration of large hydro above 25 MW as renewable energy
na22799804d9.x: The March 2019 package included renewable-energy status, tariff rationalisation and budgetary support; abolition of all renewable purchase obligations was not included.
na22799804d9.tq: Identify the option that goes beyond the stated reform package.
xs: **Abolishing all renewable purchase obligations** was **not** part of the March 2019 package — so option **(1)** is correct.
The package had **large hydro (>25 MW) declared renewable**, **tariff rationalisation** and **budgetary support for flood moderation/storage HEPs**.
It actually added a separate **Hydro Purchase Obligation (HPO)** on discoms.
xa: Reforms apply to projects taken up by **31 March 2030**.
The **RPO/RCO** process has since been simplified (2026).

n39eaebc7d0a.s: Under India's dam safety framework, which body is the regulator and implements policy?
n39eaebc7d0a.x: NDSA is the regulator and implements policy; NCDS handles policy and standards and SCDS provides State oversight.
xa: ⚠ **NCDS** = policy; **NDSA** = regulator; **SCDS** = state.
India is **3rd** in large dams, with **6,628 specified dams**.
**98.5%** of dams are owned by **States**.

nbf3220bf187.s: The World Commission on Dams was set up in 1998 with the association of:
nbf3220bf187.x: The World Commission on Dams was associated with the World Bank and IUCN in 1998.
xa: Its report: **Dams and Development** (**2000**).
Dam trade-offs: displacement, sedimentation, ecology, seismic risk.
India's dam regulator: **NDSA** under the **Dam Safety Act, 2021**.

ndcbad781ee8.s: The Hydro Purchase Obligation requires discoms to buy a prescribed share of power from:
ndcbad781ee8.x: HPO is a separate obligation for discoms to buy large-hydro power, part of the March 2019 reforms.
xa: March 2019: large hydro (**>25 MW**) declared **renewable**.
The **RPO/RCO** process has since been simplified (2026).
Reforms cover projects taken up by **31 March 2030**.

ne825e8183b4.s: The waiver of Inter-State Transmission System charges for Battery Energy Storage Systems and Pumped Storage Projects is available until
ne825e8183b4.x: ISTS charges for BESS and PSP are waived until 2028 as a policy support measure.
ne825e8183b4.tq: Distinguish the policy deadline from other planning horizons.
xs: **ISTS charges** are **waived for BESS and PSP till 2028** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is a policy support measure for storage, which the grid needs for the evening peak.
xa: **Off-stream closed-loop PSPs** are exempted from **CEA concurrence** (2026).
Storage need by **2035-36**: **174 GW / 888 GWh**.
AP has the **Pumped Storage Promotion Policy 2022**.

ndacb81585d9.s: The projected storage composition of 174 GW under the CEA National Generation Adequacy Plan is
ndacb81585d9.x: The projected storage comprises 94 GW of pumped-storage projects and 80 GW of battery energy storage systems.
ndacb81585d9.tq: Match the total with its two component technologies rather than confusing their order.
xs: NGAP storage of **174 GW** = **94 GW PSP + 80 GW BESS** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (1) swaps the two figures.
xa: Storage energy: **888 GWh**.
NGAP (**May 2026**): peak **459 GW**, capacity **1,121 GW**, **70%** non-fossil.
ISTS charges **waived for BESS and PSP till 2028**.

n8a389cc1347.s: The capacity of the Pinnapuram pumped-storage project, the world's first integrated renewable energy storage project, is:
n8a389cc1347.x: Pinnapuram in Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh, has a capacity of 1,680 MW.
xa: Pinnapuram (Greenko, **Kurnool**) and **Tehri (500 MW)** are the two large PSPs commissioned recently.
**Kamalapadu 950 MW**, **Yaganti 1,000 MW** among six new PSPs.

nd3a7a8dd324.s: Gandikota pumped storage project is located in:
nd3a7a8dd324.x: The Gandikota pumped storage project is located in YSR Kadapa district.
nd3a7a8dd324.tq: Confusable district discrimination among Andhra Pradesh energy projects.
xs: **Gandikota PSP** is in **YSR Kadapa** district — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Pinnapuram** (Greenko) is in **Kurnool**; **Srikakulam** hosts an APGenco ultra mega plant plan.
xa: Six new PSPs approved incl. **Kamalapadu 950 MW**, **Yaganti 1,000 MW**.
AP PSP potential: **29 locations = 33,240 MW**.
**Upper Sileru PSP** = **1,350 MW**, largest in AP.

n1cfab04cb52.s: The under-construction Polavaram hydro project of APGENCO is associated with which of the following combinations?
n1cfab04cb52.x: The Polavaram hydro project is located on the Godavari and has an installed capacity of 12 × 80 MW, or 960 MW.
n1cfab04cb52.tq: Use the project–river–capacity combination to distinguish closely related hydro projects.
xs: **Polavaram** hydro project (APGENCO) is on the **Godavari** with **12 x 80 MW = 960 MW** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**460 MW** is **Lower Sileru**; **815.6 MW** is **Nagarjuna Sagar** main PH; **114.75 MW** is **Machkund**.
xa: Polavaram is under construction with **phased commissioning** (APPSC 2019 asked **960 MW**).
The AP power plan lists **Polavaram hydro + Upper Sileru PSP** (Aug 2026).
**Upper Sileru** hydro = **240 MW (4 x 60 MW)**.

n9385d50a118.s: Which multipurpose project on the Krishna is one of the largest masonry dams in the world?
n9385d50a118.x: Nagarjuna Sagar on the Krishna is one of the world's largest masonry dams and serves irrigation, power and drinking water. Srisailam is also on the Krishna but is not the cited masonry dam, Polavaram is on the Godavari, and Machkund is an AP-Odisha project on the Machkund river.
n9385d50a118.tq: Nagarjuna Sagar = largest masonry dam; Polavaram = 960 MW.
xs: **Nagarjuna Sagar** on the Krishna is one of the **largest masonry dams** in the world — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Srisailam** is also on the Krishna but not the cited masonry dam; **Polavaram** is on the **Godavari**; **Machkund** is AP-Odisha.
xa: Nagarjuna Sagar is **multipurpose**: irrigation, power, drinking water.
Main PH **815.6 MW** (Telangana); Right Canal PH **90 MW** (AP).
Srisailam: Right Bank **770 MW** (AP), Left Bank **900 MW** (Telangana).

n9ecdb108fd7.s: An Ultra Mega Power Project (UMPP) is a 4,000 MW ____ plant awarded through tariff-based bidding.
n9ecdb108fd7.x: A UMPP is a 4,000 MW supercritical coal plant awarded through tariff-based bidding.
xa: UMPPs: **Sasan** (MP), **Mundra** (Gujarat), **Krishnapatnam** (AP, stalled), **Tilaiya** (Jharkhand, given up).
**Mundra UMPP** = **Tata Power**; the others = **Reliance Power**.
APGenco plans two **3,200 MW ultra mega supercritical** plants.

nf1aecc8fdcf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about flexible operation of the power system?
o: It includes cyclical operation of gas plants
It includes optimising hydro generation alongside coal
nf1aecc8fdcf.x: Batteries are one of the flexible-operation measures, along with pumped storage, cyclical gas operation and hydro optimisation.
xa: Heatwave 2026: peak **256 GW**, **18-21 GW** coal units out, ~**150 GW** solar off after sunset.
NGAP storage: **94 GW PSP + 80 GW BESS**.
PSP = the **grid battery** for the **500 GW non-fossil** target.

n2c011d3884c.s: APGenco's proposed two 3,200 MW ultra mega supercritical plants are planned at
o: Srikakulam and a pithead site at Talcher (Odisha)
n2c011d3884c.x: APGenco plans two 3,200 MW ultra mega supercritical plants: one at Srikakulam and one at a pithead site at Talcher (Odisha), likely as a JV with Coal India. Krishnapatnam, Muddanur and Ibrahimpatnam host existing plants (SDSTPS, RTPP, Dr NTTPS). Polavaram is a hydro project and Singareni is a coal company.
n2c011d3884c.tq: APGenco 2 x 3,200 MW: Srikakulam + Talcher pithead.
xs: APGenco's two **3,200 MW ultra mega supercritical** plants are at **Srikakulam** and a **pithead site at Talcher (Odisha)** — option **(1)**.
**Krishnapatnam**, **Muddanur** and **Ibrahimpatnam** host existing plants; **Polavaram** is hydro.
xa: Talcher plant is likely a **JV with Coal India** (Mar 2026).
APERC resource plan: **11,544 MW** extra capacity in **five years**.
**Krishnapatnam UMPP** (Reliance Power) is **stalled**.

n3d878da4b7a.s: Which State has the largest hydropower potential in India?
n3d878da4b7a.x: Arunachal Pradesh has the largest State-level hydropower potential.
xa: NE flagship: **Subansiri Lower (2,000 MW)**; **Tato-II** **700 MW**.
Other major hydro states: **Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, J&K**.
Only about **36%** of the **>145 GW** potential is developed.

n41e669f6db4.s: A major weakness of hydropower is its dependence on:
n41e669f6db4.x: Hydropower is renewable and flexible, but its output depends on drought and snowpack variability.
xa: Strengths: clean (**near-zero operating emissions**), renewable, flexible.
El Niño years hurt hydro output.
Major projects take **10-20 years** to build.

n75c6bce5548.s: The Subansiri Lower hydroelectric project is located across which States?
n75c6bce5548.x: The Subansiri Lower project is associated with Arunachal Pradesh and Assam and has a capacity of 2,000 MW.
n75c6bce5548.tq: Distinguish the two-State location from projects located wholly within one State.
xs: **Subansiri Lower** lies in **Arunachal Pradesh-Assam** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It has a capacity of **2,000 MW** on the Subansiri river.
xa: Arunachal has the **largest state hydro potential**.
**Tato-II** (Arunachal): **700 MW**, **2,738 MU/yr**.
**Teesta** projects — **Sikkim**.

ndffaece6494.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about renewable energy in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Its current renewable-energy share is about 30%
It targets a renewable-energy share of more than 75% by 2047
Its target is associated with the Swarna Andhra Vision
Renewable energy already accounts for more than 75% of its share
ndffaece6494.x: Renewable energy is currently about 30% of the State's share; more than 75% is the 2047 target under the Swarna Andhra Vision.
xa: AP has about **4 GW** of hydro/reverse-pumped potential.
RE allocated in AP = **112.45 GW** (June 2026).
AP PSP policy (**2022**): **29 locations = 33,240 MW** potential.

ne62dd574548.s: The Srisailam hydroelectric project is situated on which river?
ne62dd574548.x: Srisailam is on the Krishna; its Right Bank Power House (770 MW) is in Andhra Pradesh and Left Bank Power House (900 MW) in Telangana.
xa: **Nagarjuna Sagar** (Krishna): main PH **815.6 MW** (Telangana); Right Canal PH **90 MW** (AP).
**Polavaram** (Godavari) = **960 MW**.
**Koyna 1,960 MW** is far larger than Srisailam right bank.

n7ab3d77bc24.s: Hydroelectricity is regarded as suitable for sustainable development mainly because it is:
n7ab3d77bc24.x: Hydroelectricity is cheap and clean once built, though large projects involve displacement and ecological trade-offs.
xa: **Hydro is the best source for sustainable development** (UPPSC 2012).
Weakness: **drought/snowpack variability**.
Trade-offs: displacement, **sedimentation**, **seismic risk**, gestation of **10-20 years**.

nc797a98ec5b.s: Light Water Reactors, which account for over 85% of world nuclear capacity, use light water as:
nc797a98ec5b.x: LWRs use light water for both moderation and cooling and make up more than 85% of global nuclear capacity.
xa: India now **prioritises LWRs** for fast capacity addition.
**Tarapur = BWR**; **Kudankulam = VVER**.

n774b52dca28.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of India's three-stage nuclear power programme?
n774b52dca28.x: India's programme begins with PHWRs using natural uranium, proceeds to FBRs using plutonium-based fuel, and culminates in thorium-based AHWRs or other thorium reactors.
n774b52dca28.tq: Use the fuel-cycle sequence to identify the correct order.
xs: **PHWR → FBR → AHWR/thorium reactors** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Stage I **PHWR** (natural uranium) → Stage II **FBR** (MOX) → Stage III **AHWR** (Th-232 + U-233).
xa: Conceived by **Homi J. Bhabha** in the **1950s**.
Aim: **self-reliance through a closed fuel cycle**.
⚠ AHWR is a **bridge from Stage I to Stage III** without Stage II.

nb14835ce6c6.s: The coolant used in Stage II Fast Breeder Reactors of India is:
nb14835ce6c6.x: Stage II FBRs use liquid sodium coolant and no moderator, since fast neutrons are needed.
xa: **PFBR, Kalpakkam**: **500 MWe**, first criticality **6 April 2026**.
PFBR designed by **IGCAR**, built by **BHAVINI**.
⚠ **Stage I PHWR = natural uranium**; **Stage III AHWR = Th-232 + U-233**.

n0f86d321dfd.s: The 2005 milestone associated with IGCAR and the Fast Breeder Test Reactor was:
n0f86d321dfd.x: IGCAR’s 2005 milestone was the reprocessing of the mixed-carbide fuel used in the Fast Breeder Test Reactor.
n0f86d321dfd.tq: Match the institution and year with the specific technological achievement.
xs: IGCAR's **2005 milestone** was **reprocessing FBTR's mixed carbide fuel** (UPSC 2006) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**KAMINI** uses U-233 but was not this milestone; **PFBR** is not yet commercial.
xa: **FBTR** runs on a unique **uranium-plutonium mixed carbide** fuel.
**IGCAR** (Kalpakkam) handles **FBR technology and fuel cycle**.
IGCAR designed the **PFBR**.

n29228e1b58d.s: In a fast breeder reactor, fast neutrons convert the U-238 blanket into:
n29228e1b58d.x: Fast neutrons turn the U-238 blanket into Pu-239, so the FBR breeds more fuel than it consumes.
xa: A **Th-232 blanket** makes **U-233**.
Fuel: **MOX (U-Pu oxide)**.

n00464f9628b.s: The AHWR acts as a bridge between which stages of India's nuclear programme?
n00464f9628b.x: The AHWR bridges Stage I and Stage III, advancing thorium use without passing through Stage II.
xa: Stage I **PHWR** = natural uranium; Stage II **FBR** = MOX; Stage III **AHWR** = Th-232 + U-233.
**ANEEL** fuel could also hasten Stage III by running in **existing PHWRs**.
Bottleneck: **thin fissile inventory** for Stage III.

n8af510eac71.s: NPCIL's proposed Bharat Small Reactors are based on the:
n8af510eac71.x: NPCIL sought proposals for 220 MW PHWR-based Bharat Small Reactors as captive plants for industry.
xa: Budget **2024-25** announced **private partnership** for BSRs.
**₹20,000 crore** for SMRs/BSRs (Budget 2025-26).
**BSR-200** = **200 MWe** BARC design.

n4c2db3bb13c.s: The Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor is significant because it is:
o: India's first indigenous Fast Breeder Reactor
n4c2db3bb13c.x: PFBR is described as India's first indigenous Fast Breeder Reactor.
n4c2db3bb13c.tq: Separate the national-first associated with PFBR from the firsts associated with Apsara and KAMINI.
xs: **PFBR** is **India's first indigenous FBR** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Apsara** = Asia's first research reactor; **KAMINI** = only U-233 reactor; **Jaduguda** = first uranium mine.
xa: PFBR = **500 MWe**, designed by **IGCAR**, built by **BHAVINI**.
Core loading on **4 March 2024**.
Next: **2 x 500 MWe** FBR 1&2 at Kalpakkam.

nchemistry-11-18.s: ³H and ⁴He, each having two neutrons, are:
nchemistry-11-18.x: Nuclides with the same number of neutrons are isotones; ³H and ⁴He both have 2 neutrons.
n: ³H and ⁴He are isotones. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 39-42]
³H and ⁴He each have two neutrons. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 39-42]
¹⁴C, ¹⁵N, and ¹⁶O are isotones. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 39-42]
¹⁴C, ¹⁵N, and ¹⁶O each have eight neutrons. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 39-42]
xa: Isotones are also called **isoneutronic species**.
Isotones differ in **atomic numbers** and **mass numbers**.
**Tritium** = 1 proton + 2 neutrons; half-life **12.3 years**.

o: Removing all radioactive isotopes from natural uranium
Increasing the proportion of U-238 through chemical separation
Increasing the proportion of U-235 through isotope separation
n3779a64f4a6.x: Enrichment raises the share of U-235, the fissile isotope, by isotope separation; it does not increase U-238.
n3779a64f4a6.tq: Discriminate between the fissile isotope U-235 and the fertile isotope U-238.
xs: **Enrichment** = raising the share of **U-235** by **isotope separation** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It does not raise **U-238** or convert U-235 into thorium.
xa: ⚠ APPSC-G1 2022 trap: the answer was "**Neither I nor II**" (both statements false).
**LWRs** use **low-enriched uranium (3-5% U-235)**; weapons-grade ≈ **90%**.
Natural uranium has only **0.72%** U-235.

n4083ee763d0.s: Tritium is produced by bombarding ____ with neutrons.
n4083ee763d0.x: Tritium (1 proton + 2 neutrons) is produced by bombarding lithium with neutrons.
xa: Tritium has **1 proton + 2 neutrons** and is a **fusion fuel**.
Fusion joins **two light nuclei** — as in the **Sun and stars**.

n281eab0c027.s: The splitting of a heavy nucleus is called:
n281eab0c027.x: Fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus, while fusion is the joining of two light nuclei.
xa: ⚠ "Breaking apart of a nucleus is called fusion" is the **incorrect** statement (APPSC 2019).
All present-day nuclear electricity is from **fission**; fusion is still **R&D**.
**Atom bomb** = fission; **hydrogen bomb** = fusion.

nd71b5ee1e66.s: All present-day nuclear electricity is generated through:
nd71b5ee1e66.x: Present-day reactors use fission; fusion occurs in the Sun and stars and fusion power is still at the R&D stage.
xa: **ITER** (Cadarache, France) is a **tokamak** fusion experiment.
**NIF** (USA) achieved the first fusion **ignition** in **Dec 2022** by laser.

ne5fa1425c5d.s: Xenon-135 is called a 'nuclear poison' because it:
ne5fa1425c5d.x: Xenon-135 absorbs neutrons and so acts as a nuclear poison in a reactor.
xa: **Fission**: U-235 + neutron → **barium + krypton** + **2-3** neutrons.
**Half-life** = time for half the nuclei to decay.
⚠ "Breaking apart of a nucleus is called fusion" is wrong — that is **fission** (APPSC 2019).

n25e76c3d91e.s: Compared with nuclear fission, nuclear fusion releases ____ energy per unit mass.
n25e76c3d91e.x: Fusion releases more energy per unit mass than fission, though it needs extremely high temperature and pressure.
xa: Fission needs a **neutron hit** and **critical mass**.
Fusion examples: **Sun and stars**, **hydrogen bomb**.
ITER is designed for **500 MW** output from **50 MW** input.

n4a779b82ec6.s: In a hydrogen bomb, the fusion reaction is initiated by:
n4a779b82ec6.x: A hydrogen bomb uses fusion triggered by a fission explosion; an atomic bomb is based on uncontrolled fission.
xa: **Hiroshima** (Little Boy) = **U-235**; **Nagasaki** (Fat Man) = **Pu-239**.
Fusion naturally powers the **Sun and stars**.
**Atomic Energy Act 1948** limited atomic energy to **peaceful uses**.

ne13fb0ad3f1.s: The half-life of a radioactive substance is the time required for:
o: Its atomic mass to become zero
Its radiation to lose half its penetrating power
Half of its radioactive nuclei to decay
ne13fb0ad3f1.x: Half-life is the time required for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to undergo decay.
ne13fb0ad3f1.tq: Choose the definition involving nuclei, not the intensity or mass of the sample.
xs: **Half-life** = time for **half the nuclei to decay** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is not the time for all nuclei to decay or for mass/penetration to change.
xa: **Tritium** half-life = **12.3 years**.
Uranium series: **U-238 → Pb-206**.
Thorium series: **Th-232 → Pb-208**.

n947949b62ff.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about radioactive series?
o: The neptunium series is a natural radioactive series
The thorium series begins with Th-232 and ends with Pb-208
The actinium series begins with U-235 and ends with Pb-207
The uranium series begins with U-238 and ends with Pb-206
n947949b62ff.x: The neptunium series is artificial, not natural.
xa: Radioactivity discovered by **Henri Becquerel (1896)**.
**Half-life** = time for half the nuclei to decay.
Emissions: **alpha, beta, gamma**.

nca9a4a0adfa.s: Stage I of India's three-stage nuclear programme is based on:
nca9a4a0adfa.x: Stage I uses PHWRs fuelled by natural uranium; its spent fuel yields Pu-239 for the next stage.
xa: Stage II **FBR** uses **MOX (Pu-239 + U-238)**.
FBR uses ~**10%**+ of fuel vs ~**1%** in PHWR.
**NPCIL fleet:** **25 reactors, 8,880 MW**.

nc06bca7a28a.s: ANEEL fuel, developed by the US firm Clean Core Thorium Energy, combines thorium with:
nc06bca7a28a.x: ANEEL is thorium plus HALEU and can be used in existing PHWRs.
xa: BARC cautions: shutdown rods **~26% less effective**; stabilisation **7-10 years**.
**NTPC** has a tie-up for ANEEL.

n126509d72a9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Advanced Heavy Water Reactor (AHWR)?
o: It is a conceptual prototype designed at BARC
It is regarded as India's flagship thorium reactor
It is designed for large-scale use of plutonium-bearing spent fuel
It forms the core of the third stage of India's nuclear programme
n126509d72a9.x: The AHWR is intended for large-scale thorium use, not large-scale use of plutonium-bearing spent fuel.
xa: APPSC-G2 2025 used this trap in an A/R item.
AHWR design: **heavy-water moderated**, **boiling light-water coolant**.

n366de7cf973.s: ITER is designed to give about 500 MW of output from an input of:
n366de7cf973.x: ITER, a tokamak fusion device, is designed for 500 MW output from 50 MW input, about ten times more out than in.
xa: Members: **EU, India, China, Japan, South Korea, Russia, USA**.
APPSC-G1 2022 had all four ITER statements correct.

n43c0cbaf0c4.s: India's tokamaks Aditya and SST-1 are located at:
n43c0cbaf0c4.x: Aditya (India's first tokamak) and SST-1 are at the Institute for Plasma Research, Gandhinagar, not BARC.
xa: **ITER** is also a **tokamak** (Cadarache, France).
First fusion ignition: **NIF**, USA, **Dec 2022**.

n05f3264f83d.s: The refuelling interval of Small Modular Reactors is about:
n05f3264f83d.x: SMRs are generally factory-built with a refuelling interval of about 3–7 years, longer than conventional reactors.
xa: SMR = up to **300 MWe** per unit.
BARC also has a gas-cooled reactor up to **5 MW** for **hydrogen**.

nchemistry-11-23.s: A positively charged beta particle is a:
nchemistry-11-23.x: Positive beta is a positron; negative beta is an electron and an alpha particle is a +2 helium nucleus.
n: An alpha particle is a helium nucleus with a +2 charge. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 39-42]
A beta particle is an electron or positron. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 39-42]
Gamma radiation is electromagnetic radiation. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 39-42]
xa: Alpha mass: about **4 atomic mass units**.
Beta penetrates a few mm of **aluminium**; gamma needs **lead/concrete**.

nee0b700d7f7.s: Which one of the following is NOT a nuclear fuel but may serve as a moderator, coolant or absorber in a reactor?
nee0b700d7f7.x: Graphite is a reactor moderator, not a nuclear fuel. U-235, Pu-239 and U-233 are fissile fuels.
nee0b700d7f7.tq: Find the non-fuel by separating reactor-support materials from fissile isotopes.
xs: **Graphite** is a **moderator**, not a nuclear fuel — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Pu-239**, **U-235** and **U-233** are all **fissile fuels**.
xa: Other non-fuels: **heavy water, sodium, boron, cadmium, zirconium**.
**Control rods** (boron, cadmium) absorb neutrons.
**Liquid sodium** is the **FBR** coolant.

n36c5805325a.s: The 300 MW Advanced Heavy Water Reactor (AHWR) designed by BARC uses which fuel combination?
n36c5805325a.x: The AHWR is a 300 MW thorium reactor with heavy-water moderator, boiling light-water coolant and Th-232 + U-233 fuel.
xa: AHWR fuel: **Th-232 + U-233**.
Designed at **BARC**; core of **Stage III**.
It is a **bridge from Stage I to Stage III**.

n749b8e05789.s: The Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam was built and commissioned by which organisation?
o: Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited
n749b8e05789.x: BHAVINI built and commissioned the 500 MWe PFBR at Kalpakkam. The reactor was designed by IGCAR.
n749b8e05789.tq: Identify the organisation directly associated with construction and commissioning.
xs: **BHAVINI** built and commissioned the **PFBR** (APPSC-G1 2024 answer) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**IGCAR** designed it; **NPCIL** builds and operates power reactors; **BARC** is the R&D centre.
xa: ⚠ **PFBR designed by IGCAR**, **built by BHAVINI** — the exam answer is **BHAVINI**.
BHAVINI was set up in **2003** under **DAE**; **NPCIL** holds equity.
PFBR: **500 MWe (1,250 MWt)**, sodium-cooled, **pool type**.

n74ed3e41254.s: The rated electrical capacity of the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam is:
n74ed3e41254.x: The sodium-cooled, pool-type PFBR is rated at 500 MWe (1,250 MWt).
xa: Final cost **₹8,181 crore** — more than double the sanction.
Criticality came **16+ years late**.
Next: **2 x 500 MWe FBR 1&2** at Kalpakkam after a year's performance review.

n947f82de37c.s: Once the PFBR operates commercially, India is expected to become the second country after which country to operate a commercial-scale fast breeder reactor?
n947f82de37c.x: India is expected to become the second country after Russia to operate a commercial-scale fast breeder reactor.
n947f82de37c.tq: Use the country comparison and identify the stated predecessor.
xs: India becomes the **2nd country after Russia** to operate a commercial-scale FBR — so option **(4)** is correct.
The notes name **Russia** only, not the USA, France or Canada.
xa: PFBR = **India's first indigenous FBR**.
Criticality = entry into **Stage II**.
PFBR fuel: **MOX (Pu-239 + U-238)**.

n24916d5d392.s: A Small Modular Reactor (SMR) has a capacity of up to ____ per unit.
n24916d5d392.x: An SMR has a capacity of up to 300 MWe per unit, about one-third the size of a conventional reactor.
xa: SMR size is about **one-third** of conventional reactors.
Refuelling every **3-7 years** vs **1-2**.

n0a2bddbe12a.s: The criticality of the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor in April 2026 signified entry into which stage of India's three-stage nuclear programme?
n0a2bddbe12a.x: PFBR criticality in April 2026 marked India's entry into Stage II of the three-stage programme.
n0a2bddbe12a.tq: Distinguish the programme stage from the reactor type instead of treating all stages as interchangeable.
xs: PFBR criticality (**6 Apr 2026**) marks entry into **Stage II** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Stage I = **PHWR**; Stage III = **AHWR/thorium**.
xa: Stage II FBR fuel = **MOX (Pu-239 + U-238)**.
India = **2nd country after Russia** to run a commercial-scale FBR.
PFBR ran **16** years late and its cost doubled.

n96907eb1995.s: The PFBR project has been reported as facing which combination of cost and schedule difficulties?
o: Its cost was halved and it finished 5 years early.
Its cost doubled and it ran 16 years late.
Its cost tripled and it ran 30 years late.
Its cost remained unchanged and it ran 2 years late.
n96907eb1995.x: The PFBR's cost was reported to have doubled, while the project ran 16 years late.
n96907eb1995.tq: Pair the two quantitative project indicators and avoid mixing the reported cost and delay figures.
xs: PFBR's **cost doubled** and it ran **16 years late** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The Parliamentary Standing Committee put the final cost at **₹8,181 crore**, more than double the sanction, with criticality **16+ years late**.
xa: Work began in **2004**; first criticality on **6 April 2026**.
The **fast-reactor fuel cycle facility** is due **2029**.
Next: **2 x 500 MWe FBR 1&2** at Kalpakkam after a year's performance review.
Other bottlenecks: **10-12-year builds**, thin fissile inventory, local protests.

nb4e98cb52a0.s: India possesses about what share of the world's thorium?
nb4e98cb52a0.x: India has about 25% of global thorium (and about 2% of uranium).
xa: Thorium **~3,60,000 tonnes** vs natural uranium **~70,000 t**.
Older 2025 notes give the thorium share as **21%**.
Thorium source: **monazite** beach sands.

n4e7b90fe371.s: Which body is permitted to process and export monazite in India?
n4e7b90fe371.x: Only government bodies such as IREL may process and export monazite, found in the beach sands of Kerala and Odisha.
xa: UPSC 2022 had statements **1, 2 and 4** correct on monazite.
Monazite yields **thorium**, **rare earths**, phosphate and a little uranium.

n25acdbf7d59.s: Jaduguda, India's first uranium mine, is located in which district and State?
n25acdbf7d59.x: Jaduguda is located in East Singhbhum district of Jharkhand and is India's first uranium mine.
n25acdbf7d59.tq: Use the location-based direct-recall method and distinguish Jaduguda from Tummalapalle.
xs: **Jaduguda** is in **East Singhbhum, Jharkhand** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**YSR Kadapa** (AP) hosts **Tummalapalle**, not Jaduguda.
xa: Jaduguda = **India's first uranium mine** and **UCIL's seat**.
Domestic reserves: mainly **Jharkhand and Andhra Pradesh**.
**AMD** (Hyderabad) explores atomic minerals.

n43ba394209c.s: The Tummalapalle uranium mine of UCIL is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
n43ba394209c.x: Tummalapalle, a UCIL uranium mine with a processing plant, is in YSR Kadapa district.
xa: **Jaduguda** (East Singhbhum, Jharkhand) = India's **first uranium mine**, UCIL's seat.
Domestic uranium reserves are mainly in **Jharkhand and Andhra Pradesh**.
AP angle: **NFC** and **AMD** are in **Hyderabad**; **CODENE** at **IIT Hyderabad**.

naba92de6a8a.s: Approximately what proportion of India's imported uranium comes from Kazakhstan?
naba92de6a8a.x: About 80 percent of imported uranium is stated to come from Kazakhstan.
naba92de6a8a.tq: Anchor the quantitative fact to the highest listed percentage without reversing the comparison.
xs: About **80%** of India's imported uranium comes from **Kazakhstan** (Dec 2025) — about **80 percent**, so option **(3)** is correct.
20%, 40% and 60% are not the notes' figure.
xa: India has only ~**2%** of world uranium vs ~**25%** of thorium.
Domestic uranium: **Jharkhand and Andhra Pradesh**.
The thorium strategy is meant to get round **scarce uranium**.

na69a9239a3c.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a bottleneck affecting the progression towards Stage III?
o: Absence of any thorium resources in India
na69a9239a3c.x: The identified bottlenecks include a thin fissile inventory for Stage III, 10–12-year construction periods and local protests. Absence of thorium resources is not identified as a bottleneck; the programme is based on India's abundant thorium.
na69a9239a3c.tq: Reject the broad contradiction and identify the item not belonging to the stated bottleneck list.
xs: **Absence of thorium** is **not** a bottleneck — India has abundant thorium — so option **(1)** is correct.
Real bottlenecks: **thin fissile inventory** for Stage III, **10-12-year builds**, **local protests**.
xa: PFBR's cost doubled and it ran **16** years late.
**ANEEL** could run in PHWRs and skip slow FBR rollout, but experts clash on it.
BARC: HALEU-thorium stabilisation takes **7-10 years**.

n235ff2bfa1b.s: The Atomic Energy Act of 1948 primarily limited atomic energy in India to:
n235ff2bfa1b.x: The Atomic Energy Act, 1948, limited the use of atomic energy to peaceful purposes.
n235ff2bfa1b.tq: Identify the stated policy purpose without importing later legal changes.
xs: The **Atomic Energy Act 1948** limited atomic energy to **peaceful uses** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It did not limit it to space, military or private ownership.
xa: **SHANTI Act 2025** (assent **20 Dec 2025**) repealed the **Atomic Energy Act 1962** and **CLNDA 2010**.
It allows **private companies and JVs** to build, own and operate plants under licence.
⚠ SHANTI repealed the **1962** Act — not the **1948** Act.

n5ec907fa4b8.s: The International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) is being constructed at:
o: Lawrence Livermore in the United Kingdom
n5ec907fa4b8.x: ITER is located at Cadarache in southern France. Gandhinagar is associated with India's Institute for Plasma Research.
n5ec907fa4b8.tq: Use the location trap by distinguishing ITER's site from Indian fusion facilities.
xs: **ITER** is at **Cadarache, southern France** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Gandhinagar** hosts the **Institute for Plasma Research**; **Lawrence Livermore** is in the **USA** (NIF).
xa: ITER = **tokamak**, the world's largest **magnetic confinement** experiment (APPSC 2018).
India joined in **2005** and supplies the **cryostat**.
⚠ **ITER = magnetic confinement, France**; **NIF ignition = laser, USA**.

n62ab693a139.s: The SHANTI Act 2025 is associated with which of the following developments?
o: It restricts nuclear power generation exclusively to government companies.
It transfers all nuclear research from BARC to IIT Hyderabad.
It abolishes the Nuclear Energy Mission and the three-stage programme.
It repeals the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the CLNDA, 2010, enabling licensed private participation.
n62ab693a139.x: The SHANTI Act 2025 repealed the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the CLNDA, 2010, allowing licensed private companies and joint ventures to build, own and operate nuclear plants.
n62ab693a139.tq: Identify the legal change by focusing on the authority and participation it enables.
xs: **SHANTI Act 2025** repealed the **Atomic Energy Act 1962** and **CLNDA 2010**, allowing **licensed private** players and JVs — option **(4)**.
It opens, not restricts, the sector; it does not abolish the mission or move BARC research.
xa: Assent: **20 Dec 2025**.
⚠ It repealed the **1962** Act, not the **1948** Act (which limited atomic energy to **peaceful uses**).
The programme is now framed as "thorium-led, private-participation, **100 GW by 2047**".

n5e2c9ea0bb2.s: The Nuclear Energy Mission (Union Budget 2025-26) targets nuclear power capacity of ____ by 2047.
n5e2c9ea0bb2.x: The mission targets 100 GW by 2047, with Rs 20,000 crore for Small Modular Reactors.
xa: NPCIL's 54 GW = **PHWRs + foreign-assisted LWRs**.
**SHANTI Act** lets private companies and JVs build plants.

n60414659877.s: AEET, set up in 1954, was renamed Bhabha Atomic Research Centre in:
n60414659877.x: BARC began in 1954 as AEET and was renamed in 1967 after Homi Bhabha.
xa: **AEE Trombay** is sometimes dated **1957**, the year of its formal inauguration.
**NPCIL** became a PSU in **1987**.

nchemistry-11-4.s: Atoms having the same mass number but different atomic numbers are called:
nchemistry-11-4.x: Isobars share mass number but differ in atomic number; isotopes share atomic number but differ in mass number.
n: An isotope has the same atomic number and different mass numbers. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 39-42]
An isobar has the same mass number and different atomic numbers. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 39-42]
xa: Isotope example: **¹H, ²H, ³H** — ²H = **deuterium**, ³H = **tritium**.
Isobar example: **³H** and **³He**.
**Isotones** share the **number of neutrons**.

ne48a856bcdf.s: Which nuclear power station has India's first fully indigenous PHWRs and is also associated with the PFBR?
ne48a856bcdf.x: Kalpakkam's MAPS units are the first fully indigenous PHWRs, and the site is associated with the PFBR.
xa: MAPS 1-2 = **2 units, 440 MW**, in **Tamil Nadu**.
⚠ **Kalpakkam (MAPS) and Kudankulam = both Tamil Nadu**.
PFBR (**500 MWe**) was developed by **BHAVINI**.

n21a5a6fb9d4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about firsts in India's nuclear power programme?
o: Tarapur began operation in 1960 with two PHWRs
Tarapur went into operation in 1969 with two BWRs
RAPS-1, the first PHWR, was built with AECL of Canada and started in 1972
Jaitapur, with a planned 9,900 MW, is the largest planned nuclear project
n21a5a6fb9d4.x: Tarapur, India's first nuclear power plant, started in 1969 with two boiling water reactors, not in 1960 with PHWRs.
xa: **Largest operating** plant: **Kudankulam, 2,000 MW**; next **Kakrapar, 1,840 MW**.
**KAPP-3** = first indigenous **700 MW** PHWR (commercial operation **30 June 2023**).
**MAPS** (Kalpakkam) = **first fully indigenous PHWR**.
⚠ **Gorakhpur NPP** is in **Haryana**, not UP; **Narora** is in UP.

nff58cffdce6.s: Which is India's second-largest operating nuclear power plant, at 1,840 MW?
nff58cffdce6.x: Kakrapar is the second-largest operating plant at 1,840 MW; Jaitapur (9,900 MW) is the largest planned plant.
xa: Kakrapar (Gujarat): **4 units**; India's first **700 MW PHWRs**.
**Kashiwazaki-Kariwa** (Japan) = world's largest NPP by capacity.
Tarapur is the **first**, not the largest, plant.

n429f3e40cc1.s: KAPP-3, India's first indigenous 700 MW PHWR, is located in:
n429f3e40cc1.x: KAPP-3 is at Kakrapar in Gujarat and began commercial operation on 30 June 2023.
xa: Kakrapar has **4 units, 1,840 MW**.
**KAPP-4** is also listed under construction.
700 MW PHWR costs ~**$2 million/MW** — among the lowest in the world.

n933f3342af8.s: The Rawatbhata (RAPS/RAPP) atomic power station, India's oldest PHWR site, is located in which State?
n933f3342af8.x: Rawatbhata (RAPS/RAPP) is in Rajasthan; its Canada-assisted RAPS-1 began in 1972 and RAPP-7 (700 MW) now operates. Kakrapar is in Gujarat, Chutka (planned) in Madhya Pradesh and Narora in Uttar Pradesh.
xs: **Rawatbhata (RAPS/RAPP)** is in **Rajasthan** (APPSC-GS 2018) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Kakrapar** is in Gujarat, **Chutka** in MP, **Narora** in UP.
xa: RAPS-1 (**Canada, AECL**) started **1972**.
RAPS 1-6 = **1,180 MW**; **RAPP-7 (700 MW)** running, RAPP-8 next.
**Kota (Rawatbhata)** heavy water plant was commissioned in **1985**.

ne2fd2a3dbbb.s: Thal is located in which State?
ne2fd2a3dbbb.x: Thal is in Maharashtra, not Gujarat; Nangal is in Punjab and Talcher in Odisha.
xa: Thal was commissioned in **1987**.
**Hazira** (Gujarat) and **Manuguru** both came in **1991**.
Manuguru, now **Telangana**, is the largest.

n878f2916b9e.s: Besides civil-society protests, which event delayed the Kudankulam nuclear project?
o: The signing of the India-US 123 Agreement
n878f2916b9e.x: The breakup of the USSR and civil-society protests are counted among the delays; the 1991 economic crisis is not.
xa: Kudankulam came from the **1988** USSR accord.
Units: **2 x 1,000 MW VVER** operating (2013, 2016).
Kudankulam faced a ransomware leak of **19,000+** files (Jul 2026).

n5d7b2259c43.s: The Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG), which takes decisions by consensus, has how many members?
n5d7b2259c43.x: The NSG has 48 members, works by consensus and has no permanent secretariat.
xa: Formed in **1975** (the **"London Club"**) in response to India's **1974 Pokhran-I** test.
India applied in **2016**; blocked mainly by **China** (India is not an NPT party).
Benefits of membership: **access to latest technology** and a **say in rule-making**.
**Australia** reaffirmed support for India's NSG bid (Jul 2026).

ne7bd958a8c9.s: Under the SHANTI Act, 2025, the Government retains control over:
o: Spent-fuel reprocessing and heavy-water production only
Enrichment, spent-fuel reprocessing and heavy-water production
ne7bd958a8c9.x: The Government retains control over all three: enrichment, spent-fuel reprocessing and heavy-water production.
xa: Private firms and JVs may **build, own, operate** plants — NPCIL's monopoly ends.
All heavy water plants are under the **Heavy Water Board, Mumbai** (DAE).
**Manuguru** (now Telangana) is India's **largest** HWP; **Nangal** the **first**.

n2ce59d9a2ed.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB)?
o: It licenses nuclear power plants and fuel-cycle facilities
It does not regulate radiation safety in medical and industrial applications
It inspects facilities and can suspend or revoke licences
It regulates management and transport of radioactive waste
n2ce59d9a2ed.x: The AERB does regulate radiation safety in medical and industrial applications, along with licensing, inspection and waste regulation.
xa: Set up **15 Nov 1983** by **executive order**; made **statutory** by the **SHANTI Act 2025**.
Zones: **exclusion 1.6 km**, **sterilised 5 km**, **emergency planning 16 km**.
Waste rules: **Safe Disposal of Radioactive Wastes Rules 1987**.

n8eaa7588256.s: The Convention on Nuclear Safety, adopted in 1994, entered into force in:
n8eaa7588256.x: The Convention was adopted in 1994 and came into force in 1996; India is a party to it.
xa: The **emergency planning zone** extends to **16 km**.
**Exclusion zone 1.6 km**; **sterilised zone 5 km**.
AERB can **suspend or revoke licences**.

nd3216611d54.s: Kashiwazaki-Kariwa is notable because it is:
o: the first nuclear plant in India
the world's oldest nuclear power plant
the world's largest nuclear power plant by capacity
the only Level 7 nuclear accident site
nd3216611d54.x: Kashiwazaki-Kariwa in Japan is the world's largest nuclear power plant by capacity.

n4921bc9e8ae.s: The Mahi Banswara nuclear power project is being built by:

xs: In **2017** India sanctioned **ten 700 MW PHWRs** in fleet mode — so option **(1)** is correct.

nd6f5715cb20.s: What was the share of nuclear power in India's total electricity generation in 2024–25?

n05c23387011.s: Under the 2047 nuclear power target, NPCIL is expected to add approximately:

n91eace19b0d.s: India's installed nuclear power capacity in 2026 is approximately:

IYB 2026 gave **25 reactors, 7 sites, 8,880 MW** incl. RAPP-7.

n768281f8581.s: The VVER units being added at Kudankulam are significant because they will increase India’s capacity of which type of reactors?
n768281f8581.x: The VVER units at Kudankulam add imported light-water reactor capacity to India’s nuclear fleet.

xa: Kudankulam: **2 x 1,000 MW VVER** operating; **Units 3-6 (4,000 MW)** under construction.
India's **largest operating station** (**2,000 MW**).
A ransomware group leaked **19,000+** KKNPP files (Jul 2026).

nef5a6ea53a8.s: Which one of the following heavy water plants was commissioned in 1962?
nef5a6ea53a8.x: Nangal in Punjab was the first heavy water plant and was commissioned in 1962.
nef5a6ea53a8.tq: Use the commissioning year to distinguish the earliest plant from later facilities.
xs: **Nangal** (Punjab) was commissioned in **1962** — India's **first** heavy water plant — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Tuticorin** came in **1978**, **Baroda** in **1980**, **Talcher** in **1985**.

All HWPs are under the **Heavy Water Board, Mumbai** (DAE).
**Kota** and **Talcher** both came in **1985**.

nb4a84f952cf.s: Manuguru heavy water plant is presently located in which State?
nb4a84f952cf.x: Manuguru was in undivided Andhra Pradesh when established, but it is presently in Telangana.

xs: **Manuguru** HWP is now in **Telangana** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was in **undivided AP** when set up (**1991**), hence the AP trap.
xa: Manuguru = **India's largest** HWP (APPSC 2021).
All HWPs are under the **Heavy Water Board, Mumbai**.
AP angle: **Kovvada** (US AP1000) is AP's planned NPP.

nc9b8a281bc9.s: Which one of the following is the largest heavy water plant in India?
nc9b8a281bc9.x: Manuguru is identified as India's largest heavy water plant.
nc9b8a281bc9.tq: Use the size claim carefully; do not confuse the largest plant with the first plant.
xs: **Manuguru** is India's **largest** heavy water plant — so option **(3)** is correct.
