xa: Manuguru: commissioned **1991**, then undivided AP, now **Telangana**.
⚠ **Nangal = first**; **Manuguru = largest**.
**Trombay** hosts BARC's early heavy-water work.

ne1f53ced705.s: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant uses which reactor technology and foreign collaboration?
ne1f53ced705.x: Kudankulam uses Russian VVER pressurised water reactors (PWRs).
ne1f53ced705.tq: Discriminate between reactor technology and collaborating country.
xs: **Kudankulam** uses **VVER (PWR)** reactors from **Russia** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**PFBR** is indigenous; **BWR** came from the USA at Tarapur; **AP1000** (USA) is for **Kovvada**.
xa: Russia link: **USSR accord 1988**; **DAE-Rosatom "Strategic Vision" (Dec 2014)**.
Operating: **2 x 1,000 MW** (2013, 2016); units **3-6** under construction.
⚠ **Kudankulam = Russia (VVER)**; **Jaitapur = France (EPR)**; **Kovvada = USA (AP1000)**.

n32374ff4891.s: Jaitapur Nuclear Power Project is associated with which combination?
o: Maharashtra, France, EDF and six EPR units
Andhra Pradesh, USA, Westinghouse and six AP1000 units
Tamil Nadu, Russia, Rosatom and six VVER units
Gujarat, Canada, AECL and six PHWR units
n32374ff4891.x: Jaitapur is located in Maharashtra and is associated with France's EDF and six EPR units.
n32374ff4891.tq: Match the project by combining location, partner company and reactor design.
xs: **Jaitapur** = **Maharashtra**, **France (EDF)**, **6 EPR** units — so option **(1)** is correct.

xa: Jaitapur = **9,900 MW**, planned world's largest NPP.
Industrial Way Forward Agreement: **March 2018**.

n0db8bf4a032.s: The Industrial Way Forward Agreement relating to Jaitapur was signed between NPCIL and EDF in:
n0db8bf4a032.x: NPCIL and France's EDF signed the Industrial Way Forward Agreement for Jaitapur in March 2018.
n0db8bf4a032.tq: Separate the project-specific agreement year from the broader civil nuclear agreement year.
xs: NPCIL-EDF signed the **Industrial Way Forward Agreement** for **Jaitapur** in **March 2018** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**September 2008** is the India-France civil nuclear deal; **December 2014** is the DAE-Rosatom Strategic Vision.
xa: Jaitapur: **6 EPR** units, **9,900 MW**.
France gave a **lifetime fuel-supply guarantee**.
⚠ **Jaitapur = France (EPR)**; **Kovvada = USA (AP1000)**.

nd88905c6139.s: India's Additional Protocol with the IAEA, signed in 2009, came into force in:
nd88905c6139.x: India signed the Additional Protocol in 2009 and it came into force in 2014; it covers only declared civilian facilities.
xa: **India-Specific Safeguards Agreement** came after the **2008** India-US deal.
**Imported fuel** goes only to **safeguarded** reactors.
Military facilities stayed **outside safeguards** under the 2006 plan.

n19069b9d6b3.s: Under the 2006 separation plan linked to the Indo-US nuclear deal, India:
o: Placed all its nuclear facilities, including military ones, under IAEA safeguards
Separated civil and military facilities and placed civil reactors under IAEA safeguards
Signed the NPT as a non-nuclear-weapon state
Shut down all its research reactors at Trombay
n19069b9d6b3.x: In 2006 India separated civil and military facilities and put its civil reactors under IAEA safeguards so that NSG members could supply fuel. Military facilities stayed outside safeguards, India has never signed the NPT, and the research reactors were not all shut by this plan.
n19069b9d6b3.tq: Separation plan: civil only under safeguards; imported fuel only to safeguarded reactors.
xs: The **2006 separation plan** split **civil and military** facilities and put **civil reactors under IAEA safeguards** — option **(2)**.
Military sites stayed out; India **never signed the NPT**; research reactors were not all shut.
xa: Purpose: let **NSG members supply fuel**.
**NSG waiver (September 2008)** ended **34 years** of exclusion.
**123 Agreement** (2008): PM **Manmohan Singh** + President **Bush**.

n03c311af0cd.s: India's nuclear doctrine is based on a policy of:
o: First Use only against non-nuclear states
n03c311af0cd.x: India follows a No First Use policy; it is not a party to the TPNW.
xa: India has **not signed** the **NPT**, which it calls **discriminatory** (only the **P5** are nuclear-weapon states).
India has not signed the **CTBT** (**1996**): no time-bound disarmament; subcritical tests still allowed.
The **TPNW** entered into force in **2021**; India says it adds nothing to customary law.
India **signed and ratified** the **PTBT** (**1963**).

nc95a01c733f.s: The Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG), popularly known as the ‘London Club’, was formed in response to which event?

nc95a01c733f.x: The NSG was formed in 1975, in response to India’s 1974 Pokhran-I nuclear test.

xs: The **NSG** ("**London Club**") was formed in **1975** in response to **India's 1974 Pokhran-I test** — so option **(3)** is correct.

xa: The NSG has **48 members**, works by **consensus** and has **no permanent secretariat**.
India **applied in 2016**; its entry is blocked mainly by **China** on NPT grounds.
The **NSG waiver (September 2008)** ended **34 years** of India's exclusion from nuclear trade.
⚠ NSG membership does **not** make a country an **NPT** member.

n05fc48d9d6a.s: Which country supplies approximately 80 per cent of India's uranium imports?

Imported fuel goes **only to safeguarded reactors**.

n7eb999bb942.s: The agreement associated with the Kudankulam project was signed in:
n7eb999bb942.x: The India-USSR agreement associated with Kudankulam was signed in 1988.

**2008** is the year of the **NSG waiver** and the **123 Agreement**, not Kudankulam.
xa: Delays came from the **disintegration of the USSR** and **civil-society protests** (APPSC-G1 2022 key).
**DAE-Rosatom "Strategic Vision" (Dec 2014)**: **12+ units**.
Kudankulam (**2,000 MW**) is India's **largest operating station**.
⚠ **Kudankulam = Russia (VVER)**; **Jaitapur = France (EPR)**; **Kovvada = USA (AP1000)**.

nff478b074cd.s: India signed its civil nuclear agreement with Japan in:
nff478b074cd.x: The India-Japan civil nuclear agreement dates to 2016; France's was of 30 September 2008 and Australia's of 2014.
xa: France was the **first post-waiver** partner, with a **lifetime fuel-supply guarantee** (Jaitapur).
**USA**: **123 Agreement** (2008); Kovvada (**AP1000**).
**Russia**: **1988** accord; **DAE-Rosatom Strategic Vision (Dec 2014)**.
Australia's **Administrative Arrangement** was finalised at the **3rd Annual Summit** (Jul 2026).

nda32b363bf0.s: Which country was the first to conclude a civil nuclear agreement with India after the NSG waiver of 2008?
nda32b363bf0.x: France was the first country to conclude a post-waiver civil nuclear agreement with India, on 30 September 2008.
nda32b363bf0.tq: Use the word FIRST to distinguish the earliest post-waiver agreement from later famous agreements.
xs: **France** signed the **first** post-waiver civil nuclear deal, on **30 September 2008** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Japan**'s agreement came only in **2016**; **Russia**'s ties go back to the **1988** Kudankulam accord.
xa: The France deal included a **lifetime fuel-supply guarantee** and the **Jaitapur** project.
**Jaitapur**: **6 EPR** units, **9,900 MW**; NPCIL-EDF "Industrial Way Forward Agreement" in **March 2018**.
The **NSG waiver (September 2008)** ended **34 years** of exclusion from nuclear trade.

n3b7830da309.s: The India-US 123 Agreement is named after Section 123 of the:
n3b7830da309.x: The name comes from Section 123 of the US Atomic Energy Act, 1954; the agreement was signed under Manmohan Singh and George W. Bush.
xa: The waiver ended **34 years** of exclusion from nuclear trade.
**France** signed the **first** post-waiver deal on **30 September 2008**.
India applied to the NSG in **2016**; blocked mainly by **China**.

na458b0b4744.s: The occupational dose limit for radiation workers, averaged over five years, is:
na458b0b4744.x: The limit is 20 mSv a year averaged over five years, with a maximum of 30 mSv in any one year and 100 mSv cumulative.
xa: Safety principles: **Defence in Depth** and **ALARA**.
Waste rules: **Safe Disposal of Radioactive Wastes Rules 1987**.
**700 MW PHWRs** carry **advanced safety features** post-Fukushima.

n14e8032940f.s: The design approach that uses multiple successive layers of protection in nuclear safety is known as:
n14e8032940f.x: Defence in Depth is the nuclear-safety design approach based on multiple successive and independent protective layers.
n14e8032940f.tq: Identify the exact technical term from its functional description.
xs: **Defence in Depth** is AERB's layered safety-design approach — so option **(2)** is correct.
It goes with the **ALARA** principle for radiation exposure.
xa: Dose limits: **20 mSv/yr** (5-year average), **30 mSv** max, **100 mSv** cumulative.
Post-Fukushima, **700 MW PHWRs** have **advanced safety features**; releases kept **<1% of AERB limits**.
Emergency preparedness needs **on-site + off-site** plans (**Convention on Nuclear Safety**).

nbc173c4a420.s: The International Conference on Nuclear Security (ICONS) is a ministerial conference organised by the:
nbc173c4a420.x: ICONS is the IAEA's ministerial International Conference on Nuclear Security.

xs: **ICONS** is the **IAEA**'s (International Atomic Energy Agency) ministerial **International Conference on Nuclear Security** — option **(1)**.
xa: **IAEA**: founded **1957**, HQ **Vienna, Austria** (APPSC 2021); India a **founding member**.
IAEA functions: **safeguards and verification**, safety standards, **nuclear security (ITDB)**, technical cooperation.
The **NSG** is a separate export-control group (**48 members**, **1975**).

n58b2d895670.s: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), founded in 1957, is headquartered at:
n58b2d895670.x: The IAEA is headquartered at Vienna, Austria; India is a founding member.
xa: APPSC 2021 asked IAEA HQ: **Vienna**.
IAEA's **INES** scale runs **0-7**.

n81d55ca3721.s: When the IAEA detects non-compliance with safeguards obligations, it may report the matter to the:
n81d55ca3721.x: The IAEA can report safeguards non-compliance to the United Nations Security Council.
n81d55ca3721.tq: Identify the correct international authority linked to safeguards violations.
xs: The IAEA reports safeguards non-compliance to the **UN Security Council** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The notes link it to no WTO, ICJ or Human Rights Council role.
xa: India placed **civil reactors under IAEA safeguards** (2006 separation plan).
**Additional Protocol**: signed **2009**, in force **2014**.
IAEA is an **autonomous** body in the UN system.

n28982399513.s: The Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), which India has never signed, entered into force in:
n28982399513.x: The NPT dates from 1968 and entered into force in 1970; India has never signed it.
xa: India calls the NPT **discriminatory** — only the **P5** are weapon states.
**NSG** membership does **not** make a country an NPT member (UPSC 2018).
China blocks India's NSG bid on **NPT grounds**.

nd9a907724e1.s: India has not signed the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) mainly because it objects to which of the following features?
o: The absence of any reference to nuclear disarmament
The absence of time-bound nuclear disarmament and the continued possibility of subcritical tests
The recognition of only five nuclear-weapon states
The treaty’s restriction of only atmospheric tests
nd9a907724e1.x: India has not signed the CTBT because it does not provide for time-bound nuclear disarmament and still permits subcritical tests.
nd9a907724e1.tq: Test the treaty-specific objection rather than the general purpose of the treaty.
xs: India has not signed the **CTBT** because it has **no time-bound nuclear disarmament** and still allows **subcritical tests** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **CTBT** (**1996**) bans all nuclear test explosions, not just atmospheric ones — so option (4) is wrong.
Recognising **only five** (the **P5**) nuclear-weapon states is India's objection to the **NPT**, not the CTBT — option (3).
xa: **PTBT** (**1963**) bans tests in **air, space and underwater**; India **signed and ratified** it.
**TPNW** (in force **2021**): first binding treaty banning nuclear weapons; India stays out as it **adds nothing to customary law**.
**NPT** (1968; in force **1970**): India **never signed**, calling it **discriminatory**.

n71847c0c613.s: The Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW) entered into force in:
n71847c0c613.x: The TPNW entered into force in 2021; India has not signed it, holding that it adds nothing to customary law.
xa: The **TPNW** is the **first binding treaty** banning nuclear weapons.
**CTBT** (**1996**) bans all nuclear test explosions; India has **not signed** it (no time-bound disarmament; subcritical tests still allowed).
**NPT** (1968; in force **1970**): only the **P5** are nuclear-weapon states; India calls it **discriminatory**.
India's doctrine: **No First Use**.

n8d3d8ab6ab6.s: India’s application for membership of the Nuclear Suppliers Group was made in which year, and which country has mainly blocked its entry?
n8d3d8ab6ab6.x: India applied for NSG membership in 2016. China has mainly blocked India’s entry, particularly because India is not a party to the NPT.
n8d3d8ab6ab6.tq: Pair the year of application with the country associated with the opposition.
xs: India applied for NSG membership in **2016**, and **China** has mainly blocked it — so option **(2)** is correct.
China objects on **NPT grounds**: India is **not an NPT party**.
xa: India is still **not a member**; **Australia** reaffirmed support for the bid (Jul 2026).
India's other regimes: **MTCR (2016)**, **Wassenaar Arrangement (2017)**, **Australia Group (2018)**.
The NSG (**1975**, "**London Club**") has **48 members** and works by **consensus**.

n86797fc3e2b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act (CLNDA), 2010?
o: Section 17(b) gave the operator a right of recourse against suppliers
The Indian Nuclear Insurance Pool was created to cover suppliers
It capped operator liability at Rs 1,500 crore
n86797fc3e2b.x: CLNDA made operator liability no-fault, capped at Rs 1,500 crore with the Centre paying beyond the cap.
xa: The **SHANTI Act 2025** repealed **CLNDA 2010** and the **Atomic Energy Act 1962**.
SHANTI caps: **₹3,000 crore** (large) / **₹1,500 crore** (medium) / **₹100 crore** (SMRs); **supplier liability removed**.
SHANTI got Presidential assent on **20 Dec 2025**.

nd4d5f81d13c.s: Along with the Atomic Energy Act, 1962, the SHANTI Act, 2025 repealed the:
o: Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010
nd4d5f81d13c.x: The SHANTI Act repealed the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the CLNDA, 2010; it only amended Section 4 of the Patents Act.
xa: Timeline: introduced in Lok Sabha **15 Dec 2025**; passed LS/RS **17 / 18 Dec 2025**; assent **20 Dec 2025**.
It **ends NPCIL's monopoly**: Indian private firms and JVs can build, own, operate.
It made the **AERB statutory**, answerable to Parliament.

n41a0f019ad5.s: Under the SHANTI Act, 2025, the liability cap for small modular reactors is:
n41a0f019ad5.x: The graded caps are ₹3,000 crore for large facilities, ₹1,500 crore for medium facilities and ₹100 crore for SMRs.
xa: Liability beyond the cap is met by a **Nuclear Liability Fund**.
**Supplier liability removed** (unlike CLNDA's **Sec 17(b)**).
CLNDA's old operator cap was **₹1,500 crore**.

n2e657c939f4.s: The SHANTI Act, 2025 caps total nuclear liability at:
n2e657c939f4.x: Total liability is capped at 300 million SDR (about Rs 3,900 crore); the excess is met through a Nuclear Liability Fund.
xa: ⚠ **CLNDA Sec 17(b)** = supplier recourse; **SHANTI** = supplier liability removed.
Graded caps: **₹3,000 crore** (large), **₹1,500 crore** (medium), **₹100 crore** (SMRs).
Critics: removing supplier liability and capping damages hurts **victims' compensation**.

nfa45f05a305.s: In August 2026, the Supreme Court issued notice to the Union and the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board in connection with a petition challenging which aspect of the SHANTI framework?
o: Its target of 100 GW nuclear capacity by 2047
nfa45f05a305.x: A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant issued notice in a petition challenging the liability caps under SHANTI.
nfa45f05a305.tq: Match the current judicial development with the precise legal issue.
xs: The Supreme Court (CJI **Surya Kant**, **3-judge Bench**) issued notice on a petition challenging SHANTI's **liability caps** — option **(1)**.
SHANTI **lets private companies and JVs enter**, so "prohibition on private participation" (option 2) is wrong.
xa: SHANTI caps: **₹3,000 crore** (large), **₹1,500 crore** (medium), **₹100 crore** (SMRs); total **300 million SDR**.
**Supplier liability removed**; excess via a **Nuclear Liability Fund**.
The **100 GW by 2047** target is the Nuclear Energy Mission, not the subject of the case.

ndisaster-management-7-12.s: What does the Emergency Planning Zone (EPZ) consist of?
o: A single exclusion area of 1–1.5 km around a reactor
A network of specialised centres for detection and response
A district-level command structure led by the District Collector
ndisaster-management-7-12.x: The Emergency Planning Zone is a set of concentric zones around a plant for planning protective actions. The 1–1.5 km exclusion area is only its inner part.
ndisaster-management-7-12.tq: Discriminate the EPZ from the exclusion zone.
n: The Emergency Planning Zone (EPZ) consists of concentric zones for protective actions. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 19-22]
xs: The **EPZ** consists of **concentric zones for protective actions** — option **(1)**, extending to **16 km**.
The **1–1.5 km** area is the **exclusion zone**, where **public habitation is prohibited** — not the EPZ.
xa: The **sterilised zone** extends up to **5 km**, curbing population growth.
⚠ APPSC-GS 2022 keyed the exclusion zone as **1 km**.
**AERB** was set up on **15 Nov 1983** and made **statutory** by the **SHANTI Act 2025**.

n23f9585adbd.s: The 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam has been developed by:
o: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre's Dhruva unit
n23f9585adbd.x: PFBR is developed by BHAVINI (APPSC-G1 2024 key) and designed by IGCAR; NPCIL holds equity in BHAVINI. ASHVINI is the NPCIL-NTPC joint venture building Mahi Banswara, AERB is the regulator, and Dhruva is a BARC research reactor.
n23f9585adbd.tq: PFBR: built by BHAVINI, designed by IGCAR.
xs: The **PFBR (500 MWe, Kalpakkam)** was developed by **BHAVINI** (APPSC-G1 2024 key) — so option **(1)** is correct.
**ASHVINI** builds **Mahi Banswara**; **AERB** is the regulator; **Dhruva** is a research reactor.
xa: PFBR was designed by **IGCAR**.
NPCIL holds **equity in BHAVINI**.
AP DISCOMs sought **100 MW** from BHAVINI's plant (2024-25).

ncd8e788e657.s: Which one of the following would NOT follow from India's membership of the Nuclear Suppliers Group?
o: Participation in the export-control decision process
Access to the latest nuclear technology
ncd8e788e657.x: NSG membership could provide access to advanced technology and a say in rule-making, but it would not make India an NPT member.
ncd8e788e657.tq: Separate membership of an export-control regime from membership of a treaty.
xs: **Automatic membership of the NPT** would **not** follow from NSG membership — so option **(2)** is correct.
NSG membership gives **access to the latest technology** and a **say in rule-making** (export rules) — options (1), (3) and (4) are genuine benefits.
⚠ **UPSC 2018** trap: NSG membership does **not** make a country an **NPT** member.
xa: The NSG was formed in **1975** in response to India's **1974 Pokhran-I** test.
India **applied in 2016**; blocked mainly by **China** on NPT grounds.
The NSG has **48 members** and **no permanent secretariat**.
ncd8e788e657.fixed: stem self-contradictory/oddly worded; answer (NPT membership) unchanged

n53de4e7bcec.s: A dirty bomb is best described as:
o: A reactor meltdown caused by loss of coolant
A missile carrying a thermonuclear warhead
A conventional explosive that disperses radioactive material
A nuclear weapon producing a sustained chain reaction
n53de4e7bcec.x: A dirty bomb, or radiological dispersal device, uses a conventional explosion to spread radioactive material.
n53de4e7bcec.tq: Discriminate between radioactive contamination and a nuclear chain-reaction explosion.
xs: A **dirty bomb** (radiological dispersal device) is a **conventional explosive that disperses radioactive material** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It has **no nuclear chain reaction** and no city-flattening blast — so it is not a nuclear weapon or thermonuclear warhead (options 2 and 4).
xa: Typical sources are **medical or industrial**, e.g. **Cs-137** and **Co-60**.
Its damage is **contamination and panic**.
The IAEA's nuclear-security work includes the **ITDB** database.

nf3be2755568.s: Which one of the following radioisotopes is supplied by BRIT as sodium iodide for the diagnosis and treatment of thyroid disorders?
nf3be2755568.x: Iodine-131 emits beta and gamma radiation and is supplied by BRIT as sodium iodide for thyroid diagnosis and treatment.
nf3be2755568.tq: Match the isotope with its characteristic organ-related application.
xs: **Iodine-131** (beta + gamma) is supplied by BRIT as **sodium iodide** for **thyroid** diagnosis and treatment — option **(2)**.
**Iron-59** = iron metabolism/anaemia; **Phosphorus-32** = leukaemia; **Tc-99m** = imaging heart, brain, bones, lungs.
xa: ⚠ **I-131 = thyroid**; **Na-24 = blood flow**; **As-74 = brain tumour**; **P-32 or Co-60 = leukaemia**.
**Tc-99m** is the **most widely used diagnostic imaging isotope**.
**I-131** is also exported, with Co-60, to **40+ countries**.

n1c5e64c99b7.s: Sodium-24 is particularly useful for studying:
n1c5e64c99b7.x: Sodium-24 emits gamma radiation and is used in blood-flow and circulation studies; it can also help detect pipeline leaks.
n1c5e64c99b7.tq: Identify the isotope from its specific diagnostic application.
xs: **Sodium-24** (gamma) is used to study **speed of blood flow** and **circulation blocks** — option **(1)**.
**Thyroid** = **I-131**; **iron metabolism/anaemia** = **Iron-59** — so options (2) and (4) are wrong.
xa: UPPSC 2012 key: blood-flow speed = **radio-sodium**.
Na-24 is also used for **pipeline leak detection**.
**As-74** locates **brain tumours**.

n73612d6dc52.s: The most widely used diagnostic radioisotope is:
n73612d6dc52.x: Technetium-99m is the most widely used diagnostic isotope, used to image the heart, brain, bones and lungs.
xa: Tc-99m is a **gamma** emitter used in **SPECT**.
BRIT supplies **Tc-99m** among its radiopharmaceuticals.
⚠ **PET = positron (F-18 FDG)**; **SPECT = single gamma (Tc-99m)**.

ne610b1aee8a.s: Radioimmunoassay is used to measure minute quantities of ____ in blood.
ne610b1aee8a.x: Radioimmunoassay uses radioisotopes to measure minute quantities of hormones, enzymes and drugs in blood.
xa: **BRIT** supplies **RIA kits**.
**Teletherapy** = external beam (**Co-60** unit); **brachytherapy** = source inside/next to the tumour.
**Tc-99m** is the most widely used diagnostic imaging isotope.

n117be65d835.s: Which one of the following radioisotopes is used in the treatment of blood cancer (leukaemia)?
n117be65d835.x: Phosphorus-32, a beta emitter, treats leukaemia and polycythaemia; exam keys (UPPSC 2012) also accept Cobalt-60. Sodium-24 is used to study blood-flow speed, Arsenic-74 to locate brain tumours, and Carbon-14 to date organic material.
n117be65d835.tq: Blood cancer = P-32 (or Co-60); blood flow = Na-24.
xs: **Phosphorus-32** (beta) treats **blood cancer (leukaemia)** and polycythaemia — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Sodium-24** = **blood-flow speed**; **Arsenic-74** = **brain tumours**; **Carbon-14** = **dating** organic material.
xa: ⚠ Keys accept both **P-32 and Co-60** for leukaemia (UPPSC 2012: either; BPSC 2016: "more than one").
P-32 also traces **plant phosphorus uptake**.
**Radon** is the radioactive **noble gas** used to treat cancer (APPSC-G1 2018).

n940132d2c98.s: SPECT imaging generally uses which radioisotope?
n940132d2c98.x: SPECT uses single gamma emitters, chiefly Technetium-99m; PET uses positron emitters such as F-18 FDG.
xa: **Tc-99m** images the **heart, brain, bones, lungs**.
⚠ **PET = positron (F-18 FDG)**; **SPECT = single gamma (Tc-99m)**.
**P-32** is a **beta** emitter used for leukaemia, not imaging.

o: An external Co-60 beam from a distant unit
Injecting F-18 FDG to detect positrons
Placing a sealed radiation source inside or next to the tumour
nb15515a5837.x: Brachytherapy places a sealed source (e.g. Ir-192 or I-125 seeds) inside or next to the tumour; teletherapy is external-beam, commonly Co-60.
xa: Radiotherapy may use **gamma rays**, X-rays or beta emitters.
New therapy: **177Lu-DOTA-FAPI-2286** (Lutetium-177), targeted radionuclide therapy (2026).
**Ir-192** is also used in **gamma radiography** of welds.

n460d3c92d88.s: Which of the following is primarily used as a positron emitter in PET imaging?
n460d3c92d88.x: PET mainly uses the positron emitter F-18 FDG. Tc-99m is commonly associated with SPECT, while Co-60 is used in teletherapy.
n460d3c92d88.tq: Separate PET positron emitters from SPECT and therapy sources.
xs: **PET** detects **positron** emitters, mainly **F-18 FDG** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Tc-99m** is a single-gamma **SPECT** isotope; **Co-60** is for **teletherapy**; **I-125 seeds** are for **brachytherapy**.
xa: The **30 MeV Medical Cyclotron, Kolkata** produces **FDG** commercially.
**Gamma rays** underpin **PET**, radiotherapy and nuclear medicine (UPSC GS).
**As-74**, another **positron** emitter, locates brain tumours.

nc6a10f25409.s: The 30 MeV Medical Cyclotron at Kolkata commercially produces:
nc6a10f25409.x: The Kolkata Medical Cyclotron produces F-18 FDG commercially for PET imaging.
xa: **F-18 FDG** is the main **positron** emitter for **PET**.
The **Kolkata accelerator** is one of India's isotope production sites.
**Co-60** teletherapy units and **I-131** come from reactors/BRIT, not the cyclotron.

n4db2cf497e9.s: Which radioactive noble gas is used in the treatment of cancer?
n4db2cf497e9.x: Radon is the radioactive noble gas used to treat cancer (APPSC-G1 2018). Argon, neon and xenon are noble gases too, but none is the cancer-therapy gas in question.
n4db2cf497e9.tq: Radioactive noble gas for cancer = Radon.
xs: **Radon** is the radioactive **noble gas used to treat cancer** (APPSC-G1 2018) — option **(1)**.
**Argon**, **neon** and **xenon** are noble gases, but the notes link only **radon** to cancer therapy.
xa: Radiotherapy rays: **gamma rays** (Co-60 teletherapy), X-rays or beta emitters.
**Brachytherapy** uses **Ir-192** or **I-125** seeds next to the tumour.
**P-32 or Co-60** treat **leukaemia**.

nc8d6a305fb6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about radiometric dating?
o: Carbon-14 dating is used mainly for volcanic rocks older than a billion years
U-238 to Pb-206 dating is used for the oldest rocks and the age of the Earth
K-40 to Ar-40 dating is used for volcanic rocks and fossil-bearing layers
Carbon-14 dating covers once-living remains up to about 50,000 years
nc8d6a305fb6.x: Carbon-14 (half-life about 5,730 years) dates once-living organic remains up to about 50,000 years, not ancient volcanic rocks.
xa: **RTG** fuel is **Plutonium-238**; it turns **decay heat** into electricity via **thermocouples**.
⚠ RTG = **Pu-238** (not Pu-239); **C-14** only for once-living remains.
RTGs power deep-space missions: **Voyager**, **Cassini**, **Curiosity**, **Perseverance**.

naf4561a0fde.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about industrial uses of radiotracers?
o: They detect leaks in buried oil and gas pipelines
Sediment tracking at ports increases the frequency of desilting campaigns
They are used to study seepage from dams
They are used for flow measurement
naf4561a0fde.x: Radiotracer tracking of sediment transport can help reduce, not increase, the frequency of desilting campaigns.
xa: Sediment tracking means **longer gaps between desilting** campaigns.
**Sodium-24** is used for **pipeline leak detection**.
**Gamma radiography** tests welds and castings non-destructively.

n084cc2c66aa.s: The Tata Memorial Centre serves as the Anchor Centre for the IAEA initiative known as:
n084cc2c66aa.x: Tata Memorial Centre is the Anchor Centre for the International Atomic Energy Agency’s ‘Rays of Hope’ initiative.
n084cc2c66aa.tq: Match the institution with the exact international initiative.
xs: **Tata Memorial Centre** is the **Anchor Centre** for the IAEA's **'Rays of Hope'** — option **(3)**.
'Rays of Hope' is an **IAEA** cancer-care initiative; Tata Memorial anchors it in India.
xa: **National Cancer Grid (2012)**: treats **7.5 lakh+** new patients a year = **>60%** of India's cancer burden.
The **30 MeV Medical Cyclotron, Kolkata** supplies **FDG** to hospitals.
New therapy: **Lutetium-177** targeted radionuclide therapy in routine practice (2026).

n94e170b70e4.s: Who first demonstrated induced mutation in crop plants (barley) using X-rays?
n94e170b70e4.x: L. J. Stadler first demonstrated mutation breeding using X-rays in 1930. Gamma and neutron radiation are also used subsequently for inducing mutations.
n94e170b70e4.tq: Use the person-year association to identify the scientific contribution.
xs: **L.J. Stadler** first showed mutation breeding in **1930** using **X-rays** — option **(3)**.
Today **gamma** and **neutron** radiation are also used.
xa: Mutation breeding: radiation changes seeds **at the genetic level** so desired traits can be chosen.
BARC has released **72** Trombay varieties (2026) — **non-GMO**, climate-resilient.
Newest: banana **TBM-9**, sorghum **RTS-43**.
n94e170b70e4.fixed: Stadler's X-ray mutation work dates to 1928, not 1930

nfd758cc425e.s: TBM-9, a newer BARC Trombay variety developed with NRCB, Trichy, is a variety of:
nfd758cc425e.x: TBM-9 is the newer banana variety developed with NRCB, Trichy; RTS-43 is a sorghum variety.
xa: ⚠ **TBM-9 = banana**; **RTS-43 = sorghum**.
BARC Trombay varieties: **72** now vs older count **23**.
The older **23**: **10 pulses**, **9 groundnut**, **2 mustard**, **1 rice**, **1 jute**.

n5dd3a5611d1.s: In the sterile insect technique, radiation-sterilised males are released so that:
o: Mating with wild females produces no viable offspring
n5dd3a5611d1.x: Gamma-sterilised males mate with wild females without producing viable offspring, so pest numbers decline.
xa: BARC also makes cheap **pheromones** for **sweet-potato** and **cotton moths**.
**Food irradiation** also **kills insects, parasites and pathogens**.
Mutation breeding uses **gamma** and **neutron** radiation.

n0e3c400d2bb.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated effect or use of food irradiation?
o: Increasing the genetic diversity of crop seeds in the field
n0e3c400d2bb.x: Food irradiation can stop sprouting, delay ripening and kill insects, parasites and pathogens. Increasing genetic diversity of field crops is associated with mutation breeding, not food irradiation.
n0e3c400d2bb.tq: Find the option belonging to a neighbouring technology rather than food irradiation.
xs: **Increasing the genetic diversity of crop seeds** is not food irradiation — option **(1)** is the answer; that is **mutation breeding**.
Food irradiation **stops sprouting**, **delays ripening** and **kills insects, parasites and pathogens** — options (2)-(4).
xa: These effects **extend shelf life**.
Works by **radiolysis** of water; sources **Co-60 gamma**, **X-rays**, **electron beams**.
**KRUSHAK** at **Lasalgaon** irradiates **onions**.

n5f44d6d95b1.s: The 'Radura' logo is an international symbol used to indicate:
n5f44d6d95b1.x: Radura is the international green symbol marking irradiated food. Organic, GM and fortified foods carry their own separate labels; Radura says only that the food was treated with radiation.
xs: The **Radura logo** is the international green symbol marking **irradiated food** — option **(1)**.
It does not denote **organic**, **GM** or **fortified** food.
xa: Food irradiation sources: **Co-60 gamma**, **X-rays**, **electron beams**.
India has **28** commercial food-irradiation facilities.
Irradiation **stops sprouting** and **delays ripening**.

n061418ff5dd.s: BRIT (Board of Radiation and Isotope Technology) is:
o: The regulator for radiation safety in India
An industrial unit of the Department of Atomic Energy for radioisotopes
A cancer hospital under the Ministry of Health
n061418ff5dd.x: BRIT is an industrial unit of the DAE dealing with radioisotopes, radiopharmaceuticals and isotope technology.
xa: APPSC-GS 2012 key: BRIT works in **isotope technology**.
Products: radioisotopes, **radiopharmaceuticals** (Tc-99m, **I-131 as sodium iodide**), **RIA kits**, **radiography cameras**, **gamma chambers**.
Serves **1,470+** user organisations plus exports.

nf8780b565d5.s: India's leading producer of radioisotopes is:
nf8780b565d5.x: BARC, set up as AEET in 1954 and renamed in 1967, is India's leading producer of radioisotopes.
xa: BARC's research reactors: **Dhruva** (largest), **Apsara** (Asia's first), **KAMINI** (only **U-233** fuelled).
Isotope production: **Trombay research reactors**, **Kolkata accelerator**, **NPCIL power plants**.
Radioisotopes (**Co-60**, **I-131**) are exported to **40+ countries**.

n27c5ad26cc8.s: The largest research reactor of BARC is:
n27c5ad26cc8.x: Dhruva is the largest research reactor; Apsara was Asia's first and KAMINI is the only U-233-fuelled reactor.
xa: All three are at **BARC, Trombay** (set up **1954**, renamed **1967**).
BARC is **India's leading producer of radioisotopes**.
BARC also runs **KRUSHAK** (onion irradiation, **Lasalgaon**).

n7f7d3b30680.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about food irradiation in India?
o: Irradiation cannot be applied to bulk food
Irradiated mangoes have been exported to the United States
Irradiation can be carried out on packed food
n7f7d3b30680.x: Irradiation can be carried out on packed or bulk food.
xa: **KRUSHAK** (BARC) at **Lasalgaon (Nashik)** irradiates onions.
The **Radura** logo marks irradiated food.
Gamma processing plants: **17 MoUs**, **40** now operating.

nda4e8aca862.s: The KRUSHAK facility at Lasalgaon is associated with the irradiation of
nda4e8aca862.x: KRUSHAK at Lasalgaon in Nashik, Maharashtra, is an onion irradiation facility. Food irradiation helps control sprouting and extend shelf life.
xs: **KRUSHAK** at **Lasalgaon (Nashik)**, Maharashtra, is BARC's irradiation facility for **Onions** — option **(2)**.
Irradiation **stops sprouting** and extends shelf life.
xa: ⚠ **KRUSHAK = Lasalgaon (onions)**; **e-beam plant = Indore**; **cyclotron = Kolkata**.
**Mangoes** irradiated in India are exported to the **USA, Australia, Malaysia, South Africa**.
**ISOMED 2.0** (May **2025**) sterilises **healthcare products**.

nb29725e065a.s: ISOMED 2.0, completed in May 2025, is a:
o: High-intensity gamma irradiator for sterilising healthcare products
nb29725e065a.x: ISOMED 2.0 is a high-intensity gamma irradiator for sterilising healthcare products, completed in May 2025.
xa: Completed **May 2025**; the **only land-based stationary** one of its kind in the world.
Gamma processing plants: **17 MoUs**, **40** now operating; **BRIT supplies Co-60**.
**Electron-beam plant, Indore**: **1.53 crore** medical devices sterilised by Sept 2025.

n608f90d3579.s: The isotope generally used as fuel in radioisotope thermoelectric generators is
n608f90d3579.x: Plutonium-238 is the fuel commonly associated with RTGs. It has been described as a by-product of weapons-development programmes.
n608f90d3579.tq: Identify the fuel isotope rather than the isotope used for dating or detection.
xs: RTGs run on **Plutonium-238** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ RTG fuel is **Pu-238**, not Pu-239; **Americium-241** is the alpha emitter in **smoke detectors**; **K-40** and **C-14** are dating isotopes.
xa: Pu-238 is a **by-product of weapons programmes**.
RTGs turn **decay heat** into electricity through **thermocouples** — **no fission**, no moving parts.
Used where **sunlight is weak**: **Voyager**, **Cassini**, **Curiosity**, **Perseverance**.

n026c4bf0ded.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of spacecraft or planetary missions associated with the use of RTG power sources?
n026c4bf0ded.x: Voyager, Cassini and Curiosity are examples of missions using RTG power where sunlight is weak. Perseverance is another such example.
n026c4bf0ded.tq: Recognise the mission group linked to RTG use.
xs: **Voyager**, **Cassini** and **Curiosity** used **RTG** power — option **(1)**.
**Perseverance** is another RTG-powered rover.
xa: RTGs suit **deep-space missions** where **sunlight is weak**.
Fuel: **Plutonium-238**; principle: **Seebeck effect** thermocouples.
RTGs are **not reactors** — no fission.

n43afa18b9c3.s: Gamma radiography for non-destructive testing of welds and castings commonly uses sources such as
n43afa18b9c3.x: Gamma radiography of welds and castings uses radiography cameras with sources such as Iridium-192 and Cobalt-60.
n43afa18b9c3.tq: Distinguish industrial radiography sources from dating and tracer isotopes.
xs: Gamma radiography of welds and castings uses **radiography cameras** with **Ir-192** (Iridium-192) and **Co-60** (Cobalt-60) — option **(1)**.
**C-14** and **K-40** are **dating** isotopes; **P-32** is for leukaemia and tracers; **Am-241** is in **smoke detectors**.
xa: It is a **non-destructive testing** method.
**BRIT** makes the **radiography cameras**.
**Ir-192** is also a **brachytherapy** source.

n25680833317.s: Which of the following is a conventional source of energy?
n25680833317.x: Firewood is a conventional source; solar energy is non-conventional and wind energy renewable.
xa: Conventional list: **coal, petroleum, natural gas, hydel, firewood, cattle-dung cake**.
Non-conventional = by definition **renewable** (UPPSC 2023).
⚠ **Hydel** is conventional yet renewable.

n066586803f6.s: Non-conventional sources of energy are, by definition:
n066586803f6.x: Non-conventional sources (solar, wind, etc.) are by definition renewable (UPPSC 2023 key). Non-renewable and fossil-based describe coal, oil and gas, which are conventional; 'imported' is not a classification of energy sources.
xs: Non-conventional sources are by definition **Renewable** (UPPSC 2023 key) — option **(1)**.
**Non-renewable**/**fossil** sources — coal, oil, natural gas — fall under **conventional**.
xa: Conventional also includes **hydel**, **firewood** and **cattle-dung cake**.
⚠ **Hydel** is conventional yet renewable.
**Natural gas is NOT green energy** (APPSC 2019).

nbf4c06d91f2.s: Which one of the following energy sources is NOT derived from the Sun?
nbf4c06d91f2.x: Geothermal energy comes from the Earth's internal heat, so it is not solar-derived (like nuclear and tidal). Wind, hydro and biomass are stored solar energy: the Sun drives winds and the water cycle and powers photosynthesis.
nbf4c06d91f2.tq: Not from the Sun: nuclear, geothermal, tidal.
xs: **Geothermal energy** comes from the **Earth's internal heat**, not the Sun — option **(1)**.
**Wind**, **hydro** and **biomass** are **stored solar energy**.
xa: Also NOT from the Sun: **nuclear** (fission) and **tidal** (Moon's pull).
UPPSC 2022 key accepted both **nuclear** and **geothermal**.
Fossil fuels too are **stored solar energy**.

n046e794919c.s: As of August 2026, which source formed the largest component of India's installed renewable-energy capacity?
n046e794919c.x: Solar, at 164.59 GW (Aug 2026), is the largest RE component. Wind (58.14 GW) is second, large hydro is about 52 GW, and bio-power about 11.75 GW. In 2014 wind was the largest, but solar has overtaken it.
n046e794919c.tq: Now solar > wind > large hydro; in 2014 wind led.
xs: **Solar** is the **largest RE component** — **164.59 GW** (Aug 2026) — option **(1)**.
**Wind** is 2nd (**58.14 GW**); **large hydro** ~**51.96 GW**; **bio-power** **11.75 GW**.
xa: In **2014** wind (**21 GW**) was the largest; solar was **2.8 GW**.
Bio-power = biomass/bagasse **10.87 GW** + waste-to-energy **0.88 GW**.
**Small hydro**: **5.18 GW**.

n57803fe8d7a.s: India's global rank in installed wind-power capacity is:
n57803fe8d7a.x: India ranks 4th in the world in wind power, while it is 3rd in total renewable capacity after China and the USA. China ranks first; India is neither second nor as low as tenth.
xs: India is **4th in wind** — option **(1)** (Fourth).
In total RE capacity India is **3rd**, after **China** and the **USA**.
xa: Wind capacity: **58.14 GW** (Aug 2026), 2nd-largest RE source.
Wind **crossed 50 GW** in **Mar 2025**.
**Gujarat** leads wind with **12,314 MW**.

ne574b477524.s: Which of the following is a renewable resource?
ne574b477524.x: Geothermal energy, like wind, is renewable; coal and nuclear fuels are finite, non-renewable resources.
xa: Renewable list: **solar, wind, hydro (incl. tidal/wave), geothermal, biomass**.
**Nuclear is NOT renewable** (APPSC 2024), though it is **non-fossil**.
**Geothermal** is **not derived from the Sun** — it is Earth's internal heat.

n6fa42af32f0.s: Which one of the following correctly gives India's cumulative solar capacity on 31 December 2022?
n6fa42af32f0.x: Cumulative solar capacity stood at 63.30 GW on 31 December 2022.
n6fa42af32f0.tq: Distinguish the dated milestone from the later 2025 and 2026 figures.
xs: Solar stood at **63.30 GW** on **31 Dec 2022** (APPSC 2023 key) — option **(4)**.
**127.33 GW** was Oct-Nov 2025; **150.26 GW** was 31 Mar 2026; **53.12 GW** is a **wind** figure.
xa: Solar in **2014**: only **2.8 GW**.
FY 2025-26: record **44.6 GW** solar added.

n45e3ca51a2c.s: In 2024–25, renewable energy contributed about ____ of India's electricity generation.
n45e3ca51a2c.x: Renewables were about half of installed capacity but supplied only about 22% of generation; coal and thermal gave about 75%.
xa: ~**40 GW** RE projects **lack PPAs**.
**8,133 GWh** solar curtailed in Apr-Jun 2026 (transmission mismatch).
Coal is ~**42%** of capacity (Jul 2026).

n2a15f2f0436.s: The original target of 175 GW renewable-energy capacity by 2022 consisted of which combination?
o: 75 GW solar, 60 GW wind, 30 GW bio-power and 10 GW small hydro
60 GW solar, 100 GW wind, 10 GW bio-power and 5 GW small hydro
100 GW solar, 50 GW wind, 20 GW bio-power and 5 GW small hydro
100 GW solar, 60 GW wind, 10 GW bio-power and 5 GW small hydro
n2a15f2f0436.x: The 175 GW target comprised 100 GW solar, 60 GW wind, 10 GW bio-power and 5 GW small hydro. The target was not achieved on time and was later superseded.
n2a15f2f0436.tq: Break the aggregate target into its source-wise components.
xs: **175 GW by 2022** = **100 GW solar**, **60 GW wind**, **10 GW bio-power**, **5 GW small hydro** — option **(4)**.
It was **missed on time** and is now **superseded**.
xa: New target: **500 GW** non-fossil capacity by **2030** (~**292 GW** solar).
**Net Zero by 2070**.
Small hydro has used only ~**24.6%** of its **21 GW** potential.

naad629677d2.s: Of India's estimated solar potential of 748 GW, about what share had been utilised?
naad629677d2.x: India's solar potential is estimated at 748 GW, of which only about 4.5% had been utilised.
xa: Top RE-potential states: **Rajasthan (23.70%)** … **Andhra Pradesh (9.10%)**.
⚠ **24.6%** is the share of **small hydro** potential (**21 GW**) used, not solar.
Solar capacity reached **164.59 GW** (Aug 2026), ~**58x** of 2014.

n31fd4aec86d.s: According to IRENA 2026 rankings, India stood at which position globally in renewable-energy capacity?
n31fd4aec86d.x: India ranked third in renewable-energy capacity after China and the United States. The stated capacities were China 2,258 GW, the USA 468 GW and India 250.5 GW.
n31fd4aec86d.tq: Rank the countries using the capacity figures rather than the order of mention alone.
xs: India is **3rd** in RE capacity after **China** and the **USA** (IRENA 2026) — option **(3)** (Third).
China **2,258 GW**; USA **468 GW**; **India 250.5 GW**; Brazil **228 GW**.
xa: India is **4th in wind** and **3rd in solar** (2025-26).
Top RE state: **Gujarat** (**42.58 GW**).

n71478f6f1c8.s: Which State was the leading renewable-energy State, with 42.58 GW and 16.5% of India's renewable capacity in June 2026?
n71478f6f1c8.x: Gujarat was the leading renewable-energy State in June 2026, with 42.58 GW and 16.5% of India's renewable capacity.
n71478f6f1c8.tq: Link the State ranking to both its capacity and percentage figures.
xs: **Gujarat** led with **42.58 GW**, **16.5%** of India's RE (Jun 2026) — option **(2)**.
**Rajasthan** leads RE **potential** (**23.70%**), not installed capacity.
xa: Gujarat also leads **wind** (**12,314 MW**).
⚠ **Top RE potential = Rajasthan**; **top installed RE = Gujarat**.
**Andhra Pradesh** has **9.10%** of RE potential.

n19ac4a35f45.s: The Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) applies to:
o: DISCOMs and large or designated consumers
n19ac4a35f45.x: RPO requires DISCOMs and large or designated consumers to procure a prescribed share of power from renewables.
xa: **Solar RPO** raised to **8% by March 2022** (2017).
A **wind RPO trajectory up to 2030** was declared.
The obligation was recast as **RCO** under the **Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act 2022**.

n8860cc048f1.s: The Solar Renewable Purchase Obligation was raised to what level by March 2022?
n8860cc048f1.x: The Solar RPO trajectory raised the solar obligation to 8% by March 2022.
n8860cc048f1.tq: Recall the specific percentage and date attached to the Solar RPO trajectory.
xs: **Solar RPO** was raised to **8%** by **March 2022** (in **2017**) — option **(3)**.
The **8%** figure belongs to the **solar** RPO trajectory.
xa: RPO binds **DISCOMs** and **large/designated consumers**.
**Wind RPO trajectory up to 2030** declared.
**RCO** recast RPO as an obligation to **consume** renewable energy.

n6e4644d3b6a.s: Under the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022, the Renewable Purchase Obligation has been recast as an obligation to:
n6e4644d3b6a.x: RPO concerns purchase of renewable power; the RCO recasts it as an obligation to consume renewable energy under the 2022 amendment.
xa: RPO applies to **DISCOMs** and **large/designated consumers**, not just households.
**Solar RPO**: **8% by March 2022**.

ne2855806bdf.s: Inter-State Green Energy Corridor lines, which evacuate renewable power to load centres, are built by:
ne2855806bdf.x: Inter-State GEC lines are built by Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL).
xa: GEC-I funding: **MNRE 40% : KfW 40% : state utility 20%**.
The **PGCIL study 2012** triggered the GEC.
Curtailment of **8,133 GWh** solar (Apr-Jun 2026) shows the transmission gap.

n5d2d2d14819.s: Which of the following States was NOT included among the eight States covered by Intra-State GEC-I?
n5d2d2d14819.x: GEC-I included Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu. Telangana was not included in the listed eight-State group.
n5d2d2d14819.tq: Find the outsider by comparing each option with the complete membership list.
xs: **Telangana** is not among GEC-I's states — option **(1)**.
GEC-I: **Andhra Pradesh**, **Gujarat**, HP, Karnataka, MP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, **Tamil Nadu**.
xa: GEC-I: ~**9,700 ckm** lines, ~**24 GW** RE.
Funding: **MNRE 40% : KfW (Germany) 40% : state utility 20%**.
AP has **9.10%** of India's RE potential.

ndf084a73254.s: The financing pattern for Intra-State GEC-I was:
o: MNRE 50%, KfW loan 25% and State utility 25%
MNRE 20%, KfW loan 40% and State utility 40%
MNRE 40%, KfW loan 20% and State utility 40%
MNRE 40%, KfW loan 40% and State utility 20%
ndf084a73254.x: The cost-sharing pattern was MNRE 40%, KfW of Germany loan 40% and State utility contribution 20%.
ndf084a73254.tq: Match each percentage with the correct financing institution or agency.
xs: GEC-I funding: **MNRE 40%**, **KfW loan 40%**, **state utility 20%** — option **(4)**.
Total cost **₹10,141.68 cr**; **KfW** is from **Germany**.
xa: ⚠ Memory aid: **40 : 40 : 20** = **MNRE : KfW : state utility**.
GEC-II approved **2022** for **7** states.
Inter-state lines are built by **PGCIL**.

nf076f2ad573.s: The Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency Limited (IREDA) is best described as:
o: A commercial bank under the Ministry of Finance
An NBFC under the administrative control of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
A statutory regulator under the Ministry of Power
A non-governmental organisation under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
nf076f2ad573.x: IREDA is an NBFC under the administrative control of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE).
nf076f2ad573.tq: Identify the institution by both its category and controlling ministry.
xs: **IREDA** is an **NBFC** under the administrative control of **MNRE** (Ministry of New and Renewable Energy) — option **(2)**.
It is a lender to RE projects — not a commercial bank, regulator or NGO.
xa: Set up **1987**; listed via IPO in **November 2023**.
It gives term loans for **renewable energy** and **energy-efficiency** projects.
Funds come from **Govt**, **multilateral agencies** and the **capital market**.

n5c4d3385fd3.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of IREDA?
o: Determining statutory electricity tariffs for all States
Providing term, bridge and working-capital loans
n5c4d3385fd3.x: IREDA undertakes project financing, appraisal, consultancy and provides term, bridge and working-capital loans. Determination of statutory tariffs for all States is not its function.
n5c4d3385fd3.tq: Find the activity that belongs to a regulator rather than a project-financing agency.
xs: **Determining statutory electricity tariffs** is not IREDA's job — option **(2)** is the answer.
IREDA does **project financing**, **appraisal**, **consultancy**, and **term, bridge and working-capital loans**.
xa: IREDA is an **NBFC** under **MNRE**.
Set up **1987**; IPO **November 2023**.
Funds: Govt, multilateral agencies, capital market.

n2b61c607aef.s: Which of the following is NOT a source of green energy?
n2b61c607aef.x: Natural gas is a fossil fuel; sunlight, wind and algae-based sources are green.
xa: Exam pattern: "NOT renewable / NOT green / NOT from the Sun" → **nuclear**, **natural gas**, **geothermal**.
**Nuclear is NOT renewable** (APPSC 2024).
**Solar energy** is the most important for India (APPSC-G2 2017).

n6c83bff1a23.s: The National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE), an autonomous body of MNRE, is located at:
n6c83bff1a23.x: NISE is at Gurugram and is the technical focal point for solar R&D.
xa: The **ISA** HQ foundation stone was laid at the **NISE campus, Gwal Pahari, Gurugram** (**25 Jan 2016**).
NISE made the first national floating-solar assessment: **102.18 GW**.
NISE estimated ground potential at **748 GW**.

n14777861be3.s: The dominant solar-cell technology in the market is:
n14777861be3.x: Crystalline silicon (mono- and polycrystalline) cells dominate the market; thin-film cells are cheaper and flexible but less efficient.
xa: IIT Bombay (MNRE) perovskite cell: **26%**, world's **2nd highest**.
Thin-film types: **CdTe, CIGS, a-Si**.
PV gives **DC**; an **inverter** converts it to AC.

n35ebe0c6cb8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about solar thermal (concentrated solar power) technology?
o: Mirrors may concentrate sunlight to heat a fluid
Solar power towers are associated with solar thermal applications
The heat can produce steam for a turbine
Heat storage is not possible in such systems
n35ebe0c6cb8.x: Solar thermal systems can store heat; they collect or concentrate solar heat for water, steam and power generation.
xa: Solar thermal heat serves **water, steam and power**.
**Agrivoltaics** = crops + panels on the same land.
Solar PV CUF is only ~**21%**.

n3c947cd196b.s: In a solar PV system, which device converts the DC produced by the cells into AC for the grid?
n3c947cd196b.x: PV cells produce direct current; an inverter converts it to alternating current. A transformer only changes voltage.
xa: PV cells: **monocrystalline**, **polycrystalline silicon**, **thin-film**.
⚠ **PV** = light → electricity directly; **CSP** = heat → steam turbine.
**Bifacial** modules absorb light on **both faces**.

ne665da0ccc9.s: Most parts of India receive solar irradiation of about ____ per square metre per day.
ne665da0ccc9.x: Most of India receives 4–7 kWh/m²/day, with 250–300 clear sunny days a year.
xa: APPSC-G1 2024: "both statements true, II explains I" on sunny days and potential.
Ground potential: **748 GW** (NISE; **3%** of wasteland); only ~**4.5%** used.
Installed solar: **157.05 GW** (2026), **29%** of total capacity.

ne10f15af291.s: NISE has estimated India's ground-based solar potential, assuming use of 3% of wasteland, at about:
ne10f15af291.x: NISE estimates about 748 GW, of which only about 4.5% has been used.
xa: Floating solar potential: **102.18 GW** on reservoirs (NISE, Jun 2026).
RE-potential leader: **Rajasthan 23.70%**; **AP 9.10%**.
⚠ **748 GW** = ground potential; **63.30 GW** = installed on **31 Dec 2022**.

n871d6820de9.s: The stated capacity-utilisation factor of solar power in India is about:
n871d6820de9.x: The stated CUFs are about 21% for solar, 36–40% for wind and about 85% for coal.
xa: Low CUF explains why RE's **capacity** share exceeds its **generation** share.
Installed solar: **157.05 GW** (2026), **29%** of capacity.
Solar pumps under **PM-KUSUM B, C**.

n3944801f431.s: India's reported installed solar capacity, about 29 per cent of total capacity, is:
n3944801f431.x: Reported installed solar capacity was 157.05 GW, about 29 per cent of total capacity.
xa: Solar in **2014**: only **2.82 GW**.

n64cc5936e78.s: India added a record solar capacity of approximately how much in financial year 2025-26?
n64cc5936e78.x: A record 44.61 GW of solar capacity was added in FY 2025-26. The 2.82 GW figure relates to the earlier 2014 level, while about 38 GW refers to the 2025 addition in another comparison.
n64cc5936e78.tq: Distinguish annual additions from historic benchmark and cross-country comparison figures.
xs: A record **44.61 GW** solar was added in **FY2025-26** — option **(3)**.
**2.82 GW** was the **2014** level; ~**38 GW** was the calendar-**2025** addition.
xa: The 2025 addition (~**38 GW**) **beat the US for the first time** (Ember).
India was the **2nd-largest solar growth market** in 2025.

naab9341f614.s: India's solar capacity addition in 2025, which beat that of the US for the first time, was about:
naab9341f614.x: India added about 38 GW in 2025, becoming the second-largest solar growth market and overtaking the US for the first time.
xa: Record **44.61 GW** added in FY2025-26.
**63.30 GW** on **31 Dec 2022** (APPSC key).
Module imports fell **65%** (**$2,152 M** in FY25 → **$758 M**).

nda92b474023.s: The Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission ('Solar India') was launched in:
nda92b474023.x: The mission was launched in January 2010 as one of NAPCC's eight missions; June 2015 is when its target was revised to 100 GW.
xa: ⚠ **20 GW** = original target; **100 GW** = revised (**40 GW rooftop + 60 GW** grid).
Off-grid targets: **200 MW** (Phase I), **1,000 MW** (II), **2,000 MW** (III).
Successor goal: **500 GW non-fossil by 2030**.

nc3df6fa53ce.s: The Indian Energy Exchange (IEX), established in 2008, is regulated by:
nc3df6fa53ce.x: IEX is regulated by CERC and trades DAM, TAM, renewable energy and ESCerts.
xa: **Green Energy Open Access Rules, 2022**: **Ministry of Power**; threshold **1 MW → 100 kW**.
RPO obliges DISCOMs to buy a share of renewable power.

n9acc53d7baa.s: On 21 March 2017, the target of the Solar Park Scheme was enhanced to:
n9acc53d7baa.x: Launched on 12 December 2014 with a 20 GW target for over 25 parks, the scheme was raised to 40 GW on 21 March 2017.
xa: Solar parks commissioned **~3,084 MW** in 2025 (to 30 Nov).
Largest commissioned park: **Bhadla** (**2,245 MW**, Rajasthan).
It provides **land, transmission, clearances**.

n0d98ba086a0.s: Rooftop solar incentives, the ARUN app and Suryamitra skilling are associated with:
n0d98ba086a0.x: SRISTI is associated with rooftop incentives, the ARUN app and Suryamitra skill development.
xa: Rooftop solar cost: about **Rs 30,000 per kW** after subsidy.
Rooftop costs **₹2.2-3.5 lakh** (a debate point).
**PM Surya Ghar** now drives rooftop solar.

n932a3c18527.s: The Green Energy Open Access Rules, 2022 cut the open-access threshold for green power from 1 MW to:
n932a3c18527.x: The Ministry of Power's Rules cut the threshold from 1 MW to 100 kW.
xa: **GTAM** (IEX, **2020**) is the RE-only trading segment.
**IEX** was set up in **2008**, regulated by **CERC**.

n5dbe7fa9611.s: Which State leads India's floating solar potential on reservoirs, with about 16 GW?
n5dbe7fa9611.x: Maharashtra (about 16 GW) and Madhya Pradesh (about 14 GW) lead the national potential of about 102.18 GW.
xa: The assessment was the **first national** one, by **NISE** (Jun 2026).
**Omkareshwar** (**278 MW**) is India's largest floating plant.
World floating capacity: ~**9.6 GW** (2024), **90%** in Asia.

nf28bfd59497.s: The first national assessment titled “Solar PV Potential of India (Floating Solar)” was associated with which institution?
nf28bfd59497.x: The first national assessment of floating solar PV potential was undertaken by the National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE).
nf28bfd59497.tq: Identify the correct technical institution rather than a project implementing agency.
xs: The first national assessment, **"Solar PV Potential of India (Floating Solar)"**, was by **NISE** (National Institute of Solar Energy) — option **(1)**.
NISE is an **autonomous body of MNRE** at **Gurugram**.
xa: It estimated **102.18 GW** floating potential on reservoirs.
NISE also estimated **748 GW** ground potential.
**SECI** implements the floating **PM Surya Sarovar Yojana**.

n939e54a8e6d.s: Which of the following is reported to be still absent in India's solar sector?
o: An approved list of module manufacturers (ALMM)
n939e54a8e6d.x: Solar-waste recycling norms are still absent; cell capacity lag and grid curtailment are other concerns.
xa: Modules ~**190 GW** vs cells ~**25 GW**.
Rooftop costs **₹2.2-3.5 lakh** — another debate point.
The **ALCM** cell mandate (Jun 2026) aims to close the gap.

nenvironment-1-1.s: India's first National Centre for Marine Biodiversity is at:
nenvironment-1-1.x: India's first National Centre for Marine Biodiversity is at Jamnagar, near the Gulf of Kachchh Marine National Park.
n: India's first National Centre for Marine Biodiversity is located in Jamnagar, Gujarat. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-4]
xa: **Jim Corbett** (**1936**), originally **Hailey National Park**, is India's first national park.
**Surat, Gujarat** is the first district with **100% solar-powered PHCs**.
**Diu** is the first UT to run **100% on solar** by day.

na8885e9218b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana?
o: It provides free power up to 500 units per month
It is a Central Sector scheme for 2024 to 2026-27
It aims to cover one crore rooftop households
It envisages 30 GW of rooftop solar capacity
na8885e9218b.x: The scheme provides free power up to 300 units per month, not 500.
xa: Launched **Feb 2024**; outlay **₹75,021 cr**.
**Model Solar Village**: **₹1 cr** to one village per district.
>**75 lakh** applications, >**39.7 lakh** RTS systems (**22 Jul 2026**).

o: Small grid-connected plants on barren land or farmland
n78d3b581f5c.x: Component B covers standalone solar pumps; A covers small grid-connected plants and C solarisation of grid-connected pumps.
xa: Progress (**30 Nov 2025**): Comp A **667.31 MW**; Comp B **9.42 lakh** pumps; Comp C **10.99 lakh** solarised.
⚠ **PM-KUSUM is a domestic MNRE scheme**, not an ISA project (APPSC-G2 2025).
PM-KUSUM projects must use **ALMM** modules.

na663321501e.s: The outlay of PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana is about:
na663321501e.x: The scheme, launched in February 2024, has an outlay of about Rs 75,021 crore.
xa: It subsumed **Rooftop Phase-II** (2019).
~**8 GW** rooftop added (2025-26).
AP: **4,11,915** rooftop systems (**4 Aug 2026**).

n2e7db30dd20.s: The PM Surya Sarovar Yojana (₹5,070 crore) targets how much floating solar capacity by 2030–31?
n2e7db30dd20.x: The scheme involves ₹5,070 crore and targets 5,000 MW of floating solar by 2030–31.
xa: CFA up to **Rs 1 crore/MW**; implemented via **SECI**.
**2-hour storage (10,000 MWh)** mandatory.
Cabinet cleared it on **31 Jul 2026**.

nb914cb9b7e2.s: Under the PM Surya Sarovar Yojana, Central Financial Assistance of up to how much is provided, and through which agency is the scheme implemented?
o: Rs 1 crore per MW, through SECI
Rs 10 lakh per MW, through NISE
Rs 1 crore per MW, through IREDA
Rs 5 crore per MW, through NTPC
nb914cb9b7e2.x: The scheme gives CFA of up to Rs 1 crore/MW and the 5,000 MW target is to be delivered via SECI. NISE did the floating-potential assessment, IREDA and NTPC are not the stated agency, and Rs 10 lakh or Rs 5 crore per MW are wrong amounts.
nb914cb9b7e2.tq: Surya Sarovar: Rs 5,070 cr, Rs 1 cr/MW, 5,000 MW by 2030-31, SECI.
xs: CFA is up to **Rs 1 crore per MW**, through **SECI** — option **(1)**.
**IREDA** is an RE financier and **NISE** a research body — neither implements this scheme.
xa: Outlay: **Rs 5,070 crore**.
**2-hour storage** (**10,000 MWh**) is mandatory.

na6a96d1791e.s: Which State has the largest share of India's estimated renewable-energy potential, at about 23.70 per cent?
na6a96d1791e.x: Rajasthan leads with about 23.70%. Maharashtra follows with 14.26%, while Gujarat and Andhra Pradesh each have about 9.10%.
na6a96d1791e.tq: RE potential: Rajasthan first (23.70%); AP 9.10%, level with Gujarat.
xs: **Rajasthan** has the largest share of RE potential, **23.70%** — option **(3)**.
Next: **Maharashtra 14.26%**, **Gujarat 9.10%**, **AP 9.10%**, Karnataka **8.59%**, MP **8.09%**.
xa: Rajasthan also hosts **Bhadla** (**2,245 MW**), the largest commissioned solar park.
Solar ground potential: **748 GW**.
AP angle: **50,000 acres** of barren land offered for solar lease (Apr 2026).

nf62ef97e603.s: The successor long-term goal associated with India’s solar-energy transition is:
nf62ef97e603.x: India’s successor goal is 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030, associated with its COP26 pledge.
nf62ef97e603.tq: Distinguish the broader non-fossil target from the earlier solar-only target.
xs: The successor goal is **500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030** (COP26 pledge) — option **(1)**.
It is **non-fossil**, not solar-only; **100 GW by 2022** was the old **NSM** solar target.
xa: The **500 GW** includes ~**292 GW** solar.
NSM's historic target: **100 GW by 2022** (**40 rooftop + 60 grid**).
Solar stood at **164.59 GW** in Aug 2026.

ne61684c9566.s: The Omkareshwar floating solar project (278 MW) is located on which river?
ne61684c9566.x: Omkareshwar floating solar is on the Narmada in Khandwa district, Madhya Pradesh, and is planned to reach 600 MW.
xa: Omkareshwar is **India's largest floating** plant.
⚠ **Bhadla** = largest park; **Khavda** = largest RE park when complete; **Omkareshwar** = largest floating.
Installed floating solar in India: ~**0.7 GW**.

n08e4deedadf.s: Compared with land-based installations, the upfront cost of floating solar projects is approximately:
n08e4deedadf.x: Floating solar costs about 25% more upfront, but saves land, reduces evaporation and gains efficiency from water cooling.
xa: Floating potential: **102.18 GW**; installed ~**0.7 GW**.
**PM Surya Sarovar** targets **5,000 MW** floating by **2030-31**.

ncd2dbbf786b.s: The ALMM module list covers approximately ____ of manufacturing capacity.
ncd2dbbf786b.x: The module list covers about 190 GW, while the cell list covers only about 25 GW.
xa: PLI added **11 GW** module + **5 GW** cell capacity in 2025.
Module capacity: **172 GW** (2026).
⚠ "Cell capacity lags module capacity" is a listed criticism.

n459b02a0f01.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as one of the three ultra mega solar parks in Andhra Pradesh?
n459b02a0f01.x: Kurnool, NP Kunta and Kadapa are the three Andhra Pradesh ultra mega solar park locations. Omkareshwar is associated with the largest floating solar plant.
n459b02a0f01.tq: Find the location belonging to a different category rather than an Andhra Pradesh park.
xs: **Omkareshwar** is a **floating** plant in **Khandwa, MP**, not an AP park — option **(4)**.
AP's three ultra mega parks: **Kurnool**, **NP Kunta**, **Kadapa** (+ **Ramagiri** hybrid park).
xa: **NP Kunta (Ananthapuramu-I)**: **1,500 MW**; **Kurnool**, **Kadapa**: **1,000 MW** each.
Omkareshwar: **278 MW**, India's **largest floating** plant.

na7b0b13d4b2.s: The State nodal agency for solar development in Andhra Pradesh is:
na7b0b13d4b2.x: NEDCAP is the State nodal agency for Andhra Pradesh's solar programme; SECI and MNRE have national-level roles.
xa: AP parks: **Kurnool**, **NP Kunta**, **Kadapa** + **Ramagiri** hybrid.
AP offered **50,000 acres** of barren land for solar lease (Apr 2026).

na086ca458ac.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra Pradesh's solar-energy cluster?
o: Kurnool and YSR Kadapa parks anchor the Rayalaseema renewable-energy cluster
NTPC Simhadri has a floating solar plant in Visakhapatnam
SECI is the State nodal agency
About 50,000 acres of barren land have been offered for solar lease
na086ca458ac.x: NEDCAP, not SECI, is the nodal agency for Andhra Pradesh's solar programme.
xa: **Ramagiri** (Ananthapuramu): hybrid solar-wind park.
AP: **4,11,915** rooftop systems (**4 Aug 2026**).
AP has **9.10%** of India's RE potential.

n6866be83356.s: Modhera in Gujarat is recognised as India's first:
n6866be83356.x: Modhera, the Sun Temple town in Mehsana district, became India's first 24x7 solar-powered village.
n6866be83356.tq: Match the place with the exact first, avoiding nearby solar superlatives.
xs: **Modhera** (Sun Temple town, **Mehsana**, Gujarat) is India's first **24x7 solar-powered village** — option **(2)**.
It runs on a **6 MW** plant + **15 MWh BESS**, opened **9 Oct 2022**.
xa: ⚠ **Bancha** = solar kitchens (MP); **Modhera** = 24x7 solar village (Gujarat).
**Diu**: first UT 100% on solar by day.
**Cochin**: first fully solar airport.

n38c2147d7dc.s: The International Solar Alliance (ISA) was launched at which place and event?

New Delhi during the founding conference of ISA

nc948a9a43cf.s: The Framework Agreement of the International Solar Alliance entered into force on:

n7e72cca8c4d.s: Which of the following initiatives was launched at the 8th Assembly of the International Solar Alliance held in New Delhi?

n9b0800de718.s: Which initiative of the International Solar Alliance is intended to share solar power across time zones through a transnational grid?

n19809f7cd20.s: The Global Solar Facility of the ISA primarily seeks to:

De-risk solar investment in underserved regions

xs: The **Global Solar Facility** is an ISA fund to **de-risk solar investment in underserved regions** (payment guarantees, insurance) — option **(4)**.

xa: ISA target: **$1 trillion** by **2030**.

The **common procurement platform** pools demand.

n1d0afdb1481.s: The International Solar Alliance aims to mobilise solar investment of approximately:

**OSOWOG** roadmap at the **8th Assembly**.

nc5bd68d0d54.s: Ramagiri in Ananthapuramu district of Andhra Pradesh is known for which type of renewable-energy park?

Output at full rated power to actual output

na3b75afc10d.s: The typical Capacity Utilisation Factor of wind power in India is about:

Wind is the **2nd-largest RE source** after solar.

n87c42ace21b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE)?

n855c3a1049c.s: The nodal agency under the National Offshore Wind Energy Policy, 2015 is:

n0df40af9f29.s: The National Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy, 2018 promotes:

n18710537193.s: The principal wind-farm cluster in Andhra Pradesh is located in:

nb82233cbc1e.s: Ramagiri in Andhra Pradesh is notable for hosting a:

n36c5c6d8516.s: Which microorganism is associated with the production of bioethanol by fermentation of sugar or starch?

nc42b9e08583.s: In biomass gasification, biomass or waste is heated with limited oxygen to produce syngas consisting mainly of:

o: Unpurified biogas stored at atmospheric pressure

xs: **CBG** is **purified, compressed biogas**, **chemically identical to CNG** — option **(3)**.
It is renewable and carbon-neutral, promoted under **SATAT**.
xa: **SATAT** was launched in **2018** by **MoPNG**.
CBG progress remains "limited" despite SATAT, even as **90%** of LPG imports pass **Hormuz**.
Draft **CAFE III** norms (from **Apr 2027**) let makers claim credit for **ethanol, CBG**.

n967e3b8e21c.s: Biodiesel is commercially produced by which of the following processes?
o: Pyrolysis of lignocellulosic residues without a catalyst
Transesterification of vegetable oils or animal fats with methanol or ethanol
Fermentation of starch by methanogenic bacteria
Electrolysis of water in the presence of vegetable oil
n967e3b8e21c.x: Biodiesel is produced by transesterifying vegetable oils or animal fats with methanol or ethanol, producing fatty-acid methyl or ethyl esters.
n967e3b8e21c.tq: Identify the precise conversion process rather than a nearby biofuel process.
xs: Biodiesel is made by **transesterification** of **vegetable oils/animal fats** with **methanol/ethanol** — option **(2)**.
**Pyrolysis** is heating without oxygen (→ biochar, bio-oil, syngas); **fermentation** gives **bioethanol**.
xa: Biodiesel = methyl or ethyl **ester of fatty acids**.
**Palm stearin oil** feeds about **94%** of India's biodiesel (mostly imported).
**Jatropha curcas** seeds give biodiesel (APPSC-GS **2019**).

n660db919e67.s: Power alcohol in India is best described as:
o: Fuel-grade ethanol made mainly from molasses
Biodiesel made exclusively from palm stearin oil
Hydrogen produced by electrolysis of water
n660db919e67.x: Power alcohol refers to fuel-grade ethanol, which in India is made mainly from molasses, a by-product of the sugar industry.
n660db919e67.tq: Discriminate between closely related fuel terms by their feedstock and composition.
xs: **Power alcohol** is **fuel-grade (anhydrous) ethanol** used as motor fuel, in India made mainly from **molasses** — option **(1)**.
Methane from dung is **gobar gas**; palm stearin feeds **biodiesel**.
xa: **Molasses** is a sugar-industry by-product.
**Gasohol** = petrol + ethanol blend, typically ~**10%** ethanol.
Sugar mills may now make ethanol directly from **cane juice**.

n968e69ea69a.s: Which of the following feedstocks is characteristic of second-generation biofuels?
n968e69ea69a.x: Second-generation biofuels use non-food lignocellulosic residues such as rice straw, straw, husk, wood chips and bamboo.
n968e69ea69a.tq: Classify the feedstock according to whether it is food-based, residual or genetically modified.
xs: **Rice straw** is a **2G** (non-food lignocellulosic) feedstock — option **(4)**.
**Corn grain** and **sugarcane juice** are **1G** food-crop feedstocks; **GM algae** is **4G**.
xa: 2G feedstocks: crop residue, **straw**, **husk**, **wood chips**, **bamboo**, forest waste, non-edible oils.
**IOCL Panipat (2022)** used **rice straw** and **bagasse** — first commercial 2G plant.
2G avoids the **food-fuel conflict** but needs complex thermochemical/biochemical conversion.

nf9a90936983.s: About 94% of India's biodiesel feedstock is:
nf9a90936983.x: Palm stearin oil accounts for about 94% of India's biodiesel feedstock.
xa: ⚠ **94%** of biodiesel = **palm stearin** (imported), not jatropha.
India has **400+ tree species** bearing **non-edible oilseeds**.
Other feedstocks: rapeseed, soybean, sunflower, animal tallow, **algae**.

n9665680147f.s: Under the National Policy on Biofuels 2018, surplus food grains can be used for ethanol production only with the approval of:
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
n9665680147f.x: Surplus food grains may be converted to ethanol only with NBCC approval (APPSC-G2 2025). FCI supplies the rice but does not approve; MNRE and NITI Aayog are not the approving body under the policy.
n9665680147f.tq: Surplus grain -> ethanol needs NBCC nod.
xs: **Surplus food grains** may be used for ethanol only with **National Biofuel Coordination Committee (NBCC)** approval — option **(2)** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
NPB 2018 widened ethanol feedstock beyond molasses to **sugarcane juice, surplus FCI rice, maize, damaged foodgrains**.
xa: The **2022 amendment** allows **new members** to be added to the NBCC.
**Food vs fuel** debate: sugar prices rising (**Sep 2026**).
Maize-ethanol pricing pulled land from **pulses and oilseeds**.

nbe4e2226863.s: In the feedstock-differentiated pricing of ethanol procured by Oil Marketing Companies, the correct order from highest to lowest price is:
nbe4e2226863.x: Ethanol made from maize has the highest price, rice-based ethanol the lowest, and molasses-based ethanol lies between them.
nbe4e2226863.tq: Arrange the three feedstocks by price instead of merely recalling one isolated value.
xs: Order: **maize** (highest), **molasses** (middle), **rice** (lowest) — option **(4)**.
Under **EBP**, OMCs pay **feedstock-differentiated prices** to distilleries.
xa: Maize ethanol price **CAGR 11.7%** (FY22-25).
Maize-ethanol pricing pulled land from **pulses and oilseeds**.
**Surplus food grains** need **NBCC** approval.

n42174f65551.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about MNRE's classification of energy sources?
o: Bio-power includes biomass, bagasse cogeneration and waste-to-energy
Geothermal, tidal and OTEC are renewable sources under development
Nuclear capacity of 8.78 GW is counted separately
Nuclear power is classified as renewable energy
n42174f65551.x: Nuclear power is non-fossil but not classified as renewable; its capacity is counted separately.
xa: **Large hydro** was added to MNRE's RE list in **2019**.
**Bio-power capacity**: **11.75 GW** (**Aug 2026**); national **WtE** capacity **0.88 GW**.
**OTEC** needs a ~**20 deg C** temperature difference; viable in the tropics (**30N-30S**).

ne3a90655653.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about biogas?
o: Methane makes up about 85–95% of biogas
It is mainly methane and CO2 from anaerobic digestion of organic matter
Its methane is formed by methanogenic archaea in the absence of oxygen
The slurry left after digestion is a good organic manure
ne3a90655653.x: Methane is about 50–75% of biogas; 85–95% is the methane share of piped natural gas.
xa: **Gobar gas** is biogas from **cattle dung** — biomass energy (APPSC 2019).
**Jashbhai Patel**'s floating-drum "**Gramalakshmi**" plant was popularised by **KVIC**.
**CBG** is purified biogas, **chemically identical to CNG**.

n7327d8e1c7f.s: The 'Gramalakshmi' floating-drum gobar gas plant of Jashbhai Patel was popularised by:
n7327d8e1c7f.x: The 1950s Gramalakshmi plant was popularised by KVIC, not MNRE.
xa: **Gobar gas** = biogas from cattle dung; it is **biomass energy**.
MNRE runs the **Biogas Programme** under the **National Bioenergy Programme 2021-26** for small/medium rural plants.
**GOBARdhan** (**2018**) is the umbrella for cattle dung → biogas/bio-CNG.

nfdee73f5cf3.s: SATAT, launched in 2018 by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, aims primarily to promote:
o: CBG production from agricultural residue and municipal waste
Ethanol production only from imported crude oil
nfdee73f5cf3.x: SATAT, or Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation, was launched in 2018 by MoPNG to promote CBG from agricultural residue and municipal waste.
nfdee73f5cf3.tq: Expand the acronym and match the initiative with its ministry and objective.
xs: **SATAT** (**2018**, **MoPNG**) promotes **Compressed Biogas (CBG)** from **agri-residue** and **municipal waste** — option **(1)**.
SATAT = **Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation**.
xa: ⚠ **SATAT** = MoPNG; **National Bioenergy Programme** = MNRE; **co-firing** = Ministry of Power (**SAMARTH**).
CBG is **chemically identical to CNG**.

na24c0629784.s: GOBARdhan (Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan) was launched in:
na24c0629784.x: GOBARdhan was launched in 2018, the same year as SATAT.
xa: **SATAT** (**2018**, **MoPNG**) promotes **compressed biogas**.
GOBARdhan models: **Zakariyapura** (household), **Varanasi** (dairy), **Banas** (large-scale).
**National Bioenergy Programme** Phase-I: **₹858 cr** (MNRE).

nf94afd10989.s: The Phase-I outlay of the National Bioenergy Programme (2021–2026) is:
nf94afd10989.x: Phase-I (1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026) has an outlay of ₹858 crore, implemented by MNRE through State Nodal Agencies.
xa: Components: **Waste to Energy**, **Biomass** (briquettes, pellets, cogeneration), **Biogas** (small/medium rural plants).
Inspection: **Sardar Swaran Singh National Institute of Bio-Energy, Kapurthala (Punjab)**.
⚠ **SATAT** belongs to **MoPNG**, not MNRE.

nbf2012e6644.s: The Ministry of Power policy of 2021 mandated biomass co-firing in coal-based plants at:
nbf2012e6644.x: The 2021 policy mandated 5% biomass co-firing in coal plants, to rise to 7%.
xa: It is run by National Mission **SAMARTH**.
As of **31 Jul 2025**: ~**29.78 LMT** pellets co-fired in **71** coal plants, cutting ~**3.57 MT CO2**.
MNRE's **Biomass Programme** funds the pellets and briquettes.

n9f87629324d.s: Which institutional mechanism is associated with implementation of biomass co-firing in thermal power plants?
n9f87629324d.x: National Mission SAMARTH is associated with the biomass co-firing initiative in thermal power plants.
n9f87629324d.tq: Distinguish the implementing mission from other energy policies and schemes.
xs: Biomass co-firing in coal plants is run by **National Mission SAMARTH** — option **(4)**.
The **NBCC** relates to biofuel policy; **CAFE III** is a vehicle-efficiency norm; the **Small Hydro Power Development Scheme** concerns small hydro.
xa: Co-firing policy: **Ministry of Power**, **2021** — **5%** rising to **7%**.
⚠ **SATAT** = MoPNG; **National Bioenergy Programme** = MNRE; co-firing = Ministry of Power.
~**29.78 LMT** pellets co-fired in **71** coal plants (as of **31 Jul 2025**).

n0994c9bee63.s: Which of the following is a limitation of algal biofuel?
n0994c9bee63.x: Energy-intensive lipid extraction is a limitation; high yield and use of wastewater and CO2 are advantages.
xa: Other limitations: high **cultivation and harvesting cost**, **contamination** and scale-up problems, heavy **water and nutrient** needs.
**CSIR-NIIST** and **DBT-ICT Centre** research algal biofuel.
**3G** biofuels = **algae** (PYQ **2023**).

n46f16323f10.s: India's target for biodiesel blending in diesel by 2030 is:
n46f16323f10.x: India targets 5% biodiesel blending by 2030; actual blending remains below 0.5%.
xa: OMC biodiesel procurement rose from **1.1 crore L (FY16)** to **36.7 crore L (FY25)**.
Belgian firm **VITO** launched a biodiesel project at **Ayodhya** (**April 2023**).
The original NPB 2018 targets were **E20 + B5** by **2030**.

n1175cad5a75.s: Which one of the following is NOT an objective of the National Policy on Biofuels?
o: Discouraging the production of advanced biofuels
n1175cad5a75.x: The National Policy on Biofuels aims to reduce import dependence, promote domestic feedstock, strengthen energy security and generate employment. It does not discourage advanced biofuels.
n1175cad5a75.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated policy objectives.
xs: **Discouraging advanced biofuels** is NOT an objective — option **(4)**; the policy actually boosts **2G/advanced fuels**.
NPB aims: cut **import dependence**, promote **domestic feedstock**, **energy security**, **jobs**.
