xa: **Advanced biofuels** = 2G ethanol, drop-in fuels from MSW, 3G biofuels, **bio-CNG**.
Original targets: **20%** ethanol and **5%** biodiesel by **2030**.
VGF, tax credits and **differential pricing** support advanced biofuels.

n996bf8f7cef.s: The 2022 amendment to the National Policy on Biofuels advanced the E20 target to Ethanol Supply Year:
n996bf8f7cef.x: The 2018 policy aimed at E20 by 2030; the 2022 amendment advanced it to ESY 2025-26.
xa: Blends in 2018 were only ~**2%** and **<0.1%**.
**E20** achieved; **mandatory E20** petrol from **1 Apr 2026**, minimum **RON 95**.
**BIS IS 19850:2026** covers **E22, E25, E27, E30** petrol.

n64ff25a4f9e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2022 amendment to the National Policy on Biofuels?
o: It barred the addition of new members to the NBCC
It permitted biofuel units in SEZs and EOUs under Make in India
It permitted exports in specific cases
n64ff25a4f9e.x: The amendment allowed new members to be added to the NBCC.
xa: It also advanced **E20** to **ESY 2025-26** from **2030**.
It gave a **boost to 2G/advanced fuels**.
**PM JI-VAN** now says "**advanced biofuels**" in place of "2G ethanol".

nb1298f55eaf.s: Under the National Policy on Biofuels, which of the following is a 'basic' biofuel?
nb1298f55eaf.x: Basic biofuels are 1G bioethanol and biodiesel; 2G ethanol, drop-in fuels, 3G biofuels and bio-CNG are advanced biofuels.
xa: **1G** uses food crops; **3G** uses **algae**.
Differential pricing, **VGF** and tax credits support advanced biofuels.
**PM JI-VAN Yojana**: **12 commercial ABPs**, outlay **₹1,969.50 crore**, extended to **2028-29**.

n2091b28d515.s: Which section of the Motor Vehicles Act permits engine conversion to biofuels?
n2091b28d515.x: Section 52 of the Motor Vehicles Act permits conversion of engines to biofuels.
xa: Other enablers: **VGF**, **tax credits**, **differential pricing** for advanced biofuels.
The **2022 amendment** allowed biofuel units in **SEZs / EOUs**.

nfad2c96fea9.s: The implementation timeline of the revised PM JI-VAN Yojana extends to:
nfad2c96fea9.x: The revised scheme covers advanced biofuels, including bolt-on and brownfield projects, up to 2028–29.
xa: Launched in **2019** to support **2G ethanol**.
**12 commercial ABPs**, outlay **₹1,969.50 crore**, ~**10** demo units.
The **Ethanol Interest Subvention Scheme** separately funds **distillery capacity**.

n6f249a5fe67.s: The PM JI-VAN Yojana was launched in:
n6f249a5fe67.x: PM JI-VAN Yojana was launched in 2019 to support 2G ethanol and subsequently expanded to advanced biofuels.
n6f249a5fe67.tq: Use the launch year, not the later revision period, as the deciding fact.
xs: **PM JI-VAN Yojana** was launched in **2019** — option **(3)**.
It began as support for **2G ethanol**; now revised to **advanced biofuels**.
xa: Extended to **2028-29**, covering **bolt-on / brownfield** plants.
⚠ **NPB** and **SATAT** are from **2018**; **National Bioenergy Programme** from **2021**.
First commercial 2G plant: **IOCL Panipat (2022)**.

ncf45919cd06.s: India's Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) target for international flights by 2030 is:
ncf45919cd06.x: The SAF roadmap sets 1% by 2027, 2% by 2028 and 5% by 2030, in line with ICAO's net-zero 2050 goal.
xa: **BioE3 Policy 2024** backs bio-jet fuel.
SAF uses **drop-in synthesised hydrocarbons**, not direct ethanol.
**IOCL Panipat** = first Indian ISCC **CORSIA**-certified SAF producer (**Aug 2025**).

n0aaaed0f04e.s: Small hydro projects are commonly developed at:
o: Hill streams and canal falls only
Canal falls and toes of dams only
Hill streams, canal falls and toes of dams
n0aaaed0f04e.x: Run-of-river small hydro may use hill streams, canal falls and water released at dam toes.
xa: Small hydro = up to **25 MW**.
Installed **5.18 GW** (~**25%** of potential).
**Small Hydro Power Development Scheme** was in the news.

ncfd3e5c9071.s: India's lead ocean-energy research body is:
ncfd3e5c9071.x: The National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Chennai, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, is the lead ocean-energy research body.
xa: First wave plant: **Vizhinjam, Kerala (1991)**.
**IIT Roorkee** supports small hydro; **Kapurthala** institute inspects bioenergy projects.
OTEC sites: **Lakshadweep**, **Andaman and Nicobar**.

n680efd77a49.s: In the food-versus-fuel debate, the rise in maize area has been accompanied by a decline in the area under:
n680efd77a49.x: Maize-ethanol pricing has been linked with diversion of land from pulses and oilseeds.
xa: EBP pricing: **maize highest**, rice lowest, molasses in between.
**Surplus food grains** need **NBCC** approval.
**2G** biofuels avoid the food-fuel conflict.

n6c1348b401c.s: Inspection under MNRE's National Bioenergy Programme is entrusted to the Sardar Swaran Singh National Institute of Bio-Energy located at:
n6c1348b401c.x: SSS-NIBE is at Kapurthala, Punjab. Chennai hosts NIWE and NIOT, Gurugram hosts NISE, and Dehradun hosts CSIR-IIP - none is the bioenergy inspection body.
xs: The **Sardar Swaran Singh National Institute of Bio-Energy** is at **Kapurthala, Punjab** — option **(1)**.
It handles **inspection** under MNRE's **National Bioenergy Programme**.
xa: **NIOT, Chennai** (MoES) is India's lead **ocean-energy** research body.
**IIT Roorkee**'s Dept. of Hydro and Renewable Energy gives **small hydro** technical support.
**CSIR-NIIST** and the **DBT-ICT Centre** do **algal biofuel** research.

nee0ac5ae0c6.s: India's first commercial-scale bamboo bioethanol plant, dedicated on 14 September 2025, is at:
nee0ac5ae0c6.x: The Numaligarh plant uses bamboo, a non-food lignocellulosic (second-generation) feedstock.
xa: **IOCL Panipat (2022)** = first commercial **2G** plant (rice straw, bagasse).
⚠ First 2G **bamboo** plant = **Numaligarh**; first commercial 2G = **Panipat**.
**Corn** and **sugarcane** are **1G** food-crop feedstocks.

n5ab3206d320.s: Which policy specifically supports bio-jet fuel among the following?
n5ab3206d320.x: The BioE3 Policy 2024 supports bio-jet fuel.
n5ab3206d320.tq: Match the policy name with its stated fuel application.
xs: **BioE3 Policy 2024** backs **bio-jet fuel** — option **(4)**.
The policy name to remember: **BioE3** (**2024**) is the biotechnology-led policy that backs aviation biofuel.
xa: SAF feedstock: **agri residues, corn grain, wastewater sludge, wood-mill waste** (UPSC **2024**).
First biojet-fuelled flight: **SpiceJet**, **Dehradun-Delhi**, **27 Aug 2018**.

n6df1b12147b.s: India's first geothermal power project, led by ONGC, is at:
n6df1b12147b.x: India's first geothermal project is at Puga Valley, Ladakh, led by ONGC.
xa: **National Policy on Geothermal Energy** was notified on **15 Sep 2025**.
Geothermal potential: **~10,600 MW** from **381** hot springs (GSI).
India's first wave plant: **Vizhinjam, Kerala** (**1991**).

n0581f60826a.s: Which of the following is NOT a listed geothermal province or region of India?
n0581f60826a.x: The listed geothermal regions include the Himalaya, Godavari Valley, Cambay, SONATA, Mahanadi, West Coast and Andaman-Nicobar. The Indo-Gangetic Plain is not included in that list.
n0581f60826a.tq: Find the option outside the stated geographical classification.
xs: The **Indo-Gangetic Plain** is NOT a listed geothermal province — option **(4)**.
Listed: Himalaya, **Godavari valley**, **Cambay**, **Son-Narmada-Tapi (SONATA)**, Mahanadi, West Coast, Andaman-Nicobar.
xa: Some notes count **7** provinces; others say **10**.
**Cambay graben** is in Gujarat; Godavari valley site is **Manuguru** (Telangana).
**Puga Valley** (Ladakh) has the highest potential.

nb14dc497aca.s: Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) are designed to:
o: Prevent all water movement in geothermal fields
Convert solar radiation directly into electricity
Replace radioactive decay with chemical combustion
nb14dc497aca.x: EGS technology artificially stimulates geothermal reservoirs to improve access to underground heat.
nb14dc497aca.tq: Match the technology with its functional purpose.
xs: **Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS)** **artificially stimulate** geothermal reservoirs — option **(2)**.
EGS works on the reservoirs that hold **Earth's internal heat** — it does not stop water movement or use solar radiation.
xa: Geothermal heat comes from **Earth's interior** (radioactive decay).
Geothermal gives **24x7 baseload** power.
**National Policy on Geothermal Energy (2025)** focuses on research, technology and ecosystem development.

nb50f6f2aa71.s: India's National Policy on Geothermal Energy (2025) provides for how many pilot projects?
nb50f6f2aa71.x: The policy, notified by MNRE on 15 September 2025, has five pilot projects, not ten.
xa: Focus: **research, technology, ecosystem and capacity development**.
First geothermal project: **Puga, Ladakh** (**ONGC**).
World's first geothermal power: **Larderello (1904)**.

nc63beac3a99.s: Mini hydro plants are those with a capacity of:
o: Above 2 MW and up to 25 MW
nc63beac3a99.x: Micro hydro is up to 100 kW, mini hydro 101 kW to 2 MW and small hydro above 2 MW up to 25 MW.
xa: Small hydro sites: **hill streams**, **canal falls**, **dam toes** (run-of-river).
**Arunachal, Himachal, J&K, Uttarakhand** hold ~half of small hydro potential.
AP small hydro: **10.5 MW** (2024-25).

n089e573cf3b.s: The Geological Survey of India has estimated India's geothermal potential at approximately:
n089e573cf3b.x: India's estimated geothermal potential is about 10,600 MW from 381 hot springs, according to the stated GSI estimate.
n089e573cf3b.tq: Match the capacity figure with the corresponding number of sites.
xs: GSI puts India's geothermal potential at ~**10,600 MW** from **381 hot springs** — option **(1)**.
The estimate is by the **Geological Survey of India (GSI)**.
xa: First geothermal project: **Puga Valley, Ladakh** (**ONGC**).
**National Policy on Geothermal Energy** notified **15 Sep 2025**.
Challenges: uneven reservoirs, **high drilling cost**, **subsidence**, water pollution.

ndc207dd2f72.s: Hot springs, geysers and volcanoes are surface expressions of:
ndc207dd2f72.x: They are surface expressions of heat originating within the Earth, i.e. geothermal energy.
xa: Others: steam and **hot dry rock**.
Heat source: **Earth's interior**, largely **radioactive decay**.
**Tattapani** springs are **45-90 °C**.

n49640d3883e.s: Which of the following sites has the greatest tidal-energy potential among the listed Indian sites?
n49640d3883e.x: The Gulf of Khambhat in Gujarat is identified as India's best tidal-energy site, with an estimated potential of about 7,000 MW.
n49640d3883e.tq: Distinguish the best tidal site from an offshore-wind site and other ocean-energy locations.
xs: The **Gulf of Khambhat (Cambay)**, Gujarat, is the best tidal site — tidal range **5-10 m**, ~**7,000 MW** potential — option **(2)** (PYQ **2025**).
**Gulf of Kutch** has a smaller range (**5-8 m**); **Lakshadweep** is an **OTEC** site.
⚠ **Gulf of Mannar** is an offshore **wind** zone, not the tidal answer.
xa: Tidal criterion: large tidal range (roughly **5 m** or more) in a **narrow gulf/estuary**.
**Sundarbans** (Gangetic delta, West Bengal) has a range of ~**5 m**.
Proposed pilots — **Durgaduani creek** and a **Gulf of Kutch** plant — neither commissioned.

na32b7d7b643.s: Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) needs a temperature difference between surface and deep water of about:
na32b7d7b643.x: OTEC needs about a 20°C difference and is viable mainly between 30°N and 30°S.
xa: Principle: temperature difference between **warm surface** and **cold deep water** runs a turbine.
OTEC sites: **Lakshadweep**, **Andaman and Nicobar**.
⚠ **Tidal** energy instead needs a large **tidal range** (~**5 m**+).

n9d8b1a63eb1.s: Which of the following is identified as an OTEC location in India?
n9d8b1a63eb1.x: Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are OTEC locations; the Gulfs of Khambhat and Kutch are tidal-energy sites.
xa: OTEC needs ~**20 deg C** difference; viable in **30N-30S**.
OTEC can also supply **desalination** for islands.
Gulf of Khambhat tidal potential: ~**7,000 MW**.

nc8c460d4f32.s: Since 2019, which source has been included in MNRE's renewable-energy classification?
nc8c460d4f32.x: Large hydro has been classified as renewable since 2019; nuclear is non-fossil but not renewable.
xa: Core MNRE RE: **solar**, **wind**, **bio-power**, **small hydro**.
**Small hydro cut-off: 25 MW** — micro up to **100 kW**, mini **101 kW-2 MW**, small **2-25 MW**.
⚠ Geothermal, tidal and **OTEC** are listed as sources **under development**.

na196bcc8a88.s: Biomass energy is best understood as:
o: Solar energy stored by plants through photosynthesis
Energy obtained from tidal currents alone
Heat stored only in the Earth's mantle
na196bcc8a88.x: Biomass energy represents solar energy captured and stored by plants through photosynthesis. It may be burned directly or converted into biogas and biofuels.
na196bcc8a88.tq: Trace the energy source through the biological conversion chain.
xs: **Biomass energy** is **solar energy stored by plants** through **photosynthesis** — option **(1)**.
It is burned directly or converted to **biogas/biofuels**.
Earth's internal heat is **geothermal**; tidal currents are **ocean energy** — not biomass.
xa: **Gobar gas** is biomass energy (**APPSC 2019**).
Agricultural waste: **crop residue** (stubble, paddy-husk), **manure**, **cattle dung**, **dairy waste** — all biodegradable.
**Biomass gasification**: biomass heated with **controlled oxygen** → **syngas** (CO + H2 + CO2).

n7f8a00eff78.s: Which of the following is an example of biomass energy?
n7f8a00eff78.x: Gobar gas is biomass energy because it is produced from organic material, especially cattle dung.
xa: **Nuclear** is non-fossil but **not renewable**.
Biogas is produced by **anaerobic digestion**; methane ~**50-75%**.
The **"Gramalakshmi"** floating-drum gobar gas plant was by **Jashbhai Patel** (**1950s**).

na38d9b1d808.s: The biodiesel project launched by the Belgian firm VITO in April 2023 was located at:
na38d9b1d808.x: VITO launched a two-year biodiesel project at Ayodhya in April 2023.
na38d9b1d808.tq: Match the foreign partner with the correct project location and date.
xs: Belgian firm **VITO** launched a **2-year biodiesel project** at **Ayodhya** in **April 2023** — option **(2)** (PYQ **2023**).
**Golaghat** hosts the Numaligarh bamboo plant; **Panipat** the IOCL 2G plant; **Vizhinjam** the first wave plant.
xa: Biodiesel blend is still **below 0.5%**; target **5% by 2030**.
Biodiesel is made by **transesterification**.

n0a3fb961332.s: The primary source of geothermal energy is:
o: Heat from the Earth's interior, largely associated with radioactive decay
Chemical energy released by surface oxidation
n0a3fb961332.x: Geothermal energy originates from the internal heat of the Earth, much of which is generated by radioactive decay in its interior.
n0a3fb961332.tq: Identify the source-process relationship rather than a surface manifestation.
xs: Geothermal energy comes from **heat of the Earth's interior**, largely from **radioactive decay** — option **(2)**.
Solar energy stored by plants is **biomass**, not geothermal.
xa: Surface expressions: **hot springs**, steam, **geysers**, hot dry rock, **volcanoes** (APPSC **2018**).
Geothermal gives **24x7 baseload** power.
**Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS)** artificially stimulate reservoirs.

n8a65b60ee10.s: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge associated with geothermal energy?
o: Subsidence and water pollution from geothermal fluids
n8a65b60ee10.x: The stated challenges are uneven reservoir distribution, high drilling costs, subsidence and water pollution from geothermal fluids. Geothermal energy necessarily depends on underground heat.
n8a65b60ee10.tq: Reject the absolute statement that contradicts the basic principle of the resource.
xs: **Complete absence of underground heat** is NOT a challenge — option **(2)**; Earth's **internal heat** is the very source.
Real challenges: **uneven distribution of reservoirs**, **high drilling cost**, **subsidence**, **water pollution** from geothermal fluids.
xa: Potential: ~**10,600 MW** from **381** hot springs.
**EGS** artificially stimulate reservoirs.
Geothermal advantage: **24x7 baseload**.

ndf5954de62e.s: Hydrogen that occurs naturally through geological processes is called:
ndf5954de62e.x: White hydrogen is naturally occurring geological hydrogen.
xa: **Green** = electrolysis of water using **renewable power** — the only **zero-carbon** type.
⚠ **Pink** = nuclear electrolysis; **Turquoise** = methane pyrolysis.
Cost: grey **$1.5-2/kg** vs green ~**$4/kg** (**Jul 2026**).

n16b960f5146.s: Pink hydrogen is produced by electrolysis using:
n16b960f5146.x: Pink hydrogen comes from electrolysis powered by nuclear energy.
xa: **Blue** = fossil route + **CCS**.
**Brown / Black** = **coal gasification**.
**Green** = electrolysis using renewable power (PYQ **2023**); also biomass gasification.

naa827a13b2c.s: Green hydrogen is produced mainly by:
o: Steam methane reforming of natural gas
Electrolysis of water using renewable power
Electrolysis of water using nuclear power
naa827a13b2c.x: Green hydrogen comes from electrolysis of water using renewable power (PYQ 2023) and is the only zero-carbon colour. Steam methane reforming gives grey, methane pyrolysis gives turquoise, and nuclear-powered electrolysis gives pink hydrogen.
naa827a13b2c.tq: Green = RE electrolysis; pink = nuclear; turquoise = pyrolysis.
xs: **Green hydrogen** is made by **electrolysis of water using renewable power** — option **(2)** (PYQ **2023**).
Reforming of natural gas = **grey**; methane pyrolysis = **turquoise**; nuclear electrolysis = **pink**.
xa: Green hydrogen can also come from **biomass gasification**.
**Green Hydrogen Standard** (MNRE, **Aug 2023**): well-to-gate emissions **not more than 2 kg CO2-eq per kg H2**.
An **electrolyser** splits water into hydrogen + oxygen using electricity.

ndeee8b8c192.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated method for storing or carrying hydrogen for vehicle use?
o: Storage only as carbon dioxide in insulated tanks
ndeee8b8c192.x: Hydrogen may be stored as compressed gas, cryogenic liquid hydrogen, or solid metal hydrides, and may also be carried as ammonia or methanol. Carbon dioxide is not a stated hydrogen-storage method.
ndeee8b8c192.tq: Identify the option that is not a hydrogen-storage form or carrier.
xs: **Storage as carbon dioxide** is NOT a hydrogen storage method — option **(1)**.
Real methods: **compressed gas** (Type-IV tanks), **liquid hydrogen at -253 °C**, **metal hydrides**, chemical carriers.
xa: Liquid hydrogen has very low density, **0.071 g/ml** → bulky tanks.
**Metal hydrides** absorb hydrogen in alloys and release it on heating.
Chemical carriers: **ammonia**, **methanol**, **LOHC**.

n5d0e2dc1664.s: Green ammonia is produced by combining:
n5d0e2dc1664.x: Green ammonia is produced from nitrogen and green hydrogen. It is important for fertiliser production and can also serve as a fuel and marine fuel.
n5d0e2dc1664.tq: Distinguish the feedstocks of ammonia from those of other hydrogen derivatives.
xs: **Green ammonia** = **nitrogen (N2)** + **green hydrogen** — option **(4)**.
Green ammonia leads green-hydrogen adoption (**fertiliser**, fuel, **marine fuel**).
xa: **7,24,000 TPA** green ammonia at weighted average **₹53.27/kg** (SECI) — among the world's lowest.
**AM Green** is building a green-ammonia plant at **Kakinada** (AP).
Green ammonia/methanol standards: **Mar 2026**.

nchemistry-10-2.x: Blue hydrogen captures CO₂ for low emissions; grey releases it, green has zero and brown/black very high emissions.
n: Grey hydrogen has high carbon dioxide emissions, which are released. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Blue hydrogen has low carbon dioxide emissions because the emissions are captured. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Green hydrogen has zero carbon dioxide emissions. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Brown or black hydrogen has very high carbon dioxide emissions. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Blue hydrogen is transitional and is not fully zero-carbon. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Green hydrogen is described as the cleanest hydrogen type. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Brown or black hydrogen is the dirtiest hydrogen type. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
xa: Grey hydrogen is about **95%** of current global production — the **cheapest**.
**Pink** = nuclear electrolysis; **turquoise** = **methane pyrolysis**.
Green Hydrogen Standard: not more than **2 kg CO2-eq per kg H2**.

nchemistry-10-6.s: Hydrogen produced from natural gas with carbon capture and storage is called:
nchemistry-10-6.x: That is blue hydrogen; green hydrogen comes from electrolysis using renewable power.
n: Green hydrogen is used to produce green steel by replacing coking coal. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Green hydrogen can be exported as green ammonia or green methanol energy carriers. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Green hydrogen is used in aviation through synthetic fuels. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Hydrogen is used in steel production through the direct reduced iron (DRI) process. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Green hydrogen is used in hard-to-abate industries. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Green hydrogen is used to produce fertiliser through green ammonia. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Green hydrogen is used to produce green methanol. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Hydrogen decarbonises steel. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Hydrogen decarbonises aviation. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Green hydrogen is used to produce other chemical derivatives. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
xa: Green ammonia = **nitrogen** + green hydrogen.
India signed green ammonia/methanol **export deals** with **Japanese** firms (Jul 2026).
Green ammonia discovered at **₹53.27/kg** (SECI).

nchemistry-10-7.s: Methane pyrolysis (natural gas heated without oxygen) produces which type of hydrogen?
nchemistry-10-7.x: Methane pyrolysis gives turquoise hydrogen; steam methane reforming gives grey or blue and renewable electrolysis green.
n: Steam methane reforming uses natural gas and steam as its source or process. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Steam methane reforming produces grey hydrogen or blue hydrogen when CCS is used. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Coal or biomass gasification uses coal or biomass as its source. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Coal or biomass gasification produces grey hydrogen or brown hydrogen. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Water electrolysis uses water and electricity as its source or process. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Water electrolysis using renewable electricity produces green hydrogen. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Methane pyrolysis uses natural gas at high temperature without oxygen. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Methane pyrolysis produces turquoise hydrogen. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Grey hydrogen is produced by steam methane reforming (SMR) of natural gas or by coal gasification. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Blue hydrogen is produced by steam methane reforming with carbon capture and storage (CCS). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Green hydrogen is produced by electrolysis of water using renewable electricity. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Green hydrogen can use solar, wind, or hydroelectricity as its renewable electricity source. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Turquoise hydrogen is produced by methane pyrolysis. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Brown or black hydrogen is produced by coal gasification without carbon capture and storage. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
xa: Methane pyrolysis produces **solid carbon** as a by-product.
**Nuclear-powered electrolysis** gives **pink** hydrogen.
**Biological / photobiological** routes (microbes, algae) are emerging green routes.

nchemistry-10-19.s: Hydrogen is especially useful in sectors such as steel, shipping and fertilisers because in them:
nchemistry-10-19.x: Hydrogen suits hard-to-abate sectors like steel, shipping and fertilisers, where direct electrification is difficult.
n: Hydrogen is useful for hard-to-abate sectors where direct electrification is difficult. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
xa: Green hydrogen **produces only water** and **reduces dependence** on imported fossil fuels.
It is **critical** for India's **2070** net-zero target.
**National Green Hydrogen Mission** (**4 January 2023**) targets **5 MMT/year** by 2030.

n3bbc69af4c0.s: The total outlay approved for the National Green Hydrogen Mission up to 2029-30 is:
n3bbc69af4c0.x: The Mission has a total outlay of ₹19,744 crore up to financial year 2029-30.
n3bbc69af4c0.tq: Use the exact headline figure rather than a component amount.
xs: The **National Green Hydrogen Mission** outlay is **₹19,744 crore** up to FY **2029-30** — option **(2)**.
**₹17,490 crore** is only the **SIGHT** component.
xa: Pilot projects **₹1,466 cr**; **SHIP** (R&D) **₹400 cr**; other components **₹388 cr**.
Approved by the Union Cabinet on **4 January 2023**; nodal ministry **MNRE**.
Target: **5 MMT/year** green hydrogen by **2030**.

n53fcbc9df99.s: SHIP under the National Green Hydrogen Mission stands for:
n53fcbc9df99.x: SHIP is the Strategic Hydrogen Innovation Partnership, a PPP for R&D.
xa: ⚠ **SIGHT** = incentives (**₹17,490 cr**); **SHIP** = R&D partnership (**₹400 cr**).
**Hydrogen Valley Innovation Clusters**: **four** sanctioned, **₹170 crore**.
**National Centre for Hydrogen Safety** is also a mission component.

n37979f74d70.s: The nodal ministry of the National Green Hydrogen Mission is:
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
n37979f74d70.x: MNRE is the nodal ministry; BEE under the Ministry of Power handles only certification.
xa: ⚠ The **Bureau of Energy Efficiency** (under the **Ministry of Power**) is the nodal authority for **certification**.
**GHCI** launched **April 2025**.

n2853618ea40.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated 2030 target of the National Green Hydrogen Mission?
o: Production of 5 million metric tonnes of green hydrogen annually
Addition of 125 GW of renewable energy capacity
n2853618ea40.x: The Mission targets 60-100 GW of electrolyser capacity, not 200 GW. The other three figures are stated 2030 targets.
n2853618ea40.tq: Find the altered numerical target among closely related figures.
xs: **200 GW of electrolysers** is NOT a target — option **(1)**; the target is **60-100 GW** electrolysers.
Stated 2030 targets: **5 MMT/year** green H2, **125 GW** added RE, **6 lakh jobs**.
xa: Also: **50 MMT/yr** GHG cut, **₹1 lakh crore+** lower fossil imports, **₹8 lakh crore+** investment.
Production could reach **10 MMT** with exports.
Progress (**Aug 2026**): **15 companies** awarded **3,000 MW** electrolyser manufacturing capacity.

n7eeb43e2499.s: Which institution is the nodal authority for certification under the National Green Hydrogen Mission?
n7eeb43e2499.x: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency, under the Ministry of Power, is the nodal authority for certification.
n7eeb43e2499.tq: Distinguish the nodal ministry from the certification authority.
xs: The **Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE)**, under the **Ministry of Power**, is the nodal authority for certification — option **(1)**.
This is under the **Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme of India (GHCI)**, launched **April 2025**.
xa: **Green Hydrogen Standard** (MNRE, **Aug 2023**): not more than **2 kg CO2-eq per kg H2**.
Standards for **green ammonia and green methanol**: **Mar 2026**.
⚠ Mission nodal ministry = **MNRE**; certification = **BEE**.

n6a335d7acad.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about applications of green hydrogen in India?
o: Hydrogen blending in city-gas networks is being evaluated as H-CNG
Fuel-cell trucks, buses and ships are potential applications
It is not being considered for steel
Long-duration energy storage is a potential application
n6a335d7acad.x: Green hydrogen is being considered for fertilisers, refineries and steel.
xa: **Green ammonia** leads adoption.
**H-CNG** buses: **Delhi**, **IOCL** (**2020**).
Steel: H2 replaces **coking coal** in **DRI**.

ncc491122791.s: V.O. Chidambaranar Port, which has a ₹35 crore green hydrogen bunkering pilot, is in:
ncc491122791.x: V.O. Chidambaranar Port is in Tamil Nadu, not Odisha.
xa: **Deendayal (Kandla)** in Gujarat is the third hub port.
Mission **shipping** pilot outlay: **₹115 cr** to **2025-26**.
First hydrogen fuel-cell ferry: **Cochin Shipyard Ltd**.

nbcf9c26b62b.s: The National Green Hydrogen Mission targets green hydrogen production of ____ per year by 2030.
nbcf9c26b62b.x: The Mission targets 5 MMT a year by 2030, possibly reaching 10 MMT including exports.
xa: Commissioned so far: ~**8,000 TPA** at **₹387-397/kg**.
Awarded: **8,62,000 TPA** production to **18** companies.
**AP** targets **1.5 MMTPA** green hydrogen by **2030**.

nbea63a00d55.s: The National Green Hydrogen Mission is expected to create about ____ jobs by 2030.
nbea63a00d55.x: The Mission expects about 6 lakh jobs, over ₹8 lakh crore investment and about 50 MMT annual GHG reduction.
xa: Also **125 GW** added RE and **60-100 GW** electrolysers.
Production target: **5 MMT/year** (up to **10 MMT** with exports).
Outlay: **₹19,744 crore**.

nc1658e0c5e3.s: Under the Green Hydrogen Standard notified by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy in August 2023, hydrogen is classified as green when well-to-gate emissions do not exceed:
o: 3 kg CO2-eq per kg H2, calculated quarterly
5 kg CO2-eq per kg H2, calculated as a 12-month average
1 kg CO2-eq per kg H2, calculated annually
2 kg CO2-eq per kg H2, calculated as a 12-month average
nc1658e0c5e3.x: The Green Hydrogen Standard permits well-to-gate emissions of not more than 2 kg CO2-equivalent per kg of hydrogen, measured as a 12-month average.
nc1658e0c5e3.tq: Discriminate between closely related numerical thresholds and averaging periods.
xs: Hydrogen is "green" if well-to-gate emissions are **not more than 2 kg CO2-eq per kg H2**, as a **12-month average** — option **(4)**.
The standard was notified by **MNRE** in **Aug 2023**.
xa: **GHCI** launched **April 2025**; certification by **BEE**.
Green ammonia and green methanol standards: **Mar 2026**.
Only **green** hydrogen is zero-carbon.

nc7e29de81f6.s: The Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme of India (GHCI) was launched in:
nc7e29de81f6.x: The Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme of India was launched in April 2025.
nc7e29de81f6.tq: Use the date as the distinguishing clue among related policy milestones.
xs: **GHCI** was launched in **April 2025** — option **(1)**.
**Aug 2023** is the **Green Hydrogen Standard**; **Mar 2026** is the green ammonia/methanol standards.
xa: Nodal certifying authority: **Bureau of Energy Efficiency**.
Threshold: **2 kg CO2-eq per kg H2** (12-month average).
Mission approved **4 January 2023**.

n2dd0dc87a43.s: India's national net-zero target year is:
n2dd0dc87a43.x: India's net-zero target is 2070; 2047 is linked with energy independence.
xa: Hard-to-abate: **fertilisers, refineries, steel**, chemicals, heavy transport.
Mission target: **5 MMT/year** by **2030**.

n2785be3a00d.s: India’s long-term green ammonia and green methanol export agreements were signed with companies from:
n2785be3a00d.x: India signed long-term green ammonia and green methanol export agreements with Japanese companies.
n2785be3a00d.tq: Use the partner-country distinction to avoid confusing international collaborations.
xs: Long-term **green ammonia and green methanol** export deals were signed with firms from **Japan** (**Jul 2026**) — option **(3)**.
**Poland** links to the **Hynfra** JV in AP, not to export deals.
xa: Export carriers: **ammonia**, **methanol**, **LOHC**.
Production could reach **10 MMT** with exports.
Green ammonia: **7,24,000 TPA** at **₹53.27/kg** (SECI).

nb4f9725695b.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or challenge associated with green hydrogen?
o: Costly cryogenic transport and water stress
Mature domestic electrolyser industry with no import dependence
High production cost compared with grey hydrogen
nb4f9725695b.x: Import dependence on electrolysers is identified as a challenge; a mature domestic industry with no import dependence is not. High cost, cryogenic transport and water stress are also recognised concerns.
nb4f9725695b.tq: Identify the option that reverses a stated criticism rather than merely changing its wording.
xs: A **mature domestic electrolyser industry with no import dependence** is NOT a criticism — option **(3)**; the industry is **nascent** and **import-dependent**.
Real criticisms: **high cost** (~**$4/kg** vs grey **$1.5-2/kg**), **costly cryogenic transport**, **water stress**.
xa: **Chinese dominance** of electrolyser supply is a concern.
US credits up to **$3/kg** compete for exports.
~**9 litres** of purified water per kg of hydrogen.

n9ab25d1bd2e.s: An electrolyser is a device that:
o: Combines nitrogen and hydrogen to produce electricity
Splits water into hydrogen and oxygen using electricity
Converts hydrogen directly into crude oil
n9ab25d1bd2e.x: An electrolyser uses electricity to split water into hydrogen and oxygen.
n9ab25d1bd2e.tq: Use the basic input-process-output relationship to identify the device.
xs: An **electrolyser** **splits water into hydrogen and oxygen using electricity** — option **(2)**.
With **renewable power** this gives **green hydrogen**; with nuclear power, **pink**.
xa: Types: **Alkaline**, **PEM**, **Solid oxide**, **AEM**.
Water need: ~**9 litres** of purified water per kg of hydrogen.
**15 companies** awarded **3,000 MW** electrolyser manufacturing capacity (**Aug 2026**).

n86757ebbc6c.s: In a PEM fuel cell, hydrogen is split into protons and electrons at the:
n86757ebbc6c.x: Hydrogen splits at the anode; protons cross the membrane to the cathode and electrons flow through the external circuit.
xa: Cathode: **1/2 O2 + 2H+ + 2e- → H2O** + heat.
Exhaust: **only water vapour and warm air** — zero tailpipe emissions.
Cochin ferry uses an indigenous **LT-PEM** fuel cell.

nchemistry-10-5.s: A fuel cell produces electricity and ____ from hydrogen and oxygen.
nchemistry-10-5.x: A fuel cell converts hydrogen and oxygen electrochemically into electricity and water, with zero emissions at the point of use.
n: A fuel cell is an electrochemical device. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
A fuel cell converts H₂ and O₂ into electricity and H₂O. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Fuel cells have zero emissions at the point of use. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Hydrogen fuel cells generate electricity. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
xa: At the anode, **H2 → 2H+ + 2e-**; at the cathode oxygen forms **H2O**.
Hydrogen is **not burnt**; exhaust is **only water vapour and warm air**.
First indigenous **hydrogen fuel-cell ferry**: **Cochin Shipyard** (LT-PEM).

n6f372e95aed.s: The first indigenous hydrogen fuel-cell ferry in India was built by which organisation?
n6f372e95aed.x: The first indigenous hydrogen fuel-cell ferry was built by Cochin Shipyard Limited. It was a fully indigenous LT-PEM fuel-cell ferry.
n6f372e95aed.tq: Match the transport type with its specific builder rather than with a testing site.
xs: **Cochin Shipyard Ltd** built India's first indigenous hydrogen fuel-cell **ferry** — option **(3)** (APPSC-G1 **2024**).
It uses a fully indigenous **LT-PEM** fuel cell and was flagged off by the PM.
**KPIT with CSIR-NCL** made the **bus**; **ICF Chennai** the tested **train coach**; **IOCL** the H-CNG buses.
xa: VOC port (**Tuticorin**) pilot: bunkering and refuelling, **₹35 crore**.
Mission **shipping** pilot: **₹115 cr**.

n711fb567431.s: The hydrogen-powered coach tested by the Railways was associated with which location and organisation?
n711fb567431.x: The first hydrogen-powered train coach tested by the Railways was associated with Chennai’s Integral Coach Factory (ICF). This is distinct from the hydrogen train in service associated with Jind-Sonipat.
n711fb567431.tq: Separate the coach-testing site from the locations of the ferry, bus and train.
xs: The first hydrogen-powered **train coach tested** by Railways was at **Chennai (ICF – Integral Coach Factory)** — option **(2)** (APPSC **2025**).
**Jind-Sonipat** is where the train runs **in service**, not where the coach was tested.
xa: ⚠ Train coach **tested** = **Chennai**; train **in service** = **Jind-Sonipat**.
The Jind-Sonipat train has **10 coaches**, **89 km** route, from **July 2026**.
Hydrogen is stored in roof-mounted **Type-IV** cylinders.

n5d719d394ae.s: India's first indigenous hydrogen fuel-cell bus (2022) was developed by:
n5d719d394ae.x: The first indigenous hydrogen fuel-cell bus was developed by KPIT with CSIR-NCL, Pune, in 2022.
xa: Hydrogen shuttle bus: **Central Vista, Delhi**.
Mission **mobility** pilot outlay: **₹496 cr**.
Fuel-cell exhaust: only **water vapour and warm air**.

nb7a13b141bd.s: The first hydrogen fuel-cell train in service is associated with which of the following descriptions?
o: A shuttle bus operating at Central Vista, Delhi, from 2022
A ferry launched from Cochin Shipyard Limited in 2024
A 10-coach train operating on the Jind-Sonipat route in Haryana from July 2026
A single coach tested at Chennai’s ICF in 2025
nb7a13b141bd.x: The first hydrogen fuel-cell train in service is described as a 10-coach train on the 89-km Jind-Sonipat route in Haryana from July 2026. It is identified as the world’s longest and most powerful broad-gauge hydrogen train.
nb7a13b141bd.tq: Distinguish the train in service from the earlier coach-testing milestone.
xs: The first indigenous hydrogen fuel-cell **train in service** is a **10-coach** train on **Jind-Sonipat** (**89 km**), **Haryana**, from **July 2026** — option **(3)**.
It is the world's **longest and most powerful broad-gauge** hydrogen train.
xa: ⚠ Single coach **tested** at **Chennai (ICF)**.
Hydrogen stored in roof-mounted **Type-IV** composite cylinders.
**Central Vista** = shuttle bus; **Cochin Shipyard** = ferry.

nfe1f1960053.s: The world's first hydrogen fuel-cell car to reach Sydney (27 December 2003) was built and driven by students of:
nfe1f1960053.x: It was built and driven by students of Tamagawa University, Tokyo (PYQ 2004). The other institutions are not linked to this run.
xs: Students of **Tamagawa University (Tokyo)** built and drove the first hydrogen fuel-cell car to reach **Sydney** (**27 Dec 2003**) — option **(1)** (PYQ **2004**).
It is a world FIRST, not an Indian or Australian university project.
xa: India's first indigenous fuel-cell bus: **KPIT with CSIR-NCL, Pune (2022)**.
Fuel cells emit **only water vapour and warm air**.
PEM anode: **H2 → 2H+ + 2e-**.

n05640466007.s: About how much purified water is required to produce one kilogram of hydrogen through electrolysis?
n05640466007.x: Approximately 9 litres of purified water are required per kilogram of hydrogen, which can constrain projects in arid solar regions.
n05640466007.tq: Retain the order of magnitude and connect it with the stated regional constraint.
xs: About **9 litres** of purified water is needed per kg of hydrogen — option **(3)**.
This is a **constraint in arid solar states**.
xa: Other constraints: **Chinese dominance** of electrolysers, high cost (~**$4/kg**), costly **cryogenic** transport.
**NTPC Simhadri** began trials with a **seawater-to-hydrogen** plant (**Jan 2026**).
US credits up to **$3/kg** compete for exports.

n46a9e31c3ab.s: Liquid hydrogen is stored at a temperature of about:
n46a9e31c3ab.x: Liquid hydrogen is kept at about −253°C; its very low density (about 0.071 g/ml) needs large tanks.
xa: Criticism: **costly cryogenic transport**.
Alternatives: **compressed gas** (Type-IV), **metal hydrides**, chemical carriers.

n6ac2994c18b.s: Which group consists only of chemical carriers used to transport hydrogen for export?
n6ac2994c18b.x: Ammonia, methanol and liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHC) are chemical carriers for transporting hydrogen.
xa: Long-term **green ammonia and green methanol** export deals with **Japanese firms** (**Jul 2026**).
**Green ammonia** = **nitrogen + green hydrogen**.
Hydrogen hub ports: **Deendayal (Kandla)**, **V.O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin)**, **Paradip**.

n511d1b65af6.s: The Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration of Andhra Pradesh (19 July 2025) was made at:
n511d1b65af6.x: The declaration was made at Amaravati to make AP India's green hydrogen capital.
xa: Aim to cut cost from **₹460/kg** to **₹160-170/kg**.
**SRM University-AP** = nodal agency; CoE with **JK Srivastava Hynfra** (**Feb 2026**).
Projects: **NTPC Green** hub at **Pudimadaka (Anakapalli)**; **AM Green** at **Kakinada**.

n472b9de8aad.s: Which institution is the state nodal agency for the Andhra Pradesh Green Hydrogen Valley?
n472b9de8aad.x: SRM University-AP is the state nodal agency for the Andhra Pradesh Green Hydrogen Valley.
n472b9de8aad.tq: Identify the designated institutional agency rather than a nearby higher-education institution.
xs: **SRM University-AP** is the nodal agency for the **AP Green Hydrogen Valley** — option **(4)**.
It runs a **CoE** with **JK Srivastava Hynfra** (Indo-Polish JV), **Feb 2026**.
xa: **Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration**, **Amaravati**, **19 Jul 2025** — to make AP India's green hydrogen capital.
AP **2030** goal: **1.5 MMTPA** green hydrogen + **5 GW** electrolyser manufacturing.
Aim: cut cost from **₹460/kg** to **₹160-170/kg** (APSES **2025-26**).

nchemistry-10-18.s: In the steel sector, hydrogen helps decarbonise production through:
o: Direct reduced iron replacing coking coal
nchemistry-10-18.x: Steel uses hydrogen-based direct reduced iron in place of coking coal.
n: Hydrogen decarbonises cement. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Hydrogen decarbonises fertilisers. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Hydrogen decarbonises heavy transport. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Hydrogen decarbonises shipping. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
xa: **4** steel pilots worth ~**₹106 cr**.
**20,000 MTPA** green H2 awarded for **IOCL, BPCL, HPCL** refineries.
Hydrogen hub ports: **Deendayal (Kandla)**, **V.O. Chidambaranar**, **Paradip**.

n620e2ccde27.s: The approximate cost comparison between green and grey hydrogen is:
o: Green hydrogen: about $4 per kg; grey hydrogen: $1.5–2 per kg
Green hydrogen: $0.5 per kg; grey hydrogen: $1.5–2 per kg
Green hydrogen: $1.5–2 per kg; grey hydrogen: about $4 per kg
Both green and grey hydrogen: $4 per kg
n620e2ccde27.x: Green hydrogen is estimated at about $4 per kg, whereas grey hydrogen costs approximately $1.5–2 per kg.
n620e2ccde27.tq: Read the comparison direction carefully and do not reverse the two technologies.
xs: Green hydrogen costs ~**$4 per kg**; grey **$1.5-2 per kg** — option **(1)** (**Jul 2026**).
Grey remains far cheaper, which is the main **high cost** criticism.
xa: **Grey** = steam methane reforming, CO2 released.
Commissioned Indian green H2: **₹387-397/kg**.
AP aims to cut cost from **₹460/kg** to **₹160-170/kg**.

nchemistry-10-8.s: Which of the following is an industrial, not a fuel or transport, use of hydrogen?
nchemistry-10-8.x: Ammonia for fertiliser is an industrial use; fuel-cell vehicles, rocket fuel and CNG blending are fuel uses.
n: Hydrogen is used as fuel for fuel-cell vehicles. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Hydrogen is used as rocket fuel. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Hydrogen can be blended in compressed natural gas (CNG). [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Hydrogen is used to produce ammonia for fertilisers. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles include buses, trucks, trains, and ships. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
Green hydrogen is used to produce fertiliser through green ammonia. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 36-39]
xa: Industry uses: **petroleum refining** (desulphurisation), **methanol**, **steel** via **DRI**.
Power uses: **backup power**, **grid balancing**.
Jind-Sonipat (**89 km**) runs India's first indigenous hydrogen fuel-cell train.

nf19e8a6478b.s: During the discharge of an electrochemical cell, oxidation occurs at the:
nf19e8a6478b.x: Oxidation (loss of electrons) occurs at the anode and reduction (gain of electrons) at the cathode.
xa: The **electrolyte** lets ions flow and keeps the electrodes apart.
⚠ Anode = **oxidation**; cathode = **reduction** (during discharge).
Li-ion: **graphite anode**, **lithium metal-oxide cathode**.

n09fd131ac05.s: In a battery, the electrolyte permits the movement of ____ between the electrodes.
n09fd131ac05.x: An electrolyte lets ions flow and keeps the electrodes apart; it does not provide a direct electronic path.
xa: **Solid-state** batteries use a **solid electrolyte** — better safety, higher energy density.
**Lead-acid** uses a **sulphuric acid** electrolyte.
**Flow** batteries keep liquid electrolytes in tanks.

n7e15cdc8afb.s: Which one of the following correctly expresses the concern regarding global critical-mineral supply chains?
o: More than 70% of lithium processing and most cobalt refining are concentrated in a few countries.
Only graphite processing is concentrated, while lithium and cobalt are geographically dispersed.
Lithium processing and cobalt refining are evenly distributed across all countries.
No significant concentration exists in the processing or refining of battery minerals.
n7e15cdc8afb.x: More than 70% of lithium processing and most cobalt refining are concentrated in a few countries, creating a supply-chain risk for battery manufacturing.
n7e15cdc8afb.tq: Reject absolute reversals of the stated concentration and identify the precise supply-chain risk.
xs: **Over 70%** of **lithium processing** and most **cobalt refining** are concentrated in a few countries — option **(1)**.
Upstream minerals are concentrated in **China and Africa**.
xa: Lithium, cobalt, nickel and **REEs** are largely imported by India.
**NCMM**: **₹16,300 crore**; **₹1,500 crore** recycling scheme.
**Sodium-ion** is pitched as a **mineral-light** alternative.

n3e3277f1d84.s: The use of nickel-cadmium batteries has declined partly because of the toxicity of:
n3e3277f1d84.x: Ni-Cd batteries are rechargeable but have become less common because cadmium is toxic.
xa: Uses: **calculators, cordless appliances, transistors**, torches, shavers (UKPSC **2016**).
**NiMH** replaces cadmium with a **metal hydride**.
⚠ Zinc-carbon dry cell = **not rechargeable**; Ni-Cd = rechargeable.

ne3feb8aba9f.s: Which non-rechargeable cell is commonly used in torches and clocks?
ne3feb8aba9f.x: The zinc-carbon dry cell is generally non-rechargeable and common in torches and clocks.
xa: Electrodes: **zinc and carbon**.
⚠ Ni-Cd = **rechargeable**.
Flow batteries: energy and power capacity **scaled separately**.

n4159df10b3c.s: The remaining 10 GWh capacity put to global bids in July 2026 was intended for:
n4159df10b3c.x: The remaining 10 GWh was put to global bids for grid-scale storage.
n4159df10b3c.tq: Link the unallocated capacity with its stated end-use rather than with vehicle manufacturing.
xs: The remaining **10 GWh** went to **global bids** in **Jul 2026** for **grid-scale storage** — option **(2)**.
It is the balance of the **50 GWh** ACC-PLI after **40 GWh** was allocated.
xa: CEA need: **336 GWh** storage by **2029-30**.
Pipeline: **43 GWh** BESS by **2028** (**13 GWh** under construction, **30 GWh** at tendering).
Storage is the **main bottleneck** in integrating RE.

n245cfbe6625.s: Sodium-ion batteries are being promoted in the storage debate primarily as which of the following?
o: A system that cannot be used for stationary storage
A technology requiring more lithium than lithium-ion batteries
A replacement for all pumped storage projects
n245cfbe6625.x: Sodium-ion technology is presented as a safer, mineral-light alternative. It is not described as a universal replacement for pumped storage or as dependent on more lithium.
n245cfbe6625.tq: Match the emerging technology with its stated policy and resource advantage.
xs: **Sodium-ion** is pitched as a **safer, mineral-light alternative** (**Feb 2026**) — option **(2)**.
It avoids **cobalt, nickel, copper** and has a **lower peak temperature in thermal runaway**.
It is used for **storage** and **low-cost EVs**, so option (1) is wrong.
xa: Global capacity ~**70 GWh (2025)** → ~**400 GWh (2030)**.
⚠ Its **volumetric density** is still **below LFP**.
**Li-ion factories** can be adapted to sodium-ion.

n17a52af492c.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as a hurdle in implementing the ACC battery programme?
n17a52af492c.x: Visa delays, local-content rules and missing technology were identified as hurdles. Shortage of pumped-storage reservoirs was not listed as an ACC programme hurdle.
n17a52af492c.tq: Find the option belonging to the neighbouring storage topic rather than the ACC implementation problem set.
xs: **Shortage of pumped-storage reservoirs** is NOT an ACC-PLI hurdle — option **(3)**.
Real hurdles: **visa hold-ups for Chinese technicians**, **local-content mandates**, **missing technology**.
xa: Only **1.4 GWh** commissioned on time; **8.6 GWh** delayed (IEEFA-JMK).
Investment to **31 Aug 2025**: **₹2,326 crore**, **1,082** direct jobs.
One firm ran **1 GWh** on trial.

n0b9206df614.s: Molten-salt storage is particularly associated with concentrated solar power because it:
o: Produces hydrogen directly from atmospheric nitrogen
Stores electricity as rotational kinetic energy
Allows generation after sunset by storing thermal energy
Uses underground caverns to store compressed air
n0b9206df614.x: Molten salt provides thermal storage in concentrated solar power plants, enabling electricity generation after sunset.
n0b9206df614.tq: Identify the technology from its practical use and time-shifting function.
xs: **Molten salt** stores **thermal** energy in **concentrated solar power** plants, allowing **generation after sunset** — option **(3)**.
Rotational kinetic energy = **flywheel**; caverns of air = **CAES**.
xa: **Pumped storage** releases water through turbines at peak.
Storage is the **main bottleneck** in integrating RE.
Flywheel: **fast response**.

n2c6104edbd3.s: Which combination best describes the energy sources and storage mode integrated at the Pinnapuram project?
o: Hydrogen, biomass and battery storage only
n2c6104edbd3.x: Greenko’s Pinnapuram project integrates solar and wind generation with pumped storage.
n2c6104edbd3.tq: Identify the correct combination rather than a single technology.
xs: **Greenko**'s **Pinnapuram (Kurnool)** Integrated Renewable Energy Storage Project combines **solar + wind + pumped storage** — option **(3)**.
**Pumped storage** uses surplus power to pump water uphill and releases it through turbines at peak.
xa: CEA plans **3,931 MW** battery + **7,370 MW** pumped storage for AP (**10 Aug 2026**).
**ISTS waiver** for **BESS and PSP** till **2028**.
⚠ **CAES** stores compressed air in caverns; **molten salt** is thermal storage for CSP.

n9f051eaed8e.s: Why is energy storage regarded as a major bottleneck in integrating renewable energy into the power system?
o: Renewable energy can never be connected to a grid without coal generation.
Storage helps balance variable renewable generation and supports round-the-clock renewable electricity.
Storage eliminates the need for electricity transmission networks entirely.
Renewable energy is available only during peak electricity demand.
n9f051eaed8e.x: Storage addresses the variability of renewable generation and helps provide 24×7 renewable electricity. It does not eliminate the need for grids or imply that renewable energy is never grid-compatible.
n9f051eaed8e.tq: Apply the system-level role of storage to the renewable-integration problem.
xs: **Storage** balances variable RE and **supports 24x7 RE** — option **(2)**; it is the **main bottleneck** in integrating RE.
CEA needs **336 GWh** storage by **2029-30**, vs ~**500 MWh** BESS operating in **Sept 2025**.
xa: Pipeline: **43 GWh** BESS by **2028**.
**Energy Storage Obligation**: **1% (2023-24)** to **4% (2029-30)**.
**Draft National Electricity Policy 2026** stresses **BESS** and hybrid RE.

n5e6f20abc58.s: The National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage is run by the:
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
n5e6f20abc58.x: The ACC programme (approved 12 May 2021, 50 GWh, Rs 18,100 crore) is run by the Ministry of Heavy Industries.
xa: Launched **Oct 2021**.
**40 GWh** allocated: **Ola Electric 20**, **Reliance 15**, **Rajesh Exports 5**.
⚠ ACC-PLI = **Heavy Industries**; ESO = **Ministry of Power**; Battery Waste Rules = **MoEFCC**.

n139c91d7b17.s: Under the Energy Storage Obligation, the share of energy that DISCOMs were required to meet through storage was to rise from:
n139c91d7b17.x: The Energy Storage Obligation provided for a rise from 1 percent in 2023-24 to 4 percent in 2029-30.
n139c91d7b17.tq: Check the direction of the policy trajectory and the exact start and end years.
xs: The **Energy Storage Obligation** rises from **1 percent (2023-24)** to **4 percent (2029-30)** — option **(3)**.
Set by the **Ministry of Power** (**2022**) for **DISCOMs**.
xa: ⚠ ESO = **Ministry of Power**; ACC-PLI = **Heavy Industries**.
**VGF** for **4,000 MWh** BESS.
**Draft National Electricity Policy 2026** stresses **BESS** and **ToD tariffs**.

n40d8ac728af.s: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026, which emphasises BESS, hybrid renewable energy, smart grids and Time-of-Day tariffs, is meant to replace the National Electricity Policy of which year?
n40d8ac728af.x: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 replaces the National Electricity Policy 2005. 2003 is the year of the Electricity Act, not the policy; 2015 is the year of UDAY; 2022 is the year of the Energy Storage Obligation and the Energy Conservation Amendment.
xs: The **Draft National Electricity Policy 2026** replaces **NEP 2005** — option **(2)**.
It stresses **BESS**, **hybrid RE**, **smart grids** and **ToD tariffs**.
xa: **National Framework for Promoting Energy Storage Systems** recognises ESS as part of the power system.
**ISTS waiver** for BESS and PSP till **2028**.

n8d8f62db187.s: India's battery swapping policy was announced in the Union Budget of:
n8d8f62db187.x: The battery swapping policy was announced in Budget 2022-23; PM E-DRIVE replaced FAME-II in 2024.
xa: PM E-DRIVE = **Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement**.
⚠ **₹18,100 crore** is the **ACC-PLI** outlay.

n3c4e6c0171a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Extended Producer Responsibility under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022?
o: Producers may dispose of collected waste batteries in landfills
Producers, including importers, must collect waste batteries
Producers must recycle or refurbish waste batteries
Producers must use recycled material in new batteries
n3c4e6c0171a.x: Landfill disposal of waste batteries is prohibited.
xa: Material recovery: **90%** by **2026-27**.
**Hazardous & Other Wastes (Amendment) Rules 2025** extend EPR to **non-ferrous scrap** from **April 2026**.
**₹1,500 crore** critical-mineral **recycling** incentive scheme (**2025-26**).

n202c091dd23.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Battery Pack Aadhaar (BPAN)?
o: It is mandatory for industrial batteries exceeding 2 kWh
It is mandatory for electric vehicle batteries
It is mandatory for portable batteries of every capacity
It does not cover all household electrical appliances
n202c091dd23.x: BPAN is mandatory only for EV batteries and industrial batteries above 2 kWh, not every portable battery.
xa: Rules cover **EV, portable, automotive, industrial** batteries.
Recovery target: **90%** by **2026-27**.
Rules replace the **2001** Batteries (Management and Handling) Rules.

n6efbfb61164.s: The outlay of the National Critical Mineral Mission, approved in 2025, is:
n6efbfb61164.x: The Mission's outlay is Rs 16,300 crore; its recycling incentive scheme is Rs 1,500 crore.
xa: **Budget 2026-27**: customs-duty exemption on capital goods for **critical-mineral processing**.
**Rare Earth Corridors**: **Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu**.
Risk: **over 70%** of lithium processing in a few countries.

n9722c5a8b27.s: The lithium resource reported by the Geological Survey of India in February 2023 was located at
o: Salal-Haimana in Reasi district, Jammu and Kashmir
n9722c5a8b27.x: The GSI reported about 5.9 million tonnes of inferred lithium resources at Salal-Haimana in Reasi district of Jammu and Kashmir in 2023. Marlagalla in Mandya, Karnataka, is another Indian lithium occurrence mentioned separately.
n9722c5a8b27.tq: Use the location-date association to distinguish the J&K find from the Karnataka occurrence.
xs: GSI (**Feb 2023**) reported lithium at **Salal-Haimana, Reasi (J&K)** — ~**5.9 million tonnes** inferred — option **(4)**.
**Marlagalla, Mandya** (Karnataka) is a separate lithium site.
xa: **KABIL** = JV of **NALCO, HCL, MECL**; **15,703 ha** in Argentina.
**Amaravati** is linked to the world's first indigenous **high-energy storage device** (**2018**).
**NCMM** approved **2025**.

ne0a525ad94b.s: Which of the following are policy measures for battery energy storage systems (BESS) in India?
o: Waiver of ISTS charges for co-located storage only
Consumer ownership or leasing of storage only
Recognition of storage as a power-system element only
ne0a525ad94b.x: All three are stated measures: ISTS waiver for co-located storage, consumer ownership or leasing, and recognition of ESS as a power-system element.
xa: **ISTS waiver** for **BESS and PSP** till **2028**.
**VGF** for **4,000 MWh** BESS.
**Energy Storage Obligation**: **1% (2023-24)** to **4% (2029-30)**.

n00773b63dab.s: Which place is associated with the world’s largest single-location BESS outside China?
n00773b63dab.x: Adani Green commissioned the world’s largest single-location BESS outside China at Khavda in Gujarat in May 2026.
n00773b63dab.tq: Use the location-operator combination to distinguish Khavda from the smaller Modhera installation.
xs: **Adani Green's BESS at Khavda, Gujarat** is the **world's largest single-location BESS outside China** — option **(3)** (**May 2026**).
**Waaree** is a gigafactory developer and **Rajesh Exports** an ACC-PLI firm — not BESS sites.
xa: ~**500 MWh** BESS operating in **Sept 2025** vs need of **336 GWh** by **2029-30**.
Pipeline: **43 GWh** BESS by **2028**.
Gujarat also hosts **Reliance** (Jamnagar) and **Tata Agratas** (Sanand).

n7c3ba733eb7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about storage for renewable-energy integration in India?
o: Existing BESS capacity equals the estimated requirement
India had about 500 MWh of BESS capacity in September 2025
Existing BESS capacity is far below the estimated requirement
CEA estimated a requirement of 336 GWh of storage by 2029–30
n7c3ba733eb7.x: The requirement is 336 GWh against about 500 MWh of existing BESS, so they are not equal.
xa: Pipeline: **43 GWh** by **2028** (**13 GWh** under construction, **30 GWh** tendering).
Storage supports **24x7 RE**.
CEA plans **3,931 MW** battery + **7,370 MW** pumped storage for AP (**10 Aug 2026**).

naa3dab64718.s: India's stated goal for EV penetration by 2030 is:
naa3dab64718.x: The goal is 30 percent EV penetration by 2030, against about 8.5 percent with over 25 lakh registrations in FY 2025-26.
xa: **PM E-DRIVE** (**₹10,900 crore**) replaced **FAME-II** in **2024**.
Battery swapping policy: **Budget 2022-23**.
**Battery Pack Aadhaar** is mandatory for **EV** batteries.

n71fbb61fe47.s: A vehicle that combines an engine with a battery-motor system and can be plugged in for charging is a:
n71fbb61fe47.x: A PHEV is a hybrid that can be charged externally; a plain HEV combines engine and battery-motor but is not plugged in.
xa: **FCEV** turns hydrogen into electricity on board.
**BEV** = battery only.
**NiMH** batteries are used in **hybrid vehicles**.

n5125522a509.s: In a fuel-cell electric vehicle (FCEV), the principal energy conversion is:
o: Hydrogen into electricity on board, with water as the exhaust
Compressed air into electricity, with carbon dioxide as the exhaust
Battery energy into hydrogen, producing water as a by-product
Petrol into electricity through an external generator
n5125522a509.x: An FCEV converts hydrogen into electricity on board through a fuel cell, and water is its exhaust product.
n5125522a509.tq: Test the distinguishing conversion pathway and exhaust product of a fuel-cell vehicle.
xs: An **FCEV** converts **hydrogen into electricity on board**, with **water exhaust** — option **(1)**.
It carries a **hydrogen tank + fuel cell + small buffer battery**.
xa: **Fuel cell-electric hybrid** = fuel cell + battery buffer (NiMH/Li-ion).
BEV, FCEV and fuel cell-electric hybrid are **alternative powertrain vehicles**.
**BEV** = large Li-ion pack only.

n02f8372dd53.s: FCEV, an alternative powertrain vehicle, stands for:
n02f8372dd53.x: FCEV is a Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle; BEVs and fuel cell-electric hybrids are also alternative powertrain vehicles.
xa: **HEV/PHEV** combine an engine with a battery-motor.
EV registrations: **>25 lakh** in FY **2025-26**; ~**8.5%** penetration.
**PM E-DRIVE** replaced **FAME-II** in **2024**.

n80d60bc01d9.s: The world's first indigenously made high-energy storage device was unveiled in August 2018 at which place in Andhra Pradesh?
n80d60bc01d9.x: The device was unveiled at Amaravati on 6 August 2018 (APPSC 2018 key). Pinnapuram in Kurnool hosts Greenko's integrated solar-wind-pumped storage project; Visakhapatnam and Tirupati are not linked to this first.
n80d60bc01d9.tq: Amaravati, 6 Aug 2018 = first indigenous high-energy storage device
xs: The world's first indigenously made **high-energy storage device** was unveiled at **Amaravati**, **6 Aug 2018** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2018** key).
**Pinnapuram** (Kurnool) is Greenko's pumped-storage project, not the device site.
xa: AP is one of four **Rare Earth Corridor** states.
CEA plans **3,931 MW** battery + **7,370 MW** pumped storage for AP.
Pinnapuram = **solar + wind + pumped storage**.

nbc980d4ac26.s: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency became operational on:
nbc980d4ac26.tq: Distinguish the operational date from the enactment year of the Energy Conservation Act and the launch year of Standards and Labelling.
xs: **BEE** became operational on **1 March 2002** — option **(3)**.
**2001** is the year of the **Energy Conservation Act**, not BEE's start; **2006** is the launch of the **Standards and Labelling** programme; **2008** is **NAPCC**.
xa: BEE is a **statutory body under the EC Act 2001**, under the **Ministry of Power**.
Aim of BEE: cut the **energy intensity** of the economy.
⚠ EC Act = **2001**; BEE operational **1 March 2002**; amendment passed **December 2022**.

nc31ee53a815.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2022 amendment to the Energy Conservation Act?
o: Efficiency norms may be prescribed for vessels
Designated consumers must use a minimum share of non-fossil energy
Efficiency norms may be prescribed for vehicles
It kept large residential buildings outside energy-conservation codes
nc31ee53a815.x: The amendment brought large residential buildings under energy-conservation codes.
xa: The amendment also created the **CCTS** under **Section 14AA**.
The building code became the **Energy Conservation and Sustainable Building Code (ECSBC, 2024)**.
Lok Sabha passed it in **Aug 2022**, Rajya Sabha in **Dec 2022**.

n3f07b5ff12d.s: The Rajya Sabha passed the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill, 2022, completing its passage, in:
n3f07b5ff12d.x: The Lok Sabha passed the Bill in August 2022 and the Rajya Sabha in December 2022, completing its passage.
xa: It was asked as an **APPSC 2021 PYQ**.
The amendment gave legal basis to the **CCTS** (**Section 14AA**).
⚠ EC Act = **2001**; BEE operational **1 March 2002**; amendment **December 2022**.

n7588e8f34b9.s: Under the star-labelling changes effective from 1 January 2026, manufacturers may be penalised when:
o: the product receives fewer than three stars irrespective of its actual consumption
actual energy consumption deviates from the declared label rating
a product is sold without an international energy certificate
the product is manufactured outside a designated consumer sector
n7588e8f34b9.x: Manufacturers may be penalised if the actual energy consumption of a product deviates from the consumption declared through its label.
n7588e8f34b9.tq: Apply the compliance rule to a manufacturer’s conduct instead of confusing rating level with accuracy of declaration.
xs: Makers are penalised when **actual consumption deviates from the declared label** — option **(2)**.
This came with mandatory labelling from **1 Jan 2026**.
xa: Groups made mandatory: fridges, TVs, **LPG stoves**, cooling towers, chillers, deep freezers, transformers, **solar inverters**.
Each extra star saves about **10-15%** energy.
The programme is run by **BEE** under the **Ministry of Power**.

nce36319e23d.s: UJALA and the Street Lighting National Programme were both launched in:
nce36319e23d.x: Both UJALA and the Street Lighting National Programme were launched in January 2015.
nce36319e23d.tq: Use the date-pair clue when two programmes were launched together.
xs: **UJALA** and **SLNP** were both launched in **January 2015** — option **(3)**.
**2012** is PAT's launch; **2018** is ECO Niwas Samhita and the Preparedness Index.
xa: Both are implemented by **EESL**.
UJALA = **Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All**.
SLNP replaced **sodium vapour** street lights with LEDs.

nc0f25fc1634.s: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency, a statutory body created by the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, functions under the:
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
nc0f25fc1634.x: BEE functions under the Ministry of Power; the JV of power PSUs that distributes LEDs is EESL.
xa: BEE has been operational since **1 March 2002**.
BEE is the **administrator** of the **CCTS**; **CERC** is its regulator.
⚠ **NECA** is given by **BEE under the Ministry of Power**, not MNRE.

n46ae927a458.s: The Standards and Labelling programme for energy-consuming equipment in India is administered by which organisation under which Ministry?
o: National Productivity Council under the Ministry of Heavy Industries
Energy Efficiency Services Limited under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power
Central Electricity Authority under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
n46ae927a458.x: The Standards and Labelling programme is administered by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power.
n46ae927a458.tq: Identify the organisation and parent ministry without confusing neighbouring energy institutions.
xs: The **Standards and Labelling** programme is run by **BEE** under the **Ministry of Power** — option **(3)**.
**EESL** implements **UJALA** and **SLNP**; it does not run labelling.
xa: Launched in **2006**; covers **40+ equipment**.
Rating: **1-5 star**; each extra star saves about **10-15%** energy.
From **1 Jan 2026**, labelling became **mandatory** for fridges, TVs, LPG stoves and more.

n4b2cf2ba999.s: Which organisation implements both UJALA and the Street Lighting National Programme?
n4b2cf2ba999.x: Both programmes are implemented by Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL), a joint venture of public-sector undertakings under the Ministry of Power.
n4b2cf2ba999.tq: Identify the implementing agency, not the supervising ministry or an associated organisation.
xs: **Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL)** implements both **UJALA** and **SLNP** — option **(1)**.
EESL is a **JV of Ministry of Power PSUs**; **BEE** is the statutory body running PAT and labelling; **PCRA** gives driving advice and launched **SAKSHAM**.
xa: EESL also runs the **National Efficient Cooking Programme**.
UJALA/SLNP distributed **36.86 crore** LED bulbs and **72.18 lakh** LED tube lights.
**Jul 2026**: an **EESL-APSECM** impact report was released by CS **G. Sai Prasad**.

nbca1eb83f63.s: The Street Lighting National Programme primarily replaced older street lighting based on which technology with LEDs?
nbca1eb83f63.x: Under the Street Lighting National Programme, older sodium vapour street lights were replaced by LED lights.
nbca1eb83f63.tq: Match the programme intervention with the specific older technology.
xs: SLNP replaced **sodium vapour** street lights with LEDs — option **(4)**.
Sodium vapour lamps have high efficacy but **yellow light** and **poor colour rendering**.
xa: SLNP was launched in **January 2015** by **EESL**.
AP: **680 LED streetlights** via the **State Energy Conservation Fund**.
AP has **MoUs with EESL** for LED street lighting.

ne9807fd1213.s: The inaugural State Energy Efficiency Preparedness Index was prepared by which of the following combinations?
o: NITI Aayog with the Bureau of Energy Efficiency
Bureau of Energy Efficiency with the Energy Efficiency Services Limited
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change with NITI Aayog
Bureau of Energy Efficiency with the Alliance for an Energy Efficient Economy
ne9807fd1213.x: The inaugural State Energy Efficiency Preparedness Index, introduced in 2018, was prepared by NITI Aayog in association with the Bureau of Energy Efficiency.
ne9807fd1213.tq: Use the institution-pair distinction to avoid swapping agencies.
xs: The inaugural **State Energy Efficiency Preparedness Index (2018)** was prepared by **NITI Aayog with BEE** — option **(1)**.
**BEE with AEEE** made the framework of the **State Energy Efficiency Index (SEEI)** — the trap in option (4).
xa: In the **2018** index, **AP = "Front Runner"** (**APPSC 2018**).
SEEI categories: **Front Runner, Achiever, Contender, Aspirant**.
SEEI is the basis for the **National Energy Conservation Awards**.

nd217f6b6444.s: Energy efficiency strengthens energy security in India, which depends on imports for about ____ of its oil.
nd217f6b6444.x: India imports about 80% of its oil, so cheap demand reduction through efficiency improves energy security.
xa: PAT, S&L and UJALA avoid **~321 MT CO2** a year.
Mandatory star labels from **1 Jan 2026**; makers penalised if use deviates from the label.
**UK CBAM** recognised India's CCTS (**Sep 2026**).

n50557cc04f4.s: The Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme is:
o: A market mechanism setting energy-reduction targets for designated consumers
A labelling programme for household appliances
A loan scheme for solarising farm pumps
A scheme for distributing LED bulbs to households
n50557cc04f4.x: PAT is a market mechanism under NMEEE that assigns energy-reduction targets to designated consumers.
xa: Over-achievers earn **ESCerts**; laggards buy them on **power exchanges** (IEX).
Launched **2012**; Cycle I (**2012-15**): **478** units in **8** sectors.
In AP, PAT covers **59** industries, saving ~**1.16 Mtoe**.

n1bad6874f7e.s: Energy Saving Certificates (ESCerts) under the PAT scheme are traded on:
n1bad6874f7e.x: Over-achievers earn ESCerts and under-achievers buy them on power exchanges, including the Indian Energy Exchange.
xa: PAT is a market mechanism under **NMEEE**, launched in **2012**.
⚠ PAT = **ESCerts** (energy intensity); CCTS = **CCCs** (emission intensity).
Later PAT sectors added: **railways, DISCOMs, refineries, commercial buildings**.

ne2b7bf35732.s: The National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency is one of how many missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change?
ne2b7bf35732.x: NMEEE is one of the eight missions under NAPCC (2008).
xa: PAT was launched in **2012**; Cycle I (**2012-15**) covered **478** units in **8** sectors.
Over-achievers earn **ESCerts**, traded on **power exchanges** (IEX).
BEE programmes: **SEEI**, **PAT**, **Standards & Labelling**, **ECBC**; it also runs **CAFE** and **NECA**.

ne6477e625d6.s: The Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022 provides a legal basis for which of the following?
o: A mandatory market for petroleum imports
A separate market for nuclear fuel
ne6477e625d6.x: The 2022 amendment gave legal basis to a carbon market through the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme.
ne6477e625d6.tq: Match the amendment with its principal legal innovation.
xs: The **2022 amendment** gave legal basis to a **carbon market** — the **Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS)** — option **(4)**.
The provision is **Section 14AA**.
xa: Other 2022 provisions: **non-fossil** energy obligation for designated consumers, codes for large **residential** buildings, norms for **vehicles and vessels**.
CCTS was notified in **2023** as India's **first mandatory compliance carbon market**.
Administrator = **BEE**; regulator = **CERC**.

n7280eb7d3d7.s: The regulator of India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme is:
n7280eb7d3d7.x: CERC is the regulator, while BEE is the administrator of the scheme.
xa: Legal basis = **Section 14AA** of the **2022 amendment**.
Mechanisms: **Compliance** (Carbon Credit Certificates) + **Voluntary Offset**.
⚠ PAT trades **ESCerts** (energy intensity); CCTS trades **CCCs** (emission intensity).

n63bbd07e2dc.s: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme supports India's target of cutting GDP emission intensity by 2030 (over 2005 levels) by:
n63bbd07e2dc.x: The stated goal is a 45% cut in GDP emission intensity by 2030 relative to the 2005 level.
xa: CCTS was notified in **2023**; legal basis **Section 14AA**.
It covers **9 heavy industries** (**208 units**).
The **UK CBAM** applies from **1 Jan 2027** and recognises CCTS.

n142d80d4c3a.s: The compliance mechanism of India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme covers:
o: 9 heavy industries with GHG intensity targets for 208 units
4 sectors: thermal power, railways, DISCOMs and commercial buildings
n142d80d4c3a.x: CCTS covers 9 heavy industries, with GHG emission-intensity targets for 208 units. 478 units in 8 sectors was PAT Cycle I; the four sectors are those PAT will retain; 60 clusters in 14 sectors is ADEETIE.
n142d80d4c3a.tq: CCTS = 9 industries, 208 units; PAT-I = 8 sectors, 478 units
xs: CCTS covers **9 heavy industries**, with GHG intensity targets for **208 units** — option **(2)**.
**478 units in 8 sectors** = PAT Cycle I; the **4 sectors** are those PAT will keep.
**60 MSME clusters in 14 sectors** = **ADEETIE**.
xa: Goal: **45% cut** in GDP emission intensity by **2030** (vs 2005).
Mechanisms: **Compliance** + **Voluntary Offset**.
Legal basis **Section 14AA**; administrator **BEE**; regulator **CERC**.

n6bec2e94175.s: Which one of the following was NOT included among the original PAT sectors?
n6bec2e94175.x: The original PAT sectors included thermal power, chlor-alkali and textiles. Railways was added later and is part of the proposed residual-sector arrangement.
n6bec2e94175.tq: Use the time qualifier to distinguish original sectors from sectors added later.
xs: **Railways** was not an original PAT sector — it was **added later** — option **(2)**.
**Chlor-alkali**, **textiles** and **thermal power** were original PAT sectors.
xa: Later additions: **railways, DISCOMs, refineries, commercial buildings**.
After CCTS, PAT keeps only **thermal power, railways, DISCOMs, commercial buildings**.
Cycle I (**2012-15**): **478** units in **8** sectors.

n8c3b8a3452e.s: After the expansion of the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), PAT is proposed to retain which four residual sectors?
o: Chlor-alkali, cement, railways and domestic buildings
Iron and steel, petrochemicals, refineries and pulp and paper
Thermal power, railways, DISCOMs and commercial buildings
n8c3b8a3452e.x: The proposed four residual PAT sectors are thermal power, railways, DISCOMs and commercial buildings.
n8c3b8a3452e.tq: Use the future-sector list as a direct four-item recall question and reject the older industrial grouping.
xs: PAT will keep **thermal power, railways, DISCOMs and commercial buildings** — option **(4)**.
The reason: **CCTS** now covers **9 heavy industries** like **cement, aluminium, iron & steel**.
xa: Of the four retained, **railways, DISCOMs, commercial buildings** were later additions to PAT.
⚠ PAT = **ESCerts**; CCTS = **Carbon Credit Certificates**.
CCTS administrator **BEE**, regulator **CERC**.

n02e8c68780a.s: The certificates issued under PAT and CCTS, respectively, are:
n02e8c68780a.x: PAT is associated with energy-intensity certificates (ESCerts), while CCTS issues emission-intensity certificates called CCCs.
xa: ESCerts are traded on **power exchanges** (IEX).
CCTS covers **9 heavy industries**; PAT will keep **4 sectors**.
CCTS: administrator **BEE**, regulator **CERC**, legal basis **Section 14AA**.

n8975b1fe2ba.s: Under BEE's Standards and Labelling programme, each additional star saves approximately:
n8975b1fe2ba.x: The one-to-five-star programme (over 40 equipment types) saves about 10–15 per cent energy per additional star.
xa: Launched **2006** by **BEE** (Ministry of Power).
Voluntary examples: **industrial motors**, **computers**, **microwave ovens**.
From **1 Jan 2026**, makers are **penalised** if actual consumption deviates from the label.

n439726be949.s: ECO Niwas Samhita, introduced in 2018, is an energy code for:
n439726be949.x: ECO Niwas Samhita (2018) covers residential buildings; ECBC (2007) covers new commercial buildings.
xa: **ECSBC (2024)** adds **sustainability** to ECBC after the 2022 amendment.
⚠ ECBC = **commercial**; ECO Niwas Samhita = **residential**.
AP model: **Super ECBC building, Sagar Nagar, Visakhapatnam** (Jan 2026).

nb24d707def1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about fuel-efficiency and conservation initiatives?
o: SAKSHAM is a fuel-conservation drive of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency
The first CAFE norms were notified in 2017
CAFE norms set average fuel-efficiency targets for M1 cars
The Bureau of Energy Efficiency enforces the CAFE norms
nb24d707def1.x: SAKSHAM is conducted by the Petroleum Conservation Research Association (PCRA), not BEE.
xa: SAKSHAM **2026** was launched by PCRA at **Chandigarh** (Jun 2026).
PCRA driving advice: correct **tyre pressure**, steady speed, engine off at signals.
**NECA 2025**: **Chandigarh** ranked first.

n37f4a1bca99.s: Energy efficiency is linked to sustainability mainly because it:
o: increases the energy intensity of the economy
reduces the need for new energy sources
requires replacing all renewable energy with fossil fuels
has no effect on energy demand
n37f4a1bca99.x: Using energy efficiently lowers demand, so fewer new energy sources need to be built (APPSC 2025). It lowers energy intensity rather than raising it, does not require fossil fuels, and directly cuts demand.
xs: Energy efficiency **reduces the need for new energy sources** — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2025**).
It **lowers** energy intensity — BEE's aim is to cut the **energy intensity** of the economy — so option (1) is wrong.
xa: PAT, S&L and UJALA avoid **~321 MT CO2** a year.
It is the **cheapest route** to cut demand and emissions.
Results (**FY 2023-24**): **53.6 Mtoe** saved.

n070ed2abe79.s: ADEETIE, launched in July 2025 with an outlay of ₹1,000 crore, promotes energy efficiency in:
n070ed2abe79.x: ADEETIE focuses on energy efficiency among MSMEs through audits and financial support.
xa: Subvention: **5%** for micro/small and **3%** for medium enterprises.
Coverage: **60 clusters** in **14 sectors**.
⚠ **60 clusters, 14 sectors** = ADEETIE; **478 units, 8 sectors** = PAT Cycle I.

n947c4848f62.s: India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, notified in 2023, is provided for under:
