n947c4848f62.x: Section 14AA provides for the CCTS, India's first mandatory compliance carbon market.
xa: Administrator = **BEE**; regulator = **CERC**.
It covers **9 heavy industries**, with GHG intensity targets for **208 units**.
Goal: **45% cut in GDP emission intensity by 2030** (vs **2005**).

n677a4c29d88.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and India?
o: In September 2026 the UK recognised India's CCTS as a qualifying carbon price
The UK CBAM covers aluminium and cement
The UK CBAM applies from 1 January 2026
The UK CBAM covers fertiliser, hydrogen, and iron and steel
n677a4c29d88.x: The UK CBAM applies from 1 January 2027, not 2026.
xa: CCTS is India's **first mandatory compliance carbon market**, notified **2023**.
CCTS is administered by **BEE** and regulated by **CERC**.
It covers **9 heavy industries** with targets for **208 units**.

nedb37170c99.s: Under UJALA, approximately how many LED bulbs have been distributed?
nedb37170c99.x: UJALA distributed about 36.86 crore LED bulbs, along with 72.18 lakh LED tube lights and 23.59 lakh energy-efficient fans. 9.5 crore is the number of PMUY LPG connections.
nedb37170c99.tq: UJALA: 36.86 crore bulbs; 72.18 lakh tubes; 23.59 lakh fans
xs: UJALA distributed **36.86 crore** LED bulbs — option **(3)**.
**72.18 lakh** = LED tube lights; **23.59 lakh** = energy-efficient fans.
xa: UJALA was launched in **January 2015** by **EESL**.
PAT + S&L + UJALA avoided **321.06 MT CO2** annually (FY 2023-24).
⚠ crore (bulbs) vs lakh (tube lights, fans).

n01c98df3ba5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the State Energy Efficiency Index (SEEI)?
o: It was developed by BEE with the Alliance for an Energy Efficient Economy
It classifies States into only three categories
Front Runner is one of its categories
It forms the basis for the National Energy Conservation Awards
n01c98df3ba5.x: SEEI uses four categories: Front Runner, Achiever, Contender and Aspirant.
xa: ⚠ **Preparedness Index (2018)** = **NITI Aayog with BEE**; SEEI = **BEE with AEEE**.
AP was **Front Runner** in the **2018** index.
**NECA 2025**: **Chandigarh** ranked first.

n3c4b6b89a0e.s: Andhra Pradesh's model Super ECBC building is located at:
n3c4b6b89a0e.x: The AP model Super ECBC building is located at Sagar Nagar in Visakhapatnam.
xa: ECBC is notified in **123 ULBs** of AP, with **1,300** compliant buildings.
**APSECM** (constituted **2012**) is India's first standalone **State Designated Agency** of BEE.
ECBC applies to new **commercial** buildings.

n81b7a2a5c07.s: In the inaugural State Energy Efficiency Preparedness Index (2018), Andhra Pradesh was placed in which category?
n81b7a2a5c07.x: Andhra Pradesh was rated a Front Runner, the top category, in the inaugural 2018 index prepared by NITI Aayog with BEE (APPSC 2018). Achiever, Contender and Aspirant are the lower categories.
n81b7a2a5c07.tq: AP = Front Runner, 2018 (NITI Aayog + BEE index)
xs: AP was a **"Front Runner"** in the inaugural **2018** Preparedness Index — option **(4)** (**APPSC 2018**).
**Achiever**, **Contender** and **Aspirant** are the lower categories.
xa: The index was prepared by **NITI Aayog with BEE**.
**APSECM** (**2012**) is India's **first standalone State Designated Agency** of BEE.
APSECM has won **First Prize in NECA**.

ncdeab7f4897.s: During National Energy Conservation Week in Andhra Pradesh in 2024, which department collaborated in the awareness activities?
ncdeab7f4897.x: The School Education Department collaborated in Andhra Pradesh’s National Energy Conservation Week awareness activities in 2024.
ncdeab7f4897.tq: Identify the collaborating department rather than the sector-wide beneficiaries of the programme.
xs: The **School Education Department** collaborated in AP's **NEC Week 14-20 Dec 2024** — option **(3)**.
The drives covered awareness across sectors.
xa: **PYQ 2024**: all three statements on AP's role were correct (**APPSC 2024**).
**National Energy Conservation Day** = **14 December**.
AP's **State Energy Conservation Awards-2024** covered thermal plants, textiles, hospitals, **RTC depots**, **ULBs**.

nca8ae16b7fa.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Energy Conservation Mission (APSECM) was constituted in:
nca8ae16b7fa.tq: Use the establishment year, not the year of the State Energy Efficiency Preparedness Index.
xs: **APSECM** was constituted in **2012** — option **(3)**.
**2001** = EC Act; **2018** = Preparedness Index (AP Front Runner).
xa: APSECM is **India's first standalone State Designated Agency** of BEE.
It **enforces the EC Act 2001** in AP.
⚠ **2012** is also the year **PAT** was launched.

n950cbf3a822.s: India's first standalone State Designated Agency of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency is:
n950cbf3a822.x: APSECM is India's first standalone State Designated Agency of BEE and enforces the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, in Andhra Pradesh.
xa: Constituted in **2012**.
Work: efficient appliances in **112 Anganwadi** schools, **Mangalagiri**; star-rated products for **PMAY** homes.
**Jul 2026**: CS **G. Sai Prasad** released an **EESL-APSECM** impact report.

n04614a429ee.s: The first IoT energy pilot associated with APSECM was undertaken at an MSME unit in:
n04614a429ee.x: The IoT energy pilot was first undertaken at an MSME unit in East Godavari and was later extended to all districts with BEE.
n04614a429ee.tq: Use the location clue to distinguish the pilot site from the programme’s later statewide extension.
xs: India's first **IoT** pilot at an MSME unit was in **East Godavari** — option **(3)**; it was extended to all districts with **BEE**.
**Mangalagiri** is where **112 Anganwadi** schools got efficient appliances; **Visakhapatnam** has the **Super ECBC** building.
xa: AP MSME energy audits covered **4** clusters: gold ornaments, imitation jewellery, food processing, pharma.
**ADEETIE** (**Jul 2025**) supports MSME efficiency nationally.
**28 W BLDC 5-star fans** were fitted in **16 APSRTC** bus stations.

n5a1b0e2a2b0.s: Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (Saubhagya) was launched in which year, and for what purpose?
n5a1b0e2a2b0.x: Saubhagya was launched in 2017 for universal household electrification. Urban distribution strengthening is IPDS (2014), DISCOM turnaround is UDAY (2015) and farm-pump solarisation is PM-KUSUM (2019).
n5a1b0e2a2b0.tq: Saubhagya 2017 = every household; IPDS 2014, UDAY 2015, KUSUM 2019
xs: **Saubhagya** was launched in **2017** for **universal household electrification** — option **(3)**.
**IPDS** (Dec **2014**) = urban distribution; **UDAY** (Nov **2015**) = discom turnaround; **PM-KUSUM** (**2019**) = farm solar.
xa: Full name: **Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana**.
It electrified **2.86 crore** willing households.
Policy shift: connections (**DDUGJY, Saubhagya**) → discom viability (**UDAY, RDSS**) → prosumers (**PM Surya Ghar**).

n0376e4796f6.s: UDAY, introduced in November 2015, aims at:
o: Financial turnaround of state electricity distribution companies
n0376e4796f6.x: UDAY (Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana) was introduced by the Ministry of Power in November 2015 for the financial turnaround of state discoms.
xa: States took over **75%** of discom debt (as of **30 Sep 2015**) via state bonds.
Targets by **2018-19**: AT&C losses **15%** and **ACS-ARR gap zero**.
⚠ IPDS = **urban** distribution; UDAY = discom **debt**.

n9bfe9746189.s: The Integrated Power Development Scheme (IPDS), launched in December 2014, primarily aims to strengthen:
o: Rural agricultural feeder separation and village electrification
Urban sub-transmission and distribution, metering and IT enablement
n9bfe9746189.x: IPDS strengthens urban sub-transmission and distribution, metering and IT enablement.
n9bfe9746189.tq: Distinguish the urban distribution focus of IPDS from the rural focus of DDUGJY.
xs: **IPDS** (Dec **2014**) strengthens **urban sub-transmission and distribution, metering and IT enablement** — option **(3)**.
Village electrification is **Saubhagya**; LPG is **PMUY**; solar pumps are **PM-KUSUM**.
xa: IPDS subsumed **R-APDRP**.
It is credited with **better urban supply**.
⚠ IPDS = **urban** distribution; UDAY = discom **debt**.

n3f555344f62.x: The Integrated Power Development Scheme subsumed the Restructured Accelerated Power Development and Reforms Programme (R-APDRP).
n3f555344f62.tq: Identify the predecessor by separating urban and rural distribution programmes.
xs: **IPDS** subsumed **R-APDRP** — option **(3)**.
**PM-KUSUM** (**2019**) and **Saubhagya** (**2017**) are separate later schemes.
xa: IPDS was launched in **Dec 2014** for **urban** distribution, metering and IT.
It is credited with **better urban supply**.
**RDSS (2021)** later focused on loss reduction and **prepaid smart metering**.

nb0984ff3bc5.s: UDAY targeted a reduction of AT&C losses to ____ by 2018-19.
nb0984ff3bc5.x: UDAY targeted AT&C losses of 15% and a zero ACS-ARR gap by 2018-19.
xa: ⚠ AT&C target: UDAY **15%**; RDSS **12-15%**.
Participating states covered **97%** of outstanding discom debt (**PYQ 2017**).

ndf480b16e6a.s: The national targets of RDSS include:
o: AT&C losses of 12–15% and an ACS-ARR gap of zero
AT&C losses of zero and an ACS-ARR gap of 12–15%
AT&C losses of 30% and an ACS-ARR gap of 15%
Only reduction of transmission losses, without an ACS-ARR target
ndf480b16e6a.x: RDSS aims at pan-India AT&C losses of 12–15% and an ACS-ARR gap of zero.
ndf480b16e6a.tq: Avoid reversing the two performance indicators and their target values.
xs: RDSS targets pan-India **AT&C loss 12-15%** and **ACS-ARR gap zero** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) swaps the two targets.
xa: ⚠ UDAY aimed at AT&C **15%** by **2018-19**.
Components: **prepaid smart metering**, loss-reduction works.
Outlay **₹3,03,758 crore**.

n05561d6820a.s: Under PM-KUSUM, Component C relates to:
o: Decentralised grid-connected solar plants on barren land
Solarisation of existing grid-connected agricultural pumps
n05561d6820a.x: Component C solarises grid-connected agricultural pumps. Component A covers decentralised grid-connected solar/RE plants on farm or barren land, and Component B covers standalone solar pumps. Urban household rooftop solar comes under PM Surya Ghar, not PM-KUSUM.
n05561d6820a.tq: KUSUM: A = plants, B = standalone pumps, C = solarise grid pumps
xs: **Component C** = **solarisation of grid-connected pumps** — option **(3)**.
**A** = plants on farm/barren land; **B** = **standalone solar pumps**; urban rooftop solar is **PM Surya Ghar**.
xa: Component C progress: **10.99 lakh** pumps.
Subsidy for B/C: **30:30:40** (Centre:State:farmer).
Benefit: **daytime irrigation** + extra income.

n02786cbd72d.s: Which of the following is correctly associated with Ujjwala 2.0?
o: Free first refill and stove, self-declaration facility for migrants, and ₹1,600 assistance per 14.2 kg connection
Free electricity up to 300 units and 60% rooftop-solar subsidy
A ₹6,521 crore package for border villages only
n02786cbd72d.x: Ujjwala 2.0 provides a free first refill and stove, permits migrants to use self-declaration, and provides cash assistance of ₹1,600 per 14.2 kg connection.
n02786cbd72d.tq: Group several features belonging to one phase instead of mixing schemes.
xs: **Ujjwala 2.0** gives a **free first refill and stove**, **self-declaration for migrants** and **₹1,600** per **14.2 kg** connection — option **(2)**.
**30:30:40** sharing is **PM-KUSUM** B/C; **300 units** free and **60%** subsidy is **PM Surya Ghar**; **₹6,521 crore** is RDSS for Saubhagya leftovers.
xa: Refill subsidy since **Oct 2023**: **₹300 × 9** a year.
Older notes: **₹200** per refill, up to **12** a year; **5 kg** double-bottle option.
PMUY is run by **MoPNG** (**2016**).

nf731b69b7d2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about UDAY?
o: States took over 75% of DISCOM debt outstanding as on 30 September 2015
The arrangement covered only half of total outstanding DISCOM debt
50% of the debt was taken over in 2015-16
25% of the debt was taken over in 2016-17
nf731b69b7d2.x: The arrangement covered 97% of total outstanding DISCOM debt.
xa: Debt was taken over through **state bonds**.
Targets by **2018-19**: AT&C **15%**, ACS-ARR gap **zero**.

n8c7a9e9c2df.s: What is the household target of PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana by March 2027?
n8c7a9e9c2df.x: The scheme targets rooftop solar installations in 1 crore households by FY 2026-27, that is, March 2027.
n8c7a9e9c2df.tq: Match the target number with the stated completion year.
xs: Target: rooftop solar in **1 crore households** by **FY 2026-27** (**March 2027**) — option **(2)**.
**PYQ (UPSC 2025)**: statements on the 1 crore target and MNRE installer training were all correct.
xa: Households become **"prosumers"** with up to **300 units** free a month.
**One Model Solar Village per district**.
AP: **2,27,549** installations done.

n01488af2c5c.s: Under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, households may receive free electricity up to:
n01488af2c5c.x: The scheme provides for free power of up to 300 units per month, with beneficiary households becoming prosumers.
n01488af2c5c.tq: Test the exact monthly ceiling rather than the broader rooftop-solar objective.
xs: Free power up to **300 units per month** — option **(2)**.
**200 units** is AP's own free power for **BPL SC/ST** households — a trap.
xa: Households become **"prosumers"**.
CFA: **60%** for 2 kW; **40%** for extra up to **3 kW**.
Outlay **₹75,021 crore**.

nd690bb69e0e.s: Under PM Surya Ghar, Central Financial Assistance covers ____ of the cost for the first 2 kW.
nd690bb69e0e.x: CFA covers 60% of the cost for 2 kW and 40% for additional capacity up to 3 kW.
xa: Free power up to **300 units per month**.
Target: **1 crore households**; **30 GW** RTS.
AP SC/ST households get **free rooftop solar** via **Virtual Net Metering**.

n5372decc0e0.s: As per the latest figure, how many willing households were electrified under Saubhagya?
n5372decc0e0.x: Saubhagya electrified 2.86 crore willing households; 2.82 crore was an older figure (March 2021).
xa: Saubhagya (**2017**) aimed at **universal household electrification** and claimed **100%**.
Leftovers: **₹6,521 crore** under **RDSS** for **13.65 lakh** households.
**Leisang (Manipur)** was the last village electrified, **28 Apr 2018**.

nddcaaa05e4a.s: What was the Phase I target of PMUY by 2019?
nddcaaa05e4a.x: Phase I of PMUY targeted 8 crore deposit-free LPG connections by 2019; the reported number of connections later exceeded 9.5 crore.
nddcaaa05e4a.tq: Distinguish the original target from the later cumulative achievement.
xs: PMUY Phase I targeted **8 crore** connections by **2019** — option **(2)**.
**9.5 crore+** is the later total of connections, not the Phase I target.
xa: **Ujjwala 2.0**: free first refill and stove; **migrants via self-declaration**.
Cash assistance: **₹1,600** per **14.2 kg** connection.
**Grameen Vitrak Yojana (2009)** raised rural LPG distributors from **18%** to **60%**.

n4bf9fbbf641.s: Since October 2023, the targeted subsidy for PMUY beneficiaries has been:
o: ₹200 per 14.2 kg refill for up to 12 refills a year
₹300 per 5 kg refill without an annual limit
₹1,600 per 14.2 kg refill for up to 5 refills a year
₹300 per 14.2 kg refill for up to 9 refills a year
n4bf9fbbf641.x: Since October 2023, the targeted subsidy has been ₹300 per 14.2 kg refill for up to nine refills a year. Older provisions cited ₹200 and up to 12 refills.
n4bf9fbbf641.tq: Give priority to the latest figure while distinguishing it from the older subsidy arrangement.
xs: Since **Oct 2023**: **₹300** per **14.2 kg** refill, up to **9** refills a year — option **(4)**.
**₹200 × 12** was the older provision; **₹1,600** is cash assistance per **connection**, not per refill.
xa: Ujjwala 2.0 gives a **free first refill and stove**.
PMUY has **9.5 crore+** connections.
Refill problem: households want clean fuel but face **cost and habit** barriers (CEEW's **IRES** survey).

nee01281f6da.s: Which village in Manipur was identified as the last village to be electrified?
nee01281f6da.x: Leisang in Manipur was identified as the last village to be electrified.
nee01281f6da.tq: Use the distinctive place-name association to distinguish the first/last fact from nearby locations.
xs: **Leisang (Manipur)** was the last village electrified, on **28 Apr 2018** — option **(1)**.
Imphal, Thoubal and Churachandpur are not mentioned as last villages.
xa: **Saubhagya (2017)** later claimed **100%** household electrification.
Saubhagya electrified **2.86 crore** willing households.
Connections came first via **DDUGJY** and **Saubhagya**.

n74f4541667b.s: In Andhra Pradesh, free power up to how many units per month is provided to BPL SC/ST households?
n74f4541667b.x: Free power is provided up to 200 units per month to eligible BPL SC/ST households in Andhra Pradesh.
n74f4541667b.tq: Use the exact numerical limit and eliminate nearby but altered figures.
xs: AP gives free power **up to 200 units/month** to **20.26 lakh** BPL SC/ST households — option **(3)**.
**300 units** is the PM Surya Ghar free-power limit.
xa: AP power subsidy (**FY 2024-25**): **₹10,449.92 crore**.
Concessional tariffs: **BC/MBC professionals, dhobi ghats, handlooms, saloons**.
SC/ST households get **free rooftop solar** via **Virtual Net Metering**.

n142e754ad3e.s: Free rooftop solar power for SC/ST households in Andhra Pradesh is proposed through:
n142e754ad3e.x: The provision of free rooftop solar for SC/ST households is associated with Virtual Net Metering.
n142e754ad3e.tq: Discriminate between closely related electricity-metering concepts.
xs: AP's SC/ST households get **free rooftop solar** via **Virtual Net Metering** — option **(2)**.
**Prepaid** smart metering is an **RDSS** component, not this.
xa: AP PM Surya Ghar: **2,27,549** installations.
Discom progress (**Aug 2026**): **SPDCL 47%, CPDCL 35%, EPDCL 32%**.
**APCPDCL**: **50,114** rooftop units, **180 MW**.

n17c326ea3ef.s: An Ultra Mega Solar Park is defined as a solar park having a capacity of at least:
n17c326ea3ef.x: An Ultra Mega Solar Park has a capacity of 500 MW or more at one location.
n17c326ea3ef.tq: Discriminate the official threshold from the higher 1,000 MW figure.
xs: An **Ultra Mega Solar Park** is **500 MW or more** at one location — option **(3)**.
⚠ "**1,000 MW**" is the trap — it is WRONG (**APPSC 2019**).
xa: **Kurnool UMSP (1,000 MW)**, Gani-Sakunala, was once the **world's largest** single-location solar park.
**Ananthapuram-I** (**1,500 MW**) is at **NP Kunta**.
Solar Park Scheme target: **40,000 MW** (raised **21 Mar 2017**).

na825432cdad.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about floating solar power in India?
o: India's estimated floating-solar potential is about 102 GW
Omkareshwar is the largest identified floating solar project
Existing floating-solar capacity is about 0.7 GW
The 278 MW Omkareshwar project is in Andhra Pradesh
na825432cdad.x: The 278 MW Omkareshwar project is in Madhya Pradesh.
xa: AP: NTPC's **25 MW** floating solar at **Simhadri, Visakhapatnam** (**APPSC 2021**).
⚠ **Simhadri** = floating solar; **Ramagiri** = hybrid park; **Talaricheruvu** = UMSP-II.

n7b1bb161c63.s: The 1,000 MW Ultra Mega Solar Park at Gani-Sakunala, Panyam mandal, is in which district?
n7b1bb161c63.x: The Kurnool Ultra Mega Solar Park (1,000 MW) is at Gani-Sakunala, Panyam mandal, Kurnool district (APPSC 2019).
xa: It was once the **world's largest** single-location solar park (**APPSC 2019**).
Krishnapatnam (**Nellore**) has APPDCL's **2,400 MW** thermal plant.

nc927e657a92.s: NTPC's 25 MW floating solar plant in Andhra Pradesh, operational by July 2022, is at:
nc927e657a92.x: The 25 MW floating solar plant is at NTPC Simhadri in Visakhapatnam (APPSC 2021). Omkareshwar (MP) is India's largest floating solar project (278 MW); Krishnapatnam has an APPDCL thermal plant; Ramagiri has the hybrid solar-wind park.
xs: NTPC's **25 MW** floating solar plant is at **Simhadri, Visakhapatnam** (**APPSC 2021**) — option **(3)**.
**Omkareshwar** (MP, **278 MW**) is India's largest floating plant; **Krishnapatnam** is thermal; **Ramagiri** is the hybrid park.
xa: **Simhadri STPS** (NTPC) is a **2,000 MW** thermal plant.
Floating solar: ~**0.7 GW** installed vs **102 GW** potential.

n4882cb40a26.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Tata Renewable hybrid project in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It has 400 MW of solar at Pathikonda
It has 400 MW of wind at Kanekallu
n4882cb40a26.x: The project has 400 MW solar at Pathikonda (Kurnool) and 400 MW wind at Kanekallu (Anantapur).
xa: Investment **₹5,750 crore**; ~**4,000** construction jobs.
Some notes place both parts in **Anantapur** district.
It is under **ICEP-2024** (Jul **2026**).

n4e0fc1b00b4.s: The 600 MW SAEL solar project in Kadapa was the first project commissioned under which Andhra Pradesh policy?
o: Andhra Pradesh Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy, 2023
n4e0fc1b00b4.x: The 600 MW SAEL project in Kadapa is identified as a development under the Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024 (ICEP-2024).
n4e0fc1b00b4.tq: Use the project-to-policy association and distinguish the State’s recent policy from older solar and green-hydrogen policies.
xs: The **SAEL 600 MW** Kadapa project is the first commissioned under **ICEP-2024** (**Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024**) — option **(4)**.
It was done in **11** months (May **2026**).
xa: Cost **₹3,000 crore**; land **2,400 acres**.
The **Tata 800 MW** hybrid (Jul **2026**) is also under ICEP-2024.
**Kadapa UMSP** (**1,000 MW**) is at **Galiveedu**.

nef963677f73.s: Which agency functions as the State nodal agency for renewable energy in Andhra Pradesh and handles land, clearances and single-window facilitation?
nef963677f73.x: NREDCAP is the State nodal agency for renewable energy and facilitates land, clearances and single-window services.
nef963677f73.tq: Identify the agency by its functional responsibility.
xs: **NREDCAP** is AP's **state nodal agency for RE** — land, clearances, single window — option **(1)**.
**APPDCL** = generation; **APSECM** = conservation; **APTRANSCO** = transmission.
xa: APTRANSCO has **13** ongoing **400 kV** works worth **₹3,698 crore**.
AP opened **50,000 acres** barren land for solar leases.

n0cf0334c5f8.s: The agency primarily associated with energy conservation in Andhra Pradesh is:
n0cf0334c5f8.x: APSECM is the agency associated with energy conservation.
n0cf0334c5f8.tq: Direct agency-role recall with closely related energy bodies as distractors.
xs: **APSECM** is AP's energy-conservation agency — option **(1)**.
**APGENCO** = generation; **NREDCAP** = RE nodal agency; **APTRANSCO** = transmission.
xa: APGENCO also runs the **Srisailam Right Bank** hydel plant.
APGENCO thermal: **4,210 MW**.

nbfa9b34bc68.s: Andhra Pradesh opened 50,000 acres of barren land for solar leases mainly to:
nbfa9b34bc68.x: The barren land was opened for solar leases to avoid diversion of farmland for renewable-energy projects.
xa: **NREDCAP** handles land, clearances and single window for RE.
SAEL **600 MW** Kadapa used **2,400 acres**.
PM-KUSUM in AP targets **2.93 lakh** farm pumps.

n27e639e5aae.s: According to the Andhra Pradesh renewable-energy mix of 10,639.75 MW, which one of the following correctly represents the approximate shares of solar and wind energy, respectively?
n27e639e5aae.x: Solar energy accounts for approximately 53% and wind energy for approximately 41% of Andhra Pradesh’s renewable-energy mix of 10,639.75 MW.
n27e639e5aae.tq: Split the options by comparing the order and approximate shares of the two energy sources.
xs: AP RE mix: **solar ~53%** and **wind ~41%** of **10,639.75 MW** — option **(2)**.
Option (4) reverses them.
xa: AP's solar is ~**5.6 GW** vs India's **162.15 GW** (Jun **2026**) — a small share.
Major **2025** wind partnership in **Anantapur** (**APPSC 2025**).
Tata **800 MW** hybrid: **400 MW** wind at **Kanekallu**.

ndcc7a42a3be.s: After bifurcation, Andhra Pradesh's coal-based power generation faced difficulty mainly because of:
o: A ban on new thermal power plants
Closure of its ports to imported coal
Transfer of its thermal plants to the Centre
Loss of coal mines, leading to long coal haulage and poor coal quality
ndcc7a42a3be.x: Andhra Pradesh lost its coal mines after bifurcation, causing long coal haulage and exposure to poor coal quality.
xa: APGENCO thermal: **4,210 MW** (NTTPS + RTPP).
**Krishnapatnam** SDSTPS (**APPDCL**): **2,400 MW**.

n9fddb649daf.s: With reference to PM-KUSUM in Andhra Pradesh, which one of the following figures represents the target number of farm pumps?
n9fddb649daf.x: PM-KUSUM in Andhra Pradesh targets 2.93 lakh farm pumps. The figure of 32,000 refers to solar pumps installed earlier.
n9fddb649daf.tq: Separate the target figure from the already-installed solar-pump figure before choosing the numerical option.
xs: PM-KUSUM in AP targets **2.93 lakh** farm pumps — option **(2)**.
**32,000** = solar pumps installed earlier; ~**5.6 GW** is AP's solar capacity.
xa: **123 MW** rooftop was installed earlier (**2024-25/2025-26**).
AP's 50,000-acre barren-land policy eases **food-vs-fuel** conflicts.

nb73d008cb8a.s: All the populations of different species living in an area together form a:
nb73d008cb8a.x: That is a community; a biome is a large region defined by climate and dominant vegetation.
xa: Order: **organism → population → community → ecosystem → biome → biosphere**.
The biosphere is absent at the **poles**, highest peaks and deepest oceans.

n6cfbd0b53ae.s: Which one of the following represents the correct ecological order from the smallest to the largest level?
o: Organism → community → population → ecosystem → biome → biosphere
Organism → population → community → ecosystem → biome → biosphere
Population → organism → community → biome → ecosystem → biosphere
Organism → ecosystem → population → community → biome → biosphere
n6cfbd0b53ae.x: The ecological order is organism, population, community, ecosystem, biome and biosphere.
n6cfbd0b53ae.tq: Check the hierarchy sequentially from the individual level upward.
xs: Order: **organism → population → community → ecosystem → biome → biosphere** — option **(2)**.
The others misplace community/population or ecosystem/biome.
xa: Full chain starts with **atoms → molecules → protoplasm → cells**.
"Ecology" was coined by **Ernst Haeckel (1869)**.
The **ecosystem** is the **basic functional unit of ecology**.

n49509864c22.s: The fundamental niche of a species refers to
o: the actual range occupied after competition
the full range of conditions and resources it could use in the absence of other species
n49509864c22.x: Fundamental niche is the potential range of conditions and resources available to a species when competition and other biological limitations are absent.
n49509864c22.tq: Distinguish potential range from actual range.
xs: The **fundamental niche** is the full range of conditions and resources a species could use **free from other species** — option **(4)** (**APPSC 2021**).
The range actually used under competition is the **realised niche** — option (1).
xa: **Niche breadth**: **specialists** (koala — eucalyptus) vs **generalists**.
**Hutchinson** gave the **n-dimensional niche** (**1957**).
Niche is **unique to each species**.

n4f0f2851bf6.s: A koala, which feeds mainly on eucalyptus, is best described as a
n4f0f2851bf6.x: A specialist uses a narrow range of resources. Dependence of the koala mainly on eucalyptus is an example of narrow niche breadth.
n4f0f2851bf6.tq: Infer niche breadth from the range of resources used.
xs: The koala, eating only **eucalyptus**, is a **specialist** with **narrow niche breadth** — option **(2)**.
**Generalists** (most animals) have broad niche breadth.
xa: **Fundamental niche** = range possible without other species; **realised niche** = range used under competition.
No two species occupy the **same niche**.

n1d66301dc99.s: The functional role ('profession') of a species in its habitat is called its:
n1d66301dc99.x: The niche is a species' functional role; it is unique to each species.
xa: Niche is set by habitat, food, reproduction and physical-chemical factors.
**Gause's competitive exclusion principle** relates to species competing for the same resource.
**Resource partitioning** lets competing species coexist.

n9a94262d135.s: Which of the following is NOT a population attribute?
n9a94262d135.x: Density, mortality, age structure and sex ratio are population attributes. Dominant vegetation is associated with the description of a biome.
n9a94262d135.tq: Find the item belonging to the neighbouring ecological level rather than the population level.
xs: **Dominant vegetation** is not a population attribute — option **(2)**; it defines a **biome**.
**Mortality**, **density** and **age structure** are population attributes (with **sex ratio**, **natality**).
xa: **J-curve** = exponential growth (dN/dt = rN).
**S-curve** = logistic growth to **carrying capacity K**.

nc3b576fa847.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the exchange characteristics of ecosystems and the Earth?
o: Ecosystems are open for energy and matter, while the Earth is open for energy but nearly closed for matter
Ecosystems are open only for matter, while the Earth is closed for energy
Ecosystems are closed for both energy and matter, while the Earth is open for both
Both ecosystems and the Earth are completely closed systems
nc3b576fa847.x: Ecosystems exchange both energy and matter with their surroundings. The Earth receives energy from outside but is nearly closed with respect to matter.
nc3b576fa847.tq: Compare open and closed characteristics across ecosystems and the Earth.
xs: Ecosystems are **open for energy and matter**; Earth is **open for energy** but **nearly closed for matter** — option **(1)**.
The other options wrongly call ecosystems or Earth closed for energy.
xa: Primary energy source = **Sun**; flow is **unidirectional**.
Energy flow obeys the **laws of thermodynamics**.

n0ea37b5a0f2.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the basic functional unit of ecology?
n0ea37b5a0f2.x: The ecosystem - a biotic community plus its non-living surroundings linked by energy flow and nutrient cycling - is the basic functional unit of ecology (APPSC PYQ). A population is one species in an area; a biome is a large climatic-vegetation region; the biosphere is the sum of all ecosystems.
xs: The **ecosystem** is the **basic functional unit of ecology** (APPSC PYQ) — option **(3)**.
A **population** is one species; a **biome** is a large climate-vegetation region; the **biosphere** is the top of the hierarchy.
xa: Term coined by **Tansley**, **1935**.
Functions: **energy flow** and **nutrient cycling**.

n54bfe19fe27.s: The rate of decomposition is likely to be fastest under which of the following conditions?
o: Detritus rich in nitrogen and sugars, with a warm and moist climate
Detritus rich in chitin, with cold and dry conditions
Detritus rich in lignin, with low temperature and anaerobic conditions
Detritus poor in nitrogen, with persistent waterlogging
n54bfe19fe27.x: Decomposition is rapid when detritus contains nitrogen and sugars and the climate is warm and moist. Lignin, chitin, low temperature and anaerobic conditions slow it down.
n54bfe19fe27.tq: Identify the combination of favourable and unfavourable decomposition conditions.
xs: Decay is fastest with detritus **rich in nitrogen and sugars** in a **warm and moist** climate — option **(1)**.
**Lignin**, **chitin**, **low temperature** and **anaerobic** conditions slow it.
xa: **Rainforest**: fast litter decay → thin, nutrient-poor soil.
**Taiga**: slow decay, thick litter, acidic soil.

n9f729dde065.s: Competing species may coexist when they
o: avoid all interaction with other species
use different parts or forms of a shared resource
n9f729dde065.x: Resource partitioning permits competing species to coexist by using different portions of a resource, such as different parts of the same plant.
n9f729dde065.tq: Apply the ecological principle of resource partitioning.
xs: Competitors coexist by **resource partitioning** — using **different parts of a shared resource** — option **(3)**.
Example: insect pests feeding on **different parts of the same plant**.
No two species occupy **exactly the same niche** (option 2).
xa: **Gause's competitive exclusion principle** governs competition (**-/-**).
Niche is **unique to each species** (**APPSC 2022**).

n04ea5342bd8.s: The sea star Pisaster ochraceus is regarded as a keystone species because it
n04ea5342bd8.x: Pisaster ochraceus is a keystone sea star that controls mussels in intertidal zones. This example is associated with the work of Robert Paine.
n04ea5342bd8.tq: Use the species–ecological effect association rather than the general definition alone.
xs: **Pisaster ochraceus** is keystone because it **controls mussels in intertidal zones** — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2024**).
It was studied by **Robert Paine**.
Building reefs is a **foundation** role (corals); SO2 indication is a **lichen** (indicator) role.
xa: Pisaster eating mussels is also an example of **predation** (+/-).
Other keystone species: **tiger, sea otter, fig**.

n6ee0eaf3314.s: Which one of the following is a foundation species?
n6ee0eaf3314.x: Foundation species create or shape the habitat itself; corals and kelp are examples.
n6ee0eaf3314.tq: Distinguish habitat-building species from charismatic and environmental-indicator species.
xs: **Coral** is a **foundation species** — it creates/shapes the habitat — option **(3)**.
**Lichens** and **amphibians** are **indicators**; the **giant panda** is a **flagship** species.
xa: Other foundation species: **kelp**, **dominant trees**.
Coral reefs are the **'rainforests of the sea'**.

nd914a486aae.s: The edge effect refers to the phenomenon in which an ecotone generally has
o: fewer species than either adjoining community
only species from the larger adjoining community
more species and higher density of some species than either adjoining community
nd914a486aae.x: The edge effect is the increased number of species and increased density of some species in an ecotone. Such organisms are called edge species.
nd914a486aae.tq: Use the comparison with adjoining communities to identify the edge effect.
xs: **Edge effect**: an ecotone has **more species** and **higher density of some species** than either community — option **(4)**.
Such species are called **edge species**.
xa: Example: higher **bird density** in the forest-desert ecotone.
Ecotone conditions are **intermediate**.

n713080be47d.s: Which one of the following does NOT belong to marine ecosystems?
n713080be47d.x: Rivers are freshwater ecosystems. Coral reefs, hydrothermal vents and tidal zones are marine ecosystems.
n713080be47d.tq: Find the freshwater item among marine ecosystem examples.
xs: A **river** is freshwater, not marine — option **(3)**.
**Tidal zones**, **hydrothermal vents** and **coral reefs** are marine.
xa: Rivers are **lotic** freshwater (**< 5 ppt**).
Vent food chains rest on **chemosynthetic bacteria**.

n96feb8659c1.s: Gloger’s rule primarily explains variation in which of the following characteristics in relation to climate?
n96feb8659c1.x: Gloger’s rule relates climate to colouration; warm and humid environments are generally associated with darker colouration.
n96feb8659c1.tq: Direct one-fact recall of a confusable rule-trait relationship.
xs: **Gloger's rule** explains **colouration** — warm-humid = **darker** — option **(3)**.
Body size = **Bergmann**; limbs = **Allen**; vertebrae = **Jordan**.
xa: **Rensch** = size dimorphism in **shorebirds**.
Asked in **APPSC 2024** as a match.

n708fe4fe52b.s: India launched its first guide to Open Natural Ecosystems at which international event and venue?
n708fe4fe52b.x: India launched its first guide to Open Natural Ecosystems at UNCCD COP17 in Ulaanbaatar.
n708fe4fe52b.tq: Match the document with the correct convention and venue.
xs: India launched its first **Open Natural Ecosystems** guide at **UNCCD COP17, Ulaanbaatar** (Aug **2026**) — option **(3)**.
The other events are not linked to this guide in the notes.
xa: ONEs = **grasslands, deserts, scrub**.
They cover over **10%** of India; less than **5%** protected.

nenvironment-25-1.s: Which term refers to the transition zone between two ecosystems or communities?
nenvironment-25-1.x: An ecotone is the transition zone where two ecosystems meet, such as forest and grassland. Lentic means still water, and a sere is a stage in succession.
nenvironment-25-1.tq: Discriminate ecotone, lentic, sere and anthrome.
n: An ecotone is a transition zone between two ecosystems or communities. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A sere is the entire sequence of communities that successively change in an area. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
Lentic water is still water. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
An anthropogenic biome is also called an anthrome. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
xs: The **ecotone** is the **transition zone** between **two ecosystems** or **communities** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Lentic** means **still water** (ponds, lakes, swamps).
A **sere** is the **entire sequence of communities** that successively change in an area; an **anthrome** is a **human-altered terrestrial biosphere**.
xa: Ecotones can be **narrow** (grassland-forest) or **wide** (forest-desert).
Ecotone examples: **mangroves** (marine and terrestrial), **estuary** (fresh and salt water), riverbank (dry and wet).
**Edge effect**: more species and higher density of some species in the ecotone — these are **edge species**.
A uniform stand of one forest type is **not** an ecotone.

nenvironment-25-9.s: The breaking of a continuous habitat into smaller isolated patches is called:
nenvironment-25-9.x: Habitat fragmentation breaks continuous habitat into small isolated patches.
n: Habitat fragmentation is the breaking of continuous habitat into smaller isolated patches. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
Species diversity is the variety of species. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
xa: **Endemic species** are **restricted** to a particular geographical area.
**Alien species** are introduced **outside** their natural range; invasive ones **adversely affect** native species.
**Ecological footprint** is measured in **global hectares**.

nenvironment-34-10.s: The niche concept is associated with:
nenvironment-34-10.x: Grinnell introduced the niche concept; Tansley coined 'ecosystem'.
n: The niche concept is associated with Grinnell. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 59-61]
The maximum sustainable population is called carrying capacity. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 59-61]
The biosphere comprises all ecosystems together. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 59-61]
xa: Niche proponents: **Grinnell** (**1917**, habitat niche), **Elton** (**1927**, functional niche), **Hutchinson** (**1957**, n-dimensional).
The biosphere is **absent** at the poles, highest peaks and deepest oceans.
⚠ Habitat = **address**; niche = **profession**.

n8600c3f7243.s: Ramdeo Misra is popularly known as the
n8600c3f7243.x: Ramdeo Misra is recognised as the father of Indian ecology.
n8600c3f7243.tq: Test a national attribution against similarly worded ecological titles.
xs: **Ramdeo Misra** = **father of Indian ecology** — option **(4)**.
**Odum** = father of modern ecosystem ecology; **Hutchinson** = n-dimensional niche.
xa: **Elton** wrote **Animal Ecology (1927)**.
**Haeckel** coined "ecology"; **Tansley** coined "ecosystem" (**1935**).

nenvironment-25-4.x: Eduard Suess coined 'biosphere' (1875); Tansley coined 'ecosystem' and Dasmann 'biological diversity'.
n: Edward Suess is associated with the biosphere reserve. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A.G. Tansley is associated with the ecosystem. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
Reiter is associated with ecology. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
Ernst Haeckel is associated with ecology. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
Raymond F. Dasmann is associated with biodiversity. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
xa: **Lindeman** — the **10% law** of energy transfer (**1942**).
**Grinnell** — the **niche** concept (**1917**); **Elton** — functional niche (**1927**); **Hutchinson** — n-dimensional niche (**1957**).
**E.P. Odum** — Fundamentals of Ecology (**1953**); **H.C. Cowles** — ecological succession (**1899**).
⚠ Haeckel coined "ecology" — the notes give **1869** and **1866** in different places.

ncfbe41024e2.s: Nutrients, water and air form which component of the environment?
ncfbe41024e2.x: Nutrients, water and air form the physical component; carbon and nitrogen cycles are its chemical interactions.
xa: Categories of environment: **physical** (lithosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere), **biotic** (plants, animals, microbes) and **cultural** (man-made).
Primary functions: **provide resources**, **assimilate wastes**, and give **habitat** for biodiversity.
⚠ Trap: **"generating synthetic chemicals"** is **NOT** a function of the environment (APPSC **2024**).
**Habitat** always has life and suits one species; the **environment** may not have life.

n158ef682613.s: Which of the following is included in the cultural category of the environment?
n158ef682613.x: The cultural environment is man-made and includes social, economic and political aspects.
n158ef682613.tq: Identify the man-made category rather than a natural component.
xs: **Political institutions** fall in the **cultural** (man-made) category — option **(2)**.
Cultural = **social, economic, political**; wild animals are **biotic**; atmospheric gases and soil minerals are **physical**.
xa: Physical = **lithosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere**.
Biotic = **plants, animals, microbes**.
Functions: resources, **assimilating wastes**, habitat for biodiversity.

ne2480305e8f.s: Which one of the following is NOT a primary function of the environment?
ne2480305e8f.x: The primary functions of the environment are providing resources, assimilating wastes and serving as a habitat for biodiversity. Generating synthetic chemicals is not one of them (APPSC 2024 trap).
ne2480305e8f.tq: Resources, waste assimilation, habitat - synthetic chemicals is the odd one out.
xs: **Generating synthetic chemicals** is NOT a function — option **(3)** (**APPSC 2024** trap).
The primary functions: **provide resources**, **assimilate wastes**, **habitat for biodiversity**.
xa: Environment includes **physical**, **biotic** and **cultural** categories.
Environment is **never static**.

n643440725e0.s: Which one of the following represents a functional process of an ecosystem rather than its structure?
n643440725e0.x: Nutrient cycling is an ecosystem function. Species composition, trophic levels and abiotic materials are elements of ecosystem structure.
n643440725e0.tq: Discriminate between the structure and function columns of an ecosystem.
xs: **Nutrient cycling** is a **function** — option **(2)**.
**Trophic levels**, **abiotic materials** and **species composition** are **structure**.
xa: Other functions: **energy flow** (one-way from the sun), primary and secondary production, self-regulation.
Nutrients **cycle** (biogeochemical cycles); energy **flows one way**.

n6310b2896e0.s: An abiotic factor is best defined as which one of the following?
o: An organism that obtains food from dead organic matter
Any non-living component that affects organisms or their environment
A living component occupying the highest trophic level
A biological interaction between two species
n6310b2896e0.x: An abiotic factor is any non-living component that affects organisms or their environment, such as light, temperature, water or soil.
n6310b2896e0.tq: Use the precise definition rather than examples alone.
xs: An **abiotic factor** is **any non-living component that affects organisms or their environment** (**APPSC 2018**) — option **(2)**.
Feeding on dead matter = **saprotrophs**; species interactions are biotic.
xa: Types: **climatic**, **edaphic** (soil), **topographic**.
Abiotic factors can be **limiting or enabling**.

n1db5895986c.s: Soil texture, pH and minerals are ____ factors.
n1db5895986c.x: Edaphic factors relate to soil; climatic are light, temperature and rainfall, and topographic are altitude, slope and aspect.
xa: Climatic factors also include **humidity** and **wind**.
**Liebig** = law of the **minimum**; **Shelford** = law of **tolerance**.

nacdb48b44e4.x: Saprotrophs feed on dead matter; reptiles are cold-blooded, humans omnivores and camels desert-adapted.
xa: Detritivores: **earthworms**, nematodes, arthropods.
Desert fauna: camels, lizards, snakes, scorpions — mostly **nocturnal**.

n7a5273f947a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about producers in ecosystems?
o: At deep-sea vents, chemosynthetic sulphur bacteria are the producers
In aquatic ecosystems, zooplankton are the main producers
In terrestrial ecosystems, herbs, shrubs and trees are producers
In aquatic ecosystems, phytoplankton and algae are producers
n7a5273f947a.x: Zooplankton are primary consumers; aquatic producers are phytoplankton, algae and submerged and floating plants.
xa: **Diatoms and cyanobacteria** are **ocean producers**; the **copepod** is a **primary consumer**.
**Photoautotrophs** use sunlight (green plants, algae, cyanobacteria); **chemoautotrophs** use chemical oxidation (e.g. **nitrifying bacteria**).
Chemoautotrophic **bacteria in deep ocean trenches** use **hydrogen sulphide** from sea-floor cracks.
Decomposers (**saprotrophs / osmotrophs**) are **bacteria and fungi**; detritivores include earthworms, nematodes, arthropods.

n684f06cfc45.s: Chemoautotrophic bacteria in deep ocean trenches obtain energy by oxidising which substance released from sea-floor cracks?
n684f06cfc45.x: Chemoautotrophic bacteria in deep ocean trenches use hydrogen sulphide released from sea-floor cracks as an energy source.
xa: Other chemoautotrophs: **nitrifying bacteria**; **methanogen** archaea.
Vent chains rest on **chemosynthetic bacteria**.

ne94cd30527d.s: Decomposers are regarded as a link between the biotic and abiotic components because they:
o: Convert dead organic matter into inorganic nutrients reused by producers
Prevent nutrient cycling in the soil
ne94cd30527d.x: Decomposers release inorganic nutrients from dead organic matter, making them available again to producers and linking living and non-living components.
ne94cd30527d.tq: Apply the link concept by tracing nutrients from dead organisms back to producers.
xs: Decomposers turn dead matter into **inorganic nutrients reused by producers** — option **(1)** — so they are the **link between biotic and abiotic** parts.
They drive, not prevent, nutrient cycling.
xa: Main decomposers: **bacteria and fungi** (saprotrophs / osmotrophs).
Nutrients **cycle** (biogeochemical cycles); energy flows **one way**.
⚠ Decomposers get **no place** in ecological pyramids despite their role.

o: Slow decay, thick litter and acidic soil
Thin, nutrient-poor soil due to fast decay
Fast decay and highly fertile soil
n6a53bd4d3e4.x: Taiga has slow decay, thick litter and acidic soil; fast decay and thin, poor soil mark tropical rainforests.
xa: Forest types: **tropical rainforest**, tropical deciduous (**monsoon**), temperate deciduous, **taiga / boreal** (evergreen coniferous).
The rainforest has the **highest species richness on land**.
Mature forests give little **net oxygen** (respiration balances photosynthesis) but are vital **carbon sinks**.

n0412eaebe11.s: Which of the following is NOT a typical adaptation of desert flora?
o: Broad, thin leaves that increase water loss
n0412eaebe11.x: Desert plants commonly have deep roots, small or spiny leaves and waxy cuticles. Broad, thin leaves would generally increase water loss.
n0412eaebe11.tq: Identify the option that contradicts the water-conservation principle.
xs: **Broad, thin leaves** are not a desert adaptation — option **(2)**; they would lose water.
Desert plants have **deep roots**, **small or spiny leaves** and a **waxy cuticle**.
xa: **Xerophytes** also show sunken stomata, succulence and **CAM** (e.g. **Opuntia**).
Desert fauna are mostly **nocturnal** and water-saving.

n1c640b8d7c5.s: Which lake zone is characterised by shallow water, light reaching the bottom and rooted plants?
n1c640b8d7c5.x: The littoral zone is the shallow edge of a lake where light reaches the bottom and rooted plants commonly grow.
n1c640b8d7c5.tq: Match the zone with its physical features and vegetation.
xs: The **littoral zone** is the shallow edge where light reaches the bottom, with **rooted plants** — option **(1)**.
**Limnetic** = open sunlit water with plankton; **profundal** = deep dark water; **aphotic** is a marine zone.
xa: Lake trophic status: **oligotrophic**, mesotrophic, **eutrophic**.
⚠ **Lentic** = still water; **lotic** = flowing water.

n3adc6e8fb96.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the profundal zone of a lake?
o: Deep, dark water below the limnetic zone with decomposers
Sunlit open water dominated by plankton
n3adc6e8fb96.x: The profundal zone lies below the limnetic zone, is deep and dark, does not support photosynthesis, and is associated with decomposers.
n3adc6e8fb96.tq: Use the vertical sequence of lake zones to identify the deepest zone.
xs: The **profundal zone** is **deep, dark water below the limnetic zone** with **decomposers** — option **(2)**.
No photosynthesis happens there.
xa: **Littoral** = shallow edge with rooted plants; **limnetic** = sunlit open water with plankton.
**Eutrophic** lakes have **low oxygen at depth**.

n03d99637804.s: Energy flow and nutrient cycling, which underlie productivity and ecosystem services, are aspects of:
n03d99637804.x: Ecosystem function includes processes such as energy flow and nutrient cycling, which support productivity and services.
xa: Energy flows **one way**; nutrients **cycle**.
The **10% law** explains why a plant-based diet supports more people per hectare.

nbiology-61-2-14.s: A lichen is a symbiotic association of:
nbiology-61-2-14.x: Lichen is fungus with algae or cyanobacteria; fungus with plant roots is mycorrhiza.
n: Mycorrhiza consists of fungi and plant roots. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61-2 · pp 114-116]
Lichen consists of fungi and algae or cyanobacteria. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61-2 · pp 114-116]
Coral symbiosis involves a cnidarian and dinoflagellate algae. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61-2 · pp 114-116]
The ant cultivates the fungus as food. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61-2 · pp 114-116]
Ant–fungus symbiosis involves an ant and a fungus. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61-2 · pp 114-116]
xa: **Fig association**: a **fig** and a specific **fig wasp** — a **highly specific pollination** relationship.
**Rhizobium**: a **bacterium** associated with **legumes**.
**Lichens** are **indicators** of **air pollution** (SO2).

nbiology-62-13.x: Lichens are sensitive to SO₂ and so indicate air pollution.
n: Lichen is an indicator of air pollution. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 116-118]
Diatoms and cyanobacteria are ocean producers. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #62 · pp 116-118]
xa: The **copepod** is a **primary consumer**.
Aquatic producers: **phytoplankton**, algae, submerged and floating plants.
Other **indicator species**: **amphibians**; indicators signal **environmental health**.
**Lichen** = **fungi** + **algae or cyanobacteria** — a **mutualistic** association.

nbiology-53-7.s: Plants that send deep roots down to groundwater are called:
nbiology-53-7.x: Phreatophytes have deep roots reaching groundwater; hydrophytes have buoyant aerenchyma.
n: Xerophytes have reduced water loss. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 92-95]
Phreatophytes inhabit groundwater zones. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 92-95]
Phreatophytes have deep roots. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 92-95]
Cactus has leaves modified into spines. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 92-95]
Cactus stores water. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 92-95]
Pitcher plants have insectivory as an adaptation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 92-95]
xa: The **cactus** lives in a **xeric habitat**; xerophytes use **CAM**.
**Pitcher plants** grow in **nitrogen-poor soil**.
Hydrophytes: reduced roots, thin cuticle, floating leaves with stomata on the **upper surface** (e.g. **Hydrilla**, lotus).

nbiology-53-18.s: Plants associated with saline habitats and salt tolerance are called:
nbiology-53-18.x: Halophytes tolerate salt; xerophytes reduce water loss in deserts and phreatophytes root deep to groundwater.
n: Xerophytes inhabit dry or desert habitats. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 92-95]
Xerophytes have reduced water loss. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 92-95]
Hydrophytes inhabit aquatic or wetland habitats. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 92-95]
Hydrophytes have aerenchyma. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 92-95]
Halophytes inhabit saline habitats. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 92-95]
Halophytes have salt tolerance. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 92-95]
Phreatophytes inhabit groundwater zones. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 92-95]
Phreatophytes have deep roots. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 92-95]
xa: Halophytes: **pneumatophores** (breathing roots) and **vivipary** (seeds germinate on the tree), e.g. **Rhizophora**.
**Epiphytes** grow on another plant for **physical support** and get moisture from their surroundings.
Halophytes cope with **salt spray** and saline roots (APPSC **2024**: both A and R correct, R explains A).

nbiology-53-22.s: Pitcher plants are characteristically associated with which type of soil?
nbiology-53-22.x: Pitcher plants grow in nitrogen-poor soils and make up for it by trapping and digesting insects.
nbiology-53-22.tq: Recall why insectivorous plants trap insects.
n: Pitcher plants grow in nitrogen-poor soil. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 92-95]
xs: Pitcher plants grow in **nitrogen-poor soil** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They are **insectivorous** — **insectivory** is their adaptation to make up for the poor soil.
**Dry/desert** soil suits **xerophytes**, **aquatic/wetland** suits **hydrophytes**, and **saline** soil suits **halophytes**.
xa: **Nepenthes** is the **tropical pitcher plant**.
**Cuscuta** is a **parasitic angiosperm**; **pea** has **tendrils**.
**Cactus** lives in a **xeric habitat** with **leaves modified into spines**.

nenvironment-25-7.s: Ponds, lakes and swamps are examples of:
nenvironment-25-7.x: Ponds, lakes and swamps are lentic (still water); rivers and streams are lotic (flowing water).
n: Ponds are examples of lentic environments. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
Lakes are examples of lentic environments. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
Swamps are examples of lentic environments. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
Lotic water is flowing water. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
Rivers are examples of lotic environments. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
Streams are examples of lotic environments. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
xa: ⚠ **Lentic** = still; **lotic** = flowing.
Freshwater covers about **0.8%** of Earth's surface (also cited as **1.8%**) and holds **0.009%** of its water.
Lake zones: **littoral** (shallow, rooted plants), **limnetic** (open sunlit water), **profundal** (deep, dark).
Trophic status: **oligotrophic** (nutrient-poor) vs **eutrophic** (nutrient-rich, algal blooms).

nenvironment-31-4.s: Secondary consumers occupy which trophic level?
nenvironment-31-4.x: Producers are 1st, primary consumers 2nd, secondary consumers 3rd and top carnivores 4th.
n: Producers occupy the first trophic level. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 55-56]
Primary consumers occupy the second trophic level. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 55-56]
Secondary consumers occupy the third trophic level. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 55-56]
Tertiary consumers or top carnivores occupy the fourth trophic level. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 55-56]
Top carnivores occupy the highest trophic level. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #31 · pp 55-56]
xa: Detritivores and decomposers recycle all levels — **not a single slot**.
A chain like "tiger, grass, snake, frog" has **no herbivore** — the **second level** is missing (PYQ **2025**).
Chains rarely exceed **4-5 trophic levels**.

nenvironment-34-6.s: An ecosystem, which exchanges energy and matter with its surroundings, is a(n):
nenvironment-34-6.x: An ecosystem is an open system, made of abiotic parts, producers, consumers and decomposers.
n: An ecosystem is an open system. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 59-61]
The components of an ecosystem are abiotic components, producers, consumers, and decomposers. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 59-61]
xa: ⚠ The **Earth** is open for **energy** but **nearly closed** for **matter**.
Main processes: **energy flow** and **nutrient cycling**.
Term "ecosystem": **Arthur Tansley**, **1935**.

nenvironment-34-7.x: Herbivores are on the second level; top carnivores occupy the highest.
n: Top carnivores occupy the highest trophic level. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 59-61]
Bacteria are main decomposers. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 59-61]
Fungi are main decomposers. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 59-61]
xa: Decomposers form the base of the **detritus** food chain and recycle all levels.
Detritivores like **earthworms** **fragment** dead matter.
**Microorganisms** collectively **recycle nutrients**.

nenvironment-33-12.s: Which of the following is true of an ecosystem?
o: It cycles nutrients and has its own productivity
It has a fixed universal boundary
nenvironment-33-12.x: An ecosystem cycles nutrients, has its own productivity and has no fixed universal boundary.
n: Nutrient cycling is a main process in an ecosystem. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
An ecosystem has its own productivity. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
An ecosystem has no fixed universal boundary. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
xa: Components: **abiotic components**, **producers**, **consumers**, **decomposers**.
**Structure** = what is there (species composition, trophic levels); **function** = energy flow, nutrient cycling, production, self-regulation.
Ecosystems are **open** for energy and matter.

nbiology-65-20.s: Which group of microorganisms acts as the main decomposers of dead organic matter?
nbiology-65-20.x: Saprophytic fungi and bacteria are the main decomposers, breaking dead matter down and recycling nutrients. Lactobacillus makes curd, while Rhizobium and Anabaena fix nitrogen.
nbiology-65-20.tq: Pick the saprophytes among microbes known for other jobs.
n: Fungi perform decomposition. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
xs: **Saprophytic fungi and bacteria** are the **main decomposers** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Bacteria** and **fungi** **decompose organic matter** into **inorganic nutrients reused by producers**.
Decomposers (**saprotrophs / osmotrophs**) are the **link between biotic and abiotic** parts.
xa: Helpers: **earthworms**, nematodes, arthropods (**detritivores**).
Steps: **fragmentation** → **leaching** → **catabolism** → **humification** → **mineralisation**.
Decomposition is **slow** with **lignin, chitin**, low temperature and **anaerobic** conditions.

n76e7e6b50dd.s: A detritus food chain begins with:
n76e7e6b50dd.x: Detritus chains begin with dead organic matter; grazing chains begin with living green plants.
xa: ⚠ "Grazing chain begins with dead leaves" = **false** (**APPSC-G2 2025**).
Grazing example: **grass → goat → human** (**PYQ 2025**).

nc6a3b9ef4c3.s: A food chain beginning with leaf litter and proceeding through earthworms to birds is classified as a:
nc6a3b9ef4c3.x: A detritus food chain starts with dead organic matter such as leaf litter and proceeds through detritivores such as earthworms to higher consumers.
nc6a3b9ef4c3.tq: Distinguish the two chains by asking whether the first component is living vegetation or dead organic matter.
xs: **Leaf litter → earthworm → bird** is a **detritus food chain** — option **(1)**.
A detritus chain begins with **dead organic matter**; a **grazing** chain begins with **living green plants**.
xa: Detritivores and decomposers form the **base of the detritus chain** and recycle all levels.
Grazing example: **grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → eagle** (UPSC).

n1bbc66b1b30.s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence in an aquatic food chain?
o: Zooplankton → phytoplankton → large fish → small fish
Large fish → small fish → zooplankton → phytoplankton
Phytoplankton → zooplankton → small fish → large fish
Small fish → phytoplankton → zooplankton → large fish
n1bbc66b1b30.x: Phytoplankton are producers, zooplankton are primary consumers, and small and large fish occupy progressively higher trophic positions.
n1bbc66b1b30.tq: Arrange the organisms from producer to successively larger consumers.
xs: Aquatic sequence: **phytoplankton → zooplankton → small fish → large fish** — option **(3)**.
Phytoplankton are **producers of the sea**; zooplankton are **primary consumers**.
xa: Pond: **phytoplankton → zooplankton → fish**, with bacteria/fungi as decomposers.
Grassland: **grass → grasshopper/rabbit → snake/hawk**.

na6a6b6b9556.s: Which of the following does NOT occupy the first trophic level?
na6a6b6b9556.x: Zooplankton are primary consumers at the second level; phytoplankton, seaweeds and green plants are producers.
xa: **Chemosynthetic bacteria** (at hydrothermal vents) are also T1 producers.
T3 = carnivores (**secondary consumers**); T4 = top carnivores.

nfef300c2fed.s: Why can the biomass pyramid in an aquatic ecosystem be inverted?
o: Fish do not consume zooplankton in aquatic ecosystems.
Energy increases at every aquatic trophic level.
Phytoplankton have a small standing crop but rapidly support larger zooplankton and fish biomass.
nfef300c2fed.x: Phytoplankton have a small standing crop but reproduce and are consumed rapidly, allowing them to support a larger standing biomass of zooplankton and fish.
nfef300c2fed.tq: Distinguish standing biomass from productivity and identify the fast-turnover producer explanation.
xs: **Phytoplankton** have a **small standing crop** but turn over fast, supporting larger **zooplankton/fish** biomass — option **(4)**.
So the **biomass pyramid** is inverted in the **sea**.
xa: On land (forest, grassland) the biomass pyramid is **upright**.
**Energy pyramid** is never inverted.

na0db54186dc.s: DDT contamination in aquatic food chains is most directly associated with:
o: Thinning of bird eggshells and crashes in seabird populations
na0db54186dc.x: DDT causes thinning of bird eggshells and has been associated with crashes in seabird populations.
xa: ⚠ Mercury → **Minamata disease**; DDT → **eggshell thinning**.
DDT is **persistent and fat-soluble**.

n370fcb08c0c.s: The association between a fig tree and a fig wasp is an example of
n370fcb08c0c.x: The fig wasp pollinates the fig and obtains a breeding site, making the association a coevolved mutualistic relationship.
n370fcb08c0c.tq: Apply the benefit-benefit relationship to a specialised natural association.
xs: **Fig and fig wasp** is **coevolved mutualism** (+/+) — option **(1)**: pollination in return for a **breeding site**.
Amensalism (-/0) and neutralism (0/0) do not fit.
xa: Other coevolved pairs: **yucca – yucca moth**; **Ophrys orchid – bee**.
**Lichen** (alga + fungus) is also mutualism.

nbiology-61-8.s: Lithophytes are plants that grow on:
nbiology-61-8.x: Lithophytes grow on rocks; hydrophytes grow in water and epiphytes on other plants for support.
n: Hydrophytes inhabit aquatic habitats. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 112-114]
Lithophytes inhabit rocks. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 112-114]
Epiphytes grow on another plant mainly for physical support. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 112-114]
Cuscuta grows on host plants as a stem parasite. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 112-114]
xa: Hydrophytes have **aerenchyma** (air-filled tissue), reduced roots and thin cuticle (e.g. **Hydrilla**, lotus).
Epiphytes get **moisture and nutrients** from their **surroundings**.
**Cuscuta** is a **parasitic angiosperm**; its parasitism is a **+/-** interaction.
**Phreatophytes** live in **groundwater zones** with **deep roots**.

nbiology-61-2-11.s: Each fig species is pollinated by its own specific:
nbiology-61-2-11.x: The fig association is a highly specific pollination relationship between a fig and a specific wasp.
n: Fig association involves a fig and a specific wasp. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61-2 · pp 114-116]
Fig association is a highly specific pollination relationship. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61-2 · pp 114-116]
The ant cultivates the fungus as food. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61-2 · pp 114-116]
Ant–fungus symbiosis involves an ant and a fungus. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61-2 · pp 114-116]
xa: Coevolved plant-pollinator pairs: **fig - fig wasp**, **yucca - yucca moth**, **Ophrys orchid - bee** (sexual deceit).
In mutualism the fig wasp gets a **breeding site** for pollination (**+/+**).
**Protozoan symbiosis**: protozoa with **bacteria, algae or animals** — **mutualistic associations**.

n: Azotobacter performs free-living nitrogen fixation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
Decomposer bacteria break down organic matter. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
Bacteria perform decomposition. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
xa: Decomposition steps: **fragmentation** → **leaching** → **catabolism** → **humification** → **mineralisation**.
Decomposers break dead matter into **inorganic nutrients reused by producers** — the **link between biotic and abiotic** parts.
Decomposition is **fast** with nitrogen- and sugar-rich detritus in **warm and moist** climate; **slow** with **lignin, chitin**, low temperature and **anaerobic** conditions.

nfa1a70723c7.s: In the carbon cycle, CO₂ is taken up from the atmosphere by:
nfa1a70723c7.x: Photosynthesis takes up CO₂, while respiration, decay and combustion release it.
xa: The carbon cycle is **CO₂ exchange** through **biological processes**.
Mature forests are vital **carbon sinks**.
The **water cycle** is driven by **solar energy**; the **phosphorus cycle** involves **rock weathering**.

ne7b4ebce995.s: Which of the following does NOT belong to the physical category of the environment?
ne7b4ebce995.x: Lithosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere are physical; microbes are biotic.
xa: **Cultural** category = man-made: social, economic, political.
Composite nature: physical + biological + chemical interactions.
⚠ "Generating synthetic chemicals" is **NOT** a function of the environment (**APPSC 2024**).

nca65e72e59a.s: Which of the following may exist even in the absence of life?
nca65e72e59a.x: A habitat always has life and suits a particular species, whereas the environment may exist without life.
xa: One habitat can hold **many species**.
All habitats are environments; **not all environments are habitats**.
⚠ Habitat = **"address"**; niche = **"profession"**.

n120732b839c.s: Which of the following is correct about habitat and environment?
o: A habitat can contain only one species
Habitat is a broader concept than environment
n120732b839c.x: A habitat is a particular place within the broader environment, so all habitats are environments; one habitat may contain many species.
xa: A habitat always has **life**; an environment may not.
Habitat = **address**; niche = **profession**.

n013fbf155a8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about population growth?
o: A J-shaped curve shows growth that levels off at carrying capacity
Carrying capacity is the maximum population an environment can sustain
A J-shaped curve shows exponential growth with unlimited resources
An S-shaped curve shows logistic growth levelling off at carrying capacity K
n013fbf155a8.x: The J-curve is exponential growth (dN/dt = rN); levelling off at K belongs to the S-curve.
xa: **Natality** = births; rate = **individuals produced per female per unit time**; **mortality** = deaths per unit time.
Age pyramids: **triangular** = expanding; **bell** = stable; **urn** = declining.
**r-selected** species: many small offspring, little care (insects, weeds); **K-selected**: few large offspring, much care, near **K** (elephants, humans).

nf9eb63d6cc5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about r-selected and K-selected species?
o: K-selected species produce few large offspring with considerable parental care
Elephants and humans commonly show K-selected characteristics
nf9eb63d6cc5.x: Weeds, like insects, commonly show r-selected characteristics.
xa: r-selected: many small offspring, short life, **unstable habitats**.
K-selected species live **near K** (carrying capacity).

n473f1a0f434.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the components of an ecosystem?
o: Fire and gravity may function as abiotic factors
Parasites and symbionts are abiotic components
Topography and wind are abiotic components
n473f1a0f434.x: Parasites and symbionts are living, biotic components.
xa: Biotic list: green plants, non-green plants, **decomposers**, parasites, symbionts, animals, man.
Abiotic list also has energy, temperature, water, **soil**.

n0d7ad132808.s: The law stating that growth is limited by the nutrient in shortest supply is:
n0d7ad132808.x: Liebig's law; Shelford's law of tolerance says both too little and too much of a factor can limit an organism.
xa: ⚠ Liebig = **minimum**; Shelford = **tolerance** (too little and too much).
**Abiotic factor**: any **non-living** component that affects organisms or their environment (APPSC **2018**).
Abiotic factor types: **climatic** (light, temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind), **edaphic** (soil) and **topographic** (altitude, slope, aspect).
Abiotic factors can be **limiting or enabling** for the distribution of organisms.

ne088c2b8bde.s:
Which of the following is the correct sequence of decomposition processes?

1. Fragmentation
2. Leaching
3. Catabolism
4. Humification
5. Mineralisation
ne088c2b8bde.x: Decomposition proceeds through fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification and mineralisation.
ne088c2b8bde.tq: Arrange the decomposition stages in their process sequence.
xs: Order: **fragmentation → leaching → catabolism → humification → mineralisation** — option **(1)**.
**Fragmentation** is by detritivores like **earthworms**; **leaching** moves soluble nutrients into soil; **catabolism** uses enzymes of **bacteria and fungi**.
xa: Fast decay: detritus rich in **nitrogen and sugars**, **warm and moist** climate.
Slow decay: **lignin, chitin**, low temperature, **anaerobic** conditions.

n811e6e03289.s: The principal decomposers in an ecosystem are:
n811e6e03289.x: Bacteria and fungi are the main decomposers whose enzymes carry out catabolism; earthworms, nematodes and arthropods are helpers.
xa: Steps: fragmentation → leaching → catabolism → **humification** → **mineralisation**.
Decomposers are the **link between biotic and abiotic** parts.

n54bbf9149cf.s: Energy flow in an ecosystem is:
n54bbf9149cf.x: Energy flows in one direction and obeys the laws of thermodynamics; nutrients, not energy, are cycled.
xa: First law: energy is **transformed**, not created or destroyed.
Second law: every transfer **loses energy as heat**.

na0721063f1c.s: Which organisms receive no place in ecological pyramids despite their vital role?
na0721063f1c.x: Ecological pyramids omit saprophytes and decomposers; they also cannot place one species at two trophic levels.
xa: Pyramids also assume a **simple chain** and do not show food webs.
Numbers are **hard to count**.

n4ac2a29ba1a.s: The relationship between a tiger and a deer is an example of:
n4ac2a29ba1a.x: Tiger and deer illustrate predation, not competition.
xa: **Competition** = -/-, explained by **Gause's** principle.
⚠ Commensalism = **+/0** (cattle egret); amensalism = **-/0** (Penicillium).

nc932b011c1c.s: A large tree shading a small plant is an example of:
nc932b011c1c.x: It is amensalism (-/0); a lichen is mutualism and the cattle egret near cattle is commensalism.
xa: **Parasitism** (+/-) examples: **Cuscuta** on host plants; ticks and lice.
⚠ Commensalism = **+/0**; amensalism = **-/0** (**Penicillium**).

n83b3cf273ea.s: Which of the following is NOT a natural terrestrial ecosystem?
n83b3cf273ea.x: Tundra, forest, grassland, desert and mountain are terrestrial ecosystems; an estuary is aquatic.
xa: Aquatic ecosystems are split by **salinity**: freshwater, brackish, marine.
Forest types: **tropical rainforest**, tropical deciduous, temperate deciduous, **taiga**.

n3cea8f234cf.s: Mature forests provide little net oxygen because:
o: They are no longer carbon sinks
n3cea8f234cf.x: In mature forests respiration roughly balances photosynthesis, though they remain important carbon sinks.
xa: Forest types: **tropical rainforest**, tropical deciduous (monsoon), temperate deciduous, **taiga**.
**Taiga** has slow decay, thick litter and **acidic soil**.

n98eeb6bad44.s: Which of the following is a cold desert?
n98eeb6bad44.x: Ladakh and the Gobi are cold deserts; the Thar of western Rajasthan and Kutch is a hot desert.
xa: The **Sahara** is a hot desert.
Desert flora: **cacti, succulents**, thorny species.

n279eb8d7d21.s: Steppe is the temperate grassland of:
n279eb8d7d21.x: Steppe is the Eurasian temperate grassland; Australia's grasslands are the Downs.
xa: **Veld** = South Africa; **Pampas** = Argentina.
Grasslands were called one of the **most threatened biomes** (Jan **2026**).

o: Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha
Himalayan foothills of Uttarakhand and Assam
Western Ghats of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu
ndece43c596d.x: Shola occurs in the Western Ghats; the tall wet Terai grasslands lie along the Himalayan foothills.
xa: **Banni** grassland is in **Kutch, Gujarat** — one of **Asia's largest natural grasslands** (about **2,600 sq km**).
Banni has been a **Reserve Forest** since **1955**; its threat is the invasive **Prosopis juliflora**.
World grasslands: **Prairie** (North America), **Pampas** (Argentina), **Steppe** (Eurasia), **Veld** (South Africa), **Downs** (Australia).

ncf311c9c019.s: The main invasive threat to the Banni grassland of Kutch is:
ncf311c9c019.x: The invasive threat named for Banni is Prosopis juliflora, not Lantana camara.
xa: One of **Asia's largest natural grasslands** (about **2,600 sq km**); Reserve Forest since **1955**.
Gujarat released **20 blackbucks** into Banni (Aug **2026**).

nd213158eeab.x: Eutrophic lakes are nutrient-rich and may develop algal blooms; oxygen at depth is often low.
xa: **Oligotrophic** lakes are clear and **oxygen-rich**.
The deep **profundal** zone has no photosynthesis; decomposers dominate.

nd4bda069f2b.s: The open water column of the ocean is called the:
nd4bda069f2b.x: The open water column is the pelagic zone; the benthic zone is the sea floor and its organisms.
xa: The **epipelagic** (top of the pelagic) holds the most marine habitats.
**Hydrothermal vents** are deep-sea habitats run on **chemosynthetic bacteria**.

ndf8a68b9408.s: Which of the following are functions of wetlands?
o: Water purification and carbon storage only
Flood moderation, water purification, biodiversity conservation and carbon storage
ndf8a68b9408.x: Wetlands moderate floods, purify water, conserve biodiversity and store carbon.
xa: Protected in India by the **Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017**.
**Ramsar Convention** signed **1971** at Ramsar, Iran.
**World Wetlands Day**: **2 February**.

nf2ab92df610.s: India became a party to the Ramsar Convention in:
nf2ab92df610.x: India joined in 1982; the Convention was signed in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran.
xa: Parties designate sites and practise **wise use**.
**World Wetlands Day** (**2 February**) marks the signing date.

n507a8656d20.s: A thick cuticle, sunken stomata and CAM are features of:
n507a8656d20.x: These are xerophyte (desert) features; hydrophytes have a thin cuticle, aerenchyma, reduced roots and floating leaves.
xa: Examples: **Rhizophora** (halophyte), **Opuntia** (xerophyte), **Hydrilla, lotus** (hydrophytes).
⚠ **Pneumatophores**, **vivipary** = halophytes; **aerenchyma** = hydrophytes; **CAM** = xerophytes.

n27a252a5219.s: Hydrilla is an example of a:
n27a252a5219.x: Hydrilla is an aquatic plant (hydrophyte); Opuntia is a xerophyte and Rhizophora a halophyte.
xa: **Lotus** is another hydrophyte.
Hydrophyte leaves have **stomata on the upper surface**.
Halophytes grow in **saline soils, estuaries, mangroves**.

n922c0b4e0e2.s: Which ecogeographic rule relates colder climates with shorter ears and limbs?
n922c0b4e0e2.x: Allen's rule concerns appendage length; Bergmann's concerns body size and Rensch's sexual size dimorphism.
xa: **Jordan** = vertebrae in fish; **Gloger** = colouration.
**APPSC 2024** matched these rules: colouration-Gloger, vertebrae-Jordan, body size-Bergmann, shorebirds-Rensch.

nf94f991aba6.s: The Nallamala and Seshachalam forests, home to tigers, leopards, sloth bears and elephants, are part of the:
nf94f991aba6.x: Nallamala and Seshachalam are Eastern Ghats forests that provide habitat for tigers, leopards, sloth bears and elephants.
xa: Eastern Ghats: dense tropical forests grading into **thorn forests** on the **Rayalaseema** plateau.
**Tiger** is a keystone, flagship and umbrella species.

n20728a0f6ac.s: Open Natural Ecosystems cover over 10% of India, but what share of them is protected?
n20728a0f6ac.x: Open Natural Ecosystems cover more than 10% of India, but less than 5% of them are protected.
xa: The guide was launched at **UNCCD COP17, Ulaanbaatar** (Aug **2026**).
**Banni** (about **2,600 sq km**) is one of Asia's largest natural grasslands.

nbiology-61-20.s: Which of the following is a stem parasite?
nbiology-61-20.x: Cuscuta is a stem parasite; Nepenthes is insectivorous.
n: Cyanobacteria inhabit terrestrial habitats. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 112-114]
Cyanobacteria inhabit aquatic habitats. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 112-114]
Protists have parasitic associations. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 112-114]
Nepenthes inhabits tropical pitcher plant habitats. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 112-114]
Cuscuta grows on host plants as a stem parasite. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 112-114]
xa: **Parasitism** is a **+/-** interaction: **Cuscuta** on host plants; **ticks and lice**.
**Pitcher plants** grow in **nitrogen-poor soil** — **insectivory** is their adaptation.
**Methanogens** live in **anaerobic wetlands** and the **digestive tract of ruminants**.

n176fd48eb4b.s: Why is an ecosystem with a more complex food web generally more stable?
o: It has more alternative feeding pathways
It eliminates all competition among organisms
n176fd48eb4b.x: A complex food web provides alternative pathways for energy and feeding relationships, increasing ecosystem stability.
n176fd48eb4b.tq: Link structural complexity with redundancy and alternative pathways.
xs: Complex webs have **more alternative feeding pathways**, so the ecosystem is more **stable** — option **(1)**.
They do not prevent every disturbance; ecosystems resist stress only **up to a limit** (**homeostasis**).
xa: Diverse systems (**rainforest, coral reef**) are more stable than simple ones (**tundra, desert, monoculture**).
⚠ **Resistance** = withstand; **resilience** = recover (**APPSC 2024**).

naf4cd203575.s: On average, the total primary production efficiency of an ecosystem is about ____ of incoming solar energy.
naf4cd203575.x: Only about 1–2% of incoming solar energy is captured in photosynthesis; 10% is the share passed between trophic levels.
xa: ⚠ **10%** is the share passed between **trophic levels** (ten percent law).
Plants fix **2-10% of PAR**.
