It **prevents**, **controls** and **abates** **water pollution** under the **Water Act, 1974**.
Air functions were given under the **Air Act, 1981**; it **improves air quality**.
xa: The CPCB **promotes** the **cleanliness** of **streams and wells**.
CPCB and SPCBs **monitor water bodies** and **industrial discharges** and can act against **violators**.
NAMP network: **1,646 stations in 603 cities** (March **2026**).

n5cc5a5b9919.s: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 is regarded as India’s first:
n5cc5a5b9919.x: The Water Act, 1974 is regarded as India’s first pollution-control law and focuses on preventing and controlling water pollution.
n5cc5a5b9919.tq: Recall the distinctive historical position of the statute among environmental laws.
xs: The Water Act 1974 is India's **first pollution-control law** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Purpose: **prevent and control water pollution**; maintain/restore **wholesomeness of water**.
Forest conservation (**1980**) and wildlife protection (**1972**) are separate Acts.
xa: It created the **Central Board (1974)** — renamed **CPCB** in **1988** — plus State Boards.
Passed under **Article 252** on resolution of states.
**APPCB** was set up in **1976** under the Water Act.

nd7630791aad.s: Which one of the following was specifically added to the definition of ‘air pollutant’ by the 1987 amendment to the Air Act?
nd7630791aad.x: The 1987 amendment expanded the definition of air pollutant to include noise.
nd7630791aad.tq: Discriminate between the statutory definition of air pollutant and other environmental pollutants.
xs: **Noise** was added to the air-pollutant definition by the **1987 amendment** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Air Act itself was enacted in **1981**; the **1987** change widened its scope to cover noise.
xa: ⚠ Water Act **8 chapters, 64 sections**; Air Act **7 chapters, 54 sections**; noise added **1987**.
**Section 31A**: power to give directions; PCBs can levy compensation.
The Air Act was also amended in **1988**.

n89ee4478b66.s: Who is empowered to declare an area as an air pollution control area under the Air Act, 1981?
n89ee4478b66.x: The State Government may declare an air pollution control area under Chapter IV, particularly Sections 19 to 31, of the Air Act.
n89ee4478b66.tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the competent authority.
xs: **Air pollution control areas** are declared by the **State Government** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This is under **Chapter 4, Sections 19-31** of the Air Act.
**CPCB** coordinates SPCBs; the **NGT** is a tribunal — neither declares these areas.
xa: Air Act special powers also include **emission standards** for industry and automobiles.
**SPCBs** enforce the Act; their chair is nominated by the **State Government**.
**Section 31A**: directions and compensation.

n267e5d8eed0.s: Which one of the following is primarily a function of the CPCB rather than an operational function of an SPCB?
o: Inspecting individual industrial plants within the State
Granting consent to individual industries in the State
Analysing samples collected for State-level enforcement
n267e5d8eed0.x: Coordination of SPCBs is a CPCB function. Inspection, sample analysis and granting consents to industries are among the operational functions of SPCBs.
n267e5d8eed0.tq: Separate the coordinating role of the central body from field-level State functions.
xs: **Coordinating SPCBs** is a CPCB function — so option **(4)** is correct.
CPCB **co-ordinates SPCBs** and gives technical assistance, research, training and national monitoring.
Granting **consent** (CTE/CTO) to industries is done by the **SPCB**.
xa: CPCB is the **enforcement body** under the EPA framework (PYQ).
Two-stage consent from SPCB: **Consent to Establish** and **Consent to Operate**.
**APPCB** uses **computerised inspection allocation** — high-risk industries inspected more often.

ncb2552cc961.s: The power of Pollution Control Boards to levy environmental compensation under Section 31A of the Air Act and Section 33A of the Water Act was upheld subject to which limitation?
o: It may be exercised without any connection to actual or imminent harm.
It may be exercised only against government-owned industries.
It may be exercised only when environmental harm is clear or imminent.
It may be exercised only after a criminal conviction.
ncb2552cc961.x: The power to levy compensation has been upheld, but its exercise must be connected with clear or imminent environmental harm.
ncb2552cc961.tq: Apply the legal power to a fact pattern while checking the limiting condition.
xs: The compensation power applies **only when environmental harm is clear or imminent** — so option **(3)** is correct.
PCBs can impose it under **S.33A Water Act / S.31A Air Act**; upheld by the SC (**Aug 2025**).
xa: **Section 31A** (Air Act): power to give directions.
**Section 33A** (Water Act): directions and penalties.
**Vanashakti v UoI**: ex post facto EC only via **Article 142** in fit cases.

n573e83f16cf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Water Act, 1974 and the Air Act, 1981?
o: The Water Act aims to maintain and restore the wholesomeness of water
The Air Act has 7 chapters and 54 sections
The Water Act has 8 chapters and 64 sections
Declaring pollution control areas is a special feature of the Water Act
n573e83f16cf.x: Declaring air pollution control areas is the Air Act's special power, not the Water Act's.
xa: ⚠ Water Act = **Article 252**; EPA = **Article 253**.
Air Act amended **1987** — **noise** added.
Both Acts use the same **CPCB and SPCBs**.

nf8e27e55dd3.s: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act was enacted in:
nf8e27e55dd3.x: The order is Water Act 1974, Water Cess Act 1977, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 and Air Act 1981.
xa: The chain continues: **EPA 1986** → **PLI Act 1991** → **Biological Diversity Act 2002** → **NGT Act 2010**.
**Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972** came before all of these.
Water Act 1974 = India's **first pollution-control law**; NGT Act 2010 = latest in the chain.

n9b8c80e8d2e.s: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977 was subsumed with the introduction of GST in:
n9b8c80e8d2e.x: The water cess, levied on water consumed by specified industries and local authorities, was subsumed with GST in 2017.
xa: ⚠ Water Cess → **Consolidated Fund of India**; EP Fund → **Public Account**.
**25% rebate** for installing treatment plants.
Cess Rules **1978**; Act of **17 sections**.

n45e32680238.s: Which one of the following is the primary purpose of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
o: To regulate only the use of forest land
To protect and improve the environment and control pollution
To levy a cess on municipal water consumption
To establish a specialised environmental tribunal
n45e32680238.x: The Act provides a framework for protecting and improving the environment and controlling pollution.
n45e32680238.tq: Match the umbrella statute with its broad statutory purpose, not with a related specialised law.
xs: EPA's purpose is to **protect and improve the environment and control pollution** — so option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC 2025**).
Forest-land diversion is the **Forest (Conservation) Act 1980**; water cess is the **1977** Act; the tribunal is the **NGT Act 2010**.
xa: It implements **Stockholm Conference (1972)** decisions under **Article 253**.
Central powers: **standards**, **location of industries**, **hazardous wastes**, public health.
Section 5: directions including **closure**.

n83db792b67d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Central Government's powers under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
o: It can lay down emission and discharge standards
It can take measures to protect public health
It cannot regulate the location of industries
n83db792b67d.x: The Centre's powers under the Act include regulating the location of industries, besides standards, hazardous waste and public health.
xa: It can also issue directions including **closure** (**Section 5**).
Standards are set by MoEF&CC with CPCB and published in the **Gazette**; lead in paints capped at **90 ppm**.
**Primary authority** under EPA: Central Government.

n0259fa1b0ba.s: The National Ganga River Basin Authority, constituted in 2009, is an example of an authority constituted under:
o: Section 5 of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010
Section 16 of the Water Cess Act, 1977
n0259fa1b0ba.x: The National Ganga River Basin Authority was an authority constituted under Section 3(3) of the Environment (Protection) Act.
n0259fa1b0ba.tq: Use the section-number and body-name pairing to avoid confusing statutory authorities with constitutional bodies.
xs: The **National Ganga River Basin Authority (2009)** was set up under **Section 3(3) of EPA 1986** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Section 16** of EPA (not the Cess Act) creates the **Environment Protection Fund**.
xa: Another Sec 3(3) authority: **Central Ground Water Authority (1997)**.
Standards under EPA are published in the **Gazette**.
EPA rests on **Article 253**.

n98ec390d383.s: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 was enacted under which constitutional provision, to implement the decisions of which conference?
n98ec390d383.x: EPA 1986 rests on Article 253 (laws to implement international agreements) and gives effect to the Stockholm Conference (1972) decisions. Article 252 is the basis of the Water Act 1974, not EPA. Rio 1992 came after the Act. Article 51A(g) is a Fundamental Duty, not a law-making power.
xs: EPA 1986 rests on **Article 253** to implement **Stockholm Conference (1972)** decisions — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **Article 252** is the basis of the **Water Act 1974**, not EPA.
xa: Trigger: the **Bhopal Gas Tragedy (Dec 1984)**.
EPA is **umbrella legislation** over Water Act and Air Act authorities.
**Primary authority**: Central Government.

ncaf328c4f90.s: The Environment Protection Fund, kept in the Public Account, is constituted under which Section of the EP Act, 1986?
ncaf328c4f90.x: The Fund is constituted under Section 16 and holds fines under the Air, Water and EP Acts; 75% goes to States/UTs and 25% to the Centre.
xa: **EPF Rules, 2026** were notified by **MoEFCC**.
⚠ Water Cess proceeds → **Consolidated Fund of India**; EP Fund → **Public Account**.
Green Credit guidelines: **16 Sep 2025**.

na82988a5f68.s: The Green Credit Rules have been notified under the:
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
na82988a5f68.x: Eco-Sensitive Zone notifications, the Plastic Waste Management Rules and the Green Credit Rules are all notified under the EP Act, 1986.
xa: Green Credit: voluntary tree planting on **degraded land** earns credits.
Other EPA notifications: **Doon Valley (1989)**, **CRZ (1991)**, **EIA (1994, 2006)**.
**APPCB** implements waste rules (Hazardous, Bio-medical, Plastic, Solid).

ndc9bc224773.s: What was the original maximum punishment provided under the Environment (Protection) Act for an offence?
o: Only a written warning issued by the Central Government
Up to 5 years’ imprisonment or a fine of Rs 1 lakh, with Rs 5,000 per day for a continuing offence
Life imprisonment and forfeiture of all property
Up to 2 years’ imprisonment or a fine of Rs 10,000, with no continuing penalty
ndc9bc224773.x: The original penalty was imprisonment up to five years or a fine up to Rs 1 lakh, with an additional Rs 5,000 per day for a continuing offence.
ndc9bc224773.tq: Read the full penalty structure, including the continuing-offence component, rather than only the headline punishment.
xs: EPA's original penalty was **up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of Rs 1 lakh**, with **Rs 5,000 per day** for a continuing offence — so option **(2)** is correct.
These were the figures before the **Jan Vishwas Act 2023** changed the regime.
xa: The **PLI Act 1991** was also decriminalised — **penalty instead of imprisonment**.
⚠ Some notes wrongly put these EPA figures under the **Water Act**.
**Water Act** penalties: **1.5 to 6 years'** jail.

na20933f3ed8.s: The penalty regime under the Environment (Protection) Act was decriminalised through the:
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977
na20933f3ed8.x: The Jan Vishwas Act, 2023 decriminalised the penalty regime under the Environment (Protection) Act.
na20933f3ed8.tq: Distinguish the original criminal penalty provisions from their later legislative modification.
xs: EPA's penalty regime was decriminalised by the **Jan Vishwas Act, 2023** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **NGT Act 2010** created a specialised tribunal; the **Forest Act 1980** and **Water Cess Act 1977** do not deal with EPA penalties.
xa: The same Act amended the **PLI Act 1991** — **penalty instead of imprisonment**.
Water Act minor offences were decriminalised by amendment in **2024**.
Original EPA penalty: up to **5 years** or **Rs 1 lakh**.

n323623f2ca3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023 amendment of the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991?
o: Offences were decriminalised, with penalties replacing imprisonment
Environmental Relief Fund money may go to CPCB/SPCBs for restoration
It amended the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991
Penalty rates are now fixed in the Act itself
n323623f2ca3.x: The amendment shifted penalty rates to the rules rather than fixing them in the Act.
xa: Relief for death raised **₹25,000 to ₹5 lakh**.
The **PLI Act** dates from **1991**.
EPA penalties were also decriminalised by **Jan Vishwas Act 2023**.

n24bf16900c4.s: Who nominates the chairperson of the CPCB and the chairperson of an SPCB, respectively?
n24bf16900c4.x: The CPCB chairperson is nominated by the Central Government, while the SPCB chairperson is nominated by the concerned State Government.
n24bf16900c4.tq: Compare the appointing authority at the Union and State levels.
xs: The **CPCB** chair is nominated by the **Central Government**, the **SPCB** chair by the **State Government** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (4) reverses the two.
xa: CPCB is a **statutory body** under **MoEFCC**.
CPCB **co-ordinates SPCBs**; SPCBs enforce the Acts.
**APPCB** was set up in **1976** under the Water Act.

ncab815d07b4.s: The Department of Environment (1980) became the Ministry of Environment and Forests in:
ncab815d07b4.x: The Ministry of Environment and Forests was formed in 1985; it was renamed MoEFCC in 2014.
xa: Bodies under it: **CPCB** (statutory), **Central Zoo Authority (1992)**, **NTCA (2005)**, BSI, ZSI, FSI.
CPCB gives **technical services** to the Ministry under **EPA 1986**.
MoEFCC notified the **EPF Rules, 2026**.

n421f553891b.s: Consent to Establish (CTE) and Consent to Operate (CTO) for polluting industries are granted by the:
n421f553891b.x: Both consents are given by the State Pollution Control Board: CTE before setting up the unit and CTO before production begins.
xa: Both Water and Air Acts require **prior consent** of the Board.
Since **29 Jan 2026**, **CTO is valid until cancelled**.
**White** category industries need **no consent/EC**.

n4ad93d30a6c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Supreme Court's ruling in Vanashakti v. Union of India?
o: Article 142 may be applied only in fit cases
Administrative orders cannot override the EIA Notification, 2006
The ruling on retrospective environmental clearance was prospective
Ex post facto clearance may be granted in every case merely on payment of a penalty
n4ad93d30a6c.x: Ex post facto clearance is not available in every case merely on payment of a penalty; Article 142 may apply only in fit cases.
xa: The SC nullified the **2021 Office Memorandum** allowing retrospective ECs on paying penalties.
Ruling dated **31 Jul 2026**.
**EIA** notification: **1994**, then **2006**.

nenvironment-5-5.s: Which Section of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 deals with penalties for contravention of the Act?
nenvironment-5-5.x: Section 15 sets penalties; Section 3(3) allows authorities to be constituted and Section 5 covers directions.
n: The last amendment mentioned for the Environment (Protection) Act was in 1991. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 10-12]
Section 3(3) of the Environment (Protection) Act provides the power to constitute authorities. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 10-12]
Section 5 of the Environment (Protection) Act concerns directions and measures. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 10-12]
Sections 15–21 of the Environment (Protection) Act contain penal provisions. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 10-12]
xa: Original EPA penalty: up to **5 years** jail or **Rs 1 lakh** fine; **Rs 5,000/day** for continuing offence.
**Environment Protection Fund** under **Section 16**: **75%** to States/UTs, **25%** to Centre.

nenvironment-5-7.s: The Fundamental Duty to protect and improve the natural environment and to have compassion for living creatures is in:
nenvironment-5-7.x: Article 51A(g) asks citizens to protect and improve the natural environment and to have compassion for living creatures.
n: Article 51A(g) directs citizens to protect the natural environment. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 10-12]
Article 51A(g) directs citizens to improve the natural environment. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 10-12]
Article 51A(g) directs citizens to show compassion for living creatures. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #5 · pp 10-12]
xa: **Article 48A** directs the **State** to protect and improve the environment and **safeguard forests and wildlife**.
Both came in via the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act**, **1976**.
The **EPA 1986** was enacted under **Article 253**.

n3f76c743166.s: The Coastal Regulation Zone notification issued under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 primarily:
o: regulates coastal stretches and prohibits ash or waste dumping
requires prior clearance for all forest diversion
n3f76c743166.x: The CRZ notification of 1991 regulates coastal stretches and prohibits ash and waste dumping in the regulated areas.
n3f76c743166.tq: Connect the environmental zone with its geographical subject and specific restriction.
xs: **CRZ** **regulates coastal stretches and prohibits ash or waste dumping** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was notified in **1991** under EPA; CRZ under EPA was confirmed in **Jul 2026**.
Forest diversion is the **Forest (Conservation) Act 1980**; the NGT came by the **NGT Act 2010**.
xa: **Dhanu Taluka (1991)**: ecologically fragile; no power plants.
**EIA (1994, then 2006)**: prior environmental clearance.
**Uppada (Kakinada)** faces coastal erosion.

nf8631438dc3.s: The Environmental Impact Assessment notification under the Environment (Protection) Act is associated with:
nf8631438dc3.x: The EIA notification was issued in 1994 and was subsequently revised in 2006; it provides for prior environmental clearance.
nf8631438dc3.tq: Pair the original notification year with its later revision and the clearance requirement.
xs: The **EIA** notification dates from **1994** with its subsequent **revision in 2006** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It requires **prior environmental clearance**.
xa: **Vanashakti v UoI**: SC nullified the **2021 Office Memorandum** allowing retrospective ECs; administrative orders cannot override **EIA Notification 2006**.
Ex post facto EC only via **Article 142** in fit cases (**31 Jul 2026**).
**White** category industries (score **20 or less**) need no consent/EC.

ndcb743629bf.s: A new category introduced for essential environmental services, such as Compressed Biogas, is:
ndcb743629bf.x: The Blue category was introduced for essential environmental services, with Compressed Biogas cited as an example.
ndcb743629bf.tq: Recall the newly added category by linking it to its representative activity.
xs: The new category for essential environmental services is **Blue** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Example: **Compressed Biogas** (**Economic Survey 2025-26**).
xa: Other categories: **Red (60 and above)**, **Orange (41-59)**, **Green (21-40)**, **White (20 or less)**.
White industries need **no consent/EC**.
Basis: **emissions, effluents and hazardous waste** (CPCB, Jun 2026).

n5c85715f11e.s: The colour categorisation of industries by the CPCB is primarily based on the pollution potential arising from:
o: Energy consumption, exports and tax contribution
Land area, workforce and annual turnover
Water availability, raw material cost and product demand
Emissions, effluents and hazardous waste generated
n5c85715f11e.x: The basis of the colour categories is the pollution potential represented by emissions, effluents and hazardous waste generated.
n5c85715f11e.tq: Identify the exact regulatory basis instead of choosing general industrial characteristics.
xs: Colour categories are based on **emissions, effluents and hazardous waste generated** — so option **(4)** is correct (CPCB, **Jun 2026**).
It uses the **CPCB Pollution Index score**, not turnover, land area or tax contribution.
xa: **Red ≥ 60** (cement, petrochemicals); **White ≤ 20** (no consent/EC).
**Blue** = essential environmental services (e.g. Compressed Biogas).
Consents are given by the **SPCB**: CTE and CTO.

n5399d497404.s: Real-time air-quality information from the monitoring network is available through which application?
n5399d497404.x: Real-time air-quality information is provided through the SAMEER app. SAFAR is a separate air-quality and weather forecasting system.
n5399d497404.tq: Discriminate between two similarly associated air-quality applications.
xs: Real-time air-quality data comes via the **SAMEER** app — so option **(3)** is correct (**12 Sep 2026**).
It draws on the **NAMP** network of **1,646 stations in 603 cities** (March 2026).
xa: Earlier NAMP figures: **516 cities**, **1,400+ stations**.
**National AQI** launched **2015**.
**NCAP (2019)**: **40% PM10 reduction by 2025-26** in **130 cities**.

nb4482585646.s: Under the consent reform introduced in January 2026, which of the following is correct?
o: A single application covers Air and Water consents as well as waste authorisations, and CTO remains valid until cancelled.
A single application is available only for mining projects.
Only waste authorisations are covered and CTO is abolished.
Separate applications remain compulsory and CTO expires annually.
nb4482585646.x: The January 2026 reform provides for a single application for Air and Water consents plus waste authorisations, while consent to operate remains valid until cancelled.
nb4482585646.tq: Apply the reform to a compliance scenario by identifying both its procedural and validity changes.
xs: The **Jan 2026** reform gives **a single application for Air and Water consents plus waste authorisations**, and **CTO valid until cancelled** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Earlier, CTO needed **periodic renewal**; the change is dated **29 Jan 2026**.
xa: **CTE** comes before setting up; **CTO** before production.
Both Water and Air Acts require **prior consent** of the Board.
Other current items: **EPF Rules, 2026**; **Vanashakti** ruling (31 Jul 2026).

nf0d5e23c711.s: The global origin of Environmental Impact Assessment is associated with the National Environmental Policy Act of the:
nf0d5e23c711.x: The global origin of EIA is associated with the United States National Environmental Policy Act, enacted in 1969.
nf0d5e23c711.tq: Pair the legislation, country and year precisely.
xs: EIA originated in the **National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA)** of the **United States, 1969** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1978** is a date given for India's first use of EIA, not the US origin; **1994** is India's first formal notification.
xa: India began in **1976-77**, when the Planning Commission asked **DST** to examine **river-valley projects**.
⚠ Sources differ on India's start: **1976-77** vs **1978**.
FIRST/LAST: first EIA law **NEPA 1969**; India's first sector appraised — **river-valley projects**.

n0c88e921e39.s: In India, the Planning Commission asked the Department of Science and Technology to examine river-valley projects during:
n0c88e921e39.x: India's EIA process began in 1976-77 when the Planning Commission asked DST to examine river-valley projects.
n0c88e921e39.tq: Distinguish the institutional beginning from the later first-use date.
xs: The Planning Commission asked **DST** to examine river-valley projects in **1976-77** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**1969** is the US **NEPA**; **1993-94** and **1978-79** are not the stated start.
xa: ⚠ Some **2026** notes date first use to **1978** (river valley projects).
Next came large public-sector projects needing **Public Investment Board** clearance.
EIA was **codified in 1994**.

n96ef435c55d.s: The EIA Notification, 2006 introduced which major change in the basis for appraisal?
o: A shift from investment size to impact potential
A shift from public consultation to administrative approval only
A shift from project categories to product certification
A shift from impact potential to investment size
n96ef435c55d.x: The 2006 notification shifted the test from investment size to impact potential and made clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.
n96ef435c55d.tq: Focus on the reversed comparison between the old and new bases of appraisal.
xs: EIA 2006 shifted focus from **investment size to impact potential** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **1994** notification covered industrial projects above **Rs 500 million** — an investment test; option (4) reverses the shift.
xa: EC is compulsory for **39 project categories**.
Safeguards: **air, water, land, biodiversity, wildlife habitat**.
Notified **14 Sep 2006** under **EPA 1986**.

n407aae086dc.s: The requirement of mandatory public hearing under the 1994 EIA framework was added through the:
n407aae086dc.x: Mandatory public hearing was added by the 1997 amendment to the 1994 framework.
n407aae086dc.tq: Separate the original notification from a later amendment.
xs: Mandatory public hearing was added by the **1997 amendment** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was added to the **1994** EIA framework.
xa: Under **EIA 2006**: notice at least **30 days**; hearing within **45 days**.
**Draft 2020** proposed cutting the notice from **30 to 20 days**.
Hearings are conducted by the **SPCB**, with the **District Collector** presiding.

ndad9d42798a.s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, Category B2 projects:
o: Require a full EIA by MoEFCC
Are appraised by the central EAC
ndad9d42798a.x: Category B1 projects require an EIA while B2 projects do not; both fall under state-level appraisal and clearance.
xa: ⚠ **A** → EAC → MoEFCC; **B1/B2** → SEAC → SEIAA; only **B2** has no EIA.
**B2** projects are also **exempt from public hearing**.
**Draft 2020** proposed moving more projects to **B2/exempt**.

o: A single-window portal for online environment, forest, wildlife and CRZ clearances
A programme for preparing baseline biodiversity data
A committee for appraisal of Category A projects
n374c1edb8ff.x: PARIVESH is an online single-window platform for environment, forest, wildlife and Coastal Regulation Zone clearances.
n374c1edb8ff.tq: Distinguish a digital clearance platform from statutory bodies.
xs: PARIVESH is a **single-window portal for online environment, forest, wildlife and CRZ clearances** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is not a tribunal (the **NGT**) or an appraisal committee (the **EAC**).
xa: Launched **2018**; now **PARIVESH 3.0** using **AI** (Economic Survey 2025-26).
Platform for the **120-day** escalation to **SCEIA**.
Expansion: **Pro-Active and Responsive facilitation by Interactive, Virtuous and Environmental Single-window Hub**.

n6703fa75d7b.s: Which one of the following has been suggested as a measure to address the criticism that EIA consultants may lack independence?
o: Transfer of EIA preparation entirely to project proponents
Permitting post-facto clearances as a routine measure
Creation of an independent EIA authority
n6703fa75d7b.x: An independent EIA authority has been suggested to improve the credibility and independence of environmental assessments.
n6703fa75d7b.tq: Match the identified institutional defect with the appropriate reform.
xs: The suggested fix is an **independent EIA authority** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It answers the criticism that EIAs are prepared by **proponent-paid consultants**.
Routine post-facto clearance and abolishing hearings would worsen, not fix, the problem.
xa: Other criticisms: **no central baseline data bank**; **weak emergency plans**.
UPSC way-forward: **sector-wide EIAs** (strategic/cumulative).
Jul 2026 concern: **bureaucrats replace scientists**.

nacb5f40c905.s: The National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), which introduced EIA, was enacted in the United States in:
nacb5f40c905.x: NEPA came in 1969; EIA was first used in India in 1978 and formally notified in 1994.
xa: ⚠ Sources differ on India's start: **1976-77** (DST, river-valley) vs **1978**.
EIA Notification **2006** replaced the 1994 notification.
Public hearing added by the **1997 amendment**.

nf9867dacb57.s: A government is assessing the environmental implications of a new transport policy before individual road projects are selected. Which tool is most appropriate?
nf9867dacb57.x: Strategic Environmental Assessment examines policies, plans and programmes upstream of individual projects. A project-level EIA is conducted for a specific project, whereas an environmental audit is generally an after-the-fact compliance check.
nf9867dacb57.tq: Identify the level of decision-making before choosing between project and strategic assessment.
xs: A new transport policy calls for **Strategic Environmental Assessment** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**SEA** covers **policies, plans and programmes**, upstream of projects.
**Project-level EIA** studies one project before it starts; **LCA** a product's life cycle; an **audit** checks an operating unit after the fact.
xa: UPSC way-forward: **sector-wide EIAs** (strategic/cumulative) needed.
**Cumulative Impact Assessment**: combined effect of several projects in one basin.
EIA requires **assessment of alternatives** in location and process technology.

n31cf646c12c.s: The 12 principles of green chemistry were formulated by:
n31cf646c12c.x: The 12 principles of green chemistry (prevent waste, atom economy, safer solvents, renewable feedstocks, design for degradation) were set out by Anastas and Warner in 1998. The Brundtland Commission (1987) defined sustainable development; Rachel Carson wrote Silent Spring (1962); the Club of Rome issued Limits to Growth (1972).
n31cf646c12c.tq: Green chemistry = 12 principles, Anastas and Warner, 1998.
xs: The **12 principles** of green chemistry are by **Anastas and Warner, 1998** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Examples: **prevent waste**, **atom economy**, **safer solvents**, **renewable feedstocks**, **design for degradation**.
xa: Green chemistry: reduce or eliminate **hazardous substances**.
**Cleaner production**: cut waste **at source** (process change, input substitution).
EIA requires assessment of alternatives in **process technology**.

na0fed2cfe61.s: The EIA stage that identifies key issues and sets the Terms of Reference is:
na0fed2cfe61.x: Scoping fixes key issues and Terms of Reference; screening decides whether EIA is needed and appraisal evaluates the final report.
xa: EIA 2006 stages: **Screening → Scoping → Public consultation → Appraisal → Decision**.
⚠ **Category A** has **no screening** — always full EIA.
**Baseline data** = survey of the existing environment.

n902794d03c9.s: Which is the first stage of the EIA process?
n902794d03c9.x: The EIA sequence is screening, scoping, appraisal and decision.
xa: **Scoping** sets the **Terms of Reference**.
**Monitoring** of EMP follows the decision.
**Category A** skips screening; always full EIA.

nd2f5fed153f.s: Under the July 2026 amendment, if a State Expert Appraisal Committee fails to decide a proposal within 120 days, the proposal may escalate to:
o: The new Standing Committee on Environmental Impact Assessment on PARIVESH
nd2f5fed153f.x: The July 2026 amendment provides for escalation after 120 days to the new SCEIA through PARIVESH.
nd2f5fed153f.tq: Link the time limit with the newly designated authority.
xs: After **120 days**, a SEAC proposal escalates to the new **SCEIA** via **PARIVESH** — so option **(4)** is correct.
This is the **Jul 2026** amendment (23 Jul 2026), with auto-transfer via PARIVESH.
xa: ⚠ **SAEIA** ↔ SEIAA; **SCEIA** ↔ SEAC.
Category B no longer defaults to the central **EAC** when a state committee lapses.
Backup bodies' tenure: **6 + 6 months** (max 1 year).

ne6beb87c27b.s: The proposal for sector-wide EIAs is intended primarily to strengthen which approach?
ne6beb87c27b.x: Sector-wide EIAs are intended to incorporate strategic and cumulative perspectives, allowing impacts across a sector or region to be assessed rather than examining projects in isolation.
ne6beb87c27b.tq: Infer the broader assessment level from the phrase sector-wide.
xs: **Sector-wide EIAs** aim to strengthen **strategic and cumulative assessment** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This is the **UPSC way-forward**: sector-wide EIAs (i.e., strategic/cumulative) needed.
xa: **SEA** = policies, plans, programmes; **Cumulative Impact Assessment** = several projects in one area/basin.
Criticism: EIAs by **proponent-paid consultants**; no central baseline data bank.
Suggested fix: an **independent EIA authority**.

n861ec154597.s: The EIA Notification, 2006 made environmental clearance compulsory for how many project categories?
n861ec154597.x: The 2006 notification made environmental clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.
xa: Focus shifted from **investment to impact potential**.
Categories: **A** (EAC → MoEFCC), **B1** and **B2** (SEAC → SEIAA).
Notified **14 Sep 2006**, replacing the **1994** notification.

ne8b40ae85a1.s: Who presides over the public hearing conducted by the State Pollution Control Board?
ne8b40ae85a1.x: The State Pollution Control Board conducts the hearing, while the District Collector presides over it.
ne8b40ae85a1.tq: Use the authority-role distinction to avoid swapping institutions.
xs: The **District Collector** presides over the public hearing — so option **(1)** is correct.
The hearing is **conducted by the SPCB** (22 May 2026).
xa: Notice at least **30 days**; hearing within **45 days** (EIA 2006).
APPCB hearing on the **Water Aerodrome at Prakasam Barrage** — HRF called the draft EIA error-ridden.
**SEIAA** and **EAC** clear projects; they do not preside over hearings.

n3f26d74883e.s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, a public hearing must be completed within how many days?
n3f26d74883e.x: The public-hearing notice must be given at least 30 days in advance and the hearing completed within 45 days.
xa: ⚠ Notice **30 days** (EIA 2006) vs **20 days** (Draft 2020); hearing within **45 days**.
Hearings are conducted by the **SPCB**.
Public consultation = hearing + **written responses**.

n08e3ac1e8fe.s: Which of the following was a provision of the July 2026 amendment to the EIA framework?
o: The Centre may remove EAC, SEAC or SEIAA members mid-term for persistent delays.
Scientists alone must replace all administrative members.
All Category B projects must automatically be transferred to the central EAC.
State committees may retain proposals indefinitely without escalation.
n08e3ac1e8fe.x: The amendment permits the Centre to remove members of EAC, SEAC or SEIAA mid-term for persistent delays. It also introduced an escalation mechanism rather than automatic transfer of all Category B projects to the central EAC.
n08e3ac1e8fe.tq: Identify the precise institutional power among reversed alternatives.
xs: The Centre **may remove EAC, SEAC or SEIAA members mid-term for persistent delays** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Category B **no longer defaults to the central EAC** — escalation goes to **SCEIA** after **120 days**, so options (3) and (4) are wrong.
xa: Member tenure: **3 to 4 years**; max **two terms**; age limit **70**.
Concern: **bureaucrats replace scientists**; speed over science.
MoEFCC had proposed **SCEIA and SAEIA** earlier (Mar 2026).

nb11d8ce000c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Draft EIA Notification, 2020?
o: It proposed reducing the public-hearing notice from 30 to 20 days
It proposed yearly instead of half-yearly compliance reports
It proposed moving more projects to Category B2 or exempting them
It allowed violations to be reported by any member of the public without restriction
nb11d8ce000c.x: The draft restricted reporting of violations to the violator or the government.
xa: It also proposed **post-facto clearance** on payment of penalties.
The draft has **not been finalised**.
EIA 2006: notice at least **30 days**; hearing within **45 days**.

nc038e6dbd5c.s: The time limit prescribed in the August 2023 direction for the Border Roads Organisation to plant the trees was:
nc038e6dbd5c.x: The NGT directed the plantation of the trees within one month.
nc038e6dbd5c.tq: Separate the quantity of the direction from its compliance period.
xs: The NGT gave the **Border Roads Organisation** **one month** to plant trees — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **Aug 2023** order (Uttarakhand) required at least **10,000 trees** within **one month** (PYQ).
xa: **Rat-hole mining** in **Meghalaya (2014)** was declared illegal/banned by NGT.
NGT fined **Maharashtra and West Bengal (2022)** for waste mismanagement.
**LG Polymers** (May 2020): **Rs 50 crore** interim deposit.

n72c66486481.s: India's first EIA Notification under the Environment (Protection) Act was issued on 27 January of:
n72c66486481.x: The EIA Notification, 1994 was issued on 27 January 1994; earlier clearance was only administrative, and the 2006 notification replaced it.
xa: Public hearing was made mandatory by the **1997 amendment**.
Later amendments: **2009** (expanded list), **2013** (thermal power), **2015** (expansion and modernisation).
**Draft 2020** (post-facto, shorter consultation) has **not been finalised**.

nb861cc7cf63.s: Cleaner production reduces environmental impact mainly through:
o: Shifting polluting units to industrial estates
Process or input changes at the source
nb861cc7cf63.x: Cleaner production is preventive and changes processes or inputs at the source rather than relying exclusively on end-of-pipe treatment.
xa: Other principles: **prevent waste**, **atom economy**, **safer solvents**.
**12 principles**: Anastas and Warner, **1998**.
APPCB encourages **cleaner production technologies**.

na20d5972bea.s: In the EIA process, comparison of alternatives is carried out during:
na20d5972bea.x: Impact prediction includes comparison of alternatives; baseline data surveys the existing environment and mitigation planning includes the EMP.
xa: **Monitoring**: EMP implementation is checked.
EIA requires **assessment of alternatives** in location and **process technology**.
Criticism: **no central baseline data bank**; thin baseline in the **Great Nicobar** EIA.

n3aaab2ea032.s: In the EIA process, who decides whether a project is 'strategic' and thus exempt from public hearing?
n3aaab2ea032.x: The Central Government decides 'strategic' status (criticised as arbitrary); the SPCB only conducts the public hearing.
xa: The SPCB only **conducts** the hearing, with the **District Collector** presiding.
The executive-exemption criticism dates to **2 Jan 2026**.
Criticism also: **hearings exempted**; EIAs by proponent-paid consultants.

n48c4bb7a99e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Supreme Court cases on environmental clearance?
o: Common Cause (2017) concerned Odisha mining without or beyond environmental clearance
In Noble M. Paikada (2024), the Court upheld the blanket exemption as valid
Common Cause ordered compensation of 100% of the value of illegally extracted minerals
Noble M. Paikada examined the 2020 exemption for extraction of ordinary earth for linear projects
n48c4bb7a99e.x: The key marks the claim that Noble M. Paikada upheld the blanket exemption as incorrect.
xa: **Alembic Pharmaceuticals (2020)**: ex post facto EC contrary to EIA; **2002** MoEF circular quashed.
⚠ Vanashakti: **May 2025** struck down → **Nov 2025** recalled (**2:1**) → **29 July 2026** final, prospective.
**S.P. Muthuraman (2025)** also held retrospective ECs illegal.

nf7792a17069.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Alembic Pharmaceuticals v. Rohit Prajapati?
o: The 2002 MoEF circular permitting such clearance was quashed
Ex post facto environmental clearance was held contrary to the EIA regime
The Court necessarily directed closure of every project concerned
nf7792a17069.x: The Court imposed compensation instead of ordering closure of every project.
xa: **Common Cause v UoI (2017)**: Odisha mining; compensation of **100%** of the mineral's value.
**S.P. Muthuraman (2025)** also held retrospective ECs illegal.
Exam angle: prior EC is **mandatory** under EIA 2006; post-facto only as a narrow exception.

n47897cbc63f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Vanashakti litigation?
o: The May 2025 ruling struck down the 2017 Notification and the 2021 Office Memorandum
The May 2025 ruling was recalled unanimously in November 2025
About Rs 20,000 crore worth of projects was reported to be at stake
The recall relied on D. Swamy (2021) and Pahwa Plastics (2022), among others
n47897cbc63f.x: The recall in November 2025 was by a 2:1 majority, not unanimous.
xa: Final verdict: **29 July 2026**, led by **CJI Surya Kant**; ruling **prospective**.
May 2025 language: "**gross illegality**" and "anathema".
**S.P. Muthuraman (2025)** also held retrospective ECs illegal.

nc0354f733d0.s: The final Vanashakti verdict of 29 July 2026 prospectively nullified which instrument?
nc0354f733d0.x: The verdict prospectively nullified the 2021 Office Memorandum, while earlier clearances under the 2017 Notification and the 2021 OM survived.
xa: Bench led by **CJI Surya Kant** (**29 July 2026**).
Ex post facto EC must pass **Arts 14 and 21** (proportionality).
SC keeps its power under **Article 142**.

n1354807d83a.s: Under the EIA framework, the general rule is that environmental clearance must be obtained:
o: After an environmental audit finds non-compliance
Only for products assessed through LCA
n1354807d83a.x: Prior environmental clearance is mandatory; post-facto approval, where recognised at all, is only a narrow exception.
xa: **Vanashakti (29 July 2026)**: ex post facto EC only via **Arts 14 and 21** test and **Article 142**.
**Alembic (2020)**: ex post facto EC contrary to the EIA regime.
**Draft 2020** proposed post-facto clearance but was **not finalised**.

n57abc25626c.s: According to the final Vanashakti verdict of 29 July 2026, any ex post facto environmental clearance must satisfy the test of:
o: Article 252 read with the Water Act, 1974
Article 323B read with the NGT Act, 2010
n57abc25626c.x: The Court held that ex post facto EC must meet Articles 14 and 21 (a proportionality test), while the Supreme Court keeps its power under Article 142. Articles 48A and 51A(g) are a Directive Principle and a Fundamental Duty, not the test laid down. Article 252 is the Water Act's basis; Article 323B concerns tribunals generally.
n57abc25626c.tq: Vanashakti 2026: Arts 14 + 21 test; Art 142 reserved for the SC.
xs: Ex post facto EC must satisfy **Articles 14 and 21 (proportionality)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The SC also **keeps its power under Article 142**.
⚠ **Article 252** is the **Water Act's** basis — not this test.
xa: The ruling was **prospective** — earlier ECs under the **2017 Notification and 2021 OM** survive.
The Centre may issue **time-limited notifications under EPA 1986**.
Verdict date **29 July 2026**; Bench led by **CJI Surya Kant**.

n9b6e2793b61.s: After the May 2020 styrene leak at LG Polymers, Visakhapatnam, the NGT took suo motu cognisance and ordered an interim deposit of:
n9b6e2793b61.x: The NGT ordered LG Polymers to make an interim deposit of Rs 50 crore.
xa: The **LG Polymers** leak is part of the AP angle, handled by NGT.
NGT **Jan 2026** suo motu: Rajasthan, MP, UP over sewage in drinking water.
Rat-hole mining: **Meghalaya (2014)**.

n1740d8a8ff5.s: The inter-state dispute concerning the Polavaram project primarily relates to submergence in:
n1740d8a8ff5.x: The Polavaram inter-state dispute concerns submergence in neighbouring Odisha and Chhattisgarh and was raised before the Supreme Court.
n1740d8a8ff5.tq: Identify the neighbouring states directly affected by the project’s submergence issue.
xs: The Polavaram dispute is over **submergence in Odisha and Chhattisgarh** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was raised before the **Supreme Court**.
xa: **Telangana** moved the SC seeking an EIA review of **Indira Sagar Polavaram** (**APPSC 2018**).
EIA in India began with **river-valley projects**.
AP angle also: APPCB hearing on the **Water Aerodrome at Prakasam Barrage**.

n7526af18ed7.s: Cleaner production is best described as a strategy that:
o: Treats pollution only after it has been generated at the end of a pipe
Cuts waste and pollution at the source through process change or input substitution
Replaces environmental assessment with an operating-unit audit
Focuses exclusively on disposal of hazardous waste
n7526af18ed7.x: Cleaner production is preventive: it reduces waste and pollution at source through measures such as process change and input substitution, rather than relying mainly on end-of-pipe treatment.
n7526af18ed7.tq: Distinguish prevention at source from treatment after pollution is generated.
xs: Cleaner production **cuts waste and pollution at source** through **process change or input substitution** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is a **preventive** strategy, the opposite of **end-of-pipe treatment**.
xa: **APPCB's** mandate includes encouraging **cleaner production technologies**.
**Green chemistry** designs products/processes that reduce or eliminate hazardous substances.
Both shrink impacts **at design stage**.

n0c6b4f5e86c.s: The Ministry of Environment and Forests was renamed MoEFCC in:
n0c6b4f5e86c.x: The sequence is Department of Environment 1980, Air Act 1981, MoEF 1985 and renaming to MoEFCC in 2014.
xa: CPCB itself is older: constituted in **1974** under the **Water Act**, renamed **CPCB** by the **1988** amendment.
⚠ Trap order: **1974** CPCB → **1985** MoEF → **1988** CPCB renamed → **2014** MoEFCC.
**EPA 1986** widened CPCB's scope — it did not add the air functions.
The **1985** formation of the Ministry was an **APPSC 2024** statement marked correct.

nc4e1d25d2ab.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Central Pollution Control Board?
o: Its air-pollution functions were added by the EP Act, 1986
It was renamed CPCB by a 1988 amendment
It was constituted in 1974 under the Water Act
It is a statutory body under MoEFCC
nc4e1d25d2ab.x: CPCB's air functions were added by the Air Act, 1981; the EP Act, 1986 only widened its scope.
xa: CPCB has a **full-time chairman nominated by the Central Government**.
CPCB (**1974**) is the **oldest national pollution body**.
CPCB runs **NAMP** and the **National AQI** (launched **2015**, daily bulletins).
Air network: **516 cities**, **1,400+** stations with real-time CAAQMS.

nac17a764343.s: Which body is primarily responsible for enforcing environmental standards under the Environment (Protection) Act framework?
nac17a764343.x: The CPCB is the body responsible for enforcing environmental standards under the Environment (Protection) Act framework.
nac17a764343.tq: Assign the enforcement function to the regulatory rather than adjudicatory body.
xs: The **Central Pollution Control Board** enforces environmental standards under the EPA framework — option **(3)**.
This was the **APPSC-G2 2025** answer.
The **NGT** only **adjudicates** disputes and awards compensation; the **NBA** deals with **biodiversity** access and biopiracy.
xa: CPCB is a **regulator**: sets standards, monitors pollution, advises the Centre.
Its scope was widened by **EPA 1986**; air functions came by the **Air Act 1981**.
CPCB coordinates the **NCAP** with SPCBs, tracked on the **PRANA** portal.
**Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules 2026** finance CPCB and SPCBs.

nc9ce1d3047c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board?
o: Its enforcement role is limited to the Water Act alone
It enforces rules on hazardous, biomedical, plastic and solid waste
It issues siting guidelines and SOPs for marine outfalls and hazardous waste
nc9ce1d3047c.x: APPCB enforces the Water Act, the Air Act and the Environment Protection Act, not the Water Act alone.
xa: APPCB was set up in **1976** by the **AP Government** under the **Water Act 1974**.
It is the body **entrusted to implement environmental laws and rules in AP** (**APPSC 2025** answer).
It runs **computerised inspection under EoDB**.
Like other SPCBs it grants **Consent to Establish** and **Consent to Operate**.

n43359a7e1f2.s: The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board was established in 1976 under the authority of the:
o: Government of India under the Air Act, 1981
Government of Andhra Pradesh under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
National Green Tribunal under the Water Act, 1974
Government of Andhra Pradesh under the Water Act, 1974
n43359a7e1f2.x: The APPCB was established in 1976 by the Government of Andhra Pradesh under the Water Act, 1974.
n43359a7e1f2.tq: Combine the correct State authority, year and parent legislation.
xs: APPCB was set up in **1976** by the **Government of Andhra Pradesh** under the **Water Act, 1974** — option **(4)**.
It is a State body, so not set up by the **Government of India** or the **NGT** (which came only in **2010**).
The **Air Act 1981** and **EPA 1986** came after **1976**, so they could not be its basis.
xa: APPCB is **entrusted to implement environmental laws and rules in AP** (**APPSC 2025** answer).
It enforces **Water, Air, EP Acts** and the **Hazardous, Bio-medical, Plastic, Solid waste** rules.
It issues **siting guidelines** and SOPs on **marine outfalls** and hazardous waste.
CPCB too began under the **Water Act** in **1974**.

na5fbaf561ed.s: Which body adjudicates environmental disputes and awards compensation?
na5fbaf561ed.x: The NGT is adjudicatory and awards compensation; the CPCB regulates, sets standards and monitors pollution.
xa: CPCB also **advises the Centre**.
CPCB is a **statutory body under MoEFCC** (**1974**); NGT is a **statutory** tribunal (**2010**).
CPCB runs **NAMP**, **National AQI** and **RTWQMS**.
NGT is guided by **natural justice**, not bound by **CPC 1908**.

n38eb42abd8c.s: Which one of the following bodies replaced the Environment Pollution (Prevention and Control) Authority (EPCA) in the National Capital Region and adjoining areas?
n38eb42abd8c.x: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), established under the CAQM Act, 2021, replaced EPCA in the NCR and adjoining areas.
n38eb42abd8c.tq: Use the replacement relationship and distinguish air-quality authority from water and biodiversity bodies.
xs: The **Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM)** replaced **EPCA** — option **(2)**.
CAQM is based on the **CAQM Act 2021** and covers **NCR and adjoining areas**.
**NMCG** implements Namami Gange; **CGWA** regulates groundwater; **NBA** handles biodiversity.
xa: **CGWA**: constituted **1997** under **S.3(3) EPA**.
NGT fined **12 stadiums ₹5,000 each** for not giving CGWA water-use data.
**NMCG** is the successor to **NGRBA** (**2009**).

n1692622c25e.s: Which is the oldest national pollution-control body in India, set up in 1974?
n1692622c25e.x: The CPCB, set up in 1974, is the oldest national pollution body; the NGT (2010) replaced the NEAA.
xa: The NEAA (Act of **1997**) heard appeals against **environmental clearances**; its Act was **repealed in 2010**.
NGT = **original jurisdiction** + the NEAA's **appellate role**.
CPCB was **renamed** in **1988**; it started as the Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution.
NGT dates: Act **2 June 2010** → set up **18 Oct 2010** → functioning **July 2011**.

nb58150651cf.s: PRANA, a CPCB portal, is used to track the:
o: Real-time water quality of the Ganga and Yamuna
nb58150651cf.x: PRANA tracks NCAP; daily AQI bulletins come from the National AQI (2015) and RTWQMS covers real-time Ganga and Yamuna water quality.
xa: CPCB air network: **516 cities**, **1,400+** stations; **CAAQMS** gives real-time data.
CPCB also runs **National Water Quality Monitoring**.
NGT told southern States and Puducherry to execute **NCAP** plans — **86%** of spend went on **road dust**.
CPCB coordinates **SPCBs** with technical help, research and training.

n49e99426f4b.s: The National Green Tribunal is a:
o: Statutory body with powers similar to a civil court
Executive body with only advisory jurisdiction
Constitutional body with only administrative powers
n49e99426f4b.x: The NGT is a statutory, not constitutional, body with civil-court powers in matters within its jurisdiction.
xa: It is **not bound by CPC 1908**; it is guided by the **principles of natural justice**.
Cases are to be disposed of within **6 months**.
Appeal lies to the **Supreme Court** within **90 days**.
It gives effect to the right to a healthy environment under **Art. 21**.

nfcd415651e2.s: The establishment of the National Green Tribunal gives effect, in the environmental context, to which Fundamental Right?
o: Right to constitutional remedies under Article 32
nfcd415651e2.x: The NGT gives effect to the right to a healthy environment, which is treated as part of the right to life under Article 21.
nfcd415651e2.tq: Match the environmental entitlement with the relevant Fundamental Right.
xs: The NGT gives effect to the right to a healthy environment under **Article 21** (**right to life**) — option **(1)**.
The notes link the NGT only to **Art. 21**, not to Articles 14, 23 or 32.

n442eb508a18.s: An appeal against an order of the National Green Tribunal lies to the Supreme Court within:

nd688ddf2a46.s: The National Green Tribunal was set up on:

n578065aa963.s: The National Mission for Clean Ganga is the successor set-up to which body?

n322dc60df37.s: The National Green Tribunal directed southern States and Puducherry to execute action plans under which programme?
n322dc60df37.x: The NGT directed southern States and Puducherry to execute action plans under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP).

xa: CPCB coordinates NCAP with SPCBs; progress tracked on the **PRANA** portal.
**Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules 2026** finance CPCB/SPCBs.
**Guntur** was **2nd** in the towns category of **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026**.

n067c4eb0c36.s: Which of the following is a zonal bench location of the National Green Tribunal?
n067c4eb0c36.x: Pune is a zonal bench; New Delhi hosts the Principal Bench and Jodhpur and Shillong are circuit benches.

Composition: **Chairperson** + **Judicial and Expert Members** (**10 to 20** each).
Exam angle: **bench-to-city matching**.

n4783f06c417.s: Which of the following Acts is outside the jurisdiction of the National Green Tribunal?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
n4783f06c417.x: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Forest Rights Act are outside the NGT's listed scope; the BD Act and EP Act are covered.
xa: Other Acts under NGT: **Water Act 1974**, **Water Cess 1977**, **Forest (Conservation) Act 1980**, **Air Act 1981**, **PLI 1991**.

The Forest Rights Act is of **2006**.
**PLI 1991** and **Water Cess 1977** were in the original **Schedule I**.

nd676465cadf.s: The National Biodiversity Authority, established in 2003 under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, is headquartered at:

xa: NBA is an **autonomous statutory body**; there is also an **NBA Fund**.

Foreigners need **NBA approval** to access bio-resources.

nenvironment-6-5.s: Which Act is described as umbrella legislation for environmental protection in India?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
nenvironment-6-5.x: The EP Act, 1986 is umbrella legislation; the NGT Act, 2010 relates to environmental justice.
n: The Environment (Protection) Act was enacted in 1986. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 12-13]
The Environment (Protection) Act is umbrella legislation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 12-13]
The NGT Act was enacted in 2010. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 12-13]
The NGT Act concerns environmental justice. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 12-13]
xa: **Biological Diversity Act 2002**: **biodiversity** and **benefit sharing**.
**Forest Rights Act 2006**: **forest-dwelling communities**.
**NEAA Act 1997**: **appeals** on environmental clearances.

nenvironment-38-1.s: The Wildlife (Protection) Act was enacted in:

n: The core area of the Wildlife (Protection) Act is wildlife. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
The core area of the Water (Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act is water pollution. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
The core area of the Forest (Conservation) Act is forest diversion and conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
The core area of the Air (Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act is air pollution. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]

Water pollution is associated with the Water Act, 1974. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
Forest conservation is associated with the Forest Conservation Act, 1980. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
Air pollution is associated with the Air Act, 1981. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
The Wildlife (Protection) Act was enacted in 1972. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
The Water (Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act was enacted in 1974. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
The Forest (Conservation) Act was enacted in 1980. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]

**Environment (Protection) Act 1986** — the **umbrella** law.
**NGT Act 2010** — **environmental justice**.

nenvironment-38-5.s: Which legislation is associated with biodiversity and benefit sharing?
nenvironment-38-5.x: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002, covers biodiversity and access and benefit sharing, following the CBD.

n: Biodiversity and benefit sharing are associated with the Biological Diversity Act, 2002. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
The core area of the Biological Diversity Act is biodiversity. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 66-68]
xs: The **Biological Diversity Act, 2002** deals with **biodiversity** and **benefit sharing** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The **EPA 1986** covers the **overall environment** (umbrella law).
The **NGT Act 2010** deals with **environmental justice**; the **Forest Rights Act 2006** with **forest-dwelling communities**.

Three tiers: **NBA** → **SBBs** → **BMCs**.
BD Act amended **2023**; **BD Rules 2024**.

ne8ee6ab5987.s: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 was distinctive because it provided for:
o: Strict liability for accidents involving hazardous substances
Establishment of the Central Pollution Control Board
ne8ee6ab5987.x: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 provided for strict liability in cases of accidents involving hazardous substances.
ne8ee6ab5987.tq: Associate the predecessor law with its distinctive liability principle.
xs: The **National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995** provided **strict liability** for damage from **hazardous-substance accidents** — option **(1)**.
**Appeals against environmental clearances** were the job of the **NEAA Act, 1997**.
CPCB was set up in **1974** under the **Water Act**, not by this Act.
xa: The **1995** Act was **never brought into force** and was **repealed by the NGT Act 2010**.
The **1995** Act was an **APPSC 2023** answer.
The **NGT** combines **original jurisdiction** with the **appellate role** of the NEAA.

n895b2305e30.s: The NGT combines which two roles associated earlier with separate environmental institutions?
o: Original jurisdiction over environmental disputes and the appellate role of the NEAA
n895b2305e30.x: The NGT combines original jurisdiction over environmental disputes with the appellate role earlier performed by the NEAA.
n895b2305e30.tq: Link the predecessor authority’s appellate role with the NGT’s original jurisdiction.
xs: The NGT combines **original jurisdiction over environmental disputes** with the **appellate role of the NEAA** — option **(2)**.
The **NEAA** (Act of **1997**) heard appeals against **environmental clearances**; the NGT absorbed that role when the NEAA Act was repealed in **2010**.
Research, education and budget work are not NGT roles — it is an **adjudicatory** body.
xa: The **National Environment Tribunal Act 1995** (strict liability) was never brought into force; repealed by the NGT Act **2010**.
The NGT disposes of cases within **6 months**; appeal to the **Supreme Court** within **90 days**.
⚠ NGT covers **7** Acts but **not** the **Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972** and **Forest Rights Act 2006**.

nenvironment-6-8.s: The role of the National Environment Appellate Authority, set up under its 1997 Act, was taken over by the:

n: The National Environment Appellate Authority was established under the National Environment Appellate Authority Act, 1997. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 12-13]
The National Environment Appellate Authority no longer exists in its original form. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 12-13]
The role of the National Environment Appellate Authority was subsequently taken over by the National Green Tribunal. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 12-13]
xa: The **National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995** was **never brought into force**; repealed by the NGT Act **2010**.

Acts under the NGT include the **Water Act 1974**, **Air Act 1981**, **EPA 1986** and **Biological Diversity Act 2002**.

n976b8d8da67.s: The Forest Survey of India is headquartered at:
n976b8d8da67.x: The Forest Survey of India, like the Wildlife Institute of India, is at Dehradun; BSI is at Kolkata and GBPNIHE at Kosi-Katarmal, Almora.

**NEERI** → **Nagpur**; **SACON** → **Coimbatore**.

n53b3e69f674.s: The Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History (SACON) is located at:

**NEERI** → **Nagpur**; **GBPNIHE** → **Kosi-Katarmal, Almora**.
CMLRE hosts **Bhavasagara**, the national deep-sea fauna repository.

n350ccde2fcd.s: The National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI) is located at:

**Lucknow** hosts **IITR** (toxicology); **Dehradun** hosts **WII** and **FSI**; **Coimbatore** hosts **SACON**.
xa: **BSI / ZSI** → **Kolkata**.
**GBPNIHE** → **Kosi-Katarmal, Almora**.
**CMLRE** (Bhavasagara) → **Kochi**.

n5beb8df537f.s: The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1971 at
n5beb8df537f.x: The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar in Iran.
n5beb8df537f.tq: Identify the treaty by its adoption place and year.
xs: The Ramsar Convention was adopted in **1971** at **Ramsar, Iran** — option **(3)**.

xa: India has been a Party since **1982**; first Indian site **Chilika (1981)**.
Three pillars: designate **wetlands of international importance**, **wise use** of all wetlands, **international cooperation**.
**World Wetlands Day** = **2 February**, the Ramsar adoption day.
Ramsar (**1971**) is **older than the Stockholm Conference** (**1972**).

n9648f816e9d.x: The Ramsar Convention Secretariat is located at Gland, Switzerland.

xs: The Ramsar Secretariat is at **Gland, Switzerland** — option **(4)**.

xa: Adopted **1971** at **Ramsar, Iran**.
**Montreux Record** (threatened sites): **Keoladeo NP** and **Loktak Lake**.
India has **101** Ramsar sites, the most in Asia; latest **Glaw Lake (Arunachal Pradesh)**, **3 Aug 2026**.

n099850f1bf3.s: The United Nations Conference on the Human Environment, 1972, was held at:

xa: It was the **APPSC 2025** answer.
Outcome: **Stockholm Declaration** (**26** principles) + Action Plan.
**UNEP** set up in **1972**; **5 June** became World Environment Day.
PM **Indira Gandhi** was the **only visiting head of government**.

n092fc2964e7.s: The headquarters of the United Nations Environment Programme, established in 1972, is located at:

xa: ⚠ **UNEP** (Stockholm **1972**) and **UNEA** (Rio+20, **2012**) are both in **Nairobi**.

nc69a68c75e6.s: The 1972 Stockholm Conference was the UN Conference on the:

**UNCCD** (**1994**) completes the three **Rio Conventions**.

na3b6aca8c02.s: CITES was adopted on 3 March 1973 at:

n8f707f4c40f.s: Which international agreement is also known as the 'Washington Convention'?

Establishment of the UNEA at Nairobi

nc9171c3bc56.s: Which of the following was an output of the Rio+20 Conference held in 2012?
o: The Montreal Protocol and Kyoto Protocol
Stockholm Declaration and creation of UNEP
The Future We Want and initiation of the SDG process
nc9171c3bc56.x: Rio+20, held in Rio de Janeiro in 2012, produced “The Future We Want”, launched the Sustainable Development Goal process and was associated with the High-Level Political Forum.

xs: **Rio+20** (**2012**) produced "**The Future We Want**" and launched the **SDG process** — option **(4)**.

xa: Rio+20 is also called **UNCSD**.

⚠ UNEA and UNEP are both in **Nairobi**.

n36cd16e2ebc.s: Agenda 21, an action plan for sustainable development at all levels, was an outcome of:
o: The UN Conference on Environment and Development, 1992
The World Summit on Sustainable Development, 2002
The UN Conference on Sustainable Development, 2012
n36cd16e2ebc.x: Agenda 21 came from UNCED, the 1992 Rio Earth Summit, the first international Earth Summit. Stockholm 1972 produced the Stockholm Declaration and UNEP, WSSD 2002 the Johannesburg Plan of Implementation, and Rio+20 'The Future We Want'.
xs: **Agenda 21** came from **UNCED** — the **UN Conference on Environment and Development** (**1992**), the Rio Earth Summit — option **(2)**.
**Stockholm 1972** gave the **Stockholm Declaration** and **UNEP**; **Rio+20** (**2012**) gave "**The Future We Want**".
xa: Rio **1992** = the **first international Earth Summit** (**APPSC 2025**).
Agenda 21 was an **APPSC-G2 2025** answer.
**Rio+5** (**1997**) reviewed Agenda 21.

n5cc48acb58e.s: The Global Biodiversity Framework Fund is set up under the:
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
Convention on Biological Diversity Secretariat alone
n5cc48acb58e.x: The Global Biodiversity Framework Fund is set up under the Global Environment Facility.

n45c3a2a05f6.s: The Convention on Migratory Species is also known as the:

nenvironment-4-2.s: The initial implementing partners of the Global Environment Facility were UNDP, UNEP and the:
nenvironment-4-2.x: GEF's first implementing partners were UNDP, UNEP and the World Bank; the CBD is a convention it funds.
n: The pilot Global Environment Facility (GEF) was agreed in 1990. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
The Global Environment Facility was established around the Rio Earth Summit. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
The initial implementing partners of the Global Environment Facility included the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
The initial implementing partners of the Global Environment Facility included the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP). [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]

xa: The GEF is the **financial mechanism** for the **CBD**, **UNFCCC**, **UNCCD**, **Minamata** and **Stockholm** Conventions.

na77859a34c9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the CITES Appendices?

Appendix II includes species not yet threatened with extinction
Trade in Appendix II species is controlled through permits
Appendix I species may be traded commercially without restrictions

n02bda03d62f.s: Red sanders, scientifically known as Pterocarpus santalinus, is
o: endemic to the Seshachalam and southern Eastern Ghats and listed as Endangered by IUCN
native only to the Western Ghats and listed as Vulnerable by IUCN
an invasive alien species of the Eastern Himalaya

n770983b1ee1.s: Under the Bonn Convention (CMS), endangered migratory species receiving strict protection are listed in:

ne5ad5bc263b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2050 goals of the Kunming-Montreal GBF?

na20fc58f093.s: Which organisation, a union of governments and NGOs, maintains the Red List of threatened species?

xa: IUCN dates from **1948**.

**WDPA** is kept by **UNEP-WCMC with IUCN**.

n7e1a67b26c0.s: Which of the following was among the first Indian sites designated under the Ramsar Convention?
