n9378bb49b67.s: Which of the following Indian wetlands are currently on the Montreux Record of the Ramsar Convention?
o: Keoladeo National Park and Loktak Lake
Keoladeo National Park and Wular Lake
n9378bb49b67.x: The Montreux Record lists Ramsar sites under threat; India's sites on it are Keoladeo NP and Loktak Lake. Chilika was on it but was removed after restoration, so options with Chilika are wrong; Kolleru and Wular are not on the Record.
n9378bb49b67.tq: Montreux = threatened list: Keoladeo + Loktak; Chilika removed.
xs: India's Montreux Record sites are **Keoladeo NP** and **Loktak Lake** — option **(2)**.
**Chilika** was removed after restoration, so options with Chilika are wrong.
The notes do not place **Kolleru** or **Wular** on the Record.
xa: ⚠ **Chilika** = first Indian site (**1981**) and removed from the Record.
The Montreux Record lists **threatened** Ramsar sites.
India: Party since **1982**; **101** sites.

neb29dabef3d.s: India has been a Party to the Ramsar Convention since:
neb29dabef3d.x: India joined in 1982 and has 101 Ramsar sites, the most in Asia.
xa: Three pillars: designate sites, **wise use**, **international cooperation**.
Earlier counts: **96** (IYB 2026), **98** (Apr 2026).
Only **26** sites till **2013**; **68** added after **2014**.

n3d4c97a05db.s: The decisions of the Stockholm Conference in India were implemented through the:
n3d4c97a05db.x: The Stockholm decisions were implemented in India through the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
n3d4c97a05db.tq: Match the international conference outcome with the specific Indian legal instrument.
xs: Stockholm decisions were implemented in India through the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** — option **(3)**.
The notes link Stockholm to the **EPA 1986** only; the **Wildlife Act 1972** implements **CITES**, and the **BD Act 2002** implements the **CBD/Nagoya**.
xa: Stockholm: **UN Conference on the Human Environment**, **5-16 June 1972**.
It produced the **Stockholm Declaration** (**26** principles) and **UNEP**.
PM **Indira Gandhi** linked **poverty and environment** there.

n31c6069983a.s: Species are moved between CITES Appendices through:
o: A vote of the Conference of the Parties
A decision of IUCN's Red List Committee
An automatic UNEP review every five years
An order of national wildlife authorities
n31c6069983a.x: Species move between CITES Appendices only through a vote of the Conference of the Parties.
xa: The COP meets **every 2-3 years**.
Example: **whale shark, oceanic whitetip, manta rays → I** at **CoP20** (2025).
**Indian star tortoise** uplisted to I on India's proposal at **CoP18, 2019**.

nfb1afd2ac5f.s: The principal Indian legislation implementing CITES is the
nfb1afd2ac5f.x: CITES is implemented in India through the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
nfb1afd2ac5f.tq: Identify the domestic implementing law instead of the related environmental statutes.
xs: CITES is implemented in India through the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** — option **(1)**.
The **BD Act 2002** implements the **CBD/Nagoya**; **EPA 1986** implemented **Stockholm**.
xa: The **2022 amendment** added a **CITES chapter** and **Schedule IV** for CITES-listed specimens.
India became a Party to CITES in **1976**.
**WCCB** was set up in **2007** under the WPA (**2006** amendment).

nb14c373d8d2.s: In which year did India become a Party to CITES?
nb14c373d8d2.x: India became a Party to CITES in 1976. 1973 is the year CITES was adopted, 1975 the year it entered into force, and 1982 the year India joined the Ramsar Convention.
xs: India became a Party to CITES in **1976** — option **(3)** (PYQ **2018**).
**1973** = adoption; **1975** = entry into force; **1982** = India joined **Ramsar**.
xa: Implementing law: **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.
India hosted **CoP3** (New Delhi, **1981**) — its only CITES COP.
India joined **CMS** in **1983**.

n70fe72be2ea.s: The Conference of the Parties to CITES ordinarily meets
n70fe72be2ea.x: The CITES COP meets every two to three years.
n70fe72be2ea.tq: Discriminate between the recurring conference interval and the fixed schedules of other environmental bodies.
xs: The CITES COP meets **every 2-3 years** — option **(3)**.
The notes give no yearly, five-yearly or UNEP-called schedule.
xa: Species move between Appendices only by **COP vote**.
⚠ **CBD** COPs meet **every two years**.

n9aeb316470b.s: Under the Kigali Amendment, India is associated with an HFC freeze by
n9aeb316470b.x: Under the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol, India's HFC freeze year is 2028.
n9aeb316470b.tq: Recall the treaty-specific target year rather than the protocol-adoption year.
xs: Under **Kigali**, India's **HFC freeze** is by **2028** — option **(3)**.
Kigali is an amendment to the **Montreal Protocol** (**1987**).
xa: Ozone Secretariat: **Nairobi**.
**Ozone Day**: **16 September**.
⚠ Some APP tables wrongly place the Montreal Protocol at **Helsinki**.

nae344767cb9.s: Kolleru Lake is associated with which of the following international conservation designations?
nae344767cb9.x: Kolleru is a Ramsar wetland of international importance.
nae344767cb9.tq: Use the location-to-treaty association without confusing wetlands with species-trade instruments.
xs: **Kolleru Lake** is a **Ramsar site** — option **(1)**.
It is AP's Ramsar wetland (designated **2002**).
xa: **Visakhapatnam wetlands** come under **Operation Lungs 2.0**.
India has **101** Ramsar sites.
Montreux Record (India): **Keoladeo** and **Loktak**.

nc84971a77ed.s: CITES CoP20 was historically significant because it was the:
o: First CITES COP held in Central Asia
First CITES COP held in Europe
First CITES COP held in Africa
First CITES COP held in South Asia
nc84971a77ed.x: CITES CoP20 was the first CITES Conference of the Parties held in Central Asia.
nc84971a77ed.tq: Test the precise regional description rather than the host-city name alone.
xs: **CITES CoP20** was the **first CITES COP in Central Asia** — option **(1)**.
It was held at **Samarkand, Uzbekistan**, **2025**.
xa: It marked **50 years** of CITES; **77 species** added.
It uplisted **whale shark, oceanic whitetip, manta rays** to App I.
India **defeated an EU proposal** on **Guggul**.

n4d7abbf4c43.s: The Cartagena Protocol primarily regulates the safe transfer, handling and use of:
o: Carbon credits generated by forest plantations
Endangered species traded across international borders
Living Modified Organisms resulting from modern biotechnology
n4d7abbf4c43.x: The Cartagena Protocol deals with the safe transfer, handling and use of Living Modified Organisms resulting from modern biotechnology.
n4d7abbf4c43.tq: Distinguish the subject matter of closely related environmental agreements.
xs: Cartagena regulates safe transfer, handling and use of **Living Modified Organisms (LMOs)** from modern biotechnology — option **(4)**.
Endangered-species trade is **CITES**; hazardous chemicals fall under **Rotterdam/Basel**.
xa: It was a **PYQ 2018** key.
**Advance Informed Agreement**: importing country consents before the first transboundary movement.
In India: nodal ministry **MoEF&CC**; GM approvals by **GEAC**.

n145c3cc1c9d.s: Under the Cali Fund on Digital Sequence Information, large users are expected to contribute:
n145c3cc1c9d.x: The Cali Fund, from CBD COP16 at Cali, expects large users of DSI to pay 1% of profits or 0.1% of revenue.
xa: COP16 resumed at **Rome, Feb 2025**.
COP16 also pushed **KMGBF** implementation incl. **30x30**.
NBA's **April 2025** regulations include rules on **DSI**.

nc1aea6c3c0e.s: Which of the following is a criticism directed at the Biological Diversity Amendment Act, 2023?
o: It transferred all biodiversity powers to the UNCCD
It completely abolished access and benefit-sharing mechanisms
It was criticised for diluting access and benefit-sharing and reducing the role of local communities
It prohibited the use of genetic resources for research
nc1aea6c3c0e.x: The amendment has been criticised for diluting access and benefit-sharing, increasing biopiracy risks and reducing the role of local communities.
nc1aea6c3c0e.tq: Find the option that accurately captures a criticism without converting it into an absolute legal prohibition.
xs: The **BD Amendment 2023** was criticised for **diluting ABS**, raising **biopiracy risk** and **cutting local communities' role** — option **(3)**.
It did not abolish ABS or hand powers to the **UNCCD**; India still runs ABS through the **NBA** and **BMCs**.
xa: India implements Nagoya via the **BD Act 2002** (amended **2023**) + **BD Rules 2024**.
NBA's **ABS/BD Regulations** (**April 2025**) include rules on **Digital Sequence Information**.
**BMCs** can **levy collection fees** on access to bio-resources.
ABS income: over **Rs 266 crore since 2008**; red sanders **45%**.

nenvironment-8-13.s: CBD COP16 was held in 2024 at:
nenvironment-8-13.x: COP14 was at Sharm el-Sheikh (2018), COP15 at Kunming and Montreal (2021-22) and COP16 at Cali (2024).
n: CBD COP 14 was held in 2018. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The venue of CBD COP 14 was Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
CBD COP 15 was held during 2021–22. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
CBD COP 15 was held in Kunming and Montreal. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
CBD COP 16 was held in 2024. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The venue of CBD COP 16 was Cali, Colombia. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
xa: COP 15 adopted the **KMGBF**: **4 goals**, **23 targets**.
COP 16 created the **Cali Fund** on **Digital Sequence Information (DSI)**.
COP 14 began the post-2020 framework — "**New Deal for Nature**".

nenvironment-3-4.x: Nagoya covers access and benefit sharing; Cartagena covers biosafety, the CBD biodiversity conservation and the UNCCD desertification.
n: The UNCCD focuses on desertification. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The UNCCD focuses on land degradation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The CBD focuses on biodiversity conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The Cartagena Protocol concerns biosafety. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The Cartagena Protocol concerns living modified organisms (LMOs) and genetically modified organisms (GMOs). [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The Nagoya Protocol concerns access and benefit sharing. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xa: Cartagena: adopted **2000**, in force **2003**, **173 parties**.
Nagoya: adopted **2010**, in force **2014**, **137 parties**; India ratified **2012**.
UNCCD was **established 1994**; linked with **SDG 15** and **Land Degradation Neutrality**.

nfffc4c151d7.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three objectives of the Convention on Biological Diversity?
o: Sustainable use of the components of biodiversity
Compulsory transfer of all genetic technologies to developing countries
Fair and equitable sharing of benefits from genetic resources
nfffc4c151d7.x: The CBD objectives are conservation, sustainable use and fair and equitable benefit-sharing. Compulsory transfer of all genetic technologies is not one of its objectives.
nfffc4c151d7.tq: Identify the option that extends the treaty beyond its stated three-objective structure.
xs: **Compulsory transfer of all genetic technologies** is not a CBD objective — option **(2)**.
The three objectives: **conservation**, **sustainable use**, and **fair and equitable benefit-sharing** from genetic resources.
xa: CBD opened at **Rio 1992**; in force **1993**; Secretariat **Montreal**.
Financial mechanism: **GEF** (also for UNFCCC).
APSBB's objectives **mirror the CBD**.

n2278bcab4b4.s: The Nagoya-Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol on Liability and Redress, adopted in 2010, is a supplementary protocol to the:
o: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
n2278bcab4b4.x: The Nagoya-Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol on Liability and Redress is supplementary to the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety and is therefore connected to the CBD framework.
n2278bcab4b4.tq: Distinguish a supplementary protocol from the principal protocol and its parent convention.
xs: The **Nagoya-Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol** on **Liability and Redress** (**2010**) supplements the **Cartagena Protocol** — option **(2)**.
Despite the "Nagoya" in its name, it is not under the **Nagoya Protocol on ABS**.
xa: Its parent chain: **Cartagena → CBD**.
Cartagena: adopted **2000**, in force **2003**, **173 parties**.
Cartagena regulates **LMOs** from modern biotechnology.

n7b9c85c6cc3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Cartagena Protocol?
o: Its Biosafety Clearing-House is a laboratory that tests all GM crops before export
Under Advance Informed Agreement, the importing country consents before the first transboundary movement of an LMO
It deals with biosafety and living modified organisms
LMO shipments carry documentation identifying the LMO
n7b9c85c6cc3.x: The Biosafety Clearing-House is an online platform for sharing LMO information and decisions, not a testing laboratory.
xa: Cartagena: adopted **2000**, in force **2003**.
**173 parties** incl. India.
India's GM approvals: **GEAC**.

n4a6a467fc41.s: In India, approvals for genetically engineered organisms are given by the:
n4a6a467fc41.x: The Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee approves genetically engineered organisms; MoEF&CC is the nodal ministry for the Cartagena Protocol.
xa: Nodal ministry for Cartagena: **MoEF&CC**.
Cartagena is named after **Cartagena, Colombia**.
⚠ Cartagena = **biosafety/LMOs**; Nagoya = **ABS**.

n10dc6b4fd5f.s: The Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety (adopted 2000) is a protocol under the:
n10dc6b4fd5f.x: The Cartagena Protocol is under the CBD; it entered into force in 2003 and is named after Cartagena, Colombia.
xa: **173 parties** incl. India.
Supplementary Protocol on **Liability and Redress** (**2010**) is under Cartagena.
**COP-15** also served as **10th MOP** Cartagena and **4th MOP** Nagoya.

n0e8d8ba533d.s: The Nagoya Protocol covers genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge relating to:
o: Only animal and human genetic material
Plants, animals and microorganisms, but not human genetic material
All genetic material, including human genetic material
n0e8d8ba533d.x: The Protocol covers plant, animal and microbial genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, while excluding human genetic material.
n0e8d8ba533d.tq: Identify the inclusion and exclusion in the scope of an international instrument.
xs: Nagoya covers **plant, animal and microbial** genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, **excluding human genetic material** — option **(2)**.
So options limited to plants/animals or including human material are wrong.
xa: **Utilisation** = R&D on genetic and/or **biochemical** composition (**APPSC 2025** key).
Pillars: **prior informed consent**, **Mutually Agreed Terms**, **compliance**.
NBA's **April 2025** regulations include rules on **Digital Sequence Information**.

n655aced79b8.s: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of the Nagoya Protocol?
o: Compliance against illegal acquisition of genetic resources
Compulsory transfer of all genetic resources to the National Biodiversity Authority
Mutually Agreed Terms for monetary and non-monetary benefits
n655aced79b8.x: The pillars are prior informed consent, Mutually Agreed Terms for benefit-sharing, and compliance against illegal acquisition. Compulsory transfer of all genetic resources is not a pillar.
n655aced79b8.tq: Find the option that introduces an authority or obligation not included among the stated pillars.
xs: **Compulsory transfer of all genetic resources to the NBA** is not a Nagoya pillar — option **(3)**.
The pillars: **prior informed consent**, **Mutually Agreed Terms** for monetary/non-monetary benefits, and **compliance** against illegal acquisition.
xa: India's implementing law: **BD Act 2002** (amended **2023**) + **BD Rules 2024**.
**BMCs** can **levy collection fees** on access to bio-resources in their area.
The NBA gives **ABS approvals** for foreign users.

n784877cd789.s: Under the Nagoya Protocol, 'utilisation of genetic resources' means:
o: Commercial sale of whole organisms across borders
Research and development on the genetic and/or biochemical composition of genetic resources
Cultivation of genetically modified crops for food
Conservation of genetic resources in gene banks only
n784877cd789.x: The Protocol defines utilisation as research and development on the genetic and/or biochemical composition of genetic resources. Cross-border sale of organisms is a trade matter (CITES), GM crop cultivation is a biosafety matter (Cartagena), and gene-bank storage alone is conservation, not utilisation.
n784877cd789.tq: Utilisation = R&D on genetic AND/OR biochemical composition.
xs: **Utilisation** = **R&D on the genetic and/or biochemical composition** of genetic resources — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2025** key).
Cross-border trade is a **CITES** matter; GM crops come under **Cartagena** (biosafety).
xa: Nagoya excludes **human genetic material**.
It is **legally binding**, under the **CBD**.
India ratified in **2012**; in force **2014**.

n5dfd6bbd3ba.s: India submitted its first National Report on the Nagoya Protocol with which of the following figures?
o: 3,556 IRCCs, constituting less than 30% of the global total
1,556 IRCCs, constituting over 60% of the global total
3,556 IRCCs, constituting over 60% of the global total
2,556 IRCCs, constituting over 50% of the global total
n5dfd6bbd3ba.x: India's first National Report recorded 3,556 IRCCs, more than 60% of the global total.
n5dfd6bbd3ba.tq: Split the option into two independently verifiable numerical parts.
xs: India's **1st National Report** on Nagoya recorded **3,556 IRCCs**, over **60%** of the global total — option **(3)**.
The other options change the count or the share.
xa: India ratified Nagoya in **2012**; in force **2014**.
NBA's **April 2025** regulations cover **Digital Sequence Information**.
India's ABS income: over **Rs 266 crore since 2008**.

nfffebaeba5e.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board aims at achieving zero loss of biodiversity and ecosystem services by:
nfffebaeba5e.x: The AP State Biodiversity Board aims at zero loss of biodiversity and ecosystem services by 2050.
nfffebaeba5e.tq: Use the stated target year rather than inferring it from the decade-based observances.
xs: APSBB aims at **zero loss of biodiversity and ecosystem services by 2050** — option **(3)**.
**2030** is the KMGBF target year, not APSBB's aim.
xa: APSBB objectives **mirror the CBD**.
APSBB Chairman: **Neelayapalem Vijay Kumar**; plans **OECMs** outside PAs to help meet **30x30**.
KMGBF goals also run to **2050**.

n9902b770fd2.s: The Aichi Biodiversity Targets were adopted at which Conference of the Parties and in which year?
n9902b770fd2.x: The 20 Aichi Biodiversity Targets were adopted at CBD COP10, held at Nagoya in 2010. COP12 at Pyeongchang reviewed their progress but did not adopt them.
n9902b770fd2.tq: Use the adoption venue and year, while distinguishing adoption from later review.
xs: The **Aichi Targets** were adopted at **COP10, Nagoya, 2010** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **COP12, Pyeongchang** (**2014**) only **reviewed** them; **COP15** adopted the **KMGBF**; **COP16** was Cali.
xa: Structure: **20 targets** under **5 strategic goals**; plan **2011-2020**.
**None of the 20** were fully met by **2020** (**Global Biodiversity Outlook 5**).
The **Nagoya Protocol** was adopted at the same **COP10**.

ncedb314570f.s: The Aichi Biodiversity Targets under the Strategic Plan 2011-2020 comprised how many targets?
ncedb314570f.x: There were 20 Aichi targets under five strategic goals; Global Biodiversity Outlook 5 found none fully met.
xa: Adopted at **COP10, Nagoya (2010)**.
Successor: **KMGBF** — **23** targets, **4** goals.
KMGBF adds numeric targets, a **monitoring framework** and finance.

na91c3a5933a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about biodiversity instruments?
o: The Cartagena Protocol concerns biosafety and living modified organisms
The Nagoya Protocol concerns access and benefit-sharing
The Kunming-Montreal GBF has four 2050 goals and 23 targets for 2030
na91c3a5933a.x: The Aichi Targets numbered 20 for 2011-2020; 23 targets belong to the Kunming-Montreal GBF.
xa: Aichi and Nagoya were both adopted at **COP10, Nagoya, 2010**.
KMGBF: **COP15, Montreal, December 2022**.

na1481155ff5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework?
o: It has four goals for 2050 and 23 targets for 2030
It was adopted at CBD COP16 at Cali in 2024
It seeks to halve food waste
na1481155ff5.x: The framework was adopted at COP-15 in December 2022 (Montreal), not at COP16.
xa: **Target 18**: cut **harmful subsidies** by at least **US$500 billion a year**.
**Target 6**: cut invasive alien species by **at least 50%**.
**Target 7**: halve excess **nutrients** and **pesticide** risk.
⚠ **30x30** = protection (Target 3); restoring **30% of degraded** ecosystems = **Target 2**.

n64d9e7cae51.s: The Aichi Biodiversity Targets were adopted in 2010 at:
n64d9e7cae51.x: The sequence is Nagoya 2010 (Aichi Targets), Kunming 2021, Montreal December 2022 (KMGBF) and Cali October 2024.
xa: ⚠ KMGBF was **adopted at Montreal**, not Kunming.
COP16 resumed at **Rome, Feb 2025**.
Aichi: **20** targets, **2011-2020**; KMGBF: **23** targets for **2030**.
COP15: **China presidency, Canada host**.

nf746e473689.s: Target 2 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework relates to which of the following?
o: Restoration of 30% of degraded land and water ecosystems
Conservation of 30% of land and oceans
Reducing harmful subsidies by US$500 billion annually
nf746e473689.x: Target 2 calls for effective restoration of 30% of degraded land and water ecosystems by 2030. Conservation of 30% of land and oceans is Target 3.
nf746e473689.tq: Discriminate between the closely related restoration and protection targets.
xs: **Target 2** = effective **restoration of 30% of degraded** land and water ecosystems — option **(2)**.
**Conservation of 30% of land and oceans** is **Target 3** (**30x30**); food waste is **Target 16**; subsidies are **Target 18**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes (Block06) wrongly call restoration "the 30x30 target".
**Target 1**: bring loss of high-biodiversity areas **close to zero**.
**Target 6**: cut invasive alien species by **at least 50%**.

nd639f09b484.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the KMGBF targets for 2030?
o: Target 3 seeks to conserve 30% of land and 30% of oceans/waters
Target 7 seeks to halve excess nutrients and overall pesticide risk
Target 6 seeks to halve global food waste
Target 16 seeks to halve global food waste
nd639f09b484.x: Target 6 seeks to cut introduction and establishment of invasive alien species by at least 50%; halving food waste is Target 16.
xa: **Target 18**: cut **harmful subsidies** by **US$500 billion a year**.
**Target 2**: restore **30% of degraded** ecosystems.
**Target 19**: mobilise **US$200 billion a year** by **2030**.

nc0b9fb0d933.s: Target 18 calls for reducing harmful subsidies by at least:
nc0b9fb0d933.x: Target 18 calls for a reduction of harmful subsidies by at least US$500 billion a year.
nc0b9fb0d933.tq: Distinguish the annual harmful-subsidy figure from the wider biodiversity-finance figures.
xs: **Target 18**: reduce harmful subsidies by at least **US$500 billion a year** — option **(1)**.
**US$700 billion** is the **Goal D** finance gap; **US$200 billion** is the **Target 19** mobilisation goal.
xa: ⚠ Remember the trio: **200** mobilise, **500** subsidies, **700** gap.
KMGBF new features: numeric targets (**30x30**, **US$500 bn** subsidies), monitoring framework, finance.
**GBF Fund** is set up under the **GEF**.

ncbf32455306.s: Target 19 of the KMGBF seeks mobilisation of at least how much annually by 2030 from all sources?
ncbf32455306.x: Target 19 seeks at least US$200 billion per year by 2030 from all sources. This is the overall resource-mobilisation target, not the size of the GBF Fund itself.
ncbf32455306.tq: Distinguish the overall annual mobilisation target from related finance figures.
xs: **Target 19**: mobilise at least **US$200 billion a year by 2030** from all sources — option **(4)**.
**US$500 billion** = subsidy cut (**Target 18**); **US$700 billion** = **Goal D** finance gap.
xa: ⚠ Some notes tie **US$200 billion** to the **GBFF** — it is the overall target.
The **GBF Fund** sits under the **GEF**.
**Cali Fund**: large DSI users pay **1% of profits or 0.1% of revenue**.

n327979aebfa.s: India’s updated National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan for 2024–2030 contains:
n327979aebfa.x: India’s updated NBSAP contains 23 national targets matching the 23 targets of the KMGBF.
n327979aebfa.tq: Match the national target count with the corresponding global framework.
xs: India's updated NBSAP (**2024-2030**) has **23 national targets**, matching the **KMGBF** — option **(1)**.
**20** was the Aichi count; **21** was an older KMGBF draft.
xa: Released at **COP16, Cali (Oct 2024)**; aligned with **30x30**.
Some notes call it **NBSAP-II, 2023-2030**.
**Target 13** = access and benefit-sharing.

nb3477c6b3ba.s: India's seventh National Report to the Convention on Biological Diversity was notable because it represented:
o: The first review of the Sendai Framework targets
The first national report under CITES
The first report on Ramsar implementation in India
The first full review against the 23 targets of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework
nb3477c6b3ba.x: India's seventh CBD National Report was the first full review against all 23 KMGBF targets.
nb3477c6b3ba.tq: Separate the reporting mechanism of CBD from those of CITES, Ramsar and disaster-risk frameworks.
xs: India's **7th National Report (NR7)** was the **first full review against the 23 KMGBF targets** — option **(4)**.
It is a **CBD** report, not a CITES, Ramsar or Sendai one.
xa: National reports come under **Article 26** of the CBD, about every **four years**.
Progress is tracked through **headline indicators** of the KMGBF monitoring framework.
NBA SOP under **Sec. 38, BD Act**: **159 plant** and **173 animal** species notified.

n9b9b0656ca8.s: The CITES Trade Database is maintained by:
n9b9b0656ca8.x: The CITES Trade Database is kept by UNEP-WCMC, not the Secretariat.
xa: **TRAFFIC**: trade-monitoring network, joint programme of **WWF and IUCN** (**1976**).
**ICCWC** links CITES with **INTERPOL, UNODC, WCO**.
**MIKE** tracks elephant poaching.

n2b2327ff0e4.s: The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau, which enforces CITES and prevents wildlife trafficking, functions under the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
n2b2327ff0e4.x: WCCB is a statutory body under MoEFCC.
xa: Set up in **2007** under the **WPA** (**2006** amendment); HQ **New Delhi**.
Helps **Customs** inspect wildlife consignments under **CITES and EXIM policy**.
Builds the **wildlife-crime database**.

nf4f98c12c75.x: MIKE tracks elephant poaching; WCCB assists Customs and builds the wildlife-crime database.
xa: WCCB: set up **2007**, HQ **New Delhi**.
**ICCWC** links CITES with **INTERPOL, UNODC, WCO**.
**TRAFFIC** = **WWF and IUCN** joint programme.

n607ff161a00.s: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 created a new Schedule IV for:
o: Specimens listed in the CITES Appendices
n607ff161a00.x: The amendment added a CITES chapter and Schedule IV for CITES-listed specimens; invasive alien species fall under a separate new section.
xa: It also provides **Management and Scientific Authorities**.
Parent Act: **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.
**WCCB** was created by the WPA's **2006** amendment (set up **2007**).

n77335ff7fc5.s: The golden gecko, endemic to Andhra Pradesh, is listed in which CITES Appendix?
n77335ff7fc5.x: The golden gecko is in Appendix II; tiger and clouded leopard are in Appendix I and red sanders in Appendix II.
xa: **Indian and Chinese pangolins** — **I**; over **500,000** pangolins seized globally **2016-2024**.
**Rosewood (Dalbergia)** and **striped hyena** — **II**.
Red sanders is IUCN **Endangered**.

nb4fd7a57bed.s: CITES CoP19 (2022), which added 54 sharks and rays to Appendix II, was held in:
nb4fd7a57bed.x: CoP19 was held in Panama in 2022; the first CITES CoP in Central Asia was CoP20 at Samarkand in 2025.
xa: CoP20 uplisted **whale shark, oceanic whitetip, manta rays** to App I.
**Rosewood (Dalbergia)** is in Appendix **II**.
COP meets **every 2-3 years**.

n4f35843ead5.s: The financial mechanism associated with the Convention on Biological Diversity, and also with the UNFCCC, is the:
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
n4f35843ead5.x: The Global Environment Facility serves as a financial mechanism for both the CBD and the UNFCCC.
n4f35843ead5.tq: Identify the common financial institution rather than a treaty body or conservation network.
xs: The **Global Environment Facility (GEF)** is the financial mechanism of the **CBD** and **UNFCCC** — option **(2)**.
**IUCN** is a union of governments and NGOs; **UNEA** is the Rio+20 assembly.
xa: The **GBF Fund** was set up under the **GEF**.
⚠ Target 19's **US$200 billion a year** is the overall goal, not the GBF Fund's size.
**COP16** added the **Cali Fund** on DSI.

n9cbb8f9cc93.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India and the Nagoya Protocol?
o: India implements it through the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (amended 2023)
India ratified the Nagoya Protocol in 2014
The NBA notified ABS/BD Regulations in April 2025, including rules on DSI
The Protocol entered into force in 2014
n9cbb8f9cc93.x: India ratified the Protocol in 2012; 2014 is the year it entered into force.
xa: India's **1st National Report**: **3,556** Certificates of Compliance, **>60%** of global total.
**Target 13** of India's NBSAP = access and benefit-sharing.
Criticism: **BD Amendment 2023** said to dilute ABS and raise biopiracy risk.

n3a27415efc7.s: Under India's biodiversity framework, which bodies can levy collection fees for access to biological resources in their area?
n3a27415efc7.x: BMCs can levy collection fees; the NBA at Chennai gives ABS approvals for foreign users.
xa: The **NBA Fund** is a statutory fund under the Act.
BMCs maintain **People's Biodiversity Registers**.
**Red Sanders** gives **45%** of India's ABS income.

n2d87d3ad785.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about indigenous peoples and local communities under the biodiversity framework?
o: COP15 recognised their essential role in conservation and management
KMGBF Target 22 seeks their full participation and rights over lands and resources
The 30x30 target seeks to conserve 30% of land and 30% of oceans by 2030
The 30x30 objective is meant to disregard indigenous territories
n2d87d3ad785.x: Implementation of 30x30 is to respect indigenous territories, not disregard them.
xa: India's route: **BMCs, PBRs and ABS** carry benefits to local and tribal communities.
**COP16** set up a permanent subsidiary body on Indigenous peoples (**Art. 8(j)**).
Criticism: **BD Amendment 2023** said to cut local communities' role.

n90bf9100bd9.s: The Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ), commonly called the High Seas Treaty, entered into force on
n90bf9100bd9.x: The BBNJ Agreement entered into force on 17 January 2026.
n90bf9100bd9.tq: Distinguish the entry-into-force date from the date of India’s signature.
xs: The **BBNJ** entered into force on **17 January 2026** — option **(4)**.
India **signed** it in **Sept 2024**.
xa: Full name: **Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction**.
Only **1.66%** of high seas are protected (WDPA).
It is listed among current developments with **UNCCD COP-17** in **Mongolia**.

nf78cc09efe3.s: India ratified the Basel Convention on hazardous waste in:
nf78cc09efe3.x: India ratified Basel in June 1992; the Convention was adopted in 1989 and entered into force in 1992.
xa: Basel has **190 Parties**; Secretariat **Geneva**.
Rotterdam = **PIC** convention; Secretariat **Geneva/Rome**.
Montreal Protocol: **1987**; Ozone Secretariat **Nairobi**.

nf1329d5500e.s: International Day for Biological Diversity is observed on
nf1329d5500e.x: International Day for Biological Diversity is observed annually on 22 May.
nf1329d5500e.tq: Recall the exact date of a named international observance.
xs: **International Day for Biological Diversity** = **22 May** — option **(4)**; CBD text adopted **22 May 1992**.
**5 June** = World Environment Day; **17 June** = Desertification and Drought Day; **16 September** = Ozone Day.
xa: ⚠ **2 Feb** Ramsar, **3 Mar** CITES, **22 May** CBD, **5 June** Stockholm.
International Year of Biodiversity: **2010**.
UN Decade on Biodiversity: **2011-2020**.

nba6b52a0193.s: The Nagoya Protocol is a legally binding supplementary agreement to the:
nba6b52a0193.x: The Nagoya Protocol is a legally binding supplementary agreement to the CBD, not a voluntary declaration.
xa: **137 parties** incl. India.
India implements it via the **BD Act 2002** (amended **2023**) and **BD Rules 2024**.
**PYQ 2025**: Nagoya is part of the **CBD**.

ne5cef07eeec.s: The '30x30' biodiversity target to conserve 30% of land and 30% of oceans by 2030 is part of the:
ne5cef07eeec.x: 30x30 is a biodiversity conservation target of the Kunming-Montreal GBF, not a renewable-energy target.
xa: ⚠ 30x30 = **protection** (Target 3); restoration = **Target 2**.
**WDPA** tracks Target 3 → ~**10%** of oceans protected, only **1.66%** of high seas.
30x30 is to **respect indigenous territories** (Target 22).

n1014729051b.s: The BBNJ Agreement, referred to in the context of marine conservation, deals primarily with:
o: Protection of biodiversity inside national parks
Biodiversity beyond national jurisdiction in the high seas
Biosafety regulation of genetically modified crops
n1014729051b.x: The BBNJ Agreement (High Seas Treaty) concerns marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction, i.e. the high seas. It entered into force on 17 January 2026; India signed it in September 2024. Wetlands (Ramsar), national parks and GM-crop biosafety (Cartagena) are covered by other instruments.
n1014729051b.tq: Expand the acronym conceptually and distinguish high-seas governance from domestic conservation.
xs: BBNJ deals with **biodiversity beyond national jurisdiction** in the **high seas** — option **(3)**.
Wetlands are **Ramsar**; GM-crop biosafety is **Cartagena**.
xa: Entered into force **17 January 2026**; India signed **Sept 2024**.
Only **1.66%** of the high seas are protected.
~**10%** of oceans are protected (WDPA).

n3acd63381cb.s: Which of the following is consistent with the scope of sustainable development?
o: Running down natural capital to maximise current output
Excluding disadvantaged groups from development planning
Treating environmental protection and development as mutually exclusive
Meeting present needs while promoting equity within and across generations
n3acd63381cb.x: Sustainable development includes meeting present needs, equity within and across generations, and inclusion. It rejects depletion of natural capital and the opposition of environment to development.
n3acd63381cb.tq: Select the option that combines present needs, equity and inclusion.
xs: Sustainable development includes **meeting present needs** with **equity within and across generations** — option **(4)**.
It **excludes** growth that **runs down natural capital** and treating **environment and development as opposites**.
It also stresses **inclusion** ("**leave no one behind**"), so excluding disadvantaged groups is wrong.
xa: **NEP 2006**: conservation and livelihood security are **linked, not opposed**.
Present generation **may use** resources but must not **compromise** future generations.
First definition: **Brundtland 1987**.

n84f9d9337f3.s: The National Environment Policy, 2006 treats conservation and livelihood security as:
o: Objectives relevant only to urban areas
n84f9d9337f3.x: The National Environment Policy, 2006 holds that conservation and livelihood security are linked rather than opposed.
xa: Sustainable development includes meeting **present needs** — development is not rejected.
It excludes growth that **runs down natural capital**.
Pillars: **economic development, social equity, environmental protection**.

n209e12f9b2d.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three classic pillars of sustainable development?
n209e12f9b2d.x: The three classic pillars are economic development, social equity and environmental protection. Military security is not one of them.
n209e12f9b2d.tq: Identify the outsider from the standard three-pillar framework.
xs: **Military security** is not a classic pillar — option **(1)**.
The three pillars: **economic development**, **social equity**, **environmental protection**.
xa: ⚠ Odd-one-out trap: **political, military or cultural** dimensions are not pillars.
**Triple bottom line**: **People, Planet, Profit** — the business version.
The idea is to **balance all three**, not maximise any one.

nc071cd3381a.s: In the business-oriented expression of sustainable development, the triple bottom line is represented by:
nc071cd3381a.x: The triple bottom line is commonly expressed as People, Planet and Profit, corresponding broadly to social, environmental and economic concerns.
nc071cd3381a.tq: Recall the exact three-part phrase used for the business version of sustainability.
xs: The **triple bottom line** = **People, Planet, Profit** — option **(1)**.
It is the **business version** of the three pillars: social, environmental, economic.
xa: Classic pillars: **economic development**, **social equity**, **environmental protection**.
The aim is **balance**, not maximising one.
⚠ Political, military or cultural dimensions are **not** pillars.

ne67fb96a2ea.s: The National Green Tribunal, headquartered at New Delhi, does NOT have a bench at:
ne67fb96a2ea.x: NGT benches are at Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai, not Hyderabad.
xa: It must apply **sustainable development**, **precautionary** and **polluter-pays** principles.
**M.C. Mehta v. UoI (1996)** applied polluter pays.
**Vellore (1996)** applied all three.

nenvironment-2-6.s: The Wetlands (Conservation & Management) Rules, 2010 were framed on the recommendation of an Expert Panel under the:
o: National Action Plan on Climate Change, 2008
nenvironment-2-6.x: An Expert Panel constituted under the National Environment Policy, 2006 led to the Wetlands Rules, 2010.
n: The National Environment Policy was formulated in 2006. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Environment Policy, 2006, provides the policy framework for environmental conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Environment Policy, 2006, provides the policy framework for sustainable development. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The Wetlands (Conservation & Management) Rules, 2010, were framed on the recommendation of an Expert Panel. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The Expert Panel was constituted under the provisions of the National Environment Policy, 2006. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
xa: NEP 2006: **conservation** and **livelihood security** are **linked, not opposed**.
Sustainable development excludes **growth that runs down natural capital**.
The present generation **may use** resources, but not so as to **compromise** future generations.

nenvironment-40-5.s: Our Common Future (the Brundtland Report) was published in:
nenvironment-40-5.x: The order is Stockholm Declaration 1972, Our Common Future 1987, Rio Declaration 1992 and Johannesburg Declaration 2002.
n: The Stockholm Declaration was issued in 1972. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
Our Common Future was published in 1987. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
The Rio Declaration on Environment and Development was issued in 1992. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
The Johannesburg Declaration was issued in 2002. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
xa: **Millennium Declaration** (**2000**): the **MDGs framework**.
**The Future We Want** (**2012**): the **Rio+20 outcome document**.
First definition of sustainable development = **Brundtland 1987**.

nbdaa1933963.s: The principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) implies that:
o: Responsibilities are shared, but developed nations carry greater duties
Only developing countries bear responsibility for environmental protection
All countries have identical environmental duties and identical capacities
Environmental duties are restricted to countries that caused no historical pollution
nbdaa1933963.x: CBDR recognises shared responsibility while assigning greater duties to developed nations in view of their capacities and historical contribution.
nbdaa1933963.tq: Discriminate between shared responsibility and identical responsibility.
xs: **CBDR**: duties are **shared but differentiated**; **developed nations carry more** — option **(1)**.
So duties are neither identical for all nor placed only on developing countries.
xa: Other principles: **intergenerational equity**, **precautionary**, **polluter pays**, **carrying capacity**.
All were endorsed at **Rio 1992** and underpin international environmental law.
The **Rio Declaration** has **27 principles**.

n80cc9ad1b41.s: The National Green Tribunal is required to apply which combination of principles while adjudicating environmental cases?
o: Sustainable development, precautionary principle and polluter-pays principle
Public trust doctrine, absolute liability and eminent domain
Common but differentiated responsibilities, prior appropriation and res judicata
Inter-generational equity, federal supremacy and parliamentary privilege
n80cc9ad1b41.x: The NGT must apply the principles of sustainable development, precautionary action and polluter pays.
n80cc9ad1b41.tq: Select the complete statutory-principle combination rather than a partly related doctrine.
xs: The NGT must apply **sustainable development**, **precautionary** and **polluter-pays** principles — option **(1)**.
The other combinations are not in its mandate.
xa: HQ **New Delhi**; benches **Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata, Chennai**.
Disposal within **6 months**.
**Vellore (1996)** brought these principles into Indian environmental law.

n5d856c906b5.s: Which of the following was NOT an outcome associated with the 1992 United Nations Conference on Environment and Development?
n5d856c906b5.x: The Future We Want was adopted at the 2012 Rio+20 Conference. Agenda 21, the Rio Declaration, the UNFCCC and the CBD were associated with the 1992 Earth Summit.
n5d856c906b5.tq: Use the summit-outcome association to eliminate the later document.
xs: "**The Future We Want**" came from **Rio+20** (**2012**), not **UNCED 1992** — option **(3)**.
Rio **1992** gave **Agenda 21**, the **Rio Declaration** (**27 principles**), **UNFCCC**, **CBD** and **Forest Principles**.
xa: UNCED: **3-14 June 1992**, **Rio de Janeiro** — the **first Earth Summit**.
Rio+20 (**UNCSD**) also decided to frame the **SDGs** and stressed the **green economy**.
**WSSD 2002** (Johannesburg) gave the **Johannesburg Plan of Implementation**.

nf2968d80572.s: The Rio Declaration adopted at the 1992 Earth Summit contained how many principles?
nf2968d80572.x: The Rio Declaration contains 27 principles relating to environment and development.
nf2968d80572.tq: Separate the numerical details of the Rio Declaration from SDG figures.
xs: The **Rio Declaration** has **27 principles** — option **(3)**.
**17** is the number of **SDGs**; **169** the number of SDG **targets**.
xa: It was adopted at **UNCED**, **3-14 June 1992**, Rio de Janeiro.
Other Rio outputs: **Agenda 21**, **UNFCCC**, **CBD**, **Forest Principles**.
⚠ **17 - 169 - 232** = SDGs - targets - indicators.

n4457b881269.s: The 2012 UN Conference on Sustainable Development (Rio+20) produced the document titled:
n4457b881269.x: Rio+20 adopted 'The Future We Want' and decided to frame the SDGs.
xa: It was held in **June 2012** at **Rio de Janeiro**.
It also stressed the **green economy**.
The SDGs were adopted in **2015** at **New York**.

n33a33e58fbe.s: The document titled 'Transforming our World: the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development' contains:
n33a33e58fbe.x: The 2030 Agenda contains 17 Sustainable Development Goals and 169 targets. It is also associated with 232 indicators.
n33a33e58fbe.tq: Separate goals, targets and indicators rather than interchanging their figures.
xs: The **2030 Agenda** has **17 goals** and **169 targets** — option **(1)**.
**232** is the number of **indicators**, not targets; **27** is the Rio Declaration's principle count.
xa: ⚠ **17 - 169 - 232** = SDGs - targets - indicators.
Adopted **25 Sept 2015**, New York; in force **2016**.
**MDGs** (**2000-2015**) came before.

n266a7a38b84.s: Agenda 2030 and the Sustainable Development Goals were adopted in:
n266a7a38b84.x: The MDGs began in 2000, WSSD was in 2002, Rio+20 in 2012 and Agenda 2030 was adopted in 2015.
xa: The MDGs ran **2000-2015**.
SDGs in force from **2016**.
Rio+20 made the **decision to frame the SDGs**.

nenvironment-3-1.s: The first World Conference on Environment was held at which place and in which year?
nenvironment-3-1.x: The first world conference on the environment was held at Stockholm in 1972 (UNCHE). Rio (1992) was the Earth Summit and Johannesburg (2002) Rio+10.
nenvironment-3-1.tq: Arrange the environment summits in time order.
n: The Stockholm Conference was the first World Conference on Environment. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The Stockholm Conference was held in 1972. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xs: The first **World Conference on Environment** was at **Stockholm** in **1972** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was the **UN Conference on Human Environment (UNCHE)** — the **origin** of **UNEP**.
**Rio de Janeiro, 1992** was the **Earth Summit**; **New York, 1997** was **Rio+5**; **Johannesburg, 2002** was **Rio+10 (WSSD)**.
xa: **Rio 1992** adopted **Agenda 21**, the **UNFCCC** and **CBD**, and the **Rio Declaration** (**27 principles**).
**Rio+20 (2012)** produced "**The Future We Want**".
**2015** UN summit: "**Transforming our World: the 2030 Agenda**" — **17 SDGs, 169 targets**.

nenvironment-3-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about UNEP?
o: Its headquarters is in Nairobi, Kenya.
It focuses on global environmental coordination.
It originated from the Rio Earth Summit, 1992.
nenvironment-3-2.x: UNEP came out of the 1972 Stockholm Conference, not the 1992 Rio summit. It is headquartered in Nairobi.
n: The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) was established in 1972. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The headquarters of UNEP is in Nairobi, Kenya. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
The origin of UNEP was the Stockholm Conference. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
UNEP is responsible for global environmental coordination. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #3 · pp 6-8]
xa: Stockholm **1972** was the **first major global environmental conference**, on the **Human Environment**.
Rio **1992** (UNCED) adopted **Agenda 21**, the **UNFCCC** and **CBD**.
The **Stockholm Declaration** (**1972**) concerns the **human environment**.

nenvironment-8-14.s: The Kyoto conference on climate change was held in:
nenvironment-8-14.x: Stockholm was 1972, Rio 1992, Kyoto 1997 (climate change) and Johannesburg 2002 (sustainable development).
n: The Stockholm conference concerned the Human Environment. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Rio conference was called UNCED or the Earth Summit. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Kyoto conference was held in 1997. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Kyoto conference concerned climate change. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Johannesburg conference concerned sustainable development. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
xa: Rio **1992** was the **first Earth Summit**; it gave **Agenda 21**.
**Rio+5** was also in **1997**, in **New York**.
⚠ **17 - 169 - 232** = SDGs - targets - indicators.

nenvironment-40-6.s: The Millennium Declaration provided the framework for the:
nenvironment-40-6.x: The Millennium Declaration set up the MDGs; Agenda 21 is the action plan and 'The Future We Want' came from Rio+20 in 2012.
n: Agenda 21 is a global action plan for sustainable development. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
The Forest Principles concern the sustainable management of forests. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
The Future We Want was issued in 2012. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
The Future We Want is the Rio+20 outcome document. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
The Millennium Declaration provides the MDGs framework. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
xa: **Agenda 21** was adopted in **1992**, for local, national and global levels.
The **MDGs (2000-2015)** preceded the SDGs.
**Johannesburg Declaration** (**2002**): **WSSD** — implementation commitments.

nenvironment-40-15.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Agenda 21 is a comprehensive action plan for the 21st century
Our Common Future defined sustainable development
The Rio Declaration sets out 27 principles on environment and development
The Forest Principles are a legally binding treaty on forests
nenvironment-40-15.x: The Forest Principles are a non-binding statement on the sustainable management of forests.
n: Our Common Future concerns sustainable development. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
The Rio Declaration on Environment and Development concerns sustainable development and environmental principles. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
Agenda 21 was adopted in 1992. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
The Forest Principles were adopted in 1992. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 70-71]
xa: Sustainable development's three pillars: **economic development**, **social equity**, **environmental protection**.
**Triple bottom line**: **People, Planet, Profit**.
Principles endorsed at **Rio 1992**: **precautionary principle**, **polluter pays**, **CBDR**, **intergenerational equity**.

o: Adding only gross industrial output to conventional GDP
Subtracting unpaid household work from GDP
Adjusting GDP for natural-resource depletion and environmental damage
Measuring only the value of protected forests
ncb2986509f9.x: Green GDP adjusts conventional GDP to account for natural-resource depletion and environmental damage.
ncb2986509f9.tq: Distinguish an environmentally adjusted economic measure from a social-progress indicator.
xs: **Green GDP** = GDP adjusted for **natural-resource depletion and environmental damage** — option **(3)**.
Subtracting pollution and adding **unpaid work** is the **GPI**.
xa: **Ecological footprint**: productive land and sea needed, in **global hectares**.
**Earth Overshoot Day**: when demand exceeds what Earth regenerates that year.
India: **99th of 167** in **SDR 2025**.

nac449a96d95.s: Which measure of sustainability adds unpaid work and subtracts pollution, crime and resource loss?
nac449a96d95.x: The Genuine Progress Indicator makes these adjustments; Earth Overshoot Day marks when humanity's demand exceeds what Earth can regenerate that year.
xa: **Green GDP**: GDP adjusted for **natural-resource depletion** and **environmental damage**.
**Ecological footprint**: productive land and sea needed to meet consumption and absorb wastes, in **global hectares**.
India ranked **99th of 167** in the **Sustainable Development Report 2025** — first time in the top 100; report by **UN SDSN**.

n8fc799b6082.s: The ecological footprint of a population refers to the:
o: Annual date on which its natural resources are exhausted
Amount of carbon dioxide emitted by its industries alone
Productive land and sea needed to meet its consumption and absorb its wastes
Total number of endangered species in its territory
n8fc799b6082.x: An ecological footprint estimates the productive land and sea area required to supply consumption and absorb generated wastes, expressed in global hectares.
n8fc799b6082.tq: Use the function of the measure to distinguish it from emissions and biodiversity counts.
xs: **Ecological footprint** = **productive land and sea** needed to meet consumption and **absorb wastes** — option **(3)**.
It is measured in **global hectares**; the annual date is **Earth Overshoot Day**.
xa: **Carrying capacity**: use must stay within what ecosystems can support.
**GPI** subtracts pollution, crime and resource loss.
**Green GDP** adjusts for natural-resource depletion.

n200d0406df9.s: Which set of measures is associated with the Sustainability and Climate Resilience pillar of Swarna Andhra @2047?
o: Renewable energy, green mobility and sustainable urban planning
Coal expansion, private transport and dispersed urbanisation
Nuclear energy, rural depopulation and industrial zoning
River diversion, road widening and conventional urban planning
n200d0406df9.x: The pillar includes renewable energy, green mobility and sustainable urban planning.
n200d0406df9.tq: Select the option containing the complete set of measures linked to the pillar.
xs: The **Sustainability and Climate Resilience** pillar covers **renewable energy, green mobility, sustainable urban planning** — option **(1)**.
The other options do not appear in the notes.
xa: Renewable energy share: **~30%** now → target **>75% by 2047**.
Framework guided by the **Ten Sutras**.
**AP-UN-Habitat MoU (Jul 2026)**: Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs in **Amaravati**.

nd9117d0d5c3.s: According to the Sustainable Development Report 2025, India was ranked among how many countries in the SDG Index?
nd9117d0d5c3.x: India ranked 99th out of 167 ranked countries in the Sustainable Development Report 2025, entering the top 100 for the first time.
nd9117d0d5c3.tq: Keep the rank and total number of countries together to avoid numerical substitution.
xs: India ranked **99th of 167** in **SDR 2025** — option **(2)**.
It was the **first time in the top 100**.
xa: The report is by **UN SDSN** (**10th** edition; first published **2016**).
NITI Aayog's **SDG India Index** ranks States.
SDR 2025 rank came out in **Jun 2025**.

nd3c4c9eb577.s: Which landmark judgment recognised sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter-pays principle as part of Indian environmental law?
o: Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India
Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India
Narmada Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
nd3c4c9eb577.x: Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India (1996) recognised sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter-pays principle in Indian environmental law.
nd3c4c9eb577.tq: Identify the landmark judgment from the specific principles associated with it.
xs: **Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India (1996)** made **sustainable development**, the **precautionary principle** and **polluter pays** part of Indian law — option **(3)**.
The notes link **M.C. Mehta v. UoI (1996)** only to **polluter pays**.
xa: Precautionary principle: lack of full scientific certainty is **no reason to postpone** preventive measures.
Polluter pays: the polluter bears the **cost of preventing and controlling** pollution.
The Tribunal must apply all three principles.

n29d91d78a5d.s: The Swarna Andhra @2047 vision for a 'Wealthy, Healthy and Happy' Andhra Pradesh is aligned with:
n29d91d78a5d.x: Swarna Andhra @2047 is aligned with Viksit Bharat @2047, not Atmanirbhar Bharat @2035.
xa: Strategic pillar: **Sustainability and Climate Resilience**.
Guiding principles: **Ten Sutras**.
Renewable energy: **~30% now** → **>75% by 2047**.

n1b116988a91.s: Under the Swarna Andhra @2047 vision, renewable energy's contribution is targeted to rise by 2047 to:
n1b116988a91.x: Renewable energy contributes about 30% now, with a target of more than 75% by 2047.
xa: Renewable energy falls under the **Sustainability and Climate Resilience** pillar.
Same pillar: **green mobility**, **sustainable urban planning**.
Vision aligned with **Viksit Bharat @2047**.

n69caa238a91.s: In Andhra Pradesh, Sustainable Development Goal targets have been built into which vision document?
n69caa238a91.x: SDG targets have been built into Swarna Andhra @2047, Andhra Pradesh's long-term vision.
n69caa238a91.tq: Swarna Andhra 2047 carries the SDGs to the centenary.
xs: AP has built SDG targets into **Swarna Andhra @2047** — option **(1)**.
It aligns with **Viksit Bharat @2047**, not "@2030".
xa: Aim: "**Wealthy, Healthy and Happy**" state by **2047**.
Guiding principles: **Ten Sutras**.
**AP-UN-Habitat MoU** targets **SDG 11**.

nb40e1b67529.s: Which of the following is NOT a goal or principle of sustainable development as generally recognised in environmental policy?
o: Maximising economic growth at any cost
nb40e1b67529.x: Maximising economic growth at any cost conflicts with sustainable development, which requires balance among economic, social and environmental concerns.
nb40e1b67529.tq: Use the absolute phrase at any cost to identify the incompatible objective.
xs: **Maximising economic growth at any cost** is not a principle — option **(4)**; it is the classic odd-one-out trap.

xa: Others: **CBDR** and **carrying capacity**.
The pillars must be **balanced**, not maximised one at a time.
Principles endorsed at **Rio 1992**.

nc1128e3ccae.s: The Sustainable Development Goals formally came into force from:
nc1128e3ccae.x: The 2030 Agenda and its SDGs were adopted in 2015 and came into force from 2016.
nc1128e3ccae.tq: Distinguish the adoption year from the year in which the framework became operational.
xs: The SDGs came into force from **2016** — option **(3)**.

xa: **17 SDGs**, **169 targets**, **232** indicators.
Preceded by the **MDGs (2000-2015)**.
UN SDSN's **Sustainable Development Report** was first published in **2016**.

ncb504da6135.s: The Sustainable Development Goals were adopted by the United Nations General Assembly during its:
ncb504da6135.x: The UN General Assembly adopted the 2030 Agenda and its 17 SDGs during its 70th session in 2015.
ncb504da6135.tq: Use the year-session pair to eliminate mismatched combinations.
xs: The SDGs were adopted at the **UNGA 70th Session in 2015** — option **(4)**.

xa: Document: "**Transforming our World: the 2030 Agenda**".
SDGs came **into force** in **2016**.
**17 goals**, **169 targets**.

o: Geneva Conventions and their Additional Protocols
Vienna Convention and the Montreal Protocol
Universal Declaration of Human Rights and international human-rights treaties
n5dd46c72dd4.x: Agenda 2030 is guided by the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948) together with international human-rights treaties.
xa: Agenda 2030 is **universal** — applies to all nations.

Adopted at **UNGA 70th Session, 2015**.

nc23808b7af3.s: The idea of the Sustainable Development Goals was first proposed at Rio+20 by:

Rio+20 was the **UN Conference on Sustainable Development**, **Rio de Janeiro, 2012**.
xa: Its outcome "**The Future We Want**" called for goals to follow the **MDGs**.
The SDGs were adopted in **2015**.

n2429f9ca2ef.s: Which outcome document of the Rio+20 Conference called for global goals to follow the Millennium Development Goals?
n2429f9ca2ef.x: The Rio+20 outcome document titled “The Future We Want” called for global goals to follow the MDGs.

"**Transforming our World**" was the **2015** adoption document.

n6025f7fe44c.s: The first SDG India Index was released in:

Agenda 2030 adopted at the **UNGA 70th Session**.

nenvironment-10-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the SDGs?

n: The SDGs have 169 targets. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 20-21]

xa: Adopted by the **UN General Assembly, 70th Session, 2015**.

n: The official framework for the SDGs is “Transforming our World: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.” [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 20-21]

na30b8ca623c.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the scope of the MDGs from that of the SDGs?

MDG focus: **poverty and basic well-being**.

ndcef9d3272c.s: Which group of SDGs extends the concerns of the Millennium Development Goals?

MDGs focused on **poverty and basic well-being**.
SDGs: **17 goals**, **169 targets**.

nb44e4ab44dc.s: Which of the following is covered under Goal 4, Quality Education?

n48746180cfa.s: SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) aims to bring remittance costs below:

n8df3906f824.s: The Saubhagya scheme is aligned with which SDG?

xa: **SDG 13** — **Climate Action**; **SDG 16** — **Peace, Justice & Strong Institutions**.

n35abf3091cd.s: MGNREGA is associated with which SDG?

o: National Action Plan on Climate Change and its eight missions
National Food Security Act and POSHAN Abhiyaan
ndc6b59049aa.x: India’s National Action Plan on Climate Change, comprising eight missions, is associated with SDG 13.
ndc6b59049aa.tq: Match the goal with the policy package designed for its subject area.
xs: **SDG 13 (Climate Action)** maps to the **NAPCC** and its **eight missions** — option **(3)**.
**Samagra Shiksha/PM POSHAN** → SDG 4; **Smart Cities/AMRUT** → SDG 11; **NFSA/POSHAN Abhiyaan** → SDG 2.
xa: **SDG 14** = Life Below Water; **SDG 15** = Life on Land.

nd7405d80c99.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the nine themes used for Localised Sustainable Development Goals in Gram Panchayats?

n5d17f00a128.tq: SDR: 99th (2025, first top-100) then 94th (2026, best ever).
xs: India's best-ever SDR rank is **94th** in **2026** — option **(2)**.

India lags on **13 of 17** goals; **SDG 2** is the biggest worry.
**SDR 2025** leader: **Finland** (**87**).

n107655556ec.s: Which one of the following is NOT the title of a Sustainable Development Goal?

It is necessarily inexpensive for developing countries.

o: the compulsory recycling of all industrial waste
making false or exaggerated claims that a product, firm or investment is environmentally friendly
the restoration of polluted water bodies through biological methods
the conversion of all investments into government securities

nfbff11b75f3.tq: Distinguish misleading environmental communication from genuine environmental improvement.

n118ce9734be.s: The Green Skill Development Programme was launched in 2017 by the

Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship alone

xs: The **Green Skill Development Programme** was launched in **2017** by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** (MoEFCC) — option **(2)**.

nf99d8a22d2c.s: The European Green Deal's legislative package to cut greenhouse gases by at least 55% by 2030 (vs 1990) is called:

nb6021156b55.s: The Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE) was launched in 2013 primarily in response to

n26d2c230c04.s: In which year did MoEFCC notify the Green Credit Programme?

**Green Pharmacy** applies green chemistry to medicines.

n422a4df1ae1.s: Green bonds were pioneered in 2007 by the:

n349fa555709.s: India's first Sovereign Green Bond issue, made in 2023, amounted to:

Finance social projects without accepting deposits

xs: The **RBI Green Deposit Framework** lets banks **raise deposits earmarked for green lending** — option **(1)**.

n45304e1948e.s: Which one of the following best describes a circular economy?
o: An economic system based primarily on the extraction and disposal of resources
An economic system based on increasing the use of fossil fuels
An economic system built on reuse, recycling and waste minimisation
An economic system focused exclusively on reducing carbon emissions

nb3ffa36a6be.s: Ozone is concentrated predominantly in which layer of the atmosphere, and at about what altitude?
nb3ffa36a6be.x: Ozone is concentrated mainly in the stratosphere, approximately between 10 and 50 km above Earth. This layer absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation.
nb3ffa36a6be.tq: Use the location-and-range combination to distinguish the ozone layer from adjacent atmospheric layers.
xs: Ozone is concentrated in the **Stratosphere, about 10-50 km** above Earth — so option **(1)** is correct.

xa: Ozone is measured in **Dobson Units (DU)**; an "ozone hole" means total ozone below **220 DU**.

PIB reported a dense ozone pocket at **21-23 km** over the **North Bay of Bengal** (16 Aug 2026).
nb3ffa36a6be.fixed: Stem had two run-on question sentences

n08a94fb9594.s: An ozone hole is conventionally identified when the total column ozone falls below:

xs: An ozone hole is identified when total ozone falls below **220 Dobson Units** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Ozone is measured in the **Dobson Unit (DU)**.
xa: The ozone hole was first detected over **Antarctica** in the mid-1980s.
First reported in **1985** by **British Antarctic Survey** scientists (some notes say discovered **1983**).
Thinning is seasonal, in **Southern Hemisphere spring, Aug-Nov**.

nebb8956a7bd.s: The seasonal thinning of the ozone layer over Antarctica is most pronounced during:
o: Southern Hemisphere autumn, March to May
Southern Hemisphere summer, December to February
Southern Hemisphere spring, approximately August to November
Northern Hemisphere spring, March to May
nebb8956a7bd.x: The Antarctic ozone hole is a seasonal phenomenon, with maximum thinning during Southern Hemisphere spring, approximately August to November.
nebb8956a7bd.tq: Link the phenomenon with the correct hemisphere and season.
xs: Antarctic ozone thinning peaks in **Southern Hemisphere spring, approximately August to November** — so option **(3)** is correct.

n6b34b5ba9cf.s: Polar stratospheric clouds contribute to ozone destruction because they:
o: Absorb all incoming solar radiation before it reaches the stratosphere
Convert oxygen directly into carbon dioxide
Prevent the return of sunlight to the polar vortex
Convert stable chlorine compounds into active forms on their surfaces in extreme cold
n6b34b5ba9cf.x: In the extremely cold polar vortex, polar stratospheric clouds provide surfaces that convert stable chlorine into active forms. When sunlight returns, these forms catalytically destroy ozone.
n6b34b5ba9cf.tq: Identify the causal mechanism rather than merely the associated location.
xs: Polar stratospheric clouds **convert stable chlorine compounds into active forms on their surfaces in extreme cold** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They form in the extreme cold of the **polar vortex**; the active chlorine **destroys ozone when sunlight returns**.
So they do not block sunlight or make CO2 — the ozone loss in fact needs the return of sunlight.
xa: Chlorine and bromine atoms destroy ozone **catalytically**.
The ozone hole is seasonal: **Southern Hemisphere spring, Aug-Nov**.
**Halons** (bromine) are about **100 times more potent** than CFCs.

nba3193b241a.s: Which one of the following is the main cause of depletion of the stratospheric ozone layer?
nba3193b241a.x: CFCs release chlorine in the stratosphere under UV, and the chlorine catalytically breaks down ozone; they are the main culprit. Carbon dioxide and methane are greenhouse gases but not the main ozone depleters, and nitrogen (N2) is an inert atmospheric gas.
nba3193b241a.tq: Ozone depletion = CFCs (chlorine); CO2, CH4, N2 are the usual traps.
xs: **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)** are the main cause of ozone depletion — so option **(3)** is correct.
CFCs release **chlorine** in the stratosphere, which breaks down ozone.
⚠ **CO2, methane and N2** are the usual wrong options — they are not the main ozone depleters.
xa: Asked in **APPSC 2025** twice.
CFC uses: refrigerators, ACs, **aerosol propellants**, foam blowing, solvents.
CFCs are also greenhouse gases — about **15%** of the greenhouse effect.

n63413d7d078.s: The Ozone-Depleting Substances (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000 were framed under the:

n783ea85dfa6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ozone-depleting substances?

SO₂ was an earlier refrigerant. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]

n5499ce06276.s: The Montreal Protocol entered into force on:

n1d3da22a832.s: The Multilateral Fund under the Montreal Protocol mainly provides:

Loans to CFC manufacturers in developed countries
Compensation to developed countries for HFC phase-down
Funds for climate adaptation in small island states

n1c42439adbb.s: In India, the National Ozone Unit is the:

xa: **Montreal + Vienna** = ozone layer.
**Kyoto (1997)** = greenhouse gas cuts by developed countries.
Basel, Rotterdam, Stockholm share one **joint secretariat under UNEP**.

n94c96904591.s: Which one of the following correctly describes species diversity?
o: The variety of climatic zones on Earth
Variation in genes within a single species only
Only the number of species in an area, irrespective of their abundance
The variety of species in an area, involving richness as well as abundance
n94c96904591.x: Species diversity concerns the variety of species in an area and includes both species richness and abundance.
n94c96904591.tq: Distinguish species diversity from the narrower concept of richness.
xs: Species diversity is **the variety of species in an area, involving richness as well as abundance** — option **(4)** is correct.
Option (3) is wrong because it ignores **abundance**; option (2) describes **genetic** diversity.
xa: **Species richness** = number of species; **evenness** = relative abundance.
Species diversity is measured by the **Shannon-Wiener** and **Simpson** indices.
**Alpha** diversity = species richness within one community.

na03bb9c1719.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ecosystem diversity?
o: It refers to the variety of ecosystems in an area
Boreal conifers cannot do the job of tropical deciduous trees in every context
Rainforests, deciduous forests and boreal ecosystems are examples of different ecosystems
One ecosystem can always replace the functions of another
na03bb9c1719.x: One ecosystem cannot simply replace another's functions.
xa: Richest ecosystem on land: **tropical rainforests**; in the sea: **coral reefs**.
⚠ **Taiga, deserts and temperate forests** are the usual wrong options for richest ecosystem.
**Gamma** diversity = total diversity across the ecosystems of a whole region.

n01521990bda.s: Species richness and species evenness refer, respectively, to:
o: Relative abundance and total number of species
Total number of species and their relative abundance
Change between ecosystems and total regional diversity
n01521990bda.x: Species richness is the number of species, while species evenness indicates their relative abundance. Low evenness means that a few species dominate.
n01521990bda.tq: Discriminate between number and proportional distribution.
xs: Richness and evenness are the **total number of species and their relative abundance** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Low evenness** means a few species dominate.
Option (1) reverses them; option (3) describes beta and gamma diversity.
xa: Example: Forest A (2 tigers, 6 deer, 7 rabbits) is **more even** than Forest B (1, 6, 8).
Indices: **Shannon-Wiener** and **Simpson**.
Functional diversity has its own **richness**, **evenness** and **divergence**.

nb3027722c52.s: Which one of the following is NOT a recognised explanation for the greater biodiversity of tropical regions?
o: Long, undisturbed evolutionary history without glaciation
Greater solar energy and higher productivity
A less seasonal and more predictable climate
Frequent continental-scale glaciation and severe seasonal fluctuations
nb3027722c52.x: Tropical richness is associated with long evolutionary time without glaciation, stable climate, solar energy and productivity. Frequent severe glaciation is not an explanation for tropical richness.
nb3027722c52.tq: Find the option that reverses the standard explanation for a biodiversity pattern.
xs: **Frequent continental-scale glaciation and severe seasonal fluctuations** is not a reason — option **(4)** is correct.
The tropics had **long, undisturbed evolutionary time** with **no glaciation**.
They have a **less seasonal, more stable** climate → niche specialisation, and **more solar energy** → higher **productivity**.
xa: **Moderate disturbance** and **habitat heterogeneity** also raise diversity.
Ant example: about **10 species** near the North Pole vs up to **2,000** at the equator.
UPPSC 2019 A/R: butterflies peak in the tropics because they **cannot tolerate low temperature**.

nb8bc7292c6f.s: The most significant aspect of biodiversity is:
nb8bc7292c6f.x: The most significant aspect of biodiversity is the maintenance of the ecosystem. Timber, ornamental plants and ecotourism are uses of biodiversity (productive or aesthetic values), but they are not its most significant aspect.
nb8bc7292c6f.tq: Most significant aspect = maintenance of the ecosystem (UPPSC 2015).
xs: The most significant aspect is **maintenance of the ecosystem** — option **(2)** is correct (UPPSC 2015).
Timber is **productive** value; ornamentals and **ecotourism** are uses (aesthetic), not the main aspect.
xa: Role in sustainable development (APPSC 2025): **supports ecosystem services**.
Losing a **keystone species** can bring an ecosystem down (rivet popper).
**Ethical / existence** value: every species has a **right to exist**.

n6d757bb8b93.s: Which of the following crop combinations is associated with the Hindustan (Indo-Burma) centre of origin?
o: Rice, sugarcane, mango, pigeon pea, brinjal, cucumber and black pepper
Wheat, barley, olive, grape and cabbage
n6d757bb8b93.x: The Hindustan or Indian centre is associated with rice, sugarcane, mango, pigeon pea, brinjal, cucumber and black pepper. It is also associated with many pulses and citrus.
n6d757bb8b93.tq: Match a named centre with its characteristic crop group.
xs: The Hindustan centre gives **rice, sugarcane, mango, pigeon pea, brinjal, cucumber and black pepper** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is also linked to **many pulses** and **citrus**.
xa: Centres identified by **N.I. Vavilov** (**8 centres**).
**Nokrek Biosphere Reserve** (Garo Hills) = **Citrus Gene Sanctuary**.
**Oryza rufipogon** is the wild ancestor of cultivated rice.

nenvironment-25-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Endemic species are restricted to a particular geographical area.
Invasive alien species harm native ecosystems or species.
Alien species are introduced outside their natural range.
Genetic diversity refers to the variety of ecosystems.
nenvironment-25-2.x: Genetic diversity is variation within a species; the variety of ecosystems is ecosystem diversity.
n: An endemic species is restricted to a particular geographical area. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
An alien species is introduced outside its natural range. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
An invasive alien species is an alien species that adversely affects native ecosystems or species. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
Genetic diversity is variation within species. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
Ecosystem diversity is the variety of ecosystems. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
xa: **Species diversity**: the **variety of species**.
Genetic example: all rice varieties are **Oryza sativa** but differ in size, aroma, nutrients.
"Biodiversity" was coined by **Walter G. Rosen** (**1985**).
CBD (**1992**) definition covers diversity **within species, between species and of ecosystems**.

n3b27b27daaf.x: Walter G. Rosen coined the word (1985) and E.O. Wilson popularised it; alpha, beta and gamma diversity terms come from Whittaker.
xa: ⚠ **Rosen** coined; **Wilson** popularised — do not swap (UKPSC 2025).
**Wilson (1992)** estimated **10-50 million** species; **Robert May** about **7 million**.
**Paul Ehrlich** proposed the **rivet popper hypothesis**; **Humboldt** the species-area relationship.

nb88eb2566f5.s: About how many living species have been described so far?
nb88eb2566f5.x: About 1.5 million species have been described; E.O. Wilson estimated 10-50 million species in all, including undescribed ones.
xa: **Robert May** estimated about **7 million** species.
About **300,000** fossil species are described.
India has identified about **1,50,000** living species.

nb6142af1a99.s: The high species richness of the Himalayas is most appropriately explained by the fact that the Himalayas
o: are a meeting point of different biogeographical zones
have no seasonal variation in climate
are entirely covered by tropical rainforests
are located close to the equator
nb6142af1a99.x: The Himalayas bring together different biogeographical zones, creating varied habitats and high species richness.
nb6142af1a99.tq: Apply the ecological cause to a geographical case rather than selecting a location-based distractor.
xs: The Himalayas are rich because they **are a meeting point of different biogeographical zones** — option **(1)** is correct.
There the **Palearctic** and **Indo-Malayan** realms meet, bringing species from both.
xa: The **Himalaya** zone has the most faunal species in India: **30,377**.
⚠ Largest zone = **Deccan Peninsula**; most faunal species = **Himalaya**.
The Himalaya zone covers **7.2%** of India's land.

n00519048dfc.s: The species-area relationship (log S = log C + Z log A) was proposed by:
n00519048dfc.x: Humboldt proposed the species-area relationship; Paul Ehrlich proposed the rivet popper hypothesis.
xa: For very large areas (whole continents), Z is **0.6-1.2**.
**R.H. Whittaker** gave the terms **alpha, beta, gamma** diversity.
⚠ **Rosen** coined "biodiversity" (**1985**); **Wilson** popularised it.

n120401ce4d9.s: According to the Rivet Popper Hypothesis, the loss of which kind of species may destabilise or collapse an ecosystem?
n120401ce4d9.x: The hypothesis holds that losing a few species may seem harmless, but losing key or keystone species may collapse an ecosystem.
xa: Proposed by **Paul Ehrlich**: ecosystem = **aeroplane**, species = **rivets**.
Each loss **weakens** the ecosystem.
Ecosystem services: **pollination**, **climate regulation**, resilience.

n2141514538e.s: Who classified India into biogeographic zones and provinces in the standard scheme associated with the year 1988?
o: Rodgers and Panwar under the Wildlife Institute of India
Alexander von Humboldt under the Zoological Survey of India
Rodgers and Panwar under the Botanical Survey of India
Madhav Gadgil and Panwar under the Indian Council of Forestry Research
n2141514538e.x: The classification was prepared by Rodgers and Panwar under the Wildlife Institute of India in 1988.
n2141514538e.tq: Apply the ‘who–institution–year’ combination without swapping the scientific survey organisation.
xs: India's zones were classified by **Rodgers and Panwar** under the **Wildlife Institute of India** — option **(1)** is correct.
The year was **1988**; it was WII, not BSI or ZSI.
xa: Scheme: **2 realms**, **3 biomes**, **10 zones**, **25 provinces**.
**Himalaya** has the most faunal species: **30,377**.
**AP** falls in the **Deccan** biogeographic zone.

n595a8d34960.s: Who identified eight centres of origin of cultivated plants?
n595a8d34960.x: N. I. Vavilov identified eight centres of origin of cultivated plants.
xs: **N. I. Vavilov** identified the **8 centres of origin** of cultivated plants — option **(1)** is correct.
**E.O. Wilson** popularised "biodiversity"; **Robert May** estimated about **7 million** species.
xa: India is the **Hindustan (Indo-Burma)** centre: rice, sugarcane, pulses, mango, citrus, black pepper.
India ranks **6th** among centres of crop diversity and origin.
India has **811 cultivated crop species** + **902 crop wild relatives**.

n80f254fcb52.s: Which pair of indices is used for measuring species diversity?
o: Simpson index and Human Development Index
n80f254fcb52.x: The Shannon-Wiener and Simpson indices are measures of species diversity.
n80f254fcb52.tq: Start from the sure pair of recognised biodiversity indices.
