n17a5316834c.s: The Irrawaddy dolphin is found in:
n17a5316834c.x: The Irrawaddy dolphin is associated with Chilika Lake in Odisha and the Godavari estuary in Andhra Pradesh.
xa: **One-horned rhino**: **Kaziranga, Assam** (**2,650** rhinos, **2018** census).
**Great Indian Hornbill**: **Western Ghats** and **North-east** hill forests.

na95cade4455.s: The pygmy hog, the world's smallest wild suid, lives in the alluvial grasslands of:
na95cade4455.x: The pygmy hog, the only surviving Porcula species, lives in Assam's alluvial grasslands, where captive breeding raised its numbers 32-fold.
xa: Captive breeding raised the Assam population **32-fold** in three decades.
As an **umbrella species** it shields the **Bengal florican, hispid hare, hog deer, rhino**.

ndca05db0d39.s: The IUCN Red List status of the tiger is:
ndca05db0d39.x: The tiger is Endangered, not Critically Endangered; the Asiatic lion is also Endangered, improved from CR.
xa: The tiger is in **Schedule I** and **CITES App. I**.
⚠ The tiger is **flagship, keystone and umbrella**.
The **Emperor penguin** is **EN** (from **NT**).

nb84bbe27884.s: How many plant taxa did India add to its records in 2025?
nb84bbe27884.x: In 2025 India added 709 animal species (483 new to science) and 353 plant taxa.
xa: India's fauna now = **1,05,953 species**.
**ZSI** in 2025: **117 new species** and **128 new records**.
Western Ghats odonate survey: **143 species**, **40 endemic**.

nb3b16e499f4.s: Tamil Nadu reported clearing which invasive species from 517 villages in 32 districts?
nb3b16e499f4.x: Tamil Nadu reported clearing Prosopis; recovery after removal depends partly on the landscape's prior condition.
xa: **Prosopis juliflora** lowers groundwater in **Rayalaseema** and degrades the **Banni grasslands**.
⚠ **Lantana** and **Chromolaena** feed butterflies in **Raimona NP, Assam** — part of the eradication debate.
Many Indian species are still **"Data Deficient"**.

n8386b4f3766.s: Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary in Kurnool district, Andhra Pradesh, is a habitat of the:
n8386b4f3766.x: The Great Indian Bustard (Godawan) inhabits the Thar grasslands and Rollapadu WLS; Keibul Lamjao is linked with the Sangai deer.
xa: The GIB is **CR** and **Rajasthan's state bird**.
Rollapadu WLS is in **Kurnool**, now **Nandyal**.
Other AP CR species: **Jerdon's Courser** (Sri Lankamalleswara WLS, Kadapa) and **Gooty tarantula**.

nc55bbb2c3b4.s: Lantana is being converted into biochar called 'Black Gold', with Joint Forest Management Committees, in:
nc55bbb2c3b4.x: In Amrabad Tiger Reserve (Nallamala), Lantana is converted into biochar called 'Black Gold' with Joint Forest Management Committees.
xa: **Lantana camara** covers **~25%** of the Amrabad TR forest floor.
Lantana is from **Central/South America (Verbenaceae)**, came as an **ornamental**, and works by **allelopathy**.
It is on IUCN's **100 of the World's Worst IAS** list.

nb9ab6670d94.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about species habitats in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Red Sanders occurs in the Seshachalam, Veligonda and Nallamala hills
Jerdon's Courser is associated with Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary, Kadapa
The Slender Loris is found in dry scrub forests
The Golden Gecko is found only in the Western Ghats
nb9ab6670d94.x: The Golden Gecko occurs in the Seshachalam Eastern Ghats micro-habitats of Andhra Pradesh.
xa: ⚠ The notes list **Slender loris** only as "**AP forest fauna**", without a specific habitat.
**Jerdon's Courser** is **CR**, **nocturnal**, of **Eastern Ghats scrub**, and it is **not flightless**.
**Red Sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus)** is **Endangered**; smuggling is driven by demand from **China and Japan**.
**Cycas beddomei** is a rare, endemic, highly endangered **cycad of the Eastern Ghats**.

n7f2c9b8621a.s: The state tree of Andhra Pradesh is:
n7f2c9b8621a.x: Neem is the state tree of Andhra Pradesh; Red Sanders is not, despite appearing as such in one list.
xa: **Red Sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus)** is **Endangered** and occurs naturally **only in AP** — Seshachalam, Veligonda, Nallamala hills.
**Red Sanders smuggling** in **Seshachalam** is driven by demand from **China and Japan** → illegal logging and violence.
AP's **CR endemics**: **Gooty tarantula** and **Jerdon's Courser**; **EN**: red sanders.

n1dd6225ba5b.s: Red Sanders, an Endangered tree, occurs naturally only in:
n1dd6225ba5b.x: Red Sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus) is Endangered and occurs naturally only in Andhra Pradesh's Seshachalam, Veligonda and Nallamala hills.
xa: Scientific name: **Pterocarpus santalinus**.
⚠ **Trap:** Red Sanders is **not** AP's state tree — that is **Neem**.
**Red Sanders smuggling** in **Seshachalam** is fuelled by demand from **China and Japan**.
**Endangered (EN)** = very high risk of extinction in the wild; part of the "threatened" group with **CR** and **VU**.

ncc69747aa55.s: Biodiversity loss in Kolleru Lake is mainly caused by:
o: Encroachment by fish and prawn tanks
ncc69747aa55.x: Fish and prawn tanks and unregulated aquaculture have converted wetlands and mangroves into ponds, causing salinity and loss of breeding grounds.
xa: **Kolleru** became a **Ramsar site** in **2002**.
**Draining wetlands** and **mangrove-to-shrimp-farm conversion** are listed as activities that disturb ecological balance.
Other AP drivers: **bauxite mining** (Eastern Ghats), **granite quarrying** (Seshachalam, Nallamala).

nf7ee387cbea.s: Illegal logging and violence associated with Red Sanders in the Seshachalam region are driven primarily by demand from:
nf7ee387cbea.x: Demand from China and Japan has driven Red Sanders smuggling, illegal logging and associated violence in the Seshachalam region.
nf7ee387cbea.tq: Match the regional biodiversity case with its external demand centres.
xs: **Red Sanders smuggling** in **Seshachalam** is driven by demand from **China and Japan** — option **(1)**.
This demand fuels **illegal logging** and **violence**.
xa: **Red Sanders** is **Endangered** and grows naturally only in AP's **Seshachalam, Veligonda and Nallamala hills**.
**Granite quarrying** also threatens **Seshachalam** and **Nallamala**.
**Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve** was notified in **2010**.

n7d22ee39b1a.s: The first community-driven programme in India for removal and restocking against suckermouth catfish, tilapia and African catfish was started at
n7d22ee39b1a.x: The Bombay Natural History Society started India's first community-driven removal and restocking programme at Ujani reservoir in Maharashtra.
n7d22ee39b1a.tq: Identify the location associated with the conservation intervention.
xs: The programme began at **Ujani reservoir, Maharashtra** — option **(1)** is correct.
**BNHS** started India's **first community-driven removal and restocking** programme (Aug 2026).
xa: It targets **suckermouth catfish, tilapia and African catfish**.
**Amrabad TR** is linked to **Lantana**; **Banni** to **Prosopis**.
⚠ Removing invasives **alone** does not restore degraded landscapes.

n960660b9868.s: Under the Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022, the power to regulate invasive alien species is associated with
n960660b9868.x: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 empowers the Centre to regulate invasive alien species under Section 62A. The new Schedule IV lists CITES-appendix specimens; it is not the provision that regulates invasives.
n960660b9868.tq: Separate the correct statutory section from the nearby Schedule IV detail.
xs: The power to regulate invasives is under **Section 62A** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **2022 amendment** to the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** empowers the Centre to regulate/prohibit IAS.
⚠ The new **Schedule IV** lists **CITES-appendix specimens** — not invasives; **8(h)** is a CBD Article.
xa: The 2022 amendment also gave IAS a **legal definition**.
**Plant Quarantine Order, 2003**: pest risk analysis.
**NAPINVAS** = national action plan on IAS.

n6617b544099.s: The Gooty tarantula, a Critically Endangered species listed in CITES Appendix II, is associated with which location?
o: Dachigam National Park of Jammu and Kashmir
n6617b544099.x: The Gooty tarantula is associated with the Nandyal forests of Andhra Pradesh and is listed as Critically Endangered and in CITES Appendix II.
n6617b544099.tq: Match the species with its precise habitat and avoid swapping nearby Andhra Pradesh locations.
xs: The **Gooty tarantula** belongs to the **Nandyal/Gooty forests** of AP and **NSTR** — option **(2)**.
It is **CR**, with **fewer than 300** mature individuals and a total range of **< 100 sq km**; listed in CITES **Appendix II**.
**Chambal** is the home of the **Gharial**; **Dachigam** is the home of the **Kashmir stag (Hangul)**.
xa: Scientific name: **Poecilotheria metallica**, also called the **Peacock tarantula**; lives in dry deciduous forest at **350-600 m**.
⚠ WPA schedule: some notes say **Schedule I**, others **Schedule IV** (CITES-listed species sit in Schedule IV after 2022).
The **AP Forest Dept** surveyed the peacock tarantula in **NSTR** (1 May 2026).

n4606366e8fd.s: Shrimp farms are a biodiversity pressure in Andhra Pradesh mainly because they:
n4606366e8fd.x: Shrimp farms are associated with replacement of mangroves; bauxite mining, granite quarrying and Red Sanders smuggling are other AP pressures.
xa: **Human-elephant conflict** is a driver in **Chittoor** and **Anantapur**.
**Prosopis juliflora (Seema Chintakaya)** spreads across **Rayalaseema** and coastal areas.
**Mangrove-to-shrimp-farm conversion** disturbs ecological balance; **protected areas** and **wildlife corridors** restore it.

nd51da00d07f.s: Which of the following is an appropriate example of captive breeding as an ex-situ conservation intervention?
o: Protecting a wetland as an OECM
Declaring a sacred grove as a Community Reserve
Breeding Gangetic gharials and releasing them into suitable rivers
Regulating tourism in a National Park
nd51da00d07f.x: Captive breeding is suitable when a species' habitat has been permanently lost; bred animals may subsequently be released, as in the reintroduction of Gangetic gharials in several states.
nd51da00d07f.tq: Recognise the sequence of off-site breeding followed by release into the wild.
xs: **Breeding Gangetic gharials and releasing them** into rivers is **captive breeding** — option **(3)**.
Captive breeding suits species whose **habitat is permanently lost**; the bred animals are **released back**.
**OECMs**, **community reserves** and **National Park** tourism rules are **in-situ** measures.
xa: The **Gangetic gharial** has been reintroduced in **several states**.
Breeding centres: **vultures** — Jatayu centre, **Pinjore**; **Great Indian Bustard** — **Jaisalmer**; **red panda** — **Darjeeling**.
The **CZA** (set up **1992**) coordinates planned **conservation breeding** in zoos.

nf8f6ddddf70.s: Which Biosphere Reserve harbours the highest number of animal species among Indian Biosphere Reserves, with 2,626 species?
nf8f6ddddf70.x: The Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve harbours the highest number of animal species among Indian Biosphere Reserves, reported as 2,626.
nf8f6ddddf70.tq: Match the largest species-count figure with the correct reserve rather than the largest area.
xs: **Sundarbans** has the most animal species of any Indian BR — **2,626** — option **(3)**.
**Great Rann of Kutch** is the **largest by area**; **Nilgiri** is the only three-state BR.
xa: Sundarbans BR (West Bengal) was designated **1989** and joined the WNBR in **2001**.
**Sundarbans NP** is a **World Heritage Site**.
**Nanda Devi** is known for **snow leopard, musk deer, blue sheep**.

n252f53d1b3d.s: The Citrus Gene Sanctuary in Nokrek Biosphere Reserve is significant because it is an in-situ conservation site for
n252f53d1b3d.x: The Citrus Gene Sanctuary in Nokrek Biosphere Reserve, Garo Hills, Meghalaya, conserves crop wild relatives in situ.
n252f53d1b3d.tq: Apply the meaning of a gene sanctuary to identify the resource conserved in its natural habitat.
xs: The **Citrus Gene Sanctuary** conserves **crop wild relatives** in situ — option **(1)**.
It lies in **Nokrek BR**, **Garo Hills, Meghalaya**.
xa: **Gene sanctuaries** are an **in-situ** method.
**Nokrek BR** was designated **1988** and joined the WNBR in **2009**.
**Field gene banks** (ex-situ) hold crops such as **mango, coconut, banana**.

n4654e6f3b0b.s: The only biosphere reserve of Andhra Pradesh, as listed by APSES, is:
n4654e6f3b0b.x: APSES lists one biosphere reserve, Seshachalam, and one tiger reserve, Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam.
xa: AP summary: **1 TR, 1 Elephant Reserve (Koundinya), 1 BR, 3 NPs, 13 WLS**.
AP has **2 zoos**: **Indira Gandhi ZP, Vizag** and **SV ZP, Tirupati**.
**NSTR** is **India's largest TR by area**.

n18c72756bd1.s: Field gene banks are most suitable for conserving:
o: vegetatively propagated crops and crops with recalcitrant seeds
only orthodox seeds kept in dry cold storage
n18c72756bd1.x: Field gene banks maintain living collections, especially of vegetatively propagated crops and crops with recalcitrant seeds, such as mango, coconut and banana.
n18c72756bd1.tq: Apply the conservation method to the biological material that cannot be conveniently stored as orthodox seed.
xs: **Field gene banks** hold **vegetatively propagated** or **recalcitrant-seed** crops — option **(2)**.
They are **living collections** grown in orchards — e.g. **mango, coconut, banana**.
Sperm and embryos go into **cryopreservation**; seeds into seed banks.
xa: NBRI's **Banthara** station (Lucknow) holds a field gene bank.
Field gene banks are an **ex-situ** method.
A **gene bank** stores germplasm under controlled temperature and humidity.

n5a36ba812a4.s: The Jatayu Conservation Breeding Centre at Pinjore is associated with the conservation of:
n5a36ba812a4.x: Jatayu Conservation Breeding Centre at Pinjore breeds vultures; the GIB is bred at Sam and Ramdevra, the red panda at Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park.
xa: **GIB** is **Critically Endangered**, population **<150**.
Breeding programmes (2026): **Snow Leopard**, **Asiatic Lion**, **GIB**.
The **CZA** coordinates planned conservation breeding.

nc365d4c78ee.s: The 2024 Supreme Court order relating to the habitat of the Great Indian Bustard mandated which measure?
o: Conversion of the habitat into a marine reserve
nc365d4c78ee.x: The 2024 Supreme Court order mandated underground power lines in the Great Indian Bustard’s habitat to reduce threats to the species.
nc365d4c78ee.tq: Match the judicial order with its precise conservation measure.
xs: The **2024 SC order** mandated **underground power lines** in the GIB's habitat — option **(3)**.
The order did not relocate villages, ban research or create a marine reserve.
xa: The **GIB (Godawan)** is **Critically Endangered**, population **<150**.
Conservation breeding: **Sam and Ramdevra**, **Jaisalmer**.
It is one of the 2026 breeding programmes, with **Snow Leopard** and **Asiatic Lion**.

nb442b32d762.s: Which one of the following correctly compares in-situ and ex-situ conservation?
o: In-situ conserves only genes, whereas ex-situ conserves complete ecosystems in nature.
In-situ protects the whole ecosystem, whereas ex-situ primarily conserves the species or its genes outside the natural habitat.
Ex-situ is used only for landscapes, whereas in-situ is used only for laboratories.
Both methods necessarily conserve the whole ecosystem in its original location.
nb442b32d762.x: In-situ conservation protects species along with their ecological setting, while ex-situ conservation focuses mainly on species or genetic material outside the natural habitat.
nb442b32d762.tq: Use the level of conservation—ecosystem versus species or genes—to distinguish the two methods.
xs: **In-situ protects the whole ecosystem**; **ex-situ saves the species or its genes only** — option **(2)**.
Options (1) and (3) reverse the roles; option (4) is wrong because ex-situ cannot save the ecosystem.
xa: In-situ is the **most effective** method — it keeps species interactions intact.
Ex-situ = **off-site**: zoos, botanical gardens, seed and gene banks, cryopreservation.
PYQ: "not an in-situ site" = **Botanical Garden**.

nenvironment-25-5.s: Sacred groves are an example of:
nenvironment-25-5.x: Sacred groves protect species where they live, so they are in-situ conservation.
n: A national park is an example of in-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A sacred grove is an example of in-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A seed bank is an example of ex-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
xa: **In-situ** is the **most effective** method — keeps species interacting with their environment.
Ex-situ also includes **pollen banks**, **tissue culture banks** and **cryopreservation**.
Sacred groves are a **traditional method of conserving tree cover** (e.g. **Devrai** — Maharashtra; **Kavu** — Kerala).

nenvironment-25-10.s: Which of the following is an example of ex-situ conservation?
nenvironment-25-10.x: A botanical garden is ex-situ; sanctuaries, reserved forests and biosphere reserves are in-situ.
n: In-situ conservation occurs within the natural habitat. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A wildlife sanctuary is an example of in-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A biosphere reserve is an example of in-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A reserved forest is an example of in-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A protected forest is an example of in-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A nature reserve is an example of in-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
xa: Other in-situ sites: **tiger reserve**, **sacred grove**, **community reserve**, **gene sanctuary**, **OECM**.
Ex-situ: **zoological park**, **seed bank**, **gene bank**, **cryobank**.
Ex-situ limits: needs space and money; **cannot save the ecosystem**.

nenvironment-25-12.s: Which of the following is an example of in-situ conservation?
nenvironment-25-12.x: A national park protects species in their habitat; botanical gardens, zoos and gene banks are ex-situ.
n: A botanical garden is an example of ex-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A zoological park is an example of ex-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
A gene bank is an example of ex-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
xa: Ex-situ value: **education**, **research**, **reintroduction**.
**Captive breeding**: for species whose habitat is permanently lost — e.g. **Gangetic gharial** reintroduced.
The **National Gene Bank** of **ICAR-NBPGR**, **New Delhi**, was set up in **1996**.

nenvironment-25-13.s: Which of the following is an example of ex-situ conservation?
nenvironment-25-13.x: A cryobank stores seeds, sperm or tissue frozen outside the habitat, so it is ex-situ. Sanctuaries, biosphere reserves and national parks are in-situ.
nenvironment-25-13.tq: Ask whether the species stays in its own habitat.
n: A cryobank is an example of ex-situ conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 43-45]
xs: A **cryobank** is **ex-situ** conservation — so option **(2)** is correct.
It stores material **outside** the natural habitat, in a **controlled environment**.
**Wildlife sanctuary**, **biosphere reserve** and **national park** are **in-situ**.
xa: **Cryopreservation** stores gametes and embryos in **liquid nitrogen at -196°C** (APPSC **2021** key).
**LaCONES** at **CSIR-CCMB, Hyderabad** is India's **frozen zoo**.
**Svalbard Global Seed Vault** (**Norway**) is the world's **largest seed bank**.

nf22c075c673.s: Meristem culture is particularly useful in ex-situ conservation because it enables:
o: Conversion of a Community Reserve into a National Park
Protection of animals in a wildlife sanctuary
Natural pollination in a protected forest
nf22c075c673.x: Meristem culture is a tissue-culture technique used for virus-free propagation of plants.
nf22c075c673.tq: Associate the specialised biotechnology term with its direct application rather than with a protected-area category.
xs: **Meristem culture** allows **virus-free propagation** of plants — option **(2)**.
It is part of **tissue culture banks**, an **ex-situ** method.
Converting reserves, protecting animals in sanctuaries and natural pollination are **in-situ** matters, not meristem culture.
xa: Disease-free **meristems** can also be stored by **cryopreservation** in **liquid nitrogen at -196°C**.
Other ex-situ tools: **pollen banks**, **captive breeding**, **animal translocation**, **in-vitro fertilisation**.
A **gene bank** stores germplasm under controlled temperature and humidity; each sample = an **accession**.

n0af2037d5d2.s: Which one of the following is NOT a protected area category under the Wildlife (Protection) Act framework?
n0af2037d5d2.x: The four protected area categories are National Park, Wildlife Sanctuary, Conservation Reserve and Community Reserve. Biosphere Reserve is not included in this four-category classification.
n0af2037d5d2.tq: Find the one item outside the legally specified group.
xs: **Biosphere Reserve** is not one of the four PA types under the Act — option **(3)**.
The four PA types: **sanctuary, national park, conservation reserve, community reserve**.
BRs rest on **UNESCO MAB recognition** and do not change the land's legal status.
xa: **Conservation reserve** and **community reserve** were added in **2002**.
**Tiger reserves** are notified under the **NTCA chapter**.
India has **18 BRs**, about **91,425.11 sq km**.

n40974ccb0e9.s: An Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measure (OECM) is best described as:
o: A temporary area protected only during a breeding season
An ex-situ facility for storing genetic material
An area outside the formal protected-area network that delivers long-term in-situ conservation outcomes
A formally notified National Park with the highest legal protection
n40974ccb0e9.x: An OECM is outside the formal protected-area network but delivers long-term in-situ conservation outcomes and is recognised on the basis of its results.
n40974ccb0e9.tq: Use the outside-the-network distinction to separate OECMs from formal protected areas.
xs: An **OECM** is a CBD-defined area **outside the formal PA network** that delivers **long-term in-situ conservation** — option **(3)**.
It is recognised for its **outcomes**, not as a notified National Park.
xa: It **confers no legal, financial or management authority** — land ownership does not change.
**4 criteria**: outside the PA network, demarcated, inclusive governance, lasting benefits.
**India's first OECM**: **Aravalli Biodiversity Park, Gurugram (2022)**.
**APSBB** plans OECMs in sacred groves, greenbelts and wetlands to help meet **30x30**.

nfdfad19b5cb.s: An Eco-sensitive Zone (ESZ) around a National Park or Wildlife Sanctuary is best understood as a
o: shock absorber and transition zone between high protection and areas where some development may be allowed
strictly urbanised buffer for industrial development
zone where all forms of human activity are permanently prohibited
separate category of biosphere reserve administered by UNESCO
nfdfad19b5cb.x: An ESZ functions as a shock absorber around a protected area, providing a transition from high protection to areas where regulated development may be permitted.
nfdfad19b5cb.tq: Distinguish the transition-zone concept from absolute protection and unrestricted development.
xs: An **ESZ** is a **"shock absorber"** / transition zone from high protection to areas where development may be permitted — option **(1)**.
ESZs have **prohibited, regulated and permitted** activities — not a total ban and not an industrial buffer.
ESZs are notified by **MoEF&CC**, not UNESCO.
xa: Legal basis: **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** — ⚠ not the WPA 1972.
**MoEF's 2011 guidelines** allow an ESZ **up to 10 km**.
Prohibited in ESZs: **commercial mining**, **quarrying**, **polluting industries**, **major hydro projects**.

ncc3516e8926.s: Projects affecting wildlife in or around protected areas require clearance from the
o: Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife
ncc3516e8926.x: Projects affecting wildlife require clearance from the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL).
ncc3516e8926.tq: Identify the authority by matching the function—wildlife project clearance—with the competent statutory body.
xs: Projects affecting wildlife are vetted by the **Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL)** — option **(1)**.
The notes name no role here for a State Biodiversity Board, NDMA or CPCB.
xa: **National Park** boundaries can be altered only on **NBWL** recommendation.
Mining **within 10 km of wetland conservation reserves** also needs wildlife clearance.
SC: mining impermissible **within 1 km** of every NP/WLS.

n1902f808c89.s: Which one of the following sets contains only activities classified as REGULATED in an Eco-sensitive Zone?
o: Tree felling, hotels and resorts, road widening
Ongoing agriculture, organic farming, rainwater harvesting
Major hydro projects, commercial mining, ongoing agriculture
n1902f808c89.x: Tree felling, hotels and resorts, and road widening are regulated activities. Commercial mining and major hydro projects are prohibited, while ongoing agriculture, organic farming and rainwater harvesting are permitted.
n1902f808c89.tq: Use category elimination by checking whether each activity belongs to the same regulatory class.
xs: **Tree felling, hotels and resorts, road widening** are **regulated** in an ESZ — option **(1)**.
**Commercial mining, quarrying, polluting industries** and **major hydro projects** are **prohibited**.
**Ongoing agriculture, organic farming, rainwater harvesting** are **permitted**.
xa: ESZ = **"shock absorber"** around an NP or sanctuary.
Notified by **MoEF&CC** under the **EP Act, 1986**.
ESZ width: **up to 10 km** (2011 guidelines).

n851621e7a4d.s: Sacred groves are best described as forest tracts that are primarily preserved by communities on the basis of
o: religious beliefs, with trees and wildlife being venerated
n851621e7a4d.x: Sacred groves are forest patches preserved by communities on religious grounds, where trees and wildlife are traditionally venerated.
n851621e7a4d.tq: Identify the defining purpose rather than a merely associated land-use activity.
xs: Sacred groves are forest tracts preserved by communities on **religious grounds**, with **all trees and wildlife venerated** — option **(4)**.
They are community-kept, not timber or shifting-cultivation land, and not exclusively government-owned.
xa: PYQ: sacred groves = a **traditional method of conserving tree cover**.
They are an **in-situ** method, like **sacred lakes**.
Local names: **Devrai** (Maharashtra), **Kavu** (Kerala), **Orans** (Rajasthan), **Sarna** (Jharkhand).

n3617379426e.s: Papikonda National Park primarily protects the:
o: mangrove forests of the Krishna delta
n3617379426e.x: Papikonda National Park protects the Papikondalu ranges situated along the Godavari River.
n3617379426e.tq: Associate the protected area with its defining landscape and river.
xs: **Papikonda NP** protects the **Papikondalu ranges on the Godavari** (Godavari gorge) — option **(4)**.
Nallamala tiger habitat is **NSTR**; the Tirupati hills belong to **Seshachalam**.
xa: Papikonda was the release site of a tiger that walked **650+ km** from **Tadoba** (Jul 2026).
⚠ A "Papikondalu Tiger Reserve" in some notes is wrong — **NSTR** is AP's only TR.
AP has **3 NPs** and **13 WLS**.

n381c4f6e48f.s: Lloyd Botanical Garden is located at:
n381c4f6e48f.x: Lloyd Botanical Garden is at Darjeeling; Ooty has the Government Botanical Garden and Lucknow the National Botanical Garden of CSIR-NBRI.
xa: NBRI's **Banthara** station holds a **field gene bank**.
**Indian Botanic Garden** (Great Banyan) is at **Shibpur, Howrah**.
**Darjeeling** also hosts the **Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park** (red panda breeding).

ne3ec767e9b9.s: The National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB), established in 2000, functions under which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
ne3ec767e9b9.x: The NMPB was established in 2000 under the Ministry of AYUSH and promotes the cultivation and conservation of medicinal plants.
ne3ec767e9b9.tq: Use the establishment year and ministry pairing to distinguish the board from environmental bodies.
xs: The **National Medicinal Plants Board (2000)** is under the **Ministry of AYUSH** — option **(2)**.
It promotes **cultivation and conservation** of medicinal plants.
⚠ The **CZA** is under **MoEF&CC** — do not confuse.
xa: **Phyto-Pharma Plant Mission** is a **CSIR** mission.
**BD Rules 2024** encourage **cultivated** medicinal plants.
NBA/SBB approvals now take **90 days** (**180** for IPR).

n64301dd85fc.s: In which zone of a Biosphere Reserve are settlements allowed?
n64301dd85fc.x: Settlements may exist in the transition zone; National Parks allow no rights or grazing at all.
xa: NP boundaries change only on **NBWL** recommendation.
A BR does not change **land ownership**.
Sanctuaries regulate human activity but **permit it to an extent**.

n3b158348603.s: Anamalai Tiger Reserve is associated with which of the following conservation firsts?
n3b158348603.x: Anamalai is associated with India's first Hornbill Conservation Centre.
n3b158348603.tq: Use the named-site and named-facility association to avoid swapping the conservation firsts.
xs: **Anamalai** is India's **first Hornbill Conservation Centre** (2026) — option **(2)**.
First OECM = **Aravalli Biodiversity Park**; first dugong reserve = **Palk Bay**; first marine BR = **Gulf of Mannar**.
xa: Palk Bay's dugong reserve covers **448 sq km**.
Aravalli Biodiversity Park (**2022**) is a restored mining site.
First community reserve: **Keshopur-Chhamb (Punjab)**.

nenvironment-14-5.s: Grazing of livestock may be regulated by the Chief Wildlife Warden in:
o: Both National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries
nenvironment-14-5.x: Grazing is fully banned in National Parks; it may be regulated only in Wildlife Sanctuaries.
n: Hunting in a Wildlife Sanctuary is prohibited without permission. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
Hunting in a National Park is completely prohibited. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
Cattle grazing is completely prohibited in a National Park. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
No human activity is permitted in a National Park except activity permitted by the Chief Wildlife Warden. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
A protected animal may not be hunted normally. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
xa: Both are under the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**.
NP boundaries can be altered only on **NBWL** recommendation.
A **Biosphere reserve** allows **settlements** in the transition zone.

nenvironment-14-12.s: A Community Reserve is declared by the:
nenvironment-14-12.x: The State Government declares a Community Reserve; land already under a national park, sanctuary or conservation reserve cannot become one.
n: Land already designated as a National Park cannot form a Community Reserve. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
Land already designated as a Wildlife Sanctuary cannot form a Community Reserve. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
Land already designated as a Conservation Reserve cannot form a Community Reserve. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
A Community Reserve is declared by the State Government. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
xa: Community Reserve = **Section 36C**; added by the **2002** amendment.
⚠ Conservation reserve = **government land**; community reserve = **private/community land**.
First community reserve: **Keshopur-Chhamb (Punjab)**.

nenvironment-14-13.s: The purpose of a Community Reserve is to conserve:
o: Fauna and flora as well as traditional and cultural values
nenvironment-14-13.x: A community reserve conserves plants and animals as well as traditional and cultural values.
n: The purpose of a Community Reserve is the conservation of fauna and flora. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
A Community Reserve conserves traditional and cultural values. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 25-27]
xa: The State declares it when a **community volunteers**.
It is run by a **CRMC** (Community Reserve Management Committee).
Four PA types: **sanctuary, national park, conservation reserve, community reserve**.

n748e16f03d7.s: Which one of the following is NOT a limitation of ex-situ conservation?
o: Maintaining captive populations can be resource-intensive.
It may support education, research and reintroduction.
It cannot by itself save the entire ecosystem.
It requires considerable space and money.
n748e16f03d7.x: Education, research and reintroduction are values of ex-situ conservation, not limitations. Space and financial requirements, as well as inability to save the whole ecosystem, are limitations.
n748e16f03d7.tq: Separate benefits from limitations before selecting the exception.
xs: **Education, research and reintroduction** are the **values** of ex-situ conservation, not its limits — option **(2)**.
The notes list the limits: ex-situ **needs space and money** and **cannot save the ecosystem**.
Keeping captive populations is resource-intensive — the same point as space and money.
xa: Ex-situ = **off-site** conservation away from the natural habitat.
In-situ protects the **whole ecosystem**; ex-situ saves only the species or its genes.
**Cryopreservation** keeps gametes and embryos viable for **decades or centuries**.

n57186a7e2bf.s: Which organisation maintains the World Database on Protected Areas (WDPA) in collaboration with IUCN?
n57186a7e2bf.x: The WDPA is run by UNEP-WCMC, based in Cambridge, in collaboration with IUCN, and tracks progress towards the 30x30 target.
n57186a7e2bf.tq: Use the institutional-identity trap by distinguishing UNEP-WCMC from neighbouring UN bodies.
xs: The **WDPA** is run by **UNEP-WCMC**, Cambridge, with **IUCN** — option **(1)**.
It **tracks 30x30 progress**.
xa: WDPA data (Apr 2026): nearly **10% of the ocean** protected; only **1.66% of the high seas**.
In **2014**, PAs covered **15.2% of land** and **8.4%** of coastal and marine areas.
Marine protection must **triple by 2030**.

nb655755d1c2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the zonation of a biosphere reserve?
o: The core zone is legally protected, usually as a National Park or sanctuary
The transition zone permits settlements, agriculture, forestry and tourism
The buffer zone is the outer interface where settlements, farming and tourism are concentrated
The buffer zone allows regulated activities such as research, education and training
nb655755d1c2.x: The buffer zone surrounds the core and allows only regulated activities; settlements, farming and tourism belong to the transition zone, the outer interface.
xa: **Seville Strategy (1995)** added social, cultural and economic needs and **community participation**.
Funding: **CSS "Biodiversity Conservation"** — **60:40**, and **90:10** for NE and Himalayan States.
UNESCO criteria include a **management authority** involving local communities.

nce0ae9e7aef.s: Which protected-area category is zoned into core, buffer and transition areas?
nce0ae9e7aef.x: A Biosphere Reserve has core, buffer and transition zones; National Parks are clearly demarcated, and sanctuary boundaries are not strictly specified.
xa: The **core** is usually an NP or sanctuary under the **WPA 1972**.
The **buffer** allows research, education, eco-restoration.
The **transition zone** holds settlements, farming, tourism.

ne64202c2143.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of an OECM?
o: Recognition automatically changes land ownership and confers new legal authority.
It is demarcated and has inclusive governance.
It is outside the formal protected-area network.
ne64202c2143.x: Recognition of an OECM is outcome-based and does not change land ownership or confer new legal, financial or management authority. The other three are among its criteria.
ne64202c2143.tq: Look for the statement that reverses the no-new-authority feature of an OECM.
xs: OECM recognition does **not** change land ownership or confer legal authority — so option **(1)** is not a feature.
An OECM **confers no legal, financial or management authority**; it is recognised for its **outcomes**.
Options (2), (3) and (4) are among its **4 criteria**: outside PA network, demarcated, inclusive governance, lasting benefits.
xa: OECM = **Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measure**, defined by the **CBD**.
**India's first OECM**: **Aravalli Biodiversity Park, Gurugram (2022)**, a restored mining site.
India's PA share of **5.32%** means **30x30** needs OECMs.

n6e1f6c352ec.s: Which of the following correctly describes the funding pattern for biosphere reserves?
o: 100 per cent central funding for all biosphere reserves
60:40 for the North-Eastern States, and 90:10 for all other States
90:10 for the North-Eastern and three Himalayan States, and 60:40 for other States
n6e1f6c352ec.x: The funding pattern is 90:10 for the North-Eastern States and three Himalayan States, and 60:40 for other States.
n6e1f6c352ec.tq: Compare the two funding ratios with the regional categories.
xs: BR funding: **90:10** for **North-Eastern and three Himalayan States**, **60:40** for others — option **(3)**.
Option (2) reverses the ratios.
Funding comes through the **CSS "Biodiversity Conservation"**, implemented by the **State Forest Department**.
xa: Umbrella scheme: **Conservation of Natural Resources and Ecosystems**.
**Integrated Management Plans**: five years, in four BRs, since **FY 2022-23**.
States prepare **Management Action Plans**; the **IN-MAB Committee** recommends sites.

n7dc6d586f0c.s: Which of the following is NOT a criterion associated with UNESCO's Biosphere Reserve framework?
o: A management authority involving local or tribal communities
Viable populations representing all trophic levels in the core
An effectively protected and minimally disturbed core
Compulsory transfer of land ownership to UNESCO
n7dc6d586f0c.x: UNESCO's criteria include a protected core, viable populations across trophic levels and participatory management. Transfer of land ownership to UNESCO is not a criterion.
n7dc6d586f0c.tq: Find the option that confuses international designation with ownership or administration.
xs: **Compulsory transfer of land ownership to UNESCO** is not a BR criterion — option **(4)**.
A BR **does not change legal status or ownership** of land.
Real criteria: a **minimally disturbed core** with **all trophic levels**, and a **management authority** involving local communities.
xa: The **Seville Strategy (1995)** added social, cultural, economic needs and **community participation**.
BRs are designated under UNESCO's **MAB Programme** (**1971**).
BRs are **nominated by national governments**.

neb97ecbfb3d.s: Biosphere Reserves are designated under the Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme, an intergovernmental programme launched in 1971 by:
neb97ecbfb3d.x: The MAB Programme, launched in 1971, is a UNESCO programme, and Biosphere Reserves were started by UNESCO, not IUCN. IUCN deals with the Red List and PA categories, UNEP with the environment programme and WDPA (via UNEP-WCMC), and WWF is an NGO.
xs: The **MAB Programme** (launched **1971**) is a **UNESCO** programme — option **(3)**.
BRs were started by **UNESCO, not IUCN**.
**UNEP** runs the **WDPA** through **UNEP-WCMC**; **WWF** publishes the Living Planet Report.
xa: ⚠ Some keys give **1972** (RPSC 2013) or **1973-74**.
India's first BR: **Nilgiri (1986)**; first Indian entry in the WNBR (**2000**).
**13** of India's **18** BRs are in UNESCO's **WNBR**.

n22799e53273.s: Which Biosphere Reserve, including Lahaul-Spiti, is India's first high-altitude cold desert site in UNESCO's World Network?
n22799e53273.x: The Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve in Lahaul-Spiti (Pin Valley NP, Kibber WLS, Chandratal) is India's first high-altitude cold desert site in the WNBR.
xa: It also covers **Pin Valley NP**, **Kibber WLS** and **Chandratal**; flagship animal **snow leopard**.
It joined the WNBR in **September 2025** at Hangzhou.
⚠ PYQ G1 **2024** marked Cold Desert as not in MAB — true then.

n70ef5aaee00.s: Of India's 18 Biosphere Reserves, how many are included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves?
n70ef5aaee00.x: 13 of India's 18 Biosphere Reserves are in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
xa: The **18 BRs** cover about **91,425.11 sq km**.
Outside the WNBR: **Manas**, **Dibru-Saikhowa**, **Dehang-Dibang**, **Great Rann of Kutch**, **Seshachalam**.
⚠ "All Indian BRs are in the UNESCO network" — false (**13 of 18**).

nf1e2a2dde6d.s: Which of the following is NOT among the five Indian biosphere reserves that are not yet included in UNESCO’s World Network?
nf1e2a2dde6d.x: Agasthyamalai is included in UNESCO’s World Network, since it received recognition in 2016. The five not yet included are Manas, Dibru-Saikhowa, Dehang-Dibang, Great Rann of Kutch and Seshachalam.
nf1e2a2dde6d.tq: Find the exception by recalling the complete list of non-WNBR reserves.
xs: **Agasthyamalai** is in the WNBR (joined **2016**), so it is not one of the five — option **(4)**.
The five outside: **Manas**, **Dibru-Saikhowa**, **Dehang-Dibang**, **Great Rann of Kutch**, **Seshachalam**.
xa: **Agasthyamalai** (Kerala-TN) was established in **2001**; home of the **Kani tribe**.
**Seshachalam** (AP, **2010**) is "under process" for the WNBR.
**13** of India's **18** BRs are in the WNBR.

n90ad2281ac2.s: Which was the first Biosphere Reserve established in India?
n90ad2281ac2.x: Nilgiri was India’s first Biosphere Reserve, designated in 1986.
n90ad2281ac2.tq: Use the first-in-sequence fact with its establishment year.
xs: India's first BR is **Nilgiri** (**1986**) — option **(4)**.
It was also the first Indian entry in the **WNBR** (**2000**).
**Agasthyamalai** came in **2001**, **Great Rann of Kutch** in **2008**, **Seshachalam** in **2010**.
xa: Nilgiri spans **TN, Kerala, Karnataka** — India's only **three-state BR**.
It lies within the **Western Ghats WHS**.
**Madhav Gadgil**'s work shaped landscape-level conservation in the Nilgiri BR.

nbc4ea1fb27d.s: The largest Biosphere Reserve in India by area is:
nbc4ea1fb27d.x: The Great Rann of Kutch in Gujarat is the largest Indian Biosphere Reserve by area.
nbc4ea1fb27d.tq: Identify the correct superlative from the area comparison.
xs: India's **largest BR by area** is the **Great Rann of Kutch (Gujarat)** — option **(3)**.
It was designated in **2008** and is **not in the WNBR**.
xa: **Sundarbans** has the most animal species of any Indian BR — **2,626**.
**Nilgiri** is the only three-state BR; **Seshachalam** is AP's only BR.
India's **18 BRs** cover about **91,425.11 sq km**.

nc09aee829b5.s: The Achanakmar-Amarkantak Biosphere Reserve covers which States?
nc09aee829b5.x: Achanakmar-Amarkantak covers Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh; Agasthyamalai covers Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
xa: WNBR years: Nilgiri **2000**, Agasthyamalai **2016**, Achanakmar-Amarkantak **2012**.
Achanakmar-Amarkantak was designated in **2005**.
**Pachmarhi** and **Panna** are other BRs in **Madhya Pradesh**.
nc09aee829b5.fixed: stem repeated 'a. Nilgiri' and trailing fragment

nenvironment-24-1.s: Seshachalam Hills Biosphere Reserve is located in which state?
nenvironment-24-1.x: Seshachalam Hills Biosphere Reserve (2010) is in Andhra Pradesh, in the Tirupati hills.
nenvironment-24-1.tq: Match each biosphere reserve to its State.
n: Seshachalam Hills Biosphere Reserve is located in Andhra Pradesh. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 42-43]
xs: **Seshachalam Hills Biosphere Reserve** is in **Andhra Pradesh** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It was established in **2010** and is **not** in the WNBR — "under process".
**Uttarakhand** has **Nanda Devi**, **Madhya Pradesh** has **Pachmarhi** and **Panna**, **Himachal Pradesh** has **Cold Desert**.
xa: Seshachalam is AP's **only** BR; area **4,755.997 sq km**.
Endemics: **red sanders**, **golden gecko**, **Cycas beddomei**.
It spans the **Tirupati and Kurnool Circles**; includes **Sri Venkateswara NP/WLS**.

nenvironment-24-4.s: The Dihang-Dibang Biosphere Reserve is located in:
nenvironment-24-4.x: Dihang-Dibang is in Arunachal Pradesh; Cold Desert is the biosphere reserve in Himachal Pradesh.
n: Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve is located in TN, Kerala, and Karnataka. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 42-43]
Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve is located in Tamil Nadu. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 42-43]
Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve is located in Himachal Pradesh. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 42-43]
Dihang-Dibang Biosphere Reserve is located in Arunachal Pradesh. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 42-43]
xa: **Nilgiri** (**1986**) was India's **first BR** and the only **three-state** BR.
**Gulf of Mannar** is India's **first Marine Biosphere Reserve**.
**Cold Desert** became India's **13th** WNBR site in **September 2025**.

nenvironment-23-5.s: TRAFFIC, the wildlife-trade monitoring network, is a joint alliance of:
nenvironment-23-5.x: TRAFFIC is a joint WWF-IUCN network; BirdLife International identifies Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas.
n: TRAFFIC is an alliance of WWF and IUCN. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
BirdLife International identifies Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
xa: TRAFFIC **monitors trade-related activities** involving **plants and animals**.
BirdLife's Indian partner is **BNHS**.
**WWF** — wildlife and biodiversity conservation; **IUCN** — conservation and the **Red List**.

nenvironment-23-6.s: The Red List of threatened species is associated with:
nenvironment-23-6.x: IUCN runs the Red List; GEF funds environmental work and FAO covers food, farming and forests.
n: IUCN is associated with conservation and the Red List. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
GEF is associated with environmental financing. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
IPCC is associated with climate-change assessment. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
FAO is associated with food, agriculture, and forestry. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
xa: **UNEP** — the **global environment**; **WMO** — **meteorology and climate**.
**WHO** — **health and environmental health**.
**TRAFFIC** — wildlife-trade monitoring; **BirdLife International** — **IBAs**.

n4f36c31ff92.s: India's first marine national park is:
o: Gulf of Kachchh Marine National Park
Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park
n4f36c31ff92.x: The Gulf of Kachchh Marine National Park is India's first marine national park; Gulf of Mannar is India's first marine biosphere reserve.
xa: **Palk Bay** reserve covers **448 sq km**.
Coral restoration succeeded at **Vaan Island**, Gulf of Mannar (Jun 2026).
India has **106 ICMBAs**.

n107d2b3f3a1.s: The National Centre for Marine Biodiversity is located at which of the following places?
o: Port Blair, Andaman and Nicobar Islands
n107d2b3f3a1.x: The National Centre for Marine Biodiversity is located at Jamnagar in Gujarat.
n107d2b3f3a1.tq: Use the location-based direct-recall approach for a national institution.
xs: The **National Centre for Marine Biodiversity** is at **Jamnagar, Gujarat** — option **(3)**.
**Palk Bay** is the dugong reserve; **Kakinada** is home to **Coringa WLS**.
xa: The **Gulf of Kachchh Marine NP**, also in Gujarat, is India's first marine NP.
India has identified **106 ICMBAs**.
**Gulf of Mannar** is India's first Marine BR.

n004b8d585a3.s: Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve, spanning the Tirupati and Kurnool Forest Circles, was notified in:
n004b8d585a3.x: Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve was notified in 2010 and spans the Tirupati and Kurnool Circles.
xa: Area: **4,755.997 sq km**; **1,756 flowering plant species**; **>220 bird species**.
Endemics: **red sanders**, **golden gecko**, **Cycas beddomei**.
It includes **Sri Venkateswara NP/WLS** and is **not in the WNBR**.

nenvironment-24-6.s: India's first biosphere reserve, Nilgiri, was established in:
nenvironment-24-6.x: Nilgiri dates from 1986; Nanda Devi came in 1988, Gulf of Mannar in 1989 and Similipal in 1994.
n: Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve was established in 1986. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 42-43]
Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve was established in 1988. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 42-43]
Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve was established in 1989. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 42-43]
Similipal Biosphere Reserve was established in 1994. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 42-43]
xa: **Sundarbans**, **Manas** and **Great Nicobar** also date from **1989**.
**Nokrek** also dates from **1988**.
Nilgiri joined the WNBR in **2000** — the first Indian entry.

n4e544be63b1.s: As of 2026, India's protected-area network comprised how many protected areas?
n4e544be63b1.x: The network grew from 981 protected areas in 2020 to 1,134 in 2026, covering 5.32% of India's area.
xa: Break-up: **109 NPs, 573 WLS, 127 Conservation Reserves, 75 Community Reserves**; **58 Tiger Reserves**.
With only **5.32%** under PAs, meeting **30x30** needs **OECMs**.
**Conservation reserves** and **community reserves** were added in **2002**.

nea58989d8b3.s: In 2014, what proportion of the world's land area and coastal-marine area was covered by protected areas, respectively?
nea58989d8b3.x: In 2014, protected areas covered 15.2% of global land and 8.4% of coastal and marine areas.
nea58989d8b3.tq: Use the paired figures carefully and avoid reversing the land and marine percentages.
xs: In **2014**, PAs covered **15.2% of land** and **8.4% of coastal and marine areas** — option **(3)**.
Option (2) reverses the two figures — a common trap.
xa: This was the **APPSC 2018** PYQ benchmark.
Now (WDPA, Apr 2026): nearly **10% of the ocean** protected, only **~3%** fully or highly protected.
**30x30** aims to protect **30% of land and oceans by 2030**.

na52f8562bed.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the present trend in global ocean protection?
o: Nearly 10% of the ocean is protected, but only about 3% is fully or highly protected.
Nearly 30% of the ocean is protected, including 15% that is fully protected.
Only 1.66% of the ocean is protected, while nearly 10% is fully protected.
The proportion of protected ocean area has declined since 2014.
na52f8562bed.x: Nearly 10% of the ocean is protected, but only about 3% is fully or highly protected; merely 1.66% of the high seas is protected.
na52f8562bed.tq: Split the overall figure from the stricter category of fully or highly protected areas.
xs: Nearly **10% of the ocean** is protected, but only **~3%** is **fully or highly protected** — option **(1)**.
**1.66%** is the protected share of the **high seas**, not of the whole ocean, so option (3) is wrong.
Ocean protection has **risen** (up **1.41%** since 2024), so option (4) is wrong.
xa: Marine protection must **triple by 2030** to meet **30x30**.
Data come from the **WDPA**, run by **UNEP-WCMC**, Cambridge, with IUCN.
India has identified **106 ICMBAs** (Important Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Areas).

n03225d7bf67.s: India's first OECM, recognised in 2022, is:
o: Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve, Tamil Nadu
Great Himalayan National Park, Himachal Pradesh
n03225d7bf67.x: Aravalli Biodiversity Park in Gurugram, a restored mining site, was recognised as India's first OECM in 2022.
n03225d7bf67.tq: Combine the identity, location and year to avoid confusing an OECM with a biosphere reserve or National Park.
xs: **India's first OECM** is **Aravalli Biodiversity Park, Gurugram (2022)** — option **(2)**.
It is a **restored mining site**.
**Gulf of Mannar** is India's first **Marine BR**; **Nokrek** BR holds the **Citrus Gene Sanctuary**.
xa: Other FIRSTs: first BR — **Nilgiri (1986)**; first marine NP — **Gulf of Kachchh**.
First Dugong Conservation Reserve — **Palk Bay (448 sq km)**; first community reserve — **Keshopur-Chhamb**.
**Anamalai** = first **Hornbill Conservation Centre** (2026).

ne5751647adb.s: The '30x30' target of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework refers to:
o: Generating 30% of electricity from renewable sources by 2030
Protecting 30% of the world's land and oceans by 2030
Reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 30% from 2030 levels
Restoring 30 million hectares of degraded land by 2030
ne5751647adb.x: 30x30 (Target 3 of the KMGBF, CBD COP-15, 2022) aims to protect 30% of land and oceans by 2030. It is not a renewable-energy target (a PYQ trap), nor an emissions-cut or land-restoration target.
ne5751647adb.tq: 30x30 = 30% land + sea protected by 2030 - biodiversity, not energy.
xs: **30x30** means protecting **30% of the world's land and oceans by 2030** — option **(2)**.
⚠ It is **not a renewable-energy target** — a PYQ trap (APPSC G1 2024).
It is **Target 3** of the **Kunming-Montreal GBF** (CBD COP-15, **2022**).
xa: Marine protection must **triple by 2030** to meet it.
**OECMs** help meet 30x30; India's PA share is only **5.32%**.
Nearly **10% of the ocean** is protected today (WDPA, Apr 2026).

na892509f3a3.s: MoEF's 2011 guidelines allow an Eco-sensitive Zone of up to ____ around a protected area.
na892509f3a3.x: The 2011 guidelines allow an ESZ of up to 10 km around a protected area.
xa: ⚠ **10 km** = guideline width; **1 km** = SC minimum.
ESZs are notified by **MoEF&CC** under the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** — **not** under the WPA (APPSC **2019** trap).
An ESZ is a "**shock absorber**" around a National Park or Sanctuary.
Projects affecting wildlife are vetted by the **Standing Committee of the NBWL**.

n580ff9cdc7d.s: In India, sites for biosphere reserves are recommended by:
n580ff9cdc7d.x: The IN-MAB Committee under MoEF&CC recommends sites, while the States prepare Management Action Plans.
xa: **MAB Programme** launched **1971**; some keys say **1972**.
A BR does **not change the legal status or ownership** of land.
India has **18 BRs**; **13** are in UNESCO's **WNBR**.

nc7c1d9c3abf.s: The strategy of 1995 that added social, cultural and economic needs to Biosphere Reserve criteria is known as the:
nc7c1d9c3abf.x: The Seville Strategy of 1995 added social, cultural and economic needs and community participation to Biosphere Reserve criteria.
xa: Earlier UNESCO criteria: a minimally disturbed **core** with viable populations of **all trophic levels**.
A **management authority** must involve **local (tribal) communities**.
BRs fall under UNESCO's **MAB Programme** (**1971**).

nccdc8be6527.s: Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve, home of the Kani tribe, was established in:
nccdc8be6527.x: Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve, spanning Tamil Nadu and Kerala, was established in 2001.
xa: It joined the **WNBR** in **2016**.
The **SC ordered eviction of encroachers** (6 Jun 2026); TN then issued eviction notices.
Evictions in Agasthyamalai are cited among conservation **debates**.

nd7ca95be5c5.s: India has identified how many Important Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Areas (ICMBAs)?
nd7ca95be5c5.x: India has identified 106 Important Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Areas.
nd7ca95be5c5.tq: Recall the exact count while rejecting nearby numerical distractors.
xs: India has identified **106 ICMBAs** (Important Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Areas) — option **(3)**.
This was the **APPSC 2018** answer.
xa: **Marine Protected Areas** = **Marine NPs + Marine Sanctuaries**, e.g. **Gulf of Mannar Marine NP**, **Malvan Marine Sanctuary**.
India's first marine NP: **Gulf of Kachchh**; first marine BR: **Gulf of Mannar**.
The **National Centre for Marine Biodiversity** is at **Jamnagar, Gujarat**.

n7b3ee070c9e.s: Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating National Park, floats on the phumdis of:
n7b3ee070c9e.x: Keibul Lamjao in Manipur floats on the phumdis of Loktak Lake and is home of the Sangai deer.
xa: **Silent Valley NP**: **Kerala** — tropical evergreen forest.
**Valley of Flowers NP**: **Uttarakhand** — alpine meadows; a UNESCO World Heritage Site with **Nanda Devi**.
**Yasuni NP** (Ecuador): voters **rejected oil drilling** in a referendum.

n35a9b5e9ccc.s: The Indian partner of BirdLife International for Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas is:
n35a9b5e9ccc.x: BirdLife International designates IBAs, and its Indian partner is the BNHS, not WII.
xa: BPSC **2025** key: **Nagi** bird sanctuary.
**BNHS** also runs the **Jatayu** vulture breeding centre at **Pinjore** and the **Ujani** invasive-fish programme.
**WII** works with Rajasthan on **Great Indian Bustard** breeding at **Jaisalmer**.

n0109a9d551d.s: Jerdon's Courser is associated with which protected area of Andhra Pradesh?
n0109a9d551d.x: Jerdon's Courser is associated with Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary; Seshachalam is known for Red Sanders, Cycas beddomei and the Golden Gecko.
xa: Seshachalam has **1,756 flowering plant species** and **>220 bird species**.
It includes **Sri Venkateswara NP/WLS**.
**Rollapadu** WLS is the home of the **Great Indian Bustard**.

nf0653522d12.s: Which facility, built inside a mountain in permafrost, serves as a global safety duplicate of seed collections?
nf0653522d12.x: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault lies inside a mountain in permafrost and holds duplicate seed samples, including India's.
xa: Location: **Spitsbergen island, Norway** (Arctic).
Capacity: **4.5 million seed samples**.
The **Millennium Seed Bank** (Kew, UK) is the largest store of **wild** plant seeds.

n9efd836d2a8.s: Cryopreservation can be used to preserve:
o: Gametes, embryos, seeds, pollen, tissues and DNA
n9efd836d2a8.x: Cryopreservation applies to gametes, embryos, seeds, pollen, disease-free meristems, tissues and DNA.
xa: Medium: **liquid nitrogen at -196°C**.
**LaCONES** (CSIR-CCMB, Hyderabad) is **India's frozen zoo**.
**Meristem culture** gives **virus-free propagation**.

naf934a62e29.s: The National Wildlife Genetic Resource Bank, storing DNA, tissues, gametes and embryos of wild animals, is at:
naf934a62e29.x: The bank is at Nehru Zoological Park and stores DNA, tissues, gametes and embryos of endangered wild animals.
xa: It is at **Nehru Zoological Park**.
**LaCONES** (CSIR-CCMB, Hyderabad) handles **assisted reproduction** and **DNA banking**.
Plant seeds go to gene banks such as **ICAR-NBPGR** and vaults like **Svalbard**.

n2978c874129.s: The zoos at Visakhapatnam and Tirupati are run by the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
n2978c874129.x: Indira Gandhi Zoological Park (Visakhapatnam) and Sri Venkateswara Zoological Park (Tirupati) are run by ZAAP; the CZA only recognises zoos.
xa: **CZA**: set up **1992**, statutory body under the **WPA 1972** (**1991** amendment).
**National Medicinal Plants Board** (**2000**) is under the **Ministry of AYUSH**.
AP zoos are noted for **conservation breeding** and visitor amenities.

n77799ff7aa6.s: The Great Indian Bustard, known as Godawan, is the State bird of:
n77799ff7aa6.x: The Godawan is Rajasthan's State bird; its population is estimated at fewer than 150.
xa: It is **Critically Endangered**.
A **2024 SC order** mandated **underground power lines** in its habitat.
Breeding centres: **Sam and Ramdevra**, **Jaisalmer**, with **WII**.

n6183e69b3c4.s: Under the Biological Diversity Rules, 2024, the approval period mentioned for IPR-related matters is:
n6183e69b3c4.x: The 2024 Rules mention 180 days for IPR-related matters and 90 days generally.
xa: They also **decriminalise some provisions**.
The **NMPB** (**2000**, AYUSH) promotes medicinal-plant cultivation.
**CSIR's Phyto-Pharma Plant Mission** develops phytopharmaceutical drugs.

ne43f8ee1f6b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about protected areas in India?
o: A Biosphere Reserve is associated with UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere Programme
Biosphere Reserve recognition does not by itself change the legal status or ownership of land
National Parks are established under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 through State notification
Wildlife Sanctuaries are established only through UNESCO notification
ne43f8ee1f6b.x: Wildlife Sanctuaries are notified by the State under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972; UNESCO does not notify them.
xa: BR boundaries are zoned **core-buffer-transition**.
NPs are **clearly demarcated**; sanctuary boundaries are **not strictly specified**.
India has **109 NPs** and **573 WLS**.

n3294b523c89.s: Which of the following best explains the role of Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (OECMs) in relation to the 30x30 conservation objective?
o: They are restricted to marine areas and cannot include community-managed landscapes.
They include only areas inside National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries.
They recognise effective conservation areas outside conventional protected areas and can help meet the 30x30 objective.
They replace all Biosphere Reserves recognised under UNESCO's MAB Programme.
n3294b523c89.x: OECMs can cover effectively conserved areas outside reserve forests, National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries, including sacred groves, greenbelts and wetlands, and thereby support the 30x30 objective.
n3294b523c89.tq: Apply the distinction between formal protected areas and conservation areas outside them.
xs: **OECMs** recognise effective conservation areas **outside the formal PA network** and help meet **30x30** — option **(3)**.
They lie **outside** NPs and sanctuaries, so option (2) is wrong; they do not replace BRs.
APSBB plans them in **sacred groves, greenbelts, wetlands** — not only marine areas.
xa: India's PA share is only **5.32%** — hence the need for OECMs.
OECMs **confer no legal, financial or management authority**.
**India's first OECM**: **Aravalli Biodiversity Park, Gurugram (2022)**.

nfad79c28213.s: TRAFFIC, the WWF-IUCN alliance that monitors wildlife trade, was established in:
nfad79c28213.x: TRAFFIC was set up in 1976 to monitor trade in plants and animals.
xa: TRAFFIC is an **alliance** of **WWF and IUCN**.
**GEF** — environmental financing; **IPCC** — climate-change assessment.
BPSC **2025** key: **Nagi** bird sanctuary (IBA).

ncda8f3f2664.s: Spitsbergen Island, associated with the Svalbard Global Seed Vault, is located in which country?
ncda8f3f2664.x: Spitsbergen Island is part of the Svalbard archipelago of Norway and hosts the Svalbard Global Seed Vault.
ncda8f3f2664.tq: Use the precise location-country association rather than the broader Arctic region.
xs: **Spitsbergen island**, home of the **Svalbard Global Seed Vault**, is in **Norway** — option **(4)**.
This is the **APPSC G2 2017** key.
xa: Svalbard is the world's **largest seed bank** and the global backup.
Capacity: **4.5 million seed samples** — ⚠ capacity, not holdings.
India's high-altitude vault is at **Chang La, Ladakh** (~**17,300 ft**).

nb0681c0a724.s: The second National Gene Bank announced in the Union Budget 2025–26 will have a capacity of:
nb0681c0a724.x: The second National Gene Bank will hold 10 lakh germplasm lines and act as a safety duplicate.
xa: It was announced in **Union Budget 2025-26**, presented by **FM Nirmala Sitharaman** (⚠ some notes wrongly credit PM Modi).
It will also support **SAARC/BRICS** nations.
The existing bank is run by **ICAR-NBPGR, New Delhi**.

nd085a86d00e.s: The stated capacity of the Svalbard Global Seed Vault is approximately:
nd085a86d00e.x: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault in Norway can hold about 4.5 million seed samples. That figure is its capacity, not what it actually holds; the trap is reading 'over 4 million varieties' as current holdings. The 10 lakh figure is the capacity of India's second National Gene Bank.
nd085a86d00e.tq: Convert lakh and million figures carefully while distinguishing capacity from present holdings.
xs: **Svalbard**'s capacity is **4.5 million seed samples** — option **(4)**.
⚠ "Stores over 4 million varieties" is a trap — the figure is **capacity, not holdings**.
**10 lakh** is the capacity of India's **2nd National Gene Bank**.
xa: Svalbard sits on **Spitsbergen island, Norway**, built inside a mountain in **permafrost**.
It is the world's **largest seed bank** and the global **"safety duplicate"**.
APPSC G2 **2017** key: Svalbard is in **Norway**.

n362ade4f870.s: NBFGR is the national bureau for the genetic resources of:
n362ade4f870.x: NBFGR deals with fish; NBAGR handles livestock, NBPGR plants and NBAIM microorganisms.
xa: **NBPGR** runs the **National Gene Bank** (set up **1996**).
All four are **ICAR** bureaus.
Each stored sample in a gene bank is an **accession**.

nebf081b3f37.s: India's National Gene Bank, run by ICAR-NBPGR for plant and crop genetic resources, is located at:
nebf081b3f37.x: The National Gene Bank of ICAR-NBPGR is at New Delhi (set up 1996, about 4.7 lakh accessions). Karnal hosts NBAGR (animal genetic resources) and Lucknow hosts NBFGR (fish); Hyderabad has LaCONES, the frozen zoo.
nebf081b3f37.tq: NBPGR - plants - New Delhi; NBAGR - Karnal; NBFGR - Lucknow.
xs: The **National Gene Bank** of **ICAR-NBPGR** is in **New Delhi** — option **(3)** (PYQ).
**Karnal** hosts **NBAGR** (livestock); **Lucknow** hosts **NBFGR** (fish); **Hyderabad** has **LaCONES**.
xa: It was set up in **1996** and holds about **4.7 lakh accessions**.
It has **12 regional stations**.
A **2nd National Gene Bank** was announced in **Budget 2025-26**.

na436aa41c21.s: Cryopreservation generally uses which medium and temperature?
na436aa41c21.x: Cryopreservation is generally carried out in liquid nitrogen at −196°C, which halts metabolic activity and preserves viability for very long periods.
na436aa41c21.tq: Match the preservation method with its characteristic cryogenic medium and temperature.
xs: Cryopreservation uses **liquid nitrogen at -196°C** — option **(3)** (APPSC 2021 key).
The other media and temperatures are not those named for cryopreservation.
xa: It **halts all metabolic activity**, keeping material viable for **decades or centuries**.
It stores **gametes, embryos**, seeds, pollen, **meristems**, tissues and DNA.
Called the **"newest application of technology"** for preserving biotic parts; allows later **IVF** and research.

n6c251851fb4.s: LaCONES at Hyderabad is best described as which one of the following?
o: A national authority for licensing zoos
India’s frozen zoo using assisted reproduction and DNA banking
India’s first botanical garden for medicinal plants
A wildlife census office under UNESCO
n6c251851fb4.x: LaCONES, the Laboratory for the Conservation of Endangered Species, is associated with CSIR-CCMB at Hyderabad and functions as India’s frozen zoo using assisted reproduction and DNA banking.
n6c251851fb4.tq: Break the institutional description into location, parent organisation and function.
xs: **LaCONES** is **India's frozen zoo**, using **assisted reproduction and DNA banking** — option **(2)**.
It is the **Laboratory for the Conservation of Endangered Species**, at **CSIR-CCMB, Hyderabad**.
Zoo recognition is the job of the **Central Zoo Authority**, not LaCONES.
xa: The **National Wildlife Genetic Resource Bank** is at **Nehru Zoological Park**.
Cryopreservation uses **liquid nitrogen at -196°C**.
The **CZA** (set up **1992**) recognises zoos.

n45a4d6deb01.s: The Bishnoi tradition of protection of khejri trees is particularly associated with the incident at Khejarli in
n45a4d6deb01.x: In 1730, Amrita Devi Bishnoi and 363 other Bishnois died at Khejarli while protecting khejri trees from the men of the Jodhpur king.
n45a4d6deb01.tq: Use the date-and-event association to distinguish the conservation sacrifice from nearby historical events.
xs: The **Khejarli** incident took place in **1730** — option **(3)**.
**Amrita Devi Bishnoi** and **363** Bishnois died protecting **khejri** trees from the **Jodhpur king's** men.
xa: The Bishnoi tradition belongs to **Rajasthan**.
Rajasthan's sacred groves are called **Orans**.
Sacred groves are a **traditional method of conserving tree cover**.

n7a612441e3a.s: Coringa in Kakinada is described as India’s—
n7a612441e3a.x: Coringa WLS in Kakinada, together with Krishna WLS, forms the Godavari-Krishna estuarine mangroves, described as India's second-largest mangrove ecosystem. ⚠ Sources differ: ISFR 2023 puts Gujarat second, so this ranking follows the AP sources. It is not an alpine, coral reef or desert ecosystem.
n7a612441e3a.tq: Test a size-ranking fact with ecological distractors.
xs: **Coringa WLS (Kakinada)** is part of AP's mangroves, **India's 2nd largest mangrove ecosystem** — option **(3)**.
These mangroves lie in the **Godavari-Krishna estuaries**.
xa: Coringa is called AP's **mangrove stronghold**.
Other AP sanctuaries: **Kolleru**, **Pulicat** (birds), **Rollapadu** (GIB), **Sri Lankamalleswara** (Jerdon's Courser).
AP's **SDG 14** priority is to expand **marine protected areas**.

nb68fb192c2e.s: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve in the Nallamala hills is significant because it is:
o: India's oldest tiger reserve, set up under Project Tiger in 1973
India's largest tiger reserve by area
India's first Biosphere Reserve in the Eastern Ghats
India's only tiger reserve with a mangrove habitat
nb68fb192c2e.x: NSTR is Andhra Pradesh's only tiger reserve and India's largest tiger reserve by area. It is not a Biosphere Reserve (Seshachalam is AP's only BR), it is not the oldest reserve, and the mangrove tiger habitat is the Sundarbans.
nb68fb192c2e.tq: NSTR = AP's only TR and India's largest TR by area.
xs: **NSTR** is **India's largest tiger reserve by area** — option **(2)**.
It is **not a BR** — **Seshachalam** is AP's only BR.
The notes give no "oldest reserve" claim or mangrove habitat for NSTR.
xa: NSTR is **AP's only Tiger Reserve**, in the **Nallamala**.
It had **63-67 tigers** (AITE 2022).
India has **58 Tiger Reserves**, notified under the **NTCA chapter**.

n659e4b3f8f8.s: With reference to Nanda Devi, which one of the following is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
o: Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve as a whole
Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks
Nanda Devi Wildlife Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh
n659e4b3f8f8.x: The World Heritage Site is Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks; the Biosphere Reserve itself is not the WHS (UKPSC 2025 key treated 'Nanda Devi BR is a WHS' as wrong). There is no Nanda Devi tiger reserve, and Nanda Devi is in Uttarakhand, not MP.
n659e4b3f8f8.tq: WHS = the NPs inside; BR = the wider UNESCO MAB area.
xs: The WHS is **Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks** — option **(2)**.
⚠ The **BR as a whole** is not the WHS — UKPSC **2025** key.
Nanda Devi is in **Uttarakhand**, not MP.
xa: **Nanda Devi BR** (**1988**) joined the WNBR in **2004**.
It shelters **snow leopard, musk deer, blue sheep**.
**Manas WLS** and **Sundarbans NP** are other WHS linked to BRs.

n633294b36f9.s: Palk Bay, covering approximately 448 square kilometres, has been designated as India's first:
o: Important Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Area
n633294b36f9.x: Palk Bay, covering about 448 square kilometres, is India's first Dugong Conservation Reserve.
n633294b36f9.tq: Use the area figure to identify the correct protected-area designation.
xs: **Palk Bay (448 sq km)** is India's **first Dugong Conservation Reserve** (2026) — option **(2)**.
The first **marine NP** is the **Gulf of Kachchh**; the first **Marine BR** is the **Gulf of Mannar**.
xa: India has identified **106 ICMBAs**.
Other FIRSTs: first OECM — **Aravalli Biodiversity Park** (**2022**); first community reserve — **Keshopur-Chhamb**.
**Anamalai** = first **Hornbill Conservation Centre** (2026).

nenvironment-24-7.s: The Khangchendzonga Biosphere Reserve is located in:
nenvironment-24-7.x: Khangchendzonga is in Sikkim; Nanda Devi is in Uttarakhand.
n: Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve is located in Uttarakhand. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 42-43]
Khangchendzonga Biosphere Reserve is located in Sikkim. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 42-43]
Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve is located in Kerala and Tamil Nadu. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 42-43]
Achanakmar–Amarkantak Biosphere Reserve is located in MP and Chhattisgarh. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #24 · pp 42-43]
xa: Years: Nanda Devi **1988**, Khangchendzonga **2000**, Agasthyamalai **2001**, Achanakmar–Amarkantak **2005**.
⚠ The Nanda Devi **NP**, not the BR, is the World Heritage Site.
Not in WNBR: **Manas**, **Dibru-Saikhowa**, **Dehang-Dibang**, **Great Rann of Kutch**, **Seshachalam**.

n9f8031532ba.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Sri Venkateswara National Park?
o: It is situated in the Seshachalam hills
It protects the mangroves of the Godavari estuary
It contains Cycas beddomei and red sanders
It forms part of the Sri Venkateswara Wildlife Sanctuary landscape
n9f8031532ba.x: Godavari-estuary mangroves are protected by Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary; Sri Venkateswara NP lies in the Seshachalam hills.
xa: It covers **353.63 sq km** in **Annamayya and Tirupati** districts.
**Boswellia ovalifoliolata**, another AP endemic, grows in the **Seshachalam-Tirumala hills**.
**Red sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus)** is endemic to **AP only**.

n9f94fa2107c.s: Which national park of Andhra Pradesh has an area of approximately 2.30 sq km and is the smallest national park in the State?
n9f94fa2107c.x: Rajiv Gandhi National Park, also known as Rameswaram National Park, covers approximately 2.30 sq km and is the smallest national park in Andhra Pradesh.
n9f94fa2107c.tq: Use the extreme-size clue to identify the smallest protected area.
xs: **Rajiv Gandhi (Rameswaram) NP**, **2.30 sq km**, is the **smallest NP in AP** — option **(2)**.
It is in **YSR Kadapa** district and dates from **2005**.
**Sri Venkateswara NP** is far larger at **353.63 sq km**; Kolleru is a **sanctuary** and Ramsar site, not an NP.
xa: **Kolleru** sanctuary covers **308.55 sq km**.
⚠ **Kasu Brahmananda Reddy NP** belongs to **Telangana**.
**NSTR** is the **largest tiger reserve** of India.

ne2cc95402fe.s: Boswellia ovalifoliolata is associated with which protected landscape?
ne2cc95402fe.x: Boswellia ovalifoliolata is endemic to Andhra Pradesh and is associated with the Seshachalam-Tirumala hills.
ne2cc95402fe.tq: Match the endemic plant with its specific hill landscape.
xs: **Boswellia ovalifoliolata** belongs to the **Seshachalam-Tirumala hills** — option **(3)**.
It is endemic to **AP**.
**Coringa** is a mangrove sanctuary; red sanders, not Boswellia, is tied to the **Nallamala** hills as well.
xa: Other AP endemics: **Cycas beddomei** ("living fossil") and **red sanders**.
⚠ **Syzygium stocksii** is **not** an AP endemic (APPSC **2022**).
**SV NP** lies in the **Seshachalam hills**.

n798e8cbdb40.s: Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary protects the mangroves of which estuary?
n798e8cbdb40.x: Coringa protects Godavari-estuary mangroves; Krishna Wildlife Sanctuary protects Krishna-estuary mangroves.
xa: **Krishna WLS** covers **194.81 sq km**.
Coringa (**Kakinada**) with Krishna WLS = **India's 2nd largest mangrove** ecosystem.
⚠ **ISFR 2023** puts **Gujarat** second.

nbf4c127d4f2.s: Which genera are specifically associated with the mangrove vegetation of Andhra Pradesh?
nbf4c127d4f2.x: Avicennia and Rhizophora are the mangrove genera specifically associated with the Andhra Pradesh coastal habitats.
nbf4c127d4f2.tq: Break the habitat association down to the characteristic plant genera.
xs: AP's mangrove species are **Avicennia** and **Rhizophora** — option **(3)**.
**Pterocarpus** is red sanders; **Cycas** and **Boswellia** are Seshachalam endemics; **Syzygium stocksii** is a distractor.
xa: Main mangrove sanctuaries: **Coringa** (Kakinada) and **Krishna WLS** (**194.81 sq km**).
Together they form **India's 2nd largest mangrove** ecosystem.
⚠ **ISFR 2023** ranks **Gujarat** second.

n02057511a42.s: Koundinya Wildlife Sanctuary in Chittoor district is part of which elephant reserve?
n02057511a42.x: Koundinya is part of the Rayala Elephant Reserve, Andhra Pradesh's only elephant reserve.
xa: Rayala ER is home of **Asiatic elephants**.
**Coringa** (Kakinada) — India's **2nd largest mangrove** ecosystem, with **Krishna WLS**.
⚠ **ISFR 2023** puts **Gujarat** second in mangroves.

nf606342d12a.s: Operation Kolleru, undertaken in 2006, was associated with which action?
o: Removal of illegal fish tanks up to the plus-five-foot contour
Declaration of Kolleru as a tiger reserve
Construction of new aquaculture tanks inside the sanctuary
nf606342d12a.x: Operation Kolleru in 2006 demolished illegal fish tanks inside the sanctuary up to the +5 ft contour.
nf606342d12a.tq: Link the named operation with its concrete conservation intervention.
xs: **Operation Kolleru (2006)** **demolished illegal fish tanks** up to the **+5 ft** contour — option **(1)**.
The threat was **aquaculture tanks inside the sanctuary**, so building more tanks is the opposite.
xa: Kolleru: Ramsar site since **2002**, sanctuary **308.55 sq km**.
It is a **freshwater lake** between the **Godavari and Krishna** deltas.
India has **100 Ramsar sites** (2026); some notes say **96**.

n31d1c594fa4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Kolleru Lake?
o: It has been a Ramsar site since 2002
It is a brackish-water lagoon on the Bay of Bengal coast
It lies between the Godavari and Krishna deltas
n31d1c594fa4.x: Kolleru is a freshwater lake between the Godavari and Krishna deltas; the brackish lagoon is Pulicat.
xa: ⚠ Some notes give **96** Ramsar sites.
Kolleru's sanctuary covers **308.55 sq km**.
It hosts **spot-billed pelican** breeding.

n360d1d36f9b.s: In June 2022, the Supreme Court made a minimum eco-sensitive zone of ____ around protected areas mandatory.
n360d1d36f9b.x: The Supreme Court mandated a minimum 1 km ESZ in June 2022; the 2002–16 Wildlife Action Plan had suggested 10 km.
xa: ESZs are notified by **MoEFCC** under the **EP Act 1986**.
**353 final ESZ notifications** cover **496** of **688** PAs (2026).

n15070f11731.s: Eco-sensitive Zones are notified by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change under the
n15070f11731.x: ESZs are notified by MoEF&CC under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and not under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
n15070f11731.tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ method and distinguish the governing statute from the protected-area statute.
xs: ESZs are notified by **MoEFCC** under the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** — option **(4)**.
The **WPA 1972** is a common wrong answer.
xa: Width norms: **10 km** suggested (**2002-16** Wildlife Action Plan); **1 km** minimum (SC, June **2022**).
**353** final ESZ notifications cover **496** of **688** PAs.

n073000bfa2d.s: Which of the following current developments was associated with the Nagarjuna-Srisailam Tiger Reserve in June 2026?
o: The permanent closure of all forest routes for tourism
The declaration of a new Ramsar site
A monsoon ban on safari vehicles
A proposal to establish a satellite launch facility
n073000bfa2d.x: A monsoon ban on safari vehicles in the Nagarjuna-Srisailam Tiger Reserve was reported in June 2026.
n073000bfa2d.tq: Use the date and event together to identify the correct current-affairs association.
xs: NSTR saw a **monsoon ban on safari vehicles** (Jun 2026) — option **(3)**.
The **satellite launch facility** threat concerns **Hope Island** near Coringa, not NSTR.
xa: **NSTR** is the **largest tiger reserve of India**.
A **peacock tarantula** survey was held in NSTR (1 May 2026).
India has **100 Ramsar sites**; AP's Ramsar site is **Kolleru** (**2002**).

nbb421516f64.s: Hope Island near Coringa was reported to face a threat from a proposed:
