nbb421516f64.x: Hope Island near Coringa was reported to be threatened by a satellite launch facility.
xa: **Coringa** (Kakinada) is part of **India's 2nd largest mangrove** ecosystem.
AP's mangroves are dominated by **Avicennia** and **Rhizophora**.
⚠ **ISFR 2023** puts **Gujarat** second in mangrove extent.

n0d40e3c21a1.s: Which of the following was NOT among the five new national projects added by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change?
n0d40e3c21a1.x: The five additions were dolphin, Asian elephant, gharial, Great Indian Bustard and Olive Ridley turtle. Project Snow Leopard was not among these five new additions.
n0d40e3c21a1.tq: Find the excluded project from a closely related list of species-specific initiatives.
xs: **Project Snow Leopard** (**2009**) is not one of the five new projects — option **(3)**.
MoEFCC's **five national projects** (2026): **Dolphin**, **Asian elephant**, **gharial**, **GIB**, **Olive Ridley turtle**.
xa: India has **718 snow leopards** (first assessment, Apr 2026).
The **GIB** is also on the **Species Recovery Programme**.
Olive Ridley mass nesting (**arribada**) occurs at **Rushikulya** and on **Srikakulam and Vizianagaram** beaches.

n32413d943c3.s: Which one of the following was the first tiger reserve under Project Tiger?
n32413d943c3.x: Corbett was the first tiger reserve under Project Tiger, formally included on 1 April 1973.
n32413d943c3.tq: Distinguish the first reserve from other reserves associated with the programme.
xs: **Corbett** was the first tiger reserve (**1 April 1973**) — option **(4)**.
**Palamau** (Jharkhand) was among the **first nine**, but not first.
**NSTR** is the **largest**, not the first.
xa: Project Tiger began with **9 reserves**, **18,278 sq km**.
Today: **58 reserves** in **18 States**.
**NSTR** core area is about **5,443 sq km**.

n0b62b825dd4.s: Projects located in tiger corridors require clearance from the:
o: Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife
n0b62b825dd4.x: Projects in tiger corridors require clearance from the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife.
n0b62b825dd4.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the competent wildlife authority.
xs: Projects in tiger corridors need **NBWL Standing Committee** clearance — option **(3)**.
The **NTCA** implements Project Tiger but does not alone clear corridor projects.
xa: A **3rd railway line** threatens the **Satpura-Melghat corridor** (4 Aug 2026).
A **growing share of tigers** disperses **outside reserves**, raising conflict.
The **Global Tiger Forum** is an international body, not a clearance authority.

n32693d7373e.s: Project Elephant was launched as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme in which month and year?
n32693d7373e.x: Project Elephant was launched in February 1992 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (some sources say 1991-92). '1990' is the trap: APPSC 2022 treated a 1990 launch as the incorrect statement.
n32693d7373e.tq: Use the precise month-year rather than confusing the financial year with the launch year.
xs: **Project Elephant** was launched in **February 1992** as a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme** — option **(3)**.
⚠ "Launched in **1990**" is wrong (APPSC **2022**); some notes say **1991-92**.
xa: It covers **33 Elephant Reserves** in **14 States**.
It also covers the welfare of **captive** elephants.
The elephant became the **National Heritage Animal** in **2010**.

n85a5d50cbe1.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the seven big cats covered by the International Big Cat Alliance?
n85a5d50cbe1.x: The seven big cats are tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma. Gharial is not a big cat covered by the IBCA.
n85a5d50cbe1.tq: Find the non-member by checking the exact species composition.
xs: The **gharial** is a crocodilian, not a big cat — option **(4)**.
IBCA's **7 big cats**: **tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar, puma**.
xa: IBCA is open to **96 range countries** plus non-range countries.
**37 countries** have consented to join; **Saudi Arabia** was the **26th** member and **Bangladesh** the **27th**.
The gharial was covered by the **Crocodile Project** (**1975**).

n3fa7b096e43.s: Rushikulya (Odisha) and the beaches of Srikakulam and Vizianagaram (Andhra Pradesh) are known for:
n3fa7b096e43.x: These beaches are associated with Olive Ridley mass nesting, known as arribada.
xa: **Operation Olivia** (Coast Guard) has protected Olive Ridleys annually since the early **1980s**.
**Olive Ridley turtle** is one of MoEFCC's **five new national projects**.
**National Marine Turtle Action Plan**: **2021**.

ndc580026109.s: Under the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016, what share of the money goes to the State Funds?
ndc580026109.x: 90% goes to the State Funds and 10% to the National Fund.
xa: ⚠ Some notes date the Act to **2021**.
CAMPA funds go to **wildlife management** and **human-wildlife conflict**.
The **National CAMPA Advisory Council** funds the Recovery Programme for **5 years**.

n8d56b79fc5d.s: Project Tiger began in 1973 with how many tiger reserves?
n8d56b79fc5d.x: Project Tiger started in 1973 with 9 reserves covering 18,278 sq km; today there are 58 reserves.
xa: First tiger reserve: **Corbett** (**1 April 1973**).
**NTCA**: statutory body via the **2006 amendment** to the WPA; chaired by the **Union Environment Minister**.
India's largest TR: **NSTR**, about **5,443 sq km** core.

n114e2d8c996.s: Which of the following was among the first nine tiger reserves under Project Tiger?
n114e2d8c996.x: Palamau was among the first nine reserves of Project Tiger, which was launched on the advice of Indira Gandhi's task force.
xa: First reserve: **Corbett**.
It is implemented by the **NTCA** under **MoEFCC**.
IBCA was launched in **April 2023** to mark **50 years of Project Tiger**.

n5272db06319.s: The Global Tiger Summit of November 2010, which set the TX2 goal, was held at:
n5272db06319.x: The summit was held in St Petersburg in November 2010 and adopted TX2; International Tiger Day (29 July) traces to this effort.
xa: TX2 = double wild tigers by **2022**; India met it early.
The **Global Tiger Forum** dates from **1993** (HQ **New Delhi**).
Other efforts: **IBCA**, **ITHCP** (led by **IUCN**), **CA|TS**.

n594da9b142c.s: The All India Tiger Estimation is conducted at what interval and jointly by which organisations?
o: Every five years by MoEFCC and BNHS
Every three years by WII and Forest Survey of India
Every four years by NTCA and WII
Every two years by NTCA and Zoological Survey of India
n594da9b142c.x: All India Tiger Estimation is conducted every four years by NTCA and the Wildlife Institute of India.
n594da9b142c.tq: Match frequency with the correct institutional partnership.
xs: The **All India Tiger Estimation** is held every **four years** by **NTCA with WII** — option **(3)**.
It uses **camera traps** and the **M-STrIPES** monitoring system.
xa: The camera-trap survey holds a **Guinness World Record**.
The old **pugmark** method gave way to **camera trapping + ExtractCompare**.

nbbbf56d5fdd.s: Which of the following correctly describes the fifth cycle of All India Tiger Estimation conducted in 2022?
o: 3,925 tigers, with an upper estimate of 3,682
3,682 tigers, with an upper estimate of 3,925
2,967 tigers, with an upper estimate of 3,682
3,682 tigers, with an upper estimate of 4,925
nbbbf56d5fdd.x: The 2022 estimation recorded 3,682 tigers, with an upper estimate of 3,925.
nbbbf56d5fdd.tq: Distinguish the principal estimate from the upper estimate in paired figures.
xs: **2022 (5th cycle)**: **3,682 tigers**, upper estimate **3,925** — option **(2)**.
Option (1) reverses the two figures.
xa: Annual growth: **6.1%**.
India holds about **70-75%** of the world's wild tigers.

n323d5884c9e.s: India holds approximately what share of the world’s wild tiger population?
n323d5884c9e.x: India holds approximately 70–75% of the world’s wild tigers.
n323d5884c9e.tq: Use the range rather than confusing it with an exact census figure.
xs: India holds about **70-75% of the world's wild tigers** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Some notes say **70%**, others **75%**.
xa: India also has **60%** of the world's **Asian elephants**.
**58 tiger reserves** cover about **2.56%** of India's area.

n9b91e839092.s: Which technique replaced the old pugmark method in all-India tiger estimation?
o: Camera trapping supported by ExtractCompare software
Counting tiger kills reported by villages
Only satellite imagery without field verification
n9b91e839092.x: The old pugmark technique was replaced by camera trapping and ExtractCompare software, which identifies tigers through stripe patterns.
n9b91e839092.tq: Identify the modern method by contrasting it with the obsolete field technique.
xs: The **pugmark** method gave way to **camera trapping** with **ExtractCompare** software — option **(1)**.
ExtractCompare identifies tigers by their **stripe pattern**.
xa: The survey uses the **M-STrIPES** monitoring system.
It is held every **4 years** by **NTCA with WII**.
It holds a **Guinness World Record** as a camera-trap survey.

n09cb93eb0ef.s: The Action Plan for Vulture Conservation that called for State-level vulture committees and more breeding centres covered the period:
n09cb93eb0ef.x: The 2020–25 Action Plan called for State-level committees and more breeding centres; its extension to 2030 came later.
xa: ⚠ **Vulture Recovery Plan** = **2006**; **Action Plan** = **2020-25**, now to **2030**.
**SAVE** (Saving Asia's Vultures from Extinction) is the partner consortium.
First vulture portal: **"The Vulture Network"**.

n93ec428024e.s: Project HANUMAN was launched by Andhra Pradesh on World Wildlife Day primarily to:
o: Restore coral reefs along the coast
Increase tiger numbers through captive breeding
n93ec428024e.x: Andhra Pradesh launched Project HANUMAN on 3 March 2026, World Wildlife Day, to reduce human-wildlife conflict.
n93ec428024e.tq: Link the project name, launch occasion and stated objective.
xs: AP's **Project HANUMAN** aims to **reduce human-wildlife conflict** — option **(3)**.
It was launched on **World Wildlife Day**, **3 March 2026**.
xa: **Human-elephant conflict** in AP: crop raids in **Chittoor** and **Anantapur**.
Nationally, human-elephant conflict causes **over 500 human deaths a year**.
**CAMPA** funds are also used for **wildlife management** and **human-wildlife conflict**.

n0338e8847c7.s: A railway line through which tiger corridor has been reported as a conservation concern?
n0338e8847c7.x: A railway line through the Satpura-Melghat corridor is a reported concern, alongside tiger dispersal and rising conflict.
xa: Projects in tiger corridors need **NBWL Standing Committee** clearance.
**58 reserves** in **18 States** cover **84,488 sq km** (about **2.56%** of India).
Tigers, **2022**: **3,682**, about **70-75%** of the world's wild tigers.

na40ecd47f85.s: Indian Rhino Vision 2020 for the one-horned rhinoceros in Assam was launched in:
na40ecd47f85.x: Indian Rhino Vision 2020 began in 2005; Project Lion and Project Dolphin began in 2020.
xa: ⚠ **Project Snow Leopard** = **2009**, not 2020.
India has **891 Asiatic lions** and **over 4,000 rhinos** (Apr 2026).
India's riverine dolphins number **6,327**.

n9be7505e625.s: Under the Wildlife Protection Act, the Ganges River Dolphin is included in:
n9be7505e625.x: The Ganges River Dolphin is listed in Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.
n9be7505e625.tq: Test the exact statutory schedule, a common legal-classification trap.
xs: The Ganges River Dolphin is in **Schedule I** of the **WPA 1972** — option **(3)**.
Its scientific name is **Platanista gangetica**; it is India's **National Aquatic Animal**.
xa: It is the **National Aquatic Animal** (**5 October 2009**).
Threats: **dams**, barrages, **pollution**, **bycatch**, poaching for oil, boat traffic.
**Project Dolphin** (**2020**) covers riverine and marine dolphins.

ne3b148e77a5.s: The first national assessment of riverine dolphins recorded a total of:
ne3b148e77a5.x: The first national assessment recorded 6,327 riverine dolphins. The survey covered 8,500 km across 28 rivers in eight States; 8,500 is therefore a distance, not the dolphin count.
ne3b148e77a5.tq: Separate the population figure from the survey-distance figure.
xs: The first national survey counted **6,327** riverine dolphins — option **(4)**.
**8,500 km** is the distance surveyed, not the count.
⚠ "Fewer than **2,000**" is an older note.
xa: The survey covered **28 rivers** in **8 States**.
Compare: **3,682** tigers, **22,446** elephants, **891** lions.
The Gangetic dolphin is in **Schedule I**.

n7293cb416a2.s: Which is the largest tiger reserve in India by area?
n7293cb416a2.x: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve (NSTR) in the Nallamala hills of Andhra Pradesh is India's largest tiger reserve, with a core area of about 5,443 sq km. Bandipur, Corbett and Kanha are smaller.
n7293cb416a2.tq: Test the largest-reserve comparison using the area-based distinction.
xs: **Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam (NSTR)** is **India's largest tiger reserve** — option **(1)**.
Its core area is about **5,443 sq km**, in the **Nallamala** hills of AP.
**Corbett** is the **first** reserve, not the largest.
xa: NSTR anti-poaching camps are rising from **89 to 150** (30 Jul 2026).
AP will receive **4 female tigers** from **Maharashtra** and **MP**.
**Gaur** are being reintroduced in NSTR (Jul 2026).

nae5a92140e2.s: Which one of the following is NOT an objective of Project Elephant?
o: Protection of elephant habitats and corridors
Protection of only captive elephants and not wild elephants
nae5a92140e2.x: Project Elephant covers wild elephants, their habitats and corridors, mitigation of conflict, and the welfare of captive elephants. It is not restricted to captive elephants.
nae5a92140e2.tq: Find the option narrowed by the extreme word ‘only’.
xs: "**Only captive elephants, not wild ones**" is not an objective — option **(3)**.
Objectives: protect elephants, their **habitats and corridors**; mitigate **man-elephant conflict**; welfare of **captive** elephants.
⚠ The reverse trap — "only wild elephants" — is also wrong (UPPSC **2017**).
xa: Human-elephant conflict causes **over 500 human deaths a year**.
**MIKE** (Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants) is a **CITES** programme.
Launched **February 1992**.

naba75276748.s: MIKE, associated with elephant conservation, stands for:
o: Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants
naba75276748.x: MIKE stands for Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants and is a CITES programme.
naba75276748.tq: Expand the exact acronym and identify the associated international programme.
xs: **MIKE** = **Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants** — option **(1)**.
It is a **CITES** programme.
xa: ⚠ **MIKE** = elephants; **M-STrIPES** = tigers.
**Project Elephant** began in **February 1992**.
India has **60%** of the world's Asian elephants.

n8ba39a368c9.s: The gestation period of the Asian elephant, the longest of any mammal, is about:
n8ba39a368c9.x: Asian elephant gestation is about 22 months, the longest among mammals.
xa: Elephant = **National Heritage Animal** (**2010**).
⚠ Gangetic dolphin = **National Aquatic Animal** (**2009**).
India has **22,446 elephants** (Apr 2026).

n5530f8e31f3.s: In which year was the elephant declared India's National Heritage Animal?
n5530f8e31f3.x: The elephant was declared the National Heritage Animal in 2010. 1992 is the launch of Project Elephant, 2009 is when the Ganges river dolphin became the National Aquatic Animal, and 2020 is the launch of Project Lion and Project Dolphin.
xs: The elephant was declared the **National Heritage Animal** in **2010** — option **(3)**.
**1992** = Project Elephant; **2009** = Gangetic dolphin as **National Aquatic Animal**; **2020** = Project Lion and Project Dolphin.
xa: The dolphin was declared on **5 October 2009** — now **National Dolphin Day**.
**Project Elephant** was a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme**.
Only male Asian elephants carry **tusks**.

o: Riverine and marine dolphins and other cetaceans
nf89691df9b8.x: Project Dolphin covers both riverine and marine dolphins as well as other cetaceans.
xa: **Dolphin** is also among MoEFCC's **five new national projects** (2026).
The **Gangetic dolphin** is the **National Aquatic Animal** (**2009**).
⚠ **Project Lion** was launched in the same year, **2020**.

n981db127e04.s: India's Vulture Conservation and Breeding Centre (Jatayu centre), the first vulture breeding centre, is located at:
n981db127e04.x: The Vulture Conservation and Breeding Centre is at Pinjore, Haryana. Keoladeo is where the decline was first noticed (1998), Jaisalmer hosts the GIB breeding centres, and Darjeeling breeds red pandas.
n981db127e04.tq: Vultures - Pinjore; GIB - Jaisalmer; red panda - Darjeeling.
xs: The **Jatayu** Vulture Conservation and Breeding Centre is at **Pinjore, Haryana** — option **(1)**.
**Keoladeo** is where the decline was noticed (**1998**); **Jaisalmer** breeds the **GIB**.
xa: It is India's **first vulture breeding centre**.
Vulture plans: **Recovery Plan 2006**; **Action Plan 2020-25**, extended to **2030**.
The plan calls for **more breeding centres**.

n48523361e68.s: India's first Dugong Conservation Reserve was established in:
n48523361e68.x: India's first Dugong Conservation Reserve was established in Palk Bay, Tamil Nadu, in 2022.
n48523361e68.tq: Distinguish the dugong reserve location from other marine protected areas.
xs: India's **first Dugong Conservation Reserve** is in **Palk Bay, Tamil Nadu** (**2022**) — option **(4)**.
**Gulf of Mannar** is linked with dugongs too, but is a marine NP/BR; **Malvan** and **Coringa** are sanctuaries.
xa: **Dugong** is on the **Species Recovery Programme**.
**Malvan Marine Sanctuary** (Maharashtra) protects **corals**.
**Coringa** (Kakinada) protects **mangroves**.

nb6ff7dffc11.s: The headquarters of the Wildlife Institute of India is located at:
nb6ff7dffc11.x: The Wildlife Institute of India (WII) is headquartered at Dehradun.
nb6ff7dffc11.tq: Test the location of the institution directly against nearby headquarters.
xs: The **Wildlife Institute of India (WII)**, set up in **1982**, is headquartered at **Dehradun** — option **(3)**.
**Gland** is the HQ of **IUCN** and **WWF**; **Mumbai** of **BNHS**; **Noida** of **WTI**.
xa: WII runs the **All India Tiger Estimation** with the **NTCA**, every **four years**.
The **Aqua Life Conservation Monitoring Centre** (Jan 2026) is at **WII Dehradun**, under **Namami Gange**.

n1acb0e87fdd.s: Rayala in Andhra Pradesh is the State's only:
n1acb0e87fdd.x: Rayala is Andhra Pradesh's only elephant reserve; the State also has India's largest tiger reserve.
xa: NSTR: about **5,443 sq km** core; anti-poaching camps going up from **89 to 150**.
⚠ **Koundinya** = sanctuary (Chittoor), AP's **only elephant habitat**; **Rayala** = elephant reserve.

n8fdb365fbb4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Species Recovery Programme under CSS-Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats?
o: The Great Indian Bustard and marine turtles are among the species it covers
Hangul and dugong are among the species it covers
Gharial and sloth bear have been covered by it from the start
n8fdb365fbb4.x: Gharial and sloth bear were only recommended for inclusion (June 2026); they were not covered from the start.
xa: The Recovery Programme is funded via the **National CAMPA Advisory Council**, for an initial **5 years**.
**CAMPA**: statutory backing by the **Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016**; split **90%** State / **10%** National.
**Vulture Action Plan 2020-25** extended to **2030**.

ne64d260d59f.s: The IUCN Red List status of the Great Indian Bustard is:
ne64d260d59f.x: The GIB is Critically Endangered, with fewer than 150 birds left in the wild.
xa: Main threat: collisions with **overhead power lines** in solar and wind zones.
Conservation breeding at **Jaisalmer, Rajasthan**.
AP site: **Rollapadu WLS** (**Kurnool**; now **Nandyal**).

n3b023466b4a.s: The principal natural range of the Great Indian Bustard is associated with which of the following regions?
n3b023466b4a.x: The Great Indian Bustard is found mainly in the Thar region of Rajasthan, although its range also extends into parts of Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka.
n3b023466b4a.tq: Use the core range as the distinguishing geographical fact.
xs: The GIB lives mainly in the **Thar (Rajasthan)** — option **(3)**.
It also occurs in **Gujarat**, **Maharashtra** and **Karnataka**.
xa: In AP: **Rollapadu WLS** (**Kurnool**; now **Nandyal**).
The GIB is **Critically Endangered**, with **fewer than 150** birds.
It is one of MoEFCC's **five new national species projects**.

n4ebc970880c.s: The major conservation threat to the Great Indian Bustard in solar and wind-energy zones is:
n4ebc970880c.x: Collisions with overhead power lines are a major threat to the Great Indian Bustard, particularly in solar and wind-energy zones.
n4ebc970880c.tq: Match the conservation problem with the habitat-specific human infrastructure causing it.
xs: The GIB's main threat is **collision with overhead power lines** in solar and wind zones — option **(1)**.
Net entanglement and pollution are **dolphin** threats; mangrove loss is a coastal issue.
xa: The SC ordered GIB-area power lines laid **underground** in **2021**.
**M.K. Ranjitsinh (March 2024)** modified the blanket order and set up an **expert committee**.
⚠ CMS **COP13** mascot **"Gibi"** was a GIB.

n996f68947ab.s: The National Dolphin Research Centre is located at:
n996f68947ab.x: The National Dolphin Research Centre is at Patna; Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary is at Bhagalpur.
xa: ⚠ **Vikramshila** = **Bhagalpur** (sanctuary); **Patna** = research centre.
New (Jan 2026): a **Dolphin Rescue Ambulance** and an **Aqua Life Conservation Monitoring Centre** (**WII Dehradun**, **Namami Gange**).
Riverine dolphins: **6,327**.

n9a6e9a63f0a.s: Which one of the following is NOT a recognised threat to the Ganges River Dolphin?
n9a6e9a63f0a.x: Pollution, entanglement or bycatch in fishing nets, dams and barrages, poaching, killing for oil and boat traffic are recognised threats. Expansion of desert grasslands is not identified as a threat to the river dolphin.
n9a6e9a63f0a.tq: Find the geographically unrelated option among the listed threats.
xs: **Expansion of desert grasslands** is not a threat to the river dolphin — option **(3)**.
Listed threats: **dams**, barrages, water diversion, **pollution**, **bycatch** in nets, poaching for oil, boat traffic.
xa: Range: **Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna** and **Karnaphuli-Sangu** systems.
A **Dolphin Rescue Ambulance** started in **Jan 2026**.
Sanctuary: **Vikramshila**, **Bhagalpur**.

n56e371e54fa.s: Which one of the following was declared India's National Aquatic Animal in 2009?
n56e371e54fa.x: The Ganges River Dolphin (Platanista gangetica) was declared the National Aquatic Animal on 5 October 2009. The Olive Ridley turtle, gharial and humpback dolphin are the distractors used in the APPSC 2019 question.
n56e371e54fa.tq: National Aquatic Animal = Ganges river dolphin (5 Oct 2009).
xs: The **Ganges River Dolphin** became the **National Aquatic Animal** in **2009** — option **(3)**.
⚠ It is **not** the Olive Ridley, humpback dolphin or gharial (APPSC **2019**).
xa: The date, **5 October**, is **National Dolphin Day**.
Elephant = **National Heritage Animal** (**2010**).
Scientific name: **Platanista gangetica**.

nbaa05e5a918.s:
Which of the following veterinary drugs were banned for animal use in 2023?
1. Aceclofenac
2. Ketoprofen
3. Diclofenac
nbaa05e5a918.x: Aceclofenac and ketoprofen were banned for animal use in 2023; diclofenac had already been banned in 2006.
xa: **Meloxicam** is the safe alternative.
**Action Plan for Vulture Conservation 2020-25** is extended to **2030**.
Breeding centre: **Pinjore (Haryana)**; also **Vulture Safe Zones**.

n1c900d3ad61.s: The decline of vultures in India was first noticed at Keoladeo in:
n1c900d3ad61.x: The decline was noticed at Keoladeo in 1998; 2006 is when veterinary diclofenac was banned.
xa: **Vultures** were added to the **Species Recovery Programme** (2026).
First vulture portal: **"The Vulture Network"**.
**5 slender-billed vultures** were released in **Assam** — a world first.

n6a2b69f7dee.s: Which place in Nagaland is called the 'Falcon Capital of the World'?
n6a2b69f7dee.x: Pangti, near the Doyang reservoir where Amur falcons gather in huge numbers, is the 'Falcon Capital of the World'.
xa: Route: **SE Russia** and **northern China** → **southern Africa**.
It is one of the **longest raptor migrations**.
Migratory species fall under **CMS** (Bonn Convention, **1979**).

n2673da72d10.s: The Great hornbill is associated as the logo of the:
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
n2673da72d10.x: The Great hornbill is the logo of the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS).
n2673da72d10.tq: Discriminate between similar conservation organisations using their emblem.
xs: The **Great hornbill** is the logo of the **Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS)** — option **(2)**.
BNHS was founded in **1883** and is based in **Mumbai**.
**WWF**'s logo is the **Giant panda**.
xa: **IUCN (1948)** and **WWF (1961)** are both headquartered at **Gland, Switzerland**.
**WTI (1998)** is at **Noida, UP**; **WII (1982)** is at **Dehradun**.
BNHS released the world's first captive-bred **slender-billed vultures** in **Assam** (**Aug 2026**).

n29088e1662f.s: The cheetahs introduced in India under Project Cheetah are:
o: Asiatic cheetahs bred in captivity in India
n29088e1662f.x: The introduced animals are African cheetahs; the critically endangered Asiatic cheetah survives only in Iran.
xa: ⚠ One report names "**Nigeria**" — the correct country is **Namibia**.
Release site: **Kuno NP**, **Sheopur, MP**.
**2** **Botswana** females were released into the wild in **May 2026**.

n6990df58a27.s: The cheetah, the only large mammal to have gone extinct in India in recent history, was declared extinct in India in:
n6990df58a27.x: The cheetah was declared extinct in India in 1952. 1947 is Independence, 1972 is the Wildlife (Protection) Act, and 2012 is when the Supreme Court first ruled on its reintroduction.
xs: The cheetah was declared **extinct in India in 1952** — option **(2)**.
It is the **only large mammal** lost in India in recent history.
**2012** is the SC's first ruling on its reintroduction.
xa: The **Asiatic cheetah** survives only in **Iran**.
**Project Cheetah** aims to restore **open forest and grassland**.
First batch to **Kuno**: **17 Sep 2022**.

n2517e014d85.s: The International Big Cat Alliance was launched in April 2023 primarily to mark
o: the declaration of the cheetah as extinct in India
the first census of Asiatic lions
n2517e014d85.x: The International Big Cat Alliance was launched in April 2023 to mark 50 years of Project Tiger.
n2517e014d85.tq: Link an organisation's launch with the milestone it commemorated.
xs: **IBCA** was launched in **April 2023** at **Mysuru** to mark **50 years of Project Tiger** — option **(4)**.
Project Tiger began in **1973**.
xa: IBCA is a **treaty-based inter-governmental organisation**.
Secretariat: **New Delhi** — ⚠ **not Geneva**.
First IBCA summit: **New Delhi**, **1-3 June 2026**.

n2c935593038.s: The Secretariat of the International Big Cat Alliance is located in:
n2c935593038.x: IBCA, a treaty-based inter-governmental body, has its Secretariat in New Delhi; Geneva is not its headquarters.
xa: The India-IBCA agreement was signed **17 April 2025**.
⚠ **Global Tiger Forum** and **IBCA** are both in **New Delhi**; **IUCN** and **WWF** are both in **Gland**.
**China is unlikely to join** (12 May 2026).

n50e8c160923.s: Kuno was initially selected as a second home for which animal before being used for Project Cheetah?
o: Gharials from the National Chambal Sanctuary
n50e8c160923.x: Kuno was initially chosen as a second home for Gir's Asiatic lions. The Supreme Court ordered lion translocation in 2013, but Gujarat did not implement it.
n50e8c160923.tq: Use the earlier conservation purpose of the same site as the discriminator.
xs: **Kuno** was first chosen as a second home for **Gir's Asiatic lions** — option **(1)**.
The SC ordered the translocation in **2013**, but **Gujarat did not carry it out**, so **Kuno went to cheetahs**.
xa: The new proposed lion second home is **Barda WLS** (Gujarat).
⚠ **Kuno** = first chosen for lions; **Barda** = proposed lion second home.
Kuno NP lies in **Sheopur, MP**, on the Kuno river.

na5219a705dc.s: Barda Wildlife Sanctuary has been proposed as a second home for Asiatic lions. The principal criticism of this proposal is that Barda:
o: Is too close to Gir to provide a genuine metapopulation safeguard
Has no forest cover at all
Is exclusively a marine protected area
na5219a705dc.x: Critics argue that Barda Wildlife Sanctuary is too close to Gir to function as an effective separate metapopulation safeguard.
na5219a705dc.tq: Identify the ecological rationale behind the second-home debate.
xs: Critics say **Barda WLS** is **too close to Gir** for a real **metapopulation** safeguard — option **(2)**.
Barda is in **Gujarat**, so option (1) is wrong.
xa: **Kuno** was first chosen for the lions but went to **cheetahs** after Gujarat ignored the **2013** SC order.
**Project Lion** (**2020**) covers surveillance, research and disease management.
The **Gir** lion translocation was **never carried out**.

n4a557a7aeb4.s: MISHTI, launched in 2023, is primarily associated with:
n4a557a7aeb4.x: MISHTI is a mangrove restoration initiative launched in 2023, covering approximately 22,561 hectares in 13 States and Union Territories.
n4a557a7aeb4.tq: Match the programme with its environmental objective rather than its geographical setting.
xs: **MISHTI (2023)** is about **mangrove restoration** — option **(3)**.
It covers about **22,561 ha** in **13** States/UTs.
xa: **National Marine Turtle Action Plan** dates from **2021**.
**Coringa** and **Bhitarkanika** are major mangrove sanctuaries.
**BBNJ Agreement (2024)** covers the high seas.

n864e7db6e05.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India?
o: In March 2024, the 2021 blanket direction was upheld without change
In 2021, the Supreme Court directed that power lines in GIB habitat be laid underground
In March 2024, an expert committee was constituted
It concerned protection of the Great Indian Bustard from power-line impacts
n864e7db6e05.x: In March 2024 the blanket undergrounding direction was modified, not upheld unchanged, and an expert committee was set up.
xa: The case recognised a **right against the adverse effects of climate change** under **Articles 14 and 21**.
⚠ Some notes describe the **2024** order as mandating underground lines.
The GIB has **fewer than 150** birds left.

nf9709373555.s: In the context of the Supreme Court’s March 2024 proceedings concerning the Great Indian Bustard, which constitutional rights were recognised in relation to adverse effects of climate change?
nf9709373555.x: The Supreme Court recognised a right against the adverse effects of climate change under Articles 14 and 21.
nf9709373555.tq: Use the exact constitutional-article pair rather than a broad description of environmental rights.
xs: The SC recognised a **right against the adverse effects of climate change** under **Articles 14 and 21** — option **(3)**.
This came in **M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India** (**March 2024**).
xa: The case was about **protecting the GIB** from power lines.
It modified the **2021** blanket underground-lines order and set up an **expert committee**.
Main GIB threat: **overhead power lines** in solar and wind zones.

n65001f17c1f.s: The National Chambal Sanctuary, India's only tri-state riverine protected area, is shared by:
o: Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh
n65001f17c1f.x: The National Chambal Sanctuary (1979) spans Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh along the Chambal river. Gujarat, Bihar and Haryana are not part of it.
n65001f17c1f.tq: Chambal = MP + Rajasthan + UP; gharial stronghold.
xs: The **National Chambal Sanctuary** spans **MP, Rajasthan and UP** — option **(1)**.
It was set up in **1979** and is India's **only tri-state riverine PA**.
xa: The SC took **suo motu** cognisance to protect **gharials** there.
**Gharials** were reintroduced in **several states** through captive breeding.
The **Crocodile Project** began in **1975**.

nabebeff60c3.s: The Recovery Programme for Critically Endangered Species funded through the National CAMPA Advisory Council was sanctioned initially for:
nabebeff60c3.x: The programme was sanctioned for an initial period of five years.
nabebeff60c3.tq: Use the programme-duration figure directly and reject nearby durations.
xs: The **Recovery Programme for Critically Endangered Species** was sanctioned for an initial **5 years** — option **(3)** (APPSC 2019 key).
It is funded via the **National CAMPA Advisory Council**.
xa: The SC set up an **ad hoc CAMPA** in **2006**.
Statutory backing: **Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016**.
CAMPA money: **90%** to State funds, **10%** to the National Fund.

nee2564d8a84.s: Which Indian locations have been identified as IUCN and Mission Blue Hope Spots?
o: Gulf of Mannar and Palk Bay
Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Palk Bay
nee2564d8a84.x: Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are India's IUCN and Mission Blue Hope Spots.
xa: Hope Spots are named by **IUCN** and **Mission Blue**.
**Palk Bay** = India's **first Dugong Conservation Reserve** (**2022**).
**Gulf of Mannar** is known for **coral reefs, islands, dugong**.

nenvironment-17-4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the whale shark?
o: The Gujarat coast is an important seasonal location for it.
It can reach about 50 feet in length.
Gujarat's whale shark protection programme started in 2006.
nenvironment-17-4.x: Gujarat's whale shark protection programme began in 2004, not 2006.
n: The Whale Shark is India's largest fish. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 31-33]
The Whale Shark can reach about 50 feet. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 31-33]
The Gujarat coast is an important seasonal location for Whale Sharks. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 31-33]
A protection programme for Whale Sharks visiting the Gujarat coast started in 2004. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 31-33]
The Whale Shark is associated with the Gujarat coast. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 31-33]
xa: **Kharai Camel** **swims** in seawater up to **3 km** and **grazes on mangroves**.
India's first **Dugong Conservation Reserve**: **Palk Bay, Tamil Nadu** (**2022**).
Olive Ridley mass nesting (**arribada**): **Rushikulya** (Odisha) and **Srikakulam / Vizianagaram** beaches (AP).

n811544df4a2.s: Reserved, protected and village forests were introduced by the Indian Forest Act of:
n811544df4a2.x: The 1878 Act introduced the three categories; the first Act was drafted in 1865, and the 1927 Act is still in force.
xa: The **Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980** came into force on **25 October 1980**; it did not repeal the 1927 Act.
Under the **1927** Act, **Sec. 26** lists acts prohibited in a reserved forest and makes **trespass** punishable.

n5783e865f4b.s: The Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act, 2023 renamed the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 as the
n5783e865f4b.x: The 2023 amendment renamed it the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980.
n5783e865f4b.tq: Distinguish the exact official title from plausible but unofficial alternatives.
xs: The 2023 amendment renamed the FCA as the **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980** — option **(2)**.
The Act was **renamed, not repealed**, so both names appear in questions; the renaming took effect from **29 Dec 2023**.
xa: **Exemptions** from Central approval: strategic linear projects within **100 km** of the **IB, LoC or LAC**, eco-tourism, zoos and safaris.
**Compensatory afforestation**: **non-forest land of equal area**, else **twice the area of degraded forest land**, plus **NPV**.
Critics say it takes **"deemed forests"** out of scope, diluting the **Godavarman** ruling.
AP had diverted **27,641.252 ha** of forest under the Adhiniyam up to **31.12.2024**.

ncefac6acb78.s: The 42nd Amendment, 1976 transferred forests to the Concurrent List through Entry:
ncefac6acb78.x: Forests went to the Concurrent List as Entry 17A, and protection of wild animals and birds as Entry 17B.
xa: The same **42nd Amendment (1976)** inserted **Art. 48A** (DPSP) and **Art. 51A(g)** (Fundamental Duty).
The **T.N. Godavarman** case (**1995**) read "forest" as every area recorded as forest in government records.
⚠ **17A** = forests; **17B** = wild animals and birds.

nbe1a1a29e41.s: Article 48A, a Directive Principle on protecting the environment, forests and wildlife, was inserted by the:
nbe1a1a29e41.x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) inserted Article 48A; it also added Article 51A(g), a Fundamental Duty.
xa: The 42nd Amendment (**1976**) moved forests and wildlife to the **Concurrent List**.
⚠ **Entry 17A** = forests; **Entry 17B** = wild animals and birds.
**T.N. Godavarman (1995)**: "forest" = every area recorded as forest, **whatever the ownership**.

nf9a2db01e25.s: The 2002 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act replaced the Indian Board for Wildlife with the
nf9a2db01e25.x: The 2002 amendment replaced the Indian Board for Wildlife with the National Board for Wildlife.
nf9a2db01e25.tq: Track the institutional replacement rather than confusing it with bodies created in 2006.
xs: The **2002** amendment replaced the Indian Board for Wildlife with the **National Board for Wildlife** — option **(2)**.
**NTCA** and **WCCB** came with the **2006** amendment; the **Animal Welfare Board** is under the **PCA Act 1960**.
xa: **NBWL** is chaired by the **Prime Minister**; its **Standing Committee** by the **Union Environment Minister**.
The **State Board for Wildlife** is chaired by the **Chief Minister**.
The full NBWL met in **2025** after a **13-year** gap; the Standing Committee cleared **over 97%** of diversion proposals.

naab64fab850.s: Which international convention’s provisions were specifically brought into the Wildlife (Protection) Act through the 2022 amendment?
naab64fab850.x: The 2022 amendment incorporated CITES-related provisions, including provisions concerning management and scientific authorities.
naab64fab850.tq: Distinguish the wildlife-trade convention from other environmental treaties.
xs: The 2022 amendment brought **CITES** provisions into the WPA — option **(3)**.
It provides for CITES **management and scientific authorities**.
xa: After 2022, **Schedule IV** lists specimens in the **CITES Appendices** (**APPSC-GS 2024**).
⚠ The **CBD** is implemented by the **BD Act 2002**, not the WPA.
The amendment came into force in **April 2023**.

ne404ac98efb.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the exemptions associated with the Forest Conservation Amendment Act, 2023?
o: Strategic projects within 100 km of international borders
Mandatory Gram Sabha consent for every new exemption
ne404ac98efb.x: The amendment is criticised because it is silent on the Forest Rights Act and does not mandate Gram Sabha consent for the new exemptions. Strategic projects, eco-tourism and zoos are among the mentioned exemptions.
ne404ac98efb.tq: Find the option that reverses the criticism about the absence of Gram Sabha consent.
xs: **Mandatory Gram Sabha consent** is not in the amendment — option **(4)**.
The amendment is **silent on FRA** and mandates no Gram Sabha consent for the new exemptions.
**Eco-tourism**, strategic projects within **100 km** of borders and **zoos** are listed exemptions.
xa: **FCR 2022** dropped the consent clause, sparking an **NCST-MoEFCC** dispute.
**Van (S.E.S.) Amendment Rules 2025**: assisted natural regeneration counts as **"forestry activities"**; CA and NPV do not apply.
Coverage excludes land converted to non-forest use before **12 Dec 1996**.

ndf513655eb8.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a change introduced by the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023?
o: All biodiversity offences were made criminal offences with imprisonment only
Benefit-sharing was abolished for all users
Offences were decriminalised and civil penalties were introduced
Foreign entities were exempted from NBA approval
ndf513655eb8.x: The amendment decriminalised offences and introduced civil penalties. It did not abolish benefit-sharing or exempt foreign entities from prior NBA approval.
ndf513655eb8.tq: Identify the precise legal-consequence change and reject extreme alternatives.
xs: The BD (Amendment) Act 2023 **decriminalised offences** and introduced **civil penalties** — option **(3)**.
It did not abolish benefit-sharing; it only exempted **AYUSH practitioners** and **cultivated medicinal plants**.
**Foreign nationals and foreign-incorporated entities** still need prior **NBA** approval.
xa: It came into force on **1 April 2024** with the **BD Rules 2024**.
NBA approval time cut from **180 to 90 days**; IPR applications stay at **180**.
The **NBA** is headquartered in **Chennai**.

n5a6d4e82efb.s: The National Green Tribunal cannot hear cases under which of the following laws?
n5a6d4e82efb.x: The NGT hears cases under seven laws including the FCA, EPA and BD Act, but not under the WPA 1972 or FRA 2006.
xa: The **FCA 1980** regulates diversion of forest land.
The **BD Act 2002** implements the **CBD**.
The **PCA Act 1960** is the parent Act of the **Animal Welfare Board**.

nde7a131f3ff.s: Which one of the following Acts was enacted to protect wild animals, birds and plants and to manage their habitats?
o: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960
nde7a131f3ff.x: The WPA 1972 protects wild animals, birds and plants and manages their habitats (APPSC 2025 key). The EPA 1986 is an umbrella law for environmental protection and pollution control; the FCA 1980 checks deforestation and regulates diversion of forest land; the PCA Act 1960 prevents cruelty to animals and is the parent Act of the AWBI.
nde7a131f3ff.tq: Wild animals, birds AND plants = WPA 1972, not EPA or FCA.
xs: The **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** protects **wild animals, birds and plants** and manages their habitats — option **(2)**.
**EPA 1986** is the pollution umbrella law; **FCA 1980** checks deforestation; **PCA Act 1960** prevents cruelty to animals.
xa: This was the **APPSC 2025** key.
The WPA has **66 sections** in **7 chapters**.

nefc89b76b5b.s: Why would a Maharashtra Bill amending Section 12 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 require the assent of the President of India?
o: Because relocation of leopards is exclusively a constitutional power of the President
Because the Bill concerns only private forests
Because it seeks to amend a central law
Because every wildlife sanctuary is administered by the President
nefc89b76b5b.x: The Bill requires Presidential assent because it amends a central law, the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. The other statements assign incorrect constitutional or administrative reasons.
nefc89b76b5b.tq: Ask who has authority when a State Bill affects a central law.
xs: The Bill needs **President's assent** because it **amends a central law** — option **(3)**.
It is the **WPA (Maharashtra Amendment) Bill 2026** on **Sec. 12** to relocate leopards.
xa: **Section 12** gives permits for education, research, scientific management, incl. **translocation**.
It also proposed moving the leopard from **Schedule I to II**.
Environmentalists called the down-listing **"regressive"**.

nenvironment-8-4.s: Which Act regulates the diversion of forest land in India?
nenvironment-8-4.x: The FCA, 1980 controls diversion of forest land; the IFA, 1927 sets the forest legal framework.
n: The Indian Forest Act was enacted in 1927. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Indian Forest Act provides a forest administration and legal framework. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Wildlife Protection Act was enacted in 1972. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Wildlife Protection Act concerns wildlife protection. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Forest (Conservation) Act was enacted in 1980. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Forest (Conservation) Act regulates forest-land diversion. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Environment Protection Act was enacted in 1986. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The Environment Protection Act concerns environmental protection. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
xa: First Indian Forest Act: **1865**; the **1878** Act introduced reserved, protected and village forests.
FCA 1980 came into force on **25 October 1980**.
**Forest Rights Act, 2006**: rights of forest-dwelling communities.

nab90d5790a8.s: The Supreme Court’s restriction relating to mining provides that mining is barred within what distance of every national park and sanctuary, unless a larger eco-sensitive zone is notified?
nab90d5790a8.x: Mining is barred within 1 kilometre of every national park and sanctuary boundary unless a larger eco-sensitive zone is notified.
nab90d5790a8.tq: Recall the statutory-distance figure and distinguish it from larger possible buffer zones.
xs: The SC bars mining within **1 kilometre** of every national park and sanctuary boundary — option **(2)**.
The bar applies **unless a larger eco-sensitive zone (ESZ)** is notified.
xa: Under the **WPA**, mining is **prohibited inside NPs and sanctuaries** themselves.
India has **1,000+ protected areas** covering **1,75,169.42 sq km**, i.e. **5.32%** of land area.
The **NBWL Standing Committee** clears projects in or near PAs and tiger corridors.

n6f4aecbfc58.s: Under the Indian Forest Act, 1927, a village forest is a ____ assigned to a village community.
n6f4aecbfc58.x: A village forest is a reserved forest (not a protected forest) assigned to a village community.
xa: Reserved forest = **Ch. II, Sec. 3-27**; village forest = **Ch. III, Sec. 28**; protected forest = **Ch. IV, Sec. 29-34**.
⚠ **Reserved** = barred unless permitted; **Protected** = allowed unless prohibited.
The three categories were first introduced by the **1878** Indian Forest Act.

n51b5592edf3.s: Section 26 of the Indian Forest Act, 1927 primarily deals with
o: regulation of forests that are not government property
assignment of reserved forests to village communities
acts prohibited in a reserved forest, including punishable trespass
removal of bamboo from non-forest land without a permit
n51b5592edf3.x: Section 26 lists prohibited acts in a reserved forest and makes trespass punishable.
n51b5592edf3.tq: Match the offence section with its specific prohibited conduct.
xs: **Sec. 26** lists **acts prohibited in a reserved forest** and makes **trespass** punishable — option **(3)**.
Regulating non-government forests is **Sec. 35**; village forests come under **Sec. 28**.
Bamboo removal without permit came from the **2017 amendment** to **Sec. 2(7)**.
xa: Sec. 26 was the **APPSC 2024** key.
Reserved forests (**Ch. II, Sec. 3-27**) are the most strictly protected category.
The 2017 change came as an Ordinance in **2017** and an Act in **2018**.

nenvironment-8-20.s: Unclassed forests are best described as forests:
o: outside the reserved and protected categories
with the highest restriction on activities
regulated more strictly than protected forests
nenvironment-8-20.x: Unclassed forests are those outside the reserved and protected classes, and they are the least regulated.
nenvironment-8-20.tq: Rank reserved, protected and unclassed forests.
n: Unclassed forests are forests outside the reserved and protected categories. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
xs: **Unclassed forests** lie **outside the reserved and protected categories** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Reserved forests** have the **highest restrictions** — activities **prohibited unless permitted**.
**Protected forests** are **more regulated** than unclassed forests.
xa: ⚠ **Reserved** = barred unless permitted; **Protected** = allowed unless prohibited.
**Sec. 26** of the IFA lists acts prohibited in a reserved forest and makes **trespass** punishable.
**Village forest**: a reserved forest assigned to a village community (**Sec. 28**).

n8a6bfda8bbd.s: The National Forest Policy, 1952 aimed to bring what proportion of the total land under forest?
n8a6bfda8bbd.x: The 1952 Policy targeted one-third of the land under forest, with 60% in hills and 25% in plains.
xa: **NFP 1988**: **33%** of geographical area under forest/tree cover; **two-thirds (66%)** in hilly and mountainous regions.
⚠ **1952** hills = **60%**; **1988** hills = **two-thirds (66%)**; national target both ≈ one-third.
NFP **1952** was the first post-Independence forest policy.

nenvironment-2-1.s: Under the National Forest Policy, 1952, which of the following was included in the forest classification?
o: National, Protected and Village forests, along with Tree-lands
Protected, Village and Urban forests, along with Wetlands
National, Private and Social forests, along with Wastelands
National, Reserved and Community forests, along with Grasslands
nenvironment-2-1.x: The 1952 Forest Policy classified forests as national, protected and village forests, plus tree-lands.
n: The National Forest Policy, 1952, classified forests as national forests. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Forest Policy, 1952, classified forests as protected forests. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Forest Policy, 1952, classified forests as village forests. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Forest Policy, 1952, classified tree-lands as a forest category. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Forest Policy was formulated in 1952. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
xs: The **National Forest Policy, 1952** classified forests as **national**, **protected** and **village forests**, plus **tree-lands** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **National parks** were **not** among its classes.
No urban, private, social, reserved or community forest classes appear in the 1952 scheme.
xa: 1952 target: one-third under forest — **60% in hills**, **25% in plains**.
The **1988** Policy set **33%** nationally and **two-thirds** in hills.
A **Draft** National Forest Policy came in **2018**.

nenvironment-2-8.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the National Forest Policy, 1988?
nenvironment-2-8.x: The 1988 Policy aims at ecological balance, biodiversity conservation and social forestry; it never promoted pesticide use.
n: Ecological balance is a major objective of the National Forest Policy, 1988. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
Social forestry is a major objective of the National Forest Policy, 1988. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
Biodiversity conservation is a major objective of the National Forest Policy, 1988. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
Wood substitutes are included in the National Forest Policy, 1988. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
xa: Other objectives: **ecological afforestation**, **soil and water conservation**.
It includes **wood substitutes** and **alternative fuels**.
It calls for a **massive people's movement involving women**.

nenvironment-8-18.s: Which of the following was a class of forests under the National Forest Policy, 1952?
nenvironment-8-18.x: The 1952 Policy included tree-lands as a class; national parks were not one of its classes.
n: The National Forest Policy of 1952 classified forests as tree lands. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
xa: NFP 1952: **60%** forest in hills, **25%** in plains.
NFP 1988: **33%** nationally; **two-thirds (66%)** in hills.
1952 was the **first post-Independence forest policy**.

nenvironment-8-19.s: The National Forest Policy that encouraged wood substitutes and alternative fuels and aimed at ecological stability was issued in:
nenvironment-8-19.x: The 1988 Policy promoted reforestation, wood substitutes and alternative fuels, and aimed at ecological stability.
n: The National Forest Policy of 1988 promoted reforestation and replantation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The National Forest Policy of 1988 encouraged wood substitutes and alternative fuel. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
The National Forest Policy of 1988 aimed at ecological stability. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 16-19]
xa: It also includes **afforestation** and **wasteland development**.
⚠ It does **not** promote **wide use of insecticides and pesticides**.
Forest-cover target: **one-third (33%)** of geographical area.

n344e5518369.s: Under Section 9 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, hunting of scheduled animals is generally:
o: Permitted throughout the year with a licence
n344e5518369.x: Section 9 prohibits hunting of scheduled animals, subject to exceptions provided by the Act.
n344e5518369.tq: Look for the general rule together with its statutory qualification.
xs: **Section 9** **prohibits** hunting of scheduled animals, **subject to specified exceptions** — option **(1)**.
Exceptions: **Section 11** (danger to human life or crops) and **Section 12** (permits for education, research, translocation).
xa: **Sec. 62**: the Centre may declare a wild animal (not in Schedule I) **vermin** for a specified area and period.
**Section 39**: wild animals, trophies and articles are **Government property**.
**Mining** is prohibited inside NPs and sanctuaries.

n0ea27afa8ac.s: Which section of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 allows action against a wild animal that endangers human life or crops?
n0ea27afa8ac.x: Section 11 covers danger to human life or crops; Section 12 permits cover education, research and scientific management.
xa: Maharashtra's **WPA (Maharashtra Amendment) Bill 2026** targets **Sec. 12** to relocate leopards; it needs **President's assent**.
**Section 9** is the basic ban on hunting scheduled animals.
⚠ **Sec. 9** = ban; **Sec. 11** = danger exception; **Sec. 12** = research/translocation permits.

n4b0a6782aba.s: Section 38V(3), inserted in the Wildlife (Protection) Act by the 2006 amendment, requires
o: a Tiger Conservation Plan for every tiger reserve
a Community Reserve Management Committee for every community reserve
the Centre to regulate invasive alien species
a Chief Wildlife Warden in every State
n4b0a6782aba.x: Sec. 38V(3) (2006 amendment) mandates a Tiger Conservation Plan for every tiger reserve. CRMCs came with the 2002 amendment's community reserves; regulation of invasive alien species and the Chief Wildlife Warden in every State are 2022-amendment changes.
n4b0a6782aba.tq: 2006 amendment = tiger provisions (NTCA, Sec. 38V Tiger Conservation Plan).
xs: **Sec. 38V(3)** requires a **Tiger Conservation Plan for every tiger reserve** — option **(1)**.
**CRMCs** came with the **2002** amendment; invasive species and a **Chief Wildlife Warden** in every State are **2022** changes.
xa: The **2006** amendment also created the **NTCA** and the **WCCB**.
The **NTCA** is chaired by the **Union Environment Minister**.
The **WCCB** was set up on the **Tiger Task Force** recommendation; HQ **New Delhi**.

nf4166c572b7.s: After deletion of the separate vermin schedule, which authority may declare a wild animal not included in Schedule I as vermin?
o: The National Board for Wildlife through a judicial order
The local authority without any restriction on area or period
The Central Government by notification under Section 62
The State Legislature by amendment of Schedule I
nf4166c572b7.x: Under Section 62, the Central Government may declare a wild animal not in Schedule I as vermin for a specified area and period by notification.
nf4166c572b7.tq: Ask who would perform the statutory power and check its area-and-period limits.
xs: The **Central Government**, by **notification under Section 62**, may declare a non-Schedule I animal **vermin** — option **(3)**.
The declaration is for a **specified area and period**, not unrestricted.
xa: Before 2022, **Sch. V** listed vermin: **common crow, fruit bats, rats, mice**.
The **2022** amendment deleted the separate vermin schedule.
The **Indian flying fox** was vermin and is now **Schedule II**.

n44c90ba222b.s: Under the amended biodiversity framework, the ordinary time limit for NBA approval was reduced from 180 days to:
n44c90ba222b.x: The ordinary NBA approval period was reduced from 180 days to 90 days. Applications relating to intellectual property rights continue to have a 180-day period.
n44c90ba222b.tq: Distinguish the general time limit from the IPR exception.
xs: NBA approval time was cut from **180 to 90 days** — option **(3)**.
Applications for **IPR** still have **180** days.
xa: **Foreign nationals and foreign-incorporated entities** still need prior NBA approval.
The amendment came into force on **1 April 2024**.
The **NBA** (HQ **Chennai**) was set up in **2003** under the **BD Act 2002**.

nafe9b45c02e.s: Operation Softgold targeted the illegal trade in:
nafe9b45c02e.x: Softgold concerned shahtoosh; Save Kurma dealt with turtles and Clean Art with mongoose-hair brushes.
xa: **Birbil** targets **wild cats and birds**.
All are **WCCB** operations; WCCB HQ is **New Delhi**.
The WCCB was constituted in **2007** under **MoEFCC**.

n06075c93a26.s: The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) is headquartered at:
n06075c93a26.x: WCCB is headquartered in New Delhi; the Chennai-based body is the National Biodiversity Authority.
xa: WCCB was constituted in **2007** under **MoEFCC**.
Five regional offices: **Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, Chennai, Jabalpur**.
⚠ **NBA** = **Chennai**; **WCCB** = **New Delhi**.

n38e12990550.s: Access and benefit sharing in India is implemented under the:
o: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960
n38e12990550.x: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 implements access and benefit sharing; the FCA regulates forest diversion.
xa: The **EPA 1986** is the umbrella pollution law.
The **NGT** hears **FCA**, **EPA** and **BD Act** cases but not **WPA 1972** or **FRA 2006**.

n1dd75bd0244.s: The 2022 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act is associated with
o: introduction of the Tiger Conservation Plan requirement under Section 38V(3)
replacement of the Indian Board for Wildlife by the National Board for Wildlife
creation of the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau
rationalisation of schedules and addition of invasive alien species
n1dd75bd0244.x: The 2022 amendment rationalised the schedules and added invasive alien species. The other options relate to the 2002 or 2006 amendments.
n1dd75bd0244.tq: Use the amendment timeline to separate later schedule changes from earlier institutional reforms.
xs: The **2022** amendment **rationalised the schedules** and **added invasive alien species** — option **(4)**.
**Sec. 38V(3)** and the **WCCB** came from the **2006** amendment; NBWL replaced the Indian Board in **2002**.
xa: Schedules were cut from **6 to 4** and the separate **vermin schedule deleted**.
**CITES** provisions were brought in (**management and scientific authorities**).
General fines rose to **Rs 1 lakh** (from **Rs 25,000**); in force **April 2023**.

n0d64091c491.s: The 2022 amendment to the Wild Life (Protection) Act changed the number of schedules from:
n0d64091c491.x: The 2022 amendment reduced the schedules from six to four and deleted the separate vermin schedule.
xa: After 2022: **Sch. I** highest protection; **Sch. II** lesser; **Sch. III** protected plants; **Sch. IV** CITES specimens.
Before 2022: **Sch. V** held **vermin** (common crow, fruit bats, rats, mice); **Sch. VI** specified plants.
The **Indian flying fox** moved from vermin (**Schedule V**) to **Schedule II**.

n0b9998428dd.s: After the 2022 amendment, Schedule IV of the Wild Life (Protection) Act contains:
n0b9998428dd.x: Schedule IV holds CITES-listed specimens; protected plants are in Schedule III.
xa: Schedule IV = CITES species was asked in **APPSC-GS 2024**.
**Sch. I** = highest protection; **Sch. II** = lesser protection.
Before 2022 there were **6** schedules, with **Sch. VI** for specified plants.

n3e31f6cadf7.s: Which of the following was listed in the former vermin Schedule V of the Wild Life (Protection) Act?
n3e31f6cadf7.x: The common crow was in the former vermin Schedule V; the mugger, rock eagle-owl and blackbuck are in Schedule I.
xa: A mugger crocodile was beaten on the **Tungabhadra** near **Kurnool** (5 Sep 2026).
A Schedule-I **rock eagle-owl** was rescued near **Dharmavaram** and released in **Nelakota RF**.
Other Schedule I species: **Asiatic lion, tiger, elephant, snow leopard, rhino, Gangetic dolphin, dugong, GIB**.

n87468b4ca54.s: In the T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad case, 'forest' was held to cover every area recorded as forest in government records:
o: only if owned by the government
n87468b4ca54.x: The Godavarman interpretation covers every area recorded as forest regardless of ownership, not just national parks.
xa: The case is from **1995**; the **2023 amendment** to the FCA narrows this reading.
Critics say the 2023 amendment takes **"deemed forests"** out of scope and dilutes **Godavarman**.
The amended Act covers only notified forest land or land recorded as forest **on or after 25 Oct 1980**.

ne04105b5d4c.s: The National Forest Policy, 1988 prescribes ____ forest or tree cover for hilly and mountainous regions.
ne04105b5d4c.x: The two-thirds target applies to hilly and mountainous regions; the national goal is 33% of the geographical area.
xa: NFP **1952** prescribed **60% in hills** and **25% in plains**.
NFP 1988 objectives include checking **soil erosion and desert spread** and a **massive people's movement involving women**.

n61c9e81a728.s: 'Wildlife' is defined in which section of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972?
n61c9e81a728.x: Section 2(37) defines wildlife, while Section 2(1) defines animal.
xa: The WPA has **66 sections** in **7 chapters**.
**Section 9** prohibits hunting of scheduled animals; **Section 39** makes wild animals **Government property**.
Its purpose is to protect **wild animals, birds and plants** and secure ecological security.

n334d319f4bb.s: Under the Forest Conservation Amendment Act, 2023, central approval is not required for certain strategic projects located within what distance of an international border?
n334d319f4bb.x: The amendment provides an exemption from central approval for strategic projects within 100 km of international borders, among other specified exemptions.
n334d319f4bb.tq: Use the distance figure as the decisive numerical clue.
xs: Strategic linear projects within **100 km** of the **IB, LoC or LAC** are exempt — option **(3)**.
**50**, **75** and **150 km** are not the limit in the amendment.
xa: Other exemptions: **eco-tourism facilities**, **zoos and safaris** under WPA, minor infrastructure.
Critics fear loss of **tribal land in border States**.
The Act was renamed **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980** w.e.f. **29 Dec 2023**.

nbde41d2978d.s: Under the original Section 2 of the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, de-reservation of a forest required prior approval of the:
nbde41d2978d.x: Section 2 required prior Central approval for de-reservation, non-forest use of forest land and clearing of trees.
xa: The Act came into force on **25 October 1980**.
**Compensatory afforestation**: **non-forest land of equal area**, else **twice the area of degraded forest land**, plus **NPV**.
The **NGT** can hear cases under **FCA 1980**, one of **7** laws.

nae6207725f5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 after the 2023 amendment?
o: It covers land notified as forest under the Indian Forest Act, 1927 or any other law
It covers land recorded as forest in government records on or after 25 October 1980
Its coverage was revised by the 2023 amendment
It covers land converted to non-forest use before 12 December 1996
nae6207725f5.x: Land converted to non-forest use before 12 December 1996 is excluded from the amended law's coverage.
xa: Renamed **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980** w.e.f. **29 Dec 2023**.
Exempt: strategic linear projects within **100 km** of the **IB, LoC or LAC**.
Compensatory afforestation: **equal area** of non-forest land, else **twice the area** of degraded forest land + **NPV**.

n5bec2d3b3cb.s: If equal-area non-forest land is unavailable for compensatory afforestation, degraded forest land of ____ the area is used.
n5bec2d3b3cb.x: Equal-area non-forest land is preferred; otherwise twice the area of degraded forest land is used, along with payment of NPV.
xa: Under the **Van (S.E.S.) Amendment Rules 2025**, CA and NPV do **not apply** to "forestry activities" on leased forest land.
The original **Sec. 2** needed **prior Central approval** for any non-forest use of forest land.
AP diverted **149.5687 ha** between **1 Apr and 31 Dec 2025** (AP SES 2025-26).

n7f97479d8f9.s: Under the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023, cultivated medicinal plants exempted from benefit-sharing must be certified by:
n7f97479d8f9.x: BMC-certified cultivated medicinal plants and registered AYUSH practitioners received benefit-sharing exemptions.
xa: Offences were turned into **civil penalties**.
**ABS Rules 2024**: NBA passes **85-90%** of proceeds to **SBBs**.
The **BD Act 2002** implements the **CBD**.

n8b7c0b9964a.s: India’s protected areas covered 1,75,169.42 square kilometres in the 2026 figures. This was stated to be equivalent to approximately:
n8b7c0b9964a.x: The protected areas covered 1,75,169.42 square kilometres, corresponding to 5.32% of India’s land area.
n8b7c0b9964a.tq: Link the absolute area figure with its reported percentage instead of treating them as separate facts.
xs: The **1,75,169.42 sq km** of protected areas equals **5.32%** of India's land area — option **(4)**.
India has **1,000+ protected areas**.
xa: SC bars mining within **1 km** of every NP and sanctuary unless a larger ESZ is notified.
AP diverted **27,641.252 ha** of forest under the Adhiniyam up to **31.12.2024**.

nc0d1638605a.s: The National Board for Wildlife (NBWL) is chaired by the:
nc0d1638605a.x: The PM chairs the NBWL; the Environment Minister chairs its Standing Committee and also the NTCA.
xa: The **State Board for Wildlife** is chaired by the **Chief Minister**.
The Standing Committee cleared **over 97%** of diversion proposals (**2014-2026**).
NBWL replaced the **Indian Board for Wildlife** via the **2002** amendment.

n3a6740d2b86.s: The State Board for Wildlife is chaired by the:
n3a6740d2b86.x: The State Board for Wildlife is chaired by the Chief Minister of the concerned State.
n3a6740d2b86.tq: Match the state-level body with the state political executive.
xs: The **State Board for Wildlife** is chaired by the **Chief Minister** — option **(2)**.
The **Prime Minister** chairs the **NBWL**; the **Union Environment Minister** chairs its Standing Committee and the NTCA.
xa: The **2022** amendment requires a **Chief Wildlife Warden** in every State.
⚠ **NBWL** = PM; **Standing Committee** = Environment Minister; **State Board** = Chief Minister.
The **Central Zoo Authority** is another WPA body.

ne51836daf26.s: The Animal Welfare Board of India was set up under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act in:
ne51836daf26.x: The PCA Act was enacted in 1960 and the AWBI was set up under it in 1962.
xa: The **Animal Welfare Board** is headquartered at **Ballabhgarh, Haryana**.
Forests became **Entry 17A** and protection of wild animals and birds **Entry 17B** of the Concurrent List.
The **PCA Act 1960** prevents cruelty to animals; the **WPA 1972** protects wild animals, birds and plants.

n87dcb32e4dc.s: A specified plant included in the protected-plant schedule cannot ordinarily be
o: cultivated in every circumstance without regulatory permission
observed or photographed in its natural habitat
picked, uprooted or traded without permission
n87dcb32e4dc.x: A specified plant cannot be picked, uprooted or traded without permission. The law regulates these activities rather than prohibiting observation or scientific description.
n87dcb32e4dc.tq: Apply the statutory restriction to the conduct described in the scenario.
xs: A specified plant cannot be **picked, uprooted or traded without permission** — option **(3)**.
The law regulates these acts; it does not bar observing, photographing or describing the plant.
xa: After 2022, protected plants are in **Schedule III**.
Before 2022, **Sch. VI** covered specified plants, with **cultivation and trade regulated**.
The WPA protects **wild animals, birds and plants**.

n1e79504a70f.s: Which of the following is NOT an Indian environmental law?
n1e79504a70f.x: There is no Nature (Protection) Act, 2000; the other three are recognised environmental statutes.
xa: Others in the framework: **PCA Act 1960** and **BD Act 2002**.
The **WPA** protects wild animals, birds and plants (**APPSC 2025** key).
The **NGT** cannot hear **WPA 1972** cases.

n60f4ecbdb90.s: The 2026 Maharashtra amendment proposal relating to leopards sought to permit relocation and also proposed moving the leopard from:
n60f4ecbdb90.x: The proposal sought to enable relocation of leopards under Section 12 and move them from Schedule I to Schedule II. Environmentalists described the proposed down-listing as regressive.
n60f4ecbdb90.tq: Watch the direction of the schedule change; the trap reverses the two schedules.
xs: The proposal would move the leopard from **Schedule I to Schedule II** — option **(4)**.
Environmentalists called this down-listing **"regressive"** (**15 Mar 2026**).
There is no **Schedule V or VI** after **2022**; only four schedules remain.
xa: After 2022: **Sch. I** highest protection; **Sch. II** lesser protection.
The Bill amends **Sec. 12** and needs **President's assent**.
The **Indian flying fox** went from vermin (**Schedule V**) to **Schedule II**.

n5acf2429a16.s: The Miyawaki method is primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Dense, multi-layered mini-forests of native species in urban areas
Conversion of agricultural land into pasture
Seed storage in inaccessible forest areas
n5acf2429a16.x: The Miyawaki method creates dense, multi-layered mini-forests using native species, particularly in urban areas.
n5acf2429a16.tq: Identify the defining application of the method rather than its associated criticism.
xs: The **Miyawaki method** makes **dense, multi-layered mini-forests of native species in urban areas** — option **(1)**.
It is named after **Akira Miyawaki**, a **Japanese botanist** (**UPSC 2022** key).
Seed storage on inaccessible land relates to **seed balls**; single-species plantations are the monocultures social forestry is criticised for.
xa: **Seed balls**: seeds packed in clay, compost and soil, used on **degraded or inaccessible land**.
**Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam** plans **1,000 micro-forests** by **March 2026**.
⚠ **Extension forestry** = roadside, canal and rail strips; **Miyawaki** = urban mini-forests.

n3d10f54888f.s: The term ‘social forestry’ was used by the National Commission on Agriculture in which year?
n3d10f54888f.x: The National Commission on Agriculture used the term ‘social forestry’ in 1976.
n3d10f54888f.tq: Distinguish the closely placed institutional and programme years.
xs: The **National Commission on Agriculture** used the term "social forestry" in **1976** — option **(2)**.
**1971** is near the **Arabari** JFM experiment (**1971-72**), **1988** is the NFP and **1990** the JFM guidelines.
xa: Components: **farm forestry**, **community forestry**, **extension forestry** and **agroforestry**.
Criticism: it drifted into **commercial monocultures**; fix is **mixed native species**.
India adopted the first **National Agroforestry Policy** in **Feb 2014**.

ne120b59e359.s: A major criticism of the implementation of social forestry is that it drifted towards:
o: Mixed native forests under community control
ne120b59e359.x: Social forestry has been criticised for drifting into commercial monocultures. The suggested corrective approach is the use of mixed native species.
ne120b59e359.tq: Test the criticism and its precise policy concern rather than the proposed remedy.
xs: Social forestry drifted into **commercial monocultures** — option **(2)**.
The suggested fix is a shift to **mixed native species**.
Urban multi-layered mini-forests are the **Miyawaki method**, not a criticism.
xa: The term came from the **National Commission on Agriculture (1976)**.
CAMPA money is similarly criticised for **exotic plantations on native grasslands**.
**Extension forestry** covers roadside, canal and rail strips.

n9563b3e6d3e.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated use of CAMPA funds?
o: Relocation of villages from protected areas
n9563b3e6d3e.x: CAMPA funds support regeneration, wildlife management, catchment treatment, relocation from protected areas, human-wildlife conflict management and forest-fire prevention; private urban housing is not a stated use.
xa: Other uses: **wildlife management**, **catchment treatment**, **relocating villages** out of PAs.
Tracking: **e-Green Watch** portal.
Criticism: CAMPA money funds **exotic plantations on native grasslands**.

nenvironment-28-1.s: Growing trees together with crops or livestock on the same land is called:
nenvironment-28-1.x: Agroforestry integrates trees with crops or livestock; reforestation replants old forest land and social forestry plants trees for community needs.
n: Agroforestry is the integration of trees with agricultural systems. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #28 · pp 50-52]
xa: India was the **first country** with an agroforestry policy — **National Agroforestry Policy 2014**.
**GROW report (NITI Aayog)**: ~**8.65%** of India's area under agroforestry.
**ICAR-CAFRI** is at **Jhansi, UP**.

nfb1ab169ff6.s: Joint Forest Management traces its origin to the Arabari experiment (1971-72) in:
nfb1ab169ff6.x: JFM began with the Arabari experiment in West Bengal; its guidelines came on 1 June 1990.
xa: The **National Afforestation Programme** runs through village-level **JFMCs**.
The **Green India Mission** also works through **JFMCs**, VFCs and SHGs under **Gram Sabha** oversight.
⚠ **Arabari** (**1971-72**) = JFM origin; **1990** = JFM guidelines; **2014** = agroforestry policy.

nd1813f31fe1.s: The Green India Mission is one of the missions under the:
o: National Action Plan on Climate Change
nd1813f31fe1.x: The Green India Mission is an NAPCC mission, implemented through JFMCs and partly funded by National CAMPA.
xa: It also works through VFCs and SHGs under **Gram Sabha** oversight.
Convergence with **CAMPA and MGNREGS** (now **VB-G RAM G**) never happened, per the CAG.

nee63c4a808f.s: India became the first country to adopt a National Agroforestry Policy in:
nee63c4a808f.x: India adopted the National Agroforestry Policy in February 2014 and was the first country to do so.
nee63c4a808f.tq: Distinguish the exact month and year from nearby policy dates.
xs: India adopted the **National Agroforestry Policy** in **February 2014**, the **first country** to do so — option **(2)**.
The policy covers **agroforestry**: trees + crops + livestock on the same land.
xa: **ICAR-CAFRI** is at **Jhansi, UP**.
Agroforestry is funded via **SMAF** under **PM-RKVY**.
⚠ **Arabari** (**1971-72**) = JFM origin; **1990** = JFM guidelines; **2014** = agroforestry policy.

nf4023fe1821.s: The National Afforestation Programme is implemented through which village-level institutions?
nf4023fe1821.x: The National Afforestation Programme runs through village-level Joint Forest Management Committees.
nf4023fe1821.tq: Identify the implementing institution at the correct administrative level.
xs: The **National Afforestation Programme** runs through village-level **Joint Forest Management Committees** — option **(2)**.
**VSS** are used for capacity-building camps in AP, and **FDAs** are federated by AP's State Forest Development Agency — neither is the NAP's village body.
xa: JFM began with the **Arabari experiment** (**1971-72**); guidelines on **1 June 1990**.
The **Green India Mission** is also implemented via **JFMCs**.
In AP, the State FDA federates **22 FDAs** and runs **NAP, GIM and NMPB** schemes.

n5a3564ed301.s: Which of the following correctly describes the role of the State Forest Development Agency in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It federates 22 Forest Development Agencies and runs NAP, GIM and NMPB schemes.
It issues Forest Rights Act titles in all ITDA areas.
It federates 22 Joint Forest Management Committees and runs only the Miyawaki programme.
It administers only compensatory afforestation under the Green Credit Programme.
n5a3564ed301.x: In Andhra Pradesh, the State Forest Development Agency federates 22 Forest Development Agencies and runs the NAP, GIM and NMPB schemes.
n5a3564ed301.tq: Test the federation count together with the agency’s programme responsibilities.
xs: AP's State Forest Development Agency **federates 22 Forest Development Agencies** and runs **NAP, GIM and NMPB** schemes — option **(1)**.
It federates **FDAs**, not JFMCs; it does not issue **FRA titles**.
xa: Capacity-building camps are held through **Vana Samrakshana Samithis (VSS)**.
AP schemes: **Great Green Wall of AP**, **Namo Van - Nagar Van**, **School Nursery Scheme**.
**AP CAMPA** prepares an **Annual Plan of Operations** every year.

n8ce112b50a2.s: The National CAMPA, which sets policy under the CAF Act, 2016, is headed by the:
n8ce112b50a2.x: The National CAMPA, headed by the Union Environment Minister, sets policy; State CAMPAs do the field work.
xa: The funds are **non-lapsable**, interest-bearing public accounts.
Tracking portal: **e-Green Watch**.
The fund held **over ₹66,000 crore** by **2024**, but only **30-35%** was used.
⚠ "People's participation is mandatory" under the **2016** Act is **wrong** (UPSC **2019**).

n9ac11f38e67.s: Before a project starts, the agency diverting forest land must pay:
o: Only the Net Present Value of the lost forest
Only the cost of compensatory afforestation
Both the cost of compensatory afforestation and the Net Present Value
Neither, if non-forest land is provided
n9ac11f38e67.x: The agency pays both the CA cost and the NPV of the lost forest ecosystem before the project starts.
xa: Exception: Central PSUs or projects with no non-forest land may use **twice the area** of degraded forest land.
**FC Rules 2022** introduced **Accredited Compensatory Afforestation** (effectively **land banks**).
**Green Credit** afforestation can be exchanged for CA under the **Van (S.E.S.) Rules 2023**.

nfbfe62438f4.s: Central PSUs, or projects with no non-forest land available, may undertake compensatory afforestation on:
o: Half the area of degraded forest land
Twice the area of degraded forest land
Equal area of degraded forest land
nfbfe62438f4.x: Central PSUs and projects lacking non-forest land may use twice the area of degraded forest land for compensatory afforestation.
xa: CA + **NPV** must be paid **before** the project starts.
**Green Credit** afforestation can be exchanged for CA under the **Van (S.E.S.) Rules 2023**.
⚠ **90 : 10** = State : National CAMPA funds.

n38178b4f9aa.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about compensatory afforestation (CA)?
o: The Forest (Conservation) Rules, 2022 introduced Accredited Compensatory Afforestation
Under Accredited CA, developers may only use plantations raised after the forest land is diverted
Accredited CA plantations raised in advance work as land banks
Green Credit Programme afforestation can be exchanged for CA under the Van (S.E.S.) Rules, 2023
