n38178b4f9aa.x: Accredited CA lets developers use plantations raised in advance, not only after diversion.
xa: Green Credit-CA guidelines were issued on **16 Sep 2025**.
FC Rules 2022 also **dropped** the forest-dwellers' **consent** clause.
⚠ **FC Rules 2022** = land banks + dropped consent; **Van (S.E.S.) Rules 2023** = Green Credit swap.

nf499820b7d6.s: Under the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016, the National and State funds are:
o: Non-lapsable accounts that earn no interest
Lapsable accounts that earn no interest
nf499820b7d6.x: The Act created National and State funds as non-lapsable public accounts that earn interest.
xa: Split: **90%** to State funds, **10%** to the National fund.
The fund held **over ₹66,000 crore** by **2024**, but only **30-35%** was used.
Progress is tracked on the **e-Green Watch** portal.

n31dd2db0f23.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016?
o: CAMPA exists at both the national and state levels
By 2024 the fund held over Rs 66,000 crore
Only about 30-35% of the fund had been used by 2024
People's participation in compensatory afforestation is mandatory under the Act
n31dd2db0f23.x: The 2016 Act does not make people's participation mandatory.
xa: The funds are **non-lapsable**, **interest-bearing** public accounts.
National CAMPA is headed by the **Union Environment Minister**.

n99479541e6b.s: Which change in the Forest (Conservation) Rules, 2022 was disputed by the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes in its interaction with the MoEFCC?
o: Dropping the clause requiring forest-dwellers’ consent before diversion
n99479541e6b.x: The 2022 Rules dropped the clause requiring the consent of forest-dwellers before diversion, and the NCST disputed this with the MoEFCC.
n99479541e6b.tq: Identify the precise legal change rather than the surrounding forest programmes.
xs: The **NCST** disputed **dropping the clause requiring forest-dwellers' consent before diversion** — option **(2)**.
**JFMCs** date back to JFM (guidelines **1990**), and the **Miyawaki method** is an urban planting technique — neither is in the 2022 Rules.
xa: The same Rules introduced **Accredited Compensatory Afforestation** (land banks).
The **Koya and Kondh** oppose **Polavaram** over land rights and rehabilitation.
Suggested fix: **FRA community titles** to pastoralists.

nd35be6f9cb9.s: The Nagar Van Yojana is run by the:
nd35be6f9cb9.x: The National Afforestation and Eco-development Board (NAEB) runs the Nagar Van Yojana.
nd35be6f9cb9.tq: Identify the correct implementing body rather than the research institution.
xs: The **Nagar Van Yojana** is run by the **National Afforestation and Eco-development Board (NAEB)** — option **(3)**.
**CAFRI** is an agroforestry research institute at **Jhansi**; the **NBA** deals with biodiversity.
xa: Target: **600 Nagar Vans and 400 Nagar Vatikas** (**2020-21 to 2026-27**).
Funding: **National CAMPA**.
Progress: **620 projects** in **28** States and **3** UTs, costing **₹654.30 crore**.

nce12e8cb037.s: The Nagar Van Yojana targets, between 2020–21 and 2026–27:
nce12e8cb037.x: The scheme targets 600 Nagar Vans and 400 Nagar Vatikas during 2020–21 to 2026–27.
nce12e8cb037.tq: Split the paired targets carefully; the figures are deliberately reversible.
xs: NVY targets **600 Nagar Vans and 400 Nagar Vatikas** — option **(2)**.
Some older notes give "**200** urban forests" — not the current target.
xa: Run by **NAEB**, funded by **National CAMPA**.
**620 projects** sanctioned; first instalment **₹458.53 crore** released.
AP runs **Namo Van - Nagar Van**.

n9a3bcd525b8.s: NITI Aayog's GROW report estimated what share of India's geographical area to be under agroforestry?
n9a3bcd525b8.x: The GROW (Greening and Restoration of Wasteland with Agroforestry) report put agroforestry at about 8.65% of India's area.
xa: **ICAR-CAFRI** is located at **Jhansi, UP**.
India's **National Agroforestry Policy** came in **Feb 2014**.

n98a0568f9b3.s: The Koya and Kondh communities oppose the Polavaram project mainly over:
n98a0568f9b3.x: The Koya and Kondh communities oppose Polavaram over land rights and rehabilitation concerns.
xa: **FC Rules 2022** dropped the forest-dwellers' **consent** clause, disputed by the **NCST**.
Suggested fix: give **FRA community titles** to pastoralists.
AP's **Red Sanders Protection Scheme** spans **Seshachalam, Veligonda, Lankamala, Nallamala and Talakona**.

n56348eb4d19.s: The revised 2021–30 framework of the Green India Mission targets:
o: Aravallis, Western Ghats, Himalayas and mangroves
n56348eb4d19.x: The revised framework targets all four: the Aravallis, Western Ghats, Himalayas and mangroves.
xa: GIM is one of the **NAPCC** missions.
A **CAG audit** found forest quality improved on only **0.11 million ha** vs **1.4 million ha** target.
It is funded partly from **National CAMPA**.

n51695606e2a.s: The Sub-Mission on Agroforestry (SMAF) is implemented under:
n51695606e2a.x: Agroforestry receives support through the Sub-Mission on Agroforestry under PM-RKVY.
n51695606e2a.tq: Separate the funding programme from related forestry schemes.
xs: **SMAF** is implemented under **PM-RKVY** — option **(3)**.
**Nagar Van Yojana** is run by **NAEB**, and the **GIM** is an **NAPCC** mission.
xa: The **National Agroforestry Policy** came in **Feb 2014**.
**ICAR-CAFRI** (**Jhansi**) is the agroforestry research institute.
**TOFI** is a **MoEFCC-USAID** programme.

n11ca9b6e704.s: A CAG audit of the Green India Mission found forest quality improved on only 0.11 million ha against a target of:
n11ca9b6e704.x: The audit found improvement on only 0.11 million hectares against a target of 1.4 million hectares.
xa: Forest-cover expansion reached about **4%**.
Convergence with **CAMPA and MGNREGS** (now **VB-G RAM G**) never happened.
GIM is one of the **NAPCC** missions.

n41d55cc9b4d.s: With respect to radiation, the atmosphere is largely:
o: Opaque to incoming short-wave radiation but transparent to outgoing long-wave radiation
Transparent to both incoming and outgoing radiation
Transparent to incoming short-wave radiation but relatively opaque to outgoing long-wave radiation
Opaque to both incoming and outgoing radiation
n41d55cc9b4d.x: The atmosphere lets much incoming short-wave solar radiation through but absorbs outgoing long-wave terrestrial infrared radiation through greenhouse gases.
xa: The surface re-emits **infrared at 8,000-25,000 nm**; CO2 and water vapour absorb strongly at **14,000-25,000 nm**.
GHGs re-radiate **in all directions**, partly back to the surface.
⚠ Transparent to **short-wave** in; opaque to **long-wave infrared** out.

nenvironment-7-6.s: Without the greenhouse effect, Earth's average temperature would be approximately:
nenvironment-7-6.x: Without the greenhouse effect Earth would average about −18°C instead of about +15°C.
n: The greenhouse effect is natural warming caused by the absorption and re-radiation of heat by greenhouse gases. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
Without the greenhouse effect, Earth’s average temperature would be approximately −18°C. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
xa: The concept was proposed by **Joseph Fourier** in the **1820s**.
The surface re-emits **infrared at 8,000-25,000 nm**.
The **enhanced** greenhouse effect comes from **human activities** raising GHG levels.

nenvironment-33-5.s: The concept of the greenhouse effect is associated with whom and with which period?
nenvironment-33-5.x: Joseph Fourier described the greenhouse effect in the 1820s. The WMO is a modern body that reports greenhouse gas levels.
nenvironment-33-5.tq: Recall who first described the greenhouse effect.
n: Joseph Fourier is associated with the greenhouse effect concept. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
The greenhouse effect concept dates to the 1820s. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
xs: The greenhouse-effect concept was proposed by **Joseph Fourier** in the **1820s** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **WMO** is a later body; options pairing it or the **1920s** with the concept are wrong.
The greenhouse effect is **natural warming** from the **absorption and re-radiation** of heat by GHGs.
xa: Without it, Earth would average about **−18°C** instead of about **+15°C**.
The atmosphere is **transparent** to incoming **short-wave** radiation and **opaque** to outgoing **long-wave infrared**.
The **primary cause of global warming** is the **increase in GHGs** (APPSC **2025**).

n049a0321815.s: Which gas has a 100-year Global Warming Potential of 1 and serves as the reference gas?
n049a0321815.x: CO2 is assigned a GWP of 1; sulphur hexafluoride (about 23,900) has the highest of these.
xa: GWP is usually measured over **100 years**.
Old IPCC values: CH4 **21**, N2O **310** — superseded.

ne673b8e096c.s: Methane, with a 100-year GWP of about 28–36, has an atmospheric lifetime of approximately:
ne673b8e096c.x: Methane has a 100-year GWP of about 28–36 and a lifetime of about 12 years.
xa: Water vapour's GWP is **variable**; lifetime **~9 days**.
**India's irrigated paddy** emits **3.9 million t methane/yr**.
The **Global Methane Pledge** targets **30%** cut from **2020** levels by **2030**.

na88dc73b499.s: The UN Secretary-General's Call to Action on Methane (June 2026) was launched at:
na88dc73b499.x: It was launched at London Climate Action Week on 24 June 2026, covering waste, agriculture and fossil-fuel operations.
xa: The **Global Methane Pledge** targets a **30%** cut from **2020** levels by **2030**.
**India has not signed** the Pledge.
Methane supplies about **16%** of long-lived GHG forcing.

n825118e3793.s: Which one of the following is the largest contributor to greenhouse-gas emissions among the sources listed below?
o: Fossil-fuel combustion for energy, transport and industry
n825118e3793.x: Fossil-fuel combustion involving coal, oil and gas for energy, transport and industry is the largest contributor. Other important sources include deforestation, industrial processes, agriculture and waste.
n825118e3793.tq: Identify the dominant sector and distinguish it from other recognised sources.
xs: **Fossil-fuel combustion** (coal, oil, gas for energy, transport and industry) is the largest contributor — option **(3)**.
Others: deforestation/land use, **cement**, agriculture, waste.
xa: Top CO2 emitters (**2024**): **China 12**, **USA 4.9**, **India 3.2** billion tonnes.
**425 "carbon bombs"** found by **LINGO** would use up the 1.5°C budget **twice over**.
India's carbon bombs: **Gevra** (Chhattisgarh) and **Rajmahal** (Jharkhand) coal mines.

n122a103624b.s: The European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) was fully enforced from 1 January:
n122a103624b.x: The EU's CBAM was fully enforced from 1 January 2026.
xa: The USA **repealed** the **2009 "endangerment finding"** on six GHGs.
India's **social cost of carbon** is **$86 per tonne** — highest globally.

nenvironment-33-4.s: Which of the following causes acid rain but is not a greenhouse gas?
nenvironment-33-4.x: SO2 causes acid rain but is not a greenhouse gas; CFCs are both greenhouse gases and ozone-depleting.
n: Water vapour is the most abundant natural greenhouse gas. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
Carbon dioxide has a 66% share according to the WMO source. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
CFCs are ozone-depleting substances and greenhouse gases. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
Sulfur dioxide (SO₂) is an acid-rain gas and not a greenhouse gas. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
xa: Anthropogenic / synthetic GHGs: **CFCs**, **HFCs**, **PFCs**, **SF₆**.
Textbook share of enhanced effect: **CO2 60% > CH4 20% > CFCs 15% > N2O 5%**.

n086c85abc0f.s: The approximate share of methane in the enhanced greenhouse effect is:
n086c85abc0f.x: The textbook shares are CO2 about 60%, methane 20%, CFCs 15% and nitrous oxide 5%.
xa: **CO2** contributes most to the **enhanced** effect (**APPSC 2025** key).
**WMO Bulletin**: CO2 accounted for about **81%** of the **54%** rise in warming effect, **1990-2024**.
**CH4** supplies about **16%** of radiative forcing from long-lived GHGs.

n267d794b11e.s: Deforestation generally ____ the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.
n267d794b11e.x: Deforestation reduces carbon uptake and may release stored carbon, raising atmospheric CO2.
xa: The same trap appeared in **APPSC 2025** and **APPSC-G2 2025**.
**CO2** sources: fossil fuels, **deforestation**, cement.
**Carbon sequestration** stores carbon in sinks: soil carbon, biochar, agroforestry, forests.

nenvironment-33-10.s: Which of the following greenhouse gases does not occur naturally and is entirely man-made?
nenvironment-33-10.x: CFCs are synthetic chemicals made for refrigerants and aerosols, so they are entirely man-made greenhouse gases. Water vapour, methane and nitrous oxide all occur naturally, though human activity adds to them.
nenvironment-33-10.tq: Pick the gas that exists only because industry makes it.
n: Nitrogen oxide is not a naturally occurring greenhouse gas in the cited PYQ. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 57-59]
xs: **CFCs** are **entirely man-made** (**synthetic**) greenhouse gases — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Water vapour**, **methane** and **nitrous oxide** are **natural** GHGs.
⚠ Other notes say nitrous oxide is **both natural and man-made**.
xa: Other synthetic GHGs: **HFCs**, **PFCs**, **SF₆**.
CFCs come from **coolants/refrigeration**, foams and **aerosol sprays**.
**Perfluoromethane** comes from **aluminium production**.

n08776b19c39.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Global Warming Potential (GWP)?
o: The amount of solar radiation reflected by a gas in comparison with water vapour
The atmospheric concentration of a gas compared with that of oxygen over one year
The heat absorbed by a gas over a specified period, usually 100 years, relative to the same mass of carbon dioxide
The time required by a gas to disappear completely from the atmosphere
n08776b19c39.x: GWP compares the heat absorbed over a specified period, generally 100 years, by a given mass of a greenhouse gas with that absorbed by the same mass of CO2.
n08776b19c39.tq: Discriminate between GWP, atmospheric lifetime and concentration.
xs: **GWP** = heat a gas absorbs over a period, usually **100 years**, **relative to the same mass of CO2** — option **(3)**.
It is not reflection, concentration or lifetime — lifetime is a separate column (e.g. **CH4 ~12 years**).
xa: Older values CH4 **21** and N2O **310** are superseded.

n4de5c3ac9aa.s: Tipping points in the climate system are best understood as:
o: Thresholds beyond which small changes may trigger self-perpetuating shifts that cannot be reversed on human timescales
Fixed temperature values that apply equally to every ecosystem
Linear changes that can always be reversed immediately
Short-term daily variations in weather with no long-term effects
n4de5c3ac9aa.x: Tipping points are thresholds at which small changes can initiate self-perpetuating, non-linear shifts that are not reversible on human timescales.
n4de5c3ac9aa.tq: Distinguish threshold-driven non-linear change from ordinary gradual variation.
xs: **Tipping points** are thresholds where small changes trigger **self-perpetuating shifts that cannot be reversed on human timescales** — option **(1)**.
They are **non-linear**, so options (2)-(4) are wrong.
xa: Example: beyond about **2°C**, parts of the **Amazon** could turn into savanna → a carbon source.
Source: **UNSG Scientific Advisory Board Brief #12**.
India sought clarity at the **Bonn talks** on using tipping points for policy.

nbbc9b780bae.s: The Keeling curve refers to the continuous record of atmospheric carbon dioxide measured at:
o: Mauna Loa, Hawaii, maintained since 1958 by Charles David Keeling
Barrow, Alaska, maintained by the IPCC
Vostok, Antarctica, maintained since 1979 by the WMO
nbbc9b780bae.x: The Keeling curve is the continuous atmospheric CO2 record from Mauna Loa, Hawaii, begun in 1958 by Charles David Keeling.
nbbc9b780bae.tq: Combine the place, starting year and scientist to avoid location and agency swaps.
xs: The **Keeling curve** is the CO2 record at **Mauna Loa, Hawaii**, since **1958**, by **Charles David Keeling** — option **(1)**.
Greenland, Barrow and Vostok are not the Keeling site.
xa: **Ice cores** give past CO2 and temperature from trapped air bubbles.
CO2 reached **423.9 ppm** in **2024**.
⚠ **Keeling curve** = **Mauna Loa** (**1958**); **climate sensitivity** = doubling of CO2.

nd433236ede9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the greenhouse effect?
o: The natural greenhouse effect occurs without human intervention
The natural greenhouse effect helps keep Earth habitable
The enhanced greenhouse effect results when human activities raise greenhouse-gas concentrations
In the natural greenhouse effect, gas levels rise sharply because of fossil-fuel burning
nd433236ede9.x: Natural greenhouse-gas levels stayed stable for thousands of years; fossil fuels drive the enhanced effect, not the natural one.
xa: Without the greenhouse effect, Earth would average about **-18°C** instead of **+15°C**.
**APPSC 2025** key: the primary cause of global warming is an **increase in GHGs**.

nc1cb71fcd85.s: The most important greenhouse gas is:
nc1cb71fcd85.x: Water vapour is the most important greenhouse gas; humans raise it mainly indirectly by warming the air.
xa: **Water vapour feedback**: warmer air holds more water vapour and traps more heat.
Its atmospheric lifetime is about **9 days**.
⚠ Natural effect: **water vapour** biggest; enhanced effect: **CO2** biggest.

na8afdcb8fbf.s: Climate sensitivity is the warming that follows ____ of atmospheric CO2 over the pre-industrial level.
na8afdcb8fbf.x: Climate sensitivity refers to the warming after a doubling of CO2, not a 50% rise.
xa: **Albedo feedback**: melting ice lowers albedo → more heat absorbed.
**Keeling curve**: CO2 record at **Mauna Loa, Hawaii**, since **1958**.
**Tipping points**: thresholds triggering **self-perpetuating shifts** that cannot be reversed.

n0d16ab65f05.s: Which of the following is NOT correct according to the WMO Greenhouse Gas Bulletin (October 2025)?
o: Methane supplies about 16% of radiative forcing from long-lived greenhouse gases
The warming effect of long-lived greenhouse gases rose by 54% during 1990-2024
Carbon dioxide accounted for about 81% of that rise
Methane accounted for most of the rise in warming effect during 1990-2024
n0d16ab65f05.x: CO2, not methane, drove most (about 81%) of the 54% rise.
xa: CH4 is at **266%** of pre-industrial; CO2 **152%**; N2O **125%**.

n76011ffa96c.s: Tropospheric ozone, formed from NOx and VOCs in sunlight, is a:
n76011ffa96c.x: Tropospheric ozone is a secondary pollutant; it is a short-lived greenhouse gas that cuts crop yields.
xa: SLCPs: **black carbon**, **methane**, **HFCs**, **tropospheric ozone** — tackled by the **Climate and Clean Air Coalition**.
**Black carbon** comes from **incomplete combustion** and **darkens snow and ice**.
Methane lifetime is **~12 years**.

nd2947759aa8.s: Black carbon, which darkens snow and ice, is produced by incomplete combustion of:
nd2947759aa8.x: Black carbon comes from incomplete combustion of both biomass and diesel, not exclusively fossil fuels.
xa: Lifetime: **days to weeks**.
It is one of the **SLCPs**, with methane, HFCs and tropospheric ozone.

na2be9ae4259.s: India's reported carbon dioxide emissions in 2024 were about:
na2be9ae4259.x: India emitted about 3.2 billion tonnes, against 12 billion for China and 4.9 billion for the USA.
xa: India's **social cost of carbon** is the **highest globally**, **$86 per tonne** of CO2.
The **GHG Emission Intensity Target (Amendment) Rules 2025** cover **208 units**.

n160306665ce.s: The atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration in 2024 was about:
n160306665ce.x: CO2 reached about 423.9 ppm in 2024, the highest in about two million years; pre-industrial was around 280 ppm.
xa: The **3.5 ppm** rise was the **largest annual rise since 1957**.
CO2 is **152%** of pre-industrial.
Earlier notes give **419 ppm**.

n4180aa82ecf.s: In 2024, atmospheric CO2 rose by ____, the largest annual rise since 1957.
n4180aa82ecf.x: CO2 rose 3.5 ppm to 423.9 ppm in 2024, the biggest rise since 1957.
xa: CO2 stood at **423.9 ppm**.
CH4 supplies about **16%** of long-lived GHG forcing.

n4e47661aff2.s: During 1971–2010, the oceans absorbed roughly what share of the extra energy from warming?
n4e47661aff2.x: The oceans took up more than 90% of the extra energy during 1971–2010.
xa: Oceans absorb CO2 → **carbonic acid** (ocean acidification).
**Coral bleaching** is driven by warming; recovery takes **15+ years**.
**Arctic sea ice** shrank **3.5-4.1% per decade** (**1979-2012**).

n012797706a4.s: During 1979–2012, Arctic sea ice shrank by approximately:
n012797706a4.x: Arctic sea ice declined by about 3.5–4.1% per decade during 1979–2012, while both ice sheets are losing mass.
xa: The collapse: **GHGs + ozone hole** strengthened the westerlies, lifting warm **Circumpolar Deep Water**.
Oceans took up **over 90%** of extra energy (**1971-2010**).
**Albedo feedback**: melting ice lowers albedo → more heat absorbed.

nfd15b9c6ce1.s: Ocean acidification is primarily caused by which of the following processes?
o: Evaporation of seawater and formation of sulphuric acid
Absorption of atmospheric CO2 by oceans and formation of carbonic acid
Freezing of seawater and release of hydrochloric acid
Absorption of atmospheric oxygen and formation of nitric acid
nfd15b9c6ce1.x: When oceans absorb carbon dioxide, carbonic acid forms, lowering ocean pH and causing acidification.
nfd15b9c6ce1.tq: Link the environmental effect with the specific chemical process responsible.
xs: Ocean acidification = oceans **absorb CO2** and form **carbonic acid** — option **(2)**.
It is not sulphuric, hydrochloric or nitric acid.
xa: **Coral bleaching** is driven by warming; recovery takes **15+ years**.
CO2 reached **423.9 ppm** in **2024**.
Oceans took up **over 90%** of the extra energy (**1971-2010**).

nf62b3eeb36d.s: Which year marked the first occasion on which the global mean temperature exceeded 1.5°C above the pre-industrial level?
nf62b3eeb36d.x: The year 2024 was reported as the first year in which the global mean temperature exceeded 1.5°C above the pre-industrial level.
nf62b3eeb36d.tq: Distinguish the specific record year from nearby climate-policy years.
xs: **2024** was the **first calendar year above 1.5°C** (WMO) — option **(3)**.
Average warming is about **1.3°C** above pre-industrial (UNSG brief, **24 Jun 2026**).
xa: The world is now described as a **1.5°C world**; a strong **El Niño** is expected in **2027**.
Each of the last three decades was warmer than any since **1850**.
CO2 rose **3.5 ppm** in **2024**, the **largest since 1957**.

nf38084860f5.s: A 'carbon bomb' is a fossil-fuel project capable of emitting over:
nf38084860f5.x: A carbon bomb can emit over 1 Gt CO2; LINGO has identified 425 of them.
xa: India's: **Gevra** (Chhattisgarh) and **Rajmahal** (Jharkhand) coal mines.
⚠ **CCUS** = point sources; **direct air capture** = ambient air.

ned59f36f76b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Carbon footprint is expressed in tonnes of CO2 per year
Carbon sequestration stores carbon in sinks such as soil, biochar, agroforestry and forests
Pulling CO2 straight from ambient air is direct air capture
CCUS refers to machines that pull CO2 straight from ambient air
ned59f36f76b.x: CCUS captures CO2 from factory flue gases (point sources); pulling CO2 from ambient air is direct air capture.
xa: ⚠ **CCUS** = point sources; **direct air capture** = ambient air.
India's **CCUS road map** covers **industry only**.

n1de8c3a9a11.s: The Global Methane Pledge, launched at COP26 in Glasgow, aims to cut methane emissions by 30% from 2020 levels by:
n1de8c3a9a11.x: The Pledge targets a 30% cut from 2020 levels by 2030; India has not signed it.
xa: India's irrigated paddy emits **3.9 million t methane/yr** — a little more than Germany's total.
The UNSG's **Call to Action on Methane** came at **London Climate Action Week** (**2026**).

nf42520da4bf.s: The UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 assessed that updated nationally determined contributions would lead approximately to warming of:
nf42520da4bf.x: The UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 projected approximately 2.3–2.5°C of warming even with updated NDCs.
nf42520da4bf.tq: Test the projected range and distinguish it from the Paris temperature goals.
xs: Even updated NDCs lead to **2.3-2.5°C** — option **(4)**.
The report is the **UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 ("Off Target")**.
xa: **UNEP Limiting Overshoot (Sep 2026)**: **1.8°C** if every pledge delivered vs **2.6°C** on current policies.
Path: **"overshoot, peak and decline"** back below **1.5°C** by **2100**.
**2024** was already the first year above **1.5°C**.

n18973101a0b.s: According to UNEP's Limiting Overshoot assessment, projected warming under current policies is:
n18973101a0b.x: The assessment projects 2.6°C under current policies and 1.8°C if every pledge is delivered.
xa: It sets an **"overshoot, peak and decline"** path back below **1.5°C** by **2100**.
The **Emissions Gap Report 2025** projects **2.3-2.5°C** even with updated NDCs.

n3afb8c776be.s: India's CCUS road map primarily covers:
o: Industry, while agricultural removal is associated with soil carbon, biochar and agroforestry
Only household cooking, while agriculture and industry are excluded
Only direct air capture facilities in urban areas
n3afb8c776be.x: India’s CCUS road map covers industry. Agricultural carbon removal is associated with measures such as soil carbon management, biochar and agroforestry.
n3afb8c776be.tq: Identify the correct sectoral allocation and reject the reversed scope.
xs: India's CCUS road map covers **industry**; agricultural removal fits **soil carbon, biochar and agroforestry** — option **(2)**.
Agriculture is left out because farm emissions are **diffuse**.
xa: Farm removals fall under **Carbon Dioxide Removal**.
**CCUS** captures CO2 from **factory flue gases** (point sources only).
**Direct air capture** machines pull CO2 from ambient air.
n3afb8c776be.fixed: odd stem wording ('as described in the context of sectoral application')

n90241a31f60.s: India's country-level social cost of carbon is reported to be:
n90241a31f60.x: India's country-level social cost of carbon is reported as $86 per tonne of CO2, the highest globally.
n90241a31f60.tq: For numerical options, distinguish the exact reported figure from nearby values.
xs: India's **social cost of carbon** is **$86 per tonne of CO2** — option **(2)**.
It is the **highest globally** at country level.
xa: India is the **3rd** largest emitter at **3.2** billion tonnes (**2024**).
India's carbon bombs: **Gevra** and **Rajmahal** coal mines.

n89b45f3cb87.s: Which one of the following is the primary cause of the present global warming?
o: Increase in the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere
Depletion of the stratospheric ozone layer
Increase in the amount of incoming solar radiation
Rise in the proportion of nitrogen and oxygen in the air
n89b45f3cb87.x: The primary cause of global warming is the increase in greenhouse gases (APPSC 2025 key): heat from sunlight re-radiated by the Earth is absorbed by CO2 and other gases. Ozone depletion is a separate problem; the warming is not explained by more incoming sunlight; and nitrogen and oxygen are not greenhouse gases.
n89b45f3cb87.tq: Global warming = more GHGs trapping re-radiated infrared.
xs: The primary cause is an **increase in the concentration of greenhouse gases** — option **(1)** (**APPSC 2025** key).
**N2, O2 and Ar are not GHGs**, so a rise in nitrogen and oxygen cannot warm the planet.
Heat re-radiated by the earth is absorbed by **CO2** and other gases (**APPSC GS 2021**).
xa: In the enhanced effect, **CO2** contributes most (**APPSC 2025** key).
**2024** was the **first calendar year above 1.5°C** (WMO).
CO2 reached **423.9 ppm** in **2024**, highest in about **2 million years**.

n3101fb96a25.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the short-lived climate pollutants listed?
n3101fb96a25.x: The listed short-lived climate pollutants are black carbon, methane, HFCs and tropospheric ozone. Water vapour is not included in that list.
n3101fb96a25.tq: Find the odd item outside the specified pollutant group.
xs: **Water vapour** is not an SLCP — option **(4)**.
SLCPs: **black carbon, methane, HFCs, tropospheric ozone** — short lifetime but strong warming.
xa: They are tackled by the **Climate and Clean Air Coalition**.
Black carbon lasts **days to weeks**; methane **~12 years**; tropospheric ozone **weeks to months**.

na0085e8b054.s: The Climate and Clean Air Coalition is associated with action against:
na0085e8b054.x: The Climate and Clean Air Coalition works to address short-lived climate pollutants such as black carbon, methane, HFCs and tropospheric ozone.
na0085e8b054.tq: Match the coalition with the precise environmental problem it addresses.
xs: The **Climate and Clean Air Coalition** tackles **short-lived climate pollutants** — option **(3)**.
SLCPs: **black carbon, methane, HFCs, tropospheric ozone**.
xa: **Black carbon** comes from **incomplete combustion** (biomass, diesel).
The **Global Methane Status Report 2025** was by **UNEP and CCAC**.
Tropospheric ozone is a **secondary** pollutant.

na6fbe0acfbc.s: Black and brown carbon ____ the air, while sulphate droplets ____ it.
na6fbe0acfbc.x: Black and brown carbon have a warming effect, whereas sulphate droplets have a cooling effect.
xa: Black carbon comes from **incomplete combustion**.
It darkens **snow and ice**, speeding glacier melt.

n24a30ffc89b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ocean carbonate chemistry?
o: Dissolved atmospheric CO2 forms carbonic acid in seawater
Carbonic acid releases hydrogen ions and bicarbonate
Extra hydrogen ions bind carbonate ions
Binding of carbonate ions leaves more carbonate for shell formation
n24a30ffc89b.x: When hydrogen ions bind carbonate ions, less carbonate remains for shell formation, not more.
xa: Shellfish get **weaker shells**; **pteropods** suffer **shell dissolution**.
Corals show **slower skeleton growth**, more bleaching and erosion.

nfee72d3c892.s: Ocean acidification is called the 'evil twin' of:
nfee72d3c892.x: Ocean acidification is the 'evil twin of global warming' because it is another consequence of anthropogenic CO2.
xa: CO2 + H2O → **carbonic acid** → less carbonate for shells.
Surface pH **8.2 → ~8.1** = roughly **30%** rise in acidity; ocean still **alkaline**.
Worst in **cold/temperate and Arctic waters**.

n619b4d3d8d5.s: The fall in surface-ocean pH from about 8.2 to 8.1 represents a rise in acidity of roughly:
n619b4d3d8d5.x: The drop from 8.2 to 8.1 is about a 30% rise in acidity; the ocean is still alkaline.
xa: Oceans absorb about **one-third** of anthropogenic CO2.
**SDG 14.3** indicator = **average marine pH** at representative stations.

n2ac09285023.s: Ocean acidification is expected to be more severe in cold and Arctic waters mainly because:
o: CO2 is more soluble in cold water and melting sea ice exposes more water
Cold waters do not exchange gases with the atmosphere
Arctic waters have no calcifying organisms
n2ac09285023.x: Cold water dissolves more CO2, and melting sea ice exposes previously covered water to atmospheric CO2.
xa: **Eutrophic bloom collapse** also raises CO2 and worsens acidification.
⚠ pH **8.2 → ~8.1** yet acidity up ~**30%**; the ocean is still **alkaline**.

nd797b9b57b6.s: Which organism is popularly known as the ‘sea butterfly’ and is vulnerable to shell dissolution under ocean acidification?
nd797b9b57b6.x: Pteropods are commonly called sea butterflies. Ocean acidification can dissolve their shells, and they are also an important food source for fish.
nd797b9b57b6.tq: Discriminate the common name from other calcifying organisms in the same ecological group.
xs: The **Pteropod** is the "**sea butterfly**", hit by **shell dissolution** under acidification — option **(4)**.
**Oysters** and **clams** are shellfish (weaker shells); **calcareous phytoplankton** show reduced growth.
xa: Pteropods are a **key food for fish**.
Calcareous phytoplankton effect was asked in **UPSC 2012**.

ne5fce54c08e.s: Since 1982, the number of marine heatwaves has:
ne5fce54c08e.x: Marine heatwaves have doubled since 1982; cyclones over them can have up to 20% stronger winds.
xa: Heatwaves are now the **strongest global driver of coral-cover decline** (GCRMN **2026**).
**Deoxygenation**: algal blooms decay → hypoxic **dead zones**.
**Pteropods** ("**sea butterflies**") suffer shell dissolution.

n2f152b781f3.s: According to recent assessments, the strongest global driver of coral-cover decline is:
n2f152b781f3.x: Marine heatwaves are identified as the strongest global driver of coral-cover decline.
n2f152b781f3.tq: Select the dominant driver rather than a possible but secondary environmental factor.
xs: **Marine heatwaves** are the strongest global driver of coral-cover decline — option **(2)** (**GCRMN 2026**).
An MHW is SST **3-4°C** above average for at least **5 days**.
xa: **INCOIS** (SAMUDRA app) issues **coral bleaching alerts**.
**NCCR, Chennai** monitors reef health via **D-COIN**.

nd8818ac1cfb.s: In hypoxic dead zones formed by nutrient runoff, oxygen is used up mainly by:
nd8818ac1cfb.x: Runoff causes algal blooms; their decomposition consumes oxygen and creates hypoxic dead zones.
xa: **Eutrophic bloom collapse** raises CO2.
Cold and **Arctic waters** are worst for acidification.

nd056fd4b944.s: In relation to the Great Nicobar project, the National Green Tribunal in February 2026 asked the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change to ensure:
o: Suspension of all marine research until 2030
Coral protection and regeneration through a proved scientific method
Complete removal of all coral colonies from the islands
Exclusive use of Biorock technology in every Indian reef
nd056fd4b944.x: The NGT asked MoEFCC to ensure coral protection and coral regeneration through a proved scientific method for the Great Nicobar project.
nd056fd4b944.tq: Match the authority with the specific direction, avoiding broader claims not stated.
xs: NGT asked for **coral protection** and **regeneration through a proved scientific method** — option **(2)**.
The project uses **coral translocation**, moving colonies away from project sites.
xa: **Biorock** is used in the **Gulf of Kutch** by **ZSI**.
**3D-printed reef modules** are off **Ramanathapuram (TN)** under **PMMSY**.

n35eadfc1900.s: The Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve is India's first ____ biosphere reserve.
n35eadfc1900.x: Gulf of Mannar is India's first marine biosphere reserve; 3D-printed reef modules were placed nearby under PMMSY.
xa: ⚠ **Biorock** = **Gulf of Kutch**; 3D-printed reefs = **Ramanathapuram**.
**Lakshadweep** is entirely **atoll reef**.

n4a07e3a8158.s: Varaha, trialled at a depth of 5,270 m, is India's:
n4a07e3a8158.x: Varaha is the deep-sea mining system trialled at 5,270 m; Matsya 6000 is the Samudrayaan submersible.
xa: Indian scientists dived to **5,002 m** in the Atlantic.
⚠ **Matsya 6000** = submersible; **Varaha** = deep-sea mining system.

n50287d2db60.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Biorock technology?
o: It passes a low-voltage current through steel frames
It involves moving coral colonies away from project sites
It deposits limestone so that coral fragments grow faster
It has been used by the Zoological Survey of India in the Gulf of Kutch
n50287d2db60.x: Moving colonies away from project sites is coral translocation/transplantation, a different method from Biorock (mineral accretion).
xa: **UPSC 2022**: Biorock = "restoration of damaged coral reefs".
⚠ **Biorock** = **Gulf of Kutch**; 3D-printed reefs = **Ramanathapuram**.

nec27620d2de.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the climate of India?
o: 2019 was the seventh warmest year in India since 1901
Bihar suffered the most among the States in 2019
The MoES assessment places India's temperature rise at about 0.7°C
The official series records a rise of more than 2°C between 1901 and 2018
nec27620d2de.x: The MoES assessment puts the rise at about 0.7°C, not more than 2°C.
xa: IMD: India's **2020** average yearly temperature was **25.78°C** (**APPSC 2021** key).
⚠ **MoES 2020** = India's first national climate assessment.

n8dcbe9fcc85.s: Which organisation published India's first national climate assessment, *Assessment of Climate Change over the Indian Region*, in 2020?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
n8dcbe9fcc85.x: India's first national climate assessment was published in 2020 by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
n8dcbe9fcc85.tq: Apply the institution-publication association and distinguish neighbouring ministries.
xs: The **Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES)** published it in **2020** — option **(3)**.
The **IMD** issues the separate annual **Statement on Climate of India**.
xa: It records about **0.7°C** warming over **1901-2018**.
IMD: **2019** was the **7th warmest year**; **2020** averaged **25.78°C**.
⚠ **MoES 2020** = first national assessment; **2019** = 7th warmest (Bihar); **2020** = **25.78°C**.

n507f7c45eb1.s: Climate change is already ____ wheat productivity in India.
n507f7c45eb1.x: Climate change is cutting wheat productivity; climate-resilient varieties and digital soil-health tools are responses.
xa: Wheat/maize lose **4-10%** yield per **1 C**.
**2,996** climate-resilient varieties released **2014-2025**; heat-tolerant wheat **HD 3385**.

n7aa2519007a.s: Which organisation monitors glacier mass balance and retreat, maps areas vulnerable to Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) and updates the Himalayan glacier inventory in India?
o: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services
National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research
n7aa2519007a.x: The Geological Survey of India performs these monitoring, mapping and inventory-related functions for Himalayan glaciers.
n7aa2519007a.tq: Identify the organisation by matching it with its specific scientific responsibility.
xs: The **Geological Survey of India** does this — option **(1)**.
It monitors **mass balance and retreat**, maps **GLOF**-vulnerable areas and updates the **Himalayan glacier inventory**.
**NCPOR** runs the **Himansh** station, a separate role.
xa: **Himansh**: above **4,000 m**, **Lahaul-Spiti**, **2016**.
**CWC** issues flood forecasts at **350** stations.

na1616b16a49.s: The Climate Risk Index 2025 ranked India as the ____ most climate-affected country over 1995-2024.
na1616b16a49.x: Germanwatch's CRI 2025 ranked India 9th over 1995-2024; India's annual rank improved from 10th to 15th.
xa: India had **430** extreme events and **$170 billion** losses over 1995-2024.
**68%** of India's area is **drought-prone** (NDMA).
NICRA: **651** districts assessed → **310** highly vulnerable.

n7d561603801.s: The Andhra Pradesh Heat Wave Action Plan is cited as an example of which adaptation measure?
n7d561603801.x: The Andhra Pradesh Heat Wave Action Plan is cited as a model of early-warning and preparedness action.
n7d561603801.tq: Recognise the function of a named action plan from its hazard context.
xs: It is cited as a model of **early warning and preparedness** — option **(2)**.
In the same row, **CWC** flood forecasts at **350** stations.
xa: **APSDMA Heatwave Action Plan 2026**: heatwaves kill more in AP than any other natural disaster.
**Ahmedabad** drew up South Asia's first Heat Action Plan (**2013**).

neb2f29d2b40.s: The 2026 edition of the WMO's State of the Global Climate report characterised climate indicators as
neb2f29d2b40.x: The 2026 edition described the indicators as 'flashing red' and highlighted accelerating change.
neb2f29d2b40.tq: Identify the exact headline phrase rather than a general description of climate change.
xs: The **2026** edition said indicators are **"flashing red"**, with **accelerating change** — option **(1)**.
The report is the **WMO State of the Global Climate**.
xa: WMO's decadal update gives a **91%** chance of one year above **1.5 C** (**2026-2035**).
WMO HQ is in **Geneva**.

n52dcca4057a.s: The India Meteorological Department declares a heat wave when the actual maximum temperature reaches
o: 42°C, only when the normal maximum is exceeded
n52dcca4057a.x: IMD declares a heat wave when the actual maximum temperature is at least 45°C, regardless of the normal maximum temperature.
n52dcca4057a.tq: Separate the absolute threshold from conditions based on normal temperature.
xs: IMD declares a heat wave when the actual maximum is **≥45°C**, **irrespective of the normal maximum** — option **(2)**.
**40°C** or **42°C** are not the IMD threshold given in the notes.
xa: Causes include **meandering Rossby waves → heat domes** and the **loo** over the Gangetic plains.
Indians faced **19.8 heatwave days** in **2024**; **6.6** due to climate change (Lancet Countdown 2025).
⚠ Heat wave = **≥45°C**; survivability = wet-bulb **~35°C**; first Heat Action Plan = **Ahmedabad** (**2013**).

nbbb206c92e9.s: The increasing frequency and intensity of heat waves in Andhra Pradesh have been specifically reported in
nbbb206c92e9.x: Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur are the Andhra Pradesh districts identified as experiencing increasingly frequent and intense heat waves.
nbbb206c92e9.tq: Test a direct geographic list without substituting nearby districts.
xs: **Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur** — option **(3)**.
AP's hottest place, **Rentachintala**, is in **Palnadu**.
xa: **Rayalaseema** faces chronic drought.
**Kurnool** has Pre-Monsoon Dry Sowing in the **2026 El Niño** plan.
AP's **Heat Wave Action Plan** is cited as a model for early warning.

ne664afedb43.s: The first Heat Action Plan in South Asia was prepared for which city in 2013?
ne664afedb43.x: Ahmedabad prepared the first Heat Action Plan in South Asia in 2013.
ne664afedb43.tq: Directly test the paired city and year.
xs: **Ahmedabad** drew up South Asia's first Heat Action Plan in **2013** — option **(3)**.
Plans like this are key because heat → **heatstroke** and **cardiovascular strain**.
xa: **APSDMA Heatwave Action Plan 2026** is AP's equivalent.
IMD heat wave: actual maximum **≥45°C**.
Lancet Countdown: **heat deaths up 23%** since the 1990s.

ndisaster-management-8-5.s: Approximately what share of India's geographical area is drought-prone?
ndisaster-management-8-5.x: About 68% of India is drought-prone, largely because of rain-fed agriculture.
n: Approximately 68% of India’s geographical area is drought-prone. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Large parts of India depend on rain-fed agriculture and are vulnerable to drought. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Surface-water availability itself becomes scarce in Peninsular India during years of insufficient rainfall. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
xa: Drought types: **meteorological**, **agricultural**, **hydrological**.
**Over 75%** of districts are extreme-event hotspots (CEEW).
Excess **groundwater withdrawal** aggravates drought in the long run.

ndisaster-management-8-10.s: More than 80% of India's rainfall is received in less than ____ days during the south-west monsoon.
ndisaster-management-8-10.x: Over 80% of rain falls in under 100 monsoon days, which, with uneven distribution, causes drought.
n: In India, drought is mainly caused by the inadequacy and uneven distribution of rainfall. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
More than 80% of India’s rainfall is received in less than 100 days during the southwest monsoon. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
Excess withdrawal of groundwater over replenishment aggravates drought in the long run. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #8 · pp 22-24]
xa: ⚠ Other notes say the SW monsoon gives about **75%** of annual rain.
The **NE monsoon** (Oct-Dec) gives about **11%** of annual rain.
Each **1°C** of warming → about **7%** more atmospheric moisture.

n2a943d6d5d2.s: The south-west monsoon gives about ____ of India's annual rainfall.
n2a943d6d5d2.x: The SW monsoon gives about 75% of annual rain; the NE monsoon (Oct-Dec) gives about 11%.
xa: Some notes give **70-90%** for the SW monsoon.
AP cyclones peak **October-December**.

n4c05e0e85c7.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the approximate yield loss associated with a 1°C rise for wheat and maize?
n4c05e0e85c7.x: Wheat and maize are reported to lose approximately 4–10 percent of yield per 1°C rise.
n4c05e0e85c7.tq: Separate crop-yield loss percentages from livestock heat-stress figures.
xs: Wheat and maize lose **4-10 percent** yield per **1°C** — option **(4)**.
**15-25%** is the milk-yield loss under extreme heat.
xa: Climate change is already **cutting wheat productivity**.
Heat-tolerant wheat: **HD 3385**.

nd15d9f76297.s: Himansh, the NCPOR glacier-research station established in 2016, is located in:
nd15d9f76297.x: Himansh is an NCPOR station above 4,000 m in Lahaul-Spiti, set up in 2016 to study glaciers.
xa: **GSI** monitors glacier mass balance and maps GLOF areas.
⚠ **Chamoli** = Uttarakhand (**2021**); **South Lhonak** = Sikkim (**2023**); **Himansh** = Lahaul-Spiti.

ndd7840715f1.s: Sea-level rise is caused principally by:
o: Decline in atmospheric water vapour alone
Cooling of seawater and expansion of sea ice
Thermal expansion of seawater and melting of glaciers and ice sheets
ndd7840715f1.x: Sea-level rise results mainly from thermal expansion of seawater and the addition of water from melting glaciers and ice sheets.
ndd7840715f1.tq: Select the option containing both major physical mechanisms.
xs: Sea-level rise comes from **thermal expansion** and **melting glaciers and ice sheets** — option **(4)**.
Cooling and sea-ice growth would not raise sea level.
xa: **IPCC SROCC (Sept 2019)**: oceans absorbed **over 90%** of excess heat.
Sea level is up **~11 cm since 1993** (WMO).
AP coastline is **1,053 km** (older **974 km**); erosion hotspot **Uppada**.

n0be437f749e.s: The Godavari delta region of Andhra Pradesh is known as:
n0be437f749e.x: The Godavari delta is Konaseema; Rayalaseema is the chronically drought-hit interior.
xa: The older coastline figure is **974 km**.
**Bio-shields**: **mangrove and Casuarina** shelterbelts on the AP coast.

n7853cf7368b.s: Which of the following act as protective bio-shields against cyclones in Andhra Pradesh's delta regions?
n7853cf7368b.x: Mangroves and Casuarina shelterbelts protect the delta coast; cyclones damage paddy and aquaculture.
xa: AP cyclones peak **October-December** (**Hudhud, Titli, Michaung**).
Hit hardest: **North Coastal AP** + **Nellore/Bapatla**.
**Marine heatwaves** raise cyclone winds by **up to 20%** and rain by **up to 12%**.

n0eeb8090117.s: Cyclones in Andhra Pradesh, such as Hudhud, Titli and Michaung, generally peak during:
n0eeb8090117.x: AP cyclones peak in October-December, hitting North Coastal AP and Nellore/Bapatla hardest.
xa: Cyclones wreck paddy and aquaculture in deltas but feed rabi crops and tanks.
The **Godavari delta** is **Konaseema**.

n7b82a801686.s: Which pair of island states is identified as being at risk from sea-level rise?
n7b82a801686.x: Kiribati and Tuvalu are identified as being at risk from sea-level rise. Tebua Tarawa and Abanuea went under in 1999.
n7b82a801686.tq: Use the specific pair rather than choosing other island states associated generally with oceans.
xs: **Kiribati and Tuvalu** are at risk — option **(1)**.
**Tebua Tarawa and Abanuea** already went under in **1999**.
xa: The **Falepili Union** (Tuvalu-Australia, **2023**) gives a **climate-mobility pathway**.
Sea level is up **~11 cm since 1993**.

nae30157e4b2.s: The APSDMA Heatwave Action Plan 2026 highlights which important feature of heatwaves in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Heatwaves are confined exclusively to the coastal districts
Heatwaves affect only agricultural workers and not urban populations
Heatwaves cause fewer deaths than every other natural hazard in the State
Heatwaves cause more deaths in Andhra Pradesh than any other natural disaster
nae30157e4b2.x: The APSDMA Heatwave Action Plan 2026 identifies heatwaves as causing more deaths in Andhra Pradesh than any other natural disaster.
nae30157e4b2.tq: Watch for reversed comparisons and absolute words such as ‘exclusively’ and ‘only’.
xs: **APSDMA Heatwave Action Plan 2026**: heatwaves **kill more in AP than any other natural disaster** — option **(4)**.
Heat is concentrated inland — **Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur**, and **Rayalaseema** — not just the coast.
xa: First **Heat Action Plan** in South Asia: **Ahmedabad**, **2013**.
The **AP Heat Wave Action Plan** is cited as a model of **early warning**.
Survivability limit: **wet-bulb temperature ~35°C** — above it sweat cannot cool the body.
Indians faced **19.8 heatwave days** in **2024** (Lancet Countdown 2025).

ncdc4aecb694.s: Wet-bulb temperature equals dry-bulb temperature when relative humidity is:
ncdc4aecb694.x: At 100% relative humidity no further evaporative cooling is possible, so wet-bulb equals dry-bulb.
xa: Survivability limit: wet-bulb about **35°C**.
IMD heat wave: actual maximum **≥45°C**.
First Heat Action Plan in South Asia: **Ahmedabad**, **2013**.

n57303cc3d4c.s: The National Water Mission under NAPCC aims to raise water-use efficiency by:
n57303cc3d4c.x: The NWM (30 June 2008) targets a 20% rise in water-use efficiency.
xa: Groundwater is falling in **Punjab, Haryana**, parts of **AP/Telangana**.
Drought types: **meteorological, agricultural, hydrological**.

nd0f0925303d.s: El Niño generally ____ the south-west monsoon.
nd0f0925303d.x: El Niño tends to weaken the SW monsoon and cut rice and sugarcane yields; La Niña usually boosts monsoon rain.
xa: AP's **2026 El Niño** plan: crop diversification — **red gram, black gram, castor**.
El Niño-linked **fodder crisis in Chittoor** (**Jul 2026**).

na02eb318462.s: National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) is led by:
na02eb318462.x: NICRA is an ICAR project launched in 2011 and led by CRIDA, Hyderabad.
xa: NICRA covers **448** climate-resilient villages in **151** districts.
**2,996** climate-resilient varieties released 2014-2025; heat-tolerant wheat **HD 3385**.
**ACASA-India**: GIS-based crop vulnerability mapping.

n5b13c64cc29.s: ICRISAT, a CGIAR centre, is located at:
n5b13c64cc29.x: ICRISAT is at Patancheru, Hyderabad, not Kurnool.
xa: **NICRA** is an ICAR project led by **CRIDA, Hyderabad**.
**ACASA-India** maps crop vulnerability with GIS.

n0d6c8bf6413.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about hanging glaciers in the Himalaya?
o: They are tributary glaciers left stranded on steep slopes as valley glaciers thin
Their detachment can cause ice-rock avalanches leading to LLOFs or GLOFs
Rising heat melts the permafrost that anchors them
They form only on valley floors below the permanent snowline
n0d6c8bf6413.x: Hanging glaciers hang on steep slopes; they do not form on valley floors.
xa: The report followed a flash flood in **Nepal**; dams, tunnels and **NH-7** are at risk.
**Permafrost thaw** also releases CH4 and CO2.

nf4c36bc4ea3.s: Glacier melt in the Himalayas most directly threatens which combination?
o: Only coastal fisheries and mangrove forests
Lean-season river flows and hydropower generation
nf4c36bc4ea3.x: Glacier melt threatens lean-season flows of rivers such as the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra and also affects hydropower.
nf4c36bc4ea3.tq: Match the environmental change with its stated downstream consequences.
xs: Glacier melt threatens **lean-season flows** and **hydropower** — option **(4)**.
The Himalayas feed the **Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra**.
xa: The Himalayan ecosystem supports **51 million** hill farmers.
**NMSHE** (NAPCC) has **12** thematic areas.

n3c478de5547.s: Which glacier in Iceland was declared the first 'dead' glacier in 2019?
n3c478de5547.x: Okjokull in Iceland was declared the first dead glacier in 2019; Quelccaya is a tropical ice cap in Peru.
xa: ⚠ **Okjokull** = first dead glacier (Iceland); **Quelccaya** = largest tropical ice cap (Peru).
**Tebua Tarawa and Abanuea** islands went under in **1999**; **Kiribati and Tuvalu** are at risk.
**Falepili Union** (**2023**): Tuvalu-Australia treaty giving a **climate-mobility pathway**.

n992061bcc6a.s: According to the IPBES 2019 assessment, about what share of amphibian species is threatened?
n992061bcc6a.x: IPBES 2019 found about 40% of amphibians threatened, among up to 1 million threatened species.
xa: **33%** of reef corals are also threatened.
IPBES 2019 met in **Bonn**; **130** members incl. India.

n26a97ea12e7.s: A climate tipping point is best described as a threshold at which
o: global temperatures immediately return to pre-industrial levels
only short-term weather changes occur without wider consequences
climate variations become completely predictable and reversible
small changes can trigger large, self-perpetuating and potentially irreversible shifts
n26a97ea12e7.x: A tipping point is a threshold beyond which small changes may produce large, self-perpetuating and irreversible shifts in a non-linear system.
n26a97ea12e7.tq: Apply the definition to distinguish a non-linear threshold from ordinary climate variability.
xs: A tipping point is where **small changes trigger large, self-perpetuating, irreversible shifts** — option **(4)**.
Behaviour is **non-linear**, so options (1)-(3) are wrong.
xa: **Coral reefs** have already crossed the **1.2 C** threshold.
Beyond ~**2 C**, parts of the **Amazon** may become savanna.

nd02feee4a86.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Amazon rainforest?
o: About 17-18% of the Amazon has already been lost
Beyond about 2°C of warming, parts may turn from a carbon source into a carbon store
The Amazon makes about 50% of its own rain
Beyond about 2°C of warming, parts may turn into savanna
nd02feee4a86.x: Beyond about 2°C parts may flip from carbon store to carbon source, the reverse of what is stated.
xa: Parts may become **savanna**.
⚠ Coral threshold **1.2 C** already crossed; Amazon risk beyond ~**2 C**.

n81e2c7252bc.s: The lead centre for the WMO Global Annual to Decadal Climate Update is the:
n81e2c7252bc.x: The UK Met Office leads the update, which projects 1.3-1.9°C warming for 2026-30.
xa: **El Nino** expected late **2026**; **2027** may set a record.
WMO's **State of the Global Climate** 2026 edition: indicators "**flashing red**", accelerating change.
UNEP **Emissions Gap Report 2025 "Off Target"**: **2.3-2.5 C** even with updated NDCs.

n3015a3d8f3d.s: The IPCC was established in 1988 by:
n3015a3d8f3d.x: WMO and UNEP set up the IPCC in 1988; it assesses literature and shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize.
xa: **WMO**: set up **1950**; UN specialised agency since **1951**; HQ **Geneva**.
**IPCC SROCC (Sept 2019)**: oceans absorbed **over 90%** of excess heat.
**IPCC SR1.5 (2018)** compares impacts at **1.5 C** and **2 C**.

n151bfd649d2.s: According to the AP SAPCC assessment, which part of Andhra Pradesh is relatively low in climate vulnerability?
n151bfd649d2.x: The northern and central regions are very highly vulnerable, the southern coast moderately, and the south-west relatively low.
xa: AP cyclones hit **North Coastal AP** + **Nellore/Bapatla** hardest.
AP heat hotspots: **Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur**.
**Rayalaseema** suffers chronic drought.

nf69e5c4e9ad.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated cause or mechanism associated with heat waves in India?
o: Cold ocean currents over the Arabian Sea
The loo over the Gangetic plains
Meandering Rossby waves creating heat domes
nf69e5c4e9ad.x: Meandering Rossby waves and the loo over the Gangetic plains are identified causes. Cold ocean currents over the Arabian Sea are not stated as a cause in this context.
nf69e5c4e9ad.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated heat-wave mechanisms.
xs: **Cold ocean currents over the Arabian Sea** are not a stated cause — option **(1)**.
Stated causes: **meandering Rossby waves → heat domes**, and the **loo** over the **Gangetic plains**.
xa: IMD heat wave: actual maximum **≥45°C**.
Survivability limit: **wet-bulb ~35°C**.
Heat → **heatstroke** and **cardiovascular strain**.

n80255e262fd.s: Gangotri glacier melting is primarily attributed to:
n80255e262fd.x: The melting of the Gangotri glacier is attributed to global warming.
n80255e262fd.tq: Identify the stated cause rather than selecting an unrelated physical process.
xs: **Gangotri** glacier melting is due to **global warming** — option **(2)** (**APPSC-G2 2025**).
Tectonics, solar dimming or ocean acidification are not the cause.
xa: Glacier melt threatens **lean-season flows** and **hydropower**.
**Zanskar** glaciers now move slower than **30** years ago (**IIT-Bombay**).

n91336aaa74a.s: Urban floods are aggravated by which combination of factors?
o: Floodplain encroachment, wetland loss, poor drainage and more intense rainfall
Afforestation, wetland restoration and improved drainage
Declining rainfall and expansion of natural floodplains
n91336aaa74a.x: Encroachment of floodplains, loss of wetlands and poor drainage increase urban flood risk, which is further worsened by more intense rainfall.
n91336aaa74a.tq: Select the complete causal combination instead of an isolated factor.
xs: **Floodplain encroachment**, **wetland loss**, **poor drainage** and **more intense rain** — option **(1)**.
Afforestation and wetland restoration reduce flood risk; they do not aggravate it.
xa: **Urban waterlogging** (e.g. Mumbai) spreads **leptospirosis, typhoid and hepatitis A**.
**Over 80%** of urban population lives in hazard-prone districts.

n30cdc933f0b.s: For about two decades, the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets have:
n30cdc933f0b.x: Both ice sheets have experienced significant mass loss for about two decades.
xa: **Greenland ice sheet** is thinning **~1 m/yr**.
Antarctic sea ice was the **3rd lowest** in **2025**.

nf0cb012bd35.s: The Rutgers University study found that warming may wipe out ocean species from their habitats at about ____ the rate of land species.
nf0cb012bd35.x: The study found ocean species may be lost from habitats at about twice the rate of land species.
xa: Asked in **APPSC-G1 2019**.
**IPBES 2019**: up to **1 million** of ~**8 million** species threatened.

n5cb4cdacabc.s: As climate conditions become cooler toward higher latitudes and elevations, many species are expected to move
o: only toward the equator, irrespective of elevation
n5cb4cdacabc.x: Species are shifting poleward and upslope as they track cooler climatic conditions.
n5cb4cdacabc.tq: Apply the directional logic of following cooler conditions across latitude and elevation.
xs: Species move **poleward and upslope** to track cooler climates — option **(1)**.
Equatorward and downslope would be warmer.
xa: Rutgers: warming may wipe out **twice as many ocean species** as land species.
**10 billion crabs** died in the **Bering Sea**.

nae5933e1700.s: Which of the following is NOT among the climate tipping elements listed by scientists?
nae5933e1700.x: Greenland and West Antarctic ice sheets, AMOC and permafrost are listed tipping elements; Sahara Desert dunes are not.
xa: Also: **Arctic sea ice**, **warm-water coral reefs**, **Amazon rainforest**.
**Permafrost thaw** releases CH4 + CO2.

n4b76613ac18.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the UNFCCC?
o: It was adopted on 9 May 1992 at New York
It entered into force on 21 March 1994
Its Conference of the Parties is the supreme body and meets annually
Its secretariat is located at Geneva
n4b76613ac18.x: The UNFCCC secretariat is at Bonn, Germany; Geneva hosts the IPCC secretariat.
xa: The UNFCCC has **198 Parties**.
⚠ Some notes say the UNFCCC was "adopted at Rio" — it was adopted in **New York**, only opened for signature at **Rio (UNCED)**.
The COP serves two instruments: the **Kyoto Protocol (CMP)** and the **Paris Agreement (CMA)**.
The subsidiary bodies **SBI and SBSTA** meet mid-year in **Bonn**.

n6691fec0610.s: The two instruments adopted under the UNFCCC framework are:
n6691fec0610.x: The Kyoto Protocol and the Paris Agreement are the two instruments associated with the UNFCCC; their governing meetings are referred to as CMP and CMA respectively.
n6691fec0610.tq: Identify the two related instruments while rejecting treaties from other environmental regimes.
xs: The two instruments under the UNFCCC are the **Kyoto Protocol** and the **Paris Agreement** — option **(1)**.
Their governing meetings are the **CMP** (Kyoto) and the **CMA** (Paris), held alongside the **COP**.
**CBD** and **Ramsar** are separate treaties (biodiversity and wetlands), not UNFCCC instruments.
xa: Kyoto: adopted **11 Dec 1997** at **COP3**, in force **16 Feb 2005**.
Paris: adopted **12 Dec 2015**, in force **4 Nov 2016**.
**Montreal Protocol (1987)** deals with ozone-depleting substances; its **Kigali Amendment (2016)** phases down HFCs.

nc06c53fe700.s: India sought dedicated agenda space at SB64 for discussion of which Paris Agreement provision?
o: Article 9.1 on finance by developed countries
Article 28 on withdrawal from the Agreement
nc06c53fe700.x: India requested dedicated agenda space for Article 9.1, which obliges developed countries to provide climate finance to developing countries. Article 13 concerns transparency, while Article 28 concerns withdrawal.
nc06c53fe700.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish provisions dealing with finance, transparency and withdrawal.
xs: At SB64 India sought dedicated agenda space on **Article 9.1**, the Paris provision obliging **developed countries to provide finance** — option **(1)**.
**Article 13** is the Enhanced Transparency Framework; **Article 28** covers withdrawal; **Article 6.4** is the UN-run **PACM**.
xa: **SB64** was held at **Bonn, 8-18 June 2026**.
India aligned with **G77+China, LMDC and BASIC** there.
India criticised the **NCQG ($300 bn)** as inadequate.
The unmet **$100 bn** promise eroded finance trust.

ned589bdb5c4.s: At the Bonn SB64 session (June 2026), India aligned itself with which negotiating groups?
o: G77 and China, LMDC and BASIC
AOSIS, LMDC and the Umbrella Group
G77 and China, AOSIS and the EU
BASIC and the Environmental Integrity Group only
ned589bdb5c4.x: India aligned with G77+China (largest developing-country group), the LMDC (of which India is a member, hard-line on equity and CBDR) and BASIC. AOSIS is the small-island bloc pressing for 1.5°C, not India's group; the Umbrella Group and EU are developed-country groupings; 'BASIC only' leaves out G77 and LMDC.
ned589bdb5c4.tq: India's three tables: G77+China, LMDC, BASIC.
xs: At SB64 India aligned with all three: **G77 and China, LMDC and BASIC** — option **(1)**.
**AOSIS** is the small-island bloc pressing for **1.5°C**, not India's alignment here.
xa: **G77 and China** is the largest developing-country group.
**LMDC** (Like-Minded Developing Countries) is hard-line on **equity and CBDR**; India is a member.
India's SB64 demand: dedicated agenda space on **Art. 9.1** finance obligations.
SB64 met at **Bonn, 8-18 June 2026**.

n5ee40c67ce5.s: The Kyoto Protocol entered into force on:
n5ee40c67ce5.x: Kyoto was adopted at COP3 on 11 December 1997 and entered into force on 16 February 2005.
xa: Kyoto was the **first legally binding climate agreement**; it has **192 parties**.
**Canada withdrew in 2011** (some notes say 2012).
1st period **2008-2012**: about **5% below 1990**; 2nd period **2013-2020** via the **Doha Amendment**: **18% below 1990**.

n38437101778.s: The Paris Agreement entered into force on:
n38437101778.x: The Paris Agreement entered into force on 4 November 2016. India ratified it on 2 October 2016.
n38437101778.tq: Distinguish adoption, ratification and entry into force dates.
xs: The Paris Agreement entered into force on **4 November 2016** — option **(3)**.
**12 Dec 2015** is its adoption date; **2 Oct 2016** is when **India ratified** it.
xa: It was adopted at **COP21, Paris**.
Goal: hold warming **well below 2°C** and pursue **1.5°C**.
Article 28: a party may withdraw **3 years** after entry into force, effective **1 year** after notice.

n2f374d47834.s: At which event did India launch the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI)?
o: The UN Climate Action Summit, 2019, New York
The UN Climate Action Summit, 2023, Dubai
n2f374d47834.x: India launched CDRI at the UN Climate Action Summit held in New York in 2019.
n2f374d47834.tq: Distinguish a summit-level initiative from an initiative launched at a COP.
xs: India launched **CDRI** at the **UN Climate Action Summit, 2019 (New York)** — option **(3)**.
It was not a COP launch: **COP21 (Paris, 2015)** saw the **ISA**, and **COP26 (Glasgow, 2021)** saw **Panchamrit**.
xa: CDRI is headquartered in **New Delhi** (2019).
**ISA**: launched at **COP21, 2015**, with France; HQ **Gurugram** — first intergovernmental body headquartered in India.
The only COP hosted by India was **COP8, New Delhi, 2002**.

na56eb083e20.s: Which of the following energy pledges was associated with COP28?
o: Reducing renewable capacity to 4,000 GW and increasing efficiency gains to 11 per cent annually
Cutting methane by 30 per cent from 2020 levels and phasing out all coal by 2025
Providing 30 adaptation outcomes for four billion people by 2030
Tripling renewable capacity to 11,000 GW and doubling energy-efficiency gains to 4 per cent annually by 2030
na56eb083e20.x: COP28 included pledges to triple renewable capacity to 11,000 GW and double energy-efficiency gains to 4 per cent per year by 2030. The other options combine targets from different initiatives or alter the figures.
na56eb083e20.tq: Pair the two numerical targets and their deadline; beware of reversed or borrowed figures.
xs: COP28 pledged to **triple renewable capacity to 11,000 GW** and **double energy-efficiency gains to 4%/yr** by **2030** — option **(4)**.
A **30%** methane cut from **2020** levels is the **Global Methane Pledge** (COP26).
**30 adaptation outcomes for 4 billion people** is the COP27 **Sharm el-Sheikh Adaptation Agenda**.
xa: India did not sign the **COP28 Global Renewables and Energy Efficiency Pledge**.
COP28 concluded the **first Global Stocktake** → **UAE Consensus**.
PM Modi offered to host **COP33** at COP28 (**1 Dec 2023**).

nc55151b4eca.s: The first IPCC Assessment Report, published in 1990, contributed to the development of the:
nc55151b4eca.x: AR1 (1990) fed into the UNFCCC of 1992. The Convention was adopted on 9 May 1992 in New York and opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit in June 1992. Kyoto (1997), Paris (2015) and Montreal (1987) came later or deal with other issues.
nc55151b4eca.tq: Connect the report to its immediate institutional outcome rather than to later climate agreements.
xs: **AR1 (1990)** fed into the **UNFCCC**, adopted in **1992** — option **(3)**.
The UNFCCC was adopted on **9 May 1992** (New York) and opened at the **1992 Rio Earth Summit**.
**Kyoto (1997)** and **Paris (2015)** came later; **Montreal (1987)** deals with ozone.
xa: The IPCC was set up in **1988** by **WMO** and **UNEP**.
UNFCCC entered into force on **21 March 1994**.

n6e7b425b339.s: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched at the:
n6e7b425b339.x: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched at the G20 New Delhi Summit (9-10 September 2023).
xa: India hosted the **Voice of Global South Summits** from **January 2023**.
**Mission LiFE** was launched in **October 2022**.

nenvironment-7-4.s: The Clean Development Mechanism is provided under which Article of the Kyoto Protocol?
nenvironment-7-4.x: The CDM is Article 12 of the Kyoto Protocol; one CER equals one tonne of CO2-equivalent.
n: The Clean Development Mechanism is covered under Article 12 of the Kyoto Protocol. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
One CER equals one tonne of carbon-dioxide equivalent. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
COP21 took place in Paris in 2015. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
COP26 took place in Glasgow. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
The Paris Agreement dates to 2015. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
xa: COP26 (**2021**) gave India's **Panchamrit** and the Glasgow Climate Pact — coal "**phase-down**".
COP21 produced the **Paris Agreement**.
**1 carbon credit** = **1 tonne CO2-equivalent** reduced, avoided or removed.

nenvironment-4-5.s: The New York Declaration on Forests was first endorsed at the UN Climate Summit in:
nenvironment-4-5.x: It was endorsed at the 2014 UN Climate Summit; it is voluntary and India was not an initial signatory.
n: The New York Declaration on Forests was first endorsed at the United Nations Climate Summit in 2014. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
The New York Declaration on Forests is voluntary. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
The New York Declaration on Forests is non-legally binding. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
India was not an initial signatory to the New York Declaration on Forests according to the source. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
xa: Its goal is to **halt or reduce global forest loss**.
It involves **governments**, **companies**, **civil society** and **indigenous groups**.
It is the basis of the **Bonn Challenge** target.

n0f935c4522f.s: Under the UNFCCC, which group is required to provide finance and technology to developing countries?
n0f935c4522f.x: Annex II, the OECD members of Annex I, must provide finance and technology to developing countries.
xa: Non-Annex I parties get special care for **LDCs and SIDS**.
The grouping reflects **CBDR-RC**: Annex I caused most historical emissions, so it must take the lead.
Under Kyoto, **binding targets** applied to **Annex I only**.

n9663a15e975.s: The principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) rests on the idea that:
o: Only developing countries must reduce emissions
All countries have identical historical responsibility and capabilities
Developed countries, having contributed most to historical emissions, should take the lead
Least developed countries must finance mitigation in OECD countries
n9663a15e975.x: CBDR-RC recognises differentiated historical responsibility and capabilities; developed countries that caused most historical emissions are expected to take the lead.
n9663a15e975.tq: Translate the principle into a practical responsibility allocation rather than memorising only its expansion.
xs: CBDR-RC holds that **developed countries**, having caused most historical emissions, should **take the lead** — option **(3)**.
It differentiates responsibility, so "identical responsibility" and "only developing countries cut" are the opposite of the principle.
It gives special consideration to **LDCs and SIDS** rather than asking them to pay.
xa: CBDR-RC = **Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities**, the foundational principle of the **UNFCCC**.
⚠ It appears as **Principle 7** (Rio Declaration), **Article 3.1** (UNFCCC) and **Article 2.2** (Paris).
India argues the **EU CBAM violates CBDR-RC** and is **green protectionism**.

n0ef582ef844.s: Which one of the following is the largest negotiating group of developing countries in the UNFCCC process?
n0ef582ef844.x: The G77 and China is the main and largest developing-country group. LMDC is a smaller hard-line group on equity and CBDR, BASIC has four members, and AOSIS is limited to small island states.
xs: **G77 and China** is the main and **largest developing-country group** — option **(4)**.
**LMDC** is a hard-line group on **equity and CBDR**; **AOSIS** is limited to **small island states**.
xa: India is a member of the **LMDC**.
AOSIS presses for the **1.5°C** goal.
At **SB64, Bonn** India aligned with G77+China, LMDC and **BASIC**.

nc02e1efdb12.s: The Kyoto Protocol's first commitment period (2008-2012) required an average cut of about 5% below ____ levels.
nc02e1efdb12.x: The first period set about a 5% (5.2%) cut below 1990; the Doha Amendment's 18% cut was also from 1990 levels.
xa: Kyoto adopted **11 Dec 1997** at **Kyoto (COP3)**; in force **16 Feb 2005**.
Kyoto was the **first legally binding climate agreement**.
Six gases: CO2, CH4, N2O, **HFCs, PFCs, SF6**; **NF3** added for the second period.

n677dba51232.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the six gases originally covered by the Kyoto Protocol?
n677dba51232.x: The original six gases were CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs and SF6. NF3 was added for the second commitment period.
n677dba51232.tq: Find the later addition hidden among members of the original list.
xs: **Nitrogen trifluoride (NF3)** was not among the original six — it was **added for the 2nd period** — option **(2)**.
The original six gases: **CO2, CH4 (methane), N2O, HFCs, PFCs and SF6 (sulphur hexafluoride)**.
xa: The 2nd period (**2013-2020**) ran under the **Doha Amendment**.
HFCs are also phased down under the **Kigali Amendment (2016)** to the **Montreal Protocol**.
The **Global Methane Pledge** (COP26) aims to cut methane **30% by 2030**; India is not a member.

n6e1274f9cd4.s: For a 50% chance of limiting warming to 1.5°C, the remaining carbon budget from 2020 was assessed at approximately:
n6e1274f9cd4.x: AR6 Working Group I placed the remaining carbon budget for a 50% chance of limiting warming to 1.5°C at about 500 GtCO2 from 2020.
n6e1274f9cd4.tq: Recall the quantitative carbon-budget estimate and its probability condition.
xs: The remaining carbon budget is ~**500 GtCO2** from **2020** for a **50%** chance of **1.5°C** — option **(3)**.
The figure comes from **AR6 WG I**.
xa: WG I report released **9 Aug 2021**: "The Physical Science Basis".
Emissions must **peak before 2025**.
CO2 reached **423.9 ppm** in **2024** (WMO State of the Global Climate 2025).

nenvironment-7-2.s: Under the Clean Development Mechanism, emission-cutting projects are run by:
o: developed countries in other developed countries
developing countries in other developing countries
nenvironment-7-2.x: Under Article 12 of Kyoto, developed countries run projects in developing countries and earn credits.
n: The Clean Development Mechanism is covered under Article 12 of the Kyoto Protocol. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
The Clean Development Mechanism involves emission-reduction projects. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
Developed countries undertake Clean Development Mechanism projects in developing countries. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
xa: ⚠ **CDM** → CERs (developing country); **JI** → **ERUs** (other Annex I).
**Article 6.4 PACM** of the Paris Agreement **replaces the Kyoto CDM**.
The **Adaptation Fund** is financed by a **2%** share of CDM proceeds.

n68b5c507cf2.s: Which negotiating bloc in climate talks, made up of small island states, is known for pressing for the 1.5°C temperature goal?
n68b5c507cf2.x: AOSIS (Alliance of Small Island States) presses for the 1.5°C goal, as its members face existential threats from sea-level rise.
xs: **AOSIS** — the bloc of small island states — presses for the **1.5°C** goal — option **(1)**.
**LMDC** is hard-line on equity and CBDR; **G77 and China** is the largest developing-country group.
xa: The Paris goal: hold warming **well below 2°C**, pursue **1.5°C**.
**SIDS** get special consideration under the UNFCCC alongside **LDCs**.
Sea-level-rise refugees fall **outside the 1951 Refugee Convention**.

nee278a33f1d.s: Which country withdrew from the Kyoto Protocol in 2011?
nee278a33f1d.x: Canada withdrew in 2011 (some sources say 2012); the USA never ratified the Protocol.
xa: The **USA never ratified** Kyoto.
Kyoto: adopted **11 Dec 1997** (COP3), in force **16 Feb 2005**, **192 parties**.
CDM projects in developing countries such as **India** earned **CERs**.

n9f8dfd242c5.s: The credits issued under the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism established under Article 6.4 are called:
n9f8dfd242c5.x: Article 6.4 credits are called A6.4ERs. CERs are associated with the Kyoto Protocol’s Clean Development Mechanism.
n9f8dfd242c5.tq: Distinguish the official abbreviation of the newer Paris mechanism from the Kyoto-era CERs.
xs: Credits under the **Article 6.4 PACM** are called **A6.4ERs** — option **(1)**.
**CERs** are the units of the **Kyoto CDM**; **NDCs** are national climate pledges, not credits.
xa: **1 credit = 1 tonne CO2-equivalent** reduced, avoided or removed.
First Article 6.4 credits went to a clean-cooking project in **Myanmar** (with South Korea).
Those credits were possibly overstated **7-14 times**.

n422b6e92045.s: Article 6 of the Paris Agreement became fully operational at:
n422b6e92045.x: Article 6 was made fully operational at COP29; its 6.4 mechanism replaces the Kyoto CDM.
xa: ⚠ **6.2** = bilateral (JCM); **6.4** = UN-run PACM.
India-Japan **Joint Crediting Mechanism** signed **Aug 2025** under Art. 6.2.
COP29 (**Baku, 2024**) is called the "Finance COP" for the **NCQG**.

n44e8ec3605b.s: India signed the Joint Crediting Mechanism with Japan in August 2025 under which provision of the Paris Agreement?
n44e8ec3605b.x: The India-Japan Joint Crediting Mechanism, signed in August 2025, is a bilateral cooperative approach under Article 6.2. Its Rules of Implementation were adopted in January 2026. Article 6.4 is the UN-run PACM, Article 9.1 covers finance from developed countries and Article 14 is the Global Stocktake.
n44e8ec3605b.tq: Discriminate between the cooperative approaches of Article 6.2 and the central mechanism of Article 6.4.
xs: The India-Japan **Joint Crediting Mechanism** (Aug 2025) is a bilateral approach under **Article 6.2** — option **(1)**.
**Article 6.4** is the UN-run PACM; **Article 9.1** is developed-country finance; **Article 14** is the Global Stocktake.
xa: JCM **Rules of Implementation** were adopted in **Jan 2026**.
⚠ **6.2** = bilateral; **6.4** = UN-run PACM replacing the CDM.
Article 6 rules were finalised at **COP29**.

n373ec4f42b1.s: Under the Paris Agreement, Nationally Determined Contributions are submitted every:
n373ec4f42b1.x: Each country sets its own NDC and submits it every five years; the targets themselves are not legally binding.
xa: ⚠ No country — USA, China, India or EU — is legally bound to its emission targets (APPSC-G2 2025 key "None of these").
**Ratchet mechanism**: each new NDC must progress beyond the previous one.
"**NDC 3.0**" was due for **COP30 (2025)**.

nbdc837431bc.s: Under the Paris Agreement, the requirement that each new NDC show progression beyond the previous one is called the:
nbdc837431bc.x: The ratchet mechanism requires each new NDC to progress beyond the last, informed by the Global Stocktake.
xa: The **Global Stocktake** is held **every 5 years**; the first concluded at **COP28 (2023)**.
NDC 3.0 was to be economy-wide, all-gas and **1.5°C**-aligned.

nb1c3ef0a1e9.s: India's 2015 INDC targeted an emissions-intensity reduction (from 2005) by 2030 of:
nb1c3ef0a1e9.x: The 2015 target was 33–35%; it was raised to 45% in 2022, and the 2031–35 NDC targets 47% by 2035.
xa: India had achieved a **36%** reduction by **2020**.
India's net-zero target is **2070**.
Each new NDC must be a progression — the **ratchet mechanism**.

n5487ab154e4.s: The first Global Stocktake under Article 14 of the Paris Agreement was concluded at:
n5487ab154e4.x: The first stocktake concluded at COP28 (Dubai, 2023), leading to the UAE Consensus; it is held every five years.
xa: **Art. 13**: **Enhanced Transparency Framework** — Biennial Transparency Reports.
**Art. 28**: a party may withdraw **3 years** after entry into force.
NDCs are submitted every **5 years**; each must be a **progression** (ratchet).
