nf0d60a6ce06.s: The United States left the Paris Agreement for the second time in:
nf0d60a6ce06.x: The United States left the Paris Agreement for the second time in January 2026.
nf0d60a6ce06.tq: Use the exact year in a current-affairs date question and distinguish it from the first withdrawal episode.
xs: The USA left the Paris Agreement a second time in **January 2026** — option **(4)**.
Its first withdrawal was announced in **2017** and took effect on **4 Nov 2020**.
xa: The USA **rejoined on 19 Feb 2021** after the first exit.
A presidential memorandum ended US participation in the **UNFCCC, IPCC, ISA and IRENA**.
The USA also **never ratified Kyoto**.

n8d23368c7d3.s: Which of the following is associated with Article 13 of the Paris Agreement?
o: The Enhanced Transparency Framework and Biennial Transparency Reports
The Global Stocktake every five years
The obligation to provide finance under Article 9.1
Withdrawal from the Agreement after notice
n8d23368c7d3.x: Article 13 establishes the Enhanced Transparency Framework, including common reporting through Biennial Transparency Reports. The first reports were due by the end of 2024.
n8d23368c7d3.tq: Use article-number discrimination to separate transparency, stocktake, finance and withdrawal provisions.
xs: **Article 13** sets up the **Enhanced Transparency Framework** with **Biennial Transparency Reports** — option **(1)**.
The **Global Stocktake** is **Art. 14**; finance is **Art. 9.1**; withdrawal is **Art. 28**.
xa: The first Biennial Transparency Reports were due **end-2024**.
The Global Stocktake is held **every 5 years**.
Paris binding elements are **procedural** — prepare, communicate and **report** NDCs.

n6b27277cd96.s: Under Article 28 of the Paris Agreement, a party may withdraw from the Agreement:
o: Three years after entry into force, with withdrawal taking effect one year after notice
Immediately after ratification, with effect on the same day
Only after unanimous consent of all other parties
Five years after entry into force, with effect after six months
n6b27277cd96.x: A party may give notice of withdrawal three years after the Agreement entered into force for it, and the withdrawal takes effect one year after the notice. Unanimous consent is not required.
n6b27277cd96.tq: Track the two separate time periods instead of merging the eligibility period with the effective period.
xs: Under **Article 28**, a party may withdraw **3 years after entry into force**, effective **1 year after notice** — option **(1)**.
No unanimous consent is needed.
xa: The USA announced withdrawal in **2017**; it took effect on **4 Nov 2020**.
The Agreement entered into force on **4 Nov 2016**.
The USA **rejoined 19 Feb 2021** and left again in **January 2026**.

n295fd4570a3.s: The United States re-entered the Paris Agreement on:
n295fd4570a3.x: The US withdrawal (announced 2017) took effect on 4 November 2020, and it rejoined on 19 February 2021.
xa: Art. 28 explains the timing: notice **3 years** after entry into force, effect **1 year** later.
The USA left a **second time in January 2026**.
That exit ended US participation in **UNFCCC, IPCC, ISA and IRENA**.

nf3212fd9376.s: Saraswathi of Malluvalasa was brought into the news for sustainability work in connection with:
o: The Glasgow Leaders' Declaration on Forests and Land Use
The Global Renewables and Energy Efficiency Pledge
nf3212fd9376.x: The APPSC-GS 2024 key links Saraswathi of Malluvalasa (AP natural-farming practitioner) with 'Sustaina India 2025'. ⚠ Sources differ: one guide links her to COP28 instead, so check the official key.
nf3212fd9376.tq: Identify the exact programme associated with the person rather than a similarly themed global pledge.
xs: The **APPSC 2024** key links **Saraswathi of Malluvalasa (AP)** to **"Sustaina India 2025"** — option **(4)**.
She is an AP woman **natural-farming practitioner** in the news for **sustainability** work.
xa: ⚠ One guide links her to **COP28** as an Indian grassroots participant, but the APPSC-GS 2024 key reads "Sustaina India 2025" — check the official key.
The **Global Methane Pledge** and the **Glasgow Leaders' Declaration on Forests** (COP26) were **not signed by India**.
India also declined the **COP28 Global Renewables and Energy Efficiency Pledge**.

nd75acb83504.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the New Collective Quantified Goal on Climate Finance (NCQG)?
o: COP29 was described as the Finance COP
Developed countries are to mobilise 300 billion dollars a year by 2035
The 300-billion-dollar goal replaces the earlier 100-billion-dollar goal
The call for 1.3 trillion dollars a year from all sources is legally binding
nd75acb83504.x: The call to reach 1.3 trillion dollars a year from all sources is non-binding.
xa: Developing nations called the core target **insufficient**; India criticised the NCQG as inadequate.
COP30 set a **Baku-to-Belem Roadmap** to **US$1.3 trillion**.
⚠ **$100 bn** (old) → **$300 bn** core → **$1.3 trillion** broader; adaptation **$120 bn**.

n9246c62ca59.s: Which one of the following is a stated feature of NDC 3.0?
o: It is economy-wide, covers all gases and is intended to align with 1.5°C.
It applies only to developed countries.
It is limited to carbon dioxide alone.
n9246c62ca59.x: NDC 3.0 calls for economy-wide, all-gas pledges aligned with the 1.5°C objective and due for COP30.
n9246c62ca59.tq: Test the scope of the pledge by checking economy-wide and all-gas coverage.
xs: **NDC 3.0** pledges are **economy-wide**, **all-gas** and **1.5°C-aligned** — option **(1)**.
They are not limited to CO2 or to developed countries: **each country sets its own targets**.
xa: NDC 3.0 was due for **COP30 (2025)**.
NDCs are submitted/updated **every 5 years**.
**Ratchet mechanism**: each new NDC must progress beyond the previous one.

n91b7bb8848d.s: COP30 (Belém, 2025) adopted how many voluntary indicators under the Global Goal on Adaptation?
n91b7bb8848d.x: COP30 adopted 59 voluntary GGA indicators and an adaptation finance target of US$120 billion a year.
xa: COP30 agreed to work towards **at least tripling adaptation finance**.
**Baku-to-Belem Roadmap** → **US$1.3 trillion**.

n838e066da2f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Adaptation Fund?
o: It was set up under the Kyoto Protocol
It is financed by a share of proceeds from the Clean Development Mechanism
NABARD is India's National Implementing Entity for it
The share of CDM Certified Emission Reductions associated with it is 20 per cent
n838e066da2f.x: The Adaptation Fund gets a 2 per cent share of CDM CER proceeds, not 20 per cent.
xa: The Adaptation Fund was set up in **2001** and has run from **2007**.
NABARD is also a **Direct Access Entity of GCF**.
CDM projects in developing countries earned **Certified Emission Reductions (CERs)**.

n87cebfda359.s: The Global Methane Pledge was launched at COP26 by:
o: the United States and the European Union
n87cebfda359.x: The US and EU launched the Pledge at COP26 to cut methane 30% from 2020 levels by 2030.
xa: **India is not a member** of the Methane Pledge.
Methane is one of Kyoto's six gases (**CH4**).
UNEP's **MARS** is a methane satellite alert system.

nbb915317632.s: Which one of the following is an India-relevant finding of the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (AR6)?
o: India's warming is confined to its coastal regions
India has experienced no significant change in heatwave intensity
India is warming more slowly than the global average
India is warming faster than the global average
nbb915317632.x: The IPCC AR6 indicates that India is warming faster than the global average and is experiencing more frequent and intense heatwaves.
nbb915317632.tq: Use the precise comparative statement and reject the reversed comparison.
xs: AR6: **India is warming faster than the global average** — option **(4)**.
India faces **more frequent and intense heatwaves**, so "no change" and "slower warming" are wrong.
xa: This was cited in **Apr 2026** on heat stress in textile hubs.
**Erratic monsoon** → severe floods; **sea-level rise** threatens **Mumbai and Chennai**.
High mountains are warming at **twice the global average**.

ncb2640a0e2a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about climate equity?
o: India's per capita emissions are higher than those of industrialised nations
Developed countries emitted most of the historical stock of greenhouse gases
Developing countries argue that they need carbon space to grow
Climate justice recognises that those who emitted least may suffer the most
ncb2640a0e2a.x: India's per capita emissions are much lower than those of industrialised nations.
xa: The **Loss and Damage Fund (COP27, 2022)** is seen as an ethical win for climate justice.
**Carbon leakage** is what the EU **CBAM** aims to prevent.
India says CBAM **violates CBDR-RC** — **green protectionism**.

nenvironment-7-10.s: In climate negotiations, INDC stands for:
nenvironment-7-10.x: INDC means Intended Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris framework.
n: The Paris Agreement aims to keep warming well below 2°C above the pre-industrial level. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
The Paris Agreement aims to pursue efforts toward limiting warming to 1.5°C above the pre-industrial level. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
INDC stands for Intended Nationally Determined Contributions. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #7 · pp 13-16]
xa: Paris adopted **12 Dec 2015**; in force **4 Nov 2016**; **India ratified 2 Oct 2016**.
**NDC targets** are nationally determined and **not legally binding**; binding elements are **procedural**.
USA rejoined **19 Feb 2021** and left again in **January 2026**.

o: Stabilise greenhouse gas concentrations at a level preventing dangerous anthropogenic interference with the climate system
Provide only financial assistance to small island developing States
Regulate international trade in endangered species
Eliminate all industrial production in developed countries
nd19a2222b3b.x: The objective of the UNFCCC is to stabilise greenhouse gas concentrations at a level that prevents dangerous anthropogenic interference with the climate system.
nd19a2222b3b.tq: Select the option stating the treaty’s precise objective rather than one of its related measures.
xs: The UNFCCC's objective is to **stabilise greenhouse gas concentrations** at a safe level, **preventing dangerous anthropogenic interference** with the climate system — option **(1)**.
Trade in **endangered species** is the subject of **CITES (Washington)**, not the UNFCCC.
Finance is not its only aim: special consideration for **LDCs and SIDS** sits inside the wider **CBDR-RC** framework.
xa: The UNFCCC was adopted on **9 May 1992** (New York) and entered into force on **21 March 1994**.
Its foundational principle is **CBDR-RC** — developed (**Annex I**) countries must **take the lead**.
**IPCC AR1 (1990)** fed into the UNFCCC.
⚠ UNFCCC secretariat = **Bonn**; IPCC secretariat = **Geneva**.

na26be7d6ac3.s: The Loss and Damage Fund was created at:
na26be7d6ac3.x: The Loss and Damage Fund was created at COP27, not COP28.
xa: COP28 (**Dubai**) concluded the **first Global Stocktake**.
COP29 (**Baku**) = "Finance COP": **NCQG**.
COP30 (**Belém**) = **Belém Political Package**.

n05e997f2590.s: COP8 was held in New Delhi in 2002 and adopted the:
o: Delhi Ministerial Declaration on Climate Change and Sustainable Development
BRICS Leaders' Framework Declaration on Climate Finance
n05e997f2590.x: COP8, held in New Delhi in 2002, adopted the Delhi Ministerial Declaration on Climate Change and Sustainable Development.
n05e997f2590.tq: Link the COP edition, host city and outcome in one factual recall question.
xs: COP8 (**New Delhi, 2002**) adopted the **Delhi Ministerial Declaration on Climate Change and Sustainable Development** — option **(2)**.
The **Paris Agreement** came from **COP21 (2015)**; the **Glasgow Climate Pact** from **COP26 (2021)**.
The **BRICS Leaders' Framework Declaration on Climate Finance** was adopted at **Rio, July 2025**.
xa: COP8 is the **only COP hosted by India**.
India launched **CDRI** at the **UN Climate Action Summit, 2019 (New York)**.
The **G20 New Delhi Summit (9-10 Sept 2023)** adopted the **Green Development Pact**.

n60c58cee284.s: COP30, held at Belem in Brazil in 2025, was described as the:
n60c58cee284.x: COP30 at Belem, Brazil, in 2025 was described as the “COP of Implementation”.
n60c58cee284.tq: Recall the official descriptive label associated with the conference.
xs: **COP30 (Belém, Brazil, 2025)** was called the "**Implementation COP**" — the **COP of Implementation** — option **(1)**.
It was also called the "**COP of Truth**" and was the **first COP in the Amazon**.
xa: Its outcome was the **Belém Political Package**, in a "mutirao" spirit, with **6 thematic axes**.
COP29 (**Baku**) was the "**Finance COP**"; COP32 (**Addis Ababa**) is the "**Africa COP**".
India delivered its COP30 National Statement on **17 Nov 2025**.

n48488ec230f.s: Which of the following was a historic outcome of COP27 held at Sharm el-Sheikh?
o: Adoption of the UAE Consensus calling for transition away from fossil fuels
Establishment of loss and damage funding arrangements, including a fund
Creation of the Joint Crediting Mechanism between India and Japan
Conclusion of the first Global Stocktake
n48488ec230f.x: COP27 produced a historic decision to establish loss and damage funding arrangements, including a fund. The UAE Consensus and the first Global Stocktake were outcomes of COP28.
n48488ec230f.tq: Distinguish COP27 outcomes from the later COP28 outcomes.
xs: COP27 (**Sharm el-Sheikh, 2022**) took the historic decision to **establish loss and damage funding arrangements, including a fund** — option **(2)**.
The **UAE Consensus** and the **first Global Stocktake** belong to **COP28 (Dubai, 2023)**.
The India-Japan **Joint Crediting Mechanism** was signed in **Aug 2025** under **Art. 6.2**, not at a COP.
xa: This decision is part of the **Sharm el-Sheikh Implementation Plan**.
COP27 reaffirmed **well below 2°C** + pursuit of **1.5°C**.
The **Loss and Damage Fund** was operationalised at **COP28** and opened to applications at **COP30**.

n262384a74a4.s: Which of the following correctly describes the UAE Consensus adopted at COP28?
o: It replaced nationally determined contributions with legally fixed national quotas.
It was the first decision to establish the Kyoto Protocol’s CDM.
It limited the Global Stocktake to once every ten years.
It was the first COP decision calling for transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems.
n262384a74a4.x: The UAE Consensus was the first COP decision calling for a transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems. It also followed the conclusion of the first Global Stocktake at COP28.
n262384a74a4.tq: Identify the distinctive wording of the COP28 decision and reject substitutions from Kyoto or Paris procedures.
xs: The **UAE Consensus** was the **first COP decision** calling for "**transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems**" — option **(4)**.
The **CDM** is a **Kyoto** mechanism, and the **Global Stocktake** is every **5 years**, so options (2) and (3) are wrong.
**NDC targets** remain **nationally determined**, not fixed quotas.
xa: The UAE Consensus followed the **first Global Stocktake**, which found the world "**severely off-track**".
COP28 (**Dubai, 2023**) also **operationalised the Loss and Damage Fund**.
COP28 pledges: **triple renewables** and **double efficiency gains** by **2030**.

nbd1db14be91.s: Which of the following correctly describes COP30?
o: It was held at Baku and finalised the Paris rulebook.
It was held at Belém, was the first COP in the Amazon and was called the COP of Truth.
It was held at Antalya and was designated the Africa COP.
It was held at Glasgow and adopted the Glasgow Climate Pact.
nbd1db14be91.x: COP30 was held at Belém, Brazil, in 2025. It was the first COP in the Amazon and was called the COP of Truth.
nbd1db14be91.tq: Combine host, distinctive title and geographical description in one identification question.
xs: **COP30** was held at **Belém**, the **first COP in the Amazon**, and was called the "**COP of Truth**" — option **(2)**.
**Baku** hosted **COP29**; **Antalya** hosts **COP31**, while the **Africa COP** is **COP32** at **Addis Ababa**.
**Glasgow** hosted **COP26** and its **Glasgow Climate Pact**.
xa: COP30 was also called the "**Implementation COP**".
Outcome: **Belém Political Package** with **6 thematic axes**.
India joined the **TFFF** only as an **observer** at COP30.

n07526291591.s: The Loss and Damage Fund was:
o: created at COP27 and made operational at COP28
created at COP21 and made operational at COP22
created in 1991 and made operational in 2001
created under the Montreal Protocol and made operational at COP29
n07526291591.x: The Loss and Damage Fund was created at COP27 and became operational at COP28.
n07526291591.tq: Arrange the creation and operationalisation conferences rather than confusing them with the Paris Agreement timeline.
xs: The Loss and Damage Fund was **created at COP27** and **made operational at COP28** — option **(1)**.
**COP21** adopted the Paris Agreement; **1991** is the GEF's founding year.
xa: **COP30 opened the fund to applications**, but capitalisation remains small.
**World Bank** = interim host and trustee until **COP33 (2028)**.
Climate justice: the fund is seen as an **ethical win**.

ne0ef5b423dd.s: The Loss and Damage Fund covers losses arising from:
o: Both economic and non-economic losses from sudden- and slow-onset events
ne0ef5b423dd.x: The Fund covers economic and non-economic losses resulting from both sudden-onset and slow-onset events.
ne0ef5b423dd.tq: Check both dimensions of the coverage instead of accepting an ‘only’ statement.
xs: The fund covers **economic and non-economic losses** from both **sudden- and slow-onset events** — option **(4)**.
It is not limited to one type of event or to insured losses.
xa: Created at **COP27 (2022)**, operationalised at **COP28 (2023)**.
Start-up phase: **Barbados Implementation Modalities**.
**World Bank** is interim host and trustee.

nb24a77165e7.s: The International Drought Resilience Alliance was launched at which event and by which countries?
o: The Rio Earth Summit; India and Brazil
nb24a77165e7.x: The International Drought Resilience Alliance was launched at COP27 by Spain and Senegal.
nb24a77165e7.tq: Match the initiative with its launch forum and founding countries.
xs: The **International Drought Resilience Alliance** was launched at **COP27** by **Spain and Senegal** — option **(1)**.
COP26 launches include the **Global Methane Pledge** (USA and EU) and **Glasgow Breakthroughs** (UK-led).
xa: The **Global Shield against Climate Risks** was also launched at COP27, by **G7 and V20**.
COP27 also created **loss and damage funding arrangements**.
**AWARe** was COP27's water initiative.

n9e43d9a318d.s: At COP26, India advocated which formulation regarding unabated coal power?
n9e43d9a318d.x: India advocated a phase-down, rather than a phase-out, of unabated coal power at COP26.
n9e43d9a318d.tq: Distinguish the closely related terms ‘phase-down’ and ‘phase-out’.
xs: India pushed "**phase down**" (not phase out) of **unabated coal** at **COP26** — option **(2)**.
The **Glasgow Climate Pact** carried the coal **"phase-down"** language.
xa: India also announced **Panchamrit** at COP26.
India relies on **clean-coal technology** and **CCS/CCUS**.
COP27's **Mitigation Work Programme** also called to phase down unabated coal.

n22a0cb2bc1a.s: India's position regarding the NCQG was that the core target of US$300 billion per year was:
o: More than sufficient for developing countries
n22a0cb2bc1a.x: India criticised the US$300 billion annual NCQG target as inadequate.
n22a0cb2bc1a.tq: Use the stated evaluation of the finance target rather than its amount alone.
xs: India **criticised the NCQG as inadequate** — option **(1)**.
The **$300 bn** goal was widely called **insufficient** by developing nations.
It is not legally binding on all countries — it is a goal for **developed countries** to mobilise.
xa: NCQG core: **US$300 billion/year by 2035**, replacing the **$100 billion** goal.
Broader non-binding call: **US$1.3 trillion/year** by **2035**.
At **Bonn SB64 (Jun 2026)** India sought an agenda on developed-country finance obligations.

na333ca2e309.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a mitigation constraint for India?
o: India's complete freedom from dependence on coal
Insufficient availability of appropriate alternative technologies
Need for growth and industrialisation for a large population in poverty
Inability to invest huge funds in research and development
na333ca2e309.x: India remains dependent on coal, so complete freedom from coal dependence is not a stated condition. Limited availability of alternatives, restricted R&D capacity and development needs are recognised constraints.
na333ca2e309.tq: Reject the absolute statement that contradicts the stated constraint.
xs: "**Complete freedom from dependence on coal**" is not a constraint — India **depends on coal** — option **(1)**.
Accepted constraints (UPSC 2010): **appropriate alternative technologies are not sufficiently available** and India **cannot invest huge funds in R&D**.
**Development first**: a large population in poverty needs growth and room to industrialise.
xa: India's coal measures: **clean-coal technology** and **CCS/CCUS**.
Outcome: **net zero by 2070**, later than **2050** of most developed countries.

n8cc1e059d31.s: Which of the following is NOT a coal-related technology or measure listed in the context of India's mitigation approach?
n8cc1e059d31.x: India's listed coal-related measures include coal washing, electrostatic precipitators, coal gasification, wet scrubbers, low-NOx burners and CCS/CCUS. Ocean fertilisation is not among them.
n8cc1e059d31.tq: Find the unrelated technology among measures belonging to the same mitigation cluster.
xs: **Ocean fertilisation** is not in India's coal-related list — option **(4)**.
Listed **clean-coal technology**: **coal washing, electrostatic precipitators, coal gasification, wet scrubbers, low-NOx burners**.
xa: India also lists **CCS/CCUS**.
LINGO "carbon bombs": **Gevra** (Chhattisgarh) and **Rajmahal** (Jharkhand).
India pushed coal "**phase down**" at **COP26**.

n5ba1d804340.s: India's target of net-zero emissions by 2070 is later than the 2050 target of most developed countries primarily because of its
o: development needs and continuing dependence on coal
n5ba1d804340.x: India links its later net-zero target to development priorities, a large population needing growth and industrialisation, and continuing coal dependence.
n5ba1d804340.tq: Connect the stated socioeconomic and energy constraints to the policy timeline.
xs: India's **net zero by 2070** reflects its **development needs** and continuing **coal dependence** — option **(2)**.
A large population in poverty needs growth and room to industrialise.
xa: Most developed countries target **2050**.
The 2070 target is criticised as late; India defends it on **CBDR** and development grounds.
India's per capita emissions are **much lower** than those of developed countries.

na72bd393680.s: The 12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting held in New Delhi described CBAM as
na72bd393680.x: The 12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi, during India's chairmanship, called CBAM unilateral, punitive, discriminatory and protectionist.
na72bd393680.tq: Recall the exact cluster of descriptive terms used in the declaration.
xs: The **12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting, New Delhi** called CBAM "**unilateral, punitive, discriminatory and protectionist**" — option **(3)**.
It was held under **India's chair** on **19 Aug 2026**.
xa: BRICS sees **EU CBAM** as **sidestepping UNFCCC principles**.
CBAM's **definitive phase** began on **1 January 2026**.
The **BRICS Leaders' Framework Declaration on Climate Finance** came at **Rio, July 2025**.

n6be1880fe51.s: Mission LiFE, associated with India's climate contribution, primarily seeks to promote:
n6be1880fe51.x: Mission LiFE is India's idea-level contribution centred on individual behaviour change.
n6be1880fe51.tq: Infer the central objective from the nature of the mission rather than its launch venue.
xs: **Mission LiFE** promotes **individual behaviour change** — option **(3)**.
It is not a treaty or carbon-trading mechanism.
xa: It was **announced at COP26** and **launched October 2022**.
COP26 also saw India announce **Panchamrit**.
India's other institutions: **ISA (2015)** and **CDRI (2019)**.

nenvironment-4-10.s: What is the goal of the New York Declaration on Forests?
o: To regulate persistent organic pollutants globally
To halt or reduce global forest loss
nenvironment-4-10.x: The New York Declaration on Forests aims to halt or reduce global forest loss.
n: The goal of the New York Declaration on Forests is to halt or reduce global forest loss. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
xs: The goal of the **New York Declaration on Forests** is to **halt or reduce global forest loss** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Operational hydrology** is a **WMO** focus; **mercury** is the **Minamata Convention**; **POPs** are the **Stockholm Convention**.
The Declaration was first endorsed at the **UN Climate Summit, 2014**.
xa: It is **voluntary** and **non-legally binding**.
India was **not** an initial signatory.
**CCAC** (launched **2012** by **UNEP**) targets **short-lived climate pollutants**.

nf3044241cb1.s: Which one of the following was agreed at COP30?
o: To replace the Paris Agreement with the Belém Protocol
To work towards at least tripling adaptation finance
To make the Copenhagen Accord legally binding
To create the Loss and Damage Fund for the first time
nf3044241cb1.x: COP30 agreed to work towards at least tripling adaptation finance. The Loss and Damage Fund had been created at COP27.
nf3044241cb1.tq: Distinguish a COP30 finance decision from earlier COP outcomes.
xs: COP30 agreed to work towards **at least tripling adaptation finance** — option **(2)**.
The **Loss and Damage Fund** was created at **COP27**, not COP30 — COP30 **opened it to applications**.
The **Copenhagen Accord** (COP15) remains a **political, non-binding** accord.
xa: COP30 adaptation finance target: **US$120 billion/year**.
**59 voluntary indicators** were adopted under the **Global Goal on Adaptation**.
**Belem 4x pledge**: quadruple sustainable fuels by **2035**.

nc7329d27c7f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Green Climate Fund?
o: It is headquartered in Washington, D.C.
It is described as the largest dedicated climate fund
It is an operating entity of the UNFCCC financial mechanism
nc7329d27c7f.x: The GCF is headquartered at Songdo, Incheon, not Washington, D.C.
xa: The GCF was set up in **2010** by UNFCCC parties.
⚠ GCF board **24**; Loss and Damage Fund board **26**.
**NABARD** is a Direct Access Entity of the GCF.

n5a69b0bb739.s: Which institution serves as the interim host and trustee of the Loss and Damage Fund?
n5a69b0bb739.x: The World Bank is the interim host and trustee of the Fund for four years, until COP33 in 2028.
n5a69b0bb739.tq: Apply the ‘who performs this function?’ institutional trap.
xs: The **World Bank** is the **interim host and trustee** of the Loss and Damage Fund — option **(1)**.
It holds the role for **four years** until **COP33 (2028)**.
xa: The fund's **26-member Board** decides by **consensus**.
Nepal sought aid from the fund after an **Aug 2026** glacial-collapse flood.
The **GCF** is a separate fund with HQ at **Songdo**.

naa0a1fe69cc.s: The Board of the Loss and Damage Fund has how many members?
naa0a1fe69cc.x: The Board has 26 members: 14 from developing and 12 from developed countries, deciding by consensus.
xa: ⚠ GCF board **24**; FRLD board **26**.
Interim host and trustee: **World Bank**, until **COP33 (2028)**.
It covers **economic and non-economic** losses.

ne1900163753.s: India argues that developed countries should provide which of the following for its transition to cleaner development?
o: A waiver from all environmental obligations
Only military technology and concessional food aid
Clean and affordable technology and finance
ne1900163753.x: India argues that developed countries should provide clean, affordable technology and finance to support the transition.
ne1900163753.tq: Identify the policy demand that directly connects technology with finance.
xs: India argues developed countries must provide **clean, affordable technology and finance** — option **(3)**.
This follows **CBDR-RC**: developed countries must take the lead.
xa: India seeks room to industrialise — **carbon space**.
India criticised the **NCQG** as inadequate.
The **unmet $100 bn** promise eroded finance trust.

n14e461e23e0.s: The International Solar Alliance, the first intergovernmental body headquartered in India, is at:
n14e461e23e0.x: The ISA is headquartered at Gurugram.
xa: CDRI: **2019**, **New Delhi**.
US exit memorandum covers **UNFCCC, IPCC, ISA and IRENA**.
COP21 (**Paris**) also adopted the **Paris Agreement**.

n6526317d69d.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the European Green Deal?
o: A voluntary forest declaration adopted at the 2014 UN Climate Summit
A UNFCCC mechanism for financing adaptation in least developed countries
A plan of the European Union to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, with Farm to Fork as a component
A scientific assessment programme jointly run by WMO and UNEP
n6526317d69d.x: The European Green Deal is an EU plan for net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. The Farm to Fork strategy is one of its components.
n6526317d69d.tq: Use the exact objective and institutional identity to distinguish the initiative from nearby climate mechanisms.
xs: The **European Green Deal** is the EU plan for **net-zero GHG by 2050**, with **Farm to Fork** as a component — option **(3)**.
The **2014** voluntary forest declaration is the **New York Declaration on Forests**.
The WMO-UNEP body is the **IPCC**, an assessment body.
xa: APPSC **2024** key: statements **1, 2 and 4** correct on the Green Deal.
The EU also runs **CBAM**, a carbon levy on imports.
India's own net-zero target is **2070**.

n0b316309652.s: The principal aim of the Early Warnings for All initiative, commonly abbreviated as EW4All, is to provide universal early-warning coverage by:
n0b316309652.x: EW4All aims to achieve universal early-warning coverage by 2027.
n0b316309652.tq: Use the year-specific numerical recall pattern and compare the closely spaced distractor years.
xs: **EW4All (Early Warnings for All)** aims at **universal early-warning coverage by 2027** — option **(2)**.
**2030** and **2035** are dates of other goals (e.g. the Methane Pledge, NCQG).
xa: **CCAC** (launched **2012** by **UNEP** and six countries) targets short-lived climate pollutants.
**MARS** is UNEP's methane satellite alert system.
India launched **CDRI** in **2019**.

n5cf58fe67c5.s: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) was established in 1988 by:
o: UNESCO and the International Union for Conservation of Nature
UNDP and the International Energy Agency
UNEP and the World Meteorological Organization
n5cf58fe67c5.x: The IPCC was set up in 1988 by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).
n5cf58fe67c5.tq: Apply the institution-founder trap by distinguishing the IPCC’s founding bodies from other environmental organisations.
xs: The IPCC was set up in **1988** by **UNEP** and the **World Meteorological Organization (WMO)** — option **(4)**.
It is not a UNFCCC or World Bank body; its secretariat is in **Geneva**.
xa: It has **195** member countries.
It won the **2007 Nobel Peace Prize**, shared with **Al Gore**.
The **CCAC** was launched in **2012** by **UNEP** and six countries.

n594c5154206.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the IPCC?
o: It conducts original research independently of published literature
Its reports are policy-relevant but not policy-prescriptive
It shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore
n594c5154206.x: The IPCC does not conduct original research; it assesses published literature.
xa: Each report carries a **Summary for Policymakers (SPM)**.
Set up **1988** by **WMO** and **UNEP**; secretariat **Geneva**.
Besides three WGs it has a **Task Force on National Greenhouse Gas Inventories**.

nc8bf37460a7.s: The secretariat of the IPCC is located in:
nc8bf37460a7.x: The IPCC secretariat is located in Geneva.
nc8bf37460a7.tq: Use location discrimination to distinguish the IPCC secretariat from the UNFCCC secretariat in Bonn.
xs: The IPCC secretariat is in **Geneva** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **Bonn** hosts the **UNFCCC** secretariat, not the IPCC.
xa: The IPCC was set up in **1988** by **WMO** and **UNEP**.
It has **195** member countries.
The **GEF** HQ is **Washington DC**; the **GCF** HQ is **Songdo**.

n68ffa2d711d.s: Each IPCC assessment report is accompanied by a ____ that presents its findings for policymakers.
n68ffa2d711d.x: The Summary for Policymakers accompanies each assessment report; it is not a legally binding instrument.
xa: The IPCC **assesses** published literature.
The IPCC's secretariat is in **Geneva**.
SR1.5 and AR6 are the **agreed scientific baseline** for UNFCCC/COP negotiations.

n53df8a31570.s: The IPCC SR1.5 pathways require net CO2 emissions to fall about 45% by 2030 from ____ levels.
n53df8a31570.x: The 45% cut by 2030 is measured from 2010 levels; SR1.5 was released in October 2018 and reaches net zero around 2050.
xa: SR1.5: human activity has already caused ~**1.0°C** warming.
Cuts must be **deep, rapid and sustained**.
Exam angle: fill-in-the-blanks on "**2030-2052**", "**45% by 2030 from 2010**" and "**net zero by 2050**".

n504dd657be1.s: Which approach is inconsistent with the mitigation pathways described for limiting warming to 1.5°C?
n504dd657be1.x: The pathways require cuts that are deep, rapid and sustained; gradual or limited cuts are not sufficient.
n504dd657be1.tq: Find the option that reverses the required characteristics of mitigation.
xs: **Gradual or limited emission cuts** are not enough for 1.5°C — option **(4)**.
SR1.5 pathways need cuts that are **deep, rapid and sustained**.
xa: Net human-caused CO2 must fall ~**45% from 2010 levels by 2030**.
**Net zero around 2050**.
AR6: emissions must **peak before 2025**.

n77332b9e93b.s: Without immediate, deep emission cuts, the 1.5°C threshold is likely to be crossed in the:
n77332b9e93b.x: The AR6 assessment states that the 1.5°C threshold is likely to be crossed in the early 2030s without immediate, deep cuts.
n77332b9e93b.tq: Distinguish the near-term threshold crossing from the longer net-zero horizon.
xs: Without immediate, deep cuts the **1.5°C** threshold is likely crossed in the **early 2030s** — option **(2)**.
This is an **AR6 Synthesis Report** finding.
xa: Emissions must **peak before 2025**, with **net zero by mid-century**.
Surface temperature is already **1.1°C** above pre-industrial.
There is **no plausible path below 1.5°C without overshoot**.

n232741a1cc0.s: In the AR6 mitigation pathway, renewables provide what share of global electricity by 2050?
n232741a1cc0.x: The pathway needs emissions to peak before 2025, net zero by mid-century and 70–85% renewable electricity by 2050.
xa: **1.5°C** likely crossed in the **early 2030s** without deep cuts.
Carbon budget: ~**500 GtCO2** from **2020** for a **50%** chance of 1.5°C.
SR1.5: CO2 to fall ~**45%** from **2010** levels by **2030**.

nd51d162350e.s: As cited in the IPCC AR6 India-relevant findings, the Gangotri Glacier has retreated by about:
nd51d162350e.x: Gangotri has retreated about 1,700 m since 1935. 170 m since 1990, 17 km since 1850 and 700 m since 2000 misstate both the distance and the base year.
xs: The **Gangotri Glacier** has retreated about **1,700 m since 1935** — option **(1)**.
The other options alter both the distance and the base year.
xa: Black carbon on snow **lowers albedo** → faster melting.
Himalayan high mountains are warming at **twice the global average**.
Nepal sought loss-and-damage aid after an **Aug 2026** glacial-collapse flood.

nbcb20471fa4.s: Shared Socioeconomic Pathways in AR6 replaced which set of scenarios used in AR5?
nbcb20471fa4.x: SSPs replaced the four Representative Concentration Pathways, or RCPs, used in AR5.
nbcb20471fa4.tq: Discriminate between scenario frameworks and climate-policy principles.
xs: SSPs replaced the four **Representative Concentration Pathways (RCPs)** of **AR5** — option **(1)**.
**NDCs** are national pledges and **CBDR** is a UNFCCC principle — neither is a scenario set.
xa: **RCP8.5** was introduced in **2011** as one of the four RCPs.
SSP narratives: **SSP1** Sustainability, **SSP2** Middle of the road, **SSP3** Regional rivalry, **SSP4** Inequality, **SSP5** Fossil-fuelled development.

nce98c3251e9.s: The IPCC Seventh Assessment Report (AR7) cycle began in:
nce98c3251e9.x: AR7 began in July 2023; Working Group reports are expected from about mid-2028.
xa: The cycle takes ~**7-8 years**, so **AR6 remains the current authority**.
The **AR6 Synthesis Report** came on **20 Mar 2023**.

nenvironment-4-4.s: Where is the headquarters of the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) located?
nenvironment-4-4.x: The WMO, a UN agency for weather and water, is headquartered in Geneva.
nenvironment-4-4.tq: Match each institution to its city.
n: The headquarters of the World Meteorological Organization is in Geneva, Switzerland. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #4 · pp 8-10]
xs: The **WMO** headquarters is in **Geneva, Switzerland** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It focuses on **meteorology** and **operational hydrology**.
It originated as the **International Meteorological Organization** (**1873**); WMO **formally established** in **1951**.
xa: The **IPCC** was set up in **1988** by **WMO** and **UNEP**; its Secretariat is also in **Geneva**.
The **UNFCCC Secretariat** is in **Bonn, Germany**.
The IPCC shared the **2007 Nobel Peace Prize** with **Al Gore**.

n17524443cc1.s: The Global Environment Facility finances which of the following groups of conventions and frameworks?
o: Only the CBD and Ramsar Convention
Only the UNFCCC and Paris Agreement
UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD, Stockholm Convention and Minamata Convention
Kyoto Protocol, CITES and Montreal Protocol exclusively
n17524443cc1.x: The GEF finances the UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD, Stockholm Convention and Minamata Convention, among others. It also houses the Global Biodiversity Framework Fund.
n17524443cc1.tq: Use the complete institutional portfolio against options that incorrectly restrict the body to one treaty.
xs: The GEF finances the **UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD, Stockholm Convention and Minamata Convention**, among others — option **(3)**.
It is not limited to one or two conventions.
xa: GEF: founded **1991**; HQ **Washington DC**.
It houses the **GBF Fund** (Global Biodiversity Framework Fund).
**Minamata Convention (2013)** deals with **mercury**.

ne41ae7eeb64.s: The sector goals of the Glasgow Breakthroughs include all of the following EXCEPT:
ne41ae7eeb64.x: The Glasgow Breakthroughs cover power, road transport, steel, hydrogen and agriculture. Mercury management is associated with the Minamata Convention, not the Glasgow Breakthroughs.
ne41ae7eeb64.tq: Find the item that belongs to a different environmental treaty or subject.
xs: **Mercury management** is not a Glasgow Breakthrough goal — option **(3)**.
The **Glasgow Breakthroughs** set goals for **power, road transport, steel, hydrogen and agriculture**.
Mercury is the subject of the **Minamata Convention (2013)**.
xa: The Glasgow Breakthroughs were launched at **COP26**, led by the **UK** with world leaders.
COP26 also produced the **Glasgow Climate Pact** with coal "**phase-down**" language.
India announced **Panchamrit** at COP26.

n65c01b2d4ca.s: Which one of the following treaties is NOT primarily concerned with reducing greenhouse-gas emissions?
n65c01b2d4ca.x: The Basel Convention concerns the transboundary movement of hazardous waste, not greenhouse-gas reduction. The UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement address greenhouse-gas emissions and climate change.
n65c01b2d4ca.tq: Find the treaty whose environmental objective belongs to hazardous-waste management rather than climate mitigation.
xs: The **Basel Convention** deals with transboundary movement of **hazardous waste**, **not GHGs** — option **(4)**.
The **UNFCCC**, **Kyoto Protocol (1997)** and **Paris Agreement (2015)** all aim to **reduce GHG emissions**.
xa: This was the **APPSC 2025** key.
⚠ **Rotterdam** = prior informed consent; **Minamata** = mercury.
The **Montreal Protocol** addresses GHGs only indirectly: CFCs are GHGs and **Kigali** targets HFCs.

n59f2771349f.s: The Kigali Amendment (2016) is an amendment to which treaty, and what does it target?
o: Minamata Convention; mercury in dental amalgam
n59f2771349f.x: The Kigali Amendment (2016) to the Montreal Protocol phases down HFCs, which is why Montreal indirectly addresses GHGs. Kyoto has no Kigali amendment (CFCs are Montreal's), Basel deals with hazardous waste and Minamata with mercury.
xs: The **Kigali Amendment (2016)** to the **Montreal Protocol** targets the **phase-down of HFCs** — option **(1)**.
Kyoto has no Kigali amendment; **Basel** deals with **hazardous waste** and **Minamata** with **mercury**.
xa: This is why Montreal **indirectly** addresses GHGs: CFCs are GHGs, and Kigali targets HFCs.
**HFCs** are also among the **six Kyoto gases**.
The Montreal Protocol dates from **1987**.

n5f755a24d70.s: Persons displaced by sea-level rise are, as a category, outside the scope of the:
n5f755a24d70.x: Climate refugees displaced by sea-level rise fall outside the legal scope of the 1951 Refugee Convention.
n5f755a24d70.tq: Distinguish a climate-migration issue from the climate treaties themselves.
xs: Sea-level-rise refugees fall **outside the 1951 Refugee Convention** — option **(4)**.
The notes treat this as a comparative gap in international law.
xa: **Sea-level rise** threatens **Mumbai and Chennai** (AR6).
**AOSIS** small island states press for **1.5°C**.
SROCC: sea level rising from **thermal expansion and ice melt**.

n610061b2d18.s: CITES, known as the Washington Convention, was signed in:
n610061b2d18.x: CITES regulates international trade in endangered species and was signed in 1973.
xa: ⚠ One source (APP) says **1963** — the correct year is **1973**.
**Ramsar (1971, Iran)** = wetlands; **CBD (1992, Rio)** = biodiversity.
**Basel** = hazardous waste; **Rotterdam** = prior informed consent; **Minamata** = mercury.

nf7e12798aa2.s: India did not sign the Global Methane Pledge and stayed out of the:
o: Glasgow Leaders' Declaration on Forests and Land Use
nf7e12798aa2.x: India stayed out of the Glasgow Leaders' Declaration on Forests and Land Use and the COP28 renewables pledge, and did not sign the Methane Pledge.
xa: Global Methane Pledge: launched at **COP26** by **USA and EU**; **30%** cut by **2030**.
India joined the **TFFF** only as an **observer** at COP30.
At COP26 India announced **Panchamrit**.

nf33c904c7a6.s: India's bid to host COP33, later withdrawn in April 2026, was announced at:
nf33c904c7a6.x: The PM announced the COP33 bid at COP28 on 1 December 2023; it was withdrawn in April 2026.
xa: The withdrawal letter was dated **2 Apr 2026** and reported **9 Apr 2026**.
**BRICS** had welcomed the bid in **July 2025**.
**South Korea** is now the only Asia-Pacific contender.

nb8c8997db63.s: The European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) applies to imports including
o: iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity
only crude oil and natural gas
nb8c8997db63.x: CBAM covers imports of iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity.
nb8c8997db63.tq: Recall the complete sector list rather than selecting a partial or unrelated list.
xs: CBAM covers **iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity** — option **(2)**.
It is an **EU carbon levy on imports** in these carbon-intensive sectors.
xa: Transitional phase from **2023**; **definitive phase from 1 January 2026**.
India says it **raises export costs for steel and aluminium**.
CBAM aims to prevent **carbon leakage**.

nb93f0d00c0a.s: India has criticised the EU CBAM mainly on the ground that it
o: eliminates all export costs for Indian producers
supports CBDR-RC and strengthens climate equity
violates CBDR-RC and represents green protectionism
applies only to domestic European production
nb93f0d00c0a.x: India argues that CBAM violates the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) and amounts to green protectionism.
nb93f0d00c0a.tq: Distinguish India's criticism from the stated purpose of the EU measure.
xs: India says CBAM **violates CBDR-RC** and is **green protectionism** — option **(3)**.
It **raises export costs** for Indian **steel and aluminium**, rather than eliminating them, and applies to **imports**.
xa: India fears **others may copy it**.
The **12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting** (New Delhi) called CBAM "**unilateral, punitive, discriminatory and protectionist**".
CBDR-RC = **Principle 7** (Rio) = **Article 3.1** (UNFCCC) = **Article 2.2** (Paris).

n04032145d45.s: India defends its net-zero target on the grounds of CBDR and development. The target year is:
n04032145d45.x: India's net-zero target is 2070, criticised as late but defended on CBDR and development grounds.
xa: A large population in poverty needs **growth** and room to industrialise.
India depends on **coal**; it uses clean-coal technology and **CCS/CCUS**.
India's NDC targets **47% by 2035**.

n95185db1c9f.s: What was the base year adopted for India's Nationally Determined Contributions relating to the reduction of emissions intensity?
n95185db1c9f.x: India's NDC commitments on emissions intensity use 2005 as the base year.
n95185db1c9f.tq: Direct recall of the base year.
xs: India's NDC emissions-intensity targets use **2005** as the base year — option **(2)**.
The target year is **2030** (APPSC 2019 asked the base year).
xa: India achieved a **36%** cut by **2020**.

n8ad3bfe1ca8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's 2015 INDC?
o: It targeted about 40% of installed electric capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030
It targeted 40% of total electricity generation from non-fossil sources by 2030
It proposed an additional carbon sink of 2.5–3 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2030
It targeted a 33–35% emissions-intensity reduction by 2030
n8ad3bfe1ca8.x: The 40% target concerned installed capacity, not actual electricity generation.
xa: ⚠ Some notes write "30-35%" and "40% of power generation"; correct = **33-35%** and **installed capacity**.
NDC 3.0 raises the sink to **3.5-4.0 bn t CO2e**; **2.29 bn t** added so far.

nb158aa06db2.s: India's updated NDC, which formalised the Panchamrit and added Mission LiFE, was communicated in:
nb158aa06db2.x: The updated NDC was communicated in August 2022 with a 45% emissions-intensity target for 2030.
xa: The Aug 2022 intensity target of **45%** was asked in **APPSC 2022**.
The 2022 non-fossil capacity target is **50%**.

nf7250f060b3.s: India's emissions intensity of GDP had fallen by what percentage below the 2005 level by 2020?
nf7250f060b3.x: India achieved a 36% reduction in emissions intensity of GDP below the 2005 level by 2020.
nf7250f060b3.tq: Direct recall of a progress figure, separated from the 2030 target figures.
xs: India's emissions intensity fell **36%** below **2005** levels by **2020** — option **(3)**.
**33%** is the lower end of the **2015** target; **45%** is the **2022** target for 2030.
xa: Panchamrit pledge 4: cut emissions intensity **45%** from 2005 by **2030**.
BTR1: **over 20%** of 2022 emissions came from industry.

n7b162fa6154.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's non-fossil electricity position?
o: More than 50% of installed capacity was non-fossil by 2025
The non-fossil generation share necessarily equals its installed-capacity share
Limited storage keeps the non-fossil generation share low
About 25% of electricity generated was non-fossil
n7b162fa6154.x: Installed capacity and actual generation are different measures, so their shares need not be equal.
xa: The **National Generation Adequacy Plan** expects **70%** of **1,121 GW** non-fossil by **2035-36**.
BESS under implementation: **43 GWh** by **2028**.

n5faab36e0fb.s: The Panchamrit commitment to meet 50 per cent of energy requirements from renewables has the target year:
n5faab36e0fb.x: The 50 per cent renewables target is for 2030; 2070 applies to the net-zero commitment.
xa: It was achieved in **June 2025**; ~**51%** by **Sept 2025**.
Only ~**25%** of power generated is non-fossil.

n545b372c99d.s: Which two Panchamrit commitments entered India's August 2022 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)?
o: 500 GW non-fossil capacity and net zero by 2070
45 percent emissions-intensity reduction and 50 percent renewable-energy commitment
One billion tonnes reduction and 500 GW capacity
Net zero by 2070 and one billion tonnes reduction
n545b372c99d.x: The 45 percent emissions-intensity reduction commitment and the 50 percent renewable-energy commitment entered the August 2022 NDC.
n545b372c99d.tq: Identify the two medium-term percentage pledges rather than the capacity, reduction-volume or long-term pledge.
xs: The **45%** intensity cut and **50%** renewable-energy pledges entered the **Aug 2022 NDC** — option **(2)**.
**500 GW**, **1 billion tonnes** and **net zero 2070** stayed outside the NDC.
xa: The 2022 NDC also added **Mission LiFE** as a qualitative element.
Panchamrit was announced at **COP26** on **1 Nov 2021**.
India's **LT-LEDS** was submitted at **COP27 (Nov 2022)**.

ne02372662f7.s: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme was designed to contribute to which intensity-reduction target?
ne02372662f7.x: The scheme was designed to meet the 45 percent intensity target.
ne02372662f7.tq: Use the nearby percentage figures as a numerical discrimination test.
xs: The CCTS was designed to meet the **45 percent** intensity target — option **(3)**.
The **45%** target (from **2005**) is in the **Aug 2022** NDC and Panchamrit.
xa: NDC 3.0 raises it to **47%** by **2035**.
India achieved **36%** by **2020**.
CCTS is **intensity-based**, not cap-based.

n20ac654b0b6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's negotiating stance on climate change?
o: India invokes equity and climate justice
India rejects the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities
NDC 3.0 is framed around continuity and incremental advance
NDC 3.0 stays within India's equitable share
n20ac654b0b6.x: India supports CBDR-RC; it does not reject it.
xa: India relies mainly on **domestic resources (about 83%)** for climate finance.
At **Bonn SB64** India sought an agenda item on developed-country finance obligations.

n39a039ad62d.s: The principal criticism concerning the capacity-versus-generation gap is that:
o: Installed capacity alone does not indicate the actual electricity generated
Renewable capacity cannot be measured in gigawatts
Generation is always greater than installed capacity
n39a039ad62d.x: The criticism is that capacity figures may overstate the transition unless actual electricity generation is also considered.
n39a039ad62d.tq: Translate a policy debate into its practical implication.
xs: **Installed capacity** does not show the **electricity actually generated** — option **(1)**.
Non-fossil **capacity** crossed **50%**, but only ~**25%** of power **generated** is non-fossil, due to **storage shortage**.
xa: NDC 3.0 is called easily achievable, but **generation, not capacity**, is what counts.
The NDC target is non-fossil **installed capacity**, not generation.

nfaee4217b50.s: The Intended Nationally Determined Contribution (INDC) of India was submitted to the UNFCCC in:
nfaee4217b50.x: India submitted its INDC to the UNFCCC in October 2015, before the Paris Climate Change Conference, COP21.
nfaee4217b50.tq: Distinguish the submission date and its position relative to COP21.
xs: India submitted its **INDC** to the UNFCCC in **October 2015**, **before COP21** — option **(4)**.
**August 2022** is when the **updated NDC** was communicated.
xa: In the INDC, **four of the eight NAPCC missions** focus on adaptation.
INDC targets: **33-35%** intensity cut and about **40%** non-fossil **installed capacity** by 2030.
**MoEFCC** prepares NDCs; the **Union Cabinet** approves them.

n0c7730dc6d4.s: Who prepares India's NDCs and who gives their final approval?
o: NITI Aayog prepares them and Parliament approves them
The UNFCCC prepares them and MoEFCC approves them
MoEFCC prepares them and the Union Cabinet gives final approval
The Ministry of Power prepares them and the President approves them
n0c7730dc6d4.x: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change prepares India's NDCs, while the Union Cabinet gives final approval.
n0c7730dc6d4.tq: Use the authority-role test to distinguish preparation from approval.
xs: **MoEFCC** prepares India's NDCs and the **Union Cabinet** gives final approval — option **(3)**.
Parliament, the UNFCCC and the President play no such role in the notes.
xa: The Union Cabinet approved **NDC 3.0** in **March 2026**.
The updated NDC was communicated in **August 2022**.
The INDC went to the UNFCCC in **October 2015**.

nd5ae32d3a24.s: NDC 3.0 for the period 2031–2035 was approved by the Union Cabinet in:
nd5ae32d3a24.x: The Union Cabinet approved NDC 3.0 for 2031–2035 in March 2026.
nd5ae32d3a24.tq: Direct recall of the approval authority and date.
xs: NDC 3.0 (**2031-35**) was approved by the **Union Cabinet** in **March 2026** — option **(4)**.
**August 2022** was the updated NDC; **June 2025** is when non-fossil capacity crossed 50%.
xa: It embeds **LiFE** and scales up adaptation.
It was described as "continuity and incremental advance" within India's **equitable share**.

na293bc977a5.s: The five commitments collectively known as 'Panchamrit' were announced by the Prime Minister at Glasgow on:
na293bc977a5.x: The Panchamrit commitments were announced at Glasgow on 1 November 2021 during COP26.
na293bc977a5.tq: Pair the named initiative with its exact announcement date and venue.
xs: **Panchamrit** was announced at **Glasgow (COP26)** on **1 November 2021** — option **(3)**.
**12 December 2015** is the date the **Paris Agreement** was adopted.
xa: Two pledges (**45%** and **50%**) entered the **Aug 2022** NDC.
The net-zero **2070** target was announced at the same COP.

nb43a9701abd.s: India announced its target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070 at which international climate conference?
nb43a9701abd.x: India announced its 2070 net-zero target at COP26 held in Glasgow in 2021.
nb43a9701abd.tq: Use the event-year association to distinguish the announcement from the later strategy submission.
xs: India announced **net zero by 2070** at **COP26, Glasgow, 2021** — option **(3)**.
It is the fifth **Panchamrit** pledge.
xa: Asked in **APPSC 2024** (key left blank).
The **LT-LEDS** went to the UNFCCC at **COP27 (Nov 2022)**.
Supporting missions: **National Green Hydrogen Mission** and **Nuclear Mission**.

n75316159b66.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Net Zero Portal (September 2026)?
o: It was launched with a NAPCC Dashboard tracking the national missions
Scope 1 and Scope 2 reporting is encouraged
It provides for mandatory disclosure of corporate net-zero targets
n75316159b66.x: The portal is for voluntary, not mandatory, disclosure of corporate net-zero targets.
xa: Both were launched in **Sept 2026**.
India's net-zero target year is **2070**.

n007e8abbb28.s: Forest and tree cover constituted approximately what proportion of India’s geographical area in 2021?
n007e8abbb28.x: Forest and tree cover accounted for approximately 24.6 percent of India’s geographical area in 2021.
n007e8abbb28.tq: Discriminate the exact percentage using the decimal figure.
xs: Forest and tree cover was ~**24.6 percent** of India's geographical area in **2021** — option **(3)**.
This cover underpins the **additional carbon sink** target of the NDCs.
xa: Official sink estimate **2005-2019**: **1.97 bn t**.
**Green India Mission**: **5 Mha** forest cover + **5 Mha** quality improvement.
**MISHTI** covers mangroves over **540 sq km**.

n6ae176dd057.s: The International Solar Alliance, the first international intergovernmental organisation headquartered in India, has its headquarters at:
n6ae176dd057.x: The ISA Secretariat is at Gurugram, Haryana; New Delhi is linked with its founding conference.
xa: **New Delhi** hosted its **Founding Conference** on **11 March 2018**.
**New Delhi** is the **CDRI** secretariat.
Framework agreement in force **Dec 2017**.

ncf4d5c3a565.s: India relies on domestic resources for about what share of its climate finance?
ncf4d5c3a565.x: India relies mainly on domestic resources (about 83%); global climate finance was about USD 1.9 trillion in 2023.
xa: India sought a dedicated agenda item on developed-country finance at **Bonn SB64**.
NDC 3.0 also demands **new, low-cost climate finance**.

ne9f227ec827.s: Which of the following correctly represents the quantitative memory sequence of the five Panchamrit commitments?
ne9f227ec827.x: The Panchamrit sequence is 500 GW, 50 percent, 1 billion tonnes, 45 percent and net zero by 2070.
ne9f227ec827.tq: Retain the five-number memory hook in its stated order.
xs: The Panchamrit memory hook is **500, 50, 1, 45, 2070** — option **(4)**.
**500 GW** non-fossil; **50%** from renewables; **1 billion tonnes** cut; **45%** intensity cut; **net zero 2070**.
Options with **2050** or a reordered sequence are wrong.
xa: The first four pledges are for **2030**.
Exam trap: **capacity** versus **generation**.
Announced at **COP26, Glasgow, 1 Nov 2021**.

nb8e754eda1a.s: India defends its comparatively later net-zero target primarily on the grounds of:
o: Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and development needs
The absence of forest and tree cover
nb8e754eda1a.x: India invokes the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) and its development requirements to justify the 2070 target, later than the 2050 targets of most developed countries.
nb8e754eda1a.tq: Identify the principle and policy rationale rather than merely recalling the target year.
xs: India defends its later target on **CBDR** and **development** grounds — option **(3)**.
Most developed countries target **2050**.
Carbon-removal technology exists in its pathway: **CCUS technology pathways** were announced on **27 Mar 2026**.
xa: The pathway also relies on **forest and tree cover**.
India's principles: **equity, CBDR-RC and climate justice**.

nf4a8dc5e0b9.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven transitions identified in India's LT-LEDS?
nf4a8dc5e0b9.x: The seven transitions include low-carbon electricity systems, low-carbon transport, urban adaptation and efficient buildings, decoupling growth from industrial emissions, CO2 removal, forest and vegetation cover, and low-carbon finance. Expansion of fossil-fuel electricity systems is not one of them.
nf4a8dc5e0b9.tq: Find the option that reverses the low-carbon direction common to the listed transitions.
xs: **Expansion of fossil-fuel electricity systems** is not an LT-LEDS transition — option **(1)**.

The seven transitions: **low-carbon electricity**, **low-carbon transport**, **urban adaptation and efficient buildings**, **decoupling growth from industry emissions**, **CO2 removal**, **forest and vegetation cover**, **low-carbon finance**.
xa: LT-LEDS was submitted at **COP27 (Nov 2022)**.
The **Green India Mission** is key for the carbon-sink transition.

n3c2765702a9.s: The Nuclear Energy Mission aims to establish how many indigenous small modular reactors by 2033?
n3c2765702a9.x: The mission targets five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033.
n3c2765702a9.tq: Match a mission with its reactor target and deadline.
xs: The **Nuclear Energy Mission** targets **5 indigenous SMRs by 2033** — option **(2)**.
It is a supporting mission for **net zero 2070**.
xa: Nuclear capacity today: **8.78 GW**.
**National Green Hydrogen Mission**: **₹19,744 crore**, **5 MMT/year** by **2030**.

n1ae76a91c3f.s: The National Green Hydrogen Mission is associated with which outlay and production target?
o: ₹1.97 lakh crore; 5 MMT a year by 2070
n1ae76a91c3f.x: The mission has an outlay of ₹19,744 crore and targets 5 MMT/year capacity by 2030, supporting energy independence by 2047 and net zero by 2070. The other options either change the target (50 or 10 MMT) or the outlay, or confuse the 2047/2070 goals with the target year.
xs: National Green Hydrogen Mission: **₹19,744 crore**; **5 MMT a year by 2030** — option **(1)**.
**2047** (energy independence) and **2070** (net zero) are the wider goals, not the target year.
xa: The mission supports India's **net-zero pathway**.
**Nuclear Mission**: **5 SMRs by 2033**.
India joined the **Global Biofuels Alliance** launched in its **G20 Presidency (2023)**.

nd0eea69d76c.s: Which one of the following is identified as a key programme for achieving the carbon-sink target in India's LT-LEDS?
nd0eea69d76c.x: The Green India Mission is identified as a key programme for the carbon-sink target in the LT-LEDS.
nd0eea69d76c.tq: Match the programme with the specific function assigned to it.
xs: The **Green India Mission (GIM)** is the key programme for the **carbon-sink target** — option **(4)**.
Solar, water and nuclear missions serve other goals.
xa: GIM: forest cover on **5 Mha** + quality improvement on another **5 Mha**.
Its **50-60 Mt/yr** goal was folded into the **2030** sink target.
A **CAG audit** found weak convergence with **CAMPA** and **MGNREGS**.

nf288052e066.s: Mission LiFE was launched in October 2022 at:
nf288052e066.x: Mission LiFE was launched at Kevadia with the UN Secretary-General; the idea was introduced at COP26, Glasgow (2021).
xa: **75 LiFE actions** under **7 themes**.
⚠ LiFE idea = **COP26 (2021)**; Mission launch = **October 2022**.

nee1ba1fa294.s: Mission LiFE lists 75 LiFE actions under how many themes?
nee1ba1fa294.x: Mission LiFE has 75 actions under 7 themes, such as save energy and save water.
xa: The 7 themes: save energy, save water, **no single-use plastic**, sustainable food, reduce waste, **reduce e-waste**, healthy lifestyles.
⚠ LiFE idea = **COP26 (2021)**; Mission launch = **October 2022**.
The **Updated NDC** (**August 2022**) added LiFE as a qualitative element.

n541b48406fa.s: UJALA and PAT are associated respectively with:
o: Single-use plastic bans and e-waste recycling
Water conservation and sustainable food systems
n541b48406fa.x: UJALA is associated with LED bulbs, while PAT is an industrial-efficiency initiative aligned with LiFE.
n541b48406fa.tq: Separate two similarly placed schemes by their specific application areas.
xs: **UJALA** = **LED bulbs**; **PAT** = **industrial efficiency** — option **(1)**.
Both are aligned with **Mission LiFE**.
xa: LiFE focuses on **individual behaviour** and mindful consumption.
**Save energy** is one of LiFE's **7 themes**.
The **CCTS** is administered by the **Bureau of Energy Efficiency**.

n2e591bbdc81.s: IRIS, the Infrastructure for Resilient Island States initiative, was launched at:
o: The UN Climate Action Summit in 2019
n2e591bbdc81.x: IRIS was launched at COP26 in 2021 and focuses on Small Island Developing States.
n2e591bbdc81.tq: Distinguish the launch year and forum of a related climate initiative.
xs: **IRIS** was launched at **COP26 (2021)** — option **(1)**.
It focuses on **SIDS** under the **CDRI**.
**COP21 (2015)** saw the **ISA**; the **2019 UN Climate Action Summit** saw **CDRI** itself.
xa: CDRI is led by India with **UNDRR** support.
**Jordan** recently joined **ISA, CDRI and GBA**.

nd35e5a70f9c.s: The Green Credit Programme is a market-based incentive mechanism for:
nd35e5a70f9c.x: The programme rewards voluntary environmental actions; its afforestation credits can be exchanged for compensatory-afforestation obligations.
xa: CA exchange guidelines came on **16 Sep 2025**.
⚠ The **CCTS** is India's **mandatory compliance** market; the GCP is voluntary.

n548de55ddfd.s: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme of India combines which of the following mechanisms?
o: A compliance mechanism and an offset mechanism
A voluntary mechanism and an import mechanism
A taxation mechanism and a subsidy mechanism
A conservation mechanism and a litigation mechanism
n548de55ddfd.x: The Indian Carbon Market combines a compliance mechanism for energy-intensive sectors with an offset mechanism for voluntary projects in ten sectors.
n548de55ddfd.tq: Distinguish the two complementary designs of the carbon market.
xs: The **CCTS** combines a **compliance mechanism** and an **offset mechanism** — option **(1)**.
**Compliance**: energy-intensive obligated entities get **GEI targets**.
**Offset**: voluntary projects in **10 sectors** (e.g. agriculture, waste).
xa: CCTS is India's **first mandatory compliance carbon market** (Indian Carbon Market).
**Nine** offset methodologies have been published.
It is designed to meet the **45%** intensity target.

n3b32f8df831.s: Under the compliance mechanism of the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, an obligated entity that performs better than its notified GHG Emission Intensity target:
o: Must purchase additional Carbon Credit Certificates
Receives a Carbon Credit Certificate that can be traded
Receives a direct compensation from the Union Budget
Is exempted from all environmental regulations
n3b32f8df831.x: Entities that beat their notified GHG Emission Intensity targets earn tradeable Carbon Credit Certificates. Entities that miss their targets must buy certificates.
n3b32f8df831.tq: Apply the compliance rule to the entity’s performance against its target.
xs: An entity that beats its **GEI target** earns tradeable **Carbon Credit Certificates** — option **(2)**.
Entities that **miss** their targets **must buy** certificates.
xa: GEI targets notified **Oct 2025** for **aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali, and pulp and paper** → **282 obligated entities**.
CCTS now covers **7 sectors**, ~**490 industries**, ~**477 Mt CO2e**.
Only **China, EU and South Korea** cover more.

n3658918bfe9.s: India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) is administered by the:
o: Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
n3658918bfe9.x: The CCTS is run by the BEE under the Ministry of Power; ICFRE administers the Green Credit Programme.
xa: ⚠ CCTS = **Energy Conservation Act** / **BEE**; GCP = **EPA 1986** / **ICFRE**.
CCTS is India's **first mandatory compliance carbon market**.

n92a890e549d.s: The United Kingdom's recognition of India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) means that:
o: CCTS counts as a qualifying carbon price under the UK CBAM from 1 January 2027, avoiding double charging of Indian exports
Indian exporters are fully exempt from all UK import duties from 2026
CCTS credits can be used to meet EU CBAM obligations
The UK will administer the CCTS jointly with the Bureau of Energy Efficiency
n92a890e549d.x: CCTS is a qualifying carbon price under the UK CBAM (from 1 Jan 2027), so Indian exports are not charged twice. It does not remove all import duties, concerns the UK (not EU) CBAM, and CCTS remains administered by BEE alone.
n92a890e549d.tq: UK CBAM 2027 recognises CCTS → no double charge.
xs: The UK treats **CCTS** as a **qualifying carbon price** under the **UK CBAM** from **1 Jan 2027**, **avoiding double charging** of Indian exports — option **(1)**.
It concerns the **UK** CBAM, not the EU, and gives no blanket exemption from import duties.
CCTS stays administered by the **Bureau of Energy Efficiency**.
xa: The recognition came in **Sep 2026**.
The **EU CBAM** definitive phase began **1 January 2026**.

n48ba8251df4.s: The Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) was launched in 2019 at the:
n48ba8251df4.x: CDRI was launched at the 2019 UN Climate Action Summit; its secretariat is in New Delhi and it is a partnership, not a treaty body.
xa: CDRI is led by India with **UNDRR** support; **30+** national governments.
Its **IRIS** initiative (COP26, **2021**) focuses on **SIDS**.

n1f3d9ab623a.s: The present membership principle of the International Solar Alliance is best represented by which one of the following?
o: Membership is restricted to countries between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn.
Membership is open to all United Nations member states.
Membership is restricted to countries that generate more than half of their electricity from solar power.
Membership is restricted to countries belonging to the European Union and SAARC.
n1f3d9ab623a.x: Although the ISA initially began with the idea of bringing together sunshine countries between the tropics, its membership is now open to all UN member states.
n1f3d9ab623a.tq: Track the change from an initial geographical conception to the present membership rule.
xs: ISA membership is **open to all UN member states** — option **(2)**.
It **began** with "**sunshine countries**" between the tropics but no longer restricts membership.
xa: Strength: **125 member and signatory countries** (Mar 2026).
**Malta** became the **119th** member in **Feb 2024**.
The apex body is the **ISA Assembly**.

n629ba442933.s: The International Solar Alliance was launched on 30 November 2015:
o: at COP21, Paris, by India and France
at the UN Climate Action Summit, New York, by India alone
at COP26, Glasgow, by India and the UK
at New Delhi, as its Founding Conference
n629ba442933.x: ISA was launched at COP21, Paris, on 30 Nov 2015 by India and France. The 2019 UN Climate Action Summit is where CDRI was launched; COP26 is linked to IRIS and Panchamrit; New Delhi hosted the Founding Conference on 11 March 2018, not the launch.
n629ba442933.tq: ISA: Paris 2015 with France; CDRI: New York 2019.
xs: The ISA was launched on **30 Nov 2015** at **COP21, Paris**, by **India and France** — option **(1)**.
**New Delhi** hosted the **Founding Conference** on **11 March 2018**, not the launch.
The **2019 UN Climate Action Summit** launched **CDRI**; **COP26** is linked to **IRIS** and Panchamrit.
xa: ISA HQ: **Gurugram, Haryana**.
Framework agreement in force **Dec 2017**.

n22e4aae07a1.s: The Surat Emissions Trading Scheme demonstrated the effectiveness of market-based regulation by reducing emissions of:
n22e4aae07a1.x: The Surat Emissions Trading Scheme reduced particulate-matter emissions by 20–30 percent.
n22e4aae07a1.tq: Link the scheme with the pollutant and the reduction range.
xs: The **Surat ETS** cut **particulate matter** emissions by **20-30%** — option **(4)**.
It was a precursor showing that **markets work**.
xa: The **CCTS** is India's **first mandatory compliance carbon market**.
**Khasi Hills Community REDD+ (Meghalaya)** is the first **Plan Vivo**-certified REDD+ project.

n80b7acb228b.s: LeadIT primarily works towards the low-carbon transition of which sectors?
n80b7acb228b.x: LeadIT focuses particularly on low-carbon transitions in the steel and cement sectors and aligns heavy industry with the Paris goals.
n80b7acb228b.tq: Match the coalition with its specialised industrial focus.
xs: **LeadIT** aligns heavy industry, especially **steel and cement**, with Paris goals — option **(3)**.
Its aim is **low-carbon transitions** in these hard-to-abate sectors.
xa: LeadIT was launched at the **UN Climate Action Summit, 2019**, by **India and Sweden**.
At **COP29 (Baku, Nov 2024)** India co-chaired its summit.
BTR1: **over 20%** of 2022 emissions came from industry.

n193b43fe454.s: The Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) is published by which group of organisations?
o: Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute and Climate Action Network International
n193b43fe454.x: The CCPI is published by Germanwatch, the NewClimate Institute and Climate Action Network (CAN) International.
n193b43fe454.tq: Use the publisher-organisation combination to distinguish the CCPI from UN and financial institutions.
xs: The CCPI is published by **Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute and Climate Action Network (CAN International)** — option **(2)**.
It is not a UN (UNEP/IPCC/UNFCCC) publication, though it is released at the **COP**.
xa: It is released **annually since 2005**.
India was **11th** in CCPI 2019 and **9th** in CCPI 2020.

nab754624a38.s: In the Climate Change Performance Index 2019 (released December 2018), India's rank was:
nab754624a38.x: India was ranked 11th in CCPI 2019 (released at COP24, December 2018); 9th was its rank in CCPI 2020. ⚠ APPSC key said 9th.
nab754624a38.tq: Distinguish the specified index edition from unspecified later editions.
xs: India ranked **11th** in **CCPI 2019** (released **Dec 2018**) — option **(4)**.
**9th** was India's rank in **CCPI 2020**.
xa: ⚠ The **APPSC 2018** key said **9th**, mixing up the two editions.
The CCPI is published by **Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute** and **CAN International**.
nab754624a38.fixed: odd exam-key wording removed; India was 11th in CCPI 2019

nc1f0c295145.s: The Khasi Hills Community REDD+ project in Meghalaya is significant because it is India’s first:
o: Compensatory-afforestation project under the Green Credit Programme
nc1f0c295145.x: The Khasi Hills Community REDD+ project is India’s first Plan Vivo-certified REDD+ project.
nc1f0c295145.tq: Use the certification body as the decisive identifier.
xs: The **Khasi Hills Community REDD+ project (Meghalaya)** is India's **first Plan Vivo-certified REDD+ project** — option **(3)**.
This was the **UPSC 2026** key.
xa: The **Surat ETS** cut particulate emissions by **20-30%**.
GCP afforestation is exchangeable for **compensatory afforestation** obligations.

nd64c78b653d.s: Which of the following correctly describes the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)?
o: It is a framework concerned exclusively with greenhouse-gas mitigation.
It deals only with air-pollution control in urban areas.
It is limited to biodiversity conservation and wildlife protection.
It is an overarching domestic framework addressing both mitigation and adaptation.
nd64c78b653d.x: The NAPCC is India’s overarching domestic climate framework and covers both mitigation and adaptation. It is not confined exclusively to greenhouse gases, biodiversity or air pollution.
nd64c78b653d.tq: Reject exclusive descriptions and identify the broader framework.
xs: The NAPCC is India's **overarching domestic** climate framework covering **both mitigation and adaptation** — option **(4)**.
⚠ It is not limited to GHGs, biodiversity or air pollution (APPSC 2023 answer).
xa: It was India's **first** overarching domestic climate policy framework, implemented through **nodal ministries**.
**Four of the eight missions** focus on adaptation.
Released **30 June 2008** by PM **Dr Manmohan Singh**.

n505b2e4e4bd.s: The Prime Minister's Council on Climate Change, under which the NAPCC was prepared, was constituted in:
n505b2e4e4bd.x: The Council was constituted in 2007; the NAPCC was released on 30 June 2008 by PM Dr Manmohan Singh.
xa: The Council sets **policy**; the **Executive Committee on Climate Change** coordinates.
The **National Water Mission** was also set up on **30 June 2008**.

n2362f907f53.s: Which institution launched the India Climate Change Knowledge Portal in 2020 as a supporting tool for tracking climate-related actions?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
n2362f907f53.x: The India Climate Change Knowledge Portal was launched in 2020 and tracks ministry-wise climate actions; it is associated with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
n2362f907f53.tq: Identify the administrative owner of the supporting climate portal.
xs: The keyed answer is the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** — option **(3)**.
The **India Climate Change Knowledge Portal (2020)** tracks **ministry-wise actions**; MoEFCC's **Climate Change Division** is the nodal unit for **NAPCC coordination**.
xa: The **NAPCC Dashboard** (MoEFCC) tracks mission progress on set indicators.
**India's Net Zero Portal** (MoEFCC) takes **voluntary** net-zero disclosures.
Both the Dashboard and Net Zero Portal were launched in **Sept 2026**.

n6364eedaed2.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the original eight National Missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change?
o: National Mission for a Green India
n6364eedaed2.x: The National Mission on Clean Air is not one of the original eight NAPCC missions. The other three are among the eight core missions.
n6364eedaed2.tq: Eliminate the plausible-looking scheme that is outside the original eight.
xs: A **National Mission on Clean Air** is not among the original eight — option **(1)**.
Clean air (**NCAP**) is listed among things **not** in the original eight.
**National Water Mission**, **Sustainable Habitat** and **Green India** are core missions.
xa: Also outside the eight: **wind, nuclear, green hydrogen, biomass (SAMARTH)**.
NAPCC has **8 core National Missions**.

n5da747a35ad.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship among NDCs, the National Adaptation Plan and State Action Plans on Climate Change?
o: SAPCCs replace the National Adaptation Plan and national missions.
NDCs are delivered only through international treaties and not through domestic plans.
NDCs are delivered through the National Adaptation Plan, national missions and SAPCCs.
The National Adaptation Plan applies only to urban local bodies.
n5da747a35ad.x: NDC implementation is pursued through the National Adaptation Plan, national missions and State Action Plans on Climate Change.
n5da747a35ad.tq: Test the relationship among national commitments and domestic implementation channels.
xs: NDCs are delivered through the **National Adaptation Plan**, **national missions** and **SAPCCs** — option **(3)**.
SAPCCs align with the NAPCC rather than replacing it.
xa: NAPCC = **domestic vehicle for NDCs**.
Adaptation spending rose from **3.7% of GDP (FY16)** to **5.6% (FY22)**.

n5ba063e85dd.s: The NAPCC Dashboard, launched in September 2026, is intended primarily to perform which function?
o: Replace the State Action Plans on Climate Change
n5ba063e85dd.x: The NAPCC Dashboard was launched in September 2026 to track the progress of the national climate missions.
n5ba063e85dd.tq: Infer the operational purpose directly from the name and stated function of the dashboard.
xs: The **NAPCC Dashboard** (Sept 2026) **tracks the national missions** — option **(1)**.
It tracks mission progress on **set indicators**; it does not replace SAPCCs.
xa: It was launched with **India's Net Zero Portal** (MoEFCC).
The **India Climate Change Knowledge Portal (2020)** tracks ministry-wise actions.

nc38478451c7.s: The National Action Plan on Climate Change serves as India’s domestic vehicle for which international climate commitment?
nc38478451c7.x: The NAPCC is the domestic vehicle for implementing India’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).
nc38478451c7.tq: Discriminate between climate commitments and instruments belonging to other environmental agreements.
xs: The NAPCC is the **domestic vehicle for NDCs** — **Nationally Determined Contributions** — option **(2)**.
NDCs are delivered through the **National Adaptation Plan**, **national missions** and **SAPCCs**.
xa: NAPCC covers **both mitigation and adaptation**.
Adaptation spending rose to **5.6% of GDP (FY22)**.

n4bd6520808e.s: The National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency includes which of the following schemes?
