n4bd6520808e.x: The Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme is included in the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency and is associated with the Ministry of Power and BEE.
xs: The **NMEEE** includes the **PAT scheme** — **Perform, Achieve and Trade** — option **(4)**.
**SAMARTH** (biomass) is outside the eight; **AMRUT** and **Ujjwala** are typical non-mission distractors.
xa: NMEEE nodal: **Ministry of Power / BEE**.
Under PAT, units beating targets earn tradeable **Energy Saving Certificates**.
Exam angle: "NOT a NAPCC mission?" distractors are schemes like **Swachh Bharat, Ujjwala, AMRUT**.

nf55fd4d71b7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the two DST missions under the NAPCC?
o: NMSHE assesses Himalayan vulnerability across 12 thematic areas
NMSKCC supports Centres of Excellence and State Climate Change Centres
Both missions have the Ministry of Jal Shakti as their nodal ministry
nf55fd4d71b7.x: Both missions are under the Department of Science and Technology, not the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
xa: NMSKCC has **4 thematic areas** and builds S&T capacity.
NMSKCC supports state- and district-level **vulnerability assessments** for SAPCCs.

nf9dff5baaf4.s: The National Solar Mission was launched on 11 January 2010 with an objective of achieving what capacity by 2022?
nf9dff5baaf4.x: The National Solar Mission was launched on 11 January 2010 and targeted 100 GW of solar capacity by 2022.
nf9dff5baaf4.tq: Link the launch date with the mission’s quantitative target.
xs: The **National Solar Mission (JNNSM)**, launched **11 Jan 2010**, targeted **100 GW** by **2022** — option **(2)**.
Its nodal ministry is **MNRE**.
xa: The **NMEEE** is under the **Ministry of Power / BEE**.
NAPCC was released on **30 June 2008**.

n95de51df0e1.s: Which one of the following is NOT a sub-mission of the Green India Mission?
o: Expansion of forest and tree cover and ecosystem restoration
Improvement of incomes of forest-dependent people
n95de51df0e1.x: The three sub-missions concern forest quality, forest and tree cover with ecosystem restoration, and incomes of forest-dependent people. Thermal power generation is not a GIM sub-mission.
n95de51df0e1.tq: Find the outsider among closely related environmental programme components.
xs: **Promotion of thermal power generation** is not a GIM sub-mission — option **(2)**.
GIM's **3 sub-missions**: **forest quality**, **forest/tree cover and ecosystem restoration**, **incomes of forest-dependent people**.
xa: GIM is under **MoEFCC**; launched **2014** (some notes say **2011**).
CAG (**Aug 2026**) found a **>90%** shortfall in GIM.

nenvironment-2-10.s: The core of the National Action Plan on Climate Change consists of how many National Missions?
nenvironment-2-10.x: The NAPCC has eight core missions, including Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Water, Green India and Sustainable Agriculture.
n: The core feature of the National Action Plan on Climate Change is eight National Missions. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency is one of the eight National Missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Water Mission is one of the eight National Missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Mission for Green India is one of the eight National Missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture is one of the eight National Missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
xa: The others: **National Solar Mission**, **Sustainable Habitat**, **Sustaining Himalayan Ecosystem**, **Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change**.
⚠ For "how many core missions" the answer is **8**; ES **2025-26** adds **health** as a ninth.
Two **DST** missions: **NMSHE** (**12** areas) and **NMSKCC** (**4** areas).

n910800c65f9.s: The nodal unit for UNFCCC negotiations and NAPCC coordination is the:
n910800c65f9.x: The MoEFCC Climate Change Division is the nodal unit; the PM's Council sets policy and the Executive Committee coordinates.
xa: NAPCC was **launched** on **30 June 2008** by PM **Dr Manmohan Singh**.
The PM's Council on Climate Change was **constituted 2007**.
Tracking: **India Climate Change Knowledge Portal (2020)**, **NAPCC Dashboard**, **Net Zero Portal**.

n1d9d512f5e2.s: Among the goals of the National Water Mission is a public water database and a focus on ____ areas.
n1d9d512f5e2.x: NWM goals include a public water database and a focus on over-exploited areas, with a 20% gain in water-use efficiency.
xa: Other goals: **impact assessment** and **citizen/state action**; efficiency via basin-level **IWRM**.
NWM is under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**, set up **30 June 2008**.
State Specific Action Plans get **₹50 lakh** for major States.

n43113db8b20.s: Under the Perform, Achieve and Trade mechanism, energy-intensive units that exceed their energy-saving targets receive:
o: Energy Saving Certificates that can be traded
Carbon tax rebates issued by State governments
n43113db8b20.x: PAT rewards industries that beat their energy-saving targets with tradable Energy Saving Certificates.
n43113db8b20.tq: Identify the market instrument generated by achievement of a performance target.
xs: Under **PAT**, units beating targets earn tradeable **Energy Saving Certificates** — option **(3)**.
PAT is a **market mechanism** under the **NMEEE**.
xa: NMEEE nodal: **Ministry of Power / BEE**.
PAT is aligned with **Mission LiFE**'s energy-efficiency theme.
NMEEE is one of the **8** core missions.

nd2055e94b09.s: Under the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture, Soil Health Cards are issued free every:
nd2055e94b09.x: Soil Health Cards are issued free every two years; micro-irrigation gets up to 55% subsidy.
xa: **₹30,000/family** for Integrated Farming Systems.
NMSA also has a **Sub-Mission on Agroforestry**.

n862862c773b.s: India's adaptation spending as a share of GDP rose from:
n862862c773b.x: Adaptation spending rose from 3.7% of GDP (FY16) to 5.6% (FY22). The reversed option swaps the years, the 0.37/0.56 option misplaces the decimal, and 1.2/2.5 is incorrect.
xs: Adaptation spending rose from **3.7% of GDP (FY16)** to **5.6% (FY22)** — option **(1)**.
Option (3) reverses the years; option (4) misplaces the decimal.
xa: NAPCC is the **domestic vehicle for NDCs**.
**WRI**: a **ten-fold return** on adaptation investment.

nb9e6e6eeadc.s: The National Implementing Entity for the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change is:
nb9e6e6eeadc.x: NABARD is the NIE for NAFCC; CCAP (2014) is an MoEFCC capacity-building scheme.
xa: CCAP strengthens the **scientific and analytical base** on climate change.
NAFCC (**2015**) is a **central sector scheme** for State/UT adaptation projects.

nfb68b57e0e5.s: In 2017, the clean energy cess that funded the National Clean Energy Fund was folded into the:
nfb68b57e0e5.x: The cess, levied on coal since 2010-11, was folded into the GST compensation cess in 2017.
xa: **NAFCC** (**2015**): funds State adaptation projects; **NABARD** is the **National Implementing Entity**.
**CCAP** (**2014**): MoEFCC scheme supporting **SAPCCs**.
⚠ NAFCC implementing entity = **NABARD**.

n60800e88f98.s: The Economic Survey 2025–26 describes the NAPCC as having nine missions. The additional mission relates to:
n60800e88f98.x: The extra mission is on climate change and human health; the core-mission count remains eight.
xa: Missions proposed **c. 2015**: **Wind Energy, Health, Coastal Areas, Waste-to-Energy**.
Only **Health** has reached the list.

n6c3f4c58672.s: The evolution of State Action Plans on Climate Change is best represented by which of the following?
o: From district-specific adaptation plans to broad mitigation plans
From broad mitigation plans during 2010–15 to district-specific, risk-based adaptation plans from 2020 onwards
From national mitigation plans to plans unrelated to local institutions
From risk-based plans during 2010–15 to purely sector-neutral plans after 2020
n6c3f4c58672.x: States have moved from broad mitigation-centric plans in 2010–15 towards district-specific, risk-based adaptation plans from 2020 onwards, linked with social schemes and local institutions.
n6c3f4c58672.tq: Use the time markers to identify the direction of policy evolution.
xs: SAPCCs moved from **mitigation-centric plans (2010-15)** to **district-specific, risk-based adaptation plans** from **2020** — option **(2)**.
Newer plans are **tied to social schemes and local institutions**.
xa: States prepare SAPCCs in line with the **NAPCC**.
**NMSKCC** supports **State Climate Change Centres** and vulnerability assessments.
SAPCCs are criticised as **weak on finance**.

n9046ccc14c8.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Climate Change Cell functions under the Department of:
n9046ccc14c8.x: AP's exclusive Climate Change Cell (November 2022) works under the Department of Environment, Forests and Science & Technology.
xa: APSCCC prescribed **eight adaptation measures for the energy sector** (**Aug 2026**).
Revised plan: **AP SAPCC 2025-30**.

ne06806a4931.s: The revised Andhra Pradesh State Action Plan on Climate Change covers the period:
ne06806a4931.x: The revised AP SAPCC covers 2025–30 and includes eight energy-sector adaptation measures.
xa: Implementing agencies: **AP-Genco, NREDCAP, AP Green Energy Corporation**.
AP green-cover goal: **37% by 2030** → **50% by 2047**.

ne98decec3e5.s: Fridays For Future Andhra Pradesh participated in its first global climate strike in:
ne98decec3e5.x: FFF-AP joined its first global climate strike in 2019.
ne98decec3e5.tq: Discriminate between closely spaced years in a movement-related fact.
xs: **Fridays For Future AP (FFFAP)** joined its first global climate strike in **2019** — option **(3)**.
This was the **APPSC 2023** key.
xa: **AP National Green Corps** was set up in **2002-03**, with **4,350 Eco-Clubs**.
APNGC involves **1.63 lakh students** and **1.31 crore saplings**.

nbcf6cdd33e2.s: Chemical fertilisers and pesticides are a major primary source of:
nbcf6cdd33e2.x: Fertilisers and pesticides mainly cause soil pollution; sewage discharge is the main source of water pollution.
xa: Air pollution impacts: respiratory and heart disease, **acid rain**, poor visibility.
Water pollution impacts: water-borne disease, **eutrophication**, fish kills.
Soil pollution impacts: loss of fertility, toxic crops, **soil fauna imbalance**.
Noise impacts: **hearing loss**, stress, sleep loss.

n2599bc085ec.s: Eutrophication and fish kills are impacts of:
n2599bc085ec.x: Water pollution from sewage and effluents causes water-borne diseases, eutrophication and fish kills.
xa: Soil pollution's major source: **chemical fertilisers and pesticides**; also industrial waste.
**Coal ash** disposal pollutes soil with **arsenic, mercury, lead, cadmium, chromium**.
Air pollution's major source: **industrial emissions** (SO2, NOx, PM).

nd8971eac25c.s: Which of the following represents a secondary pollutant?
nd8971eac25c.x: Secondary pollutants are formed by reactions in the environment. Ozone and peroxyacyl nitrate are examples, whereas plastics are listed as primary pollutants in the classification table.
nd8971eac25c.tq: Use the defining distinction between emitted pollutants and reaction products.
xs: **Ozone** formed by atmospheric reactions is a **secondary pollutant** — option **(4)**.
Secondary pollutants are **formed by reaction**; primary pollutants are present **as emitted**.
**Plastics** are the notes' example of a primary pollutant; sewage and CO2 are emitted directly.
xa: Other secondary pollutant: **peroxyacyl nitrate**.
Quantitative vs qualitative: **CO2** vs **insecticides, herbicides**.
Biodegradable vs non-biodegradable: **sewage, heat** vs **plastics, DDT**.

n088478bb069.s: Insecticides and herbicides are examples of:
n088478bb069.x: Insecticides and herbicides are qualitative pollutants; CO2 is a quantitative pollutant.
xa: By form: **primary** (as emitted, e.g. plastics) vs **secondary** (formed by reaction, e.g. **ozone**, **peroxyacyl nitrate**).
By source geometry: **point** (chimney), **line** (vehicles), **area**, **diffuse** (non-point).
**Xenobiotics** resist degradation — pesticides, **PCBs**, plastics.

n26758bda43e.s: A thermal plant chimney, vehicles along a highway, a mining area and farm runoff are respectively examples of which types of pollution source?
n26758bda43e.x: By source geometry: a chimney is a point source, a highway with vehicles is a line source, a mining area is an area source and farm runoff is a diffuse (non-point) source. Option A alone gives this order; B swaps chimney and highway and also mining and runoff, C swaps highway and mining, D swaps chimney and mining.
xs: The order is **point, line, area and diffuse** — option **(1)**.
**Thermal plant chimney** = **point**; **highway vehicles** = **line**; **mining area** = **area**; **farm runoff** = **diffuse (non-point)**.
Option (2) swaps chimney/highway and mining/runoff; (3) swaps highway and mining; (4) swaps chimney and mining.
xa: Other bases of classification: **primary vs secondary**, **quantitative vs qualitative**, **biodegradable vs non-biodegradable**.
Farm runoff carries **chemical fertilisers and pesticides**, the major source of soil pollution.
NCR: fertilisers + livestock excreta = **77-80% of ammonia** emissions (CAQM).

o: Only radioactive elements released by reactors
Synthetic chemicals foreign to living systems that resist degradation
Naturally occurring nutrients essential to all organisms
n11d7aaf3beb.x: Xenobiotics are synthetic chemicals foreign to living systems, such as pesticides, PCBs and plastics, and they generally resist degradation.
n11d7aaf3beb.tq: Identify the exact definition and use representative examples to eliminate near matches.
xs: **Xenobiotics** are **synthetic chemicals foreign to living systems** that **resist degradation** — option **(2)**.
Examples: **pesticides, PCBs, plastics** — not radioactive elements, nutrients or livestock waste.
xa: **Biomagnification** pairs with **DDT** (APPSC 2023).
**Brominated flame retardants** are **persistent + endocrine-disrupting**, released from **e-waste**.
**Plastics and DDT** are **non-biodegradable**; sewage and heat are biodegradable.

n60d1fe67e48.s: MoEF&CC caps lead in household and decorative paints at:
n60d1fe67e48.x: The cap is 90 ppm, not 900 ppm; lead from vehicles and smelters can cause brain damage.
xa: **Mercury** sources: coal combustion, smelters, chemical effluents.
Synthetic **idol paints** release **mercury, cadmium, lead**.
**Coal ash** heavy metals: **arsenic, mercury, lead, cadmium, chromium**.

n949778ad2bb.s: Burning tyres, plastics, flex and e-waste in open fires can release which combination of pollutants?
o: Ozone and peroxyacyl nitrate without other pollutants
Dioxins, furans, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and toxic metals
n949778ad2bb.x: Such burning can release dioxins, furans, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, lead, cadmium and mercury.
n949778ad2bb.tq: Select the option containing both gaseous pollutants and toxic metals associated with open burning.
xs: Open burning releases **dioxins, furans**, **CO, SO2, NOx** and toxic metals (**lead, cadmium, mercury**) — option **(4)**.
Burnt materials: **tyres, plastics, flex, e-waste** — e.g. **Bhogi bonfires**.
Ozone and peroxyacyl nitrate are **secondary** pollutants formed by reaction, not released directly by burning.
xa: Source: **APPCB advisory**, **11 Jan 2026**.
APPCB chairman **P. Krishnaiah** urged an **eco-friendly Bhogi**.
**Brominated flame retardants** are also released from **e-waste**.

n3d0c470f6d9.s: The Comprehensive Environmental Pollution Index (CEPI) was developed by the CPCB in 2009 with:
n3d0c470f6d9.x: CEPI was developed with IIT Delhi and scores clusters 0-100 for air, water and land.
xa: Three CEPI factors: **pollutant, pathway, receptor** (exposed people).
**≥70** = **critically polluted**; **60-70** = **severely polluted**.
**2009**: **43 of 88** clusters critically polluted.

n1fd3fd820db.s: Patancheru-Bollaram, classified as critically polluted under CEPI, is now located in:
n1fd3fd820db.x: Patancheru-Bollaram was then in AP and is now in Telangana; Visakhapatnam was another AP cluster assessed.
xa: Critically polluted = CEPI **≥70**; **2009**: **43 of 88** clusters.
CEPI was developed by **CPCB with IIT Delhi (2009)**.
Visakhapatnam also saw the **LG Polymers styrene** leak (**7 May 2020**).

n4f84e7159d3.s: The Central Pollution Control Board was established in 1974 under which legislation and was renamed in 1988?
o: Environment Protection Act; renamed as the National Green Tribunal
Water Act; renamed as the Central Pollution Control Board
Air Act; renamed as the National Pollution Board
Wildlife Protection Act; renamed as the Wildlife Board
n4f84e7159d3.x: The CPCB was established in 1974 under the Water Act and was renamed in 1988. Its headquarters are in New Delhi.
n4f84e7159d3.tq: Link the institution with its establishing statute and the date of renaming.
xs: The **CPCB** was set up in **1974** under the **Water Act** and renamed **Central Pollution Control Board** in **1988** — option **(2)**.
It is headquartered in **New Delhi**.
xa: CPCB developed **CEPI** with **IIT Delhi** in **2009**.
**CSE** is also in **New Delhi**; **NEERI** is in **Nagpur**.
**Environment (Protection) Fund Rules**: **25%** kept by the Centre.

nenvironment-23-1.s: The Central Arid Zone Research Institute (CAZRI) is located at:
nenvironment-23-1.x: CAZRI is at Jodhpur; ICFRE is in Dehradun, IIFM in Bhopal and BNHS in Mumbai.
n: The ICFRE is located in Dehradun. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
The IIFM is located in Bhopal. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
The CAZRI is located in Jodhpur. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
The BNHS is located in Mumbai. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
xa: **FRI** and **WII** are also in **Dehradun**.
**ICFRE** is the **apex body** in the **national forestry research system**.
**INCOIS** is in **Hyderabad**; the **NBA** is in **Chennai**.

nenvironment-23-2.s: The roots of the Forest Research Institute (FRI) can be traced to which institution and year?
o: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services, 1999
nenvironment-23-2.x: FRI Dehradun grew from the Imperial Forest Research Institute of 1906. BNHS dates from 1883 and INCOIS from 1999.
nenvironment-23-2.tq: Match each institute to its founding year.
n: The FRI is rooted in the Imperial Forest Research Institute. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
The Imperial Forest Research Institute was established in 1906. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
The IIFM was established in 1982. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
The BNHS was established in 1883. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
xs: The **FRI** is rooted in the **Imperial Forest Research Institute (1906)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**INCOIS** was **established 1999** and **BNHS** in **1883**; neither is FRI's root.
**IIFM** (**Bhopal**) was **established 1982** for **forest management**.
xa: **FRI** is located in **Dehradun** and works on **forest research**.
**ICFRE** and **WII** share Dehradun with FRI.
**INCOIS** is an **autonomous body** under the **Ministry of Earth Sciences**.

nenvironment-23-8.s: Which body is associated with delivering environmental justice?
nenvironment-23-8.x: The NGT delivers environmental justice; CPCB controls pollution, NBA implements the BD Act and NTCA handles tigers.
n: The CPCB is associated with air and water pollution control. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
The NGT is associated with environmental justice. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
The NBA is associated with Biological Diversity Act implementation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
The NTCA is associated with tiger conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
xa: **CPCB** was set up in **1974** under the **Water Act** and renamed in **1988**.
The **NBA** sits in **Chennai**; the **NGT** and **NTCA** in **New Delhi**.
The NBA houses the **Centre for Biodiversity Policy and Law**, an **India–Norway** collaboration.

nenvironment-23-9.x: INCOIS is in Hyderabad; NBA is in Chennai, WII in Dehradun and BNHS in Mumbai.
n: The CPCB is located in Delhi. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
The NGT is located in New Delhi. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
The NBA is located in Chennai. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
The NTCA is located in New Delhi. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
xa: **INCOIS** was **established 1999** under the **Ministry of Earth Sciences**.
**BNHS** (**1883**) does **wildlife research** and **nature conservation**.
⚠ **BSI** and **ZSI** are both in **Kolkata**.

nenvironment-23-13.s: Which of the following is the apex body in the national forestry research system?
o: Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE)
nenvironment-23-13.x: ICFRE (Dehradun) is the apex body of India's forestry research system. FRI, IIFM and CAZRI are institutes under it or elsewhere.
nenvironment-23-13.tq: Discriminate the apex body from its institutes.
n: The ICFRE is an apex body in the national forestry research system. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-42]
xs: The **apex body** in the **national forestry research system** is **ICFRE** — so option **(2)** is correct.
ICFRE **promotes** and **undertakes** **need-based forestry research and extension** from **Dehradun**.
**FRI** does **forest research**, **IIFM** (**Bhopal**) **forest management** and **CAZRI** (**Jodhpur**) **arid zone research** under **ICAR**.
xa: **FRI** traces its roots to the **Imperial Forest Research Institute** (**1906**).
**IIFM** was **established 1982**.
**WII** in **Dehradun** is a **wildlife research and training** institution.

nc84a3d0880a.s: Industrial disasters such as Bhopal (MIC) and LG Polymers (styrene) are mostly caused by:
nc84a3d0880a.x: Industrial disasters are mostly caused by toxic gas leaks; radioactive leaks such as Chernobyl are a separate category.
xa: **Bhopal** (**2-3 Dec 1984**): **methyl isocyanate (MIC)** leak from Union Carbide's pesticide unit.
**LG Polymers** (**7 May 2020**): **styrene** vapour leak at Visakhapatnam.
**Chernobyl** (**26 April 1986**): **radioactive leak** from a reactor.

n7ab9ccb4834.s: The Los Angeles smog episode of 1943 was primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Photochemical smog formed by sunlight acting on nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons from vehicle exhaust
Methyl mercury released into an industrial water body
Radioactive pollution caused by a reactor leak
Classical smog caused by sulphur dioxide and water vapour at low temperature
n7ab9ccb4834.x: The Los Angeles smog was photochemical smog, produced when sunlight acted on nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons from vehicle exhaust, particularly at about 24–32°C.
n7ab9ccb4834.tq: Identify the event by linking its characteristic pollutant mixture and atmospheric condition.
xs: The **Los Angeles smog (1943)** was **photochemical smog** — sunlight on **NOx and hydrocarbons** from vehicle exhaust — option **(1)**.
It formed at **24-32°C**.
**Classical smog** (SO2 + water vapour at low temperature) was the **London smog** of **1952**.
xa: **Minamata** (**1956**) involved **methyl mercury**.
**Ozone** and **peroxyacyl nitrate** are **secondary pollutants**.

n98fcaf476c2.s: Minamata disease was caused by the release of which pollutant into the environment?
o: Styrene vapour from a polymer plant
Methyl isocyanate from a pesticide unit
n98fcaf476c2.x: Minamata disease resulted from methyl mercury in industrial effluent. The mercury was biomagnified in fish and entered the human food chain.
n98fcaf476c2.tq: Use the pollutant-to-disaster association to distinguish closely related industrial incidents.
xs: **Minamata disease** was caused by **methyl mercury** in industrial effluent — option **(3)**.
It was **biomagnified in fish**.
**Styrene** = **LG Polymers**; **methyl isocyanate** = **Bhopal**.
xa: **Minamata disease**: **1956**, Minamata, **Japan**.
⚠ **Bhopal** = **MIC**; **LG Polymers** = **Styrene**; **Minamata** = **Methyl mercury**.
**Mercury** sources: **coal combustion**, smelters, chemical effluents.

n47ba75c80c2.s: The Bhopal gas tragedy took place during which period and involved the leakage of which substance?
n47ba75c80c2.x: The Bhopal gas tragedy occurred on 2–3 December 1984 when methyl isocyanate leaked from Union Carbide’s pesticide unit. More than 2,500 deaths were reported in the cited assessment.
n47ba75c80c2.tq: Pair the exact date range with the distinctive industrial chemical.
xs: **Bhopal gas tragedy**: **2-3 Dec 1984**, **methyl isocyanate** — option **(1)**.
MIC leaked from **Union Carbide**'s pesticide unit; over **2,500** killed (per APP).
**5-11 Dec 1952** = **London smog**; **7 May 2020** = **LG Polymers** (styrene); **26 April 1986** = **Chernobyl**.
xa: Bhopal = gas leakage / MIC / **1984** is asked almost every year.
**Industrial disasters** are mostly caused by **toxic gas** leaks.
⚠ **Minamata** = **methyl mercury**.

nenvironment-6-4.s: The National Environmental Engineering Research Institute focuses primarily on which of the following?
nenvironment-6-4.x: NEERI (Nagpur, CSIR) works on environmental science and engineering. Clearances, tribunals and forest diversion belong to other bodies.
n: The National Environment Appellate Authority dealt with appeals concerning environmental clearances and restrictions. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 12-13]
The NGT Act concerns environmental justice. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 12-13]
The Forest (Conservation) Act concerns forest diversion and conservation. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 12-13]
The focus of the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute is environmental science and engineering. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #6 · pp 12-13]
xs: **NEERI** focuses on **environmental science and engineering** — so option **(4)** is correct.
NEERI (**Nagpur**) works under **CSIR**; it was **established 1958**, earlier as **CPHERI**.
**Environmental justice** is the role of the **NGT**, not NEERI.
xa: The **NGT** is located in **New Delhi**.
The **CPCB** handles **air and water pollution control**.
⚠ **NEERI** = **Nagpur**; **WII** = **Dehradun**.

nfaf862d1da8.s: In Indian cities, the principal source of air pollution is generally regarded as
nfaf862d1da8.x: Automobile emissions are identified as the main source of air pollution in Indian cities.
nfaf862d1da8.tq: Use the dominant-source clue rather than selecting a naturally occurring source.
xs: The main source of air pollution in Indian cities is **automobile emissions** — so option **(3)** is correct (**APPSC 2025**).
**Forest fires**, **volcanic eruptions** and **dust storms** are **natural** sources, not the main urban source.
Vehicle/fuel combustion releases **CO, NOx, VOCs, PM**, unburnt hydrocarbons and **lead**.
xa: In the **NCR**, **transport** is the largest primary source → **23% of winter load** (CAQM synthesis report, **Jan 2026**).
**Delhi** is the city most often in the news for bad air.
Anthropogenic sources also include **power plants**, industry, **biomass burning**, agriculture (**ammonia, methane**) and **waste burning**.

o: Los Angeles and warm, sunny conditions
Los Angeles and cold, humid conditions
n268fd9b0cdf.x: Photochemical smog is linked with Los Angeles and warm, sunny weather; classical smog with London and cold, humid weather.
xa: ⚠ Trap: **London** smog = cold + **SO2**; **Los Angeles** smog = warm + **sunlight**.
**Photochemical smog** is itself listed as a **secondary pollutant**.
**Asian Brown Cloud**: soot + **black carbon** + aerosols over South Asia and the Indian Ocean in the **dry season**.

nf24b05b5741.s: The Asian Brown Cloud is best described as
o: A layer of soot, black carbon and aerosols over South Asia and the Indian Ocean during the dry season
A permanent ozone layer over the Himalayan region
A layer of volcanic ash restricted to Europe
A seasonal band of water vapour over the Pacific Ocean
nf24b05b5741.x: The Asian Brown Cloud is a dry-season layer of soot, black carbon and aerosols over South Asia and the Indian Ocean, arising mainly from biomass and fossil-fuel burning.
nf24b05b5741.tq: Identify the phenomenon from its composition, region and season together.
xs: The **Asian Brown Cloud** is soot, **black carbon** and aerosols over **South Asia and the Indian Ocean** in the **dry season** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It comes from **biomass and fossil-fuel burning**, not from volcanic ash, ozone or water vapour.
xa: **Photochemical smog** (Los Angeles) = NOx + VOCs + sunlight → **ozone, PAN**.
**Classical smog** (London) = **SO2**, smoke, particulates + fog in cold, humid conditions.
**Biomass burning** is also listed among **anthropogenic** sources of air pollution.

nd6c7f5438a4.s: Which one of the following is a natural source of air pollution?
nd6c7f5438a4.x: Forest fires, volcanic eruptions and dust storms are natural sources (APPSC 2025 answer: forest fires). Automobile emissions, power plants and waste burning are anthropogenic sources.
nd6c7f5438a4.tq: Natural = fires, volcanoes, dust storms; APPSC 2025 picked forest fires.
xs: **Forest fires** are a natural source of air pollution — so option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC 2025** answer).
**Automobile emissions**, **coal-fired power plants** and **waste burning** are **anthropogenic** sources.
xa: Other **natural** sources: **volcanic eruptions** and **dust storms**.
Main source in Indian cities = **automobile emissions** (**APPSC 2025**).
Agriculture is an anthropogenic source of **ammonia** and **methane**.

n88798ac3aa8.s: The characteristic rotten-egg smell associated with polluted air is mainly due to
n88798ac3aa8.x: Hydrogen sulphide, released from sources such as sewage, refineries and volcanoes, has a characteristic rotten-egg smell.
n88798ac3aa8.tq: Use the distinctive sensory clue to identify the pollutant.
xs: The **rotten-egg smell** is due to **hydrogen sulphide (H2S)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
H2S comes from **sewage, refineries and volcanoes** and causes eye and respiratory irritation.
**CO** reduces the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity; **SO2** comes from burning coal/oil; **ammonia** comes from fertilisers and livestock.
xa: **SO2** effects: eye irritation, breathing problems, **acid rain**, secondary PM2.5.
**Ammonia**: **fertilisers and livestock (77-80%)** → drives secondary particle formation.
**Magnetite** particles from brake wear are found in human **brain tissue**.

n70a541aefb6.s: Lichens disappear from areas with high levels of:
n70a541aefb6.x: Lichens are sensitive to SO2; mosses accumulate and indicate heavy-metal deposition.
xa: Lichens as SO2 indicators is an **APP PYQ**.
**Acid rain** also leaches **calcium and magnesium** from soil and releases toxic **aluminium**.
Acid rain releases **heavy metals** from soil into drinking water.

n8a9b77b4a8d.x: CNG is mainly methane; SATAT promotes compressed biogas.
xa: **Methanol Economy** = **NITI Aayog** programme for methanol as fuel/blend.
**LPG, PNG** and **BS-VI** fuels are also promoted.
All new vehicles must support **E20** (Ethanol Blending Programme).

ne4a390e7ba8.s: Fuel injection helps reduce vehicular pollution primarily by promoting
ne4a390e7ba8.x: Fuel injection promotes more complete combustion, thereby reducing the formation of pollutants associated with incomplete combustion.
ne4a390e7ba8.tq: Apply the stated mechanism rather than choosing a pollutant name.
xs: **Fuel injection** promotes **complete combustion** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Incomplete combustion** is what produces **CO**, so option (3) is the opposite.
xa: **Catalytic converters** (**platinum, palladium, rhodium**) convert CO, HC, NOx into CO2, H2O, N2.
Catalytic converters need **unleaded petrol**.

nenvironment-36-12.s: Cadmium in the air mainly comes from:
o: Photochemical reactions of NOx and hydrocarbons
nenvironment-36-12.x: Cadmium comes from metal production and smelting; PAHs come from incomplete combustion and ozone from photochemical reactions.
n: Fuel combustion is a major source of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 62-64]
Industrial emissions are a major source of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 62-64]
Fuel-originated particles are a source of lead pollution. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 62-64]
Soil-originated particles are a source of lead pollution. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 62-64]
xa: Ground-level **ozone** is a **secondary pollutant**.
**Lead** causes **brain damage**; sources include motor vehicles and smelters.
**Benzene** comes from **petrol combustion** and **petrol stations**.

nchemistry-12-47.s: Which of the following is a potent greenhouse gas?
nchemistry-12-47.x: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas; hydrogen sulphide is a toxic air pollutant.
n: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 42-45]
Hydrogen sulphide is a toxic air pollutant. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #12 · pp 42-45]
xa: **Carbon dioxide** is a **greenhouse gas** — **global warming** and **climate change**.
**Chlorine and fluorine compounds** can form **toxic compounds**.
**H2S** gives a **rotten-egg smell** and comes from sewage, refineries, volcanoes.

n49dd0d025c0.s: Which pollutant reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood?
n49dd0d025c0.x: CO reduces the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity; lead damages the brain and SO2 irritates the eyes and airways.
xa: **NO2 / NOx** → respiratory illness, acid rain and smog.
**H2S** → **rotten-egg smell**; eye and respiratory irritation.
**PM2.5** crosses the placenta → **pre-term birth**, **low birth weight** (AIIMS study, **3 Jun 2026**).

n0f41c8aac48.s: Ammonia released from fertilisers and livestock contributes principally to
o: The direct formation of carbon monoxide
The conversion of ozone into oxygen
The destruction of all particulate matter
n0f41c8aac48.x: Ammonia is a major driver of secondary particle formation in the atmosphere, particularly through the formation of ammonium salts.
n0f41c8aac48.tq: Connect the pollutant source with its atmospheric transformation rather than with a primary emission.
xs: Ammonia mainly drives **secondary particle formation** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Ammonia comes from **fertilisers and livestock (77-80%)**.
With **SO2** it forms **ammonium sulphate** — nearly **1/3 of India's PM2.5**.
xa: **Ammonium nitrate**, another secondary particle, adds up to **50%** of India's PM2.5.
Agriculture is an **anthropogenic** source of **ammonia and methane**.
**NH3** is one of the **8 pollutants** of the National AQI.

n16c40876098.s: Which of the following is a primary pollutant?
n16c40876098.x: Lead from vehicles is emitted directly; ozone, PAN and ammonium sulphate form in the atmosphere.
xa: Primary pollutants: **CO, SO2, NOx (NO), PM, lead**.
**Ammonium nitrate** is also secondary → up to **50%** of India's PM2.5.
**Lead** from motor vehicles and smelters causes **brain damage**.

n7e48ab7e272.s: Which pollutant can cross the placenta and is linked to pre-term birth and low birth weight?
n7e48ab7e272.x: PM2.5 penetrates deep into the lungs and crosses the placenta, linked to pre-term birth (AIIMS study, 3 June 2026).
xa: **NCR winter PM2.5** is nearly **35 times** the WHO limit.
**WHO AQG 2021** PM2.5: annual **5 µg/m³**, 24-hour **15 µg/m³**; NAAQS 24-hour PM2.5 = **60 µg/m³**.
**Secondary PM2.5**: ammonium sulphate nearly **1/3**, ammonium nitrate up to **50%**.

n914cabb7cf3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about indoor air pollution?
o: It is caused exclusively by biological agents
Biomass and coal used for cooking and heating contribute to it
Radon and carbon monoxide are gaseous indoor pollutants
Women and children are among the groups most affected
n914cabb7cf3.x: Indoor pollution also comes from dust, smoke, pesticides, gases and mosquito coils, not only biological agents.
xa: Health effects: **COPD, lung cancer, heart disease**.
**Mosquito coils** give off smoke and **PM**.
Intercity bus cabin air = **2-3 times** WHO limits.

nc1386a3649a.s: Precipitation is classed as acid rain when its pH is below:
nc1386a3649a.x: The acid-rain threshold is pH 5.6; typical acid rain has a pH of about 4.2-4.4.
xa: **pH 7** = neutral; each pH step = **tenfold** change in acidity.
⚠ Trap: **CO2** alone does not make "acid rain" in the exam sense.
Term coined in **1872** by **Robert Angus Smith** (coal burning in **Manchester**).

n688c83ebf8e.s: The main single factor identified in acid rain is:
n688c83ebf8e.x: SO2 and NOx are the principal acid-rain gases, with SO2 the main single factor; CO and methane are not principal causes.
xa: Acid rain = precipitation with **pH below 5.6**; typical **4.2-4.4**.
**Sulphuric acid** gives ~**two-thirds** of the acidity, **nitric acid** ~**one-third**.
RPSC asked: "excess of which causes acid rain" → **NOx + SO2** only.

n9033732cccd.s: Sulphuric acid accounts for about ____ of the acidity of acid rain.
n9033732cccd.x: Sulphuric acid gives about two-thirds of acid-rain acidity and nitric acid about one-third.
xa: Main single factor behind acid rain = **SO2**.
Acids form from SO2 + NOx with **oxygen, water and photo-oxidants**.
India = **largest SO2 emitter globally (2022)**, over **20%** of anthropogenic emissions.

n24d20ec4b05.s: About half of atmospheric acidity returns to the Earth's surface through:
n24d20ec4b05.x: About half returns by dry deposition; in wet deposition acids fall with rain, snow or fog.
xa: In dry deposition, acidic gases and particles **stick to dust/smoke** and settle.
Acid rain = **pH below 5.6**; typical **4.2-4.4**.
Pollutants travel **hundreds of km** by wind → a **transboundary** problem.

n4ae65adfbcb.s: Which of the following monuments is NOT protected under the Taj Trapezium Zone?
n4ae65adfbcb.x: The TTZ protects the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri; Sanchi Stupa is not included.
xa: TTZ = ~**10,400 sq km** trapezium around the Taj.
Districts: **Agra, Firozabad, Mathura, Hathras, Etah** (UP) + **Bharatpur** (Rajasthan).
**M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1996)**: SC barred **coal/coke** in TTZ industries → shift to **natural gas** or relocation.

n2cf4c13c696.s: The yellowing and loss of lustre of the Taj Mahal marble due to pollution is commonly called
n2cf4c13c696.x: The yellowing and loss of lustre of marble caused by pollution is popularly called “marble cancer.” Acid rain accelerates the decay of limestone and marble structures.
n2cf4c13c696.tq: Exact-term recall using plausible but non-standard expressions as distractors.
xs: The yellowing of Taj marble is called **marble cancer** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Acid rain decays **limestone and marble (CaCO3)** → yellow, lustreless surface.
xa: The Taj threat is mainly **SO2** (**APPSC 2018**), notably from the **Mathura refinery**.
Acid rain also corrodes **metals** and **paint**.
**TTZ** of ~**10,400 sq km** protects the Taj, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri.

nd61109c36cf.s: Because winds carry pollutants hundreds of kilometres, acid rain is a ____ problem.
nd61109c36cf.x: Acid rain is transboundary; Scandinavian lakes were acidified by emissions from the UK and central Europe.
xa: Industrial **China** is another classic case.
**India** = **largest SO2 emitter globally (2022)**, over **20%** of anthropogenic emissions.
**Helsinki Sulphur Protocol (1985)** sought a **30%** cut in sulphur emissions.

ncfad542a71b.s: In forest soils, acid deposition leaches calcium and magnesium and releases toxic ____ that damages roots.
ncfad542a71b.x: Acid deposition releases toxic aluminium; acidification also lowers lake pH, harming fish.
xa: Trees then become susceptible to **cold, pests, drought**.
On buildings, acid rain corrodes **limestone and marble** — "**marble cancer**" of the **Taj Mahal**.
Acid rain = precipitation with **pH below 5.6**.

n82fa611a6b4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about air-pollution control?
o: Low-NOx burners are used in power plants
Catalytic converters reduce NOx, carbon monoxide and hydrocarbons
Liming of lakes and soils neutralises acidity
Liming is a preventive measure that stops emissions at the source
n82fa611a6b4.x: Liming is a remedial measure that neutralises existing acidity; it does not prevent emissions.
xa: Catalytic converters use **platinum, palladium, rhodium**.
**IMO** caps sulphur in **ship fuel**.
**FGD** removes **up to 95% of SO2**.

n56f15c74e81.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the implementation of the National Clean Air Programme?
o: It is implemented exclusively by the CPCB without State Pollution Control Boards
It is funded through the Centrally Sponsored Scheme 'Control of Pollution'
The CPCB coordinates the programme with State Pollution Control Boards
State Pollution Control Boards are involved in its implementation
n56f15c74e81.x: SPCBs are involved; the CPCB coordinates NCAP with them.
xa: NCAP launched **January 2019** by **MoEFCC**.
**PRANA** portal tracks NCAP progress.
Tools: **City/State Action Plans**; Steering, Monitoring and Implementation Committees.

n7a637aa44a9.s: Catalytic converters in vehicles use which metals as catalysts?
n7a637aa44a9.x: Converters use platinum, palladium and rhodium; silver iodide is a cloud-seeding agent.
xa: Catalytic converters need **unleaded petrol**.
**Fuel injection** gives complete combustion.
Cloud seeding uses **silver iodide**, potassium iodide, **dry ice**, common salt.

ne9eeee9a106.x: Cloud seeding may use silver iodide, potassium iodide, dry ice and common salt.
xa: ⚠ **Silver iodide** is a cloud-seeding agent, not a catalytic-converter metal (those are **platinum, palladium, rhodium**).
**Smog towers**: **Connaught Place**, Delhi; **Xi'an** (China) has a **100 m** tower.
**VAYU** (Wind Augmentation PurifYing Unit) = roadside purifier by **CSIR-NEERI**.

nchemistry-9-24.s: Which of the following household fuels burns without smoke?
nchemistry-9-24.x: LPG (like biogas) is a clean gaseous fuel; wood and cow-dung give smoke, CO and fine particles.
n: Wood and cow-dung produce smoke, CO, and particulate matter. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 33-36]
Wood and cow-dung contribute to indoor air pollution. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 33-36]
Coal causes severe air pollution. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #9 · pp 33-36]
xa: Biogas is **renewable** and **relatively clean** when **purified**.
**Coal** causes **severe air pollution** — **SO₂**, **NOₓ**, **ash**.
**Hydrogen** gives **only water** when burned.

nf769f25fc41.s: Lichens are particularly useful as bioindicators of pollution by which pollutant?
nf769f25fc41.x: Lichens indicate sulphur dioxide pollution and disappear from areas with high SO2 levels.
nf769f25fc41.tq: Use the organism–pollutant association central to bioindicator questions.
xs: **Lichens** are bioindicators of **sulphur dioxide (SO2)** — so option **(3)** is correct (**APP PYQ**).
They are **absent or disappear** where SO2 is high.
xa: **Mosses** accumulate **heavy metals** → indicate their deposition.
SO2 is the **main single factor** behind **acid rain**.
SO2 sources: **coal-fired power plants**, metal-ore smelting, vehicles, volcanoes.

nb6c898e5807.s: The term “acid rain” was coined in 1872 by
nb6c898e5807.x: Robert Angus Smith coined the term “acid rain” in 1872 while describing pollution associated with coal burning in Manchester.
nb6c898e5807.tq: Direct name–date recall with scientifically related distractors.
xs: **Robert Angus Smith** coined "acid rain" in **1872** — so option **(4)** is correct.
He described **coal burning** in **Manchester**.
**M.C. Mehta** is linked to the **1996** Taj Trapezium case, not the term.
xa: Acid rain = any precipitation (rain, snow, fog, mist, hail) with **pH below 5.6**.
Typical acid rain **pH 4.2-4.4**; normal rain ~**5.6**.
Main culprits: **SO2 and NOx**.

n72fd5385d6d.s: The principal pollutant identified as threatening the Taj Mahal, especially from industries around Agra, is
o: sulphur dioxide, notably associated with the Mathura refinery
n72fd5385d6d.x: Sulphur dioxide is the principal pollutant identified in relation to the Taj Mahal, with industrial sources around Agra, notably the Mathura refinery.
n72fd5385d6d.tq: Link the monument with the specific pollutant and nearby industrial source.
xs: The Taj is threatened mainly by **sulphur dioxide**, notably from the **Mathura refinery** — so option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC 2018**).
SO2 comes from **industries around Agra**; methane, CFCs and CO are not named.
xa: The resulting damage is called **marble cancer**.
**M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1996)**: SC barred **coal/coke** use by TTZ industries.
TTZ covers **Agra, Firozabad, Mathura, Hathras, Etah** + **Bharatpur**.

na5cbc6552b5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Taj Trapezium Zone?
o: The order permitted industries in the zone to keep using coal and coke without restriction
It includes districts in Uttar Pradesh and Bharatpur in Rajasthan
The Supreme Court order in M.C. Mehta v. Union of India was delivered in 1996
na5cbc6552b5.x: In 1996 the Supreme Court barred coal and coke use by TTZ industries and directed a shift to natural gas or relocation.
xa: TTZ protects the **Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri**.
Main Taj threat = **SO2**, notably the **Mathura refinery**.
Acid-rain decay of marble = **marble cancer**.

n21a0a73cc77.s: Although FGD was mandated in 2015, only ____ of India's 537 coal plants had installed it before the mandate was relaxed.
n21a0a73cc77.x: Only 39 of 537 coal plants had FGD; the mandate was later relaxed citing high costs.
xa: **FGD** removes **up to 95% of SO2** from flue gas.
Debate: **FGD relaxation (2025)** vs India being the **top SO2 emitter**.
India = **largest SO2 emitter globally (2022)** → over **20%** of emissions.

n401e0798146.s: Ammonium sulphate, which makes up nearly one-third of India's PM2.5, forms in the air from:
n401e0798146.x: Ammonium sulphate is a secondary particulate formed from SO2 and NH3.
xa: **Ammonia** comes from **fertilisers and livestock (77-80%)**.
**SO2** sources: coal and oil burning, esp. **coal-fired power plants**, smelting, vehicles, volcanoes.
India is the **largest SO2 emitter globally (2022)** → over **20%** of anthropogenic emissions.

n9a37f66f4ae.s: Which organisation monitors precipitation chemistry in India under the WMO Global Atmosphere Watch and the Background Air Pollution Monitoring Network?
n9a37f66f4ae.x: The India Meteorological Department monitors precipitation chemistry under the WMO Global Atmosphere Watch and BAPMoN.
n9a37f66f4ae.tq: Use the institutional-function pairing to identify the responsible agency.
xs: **IMD** monitors precipitation chemistry — so option **(4)** is correct.
This is under the WMO **Global Atmosphere Watch** / **BAPMoN**.
The **IMO** caps sulphur in ship fuel; it does not monitor rain chemistry in India.
xa: **NAMP** was started by **CPCB** in **1984**.
**SAFAR** is run by **MoES (IITM Pune)**.
Acid rain = precipitation with **pH below 5.6**.

nddc81c02dbd.s: The WHO Air Quality Guideline (2021) for annual PM2.5 is:
nddc81c02dbd.x: The WHO annual PM2.5 guideline is 5 µg/m³, against India's NAAQS of 40 µg/m³.
xa: WHO PM2.5 annual limit (**5**) is **8 times** stricter than India's NAAQS (**40**).
**WHO AQG 2021**: PM10 24-h **45**; NO2 annual **10 µg/m³**.
**NCR winter PM2.5** is nearly **35 times** the WHO limit.
nddc81c02dbd.fixed: stem said 'annual' but pair 3 is a 24-hour standard

nd310a618bad.s: How many pollutants are covered under India's National Ambient Air Quality Standards?
nd310a618bad.x: NAAQS cover 12 pollutants, including PM10, PM2.5, SO2, NO2, CO, O3, NH3, lead, benzene, benzo(a)pyrene, arsenic and nickel.
xa: NAAQS notified **1982**; revised **1994** and **2009**.
**Ozone** first included in the **2009** revision.
**NAQI** uses a **0-500** scale.

n255e8ebd906.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the eight pollutants covered by the National Air Quality Index?
n255e8ebd906.x: Benzene is included in the 12-pollutant NAAQS set, but not among the eight pollutants used in the NAQI list stated here.
n255e8ebd906.tq: Find the pollutant belonging to the broader NAAQS list rather than the AQI eight.
xs: **Benzene** is not among the NAQI's eight — so option **(3)** is correct.
NAQI's **8 pollutants**: **PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, Pb** — so **ammonia**, **PM2.5** and **lead** are included.
Benzene is one of the extra four in the **12-pollutant NAAQS** (with benzo(a)pyrene, arsenic, nickel).
xa: **CAAQMS** does track **benzene**.
NAQI was launched in **2015** under **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan**, published by **CPCB**.
Motto: "**One Number - One Colour - One Description**".

n285ad03aa49.s: Which pollutant was included for the first time in the 2009 revision of the National Ambient Air Quality Standards?
n285ad03aa49.x: Ozone was included for the first time in the 2009 revision of the NAAQS.
n285ad03aa49.tq: Identify the pollutant linked to the specific revision year.
xs: **Ozone** was included for the first time in the **2009** revision — so option **(3)** is correct.
**CO, SO2** and **lead** are among the other AQI pollutants in NAAQS.
xa: NAAQS: notified **1982**; revised **1994** and **2009**.
NAAQS covers **12 pollutants**.
Ground-level ozone forms from **NOx + VOCs in sunlight** → asthma, eye irritation, crop damage.

nc1071a0a42d.s: India's NAAQS annual limit for SO2 in ecologically sensitive areas is:
nc1071a0a42d.x: SO2 limits are 80 µg/m³ (24-hour), 50 µg/m³ annual urban and 20 µg/m³ annual in ecologically sensitive areas.
xa: The SO2 limits are under NAAQS (**Air Act, 1981**).
**FGD** removes **up to 95% of SO2** from thermal-plant flue gas.
NAAQS revised in **1994** and **2009**.

n7b99a66ee35.s: The National Air Quality Index covers how many pollutants on a scale of 0–500?
n7b99a66ee35.x: The NAQI covers eight pollutants—PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3 and Pb—on a 0–500 scale.
n7b99a66ee35.tq: Split the options by matching the exact number with the listed components.
xs: The **NAQI** covers **8 pollutants** on a **0-500** scale — so option **(1)** is correct.
They are **PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, Pb**.
**12** is the NAAQS count, not the AQI.
xa: Published by **CPCB**; launched **2015** under **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan**.
Generated **hourly** from **CAAQMS**; shown on the CPCB website.
Motto: "**One Number - One Colour - One Description**".

n91179827834.s: The National Air Quality Index, implemented by the CPCB, was launched in 2015 under the:
n91179827834.x: The index was launched in 2015 under the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan and is implemented by the CPCB.
xa: Motto: "**One Number - One Colour - One Description**".
Covers **8 pollutants** on a **0-500** scale.
Data generated **hourly** from **CAAQMS**.

ncad8a3b1709.s: The expression “One Number – One Colour – One Description” is associated with which of the following?
ncad8a3b1709.x: “One Number – One Colour – One Description” is the communication principle associated with the AQI.
ncad8a3b1709.tq: Discriminate between closely related air-quality instruments and programmes.
xs: "**One Number - One Colour - One Description**" is the motto of the **National Air Quality Index** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**NAAQS** are standards (**12 pollutants**); **GRAP** is the Delhi-NCR action plan; **SAFAR** is MoES forecasting.
xa: NAQI: **CPCB**, launched **2015** under **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan**.
**8 pollutants**, **0-500** scale.
**0-50** Good (dark green) up to **401-500** Severe (maroon).

n11c8966a90b.s: The National Air Quality Monitoring Programme (NAMP) was started by the CPCB in:
n11c8966a90b.x: NAMP began in 1984 and monitors SO2, NO2, PM10 and PM2.5.
xa: NAMP now has **1,646 stations in 603 cities** (March **2026**).
**CAAQMS** data reach the public through the **SAMEER** app.
⚠ **SAMEER** = CPCB/CAAQMS app; **SAFAR-AIR** = MoES app.

n7e21e734298.s: SAFAR, the air-quality forecasting system of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, is run through:
n7e21e734298.x: SAFAR is run by MoES through IITM Pune, with the SAFAR-AIR app.
xa: ⚠ **SAMEER** = CPCB/CAAQMS app; **SAFAR-AIR** = MoES app.
**GRAP** is enforced in Delhi-NCR by **CAQM**.
GRAP stages: **I** Poor, **II** Very poor, **III** Severe, **IV** Severe+.

n21a2edb6f5a.s: Which one of the following is a Government of India initiative to control industrial emissions and improve air quality?
n21a2edb6f5a.x: NCAP is the answer to 'government initiative to control industrial emissions' (APPSC 2025). Namami Gange, NRCP and the National Lake Conservation Plan are water-body conservation programmes.
n21a2edb6f5a.tq: APPSC 2025: industrial emission control initiative = NCAP.
xs: The **National Clean Air Programme** is the initiative to control **industrial emissions** — so option **(1)** is correct (**APPSC 2025**).
**Namami Gange**, **NRCP** and the **National Lake Conservation Plan** deal with water bodies, not air.
xa: NCAP launched **January 2019** by **MoEFCC**.
Revised target: **up to 40%** cut in PM10 by **2025-26**.
NCAP covers **130 cities in 24 States/UTs**.

n56f101d356a.s: VAYU (Wind Augmentation PurifYing Unit), a roadside air purifier, was developed by:
n56f101d356a.x: VAYU was developed by CSIR-NEERI; MoES supports GRAP with a 400 m forecasting system.
xa: VAYU = **Wind Augmentation PurifYing Unit**.
Cloud seeding uses **silver iodide**, potassium iodide, **dry ice**, common salt.
**SAFAR-AIR** is the MoES app.

nd8980d85c9e.s: Clean Air for Blue Skies Day is observed in India as Swachh Vayu Diwas on:
nd8980d85c9e.x: Clean Air for Blue Skies Day, observed on 7 September, is marked in India as Swachh Vayu Diwas.
nd8980d85c9e.tq: Recall the event-date equivalence without substituting another environmental observance.
xs: **Clean Air for Blue Skies Day** (**7 September**) is **Swachh Vayu Diwas** in India, so option **(2)** is correct.
It is also **National Clean Air Day**.
xa: **SVS 2026** awards were given on National Clean Air Day, **7 Sep 2026**.
Swachh Vayu Survekshan ranks **130** NCAP cities yearly since **2022-23**.
Vijayawada **ward 60** ranked **2nd** nationally in SVS 2026.

n7834d81cc64.s: The revised NCAP target is a reduction in PM10 of up to ____, or meeting the NAAQS, by 2025-26.
n7834d81cc64.x: The revised target is up to 40% PM10 reduction by 2025-26; 20-30% by 2024 was the original target.
xa: The PM10 NAAQS is **60 µg/m³**.
Base: **2019-20** levels in some notes; others use **2017-18**.
Progress: **103 cities** cut PM10; **22 cities** met NAAQS (2024-25 vs 2017-18).

n7b437643c48.s: The term “non-attainment city” under NCAP refers to a city that has:
o: Exceeded WHO guidelines for one consecutive year
Not prepared a City Action Plan for two years
Recorded PM10 levels above 100 µg/m³ for three months
Failed to meet NAAQS for five years
n7b437643c48.x: A non-attainment city is one that has failed to meet the National Ambient Air Quality Standards for five years.
n7b437643c48.tq: Discriminate the official definition from plausible duration and threshold substitutes.
xs: A **non-attainment city** has **failed NAAQS for 5 years** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The data used were **2014-2018**.
xa: **Million Plus** cities are also covered by NCAP.
NCAP covers **130 cities in 24 States/UTs** (older notes: **131/132**).
**PRANA** = Portal for Regulation of Air-pollution in **Non-Attainment** cities.

naafb30ead4a.s: PRANA, associated with the National Clean Air Programme, stands for:
o: Programme for Restoration of Natural Air in Non-Attainment areas
Portal for Registration of Ambient National Air standards
Programme for Reduction of Atmospheric Nitrogen and Aerosols
Portal for Regulation of Air-pollution in Non-Attainment cities
naafb30ead4a.x: PRANA means Portal for Regulation of Air-pollution in Non-Attainment cities and is used to track NCAP progress.
naafb30ead4a.tq: Exact acronym expansion and look-alike phrase discrimination.
xs: PRANA = **Portal for Regulation of Air-pollution in Non-Attainment cities** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It **tracks NCAP progress**.
xa: Non-attainment city = failed NAAQS for **5 years**.
NCAP is implemented by **CPCB** with SPCBs.
**Swachh Vayu Survekshan** ranks the **130** NCAP cities yearly.

ndec4321d88b.s: The Swachh Vayu Survekshan, an annual ranking of NCAP cities, has been held since:
ndec4321d88b.x: SVS has ranked NCAP cities annually since 2022-23; in SVS 2025 Indore topped the million-plus category.
xa: **SVS 2026**: Vijayawada **ward 60** ranked **2nd** nationally (Best Performing Wards).
SVS 2026 awards were given on **National Clean Air Day**, **7 Sep 2026**.
**Varanasi** recorded the highest % PM10 reduction (**APPSC 2024**).

n99315698b66.s: Which city recorded the highest percentage reduction in PM10 from 2017–18 to 2023–24 under the NCAP assessment?
n99315698b66.x: Varanasi recorded the highest percentage reduction in PM10 during the period 2017–18 to 2023–24.
n99315698b66.tq: Direct city-performance recall using nearby NCAP cities as distractors.
xs: **Varanasi** had the highest % PM10 reduction, **2017-18 to 2023-24** — so option **(3)** is correct (**APPSC 2024** key).
**Indore** topped **SVS 2025** (million-plus), a different ranking.
**Visakhapatnam** is AP's pollution hotspot: PM2.5 up **33%**.
xa: **103 cities** cut PM10; **22 cities** met NAAQS (2024-25 vs 2017-18).
Original NCAP goal: **20-30%** cut by **2024**.
NCAP outputs include **1,433 e-buses** and **309** mechanical road sweepers.

n3071cefe461.s: The National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) was launched in January 2019 by which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
n3071cefe461.x: NCAP was launched in January 2019 by MoEFCC and is coordinated by CPCB with the SPCBs. MoES runs SAFAR forecasting, MoRTH notifies vehicle emission norms, and Jal Shakti oversees Namami Gange.
xs: NCAP was launched in **January 2019** by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**MoES** runs **SAFAR** (IITM Pune), not NCAP.
xa: NCAP is implemented/coordinated by **CPCB** with **SPCBs**.
Funded via CSS "**Control of Pollution**".
NCAP linked to **SDGs** and **Viksit Bharat 2047**.

n025e5403d23.s: Flue Gas Desulphurisation can remove up to ____ of sulphur dioxide.
n025e5403d23.x: FGD can remove up to 95 per cent of SO2, which comes mainly from burning coal and oil and from ore smelting.
xa: IIT Delhi study: curbing power-plant SO2 could prevent **~1.24 lakh deaths a year**.
Only **39 of 537** coal plants had FGD despite a **2015** mandate; the government later **relaxed** it.
**Lichens** are bioindicators of SO2 → they disappear where SO2 is high.

nd307ae28347.s: Stubble burning after paddy and wheat harvest is especially associated with which months and states?
o: July–August in Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
October–November in Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh
April–May in Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra
January–February in Bihar, Jharkhand and Odisha
nd307ae28347.x: Paddy and wheat stubble is mainly burnt during October–November in Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh.
nd307ae28347.tq: Combine the seasonal and geographical clues to identify the correct pair.
xs: Stubble burning peaks in **October-November** in **Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh**, so option **(2)** is correct.
It follows the **paddy/wheat harvest**.
xa: **In-situ** management: **Happy Seeder** machinery subsidy + **Pusa bio-decomposer** (**IARI**).
CSS on **in-situ crop residue management machinery** started in **2018**.
**Bihar** suspended DBT registration of **1,807 farmers** for stubble burning in **2025-26**.

nbcda33f51a1.s: The Pusa bio-decomposer used for crop-residue management was developed by which institution?
nbcda33f51a1.x: The Pusa bio-decomposer is associated with the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI).
nbcda33f51a1.tq: Match the named technology with its developing institution.
xs: The **Pusa bio-decomposer** was developed by the **Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI)**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**CPCB** runs NAQI/NAMP; **IITM Pune** runs **SAFAR** for MoES.
xa: It is an **in-situ** residue-management method, along with **Happy Seeder** machinery.
**Ex-situ** methods: **pelletisation**, torrefaction, briquetting, co-firing.
Stubble burning: **Oct-Nov**, mainly **Punjab, Haryana, UP**.

n37b33b33883.s: Which authority enforces the Graded Response Action Plan in Delhi-NCR?
o: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
n37b33b33883.x: GRAP is enforced in Delhi-NCR by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM).
n37b33b33883.tq: Who-would-do-this-job identification of the implementing authority.
xs: **GRAP** in Delhi-NCR is enforced by the **Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM)**, so option **(4)** is correct.
It is supported by **MoES 400 m** forecasting.
xa: CAQM chairperson tenure: **3 years or age 70**.
**SAFAR** (MoES, IITM Pune) runs the Delhi forecast tied to GRAP.

n53ba54660f1.s: Which city emerged as Andhra Pradesh's pollution hotspot, with PM2.5 rising 33% between January 2024 and April 2026?
n53ba54660f1.x: Visakhapatnam's PM2.5 rose 33 per cent in that period and exceeded national limits.
xa: Source: **Respirer Living Science**, **21 Aug 2026**.
**Simhadri** thermal plant is in **Visakhapatnam**.
APPCB state action plan: **123 urban local bodies including 17 municipal corporations**.

n4fda6bc3f81.s: The APPCB state-level air-quality action plan covers how many urban local bodies?
n4fda6bc3f81.x: The plan covers 123 urban local bodies, including 17 municipal corporations.
xa: APPCB: **12 CAAQM stations** + **9 more** being installed.
Industries: **735 CAAQMS** across **682** units.
**Visakhapatnam** PM2.5 up **33%** (Jan 2024-Apr 2026).

n9c5bc206013.s: Which pollutant emitted during incomplete combustion can reduce the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood?
n9c5bc206013.x: Carbon monoxide combines functionally with blood haemoglobin and reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood, causing giddiness and potentially death.
n9c5bc206013.tq: Link the physiological effect directly with the pollutant associated with incomplete combustion.
xs: **Carbon monoxide** reduces the **oxygen-carrying capacity of blood** — so option **(1)** is correct.
CO comes from **vehicle exhaust**, **incomplete combustion** and smoking; it causes giddiness and even death.
**Ozone** causes asthma and eye irritation; **SO2** irritates eyes and lungs; **ammonia** drives secondary particle formation.
xa: Exam angle: "pollutant from vehicles that reduces O2 carrying capacity of blood" = **carbon monoxide**.
**CO** is a **primary** pollutant and also a gaseous **indoor** pollutant, along with **radon**.
**Catalytic converters** turn **CO**, HC and NOx into CO2, H2O and N2.

nd12adcbca08.s: Which technology is used to trap sulphur dioxide in power-plant smokestacks?
nd12adcbca08.x: Flue gas desulphurisation systems, commonly called scrubbers, trap SO2 in smokestacks.
nd12adcbca08.tq: Match the control device with the pollutant and point of application.
xs: **Flue gas desulphurisation (FGD) scrubbers** trap SO2 in power-plant smokestacks — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Catalytic converters** cut NOx, CO and hydrocarbons from vehicles; **liming** neutralises acidity in lakes and soils.
**Low-NOx burners** cut **NOx**, not SO2.
xa: FGD removes **up to 95% of SO2** from thermal plant flue gas.
FGD mandate came in **2015**; only **39 of 537** coal plants had it.
**US Clean Air Act** cut SO2 by over **90%** in several regions.

n400baf1086e.s: An electrostatic precipitator installed in an industrial unit is primarily intended to remove
o: fine particulates such as fly ash
n400baf1086e.x: An electrostatic precipitator removes fine particulates, particularly fly ash, from industrial emissions.
n400baf1086e.tq: Direct device–function recall with pollutant-category distractors.
xs: An **electrostatic precipitator** removes **fine particulates (fly ash)** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It does not remove CO2 or nitrogen; **SO2** is removed by **FGD** and **wet scrubbers**.
xa: **Bag filter** → dust/particulates by **fabric filtration**.
**Cyclone separator** → **coarse** particles by **centrifugal force**.
**Wet scrubber** → gases (**SO2**) and particles; **FGD** → **up to 95% of SO2**.

n53c77f1e8b4.s: BS-VI emission norms are equivalent to which European standard?
n53c77f1e8b4.x: BS-VI is equivalent to Euro 6; Euro 5 would have matched BS-V, the stage India skipped.
xa: India typically lagged Europe by **~5 years**.
**BS-VI** came nationwide on **1 April 2020**.
**BS-VII** (Euro 7 equivalent) is planned for **2026-27**.

n8b10b749a23.s: India's first vehicle emission norms for petrol vehicles came in:
n8b10b749a23.x: The first norms came in 1991 for petrol and 1992 for diesel vehicles; Euro-based Bharat Stage norms began in 2000.
xa: BS-I went nationwide from **1 April 2000**.
**Tractor norms** were first notified in **1999**.
Norms are notified under **Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989** by **MoRTH**.

n92d2fcfc606.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the first implementation of Bharat Stage-II norms?
n92d2fcfc606.x: BS-II was introduced in Delhi from 1 April 2000 and was extended nationwide in 2005.
n92d2fcfc606.tq: Distinguish the first-city date from the later nationwide date.
xs: **BS-II** was first introduced in **Delhi from 1 April 2000**, so option **(2)** is correct.
It went nationwide in **2005**.
**NCR from 1 April 2005** is BS-III; **April 2017** nationwide is BS-IV; **13 cities, 2010** is BS-IV's first phase.
xa: BS-II fuel sulphur = **500 ppm**.
BS-II brought the shift from carburettor to **multi-point fuel injection**.
**Euro II** in India = BS-II.

n5ab76e2f1ac.s: BS-IV emission norms were implemented nationwide in India in:
n5ab76e2f1ac.x: BS-IV became applicable nationwide in April 2017; BS-III had gone nationwide in 2010.
xa: BS-IV first came in **13 cities** in **2010**.
Fuel sulphur: BS-III **350 ppm**; BS-IV **50 ppm**.
**BS-V** was skipped; **BS-VI** from **1 April 2020**.

n625f5748c65.s: The decision to leapfrog from BS-IV to BS-VI was taken in:
n625f5748c65.x: The decision to skip BS-V and leapfrog to BS-VI was taken in 2016.
n625f5748c65.tq: Distinguish the decision year from the implementation and court-order years.
xs: The decision to skip **BS-V** and leapfrog to **BS-VI** was taken in **2016**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**2018** was the year of the **Supreme Court** order on BS-IV sales.
xa: BS-VI applied to all new vehicles from **1 April 2020**.
**BS-V** = the only stage India **skipped**.
BS-IV first came in **13 cities** in **2010**.

ne1fd224555d.s: BS-VI norms became applicable to all new vehicles in India from:
ne1fd224555d.x: BS-VI became applicable to all new vehicles from 1 April 2020.
xa: Leapfrog decision taken in **2016**.
**BS-VI Phase 2 (RDE)** from **April 2023**.
BS norms are notified by **MoRTH**.

ne026371c8e9.s: Euro emission norms cover carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and ____.
ne026371c8e9.x: The pollutants covered by Euro norms include carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and lead.
xa: **CO** binds **haemoglobin** and cuts oxygen supply.
**Lead** is a **neurotoxin**; leaded petrol phased out by **2000**.
BS-I limits: **CO 2.72-6.90 g/km**, **HC+NOx 0.97-1.70 g/km**.

nc7afeedb559.s: Real Driving Emissions testing under BS-VI Phase 2 differs from conventional laboratory testing because it is conducted:
o: only on a dynamometer in a laboratory
only after a vehicle is scrapped
on actual roads under real driving conditions
nc7afeedb559.x: RDE testing measures emissions on-road under real driving conditions and became applicable under BS-VI Phase 2 from April 2023.
nc7afeedb559.tq: Use the expansion of RDE and the laboratory-versus-road contrast.
xs: **RDE** tests are done **on-road under real driving conditions**, not only in a lab, so option **(4)** is correct.
They came under **BS-VI Phase 2** from **April 2023**.
xa: BS-VI itself went nationwide on **1 April 2020**.
**OBD-II** monitors emission performance continuously.
**BS-VII** (Euro 7 equivalent) is planned for **2026-27**.

nd5d006ba949.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the planned next step in the Bharat Stage sequence?
o: BS-VIII, equivalent to Euro 6, planned for 2026–27
BS-VII, equivalent to Euro 5, planned for 2035–36
BS-VII, equivalent to Euro 7, planned for 2026–27
BS-V, equivalent to Euro 7, planned for 2026–27
nd5d006ba949.x: BS-VII, planned for 2026–27, is expected to be equivalent to Euro 7.
nd5d006ba949.tq: Check both the stage number and the corresponding Euro equivalence.
xs: The next stage is **BS-VII**, equivalent to **Euro 7**, planned for **2026-27**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**BS-V** was **skipped**; **Euro 6** = BS-VI.
xa: **BS-VI** nationwide **1 April 2020**; **Phase 2 (RDE)** from **April 2023**.
**CAFE III** draft (**Jul 2026**) is also current.
India typically **lagged Europe by ~5 years**.

nca82034c615.s: The Chernobyl disaster is an example of:
nca82034c615.x: Chernobyl was a nuclear pollution accident; photochemical smog forms from NOx and hydrocarbons in sunlight.
xa: **Nanoparticles** pollute **water**, **soil** and the **food chain**.
**Bioremediation** uses **microorganisms** to remove or detoxify pollutants.
**Benzene** is a **carcinogen** (leukaemia).

na42b33148a5.s: In adopting equivalent emission standards, India has generally lagged Europe by about:
na42b33148a5.x: India generally lagged Europe by approximately five years in adopting equivalent emission standards.
xa: **Euro I** in Europe came in **1992** (some notes say **1983**); **BS-I** in India in **2000**.
**Euro II** in India = Delhi from **1 April 2000** (= BS-II).
Leapfrogging **BS-V** helped **close the gap with Europe** in one step.

n1584f9047b6.s: The Bharat Stage emission norms are notified under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 by which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
n1584f9047b6.x: The norms are notified under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, on the advice of CPCB and MoEFCC.
n1584f9047b6.tq: Apply the “who would do this job?” method to identify the notifying authority.
xs: BS norms are notified under the **Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989** by the **Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH)**, so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ They are set on **CPCB / MoEFCC** advice, but notified by **MoRTH**, not MoEFCC.
xa: **PUC** certificates are also mandatory under **CMV Rules 1989**.
Transport officers are trained at **ARAI Pune** and **IIP Dehradun**.
After a norm takes effect, registering authorities **cannot register** non-compliant vehicles.

ne7acde73805.s: A Pollution Under Control certificate is mandatory under:
ne7acde73805.x: A PUC certificate is mandatory under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.
ne7acde73805.tq: Identify the exact legal instrument instead of choosing a broader environmental law.
xs: A **PUC certificate** is mandatory under the **Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989**, so option **(4)** is correct.
Transport officers are trained at **ARAI Pune** and **IIP Dehradun**.
xa: BS norms are also notified under **CMV Rules, 1989**, by **MoRTH**.
**Vehicle Scrappage Policy (2021)**: fitness-based de-registration.
⚠ Notified by **MoRTH**, not **MoEFCC**.

nenvironment-2-5.s: The National Auto Fuel Policy of 2003 was based on the report of which committee?
nenvironment-2-5.x: The Auto Fuel Policy (2003) followed the Mashelkar Committee report.
n: The sequence was Mashelkar Committee followed by the National Auto Fuel Policy and then Euro norms. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
Euro-I was introduced in Europe in 1992. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
BS-IV was implemented in India from 1 April 2017. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
The National Auto Fuel Policy recommended the implementation of Euro emission standards. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
xa: India's first vehicle norms: **1991 (petrol)**, **1992 (diesel)**.
**Euro II** came to **Delhi** on **1 April 2000** (= BS-II).
⚠ BS norms are notified by **MoRTH**, not MoEFCC.

nb6acae23469.s: The principal rationale for moving directly from BS-IV to BS-VI was to:
o: eliminate the need for refinery modifications
reduce the number of vehicle manufacturers in India
address urgent urban air pollution and close the gap with Europe in one step
replace all petrol vehicles with electric vehicles
nb6acae23469.x: The leapfrog was intended to address urgent urban air pollution, particularly in the Delhi-NCR region, and to close the technology gap with Europe without two successive changeovers.
nb6acae23469.tq: Match the policy decision with its stated environmental and technological objective.
xs: The leapfrog aimed to tackle **urgent urban air pollution** and **close the gap with Europe in one step**, so option **(3)** is correct.
It avoided **two changeovers**; refineries still had to produce **10 ppm** fuel, so option (1) is wrong.
xa: Urgent pollution was especially in **Delhi-NCR**.
Decision taken in **2016**; BS-VI from **1 April 2020**.
Vehicle prices **rose** with new technology, offset by **health savings**.

n92157f6e033.s: What is the fuel-sulphur limit under BS-VI norms?
n92157f6e033.x: Sulphur limits fall from 500 ppm (BS-II) to 350 ppm (BS-III), 50 ppm (BS-IV) and 10 ppm (BS-VI).
xa: **Euro II** ultra-low sulphur diesel = **0.05% or less** (= **500 ppm**).
Fuel sulphur fell from **500** to **10 ppm** in about **15 years**.
Refineries had to produce **10 ppm** BS-VI fuel nationwide.

n64cf9323b6b.s: Which of the following was a direct implication of BS-VI implementation for oil refineries?
o: They had to produce nationwide fuel containing 10 ppm sulphur.
They were permitted to increase fuel sulphur to 500 ppm.
They no longer needed to modify fuel-production facilities.
They had to stop producing petrol and diesel entirely.
n64cf9323b6b.x: Refineries had to upgrade their facilities to produce BS-VI fuel with a sulphur limit of 10 ppm nationwide.
n64cf9323b6b.tq: Connect the stricter fuel standard with the required refinery upgrade.
xs: Refineries had to produce **10 ppm** sulphur fuel nationwide, so option **(1)** is correct.
**500 ppm** was the **BS-II** level, so option (2) is the reverse.
xa: BS-VI fuel sulphur is **80%** lower than BS-IV (**50 ppm**).
Vehicle prices **rose** with new technology, offset by health savings.
Fuel sulphur fell from **500 to 10 ppm** in about **15 years**.

nfea98330031.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the CAFE III draft?
o: Its targets are about 21% stricter than the September 2025 proposal.
It proposes fuel-efficiency norms for cars from April 2027.
It provides credits for ethanol, CBG and biofuels.
It proposes a flatter weight curve.
nfea98330031.x: The CAFE III third draft (16 July 2026) has targets about 21% more relaxed, not stricter, than the September 2025 proposal.
xa: Targets relaxed **~21%** vs the **Sept 2025** proposal.
Industry average weight = **1,229 kg**.
**E20** rollout notified **17 Feb 2026**.

nenvironment-36-23.s: Nanoparticles cause pollution of which of the following?
o: Food chain, acid rain and industrial emissions
Water, soil and the food chain
nenvironment-36-23.x: Nanoparticles pollute water and soil and enter the food chain.
n: Nanoparticles cause pollution of water, soil and the food chain. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 62-64]
xs: **Nanoparticles** pollute **water**, **soil** and the **food chain** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The other options mix in unrelated items such as **acid rain**, the **ozone layer** and **radioactive waste**.
xa: **Acid rain** is caused by **sulfur dioxide** and **nitrogen oxides**.
**Radioactive pollution** causes **hereditary changes** and **carcinogenesis**.
**Bioremediation** — **microorganisms** **remove** or **detoxify** pollutants.

n1557216cff6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the E20 rollout?
o: E20 was to be sold with a minimum RON of 91 from 1 April 2026.
Concerns include mileage reduction and possible damage to older vehicles.
n1557216cff6.x: E20 was to be sold in all States and UTs with a minimum RON of 95 (not 91) from 1 April 2026. The other statements are correct.
xa: **CAFE III** draft gives credits for **ethanol**, CBG and biofuels.
**CAFE III**: fuel-efficiency norms for cars from **April 2027**.
E20 debate was current in **Aug 2026**.

n1be73f18ff0.s: Euro II ultra-low sulphur diesel refers to diesel containing:
o: 0.005% sulphur or less, equivalent to 50 ppm
0.05% sulphur or less, equivalent to 500 ppm
0.001% sulphur or less, equivalent to 10 ppm
0.5% sulphur or less, equivalent to 5,000 ppm
n1be73f18ff0.x: Euro II ultra-low sulphur diesel contains 0.05% sulphur or less, which is equivalent to 500 ppm.
n1be73f18ff0.tq: Convert percentage to parts per million before selecting the answer.
xs: Euro II ultra-low sulphur diesel = **0.05% or less**, equal to **500 ppm**, so option **(2)** is correct (**UPPSC 2013** key).
**50 ppm** is the **BS-IV** limit and **10 ppm** the **BS-VI** limit.
xa: **BS-II** = Euro II, with **500 ppm** fuel sulphur.
**BS-III** fuel sulphur = **350 ppm**.
BS-II began in **Delhi** on **1 April 2000**.

nbc4ccec3e08.s: Which one of the following sets contains only correct water-quality associations?
o: NTU—turbidity; TDS—dissolved salts; coliform count—faecal contamination
nbc4ccec3e08.x: NTU is used for turbidity, TDS represents dissolved salts, and coliform count indicates faecal contamination.
nbc4ccec3e08.tq: Start with the sure measurement unit and eliminate mismatched parameters.
xs: **NTU—turbidity; TDS—dissolved salts; coliform count—faecal contamination** is all correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
The other sets mix up these terms, e.g. NTU is not BOD or COD.
xa: Coliform count is expressed as **MPN/100 ml**.
Ganga bathing standard: faecal coliform **2,500 MPN/100 ml**.
**BOD** = oxygen bacteria need; **COD** = oxygen to oxidise all organic matter.

n436fc0cbbeb.s: The bathing-water standard cited for faecal coliform in the Ganga is
n436fc0cbbeb.x: The cited Ganga bathing standard for faecal coliform is 2,500 MPN/100 ml.
n436fc0cbbeb.tq: Compare the bathing standard with the stricter drinking-source standard.
xs: The **Ganga bathing** standard is faecal coliform **2,500 MPN/100 ml**, so option **(3)** is correct.
**50** is the CPCB **Class A** total coliform limit; **500** is **Class B**.
xa: **Class C** total coliform ≤ **5,000**.
Namami Gange's **main problem** is high **faecal coliform**.
**Class B** = outdoor bathing.

n13d42b4178c.s: Under CPCB water-quality criteria, the minimum dissolved oxygen for Class B water is:
n13d42b4178c.x: Class A, B and C require at least 6, 5 and 4 mg/L of dissolved oxygen; Class D also requires at least 4 mg/L.
xa: BOD: Class A **≤ 2**, Class B and C **≤ 3** mg/L.
Class D = **wildlife and fisheries**.
Clean water DO **> 8.0 mg/L**.

nf37e2ab6018.s: For CPCB Class A water, namely a drinking-water source requiring disinfection but not conventional treatment, the total coliform limit is
nf37e2ab6018.x: The CPCB Class A standard specifies total coliform not exceeding 50 MPN/100 ml.
nf37e2ab6018.tq: Distinguish the Class A total-coliform value from the bathing faecal-coliform value.
