nd83fd4700e4.s: EPR was first introduced into Indian waste law through the:
nd83fd4700e4.x: EPR first entered Indian waste law through the E-waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2011.
nd83fd4700e4.tq: Use the exact first-introduction instrument rather than a later plastic-specific rule.
xs: EPR first entered Indian law via the **E-waste (Management and Handling) Rules 2011** — option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ Some notes say the **Hazardous Wastes Rules 2016** introduced it first — not correct.
xa: SWM Rules 2016 also put **EPR** on producers/brand owners.
E-waste Rules lineage: **2011 → 2016 → 2022**.
**Battery Waste Management Rules 2022** cover batteries under EPR.

n69a528cf963.s: China's National Sword Policy of 2018 and Thailand's 2025 measure primarily restrict:
o: Domestic manufacture of all plastic products
n69a528cf963.x: China's National Sword Policy and Thailand's 2025 measure restrict imports of plastic waste.
n69a528cf963.tq: Identify the regulated activity rather than the broad environmental theme.
xs: China's **National Sword Policy (2018)** and **Thailand's 2025 ban** restrict **plastic waste imports** — option **(1)** is correct.
They do not target hospital use, domestic manufacture or microplastics in food.
xa: **Basel** amendment on **plastic waste** is now operative.
**Global Plastics Treaty** process began at **UNEA-5.2 (Nairobi, March 2022)**.
Transboundary issue = physical transfer of hazardous waste, often to **developing countries**.

nbcefdf2024a.s: UNEA-5.2, held in Nairobi in March 2022, adopted which resolution that led to the establishment of the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC)?
nbcefdf2024a.x: The UNEA-5.2 resolution titled “End Plastic Pollution” established the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee.
nbcefdf2024a.tq: Use the exact title of the resolution rather than a broad subject description.
xs: **UNEA-5.2** (Nairobi, March 2022) adopted the resolution "**End Plastic Pollution**" — option **(3)** is correct.
It set up the **Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC)**.
xa: INC venues: **Punta del Este, Paris, Nairobi, Ottawa, Busan (INC-5, 2024), Geneva (INC-5.2, Aug 2025)**.
No agreement — sticking points: **production caps**, chemicals of concern, finance.

n940c494fce0.s: Which of the following persons or entities may legally deal in e-waste under the E-waste (Management) Rules, 2022?
o: Only registered producers, manufacturers, refurbishers and recyclers
n940c494fce0.x: The Rules permit only registered producers, manufacturers, refurbishers and recyclers to deal in e-waste.
n940c494fce0.tq: Apply the registration requirement to a practical e-waste transaction.
xs: Only **registered producers, manufacturers, refurbishers and recyclers** may deal in e-waste — option **(4)** is correct.
**Unregistered scrap dealers** and informal dismantlers are excluded.
xa: E-waste must **not be mixed** with other waste.
Producers register on the **CPCB portal** and buy **digital EPR certificates**.
Rules in force **1 April 2023**.

n99b01bfc8f0.s: Which of the following was issued by the CPCB in response to biomedical waste generated during the COVID-19 period?
o: Global E-waste Monitor and Basel Protocol
R2 electronics recycling code and plastic treaty guidelines
COVID19BWM tracking app and COVID-19 waste guidelines
n99b01bfc8f0.x: The CPCB issued COVID-19 biomedical-waste guidelines in 2020 and introduced the COVID19BWM tracking app.
n99b01bfc8f0.tq: Match the emergency, authority and digital tracking instrument.
xs: **CPCB** issued **COVID-19 waste guidelines** in **2020** and the **COVID19BWM** tracking app — option **(3)** is correct.
**Global E-waste Monitor** is by ITU/UNITAR; **R2** is an e-waste certification; **Swachh App** is Guntur's plastic-fine tool.
xa: BMW Rules 2016 use **barcoding and GPS tracking**.

nf4a67bd757c.s: Bisphenol A (BPA) is particularly associated with which resin-code category?
nf4a67bd757c.x: Resin code 7 ('others') includes polycarbonate, which releases bisphenol A (BPA), an endocrine disruptor. PET (1), PVC (3) and PP (5) are not the BPA-linked category.
nf4a67bd757c.tq: Link a chemical concern with the correct resin category.
xs: **BPA** is linked to resin code **7**, which includes **polycarbonate** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Polycarbonate** (hard bottles, containers) releases **bisphenol A**, an **endocrine disruptor**.
**PET (1)**, **PVC (3)** and **PP (5)** are not the BPA category.
xa: **PET** leaches additives when heated.
Resin codes: 1 PET, 2 HDPE, 3 PVC, 4 LDPE, 5 PP, 6 PS, 7 others.

nad5aa9d5070.s: Which standard must compostable plastics meet?
nad5aa9d5070.x: Compostable plastics must meet the IS/ISO 17088 standard.
nad5aa9d5070.tq: Recall the exact technical standard rather than a general environmental certification.
xs: Compostable plastics must meet **IS/ISO 17088** — option **(3)** is correct.
The notes name no other standard for compostable plastics.
xa: **PWM Amendment Rules 2024** defined **biodegradable plastics** and required **CPCB certification** for makers.
**PWM Amendment Rules 2026**: **QR-code traceability**; classes rigid, flexible, multi-layered.

n85dc9c9cffa.s: What does the R2 Code of Practices primarily promote?
o: Environmentally responsible practices in electronics recycling
n85dc9c9cffa.x: R2, or Responsible Recycling, is a code of practices promoting environmentally responsible electronics recycling.
n85dc9c9cffa.tq: Expand the abbreviation and link it to its specific sector.
xs: The **R2 Code of Practices** promotes **environmentally responsible practices in electronics recycling** — option **(1)** is correct (UPSC 2021).
**R2 = Responsible Recycling**, a global certification for **e-waste recyclers**.
xa: Formal chain: consumer → collection centre / producer take-back → **authorised dismantler** → **authorised recycler** → recovered materials.
**78%** of e-waste is processed informally, by **open burning and acid baths**.
**468 authorised recyclers**, **1.6 MT** capacity (CPCB 2024).

n41f395e3d6b.s: How many colour categories does the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016 use?
n41f395e3d6b.x: The 2016 Rules use four colour categories with barcoding and GPS tracking; ten categories belonged to the 1998 Rules.
xa: Tracking: **barcoding and GPS tracking**.
Scale (2024): **1.89 lakh** health-care facilities generate **800+ tonnes/day**.

n4df3111c6a7.s: Biomedical waste is waste arising from the diagnosis, treatment or immunisation of:
n4df3111c6a7.x: Biomedical waste arises from the diagnosis, treatment or immunisation of humans or animals and includes blood, sharps, cultures and expired medicines.
xa: About **85%** of healthcare waste is general non-hazardous; **~15%** hazardous (WHO).
Biomedical category examples: **syringes, gloves**.

n4dc2d16acff.s: Biomedical waste in Andhra Pradesh is sent to Common Bio-Medical Waste Treatment Facilities primarily for
o: Production of RDF for cement kilns only
n4dc2d16acff.x: Biomedical waste is sent to Common Bio-Medical Waste Treatment Facilities for incineration. It is not intended for open dumping or untreated agricultural composting.
n4dc2d16acff.tq: Identify the prescribed treatment route for a specialised waste stream.
xs: AP sends biomedical waste to **CBMWTFs** for **incineration** (2024-25) — option **(3)** is correct.
Open dumping and untreated composting are not permitted routes.
xa: **Yellow** category BMW → incineration / **plasma pyrolysis** / deep burial.
BMW Rules 2016 use **barcoding and GPS tracking**.
India (2024): **1.89 lakh** facilities generate **800+ tonnes/day**.

n155efc03894.s: Which one of the following best illustrates the contribution of biomining of legacy waste to a circular economy?
o: It permanently stores all waste without recovery.
It increases the generation of mixed municipal waste.
It recovers useful materials from old waste dumps for productive reuse.
It replaces source reduction with open dumping.
n155efc03894.x: Biomining of legacy waste supports the circular economy by recovering materials from old waste accumulations for reuse or further processing.
n155efc03894.tq: Identify the option that reflects resource recovery and circularity.
xs: Biomining **recovers useful materials from old waste dumps for productive reuse**, supporting the **circular economy** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Biomining** = excavating legacy waste and separating it into **recyclables, RDF, bio-soil and inert fill**.
It does not store waste permanently, increase mixed waste or replace source reduction — options (1), (2), (4) are wrong.
xa: **Legacy waste** = old MSW piled in dumpsites for years; emits **methane**, pollutes groundwater.
**SWM Rules 2026:** legacy dumps mapped, time-bound biomining with **quarterly** reports.
AP example: **Ongole** is biomining its **Guthikondavaripalem** yard — **1.76 lakh t** of 2.56 lakh t processed.
**Urban mining** recovers iron, steel, copper, aluminium, plastics from e-waste.

necf49ca50cf.s: Old municipal solid waste piled in dumpsites for years, emitting methane and polluting groundwater, is called:
necf49ca50cf.x: That is legacy waste; biomining excavates it and separates it into recyclables, RDF, bio-soil and inert fill.
xa: Biomining of legacy waste supports the **circular economy**.
**3R** = **Reduce, Reuse, Recycle**; **source reduction** is the top of the hierarchy.
⚠ "**Regain**" is not one of the 3R (APPSC-GS **2025**).

n1ad562e5c35.s: As stated by the Chief Minister in February 2026, Andhra Pradesh inherited about how much legacy waste?
n1ad562e5c35.x: AP inherited about 108 lakh tonnes of legacy waste; Ongole is biomining its Guthikondavaripalem dump yard and supplying RDF to cement plants.
xa: **Anantapur** is setting up a **170 TPD** waste-processing plant (Jul 2026).
AP: **2 CHWTSDFs** at **Anakapalli** and **SPSR Nellore**; **6 pre-processing** facilities.
AP **Circular Economy and Waste Recycling Policy 2025-30** — guidelines via **G.O. Ms. No. 26**.

n16902fbe2ef.s: Which one of the following is NOT a hazardous constituent released by old computers?
n16902fbe2ef.x: Old computers can release beryllium, cadmium, chromium, mercury and lead, besides PCBs and PBBs. Plutonium is not included in this list.
n16902fbe2ef.tq: Find the outsider among the listed hazardous constituents.
xs: **Plutonium** is not released by old computers — option **(2)** is the answer (UPSC 2013 key).
Old computers release **beryllium, cadmium, chromium, mercury, lead**, plus **PCBs, PBBs**.
⚠ Trap: NOT heptachlor, NOT plutonium.
xa: **Mercury** — brain and kidney damage; **cadmium** — kidney and bone damage.
**RoHS** limits lead, mercury, cadmium in new EEE.

nac84d0a01ad.s: India is presently described as the world’s ______ largest generator of e-waste, after China and the United States.
nac84d0a01ad.x: India is the third-largest e-waste generator, after China and the United States.
nac84d0a01ad.tq: Read the ranking together with the named countries to avoid reversing the order.
xs: India is the **third** (3rd) largest e-waste generator, after **China** and **USA** — option **(4)** is correct.
So **second**, **fourth** and **fifth** are wrong.
xa: India's e-waste: **2.2 million tonnes (2025)**.
**First e-waste clinic**: **Bhopal**.
India also ranks third among dry MSW generators for **textile waste**.

n3a6d8f849c6.s: The e-waste generation attributed to India for 2025 was approximately:
n3a6d8f849c6.x: India’s e-waste generation was reported as approximately 2.2 million tonnes in 2025. The 3.54 lakh tonnes figure refers to e-waste collected and processed in FY 2021.
n3a6d8f849c6.tq: Separate generation figures from collection-and-processing figures and compare their units.
xs: India generated about **2.2 million tonnes** of e-waste in **2025** — option **(2)** is correct.
**1.75 MT** is an earlier figure (Oct 2025); **1.6 MT** is recycler capacity; **3.54** lakh tonnes was processed in FY 2021.
xa: **468 authorised recyclers**, **1.6 MT** capacity (CPCB 2024).
**78%** processed informally; only **10-20%** of materials recovered.

n53f4a9d4ba6.s: The Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 replaced the battery rules of:
n53f4a9d4ba6.x: The 2022 Rules replaced the 2001 rules and cover EV, portable, automotive and industrial batteries under EPR.
xa: **E-waste Rules 2022** replaced the **2016** Rules (which replaced 2011).
**Household examples** of hazardous waste include **batteries**; under SWM 2026 they go to the **special care** bin.

n20f2766d8d9.s: Which pair of places is correctly associated with informal e-waste recycling hubs?
n20f2766d8d9.x: Seelampur in Delhi and Moradabad are identified as informal e-waste recycling hubs.
n20f2766d8d9.tq: Match the locations with the distinctive informal e-waste activity.
xs: **Seelampur** (Delhi) and **Moradabad** (UP) are informal e-waste hubs — option **(1)** is correct.
**Indore**, **Tirupati** and **Visakhapatnam** feature in cleanliness rankings, not as e-waste hubs.
xa: **78%** of e-waste is processed informally (Jun 2026).
Informal workers use **open burning and acid baths**.

n69b19082b29.s: Which one of the following is the most appropriate action for a citizen disposing of an old electronic device?
o: Burn it to recover copper and aluminium
Mix it with municipal solid waste after removing the battery
Sell or deposit it with an authorised recycler or collection centre after wiping data
Hand it over to any informal dismantler without data removal
n69b19082b29.x: Citizens should use authorised recyclers or collection centres and wipe personal data before handing over old electronics.
n69b19082b29.tq: Apply the recommended citizen action while avoiding unsafe informal handling.
xs: Citizens should **sell or deposit old electronics with authorised recyclers or collection centres** after **wiping data** — option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-GS 2025).
**Burning** and **informal** dismantling are harmful; e-waste must **not be mixed** with MSW.
xa: "Invisible e-waste": **vapes, USB cables, LED accessories** thrown in regular trash (Jun 2026).
AP collected **60,392 kg** of e-waste (SES 2025-26).

n902ef6f9c9b.s: The Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016 replaced which earlier rules?
o: Municipal Solid Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2000
n902ef6f9c9b.x: The Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016 replaced the Biomedical Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 1998, which had ten categories.
n902ef6f9c9b.tq: Use the predecessor-successor relationship to distinguish rules with similar environmental subject matter.
xs: The **BMW Management Rules 2016** replaced the **BMW (M&H) Rules 1998** — option **(3)** is correct.
The 1998 Rules had **10 categories**; the 2016 Rules use **4 colour categories**.
xa: Amended in **2018** and **2019**.
Cover **100%** of healthcare facilities; **barcoding and GPS tracking**.
⚠ "**10** colour-coded categories" mixes up the 1998 Rules.

nda15a7722ba.s: Mercury-added products such as fluorescent lamps are being phased out under which convention?
nda15a7722ba.x: Mercury-added products are phased out under the Minamata Convention; Stockholm deals with persistent organic pollutants.
xa: Minamata Convention (**2013**): dental amalgam phase-out by **2034**.
**PFAS** ("forever chemicals") are now listed under **Stockholm**.
Old computers release **beryllium, cadmium, chromium, mercury, lead** — ⚠ NOT heptachlor or plutonium.

nae0cacf84e2.s: Under the Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016, which is at the top of the waste-management hierarchy?
nae0cacf84e2.x: Prevention is at the top of the hierarchy; co-processing comes later, before safe disposal.
xa: Hierarchy: **prevention > minimisation > reuse > recycling > recovery > co-processing > safe disposal**.
**PIC** for import/export; **2024**: household **Deposition Centres**, simpler manifests.

n11d04c0e19d.s: The Fly Ash Utilisation Notification requires use of fly ash in bricks, cement and roads within ____ of thermal plants.
n11d04c0e19d.x: The notification applies within 300 km of thermal plants; fly ash can make bricks and partly replace Portland cement.
xa: Fly ash comes from **coal-based thermal power plants**.
**Steel slag** is used in road bases, agricultural soil and cement (UPSC **2020**).
**Red mud** comes from **alumina refining**; **phosphogypsum** from phosphatic fertiliser plants.

n14bb81cab17.s: Surat is known for a road built using which industrial waste?
n14bb81cab17.x: Surat has a steel-slag road; steel slag is used as road base, to improve agricultural soil and in cement production.
xa: **Surat** has a **steel-slag road**.
**Fly ash** — bricks, cement, roads within **300 km** of plants.

n1a7cd770bda.s: The Environment (Construction and Demolition) Waste Management Rules, 2025 took effect from:
n1a7cd770bda.x: The 2025 C&D Rules took effect from 1 April 2026; 1 October 2025 was the date in the draft SWM Rules.
xa: MoEFCC notified an **EPR framework for C&D waste** (2026).
India generates about **12 million tonnes** of C&D waste a year.

ne7909d1426f.s: Which scheme aims to formalise informal sanitation and waste workers?
ne7909d1426f.x: The NAMASTE scheme aims to formalise informal workers, who handle more than 70% of recycled plastic.
xa: Segregation at source is **under 25%** (Oct 2025).
**78%** of e-waste is also processed informally.

n74018bad140.s: Which group of chemicals is often called 'forever chemicals'?
n74018bad140.x: PFAS persist in the environment, occur in products such as food packaging and can accumulate in animal bodies.
xa: PFAS are now listed under the **Stockholm** Convention.
Stockholm now covers **34 chemicals**, incl. **chlorpyrifos** and PFAS.

n69d6a825b14.s: In the context of transboundary movement of hazardous waste, PIC refers to:
n69d6a825b14.x: PIC means Prior Informed Consent, a control associated with the import and export of hazardous waste.
n69d6a825b14.tq: Break the abbreviation into its regulatory meaning before evaluating the options.
xs: **PIC** = **Prior Informed Consent** — option **(4)** is correct.
Under **HOWM Rules 2016**, imports/exports follow **Basel** with PIC.
xa: **Rotterdam** (in force **2004**) is the PIC convention for hazardous chemicals and pesticides; India acceded **2005**.
**Basel** in force **5 May 1992**; India ratified **June 1992**.

n3f435069bb6.s: Under the Minamata Convention framework, dental amalgam phase-out is targeted by:
n3f435069bb6.x: The Minamata Convention concerns mercury, and dental amalgam phase-out is targeted by 2034.
xa: ⚠ **Basel** = hazardous waste; **Rotterdam** = PIC; **Stockholm** = POPs; **Minamata** = mercury.
**Coal power plants** are a big mercury source.

n18565da0f9b.s: The global issue involved in the transboundary movement of hazardous waste refers to:
o: exchange of agricultural seeds under biodiversity agreements
movement of only biodegradable waste between rural districts
transport of clean energy equipment to developed countries
physical transfer of hazardous waste for reprocessing or storage, often to developing countries
n18565da0f9b.x: Transboundary hazardous-waste movement involves the physical transfer of hazardous waste for reprocessing or storage, frequently to developing countries.
n18565da0f9b.tq: Use the operational meaning of the term rather than an unrelated environmental transfer.
xs: The issue is the **physical transfer of hazardous waste for reprocessing or storage**, often to **developing countries** — option **(4)** is correct (APPSC-G2 2025).
It is not about seeds, rural biodegradable waste or clean-energy equipment.
xa: Governed by the **Basel** Convention (1989; in force **5 May 1992**); India ratified **June 1992**.
HOWM Rules 2016 prohibit **import for disposal**.
China's **National Sword Policy (2018)** curbs plastic waste imports.

nenvironment-37-13.x: ITPGRFA covers plant genetic resources; Ramsar covers wetlands and Stockholm covers POPs.
n: The Ramsar Convention concerns wetlands. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 64-66]
The World Heritage Convention concerns natural and cultural heritage. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 64-66]
The ITPGRFA, or International Seed Treaty, concerns plant genetic resources. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 64-66]
The Stockholm Convention concerns persistent organic pollutants. [Environment · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 64-66]
xa: **Stockholm Convention** (**2001**) now lists **34 chemicals** incl. chlorpyrifos and PFAS.
**Basel Convention** (**1989**) covers transboundary movement of **hazardous wastes**.
**Rotterdam Convention** (in force **2004**) covers **prior informed consent**.

n9553acdb4f1.s: Every city is intended to have a permanent RRR Centre under
o: The Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016
n9553acdb4f1.x: Every city has a permanent RRR Centre under SBM-U 2.0. RRR is expanded in the cited context as Reduce, Reuse and Recover.
n9553acdb4f1.tq: Link an institutional facility with the correct mission.
xs: A permanent **RRR Centre** in every city is set up under **Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0** — option **(4)** is correct.
RRR here = **Reduce, Reuse, Recover**.
**GOBARdhan** is a **SBM-G** biogas scheme; the **HOWM Rules 2016** deal with hazardous waste.
xa: **SBM-U 2.0** launched **1 Oct 2021**, till **2026**; **₹1.41 lakh crore** over 5 years; goal **"Garbage Free" cities**.
**Challenge Fund ₹13,029 crore** for 10 lakh+ cities (2026).
SBM-U 2.0 target: **10,000 TPD** additional WtE capacity.

n510ea8f5f5b.s: Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan, introduced in 2012, was the renamed form of the:
n510ea8f5f5b.x: Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan was the renamed Total Sanitation Campaign and followed a saturation approach.
n510ea8f5f5b.tq: Discriminate between predecessor programmes with similar sanitation objectives.
xs: **Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan (2012)** was the renamed **Total Sanitation Campaign** — option **(3)** is correct.
It followed a **saturation approach**.
xa: **TSC (1999)** was **demand-driven, community-led**.
**CRSP (1986):** subsidised rural latrines; **ILCS (1980-81):** dry latrines to pour-flush.
**SBM (2014)** followed, with toilets for all and ODF villages and cities.

ne64ea898f91.s: Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban was launched on:
ne64ea898f91.tq: Use the exact launch date and reject nearby national-day distractors.
xs: SBM was launched on **2 October 2014** (Gandhi Jayanti) — option **(4)** is correct.
It was **announced** on **15 Aug 2014**; some notes give that as the launch date — the launch was 2 October.
xa: **Swachh Bharat Diwas** = **2 October**.
**SBM-U** covers urban toilets + solid waste management; **SBM-U 2.0** launched **1 Oct 2021**.
**SBM-G** was also launched on **2 October 2014**.

n3c338130118.s: GOBARdhan, launched in 2018 under SBM-Grameen, is associated with conversion of cattle dung, agricultural waste and solid waste into:
n3c338130118.x: GOBARdhan promotes conversion of cattle dung, agricultural waste and solid waste into biogas and bio-slurry, supported by a unified portal.
n3c338130118.tq: Identify the input-output relationship in a waste-to-resource initiative.
xs: **GOBARdhan** converts cattle dung, agri and solid waste into **biogas and bio-slurry** — option **(3)** is correct.
It was launched in **2018** under **SBM-G**, with a **unified GOBARdhan portal**.
xa: **SATAT + GOBARdhan** linkage targets **500 new CBG plants**.
**Anaerobic digestion** gives **methane** biogas + slurry used as manure.
**Swachhata Hi Seva** — fortnight shramdaan campaign every year since **2017**.

n551b27a871e.s: Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen is implemented by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation under the:
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
n551b27a871e.x: SBM-Grameen is run by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation under the Ministry of Jal Shakti. The ministry was renamed in June 2019.
n551b27a871e.tq: Identify the authority responsible for the programme.
xs: **SBM-G** is run by the **Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation**, **Ministry of Jal Shakti** — option **(2)** is correct.
The ministry was **renamed in June 2019**; **MoHUA** runs the urban mission and Swachh Survekshan.
xa: SBM-G launched **2 October 2014**; over **10 crore** toilets by 2019-20.
DDWS prepared the **Rural Sanitation Strategy 2019-2029**.
**IHHL incentive**: **₹12,000**.

n1b6d91cb943.s: Phase I of SBM-Grameen aimed to construct over how many toilets by 2019-20?
n1b6d91cb943.x: Phase I aimed at over 10 crore toilets and ODF villages; rural sanitation coverage rose from 39% (2014) to 100% (2019).
xa: Now nearly **12 crore** rural toilets (Aug 2026).
**ODF Plus** levels: **Aspiring → Rising → Model**; **95%+** villages ODF Plus (Aug 2026).

nf6b643848fa.s: The highest of the three progressive levels of ODF Plus villages under SBM-Grameen is:
nf6b643848fa.x: ODF Plus levels run Aspiring, then Rising, then Model, which is the highest.
xa: **Status (Aug 2026):** **95%+ villages ODF Plus**; **5 lakh+ ODF Plus Model**.
**SBM-G** is run by the **Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti**.
**IHHL incentive** = **₹12,000**.

n96284080b21.s: Under SBM-Grameen, the incentive provided for construction of an Individual Household Latrine (IHHL) is:
n96284080b21.x: The IHHL incentive under SBM-G is ₹12,000. ₹6,000, ₹10,000 and ₹15,000 are not the stated amount; separately, greywater support is ₹280/capita (villages up to 5,000) and ₹660/capita (above 5,000).
xs: The **IHHL incentive** under SBM-G is **₹12,000** — option **(3)** is correct.
**₹6,000**, **₹10,000** and **₹15,000** are not the stated amount.
xa: Greywater support: **₹280/capita** (villages up to 5,000) and **₹660/capita** (above 5,000).
Over **10 crore** toilets built by 2019-20; nearly **12 crore** now.
**Rural Sanitation Strategy 2019-2029** by DDWS.

ndef6b492e7c.s: The principal target of SBM-Urban 2.0, implemented during 2021-26, is to create:
ndef6b492e7c.tq: Separate the mission’s current target from the objectives of related urban programmes.
xs: SBM-U 2.0's goal is **"Garbage Free" cities** by **2026** — option **(2)** is correct.
SBM-U 2.0 runs **2021-26** and covers **all statutory towns**, not only riverfront or heritage cities.
xa: Launched **1 Oct 2021**; **₹1.41 lakh crore** over 5 years; **Centrally Sponsored**, all statutory towns.
Components: **100% source segregation**, door-to-door collection, **legacy dumpsite remediation**, C&D waste management.
**Garbage Free City** star ratings: **1, 3, 5 and 7** stars.

n751929d97eb.s: Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0 was launched on:
n751929d97eb.x: SBM-U 2.0 was launched on 1 October 2021, runs till 2026, has an outlay of about ₹1.41 lakh crore and is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme covering all statutory towns.
xa: Goal: **"Garbage Free" cities by 2026**.
**Challenge Fund ₹13,029 crore** for 10 lakh+ cities (2026).
Every city gets a permanent **RRR Centre** under SBM-U 2.0.

n41eee14edbf.s: The Garbage Free City star-rating system provides which of the following ratings?
n41eee14edbf.x: The Garbage Free City certification uses 1-star, 3-star, 5-star and 7-star ratings for waste management.
n41eee14edbf.tq: Recall the distinctive non-consecutive rating sequence.
xs: The **Garbage Free City** star rating uses **1, 3, 5 and 7** stars — option **(3)** is correct.
The ratings measure **waste management** under SBM-U 2.0.
xa: **ODF+** — toilets functional, clean, maintained; **ODF++** — plus safe faecal sludge management.
**Water+** — used water treated before discharge.
SBM-U 2.0 goal: **"Garbage Free" cities by 2026**.

nba3df798c1f.s: Swachh Survekshan, run by MoHUA under SBM-Urban, is conducted by:
nba3df798c1f.x: Swachh Survekshan, begun in 2016 under MoHUA, is conducted by the Quality Council of India.
xa: It is the world's **largest annual urban cleanliness survey**, with **160+ indicators**.
**Indore (MP)** keeps ranking **#1** as the cleanest city.
**Swachh Survekshan 2024-25** awards were conferred by the **President**.

ne402ef5e394.s: Which of the following correctly represents the cleanest-city result for the 2023 edition of Swachh Survekshan in the 10 lakh-plus category?
ne402ef5e394.x: Indore and Surat jointly occupied the cleanest-city position in the 2023 edition for cities with more than 10 lakh population.
ne402ef5e394.tq: Distinguish a joint ranking from single-city results in adjacent editions.
xs: In **2023**, **Indore and Surat** were jointly the cleanest city (10 lakh+) — option **(4)** is correct.
Indore alone had topped every edition from **2017 to 2022**; 2023 was shared.
xa: **2017 to 2022**: **Indore** every year.
**2024-25**: Indore, Surat, Navi Mumbai placed in the **Super Swachh League**; **Ahmedabad** topped the regular 10 lakh+ list.
Indore topped the Super Swachh League for the **8th time** (Jul 2025).

n7edefa80ea2.s: Which one of the following cities is described as India’s model zero-waste and landfill-free city?
n7edefa80ea2.x: Indore is identified as India’s model zero-waste or landfill-free city and has repeatedly ranked first in cleanliness assessments.
n7edefa80ea2.tq: Associate the distinctive zero-waste description with the correct city.
xs: **Indore (MP)** is the model **zero-waste / landfill-free** city — option **(1)** is correct (APPSC-G2 2025).
**Visakhapatnam** was 'Top Impact Creator' and **Tirupati** first in 'Safai Mitra Surakshit Shehar' (SS 2022).
xa: Indore topped the **Super Swachh League** for the **8th time** (Jul 2025).
Guntur Commissioner studied **Indore's model** (24 Jun 2026).
Indore uses the **Indore method** of aerobic composting — turning at intervals.

nb73c6b84ca3.s: Operation Clean Sweep, launched in May 2026, is a campaign of the Municipal Administration Department for:
o: Scientific solid-waste management in Tier-1 and Tier-2 corporations
Only coastal plastic clean-up in villages
nb73c6b84ca3.x: Operation Clean Sweep is the Municipal Administration Department’s campaign for scientific solid-waste management in Tier-1 and Tier-2 corporations.
nb73c6b84ca3.tq: Link the campaign with its department, timing and operational scope.
xs: **Operation Clean Sweep** (May 2026) is the Municipal Administration department's drive for **scientific SWM in Tier-1/2 corporations** — option **(3)** is correct.
It covered all **123 ULBs**, **23 May-20 Jun 2026**, under **Swarna Andhra-Swachh Andhra**.
xa: **Swarna Andhra-Swachh Andhra** was launched in **January 2025**.
GVMC threatened to seal an apartment without **two segregation bins** (28 Aug 2026).
Guntur Commissioner studied **Indore's model** (24 Jun 2026).

n40b1041d819.s: The two Common Hazardous Waste Treatment, Storage and Disposal Facilities (CHWTSDFs) in Andhra Pradesh are located at:
n40b1041d819.x: The two CHWTSDFs identified for Andhra Pradesh are located in Anakapalli and SPSR Nellore.
n40b1041d819.tq: Use location-based recall and distinguish the named facility sites from other Andhra Pradesh cities.
xs: AP's two **CHWTSDFs** are at **Anakapalli** and **SPSR Nellore** — option **(2)** is correct.
They are used for **secure landfilling** (2024-25).
xa: **6 pre-processing** facilities and **APEMC GPS tracking**.
AP **Circular Economy and Waste Recycling Policy 2025-30** targets industrial hazardous waste.
AP has **4,000+ industries** producing hazardous and non-hazardous waste (APPCB, 6 Feb 2026).

n1658d64e3a4.s: Which system is used by APEMC for tracking hazardous-waste movement in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Biometric tracking of every waste container
n1658d64e3a4.x: APEMC uses GPS tracking for monitoring hazardous-waste movement and management.
n1658d64e3a4.tq: Match the institution with the specific monitoring technology stated for it.
xs: **APEMC** uses **GPS tracking** of hazardous waste via GPS-fitted vehicles — option **(4)** is correct.
The **APEMC portal** tracks the movement in real time.
xa: **APCMMS** portal — real-time monitoring.
AP CHWTSDFs: **Anakapalli**, **SPSR Nellore**.
BMW Rules 2016 also use **GPS tracking** with **barcoding**.

n584c83793cd.s: Which agency functions as the state agency running urban sanitation under SBM-U 2.0 in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education
n584c83793cd.x: Swachha Andhra Corporation, or SAC, is the state agency running urban sanitation under SBM-U 2.0 in Andhra Pradesh.
n584c83793cd.tq: Identify the correct state agency from closely related institutional names.
xs: **Swachha Andhra Corporation (SAC)** runs urban sanitation under **SBM-U 2.0** in AP — option **(2)** is correct.
For SS 2026, SAC operationalised **Project Monitoring Units in 46 ULBs**, chosen on SS 2024 ranks.
xa: **CBMWTFs** handle biomedical waste — not the sanitation agency.
AP urban profile: **17 Municipal Corporations**, **113 Municipalities**, **7 Cantonment Boards**.
**Re Sustainability MoU** covers all **123 ULBs**; **ITC MoU** covers **30 ULBs**.

n25c3349cd0d.s: Clean Andhra Pradesh, popularly known as the CLAP programme, was launched on 2 October 2021 as:
n25c3349cd0d.x: CLAP was launched on 2 October 2021 under the name Jagananna Swachha Sankalpam. Swarna Andhra-Swachh Andhra is a later state drive launched in January 2025.
n25c3349cd0d.tq: Use the exact official name to distinguish related sanitation initiatives.
xs: **CLAP** was launched on **2 Oct 2021** as **Jagananna Swachha Sankalpam** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Swarna Andhra-Swachh Andhra** is the later State drive, launched **January 2025**.
xa: **Operation Clean Sweep** (May 2026) runs under Swarna Andhra-Swachh Andhra.
**SBM-U 2.0** was launched a day earlier, on **1 Oct 2021**.

n26751e623ea.s: APPCB has permitted how many cement industries to co-process incinerable, plastic and municipal waste?
n26751e623ea.x: The APPCB permitted 12 cement industries to co-process incinerable, plastic and municipal waste.
