n: Heat Action Plans are prepared by states and cities with support from NDMA and IMD. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 70-72]
xs: **Heat Action Plans** are **prepared** by **states** and **cities** — so option **(1)** is correct.
They get **support** from **NDMA** and **IMD**; neither body prepares them alone.
xa: Public awareness: **do's and don'ts**, **ORS distribution**, **cooling centres**.
Structural measures: **shade structures**, **drinking water points**.
NDMA heatwave guidelines were **updated 2019**.

ndisaster-management-34-6.s: A cold wave is best defined as:
o: A significant drop in minimum temperature below the normal climatological average during the winter season
A significant drop in maximum temperature below the normal climatological average during the summer season
A rise in minimum temperature above the normal climatological average during the winter season
A significant drop in rainfall below the normal climatological average during the winter season
ndisaster-management-34-6.x: A cold wave is a sharp drop in minimum temperature below normal in winter. The other options reverse the season or the direction.
ndisaster-management-34-6.tq: Recall the definition of a cold wave.
n: A cold wave is a significant drop in minimum temperature below the normal climatological average during the winter season. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
xs: A **cold wave** is a **significant drop** in **minimum temperature** **below** the **normal climatological average** in **winter** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The other options wrongly use **maximum temperature**, a **rise**, or **rainfall**.
xa: Cold-wave impacts: **hypothermia**, **frostbite**, **respiratory diseases**.
Most vulnerable: **homeless people**, **elderly**, **children**, **outdoor workers**, **street vendors**.
**Crop damage** due to **frost**; it **affects livestock**.

ndisaster-management-34-11.s: Which body issued the cold-wave guidelines that focus on preparedness, vulnerability mapping and community awareness?
ndisaster-management-34-11.x: These are the NDMA's guidelines on cold waves.
n: The NDMA guidelines focus on preparedness. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
The NDMA guidelines focus on vulnerability mapping. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
The NDMA guidelines focus on community awareness. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #34 · pp 72-74]
xa: IMD issues **Yellow**, **Orange** and **Red** cold-wave alerts.
Cold wave is a **notified disaster** eligible under **SDRF** and **NDRF**.
**Medical preparedness** is a protective measure.

nf89c9f6b82e.s: Disaster risk reduction (DRR) works best when it:
o: Concentrates only on post-disaster relief distribution
Addresses the underlying causes of vulnerability
Relies only on rescue by national forces
Focuses solely on rebuilding damaged infrastructure
nf89c9f6b82e.x: DRR is most effective when it tackles the underlying causes of vulnerability (APPSC 2024 key). Relief, rescue and rebuilding are response or recovery activities, not the core of risk reduction.
nf89c9f6b82e.tq: DRR = fix root causes of vulnerability (APPSC 2024).
xs: **DRR** works best when it **addresses the underlying causes of vulnerability** — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2024** key).
**Relief** and **rescue** belong to the **response** phase; **rebuilding** belongs to **recovery** — not the core of risk reduction.
xa: **Mitigation** (pre-disaster): **embankments, mangroves, zoning**.
**Significance:** the **DM Act 2005** moved India from **relief → risk reduction**.
**Risk = Hazard x Vulnerability / Capacity**.

ndaf746b86eb.s: The gas that leaked in the Bhopal Gas Tragedy of 1984 was:
ndaf746b86eb.x: The Bhopal leak was of methyl isocyanate (MIC). Chlorine, carbon monoxide and ammonia are common distractors but were not the gas released at Bhopal.
xs: The Bhopal gas was **methyl isocyanate (MIC)** — option **(2)**.
It was **not chlorine, CO or ammonia** — these are the usual distractors.
xa: Date: night of **2-3 December 1984**.
Plant of **Union Carbide India Ltd**, Bhopal.
A chemical leak = **anthropogenic / man-made** hazard.
Chemical accident rules: **MSIHC Rules 1989** + **CAEPPR Rules 1996**.

ndisaster-management-33-11.s: 'Cool roofs' as a heatwave-management measure involve:
o: Reflective coatings or white painting of roofs
ndisaster-management-33-11.x: Cool roofs use reflective coatings or white paint to keep buildings cooler.
n: Cool roofs use reflective coatings or white painting of roofs. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #33 · pp 70-72]
xa: **Heat Action Plans** are prepared by **states** and **cities**.
IMD issues **colour-coded alerts** for heatwaves.
Heatwave season runs mainly **March to June**.

ndisaster-management-20-14.s: Floods worsened by deforestation and landslides caused by unscientific construction are examples of:
ndisaster-management-20-14.x: They are socio-natural hazards, mixing natural processes and human action.
n: Floods can be worsened by deforestation. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 47-49]
Landslides can be caused by unscientific construction. [Disaster Management · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 47-49]
xa: **Technological** hazards include **dam failure**.
**Man-made** disasters arise from **human activity, negligence or technological failure**.
**Landslide** mitigation: **hazard zonation mapping**, early warning.

nc8d3fb07d5a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's legal framework for epidemics?
o: The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 provides the legal framework for biological disasters.
The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 was used during COVID-19.
The 2017 draft Public Health Bill was enacted and replaced the 1897 Act.
The 2017 draft Bill dealt with epidemics, bio-terrorism and disasters.
nc8d3fb07d5a.x: The 2017 draft Bill was meant to replace the 1897 Act but was never enacted.
xa: The **2020 amendment** made violence against health workers **cognizable and non-bailable**.
Penalty: **3 months to 5 years** jail + **Rs 50,000 to Rs 2 lakh** fine.
Critics note the 1897 Act does not define "**dangerous epidemic disease**".

ne916b26ad90.s: The 2020 amendment to the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 made violence against health workers:
ne916b26ad90.x: The 2020 amendment (ordinance April, Act September 2020) made such violence cognizable and non-bailable.
xa: Penalty for violence: **3 months to 5 years** jail + **Rs 50,000 to Rs 2 lakh** fine.
Grievous hurt: **6 months to 7 years** + **Rs 1-5 lakh** fine.
PM-ABHIM builds preparedness at **50 points of entry**.

n7f2159aeb70.s: NDMA's Biological Disaster Management guidelines were issued in:
n7f2159aeb70.x: NDMA, chaired by the Prime Minister, issued its Biological Disaster Management guidelines in 2008 under the DM Act.
xa: NDMA issued the **Biological Disaster Management guidelines** in **2008**.
The **March 2020** lockdown was ordered by **NDMA + MHA** under the **DM Act, 2005**.
**MoHFW** is still the **nodal ministry for epidemics**.

nc0859225d3c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about INSACOG?
o: Its full form is Indian SARS-CoV-2 Genomics Consortium.
It is a network of genome-sequencing laboratories that tracks SARS-CoV-2 variants.
It functions under DBT, ICMR, CSIR and MoHFW.
It was set up in December 2021.
nc0859225d3c.x: INSACOG was set up in December 2020, not 2021.
xa: INSACOG was set up in **Dec 2020**.
**ICMR-NIV Pune** is the apex virology lab with **BSL-4** containment.
COVID testing reached **1,364 government + 1,753 private labs** by Jan **2022**.

n0585e9e7647.s: Under PM-ABHIM, how many Integrated Public Health Laboratories are planned, one in every district?
n0585e9e7647.x: 744 IPHLs are planned, one per district; 631 is the number of Critical Care Hospital Blocks.
xa: PM-ABHIM also has **15 Health Emergency Operation Centres** + **50 BHISHM Cubes**.
Points of entry: preparedness at **50**.
AP got **10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 IPHLs** costing **Rs 250 crore**.

n34a8c1f0c40.s: Under the IHR (2005), Member States must report a possible PHEIC to WHO within:
n34a8c1f0c40.x: Member States must report possible PHEICs within 24 hours, build surveillance capacities and name a National IHR Focal Point.
xa: IHR (2005) has been **in force since 2007**.
⚠ **24 hours** is also the deadline for **urgent notifiable cases** under the **1897 Act**.
The **2024 amendments** added a **"pandemic emergency"** tier.

n474a539d305.s: The 2024 amendments to the International Health Regulations (2005) added a higher tier called:
o: Public Health Emergency of International Concern
n474a539d305.x: The 2024 amendments added a higher 'pandemic emergency' tier above the PHEIC.
xa: Centre asked states to step up **IDSP** surveillance for **Ebola** (23 May **2026**).
PHEICs must be reported to WHO **within 24 hours**.
The **WHO Pandemic Agreement** was adopted on **20 May 2025**.

n6f46b70b21c.s: Which of the following developments is associated with the BRICS New Delhi Declaration?
o: Adoption of the WHO Pandemic Agreement
Declaration of the May 2026 Ebola outbreak as a pandemic emergency
Creation of a sub-working group on an integrated early-warning system for infectious diseases
n6f46b70b21c.x: The BRICS New Delhi Declaration set up a sub-working group on an integrated early-warning system for infectious diseases.
n6f46b70b21c.tq: Match the international forum with its specific institutional outcome.
xs: The **BRICS New Delhi Declaration** created a **sub-working group on an integrated early-warning system for infectious diseases** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **WHO Pandemic Agreement** was adopted on **20 May 2025** by WHO, not BRICS.
The **Ebola** outbreak **did not meet** the pandemic-emergency criteria.
xa: Dated **13 Sep 2026** — the same day **CCBs and IPHLs** opened in AP.
Ebola advisory to states: **23 May 2026**.
**744 IPHLs** are a **PM-ABHIM** component.

n65d23d6f92e.s: India's national COVID-19 lockdown of March 2020 was ordered under the:
n65d23d6f92e.x: The lockdown was ordered by NDMA and MHA under the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
xa: **NDMA** is chaired by the **PM**; **SDMAs** by the **Chief Ministers**.
**MoHFW** remains the **nodal ministry for epidemics**.
The **MoHFW Disaster Management Cell** (Dec **2020**) is the nodal unit for pandemic planning.

n57e5fff0f18.s: India's NDMP (2016) aligns with the Sendai Framework, the SDGs and the:
n57e5fff0f18.x: The 2016 NDMP aligns with Sendai (2015-30), the SDGs and the Paris Agreement and covers all phases of disaster management.
xa: NDMA issued the **Biological Disaster Management guidelines** in **2008**.
The **DM Act 2005** is the law under which NDMA operates.
PYQ key: **vaccines before an outbreak** = **mitigation**.

nf4e3870535f.s: The WHO Pandemic Agreement was adopted on:
nf4e3870535f.x: It was adopted on 20 May 2025; the legally binding IHR (2005) have been in force since 2007.
xa: IHR: report possible **PHEICs** to WHO **within 24 hours**; name a **National IHR Focal Point**.
**2024 amendments** added a higher "**pandemic emergency**" tier.
⚠ **24 hours** = both urgent notifiable cases (1897 Act) and PHEIC report (IHR).

na9f8ee9ee8c.s: Which Ministry is the nodal ministry in India for the management of epidemics (biological disasters)?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
na9f8ee9ee8c.x: MoHFW is the nodal ministry for epidemics (PYQ), with DGHS as its technical arm and NCDC as the surveillance agency. MHA coordinates disasters in general, while Science and Technology and Environment ministries are not nodal for epidemics.
na9f8ee9ee8c.tq: Epidemic nodal = MoHFW; general DM = MHA.
xs: **MoHFW** is the **nodal ministry for epidemics** (PYQ) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**MHA** coordinated the COVID lockdown with **NDMA** under the DM Act, but is not nodal for epidemics.
Within MoHFW, **DGHS** is the **technical arm** and **NCDC** the surveillance agency.
xa: The **MoHFW DM Cell** (Dec **2020**) is the nodal unit for pandemic planning.
Epidemics count as **biological disasters**.
The **Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897** is the legal framework for biological disasters.

n7c4c3ef4a01.s: Which laboratory is regarded as the apex virology laboratory in India and has BSL-4 containment?
n7c4c3ef4a01.x: ICMR-NIV Pune is the apex virology laboratory and has BSL-4 containment facilities.
n7c4c3ef4a01.tq: Match the apex laboratory with its location and containment level.
xs: **ICMR-NIV, Pune** is the apex virology lab with **BSL-4** containment — so option **(3)** is correct.
**INSACOG** is a genome-sequencing consortium, and a **State Surveillance Unit** is part of IDSP.
xa: **BSL-3 labs** are being added through **VRDLs** and **PM-ABHIM**.
**INSACOG** was set up in **Dec 2020** under **DBT, ICMR, CSIR, MoHFW**.
COVID testing: **1,364 government + 1,753 private labs** by Jan **2022**.

n9d68493ac30.s: Distributing vaccines before the occurrence of an epidemic is classified under which phase of the disaster management cycle?
n9d68493ac30.x: Pre-outbreak vaccine distribution reduces the potential impact of an epidemic and is therefore a mitigation measure.
n9d68493ac30.tq: Classify the measure by asking whether it reduces impact before the event.
xs: **Distributing vaccines before an outbreak** is a **mitigation** measure (PYQ key) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Preparedness** = surveillance, stockpiles, hospital readiness, mock drills.
**Response** = isolation, quarantine, contact tracing; **Recovery** = restoring services, rehabilitation.
xa: Other epidemic mitigation measures: **sanitation** and **vector control**.
Epidemics count as **biological disasters**.
⚠ Vaccines **before** an outbreak = mitigation; treatment **during** it = response.

n4ca7af0c04d.s: Isolation, quarantine and contact tracing belong to which phase of epidemic management?
n4ca7af0c04d.x: They are response measures; sanitation is mitigation, mock drills are preparedness and rehabilitation is recovery.
xa: PYQ key: **distributing vaccines before an outbreak** = **mitigation**.
**Lockdown** and **treatment** also fall under the **response** phase.
The **NDMP (2016)** covers prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery.

na3e12ba3c1b.s: BHISHM Cubes, deployed during Operation Sindoor, are associated with which programme?
o: PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM)
na3e12ba3c1b.x: Under PM-ABHIM, MoHFW's DM Cell has 15 Health Emergency Operation Centres and 50 BHISHM Cubes, which were deployed during Operation Sindoor. NDRF, IDSP and Aapda Mitra are separate programmes.
xs: **BHISHM Cubes** belong to **PM-ABHIM (PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
PM-ABHIM provides **15 Health Emergency Operation Centres** + **50 BHISHM Cubes**, deployed during **Operation Sindoor**.
**IDSP** is a surveillance programme (**2004**), not the cubes' parent scheme.
xa: PM-ABHIM: **744 IPHLs**, one in every district.
PM-ABHIM: **631 Critical Care Hospital Blocks** in districts with over **5 lakh** people.
PM-ABHIM: preparedness at **50 points of entry**.

n840ef8869b3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about disease surveillance in India?
o: The Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP) was launched nationwide in 2018.
IDSP was launched in 2004 and now runs under the National Health Mission.
IDSP has a Central Surveillance Unit in Delhi.
IDSP works through State and District Surveillance Units.
n840ef8869b3.x: IHIP began in a few states in 2018 and went nationwide only from September 2021.
xa: IDSP is implemented by **MoHFW** and run by **NCDC**.
The **IHIP** portal pools grassroots data in **real time**.
Centre asked states to step up IDSP surveillance for **Ebola** (May **2026**).

n15f976d8c07.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three categories of reporting used in disease surveillance?
n15f976d8c07.x: Surveillance data are reported through syndromic (S), presumptive (P) and laboratory-confirmed (L) categories.
n15f976d8c07.tq: Expand the surveillance abbreviations and distinguish them from site categories.
xs: The three reporting categories are **Syndromic, Presumptive and Laboratory-confirmed** (S, P, L) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Sentinel and private sites** are additional data sources, not reporting categories.
xa: These feed **IDSP**, launched in **2004** under **NHM**.
The **IHIP** portal pools this grassroots data in **real time**.
IDSP units: **Central Surveillance Unit** (Delhi) + State and District units.

n3103351a9b0.s: Mapping hotspots and containment zones during an epidemic chiefly uses:
n3103351a9b0.x: Geospatial technology supports contact tracing, hotspot and containment-zone mapping and vaccine distribution planning.
xa: **BBMP** ran a **COVID war room with GIS** (PYQ).
AP's **Covid Pharma app** (**25 Apr 2020**) tracked buyers of cough, cold and fever medicines.

n3b275dbd933.s: The COVID war room supported by GIS was set up by which organisation?
n3b275dbd933.x: The GIS-supported COVID war room was set up by the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP).
n3b275dbd933.tq: Identify the local authority associated with the operational measure.
xs: The GIS-based **COVID war room** was set up by **Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP)** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**NCDC** runs IDSP; **ICMR-NIV Pune** is a BSL-4 lab; **MHA** coordinated the lockdown.
xa: **GIS real-time spatial mapping** works best for **vaccine distribution** (PYQ).
Geospatial technology can **perform contact tracing** and map **containment zones**.
AP's **Covid Pharma app** was launched on **25 Apr 2020**.

ndb9c45a62b2.s: The Covid Pharma application launched in Andhra Pradesh on 25 April 2020 was used to track persons purchasing which medicines over the counter?
o: Medicines for cough, cold and fever
ndb9c45a62b2.x: The AP Medical and Health Department launched Covid Pharma on 25 April 2020 to track people buying over-the-counter medicines for cough, cold and fever.
ndb9c45a62b2.tq: Combine the app’s launch date, authority and precise purpose.
xs: **Covid Pharma** tracked people buying OTC **medicines for cough, cold and fever** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was launched on **25 Apr 2020** by AP's **Medical and Health Department** (PYQ).
xa: **BBMP** ran a **COVID war room with GIS** (PYQ).
Geospatial technology supports **contact tracing** and **hotspot mapping**.
Other AP angles: **zoonoses action plan** (Jul **2026**) and **PM-ABHIM** units in **Vijayawada**.

n4016de7a080.x: Blue biotechnology covers marine applications; red is medical, green agricultural and white industrial.
xa: White biotech covers **enzymes, biofuels, bioplastics, precision fermentation** and green chemicals.
Red biotech example: **Cervavac** (qHPV) by **Serum Institute of India**.
Green biotech example: **Sub1** flood-tolerant rice via **marker-assisted selection**.

n468e5d10182.s: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic area of white biotechnology?
n468e5d10182.x: White biotechnology includes enzymes, biofuels, bioplastics, precision fermentation and green chemicals. Marine ecosystems relate to blue biotechnology rather than white biotechnology.
n468e5d10182.tq: Find the item belonging to a neighbouring biotechnology branch.
xs: **Marine ecosystems** belong to **blue** biotechnology, not white — so option **(1)** is correct.
**White** (industrial) biotech covers **enzymes, biofuels, bioplastics**, precision fermentation and green chemicals.
xa: Branches: **Red** = medical, **Green** = agriculture, **White** = industrial, **Blue** = marine.
Visakhapatnam was chosen for a **marine biomaterials** research facility (Jan **2026**).
Recombinant enzymes: **chymosin** (cheese), **amylase** (bread), **pectinase** (juice).

n65d8342c260.s: The fern Pteris vittata is a hyperaccumulator of:
n65d8342c260.x: Pteris vittata accumulates arsenic; Alyssum accumulates nickel and Thlaspi caerulescens zinc and cadmium.
xa: **Sunflower** → heavy metals; **uranium** and other radionuclides.
**Water hyacinth** → heavy metals and toxic materials in water.
⚠ **Cadmium** appears twice: Indian mustard and Thlaspi.

nd9f7fdcd3ca.x: Noori was a Pashmina goat (2012); Garima was a buffalo (NDRI, 2009) and Dolly a sheep (1996).
xa: **Ganga**, the first cloned **Gir** calf, came from **NDRI Karnal** (**2023**).
Dolly was the **first cloned mammal**.
⚠ Two clones from **NDRI Karnal**: **Garima** (buffalo) and **Ganga** (Gir calf).

n3a604e1b5dc.s: India accounts for approximately what share of global vaccine demand and is described as the world's largest vaccine manufacturer?
n3a604e1b5dc.x: India is identified as the largest vaccine manufacturer and meets approximately 60% of global vaccine demand.
n3a604e1b5dc.tq: Use the numerical figure as the deciding clue.
xs: India meets about **60%** of global vaccine demand and is the **largest vaccine manufacturer** — so option **(2)** is correct.
India's vaccine strength rests on indigenous platforms and makers such as **Serum Institute** and **Bharat Biotech**.
xa: Indigenous platforms: **mRNA, viral vector, protein subunit**.
**Cervavac** (qHPV) by **Serum Institute of India** targets HPV / cervical cancer.
**ZyCoV-D** by **Zydus Cadila** was the **first DNA vaccine** (COVID-19).

n31f0a7f0612.s: ZyCoV-D, associated with Zydus Cadila, is notable as India’s first indigenous:
n31f0a7f0612.x: ZyCoV-D was developed by Zydus Cadila and is identified as the first DNA vaccine, targeting COVID-19.
n31f0a7f0612.tq: Discriminate between vaccine platform and disease target.
xs: **ZyCoV-D** (**Zydus Cadila**) is the **first DNA vaccine**, against **COVID-19** — so option **(4)** is correct.
HPV is targeted by **Cervavac**, malaria by **R21/Matrix-M**, rotavirus by **Rotavac**.
xa: **Covaxin** = **Bharat Biotech with ICMR**, COVID-19.
Indigenous platforms: **mRNA, viral vector, protein subunit**.
⚠ First **DNA vaccine** = ZyCoV-D; first indigenous **gene-therapy** trial = haemophilia A at **CMC Vellore**.

nae7d672d0a4.s: The hybridoma technique for monoclonal antibodies dates to:
xa: Hybridoma = **B-cell + myeloma** fusion (**Kohler and Milstein**).
Haemophilia A gene therapy: **CMC Vellore**, DBT-supported.
**Diamond v. Chakrabarty** (**1980**): first living organism patented.

n679665cd059.s: Which recombinant enzyme is used in cheese production?
n679665cd059.x: Recombinant chymosin is used in cheese production; amylase is associated with bread and pectinase with juice processing.
n679665cd059.tq: Match each enzyme with its specific industrial application.
xs: Recombinant **chymosin** is used for **cheese** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Amylase** is for **bread**, **pectinase** for **juice**; **ligase** is a DNA-joining tool.
xa: White biotech: **enzymes, biofuels, bioplastics, precision fermentation**.
BioE3 promotes **high-performance biomanufacturing**.

nbiology-1-12.s: Who first identified transposable elements ('jumping genes')?
nbiology-1-12.x: Barbara McClintock first identified transposable elements.
n: Schleiden and Schwann proposed the first theory of cell structure, known as cell theory. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-4]
Prokaryotic cells were the first form of life. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-4]
Barbara McClintock first identified transposable elements. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-4]
Gregor Mendel conducted the first hybridization experiments on pea. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-4]
xa: Mendel **formulated** the **laws of inheritance**.
McClintock's transposons are called **jumping genes**.
**A. P. de Candolle** gave the **vascular-tissue-based classification**.

nbiology-1-17.s: Samrupa was the world's first cloned:
nbiology-1-17.x: Samrupa was the first cloned buffalo; Dolly (Scotland, 5 July 1996) was the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell.
n: Dolly was the first living cloned genetically engineered organism. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-4]
Dolly was born on 5 July 1996. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-4]
Dolly was born in Scotland. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-4]
Samrupa was cloned in 2009. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-4]
xa: **Ganga** is **India's first cloned cow** (**Gir breed**, NDRI Karnal).
**Injaz** is the world's **first cloned camel**.
⚠ Some notes name the 2009 cloned buffalo **Garima** (NDRI Karnal).

nbiology-11-4.s: GM Mustard DMH-11 is associated with:
o: Prof. Deepak Pental and the Delhi University team
nbiology-11-4.x: DMH-11 is from Deepak Pental's Delhi University team; Mahyco made Bt brinjal and Gurdev Khush super rice.
n: Bt brinjal was developed by Maharashtra Hybrid Seeds Co. (Mahyco). [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]
GM mustard (DMH-11) was developed by Prof. Deepak Pental and the Delhi University team. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]
Super Rice was developed by Gurdev Singh Khush. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]
Flavr-Savr tomato was developed using PG gene antisense insertion. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]
xa: **Bollgard-I Bt cotton** was **India's first biotech crop** approved for commercialisation (**2002**).
**Triticale** is the **first man-made cereal crop**.
**Jaya** is the **first dwarf rice variety** in India.

nbiology-11-5.s: The Dapog rice nursery method is associated with:
nbiology-11-5.x: The Dapog nursery method comes from the Philippines.
n: The Dapog rice nursery method was developed in the Philippines. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]
Jaya was the first dwarf rice variety in India. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]
xa: **Super Rice** was developed by **Gurdev Singh Khush**.
The **crop-logging concept** came from **Clements** of the **USA**.
**Sub1** is a flood-tolerant rice from **marker-assisted selection**.

nbiology-66-18.s: Which of the following is made by bacteria rather than yeast?
nbiology-66-18.x: Curd is made by Lactobacillus bacteria; wine, beer and bread use yeast.
n: Yeast is used in wine fermentation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Yeast is used in beer fermentation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Yeast is used in bread fermentation. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Lactobacillus is associated with curd production. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
xa: Yeast also ferments **toddy** and gives **alcoholic beverages**.
**Acetobacter** makes **vinegar**.
**Bacteria** are linked to **cheese**, **butter**, **curd**.

nbiology-44-6.s: In an mRNA vaccine, the mRNA instructs the body's cells to produce:
nbiology-44-6.x: The vaccine mRNA makes cells produce the target antigen, which the immune system then responds to.
n: The immune system recognises the antigen and produces an immune response. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #44 · pp 73-75]
xa: Indigenous platforms: **mRNA, viral vector, protein subunit**.
The **Moderna** vaccine came from **Moderna**, **NIAID** and **BARDA**.
**microRNA** **regulates gene expression** post-transcriptionally.

DNA **bases** are **A, G, C and T**.
Sequencing **detects sequence differences** (genetic variation).

nbiology-40-12.s: The human genome contains approximately how many DNA bases?
nbiology-40-12.x: The human genome has about 3 billion bases, over 99% of them shared among humans.
n: The human genome contains approximately 3 billion DNA bases. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 63-66]
More than 99% of DNA bases are the same among humans. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 63-66]
A genome is roughly fixed for a line except for mutations. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 63-66]
A transcriptome can change with environmental conditions. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 63-66]
xa: The transcriptome = **sum total** of **expressed mRNA molecules**.
A **zygote genome** combines **DNA** from **two gametes**.
**Genome India Project** targets **10,000 genomes**.

nf3f028ea56a.s: Which of the following sets contains only ex-situ bioremediation techniques?
nf3f028ea56a.x: Landfarming, composting and biopiles require contaminated material to be treated outside its original location and are ex-situ techniques.
nf3f028ea56a.tq: Classify the techniques by whether the contaminated material remains at the site.
xs: **Landfarming, composting and biopiles** are all **ex-situ** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Bioventing, biosparging and bioaugmentation** are **in-situ** techniques.
Option (3) mixes ex-situ **slurry reactors** and landfarming with in-situ **biosparging**.
xa: Ex-situ = material **excavated/removed** and treated elsewhere in beds or reactors.
Ex-situ **bioreactors** (slurry, aqueous) are the **costliest** but **fastest**.
**Landfarming/biopiles** are low-cost ex-situ options.

nea5438d9d6e.s: A contaminated site is treated without excavating the polluted material, using a passive and relatively cheaper method. This approach is known as:
nea5438d9d6e.x: In-situ bioremediation treats contamination at its original site and is generally cheaper and more passive than ex-situ treatment.
nea5438d9d6e.tq: Apply the site-treatment condition first: treatment at the original location indicates in-situ remediation.
xs: Treatment at the site without excavation, cheap and passive, is **in-situ bioremediation** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Ex-situ** needs the material **excavated/removed**; **thermal remediation** is not biological; **biomagnification** is a food-chain process.
xa: In-situ = "**treats contaminated material directly at the site**" (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
In-situ techniques: **bioventing**, **biosparging**, **bioaugmentation**.
In-situ limits: **slow**, long treatment time; **metals/inorganics** complicate.

n3ed307b9b75.s: Which bioremediation approach is the most cost-efficient and relatively passive?
n3ed307b9b75.x: In-situ treatment is the most cost-efficient and passive but slow; ex-situ bioreactors are the fastest.
xa: Ex-situ also suffers **abiotic loss**.
Bioreactors have **high capital and operating cost** (costliest).
In-situ = "**treats contaminated material directly at the site**" (APPSC-G2 **2025**).

ne88c30bf391.s: Which one of the following is NOT an advantage of bioremediation?
o: It is usually cheaper than conventional clean-up methods
It invariably produces rapid results irrespective of pollutant and site conditions
In-situ treatment can cause little disruption at the contaminated site
It generally uses fewer chemicals and may avoid secondary pollution
ne88c30bf391.x: Bioremediation is often slow, and its results vary with the pollutant, organism, site conditions and co-contaminants. The other three are recognised advantages.
ne88c30bf391.tq: Identify the absolute claim that conflicts with the variable performance of biological treatment.
xs: **"Invariably rapid results"** is NOT an advantage — bioremediation is **slow** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Results **vary with pollutant, organism, site conditions and co-contaminants**.
**Cheaper**, **little site disruption** (in-situ) and **few chemicals / no secondary pollution** are real advantages.
xa: Bioremediation also **restores ecosystems**.
Conventional methods are **faster** but costly, with residues and emissions.
**Metals/inorganics** complicate bioremediation.

nef444c648a7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about bioremediation and conventional remediation?
o: Bioremediation is generally slower than conventional remediation.
Bioremediation can be scalable and community-applied.
Conventional remediation is generally less dependent on site biology.
Bioremediation has uniform reliability irrespective of pollutant, organism and site.
nef444c648a7.x: The reliability of bioremediation varies with the pollutant, organism, site and co-contaminants.
xa: Cost: bioremediation **low** ("fraction of the funds"); conventional **high**.
Side effects: bioremediation has **no secondary pollution**; conventional leaves **residues, emissions**.
Conventional = **thermal, chemical, excavation**.

n941c71712ae.x: PETase-producing bacteria break down plastic; engineered Pseudomonas targets oil spills and biofilters treat air streams.
xa: Bioplastic pilot plants: **Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu**.
Waste-to-energy: **Gobar-Dhan** biogas; municipal waste to **CNG** in **Hyderabad and Pune**.
**2G ethanol** at **IOCL Panipat**; **E20** target **2025-26**.

n2db1df6d6bc.s: Bioaugmentation of an oil spill involves adding:
n2db1df6d6bc.x: Oil spills and oily sludge can be treated by bioaugmentation with oil-degrading bacteria.
xa: **TERI** consortium was used at **Chennai port**.
**CPCB** handles bioremediation of oil-contaminated soils.
Sewage drains: **biostimulation**, aquatic plants, **constructed wetlands**.

n4b1c3ddb8e0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about bioaugmentation and biostimulation?
o: Bioaugmentation introduces specific pollutant-degrading microbes into a site.
Biostimulation boosts existing microbes by supplying nutrients and oxygen.
TERI's Oilzapper is an example of bioaugmentation.
Adding nitrogen and phosphorus to polluted lakes is an example of bioaugmentation.
n4b1c3ddb8e0.x: Adding N and P to polluted lakes boosts existing microbes, so it is biostimulation, not bioaugmentation.
xa: Oil spills → **bioaugmentation** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
**Oilzapper** was developed by **TERI** (with Indian Oil).

n48ccd151880.s: In phytoremediation, Indian mustard (Brassica juncea) is associated with accumulating:
n48ccd151880.x: Indian mustard accumulates lead, cadmium and selenium; sunflower accumulates uranium and other radionuclides.
xa: **Pteris vittata** → **arsenic**; **Alyssum** → **nickel**.
**Thlaspi caerulescens** → **zinc, cadmium**.
Water hyacinth is the standard **phytoextraction** example.

n1bc7f6a9d54.s: Constructed wetlands are best described as systems in which:
o: Excavation removes contaminated soil for off-site disposal
Thermal treatment incinerates all sewage solids
Only chemical agents remove pollutants from groundwater
Plants and microbes break down and absorb pollutants
n1bc7f6a9d54.x: Constructed wetlands may be natural or engineered systems where plants and microbes break down and absorb pollutants, especially in sewage treatment.
n1bc7f6a9d54.tq: Identify the biological mechanism from the functions performed by plants and microbes.
xs: In **constructed wetlands**, **plants and microbes break down and absorb pollutants** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They are natural or engineered wetlands used in **sewage treatment** — not excavation, thermal or chemical methods.
xa: **Phytorid** (CSIR-NEERI): wastewater passes through a **planted gravel bed**.
Constructed wetlands are a **biological** method — counted as bioremediation.
Ponds use **water hyacinth** and **duckweed**.

n292b5c53573.s: Which of the following is included among the DBT biofuel targets?
o: Fuel from agricultural residue and municipal waste
n292b5c53573.x: The targets include fuels from agricultural residue and municipal waste, algal fuels, sustainable aviation fuel and integrated biorefineries.
n292b5c53573.tq: Prefer the option stated as a positive biotechnology application.
xs: DBT's biofuel targets include **fuel from agricultural residue and municipal waste** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The targets also list **algal fuels**, **SAF** and **integrated biorefineries** — so (1) and (3) contradict them.
xa: **2G ethanol** from crop residue at **IOCL Panipat**.
**E20 blending** target: **2025-26**.
Waste-to-energy: municipal waste to **CNG** in **Hyderabad and Pune**.

o: Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone located at Visakhapatnam
Agricultural Microbial Technology Zone located at Vijayawada
Advanced Medical Training Zone located at Amaravati
Andhra Pradesh Marine Technology Zone located at Kakinada
n4d1eeba2ea7.x: AMTZ is the Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone located at Visakhapatnam.
n4d1eeba2ea7.tq: Discriminate between similar expansions and locations.
xs: **AMTZ** = **Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone, Visakhapatnam** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is not located at Vijayawada, Amaravati or Kakinada.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say "**Amaravati Medtech Zone**" — the accepted form is Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone.
Visakhapatnam was also chosen for a **marine biomaterials** research facility (Jan **2026**).
**IBDC** is at **RCB, Faridabad**.

n63d1b210c02.s: Which of the following most appropriately describes bioremediation?
o: Thermal destruction of contaminated soil by incineration
Removal or degradation of pollutants by organisms or their enzymes
Physical excavation and permanent burial of contaminated material
Chemical conversion of all pollutants into radioactive substances
n63d1b210c02.x: Bioremediation uses organisms such as bacteria, fungi, algae and plants, or their enzymes, to degrade or remove pollutants and restore a contaminated environment.
n63d1b210c02.tq: Use the exact definition and distinguish biological treatment from thermal or physical treatment.
xs: **Bioremediation** is **removal or degradation of pollutants by organisms or their enzymes** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Incineration** is thermal, and **excavation/landfilling** physical — both are **not** bioremediation.
xa: APPSC-GS **2019**: "**Removal of pollutants from the biosphere by biological processes**".
Agents: **bacteria, fungi, algae and plants**; microbes can be genetically engineered.
Primary objective: **neutralising pollutants in contaminated soil and groundwater** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
Nodal R&D body: **CSIR-NEERI** (Jun **2026**).

n64c8cfba9a0.s: The rising concentration of persistent toxins such as DDT or mercury along a food chain is called:
n64c8cfba9a0.x: That is biomagnification; bioremediation is the biological degradation or removal of pollutants.
xa: **Biofortification** = raising micronutrient content of crops.
**Eutrophication** = nutrient enrichment causing **algal blooms**; bioremediation can **control** it.
Oil spills are treated by **bioaugmentation**.

n0770b50abf5.s: A municipal authority uses bacteria to break down organic waste. This activity is best classified as:
n0770b50abf5.x: The biological breakdown of organic waste by bacteria is microbial degradation and therefore constitutes bioremediation.
n0770b50abf5.tq: Identify the biological agent and process before distinguishing it from physical or thermal treatment.
xs: Breaking down organic waste with bacteria is **bioremediation** (APPSC-GS **2022**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ The distractors **desalination, fossilisation, incineration** are not biological clean-up.
xa: **Composting** organic waste and bacterial oil clean-up **are** bioremediation.
**SWM Rules 2026** mandate **biomining and bioremediation** of legacy dumpsites.
Only **60-70%** of waste is collected and **15-20%** processed.

n2193af0e511.s: Which one of the following is NOT an example of bioremediation?
o: Cleaning an oil spill with oil-degrading bacteria
Growing plants that absorb heavy metals from soil
n2193af0e511.x: Burning contaminated soil is thermal destruction, not a biological process, so it is not bioremediation (APPSC-G2 2025). Composting, bacterial oil clean-up and phytoremediation all use organisms to degrade or remove pollutants.
xs: **Burning contaminated soil** is thermal destruction, so it is **NOT bioremediation** (APPSC-G2 **2025**) — option **(3)** is correct.
**Composting** and **bacterial oil clean-up** ARE bioremediation; plants absorbing heavy metals is **phytoremediation**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "Which is NOT bioremediation?" = **burning contaminated soil**.
**Incineration** (thermal), **chemical treatment** and **desalination/excavation** (physical) are also not bioremediation.
APPSC-GS **2022**: breaking down organic waste with bacteria = **bioremediation**.
Agents: **bacteria, fungi, algae and plants**.

n288866858d1.s: TERI developed Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S in collaboration with:
n288866858d1.x: These bacterial consortia were developed by TERI with Indian Oil to degrade oily sludge and oil-contaminated sites.
xa: **UPSC 2011**: Oilzapper = eco-friendly remediation of **oily sludge and oil spills**.
A TERI consortium was used at **Chennai port**.
⚠ **Oilzapper** = TERI; **Phytorid** = **CSIR-NEERI**.

nbaa689f1a02.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Phytorid technology?
o: A chemical oxidation process developed by the US EPA
A constructed-wetland sewage-treatment technology developed by CSIR-NEERI
A thermal sewage-treatment system developed under SBM-U
An excavation-based technology developed by AMTZ
nbaa689f1a02.x: Phytorid is a constructed-wetland sewage-treatment technology developed by CSIR-NEERI.
nbaa689f1a02.tq: Link the technology with its developer and treatment category, avoiding swapped institutions.
xs: **Phytorid** is a **constructed-wetland sewage-treatment technology** by **CSIR-NEERI** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Wastewater passes through a **planted gravel bed**; it is not chemical, thermal or excavation-based.
xa: ⚠ **Phytorid** = CSIR-NEERI; **Oilzapper** = TERI.
CSIR-NEERI, Nagpur, is the **nodal bioremediation R&D** body.
**US EPA Superfund** guidelines are cited as the model for bioremediation.

ne613cbbdb8b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Visakhapatnam sewage-discharge issue?
o: The drain enters the sea at Pedda Jalaripeta.
It involved a PIL before the Andhra Pradesh High Court.
The stormwater drain passes through MVP Colony and Lawson's Bay Colony.
The proposal favoured only large-scale pumping schemes.
ne613cbbdb8b.x: Immediate bioremediation and decentralised STPs were proposed as a lower-cost alternative to pumping schemes.
xa: Petitioner: **Bollisetty Satyanarayana**.
Bioremediation cost: "**fraction of the funds**" of conventional methods.
Visakhapatnam was also chosen for a **marine biomaterials** research facility.

ne7505e310af.s: Under the SWM Rules, 2026, landfills are intended only for:
ne7505e310af.x: Landfills are only for non-recyclable, non-energy-recoverable and inert waste; the Rules also mandate annual landfill audits.
xa: Target: "**Lakshya Zero Dumpsites**" (**SBM-U 2.0**).
Only **60-70%** of waste collected; **15-20%** processed.

nbiology-2-12.s: The first antibody produced during an infection is:
nbiology-2-12.x: IgM is the primary antibody, the first made in a new infection.
n: IgM is the primary antibody. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
IgM is the first antibody produced during an infection. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
xa: **hCG** is the **placental hormone**.
**OAA** is the **organic product** in the **C4 pathway**.
**Edward Jenner** made the **smallpox vaccine**.

nbiology-2-8.x: Triticale was the first man-made cereal.
n: Gregor Mendel conducted pea hybridisation experiments. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
Triticale was the first man-made cereal. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
Barney Clark was the recipient of an artificial heart. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #2 · pp 4-6]
xa: **Christian Barnard** did the first **heart transplant** in **South Africa**.
**Jaya** is the **first dwarf rice variety** in India.
**hCG** is the **placental hormone** listed among firsts.

nbiology-14-7.s: Who explained how the nucleotide sequence controls protein synthesis?
nbiology-14-7.x: Khorana, Nirenberg and Holley cracked the genetic code, showing how nucleotide triplets specify amino acids (Nobel 1968). Watson and Crick gave the structure.
nbiology-14-7.tq: Discriminate DNA structure from the genetic code.
n: Khorana, Nirenberg, and Holley explained how nucleotide sequences control protein synthesis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 21-24]
Khorana, Nirenberg, and Holley studied the genetic code. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 21-24]
Khorana, Nirenberg, and Holley worked in molecular biology. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #14 · pp 21-24]
xs: **Khorana, Nirenberg and Holley** explained how **nucleotide sequences** **control** **protein synthesis** — so option **(4)** is correct.
They worked out the **genetic code**.
**Miescher** **first isolated** DNA; **Watson, Crick and Wilkins** gave the **double helix**; **Kornberg** showed **DNA synthesis**.
xa: **Mendel** **laid** the **foundation** of **modern genetics**.
**Barbara McClintock** found **jumping genes**.
**Arber, Nathans and Smith** are linked to **restriction endonucleases**.

nbiology-11-6.s: Lukoskin, developed by DRDO and DIBER, is used to treat:
nbiology-11-6.x: Lukoskin treats leucoderma; Eczit is for eczema and Amtooth for toothache.
n: Saheli contraceptive was developed by CDRI, Lucknow. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]
Lukoskin was developed by DRDO and DIBER. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]
Amtooth was developed by DRDO. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]
Eczit was developed by DRDO. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 18-19]
xa: **Bt brinjal** was developed by **Mahyco**.
**GM mustard (DMH-11)** by **Prof. Deepak Pental**'s team.
**Hybridoma technique** by **Georges Köhler** and **César Milstein**.

nee7debb3bcc.s: Marker-assisted selection is exemplified by the development of:
nee7debb3bcc.x: Sub1 flood-tolerant rice is given as an example of marker-assisted selection.
nee7debb3bcc.tq: Link the breeding method to its crop example.
xs: **Sub1 flood-tolerant rice** is the example of **marker-assisted selection** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**R21** is a malaria vaccine, **Garima** a cloned buffalo, **Cervavac** an HPV vaccine.
xa: **Tissue culture**: **BARC** (banana, pineapple).
Biofertilisers: **Rhizobium**, **Azotobacter**, **Azolla**, blue-green algae.
Green biotechnology = **agriculture**.

n311b42c2558.s: Which one of the following is NOT a component of Bio-RIDE?
o: National wildlife census and habitat mapping
n311b42c2558.x: Bio-RIDE has three components: R&D; industrial and entrepreneurship development; and bio-manufacturing and bio-foundry. Wildlife census is not one of them.
n311b42c2558.tq: Identify the unrelated component among a policy’s stated pillars.
xs: **National wildlife census** is not a **Bio-RIDE** component — so option **(3)** is correct.
Bio-RIDE's **3 components**: **R&D**, **Industrial/entrepreneurship development**, **Bio-manufacturing and bio-foundry**.
xa: Bio-RIDE merged **two DBT umbrella schemes**.
**BioE3** (**August 2024**) promotes high-performance biomanufacturing.
**BIRAC** is a DBT PSU.

n4bd946026d8.s: The Dumpsite Remediation Accelerator is associated with which of the following?
o: Ministry of Jal Shakti under Namami Gange
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change under AMRUT 2.0
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs under SBM-U 2.0
n4bd946026d8.x: The Dumpsite Remediation Accelerator is an initiative of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0.
n4bd946026d8.tq: Use the ministry-and-scheme association to eliminate swapped-authority options.
xs: The **Dumpsite Remediation Accelerator** belongs to **MoHUA** under **SBM-U 2.0** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**BioE3** is a DBT policy, unrelated to dumpsites.
xa: Target: "**Lakshya Zero Dumpsites**".
It clears legacy dumpsites through **accelerated bioremediation** (Jun **2026**).
**SWM Rules 2026** mandate **biomining and bioremediation** of legacy dumpsites.

nd08741ee5e8.s: Which tree, planted along sewage ponds, transpires surplus wastewater?
nd08741ee5e8.x: Eucalyptus along sewage ponds transpires surplus wastewater; mangroves and wetland vegetation are natural phytoremediators.
xa: Ponds use **water hyacinth** and **duckweed**.
**Constructed wetlands**: plants + microbes break down and absorb pollutants.
**Eucalyptus** is planted **along sewage ponds** for this purpose.

n86ac0302a5c.s: The primary goal of sustainable agriculture is to:
o: Replace all farm labour with mechanisation
Maximise yields through continuous use of chemical inputs
Produce food while protecting the environment and conserving resources for future generations
n86ac0302a5c.x: Sustainable agriculture seeks to produce food while protecting the environment and conserving resources for future generations.
n86ac0302a5c.tq: Identify the definition that combines production, environmental protection and intergenerational resource conservation.
xs: Sustainable agriculture aims to **produce food while protecting the environment and conserving resources for future generations** (PYQ) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Monoculture** and continuous **chemical inputs** are listed as **harmful** practices, not goals.
xa: Sustainable practices: **crop rotation**, **organic farming**, mixed cropping, green manuring, **drip irrigation**, **IPM**.
Harmful practices: **excessive chemical fertilisers**, **overuse of pesticides**, **monoculture**, **over-irrigation**.
Shift: Green Revolution → "**evergreen revolution**" (ZBNF, organic farming, water conservation, IPM).

nd6ef8f9a52c.s: Which one of the following is NOT generally regarded as a harmful agricultural practice?
nd6ef8f9a52c.x: Integrated pest management is a sustainable practice. Excessive chemical fertiliser use, pesticide overuse and monoculture are listed as harmful practices.
nd6ef8f9a52c.tq: Find the one sustainable practice hidden among harmful practices.
xs: **Integrated pest management** is a **sustainable** practice — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Excessive chemical fertilisers**, **overuse of pesticides** and **monoculture** are the listed **harmful** practices.
xa: **Over-irrigation** is also harmful.
IPM keeps pests **below economic injury levels**; aim = **optimise, not maximise** control.
Other sustainable practices: **cover crops**, **reduced tillage**, **drip irrigation**.

ncce3ddac056.s: The main advantage of organic farming as an eco-friendly agricultural technology is:
o: Reduced chemical input and improved soil health
Complete elimination of pests without any management
Lower labour requirement than every other system
ncce3ddac056.x: Organic farming's main advantage is reduced chemical input and improved soil health (PYQ). It does not guarantee higher yields in all conditions (the trap), does not eliminate pests by itself, and is not necessarily less labour-intensive.
ncce3ddac056.tq: Organic = less chemicals, better soil; not always more yield.
xs: Organic farming's main advantage is **reduced chemical input and improved soil health** (PYQ) — so option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ Trap: it does **NOT** give **higher yields in all conditions**.
xa: Organic farming is the PYQ answer for an **eco-friendly technology**.
Organic farming is **certified** and allows **approved organic inputs**.
Transition debate: **yield dip for 2-3 years** in natural farming.

nchemistry-19-50.s: Bordeaux mixture, a fungicide, contains copper sulphate and:
nchemistry-19-50.x: Bordeaux mixture is CuSO4 with Ca(OH)2 (lime).
n: Bordeaux mixture contains CuSO₄ and Ca(OH)₂. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
Fungicides are used for crop protection. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
Fungicides are used in water tanks. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
xa: **Blue vitriol** is **CuSO₄**, also a fungicide.
**Chloropicrin** is a broad-spectrum fungicide, herbicide, insecticide and tear gas.
Pesticide residues **bioaccumulate** in the food chain.

n27e0e386623.s: The primary objective of Integrated Pest Management, as defined by the FAO, is to:
o: Replace all biological methods with resistant varieties
Maximise pest mortality through continuous chemical spraying
Keep pests below economic injury levels by optimising the use of suitable methods
Eliminate every pest from the agricultural ecosystem
n27e0e386623.x: IPM uses all suitable methods to keep pest populations below economic injury levels. Its aim is to optimise control, not maximise it.
n27e0e386623.tq: Distinguish the stated management objective from the extreme goal of total eradication.
xs: IPM (**FAO**) keeps pests **below economic injury levels** using all suitable methods — so option **(3)** is correct.
Its aim is to **optimise, not maximise** control, so continuous spraying and total elimination are wrong.
xa: Components: **resistant varieties**, **cultural**, **mechanical/physical**, **biological**, **chemical only when needed**.
Biological example: **green lacewing** vs **aphids**.
IPM is a **sustainable** practice (PYQ).

n7263b9782c1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Integrated Pest Management (IPM)?
o: Resistant varieties form one component of IPM.
Chemical control is the first and routine line of defence.
Crop rotation and changes in irrigation are cultural methods.
Traps and mulches are mechanical or physical methods.
n7263b9782c1.x: In IPM, chemical control is used only when needed, not routinely as the first option.
xa: **Biological** component: natural enemies (**green lacewing** vs aphids), **pheromone traps**.
IPM aim: **optimise, not maximise** control.
IPM keeps pests **below economic injury levels** (FAO).

ncebb120ea0b.s: Beauveria bassiana is best described as a:
o: Entomopathogenic fungus used against borers and whitefly
Plant extract used as an antifeedant
ncebb120ea0b.x: Beauveria bassiana is an entomopathogenic fungus effective against borers, whitefly and other insects.
ncebb120ea0b.tq: Distinguish closely related biopesticides by source and target.
xs: **Beauveria bassiana** is an **entomopathogenic fungus** used against **borers and whitefly** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **baculovirus** is **NPV**; the plant antifeedant is **neem**; the bacterium against bollworms is **Bt**.
xa: **Trichoderma** is also a fungus (antagonist) against **wilt, root rot**.
⚠ Fungi: **Trichoderma**, **Beauveria**; virus: **NPV**; bacterium: **Bt**.
Biopesticides are a **crucial IPM component**.

nf21590e528b.s: Carbosulfan was proposed for banning because it:
o: Fixes nitrogen but causes nitrate leaching
Improves soil microbial activity but reduces crop yield
Breaks down to highly toxic carbofuran and harms birds and aquatic life
Is a natural pesticide that attracts secondary pests
nf21590e528b.x: Carbosulfan breaks down into highly toxic carbofuran and is harmful to birds and aquatic life. The proposed ban was recommended by the Registration Committee under the Insecticides Act, 1968.
nf21590e528b.tq: Link the pesticide with its breakdown product and ecological harm.
xs: **Carbosulfan** breaks down to highly toxic **Carbofuran** and **harms birds and aquatic life** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The Centre proposed the ban (29 Aug **2026**) on the recommendation of the **Registration Committee under the Insecticides Act 1968**.
xa: ⚠ **Carbosulfan** (proposed ban) → breaks down to **Carbofuran**.
**Punjab** banned the sale of **glyphosate** in **2018**.
Indiscriminate use → **secondary pest outbreaks** and **pesticide resistance**.

n7fe945a9768.s: Charcoal produced by pyrolysis of biomass, used for long-term carbon sequestration in soil, is called:
n7fe945a9768.x: Biochar is pyrolysis charcoal that gives long-term carbon sequestration and water/nutrient retention.
xa: Green manure crops: **sunn hemp** and **dhaincha** — they add nitrogen and organic matter.
**Compost**: decomposed crop residues; AP plans **1,500 MT/day** manure from **107 waste-processing centres**.
Farmyard manure gives **slow-release nutrients** and better soil structure.
Biochar also improves **water and nutrient retention**.

nc6c5b0be48e.s: Which one of the following is an example of a biological component of Integrated Pest Management?
o: Use of a resistant seed variety only
Use of green lacewings against aphids
nc6c5b0be48e.x: Green lacewings act as natural enemies of aphids and therefore represent a biological IPM method. Pheromone traps are also included among the listed IPM tools.
nc6c5b0be48e.tq: Separate biological control from cultural and physical control methods.
xs: **Green lacewings against aphids** is a **biological** IPM method — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Resistant varieties** are a separate component; **irrigation change** is **cultural**; **mulches** are **mechanical/physical**.
xa: **Pheromone traps** are also listed under biological methods.
Biopesticides (**Bt**, **NPV**, **Trichoderma**) are a crucial IPM component.
Chemicals in IPM: **only when needed**.

nchemistry-16-6.s: Which plants are mainly used as green manure?
nchemistry-16-6.x: Green manure is a crop ploughed in while green; legumes are preferred because they fix nitrogen.
n: Green manure is a cover crop grown and ploughed in while green or just after flowering. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Legumes are the main plants used as green manure. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Clover is a green-manure plant. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Vetch is a green-manure plant. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Sesbania is a green-manure plant. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
xa: Green manure adds **organic matter** and **humus**, and fixes nitrogen through **root nodules**.
Other green-manure crops: **sunn hemp** and **dhaincha**.
AP **Kharif 2026**: **Rs 62.20 crore** subsidy; **91,918 quintals** of green-manure seed.

nchemistry-16-32.s: Excess nitrogen fertilisers leach ____ into groundwater.
nchemistry-16-32.x: Excess nitrogen acidifies soil, leaches nitrate into groundwater and causes eutrophication.
n: Excess nitrogen fertilizers cause soil acidification. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Excess nitrogen fertilizers cause nitrate leaching to groundwater. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Excess nitrogen fertilizers cause eutrophication. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
xa: Continuous chemical fertilizer use lowers **soil organic matter**, **microbial activity** and **nutrient density** in food.
Solutions: **organic manure**, **vermicompost**, **biofertilizers**, **neem-coated urea**.
Broadcasting granular fertiliser loses **50-70%** of applied nitrogen.
**PM-PRANAM**: states keep **50%** of saved fertiliser subsidy as grants.

nchemistry-16-35.s: Continuous use of chemical fertilisers leads to:
o: A decline in soil organic matter
An increase in soil organic matter
nchemistry-16-35.x: Continuous chemical fertiliser use depletes soil organic matter, reduces microbes and lowers nutrient density in food.
n: Continuous chemical fertilizer use causes a decline in soil organic matter. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Continuous chemical fertilizer use reduces microbial activity. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
Continuous chemical fertilizer use lowers nutrient density in food. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 55-59]
xa: Excess nitrogen causes **soil acidification**, **nitrate leaching** and **eutrophication**.
**Vermicompost** restores soil microbes and organic carbon.
⚠ Organic farming's main advantage = **reduced chemical input and improved soil health**, NOT higher yields everywhere.

n23ccb03f229.s: Unlike the stricter approach of organic farming, sustainable agriculture may:
n23ccb03f229.x: Sustainable agriculture may use synthetic inputs judiciously and include IPM and precision farming.
xa: Organic = **certified**, approved organic inputs; natural farming = **on-farm cow-based** inputs.
Organic farming's main advantage: **reduced chemical input and improved soil health**.

n616bf5a9ae1.s: Indiscriminate use of synthetic fertilisers and pesticides may result in:
n616bf5a9ae1.x: It can cause secondary pest outbreaks, pesticide resistance and contamination of ecosystems, soil and water.
xa: Pesticide residues **bioaccumulate** in the food chain.
Broadcasting granular fertiliser loses **50-70%** of applied nitrogen.
Remedies: **neem-coated urea**, **PM-PRANAM**.

n056866422cb.s: Under PM-PRANAM, States may retain what share of the fertiliser subsidy saved by reducing fertiliser use, in the form of grants?
n056866422cb.x: PM-PRANAM allows States to retain 50 percent of the saved fertiliser subsidy as grants.
n056866422cb.tq: Recall the exact percentage associated with the incentive mechanism.
xs: Under **PM-PRANAM**, states keep **50 percent** of the saved fertiliser subsidy as **grants** — so option **(3)** is correct.
PM-PRANAM is a remedy for fertiliser overuse, alongside **neem-coated urea**.
xa: Broadcasting fertiliser loses **50-70%** of nitrogen.
⚠ Do not confuse: **50%** = PM-PRANAM share; **50 farmers / 50 acres** = PKVY cluster.

n818010bde6d.s: Biopesticides are an important IPM component mainly because they are:
o: Biodegradable, low in toxicity and short-lived
Able to eliminate all pests permanently
n818010bde6d.x: Biopesticides are biodegradable, comparatively low in toxicity and short-lived; they are not meant to eliminate all pests.
xa: IPM aim = **optimise, not maximise** control.
Biopesticides: **Bt**, **Trichoderma**, **NPV**, **Neem**, **Beauveria bassiana**.
In IPM, **chemicals are used only when needed**.

n0b4b72f9cf8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)?
o: A standard cluster consists of 20 farmers covering 20 acres.
It was the first comprehensive Centrally Sponsored Scheme for organic farming.
n0b4b72f9cf8.x: A standard PKVY cluster consists of 50 farmers covering 50 acres.
xa: Coverage: **15.08 lakh ha**, **25.38 lakh farmers** (to 31 Jul **2025**).
Portal: **jaivikkheti.in**.
⚠ **PKVY** = rest of India; **MOVCDNER** = North-East.

nbab033056eb.s: Which one of the following schemes is specifically associated with the development of organic value chains in the North-Eastern States?
nbab033056eb.x: MOVCDNER promotes organic value chains in the North-Eastern Region, whereas PKVY covers the rest of the country.
nbab033056eb.tq: Distinguish schemes by geographical scope and objective.
xs: **MOVCDNER** builds **organic value chains in the North-East** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**PKVY** covers the **rest** of India; **NPOP** and **PGS-India** are certification systems.
xa: MOVCDNER was launched in **2015-16**, the same year as PKVY.
**PGS-India** = farmer-group certification for the **domestic** market.
**NPOP** = **third-party** certification, mainly for **exports**.

n758a09d515b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about organic-farming certification in India?
o: NPOP is based mainly on third-party certification.
PGS-India is mainly associated with exports.
NPOP is mainly associated with exports.
n758a09d515b.x: PGS-India is intended for the domestic market; NPOP is the export-oriented system.
xa: NPOP dates from **2001**.
⚠ **PGS-India** = domestic, farmer groups; **NPOP** = third-party, exports.
Organic farming is **certified**; natural farming relies on **on-farm** inputs.

n90c2af588ee.s: What is the total outlay of the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF)?
n90c2af588ee.x: The total NMNF outlay is ₹2,481 crore; ₹897 crore is the States' share.
xa: Centre's share: **Rs 1,584 crore**.
Coverage also reached **18.19 lakh farmers**.
**BPKP** also promotes natural farming.

ned4c536b8c9.s: Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming (APCNF) was formerly known as:
ned4c536b8c9.x: APCNF was formerly ZBNF; it uses jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham and covers over seven lakh farmers.
xa: APCNF won the **Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity 2024**.
A **Kenyan delegation** praised it after visiting **Guntur** district farms (8 Jul **2026**).
**NTR district**: natural-farming model with **QR-based traceability**.

n03d318c88ee.s: India's first fully organic State is:
n03d318c88ee.x: Sikkim is the first fully organic State; PKVY was the first comprehensive organic-farming scheme.
xa: Sikkim became fully organic in **2016**.
PKVY began in **2015-16** with **50 farmers / 50 acres** clusters.
PKVY portal: **jaivikkheti.in**.

nchemistry-19-11.s:
Which of the following are insecticides?
1. DDT
2. BHC
3. 2,4-D
nchemistry-19-11.x: DDT and BHC are insecticides; 2,4-D is a herbicide.
n: DDT is an insecticide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
BHC is an insecticide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
2,4-D is used as a herbicide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
2,4-D is a herbicide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
Zinc phosphide is a rodenticide. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
xa: Other insecticides: **allethrin**, **prallethrin** (mosquito repellents), **Sevin**, **Bt**.
**BHC** = **benzene hexachloride**.
Fungicides: **Bordeaux mixture**, **blue vitriol**, **chloropicrin**.

n72445f8c7a2.s: The shift from the Green Revolution towards the ‘evergreen revolution’ is associated with which combination?
o: ZBNF, organic farming, water conservation and integrated pest management
Only genetically modified crops and mechanised harvesting
Monoculture, over-irrigation, pesticide intensification and soil mining
Expansion of chemical fertilisers without resource conservation
n72445f8c7a2.x: The evergreen revolution approach is associated with ZBNF, organic farming, water conservation and integrated pest management.
n72445f8c7a2.tq: Match the newer sustainability-oriented approach with its defining practices.
xs: The **"evergreen revolution"** shift rests on **ZBNF, organic farming, water conservation and IPM** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Monoculture**, **over-irrigation** and pesticide overuse are the **harmful** practices it moves away from.
xa: ZBNF was developed by **Subhash Palekar**.
First fully organic state: **Sikkim (2016)**.
First comprehensive CSS for organic farming: **PKVY** (**2015-16**).

nf05a52e2b3c.s: Zero Budget Natural Farming was developed by:
nf05a52e2b3c.x: Subhash Palekar developed ZBNF; Bill Mollison and David Holmgren coined 'permaculture'.
xa: ZBNF terms: **Jeevamrutha** (cow dung-urine microbial culture), **Beejamrutha** (seed treatment), **Achhadana** (mulching).
Organic farming is **certified**; natural farming uses **on-farm** cow-based inputs.
Natural farming cuts cultivation cost by **20-40%**.
⚠ **PGS-India** = domestic, farmer-group certification; **NPOP** = third-party, exports.

n7272ff27257.s: AP Community-managed Natural Farming received global recognition through the:
o: UNEP Champions of the Earth Award, 2024
n7272ff27257.x: APCNF received the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity in 2024.
n7272ff27257.tq: Discriminate among similarly prestigious awards using the exact award-name and year pair.
xs: APCNF won the **Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity, 2024** — so option **(2)** is correct.
No World Food Prize, UNEP or Ramsar award is linked to APCNF.
xa: A **Kenyan delegation** praised APCNF as a **climate-resilient** model (8 Jul **2026**).
Guntur farms showed **20+** crop diversified plots and **trap crops** (marigold, castor).
AP is described as a **global pioneer** in natural farming.

n86eca16073e.s: Which irrigation method has the highest water-use efficiency, about 90%?
n86eca16073e.x: Drip irrigation is about 90% efficient, sprinklers about 70–80% and flood or furrow irrigation about 30–50%.
xa: Drip is the PYQ answer for **water-scarce regions** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
Drip's limitation: **higher initial investment**.
Sprinklers lose **more to wind and evaporation** than drip.

nad5c4414aa6.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes drip irrigation from sprinkler irrigation?
o: Drip irrigation applies water through nozzles as rainfall, whereas sprinkler irrigation uses emitters near roots.
Drip irrigation is suitable only for uneven terrain, whereas sprinkler irrigation is suitable only for level fields.
Drip irrigation applies water directly to the root zone through emitters, whereas sprinkler irrigation applies water under pressure through pipes and nozzles.
Both systems apply water only through underground channels without pressure.
nad5c4414aa6.x: Drip irrigation delivers water directly to the root zone through emitters on lateral pipes. Sprinkler irrigation distributes pressurised water through pipes and nozzles in the form of simulated rainfall.
nad5c4414aa6.tq: Use the application-method contrast to separate two closely related irrigation systems.
xs: **Drip** applies water **directly to the root zone through emitters**; **sprinkler** applies it **under pressure through pipes and nozzles** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (1) swaps the two; sprinklers **simulate rainfall**.
Sprinklers are **useful on uneven terrain**, so (2) is wrong.
xa: Drip emitters sit on **lateral pipes**.
Drip is **most efficient** (~**90%**), minimising evaporation and runoff.
Drip limitation: **higher initial investment**.

ne79b85fadb8.s: The shift in agricultural policy from ‘more output’ to ‘more output at lower ecological cost’ is associated with which concept?
ne79b85fadb8.x: The policy emphasis on higher output with lower ecological cost is described as the Evergreen Revolution, associated with M.S. Swaminathan.
ne79b85fadb8.tq: Identify the exact policy concept from its defining contrast.
xs: The shift from "more output" to "**more output at lower ecological cost**" is the **Evergreen Revolution** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The concept is associated with **M.S. Swaminathan**.
xa: **APSES 2024-25** lists **precision farming, drones, IoT**, drip/sprinkler and **rainwater harvesting** as the way forward.
Criticism: **high upfront cost of drip**; irrigation **still skewed to rice**.
**SRI** cuts **seed, methane and electricity** use (UPSC **2022**).

n482176d6f37.s: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of fertigation?
o: Control of the alkalinity of irrigation water
Increased availability of nutrients to plants
Reduction in the leaching of chemical nutrients
n482176d6f37.x: Fertigation helps control water alkalinity, raises nutrient availability and reduces leaching; efficient application of rock phosphate is not one of its advantages.
xa: Fertigation = fertiliser applied **through the irrigation water**.
**PDMC** promotes drip/sprinkler with fertigation.

n0cc92d9b824.s: Drone Shakti is associated with building the drone ecosystem through:
o: manufacturing and Remote Pilot Certificate training
n0cc92d9b824.x: Drone Shakti supports the drone ecosystem through manufacturing and training for Remote Pilot Certificates.
n0cc92d9b824.tq: Match the programme with its stated ecosystem-building functions.
xs: **Drone Shakti** builds the drone ecosystem through **manufacturing and Remote Pilot Certificate training** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Crop insurance is **PMFBY**; solar pumps belong to **PM-KUSUM**.
xa: Drones are regulated by **DGCA** (**Drone Rules 2021**).
Kisan drone uses: **crop assessment, soil health analysis, spraying**.
AP's **APDC** offers **drone-as-a-service**.

n8a2b0b54df8.s: Direct-seeded rice differs from transplanted rice mainly because it involves:
n8a2b0b54df8.x: Direct-seeded rice is planted without nursery raising or transplanting. It has also been promoted together with zero-till wheat under NICRA.
n8a2b0b54df8.tq: Use the presence or absence of nursery and transplanting as the decisive distinction.
xs: **Direct-seeded rice** needs **no nursery or transplanting** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is promoted with **zero-till wheat** under **NICRA**.
xa: **SRI** with alternate wetting and drying needs **less seed** and produces **less methane**.
Zero tillage also lets **paddy seed be planted directly** without a nursery (UPSC **2020**).
**Laser land levelling** saves irrigation water.

n12bbb119e0f.s: Alternate wetting and drying in the System of Rice Intensification mainly reduces the emission of which gas from paddy fields?
n12bbb119e0f.x: Alternate wetting and drying avoids continuous flooding, cutting methane production from paddies; SRI also uses less seed and saves electricity on pumping.
xa: **Direct-seeded rice**: no nursery or transplanting.
Rice GHG emissions could fall **~10%** by mid-century with better practices.
**Sustainable Sugarcane Initiative** saves seed cane and water.

nc34ac86787f.s: Variable-rate technology in agriculture refers to the practice of:
o: changing the crop variety every season without field data
applying the same quantity of inputs throughout a field
using only variable rainfall for crop production
applying inputs at varying rates within a field according to sensor or GIS maps
nc34ac86787f.x: Variable-rate technology applies agricultural inputs at different rates within a field, based on sensor information or GIS maps.
nc34ac86787f.tq: Distinguish precision-based variation from uniform field application.
xs: **Variable-rate technology** applies inputs **at varying rates within a field** per **sensor/GIS maps** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Applying the **same quantity** throughout a field is the opposite of VRT.
xa: **GPS, drones, AI, sensors** are the core of the "**Second Green Revolution**".
**Soil and Land Use Survey of India** maps soil from satellite data.
**Kisan e-Mitra**: AI chatbot for **PM-KISAN** queries.

n0face4ac5d5.s: GPS, drones, artificial intelligence and sensors are identified as core elements of which agricultural approach?
o: The Second Green Revolution and sustainable intensification
n0face4ac5d5.x: GPS, drones, AI and sensors form the technological core of the Second Green Revolution and sustainable intensification.
n0face4ac5d5.tq: Identify the exact conceptual grouping of related technologies.
xs: **GPS, drones, AI and sensors** are the core of the **Second Green Revolution** / **sustainable intensification** — so option **(3)** is correct.
They are precision tools, not organic certification or shifting cultivation.
xa: **Agritech startups** offer AI advisories, precision irrigation, crop-health monitoring.
**Kisan e-Mitra**: AI chatbot answering **PM-KISAN** queries in several languages.
The broader shift is the **Evergreen Revolution** (**M.S. Swaminathan**).

n91e6d933fe8.s: Component A of PM-KUSUM relates to
o: Installation of standalone off-grid solar pumps
Solarisation of existing grid-connected agricultural pumps
Decentralised grid-connected solar/renewable power plants on barren or fallow land
n91e6d933fe8.x: Component A of PM-KUSUM covers decentralised grid-connected solar/renewable plants on barren or fallow land. Standalone pumps and solarisation of grid-connected pumps are the other components.
xs: **PM-KUSUM Component A** = **decentralised grid-connected solar/renewable power plants on barren or fallow land** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is about **power plants on unused land**, not rooftop solar on households.
xa: **Assam's** State Irrigation Plan uses **solar pumps**.
Micro-irrigation saves **water, labour, power and fertiliser**.
**PDMC** priority: **rainfed areas**, water-stressed districts, **critical groundwater blocks**.

na5a0c9827d8.s: Which of the following protected-cultivation practices grows crops in a controlled environment and can provide protection from weather, pests and diseases?
na5a0c9827d8.x: Protected cultivation in greenhouses, polytunnels or shade nets provides a controlled environment and protection from adverse weather, pests and diseases.
na5a0c9827d8.tq: Identify the common functional feature of protected-cultivation structures.
xs: **Greenhouse or polyhouse cultivation** is protected cultivation in a **controlled environment** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It protects crops from **weather, pests, disease** and allows **year-round** cropping.
xa: Protected cultivation also uses **polytunnels** and **shade nets**.
Typical crops: **tomatoes, cucumbers, flowers**.
AP's automation micro-irrigation covers **greenhouses and shade-net** crops.

n0fdf997bc2c.s: A farmer wants year-round crop production in a non-tropical or harsh setting by using stacked layers indoors under controlled conditions. Which technology is most appropriate?
n0fdf997bc2c.x: Vertical farming grows crops in stacked indoor layers under controlled conditions and can provide year-round output even in non-tropical or harsh settings.
n0fdf997bc2c.tq: Translate the production setting and structural clues into the appropriate technology.
xs: **Vertical farming** grows crops in **stacked layers indoors** for **year-round** output in harsh settings — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is **more efficient than land farming** (APPSC-GS **2021**).
**Zero tillage** and **direct-seeded rice** are field practices, not indoor systems.
xa: **Protected cultivation** (greenhouse, polytunnel) also gives year-round crops.
**Hydroponics** saves water and space.

n60a5f1e18f1.s: From 2022–23, Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) has been implemented under which scheme?
n60a5f1e18f1.x: PDMC, launched in 2015–16, was part of PMKSY up to 2021–22 and has been implemented under RKVY since 2022–23.
xa: ⚠ Some notes still call PDMC a **PMKSY component**.
Priority: **rainfed areas**, **water-stressed districts**, **critical groundwater blocks**.
PDMC: **102 lakh ha** and **₹24,789.16 crore** central assistance (**2015-16** to **2025-26**).

n4a2928313ed.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Micro Irrigation Fund (MIF)?
o: It is a Rs 10,000 crore corpus with NABARD
Another Rs 5,000 crore was added for the 15th Finance Commission period
It was set up with an initial Rs 5,000 crore
It was operationalised in 2015-16 along with Per Drop More Crop
n4a2928313ed.x: MIF was operationalised in 2019-20; it is Per Drop More Crop that began in 2015-16.
xa: MIF progress: projects worth **₹4,709.06 crore** approved; **₹3,970.61 crore** disbursed.
**PDMC** was a PMKSY component till **2021-22**; from **2022-23** it runs under **RKVY**.
**NMSA**: up to **55%** subsidy for micro-irrigation, capped at **5 ha**.

ncee54429b4c.s: PMKSY, with the State Agriculture Department as nodal authority, is a:
ncee54429b4c.x: PMKSY is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme and the State Agriculture Department is its nodal authority.
xa: **PDMC** was part of PMKSY from **2015-16** to **2021-22**.
AP's micro-irrigation project runs **State-wide under PMKSY**.
PMKSY at **10 years** (Jul **2026**).

n8390d4780d2.s: Under which scheme is the Andhra Pradesh Micro Irrigation Project implemented throughout the State with financial assistance?
n8390d4780d2.x: The Andhra Pradesh Micro Irrigation Project is implemented State-wide under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana with financial assistance.
n8390d4780d2.tq: Identify the parent scheme associated with the State-level project.
xs: AP's micro-irrigation project runs State-wide under **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**PMFBY** is crop insurance; **PM-KUSUM** concerns solar plants on barren land.
xa: AP ranked **1st** in micro-irrigation implementation (**2024-25**).
PMKSY is a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme**; State Agriculture Department is nodal.
APMIP reports **30-40% higher productivity** (**2025-26**).

n002803afedc.s: Which centre, set up in 2012, runs ISRO's crop forecasting under FASAL?
n002803afedc.x: The Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast Centre (2012) runs ISRO's FASAL crop forecasting.
xa: MNCFC does satellite monitoring of **29 double-risk districts**.
KISAN pilots: **Haryana**, **Karnataka**, **Maharashtra**, **MP**.
**Soil and Land Use Survey of India** maps soil resources from satellite data.
**Kisan e-Mitra** is an AI chatbot answering **PM-KISAN** queries.

n01807f31a37.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Drone Corporation of Andhra Pradesh?
o: A privately owned body providing only drone imports
A central regulatory authority under the Ministry of Civil Aviation
n01807f31a37.x: The Drone Corporation of Andhra Pradesh is State-owned and provides drone-as-a-service.
n01807f31a37.tq: Use ownership and function together to identify the correct institution.
xs: The **Drone Corporation of AP (APDC)** is **State-owned** and provides **drone-as-a-service** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **central regulator** is **DGCA**; the Farmers' Registry belongs to **AgriStack**.
xa: APDC extended **drone pesticide spraying** to **all 26 districts** (Jan **2026**).
**Kisan drones** save water **up to 30%**.
**Drone Shakti** builds the drone ecosystem.

neecf0b99bad.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated use or benefit of Kisan drones?
o: Reduction of human exposure to chemicals
Elimination of the need for all irrigation water
