nd4b4a63554a.tq: Use the institutional mission association and reject the prominent but unrelated mission.
xs: **IIT Roorkee**'s facility complements the **Semiconductor, Nano and Quantum missions** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ Trap: it is **not linked to Samudrayaan** (UKPSC **2025**).
xa: It is Uttarakhand's **first nano-fabrication facility**.
**Nano Mission**: launched **2007** under **DST**.

nchemistry-19-44.s: Nano-fabrication using which material is used in advanced semiconductor research?
nchemistry-19-44.x: Nano-fabrication of silicon is central to advanced semiconductor research and chip making. ITO is for displays and selenium for sensors.
nchemistry-19-44.tq: Recall the nano uses of silicon.
n: Nano-fabrication uses silicon. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
Nano-fabrication is used in advanced semiconductor research. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 64-70]
xs: Nano-fabrication uses **silicon** for **advanced semiconductor research** — option **(4)**.
The notes link nano-fabrication only with **silicon**.
xa: **IIT Roorkee** set up Uttarakhand's **first nano-fabrication facility**, complementing **Semiconductor, Nano and Quantum missions**.
⚠ The IIT Roorkee facility is **not** linked to **Samudrayaan** (UKPSC 2025).
**Quantum dots** are used in **displays** and **solar cells**.

nf6544df0ef3.s: The indicated nitrogen-use efficiency of Nano Urea is about:
nf6544df0ef3.x: Nano Urea has an indicated nitrogen-use efficiency of about 70%, against about 30–35% for conventional urea.
xa: It is a **liquid foliar spray**, **~20-50 nm** (**IFFCO**).
Cuts urea use up to **~25%** (LENS May **2026**).
**Nano urea does not fully replace** conventional urea.

na82df57fe32.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Nano Urea?
o: Its particle size is about 20–50 nm
It is applied as a foliar spray
It may reduce urea use by up to about 25%
na82df57fe32.x: Nano Urea does not fully replace conventional urea; it is a 20–50 nm foliar spray that may cut urea use by up to about 25%.
xa: N-use efficiency **~70%** vs **30-35%**.
**8 plants**; sales **11.31 crore** bottles (**30 Sep 2025**).

n412412ab066.s: The specification of Nano DAP was notified under the Fertiliser Control Order in:
n412412ab066.x: Nano DAP was notified under the FCO on 2 March 2023; it is used for seed treatment and foliar application.
xa: Nano DAP: **3 plants**, **7.64 crore** bottles/yr; sales **3.19 crore** (**30 Sep 2025**).
Nano Urea **8%** spec was also notified on **2 Mar 2023**.
Criticism: rapid **nano-urea** rollout **without long-term studies**.

n3bbffa1dfb4.s: The Nano Mission was launched in 2007 as an umbrella programme under:
n3bbffa1dfb4.x: The Nano Mission (2007) is a DST umbrella programme, with an initial outlay of about Rs 1,000 crore for five years.
xa: National Quantum Mission outlay: **Rs 6,003.65 crore**, **2023-24 to 2030-31**.
**DST Nano Programme**: **Rs 350 crore** in FY **2024-25**.
Nano Mission continues under DST; institutes include **INST Mohali**.

n6bb3d6ae8cd.s: Which of the following is an engineered, not natural, nanoparticle?
n6bb3d6ae8cd.x: Nano-silver is deliberately manufactured; volcanic ash, sea spray and smoke are natural sources of nanoparticles.
xa: Other engineered nanoparticles: **CNTs**, **TiO2**.
**Nanotoxicity**: oxidative stress, inflammation, **bioaccumulation**.
**FSSAI guidelines 2022** cover food.

n8d67cad57cb.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the regulation of nanotechnology in India?
o: India has a dedicated comprehensive nano law
DGFASLI has issued guidelines on occupational risk
Dual-use concerns are addressed under the SCOMET list
n8d67cad57cb.x: India does not have a dedicated nano law; DGFASLI guidelines, FSSAI's 2022 guidelines and the SCOMET list are the relevant frameworks.
xa: Agri: **Guidelines for Evaluation of Nano-based Agri-input and Food Products** — **DBT**, **2020**.
Another gap: the **"nano-divide"**.
Criticism: rapid **nano-urea** rollout without long-term studies.

n32068721632.s: Which of the following concerns has been raised regarding the rapid rollout of nano-urea?
o: The lack of long-term studies before widespread deployment
The complete prohibition of nano-inputs under a nano-specific law
Its inability to be absorbed by plants under any condition
The absence of any possible agricultural use
n32068721632.x: A major criticism is that nano-urea has been rolled out rapidly without adequate long-term studies. The concern is about evidence and safety assessment, not the complete absence of agricultural use.
n32068721632.tq: Find the specific criticism rather than an extreme or absolute claim.
xs: Nano-urea was criticised for **rapid rollout without long-term studies** — option **(1)** is correct.
There is **no nano-specific law**, so option (2) is wrong; nano inputs actually **raise absorption efficiency**.
xa: Nano-urea **safety concerns** in news (**2 May 2026**).
Nano urea **does not fully replace** conventional urea.
Benefit: **cuts fertiliser subsidy and imports**.

n8c5afcb7c95.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the vector and pathogen of malaria?
n8c5afcb7c95.x: Malaria is transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito and is caused by Plasmodium, a protozoan.
n8c5afcb7c95.tq: Match the disease with its characteristic vector and pathogen.
xs: Malaria is spread by the **female Anopheles** mosquito and caused by **Plasmodium** (a protozoan) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Aedes aegypti/flavivirus** = **dengue**; **Culex/JE virus** = **Japanese Encephalitis**; **sandfly/Leishmania donovani** = **kala-azar**.
xa: Plasmodium species: **falciparum** (deadliest), **vivax**, **malariae**, **ovale**; it destroys **RBCs**.
**National Framework for Malaria Elimination (2016-2030)**: malaria-free India by **2030**.
⚠ Malaria is vector-borne but **not zoonotic** in routine classification.

nb1edcefed7b.s: Which of the following diseases is transmitted by Culex mosquitoes and is amplified by pigs?
nb1edcefed7b.x: Japanese encephalitis is transmitted by Culex mosquitoes, and pigs act as amplifying hosts.
nb1edcefed7b.tq: Combine the vector clue with the amplifying-host clue.
xs: **Japanese Encephalitis** is spread by **Culex**, and **pigs amplify** the virus — option **(1)** is correct.
**Lymphatic filariasis** is also Culex-borne (**Culex quinquefasciatus**) but has no pig amplifier; **yellow fever** = Aedes/Haemagogus; **kala-azar** = sandfly.
xa: JE is in the **UIP** for **endemic districts**.
AP **AES/JE 2025**: **146** cases, **2** deaths.
NCVBDC covers six diseases incl. **JE**.

nf3037b27164.s: Which one of the following diseases is NOT spread by a mosquito?
nf3037b27164.x: Scrub typhus is transmitted by the chigger mite. Lymphatic filariasis, Japanese encephalitis and dengue are mosquito-borne diseases.
nf3037b27164.tq: Find the non-mosquito vector among otherwise mosquito-associated diseases.
xs: **Scrub typhus** is spread by the **chigger mite**, not a mosquito — option **(4)** is the answer.
**Lymphatic filariasis** (Culex quinquefasciatus), **dengue** (Aedes) and **JE** (Culex) are mosquito-borne.
xa: Scrub typhus pathogen: **Orientia tsutsugamushi**.
AP: **941** scrub typhus cases, rising in **ASR** and **Parvathipuram Manyam**.
Other non-mosquito diseases: **kala-azar** (sandfly), **sleeping sickness** (tsetse fly).

n066f3b8fd6a.s: Scrub typhus is transmitted by the:
n066f3b8fd6a.x: Scrub typhus is spread by the chigger mite; plague by the rat flea and sleeping sickness by the tsetse fly.
xa: Plague is zoonotic: **rodents** via rat flea.
Kala-azar vector: **sandfly**.
Filariasis targets the **lymphatic system** (elephantiasis).

n3dd4e606822.s: Which species of Plasmodium is most lethal and is particularly associated with cerebral malaria?
n3dd4e606822.x: Plasmodium falciparum is the most lethal human-infecting malaria parasite and may cause cerebral malaria.
n3dd4e606822.tq: Identify the species linked with the severe clinical form.
xs: **Plasmodium falciparum** is the most lethal and causes **cerebral malaria** — option **(4)** is correct.
**P. vivax**, **P. malariae** and **P. ovale** also infect humans but are not the deadliest.
xa: Fifth human species: **P. knowlesi**.
Vector: **female Anopheles**; Plasmodium destroys **RBCs**.

n034b4b51d06.s: In forests, yellow fever is spread by which mosquito?
n034b4b51d06.x: Forest yellow fever is spread by Haemagogus; malaria is spread by female Anopheles and Culex spreads JE and filariasis.
xa: **Dengue**: **Aedes aegypti**; mainly hits **platelets**.
**Kala-azar**: **sandfly** — not a mosquito.
**Chikungunya** virus is an **alphavirus**.

n432f3e9b8dc.s: Which one of the following zoonotic diseases is transmitted through the bite of a rat flea?
n432f3e9b8dc.x: Plague is associated with rodents and is transmitted through rat fleas. Rabies is generally transmitted by the bite of infected animals, Nipah is associated with fruit bats and anthrax with infected livestock.
n432f3e9b8dc.tq: Match the disease with its animal source and transmission route.
xs: **Plague** comes from **rodents via the rat flea** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Rabies** spreads by **animal bite** (dogs, bats); **Nipah** from **fruit bats**; **anthrax** from **infected livestock**.
xa: Plague pathogen: **Yersinia pestis**.
**Epidemic Diseases Act 1897** was enacted against **bubonic plague** (Bombay).
**Mpox**: rodents and primates.

n4ce87bac0da.s: Which one of the following is the odd one out on the basis of its usual classification as a zoonotic disease?
n4ce87bac0da.x: Rabies, anthrax and Nipah are zoonotic diseases associated with animal sources. Malaria is vector-borne but is not classified as zoonotic in the routine sense used here.
n4ce87bac0da.tq: Separate zoonotic diseases from a vector-borne disease that is not routinely classified as zoonotic.
xs: **Malaria** is vector-borne but **not zoonotic** in routine classification — option **(2)** is the odd one out.
**Anthrax** (livestock), **Nipah** (fruit bats) and **rabies** (dog bite) are zoonoses.
xa: ⚠ Not all zoonoses are vector-borne — **rabies** is zoonotic but **not vector-borne**.
Other zoonoses: **scrub typhus**, **KFD**, **avian influenza**.
**One Health** = human, animal and environmental health managed together.

nf074a37b7d9.s: Which two diseases under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme are described as outbreak-prone and climate-sensitive?
nf074a37b7d9.x: Malaria and dengue are identified as outbreak-prone and climate-sensitive diseases under the programme.
nf074a37b7d9.tq: Focus on the stated comparison within the programme list.
xs: **Malaria and dengue** are the **outbreak-prone, climate-sensitive** NCVBDC diseases — option **(2)** is correct.
**Kala-azar** and **LF** are **elimination targets** (with malaria); **yellow fever** is not among the six covered diseases.
xa: NCVBDC's six: **malaria, JE, dengue, chikungunya, kala-azar, LF**.
Warming **expands the range** of dengue and malaria vectors.

nff4fe8cafd6.s: Under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (now NCVBDC), which diseases are targeted for elimination?
nff4fe8cafd6.x: Of the six diseases covered (malaria, JE, dengue, chikungunya, kala-azar, LF), the elimination targets are malaria, lymphatic filariasis and kala-azar. Dengue, chikungunya and JE are controlled, not targeted for elimination.
xs: The elimination targets are **malaria, lymphatic filariasis and kala-azar** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Dengue**, **chikungunya** and **JE** are covered but not slated for elimination.
xa: **Malaria and dengue** = **outbreak-prone and climate-sensitive**.
Malaria-free India target: **2030**.
**Kala-azar** vector: **sandfly**; **LF** pathogen: **Wuchereria bancrofti**.

n72a14da5664.s: Which of the following measures is most directly associated with the response to vector-borne disease burden in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Indoor residual spraying, LLIN mosquito nets and source reduction
Removal of all livestock from tribal districts
Replacement of mosquito control with vaccination alone
Exclusive use of antibiotics and suspension of surveillance
n72a14da5664.x: The response includes indoor residual spraying, long-lasting insecticidal nets and source reduction. These measures target mosquito vectors and their breeding sites.
n72a14da5664.tq: Apply the control method to the vector-borne disease scenario.
xs: AP's response: **indoor residual spraying (IRS)**, **LLIN mosquito nets** and **source reduction** — option **(1)** is correct.
These target the vectors; removing livestock, vaccination alone or antibiotics are not the measures.
xa: Free **LLINs** for **7.80 lakh** people (**Rs 19.25 crore**) (**23 Apr 2026**).
**24-member State task force** (Jan **2026**).
Bio-control options: **Gambusia**, guppy, **Bti**, **Wolbachia**.

nbiology-63-4.x: Mycoplasma pneumoniae causes atypical pneumonia; C. tetani causes tetanus, Y. pestis plague and M. leprae leprosy.
n: Clostridium tetani causes tetanus. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 118-120]
Yersinia pestis causes plague. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 118-120]
Mycoplasma pneumoniae causes atypical pneumonia. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 118-120]
Mycobacterium leprae causes leprosy. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #63 · pp 118-120]
xa: Yersinia pestis = **Pasteurella pestis**; plague affects **lymph nodes** (**buboes**).
Leprosy affects **skin** and **peripheral nerves**.
Tetanus follows a **contaminated wound**; causes **muscle spasms** and **jaw involvement**.

nbiology-15-25.s: Besides mosquitoes, Zika can be transmitted through:
nbiology-15-25.x: Zika virus spreads by mosquitoes, blood and sexual transmission, and causes fever, rash and joint pain.
n: Zika is caused by Zika virus. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Zika is a viral disease. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Zika can spread through mosquito transmission. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Zika can spread through blood transmission. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Zika can spread through sexual transmission. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Zika can cause fever. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Zika can cause rash. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Zika can cause joint pain. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xa: Zika is also transmitted by **Aedes albopictus** — the **tiger mosquito**.
2024 PYQ key: **Zika – Aedes**; **Yellow fever – Haemagogus**.
**Chikungunya** (**CHIKV**) causes **severe joint pain**.

nbiology-15-32.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Japanese encephalitis?
o: It is caused by the Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV)
Pigs and wild birds are its reservoirs
It spreads mainly through contaminated water
nbiology-15-32.x: Japanese encephalitis spreads by mosquito bite, not through water; JEV causes it and pigs and wild birds are its reservoirs.
n: Japanese encephalitis is caused by JEV. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Japanese encephalitis is a viral disease. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Pigs and wild birds are reservoirs for Japanese encephalitis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Japanese encephalitis is transmitted through mosquito bites. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xa: **Pigs amplify** JE; it affects the **brain**.
**Culex** also spreads **filariasis**.
JE vaccine is under **UIP** in **endemic districts**.

nbiology-15-61.x: Fascioliasis, caused by the liver fluke Fasciola, mainly in ruminants, is caught from raw water plants and damages the liver and bile ducts.
n: Fascioliasis is caused by Fasciola hepatica or Fasciola gigantica. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Fascioliasis is caused by a parasitic worm. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Ruminants are the main hosts for fascioliasis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Fascioliasis can spread through raw water plants. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Fascioliasis affects the liver and bile ducts. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xa: **Schistosomiasis** spreads through **unsafe water** with **snails** as intermediate hosts.
**Neurocysticercosis** is caused by **Taenia solium eggs**.
**Ascariasis** affects the **small intestine**.

nbiology-15-68.s: Ascariasis, caused by Ascaris lumbricoides, is a disease caused by a:
nbiology-15-68.x: Ascariasis is a nematode infection by Ascaris lumbricoides, caught by swallowing its eggs.
n: Ascariasis is caused by Ascaris lumbricoides. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Ascariasis is a nematode disease. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Ascariasis has humans as hosts. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Ascariasis spreads through ingestion of eggs. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xa: Ascariasis affects the **small intestine**.
**Filariasis** (**Wuchereria bancrofti**) is also a **nematode** disease.
**Guinea worm disease** is caused by **Dracunculus medinensis**.

nbiology-16-1.s: Rice tungro disease is spread by the:
nbiology-16-1.x: The leafhopper spreads rice tungro; the sandfly spreads kala-azar, the rat flea plague and the snail schistosomiasis.
n: Phlebotomus argentipes is a sandfly. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 28-29]
Sandflies transmit kala-azar. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 28-29]
Rat fleas transmit plague. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 28-29]
Leafhoppers transmit rice tungro. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 28-29]
Snails are intermediate hosts of schistosomiasis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 28-29]
xa: **Cyclops** (a water flea) — **Guinea worm**.
**Whitefly** (**Bemisia tabaci**) — **yellow vein mosaic** of okra.
**Tsetse fly** (**Glossina**) — **sleeping sickness**.

nbiology-16-6.s: Guinea worm larvae are carried by:
nbiology-16-6.x: Cyclops carries Guinea worm larvae; Culex spreads filariasis and JE, Anopheles malaria and Aedes albopictus dengue and chikungunya.
n: The female Anopheles mosquito is a vector of malaria. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 28-29]
Aedes albopictus is a vector of dengue. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 28-29]
Aedes albopictus is a vector of chikungunya. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 28-29]
Aedes albopictus is a vector of Zika. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 28-29]
Aedes albopictus is a vector of yellow fever. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 28-29]
Anopheles mosquitoes are also associated with filariasis in some regions. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 28-29]
Anopheles mosquitoes are also associated with encephalitis in some regions. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 28-29]
Cyclops transmits guinea worm. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #16 · pp 28-29]
xa: Malaria cycle: **humans** and **mosquitoes**; also spread by **blood transfusion** and needles.
Culex **quinquefasciatus** spreads filariasis.
JE reservoirs: **pigs and wild birds**.

nbiology-17-12.x: Zika fever is caused by Zika virus; yellow fever virus causes yellow fever.
n: Zika virus causes Zika fever. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
Yellow fever virus causes yellow fever. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
Ebola virus causes Ebola. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
Nipah virus causes Nipah disease. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
xa: Zika causes **fever**, **rash**, **joint pain**.
Yellow fever can cause **haemorrhagic disease**.
Ebola and Nipah are **viral zoonotic** diseases.

nbiology-18-4.x: Dracunculus medinensis causes Guinea worm disease; Ascaris causes ascariasis and Trypanosoma sleeping sickness.
n: Plasmodium causes malaria. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 31-32]
Trypanosoma causes sleeping sickness. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 31-32]
Ascaris lumbricoides causes ascariasis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 31-32]
Dracunculus medinensis causes Guinea worm disease. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 31-32]
xa: Guinea worm is carried by **Cyclops**, a **water flea**.
Plasmodium and Trypanosoma are **protozoans**.
Ascariasis is a **nematode** disease.

nbiology-64-19.x: Leishmania donovani causes kala-azar; Entamoeba histolytica causes amoebic dysentery and Candida candidiasis.
n: Influenza virus causes influenza. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 120-122]
Candida causes candidiasis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 120-122]
Entamoeba histolytica causes amoebic dysentery. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 120-122]
Leishmania donovani causes kala-azar. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 120-122]
xa: Kala-azar (**visceral leishmaniasis**) affects **liver, spleen and bone marrow**.
Amoebiasis spreads via **contaminated food or water**.
**Swine flu** (**H1N1**) is an influenza.

nbiology-23-5.x: Morbillivirus causes rinderpest; Aphthovirus causes foot-and-mouth disease.
n: The virus Ebola virus causes Ebola. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-41]
The virus Morbillivirus causes rinderpest. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-41]
The virus Aphthovirus causes foot and mouth disease. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-41]
The virus Zika virus causes Zika. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-41]
The virus Yellow fever virus causes yellow fever. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #23 · pp 39-41]
xa: Both Zika and yellow fever are spread by **Aedes aegypti**.
Yellow fever is also spread by **Haemagogus** in forests.
Rinderpest was eradicated in **2011**.

nbiology-15-16.s: Polio, which can cause paralysis, attacks the:
o: Spinal cord and central nervous system
nbiology-15-16.x: Polio is a human viral disease spread by the faecal-oral route that attacks the spinal cord and central nervous system.
n: Polio is a viral disease. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Polio has humans as hosts. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Polio is transmitted by the fecal–oral route. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Polio can spread through contaminated food or water. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Polio affects the spinal cord and central nervous system. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Polio can cause paralysis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xa: Polio is on the **faeco-oral** list with cholera, typhoid and hepatitis A and E.
Polio is one of the diseases under the **UIP** (**1985**, **12 diseases**).
**Mission Indradhanush** (**Dec 2014**) aims at **>90% full immunisation**.

nbiology-15-21.x: Mumps is a human viral disease caused by mumps virus and spread through saliva and nasal secretions.
n: Mumps is caused by mumps virus. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Mumps is a viral disease. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Mumps has humans as hosts. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Mumps spreads through saliva and nasal secretions. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xa: Mumps affects the **salivary** or **parotid glands**.
**Measles** is caused by **measles virus** and is **highly contagious**.
**Measles** and **rubella** are among the **UIP** diseases.

nbiology-15-46.s: Which disease forms a false membrane in the throat and nose?
nbiology-15-46.x: Diphtheria forms a false membrane in the throat and nose; pertussis is whooping cough.
n: Diphtheria affects the throat and nose. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Gonorrhoea affects the reproductive organs. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Syphilis affects the genitals, rectum and mouth. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Pertussis causes whooping cough. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xa: Diphtheria: **Corynebacterium diphtheriae**; pertussis: **Bordetella pertussis**.
Syphilis: **Treponema pallidum**; gonorrhoea: **Neisseria gonorrhoeae**.
Syphilis affects **genitals, rectum and mouth**.

nbiology-15-51.x: Tuberculosis mainly attacks the lungs, though it can spread to other organs.
nbiology-15-51.tq: Recall the organ affected by tuberculosis.
n: Tuberculosis affects the lungs. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xs: Tuberculosis primarily affects the **lungs** — option **(2)**.
**Mycobacterium tuberculosis** spreads by **respiratory transmission**.
xa: **Pneumonia** also affects the **lungs**.
**Rheumatic fever** affects the **heart**, **brain**, **joints**, **skin**.
WHO 2024 critical priority pathogens include **rifampicin-resistant TB**.

nbiology-15-55.s: Botulinum toxin, which can cause paralysis, mainly acts on the:
nbiology-15-55.x: Botulinum toxin blocks nerves and can cause paralysis; the liver is not its target.
n: Botulism affects the nerves. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Botulism can cause paralysis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xa: Botulism is a **bacterial intoxication** by **Clostridium botulinum toxin**.
Spread via **food** or **wounds**; it also affects **infants**.
**Ergotism** is a fungal intoxication from **Claviceps purpurea**.

nbiology-15-9.s: Which disease may lead to elephantiasis by involving the lymph glands?
nbiology-15-9.x: Filarial worms block lymph vessels, causing elephantiasis; Ascaris lives mainly in the small intestine.
n: Filariasis affects the lymph glands. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Filariasis can cause elephantiasis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Ascariasis affects the small intestine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xa: Filariasis is spread by **Culex quinquefasciatus**.
Ascariasis spreads by **ingestion of eggs**.
**Lymphatic filariasis** is among NCVBDC **elimination targets** with **malaria** and **kala-azar**.

nbiology-15-58.x: Kala-azar attacks the liver, spleen and bone marrow; amoebiasis affects the intestine and late sleeping sickness the brain.
n: Kala-azar affects the liver, spleen and bone marrow. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Sleeping sickness affects the brain and central nervous system in later stages. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Amoebiasis affects the intestine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Schistosomiasis affects the urinary tract and intestine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xa: Kala-azar: **Leishmania donovani**, spread by **sandflies**; **dogs** are reservoirs.
Sleeping sickness: **Trypanosoma brucei**, spread by **tsetse flies**.
Amoebiasis: **Entamoeba histolytica**, via **contaminated food or water**.
⚠ **Leishmaniasis** is spread by sandfly, NOT mosquito (APPSC 2025 PYQ).

nbiology-15-65.x: Neurocysticercosis comes from swallowing Taenia solium eggs, and its larvae lodge in the brain and CNS.
n: Neurocysticercosis is caused by Taenia solium eggs. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Neurocysticercosis is caused by a parasite. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Neurocysticercosis has humans as hosts. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Neurocysticercosis spreads through contaminated food or water. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Neurocysticercosis affects the brain and central nervous system. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xa: Taenia solium is associated with **pork** and also causes **taeniasis**.
**Sleeping sickness** also affects the **brain and CNS** in later stages.
**Japanese encephalitis** affects the **brain**.

nbiology-15-70.s: Ergotism is caused by a toxin of:
nbiology-15-70.x: Ergotism comes from Claviceps purpurea toxin; Aspergillus causes aspergillosis and Trichophyton athlete's foot.
n: Athlete's foot has humans as hosts. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Mucormycosis is caused by Mucormycetes. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Aspergillosis is caused by Aspergillus. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Ergotism is caused by Claviceps purpurea toxin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xa: Ergotism is a **fungal intoxication** from **rye and cereals**.
Mucormycosis affects **nose, sinuses, eyes and brain**.
Aspergillosis can be **respiratory** or **systemic**.

nbiology-15-71.x: Athlete's foot affects the skin of the foot and spreads through contaminated floors, towels or clothes.
n: Athlete's foot can spread through contaminated floors, towels or clothes. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Athlete's foot affects the skin of the foot. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Mucormycosis has the environment as a source. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Mucormycosis has no specified vector. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Mucormycosis can affect the nose, sinuses, eyes and brain. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xa: Mucormycosis is caused by **Mucormycetes**.
**Aspergillosis** hosts: **humans, birds and animals**.
**Ringworm** is caused by **dermatophytes**.

nbiology-17-6.s: Which malaria parasite causes relapsing malaria because it forms dormant liver stages (hypnozoites)?
nbiology-17-6.x: P. vivax forms dormant hypnozoites in the liver, which reactivate and cause relapses of malaria. P. falciparum causes malignant malaria without relapse, while Leishmania and Trypanosoma are not malaria parasites.
nbiology-17-6.tq: Link relapses to the parasite with dormant liver stages.
n: P. vivax accounts for a major share of malaria cases. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
xs: **P. vivax** causes relapsing (**recurring**) malaria — option **(3)**.
**P. falciparum** causes **malignant malaria**; **Leishmania** causes **kala-azar**; **Trypanosoma** causes **sleeping sickness**.
xa: P. vivax accounts for a **major share** of malaria cases.
Other human species: **P. malariae**, **P. ovale**, **P. knowlesi**.
Malaria affects the **liver** and **red blood cells**, with an **enlarged spleen**.

nbiology-64-7.x: Dermatophytes cause ringworm; Candida causes candidiasis, Aspergillus aspergillosis and Mucormycetes mucormycosis.
n: Dermatophytes cause ringworm. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 120-122]
Candida causes candidiasis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 120-122]
Aspergillus causes aspergillosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 120-122]
Mucormycetes cause mucormycosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #64 · pp 120-122]
xa: Athlete's foot: **Trichophyton**, **Epidermophyton**, **Microsporum**.
**Aspergillus flavus** produces **aflatoxin**.
Mucormycosis source: the **environment**.

n08d67cbe09b.s: The Widal test is associated with the diagnosis of which disease?
n08d67cbe09b.x: Typhoid is caused by Salmonella Typhi, and the Widal test is associated with its diagnosis.
n08d67cbe09b.tq: Link the named diagnostic test to its specific water-borne disease.
xs: The **Widal test** is for **typhoid** (**Salmonella Typhi**) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Cholera** is caused by **Vibrio cholerae**; **hepatitis A** is viral; **dysentery** by **Shigella**, **E. coli**, **rotavirus**.
xa: Typhoid spreads by the **faeco-oral route**.
Floods spread **cholera, typhoid, hepatitis** and **leptospirosis**.
Cholera toxin → severe **dehydration**; treated with **ORS**.

na699f254ebf.s: Which hepatitis viruses spread through the faecal-oral route?
na699f254ebf.x: Hepatitis A and E are faecal-oral, while hepatitis B and C are generally blood-borne.
xa: Faeco-oral group: **cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A and E, acute diarrhoea, dysentery, polio**.
TB: **Mycobacterium tuberculosis**, **droplet nuclei**, targets the **lungs**.
Hepatitis A and E cause **jaundice**.

n2da62587d7e.s: Which one of the following is the correct set of diseases commonly spread through the faecal-oral route by contaminated water or food?
o: Tuberculosis, hepatitis B, malaria, dengue and rabies
Japanese encephalitis, cholera, hepatitis B, scrub typhus and influenza
Cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A and E, acute diarrhoea, dysentery and polio
Hepatitis C, sleeping sickness, yellow fever, typhoid and plague

n380c6e36c41.x: NCVBDC covers malaria, Japanese encephalitis, dengue, chikungunya, kala-azar and lymphatic filariasis. Tuberculosis is not a vector-borne disease covered under this programme.
n380c6e36c41.tq: Find the disease belonging to a neighbouring health programme rather than the listed vector-borne group.
xs: **Tuberculosis** is not covered by NVBDCP/NCVBDC — option **(2)** is the answer.
NCVBDC covers six: **malaria, JE, dengue, chikungunya, kala-azar, lymphatic filariasis**.
xa: TB is **air-borne** — spread by **droplet nuclei**, targets the **lungs**.
Elimination targets: **malaria**, **LF**, **kala-azar**.
AP **Adult BCG drive** (from **16 May 2024**): **27.10 lakh** doses — **leader in India**.

n5c66e54c74b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's response to antimicrobial resistance?
o: The Red Line campaign puts a red line on the packs of all over-the-counter medicines
Kerala's KARSAP (2018) was the first State-level AMR action plan
The National Action Plan on AMR (2017) is based on the One Health approach
The Red Line campaign was launched in 2016
n5c66e54c74b.x: The Red Line (2016) marks prescription-only antibiotics, not all over-the-counter medicines.
xa: **National One Health Mission** (**PM-STIAC**) tackles **AMR**, rabies, Nipah, avian influenza.
**National Institute of One Health**: **Nagpur**.
AMR causes include **self-medication** and unregulated veterinary drugs.

n3678c3c54bf.s: The National One Health Mission is associated with which of the following institutions or bodies?
n3678c3c54bf.x: The National One Health Mission is associated with PM-STIAC and provides institutional multisectoral coordination for One Health actions.
n3678c3c54bf.tq: Use institutional association to distinguish the mission from unrelated national bodies.
xs: The **National One Health Mission** comes under **PM-STIAC** — option **(3)** is correct.
It provides **institutional multisectoral coordination**; ECI, CPCB and ILO are unrelated.
xa: Used against **rabies**, **Nipah**, **avian influenza** and **AMR**.
**National Institute of One Health**: **Nagpur**.
AP's **State Action Plan on zoonotic diseases** (Jul **2026**) is under One Health.

ne48133ae784.s: The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 was enacted against which disease in Bombay?
ne48133ae784.x: The four-section Act was enacted against bubonic plague in Bombay; the amendment protecting health workers came in 2020.
xa: **Plague**: rodents via **rat flea**; pathogen **Yersinia pestis**.
**IDSP (2004)**: disease surveillance under **MoHFW/NCDC**.
**NCDC** leads **surveillance and response**; IDSP now runs on the **IHIP** platform.

na8bb6e6a92d.s: The Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP) was introduced in which year?
na8bb6e6a92d.x: The Universal Immunisation Programme was introduced in 1985.
na8bb6e6a92d.tq: Select the programme year from the sequence of major immunisation milestones.
xs: The **Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP)** began in **1985** — option **(2)** is correct.
It covers **12 diseases**.
xa: **Mission Indradhanush**: **Dec 2014**, **>90%** full immunisation target.
**U-WIN** registers every UIP vaccination.
UIP includes **JE** in **endemic districts**.

nd8bf0ba21a1.s: What is the principal function of the U-WIN digital portal?
o: Registering every vaccination provided under UIP
Monitoring only antimicrobial resistance in hospitals
Recording only adult BCG doses in Andhra Pradesh
nd8bf0ba21a1.x: U-WIN is a digital portal for registering every vaccination administered under the Universal Immunisation Programme.
nd8bf0ba21a1.tq: Match the digital platform with its exact record-keeping function.
xs: **U-WIN** is the digital portal **registering every UIP vaccination** — option **(2)** is correct.
It does not license manufacturers, monitor AMR or record only AP BCG doses.
xa: **Mission Indradhanush** (**Dec 2014**): **>90%** full immunisation.
**IDSP** surveillance now runs on the **IHIP** digital platform.

nbiology-65-13.s: Acetobacter is used in the production of:
nbiology-65-13.x: Acetobacter gives vinegar; Penicillium gives penicillin, Streptomyces streptomycin and Bacillus several antibiotics.
n: Penicillium produces penicillin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
Acetobacter produces vinegar. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
Acetobacter produces acetic acid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
Streptomyces produces streptomycin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
Bacillus produces several antibiotics. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 122-124]
xa: **Streptomyces** and **Bacillus** are **important bacterial sources** of antibiotics.
Penicillin was discovered from **Penicillium notatum** in **1928**.
Streptomycin is used against **tuberculosis**.

nbiology-66-2.s: Which antibiotic is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm?
nbiology-66-2.x: Griseofulvin treats ringworm; chloramphenicol is used for typhoid and streptomycin was the first anti-TB drug.
n: Penicillin is associated with bacterial infections. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Streptomycin is associated with tuberculosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Tetracycline is associated with bacterial infections. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Chloramphenicol is associated with typhoid. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
Chloramphenicol is associated with bacterial infections. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 124-126]
xa: Fleming found penicillin in **1928** from **Penicillium notatum**.
Chloramphenicol is **broad-spectrum**.
**Ringworm** is caused by **dermatophytes**.

nbiology-20-12.s: Epidemic dropsy is caused by the oil of:
nbiology-20-12.x: Epidemic dropsy comes from mustard oil adulterated with Argemone mexicana oil, which contains sanguinarine and dihydrosanguinarine.
n: Epidemic dropsy is caused by Argemone mexicana oil. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 33-35]
Argemone mexicana oil contains sanguinarine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 33-35]
Argemone mexicana oil contains dihydrosanguinarine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 33-35]
xa: **Mushroom poisoning**: **Amanita**, with **α-amanitin**.
**Aflatoxin**: **Aspergillus flavus** and **Aspergillus parasiticus**.
**Ergotism**: **ergot alkaloids** of **Claviceps purpurea**.

n569f7527c6d.s: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination (2016–2030) aims to achieve which of the following?
o: Elimination of all communicable diseases by 2030
n569f7527c6d.x: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination covers the period 2016–2030 and aims at a malaria-free India by 2030.
n569f7527c6d.tq: Match the programme period with its precise national target.
xs: The **National Framework for Malaria Elimination (2016-2030)** aims at a **malaria-free India by 2030** — option **(2)** is correct.
It targets malaria only, not dengue or all communicable diseases.
xa: Malaria is an NCVBDC elimination target alongside **LF** and **kala-azar**.
WHO malaria-free in South Asia: **Maldives (2015)**, **Sri Lanka (2016)**.
AP response: **IRS**, **LLINs**, source reduction.

nced42d88767.s: The antibiotic Nafithromycin, launched in November 2024, was developed by:
nced42d88767.x: Nafithromycin was developed by Wockhardt with BIRAC support and launched on 20 November 2024 by Dr Jitendra Singh; it was not developed by Sun Pharma.
xa: Brand name **"Miqnaf"**; a **macrolide** for community-acquired bacterial pneumonia.
**National Action Plan on AMR**: **2017**.
**Kerala KARSAP (2018)**: first State AMR plan.

n531c798b43e.s: The 2026 rise in malaria cases in Andhra Pradesh was particularly concentrated in which districts or area?
n531c798b43e.x: The rise in malaria in 2026 was concentrated in Alluri Sitharama Raju, Polavaram and Vizianagaram districts.
n531c798b43e.tq: Use location-based elimination and avoid substituting other district groups.
xs: The **2026** malaria rise was concentrated in **ASR (Alluri Sitharama Raju), Polavaram and Vizianagaram** — option **(1)** is correct.
These are **tribal/agency** districts, not the coastal or Rayalaseema districts in other options.
xa: Free **LLINs** for **7.80 lakh** people (**Rs 19.25 crore**) in ASR and Parvathipuram-Manyam.
Response: **IRS**, **LLINs**, source reduction.

nd0cf777f058.s: Which of the following correctly represents the reported 2026 burden of scrub typhus in Andhra Pradesh and its concentration?
o: 1,475 cases, rising in all coastal districts
941 cases, rising in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam
52 cases, rising in ASR and Kurnool
146 cases, rising in Polavaram and Vizianagaram
nd0cf777f058.x: Scrub typhus accounted for 941 cases and was rising in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam districts.
nd0cf777f058.tq: Match the disease burden figure with the correct geographical concentration.
xs: AP had **941** scrub typhus cases, **rising in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam** — option **(2)** is correct.
xa: Scrub typhus vector: **chigger mite**; pathogen **Orientia tsutsugamushi**.
**High-level committees** were set up for scrub typhus.
**Agency districts** carry most of AP's scrub typhus.

nbiology-15-73.s: Ergotism is associated with eating infected:
nbiology-15-73.x: Ergotism comes from eating rye or cereals infected by the ergot fungus and affects the nervous, vascular and endocrine systems.
n: Ergotism is associated with rye and cereals. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Ergotism can spread through ingestion. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Ergotism affects the nervous, vascular and endocrine systems. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xa: It is caused by **ergot alkaloids** produced by **Claviceps purpurea**.
Ergotism is a **fungal intoxication**.
**Aflatoxin** comes from **Aspergillus flavus** and **Aspergillus parasiticus**.

n51102e8f353.s: Amoebiasis is primarily an infection of the:
o: Lymphatic system caused by filarial worms
Small intestine caused by Ascaris lumbricoides
Large intestine caused by Entamoeba histolytica
n51102e8f353.x: Amoebiasis affects the large intestine and is caused by Entamoeba histolytica.
n51102e8f353.tq: Discriminate between similar disease-organ and causative-organism combinations.
xs: **Amoebiasis** infects the **large intestine**, caused by **Entamoeba histolytica** — option **(3)** is correct.
**Ascaris lumbricoides** = **ascariasis** (small intestine); **filariasis** = lymphatic system; **Mycobacterium tuberculosis** = TB (lungs).
xa: **Dengue** targets **platelets** (APPSC **2023**).
**Malaria**: liver, then RBCs.
Water-borne **dysentery** pathogens: **rotavirus**, **E. coli**, **Shigella**.

nbiology-17-7.x: Taenia solium causes neurocysticercosis; Ascaris causes ascariasis and Fasciola fascioliasis.
n: Ascaris lumbricoides causes ascariasis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
Taenia solium causes neurocysticercosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
Schistosomes cause schistosomiasis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
Fasciola hepatica/gigantica causes fascioliasis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #17 · pp 29-31]
xa: Taenia solium also causes **taeniasis**; associated with **pork**.
Schistosomiasis affects **urinary tract and intestine**.
Fascioliasis affects **liver and bile ducts**.

nbiology-18-7.s: Taenia solium, which causes taeniasis and neurocysticercosis, is associated with:
nbiology-18-7.x: Taenia solium is the pork tapeworm; it infects humans, causing taeniasis and, from its eggs, neurocysticercosis.
n: Taenia solium has humans as hosts. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 31-32]
Taenia solium is associated with pork. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 31-32]
Taenia solium causes taeniasis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 31-32]
Taenia solium causes neurocysticercosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #18 · pp 31-32]
xa: Neurocysticercosis is caused by **Taenia solium eggs** via **contaminated food or water**.
It affects the **brain and central nervous system**.
**Fascioliasis** hosts are **ruminants** (cattle and sheep).

nbiology-15-27.s: AIDS is caused by which of the following pathogens?
nbiology-15-27.x: AIDS is caused by HIV, a retrovirus that destroys helper T cells. CHIKV, Zika and yellow fever viruses cause other diseases.
nbiology-15-27.tq: Recall the virus behind each disease.
n: AIDS is caused by HIV. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xs: AIDS is caused by **HIV** — option **(4)**.
**CHIKV** causes **chikungunya**; **Zika virus** causes **Zika**; **yellow fever virus** causes **yellow fever**.
xa: AIDS is a **retrovirus-related** disease that affects the **immune system**.
HIV spreads through **blood**, **sexual transmission** and **mother to child**.
**Hepatitis-B** (**HBV**) shares the same blood, sexual and mother-to-child routes.

nbiology-15-44.x: Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum; gonorrhoea by Neisseria gonorrhoeae and diphtheria by Corynebacterium diphtheriae.
n: Diphtheria is caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Gonorrhoea is caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Pertussis is caused by Bordetella pertussis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xa: Diphtheria and pertussis spread by **respiratory transmission**.
Gonorrhoea and syphilis spread by **sexual transmission**.
Pertussis = **whooping cough**.

nbiology-15-49.s: Which of the following effects is associated with tetanus?
nbiology-15-49.x: Tetanus toxin causes jaw spasms (lockjaw). Whooping cough is pertussis, and reproductive-organ effects belong to gonorrhoea and syphilis.
nbiology-15-49.tq: Recall the key symptom of tetanus.
n: Pertussis causes whooping cough. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Gonorrhoea affects the reproductive organs. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Syphilis affects the genitals, rectum and mouth. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
Tetanus can cause jaw involvement. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 24-28]
xs: **Jaw spasms** are associated with **tetanus** — option **(1)**.
Tetanus (**Clostridium tetani**) causes **muscle spasms** with **jaw involvement**.
**Whooping cough** is **pertussis**; **reproductive organs** — **gonorrhoea**; **genitals, rectum and mouth** — **syphilis**.
xa: Tetanus source: **soil**; it can follow a **contaminated wound**.
**Botulism** affects **nerves** and causes **paralysis**.
Tetanus is covered under **UIP**.

nbiology-20-14.x: Aspergillus flavus and A. parasiticus produce aflatoxin; Amanita mushrooms contain α-amanitin.
n: Aspergillus flavus produces aflatoxin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 33-35]
Aspergillus parasiticus produces aflatoxin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 33-35]
Mushroom poisoning is caused by Amanita. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 33-35]
Amanita contains α-amanitin. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #20 · pp 33-35]
xa: **Epidemic dropsy**: **Argemone mexicana oil** (**sanguinarine**).
**Botulism**: **botulinum toxin** of **Clostridium botulinum**.
**Aspergillus** also causes **aspergillosis**.

nchemistry-15-34.s: Which of the following antibiotics is broad-spectrum?
nchemistry-15-34.x: Chloramphenicol is a broad-spectrum antibiotic, acting on many Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Penicillin G is narrow-spectrum, iodoform is an antiseptic and reserpine a tranquillizer.
n: Chloramphenicol is broad-spectrum. [Chemistry · ROCKET SHEET #15 · pp 51-55]
xs: **Chloramphenicol** is the **broad-spectrum** antibiotic — option **(2)**.
Chloramphenicol is used against **typhoid** and other **bacterial infections**.
xa: **Penicillin** (from **Penicillium**) treats **bacterial infections**.
**Tetracycline** is used for **bacterial infections**.
Antibiotics act against **bacteria only**.

n75bda35bc1b.s: The India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative is associated with which combination of institutions and study?
o: ICMR, PHFI and IHME; Global Burden of Disease study
WHO, UNICEF and FAO; World Health Survey
NCDC, FSSAI and NITI Aayog; National Family Health Survey
ICMR, ISRO and DRDO; Census of India
n75bda35bc1b.x: The estimates are produced through the ICMR-PHFI-IHME India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative, which forms part of the Global Burden of Disease study.
n75bda35bc1b.tq: Match the institutional group with the named study rather than with a nearby health survey.
xs: Data come from the **ICMR-PHFI-IHME India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative**, part of the **Global Burden of Disease study** — option **(1)**.
WHO/UNICEF, NCDC/FSSAI/NITI and ISRO/DRDO are not its partners.
xa: **DALY** (**YLL + YLD**) is the burden metric.
**NFHS-5** gives overweight/obesity data.

n69c66af150f.s: The 'dual burden of disease' in India refers to:
o: Rising rates of both infectious and non-communicable diseases
Coexistence of undernutrition and obesity in the same household
High maternal mortality alongside high infant mortality
Simultaneous rise of injuries and mental illness
n69c66af150f.x: Dual burden (PYQ answer) means persistent communicable diseases such as TB, malaria and dengue coexisting with rising NCDs. Undernutrition with obesity is the dual burden of malnutrition; adding injuries gives the triple burden; the other option is not the term.
n69c66af150f.tq: Dual = CDs + NCDs; triple adds injuries.
xs: The **dual burden of disease** = **rising rates of both infectious and non-communicable diseases** (PYQ) — option **(1)** is correct.
Persistent CDs (**TB, malaria, dengue**, vector-borne) coexist with rising **NCDs**.
**Undernutrition + obesity** is the **dual burden of malnutrition**; adding **injuries** makes the **triple burden**.
xa: India's path: a **"linear shift"** from infectious diseases to NCDs.
Health systems must shift from **curative care to screening and prevention**.

n7702866757b.s: In Omran's theory of epidemiological transition, the first stage is the Age of:
n7702866757b.x: Omran's sequence runs from the Age of Pestilence and Famine to Receding Pandemics and then Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases.
xa: Receding Pandemics: improved **sanitation and vaccination**.
India's path: **"linear shift"** to NCDs.
**NCDs** now cause **57%** of deaths.

nab3528e485d.s: Which is the leading cause of death in India?
nab3528e485d.x: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death; NCDs account for 57% of all deaths in India.
xa: World's single biggest killer: **ischaemic heart disease** (WHO).
Data: **ICMR-PHFI-IHME India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative**.
⚠ Older notes give NCD share as **">60%"**.

nb4687ca7e05.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the leading causes of death in India and in the world?
o: Tuberculosis leads in India, while dengue is the single biggest killer in the world.
Cardiovascular diseases lead in India, while ischaemic heart disease is the single biggest killer in the world.
Cancer leads in India, while cardiovascular disease is absent from the global ranking.
Injuries lead in India, while chronic respiratory disease is the single biggest global killer.
nb4687ca7e05.x: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of death in India, while WHO estimates identify ischaemic heart disease as the world's single biggest killer.
nb4687ca7e05.tq: Keep the country-level and global-level comparisons separate before matching the two answers.
xs: **Cardiovascular diseases lead in India**, while **ischaemic heart disease** is the **world's single biggest killer** — option **(2)** is correct.
TB, cancer and injuries are not India's leading cause in the notes; dengue is not the global top killer.
xa: **NCDs** cause **57%** of deaths in India (ES **2025-26**).
"**Big four**" NCDs: **cardiovascular**, **cancers**, **chronic respiratory**, **diabetes**.
India's probability of dying from an NCD **rose** (**2001-2019**).

n4add7b835e4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's health transition?
o: Under-five mortality rate has risen since 1990
Life expectancy rose from 49.7 years in 1973 to 70.3 years in 2023
Maternal mortality ratio has fallen by 86% since 1990
India is undergoing a linear shift from infectious to non-communicable diseases
n4add7b835e4.x: Under-five mortality has fallen, by 78% since 1990, not risen.
xa: **NCDs** cause **57%** of deaths.
**Cardiovascular diseases** lead in India.
Omran's third stage: **Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases**.

n43ed6e9a91b.s: Japanese encephalitis is carried by which mosquito?
n43ed6e9a91b.x: Japanese encephalitis is carried by Culex, while dengue, chikungunya and Zika are carried by Aedes.
xa: **Meningococcal meningitis** spreads by **respiratory droplets**, not mosquitoes.
AP **2025**: dengue **2,686** cases, **5** deaths; AES/JE **146** cases, **2** deaths.
**Malaria is NOT a lifestyle disease**.

n11b91749577.s: To limit NCD risk, FSSAI caps trans fat in fats and oils at:
n11b91749577.x: Excess trans fats, common in bakery products made with hydrogenated fats, raise NCD risk, so FSSAI caps trans fat at 2%.
xa: **FSSAI** caps trans fat at **≤2%** in fats and oils.
Another PYQ: **sedentary lifestyle** + **energy-dense foods** → degenerative diseases (both correct).
**Eat Right India** promotes healthy eating.

n673043878ff.s: Although cancer is not nationally notifiable, how many States have made it a notifiable disease?
n673043878ff.x: Seventeen States have notified cancer, Telangana being the most recent.
xa: Registries cover only **10-16%** of people.
**UNGA** declaration adds **childhood cancer** as a new area.

n28d1be5af60.s: Which one of the following is NOT a lifestyle disease?
n28d1be5af60.x: Malaria is a communicable disease caused by Plasmodium and spread by mosquitoes, so it is not a lifestyle disease (PYQ). Diabetes, hypertension and obesity are lifestyle-related NCDs.
xs: **Malaria** is a communicable, pathogen-caused disease — **NOT a lifestyle disease** (PYQ) — option **(3)** is the answer.
**Diabetes**, **hypertension** and **obesity** are lifestyle NCDs.
xa: ICMR's malaria initiative: **MERA**.
Main NCD risk factors: diet, **physical inactivity**, **tobacco**, **alcohol**.
**Obesity**: excess energy intake + low physical activity.

na6580ab5e55.s: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has capped trans fat in fats and oils at:
na6580ab5e55.x: FSSAI has capped trans fat in fats and oils at 2%.
na6580ab5e55.tq: Use the precise regulatory limit rather than the broader dietary-risk information.
xs: **FSSAI** caps **trans fat** at **≤2%** in fats and oils — option **(2)** is correct.
The cap targets trans fats because excess intake **raises NCD risk** (PYQ).
xa: **Bakery products** are rich in **hydrogenated fats** containing trans fats.
Programmes: **Eat Right India**, **Fit India** (**18 May 2026**).
The **UNGA declaration** seeks stronger regulation of **tobacco, trans fats** and **e-cigarettes**.

nab656dc05eb.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the UN General Assembly declaration on NCDs and mental health?
o: It covers oral health, lung health and childhood cancer
It calls for relaxing the regulation of e-cigarettes
It covers air pollution and lead as determinants
It covers digital harms such as screen time
nab656dc05eb.x: The declaration calls for stronger, not relaxed, regulation of tobacco, trans fats and e-cigarettes.
xa: Targets for **2030**.
Stronger regulation of **tobacco, trans fats and e-cigarettes**.
**SDG 3**: cut premature NCD deaths by **one-third**.

ne0827854765.s: Under NP-NCD (formerly NPCDCS), screening for non-communicable diseases covers everyone above:
ne0827854765.x: NP-NCD screening covers everyone over 30, not 40; it runs NCD clinics at district hospitals and CHCs.
xa: Funding **60:40** (**90:10** for NE and hilly states).
**Ayushman Arogya Mandirs** screen for hypertension, diabetes, cancers.
**SDG 3**: cut premature NCD deaths by **one-third**.

nb08aa8c8bd1.s: Tele-MANAS, available in all 36 States and Union Territories, provides:
o: Online registration of every UIP vaccination
nb08aa8c8bd1.x: Tele-MANAS gives round-the-clock tele-mental-health support across all 36 States and UTs. Vaccination registration is U-WIN; cancer screening and trauma surgery are not its role.
xs: **Tele-MANAS** gives **24x7 tele-mental-health support** in all **36** States/UTs (**12 Jun 2026**) — option **(1)** is correct.
Vaccination registration is **U-WIN**; cancer screening is at **Ayushman Arogya Mandirs**.
xa: **SDG 3** promotes **mental health**.
**UNGA declaration on NCDs and mental health**: first time **digital harms**.
**NP-NCD** runs NCD clinics at district hospitals and CHCs.

nbiology-27-11.s: Excess saturated fat is associated with which of the following effects?
o: Night blindness due to vitamin A deficiency
Increase in blood lipids and cholesterol
nbiology-27-11.x: Excess saturated fat raises blood lipids and cholesterol. Bleeding, night blindness and goitre are deficiency effects, not effects of excess fat.
nbiology-27-11.tq: Discriminate saturated fat effects from trans fat effects.
n: Excess saturated fat increases blood lipids and cholesterol. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 45-46]
xs: Excess **saturated fat** causes an **increase in blood lipids and cholesterol** — option **(4)**.
The other options are deficiency effects, not effects of excess fat.
xa: Excess **trans fat** **increases LDL** — cardiovascular risk.
**FSSAI cap**: trans fat ≤ **2%** in fats and oils.
Saturated fatty acids: **palmitic** (butter, palm oil, meat), **stearic** (meat, cocoa butter).

nbd7d5b6fc20.s: Uddanam, associated with chronic kidney disease of unknown cause (CKDu), is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
nbd7d5b6fc20.x: Uddanam lies in Srikakulam district and is associated with CKDu; the kidney centre for the region is at Palasa.
xa: Interim report: high kidney disease in **Kaviti mandal** (**13 Sep 2026**).
Samples tested for **pesticides/heavy metals** with **CSIR-IICT Hyderabad**.
**AIIMS Mangalagiri** runs CKDu screening camps.

na426921ea22.s: In the Uddanam CKDu investigation, soil, water, blood and urine samples are being tested for:
na426921ea22.x: The samples are tested for pesticides and heavy metals, with CSIR-IICT Hyderabad.
xa: CKDu = **chronic kidney disease of unknown cause**.
High kidney disease in **Kaviti mandal**.
Among those covered: tobacco **38.8%**, alcohol **23.7%**.

nd839f120e5d.s: Which institution conducts CKDu screening camps in the Uddanam region?
nd839f120e5d.x: AIIMS Mangalagiri conducts screening camps for chronic kidney disease of unknown cause in the Uddanam region.
nd839f120e5d.tq: Distinguish the institution conducting field screening from the laboratory involved in testing.
xs: **AIIMS Mangalagiri** runs **CKDu screening camps** — option **(3)** is correct.
**CSIR-IICT Hyderabad** tests samples; it does not run camps.

n32676c5b1fc.s: The increasing importance of non-communicable diseases requires the health system to shift primarily from:

Curative care to screening and prevention
Prevention and screening to curative care

**Ayushman Arogya Mandirs** screen for hypertension, diabetes and cancers.

nd35542b6cb8.s: The Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital associated with the Uddanam kidney disease issue is located at:

n77b046a5617.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of the four major non-communicable disease groups?

n3922c07fc28.s: An epidemic that spreads across countries and continents is called a(n):

n0b96e64fc58.s: A sudden outbreak of a disease in a severe form in a particular region at a particular time is termed:

**Endemic** = constant baseline; **pandemic** = across countries and continents; **epizootic** = among animals.
xa: India example: **Chandipura**, **Gujarat 2024**.
**Plague**: **Surat**, Gujarat **1994**.
**Nipah**: **West Bengal**, **2** cases, Jan **2026**.

n2c375e718a8.s: The first Indian outbreak of avian influenza was reported at Navapur in:

**Chandipura**: Gujarat **2024**.
**Nipah**: West Bengal Jan **2026**.

nbiology-22-6.s: In India, Nipah outbreaks have occurred in:

Nipah had an outbreak in Kerala. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 37-39]
xa: Nipah first identified in **1998**, **Malaysia**.
COVID-19 PHEIC: **30 Jan 2020**.

n07c100c56cb.s: The MERS outbreak is associated with the year:

MERS host: **dromedary camels**; SARS host: **civet cats**.
**H1N1** spike in India in **Aug 2026**.

nabd3f1404b6.s: Which one of the following combinations contains only diseases or outbreaks that were declared PHEICs before or during the COVID-19 period listed?

xa: Other PHEICs: **Ebola 2014 and 2019**; **COVID-19** (**30 Jan 2020**).
**Ebola (Bundibugyo)**: May **2026**.

n8d4cb7ad884.s: The causative organism of the plague outbreak reported in Surat in 1994 was:
n8d4cb7ad884.x: The plague outbreak in Surat, Gujarat, in 1994 was associated with Yersinia pestis and transmission through rat fleas.

**Zika** Kerala **2021**.
**Nipah** Kerala **2018** onwards.

nc5f6c66b7cc.s: SARS-CoV-2 was first identified in which place and month-year?
nc5f6c66b7cc.x: SARS-CoV-2 was first identified in Wuhan in Hubei province of China in December 2019.

xs: **SARS-CoV-2** was first identified in **Wuhan, Hubei, China, December 2019** (UPSC) — option **(2)** is correct.

India's first case: **Kerala, 30 Jan 2020**.
COVID-19 **PHEIC**: **30 Jan 2020**.

nbiology-12-6.s: Anopheles is identified by which characteristic?
nbiology-12-6.x: Anopheles rests with its body at an angle to the surface, head down and tail up, unlike Culex, which rests parallel.

**Aedes aegypti** transmits **dengue**, **yellow fever**, **chikungunya**, **Zika**.

n181ccf1a060.s: WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic on:

xs: WHO declared COVID-19 a **pandemic** on **11 March 2020** — option **(2)** is correct.
**30 Jan 2020** = COVID-19 **PHEIC** (and India's first case); **24 Feb 2022** = Lancet report; **16 Jan 2021** = vaccination start.
xa: **H1N1** pandemic: **June 2009**.
First identified: **Wuhan**, **December 2019**.
**Delta** second wave: **April-May 2021**.

n0e5205f555f.s: The first COVID-19 case in India was reported in Kerala on:

xa: Vaccination began **16 Jan 2021**.

**200 crore** doses by **17 Jul 2022**.

n596804ad747.s: India's COVID-19 vaccination drive, guided by NEGVAC, began on:

**CoWIN** handled booking, tracking and certificates.

n60dc7349a77.s: The COVID-19 vaccine Corbevax was developed by:
n60dc7349a77.x: Corbevax is from Biological E, Hyderabad; Covaxin is from Bharat Biotech with ICMR-NIV and ZyCoV-D from Zydus.

Free at government centres: **Covaxin, Covishield, Corbevax**.

nb34904e0ffb.s: Covishield, made in India by the Serum Institute, used which platform?
nb34904e0ffb.x: Covishield was the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine and used an adenovirus viral-vector platform.
xa: **Sputnik V** (**Gamaleya Institute**, Russia) is also a viral vector.
**iNCOVACC** uses an **adenovirus vector** too (intranasal).
Free at government centres with **Covaxin** and **Corbevax**.

n49df8c9eb5c.s: Which of the following vaccines was described as the world's first intranasal COVID-19 vaccine approved for the primary two-dose schedule and the heterologous booster?
n49df8c9eb5c.x: iNCOVACC, developed by Bharat Biotech, was described as the world's first intranasal COVID-19 vaccine approved for the primary two-dose schedule and the heterologous booster.
n49df8c9eb5c.tq: Use the distinctive route and approval description to identify the vaccine.
xs: **iNCOVACC** (**Bharat Biotech**) is the world's first **intranasal** vaccine for the **primary 2-dose schedule and heterologous booster** (PYQ) — option **(3)**.
**Corbevax** = protein subunit; **ZyCoV-D** = DNA vaccine; **Gemcovac-OM** = mRNA.
xa: It uses an **adenovirus vector**.
Available at **private centres**.
**ZyCoV-D** = first **DNA** vaccine (FIRST/LAST).

n4f4ec11f55a.s: Which vaccine was described as the world's first DNA vaccine approved for use in humans and was administered through a needle-free injector?
n4f4ec11f55a.x: ZyCoV-D, developed by Zydus, was described as the world's first DNA vaccine approved for humans and used a needle-free injector.

xs: **ZyCoV-D** (**Zydus**) is the world's first **DNA vaccine** approved for humans, given by a **needle-free injector** — option **(4)**.
**iNCOVACC** = intranasal; **Covishield** = viral vector; **Covaxin** = inactivated virus.
xa: Available at **private centres**.
**iNCOVACC** = first **intranasal** COVID vaccine.
**mRNA** vaccines: **Moderna**, **Pfizer-BioNTech**, **Gemcovac-OM**.

nbiology-71-1.s: Covaxin is based on which vaccine platform?
nbiology-71-1.x: Covaxin is an inactivated-virus vaccine; Moderna is mRNA, Sputnik V an adenovirus vector and Novavax a recombinant protein nanoparticle.
n: Moderna uses an mRNA vaccine platform. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 133-135]
Sputnik-V uses an adenovirus viral-vector platform. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 133-135]
Covaxin uses an inactivated-virus platform. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 133-135]
Novavax uses a protein-based recombinant nanoparticle platform. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 133-135]
xa: **Pfizer-BioNTech** is also **mRNA**.
**Covishield**: **recombinant viral-vector** (adenovirus).
Free at government centres: **Covaxin**, **Covishield**, **Corbevax**.

nbiology-70-11.x: DPT covers diphtheria, pertussis and tetanus; MMR covers measles, mumps and rubella.

DPT/DTaP is used against tetanus. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]
MMR is used against measles. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]
MMR is used against mumps. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]
MMR is used against rubella. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]

n: The smallpox vaccine is used against smallpox. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]
The polio vaccine is used against poliomyelitis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]
BCG is used against tuberculosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]
The rabies vaccine is used against rabies. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #70 · pp 131-133]

**Louis Pasteur** — **rabies vaccine**.

nbiology-71-16.s: Edward Jenner's smallpox vaccination, the first vaccination, took place in:

n: The first vaccine was the smallpox vaccine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 133-135]
Edward Jenner was the first scientist or doctor to attempt vaccination. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 133-135]
Jenner's vaccination attempt occurred in 1796. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 133-135]
The world's first vaccine was the smallpox vaccine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 133-135]
Jonas Salk is linked to the first successful polio vaccine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 133-135]
xa: Jenner is the **Father of Immunology**.
**Albert Sabin** developed the **oral polio vaccine**.
**Louis Pasteur**: **rabies vaccine** and **germ theory**.

n: Robert Koch was not the father of immunology. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 133-135]
xa: Koch also worked on **disease pathogens**.
Jenner attempted vaccination in **1796** (smallpox).
Pasteur is linked to **germ theory** and **microbiology**.

n0f766408510.s: Under PM CARES for Children, financial support is given to the child at the age of:

n1af1ad874c5.s: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed which of the following combinations of challenges in India?

Only vaccine hesitancy, urban congestion, and shortage of agricultural labour
Defence production gaps, decline in exports, and shortage of school textbooks
Decline in forest cover, coastal erosion, and shortage of irrigation water
n1af1ad874c5.x: The pandemic exposed gaps in health infrastructure and oxygen supply, created a migrant crisis, and revealed dependence on external supply chains.

Nearly all **20+ reagents** for vaccine and diagnostic kits were **imported** in **2020**.
xa: Digital tools born: **CoWIN, U-WIN, ABDM, eSanjeevani**.

UNICEF-ILO: **8.9 million** more child labourers by end-**2022**.

n2a58cf5cce9.s: The Covid Pharma app in Andhra Pradesh was used to track:
o: the number of migrant workers returning to villages
over-the-counter sales of fever and cough medicines

neaffb2f4944.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Ebola?

The Zaire species is regarded as the deadliest
Fruit bats are identified as its reservoir

n2585a99d68a.s: The 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak, declared a PHEIC in May 2026, involved:

**COVID-19** PHEIC: **30 Jan 2020**.

xa: Disease: **COVID-19** = Coronavirus Disease 2019.

n4d66baadab0.s: Which COVID-19 variant was first found in India?

ne492522c153.s: The Lancet report of 24 February 2022 estimated that about how many children in India lost a parent or caregiver to COVID-19?

UNICEF-ILO: **8.9 million** more child labourers by end-**2022**.
Support under PM CARES at **23 years**.

n4d6e0c0c426.s: The 'Dharavi model' ('chasing the virus') of COVID-19 containment belonged to which State?

AP added COVID treatment to **YSR Aarogyasri**.
AP's **Covid Pharma app** tracked OTC fever/cough medicine sales.

nbiology-71-17.s: Who is associated with cellular immunity and phagocytosis?
nbiology-71-17.x: Élie Metchnikoff discovered phagocytosis and founded the idea of cellular immunity. Koch worked on TB and Pasteur on rabies.

Elie Metchnikoff was associated with phagocytosis. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 133-135]
Elie Metchnikoff was associated with immunology. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #71 · pp 133-135]
xs: **Elie Metchnikoff** is associated with **cellular immunity** and **phagocytosis** — option **(2)**.
**Robert Koch** — **tuberculosis**, **bacteriology**; **Louis Pasteur** — **rabies vaccine**; **Jonas Salk** — **polio vaccine**.
xa: **Karl Landsteiner** — **blood groups**.
**Edward Jenner** — **Father of Immunology**.

nf36b6a55310.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the first contact point in the primary healthcare tier?

n236aa0432e8.s: In Indian cities, which sector dominates secondary, tertiary and quaternary care?

n5d2421cc005.s: Which of the following health committees was the earliest?

na061882e603.s: The latest revision of the Indian Public Health Standards is:

n55d9b4077f5.s: Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (earlier Health and Wellness Centres) were launched in:
