AP converted **10,032 sub-centres, 1,144 PHCs and 560 UPHCs** into AAMs (APSES 2024-25).

n6e2ff4bb09a.s: Under the Comprehensive Primary Health Care package at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, NCD screening covers hypertension, diabetes and which cancers?
n6e2ff4bb09a.x: The CPHC package screens for hypertension, diabetes and the three common cancers: oral, breast and cervical. Lung, liver, stomach, blood, bone, skin, prostate, colon and pancreatic cancers are not part of the stated population-based screening.
n6e2ff4bb09a.tq: AAM cancer screening = oral, breast, cervical (the 'common three').
xs: NCD screening at AAMs covers **oral, breast and cervical cancer** besides hypertension and diabetes — option **(1)**.
The other cancer sets are not part of the CPHC NCD screening.
xa: CPHC also covers **mental health**, **ENT, eye, oral health**, **geriatric and palliative care**, **Yoga** and wellness.
**ONCONET** links **108** peripheral and **27** regional cancer centres.
AAM-PHCs: **172 drugs**, **63 diagnostics**.

ne8df6062a3b.s: Which of the following correctly describes human-resource challenges in rural healthcare?
o: The nurse ratio exceeds global norms and rural CHCs have no vacancies.
The nurse ratio is below global norms and specialist posts at rural CHCs have high vacancies.
Only urban CHCs face specialist vacancies.
Rural CHCs have surplus specialists and no nursing shortage.
ne8df6062a3b.x: The nurse ratio is below global norms, while specialist posts at rural CHCs have high vacancies.
ne8df6062a3b.tq: Identify the option that preserves both linked shortages.
xs: The **nurse ratio is below global norms** and **specialist posts at rural CHCs have high vacancies** — option **(2)**.
So the options claiming surplus specialists, no vacancies or urban-only vacancies are wrong.
xa: Doctor-population ratio about **1:834** vs **WHO norm 1:1000**, but doctors **cluster in cities**.
**Community workers** carry the heaviest workload.
"Urban concentration of doctors" is a listed criticism of India's health system.

n06edc437390.s: eSanjeevani was developed by which organisation?
o: Indian Council of Medical Research, New Delhi
n06edc437390.x: eSanjeevani was built by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), Mohali.
n06edc437390.tq: Identify the correct technology agency rather than the health-sector organisation.
xs: **eSanjeevani** was developed by **C-DAC, Mohali** — option **(4)**.
ISRO, ICMR and NIC are not its developers.
xa: **eSanjeevani AAM**: provider-to-provider, **hub-and-spoke**; **eSanjeevani OPD**: patient-to-provider from home.
Network: **1,35,915 AAM spokes** + **17,893 hubs**.
Over **1.75 lakh AAMs** now linked (12 Jun 2026).

n589c4bba629.s: Which of the following correctly describes eSanjeevani AAM?
o: Teleconsultation exclusively for armed forces personnel
Patient-to-provider consultation from the patient's home
Mental-health counselling through a national helpline
Provider-to-provider consultation through a hub-and-spoke model
n589c4bba629.x: eSanjeevani AAM provides provider-to-provider teleconsultation through a hub-and-spoke model.
n589c4bba629.tq: Separate the two eSanjeevani variants by user relationship and service setting.
xs: **eSanjeevani AAM** is **provider-to-provider** teleconsultation through a **hub-and-spoke model** — option **(4)**.
**Patient-to-provider from home** is **eSanjeevani OPD**; armed-forces teleconsultation is **SeHAT**.
xa: Developer: **C-DAC (Mohali)**.
**1,35,915 AAM spokes** and **17,893 hubs**.
**ONCONET** links **108** peripheral and **27** regional cancer centres.

n87d4aaedeef.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's doctor-population ratio?
o: Real availability is higher than the ratio suggests because doctors are spread evenly in rural areas
It is compared with the WHO norm of 1:1000
The ratio for NMC-registered allopathic doctors is about 1:834
Doctors tend to cluster in cities
n87d4aaedeef.x: Real availability is lower than the ratio suggests, because doctors cluster in cities.
xa: **Nurse** ratio is below global norms; **specialist vacancies** are high at rural CHCs.
**Community workers** carry the heaviest workload.
About **70%** of health infrastructure is urban, serving only **30%** of the population.

n929ce80120d.s: According to NFHS-3, the private sector was the main source of care for what proportion of urban households?
n929ce80120d.x: NFHS-3 reported that the private sector was the main source of care for 70% of urban households.
n929ce80120d.tq: Recall the survey-linked percentage without confusing it with other health-sector shares.
xs: **NFHS-3**: the private sector was the main source of care for **70% of urban households** — option **(3)** (PYQ).
In cities the private sector dominates **secondary, tertiary and quaternary** care.
xa: Private sector today: **over 60% of inpatient** and **about 70% of outpatient** care.
⚠ Don't confuse with the urban skew: **70%** of infrastructure in urban areas holding **30%** of population.
Average hospitalisation: **Rs 50,508** private vs **Rs 6,631** government.

n5ca51f8589b.s: Approximately what proportion of health infrastructure is located in urban areas, which contain what proportion of the population?
n5ca51f8589b.x: About 70% of health infrastructure is in urban areas, which contain only 30% of the population.
n5ca51f8589b.tq: Identify the reversed infrastructure-population distribution trap.
xs: About **70%** of health infrastructure is in **urban areas**, which hold only **30%** of the population — option **(4)**.
Option (1) reverses the figures.
xa: **Urban concentration of doctors** is a listed criticism; the doctor ratio is **1:834** vs WHO **1:1000**.
⚠ **NFHS-3**: private sector = main source for **70% of urban households** — a different 70%.
**Missing middle**: over **40 crore** people without cover.

n9f5e1a979e6.s: As of December 2021, what was the total number of Primary Health Centres (PHCs) in India?
n9f5e1a979e6.x: The stated December 2021 figure is 23,391 PHCs.
n9f5e1a979e6.tq: Distinguish the dated count from the historical and alternative counts.
xs: India had **23,391 PHCs** as of **Dec 2021** — option **(3)** (PYQ key).
**725** was the count in **1950-51**; **30,045** is a **2019** figure that includes urban PHCs.
**11,086** is the number of **Sub Centres in AP**.
xa: PHC norm: **30,000** (plain) / **20,000** (hilly-tribal).
Urban PHCs cover **25,000-30,000** people within **2-3 km**.
AP has **1,293 rural** and **559 urban PHCs**.
n9f5e1a979e6.fixed: 'According to the stated figures' is odd wording; y1decdc1c7dd

nacca8487e21.s: The Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY), for AIIMS-like institutions, was launched in:
nacca8487e21.x: PMSSY was launched in 2003 to establish AIIMS-like institutions and upgrade government medical colleges.
xa: AP's AIIMS is **AIIMS Mangalagiri** — a telemedicine anchor with over **2,500 OPD** patients a day.
**PM-JAY**: **Rs 5 lakh per family per year** to **12 crore families**.
Dental colleges in **2024-25**: **319 BDS** and **281 MDS**.

nad94a1313f5.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the AIIMS serving Andhra Pradesh?
nad94a1313f5.x: AIIMS Mangalagiri is the AIIMS institution associated with Andhra Pradesh.
nad94a1313f5.tq: Discriminate among nearby place-based institutional names.
xs: AP's AIIMS is **AIIMS Mangalagiri** — option **(4)**.
It is AP's **telemedicine anchor**, seeing **over 2,500 OPD** patients a day.
xa: AIIMS-like institutions come under **PMSSY (2003)**.
Other AP specialty centre: **Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital, Palasa, Srikakulam**.
Greyfield super-specialty blocks: **Anantapur, Nellore and Eluru** (Feb 2026).

n097a735d74f.s: Under PM-JAY, the annual health cover provided per family is:
n097a735d74f.x: PM-JAY provides health cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year.
n097a735d74f.tq: Recall the scheme amount by separating it from other plausible insurance figures.
xs: **PM-JAY** gives **Rs 5 lakh per family per year** — option **(4)**.
It covers **12 crore families**.
xa: Criticism: a **"missing middle"** of over **40 crore** people without cover.
Average hospitalisation: **Rs 50,508** private vs **Rs 6,631** government.
AP's **Sanjeevani** digital health programme issues **ABHA IDs**.

nef5c31fc0f2.s: Which institution functions as the telemedicine anchor in Andhra Pradesh and has over 2,500 out-patients a day?
nef5c31fc0f2.x: AIIMS Mangalagiri is the telemedicine anchor and has over 2,500 OPD patients a day.
nef5c31fc0f2.tq: Match the institution with its distinctive service role and patient figure.
xs: **AIIMS Mangalagiri** is AP's **telemedicine anchor**, with over **2,500 OPD** patients a day — option **(4)**.
**Palasa** hosts the Kidney Research Centre; **Eluru** and **Nellore** are greyfield block sites.
xa: AIIMS-like institutions are built under **PMSSY (2003)**.
**eSanjeevani** (by **C-DAC Mohali**) is the national telemedicine platform.
AP's **Sanjeevani** programme integrates telemedicine with 104 and 108.

nd3204f062df.s: The Bhore Committee was appointed primarily to:
o: Survey the state of public health
nd3204f062df.x: The Bhore Committee was appointed to survey the state of public health.
nd3204f062df.tq: Match a committee with its stated mandate, not merely its broad sector.
xs: The **Bhore Committee** (Health Survey and Development) was appointed **"to survey the state of public health"** — option **(2)**.
**Multipurpose health workers** were the **Kartar Singh Committee's** (**1973**) idea; **village health guides** came from **Shrivastava** (**1975**).
**Consolidating existing PHCs** before expansion was the **Mudaliar Committee's** (**1959-62**) advice.
xa: The Bhore Committee worked in **1943-46**.
It recommended **integrated preventive and curative care** and a **three-tier PHC-based system**.
Kartar Singh also set the norm of **one PHC per 50,000** people.

n219e028754e.s: The Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital mentioned in relation to Andhra Pradesh is located at:
n219e028754e.x: The Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital is located at Palasa in Srikakulam.
xs: The **Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital** is at **Palasa, Srikakulam** — option **(3)** (PYQ).
**Anantapur** and **Eluru** are greyfield super-specialty block sites; **Mangalagiri** has AIIMS.
xa: **AIIMS Mangalagiri** is the telemedicine anchor with over **2,500 OPD** patients a day.
Greyfield blocks: **Anantapur, Nellore and Eluru** (Feb 2026).
AP has **9 District Hospitals** and **54 Area Hospitals**.

n5ff2bc8b998.s: Which of the following is identified as a major criticism or concern in India's healthcare system?
o: Excessive coverage of the missing middle and equal distribution of doctors
Low out-of-pocket expenditure and rural concentration of doctors
Absence of any public healthcare infrastructure and universal insurance coverage
High out-of-pocket expenditure, a missing middle of over 40 crore people without cover, and urban concentration of doctors
n5ff2bc8b998.x: The stated concerns are high out-of-pocket expenditure, more than 40 crore people forming a 'missing middle' without cover, and the urban concentration of doctors.
n5ff2bc8b998.tq: Reject options that reverse the direction of the stated healthcare problems.
xs: The criticisms are **high out-of-pocket expenditure**, a **missing middle** of over **40 crore** people without cover and **urban concentration of doctors** — option **(4)**.
The other options invert these (low OOPE, rural concentration, no public infrastructure).
xa: Older notes put **OOPE** at about **47-48%**.
**PM-JAY** covers **Rs 5 lakh per family per year** for **12 crore families**.
About **70%** of health infrastructure is urban, serving **30%** of the population.

nf1cfba29529.s: According to the SRS 2023 figure cited for the latest estimates, India’s IMR was
nf1cfba29529.x: The IMR was 25 according to SRS 2023, as cited in the Economic Survey 2025-26. The figures 28 and 35.2 refer to older or different sources.
nf1cfba29529.tq: Match the latest year with the correct numerical value rather than using a stale estimate.
xs: India's IMR was **25** as per **SRS 2023** (ES 2025-26) — option **(2)**.
**28** is the stale **SRS 2020** figure; **35.2** is the **NFHS-5** survey value; **24** is **AP's** IMR (SRS 2020).
xa: IMR = infant deaths under 1 year per **1,000 live births**.
**Kerala** has the lowest IMR thanks to adequate basic health and education facilities.

nd98025cb492.s: As per SRS 2018-20, India's Maternal Mortality Ratio (maternal deaths per 1,00,000 live births) was:
nd98025cb492.x: India's MMR was 97 per 1,00,000 live births in SRS 2018-20. 25 is India's IMR (SRS 2023), which is per 1,000 live births; 45 is Andhra Pradesh's MMR; 130 is not the SRS 2018-20 figure.
nd98025cb492.tq: MMR 97 per lakh; IMR 25 per thousand: watch the base.
xs: India's **MMR** was **97** per 1,00,000 live births (**SRS 2018-20**) — option **(1)**.
**25** is India's **IMR** (SRS 2023, per 1,000 live births); **45** is **AP's MMR**.
xa: MMR is the only indicator here on a **1,00,000 live births** base.
**Telangana (2026)**: **MMR 43**.
AP beats national averages on IMR (**24**), MMR (**45**) and TFR (**1.5**) (APSES 2024-25).

n924d8f85466.s: India's Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) in 2016 was:
xa: ⚠ The older **28 (SRS 2020)** figure is now stale.
Exam angle: year → IMR value matching, and per-1,000 vs per-1,00,000 base.

n3e1621b147d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct according to the SRS abridged life tables for 2016–20?
o: Andhra Pradesh's male life expectancy was 69.1 years
India's male life expectancy was 68.6 years
India's female life expectancy was 71.4 years
Andhra Pradesh's female life expectancy was lower than India's
n3e1621b147d.x: AP's female life expectancy was 72.2 years, higher than India's 71.4 years.
xa: Women live **~3 years** longer than men.
Life expectancy rose from **49.7 years (1973)** to **70.3 years (2023)**.
At Independence it was about **32 years**.

nf35470e3daa.s: Which State is credited with having the lowest IMR owing to adequate basic health and education facilities?
nf35470e3daa.x: Kerala has the lowest IMR, attributed to adequate basic health and education facilities.
nf35470e3daa.tq: Use the state-specific association rather than confusing it with AP or Telangana figures.
xs: **Kerala** has the lowest IMR owing to **adequate basic health and education facilities** — option **(2)** (APPSC 2025 PYQ).
**Madhya Pradesh** is noted for high child wasting and underweight in NFHS-6.
xa: **Telangana (2026)**: **MMR 43, IMR 18, TFR 1.5**; **99.9%** institutional deliveries.
India's latest IMR: **25** (SRS 2023).

n1f2abdefdab.s: At the time of Independence, life expectancy in India was approximately
n1f2abdefdab.x: Life expectancy at Independence was approximately 32 years.
n1f2abdefdab.tq: Identify the historical baseline rather than a later SRS life-table value.
xs: Life expectancy at Independence was about **32 years** — option **(1)** (APPSC 2023 PYQ).
**49.7** was the **1973** level; **70.3** the **2023** level; **68.3** the older SRS 2011-15 figure.
xa: SRS 2016-20: India **68.6** (males), **71.4** (females).
Women live **~3 years** longer.

nae8e0f3590e.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, India's life expectancy rose from 49.7 years in 1973 to how many years in 2023?
nae8e0f3590e.x: Life expectancy rose to 70.3 years in 2023; 68.3 is the older SRS 2011-15 figure and 72.2 is AP's female life expectancy for 2016-20.
xa: SRS 2016-20: India males **68.6**, females **71.4**.
AP: males **69.1**, females **72.2**.
Women live **~3 years** longer.

nd2431dd7b23.x: NFHS-1 was in 1992-93, NFHS-2 in 1998-99, NFHS-3 in 2005-06 and NFHS-4 in 2015-16.
xa: **NFHS-5**: **2019-21**; **NFHS-6**: scheduled **2023-24**, results released **2026**.
Conducted by **MoHFW**; nodal agency **IIPS, Mumbai**.
Exam angle: round → year matching.

n77aa33aeea1.s: NFHS is conducted under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, with which institution serving as the nodal agency?
o: Indian Council of Medical Research, Hyderabad
International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai
n77aa33aeea1.x: NFHS is conducted under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and the International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS), Mumbai, is the nodal agency.
n77aa33aeea1.tq: Apply the institutional-authority trap by distinguishing the conducting ministry from the nodal agency.
xs: The nodal agency for NFHS is the **International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS), Mumbai** — option **(2)**.
The survey is conducted under the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)**.
xa: Rounds: NFHS-1 **1992-93** … NFHS-5 **2019-21**; NFHS-6 results released **2026**.
Coverage: maternal and child health, mortality, nutrition, immunisation, fertility, family planning, women's empowerment, sanitation and drinking water.
⚠ NFHS gives **no single overall "malnutrition %"**.

n21da8445614.s: According to NFHS-6, which State recorded high child wasting and underweight?
n21da8445614.x: Madhya Pradesh showed high child wasting and underweight; Meghalaya showed a decline in stunting.
xa: NFHS-6: stunting fell to **29.3%**; underweight stuck at **31.8%**.
NFHS-6 + Vellore cohort study: thinness and overweight rise sharply between **ages 7 and 9**.
Rising **double burden** is a 2026 concern.

n07a794d72b3.s: Under WHO's classification, overweight, obesity and diet-related NCDs are counted as forms of:
n07a794d72b3.x: WHO's malnutrition in all its forms covers undernutrition, inadequate vitamins and minerals, and overweight, obesity and diet-related NCDs.
xa: **Double burden** = undernutrition + overnutrition together.
**Triple burden (SOFI 2025)** = undernutrition + micronutrient deficiency/anaemia + overweight.
NFHS reports stunting, wasting and underweight **separately**.

n2e6fa9eb130.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about malnutrition burdens?
o: SOFI 2025's 'triple burden' is wasting, stunting and underweight
Wasting, stunting and underweight are all forms of undernutrition
The 'double burden' is undernutrition and overnutrition occurring together
A Vellore cohort study found thinness and overweight rising sharply between ages 7 and 9
n2e6fa9eb130.x: SOFI 2025's triple burden is undernutrition, micronutrient deficiency/anaemia and overweight.
xa: WHO: malnutrition in all its forms includes **undernutrition** (wasting, stunting, underweight).
SOFI 2025: India's wasting rate **18.7%** (**21 million** children) — world's highest.
⚠ NFHS gives **no single overall "malnutrition %"**.

nb16ae9d30b5.s: Wasting in children refers to low:
nb16ae9d30b5.x: Wasting is low weight-for-height; stunting is low height-for-age and underweight low weight-for-age.
xa: Wasting (NFHS-5): **19.3%**; severe wasting **5.2%** in NFHS-6.
Underweight barely moved: **32.1%** → **31.8%**.

n8515765ca85.s: Which of the following correctly presents the NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 figures for underweight children?
n8515765ca85.x: Underweight declined from 32.1% in NFHS-5 to 31.8% in NFHS-6. The 35.8% figure belongs to NFHS-4.
n8515765ca85.tq: Track both survey round and indicator before choosing the pair.
xs: Underweight: **32.1%** (NFHS-5) and **31.8%** (NFHS-6) — option **(2)**.
**35.5% / 29.3%** are **stunting**; **35.8%** is the **NFHS-4** underweight figure; **19.3%** is wasting and **5.2%** severe wasting.
xa: Underweight **barely moved** in NFHS-6.
NFHS-5: underweight highest among **STs (44.1%)** and **SCs (39.1%)**, higher in rural areas.
Underweight = low **weight-for-age**.

n9d8b18c004d.s: According to NFHS-5, anaemia affected approximately what proportions of children aged 6–59 months and women aged 15–49 years respectively?
n9d8b18c004d.x: NFHS-5 reported anaemia among 67.1% of children aged 6–59 months and 57.0% of women aged 15–49 years.
n9d8b18c004d.tq: Keep the age group and percentage in the same order as asked.
xs: NFHS-5 anaemia: **children 6-59 months 67.1%**, **women 15-49 57.0%** — option **(4)**.
**41%** is the share of women with **10+ years of schooling**, not anaemia.
xa: **Anemia Mukt Bharat** (2018) uses a **6x6x6** strategy.
Fortified rice carries **iron, folic acid, vitamin B12**.
AP's **Anna Amrutha Hastam** gives **iron and folic acid tablets** to pregnant and lactating women.

n761469b676b.s: Underweight prevalence was highest among which of the following social groups according to NFHS-5?
o: Other Backward Classes, followed by Scheduled Tribes
Scheduled Tribes, followed by Scheduled Castes
Scheduled Castes, followed by Scheduled Tribes
Urban households, followed by rural households
n761469b676b.x: Underweight was highest among Scheduled Tribes at 44.1%, followed by Scheduled Castes at 39.1%. It was also higher in rural areas.
n761469b676b.tq: Rank the groups using the reported percentages rather than merely identifying both groups.
xs: Underweight was highest among **Scheduled Tribes (44.1%)**, followed by **Scheduled Castes (39.1%)** — option **(2)** (NFHS-5).
It was **higher in rural** areas, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: National underweight: **32.1%** (NFHS-5) → **31.8%** (NFHS-6).
NFHS-4 underweight: **35.8%**.
Underweight = low **weight-for-age**.

n4042c6b4662.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the six services provided through Anganwadi Services?
n4042c6b4662.x: The six services include supplementary nutrition, pre-school education, nutrition and health education, immunisation, health check-up and referral services. Old-age pension distribution is not one of them.
n4042c6b4662.tq: Locate the option that does not belong to the programme’s fixed list of six services.
xs: **Old-age pension distribution** is not an Anganwadi service — option **(4)**.
The **six services**: **supplementary nutrition**, **pre-school education**, nutrition & health education, immunisation, health check-up and **referral**.
xa: Beneficiaries: children **6 months-6 years**, pregnant and lactating women.
**2.9 lakh** AWCs co-located with schools (3 Sep 2025).
**POSHAN Abhiyaan** converges ICDS with NHM and Swachh Bharat.

nbiology-27-7.s: Pellagra is caused by deficiency of:
nbiology-27-7.x: Lack of B3 causes pellagra; vitamin K deficiency causes bleeding, iron deficiency anaemia and iodine deficiency goitre.
n: Vitamin B3 deficiency causes Pellagra. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 45-46]
Vitamin K deficiency causes bleeding. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 45-46]
Iron deficiency causes anaemia. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 45-46]
Iodine deficiency causes goitre. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 45-46]
xa: **Vitamin B1** — **beri-beri**; **vitamin B12** — **pernicious anaemia**.
**Vitamin C** — **scurvy**; **vitamin D** — **rickets**.
**Protein** — **kwashiorkor**; **energy and protein** — **marasmus**.

n3e618f6a50f.s: Which of the following correctly describes the beneficiaries of Anganwadi Services under ICDS?
o: Only children below six months of age
Only elderly persons and persons with disabilities
Children aged six months to six years, and pregnant and lactating women
Only school-going children aged six to fourteen years
n3e618f6a50f.x: Anganwadi Services cover children from six months to six years and pregnant and lactating women.
n3e618f6a50f.tq: Distinguish the programme’s target groups from beneficiaries of school or social-security schemes.
xs: **Anganwadi Services (ICDS)** cover **children 6 months-6 years** and **pregnant and lactating women** — option **(3)**.
School meals for older children come under **PM POSHAN**.
xa: ICDS provides **six services**: supplementary nutrition, pre-school education, nutrition & health education, immunisation, health check-up, referral.
**2.9 lakh** AWCs are co-located with schools (guidelines **3 Sep 2025**).
AP's **Anna Amrutha Hastam** works through Anganwadis.

n653cea5a7a8.s: The 6x6x6 strategy is associated with which programme?
o: Rice fortification under the Public Distribution System
n653cea5a7a8.x: Anemia Mukt Bharat uses a 6x6x6 strategy consisting of six interventions, six target groups and six institutional mechanisms.
n653cea5a7a8.tq: Discriminate between similarly themed nutrition programmes by their signature strategy.
xs: The **6x6x6** strategy belongs to **Anemia Mukt Bharat** — option **(3)**.
It means **6 interventions, 6 target groups, 6 institutional mechanisms**.
xa: Anemia Mukt Bharat was launched in **2018**.
NFHS-5 anaemia: children **67.1%**, women **57.0%**.
Rice fortification with **iron, folic acid, vitamin B12** is a separate measure.

nced58802ace.s: Fortified rice supplied through the Public Distribution System, ICDS and PM POSHAN is fortified with:
o: Calcium, vitamin C and vitamin D
Iron, folic acid and vitamin B12
Iodine, zinc and vitamin A only
nced58802ace.x: The specified fortified rice contains iron, folic acid and vitamin B12 and is supplied through the PDS, ICDS and PM POSHAN.
nced58802ace.tq: Match the intervention with its exact micronutrient combination and delivery channels.
xs: Fortified rice carries **iron, folic acid and vitamin B12** — option **(3)**.
It is supplied through **PDS, ICDS and PM POSHAN**.
xa: **Anemia Mukt Bharat** (2018) follows the **6x6x6** strategy.
AP's **Anna Amrutha Hastam** adds **iron and folic acid tablets** to meals.
NFHS-5 anaemia among children 6-59 months: **67.1%**.

n44df239d8c9.s: Which Andhra Pradesh scheme provides a nutritious meal along with iron and folic acid tablets to pregnant and lactating women through Anganwadis?
n44df239d8c9.x: Anna Amrutha Hastam provides a nutritious meal and iron-folic acid tablets to pregnant and lactating women through Anganwadis.
n44df239d8c9.tq: Match the scheme name with its specific beneficiary and service.
xs: **Anna Amrutha Hastam** (AP) gives a **nutritious meal** plus **iron and folic acid tablets** to **pregnant and lactating women** via **Anganwadis** — option **(3)** (APPSC 2019 PYQ).
**PMSMA, LaQshya, JSSK** are other maternal services listed in APSES 2024-25.
xa: Its aim: cut **infant and maternal mortality**.
**JSY** had **1,76,966** beneficiaries (Apr-Dec 2024).
Other services: **PMMVY, SUMAN, MCP cards**.

n8a01b2fe99c.s: Food insecurity and poverty may contribute to both undernutrition and overnutrition because they can lead to consumption of
o: Only locally produced fruits and vegetables
n8a01b2fe99c.x: Food insecurity and poverty can produce undernutrition while also encouraging consumption of inexpensive energy-dense, nutrient-poor foods that contribute to overnutrition.
n8a01b2fe99c.tq: Apply the cause-effect relationship to a realistic dietary situation.
xs: Food insecurity and poverty lead to **energy-dense but nutrient-poor foods** — option **(2)**.
This causes **both under- and overnutrition**, plus **anaemia** and **cognitive delays**.
xa: The main driver of malnutrition: **poor dietary habits and food insecurity** (APPSC 2025 key).
**Poor maternal nutrition** impairs the child's **brain development**.
**Double burden** = undernutrition + overnutrition.

n334244e0f01.s: Which one of the following is regarded as the main driver of malnutrition in India?
o: Poor dietary habits and food insecurity
n334244e0f01.x: Poor dietary habits and food insecurity are the main driver of malnutrition (APPSC 2025 key). Fortified rice is a remedy, not a cause; women's schooling improves child nutrition; overuse of supplements is not cited as a driver.
n334244e0f01.tq: Malnutrition driver = poor diet + food insecurity.
xs: **Poor dietary habits and food insecurity** are the main driver — option **(1)** (APPSC 2025 key).
**Fortified rice** is a remedy (iron, folic acid, vitamin B12); **women's schooling** is a protective factor.
xa: Food insecurity & poverty → **energy-dense, nutrient-poor food**, anaemia, cognitive delays.
**Poor maternal nutrition** impairs the child's brain development.
Child marriage: **23.3%** married before 18.

n6ad66b09183.s: India's National Health Accounts, prepared by NHATS under NHSRC, use which framework?
n6ad66b09183.x: The NHA use the System of Health Accounts 2011 (with NHA Guidelines 2016); the first NHA was for 2013-14.
xa: The latest is the **10th edition** for **2022-23** (May 2026).
OOPE share of THE: **64.2%** → **43.4%**.

nbbd10d8a873.s: The government share of India's Total Health Expenditure rose from 28.6% in 2013–14 to:
nbbd10d8a873.x: The government share rose to 43.7%; 39.4% is the OOPE share during COVID-19.
xa: OOPE share fell from **64.2%** to **43.4%**.
**Social security expenditure** share rose from **6%** to **9.9%**.

nd9bc64cfb6c.s: During COVID-19, household out-of-pocket expenditure fell to what share of Total Health Expenditure?
nd9bc64cfb6c.x: OOPE fell to 39.4% of THE during COVID-19, when government health expenditure peaked; 28.6% was the government share in 2013–14.
xa: NHA is prepared by **NHATS under NHSRC**, first for **2013-14**.

nddf87f085a6.s: Which of the following correctly represents the trend in OOPE as a share of Total Health Expenditure between 2013–14 and 2022–23?
nddf87f085a6.x: OOPE declined from 64.2% of Total Health Expenditure in 2013–14 to 43.4% in 2022–23, although it remained about half of current health expenditure.
nddf87f085a6.tq: Reject the reversed trend and distinguish total health expenditure from current health expenditure.
xs: Option (4) reverses it; **28.6%** is the 2013-14 government share.
xa: OOPE is still about **50% of current health expenditure** (NHA 2022-23).
⚠ During COVID OOPE **fell** to **39.4%** of THE.

nd604ce82452.s: Government Health Expenditure reached what percentage of GDP during the COVID peak in 2021–22?
nd604ce82452.x: GHE reached 1.84% of GDP during the COVID peak in 2021–22.
nd604ce82452.tq: Distinguish the exceptional COVID-year peak from the regular annual figures.
xs: GHE reached **1.84% of GDP** in **2021-22**, the **COVID peak** — option **(3)**.
xa: ⚠ OOPE **fell**, not rose, during COVID — to **39.4%** of THE.
Centre + States spent about **1.3% of GDP** in **2019-20** (Economic Survey 2021-22).

n14b6d1a9f77.s: The 15th Finance Commission recommended health grants of approximately what amount through local governments for the period 2021–2026?
n14b6d1a9f77.x: The 15th Finance Commission recommended health grants amounting to ₹70,051 crore through local governments for 2021–2026.
n14b6d1a9f77.tq: Use the exact figure and period to eliminate nearby numerical distractors.
xs: The **15th Finance Commission** gave **₹70,051 crore** of health grants through **local governments** for **2021-26** — option **(3)**.
The grants go to local bodies for primary-level and block-level health infrastructure.
xa: Components: **diagnostic infrastructure** for sub-centres/PHCs and **block public health units**.
Also **urban health and wellness centres**.
And **buildings for building-less SCs/PHCs/CHCs**.

n761ad9dd9a3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA)?
o: It fixes ceiling prices of scheduled drugs
Scheduled drugs are those in the National List of Essential Medicines
Its price control operates under the Drugs Price Control Order, 2013
n761ad9dd9a3.x: NPPA was established in 1997; 2013 is the year of the Drugs Price Control Order under which it fixes ceiling prices.
xa: **Free Drugs Service Initiative (NHM)**: free generic medicines; **DVDMS** handles procurement/inventory.
**Clinical Establishments Act 2010** adopted in only ~**11 states** and **6 UTs**.
Medicines are part of the **over 50%** of OOPE not covered by insurance.

n79b4b8ba778.s: The Clinical Establishments Act, adopted by only about 11 States and 6 UTs, was enacted in:
n79b4b8ba778.x: The Act dates to 2010; 2013 is the Drugs Price Control Order and 2017 the National Health Policy.
xa: **NPPA** was set up in **1997**.
Hospitalisation OOP rose sharply, especially in **private hospitals** (NSS 80th round).
Private childbirth costs **₹37,630** vs **₹2,299** public.

n2779c904db6.s: Which of the following components account for over 50% of OOPE because they are generally not covered by insurance?
o: Only inpatient surgery and intensive care
Ambulance services and health education alone
n2779c904db6.x: Outpatient care, diagnostics and medicines account for over half of OOPE because insurance commonly does not cover them.
n2779c904db6.tq: Apply the coverage gap to identify the major sources of household spending.
xs: **Outpatient care, diagnostics and medicines** are **over 50%** of OOPE — option **(4)**.
They are the uncovered costs; inpatient care is what insurance mainly covers.
xa: Chronic NCDs keep households paying: **diabetes 11.4%**, **hypertension 35.5%** of adults.
Private outpatient medicine bills are about **6 times** those at **Jan Aushadhi**.
Fix suggested: more spending on **primary care** + **OPD cover**.

n841e89f47b8.s: The term “missing middle” in the context of health financing refers to:
o: More than 40 crore Indians lacking financial protection
People covered simultaneously by both public and private insurance
The middle-income group receiving free medicines at public facilities
Households whose insurance claims are pending for less than one month
n841e89f47b8.x: The “missing middle” refers to more than 40 crore Indians who lack adequate financial protection; NITI Aayog first flagged the term.
n841e89f47b8.tq: Match the distinctive policy term with its precise population description.
xs: The **"missing middle"** = **40 crore+** Indians lacking **financial protection** — option **(1)**.
**NITI Aayog** first flagged the term; the parliamentary panel used it on **4 Sep 2026**.
xa: NSS 80th round: insurance covers **47.4%** rural and **44.3%** urban households.
Childbirth OOP: **₹37,630** private vs **₹2,299** public (over **16x**).
Government-financed insurance rose **2.5-fold** (**2017-18** to **2025**).

n5cac843e5b4.s: Which of the following is regarded as a criticism of insurance-led health financing models?
o: They provide universal outpatient coverage in all circumstances.
They increase coverage without necessarily increasing the availability of care.
They reduce coverage while automatically increasing the quality of care.
They eliminate the need for primary healthcare expenditure.
n5cac843e5b4.x: A stated criticism is that insurance-led models may expand coverage without a corresponding increase in actual care. Greater spending on primary care and outpatient care is suggested as part of the corrective approach.
n5cac843e5b4.tq: Distinguish nominal financial coverage from actual access to healthcare.
xs: Insurance-led models **increase coverage without increasing care** — option **(2)**.
The suggested fix is more spending on **primary care** plus **OPD cover**.
xa: Outpatient care, diagnostics and medicines = **over 50%** of OOPE, mostly uncovered.
Government-financed insurance grew **2.5-fold** but OOPE still ~**50%** of current health expenditure.
**Missing middle**: **40 crore+** lack protection.

n9bfa35f6688.s: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva, formerly known as YSR Aarogyasri, is primarily intended to provide which of the following?
o: Subsidised insurance exclusively for private-sector employees
Free crop insurance to small farmers
Pension support to retired government employees
Cashless health assurance to economically vulnerable families in Andhra Pradesh
n9bfa35f6688.x: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva, earlier YSR Aarogyasri, is Andhra Pradesh’s flagship cashless health assurance scheme for economically vulnerable families.
n9bfa35f6688.tq: Directly identify the purpose of the flagship state scheme.
xs: **Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva** (earlier **YSR Aarogyasri**) is AP's flagship **cashless health assurance** for **economically vulnerable families** — option **(4)**.
It is not an employee-only, crop-insurance or pension scheme.
xa: It runs **in convergence with PM-JAY** (portability, wider empanelment).
**Mar 2026**: **five more critical cardiovascular procedures** added.
AP Budget 2024-25 BE: **₹4,000 Cr** for the Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva Trust.
AP households covered by all schemes: **70%**.

nba61393491f.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva and PM-JAY in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva is restricted to government hospitals under PM-JAY.
PM-JAY replaced Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva completely in Andhra Pradesh.
The two schemes operate without any institutional relationship.
Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva is implemented in convergence with PM-JAY, enabling portability and wider empanelment.
nba61393491f.x: The Andhra Pradesh scheme is implemented in convergence with PM-JAY, particularly providing portability and wider hospital empanelment.
nba61393491f.tq: Test the functional relationship between two similar health-assurance schemes.
xs: **Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva** is implemented **in convergence with PM-JAY**, giving **portability and wider empanelment** — option **(4)**.
PM-JAY did not replace it, and it is not restricted to government hospitals.
xa: **2,700 private hospitals** are registered; **540** speciality.
Coverage also includes the **Employee Health Scheme**, RSBY, ESIS and CGHS.

ne8164af0506.s: According to the Economic Survey 2021–22 context, Centre and States together spent approximately what percentage of GDP on health in 2019–20?
ne8164af0506.x: Centre and States together spent about 1.3% of GDP on health in 2019–20.
ne8164af0506.tq: Recall the approximate combined public-spending figure rather than the NHP target.
xs: Centre + States spent about **1.3% of GDP** on health in **2019-20** — option **(2)** (Economic Survey 2021-22).
**2.5%** is the **NHP 2017** target; **1.84%** was the **2021-22** COVID peak.
xa: On the new GDP base: **1.48%**.
The Centre's own spending is **~0.29% of GDP**.

n150a5a08f53.s: DVDMS is associated with which function in the public medicine-supply system?
o: Setting the list of essential surgical procedures
n150a5a08f53.x: DVDMS manages drug procurement and inventory under the Free Drugs Service Initiative.
n150a5a08f53.tq: Match the digital system with its operational function.
xs: **DVDMS** manages **drug procurement and inventory** — option **(2)**.
It works under the **Free Drugs Service Initiative (NHM)**, which provides free generic medicines at public facilities.
xa: **NPPA (1997)** fixes ceiling prices of scheduled (**NLEM**) drugs.
NPPA acts under the **Drugs Price Control Order, 2013**.
Private pharmacies dominate over **Jan Aushadhi**, with bills about **6 times** higher.

n946b8d19feb.s: India's first National Health Policy was issued in:
n946b8d19feb.x: India's National Health Policies came in 1983, 2002 and 2017.
xa: **India Newborn Action Plan**: **2014**.
**National Policy for Rare Diseases**: **2021**.
NHP 2017 target: public health spending **2.5% of GDP by 2025** — missed (**1.43%** in 2022-23).

ne39f04a0b81.s: Which of the following best characterises the approach of the National Health Policy, 2017?
o: A private-sector-only approach to emergency care
An assurance-based approach with comprehensive primary care
An insurance-only approach without public-sector services
A disease-specific approach limited to communicable diseases
ne39f04a0b81.x: NHP 2017 adopted an assurance-based approach and envisaged comprehensive primary care rather than an insurance-only or disease-specific model.
ne39f04a0b81.tq: Identify the official policy approach while rejecting extreme alternatives such as “only” and “private-sector-only.”
xs: **NHP 2017** took an **assurance-based approach** with **comprehensive primary care** — option **(2)**.
Its primary care package covers **NCDs, mental health, geriatric and palliative care** via **Health and Wellness Centres** — not communicable diseases alone.
xa: Public hospitals: **free drugs, diagnostics + emergency care**.
Targets: **TFR 2.1 by 2025**; life expectancy **67.5 → 70 by 2025**.
⚠ Spending target **2.5% of GDP by 2025** was missed.

ndd993861f36.s: The National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) and the National Urban Health Mission (NUHM) were launched respectively in:
ndd993861f36.x: NRHM was launched in 2005 and NUHM in 2013; together they form the National Health Mission.
xa: NRHM was asked in **APPSC 2023** PYQ.
NRHM goal: **accessible, affordable, quality care** for rural India.
NHM funding: **60:40**; NE and Himalayan states **90:10**.

n023e2c26b68.s: The Indian Research Fund Association, the predecessor of the Indian Council of Medical Research, was established in:
n023e2c26b68.x: The Indian Research Fund Association was established in 1911 and was later renamed the ICMR in 1949.
n023e2c26b68.tq: Distinguish the founding year from the later renaming year.
xs: The **Indian Research Fund Association (IRFA)** was set up in **1911** — option **(2)**.
It was renamed **ICMR** in **1949**; **1948** is the year **WHO** was founded.
xa: ICMR is among the world's **oldest medical research bodies**.
ICMR consortia: **MERA India** (malaria), **India TB Research Consortium**, **India Hypertension Control Initiative**.
The **Medical Device and Diagnostic Mission Secretariat** reduces import dependence.

n9f3442fcc6b.s: Which of the following is NOT a disease consortium or initiative listed in connection with the ICMR?
n9f3442fcc6b.x: MERA India, the India TB Research Consortium and the India Hypertension Control Initiative are listed ICMR-related initiatives; India Food Security Consortium is not.
n9f3442fcc6b.tq: Find the invented-looking member by comparing every option with the named ICMR initiatives.
xs: **India Food Security Consortium** is not an ICMR consortium — option **(4)**.
**MERA India** (malaria), the **India TB Research Consortium** and the **India Hypertension Control Initiative** are ICMR consortia.
xa: Others: **Mission Delhi**, **India Cancer Research Consortium**, **Stroke Network**.
ICMR began in **1911** as IRFA; renamed **1949**.
**Medical Device and Diagnostic Mission Secretariat**: reduces import dependence.

n6af44af2813.s: Along with increased public spending on health, the National Health Policy, 2002 emphasised:
o: Withdrawal of the Centre from health funding
Exclusive provision of health services by the public sector
A larger role for the private sector and NGOs
n6af44af2813.x: NHP 2002 called for more public spending and a larger role for the private sector and NGOs, not exclusive public provision.
xa: The first National Health Policy came in **1983**.
**NHP 2017** adopted an **assurance-based** approach.
NHP 2017 promised **free drugs, diagnostics + emergency care** in public hospitals.

nf1cbdeb9907.s: The National Health Policy, 2017 set a life expectancy target of how many years by 2025?
nf1cbdeb9907.x: NHP 2017 aimed to raise life expectancy from 67.5 to 70 years by 2025, alongside 2.5% of GDP public spending and TFR 2.1.
xa: MMR target: **100 by 2020**.
⚠ The spending target was **missed** — **1.43%** in **2022-23** (NHA).
NHP 2017 is **assurance-based**.

nd7ab6d6055e.s: Mission Indradhanush aims at what level of full immunisation?
nd7ab6d6055e.x: The December 2014 catch-up drive under UIP for zero-dose and partly immunised children targets 90% full immunisation.
xa: **U-WIN** digitises maternal and child vaccination records.
**MR-1** at **9-12 months** is the correct PYQ pair.

nf0a68eb0b50.s: The Eat Right India campaign (2018) was launched by:
nf0a68eb0b50.x: Eat Right India is an FSSAI campaign; FSSAI was created under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
xa: FSSAI was created under the **Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006**.
Eat Right India + Fit India together aim to **cut NCD deaths**.
**ICMR** began in **1911** as **IRFA**; renamed in **1949**.

n8a81cef0c98.s: Which scheme entitles pregnant women to free ('zero expense') delivery and newborn care at public facilities?
n8a81cef0c98.x: JSSK is the free-entitlement scheme; JSY gives cash assistance for institutional delivery and is 100% centrally sponsored.
xa: AP JSY: **1,76,966** beneficiaries (Apr-Dec **2024**).
**RKSK** covers adolescents **10-19 years**.
NHM funding: **60:40**; NE and Himalayan states **90:10**.

n0c40415e380.s: The usual Centre–State funding pattern under the National Health Mission is:
o: 60:40, with 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States
n0c40415e380.x: The normal funding pattern is 60:40 between the Centre and States, while North-Eastern and Himalayan States receive a 90:10 pattern.
n0c40415e380.tq: Compare the general funding ratio with the special ratio for specified regions.
xs: NHM funding: **Centre:State 60:40**, **90:10** for **NE and Himalayan states** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **JSY** is **100%** centrally sponsored.
xa: NRHM aims at **accessible, affordable, quality care** for rural India.
ASHAs + ANMs form the **backbone of rural care**.

nc135212c40e.s: Primary care, delivered through Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, is expected to meet about what share of health needs?
nc135212c40e.x: Primary care meets 80-90% of health needs; the AAM target was 1,50,000 centres and over 1.73 lakh have been converted.
xa: AAM services: NCD screening (hypertension, diabetes, **oral/breast/cervix** cancers), mental health, ENT, eye, geriatric, palliative + trauma care.
Campaigns: **Ayushman Sabhas**, weekly **Ayushman Melas**, **Ayushman Gram**.
Telemedicine is available in **all AAMs in AP**.

nc38ec89ef0a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about PM-ABHIM?
o: It focuses on health infrastructure for pandemics
Its approved outlay of ₹64,180 crore covers FY 2016–17 to FY 2020–21
It was launched on 25 October 2021 at Varanasi
It includes critical care blocks, Integrated Public Health Laboratories and BSL-3 laboratories
nc38ec89ef0a.x: The ₹64,180 crore outlay covers FY 2021–22 to FY 2025–26.
xa: In AP, **J.P. Nadda** inaugurated **10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 IPHLs** (**₹250 crore**) from **Vijayawada** (13 Sep 2026).
The other Ayushman Bharat pillars: **Ayushman Arogya Mandir** and **ABDM**.

n54de8bf4ddf.s: ABHA, the health ID under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, has how many digits?
n54de8bf4ddf.x: ABHA is a 14-digit health ID; accounts crossed 90 crore by June 2026.
xa: Earlier (Aug 2025): **79.91 crore** accounts; **67.19 crore** linked records.
**NMC (Mar 2026)**: all medical colleges to link ABHA IDs for OPD/IPD/emergency patients.

n311572a5ea6.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four principal registries of ABDM?
n311572a5ea6.x: The four registries are ABHA, Healthcare Professionals Registry, Health Facility Registry and Drug Registry. Arogya Mitra is not an ABDM component.
n311572a5ea6.tq: Use the ‘not part of the architecture’ trap to distinguish a familiar health term from an official registry.
xs: **Arogya Mitra registry** is not an ABDM registry — option **(1)**; Arogya Mitra is a **PM-JAY hospital facilitator** (APPSC 2025 PYQ).
The four registries: **ABHA**, **Healthcare Professionals Registry**, **Health Facility Registry** and **Drug Registry**.
xa: ABHA is a **14-digit** ID; **90 crore+** accounts (Jun 2026).
ABDM is run by the **National Health Authority**.
Gateways: **Consent Manager**, **UHI**, **NHCX**.

n44669c4d7a7.s: The March 2026 direction of the National Medical Commission required medical colleges to generate and link ABHA IDs for:
o: All OPD, IPD and emergency patients
n44669c4d7a7.x: The NMC directed medical colleges to generate and link ABHA IDs for all OPD, IPD and emergency patients, partly to detect fake patients during inspections.
n44669c4d7a7.tq: Identify the complete beneficiary category rather than narrowing the order to one department or scheme.
xs: **NMC (Mar 2026)** ordered medical colleges to generate and link **ABHA IDs** for **all OPD, IPD and emergency patients** — option **(2)**.
The aim: **weed out fake patients** during inspections.
xa: ABHA is a **14-digit** health ID; **90 crore+** accounts (Jun 2026).
Aug 2025: **79.91 crore** accounts, **67.19 crore** linked records.
AP's **Sanjeevani** gives an ABHA ID to every citizen.

n34c677c01b7.s: The Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK) covers adolescents aged:
n34c677c01b7.x: RKSK covers 10-19 year-olds through Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics, weekly iron folic acid supplementation and peer educators.
xa: RKSK also covers **menstrual hygiene**.
**Anaemia Mukt Bharat** (2018) follows the **6x6x6** strategy.

n4a35b31f7ae.s: Which one of the following sets of vaccines is administered at birth under the Universal Immunisation Programme?
o: BCG, OPV-0 and Hepatitis B birth dose
MR-2, DPT booster-1 and OPV booster
Td, DPT booster-2 and Rotavirus vaccine
n4a35b31f7ae.x: The birth schedule includes BCG, OPV-0 and the birth dose of Hepatitis B.
n4a35b31f7ae.tq: Start with the age column and eliminate vaccines belonging to later schedules.
xs: At birth: **BCG, OPV-0 and Hepatitis B birth dose** — option **(1)**.
**MR-1, JE-1, PCV booster** = **9-12 months**; **MR-2, DPT booster-1, OPV booster** = **16-24 months**; **Td** = **10 and 16 years**.
xa: **6, 10, 14 weeks**: OPV 1-3, Pentavalent 1-3, Rotavirus, fIPV; **PCV** at 6 and 14 weeks.
**DPT booster-2**: **5-6 years**.
Mission Indradhanush targets **90%** full immunisation.

nccc6acc3d16.s: Which one of the following is the principal benefit of maintaining digital health records under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission?
o: They improve the sharing and use of patient information across providers
They replace the need for doctors at primary health centres
They make health insurance compulsory for every citizen
They allow hospitals to share records without the patient's consent
nccc6acc3d16.x: Digital records improve the sharing and use of patient information (APPSC 2023 PYQ answer). They support doctors rather than replace them; ABDM does not make insurance compulsory; and the ABDM ecosystem is consent-based, so sharing without consent is wrong.
nccc6acc3d16.tq: ABDM benefit = better sharing of records, always consent-based.
xs: Digital records **improve the sharing and use of patient information** — option **(1)** (APPSC 2023 PYQ answer).
ABDM is **consent-based**, so sharing without consent is wrong; it does not replace doctors or make insurance compulsory.
xa: ABHA is a **14-digit** health ID; **90 crore+** accounts.
ABDM is **interoperable** and built on **Digital Public Infrastructure**.
Telemedicine via **eSanjeevani** uses a Clinical Decision Support System.

nfe27793a0a0.s: World Health Day is observed on 7 April every year because on that date in 1948:
o: the World Health Organization was founded, with its headquarters at Geneva
the Alma-Ata Declaration on primary health care was adopted
the World Health Organization was founded, with its headquarters at New York
smallpox was declared eradicated by the World Health Assembly
nfe27793a0a0.x: WHO was founded on 7 April 1948 and is headquartered at Geneva, so World Health Day falls on 7 April. WHO's headquarters is not New York; the Alma-Ata Declaration and the eradication of smallpox are later events and not linked to 7 April 1948.
nfe27793a0a0.tq: WHO: Geneva, 7 April 1948 = World Health Day.
xs: **WHO** was founded on **7 April 1948**, headquartered at **Geneva** — option **(1)**.
Hence **World Health Day is 7 April**; WHO's headquarters is not New York.
xa: ⚠ **1949** is when IRFA was renamed **ICMR**.
ICMR's origin: **IRFA**, **1911**.
**One of the oldest** medical research bodies is ICMR.

nf2929a43058.s: The Sanjeevani digital health programme of Andhra Pradesh, commencing in August 2026, is primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Replacement of all public hospitals by private hospitals
Universal distribution of fortified food through fair-price shops
Free insurance cover of ₹5 lakh for every citizen
A digital health profile and ABHA ID for every citizen
nf2929a43058.x: Sanjeevani aims to create a digital health profile and ABHA ID for every citizen of Andhra Pradesh.
nf2929a43058.tq: Identify the defining feature of the programme rather than confusing it with an insurance scheme.
xs: AP's **Sanjeevani** (from **Aug 2026**) gives a **digital health profile and ABHA ID for every citizen** — option **(4)**.
It does not privatise hospitals, distribute food or give a fixed insurance cover.
xa: It links PHCs, hospitals, labs, **e-Aushadhi**, **108**, **104**, telemedicine + **AI assistance**.
The **Sanjeevani Citizen Wellness App** came in **Jul 2026**.
It makes AP an **ABDM-linked**, citizen-wide digital health state.

n133bdf9b8eb.s: The Pulse Polio programme was launched in:
n133bdf9b8eb.x: Pulse Polio began in 1995, after India became smallpox-free in 1977; the last wild polio case was in 2011.
xa: **Guinea worm** certified free: **2000**.
**Maternal and neonatal tetanus** eliminated: **2015**; **Yaws** declared free: **2016**.
Switch from trivalent to **bivalent OPV**: **Apr 2016**.

n93e7feabd40.s: Which of the following polio milestones is NOT correct?
o: India's last wild polio case was reported from Howrah in January 2011
The WHO South-East Asia Region was certified polio-free on 27 March 2014
Bivalent OPV covers polio types 1 and 3
India switched from trivalent to bivalent OPV in April 2014
n93e7feabd40.x: The switch from tOPV to bOPV took place in April 2016, not 2014.
xa: **Pulse Polio** was launched in **1995**.
**Yaws** was declared free in **2016**; **MNT** eliminated in **2015**.

n567304b2b18.s: The national target for tuberculosis elimination in India is:
n567304b2b18.x: India’s national target for TB elimination is 2025, five years ahead of the SDG target of 2030.
n567304b2b18.tq: Compare the national target with the later SDG target.
xs: India's national TB elimination target is **2025** — option **(2)**.
That is **five years ahead** of the SDG target of **2030**.
xa: Programme: **NTEP** — free diagnosis + treatment.
TB incidence fell **21%** and mortality **28%** (2015-2024).
⚠ **2030** is the target for **malaria**; **2027** for lymphatic filariasis; **2047** for sickle cell anaemia.

n5b9207f51a9.s: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination covers which period?
n5b9207f51a9.x: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination covers 2016–2030 and targets malaria elimination by 2030.
n5b9207f51a9.tq: Combine the official framework name with its exact period.
xs: The **National Framework for Malaria Elimination** covers **2016-2030** — option **(3)**.
It targets **malaria elimination by 2030**.
xa: Malaria cases fell **80%** during **2015-2023**.
**MERA India** = Malaria Elimination Research Alliance India, led by **ICMR**.
⚠ **2021-26** is **NACP Phase V**.

n3b196d3b18e.s: Which of the following is NOT a tool under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme for malaria control?
n3b196d3b18e.x: IRS, LLINs, larvivorous fish, bio-larvicides and source reduction are listed malaria-control tools. Universal antibiotic prophylaxis is not one of them.
n3b196d3b18e.tq: Identify the non-vector-control measure among operational tools.
xs: **Universal antibiotic prophylaxis** is not an NVBDCP tool — option **(4)**.
NVBDCP tools: **IRS** (indoor residual spraying), **LLINs**, **larvivorous fish**, **bio-larvicides**, **source reduction**.
xa: NVBDCP elimination targets: **malaria, LF + kala-azar**.
NVBDCP handles outbreaks of **malaria, dengue, chikungunya** (PYQ key).
Malaria cases fell **80%** during **2015-2023**.

n49d49a2f63a.s: Under Sustainable Development Goal 3.4, the target for premature deaths from non-communicable diseases by 2030 is to:
n49d49a2f63a.x: SDG 3.4 calls for reducing premature mortality from non-communicable diseases by one-third through prevention and treatment by 2030.
n49d49a2f63a.tq: Focus on the exact target fraction and distinguish it from stronger but unsupported claims such as elimination.
xs: **SDG 3.4**: **reduce premature NCD deaths by one-third** by **2030** — option **(3)**.
It is a one-third cut, not halving, a quarter or complete elimination.
xa: ⚠ **SDG 3.3** is about ending **AIDS, TB, malaria and NTD** epidemics by 2030.
**NP-NCD** (earlier NPCDCS) links high-risk people to care.
AP screened **53.02 lakh** citizens under **NCD-CD 3.0**.

ne0183be49ea.s: The national target of eliminating sickle-cell anaemia is set for:
ne0183be49ea.x: India has set a target to eliminate sickle-cell anaemia by 2047 and to screen seven crore at-risk people.
ne0183be49ea.tq: Separate the long-term disease mission year from 2025 and 2030 targets.
xs: India aims to **eliminate sickle cell anaemia by 2047** — option **(4)**.
It plans to **screen 7 crore** at-risk people (APPSC 2022 PYQ: A and R both true, R explains A).
xa: **Lymphatic filariasis**: **2027**; **malaria**: **2030**; **TB**: **2025**.
**Ayushman Gram** includes **sickle-cell screening**.

n6b75e6d6a87.s: The triple-drug IDA regimen for lymphatic filariasis uses Ivermectin, DEC and:
n6b75e6d6a87.x: IDA = Ivermectin, DEC and Albendazole; India targets LF elimination by 2027, three years ahead of the SDG target.
xa: LF is eliminated through **MDA** with the triple-drug regimen.
LF is an **NVBDCP** elimination target with malaria and kala-azar.
Sickle cell anaemia target: **2047**.

nba2f77190ae.s: The Sustainable Development Goal 3.3 seeks, by 2030, to:
o: Reduce premature NCD deaths by one-third only
Eliminate all forms of environmental pollution
Provide universal mental-health counselling through telemedicine
End epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases
nba2f77190ae.x: SDG 3.3 specifically seeks to end the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases by 2030.
nba2f77190ae.tq: Distinguish SDG 3.3 from SDG 3.4, which concerns premature deaths from NCDs.
xs: **SDG 3.3** aims to **end the epidemics of AIDS, TB, malaria and NTDs** by **2030** — option **(4)**.
⚠ Cutting premature NCD deaths by **one-third** is **SDG 3.4**.
xa: India's TB target **2025** is five years ahead of the SDG target of 2030.
**Lymphatic filariasis** target **2027** is three years ahead of SDG 3.3.
Malaria elimination target: **2030** (framework **2016-2030**).

o: An insurance scheme for TB patients
A digital portal for TB notification and tracking
n9ab60c28d53.x: Ni-kshay is the digital TB notification and tracking portal; Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana gives nutritional DBT to all notified TB patients.
xa: **Ni-kshay Mitras** adopt patients under the **PM TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan** (**Sept 2022**).
Dec 2025: **3.78 lakh+ Mitras**, **20 lakh+** patients, **45 lakh+** food baskets.

nba1670418c7.s: According to the India TB Report 2022, TB notifications in 2021 compared with 2020:
nba1670418c7.x: The India TB Report 2022 recorded a 19% rise in notifications in 2021 over 2020 (APPSC 2022 PYQ). 'Fell by 19%' reverses the direction; 53% is the 2015 treatment-coverage figure; 28% is the fall in TB mortality during 2015-2024.
xs: Notifications **rose by 19%** in 2021 over 2020 — option **(1)** (**India TB Report 2022**, APPSC 2022 PYQ).
**53%** is the 2015 treatment coverage; **28%** is the fall in TB mortality (2015-2024).
xa: TB incidence fell **21%** (2015-2024).
**Himachal Pradesh** screens all indoor hospital patients for TB (intensified case finding).
**Ni-kshay** is the digital notification portal.

ne4de4b57f80.s: In HIV services, VCTC stands for:
ne4de4b57f80.x: VCTC is the Voluntary Counselling and Testing Centre; ART is free for life at ART centres, and ICTC testing is voluntary with counselling.
xa: **PEP** must be taken **within 72 hours**.
Other prevention tools: **Treatment as Prevention, Test and Treat, PrEP**, condoms.

n7a10f97c09c.s: The HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 primarily seeks to prevent which of the following?
o: Discrimination against people living with HIV
n7a10f97c09c.x: The Act of 2017 bars discrimination against people living with HIV and provides a legal framework for their protection.
n7a10f97c09c.tq: Link the legislation with its principal legal protection.
xs: The **HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017** bars **discrimination against people living with HIV** — option **(2)**.
It does not restrict ART centres, medicines or voluntary testing.
xa: ⚠ **2017** also saw the **Mental Healthcare Act**.
India has **over 2.5 million** people living with HIV.
Free **lifelong ART** is given at ART centres.

n94faf34044e.s: AVAHAN, an HIV prevention initiative in India, belongs to:
n94faf34044e.x: AVAHAN is the Gates Foundation's HIV prevention initiative, not a World Bank project; the Red Ribbon Express is an awareness train.
xa: NACO held the **'Suraksha Sankalp Karyashala'** district review at **Vijayawada** (Mar 2026).
NACP was launched in **1992**, led by **NACO**.
Prevention tools: **PEP within 72 hours**, PrEP, Test and Treat.

n5b86dfdcaed.s: Which strain of HIV is dominant in India?
n5b86dfdcaed.x: HIV-1 subtype C is the dominant strain in India. HIV-2, HIV-1 subtype B and HIV-1 subtype A are other HIV types or subtypes but are not the dominant strain in India.
xs: The dominant strain in India is **HIV-1 subtype C** — option **(1)**.
So HIV-2 and the other HIV-1 subtypes listed are not India's dominant strain.
xa: India has **over 2.5 million** people living with HIV.
Highest burden: **Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka**.
Goal: end AIDS as a public health threat by **2030**.

n0c2592579c9.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the 2026 Andhra Pradesh HIV target and reported three-part status?
n0c2592579c9.x: Andhra Pradesh reported 88%, 87% and 96.2% across the three indicators, with a target for December 2026.
n0c2592579c9.tq: Preserve the order of a multi-part numerical indicator.
xs: AP targets the HIV cascade by **Dec 2026**; option (4) jumbles the order.
xa: **95-95-95** is the UNAIDS target adopted by India.
AP's minister called the national target **95-95-99**.
AP launched the **Suraksha Dashboard** (13 Aug 2026).

n108c0d0fef6.s: The India Hypertension Control Initiative, implemented with the involvement of ICMR, primarily seeks to reduce deaths due to:
o: Heart attack, stroke and kidney failure
n108c0d0fef6.x: The India Hypertension Control Initiative targets hypertension-related deaths from heart attack, stroke and kidney failure.
n108c0d0fef6.tq: Match the named initiative with its specific disease-outcome targets.
xs: The **India Hypertension Control Initiative (ICMR)** targets deaths from **heart attack, stroke and kidney failure** — option **(4)**.
Rabies, snake-bite and leptospirosis are separate programmes run in AP.
xa: **NP-NCD** finds high-risk people and links them to care.
**SDG 3.4**: cut premature NCD deaths by **one-third** by 2030.
⚠ **MERA India** is ICMR's malaria alliance.

n48152150061.s: Cervavac, announced in September 2022, is best described as:
o: India's first indigenous quadrivalent HPV vaccine against cervical cancer, made by the Serum Institute of India
India's first indigenous malaria vaccine, made by Bharat Biotech
An intranasal COVID-19 vaccine developed with ICMR-NIV
The world's first DNA vaccine approved for humans, made by Zydus
n48152150061.x: Cervavac is India's first indigenous quadrivalent HPV vaccine, made by the Serum Institute of India against cervical cancer (Sept 2022). The intranasal COVID vaccine is iNCOVACC; the first DNA vaccine is ZyCoV-D by Zydus; and Cervavac is not a malaria vaccine (R21 is the Oxford-SII malaria vaccine).
n48152150061.tq: Cervavac = HPV, quadrivalent, SII, cervical cancer.
xs: **Cervavac** is **India's first indigenous quadrivalent HPV vaccine** against **cervical cancer**, made by **Serum Institute of India** — option **(1)**.
It was announced in **Sept 2022** (two PYQs).
⚠ The malaria vaccine made by Serum Institute is **R21/Matrix-M**, developed by Oxford.
xa: **RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix)** is GSK's malaria vaccine.
AAMs screen for **oral, breast and cervical** cancers.

n76f243e70d5.s: During 2015-2024, TB mortality in India fell by:
n76f243e70d5.x: TB mortality fell 28%, while incidence fell 21% and treatment coverage rose from 53% to 92%.
xa: IYB gives coverage of **85%** in **2023**.
⚠ India TB Report 2022: notifications rose **19%** in 2021 over 2020.

n8cfb557e619.s:
In Andhra Pradesh, NP-NCD additionally covers:

2. Iodine Deficiency Disorders and tobacco control
3. Fluorosis and oral health
Which of the above is/are correct?
n8cfb557e619.x: AP's expanded NP-NCD covers mental health, elderly care, IDD, tobacco control, fluorosis and oral health.
xa: AP's ANMs screen at home using the **ANM AP Health App**.
**NCD-CD 3.0**: universal screening from **14 Nov 2024** → **53.02 lakh** citizens screened (2024-25).
AP also runs **NTEP, NCVBDC, NPCBVI, NLEP** and rabies, leptospirosis, snake-bite programmes.

nc3b462e7580.s: Tele-MANAS, the tele-mental health service, was launched in:
nc3b462e7580.x: Tele-MANAS came in 2022, after the NMHP (1982), the Mental Health Act (1987) and the Mental Healthcare Act (2017).
xa: The 2017 Act **repealed** the 1987 Act.
It **decriminalised suicide** and gave a **right to access** government mental healthcare.
Prevalence of mental illness: about **1 in 7 Indians**.

n2b7386d6d42.s: Which of the following sets consists only of countries certified malaria-free by WHO among the countries listed?
n2b7386d6d42.x: Sri Lanka, China and Timor-Leste are the three countries identified as WHO-certified malaria-free in this group.
n2b7386d6d42.tq: Use set comparison to eliminate a list containing an unlisted country.
xs: **Sri Lanka, China and Timor-Leste** are WHO-certified **malaria-free** — option **(1)**.
**Timor-Leste** is the most recent of the three (Jan 2026); **India** targets elimination only by **2030**.
xa: Only about **42%** of global malaria financing needs are met.
Malaria cases in India fell **80%** in **2015-2023**.
Vaccines: **RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix)** by GSK; **R21/Matrix-M** by Oxford, made by **Serum Institute**.

nc7fcf28c8fc.s: Which of the following States are identified as carrying the highest HIV burden among the listed States?

xs: The highest HIV burden is in **Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka** — option **(1)**.

xa: Dominant strain in India: **HIV-1 subtype C**.
NACO's **'Suraksha Sankalp Karyashala'** district review was held in **Vijayawada**, Mar 2026.

n5dc4a97f224.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP)?
o: It handles outbreaks of malaria, dengue and chikungunya
It provides free multidrug therapy for leprosy at PHCs
It targets elimination of malaria, lymphatic filariasis and kala-azar
It deals with vector-borne diseases such as malaria and dengue
n5dc4a97f224.x: Free MDT for leprosy at PHCs is under the National Leprosy Eradication Programme (with the Sparsh campaign), not NVBDCP.
xa: Malaria elimination target: **2030**.
Lymphatic filariasis target: **2027**, using triple-drug **IDA**.
**Anti-Leprosy Day**: **30 January**.

nbiology-19-1.s: Who developed the first polio vaccine?
nbiology-19-1.x: Jonas Salk made the first (injected, inactivated) polio vaccine in 1955. Albert Sabin made the oral polio vaccine.
n: Jonas Salk developed the first polio vaccine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
Albert Sabin developed the Oral Polio Vaccine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
xs: **Jonas Salk** developed the **first polio vaccine** — option **(2)**.
**Albert Sabin** developed the **Oral Polio Vaccine**; **Edward Jenner** — **smallpox vaccine**; **Louis Pasteur** — **rabies vaccine**.
xa: India switched from **trivalent** to **bivalent OPV** in **Apr 2016**.
WHO SEAR certified polio-free: **27 Mar 2014**.
**Pulse Polio** launched **1995**.

nbiology-19-5.s: Bivalent OPV covers which polio virus types?
nbiology-19-5.x: Bivalent OPV covers types 1 and 3, while trivalent OPV covers types 1, 2 and 3.
n: Trivalent OPV protects against poliovirus types 1, 2, and 3. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
Bivalent OPV protects against poliovirus types 1 and 3. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
ZyCoV-D is a DNA-based COVID-19 vaccine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
xa: OPV was developed by **Albert Sabin**.
Switch to **bivalent OPV**: **Apr 2016**.
Last wild polio case: **Howrah, WB**, **Jan 2011**.

nbiology-19-7.s: Diphtheria is prevented by which type of vaccine?
nbiology-19-7.x: Diphtheria is prevented by a toxoid vaccine; hepatitis B also has a vaccine.
n: Diphtheria is prevented with a toxoid vaccine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
Hepatitis B has a vaccine. [Biology · ROCKET SHEET #19 · pp 32-33]
xa: **DPT** covers **diphtheria**, **pertussis** and **tetanus**.
⚠ The source does **not** attribute a vaccine to **AIDS**.
**Cervavac** — India's first indigenous **quadrivalent HPV** vaccine (**Serum Institute of India**).

Port: Mulapeta; District / location: Srikakulam; Details: State port [October 2026 · AP greenfield ports — doubling OTMP cargo capacity]
xa: Ramayapatnam: **81%** done; Phase 1 ₹4,922.62 crore.

cae69349ee9342.s: The Machilipatnam greenfield state port is being built by:
cae69349ee9342.x: MEIL is building Machilipatnam, while Kakinada Gateway Port is an Aurobindo Group multi-cargo facility under PPP.

xa: Kakinada Gateway Port: **33%** done; **16 MMTPA**, commissioning early **2027**.
Machilipatnam: **59%**; Mulapeta: **76%**.

cad2e83954429c.s: Which organisation from Machilipatnam was identified as an MSME component partner for Q-SHIVA?

na0abbdb399a.s: Which of the following is NOT one of Andhra Pradesh's four greenfield Other Than Major Ports (OTMPs)?

A **July 2019** law reserved **75%** of private-sector jobs for locals.

n713ba170bc3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Bills passed by the Andhra Pradesh Assembly in 2026?

The AP Municipal Laws (Third Amendment) Bill provided a Uniform Mutation Fee

**July 2019** law reserved **75%** private jobs for locals.

n3c9327f29e3.s: The 2019 secretariat model and the new Swarna Gramam system are described as the delivery arms of:
n3c9327f29e3.x: The 2019 secretariat model and Swarna Gramam are the delivery arms of Super Six welfare.

e-KYC for **1.71 crore** families (**11 Jun 2026**).
The **8th Collectors' Conference** reviewed **Super Six**, **P4** and **Swarna Andhra @2047**.

n5d9a5fef4ae.s: The "new welfarism" critique argues that direct cash transfers may:
o: Raise the State's own tax revenue
Crowd out public goods and strain State finances
Reduce the number of welfare beneficiaries
n5d9a5fef4ae.x: The critique holds that direct cash transfers can crowd out public goods and pressure State finances.
xa: The **16th Finance Commission** found AP has the **highest per-capita pension spending**.
**P4** offers a voluntary, **whole-of-society** model with government as **facilitator**.
Opposition also attacked the **₹2.5 lakh** insurance plan.

n38738e28485.s: V.A.V.S. Suryanarayana Raju became associated with which body from 30 March 2026?

xs: **V.A.V.S. Suryanarayana Raju** heads the **APSCPCR** — the **AP State Commission for Protection of Child Rights** — from **30 Mar 2026**: option **(2)** is correct.
The **State Information Commission** is headed by **Vajja Srinivas Rao**; the **State Election Commissioner** is **Anil Chandra Punetha**.

**Anil Chandra Punetha** became SEC in **Apr 2026** (Art. **243K/243ZA**).
Lokayukta = **Justice T. Mallikarjuna Rao** (**Aug 2026**, **5 years**).

nc20172de3d2.s:
The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet constituted task forces in 2026 on which of the following?

2. Godavari pollution

n5ab34dbb12e.s: Which institutions provide three-tier monitoring of Vision 2047 in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Village Secretariats, Ward Secretariats and Rythu Seva Kendras
District Collectors, Gram Sabhas and Municipal Corporations
State Election Commission, APCRDA and Planning Department
District Vision Units, Mandal Vision Units and Constituency Development Committees

n5ab34dbb12e.tq: Match the institutional structure with its stated function.
xs: **District/Mandal Vision Units** + **Constituency Development Committees** form the **three-tier monitoring** of **Vision 2047** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Rythu Seva Kendras** are farmer-service centres; **APCRDA** is the capital authority — neither monitors Vision 2047.
xa: The **8th Collectors' Conference** covered district roadmaps under **Swarna Andhra** and **Super Six**.
At the **NITI Aayog Governing Council** (**11 Jun 2026**) the CM presented **Swarna Andhra @2047**.
AP was first to institutionalise **Monthly Economic Reports** (**651 KPIs**, **Jul 2026**).

n7f8c4f2cb92.s: Which Andhra Pradesh programme is the Adult Education Department's 100% literacy drive?
n7f8c4f2cb92.x: Akshara Andhra is the 100% literacy drive (literacy said to rise from 73% to 83%); Vidya Shakti is the IIT Madras STEM coaching tie-up.

"Akshara Andhra" was the **APPSC 2025** key.

nb54262fbe19.s: Jeeva Kranthi scheme of Andhra Pradesh is primarily associated with which department and beneficiary group?
o: Animal Husbandry; women beneficiaries of YSR Cheyutha
Fisheries; marine fishermen during the fishing ban

**2,22,754** units with **Paala Velluva** (Phase III, **2022-23**).

n33328c4fb76.s: SHRESTH (State Health Regulatory Excellence Index) is run by:

n4a8dce8ad33.s: Which of the following correctly describes the housing targets mentioned for Andhra Pradesh?

5.52 lakh houses by March 2027 and a house for every eligible family by 2029
5.52 lakh houses by 2026 and universal housing by 2027

n4a8dce8ad33.x: The current target is 5.52 lakh houses by March 2027 and a house for every eligible family by 2029; 7.60 lakh by 2026 was the earlier target.

The **2029** goal was stated on **16 Sep 2026**.
**2014** renaming: **Indiramma housing → NTR Housing**.

na8839ae659b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Andhra Pradesh Budgets presented on 14 February 2026?

Payyavula Keshav presented the main Budget 2026-27
K. Atchannaidu presented the Agriculture and Allied Sectors Budget
The Agriculture Budget was K. Atchannaidu's first

Farm Budget outlay about **₹53,753 crore**.

**₹31,256** crore is the **2021-22** agriculture budget (**APPSC 2021 key**).
xa: Farm organisations put total farm allocation at about **₹52,000 crore** (**24 Feb 2026**).
Electricity subsidy (farm power): **₹13,722 crore**.
Agriculture Department: **₹12,153 crore**.

n9ef32d64cfe.s: What growth target was fixed for fisheries in Andhra Pradesh for 2026-27?

AP produces ~**10%** of India's agricultural output.
Outlay of the farm Budget: about **₹53,753 crore**.

ncb1d52454ee.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about agriculture in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Agriculture accounts for ₹5,39,454 crore of ₹17,62,357 crore (2025-26 AE)
Agriculture accounts for about half of the State's GSDP
AP produces about 10% of India's agricultural output

Largest farm-budget head: **Irrigation projects** (**₹14,277 crore**).
Farm Budget presented by **K. Atchannaidu**.

n7e09930ab64.s: In the projected revenue receipts of Andhra Pradesh for 2026-27, the shares of own resources and central transfers are respectively:
n7e09930ab64.x: Revenue receipts of ₹2,34,140 crore are expected to comprise 59% own resources and 41% central transfers.
xs: Revenue receipts of **₹2,34,140 crore**: **own resources 59%** + **central transfers 41%** — option **(1)** is correct.

**2025-26 RE**: own tax **₹98,025 crore** vs central transfers **₹1,04,493 crore**.

xs: **SGST** (**₹45,078 cr**, **36%**) is the largest own-tax source — option **(4)** is correct.

xa: Own tax revenue: **₹1,25,846 crore** (**6.4% of GSDP**).
**Commercial taxes** rose **16%** YoY in **Jun 2026** (Q1 FY27 **₹15,323 crore**).
State GST and commercial-tax revenue hit **record highs** in June 2026.

Capital outlay was only **₹16,141 crore**, **51% below** BE.
A **Feb 2026** planning review quoted **₹60,481 crore** and **₹85,269 crore**.

n130a242d0fd.s: According to the 2025-26 Revised Estimates, the outstanding debt of Andhra Pradesh is estimated at approximately what percentage of GSDP?

**33%** was the liabilities level in **2021-22**.

Guarantees availed: **₹3,11,182 crore**.

na4898daddc0.s: Guarantees availed by Andhra Pradesh of about Rs 3,11,182 crore are cited mainly as evidence of:
na4898daddc0.x: Large guarantees (outstanding principal Rs 1,77,034 crore) point to growing off-budget borrowing. The State has a revenue deficit, not a surplus; interest payments are not said to be falling; and revenue-deficit grants have ended under the 16th FC.
xs: Guarantees of **₹3,11,182 crore** point to **growing off-budget borrowing** — option **(1)** is correct.

xa: Outstanding principal on guarantees: **₹1,77,034 crore**.
Critics cite **₹1.28 lakh crore** off-budget debt.
Debt ~**36%** of GSDP.

n3237174253d.s: Critics of Andhra Pradesh's fiscal position cited debt of about what share of GSDP, along with heavy guarantees and off-budget loans?
n3237174253d.x: The criticism centred on debt of about 36% of GSDP, heavy guarantees and off-budget loans.
xa: Critics cite **₹1.28 lakh crore** of off-budget debt.
Guarantees availed: **₹3,11,182 crore** (outstanding principal **₹1,77,034 crore**).
Outstanding debt: **₹6,35,177 crore** = **36.04%** of GSDP (**2025-26 RE**).

Only a sitting High Court Chief Justice can be appointed, for 3 years
Any eminent person in human rights can be appointed, for 5 years or up to age 65
nfbea443d2ad.x: After the 2019 amendment, a Supreme Court judge (not only a former CJI) can be NHRC chair, and the term is 3 years or up to age 70. nfbea443d2ad.tq: 2019: 'CJI only' widened to 'SC judge'; term cut to 3 years, age cap 70.
xs: After the **2019 amendment**, an **SC judge** (not only a former CJI) can be NHRC chair, for **3 years** or up to age **70** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option (1) is the old CJI-only rule with the wrong term; HC Chief Justices and non-judges are not given as eligible for chair.
xa: Latest NHRC chair: **Justice V. Ramasubramanian**.
The NHRC (**1993**) is **statutory**; the **NCW** (**1992**) also.
⚠ **NCSC/NCST** = constitutional; **NCM**, **NHRC**, **NCW** = statutory.
