nfb7c4190ed2.s: India's first Vande Bharat Express ran between which two cities?
nfb7c4190ed2.x: The first Vande Bharat Express ran on the New Delhi-Varanasi route, a fact asked in 2024-25. New Delhi-Katra, Chennai-Mysuru and Mumbai-Gandhinagar were later Vande Bharat routes, not the first.
nfb7c4190ed2.tq: First Vande Bharat: Delhi to Varanasi.
xs: India's **first Vande Bharat** Express ran between **New Delhi and Varanasi** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is a FIRSTs fact asked in **2024-25**; the other city pairs are distractors, not the first route.
xa: **RDSO** designs are built by **ICF Chennai**.
Other FIRSTs: **Vikram-1** = first privately developed orbital rocket; **EOS-05** = first Earth-imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit.
**Qdenga** (Takeda) = India's first dengue vaccine.

n59301403cf3.s: The 2nd AIIMS Oncology Conclave 2025 was held at:
n59301403cf3.x: The 2nd AIIMS Oncology Conclave 2025 was held at AIIMS Jhajjar, the National Cancer Institute (asked 2024). The other AIIMS campuses were not the venue.
n59301403cf3.tq: Oncology conclave = cancer institute = Jhajjar NCI.
xs: The **2nd AIIMS Oncology Conclave 2025** was at **AIIMS Jhajjar**, the **National Cancer Institute (NCI)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
This was asked in **2024**.
xa: **NIMHANS-2** was announced in **Budget 2026-27**.
**NexCAR19** is India's first indigenous CAR-T therapy for **blood cancer**.
A dual-targeting CAR-T (**BCMA + CD19**) targets **multiple myeloma**.

nf1c83bb7e7f.s: The flight-test centre for AMCA is located at:
nf1c83bb7e7f.x: The AMCA flight-test centre is located at Puttaparthi in Andhra Pradesh. AMCA is a fifth-generation twin-engine stealth fighter associated with ADA and DRDO.
nf1c83bb7e7f.tq: Test location separately from platform type and developer.
xs: The **AMCA** flight-test centre is at **Puttaparthi, Andhra Pradesh** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Chandipur** hosted the **Agni-4** user trial; **Hanle** hosts the **Himalayan Chandra Telescope**; **Hingoli** is the site of **LIGO-India**.
xa: AMCA is a **5th-generation** twin-engine stealth fighter by **ADA (DRDO)**.
**Agni-4** (about **4,000 km**) had its user trial at **Chandipur** (Aug 2026).
Other AP angles: **Amaravati Quantum Valley**; **NARL at Gadanki** (Chittoor); DSV **Nipun** from HSL.

n51baa7cd6bc.s: The first domestic packaging plant for memory chips at Sanand is associated with which company?
n51baa7cd6bc.x: Micron’s ATMP facility at Sanand is identified as the first domestic packaging plant for memory chips.
n51baa7cd6bc.tq: Use the company–facility association rather than confusing chip packaging with processor development.
xs: **Micron**'s **ATMP** at **Sanand** (2026) is the **first domestic packaging plant for memory chips** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Google** set up the **Ananta** campus (Bengaluru); **Microsoft** made **Majorana 1**; **C-DAC** made **VEGA** and **DHRUV64**.
xa: **ISM 2.0** (Jul 2026): **₹1,27,500 crore**; up to **40%** capex for CMOS fabs; first commercial fab by **2028**.
**ISM 1.0** approved **4** semiconductor units by **2024**.
**DIR-V** = MeitY's Digital India RISC-V programme.

n064f3b5cecc.s: Dipturus dhritiae, reported in September 2026, is a:
o: Wolf snake from Great Nicobar Island
Deep-sea skate from the Arabian Sea
Ray spider from a cave in Meghalaya
n064f3b5cecc.x: Dipturus dhritiae is a deep-sea skate from the Arabian Sea, discovered under the Deep Ocean Mission and named after Dhriti Banerjee, the first woman Director of ZSI.
xa: It came from the **Deep Ocean Mission** (**Sep 2026**).
**Dhriti Banerjee** is the **ZSI's first woman Director**.
**Lycodon irwini** (**2025**) is **Irwin's wolf snake**.

nc9bdde82de6.s: Lycodon irwini, reported in 2025, was discovered in:
nc9bdde82de6.x: Lycodon irwini, or Irwin's wolf snake, was reported from Great Nicobar Island.
nc9bdde82de6.tq: Use the common name and island location as the decisive clues.
xs: **Lycodon irwini** (Irwin's wolf snake, **2025**) was found on **Great Nicobar Island** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Arabian Sea** gave **Dipturus dhritiae**; the **Sundarbans** gave **Piratula acuminata**; **Papikonda NP** gave **Hamataliwa papikonda**.
xa: **Piratula acuminata** is a **wolf spider** — do not confuse it with the **wolf snake**.
**Dipturus dhritiae** is a deep-sea skate from the **Deep Ocean Mission**.
**Kerala (98)** had the most new animal species in 2025.

nab896d7a79b.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh tiger-conservation plan described, four female tigers are to be moved into NSTR from:
nab896d7a79b.x: Four female tigers are to be brought into Andhra Pradesh's NSTR from Chandrapur (Maharashtra) and Madhya Pradesh. Gaur are also to be translocated to NSTR from September 2026.
nab896d7a79b.tq: Test the source locations and the two-each distribution together.
xs: The **4 female tigers** for AP are to come from **Chandrapur (Maharashtra) and Madhya Pradesh** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The other pairs are not the source reserves named in the notes.
xa: **Gaur** are also to be translocated to **NSTR** from **Sep 2026**.
**NSTR** is the **largest TR**.
**MP** has the most tiger reserves (**9**).

n8c320e9e211.s: Which State has the largest number of tiger reserves in India?
n8c320e9e211.x: Madhya Pradesh has the most tiger reserves (9), including Madhav NP (Shivpuri), India's 58th. Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh have fewer.
n8c320e9e211.tq: MP: Tiger State, 9 reserves incl. the 58th, Madhav.
xs: **Madhya Pradesh** has the most tiger reserves, **9** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It includes **Madhav NP (Shivpuri)**, India's **58th** TR.
xa: MP also holds **Kuno NP** and the 3rd cheetah site, **Veerangana Durgavati TR**.
AP's **NSTR** is the **largest** TR.
PA network (**2026**): **109 NPs, 573 WLS, 58 TRs, 33** Elephant Reserves, **18** BRs.

n805ac2af9bf.s: The World Air Quality Report 2025 was released by which organisation, headquartered in Switzerland?
n805ac2af9bf.x: The World Air Quality Report 2025 was released by IQAir, a Switzerland-based organisation.
n805ac2af9bf.tq: Identify the releasing agency rather than the subject of the report.
xs: The **World Air Quality Report 2025** was released by **IQAir, Switzerland** (**Mar 2026**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **WHO** sets the **PM2.5** guideline the report measures cities against (**5 µg/m³**).
xa: Only **14%** of cities met that guideline.
Most polluted city: **Loni (UP)**; most polluted country: **Pakistan**; **India 6th**.
⚠ Most polluted city: **2024 = Byrnihat**; **2025 = Loni**.

n3b6b47c08cd.s: According to the World Air Quality Report 2025, what proportion of cities met the WHO guideline of 5 µg/m³ for PM2.5?
n3b6b47c08cd.x: Only 14% of cities met the WHO PM2.5 guideline of 5 µg/m³.
n3b6b47c08cd.tq: Retain the exact percentage and the associated pollutant guideline.
xs: Only **14%** of cities met the **WHO PM2.5 guideline** of **5 µg/m³** — option **(2)**.
The figure is from the **World Air Quality Report 2025** of **IQAir, Switzerland**, released in **Mar 2026**.
xa: Most polluted country: **Pakistan**; most polluted city: **Loni (UP)**; **India 6th** (improved from 5th in 2024).
**New Delhi** was again the most polluted **capital**.
⚠ The **2024 edition** named **Byrnihat (Meghalaya)** the most polluted city.
In India, the **NCAP** (**2019**) covers **130 cities**, tracked on the **PRANA** portal.

n645e3c5c3d5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Climate Change Performance Index 2026?
o: The top three positions were left vacant
India improved its position by 13 places
n645e3c5c3d5.x: India declined by 13 places, to 23rd, because of slow coal phase-down.
xa: The CCPI is published by **Germanwatch**, **NewClimate Institute** and **CAN**.
⚠ **Germanwatch** also publishes the **Climate Risk Index**: India **9th** worst hit (1995-2024).
Contrast: in **EPI 2026** (Yale and Columbia) India was **176th of 177**.

nec98fc2737b.s: Which state topped the State of India's Environment 2026 in Figures?
nec98fc2737b.x: Goa was identified as the top state in the State of India's Environment 2026 in Figures.
nec98fc2737b.tq: Use direct state-ranking recall for a named national report.
xs: **Goa** was the **top state** in the **State of India's Environment 2026 in Figures** — option **(4)**.
The report is by **CSE and Down To Earth**.
**Andhra Pradesh** topped a different index — the **State Energy Efficiency Index 2024**; **Karnataka** topped **SEEI 2023**.
xa: The same report notes **PM2.5 deaths up 61%** in a decade.
⚠ **Kerala (98)** had the most **new animal species** in the ZSI-BSI 2025 tally — a separate list.
**EPI 2026** (Yale and Columbia) ranked India **176th of 177**.

n5faa335a04b.s: The Living Planet Report is released by which organisation, and what decline in wildlife was cited for its 2022 edition?
n5faa335a04b.x: The Living Planet Report is released by WWF, and its 2022 figure cited a 69% decline in wildlife.
n5faa335a04b.tq: Link the publisher with the specific edition and figure.
xs: The **Living Planet Report** is released by **WWF** and cited a **69% wildlife decline** in its **2022** edition — option **(2)**.
It is **biennial**, published **since 1998**.
**61%** is the rise in **PM2.5 deaths** in a decade, from the **State of India's Environment 2026** (CSE and Down To Earth).
xa: ⚠ The **69%** figure is from **LPR 2022**; these notes do not give the LPR 2024 figure.
Other indices: **EPI** = Yale and Columbia; **CCPI** and **CRI** = Germanwatch.
**IUCN** runs the **Red List**: e.g. **Emperor penguin** and **Antarctic fur seal** uplisted to **Endangered** (Apr 2026).

nd7066b82109.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the State Energy Efficiency Index?
o: The 2024 index was prepared by BEE with AEEE
Andhra Pradesh's score rose from 83.25 to 87.25
nd7066b82109.x: Andhra Pradesh, not Karnataka, topped the 2024 index; Karnataka led the 2023 index.
xa: ⚠ **SEEI 2024** top = **AP**; **SEEI 2023** top = **Karnataka**.
In **SEEI 2023**, **Assam and UP** were "**Achievers**" (asked 2024).
**BEE** also runs India's **CCTS**, which got **UK CBAM** recognition (Sep 2026).

n09ec4520a86.s: From September 2026, gaur are to be translocated to which tiger reserve in Andhra Pradesh?
n09ec4520a86.x: From September 2026, gaur are to be translocated to NSTR, which is also to receive four female tigers from Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.
xa: **Kumki** camps at **Musalimadugu** and **Guchimi** (Parvathipuram-Manyam) cut human deaths by **70%**.
**NSTR** is the **largest TR**; **Koundinya** is the only **Elephant Reserve** in AP.
India now has **58** tiger reserves; **Madhav NP (MP)** is the **58th**.

n3aa6bb54372.s: The Environmental Performance Index 2026 was prepared by:
n3aa6bb54372.x: The Environmental Performance Index 2026 was prepared by Yale and Columbia.
n3aa6bb54372.tq: Match the index with its institutional producers rather than its subject area alone.
xs: **EPI 2026** was prepared by **Yale and Columbia** Universities — option **(1)**.
**Oxford** (with Gallup) does the **Happiness Report**; **IEP** the **Global Peace Index**; **Germanwatch** the **CRI/CCPI**.
xa: India **176th of 177**, score **22.46**; only **Laos** below.
**Estonia** (**74.79**) tops, then Luxembourg and UK.
**47** indicators: Ecosystem Vitality **45%**, Climate Mitigation **30%**, Environmental Health **25%**.
Criticism: the EPI **ignores per-capita emissions**.

nb7b91d8aa6a.s: Under IUCN Red List 2026-1, the numbat was moved from:
nb7b91d8aa6a.x: The numbat was downlisted from Endangered to Near Threatened; the desert rain frog was uplisted from Near Threatened to Vulnerable.
xa: The **Emperor penguin** and **Antarctic fur seal** were uplisted to **Endangered** earlier (**Apr 2026**).
⚠ Numbat moved **down** (better); desert rain frog moved **up** (worse).
**Asiatic lions** now number **over 1,000**.

n03923739b2a.s: The Global River Cities Alliance (GRCA) was launched at:
n03923739b2a.x: The GRCA was launched at COP28 in Dubai in December 2023 and is led by the National Mission for Clean Ganga under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
n03923739b2a.tq: Distinguish the launch venue from the venues of other climate initiatives.
xs: The **Global River Cities Alliance** was launched at **COP28, Dubai (Dec 2023)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**COP27** (Sharm el-Sheikh) launched **MAC**; **COP30** (Brazil) launched the **TFFF**; **COP31** (Antalya) is linked to **"35 by 35"**.
xa: It is led by the **National Mission for Clean Ganga** (**Ministry of Jal Shakti**).
⚠ It was launched at Dubai, **not New Delhi**.
COP28 also saw the **Global Stocktake** and the **Loss and Damage Fund** made operational.

nf983da7e723.s: The proposed target under “35 by 35” is that electricity should account for what share of final energy by 2035?
nf983da7e723.x: The “35 by 35” initiative targets electricity constituting 35% of final energy by 2035. It is associated with COP31 under the Australia–Turkey co-presidency at Antalya.
nf983da7e723.tq: Do not reverse the numerical target and the target year in a slogan-based initiative.
xs: **"35 by 35"** targets electricity at **35%** of final energy by **2035** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It is linked to **COP31** (Australia-Turkey co-presidency, **Antalya**).
xa: COP31 (**Nov 2026**) focuses on **electrification, grids and storage**.
**COP32** (**2027**): **Addis Ababa** — the "Africa COP".
India **withdrew its bid** for **COP33** (**2028**).

n4fb867e585b.s: Which one of the following was a key outcome of COP28 held in Dubai?
o: The Global Mutirão and 59 adaptation indicators
The first Global Stocktake and a transition away from fossil fuels
A roadmap to US$1.3 trillion per year by 2035
A US$300 billion annual finance commitment by 2035
n4fb867e585b.x: COP28 produced the Global Stocktake and called for a transition away from fossil fuels. The other outcomes are associated with COP29 or COP30.
n4fb867e585b.tq: Use the COP number and venue to separate outcomes across successive conferences.
xs: **COP28 (Dubai, 2023)** produced the **Global Stocktake** and the call for a **transition away from fossil fuels** — option **(2)**.
**Global Mutirão** and the **59 adaptation indicators** belong to **COP30** (Belém).
The **US$1.3 trn/yr by 2035** Baku-Belém Roadmap is **COP30**; the **US$300 bn** NCQG is **COP29** (Baku).
xa: The **Loss and Damage Fund** was also **operationalised at COP28**.
The **Global River Cities Alliance (GRCA)** was launched at **COP28, Dubai (Dec 2023)**, not New Delhi.
**COP30** also launched Brazil's **TFFF** (US$125 billion forest fund).

n562cfc0ffba.s: The New Collective Quantified Goal on Climate Finance (NCQG) adopted at COP29 envisaged:
n562cfc0ffba.x: COP29 at Baku adopted an NCQG of US$300 billion annually by 2035, replacing the earlier US$100 billion commitment.
n562cfc0ffba.tq: Distinguish the new quantified goal from the earlier finance figure.
xs: The **NCQG** adopted at **COP29 (Baku)** set **US$300 bn per year by 2035** — option **(3)**.
It replaced the earlier **US$100 bn** goal.
**US$1.3 trn/yr by 2035** is the **Baku-Belém Roadmap** of **COP30**.
xa: ⚠ **US$300 bn** = NCQG (COP29); **US$1.3 trn** = Baku-Belém Roadmap (COP30).
**COP30** also agreed to **triple adaptation finance by 2035** and adopted **59 Belém adaptation indicators**.
**COP28 (Dubai)** gave the **Global Stocktake** and operationalised the **Loss and Damage Fund**.

nf318f3d4a94.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about UNFCCC COP30?
o: It was held at Belem, the first COP in the Amazon
It operationalised the Loss and Damage Fund
It set a roadmap to US$1.3 trillion a year in climate finance by 2035
nf318f3d4a94.x: The Loss and Damage Fund was operationalised at COP28 in Dubai, not COP30.
xa: COP30 was called the "**COP of Implementation**"; outcome text: "**Global Mutirão**" / Belém Political Package.
It agreed to **triple adaptation finance by 2035**.
Brazil's **US$125 billion TFFF** was launched at COP30; **India joined as an observer** (2026).

n5f75480cbed.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra Pradesh?
o: Guntur stood second in Swachh Vayu 2026
Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam is its largest tiger reserve
n5f75480cbed.x: Andhra Pradesh ranked second, not first, under MISHTI.
xa: **SEEI 2023** was topped by **Karnataka** (**86.5**).
**Rourkela** topped the 3-10 lakh category of Swachh Vayu 2026.
AP's MISHTI work includes a "**Great Green Wall**" and the **fish-bone technique**.
Other AP facts: **Seshachalam BR (2010)**; **Koundinya** the only Elephant Reserve.

nda78da3de79.s: Which of the following groups of species was moved to Appendix I at CITES CoP20?
o: Whale shark, oceanic whitetip shark and manta rays
Guggul, whale shark and snow leopard
Olive Ridley turtle, whale and dugong
nda78da3de79.x: Whale shark, oceanic whitetip shark and manta rays were included in Appendix I at CITES CoP20.
nda78da3de79.tq: Test the exact species grouping instead of relying on a general wildlife association.
xs: **Whale shark, oceanic whitetip and manta rays** were moved to **Appendix I** at **CITES CoP20** — option **(1)**.
**Guggul** was not listed: **India blocked the EU bid** to list it.
xa: CoP20 was held at **Samarkand, Uzbekistan** (2025), the **first in Central Asia**.
In all, **77 species** were added at CoP20.
**Olive Ridley** turtles are protected in India by the Coast Guard's **Operation Olivia**, using **Turtle Excluder Devices**.

nb67de092b0c.s: The Victoria Falls Declaration and the 5th Strategic Plan for 2025–30 are associated with which meeting?
nb67de092b0c.x: Ramsar COP15, held at Victoria Falls in Zimbabwe, produced the Victoria Falls Declaration and the 5th Strategic Plan for 2025–30.
nb67de092b0c.tq: Start from the distinctive decision and identify the correct convention meeting.
xs: The **Victoria Falls Declaration** and the **5th Strategic Plan 2025-30** came from **Ramsar COP15** (Jul 2025, **Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe**) — option **(1)**.
**CMS COP15** was at **Campo Grande, Brazil**; **UNCCD COP17** at **Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia**; **UNFCCC COP30** at **Belém**.
xa: At Ramsar COP15, **Jayshree Vencatesan** became the **first Indian** to win the **Ramsar Award**.
The **Ramsar Convention** dates from **1971**; India joined in **1982**.
India's **101st** Ramsar site is **Glaw Lake (Arunachal)**, 3 Aug 2026.
⚠ **COP15** twice: **Ramsar** = Victoria Falls; **CMS** = Campo Grande.

n0748a9b9f42.s: Who became the first Indian to win the Ramsar Award?
n0748a9b9f42.x: Jayshree Vencatesan became the first Indian to win the Ramsar Award.
n0748a9b9f42.tq: Use the first-person distinction in a current-affairs award question.
xs: **Jayshree Vencatesan** became the **first Indian** to win the **Ramsar Award** — option **(2)**, at **Ramsar COP15** (Victoria Falls, Jul 2025).
**Hamataliwa papikonda** is not a person: it is a new **lynx spider** found in **Papikonda NP, AP**.
xa: Ramsar COP15 adopted the **Victoria Falls Declaration** and the **5th Strategic Plan 2025-30**.
India: **1st in Asia, 3rd in the world** in Ramsar sites, after **UK (176)** and **Mexico (144)**.
**Tamil Nadu** has the most Ramsar sites (**20**); **Indore** was India's first **Wetland City**.

na9b1403cf9c.s: The Central Empowered Committee of the Supreme Court pulled up which State over mining near a national park known for rhinoceroses?
na9b1403cf9c.x: The Central Empowered Committee pulled up Assam over mining near Kaziranga National Park, an important rhinoceros habitat.
na9b1403cf9c.tq: Match the environmental issue with the State and protected area.
xs: The SC's **Central Empowered Committee** pulled up **Assam** over mining near **Kaziranga** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Kaziranga is the **rhino** park; Jharkhand has **Palamu TR**, Odisha the Olive Ridley beaches, Karnataka the **Gaja Mitra** scheme.
xa: This came in **Aug 2026**.
**Asiatic lions**: **over 1,000**, only in **Gujarat**.
The PA network has **109 NPs**, **573 WLS** and **58 TRs** (**2026**).

n1a4295f0fcc.s: Mission LiFE, or Lifestyle for Environment, was launched by India in:
n1a4295f0fcc.tq: Distinguish the launch year of Mission LiFE from the years of other climate initiatives.
xs: **Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment)** was launched by India in **2022** — option **(3)**.
**2014** is the year of the **Green India Mission**; **2023** is the year of **MISHTI** and the **Green Credit Programme**.
xa: **Green India Mission** was criticised by the **CAG** (Aug 2026).
**Green Credit Programme**: credits are **non-tradable**; **1 credit = 1 tree older than 5 years**.
India's long-term goal is **net zero by 2070**.

nbdf25cfc2c1.s: The Green India Mission, launched in 2014, was criticised by which institution in August 2026?
o: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
nbdf25cfc2c1.x: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India criticised the Green India Mission in August 2026.
nbdf25cfc2c1.tq: Match the programme with the auditing institution rather than an environmental implementing agency.
xs: The **Green India Mission** (**2014**) was criticised by the **CAG** in **Aug 2026** — option **(1)**.
The **Ramsar Secretariat** deals with wetlands and the **GSI** with geo-heritage sites — neither is linked here.
xa: **Mission LiFE** was launched in **2022**; **MISHTI** and the **Green Credit Programme** in **2023**.
**CCTS**, run by **BEE**, received **UK CBAM** recognition (Sep 2026).
Updated NDC: **60%** non-fossil power by **2035**; **net zero by 2070**.

n12286ed14aa.s: The oil spill off Qeshm Island in August 2026 posed a threat to which ecological area?
n12286ed14aa.x: The oil spill in the Strait of Hormuz, off Iran’s Qeshm Island, threatened the Hara mangroves, a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.
n12286ed14aa.tq: Application of location to the threatened ecosystem.
xs: The oil spill off **Qeshm Island** (**Iran**, **Strait of Hormuz**, Aug 2026) threatened the **Hara mangroves** — option **(1)**, a **UNESCO BR**.
**Rushikulya** (Odisha) is an **Olive Ridley** nesting beach; **Keoladeo** is on the **Montreux Record**; the **Cold Desert BR** is in **Lahaul-Spiti, HP**.
xa: **Kerala** is drafting an **Oil Spill Contingency Plan**.
**Trinidad and Tobago** declared a **national emergency** over an **offshore oil spill** (2024, PYQ).
**Cold Desert BR** = India's **13th** in the UNESCO World Network (**Sep 2025**).

nf14349cba52.x: Madhav National Park in Shivpuri district of Madhya Pradesh became India's 58th Tiger Reserve.
xa: **MP** has the most TRs (**9**).
TRs cover **84,488 sq km** (**~2.6%** of India), up from **9** reserves in **1973**.

n2b9a2477258.s: Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve, located in Lahaul-Spiti, Himachal Pradesh, became India’s which Biosphere Reserve in the UNESCO World Network?
n2b9a2477258.x: Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve became India’s 13th Biosphere Reserve in the UNESCO World Network in September 2025. India has 18 Biosphere Reserves in all.
n2b9a2477258.tq: Separate the national total from the World Network sequence number.
xs: **Cold Desert BR** (Lahaul-Spiti, HP) became India's **13th** in the **UNESCO World Network** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**18** is the total of India's Biosphere Reserves, not the World Network count.
xa: ⚠ **13th** = UNESCO World Network BRs; **18** = all BRs in India.
It was added in **Sep 2025** at the **37th MAB ICC**, **Hangzhou**.
It is India's first **high-altitude cold-desert** UNESCO BR.

nd0f57a9dd9f.s: Cold Desert is recognised as India’s first:
nd0f57a9dd9f.x: Cold Desert is India’s first high-altitude cold-desert UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.
nd0f57a9dd9f.tq: Distinguish the UNESCO designation from Ramsar, geo-heritage and tiger-reserve categories.
xs: **Cold Desert** is India's **first high-altitude cold-desert UNESCO Biosphere Reserve** — option **(1)**.
It is in **Lahaul-Spiti, HP**, and became India's **13th** BR in the **UNESCO World Network** in **Sep 2025** (37th MAB ICC, Hangzhou).
xa: ⚠ **13th** = UNESCO World Network BRs; **18** = all BRs in India.
**National Geo-Heritage Sites** are declared by the **GSI**: **Kalinjar Hill** (Banda, UP), **Erra Matti Dibbalu** (near Visakhapatnam).
**Glaw Lake** (Kamlang TR) is **Arunachal's first** Ramsar site and India's **101st**.

ndaf25255f6e.s: Sphaerotheca varshaabhu, recently reported from India, is best described as which one of the following?
o: A lynx spider from Papikonda National Park
A burrowing frog from the urban landscape of Karnataka
A freshwater flowering plant from Telangana
ndaf25255f6e.x: Sphaerotheca varshaabhu is a new burrowing frog reported from the urban landscape of Bengaluru, Karnataka.
ndaf25255f6e.tq: Use the exact species–taxon–location association to eliminate nearby biological distractors.
xs: **Sphaerotheca varshaabhu** is a new **burrowing frog** from the urban landscape of **Karnataka** (Bengaluru) — so option **(3)** is correct.
The lynx spider of Papikonda NP is **Hamataliwa papikonda**; the Rajasthan lizard is **Mesalina bishnoi**; the Telangana plant is **Ammannia telanganensis**.
xa: It is a PYQ species, like **Impatiens karuppusamyi**, a new **plant** described by the **BSI**.
Exam angle: "new species" questions match the name with its **taxon** (plant/frog/spider) and the body (**BSI/ZSI**).
⚠ **Hamataliwa papikonda** = spider in **AP**; **Ammannia telanganensis** = plant in **Telangana**.

n43dfb63ebb8.s: Simonia lawbah is significant because it represents:
o: The first deep-sea skate discovered under the Deep Ocean Mission
India's first species of the Mesalina genus
The first wolf snake from Great Nicobar Island
India's first species of the Simonia genus
n43dfb63ebb8.x: Simonia lawbah, a ray spider from Krem Lawbah cave in Meghalaya, is India's first recorded Simonia species.
n43dfb63ebb8.tq: Focus on the genus-level distinction rather than the broader animal category.
xs: **Simonia lawbah** is **India's first species of the Simonia genus** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The first **Mesalina** in India is the lizard **Mesalina bishnoi**; the deep-sea skate is **Dipturus dhritiae**; the Great Nicobar wolf snake is **Lycodon irwini**.
xa: It is a **ray spider** (**ZSI**) from **Krem Lawbah cave, Meghalaya** (**Jul 2026**).
⚠ **Simonia lawbah** = first **Simonia** (spider); **Mesalina bishnoi** = first **Mesalina** (lizard).
**Hamataliwa papikonda**, another ZSI spider, is a **lynx spider** from **Papikonda NP, AP**.

n04c608306dc.s: Ammannia telanganensis is a freshwater flowering plant reported from:
o: Alpine meadows of Jammu and Kashmir
Ranga Reddy wetlands and Amrabad Tiger Reserve in Telangana
n04c608306dc.x: Ammannia telanganensis was reported from the Ranga Reddy wetlands and Amrabad Tiger Reserve in Telangana in August 2026.
n04c608306dc.tq: Use the habitat and State together to distinguish a plant discovery from aquatic and cave species.
xs: **Ammannia telanganensis** is a freshwater flowering plant from the **Ranga Reddy wetlands and Amrabad TR (Telangana)** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Alpine meadows of **J&K** gave three **Conocephalus katydids**; **Krem Lawbah** gave **Simonia lawbah**; **Kavaratti** gave a **laophontid copepod**.
xa: It was reported in **Aug 2026**.
⚠ **Ammannia telanganensis** = plant in **Telangana**; **Hamataliwa papikonda** = spider in **AP**.
Five **Allographa** lichen-forming fungi were found in the **Western Ghats**.

nf1b912a891e.s: Impatiens karuppusamyi, in the news, is a new species of:
nf1b912a891e.x: Impatiens karuppusamyi is a new plant species described by the Botanical Survey of India.
xa: It was asked in a PYQ (**2024**).
Flora added in 2025: **353** taxa, **221** new to science.
Most new plants in 2025: **Arunachal Pradesh (49)**.

na66dbb58331.s: Which species were uplisted to Endangered in the earlier IUCN update of April 2026?
o: Emperor penguin and Antarctic fur seal
Olive Ridley turtle and greater one-horned rhinoceros
na66dbb58331.x: The emperor penguin and Antarctic fur seal were uplisted to Endangered in the April 2026 update.
na66dbb58331.tq: Direct recall of a paired species-list update.
xs: The **Emperor penguin** and **Antarctic fur seal** were uplisted to **Endangered** in **Apr 2026** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **numbat** and **desert rain frog** changed in the later **IUCN Red List 2026-1** (**Jul 2026**).
xa: Numbat: **EN → NT** (downlisted).
Desert rain frog: **NT → VU** (uplisted).
**Olive Ridley** nesting beaches in Odisha are threatened by **coastal erosion**.

nee92833a157.s: India’s first AI-based human-elephant conflict research centre has been established at:
nee92833a157.x: India’s first AI-based human-elephant conflict research centre is located at Palamu Tiger Reserve in Jharkhand.
nee92833a157.tq: Direct recall of institution and location.
xs: India's first **AI-based human-elephant conflict research centre** is at **Palamu TR, Jharkhand** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Kuno NP** is the Project Cheetah site; **Gahirmatha** hosts Olive Ridley nesting; **Kaziranga** is the rhino park.
xa: The **'Gaja Mitra'** scheme for human-elephant conflict was approved by the **Karnataka** Cabinet.
AP uses **Kumki** elephants: **6** at the **Musallamadugu** camp, Palamaner (Chittoor).
AP's Kumki camps saw a **70%** fall in human deaths.

ne9da3665f76.s: The mass nesting or arribada of Olive Ridley turtles in Odisha is associated with:
ne9da3665f76.x: Olive Ridley arribada occurs at Gahirmatha and Rushikulya in Odisha. Coastal erosion threatens these nesting beaches.
xs: The **Olive Ridley arribada** in Odisha is at **Gahirmatha and Rushikulya** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Keoladeo and Loktak** are on the **Montreux Record**; **Qeshm Island** and the **Hara** mangroves are in **Iran**; **Kamlang** and **Cold Desert** are a TR and a BR.
xa: The threat is **coastal erosion** of the nesting beaches (**Aug 2026**).
**Operation Olivia**: Indian Coast Guard protection of Olive Ridley mass nesting.
It promotes **Turtle Excluder Devices** in fishing nets.

n9bc5e179f76.s: The 'Gaja Mitra' scheme to address human-elephant conflict was approved by the Cabinet of which State?
n9bc5e179f76.x: The Gaja Mitra scheme for human-elephant conflict was approved by the Karnataka Cabinet (asked 2025). Jharkhand hosts India's first AI-based human-elephant conflict research centre at Palamu TR; Kerala and Odisha are not linked to Gaja Mitra.
n9bc5e179f76.tq: Gaja Mitra = Karnataka; AI elephant centre = Palamu, Jharkhand.
xs: The **'Gaja Mitra'** scheme was approved by the **Karnataka** Cabinet — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Jharkhand** hosts the first **AI-based** human-elephant conflict centre (**Palamu TR**), not Gaja Mitra.
xa: It was asked in a PYQ (**2025**).
AP's **Kumki** elephants came **from Karnataka**.
AP has **Kumki** camps at **Musalimadugu** and **Guchimi**.

nbff1e658219.s: 'Operation Olivia', conducted by the Indian Coast Guard, is aimed at:

Protecting the mass nesting of Olive Ridley turtles
Containing oil spills off the Odisha coast
Translocating cheetahs to Kuno National Park
nbff1e658219.x: Operation Olivia is the Indian Coast Guard's operation to protect Olive Ridley mass nesting, with Turtle Excluder Devices promoted in fishing nets. It is not a cyclone rescue, oil-spill or cheetah operation.
xs: **Operation Olivia** is the Indian Coast Guard's operation to **protect Olive Ridley mass nesting** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is not a cyclone-rescue, oil-spill or cheetah operation.
xa: It also promotes **Turtle Excluder Devices** in nets.
Arribada sites: **Gahirmatha and Rushikulya (Odisha)**.
⚠ Do not confuse it with **Operation Sagar Bandhu**, India's response to Cyclone **Ditwah** in **Sri Lanka**.

n64439295d33.s: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, which received UK CBAM recognition, is run by:
n64439295d33.x: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme is run by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency and received UK CBAM recognition.
n64439295d33.tq: Use the implementing-body trap in which a ministry or regulator is substituted for the actual bureau.
xs: The **CCTS** is run by the **Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE)** — option **(3)**; it got **UK CBAM recognition** (Sep 2026).
**NTCA** manages **tiger reserves**, and the **Geological Survey of India** declares **National Geo-Heritage Sites**.
xa: **BEE** (Ministry of Power) with **AEEE** prepares the **State Energy Efficiency Index**: **AP** top in **2024**.
AP's SEEI score rose to **87.25** from **83.25**.
⚠ The **Green Credit Programme** (2023) credits are **non-tradable**.

n37525af3bc6.s: Which country was identified as the most polluted country in the World Air Quality Report 2025?
n37525af3bc6.x: Pakistan was identified as the most polluted country in the World Air Quality Report 2025.
n37525af3bc6.tq: Use direct country-result recall while distinguishing country rankings from city rankings.
xs: **Pakistan** was the **most polluted country** in the **World Air Quality Report 2025** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**India** ranked **6th**, improving from **5th** in **2024**.
xa: Most polluted city: **Loni (UP)**; **New Delhi** was again the most polluted capital.
The report is by **IQAir, Switzerland** (**Mar 2026**).
In the **2024** edition, **Byrnihat (Meghalaya)** was the most polluted city.

n4b39898dfd3.s: According to the World Air Quality Report 2025, which was the most polluted city?
n4b39898dfd3.x: Loni in Uttar Pradesh was the most polluted city, India stood sixth and New Delhi was the most polluted capital. (Sequence not buildable: no dates.)
xa: The report is published by **IQAir**, a **Swiss** body; only **14%** of cities met the WHO PM2.5 guideline of **5 µg/m³**.
⚠ Most polluted city: **2024 = Byrnihat (Meghalaya)**; **2025 = Loni (UP)**.
⚠ Sources differ on how many years in a row Delhi has been the most polluted capital: **Drishti IAS** says the **8th** straight year; **RAU's IAS** implies the **7th**.
**Delhi** is the city most often in the news for poor air (asked 2025).

ncb2ee134d84.s: The State of emergency in August 2026 due to the Bald Range wildfire was declared in:
ncb2ee134d84.x: The Bald Range wildfire occurred in British Columbia, Canada, where a state of emergency was declared and more than 20,000 people were evacuated.
xs: The **Bald Range wildfire** (Aug 2026) was in **British Columbia, Canada**, which declared a **state of emergency** — option **(4)**.
**20,000+** people were evacuated.
**Nepal** had flash floods, **Iran** an oil spill off **Qeshm Island**, and **Sri Lanka** was hit by **Cyclone Ditwah**.
xa: **Trinidad and Tobago** (PYQ) declared a **national emergency** over an **offshore oil spill** (2024).
**Nepal** floods (Bhotekoshi-Trishuli, 26 Aug 2026): toll **1,259**; **13 hydropower projects** damaged.
The Qeshm spill threatened the **Hara mangroves** (UNESCO BR).

nd1b02c7517d.s: The Human Development Index and the Gender Inequality Index are associated with which organisation?
o: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs
United Nations Conference on Trade and Development
nd1b02c7517d.x: UNDP releases both the Human Development Index and the Gender Inequality Index.
xs: Both the **HDI** and the **Gender Inequality Index** come from **UNDP (United Nations Development Programme)** — option **(2)**.
**UN DESA** releases the **World Economic Situation and Prospects**; **UNCTAD** the **World Investment Report**.
The **WEF** releases the **Global Gender Gap** Index — a different gender index.
xa: ⚠ **Gender Gap** = **WEF**; **Gender Inequality Index** = **UNDP**.
The **HDR** has appeared **since 1990**; the HDI was conceived by **Mahbub ul Haq** with **Amartya Sen**.
India: **HDI 130th of 193** (HDR 2025); **GII 108th** (2022 data).
The **Multidimensional Poverty Index** is by **UNDP + OPHI**.

n68f8085ec5f.s: The World Competitiveness Ranking is released by which institution?
n68f8085ec5f.x: The World Competitiveness Ranking is released by IMD in Lausanne.
n68f8085ec5f.tq: Discriminate between the IMD ranking and the WEF competitiveness report.
xs: The **World Competitiveness Ranking** is released by **IMD, Lausanne** — option **(1)**.
The **WEF** publishes the **Global Competitiveness Report / Index** — a different ranking.
The **OECD** publishes the **International Migration Outlook 2025**.
xa: **Global Talent Competitiveness Index** = **INSEAD**.
⚠ The notes do not give India's latest IMD rank.
WEF also issues the **Global Gender Gap**, the **Global Risks Report 2026** and the **Travel and Tourism (now Development) Index**.

n457f8fb0c20.s: Which of the following reports is NOT released by the World Bank?
n457f8fb0c20.x: The International Migration Outlook 2025 is released by the OECD. The Logistics Performance Index, Human Capital Index and Global Economic Prospects are associated with the World Bank.
n457f8fb0c20.tq: Find the one report belonging to a different international organisation.
xs: **International Migration Outlook 2025** is by the **OECD**, not the World Bank — option **(2)**.
**Global Economic Prospects**, the **Human Capital Index** and the **LPI** are all **World Bank** reports.
xa: The World Bank also publishes the **World Development Report 2025**.
India in **LPI 2023**: **38th of 139** (PYQ; 44th in 2018).
**World Economic Situation and Prospects 2026** = **UN DESA** (New York).

n738e8d5099f.s: India's rank in the Global Innovation Index 2025 (out of 139 economies) was:
n738e8d5099f.x: India ranked 38th of 139 in GII 2025, up from 81st in 2015 and 48th in 2020.
xa: The GII is by **WIPO**; **NITI Aayog** is India's nodal agency.
**GII 2025** top: **Switzerland**, Sweden, USA; **China 10th**.
⚠ **GII** here = **Global Innovation Index**, not UNDP's **Gender Inequality Index**.

n830aacc0fc1.s: India's rank in the Gender Inequality Index based on 2022 data, reported in HDR 2023-24, was:
n830aacc0fc1.x: India ranked 108th in the Gender Inequality Index based on 2022 data.
n830aacc0fc1.tq: Avoid confusing the Gender Inequality Index with the HDI and other gender-related indices.
xs: India was **108th** in the **Gender Inequality Index 2022** (UNDP HDR 2023-24) — option **(3)** (PYQ fact).
**130th** is India's **HDI** rank; **91st** its **CPI 2025** rank; **118th** its **Happiness 2025** rank.
xa: ⚠ **Gender Inequality Index** = **UNDP**; **Gender Gap Index** = **WEF** (India **131st** in 2026).
⚠ "GII" in ranking tables usually means WIPO's **Global Innovation Index** (India **38th**).

ncc039201fde.s: In V-Dem 2026, India was classified as:
ncc039201fde.x: V-Dem 2026 ranked India 106th of 179 in the Electoral Democracy Index and classified it as an electoral autocracy.
xa: India's score is the **lowest since 1975**.
V-Dem is by the **V-Dem Institute, University of Gothenburg** (Sweden).
India contests it: **V-Dem relies on expert opinion**.

n8c54156af1e.s: Which State had the lowest score in the SDG India Index 2023–24?
n8c54156af1e.x: Bihar had the lowest score, 57, in the SDG India Index 2023–24.
n8c54156af1e.tq: Identify the bottom performer against the two top-performing States.
xs: **Bihar** had the lowest score (**57**) in the **SDG India Index 2023-24** — option **(2)**.
**Kerala** and **Uttarakhand** were top with **79**; **AP** was in the **top 10**.
xa: India's overall score: **71**.
The index is by **NITI Aayog** (**4th edition**, July 2024).
AP is **1st in SDG 7** and **2nd in SDG 14**.

n0cdd77b82e4.s: The Human Development Index, published by UNDP in its Human Development Report since 1990, was conceived by:
o: Mahbub ul Haq, with Amartya Sen
n0cdd77b82e4.x: The HDI was conceived by Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq, working with Amartya Sen; UNDP has published the HDR since 1990. Sen contributed but was not the sole originator. Stiglitz and Bhagwati are not linked to the HDI.
n0cdd77b82e4.tq: HDI: Mahbub ul Haq (with Sen), UNDP, 1990.
xs: The **HDI** was conceived by **Mahbub ul Haq, with Amartya Sen** — option **(2)**.
So Sen worked **with** Haq: he was not the sole originator.
**UNDP** has published the **HDR since 1990**.
xa: HDI uses **GNI per capita (PPP)** and combines dimensions with a **geometric mean**.
**HDR 2025** theme: "**A Matter of Choice: People and Possibilities in the Age of AI**".
India: **130 of 193**, HDI **0.685** (from 0.676), **Medium** category.
⚠ UNDP's **Gender Inequality Index** (India **108th**) differs from the WEF's **Gender Gap** (India **131st**).

na3b60a12e14.s: According to the India Skills Report 2026, which group recorded higher employability for the first time in five years?

Men, at 54%, compared with women at 51.5%
Women, at 51.5%, compared with men at 54%
na3b60a12e14.x: Women’s employability was 54%, exceeding men’s 51.5% for the first time in five years.
na3b60a12e14.tq: Check both the direction of comparison and the associated percentages.

**ISR 2024** (asked): top talent states = **Maharashtra, UP, Kerala**.
**QS Future Skills Index 2027**: India **13th**, **1st** among lower-middle-income economies.

n05e47e88460.x: The India Skills Report 2024 named Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Kerala as the top talent States (asked in the exam). The other combinations are incorrect.

xa: **ISR 2026**: women's employability **54%** above men's **51.5%**.

**Tamil Nadu** has the most **NIRF 2025** top-100 institutions (**17**).

n0cd7c2f5699.s: Which States topped the SDG India Index 2023-24 with a score of 79?
n0cd7c2f5699.x: Kerala and Uttarakhand topped the NITI Aayog's 4th edition (July 2024) with 79.
xa: India's score **71**; **Bihar (57)** bottom.
**AP in top 10**; but AP slipped in **SDG 9** (13→21), **SDG 5** (5→14) and **SDG 8** (6→16).
⚠ UN SDSN's **SDG Index 2025**: India **99th of 167**.

n2d596007b7a.s: Under the new Super Swachh League of Swachh Survekshan 2024–25, which city ranked first in the 10 lakh-plus category?
n2d596007b7a.x: Indore ranked first in the 10 lakh-plus category and achieved the distinction for the eighth time. Surat and Navi Mumbai followed it.

n1b84f64e9ab.s: Swachh Survekshan 2024-25 is conducted by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs with the survey being run by:
o: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

xs: **Swachh Survekshan 2024-25** is a **MoHUA** survey run by the **Quality Council of India (QCI)** — option **(3)**.
**BEE** runs the **State Energy Efficiency Index**; **MoEFCC** runs **NCAP**.
xa: Started in **2016** with **73** cities; **4,589** cities in 2024-25.
**Super Swachh League** (10 lakh+): **Indore** → Surat → Navi Mumbai.

ncb26a0b4792.s: Which State ranked first among 19 large and medium States in consumer justice delivery according to the India Justice Report Consumer Justice Report 2026?
ncb26a0b4792.x: Andhra Pradesh ranked first among 19 large and medium States in consumer justice delivery. Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Karnataka and West Bengal followed it.
ncb26a0b4792.tq: Read the ranking order from the first position rather than selecting a familiar State.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** ranked **1st** among **19** large/mid States in the **IJR Consumer Justice Report 2026** — option **(3)**.
**MP, Rajasthan, Karnataka and West Bengal** followed.
xa: It was released in **Mar 2026**.
⚠ **IJR 2025** = AP **2nd**; **IJR Consumer Justice 2026** = AP **1st**.
The IJR is supported by **Tata Trusts** (first in **2019**).

n8b21f374967.s: In the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index 2023 (the latest edition), India's rank was:
n8b21f374967.x: India ranked 38th of 139 in LPI 2023, up from 44th in 2018 (PYQ). 44th was the 2018 position; 54th and 22nd are not India's LPI ranks. Note that India's GII 2025 rank is also 38/139, but that index is by WIPO, not the World Bank.
n8b21f374967.tq: LPI 2023 and GII 2025: both 38/139 - don't mix the publishers (World Bank vs WIPO).
xs: India was **38th of 139** in **LPI 2023** (latest) — option **(2)**, a **PYQ** fact.
**44th** was India's **2018** rank.
xa: The **LPI** is a **World Bank** index.
⚠ **38th of 139** is also India's **GII 2025** rank, but the GII is by **WIPO**.
The World Bank also publishes the **Human Capital Index** and **Global Economic Prospects**.

n1b5f730692a.s: Which case held that Padma awards are not 'titles' prohibited by Article 18?
n1b5f730692a.x: The Balaji Raghavan case (1996) held Padma awards are not titles under Article 18, though they cannot be used as prefixes or suffixes.
xa: The same rule applies to the **Bharat Ratna**.
**Padma Vibhushan** is the **2nd highest** civilian award; **Padma Bhushan** 3rd; **Padma Shri** 4th.
AP demanded the Bharat Ratna for **NTR** (Feb 2026).

nbe00a9eb93d.s: In which case was it held that national civilian awards such as the Padma awards are not titles under Article 18?
nbe00a9eb93d.x: The Balaji Raghavan case of 1996 dealt with the status of national awards under Article 18.
nbe00a9eb93d.tq: Match the constitutional issue with the case specifically associated with it.
xs: The **Balaji Raghavan case (1996)** held that national awards are **not "titles" under Art. 18** — option **(4)**.
Hence they cannot be used as a **prefix or suffix** to the name.
xa: **Art. 18** exempts **military and academic distinctions**.
The ruling covers both the **Padma awards** and the **Bharat Ratna**.
**Bharat Ratna** last given in **2024** to **5** awardees.

ncd7925487da.s: The Padma awards announced on 25 January 2026 comprised:
o: 131 awards: 5 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri
139 awards: 7 Padma Vibhushan, 19 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri
131 awards: 7 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan and 111 Padma Shri
113 awards: 5 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan and 95 Padma Shri
ncd7925487da.x: The 2026 list had 131 awards: 5 PV, 13 PB, 113 PS. 139 awards with a 7/19/113 split was the 2025 list; the other splits do not match either year.
xs: The **2026** list had **131** awards: **5 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan, 113 Padma Shri** — option **(1)**.
**139** with **7 / 19 / 113** was the **2025** list; the other splits match neither year.
xa: ⚠ Padma Shri = **113** in both **2025** and **2026**.
2025: **23** women and **9** posthumous awardees; one award to a **duo**.
2026 PV awardees include **V.S. Achuthanandan** and **Dharmendra** (both posthumous).

n4395c8cff35.s: The Sahitya Akademi Award 2025 was given in
o: 24 languages, comprising only Eighth Schedule languages
22 languages, all from the Eighth Schedule
26 languages, including Hindi and Sanskrit only
24 languages, comprising 22 Eighth Schedule languages, English and Rajasthani
n4395c8cff35.x: The 2025 Sahitya Akademi Awards covered 24 languages: 22 Eighth Schedule languages, English and Rajasthani.
n4395c8cff35.tq: Separate the total number of languages from the constitutional-language component.
xs: Sahitya Akademi 2025 was given in **24 languages**: **22 Eighth Schedule** languages + **English** + **Rajasthani** — option **(4)**.
So it is not limited to Eighth Schedule languages: **English** and **Rajasthani** are the two extra.
xa: The award carries **₹1 lakh**.
The Akademi was founded in **1952**, inaugurated **12 Mar 1954**, registered as a society in **1956**.
2025 winners include **Navtej Sarna** ('Crimson Spring', English) and **Mamta Kalia** (Hindi).

naa5043d9be8.s: The International Booker Prize 2025 was awarded for
o: Heart Lamp by Banu Mushtaq, translated by Deepa Bhasthi
The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny by Kiran Desai
naa5043d9be8.x: Banu Mushtaq’s Kannada story collection Heart Lamp, translated by Deepa Bhasthi, won the International Booker Prize 2025.
naa5043d9be8.tq: Match the year, work, author and translator while separating shortlisted works from winners.
xs: **International Booker 2025**: **'Heart Lamp'** by **Banu Mushtaq** (Kannada stories), translated by **Deepa Bhasthi** — option **(2)**.
**'Flesh'** (David Szalay) won the **Booker 2025**; **Taiwan Travelogue** won the **International Booker 2026**.
Kiran Desai's novel was only **shortlisted** for the Booker 2025.
xa: International Booker 2026 was the **first Mandarin Chinese** winner.
The International Booker prize is **£50,000**, split between **author and translator**.

n43bf7daa0e5.s: Which one of the following was shortlisted for the Booker Prize 2025?
o: The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny by Kiran Desai
n43bf7daa0e5.x: Kiran Desai’s The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny was shortlisted for the Booker Prize 2025; David Szalay’s Flesh was the winner.
n43bf7daa0e5.tq: Distinguish the winner from a shortlisted title and from International Booker entries.
xs: **Kiran Desai's 'The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny'** was **shortlisted** for the **Booker 2025** — option **(3)**.

nbacd86d0d85.s: Who is the author of the autobiography 'Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles'?

n9ad51a13a53.s: The book 'An Accidental Lawyer - My Adventures in Law and Life' is the autobiography of:

na20b65f8f33.s: In the UNSC straw poll for a candidate for UN Secretary-General, which condition is required?
o: At least 9 ‘Encourage’ votes and no ‘Discourage’ vote from a permanent member
A unanimous vote of all 15 Security Council members
At least 10 ‘Encourage’ votes irrespective of permanent-member votes
A two-thirds vote of the UN General Assembly before the straw poll
na20b65f8f33.x: A candidate needs at least 9 ‘Encourage’ votes out of 15 and must receive no ‘Discourage’ vote from any permanent member.
na20b65f8f33.tq: Break a procedural rule into its numerical threshold and veto-related condition.
xs: A candidate needs at least **9 "Encourage"** votes out of **15** and **no P5 "Discourage"** vote — so option **(1)** is correct.
Unanimity, a 10-vote rule ignoring the P5, or a prior UNGA vote are not part of the rule.
xa: The **first straw poll** was held in **Aug 2026**, as **Guterres** leaves at the end of 2026.
The Secretary-General has a **5-year** term; appointment under **Art. 97** (UNGA on UNSC recommendation).

n8af39566811.s: The tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners is:
